{"observedAt":"2026-10-22T17:55:09.142Z","queryTruncated":false,"rows":[{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fleet-leadership-continuity-and-actuation-2026-08-01","title":"Fix what made leading a fleet expensive: lost work, two conflicting truths, polled leadership, and gauges without levers","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Fix what made leading a fleet expensive: lost work, two conflicting truths, polled leadership, and gauges without levers\nslug: fleet-leadership-continuity-and-actuation-2026-08-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-01\nupdated: 2026-10-13\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** **19 of 20 done.** P-011 (Phase 3's verification item) is the only one open.\n\n**P-011's blocker MOVED 2026-08-02 ~15:47Z: the fix is now LIVE. The prior Now — \"not on origin/main, :3070 contains 0 occurrences\" — is SUPERSEDED and false.** Verified ~17:05Z in four hops, none of them inferred: (1) `origin/main` = `1e0ddc5864`; (2) release checkout `papercup-release` is at that sha and contains the change; (3) `:3070` = pid 4191737, cwd `papercup-release/apps/operator`, started **15:47:57Z** — after the 15:32:49Z green; (4) deployed source read directly at `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/loop/arm.ts:553` — gated `args.mode === 'monitor'`, emitting `fleet:member-dead · fleet:claim-released · fleet:item-completed · fleet:context-critical` plus the `events:await` call shape. A live `loop:arm { mode:'monitor' }` returned it verbatim at 16:23Z.\n\n**What P-011 now waits on is ELAPSED TIME, not work.** The treatment reaches an agent only when it CALLS `loop:arm`; agents already looping never re-arm and so never see it. Fleet baseline: **251 `loop:arm` calls / 74 distinct agents / 7d ≈ 36/day ≈ 1.5/hr.** In the 75 min since restart: 2 calls, **both from `su-6fa6afdb`, this plan's own author**. Expected non-self exposure ≈1.9, observed 0 — inside Poisson noise, **NOT a negative result**.\n\n**Next:** HOLD P-011 until ≥ ~2026-08-03T16:00Z (24h post-restart ≈ 36 expected exposures), then run the test in TWO ORDERED steps — exposure BEFORE adoption. (1) EXPOSURE: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT coord_owner_id) FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations WHERE tool_name='loop:arm' AND invoked_at > '2026-08-02T15:47:57Z'` — if distinct NON-SELF agents < 10, report \"insufficient exposure\" and hold; never publish a bare adoption count. (2) ADOPTION: `harness_shared.event_awaits` WHERE `event_key LIKE 'fleet:%'` AND created_at > that same instant, EXCLUDING `subscriber_id='su-6fa6afdb-860d-4812-a575-6a6656e07160'` (exposure #1 is this plan's author; self-awaits are contamination). Do NOT manufacture exposure by arming loops to create data points.\n\n## Background\n\nLeading `push-not-poll` produced a clean result (1 polling violation across ~1,050 scheduled things, fix measured-verified, enforcement shipped). It also produced an unusually clear picture of where the fleet-leadership surface is thin, because the same failure shapes recurred often enough in one session to be diagnosable rather than anecdotal.\n\nThree shapes account for almost all of it:\n\n1. **Work that was DONE presented as work that was NOT.** Three times. A landed implementation whose migration was never applied; a fully-built, CI-wired guard whose holder compacted and left an empty checkpoint; and a cleared plan dependency that never reached the work-item. Each time the surface consulted was individually convincing and simply described a different object than the one governing behaviour. Written up as the (now normative) agent-insights doc `verify-the-surface-that-governs-behaviour` — that is the human-side mitigation. This plan is the machine-side.\n\n2. **Two claims on one unit of work, with nothing asserting they agree.** The plan-item lane and the work-item claim diverged in three separate ways in a single day.\n\n3. **A leader that can see everything and change almost nothing.** `fleet:leader-brief` reports dead / stalled / orphaned / idle / context-critical / unanswered. For nearly all of it the only available response is a coord message and hope. The one real lever is reclaiming a claim.\n\nFiled bugs this plan discharges: EI-18730414627683753, EI-18731480441007330 (downgraded — read its correction), EI-18732218464905145, EI-18732669095544832, EI-18734870651452334, EI-19278588744322125, EI-19278589690487622, EI-19278590581840106, EI-19278591489507332.\n\n## Phase 1 — Stop losing and hiding completed work\n\n- **P-001** `done` Surface PRIOR WORK at claim time: when a work-item has any prior holder, attempt, or release, `work_items:claim` / `work_items:get` / `scheduler:get_next` return a banner naming who held it, how long, when they released, whether a checkpoint exists, and (ideally) the files their tool-invocations touched. Data already exists in `worked_by_history` / `attempts` / `claims` / `last_released_by` / `last_released_at` — this is presentation, not new storage. importance: high — note: ← WI-6701 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Auto-checkpoint IMMEDIATELY BEFORE a compaction boundary, not only at turn-end. This is the item that removes the race rather than managing it — \"checkpoint, then compact\" is two steps with no interlock, and the second destroys the context the first needs. importance: high — note: Already shipped (flush gate HOLDS the boundary — stronger than specified); verified green.\n- **P-003** `done` Auto-checkpoint on claim RELEASE whenever the releasing holder has no agent-written checkpoint. The mechanical turn-end snapshot already exists and fired for a sibling item in the same run; it simply does not run on the release path. Even \"released at T after N tool calls, no agent checkpoint, files touched: [...]\" is enough to stop the next holder rebuilding. importance: high — note: Already shipped, covering all three release routes; verified green 32/32.\n- **P-004** `done` Regression test: an item that has been worked and released with no checkpoint must be programmatically DISTINGUISHABLE from a never-started item at every read surface an agent uses to decide whether to build. This is the invariant P-001..P-003 exist to establish; without it they can silently regress. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n\n## Phase 2 — Make plan-item and work-item one truth\n\n- **P-005** `done` Make `plans:set-item-blocked-by` propagate to the linked work-item in the same transaction, BOTH directions: clearing the last edge clears the `plan-lane` externalBlocker and reopens the item; adding an edge to an open item re-blocks it. Today only the completion-driven path propagates, so a manual unblock returns ok and silently changes nothing. importance: high — note: Already shipped as a reaction rule, symmetric by construction; verified green 20/20.\n- **P-006** `done` Make claim release ATOMIC across both surfaces: at a session/compaction boundary, release the work-item claim and the plan-item lane together, or neither. A half-released pair is worse than either behaviour applied consistently, because the two surfaces then actively contradict each other. importance: high\n- **P-007** `done` Warn at claim time when the item's linked plan lane is held by a DIFFERENT live agent — \"this work-item is unassigned BUT its plan lane is claimed by <agent> (live)\". Cheap guard that catches the divergence at the moment it matters even if P-006 misses a path. blocked-by: P-006 importance: normal\n- **P-008** `done` DECIDE (then implement): should there be ONE authoritative claim rather than two mirrored ones? P-005..P-007 are three point-fixes for one architectural duality; if the duality is not load-bearing, collapsing it retires this whole class instead of patching instances. Produce a recommendation with the migration cost before building more mirrors. importance: normal — note: ← WI-6708 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Make leading push-based, not polled\n\n- **P-009** `done` Emit fleet transition events the leader actually reacts to — member-dead, claim-released, item-completed, context-critical, idle-with-claimable — catalogued under a `fleet:<slug>:` prefix so a leader DISCOVERS them via `events:catalog` without being told. `leader-brief` already computes every one as a derived field; nothing publishes them. importance: high — note: ← WI-6709 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Re-document leading as event-driven: a composed `events:await` over the Phase-3 event set as the PRIMARY mechanism, with `loop:arm` demoted to a long fallback heartbeat for what is genuinely not event-shaped. Include the ready-to-paste spec in the fleet-leader guidance. blocked-by: P-009 importance: normal — note: ← WI-6710 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `todo` Verify the win on a real fleet: a leader using P-009/P-010 should burn materially fewer wakes AND react faster to a released claim than the 180s poll did (~14 wakes, mostly near-noops, up to 3min to notice the last item's claim drop). Measure both, because reducing wakes while worsening latency would be a regression. blocked-by: P-010 importance: normal — note: ← WI-6711 blocked (1 external blocker)\n\n## Phase 4 — Give the leader levers, not just gauges\n\n- **P-012** `done` Add a leader-initiated forced checkpoint (`fleet:require-checkpoint { member, itemId }`) that RETURNS whether it landed, so the leader knows state is safe before advising a compaction rather than hoping. Complements P-002 rather than duplicating it: P-002 removes the common race, this covers the general case (a member about to be stood down, killed, or reassigned). importance: normal — note: ← WI-6712 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Distinguish DELIVERED from ACTED-ON for directives: `coord:send { wake:'required' }` returning `woken: 1` currently proves only that a session woke. For a safety-critical directive the leader needs to know whether the instruction was carried out — minimally, whether the named side effect (a checkpoint write, a claim release) occurred. importance: normal — note: expectEffect on coord:send + directive-effect(.read) probe + fleet:leader-brief `directives`\n- **P-014** `done` Let a leader register a CUSTOM invariant evaluated each brief, rather than only reading the fields the brief was designed to expose. Motivating case: a ~6-line check cross-referencing each member's parked keys against the assignee of the items named in them caught a real problem no built-in counter surfaced — and died with the turn that wrote it. importance: low — note: fleet:invariant + evaluation in leader-brief; migration 713 applied; invariants.test.ts 17/17, tools-md-sync 54/54, typecheck clean (WI-6777)\n\n## Phase 5 — Fix the monitoring surfaces that produced wrong verdicts\n\n- **P-015** `done` Render a composed await in `fleet:leader-brief` as ONE entry carrying its own verdict — mode (any/all), required-of-total, the ROOT's effective deadline and timeout behaviour — and never list a root as a sibling of its own leaves. This rendering is what turned the most benign possible park into the most alarming possible reading and produced a false fleet-halting-deadlock report to the owner. importance: high — note: Already shipped by a peer since the bug was filed; verified green (93/93).\n- **P-016** `done` Resolve a composed LEAF to its root's effective deadline anywhere liveness is judged, not just in leader-brief. A leaf row with a non-null root_id is not self-describing, so every consumer of `event_awaits` can draw the same wrong conclusion; a view or helper fixes the class rather than one surface. blocked-by: P-015 importance: normal — note: migration 710 view event_awaits_effective + shared TS resolver events/await/effective-deadline.ts applied at listActiveAwaits + listParkedAwaitsForSubscribers + adv-roster\n- **P-017** `done` Make `events:await` REFUSE a work-item status key when the caller is that item's assignee — unsatisfiable by construction, and a precondition check against state already in hand. Enforce at CLAIM time too: in the observed case the park was registered BEFORE the conflicting claim, so either call can be the one that completes the cycle. importance: normal — note: Already shipped by a peer; verified green (68/68).\n- **P-018** `done` Detect the dormancy shape: a member that finishes a turn with no loop armed and no event park is permanently asleep and invisible in every summary counter. Surface it as a first-class brief verdict, distinct from \"parked\" (which is healthy). importance: normal — note: Already shipped by a peer; verified green (93/93).\n\n## Phase 6 — Small footguns with outsized blast radius\n\n- **P-019** `done` `code:run`: strip undefined-valued keys before strict-args validation. Passing a key with an explicitly-undefined value is idiomatic JS for \"not provided\" and is currently rejected as an unrecognised key. importance: normal\n- **P-020** `done` `code:run`: when a validation error ABORTS a script, report which already-ordered writes did NOT execute — the way `okFalseMutations` / `partial: true` already report failed ones. A read's arg typo silently cancelled a time-critical recovery message in this run, and only careful reading of the result caught it. importance: normal\n\n## Decisions\n\n- **D-001** Fix the READ side and the WRITE side of lost work INDEPENDENTLY. P-002/P-003 make a checkpoint more likely to exist; P-001 makes prior work visible even when it does not. Both are needed, because a checkpoint can always be absent for reasons the platform cannot control (a hard kill, an OOM, a crash), and the read-side banner is the cheaper of the two while covering every cause.\n\n- **D-002** Prefer REMOVING a race to giving the leader a tool for managing it. The observed loss came from instructing a member to \"checkpoint, then compact\" — a race, not a procedure. P-002 (auto-checkpoint at the boundary) is therefore ranked above P-012 (the forced-checkpoint verb), though both are worth having: the verb still serves stand-down, kill, and reassignment.\n\n- **D-003** `loop:arm` is NOT removed by Phase 3. Events become the primary wake mechanism; the loop stays as a long fallback heartbeat. A purely event-driven leader with a missing or unfired event is a leader that never wakes at all, which is strictly worse than polling. P-011 must confirm latency improves, not just that wake count drops.\n\n- **D-004** Phase 2 is deliberately sequenced point-fixes THEN an architecture question (P-008), not the reverse. P-005/P-006 are small, independently valuable, and unblock real work now; P-008 asks whether the plan-item/work-item duality should exist at all. Shipping the point-fixes first buys time to answer that properly instead of pausing everything on a redesign.\n\n- **D-005** Phase 1 is the recommended minimum if scope must be cut. It is nearly all presentation of data already stored, it needs no new architecture, and it prevents the most expensive observed failure — an agent rebuilding a finished, CI-wired feature. The whole phase is plausibly smaller than P-009 alone.\n\n- **D-006** Severity here comes from BLAST RADIUS, not from how hard the bug was to hit. Several of these are rare per-session and near-certain across a fleet-week: three plan/work-item divergences and two nearly-rebuilt features happened in ONE afternoon with six members. Frequency scales with fleet size and with how often members compact, and both are increasing.\n\n### D-007 — Do NOT collapse the plan-item/work-item CLAIMS — collapse the two LINKAGE mechanisms instead\nDate: 2026-08-02\nP-008 asked whether the plan-item/work-item claim duality is load-bearing, and if not to collapse it. Answer: **the CLAIM duality is load-bearing and must stay. The genuinely collapsible duality is one level down — the two LINKAGE mechanisms — and that one is already 58% converged and cheap to finish.**\n\n#### Why the claim duality must stay (neither surface can subsume the other)\n\n1. **Population.** 29,233 work-items in this workspace; only **2,704 (9.2%)** carry any plan-item linkage. The other 90.8% — the whole issue family (bug/change/task) — have no plan lane at all, and `resolvePlanItemStampFromColumns` returns null for anything not `family === 'feature'`. So `plan_item_claims` structurally cannot become the one authoritative claim.\n2. **Semantics.** `plan_item_claims` carries `intent` (NOT NULL), `liveness_mode` (availability|activity), `ttl_sec`/`expires_ts`, `owner_name`/`owner_label` — none of which exist on `work_items`. And moving the one that matters is already **forbidden by a standing ruling**: `_holder-lens.ts` states in capitals that an intent column must NEVER be added to `work_items`, because it would be a THIRD place a goal is written (`coord_presence`, `plan_item_claims`, `work_items`) — a transcribed copy that silently rots. So `work_items` cannot subsume `plan_item_claims` either.\n3. **Precedent — this exact question already has a house answer.** `claim-ssot-agreement.integration.test.ts` (D-003 of work-item-claimability-clarity-2026-07-20) resolved the structurally identical case for the issue-family claim floors: a physical merge would have regressed federation own-node recovery, so the two representations stay PHYSICALLY SEPARATE and are bound by an **anti-drift agreement test** that pins each intentional divergence. P-005/P-006/P-007 are the same shape; the missing piece is the binding invariant, not a merge.\n\n#### What IS collapsible, with measured cost\n\nA work-item links to its plan item by **two** mechanisms — the `payload->'plan_item'` back-pointer and the `source_plan_slug`/`source_plan_item_ids` columns — and `resolvePlanItemStamp` must try BOTH. Measured today:\n\n| linkage | rows | oldest | newest |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| both | 1,134 | 2026-06-17 | **2026-08-01 (today)** |\n| payload-only | 1,569 | 2026-06-15 | 2026-07-28 |\n| columns-only | 1 | 2026-06-10 | 2026-06-10 |\n\nThe live promotion path already writes BOTH (the `both` bucket runs through today; `payload-only` stopped 2026-07-28). So this is **not an active divergence — it is a completed migration with an un-backfilled tail.**\n\nThe hazard is real and was demonstrated while producing this decision: a column-only join reported \"no linked work-item\" for BOTH currently-live plan-item claims, when in fact both link fine via payload (WI-5135, WI-6708). Any consumer that resolves via one mechanism gets a different answer than one that resolves via the other.\n\n**Migration cost: one idempotent UPDATE backfilling 1,569 rows** (`source_plan_slug`/`source_plan_item_ids` from `payload->'plan_item'`), plus a decision on the single 2026-06-10 columns-only row. After that the column mechanism alone is sufficient and `resolvePlanItemStamp`'s dual resolution can collapse to one path, retiring the \"resolve via EITHER mechanism\" caveat in `plan-item-lane-guard.ts` and `plan-item-claim-collision.ts`.\n\n#### Recommended follow-on work (instead of more mirrors)\n\n- **B1** Backfill the 1,569 payload-only rows, then collapse `resolvePlanItemStamp` to the column path.\n- **B2** Add the claim-pair agreement invariant in the `claim-ssot-agreement` mould: for a seeded state, a feature-family work-item's holder and its linked plan-item lane's owner agree, with the deliberate divergences pinned.\n- **B3** Close the one gap the point-fixes genuinely miss: `reconcileLinkedWorkItemsForPlanItem` fires only on the plan-item's done TRANSITION, so a work-item landing in `todo` AFTER its plan item is already terminal is never reconciled — the documented cause of EI-13337 / EI-13352 / EI-13267 / EI-14693 (the backlog-drain fleet re-claiming finished work, re-verifying \"already done\", and re-closing it by hand). That is a missing reconciler, not a missing merge.\n\nEvidence gathered 2026-08-01 against the live operator DB; counts are workspace-scoped to papercusp-workspace.\n\n### D-008 — P-009 scoping: fleet-scoped `fleet:<slug>:<transition>` keys — payload_filter on global keys is NOT the reuse-first option it looks like\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\n\nP-009 asks for five leader-facing transitions under a `fleet:<slug>:` prefix. I surveyed the live `events:catalog` (34 families) first. Two findings; the second inverts my own first read.\n\n#### Finding 1 — \"3 of 5 already fire\" was WRONG. Only 1 is.\n\n| P-009 transition | existing key | leader-usable? |\n|---|---|---|\n| claim-released | `claim:released:<id>` | **NO — id-scoped** |\n| item-completed | `work-item:done:<id>` | **NO — id-scoped** |\n| idle-with-claimable | `work-item:claimable` | **YES — global + payload_filtered** |\n| member-dead | — | missing |\n| context-critical | — | missing |\n\nName-matching is not capability-matching. The first two are **ID-SCOPED**: they fire for ONE known item id. A leader does not know in advance which of its fleet's items will be released or completed next, so using them means registering N awaits and RE-REGISTERING whenever the set changes — a subscription treadmill driven by polling the item set, i.e. exactly the clock-driven anti-pattern this plan exists to kill. They are right for a delegator awaiting a SPECIFIC child; they are not a fleet feed.\n\nOnly `work-item:claimable` is genuinely global + payload-filtered (`{id,kind,severity,harness,title,state,reason,plan,tags}`), so a leader can park on it today via `payload_filter: { plan: { eq: '<slug>' } }`. That one is a docs pointer, not a build.\n\n**P-009 is therefore 4 new emissions + 1 catalog pointer, not 2 + 3.**\n\n#### Finding 2 — route (b) (payload_filter on global keys) is not reuse; it mints the same families and is worse.\n\nThe reuse-first instinct says filter an existing global key instead of adding `fleet:<slug>:item-completed`. **There is no global key to filter.** Verified in `work-items-events.ts`: the only settle key is `work-item:done:${wi.id}`, the only release key `claim:released:${wi.id}` — both id-scoped. Route (b) must MINT global families first. Same new-family count, then strictly worse:\n\n1. **Payloads carry no fleet identity.** Every work-item payload is `{id,state,kind,harness,title}` (claimable adds severity/reason/plan/tags). No `fleet`; `done`/`released` do not even carry the holder. So \"any member of MY fleet\" is INEXPRESSIBLE as a payload_filter without first adding a fleet field — the same emit-time `fleetOfAgent()` lookup route (a) needs. No lookup saving.\n2. **Wake amplification.** A global settle key loads EVERY leader's await row on EVERY system-wide settle, then filters them out. A fleet-scoped key loads only that fleet's. In route (a) the filtering is free because it is in the key.\n3. **Discoverability is the stated requirement** — P-009: \"catalogued under a `fleet:<slug>:` prefix so a leader DISCOVERS them via `events:catalog` without being told.\" A payload_filter convention is not discoverable as a fleet concept; the leader must be told, which is the failure the item names.\n4. **Precedent exists.** `fleet:drained:<slug>` is an established fleet-scoped, slug-templated awaitable key with a catalog entry and sugar verb (`fleet:await-drained`). Route (a) extends a working pattern; route (b) invents a second alongside it.\n\n**DECISION: route (a).** New families `fleet:<slug>:member-dead`, `fleet:<slug>:context-critical`, `fleet:<slug>:claim-released`, `fleet:<slug>:item-completed`, modelled on `fleet-drained-events.ts` (pure detector + fire-and-forget emitter + injectable seams). `idle-with-claimable` is served by EXISTING `work-item:claimable` + `payload_filter { plan }` and gets a catalog cross-reference, not a new key.\n\n#### Consequence for the two derived detectors\n\n`claim-released` / `item-completed` co-fire from the existing transition sites in `work-items-events.ts` (the co-fire shape `emitWorkItemClaimableEvent` already uses), resolving the holder's fleet at emit time.\n\n`member-dead` / `context-critical` have NO single transition site — death is the ABSENCE of a write; context pressure is derived from reported token counts. They are DERIVED detectors, exactly as `fleet-drained-events.ts` documents for its own case (\"there is no single transition site that MEANS 'the fleet drained' — it is a COMPUTED condition\"). They need a periodic sweep with edge detection against a prior snapshot.\n\nBest-effort in-process edge state (lost on restart) is acceptable and is not a storage-policy violation, because P-010 explicitly retains `loop:arm` as a long fallback heartbeat: the architecture is push-primary WITH a heartbeat backstop, so a missed edge across a restart degrades to the backstop rather than losing the signal. Same shape and justification as the documented in-process throttle already in `work-items-events.ts` (`lastClaimableReleaseFireAt`).\n\n#### Follow-on\n\nThe id-scoped-vs-global distinction bit me and would bite the next agent: `events:catalog` lists a family but never says whether a subscriber who does NOT know the id can use it. Filed as a catalog-legibility follow-on.\n\n### D-009 — P-011 is blocked on ADOPTION of P-009's events, not on fleet availability — do not benchmark until a treatment arm exists\nDate: 2026-08-02\nP-011 was carried for a day as \"blocked until a real multi-member fleet is live, and do not manufacture one.\" That framing is now known to be wrong, and acting on it would have produced a meaningless benchmark.\n\n**A real fleet IS live.** `nonp2p-bug-drain-0801`: 11 members, 10 active within 5 minutes, draining real bugs. Nothing manufactured.\n\n**The actual blocker is that the treatment arm does not exist.** P-009's fleet-transition events have essentially no adoption. From `harness_shared.event_awaits` over 48h across 310 agents: fleet-transition awaits = **1** (one agent, 08-01 22:26), against 38 `release:*` and 28 `green-checkpoint:*` awaits spread over 11 distinct agents each.\n\nThat contrast is the load-bearing part. It refutes the easy explanation that agents avoid event-driven waiting — they adopt it readily for gate events. P-009's fleet events specifically are the ones nobody reaches for.\n\nMeanwhile the live fleet's leader `su-707029ce` runs `loop:arm` at `intervalSec: 600` with `fireCount: 91` over ~13h, and members burn 70-132 wakes each per 24h with `suppressed-redundant` counts of 13-29 already appearing.\n\n**Ruling.** Benchmarking P-011 today would compare a polled leader against another polled leader and report no win — a false negative that would look like evidence P-009 does not help. So:\n\n1. P-011 stays `todo` and MUST NOT be claimed as a measurement task until at least one leader actually parks on the fleet events.\n2. The blocking work is adoption, filed as EI-19326284032085138's sibling capture (fleet-event adoption gap): surface the event park at the point where a leader arms its monitor loop, so the push path is the default and the clock loop the fallback.\n3. Whoever picks P-011 up must first confirm a treatment arm exists — check `harness_shared.event_awaits` for fleet-transition awaits in the measurement window. If that count is still ~0, the item is not ready and this decision is why.\n\nThe polled BASELINE recorded above is real and worth keeping: leader 600s/91 fires per 13h; members 70-132 wakes/24h; only 1 deliberate fleet-event await in 48h across 310 agents.\n\n### D-010 — P-009's item text states the fleet-transition key shape BACKWARDS — the real keys are transition-first, and only four exist\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\n\nFound while closing EI-19326580626849271 (D-009's named unblocker). This is a correction to a documented fact that P-011's implementer will act on directly, so it is recorded here rather than only as a fact or a coord message.\n\n#### The error\n\nP-009's item text says the transitions are \"catalogued under a `fleet:<slug>:` prefix\" — SLUG-FIRST. Verified against `packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/catalog.ts:313-347`, the real keyTemplates are TRANSITION-FIRST:\n\n    fleet:member-dead:<slug>\n    fleet:context-critical:<slug>\n    fleet:claim-released:<slug>\n    fleet:item-completed:<slug>\n\n#### Why it matters more than a typo\n\nP-011 is precisely the item that arms these awaits. An agent who retypes the documented shape (`fleet:push-not-poll:member-dead`) registers an await on a key nothing ever emits — and the failure is SILENT: the waiter simply sleeps forever, exactly the hand-typed-key drift that never rendezvouses. A benchmark built on such an await would record zero push-wakes and read as \"P-009 does not help,\" which is the same false-negative D-009 already warned this item is prone to, arriving by a different route.\n\n**Copy the key from `events:catalog` or the catalog.ts template. Never retype it from prose — including from this decision.**\n\n#### Second correction\n\nP-009 lists FIVE transitions. Only FOUR exist. `idle-with-claimable` is deliberately ABSENT from the catalog — see the comment at `catalog.ts:307`. An await on a fifth key is unsatisfiable by construction.\n\n#### Scope of this correction\n\nThe item text is wrong; the IMPLEMENTATION is correct and P-009 stays `done`. Nothing needs rebuilding. What needed recording is that the plan's own prose cannot be used as the key source — which is why this is a decision (addressable, re-readable at claim time via `planDecisions`) rather than an edit to a closed item's text.\n\n### D-011 — Preserve dual plan-item linkage semantics; D-007 B1 is superseded\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured: 2026-09-04 against current source at HEAD 51c68dcaa2 and the live papercusp-workspace work_items table via dev:pg_query.\n\nD-007's conclusion that the plan-item/work-item CLAIM duality is load-bearing remains valid. Its B1 follow-on — backfill every payload-only linkage and collapse resolvePlanItemStamp to the source-plan columns — is superseded and MUST NOT be implemented.\n\nThe two linkage representations no longer mean the same thing in every supported path. plan-workitem-promotion-run.ts deliberately writes payload.plan_item.plan_slug as the immutable INSTANCE plan for a scheduled/event/manual run, while source_plan_slug groups the execution under the stable TEMPLATE. The live census contains 102 rows where both representations are present and their slugs deliberately differ; all 102 carry payload.plan_run. Replacing one with the other would conflate run execution with template provenance.\n\nThe premise that payload-only rows were a closed historical tail is also false today. The live workspace contains 4,367 payload-only rows, with creation continuing through 2026-08-27, plus one columns-only row. Current source explicitly treats promoted rows as column-linked and ad-hoc rows as payload-linked in findOpenPlanItemCollision, and the work-items/create/update paths preserve both where a normalized plan_item argument is available. resolvePlanItemStamp's payload-first, columns-fallback behavior is therefore compatibility logic for supported populations, not migration residue.\n\nDecision: keep both representations and the shared dual resolver. Do not add the proposed bulk UPDATE or retire the EITHER-mechanism caveats. Any future convergence must first introduce a single schema capable of representing both template provenance and instance execution identity, migrate all active writers, and prove zero semantic disagreement before removing either read path.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-012 — P-011 verdict: D-009's block is discharged, the wake-count win is real (~4x), but the LATENCY leg REGRESSES — cause is delivery-pump attempts-tier starvation, not push itself\nDate: 2026-09-05\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured: harness_shared.event_wake_deliveries and harness_shared.event_awaits via dev:pg_query over a 48h window ending 2026-09-05T10:40Z (every query run with positiveControlSql; all controls passed). Pump ordering read at packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/store.ts:1836-1840.\n\n#### D-009's precondition is CLEARED\nD-009 ruled P-011 must not be claimed until at least one leader actually parks on the fleet events, and named the probe: count fleet-transition awaits in event_awaits. Re-run now:\n- fleet:* awaits = 239 across 19 agents (D-009 measured 1 across 1)\n- control families, same window: release:* 20/5, green-checkpoint:* 5/3\nFleet-event adoption now EXCEEDS the gate families D-009 used to prove agents adopt event-waiting readily. The treatment arm exists; the benchmark is valid and was run.\n\nMethod note for anyone re-running it: match the `fleet:%` PREFIX, never an enumeration of transitions. D-010 catalogued four; there are now at least six live (fleet:admission-blocked:* and fleet:headcount:* both post-date it), so enumerating D-010's list silently drops ~31 awaits and understates adoption. This is D-010's own \"never retype the key from prose\" warning arriving from the counting side.\n\n#### P-011 asked for TWO measurements. The verdict is SPLIT.\n\n(A) WAKE VOLUME — PASSES. Push wakes burned vs a 180s poll over each adopter's own observed span: 1.6x, 2.3x, 3.0x, 3.4x, 3.9x, 4.7x, 8.9x, 12.9x, 13.9x, 15.3x (n=10, median ~4x). Materially fewer — though only 1.6-3.4x for the heaviest multi-key subscribers, who take a delivery per transition.\n\n(B) REACTION LATENCY — REGRESSES. fire -> wake-delivered for fleet:claim-released: p50 360.0s, p95 3979.2s, max 7059.2s. P-011's own baseline is a 180s poll noticing a dropped claim in UP TO 3 minutes. The push path's MEDIAN is twice the poll's WORST case.\n\nP-011's text pre-declared exactly this shape a regression: \"reducing wakes while worsening latency would be a regression.\" Measuring only (A) would have reported a clean win. This is why the item demanded both.\n\n#### Cause: NOT that push is slow\nLatency tracks delivery ATTEMPTS, not the key family:\n  tier    fleet p50 (n)     inbox p50 (n)\n  1        84.4s (90)         8.1s (413)\n  2-4      96.5s (111)       51.4s (3244)\n  5-9     414.6s (90)       252.2s (134)\n  10+    1607.2s (131)      987.4s (73)\nPer tier the families are comparable; the family-level gap (fleet p50 542.6s vs inbox 51.1s) is a MIX effect — 31% of fleet deliveries reach 10+ attempts against 1.9% of inbox ones.\n\nclaimDueDeliveries claims a bounded batch ORDER BY (attempts = 0 AND last_error IS NULL) DESC, attempts ASC, ... LIMIT 10 — untouched rows first, retried rows deprioritized, deliberately so a permanently uninjectable subscriber cannot monopolize the batch (EI-21303383797798186). But coord:inbox-wake supplies 4508 fresh tier-0 rows per 48h against fleet's 606, so a fleet row that misses its early attempts falls behind an effectively endless tier-0 stream.\n\nThe perverse consequence: an agent that does what push-not-poll asks — PARK and await — is un-injectable on early attempts, climbs the attempts ladder, and is then deprioritized by design. The behaviour P-009 exists to encourage is the one the pump punishes. Gate families escape it because their subscribers are usually mid-turn and injectable on the first attempt.\n\nPopulation confound excluded within-subject: all 13 agents receiving BOTH families show fleet_p50 >= inbox_p50 (ratios 1.0-23.9), same agent, same session, same loop. min_sleep_sec (60.0 both) and urgent (0 both) are excluded as differentiators.\n\n#### RULING\n1. D-009's block on P-011 is DISCHARGED. Do not re-block it on adoption.\n2. The P-009/P-010 win is NOT verified as a whole. Cite the wake-count reduction freely; do NOT cite these events as a latency improvement until the starvation is fixed. A leader parking on fleet:claim-released today learns of a released claim ~6min at the median, over an hour at p95.\n3. The starvation is filed as WI-2145698 (major). P-011 stays open pending that fix, then a re-measure.\n4. Expect the win to be RECOVERABLE, not absent: at low attempts the push path delivers in 8-97s, well inside the 180s poll. The mechanism is sound; its scheduling is what fails.\nRelated: P-011, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-013 — Discharge WI-2145698 fix/deployment parking; retain P-011 leg-B remeasurement\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nMeasured: WI-2145698 is DONE with COMMITTED authority and exact settlement source blob cc8edb4c4596df3b0233757a78fb843c255c8234 at e6de7d6b8e1a573d965f35f343b4aca95600e832. Its source and canonical65-test proof reserve one batch slot for an attempts>0 retry aged60 seconds. Current release artifact is d740fc3802877d1c8c3b1068768681ee32ef0025; reading its actual store.ts shows that specific retryStarvationAgeSec60/retryReserveSlots1/aged_retry/order reservation unchanged. Current runtime read reports release-operator d740fc3802 and bg-host d40a956249; the latter committed source also contains the same bounded reserve.\nThe current path-wide blob comparison reports containsChange:false because it compares newer store.ts edits. That is not a measurement of containment of this historical fix; the specific source control above distinguishes the two. No gate status, checkpoint run, deploy or runtime restart was operated.\nRuling under owner-directed blocked-queue cleanup WI10005820: discharge only the historical fixed-and-deployed parking condition, restore P011 to TODO and WI6711 to OPEN, and clear the obsolete claim hold. Preserve D012: legA wake-volume measurement remains settled and must not be repeated; legB reaction latency must be measured anew against the180s baseline. Reopening is not a claim of latency improvement, whole-plan acceptance or new shipment. Any different current measurement or contract prerequisite remains mandatory.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-014 — P-011 leg-B remeasurement remains nonpassing; delivery channel is not proof of leader reaction\nDate: 2026-10-05\nMeasured: 2026-10-05T21:59:26.169705Z, canonical source engine.ts/store.ts/wake-executor.ts read; real fleet claim-release ledger rolling48h via read-only dev:pg_query, positiveControlSql passed and untruncated. Evidence: WI-6711#comment:1158244 and recipe measure-p011-fleet-claim-release-latency-by-delivery-channel-and-paired-recipient.\nD-013's old fixed-and-deployed prerequisite remains discharged; D-012 legA stays settled and was NOT rerun. Remaining legB, using D012's delivered_at-created_at instrument, still does NOT beat180s:58 rows (56 delivered/1 dead/1 parked), delivered median331.734s/p95815.724s. Native delivery9 across4 recipients has median2.905s/p9528.043s/max36.401s; non-native/coalesced47 across6 recipients median346.565s/p95826.373s. Paired recipients with>=3 fleet and inbox deliveries show median ratios0.913,3.416,5.901,0.039, so population mix alone does not establish a pass.\nWriter semantics: markDeliveryDelivered records engine inbox fallback and native outcomes; coalesced siblings also get delivered timestamps. resume-headless returns after process spawn/PID recording rather than measured first meaningful leader action. Thus neither all delivered rows nor selecting only fast native rows establishes the unchanged reaction-win contract. No cause of current runtime latency is asserted from this mixed instrument.\nDisposition: retain P011 as nonpassing until real leader reaction evidence and the unchanged180s criterion are met; this decision DOES NOT change acceptance scope, grant a grading eligibility exception, reopen WI2145698, or authorize live gate/deploy/restart work. Existing focused engine guard check passed2 selected tests (94 unselected), HEAD090c9b90d8; only inbox/pending-text semantics were checked, not an end-to-end reaction. Reaction-proof follow-up ownership must be resolved before any claimed terminal success. Feature-specific measurement permitted by fleet-leader reply coord-send-27b1a6f1421f676f8376985d58bfc9fa3f9d014e8f23e1369bdba8c7b15c1b03; PERSONAL cleanup METHOD exclusion is a separate lane.\nRelated: P-011\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01","title":"Silent wrong answers: results that look right and are not","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Silent wrong answers: results that look right and are not\nslug: silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-01\nupdated: 2026-09-03\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation is COMPLETE. Acceptance is REJECTED and the reject STILL STANDS — but the ground under it is now clean and singular, which it was not an hour ago.\n\nSETTLED AT 21:59Z (D-129). The question D-128 raised and deliberately refused to answer in-house — the enumerated C1 fail clauses and the criterion's own title disagreeing — has been adjudicated independently by su-0300ecfc (eligible: no item implemented, no part of the rubric authored, outside the author's lineage, had not graded rev 9). Verdict: C1 = PARTIAL, CONFIRMING the author's own rating rather than overruling it. The reasoning generalizes: the enumerated clauses are a FAIL FLOOR, never a PASS CEILING — they say what forces a fail, never what earns a pass; the title governs pass, and the space between is exactly partial. A criterion is not passed by failing to fail. The deployment-position fallback is an alternative INSTRUMENT for determining liveness, not an alternative VERDICT that liveness holds.\n\nSo the reject now rests on ONE ground and only one: the population-denominator remedy is committed on staging and ABSENT from the deployed sha 6e898b6cf8, re-measured 21:56Z and unchanged since at least 21:00Z. The documentation-tier ground closed earlier with demonstrated falsifiability; the two-demonstration bar is met.\n\nNO RUBRIC EDIT (D-129b). The adjudicator found a real gap — clause 3's conjunction means an honestly-recorded not-deployed remedy can never reach fail — and advised against closing it now. Adopted: any rubric edit would invalidate the standing attestation and both banked independent cards, and the author would be the beneficiary of the change. Filed as tracked work instead, to be taken only when a revision is already being paid for.\n\n**Next:** Nothing on the ship path is closable from inside this plan, and that is the correct state rather than a stall. The remedy comes into force ONLY through a legitimate, independently-owned deploy — do NOT request, schedule or accelerate gate work to flip it (D-127, D-128d, D-129c); the gate is not this fleet's to touch. When it greens on its own merits: re-measure directly against the then-deployed sha (a live call must actually RETURN population/populationNote — never infer it from the fact that a deploy happened, and keep a positive control in the same call), then RE-GRADE C1 (it does not auto-promote), then obtain a fresh superseding author acceptance card, then ship WITHOUT force (D-123). Ineligible graders unchanged.\n\n## The finding\n\nSeven defects surfaced in one session. They are not seven problems; they are ONE, in seven places:\n\n> A tool returns a WELL-FORMED, PLAUSIBLE result that carries NO SIGNAL it is wrong.\n\nNot a crash, not an error, not an empty. A confident answer to a question the tool did not actually answer. Every instance below was structurally valid output a reasonable caller would build on.\n\n### Why this class is agent-specific, and why it compounds\n\nA human running these interactively notices 'wait, every row is null'. An agent receives ONE result, it looks correct, and it becomes a PREMISE. In a fleet that premise propagates into checkpoints, into reports to the owner, and into peers' work before anything tests it. Two instances this session reached the owner as false statements before being caught.\n\n### Why documentation is the WEAKEST fix available (proven twice, this session)\n\n1. CLAUDE.md WARNS about exactly this failure mode -- 'returns zero rows, which reads exactly like no criticals even when there are plenty' -- then, in the same sentence, prescribes the accessor that produces a fresh instance of it. I followed the doc and got 0 of 13,332.\n2. I wrote myself the correct rule ('verify the effect, not the receipt'), then violated it ONE TICK LATER, because the rule was subtly insufficient (post-state vs delta).\n\nSo this plan is ordered by MECHANICAL STRENGTH, not by effort. Doc and prompt changes come last on purpose and are explicitly not relied upon.\n\n## The seven instances\n\n| # | Instance | Filed |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | A backlog COUNT with no composition: 1,174 'claimable' was 98.7% nit-severity auto-filed observations | WI-6673 |\n| 2 | payload->'_ei'->>'severity' returns NULL for 13,332/13,332 rows on the engineer_issues VIEW; a critical audit returns zero rows, reading as 'no criticals' when there are 27 | WI-6674 |\n| 3 | work_items:claimable returns severity:null on EVERY row -- pool composition is unknowable caller-side by ANY diligence | WI-6673 |\n| 4 | My own audit predicate state <> 'open' swept in needs-human/blocked, manufacturing a false 'bare close' accusation against a peer | this plan |\n| 5 | work_items:release on an already-unassigned item returns ok:true and does nothing -- produced a FALSE COMPLETION CLAIM to the owner | WI-6678 |\n| 6 | 12,564 nit/minor auto-filed observations sit in the CLAIMABLE pool -- the root cause that made #1 possible | WI-6675 |\n| 7 | The p2p fence is title-WORD matching, so p2p-adjacent items whose titles dodge the words leak into the lane | this plan |\n\n## The two rules this session earned\n\n**READS -- never accept a null/zero/empty as a finding.** Cross-check against a DIFFERENT accessor for the same fact and demand the two agree. 100% absence is a wrong-path signature, not data; real data is essentially never entirely absent.\n\n**WRITES -- verify the DELTA, not the post-state.** A post-state read only verifies a write whose SUCCESS state differs from its NO-OP state. Before believing any mutation, ask: what would this tool have returned if it had done nothing? If the answer is 'the same thing', the verification is worthless. (Priority write: unprioritized -> featureOrder 14 is a real delta, sound. Release of an unassigned item: unassigned -> unassigned, unsound.)\n\nBoth belong in code as guarantees, not in prose as advice. That is what the tiers below do.\n\n## Tiers\n\n- **Tier 1 (P-001..P-003) -- make the wrong answer IMPOSSIBLE.** Structural. Highest value.\n- **Tier 2 (P-004..P-006) -- make the wrong answer LOUD.** Detection where impossibility is impractical.\n- **Tier 3 (P-007..P-008) -- fix the POOL.** Root cause of instance #1.\n- **Tier 4 (P-009..P-011) -- doc and prompt.** Weakest lever; last; not relied upon.\n\n## Open decisions -- need Avi; P-008 and P-012 are blocked on them\n\n1. **The 159 mis-kinded severe changes** (154 major + 5 critical) are real defects filed as kind=change, distinct from the 12,564 nit/minor that should never be claimable. Bulk re-kind to bug, or priority-promote into a kind-agnostic lane?\n2. **The p2p fence** is title-word based and leaks (WI-5168 cross-machine repoKey, WI-6359 joiner drops hive announce). Re-fence semantically or by tag, or accept the leak? It is your lane definition -- I have not touched it.\n\n## Phase 1 — Make the wrong answer impossible (structural)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Compute admittedBreakdown SERVER-SIDE in work_items:claimable + scheduler:get_next — kind x severity of the ADMITTED set, plus a filing-rate skew flag. Composition then ships WITH the count and cannot be quoted without it. MUST be server-side: the caller is handed severity:null, so no caller-side workaround exists. [WI-6673] importance: high — note: admittedBreakdown live in work_items:claimable + scheduler:get_next (aggregateAdmittedComposition). Tests: admitted-composition.test.ts + claimability-snapshot.test.ts + claimable.test.ts = 41/41 pass 20:14Z.\n- **P-002** `done` Stop nulling severity in the work_items:claimable projection. It currently returns severity:null for rows that are severity='critical' in engineer_issues — the tool a leader is told to use for 'what is claimable' cannot report that critical work is critical. [WI-6673] importance: high — note: get-next.ts:1118 now COALESCE(payload->'_ei'->>'severity', payload->>'severity'). NEW DB-backed guard: 4 assertions in get-next-exclusion-breakdown.integration.test.ts, 8/8 pass 20:17Z.\n- **P-003** `done` Resolve the severity DUAL-ACCESSOR. On the engineer_issues VIEW severity is a real column; payload->'_ei'->>'severity' (correct for the work_items TABLE) yields NULL for all 13,332 rows, so a critical audit returns zero and reads as 'no criticals'. Pick one: expose _ei.severity in the view's payload so both paths agree, or drop the payload path. Removing the footgun beats documenting it. [WI-6674] importance: urgent — note: ← WI-6688 completed (done)\n- **P-014** `done` **A registry-read FAULT must not render as \"not registered\" (EI-19286551248996972).** Observed live 2026-08-01: `plans:list` returned ok:true with `plans:[]` and `plans:get` returned not_found for `papercusp`, while psql held 960 plans. Four defensible layers compose the wrong answer: (1) `harness-core.ts:371-374` + `:377-383` wrap both registry reads in bare `catch {}` that deliberately fold \"unreadable\" into \"absent\", returning a `null` byte-identical to a genuine miss; (2) `plans/source.ts:368` propagates it; (3) `plans/source.ts:412-419` restates that null as an ASSERTION ABOUT THE WORLD — \"harness '<x>' is not registered in the harness registry\" — whose own advice is to go register it (a WRITE, i.e. actionable in the wrong direction); (4) `plans/list.ts:549` regex-matches that message and swallows it into `unknownHarnesses`, returning ok:true + []. `host-benign-errors.ts:141-159` also marks it benign, so it never raises the error rate — invisible in telemetry too. FIX (structural, not detection): give `resolveWorkspaceForHarnessSlugIn` a discriminated verdict (found | absent | unreadable-with-cause) instead of one `null`; let `resolvePlanScope` assert \"not registered\" ONLY after a read that genuinely SUCCEEDED and returned no row; make list.ts's swallow key off that typed verdict rather than a regex over an error string; drop the fault variant from the benign classifier. Note the general rule this earns: an error-STRING match can never separate a real absence from a fault that renders the same words — the distinction must be typed at the source. Testable without a live DB via the existing injectable seams (`resolvePlanScope`'s `registryFallback`, `fill_workspace_id_from_projects`'s `lookup`): inject a throwing `loadHarnessRegistry` and assert plans:list does NOT answer ok:true/[] for a harness whose rows are present. importance: high — note: ← WI-2141821 completed (done)\n- **P-015** `done` Apply the SHIPPED field-reliability caveat to `ended_at`, then audit the rest of the observer-written class (EI-19375527037368001). `packages/operator-core/lib/field-reliability.ts` shipped 2026-08-02 (WI-7078) and is wired to exactly ONE call site. `adv_sessions.ended_at` is stamped by the idle-session-reaper when it NOTICES a dead row — 9 sessions stamped inside 13ms, one dead since 20 July — and is typed, named and rendered exactly like an observation. Add the caveat wherever it surfaces (sessions:*, fleet:*, adv_sessions reads): \"sweep-time write; true end UNKNOWN; insteadRead: coord_presence.last_active_at\". Then enumerate the class — ANY column written by a process other than the one it describes. `adv_sessions.exit_code` is the live suspect: NULL for all 9 ghosts, silently unable to answer \"how did this end\". Cost of the missing line: ~3h, two retracted causal claims to the owner. importance: high — note: su-70702: DONE. Migration 735 ended_by (self|reaper|reconciler|cleanup); markAdvSessionEnded REQUIRES endedBy; all 7 write sites attributed; SELECTs threaded in adv-sessions.ts AND agent-launch-core.ts; advSessionEndedAtCaveat + describeSessionEndTime; wired to fleet:status (structured) + launch-agent (prose). AUDIT: fixed 2 fabricated exit_code=1 writes (cleanup.ts, bootstrap-su:2041). 16 new tests; 25 launch-agent + 19 combined green; lint:tsc EXIT=0.\n- **P-016** `done` PROMOTE THE CONVENTION — this plan already has FOUR implementations of one rule, each wired to one thing. (1) `field-reliability.ts` — one call site. (2) `code:run`'s `fieldMisses` — reading an absent field is reported, not silently `undefined`; caught two live misreads while this wave was authored, one rendering as `completion: \"\"` i.e. \"shipped with no evidence\". (3) `work_items:complete` requiring `assumptions` or literal `\"none\"`. (4) undeclared-arg rejection (EI-10883) — \"returns ok:true while quietly doing something else... indistinguishable from success\". State the rule once — A SURFACE MUST NOT RENDER AN ABSENT, UNRELIABLE OR UNANSWERED RESULT AS A REAL ONE — and give it a guard, so instance #5 is caught at review rather than filed after the fact. Same hour, three OTHER agents filed the same shape independently (EI-19375525140589446, EI-19375451000390205, WI-7140): point fixes are not keeping up with discovery. importance: high — note: ← WI-7178 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `done` fleet:launch-on-plan returns ok:true after SILENTLY discarding the launch brief (WI-7131). `launchContext` takes a PATH; prose fails ENAMETOOLONG; ten agents then launched with the baseline only and the failure was reported as success. Everything the members needed — priority order, evidence bar, why the prior cohort died — reached nobody. Caught only because the error text happened to survive the truncation door. Fix: resolve/validate launchContext BEFORE spawning and FAIL the launch, or accept prose by writing it to a temp path. Spawning ten agents without their instructions is not a partial success. Blocking rather than dropping because the underlying defect is real and the surviving remedy is now specified and de-risked in WI-2141982; dropping would discard a genuine incident, a…\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Make the wrong answer loud (detection)\n\n- **P-004** `done` Mutations must report their DELTA. work_items:release returns ok:true on a semantic no-op with no released:false / previousAssignee. Add the delta, then AUDIT every other mutation verb for the same shape — any write whose no-op result is byte-identical to its success result is unverifiable by ANY caller discipline. The items are unassigned BY DEFINITION, so 'orphan' + the standing 'reclaim orphans' loop instruction both point at release — which cannot clear it. Only a CLAIM resolves it. Suggest abandoned_unclaimed / stalled_unowned. [WI-6678] — note: fleet:leader-brief orphaned_in_flight -> abandoned_unclaimed/abandonedUnclaimed + abandonedUnclaimedAction carrying the resolving action inline. leader-brief.test.ts 93 tests pass 20:19Z.\n- **P-007** `done` Launch-time guard: the DUAL of confirmClaimCollapse. fleet:launch-on-plan already refuses a lane matching 0 rows (starvation). Add the opposite — warn/refuse when the matched pool is large AND compositionally degenerate (>80% nit+minor): the 'launched a fleet at an observation firehose' shape. That is precisely what happened this session. importance: high — note: fleet:launch-on-plan now WARNS (never refuses) when a claimKinds lane is large AND >=80% nit/minor — the dual of confirmClaimCollapse. launch-on-plan.test.ts 92 tests pass 20:19Z; constants pinned in admitted-composition.test.ts (both directions: fires on degenerate, does NOT fire on healthy).\n- **P-013** `done` NEW INSTANCE (#8, found 19:35Z auditing the WI-6674 fix): documentation asserting a guarantee whose implementation is NOT LIVE. CLAUDE.md was updated to say dev:pg_query 'now emits an always-NULL-accessor advisory'; the advisory is absent from origin/staging, main AND deployed (verified by marker), and the live operator silently returned 0 criticals against a true 25. This is the class in its most dangerous form: CLAUDE.md is spliced into EVERY su launch context, and an agent who believes a safety net exists is LESS likely to double-check — so the doc actively REDUCES vigilance against the very bug it has not yet shipped. FIX: gate present-tense capability claims in agent-facing docs on deployed:true, not on the edit existing locally. A dead member drops out of the roster, so `summary.dead: 0` was literally true and completely misleading; the only alert raised was about the leader sitting idle. A monitor loop calls this tool every wake BY DESIGN, so the one question a monitor most needs — did I lose anyone — is the one its own tool cannot ask. Worse: because loss is discovered late and all at once, BATCHED DISCOVERY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A BATCHED EVENT. That is what put \"mass death\" in the leader's head before a single timestamp was read, and it aimed two successive hypotheses at a simultaneous killer that never existed. Fix: either accept `projection` generically at the door, or narrow the advertisement to the tools that actually declare it. importance: low — note: ← WI-2141829 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — P-008/P-009 rest on a query I got wrong — the observation lane ALREADY excludes those 11,674 items; do not run the bulk reclassify\nDate: 2026-08-01\n> ⚠ STILL AUTHORITATIVE ON ITS CENTRAL POINT, BUT PARTLY OVERTAKEN — read the pointers before acting on anything below.\n> - **The numbers below are a 2026-08-01 SNAPSHOT, not a standing fact.** They were correct when measured; D-105 re-measured the same oracle on 2026-09-02 and got claimableCount 2,410 with a different composition. The filing path is correct and the floor works.\n\nHOW I GOT IT WRONG: I grouped engineer_issues by kind+severity WHERE state='open' and called the result \"the claimable pool\". It is the OPEN pool. CLAUDE.md warns about exactly this (\"status=open is NOT claimability... overcounts ~13x\") and I had read it the same day.\n\nDECISIONS:\n1. P-009 is VOID as written. Any residual value is in the second half (promote the genuinely severe ones), which needs a re-count against the ADMITTED set, not the open set.\n2. P-008's exclusion half is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. Anyone who reads those items needs to reach this correction from them.\n\nNOTE ON THE IRONY, because it is the strongest argument for P-001: admittedBreakdown — the feature this plan's P-001 adds — computes the composition of the ADMITTED set. That is precisely the population I failed to query. The fix built under this plan would have prevented the mistake I made while diagnosing the need for it.\n\n### D-002 — A delta must be reported from the mutation's OWN read, never a call-site pre-read — the first cut of P-004 was itself racy\nDate: 2026-08-01\nP-004 says mutations must report their DELTA. The first implementation added a `getWorkItem` pre-read at the work_items:release call site to capture the prior assignee. That was wrong twice over, and an existing test caught it:\n\n1. REDUNDANT. `releaseWorkItem` (work-items.ts:4597) already reads the row before its UPDATE and already computes `wasClaimed = Boolean(wi.assignee)` — exactly the delta being sought. The call-site read was a second round-trip for information the library had in hand.\n2. RACY — and this is the part that matters. Between the call site's read and the library's read, the assignee can change. The reported `previousAssignee` would then describe a state the release never acted on: a well-formed, plausible, WRONG answer. A fix for silent wrong answers must not itself be able to emit one.\n\nHOW IT SURFACED: `release.test.ts` asserts `expect(getM).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` on the plain release path. The pre-read tripped it. The test was pinning a real property (this path does not re-read the row) and the correct response was to fix the code, not relax the assertion.\n\nDECISION (applies to the rest of the P-004 audit, not just release): when adding delta reporting to any mutation verb, expose the pre-state from INSIDE the mutation — the read it already performs — rather than re-reading at the call site. The seam used here is an additive optional callback:\n\n    onPriorState?: (prior: { assignee: string | null; wasClaimed: boolean }) => void\n\nIt fires once, before any UPDATE, whenever the row exists (so `wasClaimed:false` is observable on a no-op), never fires when the row is not found, and is fail-soft so a caller's bookkeeping can never break the mutation. Additive: all 23 existing `releaseWorkItem` call sites are untouched, and the delta is now correct for every one of them (including the stale-claim reaper and the SessionEnd force-release path), not just the tool.\n\nSECOND-ORDER NOTE, worth carrying to the audit: adding this option broke 7 tests that asserted the opts object by EXACT match. They were updated to include `onPriorState: expect.any(Function)` rather than relaxed to `objectContaining` — relaxing would have silently given up their ability to catch a stray option such as `announceClaimable: false`, which changes behavior. This is the repo's documented \"adding a field to a shared interface breaks fixtures elsewhere\" trap; the fix is to update the fixtures, not to weaken them.\n\n### D-003 — REJECTED: the \"fleet mass-death detector\" spec — the event it detects does not occur, and its signal is coroner-written\nDate: 2026-08-02\nWI-7129 was filed as \"when >=3 sessions in one fleet end within a few seconds, emit an incident\". **Do not build that.** It is quoted verbatim in the owner's 2026-08-02 brief and in several session transcripts, so it will be proposed again unless this decision is on record.\n\nTwo independent refutations, both from WI-7126 (closed as a refuted premise):\n\n1. **The event never happened.** True last-activity of the 8 members (coord_presence.last_active_at) was staggered over 40 minutes: 18:16:40, 18:23:25, 18:25:04, 18:25:46, 18:26:03, 18:26:27, 18:32:11, 18:56:15. The minute-histogram of last_active_at across 17:00-19:10Z is flat at 1-2 sessions/min. No cliff exists to detect.\n2. **The proposed signal is the coroner's pen.** `ended_at` is written by the idle-session-reaper when it NOTICES a dead row, so it clusters by construction — 9 rows stamped inside 13ms, one of them dead since 20 July. A detector keyed on it reports a mass death at every sweep and never once a real one.\n\nThe apparent 13ms batch that motivated the item was that write. Re-keyed onto the failure that DID occur — agents degenerating into telemetry-only wake loops (205 of 254 final calls telemetry, 1-11 work calls) — now tracked as the degenerate-wake detector.\n\nSame shape as this plan's D-001 and as agent-epistemics D-001: a detector drafted against a signal with no real producer. **Before building a detector, verify its trigger fired at least once historically on real data.**\n\n### D-004 — A detector spec must MEASURE separation between the firing and non-firing populations before any code is written\nDate: 2026-08-02\nFourth occurrence of the same defect in this codebase, and the third recorded as a decision. A detector is drafted against a signal that sounds diagnostic, and nobody measures whether it actually separates the population it is meant to catch from the one it is not.\n\n- `facts:conflicts` (WI-6545 / D-103): retired — \"passed identically whether the fleet wrote assumptions or not\".\n- `agent-epistemics-2026-08-02` D-001: \">=3 agents contradicting on one key inside N minutes\" measured to fire ZERO times in 14 days.\n- This plan's D-001: P-008/P-009 rested on a claimable count that was wrong by ~13x.\n- **This decision (2026-08-02 21:30Z):** the degenerate-wake detector's proposed signal — telemetry:work call ratio > ~0.75 — has ZERO discriminating power.\n\nThe measurement that killed it, which took one query:\n\n| population | telemetry ratio |\n|---|---|\n| ALL 46 agents on the box (>=100 calls / 6h) | **67-79%** |\n| the 8 agents that stopped, final 30 min | 72-81% |\n| the 8 agents that stopped, **whole 24h lifetime** | **76-77%** |\n| the box's TOP work-item closer (16 closed) | 72% |\n\nThe ratio never spiked before death — it was 76-77% for the dead cohort's entire life, indistinguishable from every healthy agent. And the \"degenerate\" agents closed **7-11 work-items each** in their final 6 hours (su-fc177b91: 8 closed at 78%; su-05239587: 11 at 76%). They were productive to the end. The spec would have fired on ~30 of 46 agents including the best performer.\n\nThe evidence that motivated it — \"205 of 254 calls were telemetry, 3 work calls\" — is a TRUE measurement of an UNREMARKABLE fact. That is the trap: a number damning in the selected set and ordinary against the population.\n\n**The rule.** Before writing detector code, state the trigger and measure it against real history, reporting BOTH populations:\n1. how often it fires on the target population (if zero historically, there is no producer — stop);\n2. how often it fires on the healthy population (if comparable, there is no separation — stop).\n\nA detector that cannot show separation is not a detector; it is an alarm wired to a constant. Neither leg alone is sufficient: D-001 of agent-epistemics failed leg 1, this one passes leg 1 and fails leg 2.\n\n### D-104 — P-016's guard: two obvious designs MEASURED and rejected — use a (surface, field) registry, not a name lint or field-keyed auto-attach\nDate: 2026-08-02\n`field-reliability.ts` already STATES the rule well (its module doc names six ad-hoc spellings — containment_warning, zeroHitCaveat, okFalseWarning, fieldMissHelp, priorWorkWarning, stateWarning — and the complaint that \"nothing can enumerate them, test them, or render them consistently\"). So P-016 is not writing the rule. It is the GUARD. Two designs suggest themselves immediately; both were measured and both fail.\n\n**REJECTED 1 — lint on the field-NAME pattern** (`*Warning` / `*Caveat` / `*Hint` / `*Help` / `*Advisory` / `*Note`), to catch a seventh ad-hoc spelling being invented.\n\nMeasured over `packages/operator-core/lib`: **96 distinct matching names**, and the top of the distribution is ordinary domain content, not epistemic caveats — `carryNote` (56 uses), `routeHint` (47), `awaitingNote` (15), `aliasNote` (14), `journalNote` (13). The genuinely epistemic ones (`priorWorkWarning` 6, `stateWarning` 3, `_fieldReliabilityWarning` 5) are a small minority buried in the noise. A lint here has no separation between the population it should catch and the one it must not — the same defect that blocked P-020, and the fourth time this plan has met it.\n\n**REJECTED 2 — a registry keyed by FIELD NAME, auto-attaching a caveat wherever that field appears.** Measured while doing P-015: `endedAt` names two unrelated concepts — an adv_session end (unreliable, sweeper-written) and a `capability:bash` job end (a real observation, `bash-jobs.ts:583` sets it from `Date.now()` at actual completion). Field-keyed attachment would caveat the bash job wrongly, i.e. manufacture a false warning — this plan's own bug with the sign flipped. `exitCode`, `startedAt` and `status` are all similarly overloaded.\n\n**THE VIABLE DESIGN: a registry keyed by (SURFACE, FIELD).** One entry per emitting site, carrying the `cannotAnswer` + `insteadRead` that `caveat()` already takes, with a coverage test asserting every registered site attaches its caveat. Model it on the repo's established shrink-only pattern (`KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS` + `DARK_FLAGS_HIGH_WATERMARK`): the allowlist of un-migrated ad-hoc spellings may only SHRINK, so a seventh spelling must either use the shared vocabulary or be deliberately added with a justification. That catches instance #7 at review — P-016's actual goal — without a lint that cannot tell a caveat from a carry note.\n\nGeneralisation worth keeping: **a guard keyed on a NAME is a guess about intent; a guard keyed on a REGISTERED SITE is a fact.** Every rejected design in this plan failed by keying on a proxy (a name, a count, a ratio, a timestamp) instead of on the thing itself.\n\n### D-105 — The claimable pool has a SEVERITY INVERSION: 0 of 46 critical items are claimable, 6 of 666 major are, while 349 nit are — D-001 disproved P-008/P-009's numbers but not their concern\nDate: 2026-09-02\n> ⚠ SUPERSEDED IN PART — do not quote this decision's headline number or its re-scoping without reading the corrections.\n> - **D-107** determines the MECHANISM this decision left open, and rules \"0 of 46 critical\" too crude: the real finding is that unservable-critical-watchdog watches 2 floors while 17 stranded criticals sit in a third. The \"NEXT PROBE for whoever takes this\" paragraph below is therefore ALREADY ANSWERED — do not re-run it as an open question.\n> - **D-110** corrects the P-008 re-scoping below: excluding nit from the claim floors moves the degeneracy metric by 0.0004 and cannot achieve its stated goal.\n> - **D-114** falsifies the root-cause premise this decision hands onward: at census the claimable pool is NOT full of non-work.\n> - **D-117** is the re-count, and finds the admitted pool 100% low-severity and self-flagged degenerate.\n>\n> WHAT STILL STANDS: the severity INVERSION itself — severe work is less reachable than trivial work — and the refusal to assert an unproven mechanism.\n\nD-001 correctly killed the 12,564 / 13,449 figures (they came from the OPEN pool; the observation lane already excludes ~79k). But D-001 invites a second inference that is FALSE and that I nearly acted on: \"the exclusion works, so the pool is fine.\" It is not fine. It is inverted.\n\nMeasured: work_items:claimable { harness:'papercusp', breakdownOnly:true } 2026-09-02T17:09Z (the SAME oracle scheduler:get_next runs) -> claimableCount 2410, admittedBreakdown.bySeverity { major:6, minor:2055, nit:349 }, critical ABSENT (0), lowSeverityShare 0.9975, degenerate:true.\n\nMeasured: dev:pg_query over harness_shared.engineer_issues (severity is a REAL column on this view; payload->'_ei' is NULL here — P-003's dual accessor), workspace_id='papercusp-workspace', scope='harness:papercusp', non-terminal, lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation' -> critical 46, major 666, minor 3367, nit 429.\n\nSo, by severity, the share of existing non-observation non-terminal work that is actually claimable:\n  critical  0 / 46   = 0%\n  major     6 / 666  = 0.9%\n  minor  2055 / 3367 = 61%\n  nit     349 / 429  = 81%\n\nThe more severe an item is, the LESS likely it is to be reachable. That is this plan's own thesis applied to the queue itself: `claimableCount: 2410` reads as a healthy backlog and is in fact 99.75% nit/minor with every critical item unreachable. The tool already warns (COMPOSITION WARNING, degenerate:true) — the warning is right and the count beside it is still what gets quoted.\n\nRE-SCOPING that follows:\n- P-008: its FIRST clause (route observation-grade captures to the observation lane at filing) is implemented and working — D-001 is right about that. Its SECOND clause (\"exclude nit-severity auto-filed items from the default claim floors\") is NOT implemented: 349 nit and 2055 minor items are claimable right now. P-008 is therefore not \"already done\", it is half done, and the unimplemented half is the half that matters.\n- P-009: DO NOT run the bulk reclassify (D-001 stands — those rows are already excluded). But its other half, \"separately promote the genuinely severe ones\", was sized at 159 (154 major + 5 critical) and is now 712 non-observation non-terminal (666 major + 46 critical). The concern grew ~4.5x while the item sat blocked on a disproved premise.\n\nMECHANISM: UNDETERMINED — do not inherit a cause from this decision. I tested two hypotheses and BOTH are refuted, which is why none is asserted here:\n  (1) \"severe items sit in a non-claimable state\" — REFUTED. states:['open'] -> 2406 claimable (~= the 2410 default); states:['todo'] -> 19. `open` IS the default claimable state; `todo` is the rare one. The state is not the discriminator.\n  (2) \"severe items are parked in the agentReview floor (1095)\" — REFUTED as the explanation for the backlog: sampleExcluded:6 returns EI-22169397154782837, EI-22164219453624409, EI-22162745262638300, EI-22166933881021603, EI-22166703532735250, EI-22166138797743784 — all filed TODAY. agentReview is the fresh-capture review queue, not where the severe backlog sits.\nLegitimately-excluded severe items are accounted for (critical: 15 blocked + 8 needs-human; major: 82 blocked + 101 needs-human) — those are correct, not the bug. The open question is the remaining ~23 open critical and ~475 open major that are non-terminal, non-observation, and still not claimable.\n\nNEXT PROBE for whoever takes this: take a known open+major id, call work_items:observe on it (claimability of a specific id you already hold), and read which floor rejects it. That names the mechanism per-row instead of by aggregate subtraction, which is what defeated both hypotheses above. A likely candidate worth checking first: the oracle's lane exclusion may not be `lane='observation'` — my SQL used that predicate and the oracle reports 79,123 excluded against 76,791 rows carrying `lane='observation'`, so the two populations are close but NOT equal, and the residual is unexplained.\nRelated: P-008, P-009\n\n### D-106 — Do NOT build P-018's statement-counting gate — measured, the count cannot discriminate the incident from a healthy mocked suite\nDate: 2026-09-02\nP-018 specifies: \"the mock counts statements and a suite asserting SQL behaviour FAILS at zero executed.\" Measured 2026-09-02, that gate has no threshold at which it discriminates. Do not build it. Measured: packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/unservable-critical-watchdog.ts:186 —\n    AND (lane = 'observation' OR state = 'needs-human')\nand its type at :79 — `export type UnservableFloor = 'observation-lane' | 'needs-human'`.\nThat watchdog exists BECAUSE a critical item hid for 19 days in a structurally unservable lane (its own header documents cup:spawn, EI-19919820196426791). What changed is that the critical half of that skew is mostly correct behaviour plus a 17-item detector gap, not a 46-item hole.\nRelated: P-008, P-009\n\n### D-108 — P-005 INVERTS: migration 1096 made the \"always a bug\" accessor correct, so the ADVISORY became the silent wrong answer\nDate: 2026-09-02\nP-005 was specified as \"a payload->'_ei'->>'severity' predicate against engineer_issues is ALWAYS a bug and is mechanically detectable\", explicitly BLOCKED BY the Phase 1 dual-accessor decision. That is this plan's own subject reproduced inside the mechanism built to prevent it.\n\nWHY IT SURVIVED ITS OWN TESTS — the transferable part. pg-read-query.test.ts asserted the advisory against HARDCODED SQL STRINGS. (4) Do not re-add an engineer_issues `_ei` trap without first reading pg_get_viewdef.\n\nREPLACEMENT DELIVERABLE (P-005 as executed): retire the false entry and PIN the claim instead — pg-read-query-engineer-issues-ei-pin.integration.test.ts reads the live view definition and fails in BOTH directions (view subtracts + no trap registered → fail; view projects full payload + trap registered → fail), carries a permanent pre-1096 control view so the detector is provably falsifiable, and grounds the text claim in behaviour by writing a row and reading severity both ways.\nRelated: P-005, P-003\n\n### D-109 — A base-rate denominator strips the SELECTING filters, never the CORPUS-CHOOSING ones\nDate: 2026-09-02\nBinding on every future caller of `packages/operator-core/lib/population-census.ts` (P-021).\n\nA census answers \"is `counted` many or few?\" by dividing it by the corpus it came from. Which\npredicates belong in that corpus is the whole design, and getting it wrong REINTRODUCES this\nplan's bug inside the fix for it.\n\nTHE RULE. Split a read's filters in two:\n  - CORPUS-CHOOSING — they say WHICH population this call is about. They stay in the denominator.\n  - SELECTING — they pick a part of that population. They are stripped, and become `withheld`.\n\nWorked instance, `issues:list` (`NARROWING_KEYS`, agent-tools/issues/list.ts:75):\ncorpus-choosing = `scope`, `kinds`, `lane`; selecting = `state`, `severity`, `assignee`, `q`, `topic`.\n\nWHY `lane` IS CORPUS-CHOOSING, THE NON-OBVIOUS HALF. It looks like an ordinary filter and the\ntidy-looking move is to strip everything that is not `scope`. That is wrong: `lane='observation'`\nrows are turn-end reflections, a different KIND of thing from work rows, and they dominate the\nrelation. Divide a work-lane count by an all-lane denominator and ordinary work-lane readings\nrender as anomalies the denominator manufactured — the failure P-021 was filed about.\n\nMeasured: `dev:pg_query` over `harness_shared.engineer_issues`, workspace `papercusp-workspace`,\n`scope='harness:papercusp'`, 2026-09-02T17:40Z, grouping `lane='observation'` vs everything else:\n  - ALL states: observation 97,309 vs work 58,100 — 1.67:1\n  - `state='open'` ONLY: observation 79,192 vs work 4,127 — 19.2:1\n\nREAD THOSE TWO LINES TOGETHER; they are the decision's real content. The SAME relation, the same\nlane split, one extra predicate — and the distortion from a wrongly-widened denominator moves from\n1.7x to 19x. So \"how bad is stripping `lane`?\" has no single answer: it depends on the population\nyou were already looking at, which is precisely why the denominator must be derived from THIS\ncall's corpus-choosing filters rather than from a ratio someone measured once and quoted later.\n(This decision's own first draft quoted \"~8:1\" from D-001 without re-measuring; neither figure\nabove reproduces it. Corrected before it shipped, by the `tree_fact_measurement_missing` advisory\n— the guard working.)\n\nTHE TEST TO APPLY. For each filter ask: if I removed this, would the remaining rows still be the\nsame KIND of thing I am counting? If yes it is selecting (strip it). If it would silently pull in\na different population, it is corpus-choosing (keep it). \"It reduces the row count\" is not the\ntest; nearly every filter does that.\n\nCOROLLARY. A denominator taken from a second query is a SECOND MEASUREMENT at a different instant,\nso it can disagree with the first. Do not paper over the disagreement: report the larger number as\na floor (`status:'bounded'`, `issueBaseRateCensus`, list.ts:91). A `withheld` that has gone\nnegative is two numbers disagreeing, and no reader parses it that way.\n\n### D-110 — CORRECTION to my own D-105 re-scoping — P-008's surviving clause (exclude nit from the claim floors) moves the degeneracy metric by 0.0004 and cannot achieve its stated goal; the driver is minor, and the inversion's mechanism is not pool composition at all\nDate: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nD-105 (mine, ~40 min earlier) re-scoped P-008 to \"the actionable half = exclude nit-severity auto-filed items from the default claim floors\" and called it \"the half that matters\". I measured that half before implementing it. Shipping it would be an instance of THIS PLAN'S OWN THESIS: a change that improves a reported number by a rounding error while leaving the condition the number is supposed to measure untouched — and it would then be recorded as \"P-008 done, pool composition fixed\", which is a silent wrong answer about our own remediation. No change to which nits are claimable can move that number. P-008 and the inversion are separate problems that D-105 wrongly fused.\n\nRE-SCOPING THAT FOLLOWS (P-008 stays todo — there IS work here, just not the work the clause names):\n- RETIRE the clause \"exclude nit-severity auto-filed items from the default claim floors\".
