That needs its own measurement before anyone proposes a mechanism; I am deliberately not asserting one here.\n\nMETHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: both of my re-scopings of P-008 (D-105 and this one) were produced by measuring the proposed fix's effect BEFORE building it, and each overturned the previous plan text. The cheap step is computing what the change would do to the number it targets. Do that before writing code for the surviving items.\n\n### D-111 — P-023 inverts: the cgroup field it proposes to EXPOSE is itself wrong for most agent sessions — fix the writer before any read surface\nDate: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nP-023 says: \"expose the agent's cgroup path / transient scope on an existing presence or process surface (`processes:list` already carries provenance), so 'what confines this agent' is a read rather than a shell excursion.\" Measured today, doing that AS WRITTEN would have shipped a silent wrong answer to the exact question the item exists to answer. The exposure half is still right; it is now BLOCKED BEHIND a correctness fix that the item did not know it needed.\n\nWHAT IS WRONG\n`completeSyncEnrolment` (task-manager/enroll-sync.ts) wrote the ledger's `cgroup_path` as `pid ? readProcessCgroupPath(pid, fs) : null` — unconditionally — while recording `confined: true`. For a confined task that is the SPAWNER's cgroup, not the task's: `systemd-run --scope` forks the payload, so an early /proc read of the client pid returns the operator. `managed-spawn.ts` already fixed exactly this in WI-37509 and its comment even names the resulting symptom (\"how a sidecar came to be recorded as living inside papercup-dev-api.service\"). The fix never reached the sync-enrolment seam, and `agent-session` goes through that seam.\n\nMEASURED, with positive controls (harness_shared.task_ledger, workspace papercusp-workspace, scope_unit NOT NULL; \"wrong\" = confined row whose cgroup_path does not contain its own scope_unit):\n- agent-session 1326 of 2373 wrong (800 naming papercusp-dev-api.service)\n- bash-job 2773 of 2856; test-run 62 of 85\n- CLEAN, via managed-spawn's derived path: sidecar 0/601, desktop 0/142, build 0/124, deploy 0/3\nThe four zero classes are the calibration: the same predicate returns 0 wherever the derived path is used, so it separates the mechanism rather than measuring itself. This satisfies D-004 — the populations were measured apart BEFORE code was written.\n\nWHY IT IS THIS PLAN'S SHAPE, NOT A COSMETIC PATH BUG\nThe wrong value is not noise, it is the PRE-EI-9748 answer. EI-9748 Route A (2026-07-11) moved agent sessions out of the operator service cgroup into papercusp.slice/papercusp-agent.slice/papercusp-agent-session.slice precisely so an operator restart stops killing them. A reader asking \"would restarting :3070 kill this agent?\" — the decision P-023 names as the one this field governs — got YES from the ledger when kernel truth was NO. Verified on this session (task 0mtkbd96m84cw7kbuap): ledger said app.slice/papercusp-dev-api.service; /proc/self/cgroup and `systemctl --user show --property=ControlGroup` agreed independently on the agent-session slice, ActiveState=active.\n\nTHE FIX (landed): derive it in the ONE shared ledger write —\n`cgroupPath: syncEnrolmentScopePath(enrolment, spec.class, fs) ?? (pid ? readProcessCgroupPath(pid, fs) : null)`\nmirroring managed-spawn:402. `syncEnrolmentScopePath` already existed, was exported and tested, and four callers (bash-jobs, pty, testing-run-store, orchestrator-runner) already derived the correct value FOR THEIR OWN USE while the shared ledger write ignored it. Deriving it at the write is what stops the next caller forgetting; unconfined tasks keep the /proc read, where it is correct.\n\nTWO NEAR-MISSES WORTH INHERITING\n1. I first concluded `syncEnrolmentScopePath` was DEAD CODE (grep of its defining file showed no local caller) and nearly filed that. It has four production call sites. A single-file grep cannot support an absence claim about a repo.\n2. `find /sys/fs/cgroup -maxdepth 6 -name 'pc-<id>*'` returned EMPTY because the real path is depth 7 — a bounded-search artifact that reads exactly like \"the scope does not exist\", which would have inverted the diagnosis. Do not cite a depth/head-bounded search as a negative.\n\nBINDING ON THE REST OF P-023: the exposure surface may report `cgroup_path` only for rows written after this fix, or must derive from `scope_unit` (which was correct all along). Historical rows are still wrong — ~1300 agent-session rows are not retroactively repaired, so a read surface must not present them as current truth.\n\n### D-112 — P-024 is refuted and dropped — its premise was a work-item TITLE, which stays a live defect statement forever\nDate: 2026-09-02\nP-024 asserted the result-door's `projection` advertisement is broken because \"it is a per-tool arg and undeclared-arg rejection refuses it (WI-7135)\". Anyone picking up a remaining item on this plan should read the STATE of every work-item its text cites before treating the citation as live evidence.\n\n### D-113 — P-010's prescribed wording was falsified before implementation; the severity claim had 3 more carriers, and it never reached CLAUDE.md at all\nDate: 2026-09-02\nThird time on this plan (after P-018/D-106 and P-005/D-108) that clearing a blocker FALSIFIED the item it was blocking rather than unblocking it. Recording the general shape, because the remaining \"BLOCKED BY\" items will hit it too.\n\n**1. The spec was stale.** P-010 said: bind accessor to relation — `work_items` table => `payload->'_ei'->>'severity'`; `engineer_issues` view => `severity` column, the nested path being dead there. Post-1096 (P-003, applied 2026-09-02T17:05:52Z) the view no longer subtracts the blob, so on the VIEW **both accessors resolve and agree — 166,941 of 166,948 rows** (measured 2026-09-02 on the live view; `pg_get_viewdef` shows bare `payload`, no `payload - '_ei'`). Every one binds a SCALAR into a fixed statement skeleton. The sample structurally excluded composition.\n\nSO D-115's Q2 SENTENCE 'including every realistic shape in this codebase' IS NOT SUPPORTED BY ITS OWN SAMPLE, and I withdraw it. Per EI-22238479367433132, composition is how most production queries here are actually built (compileRank, compileFilter, specFilterSql, specOrderSql). The generalization was drawn over the shape class the codebase most uses and the sample least covered.\n\nD-106 ALREADY SAW THIS COMING AND IT WAS NOT DISCHARGED. D-106's UNPROBED REMAINDER (2) reads: 'parameter-type inference when a tagged-template query is reassembled into $1..$n placeholder text. Specify both before scaling this beyond one adopter.' D-115 answered remainder (2) with the nine-shape probe and declared it 'NOT A BLOCKER'. That probe did not exercise reassembly of a FRAGMENT — only of scalars — so remainder (2) was closed on evidence that did not address it. EI-22238479367433132 is the real discharge, and it comes back UNFAVOURABLE.\n\nTHE MIS-CALIBRATION, which is this plan's own subject class occurring inside this plan's own remedy. Two different populations produce an IDENTICAL error signature:\n- RARE + BENIGN: `WHERE $1 IS NULL` -> 'could not determine data type of parameter $1' (42P18). D-115 correctly called this narrow and fixable with an explicit cast.\n- COMMON + MALIGNANT: a composed query captured as `WHERE $1 $2` -> the SAME 42P18 string, classified `untypeable`. NOT rare, NOT fixable by a cast, and the capture cannot represent the statement at all.\nBecause `untypeable` is a TOLERATED outcome, the tolerance calibrated on the first population silently absorbs the second. `report.invalid` comes back empty and the adopter reads a green over SQL that was never parsed. That is precisely a result that looks right and is not.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR ACCEPTANCE — binding on whoever writes the next card. This plan's standing acceptance is REJECT (EI-22188021030989262) on the population-denominator ground alone. It now rests on TWO grounds. A superseding acceptance card MUST address this one explicitly; do NOT emit a fresh card that clears only the deploy blocker and ships. Recording it here because the carried ship sequence ('on a real deploy: re-measure population -> re-grade C1 -> fresh card -> ship') would otherwise walk straight past it.\n\nNOT RULED HERE, deliberately: the repair. Whether to widen the capture to render fragments, to make `unjudged` mandatory, or to narrow the guard's advertised scope is su-f47736da's call as WI-7132's holder; note only that `unjudged` can never reach 0 for a composed query, so 'assert unjudged===0' is not a repair on its own.\n\nMeasured 2026-09-03: D-115 body re-read via plans:get { decisions:['D-115'] } — nine shapes enumerated above, zero composed. D-106 body re-read via plans:get { decisions:['D-106'] } — remainder (2) quoted verbatim. Probe chain and call-site counts are su-f47736da's, recorded on EI-22238479367433132, not re-run by me.\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-138 — A SUBJECT-PLAN edit does NOT invalidate banked acceptance cards — the revision pin is the RUBRIC's own harness_plans row, so only a rubric edit invalidates\nDate: 2026-09-03\nDate: 2026-09-03\nCORRECTS an over-broad reading that has been chilling ordinary work on this plan, mine included.\n\nTHE CLAIM AS IT WAS CIRCULATING (D-129b's rationale, and my own carry notes): 'cards pin to harness_plans.version, so ANY edit invalidates BOTH the standing author attestation AND both banked independent cards.' Read literally, that says any plan write at all — a Decision, an item status flip, a ## Now update — destroys expensive, independently-obtained grading cards. I had been treating this plan as frozen on that basis.\n\nIT IS NOT TRUE AS STATED. The pin is real but it is the RUBRIC's row, not the subject plan's. Rubrics are themselves stored in harness_shared.harness_plans (template = RUBRIC_TEMPLATE_NAME), each with its own version counter, and the gate reads THAT row.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-03, packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts:711 — readRubricPlanRevision(rubricId) runs SELECT plan_slug, version FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE workspace_id = <scope> AND template = RUBRIC_TEMPLATE_NAME AND template_slug IS NULL AND plan_slug = <rubricId>. The predicate is plan_slug = the RUBRIC ID, so the version returned is the rubric's own.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-03, packages/operator-core/lib/plan-acceptance-gate.ts:840 — the gate calls readRubricPlanRevision(rubric.rubricId) and compares the result against the vetted revisions, refusing via the acceptance_rubric_revision_unreadable / stale-vetting branch at :893-:906.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: editing the acceptance rubric bumps the rubric row's version and DOES invalidate the attestation and the banked cards — so D-129b's deferral of WI-2142667 remains CORRECT and its conclusion is unchanged. But editing THIS plan (adding a Decision, closing an item, rewriting ## Now) bumps silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01's own version and leaves the rubric row untouched, so it cannot invalidate any card. This decision is itself the demonstration: it bumps the plan from version 137 and the cards stand.\n\nWHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PLAN: the imprecise form is the more memorable one, it sounds appropriately cautious, and it converts a narrow true constraint into a blanket freeze on the exact surface — plan Decisions — that cross-lane rulings are supposed to be recorded on. An agent obeying it stops recording rulings at precisely the moment a ruling is most needed. State the constraint as 'a RUBRIC edit invalidates cards'; do not restate it as 'any edit'.\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-139 — The adopter assertion is `invalid` empty AND `vacuous` false — NEVER `unjudged === 0`; ratifying su-f47736da's departure and the prepare validator's first production adoption\nDate: 2026-09-03\nDate: 2026-09-03\nRecorded by su-da016d95, ratifying a departure su-f47736da flagged for me at 11:16:25Z. Discharges the remainder D-137 left open.\n\nTHE DEPARTURE. su-f47736da declined to wire `report.unjudged === 0` as the adopter assertion for the SQL prepare validator, substituting `invalid` empty AND `vacuous === false` (where judged = valid+invalid, vacuous = judged===0). They flagged it as a deliberate departure from the wording they had been given. RATIFIED IN FULL.\n\nI ALMOST RULED THE OTHER WAY, AND THE CODE SAVED ME. My prior was that tolerating unjudged leaves an unbounded coverage hole: statements could drift from judged into unjudged and the guard stay green on judged>=1. I went to write that as a finding. It is wrong on every count, and the instrument's OWN DOCUMENTATION prescribes exactly what su-f47736da did — a warning aimed precisely at the mistake I was about to make.\n\nWHY `unjudged === 0` IS THE WRONG ASSERTION. It is the obvious one, and it is unsatisfiable for fragment-composed SQL: a composed statement cannot be judged at all until someone splices the fragment's own parameters back in. An adopter that asserted it would be permanently red, so it would be deleted or its guard weakened — the assertion defeats itself.\n\nWHY THE HOLE IS NOT SILENT. `composed` is a SEPARATE named counter (the subset of unjudged that went unjudged because the CAPTURE was composed), so the gap is stated per run rather than buried in a lump. `empty` is deliberately excluded from `judged` so it cannot inflate coverage (EI-22238479367433132). `formatCoverage` prints `judged N/total` and says NOTHING WAS CHECKED out loud when vacuous.\n\nAND THE ADOPTER DOES BETTER THAN A COVERAGE FLOOR. I went looking for a minimum-judged ratchet and found none. It is not needed: rather than TOLERATING its hole, the first adopter PINS it — asserting `judged === 0` and `vacuous === true` as exact expected values over the real composed query. So the day the composition is fixed, vacuous flips false and THE TEST FAILS, forcing the update. A floor is a lower bound that rots quietly; an exact assertion is a tripwire that cannot. This is the better mechanism and it should be the pattern for later adopters.\n\nTHE ADOPTION IS REAL, AND IT IS THE POINT. WI-7132's finding was that `validateManyByPrepare` was called from exactly one file — its own test — so every statement it had ever judged was hand-written inside its own fixture: a shipped guard protecting nothing, this plan's subject class. That is now false. `scheduler/active-claims-sql-validity.integration.test.ts` is the first production adopter and names itself as such, citing D-137.\n\nGENERALIZABLE, and the third instance in this lineage in one session: before reporting a finding about how an instrument counts, read the instrument. The obvious assertion is obvious to the author too, and a mature guard often documents why it is wrong — in this case in a comment addressed to exactly the reader I was being. A critique that the source already answers is not a finding; it is a failure to read.\n\nSCOPE. WI-7132 is su-f47736da's (claimed 11:04:33Z after fleet:leave, the lever D-132 named). This ratifies their design call and does not direct their implementation. No bearing on C1 or on the ship gate, which remains deploy-blocked per D-126/D-129.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-03. packages/operator-core/lib/testing/sql-prepare-validation.ts:306-311 — \"⚠ Do NOT assert `unjudged === 0`. It is the obvious assertion and it is [wrong] … assert invalid empty AND vacuous false, and let `composed` state the hole.\" Same file :313 unjudged = untypeable+unpreparable+composed+empty; :319 judged = valid+invalid; :334/:363 vacuous = judged===0; :102-105 empty excluded from judged, citing EI-22238479367433132. grep for floor|ratchet|minJudged|minimum|atLeast|coverageFloor in that file returned no lines. Adopters calling validateManyByPrepare outside its own definition: sql-prepare-validation.integration.test.ts, testing/sql-mock.ts, scheduler/active-claims-sql-validity.integration.test.ts. That last file :5-6 \"THE FIRST PRODUCTION ADOPTER … until this file, every statement that validator had ever judged was hand-written in its [own fixture]\"; :20-37 documents the unjudged===0 trap; :119-122 expects invalid length 0, judged 0, vacuous true; :144-146 expects judged 2, vacuous false, invalid labels ['incident'].\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-140 — Reject ground (ii) is REMEDIED and committed — and a TEST-TIME guard's \"in force\" test is tree-presence + a live adopter, NOT deployment; only ground (i) is deploy-gated\nDate: 2026-09-03\nDate: 2026-09-03\nRecorded by su-da016d95. Updates the standing acceptance reject. Does NOT re-grade C1 (settled by D-129, moves only on a deploy) and does NOT unblock the ship.\n\nWHAT THE REJECT SAID. Two grounds: (i) the population/populationNote remedy committed but NOT in force on deployed 6e898b6cf8; (ii) a composed-query hole INSIDE this plan's own remedy — a fragment-composed query classified `untypeable`, which is TOLERATED, so `report.invalid` came back empty over SQL that was never parsed. Ground (ii) was this plan's subject reproduced inside its own fix.\n\nGROUND (ii) IS NOW REMEDIED, AND THE FIX IS COMMITTED. `composed` is now its own verdict that SHORT-CIRCUITS BEFORE PREPARE — the database is never consulted, so no classification can occur and nothing can be tolerated by mistake. It is excluded from `judged`, surfaced as its own counter, and the flag is supplied by the CAPTURE (`sql-mock.ts`'s `capturedForValidation`), never guessed from the text — the capture is the only thing that knows a fragment was erased.\n\nWHY SHORT-CIRCUITING BEATS CLASSIFYING, per su-f47736da: they measured exactly ONE composed shape (`status NOT IN ${sql([...])}` -> 42P18 -> untypeable) and correctly refuse to generalize from it. The remedy is deliberately INDEPENDENT of that unmeasured question, because the untested shapes could be WORSE, not better: an erased fragment might reassemble into something that parses clean and returns `valid`, which would count as COVERAGE. Tolerated-untypeable is the benign end of the range; a false `valid` is the end nobody can rule out. Refusing to judge is the only verdict correct at both ends. Adopt that shape generally — when a capture is known to be lossy, refuse to judge it; do not classify what the instrument cannot see.\n\nTHE DISTINCTION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS FOR THE CARD. The two grounds are NOT deploy-gated alike, and I had been treating them as if they were. Ground (i) is a RUNTIME operator behaviour: `issues:list` must actually RETURN population/populationNote to a live caller, so it is in force only when DEPLOYED, and remains blocked. Ground (ii) is a TEST-TIME guard: its in-force test is presence in the tree the gate runs PLUS a live adopter exercising it — deployment to :3070 is irrelevant to it, and the whole validator file being absent from deployed 6e898b6cf8 is expected, not a finding. Reading \"not in the deployed sha\" as \"not in force\" is correct for (i) and a category error for (ii).\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR STEP (d). The superseding acceptance card must still address BOTH grounds, but it must now record (ii) as REMEDIED WITH EVIDENCE rather than restating it as an open defect. Restating a fixed defect because the note describing it still reads plausibly is precisely this plan's subject class, one level up — the same trap WI-7132's own superseded checkpoint fell into. Ground (i) alone survives as a ship blocker.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-03. packages/operator-core/lib/testing/sql-prepare-validation.ts validateSqlByPrepare — `if (opts.composed) return { verdict: 'composed', ... }` sits ABOVE the `isPreparable` check and above the `PREPARE` call, note citing EI-22238479367433132 verbatim: \"Judging it anyway is what silently returned green over unparsed SQL.\" Same file: unjudged = untypeable+unpreparable+composed+empty; judged = valid+invalid. Committed state via blob containment with a positive control: git rev-parse staging:<validator> = 3080f11ece864ab79813da5181becf264cff2117; `grep -c \"verdict: 'composed'\"` = 1 in BOTH the committed staging copy and the working tree; positive control `validateSqlByPrepare` = 2 occurrences in the committed copy. Adopter: git rev-parse staging:packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/active-claims-sql-validity.integration.test.ts = b5d2e3930c9277d2e88090a7ddee3d1c152fd248, committed copy contains 4 `vacuous` and 4 `validateManyByPrepare` occurrences. Deployed containment: git rev-parse 6e898b6cf88316fcf1574f049554a6caf16318f0:<validator> resolves to nothing (file absent from that sha) — expected for a test-time guard. deploy.3070.sha unchanged at 6e898b6cf8 as of 11:19Z.\nRelated: P-018\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"trap-guards-followups-2026-08-01","title":"Trap-guards follow-ups — fix the ambiguous signals the fleet run exposed","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-01","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Trap-guards follow-ups — fix the ambiguous signals the fleet run exposed\nslug: trap-guards-followups-2026-08-01\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-01\nupdated: 2026-08-01\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — 5/5 settled, solo, each flipped only on evidence. P-001 DONE: the ?lhive= red was fixed by the retirement author after I routed it; I verified the LINK is correct, not merely the assertion (`slug` is the canonical pot param the top-bar selector reads; `learnings` is in HIVE_AWARE_VIEWS), 28/28 green, EI-18742382546783068 auto-resolved on 3 consecutive greens. P-002 DONE: implemented from my filing by su-1f464b1c, re-verified independently 73/73 — `all_matches_gated` is now the explicit effect-vs-cause counterpart of `spec_matches_nothing`. P-003 DONE (mine): the lint had been redesigned better than either remedy I proposed, so the real gap was that its rationale lived only in header prose; extracted `scanTextForCallReferences` and pinned 5 guards against SYNTHETIC fixtures, then PROVED teeth by replaying bare-token CALL_RE (4+3 false positives incl. `messages:write`). 7/7, TSC clean. P-004 DROPPED with a public retraction — both halves already existed (pc-heavy.sh flock semaphore, 4 slots; the durable log path is printed before the run); my \"17 concurrent sweeps\" was a process-line miscount of 4 real runs at the cap. Residue filed rather than left in prose. P-005 DONE (mine): split `CoverageLevel` — new `held-not-live` band separates \"never taken\" from \"taken by a holder who is gone\", covering the direct-claim case that read as `none`. 136/136 green, TSC clean on all 5 files. D-001 corrects my own wrong 2026-07-26 coord ruling that the ledger's `assignee` is authoritative over coverage.\n\n**Next:** Nothing on this plan — it is closed. One incidental finding is filed and owned elsewhere: WI-6753 (a peer's new `fleet/require-checkpoint.ts:400` passes `text` to `SendOptions`; one TS2353 that reds `lint:tsc` for the whole fleet until its author fixes it).\n\n## Background\n\nThe `agent-trap-guards-2026-07-26` fleet run (7/7, closed) shipped guards against references that survive a retirement. While running it, six instances of ONE defect shape appeared — **a signal that cannot say WHICH thing it means, acted on confidently** — three of them committed by the fleet leader. Each item below fixes one such signal at its source rather than teaching agents to work around it.\n\nThe shape, concretely: an error token that spans two causes with opposite remedies; two surfaces that disagree about the same fact; a state read used to infer causal history it cannot express. In every observed case the cheap wrong move looked reasonable — which is why a convention cannot fix it. The emitter has to stop being ambiguous.\n\nFiled during the run: EI-18742382546783068, EI-18741523426513509, EI-18742214647740308, plus a load measurement on EI-18699972365875475.\n\n## Phase 1 — the red gate\n\n- **P-001** `done` Fix the deterministic red test behind EI-18742382546783068. `apps/operator/app/harness/__tests__/EntryGithubUrlForm.test.tsx:395` asserts the href `/adv?tab=learning&lview=learnings&lhive=web-hive` while `EntryGithubUrlForm.tsx:786` emits `slug=web-hive`. `?lhive=` is RETIRED (`LearningTab.tsx:3561`, `:404`). Red 6h+ with 10 identical failures — deterministic, NOT flaky (a peer's completion evidence mischaracterised it as flaky, which leads to quarantine instead of a fix). MUST determine what the /adv learnings view actually honours post-retirement and make the LINK correct, not merely make the assertion pass: if no pot param is honoured then emitting `slug=` is a dead user-facing link and the COMPONENT is what changes. Verify against the live param wiring, never by flipping the expectation to match observed output. importance: high — note: RESOLVED — fixed by the retirement author after my routing; I verified it is CORRECT, not merely green\n\n## Phase 2 — the ambiguous signals that cost the most agent time\n\n- **P-002** `done` Split `spec_matches_nothing` (EI-18741523426513509). `scheduler:get_next` returns one cause-asserting token for two conditions with opposite remedies: (a) the filter genuinely matches nothing of a NONEMPTY claimable pool — a real spec problem; (b) the filter matched rows but every one was excluded by a TRANSIENT floor (uncleared externalBlockers/live-dependency gates, peer-held claims, maxConcurrentClaims) — where the correct action is to WAIT, not escalate. Emit a distinct token for (b) carrying matched-count, the dominant excluding floor, and the blocker refs plus who clears them. The per-floor `excludedBreakdown` machinery already exists; this is about the RESULT TOKEN reflecting it. Measured cost unfixed: two phantom escalations in ~10min, a member parked awaiting a fix that was never coming, and a leader one call from rewriting a correct claim spec — twice. importance: high — note: Already implemented from my filing by su-1f464b1c; I re-verified independently — 73/73 green\n- **P-003** `done` Teach the prompt verb-liveness lint the capability namespace (EI-18742214647740308). `packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/prompt-blueprint-verb-catalog.test.ts` resolves backtick `group:verb` tokens against the live TOOL catalog only, so a CAPABILITY name in a scanned prompt (`messages:write`, `coord:read`, `plans:read`, `intel:read`, `data:read:*`) reds the build as a dead verb. Green today only because none currently appear in `apps/operator/prompts` — an accident of content, not a property of the lint. Resolve tokens against the capability registry as well as the tool catalog, and pin the distinction with a test asserting a live capability passes while a genuinely retired tool verb still fails. This is `agent-trap-guards-2026-07-26#D-003` applied to the guard D-003 constrains. importance: normal — note: Pinned the surface distinction as 5 tests + extracted a pure scanner core; guards proven to have teeth. EI-18742214647740308 closed.\n\n## Phase 3 — the load pathology\n\n- **P-004** `dropped` Bound concurrent affected-sweeps and make their verdict durable (EI-18699972365875475). Measured: 17 concurrent `affected-tests.mjs` sweeps at loadavg 137.8. Mechanism — every agent runs `test:affected` as CLAUDE.md instructs, nothing serializes them, each fans out to many vitest workers, so N agents produce N full fan-outs (multiplicative, not additive). This is a correctness hazard rather than mere slowness: sweep duration outliving a session boundary converted a PASSING run into an unreadable one (native `run_in_background` bookkeeping dies on respawn, EI-16611) and blocked a 7-item plan's last lane on a verdict that already existed. Add a concurrency cap with queueing reusing `scripts/lib/fs-mutex.mjs`, and make the durable log path the ADVERTISED way to read a verdict. importance: normal — note: DROPPED — premise was wrong and I retracted it. Both halves already exist and work; my measurement was a miscount.\n\n## Phase 4 — the remaining surface disagreement\n\n- **P-005** `done` Reconcile `plans:items`' `working` field with the work-item ledger. During the run it reported P-006/P-007 as `working:'unclaimed'` while `work_items:get` showed both with a live assignee + takenAt, and reported P-002/P-005 correctly — so it reads as trustworthy while being wrong. This MANUFACTURED both phantom escalations in P-002: members judged claimability from the plan view, correctly concluded \"free\", pulled, got nothing, and escalated upward instead of coordinating with the holder. Diagnose whether the field is stale-by-lag or wrong-by-derivation, then either fix the derivation or stop exposing a claim-state field the ledger owns. P-006 shipped `planItemClaimCollision` on `work_items:get`, which covers the mid-execution case but NOT this read-side divergence. importance: normal — note: Split CoverageLevel: added `held-not-live` (holder on record, none live ⇒ reclaimable) so coverage stops reporting a dead holder as \"nobody on it\". Also fixes the direct-claim case that read as `none`. 136/136 green, TSC clean on all 5 files. Root cause + my own wrong 2026-07-26 ruling corrected in D-001.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — plans:items `working` and the work-item `assignee` answer DIFFERENT questions — neither is \"authoritative\" over the other; my 2026-07-26 ruling that the ledger wins was wrong\nDate: 2026-08-01\nRULING, and a CORRECTION of my own earlier one. Binding on anyone reconciling plan-item coverage against the work-item ledger.\n\n**What I told a fleet member on 2026-07-26 (coord msg `ms29xxeb-0000-cfc95bf3d9d947f0aaf5e4e652f0aa32`, 16:52:27):** that when \"the plan-item view and the work-item ledger disagree\", the ledger — `work_items:get` / the `assignee` field — \"is authoritative.\" **That is wrong.** It is not a priority ordering at all, because the two surfaces are not answering the same question.\n\n- `harness_shared.work_items.assignee` is a **stored column**. It records who TOOK the item. It survives its holder's death, its stall, and its respawn — nothing rewrites it when a session ends.\n- `plans:items` → `working` (`CoverageLevel`, `plan-item-coverage.ts`) is **recomputed from live activity on every read**: `classifyCoverage` counts a link as covered only at `progressing|alive` (`isLiveActivity`), the same liveness truth `fleet:assignments` enforces (agent-activity-liveness-truth).\n\nSo \"assigned in the ledger, nobody working per coverage\" is not a contradiction, a lag, or a stale cache — **it is the two surfaces working correctly and reporting different facts.** It is the *normal* reading of an item whose holder died. Treating the ledger as the tiebreak means treating a dead holder's name as live coverage, which is precisely the double-start that plan-item coverage exists to prevent. My message inverted the safe direction.\n\n**The trap that made this easy to get wrong, now fixed (P-005).** The old `CoverageLevel` collapsed \"never taken\" and \"taken by someone who is gone\" into one band — `unclaimed`, documented as \"nobody on it\" (and, for a lapsed *direct* plan-item claim with no links, into `none`, documented as \"genuinely unworked\"). A reader who saw `working:'unclaimed'` beside a named assignee had no way to tell a real link-path bug from correct liveness-aware behaviour, so the natural conclusion was \"one of these surfaces is broken\" — which is the conclusion I reached, and then broadcast. P-005 splits out **`held-not-live`**: a holder IS on record (link or direct claim) but none is live, so the item is RECLAIMABLE and the ledger's assignee is a ghost. The disagreement is now stated by the data instead of inferred from it.\n\n**How to read them, going forward:**\n- \"Should I start this / would I be duplicating?\" → `working`. A non-live band (`unclaimed`, `held-not-live`, `none`) means go.\n- \"Who took it, and when?\" → the ledger's `assignee`/`takenAt`. Historical, not a liveness claim.\n- \"Is the recorded holder actually alive?\" → `sessionState` / the item's `activity`, never the presence of an assignee.\n\n**Meta-point, which is the reusable part.** This ruling reached a peer only as a coord message, so when it turned out to be wrong there was no addressable artifact to correct — the peer's copy is un-revisitable by construction. That is D-002 (`agent-trap-guards-2026-07-26`) demonstrated from the failure side: I followed it for rulings I was confident in and skipped it for one I issued in passing while unblocking someone. A ruling issued casually is exactly the one most likely to be wrong, and therefore the one that most needs a decision record. Confidence is not the criterion; whether other lanes will act on it is.\nRelated: P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"abolish-human-review-agent-review-only-2026-08-02","title":"Abolish human review — agents review, Blender-style","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Abolish human review — agents review, Blender-style\nslug: abolish-human-review-agent-review-only-2026-08-02\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nP-001 through P-005 DONE. The audit and implementation work landed through D-001 and the completed items; the plan now reflects the five completed plan items instead of stopping at P-001.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: P-006 — migrate the live parked items per the P-002 classification: review-parked rows enter agent review and escalation rows use the renamed path. WI-40108 is the active implementation; state the expected row count and verify it before any bulk mutation. After P-006, continue with P-007 (recurrence guard) and P-008 (agent-facing prompt/doc sweep).)\n\n## Background\n\n**The directive.** [owner:Avi 2026-08-01, verbatim] \"NOTHIGN SHOULD BE HUMAN-REVIEWED. THERE SHOULD BE REVIEWED BY AGENTS ONLY LIKE THE BLENDER\". Verified against the transcript (not a paraphrase) and recorded as workspace fact `no-human-review-agents-review-like-blender`.\n\n**What exists today** (`improvements/capture.ts:59`), three tiers:\n- `lane:'observation'` — never enters the work queue regardless of kind; read only by the Blender corpus-digest + the Observations pane.\n- `kind='bug'` — enters the queue, auto-implement-eligible. The only direct path.\n- `kind='change'|'feature'` — enters the queue but **human-reviewed**. This tier is what the directive abolishes.\n\n**Live scale** (measured 2026-08-01, harness papercusp): **131** open items carry `payload.needsHuman:true` (75 change, 52 bug, 3 task, 1 observation) and **45** sit in state `needs-human` (40 bug, 3 feature, 2 change) — ~176 items parked on a human. 88 files under `packages/operator-core/lib` reference `needsHuman`/`needs-human`.\n\n**The reference model.** The Blender: a PEER agent grades (`blender:grade-idea`, which refuses a self-grade), a low grade plus feedback WAKES the originator to revise, and outcomes feed back as win-rates (`blender:ideation-feedback`). Review is a revision signal produced by someone other than the author — not a queue that waits on a person.\n\n**The distinction this plan draws, and the one place it could go wrong.** \"Review\" (judging whether work is good / should proceed) is what the directive abolishes. That is NOT the same as **capability escalation** — an action no agent can physically perform: provisioning hardware, supplying a credential, authorizing spend. Live example: EI-18664933641195210, three owner-provisioned squid proxies unreachable; no amount of agent review fixes that. If P-001 collapses both into one bucket, those items silently enter an agent queue and spin forever. So the audit must SEPARATE them, and the escalation path must be renamed so it can never masquerade as review. This is the assumption to challenge first if the plan feels wrong.\n\n## Phase 1 — audit before edit\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit all 88 `needsHuman`/`needs-human` references and classify each into exactly one of: (a) REVIEW — judging merit/quality, abolish per the directive; (b) CAPABILITY ESCALATION — an act only the owner can perform (credential, spend, hardware, external account); (c) INCIDENTAL — a mention, type, or display that is neither. Deliverable is the classified inventory; nothing is edited in this item. — note: ← WI-6761 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Classify the ~176 currently-parked live items (131 `payload.needsHuman`, 45 state `needs-human`) against the same taxonomy, so the migration knows which rows convert to agent-review and which stay escalations. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40103 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — build the agent reviewer\n\n- **P-003** `done` Design the agent-review step for `kind=change|feature` on the Blender pattern: a peer agent grades, self-grade refused, a failing grade wakes the filer with feedback to revise rather than parking the item. Reuse `blender:grade-idea` / the routed-idea ledger rather than standing up a parallel grading system. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40104 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Implement the agent-review step and flip `capture.ts` so `change|feature` route to it instead of to human review. Update the tool description (`capture.ts:59`), which currently states \"human-reviewed\" and is itself the spec agents read. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-40105 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Rename the surviving capability-escalation path so it cannot be read as review (e.g. `needsOwnerAction`), and make the claim floor reflect the split. The current single `needsHumanExclusionSql` floor cannot distinguish the two. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40107 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — migrate and guard\n\n- **P-006** `done` Migrate the live parked items per the P-002 classification: review-parked rows enter agent review; escalation rows move to the renamed path. Bulk mutation — state the expected row count and verify against it before executing. blocked-by: P-002, P-005 — note: ← WI-40108 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `todo` Add the recurrence guard: a detector that fails when a NEW human-review gate appears, so the directive is enforced structurally rather than by memory. Without this the surface regrows the moment someone adds a gate. blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-008** `todo` Sweep the agent-facing prompts/docs that still instruct agents to route to a human for review, so the written guidance matches the mechanism. blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The REVIEW / CAPABILITY-ESCALATION split already exists in code — it is enforced at 1 of ~5 write sites, and the audit must be by WRITE SITE, not by reference count\nDate: 2026-08-02\nP-001 deliverable. Three findings, each of which changes what Phases 2-3 should do.\n\n#### 1. The plan's \"88 references\" is wrong by 3-10x — and counting references was the wrong unit anyway\n\nMeasured in live non-test source (excluding node_modules, _retired, dist-sidecar):\n\n| token | refs |\n|---|---|\n| `needsHuman` | 275 |\n| `needs-human` | 461 |\n| `needs_human_review` (feature-family column — a DIFFERENT mechanism) | 210 |\n\nActing on \"88\" would have audited a fraction and declared the surface covered. But classifying ~946 line-refs individually is the wrong altitude regardless: the overwhelming majority are reads, types, display and plumbing that cannot park anything. What determines the taxonomy is the WRITE sites — what CAUSES a park. There are ~5.\n\n#### 2. The taxonomy this plan proposes to invent ALREADY EXISTS, and was built for exactly this reason\n\n`resolve-core.ts` gates on `isGenuineHumanCapability(cap)` -> `externalBlockerCapabilityPolicy(cap).requiresOwnerCapability`. Its own comment (P-004 / WI-5679):\n\n> \"only a TYPED, genuinely owner-gated capability reaches the OWNER's inbox. An untyped 'needs-human' from a worker was the DOMINANT (209x) over-application — usually an operational give-up, not a real human need — so it now routes to the LEADER-TRIAGE lane (status='blocked') instead: out of the auto-dispatch loop, but a leader (not the owner) triages it.\"\n\nThat IS review-vs-escalation, already implemented. Phase 2 should EXTEND this seam, not build a parallel one.\n\n#### 3. But it is enforced at only ONE write site, so the live data is 98.5% unclassifiable\n\nLive parked rows (`payload.needsHuman = true`, non-terminal, papercusp):\n\n| | rows |\n|---|---|\n| carry `humanCapability` (typed escalation) | **2** |\n| carry NO capability field (untyped) | **136** |\n\nThe 2 typed rows carry `product-decision` — not a credential, spend, or hardware. So ZERO live rows are owner-capability escalations in the strict sense. State split: 89 `open`, 42 `needs-human`, 7 `blocked`.\n\n#### The classified inventory, by write site\n\n| site | classification | note |\n|---|---|---|\n| `resolve-core.ts:281` | **CAPABILITY ESCALATION** | the only TYPED path; gated by `isGenuineHumanCapability`; 2 live rows |\n| `resolve-core.ts:242` | **ESCALATION (non-owner)** | federated/remote-owned row cannot be mutated locally; needs reconciliation on the OWNING PEER, not owner judgement. Do NOT fold into review — no agent-reviewer can resolve it |\n| `triage-core.ts:209` (`decision === 'gate'`) | **REVIEW** | protected-path / process-change gates; judging merit. THE target of the directive |\n| `work-items.ts:2459` | **MIRROR (derived)** | mirrors state='needs-human' into payload; inherits whatever caused the state — not an independent decision |\n| `work_items:update { needsHuman }` tool arg | **UNTYPED — either** | agent-driven, arbitrary reason, no typing. The hole through which most of the 136 arrived |\n| `attention/adapters.ts` (15 sites) | **INCIDENTAL** | all collapse to ONE rule: `needsHumanForTier(tier) => tier === 'decision'`. Display/routing derivation; parks nothing |\n\n#### Consequences for Phases 2-3\n\n- **P-005 (rename the escalation path) must not treat `resolve-core.ts:242` as review.** Federated-remote rows are neither review nor owner-capability; collapsing them into an agent-review queue makes them spin forever, since no local agent can resolve them by construction. They need a third destination.\n- **P-002's classification cannot be data-driven.** 136 of 138 rows carry no capability field, so the taxonomy is not recoverable from `payload` — it must come from the SITE that wrote each row, or from re-triage.\n- **The untyped `work_items:update` arg is the leak.** Typing the escalation path (P-005) is defeated if this stays untyped; it is how the 136 got in.\n- **Reframing worth stating plainly:** the queue's problem was never filing quality (a random sample of queue-entering filings was 14/14 substantive; gross duplication 3.4%). It is CONSUMPTION and DEDUP. An agent reviewer that grades filings but leaves ~1,400 real bugs unclaimed changes nothing — so Phase 2's success metric should be items REACHING TERMINAL, not items reviewed.\n\n### D-002 — The live parked cohort partitions 357 federated / 365 agent-review / 8 owner-capability / 20 operational-re-admit\nDate: 2026-08-20\nDate: 2026-08-20\nP-002 deliverable. This is a migration inventory, not a mutation of the live rows.\n\nThe current non-terminal Papercusp parked cohort is **750** rows after excluding `lane='observation'`. Classification uses originating-writer semantics first, with content re-triage only for the 41 rows whose payload cannot identify a writer:\n\n| destination | rows | basis |\n|---|---:|---|\n| **FEDERATED PEER RECONCILIATION** | **357** | `origin='remote'` takes precedence over every local review marker; these rows cannot be resolved by a local reviewer |\n| **AGENT REVIEW** | **365** | 350 local `ideaLifecycle.triageDecision='gate'` rows + 2 local typed `humanCapability='product-decision'` rows + 13 untyped rows re-triaged as judgment/review |\n| **OWNER CAPABILITY** | **8** | untyped rows whose content proves a missing credential, physical device/guest, or external-service action |\n| **AGENT OPERATIONAL / RE-ADMIT** | **20** | untyped bugs/tasks whose content describes ordinary agent-fixable or agent-operable work; neither review nor owner escalation |\n| **TOTAL** | **750** | exact disjoint partition |\n\nNo current local row carries a typed strict owner capability: the three typed `humanCapability` rows are `product-decision`; two are local and one is remote. The eight genuine owner-capability rows are therefore precisely the rows that the migration must type rather than infer from their current payload.\n\n#### Exact re-triage of the 41 untyped local residuals\n\n**Owner capability (8):** EI-20192345878553998, EI-20360519880305472, EI-20395113508971679, EI-20578449222009534, WI-38516, WI-38664, WI-39114, WI-39622.\n\n**Agent review (13):** EI-1831, EI-1835, EI-20565859968567853, EI-240, EI-419, EI-420, EI-515, WI-199, WI-37424, WI-37911, WI-3796, WI-3915, WI-4271.\n\n**Agent operational / re-admit (20):** EI-11110, EI-11258, EI-12198, EI-12643, EI-13224, EI-13317, EI-1416, EI-14166, EI-14380, EI-18186974315578623, EI-20326449630295528, EI-20329308392406247, EI-20337293459706703, EI-20417341810957263, EI-20451293817259494, EI-2470, WI-3573, WI-37494, WI-39344, WI-39345.\n\nThe 41-ID map was verified against the live residual with: residual=41, manual rows=41, distinct=41, missing=0, extra=0.\n\n#### Migration constraints\n\n1. Remote wins over review: a remote row carrying `triageDecision='gate'` still goes to peer reconciliation.\n2. Review and capability escalation are separate destinations. `product-decision` is review for this plan; credentials/devices/external actions are owner capability.\n3. Untyped operational rows must be re-admitted to an agent-operable lane; converting them to agent review would merely replace one parking lot with another.\n4. The migration should stamp destination/provenance so this census is not repeated from title text later.\n5. Success is rows reaching terminal, not rows merely being graded.\n\n### D-003 — Agent review is a work-item lifecycle driven by the existing routed-idea grade row; 4–5 approves and 1–3 requests revision\nDate: 2026-08-20\nDate: 2026-08-20\nP-003 design deliverable. Extend the existing Blender seam; do not create a review table, a second grade tool, or a human-shaped parking state.\n\n#### Authority split\n\n- `harness_shared.scout_routed_ideas` remains the sole grade authority: one row keyed by the work-item id, `routed_ref='wi:<id>'`, `rail='improvement'`, `created_by=<original filer>`, with the existing `human_grade`, `human_feedback`, `graded_by`, and `graded_at` columns. `graded_by` stays caller-derived and `blender:grade-idea` keeps refusing `created_by === caller ownerId`.\n- `work_items.payload.agentReview` is only the routing state: `{ status: 'pending' | 'revision-requested' | 'approved', submittedBy, ledgerIdeaId, round }`. It must not copy grade/feedback; readers join the ledger for those. Work-item comments carry round history while the ledger row carries the current grade.\n- Entering review ensures that ledger row idempotently. If a feature already has an `origin='su-ideate'` row, preserve its origin, lens, grounding refs, and creator. A change without a row may use a new `origin='agent-review'` / `lens='agent-review'`; every learning reader must keep origin filtering explicit so review-only rows never affect Scout or su lens learning.\n\n#### State machine and queue ownership\n\n1. The local `kind=change|feature` writer that would currently emit a review gate calls one `enterAgentReview` seam. It stamps `status='pending'`, records the ledger row, and ensures `needsHuman=false`. Normal implementation selectors exclude `pending` and `revision-requested`; an agent-review selector admits `pending`. This is an active agent lane over the existing work-item queue, not a new queue.\n2. A peer calls the existing `blender:grade-idea { routedRef:'wi:<id>', grade, feedback? }`. The current caller-derived attribution and no-self-grade guard are binding.\n3. Grade 4 or 5 means APPROVED: atomically set `agentReview.status='approved'`, release the reviewer claim, and re-admit the still-open item to normal implementation. Approval never closes the work item; success remains the implementation reaching a genuine terminal state.\n4. Grade 1–3 means REVISION REQUESTED and requires non-empty feedback. Atomically set `status='revision-requested'`, persist a work-item comment for the round, and send the existing durable grade note plus a required wake/dispatch to `submittedBy`. The item is not marked `needsHuman`, `blocked`, or `_claimHold`; it becomes filer-owned revision work. Resubmission increments `round` and returns to `pending`, after which another peer grade overwrites the ledger's current grade.\n5. For an agent-review row, a 1–3 grade without feedback is refused before the grade write, because otherwise no actionable revision signal exists. General Scout/su grading semantics stay unchanged.\n\n#### Consistency and taxonomy rails\n\nThe grade write and `agentReview` transition must share one PG transaction, or be exposed through one idempotent write seam whose retry deterministically reconciles the payload from the standing ledger grade before returning success. Coord delivery happens after commit and remains retryable/best-effort; durable work-item comment + state are the reliable half.\n\nD-001/D-002 destinations remain disjoint: remote-origin rows never enter local review (peer reconciliation wins); strict credential/device/external-action rows stay on the typed owner-capability path; operational rows are re-admitted directly. `product-decision` is review, not owner capability. Migration must stamp destination provenance instead of re-inferring titles.\n\n#### Acceptance guard for P-004/P-007\n\nTests must prove: self-grade cannot mutate either store; 1–3 without feedback cannot land; 1–3 wakes/returns the filer to revision without any human/blocked flag; 4–5 re-admits but does not close; duplicate/retried grade calls converge; existing su-ideate provenance survives review enrollment; remote and strict owner-capability rows cannot enter this lane. The plan succeeds on reviewed items reaching terminal, not on grade counts.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-004 — P-006 migration preserves historical kinds and uses deterministic provenance fallbacks\nDate: 2026-08-21\nP-006 extends D-003 only for the live legacy migration. Review enrollment must preserve each work item's existing kind (bug/change/task/feature); selectors and reviewer pickup must consume those preserved kinds rather than rewriting them to change or feature. When a same-ID scout_routed_ideas row already routes to another artifact, keep that row unchanged and create the review authority at deterministic id agent-review:<work-item-id>; payload.agentReview.ledgerIdeaId records the actual ledger id. For the 30 review rows whose original submitter cannot be recovered from work-item or same-ID ledger provenance, stamp a stable legacy-system submitter sentinel. A 1–3 grade on such a row must not wake or assign that nonexistent principal: it re-admits the item to normal implementation, the real reviser claims it, and resubmission rebinds submittedBy to that real caller. These are narrow compatibility rules for migrated history; new review enrollment continues to require real caller-derived provenance. The migration remains idempotent, stamps destination/provenance, and re-counts the live cohort immediately before mutation because D-002's 750-row census is a historical snapshot, not an execution-time invariant.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-005 — RED-23 repair and successor admission remain separate lanes\nDate: 2026-08-21\nAfter b39c207b terminalized as authoritative RED-23 and its automated release-fixer became owner-gone, WI-40108/P-006 may diagnose and patch the seven exact failing checks. WI-40086 remains the sole authority for the frozen repair queue, checkpoint/Cargo launch, and at most one qualifying current-tip successor. WI-40108 must hand patch and verification evidence to the WI-40086 owner; it must not launch or refire a checkpoint itself.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-006 — Correction: RED-23 fixer is physically live; D-005 owner-gone premise withdrawn\nDate: 2026-08-21\nD-005's statement that the automated RED-23 fixer became owner-gone is withdrawn. Exact task 0mt34jvrw1habcq51ft and scope pc-0mt34jvrw1habcq51ft.scope are active/running; a two-sample probe showed CPUUsageNSec advancing 9,411,220,000 to 9,453,296,000 with 35 tasks. release:trace returned owner-gone because the liveness join lacks spawnRecordId for this task. The surviving ruling is narrower: WI-40108's 49b75556c2 focused green is useful evidence, but the lane must not take over, launch, or refire while the physical fixer lives. WI-40086 remains the sole serializer and will admit at most one successor only after the physical fixer terminalizes and current-tip evidence is re-read.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-007 — Frozen RED-23 repair finalizes only through the queue-aware checkpoint path\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMeasured transition from WI-40086 serializer at 2026-08-21T16:11:02Z (coord mt35c6nv): exact fixer task 0mt34jvrw1habcq51ft exited 0 and its scope is dead, but the six-file b39 repair remains dirty/uncommitted in the frozen worktree with diff hash 34cd20cb3059205e6b181497d9d127bf09851b2b. Canonical repair_queue remains awaiting-fixer attempt 1 on b39; origin/staging was d809313f298b64c4cb9784243daa30cf7e2e348e. Do not discard or manually commit the frozen edits, and do not launch an ordinary current-tip checkpoint. The serializer successor must re-read the exact queue/worktree/tip cells and fire exactly one queue-aware release:checkpoint-run, which is the path that finalizes/commits and verifies the repair. Only that fresh verdict can open deploy/P-006 progression.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-008 — Terminal update: RED-23 fixer exited; WI-40086 alone admits the verifier\nDate: 2026-08-21\nD-006 correctly retracted the false owner-gone inference while the exact fixer was physically live. That live state has now terminalized: task 0mt34jvrw1habcq51ft exited 0 and scope pc-0mt34jvrw1habcq51ft.scope is gone/dead. RED-23 remains authoritative. Six targeted repairs may feed exactly one queue-aware verifier under WI-40086/su-271f; WI-40108 and other lanes remain evidence-only and must not launch a parallel verifier or successor.\nRelated: P-006\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/abolish-human-review-agent-review-only-2026-08-02 (\"Abolish human review — agents review, Blender-style\"): no plan update since 2026-08-25 (46 days idle), 6/8 items terminal, 2 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"cdn-egress-fixes-2026-08-02","title":"Eliminate runtime public-CDN dependencies (the vditor class) — 6 remaining instances","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Eliminate runtime public-CDN dependencies (the vditor class) — 6 remaining instances\nslug: cdn-egress-fixes-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all 7 items terminal, verified at RUNTIME (D-004: a bundle grep cannot decide this class; every fix overrides behaviour at runtime, so the CDN strings survive in the bundle either way). FIXED + VERIFIED: P-001 Monaco (local /monaco/vs/* incl. all 4 workers, mirror 151/151), P-002 PlantUML (end-to-end probe: block rendered, class neutralized 1/raw 0, zero <object>, zero plantuml.com requests — the only content-egress finding), P-003 Porcupine (vendored, immutable-sha + sha256 pinned and matching, served HTTP 200, NEW guard test porcupine-cdn.test.ts 6/6 negative-controlled; live wake-word NOT exercised — needs mic + access key), P-004 Excalidraw (asset path active, esm.sh=0, mirror complete 300/301 zero missing so the unconditional fallback is unreachable). PROVEN NOT LIVE, dropped: P-005 emoji-mart (bare-specifier import, Vite resolves at build time; picker loaded only local chunks) and P-006 speech-rule-engine (SRE is in vditor's MathJax bundle, we pin KaTeX; real math rendered katexNodes=4 mathjaxNodes=0, zero mathmaps requests). Non-local fetches across every surface exercised: 0. Both scratch probe plans archived.\n\n**Next:** Nothing on this plan — it is drained. Follow-ups live as their own items: EI-19369470572700441 (major: verify-tauri-headless.sh bypasses the WI-7101 target-dir claim) and EI-19370965762703309 (minor: extend the every-entry-point invariant to math.engine). Next work is the sibling plan egress-monitor-origin-axis-2026-08-02.\n\n## Background\n\nAudit 2026-08-02 (su-b9269) of the BUILT operator bundle found 6 runtime dependencies on\npublic CDNs — the same class as the vditor/unpkg 4.9 MB bug fixed under WI-7088.\n\n**The method that found them, and why the obvious one fails.** Grep the BUILT bundle,\nnot the source. `unpkg.com` appears NOWHERE in our source — it is a default baked inside\nvditor. A source grep over `apps/**` therefore returns a clean bill of health and you\nconclude you are fine. `apps/operator-vite/dist` contains our code PLUS every\ndependency's baked-in default, and is the only artifact in which this class is visible\nat all. That single shift surfaced all 6 in about two minutes with no app running.\n\nClassify by CONTEXT, not by origin: the bundle carries 193 external origins, but the\noverwhelming majority are license headers, the docs site folded into `dist/`, and ajv\n`$ref` schema IDENTIFIERS (never fetched). Only 6 sit in a fetch/src/path position.\n\n**Ruled out as clean:** no external fonts (no `@import`/`@font-face` hitting the\nnetwork), no external `<script>`/`<link>` in `index.html`.\n\n**Root cause that lets the class exist at all:** `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`\ncarries `\"csp\": null` + `dangerousDisableAssetCspModification: true` — the desktop app\nships with NO Content Security Policy, so nothing structurally prevents any of it.\nPrevention + detection are the sibling plan `egress-monitor-origin-axis-2026-08-02`;\nTHIS plan fixes the 6 known instances.\n\n**Precedent to follow exactly:** WI-7088's vditor fix — a gitignored/generated runtime\nmirror under the publicDir populated by a `prebuild` script, a single constant for the\nbase path, and a source-level guard test (`apps/operator/app/_components/vditor-cdn.test.ts`)\nthat fails when a new call site forgets the option. Reuse that shape; do not invent a\nsecond one.\n\n## Phase 1 — the six fixes\n\n- **P-001** `done` Monaco: mirror `node_modules/monaco-editor/min/vs` into the publicDir and call `loader.config({ paths: { vs } })` once, before any editor mounts; add a guard test mirroring `vditor-cdn.test.ts`. `@monaco-editor/loader` defaults to `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/monaco-editor@0.55.1/min/vs` and `loader.config` appears in ZERO files. Live in the Gym dashboard, harness Plugins section and the dev SQL tab. ~4 MB core (editor chunk 2.3 MB + toggleHighContrast 1.2 MB + editor.main.css 342 KB), ~11 MB once the TypeScript worker loads. ALSO a correctness bug: we install 0.56.0 and run 0.55.1 at runtime — mirroring fixes both. importance: high — note: Mirror + loader.config + guard test landed; 8/8 tests pass, typecheck clean. Also fixed a latent bug in the INHERITED stripComments helper (now shared strip-js-comments.ts).\n- **P-002** `done` PlantUML: stop vditor shipping document content to plantuml.com. `plantumlRender(element, cdn)` ACCEPTS a cdn arg and its body IGNORES it, hardcoding `https://www.plantuml.com/plantuml/svg/~1` + `plantumlEncoder.encode(source)` (public/vditor/dist/index.js:3897 signature vs :3915 body) — so the WI-7088 `cdn` fix does NOT close this. The diagram SOURCE is encoded into the URL and rendered by a third party: this is egress of user content, not a latency bug. Zero plantuml blocks exist in our content today, so failing closed costs nothing. importance: high — note: Intercepted in vditor's transform hook (runs before plantumlRender in both render paths), so the &lt;object&gt; is never created. 24/24 tests green incl. the existing MarkdownEditor suite.\n- **P-003** `done` Porcupine wake-word: serve the model locally instead of `raw.githubusercontent.com/Picovoice/porcupine/master/lib/common/porcupine_params.pv` (packages/operator-core/lib/voice-engines/porcupine.ts:48). This one is OUR code, not a library default — and it is not even a CDN: an unpinned `master` ref on a source host with rate limits and no availability guarantee. No `.pv` ships in node_modules, so the mirror script fetches it once at setup time (build-time, never runtime) into the gitignored publicDir mirror. importance: high — note: P-003: model vendored at setup time, pinned by commit sha + sha256 (verified byte-identical to what master serves today, so zero behaviour change); publicPath now /porcupine/. P-004: 18MB dist/prod mirrored + window.EXCALIDRAW_ASSET_PATH set. Both wired into postinstall + prebuild + gitignore.\n- **P-004** `done` Excalidraw: set `window.EXCALIDRAW_ASSET_PATH` and mirror `node_modules/@excalidraw/excalidraw/dist/prod/` (fonts, locales, data) into the publicDir. Bundle carries `ASSETS_FALLBACK_URL = https://esm.sh/@excalidraw/excalidraw@<ver>/dist/prod/` and `EXCALIDRAW_ASSET_PATH` is set in ZERO files. Live at apps/operator/app/harness/brainstorm/CanvasView.tsx. Also audit the export-to-link affordances in the same pass — `json.excalidraw.com/api/v2/post/` UPLOADS the drawing to Excalidraw's servers, and `libraries.excalidraw.com`. importance: high — note: P-003: model vendored at setup time, pinned by commit sha + sha256 (verified byte-identical to what master serves today, so zero behaviour change); publicPath now /porcupine/. P-004: 18MB dist/prod mirrored + window.EXCALIDRAW_ASSET_PATH set. Both wired into postinstall + prebuild + gitignore.\n- **P-005** `dropped` emoji-mart via BlockNote: CONFIRM LIVENESS FIRST, then fix if live. Bundle carries `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@emoji-mart/data@latest/...` (unpinned `@latest` — no immutable caching, silent upstream drift) plus per-emoji PNGs from `emoji-datasource@15.0.1`. `@emoji-mart/data@1.2.1` is already installed locally. Reached via @blocknote/core + @blocknote/react at brainstorm WriteView. Fires only if BlockNote does not pass local `data` — this is the one finding static analysis cannot settle, so settle it at runtime before changing anything. importance: medium — note: NOT LIVE — verified at runtime, no fix needed. The premise was wrong.\n- **P-006** `dropped` speech-rule-engine: `sre.Variables.url = cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/speech-rule-engine@<ver>/lib/mathmaps` lives INSIDE the vditor tree we now mirror locally — mirroring a package does not fix URLs baked inside it. Only fires on MathJax accessibility paths. Fix if cheap, otherwise record as an accepted, documented residual with the reason. importance: low — note: NOT LIVE — verified at runtime with real math. Dead code inside the MathJax bundle we never load.\n\n## Phase 2 — verification\n\n- **P-007** `done` Verify every fix at RUNTIME in a headless Tauri instance under Xvfb driven by tauri-agent-tools, reading `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` for non-local origins. Static proof that a URL left the bundle is not proof the app stopped requesting it. blocked-by: P-001 — note: All six findings resolved at runtime: 4 fixed + verified, 2 proven not-live.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Mirror locally rather than bundle through Vite\n\nEach of these libraries resolves its assets from a configurable base at RUNTIME (an AMD\nloader path, an `options.cdn`, a `publicPath`, a global asset path). Re-bundling them\nthrough Vite would mean fighting each library's own loader and, for Monaco, its worker\nbuild. Mirroring the vendor's own dist tree into the publicDir and pointing the library's\nexisting base-path option at it is the smaller, more reversible change — and it is\nexactly the shape WI-7088 already proved on vditor.\n\n### D-002 Mirror the WHOLE vendor dist, not the measured subset\n\nWI-7088's reasoning applies unchanged: the files one screen happens to request are not\nthe files every screen requests. These libraries lazily pull additional assets the moment\ncontent demands them (a language grammar, a font, a diagram renderer). A partial mirror\nconverts \"slow\" into \"404 — renders nothing\" for exactly those paths: strictly worse than\nthe bug being fixed.\n\n### D-003 Fail CLOSED on PlantUML\n\nThe PlantUML path is content egress, not latency, and the `cdn` option is a decoy that\ncannot redirect it. With zero plantuml blocks in our content there is no user-visible\nloss from disabling it, so the correct default is off. Re-enabling later requires a\nself-hosted renderer, not a config flip.\n\n### D-004 — Only a RUNTIME resource-timing read can verify this class — never a bundle grep\nDate: 2026-08-02\nEstablished while executing P-007, and it governs every remaining item on this plan.\n\nEach of the six findings is a library DEFAULT string. That string survives in the built bundle whether or not the fix works, because every fix here overrides behaviour at RUNTIME rather than removing the string: Monaco's loader default is overridden by loader.config; vditor's plantuml URL is bypassed by renaming the class the adapter selects; Excalidraw's ASSETS_FALLBACK_URL is appended unconditionally and simply never reached; emoji-mart's URL builders are for sets we do not select.\n\nMeasured on the served bundle AFTER all four fixes were verified working: cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/monaco-editor@0.55.1/min/vs still appears (2 files), plantuml.com still appears (1), raw.githubusercontent.com/Picovoice still appears (1), and @emoji-mart/data@latest still appears (1). A grep therefore reports FOUR live CDN dependencies on a codebase where all four are provably dead. The inverse is equally possible — a fix that regresses leaves the bundle byte-identical.\n\nSo: do not let a future agent 'confirm' any item here by grepping the bundle, and do not treat a surviving string as a regression. The verdict is performance.getEntriesByType('resource') filtered to non-local origins, read from a live desktop instance while the relevant surface is actually mounted.\n\nTwo corollaries earned the hard way. (1) Mounting matters more than navigating: a baseline read of /adv shows 0 non-local fetches, which proves nothing at all until the library in question has actually loaded — the tell for a route that did not really mount is a FLAT resource count, not the pathname, which can read correctly while a flag gate silently rendered the shell instead. (2) For a fix whose fallback is appended unconditionally (Excalidraw), 'no fetch observed' is necessary but not sufficient, because an unexercised surface requests nothing; there, also prove mirror COMPLETENESS against the source package (measured: 300 source files, 301 mirrored, zero missing) so the fallback cannot be reached even in principle.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"egress-monitor-origin-axis-2026-08-02","title":"Egress monitor: add the destination axis (foreign-origin), so the vditor class cannot recur unseen","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Egress monitor: add the destination axis (foreign-origin), so the vditor class cannot recur unseen\nslug: egress-monitor-origin-axis-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all 7 items terminal, all three legs of D-003 now shipped. Phase 1 (P-001..P-003): the foreignOrigin axis runs in classifyEgress BEFORE the same-origin narrowing that used to discard the class. Phase 2: P-004 lint:no-cdn-egress (static bundle scan, 24-row classified baseline, negative-controlled); P-005 the RUNTIME leg — apps/operator/e2e/_egress.ts, an auto Playwright fixture that makes all 46 specs network-egress tests at zero authoring cost, reusing classifyEgress (D-001) rather than a second rule, with the silent-opt-out hole closed by a 9-test guard. Phase 3: P-007 the agent-insights doc; P-006 the PREVENTION leg — one shared LOCAL_ONLY_CSP constant served report-only by the vite dev server and the SPA host, plus a securitypolicyviolation listener as a second sensor with different blind spots from resource timing. VERIFIED, not asserted: the fixture FAILS on a real foreign-origin fetch naming the exact URL (and the in-page monitor agreed independently); :3055 live-returns the expected CSP header with the dev shell unaffected; the 50 failing e2e specs are PRE-EXISTING, proven by a fixture-bypassed baseline whose failure set is byte-identical.\n\n**Next:** Nothing on this plan — drained. Two follow-ups live as their own items: EI-19374608033400911 (the report-only CSP is not yet on the packaged papercusp:// path — the shipping target; deferred only because two live `tauri dev` instances made a src-tauri edit a WI-7101 desktop-crash risk) and EI-19373923898562595 (the e2e suite is ~19% red pre-existing, which also means those 50 tests are not being egress-audited, since the fixture skips its assertion on an already-failing test). Also still open from P-004's scan: WI-7115/7116/7117/7118, all bundle DISCOVERIES whose liveness is unverified per D-004 — the P-005 fixture is now the tool to settle them.\n\n## Background\n\nSibling plan: `cdn-egress-fixes-2026-08-02` fixes the 6 KNOWN instances. This plan\nchanges the DETECTOR so the class cannot recur unseen. No file overlap.\n\nWe already have a live, well-built webview egress monitor:\n`libs/generic/desktop-ipc/src/egress-monitor.ts`, installed at\n`desktop-bootstrap.ts:192` in every shell, exposed at `window.__papercusp_egress__`,\nalready asserted by an admin test suite. It got the hard parts right, and those parts\nmust be PRESERVED, not rebuilt:\n\n- **Resource timing, not a fetch counter.** A `fetch` wrapper would have missed every\n  finding in the sibling plan: PlantUML is an `<object data=…>`, Monaco arrives via an\n  AMD-loader `<script>`, emoji are `<img>`. The file's own header says it: it sees\n  requests \"made by code that never went through our polyfill… which a fetch-level\n  counter cannot see by construction.\"\n- **`buffered: true`** — replays entries recorded BEFORE the monitor installed, which is\n  where the known offenders live.\n- **Wraps `WebSocket` / `EventSource`** — measured to produce no resource-timing entry\n  at all, so a wrapper is the only way to see them.\n- **A three-valued verdict** — `unknown` is a FAILURE, not a pass, gated behind a\n  proof-of-life control request. A dead detector and a clean run both report zero.\n\n**Why it did not catch the vditor class — two lines.**\n\n    const API_PREFIX = '/api/';                              // :174\n    if (restrictTo && url.origin !== restrictTo) continue;   // :243\n    if (!path.startsWith(API_PREFIX)) continue;              // :248\n\nFor `https://unpkg.com/vditor@3.11.2/dist/js/lute/lute.min.js`: in the DEV shell\n(document origin `http://127.0.0.1:3270`) line 243 discards it as not-our-origin; in the\nPACKAGED shell (`papercusp://`, so no origin filter applies) line 248 discards it because\nthe path is not `/api/`. Blind in both, and not by accident.\n\nIt audits a **transport** invariant — *an `/api/*` call must travel over IPC, never HTTP*\n(no-http-anywhere D-005). What this class needs is a **destination** invariant — *no\nrequest may go to a host we do not own*. Same sensor, orthogonal rule. The monitor\nfilters out the entire class as its FIRST act, precisely because those requests are\nsomeone else's API.\n\n**What no runtime watcher can see**, hence P-004: code that never ran. Monaco was\ninvisible to any monitor until someone opened the Gym. The static bundle scan is a\nCOMPLEMENT to this plan, not an alternative.\n\n## Phase 1 — the rule\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add a `foreignOrigin` rule to `classifyEgress`: any entry whose origin is not in a local allowlist (localhost / 127.0.0.1 / the custom scheme / our own API hosts) is a finding REGARDLESS of path. `classifyEgress` is already a pure entries→report function, unit-testable without a browser — extend it there, with unit tests for both shells (http origin AND custom scheme). importance: high — note: foreignOrigin axis added to classifyEgress (runs BEFORE the same-origin narrowing that used to discard it); axes kept separate with independent 3-valued verdicts + per-ORIGIN rollup; loud in every shell (does not inherit expectsIpc suppression). 52/52 tests incl. 10 new regression tests using the real audit URLs, asserted under BOTH document origins. tsc -p libs/generic/desktop-ipc = 0.\n- **P-002** `done` Keep the two axes SEPARATE in the report (`ipcEscape` vs `foreignOrigin`) — they have different owners and different fixes, and collapsing them into one number destroys the triage signal that makes either useful. Preserve the three-valued verdict on the new axis: a zero from an unproven sensor stays `unknown`. importance: high — note: foreignOrigin axis added to classifyEgress (runs BEFORE the same-origin narrowing that used to discard it); axes kept separate with independent 3-valued verdicts + per-ORIGIN rollup; loud in every shell (does not inherit expectsIpc suppression). 52/52 tests incl. 10 new regression tests using the real audit URLs, asserted under BOTH document origins. tsc -p libs/generic/desktop-ipc = 0.\n- **P-003** `done` Make it loud in EVERY shell. The existing `onEgress` hook returns early unless `expectsIpc` (correct for the transport axis — HTTP is sanctioned in a browser). A foreign-origin hit is a bug in every shell, so it must not inherit that suppression. importance: high — note: foreignOrigin axis added to classifyEgress (runs BEFORE the same-origin narrowing that used to discard it); axes kept separate with independent 3-valued verdicts + per-ORIGIN rollup; loud in every shell (does not inherit expectsIpc suppression). 52/52 tests incl. 10 new regression tests using the real audit URLs, asserted under BOTH document origins. tsc -p libs/generic/desktop-ipc = 0.\n\n## Phase 2 — make it an actual watcher\n\n- **P-004** `done` Static bundle scan as a lint (`lint:no-cdn-egress`) over the built dist with an explicit allowlist — the generalization of the per-library `vditor-cdn.test.ts` guard, which is the right idea scoped to one library and one option. This is the ONLY leg that catches code nobody exercised. Note ~90 `lint:*` guards exist and none covers network egress; the closest, `lint:bundle-budget`, guards bundle SIZE and is structurally blind here because the whole problem is that the payload LEFT the bundle. importance: high — note: lint:no-cdn-egress shipped: scripts/check-no-cdn-egress.mjs + baseline (24 rows, all classified: 13 unresolved/7 inert/4 not-live-verified) + npm scripts + CI step + 5 unit tests. Negative-controlled (injected URL = exit 1; empty dir = SENSOR FAILURE). Discovered 4 egress candidates the original 6-finding audit missed: WI-7115/7116/7117/7118.\n- **P-005** `done` Wire the assertion into the e2e suite via a shared fixture, so all 46 existing specs (6 already reference egress) become network-egress tests at zero authoring cost. This is the automated, maintained form of \"click through the whole app watching the network\" — the coverage already exists and is already kept up to date. importance: high — note: ← WI-7122 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — prevention\n\n- **P-006** `done` CSP: `tauri.conf.json` currently has `\"csp\": null` + `dangerousDisableAssetCspModification: true`, i.e. the desktop app ships with NO policy — the structural reason this class can exist. Land `default-src 'self'` REPORT-ONLY first, listening on `securitypolicyviolation`, which doubles as a second sensor independent of resource timing (a useful cross-check: the two have different blind spots). Enforce only once the report-only stream is clean. importance: medium — note: ← WI-7128 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Write the agent-insights doc: how to audit for CDN egress in this repo (grep the BUILT bundle, not the source — the URL is not in our code), the three complementary legs, and the two-axis egress model. blocked-by: P-001 — note: agent-insights/auditing-cdn-egress-in-this-repo.mdx written. Leads with the D-004 boundary (a bundle hit is a DISCOVERY, never a verdict — two of six findings were false positives whose URLs are still in the bundle), then the three complementary legs, the two-axis monitor, the probe-plan liveness technique, and the two silent-pass traps. MDX compile + all 4 content lints green; docs mirror rebuilt (831 pages, page confirmed rendered).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Extend the existing monitor; do not build a second one\n\nReuse-first is a hard repo rule, and here it is also simply correct: the existing sensor\nalready solved the genuinely hard problems (initiator-agnostic observation, pre-install\nreplay, stream transports, and an honest three-valued verdict). The gap is one\nclassification rule, not an architecture. A second monitor would duplicate the sensor and\nthen disagree with it.\n\n### D-002 Detect on URL presence, never on byte counts\n\nCross-origin resources without `Timing-Allow-Origin` report `transferSize: 0`, so a\nbyte-budget assertion silently reads zero for exactly the worst offenders. That is this\nsame file's documented \"a zero and a blind sensor look identical\" trap reappearing on a\nnew axis. The finding is the URL.\n\n### D-003 The three legs are complementary, not alternatives\n\nStatic bundle scan catches unexercised code; the runtime monitor catches dynamically\nconstructed URLs and proves liveness; CSP prevents rather than observes. Each covers a\nblind spot the others structurally cannot. Shipping only one leaves a known hole.\n\n### D-004 — P-006 cannot be report-only via tauri.conf.json — Tauri emits only the enforcing header\nDate: 2026-08-02\nRecorded before implementing P-006, because it invalidates the mechanism the item assumes.\n\nP-006 is written as \"land `default-src 'self'` REPORT-ONLY\" in tauri.conf.json. That is not achievable there. Verified against the vendored crate source, not from memory:\n\n- `tauri-utils` config exposes exactly one field: `pub csp: Option<Csp>`. There is no report-only sibling.\n- Tauri 2.11.3 emits exactly one header name across its whole source tree: `Content-Security-Policy` (grep over tauri-2.11.3/src). The enforcing one.\n- `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` is header-only BY SPEC — browsers ignore it in a `<meta http-equiv>`.
