So the usual \"inject a meta tag into index.html\" escape hatch does not exist for report-only either.\n\nSo there are three real options, and the choice matters because the whole point of report-only is to learn what a policy WOULD break before it breaks it:\n\n1. Set the report-only header in the custom `papercusp://` protocol response (the app already owns that handler). Keeps report-only semantics; costs a Rust-side change.\n2. Ship an ENFORCING `csp` in tauri.conf.json. Simple and fully supported, but it BLOCKS on first violation in the shipped desktop app — the opposite of the staged rollout the item wanted, and a bad trade while WI-7115..7118 are still unverified for liveness.\n3. Defer the header and rely on the other two legs (P-004 static scan + P-005 runtime fixture) until the liveness questions are settled.\n\nPreference is (1): it preserves the item's intent. Note this does NOT weaken D-003 — CSP is still the only leg that PREVENTS rather than observes; only the delivery mechanism changed.\n\nAlso recorded: both `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` and `libs/papercusp/apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` currently ship `csp: null` + `dangerousDisableAssetCspModification: true`, and there is no CSP handling anywhere in the tree — so this is a greenfield add, not a tightening.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"false-premise-in-prescriptive-artifacts-2026-08-02","title":"The most-filed agent-confusion class is a false premise inside a PRESCRIPTIVE artifact — skipped so far because it had no obvious producer, but the claim event is one","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: The most-filed agent-confusion class is a false premise inside a PRESCRIPTIVE artifact — skipped so far because it had no obvious producer, but the claim event is one\nslug: false-premise-in-prescriptive-artifacts-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-03\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** **PLAN COMPLETE — all six items closed** (owner-directed 2026-08-02, AUTO, solo).\n\nP-001/P-002 put derived premise-checks on work-item + plan-item bodies, rendered at the claim event. P-003 investigated rather than re-proposed a twice-dropped idea (it had already shipped 40 min earlier). P-004 asserted CLAUDE.md's executable claims in CI, driving the real heavy-command gate as an oracle. P-005 added the diagnosis-cluster lane. P-006 was REFUTED by measurement.\n\nThe plan's own thesis held against itself **five times**: a premise stated in an item's text was refuted by measurement before it was built — P-001 twice, P-004 once (it named the wrong surface), P-005 three times (D-004), and P-006 entirely (D-005). The Background's opening premise was also retracted before reaching the owner. Every one was cheap to check and expensive to have built.\n\nFive decisions: **D-001** verify a prescription before emitting it (an allowlist of known-false cases is the anti-pattern). **D-002** derive premises from text the author already wrote — now measured: declared shape fields sit at 0.08%–8.8% fill. **D-003** a detector's SCOPE is a premise too; a zero result in an unmeasured artifact means UNSUPPORTED, not clean. **D-004** a recurring DIAGNOSIS is not a recurring TOPIC. **D-005** match the substrate's lifetime to the ERROR's lifetime.\n\nFiled en route: **EI-19393516222436864** (near-dup pass never runs at production scale while scope reports full coverage) and **EI-19389924161930888** (su prompt prescribes a gate-denied command).\n\n**Next:** Plan drained — nothing further here. The highest-value follow-on is EI-19393516222436864: this plan's own class sitting inside the clustering code, already diagnosed with an in-idiom fix proposed (add `nearDupPass: 'ran' | 'skipped-cost-gate'` to likelyDuplicatesScope; do NOT raise the 4,000 bound, it is load-bearing per WI-5820).\n\n## Background\n\n### Predecessor, and the correction it forced\n\n`agent-epistemics-2026-08-02` (SHIPPED, same day) closed six items: field-reliability metadata + tools that refuse (WI-7078), a first-class UNDECIDABLE record (WI-7105), the compact spill index (WI-7108), `coord:supersede` (WI-7109), `scheduler:preview_spec_delta` (WI-7113), the dispute detector (WI-7120).\n\nThe tempting story — \"agents file reflections and nothing ever happens\" — is therefore FALSE, and was retracted before it reached the owner. ~8k `EI-%` items have reached a terminal state. Drafting this plan on the un-checked version of that premise would have reproduced, in the plan ABOUT false premises, the exact defect it documents.\n\n### The real pattern\n\nNot \"nothing drains\" but **the lane drains selectively toward classes that have an obvious trigger point**, and the single most-filed class has been skipped because it appeared not to have one.\n\nMeasured 2026-08-02, `harness_shared.work_items` (harness `papercusp`, `EI-%`): 14,908 open / 4,934 resolved / 3,030 done / 543 dropped / 399 closed; open avg age 13.3d, oldest 06-04.\n\nA search on premise-shaped titles returns 15 OPEN items, filed by DIFFERENT agents, independently, all saying one thing:\n\n- `EI-19375905555183196` — \"THE PREMISE WAS THE BUG — the same shape recurred three times in one session\"\n- `EI-19342313216721918` + `EI-19342092196943323` — \"THE PLAN'S ITEM TEXT IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A SPEC — now 4-for-4\" (filed TWICE)\n- `EI-19342962352488161` — \"THE CARRY NOTE ITSELF PLANTED A FALSE PREMISE, AND I ALMOST BUILT A FIX ON IT\"\n- `EI-19372214294975623` — \"checkable in ten minutes, stood unexamined for six days, across four plan...\"\n- `EI-19366211923471677` — \"P-010's stated premise was PARTLY FALSE (the 7th on this plan)\"\n- `EI-19369955448231764` — \"P-005 WAS A FALSE PREMISE and the reasoning generalizes to the whole plan\"\n\nNone of the six shipped items addresses it. They address unreliable tool FIELDS, undecidable QUESTIONS, wrong BROADCASTS, spec DELTAS — every one of which has a crisp producer. A false premise sitting inside a work-item body has no event, which is why it kept being skipped despite being filed most.\n\n### Live confirmation from the filing session\n\nWI-7042's own body asserted \"there is no exported read helper for `harness_shared.p2p_work_offers`\" and prescribed writing a new PG module on it. False: `offer-store.ts` exports `getWorkOffer` + `listWorkOffers`. The premise came from grepping `projections/work-offers.ts` — the receive/apply leg. The error was SCOPE OF INFERENCE, not method. Catching it deleted the prescribed module before it was written; that was the FOURTH such self-correction in four consecutive wakes by one agent, and this plan's own retraction above was the fifth.\n\n### The producer that was there all along\n\n**The CLAIM event.** `scheduler:get_next` / `work_items:claim` already inline a plan's `planDecisions` at claim time — an established hook, firing exactly when an agent is about to act on the artifact, i.e. the moment before the cost is paid. That satisfies the predecessor's governing decision:\n\n> **D-001 (agent-epistemics-2026-08-02)** — the dispute detector's drafted trigger fired ZERO times in 14 days; the same no-producer defect that retired `facts:conflicts` (WI-6545/D-103). Re-key onto a substrate whose producer actually exists.\n\nApplied here: the claim event fires on every claim, and the premise class has 15 measured filings. Producer and demand are both demonstrated, not assumed.\n\n### The primitive also already exists\n\n`work_items:checkpoint` / `loop:checkpoint` already take `checks: [{ claim, recheck, verified }]`, where `verified` is deliberately an evidence STRING (not a boolean) and omitting it renders `? PREDICTED`. Correct design; wrong location. It guards state an agent CARRIES, not the premises an artifact PRESCRIBES.\n\n### The asymmetry that makes it cheap\n\nAn ABSENCE claim (\"there is no X\") is expensive to act on — you build X — and cheap to falsify — one grep. So absence claims are where a forced `recheck` pays most, and the `recheck` must record the SCOPE searched, since scope is where the inference actually broke.\n\n## Phase 1 — the premise class\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend `checks: [{claim, recheck, verified}]` from checkpoints to work-item and plan-item bodies: an artifact that PRESCRIBES an approach declares its load-bearing premises. Render at CLAIM time next to the existing `planDecisions` inline: \"rests on N premises, M unverified — recheck before building.\" Producer = the claim event. importance: high — note: ← WI-7220 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Special-case ABSENCE claims in P-001: a premise of the form \"there is no X / X does not exist\" REQUIRES a `recheck` naming the search AND its scope, because scope-of-inference is the measured failure mode, not method. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: evidenceNamesScope + enforceAbsenceScope: a scope-less declared absence premise is downgraded to PREDICTED and can no longer silence the derived row; 17/17, tsc EXIT=0\n- **P-003** `done` Find out WHY the `dev:pg_query` 0-row positive-control idea was DROPPED twice (`EI-19363764229273232`, `EI-19343277144265759`) before re-proposing it. Filed twice and dropped twice is evidence about the proposal, and re-filing blind would be this plan's own anti-pattern. Only then decide whether a 0-row scoped result should report the unscoped count. — note: NOT rejected — both were dropped as DUPLICATES of EI-19324633485547042, which shipped 23:02Z. Re-proposing would have duplicated shipped work. Generalized the fix instead: verify-before-prescribe, 104/104, tsc-clean.\n- **P-004** `done` Test the docs' executable claims: extract fenced commands / named npm scripts from CLAUDE.md and assert they resolve AND are permitted by the load-admission gate. Caught live today — the MANDATED `npx vitest run tools-md-sync` pre-commit check is refused under fleet load (`EI-19364889235428417`). Producer = CI.\n- **P-005** `done` Rank the reflection lane by CLUSTER, not by singleton: group open `EI-%` by diagnosis similarity and surface the count. \"Filed 15 times by 15 agents\" is a different and rankable signal from 15 minor singletons — and is exactly why this class stayed invisible while narrower ones shipped. — note: ← WI-7241 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Consider moving CLAUDE.md's inline \"this file used to say X — that was WRONG\" archaeology into TTL'd facts (deterministic delivery to whoever might still carry the stale rule), so the doc states only the current rule. The archaeology exists for a real reason; length is nonetheless itself a failure mode. Lowest confidence item here — measure reader cost before acting. — note: REFUTED by measurement — D-005. Archaeology stays in CLAUDE.md.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — A prescriptive artifact must VERIFY its prescription before emitting it — an allowlist of known-false cases is the anti-pattern, not the fix\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02. Established while executing P-003; governs P-001/P-002 and any future advisory, hint or prescription this codebase emits.\n\n#### What P-003 found\n\nThe two `dev:pg_query` filings were NOT rejected. Both were dropped as DUPLICATES of EI-19324633485547042 by agents who compared carefully and posted their unique findings as comments on the canonical item. That canonical item then shipped at 23:02Z tonight (pg-read-query.test.ts 95/95). Building the original proposal would have duplicated work completed ~40 minutes earlier.\n\nThis vindicates writing P-003 as an INVESTIGATION rather than a proposal. \"Filed twice and dropped twice\" read as evidence against the idea; it was actually evidence the idea had already been consolidated and actioned. Both readings are consistent with the status field, which is exactly why the status field alone could not settle it.\n\n#### The defect that survived the shipped fix\n\n`dev:pg_query`'s tenant-scope advisory infers a predicate from `information_schema`: the table HAS a `workspace_id` column, therefore scope by `workspace_id = <session workspace>`. That is a PREMISE, not an observation, and it is measured false on at least three unrelated tables:\n\n- `agent_facts` — `harness_slug` NULL for ~99.6% of rows (EI-18669912007336072)\n- `event_awaits` / `event_wake_deliveries` / `event_key_fires` — every row keyed the literal `'default'` (WI-6847: 0 rows returned against 32,152 and 37,756 real rows)\n- `test_runs` — CI rows env-stamped, NULL on both keys (EI-19324633485547042: 25,214 pass + 246 fail rows, all NULL)\n\nEach was handled by ADDING THE TABLE TO A HARDCODED LIST. That costs one agent-incident per table discovered and leaves every not-yet-discovered table armed. The code comment above `TENANT_SCOPE_OVERRIDES` already states the defect precisely — \"a column's PRESENCE in information_schema is not evidence it is POPULATED\" — so the knowledge was never missing. Only the check was.\n\nNote the direction of the failure. The advisory exists to stop you reading ANOTHER tenant's rows, which is wrong-but-visible. Applying it to these tables produces an EMPTY result, and a zero is never re-checked because it reads as \"no rows exist\" rather than \"your predicate is wrong\". A guardrail that manufactures confident false negatives is worse than no guardrail.\n\n#### The ruling\n\nWhen this codebase emits a prescription an agent is expected to ACT on — an advisory, a hint, a suggested predicate, a \"next action\", a work-item body prescribing an approach — it must either verify the prescription or mark it unverified. It must never assert an unchecked premise in the imperative voice.\n\nWhere verification is cheap, verify. The pg_query implementation is one bounded `EXISTS` per table asking the question the advisory was assuming the answer to.\n\nThree constraints, each learned from a real failure:\n\n1. **A refutation REPLACES the prescription, never annotates it.** Telling an agent to add a predicate AND that the predicate is wrong invites them to add it anyway.\n2. **Fail OPEN in every uncertain direction.** A probe error, a timeout, an unparseable relation, an empty table, an unresolved session workspace all restore the prior behaviour exactly. A guard against false-empty results must never become the reason a genuine warning stops firing.\n3. **Name the REAL key, not just the refusal.** \"Do not scope by X\" leaves the agent stuck; \"rows are keyed 'default'\" hands them the working query.\n\n#### Consequence for P-001/P-002\n\nThis is the same claim shape those items address, one layer down. P-001 makes a work-item's premises declarable and re-checkable at claim time; this decision says a tool's own emitted premises are under the identical obligation. Neither is satisfied by documenting the exception — an allowlist IS documentation of exceptions, and it is what this decision rejects.\n\n### D-002 — Premises must be DERIVED from the text the author already wrote, not declared by the author — a declaration field would have been filled in with the false premise\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02. Established while building P-001; governs P-002 and any future premise surface.\n\nP-001's item text says an artifact that prescribes an approach *declares* its load-bearing premises. Building it that way would have produced a field that never fires, for the reason the PREDECESSOR plan already recorded: agent-epistemics-2026-08-02 D-001 retired a dispute detector whose drafted trigger fired ZERO times in 14 days, and ruled that a mechanism must key onto a producer that ALREADY EXISTS.\n\nThe same test applied to a declared-premises field fails it. WI-7042 is the root incident, and its author BELIEVED the premise (\"there is no exported read helper for harness_shared.p2p_work_offers\"). A \"declare your premises\" field would have been left empty, or filled in with that same false premise stated just as confidently. A field only the already-careful fill in cannot catch the un-careful case it exists for.\n\nSo premises are DERIVED from the body text the author already wrote, at the claim event, which fires on every claim with no new authoring behaviour. A DECLARED premise still wins where present — and per D-001(a) a declared premise carrying EVIDENCE replaces the derived row rather than sitting beside it — but nothing depends on anyone declaring one.\n\nMEASURED BEFORE SHIPPING, as D-001 requires of any prescriptive artifact (31,090 papercusp work-item bodies):\n- 1,442 (4.6%) carry an absence-shaped claim — it fires on ~1 claim in 22, not on everything.\n- 1,431 of those 1,442 are in substantial bodies (>200 chars): the class concentrates in real prescriptions, not stubs.\n- Hand-read precision sample: the dominant FALSE POSITIVE is an absence phrase inside QUOTED TOOL OUTPUT (WI-7132 matched entirely within a backticked `column \"payload\" does not exist`). That single measurement is why stripNonProse() exists and runs first — without it the detector fires hardest on the best-evidenced items, inverting its own signal.\n\nScope note for P-002: the detector already classifies kind:\"absence\" and emits a recheck naming the SCOPE requirement, so P-002 has something to key on rather than re-deriving the classification. Where the subject is a pronoun (\"...and it does not exist\") the premise still fires but the recheck asks the reader to NAME the referent — D-001(c) requires naming the real answer where one is knowable, and saying so where it genuinely is not, rather than fabricating a search term.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-003 — A detector's SCOPE must be measured against the real artifact before it is chosen — and a zero result in an unmeasured artifact means UNSUPPORTED, not clean\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03. Established while building P-004; governs P-005 and any future detector this plan produces.\n\n#### P-004's own text named the wrong surface\n\nThe item says \"extract fenced commands / named npm scripts from CLAUDE.md\". Measured: the live instance it was written for — `cd packages/operator-core && npx vitest run tools-md-sync` — is an INLINE backticked span inside a numbered `**Run**` step at CLAUDE.md:1327. It is not in a fenced block. A fenced-only extractor, built exactly as specified, would have shipped green and missed the one case that motivated it.\n\nThis is the THIRD item in this plan whose text was corrected by measurement before the build (after P-001's two). The pattern is now consistent enough to name: an author writing a detector spec describes where they REMEMBER the instance being, and that memory is a premise like any other.\n\n#### Negation cues do not classify prose\n\nThe first classifier treated a command as proscribed when its line carried a negation cue (never/not/don't/⚠). Measured against the real CLAUDE.md it was wrong in BOTH directions:\n\n- FALSE PRESCRIBED: `git reset --hard HEAD` (inside the 🚨 do-not-run block), `git.pipelinePosition` (a state-cell name)\n- FALSE PROSCRIBED: `npm run install:safe`, `npm run lint:required-field-strands` (lines carrying \"cannot\" for unrelated reasons)\n\nDense prose says \"not\"/\"never\"/\"cannot\" constantly. Proximity carries almost no signal. What works is the inverse: WHITELIST the sites where the document genuinely prescribes (```bash fences, `**Run** \\`cmd\\`` imperatives, the prescribed column of a `| use | not |` table) and treat everything else as unknown → skipped. Measured: 109 command-shaped spans → 13 sites → 11 checkable, 11/11 genuine on inspection, live instance among them.\n\nThat is D-001 constraint 2 applied to a detector. A missed prescription costs nothing; a fabricated one reds a shared gate and trains readers to ignore the check.\n\n#### The ruling — the zero-result trap\n\nA detector calibrated to one artifact's voice does not generalise for free, and its failure to generalise is SILENT: it returns \"clean\", not \"unsupported\".\n\nMeasured: pointed at `apps/operator/prompts/pot-instances/papercup-pot.su.md`, this extractor finds ZERO prescriptions — not one it judged safe, zero it could see. That file prescribes declaratively (``docs don't hot-reload — \\`cd apps/operator-docs && npm run build\\` regenerates the served mirror``), naming no imperative before the span. It contains a REAL instance of the very defect (`npm run build` is refused by the same gate — filed EI-19389924161930888), so accepting that green would have been a confident all-clear over a known-bad line, in the artifact spliced into every su agent's prompt.\n\nSo, for every detector this plan ships:\n\n1. **Measure the site set against the target artifact before choosing it.** The spec's stated surface is a premise, not an observation.\n2. **Read `found: 0` on a non-trivial artifact as \"the voice is unsupported\"**, never as \"the artifact is clean\". Same shape as the `tsc -p .` trap CLAUDE.md documents: checked zero files, grep printed nothing, reads exactly like a pass.\n3. **Pin the limitation as a TEST, not a comment.** The boundary above is now `KNOWN LIMIT: a declarative prescription voice yields zero sites`, which also asserts the missed command really is gate-denied — so the miss cannot quietly become a case that \"would have passed anyway\".\n\nNote which leg travelled and which did not: the npm-run-resolution leg keys on command text alone and works on any document; only the gate-admission leg is voice-dependent. When a detector has legs of differing portability, say so per leg rather than per detector.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-004 — A recurring DIAGNOSIS is not a recurring TOPIC — every clustering key the lane owned measures topic, which is why the most-filed class was invisible to all of them\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03. Established while building P-005; governs P-006 and any future detector or ranking key this plan produces.\n\n#### The lane already clustered — by the wrong axis\n\nP-005's premise was that the reflection lane ranks by singleton. Measured, that is not quite right, and the correction matters. The lane HAS clustering: `findLikelyDuplicates` (quoted-error signature, exact title signature, token Jaccard), `signatureRecurrence`, and `recurrence-escalation` bumping severity at >=3. Every one of those keys measures TOPIC.\n\nThe most-filed agent-confusion class is topically DIVERSE BY CONSTRUCTION — it recurs precisely because it happens across unrelated subject matter. So it is not that the lane failed to cluster; it is that no key it owned could see this axis at all. Measured against 15,166 open EI-% rows (harness papercusp) on the seven members named in the Background:\n\n- lexical: 6 of 7 are SINGLETONS. The 7th clusters only via an incidental quoted string (`quote:import(\"@emoji-mart`) — a false merge on unrelated topic, not recognition.\n- title Jaccard: max 0.556, median 0.133, ZERO pairs at the 0.8 bar. Zero pairs share a quoted signature.\n- stored-embedding cosine (96.5% of the corpus carries a gemma vector): 0.41-0.64, against a random-pair baseline of p50 0.361 / p95 0.531 / p99 0.641 (n=79,800). The `digest-embed-cluster-leg` threshold of 0.92 catches NONE — including the pair that is literally the same observation filed twice (0.829). No threshold rescues it: at 0.64 roughly 1% of all pairs merge.\n\nThat last result is the load-bearing one, because \"just use the embedding leg\" is the first idea any reader has. Whole-text embeddings are dominated by subject matter, so they are the wrong instrument for a subject-diverse class. It is pinned as a test (`EMBEDDING_CANNOT_SEPARATE`) rather than left as prose.\n\n#### The key is ONE marked word, and every refinement made it worse\n\nThe first draft was a five-pattern regex requiring an asserted falsity term near the marked word — the shape P-004's D-003 would predict. Hand-reading its output and then re-measuring BOTH directions refuted it: tightening dropped `THE PREMISE WAS THE BUG` (the canonical member), `A WORK-ITEM'S OWN PREMISE IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE THING TO VERIFY`, and `SUSPECT THE PREMISE THEY SHARE`. Recall fell 7/7 -> 5/7 to remove almost nothing genuine.\n\nThe reason is a property of the REGISTER, not the pattern: in agent reflections \"premise\" is already a MARKED term — written almost only when flagging one as suspect. Hand-read precision on a 40-row deterministic sample of the bare word: 39/40 genuine. My own intuition that `premise is` read as neutral usage was simply wrong, and only measuring the dropped set caught it.\n\nGeneral rule: before engineering a discriminator, check whether the vocabulary is already marked in the corpus's register. Where it is, the simple key wins and every refinement is pure recall loss. The refuted tightening is pinned as a test.\n\n#### Rank by independent convergence — but exclude the ritual population STRUCTURALLY\n\nRow count is the wrong rank key: 67.8% of incumbent clusters (661/975) are one author re-filing. Distinct authors is the right axis — \"filed 15 times by 15 agents\" is the signal.\n\nBut distinct-authors alone does NOT demote ritual filings, which I assumed it would and then measured: the two largest incumbent clusters are 822 and 342 rows filed by 822 and 342 DISTINCT authors — every agent files its own coordination-health scorecard. They pass an author rank on their own merits and would top the lane forever. They are held out structurally (`observation.rubricRef` present, 1,326 rows / 1,208 authors), never by matching their title text — a title-text exclusion would silently eat a genuine diagnosis that merely mentions scorecards, which is asserted as a test.\n\n#### D-002 is now measured, not just argued\n\nD-002 ruled premises must be DERIVED from text the author already wrote, because a declared field is filled in only by the already-careful. This corpus measures that prediction: the declared shape fields are empty — `findingClass` on 12 of 15,169 rows (0.08%), `watchdogKey` on 49, and the author-declared `observation.kind` on 8.8%. A \"declare your diagnosis\" field would inherit exactly that fill rate.\n\n#### Consequence\n\nThe result on production data: one rankable line — filed 375x by 73 DIFFERENT agents over six weeks — where there were 375 invisible singletons. Reported alongside `unshaped` (13,465) so a small cluster count reads as \"the registry does not cover this corpus\", never \"this corpus has no recurring diagnoses\", per D-003.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-005 — P-006 REFUTED by measurement — do NOT move the correction-archaeology into TTL'd facts: a correction's lifetime is unbounded and a fact's is capped at 90 days\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03. Established while executing P-006, the plan's own lowest-confidence item. It is REFUTED, and the archaeology stays in CLAUDE.md.\n\n#### What P-006 proposed\n\nMove CLAUDE.md's inline \"this file used to say X — that was WRONG\" passages into TTL'd facts, for deterministic delivery to whoever might still carry the stale rule, leaving the doc stating only what is true now.\n\n#### The measured cost is real but small\n\n9 archaeology paragraphs, 8,695 chars = **8.7% of CLAUDE.md** (~2,174 tokens of ~24,881), spliced into every su prompt. Worth attention; not worth a structurally wrong substrate.\n\n#### Three independent structural refutations\n\n**1. LIFETIME — the decisive one.** `FACT_DEFAULT_TTL_SEC` is 7 days; the ceiling is 90 days even for the longest-lived `wall` slot. But the reader an archaeology block targets is one who still carries the stale rule, and THAT staleness has no expiry: it arrives via a compaction carry, a mem0 recall, a months-old habit, or a fresh model prior. A correction must live at least as long as the error it corrects. 7 days is off by orders of magnitude and 90 is still a bound where the error has none.\n\n**2. CAPACITY.** `FACT_BODY_MAX_CHARS` is 1,200 and over-cap writes are silently CLIPPED, not rejected. 3 of the 9 blocks exceed it (1,942 / 1,477 / 1,471 chars). Clipping drops the TAIL, which in these blocks is the operative \"do this instead\" clause — precisely the failure EI-18681984560352579 was filed for. The move would convert three correct warnings into three truncated ones.\n\n**3. TARGETING.** Every fact scope except `workspace` requires a `scopeRef` and folds only for agents oriented in that scope. The archaeology's audience is \"anyone who might still carry the old rule\" — unscoped by nature. The doc is spliced unconditionally into every su prompt; that IS the deterministic delivery P-006 was reaching for, and facts would narrow it.\n\n#### Demonstrated live, this session\n\nThe carry note driving this very turn asserted that fact bodies store at ≤500 chars. The real cap is 1,200, raised by EI-18681984560352579 / migration 664. I carried a stale rule into the turn, and what corrected it was READING THE SOURCE — not a fact, which would have expired weeks earlier. The plan's own working state contained an instance of the class the plan is about, and the archaeology-style correction in the code comment is what caught it.\n\n#### The rule this generalizes to (per D-001: name the real key, don't just refuse)\n\n**Match the substrate's lifetime to the ERROR's lifetime, not to the writer's convenience.**\n\n- A TTL'd fact is right for a BOUNDED CONDITION whose expiry is real and whose silent disappearance is correct once it lapses: an owner wall, a current gate state, a temporary routing choice.\n- A permanent CORRECTION — \"the rule you may be carrying is wrong, here is the right one\" — belongs in the artifact that is delivered unconditionally and never expires.\n\nThey are not substitutes and neither is a cheaper version of the other. The archaeology earns its 8.7%: it is the only mechanism that reaches a reader whose staleness predates every TTL in the system.\n\nWhat MAY still be trimmed is narrative, not the correction: each block needs the stale rule named + the correct rule + why the stale one was seductive. The incident retelling around that can compress. That is an editing question, not a substrate question.\nRelated: P-006\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fed-drill-cross-machine-admission-probe-2026-08-02","title":"Cross-machine federation admission probe (WI-5211 drill payload)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cross-machine federation admission probe (WI-5211 drill payload)\nslug: fed-drill-cross-machine-admission-probe-2026-08-02\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Why this plan exists\n\nWork payload for the WI-5211 three-machine fleet drill. It is deliberately **not** busywork: its\nitems cannot be completed by one agent on one machine, because each item's input is another\nmachine's *output*. Coordination is forced by the data flow, not by instruction.\n\nIt also advances a live bug — **EI-19304844689981989**. As of 2026-08-02 03:40Z we know:\n\n- `p2p_work_offers` federation **works** from the mac (`Lm1ABoMRKVoo` / gh 1567022): a fresh\n  offer crossed to the tower in ~26s.\n- It has **not** worked from the Win VM (`zo+zgpk8fY0f` / gh 279242982) since ~Jul 19, even\n  though Win's `shared_presence` federates in real time over the same link and Win's donor-side\n  `substrate_outbox` shows capture+drain firing.\n- So the fault is a narrow **per-donor / per-table** intersection, and the leading hypothesis is\n  a **per-record admission mismatch** (`pot_slug` / `fleet_slug` / `audience` /\n  `record_version`), not a transport fault.\n\nThe fastest way to settle it is to have an agent **on each donor machine** emit a record while an\nagent **on the receiver** reports what arrived. That is what this plan does.\n\n## Coordination contract\n\nEvery item names the machine it must run on and the peer it hands off to. An item is not done\nuntil its successor has *confirmed receipt of its output* — a member that finishes and goes quiet\nhas not finished. Hand off with `coord:send`; park on the peer's event (`events:await`) rather\nthan polling.\n\n## Ground rules (each has already cost someone hours)\n\n- Verify federation claims **by data** (a row with a fresh `fed_ts`), never by a log line — a\n  `peer_connected` line is emitted for signalling-only links with no data path.\n- Do **not** reason from the `origin` column: `stamp_local_federated_write` rewrites it to\n  `'local'` on any local content update. Use **signer identity + `fed_ts`**.\n- `resource:delegate` republishes **only on a substantive change** — an identical re-run returns\n  `ok:true` and republishes nothing. Always change the count.\n- Never restart the tower (EI-13317). The mac has a boot script; see the runbook\n  `agent-insights/swarm-link-severed-restart-the-wedged-side`.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nP-001 is the entry point and runs on the **mac**. P-002 cannot start until P-001 reports its\nemitted offer id, so the handoff is real rather than ceremonial.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Phase 1 — Cross-machine admission probe\n\n- **P-001** `todo` **[runs on: MAC]** Emit a fresh donor seat-offer from the mac and publish its full identity to the fleet. Use `resource:delegate { fleetSlug:'fed-drill', kind:'agent_slot', hive:'papercusp', count:<a NEW value, different from the current one> }` — an identical re-run republishes NOTHING and returns ok:true anyway. Then read your OWN harness_shared.p2p_work_offers row and report to the fleet via coord:send: offerId, signer_device_pubkey, publisher_github_user_id, fleet_slug, pot_slug, audience, record_version, fed_ts. NOT done until P-003 confirms it received these fields. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` **[runs on: WIN VM]** Emit the SAME-SHAPED donor seat-offer from the Win VM (resource:delegate, same args, a NEW count) and report the SAME field list to the fleet. Expect this to be the FAILING donor (EI-19304844689981989) — its record is interesting precisely because it does not arrive. Also capture donor-side proof it left: the substrate_outbox row for p2p_work_offers (n, drained_at). NOT done until P-003 confirms receipt of your fields. importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` **[runs on: TOWER (receiver)]** You cannot start until BOTH donors have reported their offerIds — your job is to say what arrived for each. For each reported offerId, query the tower's harness_shared.p2p_work_offers and report arrival BY DATA (row present + fresh fed_ts), never from a log line. Do NOT reason from the `origin` column — it is rewritten to 'local' on any local update; discriminate on signer_device_pubkey + fed_ts. Report per donor: arrived yes/no, fed_ts, and lag from that donor's emit time. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` **[runs on: TOWER]** Diff the two donors' records field-by-field (fleet_slug, pot_slug, audience, record_version, publisher_github_user_id, signer_device_pubkey) and name the single field that differs between the donor that ARRIVES and the one that does NOT. That field is the admission-mismatch candidate for EI-19304844689981989. Post the finding as a comment on EI-19304844689981989 with the evidence table, and record any cross-lane ruling as a plan Decision (plans:add-decision). blocked-by: P-003 importance: high\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Not real work.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"local-reranker-gte-modernbert-2026-08-02","title":"Local ONNX cross-encoder reranking via gte-reranker-modernbert-base (replaces the dark ZeroEntropy seam)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Local ONNX cross-encoder reranking via gte-reranker-modernbert-base (replaces the dark ZeroEntropy seam)\nslug: local-reranker-gte-modernbert-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — 12/12. P-012 verified live 2026-08-02 23:15-23:40Z in an ISOLATED Tauri shell (scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh --boot-only: own Xvfb :91, own devUrl :33710, own operator sidecar, own cargo target slot). The owner's :0 window and the 7-day-old :3270 stack were never driven — note that a bare `tauri-agent-tools probe` defaults to the OWNER'S bridge, so every call was --pid-targeted.\n\nPRECONDITION CLEARED: dev:restart{embed-sidecar} took the running sidecar from a 16.9-day-old build (pid 2034810) to pid 116595. /healthz capabilities now ['GET /healthz','POST /embed','POST /rerank'] and rerankExecution reports {device:cpu, dtype:q8} — D-006's active-pair reporting working as designed.\n\nEVIDENCE (all falsifiable, all bound to the real /api/user/search path driven from inside the window):\n- INVOCATION: sidecar CPU delta measured across a SINGLE request = 4170ms CPU / ~1.3s wall (~3.2 ORT threads). Rerank is genuinely called on the user-facing path, not bypassed.\n- ORDERING CHANGES: 3 of 4 queries returned hits whose RRF `rank` is NOT monotonically descending — a lower-RRF hit was promoted above a higher-RRF one, which only the cross-encoder can cause. The 4th query is the documented single-bucket case where the qualityScore tiebreak deliberately preserves RRF order.\n- LATENCY: 24 candidates = 1316ms (54.9 ms/pair), reproducing P-009's 52 ms/pair and comfortably inside PROSE_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS (4000ms). Whole search 3.4-4.5s end-to-end at box load ~96.\n- Per D-006, NO GPU figure is reported.\n\n**Next:** Nothing — plan complete. Two verification traps worth carrying: (1) `rank` in the /api/user/search response is the RRF score carried through untouched, NOT the rerank score, so it can never be used to check rerank ordering directly; test RRF-monotonicity instead. (2) Recomputing rerank scores externally cannot settle ordering — bucketing is round(score*20), so a 0.9026 lands in bucket 18 while 19 needs >=0.925, and any small text-reconstruction difference flips the bucket. I nearly filed a false \"rerank is discarded\" defect on exactly that before catching it.\n\n## Background\n\n`rerankProseHits` (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/search/rerank.ts`) is an\nEXISTING Stage-B seam over `@papercusp/search`'s RRF-fused output, already called\nfrom three places:\n- `agent-tools/search/semantic.ts:113` (`search:semantic`)\n- `agent-tools/search/fulltext.ts:101` (`search:fulltext`)\n- `endpoint-route/routes/user/search.ts:82` (the user-facing search route)\n\nIt has NEVER EXECUTED. It requires a ZeroEntropy API key; `operator_credentials`\nhas `zeroentropy_api_key: null` and the operator env has no `ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY`,\nso every call has returned RRF order unchanged. Owner constraint (2026-08-01): the\nreplacement must be free.\n\nMODEL: `Alibaba-NLP/gte-reranker-modernbert-base` — 149M params,\n`ModernBertForSequenceClassification` (an ENCODER cross-encoder, not a decoder LLM\nscoring yes/no logits), Apache-2.0, 8192 token context, native ONNX with documented\nTransformers.js dtypes (fp32/fp16/q8/q4/q4f16), BEIR avg 56.73, CoIR code avg 79.99.\nIt ties Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B on BEIR (56.94) at a quarter of the parameters, and it\nis the only strong candidate with first-class Transformers.js support. Tradeoff\naccepted: ENGLISH-ONLY (the corpus is English code + engineering prose).\n\nINFRASTRUCTURE ALREADY PRESENT — this is an extension, not a new surface:\n- `@huggingface/transformers` ^4.2.0 is a real dependency (apps/operator + operator-core)\n- `embedViaWorker` — a generalized worker-thread ONNX seam already carrying three models\n- `papercup-embed-sidecar.service` on :3384 (`memory/embed-sidecar-server.ts`, plain\n  node:http, currently exactly two routes: `POST /embed`, `GET /healthz`)\n- `libs/generic/rerank` — already documents itself as \"engine-agnostic cross-encoder\n  reranking\"; it simply has only one engine (ZeroEntropy) today. Add a LOCAL engine\n  behind the same `RerankDoc`/`RerankOptions`/`RerankResult` interface rather than\n  forking a parallel lib.\n\nTWO THINGS MATTER MORE THAN THE MODEL:\n1. Today the rerank runs on the ALREADY-SLICED page, so it can only reorder — never\n   rescue a buried hit. Over-fetching is what makes any reranker worth having, and\n   it is free. Phase 1 lands it before the model exists.\n2. Quantization hurts CALIBRATION more than ORDERING. No GPU figure per D-006.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Adopt gte-reranker-modernbert-base, but CAP candidates and keep the model host-selectable; drop mxbai-xsmall\nDate: 2026-08-02\nP-001 spike MEASURED on this box (2026-08-01), all models q8, identical pairs, pinned to 4 cores (taskset 0-3, OMP/ORT_NUM_THREADS=4) to simulate a laptop:\n\n| model | params | arch | n=20 | n=50 | n=100 | per-pair | RSS |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Alibaba-NLP/gte-reranker-modernbert-base | 149M | ModernBERT | 932ms | 2406ms | 4182ms | ~42-48ms | 1473MB |\n| mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-xsmall-v1 | 71M | DebertaV2 | 995ms | 2228ms | 3435ms | ~34-50ms | 971MB |\n| Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 | 23M | BERT-6L | 119ms | 378ms | 576ms | ~6-7.5ms | 615MB |\n\nALL THREE load and score correctly under the repo pinned @huggingface/transformers v4.2.0 in Node (CJS, transformers.node.cjs). All three ranked the single relevant doc first with a clear margin, so the runtime question is settled GREEN — ModernBERT works.\n\nFINDINGS THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN:\n1. CORES DO NOT HELP. gte on 4 pinned cores (~45ms/pair) is indistinguishable from gte on the full 128-core box under load 136 (~44-49ms/pair). So the box being saturated was NOT the confound, and adding cores will not rescue latency. ~45ms/pair is the real number.\n2. PARAM COUNT IS NOT COST. mxbai-xsmall is HALF gte parameters and NOT faster (DebertaV2 disentangled attention costs far more per param than ModernBERT). DROPPED as a fallback candidate - it is strictly dominated: same speed as gte, weaker quality.\n3. THE FAST TIER IS REAL. ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 is ~7.5x faster than gte (6ms vs 45ms per pair) at 23M/6-layer/384-hidden. Quality is 2021-baseline, but latency is imperceptible.\n4. PRODUCTION SHAPE IS SMALL. Both tool sites default to limit=5 (max 20), so realistic over-fetch is ~20 candidates, not 50. gte at 20 pairs = 932ms - acceptable for an agent tool call, marginal for the user-facing search route, and a laptop is ~1.5-2x slower again.\n5. q8 PRESERVES ORDER, COMPRESSES SCORES. gte fp32 top-vs-runner-up margin 4.73 vs q8 3.37; ordering identical. Confirms quantization costs CALIBRATION more than RANKING - so any admission threshold must be fitted on the DEPLOYED dtype.\n\nDECISION:\na) ADOPT Alibaba-NLP/gte-reranker-modernbert-base @ q8 as the default engine. It passes functionally; its BEIR 56.73 is worth ~1s on an agent tool call.\nb) The kill criterion (<=1.5s per 50 pairs) is FORMALLY MISSED at n=50 (2406ms) but is the WRONG GATE - n=50 never occurs in production. Re-gate on the real shape: <=1s at n=20, which gte MEETS (932ms). Recording rather than silently reinterpreting.\nc) CAP THE CANDIDATES. P-002 must use min(limit * OVERFETCH, RERANK_MAX_CANDIDATES) with a cap around 24, NOT a raw multiplier - otherwise limit=20 x 4 = 80 pairs = ~3.6s.\nd) MODEL IS HOST-SELECTABLE. ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 is the CPU/desktop fast tier; gte is the sidecar/GPU default. Same engine seam, different model id.\ne) DROP mxbai-rerank-xsmall-v1 from consideration entirely (finding 2).\nf) FOLLOW-UP: measure ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2 (12 layers) as the middle rung - likely ~2x MiniLM-L6 cost for meaningfully better quality.\n\n### D-002 — Rerank scores the MATCH-CENTRED text (highlight), never the head-of-doc excerpt\nDate: 2026-08-02\nP-003 investigated what `hit.excerpt` actually contains. Finding, from packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/search/sources.ts:\n\n- `const trunc = (s) => s.slice(0, 200) + (s.length > 200 ? \"…\" : \"\")`\n- every one of the surfaces maps `excerpt: trunc(body)` — i.e. THE FIRST 200 CHARACTERS of the document.\n- the MATCH-CENTRED text — `ts_headline(...)` with MaxFragments=2, MaxWords=18, wrapped in <mark> — is mapped to a SEPARATE `highlight` field.\n\nSo the pre-existing rerank seam scored `hit.excerpt`, which asks the cross-encoder \"is this document OPENING about the query?\" That is the wrong question for any document whose relevant passage is not in its first 200 chars — and it silently demotes precisely the long documents a reranker is most valuable for. It also fed ~200 chars to a model with an 8192-token context.\n\nDECISION: added `rerankText(hit)` in agent-tools/search/rerank.ts and routed the cross-encoder input through it.\n- Leads with the matched fragments, `<mark>`/`</mark>` stripped (markup is a rendering concern and is pure tokenizer noise to a cross-encoder).\n- Appends the head-of-doc excerpt for topical context when it adds anything.\n- De-duplicates when either field contains the other (the common short-document case).\n- Falls back to the excerpt when `highlight` is empty — the vector/semantic leg runs no ts_headline.\n- Costs ZERO extra retrieval: both fields are already on every SearchHit.\n\nThis is independent of which reranker model is chosen and applies to any future engine (incl. a self-hosted zerank-2).\n\n### D-003 — @papercusp/rerank must be \"type\":\"module\" — a re-export in a typeless lib silently empties the namespace for every ESM consumer, and neither tests nor tsc can see it\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\nItems: P-004\n\nP-004 split the lib into `index.ts` + `local-engine.ts` and re-exported the engine's surface:\n\n```ts\nexport { LOCAL_RERANKER_MODEL, scoreCrossEncoder, ... } from './local-engine';\n```\n\n`@papercusp/rerank` was TYPELESS (no `\"type\"` in package.json). Under tsx a typeless package's\n`.ts` is transpiled to CJS, and Node links named imports through **cjs-module-lexer**, which\ncannot see `export … from` re-export chains. The namespace links EMPTY and EVERY named import\nthrows:\n\n```\nSyntaxError: The requested module '.../rerank/src/index.ts'\ndoes not provide an export named 'LOCAL_RERANKER_MODEL'\n```\n\nThis is the recorded class in memory `1d389f25-509c-4db5-99b0-1a9ee17c5548`; the recorded fix\n(`\"type\": \"module\"` on the lib) is what landed, plus a `$comment_type` in package.json and a\nREADME warning so it is not silently reverted.\n\n**The part that matters for the rest of this plan: our normal verification could not see it.**\n\n| check | verdict while the bug was live |\n|---|---|\n| 4 affected vitest suites (rerank, local-engine, search-core, operator-core) | **51/51 green** |\n| `tsc --noEmit` on rerank AND search-core | **exit 0 both** |\n| `npx tsx` loading the real consumer chain | **threw** |\n\nvitest/vite BUNDLE (cross-module analysis, no lexer), so the whole documented loop reports\nclean. Only the tsx runtime — which is what serves `:3070` — hits it. And the breakage is not\nconfined to new code: `@papercusp/search-core` (ESM) named-imports `{ rerank }` and works today\nonly because `rerank` is a direct export the lexer can see, so the re-export would have broken a\ncall site P-004 never touched.\n\n**Consequences adopted:**\n\n1. P-005 (sidecar route) and P-007 (swapping `rerankProseHits`) both add operator-core→lib\n   imports under tsx. Green tests are NOT sufficient evidence for those items — each must also\n   be loaded under `npx tsx` before being called done.\n2. P-012's Tauri verification stays mandatory for the same reason: it exercises the real runtime\n   rather than a bundler's view of it.\n3. Filed EI-19306560664954248 (claimed) for the durable guard: lint a typeless workspace package\n   that has re-export chains and ESM consumers. Census: `libs/generic/*` is now 56 ESM / 3\n   typeless (git-graph, ui-primitives, papergrid), all three consumed only from bundled `.tsx`,\n   so they are latent rather than broken.\n\n### D-004 — The local rerank path needs the sidecar PROCESS restarted on post-P-005 code — a pre-P-005 sidecar 404s /rerank and every search silently degrades to retrieval order\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\nItems: P-007, P-008, P-012\n\nFound while verifying P-007 end-to-end. The sidecar is a LONG-RUNNING process, so it does not pick up P-005's new route when the code deploys — it picks it up when it RESTARTS. The box's live sidecar (127.0.0.1:3384, started well before P-005) answers:\n\n    POST /rerank -> {\"error\":\"no route POST /rerank\"}\n\nWhat that does to the new default path, in order: the client gets a 404 -> `isNonRetryableSidecarError` correctly classifies 4xx as permanent and does NOT retry -> it throws -> @papercusp/rerank's fail-safe seam converts the throw into 'keep retrieval order'. So search keeps working, correctly, and reranking simply never happens.\n\nWhy this is worth a decision rather than a note: EVERY layer behaves exactly as designed, so there is no failure anywhere to find. The flag is on, the code is deployed, the tests are green, search works — and Stage B is doing nothing. The only evidence is one `[sidecar-reranker] rerank sidecar rejected` line in the operator log. This is precisely the shape of thing that gets misdiagnosed as 'the model is weak' or 'the flag didn't take'.\n\nRULE for P-008 and P-012: before concluding anything about rerank quality or latency from a live search, confirm the sidecar serving this host actually has the route:\n\n    curl -s -X POST $PAPERCUSP_EMBED_SIDECAR_URL/rerank -H 'content-type: application/json' \\\n      -d '{\"model\":\"rerank\",\"query\":\"x\",\"texts\":[\"y\"]}'\n\nA `no route POST /rerank` reply means the sidecar predates P-005 — restart it, do not re-diagnose the reranker. A P-012 desktop verify is NOT subject to this (the Tauri shell spawns its own sidecar from the current tree); it is the long-lived shared box sidecar that goes stale.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-012\n\n### D-005 — Three nested rerank timeouts, ordered search(4s) < sidecar(15s) < lib backstop(20s) — a UX budget and a hang guard are different things and must not be collapsed\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\nItems: P-010\n\nP-010 asked for \"the whole rerank inside a timeout\". Implementing it surfaced that ONE timeout cannot serve both callers, because two unrelated failure modes were being conflated:\n\n- A HANG (a wedged in-process engine, a scorer that never settles) — must be bounded for ANY caller, including batch/offline ones, but bounding it aggressively is wrong.\n- A LATENCY CONTRACT (a user waiting on a search page) — must be bounded TIGHTLY, and the right value depends on the caller, which a generic library cannot know.\n\nDECISION — three nested bounds, each owned by the layer that has the information to set it:\n\n1. `PROSE_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS = 4_000` (operator-core search call site) — the UX budget. SIZED FROM D-001's MEASUREMENT, not guessed: RERANK_MAX_CANDIDATES(24) x ~45ms/pair = ~1.1s here, and P-001 found a laptop is ~1.5-2x slower => ~2.2s. 4s leaves ~1.8x headroom, so a HEALTHY rerank never trips it and only pathology does.\n2. `DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000` (unchanged, P-006) — the sidecar client's total retry budget.\n3. `DEFAULT_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000` (new, @papercusp/rerank) — the hang backstop.\n\nTHE ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING, in both directions:\n- The lib backstop sits ABOVE the sidecar budget deliberately. Had it been placed below, it would silently truncate P-006's retry policy and convert a RECOVERABLE sidecar blip into a permanent-looking degradation — re-introducing the exact invisibility P-006 was built to remove.\n- The search budget sits BELOW both deliberately. A budget above 15s would never bind (the sidecar gives up first), making it decorative.\nThe ordering is asserted by a test, so a later bump to any of the three must stay coherent rather than quietly inverting.\n\nMECHANISM: the timeout resolves the scores promise to `null`, which is ALREADY what both engines return when they cannot score — so it reuses the single fail-safe passthrough instead of adding a second degradation path. A timeout is therefore indistinguishable, downstream, from any other rerank outage: retrieval order, `reranked:false`, never a throw. The race loser is not cancellable (neither ONNX inference nor an in-flight fetch aborts here), so it runs to completion in the background, its result is discarded, and a LATE rejection is swallowed rather than surfacing as an unhandled rejection after we have already degraded.\n\nACCEPTED TRADEOFF (matters for P-012): an in-process COLD START — the first query in a fresh process loading a ~150M model — can exceed the 4s search budget, so that first search returns RRF order and later ones rerank normally. This is the correct failure direction: correct results slightly less well ordered, rather than a multi-second stall on someone's first search. It does not arise in the intended deployment, where the sidecar holds the model warm across processes. Do NOT \"fix\" this by raising the search budget — that trades every user's worst case for one cold query.\n\nVERIFIED: 25/25 rerank-lib + 24/24 consumer + 4/4 search-core; both libs tsc EXIT 0; and out-of-band under real tsx ESM linking (D-003) a scorer that NEVER settles returned in 201ms against a 200ms bound, while a healthy 20ms scorer still reranked.\nRelated: P-010, P-006, P-012\n\n### D-006 — dtype is a property of the DEVICE — select the (device, dtype) pair atomically, and prove a GPU by constructing a session, not by detecting a card\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\nItems: P-009\n\nP-009 asked for \"q8 on CPU/desktop, fp16 on the GPU host\" plus \"measure the q8-vs-fp32 ranking delta\". Measuring it turned a config knob into a correctness rule, because BOTH ways of splitting the pair are silent failures rather than slow ones.\n\n#### Measured (this box, 4 pinned cores: taskset -c 0-3, OMP/ORT_NUM_THREADS=4 — D-001's laptop-simulating idiom; box load 87-151; gte-reranker-modernbert-base, max_length 512, batch 16, 6 queries x 20 docs = 120 pairs per dtype)\n\n| dtype | per-pair | load | usable on CPU? |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| fp32 | 83.0 ms | 2511 ms | yes |\n| q8   | 52.0 ms |  782 ms | yes (**1.60x faster**; 1.58x on a repeat run) |\n| fp16 | — | — | **NO — no session at all** |\n\nq8 vs fp32 RANKING delta (fp32 = reference): **top-1 agreement 1.000** (6/6 queries — q8 never changed the top result), top-3 0.833, top-5 0.833, **NDCG@5 0.9855**, Kendall tau 0.805 full-list / 0.714 over the top-8.\n\n⚠ An expectation this DISPROVED, recorded because it changes how to read the numbers: I predicted q8's disagreement would sit in the irrelevant tail. It does not — head-8 tau (0.714) is LOWER than full-list tau (0.805). The full list is inflated by easy relevant-vs-irrelevant pairs both dtypes order identically; the real disagreement is INSIDE the page, among near-tied documents. It stays acceptable because the top result never moved and NDCG@5 is 0.986 (reordering near-equals is cheap), but the honest reason is \"near-ties reorder\", not \"only the tail reorders\".\n\n#### The two traps, both confirmed empirically\n\n1. **fp16 on the CPU provider does not construct a session.** Not a pessimization — an outright failure: `graph_utils.cc GetIndexFromName ... InsertedPrecisionFreeCast_/model/embeddings/norm/Constant_output_0 for node /model/embeddings/norm/Mul/SimplifiedLayerNormFusion/`. ORT's precision-free-cast insertion breaks ModernBERT's layernorm fusion.\n2. **A present GPU is not a usable GPU.** This box has an RTX 3090, CUDA 12, and ships `libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so` — and still cannot execute on it: `libcudnn.so.9: cannot open shared object file`. Every cheap capability probe (`nvidia-smi`, `/dev/nvidia*`) answers \"GPU available\" here and is WRONG.\n\nBecause `localEngineScores` is deliberately fail-safe (any throw → `null` → keep retrieval order), EITHER trap degrades search to unranked order **silently and permanently**. Same invisibility class as D-004.\n\n#### Decision\n\n- The selectable unit is a `RerankExecutionTarget` — a **(device, dtype) PAIR**. `cpu→q8`, `cuda→fp16`, `webgpu→fp16` (`libs/generic/rerank/src/execution-target.ts`). Defaulting resolves the whole pair; it never takes one field from the host and one from a constant.\n- **Every fallback moves BOTH fields.** A naive \"GPU failed, use the CPU\" retry that resets only `device` leaves fp16 on the CPU provider — precisely the one configuration that cannot load. A test asserts this and was mutation-verified to red when the fallback is weakened to device-only.\n- **GPU is opt-in AND verified.** `PAPERCUSP_RERANK_DEVICE=cuda|webgpu` opts in; the engine then proves it by CONSTRUCTING a session, and on failure demotes the whole pair to cpu/q8 — once per process (remembered, so a broken GPU host does not re-pay a multi-second failed load per search) and logged, so the demotion is visible rather than a silent quality loss. `activeExecutionTarget()` reports the real pair, not the requested one.\n- An unknown/misspelled env value resolves to the CPU pair rather than throwing: a typo in a deployment var must not be able to take search down.\n- **q8 stays the CPU default on measured grounds**, not assumed ones: 1.60x faster, ~4x smaller weights, top-1 unchanged, NDCG@5 0.986. fp32 buys back only near-tie ordering for +60% latency.\n\n#### Not verified here\n\nThe `cuda→fp16` pairing is DECLARED-correct, not measured — this box cannot load the CUDA provider (no cuDNN 9), so no GPU number in this plan is measured. Installing cuDNN 9 is tracked as EI-19320976824112874; until then P-012 must not report GPU figures, and (per D-004) still needs the sidecar bundle rebuilt.\nRelated: P-009, P-012\n\n### D-007 — CORRECTION to D-004: a plain systemctl restart DOES rebuild the sidecar bundle — the artifact is stale because the service has not restarted in 17 days, not because restarting re-serves it\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\nItems: P-012\n\nD-004 correctly concluded that P-012 is blocked (the :3384 sidecar serves a pre-P-005 bundle that 404s POST /rerank, so a P-012 run would measure RRF and report it as rerank). Its stated MECHANISM is wrong, and the wrong mechanism prescribes a much more expensive remedy than the situation needs — so correcting it is worth its own entry.\n\n#### What D-004 says\n\n\"The sidecar is a LONG-RUNNING process, so it does not pick up P-005's new route when the code deploys — it picks it up when it RESTARTS\", carried forward operationally as: *a restart alone re-serves the same stale artifact, so the BUNDLE must be rebuilt first.*\n\n#### What is actually true\n\nThe systemd unit rebuilds the bundle on every start:\n\n```\n# ~/.config/systemd/user/papercup-embed-sidecar.service\nWorkingDirectory=/home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp/apps/operator\nExecStartPre=/usr/bin/bash -c 'exec bin/bundle-host.sh bin/embed-sidecar.ts dist-sidecar/embed-sidecar.mjs'\nExecStart=/usr/bin/bash -c 'exec node dist-sidecar/embed-sidecar.mjs'\n```\n\nSo a restart re-runs esbuild against CURRENT source and WILL pick up P-005's route. The evidence that this is the real story rather than a caching quirk is that the process start time and the bundle mtime are the SAME instant:\n\n- running sidecar pid 2034810 `lstart` = **Thu Jul 16 20:11:48 2026**\n- `apps/operator/dist-sidecar/embed-sidecar.mjs` mtime = **2026-07-16 20:11:48**, 193800 bytes, `grep -c rerank` = **0**\n- live: `POST 127.0.0.1:3384/rerank` → **404**\n\nThat identity is the tell. The bundle is 17 days old because ExecStartPre last ran 17 days ago — i.e. **the service has simply not been restarted since before P-005 existed**. Nothing is re-serving a stale artifact past a rebuild; no rebuild has been attempted at all.\n\n#### Why the distinction matters\n\nUnder D-004's mechanism the next agent believes it must hand-rebuild the bundle (find bundle-host.sh, run esbuild correctly, land the artifact) and treats a restart as useless. Under the actual mechanism the remedy is one restart of `papercup-embed-sidecar.service`, and ExecStartPre does the build. A recorded-but-wrong mechanism is worse than no mechanism, because it is followed confidently.\n\nGeneral form, worth carrying past this plan: **\"the artifact is stale\" and \"the build step is broken\" are different diagnoses with different fixes, and process-start-time vs artifact-mtime distinguishes them in one command.** Equal timestamps mean the build ran at the last start and the process is simply old; an artifact OLDER than the process start means the build genuinely did not run or did not land.\n\n#### Standing\n\nD-004's CONCLUSION stands unchanged — P-012 must not run against the current :3384 process, and any rerank figure taken from it today is RRF wearing a rerank label. Only its remedy changes: restart the service (ExecStartPre rebuilds), then re-probe `POST /rerank` for a non-404 BEFORE trusting any P-012 measurement. Note the restart is a SHARED-service action on this box (every agent's embed/memory path uses :3384), so it is a coordinated action, not a casual one — and per D-006, P-012 still must not report any GPU figure on this host.\nRelated: P-012, P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"mathmaps-egress-probe-scratch-2026-08-02","title":"SCRATCH — P-006 speech-rule-engine mathmaps egress probe (archive after verification)","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SCRATCH — P-006 speech-rule-engine mathmaps egress probe (archive after verification)\nslug: mathmaps-egress-probe-scratch-2026-08-02\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\nScratch plan — exists only to render real math through the production vditor path.\n\n## Background\n\nIf P-006 is live, rendering the math below pulls in vditor's MathJax bundle, which loads\n`sre_browser.js`, which sets `sre.Variables.url` to\n`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/speech-rule-engine@<ver>/lib/mathmaps` and fetches map files\nfrom jsdelivr. If we are genuinely on KaTeX, no MathJax and no SRE should load at all.\n\nInline math: $E = mc^2$ and $\\sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$.\n\nBlock math:\n\n$$\n\\int_{-\\infty}^{\\infty} e^{-x^2}\\,dx = \\sqrt{\\pi}\n$$\n\n$$\n\\frac{\\partial u}{\\partial t} = \\alpha \\nabla^2 u\n$$\n\n## Phase 1 — probe\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Render this plan and confirm zero jsdelivr / mathmaps / MathJax requests.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"opencode-omp-token-reduction-research-2026-08-02","title":"RESEARCH ONLY — what opencode and OMP actually do for token reduction and context management, cited to file:line","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: RESEARCH ONLY — what opencode and OMP actually do for token reduction and context management, cited to file:line\nslug: opencode-omp-token-reduction-research-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-04\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** RESEARCH COMPLETE and DELIVERED. All 8 items done. Two of the three remaining \"Could not determine\" gaps closed 2026-08-04 (D-012) — **O10:** opencode does NOT roll child-session cost into the parent's displayed total (`session-context-metrics.ts:51`; children excluded at `session-trim.ts`/`event-reducer.ts`), so the subagent firewall's price is invisible where an operator looks, sharpening P-004. **O11:** the \"Code Mode\" cell is **Cloudflare's** feature, not opencode's — its only tree-wide occurrence is a Cloudflare Agents SDK test fixture (`test/fixture/skills/agents-sdk/SKILL.md:152`); no script-executing tool is registered (`tool/registry.ts:1-26`). Two missed mechanisms added: **M8** (skill deferral) and **M9** (`codesearch` `tokensNum`). Tallies reconciled 4→6 mechanisms, 6→8 of 9 gaps.\n\n**Repaired 2026-08-04 (WI-10730, D-013).** The previous Next sent Avi to Claude artifact `4ddb1a4e` for the 14-item borrow list. That artifact was **DELETED** — absent from the owner's gallery under both `scope:'mine'` and `scope:'all'`, WebFetch `artifact not found` — and the \"republish to the same URL\" it prescribed was never executable (only an owned artifact can be updated in place). The list existed in NO durable store. It was **recovered** from the publishing session's local `tool-results/` cache (Claude Code caches every publish's rendered HTML; deletion on claude.ai does not touch it) and now lives in the report MDX as its final addendum, preserving the original \"added on request — judgment, not research\" framing so the doc's no-recommendation guarantee still holds. Both docs builds green.\n\n**Next:** **Avi's decision surface — 14 items, 4 tiers, each naming the measurement that would kill it, plus a \"would not borrow\" list.** Read it either way: **artifact (new URL)** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/59121719-f59b-4af7-8bf4-604c83c8afea — or the canonical copy at `/internal/docs/agent-insights/opencode-and-omp-token-reduction-mechanisms#addendum--what-id-borrow-added-on-request-judgment-not-research`. The MDX is authoritative; the artifact is a rendering of it (D-013). **The old `4ddb1a4e` URL is dead — do not cite it.** One research gap remains, the only one needing an instrumented RUN rather than a read: wall-clock cost of an opencode subagent spawn, which is also what gates borrow-item 6 (the context firewall).\n\n## Background — why this is being researched at all\n\nAnswering \"we are using rtk for token reduction, will we still be taking advantage of this?\" produced three decisions on `bash-substitution-reachable-ceiling-2026-08-01` (D-044, D-046 and the D-041 projection stage) and one loose thread: a comparison of our token-reduction mechanisms against opencode and OMP that existed only as a **recalled reading in a conversation**, with no citations. That recalled table is reproduced below **as a hypothesis to test, not a starting fact**.\n\nThe programme this feeds exists because a previous effort optimised against an unmeasured premise and produced a number that could not move. So: a cell you cannot cite gets struck, not softened. **Striking a cell is a result.**\n\n### The recalled table — every cell is a claim to verify or kill\n\n| mechanism | opencode (claimed) | OMP (claimed) |\n|---|---|---|\n| batch tool calls in a script | `code-mode.ts` — \"confined orchestration script with access to connected MCP tools\" | — |\n| output caps | 1 MB + explicit `truncated` / `timeout` flags | 3000 lines / 50 KB / 512 columns |\n| spill full output, reference by id | — | `output-meta.ts` (~825 lines), `formatFullOutput…` |\n| subagent as context firewall | `Task`, mandated in the system prompt | `task.ts` + `vibe-spawn` / `send` / `wait` / `kill` / `list`, async task contracts + summary prompts |\n\n### ⚠ Context you must carry when you describe opencode's subagent design\n\nopencode reportedly *mandates* `Task` for non-needle exploration. **On this platform `Task`/`Agent`/`Workflow` are DENIED** for every psu launch by owner mandate 2026-07-02 (`NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY`, `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/no-subagent-deny.ts`), opt-in only. Verify in your own session: `ToolSearch { query:\"select:Task,Agent\" }` → no match = denied.\n\nThis does not change your job — **describe opencode's design faithfully regardless**. It changes what your report must say alongside it: that the mechanism as opencode implements it is unavailable here, so the leader is not misled into designing around a denied tool. Precedent for exactly that failure: our own su prompt recommended `Task` for a month after the deny landed (EI-19277117902219188).\n\n## Phase 1 — Pin the ground\n\n- **P-001** `done` **Locate both codebases and pin exactly what you read.** Install path, version, and commit/build id for `opencode` and for `OMP`. A finding against an unnamed version is not reproducible and cannot be re-checked when either upgrades. Record both in the report header. importance: high — note: ← WI-6916 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — opencode\n\n- **P-002** `done` **Enumerate EVERY token-reduction and context-management mechanism in opencode, each cited to `file:line`.** Do not limit yourself to the four rows in the recalled table — that table is one conversation's memory and is likely incomplete. Look for: output truncation and its flags, context-window management and compaction, tool-result shaping, prompt caching, retrieval/search strategy, and anything that decides what does NOT enter the model's context. importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-6917 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` **Verify or strike two quoted prompt lines, verbatim.** \"prefer to use the Task tool in order to reduce context usage\" and \"VERY IMPORTANT... it is CRITICAL that you use the Task tool instead of running search commands directly\". Quote what is actually there with its file:line, or record that neither exists. A near-match is a miss — report the real text. importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-6918 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` **Describe opencode's subagent context-firewall mechanism precisely.** What the prompt instructs, what the subagent returns to the parent, what is discarded, how the parent is billed, and what the spawn costs in tokens and in wall-clock. The economics are the part the leader needs and the part a summary always loses. Pair it with the deny note from `## Now`. importance: high blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-6919 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — OMP\n\n- **P-005** `done` **Enumerate every equivalent mechanism in OMP, each cited to `file:line`.** The recalled table names `task.ts`, `vibe-spawn`/`send`/`wait`/`kill`/`list`, `output-meta.ts` and per-dimension caps (3000 lines / 50 KB / 512 columns). Confirm each, correct the numbers, and add whatever the table missed. importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-6920 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` **Describe OMP's output-spill design precisely.** What gets stored, where, under what identifier, how an agent fetches it back, what the agent sees INSTEAD of the full output, and whether anything expires. This is the mechanism most likely to be genuinely absent on our side, so its details matter more than the others. importance: high blocked-by: P-005 — note: ← WI-6921 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Deliver\n\n- **P-007** `done` **Produce the comparison report: mechanism × {opencode, OMP}, every cell cited or struck.** Leave the \"us\" column OUT entirely — the leader fills it from measurements you do not have, and a guessed cell there is exactly the failure this plan corrects. Mark each row with your confidence and what you could NOT determine; an explicit \"could not determine\" is worth more than a plausible guess. importance: high blocked-by: P-004, P-006 — note: ← WI-6922 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` **Write it up as an agent-insights doc, record the findings as plan decisions, and hand it to the leader.** Doc at `apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/agent-insights/<slug>.mdx` (docs are the one place you may write — it is not papercusp source). Then `coord:send` the leader a ONE-LINE pointer, not the report body. importance: high blocked-by: P-007 — note: ← WI-6923 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Four cells of the recalled table are STRUCK; the report supersedes it\nDate: 2026-08-02\nVerified against opencode 1.4.0 (upstream tag v1.4.0 = 98325dcdc6a566de6b7ab42cc87af544bed3658d) and OMP @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent 17.0.7 (ships full TS src; cited in place).\n\nSTRUCK:\n1. opencode `code-mode.ts` / \"confined orchestration script\" — DOES NOT EXIST at v1.4.0. No file matches *code-mode*; the phrase appears in no .ts/.txt/.md.\n2. opencode output cap \"1 MB\" — WRONG. The cap is 2000 lines AND 50 KB (tool/truncate.ts:17-18). No 1 MB constant exists on the tool-output path.\n3. \"spill full output, reference by id | opencode: —\" — WRONG, the opposite is true. opencode writes the FULL untruncated output to ~/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/<ToolID> and hands the model that id-named path (tool/truncate.ts:104-107), swept hourly on a 7-day retention (:15, :51-61, :123-131).\n4. OMP \"vibe-spawn/send/wait/kill/list\" as the subagent firewall — MISATTRIBUTED. Names are underscored (VIBE_TOOL_NAMES, tools/vibe.ts:50) and vibe drives EXTERNAL CLI worker sessions (:4-5), not a context firewall. The firewall is the `task` subsystem (src/task/, 25 files). There is no single task.ts under src/.\n\nCONFIRMED with corrected location: OMP's 3000 lines / 50 KB / 512 columns are real but live at session/streaming-output.ts:10-12, NOT output-meta.ts (which is the 825-line metadata builder, as recalled).\n\nFull cited report: /internal/docs/agent-insights/opencode-and-omp-token-reduction-mechanisms\n\n### D-002 — P-003: both quotes VERIFIED verbatim — but the hard mandate is Anthropic-prompt-only\nDate: 2026-08-02\nQuote 1 \"prefer to use the Task tool in order to reduce context usage\" EXISTS in THREE prompt variants, identical text:\n- packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/anthropic.txt:79\n- .../trinity.txt:83\n- .../default.txt:91\nFull line: `- When doing file search, prefer to use the Task tool in order to reduce context usage.`\n\nQuote 2 EXISTS in ONE prompt only — packages/opencode/src/session/prompt/anthropic.txt:86:\n`- VERY IMPORTANT: When exploring the codebase to gather context or to answer a question that is not a needle query for a specific file/class/function, it is CRITICAL that you use the Task tool instead of running search commands directly.`\n\nNUANCE THE RECALLED READING COULD NOT CARRY: the SOFT preference is broad; the HARD CRITICAL mandate is Anthropic-prompt-only. default.txt and trinity.txt carry no CRITICAL line. opencode ships >=10 prompt variants (session/system.ts:5-13 + the prompt dir). So \"opencode mandates Task\" is true for one model family and false for the rest — anyone attributing opencode's context saving to the mandate must condition on which prompt is loaded.\n\nCARRIED DENY NOTE: Task/Agent/Workflow are DENIED for every psu launch here (owner mandate 2026-07-02, NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY). Verified in-session this turn: ToolSearch {query:\"select:Task,Agent\"} -> no matching deferred tools found. The mechanism is described faithfully in the report; it is not available on this platform.\n\n### D-003 — P-004 economics: what an opencode subagent spawn actually costs the parent\nDate: 2026-08-02\npackages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts (169 lines).\n\nWHAT CROSSES BACK — only the child's LAST text part:\n  :136  const text = result.parts.findLast((x) => x.type === \"text\")?.text ?? \"\"\n  :138-144  parent-visible output = `task_id: <sessionID> (for resuming...)` + `<task_result>` + text + `</task_result>`\nEvery child tool call, intermediate assistant message and file read is DISCARDED from the parent's context. Because task.ts sets no metadata.truncated, that result is ALSO capped by the universal truncate (2000 lines / 50 KB).\n\nWHAT IS MERELY HIDDEN, NOT DELETED: the child is a real session row with parent_id (session/index.ts:96), enumerable via Session.children (session/index.ts:448-454).\n\nBILLING: child inherits the PARENT's model unless the agent config overrides (:98-101) -> same per-token rate, same account, accounted to a different session id. Cost is per assistant message from tokens.input/output/cache.read/cache.write/reasoning (session/index.ts:296-302). No aggregate roll-up of child cost into the parent was located (recorded as undetermined).\nONE EXPLICIT SAVING: session/prompt.ts:193 `if (input.session.parentID) return` inside ensureTitle — a child session SKIPS the title-generation model call.\n\nBOUNDS: child created with `task` DENIED unless the subagent itself has it (:78-86, :130) -> depth-1 by default; `todowrite` likewise (:69-77, :129). Resumable via task_id (:29-34, :60-62) — the child's context persists server-side across calls while never entering the parent.\n\nTHE COUPLING THAT MATTERS: truncate.ts:30-33 hasTaskTool() + :109-111 — the TRUNCATION HINT BRANCHES on whether the agent may call `task`. With it: \"Use the Task tool to have explore agent process this file... Do NOT read the full file yourself - delegate to save context.\" Without it: \"Use Grep to search the full content or Read with offset/limit.\" The spill and the firewall are ONE system: overflow is spilled to disk, then a disposable subagent is directed to read the spill so the bytes never enter the parent's context.\n\nWALL-CLOCK cost of a spawn: NOT MEASURED (would require a run) — recorded as undetermined.\n\n### D-004 — P-006 OMP output-spill: per-session sequential ids, artifact:// with sub-range selectors, NO expiry\nDate: 2026-08-02\nSTORED WHERE: per-session on disk. artifactsDirectoryFor(sessionFile) = the session path minus its .jsonl suffix (session/session-manager.ts:94-96) — <x>.jsonl -> <x>/. Created lazily on first write (session/artifacts.ts:59-63).\n\nUNDER WHAT ID: sequential integers per session. allocatePath(toolType) -> { id: String(nextId++), path: <dir>/<id>.<toolType>.log } (artifacts.ts:101-106, :92-94). On resume #scanExistingIds re-derives the counter from /^(\\d+)\\..*\\.log$/ so a resumed session cannot overwrite prior artifacts (:74-86).\n\nONE ID SPACE ACROSS THE AGENT TREE: \"Subagents do not own their own ArtifactManager. The parent's instance is adopted via SessionManager.adoptArtifactManager, so the whole parent + subagent tree shares one ID space and one directory\" (artifacts.ts:34-36; session-manager.ts:1347-1349, :1342-1345). A child's artifact://7 resolves for the parent.\n\nWHAT THE AGENT SEES INSTEAD: preview + URL. sdk.ts:1577 `${preview}\\nFull output: artifact://${artifactId}`; streaming-output.ts:631 appends `[raw output: artifact://<id>]` so the composed result stays under maxBytes (:614); tools/gh.ts:2432 same.\n\nHOW IT IS FETCHED BACK — WITH SUB-RANGES: artifact:// is an internal URL scheme in the read tool (tools/read.ts:2195, :3108; scheme list tools/bash-skill-urls.ts:272). Real selector forms cited in source: artifact://5:1-50, artifact://3:raw:-100 (tools/path-utils.ts:401, :376), artifact://5:conflicts:1-1 (tools/read.ts:822). splitInternalUrlSel (path-utils.ts:387) peels selectors incl. malformed shapes so errors surface as selector errors.\n\nEXPIRY: NONE. ArtifactManager (session/artifacts.ts, 153 lines, full surface read) has no retention/TTL/sweep/prune — surface is allocateId/allocatePath/save/exists/listFiles/getPath. Artifacts live as long as the session dir. THIS IS THE SHARPEST CONTRAST WITH OPENCODE, whose spill is swept hourly on a 7-day retention (tool/truncate.ts:15, :51-61, :123-131).\n\nSTREAMING, NOT POST-HOC: OutputSink mirrors the RAW pre-column-cap chunk to the artifact file, triggered on in-memory overflow OR this chunk's column cap dropping bytes OR file already open (streaming-output.ts:877-880). spillThreshold defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES=50KB (:787). ARTIFACT_DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES=0 = unbounded so \"advertised artifact://<id> captures are lossless\" (:17-20, :772-773).
