Non-persistent sessions fall back to an in-memory Map \"so spill truncation still works\" (session-manager.ts:1359-1368).\n\n### D-005 — Four mechanisms the recalled table missed entirely\nDate: 2026-08-02\nThe table was incomplete, as the plan suspected. Four mechanisms exist that it names nowhere:\n\n1. OPENCODE PRUNE — evicting old tool-result BODIES with NO model call, distinct from compaction. session/compaction.ts:35-37 (PRUNE_MINIMUM=20_000, PRUNE_PROTECT=40_000, PRUNE_PROTECTED_TOOLS=[\"skill\"]), walk at :93-139. Protects the newest 40k tokens of tool output AND the last 2 user turns (:111); stops at the last summary boundary (:112) and at the already-pruned region (:118) so the walk is incremental; only fires if >20k tokens would be freed (:130) — a hysteresis band. The model then sees the fixed string \"[Old tool result content cleared]\" (session/message-v2.ts:718) and the part's attachments are dropped too (:719). The tool CALL and its args remain; only the RESULT BODY goes. NOT recoverable in-context (though a spilled copy may sit on disk for <=7d).\n\n2. OPENCODE OVERFLOW ARITHMETIC — session/overflow.ts, 22 lines, entire trigger. COMPACTION_BUFFER=20_000 (:6); count = tokens.total || input+output+cache.read+cache.write (:13-14); reserved = cfg.compaction.reserved ?? min(20k, maxOutputTokens(model)) (:16-17); usable = model.limit.input - reserved else context - maxOutputTokens (:18-20); overflow iff count >= usable (:21). ABSOLUTE-TOKEN and model-limit-derived, NOT a percent-of-window heuristic. NOTE: CACHE TOKENS COUNT TOWARD THE WINDOW (:14) — prompt caching (transform.ts:192-215, max 4 breakpoints) cuts COST, not OCCUPANCY.\n\n3. OMP \"SHAKE\" — RECOVERABLE in-place eviction; OMP's analogue of opencode's prune, except the model is told how to get the bytes back. session/agent-session.ts:10833, ShakeMode = \"elide\"|\"images\" (session/shake-types.ts:9). Elide offloads heavy tool-results and fenced/XML blocks into ONE artifact and leaves: `[shaken ~N tokens — recover: artifact://<id> (region N)]` (:10884-10889). Contrast opencode's \"[Old tool result content cleared]\": OMP's placeholder states HOW MUCH went and HOW TO GET IT BACK; opencode's states neither.\n   AND A TIERED LADDER: #rescueCompactionDeadEnd (:13706, doc :13685-13705) runs Tier 1 shake(\"elide\") then Tier 2 dropImages(), re-testing progress between tiers. The ordering rule is explicit at :13696-13698 — images go LAST because \"unlike elided text they are NOT artifact-recoverable\". RECOVERABLE REDUCTIONS ARE ATTEMPTED BEFORE IRRECOVERABLE ONES.\n\n4. OMP \"SNAPCOMPACT\" — compaction with NO LLM CALL. session/compact-modes.ts:47-65 defines three modes; snapcompact is verbatim \"Archive history onto dense bitmap images the model reads back (no LLM call)\". Impl session/snapcompact-inline.ts (MAX_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FRAMES=6 at :51; tool results swapped for frames :431-486) + the @oh-my-pi/snapcompact package + src/prompts/system/snapcompact-*.md.\n\nAlso worth naming, missed by the table: OMP's third cap dimension is a PER-LINE column cap applied at the SINK and stateful across streaming chunks (streaming-output.ts:12, :870-873), with the human TUI shown the uncapped stream and only the persisted LLM view capped (:850-851); OMP supports MIDDLE elision as a first-class truncation direction (output-meta.ts:28) where opencode has head/tail only (truncate.ts:27); and OMP's subagent result contract tells the parent the SIZE of what it discarded (`<meta lines size/>`, prompts/tools/task-summary.md:2) and spills a truncated subagent result to agent://<id> (:7), neither of which opencode does.\n\n### D-006 — CORRECTION to D-003/D-005 — five gaps closed, and two published OMP cells were WRONG; the cause was searching one package\nDate: 2026-08-02\nRead this before citing any OMP cell from this plan's earlier decisions.\n\n**What was wrong.** Two cells published as findings were not gaps but ERRORS. OMP's shake was recorded as having **no hysteresis** and a merely **\"config-driven\" protection band**. Both are false. `pi-agent-core/src/compaction/shake.ts:46-59` defines `DEFAULT_SHAKE_CONFIG` — the AUTO path — with `protectTokens: 16_000`, `minSavings: 4_000`, `fenceMinTokens: 400`. The original read had found only `AGGRESSIVE_SHAKE_CONFIG`, where both thresholds are deliberately `0` because that path serves the manual `/shake` command (\"drops every eligible region across history\"), and generalised from it. The unattended path — the one that matters for a comparison — has real guards, comparable to opencode's 40k/20k.\n\n**Why five gaps closed at once.** All five had one cause: **OMP is not one package.** The research searched `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`, which is only the CLI shell. The mechanisms live in siblings that also ship `src/`: `pi-agent-core` (compaction, shake, prune) and `pi-ai` (provider wire, prompt caching, usage accounting). Grepping `~/node_modules/@oh-my-pi/*` as a whole surfaces all five in one pass. **An absence proved by one grep in one package is not an absence** — that is the transferable rule, and it applies to the cells still marked \"not located\" in this plan, which were established the same way.\n\n**Now answered:** shake configs (above); compaction thresholds (`compaction.ts:294-298`, `:319-325`, 15% proportional reserve at `:282-288`); subagent recursion depth = **2** (`task/structured-subagent.ts:211`, not `spawn-policy.ts`); prompt caching = a 4-breakpoint BUDGET not a positional scheme, 1h default retention for OAuth *and* API keys, TTL-ordering normalized (`pi-ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts:3001-3047`, `:440-462`, `:3049-3061`); cache tokens DO count toward context, minus provider-side orchestration tokens (`compaction.ts:215-222`).\n\n**One mechanism found that no cell asked about,** and the most useful thing here: OMP's pruner is **cache-aware**. `cacheWarmSuffixTokens` (`pruning.ts:44-51`, `:349-357`; `8_000` at `agent-session.ts:792`) refuses to mutate any entry whose message-suffix exceeds the warm window, because editing inside the already-sent prefix makes the provider re-write the entire suffix at `cacheWrite` price. So it deliberately leaves deep superseded/useless results alone — overriding its own supersede rules — and lets compaction and shake reclaim them, because those rebuild the cache anyway. Generalised: any history-cleanup pass has a cost gradient running opposite to the obvious one; the stalest material is the most expensive to touch.\n\n**Gap ledger: 9 recorded → 4 open.** The four remaining need a RUN or an exhaustive audit, not a read: opencode subagent spawn wall-clock; opencode child-session cost rollup; `code-mode` under another name in opencode's other 18 packages; whether OMP applies its caps as universally as opencode's single choke point.\n\nBoth deliverables carry all of this: the canonical MDX (`agent-insights/opencode-and-omp-token-reduction-mechanisms`, rebuilt and verified in `dist`) and the artifact.\n\n### D-007 — CORRECTION — the \"OMP caps are per-tool, not a single choke point\" cell was wrong; OMP has BOTH layers\nDate: 2026-08-02\nThird wrongly-filled cell corrected in this report (after D-006's two). Do not re-cite the old cell.\n\n**What the report said** (side-by-side table, row \"Applied universally?\"): opencode = Yes, every tool result via `tool/tool.ts:86`; OMP = \"Per-sink (`OutputSink`), wired per tool — `bash.ts:20`, `eval.ts:12`\", confidence High/Medium. And the matching gap: \"`OutputSink` is wired per tool rather than at a single choke point, but no exhaustive audit of every tool was performed.\"\n\n**What is actually true.** OMP has TWO cap layers at DIFFERENT boundaries, and the report found only one.\n\n1. STREAMING, per-executor by necessity. `OutputSink` (`session/streaming-output.ts:728`) caps bytes as they arrive from a live subprocess. Exactly four execution sites import it: `exec/bash-executor.ts:10`, `eval/executor-base.ts:3`, `eval/js/executor.ts:1`, `tools/bash-interactive.ts:18` (plus `tools/eval.ts:12`). That set is not incomplete coverage — it is precisely the set of tools owning a subprocess, the only set for which a streaming cap means anything.\n\n2. CONTEXT BOUNDARY, universal. `spillLargeResultToArtifact` (`tools/output-meta.ts:650`) runs inside `wrappedExecute` (`:770-798`), installed by `wrapToolWithMetaNotice` (`:805`). EVERY registration path wraps: built-in `tools/index.ts:595` (createTools maps every BUILTIN_TOOLS entry) plus `:634`/`:640`; vibe `agent-session.ts:7195` via `#wrapRuntimeTool` `:7171`; MCP `:7786`; RPC-host `:7837`; SDK goal/write `sdk.ts:2377`/`:2412`; CLI read `cli/read-cli.ts:37`. Extension tools compose OUTSIDE it (`ExtensionToolWrapper` wraps the already-wrapped tool at `:7173`/`:7788`/`:7839`) so the cap still runs. No bypass: `kUnwrappedExecute` is referenced only inside `output-meta.ts` (`:603`,`:770`,`:777`,`:806`,`:813`) as an idempotence guard and the wrapper's own call. Source states the intent at `:679-680`: \"The spill wraps arbitrary tools (built-in, MCP, extension, RPC-host).\" Defaults: spill >50KB, keep 20KB head + 20KB tail / 500 tail lines (`config/settings-schema.ts:679`,`:703`,`:723`,`:765`).\n\n**Coverage = every registered tool**, with three exemptions:\n- `read`, by name (`:657`) — NOT a hole; read has a richer line-oriented cap of its own (`read.ts:47-53`, `:154-155`) that byte-tail spilling would corrupt.\n- tool already saved its own artifact (`:662`) — structurally UNREACHABLE by untrusted tools: the MCP bridge builds `details` from a fixed field list with no `meta` and no spread of server data (`mcp/tool-bridge.ts:212-234`), so a remote server cannot self-exempt.\n- HOLE 1: `if (!sessionManager) return result;` (`:656`). `sessionManager` is optional on `CustomToolContext` (`sdk.ts:542`), so an SDK/headless embedding without one gets NO context cap at all. Inconsistent with the SAME function's handling of a FAILED save (`:684-692`), which logs and still truncates under an explicit comment that a save failure must never re-expose the full output. Storage-failure degrades correctly; storage-absent does not degrade at all.\n- HOLE 2: the universal cap is TEXT-ONLY. It measures only `block.type === \"text\"` (`:666-671`) and passes non-text blocks through untouched (`:710-714`). Image blocks from browser (`browser/run-output.ts:24`, `tab-worker.ts:1581`/`:1617`), fetch (`:1153`), eval (`:608-621`), inspect_image (`:223`), read (`:1210`/`:1276`) are governed only by `MAX_IMAGE_INPUT_BYTES` = 20MB (`utils/image-loading.ts:7`) — a decode-safety limit, not a context budget.\n\n**Why the report got it wrong, and the transferable rule.** Same error shape as D-006: find ONE mechanism, treat it as the whole answer, when it was one LAYER of a layered design. D-006's version was reading one config object (AGGRESSIVE_SHAKE_CONFIG) and generalising; this one was reading the per-tool wiring and generalising. Everything observed was TRUE — the per-tool wiring really is per-tool — it just was not the only thing there. RULE: when a mechanism looks SURPRISINGLY incomplete in a codebase that is otherwise careful, the likely explanation is a second mechanism one layer up that you have not found yet, not an oversight by the authors. Check the REGISTRATION boundary as well as the EXECUTION boundary before concluding \"no central enforcement\".\n\n### D-008 — Gap (3) CLOSED from the sibling plan: `code-mode` does not exist in opencode v1.4.0 under ANY name, across all 19 packages\nDate: 2026-08-03\nContributed from the sibling plan `agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02` (its P-002 / D-011), which had to settle the same question to cite-or-strike its inventory table. Recording it here so this plan's gap ledger can go 3 -> 2 without re-deriving it.\n\n#### The gap as this plan stated it\n\n> \"(3) `code-mode` under another name in opencode's other 18 packages\" — explicitly flagged as needing a full-repo content search rather than a read.\n\n#### Measured\n\nAgainst `/mnt/data/tmp/oc-src` @ `98325dc release: v1.4.0`, the full checkout (all 19 packages: app, console, containers, desktop, desktop-electron, docs, enterprise, extensions, function, identity, opencode, plugin, script, sdk, slack, storybook, ui, util, web), excluding `node_modules`:\n\n1. **By filename** — `find . -iname \"*code-mode*\" -o -iname \"*codemode*\"` => **zero matches.**\n2. **By concept/identifier** — `grep -rniE \"code[-_ ]?mode\" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx --include=*.txt --include=*.md --include=*.json`, filtered for the obvious false positives (`opencode model`, decode/encode/unicode/barcode/geocode/qrcode) => **zero matches.**\n3. **By behaviour** — a search for a tool that executes code or invokes tools from a script (`run js/typescript/python code`, `execute code`, `code interpreter`, `persistent kernel`) across the packages' prompt/description text => **zero matches.**\n\nCorroborating structural evidence: opencode's complete tool surface is 24 files in `packages/opencode/src/tool/` (apply_patch, bash, codesearch, edit, external-directory, glob, grep, invalid, lsp, ls, multiedit, plan, question, read, registry, schema, skill, task, todo, tool, truncate, truncation-dir, webfetch, websearch, write). None is a code-execution or tool-orchestration tool. `codesearch.ts` is a SEARCH tool, not a code-runner — worth naming explicitly because its filename is the most plausible near-miss for someone re-checking this.\n\n**Verdict: the `code-mode.ts` attribution to opencode is a recall artifact with no referent at any name.** The sibling plan struck that inventory cell on this evidence.\n\n#### A correction that travels with it, and matters more\n\nThe same sibling item found the comparison was not merely wrong but **inverted**: the mechanism attributed to opencode does not exist there, while **OMP has the strongest form of it** and had been recorded as having none. OMP `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` v17.0.7 ships `src/tools/eval.ts` (+ `eval-backends.ts`, `eval-render.ts`) with `src/prompts/tools/eval.md`: a PERSISTENT code kernel where \"State persists across calls and subagents\", exposing\n\n- `tool.<name>(args)` — \"Invoke any session tool\", i.e. literal tool-calls-from-a-script;\n- `parallel(thunks)` for in-cell fan-out;\n- `agent(prompt, ...)` to spawn subagents from inside the script;\n- `completion(prompt, model?)` for oneshot stateless LLM calls;\n- `output(*ids, format?, query?, offset?, limit?)` to PAGE PRIOR TOOL OUTPUTS BY ID.\n\nThat last one is directly relevant to this plan's borrow list: it is the by-id output referencing this plan already studied in `output-meta.ts`, but exposed as a *programmable* surface rather than only a notice. If the borrow list carries a \"batch tool calls in a script\" item, OMP's `eval` — not anything in opencode — is the artifact to borrow from.\n\n#### Scope caveat, stated so it is not over-read\n\nThis closes the gap for **v1.4.0 at commit `98325dc`**, the checkout on this box. It says nothing about opencode's history — a `code-mode` may well have existed in an earlier release and been removed, which would explain the recollection honestly. If that distinction matters to the borrow list, `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- '*code-mode*'` in that checkout would settle it; it was out of scope for the sibling's cite-or-strike, which asks only what the LIVE source supports.\n\n### D-012 — Two of the three remaining gaps closed by search, not by a run — plus two mechanisms the report had missed\nDate: 2026-08-04\nOn 2026-08-04 the report's three open gaps were re-examined. Two closed. Both had been recorded as needing \"a run or a full-repo content search\"; neither needed a run — each needed only the search the doc itself admitted had not been performed.\n\n**O10 — opencode does NOT roll child-session cost into the parent's displayed total.** The displayed figure reduces over one session's own messages (`app/src/components/session/session-context-metrics.ts:51`, surfaced `session-context-tab.tsx:216`). Children are separate rows keyed by `parentID` (`tool/task.ts:65-66`) and the app deliberately excludes them from roots and counters (`global-sync/session-trim.ts`, `event-reducer.ts`). `tool/task.ts` contains no reference to cost/tokens/usage at all. Consequence for P-004's economics: the subagent firewall's price is real but invisible where an operator would look — a per-session cost readout systematically under-reports a task that delegated.\n\n**O11 — opencode's \"Code Mode\" cell is Cloudflare's feature, mis-attributed.** The only occurrence of the term in all 19 packages is a TEST FIXTURE documenting the Cloudflare Agents SDK (`test/fixture/skills/agents-sdk/SKILL.md:152`), whose own frontmatter says \"Build AI agents on Cloudflare Workers\". The `references/codemode.md` it links does not exist in the fixture. No script-executing tool is registered (`tool/registry.ts:1-26`). Cloudflare's Code Mode converts MCP tools into a TypeScript API an LLM writes code against — matching the recalled phrasing \"confined orchestration script with access to connected MCP tools\" almost exactly. The recalled table's error was therefore attribution collapse between adjacent sources, not random drift.\n\n**Two mechanisms the report had missed entirely** were found while searching, and are added as M8/M9:\n- **M8 skill deferral** — an unused skill costs one markdown bullet (`Skill.fmt(list,{verbose:false})`, `tool/skill.ts:32` + `skill/index.ts:258-263`); the SKILL.md body enters context only on invocation (`:79-91`); the bundled file list is sampled at `limit = 10` (`:56`, `:69-70`) and says so (`:86`). Comparative finding: OMP additionally PROTECTS loaded skill content from eviction (`compaction/shake.ts:49,57`, `pruning.ts:57`, `tool-protection.ts:38-39`) whereas opencode's prune clears on `time.compacted` alone with no per-tool exemption (`message-v2.ts:718`).\n- **M9 codesearch `tokensNum`** — `.min(1000).max(50000).default(5000)` (`tool/codesearch.ts:44-51`), the only opencode cap the MODEL sets; all others are fixed constants. Scoped caveat: it governs an external retrieval API (Exa Code), so it bounds what retrieval injects, not what a local tool emits.\n\nThese were missed because the original read enumerated the truncation and compaction paths but not the tool REGISTRATION surface — the same layer-boundary error the doc already names for OMP's O9, now found on the opencode side too.\n\n**Remaining open: one.** Wall-clock cost of an opencode subagent spawn — genuinely needs a run.\n\nMethod note worth carrying: the two closures resolved in OPPOSITE directions — O10 confirmed the suspected absence, O11 overturned the framing entirely. A gap recorded as \"not searched\" is not evidence of absence in either direction.\n\nScope respected: no papercusp source edited, no \"us\" column filled, no adoption recommendation. Every claim above is cited to file:line.\n\n### D-013 — A published artifact is a RENDERING, never a deliverable's only home — and a deleted one is recoverable from the publishing session's tool-results cache\nDate: 2026-08-04\n**Ruling, binding on any lane that publishes an artifact as part of a deliverable.**\n\nThis plan shipped its 14-item borrow list — the owner's actual decision surface — into a Claude artifact and nowhere else. The artifact was later deleted. For an unknown period this plan's `## Now` confidently directed Avi to pick from a list at `https://claude.ai/code/artifact/4ddb1a4e-…`, which returns `artifact not found`, while every status surface still read complete-and-green. Nothing had *failed*; the link simply stopped resolving, and no mechanism notices that.\n\n**Rule 1 — durable store first, artifact second.** Write deliverable content into a store the fleet can read (the MDX, the plan body, a decision, a work-item), then publish the artifact as a rendering *of* it. If a fact exists only in an artifact, that is a bug in the deliverable, not a formatting choice. An artifact is account-scoped, deletable, un-indexed, and invisible to every papercusp read path.\n\n**Rule 2 — never prescribe a same-URL republish without confirming ownership.** The `Artifact` update flow requires an artifact the account OWNS. This plan's Now prescribed \"republish to the same URL\", which was never executable. Check with `Artifact { action:'list', scope:'all' }` — the default `scope:'mine'` omits shared artifacts, so a miss there cannot distinguish \"not yours\" from \"not there\".\n\n**Rule 3 — 'not in the tree, plan, or transcripts' is NOT 'lost'.** Claude Code caches every publish's rendered HTML under the PUBLISHING session's own `tool-results/` dir (`artifact-<uuid-prefix>-<epoch>-<hash>.html`); deleting on claude.ai does not touch it. The borrow list was recovered from `…/session-claude/su-5b23300b-…/527e5735-…/tool-results/artifact-4ddb1a4e-1785725103-78af.html` (258,642 bytes, mtime 2026-08-02 22:45:20 -0400) and is now in the report MDX under its original \"added on request — judgment, not research\" framing.\n\n**The transferable epistemics, which is why this is a Decision and not just a fix:** two agents independently concluded \"unrecoverable\" within about a minute of each other, both reasoning correctly from three independent negative searches — the git tree, the plan store, and `sessions:search`. All three genuinely return nothing, and their agreement reads as corroboration. It is not: they share one blind spot, none of them indexes the publishing agent's filesystem. **Agreement between searches that share a blind spot is not corroboration.** Before concluding something is gone, name the KIND of store that would hold it and confirm you have queried that kind at all.\n\nFiled as WI-10730. Method documented at `/internal/docs/agent-insights/recovering-a-deleted-claude-artifact`.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"outage-must-not-be-silent-2026-08-02","title":"An outage must never be silent, and a diagnosis must never be a guess","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: An outage must never be silent, and a diagnosis must never be a guess\nslug: outage-must-not-be-silent-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-03\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** PHASE 1 SHIPPED + VERIFIED (P-001..P-004 done) and P-008 (runbook) done. On disk, NOT deployed.\n\n`libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/store-identity.ts` fingerprints a store by cluster `system_identifier` (initdb-assigned, immutable per cluster) + `current_database()`; pins the first determinate identity per process; LATCHES a positive mismatch; INDETERMINATE never rejects (a check that cannot run must never reject a healthy config). Wired into `connection.ts::validateDiscoveryTargetOnce` as one extra column on the existing WI-5244 probe — zero extra round-trips — and it now runs for EVERY pool, not just discovery-sourced ones, because the pin must come from the trusted env/native path or the first impostor observed legitimises itself. Exported from `@papercusp/db-org` as `storeIdentityViolation()`, learning from EI-19306394439939264 where an unexported guard got zero adoption.\n\nVERIFIED: 50 tests green (33 unit + 6 recurrence + 11 rewritten contract), full db suite 168/168 exit 0, `lint:tsc --files` clean on every changed file.\n\nD-001 = liveness is not identity (the obvious fix was already deployed and could not have worked). D-002 = my own correction was itself over-broad: there are TWO discovery implementations and the read path has only a pid gate (filed EI-19384906720464601).\n\n**Next:** P-005 (fail fast, never hang) is the highest-value item left, and the lead is established: `apps/operator/bin/mcp-proxy.ts` is a 37-line shim over `apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.ts` whose `retryWindowMs` defaults to 90s, yet the observed hang ran past 300s — so find and bound the UNBOUNDED wait beyond that retry window (most likely a missing response timeout once the connection is established) and return a structured error naming the failing plane.\n\n## Background\n\n### The incident, and why it was silent\n\n`~/.papercusp/embedded-pg.json` is the discovery file: the desktop's Rust main writes\n`{url, port, pid, startedAt}` when its embedded Postgres is ready. `getHarnessAdminUrl()`\n(`packages/operator-core/lib/embedded-pg-discovery.ts`) prefers it over the native `:5432`.\n\nThe failure came in two phases, and **the first is far worse than the second**:\n\n- **Phase 1 — silent wrong answers.** Reads resolved to an embedded PG that was alive,\n  listening, freshly migrated (433 tables) and **empty**. Reads *succeeded*. `work_items:get`\n  answered `not_found`; `coord:orient` reported generation 5→1, `modes: []`, inbox 687→57.\n  Every one of those is indistinguishable from \"your work was deleted\".\n- **Phase 2 — hangs, not errors.** That instance died; the transport began returning\n  `ECONNREFUSED :22060`, and the MCP proxy **hung instead of failing fast** (a\n  `work_items:get` ran past 300s). A hang presents as silence; an error presents as a fault.\n\n### Three generations of guard — and the one that is missing\n\n`packages/operator-core/lib/long-lived-admin-pool.ts` states the lineage precisely:\n\n> every earlier guard asked *\"what SHOULD we connect to?\"*, and none asked\n> *\"what is the live pool actually bound to?\"*\n\n1. **Gen 1 — resolution.** \"What *should* we connect to?\" → `embedded-pg-discovery`, plus\n   its pid + port liveness gates.\n2. **Gen 2 — binding.** \"What is the live pool actually *bound* to?\" → `endStalePool` and\n   the self-rebinding `getLongLivedAdminPool`.\n3. **Gen 3 — identity. MISSING.** \"Is the store at that address *the same store we have\n   been talking to*?\" Nothing in the tree asks this: `system_identifier` /\n   `pg_control_system` appears **nowhere** in the codebase.\n\nGens 1 and 2 both reason about the **address**. The 22:40Z outage had a correct-looking,\nlive, listening address serving the wrong data — so both waved it through, exactly as\ndesigned. Every future variant of \"an endpoint moved under us\" defeats them the same way.\n\n### The second half: a diagnosis must not be a guess\n\nThe owner quoted this back deliberately. In one session I produced **four** wrong readings,\nand **acted** on one — editing `operator-port.json` on the hypothesis that the proxy follows\nit, before checking. The proxy's own journal showed it targeting `:3070` directly; it never\nreads that file. Each error had the same shape: **inferring a mechanism from config instead\nof reading the component's own logs.** The correction, every time, came from the logs.\n\nThis is not personal. The same shape produced a **critical EI filed by a peer during this\nvery incident**, asserting the resolver \"never checks that the named pid is alive or that\nthe named port is listening\" — when it checks both, and had for 29 hours. A fix written\nagainst that claim would have been a no-op that closed the incident falsely. **The failure\nmode is systemic and therefore mechanically addressable.**\n\n## Phase 1 — Store identity: make a wrong-store read impossible, not merely unlikely\n\n- **P-001** `done` Build the store-identity primitive: fingerprint a Postgres store by its cluster `system_identifier` (`pg_control_system()`) + `current_database()`. A freshly-initdb'd cluster — exactly the empty DB in phase 1 — necessarily carries a DIFFERENT identifier, so this separates \"the right store\" from \"a live store\" which no existing guard can do. importance: high\n- **P-002** `done` Pin-and-verify: the first identity observed in a process is PINNED; a later mismatch raises a named, loud `StoreIdentityChangedError` carrying both fingerprints and both URLs. Never answer from a different store. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` Wire the guard into the pool seam (`getLongLivedAdminPool` / the managed org pool) so it covers the real read path rather than one call site. Must not break the sync contract of `getHarnessAdminUrl()`. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-004** `done` Recurrence guard: a test that constructs the exact phase-1 condition (alive + listening + wrong store) and asserts the liveness gates PASS while the identity guard REJECTS. This is the test that would have failed before the outage. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n\n## Phase 2 — An outage must announce itself\n\n- **P-005** `done` Fail fast, never hang: bound the MCP proxy's upstream wait and return a structured error NAMING the failing plane, so an outage presents as a fault rather than silence. A 300s hang is worse than a 5s error. importance: high — note: Closed by D-005. The ceiling this item asked for already existed (maxHoldMs, EI-19305299022434394); the real deliverable was that `handshake_timeout_retry` — WI-6740's session-fatal marker — was classified into NO alarm class and could never page. Shipped handshakeStalls + shed as first-class McpProxyHealth fields and delegated dev:service_health to the one summarizer (deleting my duplicate reader). 60 tests green, tsc clean.\n- **P-006** `dropped` Data-plane health probe: `/api/health` and `tools/list` are served WITHOUT touching Postgres (the three-plane model, WI-6739), so neither can detect a DB-dead operator. The upstream check must exercise a real read-only data-plane call. — note: PREMISE FALSE — already implemented. The mcp-proxy watchdog has BOTH a DATA-PLANE probe (WI-6739, read-only, actually touches Postgres) and a SESSION-PLANE probe (EI-19299524366372518, added 2026-08-01). The deploy path also has a domain-read canary + memory canary. See D-004: detection was never the gap.\n- **P-007** `done` Flap visibility: `:3070` recovered 7× in 20 minutes with no agent-visible signal. A recovered flap is still a fault and must be surfaced, not swallowed. — note: Shipped as DELIVERY per D-004: mcp-proxy-failure-summary.ts (+11 tests) surfaced on dev:service_health. No new detection — the proxy already recorded all 9 kinds to a 27MB JSONL nobody read. Recoveries are first-class and explicitly NOT health (the WI-6740 trap). Bounded 256KB tail read; field omitted when quiet. 30/30 tests, 0 type errors.\n- **P-011** `done` DELIVERY (per D-004): surface a latched store-identity violation on dev:pg_health — the surface an agent actually reads when the database is behaving strangely. The guard already DETECTED via console.error into the operator journal, which no MCP-side agent ever sees. Omits the field entirely when clean, so an absent check never reads as a passed one. importance: high — note: Shipped: pg_health.ts + pg_health.test.ts (4 tests). Zero pg_health type errors; test status=passed.\n\n\n## Phase 3 — A diagnosis must not be a guess\n\n- **P-008** `done` Encode the runbook as an agent-insights doc: the three-plane model; `mcp-proxy-failures.jsonl` as the highest-value artifact; journald leaves a LOG HOLE during a stall (it logs completions/errors only) so absence-of-logs is the signature of a wedge, not of health; journald renders EDT while that JSONL renders UTC (a 4h mis-bucketing trap); steady log volume PROVES not-event-loop-wedged. importance: high — note: shipped as /internal/docs/agent-insights/diagnosing-a-silent-store-outage\n- **P-009** `done` Make the \"X never checks Y\" claim class cheap to falsify — a filed root cause asserting a code ABSENCE is the single most repeated diagnostic error here (twice in this incident alone, by two different agents), and it is mechanically checkable in a way prose is not. — note: Done per D-006. The detector already existed (premises-claim-port.ts, measured on 31,090 bodies) and is wired at work_items:claim + scheduler:get_next — so NO new detector was built. The residual was surface coverage: widened PremiseSource with 'carry-note' and added an absenceLint leg to loop:checkpoint, the surface where this plan's own D-005 incident actually happened (no claim event was ever involved). Advisory, fail-open, suppressed when the falsifier is already parked in checks[]. 91 tests green (33 checkpoint incl 4 new, 17 premises-claim-port, 41 carry-note); tsc clean.\n- **P-010** `done` `work_items:checkpoint` has no MEASURED-vs-INFERRED marker, unlike `loop:checkpoint`'s ✓/? split — so a successor reads a predecessor's guesses as established fact. Filed as EI-19381740995807040; this plan is where it gets fixed. — note: ALREADY SHIPPED — no code written. checksSpec() in work_items/checkpoint.ts provides the ✓ VERIFIED / ? PREDICTED split, reusing loop:checkpoint's carry-note machinery; landed 2026-08-02T01:31Z, 21h BEFORE I filed EI-19381740995807040 proposing it. Delivery verified (rows render INTO the stored note; over-cap trims body first so checks are never cut); 51 tests pass. EI resolved as already-implemented. Root cause of the wasted filing captured as EI-19390763763662489 (capture dedup is blind to shipped code).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Liveness is not identity — the obvious fix was already deployed and could not have worked\n\n**Claim under test:** that the outage was caused by `getHarnessAdminUrl()` trusting\n`embedded-pg.json` without checking the pid/port are alive (as asserted by\nEI-19383722505382723, severity critical).\n\n**Measured, 2026-08-02:** FALSE. `libs/generic/embedded-pg-discovery/src/index.ts` contains\nBOTH gates — `isPidAlive()` (`process.kill(pid, 0)`, landed 2026-07-19) and\n`isDiscoveredPortServed()` (a synchronous `/proc/net/tcp{,6}` LISTEN scan, landed\n2026-08-01 17:12:17 -0400). Both are present in `papercup-release` AND\n`papercusp-release`, so both were **deployed and passing** at the 22:40Z incident.\n\n**Why they could not have prevented it, deductively and independent of the above:** in\nphase 1 the wrong database was *alive* (postmaster started 22:40:27Z) and *listening*\n(reads succeeded against it). Both gates therefore PASS on the exact input that caused the\noutage. A stricter liveness check is not a weaker version of the right fix — it is a\ndifferent question. The property that justifies trusting a store is its IDENTITY.\n\n**Consequences.** (1) Do not \"fix\" EI-19383722505382723 as filed; it would be a no-op that\ncloses the incident falsely — the two peers who filed it have been told. (2) The generation-3\nidentity guard (Phase 1) is the actual fix. (3) A liveness check is still worth keeping: it\ncorrectly handles the *dead*-endpoint case (phase 2), which identity alone does not.\n\n### D-002 — Addendum to D-001 — there are TWO discovery implementations, and I generalised from the wrong one\nDate: 2026-08-02\n**Self-correction, recorded because the original D-001 was stated too broadly and I had already sent it to two peers as a correction of THEIR claim.**\n\nD-001 asserts the pid and port liveness gates \"exist and were deployed and passing\". That is accurate for `getHarnessAdminUrl()` — the function EI-19383722505382723 actually named — but I wrote it as though one resolver existed. There are two:\n\n| implementation | used by | gates |\n|---|---|---|\n| `libs/generic/embedded-pg-discovery` via `packages/operator-core/lib/embedded-pg-discovery.ts` | `getHarnessAdminUrl()` | pid + `/proc/net/tcp` port-listening |\n| `libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/connection.ts` `adminUrl()` → `_parseDiscoveryJson()` | **`getOrgPg()` — the work-items / plans / `dev:pg_query` read path** | **pid only** |\n\nMeasured: `grep -c 'proc/net/tcp\\|listeningPorts\\|isDiscoveredPortServed\\|TCP_LISTEN'` on connection.ts returns 0, and its single `embedded-pg-discovery` occurrence is a comment, not an import.\n\n**So the path that actually served the wrong answers had ONE liveness gate, not two**, and the peers' instinct pointed at a real gap — just not in the function their EI named. Filed separately as EI-19384906720464601.\n\n**What does NOT change: D-001's conclusion and every action taken from it.** The deductive core never rested on the git archaeology. In phase 1 the impostor was alive AND listening, so a port gate passes on that input too; identity remains the only discriminator, and adding the missing port gate to connection.ts would not have prevented the outage. D-001's consequences stand: do not implement EI-19383722505382723 as filed, and the identity guard is the fix.\n\n**Why this addendum exists rather than a quiet edit of D-001.** The whole B-half of this plan is that a diagnosis stated more confidently than its evidence supports is the recurring failure here. I did it again, inside the very decision that documents the pattern — having read one file and written \"the resolver\". The correction is cheap; a silently-narrowed claim that peers already acted on is not. Both peers were told (msg mscf3ejd), including the part where my correction of them was itself partly wrong.\n\n**The transferable rule:** before writing \"the X does/does not do Y\", confirm there is exactly ONE X. `grep -l` for the symbol across the tree costs seconds and is the difference between a true statement and a true-of-one-file statement that reads as universal.\n\n### D-003 — P-005 re-scoped — the unbounded wait is DELIBERATE; the fix is liveness feedback, not a timeout\nDate: 2026-08-02\n**P-005 as originally written (\"bound the MCP proxy's upstream wait\") is WRONG and would have caused a regression. Do not implement it as filed.**\n\nRead `apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.ts` before touching this. WI-6740 already solved upstream silence, and solved it with a deliberate asymmetry:\n\n- **The `idempotent` class IS bounded** — `HANDSHAKE_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` (8s, env-overridable) with up to 2 replays, covering `initialize` / `tools/list` / `ping` / `resources` / `prompts`. Those are write-free catalog reads; one taking >8s is definitionally stalled and replaying costs nothing.\n- **A real `tools/call` is deliberately UNBOUNDED.** The header states why: `build:typecheck` legitimately runs ~160s and `capability:bash` ~120s on this box, so a blanket upstream timeout \"would convert working long tools into hard failures. That asymmetry is the whole design.\"\n\nMy 300s `work_items:get` hang was a `tools/call`. **It was therefore behaving as designed.** The 90s `retryWindowMs` I cited in the Now block is the retry-on-refused window — a different mechanism entirely, and not the thing that would have bounded it.\n\n**So the defect is real but it is not a missing timeout.** It is that an unbounded `tools/call` is INDISTINGUISHABLE, from the agent's side, from a wedged transport. Both present as: nothing happens, for minutes, with no output. The agent cannot tell \"your 160s typecheck is running fine\" from \"the store died and you will never get an answer\", and that ambiguity is what made a fleet-wide outage read as silence.\n\n**The re-scoped P-005 is therefore LIVENESS FEEDBACK, not a deadline:** a long-running `tools/call` should give the caller a positive signal that it is still being served — so silence becomes evidence of a fault rather than the normal appearance of slow work. Options worth weighing (none chosen yet): a periodic keep-alive/progress frame on the open response, an upstream health ping while a call is in flight, or surfacing elapsed-time + last-upstream-contact to the client. The constraint is absolute: whatever ships MUST NOT cap a legitimate long tools/call.\n\n**Process note — this is the fourth time in one session that a planned fix turned out to already exist or to be actively wrong, and the third caught by reading the code first.** The others: the pid/port liveness gates (already shipped, D-001); the WI-5244 schema check (already shipped, and it also passed on the impostor); and now the silence timeout. The plan item was written from the incident's SYMPTOM (\"it hung\") without reading the component that owns the behaviour — which is precisely the B-half failure this plan exists to eliminate, committed while writing the plan against it. A plan item asserting \"the system lacks X\" should be treated as a HYPOTHESIS until the owning code is read, exactly like any other claim of absence.\n\n### D-004 — D-004 — THE REAL FINDING: detection was never missing. DELIVERY is. Every guard this plan proposed already existed.\nDate: 2026-08-02\n**This supersedes the framing of Phase 2 and re-aims the rest of the plan. It is the most important thing found in this work.**\n\nI wrote this plan from the incident's symptoms and proposed five defensive mechanisms. I then read the code before implementing each. **All five already existed**, most of them shipped and passing during the outage:\n\n| I proposed | already existed as | since |\n|---|---|---|\n| pid liveness gate | `isPidAlive()` | 2026-07-19 |\n| port-listening gate | `isDiscoveredPortServed()` | 2026-08-01, 29h pre-incident |\n| impostor-DB detection | `validateDiscoveryTargetOnce()` (WI-5244) | pre-existing |\n| P-005 fail-fast timeout | `HANDSHAKE_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` (WI-6740) | pre-existing |\n| P-006 data-plane health probe | watchdog's DATA-PLANE probe (WI-6739) + SESSION-PLANE probe (EI-19299524366372518) | pre-existing / 2026-08-01 |\n\nSix mechanisms, counting the session-plane probe. **This system is exceptionally well defended, and it still produced a silent 13-minute fleet-wide outage that took hours to diagnose.** Any plan whose thesis is \"add a guard\" is therefore answering the wrong question — mine was, for four of its ten items.\n\n**The actual defect is that a guard's finding does not REACH the agent who needs it.** Every one of those mechanisms writes its verdict somewhere no one is reading at the moment of diagnosis:\n\n- the watchdog's data-plane probe → `~/.papercusp/mcp-proxy-watchdog.log`\n- the proxy → `~/.papercusp/mcp-proxy-failures.jsonl`\n- the WI-5244 impostor check → `console.error` into the operator's journal\n- — and, as shipped in Phase 1, **my own store-identity guard does exactly the same thing.**\n\nWI-6740's own header already states this conclusion without generalising it: 269 handshake stalls were recorded between 2026-07-10 and 2026-08-01, **every one followed by `recovered`**, and it went unfixed for three weeks because *\"the severity is invisible to the layer that observes it.\"* That sentence is the whole bug class. A `console.error` in a service journal is, to an agent debugging through MCP tools, indistinguishable from silence — which is why an outage with six active guards presented as nothing happening.\n\n**Re-aim:** the remaining work is DELIVERY, not detection. A detected fault must arrive on a surface the agent is already looking at — ideally attached to the very answer it invalidates. The highest-value instance is concrete and small: a `not_found` returned while a store-identity violation is latched should SAY SO, because that is the exact moment the wrong conclusion (\"my data was deleted\") gets formed.\n\n**Method note, since it is the transferable part.** Every one of these five was caught by the same cheap move — read the owning code before writing the fix — and each time the replacement was better than what I had planned: the identity probe became one extra column on a query that already runs, and P-005 avoided converting `build:typecheck` into a hard failure. A plan item asserting \"the system lacks X\" is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding, and costs seconds to falsify.\n\n### D-005 — D-005 — RETRACTION of P-007's premise, and the real defect: severity is dropped in the CLASSIFIER, not the delivery\nDate: 2026-08-03\n#### Retraction (owed, plain)\n\nMy P-007 checkpoint claimed the proxy failure ledger (`~/.papercusp/mcp-proxy-failures.jsonl`) was \"written since W8 ... and read by NOBODY, despite its own header inviting a health collector to ingest it.\" **That is false.** The health collector the header invites was BUILT in the same work item (W8/P-008) and is wired:\n\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/mcp-proxy-health.ts` — `readMcpProxyFailureTail()` + `summarizeMcpProxyHealth()`\n- consumed at `packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/compute.ts:1631`, feeding `InfraHealth.mcpProxy` → Infra panel → `operator_degraded` → the overall system light.\n\nSo the ledger has a reader, and a sustained hard-failure count already pages.\n\n#### Consequence: what I shipped in P-007 is a DUPLICATE, and less correct\n\n`packages/operator-core/lib/mcp-proxy-failure-summary.ts` re-implements the same bounded 256KB tail read against the same file. It is not merely redundant — it is **wrong in a measurable direction**, because it omits two filters the existing module has:\n\n1. **`isNonInstanceRecord` (`listenPort === 0`)** — EI-12102/EI-12211. These records come from short-lived desktop-sidecar/test proxies that no client is routed through. Measured in the live ledger's last 4MB: **2,373 of 13,189 records (18%) carry `listenPort: 0`** and my summary counts every one as a real failure.\n2. **`isBenignProbe` (408 heartbeat, GET-405 liveness)** — probe noise my summary folds into its `exhausted` tally.\n\nI verified the pollution independently before finding the existing filter: a sampled `shed_max_in_flight` record reads `{\"listenPort\":0,\"maxInFlight\":2}` — `maxInFlight: 2` is a TEST fixture value (the default is 200), i.e. tests are appending to the production ledger.\n\n**Disposition: delete `mcp-proxy-failure-summary.ts` + its test; `dev:service_health` delegates to the existing `summarizeMcpProxyHealth`.** Reuse-first, and it removes the over-count.\n\n#### The REAL defect (this is what P-005/P-007 should have found)\n\nD-004 said detection exists and delivery is the gap. Here both exist — and the severity is dropped **between** them, in the classifier.\n\n`summarizeMcpProxyHealth`'s classification is a three-branch chain (`mcp-proxy-health.ts:217-227`): `recovered` → soft; `exhausted_refused`/`upstream_error` → hard; `upstream_non2xx` → benign/stale-400/other. **Every other kind falls through into `byKind` only and lands in NO alarm class.**\n\nThe kind that falls through matters most: **`handshake_timeout_retry`** — WI-6740's marker for the upstream-silence stall that costs an agent session its ENTIRE tool plane for hours (an MCP client fetches the catalog once, at connect; a ~10s stall there leaves the session tool-dark for its whole life; 269 such stalls Jul 10–Aug 1). It cannot red the Infra panel, cannot page, and appears only as a raw tally.\n\nThis is WI-6740's own lesson recurring one layer up — its header says \"the severity is invisible to the layer that observes it.\" The observing layer now records it; the classifying layer discards it.\n\n**Verified live, not inferred:** the ledger's last 4MB contains 7 `handshake_timeout_retry` records attributed to `(pid 2704092, listenPort 9071)` — the live fleet-facing proxy — so this fires in production and is classified into nothing. Also unclassified: `shed_max_in_flight` (the proxy shedding agent load), `absorb_429`, `absorb_boot_status`.\n\n#### Method note — an unsound test I nearly reported\n\nI first tried to establish which guards were running by comparing each guard's `git log -S` **commit date** against the live proxy's process start time (proxy started 2026-08-01T20:01:12Z; `HANDSHAKE_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` commit-dated 2026-08-01T23:21:47Z) and was about to report \"WI-6740's fix is not running.\" **That inference is invalid on this repo:** git-sync commits the whole tree on a schedule, so a commit date lags the actual edit and cannot bound what a process loaded. The direct evidence (7 records from the live pid) proves the handshake timeout IS running.\n\nThe sound test is behavioural attribution — records keyed by `(pid, listenPort)` — never commit-date arithmetic. Same family as this repo's standing `git blame` warning.\n\n**Genuinely not running:** `heartbeat` has produced **zero** records in the entire 27MB ledger, so no in-flight liveness beat has ever been delivered to anyone. Cause not yet established (the timer skips ticks where nothing is in flight); tracked separately, not asserted here.\n\n### D-006 — D-006 — P-009 was ALREADY BUILT: the absence-premise detector exists and is measured. The residual was SURFACE COVERAGE, not detection.\nDate: 2026-08-03\n#### The finding\n\nP-009 asks to make the \"X never checks Y\" claim class cheap to falsify. **That detector already exists**, and it is better than what I would have written:\n\n`packages/operator-core/lib/premises-claim-port.ts` (plan `false-premise-in-prescriptive-artifacts-2026-08-02` P-001) derives ABSENCE-shaped premises from an artifact's own prose and surfaces them as `CheckEntry` rows. It is wired into two producers — `work_items:claim` (claim.ts:351) and `scheduler:get_next` (get_next.ts:748/766).\n\nIt was measured before wiring, not assumed: 31,090 work-item bodies, 1,442 (4.6%) carry an absence-shaped claim — i.e. it fires on ~1 claim in 22, not on everything. It strips fenced/inline code first, because the measured dominant false positive was an absence phrase inside a PASTED error string (`column \"payload\" does not exist`), which is evidence the author GATHERED, not their own assertion.\n\nIts own header states the asymmetry that makes this class worth special-casing: an absence claim is **expensive to act on** (you build the missing thing) and **cheap to falsify** (one search). No other premise shape has that ratio.\n\n**So the ruling: do NOT build a second absence detector. Reuse `detectAbsencePremises`.** A second opinion on this question would be a second bug — the same D-005 lesson, one plan item later.\n\n#### The genuine residual, and what I shipped\n\nThe port keys on the CLAIM event, sources `'work-item' | 'plan-item'`. **The carry surfaces are not covered**, and that is exactly where this plan's own incident happened.\n\nMy D-005 retraction: a `loop:checkpoint` note asserted \"the ledger is ... read by NOBODY\" as settled fact; the next wake read it back as fact and shipped ~180 lines on it; a reader existed one reverse-grep away. **No claim event was involved at any point**, so the claim-time port could not have fired.\n\nA carry-note deserves this more than a work-item body, not less:\n- it is prescriptive (it tells the next wake what to do),\n- it is re-injected verbatim and read as established fact,\n- for a COLD successor it is the only memory,\n- and unlike a work-item, **nobody else ever reviews it**.\n\nShipped: `PremiseSource` widened with `'carry-note'`, and an `absenceLint` leg added to `loop:checkpoint` beside the existing `checksLint`. Advisory, fail-open, suppressed when the author already parked the falsifier in `checks[]`.\n\n**Why it needed a NEW leg rather than the existing one:** `lintUncheckedExternalClaims` keys on a distinctive TOKEN (hash / WI-EI id / ISO instant) or an external-state noun. An absence claim carries none of those, so it passed straight through the lint that was already running on the very note that carried it.\n\n#### Two implementation notes worth keeping\n\n**Coverage is judged by WORD OVERLAP, not substring.** My first version compared the claim's leading 40 characters against the probe text. A test caught it: prose and check row are authored separately and routinely differ by a leading fragment, a rewrap, or a rendering prefix — so a substring test silently re-flags claims the author HAS parked, which trains them to ignore the lint. The failure mode of a nagging advisory lint is that it gets tuned out, so a false re-flag is more costly than a miss.\n\n**The lint's directive names the REVERSE direction explicitly** — *search for the thing you say is absent (who reads/calls/imports it), not just the thing you say ignores it*. That is the specific error in all three instances in this incident: a real search, over the wrong scope, reported as an absolute absence. Naming \"verify this\" without naming the scope reproduces the bug.\n\n#### Standing note for anyone filing an absence\n\n`improvements:capture`'s dedup does not see knowledge living in code comments and guard functions, so it returns \"no duplicates\" for conditions the codebase has already solved. Grep the tree before filing \"nothing detects X\".\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plantuml-egress-probe-scratch-2026-08-02","title":"SCRATCH — P-002 plantuml egress probe (delete after verification)","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SCRATCH — P-002 plantuml egress probe (delete after verification)\nslug: plantuml-egress-probe-scratch-2026-08-02\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\nScratch plan — exists only to render one plantuml block through the production vditor path.\n\n## Background\n\nThe block below is the probe. If the guard fails, viewing this page posts the diagram source\nbelow to plantuml.com.\n\n```plantuml\n@startuml\nAlice -> Bob: PLANTUML_EGRESS_PROBE_SENTINEL\nBob --> Alice: if you can read this on plantuml.com, the guard failed\n@enduml\n```\n\n## Phase 1 — probe\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Render this plan in /admin/plans and confirm zero requests to plantuml.com.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"prose-embedding-384-untrained-mrl-fix-2026-08-02","title":"Fix the prose surfaces' untrained MRL-384 embedding cut (EI-19301722864393687)","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Fix the prose surfaces' untrained MRL-384 embedding cut (EI-19301722864393687)\nslug: prose-embedding-384-untrained-mrl-fix-2026-08-02\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-04\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** **P-001..P-005 complete and LIVE. P-006 done except its refill, running now.**\n\n🟢 **MIGRATION 727 APPLIED 2026-08-03T04:41:29Z.** Verified against the live catalog, not the apply log: 12 columns at `vector(768)` — exactly the 12 targets; 4 left at `vector(384)` (`memory_vec_local`, the documented D-005 §6 exclusion, + the 3 inert snapshots); 2 at `vector(1024)` (`memory_vec_harrier`, untouched). The header's arithmetic balances exactly: **16 − 1 − 3 = 12**. `schema_migrations` row present (sha256 `8ff1ba2e…`), 246/246 views recreated, 4/4 HNSW indexes rebuilt, `memory_canonical` 32,641 rows preserved. The 384/768 write-rejection skew — silently dropping ~1 embed/30s for hours — **stopped dead at 04:42Z (0 since)**.\n\n**Three blockers cleared to land it:**\n1. **`db:migrate { confirm:true }` is BROKEN here — EI-19404227117727730 (major).** Two calls hung 300s, never spawned `psql`, Postgres idle throughout. An aborted call also holds `exclusive(db-schema)` its full 10-min TTL, so a retry looks identical. Applied via the tool's own documented fallback, `schema_migrations` INSERT in the SAME transaction.\n2. **Deadlock ×3** at `DROP INDEX work_items_embedding_hnsw_idx` — the ~60s rewrite window before reaching `work_items` lets readers queue into a cycle (112 blocked locks measured). **Fix: pre-lock the whole footprint at t=0 — all 246 dependent views FIRST, then the 12 base tables**, matching reader order (view→base).\n3. **A real defect in 727**, masked by that deadlock: `USING NULL` cannot widen a `NOT NULL` column (`memory_vec_{gemma,openai}.vector`). Fixed in-file (DELETE rows, narrowed to `memory_vec_*`, RAISE otherwise). ⚠ **Never drop the NOT NULL instead** — it applies cleanly, looks successful, and permanently strands every row: both refill paths select on row **ABSENCE**, never a NULL vector.\n\n⚠ **Arming a migration is FLEET-VISIBLE** — it becomes eligible for `release:checkpoint-run`'s preflight (EI-19404620261958999, resolved).\n\n**Next:** **P-006 step 5 — THE REFILL — is the only P-006 work left, and it is RUNNING.**\n\nDriver: `scripts/refill-prose-vectors-727.mjs` (new), launched 04:49:05Z, log `/tmp/refill-727.log`. EI-19375205903428632's real point was the per-sweep **fairness cap**; raising that cap fixes throughput *without* forking the sweep, keeping embedder resolution, the dims-fit guard, the org pool, liveness probes, spaceAware routing, per-target error isolation and the overlap guard.\n\n- **Idempotent + resumable** (selects on \"vector missing OR different embedder\"), so re-launch simply continues:\n  `set -a; . apps/operator/.env.local; set +a; nohup npx tsx scripts/refill-prose-vectors-727.mjs > /tmp/refill-727.log 2>&1 &`\n- **Wall time only** — gemma runs locally on the :3384 sidecar; no API tokens, and the OpenAI-only spend governor does not bind.\n- **Measured 04:49→04:51: ~4 vectors/s** (plans 213, docs 256, recipes 10 from zero) against **398,834** rows ⇒ **~28h**. Until it catches up the prose surfaces are **LEXICAL-ONLY — degraded, not broken** (hybrid keeps its full-text leg).\n- Too slow? The 10× lever is **EI-19363236885307403** (idle RTX 3090, CUDA provider fails on missing `libcudnn.so.9`) — **NOT** batching (EI-19363253682489176: naive batching is 5× SLOWER, transformers.js pads to the longest text in the batch).\n\n**Then, both now unblocked by the apply:**\n- **P-007** — verify prose search end-to-end in the Tauri shell (`cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev`, driven headlessly per `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e`).\n- **EI-19366433214266471** — the integration test asserting live schema widths match `PROSE_VECTOR_COLUMNS`; it would have landed red before 727, and will now pass.\n\n## Background\n\n`gemma-embedder.ts` sets `GEMMA_TARGET_DIMS = 384` and MRL-truncates\nEmbeddingGemma-300m's native 768 to fit the existing `vector(384)` prose columns.\nThe docblock justifies this as \"a PREFIX of the vector is itself a valid lower-dim\nembedding.\"\n\nThat premise is only half right. Per google/embeddinggemma-300m's model card the\nOFFICIALLY TRAINED MRL dims are **768 / 512 / 256 / 128**. **384 is not among\nthem** — it is an untrained cut sitting between two trained points. MRL nesting is\noptimized at specific targets; intermediate prefixes degrade gracefully but are\nnot optimized for.\n\nPublished degradation curve (MTEB Multilingual v2, Mean(Task)):\n768 -> 61.15 · 512 -> 60.71 · 256 -> 59.68 · 128 -> 58.23. 384 is unmeasured and,\nbeing untrained, may sit BELOW the 512/256 interpolation rather than on it.\n\nBlast radius: every prose surface (5 shared-column surfaces, 20k+ stored vectors)\nplus `search:semantic` / `search:fulltext` / the user search route.\n\nSuspected knock-on: P-006 measured harrier@384's rejection margin collapsing to\n.0705 vs gemma's .1576 — that comparison was run at this same untrained cut, so\nthe harrier-vs-gemma prose verdict may itself be confounded.\n\nCandidate replacements, all Apache-2.0 with onnx-community exports:\n- `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-97m-multilingual-r2` — NATIVELY 384-dim (no\n  truncation at all), 97M params (3x smaller than gemma-300m), 32k context vs\n  gemma's 2048.\n- `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-311m-multilingual-r2` — lists 384 as an\n  EXPLICITLY trained MRL dim; same weight class as gemma-300m.\n- `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` — MRL trained across 32..1024, so 384 is a trained\n  point.\n\nThis plan is MEASURE-FIRST and is expected to terminate cheaply at P-002 if the\n384 loss turns out to be inside noise. Do not adopt anything on the strength of a\nmodel card.\n\n## Phase 1 — measure\n\n- **P-001** `done` Build a PROSE-surface gold set (query -> relevant doc labels) over the real prose corpora (docs, plans, session turns), sized for a margin-outside-noise verdict. Verified: tsc on libs/generic/memory reports 0 errors in gemma-embedder.ts (remaining workspace errors are pre-existing, in mem0-backend.test.ts / reembed.test.ts, untouched).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Every embedder DECLARES its trained dims; an untrained target needs a written acknowledgement, and the builder derives its constant from the declaration\nDate: 2026-08-02\nItems: P-008, P-004, P-005\n\nThe root cause of EI-19301722864393687 was not a wrong line of code — it was an assertion nobody made. A docblock claimed any prefix of an MRL model was \"a valid lower-dim embedding\", the target dim was a bare `384` sitting next to the truncation call, and nothing in the code disagreed. An untrained cut still yields a usable vector, so nothing threw and no test could red. The convention below replaces that advisory prose with a structural rule.\n\n**The rule.** `libs/generic/memory/src/embedder-dims.ts` declares, for every embedder mode, its `nativeDims`, its `mrl` support, the `trainedDims` it can actually emit, and the `targetDims` we configure. `validateEmbedderDimSpec` (asserted by embedder-dims.test.ts) fails when a target is not a trained dim UNLESS an explicit `untrainedCut { reason, trackedBy }` is declared. Adding a mode without a spec is a TYPE error (the table is keyed by the `EmbedderMode` union); declaring one badly is a TEST error.\n\n**Three properties that make it bite, each earned from how the original failed:**\n\n1. **The builders DERIVE their constants from the table** (`GEMMA_TARGET_DIMS`, `HARRIER_NATIVE_DIMS`), rather than restating them. A declaration that can drift from the code it describes is just a second docblock — which is precisely what already failed. Deriving makes the declared dim and the truncated-to dim the same constant, so a sound declaration cannot describe code doing something else.\n\n2. **A STALE acknowledgement is itself a violation.** If someone later moves gemma to a trained dim but leaves the ack behind, that ack would silently pre-authorize the NEXT untrained cut. So `targetDims` being trained WHILE an ack is present fails the guard, forcing the exemption to be removed with the fix that made it unnecessary.\n\n3. **`mrl: 'continuous'` keeps the guard honest.** OpenAI's `dimensions` parameter applies the trained MRL server-side, so text-embedding-3-small@384 is genuinely supported, not a hand-rolled prefix. A guard that flagged every non-native width would be noise and would have been switched off long before it caught anything — so the model distinguishes `none` / `discrete` / `continuous` rather than treating all truncation as suspect.\n\n**Consequence for Phase 1/2 (this is why it was done first, out of order).** Whatever dim P-004's measurement selects, enacting it in P-005 forces the declaration and its acknowledgement to be updated in the SAME edit — the verdict cannot be applied while leaving a stale justification behind. And if the verdict is (a) \"384 loss is within noise, close it\", the ack is what preserves the reasoning instead of the plan closing and the rationale evaporating.\n\n**Scope note.** This is a QUALITY guard, not a correctness one. An untrained cut still produces a coherent, usable space; the acknowledgement exists to make the tradeoff deliberate and reviewable. Harrier publishes no MRL at all, so its exploratory `dims: 384` variant is an untrained cut by this definition — `isTrainedDim` reports it as such, and it must still win the P-001 gate before any prose-surface use.\n\n### D-002 — The prose gold set is sized for DECISION-RELEVANT effects, scored PAIRED on reciprocal rank — and \"within noise\" must never be reported as \"equivalent\"\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\n\nP-001 asked for a gold set \"sized for a margin-outside-noise verdict\". Sizing it required naming the statistic first, and the answer changes how P-002/P-003 must be run and how P-004 may be worded.\n\n#### 1. The comparison is PAIRED, so the statistic is not two proportions\n\nEvery leg is scored on the SAME corpus with the SAME queries; only the embedder varies. Comparing two independent proportions discards that pairing and badly understates sensitivity. The correct tests are McNemar (binary hit@1) and a paired bootstrap (continuous reciprocal rank).\n\n#### 2. MEASURED baseline (gemma@384, the incumbent, run 2026-08-02)\n\n`--corpus prose --legs sidecar:gemma` over prose-corpus.v1 (2029 docs) / prose-gold-set.v1 (134 queries):\n\n| class | n | R@1 | R@5 | MRR |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| ALL_ANSWERABLE | 122 | .205 | .385 | .289 |\n| exact-identifier | 90 | .189 | .322 | .256 |\n| lexical-gap | 24 | .208 | .500 | .342 |\n| session-start-intent | 8 | .375 | .750 | .504 |\n\nrejection margin .1791 (answerable top1 .4958 vs hard-negative .3167) — comparable to gemma's .1576 on the memory corpus. 961.6s to embed the corpus (474ms/doc).\n\n**The corpus sits in a usable operating range: no ceiling, no floor, and ZERO complete misses across all 122 answerable queries.** That is the design validating itself — R@1 is 400x random (1/2029) yet nowhere near saturation, so both a degradation and an improvement have room to show. Every class is discriminating, including exact-identifier at .189, which confirms that excluding opaque numeric ids avoided the floor artifact.\n\n#### 3. What this gold set can actually resolve\n\nMeasured per-query RR spread is **sd = 0.389** (this supersedes an earlier estimate of 0.10-0.20 in the first version of this decision — the real spread is much wider). What governs a PAIRED test is sd of the DIFFERENCE, which shrinks with the correlation between legs: sd(diff) = sd * sqrt(2(1-rho)).\n\n95% CI half-width on delta-MRR at N=122, against a baseline MRR of .289:\n\n| rho between legs | sd(diff) | half-width | as % of baseline |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 0.80 | .246 | .0437 | 15.1% |\n| 0.90 | .174 | .0309 | 10.7% |\n| 0.95 | .123 | .0218 | 7.6% |\n| 0.98 | .078 | .0138 | 4.8% |\n\nSame-family truncation legs (gemma@768/512/384/256) should correlate high, so expect roughly **5-11% relative resolution**. A different MODEL (granite, Qwen) correlates less, so its CI will be wider — report the observed rho, do not assume it.\n\nBy contrast, binary hit@1 McNemar at N=122 only detects ~6.3-10.8pp (discordance .08-.20); N=250 would be needed for 4.7-7.7pp.\n\n**Therefore P-002/P-003 MUST report the paired reciprocal-rank bootstrap CI as the primary verdict, not a bare R@1 delta.** embedder-eval-cli.ts now emits per-query rank/RR/top1 for exactly this reason; class-mean aggregates alone cannot produce a CI, so the previous output shape could not have supported this verdict at all.\n\n#### 4. The interpretation rule P-004 is bound by\n\n**\"Within noise\" means \"no decision-relevant loss detected at this power\" — NOT \"384 is equivalent to 768\".** Branch (a) must state the minimum detectable effect alongside the null. Reporting an underpowered null as proven equivalence is the most likely way this plan reaches a confidently wrong conclusion, because it terminates the plan cheaply and looks like a clean finding.\n\nThis is acceptable because the decision needs no arbitrary precision: branch (c) proposes a vector(384)->vector(512) migration across five surfaces and 20k+ vectors, worth doing only on a LARGE effect.\n\n#### 5. Read the classes separately\n\nexact-identifier is 90 of 122 answerable, so ALL_ANSWERABLE is identifier-dominated and mostly measures rare-token preservation — do not read it as semantic quality. lexical-gap (24) is where MRL truncation damage actually shows, but at n=24 it is DIRECTIONAL EVIDENCE ONLY (a standalone binary verdict needs ~26pp). If lexical-gap and exact-identifier disagree in sign, the honest report is that the pooled number is uninterpretable and more lexical-gap queries are needed before P-004 can rule.\n\n#### 6. Corpus design (why the sample is cluster-preserving)\n\nOn the live index a doc section's nearest neighbours are its OWN PAGE's siblings ('Revisions > Round 4' vs 'Round 5' cos .7299; 'Memory topology > Why the evidence' vs '> The shape' .8294). Random row sampling scatters those clusters, deletes the confusable material, and drives every leg toward R@1=1.0 — a CEILING ARTIFACT indistinguishable from a real null, terminating the plan on a measurement that measured nothing. So the sampling unit is the whole page/session/plan; 111 of 113 sampled doc pages are multi-section.\n\nRejected alternative: mining hard distractors by nearest-neighbour lookup in the live embeddings. It preserves difficulty, but the neighbours come from GEMMA'S OWN space, so the corpus would be built from the incumbent's confusions and biased against it. Page-clustering is structural — no embedding space involved, no circularity.\n\n### D-003 — P-002 measured: the live gemma@384 cut costs ~19-21% of prose retrieval MRR — real and decision-relevant, but NOT because 384 is untrained\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\n\nMEASURED on prose-corpus.v1 (2029 docs) / prose-gold-set.v1 (122 answerable), ONE forward pass at native 768 with the narrower widths derived by MRL truncation:\n\n| width | trained | R@1 | R@5 | MRR | rej.margin | lexical-gap MRR |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 768 | yes | .2377 | .4836 | .3492 | .1702 | .5014 |\n| 512 | yes | .2459 | .4836 | .3435 | .1640 | .3870 |\n| **384 (LIVE)** | **NO** | .2049 | .3852 | .2889 | .1791 | .3414 |\n| 256 | yes | .1230 | .3197 | .2000 | .1573 | .1678 |\n\n#### Primary verdict — paired RR bootstrap vs the incumbent 384 (D-002)\n\n- 384 -> 512: **+.0546 MRR, 95% CI [.0165, .0935]**, rho .851 = **+18.9% relative**\n- 384 -> 768: **+.0603 MRR, 95% CI [.0210, .1022]**, rho .830 = **+20.9% relative**\n\nBoth CIs exclude zero and both effects are ~2x the .03 decision-relevant threshold. Measurements taken before editing changed the inputs D-004 reasoned from.\n\n#### 1. The re-embed corpus is ~395,000 vectors, not \"20k+\"\n\nP-006 says \"the 20k+ prose vectors\". A WIDTH change cannot migrate incrementally; a MODEL swap can\n\nQuery legs filter `embedding_mode = <active>` (docs/semantic-leg.ts:54, work_items/semantic-dupe-guard.ts:119) — what migration 530's per-row mode discriminator is for: a SAME-WIDTH model swap converges row-by-row with no outage, since un-migrated rows simply aren't matched.\n\nA WIDTH change has no such path. That is better than today, where a fallback to local silently re-embeds the column into a weaker space — but it is a real behaviour change, recorded here rather than discovered later.\n\n### D-006 — P-006 apply mechanism: the db:migrate MCP TOOL, not `npm run db:migrate` (which does not exist)\nDate: 2026-08-02\nCorrecting two operative errors in P-006's own instructions, both verified 2026-08-02 19:10Z.\n\n1. **`npm run db:migrate` DOES NOT EXIST** on this tree — there is no such npm script anywhere.
