It is not: `migration-runner.js:105` selects with `if (applied.has(f)) continue` — i.e. anything NOT RECORDED, never \"everything after the max applied\". Unparking 727 later still applies it. Parking works because `:79` filters `.endsWith('.sql')`, so `.sql.PENDING-CODE-DEPLOY` is invisible to the runner.\n\n⚠ Renaming to `.sql` ARMS auto-apply at the next operator boot (728/729 auto-applied unattended at 17:58Z/18:15Z). So the rename is the trigger — do it only once the 768 code is live, per D-005's ordering constraint.\n\n**Migration 727 coverage is verified complete**: all 12 targets = the 10 `PROSE_VECTOR_COLUMNS` + `memory_vec_gemma`/`memory_vec_openai` (which move with their mode's `targetDims`; openai is 768, gemma native 768). `memory_vec_local` (384) and `memory_vec_harrier` (1024) are deliberately excluded and documented. The 10-vs-12 asymmetry is DELIBERATE — see the standing fact; deleting the two `memory_vec_*` entries to \"fix drift\" would strand both spaces at 384.\n\nAlso note P-006's ITEM TEXT is stale: it says \"20k+ prose vectors\" (measured ~414k) and \"dual-read or swap-on-complete, not a truncate-and-refill\" — which D-005 established is IMPOSSIBLE for a WIDTH change, since pgvector cannot cast between widths and the ALTER drops every vector at once. The `Now`/`Next` sections carry the correct account; the item text does not.\n\n### D-007 — The P-006 code-is-live gate requires positionsMarker.deployed.present, NOT serving.startedSinceCodeChange alone\nDate: 2026-08-02\nMigration 727's own TO-ENACT header gated step 1 on `serving.startedSinceCodeChange must be true`. That gate is BROKEN IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION and has been corrected in the file.\n\nMEASURED 2026-08-02 19:41Z, both legs in the SAME dev:pipeline_position result for packages/operator-core/lib/search/prose-vector-dims.ts:\n  serving.startedSinceCodeChange = true\n  positionsMarker.deployed.present = false  (\"a genuine miss, not a newer-commit artifact\")\n\nSo the old gate was ALREADY SATISFIED while the 768 code was provably not deployed. Following it would have applied 727 — dropping ~414k vectors — with the deployed code still emitting 384, i.e. exactly the migration-first ordering the same header warns costs an outage of unbounded length (every refill write fails until the code ships, which is gate-dependent and can be many hours).\n\nWHY THE FIELD MISLEADS: the two legs answer different questions and only their CONJUNCTION means \"my code is live\". startedSinceCodeChange says the serving process is not stale relative to ITS OWN checkout — a statement about a PROCESS, silent on whether YOUR change is in that checkout. positionsMarker.deployed.present greps the deployed sha for YOUR marker.\n\nRULE: gate on BOTH, in order — positionsMarker.deployed.present === true, THEN serving.startedSinceCodeChange === true.\n\nThis does not contradict the repo guide's \"is the running process executing my code -> serving.startedSinceCodeChange\" row; that row steers away from the git-side positions.deployed boolean, and the marker leg is a different, stronger read.\n\nAlso corrected in the same header (D-006 restated where an enactor will actually see it): step 3 said `npm run db:migrate`, which DOES NOT EXIST — the lever is the db:migrate MCP tool. The only migration-ish root scripts are db:next-migration, lint:migrations, lint:migration-forward-compat, so the old instruction fails as a bare npm \"Missing script\" and reads like a broken environment rather than a wrong instruction.\n\n### D-008 — The canonical memory-vector sweep covers LOCAL rows too — a width wipe is not a mode switch (WI-7326)\nDate: 2026-08-03\n727's header justified wiping `memory_vec_gemma`/`memory_vec_openai` on the premise that \"the embed-backfill sweep refills them\" and the refill is \"self-healing\". **That premise was false for these two tables**, and the result was 32,641 canonical memories with 0 vectors and no automatic path back — workspace `memory:search` running lexical-only with no error and no log line.\n\n**Ruling: the background memory sweep's scope is now ALL recallable canonical rows, not just federated ones.** `memory/federated-vec-backfill.ts` -> `memory/canonical-vec-backfill.ts`; the `c.source_hive IS NOT NULL` predicate is removed.\n\n**Why this APPLIES the old decision rather than overriding it.** The exclusion's own docblock stated its discriminator: local rows missing a vector are mode-switch residue and belong to the user-initiated /reembed pass, whereas \"federated rows have no such path — NOTHING ELSE WILL EVER EMBED THEM.\" That last clause is the real criterion. 727 created a case its author had no reason to foresee: a SAME-MODE wipe, which no path repairs.\n\n- `reembedMemories` throws `reembed_noop_same_mode` when from === to, and otherwise selects `FROM memory_canonical JOIN <fromTable>` — it copies a vector between modes, it cannot rebuild one from text.\n- `embed-backfill`'s TARGETS sweep only ever runs `UPDATE <table> SET <col>` over rows that already exist. 727 had to DELETE these rows (`vector` is NOT NULL; pgvector cannot cast widths), so an emptied join table stays empty forever. **A TARGETS entry here is structurally inexpressible, not merely missing** — and it would report a clean `scanned:0` pass while doing nothing.\n- The sweep matched `source_hive IS NOT NULL`; measured 2026-08-03: 32,641 local rows, **0 federated**. It matched nothing at all, permanently.\n\nObserved live while the P-006 refill driver ran: plans 213->510 and recipes 10->536 climbing (TARGETS surfaces, working correctly) with `memory_vec_gemma`/`openai` at 0, unmoved. The two halves of 727's wipe set have different refill mechanisms, which is exactly why one could complete while the other stayed empty.\n\n**On the quota concern the old scope protected:** it is bounded by BATCH, not by which rows are eligible, and the catch-up is one-time before converging to an empty sweep. gemma/local are local-sidecar compute (free); the whole 3,854-row live backlog under `openai` is ~200k tokens ~= $0.004. BATCH raised 25 -> 100 (env `PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_VEC_BACKFILL_BATCH`): 25 was sized for a federated trickle and would take ~13h to clear a cold start; 100 sequential embeds is ~22s of a 300s tick (<8% duty cycle) and clears it in ~3.2h. The eager, progress-reporting /reembed route is unchanged for a user who wants a mode switch completed now.\n\n**Guard against the class, not the instance.** `prose-vector-dims.ts` gains `PROSE_MEMORY_VEC_COLUMNS` (DERIVED from `PROSE_ELIGIBLE_MODES`, so a newly prose-eligible mode automatically joins it) and `WIDTH_MIGRATION_WIPE_SET` = that plus `PROSE_VECTOR_COLUMNS`. The pre-existing refill-coverage guard was written against `PROSE_VECTOR_COLUMNS` alone — correct on its own terms, but strictly narrower than what a width migration wipes, which is precisely how this got through. Three assertions now cover both halves, deliberately non-circular: base-table columns need a TARGETS entry; each prose-eligible mode must have `VEC_TABLE[mode]` naming the wiped table and `MODE_DIMS[mode] === PROSE_VECTOR_DIMS` (that width guard RETURNS FALSE rather than throwing, so a stale entry makes every refill write a silent no-op); and `memory_vec_*` must NOT appear in TARGETS, catching the tempting non-fix.\n\nVerified: 24 tests green (16 unit + 8 real-PG). Falsified by re-adding the `source_hive` filter — 6 of 8 integration tests red, including the named WI-7326 guard — then restored byte-identical.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"published-routine-set-capability-2026-08-02","title":"Publish the SET of active routine names in presence, so each election asks its OWN capability question (git-sync integrator vs cadence loops)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Publish the SET of active routine names in presence, so each election asks its OWN capability question (git-sync integrator vs cadence loops)\nslug: published-routine-set-capability-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all six items done (P-001..P-006), each verified and closed with evidence.\n\nThe git-sync integrator election now asks its OWN capability question: `requiresRoutine: 'git-sync'` against the peer's published `shared_presence.active_routines` (mig 724), instead of borrowing `routineHostsOnly` — a CADENCE-loop bit that is null on every row here, so the old narrowing excluded ALL peers and left integrator arbitration OFF rather than tightened (WI-6996).\n\nLanded:\n- P-002 mig 724 `active_routines text[]` (applied, fence_seq 271); P-001 the publish path (resolver → announce → wire → gossip signing → projection).\n- P-003 `requiresRoutine` on LockAuthorityDeps; `effectiveEligibility` generalized to a NECESSARY-CONDITIONS list so every opted-in predicate intersects (with each other and with `eligibleDevices`). Byte-identical behaviour when nothing is opted in.\n- P-004 `routineHostsOnly` DERIVED from the set (∩ CADENCE_RUNNER_ROUTINES) **with a fallback to the legacy bit when the set is ABSENT** — see D-006.\n- P-005 the git-sync call site swapped; comment block rewritten.\n- P-006 16 new lock-authority tests (63/63 total), incl. both selectors, the intersections, and the empty-capable degenerate case.\n\n⚠ D-006 is the one thing a successor must not undo: `runs_routines` stays DUAL-PUBLISHED. The reader prefers the set and falls back to the bit, because a pre-mig-724 peer publishes the bit and no set; and symmetrically, if new nodes stopped publishing the bit an OLD reader would see null and exclude them. Removing the column is the CONTRACT half and is deliberately NOT done.\n\nVerified: lock-authority 63/63 · hive-single-runner + cadence-runner-capability 35/35 · git-sync-action + lock-authority-hive 69/69 · lint:tsc EXIT=0 on every changed file. Routine name confirmed in PG as literally 'git-sync' (note `foreign-git-sync` also exists, so exact array membership — not substring — is load-bearing).\n\n**Next:** Nothing on this plan. Follow-on candidates, both explicitly OUT of scope here: (1) the CONTRACT half — stop publishing `runs_routines` and drop the column, only once no reader depends on it (D-006); (2) D-005's deferred options-object refactor of `buildPresenceAnnounceRow`, which was waiting on P-004 'collapsing the two into one derived value' — dual-publish means that never happens, so it is now unblocked-but-independent.\n\n## Background\n\n`shared_presence.runs_routines` (migration 682, EI-18761517980514694) is a boolean meaning \"this node fires the pot's autonomous CADENCE loops\". It is published only for a node with an ACTIVE routine NAMED in `cadence-runner-capability.ts` `CADENCE_RUNNER_ROUTINES` — today exactly `['gym-cycle','scout-cycle']`.\n\nWI-6996 (`git-sync-action.ts:2716`, db1542fa6f) pointed the **git-sync integrator** election at that bit via `LockAuthorityDeps.routineHostsOnly`. That election asks a different question. Two measured consequences (EI-19330771435294981):\n\n1. **Today it disables the election.** gym-cycle is inactive on this pot and scout-cycle does not exist, so the bit is null on every live presence row. `effectiveEligibility` returns ∅, `withEligibility` excludes every row, and every node reaching the election elects itself. Peer arbitration for the integrator is OFF, not tightened.\n2. **It is a time-bomb.** Arm gym-cycle (or scout-cycle) on a peer that also holds a device namespace in the bare store, and that peer becomes the only `capable` device, wins on the strength of a bit about a different loop, and the ~5.5h WI-6996 freeze returns — with the same self-disabling detector (`origin-freshness-watchdog.ts` compares canonical-vs-origin, which this freeze class pins equal).\n\nDeleting the opt-in is NOT the fix: it restores the exact freeze, because `eligibleDevices` at that call site is a HISTORICAL fact (a peer namespace that ever published a head stays eligible forever), not a liveness one.\n\n### What the integrator actually requires (verified against the code, not assumed)\n\nRead from `runIntegratorTick` (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync/pot-git/integrator-tick.ts:48-144`), the requirement splits in two:\n\n- **(i) holds the store** — already covered by `eligibleDevices` (self iff `rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds; a peer iff its device namespace exists locally).\n- **(ii) will actually tick** — checked by NOTHING today. A node can satisfy (i) forever while its git-sync routine is disabled or absent. That is exactly the WI-6996 failure: the iMac had a namespace in the store and no papercusp integrator.\n\n\"Has an ACTIVE `git-sync` routine at `(workspace_id, install_slug)`\" is precisely (ii). It is node-local and locally knowable from `harness_shared.routines` (no `fed_ts`/`fed_hlc`), at the same grain `defaultHasActiveCadenceRoutine` already queries — so it must be PUBLISHED to be usable by peers, which is what this plan does.\n\n### The publish path (six touch points, mapped)\n\n1. `cadence-runner-capability.ts` → `nodeRunsCadenceLoops(workspaceId, harnessSlug)` → boolean\n2. `sync/hyperbee/wire-presence.ts:211` binds it as `resolveRunsRoutines`; L421-436 stamps it (`catch ⇒ null`)\n3. `sync/hyperbee/presence-announce.ts:114/131` → wire row `runs_routines: runsRoutines === true ? true : null`\n4. `sync/hyperbee/projections/presence.ts:81-85` validates (tolerates undefined/null for pre-upgrade peers), L112-129 upserts\n5. `authority/lock-authority.ts` `queryPresenceRows` L328 selects it; `effectiveEligibility` L267-280 consumes it\n6. `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/682-shared-presence-runs-routines.sql` is the column\n\n## Phase 1 — publish the set, derive both predicates from it\n\n- **P-001** `done` Publish `active_routines` (this node's ACTIVE routine names at `(workspace_id, install_slug)`) through the presence path: resolver in `cadence-runner-capability.ts` alongside `nodeRunsCadenceLoops`, wire row in `presence-announce.ts`, binding in `wire-presence.ts`, validation + upsert in `projections/presence.ts`. Additive optional field — `projections/presence.ts:81-85` already tolerates an absent field from pre-upgrade peers, so wire compat is free. importance: high blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-7038 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Migration for `shared_presence.active_routines text[]` (nullable). ⚠ Allocate the number with `node scripts/next-migration.mjs --name <slug> --intent \"...\"` — never `ls sql/ | tail` (EI-6843) — then `node libs/papercusp/libs/db/scripts/pull-schema.mjs`. Apply via `db:migrate`, never a raw `psql -f`. — note: mig 724 applied via db:migrate (fence_seq 271, sha 2fdd7420); active_routines text[] live; pull-schema run\n- **P-003** `done` `lock-authority.ts`: select `active_routines` in `queryPresenceRows`, add `LockAuthorityDeps.requiresRoutine?: string`, and fold it into `effectiveEligibility` the same way `routineHostsOnly` folds (INTERSECTION with `eligibleDevices` when both are given). blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-7046 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Derive `runs_routines` from the set instead of publishing it separately: `routineHostsOnly` ⇒ `active_routines ∩ CADENCE_RUNNER_ROUTINES ≠ ∅`. Semantics must stay IDENTICAL to today's bit — do not widen it. Keep the column readable for pre-upgrade peers that still publish only the boolean. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-7091 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Swap the git-sync call site (`git-sync-action.ts:2716`) from `routineHostsOnly: true` to `requiresRoutine: 'git-sync'`, and rewrite the EI-19330771435294981 comment block above it to describe the new mechanism. ⚠ This file is hot — check `locks:list` first. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-7095 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Tests: extend the `routineHostsOnly … empty-capable degenerate case` describe in `authority/__tests__/lock-authority.test.ts` to cover `requiresRoutine` on both selectors (argmin + HRW), the intersection with `eligibleDevices`, and the empty-capable degenerate case for the new predicate. Add projection round-trip coverage for the new field including a pre-upgrade peer that omits it. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-7071 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 `accepted` Publish the SET of active routine names, not a second boolean column\n\n`cadence-runner-capability.ts:22-32` measured and REJECTED widening the shared bit — marking a node capable because it runs `git-sync` would make a gym-less node look gym-capable and ship a no-op. That argument is against widening a SHARED predicate; it is not an argument against publishing the underlying facts and letting each caller ask its own question. Publishing the set gives git-sync a real predicate while the cadence predicate keeps its exact current meaning. One mechanism, two callers, no second column.\n\n### D-002 `accepted` Do NOT delete `routineHostsOnly: true` from the git-sync call site before P-005 lands\n\nRemoving it restores the exact WI-6996 freeze, because `eligibleDevices` is a historical fact, not a liveness one. Leaving the (currently election-disabling) opt-in ON is the deliberate lesser evil until a real predicate exists.\n\n### D-003 `accepted` Do NOT add `'git-sync'` to `CADENCE_RUNNER_ROUTINES`\n\nMeasured and rejected at `cadence-runner-capability.ts:22-32`; it regresses EI-18761517980514694 by trading this freeze for a dark gym.\n\n### D-004 `accepted` Reject namespace-ref freshness as the liveness signal\n\nA device namespace head advances when that device COMMITS, not when it integrates, so a stale head does not imply a dead integrator. Capability must be published; it cannot be inferred from the store — the same conclusion `cadence-runner-capability.ts` reached about cycle evidence.\n\n### D-005 — `accepted` P-001 publish-path shape — the four choices P-003/P-004/P-005 inherit\nDate: 2026-08-02\nSettled while implementing P-001; recorded because later lanes build directly on each.\n\n**1. `dbosLaunches()` gates the SET, not just the boolean.** `nodeActiveRoutines` returns `[]` on a request-only host even when routines are armed — an armed routine on a host that never launches the routine host NEVER FIRES, so publishing it would advertise a capability the node lacks (the WI-6996 shape). This is also what makes P-004 semantics-preserving: `set ∩ CADENCE_RUNNER_ROUTINES ≠ ∅` is then EXACTLY today's `dbosLaunches() && ∃ active cadence routine`. Pinned by the `nodeActiveRoutines ⊃ nodeRunsCadenceLoops` describe (5 cases incl. the dbos leg) so P-004 cannot silently widen or narrow the predicate.\n\n**2. Empty set collapses to `null` on the wire**, mirroring `runs_routines === true ? true : null` (mig 682). An empty set and \"unknown\" are the identical verdict to every consumer — not a candidate for any election — so collapsing both keeps a routine-less node's SIGNED frame byte-identical to the pre-mig-724 form. Consumers in P-003 must therefore treat absent/null/empty as one case, never distinguish them.\n\n**3. The set rides `presenceFrameSigningBytes`, appended LAST and emitted only when present.** Required: the git-sync integrator election decides candidacy from it, so an unsigned field would let a tamperer claim `'git-sync'` on any peer and capture the lease. Appending last + omitting when absent preserves cross-version verification. NOTE: neither capability field had ANY signing test before this — the wire-compat claim in the code comment was unpinned. Now covered by 5 tests (byte-identical-when-absent, empty≠populated, two tamper cases, order-sensitivity).\n\n**4. The resolver dedupes + sorts.** Determinism is the resolver's job, not the reader's, so an unchanged routine set can never churn the signed bytes on incidental row ordering. Result is frozen — it is cached by reference and handed to every announce, so a caller mutation would silently rewrite what this node advertises.\n\n**Deferred deliberately:** `buildPresenceAnnounceRow` now takes a 6th positional param. A trailing bag of nullables is a smell, but TS makes a swap a compile error (boolean|null vs readonly string[]|null) and P-004 collapses the two into one derived value — fold them into an options object THEN, not now, to keep this diff reviewable during a red-gate window.\n\n### D-006 — P-004 is EXPAND/CONTRACT — the reader derivation keeps a runs_routines fallback, and the publisher keeps dual-publishing\nDate: 2026-08-02\nDate: 2026-08-02\nSettled while starting P-004; it changes the shape of BOTH P-004 and P-005, so it is recorded before implementing.\n\nP-004 says `routineHostsOnly` => `active_routines INTERSECT CADENCE_RUNNER_ROUTINES != empty`. D-005 point 1 justifies that as semantics-preserving — but that argument is about the PUBLISHER (dbosLaunches() gates the set, so a new node's set and bit always agree). The READER faces a case D-005 does not cover.\n\n**Hazard 1 (reader).** A pre-mig-724 peer publishes `runs_routines: true` with `active_routines` NULL. Derive purely from the set and that peer is silently INELIGIBLE — which is exactly the WI-6996 narrowing failure this plan exists to remove, reintroduced by its own fix. D-005 point 2 (\"treat absent/null/empty as one case\") is correct for `requiresRoutine`, where absent really does mean not-a-candidate; it must NOT be carried across to the derived cadence predicate, where absent means unknown-but-the-bit-still-speaks.\n\n**Ruling:** the reader derivation keeps a fallback to the published bit —\n\n    r.active_routines != null\n      ? r.active_routines.some((n) => CADENCE_RUNNER_ROUTINES.includes(n))\n      : r.runs_routines === true\n\nExactly semantics-preserving on all four cases: new+cadence => true; new+git-sync-only => false (matching today's null bit); old+cadence => true via the fallback; new+none => false. Cost is one ternary.\n\n**Hazard 2 (publisher), same bug with the arrow reversed.** If new nodes STOP publishing `runs_routines`, an OLD reader sees null and excludes them. So the column's removal is the CONTRACT half and does not belong in P-004: land the reader derivation + fallback first, keep dual-publishing `runs_routines` alongside `active_routines`, and only drop it once no reader depends on it.\n\n**Consequence for D-005's deferred item.** D-005 deferred folding the two positional publish params into an options object until \"P-004 collapses the two into one derived value\". P-004 no longer collapses them — dual-publish means both params survive — so that refactor is now unblocked-but-independent and should be judged on its own merit, not waited on.\n\n**Consequence for P-005.** Unchanged: D-002 still holds, `routineHostsOnly: true` stays at the git-sync call site until P-005 swaps it for `requiresRoutine: 'git-sync'`.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"qm-borrowed-ideas-2026-08-01","title":"Borrow from yc-software/qm: command-policy normalizer, harness adapter profiles, external-content provenance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Borrow from yc-software/qm: command-policy normalizer, harness adapter profiles, external-content provenance\nslug: qm-borrowed-ideas-2026-08-01\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nP-001–P-009 are done. P-010–P-015 remain intentionally blocked by the owner's 2026-08-02 deferral directive; this is a deliberate product-scope hold, not missing implementation evidence.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Recheck only when the owner explicitly lifts or revises the deferral directive; until then keep P-010–P-015 blocked and do not schedule them.)\n\n## Background\n\nSource review of [yc-software/qm](https://github.com/yc-software/qm) — YC's multiplayer\nagent harness (~140k LOC TS, MIT). Close cousin to papercusp: headless core, Postgres\nsessions/memory/queue, per-scope durable sandbox, agent loop, skills, crons. Eight\nborrowable ideas were identified by reading their source (not the README) and, where\npossible, by running their code against papercusp inputs.\n\nThe review produced one verified defect in papercusp, filed as **EI-19294800751120438**\n(critical): every deny-guard in `pretooluse-bash-resource-gate.sh` matches RAW command\ntext, so `bash -c \"…\"`, `eval`, `$( )`, quoted tokens and `timeout` bypass the shared-tree\ngit guard, the pkill guard, the systemctl-exit guard and the crontab deny. Measured 4\nDENY / 14 probes for ours vs 13/14 for qm's evaluator running OUR rules. Item group #1\nbelow is that fix.\n\nProvenance note: directives here are `[owner:Avi 2026-08-01]` — \"write a plan for all 1-8\",\n\"mark them all as deferred except #1,#2, and #4\", \"implement #1 #2 and #4 now from start\nto finish yourself on auto mode\".\n\n## Phase 1 — #1 Shell-aware command normalizer for the bash gate\n\nReference: `qm/src/policy/command-policy.ts` (`scannableCommand` + `evaluateCommand`).\nCanonical papercusp source: `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/pretooluse-bash-resource-gate.sh`\n(the `~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/` copy is deployed by `apps/operator/scripts/install-standalone-mcp.sh`\n— never edit the deployed copy, nor the `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/sidecar/` build artifact).\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add `scannable_command()` to the gate: strip written heredocs, de-quote `\"…\"`/`'…'`/`$'…'` with ANSI-C decoding, unescape backslashes, then recursively (bounded depth) append the payloads of everything that executes a shell — `$( )`, backticks, `bash|sh|dash|zsh|ksh -c`, here-strings, pipe-to-shell — plus structural argv descent through `env` (incl. `-S`), `sudo`, `exec`, `command`, `nice`, `timeout`, `time`, `nohup`, `xargs`. Structural descent replaces the hand-maintained `_WRAP_STRIP` name-list, which is what rotted (`timeout` absent).\n- **P-002** `done` Route every deny-guard in the gate (shared-tree git, pkill/killall, systemctl-exit, os-scheduler/crontab, and any other `re.match`-on-raw-text guard) through the scannable form instead of raw `_seg`. Compute once at the top; keep each guard's existing patterns unchanged so blast radius stays in the matching layer. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `done` Regression test in `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/bash-resource-gate.test.ts`: a table of (command, expected decision) covering every evasion form in EI-19294800751120438 plus the benign-command false-positive set. The absence of this table is why the 2026-07-06 `rtk` fix did not surface `timeout`. blocked-by: P-002\n\n## Phase 2 — #2 Harness adapter profile + conformance test\n\nReference: `qm/src/harness/harness.ts` (`HarnessAdapterProfile`, capability set, `turns`\nvs `models` split) and `qm/test/harness-adapter.test.ts`. Papercusp today: `AGENT_BACKENDS\n= ['claude-code','omp','codex']` with ~20 scattered `agentBackend === '…'` equality\nbranches in `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/invoke.ts` and no capability\ndeclaration anywhere.\n\n- **P-004** `done` Define `HarnessAdapterProfile { id, controlTransport, streamFormat, capabilities: ReadonlySet<HarnessCapability> }` in the orchestrator's types, plus a per-backend registry covering claude-code / omp / codex. Capabilities derived from what the existing branches actually decide (session resume, model-flag spelling, stream format, native session ids, MCP config shape) — do not invent capabilities no branch consumes.\n- **P-005** `done` Replace the scattered `agentBackend === '…'` capability checks in `invoke.ts` with profile lookups, so \"does this backend support X\" is a declared fact rather than an inline conditional. Keep behavior byte-identical; this is a routing refactor, not a semantics change. blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `done` Conformance test pinning every backend's declared profile (the qm pattern: assert the full transport/capability matrix in one place), so adding a backend forces a declaration and a silently-rotting path is caught. blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Phase 3 — #4 External-content provenance + screening seam\n\nReference: `qm/src/security/security-posture.ts` (provenance-labelled payloads, tighten-only\nposture ladder, unscreened-notice) and `qm/src/security/security-screener.ts`. Papercusp\ntoday has two narrow point-solutions: `packages/operator-core/lib/scout/foreign-priming-sanitize.ts`\n(ONE caller — `scout-archive-port.ts`) and `packages/operator-core/lib/text-safety.ts`\n(`createIssue` only). Nothing covers `capability:fetch`, which returns a raw remote body\nstraight into agent context unlabelled.\n\nReuse-first: GENERALIZE `foreign-priming-sanitize` (it already has the right shape — bound,\nstrip control chars, drop injection-marker lines, quote as inert data) rather than adding a\nparallel module.\n\n- **P-007** `done` Promote the foreign-priming sanitizer into a shared external-content ingress module with an explicit provenance envelope: every untrusted body is wrapped labelled by SOURCE (`fetch:<host>`, `tool_result:<name>`, `peer:<ownerId>`, …) and marked inert data, never instructions. Keep the existing Scout call site working on the generalized surface.\n- **P-008** `done` Wire the envelope into `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/capability/fetch.ts` — the raw-remote-body ingress with zero labelling today. Body is returned inside the labelled envelope; the spilled-to-file path gets the same treatment. blocked-by: P-007\n- **P-009** `done` Add the screening SEAM: a `screenExternalContent`-shaped interface plus a tighten-only posture resolution (qm's `dangerous < auto < strict` compose), defaulting to the existing heuristic screen, so a real classifier can be dropped in later without re-plumbing every call site. Include qm's unscreened-notice behavior — when the screener is unavailable, say so visibly rather than failing open silently. blocked-by: P-007\n\n## Phase 4 — DEFERRED (owner directive 2026-08-01)\n\nThese are authored and ranked but deliberately not scheduled. `blocked` status is the\nhonest \"not actionable now\" marker — none of them is stalled or waiting on a dependency.\n\n- **P-010** `blocked` DEFERRED — #3 Memory benchmark with build-failing floors. Port qm's `src/memory/bench.ts`: replay fixed conversation fixtures through each memory strategy, judge the resulting notebook on signal/noise + staleness + inference-vs-observation, average per strategy, fail under floors. Put mem0 strategies behind an A/B-able seam. Motivation: we currently cannot answer \"did that change make recall better or worse\".\n- **P-011** `blocked` DEFERRED — #5 Doc-truth tests. Port qm's `test/public-architecture-docs.test.ts` pattern: assert README/CLAUDE.md claims against the code, and pin RETIRED claims with `doesNotMatch` so they cannot come back. First target: the hand-maintained \"WRITTEN BUT NOT YET LIVE (WI-6674)\" caveat in CLAUDE.md that someone must remember to flip.\n- **P-012** `blocked` DEFERRED — #6 Exemplar end-to-end behavior tests. Port qm's `test/exemplar-*.test.ts` pattern: boot the whole stack in-process with a faked model and assert the PLUMBING around the model (did the standing order reach the wake verbatim, did the reply thread correctly). Deterministic and fast, complementing our judged llm-testing scenarios.\n- **P-013** `blocked` DEFERRED — #7 `routeWake` as a pure total function. Port qm's `src/wake/wake.ts`: `(wake, runIsLive, liveRunGated) → engage | steer | drop(reason)` as one unit-testable function, making \"steer a live turn\" vs \"engage a new one\" explicit. Ours is spread across the wake pump, coord injection and the wake executor.\n- **P-014** `blocked` DEFERRED — #8a Verb-multiplexing to cut tool prompt-weight. qm exposes 13 agent-facing tools (several multiplexed: `memory`, `cron`, `background`, `share` take an action arg) against our ~741 `defineTool` sites. Not a straight swap — most of ours are coordination/datastore verbs with no shell equivalent — but multiplexing directly attacks the prompt-weight budget we already gate in CI.\n- **P-015** `blocked` DEFERRED — #8b Governance: qm's mandatory fresh-context adversarial review before merge (\"the context that produced a diff already believes it is correct\"), depth scaled by blast radius judged by CALLERS not files, reviewer holds last word on depth; plus ADR-as-prose contribution (`adrs/*.md`, human-written, maintainers implement) if Cupboard ever takes outside input.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 `blocked` is the deferral marker, not `dropped`\n\nThe plan-item status vocabulary has no `deferred` token. `dropped` means abandoned and\nwould lose the work; `todo` would let a peer or the scheduler claim work the owner\nexplicitly deferred. `blocked` is the honest \"authored, not actionable now\" state and\nkeeps the items out of the claimable pool. Phase 4's heading and each item's `DEFERRED —`\nprefix carry the reason so no one reads them as stalled dependencies.\n\n### D-002 Fix the matching LAYER, not the individual guards\n\nEI-19294800751120438 is a defect in every guard, but the durable fix is one shared\nnormalizer that all guards match through — not N pattern patches. Patching patterns\nindividually is what produced the rotting `_WRAP_STRIP` allowlist (the 2026-07-06 `rtk`\nfix added one name and left `timeout` open). P-001/P-002 deliberately leave every guard's\npatterns untouched so the change is confined to the matching layer and the regression\ntable in P-003 measures exactly that layer.\n\n### D-003 Generalize the existing sanitizer; do not add a parallel one\n\n`foreign-priming-sanitize.ts` already bounds, strips control characters, drops\ninjection-marker lines and quotes foreign text as inert data — the right shape, wired to\nexactly one caller. Reuse-first says promote it to the shared ingress surface rather than\nintroduce a second external-content module beside it. The screening seam (P-009) is added\nas an interface over that surface, so a classifier is a later drop-in rather than a\nre-plumb.\n\n### D-004 — Two normalizer variants, chosen by whether the guard is ANCHORED\nDate: 2026-08-02\nThe first cut routed every deny-guard through one `_scannable()` form, which surfaces the words of quoted spans. That is correct for an ANCHORED guard (`re.match` at command position) — `git commit -m \"explain git reset --hard\"` still starts its segment with `git commit`, which no destructive pattern matches — and it is what makes `git \"reset\" \"--hard\"` and `pkill -f \"npm run test\"` catchable.\n\nIt is WRONG for a guard that matches a subcommand anywhere in the text. The existing suite caught it: the tauri-agent-tools target guard (EI-10939) started denying `echo \"you could run tauri-agent-tools eval document.title\"` — a prose mention — because it had relied on `_strip_shell_quotes` DELETING the quoted span.\n\nSo there are two accessors:\n  - `_scannable()` — dequoted base + executed payloads. For anchored guards: shared-tree git, pkill/killall, systemctl-exit.\n  - `_scannable_quote_stripped()` — the ORIGINAL quote-deleted base + executed payloads appended as their own lines. For substring-matching guards: tauri target, native-scheduler.\n\nBoth gain the `bash -c` / `eval` / `$( )` / here-string / pipe-to-shell payload coverage; only the anchored ones additionally gain quoted-token visibility. A new guard picks its accessor by asking whether it anchors.\n\n### D-005 — Provenance LABELS a structured payload; it never rewrites it\nDate: 2026-08-02\nqm applies its sanitizer to prose entering a prompt. Papercusp's highest-value unlabelled ingress is `capability:fetch`, which returns a remote body the caller frequently intends to PARSE (a JSON API, a CSV, a raw file).\n\nRunning the Scout-style treatment over that body would corrupt it: dropping \"injection marker\" lines from a JSON response yields invalid JSON, and stripping control characters changes bytes the caller may checksum. A safety measure that silently corrupts data is worse than the gap it closes.\n\nSo the module has TWO entry points and callers pick by SHAPE:\n  - `quarantineExternalProse()` — lossy on purpose (bound → strip control chars → drop marker lines → quote). For prose destined for a prompt. Scout uses this.\n  - `labelExternalContent()` — provenance METADATA only, bytes untouched. For structured payloads. `capability:fetch` uses this, returning `provenance: { source: 'fetch:<host>', trust: 'untrusted', notice, screened }` alongside a verbatim `body`.\n\nThe labelling is most of the value: qm's own screener reasons about the SOURCE LABEL (`tool_result:<name>`, `fetch:<host>`), and a reader who knows a body is untrusted remote text is already most of the way to treating it as data. A screener fault degrades to `screened: { decision: 'unavailable', reason }` rather than silently failing open.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/qm-borrowed-ideas-2026-08-01 (\"Borrow from yc-software/qm: command-policy normalizer, harness adapter profiles, external-\"): no plan update since 2026-08-24 (47 days idle), 9/15 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"scratch-p013-inputs-verify-2026-08-02","title":"SCRATCH — P-013 live verification of the plan-inputs start gate","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SCRATCH — P-013 live verification of the plan-inputs start gate\nslug: scratch-p013-inputs-verify-2026-08-02\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n# SCRATCH — P-013 live verification of the plan-inputs start gate\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"vditor-local-assets-plan-popup-latency-2026-08-02","title":"Plan popup opens in seconds, not instantly: Vditor pulls 4.9MB from unpkg.com per cold render","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-02","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Plan popup opens in seconds, not instantly: Vditor pulls 4.9MB from unpkg.com per cold render\nslug: vditor-local-assets-plan-popup-latency-2026-08-02\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-02\nupdated: 2026-08-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\nP-001 — copy Vditor's runtime assets into the served publicDir at build time.\n\n## Background\n\n**Owner report** [owner:Avi 2026-08-02]: opening a plan from the chat ref-pill\npopup takes several seconds; it should be near-instant.\n\n### Root cause (measured, not inferred)\n\n`MarkdownPreview` / `MarkdownEditor` / `preloadVditor` never set Vditor's `cdn`\noption, so it falls back to its built-in default `https://unpkg.com/vditor@3.11.2`.\nEvery cold markdown render therefore fetches **4.9 MB over the public internet**.\n\nConfirmed by reading the DOM of the owner's LIVE desktop window (read-only eval,\nno state mutation) — these script tags are present:\n\n| asset | size | fetch (this box, warm DNS, wired) |\n|---|---|---|\n| `js/lute/lute.min.js` | 3907 KB | 0.35s |\n| `js/highlight.js/highlight.min.js` | 1025 KB | 0.15s |\n| `js/icons/ant.js` | 42 KB | 0.08s |\n| `js/highlight.js/third-languages.js` | 21 KB | 0.07s |\n| `js/i18n/en_US.js` | 2 KB | 0.07s |\n| **total** | **~4.9 MB** | |\n\n`lute.min.js` is a 3.9 MB Go→WASM-transpiled blob — expensive to fetch AND to\nparse/execute. All five files already exist in `node_modules/vditor/dist/`;\n**none** are in our built `apps/operator-vite/dist/`.\n\n### Ruled out\n\n- **Server is not the problem.** `plans:get` (mode:full, 47 KB plan) = **45 ms**,\n  3/3 runs against `:3070`.\n- **The lazy popup chunk is not the problem.** `PlanPopupModal-*.js` = 65 KB, local.\n\n### Contributing factors\n\n1. **The chat path never warms Vditor.** `preloadVditor()` exists (WI-5547, added\n   for this exact \"several seconds to load a plan\" report) but is called from\n   exactly ONE place — `apps/operator/app/_components/plans/PlansPane.tsx:154`,\n   the sidebar Plans face. The chat popup path\n   (`ChatRefPopupHost` → `PlanPopupModal` → `PlanDetail` → `PlanEditor` →\n   `MarkdownPreview`) warms nothing, so it pays full cold cost on the click.\n2. **`<Suspense fallback={null}>`** in `ChatRefPopupHost` renders NOTHING while the\n   chunk loads — the click has no visible response at all.\n\n### Scope note\n\nThis is broader than the plan popup: EVERY markdown surface in the app (docs,\nwiki, config tabs) pays the same 4.9 MB. Fixing `cdn` fixes all of them, and\nmakes markdown rendering work **offline** — today it is at the mercy of the\nnetwork.\n\n### Open question (does not block the fix)\n\nunpkg sends `cache-control: max-age=31536000`, so if the WebKitGTK cache persists\nacross launches the network cost is once-per-webview-session and the residual is\nparse/exec cost. Both are fixed by P-001+P-002 (local serving) and P-003\n(warming moves the one-time cost off the click). P-006's before/after measurement\ndisambiguates which dominated.\n\n## Phase 1 — serve Vditor's assets locally\n\n- **P-001** `done` Copy `node_modules/vditor/dist/{js,css,images}` (excluding `mathjax`, ~6.5MB, never requested since `math.engine` is KaTeX) into `apps/operator/public/vditor/dist/` as a build step. `publicDir` is `apps/operator/public` per `apps/operator-vite/vite.config.ts:102`. Must be idempotent, must run before/with the vite build, and must not be committed as 16MB of tree churn — prefer a generated/ignored dir populated by a script wired into the build. importance: high\n- **P-002** `done` Set `cdn: '<local base>'` at every Vditor entry point so `${cdn}/dist/js/...` resolves locally: `MarkdownPreview`'s `previewOpts`, `preloadVditor`'s `Vditor.preview` opts, and the `MarkdownEditor` constructor opts (all in `apps/operator/app/_components/MarkdownEditor.tsx`). blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` Warm the Vditor stack on the CHAT path — `preloadVditor()` on plan/work-ref pill hover plus an idle warm when the chat conversation mounts, so the one-time cost is paid before the click rather than on it. Do not warm unconditionally from the router root (that would pay it on `/login`). importance: high\n\n## Phase 2 — perceived latency + regression guards\n\n- **P-004** `done` Replace `<Suspense fallback={null}>` in `ChatRefPopupHost` with the modal frame + a skeleton, so the click responds instantly instead of dead-space.\n- **P-005** `done` Regression guard: a test asserting (a) the local Vditor assets are present where the `cdn` base points, and (b) no Vditor call site omits `cdn` — so a future surface cannot silently re-introduce the unpkg dependency. blocked-by: P-002 — note: 3/3 green. First cut had 2 bugs IN THE TEST (doc-comment mentions counted as call sites; git grep matched prose + a JSON fixture) — fixed with a stripComments helper.\n- **P-006** `done` Verify before/after: measure click→rendered on MY OWN Tauri instance under Xvfb with a dedicated `PAPERCUSP_BRIDGE_PORT` — never the owner's live `:0` window. Record both numbers and confirm zero remote `unpkg.com` resource-timing entries after the fix. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 — note: PARTIAL — asset-layer A/B measured in a real Xvfb Tauri webview (local ~30ms vs unpkg ~225ms, interleaved x3); composite click->painted NOT captured, see rationale.\n- **P-007** `done` Serve the /vditor/** mirror with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (host-spa.ts serveFile). Found during P-006: unpkg was sending max-age=31536000 and we sent NO cache headers at all, so the local mirror won the COLD fetch (~30ms vs ~225ms) but lost the WARM one (~30ms vs ~4ms) — serveFile readFileSync's all 3.9MB per page load. The mirror is a wholesale copy of one PINNED version, replaced not mutated on upgrade, so `immutable` is safe. Verified on :3170 after a restart: header present on /vditor/*, absent on /favicon.ico.\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Copy all of `dist/` except `mathjax`, not just the 5 measured files\n\nA minimal copy (~6 MB: lute + i18n + icons + highlight.js) covers only what was\nobserved on one plan. Plans in this repo genuinely contain **mermaid** diagrams,\nand `katex`/`echarts`/`graphviz` are reachable from plan content too — a partial\ncopy leaves *some* plans still hitting the internet and still slow, which is the\nworst outcome (an intermittent bug that looks fixed). `mathjax` (6.5 MB) is\nexcluded because `previewOpts` pins `math: { engine: 'KaTeX' }`, so it is never\nrequested. Net ~16 MB into `apps/operator/public`, which is already 491 MB.\n\n### D-002 — Set `cdn`, not `_lutePath`\n\nVditor's editor constructor honours `_lutePath`, but the static `Vditor.preview()`\npath — which is what the plan READ view uses — only reads `options.cdn`. So\n`_lutePath` would fix the editor and leave the read path (the reported symptom)\nstill hitting unpkg. `cdn` covers both, plus i18n/icons/highlight/emoji/theme.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"context-injection-retrieval-reach-and-visibility-2026-08-03","title":"Dynamic context injection: close the retrieval-reach gap (work-items are lexical-only), make the legs report what actually ran, and surface pushed context in the HUD","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-03","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Dynamic context injection: close the retrieval-reach gap (work-items are lexical-only), make the legs report what actually ran, and surface pushed context in the HUD\nslug: context-injection-retrieval-reach-and-visibility-2026-08-03\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-03\nupdated: 2026-08-12\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** **ONLY P-019 REMAINS NON-TERMINAL — and it is OWNER-GATED, not unowned work.**\n\n**P-019 — predictor delivered, ruled (D-095), RE-TARGETED in code (D-098, 2026-08-12), and now fully VERIFIED.** `clarityWarrantsEscalation()` fires on `unretrievable` ALONE. D-095 §4 measured `unfocused` — the bucket that used to escalate — as the BEST-reaching of any (5.82/6 admitted, 92.4% full, **0.0% zero-hit**), while the bucket that actually fails is `unretrievable` (21.7% zero-hit, 0.93 admitted). The old predicate armed the expensive tier exactly where retrieval already works. Measured effect: escalation **29.4% → 9.6%** of traffic. Three tests block re-adding `unfocused`; the probe sums THROUGH the predicate instead of keeping its own copy of the rule.\n\n✅ **The prior ## Now's \"ONE OPEN VERIFICATION\" is CLOSED — do not re-run it.** `npm run lint:tsc -- --files=…/memory/corpus-query-clarity.ts,…/memory/bench/corpus-query-clarity-cli.ts` returned `exit=0 status=clean` at 2026-08-12T19:08Z. It had been starved at 0.10 cores under box load 220 (not wedged) — the root cause of that starvation is itself fixed now (EI-19480850505352533 + WI-38277: every typecheck entry point routes through the pc-heavy semaphore). Tests 21/21 green; bench CLI clean end-to-end printing 9.6%. No verification debt remains on this plan.\n\n**P-021 — CLOSED, recorded-not-adopted (WI-38251).** Learned sparse retrieval (SPLADE family) stays rejected for this stack under D-061: no paper in that sample deploys on Postgres/pgvector. Its revisit condition (\"only if P-017+P-018 underdeliver against the bench\") is unmet — P-018 terminal, P-017 shipped (D-097).\n\n`CORPUS_CLARITY_FOCUSED_BITS = 5` stays UNCALIBRATED **and now governs NO SPEND** — with `unfocused` no longer escalating it only re-labels two buckets that both retrieve well. D-095 §5: no knee in the decile curve; do NOT pick a percentile.\n\n**Next:** P-019's only remaining work is the ESCALATION TIER, which is the PARENT plan's P-006 OWNER GATE (`context-injection-audit-2026-07-28`) — not claimable here, and not to be self-answered. Whoever builds it: start from D-095 §4 + D-098, target `unretrievable` (~9.6% of traffic), and decide EXPLICITLY about the high-SCS deciles 7–10 (zero-hit 12–14%) that D-098 deliberately leaves uncovered rather than inheriting silence about them. Do not wire an LLM leg.\n\n## Background\n\nDynamic context injection pushes memory into an agent's turn at three moments — `turn-start` (UserPromptSubmit hook, 4000-char budget), `mid-turn` (PostToolBatch hook, 350-char mem0 budget + the corpus pointer section), and several in-process callers. `buildMemoryContextBlock` runs two legs concurrently and concatenates them:\n\n- **mem0 leg** — facts, `harrier@1024`, one multi-scope search, RRF-fused, sliced to `INJECTION_TOTAL_LIMIT=12` globally, `MEMORY_INJECTION_COSINE_FLOOR=0.58`, `fusionMode: 'cosine-gated'`.\n- **corpus leg** (P-008 / D-037) — resolvable POINTERS into `session_turn` + `work_item`, `gemma@768`, deliberately no absolute score floor (fused RRF is rank-derived), caps 6 items / 1800 chars after D-060.\n\nThe legs stay separate because the vector spaces are incompatible; merging could only be done by fixed priority, which D-011 names *\"a quota under another name.\"*\n\n**Why this plan exists.** su-373a9's audit of the app's *search* surfaces found a systemic defect: capabilities are built per-caller, not in the engine, so each lands on whichever surface prompted it and stops there. Injection is one of those surfaces (row 7 of their matrix), and it inherited the same gaps — no rerank, no recency, no leg-honesty, plus the work_item reach gap. The mechanics are worth borrowing; the reach gap is a correctness bug.\n\n## Phase A — make the legs report what actually ran (highest value, smallest change)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Wire `embedderAvailable` through the corpus leg into the injection path. It is computed and returned by `recallCorpusContext` (`corpus-recall-io.ts:224`) and DISCARDED by `startCorpusLeg` (`injection.ts`). `search:semantic` and `ask-knowledge-tier` both surface it; injection is the only consumer that drops it. Today injection cannot distinguish \"semantic ran and found good matches\" from \"semantic was absent and these are lexical scraps\". importance: high — note: landed WI-7507 — 266 tests/18 files green, lint:tsc clean; rendering deliberately unchanged (P-003 owns that)\n- **P-002** `done` Record per-leg provenance on every injection: which legs ran, which produced each admitted line, and the per-surface coverage at query time. Extend the existing `memory_recall_stats` telemetry (it already carries `pools`, `scores`, `score_scale`, `surface`) rather than adding a second store. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10888 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Coverage-gated degradation: when a corpus surface is below threshold, the pointer section must either sit out or mark itself degraded, instead of confidently emitting nearest-neighbours from a near-empty index. Injection needs this MORE than interactive search — a human sees a bad result list and re-queries; an agent gets one silent block and no signal. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-37380 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Alarm on injection's own surface coverage (`session_turn`, `work_item`), including the 24h-new-row signal that catches recurrence. Mirrors su-373a9's P-008 but scoped to the surfaces injection actually reads — do not rebuild their metric, consume it if they expose one. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-37383 completed (done)\n- **P-023** `done` Session-epoch DEDUP is the single largest loss on the memory leg — it discards 42.6% of everything retrieved (1,190 of 2,792 rows over 284 live recalls, D-071), and zeroes whole recalls (returned 12 → admitted 0). Establish whether those drops are correct (genuinely already-seen lines) or over-aggressive, and if over-aggressive, fix the epoch/keying. Acceptance: measured against the `admission.dropped.dedup` column, paired arms, not a bench. importance: high — note: ← WI-36074 completed (done)\n- **P-024** `done` The char BUDGET drops 34.8% of retrieved rows (973 of 2,792, D-071) — the second-largest loss, and it cuts AFTER ranking, so it silently discards the tail of a well-ordered list. Determine whether the budget is too small, mis-allocated across surfaces, or cutting mid-list where it should cut by score. Acceptance: `admission.dropped.budget` + `admission.truncated`. importance: high — note: ← WI-36075 completed (done)\n- **P-025** `done` The memory leg's LEXICAL arm is inert and should be fixed or retired: 25,778 candidates, 11 qualifying (0.04%), and 0 of 627 admitted lines (D-071). It only perturbs cosine's ordering via RRF. Either recalibrate `minLexScore` so it can qualify, or remove the arm and its fusion bonus. Do NOT widen it for reach. Acceptance: `legs.lexical.qualifying` and `admission.byLeg.lexicalOnly` both move off zero, or the arm is gone. importance: high — note: Resolved as NOT-A-DEFECT — see D-074. Recording this explicitly because \"add a floor\" and \"add recency\" both superficially look like the thing D-037 forbids, and they are not.\n\n### D-002 — The `work_item` embedding leg is su-373a9's P-012: coordinate, do not duplicate\n\n`semantic-search-fingerprint-coverage-2026-08-03` already carries \"give `work_item` an embedding leg\" as P-012, and su-373a9 is implementing that plan now [owner:Avi 2026-08-03]. P-005 here is a dependency edge plus one argument to hand them:\n\n**P-012 is blocked behind their backfill (P-007) and should not be.** The two are independent — the backfill populates `work_items.embedding` (already 12.22% full), while the leg is what lets any query reach those vectors from the shared engine. Ordered as written, the backfill completes and injection still cannot retrieve a work-item semantically. The leg should land first or in parallel; it is also the cheaper half.\n\nCorollary worth stating: we are currently paying to embed work-items whose vectors are unreachable from unified search — only the hand-rolled `semanticSearchIssues` consumes them.\n\n### D-003 — WI-6857 is NOT reopened; the third cut is new scope\n\nWI-6857's stated acceptance was *\"replaying the same 7 batches against the live endpoint surfaces WI-6512 on batch 1 or 2, without the query naming the id.\"* That passed, measured three times, and the two cuts it named (corpus caps; the mid-turn clamp deleting the pointer section) were real and are fixed under D-060.\n\nBut its TITLE claim — \"matches surface tokens, not the problem\" — has a third cause I did not find: work-items are lexically retrievable only. Reopening a correctly-passed acceptance would misrepresent it; carrying the unfixed remainder silently would be worse. So it stays `done`, gets a comment pointing here, and Phase B owns the remainder.\n\n### D-004 — The HUD panel READS existing ledgers; it adds no write path\n\nEverything the \"Dynamically pushed context\" section needs is already persisted and live: `memory_session_surfaced` (the port-agnostic dedup ledger, D-006), `memory_recall_stats` (per-recall telemetry, EI-366 / migration 240), and the corpus surfaced-refs ledger (migration 712). Measured 2026-08-03: 16,993 and 37,412 rows respectively in the last 24 hours.\n\nNo new table, no new write on the injection hot path. This matters because the injection path is fail-soft by contract and budget-sensitive per tool call — a UI feature must not add work there. If a field turns out to be missing, extend the EXISTING telemetry write (P-002), never add a second store.\n\n### D-005 — Measure this system's own numbers; do not inherit another agent's\n\nThe coverage figures that prompted this plan arrived via a pasted report. Re-measuring changed them materially (`session_turns` 0.86% → 4.44%, `work_items` 6.9% → 12.22%, 24h coverage 7% → 36%) because a backfill was running between the two readings. The conclusions survived; the numbers did not.\n\nStanding rule for this plan: every coverage/recall figure carries its own measurement timestamp, and any figure older than a few hours is re-measured before it is acted on. This is the same discipline D-041 imposes for relevance claims, applied to coverage.\n\n### D-006 — Plan-overlap review: this is a new effort, and the lineage is recorded\n\nThe dedup guard flagged five plans. Reviewed rather than forced past:\n\n- **`memory-pg-lexical-own-injection-2026-07-13`** (draft, but its Now reads \"✅ PLAN COMPLETE, all 11 items done\") — genuinely the ANCESTOR: it built the one-PG-store / two-leg / RRF architecture this plan improves, and cut over to `hybrid-pg`. Complete, not a continuation.\n- **`hud-session-launcher-and-board-tabs-2026-07-26`** (active, Now reads \"ALL 9 ITEMS DONE — the plan is drained\") — built the HUD Sessions board and dossier that Phase D extends. Drained, not a continuation. ⚠ Phase D touches its surface, so whoever takes P-011 should read its D-002 (Combobox reuse) and its live-drive finding about `.hud__fleets` overflow before adding a section.\n- The other three (`opencode-omp-token-reduction-research`, `unread-count-truthfulness`, `project-centric-harness-rethink`) share only common English tokens and are unrelated.\n\nRecording this so the history is not silently split — the two real ancestors are named above and should be read as context by anyone picking up Phase D.\n\n### D-061 — Query construction from a large input is a studied problem with a 2026 literature; it names our exact failure mode, our number matches the state of the art, and it REVERSES two of my recommendations\nDate: 2026-08-03\nLiterature review 2026-08-03 (arXiv API, cs.IR/cs.CL, submitted-date descending). Cited by title + date, not by id — I did not verify ids and will not invent them.\n\n#### Our failure mode has a name, a benchmark, and a state of the art we already match\n\n**\"InMind\" (2026-07-27)** isolates the **implicit-association blind spot**: a needed memory that *shares no surface cue with the query*. That is WI-6857's title claim verbatim (\"matches SURFACE TOKENS, not the problem\"). Its measurement: the backbone answers **84.0%** with the fact already in context, but **six memory systems reach at most 14.4%** when it must be retrieved.\n\nOur post-fix acceptance is **1 of 7 = 14.3%**. We are not uniquely broken — we are at the published ceiling for this specific failure mode. This does NOT excuse the gap; it sets a realistic bar and says the remaining win comes from retrieval mechanics, not from a bug hunt.\n\n#### What the evidence says to do\n\n1. **Retrieval is the right lever.** The *LightMem* reproduction (2026-07-31) finds retriever choice dominates: accuracy swings **58.1% → 75.5% over a FIXED store**. Our store is healthy (mem0 100% covered) — so the ~17-point class of gain is on our side of the line.\n2. **Spend compute on RERANK, not expansion.** *Compute Allocation for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval Agents* (2026-03-15) measures expansion at diminishing returns beyond lightweight models (**+1.1 nDCG@10** weak→strong) and concentrates budget on reranking. Independently confirms **P-008 over P-010**.\n3. **Cheapest-first cascade, not always-on LLM.** *The Coverage Illusion* (2026-05-26): synthetic distributions imply >90% of queries need LLM augmentation; **real traffic needs 27.8%**. Their cascade cuts latency **31.8%** and avoids the LLM for **72.2%** of traffic. This answers D-046's latency/cost objection with a design instead of a refusal.\n4. **Statistical term selection is competitive.** *SIRA* (2026-05-07) compresses multi-round agentic search into ONE **corpus-discriminative weighted BM25** call. *Resource-Lean Lexicon Induction* (2026-04-26): random forests beat a 123B model and lift BM25 expansion **+28.9% nDCG@10**. This is our **P-018** (corpus frequency over length) with support — NOT P-010, which is the per-ranker floor; this decision was written before the Phase C items it created were numbered.\n5. **Amortize to the index.** *RAG without Forgetting* (2026-02-05) converts query-time expansion into persistent index-side updates at **zero inference-time overhead** — the Doc2Query idea, current, and it composes with the fingerprint-coverage work already underway.\n6. **Two parallel views, no LLM in the path.** *Zero-Mem* (2026-07-31) retrieves from raw interaction traces via an entity-context graph plus a temporal hierarchy, weighted per query, **no LLM calls**, −57.6% memory-op time. Architecturally our two-leg shape, and independent support for P-006 option (b) on the parent plan.\n\n#### What this REVERSES — I was wrong on multi-query\n\nI recommended multi-query + RRF to the owner. **Three independent 2026 results say naive diversification hurts:**\n- *Caraman @ SemEval-2026* — multi-query expansion and domain-aware prompting actively hurt; temperature tuning helped.\n- *Benchmarking Retrieval Strategies for Biomedical RAG* (2026-05-04) — Multi-Query Expansion had the **weakest** contextual precision (0.671), attributed to \"noise from naive diversification.\"\n- *From BM25 to Corrective RAG* (2026-04-02) — HyDE and multi-query of \"limited benefit\"; BM25 beat dense retrieval outright on that corpus.\n\n**RETRACTED.** Multi-query is not a Phase C candidate. Note this does NOT touch P-006 option (b) on the parent plan: that is a *distinct signal retrieved as its own leg and unioned*, which is Zero-Mem's shape, not one query fanned into N paraphrases.\n\n#### What I under-weighted\n\n**Learned sparse retrieval is now strong for code.** *SPLADE-Code* (2026-03-23) is the first large-scale LSR family for code retrieval, sub-millisecond on 1M passages; *GPUSparse* (2026-06-24) reports 235× over CPU Pyserini. LSR learns term weights AND expansion in the sparse space — it would subsume both **P-018** (term weighting) and **P-017** (the AND-semantics problem) at once.\n\n⚠ **Constraint, stated honestly: not one paper in the sample mentions Postgres or pgvector.** Every LSR deployment assumes a purpose-built inverted index. For us that is a real integration lift, not a config change. Recorded as a candidate, NOT adopted.\n\n#### Acceptance for every Phase C item\n\nThe retrieval bench (`memory/bench/`, corpus.v1, the D-041 real-corpus rule) with a **null control first** — the D-051/D-053 discipline that has already caught one false positive on this plan. Adoption bar stays **0.05 MRR**, and the class to watch is **lexical-gap** (0.195 of headroom): D-053 showed an oracle-grade prose signal moved it −0.0021, so any candidate that cannot move lexical-gap is not worth shipping regardless of its ALL_ANSWERABLE number.\nRelated: P-008, P-009, P-010, P-017, P-018, P-019, P-020, P-021, P-022\n\n### D-062 — MEASURED: flat disjunction + ts_rank_cd is WORSE than today's AND, not better — P-017's prescribed mechanism is falsified. The lever is COVERAGE-GRADED retrieval, and ts_rank_cd cannot express coverage\nDate: 2026-08-03\nMeasured live 2026-08-03 ~09:3xZ against `harness_shared.session_turns` (421k rows, the real corpus), query `corpus recall pointer section clamp` (5 lexemes). D-005 discipline: our own numbers, timestamped.\n\n#### The premise HOLDS — AND is genuinely the constraint\n\n`plainto_tsquery` → `'corpus' & 'recal' & 'pointer' & 'section' & 'clamp'` → **7 rows**.\nOR'd → **23,011 rows**. A 3,287× difference. P-017's diagnosis was right.\n\n#### The PRESCRIBED FIX IS WRONG, and it fails in the expensive direction\n\nP-017 says: switch to disjunction \"scored by `ts_rank_cd`\". Measured, under exactly that change, the positions of the 7 documents containing ALL FIVE terms are:\n\n**36, 41, 64, 153, 213, 277, 427.**\n\nThe corpus leg admits **6** items (`CORPUS_MAX_ITEMS`). So every precise match falls outside the cut — the leg would go from surfacing precise hits to surfacing **none**, while looking like it retrieved more. Normalization flag 16 does not rescue it (44, 41, 38, 173, 298, 500, 380).\n\n**Mechanism:** `ts_rank_cd` scores term FREQUENCY and cover density — not how many DISTINCT query terms a document matches. Under AND, coverage was guaranteed by the filter, so the ranker never had to express it. Remove the filter and *nothing in the query expresses coverage at all*: an 8,000-char document repeating one common term outranks a short one containing all five.\n\nThis is the whole trap. \"Extra terms add evidence instead of eliminating documents\" is the right goal; `ts_rank_cd` is simply not an instrument that can deliver it.\n\n#### What DOES work, measured\n\nOrder by `(count of distinct query lexemes matched) DESC, ts_rank_cd DESC`:\n\npositions 1-7 = exactly the 7 five-of-five documents; **position 8 = a four-of-five document AND discards entirely.** That is the intended behaviour, achieved.\n\n⚠ But the naive implementation — a correlated `unnest(lexemes) … WHERE tsv @@ l::tsquery` per row — costs **745ms on ONE source** against the corpus leg's **2s whole-leg** bound (`corpusRecallTimeoutMs`). Correct and too slow; grading a `ts_rank_cd`-truncated window is NOT a fix, because the measurement above shows the precise matches are not in that window.\n\n#### Rulings\n\n1. **P-017 is RE-SCOPED, not dropped.** Its acceptance is coverage-graded ordering, and any implementation must be measured against the whole-leg budget, not only the bench. A pure `websearch_to_tsquery` swap is explicitly NOT the fix and would not even change the semantics: `websearch_to_tsquery('english','a b')` also ANDs — only the literal word \"or\" disjoins. The item's own wording invited that misread.\n2. **A no-regression shape is available and preferred: cascade, don't replace.** Run today's AND query first (unchanged, index-cheap, 73ms); relax only when it under-fills. Stage 1 identical to today means no regression BY CONSTRUCTION, rather than \"hopefully clears the 0.05 MRR bar\".
