A 76%-confident label rendered beside exact fields reads as exact, and this section's entire purpose is to stop \"was given context\" being confused with \"was given the context that survived\" — shipping a probabilistic column into it would re-create that conflation one level down. The `sem ✓/✗/?` marks stay on the INJECTION rows, where they are measured directly.\n\nClosing the gap would mean writing the producing leg onto each surfaced row — a NEW write path, which D-004 forbids. That is a deliberate cost, not an oversight: if a future item wants per-ref leg provenance it must first reopen D-004, and the argument would have to beat \"the injection moment already carries per-leg health, one row up\".\n\nAlso settled here: `corpus_session_surfaced.port` is NULLABLE (0 of 33,485 rows in 24h are NULL, but the column permits it), so an absent label renders `(unrecorded)` rather than a port named \"null\".\nRelated: P-013, P-012\n\n### D-086 — P-020: index-side expansion is ALREADY SHIPPED (one surface, zero-inference form) — adopt Tier 0 (ref-title) before Doc2Query, and NOT until the sweep can force a re-embed\nDate: 2026-08-09\nRULING (measured 2026-08-09, not argued). P-020 was framed as \"evaluate Doc2Query\". That framing is wrong on its premise: **index-side expansion already ships here**, in its cheapest possible form, and has for ~4 weeks.\n\n#### 1. What exists\n`packages/operator-core/lib/memory/ref-expand.ts` (88 lines, 2026-07-12) — `expandRefsForEmbed(text, resolver)`: extracts `WI|EI|F|D-NNNN` refs (`MAX_REFS=6`), resolves each to its TITLE, appends a `[refs]` appendix to the EMBED text only (stored payload unchanged). Zero inference. Bench (EI-10048): paraphrase-query recall@10 **0.115 -> 0.769** on the memory surface. Kill switch `PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_REF_EXPANSION`.\n\nThe primitive is ALREADY domain-free (text + resolver in, text out). Nothing needs building to reuse it.\n\n#### 2. Why it does not help injection today\nIt is wired at **exactly one call site**: `agent-tools/memory/remember.ts:528`. Verified by grep — `expandRefsForEmbed` is imported in that one file and nowhere else.\n\nThe two surfaces the corpus leg actually retrieves are embedded by a different path entirely: `search/embed-backfill.ts` composes embed text in **pure SQL** (`bodySql`) and never enters JS —\n- `work_items`: `COALESCE(title,'') || E'\\n' || left(COALESCE(summary,''),2000)`\n- `session_turns`: `CASE WHEN length(text)>=80 OR (speaker='user' AND length(text)>=20) THEN left(text,2000) ELSE '' END`\n\nSo the proven mechanism and the surfaces that need it have never met.\n\n#### 3. Measured population (live PG, workspace-scoped)\n| surface | embed-eligible | >=1 ref | share |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `work_items` | 36,526 | 14,966 | **41.0%** |\n| `session_turns` (10d) | 65,200 | 11,140 | **17.1%** |\n\nResolvability, 3,987-row sample: 9,115 ref mentions, 2,362 distinct, **80.1% resolve** to a real title, avg title 154 chars, ~2.3 refs/row. Under `MAX_REFS=6` that is up to ~900 chars of highly-topical text on 41% of the work-item corpus at zero inference cost.\n\nFor `work_items` the resolver is a **self-join** — expressible in `bodySql`, so Tier 0 needs no JS seam on that surface at all.\n\n#### 4. HONEST CAVEAT — do not quote the 6.7x for these surfaces\nThe memory bench measured **id-only memories** (\"...per WI-4028\") going from ~invisible to retrievable. A work-item ALREADY embeds its own title, so it is already retrievable by its own topic. Expansion makes it retrievable by the topic of what it **CITES** — a real but strictly NARROWER win. Expect a smaller delta and MEASURE it; do not carry 0.115->0.769 across.\n\n#### 5. THE BLOCKER, and it governs every future `bodySql` edit\n`stalePredicateSql` (embed-backfill.ts:377) is `embedCol IS NULL OR <embedCol>_mode IS DISTINCT FROM <mode>`. **There is no content hash.** Changing `bodySql` therefore marks NOTHING stale: only rows embedded after the change get the new recipe, and the ~15k work-items that already have vectors keep the old one forever, indistinguishable from the new. That is a SPLIT CORPUS with no convergence path — and it applies to Tier 0 and Doc2Query alike.\n\n`*_mode` exists on all three targets (`work_items.embedding_mode`, `session_turns.text_embedding_mode`, `session_turn_chunks.embedding_mode`) but encodes the EMBEDDER SPACE, not the text recipe. Reusing it conflates two independent axes.\n\n#### 6. THE RULING\n1. Doc2Query (Tier 1, LLM at write time) is **NOT adopted now**. It is strictly more expensive than Tier 0 and would land on the same broken convergence path.\n2. Tier 0 (ref-title expansion on `work_items`, then `session_turns`) is the recommended next step, and is nearly free.\n3. **PREREQUISITE, non-negotiable:** the sweep needs a text-recipe discriminator (composite `mode`, or a sibling `<embedCol>_recipe` column) so a `bodySql` change forces re-embed. Shipping Tier 0 without it is the half-fix this repo warns about — it would silently split the corpus it is meant to improve.\n4. This is the concrete content of P-020's \"embed once, not twice\": the coordination constraint is not scheduling, it is the missing recipe discriminator.\n\nCost of convergence once armed: ~26k texts x ~0.22s sidecar ≈ 95 min of background sweep (5-min tick, fail-soft) — bounded, non-blocking, and subject to the existing daily embed cap.</body>\nRelated: P-020\n\n### D-087 — P-026: the text-recipe discriminator MUST be a sibling column — folding it into `*_mode` is measured-unsafe (silently zeroes three semantic legs)\nDate: 2026-08-09\nRULING, from a consumer audit run 2026-08-09 after building the cheap design and PROVING IT UNSAFE. Recorded because the unsafe design is the one that looks obviously right, needs no migration, and is what D-086 §6.3 listed FIRST (\"a composite mode, or a sibling `<embedCol>_recipe`\"). It is the wrong branch of that or.\n\n#### The attractive-but-wrong design\nFold the recipe version into the token stored in `<embedCol>_mode`: render `<embedder>` for v1/absent (so introducing it re-embeds nothing) and `<embedder>#r<N>` after a bump. It reuses WI-3616's converge-then-quiesce machinery exactly, touches ~5 lines, and needs NO migration. I implemented it end-to-end.\n\n#### Why it is unsafe — MEASURED, not argued\n`<embedCol>_mode` is not private to the sweep. Readers EQUALITY-MATCH it to keep cosine within one embedder space:\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts:1256` and `:1318` — `AND embedding_mode = ${embeddingMode}` — **the work_item semantic leg, i.e. exactly what P-005 shipped**\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/semantic-leg.ts:77`\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/search/doc-section-overlap.ts:179` and `:213`\n\nThe first target anyone would bump is `work_items` (41% ref density, D-086 §3). Its rows would then store `gemma#r2` while every reader above filters `embedding_mode = 'gemma'` — matching ZERO rows. The result is not an error: the semantic leg returns empty and the corpus leg silently degrades to lexical-only. That is the P-005 regression, re-introduced by the very change meant to improve retrieval, and invisible to types and tests.\n\nPatching the readers to prefix-match (`split_part(embedding_mode,'#',1) = $1`) also fails: it is non-sargable and these are hot per-query filters, so it trades a silent outage for a silent index regression.\n\n#### THE RULING\n1. The discriminator is a SIBLING COLUMN — `<embedCol>_recipe` — never a widened `*_mode` token. `*_mode` keeps ONE meaning: the embedder space. Two independent axes get two columns.\n2. Readers stay untouched, which is the whole point: a recipe bump must be invisible to every query-time consumer and visible only to the sweep.\n3. Presence is PROBED per target, exactly like the existing `spaceAware` flag (embed-backfill.ts ~L1230), so a table without the column degrades instead of throwing.\n4. `stalePredicateSql` gains a recipe term ONLY when the target declares a version AND the column exists; `embed-coverage.ts:267` must bind the SAME value — sharing the predicate SQL is not enough when the bound VALUE can drift, and coverage is the surface that would otherwise report 0% and blame the sweep.\n5. Blast radius is per-target and must be opted into deliberately. Measured at ~0.22s/text: `work_items` 36,523 rows ≈ 2.2h; `session_turn_chunks` 120,982 ≈ 7.4h; `session_turns` 296,392 ≈ 18.1h. Ship `work_items` first.\n\n#### Transferable lesson\nA column named for one axis had silently become load-bearing for four consumers outside the module that owns it. \"Does this module own this column?\" is not answerable from inside the module — grep every reader BEFORE widening a stored token's grammar. The cheap design failed for a reason that lives two files away from where the change is made.\n\nNo code landed: both files were reverted and verified byte-identical to HEAD, and `git log -S embedModeToken --all` is empty, so the intermediate never reached a gate candidate.</body>\nRelated: P-026\n\n### D-088 — P-019: the cheapest-first cascade is EMPIRICALLY JUSTIFIED (19.7% escalation) — and query clarity MUST be scored on the ISSUED query, never the candidate pool\nDate: 2026-08-09\nMEASURED 2026-08-09 over 2,000 real submitted prompts against the live 40,600-term / ndocs=40,000 `corpus_term_df` table. Probe: `packages/operator-core/lib/memory/bench/corpus-query-clarity-cli.ts`. Predictor: `packages/operator-core/lib/memory/corpus-query-clarity.ts` (pure, DF injected, 17 tests).\n\n#### R1 — the cascade thesis holds for us; do NOT build an always-on rewriter\n\nTraffic-weighted escalation rate (unfocused + unretrievable) = **19.7%**, over 98.6% of recalls. Per surface: mid-turn 19.7%, turn-start 8.4%, claim 16.0%, orient 40.6%, initialize 42.0%. **10.7% of traffic is `keyed`** — an id-prefixed handle that short-circuits to a near-unique retrieval key and can never be improved by rewriting.\n\nSo ~80% of injection traffic needs nothing beyond the statistical path. That is close to The Coverage Illusion's real-traffic 27.8% and nowhere near its synthetic >90%. D-046's latency/cost objection is answered on the numbers, not argued away.\n\n#### R2 ⚠ SCORING THE CANDIDATE POOL REPRODUCES THE SYNTHETIC ILLUSION — 87.7% vs 19.7% ON THE SAME QUERIES\n\n`SCS = avgIdf − log2(n)`. Score the full `corpusTerms` pool and every doubling of the candidate count costs a bit of \"clarity\" — and n is set by the injecting SURFACE's clamp width, not by content. Pool-scored median SCS falls MONOTONICALLY as the clamp widens (82ch 2.73 → 116ch 1.91 → 153ch 1.79 → 300ch 0.95 → 979ch 0.26 bits), i.e. it ranks the LONGEST envelopes least clear — backwards. Scoring the ≤2 terms `corpusQueryText` actually issues holds n≈2, and the ordering REVERSES to the sensible direction (5.41 → 6.39 → 6.44 → 7.11 → 7.83).\n\nSame queries, same threshold, opposite verdicts: **87.7% pool-scored vs 19.7% issued-scored**. The pool-scored number would have justified the always-on rewriter this item exists to avoid. `assessCorpusQueryClarity` therefore defaults to `scope:'issued'`; `scope:'pool'` is retained ONLY as the control that demonstrates the artifact. A test locks the default.\n\n⚠ The issued query is derived with NO `df` — exactly as the leg derives it. Passing a DF signal through re-enables the BANDED selection D-066 measured worse and reverted, so the reading would describe a query production never issues.\n\n#### R3 — measure the SURFACE MIX before characterising \"real traffic\"\n\n7d live: **mid-turn is 87.1% of recalls at a 153-char median query; turn-start is 5.4% at 981**. `corpusQueryText`'s docstring describes the 1000-char turn-start envelope, so that is the case an author reaches for — and it is the 5% tail. Any claim about injection traffic that is not surface-weighted is characterising the tail.\n\n#### R4 — P-019's stated economy is STALE; the predictor stands on its own\n\nP-019 says \"the SAME predictor is the degradation signal P-003 needs, so build it once and use it twice.\" P-003 shipped `search/coverage-gate.ts`, which reads persisted embedding-COVERAGE samples — index health, an entirely different signal from query difficulty. Nothing is shared. The predictor is justified by R1 alone; do not cite P-003 for it.\n\n#### R5 ⚠ PREDICTIVE VALIDITY IS UNTESTED — this measures the DISTRIBUTION, not the predictor's accuracy\n\nEverything above characterises how clarity is DISTRIBUTED across real traffic. NOTHING here shows that a low-clarity query actually retrieves worse. That correlation — clarity bucket vs admitted lines / known-item hit rate, run through the real leg — has not been measured, so \"19.7% of traffic is unfocused\" must NOT be restated as \"19.7% of traffic retrieves badly\". Until it is measured the predictor is a well-behaved statistic of unproven relevance, and the honest calibration of `CORPUS_CLARITY_FOCUSED_BITS` (still the arbitrary 5-bit placeholder every rate above is quoted at) depends on that outcome study, NOT on picking a percentile and NOT on fitting to the paper's 27.8% — fitting to the number you set out to reproduce is circular.\n\n#### What is NOT decided, and is NOT mine to decide\n\nThe predictor is built and measured; the ESCALATION TIER is not built and no LLM is wired. What the expensive tier should DO for the 19.7% is exactly the owner-gated question open on the PARENT plan's P-006 (option (c) model-based intent extraction, rejected D-046). Do not self-answer it. Rarity-as-weight is used here to score a query that already exists — this does not reopen D-066, which barred rarity as a SELECTOR.\nRelated: P-019, P-003\n\n### D-089 — P-024 ANSWERED: turn-start reach is bound by the PRODUCT budget÷entry-cost, and the 900-char clamp is the de-facto allocation policy\nDate: 2026-08-09\nMeasured live on the first data the D-081 instrumentation produced after it deployed (n=23 turn-start rows, workspace-scoped, 2026-08-09 17:16-18:15Z). recall-stats.ts @05bda70a is now committed+staging+main+DEPLOYED; telemetry confirmed WRITING (28/34 turn-start rows carry spent+budgetChars).\n\nNUMBERS: mean utilization 66.5%, median 75.5%, p90 95.7%. 8/23 rows >=95% full. 13/23 dropped entries for budget. Admit rate 45.1% (87 of 193). avg returned 8.4 -> admitted 3.8.\n\nTHE MECHANISM (read at the writer, not inferred): median cost per ADMITTED entry = 909 chars. injection.ts:1387 builds the line as `- {scope}{id} {displayText}`, so the scope/id prefix is added ON TOP of the MAX_ENTRY_CHARS=900 clamp (injection.ts:436). Slots = 4000 / 909 ~= 4.4 — exactly the observed admitted count. The budget is not 'too small' in isolation and the clamp is not 'too tight' in isolation; REACH IS THEIR QUOTIENT.\n\nSATURATION IS REAL BUT SUB-ENTRY: all 13 budget-dropping rows leave <1000 chars headroom, 10 of 13 under 400 — less than one clamped entry can occupy. dropped.budget counts skip-and-continue misses (WI-6870, injection.ts:1410-1421), so it is NOT 'the tail was cut'.\n\n⚠ CORRECTION of my own first read this session: I initially read a single row (spent 3018/4000, dropped.budget 9) as '982 chars sat unspent, therefore the budget is not binding'. That was WRONG — 982 is less than one entry's cost. Never read leftover headroom as slack without comparing it to entry cost.\n\nHypothesis (c) 'cuts mid-list where it should cut by score' stays REFUTED (injection.ts:1375-1423 walks `ranked` in relevance order).\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR TUNING: budget and clamp are interchangeable on SLOT COUNT but not on COST. 4000->8000 buys ~8.8 slots at 2x context cost; 900->450 buys ~8.8 slots at the SAME cost. Truncation is recoverable — the clamped line keeps scope+id+lede and an explicit 'memory:search for the rest' (injection.ts:1384) — whereas an omitted entry is invisible. That argues CLAMP-FIRST.\n\nDELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED: which lever and how far. n=23 over ~1h in one workspace is thin for a fleet-wide context change. Any A/B reads the ADMITTED rate, never %budget (D-077: %budget falls by construction when the budget rises). Note MAX_ENTRY_CHARS is a hardcoded const, NOT env-tunable, so A/B-ing it needs a code change; PAPERCUSP_TURN_START_BUDGET_CHARS is env-tunable. D-073 unchanged: do NOT touch MID_TURN_BUDGET_CHARS.\n\n### D-090 — P-024 tuning lever CHOSEN BY OWNER: halve MAX_ENTRY_CHARS 900->450, do NOT raise the turn-start budget\nDate: 2026-08-09\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-09 ~18:20Z] Asked as an explicit 3-option choice against the D-089 measurement; Avi picked the clamp and declined both 'double the budget' and 'wait for more data'.\n\nTHE RULING: halve the per-entry clamp MAX_ENTRY_CHARS 900 -> 450 (injection.ts:436). Do NOT raise PAPERCUSP_TURN_START_BUDGET_CHARS off this finding.\n\nWHY THE CLAMP AND NOT THE BUDGET (per D-089, reach = budget / cost-per-entry): both levers buy ~2x delivered memories, but the clamp buys it at the SAME total context cost while the budget DOUBLES per-turn cost for every agent on every turn. And the two failure modes are asymmetric: a clamped entry stays RECOVERABLE (the line keeps scope+id+lede plus an explicit 'memory:search for the rest', injection.ts:1384), whereas an entry dropped for budget is INVISIBLE to the agent. Free reach beats paid reach.\n\nBINDING CONSTRAINTS ON WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS:\n1. The A/B metric is the ADMITTED rate. NEVER %budget — it falls by construction when you change the allocation, so it cannot validate the change (D-077). Read admission.admitted / admission.returned from harness_shared.memory_recall_stats WHERE surface='turn-start'.\n2. MAX_ENTRY_CHARS is a HARDCODED CONST (injection.ts:436), unlike the env-tunable budget — so this cannot be A/B'd or rolled back without a code change. Consider making it env-tunable in the same edit; that is an implementation choice this decision does not settle.\n3. D-073 stands: do NOT touch MID_TURN_BUDGET_CHARS. Mid-turn's low admit rate is the design working.\n4. Baseline to measure against, captured pre-change: n=23, admit rate 45.1% (87/193), avg returned 8.4 -> admitted 3.8, mean utilization 66.5%, median chars-per-admitted 909.\n\nEXPLICITLY NOT SETTLED BY THIS DECISION: that 450 is optimal rather than 600 or 300 (n=23 over ~1h, one workspace — the QUOTIENT mechanism is solid, the specific setting is not), and whether shorter entries cost ANSWER QUALITY rather than only bytes — nothing in the admission telemetry measures usefulness of a delivered memory, only delivery. Ship it behind the measurement, do not assert it is optimal.\n\n### D-091 — P-008 re-measured after P-024: the reach-ceiling objection is FALSIFIED and stage-1 latency is safe — but the item is gated on WIDENING THE FETCH, not on wiring\nDate: 2026-08-09\nDate: 2026-08-09. P-024 moved that baseline as predicted: survivors/query 7.2 -> 9.7 against a 6-slot page, so ranking matters MORE after P-024.\n\n#### 3. ⚠⚠ CORRECTED — THE FETCH IS ALREADY WIDE ENOUGH\n\nTHIS SECTION ORIGINALLY RULED: \"P-008 is gated on WIDENING THE CORPUS LEG'S FETCH — it fetches at page width, so reranking can only permute rows already chosen.\" That came from a peer's verification and I recorded it as the RULING without reading the fetch site. **FALSE. Do not act on it.**\n\nMEASURED AT SOURCE:\n  corpus-recall-io.ts:372  retrievalDepth = Math.max(maxItems * 4, 8)   // -> `limit:` at :435\n  corpus-recall.ts:182     CORPUS_MAX_ITEMS = 6                          => retrievalDepth = 24\n  rerank.ts:57/72/103      RERANK_OVERFETCH=4, RERANK_MAX_CANDIDATES=24\n                           rerankCandidateCount(6) = max(6, min(24,24)) = 24\n\nThe leg ALREADY over-fetches 4x and lands on EXACTLY the 24 candidates rerankCandidateCount would ask for — identical, not merely close. (c) Acceptance via bench/wi-6512-known-item-replay-cli.ts, answer-bearing paired arms, NEVER line counts (a reorder cannot move a line count — confident null, D-066).\n\nPROCESS NOTE: I recorded a peer's claim as a RULING without reading the code behind it, and a plan Decision is precisely the surface other lanes follow without re-deriving. THE VALUE QUESTION IS STILL OPEN AND MAY ANSWER \"NO\"\n\nD-079's survivor finding (the FILTERS, not the ranking cut, do the selecting) still argues the value is modest, and one-stage cost is ~1185ms p50 onto a leg whose p50 is 105ms. Wiring it is cheap; JUSTIFYING it is the real work. \"Not worth the latency\" remains a legitimate verdict — reached by the acceptance bench, not by assertion in either direction.\n\n### D-092 — D-004's \"no new write path\" does NOT forbid resolving a surfaced ref's title at READ time — the HUD now does, and the DTO comment that said otherwise was over-reading it\nDate: 2026-08-09\nRULING, recorded because the wrong reading is already written into shipped source and the next lane to touch Phase D would inherit it.\n\nWHAT D-004 SAYS: back the pushed-context section with the EXISTING ledgers — no new WRITE path. That is a constraint on what we STAMP into `memory_session_surfaced` / `corpus_session_surfaced`: they stay pointer stores, and enriching a ledger row with a denormalised title at surface time would be exactly the write path D-004 forbids (it would also go stale the moment the underlying row was edited).\n\nWHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: that the READER may not follow the pointer. `PushedContextRef`'s header in `packages/operator-core/lib/adv-agent-detail.ts` had generalised it to \"resolving them here would invent the write path that decision forbids\" — which is false: a read-side join persists nothing, invents no ledger column, and cannot go stale because it is computed per read. The over-reading had a real cost: it is the stated reason the section shipped rendering `mem 89f230d3…` / `ptr WI-7005`, i.e. handles the operator cannot act on, which the owner then had to ask to be fixed [owner 2026-08-09: \"the user doesn't care about the ids, it should show a title\"].\n\nWHAT LANDED (WI-37543): `resolvePushedRefTitles()` resolves the capped 40-ref slice at read time — `WI-*`/`EI-*` → work_items.title, mem0 uuid → memory_canonical.payload->>'data', `claude:<uuid>` → the session's first user turn. Three properties are load-bearing and should survive any later edit:\n\n1. It runs in its OWN transaction, not the ledgers'. `withWorkspace` wraps its callback in a TRANSACTION, so any error inside (missing relation, cast, statement timeout) would abort the surrounding one and take the ledger read down with it — the same trap the corpus-ledger read is already fenced against with `to_regclass`. A second round-trip is the price of keeping the failure local.\n\n2. Failure degrades to a TRI-STATE, never to silence: `titleState` is `'ok'` | `'unresolved'` (we looked, the row is gone — a finding about the pointer) | `'unavailable'` (our own lookup failed — says nothing about the row) | undefined (never attempted). Collapsing the middle two would report our outage as the system's data loss, the same conflation `unavailable` on the parent DTO and the three `semanticRan` glyphs already exist to prevent.\n\n3. It is deliberately NOT workspace-scoped, against the usual rule for these tables, and the reason is measured (2026-08-09): the ref set is already bounded by this session's own ledger rows so there is no cross-tenant fan-in; `memory_canonical` legitimately holds these rows under TWO workspace ids (`default` and the active workspace) so a predicate would drop real rows and report them as `'unresolved'`; and `session_turns.workspace_id` is always the literal `default` (a corpus namespace, not a tenant). `work_items` IS keyed (harness_slug, feature_id), so that one uses DISTINCT ON rather than letting the join fan out.\n\nGENERAL FORM, for whoever hits the next one: a decision that constrains WRITES constrains writes. Before citing one to rule out a READ, re-read the decision rather than the comment that cites it — this comment was accurate about D-004's existence and wrong about its scope, which is the shape that survives review.\n\n### D-093 — P-008 stage-1 rerank: MEASURED AND NOT ADOPTED — the reorder is real, it does not move the answer, and it costs +1,801ms on a 2s-bounded hot path whose bound cannot fire in-process\nDate: 2026-08-09\nDate: 2026-08-09. Closes P-008, answering D-091's open question (\"does it EARN the latency\"). The wiring D-091 specified was built, is correct, and is left **default OFF**.\n\n#### 1. THE MEASUREMENT (paired arms, one process, same corpus instant)\n\n`bench/wi-6512-known-item-replay-cli.ts --mode none --ceiling --rerank-arms`. CONTROL `rerank:false` vs TREATMENT `rerank:true`, HYBRID, 7 answer-bearing WI-6512 batches, back-to-back per batch.\n\n```\ninstrument: stage ran on 7/7 batches; admitted ORDER moved on 5/7.\nCONTROL   (RRF order):  known-item admitted 0/7  reachable 2/7   233ms/batch\nTREATMENT (reranked) :  known-item admitted 0/7  reachable 2/7  2034ms/batch\nADMITTED delta 0 · REACH delta 0 · COST +1,801ms/batch\n```\n\n**The reorder is REAL and it does not move the ANSWER.** The admitted order changed on 5/7 batches — not a dead instrument (§2). It never changed WHICH answer-bearing line was admitted.\n\nNote the ceiling, which bounds what this set could show: only **2 of 7** batches were rescuable by ANY reordering (`order-blocked` — survived the filters, lost on rank). The other 5 were `NOT-RETRIEVED`, which no reorder can fix. It rescued neither of the 2 — and on turn 63 reproduced the RRF order exactly, i.e. the cross-encoder agreed with the fusion.\n\n#### 2. THE INSTRUMENT ASSERTS ITS OWN VALIDITY — this null is REAL, not a dead engine\n\nThe stage is fail-soft: with no engine it returns the RRF order, **byte-identical to the control**. So a treatment arm that quietly lost its engine reports a clean 0/7 reading exactly like \"reranking does not help\" — and the response to that null is to abandon the feature. Indistinguishable from a real result by the numbers alone.\n\nSo `CorpusRecallResult.rerank` reports whether the stage engaged, and the bench **VOIDS the run** — refuses to print a verdict — if the treatment never reranked, or reranked but the order never moved on any batch. Both counters print with the result. Same discipline this bench already applies to `embedderAvailable`. Prompted by su-90cc5cbd's warning that a real win can read as \"no effect\" when another stage decides the page.\n\n#### 3. ⚠⚠ THE FAIL-SOFT CONTRACT IS INOPERATIVE IN-PROCESS (the bigger finding)\n\nFound because a number contradicted the design: TREATMENT batches took **2,473 / 2,455 / 2,302ms** through a **2,000ms** `withBound` and still returned `outcome:'ok'`. Had the timer fired they would be `'timed-out'` at ~2,000ms. `PAPERCUSP_MEMORY_CORPUS_TIMEOUT_MS` confirmed unset.\n\nCause: every bound here is `Promise.race` + `setTimeout`, and **a timer cannot preempt a stage that blocks the event loop**. With no sidecar the cross-encoder runs in-process on the main thread. Confirmed independently: a 200ms timer armed before a 1,200ms synchronous spin fires at 1,200ms. Same family as WI-37480 (`await` is not a yield). All three protections — the leg's 2s bound, `corpusRerankTimeoutMs`, and the `rerankTimeoutMs` override built as P-008's prerequisite — are unenforceable on a sidecar-less host.\n\n**Scoped honestly, and I nearly got this wrong.** `papercup-release.service`'s unit env shows no sidecar var, which looks like \"production is exposed\". It is not: `:3070` is served by `papercup-dev-api.service`, whose LIVE pid has `PAPERCUSP_EMBED_SIDECAR_URL`. Out-of-process the stage is an HTTP call, genuinely async, and the bounds work. The exposed case is a host with **no sidecar** — per the local engine's own rationale (no credential, no network), the **desktop install**, i.e. the shipping target. Pre-existing defect in the SHIPPED prose rerank, independent of P-008 — filed **EI-20005411672741677**. Doc comments claiming a degrade-to-RRF guarantee are corrected in tree.\n\n#### 4. RULING\n\n**DO NOT ADOPT.** Zero measured relevance gain against +1,801ms charged to EVERY turn's prompt build on a leg whose control p50 is 40-240ms — and, on the deployment we ship, no working ceiling on that cost. Even out-of-process the calibrated floor is ~1.1s (24 pairs x ~45ms), an order of magnitude over the leg. Corroborates D-079 from a second direction: the FILTERS, not the ranking cut, do the selecting.\n\n**Kept as a re-measurable seam, NOT flag-gated.** `CorpusRecallInput.rerank` defaults false, documented with this verdict. Precedent: `anchorDfBudget`, likewise pinned to its control because the widening measured neutral. A runtime FLAG was rejected — an unadopted feature behind a flag is dead code awaiting a flip by someone who has not read this decision.\n\nSHIPPED regardless of the verdict: `rerankRows<T>`, the row-shape-agnostic core extracted from `rerankProseHits` so engine resolution + the fail-safe seam live in ONE place (thin binding; behaviour unchanged; 6 new tests, 37/37).\n\n#### 5. WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS\n\nA changed COST (worker-thread scorer, distilled model, batched GPU), not a better argument. **7 batches with a 2/7 reordering ceiling can establish a rescue, but a 0/7 delta bounds the effect — it does not prove absence.**\n\n### D-094 — A surface that renders admission/leg counters to a HUMAN must carry the stage's design intent inline\nDate: 2026-08-09\nEstablished building WI-37549 (the agent-dossier injection-row hover panel).\n\nRULE: any UI that renders `admission.dropped`, `admission.byLeg`, or `legs.*.qualifying` to a person must render the stage's WHY beside the number — never a bare count, and never a bare glyph. For the drop stages the vocabulary is `ADMISSION_STAGE_SHORT_WHY` (new in recall-stats.ts, beside the existing `ADMISSION_STAGE_DESIGN_INTENT`); resolve it SERVER-side and ship it on the wire, because `recall-stats.ts` imports `@papercusp/flags/server` and a client cannot import the vocabulary — a re-typed gloss in a component is how a count and its explanation drift apart.\n\nWHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A STYLE NOTE: two of these numbers are DESIGNED ZEROS, and both have been read as defects repeatedly — D-063, D-073, D-074, D-076 are all the same failure, and it recurred a fifth time INSIDE WI-37549's own commissioning body, which framed `lexical: 108 candidates / 0 qualifying` as \"P-025's 'the lexical arm is inert' finding visible per row\". The writer says otherwise (`recall-admission.ts:48-72`): `byLeg.lexicalOnly` is STRUCTURALLY zero on the push path because `cosine-gated` fusion seeds candidates only from cosine hits (moving it off zero means reverting to `floored-union`, the defect D-010 fixed), and a near-zero lexical `qualifying` is INTENDED because the lexical score is normalized by query-token count — the leg exists for exact-identifier recall and \"should contribute nothing rather than decide the outcome\" (WI-7154).\n\nSo the panel states both facts plainly AND attaches their intent, ending with \"Not a defect.\" Rendering them as an alarm would have shipped the exact misreading `ADMISSION_STAGE_DESIGN_INTENT` was written to prevent — to the one audience least equipped to check it against the source.\n\nCOROLLARY (same shape, different field): the panel reads `spent > budgetChars` as the ALWAYS-EMIT-ONE-ROW exemption rather than as an overrun, per the third reading in recall-stats.ts's `spent` doc. That is what actually explains an admitted count of exactly 1, which is the single most common shape on the mid-turn port.\n\nA UI threshold that the data does not define is labelled as the UI's own: `BUDGET_BOUND_FRACTION` (0.9) decides budget-bound vs clamp-bound, and the panel always prints both raw numbers beside the verdict so a reader can judge a borderline themselves. Relatedly, `depth` is PER-SCOPE while `candidates` aggregates across scopes (measured: depth 12, candidates 25), so no surface may derive a saturation verdict by comparing them.\n\n### D-095 — P-019 R5 RULED: predictive validity HOLDS after controlling for reach (partial rho ~+0.35) — but D-088 named the WRONG outcome measure, and the escalation bucket is not the failing bucket\nDate: 2026-08-10\nDate: 2026-08-10. Amends D-088's R5 clause, which said validity was UNTESTED. It is now tested. Study re-run at scale on TWO independent seeds, warm/hybrid arm both times (`corpus-clarity-validity-cli.ts --queries 1500`): s17 99.1% completed / embedder 98.9% / 171s; s29 99.0% / 98.8% / 114s. Logs /tmp/r5-{full,ctl}-s{17,29}.log.\n\n#### 1. THE RULING\nPre-retrieval clarity (issued-scope SCS) DOES predict a quality-shaped retrieval outcome. rho(SCS -> post-retrieval KL) = +0.477 (s17) / +0.473 (s29), p=0.001, against a permutation null centred at ~0 with a 95% band of only +/-0.06 at this n. Replication across seeds is near-exact. The predictor is NOT a well-behaved statistic of unproven relevance; keep it.\n\n#### 2. ⚠⚠ BUT THE RAW NUMBER IS INFLATED, AND D-088 ASKED FOR THE MEASURE THAT MANUFACTURES A FALSE POSITIVE\nD-088's R5 clause named \"clarity bucket vs admitted lines\" as an acceptable outcome. It is NOT. rho(SCS -> admitted) = -0.686 p=0.001 is MECHANICALLY GUARANTEED — rarer terms match fewer documents — so ruling on it would have \"confirmed validity\" from arithmetic that cannot fail. Admitted-count is a REACH proxy, never a quality measure.\n\nWorse, the two outcome columns are NOT independent. `postRetrievalClarity` (corpus-clarity-validity.ts:176-204) is a PLUG-IN KL estimator over the RETRIEVED SET's term distribution: fewer texts => sparser => peakier => bits rise for a purely mechanical reason. By decile 10 mean admitted is 0.95 lines, and a 1-line set is trivially \"concentrated\". So a query could score high on the quality column by retrieving almost NOTHING.\n\nNEW CONTROL BUILT (this is the load-bearing addition): `partialSpearman` in corpus-clarity-validity.ts, wired into the CLI as a \"Reach control\" table plus the previously-missing `admitted -> post-clarity` pairing. Partialling reach out of the headline:\n- s17: raw 0.471 -> **0.338** (28.2% of the magnitude removed), n=1185\n- s29: raw 0.478 -> **0.370** (22.5% removed), n=1193\nA substantial association SURVIVES (~11 standard errors from 0 at this n), so the confound is real but partial. Report the PARTIAL, never the raw. The pre-existing within-surface control does NOT cover this: it rules out CLAMP WIDTH, and reach varies inside every surface. Guarded by 4 permanent unit controls, one building a KNOWN full confound where the partial must collapse to ~0 while raw rho = -1 (29/29 green).\n\n#### 3. ⚠ WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT ESTABLISH\nPost-retrieval KL measures how topically CONCENTRATED the retrieved set is. It is not a RELEVANCE judgement: nothing in this study labels whether an admitted line was actually USEFUL. \"Clarity predicts concentration\" is what was shown. Do not restate it as \"clarity predicts usefulness\".\n\n#### 4. ⚠⚠ THE ESCALATION BUCKET IS NOT THE FAILING BUCKET — this inverts the cascade's premise\nFrom the s17 verdict table: `unfocused` (15.9% of traffic, the bucket that WOULD escalate) has mean admitted 5.82, full-6/6 92.4%, and zero-hit **0.0%** — the BEST reach of any bucket. \"Would escalate\" (19.9%) beats \"would not\" on reach (4.83 vs 3.76 admitted; 73.6% vs 37.2% full). The bucket that actually FAILS is `unretrievable`: 4.0% of traffic, zero-hit 21.7%, admitted 0.93.\nSo spending an expensive tier on `unfocused` would spend it where retrieval is already working. Whoever builds the tier must re-target it — the candidate trigger is `unretrievable` (and the high-SCS deciles 7/10, zero-hit 12-14%), NOT `unfocused`. This is a design finding, not a calibration detail.\n\n#### 5. STILL NOT DECIDED\n`CORPUS_CLARITY_FOCUSED_BITS = 5` remains UNCALIBRATED — the decile curve shows no clean knee, so there is nothing to calibrate against yet. Do NOT pick a percentile and do NOT fit to the paper's 27.8%. The escalation TIER remains the parent plan's P-006 owner gate; not self-answered here.\n\n#### 6. METHOD WARNING WORTH CARRYING\nAn n=34 smoke of this SAME study reported rho(SCS,post)=0.172 INSIDE a +/-0.34 band, i.e. \"no association measured\". At n=1189 it is +0.477. The band shrank from +/-0.34 to +/-0.06. Reading that smoke as a finding would have declared a dead end incorrectly. Small-n nulls here are POWER FAILURES, not results — the same class as D-093's known-item null, whose effective n is 2 (5 of its 7 batches were NOT-RETRIEVED and could not move).\nRelated: P-019\n\n### D-096 — Do NOT integrate reranking on the default retrieval path — the win is real but capped at +0.009 nDCG, and the binding constraint is reach, not ranking\nDate: 2026-08-10\nSupersedes the *reading* of D-093 (not its cost finding). WI-37653 built the conclusive bench D-093 lacked; both runs completed 2026-08-10.\n\n#### The measurement\nPool=24 (production over-fetch), seed 17, 500 requested → **422 usable** derived targets. Instrument valid: 422/422 stage-engaged, order moved on 274.\n\n| stratum | n | share | Δ nDCG@6 | 95% CI | reading |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|\n| admitted | 31 | 7.3% | -0.0363 | -0.113 … 0.041 | UNDECIDABLE (underpowered) |\n| **order-blocked** | 18 | **4.3%** | **+0.2725** | **0.091 … 0.454** | **REAL GAIN** |\n| not-retrieved | 373 | 88.4% | 0 | — | structural zero |\n\n**Population Δ nDCG@6 = +0.0090** (95% CI -0.0006 … 0.0185, MDE@80% = 0.0154).\n\n#### Reading it honestly, in both directions\nReranking is **not** ineffective — where it can act it is strongly effective (+0.27, CI excludes 0). D-093's \"no effect\" was a power failure at effective n=2 and must not be cited as an effect null. But a within-stratum win is not a production effect: reweighted to a 4.3% base rate it becomes +0.009, below any threshold worth 1.8s/batch.\n\n**Ceiling:** Wilson-upper on 18/422 = 6.64%, × max per-pair gain 1.0 = **+0.066**. That is the most a *perfect* reranker could ever add. A larger sample only tightens it. So this is a bounded conclusion, not an underpowered one — no more data is needed to decide.\n\n**Cost:** D-093's sound half — +1,801ms/batch against a 233ms control, ~8× latency for +0.009 nDCG.\n\n#### \"Just over-fetch more\" is dead — measured, not assumed\nPaired on the same 238 targets, pool 24 → 100:\n\n- not-retrieved 86.1% → 79.4% (quadrupling the pool recovers only 7.8% of misses)\n- order-blocked 5.0% → 11.8%\n- but **all 16** newly-reachable targets sit at control rank **26–98**, and `RERANK_MAX_CANDIDATES = 24` makes every one of them invisible. The reranker-reachable share is **5.0% at both pools** — identical.\n\nSo a wider pool feeds the reranker nothing. It is also actively harmful: at pool=100 the 4s budget (sized for 24 pairs at ~45ms) is exceeded on every query, the reranker returns input order 238/238 with no warning, and the run reads as a clean null. Filed **WI-37670**; the bench's `instrumentValidity` caught it and voided the p100 effect, which is why no false null was published.\n\n#### Decision\n1. **Do not wire reranking into the default retrieval path.** Cost/benefit does not clear.\n2. **The lever is retrieval REACH.** ~80–88% of targets are never retrieved at all; no ranking change can touch them. Recall work strictly dominates ranking work here.\n3. Reranking may still ship on a **narrow, opt-in deep-dive surface** where ~1.8s is acceptable — and only with the cap+timeout moved together, else it is a silent no-op.\n4. Any future proposal to raise over-fetch **for reranking's benefit** is refused by this decision unless it also lifts `RERANK_MAX_CANDIDATES` and re-sizes the timeout.\n\nArtifacts: `/tmp/rr-p24-v3.json` (422 outcomes), `/tmp/rr-p100-v3.json` (238, effect void, strata sound). Bench: `packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/rerank-decision{,-cli}.ts`.\n\n⚠ Ground truth is DERIVED (a turn citing an item), not labelled — it measures known-item placement, which is what reranking claims to improve, not overall answer quality.\n\n### D-097 — P-010 ANSWERED: the pre-fusion per-ranker minScore is ALREADY IN FORCE on the corpus leg — and it is INERT there, rejecting 0 of 2,161 candidates including on off-domain queries\nDate: 2026-08-10\nDate: 2026-08-10 (su-90cc5, WI-37542). P-010 asks us to *evaluate adopting* a per-ranker `minScore` before fusion. **It was adopted already** — not by this item, but as a side effect of P-017's central embedder stamp. The live question is not whether to apply it; it is that applying it does nothing here.\n\n#### 1. Already in force — measured, not read\nResolved live from a warm process, using the leg's own embedder instance:\n\n```\nembedderModeOf(instance)                        = \"gemma\"\nproseMinScoreFloors(\"gemma\")                    = { embeddings: 0.45 }\nresolveSearchDefaults(hybrid, thatEmbedder)     = { minScore: { embeddings: 0.45 },\n                                                    applied: { policyRegistered: true } }\nresolveSearchDefaults(hybrid, FOREIGN embedder) = { minScore: null }      <- control passes\n```\n\nChain: `buildQueryEmbedderResolved` stamps the mode onto the memoized `embed` object (`embedder.ts:245`); `buildQueryEmbedder` returns **that same object** (`:269-271`); `corpus-recall-io.ts:381-391` stores it **unwrapped**, so WeakMap identity survives; `corpus-recall-io.ts:32` imports `SEARCH_SOURCES` and `sources.ts:26` side-imports `configure-search-defaults`, registering the engine default; the leg passes no `minScore`, so `hybrid.ts:378` falls through to it; applied per source at `hybrid.ts:411-421`.\n\n#### 2. And it rejects nothing\nWarm run (`embedderAvailable` 10/10), 5 in-domain + 5 deliberately off-domain — off-domain being the population a floor exists to reject:\n\n| arm | queries | candidates | **floored** |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| in-domain | 5 | 1,292 | **0** |\n| off-domain | 5 | 869 | **0** |\n\n`legs.semantic` on \"nutritional differences between quinoa and millet\": `{ status:\"ran\", candidates:144, floored:0 }`. Zero of 2,161 — independently corroborating WI-7020's \"minScore=0.45 is rejecting nothing\".\n\n#### 3. Why — the transferable part\n`prose-min-score.ts`'s own measurement (n=16,110 pairs; not re-derived here) records that **gemma carries a large POSITIVE cosine offset on this corpus: two RANDOM UNRELATED session_turns average .6119** (p95 .8105). The floor sits at .45, i.e. ~0.16 BELOW the noise mean, so it is beneath everything and cannot separate anything.\n\n0.45 was not wrong when set — it came from the query→doc top-1 direction (worst in-domain .4825) for `search:semantic`, where it demonstrably works (an off-domain query went 30 fused hits → 0; WI-7505/D-010). It is the wrong statistic for the *candidate-pool* distribution this leg feeds it.\n\n#### Decision\n1. **No adoption work to do.** The mechanism is present and correctly wired. Close P-010 on this evidence, not on an implementation.\n2. **Do NOT raise the floor to make it bite.** The tails overlap by measurement (worst in-domain .4825 < best off-domain .5629), so no absolute cut separates the populations here — a floor is a noise reducer, never a classifier. Raising it past gemma's ~.6119 noise mean deletes real hits first; a dropped true hit is unrecoverable, a kept noise row is still demotable downstream.\n3. **The live risk is the opposite one, and it is unmeasured.** `CORPUS_SOURCE_NAMES = ['session_turn','work_item']`, but `applyMinScore` is keyed per RANKER, not per SOURCE — so the session_turns/doc_sections-calibrated .45 also lands on `work_item` rows. EI-19899975562178082 records the precedent: `doc_sections` could inherit .45 unmeasured, but **work_items and plans had to be re-measured** (plans: worst in-domain top-10 .5370 vs best off-domain top-1 .5404 — a 0.0034 margin). That inheritance is harmless *only because the floor is inert*. Any future change to `EMBEDDING_FLOOR_GEMMA` must re-measure the `work_item` corpus first.\n4. **Fix the false comment** at `corpus-recall-io.ts:643-646`: *\"D-037 forbids an absolute score FLOOR on this leg\"*. Both halves are wrong — D-037 lives on plan `context-injection-audit-2026-07-28` and contains no such prohibition (4,097-char body: exactly one \"floor\", the phrase *\"evict a floor-passing memory\"* about mem0 pools; zero \"minScore\") — and the leg **is** floored. Keep the reasoning, drop the citation: it is mathematics, not a ruling. An absolute constant compared against a rank-derived FUSED value is meaningless, which is precisely why the pre-fusion per-ranker shape is the correct one.\n\n#### Method note\nThe static trace came first and was correct — but the runtime probe's own verdict logic read `floored: 0` as \"the floor never fired\" and printed **\"Static trace FALSIFIED\"**. It had not been: `floored: 0` means the floor RAN and rejected nothing. Same zero, opposite conclusions, and the wrong reading was the confident-looking one; `legs.status:\"ran\"` is what separated them.\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-098 — P-019 escalation RE-TARGETED in code to `unretrievable` alone, per D-095 §4 — the predicate now fires on 9.6% of traffic instead of 29.4%, and the probe that reports it no longer keeps its own copy of the rule\nDate: 2026-08-12\nDate: 2026-08-12 (su-2bbbd, WI-37504). Owner-directed. Implements the design finding D-095 §4 recorded but left unapplied; supersedes nothing in D-095, it executes it.\n\n#### 1. THE CHANGE\n`clarityWarrantsEscalation()` (corpus-query-clarity.ts) returned true for `unfocused` OR `unretrievable`. It now returns true for **`unretrievable` alone**.\n\nD-095 §4 is explicit and this is its direct application: \"the candidate trigger is `unretrievable` (and the high-SCS deciles 7/10, zero-hit 12-14%), NOT `unfocused`. This is a design finding, not a calibration detail.\" The measurement behind it: `unfocused` (15.9% of traffic, the bucket that WOULD have escalated) had the BEST reach of any bucket — mean 5.82 of 6 lines admitted, 92.4% filling all six, zero-hit 0.0% — while `unretrievable` (4.0%) is the bucket that fails: zero-hit 21.7%, mean admitted 0.93. The old predicate armed the expensive tier precisely where retrieval already works.\n\n#### 2. THE CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED BOTH WAYS\n`bench/corpus-query-clarity-cli.ts --queries 2000` against the live DF table (40,325 terms / 40,000 docs), run before and after:\n- BEFORE (`unfocused`+`unretrievable`): **29.4%** of traffic\n- AFTER (`unretrievable` alone): **9.6%** of traffic, over 99.3% of recalls\nDerived by hand first from the per-surface table weighted by the live 7d surface mix (~9.6%), then printed independently by the CLI (9.6%) — agreement between two routes, not one number trusted twice.\n\n⚠ RATES DRIFT — never quote a stored one. The SAME rule and threshold gave 19.7% on 2026-08-09 and 29.4% on 2026-08-12. The corpus moves under these figures. Any comparison must re-run both arms.\n\n#### 3. A DRIFT BUG THIS SURFACED (fixed here)\nThe probe kept its OWN hardcoded `unfocused + unretrievable` sum rather than calling the predicate, so after this re-target it would have gone on printing 29.4% for a predicate firing on 9.6% — a confident, wrong number with nothing failing. It now sums THROUGH `clarityWarrantsEscalation`, and the headline's bucket label is DERIVED from the predicate (`VERDICTS.filter`) so the label cannot describe a rule the number was not computed with. Same reasoning that pulled `corpusQueryIdToken` out of corpus-recall instead of copying it.\n\n#### 4. A SECOND-ORDER EFFECT CAUGHT ONLY BY RE-RUNNING — do not \"restore\" it\nRouting the POOL control arm through the predicate too made it read 0.0%, silently falsifying the sentence beside it (\"the gap is entirely an artifact of −log2(n)\"). Pool scope scores every candidate term, so a query is almost never WHOLLY unattested, and `unretrievable` is an ATTESTATION verdict, not a clarity one — the −log2(n) artifact lives entirely in the focused/unfocused cut. The pool arm is therefore now measured on the `unfocused` SHARE (issued vs pool), which is what it was always actually controlling for. The lesson generalises: when a predicate changes, every control derived from it must be re-justified, not just recompiled.\n\n#### 5. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DECIDE\n- **The TIER stays the parent plan's P-006 OWNER GATE** (`context-injection-audit-2026-07-28`). This ruling says WHEN a tier should be paid for, never WHAT it does. No LLM leg was wired and none should be.\n- **`CORPUS_CLARITY_FOCUSED_BITS = 5` stays UNCALIBRATED, now on stronger grounds.** D-095 §5 found no knee to calibrate against; since `unfocused` no longer escalates, the constant additionally governs NO SPEND — it only re-labels between two buckets that both retrieve well. Calibrate it if and only if a tier exists that spends differently across it. A test asserts neither side of the threshold escalates, so this property cannot rot silently.\n- **A KNOWN GAP is left open on purpose, and documented in the predicate rather than left as silence:** D-095 §4's other candidate — high-SCS deciles 7–10, zero-hit 12–14% — reads `focused` and is NOT escalated, because separating it needs the calibrated cut that does not exist. Whoever builds the tier inherits that question explicitly.\n\n#### 6. GUARDS\nThree tests pin the BEHAVIOUR, not the constant: `unfocused` does not escalate; `unretrievable` does; and an ENUMERATED check that exactly one verdict escalates, so a new verdict cannot default into the expensive path. The reverted premise is the intuitive one and will be re-proposed by anyone reading only the verdict names — that is what these block.\nRelated: P-019\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"decouple-generic-libs-private-deps-2026-08-03","title":"Decouple public libs/generic/* libraries from private/coupled workspace packages (WI-4973)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-03","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Decouple public libs/generic/* libraries from private/coupled workspace packages (WI-4973)\nslug: decouple-generic-libs-private-deps-2026-08-03\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-03\nupdated: 2026-08-03\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** DONE — all 6 items (P-001..P-006) complete. WI-4973 closed. Gate lint:generic-independence reports 0 findings across 53 borrowable libs. agent-chat confirmed out of scope (private, not under libs/generic/, not in BORROWABLE.md). Verification via test:affected across 21 downstream workspaces surfaced 4 pre-existing/unrelated reds, none caused by this change: 1 already claimed by a peer (EI-19411367924293520), 2 newly filed (WI-7376, WI-7377), 1 was a test-group-interaction artifact (passed clean in isolation).\n\n**Next:** Plan complete — no further action needed. See WI-4973 for full completion evidence.\n\n## Background\n\nOriginal ticket (WI-4973, filed 2026-07-15 by Avi): \"Decouple the 30 public generic libraries from private and missing workspace packages... keep the libraries public while coupled, then make them independently consumable later.\" No decoupling was performed during the original 2026-07-15 publication rollout. Follow-up to plan `generic-libraries-publication-2026-07-15` (shipped — that plan shipped the catalog/visibility, not the decoupling).\n\nAlso checked `BRIEF-tooldef-P054-handoff-2026-05-31` (shipped, tooldef-specific, \"attempted, reverted; here's how to finish it\") — superseded: `tooldef` now lives at `libs/generic/tooldef` and is in BORROWABLE.md, so that extraction has since completed via some other path.\n\nPrior claim history on WI-4973: claimed+released once (su-3f7a1836, released 2026-07-17) with NO checkpoint written — genuinely unknown whether any work happened, but the current-state audit above (fresh grep + package.json reads, 2026-08-03) did not find evidence of it. Re-claimed and this plan created same day (su-70390c8c) rather than guessing from the stale ticket text.\n\n## Phase 1 — Build the gate\n\n- **P-001** `done` Write `scripts/check-generic-independence.mjs`: reads the curated BORROWABLE list (reuse/import from `scripts/gen-borrowable-catalog.mjs` rather than re-curating), reads each `libs/generic/*` package's declared `@papercusp/*` deps, flags any dep whose target is not BORROWABLE-and-submodule-sourced. Modes: report (default, informational like `lint:generic-first`) and `--strict` (exit 1). Add an npm script `lint:generic-independence`.\n- **P-002** `done` Run the gate once, diff its output against this plan's \"Confirmed-still-coupled\" list above, and replace that list with the gate's authoritative output — retire the manual audit.\n- **P-003** `done` `blocked-by: P-002` For each genuinely-remaining coupled edge the gate reports: either (a) the target dep is itself borrowable+submodule-sourced already and the edge is actually fine (close as false-positive / tune the gate), or (b) extract the target to a real standalone `libs/generic/*` submodule (follow the extraction recipe already used for model-pricing/result-encoding), or (c) the coupling is genuinely internal-only and the SOURCE lib should be removed from the public BORROWABLE set instead of the target being extracted (a legitimate third outcome — not every listed lib may deserve to stay public). — note: All 13 hard-section findings fixed via peerDependencies; gate now clean.\n- **P-004** `done` `blocked-by: P-002` Resolve `agent-chat`'s ambiguous status: confirm whether it is actually one of \"the 30 public generic libraries\" this ticket is scoped to (it currently lives at `libs/agent-chat`, not `libs/generic/`, and is absent from BORROWABLE.md) — if it's out of scope, drop its edges from this plan; if in scope, move it under `libs/generic/` first per the reuse-first/generic-first convention. — note: agent-chat confirmed OUT of scope; dropped from this plan.\n- **P-005** `done` `blocked-by: P-003` Define the \"independent build/test/package-consumer gate\" WI-4973 asks for as a closing criterion: each of the 30 public libs must (i) build standalone (`npm run build` inside the lib with only its declared deps installed), (ii) test standalone, and (iii) be consumable by an external project pulling only its own submodule + its declared `@papercusp/*` deps. Land as a CI/lint check, not a one-time manual verification. — note: Landed as an advisory npm lint script with a --strict CI mode, matching the established lint:generic-first convention.\n- **P-006** `done` `blocked-by: P-005` Close WI-4973 citing the landed gate + a clean gate run across all 30 libs (or documented, owner-approved exceptions). — note: WI-4973 completed.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001\n**Title:** `\"private\": true` in a libs/generic/* package.json is NOT a public/private signal\n**Body:** Verified 2026-08-03: `sse`, `rrf`, `ipc-framing`, `model-pricing`, `result-encoding` all carry `\"private\": true` despite being fully public per BORROWABLE.md — it only means \"not npm-published, workspace-local install\". The real classification is the curated `BORROWABLE` array in `scripts/gen-borrowable-catalog.mjs`. Any future gate/audit here must classify off that array (or BORROWABLE.md, its generated projection), never off the package.json `private` field.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"memory-corpus-hygiene-and-release-distribution-2026-08-03","title":"Memory corpus hygiene + what knowledge ships in public releases","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-03","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Memory corpus hygiene + what knowledge ships in public releases\nslug: memory-corpus-hygiene-and-release-distribution-2026-08-03\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-03\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-014 is now BLOCKED on WI-37480, and the previous Now block was stale in a way that actively misled: it pointed at blocker EI-19899917753028359 (since CLOSED) and at lock-holder pid 2567270 (long gone). Do not chase either.\n\nWhat actually happened (2026-09-05, WI-8488): P-014's implementation half is shipped and verified by reading — fresh-head-snapshot-after-drain, the fail-fast sparse precondition guard, and the P-015 degradation guard all exist in cut-seed-cli.ts and cite P-014/D-012. The VERIFICATION half was then executed for real: `cut-seed-cli --sparse` drained the outbox to zero in 350,312ms, failed the head-snapshot leg 4x over 948,685ms, and REFUSED (exit 1) rather than shipping a full core. That refusal is a PASS for the guard, and it is why coreSparseFrom was never measured.\n\nRoot cause is external to this plan and measured, not inferred: a fixed ~300.7s SERVER ceiling truncates the head-snapshot POST (attempts 1 and 2 died 51ms apart at 300,708 / 300,759ms). Node v25.9.0 defaults server.requestTimeout to 300000ms and applyServerTimeouts() only overrides it when PAPERCUSP_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS is set, which it is not on the bg-host holder; the client meanwhile waits 900s, so its patience is unreachable. The holder was NOT mid-recycle despite the cut saying so (probeOnly answered booted:true in 0.507s), and it then died of a V8 heap OOM at 11.4G — so raising the timeout alone is a mitigation, not a fix.\n\n**Next:** Nobody should re-run the sparse cut unchanged — it will re-drain for ~6 minutes and fail identically; P-014 resumes only after WI-37480 (which now carries the measured evidence as post 93406) makes a head snapshot survivable within the server's request ceiling and within memory.\n\n## Background\n\nOwner question (2026-08-03, interactive): *\"Are all our papercusp memories other than user memories — and documentation and agent insights and shared memories — bundled with our public papercusp builds so that end-users get them too? Are user memories like 'I'm Avi' being excluded?\"*\n\n### What ships today (verified against code + live DB, not assumed)\n\n| Store | Lives in | Ships? |\n|---|---|---|\n| Docs + agent-insights (645 pages) | repo files, `apps/operator-docs` | YES — rendered site + source tree in the sidecar, minus ~8 pruned build-infra docs |\n| Built-in knowledge packs | `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/knowledge-packs/` | YES — `papercusp-default` (39), `coding` (39), `work` (30); verified present in the built sidecar |\n| Pot substrate: issues, plans, features, coord, members, policy, settings | seed corestore | YES — 12 federated tables, 2.0 GB seed |\n| Source repo | seed git bundle | YES — encrypted depth-1, 37 submodules |\n| **Memories** (32,824) | PG `memory_canonical` | **NO** |\n| **Facts** (2,957) | PG `agent_facts` | **NO** |\n| Recipes, scorecards, curation digests, tool_invocations | PG | NO |\n| Session transcripts, `MEMORY.md` | `~/.papercusp/`, `.claude/` | NO — explicitly excluded by the release allowlist |\n\n### Measured corpus baseline (2026-08-03)\n\n- **Total** 32,824 · active 31,857 · forgotten 415 · broken_anchor 350 · archived 202\n- **By scope (active):** harness 19,466 · user 9,900 · hive 2,467 · workspace 24\n- **By kind:** only 4,013 rows carry one (reference 1,595 · feedback 1,442 · project 966 · `user` 9 · preference 1). The other 28,811 predate the taxonomy (mem0-era `entityType`/`linkedMemoryIds` shape). NOTE: \"user memories\" is a SCOPE (9,900), not the kind literally named `user` (9 rows).\n- **Shape (the quality problem):** of 19,466 harness-scoped active, **17,613 (90%) are under 60 chars** and 12,820 (66%) start mid-sentence. Samples: `` `bash -c`) `` · `against the DEPLOYMENT` · `a decision and auto-assigns`. Well-formed (60+ chars) across harness+hive+workspace: **~2,809**.\n- **Residue in the non-user set (21,957 active):** 101 mention \"Avi\" · 44 absolute `/home/` paths · 31 `marsh-office` · 92 agent-session ids · 294 localhost/ports · **1,142 dangling WI-/EI-/F- ids**.\n- **Federation:** `shareable=true` on 1 memory and 5 facts. Capture triggers (migrations 563 / 461) fire only `WHEN (shareable = true)`, so nothing else can reach the substrate outbox. A user-scoped personal memory marked shareable is REFUSED (`remember.ts:299`).\n- **Pack provenance in PG:** 1,048 rows carry `pack_id` — `papercusp-default` 548, `coding` 461, `fleet-lessons` 30, `work` 9 (pack items × the pots they were seeded into).\n\n### How the knowledge-pack system works (as built)\n\nTwo ranked roots — `builtin` at `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/knowledge-packs/<id>/` (**ships in the bundle**) and `installed` at `~/.papercusp/knowledge-packs/<id>/` (Comb-installed); builtin wins an id clash so a community pack can never shadow a first-party one. A third `shared` root at `<workspaces>/shared/knowledge-packs/` holds fleet-global packs. Format is `manifest.json` + one-learning-per-file, semver-versioned — reviewable as a git diff.\n\nLifecycle: `pot:create` seeds `papercusp-default` (or `'none'`) → `knowledge_packs:install` runs an install-time conflict review (clean/duplicate/conflict; default SKIPS clashes, existing content outranks incoming) → `set_enabled` mutes without uninstalling → `uninstall` is provenance-driven (keeps user-edited rows, never touches organic) → `sweep` re-runs the conflict judge over the whole pool afterwards. Promotion: the recurrence-escalation loop stages CANDIDATES (carrying friction signature, scopes, recurrence count, source improvement ids) → a scheduled auto-review adopts/dismisses → adopted items land in `fleet-lessons` with a version bump → pots see `updateAvailable` → `upgrade`. Outward: `knowledge_packs:publish` exports organic learnings only (re-exporting installed packs needs explicit `includePackRows`) into a repo working tree, then lists on the Comb as PENDING with operator approval gating public visibility. Targeting: pack items declare `domains`, pots declare `knowledge-packs:domains`, manifests carry `applies_to`.\n\n## Phase 1 — Corpus hygiene (fix it for ourselves)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Measure the corpus: classify all 32,824 by scope × shape (fragment <60 / fact 60–300 / longform 300+) × transferability tier, and publish the counts as the durable baseline. Run via `code:run` or direct psql — `dev:pg_query` timed out twice on multi-regex scans during the audit. importance: high — note: Baseline measured and published as D-013.\n- **P-002** `done` Root-cause the fragments BEFORE deleting anything: determine whether any LIVE write path still produces sub-60-char extraction debris, or whether it is all mem0-era residue frozen by the `hybrid-pg` backend cutover. Deleting while a producer still runs just refills the store. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: Answered by D-013: the sub-60-char writes are NOT a defect.\n- **P-003** `dropped` Reversible purge of the confirmed debris class — `state` transition (archived/forgotten), never a hard delete — plus a recurrence guard that fails when the fragment share of new writes crosses a floor. blocked-by: P-002 — note: DROPPED as unsafe — its premise is disproven (D-013).\n- **P-004** `done` De-duplicate and reconcile contradictions across our own pool, reusing the `knowledge_packs:sweep` conflict judge rather than authoring a second one. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-8478 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Backfill `kind` + `scope` on surviving legacy rows (28,811 carry neither). The taxonomy is the input to every selection step downstream, so this gates Phase 2. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-8479 completed (done)\n- **P-020** `done` Give memory_canonical a first-class discriminator between MEMORIES and GRAPH ENTITY NODES (D-013). Today the only difference is the presence of a jsonb key (`payload->>'entityType'` + `linkedMemoryIds`), so every naive count over the table over-reports the memory corpus by ~8× (33,478 rows vs 4,089 actual memories) — which is exactly how this plan came to believe in a 28k-row 'fragment debris class' that is really a working entity index, and nearly purged it. Options: a real `row_kind` column with an index (migration; scope entity rows out of every memory read path by default), or a separate table. Also worth deciding: whether entity nodes should be recall-eligible at all, and whether they should count toward any corpus/size metric or ship in a seed. Whatever is chosen, add a recurrence guard: a test asserting that the canonical 'how many memories do we have' read excludes entity nodes, so the 8× over-count cannot come back. importance: high — note: ← WI-9355 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Distribution selection (extend the pack system, do not replace it)\n\n- **P-006** `done` Ship `fleet-lessons`. It materializes to `<workspaces>/shared/knowledge-packs/fleet-lessons` — outside the repo, outside the bundle — so the ONE pack our automated curation loop actually feeds never reaches a fresh install. Decide the mechanism (materialize into the builtin dir at release cut vs teach the cut to copy it) and implement. importance: high — note: ← WI-8480 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Measure promotion throughput: well-formed organic learnings → staged candidates → adopted pack items. 108 curated items against ~2,809 well-formed suggests the recurrence-escalation loop may be under-promoting — confirm before assuming, since the gap may be correct tier-2/3 exclusion. blocked-by: P-001 — note: measured (D-018): promotion is not under-throttled — the ≥2-scope gate is UNSATISFIABLE (98.1% one scope) and a newest-N window hides cross-scope recurrence. Fix filed as WI-9333.\n- **P-008** `done` Promotion pass over the cleaned corpus: lift tier-1 product knowledge into `papercusp-default`/`coding`, and tag tier-2 dev-infrastructure items with a contributor `domains` value instead of excluding them (per D-003). blocked-by: P-005, P-007 — note: ← WI-8482 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Pack-admission gate: length/kind floor + box-identity scan + dangling-ledger-id check, so no pack item can carry tier-3 residue. Reuse `audit-release-bundle.py`'s identity-literal rule as the single source of truth — never a second hand-kept list. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-8483 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — The ungated channels\n\n- **P-010** `done` OWNER DECISION: seed-corestore policy. 44k engineer issues, 3k coord messages and every plan ship with no pack review, no `applies_to` and no approval gate, while memories must pass three. Options: (a) accept as a deliberately contributor-oriented seed, (b) filter at cut time, (c) split a contributor seed from a product seed. importance: high — note: ← WI-8484 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Close the `seed.dump` hole: `build-desktop-sidecar.sh:2732` pg_dumps an ENTIRE database into the bundle when `PAPERCUSP_SEED_PG_URL` is set — no shareable filter, no personal-memory exclusion — and once baked it is silently carried forward from the last published sidecar on later builds. Dormant today (no dump exists, nothing sets the var); make it refuse by default. — note: DONE 2026-08-08. Both clauses closed, and the guard now actually RUNS. (1) The pg_dump bake is GONE, not merely refusing — EI-19455334533123459 deleted it 2026-08-03 (its consumer had been gone since D-004); PAPERCUSP_SEED_PG_URL appears nowhere in the tree outside the guard itself. (2) The silent carry-forward is covered: the WI-3346 republish overlay loop is asserted to stay the two-entry allowlist (source.tar.zst, env-sidecars) and to never widen to a wholesale copy of the outgoing bundle. (3) THE REAL REMAINING WORK, found today: the recurrence guard sidecar-no-database-bake-guard was committed and passing but NEVER EXECUTED — test:shell enumerates its files BY HAND and nothing named it. Measured: 16 test files on disk, 14 reachable from `npm test`; the two orphans were this P-011 guard and updater-e2e-vm (static analysis, no VM, 156ms — it had a dedicated script nothing chained). Both are now in test:shell. Fixed as a CLASS, not a one-off: a new test-registry-coverage guard fails…\n- **P-012** `done` Teach the release gate to inspect archives. `audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir` uses `grep -rIlE`, and `-I` skips binary files, so `seed.dump`, `db-seed.tar.gz` and the corestore are invisible to the identity scan that guards every other shipped byte. blocked-by: P-011 — note: ← WI-8486 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` DIAGNOSE the degraded sparse cut (D-009): the shipped manifest carries `coreSparseFrom: 0` on a 461,475-block / 1.9 GB core, meaning a sparse cut was requested and fell back to full history. Determine which cause: (a) no complete snapshot inside read-merge's SNAPSHOT_SCAN_LOOKBACK at cut time, or (b) inherited from a committed full-history corestore via PAPERCUSP_SEED_REUSE_CORESTORE=auto, which preserves coreSparseFrom. Do not fix before the cause is named — the remedies differ. importance: high — note: Root-caused — see D-012.\n- **P-014** `blocked` FIX the cut so releases ship CURRENT STATE, not history: append a fresh head snapshot (produceLogSnapshot) after the pre-cut drain, force a non-reuse sparse cut, and verify the manifest lands `coreSparseFrom > 0` with the size dropping toward the ~40 MB the tooling advertises. Then verify a restore-from-sparse still reconstitutes full current state on a cold install (the snapshot-aware reader SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT is REQUIRED for a sparse seed — confirm it is on in the shipped build before cutting sparse). importance: high — note: BLOCKED on WI-37480. Impl half shipped+verified; verification half ran 2026-09-05 and the sparse cut correctly REFUSED — head-snapshot POST to the hive holder is truncated at a fixed ~300.7s server ceiling (node requestTimeout default 300s vs the client's 900s patience), so coreSparseFrom is never measured. Evidence: WI-8488 checkpoint + WI-37480 post 93406. Do NOT re-run the cut unchanged.\n- **P-015** `done` Add a release-cut guard that FAILS when the seed manifest reports `coreSparseFrom: 0` (or a core length above a size floor) without an explicit acknowledgement env — the current failure is silent, degrades to a 50x larger installer, and self-perpetuates through reuse. This is the recurrence guard for the D-009 class. blocked-by: P-014 — note: ← WI-8489 completed (done)\n- **P-016** `done` COORD RETENTION (D-010, the mechanism that actually cuts coord from the seed): add a retention sweep that issues `del` ops for federated coord_event_log rows past a horizon, so they tombstone and then GC out of the snapshot. Pick the horizon from what a JOINING peer genuinely needs (recent handoffs/claims/escalations — likely days, not weeks), not from what is convenient to keep. Verify the seed's snapshot row-count drops accordingly. Keep live federation intact — this trims history, it does not stop the stream. importance: high — note: ← WI-8490 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `done` Verify the retention sweep does not break a cold joiner: a peer restoring from a trimmed seed must still reconstitute correct CURRENT coordination state (open claims, live handoffs, unacked escalations). Tombstone horizon must exceed the retention horizon, or a late-arriving stale PUT can resurrect a deleted key (EI-1688). blocked-by: P-016 importance: high — note: ← WI-8491 completed (done)\n- **P-018** `done` INVESTIGATE per-recipient coord routing (D-011): today an A-to-B message replicates to every peer that admits our log and is filtered by envelope `to[]` at READ time — cost grows as peers x messages with no bound. Scope the two candidate directions (direct-addressed DM transport with only pot-wide events on the shared log; or recipient-scoped sub-logs) and report a recommendation with a cost model. Investigation only — do not build from this item. — note: ← WI-8492 completed (done)\n- **P-019** `done` Restore the NO-OUTAGE sparse cut: let the LIVE operator produce a head snapshot on demand, so a sparse seed can be cut without quiescing (D-012). Today only the writable/quiesced cut branch can append the head snapshot a sparse cut requires; the WI-4487 read-only path holds no write lock, so P-014's guard correctly REFUSES sparse there and falls back to an honest full cut — which still ships ~1.9GB. Mechanism to design: an operator-side one-shot `produceLogSnapshot` on the booted harness's own log (getBootedHarness is already exported from boot-all.ts:624), requested by the cutter and awaited before its read-only open (cut-seed-cli.ts, after waitForOperatorDrain, before the openStore readOnly at the `if (!sourceWritable)` block). ⚠ COST TO DESIGN AROUND, measured during P-013: produceLogSnapshot reads the ENTIRE own log ([0,length), log-snapshot.ts:414-419) — 461,475 blocks today — and boot.ts runs compaction INSIDE the serialized merge block, so a one-shot at this size would stall the merge loop for the duration. That cost is why the periodic cadence is 1-per-1000-ops, and it applies wherever the snapshot runs (the quiesced path pays it too). Do NOT route around this by flipping SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT: it is a genuine case:'incomplete' dark flag gated on the P-008 two-machine convergence proof, and it is read ONCE at boot (boot.ts:1939-1940) so it would need an operator restart anyway. importance: high — note: ← WI-9635 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Corpus noise is OUR bug, not a distribution filter\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-03] *\"noise is noise whether its them or us, no? if there is noise we should fix it for ourselves, no?\"* — I had presented the 90%-fragment finding as the leading reason not to ship memories. That was a workaround dressed as an argument. The remedy is to clean our own store, which is also what our own standing hive memory says (*\"Fix wrong memories instead of working around them\"*). Distribution decisions are then made on the cleaned corpus, separately.\n\n### D-002 Quality and transferability are ORTHOGONAL axes\n\nCleaning for ourselves asks: well-formed, true, non-duplicate, still valid? Selecting for distribution asks: true anywhere other than this machine? A memory can pass the first and fail the second — `\":3070 runs the frozen release checkout\"` is an excellent memory and unshippable. Therefore cleaning raises the ceiling but does NOT produce a shippable set, and a selection step is required regardless of how clean the corpus gets.\n\n### D-003 Three transferability tiers — and dogfooding means tier 1 dominates\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-03] *\"we are dogfooding papercusp inside papercusp so not all of this is misleading\"* — correct, and my earlier \"much of it is true only of this box\" was too broad. **Tier 1 PRODUCT** knowledge (tool semantics, table shapes, caps, gotchas) is what dogfooding actually teaches, transfers perfectly, and SHOULD ship. **Tier 2 DEV-INFRASTRUCTURE** (release pipeline, build VMs, systemd units, the fleet gate) transfers to a CONTRIBUTOR but not a product user — express via pack `domains`/`applies_to` rather than excluding it, especially since the seed already ships the source repo and the issue ledger to exactly that audience. **Tier 3 THIS-BOX** (hostnames, absolute paths, VM aliases, agent session ids) never ships.\n\n### D-004 The knowledge-pack system IS the distribution allowlist — do not build a parallel selector\n\nIt already provides versioned pack dirs shipped in the bundle, seeding at pot creation, install-time conflict review, enable/disable, provenance-driven uninstall, a post-hoc conflict sweep, automated promotion via recurrence-escalation candidates, Comb publication gated by operator approval, and `domains`/`applies_to` targeting. Default is NOT-shared; promotion into a pack is the only path from our store to a user's. Any new \"what ships\" mechanism must extend this per reuse-first, not sit beside it.\n\n### D-005 Keep-but-never-distribute classes\n\nCredentials and access topology (ssh targets, VM aliases, token paths) · owner-personal facts — which is also a CORRECTNESS bug, since shipping \"[owner:Avi] wants X\" makes a stranger's agent apply Avi's preferences to a different human · unfixed security findings and the known-limitations inventory (we already prune `federation-public-release-known-limitations` from shipped docs; the same reasoning binds memories) · unreleased strategy (competitors, pricing, roadmap) · other pots' content, which is not ours to redistribute · in-flight temporal state, since memories carry no TTL and ship as a frozen lie · attributed critiques of specific agents or sessions.\n\n### D-006 RETRACTION — the seed bundle does ship, and ships real pot data\n\nMy earlier claim in this audit — *\"the public build ships a schema-only database; none of it ships\"* — was WRONG and is retracted. `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/seed/` is a 2.0 GB bundle (corestore 1.9 GB / 461,475 blocks + encrypted git 126 MB + `epoch-keys.json`), cut 2026-07-21, restored BEFORE the pot join so the join carries only the delta. It ships via `tauri.server.conf.json` and the gate overlay; the GUI base config deliberately excludes it, pinned by `test/tauri-config-resources.test.js` (\"GUI/base resources must not include the multi-GB seed\"), and `ensure-release-seed.sh` is wired into `beforeBuildCommand` so a fresh cut is intrinsic to `tauri build`. The error was reasoning from one artifact (`db-seed.tar.gz`, which genuinely is schema-only) without searching for the system the owner had built. What survives the correction: memories and facts really are absent from the seed, because federation is `shareable`-gated.\n\n### D-007 The seed carries its own decryption key — shipping into it is publication\n\n`epoch-keys.json` ships inside the seed so a fresh install can decrypt offline with no sign-in (the \"offline pot\" path). Anything placed in the corestore is therefore readable by anyone holding the installer — this is publication, not member-gated sharing, and a 2.0 GB installer cannot be unshipped. Any proposal to add memories to the seed must clear that bar, not merely the federation bar.\n\n### D-008 — AMENDS D-003 — dev-infrastructure knowledge SHIPS too (tier 2 is not contributor-gated)\nDate: 2026-08-03\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-03, verbatim] \"ship dev-infra too\" — supersedes D-003's contributor-gating of tier 2. The shipping rule is now TWO tiers, not three-with-a-gate: **tier 1 PRODUCT and tier 2 DEV-INFRASTRUCTURE both ship**; only **tier 3 THIS-BOX** (hostnames, absolute paths, VM aliases, agent-session ids, credentials/access topology) is excluded. Rationale consistent with the seed already shipping the full source repo and the 44k-row issue ledger — an install that receives the code and the engineering history should also receive the knowledge about how that code is built, released and operated. `domains`/`applies_to` remain available as ORGANIZING metadata (so a pack can say what a learning is about) but are no longer an admission gate for tier 2. Consequence for P-008: the promotion pass lifts tier 1 AND tier 2 into packs; only D-005's keep-never-distribute classes and tier-3 residue are filtered.\n\n### D-009 — Coord federates BY DESIGN; shipping its HISTORY is a degraded sparse cut, not a policy choice\nDate: 2026-08-03\nOwner question: \"why are we shipping coord messages at all?\" Two separate answers.\n\n**(a) Coord federation is deliberate and correct.** Migration 150 (plan distributed-coordination-shared-harness-2026-06-04, Track A) federates harness-scoped coord_event_log rows because cross-machine agent-to-agent messaging is, in its own words, \"the highest-value coord surface\" — in a multi-peer pot an agent on machine A must reach an agent on machine B. It is already carefully scoped: only ORIGINAL content federates (authored messages, handoffs, escalations); per-subscriber fan-out DELIVERY copies stay local (D-002 \"content federates, delivery stays local\"); operator/workspace-scope coord stays local (D-007, \"it has no swarm to ride\").\n\n**(b) The seed shipping 131k rows of coord HISTORY is an accident.** The corestore is cut with `coreSparseFrom: 0` — the entire log from genesis, 461,475 blocks, 1.9 GB.
