The system has a SPARSE mode built for exactly this: cut only `[latest complete snapshot, len)`, the span a snapshot-aware reader folds to reconstitute CURRENT state (ensure-release-seed.sh cites ~40 MB vs ~2.1 GB, and PAPERCUSP_SEED_SPARSE defaults to 1). Our manifest CARRIES the `coreSparseFrom` key — which seed-provider-corestore.ts only emits when `sparse` was true — resolved to 0, which that provider documents as \"no complete snapshot within the reader's scan window\" and warns about, prescribing a fresh head snapshot via produceLogSnapshot after the pre-cut drain. Compounding it, PAPERCUSP_SEED_REUSE_CORESTORE defaults to `auto`, which reuses the committed corestore and PRESERVES its coreSparseFrom — so once a full-history core was committed, every later release has re-shipped it.\n\n**Consequence:** the honest answer is that we are not shipping coord messages *per se* — we are shipping EVERYTHING ever appended, of which historical coord traffic, superseded plan revisions and closed-issue churn are the visible symptoms. Fixing the sparse cut ships current state instead of history, needs no new gate, and is a ~50x installer size reduction. This is a fourth option for P-010, and strictly better than the three originally posed (accept / filter at cut / split seeds) because it is the DESIGNED behavior rather than new machinery. NOT yet verified: whether the degradation is a missing snapshot or inherited via reuse — P-013 diagnoses before P-014 fixes.\n\n### D-010 — CORRECTS D-009 — a sparse cut does NOT drop coord messages; coord needs RETENTION, not sparsity\nDate: 2026-08-03\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-03, verbatim] \"lets just cut coord messages entirely\" — and the owner was right to challenge the sparse recommendation, which does not achieve it.\n\n**What a sparse cut actually does.** log-snapshot.ts builds \"the minimal current-state put-set — latest live put per key\"; a key whose latest op is a `del` becomes a TOMBSTONE, GC'd after `tombstoneHorizonMs`. So sparsity collapses SUPERSEDED VERSIONS — plan revisions, issue updates, feature churn — where many ops share one key. It does NOT collapse DISTINCT KEYS.\n\n**Coord messages are distinct keys.** Migration 150: \"KEY for the peer-log: the globally-unique msg_id\". Every coord message is its own key with exactly one live put and no superseding op — so all 30,953 federated coord rows survive into a snapshot and ride a sparse seed unchanged. The D-009 claim that fixing the sparse cut resolves the coord-history problem was WRONG for coord specifically. It remains correct for plan/issue/feature churn, which is where the size win comes from.\n\n**Also retracts P-010 option (b) \"filter at cut\" as architecturally unavailable.** The seed is a byte-level copy of a signed, merkle-verified append-only log. A suffix can be shipped (sparse); individual ops CANNOT be excised without re-authoring the log, which changes the core key and breaks log identity. Per-table filtering of an existing seed is not an option that exists.\n\n**The mechanism that DOES cut coord: retention.** Issue `del` ops for federated coord rows past a retention horizon; the dels federate, become tombstones, and GC out of the snapshot after the tombstone horizon — machinery that already exists rather than new filtering. Correct on the merits independent of shipping: coord is an ephemeral coordination stream (intents, presence, handoffs), not durable substrate, and nothing needs a six-week-old declared-intent message. Durable work-item-scoped direction already lives in work_items:comment / checkpoint by design.\n\n**What must NOT be cut: live coord federation.** Stopping the capture triggers kills cross-machine agent-to-agent messaging (the LIVE-2 capability, gate item P-059). It is not dormant: 3,646 rows on this box carry origin<>'local', i.e. they arrived from peer machines. Cut the HISTORY and the SEED payload; keep the live stream.\nRelated: P-010, P-014\n\n### D-011 — Coord federation IS broadcast-to-all-peers with read-time filtering — no per-recipient routing\nDate: 2026-08-03\nOwner question: \"only machine A and machine B should get the messages between A and B — not everyone in the shared pot. Is that how it works?\" **No. It is broadcast.**\n\n**Mechanism.** A federated coord row is appended to the author's own peer-log. boot.ts maintains an ADMITTED SET of logs and reads MERGE across all of them, so every peer that admits our log replicates every federated row we write. Migration 150 states the delivery model explicitly: \"on the remote machine the recipient's coord:inbox read finds it by the envelope `to[]`\" — i.e. addressing is a READ-TIME FILTER, not a transport-time route. There is no per-recipient channel.\n\n**Measured scope (2026-08-03).** coord_event_log holds 129,834 rows; 30,953 (24%) are harness-scoped and therefore federate; 3,646 arrived from peers. The 76% majority is operator/workspace-scope and stays local — migration 150 short-circuits on `harness_slug IS NOT NULL`, and per-subscriber fan-out DELIVERY copies never federate (\"content federates, delivery stays local\"). So the broadcast is already scoped to a quarter of coord traffic; within that quarter it is genuinely all-peers.\n\n**Assessment.** Tolerable at today's pot size (a handful of our own machines, small message bodies) but it does not scale: cost grows as peers x messages, with no retention bound. The owner's concern is structurally correct. Two candidate directions, neither yet designed: (a) a direct-addressed transport for agent-to-agent DMs, keeping only genuinely pot-wide events (handoffs, escalations, claims) on the shared log; (b) recipient-scoped sub-logs. Both are larger than this plan — scoped as P-018 to investigate, not to build here.\n\n### D-012 — P-013 root cause: the sparse cut's head-snapshot step is missing from the live-operator branch (and the periodic producer is dark)\nDate: 2026-08-03\nMEASURED (shipped manifest papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/seed/manifest.json, cutTs 2026-07-21T14:48:54Z): one core 5b00878b…, coreLengths 461,475, coreSparseFrom {5b00878b…: 0}, sizeBytes 1,998,388,355.\n\nRULED OUT — candidate (b), inheritance via reuse. `coreSparseFrom` is emitted ONLY when the cut ctx has sparse:true (seed-provider-corestore.ts:266) and cut-seed-cli.ts:734 THROWS if --sparse is combined with --reuse-corestore. The shipped core's newest op HLC is 2026-07-21T14:47:27Z — 87s before cutTs — so this was a FRESH sparse cut from the live store, not a stale graft. The core spans 2026-06-25T00:47:47Z → 2026-07-21T14:47:27Z.\n\nWHY from=0. Snapshot sets actually present in the shipped core (enumerated by scanning the staged corestore for `snapshot/<n>/<i>-of-<k>` keys): single-chunk sets at coversUpTo 1000/2002/3109/3141/3838/7134/7783/9012/12606/14554, then ONE 10-chunk set at coversUpTo=184403 (~2026-07-10T21:38Z). NOTHING after 184,403. SNAPSHOT_SCAN_LOOKBACK = SNAPSHOT_COMPACT_EVERY_OPS(1000) × 4 = 4,000 (read-merge.ts:414, log-snapshot.ts:358), so the scan floor at cut time was 461,475 − 4,000 = 457,475. The latest snapshot sits 273,072 blocks BELOW that floor → findLatestCompleteSnapshot returns null → computeSparseFrom returns 0 (seed-provider-corestore.ts:201-207) → the cut warns and ships FULL.\n\nROOT CAUSE — a two-factor conjunction:\n\n(i) THE HEAD-SNAPSHOT STEP EXISTS ONLY IN THE WRITABLE CUT BRANCH. openCorestoreSourceForCut (cut-seed-cli.ts ~450) branches on `sourceWritable`. The quiesced/writable branch (480-485) calls refreshCorestoreStateForSeed({…, sparse: inp.sparse}), which after the drain appends a fresh head snapshot (389-396) — the step whose own comment states that without it \"the 'sparse' cut silently ships FULL\". The live-operator branch (486-507) — the WI-4487 no-outage read-only path — does backfill + waitForOperatorDrain ONLY: it never consults `sparse` and cannot append (it holds no write lock). That branch is the only one consistent with both observations (the drain plainly happened — ops exist up to 87s pre-cut — yet no snapshot at ~461,475 was appended). So on ANY box running the operator, the sparse cut's stated precondition is silently unmet.\n\n(ii) THE PERIODIC PRODUCER IS DARK. SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT (producer leg) is default-OFF in KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS (case:'incomplete', WI-3370, 2026-07-10) pending the P-008 two-machine convergence proof; harness_shared.operator_flag_overrides holds no matching override, so the default stands. The last snapshot in the log is dated 2026-07-10T21:38Z — the split date itself. 277,072 ops have been appended since with none produced.\n\nEither factor alone is survivable: with (i) fixed the cut makes its own snapshot regardless of the flag; with (ii) ON the operator keeps one inside the 4,000-op window. Together they make --sparse a silent no-op.\n\nCORRECTION to my earlier framing in this plan: I expected the dark producer flag to be the blocker for the cutter itself. It is NOT. produceLogSnapshot carries no internal flag check — the gate deliberately lives at boot.ts's call site (log-snapshot.ts:404-408) — so the cutter's head-snapshot call would run today if the branch reached it. The flag explains why no OTHER snapshot is fresh, not why the cut skipped one.\n\nCONSEQUENCES:\n\n- P-014 fixes (i): the head snapshot must also happen on the live-operator path. Because that branch cannot write, the snapshot has to be produced BY the live operator (ask it to run produceLogSnapshot once on its own log) rather than by the cutter. Sequencing is load-bearing: AFTER waitForOperatorDrain returns, BEFORE the read-only open at line 529.\n- DO NOT 'fix' this by widening SNAPSHOT_SCAN_LOOKBACK. Seeding at the existing 184,403 snapshot ships [184403, 461475) = 277,072 of 461,475 blocks — only ~40% off (~1.1 GB), because that snapshot is 26 days stale. A FRESH head snapshot at ~461,475 is what delivers the ~40 MB the design claims.\n- Flipping SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT ON is NOT the fix and is not ours to take unilaterally: it is a genuine case:'incomplete' dark flag gated on the P-008 cross-machine proof, not parking-lot abuse.\n- P-015's guard is CONFIRMED necessary and should assert coreSparseFrom > 0 on a --sparse cut. Today the only signal is a console.warn on a non-fatal path — which is exactly how a 1.9 GB 'sparse' seed shipped unnoticed for three weeks.\n\n### D-013 — P-001 measurement: the corpus is 4,089 memories + 29,389 GRAPH ENTITY NODES — the 'fragment debris class' does not exist, and purging it would destroy the entity index\nDate: 2026-08-03\nMEASURED 2026-08-03 over harness_shared.memory_canonical (33,478 rows total; the audit's 32,824 was 5 days ago — it grows ~650/wk).\n\nTHE TABLE HOLDS TWO POPULATIONS, and every prior count in this plan conflated them. The discriminator is `payload->>'entityType'`:\n\n| entityType | rows | linkedMemoryIds | avg len | new in 24h |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| COMPOUND | 24,555 | 24,555 | 23 | 1,190 |\n| PROPER | 3,630 | 3,630 | 14 | 177 |\n| QUOTED | 1,204 | 1,204 | 28 | 96 |\n| (absent) = REAL MEMORIES | 4,089 | 0 | 828 | 59 |\n\nThe three entityType classes are mem0's ENTITY-GRAPH NODES, not memories: every one of the 29,389 carries `linkedMemoryIds` pointing back at the memory it was extracted from. Verified on a 5,000-edge sample: 4,995 resolve to a real memory (entityType absent), 0 resolve to another entity node, 5 dangle. It is a working entity→memory index, structurally correct for what it is.\n\nWHAT THIS OVERTURNS:\n\n1. P-003 (\"reversible purge of the confirmed debris class\") IS DANGEROUS AS WRITTEN. The 28,557 sub-60-char rows this plan called debris ARE the entity index. Purging by length would have deleted the memory graph and silently degraded recall. P-003 must be re-scoped or dropped; do NOT execute it against a length predicate.\n\n2. P-002 (\"root-cause the fragments BEFORE deleting\") is ANSWERED, and the answer is 'not a defect'. The sub-60-char writes are mem0's entity extraction working as designed — not a broken splitter. They are still being produced (1,463 entity nodes in the last 24h vs 59 real memories) because extraction runs on every memory write. Nothing to fix; P-002 can close on this finding.\n\n3. P-005 (\"backfill kind+scope on 28,811 legacy rows carrying neither\") is largely ILLUSORY. Those 28,811 are the entity nodes, which correctly carry neither. Scoped to REAL memories the taxonomy is already near-complete: 4,036/4,089 have `kind` (98.7%) and 3,486/4,089 have `scope` (85.2%). The real backfill is ~600 rows missing `scope`, not 28,811.\n\n4. The corpus-size framing for distribution changes shape. Real memories: 4,089 — 3,279 in papercusp-workspace, 3,117 active, avg 828 chars, and exactly ONE marked shareable. The shareable gate (D-007) therefore still holds: memory_canonical does not federate on content.\n\nMETHOD NOTE / SELF-CORRECTION: my first pass sampled fragment texts with `ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 18`, every row of which showed multiplicity 10, and I read that as '10× duplication across the fragment population'. That was a sampling artifact of ordering by the count I was measuring. The true multiplicity distribution is 22,362 of 25,003 distinct texts at multiplicity 1; only 44 distinct texts reach 10. There is no systematic 10× duplication.\n\nRESIDUAL ISSUE WORTH ITS OWN ITEM: memories and entity-graph nodes share one table with no column-level discriminator (only a jsonb key), which is precisely why every count in this plan — and the 'debris' framing itself — came out wrong. Any consumer treating memory_canonical as 'the memories' over-counts by 8×. Filed as P-020.\n\n### D-014 — D-014 — coord retention must EXEMPT health state, not just age it out\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03\n\nImplementing D-010 naively — \"expire federated coord rows past a short horizon\" — would have caused a silent health regression, caught by reading the READERS of the surface before shipping rather than after.\n\n**The trap.** `openSinglePrimaryConditions` (system-health) and the coord conditions fast path both scan `surface=messages` with a `ts >= now() - MESSAGE_GC_RETENTION_DAYS` bound, and both justify that bound in comments with \"nothing older survives GC anyway\". That justification silently BINDS the reader window to the GC horizon. Introducing a SECOND, shorter horizon for one class of rows breaks it for that class without touching either reader: harness-scoped condition alarms would have started expiring at 7d while the reader still believed its window was 30d.\n\n**Why the failure is worse than data loss.** These messages are health STATE, not chatter. The reader computes \"open\" as an alarm with no later resolution in the window. An alarm aged out with no resolution therefore reads as RESOLVED — not as missing. A shortened horizon would have made open single-primary conditions quietly disappear.\n\n**The ruling.** A condition-carrying thread (`body ? condition_key OR body ? resolves_condition`) stays on the LONGER operator horizon whatever its scope. Measured cost: 12 rows exempted today, 52 harness-scoped condition rows total — nothing, against a whole failure class.\n\n**The generalizable rule for the rest of this plan.** Before shortening ANY retention horizon, find the readers that bound their scans by the old one. A retention change is an API change to every consumer that assumed the old window, and those consumers do not fail loudly — they return a shorter history that looks like a real answer. This applies directly to the remaining plan items that trim history.\n\nRelated: P-016, D-010\n\n### D-015 — The memory taxonomy is DERIVABLE from user_id, and 'bench' is a fail-safe scope Phase 2 must exclude\nDate: 2026-08-03\nSettled while implementing P-005 (migration 747). Three rulings that bind Phase 2 distribution selection.\n\n1. `payload.scope` IS RECOVERABLE, NOT GUESSED. memory:remember computes a scopeKey and mem0 stores it as `payload.user_id` (libs/generic/memory/src/mem0-backend.ts: \"the neutral `scope` string maps onto mem0's `user_id` filter\"); `payload.scope` is the separate TAXONOMY value carried in metadata. So the taxonomy is a pure function of a prefix already on every row, and the backfill inverts exactly the mapping remember.ts applies on the way in: 'harness:<slug>'->'harness', 'hive:<slug>'->'hive', 'bench'->'bench', anything else (a user id)->'user'. Measured 2026-08-03: 603 real memories missing scope, ZERO undecidable. Do not re-derive this by sampling bodies.\n\n2. RECALL DOES NOT FILTER ON scope OR kind — so this was never a recall bug. mem0 fans every search out per scope on a `user_id` filter (mem0-backend.ts:391 \"Scope invariant\"), and remember-coerce.ts states it independently: \"recall is semantic (not kind-filtered), so the blast radius of a defaulted kind is tiny\". The 603 rows were fully retrievable the whole time. The gap is TAXONOMY COMPLETENESS, and it bites only where the plan says it does — Phase 2 selection, which cannot reason about a fact with no taxonomy. This is also why the loss stayed invisible for two months: nothing user-facing degraded.\n\n3. 'bench' IS A DELIBERATE FIFTH SCOPE, AND PHASE 2 MUST EXCLUDE IT BY CONSTRUCTION. 342 of the 603 are recall-benchmark fixtures (BENCH_SCOPE, bench/run-bench.ts:53) seeded into the live canonical table and never swept; their bodies are ANOTHER project's content, incl. a production IP and deploy paths (filed EI-19451290686156597). They were given scope='bench' rather than being laundered into 'user'/'harness' so that a Phase 2 selector admitting only real pools — scope IN ('harness','hive','user') — drops them by construction rather than by remembering to. WRITE THE SELECTOR AS AN ALLOWLIST OF REAL POOLS, NEVER AS A DENYLIST OF 'bench': an allowlist also excludes the 24 out-of-enum 'workspace' rows and any future pool, and fails safe on anything it has not seen.\n\n4. A DERIVED TAXONOMY VALUE MUST NEVER MASQUERADE AS AN AUTHORED ONE. Every value 747 writes is stamped (`scope_provenance` / `kind_provenance` = 'migration-747:...'). Phase 2 can weigh an inferred taxonomy differently from one the writing agent chose; query `payload ? 'kind_provenance'` for the 53 defaulted kinds. A missing kind becomes 'reference' because that is the codebase's own documented default (normalizeMemoryKind, remember-coerce.ts), not a value I invented.\n\n5. THE PRODUCER IS STILL RUNNING, so 747 is a MITIGATION and the drift will recur. 53 rows land with a bare payload (no kind/scope/metadata at all), newest 2026-08-03, mechanism unconfirmed — filed EI-19451352980847889. 747 is idempotent and re-runnable, but P-005 closing does NOT mean the class is closed.\n\n### D-016 — Corpus hygiene is THREE layers, and an unwired judge must never report \"clean\"\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03\nSettled while implementing P-004 (memory:sweep). Binds any future corpus-hygiene or distribution-selection work.\n\n1. DEDUPE AND CONTRADICTION ARE DIFFERENT LAYERS WITH DIFFERENT AUTHORITY. Exact duplicates (same pool, identical after NFKC+whitespace+case fold) are DETERMINISTIC and provably redundant, so they are the ONLY thing allowed to auto-resolve. Contradictions are a JUDGEMENT between two organic memories with no asymmetry to arbitrate on — they are FILED, never auto-resolved. The hive case can auto-resolve only because a PRISTINE pack row is provably not the user's words (D-002); our own pool has no such tiebreak. Cheapest layer first: the judge is an LLM call per row, so dedupe runs free and first.\n\n2. RESOLUTION IS SOFT AND LOCAL-ONLY. Redundant rows are closed via the temporal-lite validity window (backend.invalidateEntry — the same primitive memory:forget { soft:true } uses), never hard-deleted, so every resolution stays retrievable via include_superseded/as_of. A row that is shareable, non-local origin, or carries source_hive is NEVER touched: capture_memory_canonical_outbox_upd_trg emits a federation op on any UPDATE WHEN (new.shareable OR old.shareable), so resolving one locally would broadcast a delete to every peer over a judgement they never made.\n\n3. AN UNKEYED JUDGE REPORTS EVERYTHING CLEAN — SO THE SWEEP MUST REFUSE TO RUN, NOT REPORT A ZERO. Measured live 2026-08-03: the corpus CLI swept 1,583 rows and returned conflictPairs:0 in a process where no ANTHROPIC key resolves, i.e. the judge was never called. That zero is indistinguishable from a clean bill of health and is exactly the false-green class this fleet keeps paying for. EI-18746586784230719 already knew this one layer down but only console.warn'd it, which no structured caller sees. Both sweeps now carry judgeUnavailable: when true, conflictPairs:0 means NOT MEASURED and the layer is skipped outright. The probe fails OPEN — a probe that cannot answer must never be the reason the layer is silently skipped.\n\n4. MEASURED RESULT. harness:papercusp held 1,583 recallable rows / 94 duplicate groups / 98 redundant rows; all 98 closed, 0 errors, re-run converged to 0 groups. Note 'recallable' is state <> 'archived', NOT state='active': canonical-store filters recall on archived alone, so forgotten/broken_anchor rows are STILL SERVED and are in scope for hygiene. A sweep scoped to state='active' would have missed 283 of them.\n\n### D-017 — Curated packs ship by COMMITTED EXPORT, not a cut-time copy — and a pack item carries no internal references\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03\nSettled while implementing P-006 (fleet-lessons). Binds any future work that ships fleet-produced knowledge.\n\n1. THE MECHANISM IS EXPORT-THEN-COMMIT, NOT A COPY AT CUT TIME. P-006 offered two options — materialize into the builtin dir at release cut, vs teach the cut to copy it. Both, as posed, run AT CUT TIME reading `~/.papercusp-workspaces/shared/`, and that axis is the wrong one: it makes the shipped bundle a function of the BUILD BOX's home directory. Four failures, any one disqualifying: (a) two builds of the same commit stop being reproducible; (b) nothing in git records what shipped, so there is nothing to review or revert; (c) whatever the loop last adopted reaches customers unvetted; (d) on a box without that directory — a CI runner, a fresh clone — the cut ships the pack MISSING while reporting success, which is today's bug relocated rather than fixed. That is the same defect class as P-011's seed.dump hole (bundle content sourced from ambient machine state, no filter, no review); we must not open a second one while closing that.\n\nSo the curated pack is EXPORTED into the repo builtin dir and committed (`npm run gen:fleet-lessons`, `:check` for drift). The commit is then the source of truth for what ships. VERIFIED: the cut needs NO change at all — build-desktop-sidecar.sh:1183-1195 already copies every file under packages/harness into sidecar/harness, so a committed pack ships by the existing path (all 4 fleet-lessons files appear in the cut's own find enumeration), and the pack now resolves as `fleet-lessons(builtin)` v0.0.11 with 3 items.\n\n2. A PACK ITEM CARRIES NO INTERNAL REFERENCES, AND THE RELEASE AUDIT DOES NOT COVER THIS. audit-release-bundle.py scans for BUILD-BOX identity — unix user, hostname, git identity, resolved from the machine doing the build. Fleet-authored pack items carry a different residue: internal REFERENCES out of our own ledger. Measured 2026-08-03: all 3 live fleet-lessons items carried a provenance footer naming EI-8288/EI-9411/... , `harness:@singleton`, `harness:papercusp-workspace` and a 12-hex signature — and the release audit flagged none of it, because none of it is this box's identity. On a fresh install those are dangling pointers into a ledger the reader has never seen.\n\nFixed at the PRODUCER (renderCandidateLearningFile renders only the recurrence COUNT — the one part a stranger can use), with the pre-fix items re-rendered. Guarded in three places sharing ONE rule (`findPackResidue`, pack-residue.ts) so they cannot drift: the exporter refuses a pack that trips it, pack-residue.test.ts gates every committed builtin pack on every test run, and the producer no longer emits it. NOTHING IS LOST: full traceability lives in the ledger, where it belongs — knowledge_pack_candidates.pack_item_id links each shipped item back to its candidate row, which retains source_item_ids/signature/scopes/recurrence_count (verified populated on all 3 adopted rows).\n\n3. THE EXPORT IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED INTO THE GREEN GATE. `gen:fleet-lessons:check` fails when the fleet has adopted knowledge that is not committed. That is a useful curation signal but a disproportionate gate failure: it would red-pin the whole fleet over a hygiene matter unrelated to the change under test. The gate that DOES run everywhere is the residue test, which fails only on a genuine ship-blocking problem. Off-fleet the exporter exits 0 (no shared root = nothing to export), so it is safe to run anywhere.\n\n4. MEASURED WHILE HERE, for P-007 rather than this item: the curation loop is IDLE. knowledge_pack_candidates holds 3 adopted / 3 dismissed / 7 pending; the newest candidate was CREATED 2026-07-20 and the newest decision made 2026-07-19 — nothing in 14 days. P-006's premise (\"the ONE pack our automated curation loop actually feeds\") is historically true, but the pack being shippable does not mean the loop is producing. Do not read a shipped fleet-lessons as evidence the loop is healthy.\nRelated: P-006, P-009, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-018 — Promotion is not under-throttled — the cross-scope gate is UNSATISFIABLE, and a newest-N window hides exactly the signal it looks for\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03\nSettled while implementing P-007. Filed as WI-9333. Binds P-008 and any future reasoning about the learning loop's health.\n\n1. THE PLAN'S BOTH HYPOTHESES ARE WRONG. P-007 framed the 108-vs-2,809 gap as either under-promotion or correct tier-2/3 exclusion. It is NEITHER. The promotion rule (recurrence-escalation.ts:94) requires a signature recurring >=3x across >=2 DISTINCT scopes. Measured against live data: the improvement corpus is 9,486 items, of which harness:papercusp is 9,307 (98.1%) and the only other live scope, harness:oddsmith-hive, is 65 (0.7%). There is no cross-scope signal to promote. The gate is structurally unsatisfiable, not selective.\n\n2. A NEWEST-N WINDOW SYSTEMATICALLY HIDES CROSS-SCOPE RECURRENCE — the generalizable trap. runRecurrenceEscalation reads newest-N ACROSS ALL SCOPES (default 500, read-items.ts:419; listIssues silently caps at 2,000 — verified, limit=5000 and limit=20000 both return exactly 2000). Within the newest 2,000 the split is 1,998 papercusp / 2 oddsmith. So the window used to detect CROSS-scope recurrence is itself ~99.9% single-scope: the minority scope is crowded out of the very sample meant to reveal it. Whenever a detector looks for co-occurrence ACROSS a dimension, sampling newest-N ACROSS that same dimension biases against the finding — window PER stratum instead.\n\n3. RULED OUT, do not re-derive: the routine is alive (system:improvement-triage fired 16:00:03Z today, no error); the pending cap is not blocking (cap 20, only 7 pending); maxActions is not starving it (maxActions=100000 changes nothing). Scope `operator` was written ONLY between 2026-07-09 and 2026-07-20 (55 items), and all 3 adopted candidates carry scopes like ['operator','harness:@singleton']. Candidate staging stopped on 2026-07-20 — the day that second scope stopped being written. Stated as correlation WITH a mechanism, not as proof.\n\n5. CONSEQUENCE FOR P-008: do not treat pack/candidate counts as a measure of how much transferable knowledge the fleet produced. They measure how much CROSS-SCOPE co-occurrence survived a single-scope newest-N window, which today is approximately zero regardless of knowledge quality. Any promotion-rate denominator built on them is meaningless until WI-9333 lands. Raising the read limit ALONE would not have changed the outcome (cross-scope is 0 even at the 2,000 ceiling) — the fix is per-scope windowing and/or relaxing the trigger to admit strong single-scope recurrence.\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n\n### D-019 — P-020 ships the memory/entity discriminator as a GENERATED column, not the plain `row_kind` the item proposed — and the gain is correctness, with a measured but secondary speedup\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03. Nobody had measured the MEMORY side, which is the mirror image at 12.1%. A partial index there does help. Live, post-ANALYZE, 3 runs each:\n     BEFORE  NOT (payload ? 'entityType')  Seq Scan          32.05 / 34.29 / 30.98 ms, 4,440 buffers\n     AFTER   row_kind = 'memory'           Bitmap Heap Scan   8.97 / 10.06 /  9.07 ms, 1,154 buffers\n   ~3.4x faster, ~3.8x fewer buffers, on a query the fleet runs ~0.68x/s.\n   ⚠ CORRECTION: an earlier draft of migration 757 claimed 70.9ms -> 5.0ms (~14x). Those numbers came from a rolled-back transaction against a table the migration had just REWRITTEN and did NOT survive contact with live steady state. Do NOT add the mirror-image index on the entity side — WI-9137 measured it and the planner correctly refuses it.\n\n### D-020 — P-009 pack-admission gate: identity legs REUSE the shared detector; kind floor narrows to 'user'; length floor re-grounded (P-009 as written predates D-013 + D-020)\nDate: 2026-08-03\nP-009's text predates D-013 and D-008, and two of its three named checks needed CORRECTING rather than implementing literally. The verdict reports `identityLiteralsScanned` separately: \"nothing to hunt\" and \"found nothing\" must not read alike.\n\n### D-021 — P-019: the no-outage sparse cut is restored by an on-demand head snapshot the LIVE OPERATOR appends on request — and it is deliberately NOT under the dark producer flag\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03. Concurrent callers COALESCE (a bare `pending = {...}` would let a second caller overwrite the first waiter and hang it forever). Both halves matter: before the drain the snapshot covers less than the seed ships; after the read-only open it lands in a log this cut's point-in-time handle cannot see.\n\nRULING 1 — **NOT gated on `SUBSTRATE_LOG_SNAPSHOT`.** That dark flag rations the PERIODIC producer, whose cross-machine convergence is P-008-unverified. This is a one-shot, operator-requested append at cut time — precisely what the QUIESCED branch already does unconditionally (`refreshCorestoreStateForSeed` calls `produceLogSnapshot` with no flag check, verified in tree). Gating it would make the no-outage cut strictly WEAKER than the outage-taking one it replaces, for zero new exposure: both paths append the SAME op at the SAME point. D-012's own correction already established the flag explains why no OTHER snapshot is fresh, not why the cut skipped one.\n\nRULING 2 — **refuse, never degrade.** P-014's direction stands: if the snapshot cannot be obtained, the cut THROWS. A harness whose drain has just completed is idle BY DEFINITION — exactly the state a cut asks in. The request would have been armed, never serviced, and the cut would have hung out its budget. Caught by the empty-own-log case timing out at 60s; moved to the TOP of the pass (measured: 60s timeout → 188ms green). Correctness is unaffected by the move — a merge pass reads the ADMITTED logs and writes PG; it never appends to the own log.\n\nKNOWN GAP, filed not dropped: `RemoteBootedHarnessHandle` (the SUBSTRATE_SIDECAR relocation path, itself dark) throws a named error instead of implementing this — the own log and the merge gate both live in the sidecar and no `substrate:produceHeadSnapshot` RPC verb exists. The route converts it to `ok:false`, so the cut refuses with the real diagnosis rather than shipping full.\n\nEVIDENCE: 79 tests green across 4 files (on-demand-head-snapshot 6, client 12, route 9, cut-seed-cli 52); `lint:tsc` + `lint:tsc:operator` clean; falsifiability PROVEN by mutation probe (removing `await servicePendingHeadSnapshot()` → `verdict=caught guard_exit=1`, tree byte-identical after, under an exclusive `git-sync:papercusp` lock).\n\nNOT VERIFIED END-TO-END: no real `--sparse` cut has been taken against the live operator yet. That is P-014's remaining work — this restores the MECHANISM; P-014 measures `coreSparseFrom > 0` and the size drop toward the advertised ~40 MB.\n\n### D-022 — --sparse is DEFAULT-ON in all three release entry points, so P-019 un-breaks the default cut rather than restoring an optimisation — and P-014 must verify with the DEFAULTS, not a hand-passed flag\nDate: 2026-08-03\nDate: 2026-08-03. A refusal on the default path is an outage, not a guard.\n\n### D-023 — D-022 REFINED: the default cut REUSES the committed corestore, so --sparse is never reached and the degraded 1.9GB core is SELF-PERPETUATING\nDate: 2026-08-04\nDate: 2026-08-04. Drive cut-seed-cli.ts directly with --out to a scratch dir instead.\n\n### D-024 — P-017's stated invariant is a CATEGORY ERROR: the tombstone horizon is clocked from the DEL, so it never needs to exceed the retention horizon\nDate: 2026-08-04\nDate: 2026-08-04. Settled while verifying P-017 (WI-8491). Binds any future tuning of MESSAGE_GC_RETENTION_DAYS, FEDERATED_MESSAGE_GC_RETENTION_DAYS, ESCALATION_GC_RETENTION_DAYS or SNAPSHOT_TOMBSTONE_HORIZON_MS.\n\n1. WHAT P-017 ASSUMED: \"Tombstone horizon must exceed the retention horizon, or a late-arriving stale PUT can resurrect a deleted key (EI-1688).\"\n\n2. MEASURED (live pg_get_functiondef, not inferred): harness_shared.capture_substrate_outbox stamps a del with v_ts := extract(epoch from now())*1000 and v_op_hlc := hlc_now() -- a FRESH clock, commented \"a del is its own event\", explicitly NOT the OLD row's fed_ts/fed_hlc. buildSnapshotRows GCs on `r.ts < now - horizon` where r.ts IS the del's ts (log-snapshot.ts:186,198).\n\n3. CONSEQUENCE: retention is an age threshold on the ROW; the tombstone horizon is measured from the DELETE. Different origins -- they are never compared. Every tombstone gets the FULL horizon starting at its own delete, whatever the row's age. Therefore (a) today's values are safe but NOT because 14 > 7; (b) ESCALATION_GC_RETENTION_DAYS = 14 equalling the 14d tombstone horizon is NOT a violation, though it reads as one; (c) raising any retention horizon ABOVE 14d would not shorten anyone's protection.\n\n4. THE REAL INVARIANT (log-snapshot.ts:117-126): horizon >= max partition-heal delay. The load-bearing property is the FRESH DEL STAMP, not any ordering between the two constants.\n\n5. DO NOT \"tidy\" the del to carry its row's own ts. Closes D-030's open items (a) and (b), and settles the practical question D-030 §2 left implicit.\n\n**(a) WHICH pack — RESOLVED: a new builtin pack dir `papercusp`.**\nCreated at `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/knowledge-packs/papercusp/` (manifest.yaml + 7 items, v0.1.0). This EXTENDS the pack system exactly as D-004 requires — a versioned pack dir alongside `coding`/`work`/`fleet-lessons`, resolved by the same loader, with no parallel selector and no new mechanism. It is NOT `coding`, per D-030 §1.\nMeasured: `loadKnowledgePack('papercusp')` returns `source=builtin`, `items=7`, `warnings=[]`, `validatePack=[]`.\n\n**Why a separate pack is also the correct DELIVERY boundary.** `pot:create` resolves `opts.knowledgePack ?? seed.packId ?? DEFAULT_KNOWLEDGE_PACK_ID` (`agent-tools/pot/_create.ts:444`), and no blueprint declares a `knowledge.pack` key today (grep over `blueprints/*.yaml`: zero hits). So `papercusp` is reached only by explicit `knowledge_packs:install`, never auto-seeded into unrelated hives — which is precisely the failure mode EI-1539 named and D-030 §1 forbids. Per D-004 (\"Default is NOT-shared; promotion into a pack is the only path\"), opt-in install IS the finished ship, not a missing step.\n\n**The `domains` half — tagging RESTRICTS, so the items are deliberately left UNTAGGED.**\nD-030 §2 correctly ruled out a contributor GATE. Measuring what the metadata actually does settles the remaining question in the opposite direction from the original P-008 wording. `domains-filter.test.ts` asserts verbatim: *\"tagged items reach only declaring hives; untagged reach everyone\"*, and *\"undeclared hive gets untagged items only\"*.\nSo a `domains:` value is a NARROWING filter. P-008 asked to \"tag tier-2 items with a contributor `domains` value **instead of excluding them**\" — the stated intent was inclusion, but tagging would have delivered the opposite, restricting these items to hives that happen to declare a matching domain. Leaving them untagged is what actually implements P-008's intent.\nThe architecture this reflects: **the PACK is the opt-in boundary; `domains` is intra-pack routing.** Every item here is Papercusp product knowledge and anyone installing the pack wants all of it, so intra-pack narrowing would be redundant restriction. Corroborating the reading, `coding` (38 items) carries zero `domains:` tags; only 2 `fleet-lessons` items use one.\n\n**(b) The ~37 other-pot-mention rows — moot for this lift.** None of the 7 promoted items mention another pot (`grep -rlio 'oddsmith\\|sidestage'` over the pack: zero hits). The corpus-wide detector question D-030 raised is untouched and stays open; it did not gate this selection.\n\n**(c) respected.** Admission is a floor, not a promotion list: 7 items were selected FROM the 1,319 admissible rows, not promoted wholesale.\n\n**Guard — this pack cannot silently rot.** The ship gate in `pack-residue.test.ts:276` is a `readdirSync` over the committed pack dirs, so a NEW pack is covered automatically with no registration step. Verified by name in verbose output: `papercusp: no item carries internal references or tier-3 identity` ✓. Same for `pack-format.test.ts:89` (every builtin manifest parses at OKF_VERSION) and `pack-sync.test.ts`.\nSuites after the lift: pack-residue + pack-format + pack-sync + load-packs + default-pack = **63 passed / 0 failed** (was 59 before the pack existed; the +4 includes the per-pack gate case above). `coding` remains at 38 against its hard 20-40 band — untouched, so no band pressure was created.\n\n**Pipeline position, disclosed:** the pack is `committedLocal` in `f68d604a3` but not yet on `main`, so `knowledge_packs:install` on the running `:3070` release build (sha `6e898b6cf8`) cannot see it until a deploy lands. The green-checkpoint is stalled (114 consecutive reds, verdict `writer-starved`) and its ownership is HELD under WI-212675 by another session — that is a separate lane and was deliberately not touched.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"dep-graph-design-pass-2026-08-08","title":"Dependency-graph view: design pass on visible glitches + selection UX (owner-reported)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-08","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Dependency-graph view: design pass on visible glitches + selection UX (owner-reported)\nslug: dep-graph-design-pass-2026-08-08\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-08\nupdated: 2026-08-09\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE 2026-08-08 — all 9 items done, one decision (D-001). Implemented, unit-tested (19 new cases), and verified LIVE AT SCALE on the papercusp pot (122 nodes / 79 edges) in an isolated headless Tauri shell.\n\nQ1 answered, and it was NOT a bug: 18,647 vs 122 is by design (only items participating in an edge are drawn — dep-graph-model.ts:255). The defect was that the pane never said so. It now reads \"122 of 18,675 items have dependencies · 79 edges\" + \"Items with no dependency are not drawn\", and WITHHOLDS that sentence whenever a selection / health mode / filter has scoped the graph, because the number would then be false.\n\nGlitches fixed: the \"Issues only\" toggle (root cause was `.pc-advpanel__iconbtn` — a fixed 28x28 ICON box holding a TEXT label, so it fragmented into three pieces; now the house `.pc-advpanel__chip` aria-pressed toggle); the bar wraps instead of crushing its controls; edges got contrast + arrowheads (per D-001: contrast and direction, never weight — the prior owner directive \"the edges are much too big\" still stands); the canvas is sized from the NODES so nothing is drawn sliced; node cards inverted to title-prominent with a state dot and a full-title SVG <title>. Selection UX: \"Clear selection\" is an accent Button placed FIRST in the bar, and Escape clears through the same single code path (guarded so it never steals Escape from a dialog/menu/field, and never preventDefaults when nothing is selected).\n\nAlso folded in the sibling WI-36234 (one line in the same file): the filtered empty state no longer claims \"No work items match the active filters\" when plenty matched and it is the EDGE set that is empty.\n\n**Next:** Nothing outstanding. If further glitches are reported, the highest-value un-taken items are (a) edge ROUTING — ELK's splines still cross heavily at 79 edges, which is the next lever after colour/opacity per D-001 — and (b) a zoom/fit control, since 122 nodes at 210px wide is a wide scroll. Neither was asked for.\n\nEvidence: DepGraphPanel.test.tsx 19/19; the whole adv/harnesses directory 40 files / 396 tests green; lint:tsc:operator clean on the named files; design-primitives 44/44 + css-tokens green; live suite = 12 exit-coded `tauri-agent-tools check --eval` assertions with 4 negative controls each correctly exiting 1, plus Esc and Clear driven for real and a clean no-errors console check.\n\n## Background\n\n### Q1 IS ANSWERED, AND IT IS NOT A BUG — 18,647 vs 122 is BY DESIGN\n\nVerified from source, not inferred. `buildDepSubgraph` (apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/dep-graph-model.ts:255-257):\n\n> \"Otherwise, only nodes that PARTICIPATE IN AN EDGE are shown. An isolated work item has no\n> dependency story to tell, and including thousands of them is what makes the picture unreadable.\"\n\nSo the pane is a dependency SUBGRAPH, never a view of the whole corpus. The 122 nodes are the distinct endpoints of the 79 `blocks` edges that resolve to papercusp. Confirmed against Postgres: `harness_shared.work_item_deps` holds 138 rows total (all under `workspace_id='default'` — it is keyed to the COORDINATION workspace, not the tenant one), and the family-aware join yields exactly 79 papercusp edges: feature->feature 38, feature->bug 14, bug->bug 8, task->task 6, task->bug 5, change->bug 3, change->change 2, bug->task 2, feature->change 1 = 79.\n\n**The real finding underneath the question: ~18,525 of 18,647 items (99.3%) have NO dependency edge at all.** That is a fact about the corpus, not a rendering fault. But the pane never SAYS any of this — it shows \"122 nodes · 79 edges\" beside a list saying \"18647 items\" and leaves the reader to guess. The owner had to ask, which is itself the defect. P-001 fixes the legibility gap; nothing about the scoping rule should change.\n\n### GLITCHES IDENTIFIED FROM THE SCREENSHOT + SOURCE\n\n1. **The \"Issues only\" toggle is visibly broken.** DepGraphPanel.tsx renders `{healthOnly ? '@ Issues only' : 'o Issues only'}` using circle glyphs — the state indicator is INLINE TEXT inside a `.pc-advpanel__iconbtn`. With the bar squeezed there is no `white-space: nowrap`, so it wraps into three fragments: a detached circle glyph on one line, \"Issues\", then \"only\". That is exactly what the screenshot shows at the top-right of the pane. A glyph carrying state must not be a wrappable text node.\n2. **The chip bar overflows.** Five chips plus a toggle plus ColumnFilterBar plus (conditionally) Clear selection share one unwrapped flex row; \"116 outside the list's current page\" is long and unstyled relative to its neighbours.\n3. **Edges are nearly invisible.** 79 edges are drawn but read as faint dotted hairlines; at a glance the pane looks like a grid of cards rather than a graph. No visible direction (which end blocks which).\n4. **Nodes clip at the right edge** — the rightmost column is cut mid-card (\"F-..\", \"Pla\", \"Co\", \"Ex\").\n5. **Node cards are typographically weak** — aggressive title truncation, id and title competing.\n\n### CONSTRAINTS THAT ALREADY APPLY (do not relitigate)\n\n- The pane is ONE pane with modes, never a second surface (dependency-health-pane-2026-08-02 P-008 / its ## Now).\n- Four orthogonal nuqs axes compose and all four are verified working at scale: `slug`, `wif`, `sel`, `dgh` (that plan's D-009). Any new user-meaningful state goes in the URL too, per the repo's nuqs rule — NOT useState.\n- `lint:design-primitives` blocks title-only tooltips on buttons; the toggle's explanation lives in `aria-label` deliberately. Keep it.\n- Read /internal/docs/design and check `design-phase:search_registry` for an existing toggle/button primitive BEFORE inventing one (repo rule: design docs are required reading before design work).\n- Verification: element/text/count assertions from scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh are sound; GEOMETRY from it is NOT (it inherits a saved dock layout — EI-18694485377422886). The dep-graph pane takes ~11s to mount cold; wait for `.pc-depgraph` to exist then poll until the node count stabilises, or a fixed sleep produces a green that measured nothing.\n- Known-open sibling: WI-36234 (filtered empty state claims \"No work items match the active filters\" while the grid says \"432 of 18601 match\" — the empty thing is the EDGE set). Fix it here if it is one line in the same file; otherwise leave it to its own item.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Answer the owner's question IN the UI\n\n- **P-001** `done` Make the corpus relationship legible in the pane, so nobody has to ask again why 18,647 items yield 122 nodes. The pane currently shows '122 nodes · 79 edges' next to a list showing '18647 items' and never states that a node only appears if it PARTICIPATES IN AN EDGE. Add that to the chip row / empty state in one short line — e.g. '122 of 18,647 items have dependencies' with the aria/tooltip explanation that isolated items are not drawn. Do NOT change the scoping rule (dep-graph-model.ts:255 is correct and deliberate); this is purely making an existing, correct behaviour self-explaining. Acceptance: a reader can answer 'why so few nodes?' without leaving the pane. importance: high — note: ← WI-36619 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — The glitch pass\n\n- **P-002** `done` Fix the broken 'Issues only' toggle. DepGraphPanel.tsx renders the state as inline circle-glyph TEXT inside .pc-advpanel__iconbtn, which wraps into three fragments (detached glyph / 'Issues' / 'only') when the bar is squeezed — visible in the owner's screenshot. Replace the text glyph with a real toggle affordance driven by aria-pressed styling (or a registry primitive if design-phase:search_registry has one), and give the control white-space:nowrap so it can never fragment. KEEP the existing aria-label explanations verbatim — lint:design-primitives blocks title-only tooltips and that label is the control's only explanation of what 'Issues only' means. importance: high — note: ← WI-36620 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Make the chip/control bar survive narrow widths without fragmenting. It packs up to five status chips + the Issues-only toggle + ColumnFilterBar + a conditional 'Clear selection' into one unwrapped flex row. Decide deliberately between wrapping to a second line and horizontal scroll (wrapping is likely right: these are status chips, not a toolbar), apply nowrap WITHIN each chip so individual chips stay atomic, and keep the D-003 guarantee that the 'Clear' affordance can never be pushed off screen by a filter that matched nothing. importance: high — note: ← WI-36621 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Make the edges actually read as a graph. 79 edges render as faint near-invisible hairlines, so the pane looks like a grid of cards; the owner's 'a lot of glitches' is substantially this. Strengthen the edge stroke against the panel background, and add DIRECTION (arrowheads or an equivalent) so blocker-vs-blocked is readable — a dependency graph whose edges have no visible direction is not conveying the one thing it exists to convey. Keep the existing semantic edge classes (dangling / satisfied) visually distinct from healthy, since integrity mode depends on that distinction. importance: high — note: ← WI-36622 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Stop clipping nodes at the pane's right edge. The screenshot shows the rightmost column cut mid-card ('F-..', 'Pla', 'Co', 'Ex'). Ensure the SVG viewBox / scroll container is sized to the ELK layout's full extent so a node is either fully visible or scrolled to, never sliced. Check the pane's own overflow too — measured scrollWidth 317 vs clientWidth 122 in one run, i.e. content genuinely exceeds the box. — note: ← WI-36623 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Typography/immediate-legibility pass on the node card: id vs title hierarchy, truncation behaviour (titles currently truncate very aggressively), and state/kind indication on the node itself. Use existing design tokens — no new hardcoded colours (npm run lint:design-primitives / the css-tokens test guard this). — note: ← WI-36624 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Selection UX (owner ask 3)\n\n- **P-007** `done` Make 'Clear selection' properly visible when a node is selected. It currently renders as a .pc-advpanel__iconbtn identical to every other control and sits at the END of a crowded bar, so it reads as chrome rather than as the exit from a filtered state. Give it real prominence (accent/primary treatment) and place it where the eye lands when something IS selected. Owner-asked verbatim: 'when you have a ndoe selected the clear selection button should be more visible'. importance: high — note: ← WI-36625 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Esc deselects. Owner-asked verbatim: 'pressing esc should also automatically deselect'. Wire a keydown handler that clears ?sel (the same setSelectedId('') the button calls, so both paths share one code path). Scope it so it does not steal Esc from a dialog/menu/filter popover that is open above the pane, do not preventDefault when nothing is selected, and keep it keyboard-accessible (the a11y node list already exposes nodes as buttons — Esc must work from there too). Add a test asserting Esc clears the nuqs param, plus one asserting it does NOT fire when nothing is selected. importance: high — note: ← WI-36626 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Verify\n\n- **P-009** `done` Verify the whole pass live at SCALE on papercusp (122 nodes / 79 edges), not on a small pot — dependency-health-pane-2026-08-02 D-009 records why a 7-node pot cannot exercise this pane. Drive scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh with exit-coded `tauri-agent-tools check --json --eval` assertions, each paired with a negative control that must exit 1. MUST wait for .pc-depgraph to EXIST (~11s cold mount) then poll until the node count stabilises — a fixed sleep silently satisfies any 'fewer than N' assertion. Assert: the toggle renders on ONE line, Esc clears sel, Clear-selection is present when sel is set, edges carry direction markers, and no console errors. Do NOT make geometry claims from this harness (EI-18694485377422886). importance: high — note: ← WI-36627 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Edge legibility is bought with CONTRAST and DIRECTION, never with WEIGHT — D-003 req 1 stands\nDate: 2026-08-08\nTwo owner reports point in apparently opposite directions and BOTH are binding, so any future edge change has to satisfy both rather than picking one.\n\n- dependency-health-pane-2026-08-02 D-003 req 1 [owner, verbatim]: \"the edges are much too big\". That complaint was about WEIGHT.\n- This plan's ask [owner 2026-08-08]: the pane shows \"a lot of glitches\" and reads as a grid of cards. That complaint is that 79 edges drawn at stroke-opacity 0.45 with no direction are effectively invisible.\n\nRULING — they are not in conflict, because they are different knobs. Hold one, spend the other:\n\n1. stroke-width STAYS 1 (hairline). Not raised now, and must not be raised later to \"make edges clearer\" — that is precisely the change the owner already rejected.\n2. stroke-opacity comes up off the floor: base 0.45 -> 0.7; satisfied 0.2 -> 0.34, raised IN STEP so the ratio that encodes \"inert\" survives. At 0.2 that semantic class was not legible at all, i.e. decorative.\n3. The legibility budget is spent on DIRECTION — a per-class arrowhead marker. A dependency graph whose edges cannot say which end blocks which is not conveying the one thing it exists to convey, and an arrowhead adds no visual weight along the edge's length.\n\nWhy three explicit markers rather than one inheriting the stroke: SVG2 `context-stroke` has uneven engine support (WebKitGTK in the desktop shell), and an arrowhead that silently falls back to black on a dark panel is worse than none. Marker ids are pane-scoped via useId() so two panes in one dock cannot adopt each other's colour.\n\nIf a later pass still finds edges weak, the next levers are colour/opacity or ELK edge routing — NOT stroke-width.\nRelated: P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"dep-graph-design-pass-2-2026-08-08","title":"Dependency graph: second design pass (visual vocabulary, focus, navigation) + a first-class plan filter","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-08","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Dependency graph: second design pass (visual vocabulary, focus, navigation) + a first-class plan filter\nslug: dep-graph-design-pass-2-2026-08-08\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-08\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nNEW 2026-08-08, second owner ask on this pane, immediately after `dep-graph-design-pass-2026-08-08` shipped. AUTO mode is ON and owner-directed → implement-then-disclose.\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-08 interactive, verbatim] \"1. do another general design imrpovement pass on the dependnacy graph view.  2. add a plan filter\"\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: P-001 FIRST — it is fact-finding, and the whole plan-filter design depends on its answer. Do not build a second filter before establishing why the existing one is not reaching the owner.\n\nPredecessor: `dep-graph-design-pass-2026-08-08` (COMPLETE 9/9, D-001). **Its D-001 binds this plan too:** edge legibility is bought with CONTRAST and DIRECTION, never with WEIGHT. Do not thicken strokes.)\n\n## Background\n\n### A PLAN FILTER ALREADY EXISTS — so the ask is about REACH, not absence\n\nRead from source before designing anything (`work-item-columns.tsx:201-215`): there IS a\n`plan` column with `filter: { type: 'enum', accessor: (r) => r.planSlug }`, deliberately enum\n\"so the filter offers a selectable checklist of the actual plans (with live counts + an\nin-list search for long sets), not a blank search box\". `DepGraphPanel` renders\n`ColumnFilterBar` over the SAME `wif` param and the SAME columns as the list pane.\n\nSo the owner is not asking for a filter that does not exist. Two candidate reasons it is not\nreaching them, and P-001 must settle which (both may hold):\n\n1. **DISCOVERABILITY.** `DepGraphPanel` renders `ColumnFilterBar` with its DEFAULT\n   `layout='compact'` — a single `+Add filter…` Select. Nothing on the pane says \"Plan\" is a\n   filterable axis; you must open a dropdown and know to look. `layout='facets'` already\n   exists in that same component and renders every filterable column as a visible labelled\n   chip group with live counts. One prop, and possibly the whole answer.\n2. **CORRECTNESS AT SCALE (suspected — MUST be measured, do not assert it).** `useColumnFilters`\n   filters `items`, which is the list's 500-row `updated_ts DESC` WINDOW. The graph's nodes are\n   NOT that set: out-of-window endpoints are HYDRATED from the edge rows (WI-36045), carry\n   `blockedPlanSlug`/`blockerPlanSlug`, and never pass through `cf`. So filtering to a plan\n   whose items fall outside the window plausibly yields an empty or badly-truncated graph —\n   the SAME defect class as WI-36045 with a different trigger. If real, a prominent plan chip\n   that quietly shows nothing is WORSE than the buried filter it replaced.\n\nAlso unstated today: with a filter active the model keeps an edge when EITHER endpoint matches\n(`filterActive` semantics), so a plan filter shows the plan's items PLUS their non-plan\nblockers. That is probably the RIGHT semantic for a dependency view — \"this plan and what\ngates it\" — but it is left for the reader to infer, which is exactly what the previous plan's\nP-001 existed to stop.\n\n### THE VISUAL VOCABULARY IS NOW UNEXPLAINED — the honest cost of the last pass\n\nThe pane encodes SIX things visually and explains NONE of them on screen:\n\n| mark | meaning |\n|---|---|\n| solid edge + arrowhead | a live blocker → blocked dependency |\n| faint dashed edge | blocker already terminal (gates nothing) |\n| red dashed edge | dangling — the blocker ref resolves to no row (INV-13) |\n| red dashed node | a dangling placeholder, not a real work item |\n| blue left bar on a node | the item came from a plan (`source_plan_slug`) |\n| coloured dot on a node | its own state bucket (done / active / blocked / open) |\n\nThe previous pass ADDED two of those (arrowheads, state dots) and made a third legible again\n(satisfied edges). Adding encodings without adding a key is a legibility regression dressed as\nan improvement, and is a strong candidate for \"still looks glitchy\".\n\n### WHAT MAKES A 122-NODE GRAPH HARD TO USE (observed live, 2026-08-08)\n\n- **No focus.** 79 edges cross heavily. Hover/selection does not emphasise a node's OWN edges\n  or dim the rest, so tracing one item's lineage by eye is near-impossible at this size. This\n  is the biggest remaining \"reads as a grid of cards, not a graph\" contributor.\n- **Selection does not scroll into view.** Clicking a row in the list pane sets `?sel` and the\n  graph re-scopes — but if the node lands off-screen the viewport looks unchanged, so the user\n  concludes nothing happened.\n- **No zoom / fit.** 122 nodes at NODE_W 210 + 72px inter-layer spacing is a very wide canvas\n  with no overview and no way out but scrolling.\n- **Depth is invisible** even though the model documents depth as \"the signal this pane exists\n  to surface\" (a seven-deep chain was the subsystem's worst escape, EI-9108).\n\n### CONSTRAINTS THAT ALREADY APPLY (do not relitigate)\n\n- Predecessor D-001: contrast + direction, never weight.\n- One pane with MODES, never a second surface (dependency-health-pane-2026-08-02 P-008).\n- User-meaningful state goes in nuqs, not useState (`ui:get_state` reads the URL).\n- No new hardcoded colours; `lint:design-primitives` + the css-tokens test guard this.\n- Verification: element/text/COUNT assertions from `scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh` are\n  sound; GEOMETRY from it is NOT (EI-18694485377422886). It also boots on whatever slug was\n  last persisted — often a tiny repro pot — so PIN `slug=papercusp` and assert a node FLOOR,\n  or the run measures nothing (EI-19930573774744721, filed during the last pass).\n\n## Phase 1 — Establish the truth about the plan filter (blocks the rest)\n- **P-001** `done` MEASURE, at scale on papercusp, what the EXISTING plan filter actually does in the graph pane — before designing any replacement. Three questions, each answered from a live isolated shell pinned to slug=papercusp, not from reading source: (a) does setting the `wif` plan filter narrow the graph at all? (b) for a plan whose items are OUTSIDE the list's 500-row updated_ts window, does it return an empty/truncated graph — i.e. is the WI-36045 defect class alive again through a different trigger? (c) how many DISTINCT plans do the 122 graph nodes span, since that decides whether an inline facet chip-group is even viable or whether it must stay a searchable picker. Record the numbers on this item; every later item's design depends on them. Drive the filter by URL param (wif codec: key:val, clauses ~, enum list comma-separated) rather than through Radix Select, which ignores synthetic Xvfb input. importance: high — note: ← WI-36782 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — The plan filter, made real\n- **P-002** `todo` Make Plan a VISIBLE, first-class axis on the graph's bar rather than an option buried in a `+Add filter…` dropdown. Strongly prefer switching ColumnFilterBar to the `layout='facets'` it ALREADY supports (labelled chip groups with live counts, picker-chip fallback above inlineMax) over inventing a bespoke plan control — reuse-first, and it fixes discoverability for every other axis at the same time. If P-001(c) shows the plan cardinality is far past inlineMax, keep Plan as a picker-chip but ensure the chip is always VISIBLE and labelled 'Plan' with its active value, never hidden behind a generic Add-filter affordance. importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` If and only if P-001(b) confirms it: fix plan filtering so it applies to the GRAPH's node set (including edge-hydrated nodes, which carry blockedPlanSlug/blockerPlanSlug) rather than only to the list's 500-row window. Push the predicate into buildDepSubgraph — where the hydrated nodes exist — instead of leaving it upstream in useColumnFilters where they are structurally invisible. Add a model test at the WI-36045 shape: a plan whose items are entirely out-of-window must still yield its subgraph. Do NOT widen the list's window to paper over it. importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` State the filter's SEMANTIC in the pane, in one short line, the way P-001 of the predecessor plan did for the corpus rule: with a filter active an edge survives if EITHER endpoint matches, so a plan filter shows the plan's items PLUS the non-plan items that gate them. That is the right behaviour for a dependency view and it must not be left for the reader to infer from a node count that looks too big.\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — The design pass\n- **P-005** `todo` Add a LEGEND for the six visual encodings the pane now uses (live edge + arrow, satisfied edge, dangling edge, dangling node, plan marker, state dot). The previous pass added two of these and explained none, which makes the picture less readable, not more, however correct each mark is. Keep it compact and non-modal — a collapsible strip or a hover key, in the pane, not a dialog — and drive any open/closed state through nuqs like every other axis here. Reuse existing tokens; the legend must derive its colours from the SAME CSS custom properties the marks use so it can never drift from what is drawn. importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` FOCUS: on hover and on selection, emphasise a node's own edges and neighbours and de-emphasise everything else. At 79 crossing edges this is the single biggest remaining reason the pane reads as a grid of cards rather than a graph — tracing one item's lineage by eye is currently near-impossible. Selection already scopes to the connected component, so this is about the WITHIN-component reading. Do it in CSS off a class on the SVG root (no per-frame React state churn on hover), respect the D-001 ruling (change opacity/colour, never stroke width), and make sure the dangling/satisfied semantic classes stay distinguishable while dimmed. importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Scroll the selected node INTO VIEW when ?sel changes from outside the pane. Clicking a row in the list pane re-scopes the graph, but if the node lands off-screen the viewport looks unchanged and the user concludes nothing happened — the interlock works and appears not to. Scroll the canvas so the selected node is visible (centred is fine), only when the selection actually changed, and never fight a scroll the user is currently performing. importance: high\n- **P-008** `todo` Give the canvas a zoom / fit-to-width control. 122 nodes at NODE_W 210 plus 72px inter-layer spacing is a very wide canvas whose only navigation is scrolling, with no way to see the shape of the whole graph. A simple SVG viewBox scale with a fit button and a reset is enough; put the zoom level in nuqs so the view is linkable and agent-drivable, and keep the node text legible (or explicitly accept that it degrades below some scale and say so).\n- **P-009** `todo` Make DEPTH visible. The model documents depth as 'the signal this pane exists to surface' — a seven-deep blockedBy chain served as claimable was the subsystem's worst escape (EI-9108) — yet nothing on screen states a node's depth or the graph's maximum. Surface it cheaply: the deepest chain as a chip, and/or depth on the node card. Do not add a seventh unexplained encoding — if it gets a visual mark, it goes in the legend from the item above.\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Verify\n- **P-010** `todo` Verify the whole pass LIVE AT SCALE on papercusp (~122 nodes / 79 edges), pinning slug=papercusp explicitly — the harness boots on whatever slug was last persisted, often an empty repro pot where every structural assertion passes on a 0-node graph (EI-19930573774744721). Exit-coded `tauri-agent-tools check --json --eval` only, each claim paired with a negative control that must exit 1, assert the eval-result count matches the flag count, and poll until the node count STABILISES rather than sleeping. Drive the plan filter through the URL and assert the graph actually changes. Make NO geometry claims (EI-18694485377422886) — assert computed styles and counts, not bounding rects. Plus the unit tier: extend DepGraphPanel.test.tsx and dep-graph-model.test.ts. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The existing plan filter is not merely buried — it cannot reach 9 of the graph's 12 plans, and silently empties 8 of them. The fix is the CORPUS, not the layout.\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-001 is ANSWERED, by measurement against the live papercusp corpus (SQL reproducing the resolver's own join + the list window's own `ORDER BY updated_ts DESC LIMIT 500`), cross-checked by reading each writer. Both suspected causes hold, and a THIRD — unanticipated, and the largest — was found.\n\n**Graph corpus as measured 2026-08-09: 84 edges, 129 nodes, 0 dangling.** (The plan's ## Background says 122/79 from 2026-08-08; the corpus moved, the shape did not.) Nodes span **12 distinct plans** + 59 nodes with no plan.\n\n#### Defect 1 — NOT OFFERED (new; the largest, and it alone explains the owner's ask)\n\n`useColumnFilters` derives an enum column's option set with `deriveEnumOptions(rows, col)` where `rows` is the RAW `items` array — the list's 500-row window. Measured: that window contains **5** distinct plan slugs. The graph contains **12**. So **9 of the 12 plans in the graph are not selectable at all** — they are absent from the dropdown, not hidden inside it.\n\nThis is why \"add a plan filter\" is a reasonable ask against a codebase that already has one: for three quarters of the plans on screen, the existing filter genuinely cannot filter to them.\n\n#### Defect 2 — NOT CORRECT (the suspected WI-36045 class, CONFIRMED, not asserted)\n\n`buildDepSubgraph` keeps an edge under an active filter iff either endpoint is in `byId`, and `byId` is built from `cf.rows` — the FILTERED 500-row window. Edge-hydrated endpoints (the ones WI-36045 added, carrying `blockedPlanSlug`/`blockerPlanSlug`) never enter it. Per-plan, true edges vs. edges the model will actually render:\n\n| plan | true | rendered |\n|---|---|---|\n| memory-corpus-hygiene-and-release-distribution-2026-08-03 | 12 | 3 |\n| agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02 | 8 | **0** |\n| p2p-git-live-activation-2026-07-09 | 6 | **0** |\n| learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08 | 5 | 5 |\n| gym-real-fitness-signal-2026-07-27 | 5 | **0** |\n| p2p-public-release-remaining-lanes-2026-07-16 | 5 | **0** |\n| coordination-spec-adoption-2026-08-03 | 4 | 1 |\n| bash-substitution-reachable-ceiling-2026-08-01 | 3 | **0** |\n| deterministic-context-carry-2026-07-14 | 2 | **0** |\n| papercup-physical-rename-phase5-2026-06-20 | 2 | **0** |\n| pot-seat-pools-prose-ux-2026-07-18 | 1 | **0** |\n| mobile-public-release-readiness-completion-2026-07-15 | 1 | **0** |\n\n**8 of 12 plans render an EMPTY graph. 54 true plan-edges; 9 render. 83% of the plan-filtered dependency data is wrong.** Exactly ONE plan (`learning-loop-…-2026-08-08`, the most recently touched, hence wholly inside the window) is correct — which is precisely the shape that makes a defect survive casual testing: check the plan you just worked on and it works.\n\n#### Defect 3 — NOT DISCOVERABLE (as suspected)\n\n`DepGraphPanel` renders `ColumnFilterBar` at its default `layout='compact'` — one `+Add filter…` Select. Nothing names Plan as an axis.\n\n#### THE RULING\n\n**Do not build a second plan filter, and do not fix this by switching the layout prop.** Layout was suspected to be \"possibly the whole answer\"; the measurement says it is the SMALLEST of three, and shipping it alone would be actively harmful — a prominent, discoverable Plan chip that empties the graph for 8 of 12 plans is strictly worse than the buried filter it replaces, because it converts an unreachable feature into a confidently wrong one.\n\nThe root cause is one thing wearing three faces: **the graph pane filters, and derives its filter options, from the LIST's corpus, while drawing from its OWN — which is strictly larger.** So fix the corpus, once:\n\n> **The graph pane must feed `useColumnFilters` the GRAPH's node corpus — `items` ∪ the endpoint rows carried on `edgeRows` — not `items` alone.** Option derivation and row filtering then both operate on what is actually drawn. This keeps ONE shared `wif` param and one filter surface (no second control, no forked component), changes no resolver and costs no fetch: the endpoint fields are already in the loaded edge payload.\n\nCONSEQUENCE to state in the pane, not to hide: hydrated rows carry only `title`/`kind`/`state`/`planSlug`, so a filter on a column they lack (assignee, severity, priority, rank) still excludes them. That is today's behaviour unchanged — no regression — but it is now the ONLY remaining scope gap and must be named on screen rather than left for a reader to infer.\n\n#### The transferable lesson\n\nWI-36045 was fixed by making the EDGE payload self-sufficient. It made the graph's node corpus larger than the list's window — and every OTHER consumer of \"the list's rows\" silently inherited the old, narrower corpus. Fixing a scope mismatch in one direction created the same mismatch one layer up, in a component (`useColumnFilters`) that was never touched and looked entirely uninvolved. **When a fix widens a corpus, re-derive every downstream reader of the narrower one.**\n\n### D-002 — P-001 live end-to-end evidence: the defect reproduces in the running pane, and the fix is an explicit `filteredIds` seam — not a wider `items`\nDate: 2026-08-09\nD-001's SQL prediction was confirmed **end-to-end in a live isolated shell** (display :90, pid 2943831, slug PINNED to papercusp per EI-19930573774744721), driving the filter through the `wif` URL param (codec confirmed from `grid-core/column-filter.ts`: `CLAUSE_SEP '~'`, `KV_SEP ':'`, `LIST_SEP ','`).\n\n**Baseline, unfiltered:** the pane reports `129 of 18,721 items have dependencies · 84 edges`, renders 129 `.pc-depgraph__node`, and chips `115 outside the list's current page`. The node/edge counts match my independent SQL EXACTLY (129/84) — two instruments, one answer, so the corpus model is right. Note `115 of 129` — only **14** graph nodes are in the list's window at all. That ratio is the defect's whole cause in one number.\n\n**The failing case, live:** `wif=plan:agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02` →\n\n> `0 nodes · 0 edges` · `84 edges hidden by filters` · empty-state: **\"No work items match the active filters.\"**\n\nThat plan has 11 nodes and 8 edges in the graph. Every one of the 84 edges was dropped. The pane's sentence is not merely unhelpful, it is the WRONG diagnosis — the items match fine; they are outside the window the filter was applied to — and it is the diagnosis that sends the reader to widen a filter that was never too narrow.\n\n**The discriminating control** (this is what makes the above a finding rather than \"filters are broken\"):\n\n| plan filter | true edges | rendered live |\n|---|---|---|\n| learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08 | 5 | **5 — correct** (7 nodes) |\n| memory-corpus-hygiene-and-release-distribution-2026-08-03 | 12 | 3 |\n| gym-real-fitness-signal-2026-07-27 | 5 | 1 |\n| agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02 | 8 | **0** |\n\nThe filter demonstrably WORKS — on the one plan recent enough to sit wholly inside the window. Three of the four predictions were exact; `gym` predicted 0 and rendered 1, which is live-corpus drift between the two measurements (an item was touched into the window), not a model error. Drift of that kind is itself evidence for the diagnosis: **which edges this pane shows depends on how recently someone touched an unrelated row.**\n\n#### REVISION TO D-001's PRESCRIBED FIX — read this before implementing\n\nD-001 said to feed `useColumnFilters` the graph's corpus. That is right for OPTION DERIVATION and for deciding which rows survive, but feeding the widened corpus onward to `buildDepSubgraph` as `items` would silently destroy two working signals: the model's endpoint HYDRATION path becomes unreachable, `hydratedNodeCount` collapses to 0, and the honest `115 outside the list's current page` chip — the one that tells a reader why a node is not in the list beside it — disappears. Fixing the filter by deleting the disclosure that made the last bug findable would repeat WI-36045's original sin in a new place.\n\nSo the seam is EXPLICIT, mirroring how `filterActive` is already handled — the model cannot infer this, so the caller states it:\n\n> **`buildDepSubgraph` gains an optional `filteredIds?: ReadonlySet<string>`.** When a filter is active, the edge-drop rule tests membership in `filteredIds` rather than in `byId`. The panel runs `useColumnFilters` over `items ∪ edge-carried endpoint rows` (options + filtering now see every drawn node), passes `filteredIds = new Set(cf.rows.map(r => r.id))`, and still passes the REAL list rows as `items` — so hydration, `hydratedNodeCount` and the outside-the-page chip all keep working unchanged.\n\nThis costs no fetch (the endpoint fields are already in the loaded edge payload), keeps ONE shared `wif` param and one filter surface, changes no resolver, and leaves the model pure and unit-testable.\n\n**Residual scope gap, to be STATED in the pane rather than hidden:** edge-carried rows have only `title`/`kind`/`state`/`planSlug`, so a filter on a column they lack (assignee, severity, priority, rank) still excludes them. That is today's behaviour unchanged — not a regression — but after this fix it is the ONLY remaining place where the filter's corpus is narrower than the graph's, and it must be named on screen.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/dep-graph-design-pass-2-2026-08-08 (\"Dependency graph: second design pass (visual vocabulary, focus, navigation) + a first-clas\"): no plan update since 2026-08-25 (46 days idle), 1/10 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"guidance-overlap-contradiction-scan-2026-08-08","title":"Workstream C — overlap + contradiction scan over the guidance corpus","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-08","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Workstream C — overlap + contradiction scan over the guidance corpus\nslug: guidance-overlap-contradiction-scan-2026-08-08\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-08\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nP-001, P-002, **P-003 DONE** — Phase 1 (corpus + core) complete; P-004 unblocked.\n\nThe prior Now's ⚠ OPEN item is CLOSED and its explanation was WRONG (D-009): the cross-source instability (310 vs 264) was NOT ANN top-K recall variance — that hypothesis is retracted. K∈{10,30,60}×3 gave **spread 0 on every leg at every K**. Real cause: a MOVING CORPUS (all 3,536 guidance sections re-written within 2h, 30 inside the scan window). Ruling `neighbourLimit = 30`, applied as the host default (K=60 identical for ~30k more work; K=10 loses 9 pairs, 5 cross-source).\n\n**D-010 — read before touching this module.** P-003's own census was lying, in D-001's exact shape one level up: `loadUnitsReal` filtered `WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL`, so numerator AND denominator came from the same filtered population — structurally 1.0 however much was missing. Caught live with 30 of 3,536 sections un-vectorised: a scan then would have skipped the 30 FRESHEST sections while printing `10,056 of 10,056`. Fixed — the null-test is a selected COLUMN not a predicate; the lib gained `{unitsUnavailable}` → `census.unitsKnown/coverage`; `minCoverage` defaults to a STRICT 1.0 (forgetting it fails safe), relaxed to 0.99 here with a reason.\n\nMEASURED (gemma, `inconclusive: null`): 10,056/10,056 comparable across 1,712 pages; 99,069 hits → 79,150 pairs → 3,027 above the 0.88 base → **861 kept**; pairsDropped 0, dimensionMismatches 0. 61/61 tests green, both typechecks exit 0, 0 control bytes.\n\n⚠ That `coverage: 1` is a TRUE 1 (verified against PG; backfill completed between measurements) but does NOT prove the shortfall path — that rests on unit tests + a control, plus the SQL expression's falsifiability against the real table (166 false / 34 true).\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Start P-004 (contradiction leg): per D-004 compute each pair's KIND deterministically and bucket the report BY KIND, never by similarity — the live run's similarity-sorted top is ~20 near-identical `fleet-*#chaining` sibling pairs that would bury real findings like the cosine-1.0000 exact duplicate between `prompts/operator.persona.engineer-mode#audience-mode-engineer` and `prompts/papercup.persona.engineer-mode#audience-mode-engineer`; only high-similarity pairs reach the LLM, asked the one narrow question (do these instruct OPPOSITE actions in the same situation?), via the inference gateway, flag-gated, and per D-001 never auto-filing from a report whose `inconclusive` is non-null.)\n\n## Background\n\nskill-git's two verbs applied to prose guidance: find semantically overlapping units across different source files, and rate whether two of them instruct OPPOSITE actions.
