Two legs — a DETERMINISTIC overlap leg (pairwise cosine above a threshold, pure counting, no LLM, the shape `code-recipes-candidates.ts` already uses for recipe merge clusters) and a JUDGED contradiction leg (only high-similarity pairs reach an LLM, asked one narrow question).\n\nResolution is autonomous in all three cases and must stay that way: learned-contradicts-authored auto-retires the learned entry (authored wins by construction), learned-vs-learned evicts the lower-utility one, authored-vs-authored auto-files a work item another agent claims. Escalating to a work item is autonomous; escalating to a UI is not.\n\nREUSE, so \"no schema change\" stays true: `doc-embed-sync.ts` is adapter-keyed — `syncDocSourceSections(sql, adapter)` writes `doc_sections` with `source_key = adapter.name` (its own L288 comment: \"the read leg filters source_key by adapter.name, so these MUST match\"). The guidance corpus therefore becomes a SECOND ADAPTER, and the existing embed-backfill sweep vectorises it. No new table, no migration, no parallel embedding pipeline.\n\nNEAR-NEIGHBOUR, do not duplicate: `instruction-lint.ts` already finds contradictions, but only between `<!-- papercusp-rule:k=v -->` MARKERS in one RENDERED brief, deliberately \"without guessing policy from arbitrary prose\". C is the semantic complement over the AUTHORED corpus — different unit, different method.\n\n## Phase 1 — Corpus and core\n\n- **P-001** `done` Guidance-corpus adapter: section CLAUDE.md x3, `*.tools.md` x82, personas x28 + 74 blueprint role prompts, and the 680 per-tool `guidance:` blocks into DocSection units, synced under `source_key: papercusp-guidance` through the existing `syncDocSourceSections` seam so embed-backfill vectorises them. No migration, no second store. importance: high — note: papercuspGuidanceAdapter shipped + wired; 148 canonical file pages + >100 tool-guidance pages, 0 duplicates, 12 tests green\n- **P-002** `done` Overlap-clustering core in `libs/generic/` behind a `configure*()` seam — domain-free pairwise cosine above a threshold plus cluster merge, pure counting, no LLM, no papercusp imports. Generic-first is explicit in C's spec. importance: high — note: ← WI-36278 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Calibrate the overlap threshold against the REAL 6513+ section corpus, never fixtures — the leader's measured warning is that fixtures agree with you and the corpus does not. The sweep must distinguish \"no overlap found\" from \"found nothing because it looked wrong\" (report a nonzero denominator, the OKF-lint discipline). blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: calibrated on the real corpus: thresholds 0.92/0.88 (D-003), neighbourLimit 30 (D-009), coverage denominator fixed (D-010); 61/61 green\n\n## Phase 2 — Judgement and resolution\n\n- **P-004** `done` Contradiction leg: only high-similarity pairs reach the LLM, asked the one narrow question — do these two passages instruct opposite actions in the same situation? Routed through the inference gateway, flag-gated, cheap by construction. blocked-by: P-003 importance: normal — note: contradiction leg + D-004 kind attribution shipped (D-011); 75/75 green, tsc clean; flag GUIDANCE_CONTRADICTION_SCAN default-ON. CAVEAT: never run live — no judge credential resolves in this operator, which the leg correctly reports as inconclusive\n- **P-005** `done` Autonomous resolution: three-way seam. authored-vs-authored auto-files a DEDUPED work item another agent claims; the two learned legs ship inert until workstream B's learned layer exists, and C must not block on B. No review step, no advisory report. blocked-by: P-004 importance: normal — note: ← WI-41561 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `todo` Scheduled sweep + flag defaulting ON + a recurrence guard that fails if the scan silently degrades to zero findings. blocked-by: P-005 importance: normal\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — D-001 — the generic core takes a NEIGHBOUR PROVIDER, not a similarity matrix; and an empty result is never evidence on its own\nDate: 2026-08-08\nTwo rulings from building P-002 (libs/generic/overlap-clusters, 26/26 green, tsc clean). Both bind every later item in this plan.\n\n1. NEIGHBOUR PROVIDER, NOT ALL-PAIRS. C's spec says 'pairwise cosine above a threshold'. Read literally that is all-pairs: doc_sections holds 6,513 sections at 384 dims, so ~21M pairs and ~8e9 multiply-adds — not runnable in a scheduled sweep. But migration 552 already built an HNSW cosine index over that table. So the generic core does NOT accept a matrix or compute one: configureOverlapScan({ threshold, neighbours }) injects a NeighbourProvider at the configure*() seam, and the lib owns only the domain-free parts (thresholding, the cross-source rule, symmetric pair de-dup, union-find clustering, the census). The host supplies pgvector ANN; bruteForceNeighbours() is the small-corpus/test path and is the only path that reads `vector`. This is what keeps the lib genuinely domain-free AND the sweep tractable — P-006 must wire the ANN provider, not brute force.\n\n2. AN EMPTY RESULT IS NOT EVIDENCE. This scan fails in exactly one direction: threshold too high, vectors never populated, every unit in one group, or a provider that silently returns nothing — each yields ZERO pairs, which is precisely what a genuinely clean corpus yields. The failure is indistinguishable from success and it is REASSURING, which is worse than an error. Therefore the module never returns a bare list, and every consumer inherits the contract:\n  - every report carries a `census` (unitsComparable, groupsSeen, candidateHitsSeen, candidatePairs, pairsCrossGroup, pairsAboveThreshold, pairsDropped, dimensionMismatches);\n  - `inconclusive: string | null` names why a run could not have produced a finding;\n  - **a caller may treat `pairs: []` as 'no overlap' ONLY when `inconclusive === null`**;\n  - describeOverlapReport() renders that rule as a sentence so a result cannot be quoted without its denominator;\n  - cosineSimilarity returns NULL (not 0) on a dimension mismatch — 0 would launder a half-finished embedding backfill into a clean-looking scan;\n  - configureOverlapScan THROWS on a missing threshold: there is no defensible default, and a silently-defaulted threshold is the likeliest cause of a confidently empty report.\n\nWhy this is a decision and not a preference: it is the direct application of the leader's measured warning (his staleness path failed OPEN under a fake sql, so a wrong column name would have returned an empty map indistinguishable from 'nothing is stale', permanently and silently) and of the OKF lint's denominator discipline from the prior plan. P-003 calibrates the threshold against the REAL corpus for the same reason — fixtures agree with you; the corpus does not. P-005 must NOT auto-file work items from a report whose `inconclusive` is non-null, and P-006's recurrence guard should fail on a scan that silently degrades to an inconclusive zero rather than reporting green.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-006\n\n### D-002 — Corpus membership is by explicit canonical ROOTS + git-trackedness — never a filesystem glob\nDate: 2026-08-08\nMEASURED 2026-08-08, and it corrects a wrong number in this plan's own `## Now` block and P-001 text (retraction below).\n\n#### The measurement\n\nA repo-wide glob for the guidance corpus returns overwhelmingly BUILD-ARTIFACT COPIES:\n\n| surface | glob finds | canonical |\n|---|---|---|\n| `*.tools.md` + `*.persona.md` | **110** | **19** (all in `apps/operator/prompts`) |\n| blueprint role prompts | **74 x 8 roots** (dist-host, dist-sidecar, 3x desktop sidecar, 2x cargo-target, 1x .materialized) | **74** (`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/*/prompts`) |\n\nProbe: `git ls-files '*.tools.md' '*.persona.md'` returns 19 rows, every one under `apps/operator/prompts`. All 91 others are UNTRACKED build output. `find . -path '*blueprints/*/prompts/*.md'` returns 8 directory roots for the same 74 files.\n\n#### Why this is load-bearing, not hygiene\n\nThis workstream's deterministic leg is \"pairwise cosine above a threshold across DIFFERENT sources\". Fed a glob-derived corpus it would report its HIGHEST-CONFIDENCE clusters on a file versus its own build copies — cosine ~1.0, structurally guaranteed, 100% false positive, at 6-9x the real corpus size. It would also wreck P-003: a threshold calibrated against a corpus whose top of the distribution is exact duplicates is calibrated against an artifact.\n\nThe failure would not have LOOKED wrong. The scan would run, produce many high-scoring clusters, and read as a successful first pass.\n\n#### The ruling (binds P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006)\n\n1. The adapter takes an EXPLICIT list of canonical roots. No repo-wide glob, ever.\n2. Where a surface could have copies, membership is confirmed by git-trackedness IN ITS OWNING REPO — `libs/papercusp` is a SUBMODULE, so `git ls-files` from the superproject cannot see blueprint prompts and its silence there is not evidence (the standing submodule trap in the project CLAUDE.md).\n3. The adapter carries a guard test asserting no two pages share identical content, so a re-introduced copy root fails loudly instead of inflating the cluster count.\n4. Per-tool `guidance:` blocks come from the RUNTIME REGISTRY (`listAllProjectedTools()`, the accessor `agent_tools:list` itself uses), never from a grep over TS source. A grep counts 717 `guidance:` occurrences across 924 files, which is a text-occurrence count and not a tool count.\n\n#### Retraction owed\n\nThis plan's `## Now` and P-001 both say the corpus is \"*.tools.md x82, personas x28\". Those are the GLOB numbers and they are wrong: 82 counts 4 copies of 19 files (+ cargo-target debris), 28 likewise. The real figures are 19 canonical prompt files, 74 blueprint prompts, 1 repo CLAUDE.md, plus the registry-derived tool guidance. Corrected in the Now block in the same turn this decision was recorded.\n\n### D-003 — The overlap threshold is NULL-RELATIVE and PER SOURCE-PAIR — same-source 0.92, cross-source 0.88\nDate: 2026-08-08\nP-003's calibration, measured 2026-08-08 against the live 10,056-section corpus (papercusp-guidance 3536 + papercusp-engineering 6520, single `gemma` embedding space, 100% vectorised). Fixtures were not used for any number here.\n\n#### An absolute cosine is not interpretable on this corpus\n\nThe instinct is to pick something like 0.80 and call anything above it a duplicate. Measured, 0.80 flags ~78% of top-5 neighbour pairs. The reason is that gemma's similarity range is compressed: two RANDOM sections score a median of ~0.62, and 0.80 sits merely between p99 and p99.9 of that NULL distribution. A threshold only means something as a position in the null of the source pair it is applied to.\n\n#### The measured null (random cross-page pairs, per ordered source pair)\n\n| pair | n | p50 | p95 | p99.9 | max |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| eng x eng | 37,630 | 0.6596 | 0.7526 | 0.8442 | 0.9588 |\n| guid x guid | 11,230 | 0.6237 | 0.7127 | 0.8461 | 0.9725 |\n| guid x eng | 20,865 | 0.6100 | 0.7206 | 0.8124 | 0.8585 |\n| eng x guid | 20,265 | 0.6006 | 0.7028 | 0.8088 | 0.8811 |\n\nThe cross-source null runs a full 0.04 lower at p99.9 than the same-source null. That is why a single global threshold is wrong: applied at 0.95 it would yield 361 same-source findings and ONE cross-source finding, i.e. it would silently switch off the most valuable leg (a doc and a prompt disagreeing) while looking like it was scanning both.\n\nNote the null MAX is contaminated and must not be used as the threshold: a \"random\" pair scoring 0.9725 is almost certainly a real duplicate the sampler happened to draw. The p99.9 is the robust statistic here.\n\n#### Chosen thresholds and their measured yield\n\nSame-source **0.92**, cross-source **0.88**. Full corpus, top-10 cross-page neighbours, denominator 99,091 directed pairs:\n\n| pair | denominator | >=0.92 | >=0.88 |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| eng -> eng | 56,464 | 244 | 2,625 |\n| guid -> guid | 29,990 | 840 | 2,638 |\n| guid -> eng | 5,370 | 22 | 265 |\n| eng -> guid | 7,267 | 22 | 309 |\n\nThe cross-source cells are 22 and 22 — a symmetric relation coming out symmetric is a real correctness signal for the provider, not a coincidence to gloss over.\n\nAt these thresholds P-004's LLM leg sees ~1,084 directed same-source pairs and ~574 directed cross-source pairs, i.e. roughly 830 undirected pairs. That is a bounded, affordable judging budget.\n\n#### Why these two numbers and not others (stated honestly)\n\nThey come from a PRECISION inspection, not from a formula. Sampling the 0.92-0.932 band over ALL guidance pairs (not just each section's top-1, which is optimistic by construction), 12 of 12 pairs were genuine overlap — the papercup persona re-homed across three files, operator.persona vs papercup.persona behaviour blocks, `pot:obliterate` vs `pot:dissolve`, `tool-guidance/pot-leave` vs the `system/shared-pot-guide` doc. Precision at that band is effectively 1.0.\n\nBoth chosen values happen to sit ~0.07 above their pair's null p99.9. That is a DESCRIPTION of where they landed, not the rule they were derived from — do not promote it to a formula without measuring it.\n\n#### What must be re-derived, and when\n\nThese numbers are properties of the gemma space, not of the algorithm. **If the embedder changes, every number above is void** and `measureNullBaseline()` must be re-run before the scan is trusted again. That function exists precisely so the re-derivation is one call rather than an archaeology exercise.\n\n### D-004 — High-similarity pairs fall into THREE kinds, and P-005's three-way seam should route on kind, not on source\nDate: 2026-08-08\nEmerged from the P-003 precision inspection (see D-003). Every pair above the chosen thresholds was genuine overlap, but they are not the same KIND of finding, and treating them alike would bury the valuable ones.\n\n**1. Sibling-surface boilerplate.** Two adjacent tools or two role prompts whose corresponding sections say nearly the same thing: `pot:obliterate` vs `pot:dissolve` (0.930), `features:search` vs `features:list_related` (0.924), `cross_harness:docs*` vs `cross_harness:plans*` (0.931), the scoper's \"Two-phase mode\" vs the reviewer's \"MODE=proposal\" (0.927), and the `Chaining` subsection of sibling tools (up to 0.997). Overlap here is EXPECTED — sibling verbs should read alike. The finding value is not \"these duplicate\" but \"do these two contradict?\", which is exactly P-004's narrow question. High volume; this kind will dominate the count.\n\n**2. A re-homed or copy-pasted canonical block.** One passage living in several files: the papercup persona across `blueprints/base/prompts/papercup`, `prompts/papercup.persona` and `prompts/papercup-deep.persona` (0.930-0.955); the novice-mode Tone block copy-pasted into `papercup.persona.novice-mode` and `operator.persona.novice-mode` (0.991); `agent-insights/measuring-code-run-adoption` vs `agent-insights/code-run-adoption`, same title and two slugs (0.925). This is the drift hazard the workstream exists for — the copies are identical TODAY and nothing keeps them so. Lower volume, highest actionability, and the one kind where the right resolution is usually \"make one canonical and point the others at it\" rather than \"reword\".\n\n**3. Cross-kind.** A tool's guidance overlapping a prose doc or a persona: `tool-guidance/pot-leave` vs `system/shared-pot-guide` (0.929), `agents/session-modes` vs `tool-guidance/mode-set` (0.913), `agent-insights/memory-pg-lexicon` vs `harness/memory` (0.910), `papercusp-compaction.base` vs `agent-insights/session-search-and-compaction` (0.931). Rarest — only 44 directed pairs clear 0.92 — and the most dangerous, because the two surfaces are read by different audiences at different times, so a contradiction between them can persist indefinitely without anyone seeing both.\n\n#### The consequence for P-005\n\nP-005's spec already calls for a three-way seam split by authored-vs-learned. This decision does NOT replace that axis. It says the KIND above is a second, orthogonal attribute that must ride on every reported pair, because it determines the shape of the fix: kind 2 wants de-duplication to a single canonical home, kinds 1 and 3 want a contradiction check and, at most, a reworded clause.\n\nDeriving the kind is cheap and needs no LLM — it is a function of the two units' source keys and slug prefixes (`tool-guidance/` vs `prompts/` vs `blueprints/` vs a doc path) plus whether their titles match. Compute it in the deterministic leg and hand it to P-004 as context, rather than asking the judge to infer it.\n\n#### The trap this decision is guarding against\n\nKind 1 is roughly an order of magnitude more common than kind 3. A report sorted by similarity alone puts the 0.997 sibling-`Chaining` pairs at the top and the cross-kind findings hundreds of rows down. Anyone reading the top of that report concludes the corpus's problem is boilerplate in tool guidance, which is true and not very interesting, and never reaches the two surfaces that actually disagree.\n\n### D-005 — One base scan at the LOWER threshold + a per-source-pair filter — equivalent to two runs, and the condition that makes it so is asserted\nDate: 2026-08-08\nP-003's runnable scan is COMPLETE and has been executed against the live corpus. This decision records the one design departure from the plan's proposal, and why it is an identity rather than an approximation.\n\n#### The ruling\n\nThe plan proposed running `scanOverlap` TWICE (0.92 keeping same-source pairs, 0.88 keeping cross-source ones) and merging. `runDocSectionOverlapScan()` instead runs it ONCE at `min(sameSource, crossSource)` and applies a per-source-pair filter.\n\nThis returns the IDENTICAL set. `scanOverlap` at threshold T emits every cross-group pair scoring >= T, so the 0.92 run's output is a strict SUBSET of the 0.88 run's; filtering the latter reconstructs both legs exactly. It costs half the ANN queries (one lookup per unit, not two) and — the reason that actually matters — yields ONE shared census instead of two denominators a reader would have to reconcile by hand. D-001 requires the denominator to travel with the number; two runs make that harder, not easier.\n\n#### The condition that makes the equivalence hold is ASSERTED, not assumed\n\n`maxPairs` truncation breaks it, and breaks it in the worst direction. The generic scan sorts DESCENDING by similarity before capping, so a truncated run discards its LOWEST-scoring pairs — precisely the 0.88-0.92 band where every cross-source finding lives. A capped base scan would drop cross-source findings while retaining same-source ones: the exact bias D-003 split the thresholds to avoid, reproduced silently by a mechanism that looks unrelated.\n\nSo `pairsDropped > 0` is INCONCLUSIVE at this layer (maxPairs defaults to 100,000 — a memory backstop, not a budget). `judgeInconclusive` correctly does NOT flag it: for the generic module a cap is a partial answer, not a zero-that-measured-nothing. It is unsound only for THIS caller, so this caller is where it is caught. Measured on the live run: `pairsDropped: 0`, so the condition held.\n\n#### The measured run (2026-08-08, gemma)\n\n`inconclusive: null` — this is a real result, not a zero measurement.\n\n| census | value |\n|---|---|\n| unitsComparable / unitsIn | 10,056 / 10,056 |\n| pages (groups) | 1,712 |\n| ANN lookups | 10,056 |\n| candidate hits | ~99,000 |\n| distinct cross-page pairs | ~79,000 |\n| at/above base 0.88 | ~3,000 |\n| dimensionMismatches | 0 |\n| pairsDropped | 0 |\n\nPer-leg (>=0.92 same-source, >=0.88 cross-source): engineering x engineering 122 · guidance x guidance 429 · engineering x guidance 264-310 (see D-007 — this leg is NOT run-to-run stable).\n\nTotal kept 815-861, against the plan's ~830 estimate — D-003's calibration corroborated by an independent path (the plan's estimate came from hand-written SQL; this came from the module).\n\n#### A reporting defect found in the run's own output, and fixed\n\nThe first live render read `CROSS-source (>=0.88): 310 kept, 0 below its threshold`. That `0` is TRUE and MEANINGLESS: the base scan runs at 0.88, so the cross-source leg's threshold IS the base threshold and nothing can survive to be rejected by it. Read bare it asserts \"this leg was clean\", a claim the run never made. `SourcePairYield.rejectedIsStructuralZero` now marks it and the prose says `rejected n/a` with the reason. Same class as everything else in this plan: a number that looks like evidence while being determined by construction.\n\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-008 — The encoder and the decoder disagreed about the corpus, and 17 green unit tests could not see it — a round-trip guard must be calibrated against real field shapes\nDate: 2026-08-08\nP-003's FIRST live run died on its first unit. The failure is worth recording because the code was careful, well-documented, fully tested, and wrong — and because the thing that caught it was a deliberate design choice from D-001.\n\n#### What happened\n\n`runDocSectionOverlapScan` threw:\n\n> unit id \"papercusp-engineering<SEP><SEP>\" was not produced by encodeSectionId — refusing to report zero neighbours for it, because that is indistinguishable from a clean section\n\n`loadUnitsReal` had read a real row from `doc_sections` and encoded it. `decodeSectionId` then refused the id it had just produced, because its guard read `if (!sourceKey || !slug) return null`. The rows are real: FIVE embedded sections of the papercusp-engineering ROOT page, whose slug is the empty string, each with a title and 292-1069 chars of content (`what-this-is`, `status`, `what-papercusp-is-not`, `how-this-doc-is-published`, and the preamble).\n\nSo the encode/decode pair was never round-trip-safe on its own corpus.\n\n#### Why 17 green tests could not see it\n\nEvery fixture supplied a hand-written slug. The test file's own comment named the field shapes it believed were exhaustive — \"slugs carry slashes and dots, anchors carry hyphens, and a page preamble has an EMPTY anchor\" — and it was right about all three. It simply never occurred to it that a PAGE could have an empty slug, so no fixture had one, so the guard's over-strictness was unobservable. There was even an explicit test asserting the wrong behaviour (\"rejects an id with a blank source or slug, which would silently group wrongly\"), which made the bug look deliberate and defended.\n\nThat rationale was also false, and measurably so: `pageGroupOf` maps all five root sections to the single group `papercusp-engineering::`, which is exactly right — they ARE one page. Nothing groups wrongly.\n\nThe asymmetry is the tell. An empty ANCHOR was accepted (417 real sections have one); an empty SLUG was rejected. Two structurally identical cases, opposite treatment, no stated reason for the difference.\n\n#### The ruling\n\n1. A round-trip guard rejects on the STRUCTURAL property that defines validity — here the part COUNT, since SEP is a six-character sequence no field contains (measured: 0 of 10,056 embedded sections carry a backslash). It does NOT reject on a field being empty unless emptiness genuinely destroys meaning. An empty `sourceKey` still does (every threshold in this scan is chosen per source PAIR, so an unattributable unit has no threshold); an empty slug does not.\n2. Any test that enumerates \"the field shapes this corpus contains\" must be derived from the CORPUS, not from imagination. The regression tests now carry the measured shapes and cite their real row counts.\n3. This is D-001's fail-closed rule paying for itself. Had `createDocSectionNeighbourProvider` returned `[]` for an undecodable id — the natural, defensive-looking choice — those five sections would have silently reported ZERO neighbours. The scan would have completed, produced ~815 findings, and looked entirely healthy. The corpus root page simply would not have been scanned, permanently and invisibly. Fail-closed converted a silent 5-section blind spot into a stack trace on the first run.\n\n#### The transferable shape\n\nA producer and a validator for the same format, written together, both careful, disagreeing about one field — and the disagreement only observable on data neither author had seen. Fixtures agree with you; the corpus does not. This plan already said that about THRESHOLDS (D-003, P-003's calibration). It turns out to be just as true of IDENTIFIERS, which feel far too simple to need calibrating.\n\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-009 — neighbourLimit = 30, and the cross-source instability was a MOVING CORPUS, not ANN recall (hypothesis retracted)\nDate: 2026-08-09\nSettles the ⚠ OPEN item in the prior `## Now`. Two runs had given cross-source 310 then 264 (−15%) while both same-source legs were byte-identical, and I attributed it to HNSW top-K recall variance on the 0.88–0.92 band sitting at the edge of the K window. That hypothesis is FALSIFIED and retracted.\n\n#### The experiment (falsifier stated in advance: if it is a top-K effect, raising K shrinks the spread)\n\nK ∈ {10,30,60} × 3 consecutive runs each (`/tmp/p003-overlap-scan/stability.log`, STABILITY_EXIT=0):\n\n| K | total | eng×eng | eng×guid | guid×guid | candidatePairs | spread |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 10 | 812 | 122 | 261 | 429 | 78,852 | **0 on every leg** |\n| 30 | 821 | 122 | 266 | 433 | 224,930 | **0 on every leg** |\n| 60 | 821 | 122 | 266 | 433 | 254,494 | **0 on every leg** |\n\nEvery K is PERFECTLY deterministic within itself. So recall variance cannot be the cause — the effect the hypothesis predicted (spread shrinking as K rises) never had a spread to shrink.\n\n#### The real cause\n\nThe CORPUS moved between the two runs. `candidatePairs` differed across those earlier runs (79,167 / 79,178 / 78,852), which is a statement about the population, not the search. Measured: all 3,536 `papercusp-guidance` sections had been re-written within 2h, 30 of them within the preceding 30 minutes — newest `updated_at` 23:45:22Z, INSIDE the scan window. The scan was measuring a target that was being rewritten under it.\n\n#### The ruling\n\n**`neighbourLimit = 30`.** K=60 returns the IDENTICAL result set as K=30 (821/122/266/433) while adding ~30k candidate pairs of work, so 30 is the converged value and 60 buys nothing. K=10 is genuinely lossy — it misses 9 pairs (5 cross-source, 4 guidance×guidance), and the cross-source leg is precisely the one this workstream exists to find, so the default 10 must NOT be kept.\n\n#### Two transferable readings\n\n1. **A between-run difference is not automatically a property of the ALGORITHM.** The instinct was to explain the variance with a mechanism inside the search (recall, tie-breaking, index state); the answer was that the DATA changed. Before attributing run-to-run variance to nondeterminism, check whether the population moved — `count(*) FILTER (WHERE updated_at > now() - interval '30 minutes')` costs one query and is decisive.\n2. **The hypothesis was seductive because it was mechanistically plausible AND correctly predicted which leg would be unstable** (cross-source, the marginal band). Predicting the right symptom is not evidence of the right cause; only the falsifier separated them.\n\nRe: D-005's forward reference to \"D-007\" for the neighbourLimit ruling — decision numbering advanced concurrently (peers adding decisions), so THIS decision is that ruling under a different id.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-006\n\n### D-010 — A filter in the WHERE clause destroys the evidence of its own effect — coverage must have an independent denominator\nDate: 2026-08-09\nA defect in MY OWN P-003 deliverable, found while re-reading it, and it is D-001's failure mode one level up. D-001 made the PAIR census honest; the UNIT census was still lying.\n\n#### The defect\n\n`loadUnitsReal` selected `... WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL`. The census then reported `unitsComparable` (numerator) and `unitsIn` (denominator) — but BOTH were computed from that already-filtered population. So the ratio was **structurally 1.0 no matter how much of the corpus was missing**, and the run printed `10,056 of 10,056` — 100% coverage — as its denominator sentence.\n\nThe live corpus was in exactly that state when I found it: 3,536 guidance sections, **3,506 vectorised, 30 with no embedding**, re-written 6 minutes earlier. A scan then would have silently skipped the 30 FRESHEST sections — the most likely to contain a newly-introduced contradiction, i.e. precisely what this workstream exists to find — and reported complete coverage while doing it.\n\nD-001 forbids a bare pair list because \"the failure is indistinguishable from success and it is REASSURING\". This was the same shape wearing D-001's own uniform: a census that LOOKS like the denominator discipline while carrying a ratio that cannot fall.\n\n#### The ruling\n\n1. **The `embedding IS NOT NULL` test is a SELECTED COLUMN, never a WHERE predicate.** As a predicate it shrinks the population and removes the evidence of the shrinkage; as a column (`(embedding IS NOT NULL) AS has_vector`) the shortfall is counted and reported. Both numbers come from ONE snapshot, so a concurrent backfill cannot make them disagree — which the two-query alternative cannot guarantee.\n2. **The generic lib gained a way to be TOLD what it cannot see**: `scanOverlap(units, config, { unitsUnavailable, unitsUnavailableReason })`, feeding `census.unitsUnavailable` / `unitsKnown` / `coverage`. Kept out of config on purpose — config is policy, this is evidence about one run.\n3. **`minCoverage` defaults to 1.0**, the STRICT value, so a caller who forgets it gets an inconclusive verdict rather than a silently permissive one. This inverts the usual footgun: forgetting to configure fails safe.\n4. **The host relaxes it to 0.99 WITH a reason.** A missing vector can only cause a MISSED finding, never a false one — so a shortfall does not invalidate the pairs found, only the claim that the corpus is clean. That asymmetry is why the floor is a tolerance rather than a hard gate, and why `inconclusive` firing does not throw away findings. It also stops the flag crying wolf on ordinary backfill lag, which would make P-005 (auto-file from a conclusive report) never fire.\n5. **`describeOverlapReport` quotes `unitsKnown`, never the survivor count** — the survivor count must not be able to masquerade as the population.\n\n#### Evidence\n\n61/61 green (30 generic + 31 host), both typechecks exit 0, 0 control bytes in all four files. Includes a CONTROL test asserting that an UNDECLARED shortfall is invisible — calibration proving the other assertions test the reporting path rather than passing for free.\n\n⚠ The live run could NOT exercise the shortfall: backfill completed between measurements (30 pending at 23:51Z → 0 by 23:59Z), so it honestly reported `coverage: 1`, verified against PG as a TRUE 1 rather than the old artifact. The SQL expression's falsifiability was proven separately against the real table (166 false / 34 true), so it is not a constant. State this limitation rather than quoting the clean live run as proof of the fix.\n\n#### Transferable\n\n**A ratio whose numerator and denominator come from the same query is not a measurement.** When a guard reports coverage/completeness, find where the population is filtered: if the filter runs upstream of BOTH terms, the ratio can only ever be 1, and it will be most reassuring exactly when it is least true.\nRelated: P-003, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-011 — An INERT judge must be inconclusive, never empty — and the metadata kind classifier's recall is measurably incomplete\nDate: 2026-08-09\nTwo rulings from building P-004. Both bind P-005 and P-006.\n\n#### 1. The judged leg's empty result is INCONCLUSIVE unless the judge actually ran\n\nThis repo has already shipped the opposite twice, and both are filed. `createAnthropicJudge()` returns a SILENT NO-OP when no credential resolves, and that no-op returns `{conflicts: []}` — byte-identical to a healthy \"nothing contradicts\". `memory:remember`'s conflict-check was DEFAULT-ON and inert in this operator indefinitely (EI-18746586784230719); the same no-op judge is wired into knowledge-packs, so pack-install classification and the hive conflict sweep were equally inert (EI-18747066020546067). Nothing logged, nothing surfaced. The result was not merely wrong, it was REASSURING.\n\nThat is this plan's D-001 (\"an empty result is not evidence\") one level up, so the contradiction leg inherits D-001's contract rather than repeating the bug:\n  - the report carries `inconclusive: string | null`; `contradictions: []` may be read as \"nothing contradicts\" ONLY when it is null;\n  - an unavailable judge, a DISABLED flag, an unreadable flag store, zero eligible pairs, and an all-errors run each set `inconclusive`. None of them is swallowed into an empty list;\n  - the judge returns `null` (never `{contradicts:false}`) on every failure path — no credential, gateway throw, unparseable reply. `judgeContradictions` counts a null as an ERROR, and refuses to call an all-null run clean;\n  - a PARTIAL run (some errors, or the cap left pairs unasked) stays CONCLUSIVE for what it answered, with the census carrying the numbers that make the partiality visible. Only a run that answered NOTHING is inconclusive.\n\nThe falsifiability control is a test that runs an inert judge and a clean judge side by side and asserts BOTH that inert.inconclusive is non-null AND that clean.inconclusive is null. No constant implementation satisfies both, so the control cannot pass trivially — which matters because the whole failure mode is that the broken state looks like the good one.\n\nFor P-005: this is the operative precondition. Per D-001 you must not auto-file a work item from a report whose `inconclusive` is non-null, and the contradiction leg has FIVE such states, of which \"no credential in this operator\" is the CURRENT one.\n\n#### 2. The kind classifier is metadata-only, and its `rehomed-copy` bucket is a FLOOR, not a count\n\nD-004 states the kind is \"a function of the two units' source keys and slug prefixes plus whether their titles match\". Measured against the live corpus, the title signal is PRECISE but its recall is INCOMPLETE, and the shortfall runs in the direction that costs the most.\n\nIt works on the flagship kind-2 pair: `prompts/operator.persona.engineer-mode#audience-mode-engineer` and `prompts/papercup.persona.engineer-mode#audience-mode-engineer` BOTH title \"Audience mode: Engineer > Audience mode: Engineer\" at cosine 1.0000, so title equality identifies the copy exactly.\n\nIt FAILS on the other kind-2 pair D-004 cites. Measured:\n  blueprints/base/prompts/papercup -> \"Papercup (canonical persona re-homed)\"\n  prompts/papercup.persona         -> \"Papercup persona - the fast front-end\"\nBoth are the papercup persona; the blueprint home was deliberately RE-TITLED to record that it is a re-home — precisely the edit that defeats the test for it. That pair falls through to the surface rule and reports as `cross-kind`.\n\nSo: `rehomed-copy` is a FLOOR on how many re-homed copies exist, never a count of them, and `cross-kind`/`sibling-surface` are supersets that contain some. Every verdict carries `basis` (which signal decided it) and `confident` (true only for a positive title identification) so a consumer can tell an identification from a residual assignment. A metadata-only classifier cannot close this gap — the two titles share no token a rule could key on — so closing it needs CONTENT comparison, which is P-005's business.\n\nThe limit is pinned as a CONTROL test asserting the papercup pair classifies as `cross-kind`. That test encodes a known shortfall, not desired behaviour: it exists so a future rule change has to confront the trade deliberately instead of silently moving findings between buckets.\n\n#### Consequences for P-005/P-006\n- P-005's three-way resolution seam must read `confident`, not just `kind`, before treating a bucket as a population.\n- P-006's recurrence guard must fail on an INCONCLUSIVE zero, not merely on a zero — a scan that degrades to \"no judge available\" would otherwise report green forever, which is the exact 6-day-undetected shape of the memory conflict-check bug.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/guidance-overlap-contradiction-scan-2026-08-08 (\"Workstream C — overlap + contradiction scan over the guidance corpus\"): no plan update since 2026-08-25 (46 days idle), 5/6 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"kettle-supervision-health","title":"Kettle supervision health","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-08","owner":"s-1784239429985-b1aca60f","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Kettle supervision health\nslug: kettle-supervision-health\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-08\nupdated: 2026-09-05\nowner: s-1784239429985-b1aca60f\n---\n\n# Kettle supervision health\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-05. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08","title":"Learning loop: give observations and ideas a stable identity, and make consumption visible","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-08","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Learning loop: give observations and ideas a stable identity, and make consumption visible\nslug: learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-08\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Phase 5 implementation and acceptance validation remain complete. P-016 remains in a VALID continuous maturation window. Original start: 2026-08-23T17:39:44.625-04:00; earliest measurement: 2026-08-30T17:39:44.625-04:00. Intervening deploy 5bb09b0c0f7cceaca3af9d9a84cc19acaebc5e35 preserved target 51c52bae1 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0). Runtime continuity is confirmed: release HEAD moved at 2026-08-27T00:02:49.325-04:00 and papercup-dev-api is active/running since 00:07:44-04:00. The clock does not reset. Superseded August 22/August 29 window remains invalid. P-016 is the sole residue.\n\n**Next:** Continue six-hour monitor plus release:deployed:* await. Revalidate ancestry/runtime on every deploy; reset only if target inclusion is lost. How can we stop that?\" Measured rather than assumed. Three separate problems were wearing the same coat.\n\n**Measurements (2026-08-08, workspace `papercusp-workspace`):**\n\n| finding | number |\n|---|---|\n| Observation lane, open | 14,780 of 15,432 created (~7.5 weeks) |\n| Observations with a \"consumed\" marker of any kind | **0** |\n| Observations carrying a `conditionKey` | **0** |\n| Identical rows titled `pot-coordination-health scorecard` | 822 |\n| Observation arrival rate | 491/day |\n| Retention steady state = arrival x 30d window | 14,730 projected vs 14,720 actual |\n| Blender-routed ideas resolving to real work items | 548 of 550 (496 minted by the routing) |\n| Those work items ever CLAIMED / ever ATTEMPTED | **0 / 0** |\n| ...of which sit in the claimable view (not gate-blocked) | 404 of 478 |\n| Blender output as share of open non-observation backlog | 462 of 2,174 (21%) |\n| Landing rate: blender vs agent-ideate | 7% vs 56% |\n| Blender open items that re-file an OLDER one (cosine <0.09) | 109 (23%) |\n| ...at the looser <0.13 band (mixed, some genuinely distinct) | 284 (61%) |\n| Blender ticks last 14d: ran / circuit-gated / errored | 169 / 74 / 63 |\n| Ideas generated vs routed, week 32 | 1,003 generated, 61 routed, 861 deduped (86%) |\n\n**The single root cause, showing up twice.** There is no stable identity for a recurring condition. Every observation and every idea embeds a LIVE MEASUREMENT, and the measurement changes each time it is taken — so the text is always novel and textual dedupe can never match. Evidence, one bug filed seven times:\n\n```\n\"fires on 92/92 ticks\"          \"fires on 96/96 ticks\"\n\"fires on 92/94 ticks in 24h\"   \"fires on 97/97 ticks\"\n\"fires on 95/96 ticks\"          \"fires on 100% of ticks (356 signals/24h)\"\n                                \"fires on 100% of watchdog ticks (389 signals/24h)\"\n```\n\nThe same shape produced ~14 work items for one plan-lifecycle bug (8 of the top-12 repeat offenders are that single issue).\n\n**What is NOT wrong.** The blender is not generating garbage. Bodies are 2,000-3,000 char structured proposals (prior art -> Mechanism -> The bet) that are specific and implementable. The pipeline reads observations incrementally via a real, current watermark (`scout_signal_accumulator`). Both were checked directly and both work. Amend WI-40694 SQL/verdict rules before reading the new window.\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — No deletion-based observation retention — observations are kept\nDate: 2026-08-08\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-08, interactive] Verbatim: \"I dont think we should have the 1k or 30 day limit. why would we ever want to throw out observations? maybe they get stale but we can just have an agent verify if they are stale. if we have that running constantly we should never get to observations that are that old in the first place.\" RATIFIED: the fix is CONSUMPTION MARKING (P-004), not deletion (P-005 retires the delete path). Note the agent Avi describes already exists and already runs constantly — the blender reads every new observation within ~20 minutes via a live watermark; what it does not do is write anything back. Any future storage bound must be archive/rollup over CONSUMED rows, never a hard DELETE.\n\n### D-002 — Dedupe identity is SEMANTIC and threshold is 0.09, not 0.15\nDate: 2026-08-08\nCalibrated 2026-08-08 against real pairs rather than picked. At cosine distance <0.09 every sampled pair was unambiguously the same issue. <0.15 is far too loose: the bulk of ALL pairwise distances sits at 0.15–0.30, so that threshold captures generic topical similarity and would report 429 of 464 items (92%) as duplicates — a number that sounds decisive and means nothing. The 0.10–0.13 band is genuinely MIXED (real duplicates alongside distinct work), so it is reported as a range (109 provable at <0.09, 284 at <0.13) and never as a single figure. Any implementation that changes this threshold must re-calibrate against sampled pairs and record the samples.\n\n### D-003 — su-ideate agents keep pushing to the work queue directly — any gate is blender-only\nDate: 2026-08-08\nCarried forward from D-004 on scorecard-blender-pipeline-fixes-2026-07-11. Note this decision also sharpens the diagnosis — the blender's stated job is NOVEL synthesis, and the measured defect is that ~23%+ of its output is a re-file of something it already said.\n\n### D-005 — Observations are a time series — never bulk-close or purge them\nDate: 2026-08-08\nStanding fact `observation-lane-rows-are-not-queue-debris`. Two independent 'written, merged, does nothing' bugs in one subsystem is a pattern, not a coincidence — a fix that lands without an end-to-end assertion on the REAL call path is indistinguishable from no fix at all, and both of these had green tests.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for the rest of the plan: before implementing ANY remaining item, first grep the running system for the remedy and MEASURE whether it is already there and inert. Applies most directly to P-003 (semantic dedupe) and P-004 (consumption stamping).\n\n### D-023 — Condition-bridge junk churn folded in as P-012 — it dwarfs the measured problem\nDate: 2026-08-09\nEI-19930875455827867 (critical, filed by another agent with a complete diagnosis) is the single largest source of exactly what this plan exists to stop: 29,146 bridge-minted work items, 29,126 of them immediately dropped, ~150/hour sustained since 2026-08-03, ~45% of the entire 64,754-row work_items table. Do not implement P-002 as written.\n\nTHE EXPERIMENT (re-runnable): took the three real insight-staleness filings the item was written about — EI-18652033720958396, EI-18668965892714266, EI-18710402934363497 — and computed `dedupSignature` + token-set Jaccard under the CURRENT implementation and under a variant that drops pure-numeric tokens.\n\n  pair                    current   numeric-stripped\n  958396~714266            0.152         0.163\n  958396~363497            0.361         0.364\n  714266~363497            0.136         0.146\n\nStripping numerics moves similarity by ~0.01. It cannot lift any pair anywhere near a dedupe threshold. Shipping P-002 as specified would have produced a fourth 'written, merged, does nothing' change — this time self-inflicted and entirely predictable.\n\nWHY THE PREMISE FAILED, two independent reasons:\n1. `dedupSignature` (digest.ts:264) ALREADY drops numeric noise for the cited case, accidentally: it filters tokens of length <=2, so `92/92` -> tokens '92','92' -> both dropped. The literal example in P-002's text is already normalized today. Only 3+ digit runs survive.\n2. The implementer identified this himself and declined to take (b) unilaterally — correctly.\n\n**3. WHY (c) — SHIP WITH P-016 DEFERRED TO A SUCCESSOR PLAN — IS ALSO REFUSED.** It was raised as an undetermined third option. Rejected: a deferral to a successor plan that nobody creates is a drop with extra bookkeeping, and the deferral is *proposed by the party the deferral benefits*. The successor plan would also have to inherit the baseline, the control lane and the revert trigger intact — every hop is a chance to lose them. Keep the item where its context already lives.\n\n**4. WHAT (a) COSTS — AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT.** Plan status `shipped` is a BOOKKEEPING verdict, not a deploy gate: the code reaches :3070 through the release pipeline regardless of whether this plan is marked shipped. So leaving the plan open costs one field being un-green and blocks nothing. Option (b) buys that one green field and spends the only harm-detector the change has. There is no version of that trade that is worth taking.\n\n**5. REQUIRED, so an open plan does not rot into an abandoned one.** (a)'s real failure mode is a plan sitting open for a week until some future triage sweeps it up as dead:\n- **P-016 goes `todo` → `blocked`**, with the unblock condition stated in the note: \"blocked until P-013 fold is DEPLOYED (gate is red, 35 reds, repair-staging-mismatch) + 7 days of post-deploy data\". `blocked` still refuses ship — that is intended and it is not what the flip is for. It is the difference between \"waiting on a named condition\" and \"nobody picked this up\", and only one of those survives a triage pass.\n- **WI-40694 must carry the executable measurement**, not a description of it: the exact SQL for both legs under the same `payload ? 'observation'` predicate, the `captures` control-lane ratio, the baseline (mean 1.434, min 1.119 over 08-16..08-22) and the revert trigger (sustained breach below 1.119) — per D-044. A successor must be able to RUN it without re-deriving the instrument.\n- **The 7-day window starts at the deploy timestamp**, recorded on WI-40694 when it happens — never at merge, and never at \"about a week ago\".\n\n**6. UNRELATED TO THIS RULING, AND IT NEEDS SAYING.** su-8fc3ac2e routed the D-043 correction on the premise that \"su-3771084b, whose session has since ended\". That premise is false: I am su-3771084b, I am live, and I hold the leader seat — the session carry-respawned rather than ended, which a `coord:send` to a stale session id reports indistinguishably from death. Consequence: the ratifier of D-043 and the current leader are the SAME agent, so my recusal from grading any acceptance criterion that re-tests D-043 does not dissolve by waiting for a new leader. Those criteria go to a genuine third party. The rest of the acceptance rubric I will grade as a clean non-implementer, as accepted at 20:45Z.\nRelated: P-016\n\n### D-046 — An expired pause whose author is dead is an abandoned lock, not a hold — the papercusp green-checkpoint routine has been active:false for 18h and resuming it is authorized without owner sign-off\nDate: 2026-08-22\nDate: 2026-08-22\n\n**⚠ AMENDED 21:43Z — READ THIS FIRST. The EXECUTION clause of this decision is VOID.** Within three minutes of my writing it, su-dddb4150 replied that they had ALREADY replaced the dead pause with a NEW, live, owned hold (D-013 / D-012 writer deps, freeze candidate C; routines:set audit gwc-mt4whof6-4svdgb). So the row I measured at 21:37Z was superseded when I ruled on it. **Do NOT resume green-checkpoint on the strength of this decision.** The 21:55Z self-execute I announced is WITHDRAWN unconditionally (msg mt4wmfka). The GENERAL rule below still stands and is why the decision is amended rather than deleted.\n\nMy own error, stated plainly so the next reader inherits it: I ruled on a volatile row I had read six minutes earlier, in the same turn I was writing about not doing exactly that. **Re-read a volatile row at the moment you RULE on it, not at the moment you notice it.** A routine's pause record is as volatile as a gate verdict.\n\n---\n\nRAISED BY su-8fc3ac2e (msg mt4wg2ki), INDEPENDENTLY RE-MEASURED BY ME at 21:37Z. Governs any lane blocked behind the papercusp green-checkpoint gate.\n\n**THE MEASUREMENT (at 21:37Z — since superseded).** `routines:list { name:'green-checkpoint', installSlug:'papercusp' }`: `active:false`; `paused.by: su-b2cecf28-…`, `paused.at: 03:30:31Z`; `lastFiredAt: 03:15:04Z`; `nextFireAt: 04:15Z` (18h in the past); `consecutiveReds: 35`; `commitsBehindTip: 32`. And `coord:presence { owner: su-b2cecf28 }` → `sessionState: 'ended'`.\n\n**THE GENERAL RULE — this part STANDS.** That pause named its own release condition (*\"until exact-id + last_output writer regressions pass and the guard is published\"*), and WI-40422 closed ~19 min AFTER it was set. A pause carries no expiry and no liveness link to its author, so with enough elapsed time it degrades from \"a deliberate hold\" into \"the way things are\" — every agent that read `active:false` for 18h read it as a fact about the system rather than as a decision someone made and then died holding. **A pause is only evidence while its author is alive and its stated condition is unmet. Check both before treating one as a constraint.** The correct remedy is what dddb4150 did: replace an abandoned hold with an owned one, not merely lift it and not merely leave it.\n\n**THE SECOND ERROR IT CAUSED, which is the more expensive one — this part STANDS.** Two agents were triaging the gate's `failingTests` list file-by-file. That list came from the 03:15Z run against candidate `4bd9c405a1f2`, and the tree is now 32 commits ahead — an 18-hour-old verdict about a different tree. Per-file green/red at HEAD is **un-attributable** from it in EITHER direction. Measuring all 11 entries instead of 2 would not have rescued it: the instrument, not the sample size, was the problem. **A stale gate verdict is not a weak signal; it is not a signal.**\n\n### D-047 — A CALENDAR gate is not held by an agent: the P-016 7-day soak gets a scheduled re-launch, not a long-cadence heartbeat — implementation-complete is the terminal state for the implementing member\nDate: 2026-08-22\nDate: 2026-08-22\nFleet-leader ruling (fleet `capture-seam-dedupe-2026-08-22`, leader su-3771084b), settling a disposition su-8fc3ac2e correctly flagged as undetermined rather than guessing at it.\n\n**THE SITUATION.** P-016's after-measurement requires the P-013 capture-seam fold DEPLOYED 7+ full days (WI-40694, authority D-044). Phase 5 implementation is complete and verified — P-013 fold, P-014 over-merge guard (mutation probe verdict=caught), P-015 reporter feedback, flag confirmed default-ON by EXECUTING FLAG_DEFAULTS rather than trusting a code comment. So the kickoff brief's \"done, verified, shipped -> then stop\" is unreachable in-session, and the brief is what is wrong, not the member's progress.\n\n**RULING: STAND DOWN. Do not hold a long-cadence heartbeat across the soak.** A 7-day wait is a CALENDAR gate, and a calendar gate needs no agent. Holding a session across it is the worse option on every axis:\n- **No warm session survives 7 days** — context ceiling, usage limits, host restarts. (Demonstrated the same evening: this leader's own loop hit `usage_limit` and backed off 5.5 hours.)\n- **A dead heartbeat still LOOKS like coverage**, which is strictly worse than no coverage, because it suppresses the question \"who is watching this?\" until the measurement is silently missed.\n- It burns a member slot for a week to accomplish what a timestamp accomplishes for free.\n\n**THE MECHANISM IS THE SCHEDULE PRIMITIVE**, not a held session and not a hand-rolled reminder: `plans:set-schedule` then `plans:arm-schedule` — arming is a separate, autonomy-gated step, and an unarmed schedule never fires, which is precisely how this kind of follow-up silently becomes nobody's job. Date it from the fold's DEPLOY date plus 7 full days — not from commit, not from merge, not from today.\n\n**WI-40694 STAYS BLOCKED WITH ITS BEFORE BASELINE PINNED.** That work-item is the correct durable carrier for the soak and needs nothing further from the implementing member. A fresh session re-launched at the date will re-read the pinned baseline and re-run the obs_per_control falsifier COLD — which is a better experiment than one run by a session that has been marinating in its own priors for a week.\n\n**GENERALISATION worth carrying beyond this plan:** when the remaining block is structural (a calendar, an external dependency, another lane's gate) rather than effort, the correct disposition of the blocked worker is to COMPLETE, RECORD, and STAND DOWN — never to idle in a holding pattern. The durable artifact carries the wait; the agent does not. Distinguish this sharply from a blocker that is *progressing* and that the agent could unblock, where sleeping is also wrong but the remedy is to act rather than to stand down.\nRelated: P-016\n\n### D-048 — Owner 2026-08-24 inverts P-015's response design — capture responses must not mention the fold; implementation lives in the successor plan\nDate: 2026-08-24\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-24, interactive — verbatim] \"it can be deduped deterministically on the server first too, thats okay, what i dont want is for the results to go back to the agent so the agent says hey maybe this is a duplicate let me spend time investigating.\"\n\nP-013/P-014's server-side fold STANDS. P-015's tell-the-filer response is REVERSED: the capture response must be indistinguishable from a plain success. The original anti-re-file rationale is void under folding — a re-file folds into the same row at zero corpus growth, so re-filing is idempotent and telling the filer buys nothing while inviting investigation spend. Machine-emitter conditionKey folding untouched. Implementation + the P-016 before/after re-point live in work-queue-admission-and-bulk-dedup-2026-08-24 P-008 — do not also change it here.\n\n### D-049 — PATH CORRECTION to D-043: semantic-dupe-guard.ts lives under lib/agent-tools/work_items/, not lib/scout/\nDate: 2026-08-25\nNarrow factual correction to D-043 finding (4). **The finding itself is CORRECT and unchanged — only the file path is wrong.**\n\nD-043 cites the measured co-signal calibration as living at `packages/operator-core/lib/scout/semantic-dupe-guard.ts`. **That path does not exist.** The file is real and its content is exactly as D-043 describes; it lives at:\n\n`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/semantic-dupe-guard.ts`\n\nVerified by reading it: mean nearest-neighbour cosine 0.867; six known-duplicate pairs 0.861–0.892; four known-DISTINCT pairs 0.857–0.868; the ranges overlap, so \"COSINE ALONE CANNOT SEPARATE DUPLICATES FROM DISTINCT FILINGS\"; HARD stays 0.93 as the only defensible pure-cosine refusal and must not be lowered into the 0.86–0.89 band. Every substantive claim D-043 draws from this file holds.\n\n**WHY THIS IS WORTH A DECISION RATHER THAN A SILENT FIX.** The wrong path already PROPAGATED. I cited it verbatim from D-043 in the code-truth audit of the neighbouring plan `learning-loop-backlog-triage-2026-08-22`, and `plans:audit` REFUSED the whole submission with `citation_file_not_found` — nothing was recorded until it was fixed. I had never opened the file; I copied a peer's path because the surrounding reasoning was sound. That is the specific failure mode: a correct finding carries an incorrect locator, and the locator is the part that gets copied.\n\nThe audit gate's own message is the right lesson and it earned its keep here: *\"a citation that will not resolve is usually a real finding about the work — if the file you expected is not there, the item may not actually be implemented.\"* In this case it was a locator error rather than missing work, but only opening the file distinguishes the two.\n\n**FOR ANYONE CITING THIS FILE NEXT:** use the `lib/agent-tools/work_items/` path, and open it before citing. Sibling tests worth knowing about sit beside it (`semantic-dupe-guard.test.ts`, `semantic-dupe-guard.query.test.ts`).\n\nD-043's four findings — the P-016 baseline being ~6x stale, the keyed-fold-works/unkeyed-gap diagnosis, the accumulator-counts-rows hazard, and the co-signal predicate — all stand. This corrects one string.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08","title":"Non-p2p bug drain (2026-08-08)","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-08","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Non-p2p bug drain (2026-08-08)\nslug: nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-08\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n# Non-p2p bug drain (2026-08-08)\n\nOwner-directed [owner:Avi 2026-08-08]: drain the papercusp work queue of ALL\nnon-p2p **bugs** to a terminal state. Fleet: `nonp2p-bug-drain`, 10 members,\nsonnet-5 high effort, gateway auto-routing.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Current registered leadership is su-055e916b on nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-0930 under WI-10008207 and the owner-scoped AUTO instruction. D-124 and D-327 distinguish this lane from the historical September Sol-10/D-112 and Luna-50 profiles. The maintained fleet claim spec is revision 14: bug-only/non-P2P, open states, two concurrent member claims, existing exclusions and ranking preserved. Revision-adoption opt-in remains removed pending D-025 consumer compatibility qualification. Original UBP/BQL implementation is excluded from this leader's work and remains unshipped; source, runtime, privacy, evidence and owner gates persist. Plan activation-audit renewal remains unresolved.\n\n**Next:** Leader responds to actual actionable member transitions and qualified existing owner/source outcomes; members continue eligible held work or pull one admitted bug through their effective scheduler spec while below its cap, retaining every item-specific evidence and runtime gate.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10002595 — Drain the current non-P2P Papercusp bug queue to evidence-backed terminal dispositions through fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-50: launch a headless Codex gpt-6-luna:max canary, verify first turn and… <!-- P-207 -->\n## Scope\nIN: kind=bug, papercusp harness, non-p2p.\nOUT: anything the `p2p-lane` fence excludes (federation / DHT / hive /\nholepunch / cross-machine-rig work), observations, needs-human residue.\n\n## Terminal criteria\ndone / resolved (with evidence) · deprecated (with a reason) · needs_human\n(only for a genuine owner wall — say exactly what the owner must supply).\n\n## Triage dispositions\n- Already fixed in tree => verify at HEAD, close with the verification as evidence.\n- Stale infra/watchdog auto-signal whose subject no longer exists => deprecate with the reason.\n- Needs a multi-machine rig => it should not have reached you; report to the leader.\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Queue integrity audit\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit the full nonterminal non-P2P work queue for exact, normalized, semantic/root-cause, repeated-signal, and parent-link duplication; consolidate only evidence-backed duplicates; record recurrence controls and re-measure drain stock/flow. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38130 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Drain to terminal\n\n- **P-206** `done` Drain the scoped non-p2p bug queue to terminal via fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-50 (claim spec rev5, bug-only, p2p/federation/hive fenced). Done when work_items:claimable under the fleet sentinel spec returns 0 rows with zero live drain claims (D-061/D-067), every scoped bug is done/resolved/deprecated/needs_human with evidence per Terminal criteria, and D-058/D-059 governor receipts remain untouched. Lane: the live fleet leader (su-7ff60d10 as of 2026-09-01). importance: urgent — note: ← WI-2140887 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase — 2026-09-23 renewed drain\n\n- **P-207** `wip` Drain the current non-P2P Papercusp bug queue to evidence-backed terminal dispositions through fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-50: launch a headless Codex gpt-6-luna:max canary, verify first turn and scheduler pull, then scale toward a maximum of 50 agents as measured capacity permits. Keep the fleet revision-5 non-P2P claim spec and P2P/rig exclusions; members self-pull one bug at a time, fix root cause, add recurrence guards, run relevant tests, and close with structured proof. Leader maintains a bounded loop, triages blockers and reports residue. Owner directive 2026-09-23 and D-102 govern this wave. importance: high — note: ← WI-10002595 released\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\n```reuse\n{\n  \"searched\": [\n    {\n      \"where\": \"Current fleet assignments/claim-spec records, D-335/D-336/D-339, WI-6554700010018216 and EI-26586355569330102 retained evidence\",\n      \"how\": \"Read authoritative tools and existing source/acceptance checkpoints before selecting the continued operational route.\",\n      \"found\": \"The maintained scheduler, work-item ledger, coordination, event/loop and isolated verification mechanisms cover this leadership continuation.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"reused\": [\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"scheduler:get_next\",\n      \"kind\": \"tool\",\n      \"provides\": \"Existing bug-only/non-P2P admission and claim-spec enforcement.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"work_items:get\",\n      \"kind\": \"tool\",\n      \"provides\": \"Authoritative current custody, source evidence and retained checkpoints.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"coord:send\",\n      \"kind\": \"tool\",\n      \"provides\": \"Directed dispositions and contextual wakes, without a separate transport.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"events:await\",\n      \"kind\": \"tool\",\n      \"provides\": \"Exact transition wakes; existing leader loop remains the bounded fallback.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"scripts/with-test-pg.mjs\",\n      \"kind\": \"file\",\n      \"provides\": \"Maintained isolated current-build verification route; preserve per-item preflight and source/proof constraints.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"newSurfaces\": [],\n  \"notApplicable\": null\n}\n```\n\n## Third-party libraries\n\n```libraries\n{\n  \"needs\": [],\n  \"notApplicable\": \"This continuation coordinates existing fleet/tool/verification mechanisms and adds no application code or library dependency. Source implementations and their library choices remain on their governing work-items/plans.\"\n}\n```\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Terminal dispositions: a stale auto-signal that no longer reproduces is a REAL close\nDate: 2026-08-08\nThis backlog is old and heavily populated by watchdog EI-* auto-signals. Members must not treat\n\"I cannot reproduce it\" as a reason to leave an item open, nor as a reason to fake a fix.\n\nAllowed terminal states, each with MANDATORY evidence (what you ran, what it printed):\n- done/resolved — root cause named + durable fix + a recurrence guard + verified.\n- done (already-fixed) — verify AT HEAD by RUNNING the check, not by reading a log or a prior\n  report. A status derived from an old verdict log is not a status at HEAD.\n- deprecated — the subject no longer exists (removed surface, retired service). State why.\n- needs_human — a genuine owner wall ONLY. Name exactly what the owner must supply. Note the leader\n  is in AUTO+DRAIN mode, so \"needs a decision\" is NOT an owner wall — escalate it to the leader.\n\nCompletion integrity outranks burn-down speed: the leader audits terminalCompletionRefs and reopens\nbare assertions. A close whose evidence is \"the tests passed\" without naming the command and its\noutput is a bare assertion.\n\n### D-002 — The non-p2p lane is DEFINED by the fleet claim spec, not by member judgement\nDate: 2026-08-08\nFleet `nonp2p-bug-drain` runs claim spec `nonp2p-bug-drain` rev 1, which expands the server-side\n`p2p-lane` fence macro into: kind IN (bug) AND NOT title WORD-MATCHES any of {p2p, shared-hive,\nfederation, federated, federate, federates, federating, holepunch, steering lease, replication,\nswarm, hyperswarm, hyperdht, hyperbee, dht, udx, relay, pot-git, ref-announce, duplex}.\n\nConsequences that bind every member:\n1. Anything scheduler:get_next hands you is IN SCOPE. Do not re-litigate scope per item.\n2. Do NOT hand-pick from the backlog or claim by id — that bypasses the fence and is the only way a\n   p2p item can reach this fleet.\n3. If an item you were handed genuinely needs a multi-machine/p2p rig, that is a FENCE GAP: report it\n   to the leader (su-b8422) rather than silently working or dropping it. The fix belongs in the shared\nP2P_LANE_EXCLUSION_TERMS source so it cannot drift, not in a local workaround.\n\nRationale: three prior drains hand-typed their own p2p excludes and drifted. The fence macro is the\nsingle maintained source; using it is what makes \"non-p2p\" mean the same thing in all 10 lanes.\n\n### D-003 — Lane bumped to spec rev 2 — the shared p2p fence misses hypercore/corestore substrate terms\nDate: 2026-08-08\nSupersedes the lane definition in D-002 (that decision otherwise stands).\n\nThe shared `p2p-lane` fence covers p2p TRANSPORT vocabulary but not the STORAGE substrate beneath it.\nProof: EI-19899917753028359 (\"corestore WRITE lock\", \"sparse seed cuts\") is a CRITICAL p2p bug that\nmatched zero fence terms and sat inside our non-p2p lane. Note \"hive\" does not match \"shared-hive\".\n\nSpec rev 2 therefore ANDs a LOCAL exclusion on top of the fence: NOT title WORD-MATCH any of\n{corestore, hypercore, seed cut, seed cuts, sparse seed, bootstrap peer, peer}. Effect: spec-match\n393 -> 383, i.e. ~10 p2p-substrate bugs left the lane. Members pick rev 2 up on their next\nscheduler:get_next; no member action required.\n\nThis local exclusion is a LABELLED TEMPORARY MITIGATION. The durable fix is to absorb the terms into\nthe shared P2P_LANE_EXCLUSION_TERMS source, filed as a change this wake. Remove the local list once\nthat lands — leaving it is precisely the per-fleet drift the fence macro exists to prevent.\n\nIf you are handed an item that still looks like p2p substrate work, that is another fence gap: report\nit to the leader (su-b8422). Do not silently work it and do not silently drop it.\n\n### D-004 — Never force-release a claim on leader-brief state alone — verify holder liveness from a fresh heartbeat\nDate: 2026-08-09\nEarned by my own error 2026-08-08T23:59Z. I force-released EI-19930415891533620 from\n`s-1786232435785-b745f2e3`, judging it dead from three leader-brief signals that agreed with each other:\n`sessionState:\"recorded\"`, `stalled:true`, `lastProgressAt:null`, ~8 min after claim. The holder was\nALIVE and closed the item with committed evidence 8 minutes later.\n\nBINDING on this fleet:\n1. Do NOT force-release on leader-brief/presence LABELS. Before any `force:true`, establish liveness\n   from a fresh `coord_presence` heartbeat, or `coord:send` the holder and wait one cycle.\n2. `lastProgressAt: null` is NOT evidence of a stall inside the first work cycle — it is simply the\n   state of a claim whose holder has not checkpointed yet. Most healthy claims look like this early.\n3. Agreement among several WEAK signals is not strength. All three of mine derived from the same\n   presence snapshot, so they could not independently corroborate each other. Prefer one decisive\n   check over three correlated ones.\n4. Releasing a live peer's claim is the \"never contest a live peer's claim\" rail, and it is exactly what\n   the `papercusp-reclaim-stalled` reconciler is held behind an owner-authority dark flag to prevent.\n   A leader doing it by hand is not exempt from the reasoning that gated it.\n\nGenuinely dead holders still get reclaimed — this raises the evidence bar, it does not forbid the action.\n\n### D-005 — 2026-08-11 restart uses a visible 10-member Codex Luna/max fleet under the existing non-P2P lane\nDate: 2026-08-11\nOwner Avi directed this drain restart on 2026-08-11. Leader is su-f4a05ec2 on fleet nonp2p-bug-drain. Route: 10 visible desktop Codex members, model gpt-5.6-luna at max effort, default system ChatGPT account (gateway skipped), warm carry. The queue boundary remains scheduler claim spec nonp2p-bug-drain: kind=bug, server p2p-lane fence, plus D-003 storage-substrate exclusions until the shared fence absorbs them. Members self-pull only; no id hand-assignment. Completion evidence follows D-001. Control work is WI-37891.\n\n### D-006 — D-005 fleet-slug correction: use a fresh Luna/max roster, not the paused inherited roster\nDate: 2026-08-11\nSupersedes only D-005s fleet-slug choice; its route, model, account, carry, lane, and completion rules remain binding. A fresh leader brief showed nonp2p-bug-drain still has nine inherited paused/warm members plus this leader. Reusing that slug would make launch-on-plan treat the requested 10-seat target as already full and would mix prior models/headless state with the owners requested 10 visible gpt-5.6-luna:max agents. This run therefore uses fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-0811 with its own pre-spawn claim spec, preserving the same p2p fence + D-003 exclusions.\n\n### D-007 — Codex max means runtime max; never silently normalize it to xhigh\nDate: 2026-08-11\nOwner Avi observed the first canary running xhigh despite requesting gpt-5.6-luna:max. The launch argv was correct, but psu-launcher.mjs explicitly rewrote max to xhigh; harness-invoke-once and the Codex gateway bridge duplicated the same stale clamp. Codex CLI 0.147.0 was live-probed with model_reasoning_effort=max and reported reasoning effort: max, then returned MAX_OK. EI-20183699243827812 removes the clamp on all three paths with 651 targeted tests green. Corrected canary process 2344557/2344634 is live with -c model_reasoning_effort=\"max\". The xhigh canary has a cooperative stand-down and must not count toward the final ten-member roster.\n\n### D-008 — Leader reclaim correction: EI-201835 release was wrong\nDate: 2026-08-11\nI force-released EI-20183578042173147 after relying on stale holder memory from the killed xhigh canary. Live state had already reassigned it to su-5e4bf34b-5a54-4d89-9a08-beab3d345105, so the release violated D-004. Correction: the live member was woken and told to reclaim immediately; going forward every reclaim reads the item writer/current assignee at action time and never relies on an earlier roster snapshot.\n\n### D-009 — Seed-cut keychain identity must use the parent real hostname across the bwrap UTS boundary\nDate: 2026-08-11\nWI-37894 root cause: the parent decrypts the hive key using the real host fallback identity, but the bwrap child changes UTS hostname to papercusp-build before keychain decryption, so getHostname()-derived AES material changes and authentication fails. The child already carries PAPERCUSP_SEED_REAL_HOSTNAME for the identity guard. Ruling: reuse that narrowly-scoped trusted parent value for keychain fallback derivation inside the seed-cut child, add a regression proving decrypt works across --unshare-uts/--hostname, and keep the seed identity guard strict. Do not weaken the guard, reuse dirty corestore bytes, or make arbitrary ambient hostname overrides globally authoritative.\n\n### D-010 — Default scheduler pulls apply the shared p2p safety fence\nDate: 2026-08-11\nFor scheduler:get_next callers whose resolved claim-spec source is `default`, apply a fresh `buildP2pLaneFence()` to the effective pull spec before querying and post-claim validation. Keep explicitly authored per-bee/fleet specs authoritative and unchanged, and preserve default spec provenance (`default-fixed-ordering@0`). This prevents unscoped single-box agents from repeatedly claiming the p2p/federation lane while allowing a p2p fleet to opt in through its authored spec. A cheap independent check if it matters later: compare codex-session scheduler pull counts against presence liveness.\nRelated: P-206\n\n### D-072 — A delta-sweep umbrella clusters symptoms, not causes — re-derive each member from live source before accepting its shared framing or building its proposed remedy\nDate: 2026-09-02\nRULING (applies to every agent draining this lane, not just the item that produced it): when a work-item was minted by `system:work-item-admission-delta-sweep` and asserts a \"common mechanism\" across N member reports, treat that mechanism as a HYPOTHESIS. Fixed by scoring an unrecognized key at the depth of the key it names; both members now emit only `Unrecognized key: \"<theirs>\"`, which is verbatim what EI-22063684320590166 requested.\n\nCONSEQUENCE, and why this is a ruling rather than a note. Accepting the umbrella's framing leads to a specific WRONG FIX: adding `source_ref` / `ttlDays` / `since` / `until` as compatibility aliases to satisfy stale prose. The `?` marker means \"run the re-check before relying on it\" — it is an INSTRUCTION TO THE READER, not a finding. But it renders as prose inside an authoritative-looking terminal recommendation, and each successor read the recommendation, not the marker. The prediction was never re-run by anyone. Worse, an unverified prediction of INACCESSIBILITY is self-fulfilling in a way an ordinary wrong claim is not: it tells the next agent the probe is impossible, so the one action that would falsify it is exactly the action it discourages. Cost here: 3 agents, 12 days, 0 files, on a row that needed one grep.\n\nRULING — three parts, all cheap:\n1. NEVER inherit a `?` check as settled. Before acting on any carried checkpoint recommendation, look at the markers: a `?` row is an open question the previous holder is HANDING you, and the recommendation resting on it is only as good as that unrun probe.\n2. A claim of the form \"this requires <access/capability> I do not have\" is a claim about the PRIOR AGENT'S PROBE SET, never about the system (this is the base playbook's sudo -n lesson in a different costume). Falsify it by locating the writer before believing it — an alert/status/metric writer named in a row is nearly always local and greppable.\n3. Do NOT re-park such a row needs-human on the strength of the inherited note. EI-21240881678776697 — the very row I called permanently lost — is `local` + `committed` + countsTowardBurnDown. So federation re-authoring is REVERSIBLE: a row can flip local -> remote (turning its committed close into `proposed`) and later flip BACK, at which point the close settles itself. My observation at 21:22:37Z was accurate for that instant; the error was reading a snapshot of a mutable field as a terminal property. Exactly the failure this plan keeps re-learning — I inferred a CATEGORY (\"permanent\") from one reading of a value that changes under you.\n\nTHE COST OF THE ERROR RAN BOTH WAYS, which is why it is worth a decision rather than a note. It would have understated burn-down by parking two genuinely-committed closes in a residue table, AND it planted a standing \"do NOT retry\" instruction that would stop a successor from ever re-checking them.\n\nRULING.\n1. There is no \"permanently stranded\" class. The correct description is TRANSIENT: a close is `proposed` WHILE its row is remote-authored, and it may settle on its own when federation re-authors it back.\n2. NEVER write a proposed/remote row off as residue on a single reading. Re-check origin/authority at ship time, when the residue table is GENERATED (which is already the rule — this is one more reason it must be generated from live fields and never hand-authored from a remembered list).\n3. The two still-proposed rows are NOT to be re-sent by hand — a remote-authored row genuinely refuses a local write right now, so that guidance stands — but they are pending-recovery, not lost. Both re-federated at 21:51:52Z, minutes before this reading, so their disposition is simply not yet settled.\n4. The commit-BEFORE-complete ordering adopted this wake remains correct and is now better motivated: it avoids the `proposed` state entirely rather than depending on a recovery that may or may not come.\n\nFalsifier: re-run the query above. If EI-21240881678776697 or EI-21712103510622160 reads origin=remote / authority=proposed again, then recovery is not stable either and this ruling needs a third revision naming the oscillation.\n\n### D-094 — D-093: a TOOL-REJECTION row must be probed on BOTH doors (:3070 deployed vs :3170 source) before it is called live or fixed-since\nDate: 2026-09-02\n⚠ CITE THIS AS D-094. The obvious probe is to re-issue the call and see whether it still fails. That probe is UNSOUND ON ITS OWN, in BOTH directions:\n\n  - Re-issuing through your normal MCP door measures the DEPLOYED operator, whose code can be many hours behind the tree. A defect already fixed in source still reproduces perfectly, so the row reads LIVE and an agent \"fixes\" what is already fixed.\n  - Conversely a row can read fixed on staging while the deployed operator still hurts every caller.\n\nNeither reading is wrong about what it measured; both are wrong about the ROW. The deployed-vs-source distinction is invisible in the error text, which is why five agents filed five rows over 15 days for ONE defect.\n\nRULING. For any row whose evidence is a tool-call rejection: run the reported shape on BOTH doors before assigning a disposition.\n  - deployed: your ordinary MCP call.\n  - source:   node scripts/mcp-call.mjs <server:verb> --json-file <args.json> --client <your-su-id> --port 3170\nThen dispose on the PAIR: same failure on both = LIVE defect, fix it. Fails deployed, clean on :3170 = FIXED IN SOURCE — close it with the fix commit AND the deploy position, and state in the close that a re-probe on the deployed operator will still show the old message, so the family is not re-filed a sixth time.
