If the deployed and :3170 doors return the SAME message for a shape this decision claims differs, the deploy has advanced past 8e90f350 and this decision's worked example is spent — the RULING still stands, only its example expires.\nRelated: P-206\n\n### D-095 — A curated NAME-SET whose lookup normalizes must STORE normalized keys — 9 of 38 READ_ONLY_TOOLS entries were silently unreachable, and the guard that should have caught it asserted a universal in its name while testing one case\nDate: 2026-09-02\nFound while disposing EI-21677017866028949 (a cohort row filed 08-28 as a one-off \"transport reset\"). It was not a transient. It is a live, fleet-wide defect, and the two instruments I reached for first BOTH reported it absent.\n\nTHE DEFECT. apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.ts classifies a forward as 'readonly' — eligible for a bounded post-connect socket-error replay — when every tools/call names a READ_ONLY_TOOLS verb. The set stored RAW curated verbs, but the lookup normalized the incoming name: normalizeMcpName (libs/generic/tooldef/src/tool-projection.ts:1554) lowercases, strips an `mcp__<server>__` prefix, and folds `[:_.-]+` to ':'. So any entry containing an UNDERSCORE normalized to a key absent from the set and could never match. `work_items:get` did not match ITSELF.\n\nMeasured (2026-09-02T22:36Z, npx tsx importing the real set + real normalizer): 9 of 38 entries unreachable — work_items:get, work_items:list, work_items:claimable, dev:pg_query, dev:pipeline_position, dev:service_health, dev:listening_ports, dev:build_status, dev:rate_governor_status. Both `work_items:get` and `mcp__papercusp-su__work_items_get` normalize to `work:items:get` → NOMATCH. `loop:status` → `loop:status` → MATCH.\n\nWHY IT SURVIVED, and this is the transferable part. The 9 dead entries are exactly the multi-word ones; the ~29 live entries are underscore-free. So the mechanism worked perfectly for every name anyone happened to test. EI-21844731354927961 (closed 08-30) ADDED loop:status and events:status to this set, verified them, and closed green — both underscore-free, so its verification could not have failed. The defect was invisible precisely to the work aimed at it.\n\nTHE DETECTOR GAP (file the guard, not just the bug). proxy.test.ts carried a case named 'every call naming a READ_ONLY_TOOLS verb → \"readonly\"' that iterates NOTHING — it asserts one literal, `build:typecheck`, which is underscore-free. Its sibling 'entries are lowercase namespaced verbs' validates the STORED form with `/^[a-z0-9_-]+:[a-z0-9_-]+$/`, a regex that explicitly blesses the underscore while nothing checks that the stored form is REACHABLE by the lookup. A test whose NAME asserts a universal and whose BODY checks one instance is worse than no test: it occupies the slot the real guard would have filled.\n\nRULING. (1) A name-set compared against a normalized key STORES normalized keys, or derives a normalized lookup beside the curated list. Fixed by adding READ_ONLY_TOOLS_LOOKUP = new Set([...READ_ONLY_TOOLS].map(normalizeMcpName)) and pointing isReadOnlyToolCall at it; READ_ONLY_TOOLS stays the human-readable curated list the writer-exclusion guard reads. The two SIBLING sets in the same file — RESERVED_CONTROL_PLANE_TOOLS and CRITICAL_CONTINUATION_TOOLS — already `.map(normalizeMcpName)` and both contain work_items:get, which is what confirms normalizing is the intended pattern and this set simply omitted it. All three now normalize; the class is swept, not patched. (2) A guard over a curated collection ITERATES it. The replacement runs it.each over all 38 entries in BOTH the canonical and mcp__-mangled forms, so a new unreachable entry — or a change to normalizeMcpName that strands existing ones — fails at the guard.\n\nMeasured: npm run testing:run apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.test.ts + plans-search-reservation.test.ts → 271 passed / 0 failed. npm run lint:tsc -- --files=<both> → LINT_TSC_RESULT label=operator status=clean exit=0.\n\nMETHOD NOTE for the remaining drain, because both first instruments lied in the SAME direction. (a) harness_shared.tool_invocations showed ZERO occurrences of this class ever — because the recorder writes server-side and a reset that kills the upstream connection produces no row at all. An error ledger is blind to exactly the failures that destroy the connection carrying the report. (b) A hand-computed epoch bound (1788618116000) was ~4 days in the FUTURE, so a \"no occurrences since the proxy restart\" query returned a clean, positive-control-passing ZERO. That zero would have closed this row as fixed. Corrected to 1788272516000 it returned the row that falsified the hypothesis: EI-22071539448944763, a direct work_items:get outcome_unknown 35 minutes AFTER the restart. ALWAYS re-derive an epoch against D-074's pinned 1788048000000 = 2026-08-30T00:00:00Z before trusting a windowed absence.\n\nTHIRD DOOR (extends D-094). D-094 says probe deployed vs source. The MCP proxy is a THIRD door: pid 1759880 is a long-lived `tsx bin/mcp-proxy.ts` run from the STAGING tree that neither hot-reloads nor restarts on deploy (started 2026-09-01T14:21:56Z, elapsed 1d08h). Source, the release checkout, and this process can all disagree. Both open + unassigned.)\n\n## Measured state (2026-08-09)\n- BUILT + DEPLOYED: unified-agent-state-plane-2026-07-27 shipped; couple.ts/decouple.ts + all four\n  coord/coupl* modules present in the papercup-release checkout serving :3070.\n- Guidance reaches 6 of 5211 rendered launch contexts (the 6 = a 10s burst on ship day 2026-07-27 20:46).\n  The 2026-08-01 fix bb547168dc added it to papercusp-su-{engineer,power}.tools.md - a layer the su\n  launch-context render does not consume; renders come from blueprints/base/prompts/su.md, which has zero.\n- Adoption since ship day: coord:couple 7 (last 2026-07-27), coord:decouple 2, presence include_coupling\n  10/249 and 0 of 88 in 7d, topics:feed coupled 3/3, forYouBecause 1 of 3709 sends in 30d,\n  agent_couplings = 1 row, state=suppressed.\n- Live probe with 48 active agents: expanded:[] / expandedTotal:0.\n\n## The correctness defect (found while answering the owner)\nD-054 (2026-07-27, from the owner s own challenge) CUT `same-fleet`: set membership, not a pairwise\nrelation, O(n^2) in fleet size, redundant with fleetSlug already on every presence row. Build it, or record its retirement as a decision. — note: ← WI-37519 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Prove it\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Re-measure adoption AFTER delivery lands: couple/decouple call counts, include_coupling rate, and derived expanded[] non-empty rate across live callers. This is the acceptance test EI-19300253346703673 has failed since ship day. — note: ← WI-37522 released\n- **P-007** `done` Build the DEAD-DERIVED-SIGNAL DETECTOR that D-088 proposes and this plan twice needed: a per-relation firing count over a window, surfaced where a human sees it. A derived coupling relation computing ZERO edges across a whole window is either dead or gated behind an unreachable flag combination — and today NOTHING distinguishes \"signal is correct\" from \"signal never runs\". That gap cost `current_files` (real field, 119 live rows, zero populated) and then `holds-a-lock-on` (shipped, tested, documented, fired zero times for 12 days until P-004 fixed it). Both were found only by a human hand-querying live data; both were green in every test throughout. Acceptance: a relation at 0 firings over a window is REPORTED, not merely absent from a dashboard, and the check names WHICH relation. This also makes P-006's acceptance test automatable instead of a manual re-measure. Added 2026-08-09 under AUTO [owner:Avi 2026-08-09 \"finish implementing this plan yourself now\"] as the plan's remaining implementation work — P-006 itself is time-gated to 2026-08-16 by statistical power (D-090), not by effort. — note: ← WI-37537 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — correctness on the path that runs\n\n- **P-008** `done` EI-20042650315152947: pass coordinationDomain in readPeerRelations (coupling-divergence-stamp.ts) so heldFiles is wired on the coord:send divergence path — the only path that runs at volume. D-088/WI-37513 fixed this on coord:presence, which has 11 calls ever. Measured consequence: 38 holds-a-lock-on assertions all scored not-comparable, 13 of them AFTER that fix shipped. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-37739 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Move the P-007 derived-signal census `observe` sink onto the paths that execute (coupling-divergence-stamp.ts, and coupled-topics-read.ts while it survives). It is wired ONLY into presence.ts today, so 0 rows in tool_invocations have EVER carried metadata_json.derivedSignals — the instrument built to answer \"has this relation fired in production\" is attached to the surface that never runs. Without this the item above is unverifiable by the mechanism built to verify it. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-37740 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` DROP the shared-file derived signal + the current_files roster field (D-002 above). — note: ← WI-37741 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `todo` DROP topics:feed and coupled-topics-read.ts (D-002 above).\n- **P-012** `done` DEFAULT include_coupling ON for the roster-derived signals; keep the querying legs behind detail (D-002 above). importance: high — note: ← WI-37742 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `todo` Re-measure after the two urgent items land: if holds-a-lock-on / blocks-me / blocked-by-me still produce zero edges, the relations are unfalsifiable and should be cut from the ASSERTED forYouBecause vocabulary too, not just the derivation. blocked-by: P-008\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The coupling drop was a SYMPTOM: all five shared base notes were silently absent from every interactive su render, because the bundle borrowed another feature's marker as its anchor\nDate: 2026-08-09\nMEASURED 2026-08-09, primary evidence, not inference.\n\n`injectSharedBaseNotes` (desktop-install/papercusp-files.ts) projects FIVE clauses authored\nonce in code into every prompt base: deploy-pipeline, wait-loop, peer-wake, COUPLING and\nstate-plane. It anchored on PROJECT_GUIDE_MARKER, which ALSO served as its \"is this a real su\nplaybook?\" test — one marker doing two unrelated jobs.\n\nThat test was sound only while the LEGACY base (apps/operator/prompts/papercusp-su-*.tools.md)\nwas live; it carries the marker. When SU_BLUEPRINT_PERSONA made the BLUEPRINT base\n(libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/su.md) live, the anchor went with it:\nmeasured, that base carries AUTO-MODE=1, WIRE-SCHEMAS=1, COORD-LEGEND=1, RESULT-DOOR=1 and\nPROJECT-GUIDE=0. The injector hit `if (!text.includes(PROJECT_GUIDE_MARKER)) return text` and\nshipped NOTHING — silently, on every interactive render.\n\nThe discriminator that proves it (live render session-14589.md): every section spliced at a\nmarker the blueprint base DOES carry landed (## AUTO mode, ## Wire schemas, ## Coordination\nglyph legend, the result-door section). NONE of the five injected notes did. Renders carrying\nthe coupling clause: 6 of 5211, and those 6 are a ten-second burst at 2026-07-27T20:46 on\nship day.\n\n#### Ruling\n\nPOSITION and ELIGIBILITY are separate questions and must be decided separately.\n  - ELIGIBILITY (\"does this base get the bundle?\") is computed by the CALLER from the ORIGINAL\n    base, before any splice consumes the markers: a base carrying PROJECT-GUIDE **or** AUTO-MODE\n    is a real su playbook. Minimal/test bases carry neither and still get nothing.\n  - POSITION is an optional hint. SHARED_BASE_NOTES_MARKER places the bundle exactly;\n    PROJECT_GUIDE_MARKER keeps the legacy `.tools.md` placement; with neither, the notes are\n    APPENDED rather than dropped.\n\nThe general rule, which is the transferable part: the splice contract \"absent marker => leave\nthe section out\" is correct for an OPTIONAL section and catastrophic for a MANDATORY one. A\nbundle that must always ship may not borrow another feature's marker as its anchor — that is an\nundeclared dependency, and it breaks silently and totally.\n\n#### Binding on implementers\n\nNO marker was added to the blueprint `.md`, deliberately. Prompts are decoupled from the release\ngate and go live immediately, while operator-core waits for a deploy — so a base edit only the\nNEW code understands would leak a raw `<!-- PAPERCUSP-SU:SHARED-BASE-NOTES -->` into every live\nrender during the window between them. Verified both directions against the real base: staging\ncode => all five notes, no leak; deployed release code => behaviour UNCHANGED, no leak. The fix\ntherefore activates on deploy with zero regression window. Do not \"finish\" this by adding the\nmarker until the code is deployed.\n\nVERIFY ANY FIX HERE AGAINST A FRESH ~/.papercusp/launch-context/session-*.md RENDER. Checking\nthe source .md is what made the 2026-08-01 prompt fix (bb547168dc) look done while changing\nnothing measurable: it added coord:couple to the .tools.md sources, which the live render does\nnot read, and adoption stayed at exactly zero for the following 8 days.\n\n### D-002 — P-002 ruling: the derived `same-fleet` edge is removed; the AUTHORED relation stays but becomes undiffable — and the 20 red fixtures are re-pointed, not deleted\nDate: 2026-08-09\nD-054 cut `same-fleet` as a COUPLING relation. It shipped anyway. Removed 2026-08-09 from:\n  - coord/couplings.ts DERIVED_COUPLING_RELATIONS (tombstone comment left in place)\n  - coord/coupling-derivation.ts deriveCouplingsFromRoster (emit block + the `myFleet` local)\n\nRULING 1 — `same-fleet` survives in FOR_YOU_BECAUSE_RELATIONS (the AUTHORED vocabulary), but\nits divergence rule flips to { confirmedBy: [], absenceIsInformative: false }: the same shape\nas `owns`. Two vocabularies share this token and only ONE of them is what D-054 ruled on. A\nsender may still say \"I am telling you because we share a fleet\"; that assertion simply is not\ndiffable against a graph that no longer computes the relation. Removing the emitter WITHOUT\nthis flip is the trap: `confirmedBy` becomes unsatisfiable, so `absenceIsInformative: true`\nwould score every correctly-asserted same-fleet as a DIVERGENCE — manufacturing sender-\ninaccuracy out of a signal we ourselves stopped computing. Chosen over deleting the token from\nthe authored enum because it is smaller, breaks no agent-facing vocabulary, and reuses a\npattern this file already documents.\n\nRULING 2 — the 20 fixtures that broke are RE-POINTED, not deleted. Counts: 9\ncoupling-derivation.test.ts, 4 couplings.test.ts, 4 coupling-divergence-stamp.test.ts, 3\nmessage-fields.test.ts. Uniform failure shape: expected\n[{relation:\"same-fleet\", because:\"same fleet (alpha)\"}], received []. They used same-fleet\nonly as a convenient two-row fixture; what they actually assert — union accumulation, dedup,\nemission ORDER, fail-soft-per-leg, never-widens — is all still real behaviour. Re-point each\nto a signal that still exists (awaitingEventKey => `awaits`, overlapping held locks =>\n`holds-a-lock-on`, recentPartners => `coord-exchange`). Deleting them would silently drop\ncoverage of behaviour that never changed, which is how a removal quietly becomes a regression.\n\nRULING 3 — one test IS genuinely obsolete: coupling-derivation.test.ts \"couples peers in the\nsame fleet, naming the fleet\". Replace it with the INVERSE assertion — two rows sharing a\nfleetSlug derive NO edge. That negative is the recurrence guard for D-054, and its absence is\nwhy the vetoed edge survived 12 days with six tests actively protecting it.\n\n### D-055 — Removing a signal turns its tests GREEN-BUT-VACUOUS and RED-ONLY-AT-TYPECHECK — re-pointing must find both, and the red set finds neither\nDate: 2026-08-09\nRecorded 2026-08-09 on completing P-002. D-002 ruling 2 said to re-point the 20 red fixtures rather\ndelete them, and that was right — but the RED SET WAS NOT THE WHOLE BLAST RADIUS. Cutting a relation\nfrom a vocabulary damages tests in three ways, and the test runner reports only one of them.\n\n1. RED (20 tests) — the ones asserting the removed signal fires. Found by running the suite.\n\n2. GREEN BUT NOW VACUOUS (4 tests) — INVISIBLE to the runner, and the dangerous class. A test whose\n   SETUP used the removed signal still passes, because its expectation was already an empty/negative\n   result; the antecedent silently stopped holding, so it now asserts nothing. Measured here:\n     - coupling-derivation.test.ts 'SUPPRESSION STILL WINS over a live derivation' — expected [], and\n       the derivation now returns [] on its own. It could no longer fail no matter what suppression did.\n     - coupling-divergence-stamp.test.ts 'drops broadcast and audience-selector recipients',\n       'returns no stamps when the coupling read throws', 'returns no stamps for an unresolvable sender'\n       — all three asserted [], and an uncomparable asserted relation now short-circuits the cost gate\n       BEFORE the audience rule / the reader / the sender check is ever reached.\n   Each was re-pointed to a signal that still exists. The suppression test additionally now asserts its\n   own antecedent (`expect(derived).toHaveLength(1)`) before suppressing, so it fails loudly instead of\n   evaporating the next time its fixture's signal is cut.\n\n3. RED ONLY AT TYPECHECK (1 file, 5 sites) — coupled-topics.test.ts built `DerivedCoupling` fixtures\n   with `relation: 'same-fleet' as const`. `DerivedCouplingRelation` is `(typeof\n   DERIVED_COUPLING_RELATIONS)[number]`, so removing the array entry removed the type member — but\n   vitest does not typecheck, so that file was GREEN in the suite and would have red the fleet gate.\n   Four more sites in message-fields.test.ts passed `['same-fleet']` as the COMPUTED array with the same\n   defect. None of these appeared in the 20.\n\n#### Ruling\n\nWhen a token is removed from a vocabulary that is BOTH a runtime constant AND the source of a derived\ntype, the completion bar is THREE checks, not one:\n  (a) the suite is green;\n  (b) `lint:tsc --files=<every file you touched>` is clean — vitest cannot see class 3, and\n      `test:affected` will not select the offending file because your diff never touched it;\n  (c) every test that MENTIONED the removed token has been re-read to confirm its antecedent still\n      holds — grep the token, do not trust the red set. A test that went from meaningful to vacuous\n      reports as a pass, so the runner actively conceals class 2.\n\nGENERAL FORM, since this is not specific to couplings: a removal's blast radius is `grep <token>`, never\n`the failing set`. The failing set is the subset whose expectations were POSITIVE; the tests whose\nexpectations were already negative go quiet instead of red, and they are exactly the tests guarding the\nfail-soft, suppression and access-boundary properties you least want silently unguarded.\n\n### D-056 — P-003 was ALREADY SATISFIED — it was authored from a checkpoint-harvest POSTMORTEM and read as a TODO; and presence `expanded[]` deliberately stays prose-only\nDate: 2026-08-09\nVerified 2026-08-09 by reading the writer at every hop, not by trusting the item text.\n\nP-003 says the typed discriminant does not reach the consumer: *\"resolveCoupledPeers joins every\nderived signal for a peer into one prose derivedBecause, so the discriminant is erased exactly one\nlayer after being introduced.\"* THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE. Measured chain, producer to consumer:\n  1. `coupling-derivation.ts` — every emit site sets BOTH `relation` and `because` from the same branch.\n  2. `couplings.ts:167` — `CoupledPeer.derivedRelations?: DerivedCouplingRelation[]`; built at :314-348,\n     deduped, in emission order, and attached BESIDE the joined prose rather than replaced by it.\n  3. `coupling-divergence-stamp.ts:193` — `byPeer.set(p.ownerId, p.derivedRelations ?? [])`.\n  4. `tools/send.ts:804` — `resolveCouplingDivergenceStamps(...)` on the LIVE `coord:send` path.\nAsserted end-to-end by `couplings.test.ts` (\"carries the TYPED relations through the join, deduped, in\nemission order\") and `coupling-derivation.test.ts` (\"the typed half survives END-TO-END, derivation\nthrough union\"). 142 passed / 0 failed across the coupling suite on 2026-08-09.\n\nWHY THE ITEM EXISTED ANYWAY, because the failure mode is reusable. Its cited source,\nEI-19280867283320939, is `lane: 'observation'`, `origin: 'checkpoint-harvest'` — a RETROSPECTIVE\nwritten by the agent who had just BUILT D-087, describing traps it had already fixed (\"the fix that\nmattered was not the one the last wake specified\"; \"a discriminant that does not survive to the\nconsumer is not a fix\"). Harvested into a plan item, a postmortem's present-tense description of a\nbug reads exactly like an open defect. **A harvested observation states the problem it SOLVED, not a\nproblem that remains** — so when an item's evidence is a checkpoint-harvest observation, verify the\ndefect still reproduces BEFORE planning the fix. Cost here was one verification pass; the cost of\nmissing it is re-implementing shipped work and \"fixing\" a green path.\n\n#### Ruling\n\nP-003 is CLOSED as already-satisfied. No code change.\n\nThe one seam the chain does NOT carry tokens through is `coupled-expansion.ts:159`, which renders each\npresence `expanded[]` row with `expandedBecause` prose and no relation array. That is DELIBERATE and\nstays: `expandedBecause` is P-013's contract field and its consumer is an agent READING the roster,\nnot code branching on it — the machine consumer (the divergence metric) already takes the typed\nchannel one layer up. Adding a per-entry token array to a bounded-25 block would cost payload and\ntool-prompt weight for no consumer that exists. If a consumer ever needs to BRANCH on the signal in\n`expanded[]`, add it then, and cite this decision when reversing it.\n\n### D-088 — P-004 RULING: the `holds-a-lock-on` signal is wired on `include_coupling` — it had NEVER fired in production, because it silently inherited an unrelated flag's gate\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-004 asked: wire the lock-hold signal on the DEFAULT presence path, or state why it stays\ndetail-gated. MEASURED FIRST, then ruled — and the measurement changed the answer.\n\n#### The finding\n\n`coord:presence` resolved `coordinationDomain` under `include_detail` ALONE. The lock store is keyed\nby that domain, so `couplingSourcesFor` arms its `heldFiles` leg only when it is supplied — meaning\nthe `holds-a-lock-on` derivation required the INTERSECTION of `include_coupling` AND `include_detail`.\n\nMeasured 2026-08-09 against `harness_shared.tool_invocations`, workspace-scoped, over the FULL\nretained history (2026-07-26 → 2026-08-09):\n\n  | flags passed                        | calls |\n  |-------------------------------------|-------|\n  | neither                             |  243  |\n  | `include_coupling` alone            |   11  |\n  | `include_detail` alone              |    9  |\n  | BOTH                                |    0  |  ← the row does not exist\n\nSo the signal has fired ZERO times since it shipped. That is not a tuning problem, it is a dead\nfeature — and it is the SECOND time this exact thing happened to the file dimension of coupling:\n`current_files` was already found real-but-always-empty (119 live rows, zero populated,\nEI-18772330418885814), and `holds-a-lock-on` was introduced specifically to replace it as \"the only\nAUTOMATIC 'this agent is on this file' signal\". The replacement was just as dead, for a different\nreason, and both were green in every test.\n\n#### Ruling\n\nWIRED ON `include_coupling`. `presenceNeedsCoordinationDomain(args)` (coupling-sources.ts) now owns\nthe rule — true when EITHER flag is set — and `presence.ts` resolves the domain through it. The\nroster lane stays gated on `include_detail` alone, so the base rows remain byte-identical whether\ncoupling is on or off (D-053 preserved: widening the lock READ must not widen the roster).\n\nThe original objection is answered rather than overridden. It read: *\"it must never become a reason\nto open a second DB connection on the default presence path.\"* Verified false as stated — `getTxPool()`\nis a MEMOIZED module-level singleton behind ~29 call sites (every `locks:*` verb), so it is already\nwarm in any operator serving lock traffic; nothing new is opened. What IS real is its `max: 10` cap on\na pool that has saturated before (2026-07-26: 34 idle `su-lock-tx` connections, second-largest\nconsumer of a 343/512 `max_connections`). That cost is now paid only on the opt-in coupling branch —\n11 calls across the entire retained window, not the 243-call default path — bounded to\n`rosterOwnerIds` and fail-soft per leg. The default lean read still touches the lock pool not at all.\n\n#### The transferable rule\n\nA GATE THAT IS CORRECT FOR ITS FIRST CONSUMER BECOMES A SILENT `AND` THE MOMENT A SECOND CONSUMER\nREUSES IT. `include_detail` was the right gate for detail's held-files lane. Coupling's lock\nderivation later needed the same INPUT for an unrelated REASON, reused the same gate, and thereby\nacquired a precondition nobody chose and nothing documents. Nothing errors; every test over injected\nfixtures passes, because the fixtures supply the domain directly; the signal simply never fires.\n\nGive each consumer its OWN reason to need an input — a named predicate, not an `if` inside a handler.\nAn `if` in a handler is unreachable by unit tests, which is exactly why the wrong one survived.\n`coupling-sources.test.ts` now pins the predicate from BOTH directions (three cases forcing true,\nthree forcing false), so neither the old rule (`!!include_detail`) nor a constant `true` can pass.\n\n#### Detection, not just the fix\n\nThe reason this was invisible for 12 days is that no test and no metric distinguishes \"signal is\ncorrect\" from \"signal never runs\". Both prior instances were found only by someone hand-querying live\ndata. P-006 (re-measure adoption after delivery lands) is the natural home for a standing check: a\nderived-signal firing count, per relation, over a window — a relation that computes 0 edges across a\nwhole window is either dead or the flag combination gating it is unreachable, and either way a human\nshould see it.\n\n### D-089 — P-005 RULING: the fifth edge (\"attempted to claim an item this agent holds\") is RETIRED as a derived coupling — the need it names is already served synchronously, and the base it would extend is unproven\nDate: 2026-08-09\nD-054 required a fifth derived edge, added by D-053: *\"attempted to claim an item this agent holds\"*.\nIt was never implemented. P-005 asked to build it or retire it. RETIRED, on three measured grounds.\n\n#### 1. The acute need is ALREADY SERVED, synchronously, at the moment of conflict\n\nA refused claim does not merely say no. `plans:set-status` (set-status.ts:574-577) returns\n`{ error:'claim_conflict', reason, holder, holderContext, hint }`, where the hint reads *\"the item is\nbeing worked by a live peer — coordinate with the holder (coord:send) or pick another item;\nfleet:assignments { plan } shows who holds what\"*. So the agent that NEEDS to act — the one blocked,\nright now — already gets the holder's identity, live context, and the exact verb to reach them, at\nthe instant it matters. A coupling edge would deliver the same fact LATER, to an agent that has\nalready been told.\n\nThat leaves exactly one genuine gap: the REVERSE direction — the HOLDER never learns that someone\ntried. That is real and worth something (it is the \"who is waiting on me\" asymmetry `blocked-by-me`\nexists to serve). But it is a much narrower claim than \"the fifth edge is missing\", and it does not\njustify a new durable signal on its own.\n\n#### 2. It needs a NEW durable surface — the data does not exist\n\n`claim_conflict` is a REJECTION CODE returned to a caller and then forgotten. It is persisted\nnowhere: no table, no event. `work-items-events.ts` emits claimed / claimable / released / blocked /\nstatus — there is no conflict kind. Building the edge therefore means emitting a new event at every\nrefusal site, retaining it, adding a windowed read beside `fetchRecentCoordPartners`, and a\nderivation leg with its own tests. Reuse-first says a new durable surface needs a stronger warrant\nthan this one has today.\n\n#### 3. The base it would extend is UNPROVEN — and its fourth edge was dead on arrival\n\nMeasured 2026-08-09 over the full retained `tool_invocations` history: `include_coupling` was passed\non 11 `coord:presence` calls, total. And per D-088, `holds-a-lock-on` — already shipped, already\ntested, already documented as \"the only automatic this-agent-is-on-this-file signal\" — had fired\nZERO times in production until it was fixed today. Adding a FIFTH edge to a set whose FOURTH never\nran, on a surface almost nobody calls, optimises the wrong end of the problem. The reason nobody\ncalls it is P-001: the coupling guidance reached 6 of 5211 rendered launch contexts, so agents were\nnever told the capability exists.\n\n#### Ruling\n\nRETIRED as a derived coupling edge. D-053's requirement is discharged by this decision rather than by\ncode. `DERIVED_COUPLING_RELATIONS` stays at six tokens.\n\nREOPEN IT when BOTH hold — stated concretely so this is a decidable test, not a vague \"later\":\n  (a) P-001's delivery has landed AND P-006 shows `include_coupling` adoption materially non-trivial\n      (a floor of ~50 calls/week is a reasonable bar against today's 11-in-two-weeks);\n  (b) the reverse-direction need is EVIDENCED — a holder actually reporting they were unaware of\n      contention, or a measured rate of repeated conflicts on the same (item, pair).\nIf (b) arrives WITHOUT (a), the cheaper fix is almost certainly to notify the holder at the moment of\nrefusal (a `coord:send` on the conflict path), not to add a coupling edge — coupling is a RELEVANCE\nre-ranking, and a one-shot contention event is better served by a one-shot notification.\n\n#### The transferable rule\n\nBEFORE BUILDING A SIGNAL THAT TELLS SOMEONE SOMETHING, CHECK WHAT THE SYNCHRONOUS PATH ALREADY TOLD\nTHEM. The fifth edge sounded obviously valuable for a year because \"agents contending for the same\nitem should know about each other\" is obviously true — but the contending agent was already being\nhanded the holder, the holder's context, and the verb to reach them. Restating a fact the error path\ndelivers better is not a feature; it is duplicated surface with an extra hop and a new table.\n\n### D-090 — P-006: the post-delivery adoption read is UNDERPOWERED and must NOT be reported as a win — baseline and re-measure pre-registered here instead\nDate: 2026-08-09\nMeasured 2026-08-09 ~15:35Z, 10.5h after delivery landed (cut 2026-08-09T05:05Z, the render cutover\nestablished in P-001). `harness_shared.tool_invocations`, workspace papercusp-workspace.\n\n  | tool                              | pre (309h)      | post (10.5h)    |\n  |-----------------------------------|-----------------|-----------------|\n  | coord:couple                      | 7 (0.023/h)     | 3 (0.286/h)     |\n  | coord:decouple                    | 2 (0.006/h)     | 0               |\n  | coord:presence include_coupling   | 11 (0.036/h)    | 0               |\n\nThe `coord:couple` rate ratio is 12.4×. **DO NOT REPORT THAT AS THE RESULT.** n = 3 events. At the\npre-delivery rate the 10.5h window expects ~0.24 couple calls and ~0.38 include_coupling calls, so\nBOTH the apparent 12× jump and the two zeros are entirely consistent with pure Poisson noise and no\nchange whatsoever. A ratio computed from 3 events is not evidence, and a 0 from an expected-0.38\nwindow is not a regression. This is exactly the shape this plan's own D-055 and the persona rule\nwarn about — a suspiciously clean number that is an artifact of the denominator, not a finding.\n\n#### Ruling\n\nP-006 STAYS OPEN. The measurement was taken, and its honest verdict is \"too early\". What IS delivered\nnow is the pre-registration, so the eventual read cannot be anchored after the fact:\n\n  - BASELINE (frozen, pre-delivery, 2026-07-26 → 2026-08-09T05:05Z, 309h):\n      coord:couple 7 · coord:decouple 2 · coord:presence+include_coupling 11.\n  - RE-MEASURE NOT BEFORE 2026-08-16 (7 days post-delivery, ~168h) — long enough that the\n    pre-rate predicts ~4 couple and ~6 include_coupling calls, so a real lift is separable from noise.\n  - PRE-REGISTERED THRESHOLD: call it adoption if `coord:couple` ≥ 20 in the 7-day post window\n    (≥5× the ~4 expected at the null rate) AND `include_coupling` ≥ 20. Below that, report NO EFFECT\n    rather than a ratio.\n  - ALSO MEASURE, and this is the one that matters most: the derived `expanded[]` NON-EMPTY rate.\n    Per D-088 the `holds-a-lock-on` leg only started working today, so any pre-delivery expanded[]\n    figure is a measurement of three legs, not four — the two eras are not comparing the same system.\n\n#### Why this item cannot simply be closed\n\nEI-19300253346703673 has failed since ship day, and the reason was never that the number was bad —\nit was that nobody could act on it. Closing P-006 on a 10.5h window would convert \"we do not know\nyet\" into \"we measured it\", which is strictly worse than leaving it open: the next reader would\ninherit a 12× headline with n=3 behind it and no reason to doubt it.\n\n### D-091 — P-007 RULING: the dead-derived-signal detector ships as a FOURTH plane probe, and records `armed` separately from `emitted` — a bare firing count could not have caught either incident\nDate: 2026-08-09\nDate: 2026-08-09\n\nD-088 asked for \"a derived-signal firing count, per relation, over a window\". Built,\nwith one deliberate departure, explained below.\n\n#### Why a fourth probe rather than a new surface\n\nA derived signal slips past all three existing reachability probes AT ONCE, which is\nwhy both incidents were found by a human hand-querying live data rather than by\nanything automated: check-plane-producers asks \"is the FIELD written?\" and is blind\n(a derived relation has no column); check-declared-consumed asks \"is it READ in\nsource?\" and is green; check-plane-adoption asks \"does an AGENT call it?\" and is\ngreen. Three green ticks over a dead signal.\n\nSo `check-derived-signal-firings.mjs` JOINS that family — same file shape, same\npure-predicate + vitest-sibling split, same `no-data`-is-neither-pass-nor-fail\ndiscipline — rather than becoming a new surface. It adds NO table and NO write path:\nthe census rides `tool_invocations.metadata_json`, which already exists.\n\nVERIFIED, not assumed, that a handler's key SURVIVES: `coord:orient`'s\nhandler-emitted `deltaServed` coexists with the dispatcher's own uiClientId/format/\nrequestOrigin on 491 of 606 rows — handler metadata MERGES. `coord:presence` already\ncarries metadata on 75/75 calls, so the sink exists on the handler instrumented.\n\n#### The departure: `armed` is recorded separately from `emitted`\n\nA bare firing count collapses two situations with OPPOSITE remedies, and this plan\nhit one of each. `holds-a-lock-on`: the input leg was never WIRED IN (its gate\nsilently required two flags) — a code defect. `current_files`: the leg was wired and\nconsulted every run, and the field it reads has no producer — an upstream defect.\nBoth read as `0 edges`.\n\nSo the census records per relation per run: `armed` (was the input supplied at all),\n`inputs` (how much it delivered), `edges` (how many survived the roster access\nboundary to reach a caller). Six verdicts follow — firing, armed-silent, starved,\nnever-armed, unobserved, no-data — and only the two DECIDABLE from data can fail:\n`never-armed` (D-088's defect exactly) and `unobserved` (the DETECTOR has gone blind:\na relation added without census coverage). `starved`/`armed-silent` never fail — a\nweek with no overlapping locks is indistinguishable from a dead relation without a\nhuman, and failing on that would red-pin the fleet on quiet traffic.\n\nBecause `couplingSourcesFor` wires `heldFiles` conditionally and the other legs\nunconditionally, `armed` on `holds-a-lock-on` IS the bit that was false on every\nproduction call for 12 days. The probe is therefore a live PRODUCTION recurrence\nguard for D-088, where a unit test can only guard the predicate.\n\n#### The detector must not itself be a dead signal\n\nWired into green-checkpoint's existing `lintPlane` leg, not shipped as a script\nsomeone must remember to run: WI-6476 recorded that `lint:plane-producers` had NO\nautomatic runner, and shipping an unrun dead-signal detector would be self-refuting.\nTwo vacuous-pass controls are pinned by tests — an empty census window reports\n`no-data` rather than declaring every relation dead, and a relation list that fails\nto parse is a HARD ERROR, never a clean run over zero subjects.\n\n#### Honest limitations, stated now rather than discovered later\n\n(a) THE DENOMINATOR IS THIN. The census writes only on the opt-in `include_coupling`\nbranch — 11 calls across the entire retained history — so `no-data` will dominate at\nfirst. That is why the review date is 2026-09-13, not a week out. Run live today it\nhonestly prints `census rows: 0` and six `no-data` rows: the code is not deployed.\n\n(b) THE OTHER TWO CALL SITES ARE NOT CENSUSED. `readCoupledTopics` and the coord:send\ndivergence stamp also call `deriveCouplings`; neither has a metadata sink without\nthreading one through two more layers of a hot path. The extension point exists\n(`observe` on the sources bag, which all three already build via\n`couplingSourcesFor`). If the denominator is still thin at review, widen THERE.\n\n(c) CHECKED, AND NOT A BUG: `readPeerRelations` never passes `coordinationDomain`, so\n`holds-a-lock-on` cannot fire on the divergence path. Safe ONLY because\nmessage-fields.ts rules it `absenceIsInformative: false` — a computed miss says\nnothing. Had it been `true`, every honest sender assertion would be scored as\ndivergence: D-002 RULING 1's trap with a different token. Verified in source before\nclaiming either way.\n\n#### The transferable rule\n\nA SIGNAL'S CORRECTNESS AND ITS LIVENESS ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES, AND TESTS CAN ONLY\nESTABLISH THE FIRST. Fixtures supply the input directly, so a test proves the\nderivation correct GIVEN INPUT and is structurally incapable of noticing that\nproduction never hands it any. Anything that computes a signal needs a liveness\nmeasurement taken in production — one that distinguishes \"the gate never opened\" from\n\"the gate opened onto nothing\".\n\n### D-092 — AMENDS D-091: the firing probe gets a STATISTICAL-POWER FLOOR as well as a review date — a review DATE alone would have repeated on P-007 the exact n=3 mistake D-090 parked P-006 to avoid\nDate: 2026-08-09\nDate: 2026-08-09\n\nCaught while reviewing my own P-007 implementation before closing it, not by a test.\n\n#### The flaw\n\nD-091 shipped the probe report-only until REVIEW_BY 2026-09-13, on the reasoning that\na date gives the census time to accumulate. But a DATE is not EVIDENCE. The census\nwrites only on the opt-in `include_coupling` branch — measured at ~11 calls per\nfortnight — so 2026-09-13 could arrive with THREE census rows and the gate would then\nred-pin the whole fleet on three samples.\n\nThat is precisely the error D-090 refused to make on P-006 three items earlier in this\nsame plan: a 12× rate jump on n=3 is indistinguishable from noise at the null rate, so\nP-006 is parked until 2026-08-16 by STATISTICAL POWER, not by effort. I applied that\nreasoning to a measurement I was judging and not to the one I was building.\n\n#### Ruling\n\n`MIN_CENSUS_ROWS_TO_FAIL = 5`. A failing verdict (`never-armed` / `unobserved`) now\nrequires BOTH that the review date has passed AND that the window holds at least that\nmany census rows. Below the floor the row is reported as `underpowered` with the count\nnamed — explicitly \"an UNFINISHED measurement, not a verdict\" — and the run exits 0.\n\nThis completes the probe's refusal-to-round-a-zero ladder rather than adding a knob:\n`no-data` already refuses to INTERPRET an empty window; the floor refuses to CONDEMN a\nnearly-empty one. Both are the same discipline `judgeProducerField` established, one\nstep apart.\n\nIt also absorbs a version-skew false positive for free, which is why it is not merely\na safety margin. A relation added to `DERIVED_COUPLING_RELATIONS` but not yet deployed\nis censused by nothing, so it reads `unobserved` — correctly, but prematurely. Under a\ndate-only rule a relation added days before the review date would fail the gate for\nbeing new. Under the floor it cannot fail until the census has actually run enough to\nhave had the chance to observe it.\n\n#### The transferable rule\n\nA REVIEW DATE IS A DEADLINE, NOT A SAMPLE SIZE, AND A GATE NEEDS BOTH. Time-gating\nsays \"you have had long enough\"; power-gating says \"and we looked at enough\". A gate\ncarrying only the first will eventually fire on a quiet week and teach everyone to\nignore it — which costs more than the defect it was built to catch, because the next\nreal finding arrives at a gate nobody believes.\n\nGeneralisation worth noticing: I built the detector, ruled on it, and only caught this\nby re-reading my own output against a decision recorded THREE ITEMS EARLIER in the\nsame plan. The plan's Decisions section is what made that catchable — a coord message\nsaying the same thing would not have been re-read.\n\n### D-093 — Three coupling retirements approved, each door-checked; @-selectors explicitly NOT dropped\nDate: 2026-08-10\nApproved [owner:Avi 2026-08-10] from the adoption audit. Applies D-002 (a zero-call verb is a retirement candidate before an adoption target) under D-102's discipline (which falsified 5 of 6 earlier proposed retirements, all from reading a zero call count as an absent function without checking who else held the door open).\n\n1. DROP the shared-file derived signal and the current_files roster field it reads. 0 edges in 14d; 0 of 119 live rows ever populated; no writer, and every declare-intent that omits it resets to []. Fully superseded by the lock-hold signal. Keeping it permanently poisons the dead-signal census with a signal that cannot fire.\n2. DROP topics:feed — 3 calls all-time, 1 agent, last 2026-07-27. Also removes coupled-topics-read.ts, one of three coupling-derivation call sites.\n3. DEFAULT include_coupling ON — retire the GATE, not the feature. 11 calls ever, 4 agents, all of them this feature's own authors, out of 316 presence calls all-time. That flag is WHY the coupling payoff is invisible. Roster-derived signals now cost no query, so the original payload/compute objection is gone; keep only the querying legs behind detail.\n\nEXPLICITLY NOT DROPPED, having FAILED the door check: @-selectors look like 2% agent adoption (39 of 1,783 agent-authored messages) but 1,348 of the 1,381 selector-bearing messages in 7d are machine emitters, and selectors GENERATE the audience history coord:catch-up is the sole door to. Load-bearing, and invisible if you measure only the agent population — which is the population the rest of the audit correctly focuses on. coord:feed (23 calls all-time) has the same smell and has NOT been cleared; do not propose retiring it without the same check.\n\n### D-094 — coord:couple gets a falsifier DATE (2026-08-16), not a verdict\nDate: 2026-08-10\nZero organic use in two weeks would normally retire coord:couple/decouple under D-002 — 13 calls EVER (11 couple + 2 decouple), every one a verification fixture or owner-directed, zero spontaneous.\n\nBut its only enforcement tier is PROMPT TEXT, which coordination-spec-adoption-2026-08-03 D-016 disqualifies as a tier at all (0-8 calls/week across 149 agents for every behaviour whose only tier is the prompt). The guidance reached the rendered prompt at 2026-08-09T05:05Z (WI-37206), 24h before measurement, so the honest forecast is that it will not move on its own.\n\nRULING: decide 2026-08-16. If organic (non-owner-directed) calls are still zero, retire on the WI-6097 precedent — auto-coupling covers the same need once the coordinationDomain fix lands. Do NOT re-measure before then, and do NOT add more prompt text. WI-37522 is already the right open instrument and its own checkpoint correctly refused to close on a 10.5h reading.\n\n### D-095 — CORRECTS D-093: current_files has a WRITER and consumers — only the shared-file SIGNAL is a clean drop\nDate: 2026-08-10\nRETRACTION. D-093 approved dropping \"the shared-file derived signal AND the current_files roster field it reads\", on the stated basis that current_files has \"no writer\". THAT IS FALSE and I am correcting it before any removal happens.\n\nWHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. `session_briefs.current_files` is a real column with a real writer — `packages/operator-core/lib/session-brief.ts` writes it (L79/L83/L106) and reads it back (L127) — and it has live consumers beyond coupling: `adv-roster.ts` (fleet-wide current_files projection), `agent-orders-notify.ts` (the brief row moves on current_files writes), plus `pre-prompt-registry-config.ts` and a dedicated integration test. Dropping the field is a MIGRATION with a wide blast radius, not a removal.\n\nWHERE THE ERROR CAME FROM. coupling-derivation.ts's own comment says current_files \"is populated ONLY by an explicit coord:declare-intent { current_files }\" and measured 119 live rows with zero populated. That is a statement about AGENTS not populating it — an empty-in-practice field — and I promoted it to \"has no writer\", which is a different claim about the CODE. Empty is not absent; the same conflation the audit itself warns about elsewhere.\n\nWHAT STANDS. The `shared-file` derived COUPLING SIGNAL is genuinely narrow and remains a clean drop — exactly three non-test sites: couplings.ts:106 (the relation list), derived-signal-census.ts:83 (the census mapping), coupling-derivation.ts:184 (the emit). It has produced 0 edges in 14 days and is fully superseded by the lock-hold signal. Removing it stops the dead-signal census carrying a signal that cannot fire, which was the actual point.\n\nWHAT IS DEFERRED. Whether current_files should survive at all is a SEPARATE question — it is an empty field with real plumbing, so the choice is \"give it a writer that agents actually trigger\" vs \"migrate it out\". Neither is this plan's business and neither is approved. Do not remove it as part of the shared-file drop.\n\n### D-096 — REFINES D-093: the whole topics:* TOOL family is dead, but its LIBRARY has live internal consumers — drop the tools, keep the libs\nDate: 2026-08-10\nD-093 approved dropping `topics:feed` on 3 calls all-time. Verified to the same standard the other two candidates failed, and the scope moves in BOTH directions.\n\nWIDER THAN APPROVED — the whole agent-facing family is dead, not just the one verb. Measured all-time in papercusp-workspace: `topics:feed` 3 calls / 1 agent / last 2026-07-27, and `topics:list` and `topics:tag` have **zero calls, ever**. So the door check that mattered — \"is topics:feed the sole READER of what topics:tag WRITES, such that dropping it strands the write side?\" — comes back clean: there is no write side in use either.\n\nNARROWER THAN APPROVED — the LIBRARY must stay. The last two disappear with their files.\n\nThis is NOT \"pure removal\", which is how D-093 characterised it. Remove the `shared-file` derived coupling signal — three non-test sites (couplings.ts:106, derived-signal-census.ts:83, coupling-derivation.ts:184). NOT `current_files`, which stays (D-095).\n2. Do not execute D-096 without a fresh owner go-ahead; read this decision first.\n\nALSO NOT A DROP: omp:sessions, per D-105 on coordination-spec-adoption-2026-08-03. It belongs to the R-2 teaching-refusal work, not here.\n\n### D-098 — include_coupling defaults ON — an opt-in flag only its own authors ever passed is not a shipped feature\nDate: 2026-08-10\nOwner-cleared 2026-08-10 [owner:Avi], executed under WI-37663 alongside the D-093 shared-file retirement.\n\nTHE RULING. `coord:presence`'s coupling block is now DEFAULT-ON: the gate in\n`agent-tools/coordination/tools/presence.ts` is `args.include_coupling !== false && self`, was\n`=== true`. Pass `include_coupling: false` to suppress.\n\nWHY. Measured over the whole retained window: `include_coupling` was passed 11 times EVER, by 4\nagents, ALL of them this feature's own authors, out of 316 `coord:presence` calls. That is the\nwhole explanation for why the coupling payoff was invisible — and it means no amount of\ncorrectness work downstream (D-088's coordinationDomain fix, P-013's derivation, the union) could\never have surfaced through it. A feature whose only callers are the people who wrote it is not\ndeployed, however green its tests.\n\nWHAT THE ORIGINAL GATE WAS PROTECTING, AND WHY IT NO LONGER APPLIES. The opt-in rationale on\nrecord was \"paying a query on every read of a hot poll surface to append an empty array is the\nwrong trade\". Both halves expired: P-013 built the derived half (D-078), so the roster signals are\ncomputed purely from snapshot rows already in hand — no query — and the block is no longer\nprovably empty. What remained was a PAYLOAD SIZE trade, and `buildCoupledExpansion` caps the block\n(presence-cost.test.ts leg d), so it is bounded rather than unbounded.\n\nTHE GATE MOVED, IT DID NOT VANISH — this is the part to preserve. `presenceNeedsCoordinationDomain`\nis deliberately UNCHANGED: `undefined` reads as false, so a DEFAULT presence read gets the free\nroster-derived signals and does NOT arm the QUERYING lane (lock holds), which needs the\ncoordination domain. An EXPLICIT `include_coupling: true` — or `include_detail` — still arms it.\nSo the cost profile of the default path is unchanged apart from the appended, capped block.\n\nCONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING, because it is a benefit and reads like a regression: the P-007\ndead-signal census now rides the DEFAULT path. It used to be bounded to the opt-in branch — all 11\ncalls of it — which is precisely why ZERO rows in `tool_invocations` have ever carried\n`metadata_json.derivedSignals`, and why the detector built to answer \"has this relation ever fired\nin production?\" could not answer it for anyone. Collecting that firings data is the point.\n\n⚠ THIS DOES NOT FIX THE DIVERGENCE PATH. `readPeerRelations` in `coupling-divergence-stamp.ts`\nstill does not pass `coordinationDomain`, so `heldFiles` remains structurally unwired on the\n`coord:send` path — the ONLY coupling path that runs at volume. D-088 fixed that on\n`coord:presence`, the path with 11 calls ever. Tracked as EI-20042650315152947 / P-008 + P-009; do\nnot read this decision as having closed it.\n\n⚠ NOTE ON IDS: an earlier draft of the code comments for this change cited \"D-094\", which is\nALREADY TAKEN by an unrelated ruling (the coord:couple falsifier date). Those citations were\ncorrected to this decision's real id before landing. `plans:add-decision` appends and auto-assigns\nthe next id — it does not honour a requested one — so a decision id must be READ BACK from the\ntool, never predicted, and any code comment citing it written only afterwards.\n\n### D-099 — holds-a-lock-on is wired on the coord:send divergence path; the SECOND omission (coupled-topics-read) is deliberately left unwired — evidence, so it is not re-opened\nDate: 2026-08-10\nEI-20042650315152947. Two sites had the identical omission. One is fixed, one is deliberately not — and the asymmetry needs recording, because an auditor grepping `couplingSourcesFor(` will find the second site and reasonably assume it was missed.\n\n#### The mechanism (read from the writer, not inferred)\n\n`couplingSourcesFor` (coupling-sources.ts:201-206) omits the `heldFiles` source ENTIRELY when `coordinationDomain` is absent. So a caller that does not pass it makes `holds-a-lock-on` STRUCTURALLY UNDERIVABLE on that path — not merely empty. This is why the relation showed 0 edges in 14 days despite being \"wired\": it was wired only on `coord:presence` (11 calls ever), never on the path at volume.\n\nThree callers exist:\n  - tools/presence.ts:268 — PASSES it. Correct already.\n  - coupling-divergence-stamp.ts:183 (readPeerRelations, the coord:send path) — DID NOT. **Now fixed.**\n  - coupled-topics-read.ts:55 — DOES NOT. **Deliberately left alone; see the ruling.**\n\n#### RULING 1 — the fix belongs in the IO leg, not threaded from the caller\n\n`readPeerRelations` now resolves `lockCoordinationDomain()` itself, dynamically imported inside the existing `Promise.all`, wrapped in try/catch (a throw degrades to the old no-lock-signal behaviour rather than failing a send).\n\nThreading it through `sendOne` was considered and REJECTED: the domain is a PROCESS fact, not a caller fact. `lockCoordinationDomain()` takes no arguments, and `readIdentity()` — the source the presence path uses — is literally a wrapper around that same call (locks/identity.ts:73). A threaded parameter would carry zero caller-specific information, and `sendOne` has no `ctx` to derive one from anyway.\n\n⚠ Correcting a wrong framing produced en route, so it does not propagate: `readIdentity(ctx).coordinationDomain` and `lockCoordinationDomain()` are the SAME VALUE, not alternatives. The presence path is not using a different or better source.\n\nThe dynamic import is mandatory, not stylistic: coupling-divergence-stamp.ts:41-55 records that `send.ts` imports this module, so a STATIC import here drags the presence-snapshot chain into the send path's load-time graph and breaks every suite that partially mocks `../presence`.\n\n#### RULING 2 — coupled-topics-read.ts stays UNWIRED\n\nIts only caller is `tools/topics-feed.ts` (`topics:feed`). MEASURED against harness_shared.tool_invocations: `topics:feed` = 3 calls EVER, last 2026-07-27 (14 days ago); `topics:list` and `topics:tag` return no rows at all, corroborating D-097's \"0 calls ever\". (The count query was not tenant-scoped, which cuts the safe way here — scoping can only reduce it.)\n\nWiring it would add a per-call lock read to a path with no users, against a pool coupling-sources.ts:186-190 itself flags as having saturated before — and would enlarge D-096's pending removal for no benefit.\n\nThis is NOT the D-097 deferral applied by analogy. D-097 defers REMOVING the topics:* tool family pending fresh owner go-ahead; it says nothing about coupling-domain wiring. The two were briefly conflated in a carried note and that shorthand is wrong. The ruling here rests on the call counts above, independently.\n\nIf topics:* is ever revived rather than removed, wire it then, the same way readPeerRelations now does.\n\n#### Guard\n\n`coupling-divergence-stamp-reader-wiring.test.ts` (new, isolated) asserts `couplingSourcesFor` RECEIVES a `coordinationDomain`. It lives in its own file because `coupling-divergence-stamp.test.ts` declares no `vi.mock` and exercises the INJECTED reader — hoisted mocks would silently re-scope its four existing describes.\n\nFalsifiability is built in rather than proved by mutating the tree: its third test drives the domain to `undefined` through the same harness — the exact pre-fix state — so the positive assertion cannot pass vacuously. Note an \"is the relation ever produced?\" test would have been VACUOUS here (no lock fixture ⇒ no edge either way); the only non-vacuous assertion is on the CALL, not the output. That is the transferable part: when a bug is a MISSING ARGUMENT, assert on the argument.\nRelated: P-008, P-009\n\n### D-100 — The `awaits` census zero is a TRUE reading from CORRECT code — caller-side self-selection, not a defect. Do not \"fix\" the predicate, and do not drop the relation\nDate: 2026-08-10\nDate: 2026-08-10\nMEASURED, and recorded as a decision because the opposite reading is the natural one and has now cost three separate investigations — two of them mine, in the same hour.\n\nTHE READING THAT LOOKS LIKE A BUG. The derived-signal census reports, for `awaits`: armed on 22/22 runs, 1023 total inputs, ZERO edges. Every element of that reads as a live predicate rejecting everything. EI-20082032160286357 was filed on exactly that basis (\"either a broken derivation or a signal that cannot fire\"), and its own first-step instruction sent the reader at the predicate.\n\nRULING 1 — THE PREDICATE, ITS INPUT, AND ITS DIVERGENCE RULE ARE ALL CORRECT. Verified in code, not inferred:\n  - coupling-derivation.ts:155-173 — `const myAwait = cleanId(selfRow.awaitingEventKey); ... if (myAwait && cleanId(row.awaitingEventKey) === myAwait)`. Correct.\n  - presence-tier1.ts:170-176 — the field IS populated, from harness_shared.event_awaits filtered to LIVE awaits (fired_at IS NULL AND cancelled_at IS NULL AND not expired). Nothing is stubbed on this path.\n  - message-fields.ts:257 — `awaits: { confirmedBy: ['awaits'], absenceIsInformative: false }`, and :326 scores an unconfirmed assertion 'not-comparable', never 'diverges'. The D-002 RULING 1 same-fleet trap (an uncomputable relation left with absenceIsInformative:true, manufacturing sender-inaccuracy) is ALREADY CLOSED for `awaits`. Do not \"fix\" it.\n\nRULING 2 — THE CAUSE IS CALLER-SIDE SELF-SELECTION, which is a property of WHO CALLS, not of the predicate or the key space. An edge requires the CALLER and a peer to hold the SAME event_key. Sort the key shapes by who holds them:\n  - SHAREABLE keys (a named gate: green-gate-verdict, gate-first-green, fleet:<slug>:<gate>) are held by agents PARKED in events:await. A parked agent makes no tool calls, so it is never the caller of coord:presence.\n  - The keys a WORKING caller holds are `coord:inbox-wake:<ownerId>` (embeds its own id) and `predicate:<uuid>` (fresh per watch) — both per-subscriber unique.\nThe population that can share a key is disjoint from the population that triggers the derivation. Hence 0 edges across 22 runs despite 1023 inputs.\n\nRULING 3 — DO NOT DROP THE RELATION, and beware the intermediate wrong answer. I first concluded key equality was \"impossible BY CONSTRUCTION\" (90% of live await keys embed the subscriber's own id) and proposed dropping `awaits` under the D-054/D-002 precedent. That is RETRACTED and was wrong: querying HISTORY rather than the live snapshot gives 74 event keys with >1 subscriber and a maximum of 139 subscribers on ONE key. The relation is genuinely fireable, the shared-gate protocol produces shared keys BY DESIGN, and D-002 RULING 2 already re-points fixtures onto `awaits` as a surviving signal — dropping it would break that remediation. The transferable error: a live snapshot generalised into a structural law. When a zero looks structural, query history before ruling.\n\nBINDING ON IMPLEMENTERS. EI-20082032160286357 is CLOSED as dropped/retracted (terminalCompletionRef carries the full trace; see its RETRACTION #3 comment, thread post 56995). Do not reopen it, and do not re-derive this. No code change is warranted on the awaits predicate. P-013 no longer has an unexplained reading and does not need to wait on this.\n\nWHAT REMAINS ACTIONABLE (extracted BEFORE the drop, so nothing was destroyed with it):\n  - EI-20088486454213771 — the census reports `inputs` as a count of PEER rows while the binding constraint is a SELF-side field, so \"armed, 1023 inputs, 0 edges\" cannot distinguish 'evaluated and rejected' from 'never evaluated'. A dead-signal census whose headline number makes correct code look broken inverts its own purpose. Fix: distinguish armed-and-evaluated from armed-but-short-circuited (or count the self-side precondition as an input, so a short-circuit reads inputs=0, matching how blocks-me / blocked-by-me already read honestly as unmeasurable).\n  - EI-20088246671600042 — fleet-roster.ts:131 and hive-roster.ts:105 hardcode awaitingEventKey:null while presence-tier1.ts:176 is the only real writer. Latent today (the census path is coord:presence), but it would produce a silent permanent zero for any derivation later fed by those rosters — the same indistinguishable-from-a-true-zero failure this decision exists to prevent.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-09] *\"put the plan through a thorough audit and compare to the code, any gaps or bugs? 2. put all the plan items through thorough testing\"*. AUTO mode ON. Auditing `opencode-omp-borrow-finish-2026-08-08` (all 12 items read `done`, P-012 parked; plan marked shipped).\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Work A→E in order, then synthesise. Nothing here is assumed clean because the ledger says so.)\n\n## Why this is not a formality\n\nAll 12 items read `done` and the plan is `shipped`. This audit assumes NONE of that:\n\n1. **Six items were closed by ME (su-c2f97) within the last two hours** — P-007/WI-36683, P-008/WI-36726, P-009/WI-36767 today. An agent auditing its own completions is the likeliest place for an over-trusted claim; my completion records are prose I wrote, not evidence anyone re-derived.\n2. **Three (P-003/WI-36047, P-005/WI-36613, P-006/WI-36048) were closed by a PREDECESSOR** and reached me only as a carry-document summary, which itself warns its claims are unverified and may have been retracted after it was written. I have never read that code.\n\n**Standing rule:** verify against the code that WRITES the behaviour — never the completion record, the plan text, or this plan's prose. A green suite is not evidence the suite tests the claim: check the fixture covers the population. That exact vacuous-guard defect was found in-flight yesterday (a D-006 \"PRESERVES every field\" test whose fixture never set the two fields being dropped).\n\n**Method per item:** (a) locate the concrete code claim; (b) read the writer; (c) confirm it is REACHABLE, not dead code behind a flag or an unreferenced export; (d) run its suite AT HEAD, never from a remembered result; (e) check the guard is FALSIFIABLE — would it red if the behaviour regressed?; (f) record gap/bug/clean WITH evidence. A clean item records what was checked, so \"audited\" never means \"skimmed\". Findings are filed as work-items, not narrated.\n\n## Tranches\n\n- **P-001** `done` **Tranche A — my own closes (highest distrust).** WI-36683: does the corrected `ambient-push-door` registry reason match what the code now does, and does the bound test still hold after WI-36688 changed that door? WI-36726: is the UNVERIFIED marker REACHABLE on a real completion path, not just in renderCompletion unit tests — trace complete.ts to renderCompletion to the notification a parent actually reads. WI-36767: is the headroom report accurate, and does the P-011 gate still red on a real breach? — note: ← WI-37024 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `todo` **Tranche B — inherited claims I have NEVER verified.** P-003/WI-36047 (result-door no longer returns the full uncapped result when the spill write fails), P-005/WI-36613 (`nonTextChars` in `_meta` + fast-path notice), P-006/WI-36048 (payload-tier omission markers self-describing; the `payloadTier:'full'` recovery pointer actually resolves). Read each writer, confirm reachable, re-run each suite at HEAD.\n- **P-003** `todo` **Tranche C — the record-only items.** P-001, P-002, P-010, P-011 claim DECISIONS and DOC edits, not code. Verify each decision exists with the cited id and says what the item claims, and that the addendum's 14-row status table matches reality — I edited rows 2/8/10/13 yesterday, so verify the OTHER ten rather than assuming them.\n- **P-004** `todo` **Tranche D — WI-36688, landed by another session after I filed it.** `fitPushesToBudget` now exists in ambient-push-delivery.ts and changes the exact door my WI-36683 bound test guards. Does it fix the real defect (recordDelivered running BEFORE the cut) or only add a fitting helper? Is the `lossless` registry reason I wrote still TRUE, or now stale in the other direction? Do non-fitting pushes genuinely re-deliver now?\n- **P-005** `todo` **Tranche E — whole-surface test + typecheck at HEAD.** Derive the file set from the work-items' `filesChanged` rather than from memory; run every covering suite, `lint:tsc` per file, and `lint:tool-prompts`. Report real numbers and NAME anything that could not be tested, rather than letting a green imply coverage it does not have.\n- **P-006** `todo` **Synthesis.** One report to Avi: per-item verdict (clean / gap / bug) with evidence, every finding filed as a work-item, and an explicit list of what was NOT verifiable and why. If the audit contradicts anything I told Avi earlier today, LEAD with the retraction.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — AUDIT VERDICT — all 12 borrow items hold up against the code; the one real defect was a STALE RECORD, not stale code, and it had gone wrong in the ALARMING direction\nDate: 2026-08-09\nAudited every item of `opencode-omp-borrow-finish-2026-08-08` against the code that WRITES the behaviour, never a completion record. Verdict: **no shipped item is wrong**. One real defect found and fixed; one prior suspicion RETRACTED.\n\n**RETRACTION (led with, per the plan's method).** The inherited \"suspected MAJOR finding\" — that WI-36688's `fitPushesToBudget` was defined-but-never-called (the inert-fix shape) — is FALSE. It IS wired: `ambient-push-delivery.ts:278`, and `recordDelivered` (:280-294) receives only the fitting set. The suspicion came from a grep COUNT (4 source / 6 test mentions) described as \"consistent with no call site\". Consistent-with is not evidence-of: the call site was one of the 4. **A count cannot distinguish a declaration from a use — read the call site.**\n\nLosslessness is genuine, not asserted: `fitPushesToBudget` composes `HEADER + n + Σ(line lengths)`, byte-identical to `renderPushBlock`, and sizes against the SAME `pushInjectionDoorTokens × CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE` that `capInjectionText` uses. So the block always satisfies `text.length <= budgetChars` and the door returns it untouched. This independently corroborates D-020 (head-keep is correct) for the push population.\n\n**THE REAL DEFECT — the record describing the door was two fixes out of date, and mis-directed the next reader with authority.** WI-36683 corrected a false re-delivery claim in the truncation-honesty registry; WI-36688 then changed the door's ORDERING, and the registry entry was never updated. It still stated \"records every selected push as DELIVERED BEFORE it renders and cuts\" and called the shipped fix pending (\"WI-36688 carries the fit-whole-teasers fix\"). Net effect: the fleet's source of truth on which doors are honest described a door that is lossless by construction as one fat handle away from a silent permanent drop. Four artifacts corrected (registry reason; the suite's describe-doc, incl. line numbers :236/:240/:286 → :294/:298/:344; the bound test's FAILURE MESSAGE, which told a future agent a breach = \"SILENT PERMANENT DROP … give the door a marker\" when it is now only a throughput signal; and `applyPushInjectionDoor`'s own doc comment).\n\nGeneralisable: **a stale-but-REASSURING reason and a stale-but-ALARMING one are the same defect.** The second is worse — it survives review because caution reads as rigour, and it spends the next reader's time on a danger that no longer exists.\n\n**Per-item verdicts.** WI-36688 ✅ wired+correct. WI-36683 ✅ (resolved by the fix above). WI-36726 ✅ CONFIRMED ON LIVE DATA — the UNVERIFIED marker is reachable on a real completion path, not just unit tests (`coord_event_log` 2026-08-09T03:52:22Z: \"EI-19944567995100280 DONE: … — UNVERIFIED\", exactly `renderCompletion`'s trailer shape). WI-36767 ✅ both legs — headroom arithmetic correct (`weight <= LIMIT && weight + 120 > LIMIT` counts only NEWLY breaching tools), and the P-011 gate proven FALSIFIABLE (1501 → soft leg flags; 1601 → hardCap leg flags; exactly 1500 → not flagged). WI-36047 ✅ fix real, and its replacement test asserts the exact contradiction on an identical fixture PLUS a CONTROL that would catch a door which simply stopped spilling. WI-36613 ✅ zero-exposure premise re-verified. WI-36048 ✅ markers self-describing with count + recovery pointer.\n\n**Tests at HEAD:** 93/93 (ambient-push-delivery, truncation-honesty-guard, result-door, coord-lifecycle/render), payload-tier 30/30, lint:tool-prompts 55/55; `lint:tsc --files` clean on the 3 edited files; `tsc -p libs/generic/tooldef` exit 0 / 0 errors. File set derived from the work-items' own `filesChanged`, not memory — 10 files, all covered.\n\n**METHOD FINDING worth more than any single verdict: a zero is not evidence until the PROBE SHAPE is validated.** `body->>'category'='completion'` returned 0 of 111,513 `coord_event_log` rows over ten weeks while 2,175 successful `work_items:complete` calls existed since Aug 1. That reads exactly like \"the intrinsic completion emission (D-002/D-004) is broken fleet-wide\" — a large, alarming, well-formed finding, and a denominator makes it MORE convincing, not less. It was wrong: the emitted `category` simply is not persisted at `body.category`. The truth came from searching the MARKER TEXT itself, not the field I assumed carried it. **Validate a probe against a row you KNOW should match before believing an absence.**\n\nFalsifiability was proven WITHOUT mutating the shared tree (CLAUDE.md sweep-race rule): the subject was a pure function, so the probe ran from `/tmp`, needing no git-sync lock, no restore, and no trap.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate.
