Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"default-deploy-account-2026-08-08","title":"Retire the Keys &amp; OAuth sign-in cards; make a deploy account settable as the default","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Retire the Keys &amp; OAuth sign-in cards; make a deploy account settable as the default\nslug: default-deploy-account-2026-08-08\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-08-09\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all 8 items done; P-007 (tests) closed 2026-08-09 with full evidence on WI-37203.\n\n⚠ CORRECTION to the earlier Now, which said the implementation left TWO suites red: the real count was SIX, all found+fixed by P-007, none caused by the test work. (1-4) account-resolver 10/27 red, bootstrap-su 27/80 red, bootstrap-su-bearer-non-transit, native-session-id-roundtrip — all the SAME trap: P-003/P-004 added `readDefaultAccountId` imports and sibling suites mocking the store with an explicit vi.mock FACTORY were never widened, so the missing export threw at RUNTIME. lint:tsc is structurally blind to this (source imports are correct + well-typed), which is why 7 clean lint:tsc runs recorded this plan \"verified\" over a red tree. (5) css-tokens — P-006's `var(--ok)` in left-sidebar.styles.ts, fixed to --good. (6) design-primitives — title-only button tooltips in AccountsTab + deploy-accounts/page, fixed via the shared Tooltip primitive. Class = 6th occurrence, consolidated onto EI-19462958615807409 (still OPEN).\n\nTRANCHES GREEN (before→after): account-session-override 11→23 · account-resolver 27→42 · bootstrap-su 80→97 · account-pool-store 14→27 · AccountsTab 3→12 · NEW api-keys/page 4/4 · chat-stream-resolve 43/43. GATES GREEN: lint:tool-prompts 55/55 · lint:tests · all three lint:tsc variants exit=0 · css-tokens + design-primitives PASS.\n\nFINAL CHECK VERIFIED (was predicted): test:affected re-run 04:19Z, verdict read from the LOG BODY not the exit code (notification said \"exit 0\" while REAL_EXIT=1). coverage=complete fileCount=4; all four of this plan's red suites GONE. The 4 remaining were re-run individually and attributed by actual failure message — none is this plan's.\n\nCARRIED FORWARD (not this plan's): 4 STANDING COMMITTED reds will red-pin green-checkpoint — resolver-backing-table-coverage (stale agentOrders/agent_modes exemption), handoff + deliver-and-wake (SAME vi.mock trap from another plan's presence.ts change), cut-seed-cli (60s hive timeout).\n\n**Next:** Nothing further on this plan — it is closed. Anyone picking up the tree: the 4 standing reds above belong to OTHER plans and need greening before green-checkpoint can pass; the deploy-accounts page test rebuild recipe is EI-19947523316032859.\n\n## Background\n\nTwo settings surfaces both authenticate a Claude account, for different reasons:\n\n- **Keys &amp; OAuth** (`/settings/api-keys`) — `AuthSignInCards` spawns `claude /login` in an\n  inline PTY, writing `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (macOS: login Keychain). That is the box's\n  ONE local login, and it is what `localLoginCredentialRef()` resolves to. It backs the `local`\n  fallback account, every `account: 'default'` spawn, and the in-process `anthropic-direct`\n  callers (judges, sim-users, summarisers, memory session-extraction).\n- **Deploy accounts** (`/settings/deploy-accounts`) — the pool. Each row is a `credentialRef`\n  (`token:` from `claude setup-token`, `file:`, `codex-cli:`) under\n  `~/.papercusp/deploy-credentials/`, never touching `~/.claude`. N accounts, gateway failover,\n  per-account headroom, shippable to remote frames.\n\nThey are not duplicates, but the same Anthropic account can sit in both and nothing in the UI\nsays which one wins. Owner's call: keep the pool, drop the sign-in cards, and give the pool a\nDEFAULT so it can take over the role the local login played.\n\n**Today's resolution (what \"default\" means mechanically), verified in tree:**\n\n- `inference-gateway/account-resolver.ts` — `resolveBoundAccount`: env `PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ID`\n  pin &gt; sole pool account &gt; `local` fallback (`localLoginCredentialRef()`).\n  `resolveAccountPool`: all pool accounts in pool order; empty claude pool ⇒ `[local]`.\n- `bootstrap-su.ts resolveAccountPin` — `''` / `default` / `none` / `system` ⇒ gateway skipped\n  entirely, emits `PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ROUTING_MODE: 'default'` so the launcher clears inherited\n  credentials and restores the system login. Governs psu sessions, fleet members, cup spawns\n  (`bootstrap-role.ts` calls the same function).\n- In-process `anthropic-direct` callers read the credential file / Keychain directly.\n\n`AccountPool` is `{ accounts: ClaudeAccount[] }` — there is no default field today. The owner's\naccount INTENT already has a durable home apart from the high-churn pool row:\n`AccountSessionOverride` (`forcedAccounts` / `excludeAccounts`) in\n`harness_shared.operator_account_override` (migration 297). Its header states the reason\nexplicitly — keeping owner intent out of the pool's rate-projection write path — so the default\nbelongs there, not on the pool.\n\nNote: the existing **Force** lever is an allow-list (restricts what the fleet MAY use). **Default**\nis a different axis (what gets picked when nothing is pinned). Both are wanted; neither replaces\nthe other.\n\n**Relationship to `authoritative-account-routing-all-backends-2026-07-16`** (active, P-005\nverification): that plan made routing fail CLOSED — an explicit `auto`/pin that cannot be honored\nmust never silently become the system login. This plan ADDS a new input those same seams must\nresolve. It must not reopen the fail-closed property: an explicit pin that cannot be honored\nstill fails, and the default only ever replaces the IMPLICIT local-login fallback.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 `defaultAccountId` lives on `AccountSessionOverride`, not on `AccountPool`\n\nReuse-first: the owner-intent row already exists, is workspace-scoped, fail-soft, and is\ndeliberately separated from the pool's high-churn rate writes. Adding a third field there needs\nno new table, no new migration, and inherits the existing route + optimistic-UI plumbing\n(`useAccountOverride`, `notifySyncInvalidate('accounts.pool')`).\n\n### D-002 `system` stays a literal escape hatch\n\n`--account system` (and `none`) keeps meaning \"the box's own `~/.claude` login, gateway skipped\"\neven when a default is set. `''` (unspecified) and `default` are what the pool default takes\nover. Without this there is no way to reach the local login once a default exists, and no way to\nrecover if the default account's credential goes bad.\n\n### D-003 The default never re-opens the fail-closed property\n\nPer the relationship note above: an explicit `auto`/pin that cannot be honored still fails\nclosed. The default substitutes ONLY for the implicit local-login fallback, and a default naming\na gone/ineligible account degrades to the local login (with a notice), never to a silent wrong\naccount.\n\n### D-004 — The in-process anthropic-direct path honors the default by TRANSPORT CHOICE, not by a pinned credential\nDate: 2026-08-09\nOwner chose the wider scope (2026-08-08): judges, sim-users, summarisers and memory session-extraction must land on the default account too, matching what the Keys & OAuth sign-in used to affect.\n\nThey live behind `libs/papercusp-shared/src/agent/chat-stream.ts`, which MUST NOT import operator-core (dependency direction, stated in-file at `GATEWAY_DELEGATED_AUTH_TOKEN` / `ROUTE_ACCOUNT_HEADER`). So the default cannot be resolved there directly.\n\nIt does not need to be. `chooseStatelessTransport({ claudeTok })` already picks between two legs: `anthropic-direct` (the local ~/.claude OAuth token) and `gateway-pool` (egress via the local inference gateway, which re-auths upstream with a pool account's own credential). Teaching that pure function to prefer `gateway-pool` when a default is set routes the whole in-process family through the gateway, whose `resolveAccountPool` (P-003) already orders the default first with the rest as failover.\n\nRejected alternative: `PAPERCUSP_ROUTE_ACCOUNT` / the `x-papercusp-account` header. That is a HARD pin with no 429 failover, and `resolveRouteAccountId` deliberately emits a once-per-process footgun warning against exactly this use. A default account is a preference, not a pin — it must keep failing over.\n\nConsequences: (a) the signal is an env marker the operator sets, keeping papercusp-shared operator-core-free; (b) `probeStatelessTransport` (health monitors) reports the new label truthfully because it shares the same resolution; (c) with NO default set, behaviour is byte-identical to today — a live local token still wins.\n\n## Phase 1 — remove the sign-in cards\n\n- **P-001** `done` Drop the \"Sign in\" `<section>` + the `AuthSignInCards` import from `apps/operator/app/settings/api-keys/page.tsx`; retune the page intro so it no longer promises OAuth. The COMPONENT stays — `SetupWizard/StepLogins.tsx` still uses it for first-run onboarding. Update `apps/operator/e2e/settings-pages.spec.ts` and the `/settings/api-keys` keyword list in `apps/operator/app/settings/layout.tsx` if either references the removed section. Add a pointer to `/settings/deploy-accounts` so the page still tells the owner where account auth now lives.\n\n## Phase 2 — persist the default\n\n- **P-002** `done` Add `defaultAccountId?: string` to `AccountSessionOverride` + `DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_OVERRIDE` (`packages/operator-core/lib/deployment/account-session-override.ts`). Validate on write: must name a live pool account with provider `claude`; unset/`null` clears it back to the local login. Extend `/api/admin/deploy-accounts/session-override` (GET + POST) and the `accounts:*` MCP surface to read/write it. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 3 — honor it\n\n- **P-003** `done` `inference-gateway/account-resolver.ts`: `resolveBoundAccount` consults the default BEFORE the `local` fallback (and before the sole-pool-account shortcut, so an explicit default wins in a 1-account pool too); `resolveAccountPool` orders the default FIRST so it is the failover primary. Local login stays the fallback when no default is set or the named account is gone. blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `done` `bootstrap-su.ts resolveAccountPin`: `''`/`default` resolve to the default account as a SOFT pin (failover preserved) instead of `PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ROUTING_MODE: 'default'`; `none`/`system` keep today's literal-local-login behaviour per D-002. `bootstrap-role.ts` inherits. Notice text must name the account a spawn actually landed on. blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-008** `done` In-process `anthropic-direct` callers (owner scope choice, 2026-08-08): make `chooseStatelessTransport` in `libs/papercusp-shared/src/agent/chat-stream.ts` prefer the `gateway-pool` leg when a default account is set, EVEN when a live local `~/.claude` OAuth token exists. The gateway then resolves through `resolveAccountPool` (P-003), which puts the default first with the rest as failover — so judges, sim-users, summarisers and memory session-extraction land on the default account. Signalled by an env marker the operator sets (papercusp-shared must NOT import operator-core), NOT `PAPERCUSP_ROUTE_ACCOUNT` (that is a hard pin with no failover and trips its own footgun warning). blocked-by: P-003\n\n\n## Phase 4 — UI\n\n- **P-005** `done` Settings → Deploy accounts (`apps/operator/app/settings/deploy-accounts/page.tsx`): a per-row \"Default\" control + a header line stating the current default (or \"this box's ~/.claude login\"), with a Clear action. Codex rows are not eligible. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-37201 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Accounts pane (`apps/operator-vite/src/components/left-sidebar/AccountsTab.tsx`): the same control on each row beside the existing Force/Exclude levers, through `useAccountOverride` (already optimistic + SSE-invalidating). Footer note when unset. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-37202 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 5 — tests\n\n- **P-007** `done` Vitest: `account-session-override` default validation + clear; resolver default-vs-local-fallback and pool ordering; `resolveAccountPin` routing for `''`/`default`/`none`/`system`/pin, including a control asserting the fail-closed property (D-003) still holds. Component tests for `AccountsTab`, the deploy-accounts page, and the api-keys page (asserts the sign-in section is gone). Typecheck each touched workspace (`lint:tsc` operator-core, `lint:tsc:operator` apps/operator, `lint:tsc:operator-vite`). blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 — note: ← WI-37203 completed (done)\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fleet-lead-instrumentation-audit-2026-08-09","title":"Fleet-lead instrumentation audit — confident zeros, wrong-field readings, and the leader signals that invert under load","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Fleet-lead instrumentation audit — confident zeros, wrong-field readings, and the leader signals that invert under load\nslug: fleet-lead-instrumentation-audit-2026-08-09\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-08-09\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all 25 items done, 13 decisions recorded. Implemented start-to-finish by su-b8422496 (fleet nonp2p-bug-drain leader) across wakes 8-52 on 2026-08-09, per an interactive owner directive. Every Phase 1 instrument named in the audit is fixed, and the Phase 3 capabilities are built: P-022 wake-to-wake delta (`delta`/`deltaSummary` on fleet:leader-brief, migration 779, D-011), P-023 per-member idle oracle (`idleVerdict`/`idleCauses`, D-012), P-024 pool reservation (`reservation`, D-013). THE RECURRING FINDING, which changed the build on four consecutive items: MEASURE THE CLAIM BEFORE BUILDING — P-015 had 1 of 3 sub-claims already shipped, P-016 had 2 of 4 (one a live peer's lane), P-022 had 2 of 4 axes already derivable from durable data, and P-024's premise was outright stale (the gateway priority substrate exists and was un-inerted by WI-4542 on 2026-08-02). The audit was written from OBSERVED SYMPTOMS, and a symptom outlives its fix. Two items were deliberately NOT built as written: P-006 (D-006 — a global fleet:capacity gate would veto every disarm invisibly; shipped as a per-loop liveness+progress veto plus a bounded revival instead) and P-024's claim-state priority half, which is not soundly buildable from the leader's side because the gateway priority label is stamped at spawn time — filed as WI-37558 rather than half-built. NOT YET DEPLOYED: all of it is in the tree; :3070 and bg-host run the RELEASE checkout, so the new leader-brief blocks appear only after the next green+deploy.\n\n**Next:** Nothing on this plan — it is drained. The one tracked follow-on is WI-37558 (per-request claim-state admission priority), which belongs to whoever owns the gateway/spawn seam, not to a fleet leader; it is linked to P-024 as `relates`, deliberately not as `implements`, so completing this plan cannot auto-resolve it.\n\n## Background\n\nThe owner's three questions were: what was broken, what caused unnecessary confusion, and what features would have made leading the fleet easier.\n\nThe answers share one shape, which is the useful finding. **Almost every failure in this run was a measurement structurally incapable of seeing the thing it was asked about, rendered with full confidence and no uncertainty marker — and in each case the action the wrong reading invited made the situation worse.**\n\n- `fleet:leader-brief` said `throttled: 0` and advised waking six idle members. The pool was at `factor 0`; waking them adds requests to the queue that is starving them.\n- `work_items:burn_down` said `terminal.total: 0` for a fleet that had closed 71 items. The natural reading is \"we have made no progress.\"\n- `coord:send` said `counts: {ok:1, failed:0}` having reached 6 of 11 members. The natural reading is \"everyone got the message.\"\n- I audited close quality against `terminal_completion_ref` and got 2.9% against a 37.8% baseline, and reported to the owner that the drain was producing thin closes. The canonical field is `payload->'_completionEvidence'`, where the same cohort reads 94.3% against 56.5% — the opposite conclusion.\n\nThe last one is mine, not the system's, and it is the most instructive: I had *just* caught the same error on a sibling column (`completion_ref`, null on 2657/2657 rows) by running a base-rate control, then repeated it one step later. The control answers \"is this field used?\" — and `terminal_completion_ref` passes that check with a healthy 37.8% baseline while still being the wrong field. Catching the class once did not inoculate against it.\n\nTwo capabilities I was about to request as missing already exist (`work_items:burn_down`, `fleet:invariant`). That reframes part of this plan from \"build\" to \"surface\" — see D-003.\n\n**What worked well**, recorded because it makes the critique credible and these are worth protecting: `dev:pg_query`'s `knownColumns` error output turned two schema dead-ends into lessons in one call each; `accounts:probe-capacity` was decisive and its advice correctly warns that a stale reading is indistinguishable from a wall; `work_items:claimable`'s `claimable_now_spec.note` pre-empted exactly the misreading I would otherwise have made about two different claimable counts; `similarOpen` on `work_items:create` showed five near-duplicates of a bug I filed, immediately telling me the class was known; `loop:checkpoint`'s verify-read plus `contentHash` meant I never had to wonder whether a checkpoint landed; and the `similar_exists` guard on `plans:new` correctly caught this very plan and made me justify a new effort.\n\n## Phase 1 — Broken instruments\n\n- **P-001** `done` `work_items:burn_down` applies `limit` BEFORE computing aggregates, so the drain leader's headline metric silently depends on a pagination arg. Identical calls, only `limit` differing: at `limit:5` → `terminal.total 0`, `delta 0`, `deltaBy.fleet 0`, `closedSince.total 0`; at `limit:2000` → `1693`, `93`, `71`. Nothing marks the aggregate as truncated — `deltaByPartitions:true` and the `basis` note still render, so it reads as a complete census of an empty queue. Fix: `limit` bounds row lists only; aggregates get their own COUNT. Guard: same fixture at `limit:N` and `limit:N*100` must return equal `terminal.total`. Filed WI-37381. importance: high — note: burn_down.ts: censusLimit pinned to WORK_ITEMS_MAX_LIMIT regardless of caller limit + truncatedByLimit flag on the aggregate. 33/33 green.\n- **P-002** `done` `fleet:leader-brief` attributes idleness to the member without consulting the inference pool, so its advice inverts exactly when the fleet is starved. Measured 02:31Z: brief reported `throttled:0`, `idle_with_claimable:6`, `bench_suggested:6` and per-member advice \"Wake it to re-run scheduler:get_next (coord:send wake:required)\", while `fleet:capacity` reported `factor 0`, `usableAccounts 1`, and tier2 `inFlight 3` against `cap 20` with `queued 28`. Its reason text also pre-commits the reader to conclude \"a claim-floor problem\" if the woken member still takes nothing — and the claim floors were healthy (293 claimable of 457 matched). Every diagnostic road it offered led away from the cause. Filed WI-37161 (now done). importance: high — note: leader-brief.ts reads the pool (buildCapacityReport + readBeeProviderAvailability); advice now says DO NOT wake / DO NOT bench, re-check fleet:capacity. 147/147 green.\n- **P-003** `done` `coord:send` to a fleet-scoped `['*']` returned `counts:{ok:1,failed:0}` with `recipients_resolved:6` against an 11-row roster, with no indication anyone was omitted or why. Some omissions were legitimate (2 recipients had ended between my roster read and the send) — the defect is that the result cannot distinguish full delivery from partial. Fix: an `omitted`/`unreachable` array with a reason per entry. Filed WI-37162 (premise self-corrected in a comment). importance: normal — note: liveFleetMemberIdsDiagnosed (fleet-roster) names every silent drop (stale-heartbeat/ended/suspect/bee-role); surfaced via optional AudienceHost.explainFleetAudience -> coord:send result field fleet_omitted. 171/171 + 31/31 green, tsc clean.\n- **P-004** `done` `harness_shared.work_items` carries three plausible completion-evidence fields with no way to tell which is canonical: `completion_ref` is null on 2657/2657 rows (dead schema), `terminal_completion_ref` is optional-secondary (37.8% prior-7d), and `payload->'_completionEvidence'` is canonical (56.5% prior-7d, 94.3% tonight). The dead column and the optional column fail differently, so each defeats a different defensive habit. Fix: drop or comment `completion_ref`; COMMENT ON COLUMN pointing at the canonical path; ideally project evidence onto the `engineer_issues` view. Filed WI-37360. importance: normal — note: Closed by the fleet as WI-37360: migration 764 COMMENTs completion_ref as DEAD and terminal_completion_ref as a pointer-not-evidence, pointing both at payload->'_completionEvidence'; dev:pg_query describe surfaces them.\n- **P-005** `done` A leader-authored claim spec can be silently rewritten by another automated actor with nothing failing loudly. CARRIED from wake 8: cup `s-1786236383559` took the fleet spec to rev4, widening `kind` from `[bug]` to `[bug,change]` — against an owner-directed BUG scope, adding ~907 mostly nit/minor items. Detected only because I re-read the spec by hand. Restored as rev5. A later rev7 by su-6dc49b99 was an honest merge (verified: kind and fence intact). Fix: leader ownership or change-alerting on a fleet spec — see P-021. importance: high — note: leader-brief.ts: computeSpecAuthorshipAlert fires when the fleet spec's last write is not attributable to the reading leader (incl. an unattributed write); silent when the reader is unresolvable. Emits specRevision/specUpdatedBy/specUpdatedAt beside specFilter. Computed from the record ALONE and BEFORE the pool preview, so a preview outage cannot swallow the drift signal. 6 new unit tests + registered in the alert-falsifier FIRING fixture; 163/163 + 201/201, tsc clean.\n- **P-006** `done` Rate-limit starvation REAPS fleet members rather than crashing them, and the two are indistinguishable from the leader's side. Mechanism observed live: pool at `factor 0` → member's wake fires → no inference capacity → no turn produced → the stalled-loops guard sees a loop that never turns and auto-disarms it. System emitted \"2 armed engine loop(s) auto-disarmed — fires kept LANDING with no turn produced behind them (WI-6639)\" during the starvation window. This very likely also explains the wake-8 \"fleet collapse\" (40% of members lost in one unattended hour) that was recorded as an unexplained mystery. Fix: the disarm guard should check pool state before attributing a no-turn fire to a dead loop. importance: high — note: SHIPPED both halves per WI-37546 (NOT as originally written — D-006 stands, no fleet:capacity gate). (A) 5th veto vetoedByToolActivity: per-loop tool-call liveness with a PROGRESS term (distinctTools>=2 || okCalls>=1) + 6h ceiling. (B) reviveDisarmedLoop: a turns-stalled disarm is no longer permanent. dead-owner path untouched (7/7 correct). 72/72 tests, lint:tsc clean.</note>\n<parameter name=\"rationale\">P-006 asked for a fleet:capacity gate on the stalled-loops disarm. D-006 ruled that UNSOUND (a workspace-wide scalar would veto every disarm during a starved window, invisibly) and mandated a census of real disarms before building. The census (WI-37546) confirmed the PREMISE decisively — 18 of 19 turns-stalled disarms on 2026-08-09 reaped owners that were making tool calls in the hour before — while the CONTROL, the same module's dead-owner path, was 7/7 correct. So the signal is fine and the turns-stalled inference is what over-fires.\n\nShipped as two coupled halves, because the censu…\n- **P-007** `done` The `fleet:capacity` account projection can silently rot, and a stale reading is indistinguishable from a real wall. Observed `blind:true`, `blindAccounts:2` alongside `degraded:false` and `factor 0.083`. Resolving it required a manual `accounts:probe-capacity`, which CONFIRMED the wall (aviynw 429, aviynw3 429 at utilization 1.00; `unwalled:[]`). The tool's own advice text is excellent and says exactly this — the defect is that the projection needs a manual probe to self-heal at all. importance: normal — note: capacity.ts blindCount now counts readingStatus!=='fresh', not only probe failures — a stale-but-unprobed pool no longer yields a confident poolExhausted + owner-escalation verdict.\n- **P-008** `done` CARRIED, not re-verified this session — confirm before acting: `scheduler:get_next` headlines a CONCURRENCY-CAP block as \"no claimable work-item matched your spec within the floors\" (EI-19931420102632438); `fleet:leader-brief` reported `sessionState:\"recorded\"` + `stalled:true` for a session that was actively working and closed its item 8 min later (EI-19931924184335892); `P2P_LANE_EXCLUSION_TERMS` misses the hypercore/corestore substrate vocabulary (EI-19928699840338901). Also carried: a peer's CLAIM-PATH/READ-PATH DIVERGENCE report (282 rows passing every floor, claim path selected nothing, twice) which is a SEPARATE issue from the starvation and must not be folded into it. importance: normal — note: All four carried findings re-verified. EI-19931420102632438 + EI-19931924184335892: already DONE by the fleet, no action. EI-19928699840338901: re-measured and INVERTED — accepted hypercore/hyperblobs/hyperdrive/autobase, REJECTED corestore/seed cut/sparse seed/peer (+replicate) into the anti-terms with measurements; `peer` alone was 3-of-4 false at crit/major. Closed with D-007; 138/138, tsc clean. Claim-path/read-path divergence: confirmed LIVE and correctly kept separate — active peer lane (su-7eb2b/su-6dc49b99), not folded into starvation.\n- **P-009** `done` `session:request-compaction` acked with `respawn:true` on wake 7 but the cut never executed — an internal claude re-exec pre-empted it and context resumed at 79%. A requested compaction is not a performed compaction, and nothing distinguished the two until the next turn opened at the old context level. importance: normal — note: DONE 12:5xZ — the acked-but-never-cut case with NO host verdict row is now surfaced. isOrphanedPendingRespawn() decides it from the host's OWN stamped re-poll budget (capMs, read off the deciding row, default 360000ms + 120000ms grace); lostRespawnAmbientLine() (renamed from droppedRespawnAmbientLine) fires per-turn via coord:inbox on dropped OR orphaned, with distinct wording so an orphan never claims a verdict the host never wrote; priorRespawnNote() stops telling an orphan it is \"still re-polling\"/SUPERSEDED. Evidence: testing:run carry-respawn-outcome.test.ts + inbox-respawn-line.test.ts = 33 passed/0 failed/files:2; lint:tsc --files=<all 5 edited> exit=0 clean. Cap values measured from a real host log (su-b8422496 2026-08-09T01:46:12Z: 180000 first attempt, 360000 rearm).\n\n## Phase 2 — Unnecessary confusion\n\n- **P-010** `done` There is no authoritative fleet headcount. Within a few minutes the same fleet read as 11 members (leader-brief summary), then 11 rows and 14 rows (leader-brief members[], `include_stale:false` hiding stale-idle members), then 8 and 9 agents (fleet:assignments, claim-scoped). Every number is defensible and nothing reconciles them inline. The default that hides stale members hides them precisely when members are dying, which is when the count matters most. Fix: name the population in each response, or one `fleet:headcount` with an explicit breakdown. importance: normal — note: DONE 13:0xZ per D-008 — every fleet headcount now ships a census COMPUTED from the same predicate that filtered the rows (population/basis/candidates/counted/withheld/withheldReason/reveal, + `shown` when a byte budget trimmed the payload below the count). New: agent-tools/fleet/fleet-population.ts (selectFleetPopulation / withShownCount / renderPopulationCensus). Wired: leader-brief summary.population (selectLeaderBriefMembers now returns {rows, census}) and assignments summary.population (incl. the 22KB trim as `shown`). No new fleet:headcount tool — that would be a THIRD number to reconcile; see D-008. Evidence: testing:run 8 files = 280 passed/0 failed; lint:tsc --files=<all 5 edited> exit=0 clean.\n- **P-011** `done` The loop goal text prescribes a metric that cannot measure the mission: \"measure burn-down via `work_items:claimable` vs baseline 286\". Claimable count is not burn-down — the queue gains items continuously (one bug closed this run concerned a condition bridge minting ~150 junk work-items/hour), so a perfectly performing fleet can leave that number flat or rising. The real metric is terminal transitions, which I hand-rolled in SQL with a hand-maintained p2p title regex in every query. importance: high — note: DONE 13:4xZ — the hand-rolled half is gone. work_items:burn_down (which already computes the RIGHT metric: terminal transitions with fleet attribution) now takes `fence: 'p2p-lane'`, applying the SHARED buildP2pLaneFence() FilterNode through the SAME evaluator the claim path uses (matchesClaimSpecFilter + claimSpecSubjectFromWorkItem) — so a drain fleet measures burn-down over exactly the lane it may claim from, and the per-query title regex cannot drift from the claim scope by construction. Fence runs BEFORE the census so terminal.*/counts.*/deltaBy.* all describe one population; cohortAudit stays deliberately UNfenced (a named id dropped by a fence would report as MISSING). Reports fence:{lane,candidates,counted,excluded,note}. Evidence: testing:run burn_down.test.ts + p2p-lane-fence.test.ts = 96 passed/0 failed; lint:tsc --files exit=0 clean; lint:tool-prompts 55/55 (max=1498 < 1500). NOT FIXED (scoped out, stated not hidden): the wrong metric in the loop GOAL TEXT was self-authore…\n- **P-012** `done` Tools give contradictory advice with nothing reconciling them. At 02:31Z `fleet:leader-brief` said \"DO NOT fleet:bench this member... Wake it to re-run scheduler:get_next\" while `fleet:capacity` said \"place conservatively (top-ranked only), prefer a warm-inject over a fresh spawn\". Both were simultaneously true and pointed opposite ways; the leader has to know which layer dominates. importance: normal — note: ALREADY BUILT — verified by reading the code, not inferred. computeFleetBlockVerdict (leader-brief.ts:1222, doc block at :1178 cites this item's own 02:31Z measurement verbatim) arbitrates the flat co-firing alerts by PHYSICAL DEPENDENCY precedence — fleet-paused > inference-pool > spec-scope > claim-floors > members — so the leader is told WHICH layer dominates instead of picking one. Wired at :2270 and emitted as `blockedAt` ABOVE `summary` (:2372-2377) precisely because reading the flat booleans in field order is what produced the inverted remedy. Undefined when every member is working (not a reassuring \"layer: none\" row); an UNREAD pool can never promote layer `members`, whose remedy is the harmful one. Evidence: 19 references in leader-brief.test.ts (describe at :1500), all green in this session's run — testing:run 8 fleet files = 280 passed/0 failed.\n- **P-013** `done` `loop:checkpoint`'s `checks` array REPLACES the carried set, so re-sending a slightly reworded claim silently drops the original. Lost carried checks twice this way. The `checksDropped` warning arrives after the write, not before. Fix: upsert-by-id, or a merge mode. importance: normal — note: Both fixes the item names, shipped. (1) upsert-by-id: optional `id` on check/wall rows; `carryRowKey` = id else claim-text, TAGGED apart, driving all four identity decisions (dedup, inheritance, merge-upsert, drop-detection); round-trips through the rendered note as a `[#id]` prefix. (2) merge mode: `rowsMode:'merge'` on loop:checkpoint → mergeCarryRows({mode}), a pure upsertOntoPrior PRE-PASS so the normalizer still applies dedup/inheritance/cap exactly once; upserts hold prior position, `replace` stays default, merge+[] is a reported no-op. Also closed an adjacent silence merge would have made likely: the row cap always ate a SUPPLIED 13th row unreported (droppedChecks compares against the PRIOR set and structurally cannot see it) → new overflowChecks/overflowWalls + overflowNote. Files: carry-note.ts, agent-tools/loop/checkpoint.ts + both .test.ts. See D-009.\n- **P-014** `done` The carry-surface lints mangle the claims they quote and cannot distinguish speaker from actor. `absence_lint` stripped backticked identifiers out of my note and echoed back the incoherent claim `\"note there is NO column and NO top-level — the id column is )\"`, with a recheck instruction to grep for that string. `provenance_lint` flagged \"su-6dc49b99 fixed my reported defect\" as an unverified-action-claim — it cannot tell \"I did X\" from \"a peer reports they did X\", so recording a peer's claim as a peer's claim trips it. Both lints catch real classes and are worth keeping; the quoting is the bug. importance: normal — note: absence_lint now quotes the ORIGINAL span (not the redacted one); provenance_lint downgrades peer-reported actions. 95/95 unit, lint:tsc clean, test:affected passed.\n- **P-015** `done` Result-door / `projection` ergonomics cost several round-trips. The `pipe` operator shape (`[{op:\"grep\",pattern:\"...\"}]`) is not discoverable from the door's own hint, which foregrounds `pick`; a shell-style string errors. A `pick` whose paths match nothing returns a near-empty body headlined \"97% saved\", which reads as success — the \"pick path(s) matched nothing\" warning is correct but subordinate to a congratulatory statistic. Nested payload paths (`payload._completionEvidence`) are invisible to anyone guessing field names from `knownColumns`. importance: normal — note: Footer now leads with the caveat and drops the congratulatory 'saved' when degraded; a 42703 whose name is a jsonb KEY now returns the accessor. 174/174, tsc clean. Door-hint half measured ALREADY SHIPPED.\n- **P-016** `done` Ambient alarms are miscalibrated and flap, which trains the reader to ignore them. \"DISK 95% used on /home/marsh-office/.papercusp — writes are about to fail\" fired repeatedly with 90G free on a 1.9T volume. `green-checkpoint STALLED` / `RECOVERED` on oddsmith alternated several times inside one window. \"unaccounted cgroup(s) holding N processes\" escalated 1→2→3→4 cgroups and 7→35 processes and never resolved. \"REAPER WEDGED\" recurred against a 49k-item queue. importance: normal — note: Ambient alarms recalibrated (green-stall flap + REAPER WEDGED).
