WI-37360 covered the completion-evidence family; migration 778 covers the id/scope/severity family.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Treat \"confident zero / wrong-field reading\" as one bug class, not N unrelated defects\nDate: 2026-08-09\nFive findings in this run look unrelated and are one class: a measurement structurally unable to see the thing it was asked about, rendered with full confidence and no uncertainty marker.\n\n- `work_items:burn_down` at limit:5 → `terminal.total 0` for a fleet that had closed 71 (P-001)\n- `fleet:leader-brief` → `throttled: 0` while the pool sat at `factor 0` (P-002)\n- `coord:send` → `counts:{ok:1,failed:0}` having reached 6 of 11 (P-003)\n- `completion_ref` → null on 2657/2657 rows, read as \"no close carries evidence\" (P-004)\n- `terminal_completion_ref` → 2.9% vs a 37.8% baseline, read as \"thin closes\", when the canonical field said 94.3% vs 56.5%\n\nThe class already has precedent in this repo: CLAUDE.md documents `tsc -p .` typechecking zero files and reporting clean, `test:affected` selecting zero suites and reporting passed, and a `-t` filter matching zero tests and exiting 0. Those are all the same defect wearing different clothes.\n\nRULING: fix these as a class, and adopt the general rule in P-020 — a bounded, filtered, or empty measurement must carry that fact ON THE AGGREGATE, not only on the row list it happened to bound. A `0` that means \"I could not see\" must be distinguishable from a `0` that means \"I looked and there was nothing\".\n\nWhy this matters more than the individual bugs: each of these failed in the direction that invited a HARMFUL next action — re-fire the gate, wake the starved members, report zero progress, re-audit healthy closes. A signal that fails toward inaction is cheap; these fail toward action.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-020\n\n### D-002 — Diagnose the substrate before the logic — check the pool that GATES the agents before the rules they run\nDate: 2026-08-09\nWhen several independent health signals all read fine but the OUTCOME is zero, suspect a shared upstream RESOURCE, not N separate bugs.\n\nMeasured this run: at 02:26Z the fleet showed 5 holding / 5 idle with zero closes in 40 minutes. Presence said every member was live. The claim spec said 293 items claimable of 457 matched, all ~12 floors passing. The loop said active. Every instrument was green and the output was zero.\n\nThe cause was one rate-limited account: `usableAccounts 1`, `factor 0`, tier2 `inFlight 3` against `cap 20` with `queued 28`. The decisive detail is `inFlight 3 << cap 20` — the tier cap was not binding, so the constraint could only be account availability.\n\nThe reason every instrument read green is that every leader-facing tool reasons from member-local fields and is blind to the pool. They therefore fail in the SAME direction simultaneously and converge on one recommendation — \"wake the members\" — which is the single action that makes starvation worse.\n\nCONFIRMED BY RECOVERY, which is what makes this a ruling rather than a theory: I changed nothing about fleet logic, spec, or headcount, and throughput went from 0 closes/40min to 18 closes/30min purely as utilization fell 0.78 → 0.39. That is a clean falsification of the claim-path hypothesis I had pre-registered in my own checkpoint.\n\nRULING: the diagnostic order for \"members idle while work is claimable\" is (1) `fleet:capacity` — factor, usableAccounts, queued-vs-inFlight, and `blind`; (2) claim floors; (3) spec scope; (4) the member itself. My previous checkpoint prescribed the reverse and cost half a wake. P-019 asks for this ordering to be built into leader-brief so a leader does not have to remember it.\n\nCOROLLARY (P-006): under starvation, members do not crash — they are REAPED. Pool at factor 0 → wake fires → no capacity → no turn produced → the stalled-loops guard disarms the loop. \"Member died\" and \"member was starved\" are indistinguishable from the leader's side, which is why the wake-8 loss of 40% of the fleet read as an unexplained mystery.\nRelated: P-002, P-006, P-019, P-023\n\n### D-003 — Prefer SURFACING existing capability over building new — two of my \"missing features\" already shipped\nDate: 2026-08-09\nBefore writing this audit I verified my \"the system lacks X\" claims, because asserting a false absence is the exact error this plan is about. Two of the capabilities I was about to request already exist:\n\n1. **`work_items:burn_down`** — \"One-call leader census for a harness work queue: terminal counts, in-flight rows with assignee liveness, parked rows, unclaimed rows... `since` for itemized closed/opened deltas... Replaces hand-joining work_items:list with coord:presence for drain/fleet leader wakes.\" It also grades structured completion evidence via `ids` cohortAudit. This is precisely the burn-down tool I hand-rolled in SQL all night, INCLUDING the evidence verdict that would have prevented my false \"thin closes\" report entirely.\n\n2. **`fleet:invariant`** — registers custom read-only SQL evaluated on every `fleet:leader-brief` read, contract rows-returned == violated. A leader can register \"claim spec revision or kind has drifted from owner scope\" and have the brief police it automatically. That is most of the spec-drift alerting requested in P-021, available today.\n\nI used neither, across a full overnight run, while actively wanting both. Nothing surfaced them: not the wake prompt, not `fleet:leader-brief`'s own \"See also\", not the loop goal text — which instead prescribed a metric that cannot measure the mission (P-011).\n\nRULING: treat this as a DISCOVERABILITY defect of equal weight to the missing-feature it masquerades as. Concretely: (a) `fleet:leader-brief` should name `work_items:burn_down` and `fleet:invariant` in its See-also; (b) the fleet-leader playbook should prescribe registering a scope invariant at fleet launch; (c) before any Phase 3 item is built, check whether it exists — P-019/P-022 have NOT been checked as thoroughly as P-021 was.\n\nCaveat recorded honestly: burn_down being present does not make it correct — it returns a confident 0 at small `limit` (P-001). Discovering it is necessary but not sufficient.\nRelated: P-019, P-021, P-022\n\n### D-004 — Why this is a new plan and not a continuation of the 2026-07-10 fleet-leader plans\nDate: 2026-08-09\n`plans:new` correctly refused this plan with `similar_exists`, naming five overlapping plans. Recording the review so nobody re-litigates it, and so plan history is not silently split.\n\nNearest neighbours:\n- `fleet-leader-frictions-six-improvements-2026-07-10` (shipped, similarity 0.854) — six improvements from the p2p-parity night: launch honesty, liveness verdict, claim renewal, inbox economics, completion audit, drained push.\n- `fleet-reliability-verification-2026-07-10` (ready, similarity 0.840)\n- `queen-fleet-authority-boundary-2026-07-02` (shipped, 0.833)\n- `backend-reliability-100pct-2026-07-03` (ready, 0.821)\n- `feature-adoption-health` (active, 0.788)\n\nDECISION: forced past the guard. These are a month old, from a different night, a different fleet, and a different failure mode — that run's theme was launch/liveness/claim-renewal honesty; this run's is measurement instruments returning confident wrong values under resource starvation. No finding in this plan appears in any of them, and the four bugs filed here (WI-37161, WI-37162, WI-37360, WI-37381) are all new this run.\n\nGENUINE OVERLAP worth a reader's attention: `fleet-leader-frictions-six-improvements-2026-07-10` includes a \"liveness verdict\" and a \"completion audit\" item. P-010 (no authoritative headcount) and P-004 (completion-evidence field triplication) are adjacent to those. Whoever picks up either item should read the 2026-07-10 plan first — if its liveness/completion work shipped and these problems persist, that is a stronger and more interesting finding than either item alone, and it should be recorded there rather than here.\n\nThe guard did its job. This note is the cost of overriding it.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-005 — A BLIND capacity reading may not instruct an owner escalation — the caveat now REPLACES the escalation clause, it no longer merely composes with it\nDate: 2026-08-09\nImplementing P-007 required reversing a deliberate prior contract, so recording it rather than leaving it in a diff.\n\n#### What changed\n`buildCapacityReport` (packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/capacity-dispatch.ts) previously PREPENDED a `⚠ BLIND READING` caveat and then still emitted the `DOMINANT CAUSE … OWNER-GATED … escalate rather than waiting for a quota reset` clause. `capacity-dispatch.test.ts` pinned that with `assert.match(r.advice, /BLIND READING[\\s\\S]*EXHAUSTED[\\s\\S]*OWNER-GATED/)` and the comment \"composes, doesn't replace\". As of this change, a majority-blind reading suppresses the causal attribution and the escalation instruction entirely, substituting \"NOT an owner escalation: re-run accounts:probe-capacity first\".\n\n#### Why the reversal is warranted, not a regression\n1. **The prior test contradicted its own stated purpose.** Its comment says the point of folding stale readings into `blindCount` was to stop the tool \"rendering a confident quota-shaped exhaustion + owner-escalation verdict off data nobody has looked at in over half an hour.\" The implementation prepended the warning but kept the verdict — so one advice string carried both \"do NOT treat an owner-escalation reading below as confirmed\" and \"escalate rather than waiting\". The imperative is the half that gets acted on.\n2. **Measured twice in one session, both false.** 2026-08-09T05:11Z on fleet `nonp2p-bug-drain`: `blind:true`, `blindAccounts:2`, `usableAccounts:0`, `factor:0`, advice asserting a broken egress path as an OWNER-GATED infra issue. A live `accounts:probe-capacity` moments later: aviynw 429, aviynw3 200 (util 0.14), aviynw10 200 (0.60), avi_storewolf.com 200 (0.99) — THREE OF FOUR ANSWERING. An earlier instance the same session was likewise falsified by probe. Relaying either would have sent the owner after infrastructure that was not broken.\n3. **The failure direction is the expensive one.** A signal that fails toward inaction is cheap; this one manufactures an OWNER ESCALATION out of a stale projection.\n\n#### Scope of the suppression — deliberately narrow\n`poolExhausted` stays true and \"HOLD placements\" is unchanged: the OPERATIONAL half of the advice was always correct. Only the CAUSAL attribution and the escalation instruction are withheld, and only when `blind` is true (majority of accounts carrying an unreliable reading). A MEASURED edge-throttle majority still escalates exactly as before — pinned by a companion test whose only difference from the suppression test is `blindCount: 0`, so the guard cannot pass for the trivial reason that the fixture never reaches the branch.\n\n#### Relationship to WI-36943 (done 03:35Z)\nDifferent axis, not a duplicate. WI-36943 added an `inFlight > 0 && edge + wall < total` guard: it DISPROVES a dead proxy from live traffic. That guard structurally could not fire on the 05:11Z reading (`inFlight:0`, and `edge + wall === total`). This one refuses to make the claim at all when the underlying measurements are stale — absence of evidence rather than evidence of absence.\n\n#### Generalization\nSame family as P-020: a measurement that cannot see the thing, rendered with full confidence, whose invited next action is harmful. The rule this ratifies: **a tool may not prescribe an irreversible or owner-facing action from a reading it has already flagged as unreliable.** Flagging unreliability and then issuing the confident imperative anyway is not a compromise between the two — it is the confident imperative.\nRelated: P-007, P-012, P-019\n\n### D-006 — P-006's stated fix is UNSOUND as written — do NOT gate the disarm on a GLOBAL pool reading\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-006 says: \"the disarm guard should check pool state before attributing a no-turn fire to a dead loop.\" Implemented literally that is WRONG, and it would re-open WI-6639 fleet-wide. Recording this before anyone picks the item up, because the item text invites exactly the wrong build.\n\nWHAT ALREADY EXISTS (check before building — D-003 again). `stalled-loops-guard.ts` already carries a `vetoedByProviderWall` exemption (EI-19441932615368003): it reads `computeLifecycleBackoff` on THAT loop's own last delivery outcome and refuses to disarm while a provider-wall backoff is still in the future. That is the sound form of P-006 and it is already shipped. It is PER-LOOP and keyed on evidence about that specific loop.\n\nWHY THE GLOBAL VERSION IS UNSOUND. `fleet:capacity.factor` is a WORKSPACE-WIDE scalar. Gating disarms on it vetoes EVERY disarm during any starved window — genuine corpses included — and starvation windows are exactly when the guard matters. Worse, per WI-36792's measured lesson, the blunting is INVISIBLE: a reaper that stops reaping still reports `checked: N`, so nobody notices it stopped working.\n\nTHE GENERAL RULE, measured on this very module 2026-08-09 (WI-36792 Part 2, memory 120a42a6): when adding a veto to a reaper, the question is never \"does this signal identify my case?\" but \"what ELSE converges on this signal's steady state, and does it then look like my case PERMANENTLY?\" A corpse does not merely tolerate a starved pool — it is indistinguishable from a starved-but-live agent for as long as the wall lasts, and a global signal cannot separate them even in principle. That is why the sound veto is keyed on per-loop evidence (a backoff this loop actually recorded), not on an ambient condition.\n\nRESIDUAL GAP, still open and genuinely narrower than P-006 claims: a fire that lands while the pool has NO capacity may produce no lifecycle-death outcome at all, so `computeLifecycleBackoff` has nothing to read and the existing veto abstains. Anyone taking this must (a) FIRST measure whether that population is non-empty — a census of real recent disarms over `harness_shared.routines` + `autoloop_state`, never fixtures alone — and (b) key any new veto on per-loop evidence with a liveness term, never on the ambient pool factor. If the census is empty, close P-006 as already-fixed rather than adding an exemption that only blunts the guard.\n\nI did NOT edit stalled-loops-guard for this: WI-36792 (done 04:10Z) was a peer's active lane in this exact file, and colliding there would be the same instrumentation-blindness this plan is about, one level up.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-007 — The p2p-lane fence takes the substrate COMPONENT NAMES but rejects corestore/seed-cut/peer — a carried finding that inverted on re-measurement\nDate: 2026-08-09\nEI-19928699840338901 asked to absorb a substrate tranche into the shared P2P_LANE_EXCLUSION_TERMS: corestore, hypercore, seed cut / seed cuts / sparse seed, bootstrap peer, and (flagged by its own author as broad) peer. P-008 exists to RE-VERIFY carried findings rather than act on them, and this one inverted.\n\nRULING — accepted: hypercore, hyperblobs, hyperdrive, autobase. Rejected into P2P_LANE_REJECTED_ANTI_TERMS with their measurements: corestore, seed cut, seed cuts, sparse seed, peer, replicate, replicates.\n\nWHY (measured 2026-08-09 against the live papercusp backlog: open, issue-family, net-new = not already caught by an existing term):\n\n- corestore — 13 net-new, and overwhelmingly LOCAL work. This repo BUNDLES a corestore seed into the desktop release, so the storage vocabulary leads a second life in release engineering that hyperbee/hyperswarm/hyperdht do not have: a git-tracked-blob history purge (WI-3065), a bundle-size review (WI-5640), a single-process advisory lock (WI-4236), the local operator's fd-lock colliding with the cut (EI-9796, EI-12625, EI-17145, EI-17165). The item's OWN motivating critical, EI-19899917753028359, is itself a LOCAL deadlock — bg-host holding the corestore write lock against a booted:false report on the same box. Fencing it would have hidden from the fleet a critical the fleet can actually fix.\n- seed cut / seed cuts / sparse seed — 5 / 1 / 2, the release pipeline rather than the wire (WI-10773 \"take a REAL release seed cut and MEASURE the size drop\"; WI-36770 bg-host self-recycling at an 11-12GB heap).\n- peer — 10 net-new open bugs, 1 critical + 3 major, and the worst false-positive ratio ever measured on this list. \"Peer\" is THE word this system uses for ANOTHER AGENT. Exactly ONE of the four critical/major hits is p2p (EI-18769415639448677); the other three are ordinary single-box bugs whose titles merely say \"a peer's committed drop\" (EI-19460048118267666), \"a peer's verified fact\" (EI-19478538852465365), \"PEER agents' session turns\" (WI-9592). This is the `hive` mistake (WI-7184) with a bigger blast radius.\n\nSEPARATELY REJECTED — the stem-closing move, which nobody asked for but which this module's own history makes the obvious next step. `replication` is a noun with one meaning here, so it stays; its verb inflections do NOT follow the federation→federated→federate→federates→federating precedent, because \"replicate\" is a common DEBUGGING VERB in this pot (\"replicate the floor set\", \"the spike replicates 2/2 boots\"). A pattern that held twice is not thereby a rule.\n\nTHE GENERAL POINT, which is why this is a Decision and not a comment: the admission test in p2p-lane-fence.ts is \"a whole-word title match must IMPLY work a single-box member CANNOT execute\" — not \"the term is p2p vocabulary\". Those come apart precisely for the substrate layer, because the substrate is also a local artifact this repo builds and ships. A term that merely CORRELATES with p2p belongs in the anti-terms list, and over-fencing is the more expensive error: it hides work while the lane still looks healthy, so nothing appears wrong.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR LIVE FLEETS: fleet nonp2p-bug-drain's spec rev7 still carries the interim hand-typed local exclusion (corestore, hypercore, seed cut, seed cuts, sparse seed, bootstrap peer, peer) that EI-19928699840338901 added as an explicitly TEMPORARY mitigation. Under this ruling that block is over-fencing ~20 open items, 3 of them legitimate majors, and it is also the per-fleet hand-typing the fence macro exists to end. It should be replaced with view.fence:\"p2p-lane\". NOT done in this pass: peers are mid-diagnosis of a claim-path divergence against rev7 and re-steering the spec would invalidate their repro.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-008 — D-008 — every fleet headcount ships a computed census; no new `fleet:headcount` tool\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-010 offered two fixes: name the population in each response, or add one `fleet:headcount` with an explicit breakdown. RULING: name the population in each response — and derive the name from the same predicate that produced the rows.\n\nWHY NOT A NEW TOOL. A separate `fleet:headcount` would be a THIRD number to reconcile, not a reconciliation. The divergence is not that no authoritative count exists; it is that each existing count is silent about which population it counted. A new tool leaves leader-brief's own `summary.members` vs `members[]` mismatch exactly as it was, and adds a round-trip a leader must know to make.\n\nWHY STRUCTURAL, NOT DOCUMENTARY. A `population: '...'` string set by hand beside a separately-computed count is the arrangement that drifts — the label keeps describing what the filter USED to do. So `selectFleetPopulation(candidates, keep, meta)` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-population.ts) takes the candidates AND the predicate and returns `{ rows, census }` from one pass. There is no supported way to publish a census that disagrees with the rows shipped beside it.\n\nTHE CONVENTION, for anyone adding or changing a fleet count: do not filter a roster and publish `x.length`. Filter through `selectFleetPopulation` and publish its census beside the count. If a later byte/row budget trims what actually ships, record that with `withShownCount` — it is a SECOND, independent reduction (the filter's verdict vs what survived transport) and one number cannot honestly stand for both.\n\nTWO JUDGEMENT CALLS worth stating, because both are places a future edit could quietly make the field useless:\n1. `withheld` counts ONLY the discretionary cut (stale-idle). Roster membership (`fleetSlug === fleet`) is not counted as withholding — folding other fleets in would make `withheld` grow with unrelated fleets and read as mass concealment.\n2. `withheldReason` is null when `withheld` is 0. A reason attached to zero rows reads as an admission that something is hidden and trains readers to discount the field on the calls where it is real.\n\nAPPLIED: `fleet:leader-brief` (summary.population) and `fleet:assignments` (summary.population, incl. the byte-budget `shown`). NOT applied to `fleet:status`, which already splits its roster into separately-named populations (memberCount = visible desktop su members, beeCount = background loop bees) and so does not have this defect.\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-009 — Carried-row identity is carryRowKey(id ?? claim); merge is OPT-IN and replace stays the default\nDate: 2026-08-09\nSettled while building P-013. Governs every carry surface that stores {claim, recheck, verified} rows — notably `work_items:checkpoint`, which has the IDENTICAL replace-semantics defect (EI-19460631385508515) and will face these same three choices.\n\n**1. Identity is `carryRowKey(row)` = `id` when present, else trimmed claim text — tagged apart (`id:` / `claim:`) so the namespaces cannot collide.** Used for EVERY identity decision at once: dedup, inheritance of recheck/verified/sinceMs, merge-upsert, and drop-detection. Keying on claim TEXT alone is what made a re-worded claim a NEW row — it silently lost its inherited evidence and age, and the old wording reported as a vanished claim. One key function, or those four decisions drift apart.\n\n**2. `replace` STAYS the default; `merge` is opt-in (`rowsMode`).** Tempting to flip the default, since the additive write is the common one — but replace is the ONLY way to retire a stale row. Making merge the default would silently change semantics for every existing caller AND leave no way to clear. Corollary: under merge, `[]` is a NO-OP, not a clear, and the reply says so — otherwise a caller reads a silent no-op as a clear that failed.\n\n**3. A row `id` must round-trip through the RENDERED note, or it is not identity at all.** These rows persist as markdown lines and are re-parsed on the next wake, so an id held only in memory would vanish exactly when it is needed (across the wake boundary that motivated the whole feature). Anchor: a `[#id]` prefix, charset `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,40}` — no whitespace, no `]`, so it can never swallow claim text. Out-of-charset input is REPAIRED (`Gate Green!` -> `gate-green`), never rejected: an id rides attached to a multi-KB note, and this file's established rule is repair-don't-refuse (WI-7264).\n\n**4. Adding a merge mode obliges you to close the cap-overflow silence too.** The row cap (12) always dropped a supplied row past the limit without reporting it, because the drop report compares against the PRIOR set and cannot see it. Under merge, carried rows hold their slots, so it is the caller's NEW row that falls off — i.e. merge makes a pre-existing silent loss far likelier to fire. Shipping the mode without `overflowChecks`/`overflowWalls` would have re-created, on the additive path, the exact silence the mode exists to remove.\n\n**What NOT to do:** do not \"fix\" this by raising the row cap (it bounds what re-injects into EVERY future wake — the reason it exists), and do not add a second dropped-rows report keyed differently from `carryRowKey`; a second opinion on identity is a second bug (the D-005 lesson).\nRelated: P-013\n\n### D-010 — REAPER WEDGED requires a real stuck backlog, not just the clock — overturns work-queue-stuck-item-recovery P-009's clock-only crit\nDate: 2026-08-09\nRULING: `workItemsStatus` no longer returns 'crit' on `reaperStale && reaperAgeSec != null` alone. Both the SEVERITY (thresholds.ts) and the \"— REAPER WEDGED\" TEXT (compute.ts) now derive from one shared predicate `isReaperWedged({ reaperStale, reaperAgeSec, stuckTotal })`, which additionally requires `stuckTotal > 0` (stuckFeatures + deadHeldClaims + deadAssignedIssues + deadHeldAssignments).\n\nTHIS OVERTURNS A PRIOR PLAN'S RATIFIED BEHAVIOUR. work-queue-stuck-item-recovery P-009 established the clock-only crit, and its test asserted `workItemsStatus({ reaperStale: true, reaperAgeSec: 600 }) === 'crit'` with no backlog. That assertion is INVERTED to 'warn' as part of this decision — recorded here rather than left as an unexplained test edit.\n\nWHY (measured, not inferred). The alarm summary appends `, N stuck` only when stuckTotal > 0. The live 2026-08-09 crit read \"20017 items — 60 todo, 9 in-flight, 120 blocked, 55 need human — REAPER WEDGED\" with NO stuck segment. Verified against the RELEASE checkout that actually emitted it (papercup-release compute.ts:526 carries the identical stuck segment; thresholds.ts:251 carries the clock-only crit), so the absent segment is genuine evidence that stuckTotal === 0, not a wording difference. A reaper with an empty recovery backlog has nothing it failed to do — \"stuck items accumulate silently\" is the harm the crit names, and that harm was measurably absent. The crit therefore recurred every tick and never resolved.\n\nCONSISTENCY: this does not invent a rule, it finishes one. EI-2534 had ALREADY decided that a stale reaper is crit-worthy only alongside a real stranded backlog, and applied it to the null-age branch (thresholds.ts:305). The known-age branch was simply never brought into line. The two branches now agree.\n\nTHE SIGNAL IS NOT LOST — it is de-escalated. `if (d.reaperStale) return 'warn'` still fires, and the `reaper age` metric still renders warn. A stale reaper remains visible; it stops paging when nothing is rotting.\n\nSCOPE / NON-GOAL: this is a calibration of the WEDGED cause-claim only. A wedged reaper WITH a stranded backlog is still crit (test: reaperStale + age 600 + deadHeldClaims 3 => crit), which preserves P-009's actual concern. Nothing about the reaper's own behaviour changed.\n\nGENERAL RULE FOR PEERS: softening an alarm's wording without moving its severity is cosmetic and strictly worse than leaving it alone — the reader still gets paged and now has less information. This fix nearly shipped in exactly that broken form: the compute.ts text was gated on stuckTotal while workItemsStatus still crit'd on the clock. Before you believe you have changed what a reader experiences, grep every OTHER consumer of the same underlying signal.\nRelated: P-016\n\n### D-011 — P-022's delta is BOUNDARY-EXPLICIT and PER-AXIS HONEST — and 2 of its 4 axes need no new storage\nDate: 2026-08-09\nMEASURED BEFORE BUILDING (the P-015/P-016 discipline — half this plan's items turned out already handled). Of P-022's four named axes:\n\n- **closes +N — ALREADY SHIPPED, and richer than P-022 asks.** `work_items:burn_down { since }` returns `terminal.delta`, a four-way attribution split `deltaBy {fleet, otherAgents, system, unattributed}` with `deltaByPartitions` proving it sums exactly, a `deltaClosedUndated` FLOOR marker, plus itemized `closedSince` / `openedSince` rows. Its own source comment already names \"the burn-down delta a monitor loop otherwise has to re-derive by diffing\". Nothing to build.\n- **members ±N — DERIVABLE, no storage.** `harness_shared.fleet_membership_events` is a durable join/leave log (workspace_id, fleet_slug, owner_id, event, at) with a `(workspace_id, fleet_slug, id DESC)` index. Count events after the boundary.\n- **spec rev X→Y — PARTIAL.** `bee_claim_specs`/`cup_claim_specs` carry `revision` + `updated_at` point-in-time only; there is no revisions history table. \"Did it change since T, by whom, when\" is derivable; the PRIOR revision number X is not, and needs a snapshot.\n- **pool factor A→B — NOT derivable.** Capacity is computed live; `routine_pool_shed_events` is a shed log, not a factor history. Needs a snapshot.\n\nWHAT ACTUALLY DOES NOT EXIST is the BOUNDARY, not the data. `fleet:leader-brief` carries no delta of any kind — every field is point-in-time, and it takes no `since` arg. `fleet-transition-events.ts` does hold a previous snapshot, but it is an in-memory Map inside a periodic sweep serving event EMISSION; it is not a per-leader wake boundary and cannot survive the leader's own cold respawn.\n\nRULING:\n\n1. `fleet:leader-brief` gains a `delta` block whose `since` is REPORTED, never implied. Precedence: explicit `args.since` > the leader's persisted last-wake snapshot > null.\n2. **Per-axis availability is explicit.** Each axis reports `{ current, previous, delta, available, reason? }`. An axis with no baseline reports `available:false` + a reason — NEVER `delta: 0`. This is the plan's own central bug class (a bounded/absent measurement rendered as a confident number, cf. WI-37381's `burn_down` limit bug reporting `terminal.total 0` against a true 1693). A \"nothing changed\" that actually means \"I have no baseline\" would be this plan reproducing the defect it was written to catalogue.\n3. **The snapshot rotates per WAKE, not per READ.** Keyed on the caller's loop `fireCount`: a second brief read inside the same wake returns the SAME delta rather than a freshly-zeroed one. Rotating on every read would make the tool blind itself — the exact failure caught in P-006, where a repair wrote to the record its own falsifier reads. With no armed loop the boundary is honestly labelled per-read instead of per-wake.\n4. **Storage is a dedicated table keyed (workspace_id, fleet_slug, owner_id).** NOT `coord_watermarks`: its `Watermark` type lives in the generic borrowable lib `libs/generic/pubsub-substrate`, so a papercusp fleet snapshot there is a domain leak, and its documented write semantics are deliberately non-monotonic for at-least-once redelivery — wrong contract for a value snapshot. NOT `agent_fleets`: its PK is (workspace, fleet_slug) with no per-leader dimension, so two readers of one fleet would steal each other's baseline — the same blinding as (3). NOT routine metadata: a leader need not have a loop, and mutable routine metadata is already the sole record of loop disarms with no audit trail (peer finding, su-145fd394).\nRelated: P-022\n\n### D-012 — The per-member idle oracle is SUBORDINATE to the fleet block verdict — and two of P-023's five named causes are not member-level causes at all\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-023 asks for a per-member oracle over five causes: throttled / spec-mismatched / floor-blocked / mid-turn / genuinely idle. Built as `computeMemberIdleVerdict` (pure, `fleet-member-idle-verdict.ts`), with three deliberate departures from the item text.\n\n**1. IT DEFERS TO `computeFleetBlockVerdict` (P-019) RATHER THAN RE-DERIVING ITS OWN ANSWER.** This is the whole design. P-002 measured the fleet-level form of this bug: the brief blamed the MEMBER while the pool sat at `factor 0`, and its remedy (\"wake it to re-run scheduler:get_next\") added another request behind the same congestion. A per-member oracle that reasons independently reproduces that inversion ONCE PER MEMBER — and does so with more apparent authority, because a specific per-member reason reads as better evidence than a fleet-wide one, so it is believed harder. When `blockedAt` names any layer, the member verdict is `fleet-blocked`, carries the dominating layer verbatim in `dominatedBy`, and its remedy points at `blockedAt.remedy`. It never emits a wake instruction in that state.\n\n**2. `spec-mismatched` AND `floor-blocked` ARE NOT PER-MEMBER CAUSES.** They are properties of the SPEC and the QUEUE: every member inheriting the fleet spec shares them identically. Reporting them per-member would print one fleet-scope fact N times as though it were N independent findings, and invite a leader to act on a member over a condition no member action can change. They resolve to `fleet-blocked` with `dominatedBy: 'spec-scope' | 'claim-floors'`. The one real exception is a member carrying its OWN bee-level spec: that member is flagged `ownSpecUnresolved: true` rather than being silently given the fleet's answer — unknown is stated, never rounded.\n\n**3. THREE CAUSES ADDED BEYOND THE FIVE, each because a flat brief cannot distinguish it from \"genuinely idle\" while its remedy differs.** `stalled-holder` (holding a claim that is not advancing); `no-self-wake` (`loopMode` null AND `nextFireAt` null — the documented signature from EI-18730414627683753, where a leader had to read exactly those two fields by hand to catch a permanently dormant member; deliberately NOT a `loopArmed` boolean, which is not plumbed to this layer and reads stale-true for a warm-dead session per EI-14702/WI-6639); and `context-exhausted` (about to compact, so do not hand it work first).\n\n**ORDERING IS PHYSICAL DOMINANCE, NOT SEVERITY** (the rule P-019 established): `working` → `mid-turn` → `stalled-holder` → `fleet-blocked` → `throttled` → `session-ending` → `no-self-wake` → `context-exhausted` → `genuinely-idle`. Each earlier cause makes every later one UNOBSERVABLE, not merely less important. Three placements are load-bearing: `mid-turn` sits ABOVE `fleet-blocked` because a member still emitting tool calls is not being prevented from anything whatever the fleet state; `throttled` sits BELOW it because when the whole pool is congested that is one story, not N; and `stalled-holder` sits ABOVE `fleet-blocked` because a stranded claim is a member-level fact the fleet state did not create — the work was taken BEFORE the block and needs reclaiming regardless.\n\n**THAT LAST PLACEMENT WAS FOUND BY RUNNING THE ORACLE OVER THIS FLEET'S REAL ROWS, NOT BY REASONING.** Two members (su-a809c, su-3fb70) held work-items with `load 1` + `stalled` during the wind-down; with `stalled-holder` absent they both reported merely `fleet-blocked`, which hid the one thing the leader actually had to act on. The unit suite was fully green at the time. A verdict oracle's ordering is only testable against a real population — synthetic cases confirm the branches, they do not reveal a missing one.\n\n**`genuinely-idle` IS THE ONLY CAUSE WHOSE REMEDY IS A WAKE**, and a test asserts no other cause can emit one. That is the single instruction P-002 showed being given at exactly the wrong times.\n\n`idleCauses` rolls the verdicts into counts as a PARTIAL map: a cause that never fired is ABSENT rather than reported as 0, since a zero reads as a measured absence — the same rule as D-011's per-axis availability.\n\n### D-013 — P-024: the priority substrate ALREADY EXISTS and is now live — the real gap is claim-state, and the buildable half is the leader's missing third option\nDate: 2026-08-09\nMEASURED BEFORE BUILDING (the discipline that has now changed the build on P-015, P-016, P-022 and P-023). P-024 reads as \"there is no priority or reservation in a scarce pool\". That premise is no longer true, and acting on it as written would have built a second priority system beside a working one.\n\n**WHAT ALREADY EXISTS.** `libs/papercusp-shared/src/resilience/priority-admission.ts` implements a full admission-priority substrate: `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_PRIORITY_MAP` (queen/interactive 1, su 2, bee/cup 3, gym/benchmark 4, default 5), `tierOf` resolving the `x-papercusp-priority` header — which ALREADY accepts a bare numeric tier — `defaultTierCaps` giving per-tier in-flight caps, a reserved tier-1 floor (`tier1Reserve`), and `priorityFromLabel` giving a numeric WITHIN-band ordering. `gateway-priority-tiers.test.ts` demonstrates exactly P-024's desired behaviour: a request \"queued LAST but tier 1\" is admitted ahead of earlier lower-tier work.\n\n**IT WAS INERT WHEN THIS PLAN WAS WRITTEN, AND IS NOT INERT NOW.** WI-4542 (\"Gateway priority tiers are ~inert in production: nearly ALL live traffic arrives UNTAGGED and lands in tier 5\") is **done**, closed 2026-08-02 with live evidence: byPriority moved from `[{priority:0,count:3}]` to `[{priority:40,...}]` and byTier from tier-5-dominant to tier-2-dominant. Confirmed independently here at 2026-08-09T21:0xZ via `gateway:status`: `byTier` = t1[0/24] t2[inFlight 2, cap 20] t3[0/15] t4[0/1] t5[0/1], `tier1Reserve: 1`, and su traffic is landing in tier 2 as designed. So P-024's motivating observation was real, but its cause was the TAGGING gap — already fixed by another lane — not a missing mechanism.\n\n**THE RESIDUAL THAT IS GENUINELY MISSING** is narrower than the item text: nothing derives priority from a member's CLAIM STATE. Every fleet member of the same role carries the same label, hence the same tier and the same numeric ordering, so a member holding work and an idle member polling for work remain indistinguishable to the gateway — which is the specific contention P-024 names.\n\n**THAT RESIDUAL IS NOT SOUNDLY BUILDABLE FROM THE LEADER'S SIDE TODAY, AND IS FILED RATHER THAN HALF-BUILT.** The priority label is stamped at SPAWN time (`spawn-env.ts` from `opts.role`), so a running member's header is fixed for its lifetime. Making priority track claim state requires a per-REQUEST derivation in the request path — a change to the gateway/spawn seam, not to fleet tooling. Building a leader-side label lever on top of a spawn-time header would produce a control that silently does nothing, which is the failure mode this whole plan catalogues.\n\n**WHAT IS BUILDABLE, AND IS THE HALF THAT ANSWERS THE ITEM'S ACTUAL COMPLAINT.** P-024's operative sentence is not about tiers at all — it is: \"instead of choosing between benching members (losing pickup readiness) and letting them add queue depth.\" That is a leader facing a two-option dilemma and wanting a third. The third option exists in this system and is not a priority change: park an idle member on the `work-item:claimable` event instead of letting it poll. That preserves pickup readiness (the member re-enters the moment work appears) while removing its polls from the queue — precisely the property benching destroys. `computePoolReservation` implements that as a pure policy, keyed on pool scarcity plus the per-member idle cause from D-012, and it recommends nothing at all when the pool is not scarce.\n\n**A RESERVATION POLICY MUST NEVER HOLD BACK A HOLDER.** The dispositions are `protect` (holds work — never held back, whatever the pressure), `hold-back` (idle poller, only under real scarcity), and `unaffected`. Recommending anything against a holder would strand in-flight work to relieve congestion the holder is not causing — the inversion P-002 measured, in a new costume.\nRelated: P-024\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"focus-kit-2026-08-09","title":"Papercusp Focus Kit — 3 local-first web apps on one shared UI + one shared store","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercusp Focus Kit — 3 local-first web apps on one shared UI + one shared store\nslug: focus-kit-2026-08-09\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-08-09\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** SHIPPED. All nine items done. The Focus Kit — Pomodoro, Habits, Journal — runs from `npm run serve` in `~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/focus-kit` (own git repo, 2 commits, working tree clean). 78 tests green on node's built-in runner, zero dependencies. The acceptance test was driven end to end in a real browser: all three apps used, tab CLOSED, fresh tab reopened, every app's data intact; a next-day rollover was simulated and streaks survived it while the new day started clean. Goal `ship-the-papercusp-focus-kit-3-local-first-web-a-84cff3` marked achieved.\n\n**Next:** Nothing autonomous remains. ONE OWNER WALL, named and not attempted: public hosting (a host, a domain, TLS) — real spend and an outward-facing publish, so it is the owner's call. It blocks distribution only, never construction. Two platform bugs were filed from this build and are the useful follow-ups for someone else: EI-19964793024613369 (dedup is unsound as documented — search:semantic does not cover plans, and plans:* return a filePath that does not exist) and EI-19964643447670242 (GOAL mode requires reporting spend the platform cannot measure). Also EI-19964308537296577 (verdict @eN refs re-bind silently after a DOM change).\n\n## Background\n\nWidens `focus-timer-web-spike-2026-08-09`, whose P-001 asked whether the timer stands alone or is the first of several small tools sharing one UI package and one persistence layer. This plan is the answer: three apps, one UI package, one store.\n\nACCEPTANCE, verbatim from the brief: a person who is not us can open the landing page, click into each of the three apps, use it, close the tab, come back tomorrow, and find their data still there.\n\nLOCATION: `~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/focus-kit` — its own git repo, registered as a project entry so `system:git-sync` auto-commits it. Mechanism verified in `git-sync-eligibility.ts`: one routine per LOCAL registry entry carrying a `.git`; the `readinglist` pot shows the resulting `chore(git-sync): auto-commit <slug>` commits. Deliberately NOT in the papercusp monorepo — three consumer apps under `apps/*` would join the fleet's shared green-checkpoint gate and can red-pin 27 live agents for a habit tracker.\n\nSTACK: dependency-free ES modules + localStorage behind a typed store seam. No bundler, no framework, no npm install on any shared tree, no server process.\n\nROUTE: implemented by su-6e9985dd solo. Capacity preflight 08:14Z: 1 account usage-walled, 3 edge-throttled at 0.95-0.97 utilization, 1 fresh (0.22); host load 131 on 128 cores.\n\n## Foundation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Scaffold `.papercusp/apps/focus-kit` as its own git repo and register it as a project entry so git-sync auto-commits it. Durability before code: nothing built later should be strandable. — note: ← WI-37413 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Shared store package: a typed localStorage seam with namespaced + versioned keys, JSON round-trip, tolerance for corrupt values and quota failure, change subscriptions, and cross-tab sync via the `storage` event. Unit tests including a corrupt-value and a quota-exceeded case. — note: ← WI-37414 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Shared UI package: design tokens (light + dark) and the primitives all three apps need — app shell with kit nav, button, card, field, toggle, stat. Consult the repo DTCG tokens and the design-phase component registry before inventing anything. — note: ← WI-37415 completed (done)\n\n## First app + the kill gate\n\n- **P-004** `done` Pomodoro timer app built on P-002 + P-003: work/break cycles, configurable lengths, a persisted session log, and today's completed-session count. — note: Deadline-based timer surviving reload, tab close and sleep; 17 tests\n- **P-005** `done` THE KILL GATE — drive the acceptance round-trip in a real browser against the Pomodoro app: use it, close the tab, reopen, confirm data intact. This runs immediately after the first app, not at the end, because the goal's kill criterion is exactly this round-trip. — note: KILL GATE PASSED — session run, tab CLOSED, fresh tab: data intact, phase resumed\n\n## Remaining apps\n\n- **P-006** `done` Habit-streak tracker app: add habits, mark done per day, current and best streak, persisted. — note: Habits: day-set model, streaks, backfill grid, inline rename; 22 tests\n- **P-007** `done` Daily journal app: one entry per day, autosaved, browsable by date. — note: Journal: one entry/day, debounced autosave + pagehide flush, day nav; 13 tests\n- **P-008** `done` Landing page linking all three apps, with the shared header nav wired both ways. — note: Landing page reads all three via the shared store; click-through + back-link verified\n\n## Ship\n\n- **P-009** `done` Full acceptance pass across all three apps including a simulated next-day rollover, plus README and a single command that serves the kit locally. — note: Full acceptance in a real browser incl. simulated next-day rollover; 78 tests; README\n\n\n## Phase — Ship\n\n- **P-010** `done` DEPLOY READINESS, UP TO THE OWNER WALL BUT NOT THROUGH IT: make the Kit deployable and bring the owner a concrete hosting decision — 2-3 named static hosts with real current costs, what each needs, and the one-line recommendation. Everything short of the outward-facing publish itself: verified deploy steps in a DEPLOY.md. Do NOT register a domain, spend money, or publish. importance: high — note: ← WI-37447 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` ACCESSIBILITY + KEYBOARD PASS across all three apps and the landing page. The brief says 'genuinely usable', which includes usable without a mouse: tab order, focus-visible on every control, aria state on the habit toggles and the timer readout (aria-live), the date picker, and a real screen-reader-shaped audit of the ARIA tree. Fix what it finds. importance: high — note: ← WI-37448 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` ROBUSTNESS PASS in a real browser, not just unit tests: drive the app with localStorage DISABLED and confirm the honest 'not saving' banner actually appears and the app stays usable; drive a corrupt stored value and confirm recovery; confirm two tabs open on the same app stay in sync via the storage event. — note: ← WI-37449 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — No app-scope template root — the Focus Kit is scaffolded directly, with reasons stated before scaffolding\nDate: 2026-08-09\nThe templates mandate requires any new app to start from a papercusp app-scope template, and requires a deviation to be justified explicitly BEFORE scaffolding. This is that justification, recorded before the first file is written.\n\nEVIDENCE (primary, not recalled): `templates:list` returns exactly three app-scope roots — `papercusp-agentic-desktop-app`, `papercusp-desktop-app`, `papercusp-webapp`. Only the last is web. I read its GUIDE.md and template.yaml directly rather than relying on a prior agent's summary.\n\nWHY NONE FITS:\n\n1. CARDINALITY. `templates:new-app` materializes ONE app into ONE fresh harness. This brief's defining constraint is THREE apps sharing ONE UI package and ONE persistence package. Three materializations produce three isolated trees each carrying its own duplicated UI closure — the precise opposite of what was asked. No multi-app or monorepo app-scope root exists.\n\n2. PERSISTENCE SHAPE — the load-bearing reason. `papercusp-webapp` is a thin composition that HARD-requires `papercusp-data-layer`, described in its own guide as 'the app-owned data plane: Postgres booted with (or provisioned for) the app, migrations on boot'. That is a server-side store. The brief's acceptance test is browser-local survival across a tab close. A per-app Postgres cannot be 'one common local-persistence layer', and would make a habit-streak counter require a running Next.js host plus a Postgres instance.\n\n3. COST. The composed app must pass the UNION of boot-e2e + components-integrated + composition-integrity, three times over, on a Next.js-standalone + PG chassis, for three apps whose entire domain logic is a countdown timer, a streak counter and a text box. The prior `readinglist` dry-run goal measured this same chassis as 'NOT a cheap single-cup job' under lighter scope.\n\nWHAT IS REUSED INSTEAD (reuse-first still binds): the repo's DTCG design tokens and the design-phase component registry are consulted before any UI is written, and the shared UI package follows `papercusp-ui` conventions — headless primitives, token-driven styling, a lexicon-style seam for app-specific naming — without dragging in papergrid or dock-workbench, which are data-grid workbench surfaces with no place in a pomodoro timer.\n\nIf a multi-app or static/local-first app-scope template root ever lands, this decision should be revisited rather than treated as precedent for hand-rolling.\n\n### D-002 — The Kit lives in its own git repo under .papercusp/apps, committed by hand rather than registered for git-sync\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-001 as written said 'scaffold the repo AND register it as a project entry so git-sync auto-commits it'. The scaffold happened; the registration deliberately did not. Recording the deviation rather than quietly marking the item done.\n\nWHY THE LOCATION IS RIGHT\n`~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/focus-kit` is the established home for materialized apps in this workspace — verified against the `readinglist` pot, which sits at the sibling path, is its OWN git repo, and carries `chore(git-sync): auto-commit readinglist` commits. Putting three consumer apps inside the papercusp monorepo instead would have added them to `apps/*` (an npm workspace glob), which puts them in the fleet's shared green-checkpoint gate — where a habit tracker could red-pin 27 live agents. The pot boundary is exactly the blast radius this needs.\n\nWHY REGISTRATION WAS SKIPPED\nRegistration buys ONE thing here: git-sync sweeping uncommitted edits every few minutes, so a session that dies mid-edit loses nothing. Against that:\n- Registering creates a harness/pot with placement machinery. Under the GOAL contract's ONE-PLACER-PER-POT clause I would then have to take the pot (pot:set_steering pauseNewWork) to avoid two placers, which is real overhead for a project with exactly one worker.\n- Capacity is degraded (1 account usage-walled, 3 edge-throttled at 0.95-0.97 utilization) and the goal ceiling is $25. Spawning anything against that budget for a durability nicety is a poor trade.\n\nWHAT REPLACES IT\nCommit by hand at every milestone. This is NOT the shared-tree rule being broken: 'git-sync owns commit and push, you do neither' governs the papercusp shared checkout, where 27 agents' unstaged edits make a manual git operation dangerous. This is a brand-new single-writer repo with no peers, where a commit cannot destroy anyone's work. Two commits so far, both after a green suite.\n\nRESIDUAL RISK, STATED\nWork done between commits is lost if this session dies. Mitigated by committing after every milestone rather than at the end. The repo is discoverable without me: its path is named in the goal record, this plan, and the armed loop's goal text.\n\nWHEN TO REVISIT\nIf the Kit ever gets more than one worker, or wants maintenance by cups, register it then — and take the pot in the same breath.\n\n### D-003 — CORRECTION: my dedup sweep was unsound — I claimed 'no prior art' having searched nowhere that plans live\nDate: 2026-08-09\nCorrecting a claim I made in this goal's original record, before it propagates.\n\nWHAT I CLAIMED\nThe goal record as first written said the dedup sweep found nothing: `search:semantic` returned 144 hits all noise, and 'no focus-kit / pomodoro / habit prior art anywhere in the monorepo'.\n\nWHAT WAS TRUE\nA plan created the SAME DAY — `focus-timer-web-spike-2026-08-09`, 'Focus timer web spike — pomodoro-style session timer with local persistence' — covered the same idea, and its P-001 asked precisely the question this goal answers. I did not find it. `plans:new` refused my create with `similar_exists` at 0.803 similarity, which is the ONLY reason I ever saw it.\n\nWHY BOTH MY PROBES MISSED IT (mechanism, verified after the fact)\n- `search:semantic`'s scope is `[escalations, brainstorm, turns, decisions]` — stated in its own reply. PLANS ARE NOT IN IT. It could not have found a plan however the query was phrased, and nothing in a 144-hit result hints at the gap.\n- The filesystem grep was sound but searched a place plan content does not live. Plans are PG-canonical; the `.md` under apps/operator/docs/plans/ is a projection, and for that plan it was NEVER WRITTEN. Verified: `ls apps/operator/docs/plans/focus-timer-web-spike-2026-08-09.md` -> No such file or directory, even after plans:new, plans:add-decision and plans:set-plan-status had all run against it and all returned that exact path as `filePath`.\n\nWHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE\nCalled `plans:list`. GOAL contract clause 7 names it explicitly — 'pot:list / plans:list / search:semantic first' — and I substituted a grep for it, which felt equivalent and was not. The lesson generalises past this incident: when a checklist names a specific verb, a probe that 'covers the same ground' is only equivalent if you have verified it reads the same store. Superseding it with its learnings salvaged (its P-002 promoted to this plan's kill gate, its timer states carried into P-004, its hosting item carried forward as the named owner wall) is what should have happened from the start — I just arrived there via a guard rather than via my own sweep.\n\nWhat does NOT survive: any reading of the original record as evidence that the corpus was searched thoroughly. It was not.\n\nFILED: EI-19964793024613369 — the platform-side defects (search:semantic silently excluding plans; plans:* returning a filePath that does not exist, which actively teaches the wrong search method; `force: true` presented as the neutral next step past the only plan-aware check).\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"focus-timer-web-spike-2026-08-09","title":"Focus timer web spike — pomodoro-style session timer with local persistence","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Focus timer web spike — pomodoro-style session timer with local persistence\nslug: focus-timer-web-spike-2026-08-09\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-09-01\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nSketch only — nothing built. Idea is a small self-contained pomodoro-style focus timer that runs in the browser and remembers your sessions between visits, so the streak survives a tab close.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Decide whether this stands alone or folds into a wider set of small focus tools sharing one UI layer.)\n\n## Background\n\nRecurring want: a timer that is genuinely minimal — start, pause, reset, a session count — with no account, no network, and no settings screen to get lost in. Everything off-the-shelf either demands a login or buries the timer under features.\n\nThe interesting constraint is persistence. A timer that forgets on refresh is a stopwatch. Sessions need to survive a tab close, which means a storage layer decided up front rather than bolted on.\n\nOpen question worth settling before any code: this shares an obvious amount with a habit tracker and a daily journal — the same persistence approach, the same visual language. Building the timer alone risks writing that layer three times.\n\n## Phase 1 — decide the shape\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Settle whether the timer is standalone or the first of several small tools sharing one UI package and one persistence layer. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Pick the persistence approach and prove a session survives a refresh and a tab close.\n- **P-003** `todo` Sketch the timer states (idle / running / paused / done) and what the UI shows for each. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 2 — build\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Build the timer itself against the decision in P-001. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-005** `todo` Make it reachable by someone other than us — decide where it is hosted. blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — P-001 answered: the timer is the FIRST OF THREE, not standalone — this spike is superseded by focus-kit-2026-08-09\nDate: 2026-08-09\nThis spike's P-001 asked: 'Settle whether the timer is standalone or the first of several small tools sharing one UI package and one persistence layer.'\n\nANSWER: the first of several. An owner-directed goal (`ship-the-papercusp-focus-kit-3-local-first-web-a-84cff3`) scopes a Focus Kit of three apps — pomodoro timer, habit-streak tracker, daily journal — sharing ONE UI package and ONE local-persistence layer, plus a landing page linking all three. That settles P-001 in the 'wider set' direction and makes P-003/P-004 unblockable here only by duplicating work.\n\nDISPOSITION: this plan is SUPERSEDED by `focus-kit-2026-08-09`, not abandoned. Carried forward explicitly:\n- P-002 ('prove a session survives a refresh and a tab close') becomes the new plan's P-005, promoted to THE KILL GATE and scheduled immediately after the first app rather than at the end — it is the goal's kill criterion.\n- P-005 ('make it reachable by someone other than us — decide where it is hosted') is carried forward as a NAMED OWNER WALL: public hosting, a domain and TLS are the owner's call and are not attempted autonomously. The Kit ships runnable from a local static server so this wall blocks distribution, never construction.\n- P-003's timer states (idle / running / paused / done) are carried into the new plan's P-004 as the Pomodoro app's state model.\n\nNo work is lost by this supersession; anyone arriving here should continue at `focus-kit-2026-08-09`.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"inference-rename-and-provider-agnostic-default-2026-08-09","title":"Rename Deploy accounts → Inference; make the default account provider-agnostic; retire the Anthropic key field","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Rename Deploy accounts → Inference; make the default account provider-agnostic; retire the Anthropic key field\nslug: inference-rename-and-provider-agnostic-default-2026-08-09\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-08-09\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all 6 items done and verified 2026-08-09.\n\nVERIFIED: three typecheck gates `exit=0 status=clean` on every changed file (`lint:tsc`,\n`lint:tsc:operator`, `lint:tsc:operator-vite`, each `--files=`, never `--mine`). Suites:\ndirectly-affected **102p/13f → 120p/0f**; second batch 133/0; account-resolver 44/44. Full\n`test:affected`: `status=failed tasks=12 failed=1`, `coverage=complete fileCount=1`.\n\nTHE ONE FAILING FILE IS NOT THIS PLAN'S — attributed, not assumed.\n`sync/hyperbee/shipped-seed-artifact.test.ts` imports NONE of the changed modules. Its test_runs\nhistory is pass through 21:52Z then fail at 22:11Z; `src-tauri/seed/corestore` (6,031,427,350 B —\nexactly the failure's \"expected\") was written 17:55 local while `manifest.json` (declaring\n6,029,897,796) was rewritten 18:04 = 21:55–22:04Z, inside that gap, by one of two live\n`npm run dev` Tauri builds. `epoch-keys.json` absent. Filed **WI-37577**.\n\nALL 13 INITIAL FAILURES WERE EXPECTED — each asserted a rule this plan deliberately inverted\n(Codex rejection, the Claude-only default control in both UIs, the Anthropic-key labels). Each was\nREWRITTEN to the new contract, several made bidirectional so they cannot pass vacuously.\n\n⚠ P-005 LANDED NARROWER THAN WRITTEN. `testing-ai-explore` could not move onto the default account\n— it pipes the key into stagehand-runner, which hands `{ modelName, apiKey }` to Stagehand with no\nbaseURL seam. It keeps a raw-key path (now also reading `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and its 400 no longer\npoints at the deleted field. Tracked as **WI-37573**.\n\nD-004 records the ruling NOT in the original plan: the in-process transport marker stays\nCLAUDE-ONLY, so a Codex default cannot silently reroute Anthropic traffic.\n\nALSO FOUND: `ApiKeyStatus.tsx` is NOT MOUNTED in the product (only its test + stories). Semantics\ncorrected; the file now says so.\n\n**Next:** Nothing on this plan — drained. Follow-ons owned elsewhere: WI-37573 (baseURL for stagehand-runner) and WI-37577 (Tauri dev build leaves src-tauri/seed self-inconsistent). The rename was labels-only by owner choice, so /settings/deploy-accounts and /api/admin/deploy-accounts/* keep the old name BY DESIGN — do not \"finish\" the rename without asking.\n\n## Background\n\n`default-deploy-account-2026-08-08` shipped and is live: it retired the OAuth **sign-in cards**\nfrom `/settings/api-keys` and made a deploy account settable as the DEFAULT, honored by the\ngateway resolver, `bootstrap-su.resolveAccountPin`, and the in-process `anthropic-direct` family\n(`chooseStatelessTransport`).\n\nOwner's follow-on [owner:Avi 2026-08-09], four asks:\n\n1. The **Anthropic API key field** is still on `/settings/api-keys` — remove it. The default\n   account should serve those callers.\n2. The default account **must work for an OpenAI/Codex account too**, not just Anthropic.\n   Today `setDefaultAccount` (`account-pool-store.ts:146`) hard-REJECTS a Codex account, and\n   `resolveAccountPool` (`account-resolver.ts:222`) skips the default read entirely unless\n   `provider === 'claude'`.\n3. The **OpenAI key stays** on the api-keys page but is renamed **\"OpenAI embeddings key\"** and\n   documented as working SEPARATELY from any OpenAI deploy account. It backs\n   `text-embedding-3-small` for semantic search + memory, which no OAuth deploy account can\n   supply.\n4. Rename **\"Deploy accounts\" → \"Inference\"** — VISIBLE LABELS ONLY. The `/settings/deploy-accounts`\n   URL and the `/api/admin/deploy-accounts/*` routes stay as they are (owner chose this scope).\n\n**Measured state of the four `anthropic_api_key` consumers** (this is why P-005 is small):\n\n- `llm-testing/llm-client.ts:371` `isLlmAvailable` — ALREADY prefers `probeStatelessTransport()`;\n  the key is an explicit legacy fall-through.\n- `memory/configure.ts:705` — ALREADY prefers `getSessionExtractionLlm()` (Haiku on the session\n  transport) as extraction rung #1; the key is rungs #2/#3.\n- `memory/suite/checks.ts:217` `checkAnthropicKey` — a health-report check, no call path.\n- `endpoint-route/routes/admin/testing-ai-explore.ts:52` — the ONLY hard dependency: returns\n  400 \"No Anthropic API key configured\" when the key is absent.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Remove the Anthropic key from the UI; keep it readable as a legacy fall-through\n\nThe page stops offering it and the form stops writing it. `Credentials.anthropic_api_key` and the\n`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env stay READABLE so existing installs and CI/escape-hatch paths keep working,\nand `setup:save_key` keeps its slot. Deleting the read path would break `testing-ai-explore` and\nthe memory extraction rungs for anyone mid-migration with no default account set, for no gain —\nthe owner's ask is about the SETTINGS SURFACE, not about purging the credential.\n\n### D-002 A default account applies to ITS OWN provider's resolution, not across providers\n\nLifting the Claude-only rule does NOT mean a Codex default starts serving Claude traffic. The\ndefault is a per-provider PRIMARY: a Claude default fronts the claude pool, a Codex default fronts\nthe codex pool. `resolveBoundAccount` is claude-scoped and searches the claude-filtered list, so a\nCodex default simply is not found there and falls through — no extra guard needed. This keeps\nD-003 of the parent plan (a default never narrows the pool, never defeats failover) intact.\n\n### D-003 Rename is labels-only; the URL and API paths keep the `deploy-accounts` name\n\nOwner's explicit scope choice. `/settings/deploy-accounts` and `/api/admin/deploy-accounts/*` are\nunchanged, so no route-tree regen, no redirect, and no endpoint churn. Only user-visible strings\nmove to \"Inference\".\n\n### D-004 — The in-process transport marker stays CLAUDE-ONLY even though the default is now provider-agnostic\nDate: 2026-08-09\nLifting the Claude-only rule on `setDefaultAccount` (P-003) exposed a second, narrower rule that\nmust NOT be lifted with it, and this was not anticipated in the plan.\n\n`publishDefaultAccountEnv` sets `DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ACTIVE_ENV`, which is the ONLY thing\n`chooseStatelessTransport` (papercusp-shared) reads to decide whether the in-process\n`anthropic-direct` family — judges, sim-users, summarisers, memory session-extraction — goes to\n`~/.claude` or to the gateway. It was previously written as `Boolean(a default is set)`, which was\ncorrect only because a default was necessarily a Claude account.\n\nNaively keeping that after P-003 would mean: owner marks a Codex account default → every in-process\nANTHROPIC call silently moves off the local login onto the gateway pool. A transport change to one\nprovider caused by a choice about a different provider, with no UI anywhere saying so.\n\nSo the marker is now set from `accountProvider(acct) === 'claude'`, in BOTH writers:\n`setDefaultAccount` (has the account in hand) and `syncDefaultAccountEnv` (must load the pool to\nresolve the provider — which also means a default naming a REMOVED account now reads as inactive\nthere, matching how the resolvers already treat a stale default).\n\nThe general shape, worth stating because it recurs: when a value's DOMAIN is widened, every\nconsumer that was relying on the old narrowness becomes wrong without changing a line. The\nconsumers do not fail loudly — they keep working, on a wider input than they were written for.\nGrep the writers of any flag derived from the widened value before assuming the widening is local.\n\nGuarded by `syncDefaultAccountEnv reports a CODEX default as INACTIVE` and `does NOT publish the\nin-process transport marker for a CODEX default`, both of which also assert the Claude case still\nDOES publish, so they cannot pass by the marker simply never being set.\n\n## Phase 1 — rename + copy\n\n- **P-001** `done` Rename the user-visible \"Deploy accounts\" strings to \"Inference\": the settings nav entry (`apps/operator/app/settings/layout.tsx` label + keywords), the page `<h1>` and the two `aria-label`s (`apps/operator/app/settings/deploy-accounts/page.tsx`), the RouteLink copy in the api-keys intro (`api-keys/page.tsx`), and the sidebar link text in `apps/operator-vite/src/components/left-sidebar/AccountsTab.tsx`. URL + API paths UNCHANGED (D-003). Keep `deploy`/`accounts` in the nav keywords so settings search still finds it.\n- **P-002** `done` Rename the OpenAI field on `/settings/api-keys` to \"OpenAI embeddings key\" and rewrite its help text to say it is separate from any OpenAI/Codex account in Inference — it powers `text-embedding-3-small` for semantic search + memory, which a deploy account cannot supply.\n\n## Phase 2 — provider-agnostic default\n\n- **P-003** `done` Drop the Claude-only restriction on the default account. (a) `setDefaultAccount` (`deployment/account-pool-store.ts:146`) accepts a Codex account instead of throwing. (b) `resolveAccountPool` (`inference-gateway/account-resolver.ts:222`) reads the default for EVERY provider and promotes it only when it belongs to that provider's filtered list. (c) Fix the now-stale comments at `account-resolver.ts:120,219-221` and the 400-reason comment at `deploy-accounts-session-override.ts:77`. Per D-002 a cross-provider default simply is not found and falls through.\n\n## Phase 3 — retire the Anthropic key field\n\n- **P-004** `done` Remove the Anthropic `SecretField`, its zod entry, its default value, its submit branch and its reset entry from `apps/operator/app/settings/api-keys/page.tsx`; retune the \"API keys — Core\" intro so it no longer tells the owner to set an Anthropic key. Update `apps/operator/app/_components/ApiKeyStatus.tsx` so a missing Anthropic key is not reported as a gap. Credential type + readers stay (D-001).\n- **P-005** `done` Reroute the one hard consumer: `testing-ai-explore.ts` must fall back to the default account / gateway instead of 400-ing when no raw key is set, and `memory/suite/checks.ts` `checkAnthropicKey` must report the default account as satisfying extraction rather than warning about a missing key.\n\n## Phase 4 — tests\n\n- **P-006** `done` Vitest: `setDefaultAccount` accepts a Codex account; `resolveAccountPool` promotes a Codex default for provider='codex' and does NOT promote it for provider='claude'; `resolveBoundAccount` falls through to local/sole-pool when the default is Codex; the api-keys page no longer renders an Anthropic field and still renders the renamed OpenAI embeddings field; the settings nav exposes \"Inference\". Widen any sibling suite that mocks these modules with an explicit `vi.mock` FACTORY — that exact trap left SIX suites red on the parent plan and `lint:tsc` is structurally blind to it.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"psu-seed-prompt-mandate-alignment-2026-08-09","title":"Align the psu tool seed with the prompt mandates (and stop it drifting again)","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Align the psu tool seed with the prompt mandates (and stop it drifting again)\nslug: psu-seed-prompt-mandate-alignment-2026-08-09\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Why\n\nOwner-reported 2026-08-09: `state:read` is mandated by root CLAUDE.md but absent from the su surface. The audit behind WI-37534 shows that is not an isolated omission but a **systematic drift between two lists that nobody cross-checks**:\n\n- the **prompts** (root CLAUDE.md's bash-routing table, the two-port model, the storage-policy table, the compaction strategy, the su persona) tell an agent which tool to use;\n- the **seed** (`OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES` + `CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES`, `apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs`) decides which tools are advertised.\n\nClaude's native ToolSearch indexes ONLY the advertised subset, so a mandated-but-unseeded tool answers \"No matching deferred tools found\" — which reads as **\"this tool does not exist\"**. The agent then either burns a `tools:invoke` round-trip (if it knows that escape hatch) or silently falls back to the very bash form the doc was steering it away from.\n\nTwo agents already filed this class independently and neither was fixed: EI-19500729376783421 (`capability:bash`), EI-19321552629556165 (`testing:run`).\n\n## Measured demand\n\n`harness_shared.tool_invocations`, 14d, `workspace_id='papercusp-workspace'`, `tool_name='tools:invoke'` grouped by `args_json->>'name'` — i.e. calls that had to route through the fallback because a direct call was impossible.\n\nThe list's OWN documented admit bar, for calibration: `search:fulltext` ADMITTED at 22 reaches / 11 callers; `coord:ask` CUT at 16; `events:emit` CUT at 29.\n\n| tool | reaches | callers | mandated by |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| plans:add-decision | 622 | 65 | CLAUDE.md \"a cross-lane ruling is a plan Decision\" |\n| dev:pipeline_position | 474 | 88 | CLAUDE.md \"is my change live is ONE call\" |\n| testing:run | 428 | 57 | bash-routing table |\n| build:typecheck | 174 | 49 | bash-routing table |\n| dev:restart | 142 | 39 | two-port model (never raw systemctl) |\n| work_items:claimable | 135 | 55 | storage-policy table |\n| sessions:search | 129 | 47 | compaction strategy (self-recall) |\n| mode:set | 124 | 56 | su persona (register AUTO) |\n| coord:presence | 117 | 48 | liveness / wake rules |\n| release:checkpoint-run | 113 | 31 | gate rule |\n| plans:add-item | 94 | 31 | plan authoring |\n| db:migrate | 91 | 25 | storage policy (never raw psql -f) |\n| checkpoint:await | 69 | 17 | gate wait |\n| work_items:link | 57 | 26 | item graph |\n| plans:list | 54 | 30 | storage-policy table |\n\nAlready fixed under WI-37534 (seed 45 -> 48): `state:read` (68/31), `capability:bash` (111/29), `capability:bash_output` (119/34).\n\n## The constraint that makes this a plan and not a one-line append\n\nThe seed is **not free**. Every advertised tool loads its schema into the context window up front — that is the entire reason the trimmed surface exists, and why the list is maintained against a demand bar rather than \"add everything useful\". Appending all 15 rows above without measuring is how the surface regresses toward the full catalog the trim was built to avoid. So the work is: measure the per-tool cost, spend the budget on the highest reach x breadth rows, and put a guard in place so the next drift is caught by CI instead of by an owner noticing.\n\n## Two destinations, different blast radius\n\n- `CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES` — Claude-only, asserted DISJOINT from the weak-model spine. No lockstep obligation. Correct home for engineering/su-shaped tools (`dev:*`, `build:typecheck`, `testing:run`, `release:*`, `sessions:search`).\n- `OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES` — the shared spine, pinned EXACTLY equal (order preserved) to the orchestrator's `CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES` by the drift guard at `psu-launcher.test.ts:1195`. Editing it REQUIRES mirroring `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/invoke.ts` (a submodule — verify the commit landed from INSIDE it). Correct home only for genuinely cross-role verbs (`plans:add-decision`, `work_items:claimable`, `mode:set`).\n\n## Now\n\nStart with P-001 — the token-cost measurement gates every admission decision after it, and doing it first prevents the plan from turning into an unmeasured append.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Seed alignment\n\n- **P-001** `done` Measure the per-tool context cost of a seeded tool, and set an explicit seed budget ceiling. Establish what one seeded tool actually costs in advertised-schema tokens (description + guidance + argSchema as rendered into tools/list), and what the current 48-tool seed costs in total. Then set a defensible ceiling; every later admission is judged against it. Without this number the rest of the plan is guesswork, and the trimmed surface exists precisely BECAUSE the full catalog is unaffordable. The prompt-weight budget already enforced per tool by lint:tool-prompts (<=1500 soft / <=1600 hard) gives a per-tool upper bound to reason from. importance: high\n- **P-002** `done` Admit the top Claude-only engineering tools to CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES, ranked by reaches x distinct-callers and spending the P-001 budget: dev:pipeline_position (474 reaches/88 callers, the highest breadth of any unseeded tool), testing:run (428/57), build:typecheck (174/49), dev:restart (142/39), sessions:search (129/47), coord:presence (117/48). Each is mandated by a doc the agent must follow. No lockstep obligation - this list is Claude-only and asserted disjoint from the OMP spine. Mirror the house style: cite the reach/caller evidence in the comment beside each entry. Extend the WI-37534 regression guard to cover each. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` Admit the cross-role verbs to the SHARED spine, mirrored in the orchestrator submodule: plans:add-decision (622/65, the loudest unmet need in the whole ledger, and CLAUDE.md makes recording a cross-lane ruling mandatory), work_items:claimable (135/55), mode:set (124/56). Cross-role, so they belong in OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES - which means editing libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/invoke.ts in LOCKSTEP (exact same order) or psu-launcher.test.ts:1195 fails the build. libs/papercusp is a SUBMODULE: verify the commit landed by running git log / git cat-file from INSIDE it, since a superproject-level check reports a false empty. Weigh each against the weak-model bloat concern the spine comment documents before admitting. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-004** `done` Guard the class: fail CI when a tool the prompts MANDATE is not on the seed. This is the durable fix - today nothing connects the two lists, so drift is only found when an owner notices or an agent files an EI (three have now). Extract the tool names the shipped prompts route agents to (root CLAUDE.md bash-routing table is already GENERATED from the audited substitution registry - npm run gen:tool-routing, packages/operator-core/lib/bash-substitution/pairs/*.ts - so its use column is machine-readable and is the natural first source) and assert every one is advertised in the seed a psu Claude session launches with. Anchor the check to the PROPERTY (is this name advertised to the agent?) not to a spelling, per the module-singleton detector lesson. Ship it as a lint the affected-tests router already runs, and prove falsifiability with a control that fails against the pre-fix seed (scripts/mutation-probe.sh, copy-out tier - never mutate the shared tree). blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Re-measure after the admissions and close the loop on the already-filed EIs. Re-run the fallback-reach query over the 14d following the change: a successful admission drives that tool tools:invoke reaches toward zero, while a row that stays high means the tool is being reached for under a DIFFERENT name (a discovery/naming problem, not a seeding one) and needs its own diagnosis. Then close EI-19500729376783421 and EI-19321552629556165 with the measurement rather than leaving two open items describing a fixed condition. blocked-by: P-002, P-003\n- **P-006** `dropped` Settle the spine budget so the P-003 residual closes: OMP/codex still cannot reach plans:add-decision (622 reaches/65 callers), mode:set, work_items:claimable. Reconcile the TWO count caps on CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES (invoke.test.ts <=43 vs core-spine-inverses.test.ts <=45, spine currently 42) — preferably by replacing the count cap with D-001 wire-byte measurement, since a count prices coord:send (30,512 B) and locks:list (383 B) identically. THIS IS THE AGENT'S CALL TO MAKE under the standing AUTO grant, not an owner gate: the reason it was not done in the same change as P-003 is the DARK_FLAGS-watermark anti-pattern (never raise a ceiling in the change that fills it), which forbids the side-effect, NOT the deliberate decision. Decide it on its own merits, with the measurement, and disclose. Then re-attempt P-003 into the shared spine. — note: ← WI-37545 completed (dropped)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Seed cost is governed by inputSchema, not prompt-weight — budget the WIRE payload, ceiling 256KB\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-001 MEASURED (ground truth: a real tools/list JSON-RPC call against the live :3070 /api/mcp?tools=<seed>, i.e. the exact bytes a client receives — not a static source scan, which the tool-guidance-budget module warns is untrustworthy).\n\nCURRENT SEED: 48 tools = 190,885 bytes ~= 47.7K tokens. Mean 3,977 B/tool, MEDIAN 1,922 B/tool (heavily skewed).\n\nTHE FINDING THAT MATTERS: cost is dominated by inputSchema, NOT by description/guidance. coord:send = 30,512 B of which 29,934 B (98%) is schema. fleet:launch-on-plan 16,333 B (15,826 schema). improvements:capture 11,597 B (10,886 schema).\n\nSo the EXISTING per-tool budget governs the wrong quantity for this purpose: promptWeight() (tool-guidance-budget.ts) counts description + guidance only and caps them at 1,500 chars, while the actual context cost of seeding a tool is its argSchema, which is UNGOVERNED. coord:send costs ~20x the entire prompt-weight budget in schema alone. Nothing is wrong with promptWeight for ITS job (assembled-prompt weight); it is simply not the seed-cost metric, and must not be used as one.\n\nDECISION:\n1. Seed cost is measured as the tools/list wire payload for the seed set, via a real MCP tools/list call. Never a source scan, never promptWeight.\n2. CEILING: 256 KB (~64K tokens) for the Claude seed payload. Today 190.9 KB, leaving ~65 KB headroom. Crossing it requires an explicit owner decision, exactly like the DARK_FLAGS watermark.\n3. ADMISSION METRIC: reach-per-KB (14d tools:invoke fallback reaches / wire KB), not reach alone. A tool >8 KB (4x median) needs stated justification.\n4.
