This deliberately does NOT propose adding a schema-size lint. The right lever is admission review; a global schema cap would fight legitimately-rich tools like coord:send, which earns its size.\n\nMEASURED CANDIDATES (reach/KB, bytes): dev:pipeline_position 252.9 (1,919) - testing:run 178.5 (2,455) - plans:add-decision 149.9 (4,250) - dev:restart 109.5 (1,328) - mode:set 73.3 (1,732) - work_items:claimable 62.9 (2,198) - release:checkpoint-run 57.5 (2,012) - sessions:search 57.3 (2,305) - build:typecheck 56.7 (3,141) - db:migrate 43.7 (2,132) - coord:presence 36.0 (3,331) - plans:add-item 28.0 (3,435) - work_items:link 24.1 (2,420) - checkpoint:await 20.0 (3,540) - plans:list 12.9 (4,292).\n\nThe P-002 + P-003 sets total 22,659 B (+11.9% -> 213.5 KB), comfortably inside the ceiling.\n\n### D-002 — P-005 baseline frozen 2026-08-09 — re-measure on/after 2026-08-23, and read a still-high row as a NAMING problem, not a seeding failure\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-005 has two halves. The EI-closure half is DONE (EI-19500729376783421 and EI-19321552629556165 both closed committed, with evidence). The re-measurement half is TIME-GATED: it compares 14d of post-change data that does not exist yet. Freezing the baseline here so the future comparison is possible rather than re-derived.\n\nBASELINE (tools:invoke fallback reaches / distinct callers, 14d ending 2026-08-09, workspace papercusp-workspace) for every tool seeded today:\n  state:read 68/31 - capability:bash 111/29 - capability:bash_output 119/34 -\n  dev:pipeline_position 474/88 - testing:run 428-432/57-58 - build:typecheck 174/49 -\n  dev:restart 142/39 - sessions:search 129/47 - coord:presence 117/48 -\n  plans:add-decision 622/65 - mode:set 124/56 - work_items:claimable 135/55\n\nTHE QUERY (unchanged, so the two runs are comparable):\n  SELECT args_json->>'name', count(*), count(DISTINCT coord_owner_id)\n    FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations\n   WHERE invoked_at > now() - interval '14 days'\n     AND workspace_id = 'papercusp-workspace' AND tool_name = 'tools:invoke'\n   GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;\n\nHOW TO READ THE RESULT — this is the part worth writing down, because the obvious reading is wrong:\n- A row that DROPS toward zero = the seeding worked; the tool is now callable directly.\n- A row that STAYS HIGH does NOT mean seeding failed. It means agents are reaching for that tool under a name the surface does not match — a DISCOVERY/NAMING problem, diagnosed separately. Re-seeding a tool that is already seeded would be the wrong reflex.\n- Note the 14d windows OVERLAP until 2026-08-23. A re-measure before then mixes pre- and post-change data and will show a partial drop that is an artifact of the window, not of the fix. Wait for the clean window.\n\nAlso note the counting caveat that applies to any comparison here: reaches are attributed by args_json->>'name', so a caller who dispatches a tool under an alias is invisible to this query in both runs. That is fine for a DELTA (the bias is constant), and misleading for an absolute.\n\n### D-003 — TWO budgets now govern the seed (count <=45 and wire <=256KB). Count is the worse proxy — but do NOT raise it silently; P-003 consumed its last 3 slots\nDate: 2026-08-09\nDiscovered while verifying P-003, not before it: core-spine-inverses.test.ts:66 caps the SHARED spine at CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES.length <= 45 (\"the spine stays SMALL — it is a seed, not a catalog\"; if it trips, justify the growth or use tools:find).\n\nSTATE AFTER P-003: the spine is at EXACTLY 45. The guard passes, and the NEXT addition to the shared spine will fail it. That is the guard working as designed, but it means P-003 spent the last three slots of that budget, and whoever adds the next cross-role verb inherits the decision.\n\nTHE TENSION, stated plainly so nobody has to rediscover it: there are now two budgets for one resource.\n  - COUNT: <= 45 tools on the shared spine (pre-existing, orchestrator test).\n  - WIRE: <= 256 KB tools/list payload for the Claude seed (D-001, this plan).\nCount is the WORSE proxy, and D-001 measured why: coord:send is 30,512 B and locks:list is 383 B — an 80x spread that a count treats as identical. A count budget therefore prices a 30 KB tool and a 0.4 KB tool the same, which is exactly the mispricing that lets a seed look \"small\" (45 tools) while costing 208.5 KB.\n\nWHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: raise the 45 cap. Raising a ceiling in the same change that fills it is how the DARK_FLAGS high-watermark got walked 22->24->25->26 for one recurring bug class, and this repo already made that mistake once. The cap is someone else's guard with a stated rationale; it deserves an explicit decision, not a side-effect.\n\nRECOMMENDED (not done here, deliberately out of scope): replace the count cap with the wire-byte measurement, or keep both and make the count cap advisory with a pointer to the byte ceiling. Either way it should be ONE decision made on purpose. Until then, treat 45 as a hard stop on the SHARED spine and prefer CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES (Claude-only, uncapped by count, still governed by the 256 KB ceiling) for anything that is not genuinely cross-role.\n\n### D-004 — P-003 OUTCOME: the three cross-role verbs ship in the CLAUDE-ONLY list, not the shared spine — the spine is capped at 43 and sits at 42\nDate: 2026-08-09\nSupersedes P-003 as originally written (\"admit to the SHARED spine, mirrored in the orchestrator submodule\"). That was attempted, verified, and REVERTED. Recording the outcome so nobody re-attempts it and rediscovers the wall.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED: the three verbs were added to OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES + the canonical orchestrator CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES in lockstep. The lockstep drift guard passed (560/560) and core-spine-inverses passed (7/7) — but invoke.test.ts:1260 failed: `assert.ok(CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES.length <= 43)`. The spine was 42; +3 = 45.\n\nSO THE SPINE HAS TWO COUNT CAPS AT DIFFERENT NUMBERS: 43 (invoke.test.ts) and 45 (core-spine-inverses.test.ts). They are not contradictory at 42 — both pass — which is exactly why the discrepancy was invisible until something tried to grow the list. The binding one is 43.\n\nWHY NOT JUST RAISE IT: raising a ceiling in the same change that fills it is the DARK_FLAGS high-watermark anti-pattern (walked 22->24->25->26 for a single recurring bug class before anyone noticed). It is someone else's guard with a stated rationale; it deserves its own decision, not a side-effect of mine.\n\nRESOLUTION: all three now live in CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES. Net effect on the thing the plan actually measured is ZERO — the Claude seed is 57 tools either way, and the measured demand is overwhelmingly su/psu traffic.\n\nKNOWN GAP, stated so it is not discovered by surprise: OMP and codex sessions still cannot reach plans:add-decision, mode:set or work_items:claimable directly. For plans:add-decision especially (622 reaches/65 callers) that is a real residual — recording a cross-lane ruling is MANDATORY, and on those clients the mandated verb still needs a discovery round-trip.\n\nFOLLOW-UP (the one decision that closes it): replace the spine COUNT cap with the wire-byte ceiling from D-001, or reconcile 43 vs 45 and raise deliberately. D-003 argues count is the wrong instrument — coord:send 30,512 B vs locks:list 383 B is an 80x spread a count prices identically, which is how a seed can look \"small\" at 45 tools while costing 208.5 KB.\n\n### D-005 — Verify the COMMITTED state, not the working tree — a lockstep pair spanning a submodule boundary can be green locally and red at HEAD\nDate: 2026-08-09\nDate: 2026-08-09\nFound at post-implementation verification, AFTER this plan was reported implemented. It did not change any decision above; it nearly cost the fleet its gate.\n\nWHAT WAS TRUE: I verified P-003's revert with 720 passing tests and an element-by-element lockstep check, and reported the plan implemented. Every one of those checks ran against the WORKING TREE, and every one was correct.\n\nWHAT WAS ALSO TRUE AT THE SAME MOMENT: the COMMITTED tree was inconsistent and would have red-pinned the fleet gate.\n  - superproject HEAD apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs: OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES = 45 entries (the pre-revert state)\n  - submodule libs/papercusp @ its own HEAD: CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES = 42 entries (the reverted state, already committed)\n  - superproject gitlink: '+5525f3ff' — the leading '+' meaning the recorded pin did NOT match the submodule's HEAD\nThe lockstep drift guard in psu-launcher.test.ts compares those two arrays EXACTLY. 45 vs 42 is a guaranteed red for any candidate cut from that HEAD.\n\nWHY THE TWO HALVES DESYNCED: the revert touched both sides of a lockstep pair that straddles a submodule boundary. git-sync committed the submodule side promptly and left the superproject side dirty, so the repo passed through a window in which the committed state was a state NO ONE had ever tested — neither the pre-revert (45/45) nor the post-revert (42/42) configuration, but the 45/42 cross-product.\n\nWHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: on this swept tree `git status` is clean within minutes of any edit, so working-tree cleanliness cannot distinguish 'committed' from 'not yet swept'. And the local test run — the strongest evidence available — reads the working tree, so it is structurally incapable of detecting this. The greener the local signal, the more confident the wrong conclusion.\n\nDECISION / RULE: when a change spans a submodule boundary, 'verified' requires a COMMITTED-vs-COMMITTED check, not a working-tree one. Concretely:\n  PIN=$(git submodule status <sub> | awk '{print $1}' | tr -d '+-')\n  git show HEAD:<superproject-file>            # the mirror, as committed\n  (cd <sub> && git show \"$PIN\":<file>)         # the canonical, at the sha the gitlink PINS\nand diff those two, not the files on disk. A leading '+' in `git submodule status` means the gitlink is stale and the two halves are not being judged together at all.\n\nDO NOT read this as 'run more tests'. The tests were right. The defect was the SUBJECT they ran against, and no amount of additional local testing would have found it.\n\nGENERAL FORM, consistent with this plan's other findings: a measurement is only as good as the object it measures. D-001 found the repo pricing seed cost with an instrument that could not see the cost. Here the verification measured a tree state that was never going to be judged. Same shape, different layer.\n\nRESOLUTION: fired git-sync:run on demand, which committed the superproject side and bumped the gitlink (HEAD f42ca0b8c6, pin b8b9fc287e). Re-verified COMMITTED-vs-COMMITTED: mirror 42 == canonical 42, element-identical. Guards re-run against that state: 720 passed / 0 failed across psu-launcher.test.ts, seed-mandate-coverage.test.ts, invoke.test.ts, core-spine-inverses.test.ts. Gate green at 508ba823, consecutiveReds 0.\n\n### D-006 — P-006 SETTLED: plans:add-decision admitted to the SHARED spine raising NO cap — and the 'two rival caps' premise was wrong; it is a ratchet + a ceiling\nDate: 2026-08-09\nDate: 2026-08-09\nP-006 asked me to reconcile two count caps and then re-attempt P-003. I did neither, because MEASURING the guards first showed the premise was wrong — and the real answer needed no cap change at all.\n\nTHE PREMISE CORRECTION (this supersedes how D-003 and P-006's own text characterise it). The two guards are NOT rival caps that happen to disagree:\n  - invoke.test.ts:1260 `<=43` is a RATCHET pinned to the array's current size. It carries a per-increment changelog (25->32->33->38->41->42->43), each step naming its demand evidence, and its stated intent is 'no unreviewed creep past the deliberate N'. Its job is to FORCE A REVIEW on every addition.\n  - core-spine-inverses.test.ts:66 `<=45` is a separate BLOAT CEILING: 'guard against the opposite failure: just seed everything would restore the ~165k-token load the trim exists to avoid.'\nRatchet + ceiling is ONE coherent two-layer design: the ratchet reviews each step, the ceiling bounds how far the ratchet may ever be walked. The 45 looks 'dead' only because the ratchet is always at or below it — that is the ceiling doing its job as a second line, not a defect. EXECUTING P-006 AS WRITTEN ('reconcile the two count caps', 'preferably replace the count cap with wire-byte measurement') WOULD HAVE DESTROYED one of the two: collapsing them into a single constant removes either the per-addition forcing function or the backstop. Do not do it.\n\nHOW THE WRONG PREMISE AROSE, since it is the same failure this plan keeps finding: D-003 was written from the FAILURE MESSAGE and the two numbers, during the P-003 attempt, without reading both guards' stated intents. Two numbers on one property genuinely look like a discrepancy until you read the writers. Same shape as D-001 (a metric that could not see what it claimed to budget) and D-005 (a verification pointed at the wrong artifact): the observation was real, the interpretation was not, and only reading the code that WRITES the constraint settled it.\n\nTHE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE THE FIX FREE. The array held 42 entries (measured twice, two independent regexes — one allowing digits per the test's own /^[a-z_]+:[a-z0-9_-]+$/ — deduped, both agreeing) while the ratchet stood at <=43. So ONE DOCUMENTED SLOT WAS ALREADY UNOCCUPIED. The changelog's running tally had reached 43; the likeliest cause of the gap is one of the deliberate 2026-07-05 cuts (locks:acquire_granular, recipes:run) decrementing the array without decrementing the tally — stated as likely, NOT verified.\n\nDECISION: admit `plans:add-decision` to the SHARED spine (canonical CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES + the psu-launcher mirror, same position, same order), and admit NOTHING else.\n  WHY THIS ONE: 622 tools:invoke fallback-reaches / 65 distinct callers in 14d — the highest demand in the entire fallback ledger — at 4,250 B = 149.9 reaches/KB on D-001's admission metric. It also discharges a MANDATORY obligation: root CLAUDE.md requires a cross-lane ruling to be recorded as a plan Decision, so the single verb an agent MUST call to comply cost a discovery round-trip on every non-Claude client. I hit exactly that this session — recording D-005 required routing through tools:invoke.\n  WHY NOTHING ELSE: with it admitted the array is EXACTLY 43 = the ratchet. Admitting mode:set (124/56) or work_items:claimable (135/55) would raise a cap in the very change that fills it — the DARK_FLAGS-watermark anti-pattern (22->24->25->26 for one bug class) that P-003 already correctly refused. They stay in CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES and remain reachable everywhere via tools:find/invoke.\n\nNET EFFECT: OMP + codex gain plans:add-decision directly (+4,250 B on their seeds). The CLAUDE seed is UNCHANGED at 57 tools — the verb moved from the Claude-only extras into the shared spine, so it is a relocation, not an addition; verified no spine/extras overlap remains.\n\nVERIFIED (working tree AND committed — per D-005, working-tree-only would not count): mirror 43 == canonical 43, element-identical and same order, zero duplicates; Claude seed 57; guards 720 passed / 0 failed across psu-launcher.test.ts, seed-mandate-coverage.test.ts, invoke.test.ts, core-spine-inverses.test.ts; node --check clean on the .mjs mirror; lint:tsc:papercusp-libs 8 packages passed / 0 failed, exit 0.\n\nRESIDUAL, deliberately left open: mode:set and work_items:claimable are still unreachable-without-discovery on OMP/codex, and the spine now has ZERO ratchet headroom, so the NEXT addition must raise it with justification. D-001 argues that when that happens the count should be replaced by a WIRE-BYTE price (coord:send 30,512 B vs locks:list 383 B is an 80x spread a count prices identically) — but that is a change to the RATCHET's instrument, and the CEILING should survive it in some form.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"session-chat-popup-timestamps-and-modes-2026-08-09","title":"Session chat popup: message timestamps, visible sends, live mode state, drain instructions","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Session chat popup: message timestamps, visible sends, live mode state, drain instructions\nslug: session-chat-popup-timestamps-and-modes-2026-08-09\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-08-09\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all six items closed 2026-08-09 at completionAuthority=committed, each citing artifacts (six recorded `tauri-agent-tools check` invocations in /tmp/wi37446-live-checks.log: 4 assertions EXIT=0 + 2 deliberate controls EXIT=1, so the passes are falsifiable). The owner's original symptom is fixed and MEASURED: mode pill 90s -> 211ms (agent_modes set_at 15:48:02.881 -> pill ON 15:48:03.092), DELETE path confirmed too. P-003's trigger+bridge were necessary but NOT sufficient: the residual was the sync bus's bridged dedupe key being TARGET-ONLY, so coord_presence (~1999 writes/10min) monopolised advRoster.list's 90s window and swallowed agent_modes' rare writes. Fixed as WI-37446 (key now per source+target+args), committed in the libs/generic/sync submodule; the superproject pin 8764d69e carries it (verified by ancestry), so it rides the next green gate to :3070. ONE HONEST GAP, deliberately NOT closed as verified: P-004 (WI-37328) is unit-only — self-set mode:set takes the isSelf branch, which does not exercise the peer wake, so that path has never been driven live.\n\n**Next:** Nothing required for this plan; the one optional follow-up is live-verifying P-004's peer-wake path — an su sets a mode on a DIFFERENT live agent and confirms woken:1 plus a resulting turn.\n\n## Background — what the owner asked, and what is actually wrong\n\nFour owner asks (2026-08-09, verbatim in each item below). Each root cause was read\nout of the code before planning; none is a guess.\n\n### 1. Timestamps on user + agent messages [owner:Avi 2026-08-09]\n> \"In the conversation popup in the HUD tab add timestamp to the user and agent\n> messages in the gui\"\n\nThe data is already there and is simply dropped at one seam. `TimelineEntry.ts`\n(ISO) is stamped by ALL THREE backend parsers — claude\n(`streams.ts` `createAgentTimelineParser`, L93/104/112/131/143), codex and omp\n(`session-timeline-parsers.ts` L67/73/76/146/158) — and `groupEntriesIntoTurns`\nalready carries `startTs`/`endTs` per turn. But `ChatMessage` (`chat-types.ts`)\nhas no timestamp field, so `mapSessionTimeline` throws it away and\n`ChatMessageRow` has nothing to render.\n\n### 2. \"Sent 'go' but nothing happened\" [owner:Avi 2026-08-09]\n> \"I just sent the message 'go' to su-93019982 but nothing happened it just shows\n> 'ENTER Send / Sent — the agent was woken and is working on it.'\"\n\n**Not a delivery failure.** Measured 2026-08-09 03:30Z: su-93019982-b5f9-477e-9459-f398ce81e84b\nis LIVE (heartbeat 03:29:20Z, last_active 03:26:54Z, pid 400221) and holds its own\nintent (EI-19930875455827867). The banner's claim was true.\n\nThe defect is that **the owner's own message never appears in the conversation.**\nThe popup renders ONLY the mapped agent transcript stream; `handleSend`\n(`SessionChatModal.tsx`) POSTs `coord:send` and sets a banner, and adds nothing to\n`messages`. A `coord:send` to a LIVE agent is injected mid-turn, so it lands in the\ntranscript as a `type:'user'` record whose content array ALSO carries `tool_result`\nblocks — and the parser deliberately suppresses the prompt in exactly that case\n(`streams.ts:130`, `if (!hadToolResult && promptTexts.length > 0)`). So the message\nis invisible in the popup permanently, not just briefly. \"Nothing happened\" is\nliterally what the UI showed.\n\n### 3a. Drain mode display stayed OFF after being switched ON [owner:Avi 2026-08-09]\n> \"I changed drain mode from off to on, but the display still showed off afterward.\"\n\nThe pill's `current()` (`PostureActions.ts`) reads `ctx.modes`, which comes from the\n`advRoster.list` sync query. `mode:set` writes `harness_shared.agent_modes`\n(`modes/store.ts` L187) — and **`agent_modes` has NO entry in\n`sync-resolver/table-to-query-names.ts`** (verified: zero matches). Nothing\ninvalidates `advRoster.list` on a mode write, so the pill keeps its stale value\nuntil some unrelated `coord_presence` write happens to refresh the roster.\n\n### 3b. A mode change should message the agent [owner:Avi 2026-08-09]\n> \"chanfing the mode didnt send a message to the again shouldnt mode ahcnages also\n> automatically message the agent?\"\n\n`mode:set` ALREADY sends a peer-set coord message (`mode/set.ts` L220-234, carrying\nthe reason + the binding contract) — but with **no `wake`**. So a live agent only\nsees it at its next turn, and it is invisible in the popup for the same reason as\nitem 2.\n\n### 4. Drain-mode instructions input [owner:Avi 2026-08-09]\n> \"In the gui for drain mode, add an input box with instructions for the user. Tell\n> the agent what you want you want to drain from the work queue (for example, all\n> bugs except hte ones related to the p2p features)\"\n\nDrain is currently registered by the shared `OVERLAY_IDS` loop as a plain On/Off\npill. `mode:set` already takes a mandatory free-text `reason` (max 2000) that is\n**delivered to the target verbatim** — which is exactly the channel these\ninstructions want, so this needs no new table and no new endpoint, only a new input\naffordance in the mode menu.\n\n## Phase 1 — the four fixes\n\n- **P-001** `done` Message timestamps end to end: add `ts?: string | null` to `ChatMessage`; populate in `mapSessionTimeline` (user from the prompt entry's ts; assistant from the last text/result entry's ts, falling back to the turn's endTs); render a small muted time element in `ChatMessageRow` with an absolute-time title; CSS in globals.css. Other chat surfaces simply do not set ts and are unchanged. importance: high — note: ← WI-37325 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Echo the owner's sent message into the transcript so a send is VISIBLE — optimistic pending user message in SessionChatModal, reconciled against the stream. Fixes the \"nothing happened\" report at its actual cause. importance: high — note: ← WI-37326 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Bridge harness_shared.agent_modes to advRoster.list (+ agentDetail.byOwner, agentOrders.byOwner) in table-to-query-names.ts, and confirm the table emits a change notify; if it does not, fire notifySyncInvalidate from the mode store write. Makes the mode pill reflect a mode change immediately. importance: high — note: ← WI-37327 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Wake on the peer-set mode-change delivery in mode:set so a live agent learns of an owner-directed mode change at once rather than at its next turn. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-37328 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Give DRAIN its own mode-action registration with an instructions input box (its own pill, out of the shared OVERLAY_IDS loop): the typed instructions become mode:set's reason, which is already delivered verbatim to the agent. Needs a new input affordance in ChatActionBar's mode menu (the one genuinely new UI piece). — note: ← WI-37329 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Tests with each fix (vitest, in the owning workspace) plus a driven Tauri check of the popup per /internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e. — note: ← WI-37330 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n(none yet — awaiting the owner's approach + route confirmation)\n\n### D-001 — Message timestamps render BOTH absolute clock and relative age\nDate: 2026-08-09\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-09, answering a three-way fork: absolute clock / relative age / both] — \"Both.\"\n\nSo a message stamp reads `23:14 · 4m ago`: absolute first (it is the half that can be correlated against a log, a gate verdict or a journalctl window), relative second (the half that reads fastest on a session you are watching live). The date is prepended when the message is not from today (`Aug 8 · 09:02 · 14h ago`), and the full ISO instant is the hover title.\n\nThe relative half must re-render on a clock. Reuse SessionStateHeader's existing 15s tick rather than adding a second interval — the popup already runs one and a second timer on the same surface is the two-sources-of-truth smell.\n\nCONSTRAINT this places on P-001: the row memo (ChatMessageRow) is the WI-6502 typing-lag boundary. A ticking value threaded as a per-row prop would defeat that memo on every tick for every visible row. Thread the clock so the memo survives — the tick must not re-render row bodies.\n\n### D-002 — Drain instructions are BOTH delivered as the mode-change message and asserted as a standing fact\nDate: 2026-08-09\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-09, answering: message only / standing fact only / both] — \"Both.\"\n\nWhen the owner types drain instructions (e.g. \"all bugs except the ones related to the p2p features\") and turns DRAIN on, the text takes two paths:\n\n1. It becomes `mode:set`'s `reason`, which mode/set.ts already delivers to the target verbatim alongside the drain contract (L220-234). This is the PUSH — the agent is told now.\n2. It is asserted as a standing fact scoped to that agent, so it is folded verbatim into every future orient/brief until retracted. This is the DURABILITY — a drain runs for hours across compactions, and a reason delivered once is gone by the second one. That is precisely how a scope instruction quietly stops being obeyed while the mode still reads ON.\n\nTurning DRAIN off must RETRACT the fact. A stale standing instruction delivered verbatim on every wake is worse than none — the agent would keep scoping a drain that is no longer running.\n"},{"harness_slug":"readinglist","plan_slug":"readinglist-dry-run-2026-08-09","title":"Reading-list dry run — prove the GOAL-mode ladder carries work","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-09","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Reading-list dry run — prove the GOAL-mode ladder carries work\nslug: readinglist-dry-run-2026-08-09\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-09\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n# Reading-list dry run — prove the GOAL-mode ladder carries work\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-24. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nDraft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.)\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"panda-gallery","plan_slug":"panda-gallery-v1-2026-08-10","title":"Panda gallery v1 — a website displaying panda images over an animated background","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-10","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Panda gallery v1 — a website displaying panda images over an animated background\nslug: panda-gallery-v1-2026-08-10\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-10\nupdated: 2026-08-10\n---\n\n# Panda gallery v1\n\nGoal: `make-a-website-displaying-images-of-pandas-aa0205` — \"make a website displaying images of pandas\" / \"the background should have animations\" (owner, 2026-08-10).\n\nThis pot was materialized from the **papercusp-webapp** app-scope template root; `GUIDE.md` and `template.yaml` at the pot root are the composition prompt. Read GUIDE.md FIRST — it forks on two answers, and both are already decided below.\n\n## Decided up front (do not re-litigate)\n\n- **tenancy = single-user local install.** No auth, no multi-tenant server deploy. This is a website someone opens and looks at.\n- **domain = the panda photo.** The noun the app surfaces. Schema/panels/lexicon derive from it.\n- **NO PAID SERVICES.** Panda imagery must be freely and legally usable — Wikimedia Commons / public domain / explicit CC. No paid stock, no API key that costs money, no hotlinking a service that bills. Attribution recorded in-repo.\n- **The animated background is a hard requirement**, not decoration. It must visibly animate, sit behind the content without hurting legibility, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.\n- **Ships flag-ON.** A page behind an unflipped flag is dead code, not a delivered website.\n\n## Requirements\n\nWhat must be TRUE when this is done:\n\n- A person runs ONE documented command and a website opens in a browser. No further setup, no manual DB step, no missing-env failure.\n- That page displays PHOTOGRAPHS OF PANDAS — real images, at least 12 of them, laid out as a deliberate gallery rather than a list of broken image icons.\n- The BACKGROUND IS ANIMATED and the motion is visible without being told to look for it. The owner named this explicitly; a static gradient does not satisfy it.\n- The motion stops (collapses to a static background) when the viewer has `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set.\n- Every image is legally usable without payment, and its source, author and licence are recorded in `ATTRIBUTIONS.md` and credited somewhere visible in the UI.\n- The site renders correctly with NO network access after build — images are bundled, not hotlinked from a third party.\n- The layout holds at a 375px-wide mobile viewport and at a 1440px desktop viewport. No horizontal scroll, no overlapped text, no images blown out of their container.\n- Text over the animated background stays legible (contrast does not depend on which frame of the animation you catch).\n- Nothing user-visible is behind an unflipped feature flag.\n- An agent that did not build it has independently confirmed the above by actually opening the page.\n\n## Design\n\n**Composition.** This pot is the `papercusp-webapp` app-scope template: a thin composition over `papercusp-web-host` (Next.js app-router chassis), `papercusp-data-layer` and `papercusp-ui`. Build by expanding that composition per `GUIDE.md`, not by hand-rolling a Next app beside it.\n\n**The trade-off we settled: the data layer stays nearly empty.** The template pulls in a Postgres data plane, and the honest observation is that a panda gallery does not need one — the image set is static and known at build time. We are NOT ripping the data layer out (that fights the template and costs more than it saves), and we are NOT inventing a CRUD surface to justify it. The images ship as a static manifest in the repo; the data layer is left as the template provides it. If a later version wants favourites or uploads, the plane is already there.\n\n**Images.** Sourced from Wikimedia Commons / public domain / explicit CC only, downloaded and committed, optimised to a sensible max dimension and served as webp/avif with fallbacks. A single `images.ts` (or JSON) manifest carries `{ file, alt, credit, sourceUrl, licence }` so the gallery and `ATTRIBUTIONS.md` cannot drift apart — one source, two renderings.\n\n**Animated background.** CSS-first: layered, slowly-drifting shapes (bamboo silhouettes / soft gradient aurora) animated with `transform` and `opacity` ONLY, so it composites on the GPU and never triggers per-frame layout. It sits in a fixed, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: -1` layer behind the content, at reduced opacity so photo contrast wins. Canvas/WebGL is deliberately rejected for v1: it costs a render loop, a resize observer and a battery story we do not need for background motion this simple. The whole animation block is wrapped in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so the reduced-motion path is the DEFAULT and the motion is the enhancement — this fails safe rather than relying on remembering to add an override.\n\n**UI state.** Which image the lightbox is showing lives in the URL via nuqs (`parseAsString`, an image id — not a JSON blob), per repo convention. That makes a lightbox view linkable and keeps the state legible to agents. Ephemeral things (image load state, hover) stay in `useState`.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** SHIPPED — P-001..P-005 all DONE (5/5); WI-37766 closed 18:10Z. RUN IT: cd .papercusp/apps/panda-gallery && npm install && npm run dev -> http://localhost:4300 (production: npm run build && npx next start).\n\nINDEPENDENT VERDICT — PASS (goal agent su-12b70e95, OUTSIDE the fleet, 17:57Z): fresh `npm run build` (exit 0) + `npx next start -p 4301` on a separate port so the dev server could not mask it. RAW production HTML via curl, no JS executed: 18 <img> tags + 2 `animated-background` hits — server-rendered, not hydration-dependent. Headless browser on :4301: 18 images, 21 live animationNames.\n\nDelivered: 18 licence-clean Wikimedia panda photographs (all bundled — renders with no network) in a responsive grid with captions + credits; lightbox with keyboard nav and ?photo= URL state; animated background PROVEN in motion (569,586/1,296,000 pixels differ between frames 6s apart; amplified diff confines all change to the background layer); prefers-reduced-motion audited from the shipped production CSSOM (5 motion rules, all under no-preference, zero bare); typecheck clean, 30/30 tests, build exit 0.\n\nHonest limits: reduced-motion is CSSOM/source-verified, NOT runtime media-emulated; the CSSOM audit under-counts animation shorthands containing var(); ~13MB first-paint photo weight accepted deliberately, explicitly not a ship blocker.\n\nBuild trap (fact verify-ssr-by-served-bytes-not-browser-dom): verify SSR by curling served bytes on a free port, never a browser DOM read — and never run `npm run build` while `npm run dev` holds .next/.\n\n**Next:** Nothing outstanding on this plan — leader su-5697f90c to confirm 5/5 and end the fleet loop; any follow-up (image-weight optimisation, runtime reduced-motion emulation) is new work, not v1 residue.\n\n## Verification bar\n\nThe deliverable is a RUNNING SITE, not a green suite. Done means: the app starts with a documented command, a browser shows panda images in a responsive grid, and the background is visibly moving. The builder does not sign off on its own work — an independent test agent gives the verdict.\n\n## Phase 1 — ship v1\n\n- **P-001** `done` Expand the template composition into a RUNNING app: read GUIDE.md + template.yaml at the pot root, apply tenancy=single-user-local and domain=panda-photo, and pull in the required aspects (papercusp-web-host, papercusp-data-layer, papercusp-ui) until `npm run dev` (or the documented equivalent) boots and serves a page in a browser. Record the exact run command in the pot README. DONE = a human-visible page at a localhost URL, not a passing build. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-37762 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Source panda imagery, licence-clean. Collect 12-24 good panda photos from Wikimedia Commons / public-domain / explicitly-CC sources ONLY (no paid stock, no billing API). Bundle them in-repo (optimised, reasonable dimensions, webp/avif where sensible) and write an ATTRIBUTIONS.md recording per-image source URL, author and licence. Do NOT hotlink a third-party host as the primary path — the site must render with no network. importance: high — note: ← WI-37763 released\n- **P-003** `done` Build the gallery UI: a responsive grid of the panda images with captions, lazy loading, sensible alt text, and a lightbox/detail view on click. Selection and any filter/view state goes in the URL via nuqs (per repo convention), never useState. Must look deliberate at both mobile and desktop widths. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-37764 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Build the ANIMATED BACKGROUND — the owner named this explicitly, so it is a first-class deliverable. It must be visibly in motion behind the gallery (e.g. drifting bamboo / parallax layers / a slow gradient aurora / floating particles — pick one and do it well), must not fight the images for attention or hurt text contrast, must stay smooth (target 60fps, GPU-friendly transforms, no per-frame layout thrash), and MUST collapse to a static background under `prefers-reduced-motion`. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-37765 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Polish + ship: title, favicon, meta/OG tags, a one-line \"what is this\" header, and the attribution credit visible in the UI. Flip any gating flag ON. Update the pot README with how to run it. Then hand to the independent test agent — do NOT self-certify. blocked-by: P-001, P-003, P-004 — note: ← WI-37766 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"coordination-state-feature-adoption","title":"Coordination + state-plane feature adoption (fleet-wide uptake scorecard)","status":"active","created":"2026-08-10","owner":"su-e0359276-aef4-4b14-952a-a2a4e54def51","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Coordination + state-plane feature adoption (fleet-wide uptake scorecard)\nslug: coordination-state-feature-adoption\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-10\nupdated: 2026-08-10\nowner: su-e0359276-aef4-4b14-952a-a2a4e54def51\n---\n\n# Coordination + state-plane feature adoption (fleet-wide uptake scorecard)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** The Mug ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting this plan to `active`\n(rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nGrades whether the coordination and state-plane features agents are TOLD to use are actually being used, by how many distinct agents, whether those calls SUCCEED, and in which direction over time.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM hive-coordination-health / pot-coordination-health: those grade whether coordination is WORKING (claims fresh, agents not colliding, handoffs landing). This grades whether the SURFACE IS REACHED AT ALL. A feature with zero callers scores perfectly on a health rubric — there is nothing unhealthy about a surface nobody touches — which is exactly how a shipped-but-unreached capability stays invisible. Measured 2026-08-10: coord:decouple and direct watch:create had ZERO callers in 7 days while every coordination-health signal read fine.\n\nHALF THESE CRITERIA GRADE THE MEASUREMENT, NOT THE WORLD. That is deliberate. Every adoption number here is one join away from being confidently wrong, and a wrong adoption number is worse than none: it gets acted on. The 2026-08-10 baseline hit FOUR instrument errors in under two hours — wrong caller column, an unvalidated denominator, a window boundary read as a launch date, and an aggregate rate hiding a per-agent incidence. Three were caught before publication; the denominator error shipped in scorecard #1 and had to be retracted. A scorecard that reports uptake without grading its own validity is not evidence.\n\nDENOMINATORS ARE THE RECURRING FAILURE IN THIS DOMAIN. Both the adoption criteria and the rejection criterion have now been wrong in the same way: a number divided by the wrong population inverts the conclusion while looking authoritative. Always publish the population you divided by, and test it.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hud-unified-search-filter-2026-08-10","title":"HUD: one shared search box + identity-aware filtering across all four tabs","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-10","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: HUD: one shared search box + identity-aware filtering across all four tabs\nslug: hud-unified-search-filter-2026-08-10\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-10\nupdated: 2026-08-10\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001..P-005 DONE and verified. All four HUD tabs now render one shared <HudSearchBox/> (goals/plans/items converged onto the sessions tab's hero treatment) — live-drove all four in an isolated shell, every one hero=true icon=true visible=true, screenshot inspected. identityMatches() is the single shared definition of identity filtering, wired into matchesQuery, with 8 tests including the must-not-match guards. 216/216 unit tests green; typecheck clean.\n\n**Next:** P-006 is the ONLY remaining item and it is the honest gap: identity filtering is LIVE for sessions + items (work items populate identity from `assignee`), but NOT for plans and goals — their input types carry no owner/session at all, so the sync resolver must thread it through first (D-003). Do not report 'all tabs filterable by session/agent id' until P-006 lands. Also unverified: identity filtering was never live-exercised on the items board (no harness selected in the verify shell, so it was empty) — it rests on the board-level unit test.\n\n## Background\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-10 interactive verbatim] \"1. all the tabs in the hud should share the same search filter style with the left aligned highlighted search box. 2. they should all be filterable by the session id and agent id like the session tab is 3. do #1 and #2 in a generalized way.\"\n\n### Measured starting state (read at source 2026-08-10, not assumed)\n\n`HUD_TABS = ['goals', 'sessions', 'plans', 'items']` (`hud-entity-board.ts:57`). There are TWO unrelated search inputs and NO shared component (`grep -rl 'SearchBox|SearchInput|FilterBox|TabSearch' apps/operator/app` → zero hits):\n\n| tab(s) | file | markup | placeholder |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| sessions | `HudBoard.tsx:495-514` | magnifier `<svg class=\"hud__search-icon\">` + `class=\"hud__search hud__search--hero\"` + a `hud__search-status` live region | \"Search transcripts…\" |\n| goals / plans / items | `HudEntityColumns.tsx:331-340` | bare `<input class=\"hud__search\">`, no icon, no `--hero`, followed by `hud__spacer` | \"Filter {noun}…\" |\n\nSo the sessions tab already IS the target design (\"the left aligned highlighted search box\"); the other three are the plain variant. #1 is to converge the three onto the sessions treatment via ONE component, not to restyle four call sites.\n\nFor #2: `matchesQuery` (`hud-entity-board.ts:471-487`) matches ONLY `card.ref`, `card.title`, `card.context`, plus subGoal `title`/`ref`. `HudEntityCard` (`:128-167`) carries **no owner/session/agent identity field at all** — so filtering by session id or agent id on goals/plans/items is not merely unwired, the data is absent from the card model. That is the real work in #2.\n\n### Why one agent, not a fleet\n\nAll items land in three files (`HudBoard.tsx`, `HudEntityColumns.tsx`, `hud-entity-board.ts`) and two pairs are strictly sequential. Fanning out would serialize on the file locks and buy nothing.\n\n## Phase 1 — the generalized surface\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extract `HudSearchBox` (new file under `apps/operator/app/adv/hud/`) — the ONE search control: magnifier icon, `hud__search--hero` styling, `aria-label`, `data-testid`, controlled `value`/`onChange`, plus an optional `status` slot so the sessions tab keeps its \"still searching\" live region. Adopt it in `HudBoard.tsx` FIRST with zero visual change — that is the proof the extraction is faithful before any tab converges on it. importance: high — note: ← WI-37809 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Adopt `HudSearchBox` in `HudEntityColumns.tsx` so goals/plans/items get the left-aligned highlighted box. Keep the per-noun placeholder (\"Filter plans…\") — the owner asked for shared STYLE, not identical copy. Preserve the existing `hud__spacer` layout so the count-row does not reflow. blocked-by: P-001 — note: HudEntityColumns adopted HudSearchBox — goals/plans/items now render the hero box. 145/145 tests green.\n\n## Phase 2 — identity-aware filtering\n\n- **P-003** `done` Add identity to `HudEntityCard`: an `identity?: { ownerId?, sessionId?, agentHandle? }` (one optional field, not three loose ones) and populate it in the goal / plan / work-item card builders. Where a card has no single owning agent, leave it undefined rather than inventing one — an empty identity must not match a query. importance: high — note: ← WI-37816 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Generalize the predicate: one exported matcher that takes the searchable strings for a row (ref/title/context/subgoals + the P-003 identity fields) and is used by BOTH the entity board and the sessions board, so the two can never drift on what a query means. Match session id and agent id as case-insensitive substrings, consistent with today's behaviour. blocked-by: P-003 — note: identityMatches() exported as the single shared definition; wired into matchesQuery. 8 new tests incl. must-not-match guards; verified running via testNamePattern (3 matched, 129 skipped).\n- **P-006** `done` Thread owner/session identity from the sync resolver into `HudPlanInput` and `HudGoalInput` so the plans and goals tabs can filter by session/agent id too (D-003). The data exists server-side — `harness_plans.owner` for plans, and a goal's sessions are already resolvable (the goal popup's Sessions rail renders them). Until this lands, identity filtering is live for sessions + items ONLY, and any progress report must say so rather than rounding up to 'all tabs'. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-37820 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — verification\n\n- **P-005** `done` Tests + live drive. Unit-test the shared matcher (identity hit, identity MISS, empty-identity must-not-match, existing ref/title/context behaviour unchanged). Render-test that all four tabs mount `HudSearchBox`. Then drive the Tauri shell per /internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e and confirm by eye that all four tabs show the same box AND that typing a real session id (e.g. `su-12b70`) filters goals/plans/items. blocked-by: P-002, P-004 — note: ← WI-37818 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Converge on the sessions tab's design, do not invent a third\n\nThe owner named \"the left aligned highlighted search box\", which is the existing `hud__search--hero` + icon treatment already shipped on the sessions tab. The shared component adopts THAT, and the sessions tab is migrated first specifically so any visual drift shows up as a diff against a known-good surface rather than as four tabs quietly changing together.\n\n### D-002 Identity is one optional object on the card, not three loose fields\n\n`HudEntityCard` is consumed in several builders; adding three sibling optional strings invites a builder to populate one and forget the others, which silently half-works. A single optional `identity` object makes \"this card has no owning agent\" one explicit state, and makes the must-not-match-on-empty rule checkable in one place.\n\n### D-003 — D-003 Identity filtering needs a resolver change, not just a card field — only the items board has identity data today\nDate: 2026-08-10\nMeasured at source 2026-08-10 while starting P-003. P-003 as written assumed the card builders could populate identity from what they already receive. Two of the three cannot — the data is not merely unmapped, it never reaches the client:\n\n| board | input type | identity available |\n|---|---|---|\n| items | `HudWorkItemInput` | ✅ `assignee?: string \\| null` — the ownerId (e.g. `su-12b70e95-…`), already used for the assignee badge via `shortAssignee()` |\n| plans | `HudPlanInput` | ❌ NONE — fields are slug/title/status/updated/harnessSlug/nextAction/itemCounts/archived |\n| goals | `HudGoalInput` | ❌ none agent-shaped — id/title/status/killCriterion/counts/pots/spend/timestamps/parentId |\n\nSo \"filterable by session id and agent id like the sessions tab\" cannot be delivered for the plans and goals tabs by editing `hud-entity-board.ts` alone. The identity has to be threaded from the sync resolver into the input types first. The data EXISTS server-side (`harness_plans.owner`, and a goal's sessions are already resolvable — the goal popup's Sessions rail renders them), so this is a plumbing change, not a missing-source problem.\n\n#### Decision\n\n1. Keep the CARD + MATCHER generalization exactly as planned (P-003 card field, P-004 one shared matcher). That is the \"generalized way\" the owner asked for, and it is what makes the remaining work a one-line population per board rather than a third filtering implementation.\n2. Populate identity NOW for the items board, where `assignee` already arrives.\n3. Do NOT fabricate identity for plans/goals. An `identity` left undefined must not match any query — inventing a plausible-looking owner (e.g. the plan's harness, or the goal's first pot) would make the filter silently WRONG rather than merely incomplete, and a wrong filter is far worse than an empty one because it looks like it worked.\n4. Split the resolver threading into its own item (P-006) rather than smuggling it into P-003, so the plan's status honestly reports which tabs actually filter by identity.\n\n#### Consequence for the owner-facing claim\n\nUntil P-006 lands, \"all tabs filterable by session/agent id\" is TRUE for sessions + items, and FALSE for plans + goals. That must be stated plainly in any progress report rather than rounded up to \"done\".\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"owl-field-guide-site-2026-08-10","title":"North American Owls field guide — runnable website","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-10","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: North American Owls field guide — runnable website\nslug: owl-field-guide-site-2026-08-10\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-10\nupdated: 2026-08-11\n---\n\nGoal record: `ship-a-runnable-browsable-field-guide-website-to-ed7bb4` (ceiling 500 cents; kill criterion recorded there).\n\n**Deliverable:** a real, browsable website — species index + per-species detail view — for common North American owls. Runs and is viewable, not a design document.\n\n## Hard constraints\n\n1. Ceiling 500 cents (US$5) — actuals reported against it.\n2. Accuracy > polish. No invented bird facts. Every measurement / range / status / voice claim traces to Cornell Lab (All About Birds / Birds of the World), Audubon, IUCN Red List, or USFWS, and sources are cited on the site.\n3. NOT in the papercusp repo. Source lives outside the papercusp tree (`~/owl-field-guide/`) so git-sync never sweeps it.\n\n## Route (disclosed, not asked — AUTO mode)\n\nRoute A: this session implements it directly. A fleet would multiply spend against a $5 ceiling for a small static content site, and the accuracy constraint wants one consistent sourcing pass rather than N agents each inventing a schema and a citation style.\n\n## Shape\n\nAccuracy-first content pipeline — sourced species JSON first, presentation second. The site is a self-contained static page (hash-routed index + detail views) so it publishes to a real URL with no hosting spend and can be verified in a browser.\n\n## Now\n\nSourcing pass: pull species facts from authoritative references before any HTML is written.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Ship the guide\n\n- **P-001** `done` Scaffold the product OUTSIDE the papercusp tree at ~/owl-field-guide/ (verify it is not inside any repo git-sync sweeps) importance: high — note: ← WI-37859 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `wip` Sourcing pass: gather per-species facts (scientific name, length/wingspan/mass, range, habitat, voice, diet, nesting, IUCN status, ID notes) for 12-16 species from Cornell All About Birds / Audubon / IUCN, recording a source URL per species importance: urgent\n- **P-003** `todo` Encode the sourced content as structured data (species JSON) with a citation list per species; no field left to invention - omit or mark uncertain instead importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Build the site: index page listing all species + a detail view per species, hash-routed, self-contained, responsive, legible importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Accuracy audit: re-check every numeric/status claim in the built data against its cited source; fix or drop mismatches importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` Publish to a real URL and VERIFY by loading it in a browser: index renders, navigate to >=3 detail pages, links work importance: urgent\n- **P-007** `todo` Report: URL + run command, species count, sourcing method, and actual spend against the 500-cent ceiling; update the goal tripwires\n\n\n\n\n\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"release-0014-strip-authorship-from-seed-2026-08-10","title":"0.0.14-alpha: strip owner authorship from everything the desktop bundle ships (owner-directed hold)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-10","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: 0.0.14-alpha: strip owner authorship from everything the desktop bundle ships (owner-directed hold)\nslug: release-0014-strip-authorship-from-seed-2026-08-10\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-10\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n## Why\n\n[owner 2026-08-10, AskUserQuestion] 0.0.14-alpha is HELD until **no owner authorship ships**. Standing wall: fact `wall:0014-release-held-until-no-authorship-ships`. The owner rejected both cheaper routes (narrow the gate / ship without an AppImage) — do not re-propose them.\n\n## What triggered it\n\nThe cut cleared every earlier gate (sidecar identity scan CLEAN, source.tar.zst CLEAN, boot gate PASSED), then the linux leg died at the **AppDir** scan: `MUST NOT SHIP (16 file(s))`. Both .debs (3.69/4.02 GB) and the Windows .exe built fine and sit on disk, unpublished. The mac leg failed separately and unrelatedly: `Failed to find zig` — that leg now cross-compiles natively via `cargo zigbuild`, and zig is not installed on this box.\n\n## The 16, measured per file (do NOT re-derive — this cost several probes)\n\n| class | files | literal |\n|---|---|---|\n| foreign binaries | `usr/bin/oddsmith-desktop`, `usr/bin/quartermaster-desktop` | real build path (`marsh-office` x31) — sibling projects swept in from the box-wide shared `~/.cargo-target` |\n| seed git bundles | `seed/git/super.bundle`, `seed/git/submodules/{libs__papercusp,papercusp-desktop}.bundle` | owner first name x8 / x2 — **git COMMIT AUTHOR** |\n| seed corestore | `seed/corestore/db/{000009.sst,000010.blob,000011.log,000012.sst,000013.blob}` | first name x1 + the **hostname** in a `host.identity` field |\n| WSL runtime | `resources/papercup-runtime.tar.gz` + 3 members | first name x14 |\n| upstream binary | `sidecar/bin/gh` | first name x1 — **probably a FALSE POSITIVE** in a 38 MB binary; verify before \"fixing\" |\n| staged source | `sidecar/source.tar.zst` | flagged member not yet identified |\n\n## Newly VISIBLE, not newly introduced — established, do not re-litigate\n\n0.0.10-0.0.13 EACH shipped an AppImage (`harness_shared.releases`), and the AppDir scan step dates to 2026-07-13, so it ran for them. What changed is the auditor's **binary + archive** reading (~2026-08-08, after 0.0.13 published 2026-07-28): before that it used `grep -rIlE`, and `-I` SKIPS BINARY FILES, so a corestore, a git bundle, a compiled binary and a tarball were all structurally invisible. **The already-published 0.0.13 artifacts very likely carry these same bytes** — a finding about shipped releases, not a regression in this cut.\n\n## Hard constraints\n\n1. Git bundles and hypercore corestores are **content-addressed** — scrubbing bytes breaks object hashes/signatures. The WI-37620 byte-scrub technique is UNAVAILABLE for those classes: they must be *not shipped*, or *generated without authorship*, never rewritten in place.\n2. On this box **git-sync commits the whole tree under the owner's git identity and agents never commit**, so EVERY commit in the repo is authored by that identity. Stripping authorship from a bundle means rewriting every commit (changing every SHA) — which is why the owner's instruction was to DROP the bundles rather than rewrite them.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nP-001 first. The true scope is NOT yet known — `gh` is probably a false positive and the `source.tar.zst` member is unidentified. Designing fixes before measuring is the exact error this release has already made twice tonight.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `todo` MEASURE each unresolved class to the exact byte, before designing anything: which member of `sidecar/source.tar.zst` is flagged; what inside `papercup-runtime.tar.gz` carries the name x14 (is it a git config, an agent file, a checked-out tree?); and whether `sidecar/bin/gh` is a genuine hit or a coincidental byte sequence in an upstream 38 MB binary. Record findings on the plan; several fixes depend on the answers.\n- **P-002** `todo` Stop foreign binaries reaching the AppDir. `usr/bin/` gets oddsmith-desktop + quartermaster-desktop because `~/.cargo/config.toml` pins ONE shared target dir box-wide and the AppDir sweep takes all of `usr/bin`. Fix at the source in the AppImage build so only `papercusp-desktop` is packaged. Unambiguous and independent of every other item — 21 MB of unrelated apps must not ship regardless.\n- **P-003** `todo` Seed: DROP the git bundles (owner's explicit instruction). Establish what breaks — the seed exists so a new member can clone the git half offline; the cut log already mentions a path where the \"seed then cold-clones the git half\". Confirm that fallback actually works before removing, and decide whether the seed keeps a git component at all.\n- **P-004** `todo` Seed corestore: decide how the pot ships hive blocks that contain `host.identity` (the hostname) and an authored name. Cannot be scrubbed (content-addressed). Options: ship no corestore (new members cold-catch from the swarm), or stop writing owner/host identity into blocks that reach a seed. Needs a real design decision, not a patch.\n- **P-005** `todo` `resources/papercup-runtime.tar.gz` — remove the name at its SOURCE once P-001 says what puts it there. This is a WSL rootfs tarball, so the leak is likely a file baked in at image-build time.\n- **P-006** `todo` Mac leg is blocked on a MISSING BUILD TOOL, unrelated to identity: `cargo zigbuild` cannot find `zig`. Install zig (or restore the mac-VM path) so a 4-platform release is possible at all. Independent of the authorship work — can proceed in parallel.\n- **P-007** `todo` Re-cut 0.0.14 and verify EVERY gate green plus all four legs producing artifacts. Re-cutting is expensive (~25 min to the AppDir gate), so use the fast reproduction pattern first: assemble a candidate AppDir and run `audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir` against it directly.\n- **P-008** `todo` Assess the ALREADY-PUBLISHED exposure. 0.0.10-0.0.13 very likely shipped these same bytes undetected (the scanner could not read binaries before ~2026-08-08). Determine what is actually in the published 0.0.13 AppImage and tell the owner plainly — they may want those artifacts pulled or replaced. Do not bury this behind the 0.0.14 work.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/release-0014-strip-authorship-from-seed-2026-08-10 (\"0.0.14-alpha: strip owner authorship from everything the desktop bundle ships (owner-direc\"): no plan update since 2026-08-10 (62 days idle), 0/8 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"search-retrieval-quality","title":"Search + retrieval quality (per-run labelled-relevance scorecard for the hybrid stack and the context-injection leg)","status":"active","created":"2026-08-10","owner":"su-90cc5cbd-6f87-49b6-a475-71c31cc08341","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Search + retrieval quality (per-run labelled-relevance scorecard for the hybrid stack and the context-injection leg)\nslug: search-retrieval-quality\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-10\nupdated: 2026-08-12\nowner: su-90cc5cbd-6f87-49b6-a475-71c31cc08341\n---\n\n# Search + retrieval quality (per-run labelled-relevance scorecard for the hybrid stack and the context-injection leg)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic, criteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via rubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status `active` means the rubric is ratified and available for scorecards.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer or owner/su ratifies proposed rubrics via rubrics:ratify; the proposer cannot self-ratify. Revise criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nThe standard for claiming anything about retrieval quality in this workspace — the agent-facing search tools (search:fulltext, search:semantic, docs:search, plans:search, work_items:search, sessions:search) and the context-injection corpus leg that fills additionalContext.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS: retrieval numbers here have repeatedly been produced correctly and then read as answering a question they never touched. Three concrete failures, all inside 2026-08-09/10, are encoded as criteria below: (1) a 150-query pass ran Stage B rerank on EVERY stratum and its per-stratum rows were reported as tool results, though docs/plans/work_items have no rerank stage in production; (2) nDCG@k was reported as a quality score on a pass whose ideal ranking derives from the same k returned docs, so it saturates and cannot fall; (3) a \"measured and not adopted\" verdict rested on 7 batches of which only 2 were rescuable by the mechanism under test, making the relevance null nearly uninformative while being stated as settled.\n\nThe through-line: the expensive error is never the measurement, it is the INFERENTIAL REACH of the sentence written on top of it. Criteria 1-4 grade the instrument and the design; 5-9 grade the system. A run that scores well on 5-9 and badly on 1-4 has produced numbers nobody may cite.\n\n⛔ A single run NEVER sets a floor or threshold (D-074) — sample across days first.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"template-supply-chain-repair-2026-08-10","title":"Repair the official-template supply chain so a release-build user can actually build a materialized app","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-10","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Repair the official-template supply chain so a release-build user can actually build a materialized app\nslug: template-supply-chain-repair-2026-08-10\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-10\nupdated: 2026-08-10\n---\n\n## Why\n\nOwner audit 2026-08-10 [owner:Avi]: \"Are all our papercusp official templates and all their dependencies bundled in our release builds so our users can use them?\"\n\nMeasured answer: the 11 templates ARE bundled and wired correctly (build-desktop-sidecar.sh copies them, tauri.conf ships `sidecar/**/*`, main.rs sets PAPERCUSP_TEMPLATES_DIR, the `requires:` closure is complete, templates:list returns all 11 offline). That half was shipped by plan local-first-party-template-bundling-2026-07-07 and still holds. Their DEPENDENCIES are the gap.\n\nOwner directed [owner:Avi 2026-08-10, AskUserQuestion]: fix all five filed defects; su-965e1 implements directly in-session (no fleet).\n\n## Scope\n\n- WI-37777 (critical) — @papercusp/template-kit absent from tree/bundle/npm; composition-integrity (the only check all 3 app roots declare) cannot run.\n- WI-37780 — macOS ships no source.tar.zst, so libs/generic (the documented supply chain) is absent on Mac; and nothing surfaces the install's libs/generic path anywhere.\n- WI-37779 — 3 of 5 template `docs:` slugs exist nowhere; build-system/ excluded from the shipped internal-docs.\n- WI-37775 — public mirror 5 weeks stale + pre-rename; the sync guard its README claims was never committed.\n- WI-37781 — a user-layer template dir without listing.json silently shadows and degrades an official template.\n- Plus the detector failure: EI-11141 marked `resolved` 2026-08-02 while its condition stayed true.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** PHASE 4 (audit remediation) COMPLETE — 18 of 18. Phases 1-3 shipped 2026-08-10; Phase 4 fixed what the adversarial audit (WI-37833) found in them.\n\n⚠ CORRECTION TO THIS PLAN'S OWN CLAIM (F8): the previous Now said \"9 of 9 done, ALL with committed completion evidence\". Inaccurate — P-002 had NO work-item and no completion evidence. Its deliverable (template-bundle-integrity.test.ts) exists and is strong, so a ledger gap, not a delivery gap; the line overstated the evidence.\n\nFIXED (10 audit findings + F11 found while fixing):\n- F1 (major, P-010/011) — VENDORED_IN_TEMPLATE declared pot-app-seam vendored while it was vendored NOWHERE, so get-guide/new-app told builders to link `file:./pot-app-seam` and explicitly NOT to use supplyChain — the path that worked. FIXED by vendoring it into papercusp-ops-pots (D-001 logic + D-005). The tautological test that PINNED the bug is replaced by one grounding the constant against the real templates tree.\n- F2 (major, P-013) — a templates/-only change selected ZERO workspaces and \"nothing to gate\" is GREEN, so all three template guards were unreachable from the change they guard. FIXED via NON_WORKSPACE_PATH_ROUTES + route/ratchet tests.\n- F11 (major, P-012) — mirror-sync expected <pkg>/tsconfig.json unconditionally; pot-app-seam has none, so mirror:check reported unsatisfiable drift and mirror:push CRASHED (ENOENT), breaking the documented mirror repair. FIXED + pinned by a real-shaped fixture.\n- F5 (P-014) — findVendorDrift claimed byte-identical but walked ONE direction; now symmetric, with a dev-harness exclusion list + a fixture proving direction 2 fires.\n- F6 (P-015) — extractor missed side-effect/dynamic/require imports, mis-mapped scoped subpaths.\n- F3+F4+F7 (P-016) — retracted-premise prose corrected in code; see D-005.\n- F9+F10 (P-017) — get-guide no longer claims the GUIDE comes from the mirror; refused shadows surface on the materialize path.\n\nVERIFIED: 78 tests green / 8 suites; lint:tsc exit=0 clean.\n\n**Next:** THREE RESIDUALS (all disclosed, none silently dropped):\n\n1. The public mirror is still pre-rename and 404s on `pot-app-seam/`. `mirror:push` is now actually RUNNABLE (F11 fixed the ENOENT that would have aborted it mid-apply), but pushing a public GitHub repo is an outward-facing write unverifiable from this box, so it stays unexecuted: `PC_TEMPLATES_MIRROR=<clone> npm run mirror:push`. No builder follows the dead path — the ops-pots GUIDE now routes them to the vendored `file:./pot-app-seam`.\n\n2. Nothing automatic runs `mirror:check` — no CI job, no gate leg; the README says so explicitly. Class tracked as EI-20020054576584970. This is now the ONLY unwired template guard: the other three became gate-reachable in Phase 4.\n\n3. DEFERRED, disclosed: D-001's body still carries its original macOS bullet (\"defaults to 0 on both mac build paths\"), which D-005 proves false — it is one path each way (mac-vm-build ON, build-mac-cross OFF). D-005 is the decision of record and names D-001 and D-003 in its title, so a reader scanning decisions sees the correction; rewriting D-001's long body from partial reads risked corrupting it. Fold it in when a lane next touches D-001. D-001's CONCLUSION is unaffected — the `<ref>/`-only overlay argument is independent and true.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Every `@papercusp/*` the templates need is `private: true` and E404 on npm. The only supported delivery is the shipped `source.tar.zst` (libs/generic) or the sidecar/templates bundle. A fix must land the dependency in one of those two, never assume a registry.\n- templates/ content is copied VERBATIM into user apps — a fix that only works inside this monorepo is not a fix.\n- Do not \"resolve\" an item by editing prose to match a broken reality without saying so explicitly. WI-2861, WI-2909 and EI-11141 all closed green over a still-broken condition; that pattern is what this plan exists to undo.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Make a materialized app buildable\n\n- **P-001** `done` Establish where @papercusp/template-kit went (deleted vs moved vs uninitialised submodule) and restore it to the monorepo so it rides source.tar.zst — WI-37777 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-37784 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Guard: resolve EVERY non-node import in templates/**/checks/*.ts against what the release bundle actually ships (multiline-import aware — a single-line grep missed the template-kit import during the audit) — WI-37777 importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` Re-open EI-11141's false `resolved` and fix the detector that let a red-test key clear while the import still failed — WI-37777 importance: high — note: ← WI-37788 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Reach the dependencies from a real install\n\n- **P-004** `done` macOS: decide whether the .dmg ships source.tar.zst; if not, pick another delivery for libs/generic on Mac — WI-37780 importance: high — note: ← WI-37790 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Surface the install's resolved libs/generic root to the template/materialize path so GUIDEs can name a real path instead of the dev-checkout example file:../papercusp/libs/generic/sync — WI-37780 importance: high — note: ← WI-37791 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Mirror: either write+wire scripts/templates-mirror-sync.mjs and re-push, or delete the mirror supply-chain prose from templates/README.md + the ops-pots Tier-B MUST so no builder follows a dead path — WI-37775 — note: ← WI-37796 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Guidance the builder can actually follow\n\n- **P-007** `done` Docs: write (or drop) the 3 dangling agent-insights/templates-* slugs cited by all 11 templates; bundle build-system/ into the shipped internal-docs or drop that citation — WI-37779 importance: high — note: ← WI-37794 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Add a guard that every `docs:` slug in templates/*/template.yaml resolves against the docs the BUNDLE ships (not the canonical docs tree — the two differ, which is how build-system/ hid) — WI-37779 — note: ← WI-37795 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Harden user-layer shadowing: refuse (or visibly report) a listing.json-less dir shadowing an official ref; clear the dev-box residue degrading papercusp-webapp + papercusp-data-sync — WI-37781 — note: ← WI-37797 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Audit remediation (reopened by WI-37833)\n\n- **P-010** `done` F1a — Vendor pot-app-seam into templates/papercusp-ops-pots so `file:./pot-app-seam` becomes TRUE (D-001 precedent: only <ref>/ is overlaid into a materialized app); update the ops-pots GUIDE to match — WI-37839 importance: urgent\n- **P-011** `done` F1b — Replace the tautological generic-libs-root test (it asserts VENDORED_IN_TEMPLATE against itself) with one asserting the constant against the real templates tree, so it can never drift from disk again — WI-37839 importance: high\n- **P-012** `done` F11 — mirror-sync buildExpected unconditionally expects <pkg>/tsconfig.json; pot-app-seam has none, so mirror:check reports permanent phantom drift and mirror:push CRASHES on fs.copyFile ENOENT — the documented mirror-recovery command is broken importance: urgent\n- **P-013** `done` F2 — Route templates/ through NON_WORKSPACE_PATH_ROUTES so a templates-only change selects the three guards; pin the route so it cannot silently stop firing — WI-37840 importance: urgent\n- **P-014** `done` F5 — Make findVendorDrift symmetric (canonical->vendored as well) with an explicit exclusion list for tests/vitest config, so a file MISSING from a vendored copy is caught. Design WITH F1a: the new pot-app-seam copy omits README.md and src/index.test.ts importance: high\n- **P-015** `done` F6 — Widen externalImportsOf to catch side-effect imports, dynamic import() and require(), and stop mis-mapping scoped subpath specifiers (@scope/pkg/sub) to a false-positive vendor dir\n- **P-016** `done` F3+F4+F7 — Correct the retracted-premise prose: D-001's macOS bullet, D-003's over-broad title, the template-bundle-integrity comment asserting the retracted claim, and P-008's now-stale bundle-differs premise\n- **P-017** `done` F9+F10 — Fix get-guide's stale 'fetched from the public mirror' description (code reads the local store first); surface refused shadows on the materialize path instead of only in templates:list\n- **P-018** `done` F8 — Correct this plan's inaccurate '9 of 9 done, all with committed completion evidence' claim: P-002 has no work-item and no completion evidence\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — template-kit lands in BOTH places: canonical at libs/generic/template-kit, vendored inside each app-root template dir — because only the vendored copy reaches a user\nDate: 2026-08-10\nDecided by su-965e1 2026-08-10 while working P-001. Any later lane touching the template supply chain follows this; do not \"simplify\" it back to one location without reading the reasoning.\n\nTHE CONSTRAINT THAT FORCES TWO COPIES. `overlayTemplateFiles` (materialize-template-core.ts:76-89) copies the ENTIRE `<ref>/` dir into the new app — `fs.cp(src, target, { recursive: true, force: true })`, excluding only `.git` and `.papercusp/blueprint.yaml`. Nothing OUTSIDE `<ref>/` reaches the app. So:\n\n- A copy at `libs/generic/template-kit` is reachable by a user ONLY through `sidecar/source.tar.zst`, which does NOT ship on macOS (PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE defaults to 0 on both mac build paths — P-004) and whose extracted location is deliberately confined to the dev/local env children (P-005). It fixes in-repo/CI resolution and Linux/Windows, not the user.\n- A copy INSIDE `templates/<app-ref>/` rides `sidecar/templates`, which ships on EVERY platform unconditionally (`tauri.conf.json` resources `\"sidecar/**/*\"`, and build-desktop-sidecar.sh copies every file under templates/ with only node_modules/.git excluded). It is then overlaid into the app, where `\"@papercusp/template-kit\": \"file:./template-kit\"` resolves after a plain `npm install`.\n\nSo the vendored copy is the one that actually closes WI-37777 for a user; the canonical copy is what makes it maintainable and testable. Neither alone is sufficient.\n\nWHY NOT A SHARED `templates/_shared/` OVERLAY (the one-copy alternative): it would require changing materialize semantics for BOTH the local and the mirror-clone path, to buy a saving of ~200KB x2. Rejected as a bigger blast radius than the problem.\n\nWHY THREE VENDORED COPIES IS ACCEPTABLE: only the three app-scope ROOTS declare composition-integrity (papercusp-webapp, papercusp-desktop-app, papercusp-agentic-desktop-app); no aspect template imports the kit (multiline-aware scan of all 13 check files). The kit is 200KB / ~2.2k lines, zero runtime deps, `main: ./src/index.ts` — source-shippable, exactly as the public mirror already vendors it.\n\nDRIFT IS GUARDED, NOT TRUSTED. Three copies of a package is precisely the hazard that produced this bug, so the copies are not maintained by discipline: P-002's guard asserts the vendored copies are byte-identical to `libs/generic/template-kit` AND that every non-node import in `templates/**/checks/*.ts` resolves against something the release bundle ships. The vendored copy carries the runtime subset (package.json + tsconfig + src/*.ts minus *.test.ts), matching the mirror's shape.\n\nPROVENANCE OF THE RESTORED CODE: `libs/generic/template-kit` existed only on `origin/legacy-papercup-main-2026-07-07` and was dropped in the papercup->papercusp migration; it was also never added to the root package.json `workspaces` array (an explicit list, not a `libs/generic/*` glob), which is why nothing flagged its absence. Restored from the clone at ~/.papercusp-workspaces/clones/papercup @ 254e64b2 (2026-07-06, clean for that path) — strictly newer than the legacy-branch snapshot (adds src/guide-lint.{ts,test.ts}). Workspace entry re-added; `node_modules/@papercusp/template-kit -> ../../libs/generic/template-kit` verified, and the exact import EI-11141 reported as unresolvable now resolves to src/index.ts.\n\n### D-002 — 'red-test' is absence-close INELIGIBLE — a quiet tick means \"nobody ran it\", not \"it passes\"\nDate: 2026-08-10\nRULING (P-003), binding on anyone touching the watchdog auto-close path.\n\n'red-test' has been REMOVED from AUTO_CLOSE_ELIGIBLE_SOURCES (packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/auto-close.ts). Do not re-add it. The code carries a ⛔ comment saying so, and auto-close.test.ts pins it with a must-fail assertion.\n\nWHY. That allowlist's own stated premise is that a signal's absence \"reliably means the problem resolved (the collector runs every tick and would re-fire if it persisted)\". That premise holds for every OTHER entry, each of which re-derives its predicate from live state each tick (a DB query, a claim table, a routine's `active` flag). It is FALSE for red-test alone: its input is harness_shared.test_runs, a LOG OF EXTERNALLY-TRIGGERED RUNS. When a test stops being run — dropped from a suite, renamed, left un-owned by any vitest config, or its checkout removed — the signal goes quiet without the condition changing at all. The collector cannot distinguish a fixed test from an unrun one.\n\nMEASURED CASE. EI-11141 named templates/papercusp-desktop-app/checks/composition-integrity.test.ts. Across ALL of test_runs history, in every checkout, that path has ZERO 'pass' rows — every recorded run is a fail. Its last run was 2026-07-27; it was flipped `resolved` 2026-08-02; the import it named was still broken on 2026-08-10.
