The runs stopped because no vitest config owns templates/**/checks/*.test.ts (testing:run answers TEST_FILE_ROUTE_ERROR), not because anything was fixed.\n\nWHY THIS COSTS NOTHING. red-test is also the ONLY source with a POSITIVE-evidence resolution path — resolveProvenGreenRedTests (P-007), which resolves on N consecutive recorded greens and attaches them as real completion evidence. Absence-closing was strictly the weaker, unfalsifiable half of that pair. A genuinely-fixed test still auto-resolves, now always with evidence.\n\nCOROLLARY, worth generalising: two pre-existing tests asserted that a red-test EI FALLS BACK to an absence close when green evidence is unavailable (a test_runs read error, or the green deps not injected). Both were rewritten. Losing the ability to READ evidence is not evidence. \"Fail-soft\" means resolve nothing and keep sweeping; closing on the weaker signal is failing OPEN.\n\nSCOPE HONESTY. The absence-close path sits behind default-OFF flag papercusp-watchdog-auto-close, so it was NOT the actor that closed EI-11141. This fixes a LATENT defect. The write path that CAN produce EI-11141's exact unattributed signature (terminal state with NULL terminal_owner, no completion ref, no audit row) is the work_items union-view INSTEAD OF trigger, filed separately as EI-20092514168581881 — that one is live and unfixed.\n\n### D-003 — macOS DOES ship source.tar.zst (Server role) — the recorded \"both mac paths default OFF\" finding was wrong; the real defect was an unverified staging step\nDate: 2026-08-10\nDecided by su-965e1 2026-08-10 while working P-004 (WI-37790). **This CORRECTS a finding recorded on WI-37790's own checkpoint.** Any lane citing that checkpoint must re-read this decision instead.\n\n#### THE RETRACTED CLAIM\n\nWI-37790's checkpoint stated, as an already-measured finding (\"do not re-measure\"):\n\n> both macOS build paths default the source stager OFF —\n>   papercusp-desktop/bin/build-mac-cross.sh:168 -> PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE=\"${PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE:-0}\"\n>   papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-build.sh:403 -> if [[ \"${PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE:-0}\" == \"1\" ]]\n> so macOS ships NO sidecar/source.tar.zst\n\nThe `mac-vm-build.sh` half is FALSE, and the conclusion drawn from it is false.\n\n#### WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES (re-measured, line-pinned)\n\n- `stage-source-tree.sh:50` — `if [[ \"${PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE:-1}\" != \"1\" ]]; then ... exit 0; fi`. The stager **self-gates DEFAULT-ON**, and says so in its own header (\"DEFAULT-ON since the all-5-buttons dogfood bundle is VM-verified\").\n- `mac-vm-build.sh:402` — `bash bin/stage-source-tree.sh`, called **UNCONDITIONALLY**. It never sets `PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE` anywhere (grep: only :396 comment, :403, :405).\n- `mac-vm-build.sh:403` is therefore **NOT the gate** — it is the *post-condition verification*, and reading it as the gate is the error. With the env unset it evaluated `0 == 1` → false → **the check was SKIPPED**, while the staging above it had already RUN.\n\nSo the mac VM build **stages and ships `source.tar.zst`**. Windows runs the identical verification at `:-1` (`build-windows-cross.sh:206`), so mac was the lone leg that staged without checking.\n\n#### THE REAL DEFECT (this is what P-004 fixed)\n\nA silent staging failure on the mac leg would produce a Server app with no `source.tar.zst`, degrade dev/local to `no-source-tree`, and leave **nothing in the build log** to explain it — because the only check was disabled by a default that contradicted both the stager it verifies and the Windows leg it mirrors. Fixed at `mac-vm-build.sh:403` (`:-0` → `:-1`, + a staged-size echo naming the role split). `bash -n` clean.\n\n#### THE DELIVERY DECISION P-004 ASKED FOR\n\nWhere the libs/generic tree does and does not reach a Mac:\n\n| macOS artifact | ships source.tar.zst | why |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Server app / DMG** (mac-vm-build) | **YES** | stager default-on; main.rs points PAPERCUSP_SOURCE_ARCHIVE at its own sidecar copy |\n| **GUI app / DMG** (mac-vm-build) | **NO — deliberate** | `mac-vm-build.sh:507-510` stashes it out for the `gui` role; a GUI copy would double the multi-GB .app + DMG on the disk-tight VM (WI-3307) |\n| **cross-built** (build-mac-cross) | **NO by default — legitimate** | Linux-native `node_modules` are the WRONG ARCH for darwin. Opt-in `PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE=1` cross-installs a real darwin tree (`cross-install-darwin-tree.sh`) |\n\n**DECIDED: do NOT ship the archive in the GUI role.** Paying multi-GB in every GUI DMG to make a minority build path able to `file:`-link component packages is the wrong trade, and the two packages a template actually REQUIRES (`template-kit`, `pot-app-seam`) are vendored into the template itself (D-001) and so are unaffected.\n\n**The residual is accepted and made VISIBLE rather than hidden:** on a GUI-only or cross-built Mac, `supplyChain.root` is `null` and P-005's surfaces say so explicitly — including that this is expected and what to do — instead of handing the builder the dev-checkout path that fails at `npm install`. That honesty is the deliverable; a fake path was the bug.\n\n#### METHOD NOTE (why this was worth re-measuring)\n\nThe retracted claim cited two real files at two real line numbers and looked fully measured — which is exactly why it survived into a checkpoint marked \"do not re-measure\". The error was reading a **post-condition check as a gate**. When a flag appears at several sites, the one that DECIDES is the one the executing statement is nested under; a `:-0` default sitting next to an unconditional call is a signal to read the call, not to trust the default.\n\n### D-004 — D-004 — the mirror-sync guard was RECOVERED, not written; WI-37775's \"never committed\" was false; the mirror push stays UNEXECUTED\nDate: 2026-08-10\nSettles P-006 and RETRACTS an absence claim recorded by this plan's own WI-37775. Read this before re-deriving anything about the mirror guard.\n\n1) THE RETRACTION. WI-37775 asserted `scripts/templates-mirror-sync.mjs` \"does not exist ... was never committed, under any path\", citing an empty `git log --all --diff-filter=A`. That is FALSE as stated. The script exists, committed and tracked, at\n  /home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/clones/papercup/scripts/templates-mirror-sync.mjs\nadded 2026-07-05 10:22 (commit 2774f136).\n\nWHY THE ORIGINAL SEARCH MISSED IT — a scope-of-inference failure worth generalizing: that clone is a SEPARATE checkout of the SAME repo (origin Papercusp/papercup) sitting 141 commits AHEAD OF ITS OWN ORIGIN — local git-sync auto-commits that were never pushed. An unpushed sibling clone is unreachable from the canonical tree, so `git log --all` there returns a truthful-looking EMPTY. **`git log --all` proves absence from THIS repo's refs, never absence from the machine.** Only a filesystem search outside the tree found it.\n\n2) WHAT SURVIVES. The operational conclusion was right: the guard was genuinely absent from the canonical repo — nothing ran it, no npm script, no gate, no test (re-verified by rg across the whole tree incl. submodules: `templates-mirror-sync|mirror:check|mirror:push` appeared ONLY in templates/README.md and its two generated copies). So the README really did advertise an enforcement mechanism that did not exist here.\n\n3) THE RECONCILED HISTORY (this also explains memory id=61785928, which asserted the script HAD been used): 2026-07-05 an agent wrote the script in that side clone and RAN it — which is why the live mirror genuinely carries `hive-app-seam/` and the supply-chain README prose. The clone's commits never reached origin, so the script never entered the canonical repo. The hive->pot rename then happened canonically with nothing able to sync the mirror — hence today's 404 on `pot-app-seam/`.\n\n4) THE RULING. P-006 is a RECOVER-AND-MODERNIZE, not a write-from-scratch. The recovered implementation already exceeded the shape this plan's `## Now` recommended, so it was restored rather than reinvented (reuse-first): canonical `templates/` + README + vendored packages diffed against a mirror clone; check mode exits 1 on drift; `--push` applies/commits/pushes; refuses a missing mirror clone (exit 2); refuses an UNINITIALIZED vendored submodule so an empty canonical source can't mass-delete the mirror; refuses to push to a non-mirror origin. Changed for current reality: VENDORED `hive-app-seam` -> `pot-app-seam`; the imperative body moved behind `main()` so the diff engine is importable and testable.\n\n5) THE PUSH IS DELIBERATELY NOT EXECUTED. `mirror:push` ships as a wired, working lever but was NOT run: pushing to a public GitHub repo is an outward-facing write whose path cannot be verified from this box, and this plan's own recommended shape was \"local check-mode only, push left manual\". So the mirror REMAINS pre-rename and still 404s on `pot-app-seam/`. That is a known, documented residual — not an oversight.\n\n6) CONSEQUENCE FOR BUILDERS (the user-facing half of the bug). Because the mirror is still stale, both places that told a builder to `file:`-link out of a mirror clone were pointing at a 404. Both now point instead at the install-resolved `libs/generic` root that P-005 surfaces as `supplyChain` on templates:get-guide / templates:new-app — the only path guaranteed to exist where the builder actually is: templates/papercusp-ops-pots/GUIDE.md (the Tier-B MUST) and templates/README.md.\n\n7) THE README RULE THAT CAUSED ALL OF THIS. The original defect was prose asserting a guarantee nothing enforced. The rewritten bullet therefore states what now exists (the check + how to run it), and states EXPLICITLY what still does not: no CI job, no green-checkpoint gate, and no publish tooling runs `mirror:check`, so nothing stops a stale mirror being published. Do not re-add a claim of automatic enforcement to that bullet without wiring the enforcement first.\n\nMEASURED at ruling time: `mirror:check` against the live mirror clone exits 1 with 132 drift items (76 missing, 26 changed, 30 extraneous), including `missing pot-app-seam/package.json` and `extraneous papercusp-ops-hives/GUIDE.md` — i.e. the guard independently reproduces the exact defect WI-37775 filed.\n\n### D-005 — D-005 — macOS source-staging: ONE path each way. D-001's \"both mac paths OFF\" and D-003's unqualified \"macOS DOES ship\" are both wrong as written; D-001's conclusion survives\nDate: 2026-08-10\nDate: 2026-08-10. Recorded by su-965e1 during the P-001..P-009 audit (WI-37833). Binding on anyone citing D-001 or D-003 about macOS source delivery.\n\nTHE MEASURED TRUTH (read the code, not either decision):\n  papercusp-desktop/bin/stage-source-tree.sh:50   ${PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE:-1}  -> default ON (self-gates)\n  papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-build.sh:411       ${PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE:-1}  -> default ON\n  papercusp-desktop/bin/build-mac-cross.sh:168    ${PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE:-0}  -> default OFF\n\nSo exactly ONE of the two macOS build paths ships source.tar.zst by default.\n\nWHAT EACH PRIOR STATEMENT GOT WRONG:\n- D-001 asserts libs/generic \"does NOT ship on macOS (PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE defaults to 0 on BOTH mac build paths — P-004)\". The \"both\" is FALSE: mac-vm-build defaults ON.\n- D-003 corrects that with the headline \"macOS DOES ship source.tar.zst (Server role)\". Read without the parenthetical — which is how a headline is usually read — this OVER-corrects: cross-built macOS bundles still ship no source tree by default.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS AND WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. D-001's CONCLUSION (vendor template-kit into the app-scope template dirs) STANDS, because its primary argument is independent of the macOS question: overlayTemplateFiles copies only `<ref>/` into a materialized app, so nothing outside `<ref>/` reaches the user on ANY platform. The macOS bullet was corroborating, not load-bearing. Do NOT read this decision as licence to de-vendor template-kit.\n\nDO NOT PROPAGATE THE RETRACTED CLAIM. It is still asserted as fact in committed code at\npackages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/template-bundle-integrity.test.ts:27-28 (\"...via source.tar.zst, which macOS builds do not ship\"). That comment should be corrected to name the cross-build path specifically. A future reader will otherwise treat it as measured.\n\nGENERALIZABLE: when a decision retracts an earlier one, check whether the retraction's own headline is scoped as tightly as its body — D-003's body was careful (\"Server role\"), its title was not, and the title is what gets quoted.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"auto-coupling-health","title":"Auto-coupling health — does the derived coupling engine produce true, bounded, retired and consumed edges?","status":"active","created":"2026-08-11","owner":"su-d41fe23c-ce13-4ecc-977e-4688dd915458","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Auto-coupling health — does the derived coupling engine produce true, bounded, retired and consumed edges?\nslug: auto-coupling-health\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-11\nupdated: 2026-08-11\nowner: su-d41fe23c-ce13-4ecc-977e-4688dd915458\n---\n\n# Auto-coupling health — does the derived coupling engine produce true, bounded, retired and consumed edges?\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`draft` ⇒ a proposed rubric.\n\n**Next:** The Mug ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting this plan to `active`\n(rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nCoupling is the RELEVANCE gate on peer state: coupled peers are the ones worth rendering to an agent in detail, and the cost is paid by BOTH sides of every edge, on every read that renders it. Resolution is ONE predicate — `derived ∪ declared − suppressed` (`resolveCoupledPeers`, packages/operator-core/lib/coord/couplings.ts) — with the AUTO half recomputed per read by `deriveCouplings` (coord/coupling-derivation.ts) from roster rows the caller is already being sent.\n\nThis rubric grades whether that machine WORKS end to end: whether agents are told it exists, whether each relation in the vocabulary can actually fire, whether the census measuring it is honest enough to be quoted, whether fan-out stays pairwise, whether edges are ever retired, and whether anything consumes them.\n\nBOUNDARY — vs `coordination-state-feature-adoption`: that rubric governs HOW ADOPTION IS MEASURED (caller attribution, denominators, incidence vs rate, boundary artifacts). It is BINDING here, not duplicated. In particular its criterion 'manual verbs with a default-ON automatic path are judged on whether the AUTOMATIC path delivers, not on verb call counts' governs `declared-path-adoption` below — do not grade a low `coord:couple` count as failure without first grading the automatic path. BOUNDARY — vs `hive-coordination-health` / `pot-coordination-health`: those grade whether coordination is working at all; this grades one mechanism inside it.\n\nGOVERNING DECISIONS (read before grading, and before proposing any new relation): D-044 + D-078 (re-ranking only, never widening; cell inputs must take the checked reader path), D-053 (relevance gate; no populated-but-contentless field), D-054 (no set-membership edges — the owner cut `same-fleet`: 'FLEETS CAN HAVE 30 MEMBERS THAT IS TOO MUCH COUPLING NO?'), D-061 (manual declare/decouple with no authorization; suppress-don't-delete; normalized pair), D-087 (every emitted signal carries a typed token AND prose from the same branch), D-093 (`shared-file` cut as permanently starved), D-098 (census default-ON). Plan: `auto-coupling-delivery-and-correctness-2026-08-09`.\n\nTHE STANDING TRAP THIS RUBRIC EXISTS TO CATCH: a coupling relation cannot announce that it has gone dark. It keeps its token, keeps appearing in the census, and keeps reading `armed: true` while emitting nothing — so PERMANENTLY-STARVED and NEWLY-BROKEN look identical from the outside. That is not hypothetical: `shared-file` sat in the vocabulary for 14 days producing exactly zero edges before anyone measured it. Grade the EDGES, never the code's appearance of health.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"auto-coupling-health-recurring-grade-2026-08-11","title":"Recurring auto-coupling-health grade — the standing check that a derived relation has not gone dark","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-11","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Recurring auto-coupling-health grade — the standing check that a derived relation has not gone dark\nslug: auto-coupling-health-recurring-grade-2026-08-11\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-11\nupdated: 2026-08-12\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Scheduled template (weekly). Each fire GRADES the auto-coupling system against the ACTIVE `auto-coupling-health` rubric (11 criteria) and escalates only when something is actually wrong. Created by coupling-signal-liveness-and-lifecycle-2026-08-11 P-007.\n\n**Why this exists:** the derived-signal detector already runs hourly inside the green-checkpoint gate (`lint:derived-signal-firings`), but it is REPORT-ONLY until each relation's review date, so between now and then a relation going dark is just a line in a gate log nobody reads. All three prior instances of this failure class were green in every test at the time and were caught only because a human went looking. This is the standing check that distinguishes \"the signal is correct\" from \"the signal never runs\".\n\n**Next:** nothing to claim between runs — the run agent executes the steps below on each fire.\n\n## Procedure (each fire)\n\n1. Run `npm run lint:derived-signal-firings`. Record, per relation: verdict, edges, armed/runs, input runs — plus the header's `census rows: N (vV)` and any `⚠ ... OLDER census instrument ... excluded` count.\n2. Emit the grade: `scorecards:emit { rubricRef: 'auto-coupling-health', ratings: { ...all 11 criteria } }`, each rating carrying CONCRETE evidence (numbers from step 1 and from the coupling tables), never a bare score. A scorecard missing criteria files as a PARTIAL and reads as a silent truncation — grade every criterion or say why it is unratable.\n3. Escalate to the human (`coord:send { to:['human'] }`) ONLY when one of these holds — otherwise file the scorecard and stop, silently:\n   - any relation has a FAILING verdict (`never-armed` / `unobserved`) AND `census rows` >= MIN_CENSUS_ROWS_TO_FAIL (5), i.e. the evidence floor is met;\n   - any relation reads `starved` on two consecutive fires (one window is scarcity; two is a dead upstream producer);\n   - `census rows` at the CURRENT version is still 0 more than 7 days after D-007 landed. That case is the detector's own dead-signal shape one level up: it means the corrected instrument never reached production, and the probe would keep reporting a confident `no-data` forever.\n4. WI-38032 TRIGGER: the first fire at which the current-version census window reaches >= 5 rows is the moment the deferred cut re-read becomes executable (D-005 deferred P-004's cut authority to a post-fix census re-read; D-007 made the corrected window identifiable as `v = 2`). On that fire, say so explicitly in the escalation and reference WI-38032.\n\n## Background\n\nParent: `coupling-signal-liveness-and-lifecycle-2026-08-11` (P-007), which answered the question \"are these relations dead?\" with \"no — the INSTRUMENT and the INPUTS were\" (D-003, D-004, D-005), then fixed the instrument's versioning (D-007).\n\n## Decisions\n\n- D-001: WEEKLY, not daily. The rubric has 11 criteria and a complete grade is real work, so cadence is a cost decision. The probe's own window is 14 days and every prior instance of this failure class went unnoticed for 12-14 days, so a weekly grade detects the class well inside the interval that has historically mattered, at a seventh of a daily grade's cost.\n- D-002: This does NOT duplicate the gate-wired probe. The probe answers \"what are the verdicts\" hourly and cheaply; this answers \"does a human know, and is it graded against the standard\" — and it is the only leg that can escalate BEFORE a relation's review date, which is the whole gap P-007 named.\n- D-003: Escalation is CONDITIONAL, not per-fire. A weekly \"all fine\" message trains the reader to ignore it, which would reproduce the very failure this plan exists to prevent — the signal nobody reads. The scorecard is filed every fire regardless, so the trend stays queryable via `scorecards:list` / `rubrics:trend` without spending the human's attention.\n\n### D-001 — A `no-data` probe verdict is NOT an unmeasurable window — `edges` is version-comparable, only `inputs` was redefined, so read the excluded rows before rating liveness `unknown`\nDate: 2026-08-12\nEstablished on fire 1 (2026-08-12T00:52Z, scorecard EI-20206402247082799, non-implementer grade).\n\nD-007 bumped the census to v2 because `inputs` was REDEFINED, and `lint:derived-signal-firings` correctly refuses to average two instruments — it excludes every v1 row and, with zero v2 rows, prints `no-data` for all five relations. A grader who stops at that verdict must rate derived-signal-liveness and signal-concentration `unknown`, and this plan's own Procedure step 2 invites exactly that.\n\nTHAT IS AN UNDER-READ. Only `inputs` changed meaning. `edges` and `armed` did not. So the excluded v1 rows still answer both criteria, and read directly they answer them sharply:\n\n  coord-exchange   635 edges  armed 327/327\n  awaits             1 edge   armed 327/327\n  blocks-me          0 edges  armed 327/327\n  blocked-by-me      0 edges  armed 327/327\n  holds-a-lock-on    0 edges  armed 176/327   <- a GATED leg, invisible in the collapsed `no-data` view\n\nCONSEQUENCES, all of which the `no-data` reading loses: (1) derived-signal-liveness is `degraded`, not `broken` (prior card) and not `unknown` — 2 of 5 relations demonstrably fire in production; (2) the single `awaits` edge is positive confirmation of this plan family's PARTIAL RETRACTION of D-001's 'true zero'; (3) signal-concentration is quantifiable at 635/636 = 99.84%, which is over its drift marker, rather than unrateable; (4) holds-a-lock-on's armed rate of 176/327 identifies it as a gated leg, which is a different defect from the 0-edge relations beside it.\n\nRULE FOR EVERY FUTURE FIRE: when the probe prints `no-data` because the v2 window is empty, do NOT rate liveness or concentration `unknown` on that basis alone. Query the excluded rows on `edges`/`armed` (lateral jsonb_each over metadata_json->'derivedSignals'->'relations', WITHOUT the version predicate) and rate on those, stating the version the reading came from. Rate `unknown` only when even that is empty.\n\nSCOPE LIMIT, so this is not over-applied: it holds ONLY for fields D-007 did not touch. `inputs` remains non-comparable across versions and must never be pooled — which is exactly what the probe's exclusion exists to prevent, and that exclusion is correct for the verdict logic it guards. This decision narrows how a GRADER reads the probe's output; it does not ask for any change to the probe.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"blender-steward-heartbeat-2026-08-11","title":"Blender steward heartbeat — ensure one live GOAL owner","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-11","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Blender steward heartbeat — ensure one live GOAL owner\nslug: blender-steward-heartbeat-2026-08-11\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-11\nupdated: 2026-08-20\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n**Purpose:** fallback recovery heartbeat for the Blender steward goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`. This schedule does NOT pace stewardship; the live steward self-paces its own loop. Current initial owner: `su-d3dd7eae-280b-47b7-b629-00c15072053f` (headless, default system account, GOAL plus GRADE health overlay).\n\n**Per-run outcome:** leave exactly one fresh, wakeable su holding GOAL subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, with GRADE stacked only for the Blender health scorecard and with a working self-wake. If the incumbent is healthy, record that evidence and do not spawn. If absent/dead, launch one replacement headless su on the default system account/default model/warm carry, then `mode:set` GOAL with the existing goal id and GRADE with the scorecard-only scope below. Never create a duplicate goal and never change Scout account routing.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Background\n\nOperational child of `blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11` D-001/D-003. The retired Mug/Queen/Cup tier no longer supervises Blender output. The replacement is one su GOAL-mode portfolio steward; GRADE is only an overlay for evidence-complete rubric scorecards. Scheduled-plan fires mint a run work-item, so this plan states the real ensure-one operation rather than claiming the schedule directly launches an agent.\n\n## Phase 1 — recurring ensure-one run\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Read the goal, mode registry, live presence, and incumbent loop. If exactly one healthy GOAL holder exists, checkpoint the owner id + liveness evidence and finish without spawning. If none exists, launch ONE headless su (default account/model, warm carry), enter `goal` with subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, then enter `grade` with standing instructions: grade only the Blender health scorecard; the GOAL contract owns post-epoch idea grading, draft disposition, ready-plan decomposition, budget/kill enforcement, and self-paced wake cadence. If multiple fresh holders exist, retain the oldest healthy holder, stop/clear the newer duplicate holders safely, and record the disposition. Verify the surviving owner has a wake source before completing. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Six-hour schedule is recovery only\nThe recurrence is a six-hour liveness backstop with skip-old/skip-overlap semantics. The steward chooses its operational cadence from eligible backlog and trend; no scheduled fire may reset or slow that self-paced loop.\n\n### D-002 — Existing goal is authoritative\nRecovery reuses goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b` ($25 ceiling and its recorded kill criterion). It must not call `goals:start`, which would mint a duplicate goal; it launches a session and attaches the existing GOAL subject instead.\n\n### D-003 — GRADE scope is narrow\nGRADE monitors the existing Blender rubric/scorecard. Draft arbitration, idea dispositions, ready decomposition, and ratification are GOAL acts, not rubric grades.\n\n### D-004 — Steward contract: ratification authority is bounded (small + reversible + not self-originated)\nDate: 2026-08-11\nTHE CONTRACT LINE for the ratification duty D-003 assigns to GOAL mode. The steward may flip a scout draft to `ready` — which auto-promotes its items into the claimable pool via `ready-plan-autostart` — subject to TWO conditions:\n\n  1. NOT IRREVERSIBLE — no promoted item in the dangerous set (migration · outward-facing publish/send · fleet-autonomy escalation · auth/security · kill-switch).\n  2. NOT SELF-ORIGINATED — the steward did not file the idea the draft came from.\n\nThere is NO SIZE LIMIT [owner:Avi 2026-08-11, interactive]: a draft of ANY item count may be ratified when both conditions hold. (An earlier ≤3-item cap was my own bounded AUTO default; the owner removed it — see blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11, the decision superseding D-008.)\n\nOtherwise: do not ratify, mark needs-human, escalate to the owner with the grade and rationale.\n\nFAIL-CLOSED, and this matters more now than it did: if the risk class or the origin cannot be determined, the draft does NOT qualify for autonomous ratification. With no size cap, these two conditions are the ENTIRE safety margin, so an undeterminable input must never be resolved optimistically.\n\n### D-005 — This heartbeat cannot recover a dead steward on its own — an unexecuted run wedges the schedule permanently (fixed 2026-08-16)\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Recorded by su-1cd24b43 while resuming the Blender GOAL steward at owner Avi's direction.\n\nD-001 calls this schedule a \"six-hour liveness backstop\". Between 2026-08-15T06:01Z and 2026-08-16T02:5xZ it was not a backstop at all: it had stopped minting runs entirely, and the Blender loop stayed dark ~21h with the producer still running (last human_grade anywhere was 2026-08-13; actionable post-epoch backlog stood at 83 when the loop was restarted).\n\nMECHANISM (verified against the writers, not inferred):\n- `runScheduledPlanFire` with `concurrency:'skip'` refuses to mint while ANY run of this template is `plan_runs.status='running'`.\n- Run 958 (minted 2026-08-15T06:01) stayed `running` because its item PR-958-P-001 was never claimed — there was no live steward to claim it, which is precisely the condition this heartbeat exists to detect.\n- `reconcileScheduledPlanRuns` structurally cannot settle it: it settles only when all work_items are TERMINAL.\n- `sweepPlanRuns` WOULD have reclaimed it after 30 min, but its only caller was the `plans:runs` read. Nobody was around to read it either.\n- Net: `routines.last_fired_at` advanced to 2026-08-16T00:02:07Z having minted nothing at 12:00, 18:00 and 00:02. No error, no failed run, no alert.\n\nTHE RULING — three things follow for anyone relying on this plan:\n\n1. **This heartbeat has a circular dependency and must not be treated as sufficient recovery on its own.** Its runs are executed by claiming a work-item, and in the failure it is meant to catch there is no agent alive to claim one. A recovery mechanism whose execution requires the thing it recovers is not a backstop. Until a steward-independent executor exists, an EXTERNAL supervisor (an su with an armed loop, or the owner) is the real recovery path; the heartbeat is a convenience on top of that. Do not read \"schedule armed + routine active\" as \"the steward is being watched\".\n\n2. **The generic wedge is fixed; the circularity in (1) is NOT.** `sweepOrphanedPlanRuns` now runs on the 30s tick from `reconcileAndGovern` (reconcile first so real outcomes are preserved, then reclaim the orphan residue), with 4 recurrence-guard tests in reconcile-plan-runs.integration.test.ts driving only the tick path. So an orphaned run can no longer permanently disable ANY schedule. Filed as EI-20577333581927016. That fix means the heartbeat will now keep firing — it does NOT mean a fired run gets executed when no steward is alive.\n\n3. **NEVER size this backlog with a hand-written query — use `classifyUngraded()`** (packages/operator-core/lib/scout/ungraded-scope.ts). CORRECTION, recorded against my own error in this same session: the resume brief I wrote cited \"143 post-epoch ungraded, routed since 2026-08-11\". That was wrong three ways, and steward su-e9d9bc18 refused it rather than acting on it. (a) The epoch is not a calendar day — floors are PER-ORIGIN under blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11#D-014: scout = 2026-08-12T00:00:00Z, su-ideate = 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z. (b) It applied no terminal/outcome filter, counting rows whose artifacts had already resolved won/lost. (c) It therefore swept in 15 scout rows routed 2026-08-11 00:18-03:34 that are PRE-EPOCH. Because grading is FORWARD-ONLY (D-002) and `blender:grade-idea` HAS NO RETRACT (EI-20347901071497589), draining that list would have burned 15 unretractable grades and repeated a defect already on file. The authoritative four buckets are graded | pre-epoch | terminal | actionable, and ONLY `actionable` is drainable. True baseline at resume: actionable 83 (scout 71 + su-ideate 12), pre-epoch 1058, terminal 45, all_ungraded 1186.\n\nALSO NOTE: this class of failure is silent by construction — `last_fired_at` advances whether or not a fire produced a run, so \"fired N times, minted nothing\" has no signal. Flagged in EI-20577333581927016 as a monitoring gap, deliberately not fixed here.\n\n### D-006 — D-004 arbitration, 2026-08-16: 8 live drafts ruled (2 ratified, 2 needs-human, 4 revise) — and ratification is currently INERT without a spec triad\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Recorded by su-e9d9bc18 (Blender steward, GOAL+GRADE) applying D-004 to the scout-routed draft queue.\n\n=== SCOPE CORRECTION (measured, not inherited) ===\nThe queue is NOT \"20 draft plans\". Joining scout_routed_ideas (rail='plan', routed_ref='plan:<slug>') to harness_plans gives 15 draft rows, split across TWO workspace_ids:\n- papercusp-workspace: 8 drafts — THE REAL QUEUE. Independently corroborated by the scout-draft-review backstop alarm (\"8 scout-routed drafts unreviewed >1h\").\n- default: 7 drafts — NOT arbitrable (separate finding, filed).\nThe other ~12 non-scout drafts (context-trimming-tiers, agent-managed-compaction, ...) are hand-authored and were never in D-004 scope.\n\n=== D-004 CONDITION 2 (not self-originated): CLEAR for all 15, verified in-ledger ===\nEvery row is origin='su-ideate' with created_by in {su-d4b9a5af, su-2c130be1, su-0b4a6333, su-bbf8a1fe, su-c474b9db}. None is su-e9d9bc18. This population has MOVED past the assumption in ratification-gate.ts's header (\"measured 2026-08-12: all 6 rail='plan' rows are origin='scout' with created_by NULL — no current row can trigger this refusal\"). created_by is now populated on every row, so the mechanical guard is live-relevant exactly as that header predicted.\n\n=== D-004 CONDITION 1 (dangerous set): MINE ALONE TO JUDGE ===\nratification-gate.ts enforces ONLY condition 2 and says so: \"(1) IS NOT ENFORCED HERE AND IS NOT SILENTLY IMPLIED TO BE ... do not read this module's existence as evidence that both guards are live.\" Each verdict below is a judgement I own.\n\n=== VERDICTS (8) ===\nRATIFY (grade>=4, mechanism within existing read/verify surfaces, no dangerous-set member):\n- named-result-views-schema-stable-recovery-capsules-with-proj-2026-08-14 (4) — server-owned named projections on the existing result-door/shape registry + receipts. Read-shaping only.\n- evidence-complete-work-item-completion-preflight-2026-08-14 (4) — typed preflight on plan-bound completions, extends the existing completion-integrity writer, explicitly \"no parallel ledger\".\n\nNEEDS-HUMAN (fail-closed):\n- typed-external-prerequisite-attestations-for-release-gates-2026-08-15 (5 — my HIGHEST grade, and still not mine to ratify). Subject matter is production Stripe variables and Apple signing identities: the auth/security member of the dangerous set. High merit is not a safety argument.\n- gate-resilience-vs-torn-git-sync-sweeps-retry-failing-files-2026-08-14 (4, graded_by=owner). UNDETERMINABLE: I read the full 1350-char body — its entire \"## Background\" is one line, \"_Routed from wi:EI-7845 ... The wi stays open for triage._\". No mechanism text exists, so risk class cannot be determined. Separately its TITLE proposes changing when the green-checkpoint gate verdicts red — the one mechanism protecting main. Both roads lead to needs-human.\n\nREVISE, stay draft (graded 3 = my revision signal; merit, not safety):\n- active-checkpoint-truth-capsule-on-release-trace-2026-08-14 (3) + progress-certified-release-trace-for-active-checkpoint-candi-2026-08-14 (3) — overlapping mechanisms; merge them.\n- executable-acceptance-closure-contract-for-exact-sha-release-2026-08-14 (3) — re-aim at exact-SHA binding only; as written it conducts canaries.\n- adversarial-campaign-compiler-plan-classes-to-exact-bounded-2026-08-14 (3).\n\n=== THE OPERATIVE FINDING: RATIFYING THESE IS CURRENTLY NEAR-INERT ===\nVerified against the writers, not assumed. D-004 says a ready flip \"auto-promotes its items into the claimable pool via ready-plan-autostart\". Today it does not reach the pool that way:\n1. plans/items.ts:269 — `if (args.actionable && triad.gated) continue;` — a plan IN SCOPE for the spec triad and missing a leg has its items HELD BACK from `actionable` (item status deliberately untouched).\n2. spec-triad-policy.ts:64 — SPEC_TRIAD_EPOCH_DEFAULT = 2026-08-09. All 8 drafts were created 08-13..08-15, so all are IN SCOPE, and none carries Requirements/Design/Acceptance.\n3. Confirmed empirically on the ONE already-ratified scout plan: counterfactual-critique-lab (ready) has P-003/P-004 `todo`, yet plans:items{actionable:true,slug} returns []. Its own ## Now records the field consequence: \"Scheduler pulled unrelated WI-6359 despite fleet scope; ... P-001 was claimed via plans:set-status\" — claimed by hand.\nCONSEQUENCE: ratification remains the correct approval act and is worth recording, but it does NOT deliver work. The bottleneck on \"keep the Blender output loop useful\" is NOT arbitration throughput — it is that every ratified scout plan is a bare 1-item stub with no triad. Each item reads \"first concrete slice of the proposal's mechanism (Mug: refine/split during review)\", and the Mug meant to do that refining is RETIRED. NOT IRREVERSIBLE — no promoted item in the dangerous set (migration · outward-facing publish/send · fleet-autonomy escalation · auth/security · kill-switch).\n  2. NOT SELF-ORIGINATED — the steward did not file the idea the draft came from.\n\nThere is NO SIZE LIMIT [owner:Avi 2026-08-11, interactive]: a draft of ANY item count may be ratified when both conditions hold. (An earlier ≤3-item cap was my own bounded AUTO default; the owner removed it — see blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11, the decision superseding D-008.)\n\nOtherwise: do not ratify, mark needs-human, escalate to the owner with the grade and rationale.\n\nFAIL-CLOSED, and this matters more now than it did: if the risk class or the origin cannot be determined, the draft does NOT qualify for autonomous ratification. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n**Purpose:** fallback recovery heartbeat for the Blender steward goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`. This schedule does NOT pace stewardship; the live steward self-paces its own loop. Current initial owner: `su-d3dd7eae-280b-47b7-b629-00c15072053f` (headless, default system account, GOAL plus GRADE health overlay).\n\n**Per-run outcome:** leave exactly one fresh, wakeable su holding GOAL subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, with GRADE stacked only for the Blender health scorecard and with a working self-wake. If the incumbent is healthy, record that evidence and do not spawn. If absent/dead, launch one replacement headless su on the default system account/default model/warm carry, then `mode:set` GOAL with the existing goal id and GRADE with the scorecard-only scope below. Never create a duplicate goal and never change Scout account routing.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Background\n\nOperational child of `blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11` D-001/D-003. The retired Mug/Queen/Cup tier no longer supervises Blender output. The replacement is one su GOAL-mode portfolio steward; GRADE is only an overlay for evidence-complete rubric scorecards. Scheduled-plan fires mint a run work-item, so this plan states the real ensure-one operation rather than claiming the schedule directly launches an agent.\n\n## Phase 1 — recurring ensure-one run\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Read the goal, mode registry, live presence, and incumbent loop. If exactly one healthy GOAL holder exists, checkpoint the owner id + liveness evidence and finish without spawning. If none exists, launch ONE headless su (default account/model, warm carry), enter `goal` with subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, then enter `grade` with standing instructions: grade only the Blender health scorecard; the GOAL contract owns post-epoch idea grading, draft disposition, ready-plan decomposition, budget/kill enforcement, and self-paced wake cadence. If multiple fresh holders exist, retain the oldest healthy holder, stop/clear the newer duplicate holders safely, and record the disposition. Verify the surviving owner has a wake source before completing. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Six-hour schedule is recovery only\nThe recurrence is a six-hour liveness backstop with skip-old/skip-overlap semantics. The steward chooses its operational cadence from eligible backlog and trend; no scheduled fire may reset or slow that self-paced loop.\n\n### D-002 — Existing goal is authoritative\nRecovery reuses goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b` ($25 ceiling and its recorded kill criterion). It must not call `goals:start`, which would mint a duplicate goal; it launches a session and attaches the existing GOAL subject instead.\n\n### D-003 — GRADE scope is narrow\nGRADE monitors the existing Blender rubric/scorecard. Draft arbitration, idea dispositions, ready decomposition, and ratification are GOAL acts, not rubric grades.\n\n### D-004 — Steward contract: ratification authority is bounded (small + reversible + not self-originated)\nDate: 2026-08-11\nTHE CONTRACT LINE for the ratification duty D-003 assigns to GOAL mode. The steward may flip a scout draft to `ready` — which auto-promotes its items into the claimable pool via `ready-plan-autostart` — subject to TWO conditions:\n\n  1. NOT IRREVERSIBLE — no promoted item in the dangerous set (migration · outward-facing publish/send · fleet-autonomy escalation · auth/security · kill-switch).\n  2. NOT SELF-ORIGINATED — the steward did not file the idea the draft came from.\n\nThere is NO SIZE LIMIT [owner:Avi 2026-08-11, interactive]: a draft of ANY item count may be ratified when both conditions hold. (An earlier ≤3-item cap was my own bounded AUTO default; the owner removed it — see blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11, the decision superseding D-008.)\n\nOtherwise: do not ratify, mark needs-human, escalate to the owner with the grade and rationale.\n\nFAIL-CLOSED, and this matters more now than it did: if the risk class or the origin cannot be determined, the draft does NOT qualify for autonomous ratification. With no size cap, these two conditions are the ENTIRE safety margin, so an undeterminable input must never be resolved optimistically.\n\n### D-005 — This heartbeat cannot recover a dead steward on its own — an unexecuted run wedges the schedule permanently (fixed 2026-08-16)\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Recorded by su-1cd24b43 while resuming the Blender GOAL steward at owner Avi's direction.\n\nD-001 calls this schedule a \"six-hour liveness backstop\". Between 2026-08-15T06:01Z and 2026-08-16T02:5xZ it was not a backstop at all: it had stopped minting runs entirely, and the Blender loop stayed dark ~21h with the producer still running (last human_grade anywhere was 2026-08-13; actionable post-epoch backlog stood at 83 when the loop was restarted).\n\nMECHANISM (verified against the writers, not inferred):\n- `runScheduledPlanFire` with `concurrency:'skip'` refuses to mint while ANY run of this template is `plan_runs.status='running'`.\n- Run 958 (minted 2026-08-15T06:01) stayed `running` because its item PR-958-P-001 was never claimed — there was no live steward to claim it, which is precisely the condition this heartbeat exists to detect.\n- `reconcileScheduledPlanRuns` structurally cannot settle it: it settles only when all work_items are TERMINAL.\n- `sweepPlanRuns` WOULD have reclaimed it after 30 min, but its only caller was the `plans:runs` read. Nobody was around to read it either.\n- Net: `routines.last_fired_at` advanced to 2026-08-16T00:02:07Z having minted nothing at 12:00, 18:00 and 00:02. No error, no failed run, no alert.\n\nTHE RULING — three things follow for anyone relying on this plan:\n\n1. **This heartbeat has a circular dependency and must not be treated as sufficient recovery on its own.** Its runs are executed by claiming a work-item, and in the failure it is meant to catch there is no agent alive to claim one. A recovery mechanism whose execution requires the thing it recovers is not a backstop. Until a steward-independent executor exists, an EXTERNAL supervisor (an su with an armed loop, or the owner) is the real recovery path; the heartbeat is a convenience on top of that. Do not read \"schedule armed + routine active\" as \"the steward is being watched\".\n\n2. **The generic wedge is fixed; the circularity in (1) is NOT.** `sweepOrphanedPlanRuns` now runs on the 30s tick from `reconcileAndGovern` (reconcile first so real outcomes are preserved, then reclaim the orphan residue), with 4 recurrence-guard tests in reconcile-plan-runs.integration.test.ts driving only the tick path. So an orphaned run can no longer permanently disable ANY schedule. Filed as EI-20577333581927016. That fix means the heartbeat will now keep firing — it does NOT mean a fired run gets executed when no steward is alive.\n\n3. **NEVER size this backlog with a hand-written query — use `classifyUngraded()`** (packages/operator-core/lib/scout/ungraded-scope.ts). CORRECTION, recorded against my own error in this same session: the resume brief I wrote cited \"143 post-epoch ungraded, routed since 2026-08-11\". That was wrong three ways, and steward su-e9d9bc18 refused it rather than acting on it. (a) The epoch is not a calendar day — floors are PER-ORIGIN under blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11#D-014: scout = 2026-08-12T00:00:00Z, su-ideate = 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z. (b) It applied no terminal/outcome filter, counting rows whose artifacts had already resolved won/lost. (c) It therefore swept in 15 scout rows routed 2026-08-11 00:18-03:34 that are PRE-EPOCH. Because grading is FORWARD-ONLY (D-002) and `blender:grade-idea` HAS NO RETRACT (EI-20347901071497589), draining that list would have burned 15 unretractable grades and repeated a defect already on file. The authoritative four buckets are graded | pre-epoch | terminal | actionable, and ONLY `actionable` is drainable. True baseline at resume: actionable 83 (scout 71 + su-ideate 12), pre-epoch 1058, terminal 45, all_ungraded 1186.\n\nALSO NOTE: this class of failure is silent by construction — `last_fired_at` advances whether or not a fire produced a run, so \"fired N times, minted nothing\" has no signal. Flagged in EI-20577333581927016 as a monitoring gap, deliberately not fixed here.\n\n### D-006 — D-004 arbitration, 2026-08-16: 8 live drafts ruled (2 ratified, 2 needs-human, 4 revise) — and ratification is currently INERT without a spec triad\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Recorded by su-e9d9bc18 (Blender steward, GOAL+GRADE) applying D-004 to the scout-routed draft queue.\n\n=== SCOPE CORRECTION (measured, not inherited) ===\nThe queue is NOT \"20 draft plans\". Joining scout_routed_ideas (rail='plan', routed_ref='plan:<slug>') to harness_plans gives 15 draft rows, split across TWO workspace_ids:\n- papercusp-workspace: 8 drafts — THE REAL QUEUE. Independently corroborated by the scout-draft-review backstop alarm (\"8 scout-routed drafts unreviewed >1h\").\n- default: 7 drafts — NOT arbitrable (separate finding, filed).\nThe other ~12 non-scout drafts (context-trimming-tiers, agent-managed-compaction, ...) are hand-authored and were never in D-004 scope.\n\n=== D-004 CONDITION 2 (not self-originated): CLEAR for all 15, verified in-ledger ===\nEvery row is origin='su-ideate' with created_by in {su-d4b9a5af, su-2c130be1, su-0b4a6333, su-bbf8a1fe, su-c474b9db}. None is su-e9d9bc18. This population has MOVED past the assumption in ratification-gate.ts's header (\"measured 2026-08-12: all 6 rail='plan' rows are origin='scout' with created_by NULL — no current row can trigger this refusal\"). created_by is now populated on every row, so the mechanical guard is live-relevant exactly as that header predicted.\n\n=== D-004 CONDITION 1 (dangerous set): MINE ALONE TO JUDGE ===\nratification-gate.ts enforces ONLY condition 2 and says so: \"(1) IS NOT ENFORCED HERE AND IS NOT SILENTLY IMPLIED TO BE ... do not read this module's existence as evidence that both guards are live.\" Each verdict below is a judgement I own.\n\n=== VERDICTS (8) ===\nRATIFY (grade>=4, mechanism within existing read/verify surfaces, no dangerous-set member):\n- named-result-views-schema-stable-recovery-capsules-with-proj-2026-08-14 (4) — server-owned named projections on the existing result-door/shape registry + receipts. Read-shaping only.\n- evidence-complete-work-item-completion-preflight-2026-08-14 (4) — typed preflight on plan-bound completions, extends the existing completion-integrity writer, explicitly \"no parallel ledger\".\n\nNEEDS-HUMAN (fail-closed):\n- typed-external-prerequisite-attestations-for-release-gates-2026-08-15 (5 — my HIGHEST grade, and still not mine to ratify). Subject matter is production Stripe variables and Apple signing identities: the auth/security member of the dangerous set. High merit is not a safety argument.\n- gate-resilience-vs-torn-git-sync-sweeps-retry-failing-files-2026-08-14 (4, graded_by=owner). UNDETERMINABLE: I read the full 1350-char body — its entire \"## Background\" is one line, \"_Routed from wi:EI-7845 ... The wi stays open for triage._\". No mechanism text exists, so risk class cannot be determined. Separately its TITLE proposes changing when the green-checkpoint gate verdicts red — the one mechanism protecting main. Both roads lead to needs-human.\n\nREVISE, stay draft (graded 3 = my revision signal; merit, not safety):\n- active-checkpoint-truth-capsule-on-release-trace-2026-08-14 (3) + progress-certified-release-trace-for-active-checkpoint-candi-2026-08-14 (3) — overlapping mechanisms; merge them.\n- executable-acceptance-closure-contract-for-exact-sha-release-2026-08-14 (3) — re-aim at exact-SHA binding only; as written it conducts canaries.\n- adversarial-campaign-compiler-plan-classes-to-exact-bounded-2026-08-14 (3).\n\n=== THE OPERATIVE FINDING: RATIFYING THESE IS CURRENTLY NEAR-INERT ===\nVerified against the writers, not assumed. D-004 says a ready flip \"auto-promotes its items into the claimable pool via ready-plan-autostart\". Today it does not reach the pool that way:\n1. plans/items.ts:269 — `if (args.actionable && triad.gated) continue;` — a plan IN SCOPE for the spec triad and missing a leg has its items HELD BACK from `actionable` (item status deliberately untouched).\n2. spec-triad-policy.ts:64 — SPEC_TRIAD_EPOCH_DEFAULT = 2026-08-09. All 8 drafts were created 08-13..08-15, so all are IN SCOPE, and none carries Requirements/Design/Acceptance.\n3. Confirmed empirically on the ONE already-ratified scout plan: counterfactual-critique-lab (ready) has P-003/P-004 `todo`, yet plans:items{actionable:true,slug} returns []. Its own ## Now records the field consequence: \"Scheduler pulled unrelated WI-6359 despite fleet scope; ... P-001 was claimed via plans:set-status\" — claimed by hand.\nCONSEQUENCE: ratification remains the correct approval act and is worth recording, but it does NOT deliver work. The bottleneck on \"keep the Blender output loop useful\" is NOT arbitration throughput — it is that every ratified scout plan is a bare 1-item stub with no triad. Each item reads \"first concrete slice of the proposal's mechanism (Mug: refine/split during review)\", and the Mug meant to do that refining is RETIRED. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n**Purpose:** fallback recovery heartbeat for the Blender steward goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`. This schedule does NOT pace stewardship; the live steward self-paces its own loop. Current initial owner: `su-d3dd7eae-280b-47b7-b629-00c15072053f` (headless, default system account, GOAL plus GRADE health overlay).\n\n**Per-run outcome:** leave exactly one fresh, wakeable su holding GOAL subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, with GRADE stacked only for the Blender health scorecard and with a working self-wake. If the incumbent is healthy, record that evidence and do not spawn. If absent/dead, launch one replacement headless su on the default system account/default model/warm carry, then `mode:set` GOAL with the existing goal id and GRADE with the scorecard-only scope below. Never create a duplicate goal and never change Scout account routing.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Background\n\nOperational child of `blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11` D-001/D-003. The retired Mug/Queen/Cup tier no longer supervises Blender output. The replacement is one su GOAL-mode portfolio steward; GRADE is only an overlay for evidence-complete rubric scorecards. Scheduled-plan fires mint a run work-item, so this plan states the real ensure-one operation rather than claiming the schedule directly launches an agent.\n\n## Phase 1 — recurring ensure-one run\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Read the goal, mode registry, live presence, and incumbent loop. If exactly one healthy GOAL holder exists, checkpoint the owner id + liveness evidence and finish without spawning. If none exists, launch ONE headless su (default account/model, warm carry), enter `goal` with subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, then enter `grade` with standing instructions: grade only the Blender health scorecard; the GOAL contract owns post-epoch idea grading, draft disposition, ready-plan decomposition, budget/kill enforcement, and self-paced wake cadence. If multiple fresh holders exist, retain the oldest healthy holder, stop/clear the newer duplicate holders safely, and record the disposition. Verify the surviving owner has a wake source before completing. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Six-hour schedule is recovery only\nThe recurrence is a six-hour liveness backstop with skip-old/skip-overlap semantics. The steward chooses its operational cadence from eligible backlog and trend; no scheduled fire may reset or slow that self-paced loop.\n\n### D-002 — Existing goal is authoritative\nRecovery reuses goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b` ($25 ceiling and its recorded kill criterion). It must not call `goals:start`, which would mint a duplicate goal; it launches a session and attaches the existing GOAL subject instead.\n\n### D-003 — GRADE scope is narrow\nGRADE monitors the existing Blender rubric/scorecard. Draft arbitration, idea dispositions, ready decomposition, and ratification are GOAL acts, not rubric grades.\n\n### D-004 — Steward contract: ratification authority is bounded (small + reversible + not self-originated)\nDate: 2026-08-11\nTHE CONTRACT LINE for the ratification duty D-003 assigns to GOAL mode. The steward may flip a scout draft to `ready` — which auto-promotes its items into the claimable pool via `ready-plan-autostart` — subject to TWO conditions:\n\n  1. NOT IRREVERSIBLE — no promoted item in the dangerous set (migration · outward-facing publish/send · fleet-autonomy escalation · auth/security · kill-switch).\n  2. NOT SELF-ORIGINATED — the steward did not file the idea the draft came from.\n\nThere is NO SIZE LIMIT [owner:Avi 2026-08-11, interactive]: a draft of ANY item count may be ratified when both conditions hold. (An earlier ≤3-item cap was my own bounded AUTO default; the owner removed it — see blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11, the decision superseding D-008.)\n\nOtherwise: do not ratify, mark needs-human, escalate to the owner with the grade and rationale.\n\nFAIL-CLOSED, and this matters more now than it did: if the risk class or the origin cannot be determined, the draft does NOT qualify for autonomous ratification. With no size cap, these two conditions are the ENTIRE safety margin, so an undeterminable input must never be resolved optimistically.\n\n### D-005 — This heartbeat cannot recover a dead steward on its own — an unexecuted run wedges the schedule permanently (fixed 2026-08-16)\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Recorded by su-1cd24b43 while resuming the Blender GOAL steward at owner Avi's direction.\n\nD-001 calls this schedule a \"six-hour liveness backstop\". Between 2026-08-15T06:01Z and 2026-08-16T02:5xZ it was not a backstop at all: it had stopped minting runs entirely, and the Blender loop stayed dark ~21h with the producer still running (last human_grade anywhere was 2026-08-13; actionable post-epoch backlog stood at 83 when the loop was restarted).\n\nMECHANISM (verified against the writers, not inferred):\n- `runScheduledPlanFire` with `concurrency:'skip'` refuses to mint while ANY run of this template is `plan_runs.status='running'`.\n- Run 958 (minted 2026-08-15T06:01) stayed `running` because its item PR-958-P-001 was never claimed — there was no live steward to claim it, which is precisely the condition this heartbeat exists to detect.\n- `reconcileScheduledPlanRuns` structurally cannot settle it: it settles only when all work_items are TERMINAL.\n- `sweepPlanRuns` WOULD have reclaimed it after 30 min, but its only caller was the `plans:runs` read. Nobody was around to read it either.\n- Net: `routines.last_fired_at` advanced to 2026-08-16T00:02:07Z having minted nothing at 12:00, 18:00 and 00:02. No error, no failed run, no alert.\n\nTHE RULING — three things follow for anyone relying on this plan:\n\n1. **This heartbeat has a circular dependency and must not be treated as sufficient recovery on its own.** Its runs are executed by claiming a work-item, and in the failure it is meant to catch there is no agent alive to claim one. A recovery mechanism whose execution requires the thing it recovers is not a backstop. Until a steward-independent executor exists, an EXTERNAL supervisor (an su with an armed loop, or the owner) is the real recovery path; the heartbeat is a convenience on top of that. Do not read \"schedule armed + routine active\" as \"the steward is being watched\".\n\n2. **The generic wedge is fixed; the circularity in (1) is NOT.** `sweepOrphanedPlanRuns` now runs on the 30s tick from `reconcileAndGovern` (reconcile first so real outcomes are preserved, then reclaim the orphan residue), with 4 recurrence-guard tests in reconcile-plan-runs.integration.test.ts driving only the tick path. So an orphaned run can no longer permanently disable ANY schedule. Filed as EI-20577333581927016. That fix means the heartbeat will now keep firing — it does NOT mean a fired run gets executed when no steward is alive.\n\n3. **NEVER size this backlog with a hand-written query — use `classifyUngraded()`** (packages/operator-core/lib/scout/ungraded-scope.ts). CORRECTION, recorded against my own error in this same session: the resume brief I wrote cited \"143 post-epoch ungraded, routed since 2026-08-11\". That was wrong three ways, and steward su-e9d9bc18 refused it rather than acting on it. (a) The epoch is not a calendar day — floors are PER-ORIGIN under blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11#D-014: scout = 2026-08-12T00:00:00Z, su-ideate = 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z. (b) It applied no terminal/outcome filter, counting rows whose artifacts had already resolved won/lost. (c) It therefore swept in 15 scout rows routed 2026-08-11 00:18-03:34 that are PRE-EPOCH. Because grading is FORWARD-ONLY (D-002) and `blender:grade-idea` HAS NO RETRACT (EI-20347901071497589), draining that list would have burned 15 unretractable grades and repeated a defect already on file. The authoritative four buckets are graded | pre-epoch | terminal | actionable, and ONLY `actionable` is drainable. True baseline at resume: actionable 83 (scout 71 + su-ideate 12), pre-epoch 1058, terminal 45, all_ungraded 1186.\n\nALSO NOTE: this class of failure is silent by construction — `last_fired_at` advances whether or not a fire produced a run, so \"fired N times, minted nothing\" has no signal. Flagged in EI-20577333581927016 as a monitoring gap, deliberately not fixed here.\n\n### D-006 — D-004 arbitration, 2026-08-16: 8 live drafts ruled (2 ratified, 2 needs-human, 4 revise) — and ratification is currently INERT without a spec triad\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n**Purpose:** fallback recovery heartbeat for the Blender steward goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`. This schedule does NOT pace stewardship; the live steward self-paces its own loop. Current initial owner: `su-d3dd7eae-280b-47b7-b629-00c15072053f` (headless, default system account, GOAL plus GRADE health overlay).\n\n**Per-run outcome:** leave exactly one fresh, wakeable su holding GOAL subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, with GRADE stacked only for the Blender health scorecard and with a working self-wake. If the incumbent is healthy, record that evidence and do not spawn. If absent/dead, launch one replacement headless su on the default system account/default model/warm carry, then `mode:set` GOAL with the existing goal id and GRADE with the scorecard-only scope below. Never create a duplicate goal and never change Scout account routing.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Background\n\nOperational child of `blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11` D-001/D-003. The retired Mug/Queen/Cup tier no longer supervises Blender output. The replacement is one su GOAL-mode portfolio steward; GRADE is only an overlay for evidence-complete rubric scorecards. Scheduled-plan fires mint a run work-item, so this plan states the real ensure-one operation rather than claiming the schedule directly launches an agent.\n\n## Phase 1 — recurring ensure-one run\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Read the goal, mode registry, live presence, and incumbent loop. If exactly one healthy GOAL holder exists, checkpoint the owner id + liveness evidence and finish without spawning. If none exists, launch ONE headless su (default account/model, warm carry), enter `goal` with subject `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b`, then enter `grade` with standing instructions: grade only the Blender health scorecard; the GOAL contract owns post-epoch idea grading, draft disposition, ready-plan decomposition, budget/kill enforcement, and self-paced wake cadence. If multiple fresh holders exist, retain the oldest healthy holder, stop/clear the newer duplicate holders safely, and record the disposition. Verify the surviving owner has a wake source before completing. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Six-hour schedule is recovery only\nThe recurrence is a six-hour liveness backstop with skip-old/skip-overlap semantics. The steward chooses its operational cadence from eligible backlog and trend; no scheduled fire may reset or slow that self-paced loop.\n\n### D-002 — Existing goal is authoritative\nRecovery reuses goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b` ($25 ceiling and its recorded kill criterion). It must not call `goals:start`, which would mint a duplicate goal; it launches a session and attaches the existing GOAL subject instead.\n\n### D-003 — GRADE scope is narrow\nGRADE monitors the existing Blender rubric/scorecard. Draft arbitration, idea dispositions, ready decomposition, and ratification are GOAL acts, not rubric grades.\n\n### D-004 — Steward contract: ratification authority is bounded (small + reversible + not self-originated)\nDate: 2026-08-11\nTHE CONTRACT LINE for the ratification duty D-003 assigns to GOAL mode. The steward may flip a scout draft to `ready` — which auto-promotes its items into the claimable pool via `ready-plan-autostart` — subject to TWO conditions:\n\n  1. NOT IRREVERSIBLE — no promoted item in the dangerous set (migration · outward-facing publish/send · fleet-autonomy escalation · auth/security · kill-switch).\n  2. NOT SELF-ORIGINATED — the steward did not file the idea the draft came from.\n\nThere is NO SIZE LIMIT [owner:Avi 2026-08-11, interactive]: a draft of ANY item count may be ratified when both conditions hold. (An earlier ≤3-item cap was my own bounded AUTO default; the owner removed it — see blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11, the decision superseding D-008.)\n\nOtherwise: do not ratify, mark needs-human, escalate to the owner with the grade and rationale.\n\nFAIL-CLOSED, and this matters more now than it did: if the risk class or the origin cannot be determined, the draft does NOT qualify for autonomous ratification. With no size cap, these two conditions are the ENTIRE safety margin, so an undeterminable input must never be resolved optimistically.\n\n### D-005 — This heartbeat cannot recover a dead steward on its own — an unexecuted run wedges the schedule permanently (fixed 2026-08-16)\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Recorded by su-1cd24b43 while resuming the Blender GOAL steward at owner Avi's direction.\n\nD-001 calls this schedule a \"six-hour liveness backstop\". Between 2026-08-15T06:01Z and 2026-08-16T02:5xZ it was not a backstop at all: it had stopped minting runs entirely, and the Blender loop stayed dark ~21h with the producer still running (last human_grade anywhere was 2026-08-13; actionable post-epoch backlog stood at 83 when the loop was restarted).\n\nMECHANISM (verified against the writers, not inferred):\n- `runScheduledPlanFire` with `concurrency:'skip'` refuses to mint while ANY run of this template is `plan_runs.status='running'`.\n- Run 958 (minted 2026-08-15T06:01) stayed `running` because its item PR-958-P-001 was never claimed — there was no live steward to claim it, which is precisely the condition this heartbeat exists to detect.\n- `reconcileScheduledPlanRuns` structurally cannot settle it: it settles only when all work_items are TERMINAL.\n- `sweepPlanRuns` WOULD have reclaimed it after 30 min, but its only caller was the `plans:runs` read. Nobody was around to read it either.\n- Net: `routines.last_fired_at` advanced to 2026-08-16T00:02:07Z having minted nothing at 12:00, 18:00 and 00:02. No error, no failed run, no alert.\n\nTHE RULING — three things follow for anyone relying on this plan:\n\n1. **This heartbeat has a circular dependency and must not be treated as sufficient recovery on its own.** Its runs are executed by claiming a work-item, and in the failure it is meant to catch there is no agent alive to claim one. A recovery mechanism whose execution requires the thing it recovers is not a backstop. Until a steward-independent executor exists, an EXTERNAL supervisor (an su with an armed loop, or the owner) is the real recovery path; the heartbeat is a convenience on top of that. Do not read \"schedule armed + routine active\" as \"the steward is being watched\".\n\n2. **The generic wedge is fixed; the circularity in (1) is NOT.** `sweepOrphanedPlanRuns` now runs on the 30s tick from `reconcileAndGovern` (reconcile first so real outcomes are preserved, then reclaim the orphan residue), with 4 recurrence-guard tests in reconcile-plan-runs.integration.test.ts driving only the tick path. So an orphaned run can no longer permanently disable ANY schedule. Filed as EI-20577333581927016. That fix means the heartbeat will now keep firing — it does NOT mean a fired run gets executed when no steward is alive.\n\n3. **NEVER size this backlog with a hand-written query — use `classifyUngraded()`** (packages/operator-core/lib/scout/ungraded-scope.ts). CORRECTION, recorded against my own error in this same session: the resume brief I wrote cited \"143 post-epoch ungraded, routed since 2026-08-11\". That was wrong three ways, and steward su-e9d9bc18 refused it rather than acting on it. (a) The epoch is not a calendar day — floors are PER-ORIGIN under blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11#D-014: scout = 2026-08-12T00:00:00Z, su-ideate = 2026-07-11T00:00:00Z. (b) It applied no terminal/outcome filter, counting rows whose artifacts had already resolved won/lost. (c) It therefore swept in 15 scout rows routed 2026-08-11 00:18-03:34 that are PRE-EPOCH. Because grading is FORWARD-ONLY (D-002) and `blender:grade-idea` HAS NO RETRACT (EI-20347901071497589), draining that list would have burned 15 unretractable grades and repeated a defect already on file. The authoritative four buckets are graded | pre-epoch | terminal | actionable, and ONLY `actionable` is drainable. True baseline at resume: actionable 83 (scout 71 + su-ideate 12), pre-epoch 1058, terminal 45, all_ungraded 1186.\n\nALSO NOTE: this class of failure is silent by construction — `last_fired_at` advances whether or not a fire produced a run, so \"fired N times, minted nothing\" has no signal. If absent/dead, launch one replacement headless su on the default system account/default model/warm carry, then `mode:set` GOAL with the existing goal id and GRADE with the scorecard-only scope below. Never create a duplicate goal and never change Scout account routing.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Background\n\nOperational child of `blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11` D-001/D-003. The retired Mug/Queen/Cup tier no longer supervises Blender output. The replacement is one su GOAL-mode portfolio steward; GRADE is only an overlay for evidence-complete rubric scorecards. Scheduled-plan fires mint a run work-item, so this plan states the real ensure-one operation rather than claiming the schedule directly launches an agent.\n\n## Phase 1 — recurring ensure-one run\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Read the goal, mode registry, live presence, and incumbent loop. If exactly one healthy GOAL holder exists, checkpoint the owner id + liveness evidence and finish without spawning. If multiple fresh holders exist, retain the oldest healthy holder, stop/clear the newer duplicate holders safely, and record the disposition. Verify the surviving owner has a wake source before completing. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Six-hour schedule is recovery only\nThe recurrence is a six-hour liveness backstop with skip-old/skip-overlap semantics. The steward chooses its operational cadence from eligible backlog and trend; no scheduled fire may reset or slow that self-paced loop.\n\n### D-002 — Existing goal is authoritative\nRecovery reuses goal `keep-the-blender-output-loop-useful-bounded-and--f5482b` ($25 ceiling and its recorded kill criterion). It must not call `goals:start`, which would mint a duplicate goal; it launches a session and attaches the existing GOAL subject instead.\n\n### D-003 — GRADE scope is narrow\nGRADE monitors the existing Blender rubric/scorecard. Draft arbitration, idea dispositions, ready decomposition, and ratification are GOAL acts, not rubric grades.\n\n### D-004 — Steward contract: ratification authority is bounded (small + reversible + not self-originated)\nDate: 2026-08-11\nTHE CONTRACT LINE for the ratification duty D-003 assigns to GOAL mode. The steward may flip a scout draft to `ready` — which auto-promotes its items into the claimable pool via `ready-plan-autostart` — subject to TWO conditions:\n\n  1. NOT IRREVERSIBLE — no promoted item in the dangerous set (migration · outward-facing publish/send · fleet-autonomy escalation · auth/security · kill-switch).\n  2. NOT SELF-ORIGINATED — the steward did not file the idea the draft came from.\n\nThere is NO SIZE LIMIT [owner:Avi 2026-08-11, interactive]: a draft of ANY item count may be ratified when both conditions hold. (An earlier ≤3-item cap was my own bounded AUTO default; the owner removed it — see blender-su-grade-integration-2026-08-11, the decision superseding D-008.)\n\nOtherwise: do not ratify, mark needs-human, escalate to the owner with the grade and rationale.\n\nFAIL-CLOSED, and this matters more now than it did: if the risk class or the origin cannot be determined, the draft does NOT qualify for autonomous ratification. With no size cap, these two conditions are the ENTIRE safety margin, so an undeterminable input must never be resolved optimistically.\n\n### D-005 — This heartbeat cannot recover a dead steward on its own — an unexecuted run wedges the schedule permanently (fixed 2026-08-16)\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16. Recorded by su-1cd24b43 while resuming the Blender GOAL steward at owner Avi's direction.\n\nD-001 calls this schedule a \"six-hour liveness backstop\". Between 2026-08-15T06:01Z and 2026-08-16T02:5xZ it was not a backstop at all: it had stopped minting runs entirely, and the Blender loop stayed dark ~21h with the producer still running (last human_grade anywhere was 2026-08-13; actionable post-epoch backlog stood at 83 when the loop was restarted).\n\nMECHANISM (verified against the writers, not inferred):\n- `runScheduledPlanFire` with `concurrency:'skip'` refuses to mint while ANY run of this template is `plan_runs.status='running'`.\n- Run 958 (minted 2026-08-15T06:01) stayed `running` because its item PR-958-P-001 was never claimed — there was no live steward to claim it, which is precisely the condition this heartbeat exists to detect.\n- `reconcileScheduledPlanRuns` structurally cannot settle it: it settles only when all work_items are TERMINAL.\n- `sweepPlanRuns` WOULD have reclaimed it after 30 min, but its only caller was the `plans:runs` read. Nobody was around to read it either.\n- Net: `routines.last_fired_at` advanced to 2026-08-16T00:02:07Z having minted nothing at 12:00, 18:00 and 00:02. No error, no failed run, no alert.\n\nTHE RULING — three things follow for anyone relying on this plan:\n\n1. **This heartbeat has a circular dependency and must not be treated as sufficient recovery on its own.** Its runs are executed by claiming a work-item, and in the failure it is meant to catch there is no agent alive to claim one. A recovery mechanism whose execution requires the thing it recovers is not a backstop. Until a steward-independent executor exists, an EXTERNAL supervisor (an su with an armed loop, or the owner) is the real recovery path; the heartbeat is a convenience on top of that. Do not read \"schedule armed + routine active\" as \"the steward is being watched\".\n\n2. **The generic wedge is fixed; the circularity in (1) is NOT.** `sweepOrphanedPlanRuns` now runs on the 30s tick from `reconcileAndGovern` (reconcile first so real outcomes are preserved, then reclaim the orphan residue), with 4 recurrence-guard tests in reconcile-plan-runs.integration.test.ts driving only the tick path. So an orphaned run can no longer permanently disable ANY schedule. Filed as EI-20577333581927016. That fix means the heartbeat will now keep firing — it does NOT mean a fired run gets executed when no steward is alive.\n\n3. **NEVER size this backlog with a hand-written query — use `classifyUngraded()`** (packages/operator-core/lib/scout/ungraded-scope.ts). Do not read \"schedule armed + routine active\" as \"the steward is being watched\".\n\n2. **The generic wedge is fixed; the circularity in (1) is NOT.** `sweepOrphanedPlanRuns` now runs on the 30s tick from `reconcileAndGovern` (reconcile first so real outcomes are preserved, then reclaim the orphan residue), with 4 recurrence-guard tests in reconcile-plan-runs.integration.test.ts driving only the tick path. So an orphaned run can no longer permanently disable ANY schedule. Filed as EI-20577333581927016. That fix means the heartbeat will now keep firing — it does NOT mean a fired run gets executed when no steward is alive.\n\n3. **NEVER size this backlog with a hand-written query — use `classifyUngraded()`** (packages/operator-core/lib/scout/ungraded-scope.ts). The authoritative four buckets are graded | pre-epoch | terminal | actionable, and ONLY `actionable` is drainable. True baseline at resume: actionable 83 (scout 71 + su-ideate 12), pre-epoch 1058, terminal 45, all_ungraded 1186.\n\nALSO NOTE: this class of failure is silent by construction — `last_fired_at` advances whether or not a fire produced a run, so \"fired N times, minted nothing\" has no signal.
