P-003 assembles both. Do not serialise them.\n\n## Background\nGoal: `a-working-browsable-visual-reference-to-the-88-m-704fcf` — \"A working, browsable visual reference to the 88 modern constellations — running and viewable, not a design document.\"\n\nBinding constraints from the principal:\n- **Hard ceiling 500 cents (US$5) for the WHOLE goal**, including every agent turn. Not a target — a ceiling actuals are reported against.\n- **Content accuracy outranks visual polish. Do not invent facts about the constellations.**\n- **NEW product — it must NOT live in the papercusp repo.** Deliverable directory: `/home/marsh-office/constellation-reference` (this plan record lives in the papercusp harness only because plans are stored per-harness; the product code does not).\n\nKill criterion (from the goal record): abandon if a running, viewable site cannot be reached within 500 cents, or if accurate per-constellation data cannot be sourced without inventing it.\n\n**Proven in-portfolio shape to copy — do not redesign it.** `/home/marsh-office/owl-field-guide` reached a running, verified site for 310 cents with exactly this shape: `data/*.json` (sourced, with per-record citations) → `build.mjs` (plain Node, no framework, zero deps) → `site/` static output → a `systemd --user` unit serving it on a fixed port. Read that directory before writing anything; copy its structure, its `check.mjs` idea, and its \"NOT STATED beats a guess\" discipline. 88 constellations is ~5x its record count, so lean harder on machine-readable sources and less on per-record prose.\n\n**THE ACCURACY RULE, binding on every item.** Every fact rendered on a page must trace to a fetched source file committed under `data/sources/`. LLM recall is NOT a source — not for areas, not for brightest stars, not for genitives, not for star coordinates. A field you cannot source is rendered as \"not stated\" and listed in the gaps report. A stated-but-unsourced figure is a DEFECT; an honest gap is CORRECT.\n\nCandidate sources (verify licence + fetch; substitute freely if a better one exists — record what you actually used):\n- The 88-name/abbreviation/genitive list and per-constellation area, quadrant, origin: the IAU constellations pages (iau.org) and/or the Wikipedia \"List of IAU-designated constellations\" table (CC BY-SA — attribute).\n- Star positions: the HYG database (astronexus/HYG-Database) or an equivalent open catalogue with magnitudes.\n- Constellation figure lines and/or IAU boundaries: `d3-celestial` data (BSD) or Stellarium's western sky-culture `constellationship.fab` (GPL — if GPL is a problem for redistribution, use the BSD/CC option and say so).\nLicences: keep an `ATTRIBUTION.md` and a site page naming every source and its licence.\n\n## Phase 1 — build\n\n- **P-001** `done` DATA: source all 88 IAU constellations into `data/constellations.json` — one record each with IAU name, 3-letter abbreviation, genitive, meaning/English name, area in square degrees, quadrant, visibility latitude range, brightest star (+ its magnitude), family/group, and origin (Ptolemy's 48 vs modern). Every record carries the source URL(s) it came from; raw fetched source files land in `data/sources/`. Missing field ⇒ literal \"not stated\", never a guess. Deliver a gaps report listing every not-stated field. importance: high — note: ← WI-37940 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` GEOMETRY: source open star data + constellation figure lines/boundaries into `data/sky/`, and write the renderer that turns them into one inline SVG star chart per constellation (stars sized by magnitude, figure lines, a labelled brightest star). Charts are DERIVED FROM DATA — never hand-drawn or positioned from memory. If figure lines cannot be sourced under an acceptable licence within budget, degrade to a boundary-outline or star-scatter chart and document the degradation rather than inventing lines. importance: high — note: ← WI-37941 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` SITE: `build.mjs` (plain Node, no framework, minimal/zero deps) renders `site/` — an index page listing all 88 (filter/sort by family, hemisphere and area; each entry showing its chart thumbnail) plus one detail page per constellation with the chart, the sourced fields, and visible per-page source citations. Plus an attribution/sources page. Dark sky-appropriate styling, responsive, accessible contrast; polish is the LAST call on the budget, never the first. blocked-by: P-001 blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-37942 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` SERVE: serve `site/` on a fixed loopback port under a `systemd --user` unit (model it on `owl-field-guide.service`), restart-durable, with README start/stop/restart instructions and evidence of a stop/start/restart cycle. No orphan `python3 -m http.server` — an unsupervised serve does not count as running. Report the URL. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-37943 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` VERIFY (independent — NOT done by whoever built P-001/P-003): a committed `check.mjs` asserting all 88 pages exist, every index link resolves, no page renders an empty required field, and every stated fact carries a citation; PLUS a manual accuracy spot-check of at least 10 constellations against the cited sources, reported constellation-by-constellation. A \"not stated\" is a PASS; a stated-but-unsourced or contradicted figure is a FAIL to be filed and fixed. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-37944 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — D-001 Deviate from the app-template mandate: plain data→build→static-site, not papercusp-webapp\nDate: 2026-08-11\nRULING (binding on every lane; do not re-litigate mid-build).\n\nThe GOAL contract carries a TEMPLATES MANDATE — every new app materializes from a `scope:\"app\"` template root. `templates:list` shows exactly three such roots: papercusp-agentic-desktop-app, papercusp-desktop-app, papercusp-webapp. The lightest of them (papercusp-webapp) is a Next.js standalone host + embedded-Postgres data layer + operator-style SPA + a materialized harness and a seeded builder agent.\n\nDECISION: deviate, deliberately and on the record. Build as a plain `data/*.json` → `build.mjs` → static `site/` tree at /home/marsh-office/constellation-reference, served by a `systemd --user` unit.\n\nWHY (the mandate's own purpose points this way):\n1. The mandate exists so nobody hand-rolls a scaffold when a maintained one fits. Here NONE of the three fits: this product has no database, no auth, no live state, no agent plane, no packaging target. It is 89 static pages rendered from a sourced JSON file.\n2. The ceiling is 500 cents for the WHOLE goal, and the kill criterion is explicitly \"abandon if a running, viewable site cannot be reached within the ceiling\". Materializing a Next.js + embedded-PG harness and kicking off its builder would plausibly consume most of that ceiling before one constellation is sourced — i.e. choosing the template makes tripping the kill criterion likely. Accuracy of 88 records is where this budget must go.\n3. There is a measured in-portfolio precedent for the chosen shape: /home/marsh-office/owl-field-guide reached a running, independently-verified site for 310 cents with exactly this structure. This is reuse of a proven shape, not a hand-rolled novelty.\n\nNOT LICENSED BY THIS DECISION: skipping structure. The shape is copied from owl-field-guide (data + sources + build + check + ops/unit + README), not improvised per-lane.\n\nIf a genuinely lightweight static-site template root is added later, this decision is the thing to revisit.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-002 — D-002 The portfolio manager does not lead this fleet — a spawned leader was installed after a launch accident\nDate: 2026-08-11\nRECORD, so nobody reads the fleet row's history as intent.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED: the first `fleet:launch-on-plan { leader:'spawn' }` was REFUSED by the claim-collapse guard (the plan's items had not become work-items — plans:start promoted nothing because the dispatcher axis is retired, so `plan=<slug>` matched 0 claimable rows and zero members opened). The refusal had ALREADY created the fleet ROW. On the retry, `leader:'spawn'` was therefore ignored (\"fleet already exists, led by nobody\") and the caller — the GOAL-mode portfolio manager su-38b44e43 — was installed as leader instead.\n\nWHY THAT IS A DEFECT, not a detail: the GOAL contract is explicit that leading a plan fleet yourself is the same mistake as implementing it. A portfolio manager who becomes a fleet leader stops managing the portfolio and nobody else is doing it.\n\nTHE FIX APPLIED: five work-items (WI-37940..WI-37944) were filed directly for P-001..P-005 so the lane is genuinely fed (the launch now reports 'matches 5 of 2350 claimable rows — this lane IS fed'), and a dedicated leader agent was launched via capability:launch-agent with `fleet:take-leadership` as its FIRST act, which demotes su-38b44e43. su-38b44e43 remains coupled and monitoring as the goal's manager, and is NOT this fleet's leader.\n\nGENERALISABLE: a refused fleet launch can still leave the fleet row behind, so a retry silently loses `leader:'spawn'`. If you need a spawned leader after a refusal, either use a NEW fleet name or launch the leader separately and have it take leadership — do not assume the retry re-honours the flag.\n\n### D-003 — D-003 The standing drain fleet is deferred until the build lane reports, on budget grounds\nDate: 2026-08-11\nRULING, disclosed as a deliberate deviation from the GOAL contract's 'keep one standing drain fleet per goal' clause.\n\nThe clause exists so small work-items filed directly still get done. Right now this goal's ENTIRE queue is WI-37940..WI-37944, all five inside the build fleet's claim lane, and all five already claimable by live members. A second fleet (leader + member = 2 more billed sessions) would therefore be launched to drain an EMPTY lane.\n\nThe binding constraint here is not organisational tidiness, it is the 500-cent ceiling, and the goal's kill criterion is literally 'abandon if a running, viewable site cannot be reached within the ceiling'. Three sessions are already running against that ceiling. Spending two more on an empty queue measurably raises the chance of tripping the goal's own kill criterion — which is the outcome the drain fleet is supposed to help avoid, not cause.\n\nTHE TRIGGER TO ESTABLISH IT (not 'someday' — a named condition the manager re-checks every wake):\n(a) any work-item lands for this goal OUTSIDE the plan-fleet lane (e.g. a defect filed by P-005's independent verification), OR\n(b) the build fleet reports the site serving and residue/fix work remains,\nwhichever comes first — AND remaining budget supports it. Scope its lane by the goal itself: claim leaf { field:'goal', op:'=', value:'a-working-browsable-visual-reference-to-the-88-m-704fcf' } (the POSITIVE form; goal is unset on most rows so a negative leaf drops them all).\n\nCHEAPER ALTERNATIVE IF BUDGET IS TIGHT AT THAT POINT: widen the EXISTING fleet's claim spec to the goal rather than launching a second fleet.\n\n### D-004 — D-004 P-005 found and fixed a real accuracy defect: 528 stated-but-unsourced fields P-001's own gaps-report silently excluded\nDate: 2026-08-11\nDate: 2026-08-11\n\nP-005's check.mjs (section 2, \"every STATED field carries a citation\") failed on its first run: pronunciation, brightestStarMagnitude, rightAscension, declination and monthBestVisibility9pm (88 records x 5 fields = 440, plus originCategory considered separately = 528 total) were populated with real values but carried no source citation. data/gaps-report.md's completeness claim (\"every field ... resolved from a cited source\") was true only of a self-selected 10-of-16-field subset -- its denominator was a hardcoded `records * 10` in scripts/build-constellations-json.py.\n\nRoot-caused and FIXED, not just filed: all 5 fields are populated straight out of the SAME source-table rows already cited for sibling fields (pronunciation + brightestStarMagnitude share the iauTable row with name/brightestStar; rightAscension + declination + monthBestVisibility9pm share the visibilityTable row with quadrant/visibilityLatitudeRange) -- verified cell-by-cell against data/sources/*.html. Fixed by adding the 5 keys to field_sources (scripts/build-constellations-json.py) and adding the two missing srcLink() calls in build.mjs (Right ascension / Declination silently had none even when the data carried a citation). originCategory stays deliberately uncited -- it's a derived label computed from the already-cited `origin` field, not an independent claim. Regenerated data/constellations.json + site/, restarted the systemd unit, check.mjs now 20/20 clean and guards this class permanently.\n\nManual accuracy spot-check (data/accuracy-spot-check.md) additionally cross-checked 12 constellations field-by-field against the raw source HTML (exceeds the plan's >=10), including the Serpens/Ophiuchus brightest-star pair and Hercules-Family prose membership: 12/12 match, zero contradictions.\n\nAll 5 plan items (P-001..P-005) are done. Site is LIVE at http://127.0.0.1:8933/, served by systemd --user constellation-reference.service (restart-durable), all 88 constellations reachable.\nRelated: P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"coupling-signal-liveness-and-lifecycle-2026-08-11","title":"Coupling: make the union actually multi-signal, and make edges retire themselves","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-11","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Coupling: make the union actually multi-signal, and make edges retire themselves\nslug: coupling-signal-liveness-and-lifecycle-2026-08-11\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-11\nupdated: 2026-08-12\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ALL 7 ITEMS DONE (2026-08-11, su-d41fe23c under AUTO mode [owner:Avi]). Drained but NOT shipped, deliberately — see Next.\n\nTHE CENTRAL QUESTION IS ANSWERED: \"NOT ONE OF THESE RELATIONS IS DEAD — THE INSTRUMENT AND THE INPUTS WERE.\" D-005 ruled CUT NOTHING. Each zero had a different cause and all three were misread the same way:\n- `holds-a-lock-on` reads `agent_granular_locks` (0 live; production left it 2026-07-02) while real locks are in `agent_file_locks` (12 live, 9 owners) — D-003, fix EI-20199756190949760.\n- `blocks-me`/`blocked-by-me` needs two agents co-holding LIVE plan_item_claims, ~6x less used than work-item claims (5 agents vs 31; 0 plans qualify) while SIX plans have 2+ agents AND blockedBy items — D-004, fix EI-20200393414409502.\n- `awaits` is UNDETERMINED; D-001's \"true zero\" PARTLY RETRACTED (111 live awaits/98 subscribers; 2 keys co-held by 2+ agents).\n\nTHE COMMON SHAPE, worth carrying past this plan: a consumer keyed to a narrow or abandoned store while the real signal accumulates in the adjacent one. The read never errors, so it degrades into a confident, permanent, error-free wrong answer no test can see — because fixtures write the same store the code reads.\n\nALSO LANDED: P-001 fixed the instrument (census counts the BINDING input, so a short-circuited run reads `starved`, not `armed-silent`). P-005 retires edges at read time on member liveness. P-006 (D-006) chose NO default TTL for `coord:couple` on measured ground — shared-live durations 3.6h-63h, every edge supervisory, zero instances of the \"couple us for the next hour\" case the migration assumed — pinned by a test plus a calibration case. P-007 shipped the standing check and en route found a defect P-001 itself introduced (D-007): `inputs` was REDEFINED while the census version stayed 1, so 280 rows carried two meanings of the field the verdict turns on. Version is now 2; the probe judges one instrument at a time and reports what it excludes.\n\n**Next:** NEEDS AN ACCEPTANCE GRADE FROM A NON-IMPLEMENTER before `plans:set-plan-status → shipped`. I deliberately did not self-grade. NOTE: `rubrics:propose` on the DEPLOYED build (7511ab5b86) rejects the acceptance args (`kind`/`subjectPlan`/`classRef`) outright, so the rubric must be authored against a build carrying that feature — not from the live :3070 operator as of 2026-08-11.\n\nTWO FILED FIXES ARE UNASSIGNED; NEITHER IS A ONE-LINE CHANGE:\n- EI-20199756190949760 DEPENDS ON WI-5987 (needs-human): the reader takes coordination_domain from readIdentity(ctx) (agent's tree) while the writer keys it to the proxying :3070 operator's checkout, so repointing the table alone may still return zero.\n- EI-20200393414409502 must NOT be \"fixed\" by dropping the peer condition to one claiming agent — that condition keeps a 90KB+ plan parse off the common path.\n\nWI-38032 (the deferred cut re-read) is now TRIGGERED AUTOMATICALLY rather than left to memory: the armed weekly grade `auto-coupling-health-recurring-grade-2026-08-11` (routine active, first fire 2026-08-18T09:00Z) escalates on the first fire where the v2 census window reaches 5 rows. Until the P-001/D-007 code DEPLOYS that window is legitimately empty — the probe reports `census rows: 0 (v2)`, 280 excluded, all relations `no-data`, exit 0, so it cannot red-pin main while it waits.\n\n## Why this plan exists\n\nThe first `auto-coupling-health` grade (scorecard EI-20185834113596983, 2026-08-11) measured the coupling system end to end and returned **4 healthy / 4 degraded / 3 broken**. The split IS the finding: everything graded healthy is a property of the CODE (containment, symmetry, single-predicate resolution, bounded fan-out — all verified against live PG and source, all test-pinned). Everything graded broken is a property of what FLOWS THROUGH it.\n\nTwo things are broken, and they are independent:\n\n1. **The union is a one-signal system.** Over 7d / 115 instrumented runs, `coord-exchange` produced 89 of 89 edges — 100.0%. The other four produced none. And the survivor is the LOWEST-information relation in the vocabulary: a recent directed exchange means the two agents have ALREADY found each other, so the edge adds least exactly where it fires most. The relations that would surface an adjacency neither agent had noticed — a shared lock, a shared gate, a blocking plan item — are the ones at zero.\n2. **Nothing ever retires an edge.** Zero `coord:decouple` calls in the full 14-day retained window. 4 of 7 live declared edges point at agents whose presence row has already been reaped, and they are still returned, unioned, and rendered with `inRoster:false` on every coupling-resolving read. Creation has two paths; retirement has one and nobody walks it.\n\n## Relationship to `auto-coupling-delivery-and-correctness-2026-08-09` — READ BEFORE CLAIMING ANYTHING HERE\n\nThat plan is the parent, is still ACTIVE, and this one must not duplicate its open items.\n\n- **P-013 there is why this plan exists.** Its text: *\"Re-measure after the two urgent items land: if holds-a-lock-on / blocks-me / blocked-by-me still produce zero edges, the relations are unfalsifiable and should be cut from the ASSERTED forYouBecause vocabulary too, not just the derivation.\"* Its blocker P-008 is DONE, so it was unblocked and waiting. **The scorecard IS that re-measurement, and its antecedent is satisfied: all three still produce zero edges.** P-013's measurement half is discharged; its consequent is taken up in P-004 below, with one deliberate refinement recorded as D-002.\n- **P-006 there** (re-measure adoption after delivery lands) is substantially answered by the scorecard's `declared-path-adoption` + `census-coverage` criteria. Left where it is — do not re-open it here.\n- **P-011 there** (drop `topics:feed` + `coupled-topics-read.ts`) is untouched and stays there. The scorecard confirms its premise (0 calls in the retained window) but the item is already correctly homed.\n- **D-088 there is BINDING on P-002 and is the first thing to read.** It already found and fixed a dead `holds-a-lock-on`: the signal required the unreachable INTERSECTION of `include_coupling` AND `include_detail`, and was rewired onto `include_coupling` via `presenceNeedsCoordinationDomain`. That fix WORKS — the relation now arms on 46 of 115 runs where before it had never armed at all. P-002 is therefore NOT \"the gate is wrong again\". It is the next failure down.\n\n## The thing to hold in your head\n\nThe file dimension of coupling has now failed **three times, in three different ways, each green in every test**:\n\n1. `current_files` — real but permanently empty (119 live rows, zero populated; EI-18772330418885814). Cut by D-093.\n2. `holds-a-lock-on` v1 — correct code behind an unreachable flag intersection; never fired in 12 days (D-088). Gate fixed 2026-08-09.\n3. `holds-a-lock-on` v2 — gate now open, arms on 40% of runs, and STILL supplies zero inputs and zero edges (P-002 here).\n\nEach removal was justified by the next mechanism working. None of them worked. That is why D-002 refuses to apply P-013's cut rule blind.\n\n## Evidence base\n\nAll figures 7d unless stated, workspace `papercusp-workspace`, from scorecard EI-20185834113596983. Every criterion in the `auto-coupling-health` rubric carries its own copy-runnable replication drill — `rubrics:get { rubricRef: 'auto-coupling-health' }`.\n\n| relation | armed | inputs | edges |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `coord-exchange` | 115/115 | 225 | **89** |\n| `awaits` | 115/115 | 4,045 | 0 |\n| `holds-a-lock-on` | 46/115 | 0 | 0 |\n| `blocks-me` | 115/115 | 0 | 0 |\n| `blocked-by-me` | 115/115 | 0 | 0 |\n\n`awaits`'s zero is a DOCUMENTED TRUE ZERO and is not in scope here: shareable gate keys are held by agents parked in `events:await`, who make no tool calls and so are never the caller, while a working caller holds only per-subscriber-unique keys. Disjoint populations, correct code. Do not \"fix\" it.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Trust the instrument\n\n- **P-001** `done` TRUST THE INSTRUMENT BEFORE TRUSTING ANY READING BELOW. Fix the derived-signal census so a zero is interpretable: `inputs` must count the BINDING input rather than a peer-side row count (EI-20088486454213771, open+unassigned), and kill the hardcoded `awaitingEventKey:null` at fleet-roster.ts:131 / hive-roster.ts:105 (EI-20088246671600042, open+unassigned, latent). WHY THIS IS FIRST AND BLOCKS THE DIAGNOSES: today 'armed, N inputs, 0 edges' cannot distinguish 'evaluated and correctly found nothing' from 'never evaluated at all' — it has already mis-led three separate readings — so P-002 and P-003 would otherwise be diagnosing with an instrument that cannot support their conclusion. ACCEPTANCE: for each relation, a zero-edge reading names which of the two cases it is, without a human reading source. Guard it BEHAVIOURALLY (a negative-control test where the leg is deliberately starved must read differently from one deliberately armed-and-empty), never by field name. importance: urgent — note: DONE. Census now counts the BINDING input on every leg (coupling-derivation.ts). Second half (EI-20088246671600042) RETRACTED as a false positive — no code change. Verified: 5 files / 94 tests passed, executed=5 matched=5; lint:tsc clean. See rationale.\n\n## Phase 2 — Diagnose the dead relations\n\n- **P-002** `done` DIAGNOSE `holds-a-lock-on`: armed on 46 of 115 runs yet supplying ZERO inputs, on a box where the fleet holds file locks constantly. ⚠ READ D-088 ON THE PARENT PLAN FIRST — it already fixed the gate (the unreachable `include_coupling` AND `include_detail` intersection) and that fix demonstrably WORKS: the relation now arms 46/115 where it previously never armed at all. So this is NOT the gate again; it is the next failure down, and re-fixing the gate would be re-solving a solved problem. LEADING HYPOTHESIS, unconfirmed: the `heldFiles` leg reads the separate papercusp_su lock DB and is opt-in + fail-soft, so a failing/empty read presents as armed-with-zero-inputs — indistinguishable from 'no locks were held', which is exactly what P-001 makes distinguishable. Confirm or refute THAT before changing anything. BOUNDED: if not root-caused within a reasonable effort box, escalate to P-004's cut decision rather than drifting — but say so explicitly, do not let it go quiet. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-38024 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` DIAGNOSE `blocks-me` / `blocked-by-me`: armed on 115 of 115 runs with ZERO inputs across the whole window. THE TELL THAT THIS IS NOT A TRUE ZERO: plan `blockedBy` edges demonstrably exist in live data — P-013 on the parent plan itself carries `blockedBy: ['P-008']`, and this very plan's items carry them. So the planEdges leg is being supplied and coming back empty against a graph that is not empty. Establish which: (a) the leg never reads plan blocking edges at all; (b) it reads only the CALLER's own plan and the instrumented callers happened to hold no blocked items; (c) it reads them but the peer-keying drops them. Only (b) would be a true zero, and it is falsifiable — check whether any instrumented caller held a blocked plan item during the window. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: DIAGNOSED — ruling D-004. (a) and (c) REFUTED; answer is a REFINED (b): the leg is wired and the rows carry what it needs, but `planSignalPossible` requires TWO agents co-holding LIVE plan_item_claims, and 0 plans satisfy that fleet-wide (13 live claims; 5 agents — vs 31 agents holding work-items). NOT honest scarcity: 6 plans right now have 2+ agents AND blocked items. Starved by its CLAIM SURFACE.\n\n\n## Phase 3 — The cut decision\n\n- **P-004** `done` APPLY P-013's PRE-REGISTERED RULE — WITH THE DIAGNOSIS IN HAND, per D-002 below. P-013 (parent plan) says: if these relations still produce zero edges they are unfalsifiable and should be cut from the ASSERTED `forYouBecause` vocabulary as well as the derivation. Its antecedent is now satisfied. Decide per relation, not as a block: CUT what P-002/P-003 show to be genuinely unfalsifiable, FIX what they show to be merely broken. ⚠ If the verdict on `holds-a-lock-on` is 'cut', that completes a three-link chain — `current_files` was cut because `holds-a-lock-on` supersedes it, and cutting it too leaves coupling with NO file-adjacency dimension at all, permanently. That is a legitimate outcome but it must be a CHOSEN one, recorded as a decision with that consequence stated, not a quiet third removal. Whatever is cut, cut it from BOTH vocabularies in the same change — a token surviving in `FOR_YOU_BECAUSE_RELATIONS` after leaving `DERIVED_COUPLING_RELATIONS` is invisible to the divergence check while still looking fine to a human. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: RULED — D-005: CUT NOTHING. holds-a-lock-on and blocks-me/blocked-by-me are MERELY BROKEN (fix targets EI-20199756190949760, EI-20200393414409502); `awaits` is UNDETERMINED, not a true zero — D-001's disjoint-populations premise is PARTLY RETRACTED on measurement (2 shareable await keys are co-held by 2+ agents right now). Also: no cut may rest on the pre-P-001 census, and no post-fix window exists yet, so cut authority is DEFERRED to a post-fix re-read (P-007 is the trigger), not discharged.\n\n## Phase 4 — Lifecycle\n\n- **P-005** `done` MAKE EDGES RETIRE THEMSELVES — treat a reaped/ended member as an implicit expiry at READ time in `listCouplingsFor` (EI-20185949236150766). Today 4 of 7 live declared edges point at agents whose presence row is already gone, and they are still returned, unioned, and rendered with `inRoster:false` on every coupling-resolving read. WHY READ-TIME RATHER THAN A REAPER: an agent that no longer exists cannot be a relevant peer by definition, so retirement then needs neither agent cooperation nor a scheduled sweep, and can leave no residue. This SUPERSEDES the 'agents never call coord:decouple' adoption problem rather than nagging agents about it — retirement stops depending on anyone remembering. ⛔ MUST NOT DELETE ROWS: D-061 R4 requires suppress-don't-delete, and the same reasoning means a retirement must not be resurrectable by the next derivation tick. Use the liveness ORACLE, never `last_active_at` — a warm-dead session reads heartbeat-fresh. importance: high — note: ← WI-37989 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` DECIDE (do not assume) whether `coord:couple` should default a TTL. Today 6 of 7 edges carry no TTL and are therefore permanent by default, and the table comment says a TTL is for the 'couple us for the next hour while we share this file' case — which is arguably the COMMON case, not the exception. Sequenced after P-005 deliberately: if read-time liveness expiry lands, a TTL may be redundant for the dominant failure (dead-agent edges) and would then only serve the live-but-finished case. Decide with that in view and RECORD the decision either way; a default nobody chose is how the current 'permanent by default' arose. blocked-by: P-005\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Keep it honest\n\n- **P-007** `done` MAKE THE GRADE RECURRING, so a relation going dark is seen without someone hand-querying live data. D-088 asked for exactly this and named P-006 as its home: 'a derived-signal firing count, per relation, over a window — a relation that computes 0 edges across a whole window is either dead or the flag combination gating it is unreachable, and either way a human should see it.' The dead-derived-signal detector was BUILT (parent P-007, done) and the `auto-coupling-health` rubric now grades it — but every instance of this failure class so far was caught only because a human went looking. Wire the scorecard to a cadence and route its verdict somewhere a human actually reads. NOTE: all three prior failures were green in every test at the time, so this is not test coverage — it is the standing check that distinguishes 'signal is correct' from 'signal never runs'.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The re-measurement P-013 was waiting for is DONE — here is the verdict, and it satisfies P-013's antecedent\nDate: 2026-08-11\nDate: 2026-08-11\n\nP-013 on the parent plan (`auto-coupling-delivery-and-correctness-2026-08-09`) was UNBLOCKED (its blocker P-008 is done) and waiting on a re-measurement that nobody had taken. Scorecard EI-20185834113596983 is that measurement.\n\nVERDICT, 7d / 115 census-instrumented derivation runs, workspace `papercusp-workspace`:\n\n| relation | armed | inputs | edges |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `coord-exchange` | 115/115 | 225 | 89 |\n| `awaits` | 115/115 | 4,045 | 0 |\n| `holds-a-lock-on` | 46/115 | 0 | 0 |\n| `blocks-me` | 115/115 | 0 | 0 |\n| `blocked-by-me` | 115/115 | 0 | 0 |\n\nP-013's antecedent — *\"if holds-a-lock-on / blocks-me / blocked-by-me still produce zero edges\"* — is SATISFIED for all three. Its measurement half is discharged; its consequent is carried by P-004 here, refined by D-002 below.\n\nTwo readings must NOT be carried forward as defects, because they are not:\n\n- **`awaits` is a documented TRUE ZERO from correct code.** Shareable gate keys are held by agents PARKED in `events:await`, who make no tool calls and are therefore never the caller, while a working caller holds only per-subscriber-unique keys (`coord:inbox-wake:<self>`, `predicate:<uuid>`). Disjoint populations. The mechanism is recorded on the parent plan's `## Now`. Do not \"fix\" it, and do not let its 4,045 inputs be read as evidence of a broken predicate.\n- **`holds-a-lock-on`'s 40% armed rate is BY DESIGN**, not decay: the querying legs stay behind `include_detail` / an explicit `include_coupling:true` (presence.ts:227). The armed rate is not the defect. The zero INPUTS on the runs where it WAS armed is.\n\nMETHOD NOTE, so the next reader does not re-derive it wrong: `tool_invocations` retains 14 days (oldest row 2026-07-28T08:00:37Z). The parent plan's \"last ever 2026-07-27\" readings for `coord:decouple` and `topics:feed` sit one day BELOW that floor, so a raw all-time count of 0 today AGREES with those readings rather than contradicting them. Before an irreversible step justified by a recent finding, re-measure the finding itself: most of all when it is your own, and when it is the thing making the step look safe.\n\n### D-006 — coord:couple keeps NO default TTL — now a chosen default, on measured ground\nDate: 2026-08-11\nRULING (P-006): `coord:couple` continues to default `ttlSec` to null — no expiry. The measurement to re-run is the shared-live-duration query recorded on WI-37988.\n\n### D-007 — The census instrument is now VERSIONED at v2, and the probe judges one instrument at a time\nDate: 2026-08-11\nRULING (found while executing P-007): `DERIVED_SIGNAL_CENSUS_VERSION` is bumped 1 → 2, and `check-derived-signal-firings.mjs` now judges ONLY rows at the version it can interpret, reporting the excluded ones.\n\nWHAT WAS WRONG — and it was MINE, introduced by P-001 about two hours before it was found. Verified by reading the writer (coupling-derivation.ts:561-564 now passes `awaitsBindingInputs(...)`/`heldFilesBindingInputs(...)`) and the tag (derived-signal-census.ts:151 still stamped `v: 1`).\n\nWHY IT MATTERS, measured not assumed: 280 census rows exist, ALL v1, still being written (40 in the last 2h, newest 3 minutes before this ruling), and 37 of the last 40 carry `awaits.inputs > 0` — i.e. the old pool semantics.
