That is the same confident-error-free-wrong-answer shape as D-003 and D-004, which is what this plan exists to remove.\n\nTHE DEEPER POINT, which is why this is a decision and not just a fix: the `v` tag's own comment promised that \"a future shape change is detectable rather than silent\" — and it failed on its first real outing, because the change was a REDEFINITION, not an addition or a rename. A rename reds something. A redefinition reds nothing: same field, same type, same range, opposite meaning. So the rule is now written on the constant itself — BUMP ON A CHANGE OF MEANING, not only a change of shape.\n\nWHAT LANDED:\n- `DERIVED_SIGNAL_CENSUS_VERSION = 2`, with the v2 rationale recorded inline.\n- The probe pins `CENSUS_VERSION = 2`, filters both queries on it (compared as TEXT — an `::int` cast would ERROR on a malformed `v` and take the probe down, where a mismatch should merely exclude the row), and counts `censusRows` from interpretable rows ONLY, so stale rows can no longer satisfy `MIN_CENSUS_ROWS_TO_FAIL` and let a verdict fail on evidence it never read.\n- The exclusion is REPORTED, never silent: during the changeover the excluded rows are the majority, and a reader who is not told would read a thin post-bump window as \"the signal went quiet\".\n- A cross-file pin test (the writer is TS, the probe is .mjs, so neither can import the other) plus a control asserting the pin is a real comparison rather than one constant read twice.\n\nVERIFIED: 65 tests green across the 4 census/probe files; the probe run live against the DB reports `census rows: 0 (v2)`, `⚠ 280 row(s) ... excluded`, all five relations `no-data`, and EXITS 0. That last part is the safety property — bumping the version cannot red-pin `main`, because \"no data at this instrument\" is uninterpretable, not a failure.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR WI-38032: \"re-read the census under the corrected instrument\" is now an executable instruction rather than an inference from deploy timestamps — the corrected window is `v = 2`, readable straight off the row. It also cannot be read early: the v2 window is empty until the fix deploys and refills, and `MIN_CENSUS_ROWS_TO_FAIL` holds the verdict until it has 5 rows.\n\n### D-008 — Fixing a surface-starved signal: widen the OCCUPANCY SURFACE, never the cost gate — and a new derivation input must be EMITTED, not merely joined\nDate: 2026-08-12\nResolves EI-20200393414409502 (`blocks-me`/`blocked-by-me` unfirable). Two rulings, the second of which is a correction to how D-082's precedent reads.\n\n**1. THE GATE SHAPE WAS NEVER THE DEFECT — the surface it measured was.** D-004 forbade dropping the two-holder peer condition, and that stands: `readPlanBySlug` parses whole plans (90KB+ here), so a lone claimant must not trigger it. The fix keeps the identical two-holder gate and widens what counts as *holding a plan item*: `planItemsHeldOn` now unions `plan_item_claims` (5 agents fleet-wide) with held, NON-TERMINAL work-items carrying a `payload.plan_item` stamp (31 agents / 3,340 stamped rows, indexed by `work_items_plan_item_stamp_idx`). MEASURED EFFECT: plans satisfying the precondition went 0 → 2, and both qualify ONLY through the stamp surface (`via_claim_only = 0`), so the union is demonstrably the thing that unblocked it.\n\nRefs are PLAN-QUALIFIED (`<slug>#<item>` via `planItemRef`) rather than bare `P-003`. That is load-bearing twice: it makes cross-plan id collision impossible, and it lets a peer count as being on your plan through work it *holds* there even when it declares a different `currentPlanSlug` — the stronger evidence of the two (43 agents declare a plan slug; only 4 also hold a live plan-item claim).\n\n**2. ⚠ A NEW DERIVATION INPUT MUST BE ADDED TO `PRESENCE_STATE_FIELDS`, NOT JUST TO THE TIER-1 JOIN — AND D-082 READS AS SAYING THE OPPOSITE.** `deriveCouplings` is handed `snapshot.active`, which is the output of `toStableRosterRow`; that projection keeps only identity + state + three liveness scalars. So a field the producer joins but the payload does not emit is not \"cheaper\" — it is INVISIBLE to the derivation, silently, with every fixture test still green. D-082 hit the same wall from the other side (`workItemClaims` is deliberately unemitted) and solved it with an INJECTED, roster-bounded source. Copying that pattern here would have been wrong: the input is needed to COMPUTE the gate, so an injected read runs BEFORE the gate and reintroduces per-poll IO on the common path — defeating D-004 while appearing to respect it. Emitting a STATE field costs nothing here because the producer OMITS it when empty (`pick` drops undefined), so a roster where nobody holds stamped work is byte-identical to before.\n\nRULE for the next signal: decide whether your input is needed to DECIDE the expensive read (⇒ must be an emitted STATE field, computed from rows in hand) or only to INTERPRET it after the gate opens (⇒ an injected source is fine, per D-082).\n\n**3. WHAT THE CENSUS SHOULD NOW SAY, and the honest limit of this fix.** At the moment of writing no coupling edge actually fires: on both newly-qualifying plans the co-held items are not in a blocking relation with each other (each is blocked by an item nobody currently holds). That is the intended end state, not a shortfall — the signal moves from `starved` (structurally zero regardless of topology, which is what it reported for 14 days) to `armed-silent` (evaluated against real edges, found none). Do NOT read a future zero here as this defect returning; read the census verdict, which now distinguishes the two.\n\nTerminal filtering unions the two CANONICAL status sets (`ISSUE_TERMINAL_STATUSES` + frontier `TERMINAL_STATUSES`), imported, never re-literalled — a local copy of exactly these sets is what made plan-item coverage read closed work as unworked after the status unification (EI-18129037155166784).\n\nVERIFIED: 234 tests green (derivation unit incl. 5 new occupancy cases + a D-004 negative that fails if the gate is ever widened; producer pinned against LIVE PG for the jsonb path, the terminal filter and the ref format — proven non-vacuous via +4/+4 pg_stat insert/delete deltas, since the file soft-skips when PG is unreachable; emit-side two-lane drift guard; all 10 consumer suites). Typecheck: zero errors in the changed files.\n\n### D-009 — D-003's fix is a NO-OP: `holds-a-lock-on` is UNSATISFIABLE under a mutual-exclusion PK, so the source must union the waiter queue — and must gate tickets on their window, never on `status`\nDate: 2026-08-12\nEstablished 2026-08-12 by su-a63b597b (NON-implementer) while grading auto-coupling-health (scorecard EI-20206402247082799). Fix landed under EI-20199756190949760. This does not overturn D-003 — it overturns the REPAIR D-003 implies.\n\n#### D-003 said: the reader points at the abandoned table; repoint it\nTrue, and insufficient. Repointing alone yields exactly zero forever, for TWO independent reasons — both measured against the live papercusp_su side-DB, neither inferred.\n\n1. DOMAIN MISMATCH (the WI-5987 dependency, now confirmed rather than suspected). 100% of live `agent_file_locks` rows carry coordination_domain `/…/papercup-release`, the proxying operator's checkout. The reader resolves its own tree. A domain-filtered read returns zero by construction.\n\n2. STRUCTURAL, and previously unidentified. Verified against pg_constraint:\n   `agent_file_locks_pkey PRIMARY KEY (coordination_domain, path)`\n   ⇒ at most ONE owner per path. But `deriveCouplingsFromHeldFiles` emits an edge only when two owners hold the SAME path. **The primary key forbids that state from existing.** A mutual-exclusion table records who WON contention; it cannot record that contention happened.\n\n#### The ruling\nThe `holds-a-lock-on` source is held locks UNION in-flight waiter tickets (`agent_lock_waiters`, whose `paths text[]` CAN carry two owners on one path), read ACROSS coordination domains. The domain is a PARTITION key, never an access control: `rosterOwnerIds` bounds the read and `deriveCouplings` re-intersects against the roster before emission (D-044 / D-078c), so cross-domain reading cannot widen.\n\n#### ⚠ THE TRAP INSIDE THE FIX — gate tickets on `wait_until`, NEVER on `status`\nThe obvious `status = 'waiting'` filter reproduces the identical always-empty defect one level over. `status` is TRANSIENT: measured on the live table, granted 20 / expired 4 / cancelled 3 / **waiting 0**. A ticket passes through `waiting` in seconds. The `[queued_ts, wait_until)` interval is the honest intent window, and a settled ticket inside its window still means the agent is working those paths. I nearly shipped the status filter; the falsification run is the only reason I did not.\n\n#### Evidence the relation now actually fires\n- Minute-by-minute replay over the retained window: non-empty on 119/311 minutes (38.3%), against the old predicate's structural 0%.\n- Real contention exists and is frequent: 56 time-overlapping owner pairs across 4 paths; `work_items/complete.ts` alone drew 6 distinct owners.\n- END-TO-END through the REAL pure derivation at a live 3-owner instant: OLD source → 0 owners / 0 binding inputs / **0 edges**; NEW source → 4 owners / 12 binding inputs / **6 edges**, e.g. `su-3c892ab0 ↔ su-87807ffb \"you are both working in …/work_items/complete.ts\"`.\n- Note `bindingInputs` 0 → 12 independently: under the old source the census could only ever read `armed, 0 inputs, 0 edges` (a supplied-but-empty leg, indistinguishable from never-evaluated). It can now read a genuine evaluation that honestly found nothing — the census-honesty property, satisfied at the source rather than in the instrument.\n\n#### Consequential wording change\n`sharedLocksPhrase` said \"you both hold locks in X\". With the waiter union, one side of an edge may be QUEUED rather than holding, so that claim is false for exactly the edges this now emits. Changed to \"you are both working in X\". A false `because` string in the one signal this rubric grades for honesty is not a cosmetic issue.\n\n#### Also repaired en route\n`fetchPresenceHeldFiles` — the `include_detail` heldFiles lane — was reading the same abandoned table and had therefore ALSO been returning an empty map on every call. It now reads `agent_file_locks` with `includeIntents:false`, deliberately holds-only: that lane answers \"what does this agent HOLD\", and reporting queued paths there would be misleading.\n\n### D-010 — `blocks-me`/`blocked-by-me` is a MEASURED true zero, not a repairable defect — D-004's suggested fix yields zero, and loosening it violates bounded-fan-out (16 edges/caller)\nDate: 2026-08-12\nEstablished 2026-08-12 by su-a63b597b (grade+auto, owner-directed) under EI-20200393414409502. D-004's DIAGNOSIS stands — `plan_item_claims` is too narrow. Its SUGGESTED FIX does not work, and neither do the two other tempting repairs. Measured, not reasoned.\n\n#### 1. The filed suggestion — union work-item claims into plan-item occupancy — YIELDS ZERO\nEI-20200393414409502 flagged the work-item→plan-item mapping as unverified. Verified now, over LIVE claims (102 claimed work-items, 75 agents):\n    source_plan_item_ids populated ....  0 / 102\n    source_plan_slug populated ........  2 / 102\n    payload.plan_item populated ....... 19 / 102   (shape { item_id, plan_slug } — snake_case)\nAnd decisively, the UNION of BOTH occupancy sources — live `plan_item_claims` (only 4 live / 4 agents / 4 plans) ∪ `work_items.payload.plan_item` — gives **ZERO plans with 2+ distinct agents holding a NAMED plan item**. Every such plan has exactly one. Adding work-item claims does not create the pair; the pair does not exist.\n\n#### 2. Loosening the precondition to plan-level co-occupancy — RULED OUT, with a number\nAgents DO co-occupy plans by `current_plan_slug`: nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08 carries 17, verify-0014-alpha 3, three more at 2. So dropping to \"both on this plan\" would fire — and would derive **16 edges for a single caller** on that one plan. That is exactly the D-054 set-membership signature the auto-coupling-health `bounded-fan-out` criterion forbids (its cited precedent: same-fleet deriving 17 edges for one caller on an 18-member fleet). Fixing `derived-signal-liveness` by breaking `bounded-fan-out` is not a fix.\n\n#### 3. A work-item-level blocking edge — DOES NOT EXIST\n`harness_shared.work_item_blocked` (52 rows) is a boolean FLAG table — columns are (workspace_id, harness_slug, feature_id, updated_at). It records THAT an item is blocked, never BY WHAT, so it cannot express a pairwise edge between two agents' items. `harness_shared.work_item_claims` is itself dead: 0 live rows, 0 agents (claims live on `work_items.taken_by`).\n\n#### THE RULING\n`blocks-me`/`blocked-by-me` is a TRUE ZERO with a MEASURED MECHANISM, not a defect to repair: **agents do not co-occupy plans at ITEM granularity.** One agent per plan is the norm even where 17 share the plan slug, so the pair the relation needs is never formed. The relation is correctly specified and correctly bounded; the fleet's working pattern does not produce its precondition.\n\nPer the rubric's own `derived-signal-liveness` model, a true zero is an acceptable reading ONLY once its mechanism is recorded where the next reader will find it — which is the purpose of this decision. KEEP the relation in the vocabulary (consistent with D-005's CUT NOTHING): it becomes live the moment plan-item claiming becomes normal practice, and it costs nothing while it does not fire.\n\n#### What would actually change the reading\nNot a code change — a PRACTICE change: agents claiming plan ITEMS (coord:orient { planItems } / plan_items:claim) rather than only declaring a plan slug. 4 live item-claims fleet-wide is the real number to move. Until then, any code fix is either a no-op (1) or a bounded-fan-out violation (2).\n\n⛔ DO NOT re-file this as \"wrong table\". It is the THIRD such diagnosis in this feature and the first two were genuinely wrong-table; this one is not.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hud-chat-owner-controls-2026-08-11","title":"HUD chat owner controls — token limit, account pin, and model+effort, requested 2026-07-27 and open since","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-11","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: HUD chat owner controls — token limit, account pin, and model+effort, requested 2026-07-27 and open since\nslug: hud-chat-owner-controls-2026-08-11\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-11\nupdated: 2026-09-01\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ALL FIVE ITEMS ARE TERMINAL (5 done, 0 dropped) as of 2026-09-01. Implementation is complete; only the validation path remains. Plan status is awaiting-acceptance with rubricActive:false — no acceptance rubric exists yet.\n\nTHE CTX DOWNSTREAM LEG WAS CLOSED BY DIRECT OBSERVATION, not composition. Throwaway subject su-1e3c9d0d had its limit written to 20000 through the pill's own writer (read back compaction_limit=20000, compaction_limit_explicit=true) and its transcript grown to 436,128 B. The watchdog then logged six times across two distinct pids:\n  ~72264/20000 tokens (361%) + CARRY-RESPAWN queued\n  ~25476/20000 tokens (127%) + CARRY-RESPAWN queued   <- decisive: after a respawn the estimate FELL, then re-flagged against the SAME 20000 denominator\n  ~47687/20000 tokens (238%)\nPositive control: 518 over-limit lines for other subjects in the same window and method. The old caveat \"the one thing NOT shown is a compaction triggered by a limit I personally set\" is RETIRED. ACCOUNT and MODEL downstream were already closed by earlier stints.\n\nTHE OLD \"BLOCKED ON ACCOUNT CAPACITY\" STORY WAS WRONG on two counts and must not be re-derived: the working route needs zero LLM turns, so capacity never blocked it; and the real blocker was the context-ESTIMATION gap, since setContextEstimate precedes both rungs. Measured 2026-09-01: 15/161 (9.3%) unestimated, but estimation reaches 2m37s-old sessions while the stuck subset runs to 9 days — a persistent ~9% bug, not a universal blocker.\n\nTWO INSTRUMENT TRAPS, both of which cost real time: journalctl -u 'papercup*' MISSES the watchdog entirely because it logs under bash[<pid>], so every unit-filtered search returns a false empty; and the recorded launchContext-ballast route lands 0 bytes in the transcript on current code, so genuine capability:read turns are what grow it.\n\n**Next:** Run the acceptance close, in order: (1) plans:audit { phase:'completion' } — per-item code-truth audit with resolving code/test citations; (2) rubrics:propose { kind:'acceptance', subjectPlan:'hud-chat-owner-controls-2026-08-11', classRef:'plan-class-feature-ship' } with 3-7 outcome criteria tracing to the goal and the 12 Decisions; (3) vet it via consult:get_feedback { policy:'rubric-vetting' }, then attest with scorecards:emit against meta-acceptance-rubric; (4) ROUTE grading to a non-implementer outside the rubric author's lineage — a grader you launch yourself is refused at emit; (5) the rubric author records acceptance:{verdict,reasoning}; (6) plans:set-plan-status shipped.\n\n## Background\n\nGoal: `the-gui-chat-surface-is-ready-to-ship-to-strange-8fa0ed`.\n\nOwner Avi requested three chat-footer controls on **2026-07-27**. All three have been open since:\n\n| item | ask |\n|---|---|\n| **WI-6507** | a control to adjust the TOKEN LIMIT |\n| **WI-6509** | a control to change which ACCOUNT the chat is pinned to (system default / auto / a pool account) |\n| **WI-6510** | controls to change the MODEL and the EFFORT level |\n\n**Why these are in the release goal at all.** They are not defect repair — they are the difference between a surface a stranger can operate and one that only its author can. A user who cannot see which model answers them, or which account it bills, is being asked to trust a black box. Shipping without them should be a decision, not an oversight — that is why they sit under this goal rather than in the general backlog.\n\n**Why they run CONCURRENTLY with the audit.** They are owner-specified and need nothing the audit produces. The audit plan's D-003 explicitly names this work as the parallelism that pays back its own serialization.\n\n## Phase 1 — decide the surface once\n\n- **P-001** `done` Settle the shared shape of the chat-footer control strip BEFORE building any single control: where it lives, how it behaves when a value is unavailable or not permitted, and — critically — whether each control is per-session or global, because that decision is invisible in a mock and expensive to reverse. Check `design-phase:search_registry` for an existing component before inventing one; the repo convention is to pick from the registry rather than hand-roll. Deliverable is a short spec the other three items render into. importance: high — note: Settled as D-005 (WI-37932 done).\n\n## Phase 2 — the three controls\n\n- **P-002** `done` WI-6510: MODEL + EFFORT control. Taken first of the three because it is the one a stranger most needs — \"which brain am I talking to\" — and because model+effort is a single compound choice (`<model>:<effort>`), so splitting them across two controls would misrepresent the underlying setting. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: BUILT + 153 tests green, both typechecks clean. Behaviour in the running app is NOT yet observed — that is P-005.\n- **P-003** `done` WI-6509: ACCOUNT PIN control. Three real values, not a free-text field: a specific pool account (pinned, no failover), `auto` (gateway-routed with failover), or `default` (the system credential, gateway skipped). The UI must make the failover difference legible — that is the whole reason a user would touch it. blocked-by: P-001 — note: WI-6509 closed (authority: committed). ACCOUNT pill lives in apps/operator/lib/chat-actions/AccountAction.ts, registered by side-effect import from the chat-actions barrel, which ChatActionBar.tsx + SessionChatModal.tsx consume; barrel-registration.test.ts pins that chain (the WI-6450 tree-shake failure mode). 35/35 unit tests green, scoped typecheck 0 errors in the changed files. The three owner-named values are distinguished against the WRITER, not the tool names: pool account -> accounts:pin (live), auto -> accounts:unpin (live), default system account -> not dynamically reachable (a --account=default session bypasses the gateway) so it renders DISABLED with that reason. Item was already built by an earlier session and simply never flipped; this claim was verification. Live behavioural drive remains P-005's, by design.\n- **P-004** `done` WI-6507: TOKEN LIMIT control. Establish FIRST what the number actually governs (the compaction soft-limit, not a hard cap) and label it accordingly — a control labelled \"token limit\" that silently means something else is worse than no control. blocked-by: P-001 — note: WI-6507 closed (authority: committed). CTX pill: ContextLimitAction + the three actionCtx keys (compactionLimit, ompThreadId, pid) present in SessionChatModal.tsx, 21/21 tests green including ctx-wiring.test.ts, the derived guard for the missing-ctx-key class that tsc cannot catch (ChatActionContext has an index signature by design). P-004's labelling requirement is met: the accessible name names the compaction SOFT-limit and self-compaction point, not a hard cap. Built + live-driven by su-ff7c78bf (2026-08-12, evidence on the item's checkpoint: isolated Tauri rig on its own DISPLAY, discriminating bundle marker, a two-session READ pair at 158k/400k, and the WRITE refusal branch); this claim was re-verification against the current tree plus the close.\n\n## Phase 3 — the honest close\n\n- **P-005** `done` Live-drive all three in the Tauri shell and confirm each one CHANGES BEHAVIOUR, not just state: set it, send a turn, verify the turn actually used the chosen model / account / limit. A control that renders correctly and does nothing is the failure mode here, and it passes every unit test. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-37933 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Decide the surface before building any control\n\nThree controls requested together, built separately, land as three different shapes in one footer — and the shared questions (per-session vs global, unavailable-value behaviour) get answered three times, differently. P-001 costs little and is the only item that cannot be parallelised away.\n\n### D-002 A control that renders is not a control that works\n\nP-005 exists because the failure mode for settings UI is silent no-op: the control renders, stores its value, and nothing downstream reads it. That passes typecheck and unit tests. The only evidence that counts is a turn that demonstrably used the chosen value — the same live-drive standard the audit plan's D-002 sets.\n\n### D-003 Ship-or-cut is explicit, never silent\n\nIf any of the three cannot land before the release, that is a decision to record and tell Avi — not an omission to discover. He asked for these on 2026-07-27; going quiet on them is the outcome this plan exists to prevent.\n\n### D-004 — Semantics research runs in parallel with C-001; only RENDERING is gated on it\nDate: 2026-08-11\nC-001 settles the shared SHAPE of the control strip (placement, per-session vs global, unavailable-value behaviour). It does not settle what each control's values MEAN downstream. Those are separable, so the fleet does not serialize on C-001 for everything: while C-001 is in flight, the other lanes establish, read-only, what each setting actually governs and where it is consumed — for the token limit (compaction soft-limit vs hard cap), the account pin (pool account / auto / default and the failover difference), and model+effort (the compound `<model>:<effort>` spec). That research is the input P-005 needs to prove behaviour changed rather than state changed, and it is the answer to D-002. What IS gated on C-001 is building any control UI: wait for the announced gate `fleet:hud-chat-owner-controls:surface-spec-ready`.\n\n### D-005 — The shared control surface already exists — all three controls are ChatModeAction axes, not new UI\nDate: 2026-08-11\nC-001 (WI-37932) settled by reading the code. The footer already has a designed control vocabulary and all three requested controls fit it exactly. No new band, no new row, no fourth button. Binding on P-002/P-003/P-004.\n\n**1. WHICH BAND.** The footer is TWO bands with different jobs, by prior ruling:\n- `SessionStateHeader` — `pc-ctl-band--status`, cap \"Status\" (SessionChatModal.tsx:404-514). INFORMATIONAL ONLY: its header comment says \"no click handlers, no write path — mode CONTROL lives in the chat action bar, not here.\"\n- `ChatActionBar` — `pc-ctl-band--do`, cap \"Controls\" (ChatActionBar.tsx:301-317). All three go HERE.\nA setter in the Status band re-creates the duplication the pill design killed: an `AUTO` chip beside an `Autonomy` button — \"one concept wearing two costumes, neither saying it was the other\" (types.ts:100-113).\n\n**2. WHAT SHAPE.** Each is a `ChatModeAction` via `registerChatModeAction` (apps/operator/lib/chat-actions/), rendering as the established PILL: filled cap + current value + caret. Three axes already ship on this contract — `mode-autonomy`, `mode-grade`, `mode-drain` (PostureActions.ts:167/287/405). Right shape because each is \"a value that is currently something, and the control that changes it\" — reporting and setting as ONE object, which a stateless ChatAction button is not.\n\n**3. PER-SESSION, NOT GLOBAL — settled.** The question invisible in a mock and expensive to reverse; the existing contract answers it. `ChatActionContext.sessionOwnerId` is the axis's whole subject (types.ts:34-41); every shipped axis gates `available: (ctx) => Boolean(ctx.sessionOwnerId)` and every setter writes for that owner. All three set the value for THE SESSION THIS CHAT IS ATTACHED TO. Do not introduce a global semantic in any of the three; if one is wanted it is a separate item, not a quiet widening.\n\n**4. BOUNDED vs UNBOUNDED is DECLARED, not inferred.** `searchable: true` → scrolling/filtering ComboboxMenu; omitted → plain Radix `Select`. MODEL → searchable. ACCOUNT → searchable (live from accounts:list). EFFORT → plain Select. TOKEN LIMIT → plain Select of presets (see 7).\n\n**5. UNAVAILABLE ⇒ NOT OFFERED — never a pill showing a guess.** `available()` false means no pill; there is no disabled-with-placeholder state and none should be invented. Precedent is explicit and is the honest reason two are missing today: \"model/effort are NOT on the roster entry and are omitted rather than guessed at\" (SessionChatModal.tsx:390-391). Corollary binding on P-002: the MODEL/EFFORT axis ships only once `current()` reads a REAL per-session value. A pill showing a plausible-but-unsourced model is WORSE than the absence — it converts a visible gap into an invisible lie.\n\n**6. READ IS SYNC, OPTIONS ARE LAZY.** `current(ctx)` must be PURE and SYNC — it reads what the surface already rendered from, so the pill cannot disagree with the rest of the popup and costs no fetch. `options(ctx)` MAY be async, resolved on menu open (`ensureOptions`, ChatActionBar.tsx:195), so an unopened menu costs no query. Do NOT fix a missing `current()` by making it async — source the value onto the roster entry instead. That is P-002's real work.\n\n**7. FREE TEXT USES A CARD, NOT AN INPUT IN THE DROPDOWN.** TOKEN LIMIT is the one non-enum axis: use `params(ctx, optionId)` → CardSpec → askUserLocal, the same plumbing ChatAction.params uses (types.ts:218-251). Not a preference — a Radix Select claims keystrokes for typeahead so an input inside it cannot reliably receive typing, and the searchable box is a FILTER, not a value collector. Shape: preset menu from the tier menu (`config:tiers-get` already carries `compactionLimit` per tier) + a \"Custom…\" row collecting the number via `params`.\n\n**8. LABEL TOKEN LIMIT FOR WHAT IT GOVERNS.** Per WI-6507, resolve the referent before building: the live wired knob is the per-session COMPACTION limit (`compactionLimit` on the roster entry, rendered `ctx N%`; setter `config:set-compaction-limit`, clamped in set-compaction-limit-core.ts). A soft compaction threshold, NOT a hard cap — do not label it in a way implying otherwise.\n\n**9. REGISTRATION GOTCHA.** Concrete axes register by SIDE-EFFECT import in lib/chat-actions/index.ts. WI-6450 records the failure: actions tree-shaken out, ChatActionBar renders null. Each new axis adds its Entry module AND its barrel line; a live check that the pill APPEARS is the only proof it landed.\n\nEvidence: read 2026-08-11 19:37-19:45Z — SessionChatModal.tsx:385-560, ChatActionBar.tsx:255-455, lib/chat-actions/types.ts:34-257, lib/chat-actions/PostureActions.ts, lib/chat-actions/index.ts.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-006 — D-005 amended: the controls are NOT symmetric — three axes, three write-costs, and a third pill state\nDate: 2026-08-11\nAmends D-005 with peer su-ff7c78bf's value-sourcing recon (msg msp2jvrh, 19:44Z; detail on WI-6507/6509/6510). D-005 stands except where this overrides it. I own the surface decision, so the correction is recorded here rather than left in a coord message.\n\n**A. D-005 §5 WAS UNDER-SPECIFIED — SPLIT IT IN TWO.** §5 said an unavailable value means `available()` false means NO PILL. That is right for ONE of the two cases and wrong for the other, and conflating them would have shipped the owner's explicitly-named option missing from its own picker.\n- **Value UNKNOWN ⇒ omit the axis.** Unchanged, and this is what §5's rationale (\"omitted rather than guessed at\") actually protects: never render a pill whose displayed value is a guess.\n- **Value KNOWN but NOT SETTABLE ⇒ render the pill, disabled, with the reason in its tooltip.** This is a THIRD state — not loading, not error. It is \"present, correct, and not clickable right now.\"\nTwo permanent, non-transient instances force it: (i) WI-6509's \"default system account\" — a `--account=default` session bypasses the gateway entirely and cannot be re-pinned live, yet the owner named that option explicitly, so it must appear in the picker while being un-appliable by click; (ii) WI-6510's model/effort — there is no live setter anywhere; changing model means relaunching the process. Neither resolves with time, so neither may be modelled as a loading or error state.\n\n**B. IT IS THREE CONTROLS, NOT FOUR — EFFORT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT AXIS.** psu carries model and effort as a single `<model>:<effort>` value, and effort-without-model is an explicit error. So the band holds: TOKEN LIMIT, ACCOUNT, and a COMPOSED MODEL+EFFORT axis. Do not register a standalone `mode-effort`; a separate effort pill could be set to a state the system rejects. This also corrects D-005 §4, which assigned MODEL and EFFORT different menu treatments as if they were separate axes — the composed axis is `searchable: true` as a whole.\n\n**C. THE THREE HAVE DIFFERENT WRITE-COSTS, AND THE PILL MUST NOT HIDE THAT.** Token limit is a live write. Account is a live write for 2 of its 3 values. Model+effort is a SESSION RELAUNCH. A relaunch is not the same interaction as setting a value and must not be reachable by the same silent one-click path as the other two — it takes a confirm step (`ChatAction`'s confirm/`params` plumbing, which the bar already runs before `set`). D-005's shared shape survives this; what does not survive is any assumption that every axis commits identically on click.\n\n**D. THE TOKEN LIMIT IS CLAMPED ON WRITE — RENDER THE EFFECTIVE VALUE, NOT THE TYPED ONE.** The write clamps by role and model window (set-compaction-limit-core.ts: member cap, self-set ceiling). The pill must display the value the setter RETURNED, and when it differs from what was asked, say so (\"asked 500k, running the member cap\"). A control that echoes its own input is the silent-no-op failure of plan D-002 wearing a different costume: it looks like it worked and the number is not the number in force.\n\n**E. STANDING ACCOUNT MANDATE APPLIES TO THE DEFAULT, NOT TO THE CONTROL.** Memory carries an owner mandate of 2026-07-01: no hard per-account pins; agents use the gateway's AUTO routing with failover. The owner's 2026-07-27 request for this control is LATER and authorises the control's existence. Both hold: the picker offers pinning, and AUTO remains the default — this control must not become a standing fleet-wide pin, and nothing here changes any agent's launch default. Flagging rather than resolving: I have not re-verified the 2026-07-01 mandate against an owner turn, so it is cited as recalled context, not as an owner directive.\n\nConsequence for lanes: P-004 (token limit) is the only one of the three that is a plain live write. P-003 (account) needs the disabled-pill state from §A. P-002 (model+effort) needs BOTH §A and the §C confirm, and is the ship-or-cut candidate.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-007 — SHIP the model/effort DISPLAY, CUT the CHANGE half — conditional on one timeboxed probe, and the cut goes to Avi as a decision\nDate: 2026-08-11\n**FINAL STATE (19:52Z, third and last revision): BUILD THE FULL MODEL+EFFORT CONTROL.** Branch 1 of the pre-committed rule fires — `psu --resume … --model` (WI-3758) carries conversation context across a changed spec, so a model change does NOT end the session. The earlier CUT is withdrawn and does not apply.\n\nWHAT SHIPS, all three controls:\n\n1. **WI-6507 token limit** — live setter (`config:set-compaction-limit` → `PgPresenceStore.setCompactionLimit`, integration-tested). MUST render the **effective** returned value, never what the user typed: `clampCompactionLimit` silently reduces by role + model window, so displaying the requested number is a control that lies (D-002).\n2. **WI-6509 account pin** — `accounts:pin`/`unpin` are live and durable, no respawn. \"A specific account\" ✓, \"auto\" ✓. \"Default system account\" needs the resume path (a `--account=default` session is a deliberate gateway-free escape hatch); label its constraint rather than hiding the option.\n3. **WI-6510 model + effort** — DISPLAY plus a real CHANGE control, labelled as changing the model. Sourced via `resolveModelSpecForOwner` off `adv_sessions.launch_argv`.\n\nTWO MECHANISM FACTS THAT ARE THE WHOLE VALUE OF THIS DECISION:\n\n**Compose via `composeModelSpec` (`agent-launch-core.ts:576`). NEVER hand-roll flag emission.** psu has no `--effort` flag, and an unrecognized flag is WARNED AND DROPPED by parseArgs — so emitting `--effort=` separately is a SILENT NO-OP. `modelArgsFor` splits the `<model>:<effort>` tail per backend (claude `--model X --effort Y`, codex `-c model_reasoning_effort`, omp verbatim). Composing at that seam is the one form every backend honours. The composer's own history records a GUI copy that silently dropped the effort choice; a footer control re-emitting its own flags would reproduce that bug AND PASS EVERY TEST.\n\n**EFFORT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT AXIS.** Effort rides `<model>:<effort>` and effort-without-model is an explicit error. The owner's \"buttons\" is ONE composed control, not two.\n\nONE HOP TO SETTLE BEFORE ANY UI: does `capability:launch-agent`'s resume path forward a `model` arg through to `resumeArgsFor`, or does only psu's CLI accept it? That is the difference between a control that re-points the session and one that appears to — the same silent-drop shape as the `--effort=` trap. **After that hop: BUILD. No further re-rulings without NEW mechanism evidence.**\n\n---\n\n#### HOW THIS DECISION MOVED, preserved because the method is the reusable part\n\nThis item held THREE positions in fifteen minutes and every move was evidence-driven:\n\n1. **19:47Z — CUT**, on recon showing no live model setter anywhere (config/ enumerated, gateway/ group enumerated, operator-core + agent-mcp grepped for setModel/setEffort/changeModel and any `*model*` tool). That absence proof still stands and is still true.\n2. **19:48Z — cut WITHDRAWN**, on finding `composeModelSpec` already takes model+effort separately and emits the one wire form, retiring the \"this is a session-relaunch flow, not footer work\" concern.\n3. **19:48Z — cut PROVEN**, on `RespawnLaunchSpec` having no model axis and `request-compaction` reading the model only to size the carry budget.\n4. **19:52Z — BUILD**, on `psu --resume … --model` (WI-3758) existing: the resume path, unlike the respawn path, does accept a changed model AND carries context. Steps 3 and 4 are not contradictory — they are about two different mechanisms, and only step 4's is the one a control would use.\n\n**The method that made this cheap rather than chaotic: the branches were named BEFORE the probe.** When I ruled the cut I attached a bounded probe AND stated in advance what each outcome would mean — context carries → full control; context does not → an honestly-labelled destructive action. So each new finding SELECTED a branch instead of REOPENING the argument. Without that, four findings in fifteen minutes would have been four rounds of re-litigation and the outcome would owe more to fatigue than evidence.\n\nWorth repeating wherever an unresolved mechanism gates a product call: name the branches before the probe, not after.\n\nPer D-003, the outcome goes to Avi as a decision — he asked for these on 2026-07-27 and gets told what shipped and why, rather than inferring it from the UI.\n\n### D-008 — Every control must model ACCEPTED-BUT-MODIFIED, not just available/unavailable\nDate: 2026-08-11\nC-001 was scoped to settle how a control behaves when a value is unavailable or not permitted. The WI-6507 research found a third case that is worse than either and is not covered by that pair: the value is permitted, the write returns ok:true, and the system stores something DIFFERENT. config:set-compaction-limit clamps rather than rejects (clampCompactionLimit is Math.min(Math.max(...)), it never refuses) and returns ok:true alongside clamped:true, requested and cap. A control that reads the bare ok reports success for a value it did not set — which is strictly worse than a control that does nothing, because it lies rather than no-ops, and it passes every unit test that asserts ok. RULING, binding on all three controls: each control reads the setter's coercion fields, not the bare ok, and renders the accepted-but-modified state distinctly from both success and rejection. C-001's spec must name this as a first-class state of the strip. The account pin plausibly has the same shape when a pinned account is rate-limited and the gateway fails over, and model+effort may coerce an unsupported effort — su-ff7c7 owns confirming both. Evidence: agent-config-constants.ts:650, config/set-compaction-limit.ts:95-98.\n\n### D-009 — Placement stays the Controls band (not the fleet row), and ACCEPTED-BUT-MODIFIED is named as a required fourth state\nDate: 2026-08-11\nSettles the two inputs the fleet leader raised against D-005 (msg msp2l1i3). Leader stated that if I concluded otherwise on placement they would take that as settled; I do, and here is the evidence.\n\n**A. PLACEMENT: the three controls go in the CONTROLS band, NOT in WI-6505's fleet-launch row. The distinction is already written in the code and it is about SUBJECT, not about buttons-vs-rows.**\nChatActionBar.tsx:308-310 states the rule directly: \"everything in this band changes THIS session, which is what separates it from the Fleet strip below (that one acts on something else entirely).\" FleetLaunchRow is deliberately not even a band — its own test asserts `container.querySelectorAll('.pc-ctl-band').length === 0` (FleetLaunchRow.test.tsx:527).\nAll three of our controls change THIS session (D-005 §3, `ChatActionContext.sessionOwnerId`). The fleet row launches a DIFFERENT thing. So they are not the same kind of object and do not share a strip.\nThe owner's \"instead of a button like the others make this its own always visible row\" was about the FLEET LAUNCHER specifically — and the reason it earned a row is exactly that it acts on something else. Reading it as a general preference for rows over buttons would put a session control inside a strip whose entire stated purpose is to not be about this session. WI-6505 is already done and shipped that way; nothing here reopens it.\n\n**B. ACCEPTED-BUT-MODIFIED is a FOURTH state, and it is CONFIRMED for two of the three controls — not plausible, measured.** The leader is right that available/unavailable is not enough. Beside D-006 §A's disabled-but-present state, a control must model: the write returned ok, and the system stored something DIFFERENT from what was asked.\n- TOKEN LIMIT: `config:set-compaction-limit` clamps rather than rejects, returning ok with clamped/requested/cap (set-compaction-limit-core.test.ts asserts the member-cap and self-set-ceiling clamps explicitly).\n- ACCOUNT: CONFIRMED by reading the writer, gateway.ts:97-102. `accounts:pin` returns `ok` with **`appliedLive: false`** plus a `warn` when the durable write succeeded but the live push to the gateway did not — \"it will load on the next poll/restart\". A control reading bare `ok` reports success for a pin that is not in force yet.\n- SEPARATELY for ACCOUNT, the DEFAULT pin is SOFT: gateway.ts:74 — soft \"prefers it but yields if it is paused/exhausted\", only `hard:true` never fails over. So even a fully successful soft pin does not guarantee the session is ON that account. The pill must not read \"pinned to X\" as though it were a guarantee.\nRule: every one of the three renders the EFFECTIVE value the setter returned, never the value the user picked, and says so when they differ. A control that echoes its own input is plan D-002's silent no-op wearing a nicer costume.\n\n**C. CORRECTION TO THE RECON, in the account control's favour.** Re-pinning a running session does NOT require a respawn. `accounts:pin` is explicitly the live re-pin verb (WI-4402): \"LIVE (no respawn) … Effective on that agent's NEXT model call — no respawn, no lost context.\" The one genuine exception is the one the recon named correctly: a `--account=default` session bypasses the gateway and cannot be dynamically re-pinned; it must be respawned. So the three ACCOUNT values split as: a specific pool account → live write (`accounts:pin`); `auto` → live write (`accounts:unpin`); `default system account` → NOT live, needs respawn ⇒ D-006 §A's disabled-but-present pill.\n\n**D. NEW CONSTRAINT ON P-003, same shape as P-002's.** D-005 §6 requires `current()` to be pure and synchronous, read from what the surface already holds. The authoritative read of an agent's current routing is `gateway:owner_report { agent }` — a fetch, not a roster field. So the ACCOUNT axis has the SAME structural problem as model/effort: its current value is not on the roster entry today. Either the pin lands on the roster row (preferred, mirrors P-002's fix) or the axis renders under D-006 §A rather than guessing. Do not solve it by making `current()` async — D-005 §6 forbids that, and an async read here would put a gateway fetch on every popup open.\n\nEvidence read 2026-08-11 19:47-19:52Z: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/gateway/gateway.ts:53-107 (accounts:pin, full handler); accounts/session-override.ts:25-49 (set-session-override is a FLEET-WIDE steer, not a per-session pin — do not wire the chat control to it); ChatActionBar.tsx:308-310; FleetLaunchRow.test.tsx:525-527.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-010 — D-008 AMENDED — the clamp premise was wrong; the write is REFUSED, not silently downgraded. The rule stands, the reason is replaced.\nDate: 2026-08-11\nD-008 said: render the EFFECTIVE returned value, never what the user typed, BECAUSE config:set-compaction-limit silently clamps and returns ok:true. I authored that. The stated reason is FALSE and is withdrawn; the RULE it produced is correct and stays binding on all three controls.\n\nVERIFIED IN THE WRITERS (2026-08-11T19:58Z, su-26ef6):\n- set-compaction-limit.ts:84-97 and set-compaction-limit-core.ts:109-123 both REJECT an over-cap request: ok:false, error:'limit_exceeds_cap', the cap returned, and NO write performed.\n- The guard and the later clampCompactionLimit call resolve the SAME ceiling through the SAME function with the SAME opts, so the clamp cannot move an already-validated value.\n- The `clamped`/`requested` fields that misled me are labelled in the source as \"Legacy diagnostic field retained for compatibility with older callers\" (set-compaction-limit-core.ts:35). I inferred behaviour from the response SHAPE instead of reading the emitting branch.\n\nWHY THE RULE SURVIVES ANYWAY — the hazard is INVERTED, not absent:\nA control written to the old premise assumes the write always lands and merely displays a possibly-clamped number. Under the real contract, an over-cap pick changes NOTHING while the pill reports success. That is the same lying-control failure D-002/D-008 exist to prevent, reached from the opposite direction. So: render the returned value, and branch on the refusal.\n\nAMENDED OBLIGATION on every control in this plan that writes through a config/mode tool:\n1. Render the EFFECTIVE value the response returns, never the requested one. (unchanged)\n2. Handle ok:false EXPLICITLY. Do not treat a non-throwing HTTP 200 as success — these tools return ok:false in a 200 body.\n3. Do not read bare ok:false as one outcome. `ok` is `persisted != null`, so ok:false means EITHER \"refused, over cap\" (carries error:'limit_exceeds_cap' + cap) OR \"no live presence row — the target session ended\" (carries a note). These need different words to the owner; a single \"failed\" message for both is a control that misinforms.\n4. Do NOT hardcode a ceiling. It varies by model spec AND fleet role (fleet member 200k vs leader/solo 825k on [1m]), and EI-19932842496005122 observed 400k where the code says 825k. Surface the cap the REJECTION returns rather than predicting it.\n\nEI-20187186554229192 is rescoped: retracted as filed, narrowed to a genuine low-end residue (a sub-20k request from a non-tool caller such as fleet:reconfigure-member clamps UP to the floor silently with ok:true) plus the ok:false ambiguity in (3).\n\nSTANDING LESSON for this fleet, since two more lanes are writing controls against tools right now: a response field's EXISTENCE is not evidence of the code path that sets it. Read the branch that emits it before you build a control — or a decision — on what it implies.\nRelated: P-003, P-005\n\n### D-011 — A control's WRITE-SUCCESS does not satisfy P-005 — the downstream turn-level check is the bar\nDate: 2026-08-27\nRecorded 2026-08-27 by su-49e66bca while closing the ACCT and CTX write-success branches\n(WI-37933), because the next reader will otherwise reasonably conclude the plan is finished.\n\n**The ruling:** proving a control's success path WRITES — the value lands durably, the server\nreturns ok, the pill re-reads it — is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for P-005. P-005's own text\npre-emptively rejects that reading: *\"set each control, send a turn, and verify the turn ACTUALLY\nUSED the chosen model / account / limit. Not that the control renders. Not that the value\npersists.\"* An item may be closed as write-success-proven; **P-005 may not be marked done on that\nevidence.**\n\n**Why the distinction is real and not pedantry.** This plan exists because of D-002's silent\nno-op: a control that renders, stores its value, and is read by nothing downstream passes every\nunit test and every persistence check. Write-success evidence is exactly the evidence a silent\nno-op also produces. Only the consumption check distinguishes them. Today's ACCT leg is the\nsharp case: the durable pin landed and the gateway returned `appliedLive:true`, which proves the\nrunning gateway ACCEPTED the pin — and still does not prove any turn was routed to that account.\n\n**The honest ceiling, so the remaining work is not over-specified.** `accounts:pin` is SOFT by\ndesign: the gateway prefers the account and yields when it is paused or exhausted, and\nAccountAction's header is explicit that the pill reports the PIN in force and never claims the\nsession IS on an account. So the ACCOUNT downstream assertion is \"the turn routed to X, **or**\nthere is a recorded pin-yield with a reason\" — never \"always X\". Asserting more than the control\nclaims would manufacture a failure rather than find one.\n\n**Applies to all three axes**, including any future session-config pill added to this bar.\n\n### D-012 — gw-route `routed=` is the route DECISION, not the served account — use the ledger/lastRoute\nDate: 2026-08-27\nThe gateway log line `gw-route: client=N want=X routed=Y` (gateway.ts:3509) is emitted at the ROUTE-DECISION point, before upstream dispatch. Under a SOFT pin the upstream retry loop can rotate off Y afterwards, so Y is NOT necessarily the account that served the turn. Measured 2026-08-27: a request logged `routed=aviynw3` completed in the ledger as `pin_yield avistorewolf.com`; gw-route timestamps lead the ledger's by ~2s (decision vs served-response).\n\nAUTHORITATIVE served-account instruments, both from `gateway:owner_report { agent }`:\n- `lastRoute {account,model,at}` — written only at the served-response chokepoint.\n- `ledger.recent[]` `ok`/`pin_yield` events plus the `pinYields` counter (recorded at gateway.ts:4424/4679/4951/5362).\n\nA flat `pinYields` across new requests is the gateway attesting it honored the pin, which is the correct way to defeat the \"round-robin would have routed there anyway\" confound.\n\nAn in-memory null (bounded Map, ROUTE_MAP_MAX=4096, delete-oldest) means not-routed-since-restart / evicted / not-gateway-routed — never that the instrument is broken. Establish a positive control with `gateway:owner_report {}` (no agent) before treating any null as a finding.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hud-session-chat-release-audit-2026-08-11","title":"HUD session-chat release audit — the surface with no verdict, driven live to a ship/no-ship call","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-11","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: HUD session-chat release audit — the surface with no verdict, driven live to a ship/no-ship call\nslug: hud-session-chat-release-audit-2026-08-11\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-11\nupdated: 2026-08-12\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** AUDIT COMPLETE, 7/7 done. VERDICT ON 0bbffcb73cce: NO-GO for \"ready to ship to strangers\" — not a claim the product is broken. Happy path passes 6/6. ONE defect remains: machine-authored text renders into the owner's chat pane attributed to the owner as their own speech.\n\n⚠ PROVENANCE CORRECTION (2026-08-12, su-91ace721, wind-down audit). This section previously said \"THE REPORT EXISTS — READ IT, DON'T REWRITE IT\" and gave two references. BOTH ARE DEAD — verified, not assumed: (a) .papercusp/scratch/p007-readiness-report.md does NOT exist (checked home + repo scratch roots and a bounded search; only an unrelated p007-operator-cpuweight is there) — scratch is session-local and was never committed; (b) the claude.ai artifact bd549c76 does NOT resolve (absent from the owning account's 9 published artifacts AND WebFetch returns \"artifact not found\").\n\nWHAT SURVIVES IS THE REPORT NOW: this verdict, root cause D-014, the 65.8% post-fix measurement, the §5 testability defect, and this plan's 18 Decisions — plus the owner delivery itself, coord msg msplilq4 (2026-08-12T04:35:09Z → human), durable in coord_event_log and carrying the verdict inline. The owner HAS the answer; what was lost is the long-form evidence document, not the conclusion.\n\nTWO AMENDMENTS ride on the figures if you re-cite any number: mspabqx7 (window drift confounds the \"~34% closed\" claim) and mspaka0g (two figures need pinned instants; one 22:53Z number does not reproduce). The NO-GO verdict is untouched by both.\n\nROOT CAUSE (D-014): three classifiers of \"did the owner author this turn\" exist in-tree; the owner-facing render path is the WEAKEST. A better deny-list cannot fix it — machine \"Continue from where you left off.\" vs owner-typed \"continue where you left off\" differ by one capital and a period.\n\n**Next:** Nothing on this plan — it is closed, and its work-item residue (WI-37903, WI-37933, WI-37954, WI-37956, WI-37957, WI-37958, WI-37955) was terminalized 2026-08-12 by the fleet leader during wind-down. If you need the full report TEXT before rewriting it, try recovering it from the authoring session first: sessions:search { session:'su-a80b0154-7891-4dc5-82e8-0bdc976c323f', query:'readiness report' } (rev 3 published ~21:12Z 2026-08-11, msg msp5pbgk). The remaining WORK is the FIX — a durable owner-authorship classifier reusing the machine-surface catalogue, plus a fixture feeding un-enveloped text — and belongs on a NEW plan, not here.\n\n## Background\n\nGoal: `the-gui-chat-surface-is-ready-to-ship-to-strange-8fa0ed`.\n\n**THERE ARE TWO CHAT SURFACES. This plan is about one of them.** Getting this wrong wastes the whole plan, so it is the first thing stated:\n\n| surface | what it is | release status |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Papercup chat** | the assistant persona — typed + voice, cards | **Conditional GO already issued** (`papercup-chat-release-grade-loop-2026-07-16`, 4 grade passes against the real desktop app, 7/8 criteria healthy) |\n| **HUD session chat** | the pane where the owner talks to a specific AGENT's session; renders that agent's transcript | **Never graded. No verdict has ever existed.** |\n\n**This plan covers the HUD session chat only.** WI-5174 (voice answered in text) and WI-5175 (dead card options) belong to the Papercup surface and are NOT in scope here — they sit behind a verdict that already exists.\n\n**Why it needs an audit.** On 2026-08-11 the owner said \"hi\" to an agent and the pane rendered Stop-hook coaching walls and tool logs back at him as his own messages. Fixed same day (EI-20135573616431912), with the search-side twin in flight (WI-37883). But that was the pane's FIRST machine-vs-human filter — it is hours old, and nobody except its author has exercised any of this.\n\n**The evidence standard: a verdict needs observation from the running app.** A green unit suite is not evidence that a rendering surface works — that is precisely how this surface arrived at today. Every item reports what was OBSERVED live, with a screenshot or DOM/console capture, or reports that it could not be observed and why.\n\n**The rig.** `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` boots it; `tauri-agent-tools` drives the webview headlessly (probe/eval/dom/click/type/screenshot/check/capture). Playbook: `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e` §0–§2. Do NOT point a browser at :3055/:3070 — that is the retired standalone webapp, it renders wrong, and a PreToolUse hook blocks it.\n\n## Phase 1 — the rig\n\n- **P-001** `done` Stand up an isolated Tauri shell and confirm `tauri-agent-tools` attaches and can drive it: probe, screenshot, read the console. Report the exact attach command that worked so no later item re-derives it. If attaching FAILS, that is the finding — the surface is unverifiable by any agent and the whole goal is blocked on it. importance: high — note: ← WI-37897 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — verify what we believe is already fixed\n\n- **P-002** `done` Live-drive the owner chat happy path: type a message, receive the reply IN THE PANE (not the Inbox), and assert all of — appears ONCE, chronological, above its reply; no turn-origin envelope, no owner-chat note, no `Stop hook feedback:` wall, no raw tool-call list. This is the owner's 2026-08-11 report re-run as an acceptance test. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-37898 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Live-verify the two leak fixes, so far only unit-pinned. (a) Search a term existing ONLY inside a machine wake blob (a nonce, `[await-event]`) and assert ZERO hits reach the owner-facing results. (b) Search a term from a genuine owner turn and assert it DOES hit AND that clicking it anchors the pane to that turn rather than opening at the tail. (b) is likeliest to still be broken — it exercises the deep-link corroboration path, not the filter. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-37899 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — find what nobody has looked for\n\n- **P-004** `done` HUNT for a third leakage surface. Enumerate every owner-facing view rendering `session_turns` or agent transcript text (sync resolvers, HUD boards, dossiers, Inbox, plan Sessions tabs, notifications, exports) and check each against the `ownerVisiblePromptText` allow-list. Two surfaces were found by the owner tripping over them; assume a third and go looking. Deliverable is a list with a verdict per surface, including the clean ones. importance: high — note: ← WI-37900 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Reproduce-or-refute the in-scope open defects against the live build, one evidenced verdict each: WI-6502 (typing lag — re-measure only, do NOT attempt the fix here), EI-13551 (op-chat header flex-squeeze), EI-20130872791260706, EI-11519 (brainstorm turn failures — establish FIRST whether it is this surface or the Papercup one; if Papercup, hand it back and say so). Several are weeks old and may be fixed, dead, or mis-described; a refutation with evidence costs less than fixing the wrong thing. Output is verdicts that SIZE the fix plan — fix nothing here. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-37901 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` The stranger pass: fresh profile, ten minutes, no prior knowledge of this codebase. Record every single thing that reveals internal tooling, confuses, or looks broken — including cosmetics nobody has filed. Most likely item to find what actually stops the release, because everyone who has looked at this surface already knows what it all means. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-37902 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — the verdict\n\n- **P-007** `done` Write the readiness report: per-line evidence, every claim traceable to an observation from P-002..P-006, an explicit ship/no-ship recommendation, and a ranked list of what stands between here and shippable. State what could NOT be verified as plainly as what could. Reconcile explicitly with the Papercup surface's existing conditional GO so the owner gets ONE answer about \"the GUI chat\", not two half-answers. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-37903 done\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Scope corrected to the HUD session chat — the Papercup surface already has a verdict\n\nThe goal was opened as \"the GUI chat surface\" without distinguishing the two. The plan-dedup guard surfaced `papercup-chat-release-grade-loop-2026-07-16` (active, 4 passes, conditional GO), which my own portfolio read had missed because I sorted plans by recency and it fell outside the window.\n\nRe-running a grade loop over a surface that already has a 4-pass verdict would be the reuse-first violation this goal can least afford. So: the Papercup surface is ADOPTED as answered, its residue tracked (EI-12995 typed msgs never render/persist; the TTFT ratification owed to the owner; WI-5071 the structural latency fix), and new effort goes where no verdict exists.\n\nConsequence to carry: two defects I had listed as chat-release blockers — WI-5174 and WI-5175 — are Papercup-surface items sitting behind that GO, not blockers here.\n\n### D-002 Live-drive is the evidence standard, not unit tests\n\nNecessary, not sufficient, for a rendering surface. WI-37883's filter is fully unit-pinned and has still never been seen working by a human. Any item reporting a verdict with no live observation is unfinished.\n\n### D-003 Audit before fix, and recover the parallelism elsewhere\n\nThe in-scope defects span 2026-07-13 to 2026-08-11 and none has been re-checked against the current build. P-005 buys verdicts cheaply and stops us fixing what is no longer broken. The serialization this introduces is paid back by running the owner-requested CONTROLS work (WI-6507 token limit / WI-6509 account pin / WI-6510 model+effort) as a concurrent plan — those are owner-specified and need no audit to begin.\n\n### D-004 — \"npm run dev\" loads :3070 — the RELEASE checkout — so the default rig verifies the OLDEST code on this box, not your fix\nDate: 2026-08-11\n❌ **REFUTED 2026-08-11T19:0xZ by the fleet leader (su-83fe746a). Root cause found, fixed and closed as WI-37907. Do not act on the warning below as stated — it is preserved for the lesson, not the instruction.**\n\n**What I claimed:** that `npm run dev` boots the desktop but loads :3070, the RELEASE checkout, so this plan's audit would verify the OLDEST code on the box and make today's landed fixes look broken.\n\n**What is actually true:** the premise was false. `desktop-dev-nohmr`'s HEADER COMMENT states a devUrl of :3070 — and the same file contradicts it about 50 lines later. I read the comment (via a memory derived from it), not the code. The leader read the code. WI-37907 fixed the lying comment so the next agent cannot inherit this.\n\n**Why this decision still earned its place, and what to keep from it.** The instruction attached to the false premise was: *before writing any verdict from a live drive, PROVE the build under test contains the change.* That instruction is correct independently of why it was given, and following it is exactly what exposed the premise as false. Mechanism-first is a COMPLETENESS CHECK, run second.**\n\n- **Surface-first** — enumerate every owner-facing view that renders `session_turns` or transcript text, by whatever route. Finds bypass surfaces. This is the one that finds what you did not know to look for.\n- **Mechanism-first** — enumerate consumers of the known-broken predicate. Finds every surface that shares a diagnosed defect, fast. Cannot find a bypass.\n\nThey answer different questions and the failure modes are opposite: surface-first can miss a consumer you did not think of; mechanism-first *systematically* misses everything that bypasses. That is the entire mechanism behind \"5 of 18908\", and it is why the refusal's suggestion to look for a shared severity/kind shape among the excluded rows would not have found it.\n\nResolution: spec bumped to revision 4 with `any: [ goal=…, id in ['WI-37908'] ]`. An id-pin is normally the wrong instrument; it was chosen because NO tool sets goal_id on an existing work-item (work_items:update rejects goalId; goals:attach-pot attaches harnesses, not items), and the alternative was mutating canonical attribution by raw SQL to satisfy a filter. Verified admitted: set_claim_spec reported poolEffect matched 1 → 2.\n\n#### Tooling defect found while doing this — EI-20189688839487977\n`scheduler:preview_spec_delta` returned `counts.net: 1` (currentClaimable 1 → proposedClaimable 2, and the tool calls its counts EXACT) alongside `newlyAdmitted: []`, `truncated: false`, and a note reading \"NO CHANGE: the proposed spec admits exactly the same items as the current one.\"\n\nBoth cannot be true, and the reassuring string is the wrong one — `scheduler:set_claim_spec` independently confirmed matched 1 → 2. An agent trusting that note concludes the widen is a no-op and reaches for a worse instrument. Filed with the verbatim payload and a suspected two-evaluator split (cf. EI-18654360178824151). Do not trust that note in this plan's remaining work; read counts.net.\n\n#### Standing caution for this fleet\nTrust exact counts over prose summaries, and verify a \"done\" against the source rather than a carried status. prepare sanitized durable reviewer access and verify it from clean install.… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004739 — P-012 acceptance R-6: configure external Apple signing/App Store Connect/APNs inputs through supported secret injection, validate/export the exact signed IPA, upload to TestFlight and verify processi… <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004740 — P-013 acceptance R-7: resolve beta defects with regressions, submit the verified candidate for App Review, drive actionable review feedback, verify public App Store availability/install/core journey,… <!-- P-013 -->\n## Background\n\nAvi renewed this campaign on 2026-10-01: update the iPhone app for the latest Papercusp platform changes, prepare a public release, enter AUTO, and carry the plan to verified shipped status. This is a continuation of the existing app and plan; P-001 through P-004 retain their historical evidence, and October work must produce fresh evidence rather than treating August passes as current.\n\n## October release scope\n\nExtend the existing SwiftUI/Rust/UniFFI companion in papercup-rust-mobile and the current TypeScript device API in papercusp. Reuse the official mobile-base/iPhone-shell contracts, shared design tokens, device/connected-app access, voice providers, and release entrypoints. Implement directly in this session under AUTO with manual file locks and the repository's managed commit routine. Do not scaffold a second client, restore the retired Tauri mobile client, introduce an embedded fleet, or treat a simulator/unsigned archive as public delivery.\n\nThe release must work with current operator/workspace access and platform contracts. Audit current hosted/account/entitlement behavior and integrate the supported companion flows; any user-visible unsupported mode must be explicit in onboarding and store claims. The app remains a companion to a user-controlled operator rather than a new standalone hosted agent product. Android changes are limited to unavoidable shared Rust or backend compatibility.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Current native client agrees with platform contracts.** Current backend/client compatibility is demonstrated for pairing and revocation, workspace switching, Inbox groups/work-items/system alerts, plans and authority-checked actions, operator chat streaming, current fleet activity, and desktop-local/cloud voice. Each changed contract has a regression in the project's real Rust/Swift/TypeScript suite; a system-alert-only Inbox never says All clear.\n\n**R-2 — Clean-install pairing and recovery work for advertised access modes.** A clean install can discover and pair with a sanitized supported operator through the current Remote access flow, on LAN and cellular/public HTTPS. Expired/revoked credentials and offline/reconnect transitions have understandable recovery. Credentials remain in Keychain and provider secrets stay server-side. Current account/hosted/paid-mode support and any exclusions agree across onboarding, APIs, and store copy.\n\n**R-3 — Exact candidate passes the current-SDK native release matrix.** The exact candidate source revision builds with Apple's current accepted Xcode/iOS SDK, regenerates matching UniFFI slices, passes Rust quality checks, Swift unit tests, and non-zero XCUITest cases with paired flows actually exercised. Unsigned archive, static release/privacy checks, and negative guards are fresh. A continuous manageable CI route reruns these checks after changes.\n\n**R-4 — Signed app passes hardware-only iPhone journeys.** A signed candidate is installed on physical iPhone hardware and passes pairing, real production APNs delivery and cold/warm tap routing, microphone permission deny/allow, cloud consent/revocation, local/cloud voice, Bluetooth/interruption, background/resume, cellular reconnect, and a bounded battery/endurance check. Simulator checks do not substitute for hardware-only properties.\n\n**R-5 — Store packet and reviewer access agree with the candidate.** App Store metadata, icon, candidate screenshots, public privacy/support URLs, data collection/export declarations, third-party SDK disclosures, and distribution rights are complete and agree with the candidate. App Review receives a sanitized internet-reachable environment and an access path valid throughout review, verified from a clean install.\n\n**R-6 — Signed candidate is validated and available through TestFlight.** Apple Developer team, valid Distribution identity and push-enabled provisioning, App Store Connect delivery credentials, and production APNs are configured through external secret injection. The exact signed IPA validates, uploads, completes Apple processing, and is available to intended TestFlight testers with candidate provenance recorded.\n\n**R-7 — Approved public App Store installation proves shipped.** Beta defects are resolved and verified, Apple approves the final candidate, the public App Store listing resolves and permits installation, and a public install passes the advertised core companion journey. Complete the plan's code-truth audit and independent feature-ship acceptance rubric without force waivers, unowned residue, or a false shipped claim.\n\n## Design\n\nKeep the existing three-layer architecture: the TypeScript operator owns authorization, workspace isolation, attention/fleet/plan data and provider secrets; the portable Rust client owns HTTP contracts and recovery; UniFFI carries typed results into thin SwiftUI views. Extend existing response/model cases rather than adding parallel endpoints or alert systems. Preserve additive/legacy response compatibility and regenerate both native binding outputs whenever the UDL changes.\n\nThe Inbox uses one shared attention count for its header and tab badge, includes typed system alerts ahead of existing work-item/group cards, and derives emptiness from every represented layer. Tests distinguish alert-only, empty legacy, mixed attention, unknown additive fields and revoked access. Current operator/account modes are reconciled through the existing device/connected-app authorization seam; no provider credential enters the app.\n\nVerification uses the existing iPhone-shell Mac runner and source-isolated current-SDK hosted gate. The platform desktop-native route builds Tauri and does not fit this SwiftUI app; retain that distinction. Build snapshots are immutable disposable candidate runtimes, not new editable app checkouts. Existing app release scripts own static metadata checks and signed export/Apple validation/upload. Store/reviewer changes reuse existing documents and the sanitized companion operator. Final beta/store/public acceptance remains on the exact signed artifact.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-006, P-007 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-008 | live |\n| R-3 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-010 | live |\n| R-5 | P-011 | live |\n| R-6 | P-012, P-005 | live |\n| R-7 | P-013 | live |\n\n## Execution and external dependencies\n\nSequence: establish the current release baseline and test route; fix API/UI drift; verify public onboarding and secure access; produce a fresh current-SDK archive; finish real-device acceptance and store collateral; export/validate/upload the signed TestFlight candidate; resolve beta findings, submit, and verify public release. Prepare Apple/account/store work alongside independent engineering in this session.\n\nApple credentials, physical-device access, copyright-holder distribution permission, and Apple review are external dependencies only when measured unavailable; do not fabricate them or silently waive acceptance. Finish every independent engineering/preparation step before asking Avi for a concrete owner-only action. The current grant authorizes TestFlight/App Store release actions for this app once candidate checks pass, but does not authorize purchases, accepting legal agreements for Avi, exposing private workspace data, or publishing unrelated source.\n\nContinue via a tracked warm work loop tied to this plan. On an external wait, use an exact event/explicit bounded recheck with a named next action and stop condition; never babysit a peer-owned live gate. Use staging/current-build for development. Final shipped means verified public App Store availability, not a plan checkbox, a local build, a successful upload, or a TestFlight beta.\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate.
