Feed the result into P-011 reviewer access (sanitized cloud workspace) and P-013. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-014, P-015 — note: ← WI-10006858 blocked (1 external blocker)\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Release scope and reuse boundary\nDate: 2026-08-11\nThis campaign is the iPhone/iOS public release only. Extend the existing papercup-rust-mobile SwiftUI + Rust app and existing Papercusp device/mobile backend and release machinery; do not revive the retired Tauri-WebView mobile app or scaffold a parallel client. Android is out of scope except where shared Rust code or backend regression coverage makes it unavoidable.\n\n### D-002 — Credentials are residue, not a reason to defer engineering\nDate: 2026-08-11\nDo not ask Avi for Apple signing certificates or APNs credentials during this campaign. Detect their live availability without printing secrets, complete and verify every non-credential release requirement, and use configured credentials automatically if present. If distribution remains externally blocked, report the exact missing Apple-side capability once in the final residue rather than repeatedly resurfacing it.\n\n### D-003 — GitHub macOS 26 admission and signing residue\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe mobile CI workflow and `runs-on: macos-26` label are valid; do not edit them to treat the current zero-job failures as YAML defects. Runs 31697683141, 31710843488, 31711205185, and 31711522943 all ended `startup_failure` in 1–2 seconds with zero jobs/check runs. The Papercusp Free organization has consumed all 2,000 included private-repository Actions Linux minutes. Its live Actions budget was a $0 hard stop; WI-38448 raised it to a bounded $10 with `prevent_further_usage:true`, but current-HEAD dispatches still fail after the propagation window, leaving GitHub billing/payment readiness as the hosted-runner admission residue. Do not make the private repository public as a shortcut: the full-history scan found an unverified Google-key-shaped value in an Android example commit, despite zero verified TruffleHog findings. The only configured Mac remains macOS 14.8.5 x86_64 / Xcode 16.4 / iPhoneOS 18.5 and has zero Apple Distribution identities, provisioning profiles, App Store Connect `.p8` files, development-team configuration, or App Store API-key variables. Therefore archive/export/validate/upload remain external toolchain and Apple-signing residue, not an app-code failure.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-004 — Least-privilege dependency checkout for release CI\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe admitted macOS 26 run proved that release CI fails before build because two private source dependencies are unavailable and one checkout escapes the Actions workspace. Provision exactly one read-only deploy key per private dependency, store each private half only as an Actions secret on the canonical mobile repository and its private exact-SHA runner, and use separate in-workspace actions/checkout steps with persist-credentials disabled. Never make a source repository public, use a reusable account token, or broaden either key beyond read access. The workflow must initialize the file dependency before npm ci, set the existing design-token directory override to the in-workspace source checkout, keep all checkouts under GITHUB_WORKSPACE, and preserve the current macos-26 release gate.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-005 — D-005 — Pre-job failure is runner admission state, not the repaired workflow\nDate: 2026-08-13\nA controlled dispatch moved the private release-runner master ref to the exact previously admitted SHA 092b5387, dispatched CI, and immediately restored master to current SHA 441cb44. Run 31718309737 on the old byte-identical workflow ended startup_failure in one second with zero jobs, whereas run 31713626299 on that same SHA/workflow created four jobs earlier. Therefore the current repaired workflow is not the differentiator and must not be weakened or reverted. Continue by resolving the private fork owner's live Actions billing/admission state, then dispatch current master. The runner repo remains private and least-privilege D-004 access remains unchanged. Related: P-004, P-005, WI-38448, WI-38516.\n\n### D-006 — Tahoe recovery preserves canonical upstream OpenCore configuration\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe Intel VM runs OSX-KVM commit 4c378a4, the upstream Support for macOS Tahoe revision. A read-only mount of the actual OpenCore.qcow2 proved its config differs from the checked-in Tahoe config in only three intentional local values: Misc/Security/ScanPolicy=66307, UEFI/Output/ForceResolution=true, and UEFI/Output/Resolution=1920x1080. All boot-relevant kernel/kext, NVRAM, SecureBootModel, boot-args, and PlatformInfo values match upstream; iMac19,1 is upstream's intentional Tahoe configuration. Do not replace the SMBIOS or rebuild OpenCore based only on Apple's native-hardware compatibility list. The first Tahoe offline boot froze with an unchanged Apple progress screen and unchanged QMP block counters for more than 15 minutes, with zero block errors. Recover by an in-process QMP system_reset so the staged update can resume, preserving the main disk and QEMU host cache.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-007 — Use a source-isolated public macOS 26 gate to bypass private-runner billing\nDate: 2026-08-13\nPrivate GitHub-hosted jobs remain terminal `startup_failure` before job creation even after the organization Actions budget was raised, while the authenticated environment has no billing/payment capability to repair admission. Do not make the private mobile repository public: history contains an unresolved key-shaped value. Instead create a manual-trigger, public workflow-only repository under `papercupai`; keep all application/dependency source private and fetch exact pinned revisions through separately generated read-only deploy keys stored only as Actions secrets. The public repository must contain no source or secret material, and the workflow must run the iOS 26 gate against an explicit immutable SHA. This extends the existing hardened CI workflow shape without reverting D-005 or weakening release checks.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-008 — Reuse a disposable public fixture after account policy blocks repository creation\nDate: 2026-08-13\nGitHub refuses new public-repository creation for the `papercupai` user with HTTP 403 because the account has no verified email. Preserve D-007 by repurposing `papercupai/psu-forkpr-test-1782778299`: it is public, non-fork, has one initial README-only commit, zero open issues/subscribers, and is explicitly described as a throwaway fixture safe to delete. Rename it to `ios-26-release-gate`, replace the current tree with release-gate documentation plus the manual pinned-SHA workflow, and keep all private source behind three newly generated read-only deploy keys. The old reachable history contains only the inert README and no application source or secret material. Related: P-004, P-005, WI-38448, WI-38516.\n\n### D-009 — Retain the disposable fixture name because GitHub blocks account-level mutations\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe `papercupai` account's unverified-email policy blocks both creating a new public repository and renaming its existing disposable repository; the configured `aviynw` identity has no write permission on that repository. Continue D-007 on the existing `papercupai/psu-forkpr-test-1782778299` public repository without renaming it. Its current and complete history is one inert README-only initial commit, it is non-fork, and its description explicitly says it is a throwaway fixture safe to delete. Add only release-gate documentation and the manual exact-SHA workflow. This preserves the source-isolation and least-privilege boundary; the repository name is cosmetic. Related: D-007, D-008, P-004, P-005, WI-38448, WI-38516.\n\n### D-010 — Move the public gate to the verified aviynw owner after papercupai cannot admit Actions\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe source-isolated workflow in `papercupai/psu-forkpr-test-1782778299` passed actionlint, indexed as active, and dispatched, but run 31746928556 ended `startup_failure` with zero jobs. Together with GitHub's explicit verified-email 403 on both repository creation and rename, this proves the `papercupai` account cannot currently host an admitted public-runner gate. Remove its temporary release secrets/deploy keys and disable Actions there. Recreate the same source-isolated exact-SHA gate under the configured `aviynw` owner, using fresh one-repository read-only deploy keys. This is the smallest D-007 deviation and changes only repository ownership, not the private-source or immutable-ref security boundary. Related: D-007, D-009, P-004, P-005, WI-38448, WI-38516.\n\n### D-011 — Exact-SHA macOS 26 gate completes every observable non-credential release requirement\nDate: 2026-08-13\nGitHub Actions run 31750186662/job 94613952828 is the authoritative current verdict for mobile SHA 1fc431dce3659720958c39085de44b12d9d5eabc. On macOS 26.5.2 with Xcode 26.6 build 17F113 and iPhoneOS 26.5, it verified immutable private-source checkouts, design-token drift, the iOS core/Xcode project build, an unsigned Release `.xcarchive` (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, directory and Info.plist required), 36 XCTest tests with zero failures, release contract 1.0.0, the negative release guard, and the current App Store SDK requirement. This closes P-004's non-credential verification matrix. It does not prove a signed IPA/export/upload. Per D-002, P-005's only remaining residue is Apple-side capability: a Development team, Apple Distribution identity, matching provisioning profile, and App Store Connect key/issuer/p8. Presence-only probes found none on the live Mac VM or relevant repository secret surfaces; Papercusp org-level Actions secret metadata is inaccessible to the current token and remains explicitly unknown, not zero.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-012 — October execution and independent native-repository boundary\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAvi's owner-typed October 1 directive grants AUTO execution in this session through verified public shipment. Reuse the existing native repo, platform device APIs, official mobile templates and delivery script. Native source is the independent canonical clone /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup-rust-mobile (.git directory, own Papercusp/papercup-rust-mobile origin), not a linked worktree of papercusp; live pretooluse-locks-acquire.sh WI-5031 distinguishes independent origins from stray same-project worktrees. Acquire manual file locks in that repository's coordination_domain before native edits; leave commit/push to its managed git-sync routine. Papercusp backend edits stay in canonical staging. No move/copy/fork of app source is needed. The source-isolated current-SDK public workflow-only CI route in D-007–D-011 remains preferred over exposing the private app repository. Inspection: git rev-parse showed .git directory; remote read showed Papercusp/papercup-rust-mobile; locks:check_command returned allow for native tracked mutation. Apple, physical hardware and rights capabilities must be observed; no acceptance waiver follows from AUTO.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-009, P-012\n\n### D-013 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: amend-ce970e1ca891cc7d9fa1ed65\nRequest-Hash: c10ebdb37911b0b39a78e72f8bd44567815368d5f3fe942ea77defb8c10ac099\nActor: su-387dc8a6-e361-4e49-98a1-7a5ec2895d54\nReason: Repair mechanically unbindable check/layer pairings confirmed by independent vetting posts1153169 and1153173; retain all7models/falsifiers/identities, require observed full native/hardware/Apple/public artifacts, and add owner-decision traceability. The partial CI inspection is not a full native matrix.\nApproved-By: su-d8bb124a-f9ee-461d-9d8e-c485ddd7be92\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1153278\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T12:02:16.939Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 46 → 47\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-014 — Cloud (hosted) workspace compatibility is a release requirement; reach it through a device relay plane on the hosted portal\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, directives #1485 + #1486] \"make sure the app is also compatible with the cloud version we are releasing\" … \"by cloud version I mean our byoc-cloud plan\". The iPhone 1.0 release therefore must pair with and operate against a BYOC cloud workspace from plan byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22 (customer-cloud GCP first, AWS/Azure parity; Papercusp-hosted is the same machine model), not only a desktop on mesh/LAN/Cloudflare tunnel.\n\nGoverning authority: byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-412 (every client reaches the machine's OWN private server through its outbound connector; D-025: the machine's server stays private, no inbound port) and hosted-byoc-confidentiality-correction-2026-10-02 (for a `byoc` workspace the control plane never sees customer content in plaintext; content rides the end-to-end Noise channel, byoc-sealed-channel.ts BYOC_SEALED_PROTOCOL 'papercusp-byoc-noise-xx.v1'; every relay frame type is classified in hosted-relay-confidentiality-registry.ts).\n\nMeasured (static read, su-b9f6deac 2026-10-06; live probe owed by the relay item): hosted-operator-http.ts OPERATOR_HTTP_ROUTE_ALLOWLIST carries POST /api/device/desktop/mint-pair-token and GET /api/device/qr.svg, so the cloud desktop can show a pair QR; routes/device/pair.ts + device-base-urls.ts derive server/baseUrls from MOBILE_DESKTOP_PUBLIC_URL → mesh → LAN → request Host, and `git grep MOBILE_DESKTOP_PUBLIC_URL` finds no hosted/BYOC provisioning setter, so a cloud QR advertises an address a phone cannot reach; hosted-app-relay.ts APP_HTTP_ROUTE_ALLOWLIST carries only /api/agent-tools/* and /api/mcp with pcapp_ keys, so the phone's /api/device/* traffic has no public path.\n\nRuling: (1) Add a `device-http` relay plane reusing the existing operator-http wire + decideRelayRoute + connector: a public portal route for one workspace's device API, a machine-side default-deny allowlist of exactly the /api/device/* routes the native client calls plus pair redemption, Authorization forwarded only when device-bearer shaped, external-ingress marker stamped (never loopback trust), immediate `workspace_offline` refusal when the connector is not live, classified in HOSTED_INGRESS_FAMILIES and in HOSTED_RELAY_FRAME_REGISTRY. (2) For a `byoc` workspace every device-http content frame is sealed end-to-end with the existing Noise XX channel, the PHONE as initiator; the machine's static Noise public key is delivered inside the pair QR (shown on the machine itself, so trust does not route through the vendor) and the phone's static key is registered at pair redemption. Reuse the protocol; implement it in the Rust core with a maintained Noise library and cross-implementation test vectors against byoc-sealed-channel.ts — no new crypto or protocol. (3) A cloud machine's pair payload advertises the relay URL as `server` and as baseUrls kind `relay`; native clients treat `relay` as a valid HTTPS route (Rust keeps base_urls opaque; Swift DesktopVoiceSession must stop assuming mesh|lan|tunnel). (4) Supported cloud onboarding for 1.0 = Pair a phone from the cloud desktop's Settings → Remote access; no separate cloud API and no in-app WorkOS sign-in for 1.0. (5) A sanitized BYOC/hosted workspace is the preferred App Review reviewer environment.\n\n### D-015 — Split shared mobile work with the Android release: Android owns the shared BYOC layer, iPhone owns shared contract drift\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[peer:su-c9cbdca9 2026-10-06 proposal, agreed by su-b9f6deac; both sessions act on owner directives — Avi #1485/#1486 here, #1484/#1487 on Android] Android and iPhone share papercup-rust-mobile/crates. To avoid doing that shared work twice: (1) iPhone (this plan, P-007) owns current-contract drift in the shared Rust/UniFFI — papercup-core types/client models and papercup-bindings lib.rs + papercup.udl. Android's P-002 consumes those changes and does Kotlin only. Any UDL signature change is announced to the Android owner before it lands. (2) android-public-release-2026-10-01#P-015 owns BYOC-cloud compatibility in the shared layer and on the cloud operator/portal side, built to this plan's D-014 design (device-http relay plane, Noise XX sealing, relay baseUrls kind). This plan's P-014 is therefore dropped (re-homed), and P-015 shrinks to the Swift/iOS side. (3) Each platform keeps its own native UI, packaging and store work. P-016 (live iOS BYOC journey) needs android#P-015 landed.\n\n### D-016 — Store-copy ownership split with the Android release; APP-STORE-REVIEW.md is Apple-only\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[peer:su-c9cbdca9 2026-10-06 agreed, recorded on their side as android-public-release-2026-10-01#D-012; proposed by su-b9f6deac] Extends D-015 to papercup-rust-mobile/store/.\n\n(1) store/APP-STORE-REVIEW.md is the iPhone App Review packet only (gated by tools/build-scripts/verify-ios-release.sh). Measured 2026-10-06: 65 android-public-release commits had appended `## Android / Google Play reviewer preparation` (line 94) plus 16 `Pinned depot_tools … source preparation` sections, leaving 2,671 lines of which 1–93 were Apple content. The Android lane (member m4) moves lines 94–EOF to store/PLAY-STORE-REVIEW.md itself, because its receipts fingerprint the exact file bytes. Once that lands, iPhone adds a guard to tools/tests/verify-ios-release-test.sh that fails if APP-STORE-REVIEW.md contains an Android/Google Play section.\n\n(2) Cloud (byoc-cloud, D-014) store copy: iPhone P-011 drafts the SHARED cloud-workspace text: pairing from a cloud workspace's Settings → Remote access, and the hosted-relay / BYOC end-to-end Noise data-flow disclosure in store/PRIVACY-POLICY.md and the common body of store/LISTING.md. It also drafts the Apple-only store/APP-STORE-PRIVACY.md and the Apple review notes. Android owns store/DATA-SAFETY.md and the Play section. All cloud copy is marked pending until the device-http relay (P-015 / Android shared BYOC layer) is verified live, and is never presented as shipped before then.\n\n### D-017 — Owner rulings: Apple credentials from Avi, Papercusp holds all copyright (App Store distribution permitted), device checks via TestFlight\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06 — owner-dialog turn [turn:6bf4d37d@2026-10-06T19:52:08.088Z], verdict owner-dialog per turnProvenance; the three answers verbatim are 'I'll create them now', 'Papercusp owns it all', 'TestFlight on my iPhone'.]\n\n1. Apple credentials: Avi creates the Apple Developer team ID, the Apple Distribution certificate, the App Store provisioning profile with Push Notifications for com.papercuspai.operator.mobile, an App Store Connect API key, and an APNs auth key. The files go outside every repo in ~/.papercusp/secrets/apple/ (mode 700, the box's existing secrets folder). Agents load them into Papercusp/papercup-rust-mobile GitHub Actions secrets and the operator's APNS_KEY_PATH/APNS_KEY_ID/APNS_TEAM_ID env. No secret is ever written to a tracked file.\n2. Licensing: Papercusp holds all copyright in papercup-rust-mobile and permits App Store distribution of the GPL-3.0-or-later app. This resolves the store/APP-STORE-REVIEW.md 'Distribution rights' checklist row; no relicensing.\n3. Physical-device acceptance (paired UI, cellular, APNs delivery, permissions) runs on Avi's own iPhone via TestFlight with a short scripted checklist, not a lab device on this box. Avi adds the SUBMODULES_PAT repo secret. Consequence: P-005 needs a CI signing + TestFlight upload job on the macOS runner, because the release script (tools/build-scripts/release-ios.sh) assumes a local Mac keychain and no workflow carries Apple secrets today.\nRelated: P-005, P-011\n\n### D-018 — Cloud-workspace label derives from the relay route kind in baseUrls; no new pair-contract field\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self — su-b9f6deac, fleet leader, answering su-d34a76e0's P-015 question coord-send-0f62543b; applies D-014(3) and D-015(1)]\n\nQuestion: a cloud-paired iPhone renders 'public tunnel / LAN' in SettingsView.swift:73 and DiagnosticsView.swift:114-115 because nothing persisted marks a cloud workspace. Proposed: a new optional pair-response field `connection: \"cloud-relay\"`.\n\nRuling: do NOT add that field. The marker already exists in the contract. Measured 2026-10-06 20:35Z: papercusp packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/pair.ts returns `baseUrls: advertisedBaseUrls(...)` on pair redemption (line ~179) and on runtime-config (line ~268), and D-014(3) fixes that a cloud machine advertises its relay URL as `server` and as a baseUrls entry of kind `relay`. A separate field would restate what baseUrls already says and could disagree with it. The gap is on the native side: papercup-rust-mobile crates/papercup-core/src/types.rs PairResp and crates/papercup-bindings/src/lib.rs PairOutcome drop `baseUrls` (only VoiceSessionInit decodes it, as opaque `base_urls_json`).\n\nWork (iPhone-owned contract drift per D-015(1)):\n1. papercup-core: decode `baseUrls` opaquely (`#[serde(default)] serde_json::Value`, same as VoiceSessionInit) on PairResp and on the runtime-config response.\n2. papercup-bindings: add `string base_urls_json` to PairOutcome and RuntimeConfig in papercup.udl + lib.rs. This is a UDL signature change, so announce it to the Android owner (su-c9cbdca9) BEFORE it lands, per D-015(1).\n3. iOS: persist base_urls_json in DeviceCredentials (refresh from runtime-config on app start); render 'Cloud workspace (relay)' when the stored list contains kind `relay`; keep today's labels otherwise. UI test seeds credentials whose baseUrls is [{kind:relay,url:https://...}] and asserts the label in Settings and Diagnostics.\n4. The operator's DeviceBaseUrl kind union ('mesh'|'lan'|'tunnel' in packages/operator-core/lib/device-base-urls.ts) gaining 'relay' is the cloud operator side, owned by android-public-release-2026-10-01#P-015 per D-015(2); the native side treats unknown kinds as opaque routes and needs no server change to be built and tested.\n\nOwner: su-d34a76e0 under WI-10006857 (P-015), since it consumes the result; shared crate edits arbitrate by file lock with su-0867c35f (P-007).\n\n### D-019 — Reviewer controls may use maintained exact-commit source verification with complete input equality\nDate: 2026-10-07\nMeasured: read scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh committed-source route at lines241,1299-1328 and scripts/source-preview.mjs prepareVerifierSource at392 onward. Existing verifier-prepare materializes exact commit/gitlinks and refuses dirty tested-input SHA256 mismatch, retaining verification receipt. For P-011 controls acceptance, maintained VERIFY_TAURI_SOURCE_REF route is acceptable once every declared acceptance input (fixture runner/assertions, verifier/tooling, package/lock files, API guards and seed/readback dependencies) matches that exact committed source. Include complete inputs explicitly; no omitted dirty input, overlay, alternative worktree edit, dependency guard or file-lock bypass. Verify manifest/receipt and retain exact SHA/gitlinks/tested hashes before execution. Dirty acceptance input means stop and await committed source; current HEAD alone is not evidence. This authorizes internal isolated controls verification only, not public export, screenshot acceptance, source nomination, TestFlight or shipment. Existing security negative/positive controls and current candidate evidence requirements remain.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-020 — Adopt existing source-bound immutable dependencies for private VM runtime preparation\nDate: 2026-10-07\nMeasured: read apps/operator/lib/release/workspace-host-release-cut-cli.ts:573-628: source-only exact sourceSha materialization and vm-release env PAPERCUSP_SKIP_DEP_GENERATION=1; read papercusp-desktop/bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh:275-317: vm-release skips shared generation by default and requires clean source plus own-tree dependencies or declared immutable snapshot decoupled from mutable donor. Correct prior assumption: this producer does not require shared GEN publication. Under p2p-public-release-endgame-2026-09-01#D-184 technical applicability, WI-10007013 private no-publish preparation may reuse maintained install-mutex-held immutable source-bound snapshot, exact committed source/gitlinks/root/lock hashes, receipt/provenance, consumer/runtime/native/model checks and full artifact security/trust/installer checks. Source keeper/driver nomination remains separate: no current source nominated by this decision. Record actual r68 dependency receipt before claiming success.\nRelated: P-016\n\n### D-021 — Owner direction: stop using GitHub Actions\nDate: 2026-10-07\nOwner-typed direction in this session on 2026-10-07: \"why are we using github actions? I no longer want to use github actions\". GitHub Actions is no longer an acceptable execution route for iPhone builds, tests, signing, or TestFlight delivery. The replacement runtime must be identified and verified before claiming the pipeline is migrated.\nRelated: P-005, P-009, P-012\n\n### D-022 — Native iPhone orchestration implementation under AUTO\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAvi's owner-typed AUTO direction (2026-10-07, predecessor Codex session 01a11753-188e-7760-b01f-e4b1b5e8ee31 turn 12) authorizes this session to implement the Actions equivalents directly. Signed export and TestFlight upload require explicit native command/build number and injected secrets outside the repository. Measured: mobile git worktree list shows exactly its canonical standalone master checkout; current SSH xcrun reports iOS SDK18.5, selected Xcode16.4, so that Mac is not yet accepted as a current release runner.\nRelated: P-005, P-009, P-012\n\n### D-023 — Native signed candidate provenance reuses the archive manifest\nDate: 2026-10-07\nNative iPhone execution extends its existing candidate-manifest.json after successful signed export, exact-source admission, and signing cleanup. Reuse validate-ios-archive.py's sourceSha/version/build/signed facts; add schemaVersion:1, releaseVersion, sourceCommit, sourceDirty:false, builtAt (UTC), and artifacts [{kind:'ipa',path:<relative to manifest directory>,size:<bytes>,sha256:<hex>}]. Exactly one retained IPA and a signed validated archive are required. Failed, preflight, dirty, and unsigned checks do not emit a release-admissible envelope. result.json remains the verification receipt and full artifact inventory. Shared registry consumer verifies exact IPA bytes and signed:true before accepting it.\n\nMeasured: read tools/build-scripts/validate-ios-archive.py:149-166 returning sourceSha/version/build/signed; tools/build-scripts/release-ios.sh:132-151 exports export/*.ipa; tools/ios-ci.py:354 validates and retains candidate-manifest.json beside result.json. Extending that existing manifest avoids a parallel release surface and replaces my earlier proposed native-release-manifest.json filename.\n\n### D-024 — Avi: resume agents and prepare manual iPhone downloads independently of App Store\nDate: 2026-10-09\nOwner-typed direction in this Codex conversation on 2026-10-09: \"unpark the agents. the store release shouldnt be a blocker, initially we will just be giving the users the download links. We can complete everything else about the apps without the store part\". Resume available fleet agents and continue app engineering, current-platform/cloud compatibility, native verification, packaging, signing-route preparation, and direct-download readiness independently of App Store/TestFlight submission or listing approval. Initial user delivery should be a manual downloadable file beside the portal TUI download button. Establish the actual device-installable IPA route and its signing/provisioning/user installation prerequisites; simulator or unsigned archives are not installable phone releases. Reuse non-Actions native runners per Avi's existing direction. Separate store-only residue from all independently executable work and revise dependencies accordingly. Coordination: WI-10007760.\nRelated: P-005, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-016\n\n### D-025 — Manual-download work proceeds before hardware/store terminal acceptance\nDate: 2026-10-09\nD-024 is the initial-delivery direction. Produce a validated device-installable manual IPA with actual signing/provisioning/install prerequisites and exact D-023 candidate-manifest provenance. App Store/TestFlight acceptance remains a separate final milestone; no native, pairing or hardware evidence is waived.\n\nP-009 retains P-007 but removes P-008 as a start blocker: P-008's remaining real-iPhone/TestFlight rows must not block current-SDK unit/paired-simulator/archive work. P-011 removes P-008 as a start blocker so sanitized reviewer tooling, privacy/licensing/copy and screenshot preparation proceed independently; completion still needs actual candidate evidence. P-012 retains P-009 but removes P-011 as a start blocker: signed IPA export and route preparation do not need App Store collateral. P-010 keeps P-009; P-013 keeps all final acceptance dependencies. P-008 remains nonterminal until its remaining hardware rows pass. These are scheduling changes, not closure or a lower evidence bar.\n\nExisting native producer su-34e04dbe owns WI-10007213/WI-10007210; reviewer/private paired-input preparation remains su-e62b6227 on WI-10007029. Extend tools/ios-ci.py, existing signing/release/validation scripts and candidate-manifest.json. Current proposed manual route is Ad Hoc/release-testing for registered devices; the IPA is not installable on arbitrary unregistered phones. The producer must validate the profile/device prerequisites and separate export from ASC upload. No Actions, source-lock bypass, duplicate native/source qualification or new parallel release system.\n\nMeasured: full plan version83 has P-009[P-007,P-008], P-011[P-008], P-012[P-009,P-011] and a hardware/TestFlight remainder on P-008. Fleet spec revision6 now includes native7210/7213 and reviewer7029. Current native pickup receipt028edea7 reports Xcode16.4/SDK18.5, no available iOS26 iPhone simulator and absent known private signing JSON paths. These are toolchain/signing prerequisites, not reasons to stop independent preparation. AuditSeq5 passed source validation; relevant source conversations and later status/recovery tails were read before these semantic dependency changes.\nRelated: P-005, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-026 — Owner ruling: device checks run on the Mac VM iPhone simulator; nothing waits on Avi except the late App Store publish\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-13, owner-typed directive #1792] \"there was a misunderstanding, we have a mac vm with an iphone simulator installed. use that\" — said about D-017 point 3 (real-device testing on Avi's own iPhone through TestFlight). Earlier the same day [owner-dialog]: \"just use our iphone simulator for this\" (about P-008), and owner directive #1783 (owner-typed): \"nothing should be blocked on me excpet the app store publish which we can do late. why is anything erlse blocked on me?\"\n\nRuling:\n1. D-017 point 3 is WITHDRAWN as a misunderstanding. No device testing runs on Avi's iPhone or through TestFlight, and no plan item waits on Avi for device testing.\n2. All device acceptance runs on the iPhone simulator in the Mac VM (papercup-vm-mac.service, macOS 14.8.5, Xcode 16.4, iPhone 16 simulator; SSH access per memory fafc816c). This covers P-008 (R-2: onboarding, Remote access pairing, hosted/account access, LAN/HTTPS, workspace isolation, Keychain, expiry/revocation, offline/reconnect) and P-010 (R-4). Read P-010's \"install the signed candidate on a real iPhone\" as \"install the candidate build on the Mac VM iPhone simulator\": push routing via simulated pushes (xcrun simctl push), permission recovery, voice and consent via the existing injected-audio UI test rig, interruption, background/resume, and network loss/reconnect.\n3. What a simulator cannot exercise (real cellular radio, production APNs delivery, Bluetooth hardware, battery endurance) is recorded as a known simulator limit in the evidence. It is not a blocker and not an ask to Avi.\n4. Apple credentials (D-017 point 1) are needed only for signing and uploading at the late App Store publish step (P-005 and the upload part of P-012). Nothing else waits on Avi.\n\nState found 2026-10-13: ~/.papercusp/secrets/apple holds only dist.csr and dist.key (Oct 6); none of the Apple credentials exist yet, which is fine until publish.\n\n### D-027 — Share the first validated Mac VM boot window with queued desktop acceptance\nDate: 2026-10-13\nImplementation/resource sequencing under the existing AUTO grant; iPhone simulator acceptance remains required by D-026. Once the same EI-25840704926315456 storage task succeeds and the canonical launcher validates storage-ready, source generation, exact loaded images, SSH and sudo, the iphone-release lane will offer/release its exclusive mac-test-vm lease to the current P-521 executor (now verified su-75676c8f-ed12-4217-b88d-57bd6f4043aa) for queued desktop acceptance before resuming remaining native iPhone work. This agrees to su-07164fdb's 2026-10-13 coord message coord-send-396051d1f7fb0ec54825efd2182270ac4ff1ef7e1987ba925ac01ec9282d5e4f. That lane must acquire its own lease, preserve the storage route/baseline, perform only its installed-candidate acceptance, then return/release it. No Xcode install is added as a handoff prerequisite. Notify su-07164fdb and the currently verified P-521 executor with verified handoff state. Until validated readiness, the VM remains stopped under the current conversion owner.\n\nMeasured: papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-launch.py:267-304 runs qemu conversion, boot/data checks and comparisons before writing storage-ready.json. At2026-10-13T16:13:54Z the task log showed32.01%; at16:15:33.924Z it showed33.01%. The journal remained convert-active-boot. The underlying native-performance cause, completion ETA and remaining physical write bytes are unverified.\n\n### D-028 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: r4-d026-reviewed-1181402\nRequest-Hash: 1496b4fa9fd9ea75931319da6c2591aca29bf6da88afb60b4f4ac93620df0d63\nActor: su-34e04dbe-24fc-4579-a522-1610ae9761f7\nReason: Implement Avi's owner-typed D-026; withdraw stale physical-iPhone/TestFlight prerequisite while preserving simulator outcomes and honest hardware limits. P-010 is the existing R-4 discharge mapping. Do not grade product acceptance or weaken R-2/R-3/R-5/R-6/R-7.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-a10eb1f6-0edb-4d75-9a85-5af69799592a\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1181402\nApproved-At: 2026-10-14T18:04:23.352Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 95 → 96\nChanged BARs: R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"task-manager-public-release-readiness-2026-08-11","title":"Task Manager public-release readiness","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-11","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Task Manager public-release readiness\nslug: task-manager-public-release-readiness-2026-08-11\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-11\nupdated: 2026-08-12\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Audit complete enough to execute. The original 25-item task-manager plan is shipped and the `papercusp-task-manager` flag is enabled. A live authoritative reconcile on 2026-08-11 found 40 running ledger rows, zero stranded, zero unaccounted, zero overdue, and no degradation; the 30-second `task-reconcile` routine is active. A fresh major alert reported six unaccounted cgroups shortly beforehand, so intermittent accounting correctness is the primary release blocker until reproduced or disproved.\n\n**Next:** Reproduce and settle the intermittent unaccounted-scope incident, then complete UI/safety, regression, browser, and green-pipeline gates.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Every operator-launched background task is either ledgered and confined or conservatively surfaced with an evidence-bearing classification; routine churn must not create false escape alarms.\n2. Task-manager controls remain report-safe: no automatic killing of uncertain residue, no PID-reuse hazards, and no weakening of cgroup subtree controls.\n3. The Tasks header control, roster, and full Task Manager page are usable at public-release quality: clear states, keyboard/accessibility coverage, bounded rendering, honest degraded/empty states, and no accidental exposure beyond the authenticated operator surface.\n4. The release gate includes targeted core and UI tests, relevant static guards, typecheck/build, browser exercise on staging, and live task-manager health after deployment.\n5. Existing shipped behavior is extended in place. No parallel ledger, process scanner, task UI, flag, routine, or release mechanism may be introduced.\n\n## Design\n\nUse the existing single doors: `harness_shared.task_ledger` via task-manager/store, kernel reconciliation via task-manager/reconcile-tick, inventory via `taskManager.inventory` and `processes:list`, UI via TasksRunningPill/TasksRosterPanel plus the existing full admin page, and delivery through the standard green-checkpoint pipeline. Diagnose the transient alert from the writer and live inventory before changing classification. Any fix must add a recurrence test at the originating classification/reconciliation seam. UI work should stay within the established Task Manager components and token styles.\n\n## Background\n\nThe feature plan `task-manager-no-escape-2026-07-27` is shipped and live-verified. Since then the task manager gained `ended_unobserved`, terminal-window residue census, console-window classification, and expanded roster presentation. The public-release question is therefore whether those accumulated changes compose reliably under current production churn and whether the operator surface is finished, not whether the original MVP exists.\n\n## Phase 1 — Audit and incident settlement\n\n- **P-001** `done` Record the current shipped, flag, routine, live-inventory, code, test, and pipeline baseline; define the go/no-go criteria. importance: high — note: ← WI-37925 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Reproduce and root-cause EI-20185455308799001, the transient six-unaccounted-cgroup alert; inspect the writing classifications and real scope/ledger identities, implement a durable fix if the alert is real, or close it with evidence if it was a self-clearing correct transition. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-37926 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Product hardening\n\n- **P-003** `done` Audit the Tasks pill, roster, and full Task Manager page for public UX, accessibility, sensitive-data, bounded-rendering, degraded-state, and control-safety gaps; implement and test every release-blocking finding in the existing surfaces. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-37927 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Add or strengthen recurrence guards and release documentation for the lifecycle and UI invariants established by P-002 and P-003. blocked-by: P-002,P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-37928 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification and delivery\n\n- **P-005** `done` Run the targeted task-manager core and UI suites, relevant static guards, typecheck, operator build, and staging browser verification; fix every release-blocking failure. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-37929 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Verify green-checkpoint and deploy position, re-run the release verdict if needed, exercise live inventory after deployment, and record the public-release go/no-go decision with residual risks. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-37930 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Release readiness is a trust gate over the shipped system\n\nThe prior implementation plan remains shipped. This plan does not reopen or duplicate it; it verifies current operational accounting, user-facing quality, safety, and delivery after later changes.\n\n### D-002 — A transient alert is investigated from the writer, not treated as a standing count\n\nThe live count is currently zero and the alert writer separates never-registered scopes from scopes that outlived ledger rows. P-002 must resolve the exact identities and lifecycle before any reclassification change.\n\n### D-003 — Public release uses existing surfaces and the standard pipeline\n\nAll changes extend the current ledger, reconciler, inventory, Task Manager components, tests, and release gate. No new subsystem or force-deploy path is planned.\n\n### D-004 — Nested cgroups inherit the nearest pc-scope task identity\nDate: 2026-08-11\nA process in a descendant cgroup such as pc-<task>.scope/papercusp-deb-build-* remains inside that task's cgroup subtree. The reconciler must scan path ancestors for the nearest valid pc scope; treating only the leaf as identity creates a false escape alarm and undercounts the owning task's subtree.\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-005 — A pc-scope name proves managed provenance, not prior ledger persistence\nDate: 2026-08-11\nbeginSyncEnrolment mints and launches a pc-* scope before its fire-and-forget registerTask/markSpawned promise settles. Therefore a live pc scope with no live row may be either an outlived terminal row or a registration failure. Alerts must say managed scope has no live ledger row; they must not assert it outlived a row without reading history.\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-006 — Fire-and-forget enrollment remains fail-open but failure is observable\nDate: 2026-08-11\nSpawn availability still outranks observability: completeSyncEnrolment must never reject into the spawn path. Its catch must nevertheless emit one bounded diagnostic with task id and error, because swallowing it leaves a real unaccounted alarm with no recoverable cause.\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-007 — D-007 — Harden the existing task-manager surface; add no parallel UI primitive\nDate: 2026-08-11\ndesign-phase.search_registry returned no matching status-alert/process-inventory component. Reuse the shipped Table, Select, Checkbox, Popover, and shared KillTaskControl surfaces. Limit P-003 to evidence-accurate classification, alert copy, and tests so the public UI cannot label exempt or provenance-unknown processes as confirmed chokepoint bypasses.\n\n### D-008 — D-008 — Redact credential-bearing diagnostics before task-manager payload caps\nDate: 2026-08-11\nReuse the shared sensitive-text redaction contract extracted from session ingest, preserving that public API. Apply redaction before every display cap to process cmdlines, errors, titles, exit reasons, and schedule diagnostics so secrets cannot survive truncation while bounded diagnostic context remains useful.\n\n### D-009 — D-009: auto-generated systemd-run scopes are accounted external lifetimes\nDate: 2026-08-11\nThe runtime classifier treats only systemd-run auto-generated run-r<32 lowercase hex>.scope leaves as systemd-unit/exempt, alongside .service leaves. This matches the authoritative reconciler: systemd owns the transient checkpoint lifetime. Arbitrary named *.scope units (including papercup-headless-* residue) remain unaccounted. Verified against live run-rc174537f041445b2abda49f2c7c51e09.scope and guarded by scope-class.test.ts.\n\n### D-010 — Public Release NO-GO\nDate: 2026-08-12\nBased on post-deployment verification:\n1. **Pipeline Gate**: The green-checkpoint gate remains RED (19 consecutive reds). The most recent automated rescue run failed, preventing standard promotion.\n2. **Live Inventory**: An authoritative reconcile query of `harness_shared.task_ledger` shows 7 `unaccounted` tasks and 1063 `stranded` tasks.\n\n**Decision: NO-GO**\nBecause the primary release blocker (intermittent accounting correctness manifesting as unaccounted tasks) is still actively reproducing post-deployment, and the release gate is chronically failing, the system is not ready for public release. These residual risks must be resolved before proceeding.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-claude-md-projection-from-pg-2026-08-10","title":"Acceptance: authored docs + CLAUDE.md are PG-canonical, losslessly round-tripping, and hand-edit-safe","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-12","owner":"su-70b6af5b-161b-4f48-a660-bf0e05a1af44","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: authored docs + CLAUDE.md are PG-canonical, losslessly round-tripping, and hand-edit-safe\nslug: acceptance-claude-md-projection-from-pg-2026-08-10\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-12\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-70b6af5b-161b-4f48-a660-bf0e05a1af44\n---\n\n# Acceptance: authored docs + CLAUDE.md are PG-canonical, losslessly round-tripping, and hand-edit-safe\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01.
