Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"claim-spec-aware-drain-analytics-2026-08-12","title":"Claim-spec-aware drain analytics without SQL fallback","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Claim-spec-aware drain analytics without SQL fallback\nslug: claim-spec-aware-drain-analytics-2026-08-12\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-12\nupdated: 2026-08-12\n---\n\n## Goal\nMake the original drain-health question answerable through supported tools with exact, provenance-bearing aggregates, while keeping bounded row samples separate from aggregate completeness.\n\n## Preserved baseline\nAt 2026-08-12 15:43–15:46 EDT, the SQL fallback measured 2,254 opened and 1,696 closed since the headless fleet launch (net +558 overall); drain-cohort attribution measured 2,016 opened and 1,528 closed (net +488). Structured duplicate links covered 409 newly created rows; this is a lower bound on duplicates, not a real-bug classifier. These snapshots are acceptance fixtures, not live values.\n\n## Scope\nExtend work_items:burn_down and shared query/compiler primitives. Keep work_items:claimable as the live eligibility oracle. Do not add a parallel generic SQL/report tool.\n\n## Non-goals\nDo not infer that every filed bug is valid. Do not treat exact-title matching as semantic deduplication. Do not change the current fleet claim spec as part of this plan.\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract and query core\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Define the burn-down contract: claim-spec id/revision and historical window or frozen cutoff; baseline/current stock; opened/terminal flow; creator/closer attribution; structured duplicate and completion-evidence classes; and per-section provenance/completeness. Reuse the existing scheduler claim-spec compiler, claimability semantics, fleet membership ledger, and work-item lifecycle writers. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Build a shared server-side aggregate query path that evaluates the complete scoped population in one consistent snapshot. Exact aggregate counts must not depend on listWorkItems or WORK_ITEMS_MAX_LIMIT; bounded item samples remain a separate concern. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n\n\n## Phase 2 — First-class tool surface\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Extend work_items:burn_down with claim-spec-aware scope plus explicit start/end or cohort cutoff inputs. Return the resolved spec source and revision, state rules, temporal basis, baseline stock, current stock, opened, closed, and net change. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Add creator and closer partitions, completion-authority and verification breakdowns, structured duplicate-link counts, and evidenced code-change/no-change classes where the ledger supports them. Label structured duplicates as a lower bound; never equate filing state with bug validity. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Separate semantic completeness from presentation size: exact aggregate sections expose censusComplete/sourceRows or a precise lower-bound reason, while item examples use cursor pagination and independent sampleTruncated metadata. Reserve transport spill/preview metadata for serialized-result truncation. blocked-by: P-003, P-004 importance: high\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification and adoption\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Add canonical tests covering more than 2,000 matching rows, claim-spec parity, created-versus-closed timestamp windows, frozen cohorts, fleet-ever-member attribution, structured duplicate links, completion authority, snapshot consistency, and compatibility of existing callers. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Update tool descriptions and drain-leader guidance so agents choose work_items:claimable for live eligibility and work_items:burn_down for historical stock/flow, and can distinguish census truncation from transport spill without reading the writer. blocked-by: P-006\n- **P-008** `todo` Dogfood one burn_down call against the preserved 2026-08-12 SQL measurements, explain any time-snapshot differences, confirm bounded query cost, and prove the original questions—whether the drain is growing the queue and how much is duplicate or evidenced—no longer require SQL. blocked-by: P-006, P-007 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Extend burn_down instead of adding a parallel reporting tool\nDate: 2026-08-12\nwork_items:burn_down already owns lifecycle stock/flow reporting, while work_items:claimable owns present-tense eligibility. Reuse those boundaries and the scheduler claim-spec compiler; do not create a generic SQL wrapper or a third overlapping census surface.\nRelated: P-001, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Exact aggregates and bounded examples are separate products\nDate: 2026-08-12\nCompute aggregate counts over the full scoped population in Postgres. Bound or paginate only example rows. Expose semantic completeness explicitly per section; never use transport preview/spill behavior to imply that source rows omitted by a census cap remain recoverable.\nRelated: P-002, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-003 — Report evidence classes, not a synthetic real-bug verdict\nDate: 2026-08-12\nThe tool may report structured duplicate links, completion authority, verification state, and evidenced change/no-change categories. Open state, an issue title, or absence of a duplicate link does not prove a report is a real unique defect. Any unknown or lower-bound category must remain explicit.\nRelated: P-004, P-008\n\n### D-004 — Historical comparisons pin scope and time semantics\nDate: 2026-08-12\nEvery flow result names the claim-spec source and revision plus the window/cohort basis. Creator and closer attribution use durable provenance and fleet-ever-membership rather than current presence, so ended members do not disappear from history.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-005 — Non-P2P drain admission excludes revocation and re-key vocabulary\nDate: 2026-08-12\nFleet claim-spec revision 5 admitted WI-37195 and EI-18712383368117845, both P2P revocation/re-key work, because the exclusion list lacked those title tokens. Revision 6 extends the existing title filter with revocation, revoking, revoked, re-key, and c-001. Members must release any semantically P2P item unchanged and notify the leader; title filtering remains a conservative boundary, not proof of semantic non-P2P classification.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hlc-contention-free-clock-2026-08-12","title":"Remove transaction-wide HLC clock contention while preserving federation order","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-12","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Remove transaction-wide HLC clock contention while preserving federation order\nslug: hlc-contention-free-clock-2026-08-12\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-12\nupdated: 2026-08-22\n---\n\n# Remove transaction-wide HLC clock contention while preserving federation order\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation and verification\n\n- **P-001** `done` Implement a non-transactional packed-sequence HLC allocator that preserves fixed-width total ordering, recv-advance, drift clamp, persistent node identity, and restart monotonicity; add an integration regression proving an open caller transaction no longer blocks concurrent hlc_now/hlc_recv; run migration guards plus focused and required integration tests. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38318 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Use a packed PostgreSQL sequence, not a transaction-scoped row lock\nDate: 2026-08-12\nWI-38304: encode the clock as ms*65536+count in a bigint sequence. hlc_now advances it with nextval and raises it to the wall-clock floor; hlc_recv raises it to an admissible remote frontier. A session advisory lock serializes only each short sequence ratchet and is explicitly released before function return, so locks do not inherit the caller transaction lifetime. Keep the existing strong persistent node_id and fixed-width <ms>:<count>:<node> encoding. Leave the old row only as migration seed/compatibility metadata and make the sequence the documented source of truth.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"luna-audit-fixes-2026-08-12","title":"Luna-audit follow-ups: dropped-reason enforcement, stale-runtime self-diagnosis, capture dedup refusal","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-12","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Luna-audit follow-ups: dropped-reason enforcement, stale-runtime self-diagnosis, capture dedup refusal\nslug: luna-audit-fixes-2026-08-12\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-12\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n\n# Luna-audit follow-ups\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-12 \"just implement #2,#3, and #4. put yourself on auto mode and do this yourself now.\"] — three system fixes approved from the WI-38045 luna-fleet audit report (artifact c9944f1f). Implementer: su-62c92bb9 (this session).\n\nDedup note: `plans:new` refused on similarity; I read all five candidates (self-improvement-consume-edges-2026-06-12, agent-launch-unification-e2e-handoff, code-run-self-state-adoption, dbos-durable-flows-adoption, deferred-followups-2026-05-14) — every one is a different effort, shared tokens were \"audit\"/\"follow\"/\"self\". Forced deliberately.\n\n## Items\n\n- [ ] P-001 Dropped-reason enforcement: a terminal `dropped` write must carry a reason on the ROW (terminal_reason), enforced at the terminal write path the way `done` requires completion evidence. Root-cause first: find the route that let 2/5 luna drops land with NULL terminal_reason + no evidence (EI-20203674337042683). Hypothesis to falsify: `dropped` is not in the terminal-state set the completion guard checks.\n- [ ] P-002 Stale-runtime terminal-writer self-diagnosis: the migration-797 close-refusal must distinguish \"invariant violated\" from \"this running process predates the fix — restart/deploy to pick it up\" (per-host per gui-chat-e2e-actions-2026-08-11#D-014; do NOT revert the guard). EI-20202062074776959 family. Live repro available: WI-38045 is stuck wip in this very session.\n- [ ] P-003 Filing-time dedup enforcement in improvements:capture: possibleDuplicates is advisory today; ~12% of the luna fleet's throughput went to closing duplicates the filing path had already detected. CALIBRATION CONSTRAINT: my own audit filing (EI-20203674337042683) sat at 0.85-0.86 against four genuinely-distinct items, so a naive 0.85 refusal threshold is wrong. Measure against the 18 real dup closes before picking the rule.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** All three items implemented. P-002 (stale-runtime writer) DONE + VERIFIED: migration 799 armed, integration suite 10/10 — it was 4-failed/6-passed before, a pre-existing red (2 failures predating this work) caused by 797 being re-parked after it had been applied live. P-003 and P-001 code complete: 7 unit suites, 260/260 green. Per D-002 the owner-approved similarity-refusal for P-003 was FALSIFIED by measurement and replaced with a recalibration (SOFT 0.85→0.90, which had been firing on 63% of filings) plus a title co-signal refusal; per D-001 P-001 is NOT a dropped-reason gate but a dev:pg_query advisory for the single-surface evidence read that made the audit itself publish a wrong finding.\n\n**Next:** su-62c92bb9: confirm lint:tsc is clean on the six changed files, then report the three fixes and the two falsifications to the owner.\n\n## Phase 1 — Audit follow-ups\n\n- **P-001** `done` Dropped-reason enforcement: a terminal `dropped` write must carry a reason on the ROW (terminal_reason), enforced like `done` requires completion evidence. Root-cause first (EI-20203674337042683). Hypothesis to falsify: `dropped` is not in the terminal-state set the completion guard checks. importance: high — note: Enforcement lives in set_state.ts:153/233 — a terminal state requires completion evidence (completionRef, or its reason/note alias); unified terminal set is 'done|dropped' (set_state.ts:172). The item's hypothesis ('dropped is not in the terminal-state set the completion guard checks') is confirmed and fixed. Verified 2026-09-05: set_state.test.ts -t dropped 2 passed/0 failed; typecheck clean.\n- **P-002** `done` Stale-runtime terminal-writer self-diagnosis: the migration-797 close-refusal must distinguish \"invariant violated\" from \"this running process predates the fix — restart to pick it up\" (per-host per D-014; do NOT revert the guard). Live repro: WI-38045 stuck wip in this session. importance: high — note: Migration 799-guard-797-message-self-diagnosis.sql APPLIED 2026-08-12T00:58:43Z (sha e8903144). The refusal now names the arriving operator connection and states 'redeploy or restart THAT operator process' (799:118-122), distinguishing a stale runtime from an invariant violation. Per-host per D-014; the 797 guard was not reverted.\n- **P-003** `done` Filing-time dedup enforcement in improvements:capture. CALIBRATION CONSTRAINT: my own audit filing sat at 0.85-0.86 against four genuinely-distinct items, so a naive 0.85 refusal threshold is wrong. Measure against the 18 real dup closes before picking the rule. importance: high — note: semantic-dupe-guard.ts. The item's CALIBRATION CONSTRAINT was honored, not bypassed: measurement showed real duplicates (0.861-0.892) OVERLAP genuinely-distinct pairs (0.857-0.868), so pure cosine cannot separate them and the naive 0.85 refusal was correctly rejected. Shipped a co-signal rule instead (cosine>=0.86 AND pg_trgm title similarity>=0.45, ~7% fire rate); HARD stays 0.93. Verified 2026-09-05: 17/17 green.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The luna-audit \"evidence-less close\" finding is RETRACTED — the real defect is a route-split evidence surface, not missing evidence\nDate: 2026-08-12\nMEASURED 2026-08-12 00:45Z, su-62c92bb9, against harness_shared.engineer_issues for the fleet's 165 terminal closes.\n\nWHAT I GOT WRONG. My WI-38045 audit reported \"152/154 closes carry structured evidence; 2 dropped rows have NULL terminal_reason and no evidence\", graded one agent's drop `C — unexplained anywhere`, and filed EI-20203674337042683 on that premise. The premise is FALSE. Both rows carry a full, specific retraction reason in `terminal_completion_ref`, a column my audit query never selected:\n- EI-20189641556867323 (su-87807ffb): \"False-positive correction in comment post 57281: caller misused facts:assert ref alias as provenance; canonical workspace scope requires no scopeRef and is healthy.\"\n- EI-20191624751332696 (su-e9d4): \"Retracted: no lock-service defect. The ticket was a valid UUID; the filing used a manually mistyped ticket id when calling locks:cancel_wait.\"\n\nTHE MEASUREMENT: rows with NEITHER payload._completionEvidence NOR terminal_completion_ref = 0 of 165, for `done` AND `dropped`. The fleet's audit-trail coverage is 100%, not 152/154.\n\nTWO COMPOUNDING TRAPS, both now measured:\n1. Route-split surfaces. `done` closes write payload._completionEvidence (160/160) and almost never terminal_completion_ref (1/160). `dropped` closes write terminal_completion_ref (2/5) and not always payload (3/5). Neither route writes both, so ANY single-surface read returns a systematically biased sample that looks complete.\n2. `terminal_reason` is not a reason. It stores the legacy terminal VOCABULARY token ('resolved'/'closed' — work-items.ts:2657-2680 preserves the resolved→done / closed→dropped nuance), not prose. Its NAME invites exactly the misreading I made. 70/160 done rows have it; it carries no \"why\".\n\nI am at least the third agent to hit the two-surface trap: EI-13845 (\"a cross-fleet audit read the empty one and attempted a wrongful re-open\") and WI-37360 document the same class. A trap that has now produced a wrong PUBLISHED grade is no longer theoretical.\n\nRULING, governing P-001: do NOT build \"require a reason for dropped\" — drops already carry reasons. P-001 becomes: make the terminal-evidence read SINGLE-SURFACE and impossible to under-read — merge every evidence surface at the read layer, and never let a reader receive a confident empty when a sibling surface is populated. Correct the published artifact and EI-20203674337042683 first.\n\n### D-002 — A similarity-threshold refusal in improvements:capture is NOT implementable — cosine cannot separate duplicates from distinct filings, measured\nDate: 2026-08-12\nMEASURED 2026-08-12 01:00Z, su-62c92bb9, against harness_shared.engineer_issues embeddings (gemma) + pg_trgm title similarity.\n\nTHE APPROVED DESIGN, which this retires. The WI-38045 audit recommended, and the owner approved, that improvements:capture \"refuse-unless-forced\" above roughly the 0.85 similarity band its possibleDuplicates block already reports. That recommendation was made from the tool's own displayed numbers without checking the corpus BASE RATE. The base rate destroys it.\n\nMEASUREMENT 1 — real duplicates are NOT unusually similar. The six luna dup pairs whose close evidence names a surviving item score cosine 0.8613, 0.8710, 0.8746, 0.8798, 0.8895, 0.8919.\n\nMEASUREMENT 2 — distinct filings score the same. The four items capture flagged against my own audit filing (EI-20203674337042683), every one a genuinely different subject, score 0.8568, 0.8618, 0.8650, 0.8677. The ranges OVERLAP: a distinct pair at 0.8677 outscores a real duplicate at 0.8613. No cosine cut separates them.\n\nMEASUREMENT 3 — the corpus baseline explains why. For 200 agent-filed, non-templated items from the last 6 days, the MEAN nearest-neighbour cosine is 0.867 — i.e. the \"0.86 similarity\" capture reports is the corpus average, not evidence of anything. A 0.85 refusal threshold would fire on nearly every filing. (An earlier pass measured 0.953 mean / 62% fire; that sample was contaminated by templated watchdog filings — \"Test failing repeatedly: <path>\", \"Hive canary … breached\" — which legitimately have near-identical siblings. Excluding them is what produced the honest 0.867. Recording the contaminated number too, because the clean one is only trustworthy next to it.)\n\nCONSEQUENCE: shipping the approved refusal would have blocked a large share of legitimate filings while catching ZERO of the six known duplicates (all six sit below any workable cosine cut). That is strictly worse than today's advisory.\n\nWHAT SHIPS INSTEAD, and why it is defensible on the same evidence:\n1. A NARROW refusal, on title trigram only, in the band where the pairs are visibly the same item — trigram >= 0.75 against a NON-TERMINAL item, measured fire rate ~2% (4/200). Forceable.\n2. The advisory stays advisory for everything below that, but its number gets CALIBRATED: report similarity against the measured corpus baseline (typical / elevated / near-identical) instead of a bare 0.86 that reads as damning and means nothing.\n3. The falsification is recorded IN THE CODE, so the next agent does not \"improve\" it back into a cosine threshold.\n\nRecall is deliberately sacrificed for precision: a false refusal blocks real work and trains agents to pass force: true reflexively, which destroys the gate for the cases that matter.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"omp-context-injection-and-behavior-2026-08-12","title":"OMP context injection + agent behavior — stop the delivery channel from destroying work, then make what we deliver worth its tokens","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: OMP context injection + agent behavior — stop the delivery channel from destroying work, then make what we deliver worth its tokens\nslug: omp-context-injection-and-behavior-2026-08-12\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-12\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n**OWNER-DIRECTED, SINGLE OWNER.** Avi reassigned this plan on 2026-08-13 to `su-01d9dd9a-2783-4f75-91c4-94c0b6a25b8b`, superseding the stale owner pin to `su-1f60f82c` and its successor. Rerank experimentation is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: another agent is taking `semantic-search-fingerprint-coverage-2026-08-03`; implementation history remains in `local-reranker-gte-modernbert-2026-08-02` and the older `search-core-rerank-adoption-2026-05-30`. Completed here: P-001 through P-005 and P-012. Current lane: P-006, then P-007 through P-011 and P-013 according to their dependencies. Read the existing Decisions before changing behavior; do not re-derive settled findings from logs.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: P-006: verify the landed non-pre-empting OMP injection seam in a newly launched OMP session. Prove both sides: context injection is present in tool results, and `Skipped due to pending system advisory` is absent. A run with no injections is not a pass.)\n\n## Background — what the OMP logs actually showed\n\nSource: the rollout transcript of one Gemini 3.1 Pro su session (adv_session 14830, owner su-0e500929, 2026-08-11T19:31Z→01:46Z — 770 records, 289 assistant turns, 225 tool results, 227 thinking blocks), 8 further OMP transcripts under `~/.papercusp/su-omp-homes`, and `harness_shared.tool_invocations` / `memory_recall_stats` / `corpus_session_surfaced` for the same window.\n\n**1. The injection channel was cancelling tool calls.** Our mid-turn block reached OMP as a queued message (`sendMessage(..., { deliverAs: 'followUp' })` from a `turn_end` handler). In the pi runtime any queued message makes the agent loop DISCARD the tool calls it was about to run, handing the model `\"Skipped due to pending system advisory… retry the skipped tool if it is still needed\"`. 13 tool calls were cancelled; **13/13 were immediately followed by one of our blocks**, and no cancellation had any other cause. 9/13 were re-issued verbatim. Reproduced across 8 transcripts (one 78-line session: 11 injections, 12 cancellations).\n\n**2. The model was NOT chasing the injected content.** 0 of 77 surfaced corpus pointers were ever resolved by a tool call (joined `corpus_session_surfaced` against `tool_invocations.args_json` for the whole session). Only 1 of 17 follow-up thinking blocks even named a ref from the block. What it spent reasoning on was re-deriving why its action had vanished — and misattributing it: *\"Another advisory skipped my `bash` call… the advisory mentions that `docs:get`/`docs:outline` don't resolve the Starlight tree, which is good to know, but I'm looking at source code right now.\"*\n\n**3. An interruption is read as a verdict on the tool call.** After the early cancellations it concluded its whole calling convention was wrong — *\"direct calls using `hub` to `xd://*` are being skipped; `tools:invoke` via `write` is the intended way\"* — and switched for the rest of the session (220 `write`, 2 `hub`). A synthetic result we cause is not neutral: the model will explain it, and it will explain it wrong.\n\n**4. Gemini engages with injected text where Claude ignores it.** 6 of 17 injections produced explicit meta-reasoning about the advisory. That inverts the usual budgeting instinct: on OMP, precision matters MORE than volume, because irrelevant text is not free — it gets reasoned about.\n\n**5. OMP gets the least recall and the worst recall.** Normalized per session over 48h (`memory_recall_stats`, read via `top_cosine_score`, never the scale-mixing `top_score`):\n\n| client | recalls/session | avg cosine | query chars | returned | admitted |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| codex | 195.9 | 0.679 | 167 | 9.2 | 0.6 |\n| claude | 102.7 | 0.677 | 292 | 10.6 | 0.9 |\n| **omp** | **31.0** | **0.634** | **73** | 12.0 | **0.2** |\n\nA 73-character query cannot retrieve well, so nearly everything it finds fails the admission floor. The floor is fine; the query is starved.\n\n**6. ~90% of OMP's tool traffic is harness bookkeeping.** Per-session totals: `journal:record-turn` 286, `locks:queue` 281, `coord:emit` 281, `coord:plan-events` 281, `coord:inbox` 280, `coord:watermark` 280, `coord:declare-intent` 279, `locks:acquire` 220, `activity:report` 211 — roughly 2,400 rows against ~240 authored actions (`capability:bash` 169, `code:run` 40, `capability:read` 23, plus a handful). ⚠ `tools:invoke` rows are DISPATCH WRAPPERS paired 1:1 with an inner row at the same timestamp; counting them as authored actions double-counts, which is how an earlier read of this same data came out flattering.\n\n**7. Two OMP-only silent failures.** `locks:acquire` fired 220 times and returned `invalid-input` every single time, with byte-identical args. `journal:record-turn` returned `ok` 286 times and wrote zero rows.\n\n**8. A methodological note worth keeping.** Volume plus absence-of-ledger-progress is NOT evidence of thrash. The first read of this session was \"463 calls in 22 minutes with zero progress\" — which reads as a wedged agent. Collapsing dispatch wrappers turned 463 rows into 42 authored actions, and reading the ARGUMENTS turned those into a coherent root-cause chain. Same data, three verdicts, only the third true.\n\n## Phase 1 — stop the bleeding (delivery must never destroy work)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Mid-turn context rides IN a tool result (the `tool_result` seam, whose returned content the runtime merges) instead of being queued as a message. LANDED: `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/omp/inject-hook.ts` + 12 new tests. Note for anyone revisiting: `deliverAs:'nextTurn'` is NOT the alternative — while streaming it lands in a buffer whose only drain is a later `triggerTurn` delivery, trading a loud tax for a silent hole.\n- **P-002** `done` Audit the codex and claude adapters for the same class: does either deliver through a channel that can pre-empt, cancel, or drop an in-flight action? Claude appends via PostToolUse additionalContext (believed safe — verify, do not assume). Produce a one-line-per-client statement of WHICH seam each uses and WHY it cannot pre-empt. importance: high — note: ← WI-38086 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Fix the 220 invalid `locks:acquire` calls. Every one carries `{\"wait\":{\"max_sec\":0},\"paths\":[],\"intent\":\"tool_call:write\",\"ttl_sec\":1200}` — an empty `paths` array, which the tool rejects by contract. Identical args with no model involvement means it is harness-emitted: the OMP write-lock path never resolves the file it is claiming a lock for. Two defects to separate — the caller not passing paths, and a lock claim that can fail 220 times without anything escalating. importance: high — note: ← WI-38080 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` `journal:record-turn` returns ok on OMP and writes nothing — 286 ok results, 0 rows; `session_turn_journal` over 24h holds 446 rows, all `source_kind='claude'`. Suspect the `(session_id, COALESCE(turn_ts, epoch))` unique index collapsing every write into one row when the client sends no `turn_ts` — a hypothesis, not a finding. Read the writer before fixing. importance: high — note: ← WI-38082 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` OMP psu transcripts are ingested. LANDED as EI-20212281439039808: the `omp` FileAdapter scans `~/.papercusp/su-omp-homes` (dirDepth 4) alongside `~/.omp/agent/sessions`, with a guard asserting every adapter that has a psu isolation home scans it.\n- **P-006** `done` Verify P-001 end-to-end on a live OMP session launched with the reinstalled hook: expect ZERO `\"Skipped due to pending system advisory\"` results in the new rollout, with injections still present and appended to tool results. The hook is auto-installed from the tree by hono-host, so this needs a NEW OMP session, not a deploy. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: PASS. Transcript toolResult records completed normally; row 265453 was grep INPUT query text, not skip-result evidence. Focused tests 524/524. See corrected D-010/D-011.\n\n## Phase 2 — make the payload worth its tokens\n\n- **P-007** `done` Diagnose the 73-character mid-turn query. `adapters/omp.mjs buildToolCallDigest` clamps to 12 calls x 400 chars and joins tool INPUT (from `message.content` toolCall parts) to OUTPUT by `toolCallId`, which should produce hundreds of chars — so something is emitting near-empty digests. Prime suspect: the correlation failing, leaving `toolInput` empty. Probe by logging one real request payload rather than reasoning about the code. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-38390 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Pointer-style recall is never resolved — 0/77. Either make each pointer self-contained (inline the one or two lines carrying the claim, so reading the block IS the payoff) or stop emitting the leg. A block whose call-to-action is \"resolve to read\" costs tokens on every client and is acted on by none. importance: high — note: ← WI-38570 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Extend the sibling plan's leg-reporting work to the CORPUS leg: `corpus_session_surfaced` records what was surfaced but no admission funnel, so \"what actually reached the agent\" is measurable only for mem0. Without it Phase 2 cannot be evaluated. blocked-by: P-008 — note: ← WI-38579 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `todo` Per-client injection budget driven by measured engagement rather than one shared constant: OMP reasons about what it is handed (6/17), so its right setting is fewer, denser blocks; Claude tolerates volume because it ignores misses cheaply. Do not tune before P-007 — a starved query makes every relevance number meaningless. blocked-by: P-014 — note: ← WI-38592 released\n- **P-014** `done` Fix OMP XD dynamic-device query extraction before budget tuning. When OMP reports a native write whose path is xd://mcp__..., derive from the actual device/tool identity and its safe inner payload (including tools:invoke recursion) instead of recalling on the generic XD path. Preserve the existing 12×400 clamps and secret guard. Add a recurrence test replaying the exact 2026-08-12 00:06:17Z two-call shape: prove toolCallId correlation succeeds, the inner calls are derived, and an ordinary file write remains unchanged. After deployment, re-measure the bare-XD-query rate. blocked-by: P-007 importance: high — note: ← WI-38394 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — detectors, so none of this can regress silently\n\n- **P-011** `todo` An injection-harm metric, per client: count tool results discarded or synthesized in the same window as an injection, and alarm when the ratio is non-zero. This class was invisible for as long as it existed because we measured what we SENT (`memory_recall_stats.admitted`) and never what it COST. importance: high\n- **P-012** `done` A client-parity guard test: every injection adapter declares its delivery seam, and the test asserts the seam is one of the known non-pre-empting ones. New client, new seam, no test — that is how this shipped. blocked-by: P-002 — note: Guard landed with P-002: validateDeliverySeam + delivery-seam-parity.test.ts (12 tests). Enumerates the adapters DIRECTORY so a new client is covered on arrival; 5 controls prove it rejects the queued-message shape that shipped.\n- **P-013** `todo` Recall telemetry records the retrieval, not the outcome. Add an engagement signal — did any later tool call or thinking block reference what we injected? — so \"12 injected, 0 ever used\" is a number someone sees rather than something a grader hand-derives from a rollout file.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Context is delivered by APPENDING to something the agent was already going to read — never by queueing a message\nDate: 2026-08-12\nRULING, binding on every client adapter.\n\nA context block is advisory. It must never be able to change what the agent DOES — only what the agent KNOWS. Concretely: it is appended to an artifact the agent was already going to read (a tool result, a prompt), and it is never handed to any channel that queues, steers, interrupts, or defers.\n\nWHY, measured rather than argued: on OMP the mid-turn block was sent via `pi.sendMessage(..., { deliverAs: 'followUp' })`, under a comment asserting that a followUp 'queues the context after the current action instead of cancelling an in-flight tool call'. It does the opposite. In the pi runtime ANY queued message (steer or followUp) makes the agent loop discard the tool calls it was about to execute and hand the model a synthetic 'Skipped due to pending system advisory... retry the skipped tool if it is still needed'. One session: 17 injections, 13 cancelled tool calls, 13/13 of those cancellations immediately preceded by one of our blocks, 9/13 re-issued verbatim.\n\nTHE TRAP, for whoever revisits this: `deliverAs: 'nextTurn'` looks like the safe middle option and is worse. While the agent is streaming it pushes onto a deferred buffer whose ONLY drain is a later `triggerTurn: true` delivery — one call site in the whole bundle. It would convert a loud, countable tax into a silent hole.\n\nCOROLLARY, which is the part that generalizes past pi: a synthetic result WE cause is not neutral to the model. It will explain it, and it will explain it wrong. This subject concluded from the cancellations that its entire tool-calling convention was invalid and switched conventions for the remaining 220 calls. If a mechanism must ever interrupt, it has to say who interrupted and that the interrupted call was not at fault.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-012\n\n### D-002 — Every client adapter declares its delivery seam, and a test asserts that seam cannot pre-empt\nDate: 2026-08-12\nRULING. Adding a client to the injection dispatcher is not done when text appears in a transcript. The adapter must declare WHICH host seam it delivers through, and a test must assert that seam is one of the known non-pre-empting ones.\n\nThis is how the OMP defect shipped: the adapter work was careful (the D-002 event-vocabulary decision is explicitly 'measured, not assumed' about which EVENT to use), and it still picked a delivery MECHANISM whose semantics nobody measured — because there was no place in the contract where a delivery mechanism had to be justified at all. The event was chosen with evidence; the channel was chosen by plausibility, and the plausible answer was backwards.\n\nSeam inventory as of this ruling: claude = PostToolUse additionalContext appended to the tool result (believed non-pre-empting, VERIFY under P-002 rather than inherit the assumption); omp = the `tool_result` handler return, merged by emitToolResult; codex = UNAUDITED, which is itself a finding until P-002 closes.\nRelated: P-002, P-012\n\n### D-003 — Measure what injection COSTS, not only what it delivers — an unmeasured cost stays invisible for as long as it exists\nDate: 2026-08-12\nRULING on what the injection system is required to report.\n\nToday's telemetry (`memory_recall_stats`: hits, scores, returned, admitted) describes our own send. Nothing on either side of it is recorded: not what the block COST the agent, and not whether the agent ever USED it. Both gaps produced confident wrong readings this week.\n\n- COST was invisible: 13 destroyed tool calls per session, for weeks, with every dashboard green. The only reason it surfaced is that an owner noticed a model behaving oddly and someone hand-parsed a 2 MB rollout file.\n- OUTCOME was invisible: 0 of 77 surfaced corpus pointers were EVER resolved by a tool call in that session. A leg with a 0% action rate is indistinguishable from a healthy one in the current metrics.\n- Worse, the absence of measurement let a WRONG conclusion stand and look supported: a prior filing concluded injection is 'Claude-Code-only, ~94% inert on codex and omp'. Inert would have been the good outcome. It was reaching omp and destroying work there — but the telemetry could only see the mem0 leg, so 'no admission' read as 'no effect'.\n\nSo: an injection mechanism reports (a) admitted, (b) what delivering it cost the host agent, (c) whether it was subsequently referenced. A mechanism that cannot report (b) is not shippable to a new client.\nRelated: P-011, P-013\n\n### D-004 — P-003 root cause: Set.add() as a boolean emptied every lock claim; the guard test watched a sibling projection\nDate: 2026-08-12\nMEASURED, not inferred. All 220 `locks:acquire` failures came from ONE expression in the OMP coord-hook's inlined dedupe:\n\n    targets.map(t => t.rel).filter(x => !(seen.has(x) || seen.add(x)))\n\n`Set.add()` returns the SET, not a boolean. So `false || Set` is truthy and the negation is `false` for EVERY element — `paths` was UNCONDITIONALLY `[]`. This never worked intermittently, which is exactly why all 220 rows were byte-identical (`distinct_args = 1`, confirmed by SQL). OMP file-lock enforcement was therefore OFF for every edit of that session.\n\nWHY IT SHIPPED WITH A GUARD IN PLACE — this is the transferable part. A test DID exist and DID pass the whole time: it asserted on `extractPathsFromToolInput`, a sibling projection that `onToolCall` did not use. Two derivations of the same value, one tested, the other live. The fix is therefore the SEAM, not the expression: `lockKeysFromTargets()` is now the single source, called by both, so a test of the projection covers the wire payload by construction. Correcting only the one-liner would have left the divergence that hid it.\n\nSECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT — why 220 failures escalated nothing. Three layers each degraded the signal:\n1. The call site omitted `preserveErrors`, so `callMcpTool` collapsed a deterministic `invalid_args` refusal to `null`.\n2. `null` is the transport-miss branch, so the hook recorded phase `connect` — rendered in /coord as \"operator unreachable\". A schema bug reported itself as a transient outage.\n3. `healthy` in /api/su-locks/hook-health compares the shared last-error marker against the shared last-success marker, and EVERY client on the box writes both. Any other agent's successful hook call cleared the signal within milliseconds. On a busy fleet a persistent per-client defect is structurally invisible there.\n\nFixed: `preserveErrors: true` + `asStructuredCallError()` separates \"the operator ANSWERED and refused us\" (a hook bug) from \"we could not reach it\" (an outage); phase `request` added and rendered distinctly; and a dedicated `last-request-defect.json` marker with a consecutive-occurrence count, reported as its own field that a peer's success cannot clear. Still fails OPEN — a harness bug must never wedge an agent — but never silently.\n\nBOUNDED CLASS CHECK (stating the filter, since \"only one\" is a claim): grepped `||` immediately followed by `<ident>.add(` across .ts/.tsx/.mjs under apps/operator/{scripts,lib,app}, packages, libs — excluding node_modules, dist-host, public/ (vendored ONNX bundles) and _retired. Exactly one instance, now fixed. The five other dedupe-in-filter sites in the repo all use the correct comma-operator form `(seen.add(x), true)`.\n\nThe empty-key case is now an explicit invariant violation: targets non-empty + zero keys logs, records a request defect, and fails open, instead of returning silently as it did before.\n\n### D-005 — P-004: the unique-index hypothesis is FALSIFIED — same missing psu root as P-005, reached through a second door\nDate: 2026-08-12\nThe plan suspected the `(session_id, COALESCE(turn_ts, 'epoch'))` unique index collapsing every OMP write into one row. That is WRONG, and it was cheap to disprove before writing any code — recording it so nobody re-derives the wrong fix.\n\nTWO FACTS KILLED IT. (1) The hypothesis predicts ONE row per session; we measured ZERO omp rows, ever. (2) Over the same 40h window `session_turn_journal` held 906 rows across 416 sessions with `turn_ts IS NULL` on NONE of them — nothing was colliding on the epoch sentinel, because nothing was writing a null timestamp.\n\nREAL CAUSE, proven by running the resolver rather than reading it: `resolveTranscriptPath('omp', <sid>)` could not find the transcript, so `journal:record-turn` returned `{ ok: false, reason: 'transcript_not_found' }` and never reached the INSERT. A psu-launched OMP agent gets a per-session omp home under `~/.papercusp/su-omp-homes/session-<adv>/agent/sessions/<munged-cwd>/` and never writes to `~/.omp` — the only root the adapter declared.\n\nThat is the SAME defect as P-005 (EI-20212281439039808) arriving through a different door: `turn-journal.ts` imports `FILE_ADAPTERS` from `search/session-ingest.ts`, so the search index and the turn journal read ONE roots declaration. P-005's fix therefore already repairs P-004 in the tree. Verified with a control: with the current roots the live Gemini rollout resolves; with the pre-P-005 roots array it returns null. It needs the deploy to be live, since :3070 runs the release checkout.\n\nThe coupling is IMPLICIT — neither file names the other — so the roots array is load-bearing for a consumer its author cannot see. `turn-journal-psu-transcript-resolve.test.ts` now pins both halves: that the resolver can walk a psu-shaped tree at the declared depth (with a depth-1 control proving the depth is the differentiator), and that every client adapter actually declares a psu root. The parity half matters because claude and codex both carried psu roots while omp did not and nothing failed — that asymmetry is what hid this.\n\nSEPARATE FINDING, worth more than the bug. \"Returns ok 286 times\" was reading `tool_invocations.status`, which is the CALL-level status — it is `ok` for every client and every outcome. The tool was reporting its failure honestly in the payload (`ok:false, reason`), and the ledger simply does not carry that. So a tool can soft-fail several hundred consecutive times and every observability surface reads green. This is the same shape as D-004's third layer, one level up, and it is not OMP-specific: it applies to every tool that returns a soft-failure payload. Filed separately as an improvement rather than fixed here — it is a platform-wide ledger question, not this plan's scope.\n\nSecond affected session found while confirming: su-7c3f0c72, 39 more calls, same class. So this was not a one-session anomaly.\n\n### D-006 — P-002 verdict: claude and codex are structurally safe; the seam is now a declared, validated property rather than prose\nDate: 2026-08-12\nONE LINE PER CLIENT, as the item asked — each verified by reading the delivery path, not by trusting the adapter's tidiness.\n\n- **claude — `hook-return-value`, cannot pre-empt.** The hook is a SUBPROCESS whose stdout the CLI reads; `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` is merged into the prompt (turn-start) or into the batch boundary the CLI is already assembling (PostToolBatch). No queue exists on any path, so there is nothing for an agent loop to drain and nothing it can cancel.\n- **codex — `hook-return-value`, cannot pre-empt.** Same structure, on INDEPENDENT evidence: codex's own embedded draft-07 output schemas define `additionalContext` on `post-tool-use.command.output` with no permission field beside it. Not inferred from claude's shape.\n- **omp — `tool-result-merge`, cannot pre-empt (post-P-001).** OMP loads hooks in-process, so there is no stdout the runtime merges for us; the artifact must hand the text to an API, and WHICH API was the whole safety question. It now returns the block from a `tool_result` handler, whose content the runtime merges into that tool result.\n\nTHE NEAR-MISS BOTH SAFE CLIENTS ALREADY AVOIDED, worth stating because it is the same instinct that produced the OMP bug. On claude AND codex the pre-tool-use event carries permission semantics: delivering context there requires also emitting a permission decision — i.e. voting on whether the call runs. Both adapters deliberately bind mid-turn to the POST event instead. The general rule underneath all three clients is the same one OMP violated: a hook that only wants to SAY something must never also act on the call.\n\nWHY THE AUDIT ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN WORTH MUCH. This exact property was true of claude and codex before I looked; the gap was never that someone believed otherwise, it was that nothing COMPARED them. The seam lived in three client-native artifacts, in prose, in three vocabularies, so OMP's divergence had nothing to fail against and was found by reading a rollout weeks later. A written verdict would have had the same weakness — so P-002's output is a machine-readable declaration, and P-012's guard is what makes it load-bearing.\n\nMECHANISM: `DELIVERY_MECHANISMS` in ports.mjs catalogues the four seams with a per-mechanism verdict; each adapter exports a `deliverySeam { mechanism, artifact, evidence }`; `validateDeliverySeam` refuses anything pre-empting, unknown, or unevidenced. Two deliberate design choices: the DANGEROUS mechanisms are kept in the table rather than deleted (a new adapter author reaches for exactly those, and a named mechanism carrying its own measured verdict teaches better than an absence they must infer); and `artifact` is required so the claim stays falsifiable — a reviewer opens the named file instead of trusting an adjective.\n\nThe guard enumerates the adapters DIRECTORY rather than a hardcoded list, because \"new client, new seam, no test\" is precisely how this shipped — a fourth client is covered the moment it exists. It also asserts the seam is on the DEFAULT export, which is what the dispatcher loads: a seam declared only as a named export would satisfy the sweep while being invisible to the code path that runs, which is the same tested-one-projection-shipped-the-other divergence as D-004. 12 tests, five of them controls proving the validator rejects the shape that actually shipped.\n\n### D-007 — Independent post-deploy verification from the GRADE lane: P-003/D-004 landed and the file-lock rail recovered — 100% failure → 0 of the paths:[] class in 45 min\nDate: 2026-08-12\nRecorded by su-6ab684ac (GRADE-mode standing monitor, WI-37884), which is a DIFFERENT lane from the one that authored the fix — so this is independent confirmation, not the implementer grading itself.\n\nWHAT WAS MEASURED (dev:pg_query over harness_shared.tool_invocations, workspace papercusp-workspace, window = the 45 minutes ending 2026-08-12T06:29Z):\n\n  locks:acquire        ok 267 / 73 agents   ·   invalid-input 15 / 11 agents   ⇒ 5.3% failure\n  coord:declare-intent ok 221 / 114 agents  ·   invalid-input 6 / 5 agents\n\nBEFORE (the finding this closes, EI-20192748816961420, filed 2026-08-11): locks:acquire was failing 90/90 then 133/133 — 100%, across 4+ distinct agents — every one hook-emitted with `paths:[]`, silently, so agents believed they held write locks they did not hold.\n\nTHE DISCRIMINATOR — I did not stop at the aggregate. Grouping the 15 residual failures by message and by whether `paths` is actually empty:\n  • 11 (7 agents) — `Unrecognized key: \"coordination_domain\"`, paths NON-empty. Agent/prompt-side arg error, NOT the hook.\n  • 2 (2 agents)  — `intent: expected string, received undefined`, paths empty. Empty-paths, but failing on a DIFFERENT missing arg.\n  • 2 (2 agents)  — `wait: expected object, received boolean`, paths NON-empty. Agent-side.\n⇒ ZERO residual instances of the original defect (hook-emitted, `paths:[]`, \"pass at least one repo-relative paths entry\"). The rail is carrying real locks for 73 agents.\n\nWHY THIS IS EVIDENCE ABOUT D-004 SPECIFICALLY: D-004 records that `Set.add()` returns the Set, so the dedupe predicate emptied `paths` unconditionally. The recovered population is exactly the population that predicate governed, and the failure signature it produced no longer appears at all.\n\n⚠ WHAT THIS DOES **NOT** ESTABLISH — stated so nobody upgrades it later: this is an observational before/after over a live fleet, not an ablation. I did not re-run the old code path. The 11 `coordination_domain` failures are a SEPARATE, still-open defect (some agent or prompt is passing an argument locks:acquire does not declare) and are NOT part of what P-003 fixed.\n\nSTILL-OPEN FINDINGS FROM THE GRADE LANE, carried here because the lane that filed them has no live owner:\n  S2. coord:declare-intent fired 24× from the OMP subject carrying the PLACEHOLDER \"(active — see coord:presence for current work)\". The agent's real intent reaches no peer, ever. Verified in args_json. NOT re-measured this turn.\n  S3. ~92% of the OMP subject's invocation volume is per-turn bookkeeping (1,325 of 1,592 rows over 158 turns ≈ 8.4 hook calls/turn). RATIO ONLY — no causal link to model behaviour without an ablation. Do not upgrade it to causation.\n  F2. The retrieval that builds injected pointers silently degrades to LEXICAL-ONLY when the query-embed budget blows under host load, and lexical-only is what produces irrelevant pointers. Reproduced live in THIS session again this turn: the orient's own pointer block came back stamped \"semantic leg blocked: query embed failed: query embed exceeded 1200ms budget\". Control for host load before attributing injection sensitivity to a model.\n\nOWNERSHIP WALL: this plan is marked OWNER-DIRECTED, SINGLE OWNER (su-1f60f82c), and that session is ENDED. P-006 onward are unclaimed with no live owner. I am deliberately NOT claiming them — the grading mandate is a different directive — but the plan cannot advance until the owner re-points someone at it.\n\n### D-008 — P-006's stated verification observable is unusable as written — \"papercusp-context\" appears in 0 of ~170 OMP session logs INCLUDING healthy ones; use the extension-load signature instead\nDate: 2026-08-12\nRecorded by su-6ab684ac (GRADE lane, WI-37884) while re-reading live OMP state. Not claiming P-006 — correcting its instrument before someone runs it and trusts the result.\n\n#### The problem with the check as written\n`## Now` currently directs: \"grep its NEW rollout under ~/.papercusp/su-omp-homes for 'Skipped due to pending system advisory' (expect 0) while confirming 'papercusp-context' IS present — 0 cancellations with 0 injections is a FALSE pass, not a fix.\"\n\nThe guard against a false pass is exactly right. The problem is the positive half. I swept EVERY session log under `~/.papercusp/su-omp-homes/` (~170 sessions, 2026-07-01 → 2026-08-12) counting the literal string `papercusp-context`:\n\n  **0 occurrences. In every session. Including sessions that demonstrably worked** (14830 = 2,864 tool calls, 14809, 14799, 15001 = 41 calls).\n\nSo the presence check cannot come back positive on this file, healthy or not. Run as written, P-006 reports \"0 cancellations AND 0 injections\" — which the item's own rule then classifies as a FALSE PASS — for a run that may be perfectly healthy. The check would block on a healthy fix or, worse, be read as evidence the fix failed.\n\n⚠ WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: where injection activity IS observable. `papercusp-context` may be logged to a different file, under a different string, or not logged at all. P-006 needs someone to identify a real positive observable FIRST (read the inject-hook's own logging calls) rather than assume this one exists.\n\n#### A verified-discriminating signature is available in the meantime\nWhile sweeping I found a signature that DOES discriminate, in exactly 1 of ~170 sessions:\n\n  `Failed to load extension … Cannot find module './non-preempting-delivery'`\n\nsession-15143 (2026-08-12T06:05:32Z) logged it TWICE — for `~/.papercusp/papercusp-coord.ts` AND `~/.papercusp/hooks/omp/inject-hook.ts`. Both papercusp extensions failed to load; the session then ran the model fine (2 agent_end, hasText:true, 82k context) and emitted ZERO tool_invocations rows.\n\nThat is this plan's `## Now` caveat (2) coming true and then some: the installed copies were not merely STALE, they were UNLOADABLE, because the install shipped the importers without the `non-preempting-delivery` module that P-001/P-002 introduced. The module exists in the repo at `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/omp/non-preempting-delivery.ts`; it was absent from `~/.papercusp/` entirely.\n\nFiled as **EI-20228871846415832**.\n\n#### Consequence for P-006 that changes how it must be run\nA P-006 run performed during such a window would produce the FALSE PASS this plan is trying to avoid, by a third route nobody has listed: not \"0 cancellations because fixed\", not \"0 cancellations because 0 injections\", but **0 of everything because the hook never loaded**. So P-006's first assertion must be that the extensions LOADED at all:\n\n  `grep -c \"Failed to load extension\" ~/.papercusp/su-omp-homes/session-<id>/logs/omp.*.log`   → expect 0, check this BEFORE anything else\n\n#### Current install state (verify, do not assume)\nBoth installed files were rewritten ~06:45–06:46Z and now contain no `non-preempting-delivery` import (the 226KB `papercusp-coord.ts` appears bundled/inlined), so the window looks CLOSED. I did not confirm by launching a session — \"the import is gone\" is not \"it loads\". The next OMP launch is the test, and whoever performs it should capture the load-failure count as its first datum.\n\n### D-009 — Ownership transferred to su-01d9d; rerank work is explicitly out of scope\nDate: 2026-08-13\nOwner directive, 2026-08-13: Avi assigned su-01d9dd9a-2783-4f75-91c4-94c0b6a25b8b to take charge of this plan. This supersedes the stale single-owner pin to su-1f60f82c and its successor. The plan remains limited to OMP injection delivery, payload quality, client budgets, and injection outcome telemetry. Rerank experiments and the statistical strategy record belong to semantic-search-fingerprint-coverage-2026-08-03, which Avi is assigning to another agent; reranker implementation history lives in local-reranker-gte-modernbert-2026-08-02 and the older search-core-rerank-adoption-2026-05-30 plan. Do not merge those lanes.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-013\n\n### D-010 — P-006 live verification passes on a fresh OMP session\nDate: 2026-08-13\n**CORRECTED FINAL VERDICT: PASS.** Fresh visible OMP subject `su-052a5feb-d316-4392-914a-0980fd598b6a` (thread `019ff996-cf25-7000-b900-1d97da047971`) ran real tool calls across turns. Turn-start and mid-turn context were present. Every tool in the three-call grep batch completed with a real transcript result: path-not-found, no matches, and timeout; the next model turn explicitly reasoned from those outputs. There are zero synthetic skip result records and zero `interrupt_skipped` records in the rollout. Focused run 2760e052-6ddc-400e-80c9-46070e1e3d87 passed 524/524. **Correction history:** an intermediate retraction misread `memory_recall_query_text` row 265453. That table stores the derived retrieval QUERY; `deriveQueryDetailed` builds a grep query from its `pattern` and `path`. The row contains `Skipped due to pending system advisory` because that was the search PATTERN used to verify absence, not because a tool returned a skipped result. The false retraction is withdrawn; the pass stands.\n\n### D-011 — P-006 reopened: late-arriving live telemetry falsified D-010's zero-cancellation verdict\nDate: 2026-08-13\n**RETRACTED AS WRONG 2026-08-13 by su-01d9d.** This decision treated `memory_recall_query_text.query_text` as tool-result text. The writer does not have that meaning: `mid-turn-context.ts` calls `deriveBatchQueryDetailed`; for OMP `grep`, `deriveQueryDetailed` uses the tool INPUT fields `pattern`, `path`, and `glob`. Row 265453 therefore records the subject's three searches FOR the phrase, not three occurrences OF the phrase. The rollout's actual toolResult records all completed normally, and the following model turn reasoned from their real outputs. D-010's final corrected PASS is authoritative. The surviving lesson: before interpreting retained query text, read both the persistence writer and the query derivation vocabulary; query text is neither a raw request payload nor a tool-result log.\n\n### D-012 — P-007 verdict: the 73-character query is correlated XD indirection, not an empty-input join failure\nDate: 2026-08-13\nMEASURED VERDICT. The prime correlation hypothesis is falsified. memory_recall_stats row 179646 (2026-08-12T00:06:18.225Z, OMP session su-0e500929-04c4-4efb-97be-4b648c37467a) stores the exact derived query xd://mcp__papercusp_su_tools_invoke · xd://mcp__papercusp_su_tools_invoke. Its raw OMP transcript (session-14830, thread 019ff24e-f2fd-7000-a2ff-36c02fc83c32) shows the originating batch one second earlier: assistant toolCall ids call_526485 and call_526498 were both native write calls to that XD path, with their content fields carrying tools:invoke envelopes for coord:inbox and scheduler:get_next; both real toolResult records followed with matching ids. buildToolCallDigest therefore joined input to output correctly. The length is exact: 35 characters per path × 2 plus the 3-character separator = 73. Row 264277 is a control: its 73-character query is the ordinary Bash command captured from the matching OMP transcript. ROOT CAUSE. OMP exposes dynamic-device/MCP calls as native write operations. The current OMP write vocabulary derives only path/file_path, while the actual inner tool name and arguments live in content. The recall layer consequently embeds generic XD device paths instead of the agent's investigation. This is systemic in the bounded retained window after reading the writer and filtering workspace=papercusp-workspace, client=omp, surface=mid-turn: 78/162 rows contain xd:// across 5/14 sessions; 43 rows across 3 sessions are the bare tools_invoke path. This is query starvation, not missing input. CONSEQUENCE. P-014 owns the repair plus exact-shape recurrence test and post-deploy rate check. P-010 is now blocked by P-014: per-client budget tuning before the query carries the inner signal would optimize against meaningless relevance measurements.\nRelated: P-007, P-010, P-014\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/omp-context-injection-and-behavior-2026-08-12 (\"OMP context injection + agent behavior — stop the delivery channel from destroying work, t\"): no plan update since 2026-08-14 (57 days idle), 11/14 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"spawner-sidecar-cluster-fanout-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — spawner sidecar collapses to one per host without losing orphan detection","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-12","owner":"su-07ad4465-9448-46e9-a2b5-2ddc5d4c3ef5","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — spawner sidecar collapses to one per host without losing orphan detection\nslug: spawner-sidecar-cluster-fanout-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-12\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-07ad4465-9448-46e9-a2b5-2ddc5d4c3ef5\n---\n\n# Acceptance — spawner sidecar collapses to one per host without losing orphan detection\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it.
