Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Resolve and pin the latest green main commit plus desktop submodule; run release preflight and record provenance. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38506 released\n## Phase — Release\n\n### D-001 — Freeze all 0.0.17-alpha platform lanes to the verified green source pin\nDate: 2026-08-13\nAll Linux, Windows, and macOS 0.0.17-alpha builds must use the already-recovered and preflighted isolated checkout at superproject ffc6da5355a34d9652538fcbe1f64508e41191cf, libs/papercusp 3ece6c100a63727af8304b719fc7fe943c5ee54c, and papercusp-desktop c5884509e559da9f7da90e76ebdf829e1a7c9e36. Do not silently rebase to a later green candidate after build work starts; a source-pin change would invalidate P-001 and requires a fresh precheck. The existing clone is /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp-relcut-0017.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Retire the failed D-001 source pin; replacement pin must contain the seed-key fix and pass a fresh precheck\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe sole cut from D-001's frozen green source ffc6da5355 failed before platform build at 08:40:35 EDT. The authoritative cut log shows the staged public seed retained an identity-bearing included-row key (`plan-parts` in `corestore/db/000012.log`), and the seed-identity guard correctly refused it. No platform artifact was emitted. Therefore ffc6da5355 is not a releasable 0.0.17 source and must not be re-cut. The durable fix is b33bd6c79df (with formatting follow-up 792508f684) and its focused fold/seed regression passes 58/58 tests. Wait for a fresh green main pin that contains this fix, then run P-001's complete precheck again on a newly pinned isolated checkout and record that exact replacement superproject/libs/desktop tuple before any corrected cut. Never patch or build from staging, never reuse the failed seed, and never launch a duplicate while a canonical cut is active.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-003 — D-003: 65b3fbd1 red is stale; replacement must include verified tip 0219651a\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe candidate 65b3fbd1 checkpoint produced a real red event, but its built-in re-triage classified it stale-candidate: all 12 failing files passed at verified head 0219651abccfba56f1f846e30e1c471351b2f4d1. The run could not auto-refire because its deadline was exhausted. The unit released successfully at 10:35 EDT. Any replacement verdict must judge 0219651a or a descendant and must be fired only after the 240-second quiet cut plus margin; 0219651a committed at 10:34:25 EDT, so earliest safe fire is 10:39:25 EDT. D-002 remains in force: retired ffc6da5355 must never be re-cut. Do not edit or chase the stale failing set.\n\n### D-004 — 0219651a red is old test-lane contamination; replacement must include test-config f18df7a+\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe exact 0219651a checkpoint is a real red, but its eight failures across five operator-core files are the old non-isolated lane contamination signature, not five product regressions: zero-duration timer measurements, four 180s deadline hangs, and inherited module-registration state. Candidate 0219651a pins libs/test-config at 91dd7ced. Descendant f18df7a adds the load-bearing classifier rules for fake timers/global state and expectation-wrapped dynamic imports, with source comments naming these same failures. On canonical committed HEAD 5896b863, all exact failures pass in their correct lanes (pure: 4 files/29 tests; isolated stateful stop-fanout: 1 file/1 test). Therefore do not edit or chase the product files from this red. Preserve the current salvage unit until it releases the singleton, then fire exactly one fresh full checkpoint on a quiet descendant whose libs/test-config gitlink is f18df7a or later; only that fresh verdict may become the replacement release pin.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-005 — Only a post-2e9532ad checkpoint may qualify the replacement release source; WI-38506 owns the single successor launch\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe active singleton 3c630bc788fecaf99e3b37f9c7210810d7a3a662 may finish for diagnostic evidence, but it cannot qualify P-001 even if green: exact git ancestry proves completed WI-38533 commit 2e9532adb3a121c2745d8617db73947f6c4c5cab is a descendant and absent from 3c630bc7. Preserve the productive singleton until terminal. After it exits and the singleton/retriage rails clear, launch exactly one quiet current-staging successor containing 2e9532ad; WI-38506/su-10ecd is the sole launch owner. Peer su-cb2b acknowledged this split and will not compete. No Linux, Windows, or macOS build begins until that successor is authoritative green and P-001 binds a fresh source/libs/desktop tuple.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-006 — Retire 937dc9ee's stale-launcher run; c1657644 is the sole repaired successor\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe first successor attempt at 937dc9ee was a real 269-second run but is not an eligible verdict: `release:checkpoint-run` was served by deployed control-plane code at ffc6da5355 and launched the staging suite without current staging's required `PAPERCUSP_MANUAL_GREEN_CHECKPOINT_WATCHDOG_MS=7215000` environment, reproducing the equal 3-hour self/systemd deadline race that killed 9e1870eb. WI-38506's owner deliberately stopped 937dc9ee and recorded its displacement in the per-run forensic log. Candidate c1657644 is the sole active repaired successor and the manual checkpoint unit is loaded active/running with zero restarts and no warning-level journal entries in the first ten minutes. Do not fire another checkpoint or chase the stale public five-red blob. No Android, Linux, Windows, or macOS release build may begin until c1657644 reaches an authoritative terminal green verdict and establishes the replacement source pin.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-007 — Live run-lock, not transient unit state, governs checkpoint liveness\nDate: 2026-08-14\nFor any green-checkpoint candidate, the shared per-root run-lock is the authoritative cross-origin liveness signal. `packages/operator-core/lib/git-pipeline-position.ts` documents and implements a live `isCheckpointRunLockHeldCheap` read: a held lock is positive, PID-verified evidence and always wins; a not-held lock wins except for the documented <=90s manual-run startup sliver where a fresh cached systemd observation may precede lock acquisition. Therefore a dead/stale manual-unit observation alone does not establish terminality and cannot authorize replacement. Before changing the singleton, reconcile the live lock owner, terminal result marker/log, and release authority. Applied on 2026-08-14: peer retracted a dead-unit inference; c1657644's live run-lock plus advancing exact log required preserving the run.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"drain-admission-integrity-remediation-2026-08-13","title":"DRAIN admission integrity, duplicate cleanup, and net-negative canary","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: DRAIN admission integrity, duplicate cleanup, and net-negative canary\nslug: drain-admission-integrity-remediation-2026-08-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nspecTriad: required\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-006 is blocked by D-004. The only D-003-authorized affected candidate completed with status=failed (6 of 28 tasks failed) and AFFECTED_TESTS_TREE_DRIFT from runStartHead b8de1000 to reportHead f4d87493 across 9 commits/22 files; 5 tracked paths remained dirty at end. WI-40113 and P-001–P-005 are complete. No snapshot, storage census, canary, or automatic rerun was performed.\n\n**Next:** Diagnose the six failed affected tasks and the concurrent tree drift. After the staging tree is settled clean, obtain an explicit fresh-run authorization, then run exactly one new candidate and re-evaluate P-006 gates; do not launch another candidate automatically.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- While DRAIN mode is active, an agent must not create an improvement, bug, issue, or observation merely because it notices a suspected incidental defect. A new defect record is permitted only when the defect directly blocks the scoped drain, and the record must identify that blocking scope.\n- Every admitted defect must carry a stable identity key and persisted dedup-coverage evidence. If required semantic deduplication is unavailable or inconclusive, admission fails closed instead of silently minting another bug.\n- Drain admission must be severity-aware and must expose opened, terminaled, and net-flow counts from the same logical-item writer semantics. A circuit breaker must stop further defect admission when the active drain is producing work at or above its terminal rate.\n- Backlog cleanup must begin with a restorable snapshot and a mutation-free manifest that distinguishes exact duplicates, probable same-root findings, distinct lookalikes, and physical twin rows.\n- Logical cleanup must preserve canonical evidence and record structured duplicate/same-root links. Physical twin repair must audit and reconcile references before a dedicated migration removes redundant rows.\n- Regression tests and a bounded canary must prove the filing exception, fail-closed admission, uniqueness evidence, absence of physical twins, and net-negative drain flow.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing mechanisms rather than adding a parallel drain system. Put the behavioral exception in the generated DRAIN policy and live mode-registry contract, and reconcile the later base-persona filing rule so the rendered prompt has one unambiguous precedence rule. Add render/unit and behavioral-scenario coverage. Trace the current improvement/work-item writer and extend its existing lexical/semantic dedup path with stable identity, coverage persistence, direct-blocker provenance, and a fail-closed DRAIN policy gate. Extend the existing claim-spec-aware drain analytics/oracle with severity-banded opened-versus-terminal flow and a reusable admission circuit-breaker verdict. Reuse the current backup verb and ledger/link writers for a dry-run cleanup manifest; apply logical duplicate dispositions before any storage repair. Implement physical-twin repair as a dedicated database migration only after reference/FK audits and manifest review, retaining rollback via the snapshot. Verify each layer with focused tests, affected/full tests, dry-run invariants, and a bounded canary whose acceptance threshold is negative net bug flow.\n\n## Phase 1 — Stop amplification\n\n- **P-001** `done` Implement the DRAIN-mode filing exception: suppress incidental suspected-defect creation while retaining defects that directly block the active drain, with regression tests. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38401 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Harden defect admission with stable identity keys, semantic deduplication, and persisted coverage evidence; degraded or unavailable dedup must not silently admit another bug. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38403 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add severity-aware queue economics, net-flow monitoring, and a circuit breaker when a drain admits work faster than it terminales work. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38411 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Repair the ledger\n\n- **P-004** `done` Create a pre-destructive snapshot and dry-run manifest classifying exact duplicates, same-root findings, distinct lookalikes, and physical twin rows without mutating data. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38444 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Preserve evidence while terminaling confirmed logical duplicates with structured links; audit references and repair physical twins through a dedicated migration. blocked-by: P-004 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38468 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Prove behavior\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Run focused and affected/full verification plus a bounded canary drain; accept only with persisted uniqueness evidence, no storage twins, and net-negative bug flow. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005 importance: urgent — note: D-004: single D-003-authorized affected candidate failed closed. Measured terminal AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT status=failed tasks=28 failed=6, with AFFECTED_TESTS_TREE_DRIFT runStartHead=b8de1000 reportHead=f4d87493 commits=9 changedFiles=22; P006_TRACKED_AT_END=5. Per D-003, no snapshot/census/canary or automatic rerun is authorized. Diagnosis/fresh explicit authorization required after a settled clean head.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — DRAIN suppresses incidental defect filing and cleanup remains evidence-preserving\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDuring DRAIN, agents do not file suspected incidental defects. A defect may be registered only when it directly blocks the scoped drain. Admission must carry stable identity and persisted dedup coverage; lack of coverage fails closed. Cleanup never fuzzy-bulk-deletes: it snapshots first, manifests proposed actions, preserves canonical history and structured duplicate/same-root links, and repairs physical twins only after reference auditing.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-002 — Finish-drain fleet admits the direct replay blocker before P-006 canary\nDate: 2026-08-21\nAuthoritative work_items:claimable under fleet spec rev 6 matched only WI-38508 and excluded it on blockedDep because WI-40113 is open. WI-40113 is the direct physical-twin replay blocker for P-006 but has no sourcePlanSlug, so a plan-only filter makes the fleet permanently idle. The fleet claim spec must be leader-authored as ANY(plan = drain-admission-integrity-remediation-2026-08-13, id in [WI-40113]), max one concurrent claim, severity-first. Global dependency floors remain authoritative: the member takes WI-40113 first, must not create/duplicate a release or Cargo/checkpoint writer, completes it only after the existing singleton produces eligible GREEN and live replay-suppression proof, then WI-38508 becomes claimable for the bounded net-negative canary.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-003 — Authorize one clean-head affected rerun before P-006 canary\nDate: 2026-09-01\nWI-40113 is terminal done and no affected verifier is live, so the P-006 holder is authorized to run exactly one fresh reduced affected candidate after the canonical staging tree is settled by the sanctioned git-sync path. Before launch, verify the tracked tree is clean, record runStartHead, and verify no competing affected process. Preserve the existing bounded resource profile and canonical aggregate/tree-drift reporting. Only terminal canonical GREEN with no tree drift opens snapshot/census/canary work. Any failed, indeterminate, or drifted terminal result closes the gate and requires diagnosis; it does not authorize another automatic rerun. At decision time staging HEAD cca50c46fbfb045701f57fc747359174596ae17c was not yet eligible because 19 tracked paths were modified.\n\n### D-004 — D-004: D-003 affected candidate failed closed on tree drift\nDate: 2026-09-01\nDate: 2026-09-01\nThe single D-003-authorized affected candidate (task 0mtir5ha3wru9nn1t5f, run token 1557680-72535fbf) reached a terminal non-green result and must close the P-006 gate. Measured: its log reports `AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT status=failed tasks=28 failed=6 quarantinedFailed=0 timedOutTasks=0 undeterminedTasks=0`; the same log reports `runStartHead=b8de1000768cfaa5bc8a379294c3abde73f4afb4 reportHead=f4d874934258c79b7ffb586e110253cc47a3c57f commits=9 changedFiles=22` and `AFFECTED_TESTS_TREE_DRIFT`. The runner exited with P006_EXIT=1 and P006_TRACKED_AT_END=5. Per D-003, this is a failed/drifted terminal result: no snapshot, storage census, canary, or automatic rerun is authorized. WI-38508 remains blocked pending diagnosis and explicit fresh-run authorization after a settled clean head.\nRelated: P-006\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"drain-control-plane-resilience-2026-08-13","title":"Drain Control Plane Resilience — Verified Recovery and Canonical Work","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Drain Control Plane Resilience — Verified Recovery and Canonical Work\nslug: drain-control-plane-resilience-2026-08-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** APPROVED AND IN EXECUTION. Avi approved start-to-finish implementation on 2026-08-13 and required acceptance grading to launch a fresh dedicated headless non-implementer rather than distract an existing peer. The requirements/design spec triad is complete; P-010 and D-006 encode the grader workflow. WI-38399 is being closed, then Phase 1 begins in dependency order. No implementation claim should skip the lossless-foundations ordering.\n\n**Next:** Close WI-38399 with plan revision 20 evidence; convert and claim P-001; inspect the universal result-door writer and existing overflow-family work before editing.\n\n## Goal\n\nMake large fleet drains recoverable, measurable, and self-correcting across partial launches, compaction/carry transitions, duplicate filing storms, scheduler exclusions, and oversized tool reads—without creating parallel control planes.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Every model-facing MCP read must return parseable, bounded JSON under the transport cap; omitted detail must be recoverable through a stable cursor, including nested `tools:invoke` calls.\n- Managed long-running work must retain a stable task/run identity across compaction and carry, support status/tail/terminal reads through that identity, and prevent duplicate restart.\n- Fleet launch and recovery must prove one canary through CLI boot and a successful tool invocation before bounded rollout; partial cohorts and recovery state must be explicit.\n- Queue reads must separate canonical issues from repeated occurrences, preserve every occurrence's provenance, coalesce low-diversity duplicate storms, and never suppress a novel critical finding.\n- A critical dependency excluded by a claim spec must be surfaced with a typed, ownership-preserving escape path rather than silently stranding the DAG.\n- One leader read must reconstruct authoritative membership transitions, speaking liveness, claim stock/flow, canonical occurrence counts, job/gate/carry events, and corrections across epochs.\n- Acceptance grading must be performed by a newly launched, dedicated headless non-implementer agent—not an existing peer—with frozen evidence, distinct identity, no implementation mutations, an emitted scorecard, visible failure/retry state, and terminal exit.\n- The complete system must pass adversarial integration scenarios for every audited failure class and the plan must remain unshippable until an independent acceptance scorecard succeeds.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing control-plane seams rather than introducing a parallel store, scheduler, launch loop, or dashboard state. Bound and project results inside the universal result door before serialization, with stable continuation cursors owned by the producing tool. Persist long-job attachment in the managed task ledger so carry successors resolve a durable task identity instead of a process-local handle. Evolve `fleet:launch-on-plan` into a transaction with capacity preflight, a verified canary, bounded waves, and explicit partial-failure recovery. Model duplicate reports as append-only occurrences linked to canonical `work_items` clusters through the existing provenance/link graph; compute admission entropy over canonical clusters while preserving critical novelty. Extend scheduler claim-spec and leader-brief surfaces with a typed excluded-dependency remedy. Compose the cross-epoch cockpit only from authoritative existing writers. Add a managed, idempotent headless-grader launch path to the plan completion gate; freeze its plan revision, rubric, decisions, evidence, and rerun commands, restrict it to grading plus `scorecards:emit`, and terminate it after verdict. Implement in dependency order: losslessness first, then queue automation, then cockpit/grader, then adversarial verification and independent scoring.\n\n## Audit Basis\n\nWI-38383 verified three material failure classes: launcher heartbeats were mistaken for working agents until tool-invocation liveness disproved it; raw work-item row flow overstated canonical bug volume because at least 455 of 2,949 cohort rows were confirmed duplicates; and required audit/feedback reads repeatedly exceeded the transport cap despite projection guidance. The same run also lost a long-running integration handle across carry, exposed a critical dependency excluded by claim-spec admission, and required manual reconstruction of fleet stock/flow across epochs.\n\n## Success Measures\n\n- A fleet launch exposes an authoritative readiness ladder through first successful tool invocation and rolls forward in verified canary waves.\n- A managed long-running job can be reattached and read after compaction/carry without restarting or guessing from logs.\n- Work-item dashboards distinguish canonical issues from occurrences; burst admission collapses duplicate exhaust without suppressing novel critical findings.\n- A typed dependency escape path prevents claim-spec exclusions from stranding critical blockers.\n- Every model-facing tool read returns valid bounded JSON or a stable cursor, including nested tools:invoke calls.\n- One leader read reconstructs membership, speaking liveness, stock/flow, gate/carry events, and corrections across epochs.\n\n## Reuse Map\n\nExtend the universal result door (EI-20244970883634313), managed task ledger and process surfaces (EI-20313008550768243), fleet:launch-on-plan and readiness verdicts (EI-20191406339204204, EI-8995), work-item dedup/links (EI-19374777429175961), scheduler claim-spec routing (EI-20313352047106971), and fleet:leader-brief/audit feed (EI-6803, EI-20191482908659901, WI-7130). Do not introduce replacement stores, schedulers, or dashboards with independent state.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- Replacing the fleet scheduler, task ledger, work-item store, result door, or leader-brief surface.\n- Treating raw created/closed row counts as unique-valid bug counts.\n- Adding dashboard-only state that is not backed by authoritative writers.\n\n## Phase 1 — Lossless foundations\n\n- **P-001** `done` Make the universal MCP result door structurally bounded before serialization: direct tools and nested tools:invoke must return valid JSON, apply projection before the transport cap, and provide stable resumable cursors for spilled detail. Extend EI-20244970883634313 and close/reconcile the scorecards, plans, sessions, fleet, and work-item overflow family with contract tests. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38402 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Add carry-safe attachment for managed long-running jobs. Persist a stable task/run identity in the existing task ledger, expose status/tail/terminal markers through that identity, and let a compaction successor reattach without relying on process-local unified-exec handles. Build on EI-20313008550768243 and prove no duplicate restart after carry. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38433 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Turn fleet launch and recovery into one verified transaction: preflight capacity, launch one canary, require CLI boot + first successful tool invocation, roll out bounded waves, and surface partial-failure recovery/rollback state. Extend fleet:launch-on-plan, EI-20191406339204204, and EI-8995; heartbeat/join alone must never count as readiness. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38513 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Canonical queue and escape paths\n\n- **P-004** `done` Represent repeated findings as canonical issue clusters plus append-only occurrences/evidence. Centralize dedup across improvements:capture and work_items:create, preserve provenance and recurrence counts, and expose canonical-versus-raw counts in reads. Extend EI-19374777429175961 and the existing duplicates links rather than creating another issue store. importance: high — note: ← WI-38577 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add a queue-admission entropy circuit breaker over canonical clusters and emitters. Detect sudden low-diversity filing bursts, coalesce occurrences without losing evidence, bound scheduler load, and always pass through novel critical findings. Include replay tests using the 2026-08-12 cohort shape and report both raw occurrences and canonical stock. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-38677 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Add a typed dependency escape lane for critical blockers excluded by a fleet claim spec. The scheduler/leader brief must identify the excluded dependency, name the concrete safe remedy (spec widen, outside-lane placement, or direct leader claim), preserve ownership, and prevent silent DAG deadlock. Start from EI-20313352047106971 and existing scheduler claim-spec surfaces. importance: high — note: ← WI-38663 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Cross-epoch leader cockpit\n\n- **P-007** `done` Extend fleet:leader-brief into a cross-epoch campaign recorder/cockpit backed only by authoritative writers: membership transitions, speaking/tool-call liveness, claim stock/flow, terminal attribution, canonical occurrence counts, gate/carry/job events, and explicit corrections/retractions. Reuse EI-6803, EI-20191482908659901, WI-7130, and the current leader-brief delta model. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-38678 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Implement a dedicated acceptance-grader launch path in the plan completion system. When an implementing agent reaches acceptance-rubric grading, it must launch a fresh headless non-implementer agent through the existing managed agent-launch/task-ledger seam instead of recruiting an active peer. Pass the frozen plan revision, rubric, decisions, implementation evidence, and exact rerun commands; enforce a distinct grader identity and read-only implementation scope; emit the scorecard through scorecards:emit; expose launch/liveness/failure state; make retries idempotent; and terminate the grader after its verdict. The plan must remain unshippable until this dedicated grader succeeds. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38679 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Adversarial verification\n\n- **P-008** `done` Run one adversarial integration campaign that forces the observed classes: partial 50-member launch, canary failure, carry during a long integration job, duplicate filing storm, claim-spec-excluded critical dependency, oversized direct and nested tool reads, and leader compaction. Verify no silent work loss, false readiness, invalid JSON, duplicate restart, or raw/canonical metric confusion. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-010 — note: Accepted live: handler commit 8500d403 is green-pinned and deployed by 075291b75eaf; direct :3070 and proxy :9071 both report automatic verified runtime-probed locks; local adversarial campaign and gate repairs green. Evidence fact p008-live-accepted-2026-08-14 and WI-38744 completion.\n- **P-009** `wip` After implementation, author the required acceptance rubric from the finished behavior, obtain a non-implementer scorecard with concrete evidence, run a bounded live canary drain, and publish before/after measurements for recovery time, stranded blockers, duplicate admission ratio, result-overflow failures, and leader reconstruction cost. blocked-by: P-008 — note: P-008 live acceptance is closed; advancing the next dependency-unblocked code-only audit item.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Readiness is speaking, not presence\nDate: 2026-08-13\nA launcher heartbeat, process existence, durable join, or presence row is not evidence that an agent is working. Launch/recovery readiness requires successful CLI boot and at least one real tool invocation (or a stronger completed-first-turn verdict), with partial cohorts reported explicitly.\nRelated: P-003, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-002 — Canonical issue stock and occurrence flow are separate metrics\nDate: 2026-08-13\nCreated/closed work-item rows measure row flow, not unique-valid bug stock. Every queue, dashboard, and retrospective must expose canonical clusters separately from occurrences and duplicates, carry the writer/units, and state any uncertainty floor or cap.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-007, P-009\n\n### D-003 — Extend the existing control-plane seams\nDate: 2026-08-13\nImplementation must reuse the universal result door, managed task ledger, fleet:launch-on-plan, work-item/coord_links store, scheduler claim specs, and fleet:leader-brief. A new parallel store, scheduler, launch loop, or dashboard-only state requires a new recorded decision proving the existing seam cannot fit.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-004 — Writer-verified measurements only\nDate: 2026-08-13\nBefore any acceptance claim or reported number, read the code that writes it and record its units, scale, exclusions, and caps. Contradictory instruments trigger a writer audit; they do not justify choosing the more convenient reading.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-005 — Losslessness precedes automation\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDeliver bounded results, carry-safe job identity, and verified launch recovery before adding admission automation or the consolidated cockpit. Automation may not suppress evidence, restart an in-flight job, or turn an unknown state into a healthy/zero reading.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance grading uses a fresh dedicated headless agent\nDate: 2026-08-13\nA plan implementer must not recruit or message an existing peer to satisfy the non-implementer acceptance-scorecard gate. The plan completion path launches a new headless agent dedicated to grading that plan, with a distinct identity, frozen plan/rubric/decision/evidence context, no implementation mutation authority, idempotent retry semantics, and a terminal lifecycle after scorecards:emit. Launch failure leaves the plan unshippable and visible; it never falls back silently to distracting a peer.\nRelated: P-009, P-010\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"gate-suite-speedup-lane-split-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: the pure/stateful lane split ships the gate speedup without spending the gate's safety budget to get it","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-13","owner":"su-67b9d93a-050e-49d2-9f67-30786f786b39","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: the pure/stateful lane split ships the gate speedup without spending the gate's safety budget to get it\nslug: gate-suite-speedup-lane-split-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-67b9d93a-050e-49d2-9f67-30786f786b39\n---\n\n# Acceptance: the pure/stateful lane split ships the gate speedup without spending the gate's safety budget to get it\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for gate-suite-speedup-2026-08-12, authored after implementation.\n\nThe plan's goal is gate CYCLE TIME, and D-001 fixes its acceptance explicitly: \"a measured reduction in gate wall-time with coverage preserved\" — NOT whether `main` goes green (a peer owns the live red under WI-38026). So a grader must not credit or penalise this plan for the gate's colour.\n\nThe hard part of this plan was never the speedup; it was shipping it without quietly degrading the gate's ability to catch real defects. D-006 through D-011 establish that fork reuse trades isolation for speed, and D-039 showed the trade can leak into the gate's own flake budget where nothing would report it. Criteria 3-5 exist because each names a way this could look finished while having made the gate worse — a false green is strictly worse than the red it replaces (green-checkpoint.ts:2951-2960).\n\nGrade against evidence in the plan's Decisions (esp. D-034, D-036, D-037, D-038, D-039), the tree, and the run logs under /tmp/lane-measure/. The grader must NOT be the implementer.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hud-pot-scope-and-dropdown-2026-08-13","title":"Fix HUD pot scoping and viewport-bounded selectors","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Fix HUD pot scoping and viewport-bounded selectors\nslug: hud-pot-scope-and-dropdown-2026-08-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-13\n---\n\n# Fix HUD pot scoping and viewport-bounded selectors\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Make the shared Select viewport-aware with bounded height, scrolling, and contained overscroll. importance: high — note: ← WI-38524 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Make selected pot scope authoritative across HUD Goals, Sessions, Plans, and Work items, including All Pots and descendant sub-pots. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-38525 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Audit and fix every top-level tab that exposes the pot selector, including Overview and other selector-bearing views. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-38526 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Add regression tests for dropdown constraints and pot-scope query behavior. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-38527 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Run focused tests and Verdict browser verification at desktop and constrained viewport heights. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-38528 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Reuse AdvShell's resolved scope as the one pot-scope authority\nDate: 2026-08-13\nAdvShell already owns ?slug + ?scope and the live harness registry. Extend its AdvScope context with the resolved harness slug set, pass that scope into lower-layer HudView through a Vite bridge, and use it for Sessions, Plans, Goals, and Work items. Extend existing goals.list/workItems.byHarness/workItems.stats/workItems.delta24h reads rather than creating parallel query names. All Pots means workspace-wide; expanded means selected pot plus descendants; self means selected pot only. Overview keeps its deliberately workspace-wide tiles, but its documented pot-scoped work-item stats/delta must consume the same resolved set.\n\n### D-002 — Scope consumers must render under AdvShell's provider boundary\nDate: 2026-08-13\nA hook call in AdvIndexPage before its returned <AdvShell> cannot observe AdvScopeContext even if its JSX appears textually near the shell; it reads the context default and silently makes HUD workspace-wide. Keep useAdvScope in a child component that AdvShell renders beneath AdvScopeContext.Provider. Route tests must make scope availability provider-order-sensitive rather than stubbing the hook to return a scoped value everywhere.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"omp-host-local-model-catalog-2026-08-13","title":"Expose OMP host-local installed model catalog in launch surfaces","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Expose OMP host-local installed model catalog in launch surfaces\nslug: omp-host-local-model-catalog-2026-08-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-29\n---\n\n# Expose OMP host-local installed model catalog in launch surfaces\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Inspect and document the existing OMP model constants, launch-options route, omp:config surface, gateway model rewriting, launcher state, and focused tests; record the exact extension seams. importance: high — note: ← WI-38519 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement a cached readOmpModelCatalog() adapter around target-user `omp models --json`, preserving exact provider/id selectors and OMP metadata without adding a second model database. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-38521 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Expose OMP-installed models through the existing launch-options endpoint and a read-only omp:config catalog operation, with explicit availability semantics and clear failure behavior. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-38529 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Update the new-session launcher to present the seven native aliases separately from OMP-installed models and launch catalog entries with backend=omp plus the exact provider/id selector. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-38532 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Enforce account compatibility: direct/default launches use the selected OMP provider; gateway auto/pinned routing maps only compatible models to papercusp-gateway/<id> and rejects incompatible combinations without fallback substitution. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-38537 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Add focused unit/UI regression coverage for catalog caching, metadata mapping, grouping, selector fidelity, and incompatible account routing; run affected tests and typechecks. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-38558 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `dropped` Verify pipeline position and green-checkpoint status, clear any red gate that blocks the change, and record completion evidence for every plan item. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-38559 dropped\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — OMP registry remains the catalog source of truth\nDate: 2026-08-13\nRead the target user's live OMP catalog via a cached adapter around `omp models --json`. Do not copy OMP model records into a Papercusp-owned database. The catalog represents enabled/auth-configured availability, not credential validity or upstream health.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Native aliases and OMP-installed models are separate launch classes\nDate: 2026-08-13\nKeep the current seven Papercusp-native aliases as their own stable list. Every discovered OMP model uses backend `omp` and its exact provider/id selector; UI labels may be friendly but launch payloads must preserve identity exactly.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-003 — Gateway routing must fail closed on incompatible models\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDefault/system routing launches the selected OMP provider directly. Auto or pinned gateway routing may rewrite only explicitly compatible models to `papercusp-gateway/<id>`; incompatible provider/account combinations return a clear validation error and must never fall back to a default model.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plan-completion-audit-and-acceptance-verdict-2026-08-13","title":"Plan completion: code-truth audit + an acceptance verdict the gate actually reads","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: \"Plan completion: code-truth audit + an acceptance verdict the gate actually reads\"\nslug: plan-completion-audit-and-acceptance-verdict-2026-08-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-25\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** [leader 2026-08-23 17:28 EDT] Plan v147/hash 70b51ddf was re-read with exact D-016/D-021/D-028 from the canonical decision index. D-028 makes live su-ccd31 the sole WI-40086 serializer/emitter/checkpoint/deploy/routine authority; D-016/D-021 admission remains conjunctive. Generation 2 is declared/unfired with actual_sha/fired_at/fired_by null. EI-21240803104955276 is terminal done: fix 351e514 is in direct origin dd4228, registry parses, an env-cleared unscoped ptool read succeeds, focused registry tests pass 34/34, and both changed files are type-clean. Stable-C remains false: sample A local 82d65262 != direct origin dd4228df with 2 dirt rows; sample B kept unequal tips and dirt changed to 3. Pins are aligned, registered nested repos clean, and locks/waiters empty. Current dirt is setup-release-checkout-workspace-builds.test.ts plus social platform-registry.ts/storm-policy.ts. WI-40905 owner su-867d is live/current with real tool activity through 17:27 and remains the active exact-witness repair lane; no stall or takeover is warranted. Gate RED-35 and checkpoint run-lock inactive. release:trace's stale release-fixer owner-gone label conflicts with D-028/WI-40086 live ownership; existing EI-212654 tracks that detector issue. No gate, release, routine, deploy, generation, or acceptance mutation occurred.\n\n**Next:** Preserve WI-40905 while its live owner progresses. On its terminal source/test checkpoint, rebuild the current sidecar and rerun the exact carry-safe witness; admit only OVERALL PASS with required K3/K4b evidence. Then verify all writer dependencies terminal or D-021-frozen, locks/waiters empty, root+nested clean, local/direct staging equal twice, and run-lock idle. Only su-ccd31 may emit generation 2, run one fresh checkpoint, deploy green, verify parity/live acceptance, and resume the routine. Leader wakes push-first on fleet transitions with a 1200s warm fallback.\n\n## Goal\n\nClose the gap named in EI-20219912008114544: *\"a gate that checks completeness is not checking correctness.\"* Today `plans:set-plan-status → shipped` verifies only that an acceptance rubric exists, that every criterion carries *some* rating, and that the grader is not the rubric's author. It never reads what the ratings SAY, never checks the plan's own items, and never reads the code.\n\nMeasured before starting: 181 criterion ratings ever emitted against acceptance rubrics (157 healthy / 23 degraded / 1 unknown / 0 fail), 8 plans shipped carrying degraded criteria, and `claude-md-projection-from-pg-2026-08-10` shipped with `P-009` still `todo`.\n\nPrior art: `borrow-plan-completion-audit-2026-08-09` ran this audit by hand on one plan under the same owner instruction and found a real defect (its D-001). This plan mechanises that practice.\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` Migration: `harness_shared.plan_audits` — one row per audit pass, history retained. Number via `scripts/next-migration.mjs`, written at the `.DRAFT` path, armed once tested — note: ← WI-38590 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` `plans:audit` verb — per-item verdict + citations, resolving `code`/`test` citations against the tree at WRITE time. Refusals: `unknown_item`, `citation_unresolved`, `uncited_verdict`, `finding_undisposed`, `drop_without_reason` — note: ← WI-40112 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Read side: surface the latest audit on `plans:get` beside `acceptanceRubric` — note: ← WI-40130 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Gate refusals `acceptance_unaudited` + `audit_coverage_stale` + `audit_citations_unresolved` in `plan-acceptance-gate.ts`, ordered ahead of the rubric checks — note: ← WI-40131 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Gate refusal `plan_items_unfinished` — todo/blocked/needs-human block, `dropped` passes — under its own flag — note: ← WI-40134 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Acceptance verdict: `scorecards:emit` accepts `acceptance:{verdict,reasoning}` for `kind:'acceptance'`; gate check 02 requires an `accept` recorded by the implementer, pre-existing gradings grandfathered — note: ← WI-40136 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Require a reason on a `dropped` item flip in `plans:set-status` — note: ← WI-40137 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` `plans:set-plan-status { status:'shipped', force:{reason} }` — bypasses the audit gate, stamps a permanent visible marker on the plan — note: ← WI-40139 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Flags `PLAN_CODE_AUDIT_GATE` + `PLAN_ITEM_COMPLETION_GATE`, both default ON — note: ← WI-40140 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Add a citation-spot-check criterion to the four `plan-class-*` rubrics so the independent grader audits the audit — note: ← WI-40141 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Vitest coverage incl. a deliberately-wrong control proving the citation resolver is falsifiable without mutating the shared tree — note: ← WI-40142 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Docs: acceptance runbook via `docs:author`; the CLAUDE.md rule via its doc-part + `scripts/project-doc-parts.mjs --write` — note: ← WI-40144 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The acceptance bar is judged per-plan AFTER grading, and the implementer records the call\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim] *\"Grading pass threshold can differ from plan to plan, lets make the implementing agent also be in charge of deciding what a 'passing grade is.' I also don't want them to be bound by an earlier decision, so lets make it part of the grading step, not something they set before. After grade they should decide if they think its acceptable or not.\"*\n\nConsequences for the build:\n\n- **No numeric threshold, and none pre-declared.** The rubric does NOT carry a passing score, and nothing is committed to before the ratings exist. Do not add a `minScore`, a required-rating floor, or a `passingGrade` field to the acceptance rubric — that is precisely the earlier-decision binding this rules out.\n- **`scorecards:emit` gains `acceptance: { verdict: 'accept' | 'reject', reasoning }`**, required for `kind:'acceptance'` rubrics only.\n- **The IMPLEMENTER records it**, after reading an independent grading — confirmed against the alternatives (grader-decides, or both-must-agree) in the same turn. The independent grader still produces the ratings + evidence; the plan's owner makes the acceptance call and their reasoning is the record.\n- **Gate check 02 changes meaning**: it stops being \"every criterion carries some rating\" and becomes \"a complete independent grading exists AND the implementer recorded `accept`\". This is the fix for the measured finding that the gate never read what the ratings said.\n- **Legacy gradings are grandfathered.** The 22 acceptance rubrics already graded have no verdict; absent-verdict scorecards created before this ships count as `accept`, or turning the gate on retroactively un-ships already-shipped plans.\n\nKnown trade-off, accepted deliberately: the plan's own author is marking its homework. The paper trail is the check — the independent ratings sit beside the implementer's reasoning, so a thin acceptance over a poor grading is visible rather than invisible.\n\n### D-002 — Audit verdicts RECORD, they do not block — the exit for an unbuilt item is an intentional drop with a mandatory reason\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim] *\"The audit part of the plan looks good but lets skip #4. We should give the agent an option to mark an item as intentionally dropped with a reason in there was an off plan decision made in the chat or maybe a decision the agent made, thats okay too, it should just be intentional that it went against the initial plan and recorded.\"*\n\n\"#4\" refers to the proposed refusal `audit_unresolved_verdicts`, which would have blocked the ship while any item was audited `partial` or `missing`. **It is not being built.** It was also largely redundant with `plan_items_unfinished` (P-005), which catches the same class from the item-status side.\n\nConsequences for the build:\n\n- **`plans:audit` verdicts are informational.** `implemented` / `not-code` / `partial` / `missing` are all recordable and none of them refuses the ship on its own.\n- **`dropped` becomes a first-class audit verdict with a REQUIRED reason** — covering the case where the chat went somewhere else, or the implementing agent made a call mid-flight. Departing from the plan is legitimate; departing silently is not.\n- **`plans:set-status { status:'dropped' }` requires a reason too** (P-007). `note` and `rationale` already exist on that verb and are both optional today; the change is making at least one mandatory on a `dropped` flip. `note` is preferred because it splices inline into the item line and stays visible in the plan body forever, where `rationale` lives on the plan revision.\n- **The reason cannot live on `plan_items.decision_refs`.** That array is parsed out of the plan body and re-derived on every write by `plan-index-rows.ts` (delete-and-reinsert), so anything written there is clobbered. It lives in the audit row and on the revision.\n\n### D-003 — A plan may be force-shipped past a failed audit — intentionally, with a recorded reason, and loudly\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim] *\"an agent should be able to force a plan to shipped even if it failed an audit, it should be intentional by the agent, and recorded with a reason\"*\n\nConsequences for the build (P-008):\n\n- **`plans:set-plan-status { slug, status:'shipped', force: { reason } }`** — `reason` is mandatory; a bare `force: true` is refused. This follows the shape `release:deploy op:'force'` already uses in this repo for a loud, audited override, so agents meet one idiom rather than two.\n- **The marker is PERMANENT and visible**, not a silent bypass: the plan carries a \"shipped over a failed audit\" stamp plus the reason and the forcing agent, surfaced wherever plan status is read (`plans:get`, `plans:list`). A force that is easy to hide is worth very little — the whole value is that the next reader sees it without going looking.\n- **Scope: the AUDIT gate only.** Force does not bypass the acceptance rubric or the independent grading (`acceptance_rubric_missing` / `acceptance_ungraded` / `self_graded_only` still refuse). Those are a different guard with a different owner ruling behind them; widening force to cover them is out of scope and would need its own decision.\n- The force reason is a legitimate input to the acceptance verdict in D-001 — an implementer who forces past a failed audit should expect their `accept` reasoning to be read alongside it.\n\n### D-004 — The IMPLEMENTER self-audits, so every anti-rubber-stamp property has to come from the mechanics\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13] Chosen over an independent auditor and over both-in-sequence. The audit runs BEFORE the acceptance rubric is authored, so gaps are found and fixed while the work is still warm, and the audit's findings inform the rubric rather than the other way round.\n\nWhat this costs, and how the design pays it back — this is the load-bearing rationale for several build choices, so do not \"simplify\" them away:\n\n- **There is no independence leg at the audit stage.** The implementer is checking their own work one step earlier than before. So the guard cannot rest on conscientiousness: it rests on citations that must RESOLVE against the real tree or the write is refused (P-002), re-resolved again at ship time because the tree moves in between (P-004).\n- **`kind:'none'` citations are the known soft spot.** Items whose deliverable is not source need an escape hatch, and a lazy audit can mark everything `none`. Mitigation: `none` requires a reason, and the result reports `citedItems / totalItems / noneItems` so the ratio is a number, not a vibe.\n- **P-010 is what recovers the lost independence.** The four `plan-class-*` rubrics gain a criterion requiring the independent grader to SPOT-CHECK the audit's citations and read the `none` ratio — turning the grader who already exists into the audit's auditor. Without P-010 this design is materially weaker; it is not optional polish.\n\nStated limit, so nobody over-claims later: fabricated paths die mechanically, mass-`none` dies at grading, and a determined faker who cites real files that do not implement the item defeats both. The gate raises the cost of a rubber stamp; it does not make one impossible.\n\n### D-005 — Force waives the CODE-TRUTH family only — the rubric family is a separate guard and stays\nDate: 2026-08-13\nRefines D-003, which said force covers \"the AUDIT gate only\" without settling where the new unfinished-items refusal falls. Implemented in `evaluatePlanAcceptanceGate`:\n\n**Waivable by `force: { reason }`** — the four refusals this plan adds:\n`plan_items_unfinished` · `acceptance_unaudited` · `audit_coverage_stale` · `audit_citations_unresolved`.\n\n**NOT waivable** — the three that already existed:\n`acceptance_rubric_missing` · `acceptance_ungraded` · `self_graded_only`.\n\nThe line is \"the completion-audit family this plan introduced\", not \"everything that can refuse a ship\". The rubric family encodes a different owner ruling (an acceptance rubric graded by someone other than its author, acceptance-rubrics-on-every-plan-2026-08-11) and was not part of the 2026-08-13 force directive. Collapsing both families into one switch would make the override materially broader than what was authorised — and would mean a single `force` silently disables the independent-grading guard, which is the one leg of the whole design that a self-audit does not already own.\n\n`plan_items_unfinished` is included in the waivable set because its intended exit — drop the item with a reason — is itself an intentional-departure record (D-002). An agent who forces past it is making the same statement more bluntly, and the force reason is captured either way.\n\nTwo implementation consequences worth not undoing:\n\n- **The two flags are read PER FAMILY, not once at the top.** The gate previously early-returned on a single `ACCEPTANCE_RUBRIC_COMPLETION_GATE` read; it now reads `PLAN_ITEM_COMPLETION_GATE` and `PLAN_CODE_AUDIT_GATE` independently. Rolling one family back must not silently disable the other, which a shared early return would do.\n- **A force does not return early either.** It records the waived check in `forcedPast.checks` and CONTINUES to the rubric family, so forcing past a missing audit still cannot skip an ungraded rubric.\n\n### D-006 — The audit binds to each plan ITEM, not to the pass — coverage is a per-item fold across passes\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim] *\"are we associating the audits with each individual plan item? I think we should, if you think we shouldn't why not?\"*\n\n**We should, and the answer is stronger than a preference: without it D-007 (incremental re-verification) is not implementable, and the gate as currently written actively forces the full re-audit the owner is trying to avoid.**\n\nThe defect, read out of the code rather than the design notes. `evaluatePlanAcceptanceGate` computes coverage as:\n\n```\naudited = new Set(getLatestPlanAudit(slug).items.map(i => i.itemId))\nuncovered = currentItems.filter(i => i.status !== 'dropped' && !audited.has(i.itemId))\n```\n\nCoverage is measured against **the latest PASS's array only**. A pass is an all-or-nothing snapshot. So when one item is added to a 12-item plan and the agent re-audits just that item, the new pass carries `items:[P-013]` and the other eleven become `uncovered` — the gate refuses again. The only way to satisfy it is to re-submit all twelve. The refusal message (\"Re-run plans:audit covering them\") reads as if a narrow pass were acceptable; the coverage rule means it is not.\n\nWorse, the cheap way out of that bind is to copy the eleven prior entries verbatim into the new pass, where they inherit the new pass's `audited_sha` and `created_at` — **falsely stamping eleven items as verified at a sha nobody checked them against**. That is a rubber stamp the mechanics currently reward, which D-004 says the design must not rely on conscientiousness to prevent.\n\nConsequences for the build:\n\n- **`AuditItemEntry` carries its own provenance**: `auditedSha` and `auditedAt` per item, plus `carriedFrom?: auditSeq` when an entry is brought forward unchanged. An item's verification is pinned to the moment it was actually verified, independent of the pass it happens to be stored in.\n- **Coverage becomes a fold, not an array read**: resolve the latest entry per `itemId` across the plan's passes (newest first, first match wins), then compare that against the current item list. `getLatestPlanAudit` stays for history; the gate gets `getEffectiveItemAudits(planSlug)`.\n- **`plans:audit` accepts a SUBSET of items.** Unchanged items are carried forward by the VERB, not re-declared by the agent — so an agent physically cannot re-stamp an item it did not look at. This is the same anti-rubber-stamp shape as the citation resolver: the guard is mechanical, not behavioural.\n- **Per-citation fingerprints**: each `code`/`test` citation records the blob sha of its path at audit time. This is what makes \"did the evidence for this item actually change?\" a git question rather than an LLM question — see D-007.\n\n**No migration is owed.** `plan_audits.items` is jsonb and nothing writes the table yet (migration 832 is applied but P-002's verb has not landed), so the entry shape is still free to change.\n\n**Amending 832's stated rationale, rather than quietly contradicting it.** That migration argued for jsonb over a child table because the per-item detail is \"written once as a unit, always read as a unit alongside its parent, and is never queried across plans.\" The third clause still holds and is the load-bearing one. The second no longer does — the fold reads entries across passes. jsonb remains correct because the fold is scoped to a single plan's handful of passes, but the comment should be corrected to say so instead of resting on a premise this decision falsifies.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-007 — Ship-time re-verification is INCREMENTAL — only items whose evidence actually moved are re-audited\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim] *\"'4 · The gate re-verifies at ship time' this si okay but there should eb an explicit instruction to only check for the changes. I dont want to run a full audit if there werent any relevant changes made.\"*\n\nRefers to §4 of the design memo: the gate does not trust the stored audit and re-resolves citations against the current tree. That property stays — the tree genuinely does move between audit and ship. What changes is the SCOPE of what a refusal demands: re-verification is per-item and change-driven, and when nothing relevant moved the gate demands nothing at all.\n\nRides on D-006: without per-item `auditedSha`, \"changed since this item was audited\" has no reference point to compare against.\n\n**An item needs re-auditing when, and only when, one of these is true:**\n\n1. It is new, or was reopened to an unfinished status, since its last audit entry.\n2. Its own text changed since that entry (compare the stored item text hash).\n3. A path it cites has different content now than at the entry's `auditedSha` — compared by blob sha, so a rewritten file is caught, not just a deleted one.\n4. It has no audit entry at all.\n\nEverything else carries forward untouched, keeping its original `auditedSha` and `auditedAt`. **If that set is empty, the gate passes with no new audit pass demanded** — which is the property the directive is asking for.\n\nConsequences for the build:\n\n- **`audit_coverage_stale` becomes per-item and self-describing.** Today it names uncovered items. It must additionally name items stale by reasons 2 and 3, and state the reason per item (\"P-007: `plan-audits.ts` changed since audit #3\"). The refusal message must say explicitly that only the listed items need re-auditing and that the rest carry forward — that is the \"explicit instruction\" the directive asks for. The current wording (\"Re-run plans:audit covering them\") is ambiguous under the old all-or-nothing coverage rule and would read as a demand for a full pass.\n- **This closes a hole, it does not only save tokens.** `audit_citations_unresolved` fires only when a citation stops RESOLVING — a deleted path or a missing symbol. A cited file that was rewritten still resolves, so today an item's evidence can be completely replaced between audit and ship and nothing fires. Blob-sha comparison catches exactly that case. The incremental rule is therefore strictly stronger than the current check, not a relaxation of it.\n- **Detection is pure git.** Per-citation blob shas at audit time (D-006) vs. the current tree; no file re-reading, no model tokens. A plan whose cited files did not move costs one sha comparison per citation.\n- **Deliberately NOT time-based.** No \"audits expire after N days\". An audit whose evidence has not moved is not stale, however old, and an audit taken sixty seconds ago is worthless if the file was rewritten since. Age is a proxy for the thing we can now measure directly.\n- **`force` still waives it** — `audit_coverage_stale` remains in the waivable code-truth family per D-005; nothing here changes that line.\n\nSettles a question that was **never actually answered**. The 2026-08-13 dialog asked how sensitive staleness should be (options: new-or-reopened items only / any item-list change / one audit stands). That dialog was dismissed with \"the user wants to clarify these questions\" and the follow-up never re-asked it, so the plan carried an unresolved policy with an implementation already written against the narrowest reading. This decision closes it on the owner's own terms, which are none of the three options offered — the right axis was per-item evidence movement, not item-list churn.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-008 — Only a resolving code/test citation counts as verification — every other kind is a declaration of NON-verification, counted and surfaced\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim] *\"with A will an agent still be verifying against the code, or just see a claimed completed work item or documentation claiming something is complete, and assume it was completed. also add that memory shouldnt be relied upon either for this audit step, code is the only source of truth\"*\n\nRestates turn A's opening instruction (*\"don't rely on any documentation or memory, the code should be the only source of truth\"*), which this plan had never recorded as a decision — the gap the 2026-08-13 provenance audit found (WI-38590 comment 61960).\n\n**The owner's challenge was correct and my proposed option A did not answer it.** A only made `doc` citations resolve — i.e. proved the doc exists. It never prevented a claim-shaped artifact from standing in for code. Two defects, read out of the built code, not the design notes:\n\n1. **`implemented` does not require a CODE citation.** `agent-tools/plans/audit.ts:156` refuses `implemented` with *zero* citations, but accepts any kind. So `verdict:'implemented', citations:[{kind:'doc',ref:'x'}]` passes the write refusal, passes ship-time re-resolution (which skips non-code/test kinds), and reports as cited. The verdict whose documented meaning is \"traced to as-built code the auditor read\" is satisfiable by a one-character string.\n2. **`not-code` is metered nowhere.** `summarizeCoverage` folds only `partial`/`missing` (→ `unresolvedVerdicts`) and `dropped` (→ `droppedItems`). A `not-code` item carrying a `doc` citation increments `citedItems` and never touches `noneItems`. An audit marking all twelve items `not-code` + `doc` reports `auditedItems 12, citedItems 12, noneRatio 0` — an immaculate audit in which no code was read.\n\n**The rule, replacing the citation-kind framing entirely:**\n\n- **`code` / `test`, resolved against the tree, are the ONLY kinds that constitute verification.** Nothing else ever counts, however well-formed.\n- **`implemented` REQUIRES ≥1 resolving `code`/`test` citation.** Refusal `implemented_without_code`. This is the load-bearing change; the citation-kind question was a symptom of its absence.\n- **`workitem` is removed from item citations** (it survives in `findings[].ref`). A work-item is a record of intent — precisely the \"documentation or memory\" the directive excludes. Citing one as evidence that code exists is circular.\n- **`doc` must resolve** (tree file or the PG docs store, since `/internal/docs` is PG-canonical) **and is classified UNVERIFIED.** It says \"the deliverable is this document\", never \"code was written\".\n- **`not-code` requires a reason and is metered**, reported beside the unverified counts. It is the real escape hatch — wider than `none`, and previously invisible.\n- **Headline number is `verifiedAgainstCode: N/total`** — items carrying ≥1 resolving code/test citation. One honest figure that no volume of doc refs can inflate, and the number P-010's grader spot-checks.\n\n**Memory is inadmissible, stated in the tool, not just the docs.** The audit is performed against the tree as it is now — not the plan text, not work-item records, not docs asserting completion, not the implementer's recollection of writing it. The gate's `acceptance_unaudited` message already says this; `plans:audit`'s own description and refusals must too, because that is the surface an auditing agent actually reads. Under D-004 the implementer self-audits, so this is the exact point where memory is most available and least trustworthy.\n\nCost accepted: an item whose deliverable genuinely is not source can no longer be recorded as `implemented`. That is the intent — it is `not-code`, reasoned, counted, and visible to the grader, rather than silently absorbed into a verified-looking total.\nRelated: P-002, P-010\n\n### D-009 — The RED-24 repair lane and checkpoint serializer remain separate single writers\nDate: 2026-08-21\nOperational ruling for the final acceptance run: WI-40271 owns the canonical lint:identity-leak repair and its verification/landing evidence; WI-40086 (su-271f) owns checkpoint admission and may launch exactly one successor only after WI-40271 reports a focused-green, content-bearing SHA that is present on origin/staging.
