WI-41117 was then handed to su-278b876c (claim landed 00:10:52Z, verified from the ledger).\n- su-ccd31f35 has since replied confirming it is NOT resuming the serializer lane.\n\nRULING: su-4f31ce63-8288-48b9-8f01-614b6ef18f88 is the sole WI-40086 serializer/emitter/checkpoint/deploy/routine authority. This supersedes ONLY D-028's named-holder clause. All other lanes remain evidence/repair-only unless a later explicit decision transfers authority again. su-278b876c holds WI-41117 and su-9e7d2 holds WI-40905 as REPAIR lanes; neither is authorised to fire release:checkpoint-run.\n\nADMISSION PREDICATES UNCHANGED AND CONJUNCTIVE. Every D-016/D-021/D-026/D-027 predicate stands byte-for-byte. Taking the named-holder role transfers WHO may act; it relaxes NOTHING about when. Timeout, expiry, an unrelated or prematurely-started checkpoint, and a declaration NEVER qualify.\n\n⚠ CORRECTION (amended 00:25Z, on a BLOCKING ruling from su-08275825 — accepted in full). The original OPERATIVE SEQUENCE in this decision read 'WI-41117 terminal -> I fire EXACTLY ONE release:checkpoint-run', which silently DROPPED WI-40905. That contradicted this decision's own admission clause and a reader following it would have fired early. The admission clause was always right; the summary was wrong. CORRECTED AND BINDING SEQUENCE, all conjunctive:\n  1. WI-41117 terminal (su-278b876c) — the setup-release-checkout materialization fix, so a checkpoint can complete at all. Root cause: canonical node_modules mutated during the independent copy (rc75); the UNSERIALIZED copy is the bug.\n  2. WI-40905 witness terminal (su-9e7d2) — terminal rc0 + WITNESS OVERALL PASS + K3 PASS + K4b seen>=1, defer>=1, decrypt-fail=0, applied=0.\n  3. Stable-C 2/2 freshly proven.\n  4. ONLY THEN, and only by the serializer: emit generation 2 once, resume the routine, fire EXACTLY ONE release:checkpoint-run, read the WRITER-BACKED verdict, fix reds, deploy the green pin, verify live parity.\nSteps 1-3 are not the serializer's to perform. The serializer owns step 4 and nothing earlier.\n\n⚠ DO NOT TRIAGE FROM gate_health: the gate has recorded no verdict in ~36h because it crashes in setup-release-checkout.sh pre-suite, so failingTests/consecutiveReds are frozen artifacts naming files deleted from the tree (EI-21288455988125992, EI-21287976275725621). su-b39c3 has RETRACTED the pc-heavy contention theory for the 30-min timeout: HEAVY_SLOT_WAIT_SEC is 120, not 900 — the crash finding stands, that cause does not.\nRelated: WI-40086, WI-40905, WI-41117, D-016, D-025, D-028\n\n### D-030 — Generation-3 acceptance remains fail-closed after D-051 infra-inconclusive; wait on D-052 provenance fix, never retry singleton\nDate: 2026-08-25\nSource authority: stable-candidate-related-gate-2026-08-23#D-052 (2026-08-25). The sole D-051 candidate 431d6f0b28991a05753d3556c769f927beece7b2 terminated before its suite with green=null/reason=infra-inconclusive after dependency-materialization admission failed. The singleton authority is consumed and MUST NOT be retried. Generation 3 remains declared/unfired with no Stable-C samples. WI-40532 therefore cannot grade or emit a superseding scorecard. Its actionable blocker is EI-21402283154473718: preserve exact transported-tip provenance across pre-suite/materialization failures, emit the candidate-bound inconclusive event, and update health with recurrence coverage. After that fix becomes terminal, re-read the governing plan for a separately authorized lawful route; D-052 itself grants no retry. A genuine generation-3 fire still wakes the independent grader, but timeout/partial progress never qualifies.\n\n### D-031 — D-053 supersedes the closed generation-3 rendezvous; independent acceptance waits only on distinct post-D-052 generation 1\nDate: 2026-08-25\nSource authority: stable-candidate-related-gate-2026-08-23#D-053 at v140. The legacy event harness:papercusp:wi-40086-qualified-current-tip generation 3 remains pending/unfired and MUST NEVER be emitted, awaited, retried, aliased, or treated as release authority. Completion-plan D-030's old-event alternative is superseded. WI-40532 now waits only on the separately declared global event wi-40086-post-d052-qualified-current-tip generation 1. D-053 authorizes the WI-40086 serializer exactly one fresh normal current-tip checkpoint after its full action-instant preflight; any refusal/red/inconclusive/timeout/abnormal exit/missing marker/wrong provenance consumes that authority and fails closed. Even exact green is insufficient to fire the new event: the serializer must first advance the green pin, perform safe green-only deploy, and verify live parity including the scorecards targetHive writer. The independent grader never launches, emits, deploys, or aliases either event.\n\n### D-032 — D-053 singleton also consumed fail-closed; global generation 1 must remain unfired while dependency-generation liveness is repaired\nDate: 2026-08-25\nSource authority: stable-candidate-related-gate-2026-08-23#D-055/#D-056 at v145. D-053 exact candidate b543faf28c9ceaaa7bbeb1150aecce22eb62cfbd / runId 6fa9b9ee-1a70-4bb2-b4cf-0cf313661d50 / invocation 3bf4b4dcce3b4b81b3761f6712a7dd35 terminated before its suite with advanced=false, green=null, reason=not-green, crashed=true after dependency generation timed out at 30 minutes. Candidate-source provenance remained tip, confirming the prior repair. D-053 authority is consumed and MUST NEVER be retried, replaced, or reinterpreted. Global wi-40086-post-d052-qualified-current-tip generation 1 remains declared and MUST remain unfired for this route. WI-40532 no longer awaits that unfireable route; it waits on critical EI-21411600805243319 completing its dependency-generation liveness/timeout root fix. Any future qualification requires a NEW explicit governing decision plus fresh serializer/action-instant preflight; no implicit retry authority exists.\n\n## Requirements\n\nEvery plan item has an auditable verdict whose code/test citations resolve against the tree at write time, and `plans:get` surfaces the latest audit. Shipping blocks on unaudited, stale, unresolved, or unfinished items before rubric checks; dropped items require a reason. Acceptance scorecards record an explicit implementer verdict, while independent rubric grading remains separate. A force ship waives only the code-truth family and leaves a permanent visible reason.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing `plans:audit`, plan acceptance gate, scorecards, and plan status tools. Fold audit coverage per item across passes, re-audit only evidence whose fingerprint moved, and order the new default-ON gate flags ahead of rubric checks. Add the dropped-item reason and narrow force marker through structured writers, pin citation falsifiability with a deliberately wrong control, and publish the runbook through `docs:author` plus the projected agent-doc part.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"pot-git-stats-tab-2026-08-13","title":"Per-pot Git statistics tab","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Per-pot Git statistics tab\nslug: pot-git-stats-tab-2026-08-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-13\n---\n\n# Per-pot Git statistics tab\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Now\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit the existing operator tabs, shared pot selector, API route conventions, and reusable loading/error/table/card components; write the implementation contract. importance: high — note: ← WI-38550 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement a bounded, cached per-pot Git statistics service and API covering repository state, push divergence, history, contributors, tracked footprint, language/code-comment-test composition, and explicit submodule scope. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-38553 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Implement the Stats tab using the shared pot selector and established operator UI patterns, with freshness, refresh, empty/error states, summary metrics, and breakdown views. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-38564 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `todo` Add focused service/API/UI tests and browser verification for pot switching, Git and non-Git pots, large repositories, errors, loading, and responsive rendering. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Base statistics describe the selected pot repository; submodules remain explicit\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe primary totals are computed from the selected pot repository's committed HEAD and do not silently traverse gitlinks. Dirty working-tree state is reported separately. Submodules are shown as their own count/list and may expose a separately labeled aggregate later, preventing the same total from mixing repository and nested-repository scope.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"release-build-vm-dev-parity-audit-2026-08-13","title":"Actual-install VM audit of release builds versus npm run dev","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Actual-install VM audit of release builds versus npm run dev\nslug: release-build-vm-dev-parity-audit-2026-08-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n- The audit contract is frozen before execution: exact public 0.0.16 artifact URLs and hashes, the source and environment used by `npm run dev`, the eventual exact 0.0.17 artifact tuple, clean guest snapshots, isolated test data, and a complete feature/acceptance matrix.\n- Public 0.0.16 Linux, Windows, and macOS artifacts are clean-installed and driven as users receive them. Each platform records installation, first launch, packaged sidecar/operator health, navigation and user actions, persistence and relaunch, update/reinstall, uninstall residue, filesystem/network/permission behavior, logs and recovery, plus artifact-to-runtime provenance.\n- The canonical `npm run dev` launch is exercised from the audited source against the same functional matrix and isolated data, with its command expansion, process topology, flags, ports, storage, permissions, logs, and exposed UI/API/tool surfaces recorded.\n- Every dev-versus-release difference is accounted for with platform evidence and the code or build writer that creates it, then classified as intended release-only, intended dev-only, missing-in-release, release-only exposure/security, or platform packaging behavior. A static grep or manifest alone is never treated as runtime proof.\n- Every confirmed defect is fixed at its root cause or has a filed and owned work-item, gains a detector for the defect class, and is verified by rebuilding and repeating the exact affected installed flow.\n- The unchanged matrix is repeated on the exact final 0.0.17 Linux, Windows, and macOS artifacts. Closure requires provenance consistency, complete platform coverage, no open confirmed release-only defect, and an owner-readable report with commands and evidence references.\n\n## Design\n\nThe audit extends the maintained release and VM chassis: the release runbook and artifact manifests, `vm-preflight`, install-and-relaunch verification, Windows VM/WSL smoke, the macOS VM rig, Linux install tooling, and the existing Bytebot desktop-driving workflow. It does not create a second build or test system.\n\nExecution follows a two-pass evidence pipeline. First, P-001 freezes immutable inputs and P-002 turns the feature inventory into one observable matrix. That same matrix drives public 0.0.16 on all three disposable guests and the isolated development launch, while P-007 independently traces artifact/build-graph differences back to their writers. Per-platform evidence bundles contain artifact URL/hash, guest snapshot, install and launch commands, installed version/provenance, screenshots, bounded logs, lifecycle results, and cleanup state.\n\nP-008 joins those bundles into one parity ledger rather than three disconnected reports. P-009 removes and guards any confirmed defects, rebuilding only through the canonical release path and re-running the failed real-install flows. P-010 then freezes the final 0.0.17 tuple from the release-cut plan and repeats the complete matrix unchanged; P-011 publishes the consolidated verdict and reproduction surface.\n\nThe settled trade-off is to spend more time on real installed execution and provenance rather than infer equivalence from source alone. Static review, package manifests, and focused tests explain observations and prevent recurrence, but only a clean installed run can establish what the release actually delivers. Platform lanes run incrementally against immutable inputs so shared release state, ports, sidecars, and VM snapshots cannot silently cross-contaminate one another.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Owner-directed AUTO remains active. WI-39304 logical-seed fix is terminal and confirmed on remote staging at historical tip 2ca66f6324596fc710d29ffb93f956390578e1b4; no duplicate test:affected run occurred. P-007/WI-38603 is now terminal under D-021: frozen 0.0.18 source 7caaed681f34 / desktop 2363b77a is reconciled against exact writers, 21/21 public objects, signatures/manifests, and authoritative Windows/Linux/macOS live transitions from WI-40324; current staging thin-GUI remediation remains a separate post-freeze population. P-006 remains blocked exactly per D-008: live node-MainThread PID 963019 owns canonical :3270 and :3274, so it is not reused or stopped. Because P-008 has a dependency edge on P-006, P-008 through P-011 remain blocked; a premature P-008 lease was released without changing status.\n\n**Next:** Re-probe canonical :3270/:3274 on the next paced loop wake. If both are free, claim and run P-006 from the frozen isolated source under D-008, then advance P-008 synthesis, P-009 defect closure, exact immutable 0.0.18 P-010 acceptance, and P-011 report. If either port remains live, keep P-006 parked and preserve the host operator.\n\n## Background\n\nThe audit measures user reality rather than inferring it from source or tests. It clean-installs signed release artifacts on Linux, Windows, and macOS guests; launches and drives the real desktop and packaged sidecar; compares the observed surface against the repository's canonical npm run dev path; inspects the produced bundles and runtime environment; and classifies every difference as intended or defective. Static review supports the result but cannot replace installed execution. Confirmed defects require root cause, recurrence guard, fix, and re-run of each affected platform.\n\nThe audit runs in two waves so it begins while 0.0.17 is building: public 0.0.16 establishes an immediate installed baseline; the unchanged matrix then runs against the exact 0.0.17 Linux, Windows, and macOS artifacts before final acceptance.\n\nReuse decision: the existing release runbook, vm-preflight, install-and-relaunch-verify, Windows WSL smoke, macOS VM rig, Linux install tooling, and Bytebot desktop-driving workflow are the execution chassis. The older cold-carry plan is behavior-specific and the v0.0.12 plan is version-specific, so neither can carry this broader product-surface audit.\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract and baselines\n\n- **P-001** `done` Freeze the audit contract and exact inputs: public 0.0.16 artifact URLs, hashes and provenance; the source commit used by npm run dev; the eventual 0.0.17 artifact tuple; clean VM snapshots; test accounts and data; and a feature inventory drawn from navigation, APIs/tools, config, Tauri capabilities, sidecar bootstrap, packaging resources, update channel, and product flags. importance: urgent — note: Satisfied as the 0.0.18 contract/source freeze by D-020: superproject 7caaed681f34b972bed6d744f16a8cbd7708dfca, desktop 2363b77a68dee8d79528a4a6a94321cc324ed2f7. Final artifact tuple remains P-010 and the active 0.0.18 release plan.\n- **P-002** `done` Define the observable acceptance matrix before testing: installation and uninstall, first launch, relaunch/update, version/provenance, startup services, UI navigation and all user-accessible actions, operator/API/tool surface, local data persistence, filesystem locations, networking/federation, permissions, logs/crash recovery, updater behavior, and security/privacy boundaries. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38598 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Real installed-platform evidence\n\n- **P-003** `done` Clean-install and live-drive the Linux release artifacts on a disposable guest. Capture installer result, desktop launch, packaged sidecar health, screenshots/logs, every P-002 flow, persistence across restart, update/reinstall, uninstall residue, and artifact/runtime provenance. Run first on 0.0.16 and repeat unchanged on 0.0.17. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39304 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Clean-install and live-drive the Windows release artifacts in the Windows VM/WSL runtime. Capture installer exit and ProductVersion, GUI launch, packaged sidecar/operator health from inside WSL, sticky-port/relaunch behavior, screenshots/logs, every P-002 flow, update/reinstall, uninstall residue, and provenance. Run first on 0.0.16 and repeat unchanged on 0.0.17. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38600 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Clean-install and live-drive the macOS release artifacts in the macOS VM. Capture DMG/app installation, Gatekeeper/signature state, GUI and Server.app launch, packaged sidecar health, LaunchAgent/autostart behavior, screenshots/logs, every P-002 flow, update/reinstall, uninstall residue, and provenance. Run first on 0.0.16 and repeat unchanged on 0.0.17. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38601 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Development baseline and build-graph diff\n\n- **P-006** `blocked` Run the canonical npm run dev launch from the same audited source and drive the identical P-002 functional matrix against an isolated data directory. Record the actual command expansion, environment, ports, startup topology, process tree, UI/API/tool catalogs, feature flags, capabilities, storage paths, logs, permissions, and lifecycle behavior. importance: urgent — note: Blocked on D-008: :3270 and :3274 both held by live operator PID 2067090 (re-verified 04:0xZ). Owner-held blocker — no agent can clear it. Was churning through 6+ agents while left in `open`.\n- **P-007** `done` Produce an artifact-level diff of dev versus each release platform: compiled SPA/source commit, sidecar source and native modules, bundled resources and templates, Tauri configuration/capabilities, build-time and runtime environment defaults, feature/update flags, binary/tool availability, service/autostart integration, filesystem/network permissions, telemetry/debug surfaces, and excluded developer-only content. Verify the writer/build script for every compared value before drawing conclusions. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38603 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Classification, remediation, and final 0.0.17 verdict\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Synthesize one complete parity ledger. For every observed difference, record platform, exact evidence, originating writer/build step, expected product contract, and one classification: intended release-only, intended dev-only, missing-in-release defect, release-only exposure/security defect, or platform-specific packaging defect. File every suspected defect immediately; absence from a single grep or test is not evidence. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007 importance: urgent\n- **P-009** `todo` Fix every confirmed release-build defect in scope at its root cause, add a test/assertion/health check that detects the defect class, run focused verification plus npm run test:affected, rebuild affected artifacts, and re-run the exact failed installed-platform flows. blocked-by: P-008 importance: urgent\n- **P-010** `todo` Repeat the complete installed and dev-parity matrix on the exact final 0.0.17 Linux, Windows, and macOS artifact tuple from plan desktop-release-0-0-17-alpha-2026-08-13; refuse acceptance if provenance differs, an audit lane is missing, or any release-only defect remains. blocked-by: P-009 importance: urgent\n- **P-011** `todo` Deliver the owner report: cut status, artifact/provenance table, full functionality verdict, all missing/extra behaviors, the exhaustive dev-vs-release difference matrix with intended/defect rationale, defects fixed, residual risks/untested scope, screenshots/log references, and exact reproduction commands. blocked-by: P-010 importance: urgent\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Measure 0.0.16 now; repeat the unchanged matrix on 0.0.17\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDo not wait idle for 0.0.17 artifacts. Use the latest public 0.0.16 signed artifacts to establish the first installed baseline immediately, then run the identical frozen matrix on 0.0.17 before accepting that cut. Historical evidence may seed hypotheses but does not satisfy this plan unless re-read and reproduced where the artifact/runtime can still be exercised.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-010\n\n### D-002 — Installed execution is authoritative; static review is supporting evidence\nDate: 2026-08-13\nA source file, packaging manifest, or unit test can explain an observation but cannot prove what a user receives. Each platform verdict requires installation of the real artifact, first launch, functional driving, lifecycle/relaunch evidence, and artifact-to-runtime provenance.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-003 — Classify every difference, including intended differences\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe report must not list only bugs. It must include intended release-only and dev-only differences, each tied to its originating writer/build step and rationale, so accidental omissions and accidental developer-surface exposure are both visible.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-011\n\n### D-004 — Fix and guard confirmed defects before closure\nDate: 2026-08-13\nA mitigation or prose finding is not closure. Each confirmed defect needs its root cause removed or a filed-and-owned work item, a recurrence detector, and a re-run of the affected real install flow. The final 0.0.17 verdict remains red while any confirmed release-only defect is open.\nRelated: P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011\n\n### D-005 — Reuse existing release and VM chassis; no parallel audit rig\nDate: 2026-08-13\nExecute through the current release runbook, vm-preflight, install-and-relaunch-verify, Windows WSL smoke, macOS VM rig, Linux install tooling, and Bytebot desktop-driving workflow. The reviewed cold-carry plan is behavior-specific and the v0.0.12 plan is version-specific, so this audit is distinct in scope but extends their maintained mechanisms rather than creating another system.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-006 — Single owner for the next checkpoint successor\nDate: 2026-08-13\nWhile candidate 3c630bc7's exact user service or release run lock remains active, preserve it and do not fire release:checkpoint-run. After both singleton signals clear, the live WI-38506 assignee is the exclusive launcher of exactly one current-staging successor; every other release lane consumes that exact candidate through release:trace/checkpoint:await and must not launch a duplicate. The successor must contain 2e9532ad, cd1b2f15b, 4c4aa5135f, and afbd42f before its verdict can satisfy dependent release acceptance. If the WI-38506 holder dies or stalls, takeover requires first updating shared ownership.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-007 — The sole repaired successor must contain 25eedae\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe next checkpoint successor governed by D-006 must additionally descend from commit 25eedae262a8e45c2087708813ee0273cb6c58c7, which repairs the operator-core plans/audit.ts tool-response envelopes. The repair commit was inspected and `npm run typecheck:operator-core` passed. Candidate adf6129c predates the repair and cannot qualify even if its verdict is green. WI-38506 remains the exclusive successor launcher after release authority and the exact user unit are both inactive.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-008 — Canonical dev parity runs only on its fixed ports in an isolated root\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDate: 2026-08-13\nP-006 must execute the repository's exact `npm run dev` expansion from the frozen detached source with private HOME, PAPERCUSP_HOME, workspace/XDG roots, discovery, DSNs, and PGDATA. Current writers hard-target the webview/API at `127.0.0.1:3270`; `dev-operator-ifneeded.sh` defaults the operator to :3270 and PTY to :3274, but it can reuse an existing listener, honor caller port overrides, or walk away from a port reserved by the enabled bg-host unit. Therefore launch is allowed only after preflight proves :3270/:3274 are unbound, `OPERATOR_DEV_PORT`, `OPERATOR_DEV_PTY_PORT`, and `PAPERCUSP_DEV_API_TARGET` cannot redirect the topology, the enabled bg-host's parsed reserved port is not :3270, and the spawned process is then observed to own :3270/:3274 with health/provenance and start time from the isolated audit source. If any condition cannot be established, P-006 is blocked; do not substitute a different port, reuse an existing operator, or stop Avi's live desktop.\nRelated: P-001, P-006\n\n### D-009 — Matrix definition is independent of late immutable input values\nDate: 2026-08-13\nP-002 is definition work and must proceed from the already-frozen feature/surface inventory while P-001 remains open for the eventual exact 0.0.17 artifact tuple and the clean post-Tahoe Mac reset point. Requiring all late-bound immutable values before defining the matrix contradicts D-001 and the plan's own Now sequence. Clear P-002's blocked-by edge; installed executions P-003 through P-006 remain responsible for consuming only verified immutable inputs.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-010 — Hold release-size build-script mutations until the 0.0.17-alpha cut is frozen and built\nDate: 2026-08-14\nWhile the 0.0.17-alpha release gate and source tuple remain unresolved, no stage-time desktop build-script or Debian packaging mutations may land into the candidate source. The active green-checkpoint singleton is pinned to d26ab592, but any successor could include newer staging state; allowing P-001/P-003 from desktop-release-size-reduction-2026-08-14 now would change the release candidate while the parity audit is still trying to freeze exact inputs. Therefore hold P-001 through P-004 until the 0.0.17-alpha source tuple is frozen and all platform artifacts are built/published; then resume them for the next cut. This minimizes release variance and keeps the installed-release versus npm-run-dev parity comparison auditable.\n\n### D-011 — D-001 0.0.16 baseline leg is RETIRED — its premise expired; acceptance is 0.0.17 only\nDate: 2026-08-16\nOwner ruling (Avi, 2026-08-16 ~01:45Z): \"0.0.16 leg? we should already be at 0.0.17\". Correct — retiring that half of D-001.\n\nWHY D-001 CALLED FOR IT. D-001 (2026-08-13) reads: \"Do not wait idle for 0.0.17 artifacts. Use the latest public 0.0.16 signed artifacts to establish the first installed baseline immediately, then run the identical frozen matrix on 0.0.17 before accepting that cut.\" The 0.0.16 leg was explicitly SCAFFOLDING against idling while 0.0.17 did not yet exist. It was never an acceptance criterion — D-001's own wording makes 0.0.17 the gate (\"before accepting that cut\").\n\nWHY THE PREMISE HAS EXPIRED. 0.0.17 artifacts now exist and are installed and exercised: mac has /Applications/Papercusp{GUI,Server}.app v0.0.17 sha=971b3ee1 with /api/health 200, relaunch verify 3/3 PASS, clean log scan; windows has both 0.0.17 installers built and hashed. There is no idle to avoid, so the only thing the 0.0.16 leg still buys is a second data point on a build we are not shipping.\n\nRULING. The 0.0.16 baseline leg is DROPPED from acceptance for this plan and from the goal the-papercusp-desktop-app-is-verified-working-in-7273ca. Platform verdicts are rendered on 0.0.17 alone. P-001 (freeze exact public 0.0.16 artifact URL/hash inventory) is retired as out-of-scope rather than left blocked; no lane should spend further turns on it.\n\nCONSEQUENCE — A BLOCKER EVAPORATES. The invalid gh CLI token blocked ONLY the 0.0.16 fetch from GitHub releases. With that leg retired, the credential wall is moot on both mac and windows, and the owner escalation for a gh token is withdrawn.\n\nSTATED TRADE-OFF, so this is reversible with eyes open: 0.0.16 is the last SIGNED public release and 0.0.17 is an UNSIGNED dev cut (both windows installers confirmed unsigned; mac .app is adhoc-signed). Dropping 0.0.16 therefore removes the only signed artifact from the matrix, so G-004 (formal signature check) can only be evaluated against an unsigned/adhoc cut. If signed-artifact behaviour must be proven, it belongs to a signing-verification effort against a real signed build, not to this parity audit. Re-add the leg only if that judgement changes.\n\n### D-012 — P-010 is the acceptance gate — Linux 0.0.17 repeat is OUTSTANDING; per-platform 0.0.16 verdicts do not satisfy it\nDate: 2026-08-16\nFollow-on to the 0.0.16-retirement decision, recording a consequence that the retirement made visible and that the progress ledger was hiding.\n\nWHAT THE PLAN ACTUALLY REQUIRES. P-003 reads: \"Clean-install and live-drive the Linux release artifacts on a disposable guest ... Capture the provisioning as a reusable script so the next destructive incident costs minutes. If the rebuild hits a genuine wall — a hardware/TPM requirement we cannot satisfy, or an ISO that will not install unattended — THAT is the point to escalate, with the specific failure, not the absence of a disk.\n\n### D-014 — P-006 is gated on P-001’s frozen 0.0.17 source — the :3270 port collision was a symptom, not the blocker\nDate: 2026-08-16\nRULING. P-006 (canonical `npm run dev` dev baseline) MUST NOT be run until P-001 has frozen the audited source tuple. Its blocked-by edge is corrected to [P-002, P-001]. Each wake recorded the visible symptom: \":3270 and :3274 are both owned by node-MainThread PID 1418333; this is Avi's live desktop topology and is untouchable.\" Measured 2026-08-16T02:26Z: PID 1418333 no longer exists. Its port preconditions were satisfied on measurement (bg-host reserves :3271 not :3270, so the EI-13139 walk-away guard does not fire; no .env.local sets the three redirect vars) and its cond.1 was cleared by the peer’s yield. A P-006 launch into an occupied :3270 would therefore silently bind the audit to a peer’s operator and still look successful. That is why cond.1 is a hard gate rather than a courtesy.\nRelated: P-001, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-015 — A re-cut deb is only shippable once RE-SIGNED — repack-deb-xz.sh silently emits an unsigned package when the signing key is empty\nDate: 2026-08-16\nRuling issued while executing WI-39364 (re-cut of the 0.0.17 Linux debs with the WI-39357 PAX fix). Binds any lane that repacks or re-cuts a published deb.\n\n**The mechanism.** `papercusp-desktop/bin/repack-deb-xz.sh` has two signature-related branches and they are NOT symmetric:\n- L47-50: it REFUSES only when `$DEB_PATH.sig` exists AND `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` is unset — \"refusing to create a stale signature\".\n- L71-91: it signs only when `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` is NON-empty.\n\nSo a repack performed on a COPY of the deb (no `.sig` sitting beside it) with an empty/unset key sails past the guard and produces a package that installs perfectly and carries NO signature. The refusal guard cannot fire, because the thing it keys on — a sibling `.sig` — was left behind with the original. Nothing in the output says the artifact is unsigned; `✓ repacked data member as xz -9` is printed either way.\n\n**Why it matters here.** Both published 0.0.17 sources ARE signed (`Papercusp GUI_0.0.17_amd64.deb.sig` and `Papercusp Server_0.0.17_amd64.deb.sig`, 396 bytes each, cut 2026-08-15 16:26/16:34). A re-cut that drops the signature is not provenance-parity with what it replaces, and the Tauri updater path consumes that `.sig`. \"dpkg -i exits 0\" is therefore necessary but NOT sufficient for shippable.\n\n**The ruling.**\n1. `dpkg -i` exit 0 + `install ok installed` is the ACCEPTANCE test for the PAX fix. It is not the ship gate.\n2. A re-cut deb that REPLACES a signed published artifact MUST carry a regenerated `.sig` before it is called shippable. Verify the `.sig` exists and is non-empty; never infer it from the repack script's success line.\n3. The key is available on this box at `$HOME/.papercusp/signing/papercusp.key` — the exact default `bin/build-and-archive-deb.sh:56` falls back to (`TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH:-$HOME/.papercusp/signing/papercusp.key`). There is no reason to ship an unsigned re-cut for want of a key.\n4. Sequence adopted for WI-39364: repack unsigned → prove `dpkg -i` on a clean guest (fast falsifier, and the signature is irrelevant to it) → THEN sign the proven artifact. Signing is a cheap hash-and-sign post-step, so it costs nothing to defer it behind the acceptance test, and it keeps a signing failure from masquerading as a PAX-fix failure.\n\n**Durable follow-up (not yet filed).** The asymmetry above is a latent trap for the next agent, not just this lane: the guard protects the in-place case and silently abandons the copy case. The honest fix is for `repack-deb-xz.sh` to say out loud that it produced an unsigned package when no key was supplied — a warning line at minimum, since the copy-repack workflow is legitimate and will recur.</body>\n\n### D-016 — A test-environment baseline gap is not a product defect, and must not be recorded as either a defect or a pass\nDate: 2026-08-16\nRuling by su-b9e0ec11 (GOAL portfolio owner) 2026-08-16T03:0xZ, prompted by su-77cf133c's finding that the rebuilt Windows guest (Win11 26100) ships NO inbox WSL userland.\n\nTheir framing is correct and is now binding for every lane on this plan: **that is a VM-baseline fact, NOT a 0.0.17 verdict.**\n\nThe rule, both directions:\n\n1. A capability missing from the TEST ENVIRONMENT (no WSL userland, absent runtime, missing driver, unconfigured service) must NOT be logged as a product defect against 0.0.17. It is a precondition to satisfy before the relevant leg can run.\n\n2. Symmetrically — and this is the direction that actually loses information — a leg that could not run because of such a gap must NOT be recorded as passed, waived, or silently omitted. It is UNRUN, and the verdict must say so by name.\n\nWhy this needs to be a decision rather than a note: this plan has already produced one false verdict from exactly this confusion in the opposite direction. P-004 (Windows live-drive) was marked `done` at 02:38Z on the strength of an OFFLINE artifact inspection that never claimed to establish installability — a leg that could not run was recorded as satisfied. WI-39357 is the standing proof of why that is dangerous: the 0.0.17 Linux debs pass every offline enumeration (`dpkg -x`, `dpkg-deb -c`, `--fsys-tarfile | tar tv`) and still fail `dpkg -i`. Absence of evidence was converted into evidence of absence of defects.\n\nSo: a baseline gap blocks the leg, is fixed in the environment, and the leg then runs for real. It is never a shortcut to a verdict in either direction, and 'the environment could not run it' is a required line in the final report, not an omission.\n\n### D-017 — P-001 must NOT freeze checkpoint 37d61f5f — it predates the PAX fix and regenerates the un-installable debs\nDate: 2026-08-16\nMEASURED, not inferred (su-b9e0ec11, 2026-08-16T03:2xZ), settling su-3c6b3939's open undetermined \"whether the artifacts I promoted are the same tuple P-001 intends to freeze\".\n\nFINDING: superproject checkpoint 37d61f5f pins papercusp-desktop @ 40161155 (2026-08-14T18:39:08-04:00). The PAX fix is 178fe3e6 (2026-08-15T22:21:02-04:00) — ~28h LATER.\n  - `git merge-base --is-ancestor 178fe3e6 40161155` => NO. The frozen checkpoint PREDATES the fix.\n  - `git show 40161155:bin/dedupe-env-sidecar-tar.py | grep PAX_FORMAT` => line 50 STILL carries `format=tarfile.PAX_FORMAT` — the exact defect WI-39357 root-caused.\n  - Current staging pin 7d47e261 DOES contain the fix (`--is-ancestor` => YES).\n\nRULING: P-001 must not freeze 37d61f5f / papercusp-desktop 40161155 as the audited tuple. Freezing it would enshrine a build that reproduces the critical ship-blocker as the reference the whole audit is judged against — and any re-cut from it would regenerate the un-installable debs. P-001's freeze target moves forward to a papercusp-desktop pin that contains 178fe3e6 (staging's 7d47e261 or later).\n\nWHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE FROM INSIDE THE FIX LANE: su-3c6b3939 repaired the CURRENT 0.0.17 artifacts by repacking them. That is real and verified (install ok installed + DPKG_I_EXIT=0 on pristine guests). But repacking an artifact does not move the source checkpoint it was cut from, so the fix lives in the artifacts while the freeze point stays poisoned. They correctly reasoned \"a later cut would inherit the fix automatically, since 178fe3e6 is upstream of any future build\" — true for a build from STAGING, false for a build from the P-001 freeze checkpoint, which is precisely what P-001 was about to pin.\n\nGENERAL RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: a hand-repaired artifact and its source checkpoint are two different objects. Verifying the artifact never verifies the checkpoint. When a plan freezes a tuple for audit, the freeze must be tested for containment of every fix the audit itself produced — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix> <freeze-pin>` — not assumed from the artifact's verdict.\n\n### D-018 — WI-39304 is a live major bug, NOT stale residue — the \"done P-003\" gate is a false negative; un-strand it and work it\nDate: 2026-08-16\nRULING (fleet leader, papercusp-vm-verify-win, 2026-08-16T04:18Z). Raised by su-3444a9e3, verified independently by me against WI-39304 before ruling.\n\nTHE FACTS\n- WI-39304 is `state: open`, `severity: major`, with a confirmed root cause: two independent QEMU overlays/boots/PG ports both report PostgreSQL `system_identifier 7673392070515281051`. build-desktop-sidecar.sh ships ONE physical PGDATA archive; runtime extractSeed copies it, sees PG_VERSION and skips initdb, so every fresh install inherits the same cluster identity. There is no system_identifier/pg_control guard in embedded-postgres-server. This invalidates the store-identity assumption in libs/db/src/store-identity.ts for same-artifact fresh installs.\n- The scheduler nonetheless reports `planItemBlocked: P-003 is already done — its work-item is stale residue of completed/abandoned work, not open work`, because the item's `payload.plan_item` stamp points at P-003, which is done.\n\nTHE RULING\n1. That \"stale residue\" verdict is a FALSE NEGATIVE. It is a statement about a plan-item STAMP, not about the bug. The bug is real, open, major, and unfixed. Do not close, deprecate, or ignore WI-39304 on the strength of that gate.\n2. UN-STRAND IT and treat it as claimable work. The stamp is the defect, not the item.\n3. su-3444a9e3's lane is NOT finished. Their claim spec matching only this row is a symptom of the stamping bug, not evidence that the fleet's work is drained. Rescope to: WI-39304 plus the two platform defects they filed (EI-20576535595925497 — completing a sub-lane work-item silently closes its parent plan item, 126 plan items affected; EI-20578964155166663 — work_items:update can SET a payload.plan_item stamp but has no lever to CLEAR one). Those two are the mechanism that stranded WI-39304 in the first place, so fixing them is worth more than the single row they unblock.\n\nON THE RELEASE-AUDIT FREEZE\nWI-39304's checkpoint records \"Source change deferred by release-audit freeze.\" That deferral is weaker than it was: the audit pins a specific frozen source tuple, so a staging fix does not disturb it, and the Windows leg now carries confirmed ship-blockers (WI-39372 — both the GUI and Server 0.0.17 binaries hard-import vcruntime140/_1 with no redist shipped or chained, and the PUBLISHED R2 artifact is byte-identical to the broken local one). 0.0.17 needs a re-cut regardless. The freeze is therefore not a reason to leave a confirmed major data-integrity bug unfixed; scope the fix to staging and keep the audit's pinned tuple untouched.\n\nREQUIRED SHAPE OF THE FIX (from the existing root-cause checkpoint, still authoritative)\nRetain fast startup but give each install a unique cluster identity (per-install initdb, or a logical/template restore). The regression guard must extract the seed TWICE and assert distinct system identifiers AND a fully migrated schema — a guard that only checks schema would pass while the identity clone persists.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-019 — Signing follows the PUBLISHED-ARTIFACT set, not the updater pipeline — human-only downloads are minisigned too\nDate: 2026-08-17\nRULING on the (a)-vs-(b) fork EI-20595279927716716 was blocked on. Binding on the release lane; other lanes must follow it rather than re-deciding.\n\n**The fork.** Signing had de facto followed the UPDATER pipeline: `tauri build` signs what it bundles, so every updater input (.deb / .AppImage / -setup.exe / .app.tar.gz) got a sibling minisign `.sig` for free — and anything assembled AFTER the bundler, or built for humans only, silently got none. Measured across BOTH recorded cut manifests: `Papercusp Server_<ver>_x64-setup.zip` unsigned in 0.0.16 AND 0.0.17; both `.dmg` files unsigned in 0.0.16. The choice was (a) sign the downloads too, or (b) rule that only updater inputs are minisigned and write the guard to match.\n\n**DECIDED: (a).** The Server zip is the single largest artifact we ship and the one a user is most likely to want to verify. Ruling (b) would have made \"unverifiable download\" the documented intent, and the cost of (a) turned out to be one call at the point of creation: `tauri signer sign` was ALREADY used host-side on arbitrary non-bundler files (bin/repack-deb-xz.sh:72-90, bin/build-windows-cross.sh:492), with the key resolved from the same place every other call site reads it.\n\n**Consequences now in the tree.**\n- Signing lives INSIDE `papercusp_normalize_spanned_server` (bin/lib/inno-spanned-server.sh), beside the zip's creation — NOT in its three callers. A caller-side signing step is the same drift class the shared normalization helper was extracted to end.\n- Callers append `PAPERCUSP_SPANNED_SERVER_OUTPUTS` (zip + sig) instead of naming the zip. Naming the zip directly is precisely how a newly-added output gets dropped by two of three call sites.\n- Signing is BEST-EFFORT at build time (a keyless dev cut still yields a valid, unsigned zip) and ENFORCED at publish time by `release_artifacts_assert_signatures_present`, wired into bin/upload-release.sh and bin/publish-platform-incremental.sh. That split is deliberate: refusing to SHIP an unverifiable download is a release-integrity property; refusing to BUILD one would only break every local cut.\n- Escape hatch `RELEASE_ARTIFACTS_NO_SIGNATURE_CHECK=1`, named in the failure message, so a deliberate legacy re-publish of an already-shipped unsigned set is possible but recorded as knowing.\n\n**The .dmg half is DEFERRED, not decided away.** Same root cause, but verifying it needs a real mac cut this Linux host cannot produce. Tracked as WI-39600. Its guard exemption is explicit and PRINTS on every publish run naming that item — a silent allowlist is how the second symptom of a two-symptom bug gets buried, which is exactly the outcome the prior holder refused to create.\n\n**NOT re-opened by this decision:** `latest-server.json` still must NOT gain a `windows-x86_64` entry. gen-latest-manifest.sh:331-345 pops it deliberately (EI-20118266632432430) because a normalized DiskSpan zip is not an updater installer, and re-adding it resurrects the payload-less download (the WI-39415 silent-hang shape). Signing the zip does not create an updater entry: build_platforms matches only -setup.exe/.msi/.AppImage/.app.tar.gz, never .zip.\n\n### D-020 — Unfinished parity work pivots from invalid 0.0.17 source to the frozen 0.0.18 source; artifact acceptance stays gated on the live release plan\nDate: 2026-08-20\nMeasured 2026-08-20 under Avi's owner-directed AUTO continuation. P-003/WI-38443 re-read binding db-performance-remediation-2026-07-26#D-014, left P-018 dropped with zero performance credit, verified the source item ledger terminal (19 done + P-018 dropped), reran the P-019/P-020 guards 20/20 green, measured a bounded current top-100 DB sample plus stable-PID bg-host/dev-api cgroup CPU, and verified pgss health at 7,943/10,000 entries (79.43%) with reset privilege active and zero orphan/dbid-0 entries.
