Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Reconciliation baseline: trust terminal item/work-item evidence over stale headers; three source plans retain real work\nDate: 2026-08-13\nBounded live reconciliation on 2026-08-13 covered all eight owner-named plans, their structured item ledgers, latest governing decisions, and linked residual work-items. Terminal now: spawner-sidecar-cluster-fanout-2026-08-12 (shipped; 7 done); gate-suite-speedup-2026-08-12 (shipped; 3 done, 1 deliberately dropped); operator-memory-and-psu-resilience-2026-06-14 (shipped; 11 done, 2 dropped); process-lifecycle-no-orphans-2026-08-02 (13 done, 1 dropped; header still stale at ready; former WI-7306 is done with live residue-census evidence); bg-host-freeze-eventloop-stall-2026-06-30 (6 done; header stale at ready). Do not rebuild those lanes; P-006 only fresh-live verifies and reconciles their headers.\n\nReal residue remains in three source plans. perf-testing-sweep-2026-07-27 has a stale 3-done/13-todo ledger even though linked WI-6530, WI-6538, WI-6539, and WI-6543 are all done; it still requires a fresh load-stamped consolidated sweep and honest status reconciliation (D-002/D-003 govern measurement validity). db-performance-remediation-2026-07-26 has 17 done/3 todo: P-019/WI-6875 and P-020/WI-9313 are done with integration/live evidence, but P-018 is genuinely open as EI-19300220274441392 (single-runner system-health snapshot replacing ~22x background-host fanout; D-004/D-012 govern). memory-write-latency-2026-07-26 has 5 done/4 dropped/1 needs-human: EI-18746586784230719, EI-18747066020546067, and memory:search residual EI-18748795522559631 are done; WI-6215 production latency confirmation is still open. Under owner-directed AUTO, the remaining conflict-check fork is resolved toward retiring the inert Anthropic-only judge rather than adding a per-write LLM call; D-001..D-004 and the measured 4.2% query-repeat ceiling remain binding.\n\nThe separate recurring host-memory incident EI-20326370033296542 is now done: it proved the preserved 08:38 event was not correlated with operator-worker RSS and added bounded cgroup-v2 attribution plus tests. Its completion explicitly says the historical generator is unknowable and no new live recurrence has occurred, so this is detector closure, not proof the host-pressure class is gone; P-002 must still verify representative-load recovery and act on any new attributed recurrence.\n\nThis decision is the P-001 baseline. Downstream execution is P-002 host memory, P-003 DB/CPU, P-004 fresh perf sweep, P-005 memory latency/conflict-check retirement, P-006 fresh lifecycle/sidecar verification; P-007 handles delivery only after those lanes are verified.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-002 — Preserve 65b3 while the run-lock owner and ledger advance\nDate: 2026-08-13\nFor candidate 65b3fbd1, liveness is determined by the per-root run-lock owner plus current candidate ledger progress, not by the lifetime of individual test-worker children. At 10:02 EDT, old worker PIDs 166271/967244 were dead, but lock owner PID 133202 was alive with two direct children, its process start preceded the lock write, phase protocol 2 remained `suite`, and the candidate ledger advanced from 4,041 to 4,296 rows through 10:03 EDT. Therefore the run is healthy and must not be replaced. Reclassify only when the lock owner dies/stales and ledger progress stops, or when an authoritative terminal verdict publishes.\n\n### D-003 — Desktop-perf block-mode stays DISARMED until measurement is load-controlled; LCP is not yet evidence of regression\nDate: 2026-08-16\n#### What was measured (WI-38449, 2026-08-16T04:2x–04:29Z)\n\nThe desktop-perf suite produced its first trustworthy web-vitals numbers ever (the instrument was\nbroken until this session — see WI-38449). Four consecutive smoke runs on this box, each stamped\nwith the 1-minute load average at launch, 112 cores:\n\n| load (1m) | FCP ms | LCP ms | vs 4000ms LCP budget |\n|-----------|--------|--------|----------------------|\n| 99        | 1013   | 3446   | pass                 |\n| 107       | 1227   | 4004   | FAIL by 4ms          |\n| 121       | 2955   | 5742   | FAIL                 |\n| (unstamped) | 1444 | 4466   | FAIL                 |\n\nLCP and FCP both track load monotonically across every sample. The spread is 3446–5742ms — the\nbudget sits INSIDE the noise band, and one run missed by four milliseconds.\n\n#### Decision\n\n1. **A desktop-perf budget miss measured under fleet load is NOT evidence of a performance\n   regression, and must not be reported as one.** On these numbers the verdict is decided by how\n   many agents happened to be running, not by the code under test. Any future claim that desktop\n   LCP/FCP regressed must carry the load stamp at measurement time, or it is unsupported.\n\n2. **`policy.block` in `apps/operator/lib/release/desktop-perf-gate.ts` STAYS `false`.** P-004's\n   \"restore EFFECTIVE blocking perf gates\" does not authorise arming this one yet. Arming it today\n   would block deploys on a measurement whose pass/fail is dominated by ambient load — converting a\n   silent fail-soft gate (13 days of it) into a loud FALSE-RED gate. That trades one broken gate for\n   another, and the second kind freezes the fleet.\n\n3. **The precondition for arming is a load-CONTROLLED measurement, not merely green numbers.**\n   Whoever arms it must first establish one of: a quiesced measurement window, a load-normalised\n   budget, or best-of-N with the load stamp recorded per sample. Until then the gate's correct\n   posture is warn-not-block, which is what it already does.\n\n#### What is NOT being claimed\n\nThat desktop LCP is fine. 3446ms at the QUIETEST sampled load is still slow against a 2500ms\n\"good\" LCP, and that is worth pursuing on its own — but it is a separate investigation from\n\"did this candidate regress\", and it needs a quiet box to measure honestly.\n\n#### Why this is a Decision and not a note\n\nIt governs a step other lanes will otherwise take: the plan text says \"restore effective blocking\nperf gates\", and the obvious reading of that is \"flip block to true once measures are green\". This\nrecords that the obvious reading is wrong here, and what has to be true first.\n\n### D-004 — D-003's ruling STANDS but its \"monotonic in load\" evidence does NOT — loadavg was the wrong instrument; use PSI\nDate: 2026-08-16\nSelf-correction to my own D-003, recorded rather than left to ride. The OPERATIVE RULING IS UNCHANGED and is now better supported; only the stated evidence was too strong.\n\n== WHAT D-003 CLAIMED ==\nThat desktop LCP \"tracks load monotonically\", from four samples stamped with the 1-minute loadavg:\n  load 87 → 2722 | 99 → 3446 | 107 → 4004 | 121 → 5742.\n\n== WHAT BROKE IT ==\nThe full-suite run at 2026-08-16T05:1xZ measured LCP = 2143ms at loadavg 98.93 — LOWER than the load-87 sample (2722ms) and far below the earlier load-99 sample (3446ms). Same code, same box, same spec. A monotonic relation cannot produce 3446 and 2143 at the same stamped load.\n\n== WHY THE STAMP WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT ==\n/proc/loadavg is a trailing EWMA of runnable+uninterruptible tasks, not current CPU contention; on this box it reads high for minutes AFTER a busy period ends. Measured side by side just now:\n  /proc/loadavg      => 56.92 72.44 87.71\n  /proc/pressure/cpu => some avg10=0.05 avg60=0.17 avg300=0.87  (full: 0.00)\nLoadavg says \"57\"; PSI says there is essentially NO CPU stall pressure. So every D-003 \"load stamp\" recorded a decaying average that may or may not describe the interval the run actually occupied. The correlation was real-looking because the samples were taken as the box drained, which makes a trailing average look like an independent variable.\n\n== WHAT IS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED ==\nLCP on identical code spans 2143–5742ms across six samples — a 2.7x spread with a budget (4000ms) sitting inside it. That is a STRONGER argument for D-003's ruling than monotonicity was: the variance is not merely load-explained, it is not yet explained at all, so a single sample cannot support any verdict.\n\n== RULING (unchanged, restated so it is quotable from here) ==\n`desktop-perf-gate.ts:233` policy.block STAYS false. Arming it would trade a silent fail-soft gate for a loud false-red one that freezes the fleet on ambient variance.\n\n== BINDING METHOD CHANGE ==\nAny future load stamp for a desktop perf measurement MUST record /proc/pressure/cpu (`some avg10`, and `full`) — captured at BOTH the start and end of the run — not /proc/loadavg alone. A loadavg-only stamp is not evidence about contention during the measured window. The LCP-on-a-quiet-box investigation D-003 deferred should be gated on `some avg10` being near zero, which is a condition that can actually be checked, rather than on a loadavg threshold, which cannot.\n\nNOT CLAIMED: that load has no effect on LCP. It plausibly does. The claim being retracted is only that the four D-003 samples DEMONSTRATED a monotonic relation — they do not, and a fifth and sixth sample contradict it.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-005 — LCP IS reproducible under a PSI-quiet window (2527–2803ms) — so the effective blocking gate is QUIET-GATED blocking, not permanent warn-only\nDate: 2026-08-16\nCloses the investigation D-003 deferred (\"LCP on a quiet box\") and supersedes the implicit conclusion that blocking must stay off forever. P-004's mandate is to restore EFFECTIVE blocking perf gates; this is the design that does it without the false-red D-003 refused.\n\n== MEASURED (3 runs, PSI-stamped per D-004's binding method) ==\n  run | PSI some avg10 | loadavg(1m) | FCP | LCP\n   1  | 0.03           | 52.45       | 727 | 2737\n   2  | 0.00           | 56.85       | 727 | 2803\n   3  | 0.08           | 50.94       | 626 | 2527\n`full` pressure was 0.00 throughout — the box was genuinely uncontended.\n\nTWO results, and the second is the important one:\n\n(1) LCP UNDER A QUIET WINDOW IS TIGHT AND REPRODUCIBLE: 2527–2803ms, a 276ms spread (~10%). That is nothing like the 2143–5742ms (2.7x) spread across uncontrolled conditions. The measurement is not inherently noisy — it was being taken without controlling the one variable that matters.\n\n(2) LOADAVG IS ANTI-CORRELATED HERE, which finishes off D-003's retracted evidence: the full-suite run at loadavg 98.93 measured LCP=2143 — FASTER than all three quiet runs at loadavg ~50-57. A variable that moves the wrong way is not the explanation. D-004 retracted monotonicity; this retires loadavg as a stamp entirely.\n\n== VERDICT ON THE NUMBER ==\n2527–2803ms sits in web-vitals' \"needs improvement\" band (good ≤2500ms, poor >4000ms). So: NOT a budget breach (budget 4000ms), NOT a regression, but genuinely a touch slower than \"good\" — worth its own optimisation item, NOT a release-blocking finding. The earlier 4466/5742 readings did NOT reproduce under a quiet window and must not be cited as evidence of a regression.\n\n== THE RULING — how P-004 restores an EFFECTIVE gate ==\n`desktop-perf-gate.ts:233` policy.block must NOT be flipped to an unconditional `true` (that is what D-003 refused, and it stands). Nor may it stay permanently `false`, which is an inert gate — the exact failure P-004 exists to fix. The gate becomes effective by making the SAMPLE, not the verdict, the thing that is gated:\n\n  1. Every desktop-perf run RECORDS its PSI stamp (/proc/pressure/cpu `some avg10` + `full`) at start and end, alongside the measures.\n  2. The gate treats a run taken OUTSIDE a quiet window as UNMEASURABLE — neither pass nor fail. An unmeasurable sample must never be published as a timing and must never satisfy the gate.\n  3. Blocking arms ONLY for a breach measured INSIDE a quiet window.\n\nThis is the same void-sample principle already applied twice in this lane: the egress spec records -1 rather than a truthful-but-meaningless 0, and plan-popup-open now throws `UNMEASURABLE:` rather than publishing a timing for a plan that never opened. A gate that cannot distinguish \"measured and fine\" from \"never measured\" is the defect class this whole plan item is about.\n\n== WHY THIS IS NOT JUST DEFERRING AGAIN ==\nThe quiet-window condition is CHECKABLE (`some avg10` near zero), unlike a loadavg threshold, which D-004 showed is not evidence about contention at all. So the precondition can be enforced mechanically rather than trusted.\n\nNOT CLAIMED: that a quiet window is always available on this box, or that the 3-run band generalises to other hardware. The band is 3 samples on one host; it justifies the DESIGN, and the threshold itself should be re-derived from a larger PSI-stamped sample before block-mode is armed for real.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-006 — D-006 — The quiet window is `some avg10 ≤ 1.0` / `full = 0`, derived from n=15; and a CONTENDED sample can read falsely FAST, so it is unmeasurable in BOTH directions\nDate: 2026-08-16\nCompletes D-005's outstanding precondition (\"the threshold itself should be re-derived from a larger PSI-stamped sample before block-mode is armed for real\") and corrects an assumption I was about to ship in code comments.\n\n== THE SAMPLE ==\n14 further smoke runs back-to-back on this box, 2026-08-16T02:08–02:15Z, plus the first stamped run at 01:47Z. n=15, each stamped at START and END per D-004's binding method; a run's pressure is the WORSE of its two stamps. Ambient fleet load varied on its own (PSI 0.00–3.26, loadavg 50–100), so the range is observed rather than manufactured. Data lives in harness_shared.desktop_perf_runs (`host:psi-cpu-*` measures) and is pinned in desktop-perf-gate.test.ts.\n\nBinned by candidate threshold T:\n\n  T      quiet n   LCP range (ms)   spread      headroom to the 4000ms budget\n  0.1        6     2206–2721        515 (20%)   1279ms (47% above worst quiet)\n  0.5        8     2206–2765        559 (21%)   1235ms (45%)\n  1.0        9     2206–2817        611 (23%)   1183ms (42%)\n  1.5       10     2206–2916        710 (27%)   1084ms (37%)\n  2.0       13     2206–3085        879 (33%)    915ms (30%)\n\n== RULING 1 — THE THRESHOLD ==\nThe quiet window is `/proc/pressure/cpu some avg10 ≤ 1.0` AND `full avg10 = 0`, BOTH phases inside it. 1.0 is the knee: it admits 9 of 15 real runs while holding the band at 611ms, and every LCP reading worse than 2817ms in the whole sample falls OUTSIDE it. Loosening to 1.5/2.0 buys 1 and 4 more runs for a spread that grows faster than the sample does. D-005's independent 3-run band (2527–2803ms at PSI 0.00–0.08) lands inside this one — corroboration from a separate session, not a restatement.\n\nWHY THIS MAKES ARMING SAFE, which is the point D-003 was right to hold out for: inside the window the worst observed LCP is 2817ms against a 4000ms budget — 42% headroom, versus a 611ms measurement spread. A breach measured inside the window is a ~40%+ move, an order of magnitude outside the noise. When D-003 refused to arm, the budget sat INSIDE a 2143–5742ms band; that gap now exists, so it can be armed. `full = 0` was 0.00 on all 15 samples and is therefore a floor against an obviously-invalidating condition, NOT a fitted parameter — stated so nobody cites it as measured.\n\n== RULING 2 — A CONTENDED SAMPLE IS UNMEASURABLE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ==\nI was about to justify \"a PASS under contention is honoured\" with \"contention can only slow an interaction down, so an under-budget reading on a busy box is a pass a fortiori\". THE SAMPLE FALSIFIES THAT, and it is a plausible-enough error to be worth recording rather than quietly deleting:\n\n  Spearman rho vs max PSI:  FCP +0.78  (quiet mean 716ms → contended 850ms)\n                            LCP +0.32\n  Contended LCP mean 2581ms vs quiet 2629ms — the CENTRE barely moves.\n  Contended LCP range 1311–3246ms vs quiet 2206–2817ms — the PRECISION collapses.\n  The single most contended run (PSI 3.26) reported LCP=1311ms — 895ms FASTER than\n  ANY quiet reading — while its FCP was simultaneously the second-worst at 996ms.\n\nMECHANISM: FCP is a first-paint timestamp and inflates under contention as expected. LCP is a largest-element-SO-FAR metric, so contention that stops the big element painting inside the observation window leaves a smaller, earlier element holding the title. Contention makes LCP arbitrary, not merely slow.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for other lanes: a green desktop LCP measured under load is NOT reassurance and must not be cited as one, exactly as D-005 already established that a red one is not evidence of regression. The two errors are symmetric and this half was previously unstated. A PASS under contention is still honoured by the gate — but only because an unmeasurable sample never blocks in either direction, so a contended pass and a contended breach produce the SAME action (advance); the difference is confined to what gets REPORTED, and the gate now names the pressure class rather than calling it a clear.\n\n== WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED ==\nThat 1.0 generalises to other hardware (n=15, one 128-core host). That the LCP number itself is good — 2206–2817ms is web-vitals \"needs improvement\" (good ≤2500), which is a separate optimisation item and NOT release-blocking. That `full > 0` was ever observed here.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-010 — P-007's D-009 wall died by events — closed with current evidence; the 2026-08-2x red streak is a DISTINCT condition outside this plan's scope\nDate: 2026-08-25\nDate: 2026-08-25\nRULING (supersedes D-009's operative block; recorded while closing P-007 under WI-41654, su-592946c2). All evidence re-measured 2026-08-25T15:04–15:07Z, not recalled.\n\nP-007's three criteria are all discharged:\n1. git-sync push failure RESOLVED — WI-39646 closed 2026-08-19 owner-directed (Avi): local staging == origin/staging (b6668fb6da, `git rev-list --count` = 0 unpushed vs the claimed 748), origin observed advancing twice within one session via the github-bridge (which never runs local hooks), origin tree intact (22,870 files / 38 gitlinks, 38/38 submodules populated). All three owner decisions D-009 waited on are MOOT. Residue: the 08-15 guard hooks remain installed and block only MANUAL pushes — tracked separately per the WI-39646 close; not a delivery blocker.\n2. Red checkpoint failures resolved + green verdict re-run — the gate-red-streak singleton WI-39450 was closed by the condition bridge 2026-08-20T15:50Z: the condition RESOLVED, i.e. a green verdict landed and main promoted past the frozen pin 4824a92b.\n3. Deployed to the owner-facing release — :3070 serves 6760f8ec31cc (state:read deploy.3070.sha, ≠ 4824a92b), and the closeout's perf block-flags (papercusp-desktop-perf-gate-block, papercusp-host-perf-gate-block) resolve ok:true/enabled:true in the LIVE process with the positive control (papercusp-desktop-perf-gate) also true (flags:get 15:06Z). Those keys measurably did NOT exist at 4824a92b (negative control on WI-38449 post 69332), so live resolution proves the serving process runs post-pin code — behavioral proof, stronger than the sha-probe's process-unverified caveat.\n\nThe CURRENT red streak (41 consecutive as of 15:05Z, verdict-stale — it judged a superseded candidate) began AFTER the 08-20 green and is a NEW gate-red-streak condition with its own singleton owner, verified HELD-LIVE (state:read gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership = held-live, 15:05Z). It is NOT P-007's scope: P-007 bound \"the current … failures\" at authoring time and \"deploy the verified closeout\", both discharged above. Per the anti-parallel-fixer rule, lanes on this plan must NOT open a second fixer against the live-owned streak; the umbrella plan's ship path (P-008) does not depend on it.\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n\n### D-007 — D-007 — The HOST perf gate was blind for 7h (dead producer) and must NOT be armed as-is: its crit tier mixes candidate-irrelevant AMBIENT host state with real operator wedges, and a dead producer currently reports `pass` SILENTLY\nDate: 2026-08-16\n⚠ THE TITLE OVERSTATES FINDING 2 AND CANNOT BE EDITED — READ THIS FIRST.\n\"a dead producer currently reports `pass` SILENTLY\" is TRUE of the DESKTOP gate and **FALSE of the HOST gate**. I asserted it of both before reading `perf-budgets.ts` closely enough. Correction in Finding 2; Findings 1 and 3 stand as measured. Measured 2026-08-16T06:5xZ.\n\n== FINDING 1 (STANDS — FIXED) — the host producer was DEAD for ~7 hours ==\n`papercup-perf-signals-capture.timer` was `Active: failed (Result: resources)`. Journal cause: at 19:57:59 EDT systemd could not open the unit file — \"No such file or directory ... Unit to trigger vanished\". The units are LINKED into ~/.config/systemd/user/ through the `papercupai-workspace/papercup` → `papercusp` symlink into the repo tree, so a peer tree operation transiently removed the target; systemd latched `failed` and NOTHING recovered it.\nLast capture 2026-08-15T23:56:38Z vs `PERF_BUDGETS.staleMs = 600_000` (10min) — ~42x past the window.\nFIXED: `systemctl --user daemon-reload` + `restart`. VERIFIED BY READING THE ARTEFACT, not an exit code: `~/.papercusp/perf-baselines/2026-08-16T065321Z-scheduled.json`, capturedAt 06:53:21Z, age 36s, timer `active`.\nSTILL OPEN (the durable half): nothing detects a vanished/failed unit file for a release-gate producer. A one-off restart is not the fix for that class.\n\n== FINDING 2 (CORRECTED) — the silent-blind hole is the DESKTOP gate's, not the host's ==\nWHAT I GOT WRONG: I claimed both gates report a bare `pass` when their producer dies, reasoning that green-checkpoint only logs/broadcasts when `action !== 'pass'` (that part is true). I wrote the \"fix\" into perf-gate.ts. It was wrong there and is REVERTED.\nWHY: `perf-budgets.ts` already solves this for the host gate, better than my change did — WI-324's `blindMs` (30min) branch splits a BRIEF gap from a DEAD producer. A capture 10–30min old stays `unknown` (skipped timer tick — quiet on purpose); past 30min it is promoted to **`warn`** carrying \"perf-signals capture Nmin stale — host SLO monitor blind; check papercup-perf-signals-capture.timer\". So during the 7h outage this gate WAS warning, and naming the exact unit. My change would have warned on every skipped tick — noise — and destroyed a deliberate distinction.\nWHAT SURVIVES (the substantive half): the DESKTOP gate has no such tier. Both its no-run and stale branches returned `pass`, so its summary (\"nothing is producing fresh runs\") reached nobody — which is why it went 13 days unnoticed while the host gate's 7h outage was audible.\nRULING (desktop gate only): an ABSENT or STALE desktop-perf run resolves to `warn`, not `pass` — still never blocking, never a breach, but audible. This is WI-324's treatment ported to the sibling that lacked it, and the principle D-005 applied to an unmeasurable sample: \"measured and fine\" and \"nobody measured\" are opposite facts a bare `pass` conflates.\nGENERAL LESSON, worth more than either finding: a sibling that looks like it shares a defect may already have solved it with a distinction you have not read. I nearly deleted a good design to apply a rule I had just derived elsewhere.\n\n== FINDING 3 (STANDS) — DO NOT ARM `perf-gate.ts` BLOCK-MODE AS IT STANDS ==\nAgainst the LIVE fresh capture, `evaluatePerfSignals` returns **crit** on exactly one reason:\n  \"PSI memory full avg60 11.45 ≥ 5 — all tasks stalled on memory reclaim/swap\"\nand `evaluatePerfGate(verdict, { enabled:true, block:true })` → **`block`**. Flipping `block` today would hold every deploy while ~100 peer agents use RAM — the false-red D-003 refused, reproduced in the host gate.\nThe crit set must first be split by ATTRIBUTION:\n  AMBIENT (about the BOX, never the candidate — must never block):\n    · `PSI cpu some avg60 ≥ 85` · memory-pressure crit (firing now)\n  OPERATOR-DEFECT (the operator is actually broken — a legitimate interlock):\n    · `:3070 unreachable` · `hostState=wedge-active` · `event-loop lag p95 ≥ 1000ms`\n    · `CLOSE_WAIT ≥ 500` · `inotify ≥ 80% of max_user_watches`\nAGAINST MY OWN CAUTION: group-two thresholds are deliberately meltdown-class (a FULL SECOND of lag p95; 500 sockets), and perf-budgets.ts:102-103 says the CPU-share signal is \"never crit on its own\". Group two is closer to a D-005 INVARIANT than a tuned budget, so arming for it is defensible — once separable from group one, which today it is not.\n\n== NOT CLAIMED ==\nThat the memory crit is spurious (`full avg60 11.45` is real thrashing, worth its own item) — only that it is not attributable to a candidate. That group two never false-reds (unmeasured). That `system_health_ticks.overall` bears on this gate: it is the system-health DASHBOARD, pinned crit by `toolEfficiency`, a different subsystem. I checked it first and it is NOT this gate's input — do not cite its 100%-crit rate here.\n\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-008 — D-007 F3 implemented: the HOST perf gate blocks by ATTRIBUTION, not by crit tier — and block-mode is now armed (default ON)\nDate: 2026-08-16\nImplements D-007 finding 3 and closes the \"restore an EFFECTIVE blocking gate\" half of P-004 for the HOST gate. Sibling of D-005/D-006, which did the same for the desktop gate via a quiet-window.\n\n#### The problem, measured (not predicted)\nArming `perf-gate.ts` block-mode as it stood would have blocked EVERY deploy. On a live capture 2026-08-16 the verdict was `crit` on the SINGLE reason `PSI memory full avg60 11.45 >= 5` — ambient RAM pressure from ~100 peer agents on this shared box — and `evaluatePerfGate(verdict, { enabled:true, block:true })` returned `block`. Nothing was wrong with any candidate. The crit tier MIXED ambient host state with genuine operator wedges, so \"crit\" could not be used as a block signal.\n\n#### The ruling\nA crit BLOCKS only for reasons attributable to the operator itself.\n\n- **operatorDefect (may block):** `:3070 unreachable` · `hostState=wedge-active` · `event-loop lag p95 >= 1000ms` · `CLOSE_WAIT >= 500`. Meltdown-class properties of OUR process; a full second of lag p95 or 500 sockets is not ambient noise.\n- **ambientHost (NEVER blocks):** PSI cpu `some avg60 >= 85` · memory-pressure crit · host-total inotify `>= 80%` of max_user_watches.\n\n**This changes what BLOCKS, never what is REPORTED.** An ambient crit is still `status:'crit'`, still `degraded`, still carries every reason in `reasons`, and still alarms. Only the deploy-hold decision is narrowed. No panel, state cell or alarm reader is affected.\n\n#### Two sub-rulings worth citing separately\n1. **inotify host-total is AMBIENT — this CORRECTS the provisional D-007 note, which listed it as an operator defect.** The kernel limit is per-UID, so the host total counts every process the owner runs; WI-6538 measured VS Code alone holding 38,937 watches (3.9x the per-proc budget) and rewrote the WARN path for exactly that reason. Blocking a release because the owner's editor watches files is a red the candidate's author cannot fix — the \"permanently amber for a reason nobody can fix\" failure WI-6538 names. The OWNED per-process balloon (our own recursive watcher — the actual 2026-07-10 meltdown class) is still budgeted on the warn path, where ownership data exists to attribute it.\n2. **Attribution is assigned where each reason is RAISED, never derived later from reason prose.** Post-hoc string-matching over text those same lines format would mis-attribute the moment anyone reworded a message, and would fail toward \"operator-defect\" — i.e. toward blocking deploys, the expensive direction.\n\n#### Fail-soft rules (all three deliberate)\n- An **unattributed** crit (both lists empty — e.g. a verdict from older code) NEVER blocks. An unclassified reason must not invent a deploy hold.\n- An **unreadable block flag** ⇒ warn-only, never armed. A flag-store hiccup must not manufacture a deploy-holding verdict.\n- `block` requires `enabled`: never report armed-but-disabled, which would read as \"this can hold a deploy\" while it evaluates nothing.\n- An armed gate that DECLINES to block **says so in its summary**, naming the ambient class. A silent non-block is the same invisible suppression that hid 13 days of fail-soft (D-007 F2).\n\n#### Armed\nNEW `FLAGS.HOST_PERF_GATE_BLOCK` = `papercusp-host-perf-gate-block`, **DEFAULT ON** by derivation (not added to DARK_FLAGS, so no watermark bump). `perfGatePolicyFromFlags` gained `readBlockFlag`; `block` is no longer hardwired false. It is a FLAGS entry rather than a hardwired `true` for the same reason as its desktop sibling: this gate holds DEPLOYS, so if it ever holds them wrongly, the green pipeline is precisely what would be unavailable to ship a code fix — it must be disarmable at runtime via /admin/features.\n\n#### Evidence\n- Live re-probe, same box, same ambient crit: `block=true -> warn` (was `block`), summary \"block-mode armed, but all 1 crit reason(s) are AMBIENT HOST state, not this candidate\", `verdictStatus` still `crit`. (`npx tsx .papercusp/scratch/host-gate-probe.ts`)\n- 487 passed / exit 0 across perf-gate + perf-budgets + desktop-perf-gate + green-checkpoint.\n- New coverage includes a single-field DISCRIMINATION pair (identical reasons, only attribution differs => block vs warn), a CALIBRATION case proving arming itself still works, an unattributed case, and a runtime case for a verdict built before the field existed (apps/operator is outside lint:tsc scope, so that is a runtime shape, not a compile error).\n- `check-required-field-strands --typecheck` over the new required `PerfVerdict.critAttribution`: `scope=all exit=0 status=clean` — no stranded construction sites.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-009 — P-007 is walled in BOTH halves, not just its git-sync-push half — a green verdict cannot promote main while the 08-15 incident pre-push guard stands\nDate: 2026-08-18\nRULING (binding on every lane touching this plan; supersedes the earlier reading that P-007's \"red-checkpoint half\" was independently completable).\n\nMEASURED 2026-08-18T19:15Z by su-2e933d99 [self-imposed ruling on a measured fact — NOT an owner directive]:\n\n1. `.git/hooks/pre-push` (the 08-15 incident guard, installed 08-15T19:59) is UNCONDITIONAL: `exit 1` for every push. `git config core.hooksPath` is UNSET, so this file — not `bin/git-hooks/pre-push` — is the hook git actually runs.\n\n2. green-checkpoint is DESIGNED to be the one writer allowed past the repo's own guard: `deps.push` (green-checkpoint.ts:9928-9945) sets `PAPERCUSP_MAIN_PUSH_OK=1`, and `bin/git-hooks/pre-push` honours that env (4 references). The INCIDENT guard does NOT (0 references) — it defeats the gate's sole-writer bypass.\n\n3. DIRECT FALSIFIER (not inference): `PAPERCUSP_MAIN_PUSH_OK=1 git push --dry-run origin 4824a92bf8fc:refs/heads/main` → \"PUSH BLOCKED - incident guard\", rc=1. Run 19:15Z with the gate's exact env; dry-run, nothing written.\n\n4. Promotion is push-first BY DESIGN: `pushGreenCandidateOrThrow` (:5002-5029) rethrows the push failure — \"swallowing it lets local `main` advance, emits a false deployable verdict\". So a push failure means local `main` does NOT advance either. `CheckpointOpts.noPush` exists but appears ONLY in green-checkpoint.test.ts — it is a test seam, not exposed on the cron or `release:checkpoint-run` path.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: P-007's text — \"resolve ... every red checkpoint failure, rerun the green verdict, and deploy the verified closeout to the owner-facing release\" — cannot reach its outcome by any amount of red-chasing. A perfectly green candidate terminates at step 3. P-007 → `blocked` on WI-39646 (needs-human, unassigned, no movement since 08-17T17:10Z); P-008 remains blocked solely on P-007.\n\nWHAT REMAINS ACTIONABLE WITHOUT THE RULING: keeping the tree genuinely green so the ruling can be executed immediately when it lands. That work continues and is NOT gated.\n\nSEPARATE, INDEPENDENT FINDING — the red streak is not evidence of a broken tree. All 26 consecutive reds examined so far are stale-candidate artifacts. Run @44159641 (17:15Z, still executing at 19:15Z) is provably unsalvageable: its range base 4824a92b..44159641 contains TWO non-overlapping breakage windows — the css-tokens break (fixed at 8aca32a8e5, 16:26Z, INSIDE the range) and the generated-declarations break (introduced 16:10Z/16:28Z, fixed at 702ce2086b/137762567f, 17:47Z, AFTER the range). Every prefix before 16:10 is red on css; every prefix after 16:26 is red on declarations. No green prefix exists, so the partial-green-gate salvage is walking a range that cannot contain one — 1h40m of run budget spent on a search with no solution, which then starves the next cron.\n\nAll four files named by the last two runs PASS at HEAD (verified 19:10Z: validate-active-routines + css-tokens 36/36; declaration-export-parity + generated-declarations 15/15 verified 18:0xZ).\n\nDO NOT read \"26 consecutive reds\" as \"the tree is broken\". Read it as \"the gate has not yet judged a candidate young enough to still be true\".\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"wake-deaf-pty-host-guard-2026-08-13","title":"Durable fix for the wake-deaf pty-host class: an external, vintage-agnostic wedge detector","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Durable fix for the wake-deaf pty-host class: an external, vintage-agnostic wedge detector\nslug: wake-deaf-pty-host-guard-2026-08-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-13\n---\n\n## Goal\nA long-lived psu-pty host runs whatever code it started with, forever. When its owner-composer\nwedges, it silently swallows every wake — and NOTHING detects it. Owner rejected per-host\nrelaunch as a mitigation and asked for a durable fix (EI-20287339148365013).\n\n## Why an EXTERNAL detector is the only correct shape (verified, not assumed)\npsu-pty-host.mjs acks `accepted` BEFORE the delivery gate runs, and its own comment states the\ncaller learns the outcome \"from the durable event log or the pty's own output, NEVER from this\nACK\". So the wake receipt is structurally incapable of reporting a deferral. The per-owner\n`~/.papercusp/psu-pty/<owner>.events.jsonl` ledger is the ONLY channel carrying the truth, and\nit is written identically by hosts of EVERY code vintage — which is what lets one detector reach\nthe 64 live pre-fix hosts that can never self-heal.\n\n## Why the in-host breaker is not enough\nb9543fc83e's shouldBreakComposerWedge + the consecutiveDefers path fix the class GOING FORWARD,\nbut a code fix cannot reach a process that started before it, and a carry-respawn restarts the\nAGENT, not the HOST (measured: su-f0c6fa5e respawned 22:56:00Z, deferred its first wake 22:59:12Z\nagainst the same phantom; host pid alive since 08:45:50Z).\n\n## Layering property worth preserving\nThe in-host breaker trips at 5 consecutive defers. This guard's threshold sits ABOVE it, so if\nthis guard ever fires, the first-line fix demonstrably did not — the trigger condition is itself\nthe evidence that the host cannot self-heal.\n\n## Reuse-first anchors (located, not to be re-invented)\n- `stalled-loops-guard.ts` + `stalled-loops-action.ts` + `seed-stalled-loops-routine.ts` — the\n  guard/action/seed triad and its deps-injection test shape.\n- `events/await/psu-pty-discovery.ts` — operator-core ALREADY owns the ledger contract:\n  `PSU_PTY_DIR`, `PsuPtyHost`, `sanitizeKey`, `listLiveHosts`, bounded-tail event reading.\n- `register-system-actions.ts` — the import barrel. Omitting it is how `sweep-stalled-loops` sat\n  seeded-but-dead for a week (\"no handler registered ... skipping\").\n\n## Known trap this must encode (retraction from the prior session)\nThe per-owner ledger OUTLIVES the host process. Counting defers WITHOUT scoping to\n`ts > host.startedAt` charges a host with its predecessor's incidents and falsely implicated 4\nextra hosts. Ground truth at 2026-08-12T23:08Z: 162 live hosts, exactly 3 genuinely wedged\n(su-efa8b152 / su-91ef0643 / su-f0c6fa5e). That population is the calibration set.\n\n## Scope decision\nPhase 1 is DETECT + SURFACE. Rewiring the wake-reachability oracle (a wedged host currently\nadvertises the BEST channel, `psu-socket` reachable:true) is deliberately deferred to Phase 2:\nthat signal feeds loop-termination guards, so a false positive there disarms live agents. Measure\nthe detector's precision against the live population first, then rewire.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Detect and surface\n\n- **P-001** `done` Pure detector: classify a host ledger tail as wedged — consecutive turn-deferred-for-owner-input since host.startedAt, constant pendingLength, no intervening clear event importance: high\n- **P-002** `done` Sweep + deps-injection seam over listLiveHosts(), modelled on sweepStalledLoops importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` Calibrate against the LIVE population — must find exactly the known-wedged hosts and reject the rest importance: high\n- **P-004** `done` registerSystemAction + import in register-system-actions.ts (the seeded-but-dead trap) + routine-classification entry importance: high\n- **P-005** `done` Seed the routine on a cadence, offset from the other janitors importance: high — note: seeded ACTIVE; dispatch arming tracked separately as P-007\n- **P-006** `done` Unit tests incl. the ledger-outlives-host scoping trap and a human-typing false-positive control importance: high\n- **P-007** `done` ARM VERIFICATION (open): the routine is seeded ACTIVE but bg-host booted 22:02Z, ~4h before the barrel import landed — so the running process has no handler and fires log 'no handler registered ... skipping' until it restarts. Registration itself is VERIFIED (routine-classification.registry.test.ts fails in both directions and passes). Deliberately did NOT restart bg-host: a green-checkpoint run was 26min in flight and dev:restart flagged the collision — starving it into a FALSE red would hit the whole fleet. Re-check after the next natural bg-host restart: last_fired_at non-null + a [sweep-wedged-pty-hosts] line in the journal, NOT a 'no handler' line. importance: high — note: ← WI-38379 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — A carry delivery is NOT evidence the composer cleared — measured, and it cost 2/3 recall\nDate: 2026-08-13\nThe first draft of `classifyComposerWedge` treated `respawn-carry-delivered` and\n`compact-carry-delivered` as streak-CLEARING events. The reasoning was plausible and wrong:\ncarry text reached the composer, so surely the gate had let it through.\n\nCalibration against the live population falsified it. On su-91ef0643 the ledger runs:\n\n    defer(len=11) … respawned … respawn-carry-delivered … defer(len=11) 4 min later\n\ntwice over, across four hours, always the SAME 11-char phantom. The phantom SURVIVES a carry\ndelivery. Trusting those kinds truncated real wedge streaks and reported 1 wedged host where\n3 were known; removing them (and treating a CHANGED pendingLength as a run boundary rather\nthan a poisoned run) took the detector to 2 currently-wedged with su-91ef0643's streak length\nreproducing the independently hand-measured count of 19 exactly.\n\nDECISION, binding on any future work in this class:\n1. Only an explicit composer-clear event (`owner-composer-wedge-cleared`,\n   `owner-composer-cleared-on-respawn`) or observed human typing\n   (`owner-input-during-compact-wait`) may be treated as clearing a staged line. Do NOT\n   re-add delivery-shaped kinds on the reasoning above — it has been tested and is false.\n2. `respawned` is likewise not a clear: a respawn replaces the AGENT while the host and its\n   composer model persist. This is the same fact that makes the whole class durable.\n3. The asymmetry that governs the set: a kind wrongly listed as clearing makes the guard go\n   BLIND (silent false negative); a kind wrongly omitted at worst lengthens a run whose\n   verdict is already governed by the same-length rule. Keep the set minimal.\n\nPinned by `pty-host-wedge-guard.test.ts` — \"does NOT treat a respawn or its carry delivery as\nclearing the staged line\" — so a future re-addition fails a test rather than quietly halving\nrecall.\n\n### D-002 — Owner ruled: do not touch the two wedged hosts, and do not force-restart bg-host to arm the guard\nDate: 2026-08-13\nAsked and answered in an owner turn on 2026-08-13 ~02:30Z [owner:Avi], both answers the\nconservative option:\n\n1. THE TWO CURRENTLY-WEDGED HOSTS — \"Leave both, just report.\"\n   su-91ef0643 (pid 570734, idle 224m, 19 defers / 888m) and su-f0c6fa5e (pid 807629, still\n   emitting, 21 defers / 259m) are NOT to be relaunched or otherwise touched. The guard\n   reports them; nothing acts on them. Do not read this as a standing licence to relaunch\n   them later either — re-ask if it comes up.\n\n2. ARMING THE GUARD — \"Wait for the natural restart.\"\n   Do NOT pass override_gate_collision to restart bg-host. The routine is seeded ACTIVE and\n   its handler is registered in the tree; it begins dispatching whenever bg-host next\n   restarts on its own (deploy or watchdog). Tracked as P-007.\n\nContext that did NOT change the ruling: minutes after the question, a peer retracted the\npromotion-stall alarm — bb026a02 went green and main advanced 369 commits — so the specific\ngate run I was protecting has cleared. The owner's answer stands regardless; the guard is\nnot urgent enough to spend a shared-infrastructure restart on.\n\nCONSEQUENCE TO STATE HONESTLY IN ANY STATUS REPORT: until that restart happens, a fire of\n`sweep-wedged-pty-hosts` logs \"no handler registered ... skipping\" and detects nothing.\n`active = true` on the routine row is NOT evidence it is working. The re-check is\n`routines.last_fired_at` non-null PLUS a `[sweep-wedged-pty-hosts]` journal line.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"wi-38376-announce-high-water-2026-08-13","title":"WI-38376 — signed announce high-water liveness repair","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: WI-38376 — signed announce high-water liveness repair\nslug: wi-38376-announce-high-water-2026-08-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-10-12\n---\n\n# WI-38376 — signed announce high-water liveness repair\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend SignedAnnounce with optional signed log_length, record the maximum verified advertised high-water for admitted logs, and feed it only into replication liveness and repair confirmation; add announce and boot regressions. importance: high — note: ← WI-38397 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Thread a rig-scoped shorter announce re-flush cadence through initial launch and restart env blocks, with a static regression and shell validation. importance: high — note: ← WI-38398 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `todo` Build the sidecar, run focused/type checks, then rerun the unfiltered 18-scenario 3-frame matrix and resolve WI-38376 from authoritative scenario evidence. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-38404 released\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Reuse signed announce as the writer-progress carrier\nDate: 2026-08-13\nUse the existing SignedAnnounce + WI-1544 periodic re-flush as the heartbeat plane. Add optional backward-compatible signed log_length. Receiver stores max advertised length only after verified/admitted announce processing and computes livenessKnownLength=max(localRemoteLog.length, advertisedLength). Merge cursors, Hypercore reads, and logs[] continue using actual local length, so no read is attempted beyond locally replicated data. The rig sets a shorter PAPERCUSP_ANNOUNCE_REFLUSH_MS only for the test process; production default remains five minutes.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"acceptance-sidestage-code-quality-2026-08-13","title":"SideStage code-quality overhaul — acceptance","status":"active","created":"2026-08-13","owner":"su-c18bab18-b507-4478-8af2-15b084d6641c","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage code-quality overhaul — acceptance\nslug: acceptance-sidestage-code-quality-2026-08-13\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-13\nowner: su-c18bab18-b507-4478-8af2-15b084d6641c\n---\n\n# SideStage code-quality overhaul — acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"acceptance-sidestage-live-selling-copilot-2026-08-13","title":"SideStage live-selling copilot — acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-13","owner":"su-c18bab18-b507-4478-8af2-15b084d6641c","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage live-selling copilot — acceptance\nslug: acceptance-sidestage-live-selling-copilot-2026-08-13\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-14\nowner: su-c18bab18-b507-4478-8af2-15b084d6641c\n---\n\n# SideStage live-selling copilot — acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-android-app-2026-08-13","title":"SideStage Android app — papercup-rust-mobile framework (Rust core + UniFFI + Compose)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage Android app — papercup-rust-mobile framework (Rust core + UniFFI + Compose)\nslug: sidestage-android-app-2026-08-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** D-009 GATE STILL CLOSED, but the blocking deliverable is DONE. The mockup Avi asked for is built, render-verified, and delivered to him for approval (msg mssn2e0h, 07:41Z): /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage/mockups/mobile-buyer-orders.html — a self-contained page showing Buyer + Orders as iPhone 15 Pro and Pixel 8 at true device proportions, drawn from the RUNNING web app's real copy, catalog rows and tokens (ivory #FFF8EF / ink #2A1F1A / vermilion #D62B1F), with 8 keyed platform deltas (D1-D8) and 3 layout decisions flagged to Avi as overrulable (chat-as-sheet vs third tab; Hold inline vs detail sheet; stage inline vs full-bleed). Scope honoured: 2 tabs only per D-007/D-008. Both fleets notified it exists and that the gate remains closed (msg mssn2e1p, 7 live members). DELIVERY CAVEAT: artifact publishing is unavailable to this session (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN takes precedence over a claude.ai login), so it is a local file path rather than a hosted link — flagged to Avi as an owner-gated wall.\n\n**Next:** WAIT on Avi's approval — it is the single condition that opens D-009. On his YES: emit the gate to both fleets and release the ~6 agents parked on screen layout / navigation / visual structure, with the mockup as the SPEC (not a reference). On any of his three flagged decisions coming back changed: revise the mockup first, then open the gate. The event and the claimability floor are SEPARATE mechanisms. `externalBlockersExclusionSql` (packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts:4420) excludes any work-item carrying a blocker with status='active'; `packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/get-next.ts:909` applies it as its own `ok_external_blocker` floor, counting rejections at :1039. That function's own comment is explicit: such items are excluded from opportunistic self-selection \"until the blocker is explicitly cleared\". NOTHING clears a blocker in response to an event firing. Therefore emitting the gate releases the PERMISSION and changes NO item's claimability. The clear is a separate, explicit per-item write (`work_items:set_blocker { clear:true }`, which records clearedBy and preserves history).\n\nSCOPE — CORRECTED.
