Both fail silently; both look fine locally. Whoever takes WI-38850 should ask whether routine registration is per-tree by construction and fix the CLASS, not this one repo.\n\n### D-016 — RETIRES the D-015 manual-push obligation: sidestage-mobile is now under real git-sync coverage\nDate: 2026-08-14\nSUPERSEDES the interim rule in D-015. Stop hand-pushing in sidestage-mobile.\n\nVERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (su-e1a3a9 @15:44Z) — I did NOT retire this on the closing agent's word: `routines:list { q:'sidestage-mobile' }` returns a git-sync routine for installSlug `sidestage-mobile`, active:true, cron `0 7,17,27,37,47,57 * * * *`, nextFireAt 2026-08-14T15:47:00Z. The repo now has its own 10-minute sync, exactly like every other covered tree.\n\nWHAT CHANGES: the standard platform rule APPLIES AGAIN in sidestage-mobile — leave verified work in the tree; git-sync owns commit AND push; you do neither. D-015's 'commit AND push before ending a turn' was a TEMPORARY MITIGATION for the window in which no routine existed. That window is closed. Do not keep hand-pushing: it now races the routine for no benefit.\n\nWHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: D-015's factual record stands (the ~21h near-loss, the bc689ab..d57da9b rescue push, and why the mitigation was correct at the time). And the RECURRENCE GUARD is still outstanding — WI-38850 (the routine) is done, but WI-38857 is open for the detector: nothing yet reports a repo being actively worked with NO sync coverage, which is the actual reason this went unnoticed for 21 hours. Coverage today does not mean the class is fixed.\n\nSTILL LIVE from the same sweep: EI-20443492691207801 — `~/papercupai-workspace/sidestage` is a VESTIGIAL `main` checkout, 69 commits stale, shadowing the real hive tree at `~/.papercusp/hives/sidestage` (branch `staging`). Editing the workspace path strands work the same way. Use the hive tree.\n\n### D-017 — A live claim is not widened around: blocked lanes park on the done-event, and claim caps are checked before blaming the filter\nDate: 2026-08-14\nRULING 2026-08-14T19:57Z, leader su-e1a3a985, on su-08298 request to widen fleet-launch-sidestage-android-plan so it could claim EI-20456110970277624 (:3100 bind-race blocking WI-38620).\n\nDECLINED. The item is assigned to su-b571258d, verified live (active 9s before the ruling) with a declared intent naming that exact item and a 3-minute-old checkpoint. Admission was working correctly; widening it would have placed two agents on one bind-race fix.\n\nTWO GENERAL POINTS, both of which cost real turns here:\n\n1. A spec widen would NOT have unblocked the requester regardless. The spec sets limits.maxConcurrentClaims=1 and the requester already held WI-38620, so the claim would have been refused on the CAP, not the filter. Before asking for (or granting) a widen, check the cap — otherwise a granted widen still fails and both parties misread the filter as the cause.\n\n2. The spec CAN already admit issue-family rows. Its filter is an `any` of {plan = sidestage-android-app-2026-08-13} OR an explicit id-pin list which already contains two EI- rows. Issue-family admission is by id pin, not structurally blocked. Do not re-derive this.\n\nSTANDING PATTERN for a lane blocked on another agent's in-flight item: events:await { event: \"work-item:done:<id>\" } and end the turn. The key is machine-derived and needs no declaration from leader or holder. Reassignment is available if the holder goes non-live or stops progressing — that is decided on evidence of stall, never on elapsed time.\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-checkout-shipping-2026-08-13","title":"SideStage checkout + shipping calculator — port from Restart shop-api [owner:Avi 2026-08-13 \"take the checkout and shipping calculator we had on our restart site and integrate it into our sidestage site\"]","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage checkout + shipping calculator — port from Restart shop-api [owner:Avi 2026-08-13 \"take the checkout and shipping calculator we had on our restart site and integrate it into our sidestage site\"]\nslug: sidestage-checkout-shipping-2026-08-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-14\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nIntegrate the Restart site's checkout + shipping calculator into SideStage. This WAS in the original spec (PRD §Checkout: \"Square sandbox sessions over the cart; orders persist with status; shipping via the box-packing estimator\") and the API side is partially built: apps/api/src/checkout/ (controller/module/service) and apps/api/src/shipping/ (box-packer + controller) exist. The delta vs Restart (/home/marsh-office/Restart/apps/shop-api/src/{shipping,checkout}): Restart's shipping.service.ts (459 lines, real rate calculation beyond box-packing) has no SideStage counterpart, and the SideStage web app has NO buyer-facing checkout UI (grep hits only copilot/auction panels).\n\n## Approach\n\nReuse-first: port Restart code where its dependencies allow, adapting to SideStage's module layout (NestJS-style modules in apps/api/src). Buyer-facing checkout UI goes in apps/web following existing tab/panel patterns. Tests ship with each port (vitest, renderToStaticMarkup pattern for web).\n\n## Now\n\nPlan created; survey item is the root — establishes the exact port set before the port items execute.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Port checkout + shipping from Restart\n\n- **P-111** `done` Survey the exact port delta: diff Restart shop-api shipping/checkout (shipping.service.ts rate calculation, checkout providers, webhook flow) against SideStage's existing apps/api/src/checkout + shipping modules AND the web app's buyer flow; record the port set and any Restart dependencies needing substitution as plan Decisions BEFORE implementation items run. importance: high — note: ← WI-38634 completed (done)\n- **P-112** `done` Port the shipping calculator: bring Restart's shipping.service rate-calculation capability into apps/api/src/shipping alongside the existing box-packer, expose calculator endpoints via shipping.controller, with vitest coverage ported/adapted from Restart's shipping tests. importance: high blocked-by: P-111 — note: ← WI-38635 completed (done)\n- **P-113** `done` Buyer-facing checkout UI with shipping calculator in apps/web: cart review, address entry, live shipping-rate calculation, Square sandbox checkout session against the existing checkout API; follow the app's existing panel/tab patterns; component tests via renderToStaticMarkup like the rest of the suite. importance: high blocked-by: P-112 — note: ← WI-38636 completed (done)\n- **P-114** `done` Integration verify + prod deploy: end-to-end cart→rates→checkout-session locally with npm run check green, deploy via deploy/deploy.sh serialized with the P-110 Typesense rollout on the shared prod host (D-003), live-verify on sidestage.buyrestart.com. blocked-by: P-113 — note: ← WI-38637 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. **Reuse the proven Restart behavior without creating a second checkout or rate-calculation system.** Port the behavior of Restart's apps/shop-api/src/{shipping,checkout} into SideStage's existing apps/api/src/shipping and apps/api/src/checkout modules, preserving the current SideStage box packer and API/module conventions. Do not import the unrelated Restart Stripe, queue, Odoo, Signifyd, Arcjet, @papercusp/db, or @papercusp/shop-sdk graph. (D-001, D-006; P-111, P-112)\n2. **Produce server-calculated shipping quotes from SideStage-native cart and catalog data.** Load the current cart through CartService/CartStore; expose optional catalog weight and dimensions through the existing catalog source; pack only valid physical items with the existing box packer; call EasyPost through a native-fetch adapter; and retain Restart's unit conversions/fallbacks, five-minute cart+address quote cache, per-parcel cheapest carrier/service deduplication, all-parcel service intersection, summed price, maximum transit time, and useful-rate selection. (D-006; P-112)\n3. **Keep shipping price server-authoritative.** The browser may submit only cartId, normalized guest/address data, and a selected shippingRateId. Checkout must resolve that ID against a fresh or still-valid quote for the same current cart contents and normalized address, derive shippingCents server-side, and reject missing, expired, mismatched, or unavailable selections. A cart or address change invalidates the prior selection. (D-007; P-112, P-113)\n4. **Persist an auditable order and fulfillment snapshot.** The checkout order must persist status, normalized shipping address, the selected quote snapshot (id, carrier, service, total cents, delivery days, parcel count, quoted time), and Square correlation identifiers so payment, fulfillment, webhook replay, and later audit all refer to the same server-approved amount. (PRD §Checkout; D-007, D-008; P-112, P-114)\n5. **Deliver the buyer-owned checkout flow in the existing buyer composition.** After a successful inventory hold, retain a durable browser cart ID, add the held variant through the existing cart endpoint, and present cart review → guest/address entry → live shipping-rate selection → Square sandbox payment. Reuse one typed web API adapter and resolveApiBaseUrl; mount the provider/drawer through the minimal approved App.tsx buyer-branch seam, notify it from BuyerProductRail, and leave the protected BuyerTab.tsx and buyer-identity.ts files untouched. (D-009, D-011; P-113)\n6. **Keep Square sandbox payment idempotent across synchronous confirmation and webhooks.** Use the existing native-fetch SquareSandboxProvider and verifySquareWebhookSignature(notificationUrl + rawBody) helper. Route confirm and raw-body webhook events through one transition: first success marks the order paid and cart ordered, redelivery is a no-op, and failure marks the order failed while leaving the cart open for retry. Do not add a live provider or expose server secrets to the browser. (D-002, D-008; P-113, P-114)\n7. **Make runtime dependencies and secrets explicit in the production image contract.** Any workspace library imported by apps/api must be declared in its package.json. Document and pass the EasyPost, warehouse-origin, Square app/location/access-token, webhook signature, and exact webhook notification URL variables through the server deployment path; real values remain only in host .env.production, while the browser receives only the sandbox app/location identifiers returned by checkout. (D-004, D-010; P-112, P-114)\n8. **Verify the complete journey before serialized production rollout.** P-111 records the exact port delta and substitutions before implementation; P-112 and P-113 ship focused API/web tests; P-114 proves cart → rates → server-validated checkout session → confirm/webhook → persisted order/cart state with npm run check green, then deploys through deploy/deploy.sh while holding the D-003 SideStage deploy path lock and live-verifies sidestage.buyrestart.com. (D-003; P-111–P-114)\n\n## Design\n\n### 1. Port survey and boundaries (P-111)\n\nTreat the Restart implementation as the behavioral reference and SideStage as the ownership boundary. The survey maps each reusable algorithm/DTO to an existing SideStage module, identifies every dependency that must be substituted, and records binding substitutions as Decisions before downstream work. The design deliberately extends the existing shipping, checkout, cart, catalog, and buyer-composition surfaces instead of introducing parallel services.\n\n### 2. Shipping quote plane (P-112)\n\nShippingService lives beside the existing box-packer in apps/api/src/shipping. It reads the current cart via CartService/CartStore, resolves optional product weight/dimensions through the existing catalog source, validates/normalizes the destination, packs parcels with the sole SideStage packer, and calls EasyPost through a server-only native-fetch adapter. The quote cache key binds normalized address plus current cart contents for five minutes. Aggregation deduplicates carrier/service choices per parcel, keeps only services available for every parcel, sums cents, takes the slowest parcel's transit days, and returns stable quote IDs for selection.\n\n### 3. Checkout authority and persistence (P-112, P-113)\n\nThe web adapter requests rates, but the API owns price. POST /checkout/sessions accepts the cart, normalized guest/address payload, and selected quote ID; it re-resolves the quote under the same cart/address key and rejects stale or mismatched selection before deriving the payable shipping amount. The order record/checkpoint JSONB stores the normalized address and immutable selected-rate snapshot alongside order status and Square correlation IDs. This makes the later payment transition and fulfillment audit independent of mutable browser state.\n\n### 4. Payment transition (P-113, P-114)\n\nThe existing SquareSandboxProvider creates sandbox sessions and confirms status. A raw-body checkout webhook verifies the exact configured notification URL and Square signature, normalizes completed/failed events, and joins synchronous confirm at one idempotent transition. The transition is monotonic: the first completed result pays the order and orders the cart; repeats do nothing; failure records a failed order without consuming the cart.\n\n### 5. Buyer composition (P-113)\n\nOne typed apps/web adapter owns cart, rate, checkout-session, and confirmation DTOs and uses resolveApiBaseUrl. The buyer branch in App.tsx receives the approved checkout provider and drawer; BuyerProductRail publishes successful holds into that provider. The drawer owns cart review, address capture, live quote selection, and Square sandbox payment state. This satisfies buyer ownership while respecting the protected BuyerTab.tsx/buyer-identity.ts boundary and avoiding a seller-dock or rail-internal checkout fork.\n\n### 6. Runtime configuration, verification, and rollout (P-112, P-114)\n\nEasyPost and warehouse-origin values stay in the API; Square server credentials and webhook secrets stay server-only; the client receives only identifiers needed by the sandbox payment UI. Workspace imports are declared so the pruned production image boots, not merely typechecks. Focused shipping, checkout, webhook/idempotency, and render/component tests cover each seam. P-114 then runs the repository check and the local end-to-end path, acquires the D-003 lock on deploy/deploy.sh, deploys the tracked manifest to the shared SideStage host, verifies configured quotes/payment/webhook/persistence live, and releases the lock.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Reuse-first port from Restart, no redesign\nDate: 2026-08-13\nCopy the Restart shop-api implementations (/home/marsh-office/Restart/apps/shop-api/src/{shipping,checkout}) and adapt imports/module wiring to SideStage's apps/api/src layout — do NOT redesign the algorithms or API shapes. Where a Restart dependency has no SideStage counterpart (carrier credentials, external rate APIs), substitute the closest SideStage-native seam and record the substitution as a follow-up Decision on this plan.\n\n### D-002 — Payments stay Square sandbox\nDate: 2026-08-13\nPer the SideStage PRD (§Checkout: \"Square sandbox sessions over the cart\"), this plan keeps payments on the Square SANDBOX. No live payment provider, no provider swap — parity with the spec, not a payments upgrade.\n\n### D-003 — Prod deploys serialize with the P-110 rollout\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDate: 2026-08-13\ndeploy/deploy.sh rsyncs the tracked manifest and re-ups the whole stack on the shared prod host (178.156.254.59:/opt/SideStage). Any deploy touching that host SERIALIZES VIA LOCK, not via a person: locks:acquire { paths: ['deploy/deploy.sh'], coordination_domain: '/home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage', ttl_sec: <sized to the deploy>, reason: '<WI + plan item> prod deploy 178.156.254.59' } BEFORE running deploy/deploy.sh; release after post-deploy verify. Blocked = another deploy is in flight: wait for the lock, never interleave. Escalation/authority: @fleet-leader:sidestage-gpt (role selector, never a session id).\nAMENDED 2026-08-14T07:58Z by su-c18bab18 (D-003's author): removed the named-session coordination point (WI-38584 done; a named session strands requesters when it ends). First grant under the amended protocol: WI-38637/P-114 (3b39b), msg mssnnina.\nRE-AMENDED 2026-08-14T08:05Z by su-c18bab18: the 07:58Z text prescribed locks:acquire_resource { resource: 'sidestage-prod-deploy:178.156.254.59' } — that resource is UNREGISTERED and unacquirable: locks:acquire_resource returns unknown_resource (registry dump: 61 rows, zero sidestage/prod-deploy entries) and NO runtime registration verb exists (lock family = acquire/release/heartbeat/list; the resource registry is code-side). Evidence: 3b39b's mssnttzm, discovered executing the first granted window. A deployer following the 07:58Z text either stalls on an unacquirable serializer or concludes the gate is broken and deploys UNSERIALIZED — strictly worse than the handshake it replaced. Replaced with the enforced path-lock form above (first used by 3b39b for WI-38637: lock_id 34a5b7ef, expires 08:32:24Z). Caveat on record: the path lock mutexes the SCRIPT PATH by convention, not the host itself — the same convention-dependence a named resource would have, minus the registration problem. Optional future hardening: register 'sidestage-prod-deploy:178.156.254.59' in the code-side lock resource registry and switch this decision back to the resource-lock form; tracked via improvements filing (see plan thread).\n\n### D-004 — Declare every @papercusp/* workspace lib used by apps/api in its package.json dependencies\nDate: 2026-08-13\nIncident 2026-08-13 21:45Z: prod api crash-looped with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for @papercusp/typesense — catalog.sources.ts imported it but apps/api/package.json never declared it, and the api Dockerfile's `npm prune --omit=dev` strands undeclared workspace libs AFTER tsc has already passed (workspace hoisting makes the build green while the runtime image is broken). Fixed by declaring \"@papercusp/typesense\": \"*\". BINDING for this plan: any Restart port that introduces a @papercusp/* or other workspace import into apps/api MUST add the matching dependencies entry in apps/api/package.json in the same change — tsc/vitest green does NOT prove the prod image boots.\n\n### D-005 — All SideStage app paths resolve against the hive root /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEvery relative app path in this plan's items resolves against the ratified SideStage checkout /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage (branch staging) — NOT the Papercusp staging tree. Verified 2026-08-14T00:12Z (apps/web/src/styles.css present at the hive root). Same ruling recorded on sidestage-standout-features-2026-08-13; incidents: EI-20384455355405385, EI-20340452128976093, EI-20342035550304021.\n\n### D-006 — Port Restart shipping behavior through SideStage-native cart and catalog seams\nDate: 2026-08-14\nP-112 MUST retain apps/api/src/shipping/box-packer.ts as the one packer, including SideStage's positive-input and physical-dimension checks, and add the missing ShippingService plus a native-fetch EasyPost adapter around it. Load carts through CartService/CartStore, and extend the existing CATALOG_SOURCE/CatalogSource.variant read model to expose optional product_catalog.weight and dimensions already present in db/schema.sql; use Restart's unit conversions and fallbacks when those fields are absent. Port the 5-minute cart+address cache, per-parcel cheapest carrier:service deduplication, all-parcel intersection, summed cents/max transit days, and useful-rate selection. Do not import Restart's @papercusp/db, @papercusp/shop-sdk, Arcjet, Stripe, queue, Odoo, or Signifyd graph; native validation plus quote caching are the substitutions available in SideStage.\nRelated: P-112\n\n### D-007 — Shipping price is server-authoritative and the selected quote is persisted on the order\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe Restart browser DTO (address -> POST /shipping/rates -> carrier:service selection) is the compatibility contract, but its client-supplied shippingCents is not an authority. POST /checkout/sessions MUST accept cartId, normalized guest identity/address, and shippingRateId; the server resolves that ID against a fresh or still-valid 5-minute quote for the same current cart contents and normalized address, derives shippingCents itself, and rejects missing, expired, mismatched, or unavailable rates. Persist the normalized address plus a selected-rate snapshot (id, carrier, service, totalCents, deliveryDays, parcelCount, quotedAt) in CheckoutOrder/checkpoint_order JSONB so payment amount, fulfillment, and later audit use the same quote. A changed cart or address invalidates the prior selection.\nRelated: P-112, P-113, P-114\n\n### D-008 — Square confirm and webhook share one idempotent order/cart transition\nDate: 2026-08-14\nKeep the existing SquareSandboxProvider native-fetch adapter and SideStage's verifySquareWebhookSignature(notificationUrl + rawBody) helper; do not port Stripe or Restart's Square SDK/raw-body-only signature implementation. Add raw-body POST /checkout/webhook handling that verifies Square's signature, normalizes completed/failed events, and routes both synchronous confirm and webhook delivery through one idempotent payment-result transition. First success marks the order paid and its cart ordered; redelivery is a no-op. Failure marks the order failed and leaves the cart open for retry. Persist Square transaction IDs needed for correlation. Do not invent absent queue, Odoo, or Signifyd side effects; those are outside this plan.\nRelated: P-113, P-114\n\n### D-009 — Buyer checkout belongs in BuyerTab and reuses a typed web API adapter\nDate: 2026-08-14\nP-113 implements the buyer flow in apps/web's BuyerTab composition, not the seller-dock CopilotPanel and not by rewriting BuyerProductRail internals. After a successful inventory hold, BuyerTab keeps a durable browser cart id, adds the held variant through the existing cart endpoint, and exposes cart review -> guest/address entry -> live rate selection -> Square sandbox payment in a buyer-owned drawer/panel following current SideStage component patterns. Centralize the cart/rates/checkout/confirm DTOs and fetch calls in one typed apps/web adapter using resolveApiBaseUrl; do not copy Restart's Stripe Elements, Stripe labels, Astro SDK shell, or styling. Port the interaction contract and Square payment step only.\nRelated: P-113\n\n### D-010 — Shipping and Square secrets remain server-only and are explicit in the deploy contract\nDate: 2026-08-14\nP-112/P-114 must document placeholders in .env.example and pass server variables through docker-compose.prod.yml for EASYPOST_API_KEY; WAREHOUSE_FROM_NAME, WAREHOUSE_FROM_STREET1, WAREHOUSE_FROM_CITY, WAREHOUSE_FROM_STATE, WAREHOUSE_FROM_ZIP, WAREHOUSE_FROM_COUNTRY; SQUARE_APP_ID, SQUARE_LOCATION_ID, SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY, and the exact SQUARE_WEBHOOK_NOTIFICATION_URL used by signature verification. Real values live only in the host's .env.production. No EasyPost or Square secret may be a Vite build arg or browser variable; the browser receives only Square app/location identifiers in the checkout session. Development may degrade to empty rates / needs-configuration, but P-114 live verification requires configured quotes, payment session, confirm, webhook, and persisted order/cart state.\nRelated: P-112, P-114\n\n### D-011 — Buyer checkout composes via an App.tsx provider seam — protected files stay untouched; D-009 is satisfied semantically\nDate: 2026-08-14\nRULING (leader, on 2d83f's WI-38636 request msg mssjkrq9): The buyer checkout integrates WITHOUT editing the protected files (BuyerTab.tsx, buyer-identity.ts). Approved seam: (1) typed adapter + checkout drawer/provider + tests live in NEW/disjoint files; (2) integration = wrap the buyer branch in App.tsx with the provider and mount the drawer there — the App.tsx edit stays MINIMAL (provider wrap + drawer mount only, no buyer-identity logic); (3) BuyerProductRail notifies the provider after a successful hold. This SATISFIES D-009's 'checkout belongs in BuyerTab composition' semantically — checkout is composed into the buyer branch, buyer-owned, outside the rail UI. The BuyerTab.tsx/buyer-identity.ts protection is treated as a HARD boundary for this item (ratifying 2d83f's default). If that protection is later lifted, folding the provider mount from App.tsx into BuyerTab.tsx is an OPTIONAL follow-up refactor — the App.tsx seam is acceptable as FINAL and must not block shipping."},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-code-quality-2026-08-13","title":"SideStage code-quality overhaul — wire the real seams the contest build faked","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage code-quality overhaul — wire the real seams the contest build faked\nslug: sidestage-code-quality-2026-08-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-13\nupdated: 2026-08-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ALL 7 ITEMS DONE (executed solo by the leader under owner-approved AUTO, D-001): P-101 durable PG data layer (+ latent tsx/Nest DI fix — explicit @Inject everywhere), P-102 one product source (real 1.1M Restart catalog imported via new scripts/load-restart-catalog.sh; 4 demo arrays deleted), P-103 real buyer holds + shared chat, P-104 monolith split + shared hooks, P-105 durable config→guardrail policy wiring, P-106 live preflight probes, P-107 density tokens per the approved mockups. npm run check green throughout (58 api + 48 web). Acceptance rubric acceptance-sidestage-code-quality-2026-08-13 active (6 criteria); independent grade requested from su-bb376 alongside the contest rubric.\n\n**Next:** bb376 emits both scorecards after their WI-38508 → leader verifies the emits → plans:set-plan-status shipped. Residue: event-manager/event-creation CSS internals to the shared density tokens (cosmetic follow-up).\n\n## Requirements\n\n- SideStage state is durable by default: auction inventory, reservations, carts, checkout orders, event configuration, and seller policy revisions survive API restarts in Postgres, while injectable in-memory implementations remain available for isolated tests and explicit offline development.\n- Product data has one authoritative read model. The web app, event setup, buyer experience, and copilot grounding consume the API catalog sourced from the real Restart export; Typesense provides Restart-parity search and facets, Postgres text search is the degraded fallback, and no production export is committed to the public repository.\n- Buyer and seller surfaces operate on the same live commerce primitives: inventory holds change real availability, chat is shared and API-backed, checkout/auction outcomes drive event statistics, and no demo arrays, fabricated stats, placeholder queues, or local fake commerce remain.\n- Seller configuration is an enforceable domain contract, not scenery: immutable draft-to-published policy revisions, validation, audit/outbox records, automation bounds, and event/seller fallback resolution drive the guarded-action policy used at execution time.\n- All four listing actions required by the product specification—push, swap, markdown, and stock adjustment—execute through the guarded-action service with validation, auditability, and rollback semantics.\n- Client reads and writes use the in-tree @papercusp sync layer and its zero-cache/invalidation path; successful mutations invalidate affected queries, replacing hand-rolled fetch/useState/polling loops rather than creating a second client-state system.\n- Every data-grid experience uses the shared papergrid/RichGrid family. Seller event setup, seller management, and buyer/catalog surfaces match the approved mockups and share explicit compact, roomy, and console density tokens.\n- The web application preserves clear component and domain seams: tab screens are split from App.tsx, repeated stream/copy/session behavior is shared, and the API retains focused NestJS modules with repository/service interfaces rather than a new parallel backend.\n- The Test tab reports live readiness from health, media, catalog, policy, and browser-capability probes; it never displays hardcoded readiness literals.\n- PRD.md and TDD.md describe the shipped product and architecture and are linked from reviewer entry points. The root validation suite remains green, the app uses one compatible React runtime, and regression tests cover every newly introduced load-bearing seam.\n\n## Design\n\nThe implementation extends the existing NestJS modules and service contracts instead of replacing them. Thin Postgres repositories sit behind the auction, inventory, cart, order, event-config, policy, catalog, chat, and stats services; the existing in-memory implementations are retained as deterministic fakes selected explicitly through dependency injection. This keeps production state durable without making unit tests depend on infrastructure.\n\nCatalog access is one source seam with three operational layers: the committed seed is a small reproducible fixture, the real Restart export is loaded locally through the repository script, and the API serves a shared catalog read model. Typesense is the primary search engine for typo tolerance and facets; Postgres text search remains the availability fallback. The maintained @papercusp/typesense dist exports stay canonical, with consumer pretest builds covering clean-clone availability rather than repointing package entrypoints at source.\n\nCommerce behavior converges on shared server primitives. Reservations own available quantity, carts and checkout orders own purchase state, shared chat/presence feeds both sides of the event, and paid orders/auction winners are the writer-backed source for event statistics. The guarded-action service is the single execution chokepoint for push, swap, markdown, and stock adjustment. Published seller policies resolve by event then seller scope, lower automation when bounds or confidence require it, and emit audit/outbox records with idempotency protection.\n\nOn the client, the existing @papercusp sync query registry and invalidation channel own server-state reads. Domain hooks register typed queries and route mutations through the common invalidation path; they do not introduce a parallel cache. App.tsx remains a small shell around extracted tab components and shared lifecycle hooks. Data grids compose the papergrid/RichGrid library, while one CSS token block supplies compact Config/Test, roomy Buyer, and console Seller density profiles.\n\nThe settled trade-off is production correctness with explicit degradation, not silent demo behavior: Postgres/Typesense are preferred, memory and Postgres-search fallbacks are named and observable, and honest empty values replace invented data. Verification is layered at the owning seams—module/service unit tests, API and web suites, live restart/persistence and endpoint smokes, clean-clone package checks, and the repository-wide check command—so failures are caught where their contracts are written.\n\n## Background\n\nAudit verdict (leader, 2026-08-13): the luna fleet built SideStage with genuinely good SMALL-scale composition — clean NestJS domain modules (9 modules, each controller/service/types/tests, 86–352 lines), framework-free web logic modules with colocated tests (105 tests green), a separated copilot pipeline (guardrail/research/latency). But the LOAD-BEARING abstractions are missing:\n\n1. **The data layer is a façade.** Zero `pg` imports in the API; every service holds state in Maps (auction, cart, chat, checkout). The carefully-ported Postgres schema (reservation functions, option axes, triggers — db/schema.sql) and the compose containers (postgres, typesense, redis, mediamtx) are never touched by the app. All state dies on restart. The auction service comments the seam it never built.\n2. **Three disconnected demo catalogs.** DEMO_PRODUCTS (App.tsx), DEMO_CATALOG (event-creation/catalog.ts), DEMO_BUYER_PRODUCTS (buyer.ts), plus TRANSCRIPT_PRODUCTS aliases — four hand-maintained copies of \"the products\"; none read the API or DB.\n3. **Buyer commerce is faked where the API is real.** BuyerTab chat is local useState (the seller side uses the real API-backed EventChat — two chat implementations); \"Hold item\" fabricates a chat message instead of calling the reservation/cart APIs that exist server-side.\n4. **App.tsx monolith (552 lines).** SellerTab, ConfigTab, and TestTab (incl. ~150 lines of judge-report JSX) live inline; only BuyerTab was extracted.\n5. **Config tab is scenery.** Uncontrolled inputs, Save wired to nothing, guardrail toggles never persist nor reach the API's guardrail module — the two guardrail surfaces are unconnected.\n6. **Test-tab preflight is hardcoded.** The four status rows are literals, not probes.\n7. **Duplicated plumbing.** SellerTab and BuyerTab each hand-roll identical streamState/copyState/session lifecycle; no shared hooks.\n8. **Shared libs underused.** libs/ ships ui-primitives, sync, sse, token-kit; only 3 files import @papercusp/*. 4 disjoint CSS files (1,210 lines), no explicit token system.\n\nOrder rationale: P-101..P-103 are the substance (state that survives restart + one product truth + real buyer commerce); This is why adoption is not yet visible in the app.\n\n### D-005 — @papercusp/typesense keeps its dist/ exports — the clean-clone gap is closed by apps/api's pretest build, NOT by repointing main at src/\nDate: 2026-08-14\nRULING (settles a cross-lane conflict that already caused one revert war on 2026-08-14 between 04:59Z and 05:15Z).\n\n#### The state that is correct\nlibs/typesense/package.json keeps `main` + all four `exports` conditions pointing at `dist/index.js` (commit aa4748b), AND apps/api/package.json keeps `\"pretest\": \"npm run build --workspace @papercusp/typesense\"` (commit ab2059e).\n\nThese two are a PAIR. Either one alone is broken:\n- dist pointer WITHOUT pretest -> `dist/` is gitignored and untracked, so it is absent in a clean clone; @papercusp/typesense is unresolvable and the apps/api leg dies at COLLECTION (vite resolveId failure in scout.service), not at assertion. That is why gate_health.failingTests was empty and no test name was ever attributable.\n- src/ pointer (with or without pretest) -> the compiled production API image fails at require.resolve on src exports (measured by su-f8686c9a at 05:06Z).\n\nnpm runs `pretest` automatically before `test`, so the clean clone builds dist before the API suite. Both paths are satisfied. No conditional exports, publishConfig, or custom resolve conditions are needed.\n\n#### Falsifier\nIf someone changes typesense's entry, the check is NOT \"does it resolve locally\" — a local tree has stale dist/ artifacts and mostly-uninitialized submodules, so local green proves nothing for this defect class. The check is: a FRESH clean clone + npm ci + the apps/api suite (which fires pretest), AND the compiled production API image resolving the package at runtime. Both, or the change is unverified.\n\n#### Do not re-open on stale reasoning\nThe dist pointer LOOKS wrong in isolation (a gitignored target) and it is a standing temptation for any agent who greps it without also reading apps/api's pretest hook. It was reverted to src/ once already (44b0fa0d, by su-598a0b42) on a clean-clone measurement taken at 04:30-04:36Z — i.e. BEFORE the pretest hook existed at 05:02:41Z. That revert was a regression and was restored by a3ed464.\n\nThe general lesson, which is the durable half of this decision: on this tree a verification carries a shelf life of MINUTES, and \"I verified it\" is meaningless without \"against which sha\". Re-read the current state immediately before acting on any measurement older than the last sweep. Before repointing this entry, read this decision and re-measure both paths.\n\n#### Outcome\nThe sidestage green-checkpoint went GREEN at 2026-08-14T05:15:56Z (consecutiveReds 0) on quiet-cut candidate 4351e0d, verified by ancestry + content to contain aa4748b + ab2059e + ad4ddd6 (the EventLineupGrid.tsx:153 TS2322 typecheck fix). [owner:Avi 2026-08-13] importance: high — note: ← WI-38648 completed (done)\n- **P-114** `done` Quantity on auctions + offers: seller creation flows for auctions AND offers get a quantity input (not just price); schema + API + downstream cart/checkout respect quantity. [owner:Avi 2026-08-13] importance: high — note: ← WI-38649 completed (done)\n- **P-115** `done` Build-history tab on the SideStage site: mimic the papercusp releases page - list all plans and their associated completed work items, grouped per plan with completion evidence/status. [owner:Avi 2026-08-13] importance: high — note: ← WI-38654 completed (done)\n- **P-116** `done` Orders tab — buyer-facing \"My Orders\" page listing the current user's orders across lives/auctions/offers with status; each order row carries its video snapshot(s) per D-014 [owner:Avi 2026-08-13 \"Add an orders tab for users to see their orders\"] importance: high — note: ← WI-38655 completed (done)\n- **P-117** `done` Demo impersonation in the buyer tab — free-text user-id entry: enter ANY id, no auth; the app then behaves as logged-in-as-that-user and the Orders tab shows that user's orders. Demo-only, per D-013 [owner:Avi 2026-08-13 \"a way in the buyer tab to impersonate the user… enter in any id, no auth\"] importance: high — note: ← WI-38656 completed (done)\n- **P-118** `done` Buyer tab EVENT SELECTOR [owner:Avi 2026-08-13 verbatim: \"inside the buyer tab there should be even selector that shows all events created by all events\" — read: all events created by all sellers]: a selector inside the buyer tab that lists ALL events across ALL sellers and switches the active event. Requires a list-events API surface (id, title, seller, live/upcoming/ended status, viewer count) — BuyerTab.tsx today hard-pins DEFAULT_EVENT_ID with no browse path. UI direction gated on Avi's pick from the mockup-options artifact (same pattern as retheme D-001); the list-events API leg is NOT gated and can start now. importance: high — note: ← WI-38668 completed (done)\n- **P-119** `done` Seller tab DEMO IMPERSONATION [owner:Avi 2026-08-13 verbatim: \"the same way the buyer tab needs a way to enter in a user name to auth as that use identity without auth, so does the seller tab\"]: mirror P-117's free-text user-id entry (enter ANY id, no auth) on the SELLER tab — the app then acts as that seller identity (their events, catalog, seller console state). Build as a SHARED impersonation mechanism with P-117 (one component/util, two mount points), never two forks. importance: high — note: ← WI-38669 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n- R1 Seller engagement meter: live, always-visible GREEN/ORANGE/RED verdict in the seller console, computed by an algorithm over MULTIPLE activity metrics (chat rate, unique chatters, viewer trend, reactions, cart adds, bids) - never one raw metric. [owner:Avi 2026-08-13]\n- R2 Buyer engagement variant: same feed, positive-only framing (D-003).\n- R3 Mockups: Avi reviews a few options for both variants (D-008: implementation does not wait on the pick).\n- R4 Voice staging (#1): product mention on stream -> stageable proposal w/ price overlay; one-word/one-tap confirm.\n- R5 Replay chapters (#2): staged-product timestamps -> scrubable chapters + post-event shoppable VOD; listings carry demo clips.\n- R6 Condition evidence (#5): tag/serial/flaw moments pin to orders as provenance.\n- R7 Shipping meter (#3): cart shows live combined-shipping via the ported rate calculator (D-005).\n- R8 Grounded chat answers (#4): buyer questions answered from the seller transcript with citation; unanswered -> seller queue.\n- R9 Lightning deals (#6): engagement-velocity dip -> PROPOSED 60s flash discount; seller tap-to-accept; never auto-fires.\n- R10 Seller pricing history: active-product sold/rejected counts per price, offer accept/reject outcomes, auction outcomes. [owner:Avi 2026-08-13]\n- R11 Quantity on auctions + offers, not just price. [owner:Avi 2026-08-13]\n- R12 Build-history tab: all plans + their completed work items, papercusp-releases-page style. [owner:Avi 2026-08-13]\n\n## Design\n\n- Engagement core (P-001): api-side scorer over existing event activity streams; EWMA smoothing + per-event baseline normalization; thresholds -> G/O/R; published on the existing event SSE channel; config-tunable weights; no new infra.\n- Meter UIs (P-003/P-004): config-switchable variants so the mockup pick re-skins without rework.\n- Voice staging (P-005): rides transcription -> catalog-variant matcher; adds proposal surface + confirm affordance.\n- Replay chapters (P-006) + condition evidence (P-007): one clip index from staging timestamps; VOD player chapter rail; P-007 pins clips to orders.\n- Shipping meter (P-008): consumes the checkout plan rate-calc service (D-005); cart-panel UI.\n- Grounded answers (P-009): message triage + transcript store; answers cite stream timestamps.\n- Lightning deals (P-010): subscribes to P-001 feed (D-004); proposal-only UX.\n- Pricing history (P-011): SQL aggregates over orders/offers/auctions keyed by product+price; seller console product panel.\n- Quantity (P-012): schema + creation forms + cart/checkout plumbing.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Scope: slate #1-#6 + engagement meter; #7 excluded\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13 \"These all look great. Fold 1-6 into the plan\"] Slate items #1-#6 from the 21:52Z feature slate are folded in as P-005..P-010; #7 rehearsal green-room was NOT picked and is excluded.\n\n### D-002 — Engagement meter shape (owner verbatim)\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13 verbatim] \"Lets also add an engagement meter so that the seller can easily see how engaged their audience is. Lets make it a very simple green, orange, red, lets make it an algorithm based on various activity metrics. 2. Lets do this for the buyer view too but something. Show me a mockup of a few different options for both the seller version and the buyer version.\" Seller: plain green/orange/red. Buyer: its own variant. Algorithm over MULTIPLE activity metrics, never a single raw metric.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-003 — Buyer variant never shows deadness\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[self-imposed, pending owner mockup pick] The buyer-facing indicator must not signal a dying stream (red = conversion killer). Positive/neutral framing only - e.g. hot/warming states, red suppressed or reframed. Final look is whatever Avi picks from the P-002 mockups.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-004 — Lightning-deal copilot rides the engagement feed\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13 \"You can make the Lightning-deal copilot ride off this too\"] P-010 consumes P-001 score/velocity - no separate metrics pipeline.\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-005 — Cross-plan dep: shipping meter consumes the checkout port\nDate: 2026-08-13\nP-008 consumes the shipping calculator port from sidestage-checkout-shipping-2026-08-13 P-112. Do NOT fork a second rate-calc implementation. P-008 starts after that port lands; coordinate with that plan lane on the service interface.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-006 — Reuse-first + prod-image loadability\nDate: 2026-08-13\nEvery feature rides existing subsystems (transcription/matching, product timestamps, judge scoring, message triage, checkout port). Lesson from WI-38629: the prod api image runs COMPILED JS - any lib a feature imports must be loadable there (no TS-source-only workspace deps; declare deps; lazy-import + degrade where optional).\n\n### D-007 — Deploy serialization\nDate: 2026-08-13\nSideStage prod deploys serialize with other lanes (same rule as sidestage-checkout-shipping D-003). Check for an in-flight deploy before firing deploy.sh; announce deploys on the fleet channel.\n\n### D-008 — Mockup gate is NON-blocking\nDate: 2026-08-13\nP-003/P-004 implement the recommended default variant behind a config switch WITHOUT waiting for the owner mockup pick; the pick re-skins, never restarts. This keeps the meter shipping while Avi reviews options.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-009 — Seller pricing history (owner verbatim)\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13 verbatim] \"lets add some history information for the seller so they can see things like for the active product, sold 5 @ this price. 2 rejected @ this price. etc. if they gave an offer to a buyer and they accepted/rejected. also for auctions. 3 x auctions sold at this.\" Aggregate from existing order/offer/auction records; no new event pipeline.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-010 — Quantity everywhere price is entered (owner verbatim)\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13 verbatim] \"When sellers create auctions and offers make sure there is a place to enter in quantity too, not just price.\" Applies to auction AND offer creation flows; quantity flows through to cart/checkout.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-011 — Sync path: SSE via @papercusp/sync - NOT the Zero WS adapter\nDate: 2026-08-13\nAll new feature surfaces use the shared libs/sync SyncProvider with syncType SSE (the path the app already mounts: EventChat SyncProvider SSE; AuctionPanel EventSource + polling fallback). The Zero-based WebSocket adapter exists in libs/sync/transports/websocket but NOTHING selects it and it stays unselected - do not hand-roll fetch loops and do not switch transports without an owner ruling. Engagement feed (P-001) publishes on the same SSE channel.\n\n### D-012 — Build-history tab mirrors the papercusp releases page\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13 verbatim] \"lets also add a tab for build history and lets make that mimic what we did for the papercusp releases page showing all the plans and associated work items that were completed.\" Reuse the releases-page pattern (plan -> completed work-items grouping) rather than inventing a new layout; data from the plan/work-item ledger.\nRelated: P-013\n\n### D-013 — Demo impersonation is auth-free by design (any id = logged in as that user)\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim]: \"This is just a demo so we should allow them to enter in any id, no auth, and once they put in that id, its as if they are logged in and shows them their orders in their order page.\" Ruling: the buyer tab gets a free-text user-id entry; the entered id becomes the app-wide current-user identity (persist it — localStorage and/or URL param so it survives reload and is agent-visible); no password, no validation beyond non-empty; entering a different id switches user. Explicitly NOT production auth — no security hardening, no session tokens, no backend auth checks in scope. The Orders tab (P-014) keys off this identity.\n\n### D-014 — The Orders page hosts the video snapshots\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13]: \"This is where we'll also put the video snapshots\" — said of the buyer's orders page. Ruling: the Orders tab/page (P-014) is the destination surface for video snapshots. [inferred interpretation, correct here if wrong: the per-purchase capture from the live stream — the moment this buyer's order happened — renders on the order row/detail, so a buyer scrolling their orders sees the video moment of each purchase.]\n\n### D-015 — Engagement meter renderings CHOSEN: S3 slim bar + trend sparkline (seller) and B3 chat-energy bar (buyer)\nDate: 2026-08-13\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-13, verbatim]: \"I like the Slim bar + trend sparkline and the Chat-energy bar.\" From the P-002 mockup slate (artifact 79b79e7d): SELLER = S3 — thin fill bar under the console header + 10-minute sparkline + delta% readout (the trend/history option). BUYER = B3 — slim gradient chat-energy bar riding above the chat input, filling/shimmering with chat velocity; positive-only per D-003 (quiet at low engagement, never a negative state). P-003 implements S3; P-004 implements B3. The other four options (S1/S2/B1/B2) are dropped — do not build them.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-016 — Fleet claim spec spans all 3 active plans; launch briefs are priorities, not scope cages; directed items get pinned\nDate: 2026-08-13\nRuling on c78d1479's claim-spec-drift report (msg mss4fmsq, 23:00Z): the sidestage-gpt claim spec (rev 17, in-filter over standout + retheme + checkout-shipping) is DELIBERATE — the fleet is one pooled lane draining all three active plans, so members MAY be handed items from any of them; a member's launch-context plan names its starting priority, never a scope cage, and executing a cross-plan claim from get_next is authorized. The one exception: items a leader has DIRECTED to a specific member are pinned via plan_items:assign so get_next never hands them elsewhere (P-111/WI-38634 → deeb7d is pinned now). Do not release a get_next claim solely because its source plan differs from your launch brief — release only on a genuine directed-assignment collision, and report it as c78d1479 correctly did.\n\n### D-017 — Spec-fed fleet plans stay at lifecycle 'ready' — 'active' reserves every promoted item away from scheduler:get_next\nDate: 2026-08-13\nRoot cause of tonight's fleet-wide ordinary_drain (c78d1479 22:53Z, 79b1c 23:10Z, 3eddd 22:57Z): this plan and the retheme plan sat at lifecycle status='active', and reservedPlanLaneExclusionSql leg 1 (work-items.ts:4177-4180 — p.op_status IN ('started','paused') OR (p.status='active' AND template_slug IS NULL)) excludes EVERY promoted feature item of such a plan from scheduler self-select, reserving it for a notional driving agent. Our fleet drains via claim-spec + get_next, so 'active' starves the whole lane while leader-brief's specMatched (pool-membership, pre-floor) still counts the items — the leader sees a fed lane, members drain. RULING: plans drained by the sidestage-gpt spec stay at status='ready' (both flipped 22:2xZ→23:2xZ; verified reservation predicate false post-flip). Do not set them 'active' or plans:start them while the fleet drains by spec. Platform bug filed for the observability gap (no plan-lane-reserved drain reason surfaced to members or leader).\n\n### D-018 — gpt-fleet members work ALL THREE plans of spec rev 17 — a member's kickoff plan binding does not narrow the fleet claim spec\nDate: 2026-08-13\nRuling (leader su-c18ba, 23:40Z, in response to c78d1479's spec-drift report mss4fmsq): fleet-launch-sidestage-gpt-plan rev 17's view.filter (plan IN [sidestage-standout-features-2026-08-13, sidestage-red-yellow-retheme-2026-08-13, sidestage-checkout-shipping-2026-08-13]) is DELIBERATE, not drift. The sidestage-gpt fleet drains all three sidestage plans as one pool; a member whose kickoff/launch context named a single plan takes the SPEC as the mission boundary, not the kickoff prose — the spec is the leader-owned, revision-controlled surface, the kickoff is a launch-time snapshot. Releasing a legitimately-claimed cross-plan item (as happened with WI-38634) is therefore unnecessary: claim what get_next admits. If a member has genuine reason to believe an admitted item is outside its competence, report it — do not self-narrow the pool.\n\n### D-019 — P-118 event selector direction CHOSEN: B \"Channel Guide\" drawer\nDate: 2026-08-13\nDate: 2026-08-13 [owner:Avi, from mockup artifact f965257e-d9f6-460b-9c48-7412679df50d]: picked option B — Channel Guide. SHAPE the implementer builds: a \"What's on\" button in the buyer tab opens a drawer/panel listing ALL events across ALL sellers, GROUPED BY STATE — \"Live now\" (red label, viewer counts), \"Up next\" (yellow label, start time), \"Ended\" (muted, replay) — each row: thumbnail, title, seller name, viewers; tapping a row switches the active event (current event check-marked); drawer steals no space from the stream until opened. Colors per retheme D-004 R3 tokens (no new hexes — use the :root tokens WI-38658 lands). Options A/C/D dropped (owner may later add a lobby view; do not pre-build). Requires the list-events API (id, title, seller, status live/upcoming/ended, viewerCount) — GET /events or equivalent in apps/api, consumed by BuyerTab.tsx replacing the DEFAULT_EVENT_ID hard-pin with selectable state.\n\n### D-020 — All SideStage app paths resolve against the hive root /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEvery relative app path in this plan's items (apps/web/..., apps/api/..., etc.) resolves against the ratified SideStage checkout /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage (branch staging) — NOT the Papercusp staging tree /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp, which has no apps/web. Verified 2026-08-14T00:12Z: apps/web/src/styles.css exists at the hive root. Root-confusion incidents this rules out: EI-20384455355405385 (WI-38658 ENOENT), EI-20340452128976093, EI-20342035550304021.\n\n### D-021 — P-008 (WI-38645) blocked on checkout P-112→P-111; scheduler admission was premature\nDate: 2026-08-14\nRuling (leader, 2026-08-14 01:52Z, confirming su-33c12's analysis): WI-38645/P-008 (combined-shipping meter) correctly moved to blocked with a typed live-dependency on sidestage-checkout-shipping-2026-08-13#P-112, which is itself blocked by P-111 (WI-38634, held+worked by su-deeb7). The cross-plan dependency was not encoded in local blockedBy, so the scheduler admitted P-008 prematurely — the blocked state now excludes it from admission. No lane picks up P-008 until P-112 lands; the fleet leader holds the dependency watch on WI-38634 and will unblock in order P-111 → P-112 → P-008.\n\n### D-022 — P-008 combined-shipping meter is server-authored and dollar claims require a proved hypothetical quote\nDate: 2026-08-15\nFor WI-38645/P-008, reuse the landed P-112 box-packer/rate-calculator port and the existing @papercusp/cart-drawer surface. The server authors parcel count and box-fill. The UI may say “Add one more — shipping stays $X” only when the server compares the current quote with a same-address, same-service hypothetical one-more-unit quote and the totals are equal. Before an address/quote exists, show truthful packing guidance without a dollar promise. Never fork a client-side rate calculator or infer cost from parcel count alone.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-023 — P-008 shipping meter is server-authored; dollar claims require an equal hypothetical quote\nDate: 2026-08-15\nP-008 extends the single P-112 ShippingService/box-packer authority. The API computes parcel fill and a deterministic one-more-unit candidate from current server-owned cart/catalog data; the browser renders that result and never recalculates packing. Before a complete address and selected carrier:service quote exist, the cart may show packing guidance but MUST NOT promise a dollar amount. The exact copy “shipping stays $X” is legal only when the server prices both the current cart and the one-more-unit hypothetical for the SAME normalized address and SAME carrier:service id and the totals are equal. If either quote is absent, the service disappears, or totals differ, return packing-only guidance. This avoids a second rate calculator and prevents parcel-count equality from being misrepresented as price equality.\nRelated: P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-android-public-release-readiness-2026-08-11","title":"Android 0.1.0 public-release readiness — acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-14","owner":"su-988a3f4e-f417-4e70-b715-5d9b45fec1d7","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Android 0.1.0 public-release readiness — acceptance\nslug: acceptance-android-public-release-readiness-2026-08-11\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-988a3f4e-f417-4e70-b715-5d9b45fec1d7\n---\n\n# Android 0.1.0 public-release readiness — acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01.
