Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"shared-cart-scout-drawer-libs-2026-08-14","title":"Shared cart drawer + Scout chat drawer libraries (Restart → SideStage, themed per app)","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Shared cart drawer + Scout chat drawer libraries (Restart → SideStage, themed per app)\nslug: shared-cart-scout-drawer-libs-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n# Shared cart drawer + Scout chat drawer libraries (Restart → SideStage, themed per app)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Active, AUTO [owner:Avi 2026-08-14]. P-001..P-007 + P-012 DONE. P-012 (WI-38946) closed with committed authority: SideStage's scout backend now has user-keyed long-term memory + a get_cart tool, and the D-003 auth trust boundary is established at the controller. Two decisions govern what follows — D-008: memory ports Restart's CONTRACT, not pgvector (SideStage has no vector extension and no embedding provider), so recall is LEXICAL over the existing pg_trgm/tsvector machinery, behind a seam an embedding store can replace. D-009: identity is server-resolved from headers and client-sent ids are stripped, but today's unsigned ss_buyer_id cookie is guest CONTINUITY, NOT authentication — so nothing sensitive goes in scout memory and no lane may call it per-user private until WI-38957 lands. Verified live on :3100: cookie identity wrote the memory, a second turn recalled it, and a forged body buyerId got nothing.\n\n**Next:** P-008 — build the SideStage scout drawer on @papercusp/scout-chat against the now-complete backend (streaming from P-007, memory + get_cart from P-012). Bound by D-009: the drawer must not describe scout memory as private. Then P-009/P-010 (blocked). Also outstanding: the promised non-implementer grade of accept-sidestage-run-of-show-planner-2026-08-14 for su-2c9ce.\n\n## Background\n\n**What exists today (verified in-tree 2026-08-14):**\n\n- **Restart / shop.buyrestart.com** (`/home/marsh-office/Restart`, Astro islands + React 19):\n  - Cart drawer: `apps/shop/src/components/CartShell.tsx` (821 L, Vaul + `@papercusp/drawer-stack` + `@papercusp/sync` + `@papercusp/shop-sdk`), plus `CartShellIsland.tsx`, `GlobalQuoteCartIsland.tsx`, `cart-events.ts`, `lib/cart-totals.ts`, `lib/cart-id.ts`, `CheckoutDrawerForm`, `CheckoutSuccess`. Backend: `apps/shop-api/src/cart/` (NestJS + drizzle; `shop_cart`/`quote_cart`; generic closure-injected resolution policy in `cart-core.ts`).\n  - Scout chat drawer: `apps/shop/src/components/ScoutDrawer.tsx` (90 L Vaul + drawer-stack wrapper) + `ScoutDrawerLauncher.tsx` + `RecommenderChat.tsx` (824 L; `@papercusp/sse` `resilientPostStream`, `@papercusp/chat-protocol` cards, `@papercusp/data-fetch` ETag transcript restore). Backend: `apps/shop/src/pages/api/scout.ts` (streaming SSE proxy = auth trust boundary) → `apps/scout-service` (NestJS ~3.7k L: scout/catalog/cart-proxy/memory/telemetry; reconnect-safe SSE `/chat/stream` with `token`/`products`/`broaden`/`tool_start` events, `Last-Event-ID` resume, ETag'd transcript `GET /session/:id`).\n  - `libs/drawer-stack`: small in-repo lib (`@papercusp/drawer-stack`: store, layout, `useDrawerStackItem`) — the generic cross-island right-edge drawer coordinator (placement, side-by-side panes, shared backdrop, ESC + scroll-lock). NOT yet a submodule.\n- **SideStage** (canonical tree `/home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage` — the `papercupai-workspace/sidestage` checkout is VESTIGIAL, see EI-20443492691207801; Vite + React 19 web, NestJS api):\n  - Cart work already begun: plan `sidestage-held-items-expiry-checkout-2026-08-14` (all 4 items done) — inventory holds with server-authored 2-minute expiry (`apps/api/src/inventory/hold-policy.ts` `BUYER_HOLD_DURATION_MS`), prune-on-read, release/remove APIs, and a buyer checkout drawer whose first state is a Held-items list with per-item countdowns (`apps/web/src/BuyerCheckout.tsx` + `buyer-checkout-api.ts`).\n  - Scout stub: `apps/api/src/scout/` (~190 L, non-streaming `POST /scout/chat`, plus `scout-catalog.adapter.ts`) and a hand-rolled `apps/web/src/CopilotPanel.tsx` (283 L).\n- **The shared-library mechanism already exists**: both repos consume standalone GitHub repos as git submodules under `libs/` (both already share `sync`, `sse`, `ui-primitives`, `agent-chat`, `token-kit`, `papergrid`, `test-config`). Restart additionally has `chat-protocol` as a submodule; SideStage does not yet.\n\n**Strategy in one line:** promote `drawer-stack` to a shared submodule, extract the two drawers out of Restart's shop app into two new shared, token-themed, backend-agnostic libs (`cart-drawer`, `scout-chat`), have Restart adopt them pixel-faithfully (its e2e suites guard the refactor), then have SideStage consume them with SideStage theming — cart adapter over its existing holds/expiry model, scout via a streaming endpoint added to its existing scout module.\n\n## Proposed decisions (ratify as D-NNN on approval)\n\n1. **Submodules, not npm publishing.** New shared code ships as standalone GitHub repos consumed as git submodules under `libs/` — the established pattern both repos already use. Three repos: `drawer-stack` (promoted from Restart in-repo lib), `cart-drawer` (new), `scout-chat` (new). Small single-purpose repos match the existing granularity (sync, sse, token-kit…).\n2. **Cart backends stay per-app.** Restart keeps `shop-api` carts; SideStage keeps inventory-holds + 2-min expiry. The shared `CartDrawer` is backend-agnostic behind a `CartAdapter` interface (read/subscribe/set-qty/remove/clear + checkout handoff slot); only genuinely generic pieces are shared (totals math; optionally `cart-core`'s closure-injected resolution policy as a server helper).\n3. **The scout backend borrow is the streaming CONTRACT + engine, not the whole service.** Shared contract: SSE stream with `token`/`products`/`tool_start` events, `Last-Event-ID` resume, ETag'd transcript restore. SideStage implements it inside its existing `apps/api` scout module (keeping `scout-catalog.adapter`), porting the reconnect-safe streaming core from Restart's scout-service. (Long-term memory / cart tools: owner-scoped question, see Open questions.)\n4. **Theming via CSS custom properties** (token-kit naming discipline): zero hardcoded colors/fonts in the shared components; each app supplies a token sheet. Restart's adoption must be pixel-faithful (guarded by existing e2e + visual check); SideStage maps tokens from its `apps/web/src/styles.css` palette.\n5. **All SideStage work happens in the canonical tree** `/home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage`. Restart-side extraction follows Restart's own repo conventions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md there).\n\n## Phase 1 — Share the drawer foundation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Promote Restart's `libs/drawer-stack` to a standalone `Papercusp/drawer-stack` GitHub repo and consume it as a git submodule at `libs/drawer-stack` in BOTH Restart and SideStage (imports stay `@papercusp/drawer-stack`; wire into each repo's npm workspaces; SideStage installs via `npm run install:safe`). importance: high — note: ← WI-38864 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Extract the two drawers into shared libs (Restart is the source of truth)\n\n- **P-002** `done` Create `Papercusp/cart-drawer` (`@papercusp/cart-drawer`): a themable CartDrawer shell extracted from `CartShell.tsx` — Vaul panel + drawer-stack registration, line-item list, quantity stepper, totals, empty state; slots for item renderer, header/footer, and checkout pane; ALL backend ops behind a `CartAdapter` interface; carry over `cart-totals` math and the `cart-events` open/close event pattern; CSS-custom-property theming only. importance: high — note: ← WI-38866 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Create `Papercusp/scout-chat` (`@papercusp/scout-chat`): a themable ScoutChatDrawer + launcher extracted from `ScoutDrawer.tsx` + `RecommenderChat.tsx` — streaming transcript + composer over `@papercusp/sse` `resilientPostStream`, chat-protocol card slots, `Last-Event-ID` resume + ETag transcript restore, all endpoints/session identity behind a `ChatTransport` adapter; fold in (or promote as a 4th submodule) the small `@papercusp/data-fetch` versioned-resource hook. importance: high — note: ← WI-38871 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Restart adopts both libs: `CartShell`/`ScoutDrawer`/`RecommenderChat` become thin app wrappers supplying the shop-sdk cart adapter and the `/api/scout` transport. Visuals unchanged — `t4-3-search-pdp-cart` + `scout-fab` e2e stay green, plus a visual spot-check of the live shop.importance: high blocked-by: P-002, P-003 — note: ← WI-38889 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — SideStage cart drawer (themed)\n\n- **P-005** `done` Wire SideStage to the shared libs: add `drawer-stack`, `cart-drawer`, `scout-chat`, and `chat-protocol` submodules to `.gitmodules` + workspaces, add the `vaul` dep via `install:safe`, and author the SideStage theme token sheet mapped from the existing web styles. blocked-by: P-001, importance: high — note: ← WI-38915 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Build the SideStage cart drawer: a `CartAdapter` over the holds/expiry APIs (2-min server-authored `expiresAt`, prune-on-read, release/remove), per-item countdown rendered in the item slot, buyer-tab entry point, handing off to the existing BuyerCheckout flow — preserving the shipped held-items behavior and its acceptance criteria. blocked-by: P-005, importance: high — note: ← WI-38916 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — SideStage Scout chat (themed)\n\n- **P-007** `done` Extend SideStage `apps/api` scout module to the shared streaming contract: SSE `POST /scout/chat/stream` emitting `token`/`products`/`tool_start` with `Last-Event-ID` resume, plus an ETag'd transcript `GET` — porting the reconnect-safe streaming core from Restart's `apps/scout-service` and keeping `scout-catalog.adapter` as the catalog source (scope of memory/cart tools per owner decision in Open questions). importance: high — note: ← WI-38930 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Wire the shared ScoutChatDrawer into SideStage web with a launcher, SideStage-themed, integrated alongside (or replacing) CopilotPanel's chat surface.blocked-by: P-007 blocked-by: P-005, P-007 — note: ← WI-38964 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Port user-keyed long-term memory + cart tools into the SideStage scout backend (per D-003): a memory store keyed to server-resolved buyer identity, and a get_cart-style tool over the holds/expiry cart, following Restart scout-service’s memory + cart-proxy modules; establish the auth trust boundary (server injects buyer id into scout requests, client-sent ids overwritten). blocked-by: P-007 importance: high — note: ← WI-38946 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Verification + ship\n\n- **P-009** `wip` Verify both apps end to end: Restart `test:affected` + cart/scout e2e + visual check (look unchanged); SideStage API/web tests + browser QA of drawer open/stacking, hold countdown → checkout handoff, and streaming scout chat, desktop + mobile viewports.blocked-by: P-008 blocked-by: P-004, P-006, P-008 blocked-by: P-004, P-006, P-008, P-012 — note: → WI-39276\n- **P-010** `todo` Author the post-implementation acceptance rubric, obtain a non-implementer grade, then ship the plan (workspace acceptance-rubric gate). blocked-by: P-009\n\n## Open questions (for Avi)\n\n- **Scout backend depth for SideStage** — streaming chat + catalog recommendations only (recommended: smallest port that delivers the full drawer UX), or ALSO port scout-service's long-term memory (user-keyed) and cart tools?\n- **Lib repo naming** — `cart-drawer` / `scout-chat` proposed; happy to rename (e.g. one combined `commerce-drawers` repo instead of two).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Packaging: git submodules, three single-purpose repos\nDate: 2026-08-14\nShared code ships as standalone GitHub repos consumed as git submodules under libs/ (the pattern both apps already use). Three repos: drawer-stack (promoted from Restart's in-repo lib), cart-drawer (new), scout-chat (new). No npm publishing. Two separate drawer repos over one combined repo. [owner:Avi 2026-08-14 — ratified via AskUserQuestion: \"Two repos: cart-drawer + scout-chat\"]\n\n### D-002 — Cart backends stay per-app behind a CartAdapter seam\nDate: 2026-08-14\nRestart keeps shop-api shop_cart/quote_cart; SideStage keeps inventory-holds + 2-minute expiry. The shared CartDrawer performs ALL backend ops through a CartAdapter interface (read/subscribe/set-qty/remove/clear + checkout handoff slot). Only genuinely generic pieces are shared (totals math; optionally cart-core's closure-injected resolution policy as a server helper).\n\n### D-003 — SideStage scout backend = FULL port (streaming + memory + cart tools)\nDate: 2026-08-14\nOwner chose the full port over the streaming-only recommendation [owner:Avi 2026-08-14 via AskUserQuestion]. SideStage's apps/api scout module gets: (1) the shared streaming contract — SSE stream with token/products/tool_start events, Last-Event-ID resume, ETag'd transcript restore — ported from Restart scout-service's reconnect-safe core; (2) user-keyed long-term memory; (3) cart tools (get_cart-style over the holds/expiry cart). The auth trust boundary follows Restart's pattern: buyer identity resolved server-side and injected into scout requests, client-sent ids overwritten. Tracked as P-007 (streaming) + P-012 (memory + cart tools).\n\n### D-004 — Theming via CSS custom properties; Restart adoption pixel-faithful\nDate: 2026-08-14\nZero hardcoded colors/fonts in the shared components — all visual identity flows through CSS custom properties following token-kit naming. Each app supplies its token sheet: Restart’s reproduces the current shop look exactly (adoption guarded by t4-3-search-pdp-cart + scout-fab e2e plus a visual check), SideStage’s maps from apps/web/src/styles.css.\n\n### D-005 — Canonical trees + execution route\nDate: 2026-08-14\nAll SideStage work happens in the canonical tree /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage (papercupai-workspace/sidestage is vestigial, EI-20443492691207801). Restart-side work in /home/marsh-office/Restart per its own AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md conventions. Execution route: single su session (su-effff9d3), owner-chosen over a fleet [owner:Avi 2026-08-14 via AskUserQuestion] — route is sticky.\n\n### D-006 — data-fetch promoted as 4th submodule; chat-protocol pulled forward into SideStage\nDate: 2026-08-14\nP-003's open sub-decision (\"fold in or promote @papercusp/data-fetch\") resolved: PROMOTED as the 4th standalone repo, https://github.com/Papercusp/data-fetch, submoduled at libs/data-fetch in BOTH apps (Restart swapped in-place — same path, imports + workspace linkage unchanged). Rationale: its only deps (@papercusp/kv-persist, kv-persist-indexeddb) live inside the papergrid submodule both apps already carry, so promotion costs nothing, and P-007/P-008 need the same ETag/304 versioned-resource hook in SideStage. Consequence for P-005: the chat-protocol submodule was ALSO already added to SideStage during P-003 (required to typecheck scout-chat there), vaul is already present via npm peer auto-install, and SideStage root gained a @types/react-dom devDep (fixed a pre-existing gap that broke any lib tsc importing react-dom, incl. drawer-stack). P-005's remaining scope: workspaces/.gitmodules audit + the SideStage theme token sheet. [self-imposed, within the fold-or-promote latitude the ratified P-003 item text grants]\n\n### D-007 — SideStage apps/api stays free of @types/express — controllers declare structural req/res shapes\nDate: 2026-08-14\nDate: 2026-08-14\n\nEstablished while implementing P-007 (WI-38930), and it governs any later lane that adds a controller needing raw req/res — notably P-012, which extends this same scout controller.\n\nThe streaming endpoint needs the underlying Node/Express request and response (`@Req()` / `@Res()`), which normally means `import type { Request, Response } from 'express'`. SideStage has NO `@types/express` — not in the root, not in any workspace, not transitively on disk — so that import fails typecheck with TS7016.\n\nDECISION: do NOT add the `@types/express` dependency. Declare the minimal structural interfaces the handler actually touches, local to the controller:\n  - `StreamRequestLike`  — `headers`, `on('close', …)`\n  - `StreamResponseLike` — `statusCode`, `setHeader`, `write`, `end`, `destroy?`\n  - `TranscriptResponseLike` — `status`, `setHeader`\n\nRATIONALE:\n1. It matches the shared lib. `@papercusp/sse`'s Node bridge (`sseResponseToNode`) is deliberately deps-free and accepts a structural `NodeResponseLike` for exactly this reason — the structural shape IS the lib's contract, so importing express types would be a heavier way of restating it.\n2. An install in this shared tree is a live hazard, not a formality. Earlier the same day a concurrent install re-hoisted `@vitejs/plugin-react` out from under the running vite dev server and 500'd every module for every agent (EI-20454872322741826). Adding a devDependency to satisfy one import is not worth re-entering that class.\n3. It keeps the handlers testable without booting HTTP: a plain object satisfies these shapes, where an express `Request` does not.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: if a future lane genuinely needs broad express typing (many handlers, middleware types), that is the point to reconsider and add the dependency deliberately via `npm run install:safe` — not as a side effect of one import.\n\n### D-008 — Scout memory ports the CONTRACT, not pgvector — Postgres FTS behind a store seam\nDate: 2026-08-14\nDate: 2026-08-14\nD-003 says SideStage's scout gets \"user-keyed long-term memory\", following Restart's memory module. Restart's MemoryService is pgvector + OpenAI text-embedding-3-small. VERIFIED that mechanism cannot be ported literally to SideStage:\n- Repo-wide search of the sidestage tree (excluding node_modules/dist/tests) finds NO OpenAI SDK and no live embedding provider. docker-compose.prod.yml sets TYPESENSE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER: none — embeddings are explicitly DISABLED, not merely absent. The only OpenAI hits are a transitive otel package-lock entry, a COMMENT in copilot.pipeline.ts about \"the eventual OpenAI SDK adapter\", and test-config console-noise filters.\n- The live dev DB reports `SELECT extname FROM pg_extension` = plpgsql, pg_trgm ONLY, and pg_available_extensions has NO 'vector' row at all — so `CREATE EXTENSION vector` cannot even succeed there. Restart's ensureSchema() would latch degraded on first use and memory would be permanently dead.\n- TRAP for anyone re-checking: grepping 'pgvector' in this tree DOES hit libs/test-config/src/pg-container.ts, which pins the `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` image as the INTEGRATION-TEST container. That is the test harness, NOT the SideStage database. Do not read those hits as \"pgvector is available\".\n\nRULING: port the memory CONTRACT — scope-keyed remember/recall, `user:<id>` + `store` scopes, degrade-safe (memory NEVER breaks a turn; recall failure yields [] and a write is dropped) — behind a `ScoutMemoryStore` seam, and implement recall on the Postgres full-text/trigram machinery SideStage ALREADY has (db/schema.sql:8 creates pg_trgm; the catalog already carries a search_tsv tsvector with to_tsvector triggers). Reuse-first: no new retrieval mechanism is invented. The seam is what makes this reversible — a pgvector/embedding implementation can replace the store with no change to the service, if TYPESENSE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER is ever turned on. Note libs/typesense/src/client.ts already models a 384-dim embedding field with a placeholder-0 semantic mode; that, not pgvector, is where semantic retrieval would land here.\n\nConsequence other lanes must respect: scout memory recall is LEXICAL, not semantic. A drawer or prompt that assumes paraphrase-tolerant recall will over-promise.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-009 — Scout identity is server-resolved at the controller; today it is guest continuity, NOT authentication\nDate: 2026-08-14\nDate: 2026-08-14\nD-003 requires the Restart auth trust boundary: \"buyer identity resolved server-side and injected into scout requests, client-sent ids overwritten\". Restart does this in its /api/scout proxy (apps/shop/src/pages/api/scout.ts:83-85 — `body.userId = user?.id ?? undefined` off a better-auth cookie), with scout-service bound to loopback so it is unreachable except through that proxy.\n\nVERIFIED SideStage has no equivalent identity source today: apps/api's only buyerId is checkout.controller.ts:13 `@Query('buyerId')` — client-supplied and unauthenticated — and a grep for auth/session/cookie middleware across apps/api finds none. There is no proxy tier either; apps/api IS the edge. So there is nothing to \"resolve from\" yet.\n\nRULING (two parts, deliberately separated):\n1. STRUCTURE — establish the boundary now, in the controller, via a `ScoutIdentityResolver` seam. The scout controller resolves identity from the REQUEST (cookie/header) and OVERWRITES any `buyerId` on the request body before it reaches ScoutService. The service takes identity only as a resolved argument and never reads it off the client payload. This makes the client-sent id structurally unforgeable regardless of what auth lands later, and reduces the future auth change to swapping one provider.\n2. HONEST SCOPE — until real auth exists, the resolved id comes from an opaque `ss_buyer_id` cookie, which is UNSIGNED and therefore self-asserted. This delivers per-visitor CONTINUITY (your scout remembers you across turns and reloads), and it is NOT an authentication or isolation boundary: a visitor who sets that cookie to another visitor's id would read their memories. Restart can claim isolation because its tooldef reads scope off a cryptographically-verified session; SideStage cannot, and must not claim it.\n\nBinding consequence: do NOT store anything sensitive in scout memory, and do NOT describe scout memory as per-user private, until the resolver is backed by a verified session. Tracked as a follow-up work-item so the seam is not mistaken for a finished security boundary.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-010 — SideStage Scout browser transport is same-origin and adapts cart context through the shared body seam\nDate: 2026-08-14\nP-008 uses same-origin browser endpoints: POST /api/scout/chat/stream and GET /api/scout/session/:id. In production Nest is mounted at API_PREFIX=api; in Vite development the existing /api proxy strips that prefix before forwarding to the bare :3100 routes. This is required for the D-009 ss_buyer_id continuity cookie to travel under fetch's same-origin default; the absolute VITE_API_URL path is not used for Scout. The web adapter ensures an opaque, non-sensitive ss_buyer_id cookie exists before constructing the transport. It is UNSIGNED guest continuity only, never privacy/authentication copy. To keep @papercusp/scout-chat's reconnect/ETag machinery and avoid an app-local transport fork, HttpChatTransportOptions gains a buildBody override; SideStage uses it to promote only cartId/eventId from pageContext into its backend's established top-level request shape. No client identity is promoted. The SideStage backend emits no interactive-card events, so answerCard is explicitly unsupported and no phantom card-response endpoint is introduced.\nRelated: P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage seller auction and public chat release","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage seller auction and public chat release\nslug: sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n\n# SideStage seller auction and public chat release\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** D-029 ADMISSION WAVE COMPLETE AND FLEET WOUND DOWN. WI-39153/P-011 is done with accepted leader audit: exact changed blobs match the completion manifest; exact 13-file behavior/contract suite independently reproduces 164/164; focused pair reproduces 28/28; API typecheck and diff validation pass. P-009 remains a separate release lane and D-028-deferred cutover items remain closed.\n\n**Next:** Resume P-016 only after the consumed identity plan's full evidence matrix is green; any downstream Zero cutover still requires the post-submission review authority preserved by D-028.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2144386 — Cut over public/shared commerce projections to Zero ZQL: Channel Guide/events, published event configuration, catalog products/options, inventory availability, active auction state and bids, public c… <!-- P-017 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144387 — Cut over buyer-owned state to principal-scoped Zero queries and optimistic mutators: carts, reservations/expiry, checkout and order status, buyer-targeted offers, Scout sessions/transcripts/memory, a… <!-- P-018 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144388 — Cut over seller-owned state to principal-scoped Zero queries and optimistic mutators: events.mine, drafts/configuration, event items and inventory, run of show, actions/offers/audits/rollback status,… <!-- P-019 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144389 — Define and implement the Zero boundary for operational, derived, and streaming surfaces: build history, readiness/rehearsal and judge results, system-test status, media-session metadata, and AI/chat … <!-- P-020 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144390 — Retire parallel client data paths after every domain is green: all server-backed reads use useSyncQuery and all writes use useSyncMutate; REST exists only as the shared library's SSE/polling fallback… <!-- P-021 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144391 — Replace SideStage's hard-coded SSE app root with one universal @papercusp/sync provider configured WEBSOCKETS-first using the SideStage server URL, selected principal, schema, named queries, and muta… <!-- P-014 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144392 — Run universal Zero acceptance across two sellers, two buyers, multiple tabs/devices, and every census row: cross-client propagation, optimistic reconciliation/rollback, ordered duplicate-free updates… <!-- P-015 -->\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Repair the Event Manager dock seed/recovery and ship an explicit, discoverable seller Start auction workflow with focused regression tests. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38878 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Enable first-class seller chat composing/replying while preserving triage, optimistic delivery, accessibility, and error feedback. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39091 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Replace process-memory chat history with the existing Postgres data-layer pattern and add public-boundary protections: authoritative seller capability, idempotent sends, pagination, rate limiting, moderation actions, and metrics. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39068 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Verification\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Run focused and full tests, seller-to-buyer browser QA across desktop/mobile, public-release checks, and verify the automated pipeline reaches a green deployed build. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-015\n\n\n## Phase — Auction public-release hardening\n\n- **P-005** `done` Persist auction aggregates, bids, lifecycle transitions, and winner orders in Postgres using the existing DatabaseModule/store pattern; make start, bid, automatic/manual close, inventory reservation ownership, and restart recovery transactional; add migration and focused restart/concurrency tests. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38937 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Establish the public auction write boundary: authenticate seller start/close, derive or verify buyer identity server-side, add bid idempotency, rate limits, payload/amount ceilings, and auditable rejection paths without breaking the intentional guest buyer experience. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-005 — note: ← WI-38966 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Harden auction realtime and client recovery: authenticated mutations, reconnect/resume from authoritative snapshots, outbid/conflict feedback, closed/winner recovery after refresh, accessible disabled/error states, and no stale-live UI after the clock expires. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-005, P-006 — note: ← WI-38985 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Run auction acceptance coverage against the current tree: focused and full API/web tests, restart and concurrent-bid rehearsals, seller-to-two-buyers browser flow on desktop/mobile, and public-boundary abuse probes with evidence. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007 — note: ← WI-39001 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Promote the verified auction build through the release pipeline, repair any red checkpoint, trigger a fresh verdict, deploy the green pin, and verify the public SideStage auction surface and health without destructive production test data. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-008, P-026 — note: closed 2026-09-04 as completion residue: the lane was campaign-completed 2026-08-16 in sidestage-public-release-drive-2026-08-16#P-007 (done) via WI-39007 (done) and WI-39399 (done); only the status flip was missed\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — WebSocket chat migration\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Universal Zero domain cutover\n\n- **P-016** `blocked` Establish the cross-plan identity and authorization gate by consuming sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14 rather than duplicating it. Record its selected-principal, public-versus-private projection, owner-check, cache partitioning, and identity-switch contracts as prerequisites for Zero row visibility and mutator authorization; private-domain cutover cannot pass until that plan's P-002 through P-008 evidence is green. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-010 — note: Blocked by the typed cross-plan live-dependency on sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14 P-002..P-008 green evidence; see D-030 and WI-2144288.\n- **P-017** `todo` Cut over public/shared commerce projections to Zero ZQL: Channel Guide/events, published event configuration, catalog products/options, inventory availability, active auction state and bids, public chat/transcript/presence/stats/replay chapters, event stats/pricing history, and other intentionally public read models. Preserve server-derived projections and pagination while eliminating component-owned polling and raw EventSource refresh paths. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-003, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014\n- **P-018** `todo` Cut over buyer-owned state to principal-scoped Zero queries and optimistic mutators: carts, reservations/expiry, checkout and order status, buyer-targeted offers, Scout sessions/transcripts/memory, and buyer identity continuity. Payment, shipping-rate, and AI-provider calls remain authoritative server commands, but their durable inputs/results/statuses must land in Postgres and return to every authorized client through Zero. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-016\n- **P-019** `todo` Cut over seller-owned state to principal-scoped Zero queries and optimistic mutators: events.mine, drafts/configuration, event items and inventory, run of show, actions/offers/audits/rollback status, policies/outbox state, Copilot proposals, auction controls, and seller-facing operational views. Enforce ownership in both query resolution and mutation transactions using the identity plan's existing event/inventory authority. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-016\n- **P-020** `todo` Define and implement the Zero boundary for operational, derived, and streaming surfaces: build history, readiness/rehearsal and judge results, system-test status, media-session metadata, and AI/chat streaming completion state. Persist durable client-visible results before syncing them; keep raw audio/video bytes, live WebRTC media, incremental model tokens, secrets, and third-party RPCs on their purpose-built transports while syncing their metadata, lifecycle, and final results through Zero. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-016\n- **P-021** `todo` Retire parallel client data paths after every domain is green: all server-backed reads use useSyncQuery and all writes use useSyncMutate; REST exists only as the shared library's SSE/polling fallback or explicit command fallback, never as component-owned fetch state. Add a generated schema/publication/query/mutator census plus lint/contract tests that fail on unclassified tables, direct server-data fetches, raw EventSource query refresh, missing publication entries, missing authorization, or client/server Zero version drift. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-017, P-018, P-019, P-020\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Universal Zero foundation\n\n- **P-010** `done` Produce a complete, machine-readable census of every SideStage client-visible data surface before migration: every Postgres table, process-local store, API controller read/write, registered sync query/invalidation, component-owned fetch/EventSource/cache, and external command result. Classify each as public, buyer-owned, seller-owned, operational, streaming, or device-local; name its authoritative store, Zero table/query/mutator, identity scope, fallback, freshness/SLO, and migration owner. Acceptance: the census is exhaustive and a contract test fails when an unclassified surface is added. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39064 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Make Postgres the sole server authority for every client-visible SideStage domain before Zero publication. Complete P-003's chat durability and migrate remaining process-local authoritative state—including actions/offers/audits, ephemeral service documents, and durable rehearsal/judge/operational results—into existing stores or the smallest new tables. Give every replicated row stable primary keys, physical column mappings, ordering/version timestamps, ownership, retention/deletion rules, idempotent transaction boundaries, and outbox/side-effect handling so API restarts never erase or fork application state. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-39153 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `todo` Create one SideStage-owned Zero contract package, following Restart's libs/zero pattern, that exports the app schema and relationships, typed named ZQL query registry, and createMutators registry. Import the exact same contract from the web SyncProvider and the API's zero-cache /query and /mutate handlers; map real Postgres physical names and timestamp types, validate query args, execute mutators transactionally, and pass the selected principal into both query visibility and mutator authorization. Add schema/query/mutator parity tests so browser, API, publication, and database cannot drift. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-010, P-011, P-016 — note: ← WI-39154 released\n- **P-013** `todo` Provision SideStage zero-cache for local, staging, and production by reusing Restart's proven operational pattern: direct Postgres logical replication; a deliberately scoped publication matching the SideStage Zero schema exactly; separate upstream/change DB settings; query/mutate URLs; least-privilege app-role grants to Zero metadata; client/server @rocicorp/zero version pinning; persistent per-instance replica and unique replication slot; TLS WebSocket routing and sticky sessions; keepalive health checks; startup replica-lock recovery; replication-lag, reconnect, heap/disk, and publication-drift alerts; and a tested re-replication/rollback procedure for published schema changes. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-010, P-011, P-012 — note: ← WI-39155 released\n- **P-014** `todo` Replace SideStage's hard-coded SSE app root with one universal @papercusp/sync provider configured WEBSOCKETS-first using the SideStage server URL, selected principal, schema, named queries, and mutators. Preserve the shared WEBSOCKETS → SSE → bounded POLLING fallback chain for reachability failures only; keep query identity/cache partitions stable across navigation and reconnect, prevent duplicate or out-of-order optimistic results during transport transitions, expose connection/fallback/lag telemetry in the app, and canary the cutover without allowing a feature-by-feature provider or parallel cache. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-010, P-012, P-013, P-016\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Universal Zero verification\n\n- **P-015** `todo` Run universal Zero acceptance across two sellers, two buyers, multiple tabs/devices, and every census row: cross-client propagation, optimistic reconciliation/rollback, ordered duplicate-free updates, API and zero-cache restarts, replica rebuild, schema migration, reconnect/resume, offline-to-online recovery, WebSocket-blocked SSE/polling fallback, identity switching, public/private row isolation, large-query pagination, and latency/error-budget SLOs. Prove the Restart failure classes are guarded—version skew, over-broad publication, stale SQLite lock, missing Zero-schema grants, replica/slot desync, and unhealthy WebSocket route—then run focused/full API/web/sync tests and P-004's green deployed public verification with zero unclassified residue. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-016, P-017, P-018, P-019, P-020, P-021\n\n\n## Phase — Open demo seller authority\n\n- **P-022** `done` Remove the browser seller-credential prompt, session storage, bearer headers, and seller-access endpoint; use the selected demo principal for seller auction actions. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39112 completed (done)\n- **P-023** `done` Remove the shared credential requirement from seller chat and transcription paths while preserving demo-principal ownership checks, rate limits, payload validation, guest bid identity, and audit logging. blocked-by: P-022 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39183 completed (done)\n- **P-024** `done` Remove obsolete seller-token deployment configuration, update regression coverage, and verify API/web typechecks, focused/full tests, and the browser auction start/close flow. blocked-by: P-022, P-023 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39185 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Owner-approved Watch room experience\n\n- **P-025** `done` Implement the owner-approved Watch room experience in the real SideStage web app: compose the existing authoritative AuctionPanel as the conditional Now selling/current-offer module and add accessible Chat, Details, and Seller tabs using existing durable chat and product/event data paths; preserve auction authority, reconnect behavior, and mobile usability. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39195 completed (done)\n- **P-026** `done` Add focused component and interaction regression coverage for the Watch current-offer composition and Chat/Details/Seller tabs, then run exact web typecheck/tests and verify desktop/mobile keyboard, responsive, console, and network behavior in a real browser. blocked-by: P-025 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39223 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase — UI theme alignment\n\n- **P-027** `done` Remove the visible Polling copy from Watch > Live Auction while preserving live-update behavior and accessibility; add or update focused regression coverage. importance: high — note: ← WI-39245 completed (done)\n- **P-028** `done` Retheme the Chat tab using the established SideStage visual language while preserving chat behavior and responsive layout; add or update focused regression coverage and browser-verify desktop/mobile. importance: high — note: ← WI-39246 completed (done)\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n**Durable authority.** Every client-visible server-backed SideStage domain has one durable Postgres authority with stable identifiers, ownership, ordering/version timestamps, retention/deletion rules, idempotent transaction boundaries, and explicit outbox/side-effect handling. Restarting the API or sync layer must not erase, fork, or silently re-own application state.\n\n**Public/private boundary.** Public projections are deliberately enumerated. Buyer- and seller-owned rows are filtered by the selected principal, every mutation repeats the ownership check transactionally, direct foreign identifiers disclose no more than absent identifiers, and identity switches partition and invalidate cached state without cross-principal residue.\n\n**Cross-plan identity gate.** P-016 reuses `sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14`; it does not create a parallel identity model. Private-domain Zero acceptance cannot pass until that plan's P-002 through P-008 evidence is green and the selected-principal, owner-check, public/private projection, cache-partition, and identity-switch contracts are recorded here.\n\n**Realtime contract.** After its deferred cutover is reopened, one `@papercusp/sync` provider backed by Rocicorp Zero is the WebSocket-first publication and mutation path. SSE and bounded polling are reachability fallbacks only. Raw media, incremental model tokens, secrets, and third-party payment/shipping/AI RPCs remain on purpose-built transports while their durable metadata and final state remain in the governed data model.\n\n**Operational safety.** Logical replication/publication scope, client/server versions, least-privilege grants, per-instance replica and slot identity, TLS/sticky routing, keepalive health, stale-lock recovery, re-replication, schema migration, and rollback are explicit and tested before production cutover.\n\n**Acceptance.** The final plan demonstrates multi-seller and multi-buyer isolation, multiple tabs/devices, optimistic reconciliation and rollback, ordered duplicate-free propagation, restart/rebuild/reconnect behavior, REST/Zero parity during migration, no bypass caches, and a green deployed release.\n\n**Current execution boundary.** D-028 remains binding. P-012 through P-015 and P-017 through P-021 stay deferred behind Avi's post-submission review gate. This admission repair exposes only the already-valid roots P-011 and P-016; it does not authorize or imply the deferred cutover.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing SideStage authority and identity surfaces instead of introducing parallel systems. P-011 completes durable Postgres authority through the existing DatabaseModule/store conventions. P-016 consumes the existing demo-user-isolation plan as the identity contract and records the cross-plan proof boundary; private data visibility and mutator authorization remain server-derived, never client-asserted.\n\nFor the later Zero phase, reuse Restart's `libs/zero` schema/query/mutator shape and production guards. The browser and API share one typed contract; the API exposes guarded query/mutate handlers; Zero publishes durable authority rather than becoming a second source of truth. Migrate domain-by-domain behind parity and rollback evidence, then remove superseded caches and transport bypasses only after acceptance.\n\nThe dependency order is durable authority and identity first, then contract/publication/operations, then public, buyer, seller, and operational domain cutovers, then no-bypass cleanup and final acceptance. D-028 temporarily stops that sequence after the two preparatory roots: P-011 and P-016 may be scheduled now, while the deferred phases remain blocked until the review gate is explicitly reopened. This preserves the shipped WebSocket submission path and avoids a high-risk pre-submission re-plumb.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Public release means an internet-facing boundary\nDate: 2026-08-14\nTreat SideStage chat as an internet-facing product surface, not an auth-free demo: preserve the existing buyer guest experience, but never trust a client-authored seller role; persist history durably; bound abuse; expose moderation and observability; verify through the real browser flow.\n\n### D-002 — Auction public-release floor is durable server authority plus authenticated writes\nDate: 2026-08-14\nDate: 2026-08-14\nAn auction is not public-release ready merely because the seller/buyer UI and happy-path tests pass. Release requires the auction aggregate, bid ordering, lifecycle transitions, inventory reservation ownership, and winner order to survive process restart under a transactional server authority. Seller start/close must be authenticated and authorized; buyer identity must be server-derived or cryptographically verified rather than trusted from a client-authored bidderId; mutations need idempotency, bounded amounts, and rate/abuse controls. Client state is a projection that must recover from authoritative snapshots after reconnect or refresh. Verification must include restart, concurrent bids, abuse probes, browser seller-to-two-buyers flow, and deployed green-build evidence.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-003 — Auction writes use a single-seller bearer boundary and server-signed guest identity\nDate: 2026-08-14\nSideStage has no verified auth provider to extend, and multi-seller onboarding is explicitly outside this build. P-006 therefore protects start/close with a constant-time-verified, server-configured seller bearer credential (never bundled into the web app), while the seller UI accepts it into session-only storage. Recorded by su-a90558eb after a measured admissibility audit (WI-2144672), because the fastest-looking repair here is destructive and a previous reading of mine got it wrong.\n\nMEASURED, from the real fleet:launch-on-plan admission path (not the plan file): planItems.actionable=0, readyWidth=0, reason='no-actionable-plan-items', rootClasses { dependency:10, sticky:1, non-actionable-status:17 }, criticalPath depth=8 P-016 -> P-012 -> P-013 -> P-014 -> P-017 -> P-021 -> P-015 -> P-004.\n\nWHY THAT ZERO IS CORRECT. Every non-terminal item is DELIBERATELY gated, by decisions still in force: (1) P-016 is held by a typed live-dependency on WI-2144288 keyed to sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14 P-002..P-008 green evidence — D-030, recorded 2026-09-04, which says in terms to clear it ONLY after a fresh canonical read shows all of P-002..P-008 effective done. Its single DAG blocker P-010 being done is therefore NOT evidence the edge is stale. (3) P-004 (Verification) is blocked solely on P-015, i.e. on that same deferral. Clearing any of these to raise `actionable` would override live decisions, not repair a defect.\n\nP-009 IS THE EXCEPTION, AND IT IS NOW CLOSED — as residue, on ledger evidence. It had sat `wip` since 2026-08-15 (rev 131) with no plan_item_claims row and no work_items row carrying source_plan_slug, which reads exactly like an orphaned claim; I first flipped it to `todo` on that reading and was WRONG.
