The lane was campaign-completed in the successor plan sidestage-public-release-drive-2026-08-16 as its P-007 ('Auction-release residual: campaign-complete sidestage-auction-chat-public-release P-009'), done, closed by WI-39399 at 2026-08-16T07:26:50Z; that successor plan is 11/11 done. Only the status flip here was missed. Returning P-009 to `todo` would have re-placed an already-shipped promote/deploy lane — a live outward-facing action.\n\nTHEREFORE: this plan is not fleet-placeable today and should not be made so by editing edges. The actual unlock is upstream — finish sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14 P-006..P-008, which is now itself admissible (actionable=1 at P-006 after its spec triad was written under WI-2144672). When P-002..P-008 there are green, clear the WI-2144288 blocker per D-030, and take the downstream Zero items only under whatever review authority D-028 has been replaced by. Related: EI-22376849517310351 records a real coverage-oracle bug found here — promotion's mint gate counts TERMINAL covering rows while admission counts only non-terminal ones, so an open item whose only coverage is closed can deadlock at 'promotion-lag'.\nRelated: P-004, P-009, P-012, P-015, P-016, P-021\n\n### D-032 — Upstream gate spec: what \"demo-user-isolation evidence matrix is green\" requires (mirrors sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14 D-012)\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-016 (via D-030) is gated on the upstream plan sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14 having a green evidence matrix. That phrase predates the specification of the bar, so this records what now satisfies it. Canonical copy is that plan's D-012; recorded HERE because the cross-reference mechanism did not deliver (see below), so this plan's readers would otherwise never see it.\n\nUpstream status at time of writing: P-001..P-007 done; P-008 is the sole non-terminal item and the last thing between these two plans. It is claimed and progressing.\n\nThe bar is four upstream decisions:\n- D-008 — browser-level assertion that Scout continuity re-keys on a demo-identity switch (transport + conversation cache + the scout-session-id sessionStorage key all follow the new buyer).\n- D-009 C1-C3 — C1: every identity-boundary assertion must be MUTATION-VERIFIED, i.e. shown to FAIL against a build with the mechanism removed, and must cross roles (buyer->seller); two ordinary personas silently pass. C2: jsdom's localStorage is partial; seed via the identity writer. C3: real-browser coverage of sessionStorage/localStorage plus the HttpOnly guest-cookie rotation.\n- D-010 — conditional seller-ownership branches must be declared with a per-branch cell, enforced by a source-scanning invariant. This already satisfies C1 for the API surface.\n- D-011 — the closure bar for P-008: clauses 1 (DB/pg parity), 2 (one principal-aware cache-invalidation cell) and 4 (event-manager two-seller) required under C1; clause 3 closes either by a deterministic identity-key-discard guard assertion or by a filed product finding that no such guard exists; clause 5 (rendered desktop/mobile QA) is struck as residue.\n\nOperative consequence: a green matrix never demonstrated capable of FAILING does not satisfy this gate. Read D-011 as the checklist, not the P-008 title, which truncates its clauses.\n\nCarried caveat, not covered by any decision above: teardown of a prior seller's live media session on identity remount is UNPROVEN. Upstream P-007 asserted it already-satisfied at verifiedHow 'unit', which cannot exercise a live publisher teardown. Do not inherit that assertion as evidence.\n\nWhy this is duplicated by hand: plans:add-decision { affects:['sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14'] } returned ok:true with unknown_affects naming that slug, twice, while plans:get resolved the same slug in the same harness seconds apart. The cross-reference plan_event and watcher notify therefore never fired. Filed as a platform defect.\nRelated: P-016\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14","title":"Make every SideStage surface follow the selected demo user","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make every SideStage surface follow the selected demo user\nslug: sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ADMISSIBLE AND RUNNING as of 2026-09-04 (WI-2144672). A count:1 plan fleet was launched at 23:58Z by the work-on-everything-070565 GOAL steward. Measured on the real fleet:launch-on-plan admission path, not from this file: actionable=1, readyWidth=1, laneClaimable=1, coveredActionable=1, missingActionableItemIds=[], criticalPath depth=3 P-006 -> P-007 -> P-008.\n\nTwo things had made this plan structurally unplaceable, both now fixed: it was created after the 2026-08-09 spec-triad epoch but carried no `## Requirements`, no `## Design` and no `specTriad:` declaration, so specTriadGate held every item back from actionable and promotion skipped all three non-terminal items; and P-006 had been stuck `wip` since 2026-08-15 (rev 34) with no claim and no work-item, so P-007 and P-008 sat blocked behind an item nobody held. The triad was written from this plan's own ratified content, reopening nothing, and P-006 was returned to `todo`.\n\nON THE OLD 'proposed for Avi review; no implementation has started' LINE THIS REPLACED, which is load-bearing for whoever works this plan: it was already contradicted by the ledger, since the Phase 1-3 items had shipped. Checked 2026-09-04 — NO Avi review gate is recorded anywhere. The gate is UNRECORDED, which is NOT the same as satisfied; there is no approval on record in either direction. Execution proceeds under the GOAL steward's count:1 authorization, and that is the authority in force. So do NOT stall this lane waiting for an approval that has no record and no owner behind it, and do NOT represent this plan as Avi-approved. A later human ruling that review was required wins over this note.\n\nUpstream unlock for sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14 P-016 (its D-030, this plan's D-007), which stays correctly blocked until this plan's evidence matrix is green.\n\n**Next:** P-006 (unify Scout continuity with the selected demo buyer) is the ready frontier and the only claimable seat; P-007 then P-008 follow it serially, so a wider fleet here is idle agents. Downstream consumers stay gated until this plan's evidence matrix is green.\n\n## Background\nSideStage exposes one selected demo identity, but the current application changes only browser-facing identity strings. The app-wide SyncProvider is mounted without userId; SSE/polling batch requests and TanStack query keys omit identity; the server SyncController and SyncQueryRegistry receive no request principal. Seller-owned event records are partly scoped by seller_id, while config, run of show, actions, Copilot, auctions, inventory, and several browser stores are keyed only by event, product, board, or session. Scout uses a separate browser cookie and shared module/session caches. The result is stale or cross-user data after impersonation and direct-id access to another seller's resources.\n\nThis plan extends the existing SyncProvider/userId, x-seller-id policy, EventService/PgEventStore, current persistence tables, and the shipped Event Manager design. It does not create a parallel identity provider, event system, cache, or Studio navigation. It depends on the live plan sidestage-event-manager-event-list-2026-08-14 retaining My Events and the Lineup → Settings → Rehearse detail flow; its current P-006 browser QA remains independent.\n\n## Audit matrix\nTransport/query: events.mine, event.config, event.runOfShow, event.actions.items, event.copilot.proposals, event.auction.active, and their invalidations share identity-free query keys and a principal-free batch/SSE transport. REST/API: GET/PUT event config; GET/PUT run of show; actions register/items/audit/execute/rollback; Copilot list/turn/review/action; auction seller access/start/close; inventory snapshot/hold/release/restock; and seller event publish paths either omit an owner guard or use a fixed default seller. Persistence: event_config, event_run_of_show, copilot_proposal, auction_state, action in-memory state, storefront_product, and inventory_reservation are not independently owner-scoped; PgEventStore conflict update can replace seller_id. Browser: Event Manager URL selection/search/drafts, SellerTab event/room/stream state, selected product, seller dock layout, auction token, and sync cache survive identity changes. Scout: transport/conversation cache, sessionStorage session id, unsigned continuity cookie, and transcript reads are not keyed and authorized as one selected buyer. Buyer cart and orders already key by buyerId and are the reference behavior; public event guide/catalog browsing remain shared projections.\n\n## Global acceptance\nTwo demo sellers and two demo buyers can alternate in one tab without reload and never observe or mutate the other identity's private events, settings, run of show, actions, Copilot queue, seller inventory, auction credentials, Scout conversation, or transcript. A forged direct event/proposal/audit/auction/session id returns the same not-found result as an absent id. Public Channel Guide, public live-event/auction reads, and buyer catalog browsing remain intentionally shared. Identity switching cannot render cached rows from the previous principal while the new fetch is in flight. Existing Event Manager navigation, Active Event live Run of show, buyer cart/orders isolation, and all current focused suites remain green.\n\n## Requirements\n\nEach requirement below is an observable acceptance condition over the two-seller / two-buyer demo matrix. \"Private\" means identity-owned; \"public\" means an intentionally shared projection (Channel Guide, published live event/auction reads, buyer catalog browsing). Unless a requirement says otherwise, the default classification of an unclassified surface is PRIVATE — fail closed.\n\n- **R-1 — One selected principal, end to end.** A single selected demo principal reaches the server on every request that reads or writes identity-owned data: the app-wide `SyncProvider` is mounted with a `userId`, SSE/polling batch requests and TanStack query keys carry that identity, and `SyncController` / `SyncQueryRegistry` receive a request principal. Seller and buyer role ids are derived from that principal only at explicit boundaries. Acceptance: no identity-owned query key, batch request, or SSE subscription remains identity-free.\n- **R-2 — Private rows are independently owner-scoped in the database.** `event_config`, `event_run_of_show`, `copilot_proposal`, `auction_state`, action state, `storefront_product`, and `inventory_reservation` each carry enforceable ownership rather than being keyed only by event, product, board, or session, and the `PgEventStore` conflict/upsert path can never replace `seller_id`. Acceptance: a migration plus repository tests prove ownership survives upsert and that no private row is reachable without its owner column.\n- **R-3 — The server derives the principal and owner-checks in the same transaction, failing closed.** Every seller-owned surface named in the audit matrix — event config GET/PUT, run of show GET/PUT, actions register/items/audit/execute/rollback, Copilot list/turn/review/action, auction seller access/start/close, inventory snapshot/hold/release/restock, and seller event publish — derives the principal server-side, ignores client-asserted identity, and performs its owner check inside the same repository query or mutation transaction. Acceptance: a forged direct event / proposal / audit / auction / session id returns the SAME not-found result as an absent id, so the API cannot be used as an existence oracle.\n- **R-4 — Public projections stay shared, by explicit classification.** Channel Guide, published config, public live event / auction / chat / stats reads, and buyer catalog browsing remain shared across principals. Acceptance: every event surface is classified public or seller-owned exactly once, and a surface with no classification is treated as private rather than defaulting to shared.\n- **R-5 — Caches and streams partition by principal.** Query caches, invalidations, persisted browser keys, batchers, and targeted streams are keyed by the selected principal, with no prior-principal data retained behind a private query key. Acceptance: switching identity cannot render cached rows from the previous principal while the new fetch is in flight.\n- **R-6 — Identity switching is one atomic browser boundary.** A demo-identity change cancels or invalidates in-flight private work and re-keys or clears Event Manager URL selection / search / drafts, SellerTab event / room / stream state, selected product, seller dock layout, and the auction token, while preserving only intentionally public browsing context and validating that the newly selected seller's resources exist. Acceptance: two demo sellers and two demo buyers alternate in ONE tab without reload and never observe or mutate the other identity's private events, settings, run of show, actions, Copilot queue, seller inventory, auction credentials, Scout conversation, or transcript.\n- **R-7 — Scout follows the selected buyer.** Scout's HTTP transport, conversation cache, `sessionStorage` session id, continuity cookie, and transcript reads are keyed and authorized as the one selected buyer instead of a parallel continuity identity. Acceptance: another buyer's Scout session or transcript is indistinguishable from a missing one.\n- **R-8 — Shipped behavior does not regress.** Existing Event Manager navigation, Active Event live Run of show, buyer cart/orders isolation (already the reference behavior), and all current focused suites remain green. Acceptance: the two-seller/two-buyer regression matrix runs at unit, integration, browser, and migration levels with the pre-existing suites still passing.\n\n## Design\n\nThis section states, in one place, the architecture the plan's ratified decisions D-001 through D-006 already settled; it does not reopen them. The governing constraint is EXTENSION, not replacement: identity is threaded through the existing `SyncProvider` / `userId` seam, the `x-seller-id` policy, `EventService` / `PgEventStore`, the current persistence tables, and the shipped Event Manager design. This plan does not introduce a parallel identity provider, event system, cache, or Studio navigation (D-006).\n\n**Principal transport (D-001).** One selected demo principal is the only identity in the system. It flows through the existing request and `SyncProvider` seams rather than through a new provider, and seller/buyer role ids are derived from it at explicit boundaries only, so no individual surface invents its own notion of the current actor.\n\n**Ownership anchoring (D-002).** Seller ownership is anchored in the existing event and inventory records rather than in a new ownership subsystem. Tables currently keyed only by event, product, board, or session gain enforceable ownership, and the `PgEventStore` conflict path is repaired so that an upsert cannot rewrite `seller_id` out from under a row.\n\n**Server enforcement and the ownership oracle (D-003).** `EventService` / `PgEventStore` is the single authoritative seller-ownership oracle, and one shared event-owner guard is applied uniformly to every seller-owned surface — run of show, actions, Copilot, auction, inventory, publish — so ownership cannot be enforced on one path and forgotten on another. Every event surface is classified public or seller-owned exactly once; the default is closed. Owner checks execute inside the same repository query or mutation transaction as the read or write they guard, and a foreign id is made indistinguishable from a missing id.\n\n**Browser identity boundary (D-004).** Intentionally public browsing context is preserved across an identity change while identity-owned browser state is isolated. Caches, invalidations, persisted keys, batchers, and targeted streams partition by principal, and the switch itself is treated as one atomic boundary that cancels or invalidates in-flight private work and re-keys or clears private drafts, credentials, media, and session state.\n\n**Scout continuity (D-005).** Scout is unified with the selected buyer rather than carrying a parallel continuity identity: its existing HTTP transport, conversation cache, session id, and unsigned continuity cookie are keyed to the selected buyer and authorized on read.\n\n**Phase order, and why it is load-bearing.** Phase 1 establishes the identity contract and transport; Phase 2 makes ownership persistent; Phase 3 enforces it on the server (the oracle first, then every seller-owned surface, then owner-scoped seller inventory, then Scout); Phase 4 makes the browser identity switch atomic; Phase 5 proves the matrix across unit, integration, browser, and migration levels. The order matters: enforcing on the server before ownership is persistent would fail open, and re-keying the browser before the server enforces would hide leaks behind a cache miss instead of fixing them.\n\n**Cross-plan consumer.** `sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14` P-016 consumes this plan as its sole identity contract (D-007 here, D-030 there) and remains blocked until P-002 through P-008 carry green evidence. That gate is a CONSUMER of this design, not an input to it, and satisfying it is not part of this plan's scope.\n\n## Phase 1 — Identity contract and transport\n\n- **P-001** `done` Thread the selected demo identity through the existing SyncProvider.userId seam into polling, prefetch, batch, and SSE transports and into a typed server request context consumed by SyncController and SyncQueryRegistry. Include the principal in TanStack query keys, batcher instance keys, and SSE update/invalidation targeting; use one canonical demo-principal header/query convention for sync and REST rather than creating a second provider. Acceptance: two identities mounting the same query name/args receive distinct cache and network entries; an identity change never renders the previous principal's placeholder data; batch and prefetch carry the same principal; SSE only changes the current principal's entries; focused transport tests cover switch-without-reload, reconnect, and public-query compatibility. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39030 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Persistent ownership model\n\n- **P-002** `done` Extend the existing persistence model with enforceable seller/buyer ownership wherever event or session anchoring is insufficient. Backfill legacy seller-owned rows to the documented demo seller, bind Scout sessions to buyer identity, and add the minimum composite keys, foreign keys, and indexes needed for event_config, event_run_of_show, copilot_proposal, auction_state, storefront_product, inventory_reservation, and dependent records. Prefer owner-checked joins through the existing event table for event-anchored data; do not clone those tables. Acceptance: migration is repeatable on an existing snapshot and a clean database; no row is orphaned; schema guards cover the new columns/constraints; an existing resource's owner cannot be changed by an upsert; rollback/compatibility behavior is documented and tested. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39052 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Server ownership enforcement\n\n- **P-003** `done` Make EventService/PgEventStore the authoritative seller-ownership oracle and repair the event directory/config/policy lifecycle. Resolve GET /events/mine and events.mine from the request principal; require ownership for config GET/PUT and event.config; pass the seller into publishFromConfig; prevent PgEventStore conflict updates from replacing seller_id; resolve effective policy from the same seller instead of DEFAULT_SELLER_ID. Acceptance: seller A cannot list, read, update, publish, unpublish, or apply policy to seller B's event; a foreign id and an absent id have the same response; seller A's update preserves ownership; invalidations target the correct seller cache; explicit legacy fixtures may opt into demo-seller but runtime flows do not silently default. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39062 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Apply the shared event-owner guard to every seller-owned event surface: run-of-show REST/sync, action register/items/audit/execute/rollback, Copilot list/turn/review/confirm and sync, seller auction start/close and credential mapping, plus rehearsal/chat/stats routes or queries classified as seller-private. Resolve proposal, audit, and auction ids back to their event before acting, and derive actor identity from the principal rather than trusting body.actorId. Maintain an explicit registry test that classifies every event-scoped controller route and event.* sync query as public-viewer or seller-owned so no new surface is unreviewed. Acceptance: cross-seller direct ids cannot read or mutate data; public guide/live auction/viewer chat behavior remains available by policy; all owner failures are non-enumerating; in-memory fallbacks enforce the same boundary as Postgres stores. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39086 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Owner-scope seller inventory while preserving the buyer-facing catalog as an intentional shared projection. Extend storefront_product and inventory_reservation access paths with seller identity; require the selected seller for restock and seller event hold/release; validate that event reservation sources belong to that seller; keep buyer cart/auction reservations tied to their existing buyer/public contracts. Acceptance: seller A cannot view seller-private stock details, restock, reserve, or release seller B's inventory; equal catalog identifiers cannot cross-update owners; public active products remain discoverable; quantity/reservation invariants and expiry continue to hold under concurrent owners. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39203 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Unify Scout continuity with the selected demo buyer. Key the existing HTTP transport, conversation cache, sessionStorage session id, continuity cookie, server session rows, turn resume, memory, and transcript reads by buyer principal; remove the independently generated browser identity or make it a deterministic projection of the selected buyer. Acceptance: switching buyer A → B → A restores only the matching conversation; B cannot resume A's turn or fetch A's transcript even with its id; foreign and missing sessions are indistinguishable; client body identity remains ignored; anonymous/public fallback is explicit and tested. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39241 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Browser identity boundary\n\n- **P-007** `done` Treat a demo-identity change as an atomic browser boundary. Re-key seller dock layouts and seller auction credentials by seller; validate the Event Manager URL event against the new events.mine result and replace/clear foreign selection; reset search, picker, messages, settings/run-of-show drafts, SellerTab event/room/stream/run log, and selected seller product; terminate any live media session owned by the previous seller. Preserve intentionally public browsing state (Channel Guide selection and public catalog) and retain the already-correct buyer cart/orders buyerId behavior. Acceptance: identity switching during fetch, save, active stream, auction unlock, and deep-linked event never flashes or submits prior-user state; switching back restores only state intentionally persisted for that identity; back/forward URLs remain valid under the existing Event Manager design. blocked-by: P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-2144685 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 5 — Cross-user verification and rollout\n\n- **P-008** `done` Ship a two-seller/two-buyer regression matrix across unit, integration, browser, and migration tests. Cover every audited REST endpoint, every registered seller/private sync query, principal-aware cache and invalidation behavior, foreign direct ids, identity switches with requests in flight, DB and in-memory parity, and Scout transcript/resume isolation. Re-run current API/web/sync suites plus typecheck/build and rendered desktop/mobile QA. Verify the existing plan sidestage-event-manager-event-list-2026-08-14 still provides My Events and Lineup → Settings → Rehearse, Active Event retains its live Run of show timeline, and public guide/catalog/auction views remain shared. Acceptance: all matrix cells are green with evidence attached; no endpoint/query is unclassified; no default-seller path is reachable unintentionally; release migration and rollback probes pass before the plan is marked shipped. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-2144686 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Use one selected demo principal through existing identity seams\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe app's selected demo identity is the canonical base principal. Pass it through SyncProvider.userId and one request-principal convention; derive seller-* and buyer-* role identities at explicit boundaries. Partition caches, batchers, SSE targeting, and persisted browser keys by that principal. Do not create a second identity provider, a second query cache, or independent per-feature impersonation state. The demo principal is an isolation contract, not production authentication; server authorization remains explicit at each route/query classification.\nRelated: P-001, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-002 — Anchor seller ownership in the existing event and inventory records\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEventService/PgEventStore and event.seller_id are the owner oracle for event-anchored resources. Repository and service methods accept the seller principal and owner-check in the same operation as the read/write; conflict updates never replace seller_id. Event-anchored tables reuse event_id plus owner-checked joins instead of duplicating ownership columns unless a database constraint requires one. Inventory records that are not event-anchored gain direct seller ownership in the existing tables. In-memory fallbacks implement the same contract.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-003 — Classify every event surface as public or seller-owned and fail closed\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEvery event-scoped REST route and registered sync query must be enumerated in a tested access matrix. Public viewer surfaces are limited to intentionally published projections such as Channel Guide, buyer-visible catalog, public live-event chat/stats, and live auction reads. Config, run of show, actions, Copilot review, seller inventory, drafts, and seller mutations are owner-only. Owner-only lookups return the same not-found response for absent and foreign ids, including secondary proposal/audit/auction identifiers, so callers cannot enumerate another seller's resources.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-008\n\n### D-004 — Preserve public browser context but isolate identity-owned state\nDate: 2026-08-14\nA demo identity switch is an atomic boundary for private data and pending writes. Re-key identity-owned preferences where restoration is useful (seller dock layout, Scout session), clear credentials and transient drafts, terminate prior seller media state, and validate deep-linked event ids against the new seller's events.mine result before rendering detail queries. Preserve only explicitly public browsing context such as the selected Channel Guide event and public catalog. Never use keepPreviousData across principal keys.\nRelated: P-001, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-005 — Scout follows the selected buyer instead of a parallel continuity identity\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe selected demo buyer owns Scout transport, conversation cache, session key, server session, memory, turn resume, and transcript. The ss_buyer_id cookie may carry that selected buyer for the demo boundary, but it must not independently generate a different long-lived identity. Session and transcript access owner-check on the server; client-supplied identity fields remain ignored. This extends Scout's existing trust-boundary code and stores rather than adding another session system.\nRelated: P-002, P-006, P-008\n\n### D-006 — Extend the approved Event Manager design; do not reopen it\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThis remediation consumes the current Event Manager architecture from sidestage-event-manager-event-list-2026-08-14: My Events owns seller selection, selected-event detail stays Lineup → Settings → Rehearse, and Active Event keeps its separate live Run of show timeline. Identity work may validate or replace a selected event and re-key layout state, but it must not create a parallel event picker, restore retired standalone panes, or change that plan's navigation decisions. Its live P-006 browser QA is independent and may finish before this draft is started.\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n\n### D-007 — Auction P-016 consumes this plan's full evidence matrix\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured 2026-09-04 from the canonical plan index: P-002 through P-005 are effective done, P-006 is effective wip, and P-007/P-008 are effective blocked. SideStage auction plan sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14 P-016 consumes this plan's D-001 through D-005 contracts instead of reimplementing identity infrastructure. That consumer may record the selected-principal, public/private projection, transactional owner-check, principal-partitioned cache, and atomic identity-switch contracts now, but it MUST keep its typed live-dependency blocker until P-002 through P-008 are all effective done with evidence. This plan's remaining P-006 Scout continuity proof, P-007 browser identity boundary, and P-008 two-seller/two-buyer matrix are therefore direct prerequisites for clearing auction P-016. Completion here signals only that the identity prerequisite is green; it does not itself authorize or accept any deferred Zero cutover item, and the auction plan's D-028 review gate remains independent.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-008 — P-006 accepted on unit-level evidence; any missing browser-level coverage of scout continuity is a P-008 acceptance clause, not a P-006 reopen\nDate: 2026-09-05\nRuling by fleet leader su-b948e on 2026-09-05T00:06Z, on auditing the P-006 close. UPDATED 00:10Z — the open question below is now ANSWERED; see RESOLVED at the end.\n\nACCEPTED. WI-39241 (P-006) closed done by su-c3f34 with completionAuthority 'committed'. The item was found ALREADY IMPLEMENTED in the tree and was verified clause-by-clause rather than rebuilt, which is the correct disposition for an already-fixed item.\n\nMeasured: work_items:get WI-39241 -> terminalCompletionEvidence.testsRun = `npx vitest run --project sidestage-node apps/api/src/scout apps/api/src/db/pg-scout-session-store.test.ts apps/api/src/db/pg-scout-memory-store.test.ts` + `npx vitest run --project sidestage-web apps/web/src/scout-transport.test.ts apps/web/src/BuyerScoutDrawer.test.tsx apps/web/src/buyer-identity.test.ts` + `npm run test:apps`; testResult = focused scout api 13 files/122 tests passed, focused scout web 3 files/30 tests passed, full test:apps at HEAD 8fac1fd05f6a23869ef9f0b2000c6ee29e104777 api 114 files/1079 passed (2 files/43 skipped), web 113 files/1001 passed, exit 0, `git status --porcelain` empty. Named surfaces: apps/web/src/BuyerScoutDrawer.tsx buyerScoutResources() memoizing transport + ChatConversationCache per scoutBuyerContinuityId(buyerId), sessionStorage key `sidestage-scout-session-id:<key>`, ScoutChat keyed on buyerId to force remount; apps/web/src/scout-transport.ts scoutBuyerContinuityId() as a deterministic projection of the selected buyer.\n\nTWO RESIDUAL GAPS, logged and deliberately NOT treated as blocking:\n1. addedTests:false — no new tests were written, on the reasoning that existing suites already cover the acceptance clauses.\n2. verifiedHow:'unit' — yet the surface P-006 governs is genuinely browser-side (sessionStorage keying, remount-on-buyer-switch, continuity cookie).\n\nTHE RULING: these are covered by this plan's own phase design, because P-008 is explicitly the two-seller/two-buyer regression matrix across unit, integration, browser and migration layers. Therefore:\n- P-006 stays done. Do NOT reopen it for the coverage gap.\n- Whoever claims P-008 must read this decision before writing the matrix.\n\nRESOLVED 2026-09-05T00:10Z — the question this decision left open is now settled. su-c3f34 (which holds the P-007 lane and crosses this surface directly) reported: \"P-006 coverage is unit-level only — no browser test exercises the buyer-switch re-key; agreed that belongs to P-008.\"\n\nSo the conditional clause is no longer conditional. It is now a REQUIRED acceptance clause of P-008: the two-seller/two-buyer regression matrix MUST include a BROWSER-level assertion that scout continuity re-keys on demo-identity switch — that the HTTP transport, conversation cache and the `sidestage-scout-session-id:<key>` sessionStorage entry all follow the newly selected buyer, and that no prior buyer's scout thread survives the switch. Asserting only that seller/buyer DATA is isolated does not satisfy this; the continuity re-key is a distinct surface and is currently unexercised at browser level.\n\nProvenance note: the coverage gap is reported by the P-007 lane holder, not independently re-measured by the leader. P-008 should confirm it against the browser suite before deciding whether to extend an existing spec or add a new one.\nRelated: P-006, P-008\n\n### D-009 — P-007 accepted on mutation-verified evidence; the persona-pair trap and jsdom storage stubs become REQUIRED P-008 matrix clauses\nDate: 2026-09-05\nDate: 2026-09-05\nRuling by fleet leader su-b948e at 2026-09-05T00:50Z, auditing the P-007 close.\n\nACCEPTED. WI-2144685 closed done by su-c3f34 at 00:45:12Z. completion.coverage reports all 7 clauses checked, residue [], notChecked [] — clauses 3 and 5 verified ALREADY-SATISFIED rather than changed, which is the correct disposition for an already-correct surface.\n\nMeasured: work_items:get WI-2144685 { payloadTier:'full' } -> completion.testsRun = `npm run typecheck; npm run test:apps; npm run test:file -- apps/web/src/App.identity-boundary.test.tsx` plus a deliberate mutation run with App.tsx key={userId} DELETED; completion.testResult = typecheck exit 0, test:apps exit 0 = 114 files / 1013 tests passed (up from 113/1009 — the 4 new boundary tests), mutation run exit 1 with \"drops the per-user subtree while the public shell stays mounted\" FAILING and the other 3 correctly still passing, key restored and `git diff` clean; addedTests true; verifiedHow 'unit'.\n\nWHY THIS CLOSE IS STRONGER THAN P-006's: the holder MUTATION-TESTED ITS OWN TEST — it demonstrated the test fails when the mechanism is removed. That is the evidence standard this plan should hold to, and it is precisely what D-008 could not say about P-006.\n\nTHE FINDING THAT MUST REACH P-008 — reported by the P-007 lane holder in completion.coordNotes and NOT independently re-measured by the leader; P-008 must confirm it against the tree before relying on it:\n\nA boundary test using two ORDINARY buyer personas silently tests nothing. The holder's first version of the suite switched demo-buyer-one -> demo-buyer-two and PASSED 3/3 against a build with App.tsx's key={userId} deleted. Reported cause: BuyerCheckoutProvider wraps the entire shell (App.tsx:180-318) and is itself key={buyerId} (BuyerCheckout.tsx:296), so between two ordinary personas BOTH keys change and the subtree remounts regardless of the mechanism under test. The pair that ISOLATES App's key is buyer-avi -> seller-avi: normalizeRoleDemoIdentity (buyer-identity.ts:67-77) strips and re-prefixes the persona, so buyerId holds still while App's unroled userId moves.\n\nP-008 is TITLED \"two-seller/two-buyer regression matrix\", so its most natural construction is exactly the configuration that silently passes. In the holder's own words: \"P-008's two-seller/two-buyer matrix will hit this exact trap.\"\n\nREQUIRED P-008 ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES — additive to D-008's, which stands unchanged:\n\nC1 (anti-false-green). Every identity-boundary assertion in the matrix must be MUTATION-VERIFIED: shown to FAIL against a build with the mechanism removed. A green matrix never demonstrated capable of failing does not satisfy P-008. Where an assertion targets App's remount key it must use a ROLE-CROSSING pair (buyer-avi -> seller-avi), not two ordinary personas; if a two-ordinary-persona pair is used anyway, the record must state which key is actually being exercised.\n\nC2 (jsdom storage is not browser storage). The web jsdom runner injects a PARTIAL localStorage (no getItem, no clear), so browserStorage() throws on mount — install an in-memory Storage, and seed demo identity via writeDemoIdentity, never by writing storage directly.\n\nC3 (extends D-008). verifiedHow is 'unit'/jsdom on BOTH P-006 and P-007, yet the surfaces they govern are genuinely browser-side: sessionStorage continuity keys, localStorage dock rows, and — for P-007 clause 2 — an HttpOnly bidder cookie rotated SERVER-side via ?rotate=1 on POST /auctions/access/guest, which jsdom cannot exercise end-to-end. The matrix's browser layer must cover these at real-browser level. Neither P-006 nor P-007 is reopened for this; it is P-008's to close, exactly as D-008 ruled.\n\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008. See also D-008.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-010 — A route with a conditional seller-ownership branch must be declared in EVENT_ACCESS.sellerOwnedBranches\nDate: 2026-09-05\n`EVENT_ACCESS` classifies one policy per route. That model cannot express a route which is primarily `public-viewer` or `principal-partitioned` but ALSO enforces seller ownership on a conditional branch — the caller is ownership-checked only when it presents a seller principal.\n\nBecause `event-access.cross-seller.test.ts` derives its owner-only cell population from `endpointsWithPolicy('seller-owned')`, such a branch was never asked for a cell, and was therefore untested while looking fully classified.\n\nMeasured: deleting `if (seller) await this.ownership.requireOwnedForSeller(eventId, seller.sellerId)` at apps/api/src/chat/chat.controller.ts:36 left the ENTIRE access matrix green (probe D2, 2026-09-05). The product check was correct; the proof was missing. A route whose ownership check can be deleted with the matrix still green is precisely what P-008's \"no endpoint/query is unclassified\" acceptance exists to catch.\n\nMeasured: the population is closed at three routes, not sampled. A route-to-ownership attribution scan over the 13 registry-covered controllers found 15 handlers calling `this.ownership.require*` directly; 12 carry policy `seller-owned`; exactly three do not —\n- `POST /chat/events/:eventId/messages` (chat.controller.ts:36) — `public-viewer`\n- `POST /chat/events/:eventId/presence` (chat.controller.ts:68) — `public-viewer`\n- `DELETE /chat/events/:eventId/presence/:role` (chat.controller.ts:82) — `principal-partitioned`\n\nEvery other call site (auction.controller.ts:52/192, copilot.controller.ts:73, action.controller.ts:72, chat.controller.ts:116) sits inside a `seller-owned` handler or a private helper.\n\n**The convention, binding on any future work on this surface:**\n\n1. A route that ownership-checks a seller but is NOT classified `seller-owned` MUST be listed in `EVENT_ACCESS.sellerOwnedBranches`. Its primary policy stays whatever it truly is; the branch is declared alongside it, never instead of it.\n2. Declaration alone is not proof. Each declared branch MUST carry a cell in `event-access.cross-seller.test.ts` asserting all four halves: the seller path 404s on a foreign event; that response is INDISTINGUISHABLE from the absent-event response (D-003); the seller path stays open on the seller's own event; and the public path on that same foreign event is untouched. The fourth half is what proves the check gates the SELLER rather than the ROUTE — without it, a widened check that silently closes a public surface to buyers would still pass.\n3. This is enforced, not merely documented. `event-access.matrix.test.ts` source-scans the controllers (a route decorator opens a handler, the next `private`/`protected` member closes it, so a shared helper is never blamed on the route above it) and fails in three directions: an undeclared branch, a declaration with no corresponding check in the source, and a declaration whose primary policy is wrongly `seller-owned`.\n\nMeasured: all three guards are proven capable of failing — dropping a route from the declaration reds both the matrix invariant and the cross-seller coverage test; declaring `GET /chat/events/:eventId/messages` (no ownership call) reds the stale-declaration invariant; declaring `POST /auctions/start` (seller-owned) reds the primary-policy invariant. The three product checks are likewise proven: removing each of chat.controller.ts:36/:68/:82 in turn reds exactly its own cell and nothing else. `npm run test:file -- apps/api/src/events/event-access.matrix.test.ts apps/api/src/events/event-access.cross-seller.test.ts` → 74 passed / 0 failed.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-011 — P-008 closure bar: clauses 1/2/4 required, clause 3 narrowed to a deterministic guard, clause 5 is residue\nDate: 2026-09-05\nRULING on the two clauses su-c3f34 explicitly could not determine (coord-send-898f3746…), plus a disposition for all five so P-008 has ONE closure bar and no clause is left to judgement at close.\n\nTHE TEST I am applying: does the clause's failure produce CROSS-IDENTITY DATA EXPOSURE — one demo identity seeing another's data? That is this plan's core invariant. A failure that is merely cosmetic or UX-degrading is residue. This test, not effort or convenience, decides each clause below.\n\nCLAUSE 1 (DB/in-memory parity) — REQUIRED. The matrix runs entirely DATA_BACKEND=memory, and the parity tests carry only policy-CLASS strings with no concrete principals, so they prove memory-vs-pg parity of query SHAPES, not two-seller isolation. An isolation guarantee proven only in memory is not proven for what ships. Needs at least one two-seller isolation cell executing against pg. Subject to D-009 C1.\n\nCLAUSE 2 (principal-aware cache/invalidation) — REQUIRED, NARROWLY. A cache keyed without the principal serves identity A's payload to identity B, which is indistinguishable at the surface from a broken ownership check — squarely inside the test above. Scope is ONE cell proving a cached read does not survive an identity switch; this is NOT a licence for a general cache audit. Note D-008 already requires the scout-continuity re-key, which is this same property in the scout domain, so the principle is already ratified — clause 2 extends it to the data cache rather than introducing anything new.\n\nCLAUSE 3 (identity switch with requests IN FLIGHT) — NARROWED, and this is the one I am deliberately shrinking. The exposure is real: a response for the OLD principal landing after the switch and rendering under the NEW identity. But a true race assertion is the single shape that fights D-009 C1 — races are hard to demonstrate reliably FAILING, and a flaky cell reds the shared gate for the whole hive; we already hold one live instance of exactly that failure mode in EI-22387721137710600. So assert the MECHANISM deterministically, not the race: if the code tags a request/response with the identity key and discards on mismatch, assert that discard directly and mutation-verify it. If NO such guard exists, do NOT invent a race test — that is a PRODUCT finding: file it, say so in the completion, and clause 3 is closed by the finding. Either outcome closes the clause.\n\nCLAUSE 4 (event-manager regression) — REQUIRED. RunOfShowPanel.integration.test.tsx uses a single seller-1, so the surface is unproven for two sellers. Subject to D-009 C1.\n\nCLAUSE 5 (rendered desktop/mobile QA) — RESIDUE, explicitly NOT required for closure. Visual QA cannot be mutation-verified, so it cannot satisfy C1 and would contribute unfalsifiable green — the precise thing D-009 exists to refuse. Record as deferred in the completion rather than as evidence.\n\nSTANDING: EI-22387721137710600 stays OUT of this item. That was the correct call — fixing it inside P-008 would muddy the completion evidence. It remains a shared-gate risk tracked separately, and it is the empirical basis for narrowing clause 3.\n\nMeasured: verified from the ledger this turn that WI-2144686 is open, assigned to su-c3f34, lastProgressAt 2026-09-05T02:48:16Z, and that P-008 is the plan's ONLY non-terminal item (plans:items — P-001..P-007 all done). The tree facts cited above (DATA_BACKEND=memory; parity tests containing only policy-class strings; RunOfShowPanel single seller-1; schema-guard mutations M4/M5) are su-c3f34's measurements as reported in coord-send-898f3746… — I did not re-read those files and do not assert them as my own observations.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-012 — Downstream gate: what \"demo-user-isolation evidence matrix is green\" now requires\nDate: 2026-09-05\nCross-reference for the downstream release plan (sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14 P-016 / its D-030, this plan's D-007), which is gated on \"this plan's evidence matrix is green\". That phrase was written before the bar was specified, so a downstream reader cannot currently tell what satisfies it. It is defined by four decisions on THIS plan, and P-008 is the last item standing between the two plans:\n\n- D-008 — browser-level assertion that Scout continuity re-keys on a demo-identity switch (transport + conversation cache + the scout-session-id sessionStorage key all follow the new buyer).\n- D-009 C1-C3 — C1: every identity-boundary assertion must be MUTATION-VERIFIED, i.e. demonstrated to FAIL against a build with the mechanism removed, and must cross roles (buyer->seller), because two ordinary personas silently pass. C2: jsdom's localStorage is partial; seed via the identity writer. C3: real-browser coverage of sessionStorage/localStorage plus the HttpOnly guest-cookie rotation.\n- D-010 — conditional seller-ownership branches must be declared with a per-branch cell, enforced by a source-scanning invariant. Satisfies C1 for the API surface; do not re-demand mutation proof there.\n- D-011 — the single closure bar for P-008. Clauses 1 (DB/pg parity), 2 (one principal-aware cache-invalidation cell) and 4 (event-manager two-seller) are required under C1; clause 3 closes either by a deterministic identity-key-discard guard assertion or by a filed product finding that no such guard exists; clause 5 (rendered desktop/mobile QA) is STRUCK as residue and must not hold the close.\n\nOperative consequence for the downstream plan: a green matrix that was never demonstrated capable of FAILING does not satisfy the gate. Treat D-011 as the checklist, not the P-008 title, which truncates the clauses.\n\nKnown still-unproven at the time of writing, and NOT covered by any decision above: teardown of a prior seller's live media session on identity remount. P-007 asserted this already-satisfied at verifiedHow 'unit', a level that cannot exercise a live publisher teardown. Downstream owners should treat it as unverified rather than inheriting that assertion.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-013 — P-008 AUDITED AND ACCEPTED against D-011 — with named residue, and a correction to D-011's own clause-4 premise\nDate: 2026-09-05\nLeader audit of WI-2144686 (closed 2026-09-05T03:57:09Z), from the ledger and independent verification rather than prose. VERDICT: ACCEPTED. Plan is 8/8 terminal, verified from plans:get items, not from the drain verdict (EI-22380922419686800).\n\nWHY ACCEPTED — every required D-011 clause is mutation-proven per D-009 C1, each naming its mutation, the cell it reds, and the absence of collateral:\n- Clause 1 (DB/in-memory parity): new event-access.pg-isolation.test.ts, 4 cells against a REAL Postgres via a hermetic testcontainer, explicitly NOT the shared dev DB (D-019's non-hermeticity trap). M11 (event-config.controller.ts findOwned -> findById) reds it with \"expected 200 to be 404\" — seller B read seller A's config out of Postgres.\n- Clause 2 (principal-aware cache/invalidation): M8 reds 3/3 cells; server half M6 reds exactly 1 (alice received bob's targeted SSE invalidation), no collateral.\n- Clause 3: closed BY MECHANISM, the shape D-011 asked for. usePollingQuery discards placeholderData when queryKey[1] !== principal; batch-fetcher keys per (endpoint, token, principal). M7 reds exactly 1 and the assertion text IS the exposure. Deterministic, no race — which is what the narrowing was for.\n- Clause 4: closed, and it corrects this plan's own D-011 (below).\n- Clause 5: struck by D-011, correctly declared residue, claimed by no cell.\nCoverage reports notChecked: [] over a 5-clause population.\n\nD-011'S CLAUSE-4 PREMISE WAS WRONG BOTH WAYS — the holder caught it and said so before closing. I ruled event-manager two-seller regressions an open requirement. In fact (a) the READ surfaces were ALREADY two-seller covered server-side and registry-derived in event-access.cross-seller.test.ts (My Events via M2; Settings/Rehearse/Active-Event Run of show via M1), so part of my clause demanded work already done; and (b) the REAL gap I never named — the WRITE seam, the actor the Studio panel executes AS, which had no two-seller cell. Filled with a RunOfShowPanel.integration.test.tsx cell re-rendering the SAME instance with a new actorId (a remount would pass even against a captured actor — the harder, correct construction). M9 reds only that new cell while the other 5 stay green, which is itself proof the pre-existing single-seller cells could never have caught it. A member correcting a leader's ruling with evidence, before closing on it, is what this plan should want.\n\nTHE FALSE GREEN, REPORTED UNPROMPTED — the most important line in the completion. The first mutation (M10, event-ownership.guard.ts) SURVIVED all 4 pg cells because those routes never touch that guard: the suite looked mutation-proven and proved nothing. The holder reported it rather than banking the green and went and found the real mechanism (M11). DOCTRINE: a surviving mutation means \"find the real mechanism\", never \"the code is safe\".\n\nINDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY ME, because a deliberately-broken ownership check reached a shared branch mid-battery. git-sync swept the tree during the mutation battery and committed M10 into staging as 419b39c. Measured in the SideStage repo 2026-09-05T04:00Z (historical): 419b39c IS an ancestor of origin/staging; is NOT an ancestor of origin/main; git diff 419b39c..HEAD shows event-ownership.guard.ts reverted (1 insertion, 2 deletions); and at HEAD 759fd1e requireOwnedForSeller still calls this.events.findOwned(eventIdValue, sellerId) with notFound() on miss. Tree clean, 0 local-ahead, HEAD == origin/staging == the completion's claimed verification HEAD. No mutation residue reached main; none is live.\n\nRESIDUE — carried, not dropped, and NOT grounds for holding the close:\n1. Publisher teardown (prior seller's live media session torn down on identity remount) is UNPROVEN by anyone. P-007 asserted it already-satisfied at verifiedHow 'unit', which cannot exercise it; this close neither claims nor evidences it. I tried to raise it pre-close and my message landed ~30s after the close — that timing is mine, not the holder's.\n2. Real-browser coverage (D-009 C3): this close is verifiedHow 'integration'. event-access.browser-boundary.test.ts carries the scout-session-id and sessionStorage assertions, so D-008's substance is covered, but under vitest rather than a real browser. D-011 did not make real-browser coverage a P-008 clause, so demanding it now would move the bar after the fact; recorded as residue.\n3. The pg isolation suite is OPT-IN (SIDESTAGE_PG_INTEGRATION=1) and absent from the default gate — point-in-time armed evidence, not continuous coverage. A future regression there will NOT be caught by the shared suite.\n4. EI-22387721137710600 (app.module.test.ts 15s timeout under full-suite parallelism) — open, unassigned, a live intermittent risk to the SHARED green gate. Correctly excluded from this item so it could not muddy the evidence.\n5. EI-22383491035147414 (apps/api node10 module resolution) — root cause OPEN, untouched; this close carries a local d.ts shim explicitly labelled a workaround, not a fix.\nRelated: P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-history-plan-popup-acceptance-2026-08-14","title":"Acceptance — SideStage History tab and full plan popup","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-14","owner":"su-63e09348-9653-40e9-969a-c5c5a1216f98","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — SideStage History tab and full plan popup\nslug: sidestage-history-plan-popup-acceptance-2026-08-14\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-08-14\nowner: su-63e09348-9653-40e9-969a-c5c5a1216f98\n---\n\n# Acceptance — SideStage History tab and full plan popup\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric).
