Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nGrades the SHIPPED plan sidestage-test-tab-rehearsals-2026-08-13 against the outcome it existed to produce: a host can find out, before going live, whether their event will actually hold up — and can trust the answer because it came from the real services rather than from fixtures or from a checkmark nothing measured.\n\nGrade against the running code in ~/.papercusp/hives/sidestage (NOT the papercusp staging tree). The repo gate is `npm run check` at the root (typecheck across all four workspaces + both vitest suites). Read plan decisions D-001 and D-002 before grading: two criteria below exist to check that those rulings were honoured rather than quietly reversed.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-page-design-audit-mockups-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage per-page design audit and responsive mockups","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage per-page design audit and responsive mockups\nslug: sidestage-page-design-audit-mockups-2026-08-14\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-08-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\nAudit the six current SideStage top-level pages, define a shared redesign system, deliver one report and one responsive mockup per page, then validate and browser-verify the complete artifact.\n\n## Scope\n\nBuyer, Orders, Seller, Build History, Config, and Test. Deliverables live as a standalone review artifact; production UI source is not changed.\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n- The review artifact covers Buyer, Orders, Seller, Build History, Config, and Test, with an explicit audit and responsive mockup for every page at desktop and mobile sizes.\n- All six page directions share one coherent SideStage system: preserve the shipped R3 Ticket cream/ink/red/yellow identity, clearly separate buyer and operator navigation, expose one dominant next action, and pair status color with readable text.\n- Desktop layouts remain readable inside a 1280px content frame; below 760px, multi-column controls collapse to one focused panel with a compact mode switch or selector.\n- Every applicable active registry component is reused. Patterns absent from the registry remain semantic layout primitives in the design IR instead of becoming duplicate components.\n- The Test page is a compact sidebar-driven testing workbench modeled on Papercusp's Testing page: persistent suite navigation on desktop, a compact selector or drawer on mobile, dense status rows, and one focused detail/run pane.\n- The final design specs validate, and the complete standalone artifact is browser-verified at desktop and mobile viewports. Production SideStage UI source remains unchanged by this plan.\n\n## Design\n\nThe deliverable is a standalone review artifact, not a production rewrite. A shared design layer carries the R3 Ticket palette, typography, spacing, readable 1280px frame, role-separated navigation, dominant-action hierarchy, and text-plus-color status language across all six page specs. It reuses action.primary, action.secondary, control.select, control.checkbox, and feedback.banner from the active registry; cards, tabs, tables, progress, navigation, accordion, and empty states are represented as semantic IR layout patterns because the registry has no matching component.\n\nEach page pairs a concise audit with one responsive mockup built from that shared layer. Desktop mockups retain the page-specific information architecture; below 760px they reduce competing columns to a focused panel and compact mode control. The Test page deliberately diverges from large dashboard cards into a Testing-page-style sidebar workbench with dense suite rows and a single detail/run pane. The settled trade-off is to preserve SideStage's distinctive shipped identity while improving hierarchy and responsiveness, and to avoid inventing registry components or touching production UI until the artifact is reviewed. Schema validation and browser verification close the artifact.\n\n## Phase — Audit and delivery\n\n- **P-001** `done` Inspect all six current SideStage pages at desktop and mobile sizes. importance: high — note: ← WI-38720 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Search the active design registry and define the shared redesign system. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-38721 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Create six per-page design reports. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-38722 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Create six responsive page mockups in a standalone review artifact. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-38723 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Validate design specs and browser-verify the finished artifact. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-38737 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Shared redesign system and registry reuse\nDate: 2026-08-14\nKeep the shipped R3 Ticket palette and its warm cream/ink/red/yellow identity, but tighten hierarchy and role separation. Reuse every applicable registry component: action.primary, action.secondary, control.select, control.checkbox, and feedback.banner. The active react-tailwind registry contains only those five entries; cards, tabs, tables, progress, navigation, accordion, and empty-state patterns therefore remain semantic layout primitives in the IR rather than new registry components. Across all six pages: group buyer vs operator navigation, surface one dominant next action, show status with text plus color, constrain desktop content to a readable 1280px frame, and replace multi-column controls with one active panel plus a compact mode switch below 760px.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Test page must use a compact sidebar-driven workbench\nDate: 2026-08-14\nOwner correction, verbatim intent: the SideStage Test page is a testing page, so it must be compact and easy to navigate with a sidebar. Use Papercusp’s existing Testing page as the interaction/layout reference. Replace the earlier large-card vertical dashboard direction: persistent test-suite navigation on desktop, compact suite selector/drawer on mobile, dense status rows, and one focused detail/run pane.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-public-release-testing-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage public-release testing campaign — pass the rubric, ship with confidence","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage public-release testing campaign — pass the rubric, ship with confidence\nslug: sidestage-public-release-testing-2026-08-14\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nExecute a full release-readiness test campaign over SideStage (prod = https://sidestage.buyrestart.com; repo = the sidestage hive tree) such that a PASSING grade on the companion rubric `release-readiness-sidestage-2026-08-14` means the app is ready for public release. [owner:Avi 2026-08-14]. Scope: the web app (Buyer/Seller/Config/Test tabs) + API + deploy path. The mobile apps ship on their own plans and are OUT of this campaign's gate. shop.buyrestart.com is a separate project (owner-ruled 2026-08-14) and is excluded.\n\n## Now\n\nPlan authored; rubric release-readiness-sidestage-2026-08-14 proposed alongside. Items are executable test lanes, parallel-safe except the fix loop and the final independent grade. Each lane produces CONCRETE evidence (commands, outputs, screenshots, latency numbers) parked on its work-item; every red routes through the fix loop before grading. Fleet ss-release-campaign (gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh, default account, visible desktop) executes it; leader su-c18ba.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Evidence per lane is concrete — commands run, outputs, screenshots, measured numbers; never \"looked fine\".\n- Every red found is filed as a work-item with a repro, fixed, and its lane re-run green before the grade.\n- The final grade is emitted by a NON-implementer of the tested surfaces via scorecards:emit; grader ≠ campaign author.\n- Prod checks run against the LIVE deployed instance; clean-clone checks run from a fresh clone OUTSIDE the shared tree.\n\n## Design\n\nHow the campaign executes — the method behind the lanes:\n\n- **API lanes** (buyer/seller flows, data integrity): drive prod endpoints with curl/scripted HTTP against https://sidestage.buyrestart.com; assert on response bodies + persistent effects (orders persisted, holds released). Square = sandbox credentials only.\n- **UI lanes** (browse/search, seller console, design integrity, console errors): ISOLATED playwright-core Chromium contexts — the shared verdict daemon is unsafe for concurrent prod QA (EI-20413679401930426 precedent); DOMContentLoaded + explicit ready selectors, never networkidle (EI-20415861399635845). Screenshots to /tmp/ss-campaign/<lane>/ and attached to completions.\n- **Clean-clone lane**: fresh git clone of github.com/Papercusp/sidestage into a throwaway dir OUTSIDE the shared trees; README-only command path; versions recorded.\n- **Judge/load/latency lane**: the app's own Test tab drives the deterministic judge + load rehearsal; research latency measured from timestamped API calls (sub-2s budget).\n- **Guardrail battery**: scripted adversarial inputs through the copilot seam; every attempt's server-side verdict + audit row captured.\n- **Fix loop**: red → work-item with repro → fix in the HIVE tree (~/.papercusp/hives/sidestage) → lane re-run green. No workaround closes a lane.\n- **Grade**: scorecards:emit on release-readiness-sidestage-2026-08-14 by a non-implementer, evidence per criterion; PASS = every criterion healthy.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — test lanes (parallel)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Clean-clone reviewer rehearsal: fresh clone OUTSIDE the shared tree → README-only path (npm install, npm run dev, npm test) reaches a working app; npm run check + npm run build green; CI (ci.yml) green at HEAD. Evidence: full command transcript + versions. (PRD success criterion 1) importance: high — note: ← WI-38793 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Buyer loop E2E on PROD: typo-tolerant search + browse → Channel Guide (thumbnails render) → join room → live chat → hold item (availability decrements, idempotent, releases correctly) → auction bid → close → winner order retains reservation → Square-sandbox checkout incl. box-packing shipping → order persists with status; demo impersonation with any free-text id. Evidence: screenshots + API responses per step. importance: high — note: ← WI-38794 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Seller loop E2E on PROD: create event with thumbnail (appears in buyer guide — EI-20426845001666103 regression), stream via MediaMTX, transcript product-mention drives on-deck, copilot suggestions carry labelled grounding sources, approve/edit/skip, guarded actions (push/swap/markdown/stock-adjust) leave audit records, markdown respects cap + floors; dockview layouts drag/resize/persist/reset. importance: high — note: ← WI-38795 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Guardrail adversarial battery: scripted attempts to violate price floors/markdown cap, claim phantom inventory, hit buyer-sensitive topics, break declared tone — every one blocked SERVER-SIDE pre-send; uncertain replies stay in review; every guarded action leaves a complete audit row; rollback path exercised once. (PRD req 2 + depth req 5) importance: high — note: ← WI-38796 done\n- **P-005** `done` Judge + load + latency thresholds: Test-tab judge passes threshold on all 4 dimensions (grounding, policy, price-correctness, tone); load rehearsal at N-user × M-msg/s covers all scripted scenario kinds green; on-demand product research latency measured against the sub-2-second budget with tracking visible. (PRD reqs 4+5, success criterion 3) importance: high — note: D-023 accepted on exact public SHA 78558bbf181e26df6b26d765061a1355df81b60b: immutable full gate green; exact-SHA health, six real catalog rows, six grounded Scout products, 12ms API latency; visible 161ms within sub-2s status with verified catalog citation and clean console; hygiene clean.\n- **P-006** `done` Data integrity + no-dummy-data sweep: prod serves the real catalog (Typesense search + SQL fallback verified by degrading one path in staging); availability always derived from reservations (attempt an oversell, must fail); config/policy round-trips persist; NO dummy/placeholder data on any surface (P-111 standard); event directory consistent with event configs. importance: high — note: ← WI-38798 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Design + responsiveness integrity: all four tabs match approved designs on R3 tokens (qa-sweep drift oracle clean); dockview chrome correct; responsive at phone/tablet/desktop widths; zero console errors across both loops; retheme D-006 caveat re-checked. — note: ← WI-38799 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Ops readiness: deploy.sh dry-run + real deploy reproducible green; /healthz + .deployed-sha correct; one rollback exercised and timed; docs current — submission.md live-URL line updated (found stale in the 2026-08-14 spec audit); zero OPEN critical/major bugs against prod surfaces at cut time. — note: ← WI-38933 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — fix loop + gate\n\n- **P-009** `done` Fix loop: every red from the lanes above filed as a work-item with repro, fixed, lane re-run green; no lane closes on a workaround; find→fix summary appended to this plan. importance: high — note: ← WI-38863 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Independent release grade: a non-implementer grades release-readiness-sidestage-2026-08-14 via scorecards:emit with concrete evidence per criterion; PASS (no criterion below its bar) = public-release confident; any FAIL routes back to the fix loop and re-grades. importance: high blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-005, P-006, P-008, P-009 — note: ← WI-38802 released\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — P-009 fix-loop ledger opened — entry 1: stale chat title on event switch (WI-38794 red), fix f557e7a deployed\nDate: 2026-08-14\nFIX-LOOP LEDGER (P-009).\n\nCLOSED: E1 stale chat title (f557e7a, deploy #1) · E2 cross-room send (useSyncMutate deps, deploy #2) · E3 WI-38815 confidence-guard bypass (decideAutomation wired fail-closed, deploy #3, independent battery green) · E4 WI-38814 ratchet floors (referencePriceCents, deploy #3, prod retest green) · E5 WI-38823 checkout drawer (deploy #3, prod retest green).\n\nOPEN:\nE6 (WIP @55549) WI-38827 judge threshold vs demo corpus — judge now 3/3 100% locally; closes with the P-005 prod rerun.\nE7 (WIP @55549) WI-38829 latency UI drop — fix in canonical 8cde8a6; closes with prod rerun.\nE8 (WIP @e59b0) WI-38835 fabricated fallback data — mode-gate constraint: prod fails HONEST when sources down; the clean-clone demo fallback stays for the reviewer path.\nE9 (WIP @61f12) WI-38836 prod probe debris — D-004 governs: closes BEFORE the cut, teardown ships WITH cleanup; sole remaining P-008 criterion.\nE10 (WIP @55549) WI-38855 broad Scout query breaches 2s warm — cold Typesense/PG bridge tail (1.8s first-hit vs 155-192ms repeats); bar: sub-2s must hold on the COLD path too (index/query-shape or boot warm-up, not cache-only); regression measures cold explicitly.\nE11 (LOGGED) 3b39b's rollback exercise found 3 defects incl. a never-passing rollback health check — fixed within his P-008 pass (4/5 criteria met, rollback 15s each way); any residual items carry P-009 stamps.\nE12 (CLOSED) WI-38853 ChannelGuide.test tsc red at exact-main — fixed by 9a5a0 during WI-38834 CI work; detector confound filed EI-20443093568975275.\nBonus in queue for deploy #5: judge-routing 404 fix 1d9a2e4 (55549, regression included).\n\nDEPLOY #5 ships when 55549's queue is green (8cde8a6 + 1d9a2e4 + E10 fix); P-005 prod rerun follows.\n\nStanding rules: (a) existing staging fix → deploy + re-run, never re-implement; (b) every entry names lane, commit, re-run verdict; (c) P-009 stamp AT FILING; (d) verify only against canonical trees (fact sidestage-canonical-tree; sidestage-mobile is NOT git-sync swept — WI-38850); (e) D-002: P-009 closes LEADER-ONLY when this ledger is all-terminal.\n\n### D-002 — P-009 (fix loop) is closed ONLY by the leader, only when the D-001 ledger shows every entry terminal — member completions must not close the meta-item\nDate: 2026-08-14\nRuling after the SECOND recurrence (14:38Z and 15:1xZ, 2026-08-14): a member completing THEIR fix-loop entries closes WI-38801/P-009, and a done P-009 planItemBlocked-gates every OPEN P-009-stamped bug out of the claimable pool (\"stale residue of completed work\") — exactly while those bugs are the campaign's critical path (first WI-38815, now WI-38835/38836). MECHANISM: the scheduler's plan-item floor treats work-items implementing a done item as residue; the fix-loop is a LONG-LIVED meta-item whose stamped children arrive continuously, so any early close silently starves the loop. RULES: (1) P-009 stays wip for the campaign's whole life; (2) only the LEADER (c18ba) flips it done, as the last act before P-010's grade, after verifying D-001 shows all entries terminal; (3) members completing their entries complete the BUG work-items only. Platform follow-up filed for the structural half (completing a plan item with open coverage-linked work-items deserves a guard).\n\n### D-003 — P-010 independent grade waits for every rubric lane and the fix loop\nDate: 2026-08-14\nDate: 2026-08-14. At 15:14Z scheduler:get_next claimed P-010 even though P-001, P-002, P-005, P-006, P-008, and P-009 were nonterminal; P-010 had blockedBy:[] despite its own contract saying to grade after the campaign runs. Restored those six blocked-by edges and released WI-38802. Do not emit the release-readiness scorecard early: fix/re-run every criterion lane first, then the independent non-implementer grades all seven criteria once against current deployed evidence.\n\n### D-004 — WI-38836 (probe-event residue in the PROD Channel Guide) CLOSES before the cut — it is not disclosable as a known limit, and the rehearsal teardown ships with it\nDate: 2026-08-14\nRULING REQUESTED BY su-3b39b6c3 (P-008 ops readiness), 2026-08-14 15:13Z. Scoping call: does WI-38836 close before the release cut, or get disclosed as a known limit? Ruling: IT CLOSES. Both halves.\n\nTHE FACTS IT RESTS ON\nPROD GET https://sidestage.buyrestart.com/api/events returns 3 public events. One is wi38795-e2e-1786717919, scheduled, thumbnailUrl https://placehold.co/320x180/png?text=WI38795. WI-38795 is closed and its own completion evidence explicitly lists wi38795-* probe events as remaining visible residue. Root cause: the PROD seller rehearsal creates durable public records and has no cleanup/archive/teardown step.\n\nWHY NOT A KNOWN LIMIT — the category is wrong, not just the severity\nA \"known limit\" is a PRODUCT limitation a user can be told about and still make an informed choice (\"no international shipping calc\"). This is not a limitation, it is CONTAMINATION: one of three events in the live public Channel Guide is our own test artifact with a placeholder image. There is no honest disclosure sentence for it — \"some events in the guide are fake\" does not describe a limit, it describes a broken release. A buyer opening the guide cannot tell which third is real.\nIt also fails the exact criterion the campaign wrote to catch it: P-006 is the no-dummy-data sweep (\"prod serves the real catalog\"). Shipping this as a disclosed limit would mean closing P-006 green while the defect P-006 exists to detect is live in production.\n\nWHY THE TEARDOWN SHIPS TOO, not just the cleanup — this is the load-bearing half\nThe work splits in two: (a) REMOVE the current wi38795-* residue; (b) add the durable rehearsal cleanup/teardown + recurrence guard. It is tempting to treat (a) as the blocker and defer (b) as follow-up. That is wrong HERE for a specific reason: we are not finished running PROD rehearsals before the cut. Deploy #3 is pending, P-008 still needs a real deploy and a timed rollback exercise (which requires a second tagged sha on prod), and WI-38814's PROD ratchet retest already created qa-wi38814-* events by the same mechanism. So (a) without (b) is a cleanup that the next rehearsal silently undoes, and the release ships contaminated anyway — with the added trap that we would have already ticked the box. (b) is what makes (a) hold.\n\nRECURRENCE GUARD (as filed on WI-38836, endorsed): a release rehearsal completion must ASSERT that no namespaced probe events remain in GET /api/events. Not a manual re-check — an assertion in the rehearsal's own teardown, so a rehearsal that leaves residue fails rather than reporting success. Verification: re-run GET /api/events after cleanup and prove no test ids and no placehold.co rows.\n\nSCOPE NOTE — WI-38814's PROD proof used event qa-wi38814-20260814-1507-61f12, and P-008's exercises will create more. The cleanup must cover EVERY namespaced probe family (wi38795-*, qa-wi38814-*, and whatever deploy #3 / the rollback drill create), not just the wi38795-* rows named in the filing. Sweeping only the ids in the ticket is how this reopens.\n\nCOMPLETION-INTEGRITY OBSERVATION, recorded without blame: WI-38795 closed with this contamination correctly DISCLOSED in its residue field — the evidence system worked. What did not work is that disclosed residue on a closed item reached live production and sat unowned until a different agent tripped over it ~20 minutes later. Disclosed residue is not the same as accepted residue. For the remainder of this campaign, residue naming a PROD-visible artifact must be filed as its own item at close, not left in the evidence blob.\n\nAUTHORITY: this is my ruling as the lane leader 3b39b asked. c18ba owns the release cut and can overrule it — if you do, say so on this plan so the reversal is as addressable as the ruling.\nRelated: P-006, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-005 — EI-20438337753986077 (event.stats global totals) is ADMITTED to the P-009 bug lane but is NOT yet a cut criterion — one question decides that\nDate: 2026-08-14\n3b39b was blocked by a fleet-scope admission trying to claim EI-20438337753986077 ('SideStage event.stats reports global paid-order totals for every event', major, filed 14:18:37Z during this campaign's own live-sync audit).\\n\\nRULING 1 — ADMITTED. The item is in scope: it was found BY this campaign's audit and is a product-correctness defect in the surface we are about to make public. I stamped it into the P-009 bug lane so it is claimable. I did NOT widen the dock claim spec to fix this: a scope refusal on a plan-scoped lane is almost always a MISSING PLAN STAMP, and the refusal's own advice ('widen the spec, matches 1 of 29883') would have admitted ~29,882 unrelated rows into a release fleet's lane. Stamp first, always; a spec revision is the last resort, not the first.\\n\\nRULING 2 — ADMISSION IS NOT PROMOTION. Being in the lane does NOT make it a release-cut blocker. P-008 is at 4/5 with WI-38836 the sole remaining criterion, and I am not expanding the blocker set on a title alone. Whether this blocks the cut turns on ONE question, cheap to answer:\\n\\n  Does 'global paid-order totals' mean a seller can see figures derived from OTHER sellers' orders?\\n\\n  - If YES — that is cross-tenant data exposure, and it is a HARD blocker. It must close before the cut regardless of P-008's count.\\n  - If NO (the number is wrong but scoped to the viewer's own data) — it is a major correctness bug that ships as known and is fixed after the cut.\\n\\nWhoever works it answers that question FIRST and reports it, before writing a fix. The answer, not the severity label, decides the promotion.\\n\\nRULING 3 — D-002 CAVEAT, carried deliberately. This item is now P-009-stamped, and per D-002 a DONE P-009 gates every open P-009-stamped bug out of the claimable pool WITHOUT erroring. So P-009 must not be closed while this item is open, or it silently vanishes from the pool rather than failing loudly. Same guard already applies to WI-38836.\n\n### D-006 — ANSWERED + PROMOTED: EI-20438337753986077 leaks platform-wide revenue to unauthenticated callers — it IS a hard cut blocker\nDate: 2026-08-14\nD-005 said one question decides whether this blocks the cut: does 'global paid-order totals' expose figures derived from OTHER sellers' orders? I answered it from source rather than leaving it for the claimer.\\n\\nANSWER: YES. Promoting to a HARD BLOCKER. Severity raised major -> critical.\\n\\nVERIFIED FROM SOURCE (apps/api/src/stats/stats.module.ts, hive tree):\\n1. EventStatsService.read() L59-63 runs:\\n     SELECT SUM(jsonb_array_length(payload->'items')), SUM((payload->>'totalCents')::bigint)\\n     FROM checkout_order WHERE status = 'paid'\\n   There is NO event predicate, NO seller predicate, NO tenant predicate of any kind. It sums the ENTIRE checkout_order table and returns the result under whatever eventId was requested (L67 returns { eventId, viewers, itemsSold, totalRaisedCents }).\\n2. StatsController L80-83 exposes it at GET /events/:eventId/stats.\\n3. There are NO guards: no UseGuards/AuthGuard in stats.module.ts, and no APP_GUARD or useGlobalGuards anywhere under apps/api/src. The route is UNAUTHENTICATED.\\n4. Contrast proving this is an omission and not a missing capability: db/pg-order-store.ts scopes its reads by payload->>'buyerId'. The codebase knows how to scope; this query simply does not.\\n\\nIMPACT: any anonymous caller who hits any event's stats endpoint receives SideStage's platform-wide gross revenue (totalRaisedCents) and total items sold across every seller and every event. That is cross-tenant aggregate exposure plus disclosure of business-confidential totals, on a surface we are about to make public. It is not merely 'a wrong number on a dashboard'.\\n\\nEXPLICIT NON-FINDING — do NOT widen the fix: the second unscoped-looking query in the same file (pricingHistory, L94-102) is CORRECT. It filters by item->>'productId' and returns price/quantity aggregates only; aggregating a product's history across its own events is the documented intent ('real seller history for the active product'), and its buyer-identified offers come from actions.listAudit(eventId), which IS event-scoped. I checked it specifically so nobody 'fixes' it by adding an eventId filter and silently breaks pricing history.\\n\\nFIX (as the filer scoped it, and I agree): filter by payload->>'eventId' or a normalized event_id column, add per-event fixtures PROVING isolation, and preserve the event.stats invalidation key/args. The isolation fixture is the recurrence guard — a fix without a test that fails on the unscoped query leaves the class armed.\\n\\nSTILL UNDETERMINED: whether PROD currently holds paid orders across more than one seller (i.e. whether the leak is presently non-trivial in magnitude). That affects urgency of disclosure, NOT whether it blocks — shipping a public endpoint that sums all tenants' revenue is a blocker at any current row count.\"}\n\n### D-007 — WI-38863 (PROD checkout dead at shipping) is the #1 cut blocker — it SUPERSEDES my WI-38836 reprioritization, and the credential reuse is pre-authorized\nDate: 2026-08-14\nREVISING MY OWN ORDER. At 15:34Z I told 61f12 that WI-38836 was the sole remaining criterion and to take it next. That is now WRONG: at 15:53Z he filed WI-38863 (critical, parent WI-38794) showing PROD buyer checkout CANNOT PROCEED. A buyer who cannot complete a purchase outranks probe-event residue in the Channel Guide. WI-38863 first; WI-38836 second.\\n\\nTHE DEFECT (61f12's diagnosis, which I verified where I could): a fresh PROD buyer holds the live product; POST /api/cart/items and POST /api/shipping/rates both return 200 but rates is EMPTY. UI shows 'No live shipping rates are available for this address' with Continue to Square DISABLED. Writer confirmed at apps/api/src/shipping/shipping.service.ts — getRates returns [] when EasyPostClient.isConfigured() is false. A live-container probe found EASYPOST_API_KEY and every warehouse-origin variable absent, and the Square sandbox app/location/token absent too, so payment would have blocked at the next step regardless.\\n\\nRULING 1 — THIS IS NOT OWNER-GATED. Do not park it as a credentials wall. I verified the secret source 61f12 identified: /home/marsh-office/Restart/.env EXISTS (23,585 bytes, 184 vars, mode 664) and defines exactly the checkout-critical names — EASYPOST_API_KEY, SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SQUARE_APP_ID, SQUARE_LOCATION_ID, and the complete WAREHOUSE_FROM_* origin set (NAME/STREET1/CITY/STATE/ZIP/COUNTRY). I listed names only and never read a value. Everything needed is already on this box.\\n\\nRULING 2 — REUSE IS PRE-AUTHORIZED, so nobody stalls waiting for permission. Provision SideStage PROD from that source. Square there is the SANDBOX app/location/token, so payment exercises carry no real-money risk. THEN advance the superproject pin; git-sync sweeps the pin bump normally.\n\nWHY THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, not ceremony: reversed, the superproject points at a submodule commit that exists on no remote, so a fresh clone cannot fetch it — converting an uncommitted-patch failure into a dangling-pointer failure, which is strictly worse because the parent LOOKS correctly pinned.
