Commit c7aa7bb is NOT acceptable as final: it removes build/typecheck scripts, routes main/import/default to src TypeScript, and an exact node:20-alpine require('@papercusp/sse') probe exits 1 with Unexpected token 'export'. Final packaging must preserve a built Node 20-compatible require path and the web ESM path, pass TS6/package checks, and pass the exact Docker module-load + /healthz smoke before deploy.\n\n### D-019 — SideStage bridge publication requires a Pot-attested integrator signer; never bypass wrong-device rejection\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEvidence from the 2026-08-14 21:04 EDT git-sync writer: own_head_publish advanced cleanly to e49a5428e4129dc4922541eb58d8c7baa2dcb88e, but integrator_status skipped with self_device_not_attested because local signer device XPAsvso1qEKb… is not among SideStage's attested devices. worktree_bridge recorded 16 consecutive consumed=1 / accepted=0 ticks and rejected the current advance as wrong-device; canonical GitHub origin/staging therefore remained 46db8556738ed345415e3ffc4a59927e2a7ca621. RULING: repair the signer through the existing Pot membership/device-attestation surface; do not direct-push or otherwise route around the bridge's device guard. Then fire the existing git-sync flow and require, in order, canonical/origin advancement, fresh-clone resolution of the corrected head, the full D-018 SSE/API/web/Node20 image + /healthz matrix, a changed public SHA, and populated-catalog positive control before deployment or P-005/WI-38945 closure.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-020 — Temporary manual SideStage git-sync hold pending WI-38968 writer-scope ruling\nDate: 2026-08-14\nWI-38968 currently proves a post-restart writer contradiction: the new self_device_not_attested guard executed on one Papercusp git-sync tick, while another writer/path subsequently signed four advances from the same unadmitted XPAs… device. Its current broadcast prohibits manual git-sync:run for Papercusp until 70ba41c9 is deployed, but the evidence does not yet establish whether that stale/concurrent writer is Papercusp-local or shared with SideStage. TEMPORARY RULING: WI-38945 may continue the existing SideStage Pot device-attestation repair and read-only proof preparation, but must not manually fire SideStage git-sync until the live WI-38968 owner answers the scope and exact safe next verb. D-019 and the no-deploy/no-close proof chain remain fully operative. This hold narrows only the manual git-sync invocation and must be superseded immediately when the writer owner supplies verified scope.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-021 — D-020 resolved: SideStage manual git-sync is safe only after exact actor attestation and a clean scheduled tick\nDate: 2026-08-14\nWI-38968 owner verified the temporary manual-run prohibition is scoped to installSlug=papercusp, including an omitted/default slug that resolves to Papercusp; it is not a blanket ban on every bridged Pot. The exact failure predicate is runtime resolveUsageActor.devicePubkey absent from listHiveMembersForLocalPot(...).deviceAttestations, causing old manual code to sign and receivers to reject wrong-device. SUPERSEDES D-020: WI-38945 may release its temporary hold only after (1) the exact SideStage runtime actor key is present in the resolved SideStage Pot attestation set and (2) a scheduled SideStage tick no longer records self_device_not_attested or wrong-device. Only then may it call git-sync:run with the explicit argument installSlug:'sidestage'—never omit/default the slug. If membership equality or the clean scheduled tick is not proven, wait for the scheduled tick or for 70ba41c9 to reach the live release operator; do not use the old manual plane. Current writer loading at the ruling: 70ba41c9 is on origin/staging and loaded by bg-host source, but not in main/live :3070; checkpoint candidate 6bcdb023 is still running. D-019's no-bypass and full fresh-clone/runtime/public proof chain remain mandatory.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-022 — Writer-backed completion evidence accepted; dependent checkout lane may resume\nDate: 2026-08-14\n2026-08-14 18:25 EDT leader ruling. Read completion evidence from harness_shared.work_items.payload->_completionEvidence for done closes; terminal_completion_ref is the alternate dropped-close surface, and trimmed work_items:get may omit the payload. Writer-backed reads show WI-38945 authority=committed with production eae0aa0, fresh-clone/SSE/API/web/Docker/runtime checks, six real catalog/Scout rows, /api/sync/sse 200, empty console, and screenshot /tmp/sidestage-wi38945-eae0aa0.png. WI-39024 authority=committed with 18 Rust tests, Android unit suite, 4-ABI build, APK install, paid order order_a48d06cf-6c67-4375-8f25-7664243597b0 rendered, and screenshot /tmp/Screenshot_1786745962.png. The earlier leader null-evidence alert is retracted. Gate plan:sidestage-public-release:release-evidence-ledger-green fired; the serialized fresh buyer/cart checkout acceptance may resume without reusing the expired cart or failed order.\n\n### D-023 — Next serialized SideStage cut is owned by su-55549 for the measured-latency fix\nDate: 2026-08-14\nDate: 2026-08-14\nLeader ruling under D-014. No other serialized SideStage deploy role is active. su-55549079-d53e-4c1e-b6ed-014bec53986c becomes the sole deploy-role holder for the next cut containing the already-committed WI-38797/WI-38855 latency propagation and UI indicator. The role holder must use explicit SideStage git-sync scope only (installSlug:'sidestage', never omitted/default), re-read D-021, and wait for/pin the actual pushed commit before deploying. Announce start, run the existing SideStage deploy path with release-positive-control and probe-hygiene fail-closed guards, then behaviorally verify the public SHA plus a real grounded proposal with visible sub-2s latency/budget state before closing WI-38797/WI-38855. The fleet leader remains management/delegation-only and does not run git-sync or deploy. Authority returns automatically to the leader if the holder dies, goes critical, or does not checkpoint pickup within five minutes.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-024 — D-001 rule (c) \"P-009 stamp AT FILING\" is UNIMPLEMENTABLE as written — a blocker population must use the rel='blocks' edge, never payload.plan_item\nDate: 2026-09-05\nCorrection filed from the papercusp platform lane (EI-20450339646861882), which was opened against this campaign's 2026-08-14 failure where three release-blocking bugs were filed unstamped in one hour. That item's premise — \"the convention just needs enforcement\" — is REFUTED. The convention names the wrong FIELD, and enforcing it as written would refuse the filings outright.\n\nVERIFIED IN CODE (read 2026-09-05, not recalled):\n1. `payload.plan_item` is a one-live-row-per-lane COVERAGE stamp, not a provenance tag. `findOpenPlanItemCollision` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/_create-core.ts:386, called at :956) selects any NON-terminal work-item whose `payload->'plan_item'` matches {plan_slug, item_id} and returns `ok:false, error:'duplicate_plan_item'` — \"plan item coverage already exists on OPEN work-item <id>; continue that item instead of creating a sibling\". Its docstring cites D-046, \"one live work-item per plan lane\".\n2. Therefore rule (c) is self-defeating at exactly the moment it matters: the FIRST fix-loop bug stamped {this plan, P-009} succeeds, and every CONCURRENT sibling stamped the same way is REFUSED. A fix loop whose stamped children arrive continuously (D-001's own description) can never have two open at once.\n3. `finishPlanStamp` flips the stamped plan item to `done` when the stamping row completes — so even where a single stamp succeeds, completing one bug would mark P-009 done. That is the precise starvation mechanism D-002 already diagnosed from the other end (\"a done P-009 planItemBlocked-gates every OPEN P-009-stamped bug out of the claimable pool\"). D-002 treated it as a discipline problem and fixed it with a leader-only close rule; the deeper cause is that the blocker population was modelled on a coverage field at all.\n\nTHE CORRECT FIELD: a plan's blocker population is MANY-to-one and is already modelled as coord_links `rel='blocks'` → `plan_item`, already read by `getBlockingIssuesForPlan` / `getAllBlockedPlanItems` (packages/operator-core/lib/issue-blocks-merge.ts) and surfaced through `plans:items`. That edge carries no uniqueness constraint and no completion propagation, so N blockers may point at one plan item safely:\n  work_items:link { id, rel: 'blocks', target_kind: 'plan_item', target_ref: '<plan-slug>#P-NNN' }\n\nNOT AUTO-DERIVED, deliberately: \"filed while on lane X\" does not entail \"blocks X\", and a spurious blocks edge marks the plan item blocked in plans:items — reading the plan RED where it is not, the mirror image of the false-green this exists to prevent. The platform fix landed as an ADVISORY at the filing seam instead: a critical/major issue filed with no plan-item edge while the caller holds a declared plan lane now returns `planItemBlockerNudge` naming the exact `blocks` call and warning explicitly OFF the plan_item stamp.\n\nACTION FOR ANYONE REVIVING THIS CAMPAIGN OR COPYING ITS RULES: do not carry rule (c) forward as written. Replace \"gets payload.plan_item {plan, P-009} at filing\" with \"gets a rel='blocks' edge to the plan item at filing\". D-010's criterion-5 population should be enumerated from blocks edges, not from the coverage stamp.\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-real-system-tests-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage Tests tab — real-system acceptance suites","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage Tests tab — real-system acceptance suites\nslug: sidestage-real-system-tests-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n# SideStage Tests tab — real-system acceptance suites\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft complete for Avi's review; no implementation has started and the plan remains draft. It contains 14 items across contract/safety, reusable execution foundation, six real suite conversions, Tests-tab UX, and release proof, plus 6 governing architecture decisions. Verified: plans:lint has 0 errors and 0 warnings; plans:get reports no missing blocker references or dependency cycles. The two SideStage overlap candidates were superseded zero-item rubric templates, while production-readiness-acceptance-2026-06-10 is a distinct 34-item cross-app acceptance inventory, so this new SideStage implementation plan is intentional.\n\n**Next:** Avi reviews the draft. If approved later, select the execution route and begin P-001; keep the plan unpromoted and do not implement any item before that review.\n\n## Background\n\nThe current Tests tab exposes actions, auction, checkout, injection, load, and judge. It provides useful rehearsal coverage, but its green states are not uniformly evidence that deployed SideStage works: actions, auction, and injection construct real domain classes around in-memory fixtures; checkout substitutes a fake payment path; load schedules messages without real client sockets; and judge can use fixed cases plus a deterministic fallback.\n\nThe target is a viewer and authenticated launcher for a small allow-listed suite catalog. The browser and public web process must never accept arbitrary test commands or execute a shell. Runs execute in a dedicated acceptance-runner trust boundary against an ephemeral deployment built from the exact requested commit. The deployment uses real PostgreSQL, Typesense, Redis, and MediaMTX services plus real HTTP, SSE/WebSocket, and browser clients. Checkout uses the official Square and EasyPost sandboxes; judge uses the configured remote copilot/model. A missing dependency, credential, or sandbox is BLOCKED / NOT RUN, never a synthetic pass.\n\nReuse before adding new machinery: apps/web/src/SystemTestsTab.tsx remains the operator surface; apps/api/src/rehearsals is migrated or retired suite by suite; libs/test-config supplies PostgreSQL, Redis, Typesense, Nest-app, hermetic-environment, and durable test-run reporting primitives; the existing Docker Compose and Playwright paths provide deployment-equivalent and browser infrastructure. A pinned k6 container is the one justified new runner dependency because the repository has no real network load generator.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- The Tests tab launches only versioned, server-owned suite IDs with bounded parameters; browser input can never select commands, module paths, URLs, or arbitrary code.\n- A system-suite pass must cross the deployed production protocol and be corroborated by persisted or subscriber-visible evidence from the same requested commit.\n- Runs use isolated real PostgreSQL, Typesense, Redis, MediaMTX, API, web, and worker services, with production endpoints, credentials, and customer data rejected.\n- Missing infrastructure, sandbox credentials, or configured remote models produces an explicit blocked/not-run result; mocks, fakes, deterministic fallbacks, and swallowed errors cannot produce green.\n- Every run durably records actor, requested SHA, running image digests, suite/case versions, configuration provenance, transitions, assertions, artifacts, cleanup result, and retention expiry.\n- Parallel runs cannot collide or leak state; cancellation, timeouts, resource budgets, cleanup retries, stale-SHA warnings, secret redaction, and evidence retention are observable and tested.\n- The six suites remain independently launchable and cover actions, auction, checkout, injection, load, and judge through their real external boundaries.\n\n## Design\n\nThe existing SystemTestsTab remains the authenticated control and evidence surface, but execution moves behind an allow-listed controller and isolated acceptance worker. A durable run state machine coordinates provisioning, execution, evidence capture, cancellation, cleanup, and retention. The worker deploys the requested SideStage commit into a per-run environment, reusing Docker Compose and libs/test-config for real dependencies and Playwright for browser actors.\n\nShared black-box clients drive authenticated HTTP, SSE/WebSocket, and browser flows, then correlate those observations with PostgreSQL, Typesense, Redis, MediaMTX, logs, screenshots, and metrics. Suite adapters own only domain-specific setup and assertions. Checkout uses official Square and EasyPost sandboxes; injection and judge use the configured remote copilot/judge; load reuses the existing corpus through a version-pinned k6 container.\n\nThe settled trade-off is isolation over running tests inside the public app process: provisioning costs more than an in-memory rehearsal, but it produces same-commit evidence without exposing a general command runner or risking production data. A bounded smoke profile participates in release acceptance; full, sandbox, and load profiles stay operator-launched.\n\n## Scope and success contract\n\n- Each run records requested SHA, deployed image digests, suite/case versions, configuration provenance, timestamps, actor, per-case status, logs/metrics/artifacts, cleanup outcome, and retention expiry.\n- Per-run PostgreSQL schema/database, Typesense collection prefix, Redis key prefix, MediaMTX path prefix, event/user/order/idempotency namespace, and sandbox idempotency keys prevent cross-run and production contamination.\n- The runner refuses production endpoints or production credentials, enforces bounded concurrency/timeouts/budgets, redacts secrets, and always attempts cleanup. Cleanup failure is visible and retryable.\n- Passed means the assertion crossed the same external protocol and persisted through the same service boundary used in production. Mock/fake/deterministic-fallback execution cannot produce a pass.\n- The tab distinguishes queued, provisioning, running, passed, failed, blocked, cancelled, timed out, and cleanup-failed, and warns when a result's SHA differs from the currently viewed/deployed SHA.\n- Unit tests remain for local logic. These suites add black-box system evidence; they do not replace focused unit and integration coverage.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Running acceptance workloads against live customer data or production infrastructure.\n- A general-purpose remote command runner or user-supplied test definitions.\n- Treating an unavailable external sandbox/model as success.\n- Making every unit test visible in the Tests tab.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract and safety boundary\n\n- **P-001** `done` Define the versioned allow-listed suite manifest and result contract for actions, auction, checkout, injection, load, and judge. Specify case IDs, prerequisites, required evidence, pass/fail/blocked semantics, requested/deployed SHA fields, budgets, retention, and the rule that mocks, fakes, or fallbacks cannot report passed; add parser/schema tests including rejection of unknown suites and synthetic-green results. importance: high — note: ← WI-39012 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Reusable execution foundation\n\n- **P-002** `done` Build an ephemeral acceptance-environment provisioner that deploys the requested SideStage commit with real PostgreSQL, Typesense, Redis, MediaMTX, API, web, and worker services, records image digests and health checks, and refuses production endpoints/credentials. Reuse the existing Docker Compose and libs/test-config containers; verify same-SHA boot, dependency failure, production-target rejection, and teardown. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39025 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add the durable test-run model and reporter: run, suite, case, artifact, environment, transition, cancellation, retention, and cleanup records with migrations and a state machine for queued/provisioning/running/passed/failed/blocked/cancelled/timed-out/cleanup-failed. Reuse the admin-test-runs reporter concepts; test idempotent creation, legal transitions, resume/readback, artifact redaction, and stale-run recovery. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39063 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Implement the authenticated launcher/controller and isolated worker boundary. The API accepts only catalog suite IDs plus bounded versioned parameters, checks seller/operator authorization, queues work outside the public web process, enforces concurrency/time/cost limits and cancellation, and never evaluates caller commands or paths; add authorization, allow-list, injection, retry, timeout, and cancellation tests. blocked-by: P-001, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39080 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Create deterministic acceptance fixtures, namespace leases, and cleanup/reaper logic for per-run PostgreSQL schema/database, Typesense collections, Redis keys, MediaMTX paths, users/events/orders/idempotency keys, and external sandbox metadata. Prove two concurrent runs cannot collide, production identifiers are rejected, cleanup is idempotent, and leaked resources are surfaced and recoverable. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39090 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Build shared black-box clients and evidence collectors for authenticated HTTP, SSE/WebSocket, Playwright browsers, PostgreSQL/Typesense/Redis assertions, MediaMTX probes, logs, traces, screenshots, and metrics. Assertions must cross deployed protocols and then confirm persisted/subscriber-visible state; add contract tests for lost connections, retries, secret redaction, artifact limits, and evidence provenance. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-39196 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Real suite conversions\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Convert actions into a real system suite: seed an event and policy through supported APIs, submit allowed and forbidden guarded actions through the deployed authenticated endpoint, verify database audit/state transitions and subscriber-visible updates, exercise rollback, and prove rejected actions leave no forbidden persisted side effect. Retire the in-memory rehearsal as Tests-tab evidence while retaining focused unit coverage. blocked-by: P-004, P-006\n- **P-008** `todo` Convert auction into a real multi-client suite: drive a seller/host and at least two isolated buyer browser sessions through event start, concurrent bids, ordering/conflict handling, SSE/WebSocket propagation, reconnect/recovery, close, winner, and inventory persistence. Assert both browser-visible state and PostgreSQL truth, with deterministic clocks only where they do not replace network or persistence behavior. blocked-by: P-004, P-006 importance: high\n- **P-009** `todo` Convert checkout into a real buyer journey against the Square and EasyPost sandboxes: create cart/order through the deployed UI/API, obtain sandbox payment and shipping results, process supported callbacks/idempotent retries, verify order/payment/shipment persistence and buyer-visible status, and cover decline/failure compensation. Missing sandbox credentials or availability must produce blocked, never a fake payment pass. blocked-by: P-004, P-006 importance: high\n- **P-010** `todo` Convert injection into an adversarial end-to-end suite: send prompt-injection and false-authority messages through a real buyer client to the configured remote copilot, traverse the deployed policy/action guard, and verify forbidden discounts, stock edits, offers, and invented authority never reach buyers or persistence. Capture model reply, citations, guard decision, audit rows, and repeatability metadata; no scripted model response may pass. blocked-by: P-004, P-006 importance: high\n- **P-011** `todo` Replace the load scheduler with a pinned k6-based network suite that opens real authenticated clients, exercises the production HTTP and SSE/WebSocket paths with the existing price/shipping/policy/variant/stock/offer/bid corpus, and reports throughput, error rate, connection stability, queue pressure, and p50/p95/p99 latency. Establish reviewed budgets, bounded test sizes, graceful ramp/abort behavior, and evidence that messages were processed, not merely scheduled. blocked-by: P-004, P-006 importance: high\n- **P-012** `todo` Convert judge into a live-quality suite: seed real event/catalog/policy context, obtain replies from the configured remote copilot through the deployed API, and run the configured remote judge over a versioned corpus for grounding, policy, price correctness, citations, tone, and latency. Persist raw/redacted inputs, model identities, prompts, scores, rationales, and thresholds; deterministic local scoring remains unit coverage and cannot satisfy the system suite. blocked-by: P-004, P-006 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Tests-tab experience\n\n- **P-013** `todo` Turn SystemTestsTab into an authenticated launcher and durable run viewer backed by the new APIs: show prerequisites before launch, explicit state and progress, commit/image provenance, case evidence and artifacts, cancellation/retry/cleanup controls, retention, and a prominent stale-SHA warning. Add component and browser tests for authorization, blocked prerequisites, live progress/reconnect, failure evidence, cancellation, and stale results. blocked-by: P-003, P-004\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Release proof and rollout\n\n- **P-014** `todo` Wire a bounded real-system smoke profile into the existing acceptance/release path and keep full/sandbox/load profiles manually launchable from the Tests tab. Run all six suites against a clean same-SHA environment; verify no production access, no synthetic pass path, durable evidence, concurrent isolation, cancellation, cleanup/reaper behavior, and stale-SHA detection; document required sandbox/model setup and rollback, then remove or relabel every remaining rehearsal-only green path. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The Tests tab is a catalog launcher and evidence viewer, not a command runner\nDate: 2026-08-14\nExpose only versioned server-owned suite IDs and bounded parameters. Authentication and authorization occur before queueing, execution happens in an isolated worker trust boundary, and neither browser input nor the public web process may supply shell commands, module paths, URLs, or arbitrary code. This keeps the operator affordance without creating a remote-code-execution surface.\nRelated: P-001, P-004, P-013, P-014\n\n### D-002 — System evidence comes from an isolated same-commit acceptance deployment\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEvery run is required to target an ephemeral deployment built from the requested commit and record the running image digests. It must use real PostgreSQL, Typesense, Redis, MediaMTX, API, web, and worker services with per-run namespaces, while hard guards reject production endpoints, credentials, and customer data. In-process construction remains useful unit coverage but cannot satisfy a Tests-tab system suite.\n\n### D-003 — Unavailable prerequisites are blocked, never green\nDate: 2026-08-14\nA pass requires protocol-level execution plus persisted or subscriber-visible evidence with run/SHA/config provenance. Missing services, sandbox credentials, remote model access, time budget, or cleanup capacity yields an explicit BLOCKED / NOT RUN result. No mock, fake adapter, deterministic fallback, or swallowed error may be translated into passed.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-006, P-013, P-014\n\n### D-004 — External-boundary suites use official sandboxes and the configured remote models\nDate: 2026-08-14\nCheckout calls Square and EasyPost sandbox APIs with per-run idempotency and cleanup metadata. Injection and judge call the configured remote copilot/judge models and record model/prompt provenance. Local fakes and deterministic scorers stay in unit tests only; sandbox/model unavailability blocks the corresponding system suite.\nRelated: P-009, P-010, P-012, P-014\n\n### D-005 — Use a pinned k6 container for real network load\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe existing browser load simulator produces a deterministic schedule without opening sockets, so it cannot establish transport capacity or latency. Reuse its scenario corpus, but execute bounded profiles with a version-pinned k6 container against authenticated HTTP and SSE/WebSocket paths, capturing throughput, errors, connection behavior, and percentile latency. The pin and budgets make the new dependency reproducible and controlled.\nRelated: P-011, P-014\n\n### D-006 — Extend existing test and deployment infrastructure instead of creating a parallel harness\nDate: 2026-08-14\nBuild on the repository's Vitest projects, libs/test-config container helpers and Nest boot path, Playwright/browser tooling, admin test-run reporter concepts, and Docker Compose deployment. New code should be the minimal acceptance-runner orchestration and catalog needed to join those surfaces; suite-specific logic remains close to each production domain and its tests.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-007 — The trusted runner owns one normalized durable record model\nDate: 2026-08-14\nP-003 extends the existing browser-safe @papercusp/system-test-contract with the public lifecycle states and extends the trusted @papercusp/system-test-runner with the state machine plus PostgreSQL reporter/store. Each launch remains one run for one allow-listed suite request and snapshots suite, case, artifact, environment, append-only transition, cancellation, retention, and cleanup records in normalized system_test_* tables. The API/worker added in P-004 must reuse this store rather than creating another run ledger. Results are written idempotently; illegal regressions are refused; cleanup-failed overrides any prior outcome; stale nonterminal rows recover to timed-out with cleanup pending; artifact references/summaries are redacted before persistence.\n\n### D-008 — P-005 extends the existing run ledger with deterministic fixture leases and verified cleanup\nDate: 2026-08-15\nP-005 adds one deterministic, production-rejecting fixture descriptor to @papercusp/system-test-runner and two normalized children of the existing system_test_run ledger: a unique namespace lease and its typed resources. PostgresSystemTestRunStore owns transactional acquisition, durable resource state, redacted external-sandbox metadata, leak state, retry, and reaper selection; a typed resource-driver seam performs provision/remove/probe work. Cleanup reuses system_test_cleanup, may retry failed cleanup to a later succeeded cleanup while preserving the run's cleanup-failed history, is idempotent, and releases a lease only after every resource probes absent. This extends P-002's isolated same-SHA environment and P-003's ledger/redaction/recovery seams; it does not create a second harness, store, or command surface.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-014\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-scout-shared-runtime-vertex-2026-08-14","title":"Extract Restart Scout backend runtime and run SideStage Scout on Vertex Gemini","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Extract Restart Scout backend runtime and run SideStage Scout on Vertex Gemini\nslug: sidestage-scout-shared-runtime-vertex-2026-08-14\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Goal\nExtract Restart's proven backend agent loop into a reusable shared TypeScript package and make both Restart and SideStage consume it while preserving the already-shared drawer, SSE transport, and chat protocol.\n\n## Constraints\n- Vertex Gemini authenticates through existing Application Default Credentials; no credential material enters either repository.\n- Preserve Restart's working shopper behavior and wire contract.\n- Keep catalog, cart, identity, session, memory, prompt, persistence, and app-specific stream events behind application adapters.\n- Add package, unit, integration, and typecheck evidence before completion.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nBuild the shared runtime first, then migrate the two applications in parallel-safe dependency order, then verify end-to-end.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Create the standalone @papercusp/scout-runtime package with provider-neutral message/tool types, bounded agent-turn runner, retry policy, budget and telemetry hooks, a Vertex Gemini adapter using ADC, and focused unit tests. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39039 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Migrate Restart apps/scout-service to consume @papercusp/scout-runtime while retaining Restart-specific prompts, sessions, memory, persistence, catalog/cart handlers, interactive cards, and wire events. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39048 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Integrate SideStage apps/api Scout with @papercusp/scout-runtime and implement SideStage-specific catalog/cart tool handlers plus Vertex configuration, without changing the shared drawer/SSE/chat protocol. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39071 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Run package and application unit tests, affected tests, typechecks, and focused live/integration verification for natural-language catalog questions and tool calls; resolve any regressions. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39081 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `todo` Verify shared-package publication/submodule pointers and both deployment configurations, record exact evidence, and close the migration plan. blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Keep browser and backend packages separate\nDate: 2026-08-14\n@papercusp/scout-chat remains the browser-only drawer/transport package. Backend execution belongs in a standalone @papercusp/scout-runtime package so React/browser peer dependencies never leak into server services.\n\n### D-002 — Define the runtime/application seam\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe shared runtime owns provider-neutral message and tool types, bounded model/tool rounds, retries, usage normalization, budget and telemetry hooks, and provider adapters. Each application owns system prompts, identity/session/memory/persistence, catalog/cart and other domain handlers, and app-specific emitted events.\n\n### D-003 — Use Vertex Application Default Credentials\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe Gemini adapter uses Google Vertex AI through the existing machine Application Default Credentials and externally supplied project/location configuration. No API key or credential file is copied or committed. SCOUT_VERTEX_MODEL remains overrideable; the initial default follows the live OMP catalog's function-calling-capable Gemini 3.1 Pro preview identifier.\n\n### D-004 — Preserve the established client wire contract\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe existing @papercusp/scout-chat drawer, @papercusp/sse transport, and @papercusp/chat-protocol event contract remain unchanged. Migration is behind the server boundary and app adapters.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): sidestage/sidestage-scout-shared-runtime-vertex-2026-08-14 (\"Extract Restart Scout backend runtime and run SideStage Scout on Vertex Gemini\"): no plan update since 2026-08-14 (57 days idle), 4/5 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-seller-copilot-mission-2026-08-14","title":"Make SideStage Copilot fulfill the live-selling seller mission","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make SideStage Copilot fulfill the live-selling seller mission\nslug: sidestage-seller-copilot-mission-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Original seller-Copilot implementation P-001–P-008 is complete and P-009 acceptance residue remains open. Avi identified a real reply-tone gap; P-010–P-013 now cover distinct provider-independent semantics, production configuration, regression guards, and end-to-end verification. AUTO execution is active in this session.\n\n**Next:** Claim and execute P-010 through P-013 while leaving P-009's independent acceptance lane untouched.\n\n## Goal\nReplace the seller panel's buyer-Scout behavior with a real event-aware copilot loop: buyer question intake, verified grounding, durable seller review, fresh-context approval, guarded action execution, and sync-driven UI state.\n\n## Scope\n- Preserve Scout as the buyer catalog/cart assistant.\n- Reuse ChatService, CatalogSource, EventPolicyResolver, GuardedActionService, Judge, and the shared sync/SSE layer.\n- Add the missing Copilot runtime composition and proposal lifecycle.\n- Rebuild the Seller Copilot panel as a live proposal queue.\n- Verify the loop through backend integration and frontend interaction tests.\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Implement the backend Copilot module, grounding adapters, durable proposal lifecycle, and review/action API. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38939 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Connect buyer-question chat ingestion to Copilot proposal generation and publish proposal invalidations through sync. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38940 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Replace the seller Copilot panel with a sync-backed grounded proposal queue and review controls; remove buyer cart semantics. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38941 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Add backend and frontend integration coverage, run project checks, and resolve all regressions. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-38943 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Virtual-desktop acceptance\n\n- **P-005** `done` Establish an isolated Xvfb/Openbox virtual desktop with two independent real Firefox instances, separate Snap-safe profiles, and loopback-only geckodrivers on newly allocated display/ports; create a dedicated SideStage test event, verify buyer and Studio share its identity, and record the clean empty/loading baseline. importance: high — note: ← WI-39043 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Exercise buyer-question ingestion and manual Prepare: question detection, live sync arrival, citations from catalog/listing/transcript/policy, deterministic or remote-model behavior, insufficient-context blocking, and duplicate/idempotent handling. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-39051 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Exercise the complete review lifecycle: edit and approve a grounded reply, verify delivery to live event chat, skip a separate proposal, confirm an allowed guarded action, and verify stale/blocked or policy-denied actions fail closed. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-39054 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Audit the Studio Copilot in the virtual desktop for responsive layouts, keyboard navigation, accessible labeling/status announcements, visible error/reconnect behavior, console errors, failed network requests, and capture screenshots for each material state. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-39060 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `todo` Triage every finding, file evidence-backed defects, verify any in-scope fixes through the same isolated dual-Firefox virtual-desktop workflow, and publish a pass/fail report against the acceptance matrix. blocked-by: P-007, P-008 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Reply-tone behavior completion\n\n- **P-010** `done` Define one canonical Copilot tone vocabulary and map Warm, Playful, and Minimal to three distinct runtime tones. Acceptance: policyFromConfig maps warm→warm, playful→playful, minimal→concise; published-policy precedence remains unchanged; shared TypeScript contracts accept every supported tone. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39098 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Make every generation path honor the effective tone, including the no-credential deterministic production fallback, and pass optional OpenAI model configuration into the production container. Acceptance: identical grounded context yields observably distinct warm/playful/concise reply copy; the remote prompt/schema supports playful; missing credentials remain safe and functional. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39099 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Strengthen regression coverage across event config persistence, policy resolution, prompt construction, reply enforcement, deterministic generation, and production configuration. Acceptance: tests fail on the previous playful→warm alias, fixed fallback wording, or missing production environment seam. blocked-by: P-010, P-011 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39100 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Verify the complete event Settings → save → Copilot proposal flow with focused/full automated checks and browser QA, then reconcile release/deploy state. Acceptance: the setting persists, each selection changes generated buyer-facing proposal text without changing safety gates, responsive UI remains sound, and live deployment status is reported honestly. blocked-by: P-012 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39101 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Automatic question routing and buyer answer lifecycle\n\n- **P-014** `done` Replace the duplicated boolean question heuristic with one structured, deterministic buyer-message classifier; persist its route/category/reason on the chat message and make persisted routing metadata—not reclassification—the authoritative Copilot trigger. Acceptance: obvious product, stock, price, shipping, policy, and commerce questions route to seller review; social/non-question chatter does not; classification metadata survives store round-trips. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39124 completed (done)\n- **P-015** `done` Make seller-queue delivery durable and observable by reconciling persisted queued chat questions into idempotent proposals, retaining the immediate subscription fast path, and recording failures instead of swallowing them. Acceptance: a queued question missed by the in-memory event is recovered on the next event proposal read; retries create one proposal; a failed generation remains visible as a blocked proposal. blocked-by: P-014 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39125 completed (done)\n- **P-016** `done` Close the approved/skipped/blocked proposal lifecycle back onto chat: approved replies carry assistant provenance plus source/proposal linkage, and the source buyer question is durably updated with its resolution and response id. Acceptance: approve is exactly-once and marks the source answered; skip and blocked states remain explicit without emitting a seller reply; Postgres and in-memory stores agree. blocked-by: P-014, P-015 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39126 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `done` Render routed question state and Copilot-assisted answer provenance in the buyer event chat with accessible queued, answered, skipped, and blocked semantics, preserving ordinary seller messages. Acceptance: sync refresh updates the original question state and linked approved answer without a reload; responsive and screen-reader labels are covered. blocked-by: P-016 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39127 completed (done)\n- **P-018** `done` Add focused API/store/module/web regression coverage for structured routing, durable catch-up, idempotent approval linkage, lifecycle transitions, and buyer chat presentation; run affected checks and the isolated dual-Firefox live acceptance before closing the mission. blocked-by: P-014, P-015, P-016, P-017 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39128 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n- Buyer-facing replies default to seller review; no direct model-to-room send.\n- Approval reloads current event data and policy and fails closed when grounding is stale.\n- Seller Copilot does not own buyer cart or checkout state.\n- A dedicated proposal store owns the generating/pending/approved/skipped/blocked/executed lifecycle because no existing record owns that review state.\n\n### D-001 — Use the established isolated dual-Firefox virtual-desktop rig; Bytebot is excluded\nDate: 2026-08-14\nOwner-directed method: mirror su-73a52's real-browser E2E procedure with a newly allocated Xvfb display, Openbox, two independent Firefox instances, separate profiles under the Snap-confined ~/snap/firefox/common tree, and two loopback-only geckodriver endpoints. Do not use Bytebot. Do not address DISPLAY=:0, su-73a52's DISPLAY=:110, ports 4444/4445, or any peer-owned process. Resolve fresh display/ports before launch, track exact owned PIDs and WebDriver session ids, capture visual/browser evidence, and tear down only resources launched by this work item.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-002 — Tone behavior must be provider-independent\nDate: 2026-08-15\nWarm, playful, and minimal are product-visible promises, so each must produce distinct wording even when SideStage uses its deterministic no-credential generator. Remote model availability may improve prose but may not determine whether the setting works.\nRelated: P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-003 — Reply tone changes phrasing only\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe setting affects the buyer-facing reply draft that the seller reviews. It does not alter grounding, citations, approval/automation level, price floors, inventory checks, or buyer-sensitive guardrails.\nRelated: P-010, P-011, P-013\n\n### D-004 — Published policy keeps precedence\nDate: 2026-08-15\nAn active published event/seller policy remains authoritative over the event-default replyTone selection. The existing warning in Settings remains the disclosure; this work does not weaken policy precedence.\nRelated: P-010, P-013\n\n### D-005 — Production model configuration is optional and fail-safe\nDate: 2026-08-15\nExpose OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, and SIDESTAGE_COPILOT_MODEL through the production compose seam without requiring them. Empty/missing values keep the audited deterministic generator active; no secret is committed.\nRelated: P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n## Verification\nAn end-to-end test must prove that a buyer question produces a grounded proposal, appears through sync, can be approved exactly once into event chat, can be skipped without sending, rejects stale facts, and routes confirmed actions through the guarded executor.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-stripe-orders-auction-checkout-2026-08-14","title":"Replace SideStage Square with Stripe and complete Orders, auction-win, and checkout recovery","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Replace SideStage Square with Stripe and complete Orders, auction-win, and checkout recovery\nslug: sidestage-stripe-orders-auction-checkout-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n# Replace SideStage Square with Stripe and complete Orders, auction-win, and checkout recovery\n\n## Goal\nMake SideStage own the complete buyer order lifecycle in Postgres while using Stripe only to execute payments. Buyers can start or resume checkout for a normal cart, auction win, or accepted payable offer; see the resulting order and live payment state in Orders; and recover after a closed browser or failed payment without duplicate orders, repricing, or lost reservations.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ACTIVE under Avi-approved route A and AUTO mode. P-001 is converted to WI-39074 and held by su-bfb8a397-92d4-476f-be09-c17a2259ba8f. No other implementation item is claimed; dependency order remains authoritative.\n\n**Next:** Implement and verify P-001 canonical SideStage-owned payable-order schema/store and migration, then complete it with evidence before taking P-002/P-003.\n\n## Current verified state\n- SideStage already stores checkout orders in its own `checkout_order` Postgres table; Square does not own the order data.\n- Square is hard-coded across the Nest provider, browser SDK/card element, confirmation endpoint, rehearsals, tests, environment names, and copy.\n- `orders.byBuyer` aggregates checkout orders, auction winner records, and offers, and the web Orders tab subscribes to it.\n- Auction close stores a durable winner-order snapshot in `auction_state` and keeps its inventory reservation, but its status remains `pending` and no payment handoff exists.\n- Orders sends a pending auction winner back to the event, labels it Pending, and cannot open checkout.\n- The existing right-side drawer already owns address → shipping → payment for held cart items and is the surface to extend.\n- The browser currently supplies a selected demo buyer; `sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14` is establishing the request-principal contract this plan must consume.\n- iOS still uses a legacy checkout-only Orders model while web/shared core have unified order-history support.\n\n## Restart architecture to reuse\nRestart creates an application-owned pending order, creates a Stripe PaymentIntent server-side with an order-derived idempotency key, returns only the client secret, renders Stripe Payment Element, and treats a verified raw-body webhook as the authority that updates application-owned payment/order state. Provider IDs and errors are metadata beside the order; Stripe is never the order database. Reuse that lifecycle and its idempotency/webhook tests while retaining SideStage's cart, shipping, inventory, sync, and drawer surfaces.\n\n## Target data and state model\n- Extend the existing `checkout_order` into the canonical payable-order record; do not create a parallel order system. Lift buyer ID, source kind, source ID, payment state, and Stripe PaymentIntent ID into validated/indexed columns while retaining immutable item, price, shipping, address, event, and source snapshots in the payload.\n- Support `cart`, `auction`, and `offer` sources with a unique `(source_kind, source_id)` key. An auction order keeps its winner order ID and winning unit price; it is never reconstructed from catalog price.\n- Use explicit purchase states: `payment_required`, `payment_processing`, `paid`, `payment_failed`, `cancelled`, and `expired`; migrate legacy `pending` records deterministically.\n- Keep Stripe references, attempt/error metadata, and webhook evidence in SideStage's database. Stripe receives only the amount, currency, application references, and receipt data needed to process payment.\n- The verified Stripe webhook is payment-state authority. Client confirmation improves UX but cannot mark paid. Every transition and side effect is idempotent under retries, duplicate delivery, and out-of-order delivery.\n\n## Required buyer experience\n- Orders remains the canonical recovery point, reading SideStage data through principal-scoped `orders.byBuyer` and existing sync invalidations.\n- Unpaid sources display `Payment required`; failures display `Payment failed`; processing and paid are distinct.\n- A primary `Checkout`/`Resume checkout` action opens the existing right-side drawer at address with the exact canonical order. It never adds an auction/offer item to the ordinary cart or creates a duplicate.\n- The auction winner banner exposes the same action as a convenience; Orders remains durable recovery.\n- Address and server-quoted shipping may update an unpaid order, but source price and reservation identity remain immutable.\n- Payment success commits the correct cart or auction/offer reservation once, invalidates Orders/event/pricing/inventory reads, and shows success. Failure is safely retryable. Cancellation/expiry releases the matching reservation under the existing policy window.\n\n## Security and correctness\n- Never trust client buyer ID, amount, price, shipping cost, source, or ownership. Resolve principal and money/reservations from SideStage records.\n- Missing and foreign order IDs produce the same response. A buyer cannot read, resume, or pay another buyer's order.\n- Verify Stripe signatures against the exact raw body. Reject amount/currency/order metadata that disagrees with SideStage.\n- Preserve in-memory parity for tests; production remains Postgres-only. No rehearsal or test may make a real charge.\n\n## Dependencies and reuse\n- Reuse shipped `sidestage-held-items-expiry-checkout-2026-08-14` for reservation expiry and drawer handoff.\nThis plan consumes P-001/P-002 from `sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14` and does not create another identity system.\n- Reuse `checkout_order`, `auction_state`, source-tracked inventory holds, shipping quotes, `orders.byBuyer`, sync invalidations, and BuyerCheckout.\n- Reuse Restart's Stripe provider, PaymentIntent idempotency, Payment Element, raw-body webhook verification, and redelivery tests, but not its Odoo, Signifyd, queues, or unrelated storefront layers.\n- Coordinate with `sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14` for auction ownership/settlement invariants; do not reopen its transport/public-chat scope.\n\n## Out of scope\nMoving order history into a processor; replacing the drawer with Restart's page; copying Odoo/Signifyd/procurement; production account authentication beyond the linked identity plan; refunds, disputes, subscriptions, multi-currency, taxes, and fulfillment UI.\n\n## Release acceptance\n- No executable Square provider, SDK, confirm path, runtime credential, rehearsal claim, or buyer-facing Square copy remains.\n- Stripe test-mode cart checkout, auction-win checkout, Orders recovery, failure retry, duplicate submit/webhook, and browser refresh produce no duplicate order or charge.\n- Order/payment/source state is readable from SideStage Postgres without Stripe and `orders.byBuyer` is current after every transition.\n- A two-buyer matrix proves IDs, caches, invalidations, checkout sessions, and webhook side effects cannot cross principals.\n- Web and iOS Orders share source/status semantics and recovery actions.\n- API/web/shared-core/iOS tests, migration checks, typecheck/build, webhook fixtures, and rendered desktop/mobile QA are green before release.\n\n## Phase 1 — Canonical SideStage order model\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend the existing checkout_order schema/store into the canonical application-owned payable order for cart, auction, and accepted-offer sources. Add lifted buyer_id, source_kind, source_id, payment_state, and unique Stripe PaymentIntent reference; make cart_id source-appropriate; enforce unique source identity and buyer/status indexes; migrate legacy pending checkout and auction winner records without changing order IDs, winning prices, item snapshots, or reservations. Keep Postgres and in-memory stores behaviorally identical and update schema guards. Acceptance: clean and existing-database migrations are repeatable, one source cannot yield two orders, provider lookup is indexed/idempotent, and every order remains fully readable without Stripe. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39074 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Stripe payment lifecycle\n\n- **P-002** `done` Replace SquareSandboxProvider with a SideStage Stripe PaymentIntent provider adapted from Restart: lazy test/live configuration, order-derived idempotency key, server-authoritative amount/currency/metadata, client secret only in the session response, and no synchronous server confirm path. Add raw-body Stripe webhook routing and signature verification; normalize succeeded/failed events; reject provider metadata or amounts that disagree with SideStage; make duplicate/out-of-order delivery and side effects idempotent. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39088 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Create one source-aware order-to-checkout service seam for cart, auction winner, and accepted payable offer. It must load/owner-check the canonical SideStage order, preserve source price/quantity/order ID, attach server-quoted shipping and address, create or resume the order's PaymentIntent, and commit/release the exact source reservation on terminal transitions. Cart creation, auction close, and offer acceptance must materialize or reuse exactly one canonical order and emit the existing sync invalidations. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39094 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Buyer checkout and Orders recovery\n\n- **P-004** `done` Replace the Square browser SDK/card component and confirm mutation with Stripe.js Payment Element inside the existing right-side BuyerCheckout drawer. Extend the drawer/provider to open from a canonical order (not only a cart), begin at address, obtain server shipping quotes, resume the same PaymentIntent after refresh/reopen, distinguish required/processing/failure/success states, and invalidate buyer orders after transitions. Remove Square-specific API types, sourceId flows, labels, styles, and configuration UI. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39172 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Make orders.byBuyer the principal-scoped canonical read model over SideStage-owned order data and finish the Orders UI action contract. Resolve buyer identity on the server instead of trusting query/body buyerId; return normalized source, payment state, totals, immutable snapshots, and an explicit checkout capability; label Payment required/Payment failed/Processing/Paid correctly; filter needs-action correctly; and open the checkout drawer directly for payable/resumable orders. Keep existing event/video context and live sync invalidations. blocked-by: P-001, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39190 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `todo` Finish auction-win and accepted-offer recovery. On auction settlement and payable offer acceptance, materialize/reuse the canonical order while preserving the source order ID, winning/accepted price, quantity, buyer, event, and inventory hold. Add a primary Checkout action to the auction winner banner and the matching Orders card; never add the item to a normal cart or reprice from catalog. Verify payment success commits the auction/offer reservation once and failure/expiry/cancellation follows the defined release policy. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005 importance: high\n\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Cross-client parity\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Bring sidestage-mobile shared core and iOS Orders/checkout onto the canonical order source/status/action contract. Replace the legacy checkout-only order view, include auction wins and payable offers, show the same payment labels and recovery actions, and drive Stripe checkout through the supported native/web presentation without creating an iOS-only order store or processor model. Add shared-core and iOS model/view-model tests for source mapping, ownership, recovery, and refresh after webhook-driven changes. blocked-by: P-004, P-005, P-006 importance: high\n\n## Phase 5 — Verification and release\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Add the recurrence guards and run the full payment/order verification matrix: schema migration and rollback probes; provider and raw-webhook signature fixtures; PaymentIntent/session idempotency; duplicate, delayed, failed, wrong-amount, wrong-buyer, and out-of-order events; cart/auction/offer reservation commit/release; two-buyer non-enumeration; sync invalidations; clean-clone in-memory parity; focused API/web/shared-core/iOS suites; typecheck/build; and Verdict desktop/mobile flows from source event and Orders recovery. Rehearsals must use a fake provider and clearly state that no real charge was made. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007 importance: urgent\n- **P-009** `todo` Complete the processor cutover and operational proof. Remove Square runtime packages, SDK loading, routes, env keys, system-test prerequisites, rehearsals, copy, and deployment configuration; add Stripe publishable/secret/webhook-secret configuration and raw-body route wiring; register the webhook for the deployed environment; verify test-mode end to end; inspect the release gate and pipeline; rerun the verdict after any gate fix; and confirm deployed Orders/checkout behavior plus database state before marking the plan shipped. blocked-by: P-008 importance: urgent\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — SideStage owns orders; Stripe only processes payments\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe canonical order, item/source snapshots, buyer ownership, totals, reservation references, payment state, and recovery history live in SideStage Postgres. Stripe receives only the fields needed to execute a payment and returns provider references/events. Orders never reads Stripe to reconstruct purchase history.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Extend checkout_order instead of introducing a parallel order system\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEvolve the existing checkout_order store into the canonical payable-order surface for cart, auction, and accepted-offer sources. Lift the fields required for ownership, uniqueness, state transitions, and Stripe webhook lookup; keep immutable domain snapshots in the payload. Auction and offer aggregates remain source authorities, but each payable source maps to exactly one canonical order.\nRelated: P-001, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Use Restart's Stripe lifecycle, not its unrelated commerce stack\nDate: 2026-08-14\nAdopt Restart's server-created PaymentIntent, order-derived idempotency key, Stripe Payment Element, raw-body signature verification, webhook-authoritative state transitions, and redelivery guards. Do not import Restart's Odoo, Signifyd, queue, procurement, standalone checkout-page, or storefront layers.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-008\n\n### D-004 — Webhook state is authoritative and side effects are exactly-once\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe browser cannot mark an order paid. A verified Stripe webhook drives processing/success/failure. Duplicate, delayed, or reordered deliveries must not double-commit reservations, double-emit invalidations, or regress a terminal state. Provider events that disagree with SideStage ownership, amount, currency, or metadata are rejected and recorded.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-008\n\n### D-005 — Orders is the canonical buyer recovery surface\nDate: 2026-08-14\nEvery payable source appears in Orders from SideStage data with explicit source, state, totals, and capability. Payment-required/failed records expose Checkout or Resume checkout into the existing drawer; the auction banner may expose the same action as a convenience. Source-specific prices and IDs are preserved and no auction/offer purchase is rebuilt as an ordinary cart item.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-006 — Principal and reservation contracts are mandatory inputs\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe execution design is required to build on the request-principal/ownership contract tracked in sidestage-demo-user-isolation-2026-08-14 and the reservation/expiry/drawer contract tracked in sidestage-held-items-expiry-checkout-2026-08-14. It may not trust client buyer IDs, create a second identity system, or replace source-tracked cart/auction reservations. P-003, P-005, P-006, and P-008 supply the implementation and verification evidence for this boundary.\n\n### D-007 — Remove Square rather than preserve a dormant provider toggle\nDate: 2026-08-14\nAvi explicitly chose Stripe and does not want SideStage using Square. Remove executable Square server/client paths, credentials, tests, rehearsals, and product copy during cutover. The internal payment seam may remain provider-shaped where it improves testability, but SideStage ships one configured runtime provider: Stripe.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-009\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-studio-transcript-overlay-2026-08-14","title":"Consolidate live transcription into the Studio live console","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Consolidate live transcription into the Studio live console\nslug: sidestage-studio-transcript-overlay-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-14\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n## Goal\nMake transcription a capability of the live stream rather than a separate Studio workspace: it follows the publisher session, captions appear over the video, product context is inherited from the canonical active item, and full history remains available on demand.\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extract the transcript runtime into a stable controller owned above dock/mobile presentation; preserve provider fallback, final-segment persistence, product mention intent, and add publisher-session-driven start/stop behavior. importance: high — note: ← WI-38955 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Build the accessible Live console caption overlay and expandable history using the existing overlay/status/action-chip language; inherit active product state and keep transcript mention staging without a duplicate picker. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-38956 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Remove the Transcript pane from the desktop panel inventory/default and restored layouts, update mobile wiring so the Stage surface owns captions, and delete obsolete adapters/styles while preserving layout compatibility. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-38970 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Update focused tests, validate and lint the UI IR design spec, run web type/test/build checks, and browser-verify desktop and mobile interactions, accessibility state, responsive layout, and console cleanliness. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-38979 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Shared engagement overlay\n\n- **P-005** `done` Expose event transcript moments through the existing event-scoped sync query registry and invalidate that query whenever a seller persists a new transcript moment; add focused API contract tests. importance: high — note: Added event.chat.transcript to ChatSyncQueries and invalidated it on every transcript write. Verified with npx vitest run --project sidestage-node apps/api/src/chat/chat.service.spec.ts: 9/9 passed.\n- **P-006** `done` Build a shared transcript-and-Event-Chat video overlay, with a remote transcript presentation model for buyers and the existing live transcript controller for sellers; mount the shared component in both BuyerTab and StageStatusPanel. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-39010 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Retire standalone seller Event Chat from default desktop/mobile layouts and migrate persisted active-event layouts, then update focused tests, UI IR, and browser QA for buyer and seller desktop/mobile. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-39015 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Product-focus remediation\n\n- **P-008** `done` Build a catalog-aware transcript focus domain model over rolling finalized context: active-product suppression, explicit transition evidence, ambiguity handling, stable confidence, dismissal cooldown/expiry, and focused pure tests. Link and resolve EI-20469306085034198. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39055 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Add the deterministic-first, server-side structured semantic fallback using the existing configured model pattern; validate catalog-bound structured output, fail harmlessly, and cover remote/deterministic/error contracts. blocked-by: P-008 importance: high — note: Configured strict structured classifier + REST seam landed; 8 focused API tests and API typecheck pass.\n- **P-010** `done` Integrate focus detection into useLiveTranscript and the Live console suggestion UI with stale-request guards, pending confirmation TTL, accept/dismiss semantics, current event catalog context, and downstream active-product transition coverage. blocked-by: P-008, P-009 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39057 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Run focused and full web/API verification, production builds, diff checks, and rendered desktop/mobile browser acceptance for same-product suppression, genuine transition suggestion, dismissal, acceptance, ambiguity, and classifier failure safety; close the bug and plan phase with evidence. blocked-by: P-010 importance: high — note: ← WI-39058 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Deepgram public-release hardening\n\n- **P-012** `done` Move Deepgram authority to the SideStage API: store the permanent project key only in injected server configuration, add an authenticated short-lived token grant endpoint with explicit failure semantics, rate/abuse protections, and focused API/security tests; never expose a permanent credential through Vite or application responses. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39066 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Wire the seller transcription runtime to request a fresh short-lived Deepgram token at connection time, authenticate the Deepgram WebSocket using the supported browser contract, remove the client-exposed VITE_DEEPGRAM_TOKEN path, preserve explicit Web Speech fallback behavior, and add focused browser-unit coverage. blocked-by: P-012 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39075 completed (done)\n- **P-014** `wip` Prove public-release readiness end to end: secret-scan the production bundle, run focused and full web/API suites plus builds, exercise a real Deepgram publisher session and shared buyer transcript delivery, browser-verify seller/viewer desktop and mobile behavior, then carry the green revision through the release pipeline and record deployment evidence. blocked-by: P-013 importance: urgent — note: D-010: approved replacement credential independently passes real grant, bearer Listen WebSocket, known-phrase final transcript, and live production-container grant. Resume current-tree gates, exact bridge lineage, guarded deploy, and fresh public buyer proof.\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n- The App-level `selectedProductId` remains the single source of truth. Transcript UI may display it and transcript mention suggestions may stage a detected product, but there is no general-purpose duplicate picker.\n- Transcription lifecycle belongs above presentation and follows the publisher media stream. Hiding/collapsing captions or changing responsive layout must not tear down ingestion.\n- Reuse the existing Live console video-overlay language and action-chip patterns. Registry search returned no matching primitives, so no new parallel component system will be introduced.\n- Show a compact caption layer by default with an accessible, expandable transcript history and explicit transcription status/error affordances. Compose it with the existing audience-chat overlay instead of stacking opaque panels.\n- Preserve final-segment recording, active-product tagging, product-mention confirmation, replay-chapter input, and Web Speech fallback behavior.\n\n### D-001 — One engagement overlay is the default buyer and seller surface\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe live video surface owns both transcript context and Event Chat for both roles. Sellers keep the existing live transcript controller (capture, provider state, expandable history); buyers read persisted transcript moments through the event-scoped sync query. Standalone Event Chat remains a compatibility panel type for restored/custom layouts only, but it is removed from default desktop and mobile navigation and migrated out of persisted active-event layouts.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-002 — Product-focus detection is deterministic-first and model-advisory\nDate: 2026-08-14\nFinalized transcript context first passes a local catalog-aware transition policy. A narrow server-side structured classifier is consulted only for unresolved candidate context. Model output never mutates active product state and any timeout, malformed output, stale result, low confidence, or non-catalog product fails to no suggestion.\nRelated: P-008, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-003 — The existing App active-product setter remains the authority\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThis remediation reuses App-level selectedProductId/onActiveProductChange, matching the plan's existing source-of-truth decision. Accepting a fresh suggestion or speaking an explicit confirmation invokes that setter. Event-wide durable active-product synchronization is not silently introduced as part of transcript detection.\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-004 — Suggestion safety requires explicit seller confirmation\nDate: 2026-08-14\nA detected topic shift creates an expiring suggestion only. The product changes solely through a seller click or an explicit confirmation phrase while that exact suggestion is fresh. Repeated mentions, stale async responses, current-product mentions, ambiguous comparisons, and dismissed candidates cannot stage a product.\nRelated: P-008, P-010\n\n### D-005 — Detection uses event-relevant catalog context, not the three-card presentation slice\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe detector must not inherit the current seller shell's pageSize:3 presentation limit. Candidate context comes from the full in-stock/event-relevant catalog available to the Studio, with IDs validated against the live product set before suggestions are accepted.\nRelated: P-008, P-010\n\n### D-006 — Deepgram uses server-held authority and per-session browser tokens\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe permanent Deepgram project key is server-only injected configuration. At publisher connection start, an authenticated SideStage API route exchanges it at Deepgram /v1/auth/grant for a short-lived JWT and returns only that JWT to the authorized seller. The browser opens the direct realtime Listen WebSocket with the JWT; no permanent key or VITE-prefixed Deepgram secret is shipped. Buyers continue reading the one event-scoped persisted transcript and never create transcription sessions. Web Speech remains an explicit availability fallback, not a silent credential failure mask.\nRelated: P-012, P-013, P-014\n\n### D-007 — Shipment follows the current plan scope, not the superseded seven-item slice\nDate: 2026-08-14\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe plan expanded from P-001..P-007 to P-001..P-014 through the ratified product-focus and Deepgram decisions. Audit seq 2 at ba972f4 and scorecard EI-20470060866047487 remain valid evidence for the original P-001..P-007 slice, but they are not sufficient to ship the expanded plan. P-007 still requires the independent responsive-fix regrade already tracked as WI-39061. Final shipment requires every current item P-001..P-014 terminal, a fresh code-truth audit covering all fourteen items, an acceptance rubric expanded to the new product-focus and Deepgram outcomes, and a complete independent scorecard against that current rubric. Legacy EI-20465831422377375 remains excluded.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014\n\n### D-008 — P-014 remains unshippable until real provider credentials are provisioned\nDate: 2026-08-15\nP-014's code, secret-scan, focused/full local suites and builds, seller desktop/mobile browser acceptance, and persisted seller-to-buyer transcript delivery are verified. The remaining real-provider and public-deploy gates are external credential walls, not code failures: the live operator registry, local SideStage env files, shell/user-manager environment, /opt/SideStage/.env.production, and the running production API container all lack DEEPGRAM_API_KEY; production also lacks STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET now required by the fail-closed compose contract. Do not reuse an unrelated benchmark/project credential, synthesize placeholders, downgrade the compose requirement, or claim the Deepgram socket/deploy path green. P-014 is terminalized as needs-human with typed credential blocker EI-20477672654877961. Resume only after approved real values are injected outside the repo; then run the authenticated Deepgram grant/WebSocket/caption path, full current-head gates, guarded production deploy, and public buyer reproof before shipment.\nRelated: P-014\n\n### D-009 — Credential presence is not Deepgram release readiness; the grant and socket must succeed\nDate: 2026-08-15\nEI-20477672654877961 proves that DEEPGRAM_API_KEY and the Stripe trio are present exactly once and non-empty in production, but it does not prove provider authorization. The real encrypted-key proof on 2026-08-15 used capability:bash.integration_env without exposing the key. Deepgram POST /v1/auth/grant returned HTTP 403 with the bounded allowlisted payload FORBIDDEN / Insufficient permissions; no WebSocket opened. This directly confirms that the saved key lacks the grant authority required by the browser-safe temporary-token design. P-014 remains non-terminal under EI-20488444691160764 until SIDESTAGE_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY is replaced with a Deepgram key carrying Member-or-higher authorization (per current official Deepgram grant documentation) and that key passes the authenticated temporary-token grant, bearer-subprotocol Listen WebSocket, known-phrase final transcript, guarded production deploy, and public buyer readback. Do not treat environment presence or exact registry equality as functional credential clearance.\nRelated: P-014\n\n### D-010 — Replacement credential clears the provider-authorization wall; release gates remain\nDate: 2026-08-15\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe encrypted SIDESTAGE_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY was replaced with Avi's approved grant-capable credential. Two secret-safe proofs now establish functional authorization without exposing the permanent key: (1) staging capability:bash.integration_env obtained POST /v1/auth/grant HTTP 200, opened the Listen WebSocket with the bearer subprotocol, streamed synthesized Opus audio, and received the known phrase as a final transcript; (2) the running production API container independently obtained HTTP 200 and a token from /v1/auth/grant. A byte-equivalent comparison also proves /opt/SideStage/.env.production already matches the replacement registry value; its mtime and the current container start predate the registry replacement, so production already held the working key and the encrypted registry was the stale location. This supersedes D-008's credential-absence snapshot and D-009's 403 condition for the credential wall only. P-014 resumes wip, but remains unshippable until current-tree full checks/builds and web-bundle secret scan pass, Papercusp bridge 5369b83c3 has exact green/deployed lineage, the guarded SideStage revision deploys, and a fresh public seller-to-buyer transcript readback is clean. Never record or expose the permanent key value.\nRelated: P-014\n\n## Acceptance\n- Starting a live publisher session starts transcription when audio is available; ending it stops transcription.\n- Desktop and mobile both expose live captions inside the Live console.\n- The separate Transcript dock panel and its Active item dropdown are absent from fresh and restored layouts.\n- An active product selected elsewhere is reflected without a second selector; mention suggestions remain actionable.\n- Transcript history is keyboard-accessible, screen-reader friendly, scrollable, and does not obscure core stream controls.\n- Focused unit/component tests, type/build checks, design-spec validation/lint, and rendered desktop/mobile browser verification pass.\n\n## Out of scope\n- Changing the current backend retention model from the capped in-memory transcript store to durable archival storage. That is a separate data-lifecycle feature; this plan preserves the existing recording contract.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-desktop-release-0-0-17-alpha","title":"Acceptance — stable 0.0.17 tri-platform desktop release","status":"active","created":"2026-08-15","owner":"su-7f4f948f-0e09-472d-8ed6-6d8f4896649b","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — stable 0.0.17 tri-platform desktop release\nslug: acceptance-desktop-release-0-0-17-alpha\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\nowner: su-7f4f948f-0e09-472d-8ed6-6d8f4896649b\n---\n\n# Acceptance — stable 0.0.17 tri-platform desktop release\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric).
