Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"generalized-project-history-pipeline-2026-08-14","title":"Generalized Papercusp project History pipeline with SideStage as first consumer","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Generalized Papercusp project History pipeline with SideStage as first consumer\nslug: generalized-project-history-pipeline-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n# Generalized Papercusp project History pipeline with SideStage as first consumer\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** OWNER AMENDMENT 2026-08-21: P-001..P-006 remain complete. P-007..P-011 reopen the plan for a validation-aware reusable History product surface. D-007 governs: schema + renderer are shared Papercusp assets; SideStage and other consumers supply styling/labels/actions/transport only. su-8d787 owns the self route from implementation through verification.\n\n**Next:** P-007 contract/provider audit and P-008 UI-boundary audit first; then implement shared validation model + reusable renderer, migrate SideStage, add Papercusp More → History, and close with cross-consumer tests.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Foundation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Define the product-neutral Project History v1 contract, compatibility fixtures, and public package boundary importance: high — note: ← WI-39133 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement the deterministic assembler, provider interfaces, validation, and generic generator command blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39135 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Repair authoritative work-item ownership propagation into edit and git-sync commit attribution, with recurrence tests importance: high — note: ← WI-39137 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — First consumer\n\n- **P-004** `done` Migrate SideStage snapshot generation and History page to the shared pipeline, including commit links and provenance blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39138 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add reusable project onboarding through the existing Papercusp template/aspect and documentation seams blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39139 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Run compatibility, unit, integration, and end-to-end verification; resolve regressions and record rollout evidence blocked-by: P-004, P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-39140 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Validation-aware reusable UI\n\n- **P-007** `blocked` Extend the shared versioned Project History contract and provider boundary with validation assertions, status, evidence provenance, timestamps, and commit linkage; preserve compatibility and fail loudly on silently incomplete validation reads. importance: high — note: → WI-40426\n- **P-008** `done` Extract SideStage's product-neutral History presentation, filtering, summaries, dialogs, and validation proof UI into a reusable Papercusp History UI package; expose consumer theming/labels/actions without product assumptions. importance: high — note: ← WI-40427 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `todo` Replace SideStage's bespoke History implementation with a thin data transport plus SideStage styling adapter using the shared History UI. blocked-by: P-008 importance: high\n- **P-010** `todo` Add a History tab under Papercusp More that renders the same shared History UI for the active project/harness. blocked-by: P-007, P-008 importance: high\n- **P-011** `todo` Add compatibility, provider, UI, adapter, navigation, accessibility, and stale-artifact regression coverage; verify both Papercusp and SideStage consumers. blocked-by: P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — History output is a disposable versioned read model\nDate: 2026-08-15\nPapercusp work-item/plan ledgers, git_sync_commit_attribution, Git, and build metadata remain authoritative. project-history.v1.json is deterministic derived output and never becomes another source of truth.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-002 — Core stays product-neutral; consumers supply thin adapters\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe schema and assembler cannot know SideStage routes, React composition, labels, or filesystem layout. SideStage is the first provider/configuration adapter and the shared viewer consumes only the versioned contract.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-004\n\n### D-003 — Commit relationships carry provenance and remote status\nDate: 2026-08-15\nAuthoritative ledger/trailer links, commit-body references, and inferred historical matches remain distinguishable. A commit URL is exposed only when repository identity is known; remote confirmation is represented separately from local commit existence. Completion treeStamp is verification metadata, never the landed commit.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-004 — Generated artifact is the default transport\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe reusable generator writes a validated versioned JSON artifact that can be served statically or through a project API adapter. Page rendering must not require a live operator/database connection.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-005 — SideStage migration is compatibility-first\nDate: 2026-08-15\nCapture current output as fixtures, run the shared assembler through a thin SideStage adapter, preserve observable History behavior, and cut over only after semantic comparison and focused tests pass.\nRelated: P-001, P-004, P-006\n\n### D-006 — Repo-root-anchored paths resolve by upward walk, never by a fixed hop count\nDate: 2026-08-15\nEstablished while verifying P-006 (WI-39140), from the root cause of EI-20491664483776609.\n\nRULING: any code locating a repo-root-anchored file MUST resolve it by a bounded UPWARD WALK that tests for the artifact itself, not by a fixed number of `..` hops from an app-root helper. Use the repoAnchoredCandidates(start, relPath, depth) pattern in packages/operator-core/lib/desktop-install/papercusp-files.ts, applied to BOTH the app-root anchor and process.cwd().\n\nWHY (measured, not inferred): resolveOperatorAppRoot() walks up 2 from the module dir. That is correct for the tsx SOURCE layout but wrong for the esbuild-BUNDLED layout, where the bundle sits at apps/operator/dist-host/ — one level DEEPER than the source file it replaces — so the identical two hops land one level high (<release>/apps instead of <release>/apps/operator). cwd is not a safe backstop either: the deployed :3070 operator runs with cwd <release>/apps/operator, not the repo root. Under those measured anchors all five previous candidates missed on disk while the target file existed.\n\nCONSEQUENCE THIS PREVENTS: the failure is SILENT and INTERMITTENT. The resolver returns null, the caller degrades to writing an install with the feature quietly absent, and the install still reports success — so it ships on a green deploy with nothing failing. Worse, because the artifact is rewritten by whichever operator last ran the installer, a canonical-tree run masks a release-tree run: the same file was observed at 966 bytes without the project-history route and 1207 bytes with it on the same afternoon. That is why EI-20491664483776609 survived roughly twenty cold wakes of \"wait for the deploy, then verify\" — the symptom was never deploy-controlled.\n\nTESTING COROLLARY (binding on any guard for this class): pin the anchors MEASURED from the deployed process, not the layout the source happens to have. The pre-existing test pinned operatorRoot='/repo/apps/operator' and stayed green throughout, because it encoded the assumption rather than the deployment. Every such guard must also carry a calibration control that reimplements the retired resolution and asserts it MISSES, so the guard cannot pass vacuously and a revert goes red instead of silently shipping the feature absent.\n\n### D-007 — History is a shared validation-aware product surface; consumers own styling only\nDate: 2026-08-22\nOwner amendment, 2026-08-21. The Project History page is no longer a SideStage product component backed by a generic data artifact. Both the versioned read model and the interactive renderer are Papercusp-owned reusable surfaces. The shared contract carries canonical inline VAL assertion definitions plus validation status/evidence provenance and exact commit linkage; the UI renders concise proof summaries with expandable details. SideStage and every other consumer may supply styling tokens, product labels, links/actions, and a transport adapter, but must not fork filtering, summaries, evidence rendering, dialogs, accessibility behavior, or schema interpretation. Papercusp exposes this same surface at More → History for the active project/harness. Raw validator logs remain out of the main timeline; proof is attached to its owning plan item/work item and incomplete/stale validation is explicit.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011\n\n### D-008 — Validated reusable History UI specification and component boundary\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe approved design pass searched the active registry by role. Only feedback.banner matched the cross-consumer History surface; tabs, filters, disclosures, dialogs, and metrics had no registry entries. UI IR v0.1 for project-history validates with zero schema errors and lints with zero errors/warnings using feedback.banner as the known component. Per the canonical operator design guide, operator-specific controls must use existing wrappers (Modal, Select, TextInput, Button, Collapsible, Popover/Radix tabs) and semantic CSS variables because design-phase tokens are disconnected from the operator theme. The shared package therefore owns headless semantics/state/filtering/render structure and exposes class/slot customization; the Papercusp adapter uses operator wrappers/tokens, while SideStage provides its own theme and transport. No raw escape hatches or new design tokens are introduced.\nRelated: P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"papercusp-bug-drain-2026-08-15","title":"Papercusp bug-queue drain — 12x sonnet5-high headless fleet","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercusp bug-queue drain — 12x sonnet5-high headless fleet\nslug: papercusp-bug-drain-2026-08-15\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nDrive the papercusp **bug** family to terminal state (done / resolved / deprecated / needs_human) with a headless sonnet-5 high-effort fleet in DRAIN mode.\n\nBaseline measured 2026-08-15T22:31Z via `work_items:claimable { harness:'papercusp' }` — the authoritative oracle (all ~12 claim floors applied), NOT a raw `status='open'` count:\n\n- **3,722** claimable items total; **2,008 are `item_kind='bug'`** (1,363 change, 351 task).\n- Filing is bursty: **1,084** of the claimable bugs were filed on 2026-08-12 alone.\n- Composition sampled: genuine agent-DX / tool-contract defects — tool schema divergences, `coord:send` arg rejections, `lint:tsc` operator-path routing, focused-test-runner gate queuing, `locks:acquire` absolute-path handling. Small, independently fixable, parallelises well. Real drain material.\n\n⚠ `harness_shared.work_items.kind` is NULL for issue-family rows — the family lives in **`item_kind`**. A census filtering `kind='bug'` returns zero and reads exactly like a drained queue.\n\n## Scope\n\n- IN: `harness_slug='papercusp'`, `item_kind='bug'`, claimable (unclaimed, not needs_human, not held).\n- OUT: `change` / `task` families; the observation lane (26,608 excluded rows); anything `needs_human_review`.\n- Rank: critical -> major -> minor -> nit; oldest-first within a severity band.\n\n## Method\n\n- Members PULL via `scheduler:get_next` against a fleet-sentinel claim spec. No hand-assignment, no id-pins. An idle member with a nonempty queue is a SPEC bug, reported to the leader.\n- Completion integrity outranks burn-down speed: nothing goes terminal without evidence. `work_items:complete { completion }` must name what was verified and how; a bare \"done\" is re-opened by the leader's audit.\n- Per the DRAIN contract: no incidental `improvements:capture` rows, issues, or observations. Incidental findings ride on the current drain item's checkpoint. Only a defect that DIRECTLY blocks the drain gets one blocker row, linked to the active item.\n- A red release gate is the fleet's to green, not to wait behind.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-24. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nCanary launch, then 11 more members. Leader: su-f731e96d. Fleet slug `papercusp-bug-drain-0815`.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Fleet sized to 12 on the default account — the inference pool is measured-walled, not stale\nDate: 2026-08-15\nOwner asked for 30x sonnet5-high headless agents. A capacity preflight refused that number on measured evidence.\n\nMEASUREMENT (accounts:probe-capacity {apply:true} — reads the authoritative upstream anthropic-ratelimit-unified-* headers, one 1-token request per account through each account's own egress + credential):\n- 10 of 11 pool accounts answered upstream 429 with utilization7d = 1.0 (100% of the 7-day budget consumed). This is a genuine token-budget wall, NOT an egress artifact — an egress fault cannot produce upstream headers reporting a spent weekly budget.\n- 1 account (aviynw3) answered 200 with utilization 0.24 (5h) / 0.10 (7d) — real headroom.\n\nWHY THE FIRST READ WAS NOT TRUSTED: fleet:capacity initially returned blind:true, blindAccounts:5 — 5 of 6 readings rested on stale/missing data, and its own advice says a merely-stale reading is indistinguishable from a real wall until re-measured (EI-19928050541357086: one probe once flipped poolExhausted true->false with no other change). The probe was run BEFORE drawing any conclusion. After it, blind:false. The post-probe advice then blamed \"6/6 edge-throttled\" as the dominant cause, which is NOT consistent with aviynw3 answering 200 on a live probe — the per-account probe is the authority here, and it says budget, not egress.\n\nOWNER RULING (2026-08-15, interactive): 12 members, on the DEFAULT account, NO pinning. Recorded verbatim as the routing authority — account routing is the owner's call, never the leader's capacity read.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR MEMBERS: members route on the direct system credential with the gateway SKIPPED, so the walled pool does not gate this fleet (capacityClamp confirmed: \"healthyAccounts=4 (pool — does NOT gate this launch: members route on the direct system credential, gateway skipped)\"). Do not read the pool wall as a reason to stand down.\n\n### D-002 — Scope: the whole bug family, severity-ranked — not the 08-12 burst, not critical-only\nDate: 2026-08-15\nOwner ruling (2026-08-15, interactive): drain all claimable bugs, severity-ranked.\n\nClaim spec `papercusp-bug-drain-0815` rev 1 (fleet sentinel, so fresh member ownerIds inherit it):\n  filter: item_kind in [bug]   rank: severity_rank DESC -> priority ASC -> age DESC   states: [open, failing]\n\nPREVIEWED BEFORE WRITING (scheduler:preview_spec_delta, read-only): 2,001 admitted / 1,715 newly excluded / 0 newly admitted. Every excluded row is change- or task-family — confirming the bug family is a clean subset and the spec drops nothing in scope.\n\nMEMBERS FEED BY SPEC, NEVER BY HAND. Re-steer by bumping the spec revision — never id-pins, never hand-assignment. An idle member while the queue is nonempty is a SPEC bug, reported to the leader.\n\nCENSUS TRAP (cost a false \"zero open bugs\" reading on 2026-07-25): harness_shared.work_items.kind is NULL for every issue-family row — the family lives in item_kind. A census filtering kind='bug' returns ZERO rows and reads exactly like a fully drained queue. Use work_items:claimable (authoritative, applies the ~12 claim floors) or filter on item_kind.\n\n### D-003 — Two launch-path traps that make a healthy fleet look dead — do not act on either verdict\nDate: 2026-08-15\nBoth hit live during this fleet's canary. Recorded so the next leader does not mis-diagnose them.\n\n1. THE \"AGENT DID NOT START\" VERDICT IS A FALSE NEGATIVE. fleet:launch-on-plan returned code 502, \"✗ AGENT DID NOT START — no session registered within 24s ... psu died before reaching the operator\". The member was ALIVE: its log showed a live spinner titled \"Advance papercusp bug drain plan\", and harness_shared.tool_invocations showed 43 calls across 18 distinct tools within ~90s of launch. A headless psu boot simply takes longer than the 24s registration window. VERIFY LIVENESS FROM TOOL CALLS (tool_invocations by coord_owner_id), never from the launch verdict — and never relaunch a \"failed\" member without that check, or you stack duplicate members onto the same lane.\n\n2. THE 300s RELAUNCH GUARD BLOCKS THE MANDATED CANARY-FIRST RAMP. RELAUNCH_SUPPRESS_MS = 300_000 (launch-on-plan.ts:257) suppresses ANY re-call of the same fleet for 300s after a wave opens, so the canary-then-top-up pattern the persona requires cannot complete without waiting out the window. Already filed — EI-13483, plus EI-20497372063255974 / EI-20264052546303929 — so per the DRAIN defect-filing exception this fleet does NOT open another row for it. Useful detail measured here: a SUPPRESSED call does not bump agent_fleets.last_launch_at, so the window really does clear 300s after the ORIGINAL wave; poll it with `SELECT last_launch_at FROM harness_shared.agent_fleets WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND fleet_slug=...` rather than guessing.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"sidestage-cart-principal-boundary-acceptance","title":"SideStage cart principal boundary acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-15","owner":"su-a769477b-815a-44a0-88f9-560c20e8bc2e","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage cart principal boundary acceptance\nslug: sidestage-cart-principal-boundary-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-a769477b-815a-44a0-88f9-560c20e8bc2e\n---\n\n# SideStage cart principal boundary acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nOutcome-based acceptance for the buyer-cart isolation fix. A passing system binds cart ownership, denies cross-buyer access before any side effect, carries the canonical principal across all supported surfaces, and retains regression evidence.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-active-event-tabbed-inventory-rail-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage Active Event tabbed Inventory utility rail","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage Active Event tabbed Inventory utility rail\nslug: sidestage-active-event-tabbed-inventory-rail-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n# SideStage Active Event tabbed Inventory utility rail\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Implement the production Tabbed utility rail: add a compact Active Event inventory panel using the existing event.actions.items, event.adjustStock, and event.addItems seams; register it beside Run of Show in the dock; migrate saved layouts idempotently; add the mobile Inventory mode; ship focused unit and regression tests. importance: high — note: ← WI-39210 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Run focused SideStage web tests and typecheck, repair every failure, and record exact verification evidence. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39215 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `todo` Verify the Active Event Inventory tab end to end on desktop and mobile with Verdict, including tab switching, quantity controls, add-item affordance, responsive layout, console, and network health; then close the plan. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Implement the owner-selected Tabbed utility rail by extending existing event and dock seams\nDate: 2026-08-15\nDate: 2026-08-15\nAvi selected the Tabbed utility rail and authorized self-directed implementation. Inventory becomes a peer dock tab beside Run of Show on Active Event, while the existing standalone Inventory route remains available for full-catalog editing. The utility panel reuses event.actions.items, event.adjustStock, event.addItems, EventCreationPanel, and dock-workbench persistence; no parallel inventory API or store is introduced. Existing saved Active Event layouts are migrated in place so geometry is preserved, and Run of Show remains the initially selected tab to avoid disrupting live-show continuity. Low stock is defined as three or fewer event-reserved units and surfaced in the Inventory tab title.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Studio inventory is store-scoped, not Demo User-scoped\nDate: 2026-08-15\nAvi corrected the product contract on 2026-08-15: Studio inventory reads and writes bind to the stable Studio/store seller principal. For the current single-store demo, that principal is the legacy demo-seller. Switching the global Demo User may change buyer, Watch, Orders, chat, or other identity-sensitive behavior, but must never change Studio inventory. Do not restore or extend the prior auto-generated-principal folding behavior; future multi-store support requires an explicit store/workspace selector and authorization seam.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-assignment-gap-remediation-2026-08-15","title":"Close SideStage original-assignment audit gaps","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Close SideStage original-assignment audit gaps\nslug: sidestage-assignment-gap-remediation-2026-08-15\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-18\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ACTIVE under owner-directed AUTO with a leader-led fleet. Target-plan D-005 mirrors release-plan D-024 and supersedes D-023 only for one corrected-build path. The independently verified seller-principal repair is cleanly committed as ec755db738c778758368be696d2a0685e2aba281 descending deployed 075ecc; the last direct remote read still had origin/staging at cf3265f9. P-009 may now publish ec755db by normal git-sync, obtain a fresh authoritative SideStage verdict, deploy exactly one green pin, and run public seller-JHGLDS inventory/Copilot acceptance. EI-20485490544986949 stays blocked under d53 and EI-20496543498783917 stays blocked/unassigned until that fresh public proof. Fixture retries, force deploy, and generation-2 fire remain forbidden. P-001 and P-002 through P-012 remain frozen outside this exact D-005/D-024 exception.\n\n**Next:** su-2469e resumes WI-39007/P-009 under release-plan D-024: normal-publish ec755db, run a fresh SideStage verdict, fix and rerun any red, then perform one serialized green deployment and fresh public seller acceptance. Only after both residues terminalize from that proof may generation 2 fire and the frozen lanes be reconsidered.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Ground every factual reply claim in fresh catalog, event-listing, availability, policy, transcript, or labelled research evidence.\n2. Enforce price, availability, policy, and tone at the final server send boundary for generated and seller-edited replies, with typed rejection reasons.\n3. Execute push, swap, markdown, stock adjustment, and offers through guarded commands whose decisions, idempotency, before/after state, and rollback history survive restart.\n4. Wire catalog-first product research plus labelled fallback, with a real-provider complete-response p95 below the two-second target or a safe timeout/fallback.\n5. Make the public clean-clone path deterministic: the default reviewer event is owned/seeded and the documented commands work without private state.\n6. Require npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build to pass and exercise both API and web suites.\n7. Make PRD, TDD, README, and submission claims match the shipped implementation.\n\n## Design\n\nReuse and extend the existing copilot pipeline, reply/action guards, Postgres stores, policy resolver, research abstraction, latency recorder, test projects, and Verdict workflow. Do not create parallel safety, audit, benchmark, or demo systems.\n\nThe final-send boundary is authoritative: reload current context, bind each claim to evidence, and re-check price/availability/policy/tone immediately before ChatService broadcasts. Edited text cannot inherit stale draft citations without revalidation.\n\nExtend the existing Postgres action-store pattern for offers, accepted/rejected audits, idempotency outcomes, before/after snapshots, and rollback links. Preserve transactional and optimistic-concurrency semantics.\n\nFlow requiredProperties through UI and API into GroundedCopilotPipeline. Compose the existing ParallelResearchFallback with real providers under one deadline/cancellation budget. Late or incomplete research produces an explicit safe response.\n\nPreserve the documented zero-private-infrastructure default: npm run dev supplies a deterministic demo event when optional services are absent; Docker remains the production-like profile.\n\n## Verification gates\n\n- **Safety:** reject the zero-stock “999 in stock” exploit, stale price, invented shipping/returns policy, forged/irrelevant citations, tone mismatch, prompt injection, and stale-context races; supported edits still send.\n- **Durability:** accepted/rejected decisions, offers, idempotency, audit, and rollback survive API restart; duplicates apply once; rollback cannot erase newer work.\n- **Research:** public UI/API exercises required-property fallback with labelled sources and safe timeouts; production-like evidence records sample count, TTFT/completion p50/p95, provenance, and errors.\n- **Reproducibility:** fresh clone starts the default event, exercises a copilot reply/action, and passes documented test/typecheck/build commands.\n- **Release:** the tested commit is the deployed commit; Verdict and API evidence pass the assignment matrix with a clean console.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- Redesigning polished Watch, Studio, Event Manager, or Inventory UI.\n- Replacing existing copilot, sync, test, or Postgres infrastructure.\n- Expanding unrelated commerce features except to clear a real release gate.\n- Deploying a red or partially verified tree.\n\n## Phase 0 — Freeze the contract and restore a green baseline\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Pin a baseline and turn the audit into versioned executable fixtures: record commit/environment, reproduce clean-checkout test/build/local-demo failures, preserve the false-availability proof, and map every challenge requirement to its command, test, source boundary, and expected outcome. Acceptance: the matrix distinguishes clean-clone evidence from the moving shared tree. importance: urgent — note: D-008: SUPERSEDED, not achieved — fixture half is OBE (no clean-clone failures remain); the matrix deliverable is unmet and carried by P-012.\n- **P-002** `done` Repair every baseline npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build failure, including ownership-before-cleanup and database-parameter regressions; retain recurrence tests and ensure the top-level test command reaches the web suite. Acceptance: all three commands exit zero twice from a clean worktree. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: D-008: acceptance measured twice green (D-007); web-suite subclause confirmed (test:apps runs sidestage-web).\n\n## Phase 1 — Enforce claim-level reply safety\n\n- **P-003** `done` Define one structured claim/evidence contract for price, availability, listing state, shipping/returns policy, and catalog properties, including evidence relevance, context fingerprints, edited replies, and typed missing/stale/conflicting-evidence reasons. Add adversarial fixtures first. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39259 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Extend the existing reply guard/judge/approval seam to bind claims to fresh evidence and enforce price, availability, policy, and tone immediately before send. Rebuild/revalidate bindings for seller edits. Acceptance: supported edits send; unsupported/stale claims never persist or broadcast and return seller-readable reasons. blocked-by: P-003 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39260 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add unit, integration, and protocol tests for zero stock/“999,” stale price, invented policy, forged/irrelevant citations, tone mismatch, injection, concurrent inventory change, and valid edits. Exercise deterministic and configured real-provider paths without treating synthetic scores as system proof. Acceptance: the original exploit cannot score/pass or reach chat. blocked-by: P-004 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39261 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Make guarded-action history durable\n\n- **P-006** `done` Extend the existing Postgres schema/store with normalized offers, immutable accepted/rejected audits, idempotency outcomes, before/after snapshots, and rollback links, including constraints, retention, migrations, and repository contracts. Acceptance: rejected decisions are durable evidence but never mutate business state; no duplicate audit system is introduced. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39262 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Rewire GuardedActionService transactionally to the durable stores while preserving PolicyActionGuard and PgActionItemStore. Add restart-safe idempotency, optimistic rollback, recovery/readback, restart tests, and concurrency tests. Acceptance: duplicates apply once and rollback refuses to erase a newer seller action. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: D-008: every acceptance clause has an exact landed test (action.service.test.ts:187/310/340, action-item.store.test.ts:68).\n\n## Phase 3 — Finish research and prove latency\n\n- **P-008** `done` Carry requiredProperties through CopilotPanel, API input, proposal creation, and pipeline; inject ParallelResearchFallback with real catalog/labelled fallback providers plus shared deadline, cancellation, provenance, and safe incomplete-context behavior. Acceptance: a missing catalog property triggers labelled fallback through public UI/API and no late/unverified finding can send. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39264 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Extend existing latency/rehearsal surfaces into a production-like real-provider benchmark for catalog-only, fallback, timeout, and concurrent load. Persist/emit sample count, TTFT/completion p50/p95, provider/config provenance, and error rate. Acceptance: complete-response p95 is below 2,000 ms; otherwise the gate remains red and the product safely times out/falls back. blocked-by: P-008 importance: high — note: ← WI-39265 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Make the reviewer path deterministic and docs truthful\n\n- **P-010** `done` Make npm run dev supply the documented sunday-drop event with deterministic catalog/listing/policy data and correct seller ownership when optional infrastructure is absent; retain Docker mode. Add a startup smoke covering presence, seller copilot, one product question, and one guarded action without 404s. Acceptance: a fresh clone using only documented placeholders completes the walkthrough. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39266 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `todo` Reconcile PRD, TDD, README, and submission with durable Config save, final reply safety, durable actions, research/provenance, measured latency, infrastructure requirements, commands, and limitations. Acceptance: every claim links to current source/tests and every documented command/URL is re-executed successfully. blocked-by: P-005, P-007, P-009, P-010 importance: high — note: D-008: unassessed behavioural item — green build says nothing about it.\n\n## Phase 5 — Clean-clone acceptance and production proof\n\n- **P-012** `todo` Run a same-commit fresh-clone gate: setup, npm run dev smoke, npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run build, restart/durability checks, real-provider benchmark, and the full assignment matrix with Verdict. After green, ship normally and repeat critical production flows. Acceptance: production is clean, critical APIs are 2xx, tested/deployed commit matches, and the reviewer packet contains commands, results, latency, safety cases, screenshots, and rollback instructions. blocked-by: P-002, P-005, P-007, P-009, P-010, P-011 importance: urgent — note: D-008: NARROWED to the unrun legs — restart/durability, real-provider benchmark, matrix+Verdict, ship+prod flows, reviewer packet. Build legs only were run.\n\n## Assumptions for review\n\n1. Preserve the no-private-database default demo promise; Docker is optional production-like infrastructure.\n2. Treat real-provider complete-response p95 below 2,000 ms as a hard research gate.\n3. Persist rejected action decisions without forbidden business mutations.\n4. Keep suggestion/confirmation as the automation ceiling until safety and durability gates pass.\n5. Start no item and deploy nothing until this draft is approved and an execution route is selected.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — A mid-deploy release trace does not clear D-010 without live-process proof\nDate: 2026-08-15\nKeep D-010/P-001 closed. release:trace generatedAtMs 1786780624945 observed green pin/deploy-checkout parity while the safe deploy was still in flight. The deploy subsequently failed pre-cutover because papercup-release/node_modules/@papercusp/sse/dist/index.js was missing, rolled back, and :3070 remained on 962664ae. Clearance requires a fresh post-deploy read proving the actual serving process SHA equals exact tested/green 1feac8dd, followed by the launcher partial-canary behavior proof. Critical deploy blocker: EI-20505072457524017; parent launcher item: EI-20497372063255974.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-002 — Pinned runtime builds must restore the workspace-local toolchain; do not replace CommonJS output with TS-loader shims\nDate: 2026-08-15\nWI-39243 exact-pin evidence: SSE submodule 92d4f43 builds successfully with its declared package-local TypeScript 5.9.3, while the same source deterministically fails TS5107 when release setup omits libs/generic/sse/node_modules and falls back to root TypeScript 6.0.3. Restore only the registered runtime workspace's local node_modules immediately before its pinned build; do not force a full dependency-forest recopy. Keep the compiled CommonJS require/default contract; `require('../src/*.ts')` shims are loader-dependent and are not valid plain-Node artifacts. Focused authority is the setup-release-checkout dependency/runtime-build suites plus exact-pin release reproduction.\n\n### D-003 — Preserve the active checkpoint, but deploy only a terminal detector-bearing verdict\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe active Papercusp checkpoint singleton is liveness-proven by the run lock. Its SHA was initially surfaced only as candidateSource=run-probe (a cron-path checkpoint-checkout HEAD inference), so that early value was not candidate authority. The run has since published candidateSource=in-flight-candidate, authoritatively confirming it is judging 68ac9f0bdef3. That candidate predates WI-39243 detector commit e0758d0795cf: dev:pipeline_position for the detector reports judgingContainsPath=false and nextContainsPath=true. Do not duplicate, replace, or deploy the active run. After it reaches terminal, read the candidate from the verdict. If the terminal verdict does not contain e0758 plus release repairs 7b37bfc712, 0700efa08a, and 1373cead0b53, launch exactly one current-staging checkpoint; deploy only a terminal green descendant containing all four, verify direct serving-process SHA and SSE health, then resume release-trigger. SideStage public-release D-020 separately governs SideStage candidate identity and forbids substituting this Papercusp checkpoint SHA for pipeline_events.detail.candidate.\n\n### D-004 — 5dd is genuine red; current fixed tip is the only next checkpoint candidate\nDate: 2026-08-15\nAt 2026-08-15 12:00 EDT, exact all-four candidate 5dd767e81a01 published terminal red. Consequences, both bad:\n(1) OVER-BLOCKS. On a live event, some other product's stock or price moves constantly. A reply about product A is blocked because product B sold one unit — and the block is DESTRUCTIVE: status goes to 'blocked' with \"Grounding changed after this reply was generated. Create a fresh proposal before sending\", so the seller must regenerate. On a busy stream this plausibly fires on most approvals.\n(2) UNDER-DETECTS. A reply that MISSTATES a value which did not change passes staleness untouched; only the judge might catch it, and the judge is a model, not a check.\n(3) NO SELLER-READABLE REASON — the clause's own last phrase. \"Grounding changed\" names neither what moved nor whether it mattered to this reply.\n\nRULING. P-004 narrows the staleness gate from context-scoped to EVIDENCE-scoped: a proposal is blocked when a source the reply ACTUALLY CITES has moved or vanished, not when the context differs anywhere. Execution owner: aa261.\n\n### D-012 — Copilot relevance: a source must answer for something it holds — identity anchors, phrasing does not gate\nDate: 2026-08-17\nRULING on the grounding contract in apps/api/src/copilot/copilot.relevance.ts (`coversQuestion` / `sourceSupportsQuestion`). Binds every caller: copilot.pipeline.ts:249, copilot.model.ts:149-151 (deterministic reply path), copilot.claims.ts:344.\n\nPROBLEM (EI-20488839136964773, reproduced live at HEAD). `coversQuestion` was an all-tokens conjunction: a citation grounded only if the source's vocabulary contained EVERY non-stopword the buyer typed, gated solely by a hand-rolled 30-word STOP_WORDS list. Grounding strength therefore FELL as the buyer wrote a longer, more natural question — ordinary English (\"right\", \"now\", \"many\") gated exactly like a real property demand (\"warranty\"). Measured on :3100: \"How much is the Harbor Kettle?\" grounded; the SAME question behind any prefix, or \"what is the event price ... and how many are available right now?\", returned \"No verified citation\" and the proposal blocked.\n\nRULE NOW IN FORCE, three tests in order:\n R1. requiredProperties stay a STRICT conjunction against the source vocabulary. Unchanged. This is the WI-39264/P-008 contract — a missing catalog property must still fall through to the labelled research fallback.\n R2. If the question names any product present in the context, the source must BE that product (a hit on its identity vocabulary: title + description + attributes). Intent words (price/stock) are deliberately excluded from identity, since every priced item knows \"how much\" and matching on it would cite the wrong product.\n R3. A residual — a question token the source cannot account for — is tolerated ONLY if the buyer also asked something the record always knows (its price, or its live quantity). With no such intent word the residual IS the substance of the question and the source cannot serve it.\n\nWHY R3 IS PHRASED THAT WAY, AND THE MISTAKE IT CORRECTS. My first version made identity alone sufficient and dropped free-text coverage entirely, on the stated rationale that assertion safety belongs to the claim/evidence contract. That version turned 21 tests red across two files. It is not safe to relocate this check to copilot.claims.ts while those two callers exist.\n\nThe discriminator is not a word list. Every must-pass case asked something the record holds (price, availability); every must-fail case asked only for a property it lacks (warranty, overnight shipping). Filler may ride along with a real ask; it may no longer BE the ask.\n\nWHAT THIS DELIBERATELY STILL REFUSES: an event-item citation about price cannot support a warranty or overnight-shipping claim, and the deterministic path stays silent rather than answering a warranty question with a price.
