New apps/api/src/copilot/copilot.relevance.test.ts carries 18 focused cases — relevance had NO test of its own before, which is exactly why the defect survived: it was exercised only through suites that ask short, well-behaved questions.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-013 — During the owner pause of sidestage-release-drive, stood-down items are leader-carried: an agent handed one by a scheduler releases it, never runs it\nDate: 2026-08-18\nContext: Owner directive 2026-08-18 03:19Z [owner, verbatim]: \"tell the fleet to pause the work. you will carry the remaining work yourself.\" All 13 fleet members stood down by 03:45Z, checkpointing and releasing their in-flight items. Released items stay state 'open', so scheduler:get_next's DEFAULT spec legitimately serves them to ANY agent — at 03:49:34Z it handed WI-39265 (this plan's P-009 benchmark item) to non-fleet agent su-659a7da9, who correctly HELD without running and asked the leader (msg msy50poa). This exposure covers every item the fleet stood down, not just WI-39265.\n\nRuling (fleet leader su-6613215b; [self-imposed] interpretation of the owner directive above): the pause routes remaining release-drive work to the LEADER, not to whichever agent the scheduler picks — \"you will carry the remaining work yourself\" is incompatible with a third party running the item, and equally incompatible with the work being silently dropped. Therefore, while the pause stands:\n1. An agent handed a stood-down sidestage-release-drive item by any scheduler spec must NOT run it: release the claim and notify the leader (thread to this decision). Holding-and-asking, as su-659a7da9 did, is the correct behavior when in doubt.\n2. The leader adopts such items into the solo carry queue.\n3. Spending paid provider API calls against a stood-down item is out of scope for everyone except the leader.\nThis ruling expires when the owner lifts the pause.\n\nApplied immediately: su-659a7da9 instructed to release WI-39265; the leader claims it and runs its one remaining leg (benchmark to completion) per the item's own checkpoint prescription — ledgered background run (capability:bash run_in_background) so the host reaper cannot collect it, then rule from the report's own acceptance block.\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-blocked-items-audit-2026-08-15","title":"Audit and reconcile every blocked SideStage plan and work item","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Audit and reconcile every blocked SideStage plan and work item\nslug: sidestage-blocked-items-audit-2026-08-15\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Approved for execution via route A.\n\n**Next:** Inventory every effective plan block and blocked/held work-item, then reconcile stale state safely.\n\n## Background\n\nSideStage currently has 61 non-archived plans and an initial census of 16 work-items stored as blocked. This audit must distinguish valid dependencies from stale plan/work-item state, temporary claim holds, external blockers, and needs-human gates; clear only demonstrably invalid blocks; and preserve live peer work.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Full block audit and reconciliation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Inventory every non-archived SideStage plan item plus every blocked, held, needs-human, and externally blocked work-item; record the complete cohort. importance: high — note: ← WI-39231 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Trace every candidate block to its writer, dependency graph, current plan Decisions, holder liveness, checkpoint, and external capability; classify valid versus stale or contradictory. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39253 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Clear every demonstrably invalid block or stale temporary hold without disturbing live peer work, and record the exact evidence for each mutation. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39270 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Re-read all SideStage plans and work-items, verify convergence, and deliver a full residue report naming each remaining block and the exact requirement to clear it. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39271 completed (done)\n\n\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-channel-guide-countdown-real-sellers-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage Channel Guide countdown and real-seller data boundary","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage Channel Guide countdown and real-seller data boundary\nslug: sidestage-channel-guide-countdown-real-sellers-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n# SideStage Channel Guide countdown and real-seller data boundary\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Implement one shared ticking clock for scheduled Channel Guide rows, with an accessible countdown, exact start time, and an honest no-start-time fallback. importance: high — note: ← WI-39143 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Make the public guide reject synthetic seller/probe records, remove runtime placeholder seller fallback, and safely withdraw the known production acceptance event. importance: high — note: ← WI-39144 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add focused web/API regressions for countdown rollover, seller provenance filtering, and acceptance-event cleanup. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39232 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `wip` Run focused and affected verification, inspect the public guide and SideStage pipeline position, and record completion evidence. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: → WI-39238\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Active-now design comparison\n\n- **P-005** `done` Specify three active-now visual treatments using identical Channel Guide data; keep live status distinct from current-watching and scheduled countdown states. importance: high — note: ← WI-39152 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Build an isolated comparison URL showing the three treatments side by side with responsive layout and existing SideStage design tokens. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-39158 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Add focused regressions, validate the design spec, and browser-verify desktop plus narrow views before delivering the URL. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-39164 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Active-now production rollout\n\n- **P-008** `done` Extract the approved Signal rail active-now treatment into a production-ready Channel Guide live-status component with token-only styles and focused accessibility/semantic regression coverage, using new isolated files only while P-001/P-002 remain in flight; do not edit ChannelGuide.tsx, channel-guide.css, or countdown tests. importance: high — note: ← WI-39202 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Integrate the approved Signal rail treatment into the real ChannelGuide live rows after the countdown/hygiene atoms settle, preserve current-watching and scheduled semantics, then run focused/full verification and responsive browser QA. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-008 importance: high — note: ← WI-39207 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Public guide excludes synthetic seller provenance\nDate: 2026-08-15\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe buyer Channel Guide may render only events tied to a non-synthetic seller identity. The legacy sentinel seller_id `demo-seller`, placeholder display name `SideStage Seller`, and production acceptance-probe events are not seller inventory and must not reach the public guide. Runtime publication must carry the selected seller principal and its real display identity; when an exact start time is absent, the guide says `Schedule pending` rather than inventing a countdown.\n\n### D-002 — Active-now comparison stays isolated from the production countdown atom\nDate: 2026-08-15\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe owner-requested active-now options will be implemented as an isolated comparison route using separate files. The lane must not edit `ChannelGuide.tsx`, `channel-guide.css`, or countdown tests while P-001/P-002 are in flight. All variants use the same content and existing SideStage tokens; live status, current-watching selection, and scheduled countdown remain separate semantics.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-003 — Three comparison variants and recommended treatment\nDate: 2026-08-15\nDate: 2026-08-14\nThe comparison will render identical guide content in three treatments: (A) Signal rail — a slim red leading rail, subtle live tint, and compact `LIVE NOW` pill; (B) Spotlight wash — a stronger red surface wash with a `HAPPENING NOW` status cluster; (C) Thumbnail flag — a small `ON AIR` overlay anchored to the thumbnail with minimal row tint. Current-watching remains a separate check indicator in every variant, and scheduled countdown remains yellow. A is the implementation recommendation because it is fastest to scan, preserves the existing row anatomy, and does not rely on color alone. The UI IR `sidestage-channel-guide-active-now-comparison` passed `design-phase.validate_spec` and `design-phase.lint_spec` with 0 errors and 0 warnings.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-004 — Production active-now integration reuses the isolated Signal rail seam\nDate: 2026-08-15\nP-008 establishes `ChannelGuideActiveNow`, `channelGuideActiveNowRowClass`, and `channel-guide-active-now.css` as the production seam for the approved Signal rail treatment. P-009 must import and use that surface after P-001/P-002 settle; it must not duplicate the rail/badge selectors in `channel-guide.css`. The helper applies the treatment only to `status === 'live'`; the component keeps the visible `Live now` label and viewer count separate, while `ChannelGuide` continues to own the independent current-room check and scheduled countdown semantics.\nRelated: P-008, P-009\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-comprehensive-e2e-browser-audit-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage comprehensive end-to-end browser audit","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage comprehensive end-to-end browser audit\nslug: sidestage-comprehensive-e2e-browser-audit-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n## Now\nState: approved for direct execution by Avi on 2026-08-14; no application changes are permitted.\nNext: establish the coverage matrix and isolated browser evidence, then execute every reachable user flow.\n\n## Scope\nRead-only application audit of SideStage as a real user across Watch, Orders, Studio, History, Tests, nested Studio/Event Manager states, identity switching, navigation, persistence, responsive behavior, accessibility, console/network health, empty/error/loading states, and cross-user isolation. Browser-created demo data is allowed only as required to exercise the product. Findings are recorded with severity, steps, expected versus actual behavior, evidence, and specification provenance.\n\n\n## Phase — Execution\n\n- **P-001** `done` Inventory current routes, user roles, active plan Decisions, approved mockups, known intentional limits, and enumerate every reachable interactive element. importance: high — note: ← WI-39218 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Establish isolated Verdict browser runs, verify the live stack, create two clean demo-user personas, and record baseline console/network evidence. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39247 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `wip` Exercise Watch and Orders end to end across desktop and mobile, including event guide, identity, catalog/product focus, chat, holds/cart/checkout, auctions, persistence, reload, history, and cross-user isolation. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: → WI-39248\n- **P-004** `blocked` Exercise Studio end to end across desktop and mobile, including all Studio views, Event Manager routes and sections, inventory, event creation, live console, overlays, auction/chat controls, guarded actions, persistence, and navigation. importance: high — note: → WI-39250 blocked-by: P-002, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n- **P-005** `todo` Exercise History, Tests, the global shell, external links, keyboard/accessibility paths, responsive layouts, and loading/empty/error states with console and network inspection. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` Cross-check all observed behavior against the current plan Decisions, PRD/TDD/submission packet, approved design artifacts, API/network results, persistence, and multi-user boundaries; deduplicate findings. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Record the final evidence-backed report with page/element coverage, passes, defects, intentional limits, blocked cases, severities, reproduction steps, and specification provenance; make no application changes. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Parallel Studio coverage\n\n- **P-008** `done` Parallel Studio lane: Event Manager desktop deep coverage — My Events, event search/selection, all section tabs, Settings derivations, Rehearse, Create-event form validation, reset/fullscreen local controls, responsive checks, console/network evidence, and source-based confirmation of WI-39274. Read-only under D-010; do not invoke any mutating action. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39278 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Parallel Studio lane: Inventory mobile and responsive coverage — inventory list/search/filter/empty/local selection/price/quantity/pagination, viewport transitions, reload persistence, keyboard/accessibility checks, and console/network evidence. Read-only under D-010; do not add, submit, save, or mutate inventory. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39279 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Parallel Studio lane: Active Event and Copilot mobile/edge coverage — all reachable controls, panels, overlays, auction/chat state, invalid-room/error states, responsive transitions, reload persistence, keyboard/accessibility checks, and console/network evidence. Read-only under D-010; do not prepare, approve, skip, start, or mutate event state. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39280 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Parallel Studio lane: Studio shell and route-matrix coverage — enumerate and exercise every Studio navigation entry and section, responsive layouts, local-only fullscreen/reset controls, loading/empty/error states, external links, focus order, and console/network inspection. Read-only under D-010; do not trigger any write-side action. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39281 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Parallel Studio lane: adversarial cross-surface/spec audit — reconcile rendered behavior with current plan Decisions and source/API writers, inspect negative and contradictory states without mutation, detect untested reachable elements, verify persistence boundaries, and produce reproducible evidence for every finding. Read-only under D-010. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39282 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — No application changes\nThis pass may inspect source and plans and may create disposable user-visible demo state through ordinary UI flows, but it must not edit code, configuration, infrastructure, or application data directly.\n\n### D-002 — Test the current contract, not obsolete labels\nThe audit uses current plan Decisions and shipped behavior as authority, while recording contradictions with older PRD/TDD/submission documents as specification drift rather than silently choosing one source.\n\n### D-003 — Findings require reproducible evidence\nEvery reported defect includes severity, affected role/page, reproduction steps, expected and actual behavior, console/network evidence where relevant, viewport, persistence/reload result, and the governing spec or plan Decision.\n\n### D-004 — Parallel Studio lanes stay read-only and evidence-isolated\nDate: 2026-08-15\nP-008 through P-012 run against production under the current D-010 freeze. Each unrelated browser flow must use a fresh VERDICT_DATA_DIR and preserve artifacts under /tmp. Testers may exercise only navigation, local UI state, validation that does not submit, responsive/keyboard behavior, reload, and read-only network/source inspection. They must not Create, Schedule, Start, Add inventory, Save, Run preflight, Prepare, Approve, Skip, or otherwise mutate SideStage data. Each lane checkpoints exact elements/routes/viewports plus console/network evidence and files one deduplicated work-item per confirmed defect.\nRelated: P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-005 — Studio acceptance must be replayed on one D-010-stable production SHA\nDate: 2026-08-15\nLeader audit found that the running production image changed during P-008 through P-012: `/healthz` is emitted from the container-baked `SIDESTAGE_SHA`; it was `eae0aa0b5eafc0a12e7efe527744fb8d42c4d293` at the 01:36 ET audit start and `fb91fed3ae0e54419f240c29d896b1830f3fff8b` by the 01:54 ET public proof/current health read. Preserved artifact mtimes place P-008, P-009, and P-011 on both sides of that interval; P-010 completed in the earlier window; corrected P-012 completed in the later window. Each child completion remains truthful for what it exercised, and its filed defects remain valid, but their aggregate cannot satisfy D-004's requirement to run under the current D-010 freeze. Keep WI-39250/P-004 open. After the generation-2 `plan:sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14:release-snapshot-complete` gate supplies one stable public SHA, replay the affected Studio route/responsive/keyboard/negative-state matrix against that exact SHA, preserve fresh isolated Verdict evidence, then re-synthesize acceptance. Do not cite work-item `treeStamp` as production identity; `/healthz.sha` is the running-image writer.\nRelated: P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n## Completion criteria\nEvery reachable interactive element in the current app navigation and nested page states has a recorded disposition (pass, defect, intentional limit, blocked/not testable with reason); representative desktop and mobile viewports are covered; two demo identities are used for isolation checks; browser console and network failures are triaged; and the final report is deduplicated and traceable to evidence.\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-event-activation-scheduling-implementation-2026-08-14","title":"Sidestage event activation and scheduling implementation","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Sidestage event activation and scheduling implementation\nslug: sidestage-event-activation-scheduling-implementation-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n## Objective\n\nImplement the corrected Studio event lifecycle end to end: persist scheduling and lifecycle state, expose seller actions and exact timing in Event Manager, surface scheduled events in Up Next, keep Active Event strictly limited to the currently running event, and verify with automated tests plus browser and pipeline evidence.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- No SideStage repository edits until the exact declared gate `plan:sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14:release-snapshot-complete` fires.\n- Reuse existing event, auction, API, and Studio surfaces before introducing new durable abstractions.\n- Existing unrelated working-tree changes must be preserved.\n- Automatic file locks are authoritative for this session.\n- Browser verification uses the verdict skill.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nA seller can schedule, reschedule, cancel scheduling, start, and end an event through Event Manager with exact date/time visible; scheduled events remain discoverable in Event Manager and Up Next; Active Event shows only a currently live event; lifecycle transitions persist through refresh/restart; focused tests, relevant repository checks, browser flows, and pipeline position are verified.\n\n\n## Phase — Discovery and contract\n\n- **P-001** `wip` Audit current event persistence, lifecycle transitions, API contracts, scheduler/background processing, and Studio surfaces; map corrected D-001 semantics to the smallest existing extension points and document acceptance cases. importance: urgent — note: → WI-39161\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-002** `todo` Implement durable event scheduling and lifecycle transitions in the existing data/API layer, including schedule, reschedule, unschedule, start, automatic due activation if supported by the current architecture, and end semantics with validation and authorization. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Implement Event Manager lifecycle controls and exact scheduled/live timing using existing Sidestage action, badge, card, and input patterns, with accessible labels and refresh-stable state. importance: high blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` Implement Up Next visibility for scheduled events and strict Active Event current-live semantics across seller-facing Studio views without leaking merely scheduled or ended events into the active slot. importance: high blocked-by: P-002\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Tests\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Add focused persistence/API/UI tests covering valid transitions, invalid/conflicting transitions, exact timing display, reload persistence, scheduled-versus-active separation, and automatic due activation behavior where applicable. importance: high blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n\n## Phase — Verification\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Run focused and repository-required checks, perform verdict browser QA for schedule/reschedule/unschedule/start/end plus Up Next and Active Event behavior, then verify pipeline position and record deploy evidence. importance: high blocked-by: P-005\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Active Event means currently live only\nDate: 2026-08-15\nInherit the corrected product ruling from `sidestage-studio-event-activation-scheduling-mockups-2026-08-14#D-001`: a scheduled event is not active. Scheduled events remain in Event Manager and Up Next until the seller starts them or their activation policy runs; Active Event contains only the event presently running. Ending the live event removes it from Active Event and preserves terminal history through the existing event surfaces.\n\n### D-002 — Repository writes wait for the exact release snapshot latch\nDate: 2026-08-15\nPlanning, metadata updates, and source inspection may proceed immediately. No file in the SideStage repository may be edited until `plan:sidestage-auction-chat-public-release-2026-08-14:release-snapshot-complete` is fired. Re-check the live latch immediately before the first product edit; do not infer clearance from a message or timeout.\n\n### D-003 — Extend the existing event row as lifecycle authority\nDate: 2026-08-15\nReuse the existing `event` table, `EventStore`, `EventService`, EventController, `events.mine`, and `events.guide` surfaces. Add only the missing persisted schedule time zone plus atomic schedule, cancel-schedule, start-now, end, and activate-due transitions. New config-created events remain drafts until one of those explicit lifecycle actions makes them buyer-visible; config saves never reset lifecycle state.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-004 — A scheduled activation performs an atomic live-event handoff\nDate: 2026-08-15\nA seller has one current Active Event. Before its scheduled instant, an upcoming event does not affect the existing live event. At manual start or due activation, the server atomically ends any other live event for that seller at the transition instant and activates the selected/due event; this preserves strict single-current-live semantics without dropping the scheduled activation. The due scheduler reuses EventService and database transitions, catches up immediately on process start, polls at one-second cadence, and invalidates the existing guide/mine streams after real transitions.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-005 — Lifecycle controls stay separate from publisher media controls\nDate: 2026-08-15\nEvent Manager owns schedule, reschedule, cancel schedule, Start now, and End event. Active Event mounts only an authoritative `status=live` row. Its Live Console buttons start/stop camera and microphone without mutating lifecycle, and are labeled accordingly. This prevents local media-session state from masquerading as event activation.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-inventory-save-semantics-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage Inventory absolute quantity and price Save semantics","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage Inventory absolute quantity and price Save semantics\nslug: sidestage-inventory-save-semantics-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nTurn the Studio Inventory tab into an editor for each existing variant's authoritative total quantity and selling price. Saving overwrites both values instead of treating the entry as incoming stock.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Reuse the existing catalog, AuctionInventory, InventoryController, and sync invalidation surfaces; do not create a parallel inventory system.\n- Qty means total physical inventory, including reserved units. Reserved remains read-only and active holds survive the edit.\n- Refuse a Qty lower than Reserved so a manual save cannot invalidate existing obligations.\n- Available stock remains derived as Qty minus Reserved.\n- Remove additive restock language from the Inventory UI and mutation contract.\n- Focused API/web regression tests and non-mutating rendered verification are required.\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Expose authoritative total qty in the catalog read model and change the existing inventory mutation/storage seam from additive restock to absolute quantity-and-price save semantics, preserving reservations and rejecting qty below reserved. importance: high — note: ← WI-39104 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `todo` Update the Inventory grid and panel to show Qty, initialize it from authoritative total quantity, save absolute Qty and Unit price, and replace Add/restock language with Save semantics. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Add focused API and web regression coverage, run relevant tests/typechecks, and verify the rendered Inventory flow without mutating live stock. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Absolute Save supersedes additive restock\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThis decision supersedes sidestage-studio-inventory-tab-2026-08-14#D-001 by owner direction. The editable Qty column represents authoritative total physical inventory, not an intake delta and not available-only stock. Save overwrites qty and selling price through the existing inventory authority. Reserved remains read-only; saves below reserved are rejected so active holds stay valid; available stock continues to derive from qty minus reserved.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-studio-event-activation-scheduling-mockups-2026-08-14","title":"Sidestage Studio event activation and scheduling UX mockups","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Sidestage Studio event activation and scheduling UX mockups\nslug: sidestage-studio-event-activation-scheduling-mockups-2026-08-14\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n# Sidestage Studio event activation and scheduling UX mockups\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Complete. Current-state audit, zero-warning interaction model (D-001), four project-bound mockups, validation, and owner delivery are complete; canonical P-001 through P-004 are done.\n\n**Next:** No further work in this design-only plan. Product implementation remains outside scope and behind the Sidestage P-009 release-snapshot gate.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Discovery and design\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit the current Studio web experience and source for event activation/start controls importance: high — note: ← WI-39119 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Search the shared UI registry and define the start-now, scheduling, and seller-visibility interaction model blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39122 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Create polished visual mockups grounded in the existing Sidestage interface blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39131 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Validate the mockups and deliver findings with implementation guidance blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39134 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `dropped` Audit the current Studio web experience and source for event activation/start controls importance: high — note: Duplicate entries created after multi-ptool output was not surfaced; canonical work remains P-001 through P-004.\n- **P-006** `dropped` Search the shared UI registry and define the start-now, scheduling, and seller-visibility interaction model blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: Duplicate entries created after multi-ptool output was not surfaced; canonical work remains P-001 through P-004.\n- **P-007** `dropped` Create polished visual mockups grounded in the existing Sidestage interface blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: Duplicate entries created after multi-ptool output was not surfaced; canonical work remains P-001 through P-004.\n- **P-008** `dropped` Validate the mockups and deliver findings with implementation guidance blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: Duplicate entries created after multi-ptool output was not surfaced; canonical work remains P-001 through P-004.\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Separate event lifecycle activation from publisher media start\nDate: 2026-08-15\nCORRECTION (2026-08-15): The earlier decision incorrectly placed a merely scheduled event inside Active Event. That assumption is retracted; mockup #4 is rejected. Active Event remains a strict representation of the event currently running. If no event is running, it shows the existing no-active-event state; it must not mount a future event's Live Console. A scheduled event appears before activation in Event Manager and in the global Up Next rail, both with an explicit localized date, time, and time zone. If another event is currently active, that event remains unchanged in Active Event while the scheduled one remains visible only in those upcoming-event surfaces. At the scheduled instant, the server transitions the scheduled event to active; only then does it become the content of Active Event. Event Manager remains the authoritative lifecycle surface for a selected event: drafts expose primary `Start now` and secondary `Schedule event` actions. `Start now` confirms that the event becomes buyer-facing but does not start camera or microphone; media start remains the separate Live Console action. `Schedule event` uses accessible date, time, and time-zone fields and rejects past times. Reuse Sidestage's shipped primary/secondary actions, badge, card, and input patterns.\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-watch-coming-up-next-mockups-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage Watch — Coming up next mockup gallery","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage Watch — Coming up next mockup gallery\nslug: sidestage-watch-coming-up-next-mockups-2026-08-14\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Complete. D-003 records Avi’s selection of Concept 02 — Drop Runway. The standalone comparison gallery now annotates that choice in the toolbar, Concept 02 card, and footer; all three UI IR specs remain schema-valid and lint-clean with zero errors/warnings, and fresh desktop/mobile Verdict QA confirmed the accessible selection state, HTTP 200 responses, and no console messages. The owner-local review URL is http://127.0.0.1:41033/; canonical source remains design/sidestage-watch-coming-up-next-mockups-2026-08-14/index.html. No production SideStage UI was changed by this plan.\n\n**Next:** The separately approved Drop Runway production implementation may use D-003 and the canonical gallery as its design basis; this mockup-only plan needs no further edits.\n\n## Background\n\nThe current Watch tab renders Next in the drop as a conventional three-card product rail. This plan produces design mockups only; it does not modify production SideStage UI. The work is explicitly separate from the adjacent live-auction-module mockup plan and from the real-event-lineup data implementation.\n\nRequirements:\n- Preserve the existing SideStage cream/red/yellow visual language and real product-card information architecture.\n- Improve sequence clarity, anticipation, browseability, and the relationship between the immediate next item and later items.\n- Provide three materially different responsive directions side by side.\n- Use the Papercusp design-phase registry-first flow and validate/lint each UI specification.\n- Publish a comparison URL and verify it resolves and renders at desktop and mobile widths.\n\n## Phase 1 — Design\n\n- **P-001** `done` Search the react-tailwind design registry, inspect relevant reusable components, and define three responsive Coming up / Next in the drop directions as validated and linted UI specifications. importance: high — note: ← WI-39167 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Gallery\n\n- **P-002** `done` Build a polished side-by-side HTML comparison gallery using the verified SideStage brand and realistic product data. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39170 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Run browser verification at desktop and mobile widths; fix layout, console, and accessibility issues found in the gallery. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39180 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Publish the gallery, re-resolve the URL independently, and hand the verified link to Avi with a concise concept summary. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-39182 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Mockup-only scope\n\nThis plan creates a review artifact and does not edit production SideStage components. Production implementation begins only after Avi chooses a direction.\n\n### D-002 — Separate from adjacent Watch work\n\nThe concurrent live-auction mockup plan targets bidding interactions; the event-lineup plan targets data authority; the completed page-audit plan covered whole-page redesign. This plan targets only the Coming up / Next in the drop product queue and may proceed independently.\n\n### D-003 — Avi selects Concept 02 — Drop Runway\nDate: 2026-08-15\nAvi selected Concept 02, Drop Runway, as the design direction on 2026-08-14. Treat it as the chosen basis for the subsequent production Watch-tab implementation; the current mockup/publishing plan remains scoped to gallery delivery until implementation is separately approved.\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-watch-event-lineup-products-2026-08-14","title":"Make SideStage Watch show the selected event's real product lineup","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make SideStage Watch show the selected event's real product lineup\nslug: sidestage-watch-event-lineup-products-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-19\n---\n\n## Now\nState: Draft for Avi review. The current Watch, event, action, catalog, inventory, access-policy, and checkout seams have been audited; no implementation has started.\nNext: Review the public projection, persistence boundary, event-aware hold semantics, and execution route. Do not start this plan until Avi approves it.\n\n## Background\nWatch changes event identity, guide metadata, room, stats, transcript, and auction correctly, but BuyerTab reads the unscoped public `catalog.page`, so every event receives the same global catalog slice. Production rows are real Postgres storefront variants (development alone may use an offline fixture), but they are not the selected event's lineup.\n\nEvent Manager already reads `event.actions.items { eventId }` and action mutations invalidate it per event. Current staging correctly owner-guards that query as seller-owned, so Watch must not consume or weaken it. GuardedActionService still keeps lineup state in process maps; restart loses it. Event inventory reservations lack event price, order, stage state, and presentation snapshot, so they cannot substitute for a lineup store.\n\nReuse EventService/PgEventStore visibility, GuardedActionService, SyncQueryRegistry/invalidation, catalog enrichment, and existing inventory/cart paths. Add no parallel event, catalog, cache, or checkout system. The one new durable surface is `event_lineup_item`, because no existing table represents stable event-item identity, event price, listed/current quantity, order, and stage state together.\n\nTwo presentation plans may overlap implementation files: `sidestage-watch-live-auction-mockups-2026-08-14` and `sidestage-channel-guide-countdown-real-sellers-2026-08-14`; the ready seller-side mockup plan `sidestage-lineup-run-of-show-mockups-2026-08-14` is also a design input. Their accepted UI decisions must be incorporated before BuyerTab work. This plan owns buyer data truth, not a competing visual redesign.\n\n## Global acceptance\nWith two published events, Watch A→B→A shows each event's persisted lineup without stale or global-fallback rows. A shared variant may use distinct event prices/allocations. Draft, missing, foreign, and unpublished ids reveal no lineup. Restart preserves lineups and action state. A Watch hold is validated against the selected published event, uses server-authoritative event price/allocation, cannot buy an unlisted item or oversell the event allocation, and does not break intentional non-event catalog/Scout purchases. Seller Event Manager, auctions, Channel Guide, and access classification remain intact.\n\n## Phase 1 — Durable lineup authority\n\n- **P-001** `done` Introduce an ActionItemStore contract with Postgres and in-memory implementations plus an `event_lineup_item` table keyed by event/product. Persist stable eventItemId, order, reference/current event price, listed/current quantity, stage state, buyer-safe snapshot attributes, version, and timestamps; wire registration and action mutations through it without weakening policy guards. Add repeatable schema/guard coverage, event/product foreign keys, transaction or optimistic-concurrency protection, and restart round-trip tests. Do not invent missing legacy event prices from the global catalog; an incomplete legacy event renders an honest empty lineup until repaired. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39157 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Public published-lineup projection\n\n- **P-002** `done` Add a public `event.lineup.items { eventId }` query in the existing ActionModule. Gate it through EventVisibilityGuard/PgEventStore so only published events resolve; read the same ActionItemStore as seller-owned `event.actions.items`; join existing catalog data for current image and variant labels while retaining event price, allocation, order, and stage state. Return a buyer-safe DTO, register it in the access matrix and data-surface census, and fan relevant action, auction, stock, visibility, and reservation changes into event-scoped invalidation. Keep `event.actions.items` seller-owned. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39165 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Watch query and interaction state\n\n- **P-003** `done` Replace BuyerTab's global `catalog.page` rail with `event.lineup.items { eventId }`, retaining the explicit products test/embed override. Add one typed lineup-to-BuyerProduct adapter; render distinct loading, empty, unpublished/not-found, and transport-error states; never fall back to unrelated global rows or fixture data. On event change clear product-local hold notices/overrides, expanded state, and selection before rendering the new result, and prevent previous-event data while the next query loads. Incorporate the accepted Watch-auction, Channel Guide, and seller Lineup mockup decisions before editing shared presentation files. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39201 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Event-aware buyer holds\n\n- **P-004** `done` Extend the existing cart hold mutation with optional eventId/eventItemId context from Watch. Server-side, resolve the published lineup row, reject missing/unlisted/unpublished combinations without enumeration, use event price/allocation as authority, and atomically transfer or decrement the event reservation while creating the buyer hold so stock is not double-reserved. Make retries idempotent and invalidate the selected lineup, cart, inventory snapshot, and affected public catalog keys. Preserve the current product-only path for intentional catalog and Scout purchases. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39192 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Complete the event-aware cart commitment lifecycle across the existing reservation, checkout, and payment flows. Persist eventId/eventItemId through the hold and sale boundary; make hold expiry, explicit removal, checkout cancellation, and payment failure idempotently release the event commitment and restore buyer-visible availability; make successful payment convert the active commitment exactly once into a paid event sale that remains consumed. Reject replayed or out-of-order transition drift, invalidate lineup/cart/inventory surfaces after every state change, and prove under concurrent retries that event availability equals seller allocation minus active event commitments minus completed paid event sales. blocked-by: P-004 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39204 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Move auction inventory authority onto the selected event lineup allocation. Auction start/publish must atomically create an event-scoped commitment rather than a separate global reservation; no-bid close, seller cancellation, auction expiry, and winner payment failure must release it; a winning auction awaiting payment remains an active commitment; successful winner payment converts it exactly once into a paid event sale that remains consumed. Prevent cross-event/global leakage and over-allocation, make all transitions idempotent and restart-safe, invalidate the affected lineup/auction/inventory surfaces, and cover the full start → close/cancel → winner/payment lifecycle with focused tests. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-39173 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Regression matrix and rendered QA\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Cover two disjoint lineups, a shared variant with different event prices/allocations, registration/update/restart persistence, per-event invalidation, published versus draft/missing/foreign reads, A→B→A during an in-flight fetch, empty/error rendering, local-state reset, event-hold idempotency and oversell rejection, and legacy non-event cart compatibility. Run focused API/web tests, schema migration/guard tests, affected typecheck/build, then desktop/mobile browser QA through Channel Guide → Watch A → Watch B → Watch A → hold/checkout; record screenshots and live query evidence. Re-read the overlapping presentation plans and serialize same-file implementation through locks. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-006, P-007\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Watch products mean the selected published event's lineup\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe Watch rail is not a generic browse surface. Its authority is the selected event's published lineup, including event price, order, allocation, and stage state. `catalog.page` remains the global browse/inventory projection and may enrich presentation, but it cannot select Watch products or serve as fallback when an event lineup is empty or unavailable.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Separate the public projection from the seller command boundary\nDate: 2026-08-15\nKeep `event.actions.items` seller-owned because it is the Event Manager/action command surface. Add `event.lineup.items` as a buyer-safe published projection over the same store, guarded by existing event visibility policy. Both reads share one persistence and invalidation authority; this is a new read contract, not a parallel lineup system.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-005\n\n### D-003 — Persist line items without overloading reservations or config\nDate: 2026-08-15\nCreate one action-domain `event_lineup_item` surface because current maps vanish on restart and no existing table contains event-item price, order, allocation, and stage state. Inventory reservations remain stock authority, event config remains settings, and run of show remains advisory planning. The Postgres store is production authority; the in-memory adapter exists for explicit fallback tests.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-004 — Watch holds carry event context; generic catalog holds remain\nDate: 2026-08-15\nA product shown with event-specific price/allocation must be held against that event item. Thread event context through the existing cart mutation and validate it server-side; never trust client price or quantity. Preserve product-only holds for deliberate catalog/Scout purchases so this extends rather than forks checkout.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-005 — Merge active presentation decisions before touching BuyerTab\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe active Watch auction and Channel Guide plans, plus the ready seller Lineup mockup plan, own current presentation decisions. P-003 must re-read their completed artifacts/decisions and place the event-scoped data contract beneath the accepted UI. This plan owns buyer data truth and switching, not a competing redesign.\nRelated: P-003, P-005\n\n### D-006 — Event allocation has one lifecycle invariant across carts and auctions\nDate: 2026-08-15\nDate: 2026-08-15\nFor every event lineup item, buyer-visible availability is seller allocation minus active event commitments minus completed paid event sales. Active commitments include unexpired cart holds and auction inventory that is live or awaiting winner payment. Hold expiry/removal, checkout cancellation, payment failure, no-bid auction close, seller cancellation, and auction expiry release the commitment. Successful cart or winner payment converts the commitment exactly once into a paid event sale that stays consumed. Every transition is event-scoped, idempotent, restart-safe, and invalidates the affected lineup/cart/auction/inventory projections; no event flow may fall back to a separate global reservation.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-007 — Event carts are single-event lifecycle aggregates\nDate: 2026-08-15\nExtend the existing cart/order aggregate rather than adding a parallel checkout system. A Watch hold persists `eventId` and `eventItemId` on each cart item; the cart becomes event-scoped and rejects items from another event (and generic product-only items) until it is emptied, preventing a current Watch room from relabeling a mixed cart at checkout. Product-only catalog/Scout carts remain valid through the legacy path. For an event cart, one atomic hold transition decrements `event_lineup_item.current_quantity`, creates/updates the cart payload, and reserves physical inventory. Expiry, explicit removal, checkout cancellation, and payment failure restore the event allocation and release inventory exactly once. Successful payment commits inventory and leaves the lineup decrement consumed exactly once. The checkout order copies the cart item context, making the paid sale auditable without a second event-sale store. Idempotency keys/replayed transitions return the existing state and must never apply the allocation delta twice. This is the shared contract for P-003, P-004, P-005, and P-006.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n"},{"harness_slug":"sidestage","plan_slug":"sidestage-watch-live-auction-mockups-2026-08-14","title":"SideStage Watch — improved live auction mockups","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: SideStage Watch — improved live auction mockups\nslug: sidestage-watch-live-auction-mockups-2026-08-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-15\nupdated: 2026-08-15\n---\n\n# SideStage Watch — improved live auction mockups\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Design and delivery\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit the current Watch tab, auction interaction states, SideStage tokens, and reusable design-registry components. importance: high — note: ← WI-39146 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Define and validate three improved live-auction UI directions grounded in the existing SideStage design language. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-39150 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Generate and assemble the three directions into a responsive comparison gallery. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-39151 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `todo` Publish the gallery, verify the public URL resolves, and document the recommended direction. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Target the running SideStage web Watch page, not the native Buyer shell\nDate: 2026-08-15\nCorrection after live verification: the owner-named Watch tab is the running React web surface at the SideStage dev server. Its current auction section uses the cream/red/yellow SideStage web theme and already includes a ring timer, current-price chip, live bid feed, leader/winner banner, and amount form. The earlier SwiftUI/native Buyer audit is adjacent context only and must not govern the mockups. All mockups and specs must use ecosystem react-tailwind and the verified web layout.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-002 — Ground concepts in the source tree serving port 5173\nDate: 2026-08-15\nThe authoritative audit source is the live Vite process cwd at /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/hives/sidestage/apps/web (PID provenance re-verified on 2026-08-15), not the stale sibling .sidestage-mobile-source-probe. The live tree's AuctionPanel.tsx and auction.css implement the ring clock, calm/soon/critical urgency, settling and closed phases, recent bid feed, leader/outbid/winner messaging, bid form states, and SOLD stamp on the SideStage cream/red/yellow token system. P-002 through P-004 must preserve those semantics and use the live tree plus /tmp/sidestage-watch-current-tall.png as the visual baseline.\n\n### D-003 — Use one conditional current-offer module in the existing right-hand Watch slot\nDate: 2026-08-15\nDate: 2026-08-15\nOwner correction superseding the three-direction comparison gallery: produce one combined module that preserves the current Now Selling card when no auction is active, then transforms that same right-hand slot in place when an auction is live. The live state includes the ring countdown, current bid, compact bid feed and leader, amount input, and Place bid action. Settling and sold are additional states of the same module. Do not add a separate Live auction block below the video. Replace the prior index.html and concept-specs.json drafts; retain stage-varsity-jacket.png.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-004 — Chat, Details, and Seller tabs reveal one room-context panel\nDate: 2026-08-15\nOwner approved interactive mockups for all three existing tabs and approved the auction module as-is. The tabs switch one stable panel directly below the video: Chat shows the live thread and composer; Details shows item facts, condition, shipping/returns, and auction terms; Seller shows identity, reputation, verification, follow, and shop actions. The four-state current-offer module remains unchanged in the right-hand slot and stays visible while room tabs switch. Registry-first audit found no tab/chat/profile composite; reuse action.primary, action.secondary, and feedback.banner semantics plus the established SideStage visual tokens.\nRelated: P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"oddsmith-hive","plan_slug":"oddsmith-recovery-and-hardening-2026-08-16","title":"Oddsmith recovery + hardening after the 2026-08-15 wipe","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Oddsmith recovery + hardening after the 2026-08-15 wipe\nslug: oddsmith-recovery-and-hardening-2026-08-16\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-16\nupdated: 2026-08-25\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nCOMPLETE — all four Phase 1 items are done (P-001 backup+staleness alarm, P-002 dist rebuild + green crons, P-003 ingestion re-home + failing health, P-004 zero-order engine diagnosis). P-001 was re-verified against disk on 2026-08-17T13:35Z rather than trusted from its mirrored status: /mnt/data/Backup/db-dumps/pg/oddsmith holds a 37MB pg_dump dir written 13:05:26Z and STATUS.json reports oddsmithOk:true, failed:[], with a live oddsmithLastSuccessEpoch (30min old). RESIDUE, none of it in this plan's scope: (a) oddsmith deploys are still frozen, but the cause is now fully proven and is NOT a gate defect — the 13:19Z green-checkpoint run stamped `green=true promoted=false reason=push-failed`, i.e. the suite is green and the sole blocker is the dead git push credential (WI-39549, owner-gated: re-auth aviynw on this box or grant papercupai push). 461 commits unpushed since 2026-07-26. (b) WI-39671 (green-checkpoint stall) is resolved pending one confirming run. (c) Untouched oddsmith backlog outside this plan: WI-6175 (daily-loss gate measures cash deployed, not loss — has halted live kalshi 7d) and WI-5735 (LLM analyst dead).\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Nothing in this plan — it is done. The one action that would move oddsmith forward is owner-gated and tracked as WI-39549: restore the git push credential so the already-green gate can promote and deploys unfreeze.)\n\n## Background\n\nVerified 2026-08-16 ~15:00 EDT:\n\n- `~/.oddsmith` birth 2026-08-15 18:54:35 EDT — the whole runtime-state dir, DB included, was destroyed. Root cause established owner-side (papercusp was restored from kopia; oddsmith had no backup).\n- Sidecar crash-looped ~3,488x through Aug 15 (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND @papercusp/embedded-pg-discovery/index.js`), systemd restart counter 4258. Recovered 08-16 01:08.\n- Embedded PG re-initialized 08-16 01:07:19; every table's oldest row is from today. All prior simulation/evidence history is gone permanently.\n- In the 13.9h since: engineTick 9,585 runs, liveLoopCycle 169, 1,627 signals, 1,625 forward forecasts, 110k+ market_data snapshots across 413 polymarket markets. Forward scorecard n=975: +$6.46 on a $1,000 flat-stake book (+0.65%), Sharpe 0.015, win rate 47.5%, CLV +0.45pp t=1.19 (not significant), Brier 0.204, ECE 0.016.\n- Engine has placed ZERO orders: orders/fills/positions all empty; every market skips `no_edge` (edge=0.0000) or `empty_book`.\n- 155/391 analyst LLM calls today (39.6%) failed with gateway 429.\n\n## Phase 1\n\n- **P-001** `done` Back up the oddsmith embedded PG (TCP 5544) into the already-kopia-covered /mnt/data/Backup/db-dumps path, plus a >24h staleness alarm. Backs WI-39502. importance: high — note: verified twice: `oddsmith ok (14M, 274 objects)`, STATUS.json oddsmithOk:true, pg_restore -l reads 274 objects\n- **P-002** `done` Rebuild the 19 stale workspace dists so the build-bin refusal clears; green paper-cycle + error-triage crons; alarm on N consecutive cron failures. Backs WI-39503. — note: ← WI-39517 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Re-home ingestion: activate oddsmith-ingest-cadence or flip the sidecar off central mode; make /api/health/ingestion FAIL when mode is central and no dispatch has arrived. Backs WI-39504. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-39532 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Diagnose the zero-order engine — is edge=0.0000 on every market correct behaviour or a broken edge calculation? Open-ended. — note: ← WI-39518 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-get-feedback-relevance-consults-2026-08-16","title":"Acceptance: relevance-routed consult threads (pull + push + checkpoint consults)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-16","owner":"su-c0fe9484-a99b-4dfc-9c98-e2e37836ac94","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: relevance-routed consult threads (pull + push + checkpoint consults)\nslug: acceptance-get-feedback-relevance-consults-2026-08-16\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-16\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-c0fe9484-a99b-4dfc-9c98-e2e37836ac94\n---\n\n# Acceptance: relevance-routed consult threads (pull + push + checkpoint consults)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01.
