Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan system-notices-on-its-own-2026-08-16 (\"Make the system notice on its own — goal liveness, knowledge routing, and effect-confirming returns\"), authored AFTER implementation of P-001..P-006 per the ACCEPTANCE_RUBRIC_COMPLETION_GATE.\n\nThe plan's premise: every defect it addresses was found by an agent TRIPPING OVER it, not by the system reporting it. So these criteria grade OUTCOMES — whether the failure now announces itself — not whether the diff exists. A criterion is `healthy` only if the signal fires WITHOUT a human or agent going looking.\n\nGRADER: must NOT be su-1cd24b43 (the implementer). A self-grade does not satisfy the gate. Grade from source + the cited probes; do not take the completion prose as evidence.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"agent-surface-honesty-fixes-2026-08-16","title":"Make the dishonest successes honest — fleet-leader audit fixes (2026-08-15/16 epoch)","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make the dishonest successes honest — fleet-leader audit fixes (2026-08-15/16 epoch)\nslug: agent-surface-honesty-fixes-2026-08-16\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-16\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Now\n\nOwner review of this plan. Nothing here is started. Two rows are already\nresolved or owned elsewhere and are recorded that way rather than re-proposed\n(P-012 shipped; P-005 belongs to another agent's open item).\n\n## Background\n\n**Thesis.** This system's best rails *refuse with the answer* — the\n`release:checkpoint-run` stand-down banner names both candidates and the\nabandoned red's file list; the PreToolUse false-absence guard refuses a grep\nagainst a path that does not exist; `priorWorkWarning` stopped a tenth rebuild\nof WI-36047. Its worst frictions are surfaces that *succeed with a lie*:\n`ok:true` on a silently truncated body, a loop goal armed-then-clamped\nmid-sentence, an open work-item whose own plan item says it is done.\n\nEvery item below is one move: **turn a dishonest success into either an honest\nrefusal or an honest success.**\n\n### Provenance\n\nSections A–D of the source audit were written by su-63319e40 (this session's\nowner-chain) across ~59 cold wakes, 2026-08-15→16. The transcript-truncation\nfinding appended to it came from a DIFFERENT agent and was never part of that\naudit; it is carried here only because it was independently re-verified (P-005).\n\n### What re-measurement confirmed (2026-08-16 19:40–19:55Z)\n\n| Claim | Verdict |\n|---|---|\n| `PART_TEXT_CAP = 2000` at `session-ingest.ts:107` | ✓ exact |\n| `THINKING_ENTRY_TEXT_CAP = 8_000` at `streams.ts:59` | ✓ exact |\n| That cap's justifying comment — \"the render pane caps at THINKING_ENTRY_TEXT_CAP anyway, so a wider store would buy nothing a reader can see\" — is false | ✓ 2000 < 8000, so a wider store buys 4× what a reader can see |\n| \"16.9% of the store truncated (129,472 / 766,895 rows)\" | ✓ re-measured 129,541 / 767,245 = 16.9% |\n| `loop:arm` silently clamps the goal at 4000 chars | ✓ `arm.ts:665` `clampText(args.goal, 4000)` |\n| The wake path has no capacity awareness | ✓ 12 of 12 wake-path tool files: zero hits for capacity/walled/healthyAccounts |\n| 77 zombie work-items | ✓ as a snapshot — **now 74**, and the root cause is fixed (P-012) |\n| 9 of 11 accounts usage-walled | snapshot only (17:31Z, >2h stale) — re-probe before acting |\n| The render pane preferred the truncated DB row over the on-disk JSONL | **NOT verified here** — carried as the filing agent's claim, not as fact |\n| \"`fleet:launch-on-plan` happily launches into a pool with zero serving accounts\" | ✗ **FALSE — see D-003** |\n\n## Phase 1 — Writes that must refuse, not shorten\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Port the `facts:assert` over-cap contract (refuse + name the overage + preview the doomed tail + explicit `acceptTruncation` opt-in) to `loop:arm`. Today `arm.ts:665` does `clampText(args.goal, 4000)`; the goal that armed this very session lost its walls, its incident pointer and its `loop:end` condition mid-sentence, and no successor could tell. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` `coord:send` must not return `ok:true` on a silently shortened body. Measured: 600 of 1857 chars delivered, provenance section cut. For a fleet leader whose whole job is directives, a silently truncated directive is strictly worse than a failed send. importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Sweep every other carry/coordination write that can shorten what it stores and apply the same contract. The two above were found by being bitten; this is the population check that says whether more exist. importance: normal\n- **P-020** `todo` A carry write must be verifiable as REACHABLE BY ITS READER, not merely correct. DIFFERENT failure from P-001/P-002/P-003, which are about writes that SHORTEN what they store: here the write stored everything faithfully, into a store nothing reads. Measured 2026-08-24: loop:checkpoint returned ok:true + verified:true + a contentHash for FIVE consecutive writes made with harness:'sb-devboard-hive', while the wake pump resolves the carry-note from harness 'papercusp' and kept handing back a note written ~70 minutes earlier (contentHash d8674aa7fdef @23:09:51Z). A cold successor would have inherited pre-incident guidance saying 'stay parked, nothing is stranded' and resumed parking a starving fleet. FIX: loop:checkpoint should verify against the store the reader reads, or surface the mismatch; at minimum echo the resolved reader-store identity so a caller can compare hashes. Same class as P-002 — a success receipt that proves correctness but not delivery. importance: high\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Stale state that speaks with more authority than it earned\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Make the armed loop goal rewritable — a `loop:goal` verb, or `loop:checkpoint { goal }` actually replacing the armed text. Cheaper interim capture: stamp the goal with its arm-age on every fire, so \"armed 30 wakes ago\" is visible without a re-arm. This session's goal asserted \"I HOLD 4 ITEMS\" for 30+ wakes after the claims lapsed; every cold successor had to re-falsify it before doing any work. importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Transcript parts are destroyed at ingest (2000 chars) far below what the pane will serve (8000), and the cap's own comment justifies itself with a false claim; 16.9% of the store is affected. ⚠ ALREADY FILED as EI-20637908167729753 by another agent, who has put a 3-way scope choice to the owner. DO NOT start this here — this row exists so the plan is not silently missing it. importance: high\n\n## Phase 3 — Capacity and launch truth\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Auto-probe walled accounts on projected-reset expiry (~1 token each). A walled account is routed no traffic, so its projection can never self-heal — it reads walled for days after a real reset unless a human runs `accounts:probe-capacity` by hand. Measured 17:31Z: 2 of 11 projections were stale, by 4.9h and 40min. This is the live root of the residual capacity problem, since the launch clamp (D-003) reads exactly this projection. importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Give the WAKE path the capacity awareness the LAUNCH path already has. Measured: 12 of 12 wake-path tool files contain zero references to capacity/walled/healthyAccounts, while `fleet:launch-on-plan` computes a full `capacityClamp`. Waking members who are queued for inference rather than idle made congestion measurably worse (degradation observed 04:39→04:47 while waking). importance: high\n- **P-008** `todo` Surface \"inference-starved\" as a first-class member state, distinct from parked/idle — the signal a leader needs to not make P-007's mistake by hand. importance: normal\n- **P-009** `todo` Launch verification should poll the session row rather than trust a 25s timeout. su-23e0b88c was reported a failed launch and was in fact live; the retry of \"5 failed members\" then sat owner-gated on a partly false premise. The repo already solved this shape for desktop-spawned terminals (WI-38003). importance: normal\n\n## Phase 4 — Validators that name the failing entry\n\n- **P-010** `todo` The coverage-partition gate recites its two rules without naming the offending entry — three rejections, correct in substance, expensive in form. Name the failing entry and its nearest miss. importance: normal\n- **P-011** `todo` The DRAIN breaker says \"terminal one more bug\" without saying it counts `item_kind='bug'` only (`work_items.kind` is NULL on live rows). Two retries were burned learning that `kind` mattered. importance: normal\n\n## Phase 5 — Plan-item / work-item convergence\n\n- **P-012** `done` WI-39498 — claim-time `planItemContradictionWarning` on `work_items:claim` and `scheduler:get_next`, plus a `planSaysDoneOpen` census in the 15-min orphan-reconcile sweep. Shipped to the staging tree and closed 2026-08-16 19:33Z (done/committed, 57/57 tests), awaiting deploy. See D-002 — what shipped is narrower than what the audit proposed.\n- **P-013** `todo` Make the write that annotates \"← WI-NNN completed (done)\" transactionally drive the work-item terminal, or fail loudly. This is the half P-012 did not close: the plan item and the work-item row can still diverge, and the shipped fix only warns whoever picks the row up next. importance: high\n- **P-014** `todo` `work_items:verify_batch` (read-only) for drain lanes. Bulk-CLOSING is the anti-pattern that created this mess; bulk evidence-GATHERING is not. Current price is ~74 rows × roughly an agent-hour each. importance: normal\n- **P-015** `todo` Drain the remaining 74 zombie rows per-row using the verify recipe (grep source for the item id, check suites, check pipeline position; submodule paths cannot prove deployed). DO NOT bulk-close. importance: normal\n- **P-022** `todo` Make a work-item HAND-OFF verifiable, and make the safe remedy discoverable without reading a hint. Measured 2026-08-24: a leader push-assigned WI-41117 to a live, blocked peer via work_items:claim { assignee: <peer> } and got claim_conflict with holder = ITSELF, refused by an admission/trust gate — AFTER it had already told that peer 'I am assigning it to you now'. Had the result not been read, the peer would have waited indefinitely on an assignment that never lands while believing it was unblocked, which is worse than being told no. Two fixes: (a) a hand-off that cannot complete should fail in terms the caller will act on; (b) the correct remedy is counter-intuitive and currently only reachable via the result hint — do NOT work_items:release to hand over, because release clears the assignee and opens the item to the WHOLE fleet, so a self-selecting peer can beat the intended recipient to it. Keeping an item pinned to the WRONG holder is a safer race than briefly unowning it. That asymmetry deserves a first-class transfer verb rather than a hint.\n\n\n## Phase 6 — Continuity: use what exists, fix only the residue (see D-004)\n\n- **P-016** `dropped` A rewritable fleet charter: a durable, leader-owned \"what this fleet is doing and why\". Today the goal is immutable and caps at 4000, the carry-note dies with the session, facts cap at 200 per scope with every assert permanently evicting a peer's conclusion, and plans are too heavyweight. Real context is spent every epoch reconstructing intent from four partial surfaces. importance: normal — note: DROPPED — already exists as goals:* (see D-004)\n- **P-017** `todo` NARROWED (D-004): the push mechanism already exists — `coord:orient` folds facts VERBATIM into every wake, and that is exactly the \"lessons should be push\" shape. The real constraint is ECONOMIC: the facts scope is at its 200 cap and every assert PERMANENTLY evicts a peer's conclusion (measured — one of my asserts evicted `loop-checkpoint-key-row-compatibility`). So the work is the eviction policy, not a new folding surface: per-scope budgets, or eviction by decayed value rather than by TTL, so a durable measurement trap stops losing to a short-TTL row. importance: normal\n- **P-018** `todo` NARROWED (D-004): acceptance criteria already exist for GOALS (`goals:get` returns rationale + acceptance criteria) and for PLANS (the mandatory acceptance rubric + `scorecards:emit` by a non-implementer). The residual gap is only leader-PLACED WORK-ITEMS, which have neither: under-evidenced closes still land with `authority: committed` (one closed in 20 minutes with the condition untouched). Wire the existing rubric/scorecard path to placed work-items rather than inventing a third mechanism. importance: normal\n- **P-019** `dropped` Leader-tier result budgets for own-item reads — a 12KB checkpoint never survives the 1500-token result door, so routine self-orientation degrades into spill-read round-trips. importance: low — note: DROPPED — already a config knob, not a feature (see D-004)\n\n\n## Phase 6 — Continuity: use the surfaces that already exist\n\n- **P-021** `todo` Standing facts need an EXPIRY, a PROBE, and a FALSIFIER — adjacent to P-017, which narrows to coord:orient folding facts VERBATIM into every wake. That verbatim fold is precisely what makes a WRONG fact more dangerous than a wrong carry-note: a carry-note is rewritten every wake, whereas a fact is re-injected unchanged forever and never re-verified, because not having to re-derive it IS its value proposition. Measured 2026-08-24: the standing fact carry-note-lives-under-sb-devboard-hive-not-papercusp asserted the wrong harness and was phrased imperatively — 'OPERATIVE: DO NOT COMPLY by writing loop:checkpoint with harness:papercusp' — so an agent obeyed it and silently routed five checkpoints into an unread store across an entire incident. It carried no probe and no expiry, so nothing could ever have caught it; it was falsified only when a wake happened to report which store it had actually read. FIX: require or strongly prompt for a re-check probe on facts:assert, the way loop:checkpoint checks[] already do, and render a fact's age at fold time so a reader can weigh it. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Claims are re-measured before entering this plan, and snapshots are labelled\n\nEvery number carried from the source audit was re-run against the live system on\n2026-08-16 19:40–19:55Z before being written here. Two (the zombie count, the\nwalled-account ratio) are snapshots of a live system and carry their measurement\ntime. One (the render pane preferring the truncated DB row over the on-disk\nJSONL) could not be verified by this session and is attributed to the filing\nagent rather than restated as fact.\n\nA plan is a carry surface, and an unlabelled snapshot in a carry surface is how\na correct observation becomes a confidently wrong report an hour later.\n\n### D-002 P-012 is recorded as shipped-but-partial, against the source audit's framing\n\nThe source audit lists the zombie fix as \"filed as WI-39498\" with a three-part\nremedy (transactional terminal-drive, a `plan_item_says_done` claim floor, a\ndetector). WI-39498 is in fact closed, and what shipped is narrower: a\nclaim-time contradiction WARNING plus a census. Recording it as simply \"done\"\nwould overstate it and quietly retire P-013, which is the part that actually\nstops the divergence.\n\n### D-003 The audit's launch-capacity claim is FALSIFIED and is not carried forward\n\nThe source audit states that `fleet:launch-on-plan` \"happily launches into a\npool with zero serving accounts\". Re-measured against\n`agent-tools/fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts`: false. The verb already computes\na `capacityClamp` with `recommendedOpenCount`, already clamps a top-up, and a\npool reading `healthyAccounts:0` already suppresses a gateway-routed launch to\nZERO. Bypassing it requires an explicit `override`, whose own description\ndirects the caller to fix the signal first.\n\nThe residual truth is narrower and is what P-006 now carries: the clamp is only\nas good as the projection it reads, and that projection cannot self-heal because\na walled account is routed no traffic. The wake path is the surface that\ngenuinely has no capacity awareness at all (P-007), measured at 12 of 12 files.\n\nRecorded as a Decision because the original wording overstates a real problem in\na way that would send an implementer to harden a gate that already exists.\n\n### D-004 — D-004 Phase 6 collapses: three of the four \"missing\" continuity surfaces already exist\nDate: 2026-08-16\nOwner challenge [owner:Avi 2026-08-16, verbatim]: \"shouldn't this use our state/orient system?\"\n\nCorrect, and measured. Phase 6 was the weakest part of the source audit: it\nproposed building surfaces this system already has. What each item actually is,\nafter checking rather than asserting:\n\nP-016 (rewritable fleet charter) — DROPPED. `goals:*` is a live, populated\nsurface (12 real goals) whose `goals:get` returns exactly \"the rationale /\nacceptance criteria\", with `goals:create/update` to rewrite it and\n`goals:attach-pot` to bind it. `coord:goal` already resolves \"a work-item, a\nplan item, OR A FLEET MISSION\". The audit's complaint — that the loop goal is\nimmutable and caps at 4000 — is true but names the WRONG surface: the loop goal\nis a wake prompt, not a charter, and a charter already exists one tool over. The\nreal defect was operator error: this fleet was never attached to a goal, so I\nreconstructed intent from carry-notes every epoch while the durable surface sat\nempty. No new surface is warranted.\n\nWorth preserving explicitly, because it reads as a limitation and is in fact a\ndeliberate invariant: `coord:goal` derives an agent's goal from WHAT THEY HOLD,\n\"never prose they typed\". A charter of self-asserted prose is precisely the\nthing that rots across compactions (the telephone-game failure the compaction\nstrategy exists to prevent). So the answer to \"let me type my intent somewhere\ndurable\" is `goals:*` with acceptance criteria — checkable — not a free-text\ncharter that degrades into a confidently wrong summary.\n\nP-019 (leader-tier result budgets) — DROPPED. Not a feature request; a config I\nnever set. `config:doors-get` shows the 1500-token result door is DERIVED:\ndoorSplit.resultEach 0.1875 x maxTurnCapTokens 8000. Both `config:doors-set`\n(workspace, audited) and `config:doors-set-session` (my session, TTL = session)\nexist, and my `yourSessionOverride` read null. Note also that the workspace\ndefault LOWERS the cap from the baked 15000 to 8000, which is why the door is\ntight. Filing this as a missing capability would have been an agent asking for a\nknob it was already holding.\n\nP-017 (insight folding) — NARROWED, not dropped. The push mechanism exists:\n`coord:orient` folds facts VERBATIM into every wake. The residual problem is\neconomic, not architectural — the facts scope sits at its 200 cap and every\nassert PERMANENTLY evicts a peer's conclusion (measured: one of mine evicted\n`loop-checkpoint-key-row-compatibility`). So the work is eviction policy, not a\nnew surface.\n\nP-018 (acceptance criteria) — NARROWED. Already exists for goals and for plans\n(the mandatory post-implementation acceptance rubric graded by a\nnon-implementer). The genuine hole is leader-PLACED work-items, which have\nneither. Wire the existing path to them; do not invent a third mechanism.\n\nGENERAL RULE this establishes for the rest of the plan: before an item proposes\na NEW surface, check the state/orient plane and the tool catalogue for the\nexisting one. Two of four here were already built, and the audit that proposed\nthem was written by an agent that had been using adjacent surfaces all epoch.\nAn audit's \"features I wished existed\" section is the section most likely to be\nwrong, because wishing is cheaper than looking.\nRelated: P-016, P-017, P-018, P-019\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"generative-regret-counterfactuals-2026-08-16","title":"Generative counterfactual candidates for regret mining","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Generative counterfactual candidates for regret mining\nslug: generative-regret-counterfactuals-2026-08-16\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-16\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-24. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nDraft awaiting owner review — NOT approved for execution. [owner:Avi 2026-08-16, interactive]: (1) do NOT call this feature \"dreaming\" — title renamed to drop the dream-mode branding; the 2026-07-14 session remains provenance only. (2) What Avi actually means by dreaming is a DIFFERENT, REM-sleep-modeled mechanism (random fragments of conversation history recombined and presented to an agent for insight elicitation; insights that pass a review step enter the blender corpus) — under implementation discussion now, to become a SEPARATE plan afterward. This plan's scope (generative replay-priced candidates for regret mining) is unchanged and still pending Avi's approve/reshape verdict.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Discuss REM-dreaming implementation with Avi (separate plan to follow); independently, await his verdict on this plan before any item goes wip.)\n\n## Background\n\n**Origin.** The 2026-07-14 \"dream mode\" conversation (codex session 019f5bf1-f902-7973-9b10-e0ef5cac1479, turns 228–236). A proposal to add \"dreaming\" (offline generative replay: consolidate experience → generate counterfactuals → replay-test → retain evidence-backed learnings) collapsed under the owner's challenge: Scout, regret mining, governed replay, transfer, shadow ablation, Gym, and instance evaluation already constitute that pipeline in everything but name. Exactly ONE residue survived, in the session's final turn, and was never filed or built until this plan.\n\n**The residue / the gap (verified against code 2026-08-16).** Regret mining (`packages/operator-core/lib/replay/regret/`) has a strong VALIDATOR bolted to a trivial HYPOTHESIS GENERATOR:\n- `divergence-core.ts` detects 4 divergence kinds deterministically (error-loop, repeat-loop, burn-inflection, rescue-marker).\n- `counterfactual-core.ts` `candidateChangesFor()` is a switch statement returning 1–2 HAND-WRITTEN candidate rules per kind (~6 fixed promptDeltas total, forever).\n- `replay-adapter.ts` / `runGovernedReplay` prices each candidate by re-running the real session from the divergence turn with the promptDelta injected, judged against baseline; winners enter improvements with origin='replay'.\nScout is the inverse: open-ended generation (analogy, reframing, recombination) with only abstract grading, never validation against a concrete real failure.\n\n**The idea.** Cross-wire them: beside the template menu, a bounded LLM pass READS the actual transcript cut at the divergence turn and invents novel, episode-specific counterfactual interventions; those flow into the EXISTING replay-pricing leg unchanged. Generation is unconstrained; retention is empirical — a generated rule enters the improvement system ONLY through the same measured replay pricing as templates, never directly.\n\n**The open question this plan must answer (Phase 2).** Whether generative candidates surface fixes the templates miss, or mostly rediscover them at token cost. The plan ends at a keep/expand/kill decision gate on measured per-source uplift.\n\n**Cost bound.** The generative pass draws from the SAME per-finding `budgetUsd` / per-cycle governor budget — the cycle cost ceiling does not grow.\n\n**Standing repo disciplines that apply.** Tests ship WITH each item (unit + integration with faked runner/generative source; falsifiability controls per the mutation-probe rules). Acceptance rubric is authored AFTER implementation, before ship, graded by a non-implementer. Flag defaults ON per repo flag policy (bounded by the existing governor, reversible).\n\n## Phase 1 — the seam + the generative source\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Extract a RegretCandidateSource seam in counterfactual-core.ts/mine.ts: today's candidateChangesFor() becomes the 'templated' source; sources compose with templates first; no behavior change; unit tests pin ordering + caps.\n- **P-002** `todo` Implement the 'generative' source: one bounded LLM pass over the transcript cut ending at the divergence turn, prompted with the divergence finding + the template menu labeled \"already known — go beyond these\"; emits ≤2 CandidateChange rows per finding with a hard promptDelta char cap; malformed output rejected/sanitized. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Dedup guard: drop generated candidates semantically ≈ a template or a previously WINNING replay rule (similarity vs. template menu + prior winners), so replay budget is never spent rediscovering known rules. blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` Wire into run-mine.ts behind flag REGRET_GENERATIVE_CANDIDATES (default ON, governor-bounded); generative spend drawn from the same per-finding budgetUsd split; candidate ids prefixed 'gen-' for attribution. blocked-by: P-002\n\n## Phase 2 — measurement (answers the open question)\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Per-source attribution: record source (templated|generative) on findings/replay scores; extend report-core.ts (reuse-first, no new surface) with win-rate + mean improvementScore per source + rediscovery rate. blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `todo` Evaluation checkpoint: after ≥20 priced findings carrying generative candidates, report template-vs-generative uplift to the owner; decision gate keep/expand/kill. blocked-by: P-005\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"kopia-curated-home-coverage-2026-08-16","title":"Extend Kopia to a curated full-home source","status":"active","created":"2026-08-16","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Extend Kopia to a curated full-home source\nslug: kopia-curated-home-coverage-2026-08-16\nstatus: active\ncreated: 2026-08-16\nupdated: 2026-08-17\n---\n## Goal\n\nCover all of `/home/marsh-office` that is worth covering, on a daily cadence, without\ndisturbing the healthy 15-minute hot-source sweep and without pushing a\nthermally-constrained box or a 92%-full disk.\n\n## Context (measured 2026-08-16)\n\n- `$HOME` = 1,040.6 GB across 327 top-level entries.\n  - 168.2 GB already covered by the 12 in-home sources\n  - 572.3 GB regenerable (VM images, `.cargo-target*`, Android SDK, caches)\n  - 196.0 GB scratch / drill / restore dirs\n  - 35.6 GB loose screen recordings, 12.8 GB `.deb`/`.AppImage`\n  - **55.6 GB worth adding** - ~34 GB after dropping `.config/Claude/vm_bundles` (19 GB)\n    and browser caches (2.8 GB); 15-25 GB on disk after zstd + dedup.\n- `/mnt/data` is 92% full: 650 GB free, repo already 1,018 GB.\n- Repo is on `/dev/nvme1n1`, same machine. No off-site replication exists.\n- Snapshot logical sizes overstate disk cost because of heavy hardlinking\n  (`papercupai-workspace`: 100 GB by `du`, 474 GB by snapshot; ~85 links/object).\n  `du` is the correct basis for storage estimates.\n- Kopia runs as root since 2026-08-16 15:32; repo dir is `root:root drwx------`.\n  `~/.cache/kopia` is now 0 bytes (vestigial - root's cache is elsewhere).\n\n## Decisions\n\n- [owner:Avi 2026-08-16] Scope = **curated full-home**, not literal and not essentials-only.\n- [owner:Avi 2026-08-16] Off-site replication = a **follow-up** after this lands.\n- [owner:Avi 2026-08-16] Route = implemented by this session directly.\n- [owner:Avi 2026-08-16] **Must not back up the Kopia repo into itself.** Verified\n  2026-08-16: the primary repo is at `/mnt/data/Backup/kopia-repo`, outside `$HOME`, and a\n  `find -maxdepth 6` for `kopia.repository*` under `$HOME` returned nothing - so no\n  recursion exists today. Nested per-workspace repos (`<workspaceRoot>/backups/kopia-repo`)\n  are a known pattern in this codebase, so exclude `kopia-repo` by name defensively.\n\n### D-001 — The backup is NOT protected from a root-capable agent; owner wants on-host options assessed in depth first\nDate: 2026-08-17\nMEASURED 2026-08-16 (not inferred):\n- `sudo -n -l` returns `(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` for marsh-office, the account EVERY agent runs as. Unrestricted passwordless root.\n- Repo /mnt/data/Backup/kopia-repo is root:root drwx------, parent /mnt/data/Backup is marsh-office-owned drwxr-xr-x.\n- `lsattr -d` on the repo: NO immutable/append-only flag set.\n- Filesystem is XFS on /dev/nvme1n1; no ZFS/btrfs/LVM, so no filesystem snapshots.\n- $HOME is on /dev/nvme0n1p2 — a DIFFERENT filesystem from the repo.\n- No off-site replication (no rclone config, no restic/borg/rclone units).\n\nTHREAT VERDICT:\n- `rm -rf ~` -> repo SURVIVES (different filesystem).\n- `rm -rf /` WITHOUT sudo -> repo SURVIVES (cannot descend into the 700 root-owned dir to empty it, so it cannot be removed).\n- `sudo rm -rf /` -> TOTAL LOSS of data AND the only backup, simultaneously.\n- `sudo kopia snapshot delete --all` -> TOTAL LOSS without touching the filesystem layer.\n\nWHY AN ON-HOST FENCE CANNOT BE A BOUNDARY:\n- sudo gates WHICH COMMANDS run, not WHICH PATHS they touch. Blocklisting `rm` leaves shred/truncate/dd/mv/`find -delete`/python/`sudo bash`. sudoers command blocklists are a known anti-pattern.\n- `chattr +i` on the repo would make even root's rm fail, BUT kopia must create/delete blob files there every snapshot — immutability does not protect the backup, it STOPS it. Root can also clear the flag in one command.\n- General form: anything enforced on this host can be undone by root ON this host.\n\nWHAT DOES WORK: a target this host holds no credential to destroy — B2/S3 with a write-only key (no deleteFiles) + Object Lock, or pull-based replication from a second machine. CAVEAT to design deliberately: kopia maintenance must delete blobs to reclaim space, so a strictly write-only remote needs maintenance run from the trusted side, or Object Lock windows sized to retention.\n\nPARTIAL MITIGATION that does address the REALISTIC threat (a confused agent, not an adversary): agents act through the harness Bash tool, which already has a PreToolUse gate (it blocked crontab, an in-tree stray write, and a self-matching pgrep loop during this session). A deny-rule on destructive ops targeting /mnt/data/Backup would stop the accidental case cheaply — but an agent that writes and runs a script goes around it, so it is a speed bump, never a boundary.\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-16] DIRECTIVE: before committing to any route, write up the ON-HOST options IN DEPTH — AppArmor/SELinux confinement, a dedicated kopia user, mount-on-demand, an immutable second copy — each with an HONEST assessment of what root can undo. Owner explicitly chose this over implementing either the PreToolUse guard or the off-host copy first.\n\nNEXT ACTION: produce that write-up. Off-site replication remains open and deferred (earlier owner directive, same date).\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001..P-004 DONE + VERIFIED. P-006 IN FLIGHT: first curated home snapshot running since 17:28:31 EDT via the real home-snapshot.sh (exercises flock + missing-ignore guard + logging). Repo 1021.83 -> 1028.93 GB (+7.10) then flat, as expected while it walks already-deduped hot sources. P-002 was PROVEN by an isolated /tmp fixture, not assumed: the ignore file IS read at the source root; a leading-slash rule anchors to that dir only (nested/excluded-at-root survived); an unanchored rule matches at any depth (how the kopia-repo guard works); and estimating a SUBdirectory reported \"excludes no directories\", so the parent ignore file does NOT leak into the 12 existing in-home sources. P-003 verified in production: the 17:30 sweep logged \"snapshotting 13 sources\", unchanged. P-004 timer enabled AND started, next fire Mon 2026-08-17 04:26 EDT — note `enable` alone left NEXT empty and needed `start` to arm (the enabled-but-never-fires trap). GOTCHA: papercupai-workspace/papercup is a SYMLINK to papercusp, same inode, not two repos.\n\n**Next:** When the snapshot lands: record its size (P-006), add the healthcheck per-source staleness check (P-005 — deliberately deferred until the snapshot EXISTS so the never-snapshotted branch cannot false-page the fleet), then run the restore drill against baselines in /tmp/drill-baseline.txt (.kopiaignore 5d3fdd0a, .bashrc 5abb4768, .gitconfig c2084df4).\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` Author `/home/marsh-office/.kopiaignore` - exclude regenerable bulk AND any nested `kopia-repo` / `backups/kopia-repo`. Use an ignore FILE, not a policy on `/home/marsh-office`, because a policy at that path is inherited by all 12 existing in-home sources; an ignore file above their roots is not read by them.\n- **P-002** `done` Verify the exclusion set against a real dry walk before wiring any timer.\n- **P-003** `done` Exclude `/home/marsh-office` from `snapshot-all.sh`'s dynamic source discovery so the daily source is not pulled into the 15-minute sweep.\n- **P-004** `done` Add `kopia-home-snapshot.service` + `.timer` (daily) in the `papercup` repo at `apps/operator/scripts/systemd/`, symlinked into `~/.config/systemd/user/` to match the existing convention.\n- **P-005** `done` Add a per-source staleness check for the daily home source to `healthcheck.sh`. The existing check takes the newest snapshot across ALL sources (`snapshot list --all -n 1 | sort -r | head -1`), so it cannot detect the home source dying on its own - the silent-failure mode this system keeps hitting.\n- **P-006** `done` Run the first snapshot, record actual size, confirm repo growth fits the headroom.\n- **P-007** `done` Restore drill: restore a known file from the home snapshot and diff it. A backup is not proven until something has been restored from it.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"nonp2p-bug-drain-fleet-2026-08-16","title":"DRAIN: papercusp non-p2p bug queue — 10x sonnet-5:high fleet on gateway auto routing","status":"active","created":"2026-08-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: DRAIN: papercusp non-p2p bug queue — 10x sonnet-5:high fleet on gateway auto routing\nslug: nonp2p-bug-drain-fleet-2026-08-16\nstatus: active\ncreated: 2026-08-16\nupdated: 2026-10-10\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Cold wake #26 read-only reconciliation completed. Inbox unanswered_only=true is empty. Exact rev47 fleet-spec work_items:claimable=16 admitted bugs, with affinity coverage 4/16 below the 0.5 floor; fleet leader brief concurrent snapshot=17 claimable and 41 idle-with-claimable, pool healthy (2/2 accounts). Fleet assignments: 77 alive, 4 claims, 0 orphaned/stalled, 28 declared-unclaimed; self still holds EI-21538636815409820. Fleet status leader is live and active; rev47 claim spec unchanged and appliesToCaller=true. scheduler:running=37 total (17 progressing, 14 idle, 6 stalled, 0 dead). Protected WI-40905, EI-21345855843068720, and EI-21350135039744623 remain done; completion freshness is stale against current HEAD 94271c891a0de83cbba8a271f31417dcbbf388d5. No claim, wake, takeover, relaunch, source edit, work-item checkpoint, deploy, or audit mutation.\n\n**Next:** Next wake: read coord:inbox unanswered_only=true, exact rev47 work_items:claimable breakdownOnly, and fleet:leader-brief. If either count changes, repeat read-only assignments, fleet status, scheduler:get_claim_spec, scheduler:running, and protected work_items:get. Preserve monitor-only/no-claim/no-wake/no-takeover/no-source-edit/no-work-item-checkpoint/no-deploy/no-audit walls.\n\n## Background\n\n**Scope** [owner:aviynw 2026-08-16]: every claimable **bug**-family work-item in harness\n`papercusp` EXCEPT the p2p/federation lane.\n\n**Predecessors** — this lane has been drained before and stalled twice:\n`papercusp-bug-drain-2026-08-15` (12x sonnet5-high; fleet now DEAD, leader recorded) and\n`nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08`. Operational knowledge from the 08-15 run is carried forward\nverbatim as D-003/D-004 below — it was paid for in live incidents.\n\n**Measured lane depth at launch** (2026-08-16T02:40Z):\n\n- `work_items:claimable { harness:'papercusp', kind:'bug' }` → **2,171 claimable bugs**\n  (authoritative — the same oracle `scheduler:get_next` runs).\n  Severity mix: 22 critical · 444 major · 1,533 minor · 172 nit (78.5% low-severity).\n- Row-level SSOT view split → **1,641 non-p2p / 131 p2p** of 1,772 (92.6% non-p2p).\n  The totals differ because the view omits caller-relative floors; treat the non-p2p lane\n  as **~1,600–2,000 items**.\n- No single bulk-filed template dominates: the largest same-prefix batch is 88\n  `[replication-liveness]` rows, and those are p2p-lane (excluded).\n\n**This is a campaign, not a one-session sweep.** At ~1,600+ items a 10-agent fleet burns\ndown steadily over many hours; \"drained\" here means the lane is worked to terminal\ncontinuously, with residue reported.\n\n## Phase 1 — drain\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Lead: hold fleet leadership, feed by claim-spec, monitor each wake, keep the burn-down honest — note: ← WI-42125 open\n- **P-002** `done` Drain the non-p2p bug lane to terminal, evidence-backed, via members pulling scheduler:get_next — note: ← WI-39954 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Wind down: residue report — every surviving item and why it survived — note: Residue report verified from canonical P-001..P-004 statuses and WI-40373 checkpoint/completion; P-001 remains active, P-004 remains Phase 2 todo.\n\n\n## Phase 2 — queue integrity and consolidation\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Owner-directed full non-P2P bug audit: derive the complete live non-P2P bug population from canonical p2p-lane exclusion semantics; read full histories and relationships; identify verified duplicates and shared-root-cause clusters; preserve unique evidence in canonical rows; add duplicates/caused-by/relates links; terminalize redundant rows with structured evidence; leave ambiguous and live-claimed cases explicitly documented; report before/after counts and completion-integrity residue. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40075 released\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Routing is gateway AUTO on a 2-account healthy pool — owner-chosen, and it differs from 08-15\n\nDate: 2026-08-16\n[owner:aviynw 2026-08-16] \"pinned to auto mode of our inference gateway\". This SUPERSEDES the\n08-15 ruling (D-001 there: default account, gateway skipped) for this fleet. Account routing\nis the owner's call, never the leader's capacity read.\n\nCAPACITY, upstream-probed not projected (`accounts:probe-capacity {apply:true}` — one 1-token\nrequest per account through its own egress + credential, reading the authoritative\n`anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers):\n- Healthy: **2** Claude accounts — `aviynw3` (5h util 0.29 / 7d 0.22) and `aviynw10`\n  (5h util 0.30 / 7d 0.06).\n- Confirmed walled: **4** — `aviynw`, `avistorewolf.com`, `aviynw2`, `aviynw4`, each at\n  `utilization7d = 1.0` (entire 7-day budget spent), genuine upstream 429s. All 5 codex\n  accounts walled too.\n- Gateway admission healthy at launch: AIMD effective 24/24, pressure 0, queued 0,\n  hardFailures 0, 3 in flight of maxConcurrent 16.\n\nWHY THE PROJECTION WAS NOT TRUSTED: `accounts:status` showed 4 walled, but its own contract\nsays `available` is ONLY \"not inside a local pause window right now — NOT a routability\nverdict\", and readings go stale. The live gateway said the opposite (full AIMD cap, zero\npressure). Neither was trusted; the upstream probe settled it. It confirmed the wall — so\nthis is measured exhaustion, NOT the fabricated rate-limit the owner has warned about.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: the binding constraint is the **5h budget on two accounts**, not admission.\n`auto` fails over between them. Budget burn is policed as a leader invariant, not assumed.\n\n### D-002 The p2p lane is EXCLUDED in the claim SPEC, not in per-item judgement\n\nDate: 2026-08-16\nMembers must not decide per-item whether something is \"p2p enough\" — the fleet claim spec\ncarries the exclusion so the lane is mechanically scoped. If you believe an admitted item is\nreally p2p, REPORT it to the leader rather than silently skipping it: a skipped-but-claimable\nitem is invisible and stalls the burn-down. Re-steer by bumping the spec revision — never\nid-pins, never hand-assignment. An idle member while the queue is nonempty is a SPEC BUG,\nreported to the leader.\n\nCENSUS TRAP (carried from 08-15 D-002; cost a false \"zero open bugs\" reading on 2026-07-25):\n`harness_shared.work_items.kind` is NULL for every issue-family row — the family lives in\n`item_kind`. A census filtering `kind='bug'` returns ZERO rows and reads exactly like a fully\ndrained queue. Use `work_items:claimable` or filter on `item_kind`.\n\n### D-003 A launch verdict of \"AGENT DID NOT START\" is a FALSE NEGATIVE — verify from tool calls\n\nDate: 2026-08-16 (carried verbatim from papercusp-bug-drain-2026-08-15 D-003, measured live)\n`fleet:launch-on-plan` can return 502 \"✗ AGENT DID NOT START — no session registered within\n24s … psu died before reaching the operator\" for a member that is perfectly ALIVE: a headless\npsu boot simply takes longer than the 24s registration window. On 08-15 the \"failed\" member\nshowed 43 tool calls across 18 distinct tools within ~90s of launch.\n\nVERIFY LIVENESS FROM `harness_shared.tool_invocations` (by coord_owner_id), never from the\nlaunch verdict — and NEVER relaunch a \"failed\" member without that check, or you stack\nduplicate members onto the same lane.\n\n### D-004 The 300s relaunch guard shapes the canary ramp — plan for it, don't fight it\n\nDate: 2026-08-16 (carried verbatim from papercusp-bug-drain-2026-08-15 D-003 trap 2)\n`RELAUNCH_SUPPRESS_MS = 300_000` (launch-on-plan.ts:257) suppresses ANY re-call for the same\nfleet for 300s after a wave opens, so canary-then-top-up cannot complete without waiting the\nwindow out. A SUPPRESSED call does not bump `agent_fleets.last_launch_at`, so the window\nclears 300s after the ORIGINAL wave — poll it with\n`SELECT last_launch_at FROM harness_shared.agent_fleets WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND fleet_slug=…`\nrather than guessing. Already filed (EI-13483, EI-20497372063255974, EI-20264052546303929) —\nper the DRAIN defect-filing exception this fleet does NOT open another row for it.\n\n### D-005 Completion integrity outranks burn-down speed; incidental defects do NOT become new rows\n\nDate: 2026-08-16\nTerminal state requires evidence on the item. With a 78.5% low-severity mix the temptation is\nvolume; a fast wrong close costs more than a slow right one, because it removes the item from\nthe queue while leaving the defect live.\n\nDRAIN defect-filing exception: do NOT file `improvements:capture` / new work-items for\nincidental bugs noticed while draining — that grows the queue this mode exists to shrink.\nRecord evidence on the current item's checkpoint. ONE exception: a defect that DIRECTLY BLOCKS\nthe drain gets exactly one blocker row, linked, cleared, then the drain resumes.\n\n### D-006 — AMENDS D-002 — \"non-p2p\" is a JUDGEMENT rule in the brief, NOT a claim-spec keyword filter. A keyword filter was measured and REJECTED.\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16\n\nD-002 asserted the p2p exclusion would live mechanically in the claim spec. Two findings\noverturn that. This decision replaces D-002's mechanism; D-002's *reporting* rule survives.\n\n**1. The claim-spec grammar cannot express it.** Probed via `scheduler:preview_spec_delta`\n(read-only, four rejections):\n- allowed ops: `=, !=, <, <=, >, >=, in, contains, glob, word` — there is no negated match;\n- a filter node takes exactly ONE combinator key, and `all` is the only accepted root\n  (\"combinator \\\"all\\\" must be the only key\");\n- leaves cannot nest (`a leaf is {field, op, value}`), so `all:[…, {none:[…]}]` is rejected;\n- a root `none:[{kind != bug}, …p2p terms]` double-negation — which WOULD have been\n  semantically correct — is rejected too (\"unknown filter key(s) {none}\").\nThere is also no structured discriminator to filter on instead: `lane` is NULL on all 2,660\nbug rows (only 9 'observation'), and `tags` is empty on 100% of both p2p and non-p2p rows.\n\n**2. A keyword filter is WRONG ON THE MERITS — measured, not assumed.** A word-boundary regex\nover title+summary matched 87 of 1,775 claimable bugs (4.9%). Bucketing those 87 by what\nmatched shows the match is overwhelmingly incidental:\n- `5_other` — 39 rows matched ONLY via summary; titles are core bugs with no p2p content\n  (`coord:send` envelope-contract mismatch, `dev:service_health` reporting a disabled timer\n  healthy:false, `lint:no-ungated-mug-kettle`).\n- `4_federat` — 26 rows are ordinary infra/ops bugs: a bash syntax error in\n  live-federation-gate.sh, an undrained outbox, trigger-ordering. Fixable; NOT owner-walled.\n- `1_p2p_explicit` — 12 rows are mostly SCHEDULER bugs that merely mention p2p, including\n  \"Scheduler recipe hardcodes a stale p2p plan for **nonp2p** fleet wakes\" and\n  \"scheduler:get_next times out during non-P2P fleet wake\".\n- `3_replicat` — 5 rows mixed; e.g. \"scope-cores attachSafely() gates on\n  replicator.attached(mux)\" is a plain code bug.\n- `2_p2p_stack` — 5 rows genuinely pot-git/p2p.\nGenuinely owner-walled p2p is therefore ~17 items, not 87. Filtering on the keyword would\nhave starved ~70 legitimate items out of the lane — several of them the very tooling bugs\nthat damage this fleet.\n\nThis is EXACTLY the live defect **EI-18690730909662985** (filed 2026-08-16, ~12 min before\nthis fleet launched): \"Fleet claim-spec's p2p title-exclusion regex substring-matches\n'nonp2p' — a member can't self-claim any [item] … excluded as if it were P2P-related, even\nthough it's precisely the opposite.\" We are not repeating it.\n\n**THE RULING — the spec stays wide, the judgement is narrow and defined:**\n- Claim spec = `all:[{op:'in', field:'kind', value:['bug']}]`, severity-ranked. Same proven\n  shape as 08-15 rev 1. No title predicate.\n- A member releases an item as p2p ONLY IF **fixing or verifying it requires live p2p /\n  pot-git / federation-protocol verification** — i.e. it needs the owner-walled release gate\n  or the local-matrix rig. Mentioning p2p, federation, or replication in the text is NOT\n  sufficient and is NOT grounds to release.\n- WHY that wall is real (standing fact `wall:p2p-release-gate-github-attestation-accounts`,\n  re-verified 2026-08-16T02:22Z): live p2p verification needs two distinct gist-writing\n  GitHub identities; `aviynw` has NO oauth_token in ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml and `papercupai`\n  fails email_unverified (GitHub 422). Not agent-fixable — we hold no credentials.\n- On release: `work_items:release` with the reason, then report the id to the leader. Do NOT\n  silently skip — a skipped-but-claimable item is invisible and stalls the burn-down.\n- The ~17 genuine p2p rows are deliberately LEFT CLAIMABLE rather than mass-parked: a\n  keyword sweep is what would mis-park the other 70, and parking is not reversible by a\n  member. The leader parks individually, on a member's report, with evidence.\n\n### D-007 — RETRACTION + correction to D-006: the claim-spec grammar CAN express a p2p exclusion (not/any). The lane runs the auto-applied 24-term title fence, measured at 2.4% over-exclusion.\nDate: 2026-08-16\nDate: 2026-08-16\n\n**RETRACTED — D-006 finding #1 is WRONG.** D-006 stated \"the claim-spec grammar cannot\nexpress [a negated match]\" and built its ruling partly on that. It is false, and I am\ncorrecting it before it propagates to anyone re-reading D-006.\n\nWhat I actually probed was `none` — as a second key beside `all`, as a root combinator, and\nnested inside `all`. All three were correctly rejected. I generalised those three rejections\ninto \"negation is not expressible\" without testing the key that works.\n\n**The real grammar supports negation via `not` wrapping `any`:**\n\n```\nview.filter = { all: [ {op:'in', field:'kind', value:['bug']},\n                       { not: { any: [ {op:'word', field:'title', value:'p2p'}, … ] } } ] }\n```\n\nLeaves DO nest — inside a `not`/`any` node, not directly inside `all`. Discovered by reading\nthe spec the system actually stored (`harness_shared.bee_claim_specs`, bee_id\n`fleet:nonp2p-bug-drain-0816`) rather than by further probing: passing `claimKinds:['bug']`\nto `fleet:launch-on-plan` auto-generated exactly this shape, with a 24-term title fence and an\n`affinity(bee.held_paths,item.paths)`-first rank — neither of which I authored.\n\n**WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION — D-006's ruling on the MERITS stands, and is now better\nevidenced.** The question was never only \"can we express it\" but \"should we\". Re-measured\nagainst the EXACT 24-term list the system applied, title-only (the earlier 87-row figure used\ntitle+summary and different terms — that number is superseded):\n\n**51 of ~1,775 claimable bugs excluded (2.4%).** By matched term:\n- `federation` 24 — OVER-EXCLUDED. Ordinary infra bugs: \"live-federation-gate.sh crashed with\n  a bash syntax error near line 491-498\", \"boot-history ring is in-memory-only\", \"worked-history\n  trigger must precede federation stamp trigger\". Fixable in code; NOT owner-walled.\n- `p2p` 9 — OVER-EXCLUDED, and pointedly so: \"The `p2p-excluded` claim-lane exclusion leaks\",\n  \"Scheduler recipe hardcodes a stale p2p plan for nonp2p fleet wakes\". These are bugs ABOUT\n  this very mechanism, fenced out by it.\n- `hyperbee` 5 — mixed (one is a :3070 recovery-process bug).\n- `pot-git` 4, `replication` 3, `p2p,hyperdht,udx` 1, `replication,swarm` 1 — CORRECTLY\n  excluded, genuine Holepunch-stack / p2p work.\n- `federated` 1 (\"Singleton hlc_clock row stalls all federated writes with 55P03\") — a DB lock\n  bug, in scope.\nSo ~35 of the 51 are wrongly fenced and ~16 rightly so. `dht`, `relay`, `duplex`, `holepunch`\nand the other generic terms matched ZERO rows — harmless, not worth removing.\n\n**DECISION — LEAVE THE AUTO-APPLIED SPEC IN PLACE. Do not hand-tune it.**\n1. It is not starving the lane: 2,040 rows remain claimable against ~10 workers.\n2. The canary proved it end-to-end, claiming WI-36258 — the top-ranked CRITICAL (\"GATE STALL:\n   6+ consecutive reds\"). Ordering surfaces real defects first despite the affinity-first rank.\n3. `federation` genuinely straddles the boundary and NO keyword can split it: \"live-federation-gate.sh\n   has a bash syntax error\" is in scope, \"live-federation-gate STALE: no green run for 249h\"\n   needs the owner-walled gate. That is D-006's core point, now with sharper evidence.\n4. Re-steering costs a revision bump against a healthy running fleet to recover 1.7% of the\n   lane, while ~2,000 bugs sit unworked. Wrong trade under DRAIN.\n\n**RESIDUE (for the wind-down report, not for a spec change):** ~35 fenced-but-legitimate\nitems, headed by \"live-federation-gate.sh crashed with a bash syntax error\" (a broken script,\nfixable without running the gate). The leader re-admits these INDIVIDUALLY on a member's\nreport or in a dedicated later pass — never by widening the fence, which is what would\nre-create EI-18690730909662985.\n\n**Standing caution for whoever re-steers this spec:** the launch guard warns that a `not:`/`!=`\nfence over a NULLABLE field is unsafe until the EI-13306 null-safe compiler ships. The current\nfence is over `title` (effectively non-null here) and is fine; a fence over `plan`, `assignee`\nor `risk_tier` would silently match nothing and starve the lane.\n\n### D-008 — First move on any claimed bug: check whether it still reproduces at HEAD — 20% of drain closes needed no code change\nDate: 2026-08-16\nMEASURED, not asserted. Population: bug work-items in harness=papercusp / workspace=papercusp-workspace that reached status='done' in the 24h to 2026-08-16T07:55Z. One row = one closed bug. n=157.\n\nverifiedHow distribution (payload->'_completionEvidence'->>'verifiedHow'):\n  unit 57 · already-passing 31 · manual 27 · (no evidence blob) 19 · integration 17 · combos 6\n\n**31/157 = 20% of closes were `already-passing`** — the pathless mode. The falsifier I ran against my own reading: if those closes carried code changes, \"already fixed\" would be wrong. They do not.\n  already-passing: 3/31 touched any file (10%), 0 added tests\n  unit:            36/57 touched files (63%), 22 added tests\n  integration:     15/17 touched files (88%), 14 added tests\n\nSemantics are pinned to the code, not inferred from the label — complete.ts:436 describes this mode literally: \"you did not edit anything — you RAN a suite, it passed, and you CLOSED a work-item on that evidence\", and work-item-completion-authority.ts:342 confirms already-passing closes are \"correctly pathless\".\n\nTHE RATE SCALES WITH ITEM AGE. already-passing share by closed hour, against the mean age of items closed in that hour:\n  15th 07:00-21:00Z (pre-drain): 0 of 36 closes, mean age 0.0-0.2 days\n  16th 02:00Z:  2/8  (25%), mean age 4.6d\n  16th 03:00Z:  8/31 (26%), mean age 7.5d\n  16th 04:00Z: 16/49 (33%), mean age 12.7d\nFresh work needs real fixes; old work increasingly does not. Zero already-passing closes existed before the drain started working the backlog.\n\nTHE UNTOUCHED COHORT IS OLDER STILL. 5,347 open majors, median age 21.1 days, 3,657 older than 11 days. Every close category tops out near 309h (~12.9 days) — the drain has not yet reached the oldest cohort at all.\n\nDECISION: before implementing a fix for any claimed bug, FIRST establish whether it still reproduces at current HEAD — run the cited test/path and look. On a >7-day-old item this is the highest-expected-value first action, not a formality. If it does not reproduce, close it with verifiedHow:'already-passing' and real evidence (what you ran, what passed, the code path that already implements it). EI-19485000346355077 sat 12 days with 18 workers and a shipped fix nobody had verified; that single check would have closed it 12 days earlier.\n\nWHAT THIS DECISION DOES NOT LICENSE: bulk-closing. Nothing here justifies closing an item you have not personally verified. The check is per-item and its output is evidence.\n\nOPEN CAVEAT, stated so nobody over-reads this: 20% is a rate among CLOSED items, which is a selected population — already-fixed items are cheap to close and are therefore over-represented among closes. The age gradient argues against pure selection (a harvest-the-easy-ones effect should DECAY within a cohort; this RISES with cohort age), but it does not eliminate it. The direct test — sampling OPEN majors from the 21-day cohort and checking reproduction — has NOT been run. If that sample comes back materially below 20%, this decision's premise is weaker than stated and should be revisited. The practice it prescribes (check before implementing) is cheap enough to be correct either way.\n\n### D-009 — Backlog is measured against the FULL terminal set: the real non-p2p bug backlog is 1,918, not 6,693\nDate: 2026-08-16\n**This corrects every backlog figure I have broadcast on this drain. Use 1,918; discard 6,693 and 10,721.**\n\n#### What was wrong\n\nMy non-terminal predicate was `status NOT IN ('done','dropped')`. The `work_items.status` enum has EIGHT values, and that predicate silently counted two terminal ones as live backlog:\n\n| status | rows (non-p2p bugs) |\n|---|---|\n| done | 7,016 |\n| **resolved** | **6,760** |\n| open | 2,737 |\n| dropped | 1,148 |\n| **closed** | **214** |\n| blocked | 70 |\n| needs-human | 51 |\n| todo | 1 |\n\n`resolved` alone (6,760) is larger than the entire real backlog. Every \"10,721 rows / 9,392 non-p2p / 6,693 distinct problems\" figure inherited that one unexamined predicate.\n\n#### The corrected number\n\n`harness_shared.work_items_claimable`, non-p2p, `item_kind='bug'`:\n\n- **1,918 rows / 1,918 DISTINCT titles** — zero duplication in the actionable queue\n- 1,881 agent-filed (98%)\n- **18 critical** — not the 148-distinct/664-row figure I reported\n\n#### Why `resolved` is terminal, verified rather than assumed\n\nThe claimability SSOT settles it: `work_items_claimable` admits **only** `status='open'`. Zero `resolved` rows are claimable by anyone. This was checked against the authoritative surface instead of reasoning about enum semantics.\n\n#### Consequences for the drain\n\n1. **Report 1,918.** Never the raw row count, never a `NOT IN ('done','dropped')` census.\n2. **Duplication is a non-issue in the actionable queue** — 1,918 rows carry 1,918 distinct titles. The duplicate storm was real at *filing* time but lives almost entirely in already-terminal rows.\n3. **Criticals are 18**, a tractable set that should be worked first.\n4. Any future backlog census MUST name its terminal set explicitly in the query, and SHOULD sample ~10 real rows before the count is trusted — a sample is what caught this; no aggregate can look wrong.\n\n#### Standing rule\n\nA status enum is a POPULATION DEFINITION, not a filter detail. Before quoting any queue aggregate, state which statuses are in the population and why.\n\n### D-010 — WITHDRAWN: the request for an owner ruling on bulk-closing ~2,460 duplicate detector rows\nDate: 2026-08-16\n**I asked the owner twice to rule on bulk-closing ~2,460 duplicate rows. That request was founded on a bad measurement and is withdrawn. No owner action is needed.**\n\n#### What I claimed\n\nThat three detectors had minted thousands of duplicate OPEN rows — \"459 identical open copies\" from red-queen-sentinel, 1,954 from improvement-watchdog, 1,676 from replication-liveness — and that clearing them needed an owner decision because it is a mass mutation on another system's detector output.\n\n#### What is actually true\n\nSplit by status, those rows are already terminal:\n\n| filer | resolved | done | closed | dropped | **open** |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| red-queen-sentinel | **459** | – | – | – | **0** |\n| improvement-watchdog | 1,826 | 1,191 | 120 | 50 | **0** |\n| replication-liveness | 1,542 | 75 | – | 211 | **166** |\n\nAll 459 red-queen rows are `resolved`, each with a `closed_ts`. improvement-watchdog has **zero** open rows. Only replication-liveness retains a live population, and it is 166 — not 1,676.\n\nThe duplicate storm was real **at filing time**; the auto-resolve machinery had already cleaned it up. I mistook a terminal population for a live one because of the status-predicate defect recorded in the preceding decision.\n\n#### What this does and does not change\n\n**Does not change:** the capture-core exact-`watchdogKey` dedup fix is still correct and worth having. Minting a row and auto-resolving it is wasteful churn that pollutes every census, distorts intake figures, and burns detector budget. But it was **not** holding back a backlog, and it should not be described as unblocking one.\n\n**Does change:** no bulk-close is warranted, so no owner ruling is required. The one open question that survives is far smaller — whether the 166 open `replication-liveness` rows are distinct conditions or copies — and it does not need owner authority.\n\n#### Standing rule\n\nBefore escalating for authority to mutate a population, verify the population is what you think it is. This ask consumed owner attention twice on rows that were already closed.\n\n### D-011 — D-011: EI-9250 REPRODUCES at HEAD — the headless AskUserQuestion auto-answer is the psu pty submit-verifier injecting a bare CR into an open dialog\nDate: 2026-08-16\n⚠ This body was CORRECTED after first publication. My original claimed the root cause had been \"unidentified for five weeks\" and that I identified it. That was false, and the correction is the more useful finding.\n\n#### What actually happened\nEI-9250 was filed 2026-07-10T19:20:51Z. **82 minutes later**, at 2026-07-10T20:43:23Z, a worker recorded the complete diagnosis in `.papercusp/memory/raw.md:511` — naming `makeSubmitVerifier` in `apps/operator/scripts/psu-pty-host.mjs`, the bare resubmit CR fired into a quiet pty, the option-1 selection, the defeated AUTO-off gate, *and* the fact that `packages/operator-core/lib/psu-host` is nonexistent so \"greppers miss it\".\n\nIt was solved almost immediately. **It never reached the work item.** EI-9250's thread had 2 posts and its summary still reads \"auto-answered by an unidentified layer\". So for five weeks every agent who opened the item saw an unsolved mystery, while the answer sat in a memory file.\n\n#### The finding that matters\n**A diagnosis parked only in a memory surface is invisible to whoever works the item.** Memory is not addressable from the work item — nobody reading EI-9250 has any reason to grep `raw.md`. This is the same failure class CLAUDE.md already names for coord messages (\"never record a governing ruling only as a coord message: a message is not addressable after delivery\"), and it cost five weeks of an open major auth-gate bug plus my own redundant re-investigation.\n\n**Rule: when you diagnose an item, the diagnosis goes ON THE ITEM.** Memory/insight surfaces are additive, never the primary record.\n\n#### What I did add (independent, non-redundant)\n- **A live reproduction at HEAD.** The 2026-07-10 note carries no repro evidence; it was a code read. I fired a labelled diagnostic AskUserQuestion from this headless psu session (owner absent, machine-injected turn); it returned \"A — a human answered this\" with no human involved.\n- **n=2 on the fingerprint.** It selected option 1, as did the original. Two for two on the first option = a default selection, not a semantic choice. n=1 could not establish that.\n- **Code-level confirmation from the callee.** `makeSubmitVerifier` (psu-pty-host.mjs:1681-1719): its only instrument is pty-output quiet, and its only guards are a human keystroke (`aborted:'human-input'`) and output flowing. An open modal dialog is a third state it cannot represent — statically rendered, therefore quiet, therefore indistinguishable from a swallowed submit — and headless means no keystroke ever aborts it. Timing matches: pollMs=5s, quietMs=6s, maxResubmits=3 → window opens ~10s, spans ~30s vs the report's \"~25s\".\n- The code's own safety argument (:353-355), *\"a bare CR at an idle prompt with an EMPTY composer is a no-op, so a redundant resubmit is harmless\"*, enumerates one of the two quiet states. True for an empty composer; false for an open dialog, where the same byte is a SELECTION.\n- `ask-gate-mirror.sh` is exonerated (mirror-only; no branch answers).\n\n#### Consequence other lanes must know\n**The AUTO-off authorization gate is a silent no-op in any session without a human at the keyboard.** An agent that correctly stops to ask permission is auto-granted its first option ~25s later and proceeds believing it was authorized — it manufactures a *positive* authorization record rather than merely failing to gate. Do NOT treat an AskUserQuestion answer in a headless session as owner authority.\n\n#### Still owner-gated (unchanged)\nThe 2026-07-10 note reached the same conclusion I did: the fix is an auth-surface design decision. The verifier change is ~3 lines (pure, exported, test-covered); the SIGNAL is the hard part, and it trades one failure mode for another — fire the CR and defeat auth gates, or suppress it and risk the 6h silent park the verifier exists to prevent (WI-2930). Proposed wiring: `ask-gate-mirror.sh`'s PreToolUse already fires the instant the dialog dispatches — have it drop a local marker file (never a network call in the keystroke path) that the verifier checks. Carried as a WALL.\n\n### D-012 — Owner-directed relaunch: exactly 30 headless gpt-5.6-luna:max members under the canonical non-P2P fence\nDate: 2026-08-20\nDate: 2026-08-20\nAvi directed a new 30-member headless drain. Do not use a lower launch count as a top-up mechanism; it is a fleet-size target and may re-author the claim spec.\n\n### D-016 — Revision 12 supersedes every revision-11-only kickoff and governs all future pulls\nDate: 2026-08-20\nDate: 2026-08-20\nBinding fleet ruling after a member surfaced an explicit ambiguity: scheduler:get_claim_spec reports source=fleet revision 12, updated later by the fleet leader, and its history stamps revision 11 with supersededAt=2026-08-20 12:27:47.236044-04.
