My original D-025 correctly recorded that the 2026-08-21 probe rewrote revision 23 to broader revision 24, and that preview measured 893 current claimable vs 809 under the prior filter (84 newly excluded, 0 newly admitted) before exact content was restored as monotonic revision 25. However, its proposed future mechanism—calling fleet:launch-on-plan without claimKinds—was wrong and is withdrawn. D-019 remains the authority: resume/respawn an existing member where possible; if a genuinely new member is required, use a launch path that cannot rewrite the fleet spec, and restore/verify the sentinel before any pull. Revision 25 is the current semantic restoration of revision 23. Target live fleet size remains 31.\n\n### D-026 — Fail closed on Excalidraw Twitter/X and Reddit content egress\nDate: 2026-08-21\nRuntime validation on WI-7115 proved that a user Web Embed action loads platform.twitter.com/widgets.js, Twitter embed frames/scripts, and syndication endpoints. This is third-party content egress with viewer-disclosure risk, not a latency-only CDN dependency. Apply the existing privacy posture used for PlantUML: disable Twitter/X and Reddit embeddables unless the implementation can guarantee a local/privacy-preserving render with no third-party script or content requests. A fix must include a recurrence guard that exercises the user path, and the no-cdn-egress baseline may be relaxed only after the bundled/runtime path is demonstrably unreachable or absent. Preserve unrelated safe embed capability only where the same guarantee holds.\n\n### D-027 — EI-21146697358057973: release promotion is part of the detector fix\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe false verified-timeout evidence was emitted by the old papercup-dev-api :3070 runtime (treeSha a2d69cef50) before the run-lock-aware observer was loaded. The durable source remediation already exists in staging at a6b917b424 and passes the focused checkpoint-verified-wait + engine suite (85/85 on HEAD d2ce387694). This item must not be closed on staging tests alone: completion requires the exact source SHA to pass the green gate, reach main/deployed, and then an independent runtime-vintage check proving :3070 runs the promoted build. Until then, report :3070 as old release code and staging as un-deployed; never force-deploy past a red gate.\n\n### D-028 — Fleet member pulls are papercusp-scoped; cross-harness oracle probes do not gate this drain\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe fleet sentinel is source=fleet, revision 37, harnessSlug=papercusp. Every member must run scheduler:get_next for the papercusp harness (or omit an override that would move the pull elsewhere) and must evaluate claim floors against that same harness. A probe performed with harness=sb-devboard-hive answers a different queue and cannot establish that the papercusp drain is blocked. EI-21183894547711702 and its two sampled sb-devboard-hive rows are therefore outside this drain's scope; do not claim or use them to widen/rewrite revision 37. Return to the papercusp scheduler lane and park on work-item:claimable when it reports zero admitted rows. Evidence: scheduler:get_claim_spec live read on 2026-08-22 reports source=fleet, revision=37, harnessSlug=papercusp; EI-21183894547711702 itself is stored under harness sb-devboard-hive.\n\n### D-029 — Headcount reconciliation uses host-backed workers; retire residue, not governor seats\nDate: 2026-08-23\nThe durable headcount_target is 30 workers and the fleet leader is excluded from that target. The governor's writer computes live workers with liveFleetMemberIds(...).filter(id => id !== fleet.leaderOwnerId), which requires a live psu host. fleet:status.memberCount is a different presence-roster count: it can temporarily include parked/resumable or unmanaged residue. Therefore the healthy steady state is leader + 30 host-backed Luna Max workers, while memberCount must be reduced to 31 only by ending verified claimless/fileless/lockless residue identities. Killing a real host-backed worker merely causes a governor replacement and does not solve roster inflation. Re-check both the governor writer and fleet:status after every retirement; preserve every work-item or plan-item claimholder.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-030 — Headcount target counts workers only; 30 means 30 workers plus the leader\nDate: 2026-08-23\nThe standing fleet mission is exactly 30 gpt-5.6-luna:max workers plus the leader. The persisted agent_fleets.headcount_target MUST therefore be 30. Writer evidence: packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/fleet-headcount-action.ts computes liveFleetMemberIds(...).filter(id => id !== fleet.leaderOwnerId).length before computeHeadcountDeficit, so the governor target excludes the leader. By contrast fleet:status.memberCount includes the live su leader (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet_registry/status.ts and its roster-count test). Operational invariant: headcount_target=30 and fleet:status.memberCount=31 are aligned; do not 'restore' the target to 31 from the total-session count.\n\n### D-031 — Root dependency recovery has one leader-owned serializer\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDuring WI-40965, agents with different TMPDIR values used different fs-mutex roots (`/tmp/pcv/fs-mutex-locks` vs `/tmp/pcv/pcv/fs-mutex-locks`), allowing concurrent root npm reifiers that hollowed packages and crash-looped papercup-staging-api. Until the stable lock-root fix is committed and verified, no fleet member may launch root `npm install` or `npm ci` (bare or wrapped). The fleet leader owns the sole recovery install; D-025 su-049 remains the only Papercusp gate serializer and must be coordinated before any dependency action.\n\n### D-032 — Dependency recovery gate satisfied; tests may resume\nDate: 2026-08-23\nWI-40965 completed at commit cfeb2a1d6a782d3e558df923599d1d8829ef73e4. The fs mutex now resolves `/tmp/pcv/fs-mutex-locks` on POSIX independent of TMPDIR; 14/14 recurrence tests and both file-scoped typecheck gates pass. All four incident packages import, papercup-staging-api is stable on :3170, and no root installer remains. Fleet lanes may resume tests. Root installs remain forbidden bare and must use `npm run install:safe` / `node scripts/npm-install-safe.mjs`; D-025 serialization remains solely su-049.\n\n### D-033 — Complete EI-212719 from scoped evidence; whole-tree authored-docs gate is unavailable\nDate: 2026-08-23\nFleet-leader ruling from coord message mt6amuj8-0000-5e1f98209616404b9ebcd4085fdb3e76 (2026-08-23T21:02Z): EI-21271940404773459 may complete from its terminal-quality scoped evidence (6/6 focused guard tests, affected-tests syntax, 96-occurrence ratchet, bundle-host shell/build, 784-file migration lint, scoped operator+scripts typechecks). The broad 100-task test:affected run is explicitly NON-VERDICT and must not block this item because gen:authored-docs:check is deliberately paused/unavailable and its reproduced federation-public-release-known-limitations.mdx vs live-PG drift is candidate-external, matching EI-21079330201572062. Completion must disclose the unavailable whole-tree verdict and preserve the docs-gate recurrence as separate residue; do not claim the broad suite green.\n\n### D-034 — Use fleet:status active headcount; suppress stale-roster refill\nDate: 2026-08-24\nAt 2026-08-24 ~07:34Z, the authoritative fleet:status read reported memberCount=31, while fleet:leader-brief reported a 69-row roster containing 38 dead historical/stale identities. Therefore the brief's roster count must not trigger a replacement launch or self-end; use fleet:status for active headcount. Pool capacity is healthy (2 usable/2 available accounts), claim spec is revision 47, and 214 issues are admitted. Four parked claimless identities were examined: su-077b6699, su-8b6ee6, and su-498a72 picked up admitted work after a required wake; su-9fc2181d remains parked under an owner-directed stand-down and is intentionally untouched. Generation 2 remains declared/pending with no live successor. WI-40539 stays validation-only: no qualification emit, serializer takeover, checkpoint/deploy, source edit, or WI-40905 claim. EI-213143 terminal evidence is stale against current HEAD and is not current gate evidence.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-035 — Rev54 roster reconciliation: preserve target 31 after claimless excess cleanup\nDate: 2026-08-24\nAt the live reconciliation on 2026-08-24, fleet:status showed memberCount=32 against the persisted target 31. The exact full roster plus fleet:assignments identified su-c287b6a3-fec4-4d18-926f-e607fd8b97f5 as parked under owner-directed stand-down with zero claims, zero queued work, and load 0. fleet:kill removed only that identity; the subsequent fleet:status verified memberCount=31, leader live, and fleet:assignments verified 24 claims with zero orphaned/reclaimable claims and zero coverage collisions. Decision: preserve target 31 and do not refill or kill another member unless a new live delta changes the count. su-9fc2181d remains a parked owner-standdown member with a durable wake queued but pickup unconfirmed; its presence is fresh, so preserve it at the target and recheck on a later wake.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-036 — Use dedicated fleet:status for seat-target deltas\nDate: 2026-08-24\nP-001 ruling: for this fleet's persisted seat target and any refill/self-end decision, use the dedicated fleet:status memberCount and leader liveness as the authoritative live roster. The current fleet:status read reports memberCount=31 with the leader live; the fleet target is therefore satisfied and no seat mutation is justified. fleet:leader-brief currently reports members=32 in its broader monitoring population, so that count is not sufficient evidence of a seat delta. Preserve all claimed workers and do not kill/refill based on the broader count alone. Reconcile again on a later wake if the dedicated status changes.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-037 — Reconcile the concurrent seat transitions before restoring one deficit\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24. D-036's prior satisfied-target read no longer describes the live state. The verified excess su-bef4bb62-34ae-4dd7-9139-9ae003d5fabd was claimless/load-zero and was ended through fleet:kill after its self-end wake queued with no pickup. The next dedicated fleet:status read reports memberCount=30 against target 31 because su-841b09c4-42f2-42dc-a411-436c8da33f40 concurrently transitioned parked→recorded; it has no claim/doing item. Full roster remains 66 rows; no claimed worker is orphaned or was taken over. Capacity preflight is healthy (codex dispatchBudget 20, poolExhausted false), but fleet:launch-on-plan existing-fleet top-up was refused at exact-plan admission: executableWidth=0, P-004 blocked, the only matched row excluded by claim floors. Treat this as one confirmed deficit, preserve all claims and D-025 validation-only walls, and restore exactly one seat only through a supported existing-fleet/capability launch route that does not claim protected work or alter the rev47 claim spec.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-038 — D-038 — Treat the paused fleet count as unresolved, not a roster-mutation trigger\nDate: 2026-08-24\nFresh live evidence at 2026-08-24 10:11 EDT: fleet:status reports memberCount=30, while fleet:leader-brief reports 68 roster records including 36 dead/historical rows and fleet:assignments reports 68 candidates with 35 alive and zero orphaned/reclaimable claims. These surfaces answer different population questions; the discrepancy does not authorize terminating or launching a member. The fleet is owner-directed winding-down and paused. WI-40086/WI-41117 are assigned to live su-4917b0b2 in workspace presence but that identity is not currently in this fleet; preserve that holder and do not take over. Recheck fleet:status, fleet:assignments, workspace presence, protected work-items, and the exact generation-2 event only after the owner lifts the pause.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-039 — Owner-verified system-wide resume supersedes the prior pause\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24. The owner-verified system-wide resume (coord message mt74imd2-0000-8af4f67838f54352a8953013010dd056) supersedes the earlier workspace-wide pause. Fleet leaders must reconcile live control before pulling; this fleet's live control is active and leader su-688f8865-067e-4d47-99ea-7ae07c9253c6 is healthy. Preserve the existing validation-only/protected-item walls. Current rev47 claimability is zero: 222 matched rows are excluded by overlapping floors (taken, claimHold, agentReview, observationLane, externalBlocker, planLaneReserved, crossMachineRig, blockedDep); do not hand-pick or widen the spec. Re-read scheduler:get_next after a claimable event or a verified floor change.\n\n### D-040 — Rev47 admission semantics: claimableCount governs; breakdownOnly returned is not post-affinity\nDate: 2026-08-24\nFor fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820 under fleet-owned spec revision 47, `work_items:claimable` is the authoritative read for admission: use its `claimableCount` together with `spec.revision` and the affinity warning. When `breakdownOnly:true`, `returned=0` only means the row list was skipped; it does not mean post-affinity filtering returned zero. `fleet:leader-brief.summary.claimable_now` is secondary telemetry and may diverge; it cannot authorize wake, roster, or claim mutations. In the live reconciliation, exact samples moved while the brief also moved (e.g. 6/233 vs 11, then peer snapshot 7/233 vs 13), so report snapshots with their read time and re-read before acting. Preserve the 1/1 WI-39943 cap and validation-only walls; no roster/spec/wake/claim mutation follows from a conflicting count alone.\n\n### D-041 — Exact rev47 oracle must use explicit tools:invoke dispatch\nDate: 2026-08-24\nFor monitor reads under fleet claim-spec revision 47, use tools:invoke with name work_items:claimable and explicit args {harness:'papercusp', kind:'bug', spec:'nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820', breakdownOnly:false, sampleExcluded:10}. That exact call returned claimableCount=12, matchedByFilter=234, affinity 4/12 below floor, matching fleet:leader-brief's 12/234. A direct client wrapper with apparently equivalent args returned 11/234; that result is retracted because wrapper parity with the fleet-spec path is unproven. Until parity is demonstrated, the direct-wrapper result must not drive claims, wakes, roster changes, or other mutation. Cause of the dispatch-path discrepancy remains undetermined. No mutation is authorized by this decision.\n\n### D-042 — Keep protected generation-3 lane frozen after replacement timeout\nDate: 2026-08-24\nAt 2026-08-24T18:02Z, the protected-lane owner reported replacement checkpoint candidate 83805ce3da009b40e848a009ab4b9194854f229f terminating with exit 1 after dependency-generation.sh --integration timed out at 1800000ms; no normal verdict was produced (green:null/not-green). The standing validation-only and fleet-control walls remain authoritative: do not take over the protected WI-40086 lane, rerun or emit generation 3, mutate source/serializer, checkpoint/deploy, claim WI-40905, wake idle members, or mutate roster/claims. Keep generation 3 declared/pending/unfired until an authorized owner changes the wall or ownership.\n\n### D-043 — Keep rev47 bug-only fleet scope closed to task admissions\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThe current admission refusal is intentional placement, not lane starvation. WI-41632 is kind=task, while fleet-launch-nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820-kinds revision 47 admits kind=bug only; the requested member su-5918 is live, claimless, and monitoring. The exact fleet-scoped work_items:claimable oracle still reports 162–163 admitted bugs with healthy pool capacity, so do not bump or widen rev47 and do not force-claim this task. Route WI-41632 to a task-capable lane/owner. Treat fleet:leader-brief summary.admission_blocked as requiring refusal-row inspection, not automatic spec revision, because the completed EI-21276891073572679 incident documents that this summary can reflect historical admission events.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-044 — Carry full rev47 fleet/spec identity, never revision-only shorthand\nDate: 2026-08-26\nFor this plan's rev47 claimability reads and cold-loop carry notes, name the exact fleet slug `nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820` or exact specId `fleet-launch-nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820-kinds`; `rev47` alone is ambiguous across active fleet/spec namespaces. `work_items:claimable` correctly rejects an unqualified revision with candidates rather than widening to the whole backlog. This removes the avoidable discovery round-trip while preserving the safe fail-closed behavior.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"observation-and-recall-surface-honesty-2026-08-16","title":"Observation lane + corpus recall: make the surfaces say what they are","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Observation lane + corpus recall: make the surfaces say what they are\nslug: observation-and-recall-surface-honesty-2026-08-16\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-16\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nPhases 1-3 CODE COMPLETE and VERIFIED — P-001..P-005 all done. P-005 installed the coord-fold census: every fold stamps `tool_invocations.metadata_json->'coordFold'` via `ctx.metadata` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/activity/coord-fold-census.ts + hook-bundle.ts wiring). Deliberately the SAME channel as coord/derived-signal-census.ts: no new table, no migration, no new write path — the fold's enclosing activity:report call already writes that row with coord_owner_id + invoked_at + duration_ms indexed, so the instrument adds ZERO queries and ZERO latency to the very hot path under investigation. Record: {v, changed, reason, complete, foldMs, gateMs, hydrateMs, reqGen, gen, inboxAdvanced, inboxTotal}. QUIET folds are censused too — the ratio is uncomputable from expensive folds alone. `reason` splits `no-client-generation` (a legitimately expensive first call) from `generation-mismatch` (the actual defect population), which would otherwise inflate exactly the number P-006 turns on. VERIFIED LIVE, not merely unit-tested (the derived-signal census shipped tested-and-silent for 12 days — that is why): :3170 rebuilt from this tree, real folds driven through it, all 4 branches observed as real rows. P-003/P-004 verification closed out 2026-08-16T17:20Z: corpus-recall+io 93/93, sources.integration 42/42, lint:tsc operator-core clean, and lint:tsc:workspaces 72 passed / 0 failed with `libs/generic/search` confirmed present in the run (not a zero-file green).\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: P-006/P-007/P-008 remain BLOCKED and must not be started — per D-001 they need the fleet RATIO, which cannot exist until this change reaches :3070 (where every agent's PostToolUse hook points; :3170 sees no peer traffic, so the ratio is NOT measurable around the deploy). ⚠ THE DEPLOY IS FROZEN, and the cause is now identified: NOT the GitHub push 403 — that is an HTTPS-vs-SSH identity defect needing no owner (workspace fact `push-403-is-https-identity-not-owner-wall`; an owner-ask asking for an email verification was withdrawn as misdirected). The single real blocker is the local incident-guard `.git/hooks/pre-push`, present in the superproject and 38/38 submodules, whose removal is owner-gated and tracked by another agent on WI-39450. So the next action is NOT to wait on git-sync or to re-probe the 403: it is to watch WI-39450 for the guard ruling, then let the deploy flow and run the census read query documented at the top of coord-fold-census.ts over a settled window (>=1h of real fleet traffic). Do NOT read the P-005 probe's own timings as fleet numbers — synthetic owner, trivial inbox.)\n\n## Background\n\nFour filings, all measured this session (su-69ba26b2):\n\n- **EI-20587312505064997** — observation recurrence detection is inert for agent filings. `dedupSignature(title)` (digest.ts:264) is a sorted bag of distinct >2-char title words. Measured over 37,051 observation titles: 35,520 distinct signatures, **35,277 singletons (99.3%)**, only **48** signatures reach `RECURRENCE_ESCALATION_THRESHOLD = 3`. Of the 1,378 rows in recurring clusters, **1,213 (88%) are scorecards** — which observation-lane-scorecard-classification-2026-08-16 is removing from the lane, so the recurring population is about to drop to ~160 rows.\n- **EI-20584804567938427** — corpus recall serves observation-lane rows into every agent turn labelled `[work-item …]`. `CORPUS_GATE_SOURCES` includes `work_item`; that source queries `engineer_issues` with **no lane predicate**. `corpusHitKindRank()` then *promotes* the tier, justified in-comment as \"the durable, curated artifact this leg exists to surface\". Measured: **56.7%** of that source (37,028 of 65,324) is the observation lane. 3 of 6 excerpts injected into one real session were observation rows, 2 of them `state=open`.\n- **EI-20582609088583997** — the activity:report coord fold's generation is `MAX(coord_event_log.id)` **workspace-global**, so any agent's event invalidates every other agent's cursor. Measured 8.5 coord events/min, mean gap 7.03s, against 2,361 folding calls/hr.\n- **EI-20582634380032313** — that fold averages **2,985ms server-side against its own 4,000ms client wall**, so a large share of hydrations are computed and discarded, and the cursor never advances — which guarantees the next call repeats the work.\n\n## Phase 1 — observation lane (low risk, pure guidance)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Observation title guidance: title is an IDENTIFIER, not a sentence — lead with the stable subject (tool name, surface, file, error class); narrative goes in the body. Update the `improvements:capture` observation field guidance + the turn-end reflection path (checkpoint-harvest.ts). Guard with a test asserting the guidance text names the identifier rule. — note: ← WI-39407 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Surface `conditionKey` in the observation guidance path — it already exists and is the DESIGNED recurrence mechanism (updates in place, bumps repeatCount) but is barely mentioned, so agent filings almost never use it. blocked-by: P-001 — note: shared rule constants in observation-title-guidance.ts; wired into capture{title,observation,conditionKey}, loop:checkpoint{insight}, complete{completion}, checkpoint-harvest doc, both su playbooks; guard test 21/21\n\n## Phase 2 — corpus recall honesty (real code, moderate risk)\n\n- **P-003** `done` Label observation-lane hits honestly in corpus-recall render: `[observation …]` vs `[work-item …]`, so a sample cannot read as a filed, triaged item. blocked-by: P-001 — note: verified: corpus-recall+io 93/93, sources.integration 42/42, lint:tsc operator-core clean, lint:tsc:workspaces 72/72 (libs/generic/search ✓ confirmed present, not a zero-file green)\n- **P-004** `done` Restrict the `corpusHitKindRank()` boost to curated lanes — the \"durable, curated\" premise is false for 56.7% of the source it ranks. blocked-by: P-003 — note: verified: corpus-recall+io 93/93, sources.integration 42/42, lint:tsc operator-core clean, lint:tsc:workspaces 72/72 (libs/generic/search ✓ confirmed present, not a zero-file green)\n\n## Phase 3 — coord fold (HIGHEST RISK: synchronous hook path, every agent, every tool call)\n\n- **P-005** `done` Instrument before changing: record the fold's `changed` ratio, which today is unobservable — the optimization's own effectiveness cannot be measured. This is the prerequisite for any gate change. importance: high — note: ← WI-39416 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `todo` Decide + implement the generation-gate fix (per-owner scoping vs global pre-filter + per-owner second gate) using P-005's numbers. blocked-by: P-005\n- **P-007** `todo` Decide + implement the timeout/discard fix (async fold vs cheaper hydration vs aligned wall). blocked-by: P-005\n\n## Phase 4 — verification\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Verify: targeted suites + `lint:tsc` on touched files; live check that new observation filings produce colliding signatures and that recall labels observations correctly. blocked-by: P-002, P-004, P-006, P-007\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Phase 3 is instrumented before it is changed, not after\n\nThe coord fold runs synchronously in a hook on every tool call for every agent in the fleet. Both filings for it were deliberately recorded as `kind:change` rather than `kind:bug` specifically so they would NOT be auto-implement-eligible. A wrong \"optimization\" there does not fail loudly — it silently drops coordination delivery. P-005 therefore gates P-006 and P-007: no gate change ships on an inferred ratio when the ratio can be measured directly.\n\n### D-002 The fix is never \"file fewer observations\"\n\nUnfiltered volume is the denominator that makes recurrence detection meaningful — ~91.5% of read observations are correctly unremarkable, and that is the design, not waste. No change in this plan may add a write-time quality filter, because no single agent can tell whether its friction is idiosyncratic or fleet-wide; only the count knows. P-001 changes the SHAPE of the title (identifier vs sentence) while leaving volume and the free-prose body untouched.\n\n### D-003 Observations stay in recall; only the label and the rank change\n\nP-003/P-004 deliberately do not exclude observation rows from the corpus. A relevant past observation is often genuinely useful context. The defect is exclusively that a sample is presented as a curated conclusion and given a rank boost earned by a premise that does not hold for it.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/observation-and-recall-surface-honesty-2026-08-16 (\"Observation lane + corpus recall: make the surfaces say what they are\"): no plan update since 2026-08-16 (55 days idle), 5/8 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-bg-host-freeze-eventloop-stall-2026-06-30","title":"Acceptance — bg-host survives its own load instead of freezing and restart-looping","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-17","owner":"su-2e933d99-2e87-4504-b8de-95fa02b4f6cf","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — bg-host survives its own load instead of freezing and restart-looping\nslug: acceptance-bg-host-freeze-eventloop-stall-2026-06-30\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-2e933d99-2e87-4504-b8de-95fa02b4f6cf\n---\n\n# Acceptance — bg-host survives its own load instead of freezing and restart-looping\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for bg-host-freeze-eventloop-stall-2026-06-30, authored post-implementation (D-007) for the resource-efficiency-closeout-2026-08-13 P-006 header reconciliation, which closeout D-001 scopes to \"fresh-live verifies and reconciles their headers\".\n\nThe incident this plan answers: bg-host RSS grew ~+1GB/min (3.3GB@7min → 46.7GB), the resulting GC saturated the main event loop, routinesTick and git-sync froze, and the watchdog restart-looped roughly every 11 minutes — during which a git-sync fire could be reaped and requeued forever without ever committing, silently stranding code for hours.\n\nThese criteria grade OUTCOMES of that failure chain, not the diff. A grader should be able to fail any of them from live host evidence alone without reading the patch. Code-truth audit for the plan is on record (auditSeq 1, sha 8be6a725, 15 citations resolved).\n\n⚠ GRADER MUST NOT BE THE RUBRIC AUTHOR. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"blender-goal-rail-first-live-goal-2026-08-17","title":"Blender goal rail — carry the shipped rail to a first live auto-created goal","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-17","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Blender goal rail — carry the shipped rail to a first live auto-created goal\nslug: blender-goal-rail-first-live-goal-2026-08-17\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-08-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nThe dispatch objective remains met: the first live Goal Rail goal `the-blender-s-goal-rail-has-never-produced-a-sin-180320` was created and later killed by Avi's close-on-success ruling; its former agent is absent and intake follow-up EI-20721521277342336 is terminal. P-006 acceptance is still not green: independent scorecard EI-21028840279165272 rejected the prior runtime state. The retired Scout :3350 probe repair remains verified (142/142 focused tests plus scoped type gates). The DBOS import/export floor repair is complete: WI-40161/P-003 and WI-40162/P-004 are terminal, commit b278a9c07 is contained in local staging, and a sanctioned git-sync advanced local staging to a916cfe712; remote egress remains pending but D-002 confirms push is not the bg-host activation precondition. The shared release gate is currently red on lint:tsc:scripts and lint:identity-leak, with live owner su-271f actively closing WI-40086; no duplicate gate work is authorized while that progress remains live.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Preserve the existing green/red/release awaits and monitor the live gate owner. When the gate settles, restart bg-host from current local staging, verify DBOS boot plus fresh ticker/current-code writers, then execute one production bp-singleton-scout-0 cycle and re-read routine ordering. Route a fresh independent non-author scorecard only after those facts are current; mark P-006 and ship through normal lint/acceptance gates only on a complete pass.)\n\n## Background\n\nThe predecessor's own completion evidence on WI-39484 named the residue honestly: `autoStartGoal`'s live path is verified only through its shared `goals:start` primitives, and the routed-ledger goal leg joins only once a terminal auto-created goal exists. Both are unprovable until the rail actually runs. Measured 2026-08-17T08:00Z:\n\n- `scout_routed_ideas` has **no `rail='goal'` row, ever** (positive control: improvement 283, gym 166, plan 15, instance 2 over 10 days — the instrument works).\n- Newest row in `goals` is 2026-08-16T00:53Z, ~23h BEFORE the rail shipped. No auto-created goal exists.\n- `positions`: committedLocal yes, onStaging no, inMain no, deployed no. `main` is behind staging; the gate is on an 8-red streak, last green ~29.5h ago.\n- 16 routines in the `self-improvement` group are `active:false`, paused 2026-08-16T18:57Z (\"owner-directed Learning-tab pause (snapshot seed, WI-39501)\"). The Blender is switched off.\n\nSequencing premise (D-002): the gate candidate is cut from LOCAL staging, so PUSH is not a gate precondition — `changeInCandidate.judgingContainsPath: true` confirms the in-flight run is already judging code containing `goal-auto-start.ts`. The blocker is the red gate, not the unpushed commit.\n\n## Phase 1 — get the rail live\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Track the green-checkpoint gate to green. Owned by su-d829205e (WI-39450, live, checkpoint run in flight). Each wake: verify the holder is alive AND the run is progressing; a stalled/dead holder makes greening it MY job (a red gate is everyone's). Re-read via `dev:pipeline_position` / `state:read { cell:'gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict' }` — never a transcribed value. — note: ← WI-39666 completed (dropped)\n- **P-002** `done` Verify the deploy actually lands and serves the rail: `main` fast-forwards, `:3070` serves a sha containing `packages/operator-core/lib/goals/goal-auto-start.ts`, and `serving.startedSinceCodeChange` is true. Expedite with `release:deploy { op:'trigger' }` if green-but-stalled. ALSO settle which process executes `bp-singleton-scout-0` (DBOS `routinesTick` host) — if it is not the deployed operator, the deploy may not be what gates P-003. blocked-by: P-001 — note: Superseded-then-met per D-005/D-006: activation was the bg-host restart, not the :3070 deploy. First live goal dispatched + verified 17:30:45Z (goal ...-180320, agent su-7c9a1f3d live).\n\n## Phase 2 — turn the Blender back on\n\n- **P-003** `done` Resume the `self-improvement` routine group (16 routines incl. `bp-singleton-scout-0`) via `routines:group-set`, per D-001 — AFTER the deploy lands, so the first cycle exercises the NEW code rather than rerouting goal-scale ideas to the plan rail. Record the resume on this plan. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-40124 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — prove it end to end\n\n- **P-004** `done` Prove the FIRST live goal-rail dispatch: a goal-scale idea routes with `rail='goal'`, `goals:create` + `goals:start` mint a real goal carrying a drafted `killCriterion` AND `budgetCents` (malformed must not start), and a headless GOAL-mode agent spawns. Capture the goal id, the routed ref, and the spawned agent's ownerId as evidence. Cap is 1 goal/cycle. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-40125 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Close the learning loop: when the auto-created goal reaches a terminal status, verify the outcome classifier writes achieved-to-won / killed-to-lost back onto the routed idea, and that the routed-ledger goal leg renders its `Status: achieved|killed` entry. This is the D-003-discipline requirement the gym rail failed. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-40129 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `dropped` Acceptance rubric (`rubrics:propose`, kind `acceptance`, classRef `plan-class-feature-ship`) + a NON-AUTHOR grade via `scorecards:emit` before this plan may be marked shipped. — note: ← WI-40135 dropped\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Blender resume is deferred until the deploy lands\n\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-17, interactive] Owner chose \"Resume after the deploy lands\" from an explicit four-option ask. Rationale carried from the ask: the rail code is not deployed, so resuming the group now would run the OLD code and merely reroute goal-scale ideas to the plan rail (never dropped, but proves nothing). Resuming after the deploy makes the very first cycle a genuine test. The pause itself (2026-08-16T18:57Z) was seeded for the WI-39501 Learning-tab snapshot, which shipped 21:37Z, so the pause is now residue rather than an active owner intent. Execution: P-003.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-002 Push is not a precondition — the red gate is the only real blocker\n\nDate: 2026-08-17\n`dev:pipeline_position` reports `blockedOn: pushed` with `nextAction: git-sync:run`, which reads as \"the commit has not reached origin\". That is TRUE but NOT load-bearing here: the green-checkpoint candidate is cut from LOCAL `staging` (`revParse(integrationRoot, 'staging')`, no fetch anywhere in green-checkpoint.ts), and `changeInCandidate.judgingContainsPath: true` confirms the in-flight run is already judging the rail code. The git-sync push failures visible in the routine ledger are on `libs/generic/cache|card-stack|chat-protocol` — separate submodule repos held by a deliberate incident guard from the 2026-08-15 tree destruction — NOT the papercusp superproject. Do not chase the push leg as if it blocked this work.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-003 Do not duplicate the gate fix\n\nDate: 2026-08-17\nThe `gate-red-streak:papercusp` claim is HELD by su-d829205e (WI-39450) whose session is live and whose stated intent is \"awaiting in-flight checkpoint run (pid 3749262)\". The playbook's \"a red gate is everyone's job\" licenses taking a red NOBODY live is working — it explicitly requires checking presence first and helping rather than colliding when someone alive is on it. This plan therefore TRACKS the gate as a dependency and escalates/takes over only on holder death or a verified stall.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-004 — The gate red was ONE stale test assertion, already fixed at 07:56Z — the gate is waiting on a fresh verdict, not on a fix\nDate: 2026-08-17\nInvestigated 2026-08-17 08:05-08:40Z. Correcting two wrong inferences of my own on the way (both recorded here so neither propagates):\n\nWHAT IS TRUE. The 9-red streak reduces to ONE file: packages/operator-core/lib/win-leg-default-roles.test.ts. The run log (~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs/2026-08-17T07-38-44-053Z-base-4824a92bf8fc-cand-9d19fdc6b982.log) carries the run's OWN re-triage: classification=real-red tip=863e5a945cd7 autoRefire=false, \"Re-ran each file ALONE at tip: 1 of 3 STILL FAIL. STILL FAILING: lib/win-leg-default-roles.test.ts. ALREADY GREEN AT TIP — do NOT re-diagnose (2): live-federation-gate-red-backoff.test.ts, desktop-selftests-registry-complete.test.ts.\"\n\nTHAT FIX ALREADY LANDED. Commit f6a15c5a97, 2026-08-17T07:56:28Z, authored by su-d829205e themselves (Papercusp-Work-Item includes WI-39450). The gate run began 07:38Z and re-triaged against tip 863e5a94 (07:36Z) — BOTH predate the fix by ~20 min. I re-ran the file at the current tree: 7 passed, 0 failed. The fix STRENGTHENS the test: the old assertion pinned the bare-zip ARTIFACTS form, which is how 0.0.16/0.0.17 shipped Windows Server UNSIGNED (EI-20595279927716716); the new one pins the OUTPUTS array, adds a not.toMatch so the regression is asserted ABSENT, and adds a case covering the updater signature. The test was red against CORRECT code.\n\nSO THE GATE NEEDS A FRESH VERDICT, NOT A FIX — exactly the trap the repo guide names (\"fixing the code is not the same as greening the gate\"). I tried release:checkpoint-run and the rail refused with condition_claimed: WI-39450 is held by su-d829205e, session live. I did NOT force. Its last_said shows su-2e933d99 independently reached the same conclusion at ~08:28Z, also tried to fire, also was refused, and also handed the holder the evidence. Three agents converging on one gate adds nothing, so this plan STANDS DOWN from the gate per D-003 and waits on a push signal (state:subscribe on deploy.3070.sha != 4824a92bf8fc) rather than polling.\n\nRETRACTED — TWO INFERENCES OF MINE THAT WERE WRONG:\n(1) I read gate_health.failingTests == [] and inferred \"9 reds with zero failing tests means runs are being KILLED rather than failing.\" WRONG: the run log names three failing files. failingTests is simply not populated on that row — an instrument gap, not evidence of absence.\n(2) I then hypothesised host memory pressure as the killer. NOT SUPPORTED: dmesg shows exactly one OOM kill in 12h, a blender-goal-steward agent at 5.4GB on Aug 16, unrelated to any checkpoint run. Dropped before acting on it.\nWHAT SURVIVES both retractions: pid 3749262 genuinely no longer exists and checkpointRunInFlight still reports it active with elapsedSec climbing — that telemetry IS stale, which is why the holder was parked on a dead pid. Also unexplained and worth a separate look: the 08:15Z fire recorded a red 5 seconds after firing with observedCandidate null, which no ~55min suite can do.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-005 — CORRECTION: the goal rail activates on a bg-host RESTART, not the :3070 deploy — D-001's decision stands, its stated mechanism was wrong\nDate: 2026-08-17\nMeasured 2026-08-17 08:45-08:55Z. This corrects the mechanism in D-001/P-002/P-003. The owner's DECISION (do not resume the Blender until the new code is actually live) is UNCHANGED and still honoured; the EVENT I told them to wait for was the wrong one, and waiting for it would have produced exactly the failure D-001 exists to prevent.\n\nWHY. The Blender/scout cycle is routine bp-singleton-scout-0, tier='durable', fired by DBOS routinesTick. routinesTick is hosted by papercup-bg-host.service ('Papercusp dedicated background host — DBOS routines/git-sync/substrate primary'), NOT by papercup-dev-api.service (:3070). Confirmed independently: the git-sync watchdog messages in my inbox are emitted by pid 134091 with cwd /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp/apps/operator, and that pid's start time matches bg-host's ExecMainStartTimestamp exactly.\n\nTHE TREES DIFFER, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT.\n- papercup-dev-api (:3070) WorkingDirectory = papercupai-workspace/papercup-release/apps/operator (the GREEN release checkout, main). goal-auto-start.ts is ABSENT there.\n- papercup-bg-host WorkingDirectory = papercupai-workspace/papercusp/apps/operator (the STAGING tree). goal-auto-start.ts is PRESENT there.\nSo the rail's code already sits in the tree the Blender runs from. The :3070 deploy is irrelevant to whether the Blender can create goals; it matters only for the operator UI/MCP surface.\n\nBUT IT IS NOT LOADED. bg-host runs `npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts` — SOURCE, not a build — and the Hono host has NO file-watch (repo guide: server-side edits get no hot-reload). Module load happened once, at boot. Timeline:\n  bg-host booted            2026-08-16T21:33:45Z\n  goal-auto-start.ts added  2026-08-16T22:19:31Z (262b1de68f)  <- 46 min AFTER boot\n  cycle-deps.ts wiring      2026-08-16T23:08:05Z (1ada597d7c)\n  rail final form           2026-08-16T23:40:02Z (bcd75fc144)\nThe running bg-host process therefore has NO goal rail loaded, however green the gate gets and however many times :3070 deploys.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING. Corrected order is: (1) restart bg-host (dev:restart — the sanctioned lever; tsx means no rebuild needed), (2) THEN resume the self-improvement group per D-001, (3) then the first cycle genuinely exercises the rail. Restarting bg-host while the group is still PAUSED is safe and is preparation, not activation — nothing cycles until P-003 resumes it.\n\nTIMING CAUTION. bg-host is shared infrastructure (git-sync, routines, substrate) for the whole fleet, and su-d829205e has a green-checkpoint run in flight since 08:30Z (separate systemd unit, so a bg-host restart should not touch it — but a restart does bounce git-sync, which mutates the tree the gate is judging). Prefer restarting AFTER that run lands its verdict; nothing is lost by waiting, because the routines are paused regardless.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-006 — The rail is live but its INTAKE is starved — \"watch for the first organic goal route\" is not a viable finish condition\nDate: 2026-08-17\nSupersedes the plan's prior `## Now` step \"watch the first cycle for the first rail='goal' dispatch\". That watch cannot succeed on its own; measured this turn.\n\nACTIVATION SUCCEEDED. bg-host was restarted (MainPID 3831274 → 1796459) with `goal-auto-start.ts` loaded, and `@singleton/bp-singleton-scout-0` was resumed. A full cycle then ran — `scout-1786986123795`, routed 2026-08-17T17:06:59Z. It produced 3 routes, ALL `gym`, zero `goal`. So the rail is loaded and the Blender is cycling; the absence of a goal is upstream of dispatch, not a deploy or activation failure.\n\nTHE FLAG IS NOT THE CAUSE (ruled out, do not re-diagnose). No `goal`/`blender` row exists in `harness_shared.operator_flag_overrides` for `papercusp-workspace`; `BLENDER_GOAL_RAIL` is absent from `KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS`, so it runs its code default ON; and `cycle-deps.ts:840` fails OPEN to `true` regardless. `goalEnabled === true`.\n\nTHE MECHANISM. `rail='goal'` has exactly two code paths:\n1. DIRECT — `classifyProposal` returns `p.routeHint` verbatim (`router.ts:145`).\n2. OVERRIDE — `makeGoalScaleOverride` (`router.ts:462`): `routeHint === 'plan' && isGoalScaleProposal(p)`, a 20-marker text match over framing/mechanism/bet/whyNew.\n\nPath 1 is UNREACHABLE in production. `recombine.ts:197-199` narrows the parsed hint to `plan|gym|improvement`, silently coercing `'goal'` (and `'instance'`) to `undefined` → `DEFAULT_ROUTING_RAIL='improvement'`. `recombine.ts` is the sole `routeHint` producer in the live path (whole-tree non-test grep; the only other site, `neologism/miner-core.ts:589`, hardcodes `'improvement'`). Consequently `router.ts:445`'s `routeHint === 'goal'` branch is dead code in production while `router.test.ts:288-297` unit-tests it as live. Filed as EI-20721521277342336.\n\nPath 2 has an EMPTY INPUT DOMAIN. Scoped counts (`workspace_id='papercusp-workspace'`): improvement 992, gym 624, plan 21, instance 5, goal 0. The last `plan`-hinted route was 2026-08-15 02:45Z; `goal-auto-start.ts` landed 2026-08-16 22:19Z. Since the rail has existed, ZERO plan-hinted proposals have been produced — the override has never had one candidate to bump. Plan-hinted routes are ~1.3% of all routes historically, and none of the 21 ever matched a goal-scale marker (a match would have persisted as `goal`, not `plan`).\n\nWHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PLAN. P-004 as written (\"watch `scout_routed_ideas` for the first `rail='goal'` row\") is an unbounded wait on a ~0-probability event, not a verification step. The plan cannot reach \"first live goal\" without a deliberate change to either the intake (paths 1/2) or the proof strategy. Options are being put to the owner rather than chosen unilaterally: (A) admit `'goal'`/`'instance'` at `recombine.ts:199`; (B) widen the override's hint domain beyond `'plan'`; (C) prove the dispatch half end-to-end with a seeded proposal, changing no organic routing; (D) leave armed and wait. Note `blender:run-drill` offers only `rubric-seeding`|`capacity-storm` — there is no goal-rail drill mode, so it is not a turnkey proof vehicle.\n\nA goal dispatch is not free: `DEFAULT_GOAL_BUDGET_CENTS = 20000` ($200) and `DEFAULT_MAX_GOALS_PER_CYCLE = 1`, and a routed goal creates a real goal record with an agent behind it. That spend + autonomy is why the intake choice is an owner decision, not an implementation detail.\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-007 — GOAL-agent arbitration: the cheap experiment CONFIRMED (kill criterion not tripped) — but the rail has still never produced an ORGANIC goal, and intake stays owner-gated\nDate: 2026-08-17\nRecorded by the GOAL-mode agent owning goal `the-blender-s-goal-rail-has-never-produced-a-sin-180320`\n(su-7c9a1f3d), 2026-08-17T17:50Z. Supersedes nothing; extends D-006.\n\n#### 1. KILL-CRITERION VERDICT: NOT TRIPPED. The goal continues.\n\nThe criterion: \"kill if the seeded proposal does NOT reach rail='goal', or reaches it but\nthe dispatch fails.\"\n\nMeasured, from the writers rather than from a summary:\n- `.vitest-tmp/goal-rail-seed/probe-routing.ts` builds proposal `seed-goal-rail-proof-001`\n  with `routeHint:'plan'` + goal-scale wording and calls the REAL router functions\n  (`decideRoutes` + `makeGoalScaleOverride` + `draftGoalRails`) — verdict ROUTES-TO-GOAL.\n- `dispatch-goal.ts` then wired the real goalDispatch port. `routedProposalId` is written\n  by EXACTLY ONE site, `goal-auto-start.ts:117` (whole-tree grep), and this goal record\n  carries `routedProposalId: seed-goal-rail-proof-001`.\n\nSo BOTH halves held: the override path (path 2) reaches rail='goal', and dispatch created\na real goal record and launched an agent. The hypothesis was CONFIRMED, not falsified:\nthe root cause is INTAKE, not dispatch. D-006's diagnosis stands unamended.\n\n#### 2. CORRECTION, so it cannot propagate: this is NOT \"the first organic goal\".\n\nIt would be easy — and wrong — to read the existence of this goal as the rail having\nproduced one. It has not.\n\n`harness_shared.scout_routed_ideas` for `papercusp-workspace`, measured 17:45Z:\nimprovement 993, gym 626, plan 21, instance 5 — and **rail='goal': ZERO rows**. The\nimprovement/gym rows carry `routed_at` of 17:34Z, i.e. AFTER this goal was created at\n17:30Z, so the ledger is live and writing; the absence is real, not a stale read.\n(Positive control run deliberately: an empty result for 'goal' alone would have been\nindistinguishable from a broken query.)\n\nWhat was proven is the MECHANISM works when handed a suitable proposal. What remains\nunproven — and is the actual goal — is that an ORGANIC Blender cycle ever produces such a\nproposal. D-006 already measured why it does not: plan-hinted routes are ~1.3% of all\nroutes, none of the 21 ever matched a goal-scale marker, and zero have occurred since the\nrail shipped.\n\n#### 3. STANDING CONSTRAINT (binding on every agent in this goal's fleets)\n\nRouting behaviour in `recombine.ts` / `router.ts` MUST NOT be changed by any agent working\nthis goal until the owner rules. Admitting 'goal'/'instance' at `recombine.ts:199`\n(option A) and widening the override's hint domain (option B) both change which rail\norganic proposals take, and D-006 reserved that to the owner because a routed goal spends\nreal money (`DEFAULT_GOAL_BUDGET_CENTS=20000`) and launches an autonomous agent.\n\nThis is recorded as a decision rather than left in a coord message on purpose: the coord\ndelivery of this constraint was truncated at 600 of 1363 chars, so the message is not a\nreliable carrier. The decision is.\n\nWork placed into the goal lane so far is deliberately routing-NEUTRAL and safe under\nEITHER ruling: WI-39721 (make the silent coercion observable), WI-39724 (drift guard with\nan explicit deliberately-unaccepted allowlist that passes today), WI-39725 (test-integrity:\nrouter.test.ts asserts a branch unreachable in production).\n\n#### 4. Why the drain fleet stalled (resolved)\n\nMember su-fcce2f84 reported `spec_matches_nothing` and self-corrected that the spec was\nright. Confirmed: the lane was genuinely empty. `EI-20721521277342336` — the diagnosis\nitem, filed before this goal existed — has `goal_id = NULL`, so the goal leaf correctly\nmatched nothing. It is deliberately being LEFT OUT of the claimable lane: its fix IS the\nowner-gated intake change, and stamping it into the lane would invite a member to\npre-empt the owner. It gets stamped once the owner rules.\n\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-008 — TRAP: you cannot measure how often the model emits routeHint='goal' — every persisted surface is post-coercion, so the obvious query returns a misleading 0\nDate: 2026-08-17\nRecorded by su-7c9a1f3d (GOAL agent), 2026-08-17T17:56Z. Extends D-006/D-007.\nWritten because I nearly shipped this error into an owner recommendation and caught it\nonly by checking the writer.\n\n#### The trap\n\nThe natural question before choosing between D-006's options A and B is \"how often does\nthe model actually ask for a goal?\" The natural query is:\n\n    SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE proposals::text ~ '\"(route|routeHint)\":\"goal\"')\n    FROM harness_shared.scout_cycle_stage_artifacts ...\n\nIt returns **0 of 30 cycles** (plan-hint: 20 of 30). That 0 is an ARTIFACT OF\nCONSTRUCTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and reading it as \"the model never wants a goal\" inverts\nthe correct conclusion about option A.\n\n#### Why (the writers)\n\n- `cycle.ts:431` — `const proposals = await deps.recombine(scored, { llmCall: recordingLlm })`.\n  The `proposals` value IS recombine's OUTPUT.\n- `scheduler.ts:871` — persists `proposals: cycle.proposals` into\n  `scout_cycle_stage_artifacts.proposals`.\n- `recombine.ts:197-199` coerces any hint outside `plan|gym|improvement` to `undefined`\n  BEFORE returning.\n\nSo `'goal'` cannot appear in that column under any circumstance. The filter can only ever\nreturn 0, whether the model emits `'goal'` every cycle or never.\n\n- `scout_routed_ideas` is likewise post-routing (rail='goal': 0 rows) — same limitation.\n- `recordingLlm` (`cycle.ts:315-341`) pushes `{ step, system, messages, responseFormat,\n  costUsd }` — the REQUEST and the cost. It does NOT record the response body, so the raw\n  emitted hint is not recoverable from there either.\n\n#### Consequence, and it is load-bearing for the owner's choice\n\n**The demand for the goal rail is currently UNMEASURABLE.** We do not know whether the\nmodel emits `routeHint:'goal'` often, rarely, or never. Therefore:\n\n- Option A's real-world effect is UNKNOWN — not \"large\", and not \"a no-op\". Anyone\n  asserting either without new instrumentation is guessing.\n- `types.ts:407` instructs the model \"GOAL-SCALE idea ... -> 'goal'\" and `types.ts:411`\n  admits it in the union, so the model is at least INVITED to emit it. That raises the\n  prior that A is not a no-op, but it is not evidence that it fires.\n\n#### What this changes\n\nWI-39721 (make the coercion observable) is NOT merely hygiene — it is the INSTRUMENT that\nproduces the one datum the owner's A-vs-B decision needs, and it is routing-neutral and\nfree of spend/autonomy risk. Sequencing it FIRST converts an irreversible autonomy\ndecision into a measured one. This also matches the goal's own stated method: \"Observe\norganic routing over several Blender cycles and adjust rather than force.\"\n\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-009 — 2026-08-20 owner-directed completion supersedes the August 18 Learning-tab pause for P-003\nDate: 2026-08-20\nAvi explicitly directed this session to finish the priority and August Blender plans and authorized visible fleet execution under AUTO. That 2026-08-20 execution directive is newer than the August 18 Learning-tab pause. For this plan, P-003 must therefore resume the `self-improvement` routine group after verifying the bg-host carries the shipped rail code (D-005). Record the prior pause and this supersession in the completion evidence; do not treat the older pause as a standing blocker.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-010 — A detached checkpoint verdict does not evaluate a repaired staging lineage it does not contain\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMeasured on 2026-08-21: observed candidate 7490aaa814f1 is a detached child of ed20de6d and contains none of repair commits 6966b6a3, 9e5d9f65, 2c7a81f, or 65b369ad. Current origin/staging b2bf50541848 contains all four. Therefore 7490's authoritative lint:tsc red is authoritative for 7490 only, not a verdict on repaired staging. Do not diagnose, deploy, or close P-006 from that detached verdict. Preserve the live WI-40195 owner fixing checkpoint candidate divergence; after that fix lands and the shared tree is clean, verify the then-current origin contains all four repairs and launch exactly one checkpoint against that lineage, with a fresh trace/unit census proving no in-flight writer.\nRelated: P-006\n\n## Requirements\n\nThe bg-host runs the shipped goal-rail code before the self-improvement group resumes. A controlled first live goal-scale dispatch creates a real goal carrying a valid kill criterion and budget, starts a headless GOAL-mode agent, and rejects malformed drafts before start. Terminal goal outcome is reflected back to the routed idea and ledger. An acceptance rubric receives a non-author grade before ship.\n\n## Design\n\nReuse the existing self-improvement routine group and goal rail. Because organic intake is starved, inject one controlled goal-scale case and trace the complete route-to-goal-to-agent-to-outcome chain. Treat D-005 as authoritative: bg-host restart, not operator deploy, activates the code. Do not duplicate unrelated green-gate repair work.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"blender-loop-repair-opus5-xhigh-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: Blender loop repair + fleet-wide Opus 5 xhigh","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-17","owner":"su-82a2be51-2976-42f9-b91c-13cd80e0ad77","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: Blender loop repair + fleet-wide Opus 5 xhigh\nslug: blender-loop-repair-opus5-xhigh-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-82a2be51-2976-42f9-b91c-13cd80e0ad77\n---\n\n# Acceptance: Blender loop repair + fleet-wide Opus 5 xhigh\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nA shared standard for a system characteristic — its criteria grade structured observations.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"deterministic-coverage-census-2026-08-17","title":"Deterministic coverage census + gated test-depth ladder","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-17","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Deterministic coverage census + gated test-depth ladder\nslug: deterministic-coverage-census-2026-08-17\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-09-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Phase A is COMPLETE — P-001..P-005 all done. The census now writes AND is read: harness_shared.testing_surfaces holds 1,105 real surfaces (http-route 832, mcp-tool 49, sync-query 224), surfaced through the testing:coverage tool, two state cells, a testing.coverage sync query and the /admin/testing Coverage panel — one derivation (readCoverage), boundedness + fidelity markers on every aggregate, pct null (verdict \"not-measured\") whenever the denominator is 0. coverage_evidence is still 0 rows, so every rung honestly reads a REAL 0%: the attribution layer is armed but no run has proved a surface yet. TWO OPEN CAVEATS, both filed: WI-39812 — the mcp-tool population is loader-dependent (675 defineTool files censused as 49, tooldef's catalog is module-split), so mcp-tool ratios are real numbers about a truncated world, and truncation always flatters. EI-20796266249712348 — system:coverage-census is absent from the RELEASE build, so the routine reports healthy fires while doing nothing there; main is frozen behind the owned 24+-red gate (WI-39450, do-not-fix). D-012 records how census read surfaces get their liveness (producer-side push + documented PUSH_EXEMPT, never a table trigger) and binds Phase D.\n\n**Next:** Phase B: P-006 (rubric integration — coverage instruments under the one-criterion↔one-instrument contract), now unblocked by P-005.\n\n## Background\n\nAgents claim \"ready\" while obvious coverage gaps ship, because completeness is asserted by the same judgment that produced the gap. Fix: compute coverage deterministically as census (surface registries) ⋈ evidence (test_runs + attribution + generated-fuzz verdicts), graded on a depth ladder L0–L4, refused at plan-ship. Full research + tradeoffs: WI-39731 / ~/.papercusp/artifacts/coverage-census-research.html. Core principle: framework-neutral core + stack-keyed SurfaceCensusProvider plugins; agents keep authoring intent tests (L3) but acceptance is a ledger delta, not a claim. Related: production-readiness-test-coverage-2026-05-30 (active) hardens the executing gate on critical paths; this plan supplies the breadth instrument its D-001 deferred.\n\n## Phase A — census core (see the gap)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Migrations: harness_shared.testing_surfaces + coverage_evidence + census_provider_registrations + coverage_waivers tables and the depth-grading view (allocator-reserved numbers, .DRAFT discipline) importance: high — note: ← WI-39770 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` SurfaceCensusProvider contract + census job in @papercusp/testing-shell (enumerate/upsert/retire diffing, fidelity stamps declared>spec>convention>observed>file-only, tier:ephemeral schedule) blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-39778 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Declared providers for the Papercusp stack: hono-routes (routeRegistrationOrder seam), mcp-tools (agent-tools index + zod schema capture), sync-queries (sync-resolver registry) blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-39788 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Attribution: test-mode Hono middleware + MCP dispatch hook + run-id threading (testing:run → env → header) writing coverage_evidence edges blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-39791 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Read surfaces: testing:coverage tool + state cells + /admin/testing coverage panel; boundedness/fidelity markers on every aggregate blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-39808 completed (done)\n\n## Phase B — the gate (done stops being claimable)\n\n- **P-006** `done` Rubric integration: coverage instruments under the one-criterion↔one-instrument contract + first-class check kind 'coverage' { scope, floor } with emit-time refusal naming failing surfaces; plan-touched scope = work-item filesChanged → source_file reverse map importance: high blocked-by: P-005 — note: ← WI-39819 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `todo` Green-checkpoint NEW-surface guard (first_seen > last green pin AND depth < floor → red) + shrink-only expiry-dated waiver registry (KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS governance) blocked-by: P-005\n- **P-016** `todo` Criterion↔behavior binding (the criterion contract): extend check:{kind:'tests'} to CASE-level binding (testNames / @verifies:<rubric>/<criterion> tags); emit-time verification that each bound case exists AND is green AND attributes to the claimed surface (coverage_evidence join via P-004); sampled falsifiability — scoped mutation over the surface's implementing files must kill ≥1 bound test, non-lethal bindings flagged; grader UX inlines bound assertion snippets beside each criterion blocked-by: P-006 importance: high\n- **P-017** `todo` Durable 'verifies' edges: at scorecards:emit, persist each graded criterion↔test binding into coverage_evidence (criterion text + rubric/plan ref + test case + surface) so the binding OUTLIVES the one-shot acceptance rubric's retirement. Consumers: a red names the ratified behavior it breaks (not just a failing file); deleting/gutting the sole proof of a behavior surfaces as 'behavior now unproven' instead of silent loss; a later plan touching the surface can read previously-ratified behaviors blocked-by: P-016 importance: high\n- **P-018** `todo` Ratified-behavior protection: a guard asserting every durable `verifies` edge still has a LIVE proof — test file present, not quarantined, green in the last run. Closes the three ways a suite-resident behavior test silently stops protecting main: workspace-scoped test:affected selection can skip it per-change, quarantine.txt can exclude it, and deletion/gutting is invisible. Surfaces as 'criterion C-NNN of plan X is now unproven' rather than silent loss; feeds the gap queue's ranking blocked-by: P-017 importance: high\n- **P-019** `todo` Amend the meta-acceptance-rubric (the rubric-rubric) with a TEST-BINDING QUALITY criterion grounded in this census — owner-directed 2026-08-17. Today the meta-rubric's `prefer-structured-check` grades only that a criterion CARRIES a check; nothing grades whether the bound test is any GOOD. Add a criterion (non-overlapping with the existing six) asserting: (a) each objectively-checkable criterion's binding DISCRIMINATES — case-level per P-016, not a fat green file that passes for unrelated reasons (D-007 property 1); (b) the surfaces the plan's work newly registered are at/above the depth floor via check:{kind:'coverage'} rather than merely L0-registered; (c) the binding is DURABLE — a `verifies` edge per P-017 with a live proof per P-018, so quarantining or gutting the sole proof of a ratified criterion surfaces instead of silently passing. Re-propose meta-acceptance-rubric with the new criterion, then have the OWNER ratify (it is still status:'proposed', ratifiedBy:null, and by its own description is owner-ratified rather than vetted). blocked-by: P-006, P-016, P-017 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase C — auto-generated floor\n\n- **P-008** `todo` zod→fast-check property harness over the MCP tool registry (one parameterized suite; @traversable/zod-test compat smoke vs zod 4 FIRST; per-tool overrides for refine-heavy schemas; fuzz verdicts → L2) blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-009** `todo` Full OpenAPI doc emission from allRouteFragments + Schemathesis lanes (quick per-change on touched routes, deep nightly) + per-operation L2 ingestion blocked-by: P-005\n\n## Phase D — UI + generalization\n\n- **P-010** `todo` UI providers: nuqs-states AST provider (parseAsStringEnum/parseAsBoolean declarations) + tauri-webview crawler v1 (every route at defaults: renders, zero console errors, axe clean) blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-011** `todo` Pot-level provider registration: census_provider_registrations seeded from template manifests + harness:generate-from-repo detection + manual verb; vendor providers into the public templates mirror (hive-app-seam WI-2891 lesson) blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-012** `todo` Universal floor providers: ts-exports/vitest-files + plan-touched changed-code coverage floor (v8 JSON × census reverse map — the PR-less diff-cover) blocked-by: P-002\n\n## Phase E — agents + hardening\n\n- **P-013** `todo` Agent gap queue: claim-spec'd below-L3 work-items ranked by severity/recency; acceptance = ledger delta (surface reaches L3 via attribution from the new green test) blocked-by: P-006\n- **P-014** `todo` Mutation backstop: extend the papercusp-publish-auth Stryker 9.6 pilot — incremental on plan-touched files + nightly sampled rotation → L4 scores blocked-by: P-005\n- **P-015** `todo` UI crawler v2 (pruned nuqs state-product, per-route opt-in VRT) + agent-roles provider (blueprint registry × LLM-scenario evidence) blocked-by: P-010\n\n## Verification\n\nEach phase ships with its own tests in the canonical frameworks; the acceptance rubric (authored post-implementation per the standing gate) must include the system grading ITSELF: the census provider for a surface class added during this plan must show that class's surfaces at their true depth.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Framework-neutral core + stack-keyed SurfaceCensusProvider plugins\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-discussion 2026-08-17] The ledger, depth ladder, gates, and gap queue are framework-neutral; the ONLY stack-coupled pieces are census extractors and attribution probes, isolated behind a SurfaceCensusProvider contract { kind, fidelity, enumerate() } in @papercusp/testing-shell (the universalDomains/applyRoleGlobs shape). Providers are keyed by STACK (hono-routes, mcp-tools, sync-queries, nuqs-states, tauri-webview, openapi-spec, ts-exports), never by project, so any pot on the same stack reuses them. Every verdict carries a census-fidelity stamp (declared > spec > convention > observed > file-only) so weak censuses can never masquerade as strong ones.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-011\n\n### D-002 — Depth ladder L0-L4 schema'd; v1 populates three rungs\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-discussion 2026-08-17] Full ladder in the schema: L0 registered, L1 executed (attribution edge from a fresh green run), L2 conformant (generated adversarial fuzz passes), L3 intent-tested (non-generated green test with an attribution edge to the surface), L4 hardened (mutation score >= floor). V1 populates L0/L2/L3 semantics (L1 as plumbing); L4 is a bolt-on via P-014 and never blocks earlier phases. Rationale: a single tested? boolean forces one threshold for everything; the ladder lets different gates demand different floors and makes the gap rankable into an agent work queue.\nRelated: P-001, P-014\n\n### D-003 — Gate placement: emit-time refusal at plan-ship; checkpoint guards NEW surfaces only\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-discussion 2026-08-17] The hard refusal lives at scorecards:emit (check kind 'coverage', same refusal semantics as kind:'tests'): a pass-claiming rating over below-floor surfaces is REFUSED naming the failing surfaces. The green-checkpoint gets only a diff-scoped guard (surfaces first_seen after the last green pin and below floor, no waiver, = red) because the checkpoint is the fleet chokepoint and retrofitting the backlog there would freeze deploys. Waivers: shrink-only, expiry-dated, reason-required registry (KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS governance) — every gate needs a managed escape valve or it grows unmanaged ones.\nRelated: P-006, P-007\n\n### D-004 — Provider registration is POT-level, never plan-level\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-discussion 2026-08-17, owner-raised] The census is a standing property of the project, not of a unit of work: gates/queues/admin read it between and across plans, and plan-level registration would let two plans disagree about what the project's surfaces ARE. Registration = census_provider_registrations in PG, fed in priority order by (1) template manifests (each app-scope root declares its provider set — templated apps are born measurable), (2) harness:generate-from-repo stack detection (proposes providers for imported repos), (3) a manual verb surfaced in /admin/testing. Plans CONSUME the census (plan-touched scope resolution) and may NARROW what they are judged on via check args — they never define what exists. Distribution: providers vendored into the public templates mirror (hive-app-seam WI-2891 lesson).\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-005 — Dependency bill: two new deps only; named rejections\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-discussion 2026-08-17] Reuse already-in-tree: fast-check 4.x, @stryker-mutator/core+vitest-runner 9.6.1 (publish-auth pilot), @vitest/coverage-v8, @playwright/test + @axe-core/playwright, zod 4, tauri-agent-tools, testing-shell, test_runs, rubrics/instruments, openapi.ts. NEW: (1) @traversable/zod-test — zod-4 support decides it over zod-fast-check (zod-3 era); compat smoke over sampled tool schemas required before P-008 commits; (2) Schemathesis as an arm's-length Python CLI in scheduled lanes — infra, not a library contract. REJECTED with reasons: monocart/c8 (no cross-runner merge need yet), diff-cover/Codecov (PR-centric; repo has no PRs — plan-scoped floor is in-house), @hono/zod-openapi (projection already exists), Storybook (docs-only value), Chromatic/Percy (SaaS VRT; Playwright built-in suffices), DeepEval/promptfoo/Inspect (in-house LLM-scenarios + behaviour-suite are already trajectory-first; mine metric vocabulary only), Keploy (eBPF vs embedded-PG/Tauri; no traffic), mcp-testing-frameworks (young; zod registry harness reaches deeper), Crawljax/monkey tools (census kills discovery; nondeterministic).\nRelated: P-008, P-009, P-014\n\n### D-006 — Agentic authoring, deterministic artifact — no runtime-LLM steps in any gate\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-discussion 2026-08-17] Agents may use intent-driven/AI exploration (Stagehand-style, Playwright MCP) to AUTHOR tests, but what lands in the tree and is graded by the ledger must be compiled, replayable, deterministic steps (Playwright / tauri-agent-tools). Natural-language steps resolved by an LLM at runtime reintroduce nondeterminism into the gate this system exists to make deterministic. Same inversion for acceptance: an agent's coverage claim counts only as a LEDGER DELTA (the surface's depth moved via attribution from its new green test) — generator untrusted, verifier deterministic (TestGen-LLM pattern).\nRelated: P-013, P-015\n\n### D-007 — The criterion contract: four properties of a behavior↔test binding, three mechanized\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-raised 2026-08-17] A rubric criterion bound to a behavior test makes four claims: (1) the bound test EXISTS and is GREEN — checked today by check:{kind:'tests'}, but at FILE granularity (a fat green file satisfies the binding with the specific case never written); (2) the test actually EXERCISES the claimed subject; (3) the test WOULD FAIL if the behavior broke; (4) the assertion MEANS what the criterion's English says. This plan mechanizes 1-at-case-level, 2 and 3 (P-016): case-level binding via testNames/@verifies tags with a missing-named-case refusal; an attribution join requiring the bound test's run to carry a coverage_evidence edge to the criterion's surface; sampled falsifiability requiring scoped mutation to kill ≥1 bound test (the mutation-probe falsifiability culture promoted into the rubric gate). Property 4 is irreducibly judgment — the non-implementer grader and vetting consult keep it — but the gate narrows what judgment must cover to exactly that one property, and aids it by inlining bound assertion snippets beside each criterion at emit time.\nRelated: P-016, P-006, P-004, P-014\n\n### D-008 — Suite tests and rubric tests are the same artifacts; the BINDING is what must be made durable\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner-raised 2026-08-17] VERIFIED, not assumed. (a) Agent-written Vitest tests DO auto-join the suite: packages/operator-core/vitest.config.ts and apps/operator/vitest.config.ts declare no `include`, so Vitest's default glob discovers any new *.test.ts with zero registration, and affected-tests.mjs runs the owning workspace's suite. Caveats that make \"in the tree\" != \"in the verdict\": selection is by WORKSPACE mapping from changed paths (a test in an untouched workspace runs only in the full/checkpoint suite); quarantine.txt can exclude tests or whole workspaces; only Vitest is glob-discovered (Playwright e2e, Cargo, LLM scenarios each need placement, which is what lint:tests guards); and a root-level vitest run matching zero files still exits 0.\n\n(b) Rubric tests are the SAME FILES as suite tests — nothing is duplicated. What is thrown away is the BINDING: rubrics.ts treats a shipped plan's acceptance rubric as retired (\"one-shot, never a lingering library entry\"), so the criterion-sentence-to-test link evaporates at ship while the test file lives forever. Three costs observed from that asymmetry: a red reports \"a test failed\" instead of \"this breaks the behavior ratified as C-NNN of plan X\" (gate triage loses semantics every time); deleting or gutting the sole proof of a behavior is SILENT; and a later plan touching the same surface cannot see which behaviors were previously ratified, so it re-derives or contradicts them.\n\nRULING: keep the one-shot rubric lifecycle as designed, but persist the EVIDENCE it produces. P-017 writes a durable `verifies` edge into coverage_evidence at scorecards:emit (criterion text + rubric/plan ref + test case + surface). Acceptance thereby stops being a one-shot ceremony and becomes the mechanism that ACCUMULATES a behavior ledger — the same test artifact, now permanently linked to the behavior it ratifies.\nRelated: P-017, P-016, P-006\n\n### D-009 — The meta-rubric grades test-binding QUALITY via the census — not merely that a check is present\nDate: 2026-08-18\n[owner-directed 2026-08-17, Avi] RULING: the rubric-rubric (meta-acceptance-rubric) must include checking for good tests that use this census system well. This governs the rubric/vetting lane as well as this plan, so it is recorded here as a Decision rather than left in chat.\n\nTHE GAP, as measured. The meta-rubric today carries six criteria (outcomes-not-diff-restatements, traces-to-goal-or-decision, falsifiable-with-evidence, failure-mode-coverage, non-overlapping, prefer-structured-check). All six grade how the acceptance rubric is WRITTEN. The closest to test quality, `prefer-structured-check`, asks only that an objectively-checkable criterion CARRY a structured check binding (kind:'tests' {files} or kind:'instrument'). Nothing grades whether the bound test is any good. That leaves three holes this plan's own D-007 already names:\n\n1. FILE GRANULARITY. check:{kind:'tests'} binds a FILE, so a fat green file satisfies the check while proving nothing about the criterion (D-007 property 1). P-016 is what makes case-level binding possible.\n2. NO DEPTH FLOOR. A plan can ship having registered its new surfaces at L0 and never exercised them; the acceptance rubric passes because no criterion ever asks. check:{kind:'coverage'} { scope, floor } (P-006) is what makes that askable.\n3. NO DURABILITY. Even a good binding is undefended: quarantining, deleting, or gutting the sole proof of a ratified criterion is invisible today. P-017's durable `verifies` edges plus P-018's live-proof guard are what make it surface.\n\nRULING. Add ONE new criterion to meta-acceptance-rubric (non-overlapping with the six, per its own `non-overlapping` criterion) covering (a) discriminating binding, (b) at/above-floor census depth for surfaces the work newly registered, (c) a durable verifies edge with a live proof. Tracked as P-019.\n\nSEQUENCING, and why it is not done now. The criterion is unsatisfiable until the mechanisms it cites exist: check kind 'coverage' is P-006, case-level binding is P-016, durable edges are P-017. Authoring it earlier would put a criterion into a live gate that no plan could pass. P-019 is therefore blocked-by P-006/P-016/P-017, not deferred by preference.\n\nSTATUS NOTE worth surfacing: meta-acceptance-rubric is status:'proposed' with ratifiedBy:null — it has never been ratified, and by its own description it is exempt from vetting and 'owner-ratified instead'. So the amendment lands on a rubric that is still open, and the owner is its ratifier.\nRelated: P-006, P-016, P-017, P-018, P-019\n\n### D-010 — Traffic evidence keys on the BINDING, holds test_run_id NULL, and hooks the mount seam — not a Hono middleware\nDate: 2026-08-18\nThree rulings settled while building P-004's attribution layer. All three bind P-005+ (which READ `coverage_evidence`), so they are recorded rather than left implicit in the code.\n\n**1.
