The chokepoints are the MOUNT SEAM and the MCP TELEMETRY SINK — not a Hono middleware.**\nThe item text says \"test-mode Hono middleware\"; the implementation instead hooks `runRouteStack`'s `finally` (which receives the `RouteDefinition` itself) and `recordInvocationImpl` (the single sink every settled `tools/call` reaches, replay branch included). Reason: a `app.use('*')` middleware would have to re-derive the surface identity from `c.req.routePath`, creating a SECOND source of truth for the one identity this system may not get wrong — and it could not tell which of several overlapping routes actually served the request without re-implementing Hono's precedence rules (the very subtlety `isCatchAll` ordering exists for). At the mount seam, observer and census read the same array: `providers/hono-routes.ts` enumerates `routeRegistrationOrder()`, and `registerRoute` mounts exactly one `runRouteStack` call per entry of it. The populations are identical by construction.\n\n**2. `verdict` on a traffic row answers \"DID THE HANDLER RUN?\", and a GATE REJECTION IS NOT COVERAGE.**\nThis layer observes one CALL, not a test outcome — the test's own verdict is written later by the reporter into `test_runs` and joins on `(run_group_id, file_path)`. So:\n- handler ran and returned (incl. 404/400/`refused`) -> `pass`\n- handler ran and threw / timed out -> `error`\n- a gate refused BEFORE it ran (`unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `quota-exceeded`, `role-not-allowed`, `replayed`) -> `skip`\nThe last line is the load-bearing one: a test that only ever gets a 401 from a route has exercised the GUARD, not the route. Recording that as `pass` would manufacture exactly the false confidence this census exists to prevent. An UNRECOGNISED status maps to `error`, never `pass`, so a future member of the dispatcher's status union cannot silently become credited coverage.\n\n**3. Traffic rows carry `test_run_id = NULL`; the row's identity is the BINDING (surface, test_file, test_case).**\nThe `test_runs` row for a file is written by the reporter when that FILE FINISHES — strictly after the traffic being attributed — so at write time there is usually no id to point at. `test_run_id` participates in the `coverage_evidence_dedup` expression index, so resolving it opportunistically would mean the SAME binding produces one row or two depending on whether the flush debounce fired before or after the file ended: the table's contents would become a function of flush TIMING, which a *deterministic* census cannot have. Holding it at NULL makes the row set stable and bounded — exactly one row per (surface, test file, test case), refreshed (verdict + `observed_at`) on every run.\n\nConsequences P-005 must honour:\n- Run correlation lives in `details.runGroupId`, which joins to `test_runs.run_group_id`. Do NOT read `test_run_id` for traffic rows; it is null by design, not by omission.\n- `details.calls` carries how many observations collapsed into the binding, so \"exercised once\" and \"hammered 400 times\" remain distinguishable after the collapse.\n- Other evidence kinds (fuzz, mutation) are genuinely per-run and SHOULD populate `test_run_id`; the index supports both, and traffic simply uses the NULL lane.\n- A surface the census has no live row for is COUNTED as `unmatchedSurfaces`, never created. Letting traffic define the population would reintroduce the hand-maintained-list drift D-001 forbids. A retired surface likewise takes no evidence.\n- Attribution REFUSES rather than guesses when the (workspace, harness) scope is unresolvable: a guessed scope writes evidence that joins to nothing or — worse — to another harness's identically-named surface. An unattributed run is recoverable; a misattributed one is not.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-011 — D-011: evidence and surfaces share ONE scope resolver — attribution may not re-derive the scope from env\nDate: 2026-08-18\n#### The ruling\n\n`coverage_evidence` and `testing_surfaces` join on `(workspace_id, harness_slug)`. That pair is now produced by exactly ONE function — `resolveCensusScope()` in `packages/operator-core/lib/coverage-census/scope.ts` — called by BOTH the census that writes surfaces (`routines/coverage-census-action.ts`) and the attribution layer that writes evidence (`attribution/context.ts` → `attribution/sink.ts`). Neither side may re-derive it.\n\nPrecedence, in the shared resolver: (1) an explicit env PIN — `PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE_ID` / `PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE`, then `PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_HARNESS` / `HARNESS_SLUG` / `PAPERCUSP_HARNESS_SLUG` (the test-runs reporter's own variables, in its order); (2) the ambient runtime resolvers `activeWorkspaceId()` / `operatorHomeHarnessSlug()`. It is TOTAL — it always answers.\n\n#### Why (the measurement, not the theory)\n\nP-004 shipped attribution with its own env-only scope lookup, mirroring the test-runs reporter on the reasoning that \"a run's `test_runs` rows and its evidence rows should land in one scope.\" Coherent, and wrong — because nobody checked what the reporter actually resolves.\n\nMeasured 2026-08-18 against the live operator DB:\n- `harness_slug` is **NULL on 100%** of the 7,202 `test_runs` rows written in the preceding 90 minutes — every source (`ci` gate 5,539+8+4+4, `local` 1,110+537). `workspace_id` was non-null on only 537 of them.\n- **Neither** live `hono-host` process has ANY of the four scope variables set (checked with a positive control: 37 and 28 other `PAPERCUSP_*` vars ARE set on those pids).\n- `green-checkpoint.ts:4694` strips every `PAPERCUSP_*` and `HOST_ENV_STRIP = [\"AGENT_MODELS\",\"HARNESS_SLUG\"]`, and its comment at :4710 states that NOT stamping the harness is deliberate.\n\nSo the scope both sides \"agreed\" on was `(NULL, NULL)`; attribution's refusal branch fired on every flush; the layer could not have written one row however much traffic it saw. Arming it would have produced silence indistinguishable from \"the tests cover nothing\".\n\n#### Why a runtime fallback is not the \"guess\" the refusal guarded against\n\nThe refusal existed to prevent MISATTRIBUTION — evidence landing on another harness's surface of the same name. A resolver SHARED WITH THE WRITER cannot do that: it returns the scope the surfaces are actually in. And `pg-evidence-store` is belt-and-braces regardless — it looks each surface up WITHIN the scope and counts a miss as `unmatchedSurfaces` instead of inserting, so a wrong scope writes zero rows loudly rather than wrong rows quietly. `resolveAttributionScope()` keeps its `| null` return, but null now means \"resolution THREW\", not \"was not configured\".\n\n#### The generalisable rule\n\nA derivation agreeing with another derivation IN PRINCIPLE is not evidence that either resolves IN FACT. When two sides must agree on a join key, share the function — do not restate the rule on both sides and trust them to stay equal. The integration test that \"proved\" the refusal was green the whole time, because a test over a condition meant to be exceptional is worth little unless someone checks how often that condition actually holds.\n\n#### Consequential sub-rulings\n\n- **The no-real-PG rail gates the STORE, never ARMING.** `PAPERCUSP_FORBID_REAL_PG=1` (the unit layer's `setup-no-real-pg.ts`) now stands the sink down at `resolveStore()` — quietly, not as a counted flush failure — and only when no store was injected. Disarming on it instead ALSO suppresses observation, which broke all 7 sink unit tests that drive the hooks against a fake store and need no database. The rail forbids exactly one thing (opening a real connection); that is the only thing it may veto.\n- **The runners arm unconditionally.** `testing:run` (`agent-tools/testing/run.ts`) and the admin-UI runner (`testing-run-store.ts`) stamp `PAPERCUSP_TEST_ATTRIBUTION=1` beside `PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_GROUP`. One `files` array routinely spans the unit and integration layers, so the runner cannot make the per-layer call — the fork can.\n- **green-checkpoint is deliberately NOT armed.** Arming the gate needs the scope pair stamped into its child env, which collides with the existing deliberate ruling at `green-checkpoint.ts:4710` (leaving harness/workspace unset keeps gate rows out of the per-harness Tests tab). That is a separate decision with its own trade-off, not a one-line stamp; deferred out of P-004 rather than taken silently.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-012 — Census read surfaces push producer-side, not by table trigger — and the exemption states the weaker guarantee\nDate: 2026-08-18\nRULING (binds every later census read surface, incl. Phase D). A sync-resolver entry reading census tables declares `backingTables` AND takes a documented PUSH_EXEMPT; it does NOT get an `emit_change_notify` trigger.\n\nWHY THIS CAME UP. P-005's `testing.coverage` entry tripped `resolver-backing-table-coverage.test.ts` (a shrink-only ratchet, 199 -> 200). Caught by su-d8292 running an unrelated suite, not by me — my own guard sweep (gen:contract:check, lint:tests, lint:tool-prompts) did not cover sync-resolver.\n\nTHE TRAP, which is the part worth carrying forward. The one-minute fix is to declare `backingTables` and move on. That would have been WRONG and silently so: `pg_trigger` shows NONE of the three census tables (testing_surfaces, coverage_evidence, census_provider_registrations) carries `emit_change_notify` — `work_items` does, as a positive control — so the `table-to-query-names.ts` bridge would have had nothing to bridge. The panel would have refreshed on remount only, looking live. That is verbatim the `accounts.pool` failure documented on `QueryEntry.backingTables`: four invalidation callsites, no writer-side path, ~7 weeks of stale numbers before the owner noticed. A declaration that satisfies a guard without arming a push is the bug the guard exists to catch, wearing the guard's own uniform.\n\nWHY PRODUCER-SIDE IS RIGHT HERE (the derived-reads precedent). Both census writers are BATCH producers whose row counts say nothing about whether the panel's numbers moved. A census run re-upserts the whole surface population (1,105 rows today), nearly all byte-identical, so a row trigger would fire ~1,105 NOTIFYs per hour to communicate one fact. So: `coverage-census-action.ts` pushes once per run; `attribution/pg-evidence-store.ts` pushes once per flush, guarded on `written > 0` (a flush matching no surfaces changed nothing). Evidence is the numerator of every coverage ratio, so that second push is the one that actually matters.\n\nTHE HONESTY CONSTRAINT. The census push fires once per RUN, not once per CHANGE — `upserted` counts no-op upserts, so a census that changed nothing still pushes. It is therefore WEAKER than the md5-guarded derived-reads push it is modelled on. The exemption text says this in as many words. Do not restate it as \"pushes when the payload changes\"; a later reader comparing the two exemptions must be able to see the difference without re-deriving it.\n\nRE-ARM (all three tables): drop the exemption and wire the table in `table-to-query-names.ts` if either producer push is removed, or if a writer OUTSIDE these two paths starts moving these rows — at that point a trigger is the only thing that can see the write.\n\nNOT DECLARED: `harness_shared.testing_surface_depth`. It is a VIEW (relkind 'v') — no rows of its own to change, and no trigger can attach to it. Declaring it would name a relation no writer could ever invalidate.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-013 — Attribution reports zero because the unit lane cannot persist, not because the seam is unreached — and 12.4% of the census has no observer at all\nDate: 2026-09-02\nReported from plan `design-to-code-coverage-seam-2026-09-02` P-006 (full detail in its D-025), which asked to arm `PAPERCUSP_TEST_ATTRIBUTION=1` on the gate paths and report what the number turned out to be. This plan owns the machinery (P-004), so it owns the consequence.\n\n**Measured 2026-09-02.** `harness_shared.coverage_evidence`: **0 rows**. `harness_shared.testing_surfaces`: **2,019 live** (886 `mcp-tool`, 882 `http-route`, 251 `sync-query`), `last_seen` minutes old. The census half is healthy and fresh; the evidence half has never produced a row.\n\n**That zero was already an ARMED zero.** `PAPERCUSP_TEST_ATTRIBUTION=1` was set on two paths before P-006 touched anything — `agent-tools/testing/run.ts:1221` and `testing-run-store.ts:435`. So the natural reading (\"nobody armed it\") was wrong, and arming more paths was never going to be sufficient on its own.\n\n**Root cause.** `flushTrafficEvidence` stands down on the unit layer's rail — `realPgForbidden()` is `!state.store && PAPERCUSP_FORBID_REAL_PG === '1'` (sink.ts:367), and `defineVitestConfig` wires `setup-no-real-pg.ts` into `layer === 'unit'` ONLY (`libs/test-config/src/vitest-config.ts:290`). The rail gates the STORE, not the hooks, exactly as `context.ts` documents. So a unit-lane process observes traffic and can never write it. Every configured `greenCmd` on this box resolves to `scripts/affected-tests.mjs` without `--integration` (default `npm run test:related`, `release-config.ts:331`), so the largest body of test execution here is permanently in the lane that cannot persist. This is a design consequence, not a defect — but it means \"coverage_evidence is empty\" has never been a statement about coverage.\n\n**The seam itself is fine.** New positive control `packages/operator-core/lib/coverage-census/attribution/seam-reachability.test.ts` (8/8 passing) drives the real `registerRoute` → `runRouteStack` path and shows the observation lands with the correct surface id, verdict and ambient test identity, reaches an injected store through the real flush, and collapses repeated calls to one binding — each paired with a control that must observe nothing. The previously untested link was precisely the one that mattered: `sink.test.ts` drove the sink's own entry points, `pg-evidence-store.integration.test.ts` drove the store, and whether REAL route traffic reaches the sink through the real call site was asserted nowhere.\n\n**A gap this plan should price in: `sync-query` has no observer.** `providers/sync-queries.ts` contributes **251 live surfaces (12.4% of the census)**, and the sink emits exactly two kinds — `HTTP_ROUTE_KIND`/`MCP_TOOL_KIND` (sink.ts:56-57, its only `kind:` literals at :188 and :215). No arming, lane, or gate change can ever attribute those 251. They are structurally unreachable evidence, so they should be excluded from the uncovered denominator or given an observer; counting them as \"uncovered\" overstates the gap by an eighth and will not converge.\n\n**Arming still landed** at both chokepoints (`buildGreenCheckpointEnv`, and the `childEnv` in affected-tests.mjs which serves BOTH lanes so `--integration` can now write), each pinned against silent regression — behaviourally in `green-checkpoint.test.ts`, and via `doc-claims/attribution-arming.{ts,test.ts}` for the `.mjs`, which exposes no seam.\n\n**Open, and handed to this plan.** Whether an integration-lane run actually persists rows is now isolatable but undemonstrated: one armed integration file (`harness-spawn-routes.integration.test.ts`, 32 passing) still left the table at 0, and two explanations remain unseparated — the suite drives no real seam, or every row is dropped as an unmatched surface at the `testing_surfaces` join in `pg-evidence-store.ts:95`. `attributionStatus()` already returns exactly the fields that would tell those apart (`buffered` / `written` / `unmatchedSurfaces` / `lastError`, added for this purpose), and **nothing anywhere prints it**. Surfacing it at the end of an armed run is the cheapest next step and would retire this whole class of ambiguity.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"file-level-test-selection-2026-08-17","title":"Run only the tests a change can actually break: import-graph test selection","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-17","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Run only the tests a change can actually break: import-graph test selection\nslug: file-level-test-selection-2026-08-17\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-08-21\n---\n\n## Now\n\nImplementing P-002..P-007 directly (owner directed implementation start-to-finish in the same turn\nas the plan). Design is settled by measurement, not assumption — see Finding 2.\n\n## Background\n\n`npm run test:affected` selects at **npm-workspace** granularity: changed paths map to their owning\nworkspace, and that workspace's ENTIRE suite runs. Touch one file in operator-core and all 4,978 of\nits test files run. The gate shows this as `AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT tasks=89`.\n\n## Finding 1 — vitest's native `related` is NOT a drop-in win here (measured, rejected)\n\n`vitest related --run lib/harness/routines/release-actions.ts` in operator-core selected hyperbee\nseed tests, scout, identity, inference-gateway, docs handlers, memory — and had not finished at a\n300s timeout. `vitest list` (plain enumeration of the package) also TIMED OUT at 200s. Vitest builds\nits module graph through vite, and at ~9,600 files in this one package that collection step alone\ncosts more than the narrowing saves. So the mechanism must be a CHEAP STATIC index, not vitest's\nruntime graph. `vitest related` stays rejected for the hot path.\n\n## Finding 2 — selection genuinely narrows, but it is BIMODAL (the number that drives the design)\n\nStatic reverse-import measurement over `packages/operator-core/lib` (9,616 files: 4,978 test,\n4,638 source; relative imports only, so cross-package edges are UNDERCOUNTED):\n\n| changing one source file selects | test files | % of 4,978 |\n|---|---|---|\n| p10 | 2 | 0.0% |\n| **median** | **915** | **18.4%** |\n| p75 | 927 | 18.6% |\n| p90 | 1,005 | 20.2% |\n| p99 | 1,570 | 31.5% |\n| max | 2,747 | 55.2% |\n\n- **~5.4x narrowing for the median change**; 31.2% of source files select <=10% of tests; 3.7%\n  select none at all.\n- But a large BARREL-CONNECTED CORE means the typical file still pulls ~915 tests. The mirror\n  statistic explains why: the median TEST reaches only 16 sources, while p90 reaches 3,026 — i.e. a\n  MINORITY of hub test files import barrels (`lib/agent-tools/index.ts` and friends) and therefore\n  get selected by nearly any change.\n\nSo: ship selection for the real 5x, and treat the barrel-importing hub TESTS as the separate,\nlarger structural win (Phase 3). Do not oversell selection as more than 5x.\n\n## Design\n\nA new `--related` mode on `scripts/affected-tests.mjs`, with the graph logic in its own testable\nmodule. NOT the default for `test:affected`, because the GATE calls that script and the gate must\nstay broad (it is what certifies `main`; import-graph selection structurally cannot see\ncross-cutting breakage such as a required field added to a shared interface — the class\n`lint:required-field-strands` and `lint:tsc` exist to catch).\n\nFail-safe rails, all in the direction of running MORE tests rather than fewer:\n1. Repo-wide invariant guards attach EXACTLY as today — selection never removes a guard.\n2. Empty selection for an affected workspace => run its FULL suite. An affected workspace that\n   somehow resolves to zero related tests must never report a vacuous pass.\n3. Selection >= 50% of the workspace's tests => run the full suite (no benefit, and it avoids\n   pathological argv lengths).\n4. A changed TEST file always selects itself.\n5. Emit `RELATED_SELECTION ws=<name> selected=<n> total=<n> mode=<related|full> reason=<...>` so\n   the narrowing is OBSERVABLE per run and a silent collapse to \"0 tests\" is impossible to miss.\n\n## Phase 1 — the selection engine\n\n- **P-001** `done` Measure whether selection can narrow at all in this repo before building anything (Findings 1 and 2). importance: high\n- **P-002** `done` Add `scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs`: static reverse-import index + `selectRelatedTests(changedPaths)`, pure and unit-testable. importance: high — note: Implemented + unit-verified; selection proven on real tree (leaf 40/4981, hub 901/4981).\n- **P-003** `done` Unit-test the engine incl. the fail-safe rails and a positive control (barrel case, leaf case, changed-test-selects-itself, empty => full). importance: high — note: Implemented + unit-verified; selection proven on real tree (leaf 40/4981, hub 901/4981).\n- **P-004** `done` Wire `--related` into affected-tests.mjs via the existing `spawnSpecFor(t, extraArgs)` seam; add the `RELATED_SELECTION` marker. importance: high — note: Implemented + unit-verified; selection proven on real tree (leaf 40/4981, hub 901/4981).\n- **P-005** `done` Add the `npm run test:related` script; leave `test:affected` (the gate path) byte-identical. importance: high — note: Implemented + unit-verified; selection proven on real tree (leaf 40/4981, hub 901/4981).\n\n## Phase 2 — verify\n\n- **P-006** `done` Verify end-to-end on a real change: `test:related` selects a strict subset, and the tests it selects actually pass. importance: high — note: ← WI-39781 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Verify the gate path is UNCHANGED — `test:affected` still selects the same workspace set (`--print-affected` diff before/after). — note: Gate path proven unchanged: 131 insertions / 1 deletion; the one changed line spreads relatedFiles ?? [] which is undefined without --related (assignment provably inside the relatedOnly guard, lines 2378-2429), so the gate's argv is byte-identical.\n\n## Phase 3 — the bigger structural win (not this turn)\n\n- **P-008** `done` Attack the barrel-importing hub TEST files. The median test reaches 16 sources; p90 reaches 3,026. Cutting barrel imports in that minority would collapse the median selection from ~915 toward ~16 — an order of magnitude beyond what selection alone buys. — note: ← WI-40118 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Static index, not `vitest related`\nVitest's graph is built through vite and costs more than it saves at this repo's size — `vitest\nlist` alone timed out at 200s on one package. Selection must be a cheap static pass.\n\n### D-002 The gate keeps its broad sweep; selection is the LOCAL fast path\nImport-graph selection cannot see cross-cutting breakage. The gate certifies `main`, so it keeps\nrunning the full affected-workspace suites; `test:related` is the developer inner loop. This is the\nsafety trade named when the owner asked, and it is why `test:affected` is left untouched.\n\n### D-003 Every rail fails toward running MORE tests\nEmpty selection, over-threshold selection, and any resolution failure all fall back to the full\nsuite. A selection bug must never manifest as a green run that tested nothing.\n\n### D-004 — The narrowing figure is PER-WORKSPACE, not end-to-end — quote it that way or Phase 3 gets mis-scoped\nDate: 2026-08-18\nMEASURED 2026-08-18 on a real end-to-end run, not modelled.\n\n`--related` narrows ONLY the workspace that CONTAINS a changed path. Every other affected\nworkspace correctly falls back to `mode=full reason=no-changed-paths-in-scope`.\n\nA leaf change (packages/operator-core/lib/tsc-diagnostics.ts) selects FIVE workspaces —\noperator-core, web, operator-vite, agent-mcp, plugin-loader — because they depend on\noperator-core. The observed selection was:\n\n    RELATED_SELECTION ws=@papercusp/operator-core selected=40  total=4981 mode=related\n    RELATED_SELECTION ws=@papercusp/web           selected=806 total=806  mode=full\n\nSo the run executed ~846 files, NOT 40. The \"124x on a leaf file\" figure is a\nPER-WORKSPACE ratio measured inside operator-core. End-to-end it is far smaller.\n\nWHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A NOTE. The per-workspace number is the one that shows up in\na log line, so it is the one that gets quoted — and quoted unqualified it justifies work\nthat will not pay off. My own carry-note stated \"leaf 40/4981, 124x\" with no qualifier,\nwhich reads as an end-to-end claim and is wrong. Anyone sizing Phase 3 (P-008,\nbarrel-breaking) off the unqualified number will over-estimate the remaining headroom.\n\nWHAT FOLLOWS FOR P-008. Breaking barrel imports in hub TEST files raises the ceiling only\nWITHIN the changed workspace. The larger structural cost — that a one-file change in a\nshared package drags four downstream workspaces to a full run — is NOT addressed by\nbarrel-breaking at all. If end-to-end wall-clock is the goal, cross-workspace narrowing is\nthe bigger lever and it is NOT in this plan's scope today.\n\nDO NOT \"FIX\" THE FALLBACK BY NARROWING DOWNSTREAM WORKSPACES ON THE CURRENT INDEX. The\nindex is per-workspace and resolves intra-repo specifiers only; a downstream workspace\nreaches operator-core through the PACKAGE ENTRY, which is the ultimate barrel. Selecting on\nit would either select everything anyway (no gain) or, if implemented carelessly against a\npartial graph, select too little — and under-selecting is the one failure mode this design\nrefuses, because it certifies nothing while reporting green. The full fallback is CORRECT\nuntil a cross-workspace graph exists that resolves package entries to real source files.\nRelated: P-006, P-008\n\n### D-005 — RETRACTION: prior closure percentiles were artifacts of cycle-truncated memoization\nDate: 2026-08-20\nDate: 2026-08-20\n\nThe plan's earlier median=16/17, p90=3,026/4,027 and modeled selection-narrowing figures are invalid. transitiveDeps memoized closures while breaking DFS cycles; the first root through a cycle cached a partial set, so results depended on file enumeration and call order. Deleting an import edge could make a reported closure increase, proving the metric was not graph reachability.\n\nEI-21017977638418975 replaces that algorithm with SCC condensation and an order-independence regression. On the live operator-core tree the exact graph contains a roughly 4,065-file strongly connected component: n=5,056 tests, median closure=4,065, p90=4,066, max=4,083. The sound selector therefore falls back to full for most changes that enter this component, as D-003 requires.\n\nP-008's removal of redundant all-op barrel imports remains behaviorally correct and shrinks a genuinely isolated contract test from a counterfactual 4,066-file closure to 20, but most target tests already reach the giant SCC through their leaf op and cannot be narrowed by import cleanup alone. Future performance work must break the runtime SCC at its source; do not quote the old percentiles or projected roughly 915-to-16 selection win.\n\n### D-006 — Retract every pre-SCC closure metric; exact cyclic reachability precedes performance claims\nDate: 2026-08-20\nWI-40118/EI-21017977638418975 reproduced an impossible monotonicity failure: removing an import edge increased a reported transitive closure from roughly 1,435 to 4,066. The writer used DFS memoization with a stack cycle guard, so it cached partial closures and made results traversal-order dependent; this can under-select tests and violates D-003's fail-wide safety contract. Therefore every closure/median/p90/performance figure produced by the pre-fix algorithm is retracted and must not be cited. P-008 completes only after the SCC-condensation implementation passes order-independence and monotonicity regressions, the repository-native test suite, and a fresh real-tree measurement whose numbers are recorded as the sole authoritative figures.\nRelated: P-008\n\n## Requirements\n\nThe local `test:related` path selects a sound superset of tests that can be affected by the changed files and fails open to running more tests whenever analysis is incomplete. The release-gate `test:affected` path remains behaviorally unchanged. The remaining barrel-import cleanup must measurably reduce the high-fanout test reachability distribution without losing coverage, and the newly selected subset must pass.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"learning-tab-filters-are-page-scoped-2026-08-17","title":"Learning tab: filters only see one page, not the corpus — push them to the server","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-17","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Learning tab: filters only see one page, not the corpus — push them to the server\nslug: learning-tab-filters-are-page-scoped-2026-08-17\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-08-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nSteps (1)-(3) and (5) are SHIPPED and live-verified; the payload work behind (4) is shipped too (tierReason interned, 259,087 -> 187,517 B). **But step (4) itself — ImproveGrid's growing window — is now RULED OUT by D-010, and the plan's goal is BLOCKED on an owner fork.**\n\nD-010 measured what D-002/D-007/D-008/D-009 never had: the corpus's GROWTH RATE. The digest's own flow block gives captured7d=156 vs resolved7d=24, net7d=132 — the open set accretes ~18.9 rows/day. That dates every client-side-window lever: today's 13-row headroom is ~0.7 DAYS, and the proposed six-field encode buys ~8.0 DAYS for the cost of decoding six RENDERED fields at every read site. Per the repo's own recorded convention (SYNC_READ_ALLOWLIST coord.plans / WI-7256), a breach that is pure ROW GROWTH is a WINDOWING trigger, not another per-row cut. A growing window is un-windowing.\n\nAlso inverted: `clampedLimitOpt(500)` (sync-resolver/index.ts:3696) is the GUARD keeping this read in budget, not the obstacle D-009 filed it as. KEEP IT.\n\n⚠ THE FORK: D-001 is an OWNER ruling (\"mimic the Work Queue, not a server-side filter push\"), made before this measurement. At ~19 rows/day, \"filters see the whole corpus\" and \"no server-side filter push\" are NOT jointly satisfiable. That is Avi's call, not an agent's — do not resolve it by cleverness, and do not start the encode or the window while it is open.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Avi to settle the D-010/D-001 fork (accept server-side filtering for ImproveGrid, or accept that its filters stay window-scoped with honest labels); no agent should start step (4), the six-field encode, or any clamp raise until then.)\n\n## Background — what is actually broken (MEASURED, not inferred)\n\nThe Learning tab's filter controls are **not inert**: they wire up, write their nuqs param, and\nrun. The defect is that each one filters **the page the client happens to hold**, while the\n*counts printed beside it* come from the **server-side corpus**. So the user picks a facet\nadvertising 992 rows and gets 17 — which reads as \"the filter doesn't work\".\n\nAll numbers below were read live from an isolated Tauri shell driving the real operator\n(`scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh --boot-only`, bridge pid 2841077, DISPLAY :90) and\ncross-checked against Postgres.\n\n### 1. Observe -> Observations (`apps/operator/app/adv/create/ObservationsPanel.tsx`)\n\n`learning.observations` ships `limit ?? 200` rows plus a corpus `total`. Search (`obsq`) and the\n`ColumnFilterBar` (`obsf`: Scope / Role / Confidence) then run **client-side over those 200**,\nand the count line renders `${rows.length} of ${total}` — a page-scoped numerator against a\ncorpus denominator.\n\n| control | UI reported | Postgres truth |\n|---|---|---|\n| search `postgres` | `10 observations match, of 36,096 total` | **305** matching observations |\n| Scope = `harness:papercusp` | `89 of 36,094` | **33,781** matching |\n| Scope enum options offered | 4 | **8** distinct scopes exist |\n\n(`SELECT ... FROM harness_shared.engineer_issues WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND lane='observation'` -> 37,671 rows.)\n\nThe resolver header already names this as owed work: *\"it backs the pane's client-side search\nacross all 200 ... The next breach is WI-7304 (on-demand body + server-side search).\"*\n\n### 2. Improve -> Improvements (`LearningTab.tsx` ImprovementsView)\n\nThe **rail facet** chips carry `snap.railCounts` — corpus-wide totals — but the filter runs over\n`snap.recent`, a recency slice:\n\n| chip | advertises | rows after clicking it |\n|---|---|---|\n| All rails | 1,639 | 503 |\n| improvement | **992** | **17 of 503** |\n\nThe `ColumnFilterBar` (`impf`) itself is *correct within the loaded set* (Kind=bug -> `3 of 503`,\nmatching its own enum count of 3) — its denominator is the loaded set, which is the honest form.\nSecondary: `learning.improvements` clamps `limit` at 500 and the scope bar renders\n`From the loop 500` — a saturated cap being read as a total.\n\n### 3. Retain -> Learnings (`LearningTab.tsx` RetainedLedgerCard)\n\n`learning.retainFeed` is keyset-paginated at `RETAIN_FEED_PAGE_SIZE = 24`. `rtab` and `rship`\nare **server** args and behave. The `ColumnFilterBar` (`rtf`) and quick-search (`rq`) were layered\non top **client-side**, so they see 24 rows:\n\n| tab badge (server corpus) | Kind filter offers |\n|---|---|\n| Memories 544 · Plans 21 · Work items 887 · Rubrics 34 · Runbooks 703 · Recipes 2.8k | `recipe 13 · rubric 2 · runbook 1 · wi 8` |\n\n`memory` and `plan` are **not offered as filter values at all**. `learning-retain-read.ts`'s own\nheader states the rule this violates: *\"a client-side filter over a paged feed drops rows\nunpredictably\"* — which is exactly why `rship` was put server-side.\n\n### Subtabs with no filters (nothing to fix)\n\nSignals, Rubrics, Analyze->Pipeline, and the Verify family (Benchmark, Pot scoring, Bake-off, EKG,\nRed Queen, Experiments, Frontier, Throughput) expose no filter controls.\n\n### Root cause, one sentence\n\nThree panels apply `useColumnFilters` / quick-search **client-side to a server-truncated page**,\nand render the result against a **server-wide count** — violating both the repo rule\n(*\"a caller's `limit` bounds ROW LISTS ONLY — never an aggregate\"*) and the retain resolver's own\nstated design.\n\n## Phase 1 — push each filter to its source\n\n- **P-001** `done` Observations: push `q` + `scope` + `sourceRole` + `confidence` + `kind` into `learning.observations` args -> SQL. `listIssues`/`countIssues` ALREADY accept `q` and `scope`/`scopes`, so those two are near-free; role/confidence/kind are `payload` JSON predicates to add. `total` becomes the FILTERED total so the count line stops lying. — note: ← WI-39675 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Observations: serve corpus-wide facet options (distinct scope / role / confidence + counts) so the enum lists are complete instead of page-derived. blocked-by: P-001 — note: Absorbed per corpus-accurate-counts-and-facets-2026-08-21#D-010 by current P-005/WI-40423 plus EI-21180067367832016 predicate-parity and client-accessibility healthy evidence.\n- **P-003** `done` Retain: push `rtf` column filters + `rq` search into `learning.retainFeed`, composed per-leg with the keyset cursor exactly as `rship` already is. Resolve the Kind-column/`rtab` redundancy (one axis, one control). Serve status/lens facets server-side. — note: Absorbed per D-010 by current P-007/WI-40538 plus WI-40590 exact-zero and predicate-parity evidence, independently graded healthy in EI-21180067367832016.\n- **P-004** `done` Improvements: make the rail facet honest — either serve a rail-filtered page from `learning.scout` or scope `railCounts` to the filterable population. Same treatment for the saturated `From the loop 500` cap. — note: Absorbed per D-010 by current P-006/WI-40440; predecessor D-010/D-011 remain preserved authority for bounded server-side Improve filtering.\n- **P-005** `done` Guard: one falsifiable test per surface asserting `filtered count == server truth` (a mutation back to client-side filtering must red it), plus a boundedness marker on every aggregate rendered next to a filter. — note: Absorbed per D-010 by current P-003/WI-40406 recurrence guard plus WI-40590 governed matrices; EI-21180067367832016 grades inventory, predicate, cursor, and control evidence healthy.\n- **P-006** `done` Live verification in an isolated Tauri shell — re-run the exact measurements in this Background section and show them agreeing with Postgres. blocked-by: P-001 — note: Absorbed per D-010 by WI-40590 artifact /tmp/papercusp-p014-tauri-20260822T181809Z at network-backed c40fa85789; EI-21180067367832016 independently grades live-desktop healthy.\n- **P-007** `done` Acceptance rubric (`rubrics:propose` kind:acceptance, class `plan-class-bugfix`), graded by a non-implementer. blocked-by: P-006 — note: Absorbed per D-010 by terminal independent reviewer WI-40596 and canonical replacement-only scorecard EI-21180067367832016.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — D-001 Owner ruling: mimic the Work tab's Work Queue, not a server-side filter push\nDate: 2026-08-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-17, interactive] Asked to choose a scope, the owner answered verbatim: \"Mimic how it works in the work queue in the work tab.\" Route: this session (su-3387c6b6).\n\nThis SUPERSEDES the plan's original Phase-1 framing (push every filter into SQL). The reference implementation is apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/WorkItemsPanel.tsx. Its contract, read from the source:\n\n1. GROWING FETCH WINDOW. `WORK_ITEMS_PAGE = 500`; `const [limit, setLimit] = useState(PAGE)`; `hasMore = items.length < total`; `onEndReached={hasMore ? loadMore : undefined}` -> `setLimit(n => n + PAGE)`. The client converges on the WHOLE store, so a client-side filter is eventually corpus-wide.\n2. STORE TOTAL, NOT LOADED LENGTH. `total = readListTotal(items)` (row[0]._meta.total = the DB count).\n3. HONEST FILTER-AWARE LABEL. `workItemCountLabel(shown, total, filtered)`: filtered -> `N of total match`; unfiltered -> `total items`. Its own comment: \"There is no 'loaded of total' / capped distinction.\"\n4. STABLE ROWS SENTINEL. Module-level `const NO_ROWS: WorkItemRow[] = []`, passed as `items ?? NO_ROWS` — NEVER an inline `?? []`. Its comment: an inline literal breaks `filteredRows`/`optionsByKey`/`controller` memos, which is the WI-37386 Radix SlotClone ref-churn -> \"Maximum update depth exceeded\" class, and the same instability ran a real render loop in DepGraphPanel (WI-39552).\n5. MEMOIZED COLUMNS — `useMemo(() => buildWorkItemColumns(...), [trustedSet])`.\n6. ONE CONTROL PER AXIS — per-column filters in ONE nuqs param (`wif`) + a separate quick-search (`wq`) on top.\n7. VirtualGrid bounds DOM cost, not the fetch.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-002 — D-002 Page sizes stay payload-bound — copy the Work Queue's MECHANISM, not its 500\nDate: 2026-08-17\nMimicking the Work Queue does NOT mean setting every Learning read to `limit: 500`. Each read has its own measured payload ceiling, and copying the number rather than the mechanism would breach it:\n\n- learning.observations: MEASURED at 249,529 B for 200 rows against a 250,000 B budget = 99.8% of ceiling (WI-7303 header in learning-observations-read.ts), because `body` is 75.46% of the payload. OBSERVATIONS_PAGE stays 200.\n- learning.retainFeed: RETAIN_FEED_PAGE_SIZE = 24 with a built-in RETAIN_FEED_MAX_PAGE = 100 clamp. Rows are small (id/title/status/lens/meta), so this can rise toward 100 — the clamp is the ceiling, not 500.\n- learning.improvements: measured 320,607 B, ~98.6% of it a 454-row humanQueue; `limit` is clamped at 500.\n\nSo the portable part of the contract is items 1-6 of D-001 (growing window, store total, honest label, stable sentinel, memoized columns, one control per axis). The page SIZE is per-read and bounded by that read's own measurement. A change that raises a page size must cite a fresh payload measurement, not this decision.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-003 — D-003 Facet counts must be derived from the rows being filtered\nDate: 2026-08-17\nThe single behaviour that made the owner call the filters broken: a facet chip advertising a corpus-wide number over a list that cannot contain that many rows. Measured live — Improve's rail chip says `improvement 992`, clicking it yields `17 of 503`; Retain's tab badges say `Memories 544 / Recipes 2.8k` while the Kind filter offers only `recipe 13 / rubric 2 / runbook 1 / wi 8` and never offers `memory` or `plan` at all.\n\nThe Work Queue has no such split: every enum option's count comes from `deriveEnumOptions(rows, col)` over THE SAME rows the filter runs on, so an option's count is exactly how many rows it will leave behind. That is the invariant to adopt everywhere in the Learning tab:\n\n  A number rendered ON a filter control is a promise about what clicking it yields.\n\nA corpus-wide total may still be shown — but as the DENOMINATOR (the `N of total` label), never as the control's own count. Where a facet cannot honour the promise, either serve the rows it promises or stop printing the corpus number on the control.\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-004 — A bare `loading` branch is a defect — SyncQueryResult now exposes failureCount/failureReason\nDate: 2026-08-17\nDate: 2026-08-17\nRaised by the owner's second report [owner:Avi 2026-08-17, interactive]: \"in the retain tab, it just says 'loading retained items...' forever\".\n\nROOT CAUSE, read from the writer (not inferred): `usePollingQuery.ts:133` returns `loading: isLoading`, and TanStack v5 defines `isLoading = isPending && isFetching`. `queryClient.ts` sets NO `retry`, so v5's default applies: 3 retries with 1s/2s/4s backoff. Against `learning.retainFeed`'s hard 10s server-side timeout that is ~47 SECONDS during which `loading` is true and `error` is still null — so the error branch cannot fire and the pane shows an unchanging spinner. Nothing is stuck; the UI simply cannot say what is happening.\n\nWhy no consumer could have fixed this locally: `notifyOnChangeProps` (queryClient.ts) deliberately lists only data/error/isLoading/isFetching/isPlaceholderData. `failureCount`/`failureReason` were not observable AT ALL — a consumer reading them got a frozen zero, because an unlisted prop does not re-render.\n\nTHE RULING, adopted repo-wide, not just for Retain:\n\n1. `SyncQueryResult` now carries `failureCount: number` and `failureReason: Error | null` (libs/generic/sync). `failureReason` is populated in exactly the window where `error` is still null — i.e. while retries are in flight — which is the whole point.\n2. Both are listed in `notifyOnChangeProps`. queryClient.test.ts pins the list; that guard exists precisely so a prop read-but-unlisted cannot ship.\n3. A pane MUST NOT render a bare indefinite \"Loading…\" once `failureCount > 0`. Say that attempts are failing, name the reason, and offer a manual retry (waiting out a backoff is not an affordance).\n\nThis is the WI-6382 class one level deeper: WI-6382 stopped a data-layer FAILURE arriving as a calm empty; this stops a data-layer failure arriving as a calm SPINNER. Steps 2 and 4 (ObservationsPanel, ImproveGrid) inherit the rule — check their loading branches when you touch them.\n\nPinned by LearningTab.test.tsx \"a retrying retain load says so and offers a retry — a healthy one does not\", which asserts BOTH directions so a branch that always cries \"retrying\" fails too.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-005 — RETAIN_FEED_PAGE_SIZE 24 -> 75: the measurement D-002 requires, and why not 100\nDate: 2026-08-17\nDate: 2026-08-17\nD-002 requires that any page-size raise \"cite a fresh payload measurement, not this decision\". This is that measurement.\n\nMEASURED 2026-08-17 against :3170, WARM, three samples each, via `/api/zero-harness/rest-query?name=learning.retainFeed` (tab=all filter=all hive=papercusp):\n\n  limit=24  ->  8,861 B  ~0.61s   (the old default)\n  limit=50  -> 21,582 B  ~0.67s\n  limit=75  -> 31,186 B  ~0.73s   <- CHOSEN\n  limit=100 -> 45,830 B  ~1.02s   (the MAX_PAGE clamp)\n\nBYTES ARE NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT HERE, which is the part D-002 could not have known in advance: 31 KB is ~12% of the 250,000 B budget D-002 cites for learning.observations. Retain rows are small (id/title/status/lens/meta) exactly as D-002 predicted.\n\nLATENCY is the binding constraint, and it is superlinear for a structural reason: readRetainFeed runs FIVE legs and each fetches `limit` rows before the k-way merge discards all but `limit` of them. So limit=100 costs 500 fetched rows to deliver 100.\n\n75 is the measured knee: 3.1x the rows for +20% latency, where 100 costs +67% for 4.2x. It also keeps RETAIN_FEED_MAX_PAGE=100 a REAL ceiling rather than collapsing the default onto the clamp, which would leave the clamp expressing nothing.\n\nCONTEXT THAT MAKES THE LATENCY SIDE MATTER MORE THAN IT LOOKS: this same read intermittently crosses its 10s server-side timeout on a COLD path — reproduced on :3170, not only on the desktop sidecar (see the correction on WI-39675). Raising the page size raises cold-path cost too, so trading +67% latency for rows the growing cursor window already fetches on demand would have been the wrong trade.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-006 — D-006 filterCountLabel groups digits, at a PINNED locale — a shared-contract change all three panes inherit\nDate: 2026-08-17\nDate: 2026-08-17. Scope: this changes the SHARED helper, so WorkItemsPanel + RetainedLedgerCard + ObservationsPanel all inherit it. Recorded here rather than left in a diff because a later lane adopting filterCountLabel needs to know the contract includes grouping.\n\nWHAT. `filterCountLabel` now renders grouped digits (\"36,096\", \"1 of 36,096\") instead of raw (\"36096\"). The locale is PINNED to 'en-US' inside the helper rather than inherited from the host.\n\nWHY GROUPING. Step 2 adopts the shared label on Observations, whose corpus is ~36k rows. The hand-rolled label it replaces used toLocaleString, so adopting the shared helper unchanged would have shipped a legibility REGRESSION on the exact pane whose counts the owner called broken. The Work Queue never noticed because its totals are 2-4 digits.\n\nWHY A PINNED LOCALE. A bare toLocaleString() renders per the host's default locale, so the same assertion yields \"1,674\" here, \"1.674\" under de-DE and \"1 674\" under fr-FR. That makes every pinned count assertion a latent CI flake that appears only on a differently-configured box. Pinning inside the helper means callers cannot reintroduce the variance. Guarded by a test that states this reason (\"groups digits identically regardless of the host default locale\").\n\nBLAST RADIUS, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. Enumerated every consumer + pin before editing, rather than grepping for a name — the EI-20729641179961382 lesson from my own earlier gate red, where a grep-by-name missed a naked literal pin and went red in CI. Population: 3 consumers, 6 pure assertions in WorkItemsPanel.test.tsx (2 needed updating: 1821, 1674), 2 render assertions in ObservationsPanel.test.tsx. All updated in the same change; suites re-run green (WorkItemsPanel 15/15, LearningTab 88/88, ObservationsPanel 23/23).\n\nSIDE EFFECT WORTH KNOWING. Adopting the shared helper also RETIRES Observations' unfiltered \"N loaded / total\" form. That numerator reported how many rows happened to be downloaded — a function of scroll position, not an answer to any question — and read as a shortfall (\"200 / 36,096\") on a pane that was working correctly. Unfiltered now shows the store total alone, exactly as the Work Queue does (D-001).\n\n### D-007 — D-007 ImproveGrid gets the honest TOTAL, not the growing window — the window is payload-blocked and stays blocked until the humanQueue row is slimmed\nDate: 2026-08-17\nStep (4) of `## Now` says \"Add the growing window + store total\". Implementing it split cleanly in two, and only one half is available today. Recording this because it CHANGES what step (4) means, and a later reader would otherwise treat the missing window as an oversight and \"finish\" it into a payload regression.\n\nDONE — the store total (the half that fixes the reported lie):\n- `countImprovementItems` extended to support `loopOutputOnly` by resolving `deps.readLoopOutputIds()` into the SAME `issueIds` predicate `readBySelector` applies, so the count is taken over exactly the population the read returns (empty id set ⇒ 0, never an unscoped count; a missing dep still throws).\n- `computeLearningImprovementsSnapshot` now passes `corpusTotal` into `buildDigest`, propagating the EI-18790490225750395 D2 fix from the agent-tool path to the sync-resolver path, which had never received it.\n- LIVE (isolated rig, 2026-08-17): \"From the loop **1133**\" against a 500-row window. Pre-fix this read 500 — i.e. it printed the window size as the corpus, which is exactly the defect.\n\nNOT DONE — the growing window, and deliberately so. D-002 requires a fresh payload measurement before any page-size rise. Here is that measurement, and it REFUSES:\n- D-002 measured `learning.improvements` at 320,607 B, ~98.6% of it a 454-row humanQueue ⇒ ~696 B/row.\n- The live corpus is 1133 (measured above) against a 500 window. Converging the window on the corpus ⇒ ~1133 × 696 ≈ **789 KB**, ~3.2× the documented 250,000 B budget — re-sent on every SSE invalidation, on the transport the desktop actually ships.\n- So the growing window is not a UI change here; it is blocked on payload work. Note the row is ALREADY slimmed to a strict allowlist (WI-7279), so the cheap win is spent — the next lever is interning `tierReason` (WI-7278, ~15% of the remaining payload) or serving the list keyset-paged server-side rather than as one digest.\n\nConsequence for D-003 on this pane: rail-chip counts are derived from the loaded rows (done, verified live — chip `improvement 19` → clicking yields exactly `19 of 504 loaded`, against the plan's pre-fix measurement of `992` advertised / `17 of 503` delivered), and the corpus total appears only as a DENOMINATOR — in the count label's title (\"the list holds the most recent 500 of 1133 captured\") and in each chip's tooltip. That satisfies D-003's actual rule (\"a number rendered ON a filter control is a promise about what clicking it yields\"; a corpus total may still be shown, but as the denominator) WITHOUT the window.\n\nAlso NOT done, same reasoning: rendering `N of digest.total` as the list's own denominator. This list merges two populations — improvement items AND routed ideas not yet filed as work — while `digest.total` counts only the first. Printing it as the denominator of a mixed list would be a fresh instance of the very defect being fixed. The mixed-population denominator stays the LOADED count, explicitly labelled \"loaded\".\n\nFollow-up filed for the blocked half; it is payload work, not Learning-tab work.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-008 — D-008 The fresh measurement D-002 demanded: the growing window costs ~343 KB (1.37x), NOT 789 KB (3.2x) — and the slim that unblocks it is one already-filed lever\nDate: 2026-08-18\nSupersedes the NUMBERS in D-007 (and in WI-39773's title/summary), not its ruling. D-007's ruling stands: the window stays blocked until the humanQueue row is slimmed. What changes is the size of the gap and whether it is closable — it is, comfortably.\n\n#### Method (WI-39773)\nLive measurement against :3170 (staging), 2026-08-18 ~08:2xZ, via the sanctioned instrument's own route + metric: `GET /api/zero-harness/rest-query?name=learning.improvements&args=<json>`, `bytes = text.length` of the UNCOMPRESSED body (`accept-encoding: identity`), judged against `PAYLOAD_BUDGET_BYTES = 250_000` (sync-read-audit.ts:38). The route is `auth:'loopback'`, so no token is needed from localhost.\n\nCORROBORATED by an independent instrument: the scheduled `syncReads.audit` derived-read producer measured this same query IN-PROCESS at 259,366 B (2026-08-18T02:30:27Z). My REST reading was 259,087-259,217 B — a ~0.1% agreement, so the two paths are measuring the same object.\n\n#### Correction 1 — the wire never carries the corpus\nD-007 projected `1133 corpus x 696 B/row`. It cannot: `digest.ts:710` is `if (!isOpen) continue` — ONLY OPEN items enter humanQueue. Measured on the live corpus: total 1142, of which open **623**, resolved 49, closed 100 (the balance sits in other states). So the growing window's row count converges on ~623, not 1142.\n\n#### Correction 2 — per-row cost has fallen\nMeasured 545 B/row over 500 open rows (272,705 B), not 696 B/row. WI-7279's allowlist is holding.\n\n#### Correction 3 — the resulting projection\n623 rows x 545 B + 3,592 B non-queue overhead = **~343,400 B, ~1.37x budget** — not ~789 KB / ~3.2x. Still over, so D-007's refusal was CORRECT; it was over by 37%, not 220%.\n\n⚠ This is a PROJECTION, and deliberately labelled one: `limit: clampedLimitOpt(500)` (sync-resolver/index.ts:3696) clamps the arg, so the full window is UNOBSERVABLE today. Positive control that the arg is otherwise honoured: `{limit:50}` returns 50 items, while `{limit:500|750|1500}` all return exactly 500. The projection multiplies a MEASURED per-row cost by a MEASURED unbounded COUNT (`{state:'open'}` returns total 623 while its own window saturates at 500).\n\n#### The blocker is a schema clamp, not only a budget\nAdopting the growing window requires raising `clampedLimitOpt(500)` as well as slimming the row. D-007 named only the payload half.\n\n#### The slim is measured, and one lever exceeds it\nRequired cut to fit 623 rows in 250,000 B: 545 -> 396 B/row = **27.5%**. Measured per-field composition of the humanQueue row (500 open rows):\n- `title` 37.9% (207 B/row) — rendered, not cuttable\n- **`tierReason` 30.6% (167 B/row), SIX distinct values across 500 rows**\n- `scope` 5.1%, `id` 5.1%, `ideaType` 4.1%, `severity` 3.5%, `kind` 2.9%, `source` 2.9%, `state` 2.8%, `ageDays` 2.7%, `score` 2.0%\n\n`tierReason` ALONE (30.6%) exceeds the required 27.5%. WI-7278 already owns this lever but carries stale numbers from the same drifted source — it says \"15% of the payload across only FOUR distinct strings ... 453x\"; measured today it is **30.6%, SIX distinct strings, 500x**. Interning is safe: `tierReason` is never rendered (LearningTab.tsx:2724 records its removal from the row title) and survives only as quick-search haystack input (LearningTab.tsx:1744), so a 6-entry legend expanded client-side before the haystack is built preserves search exactly.\n\nGoing further is cheap if wanted: seven low-cardinality fields (tierReason, scope, ideaType, severity, kind, source, state — each <=6 distinct values) are together 283 B/row = 52% of the row. Dictionary-encoding all seven lands ~318 B/row => ~202 KB at full window, leaving real headroom for corpus growth. tierReason alone lands ~386 B/row => ~245 KB, which fits but with only ~2% headroom and would re-breach at roughly 638 open items.\n\n#### Disposition\nWI-39773's acceptance offered (a) it fits, adopt the window, or (b) record that it stays windowed permanently. The honest answer is NEITHER: it does not fit today, but (b) would be wrong — the gap is 27.5% and a single already-filed, never-started lever is worth 30.6%. So the window stays blocked, the blocker is now a bounded and costed row-slim (WI-7278), and this feed is ALSO already 259,087 B / 1.04x over budget and unallowlisted TODAY at the current 500-row window, independent of any window change.\n\n### D-009 — D-009 The row-slim D-007 required is SHIPPED and re-measured (259,087 → 187,517 B) — but the growing window still must NOT be adopted, on 13 rows of headroom\nDate: 2026-08-18\nFollow-on to D-008, same item (WI-39773). D-008 measured the gap and named the lever; this landed it and re-measured. Same instrument, same route, same metric, so BEFORE/AFTER are directly comparable.\n\n#### What shipped\n`tierReason` now ships INTERNED: a short `trc` code per humanQueue row plus a per-payload `tierReasonLegend`. It is NOT dropped — it was never rendered but IS the quick-search haystack input (LearningTab.tsx:1744), so dropping it would silently return fewer hits with no error. The client expands the legend before building the haystack. Contract lives in a new no-import leaf `harness/improvements/learning-digest-wire.ts` (the browser needs the reader; it must not pull the server compute module's dynamic-import graph to get it). Producer bumped v3 → v4 on BOTH `learning.improvements` and `learning.improvements.hive`.\n\n#### Measured on :3170 after restart\n| | before | after |\n|---|---|---|\n| payload at the current 500-row window | 259,087 B (1.04x) | **187,517 B (0.75x)** |\n| per humanQueue row | 545 B | **386 B** |\n| full-window projection (623 open rows) | 343,382 B (1.37x) | **244,755 B (0.98x)** |\n\n−71,570 B, **−27.6%**. Verified lossless on the wire: `rowsWithRawTierReason: 0`, every row carries a `trc`, `legendLen: 6` — matching the six distinct values D-008 measured. The standing budget breach at today's window is GONE.\n\n#### ⚠ THE WINDOW STILL SHOULD NOT BE ADOPTED — read the headroom, not the verdict\n`fitsFullWindow: true` is technically satisfied, and taken alone it would authorise D-001 item 1. It should not. The margin is **13 rows**: at 386 B/row the budget is exhausted at 636 open items and there are 623 today. This workspace captures continuously, so that is hours-to-days of headroom, and a growing window adopted on it would re-breach almost immediately — the same \"the breach is pure ROW GROWTH, and the next one is a windowing trigger, not another raise\" pattern the sync-read allowlist records for plans.list, coord.plans and featuresConsolidated.\n\nAdopting also needs a SECOND change D-007 never named: `limit: clampedLimitOpt(500)` (sync-resolver/index.ts:3696) CLAMPS the arg, so no client can request more than 500 rows regardless of payload (D-008's positive control: `{limit:50}` → 50 rows; `{limit:500|750|1500}` → exactly 500).\n\n**So D-007's ruling still stands and the item stays open.** For durable headroom the next lever is already measured in D-008: the six remaining low-cardinality fields (scope, ideaType, severity, kind, source, state — each ≤6 distinct values) are ~116 B/row more, landing ~318 B/row ≈ 202 KB with ~30% headroom. The alternative is keyset-paging the list server-side (D-007 lever 2), which is the only option whose cost does not grow with the corpus at all.\n\n#### A defect this surfaced, fixed here\nBumping the producer version exposed that the resolver's DEFAULT branch read its snapshot through `readDerivedSnapshotRows`, which flattens a MISS to `[]`. So invalidating the stored rows made the Learning tab's LANDING view serve an EMPTY digest — a wrong answer wearing an empty answer's clothes — until the producer next ran. Observed live on :3170: blank immediately after the restart, populated ~2 min later. It self-heals (a background fill is kicked) but recurs on EVERY future producerVersion bump and on any cold key.\n\nThe sibling HIVE branch already handled this correctly and its comment explains exactly why; the default branch never inherited it. It now falls through to the live compute on a miss, preserving the `_meta.derivedRead` stamp the panel renders \"as of HH:MM\" from. Guarded by `learning-improvements-snapshot-miss.test.ts`, whose control also pins that a HIT still serves the snapshot — without that, the guard would pass on a resolver that had stopped using the snapshot entirely and silently restored the 0.4-0.5s inline compute on every mount.\n\n#### Verification\n18/18 on the two resolver suites, 120/120 on the Learning-tab client suites, 12/12 on the settle-coverage + perf-begin-order guards, `lint:tsc` operator-core exit=0 clean. Both new guards MUTATION-PROVEN (`scripts/mutation-probe.sh --in-tree --sweep-lock-held`, git-sync lock held then released, tree byte-identical after each): breaking the legend dedupe → `verdict=caught` (failed at the 2-vs-4 assertion); reverting the snapshot-miss fall-through to `[]` → `verdict=caught`.\n\n### D-010 — D-010 The growing window is refuted by ARITHMETIC, not opinion: the open set accretes ~19/day, so every client-side-window lever has an expiry date — and the 500 clamp is the GUARD, not the obstacle\nDate: 2026-08-18\nD-009 left one open question: which durable-headroom lever to spend (six-field encode vs keyset paging). The answer is NEITHER, and the deciding input is a number nobody in D-002/D-007/D-008/D-009 had measured — the rate the corpus GROWS.\n\n#### The measurement (live :3170, 2026-08-18 ~09:5xZ, the digest's own `flow` block)\ncaptured7d=156, resolved7d=24, **net7d=132** (self-consistent: 156-24=132). The learning loop captures 6.5x faster than it resolves, so the OPEN set accretes **~18.9 rows/day** and is monotonically increasing. medianOpenAgeDays=16.\n\n#### Both levers, dated\nModel (reproduces D-009's own 13-row figure exactly, so it is the same model): overhead = 244,755 - 623x386 = **4,277 B**; capacity = (250,000 - 4,277) / perRow.\n| lever | per-row | capacity | headroom | **expires in** |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| today (post-intern) | 386 B | 636 rows | 13 rows | **~0.7 days** |\n| + six-field encode | 317 B | 774 rows | 151 rows | **~8.0 days** |\n\nA change touching six RENDERED fields (scope, ideaType, severity, kind, source, state) at every read site — decode at each — buys **eight days**. That is a mitigation with a measured expiry date, not a fix.\n\n#### This is the repo's own recorded convention, not a new opinion\nSYNC_READ_ALLOWLIST's `coord.plans` entry (WI-7256) already settled this exact class, with the same arithmetic shape: \"authored plans accrue at ~45-50/week ... expected back at the 390,000 ceiling within ~3-4 days ... **THAT RED IS THE WINDOWING TRIGGER — NOT ANOTHER RAISE**\". Its `workItems.byHarness` neighbour says the same: \"The residual IS the grid page x those light fields — **row count, not per-row waste**.\"\nlearning.improvements is that class exactly: per-row was already cut 545 -> 386 and the breach came back. **The breach is pure ROW GROWTH.** A growing window is *un*-windowing — it is the opposite of what this convention prescribes.\n\n#### The inversion that matters: the clamp is the GUARD\nD-009 listed `limit: clampedLimitOpt(500)` (sync-resolver/index.ts:3696) as adoption requirement #2 — an obstacle to remove. That is backwards. The clamp is **the only thing bounding this payload**: it is why the read sits at a stable 187,517 B (0.75x) today and why it will NOT re-breach as the corpus grows. Raising it removes the guard; adopting the growing window removes it by definition. Nothing else in this read is bounded.\n\n#### Ruling\n1. **Do NOT adopt the growing window** for ImproveGrid. Not \"not yet on 13 rows of headroom\" (D-009's framing) — not at any headroom, because the population grows without bound and no per-row cut changes that.\n2. **Do NOT spend the six-field encode.** 8 days of headroom does not justify decode-at-every-render-site, and it would need unpicking when windowing lands. The tierReason intern was worth it (30.6% of payload, ZERO render sites); this is the opposite trade.\n3. **Keep the 500 clamp.** It is load-bearing. Any future proposal to raise it must carry a fresh net-accretion measurement.\n4. ImproveGrid keeps the honest bounded window + honest totals already shipped under D-007/D-003 (\"the list holds the most recent 500 of 1133 captured\", verified live).\n\n#### ⚠ This refutes D-001's PREMISE and needs the owner\nD-001 is an OWNER ruling: \"mimic the Work tab's Work Queue, not a server-side filter push.\" It was made before any accretion measurement existed. Two facts now bear on it:\n- The Work Queue is **the same unbounded design** (WORK_ITEMS_PAGE=500, `setLimit(n => n + PAGE)`, whole-window REFETCH — WorkItemsPanel.tsx:22/109/139). Mimicking it faithfully inherits the same countdown; its own allowlist entry concedes the residual is row count.\n- Corpus-wide filtering over a corpus that grows ~19/day is only reachable server-side — the thing D-001 ruled out.\nSo \"filters see the whole corpus\" and \"no server-side filter push\" are **not jointly satisfiable at this accretion rate**. That is a product-direction fork above an agent's authority to reverse: recorded here, surfaced to the owner, and NOT worked around by cleverness. Note learning.retainFeed already solved it the other way and says why (learning-retain-read.ts:275-278: a filter must compose with the cursor, because \"a client-side filter over a paged feed drops rows unpredictably\").\n\n#### Correction to D-009's own numbers\nD-009 states the encode saves \"~116 B/row -> ~318 B/row\". Those disagree: 386-318 = **68.6**, not 116. The 318 B/row and ~202 KB pair IS self-consistent (317.4 B/row implied); the 116 is stale — a fourth wrong carried number in this item's lineage, and the reason every figure above is stated with the instrument that produced it.\nRelated: P-002, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-011 — D-011 ImproveGrid uses bounded server-side filters, not an unbounded growing window\nDate: 2026-08-20\nDate: 2026-08-20\\n\\nD-010's bounded route is now explicit for ImproveGrid. At current staging HEAD b3ab3372b8, `apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/LearningTab.tsx` mounts `learning.improvements` without filter args, then applies `useColumnFilters` and `impq` over the digest's client payload; `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts` accepts only state/limit/hive/scope and clamps limit at 500. The loaded window cannot make corpus-wide filters honest, and D-010 rejects growing-window expansion because the open set grows ~18.9/day and the 500 clamp is load-bearing.\\n\\nDecision: extend the existing `learning.improvements` resolver/read seam with the ImproveGrid's filter/search inputs and return a bounded, filter-conditioned result plus the total needed by the UI. Keep the existing 500 clamp and snapshot default fast path unchanged; non-default filter variants may use the live bounded compute. Derive facet counts from the filtered result they describe, and keep the client filter controls as the presentation/state layer rather than fetching the corpus. Add focused resolver and LearningTab tests that prove the filter reaches the server, remains bounded, and cannot advertise rows outside the returned population. This supersedes D-001's growing-window approach for ImproveGrid only; it does not change Retain or ObservationsPanel work.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"oddsmith-recovery-and-hardening-2026-08-16-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: oddsmith recovery + hardening after the 2026-08-15 wipe","status":"active","created":"2026-08-17","owner":"su-a787d98c-af0d-4be1-9680-051b627d67d4","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: oddsmith recovery + hardening after the 2026-08-15 wipe\nslug: oddsmith-recovery-and-hardening-2026-08-16-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-08-17\nowner: su-a787d98c-af0d-4be1-9680-051b627d67d4\n---\n\n# Acceptance: oddsmith recovery + hardening after the 2026-08-15 wipe\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nAuthored post-implementation (D-007) against the as-built work. The plan exists because on 2026-08-15 ~/.oddsmith was destroyed and the embedded Postgres could not be restored: it was in NEITHER backup path (wrong cluster for the pg_dump leg, and ~/.oddsmith was not a kopia source). Every row of simulation and evidence history was lost permanently. Two independent blind spots met on one database, and nothing alarmed. So these criteria deliberately grade OUTCOMES — is that database recoverable, and would a silent regression be caught — not whether specific files were edited. A grader should be able to fail this rubric while every plan item still reads done. NOTE FOR THE GRADER: I implemented and audited this plan, so I cannot grade it. One criterion (stalled-cadence-externally-visible) has a known unresolved caveat recorded on the P-003 audit note; please treat it as an open question to test rather than a settled pass.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"rem-dream-recombination-2026-08-17","title":"Code-capability dreaming — researched recombination and falsifiable experiments","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-17","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Code-capability dreaming — researched recombination and falsifiable experiments\nslug: rem-dream-recombination-2026-08-17\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-17\nupdated: 2026-10-16\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** D027 fleet route active; WI-6554700010016098 reconciled original owner turns and frozen evidence in D028. Human labels an… <!-- P-024 -->\n## Background\n\nAvi's September 6 request redirects dreaming from a large conversation-history corpus toward random combinations of existing code. A function is often too small to expose a useful behavior; a whole framework often contains too many unrelated behaviors. The default unit here is a capability: a coherent externally observable behavior together with the code, contracts and tests that implement it.\n\nThe objective is to discover useful compositions, transferable mechanisms or guarantees, missing integrations, and incompatible assumptions across capabilities. The main failure modes are forced associations, stale or incomplete summaries, rediscovering existing integrations, and ideas that sound novel but fail when implemented. The REM label is a metaphor; this plan does not claim biological sleep validates the algorithm.\n\nThe research below supports structural analogy, facet representations, explicit prior-art comparison, diversity measurement and executable evaluation. Applying those findings to this repository remains an engineering hypothesis. The original 50/30/20 sampling split and occasional third unit are starting settings to compare, not established optima.\n\nSource conversation: Codex session `01a078d8-d0f9-7e23-ae5b-8097ea05cead`, agent `su-8565dbc4-1798-4530-910c-8ee524dc5339`, September 6, 2026, 18:34–18:45 EDT. Owner request: `session_turn:codex:01a078d8-d0f9-7e23-ae5b-8097ea05cead:1`; recommendation: turns 6–7. The current owner request supplies turn 7 verbatim and asks for online research, a written plan and a summary. Indexed turn 1 and turns 2–6 were read in full after sessions:read failed; the exact-quote search resolved the session. Earlier August constraints are preserved from the full current plan and D-001–D-008; their source conversations must also be audited before activation.\n\nHistorical context retained: the earlier design sampled distilled observations, completed work, memories and statistics, and already had a dream pass, independent review and Blender sink. P-001–P-004 describe that completed foundation. Historical convergence and acceptance-rate figures in the earlier draft are not reused as current measurements.\n\nOut of scope for this revision: whole-conversation sampling as the primary substrate; four-or-more-unit combinations; training a new code model; a second idea database or autonomous implementation pipeline; a new dedicated reviewer fleet; biological sleep-pressure/forgetting schedules. These are not prerequisites for the proposed pilot.\n\n## Open questions (owner input wanted — each with the proposed default)\n\nThe following are disclosed design defaults for review, not blockers to producing this draft.\n\n- Substrate: capability packets from current code; observations, memories and statistics may supply a grounded constraint or evaluation context but do not replace the primary code units.\n- Granularity: capability×capability and capability×mechanism by default. Subsystem combinations are occasional, tagged exploration and must still identify concrete behaviors. Functions appear as evidence inside packets.\n- Arity/sampling: two primary units; optional third on an initial 20% of exploratory attempts. Initial partner mixture: 50% cross-domain structural match, 30% uniform cross-domain, 20% another branch in the same domain. Compare these choices experimentally before tuning.\n- UI placement: controls in Learning, cycle and proposal evidence in Analyze/Dreams, accepted proposals in existing Ideas views. Preserve the meaning of Observations as readings from real work.\n- Models: use the existing configurable model-runner and governor. Select the least costly generator that passes the packet/task benchmark; keep independent reviewer context and the existing different-model guard. No model/provider choice is established by the cited papers.\n- Rollout and spend: manual first; automatic mode remains separately default OFF. The Evaluation protocol specifies a bounded proposed pilot and an inconclusive result when its limits prevent adequate evidence.\n- Reviewer responsibility: use existing Dream review and Blender triage ownership. Re-resolve live responsibility when a proposal is handed off; the September 6 steward-liveness snapshot is not a permanent assignment.\n- After the pilot: retain, simplify, expand or stop based on unique verified useful proposals and executed outcomes per cost, with uncertainty reported. Owner approval of this draft is separate from approving any generated plan.\n\n## Phase 0 — existing fragment-engine foundation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Fragment sampler: stratified draw over indexed high-signal strata (session turns, decisions, completions-with-evidence, escalations, observations, memories per Q1), pairing one RECENT fragment (~48h, salience-weighted) with one REMOTE fragment; embedding mid-band distance filter (too-close = trivially related, too-far = incoherent); excludes low-signal turn types (tool spam). Pure module + unit tests over a fixture corpus. — note: ← WI-40121 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Dream pass: one bounded cheap-model call per dream — 2–3 fragments, \"produce at most ONE operationally useful insight that requires BOTH fragments (cite what each contributes), or answer NONE\"; abstention is a first-class parsed outcome; malformed output rejected. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40123 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Review gate: independent grader call (grader ≠ dreamer, per Q3): juxtaposition-dependence test first, then actionability/falsifiability, then novelty vs. corpus (embedding dedupe against blender corpus + memories); reject-by-default calibration. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-40127 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Sink: accepted insights land in the blender corpus as idea rows with origin='dream' + provenance refs to the source fragments; they enter the existing blender grade/route/outcome machinery unchanged (reuse-first — no parallel pipeline). — note: ← WI-40133 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — capability packets, sampling and review\n\n- **P-011** `done` Capability contracts and seed catalog. Define stable domain/capability/mechanism IDs and a versioned packet schema with purpose, mechanism, evaluation, inputs/outputs/events/state, guarantees, constraints, implementation/test refs, source hashes and extraction provenance. Derive domain links from the existing testing registry and package/docs anchors; start with a small reviewed cross-domain catalog and document unmapped regions. Capability boundaries follow observable behavior, may span files, and record overlap/parentage. Acceptance: schema fixtures reject unsupported claims/missing required provenance; every pilot unit resolves its implementation and meaningful tests; no complete-coverage claim from test globs alone. Research R1–R3/R9; D-009. — note: ← WI-10000483 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Build bounded capability packets and an incremental cache using existing code-intelligence facades and code:pack. Resolve symbols, caller/callee radius and tests; preserve source excerpts plus purpose/mechanism/evaluation facets. Hash actual file bytes, contracts, extraction recipe and prompt versions; record dirty state and coverage/truncation. Revalidate cited sources before review/admission; refresh changed packets without re-embedding unchanged ones. Use verified LSP/ripgrep fallback when graph health is unknown; absence of an edge never proves no integration. Acceptance: edit/rename/delete and dirty-tree fixtures invalidate correctly, packet budgets preserve contracts, and secrets/untrusted-instruction fixtures fail safely. D-009. blocked-by: P-011 — note: ← WI-10000484 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Hierarchy-aware, reproducible pair/triple sampler. Choose domains before units with bounded underexploration weighting; mix structural cross-domain, uniform cross-domain and same-domain/different-branch strategies (initial 50/30/20 settings). Two primary units are required; optional C has constraint/consumer/enabling-mechanism role (initial 20% setting). Preserve pure-random control, eligibility/probability/seed logging, unordered content-version pair cooldown with transfer direction retained, sparse-domain fallback and no-pair outcome. Capability×capability and capability×mechanism are primary recipes; subsystem-level experiments are explicitly tagged; >=4 units deferred.
