Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nGrades the OUTCOMES this plan promised: a consult router that (1) revives the best-qualified DEAD expert rather than silently under-filling — at creation AND at refill exhaustion, (2) refuses to die under-answered while untried above-floor candidates exist, and says WHY when it must, (3) never lies about how a consult ended, and (4) is actually reachable — from the su seed and from orient's peers-know fold — without ever degrading the surfaces it rides on.\n\n⚠ GRADER: where a criterion carries a structured check, a green run is NECESSARY, NEVER SUFFICIENT — each method names what the check cannot see. c3 carries LIVE archival evidence already on record (consult conv-msz1r23x-0000-6b5543124b5046fa9566c8900721c3d0: expired after 3 substantive PASS answers, and attestation EI-20823207556229226 was accepted citing it) — verify that record rather than re-deriving it. The honesty invariant of the underlying router (below-floor ⇒ 'no one knows more than you do', never a costumed expert) is load-bearing background for c1/c2: neither leg may widen selection past the relevance floor to satisfy its guarantee. Vetted via consult conv-mszpqo7t (2 reviewers, both FAIL-as-written verdicts incorporated: F1/F2 refill-exhaustion revival + persisted budget — fixed in code as EI-20864690354207496 and pinned by c2's probes; F6 c1 trigger semantics corrected to the WI-39852 owner ruling; F3 c3 structured checks; F4 c4 outcome-grading; F5 real-path check bindings).\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-goal-dag-shared-substrate-2026-08-18","title":"Acceptance — goals join the shared work-queue DAG substrate (readiness, not dispatch)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-19","owner":"su-7a287117-8c3e-4b4f-92d7-453b386b56fd","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — goals join the shared work-queue DAG substrate (readiness, not dispatch)\nslug: acceptance-goal-dag-shared-substrate-2026-08-18\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-19\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-7a287117-8c3e-4b4f-92d7-453b386b56fd\n---\n\n# Acceptance — goals join the shared work-queue DAG substrate (readiness, not dispatch)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nGrades the OUTCOMES this plan promised, not the diff it produced. The plan's goal has TWO halves — stop a ~20GB idle llama-server pinning the GPU, automatically, AND do it without making local inference unreliable — and both halves are graded here. Its hardest-won rulings (D-012, D-013/D-014) are both instances of one failure — a liveness signal taken from a stand-in that survives the failure it is meant to report — so a criterion for that is included even though no single line of the diff implements it.\n\n⚠ GRADER: c2 (reclaim-invisible-to-callers) deliberately names NO test file as sufficient evidence. This plan produced 8 green, typechecked unit tests for a cold-start path that was NON-FUNCTIONAL in production; every one manufactured its precondition with an injected dependency the real system could not reach. Grading c2 from a passing test suite would repeat exactly the error this plan exists to have learned. Require the live evidence named in its method.\n\n⚠ GRADER: where a criterion carries a structured `check`, a green run is NECESSARY, NEVER SUFFICIENT. The check proves the named tests pass; it does not prove the criterion's claim. c7 in particular carries a check that covers only its FIRST clause — read its method for the partition.\n\n⚠ GRADER: c6 grades PROCESS (the authoring agent's claim hygiene), not system behaviour. It is not commensurable with c1–c5 and c7 — do not average it against them or let a strong c6 offset a weak functional criterion.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend the existing durable substrate merge-cursor schema/store with nullable peer identity and explicit lifecycle state, including an additive migration and store-level recurrence tests. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40001 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Wire the existing boot admission, revocation, unrevocation, and admitted-set change paths to persist log-key ↔ device identity plus active/retired lifecycle without erasing unknown historical cursors. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40013 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Update the shared-pot peer-silence monitor input/judge to exclude only explicitly retired cursors while preserving alerts for unknown or unexpectedly unannounced peers; add detector regression tests for active, retired, and unknown cases. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40017 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Run scoped schema/store/boot/monitor tests, operator-core typecheck, and live papercusp cursor/admission verification; record whether the four historical keys remain unknown versus explicitly retired and close EI-209528 with bounded evidence. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-40020 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Reuse canonical cursor, admission, and revocation surfaces; unknown remains alertable\nDate: 2026-08-20\nPer shared-hive-federation-2026-06-08 D-003/D-004, extend the existing peer-log, substrate_merge_cursor, and per-Hive admission/revocation machinery. Do not introduce a parallel peer registry or infer retirement from silence. Only an explicit durable lifecycle writer may mark a cursor retired and remove it from the absence population; cursors with no durable identity/lifecycle evidence remain unknown/unadmitted and continue to trigger PEERS ABSENT. This preserves WI-39489's operational-safety ruling while making intentional revocation/retirement distinguishable after restart.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"goal-mode-design-intent-hardening-acceptance","title":"Goal-mode design-intent hardening — shipped outcomes","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-20","owner":"su-a79eb6a4-c513-4c40-8641-c2255811d326","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Goal-mode design-intent hardening — shipped outcomes\nslug: goal-mode-design-intent-hardening-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-20\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-a79eb6a4-c513-4c40-8641-c2255811d326\n---\n\n# Goal-mode design-intent hardening — shipped outcomes\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"official-mobile-app-templates-2026-08-20","title":"Papercusp Official Android and iPhone app templates","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-20","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercusp Official Android and iPhone app templates\nslug: official-mobile-app-templates-2026-08-20\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-20\nupdated: 2026-09-24\n---\n\n# Papercusp Official Android and iPhone app templates\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE, SHIP BLOCKED AT THE RUBRIC RUNG. All 20 plan items are terminal (20 done, 0 dropped) — including P-018, P-019 and P-021, which the previous ## Now still described as wip/todo. Both platforms were materialized through the REAL templates:new-app flow and carried to install+launch evidence: Android `stonebrook-android-20260821` (\"Stonebrook Ledger\", WI-40367, closed by su-8da46cd0 at completionAuthority=committed on a minified RELEASE APK — installs, cold-launches, stays resumed, and visibly renders live Rust-core output) and iPhone `thornbury-iphone-20260821` (\"Thornbury\", WI-40368, done). Plan status has been `awaiting-acceptance` since 2026-08-28.\n\nVERIFIED 2026-09-24 by su-2590ac9b (read-only): 20/20 items terminal; frontmatter status `awaiting-acceptance`; `rubrics:list { subjectPlan }` returns ZERO rubrics; `coord:roster { view:'live' }` returns ZERO live agents workspace-wide (the mobile-greenfield-build fleet and both of its leaders are gone). Every per-clause claim in the previous ## Now (12 decision points, 0.1.0 pins, checks union, no committed secrets) is INHERITED from the August lanes and was NOT re-verified in that pass.\n\nKNOWN OPEN DEFECT from the Android lane: WI-40435 (major, open, unassigned) — 16KB-page emulator images (sdk_gphone16k_x86_64) cannot resolve ANY third-party launcher activity; install succeeds and `am start` returns START_CLASS_NOT_FOUND (-92) with no crash. It is an environment defect, not app breakage — the byte-identical APK launches on a standard-page AVD, which is how WI-40367 was closed.\n\n**Next:** SHIP IS BLOCKED AT STEP 3 OF THE ACCEPTANCE GATE, NOT ON IMPLEMENTATION — no acceptance rubric has ever been authored for this plan, so `plans:set-plan-status { status:'shipped' }` cannot recruit a grader (recruitment fires only on `acceptance_ungraded` / `self_graded_only`; with no rubric the refusal is `acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready`, whose repairs belong to the author). The remaining ladder: (1) per-item `plans:audit` code-truth over all 20 items, (2) `rubrics:propose { kind:'acceptance', subjectPlan }` with 3-7 OUTCOME criteria authored against as-built reality, (3) vet via `consult:get_feedback { policy:'rubric-vetting' }` then attest with `scorecards:emit` against meta-acceptance-rubric, (4) a NON-implementer grades it, (5) an implementer records the acceptance verdict, (6) `plans:set-plan-status { status:'shipped' }`.\n\nWHO SHOULD DO IT: not su-2590ac9b. That session implemented a single Android greenfield lane and has no basis to author outcome criteria for the earlier phases, the iPhone shell, the listings/storefront work, or the PUBLIC RELEASE work — authoring them would manufacture acceptance evidence for work it cannot verify, and the release surface is outward-facing. This needs an owner decision or a fresh lead with scope over the whole plan.\n\n## Relationship to existing programs\n\nThis is a distinct expansion of `app-templates-2026-07-04`, not a replacement for or replay of it. That plan established the generic template substrate, thin app roots, aspect composition, portable checks, storefront, mirror, and gym; this plan reuses those shipped mechanisms to add a new mobile family and migrate two independent reference consumers. It also consumes the `mobile-app-release-readiness` rubric for acceptance evidence but does not duplicate product release work.\n\n## Outcome\n\nShip two first-party storefront entries:\n\n- `papercusp-android-app` — **Papercusp Official: Android App**\n- `papercusp-iphone-app` — **Papercusp Official: iPhone App**\n\nBoth roots must require the same `papercusp-mobile-base` aspect and their respective platform shell aspect. The current Papercusp and SideStage Android/iPhone applications remain product-specific reference consumers and must all pass the shared template contract.\n\n## Evidence and starting point\n\n- `/home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup-rust-mobile` and `/home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/sidestage-mobile` both use a Rust workspace with core/bindings/CLI crates, UniFFI-generated Kotlin and Swift bindings, Jetpack Compose, SwiftUI, Gradle/cargo-ndk, XcodeGen/XCFramework builds, DTCG-style design-token sources, and store-release scripts.\n- The Papercusp app is the richer production/reference implementation for push, biometrics, deep links, voice, privacy declarations, signing, store metadata, and mature release verification.\n- The SideStage app is the cleaner second implementation for scaffold verification, generated-binding build integration, host-side UniFFI smoke tests, media/WebRTC seams, and smaller product-independent build scripts.\n- Existing official app templates in `templates/` are thin app roots whose `requires` closure pulls aspect templates; correctness comes from the union of portable checks. The mobile templates should extend that system, not introduce a parallel scaffold engine.\n\n## Proposed composition\n\n```text\npapercusp-android-app (scope: app)\n├── papercusp-mobile-base (scope: aspect)\n└── papercusp-android-shell (scope: aspect)\n\npapercusp-iphone-app (scope: app)\n├── papercusp-mobile-base (the exact same aspect)\n└── papercusp-iphone-shell (scope: aspect)\n```\n\n### `papercusp-mobile-base`\n\nOwns only cross-platform invariants:\n\n- Rust workspace layout: domain core, UniFFI bindings, and host-side CLI/smoke target.\n- The rule that business/network/realtime/cache logic lives in Rust and native UI shells call a narrow binding facade.\n- Binding generation and ABI/checksum compatibility contracts.\n- Shared design-token source and drift contract, while generated Kotlin/Swift outputs remain platform-owned.\n- Common endpoint/auth/error/storage interfaces and a no-secrets-in-source policy.\n- Shared host checks: format, clippy, Rust tests, wire-contract tests, UniFFI smoke, scaffold-shape and placeholder-leak guards.\n- Decision points for app identity, license, domain API, authentication, local persistence, realtime transport, telemetry, capability set, and brand tokens.\n\nIt does not own product screens, product API types, Papercusp operator behavior, SideStage commerce behavior, signing credentials, app-store accounts, or a cross-platform widget toolkit.\n\n### `papercusp-android-shell`\n\nOwns the Android-specific chassis: Kotlin/Compose entrypoint, Gradle/AGP/Kotlin pins, cargo-ndk ABI matrix, lifecycle and secure-storage seams, deep-link/push/biometric capability hooks, package/application identity parameters, lint/unit/instrumentation checks, APK/AAB signing inputs, 16 KB alignment, and provenance verification.\n\n### `papercusp-iphone-shell`\n\nOwns the iPhone-specific chassis: SwiftUI entrypoint, XcodeGen project, UniFFI XCFramework packaging, lifecycle/Keychain/deep-link/push/biometric capability hooks, bundle/team/deployment-target parameters, privacy manifest and entitlement inputs, XCTest/XCUITest checks, and archive/export/TestFlight preflight.\n\n### Thin app roots\n\nThe two app-scope templates contain decision ordering, guidance, and composition-integrity checks only. They add no product component of their own. Each root hard-requires `papercusp-mobile-base` plus its platform shell and must pass the union of the closure's checks.\n\n## Parameter and safety contract\n\nA freshly materialized app must require explicit or generated values for display name, app slug, Rust crate/module prefix, reverse-DNS application/bundle id, API base URL, URL scheme/universal-link domain, license, minimum OS level, brand assets/tokens, and optional platform capabilities. Signing team IDs, keystores, provisioning profiles, service-account files, DSNs, API keys, and store credentials stay outside the repository. Optional services must compile as no-ops until configured.\n\nA template guard must reject leaked source-product values, including Papercusp/SideStage package ids, endpoints, buyer/device ids, app icons, signing metadata, Firebase files, voice keys, and store copy.\n\n## Scope boundaries\n\nIn scope:\n\n- Five new official template directories: the shared base aspect, two platform shell aspects, and two app roots.\n- Template-kit reference manifests, catalog/composition pins, portable checks, listings, GUIDE files, reference evidence, docs, storefront discovery, materialization, mirror distribution, and gym coverage.\n- Conformance work in both existing mobile repositories so Papercusp Android/iPhone and SideStage Android/iPhone are reference consumers of the same contract.\n- Greenfield materialization and native build proof on Linux/Android and macOS/iPhone.\n\nOut of scope:\n\n- Rewriting product features or forcing product API models into a shared library.\n- A generic cross-platform widget framework.\n- An agentic-mobile app root; it can later layer onto these roots if a real consumer requires it.\n- Publishing to Play Store/App Store or storing production signing credentials.\n- Replacing the existing Papercusp template store/composer with a mobile-only generator.\n\n## Phase 0 — Approval and baseline\n\n- **P-001** `done` Approve this plan's architecture and choose the execution route; keep the plan draft and make no implementation changes before that approval. importance: high — note: Avi explicitly approved the plan, selected route A (this session), and directed AUTO mode implementation from start to finish on 2026-08-20.\n- **P-002** `done` Capture a reproducible baseline for Papercusp Android, Papercusp iPhone, SideStage Android, and SideStage iPhone: toolchain pins, successful test/build commands, generated artifacts, known host constraints, and current failures. Record exact commands and outputs. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-39957 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Build a two-source extraction matrix that classifies every recurring surface as shared invariant, Android shell, iPhone shell, product-specific, optional capability, generated output, or secret/external config. Select the strongest verified implementation per invariant rather than copying either repository wholesale. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-39959 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Freeze template IDs, versions, decision points, parameter names/defaults, supported OS/toolchain matrix, and the substitution/no-secret contract. Add a decision record for any deviation from the proposed five-template composition. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-39962 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Define the cross-platform parity matrix and acceptance assertions: which behaviors belong in Rust, which are native seams, which capabilities are optional, and which tests prove Android/iPhone parity without requiring identical UIs. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-39963 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — Shared mobile base\n\n- **P-006** `done` Author `templates/papercusp-mobile-base/` with `template.yaml`, `listing.json`, MUST/SHOULD/FREE `GUIDE.md`, component catalog/reference notes, and portable checks for Rust/UniFFI architecture, design-token source, scaffold shape, secret hygiene, placeholders, and host verification. blocked-by: P-004, P-005 — note: ← WI-39964 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Extract only genuinely reusable code surfaces justified by the audit—such as neutral binding/ABI verification, provenance helpers, token drift checks, or scaffold validators—into existing reusable component/package locations where one fits; otherwise keep them as checked template reference assets. Parameterize product names and add regression tests for every substitution. blocked-by: P-003, P-004 — note: ← WI-39965 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Add shared-base checks configuration to both mobile repositories and refactor duplicated invariant plumbing to the agreed contract without moving product domain logic out of its app. Prove both Rust cores and both UniFFI boundaries remain green. blocked-by: P-006, P-007 — note: ← WI-39980 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Android official template\n\n- **P-009** `done` Author `templates/papercusp-android-shell/` for the Compose/Gradle/cargo-ndk chassis, including package/SDK/capability decision points and checks for generated bindings, ABI coverage, lint, unit/instrumentation smoke, secure cleartext policy, release APK/AAB provenance, signing-input absence, and 16 KB alignment. blocked-by: P-004, P-005, P-007 — note: ← WI-39991 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Author thin `templates/papercusp-android-app/` as the official app root requiring exact pinned versions of `papercusp-mobile-base` and `papercusp-android-shell`; add its listing, guide, composition-integrity check, and template-kit reference manifest. blocked-by: P-006, P-009 — note: ← WI-39996 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Make Papercusp Android and SideStage Android first-class reference consumers of the Android template closure. Run each app's Rust checks, binding generation, Android lint/unit/instrumentation tests, debug build, and release-preflight/provenance checks; record any intentionally optional capability differences. blocked-by: P-008, P-010 — note: ← WI-40006 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — iPhone official template\n\n- **P-012** `done` Author `templates/papercusp-iphone-shell/` for the SwiftUI/XcodeGen/XCFramework chassis, including bundle/OS/capability decision points and checks for generated bindings, framework slices, project generation, privacy manifest, entitlements, Keychain/deep-link seams, XCTest/XCUITest smoke, and archive/export/signing preflight. blocked-by: P-004, P-005, P-007 — note: ← WI-40015 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Author thin `templates/papercusp-iphone-app/` as the official app root requiring exact pinned versions of `papercusp-mobile-base` and `papercusp-iphone-shell`; add its listing, guide, composition-integrity check, and template-kit reference manifest. blocked-by: P-006, P-012 — note: ← WI-40018 completed (done)\n- **P-014** `done` Make Papercusp iPhone and SideStage iPhone first-class reference consumers of the iPhone template closure. On the supported macOS/Xcode host, run Rust/binding checks, generate both projects, build simulator apps, run XCTest/XCUITest smoke, and run archive/export preflight without production credentials. blocked-by: P-008, P-013 — note: ← WI-40023 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Storefront, distribution, and anti-rot\n\n- **P-015** `done` Extend the canonical template set: `templates/README.md`, template-kit reference manifests/catalog/composition tests, all vendored template-kit copies or their canonical generation path, and docs that enumerate whole-app roots. Ensure `templates:list` and `templates:get-guide` return the two new official entries with correct titles, scope, category, versions, and closure. blocked-by: P-010, P-013 — note: ← WI-40031 completed (done)\n- **P-016** `done` Extend bundled-resource packaging, local template-store tests, materialization tests, mirror-sync coverage, and Cupboard listing metadata for all five new template directories. Run the manual public-mirror drift check, synchronize the mirror, and verify the published refs resolve before calling them delivered. blocked-by: P-015 — note: ← WI-40032 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `done` Add template-gym legs and fixtures that exercise the shared base and both platform roots, including manifest/reference drift, union-of-checks, no-product-string/no-secret guards, and reference-consumer conformance for all four existing app/platform combinations. blocked-by: P-011, P-014, P-016 — note: ← WI-40033 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 5 — Greenfield proof and release\n\n- **P-018** `done` Materialize one disposable greenfield app from `papercusp-android-app` and one from `papercusp-iphone-app` using the real `templates:new-app` flow. Use non-Papercusp/non-SideStage identities; prove the builder can answer decision points, wire the checks union, and produce installable simulator/emulator builds without private source-tree assumptions or committed secrets. blocked-by: P-017 — note: ← WI-40034 completed (done)\n- **P-019** `done` Run the final acceptance matrix, resolve every red, publish/update the two official listings, verify storefront discovery and GUIDE reads from the shipped bundled store and public mirror, and record a release decision with exact evidence. Mark the plan shipped only when both greenfield apps and all four reference consumers are green. blocked-by: P-018 — note: ← WI-40035 completed (done)\n- **P-021** `done` Ship papercusp-android-app and papercusp-iphone-app in the PUBLIC RELEASES as official Papercusp templates (D-007, owner-directed 2026-08-21). Include both app roots plus their required aspect closure (papercusp-mobile-base, papercusp-android-shell, papercusp-iphone-shell) in the released bundled template store and the public mirror; prove each resolves and materializes from the RELEASED artifact rather than the dev tree; verify storefront discovery lists both with official review status and readable GUIDEs. blocked-by: P-019 importance: high — note: ← WI-40547 completed (done)\n\n\n## Acceptance matrix\n\nThe plan is complete only when all of the following are true:\n\n1. Both app roots resolve to exactly one root app and the expected requires closure.\n2. Both roots require the same version of `papercusp-mobile-base`; shared checks are not copied and allowed to drift between roots.\n3. Papercusp Android, Papercusp iPhone, SideStage Android, and SideStage iPhone each pass their platform closure's configured checks.\n4. A fresh Android materialization builds and launches on an emulator/device; a fresh iPhone materialization builds and launches on a simulator.\n5. Rust/UniFFI tests prove native shells do not duplicate product business/network logic.\n6. No committed credential, production signing material, source app package id, source endpoint, source device/buyer id, or source brand asset leaks into either greenfield app.\n7. Android release preflight validates APK/AAB ABI set, 16 KB alignment, version/provenance, and external signing inputs.\n8. iPhone release preflight validates project generation, framework slices, privacy declarations, entitlement inputs, archive/export configuration, and external signing inputs.\n9. `templates:list`, `templates:get-guide`, and `templates:new-app` work from the bundled store; the public mirror resolves the same refs; template-gym reports green.\n10. Documentation names the new roots alongside web, desktop, and agentic desktop and explains that mobile shares a Rust/UniFFI base while platform UI remains native.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — One shared mobile base is mandatory\nDate: 2026-08-20\n\nThe owner-directed requirement is that Android and iPhone not become independent template lineages. Both official app roots therefore require the same version-pinned `papercusp-mobile-base` aspect, and both current products are conformance consumers.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse the official template composition model\nDate: 2026-08-20\n\nMobile extends the existing template substrate: thin app roots, aspect templates, pinned requires closure, portable GUIDE/check content, local bundled store, Cupboard listing, public mirror, and template-gym. No parallel mobile scaffold engine is introduced.\n\n### D-003 — Extract by intersection plus verified superiority, not by cloning one app\nDate: 2026-08-20\n\nPapercusp and SideStage are co-equal evidence sources. A shared invariant must be demonstrated by both architectures or generalized with tests; where implementations differ, the plan adopts the better verified behavior and backports it to both reference consumers.\n\n### D-004 — Product features remain product-owned\nDate: 2026-08-20\n\nThe common base captures architecture, build, binding, token, configuration, security, and release contracts. Papercusp operator capabilities and SideStage commerce/media behavior remain in their products, exposed only through optional capability seams where reuse is proven.\n\n### D-005 — Freeze the five-template mobile composition and v0.1 contract\nDate: 2026-08-20\nRetain the proposed five-template composition with no deviation: `papercusp-mobile-base`, `papercusp-android-shell`, `papercusp-android-app`, `papercusp-iphone-shell`, and `papercusp-iphone-app`, all at `0.1.0`. The two roots are scope/category `app` and hard-require exact pins to the shared base plus their platform shell; the base and shells are scope `aspect`, category `shell`. Reuse the existing manifest/composition/checks/store/mirror/gym substrate—no new scope, category, schema, registry, or materializer. Stable decision-point IDs, parameter keys/defaults, supported-host/toolchain matrix, identity substitution rules, and no-secret contract are frozen in `docs/decisions/official-mobile-app-templates-contract.md`. Any breaking change to those surfaces requires a coordinated template version bump and updated root pins.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-009, P-010, P-012, P-013, P-015, P-016, P-017, P-018\n\n### D-006 — Define parity as portable outcomes plus platform-native acceptance\nDate: 2026-08-20\nFreeze stable MOB-PAR, MOB-AND, MOB-IOS, MOB-OPT, MOB-SRC, and MOB-REF assertion IDs in docs/decisions/official-mobile-app-templates-parity-matrix.md. Cross-platform parity means equivalent portable Rust results, state transitions, configuration/error semantics, and generated UniFFI contract agreement; it does not mean identical UI, framework types, lifecycle timing, navigation, packaging, or product domain flows. Android and iPhone shells own distinct host-capable acceptance assertions, optional-capability assertions become mandatory only when selected, and every non-capable host must report host-constrained rather than green. Thin roots verify dependency closure and answer completeness without duplicating base/shell checks. Reference consumers must prove conformance while keeping Papercusp operator behavior and SideStage commerce/media behavior product-owned.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-015, P-016, P-017, P-018\n\n### D-007 — Ship both mobile app roots in the PUBLIC releases as official templates; keep the frozen -app ids\nDate: 2026-08-22\n**Owner directive [owner:Avi 2026-08-21]**, verbatim: *\"also include these android and iphone app templates as papercusp offical papercusp-android and papercusp-iphone templates in our public releases\"*.\n\nThis extends the plan's delivery target. P-019 already required publishing/updating the two official listings and verifying storefront discovery + GUIDE reads \"from the shipped bundled store and public mirror\", but it did not state that the two app roots must ship in the PUBLIC RELEASE artifacts as first-class official Papercusp templates. It does now, tracked as P-020.\n\n**Naming call (made under AUTO, disclosed to the owner):** the owner wrote the names as `papercusp-android` and `papercusp-iphone`. The templates keep their existing frozen ids — **`papercusp-android-app`** and **`papercusp-iphone-app`** — for three reasons:\n\n1. **D-005 froze the five-template composition and the v0.1 contract**, ids included. The ids are not cosmetic: both app roots hard-require `papercusp-mobile-base@0.1.0` and their platform shell at an exact pin, and each resolved manifest is retained as build provenance. Renaming a root is a coordinated version bump across the closure, not a label change.\n2. **Four reference consumers already pin these ids** — Papercusp Android, Papercusp iPhone, SideStage Android, SideStage iPhone (P-011, P-014, both done). A rename breaks all four and invalidates the retained manifests.\n3. **The `-app` suffix is the existing app-scope family convention**, not an accident: `papercusp-webapp`, `papercusp-desktop-app`, `papercusp-agentic-desktop-app`. Dropping it for mobile alone would make the two mobile roots the odd ones out in the storefront.\n\nThe owner-facing *titles* already read as the plain names — \"Papercusp Official: Android App\" and \"Papercusp Official: iPhone App\" — so the storefront presents them the way the owner described them regardless of the internal id.\n\nThis is a reversible call. If the owner wants the literal ids `papercusp-android` / `papercusp-iphone`, that is a coordinated v0.2 bump of the closure plus a re-pin of all four reference consumers, and should be done as its own item rather than folded into the release.\n\n### D-008 — Shipped template checks must not dereference sibling template directories; route closure resolution through a tri-state resolver\nDate: 2026-08-22\nEstablished while executing P-018, from a defect the greenfield proof surfaced (EI-21110451200329856).\n\n**The rule.** A check that ships inside a template's `checks/` directory may NOT resolve a dependency manifest through a sibling path such as `../../<other-template>/template.yaml`. Sibling templates exist only in this repo's `templates/` dir; `templates:new-app` overlays ONLY a template's own root into the new app, so any such path ENOENTs in every materialized app.\n\n**Why this is a rule and not a bug fix.** Both official mobile app roots shipped exactly this, which made the additive union a greenfield builder is instructed to run RED out of the box — inside the very check contract whose job is to prove these templates make no private source-tree assumptions. The failure mode is invisible in-repo (where it always passes) and universal out-of-repo, so it will recur unless it is stated as a constraint on how checks are written.\n\n**The required shape.** Route every such path through the template's own `checks/closure-manifests.ts`, whose `resolveSiblingClosure()` is deliberately TRI-STATE:\n\n- all sibling manifests resolve -> `repo` context, run every leg exactly as authored;\n- none resolve -> `materialized` context, skip the repo-only leg with a stated reason;\n- **some but not all resolve -> THROW.**\n\n**The partial branch is load-bearing and must not be simplified away.** The obvious implementation — skip whenever a file is missing — silently downgrades a DELETED canonical manifest into a green run, weakening the in-repo guarantee this fix was required to preserve. Anyone tempted to collapse the three states into two should read this paragraph first.\n\n**Enforcement.** `libs/generic/template-kit/src/templates-dir.test.ts` carries the guard: any shipped check naming a sibling template must import `./closure-manifests.js`, and that resolver must ship in the same `checks/` directory so it travels with materialization. The guard was proven falsifiable against the pre-fix copies rather than asserted.\n\n**Scope.** Only `papercusp-android-app` and `papercusp-iphone-app` were affected; a repo-wide sweep of every template's `checks/*.ts` for `../../papercusp-` returns those four files and nothing else. The copies under `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/sidecar/templates/` are an untracked build artifact regenerated from `templates/` and inherit the fix.\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-009 — P-018 greenfield identities are Stonebrook Ledger (Android) and Thornbury (iPhone)\nDate: 2026-08-22\nP-018 requires the greenfield proofs use non-Papercusp/non-SideStage identities. Fixing them here so P-019's acceptance matrix and the release evidence resolve to the same named artifacts instead of re-deriving them.\n\n**Android** — `stonebrook-android-20260821`, product \"Stonebrook Ledger\", applicationId/namespace `com.stonebrook.ledger`, external signing input prefix `STONEBROOK_ANDROID_RELEASE_`. Domain: an offline-first stock-count ledger for independent retailers. Materialized at `/tmp/papercusp-mobile-greenfield-20260821/stonebrook-android-20260821`.\n\n**iPhone** — `thornbury-iphone-20260821`, identity \"Thornbury\", materialized alongside it.\n\nThese identities are not decorative. `papercusp-mobile-base` declares `forbiddenTokens` banning the literal strings `Papercusp`, `Papercup`, and `SideStage` anywhere under its scanRoots, so the greenfield apps must be built by PORTING the shape of the two extraction sources (`papercup-rust-mobile`, `sidestage-mobile`) under these new names — never by copying their files, which would carry the banned tokens and fail the check. That constraint is what makes the greenfield proof meaningful: it demonstrates the templates are buildable by someone who does not have the original products.\n\nBoth apps are disposable proof artifacts, but until P-019 records its release decision they are EVIDENCE — do not obliterate or re-materialize them.\nRelated: P-018, P-019\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance #4 is satisfied by INSTALL + LAUNCH evidence only — a successful compile does not close a lane\nDate: 2026-08-22\nRuling for every P-018 build lane (WI-40367 Android/Stonebrook, WI-40368 iPhone/Thornbury) and for any lane that inherits this work.\n\n**The bar.** Acceptance #4 requires an installable artifact that ACTUALLY LAUNCHES on the target: an emulator APK for Android, a simulator .app for iPhone. A green `cargo build` / `gradle assemble` / `xcodebuild` is NOT sufficient evidence and will not close the item. The whole point of P-018 is proving a materialized greenfield app RUNS, because the templates are contract-only — everything up to compile can be green while the app fails to install or crashes at launch.\n\n**Evidence required on the work-item before `work_items:complete`:**\n1. The artifact path and how it was produced.\n2. The install command and its result (`adb install` / `xcrun simctl install`).\n3. The LAUNCH command and its result (`adb shell am start` / `xcrun simctl launch`), plus something showing the process is alive after launch and did not immediately crash — a screenshot, a logcat/os_log line from the app itself, or a pid that survives.\n\nA lane reporting done with compile logs only will be REOPENED. This is not a paperwork preference: \"it built\" and \"it runs\" have already diverged once on this plan (EI-21110451200329856 — the shipped check union was RED in every materialized app while everything in-repo looked green), which is exactly the class of gap a launch requirement catches and a compile requirement does not.\n\n**Why this is recorded here rather than only in coord.** It governs both lanes and any successor, and a coord message is not addressable after delivery — a member who received a paraphrase has no way back to the source. Cite it as `official-mobile-app-templates-2026-08-20#D-010` when relaying.\n\n### D-011 — Android needs the same post-launch OUTCOME proof as iPhone, but NOT the same test framework — parity is outcome-level (D-006), not GUIDE-symmetry\nDate: 2026-08-22\nRuling on the question raised by the iPhone lane (su-ca7336d6): the `papercusp-iphone-shell` GUIDE mandates an XCUITest while the `papercusp-android-shell` GUIDE mandates no UI test at all — is that deliberate scope or an oversight?\n\n**Neither, as posed.** Both offered answers are wrong because they assume GUIDE symmetry is the parity test. It is not.\n\n**What D-006 already settles.** D-006 defines parity as *\"equivalent portable Rust results, state transitions, configuration/error semantics, and generated UniFFI contract agreement\"* and states explicitly that it *\"does not mean identical UI, framework types, lifecycle timing, navigation, packaging, or product domain flows\"*, and that *\"Android and iPhone shells own distinct host-capable acceptance assertions.\"* So the Android GUIDE is NOT required to mandate an instrumented test merely because iPhone mandates XCUITest. Copying XCUITest's shape into Android would contradict D-006. To that extent the asymmetry is deliberate and stays.\n\n**What is nevertheless a real gap.** D-010 sets a SYMMETRIC evidence floor for Acceptance #4: install + launch, on both platforms, with something showing the process is alive after launch and did not immediately die. The iPhone lane cleared that floor and then went further — its XCUITest proved the launched app RENDERS REAL CORE OUTPUT, and in doing so caught a genuine app bug plus a template-class GUIDE gap (the prior run's XCUITest failed; see WI-40368 completion evidence, `verifiedHow: live-drove-ui`, artifact /tmp/thornbury-evidence/launch.png). That render-proof is an OUTCOME, and outcomes are exactly what D-006 says must be equivalent across platforms. If the Android lane can close Acceptance #4 while proving only that a process started, the two platforms are being held to different OUTCOME bars — which D-006 forbids even though it permits different frameworks.\n\n**The ruling.**\n1. The Android shell GUIDE MUST carry a host-capable acceptance assertion that proves the launched app renders real Rust-core output — not merely that the process is alive. This is a NEW requirement on the Android GUIDE.\n2. It MUST NOT be specified as \"an XCUITest equivalent\". Any Android-native idiom that produces the evidence satisfies it: an instrumented Espresso assertion, or a screenshot artifact plus a logcat assertion tying rendered content to core output. The lane picks the idiom; the OUTCOME is what is mandated.\n3. Acceptance #4 for Android is therefore NOT closable on install+launch alone once this lands. D-010's floor stands unchanged as the minimum; this adds the render-proof as the outcome-parity requirement.\n4. P-019's acceptance matrix records this as one shared outcome assertion with two platform-native satisfactions — NOT as two different acceptance bars, and NOT as \"Android is contract-only by design\".\n5. Where a host genuinely cannot run the assertion, D-006's existing rule applies verbatim: report host-constrained, never green.\n\n**Scope note.** This does not reopen WI-40368 (iPhone), whose evidence exceeds the bar. It binds the Android lane (WI-40367) and any lane inheriting this work.\nRelated: P-018, P-019\n\n### D-012 — P-019 final acceptance matrix is green; public-release artifact proof remains P-021\nDate: 2026-08-22\nDate: 2026-08-22\n\nP-019 is accepted on exact, independently re-read evidence. This decision does NOT mark the plan shipped and does NOT claim the Papercusp operator release gate/deploy is green; P-021 remains the owner-directed public-release artifact lane.\n\nAcceptance evidence:\n1. Closure/root uniqueness + shared-base pinning: writer-produced gym run `template-gym-2026-08-22T05-22-23-751Z` is 7/7 green; `mobile-manifests`, `mobile-check-union`, and `mobile-capability-diversity` all pass.\n2. Four reference consumers: the same committed gym run passes `papercusp-android`, `papercusp-iphone`, `sidestage-android`, and `sidestage-iphone`. Historical committed host evidence remains WI-40006 (Android 19/19 per consumer plus SideStage instrumentation 3/3) and WI-40023 (iPhone nine writer-produced evidence identities, SideStage unit 140/140, UI 5/5, archive green).\n3. Greenfield apps: P-018/WI-40034 remains terminal and was NOT rerun. Its committed `live-drove-ui` evidence names Stonebrook Ledger and Thornbury, install/cold-launch, process survival, rendered Rust-core 0.1.0 output, minified Android APK SHA-256 `81c633254ad806e14f1e6c33c07871fecab9b156c657632101e44e06d24f42a0`, Android screenshot SHA-256 `b801d0dd804cc8baa2b38cd072650539d516459cb9ea5a784cf0fa7ebd3a5a57`, and iPhone UI tests 1/1 plus unit 7/7.\n4. Android release hardening: WI-40535 corrected the late JNA/R8 consumer drift and gym isolation defect. Papercusp commit `b1f536e54772de5dd9a6f5e089568b86d29bd27b`; Papercup consumer commits `ecf4b833fa6c077aa56841249618727cefe3d9d3` + `f693cd0ebd0dfefde14f64df425e04054df4c3c9`; SideStage consumer commits `330f7627bd6339e35f17858caa734aab73d74049` + `02945c5aa6cc3f27d345093d1d17fede770bbe8b`. Remote egress confirmed for both consumer heads; focused detector/runner tests 17/17 clean and changed TypeScript projects compile.\n5. Bundled storefront/GUIDEs: live `templates:list` returns both roots as scope/category `app`, reviewStatus `official`; live `templates:get-guide` returns branch `local`, untruncated GUIDE, template.yaml, and exact 0.1.0 base+platform-shell closure for both.\n6. Public mirror: canonical `mirror:push` published commit `e5e2cf15c0d7c0a4daed634e68479a02b3184538`; a fresh independent clone then reported 189 expected files with 0 missing / 0 changed / 0 extraneous. Android/iPhone GUIDE, template.yaml, and closure-manifests.ts hashes match canonical byte-for-byte.\n7. Public Cupboard listings: Android listing `9f781e26-7087-47d5-81f3-360f82750d03` and iPhone listing `9753067b-45cd-4147-9989-ad2cdaac0d68` are approved and public search returns each exact title/ref against `https://github.com/Papercusp/templates`.\n8. Documentation: `templates/README.md` lists all five whole-app roots together and identifies `papercusp-mobile-base` as the shared cross-platform Rust/UniFFI contract; the contract/parity decisions preserve native Android/iPhone UI ownership.\n\nDisposition: close P-019/WI-40035 and unblock P-021. P-021 must still prove both roots and their aspect closure materialize from the RELEASED public artifact rather than the development tree, then the plan may be marked shipped.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"popup-agent-state-coverage-acceptance","title":"HUD conversation popup agent-state coverage acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-20","owner":"su-5508ff2e-c069-4650-9cab-9c84722c046a","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: HUD conversation popup agent-state coverage acceptance\nslug: popup-agent-state-coverage-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-20\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-5508ff2e-c069-4650-9cab-9c84722c046a\n---\n\n# HUD conversation popup agent-state coverage acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation acceptance for the popup-agent-state-coverage plan: the popup must expose decision-relevant agent/fleet state honestly, preserve uncertainty and provenance, remain operationally bounded, and carry a durable audited exclusion boundary. Shared method preconditions: evaluate the current acceptance source revision against the current resolved audit sequence in the canonical test environment, and record the evidence timestamp plus source/audit revisions with every grade.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"hotel-reservations","plan_slug":"hotel-reservations-mvp-20260821-2026-08-21","title":"Hotel Reservations MVP — Papercusp web app","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Hotel Reservations MVP — Papercusp web app\nslug: hotel-reservations-mvp-20260821-2026-08-21\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-22. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nOfficial papercusp-webapp materialized at /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/hotel-reservations. Product assumptions, architecture, domain invariants, 12 dependency-linked items, and six governing decisions are registered. Fleet launch is approved: 10 visible Codex gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh agents, default account, warm carry.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Launch hotel-reservations-build-20260821 on this plan, verify all ten members join and complete a first tool turn, then monitor P-001 to green before parallel lanes fan out.)\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-40290 — Materialize the complete Papercusp composition and runnable chassis <!-- P-001 -->\n\n## Goal\n\nShip a coherent, locally runnable and container-ready multi-user hotel reservation web app for a multi-property hotel group. Guests can find available rooms, reserve, manage, and cancel bookings; staff can manage properties, room inventory, rates, guests, and reservation operations.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- The delivered application is a runnable, container-ready Papercusp web composition whose required and selected optional template checks pass: web host, data layer, UI, data sync, and search.\n- Guests can search a property's available room types for property-local stay dates, receive an explicit-currency quote, create one confirmed reservation, and later retrieve or cancel it through an authenticated account.\n- Front-desk and manager roles can administer properties, room types, physical room capacity, rate plans, nightly inventory, guest records, and reservation state through authorized staff surfaces; guest accounts cannot access staff operations.\n- Availability and confirmation remain correct under concurrency: a stay cannot consume more nightly capacity than exists, idempotent retries cannot duplicate a booking or payment state transition, and cancellation restores each consumed night exactly once.\n- Reservation records retain immutable quote and guest snapshots, explicit money/currency values, property-local stay dates, auditable state transitions, and timestamps suitable for reconstructing who changed what.\n- Search indexes and live UI updates reflect committed Postgres state without becoming alternate sources of truth; rebuild or replay can recover their derived state.\n- Payment behavior is exercised through a provider contract and deterministic local adapter only; the app stores no provider credentials and initiates no live charge.\n- The repository includes repeatable migrations, seed data, focused domain and concurrency tests, integration coverage for API/auth boundaries, responsive guest and staff UI verification, a production Docker build, and documented local/container startup.\n\n## Design\n\nBuild the product as one Next.js App Router host composed from `papercusp-webapp`, `papercusp-web-host`, `papercusp-data-layer`, and `papercusp-ui`, with `papercusp-data-sync` and `papercusp-search` layered on explicitly. UI and API remain in the same deployable process; Postgres is the authoritative state store. This keeps the MVP operationally simple while preserving typed module boundaries that can be extracted only if measured scale later requires separate services.\n\nOrganize domain behavior behind server-side services and typed repositories rather than route-local SQL. Model availability as nightly capacity by property, room type, and property-local date; assign a physical room independently when operations require it. Quote and confirmation run in database transactions that lock the affected inventory rows, validate every requested night, write an immutable monetary snapshot, consume capacity, and persist an idempotency key atomically. Cancellation uses the same transaction boundary and a guarded state transition so inventory is restored once. This favors explicit relational invariants over an event-sourced booking core for the MVP.\n\nUse server-backed sessions with role checks at both route and service boundaries. Validate every trust-boundary write with shared typed contracts. Keep payment, search, and live-sync integrations behind ports: payment uses the deterministic adapter; search and sync consume committed changes and remain rebuildable projections. Guest and staff experiences share one responsive design specification assembled from registered Papercusp components, while authorization and domain services—not hidden UI state—decide what each role may do.\n\nMigrations and seed fixtures establish a reproducible multi-property dataset. Tests concentrate below the UI on money/date/state invariants and concurrent confirmation, then cover repositories, auth/API contracts, the principal guest and staff journeys, composition integrity, production build, Docker boot, and accessibility/responsive behavior.\n\n## Product assumptions\n\n- Multi-user server deployment with real sessions and role-based access: guest, front-desk, manager.\n- Multi-property hotel group, not a third-party marketplace.\n- Currency and timezone are explicit per property; all inventory and stay calculations use property-local dates.\n- Payments use a provider interface and deterministic test adapter; no live charges or credentials in this MVP.\n- Live UI synchronization and search are composed now via papercusp-data-sync and papercusp-search.\n\n## Architecture\n\nUse the papercusp-webapp required closure in dependency order: papercusp-web-host → papercusp-data-layer → papercusp-ui, then compose papercusp-data-sync and papercusp-search. Keep UI and API in one Next.js app-router process, Postgres as the source of truth, typed trust-boundary writes, and Docker deployment from day one. No agent plane.\n\n## Domain invariants\n\n- Room-night inventory cannot fall below zero or exceed configured capacity.\n- Reservation confirmation is transactional and idempotent; concurrent attempts cannot double-book.\n- Quote totals are derived from immutable nightly price snapshots and explicit taxes/fees.\n- Reservation state transitions are validated and audited.\n- Cancellation restores inventory exactly once.\n- Staff mutations require server-side role authorization.\n\n## Verification bar\n\nPass the full composed template checks union, focused unit tests, Postgres integration tests including concurrency, guest and staff end-to-end flows, production build, Docker boot check, and accessibility smoke checks. No item is done on typecheck alone.\n\n\n## Phase — Foundation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Materialize the complete Papercusp composition and runnable chassis: expand papercusp-webapp requires closure, compose papercusp-data-sync and papercusp-search, wire the vendored template-kit, Next.js app-router host, Postgres discovery/migrations, Dockerfile, test rig, and checks union. Establish package scripts and a green boot/build baseline before domain lanes branch. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40290 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `dropped` Define the hotel domain and land migrations plus typed repositories for properties, room types, physical rooms/capacity, rate plans, nightly inventory, guests, reservations, nightly price snapshots, payments, and audit events. Include property-local date/time and currency constraints. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-40630 completed (dropped)\n- **P-003** `dropped` Replace auth placeholders with real session authentication and server-side RBAC for guest, front-desk, and manager roles. Add seeded development identities, authorization middleware, route guards, and focused security tests. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-40631 completed (dropped)\n- **P-004** `dropped` Run design-phase.search_registry, specify the guest and hotel-operations information architecture using existing Papercusp registry components, then pass design-phase.validate_spec and design-phase.lint_spec. Cover responsive navigation, booking steps, tables/forms, empty/error/loading states, and accessibility behavior. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-40632 completed (dropped)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Core domain\n\n- **P-005** `dropped` Implement the availability and rate-quote engine over nightly inventory with occupancy rules, blackout handling, minimum stays, deterministic taxes/fees, immutable nightly price snapshots, property-local dates, and transaction-safe inventory adjustments. Add Postgres integration and concurrency tests. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40633 completed (dropped)\n- **P-006** `dropped` Implement the reservation lifecycle and typed API/actions: draft/hold/confirm/modify/cancel, idempotency keys, validated state transitions, transactional double-booking prevention, exact-once inventory restoration, audit trail, and guest ownership/staff authorization. Add concurrency and lifecycle integration tests. blocked-by: P-002, P-005 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40634 completed (dropped)\n- **P-007** `dropped` Implement property and room search/read models plus live data synchronization: filter by destination, stay dates, occupancy, amenities, and price; return availability-aware summaries; index only app-owned data; publish reservation/inventory updates to affected UI surfaces. Add search and sync integration tests. blocked-by: P-002, P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-40635 completed (dropped)\n\n\n\n## Phase — Guest experience\n\n- **P-008** `dropped` Build the responsive guest discovery experience from the accepted design spec: home/search form, results, property detail, room/rate selection, price breakdown, loading/empty/error states, and accessible mobile/desktop interactions using Papercusp UI components. blocked-by: P-004, P-007 importance: high — note: ← WI-40636 completed (dropped)\n- **P-009** `dropped` Build authenticated guest checkout and self-service reservation management: guest details, review/confirm with idempotency, confirmation page, booking list/detail, cancellation, and permitted modifications. Preserve quotes safely across validation errors and live inventory changes; add guest E2E coverage. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-006, P-008 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40637 completed (dropped)\n\n\n## Phase — Hotel operations\n\n- **P-010** `dropped` Build the front-desk/manager operations console from the accepted design spec: property/room/rate/inventory management, reservation search/detail, create/modify/cancel/check-in style operational views, guest context, role-aware controls, optimistic/live refresh, and audited typed writes. Add staff E2E coverage. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-40638 completed (dropped)\n\n## Phase — Integrations\n\n- **P-011** `dropped` Implement a payment-provider interface with a deterministic test adapter, payment intent/state persistence, idempotent capture/refund semantics, and confirmation/cancellation notification seams. No live provider credentials or network charges. Add contract tests and wire confirmation states into booking UI. blocked-by: P-006 — note: ← WI-40639 completed (dropped)\n\n## Phase — Quality and delivery\n\n- **P-012** `dropped` Integrate and verify the complete app: full composed template checks union, type/lint/unit suites, serial Postgres integration suite, double-booking race tests, guest and staff end-to-end flows, production standalone build, Docker boot/readiness, auth-placeholder absence, accessibility smoke checks, and a concise run/deploy guide. Fix all discovered regressions before closing. blocked-by: P-003, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40640 completed (dropped)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Tenancy and product domain\nDate: 2026-08-21\nBuild a multi-user server deployment for a multi-property hotel group, not a marketplace. Roles are guest, front-desk, and manager. Property-local dates/timezones and explicit currencies are part of the domain contract.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-002 — Papercusp composition boundary\nDate: 2026-08-21\nUse papercusp-webapp with required papercusp-web-host, papercusp-data-layer, and papercusp-ui, plus optional papercusp-data-sync and papercusp-search from day one. Keep UI and API in one Next.js host, use Postgres as source of truth, ship Docker, and add no agent plane.\nRelated: P-001, P-007, P-012\n\n### D-003 — Reservation correctness model\nDate: 2026-08-21\nAvailability is nightly capacity in property-local dates. Confirmation is transactional and idempotent, quote snapshots are immutable, state transitions are validated/audited, and cancellation restores inventory exactly once. Concurrency tests are release-blocking.\nRelated: P-002, P-005, P-006, P-012\n\n### D-004 — Design registry gate\nDate: 2026-08-21\nBefore guest or staff UI implementation, use design-phase.search_registry, author one coherent responsive spec from existing registry components, and pass design-phase.validate_spec plus design-phase.lint_spec. UI lanes consume that accepted spec rather than inventing parallel primitives.\nRelated: P-004, P-008, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-005 — Payment boundary\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMVP includes a provider interface and deterministic test adapter only. Persist payment state and idempotency, but perform no live network charges and store no credentials in the tree.\nRelated: P-011, P-009, P-012\n\n### D-006 — Approved fleet route\nDate: 2026-08-21\nOwner selected a new visible fleet: 10 Codex agents on gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh, default system account with gateway skipped, warm carry. This session is leader and monitors until the plan is terminal.\nRelated: P-001, P-012\n\n### D-007 — Current hotel-app directive supersedes earlier ambient pause for this fleet\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThe owner's current interactive instruction is to launch ten visible agents and build hotel-reservations. Any earlier ambient/system-wide pause discovered by members predates this direct task instruction and does not stop this named fleet. Members should resume the plan, claim only scheduler-admitted work, and park only on real dependency gates.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-008 — Owner cancellation supersedes build and fleet decisions\nDate: 2026-08-22\nOn 2026-08-22 at 13:43 ET, the owner directly instructed the live fleet member that the hotel-reservations build is stopped, will not be built, and all agents working on it must be killed. This decision supersedes D-006 and D-007. Do not relaunch the fleet or resume implementation. Preserve completed P-001 only as historical scaffold evidence; drop P-002 through P-012 and their work-items as cancelled, and keep the fleet in terminal wind-down.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-plan-completion-audit-verdict-2026-08-13","title":"Acceptance — plan completion code-truth audit and author verdict gate","status":"active","created":"2026-08-21","owner":"su-8e97d231-65fc-479d-88c3-9fa6dc014965","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — plan completion code-truth audit and author verdict gate\nslug: acceptance-plan-completion-audit-verdict-2026-08-13\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-21\nowner: su-8e97d231-65fc-479d-88c3-9fa6dc014965\n---\n\n# Acceptance — plan completion code-truth audit and author verdict gate\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Blind audit execution\n\n- **P-001** `done` BLIND PROTOCOL (governs every item on this plan): you are executing the derived-truth audit METHOD against ONE subsystem as a calibration exercise — findings will be scored against a held-out answer key to validate the METHOD itself, so work from CODE and RUNTIME LEDGERS ONLY. THIS ITEM: enumerate every registry/config/manifest surface in scope, then classify EVERY field of each as derived | pinned | attested | curated-claim-about-code | pure-judgment. Every curated-claim-about-code is a finding candidate. importance: high — note: ← WI-40296 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Four sweeps over the scoped subsystem: (a) MECHANICAL CROSS-REFERENCE — identity-namespace literals (event keys, tool names, file paths) appearing outside their defining registry; (b) COMMENT-CLAIMS — prose in code asserting sync-by-construction (e.g. 'by construction', 'kept in sync', 'mirrors', 'must match') with no recurring check behind it; (c) UNDECLARED-CONTRACT INVENTORY — shapes code CONSUMES programmatically (filter paths, jsonb reads, destructured payload fields) that NO surface declares; (d) RUNTIME-LEDGER FALSIFICATION — diff claimed vs observed against the fires/invocation ledgers: claimed-true-but-never-observed AND observed-but-never-claimed, both directions. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40297 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` DELIVERABLE: findings table — surface → field/site → class → proposed rung → concrete evidence citation — plus at least one POSITIVE classification (a surface verified as already correctly derived) as a control, and per-finding contamination flags. Proposed rungs must prefer ELIMINATING the hand-maintained copy over guarding it; any proposed guard/pin states its structural-impossibility reason. P-001..P-005 are all DONE. P-005 closed 2026-08-24 (WI-41201, completionAuthority:committed): state:read renders the assessment FIRST on the resolved branch as well as the unavailable one; cell-wake-fold is off CellFalsifierRead and onto the shared CellAssessmentRead, both rendering from ONE renderer in cell-read.ts; state:subscribe's `of` became `target: assessment|measurement|material`. Evidence: 422 passed / 0 failed across 12 unit files (runIds 349b85d2, ac9f61b5, 13caf369), 16/16 affected guards exit 0 incl. gen:tool-catalog:check, lint:tsc clean on all 6 changed files, lint:tool-prompts exit 0. TWO RULINGS BIND EVERY REMAINING ITEM and each INVERTS an in-code rationale, so a reader who has not seen them will \"fix\" the code back: D-014 (state:read's assessment-first render is NOT the D-008 violation its own former comment implied) and D-015 (D-007's assessment default is confined to OPERAND-FREE conditions; a valued `on` with no target is refused, because comparePredicate fails BOTH ways against a code enum — `ne` fires on the first poll, `gt` never fires at all). RESIDUE carried to P-008: (a) the full cross-workspace `npm run test:affected` still has never completed — killed three times in P-004, cause UNDETERMINED and deliberately unattributed; (b) predicate-watch.integration.test.ts (docker) is tsc-verified only; (c) LIVE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — dev/pipeline_position.ts:595 and release/checkpoint-run.ts:158 emit operand-free `state:subscribe { cell: 'gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict' }`, which now follows assessments.gateVerdict; live-verify, do not assume. NOTE: a direct plans:get TRUNCATES decision bodies — recover with tools:invoke { name:'plans:get', args:{ ..., decisionId, payloadTier:'full' } }.\n\n**Next:** Take P-006 (hard cutover): delete CellFalsifier / CellSpec.falsifier / CellFalsifierRead / falsifierFrom+path helpers / kills+measurement declarations / legacy fixtures / falsifier-named test files, make `assessment` REQUIRED on CellSpec, and add a focused ratchet rejecting reintroduction of the removed cell-subsystem identifiers plus asserting every value-bearing built-in cell has exactly one assessment — scoped to the cell subsystem so unrelated uses of the word \"falsifier\" stay legal. TWO THINGS THAT WILL SAVE A TURN: cell-wake-fold.ts is ALREADY clean (D-014 §3 moved it in P-005 — expect no work there), and making `assessment` required will strand every test fixture that hand-builds a CellSpec, so run `npm run lint:required-field-strands` and fix the sites rather than re-weakening the field to optional. Do NOT run `npm run test:affected` for the ripple — derive the radius with `node scripts/affected-tests.mjs --changed-paths <...> --print-affected`, then run the named guards directly and the importer-derived unit population through testing:run.\n\n## Goal\n\nRemove the falsifier concept from the cell system completely. Every value-bearing built-in cell instead exposes a separate, stable, domain-owned assessment enum whose declared meaning and safe action tell the consumer what the evidence warrants. Keep the raw measurement available and stable for auditing, predicates, thresholds, and debugging. Pull reads and automatic delivery-time injection must present the same assessment, evidence, provenance, unknown state, and reread handle.\n\n## Problem\n\nThe current contract returns a headline plus an independent field and prose naming a false reading it kills. The false reading is not otherwise present, so the consumer must imagine a mistake, decide whether the independent value contradicts it, and invert that result. The abstraction is negative, domain semantics remain implicit, and a sign error in interpretation can make the guard itself harmful. Recent work also had to teach the push renderer to carry the same negative apparatus, duplicating the cognitive burden on both delivery paths.\n\n## Existing surface\n\nThe public and runtime contract currently spans CellFalsifier and CellSpec.falsifier in cell-registry.ts; CellFalsifierRead, falsifierFrom, and the value branch of readCell in cell-read.ts; state:read and its directory response; falsifierLines in cell-wake-fold.ts; ten built-in registrations; registration, read, door-shaping, reality, and wake-fold tests; comments and canonical documentation; and three governing decisions: unified-agent-state-plane-2026-07-27 D-038/D-039 and state-plane-interest-and-hardening-2026-08-21 D-017.\n\nThe ten registrations are git.pipelinePosition, gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict, gate.greenCheckpoint.candidate, gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership, deploy.3070.sha, git.mainBehindStaging, host.memoryPressure, agent.goal, testing.census.population, and testing.coverage.floor.\n\n## Target contract\n\nEach value-bearing cell keeps its raw measurement path and adds one required assessment declaration. The assessment declares a resolver-output path, a closed set of enum codes, a meaning and safe action per code, and one or more evidence paths from the same resolver payload. The domain resolver computes the enum; the generic registry never invents domain semantics.\n\nA successful read returns the raw measurement plus assessment status, code, meaning, safe action, timestamp/provenance, and extracted evidence. Assessment path drift, an undeclared enum code, or door truncation is loud and renders the assessment unavailable or unverified; it never converts to a valid enum. Existing in-band cell unknown codes remain separate because resolver/read health is not a domain assessment.\n\nState reads render assessment first and measurement/evidence second. Delivery-time wake folds call the same readCell path and render the identical contract. Assessed subscriptions can target the assessment transition; raw measurement and material-lens subscriptions remain explicitly selectable. A cell field has one stable type: the raw value never alternates between number and enum.\n\n## Migration rules\n\nThe migration may introduce assessment support additively while producers and registrations are converted, but no compatibility alias or dual public contract survives the plan. The terminal cutover deletes every cell-system falsifier symbol, property, renderer, fixture, test name, comment, and generated declaration. Historical plan decisions remain historical; new decisions explicitly supersede only their falsifier clauses.\n\nThe independent facts previously used as falsifiers are preserved as assessment evidence or resolver inputs. In-band unknowns, result-level hoists, caller relativity, per-read provenance, live-exercise attestation, visibility/federation, materiality, one resolver/many lenses, ordered stages, and reread handles remain intact.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nAll ten built-in cells have exhaustive assessment truth tables and runtime outputs. Registry validation rejects missing assessment declarations, unknown enum codes, absent meanings or safe actions, duplicate/empty codes, missing evidence paths, and assessment paths derived outside the cell's one resolver payload. Reality tests execute every real resolver and prove its assessment and evidence paths exist. Direct state:read and automatic context injection show the same assessment and evidence. Subscription tests prove semantic transitions wake without requiring raw measurement changes and raw-target subscriptions remain available.\n\nThe final tree contains no CellFalsifier, CellFalsifierRead, falsifierFrom, falsifierLines, CellSpec.falsifier, falsifier registrations, falsifier-specific test filenames, or cell-system prose teaching consumers to reconstruct a false inference. A permanent ratchet fails if those cell-system identifiers return. Focused suites, operator-core baseline-aware typecheck, affected tests, declaration/doc projections, and live reads of every built-in cell are green with explicit zero residue.\n\n## Non-goals\n\nDo not create a second state or subscription mechanism. Do not move domain interpretation into the generic registry. Do not erase generic engineering uses of the word falsifier outside the cell subsystem. Do not rewrite historical decisions as though the old design never existed. Do not collapse resolver failure, missing data, or access denial into assessment enum values.\n\n## Phase — Contract and truth tables\n\n- **P-001** `done` Define the replacement contract and an exhaustive truth table for all ten built-in cells before changing runtime code. Specify CellAssessmentSpec and CellAssessmentRead: stable assessment code path, closed enum map, meaning, safeAction, same-payload evidence paths, resolved vs unavailable integrity state, and separation from CellUnknownCode. For each cell, name every enum code and the exact raw conditions that produce it; include negative controls for polarity/sign mistakes. Record that raw value types stay unchanged and that generic registry code transports but never derives domain meaning. Acceptance: the table covers every existing falsifier field and every nullable/unknown branch with no ambiguous catch-all and is recorded as plan decisions governing later items. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40645 completed (done)\n\n## Phase — Producer assessments\n\n- **P-002** `done` Make each owning resolver emit the domain assessment enum and its evidence in the existing payload, using pure domain helpers and table-driven tests. Cover the pipeline/gate family in git-pipeline-position and dev:pipeline_position; host memory pressure; coord goal and gate ownership; and testing census/coverage. Derive each enum once at the resolver boundary from the truth table, preserve current raw fields, provenance, and unknowns, and fail tests on unhandled input combinations. No cell-registry interpretation logic and no second resolver dispatch. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-40648 completed (done)\n\n## Phase — Core assessment contract\n\n- **P-003** `done` Add the assessment schema and read projection to cell-registry.ts and cell-read.ts additively for migration. Validate unique non-empty codes, complete meaning/safeAction maps, assessment path distinctness, evidence path declarations, and one-resolver lineage. Read assessment code and evidence from the same payload with MISSING-not-equal-NULL and door-truncation handling; undeclared codes or absent/truncated paths yield a loud assessment-unavailable result rather than a fabricated enum. Extend state:read's directory and value result shape, generated declarations, and focused registry/read/door-shaping tests. Falsifier remains only temporarily until P-006; no public alias between the two. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-41152 completed (done)\n\n## Phase — Registration migration\n\n- **P-004** `done` Migrate all ten BUILTIN_CELLS registrations from falsifier declarations to assessment declarations using the P-001 truth tables and producer paths. Preserve each old independent fact as assessment evidence where it still carries information; do not translate kills prose mechanically. Replace cell-falsifier-reality.test.ts with assessment-reality coverage that invokes every real resolver, proves every assessment/evidence path exists, proves every declared enum can be produced or has a permanent synthetic control, and detects constant or sign-inverted assessments. Update registration tests and live-exercise attestations with an explicit ten-of-ten coverage partition and zero residue. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-41162 completed (done)\n\n## Phase — Pull, push, and subscriptions\n\n- **P-005** `done` Make explicit assessment semantics the first-class consumer surface. state:read renders assessment code, meaning, safe action, and evidence before the raw measurement. cell-wake-fold uses the same CellAssessmentRead and renders the identical delivery-time contract, including loud unavailable/truncated states and the reread handle. Extend state:subscribe with an explicit target of assessment|measurement|material; assessed cells default new subscriptions to assessment while existing stored predicate rows keep their concrete path until lifecycle expiry. Prove semantic transitions wake even when raw measurement is unchanged, raw-target predicates retain numeric operators, material subscriptions retain current behavior, and push/pull outputs remain shape-equivalent. blocked-by: P-003, P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-41201 completed (done)\n\n## Phase — Hard cutover and recurrence guard\n\n- **P-006** `done` Delete the falsifier concept from the cell subsystem after every registration and consumer is on assessments: CellFalsifier, CellSpec.falsifier, CellFalsifierRead, falsifierFrom/path helpers, falsifierLines, kills/measurement declarations, legacy fixtures, compatibility branches, and falsifier-specific test filenames/comments. Scope the ratchet to the cell subsystem so unrelated scientific/test uses of the word falsifier remain legal. blocked-by: P-004, P-005 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-41222 completed (done)\n\n## Phase — Authority and documentation\n\n- **P-007** `done` Update canonical cell documentation, state:read/state:subscribe guidance, state-plane stamps, examples, and generated declaration/doc projections to teach measurement plus explicit assessment, not hypothetical false inference. Add explicit supersession decisions: the axis-one falsifier contract and its registration refinement in unified-agent-state-plane-2026-07-27 are replaced by the assessment contract; the delivery-time push-falsifier decision in state-plane-interest-and-hardening-2026-08-21 is replaced by assessment parity on delivery-time reads. Exact historical decision IDs are carried by this plan's structured D-006 authority record. Preserve all other axes and historical text as history. Use docs:author for canonical agent-insights sources and regenerate projections rather than editing generated/public copies. blocked-by: P-006 — note: ← WI-296256 completed (done)\n\n## Phase — Integrated verification and cutover\n\n- **P-008** `done` Run the terminal acceptance matrix on current HEAD: focused registry/read/reality/door-shaping/subscribe/wake-fold suites; producer truth-table suites; generated declarations and doc-projection checks; operator-core baseline-aware typecheck; npm run test:affected; and git diff --check. Live-read every one of the ten built-in cells under an authorized identity and record assessment code, meaning, safe action, evidence, raw measurement, provenance/unknown state, and zero unresolved registrations. Drive one real or controlled assessment subscription through automatic context injection and compare it to a direct state:read.
