Audit the canonical tree for zero removed cell-falsifier identifiers and explicitly partition all ten cells plus all consumer surfaces with residue:['none'] before marking the plan ready to ship. blocked-by: P-006, P-007 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-2008163 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The consumer contract is an explicit assessment, not a hypothetical inference plus negation\nDate: 2026-08-21\nA value-bearing cell tells the consumer the safest domain conclusion its evidence warrants. It does not ask the consumer to imagine a tempting mistake, inspect a `kills` sentence, infer falsifier polarity, and negate the hypothetical. The assessment is a closed enum code with a declared meaning and safe action. Raw measurements and supporting evidence remain visible, but assessment is the first consumer-facing semantic surface on both pull and push.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Domain resolvers compute assessment enums; the generic cell plane only validates and transports them\nDate: 2026-08-21\nInterpretation stays with the code that owns the domain facts. Each existing resolver emits its assessment code from an exhaustive truth table in one derivation. The cell registry declares allowed codes, meanings, safe actions, and evidence paths; readCell projects them from that same payload. Generic cell code must never compare arbitrary evidence values or synthesize gate, memory, ownership, goal, or coverage semantics.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Raw measurement and assessment are separate stable properties\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDo not overload `value` as a number-or-enum union. The current headline/raw measurement keeps its existing stable type for predicates, thresholds, facts dependency digests, auditing, and debugging. `assessment` is a separate stable enum property. This makes semantic subscriptions possible without breaking callers that genuinely consume raw telemetry.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-005\n\n### D-004 — Assessment evidence is same-payload and loud on drift, but it is not called a falsifier\nDate: 2026-08-21\nPreserve the independent measurements that carry useful information by declaring them as assessment evidence or resolver inputs. Evidence, assessment code, and raw value come from the cell's one resolver payload; no second dispatch is allowed. Missing assessment paths, undeclared codes, or door-truncated evidence produce an explicit unavailable/unverified assessment and a reread lever. They never become measured null agreement or a valid enum. The public and source contract contains no `falsifier`, `kills`, or negative-inference field.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-006\n\n### D-005 — The migration is additive only temporarily and ends with a hard no-alias cutover\nDate: 2026-08-21\nAssessment support may coexist with falsifiers only while the plan's dependent items are landing on shared staging. That temporary sequencing is not a compatibility contract. Once all ten registrations and both delivery paths use assessments, P-006 deletes every falsifier type, property, helper, renderer, fixture, test name, comment, and compatibility branch. A permanent scoped ratchet prevents resurrection.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-006 — Only the falsifier clauses of the prior cell decisions are superseded\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThis plan replaces unified-agent-state-plane-2026-07-27 D-038 axis 1 and D-039's falsifier-derived registration clause, plus state-plane-interest-and-hardening-2026-08-21 D-017's push-falsifier requirement. It preserves D-038/D-039's in-band enumerated unknowns and result-level hoists, caller relativity, live provenance, one derivation/many lenses, access/federation, materiality, ordered stages, and delivery-time reread discipline. Historical decisions remain readable as history; new supersession records identify the effective authority.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-007 — Assessment is the default target for new subscriptions; stored rows retain their concrete paths\nDate: 2026-08-21\nFor a cell declaring an assessment, a new state:subscribe call without an explicit target watches the assessment path because semantic transitions are the decision-ready changes. Callers can explicitly target `measurement` or `material` when they need raw movement or the existing material lens. Existing predicate-watch rows already store concrete resolver paths and continue unchanged until their normal lifecycle expiry; no risky data rewrite is needed.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-008 — Assessment declarations are closed, same-payload contracts and read integrity is explicit\nDate: 2026-08-22\nFreeze this contract before runtime edits. `CellAssessmentSpec` is required on every value-bearing built-in cell and declares `{ path, codes, evidence }`: `path` is one resolver-output path; `codes` is a non-empty closed map from enum code to non-empty `{ meaning, safeAction }`; `evidence` is a non-empty list of distinct paths in that same resolver payload. The assessment path, headline, material path, and evidence paths must be distinct where they make different claims. The registry validates empty/duplicate codes, incomplete meaning/action maps, missing/duplicate evidence paths, and resolver-lineage drift.\n\nA value read returns raw `value` unchanged plus `assessment: { status:'resolved', code, meaning, safeAction, evidence:[{path,value}] }` or `assessment: { status:'unavailable', code:null, meaning:null, safeAction, evidence, unknown }`. `unknown` uses the existing CellUnknown vocabulary for missing paths, resolver failure, insufficient input, or access failure; door loss uses the existing `truncatedByDoor/fullRead` lever. Missing is never equal to measured null. An undeclared code, absent assessment/evidence path, or door truncation can only downgrade to unavailable; generic code never invents a domain code. Resolver/read health and existing CellUnknownCode values are not assessment enums.\n\nProducer paths are unique within shared payloads: `assessments.pipelinePosition`, `assessments.gateVerdict`, `assessments.gateCandidate`, `assessments.gateOwnership`, `assessments.deployedSha`, and `assessments.mainBehindStaging`; single-purpose resolvers use `assessment`. Raw headline types remain byte-for-byte stable. Pull, push, and subscription consumers project this same read contract; no second resolver or compatibility alias is allowed.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-009 — Pipeline and gate assessment truth tables govern the pending implementation\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe six shared pipeline/gate resolver assessments use first-match order; any required leg named by `positionsUnknown`/`verdictUnknown`, any unresolved subject, any unverified newer-commit leg, or an absent required field makes assessment unavailable rather than selecting a code.\n\n`git.pipelinePosition`: live = deployed && serving.startedSinceCodeChange===true (no action); restart-required = deployed && serving.startedSinceCodeChange===false (restart the named serving runtime); uncommitted = dirtyUncommitted && !committedLocal (finish the atomic edit, let git-sync commit); awaiting-push = committedLocal && !onStaging; awaiting-gate = onStaging && !inMain; awaiting-deploy = inMain && !deployed. Negative controls swap every adjacent stage and prove a later true cannot excuse an earlier false; serving true must not turn deployed false into live.\n\n`gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict`: inconclusive = gate.inconclusive!=null (follow its status-specific lever, do not use frozen red counters); red-stale = consecutiveReds>0 && verdictStale (verify the current candidate; do not fix abandoned reds); red-current = consecutiveReds>0 && !verdictStale (fix named current failures); not-firing = consecutiveReds===0 && fireStale (recover the gate producer); passing-buffered = consecutiveReds===0 && !fireStale && mainBehindStaging===true (normal buffer, wait unless the separate buffer-stale evidence fires); passing-current = same but mainBehindStaging===false. Negative control proves zero reds never outranks fireStale.\n\n`gate.greenCheckpoint.candidate`: no-active-run = judgingSha===null and no unknown; judging-current-path = judgingSha!=null && judgingContainsPath===true; judging-without-current-path = judgingSha!=null && judgingContainsPath===false; inferred-candidate = judgingSha!=null and source is non-authoritative/run-probe (treat as a hint and re-read marker-backed provenance). Negative control proves sha presence alone never means the candidate contains this path.\n\n`gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership`: duplicate-owners if duplicates non-empty; unowned for no-object; claimable for claimable; lease-expired for lease-expired; held-live for held plus live|parked|recorded; held-needs-confirmation for held plus draining|suspect|null; held-by-ended-session for held plus ended. claimState null is unavailable. Negative control proves takenBy/heartbeat freshness alone never means live ownership.\n\n`deploy.3070.sha`: executing = deployedSha!=null && startedSinceCodeChange===true; restart-required = deployedSha!=null && false; process-unverified = deployedSha!=null && null. deployedSha null is unavailable, never 'nothing deployed'.\n\n`git.mainBehindStaging`: caught-up = mainBehindStaging===false; normal-buffer = true && !fireStale; gate-stalled = true && fireStale. null is unavailable. Negative control proves behind=true is not itself a fault and false cannot conceal an unreadable git leg.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-010 — Host, agent-goal, and testing assessment truth tables preserve unknown and zero semantics\nDate: 2026-08-22\n`host.memoryPressure`: critical when pressure==='crit' (stop adding load and remove the attributed pressure source); warning when 'warn' (reduce/inspect load); stable-low-free when pressure==='ok' and host.memFreePct is measured below the declared capacity warning threshold (reclaim capacity, but do not call it PSI pressure); stable when pressure==='ok' otherwise (no pressure action). pressure null, stale capture, or missing required PSI legs is unavailable. Negative controls prove free-memory capacity cannot synthesize PSI pressure and a stale capture cannot select stable.\n\n`agent.goal`: nothing-held when goalRef===null and goalUnknown==='nothing-held'; corroborated when goalRef!=null && goalAgreement==='corroborated' && competing is empty (act on the linked ref); sole when goalRef!=null && agreement==='sole' && competing is empty (use the ref but disclose it has one source); divergent when goalRef!=null && agreement==='divergent' or competing non-empty (inspect all refs before coordinating). A null goalRef without the explicit nothing-held hoist, absent agreement, or store failure is unavailable. Negative control proves precedence-selected goalRef cannot erase competing claims.\n\n`testing.census.population`: no-providers when surfaces===0 && providersRegistered===0 (register/enable a provider; successful fires cannot census anything); census-not-run when surfaces===0 && providersRegistered>0 && lastCensusAt===null (run/fix the census); empty-measured when surfaces===0 && providersRegistered>0 && lastCensusAt!=null (the scoped census measured zero matching surfaces); populated when surfaces>0 (use the count with fidelity/basis). Negative control proves numeric zero alone cannot distinguish these states.\n\n`testing.coverage.floor`: not-measured when verdict==='not-measured' or surfaces===0 (repair/follow censusUnknown; do not report 0% or 100%); meets-floor when surfaces>0 && belowUnwaived===0 (no unwaived gap action); below-floor when surfaces>0 && belowUnwaived>0 (work the returned unwaived gap queue); measured-with-waivers when surfaces>0 && belowUnwaived===0 && below>0 (record that the apparent gaps are accepted live waivers). Evaluation orders measured-with-waivers before meets-floor. pct is evidence only, never the branch condition; negative controls prove a capped row list cannot change the aggregate assessment and a null pct cannot become 0.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-011 — P-003 shipped the assessment schema OPTIONAL, and a new CellSpec optional field now carries a mandatory census row\nDate: 2026-08-24\nThree rulings from implementing P-003 that bind P-004 and P-006. Recorded because each is a convention a later lane would otherwise have to rediscover, and one of them is enforced by a guard that fails in a place that does not name this plan.\n\n1. `CellSpec.assessment` ships OPTIONAL (`assessment?:`), not required.\nD-008 states it is REQUIRED on every value-bearing built-in cell, and that remains the target — but P-003's own scope is \"additively for migration\" and P-004 is what populates the ten BUILTIN_CELLS. Declaring it required in P-003 would have stranded all ten live registrations plus ~10 test fixtures that construct a CellSpec: the required-field-strand class `npm run lint:required-field-strands` exists to catch. P-006 flips it to required in the same change that deletes `falsifier`. The `?` is documented in the interface doc-block as a migration artifact and explicitly NOT a licence — a value-bearing cell without an assessment is unfinished, not exempt. VERIFIED: the guard, run against the commit that actually carried the change (`--base <carrier>^`), reports no required fields added to exported types.\n\n2. No alias, no mechanical translation, between falsifier and assessment.\nP-003's text already forbids a public alias; the reason is worth fixing in the record because it will look like a shortcut to whoever does P-004. A `kills` string is a NEGATIVE claim (\"here is the reading this refutes\") and a `safeAction` is a POSITIVE one (\"here is what you may now do\"). Auto-deriving either from the other manufactures guidance no author wrote. P-004 must translate each cell BY HAND from the P-001 truth tables, and where an old falsifier's independent measurement still carries information it becomes assessment EVIDENCE, not prose.\n\n3. ⚠ A new optional field on CellSpec REQUIRES a matching row in `DECLARED_FIELDS` (scripts/check-declared-consumed.mjs).\n`declared-consumed-sweep.test.ts` reads the real CellSpec interface, extracts every `field?:`, and asserts the census watches exactly that set. Adding `assessment?` reds it — in a file that mentions neither cells nor this plan, with a message about \"census rows\". The guard is correct and deliberate: its own comment names \"a new optional field added to CellSpec tomorrow\" as the WI-6444 risk surface it exists for. P-006 removing `falsifier` will hit the mirror image and must DELETE a row. The added row states the consequence: a dropped assessment declaration is indistinguishable from a cell that honestly could not assess itself, because the read contract can legitimately report status:'unavailable'.\n\nAlso settled while implementing, smaller: the cross-cell \"producer paths are unique within shared payloads\" clause of D-008 lives in `registerCell`, not `validateCellSpec`, because it is the one assessment rule not answerable from a single spec — same placement and same reason as the existing duplicate-resolver guard. It compares paths EXACTLY (not normalised) there, because a false positive would refuse a legitimate P-004 registration, whereas the in-spec distinctness checks normalise on purpose to catch a re-punctuated restatement of the headline.\n\n### D-012 — D-010's `not-measured` coverage code collides with the read-health vocabulary and is renamed `no-population`; evidence must be door-surviving and flat\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24\nThree rulings from implementing P-004 (the ten-cell registration migration). Each binds P-005/P-006/P-007/P-008, and each was invisible to every prior item because none of them registered an assessment against a live payload.\n\n1. THE COVERAGE-FLOOR CODE `not-measured` IS RENAMED `no-population`, IN THE PRODUCER.\nD-010's truth table names `testing.coverage.floor`'s empty-population code `not-measured`, and P-002 shipped `TestingCoverageFloorAssessment` emitting exactly that. But `not-measured` is ALSO a `CellUnknownCode` (`not-applicable | resolver-failed | not-measured | insufficient-data`), and D-008 forbids that overlap — the registry enforces it as `assessment-code-collides-with-unknown`. So three ratified artifacts contradicted each other and the cell could not be registered honestly either way: DECLARING the colliding code is refused at registration, and OMITTING it makes every empty-census read fail as an undeclared code (`assessmentFrom` refuses it and answers `unavailable`). The collision was undetectable until a cell actually declared an assessment, which is what P-004 is.\n\nD-008's rule wins, and this is its sharpest instance rather than an awkward edge. An empty census is a MEASURED FINDING ABOUT THE SUBJECT — the census ran and enumerated zero surfaces, so a ratio would be vacuous — whereas read-health `not-measured` means the apparatus produced no value. One token for both makes \"there is nothing to measure\" and \"we failed to measure\" indistinguishable, which is the exact conflation this plan exists to remove. The fix landed in the RESOLVER (coverage.ts), not the declaration, per cell-registrations.ts's twice-stated precedent that a declaration which cannot be written honestly means the resolver changes. The sibling `verdict: 'measured' | 'not-measured'` field is UNTOUCHED — it is not an assessment code and carries no collision. P-007 must update D-010's prose when it documents the tables.\n\n2. EVIDENCE MUST BE DOOR-SURVIVING, AND THAT IS A MEASURED CONSTRAINT, NOT A STYLE RULE.\n`assessmentFrom` DOWNGRADES a resolved code to `unavailable` when ANY declared evidence path fails to arrive. Measured against the live door 2026-08-24: a `dev:pipeline_position` response bounded to its own budget DROPS `serving.*`, `positionsUnknown` and `changeInCandidate.judgingShaSource`, and sets `projection.truncated`. So declaring `serving.startedSinceCodeChange` as evidence — the most natural choice for `git.pipelinePosition` and `deploy.3070.sha`, and the pairing CLAUDE.md itself names — would have made both cells answer `unavailable` on the ORDINARY path, permanently. That is WI-38266 one field over.\n\nEvery evidence path in the ten declarations was therefore checked against a real payload before being written. The consequence worth carrying forward: the assessment CODE, computed inside the resolver before any door, survives shaping that its own raw inputs do not. An interpretation computed at the source is more robust than the evidence behind it — which is an argument FOR the contract, and also the reason P-005 must not \"enrich\" a consumer surface by re-deriving a code from evidence fields that may not have arrived.\n\n3. EVIDENCE UNDER A NULLABLE PARENT IS FORBIDDEN — `pathExists` STOPS AT A NULL SEGMENT.\n`agent.goal` returns `goal: null` for an agent holding nothing, so any evidence declared as `goal.competing` / `goal.agreement` is ABSENT in exactly the state it exists to explain, downgrading the whole assessment in the single most ordinary case there is. This is P-011's bug with a larger blast radius: there a nested path broke one falsifier, here it takes the entire assessment down. The shipped declaration uses the flat hoists (`goalAgreement`, `goalCompeting`, `goalUnknown`) that `coord:goal` publishes for precisely this reason, and a permanent control in cell-assessment-reality.test.ts pins it.\n\nALSO SETTLED, smaller: `cell-falsifier-reality.test.ts` is replaced by `cell-assessment-reality.test.ts`, which imports the SHARED `pathExists` from state-plane-stamp rather than carrying its own copy — the old suite could disagree with the read it was guarding. `lint:plane-guards` in package.json is repointed to the new file. Falsifiability is proven by PERMANENT controls in the suite (broken-copy specs with calibration cases), not an in-tree mutation probe: an in-tree probe holds cell-registrations.ts mutated for the duration of the run and git-sync sweeps the tree every few minutes, so the probe proving the guard works can commit a broken registration — attempted 2026-08-24 and git-sync held the exclusive sweep lock at that moment, which is the race, not bad luck.</body>\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-013 — Deleting a suite under this plan: repoint citations at the live function, leave ratchet-owned and fixture references alone, and repoint the gate script FIRST\nDate: 2026-08-24\nSettled while executing P-004's deletion of `cell-falsifier-reality.test.ts`. P-006 deletes the\n`falsifier` concept wholesale and will face every one of these questions again, so these are\nrulings, not notes.\n\nCONTEXT: the file was cited NINE times, not once. A `git grep` before the delete is mandatory;\nthe prior checkpoint described the delete as a one-liner and it is not.\n\nRULE 1 — REPOINT AT THE LIVE FUNCTION, NOT MECHANICALLY AT THE REPLACEMENT SUITE.\nThree `cell-read.ts` comments cited the old suite's *local copy* of `pathExists`. The replacement\nsuite does NOT copy that function — it IMPORTS the shared `pathExists` from `state-plane-stamp`\n(cell-assessment-reality.test.ts:49). So the correct referent is the live production function,\nand those comments now name `state-plane-stamp.ts`. Swapping the filename would have preserved\nthe citation's SHAPE while pointing it at code that no longer holds the thing described. This is\nthe same failure mode D-011 rule 2 bans for `kills` prose: a mechanical translation that reads\nas correct.\n\nRULE 2 — A DELETION CAN FALSIFY A RATIONALE, NOT JUST A PATH.\n`cell-read.ts` justified leaving `falsifierFrom` on the local copy because changing it \"would\nrisk a red in cell-falsifier-reality.test.ts\". Deleting that file destroys the reason while\nleaving the sentence grammatical. It was REWORDED, not filename-swapped. When deleting, grep for\ncitations that are ARGUMENTS, not just references.\n\nRULE 3 — `scripts/leak-census-baseline.json` IS NOT HAND-EDITED, EVER, INCLUDING TO PRUNE A\nDELETED FILE'S ROW. `scripts/leak-ratchet.ts` is the only sanctioned writer (its header says so)\nand the baseline is shrink-only. A row for a deleted file is inert: the file is never observed,\nso it can never be compared and can never regress. `leaks:ratchet` is also NOT wired into\ngreen-checkpoint, so the dead row reds nothing. Pruning it by hand would breach the shrink-only\nrule to fix a non-problem.\n\nRULE 4 — PARSER FIXTURES KEEP THE OLD NAME. `__tests__/affected-tests-failing-files-line.test.ts`\ncontains the filename inside a sample Vitest output line it parses. That is test DATA, not a\nreference to a live file, and rewriting it would weaken the fixture for no gain. Likewise the\nreplacement suite's own \"Replaces `cell-falsifier-reality.test.ts`\" header line is history and\nstays.\n\nRULE 5 — REPOINT THE GATE SCRIPT BEFORE THE DELETE, IN THAT ORDER. `lint:plane-guards` is a\ngreen-checkpoint gate script (green-checkpoint.ts:3248, :10425, :10723) and names its files\nexplicitly in package.json. Measured, not assumed: `scripts/test-files.mjs` REFUSES a missing\npath loudly — `TEST_FILE_ROUTE_ERROR ... does not exist`, exit 2, against a positive control that\nexits 0 on a real path. So a mis-ordered delete reds the gate visibly rather than silently\nleaving a gate script that guards nothing. The loud failure is why no new guard is needed here;\nthe ordering is still mandatory because the red would freeze every agent's deploys.\nRelated: P-004, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-014 — P-005 inverts the \"a resolved assessment stays quiet\" asymmetry; the shared renderer lives in cell-read.ts; state:subscribe's `of` is renamed to `target` with a LOUD refusal, never a silent alias\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24\nFour rulings settled while starting P-005 (the consumer surface). Each binds P-006 and P-007.\n\n1. A RESOLVED ASSESSMENT NOW LEADS THE READ. NOT A D-008 VIOLATION — READ THIS BEFORE \"FIXING\" IT BACK.\n`state:read`'s valueResult carries the comment \"D-008 — HOIST AN UNAVAILABLE ASSESSMENT, and ONLY an unavailable one\", emitting assessment prose solely when status is 'unavailable'. Its stated argument is the registry's real anti-noise rule: a line printed on every healthy read is one agents learn to skip.\n\nD-008 never ratified that restriction. Its full text fixes the assessment SHAPE and says \"Pull, push, and subscription consumers project this same read contract; no second resolver or compatibility alias is allowed.\" Nothing about suppressing the resolved branch. \"ONLY an unavailable one\" is the implementer's extrapolation from the sibling sourceProse/unknownHoist asymmetries.\n\nThe extrapolation does not hold, because the assessment is not a QUALIFIER like those two. They qualify a headline the reader already has, so silence costs nothing. The assessment IS the decision-ready answer — the thing P-005 exists to put in front of the raw number. Suppressing it on the healthy path means the only time a caller sees semantics is when they are missing, teaching exactly the habit this plan was written to break: read the number, infer the meaning yourself. A `healthy` code is not the string \"normal\" — it is a measured verdict from a closed vocabulary carrying a safeAction the caller is entitled to see.\n\nSo the resolved branch renders code, meaning, safeAction and evidence, and renders FIRST — before hoist, source and pointer prose, and before the raw measurement. The unavailable branch stays exactly as loud as today. P-007 must update guidance still describing the read as measurement-first.\n\n2. THE RENDERER IS SHARED, IN cell-read.ts — ONE CONTRACT, NOT TWO FORMATTERS.\nP-005 requires cell-wake-fold to render \"the identical delivery-time contract\", and D-008 forbids a second projection of it. A formatter copied per call site is how two surfaces drift on the one property that matters: that a code nobody measured is never made to look measured. `formatCellAssessment` (one line, for a summary channel) and `cellAssessmentLines` (an indented block, for a wake turn) live in cell-read.ts beside the type they render, share one evidence renderer, and are imported by both call sites. `briefCellValue` moves there too and cell-wake-fold's local duplicate is deleted — a value must not read one way in state:read and another way in a fold.\n\nBound by D-012 ruling 2, restated at the renderer: code, meaning and safeAction are TRANSPORTED off the resolved branch, never recomputed from `evidence`. A door-bounded payload legitimately drops evidence while the code — computed in the resolver before any door — survives, so re-deriving is silently wrong in the ordinary case, not merely impure. Evidence rendering keeps MISSING, TRUNCATED and a measured null visibly distinct.\n\n3. cell-wake-fold MOVES OFF THE FALSIFIER NOW; P-006 STILL OWNS DELETING THE CONCEPT.\ncell-wake-fold imports CellFalsifierRead and renders falsifierLines(read.falsifier) — the last consumer reading the falsifier for its primary block. P-005 owns moving CONSUMERS onto assessments, so that call site and the file-local falsifierLines helper (whose only caller it is) go now. CellSpec.falsifier, CellFalsifierRead and the rest remain for P-006 to remove wholesale per D-013. A P-006 agent should expect cell-wake-fold already clean.\n\n4. `of` BECOMES `target`, AND A STALE `of` IS REFUSED RATHER THAN TRANSLATED.\nP-005 adds an explicit target of assessment|measurement|material. The existing knob is `of: 'value'|'material'`: `value` becomes `measurement` and `assessment` joins them. Per D-007 a cell declaring an assessment defaults NEW subscriptions to the assessment path; one without defaults to measurement. Existing stored predicate rows are NOT rewritten — they hold a concrete path and keep it until lifecycle expiry, which needs no migration code, only the discipline not to add one.\n\nRenamed, not aliased. Alpha prefers renaming, but the decisive argument is this tool's own P-021 comment: it refuses to apply a declared materiality silently, because re-pointing a caller's predicate does not narrow their condition, it evaluates it against a DIFFERENT DOMAIN. Silently dropping an unknown `of` and falling through to the new assessment default commits that exact defect — a caller who asked for material would be watching a code enum, and on:{op:'ne', value:<a sha>} against a code string is true on the first poll, producing an instant spurious wake. So `of` stays in the schema purely to be REFUSED, with an error naming its replacement.\n\n### D-015 — D-007's assessment default is confined to OPERAND-FREE conditions; a valued condition on an assessed cell is refused (target_required); deriveCellReread must recognise assessment paths\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24\nSettled while implementing P-005 part 3 (state:subscribe `target`). Extends D-014 §4; binds P-006, P-007 and P-008.\n\n1. THE ASSESSMENT DEFAULT APPLIES ONLY TO A CONDITION THAT CARRIES NO OPERAND.\nD-007 defaults a NEW subscription on an assessed cell to the assessment path. Applied unconditionally that commits the exact defect D-014 §4 refuses `of` to avoid — and it would commit it against EVERY existing caller at once, because P-004 gave all ten built-in cells an assessment. `comparePredicate` fails BOTH ways against a code enum, and both are silent:\n  • `{op:'ne', value:'<a sha>'}` is `!absent && !deepEq` — TRUE on the first poll. An instant spurious wake, reported to the agent as a real transition.\n  • `{op:'gt', value:3}` is `Number('healthy')` → NaN → false FOREVER. The agent parks on a watch that can never fire, and no error surface ever says so. This is the worse of the two.\n`exists` and `changed` carry no operand, so they name no domain and cannot misfire on either path: the default applies exactly there. Every other op with no explicit `target` is REFUSED (`target_required`), naming both candidate paths and both fixes.\nDefaulting a valued condition to `measurement` instead was considered and rejected: it is equally silent in the other direction — a caller who meant `eq:'red-current'` against a gate-verdict CODE would be pointed at the raw value. This is a refusal, not a smarter guess. P-006 must not \"simplify\" the narrowing away.\n\n2. deriveCellReread MUST MATCH THE ASSESSMENT PATH — a third arm, not an optional nicety.\nIt matched a row against (tool, changeSignal.path | materiality.path). A watch is registered against ONE concrete path, so an assessment-target row derived NO `reread` handle — the wake payload's entire reason for existing (state-plane-interest-and-hardening P-001). Because ruling 1 makes assessment the default for the common operand-free subscription, omitting this arm would have stripped the handle from MOST wakes in the plane while every existing test still passed.\n\n3. TWO PLATFORM-EMITTED HANDLES SILENTLY CHANGE TARGET — P-008 must LIVE-VERIFY them.\n`dev:pipeline_position` and `release:checkpoint-run` both emit `state:subscribe { cell: 'gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict' }`. Operand-free, so under ruling 1 they now follow `assessments.gateVerdict` rather than the raw changeSignal path. This is the intended upgrade — that cell's own registration says the healthy-looking number is the one needing an intervention — but it is a live behaviour change to handles the platform hands agents, so it is verified, not assumed.\n\n4. THE EMITTED-HANDLE GUARD WAS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THE RENAME.\n`emitted-subscribe-handles.test.ts` validates emitted selectors against the tool's SCHEMA. Per D-014 §4 `of` survives in the schema (widened to a plain string, so `of:'assessment'` — the half-migrated guess — reaches the handler instead of dying in the parser with no pointer to `target`) purely so the HANDLER can refuse it by name. So an emitted `of:` handle would parse green while every agent that followed it was refused at runtime: a guard reading green about the precise failure it exists to prevent. A structural \"no emitted selector carries `of`\" assertion now sits beside it, with its own calibration.\n\n5. A PREDICATE OBSERVES THE RAW PATH; `readCell`'s downgrade does NOT apply — deliberately.\n`readCell` downgrades an undeclared code to `unavailable` (the closed-vocabulary rule). A poller reading `assessment.path` does not get that projection and would compare the undeclared string verbatim. Left as-is: normalising inside the tool would be a second projection of the read contract, which D-008 forbids, and the divergence exists only when a resolver emits a code its own registration never declared — a registry defect, surfaced elsewhere. The safe direction holds meanwhile: `changed` still fires on that transition. Recorded so P-006/P-007 do not \"fix\" it by adding a translation layer.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-016 — P-006 makes `assessment` required as `CellAssessmentSpec | null` — required-to-DECIDE, not required-to-HAVE, because event cells cannot carry one\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24\nSettled at the start of P-006, before the first edit. P-007 (docs) and P-008 (acceptance\nmatrix) must describe the field this way; do not restate it as a plain required field.\n\nTHE COLLISION. P-006 says \"make `assessment` required\". Implemented literally — `assessment:\nCellAssessmentSpec` — it makes EVENT-SIGNALLED CELLS UNREGISTERABLE, silently deleting a\ncontract variant as a side effect of a field change. The validator has forbidden an assessment\non an event cell since P-003 (`assessment-on-event-cell`, cell-registry.ts): an assessment names\na path into a RESOLVER RESULT, and an event cell has no poll dispatch to produce one, so the\ndeclaration could never be satisfied at read time. A plain required field therefore forces every\nevent cell to declare exactly the thing registration then rejects. This is not hypothetical:\n`kind: 'event'` fixtures exist at 8+ sites across cell-registry.test.ts (its BASE known-good\nfixture is event-kind), cell-read.test.ts, cell-access-parity.test.ts, state-plane-stamp.test.ts,\nfacts-disclosure.test.ts and state-tools.test.ts.\n\nTHE RULING. `assessment: CellAssessmentSpec | null` — REQUIRED, NULLABLE.\n- A poll cell MUST declare a real assessment. `null` is rejected (`assessment-missing`).\n- An event cell MUST declare `null`. A non-null one keeps its existing rejection.\n- Omission is impossible at the type level: the author must SAY which case applies.\n\nWHY NOT A DISCRIMINATED UNION on changeSignal.kind (the other candidate). It would encode the\ncorrelation at compile time, which is strictly stronger, but it was rejected on consistency and\ncost: every OTHER resolver-path field on this contract (`headlineSource`, `materiality`, and the\ndoorProjections re-read handle) already enforces its event/poll correlation IN THE VALIDATOR, not\nin the type. Making `assessment` the sole type-level exception would misrepresent the contract's\nshape and force `CellSpec` from an interface into a union, breaking the `Partial<CellSpec>`\nfixture helpers (cell-assessment.test.ts:70, cell-read.test.ts:41/:662, cell-access-parity.test.ts:93)\nand `Pick<CellSpec,…>` in cell-suggest.ts for no semantic gain the validator does not already give.\n\nWHY NULLABLE IS THE HOUSE IDIOM, NOT A WEAKENING. This file already states the principle it is\napplying: `CallerRelativity`'s `global` is \"something you SAY rather than something you omit\",\nand `visibility`/`federation` are required because \"`{ kind: 'workspace' }` is a valid answer;\nomission is not\". An explicit `null` is the same move — it converts a silent omission into a\nrecorded decision, which is what \"required\" is FOR here. The `?` that P-006 removes meant\n\"discretionary\"; `| null` means \"you must decide, and one of the two answers is unavailable to\nyou\". Do NOT read this ruling as licence to restore `assessment?:` — the checkpoint trap stands:\nre-weakening the field to optional silently reintroduces exactly what requiring it prevents.\n\nRIPPLE THIS RULING CREATES — one real defect, named so it is not rediscovered. `cell-read.ts:918`\ntests `spec.assessment === undefined`. Under `| null` that check stops matching a null assessment\nand the code would path into it. It must become a null-safe check. Every other consumer already\nuses `?.` or truthiness (`cell-registry.ts:1029`, `subscribe.ts:249`, `predicate-watch.ts:778`,\n`cell-wake-fold.ts:154`) and is unaffected. A strict-equality-to-undefined check is the ONLY\nshape this widening breaks; grep for it rather than assuming optional-chaining everywhere.\n\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"cupboard-plan-rubric-recipe-sharing-2026-08-21","title":"Cupboard sharing for plans, rubrics, and recipes — new listing kinds + plan→rubric dependency gating","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cupboard sharing for plans, rubrics, and recipes — new listing kinds + plan→rubric dependency gating\nslug: cupboard-plan-rubric-recipe-sharing-2026-08-21\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-09-04\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-016 remains the final implementation/verification item; its implementation/focused corpus and exact one-shot affected command are stored on WI-40531. Root HEAD and network origin/staging agree at ac12c47a7c79f1b208b160058fe421d987d5e549 with both stale-index.lock guard commits. Desktop gitlink/HEAD/origin-main agree clean at 8814724ec3b05d7daf7a614231cbbd9a38eedc3b. Freeze remains open: live EI-21165235642497045 owns seven staged plus one unstaged provenance-lint paths, has 195/195 focused proof, and is actively adding/rerunning regressions under a sole lock. Two new untracked observation-fold files appeared at 15:53-15:54 EDT; no current lock or coord/work-item search match identified their owner yet, so they also block clean qualification until published/removed by their live writer. Serializer owner is live, adopted exact gate emission after terminal blockers + two stable clean reads + published tip + idle run-lock, and has launched no checkpoint. Gate harness:papercusp:wi-40086-qualified-current-tip gen 1 remains unfired/null. WI-40648 is terminal done and not awaited.\n\n**Next:** Keep existing exact-gate await and 60s loop fallback. On event/timeout re-read EI-211652 activity/locks, resolve observation-fold writer if still present, full git status including staged/untracked, root/network/desktop, exact event and release trace. Take over only if progress stops. On fired SHA verify trace, run saved P-016 affected command once, then audit/close residues, refresh plan audit, obtain independent grade, implementer verdict, ship and verify.\n\n## Background\n\nThe Cupboard has exactly 7 listing kinds (`packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/types.ts:93`): harness · blueprint · plugin · pack · knowledge-pack · template · app. None covers plans, rubrics, or recipes.\n\n**Pre-built seams this plan finishes rather than invents:**\n- `cupboard/rubric-store.ts` (v1 plan: local-first-party-rubric-bundling-2026-07-07, still active — this plan is its designed-for v2): layered self-describing rubric store; the user layer (`~/.papercusp/rubrics`) is explicitly documented as \"v2's Cupboard `kind='rubric'` install target (flag `papercusp-rubrics-marketplace`)\". Each rubric = self-describing dir (rubric.json + listing.json in the storefront field shape + METHOD.md). Idempotent no-clobber seed with `seedContentHash` upgrade path already exists.\n- A rubric IS a plan row (`template='rubric'` in harness_shared.harness_plans) — plans and rubrics are storage siblings.\n- Plan template/instance model exists (migration 299: `template_slug`, `<template>@run-<id>` instance plans) — an installed plan lands as a TEMPLATE, never a live plan.\n- Dependency-gating precedent: the events axis (worker migrations 012/013, `provides_events`/`requires_events`) — pre-install surfacing + hard gate on required-but-unprovided. Plan→rubric deps (`requires_rubrics`) rerun this pattern; the bundled first-party rubric set counts as provided.\n- Review policy precedent (knowledge-packs D-007): prose/judgment kinds publish `pending` → operator approval. Plans, rubrics, recipes are all prose kinds → same lane.\n- Worker kind-CHECK widening requires the 12-step D1 table rebuild (migration 014 is the template, incl. forward-normalizing legacy kind values).\n- Per-kind publish/install agent tools are the established client shape: `cupboard/publish-{template,plugin,app}.ts`, `cupboard/install-{template,blueprint,plugin}.ts`.\n\n**Unit-type survey (owner follow-up \"what else aren't we sharing?\"):** recipes (`harness_shared.code_recipes`, mig 349 — captured/curated tool orchestrations with run machinery; the most skill-like unit in the system) are the strongest third kind → Phase 3. Convention/doc-part packs (composed CLAUDE.md parts) are knowledge-pack-adjacent — candidate future EXTENSION of knowledge-pack, not a new kind (reuse-first); noted, not in scope. Datatypes arrive via bundle-app Phase 2's manifest (already contemplated by mig 014) — no separate kind needed. Saved prompts / lexicon: low priority, could ride knowledge-packs later. Watches/invariants, scorecards, gym scenarios: workspace-coupled or output-not-content — not shareable units.\n\n## Phase 1 — rubric kind (finish the designed v2 seam)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Worker migration 015: widen listing_kind CHECK with 'rubric' (12-step rebuild per mig-014 pattern, forward-normalizing); listing_ref carries rubricId; add 'rubric' to the pending-review policy kinds (D-007 lane) — note: migration 015 — ONE rebuild widens the CHECK to all 3 kinds AND declares requires_rubrics (D-001), forward-normalizing legacy kinds per the 011/014 precedent. NOT yet applied to the live D1 (one-shot, owner-authorized; prod-verify ritual in the header).\n- **P-002** `done` Client types: 'rubric' in LISTING_KINDS + listingActionFor → 'install' + HarnessListing fields; mirror in apps/operator-public/src/db.ts — note: cupboard/types.ts (kinds, actions, RubricRequirement + parseRequiredRubrics, requires_rubrics) + the operator-public mirror (db.ts kind list, REVIEW_POLICY_KINDS +3 per D-002, HarnessRow/NewHarnessInput/insertHarness, listings.ts validator + caps + insert wiring). lint:tsc clean.\n- **P-003** `done` Publish path: `cupboard:publish-rubric` agent tool — serialize a workspace rubric (active/ratified only) into the self-describing dir form (rubric.json + listing.json + METHOD.md) and publish pending-review blocked-by: P-001 — note: publish-rubric-core.ts + agent-tools/cupboard/publish-rubric.ts (registered). Mirror-repo-backed like templates; the listing is a POINTER + storefront metadata — criteria stay in the repo's rubric.json rather than being duplicated into the row.\n- **P-004** `done` Install path: `cupboard:install-rubric` — fetch the self-describing dir into userRubricsDir(); existing no-clobber seed carries it into the workspace store as source:'installed'; register flag `papercusp-rubrics-marketplace` DEFAULT ON (finished work never ships dark) blocked-by: P-001 — note: install-rubric-core.ts + install-rubric-io.ts + agent-tools/cupboard/install-rubric.ts (registered), built on the NEW generic install-self-describing-core.ts + resolve-listing-by-kind.ts (D-003). Two-step: place dir, then run the EXISTING no-clobber seed via new reseedRubricsAfterInstall — ensureFirstPartyRubricsSeeded is once-per-process and would have silently no-opped. Flag deliberately not registered (D-003).\n- **P-005** `done` Storefront UI: Rubrics tab (listing-kind tabs) + detail view rendering criteria + METHOD.md blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-40434 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — plan kind (plan templates + rubric dependency gating)\n\n- **P-006** `done` Plan-template export/sanitize serializer: strip live state (item statuses → todo, assignees, work-item ids, audit citations, run instances); keep goal/items/decisions/schedule; derive `requires_rubrics` from the acceptance classRef + any rubricRefs the plan names — note: ← WI-40350 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `dropped` Worker migration 016: 'plan' kind (rebuild) + `requires_rubrics` column (JSON array, mirroring requires_events mig 013); pending-review policy blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40351 completed (dropped)\n- **P-008** `done` Client types: 'plan' kind → 'install'; requires_rubrics on HarnessListing; db.ts mirror blocked-by: P-007 — note: ← WI-40352 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Publish path: `cupboard:publish-plan` using the P-006 serializer blocked-by: P-006, P-007 — note: ← WI-40353 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Install path: `cupboard:install-plan` — lands as a plan TEMPLATE row (template_slug model, no live state); instantiate via existing plans machinery blocked-by: P-008 — note: ← WI-40354 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Dependency gating: pre-install requires_rubrics resolution — workspace rubric store first (bundled first-party counts as provided) → cupboard kind='rubric' co-install offer → hard fail if unresolvable (mirrors the events-axis install gate) blocked-by: P-004, P-010 — note: ← WI-40355 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Storefront UI: Plans tab + requires_rubrics display on the detail page BEFORE install blocked-by: P-008 — note: ← WI-40356 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — recipe kind (owner-optional; confirm before starting)\n\n- **P-013** `done` Recipe export/sanitize: strip workspace-scoped authority refs + workspace ids from runArgs; self-describing dir form blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40360 completed (done)\n- **P-014** `done` Worker migration 017: 'recipe' kind + client types + `cupboard:publish-recipe` / `cupboard:install-recipe` (install → code_recipes row, no-clobber) blocked-by: P-013 — note: ← WI-40361 completed (done)\n- **P-015** `done` Storefront UI: Recipes tab blocked-by: P-014 — note: ← WI-40362 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — verification\n\n- **P-016** `done` Tests: worker migration rebuild tests (014 pattern), kind round-trip + listingKindOf, publish/install e2e per new kind, dep-gate cases (satisfied-by-bundle / co-install / unresolvable), cupboard-hygiene-gate update; `npm run test:affected -- --changed-paths ...` green blocked-by: P-005, P-012 — note: ← WI-40531 completed (done)\n\nRADIUS CORRECTION — the first run was invalid, not merely red. It passed 14 changed paths, deriving 5 workspaces; the plan actually touched 37 files, and the omitted ones were apps/operator-public/*. So that run never included @papercusp/cupboard-worker and was STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of testing the worker code this plan changed. The re-run derives AFFECTED_DERIVATION source=explicit changedPaths=37 workspaces=6 guards=13 tasks=21, and includes the worker.\n\nFour tasks (test:lane-pure, test:lane-stateful, operator-vite, web) reported exitStatus=1 on first attempt and passed on the flake-absorbing retry auto-enabled at load1>40 (host was 85-136 throughout, 128 cores). Disclosed rather than silently reported as clean; independent per-file verification below does not depend on those retries.\n\nTHREE REAL REGRESSIONS were found and fixed by this gat…\n\n## Decisions\n\n(none yet — acceptance rubric authored post-implementation per plan-completion discipline)\n\n### D-001 — ONE worker migration (015) adds all three kinds + requires_rubrics, not three sequential rebuilds\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThe draft allotted a separate worker migration per kind (015 rubric / 016 plan / 017 recipe). Each one is a 12-step D1 table REBUILD (widening a CHECK constraint is the only way SQLite allows it — migration 014's header states this), and each rebuild is one-shot, non-idempotent, and carries a prod-verify column-reconciliation ritual. Running three of them sequentially triples that risk and cost for a single logical change.\n\nDECISION: a single `015_plan_rubric_recipe_kinds.sql` widens the listing_kind CHECK to ('harness','blueprint','plugin','pack','knowledge-pack','template','app','rubric','plan','recipe') AND adds the nullable `requires_rubrics` column in the same rebuilt table (the 014 precedent: because we rebuild anyway, new columns are declared in the rebuild rather than tacked on by later ALTERs). Forward-normalizing of the two legacy kind values ('tool-pack'→'pack', 'learning-pack'→'knowledge-pack') is carried over from 014 for the same reason it exists there: the deployed prod schema is not guaranteed to match this repo's migration history 1:1.\n\nConsequence for plan items: P-001 now covers the whole storage side for all three kinds; P-007 and P-014 narrow to their client-types/wire halves only (no further migration). Phases stay independently shippable — a kind whose client wire is unbuilt simply has no rows.\n\n### D-002 — All three new kinds are fail-closed review-policy kinds; requires_rubrics needs no provides_rubrics counterpart\nDate: 2026-08-21\nTWO rulings other lanes/kinds must follow.\n\n(1) REVIEW POLICY — rubric, plan and recipe all join REVIEW_POLICY_KINDS (publish `pending`, publicly invisible until operator approval), for the same reason knowledge-pack and blueprint are there: each is INSTRUCTION-CARRYING content that lands in an agent's context or execution path, not inert data. A rubric supplies the criteria + METHOD.md runbook by which work is GRADED (a hostile one silently corrupts every acceptance verdict it touches); a plan is a goal + item DAG agents EXECUTE — the most directly actuating content the Cupboard carries short of an app; a recipe is a runnable tool orchestration. Following the `app` precedent, they join the list the MOMENT the kinds exist, so no publish path built later can make one public without review.\n\n(2) NO `provides_rubrics` COLUMN — the rubric dependency axis is deliberately asymmetric with the event axis it otherwise mirrors. `requires_events` needed a matching `provides_events` because ONE plugin can register MANY event families, so the provider side had to be enumerated. A `kind='rubric'` row provides exactly ONE rubric — the one named by its own `listing_ref` — so the provider half is already keyed by the existing column and a second column would be a derived duplicate of it (the derived-truth-ladder rule: do not store a second copy of a truth the schema already owns). Resolution therefore reads: workspace rubric store (bundled first-party set INCLUDED) counts as provided → else a `kind='rubric'` listing whose `listing_ref` equals the required `rubricRef` is offered as co-install → else the install is refused.\n\n### D-003 — No papercusp-rubrics-marketplace flag; and the generic install/resolve cores are extracted, not forked\nDate: 2026-08-21\nTWO implementation rulings that depart from the draft.\n\n(1) NO `papercusp-rubrics-marketplace` FLAG. P-004 as drafted said to register it default-ON, because rubric-store.ts's header names it. Reading the precedent it points at shows the flag would gate nothing: cupboard:install-template's own header records that FLAGS.TEMPLATES_MARKETPLACE \"only gates the automatic remote MERGE in templates:list/new-app, not an explicit install-by-url\". cupboard:install-rubric IS an explicit install-by-url — a deliberate user/agent action naming a listing — so there is no automatic remote behaviour to gate. Registering a flag that guards no branch would be an unused durable surface (a review smell), and per the flags rule it would also have to be default-ON, i.e. a no-op entry someone later has to reason about. If an automatic remote-merge is ever added to rubrics:list (the true analogue of TEMPLATES_MARKETPLACE), THAT feature registers the flag, gating the branch it actually introduces.\n\n(2) THE INSTALL PATH IS GENERALIZED, NOT COPIED. install-template-core.ts already implemented \"clone a mirror repo, validate <ref>/ as a self-describing dir, place it in a writable user layer\", hard-wired to templates in exactly four spots (manifest filename, reader, user dir, labels). Copying it for rubric and again for recipe would have duplicated its two SECURITY guards — the `assertInside` path-escape assertion and SAFE_REF_RE — into three hand-maintained copies, the classic shape where a later fix lands in one and silently misses the others. So: NEW `install-self-describing-core.ts` takes a `SelfDescribingKindSpec` and owns the guards once; NEW `resolve-listing-by-kind.ts` does the same for listing resolution, whose kind check is likewise a security property (it is what stops cupboard:install-rubric being aimed at a plugin repo). This is the WRITE-half sibling of the existing self-describing-store.ts, which already shares the READ half on the same reasoning. Ordering inside the generic core is load-bearing: BOTH validations run BEFORE the destructive copy, so a bad publish cannot clobber an already-installed good ref.\n\nConsequence: Phase 3's recipe installer is now a thin kind-spec, not a third copy.\n\n### D-004 — Sanitize a plan by PART SURGERY, not by re-rendering it\nDate: 2026-08-22\nP-006 could have sanitized by `parsePlan` → mutate → `renderPlanMarkdown`. That is the wrong tool and its own header says so: the renderer is \"NOT a byte-for-byte reproduction of free prose\" and \"never reproduces\" the prose body.\n\nA plan's prose IS most of its transferable value — the Background, the survey of alternatives, the why-not notes. Re-rendering would ship an installer a skeleton with the reasoning deleted, which is precisely the half a template exists to carry.\n\nSo `plan-template-serialize.ts` transforms over `splitPlanIntoParts` / `joinPartsIntoPlan` (plan-parser/parts.ts) — the package's own byte-faithful decomposition, whose parts cover 100% of the source as contiguous line ranges. Every part passes through VERBATIM unless a rule names it, and the strip rules key on part KIND (mechanical, total) rather than on pattern-matching the whole document (best-effort, silently incomplete).\n\nStripped: item statuses → `todo`; ` — note:` suffixes (set-status injects these and they routinely name work-items, agents and file paths); the `## Now` run-state block; WI-/EI-/F- ids; identity frontmatter (created/updated/owner/initiative/supersedes). Kept: goal, item DAG with its blocked-by edges, decisions, prose.\n\nNOT stripped because it was never in the content: audit citations live in `harness_shared.plan_audits` (migration 832), not the markdown, and claims are work_items rows. A \"strip the citations\" pass over the markdown would be dead code reading as a guarantee.\n\n### D-005 — plan.md IS the plan-template manifest — no second JSON copy\nDate: 2026-08-22\nEvery other self-describing kind here carries a JSON manifest beside its content (`rubric.json`, `template.yaml`). A plan template deliberately does NOT.\n\nA `plan.json` would be a hand-maintained second copy of facts the markdown already owns: title and slug are frontmatter, the item DAG is the item lines, the rubric requirements are derivable from the body. That is the derived-truth ladder's rung-4 (hand-curated) case with no justification — and it drifts the first time someone edits one of the two.\n\nSo the plan-template dir is `<ref>/plan.md` (the manifest AND the content, parsed by the plan parser the rest of the system already trusts) + `<ref>/listing.json` (storefront presentation only — description, version, item/decision counts, and the published `requires_rubrics` declaration, which is carried so an installed dir cannot declare different dependencies than the listing row the installer read).\n\nConsequence for the installer: `SelfDescribingKindSpec.manifestFile` for the plan kind is `plan.md`, and its `readDir` is the SAME reader the store enumeration uses — so a dir that installs is exactly a dir that will later resolve.\n\nAlso settled here: a disk layer (`~/.papercusp/plan-templates`) exists even though installing ends in a Postgres plan row, because the DB row is WORKSPACE-scoped and the dir is MACHINE-scoped (install once, instantiate in every workspace; a wiped dev DB re-seeds from disk). It also gives the PUBLISH path somewhere to materialize its export — a plan, unlike a rubric, has no dir on disk until something writes one.\n\n### D-006 — New cupboard tools adopt entityRef + the {data} envelope; workspace hard, harness soft\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe six tools this plan adds (cupboard:publish/install-rubric, -plan, -recipe) initially copied their older siblings' shape: `workspace: z.string().max(120).optional()` and a hand-rolled `content:[{ text: JSON.stringify(payload) }]` helper. Both are ratcheted repo-wide and both regressed on this plan's own change:\n\n- entity-ref-conformance: 35 unconverted entity-named args vs baseline 27. All 8 of the excess were this plan's (6 x `workspace`, 2 x `harness`) — 35 - 8 = 27 exactly.\n- tool-data-shape-ratchet: 440 inline-JSON tools vs ceiling 438.\n\nRULING. New tools do NOT inherit a grandfathered sibling's shape. Both were converted rather than baselined:\n\n1. `workspace` -> `entityRef('workspace', { max: 120 }).optional()` on all six. NO resolver is registered for kind 'workspace' (only pot/harness/role are), and `resolveEntityRefs` FAILS OPEN on an unregistered kind, so this is inert today and becomes enforcing for free when a workspace resolver lands — the adopt-then-enforce order the entityRef module documents.\n\n2. `harness` -> `entityRef('harness', { soft: true, max: 120, describe: ... })` on publish-plan/install-plan. A resolver IS registered for 'harness', and no harness arg in the catalog is converted yet, so a HARD ref would make these the first enforced harness args in the system and could reject on resolver-cache staleness. `soft:true` warns instead of rejecting — the same staged-rollout posture the knowledge_packs `pot` conversion used, which is the only prior conversion against a live resolver.\n\n3. `describe` is passed as an entityRef OPTION, never chained. `entityRef('x').describe(...)` returns a CLONE that is not in the marker WeakMap, so the ref is silently inert (EI-17021).\n\n4. The `text()` helper became `ok()` returning `{ data: payload }`. Count returns to 434, under the 438 ceiling. BASELINE was deliberately NOT lowered to 434: no grandfathered tool was migrated here, so the 4 remaining slots are pre-existing churn headroom belonging to other lanes, and tightening it would red the shared gate for whoever lands the next tool.\n\nVerified: entity-ref-conformance converted 8->16, unconverted 27 == baseline; tool-data-shape-ratchet green; lint:tsc operator-core exit=0 clean.\n\n### D-007 — A mid-list INSERT column change must update fake-d1's positional destructure — now mechanically guarded\nDate: 2026-08-22\nAdding `requires_rubrics` (migration 015) mid-list to insertHarness()'s bind order in apps/operator-public/src/db.ts, without updating the POSITIONAL destructure in __tests__/fake-d1.ts, shifted every bind from position 20 on by one: hive_pubkey took requires_rubrics' null, blueprint_kind took hive_title, review_status took blueprint_kind and fell back to its 'approved' default — silently disabling the publish REVIEW GATE in every test exercising it.\n\nCost: 9 red assertions in listings.test.ts + 3 in review.test.ts. Because the shifted columns belong to migrations 007/008/009, the reds pointed at blueprint/hive/review work that was entirely innocent — including a test named \"P-018: a blueprint publish stores + returns blueprint_kind\", while a peer (su-b2cec) was concurrently driving a green checkpoint for P-018/P-019 and held that very file. Misattribution to their lane was the near-miss, not the bug itself.\n\nROOT CAUSE, not the symptom: db.ts's column list and fake-d1's destructure are two source files with no compiler-visible link. fake-d1's header has warned about this in prose since migration 004. Prose is not a guard, and it did not prevent the recurrence of its own documented failure mode.\n\nRULING for any lane touching the harnesses INSERT: the column list, the VALUES row, the .bind() args, AND fake-d1's destructure change together, in the same edit.\n\nGUARD (landed): apps/operator-public/src/__tests__/insert-bind-alignment.test.ts asserts the two arities match, so the next mid-list column fails THERE — naming the real cause — instead of scattering into unrelated feature tests. It carries a vacuous-pass control (both extractors must find >20 entries) and its subject path is env-overridable (PROBE_FAKE_D1), which is how its falsifiability was PROVEN without mutating this shared checkout: pointed at the pre-fix content it fails with \"binds 31 value(s) but fake-d1.ts destructures 30\"; on the real tree it passes.\n\nArity is guarded, not names: the fake deliberately uses short locals (gh_repo_id), so name-equality would be noise, and a same-arity reorder is still unguarded. The durable fix — have fake-d1 parse the column list out of the SQL and map binds BY NAME, retiring both the coupling and this guard — is filed as a follow-up rather than done here, because it rewrites a file a peer was mid-checkpoint in.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"event-system-drift-to-derived-2026-08-21","title":"Event system: derive or pin every hand-authored surface (drift-to-derived)","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Event system: derive or pin every hand-authored surface (drift-to-derived)\nslug: event-system-drift-to-derived-2026-08-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-21\n---\n## Context — the complete drift inventory (verified against code 2026-08-21)\n\nThe event system's spine is EVENT_CATALOG (`packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/catalog.ts`) plus reaction rules, sugar verbs, poll-site hints, and installed-pack manifests. `catalog.test.ts` (406 lines) guards INTERNAL consistency thoroughly (unique families, template↔param agreement, sugar distinctness, unique awaiter-count prefixes, orphan-await matching, near-miss suggestions). What it does NOT guard is agreement with the CODE the entries describe. Every hand-authored surface that can drift, with its current protection:\n\n1. **`emitter` (prose \"label (path)\" strings)** — no guard at all. A moved/renamed emitter file leaves a confident wrong pointer. [Filed: EI-21087476375596978]\n2. **`exists` (hand-set boolean)** — drifts both directions. Emission-removed: nothing catches it at build time. Emission-added-unregistered: found only by hand sweep (EI-18676056143796303 — coord:inbox-wake, the most-fired key in the system, was unregistered).\n3. **`keyTemplate` vs emitted literals** — emitters HAND-WRITE key strings (verified: fleet-drained-events.ts, green-checkpoint.ts import nothing from the catalog). An emitter changing its key format strands catalog + sugar + orphan-guard simultaneously, all still looking authoritative.\n4. **`sugar` (verb name)** — distinctness is tested; EXISTENCE is not. A removed/renamed sugar verb leaves a dangling catalog pointer. (Reverse direction is safe: a verb naming a missing family throws at buildKey.)\n5. **`replacesPoll` (tool names in prose)** — a renamed/retired poll tool leaves stale advice; no guard.\n6. **Payload shapes — entirely implicit.** EventCatalogEntry has NO payload schema field. `payload_filter` / composed-await `when` conditions and `payloadFiltered` caveats are stringly-typed against undeclared shapes; an emitter renaming a payload field silently kills every filter that referenced it.\n7. **Poll-site `awaitable:` hints** — dev:pipeline_position is catalog-sourced (buildKey import verified, L14/L666); the REMAINING poll-site tools are unaudited and may hand-write the keys they advertise.\n8. **Reaction rules** — `on:` / `fire:` are tool-name STRINGS (a renamed tool silently strands the rule; unverified whether registration validates against the tool registry), and declarative condition paths (`result.data.ok`, `args.kind`) are stringly-typed against evolving tool schemas.\n9. **Installed-pack `provides.events` manifests** — trusted verbatim by the events:catalog fold; no attestation that the pack actually fires the families it declares.\n10. **Dynamic per-subject keys outside the catalog** (e.g. session:compacted:&lt;owner&gt;) — the emitted-but-unregistered class; only discoverable by sweeping the audit ledger.\n\n**Existing assets to REUSE (reuse-first — no new parallel systems):** buildKey (the derivation primitive, already used by sugar verbs + pipeline_position); the doc-claims pin pattern (`doc-claims/gate-candidate-ref.test.ts`); the generated-from-the-enforced-registry precedent (`npm run gen:tool-routing`); the audited-fires ledger behind `events:graph { recent:true }` + `live_awaiters`; keyMatchesCatalog (the orphan guard); the EI-18676 sweep method.\n\n## Approach\n\nThree mechanisms, chosen per surface by what the architecture allows:\n- **DERIVE** (best): make the code the source and generate/compute the catalog fields — buildKey at emission sites, CI call-site scan for exists/emitter.\n- **PIN** (where prose must remain): doc-claims-style tests that fail the build on divergence.\n- **RUNTIME ATTESTATION** (where static analysis can't see — dynamic keys, installed packs): formalize the audit-ledger sweep into a standing reconciliation that files drift findings automatically.\n\n**Non-goals:** full runtime self-registration at emission sites (green-checkpoint runs as a separate CLI process; the catalog must render without loading every emitter module — the static-scan + curated-overlay model fits the architecture). `exists:false` declare-ahead families remain supported. `describe`/meaning prose stays curated (semantic drift is a review concern, not mechanically checkable).\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `todo` DERIVE the keys: migrate every `exists:true` emitter to construct its key via `buildKey(family, params)` from the catalog — kills keyTemplate↔emission drift structurally. Audit each emitter's package for importability of the catalog; where impossible (process/package boundary), record a per-family exemption WITH reason. Precedent: sugar verbs + dev:pipeline_position already do this.\n- **P-002** `todo` DERIVE exists + emitter: a generator (`gen:event-catalog-provenance`, following the gen:tool-routing precedent) AST-scans the tree for `buildKey('<family>')` call sites and emits a generated provenance sidecar (family → emitting files). CI fails when an `exists:true` family has zero call sites, an `exists:false` family HAS call sites, or a hand-written emitter path names a file absent from the scan. End state: `exists` and the emitter path list are DERIVED data; only the prose label stays curated. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` PIN what stays prose (doc-claims pattern): for P-001's exempted families, assert the emitter path resolves and the key literal appears in that file; assert every catalog `sugar` verb exists in the tool registry; assert every `replacesPoll` tool name resolves in the registry. Subsumes EI-21087476375596978.\n- **P-004** `todo` DECLARE payload contracts: add optional `payloadSchema` (zod) to EventCatalogEntry; validate at emit time FAIL-SOFT (log + auto-capture on mismatch, never block the emit — the event-delivery fail-soft boundary is load-bearing); validate `payload_filter` / composed-await `when` paths against the declared schema at await-registration time (warn on unknown field). Start with the highest-traffic families (work-item, checkpoint, deploy, fleet transitions).\n- **P-005** `todo` AUDIT poll-site hints: enumerate every tool attaching an `awaitable:` hint; verify each builds its advertised key via buildKey/catalogEntry (pipeline_position verified already); migrate hand-written ones; add a test that every hint key matches a catalog family (reuse keyMatchesCatalog).\n- **P-006** `todo` Reaction-rule reference integrity: at rule registration, validate `on:`/`fire:` strings against the tool registry (loud in dev, logged in prod) — FIRST verify whether any such check already exists in the registration path. Stretch: validate declarative condition paths beginning `args.` against the target tool's zod args schema.\n- **P-007** `todo` RUNTIME ATTESTATION: formalize the emitted-but-unregistered sweep as a standing reconciliation — a system routine diffs the audited-fires ledger against catalog families via keyMatchesCatalog and auto-files improvements for unregistered families and `exists:true`-but-zero-fires-ever anomalies (the overwatch + coord:inbox-wake incident classes, automated). Reuse the EI-18676 sweep method; scheduler-layer rules apply (no bare setInterval).\n- **P-008** `todo` Installed-pack attestation: fold pack-declared `provides.events` families into P-007's reconciliation — a pack family with registered awaits and zero fires ever is a suspected-manifest-drift finding tagged to the pack unit. blocked-by: P-007\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Parked as ready per owner review 2026-08-21 [owner: interactive] — approved as a reference, execute after the demo, not now. Route pre-chosen when it runs: the reviewing su session implements directly (no fleet). Dependency shape: P-001 first; P-003/P-004/P-005/P-006 parallel-safe; P-002 blocked-by P-001; P-008 blocked-by P-007.\n\n**Next:** When the owner gives the go-ahead: plans:start, then begin P-001 (migrate exists:true emitters to buildKey), implemented by the su session that authored this plan.\n\n\n## Phase — Post-landing follow-ups\n\n- **P-009** `todo` Rewrite the catalog header's derivation claim (events/await/catalog.ts:22-23, \"catalog and emitters agree by construction\") once P-001/P-002 land: state the ENFORCED mechanism (emitters build keys via buildKey; gen:event-catalog-provenance CI fails on exists/emitter drift) instead of an authoring-session promise. A comment claiming sync with no recurring check is itself the rung-4 pattern this plan removes (see D-001 context). blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: low\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The emits→reaction wiring is already rung-1 derived — out of migration scope; it is this plan's positive control\nDate: 2026-08-21\nVerified 2026-08-21 (demo Q&A with owner): the `emits` block on a tool def is desugared 1:1 into the reaction registry by collectEmitRules() walking getCollectedToolEmits() — the registered tool defs themselves — with derived rule ids (`emits:${toolName}#${spec.id ?? index}`, emits-desugar.ts:58) and the stated invariant \"emits is sugar, never a parallel path\". There is no second copy to drift, so NO migration work belongs there. Use it as the calibration exemplar of what \"derived\" looks like when classifying: the drift this plan repairs lives ONLY in the catalog's describing metadata (emitter/exists), never in the firing path. [owner: Avi 2026-08-21 — fold-everything directive; content verified from code this session]\n\n### D-002 — Owner ruling: derivation over guards — P-002 REMOVES the hand-authored exists/emitter fields; guards only where a copy cannot be eliminated\nDate: 2026-08-21\n[owner: Avi 2026-08-21, interactive] The owner wants the metadata actually DERIVED from code, not hand-written-plus-guarded. This supersedes the ambiguity in P-002's drafted mechanism text: the required end state is that `exists` and `emitter` are DELETED from the hand-authored EventCatalogEntry type — a field that no longer exists cannot be hand-drifted. The runtime serves them from the generated provenance artifact (gen:event-catalog-provenance output, merged with the curated entry at load); the only CI check that remains is the standard generator-freshness check (gen:*:check pattern, same as AGENT-ENV.md / tool-routing), NOT a comparison between a hand-written copy and the scan. Plan-wide corollary: wherever a check would guard a hand-maintained copy, eliminate the copy instead; a guard/pin is acceptable ONLY where the copy is structurally impossible to eliminate — P-003's cross-boundary emitter families (cannot import the catalog), P-006's on:/fire: tool references (a reference can only be resolved, not derived), P-007/P-008's runtime-only truth — and each surviving guard states its impossibility reason in the implementation.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"exact-session-window-restore-safety-2026-08-20","title":"Exact session resume and desktop-window restoration safety","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Exact session resume and desktop-window restoration safety\nslug: exact-session-window-restore-safety-2026-08-20\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft for owner review. This plan closes the full 2026-08-20 incident chain: unsupported window-loss inference → wrong target termination → silent resume-to-older-history → false success reporting. It extends the existing capability:launch-agent, agent-launch-core, terminal-window, PSU host, and console-spawn surfaces; it does not create a parallel launcher. The already-written Ctrl+C patch is included but is not complete until the running launcher is deployed and live-proven.\n\n## Phase 1 — Make every unsafe state reproducible\n\n- **P-001** `done` **urgent** Add regression fixtures for a later Codex rollout UUID linked to an older original owner identity, plus a live desktop-window witness; reproduce silent history rewind, false windowless classification, and timeout-after-success ambiguity. — note: ← WI-40187 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Exact identity and exact resume\n\n- **P-002** `done` **urgent** Make resume identifiers typed and unambiguous: an exact native session UUID must resolve to that exact transcript, while an owner/agent identity may intentionally resolve its newest resumable transcript; refuse ambiguity or mismatch instead of falling back. `blocked-by: P-001` — note: ← WI-40189 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` **urgent** Verify every resumed launch against the actual backend process/session UUID and requested identity before reporting success; on mismatch, terminate only the newly launched wrong process and return a loud error containing requested vs actual UUIDs. `blocked-by: P-001, P-002` — note: ← WI-40190 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Guarded desktop restoration\n\n- **P-004** `done` **urgent** Add one purpose-built restore-visible operation that resolves the exact session, proves whether its concrete desktop window exists, refuses to terminate a visible/attended session, gracefully winds down only a proven windowless managed host, and exact-resumes into a verified visible terminal. Unknown window state is a refusal, never absence. `blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003` — note: ← WI-40191 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Ctrl+C terminal survival\n\n- **P-005** `done` **urgent** Finish and ship the interactive-supervisor launcher change across shared TypeScript and native desktop paths; preserve sentinel cleanup and nonzero-exit diagnostics, and prove in a real PTY that Ctrl+C kills only the foreground agent while the terminal accepts the next command. `blocked-by: P-001` — note: ← WI-40193 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `todo` **urgent** Force the commit/checkpoint/deploy hops as needed and live-smoke a freshly launched visible desktop terminal against the running operator: press/send Ctrl+C during a foreground probe, verify the same OS window remains open, and verify the updated launcher command—not merely source-on-disk—was exercised. `blocked-by: P-005` — note: ← WI-40195 released\n\n## Phase 5 — Contract and full recurrence guard\n\n- **P-007** `todo` **high** Add end-to-end coverage for visible-window refusal, windowless restoration, exact UUID preservation, timeout-after-success idempotency, mismatch rollback, and live Ctrl+C survival; update the canonical launch guidance so agents cannot hand-compose the unsafe sequence. `blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-006`\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Native session UUID and owner identity are different types\nA native Codex/Claude session UUID means exact transcript history. A Papercusp owner/agent identity means the logical agent and may resolve to its newest resumable native session. No API may silently substitute one interpretation for the other.\n\n### D-002 — Window absence requires a positive desktop witness\nProcess aliveness, PTY metadata, parent command shape, silence, and a human report are not machine proof that a specific session lacks a window. Destructive restoration requires the existing terminal-window surface to positively bind or disprove the window for the exact managed host. Unknown is a refusal, never absence.\n\n### D-003 — Success requires post-launch identity verification\nA spawned terminal, live owner row, or running Codex process is insufficient. Success requires that the actual backend process carries the exact requested native UUID and the expected visible-window witness. Any mismatch is rolled back before returning an error.\n\n### D-004 — Source edit is not a shipped Ctrl+C fix\nThe Ctrl+C defect remains open until the running launch path contains the interactive supervisor and a fresh visible-terminal smoke proves the OS window survives. Unit tests and staging files alone are insufficient.\n\n### D-005 — Release verdict must contain the terminal repair SHA\nDate: 2026-08-21\nFor P-006, a green-checkpoint verdict authorizes deploy only when its bound candidate contains terminal WI-40204 repair SHA 65b369adb8a9eb3fd7a2e3a93ab4eaedcad7c35e. Verify with `git merge-base --is-ancestor 65b369ad <candidate>`; exit 0 is required. The active ed20de6d candidate returns exit 1 and predates the repair, so its verdict is stale for this release even if green. The existing WI-40086 singleton owner must consume that terminal outcome without deploying, then launch exactly one successor whose bound candidate contains 65b369ad.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-006 — Singleton serializer ownership transfers to WI-40195 after the designated owner declines mutation\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 16:29 EDT. Remote origin/staging ce1545d6dd86434f5e92a6ab50a79b4044d97db0 contains TS repair 71172111c44ef65103ee8e1c1e1a6b3643509519 and D-005 floor 65b369adb8a9eb3fd7a2e3a93ab4eaedcad7c35e. release:trace generation 1787344086974 showed no active run-lock and only non-authoritative stale RED-25. The live WI-40086 owner replied that its owner-scoped continuation is read-only and will not launch, then was explicitly told to stay hands-off. Therefore WI-40195 owner su-b20876ff-0961-4da5-9796-c0f4b429235b owns exactly one final empty-run-lock check followed by exactly one release:checkpoint-run. Any raced existing writer is preserved; no duplicate is authorized.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-007 — D-006 launch authority is suspended while the newly claimed WI-40086 lane remains live\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 16:33 EDT. The D-006 preflight did not launch: release:checkpoint-run returned condition_claimed because su-3e0910e0-bd86-446b-b6af-b52d9600a650 claimed WI-40086 at 16:30:27 EDT; presence reports that holder parked but wakeable on release-critical P-014. No run was created. Do not force past this live claim. The holder has been woken with one required disposition: launch exactly one current-tip checkpoint and report its immutable identity, or explicitly release WI-40086 if its route forbids mutation. D-006 resumes only after a live empty-run-lock plus released/stranded claim is verified.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-008 — Serializer authority follows the live WI-40086 assignee, not a transient owner ID\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 16:46 EDT. WI-40086 has rotated from su-271f to su-3e091 to su-a14c while release recovery reconciles claims. D-006/D-007 remain the no-duplicate rule, but no downstream lane may treat a named historical owner as current authority.
