Before any checkpoint mutation, re-read work_items:get WI-40086 plus release:trace in the same window. A live assignee owns the singleton and must be driven directly; a rotated/released assignee is no longer the serializer. Current assignee su-a14c was required-woken with the two live dirty units and must hold launch until the tree is clean, origin/staging equals the completed HEAD containing 71172111 and 65b369ad, and the run-lock remains empty.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-009 — CORRECTION — checkpoint candidate is cut from local staging HEAD; remote egress is not an admission precondition\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 16:56 EDT. RETRACTION of the remote-backed clause in D-008 and the 16:52–16:53 WI-40195 checkpoints/messages: I incorrectly required origin/staging to contain P-017 commit 8344fbf5 before launch. The live enforced contract in packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/gate-candidate-ref.test.ts proves green-checkpoint cuts candidate from the LOCAL integration branch and MUST NOT fetch or resolve origin/staging first; packages/operator-core/lib/release-checkpoint-launch.ts currentCheckpointCandidate resolves git rev-parse HEAD. Therefore clean local HEAD 5b7223ae5b258a104289bf661460b0c51b4cea56, which contains P-017 and required repairs, is launch-eligible even while origin/staging lags. D-008 still governs live-assignee/run-lock singleton authority; only its remote-backed admission clause is superseded. Recheck local cleanliness, candidate ancestry, current WI-40086 assignee, and run-lock in one window, then launch exactly one checkpoint.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-010 — WI-40292 affected-radius red is not checkpoint admission; the fresh checkpoint is the authoritative verdict\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 16:58 EDT. WI-40292's own checkpoint states its affected run only reads the committed tree and is not an admission blocker for the WI-40086 gate. Owner su-0eea classified all eight failing files as pre-dating WI-40292 commit d6c25fa2, with zero attributable failures, and directed peers to stop waiting on it. This does NOT assert those eight failures are healthy or dismiss a red gate. It means serializer admission remains clean/local-candidate/run-lock based under D-009, and the full checkpoint must run now to produce the authoritative current verdict. If that fresh verdict is red, diagnose and fix its exact failures before deploy; do not deploy or call the gate green.\nRelated: P-006\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21","title":"Fleet friction remediation — correct contracts, fast wakes, and recoverable drains","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Fleet friction remediation — correct contracts, fast wakes, and recoverable drains\nslug: fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-10-10\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** 10 of 13 items DONE (2026-09-05T02:16Z, leader su-44b47b2b). Phases 0-4 implementation is essentially complete — every item through Phase 4 is terminal except the two named below. P-007 (WI-2144779) closed at 02:05Z on unusually strong evidence: blob-equality rather than a clean `git status`, gitlink containment proved for migration 1118, and a falsifiable concurrency test (4 concurrent attestations against maxChain 2). Its cited lint:tsc predated the final guard fix, so I re-ran `lint:tsc --files` over the full 7-file changed set myself at 02:09:47Z (status=clean, head c8bdf1d79e); the close stands on independent evidence.\n\nLIVE FRONTIER — two items. P-009 (WI-2144781): all 5 named surfaces landed and verified; the ONLY thing blocking close is mapping the 6 acceptance scenarios to named tests. Its original holder su-8fe41063 DIED at ~02:02:54Z (pid 1994861 gone; presence still rendered `suspect` while the same payload's coupling detail read \"counterpart ended\" — filed as EI-22385966854978352), so at 02:12Z I force-reclaimed on basis `holder-not-live` and reassigned to su-4874d15e with a full handover at comment 83973. P-011 (WI-2144783) is held by su-4b480272, running the CHECK-FIRST already-fixed pass over the 4 residual contract gaps before writing code.\n\nPHASE 5 AHEAD. P-012 now blocks on the two live items alone; P-013 blocks on P-012. P-012's runnable half — the focused suites across the ten completed lanes — needs neither live item.\n\nSHIP GATE NOT STARTED. All-items-terminal will NOT finish this plan: it still owes a per-item code-truth audit (`plans:audit`, code/test citations only) and a post-implementation acceptance rubric graded by a NON-implementer outside the rubric author's spawn lineage. `acceptance.rubricActive` is false. Route that grading to an existing live session; a grader launched by the rubric author is ineligible by construction. D-007's execution-route gate remains unresolved and is left standing, not discharged.\n\n**Next:** su-4874d15e finishes the 6-scenario-to-test mapping and closes P-009 (WI-2144781), then starts P-012's runnable half without waiting for P-011.\n\n## Goal\n\nRemove the nine fleet-friction classes proven by WI-40280 so a large bug-drain fleet spends its turns on work rather than tool-contract mismatches, lost results, repeated orientation, ambiguous scope, compaction ceremony, misleading release state, or unrecoverable members.\n\nThe plan is implementation-ready but remains a proposal. It is deliberately **draft** until Avi reviews the scope and chooses the execution route.\n\n## Source and baseline\n\n- Audit: WI-40280, Claude session `86d58760-a7c2-492c-9e03-aa5ff98b6808`.\n- Report: `/home/marsh-office/.papercusp/scratch/owner-reports/luna-max-drain-audit.html`.\n- Fleet/window reported by the audit: `nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820`, 2026-08-20 21:00Z through 2026-08-21 14:00Z.\n- Primary already-filed issues: EI-21085901530859364 (invalid-input drift repair) and EI-21085909106162110 (Codex result-door continuation).\nAudit baseline note: the audit's numbers are planning baselines, not unquestioned acceptance measurements. P-001 must re-run each metric from the writer that defines its units before any implementation lane reports improvement.\n\n## Scope\n\n1. Repair taught-but-invalid tool argument shapes and add a durable drift-repair loop.\n2. Make result-door continuation byte-complete and usable from Codex, Claude, OMP, direct calls, and nested dispatch; record refusal reasons.\n3. Keep semantic/embedding consumers healthy under fleet concurrency and make degradation explicit everywhere.\n4. Add a fast member delta-orient path and reduce redundant ambient telemetry without weakening liveness.\n5. Infer unique harness scope from existing session/fleet/plan/work-item bindings.\n6. Make compaction flush requirements precise and cheap to satisfy.\n7. Make release traces distinguish a dead automated fixer from a live repair owner.\n8. Give fleet leaders a bounded, idempotent recovery path for wedged/context-critical members.\n9. Deliver Codex-specific execution guardrails to fresh sessions and enforce deterministic traps where possible.\nResidual scope: close four small contract gaps only where P-001 proves they still exist: inbox time bounds, pg-query result shape, claimable-query timeouts, and reasonless refusals.\n\n## Reuse and adjacent-plan boundaries\n\nArgument-contract reuse: extend the generic tool schema/dispatch and existing issue-occurrence ledger for argument repair; do not create a second telemetry or issue system. `state-plane-interest-and-hardening-2026-08-21#P-006` fixed one tool and is the precedent, not duplicate scope.\n- Extend the existing result door and `capability:read`/dispatch continuation contract. `named-result-views-schema-stable-recovery-capsules-with-proj-2026-08-14` is adjacent: it owns stable named projections and recovery views, not byte continuation or Codex authorization. Reuse its receipts and versioning conventions.\n- Extend the existing embedding client/sidecar and generic hybrid-search leg health; do not stand up another embedding service.\nOrient coordination: coordinate P-005 with the still-open items in `fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21`. That plan owns leader snapshot content; this plan owns orient latency, member deltas, and hook-call economics. Serialize any shared-file edits through locks and the live holder.\n- Extend `_harness-scope`, compaction, `release-trace`, fleet registry/respawn, and existing Codex runtime-boundary guidance in place.\nRelease boundary: `gate-stop-chasing-the-tip-2026-08-19` owns frozen-candidate repair mechanics. P-008 only fixes truthful ownership display.\nCodex-guidance reuse: the existing `codex-functions-exec-runtime-boundary` agent insight is the documentation base for P-010; the gap is delivery/coverage and deterministic guards, not creation of a second guide.\n\n## Success criteria\n\n- Every captured taught argument shape either canonicalizes unambiguously or the generated client guidance teaches the accepted schema; truly unknown keys still fail loudly.\n- A response above the door cap reconstructs exactly, with checksum/offset continuity, on every supported client and nested dispatch; any refusal has a stored reason.\n- In the audit-shaped concurrency replay, repeated identical semantic queries coalesce/cache, semantic consumers stay within the measured budget, and forced backend failure produces explicit degraded markers rather than silent lexical-only success.\nOrient acceptance: member delta-orient preserves truth parity with full orient, meets the P-001 latency/size budget, and ambient activity/glance traffic falls materially without weakening death/stall detection.\n- No `harness_required` occurs when exactly one valid binding chain exists; ambiguous chains fail with candidates.\n- A clean compaction request succeeds without no-op checkpoint churn; an unclean request enumerates the exact remaining obligations.\n- Release trace never says simply “owner gone” while a live work-item owner exists.\n- Kill failure and context-critical state converge to one explicit terminal disposition—recovered, benched/stranded, or actionable failure—without duplicate replacements or lost claims.\n- Fresh Codex sessions receive the runtime-boundary guardrails, and deterministic traps fail before executing the malformed command.\n- Focused tests, affected tests, audit-shaped replay, independent acceptance, and the normal green pipeline all pass before the plan ships.\n\n## Requirements\n\nFirst-class restatement of obligations this plan already carries in its Goal, Scope, Success criteria, Non-goals and Execution safety sections. No new scope is introduced here; each clause names the section or item it is drawn from so it can be audited against the original.\n\n### Functional requirements (one per Scope lane)\n\n**R-01 — Tool-contract truth [Scope 1 → P-002].** Taught-but-invalid tool argument shapes must be repaired and a durable drift-repair loop must exist. Executable call facts (tool names, availability, argument keys, required fields, enum values, aliases, retry shapes) must derive from the live projected registry, the client-filtered tool surface and the live scope/admission predicate — never independently from hand-authored prose (D-005). Strict unknown-argument rejection is preserved; permissive input swallowing is explicitly excluded (Non-goals).\n\n**R-02 — Result continuity [Scope 2 → P-003].** Result-door continuation must reconstruct exactly, with checksum/offset continuity, on every supported client (Codex, Claude, OMP, direct calls) and through nested dispatch. Every refusal must persist a stored reason.\n\n**R-03 — Semantic health under load [Scope 3 → P-004].** Semantic/embedding consumers must remain within the writer-backed budget under fleet concurrency; identical queries must coalesce or cache; and forced backend failure must mark every consumer explicitly degraded rather than reporting semantic dedupe/search as successful.\n\n**R-04 — Cheap truthful orientation [Scope 4 → P-005].** A member delta-orient path must be truth-equivalent to full orient at the same cursor, must meet the P-001 latency/size budget, and must materially reduce ambient telemetry share without weakening death/stall detection latency or audit attribution.\n\n**R-05 — Unambiguous scope inheritance [Scope 5 → P-006].** Unique harness scope must resolve from existing session/fleet/plan/work-item bindings through a single precedence chain. `harness_required` must not occur when exactly one valid binding chain exists; multiple valid chains must fail deterministically with the candidates and conflicting bindings, never a guess.\n\n**R-06 — Precise compaction flush [Scope 6 → P-007].** A clean agent must compact in one request without no-op checkpoint churn. A refusal must enumerate the exact stale held items and missing evidence; bounded writes must append or refresh rather than fail opaquely at the row cap; and an unchanged attestation must not be able to conceal changed state.\n\n**R-07 — Truthful release ownership [Scope 7 → P-008].** Release trace must report automated-fixer state separately from the live singleton work-item holder, including liveness and progress freshness, and must never emit a bare owner-gone while a live repair owner holds the item. Frozen-candidate repair behaviour is unchanged.\n\n**R-08 — Recoverable members [Scope 8 → P-009].** Leaders must have a bounded, idempotent recovery path for wedged and context-critical members. Kill failure, ignored wake, dead PID, context-critical claim, duplicate leader request and leader crash must each converge to exactly one explicit terminal disposition — recovered, benched/stranded, or actionable failure — with no duplicate replacements, no lost claims, and no indefinitely live wedge.\n\n**R-09 — Client execution guardrails [Scope 9 → P-010].** A newly launched Codex session must demonstrably receive the runtime-boundary guidance, and deterministic traps must fail before the malformed command executes, while valid templates, heredocs and patches remain accepted.\n\n**R-10 — Residual contract gaps [Scope residual → P-011].** The four residual gaps — coord:inbox `since` boundary, dev:pg_query envelope shape, work_items:claimable statement timeouts, and refusal-reason persistence — must be closed only where P-001 still reproduces them. A falsified or already-fixed gap closes with evidence and no duplicate implementation.\n\n### Evidence and acceptance requirements\n\n**R-11 — Writer-backed measurement (D-002).** No lane may report a number or percentage until P-001 has identified and read the writer/query defining its units, client scope, error taxonomy and time window. P-012 and P-013 must compare the same definitions at exact recorded revisions; a changed query definition is disclosed as a metric migration, never as product improvement.\n\n**R-12 — Recurrence guards ship with the fix (Execution safety).** Each implementation item ships its recurrence guard in the repository test framework. A typecheck alone is not acceptance.\n\n**R-13 — Full verification before ship (Success criteria).** Focused tests, affected tests, the audit-shaped replay, independent acceptance and the normal green pipeline must all pass before the plan ships. Any miss reopens the owning implementation item rather than being waived.\n\n### Constraint requirements\n\n**R-14 — Extend canonical surfaces (D-001).** Every lane extends its existing canonical surface. New stores, registries, services, schedulers or lifecycle planes are out of scope unless a current-head trace in P-001 proves no canonical surface can express the fix.\n\n**R-15 — Explicit exclusions (Non-goals).** Do not rebuild metrics owned by `fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21`, rework frozen-candidate release repair, replace strict unknown-argument rejection with permissive swallowing, or add compatibility aliases for ambiguous or obsolete semantics.\n\n**R-16 — Serialize shared hot files (D-003, Execution safety).** Lanes may run concurrently only where their resolved current-head file sets are disjoint. Shared hot files — generic dispatch, tool invocation logging, orient folds and the fleet registry — must be serialized through the enforced lock system rather than launched as competing fixes.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- Rebuilding fleet metrics already owned by `fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21`.\n- Reworking frozen-candidate release repair.\n- Replacing strict unknown-argument rejection with permissive input swallowing.\n- Adding compatibility aliases for ambiguous or obsolete semantics.\n- Creating parallel result stores, scope registries, embedding services, schedulers, or fleet lifecycle systems.\n\n## Execution safety\n\nExecution precondition: P-001 records exact current writers, units, files, tests, live holders, and neighboring decisions before implementation.\n- Lanes may run in parallel only when their resolved file sets are disjoint. Shared hot files—generic dispatch, tool invocation logging, orient folds, and fleet registry—must be serialized through the enforced lock system.\n- Each implementation item ships its recurrence guard in the repository test framework. A typecheck alone is not acceptance.\n- A red release gate encountered during execution is part of this plan's path to green; diagnose and fix it, rerun the verdict after the quiet cut includes the fix, then deploy the green pin.\n\n\n## Design\n\nHow this plan is built, drawn from its phase structure, its recorded Decisions D-001..D-006 and its Execution safety section. This is a first-class restatement of design already agreed in the plan; it introduces no new approach.\n\n### Governing design invariants\n\nD-001 — Extend canonical surfaces, never add a parallel control plane. Each lane has one named extension point: generic schema/dispatch plus the occurrence ledger (P-002), the result door plus capability-read/dispatch continuation (P-003), the existing embedding client and generic search-leg health (P-004), coord read cursors/orient and existing hooks (P-005), the `_harness-scope` resolver (P-006), the compaction continuation gate (P-007), release-trace (P-008), the fleet registry/process-kill/scheduler bench model (P-009), and the existing Codex runtime-boundary insight and prompt projection (P-010). A new store, registry, service, scheduler or lifecycle plane is admissible only if a current-head trace in P-001 proves no canonical surface can express the fix.\n\nD-002 — Writer-backed metrics are the acceptance authority. The WI-40280 report is the planning baseline only. P-001 freezes the baseline and thresholds by reading the actual writer/query behind each metric; P-012 and P-013 then compare the same definitions at exact recorded revisions.\n\nD-005 — Executable guidance is generated; prose owns intent, not call contracts. The projected tool registry, the client-filtered tool surface and the live scope/admission predicate are the authorities for executable facts. Prompt prose may own workflow semantics — when, why, sequence, safety rationale — but may not independently own call shapes. Examples are produced through schema-backed fragments/macros or rejected by deterministic registry-conformance checks, so a stale contract fails render/CI before release rather than teaching an agent a wrong shape. Semantic contradiction scanning stays a secondary detection rail, not the source of truth.\n\n### Phase structure and sequencing\n\nThe plan is an evidence gate followed by four implementation phases and a proof phase. Phase 0 (P-001) freezes current-HEAD evidence, ownership, writers, units, files, tests and live holders; every other item is blocked-by P-001 so no lane may begin from the report alone. Phase 1 (P-002, P-003) repairs contract and result integrity, the two surfaces every other lane's diagnostics travel through. Phase 2 (P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007) addresses performance and scope: semantic saturation, orient cost, harness-scope inheritance and the compaction flush gate. Phase 3 (P-008, P-009) restores fleet truth and member recoverability. Phase 4 (P-010, P-011) delivers client guardrails and closes the residual contract gaps that P-001 still reproduces. Phase 5 (P-012, P-013) is system proof: a cross-lane audit-shaped scale replay, then independent non-implementer acceptance, gate-green on the exact revision, and a bounded drain canary.\n\n### Concurrency design\n\nD-003 — Parallelize by resolved file set, not by finding count. After P-001, lanes proceed concurrently only where their current-head file sets are disjoint. Three explicit hot zones must be serialized rather than run as competing fixes: generic dispatch and invocation logging (P-002, P-003, P-011), orient and fleet-snapshot folds (P-005, shared with `fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21`), and fleet lifecycle/process-kill paths (P-009). Live holders and plan decisions are re-read before editing, and the enforced file lock serializes each atomic edit. P-005 additionally partitions ownership with the adjacent metrics plan: that plan owns leader snapshot content, this one owns per-fold latency budgets, member cursors/deltas, full-orient fallback and ambient-call batching.\n\n### Placement and claim-scope design\n\nD-006 — Pre-promotion plan lanes require feature-admitting claim scope. Pre-promotion P-NNN assignment subjects are constructed with `kind='feature'`, so a goal-drain fleet spec whose effective kind leaves are bug/change/task will refuse them even when the plan slug is explicitly allowed. Until EI-22042825344838662 lands, a goal-drain member assigned P-006..P-011 must receive an exact per-member claim spec admitting its plan and plan_item before `plan_items:assign`, and must not use generic `scheduler:get_next` for that lane. The override is cleared when the lane ends. Implementation is routed to launched members, never to the GOAL steward, and the non-P2P fence is preserved.\n\n### Verification design\n\nEvery implementation item ships its own recurrence guard in the repository test framework; a typecheck alone is not acceptance. P-012 executes the focused suites, affected tests, schema/prompt generation checks, the cross-client continuation matrix, a forced semantic-degradation drill, orient truth-parity and load replay, ambiguous-scope cases, compaction concurrency cases, the release-owner matrix and fleet-recovery fault injection together, comparing only writer-verified units from P-001 and recording raw run identities plus exact revisions. A miss reopens the owning implementation item instead of being waived. P-013 then requires an independent non-implementing grader, gate-green on the exact staging revision through the normal green deployment path, and a bounded drain canary compared against the P-001 baseline. A red release gate met during execution is part of this plan's path to green: diagnose it, fix forward, rerun the verdict once the quiet cut includes the fix, then deploy the green pin.\n\n## Phase 0 — Reproduce and pin truth\n\n- **P-001** `done` Freeze the current-HEAD evidence and ownership matrix before changing code. Re-run the WI-40280 invocation-ledger queries from the code/SQL writers that define each metric; reproduce all nine findings plus the four small gaps; record exact units, client/runtime versions, schema revisions, current source files/tests, live file holders, neighboring plan decisions, and target thresholds. Close any lane already fixed at HEAD with a recurrence test instead of reimplementing it. Acceptance: one checkpointed evidence pack maps every finding to a current reproduction or falsification, a writer-backed metric, an owning surface, and an unambiguous test plan. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40319 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract and result integrity\n\n- **P-002** `done` Make executable tool guidance a projection of the live accepted contract, then adopt EI-21085901530859364. First map every delivery path that can teach an agent a tool name, availability claim, argument shape, required field, alias, or corrective retry: the projected registry and tools/list surface, tools:find/tools:invoke, coord:orient taskToolSchemaPack, renderWireSchemasSection/renderSuPlaybook and client overlays, per-tool guidance, and shared error builders such as HARNESS_REQUIRED_DETAIL. Preserve authored workflow semantics (when, why, and sequence), but stop prose from owning executable call shapes: add schema-backed prompt macros or generated fragments for tool examples and availability; derive invalid-input corrections from the same registry plus the live client/scope admission predicate; retain only explicit semantically unambiguous aliases with provenance. Extend the existing guidance-adapter/contradiction rail with deterministic registry conformance, and fail render/CI on an unavailable tool, undeclared or missing required key, invalid enum literal, stale hard-coded remedy, or client-specific capability claim absent from that client's filtered surface. Migrate the measured rejection corpus and feed repeated clusters through the existing issue-occurrence pipeline. Acceptance: across supported clients and direct/nested dispatch, a registry change automatically updates every rendered signature, availability statement, and corrective retry without a second hand edit; deleting or renaming a tool/required arg makes generation or CI fail before release; the reproduced plans:get harness_required → harness:'all' → harness_forbidden contradiction is a pinned regression fixture; the improvements:capture toolFailure shorthand either becomes a canonical schema-backed shorthand or generated guidance includes every required field; truly unknown or ambiguous keys still fail loudly; live launch context, tools/list_changed, tools:find, orient schema pack, and invalid-input errors report one registry revision/provenance. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← EI-21085901530859364 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Make result-door continuation exact and cross-client, adopting EI-21085909106162110. Extend the existing result door and capability:read/dispatch continuation path—not a new result store—with caller-scoped cursor authorization, consistent file_path/URI instructions per client, offset/checksum receipts, and support through direct calls plus tools:invoke nesting. Persist refusal error_code/error_message at the invocation writer. Reuse the named-result-view plan's receipt/version conventions without taking over its projection scope. Acceptance: payloads above the cap reconstruct byte-for-byte on Codex, Claude, OMP, ptool, and nested dispatch; expired/foreign cursors fail loudly; no continuation response is silently empty; every refusal row has a reason; repository tests cover cap boundaries, multi-page reads, auth, and encoding. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← EI-21085909106162110 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Performance and scope\n\n- **P-004** `done` Remove semantic/embedding saturation as a fleet-load failure. Extend the existing embedding client/sidecar and generic hybrid-search leg health with normalized exact-query coalescing/cache, bounded priority/admission so fleet bursts do not starve interactive consumers, and a consistent degraded-mode receipt on every semantic consumer (tools:find, work-item search/admission dedupe, memory/context retrieval, and other registered legs). Acceptance: an audit-shaped concurrency replay stays within the writer-backed P-001 budget with no semantic timeouts; identical queries dispatch at most one embed per valid cache/coalescing window; forced backend failure marks every consumer degraded and never reports semantic dedupe/search as successful; recovery clears the marker without restart. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-2012159 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add a cheap, truthful member delta-orient and reduce redundant ambient telemetry. Coordinate shared files with the live holders of fleet-spec-scoped-metrics P-005/P-007/P-009: that plan owns leader snapshot content; this item owns per-fold latency budgets, member cursors/deltas, full-orient fallback, and activity:report/coord:glance batching or sampling that preserves liveness semantics. Acceptance: delta and full orient are truth-equivalent at the same cursor; forced cursor loss falls back safely; the audit-shaped replay meets the P-001 p95 latency/size threshold and materially reduces ambient-call share; death/stall detection latency and audit attribution do not regress; per-fold measurements identify future budget breaches. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-2098700 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Make unique harness scope inheritance work consistently. Extend the canonical _harness-scope resolver with a single precedence chain—explicit argument, claimed work item, bound plan, fleet, then session—and apply it to plans:get/items, scheduler:get_next, nested tools:invoke, coord:presence, and every audit-reproduced caller. Never guess across multiple valid harnesses: return the candidates and the conflicting bindings. Acceptance: bound-session integration tests eliminate harness_required whenever exactly one chain resolves; ambiguous and stale bindings fail deterministically; cross-harness isolation remains intact; the scope-default lint guards new tools from bypassing the resolver. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2105007 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Make the compaction flush gate precise and cheap. Extend session:request-compaction and the existing checkpoint/continuation gate so a refusal enumerates the exact stale held items and missing evidence, an explicit unchanged attestation refreshes a genuinely unchanged item without prose churn, and bounded writes append/refresh rather than failing opaquely at the 12-row cap. Acceptance: the audit's 18-agent/37-refusal pattern is reproduced pre-fix and eliminated post-fix; a clean agent compacts in one request; a dirty agent receives a complete actionable list; unchanged attestations cannot conceal changed state; cap and concurrency tests prevent lost checkpoint evidence. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2144779 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Fleet truth and recovery\n\n- **P-008** `done` Make release ownership truthful without changing frozen-candidate repair. Extend release-trace's existing writer/view to report automated fixer state separately from the current live singleton work-item holder, including liveness and progress freshness; use the canonical work-item/presence sources rather than another ownership registry. Acceptance: the trace never emits a bare owner-gone while a live repair owner holds the item; test every auto-fixer/live-owner combination, stale progress, claim release, and handoff; the red-gate UI/CLI render the same structured truth; gate-stop-chasing-the-tip behavior is unchanged. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2144780 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Give leaders bounded, idempotent recovery for wedged and context-critical members. Extend fleet:respawn-member, process-kill, transition events, scheduler claim gating, and the existing bench/strand model so kill failure freezes and marks the old member, preserves or safely releases claims, and launches at most one replacement only after a durable recovery token; auto-bench context-critical members before claim evaluation. Acceptance: injected kill failure, ignored wake, dead PID, context-critical claim, duplicate leader request, and leader crash all converge to recovered, benched/stranded, or actionable-failure state—never duplicate replacements, lost claims, or an indefinitely live wedge; transition events and leader brief carry the reason. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: Completed via WI-2144781. Implementation landed by su-8fe41063 across 5 surfaces; taken over on the leader's dead-holder ruling (independently confirmed: sessionState 'ended', wakeable false, claims 0) and closed after re-verification against current HEAD — 472 passed / 0 failed across 10 files, lint:tsc clean over all 19 changed paths. The gap that agent named honestly in their handover — the 6 acceptance scenarios never mapped to specific tests — is now mapped in the completion evidence, all 6 to literal describe('acceptance: …') blocks, with falsifiability controls checked rather than assumed.\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Client guardrails and residual gaps\n\n- **P-010** `done` Deliver and enforce Codex runtime-boundary guardrails. Extend the existing codex-functions-exec-runtime-boundary insight and canonical Codex prompt/projection rather than creating another guide; cover functions.exec JavaScript interpolation, shell/heredoc quoting, and apply_patch atomic-update constraints; add pre-execution/static guards and targeted diagnostics wherever a trap is deterministic. Follow the persona render/edit runbook for any prompt change. Acceptance: a newly launched Codex session demonstrably receives the guidance; scenario tests catch the known malformed forms before side effects; valid templates/heredocs/patches remain accepted; generated/materialized prompt tests prove the canonical edit reaches live launch context. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2144782 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Close the four small residual contract gaps only where P-001 still reproduces them: add a cursor-compatible since boundary to coord:inbox; normalize dev:pg_query describe/SELECT envelopes or publish one explicit discriminated union; remove work_items:claimable statement timeouts through query/index/bound work rather than a wider timeout; and finish reason persistence for any refusal paths not covered by P-003. Execute every focused suite, affected tests, schema/prompt generation checks, cross-client continuation matrix, forced semantic-degradation drill, orient truth-parity/load replay, ambiguous-scope cases, compaction concurrency cases, release-owner matrix, and fleet recovery fault injection. Goal work-on-everything-070565 was auto-killed 2026-09-05T02:17:39Z on a spend-floor breach (59,083c vs a 50,000c/7d budget); goal-stop-fanout disarmed the leader loop and the fleet stood down at 02:35Z. This item went claimable only because P-009 and P-011 closed, so the scheduler would hand a full cross-lane verification + scale replay to any live agent, whose spend rolls up to the dead goal.
