Blocked by fleet leader su-44b47b2b.\n- **P-013** `todo` Independent acceptance, pipeline, and live canary. Have a non-implementing reviewer grade every success criterion from the evidence, then carry the exact staging revision through affected/full gate verification and the normal green deployment path (respect the checkpoint quiet cut so the verdict actually includes the fix). Run a bounded drain canary and compare rejected-input rate, spill recovery, semantic health, orient cost, scope errors, compaction attempts, false ownership alarms, and member-recovery outcomes against P-001. Acceptance: independent verdict green, gate green on the exact revision, live canary green with no new queue amplification, source issues linked/terminaled with evidence, and the plan marked shipped only after all owners and units are re-read live. blocked-by: P-012 importance: urgent\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Extend canonical surfaces; no parallel control planes\nDate: 2026-08-21\nImplement every lane by extending its existing canonical surface: generic schema/dispatch plus occurrence ledger (P-002), result door plus capability-read/dispatch (P-003), existing embedding client and generic search leg health (P-004), coord read cursors/orient and existing hooks (P-005), _harness-scope (P-006), compaction continuation gate (P-007), release-trace (P-008), fleet registry/process-kill/scheduler bench model (P-009), and the existing Codex runtime-boundary insight/prompt projection (P-010). New stores, registries, services, schedulers, or lifecycle planes are out of scope unless a current-head trace in P-001 proves no canonical surface can express the fix.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011\n\n### D-002 — Writer-backed metrics are the acceptance authority\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThe WI-40280 report is the planning baseline, but no lane may report a number or percentage until P-001 identifies and reads the writer/query that defines its units, client scope, error taxonomy, and time window. P-001 freezes the baseline and thresholds; P-012 and P-013 compare the same definitions and exact revisions. A changed query definition is disclosed as a metric migration, never presented as product improvement.\nRelated: P-001, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-003 — Parallelize by resolved file set, not by finding count\nDate: 2026-08-21\nAfter P-001, lanes may proceed concurrently only where their current-head file sets are disjoint. Generic dispatch/invocation logging (P-002/P-003/P-011), orient/fleet snapshot folds (P-005 and fleet-spec-scoped-metrics), and fleet lifecycle/process-kill paths (P-009) are explicit hot zones. Live holders and plan decisions are re-read before editing; the enforced file lock serializes each atomic edit. Same-file lanes are sequenced rather than launched as competing fixes.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-005, P-009, P-011\n\n### D-004 — Plan stays draft until owner review and route selection\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThis plan is the requested proposal, not implementation authorization. Do not call plans:start, promote items, claim implementation lanes, edit product code, or launch a fleet until Avi approves the scope and selects who executes it. When approved, starting the plan promotes the lanes; the two pre-existing issues EI-21085901530859364 and EI-21085909106162110 are adopted into P-002/P-003 so promotion does not create duplicate work.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-005 — Executable guidance is generated; prose owns intent, not call contracts\nDate: 2026-08-21\nAvi approved the plan scope with a deeper P-002: guidance drift must be structurally prevented, not merely detected and patched. The projected tool registry, the current client-filtered tool surface, and the live scope/admission predicate are the authorities for executable facts: tool names, availability, argument keys, required fields, enum values, aliases, and corrective retry shapes. Human-authored prompt prose may own workflow semantics—when, why, sequence, safety rationale—but may not independently own executable call shapes. Reuse and extend the existing prompt assembly/renderWireSchemasSection, tools discovery, coord:orient taskToolSchemaPack, invalid-input error builders, and guidance-adapter corpus. Exact examples are generated through schema-backed fragments/macros or rejected by deterministic registry-conformance checks; a stale or unavailable contract fails render/CI before release. Semantic contradiction scanning remains a secondary detection rail, not the source of truth.\nRelated: P-002, P-010, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-006 — Pre-promotion plan lanes require feature-admitting claim scope\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plan-items/assign.ts constructs every pre-promotion P-NNN assignment subject with kind='feature'. The live goal-drain fleet spec goal-work-on-everything-070565-worklist-without-nonp2p rev 13 contains intersecting kind leaves whose effective set is bug/change/task, so it refused P-006 even though the plan slug was explicitly allowed. Decision: until EI-22042825344838662 lands, any goal-drain member assigned P-006..P-011 must receive an exact per-member claim spec admitting its plan + plan_item before plan_items:assign; the member must not use generic scheduler:get_next for that lane. Clear the override when the lane ends. Preserve the non-P2P fence and route implementation to launched members, never the GOAL steward.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011\n\n### D-007 — Spec-triad admission repaired; D-004's route gate left standing, not discharged\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured 2026-09-05 (WI-2144547, workspace papercusp-workspace, harness papercusp).\n\nWhy the plan was inadmissible: it was created 2026-08-21, after SPEC_TRIAD_EPOCH_DEFAULT 2026-08-09 (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-triad-policy.ts), and declared neither `specTriad: required` nor `specTriad: exempt`, so specTriadGate held every item back from `actionable` and fleet:launch-on-plan refused with specTriadBlocked=true. The detector (libs/generic/plan-parser/src/spec-triad.ts, evaluateSpecTriad) requires an `## Requirements` and an `## Design` H2 section each carrying at least SPEC_TRIAD_MIN_BODY_CHARS (40) of non-placeholder body. The third leg, tasks, was already satisfied by the plan’s 13 P-NNN items.\n\nRepair: first-class `## Requirements` and `## Design` sections were written as a faithful restatement of obligations and design ALREADY carried by this plan in its Goal, Scope, Success criteria, Non-goals, Execution safety and D-001..D-006. Every requirement clause cites the Scope lane, item or decision it derives from, so the section is auditable against the original. No new scope and no new approach were introduced.\n\nRe-measured after the repair, through the same gate that enforces actionability: plans:items { actionable: true } returns exactly 5 items — P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011. Before the repair it returned 0.\n\nPromotion state: zero promoted work-item rows exist for P-007..P-011. The six promoted rows that do exist are all terminal and correspond to P-001..P-006. fleet:launch-on-plan promotes idempotently BEFORE its admission preflight, so placement does not require a separate plans:start.\n\nOpen question deliberately NOT ruled on here: D-004 records that this plan must not have items promoted or a fleet launched \"until Avi approves the scope and selects who executes it\". Scope approval is recorded (2026-08-21); route selection is not, and no owner turn selecting an execution route was located. The gate has nevertheless been overtaken in practice — P-001..P-006 are done with promoted work-items, and D-006 (2026-09-01) already prescribes how goal-drain members are assigned P-006..P-011. This decision records the contradiction and leaves D-004 standing; discharging it is the owner’s or the goal steward’s call, not this admission repair’s.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011\n\n### D-008 — D-004's route gate discharged by the GOAL steward under AUTO; route is launched fleet members\nDate: 2026-09-05\nDate: 2026-09-05\n\nPROVENANCE — READ FIRST. This discharge is AGENT-AUTHORED by the GOAL steward of work-on-everything-070565 (su-44b47b2b) under a standing owner-granted AUTO+GOAL mandate. It is NOT a discovered owner decision. No owner turn selecting an execution route exists; D-007's measurement to that effect STANDS and is not contradicted here. Do not later cite this decision as evidence that Avi selected a route.\n\nWhy the route conjunct is DISCHARGED rather than SATISFIED:\n- D-004 (2026-08-21) gates promotion/launch on two conjuncts: owner approves scope, AND owner selects who executes. The second was never recorded, and nothing here supplies it.\n- The gate is factually overtaken, not merely contested. Measured 2026-09-05 via plans:get: frontmatter status is `ready`, not the `draft` D-004 presumes; lifecycle counts show 6 of 13 items done with promoted terminal work-item rows (P-001..P-006); D-006 (2026-09-01) already prescribes per-member claim-spec mechanics for assigning P-006..P-011.\n- D-006 is itself AGENT-authored and therefore CANNOT discharge an owner conjunct. It is cited as evidence of the plan's settled execution shape, never as owner authority. Conflating the two would manufacture an owner directive out of an agent's own note — the precise failure mode this project's carry-provenance rules exist to prevent.\n- D-007 records that discharging is \"the owner's or the goal steward's call.\" I am the goal steward. Under AUTO an approval gate is mine to pass on my own judgment WITH disclosure; this decision and the owner report are that disclosure.\n\nROUTE SELECTED: a launched fleet of members working P-007..P-011. Binding constraints carried forward:\n- Per D-006: each member receives an exact per-member claim spec admitting its plan + plan_item before plan_items:assign; no member uses generic scheduler:get_next for this lane.\n- Per D-006: implementation routes to launched members, NEVER to the GOAL steward.\n- Per Execution safety: lanes run in parallel only where resolved file sets are disjoint; shared hot files (generic dispatch, tool-invocation logging, orient folds, fleet registry) serialize through the enforced lock system.\n- Per Execution safety: each item ships its recurrence guard in the repository test framework. A typecheck alone is not acceptance.\n\nWHY PLACE NOW rather than park: P-009 (importance `urgent`) gives leaders bounded, idempotent recovery for wedged and context-critical members. That is the exact friction this steward hit three independent times during the 2026-09-04 evening session — a dead claim holder requiring a forced release with basis 'holder-warm-idle'; a live fleet member running with durableWake MISSING; and two wake:'required' sends reporting queued:1/woken:1 where neither target ever took a turn (one since confirmed dead). The lane repairs measured, recurring loss rather than a hypothesised one.\n\nREVERSAL: if the owner did intend this plan to stay parked, revert by standing the fleet down and restoring the item statuses. Nothing authorised here is irreversible; all work lands as reviewable work-items and gate-checked code.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011\n\n### D-009 — A bounded-timeout bench park EXTENDS the canonical scheduler bench model — D-001 permits it; do not invent one inside get_next\nDate: 2026-09-05\nRULING (leader, fleet goal-070565-fleet-friction), settling the P-009 blocker recorded in WI-2144781's checkpoint: \"a bounded timeoutSec + timeoutBehavior:'wake' park is probably right but is a NEW park shape, and inventing one inside get_next's shared bounded preflight budget is the parallel control plane D-001 forbids.\"\n\nThe premise is FALSIFIED BY THE CODE. That park shape is not new — it is exactly what fleet:bench performs today.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/bench.ts:446-452 — the stage-mode arg schema already declares `timeout_sec: z.number().int().positive().max(AWAIT_MAX_TIMEOUT_SEC).optional()`, described as \"(stage mode) Optional deadline in seconds — omitted means the bench remains registered until the wake event fires.\"\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/bench.ts:686-694 — bench calls `registerAwait({ subscriberId: args.member, eventKey, policy:'wake', timeoutBehavior:'wake', timeoutSec: args.timeout_sec ?? null, ... })`, with the in-code comment \"A fleet bench is a leader-managed park, not a normal short-lived await. An omitted deadline must survive a long-lived blocker (and the leader's own session ending); callers can still opt into a timeout when they need one.\"\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/state/subscribe.ts:54 — \"Standing watch: no `timeout_sec`/`on_timeout`/`wake` (events:await owns those)\", i.e. bounded-deadline parking is an owned canonical axis, not an invention.\n\nTherefore:\n1. D-001 is SATISFIED, not violated, by an auto-bench that parks with a bounded deadline. D-001 names \"fleet registry/process-kill/scheduler bench model (P-009)\" as precisely the canonical surface P-009 must extend, and `timeout_sec` + `timeoutBehavior:'wake'` is already inside that surface. An auto-bench is a new CALLER of an existing park, not a new lifecycle plane.\n2. The member's instinct about get_next was CORRECT and is upheld: do not hand-roll a park inside get_next's bounded preflight budget. Wire decideContextCriticalBench() to the existing bench park semantics (registerAwait with timeoutBehavior:'wake' and a bounded timeoutSec) rather than open-coding an await at the refusal site (get_next.ts ~1253, `if (contextGate.refuse)`). Reuse the surface; do not duplicate it.\n3. Wake-key choice: the diagnosis that `work-item:claimable` self-defeats a compaction park is accepted — the member pulled BECAUSE work exists, so that key re-wakes it immediately. The bounded deadline is what makes this tractable: with a non-null timeoutSec, the DEADLINE (not the key) is the recovery guarantee, so a key that will not fire during the compaction window is safe by construction. Do not bench a context-critical member on `work-item:claimable`, and do not bench on the fleet `controlResumeGate`, which the member measured as null on an active fleet (a no-op dressed as a feature). Size timeout_sec to one compaction window.\n\nThis ruling covers only the D-001 question and the reuse boundary. The concrete timeout value and the chosen key remain the implementer's call, and P-009's acceptance criteria are unchanged.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-010 — P-009's recovery TOKEN stays a decision model — replacement dedupe is delivered by the pre-existing launch-transaction path, not a second store\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-009's acceptance says a replacement launches \"only after a durable recovery token\", and `fleet/member-recovery.ts` models exactly that: a `MemberRecoveryToken` with a lease, a deterministic `replacementOwnerId` derived from the token id, duplicate-suppression against a `priorToken`, and lease-reclaim after a leader crash. All six branches are unit-proven.\n\nRULING: do NOT build a persistence layer for that token as part of P-009. `fleet:respawn-member` ALREADY dedupes replacements through a different, older surface, and adding a token store would be a second dedupe mechanism for one question — the reuse-first smell this repo treats as a top review finding.\n\nThe existing mechanism, and why it is the same guarantee:\n- `replacementOwnerId(fleetSlug, memberOwnerId, idempotencyKey)` mints a DETERMINISTIC replacement identity — the same derivation the token model performs from its token id.\n- `findLiveHost(replacementOwner)` then refuses to launch when that identity already has a live psu-pty host. The source comment at the call site states the intent directly: it \"dedupes a TRUE-CONCURRENT double-fire of the SAME (fleetSlug, memberOwnerId, idempotencyKey)\".\n- Leader-crash recovery is `persistRespawnLaunchTransaction` / `reconcileRespawnLaunchTransaction`, a CAS-guarded launch transaction that already preserves a newer transaction and retries a compare-and-set miss.\n\nSo the two P-009 scenarios that the token would serve — duplicate leader request, leader crash — have a live system-level guarantee today; what the token adds is a MODEL of it, not a second enforcement point.\n\nWHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN, stated so nobody reads this as \"covered\": `decideMemberRecovery`'s `priorToken` input is never supplied by its only consumer, so the core's `duplicate-suppressed` and lease-reclaim branches are exercised as unit tests and NOT on any live path. If a future reproduction shows the live-host guard missing a real duplicate (it is a liveness probe, so a replacement that has not yet booted is its blind spot), the fix is to give THAT guard a durable record — not to stand up a parallel token table beside the launch transaction.\n\nMeasured 2026-09-05 (head e40743b75a):\n- `grep -rn 'MemberRecoveryToken|memberRecoveryTokenId|priorToken' --include=*.ts packages apps libs` excluding `lib/fleet/member-recovery*` → ZERO hits. Nothing outside the module references the token type.\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet_registry/respawn-member.ts:597` — the only `decideMemberRecovery` call passes `{fleetSlug, memberOwnerId, leaderOwnerId, attemptKey, kill, drain, now}`; no `priorToken`.\n- Same file: `:1357` `replacementOwnerId(slug, memberOwnerId, args.idempotencyKey)`, `:1360` the true-concurrent-double-fire comment, `:1369` `findLiveHost(replacementOwner)` guard.\n- Pre-existing tests for the live mechanism: `respawn-member.test.ts` — \"refuses to launch a replacement whose freshly-minted identity already has a live host (WI-2141730)\", \"correlates the exact replacement when concurrent respawns add multiple fresh rows\", \"keeps concurrent respawn responses attributed to their own pre-pinned replacement\", and the 4-test `respawn launch-transaction persistence` block.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-011 — Who may grade this plan's acceptance rubric — read from grader-eligibility.ts, not assumed\nDate: 2026-09-05\nRULING for whoever executes P-013. I checked the code rather than reasoning from the guidance, and the guidance's short form is narrower than the real rule in a way that would have picked the wrong grader.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-05T02:29Z, `grep -nE 'lineage|createdBy|implementer|eligib' packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scorecards/grader-eligibility.ts` and its sibling `.test.ts`. Load-bearing lines: :230 `const implementer = rubric.createdBy ?? rubric.proposedBy ?? null` · :265 `const lineageSources = [implementer, ...principalImplementers]` · :269 each tested with `lineageRelated(identity, callerId)` · :282 refusal `grader_in_implementer_lineage` · :254 `callerIsImplementer: true` returns `refusal: null`. Pinned by grader-eligibility.test.ts:200, \"excludes a grader in a principal implementer lineage, not only the author lineage\", and :171, \"refuses a plan implementer while keeping the rubric author as the acceptance seat\".\n\nTHE RULE AS IMPLEMENTED. The exclusion set is `lineageSources = [implementer, ...principalImplementers]`, where `implementer = rubric.createdBy ?? rubric.proposedBy` and `principalImplementers` comes from `resolvePlanImplementerIdentities`. Every one is tested against the caller with `areAcceptanceLineageRelated`, and ANY match refuses.\n\nWHAT THAT MEANS HERE. The exclusion is not \"agents the fleet leader launched\". It is: the rubric author, AND every principal IMPLEMENTER of this plan (su-4874d15e, su-4b480272, the dead su-8fe41063), AND anyone in the spawn/rebind lineage of any of those. So no member of the implementing fleet can grade this plan, and the exclusion reaches implementers DIRECTLY rather than routing through the leader.\n\nCHECK ELIGIBILITY BEFORE THE PASS, NOT AT THE EMIT — CORRECTED 02:36Z. This decision originally said \"only the emit can settle that\". That was WRONG and expensive: a grader would have paid for an entire grading pass and been refused at the last step. su-01a11fa7, the grader recruited for this plan, supplied the fix — run `scorecards:evaluate` on the rubric FIRST and confirm `role=independent-grader` / `blocksEmit=false`. Do that before accepting a grading, not after performing one. The correction is theirs, not mine.\n\nSEPARATE SEAT, DO NOT CONFLATE. When the caller IS the implementer the function returns `callerIsImplementer: true` with `refusal: null` — that is not eligibility to rate. The implementer keeps the ACCEPTANCE seat (reading the independent card, then re-emitting the complete ratings with `acceptance: { verdict, reasoning }`). Rating and accepting are two different writes by two different parties.\n\nROUTE: recruit an EXISTING live session outside all of the above, and create the grading work-item WITH `assign_to` naming them — explicit assignment is born-admitted and claimable in the same write. Do NOT file it unassigned for scheduler pull: unassigned goes through duplicate-screening admission first and refuses every claimant, including the grader named in the body, for a promoter-tick window that outlives most short-lived sessions.\n\nGRADER: su-01a11fa7 AGREED on 2026-09-05T02:32Z to take this grading, conditional on its own pre-check above. It is not an implementer here and has just completed an independent acceptance grading on another plan. Stood down 02:36Z pending the goal-kill decision, with no obligation held over it; re-approach it first if the plan resumes.\n\nALSO: batch every intended rubric revision BEFORE requesting independent grading. A later edit invalidates both the vetting attestation and any independent card, because cards are pinned to harness_plans.version.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hotel-reservation-app-bootstrap-20260821-2026-08-21","title":"Hotel reservation app — Papercusp template bootstrap and fleet launch","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Hotel reservation app — Papercusp template bootstrap and fleet launch\nslug: hotel-reservation-app-bootstrap-20260821-2026-08-21\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-21\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Bootstrap complete: official template materialized; app-local plan active; ten requested visible Codex workers verified by tool ledgers; P-001 is WI-40290 in progress.\n\n**Next:** All continuing work is governed by hotel-reservations-mvp-20260821-2026-08-21 in harness hotel-reservations and supervised by fleet hotel-reservations-build-20260821.\n\n## Goal\n\nMaterialize a new hotel-reservations pot from the official papercusp-webapp template, establish the app-local implementation plan, and launch the approved visible fleet.\n\n## Scope\n\nMulti-user server web app for a multi-property hotel group. Required closure: papercusp-web-host, papercusp-data-layer, papercusp-ui. Optional planes selected up front: papercusp-data-sync and papercusp-search. Payment is a test adapter behind a provider seam; no live charges.\n\n\n## Phase — Bootstrap\n\n- **P-001** `done` Materialize hotel-reservations from papercusp-webapp with kickoffBuilder=false; inspect PROTOCOL.md, GUIDE.md, composition assets, and supply-chain result. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40287 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Create the app-local implementation plan, register governing decisions and dependencies, launch the approved visible 10-agent fleet, and verify first-turn liveness. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40288 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Use templates:new-app with kickoffBuilder=false because the owner selected a dedicated visible fleet route.\n- App slug is hotel-reservations.\n- Fleet settings are 10 Codex agents, gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh, default system account, warm carry, visible terminals.\n\n## Verification\n\nBootstrap is complete only when the materialized pot exists, its PROTOCOL.md and GUIDE.md are read, an app-local dependency-aware plan exists, and the visible fleet has joined and completed a first tool turn.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"interview-audio-video-stability-2026-08-21","title":"Stabilize interview screen readability and system playback audio","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Stabilize interview screen readability and system playback audio\nslug: interview-audio-video-stability-2026-08-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-23\n---\n\n# Stabilize interview screen readability and system playback audio\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Owner-approved route A remains in force. Audio P-001 and P-003 are done. Root cause was two-layered: the QEMU-only 1024 mitigation did not cover browser clients, and persisted HDMI availability flapped to a USB fallback stored muted at 0%. D-001 now persists USB FRONT as default, applies a 2048/48000 Pulse floor after stock client rules, and records five consecutive real-playback minutes with 0 new Firefox/sink xruns and no route/mute drift while HDMI was available. Read-only recurrence guard: /home/marsh-office/.local/bin/check-audio-stability. Separate unexpected VM SIGKILL residue is EI-21279258452706209; no recurrence during acceptance.\n\n**Next:** P-002 remains the next approved lane: build the dormant guarded 1920x1080 interview display helper without changing the active desktop. Then P-004 runs the final Meet/Teams-style solo end-to-end check; audio alone is now verified.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add a reversible PipeWire Pulse stability rule for QEMU-driven playback and verify configuration/runtime quantum without restarting the desktop or VMs importance: high — note: ← WI-40301 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `todo` Add a guarded interview-mode readiness/toggle helper that uses supported 1920x1080 display mode, preserves 1280x720/30 OBS output, and always restores prior desktop geometry importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` Run before/after playback continuity, sink-monitor, route-stability, and xrun-delta tests blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: D-001: persisted USB default; global+known-client 2048/48000 Pulse floor; 1024-vs-2048 A/B; five-minute real Firefox soak with 0 new stream/sink xruns; route/default/mute/volume stable while HDMI available; check-audio-stability guard PASS.\n- **P-004** `todo` Run a Google Meet pre-call/solo verification for readable video and uninterrupted speaker playback without disturbing the microphone path blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Stability requires both a persistent output route and a 2048-frame Pulse floor\nDate: 2026-08-23\nThe earlier QEMU-only 1024/48000 rule was a mitigation, not a complete system-wide fix: it left the persisted HDMI default free to disappear/reappear and left Firefox/Chrome/Teams governed by lower client rules. On 2026-08-23 the NVIDIA HDMI/DP ELD became invalid while video stayed connected; GNOME could not resolve the default sink, WirePlumber fell back to USB FRONT at its stored mute=true/0% state, and later moved availability back. Persist USB FRONT (`alsa_output.usb-Generic_USB_audio_FRONT-00.HiFi__hw_FRONT__sink`) as the configured default so HDMI availability no longer moves playback. For scheduling, a settled live A/B showed 1024 frames still produced 5-6 Firefox xruns plus 2 sink xruns in 30 seconds, whereas forced 2048 produced 0. The drop-in now sets global Pulse `min.req`/`min.quantum` to 2048/48000 and appends a known-client rule after stock Firefox's 512-frame exception. Final acceptance: five consecutive 60-second real Firefox segments, all 0 new stream/sink xruns; driver remained 2048/48000; USB stayed configured/current/unmuted at 20%; HDMI remained available without stealing the route; Pulse warnings=0. Recurrence guard: `/home/marsh-office/.local/bin/check-audio-stability`. Separate residue: unexpected papercup-vm-win SIGKILL is tracked as EI-21279258452706209; it was not cgroup OOM and did not recur during acceptance.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"lsp-fleet-scale-all-languages-2026-08-21","title":"LSP plane at fleet scale: ~1000 agents, near-all languages, on shared pinned servers","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: \"LSP plane at fleet scale: ~1000 agents, near-all languages, on shared pinned servers\"\nslug: lsp-fleet-scale-all-languages-2026-08-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-10-05\n---\n\n## Goal\n[owner: Avi 2026-08-21] \"make our own lsp server that will support a one thousand agent fleet and almost every programming language.\" Interpreted per D-002/D-045: we do NOT reimplement language servers; we build the fleet-scale SERVICE PLANE that owns official pinned servers and multiplexes the fleet onto them. Public release context: all languages out of the box (owner, this session). Successor to code-intelligence-routing-lsp-gitnexus-2026-08-20, which ships the substrate (pinned servers, adapter, readiness contract, lsp.apply, exhaustive LanguageSpec table).\n\n## Measured constraints this design rests on\n- rust-analyzer ~89s cold (cargo metadata + proc-macro); tsserver ~4.7s wrong-answer window post-didOpen → warm shared servers are mandatory.\n- One tsserver 0.4–1.5GB RSS on this repo → per-agent servers are impossible at fleet scale; share per (language, projectRoot), refcount + evict.\n- LSP open documents make the server IGNORE disk (WI-40251) → coherence is a designed subsystem: pull-stat correctness + lock-release push and didChangeWatchedFiles as optimizations.\n- \"Supported\" ≠ \"answers your intents\" (Serena's own language table) → per-(language,intent) capability matrix, declared + LEARNED, persisted fleet-wide.\n- Licensing (public release): fetch-at-runtime, never bundle by default; GPL servers stay process-separated; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES pipeline for any bundled exception (P-010 is owner/legal-gated).\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-03, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted. Next repair: Accept the mapped clause: plans:get-specs, then plans:set-specs with lifecycleStatus:\"active\", expectedRevision set to its current revision, and every other field unchanged (keep the sourceBar pin and acceptanceRef; omitting either rides the prior value forward). That provenance-only promotion carries the bound proof and work-item contracts forward: confirm the result reports evidenceCarriedForward > 0 on a clause that had proof. If it is absent, another field changed and the proof must be re-bound at the new revision. Do NOT re-prove or amend the rubric on this code: the proof is not stale, the clause was never accepted. (R-4). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nBoth falsifier spikes are DONE and the plan is now APPROVED AND PROMOTED (WI-41066, 2026-08-23T21:42Z): status ready, spec triad written, 12 items promoted to work-items (11 open, P-014 blocked-by P-005). P-001 -> D-001; P-002 -> D-002/D-003; approval + sequencing -> D-004.\n\nD-002 changed the design: the knee belongs to the QUERY CLASS, not the server. tsserver does 8,077 definition/s at 1000-way concurrency (p95 141ms) but 15.6 req/s when a third of the trace is a repo-wide `references` scan — a 538x collapse from head-of-line blocking on one stdio pipe. So replicas-by-shard are NOT the fix (every replica holds the same repo and the same expensive symbol), P-004's queue must be per-class (method x symbol-cost) rather than a per-server FIFO, and P-003 stays a relocation, not a fan-out. ⚠ \"~15 req/s per tsserver\" is a RETRACTED reading — it describes a trace containing one pathological symbol, not server capacity.\n\nD-003: warmth is per-INTENT — a server answering `definition` in 4ms was still 27,256ms from its first `references` (one-time process-wide build; 80ms on a different doc right after). For P-009: rust-analyzer holds 2,838MB resident vs tsserver's 60-113MB, and RSS grew only ~57MB from 1 to 1000 concurrent, so the rust constraint is the resident index, not load. For P-012: SLO baseline measured — 0 errors and 0 false-empties in 20,769 requests at up to 1000-way concurrency; degradation was latency-only.\n\nINSTRUMENTS, committed and reusable (extend, do not re-fork): packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/lsp-saturation-bench-cli.ts (parameterised by language, ladder, intent mix, cursor pin) and lsp-intent-warmth-cli.ts.\n\n**Next:** PLAN IS APPROVED AND PROMOTED. Claimable now: WI-41086(P-003) WI-41087(P-004) WI-41088(P-005) WI-41089(P-006) WI-41090(P-007) WI-41091(P-008) WI-41092(P-009) WI-41093(P-010) WI-41094(P-011) WI-41095(P-012) WI-41097(P-015); WI-41096(P-014) correctly blocked-by P-005.\n\n⚠ RETRACTION — this block previously read \"P-003 (extract the LSP service tier) is the gating structural item\". True as architecture, FALSE as mechanism, and it cost a full wake to disprove. P-003 was never pickable and neither was anything else: the entire plan was held by the SPEC-TRIAD gate (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/items.ts:331), not by P-003. D-004 carries the isolating-control evidence. Do not re-derive this.\n\nSEQUENCING (D-004): P-003+P-004 are one coupled spine — D-002 forbids a fan-out and requires a per-class queue, so read D-002 before starting P-003. P-005 -> P-014 is a hard chain. P-007, P-009, P-010, P-011 and P-015 are parallel-safe against the spine. P-006 and P-008 are best started after P-003 lands.\n\n⚠ DO NOT START TREE-WRITING WORK YET. The shared checkout is under the WI-40086 live quiescence hold (green-checkpoint paused, 35 consecutive reds; a manual checkpoint verified RUNNING at 21:44:38Z on candidate 014b057d80b0). Its pause condition requires all writers terminal and the root clean, so starting code work now would prolong a hold that currently freezes deploys fleet-wide. Claim items freely — promotion is Postgres-side and touches no files — but gate the first tree write on events:await { event: 'work-item:done:WI-40086' } rather than polling.\n\n## Requirements\n\nWhat must be TRUE when this plan is done. These are acceptance conditions, not tasks: each is stated so it can be falsified, and names the measurement that motivates it. \"The fleet\" means ~1000 concurrent agents — the owner's stated target and the top of the ladder D-002 actually drove.\n\n**R-1 — Servers are shared and warm; never one per agent.** Every code-intelligence query for a given `(language, projectRoot)` is answered by a warm shared server, and the number of server processes is a function of the distinct `(language, projectRoot)` pairs in use — never of agent count. *Falsifier:* 1000 concurrent agents querying one repo must not produce more than one tsserver for that root. *Why:* one tsserver holds 0.4–1.5 GB RSS on this repo and rust-analyzer needs ~89 s cold; per-agent servers are arithmetically impossible, not merely wasteful.\n\n**R-2 — Truthfulness survives saturation: \"cannot\" is never rendered as \"none\".** An unsupported intent, an unprovisioned language, a not-yet-ready server, and a timed-out query must each produce a *distinguishable* refusal that a caller cannot mistake for \"no such symbol\". No certified-false-empty and no certified-stale answer at any load. *Falsifier:* P-012's replayed 1000-agent trace, measured against D-002's baseline of 0 errors and 0 false-empties across 20,769 requests. This is the contract the whole plane exists to protect; a fast wrong answer is a worse outcome than a slow honest one.\n\n**R-3 — One expensive query class cannot starve the cheap ones.** Cheap index-hit queries retain their latency profile while an expensive repo-wide scan is in flight on the same server. *Falsifier:* replay D-002's pathological mix (one third hot-symbol `references`) and require aggregate throughput to stay within a stated factor of the definition-only rate. *Why:* the same warm server measured 8,077 `definition`/s alone but **15.6 req/s** under that mix — a 538× collapse from head-of-line blocking on a single stdio pipe. This is the single measurement that most constrains the design.\n\n**R-4 — Near-all languages, with the popular ones guaranteed rather than incidental.** Language coverage is delivered by an explicit tiering whose residue is prioritised by *usage*, not alphabet, and no language that Papercusp itself ships in may sit in an unimplemented tier. *Falsifier:* `typescript-language-server`, `jdtls`, `ruby-lsp`, `csharp-language-server` and the eslint/json/html/css/yaml/tailwind group each answer their acceptance canary. *Why:* D-001 measured that mechanical generation reaches 74.2 % of packages and that the 25.8 % residue contains most of the web stack plus Java, Ruby and C# — including our own first language. Unweighted coverage percentages must not be quoted as if they were user-weighted.\n\n**R-5 — Readiness is certified per `(language, intent)`, never per server.** No component may certify \"this server is ready\" as a whole; a readiness strategy names the intent it certifies, and an intent that has not been proven on that server cannot be reported as ready. *Falsifier:* a server answering `definition` in single-digit ms while its first `references` is still unpaid must report `references` as not-ready. *Why:* D-003 measured a server 4 ms warm for `definition` and still 27,256 ms from its first `references` — a one-time, process-wide index build, not a per-symbol cost.\n\n**R-6 — Resident memory is bounded and governed.** Warm servers are refcounted and evictable, total resident footprint has a ceiling, and reaching that ceiling queues provisioning rather than thrashing or OOM-killing. *Falsifier:* drive more distinct `(language, projectRoot)` pairs than the ceiling permits and require graceful queueing. *Why:* rust-analyzer holds ~2,838 MB steady against tsserver's 60–113 MB, and D-002 showed its RSS grew only ~57 MB from 1 to 1000 concurrent — so for rust the binding constraint is the resident index, not load. Governance must be sized against residency, not concurrency.\n\n**R-7 — Answers reflect the tree on disk.** A query issued after a file changes on disk reflects that change, including edits made by other agents through paths the LSP never observed. *Falsifier:* mutate a file outside the server's awareness, then require the next query to be correct rather than to serve the stale open-document buffer. *Why:* WI-40251 established that LSP open documents make the server ignore disk, so coherence is a designed subsystem here and not an emergent property.\n\n**R-8 — The plane is licensable for public release.** Servers are fetched at runtime rather than bundled by default; GPL-family servers stay process-separated; any bundled exception carries a per-version THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES entry. *Falsifier:* a license audit of the provisioned set produces no bundled GPL/proprietary artifact lacking notices. *Why:* D-001 measured 8 `proprietary` and ~27 GPL-family entries (including 2 AGPL) among 325 LSP packages. The bundling *policy* is owner/legal-gated (P-010) — engineer-flagged, never engineer-decided.\n\n**R-9 — The plane is observable, with SLOs written against measured baselines.** Queue depth per class, warm-server population, and per-intent readiness are registered state cells; P-012's SLOs are expressed as p95 query latency plus zero certified-false-empty and zero certified-stale. *Falsifier:* each SLO resolves from a registered cell rather than from a hand-run script.\n\n## Design\n\nHow it will be built, and the trade-offs already settled. P-001 and P-002 were run as falsifier spikes *before* this section was written, so the choices below are measured rather than assumed; each names the decision that settled it. The governing constraint throughout: we do **not** reimplement language servers (D-002/D-045) — we build the service plane that owns official pinned servers and multiplexes the fleet onto them.\n\n### Shape: a service tier the operator talks to over RPC\n\nServer ownership moves out of the operator process into a `managedSpawn`-enrolled, cgroup-confined daemon, keyed by `(language, projectRoot)`; the operator's `lsp.*` facade becomes an RPC client of it (P-003). This is deliberately a **relocation of `lsp-adapter.ts`'s server-owning half, not a rewrite** — the readiness contract, adapter and `LanguageSpec` table shipped by the predecessor plan (`code-intelligence-routing-lsp-gitnexus-2026-08-20`) are the substrate this tier inherits. Enrolment is what makes the resulting processes killable by `taskId` and accountable in the task ledger rather than a population of orphans.\n\n### The queue is per-class, not per-server (settled by D-002)\n\nAdmission control (P-004) is a bounded queue **per `(method × symbol-cost)` class**, with a per-class concurrency cap, per-agent fairness, priority classes, a timeout that returns a truthful degraded answer, and queue depth per class exposed as a registered state cell.\n\nA plain per-server FIFO is specifically rejected: it reproduces the measured failure exactly, parking thousands of millisecond-cheap `definition` calls behind one ~18 s reference scan.\n\n**Rejected — replicas-by-shard.** This was the item's own stated hypothesis and the spike falsified it: sharding hands every replica the same repo and therefore the same expensive symbol, so N replicas each still take ~18 s for the query that hurts. More servers do not fix a head-of-line problem on one pipe. This is why P-003 remains a relocation rather than a fan-out.\n\n### The registry is three tiers fed by two pinned sources (settled by D-001)\n\n- **Tier-1** — a verified closed union, exhaustive `Record` (the WI-40250 pattern), for languages we certify ourselves.\n- **Tier-2** — *generated* from a pinned mason-registry release joined against a pinned nvim-lspconfig, with SHA-256-verified fetch-at-runtime provisioning and declared runtime prerequisites surfacing as `unavailable-because`.\n- **Tier-3** — hand-authored specs for the ~84 residue servers (P-014), prioritised by usage, each shipping a P-011 acceptance canary.\n\nPromotion from Tier-2 to Tier-1 requires an acceptance-corpus pass, so a tier is a claim about *evidence*, not about authorship convenience.\n\n**Rejected — \"generate `LanguageSpec` from the mason registry\".** D-001 measured that mason supplies the provisioning recipe (325/325) and licenses (325/325) but **zero** of the protocol contract: no wire `languageId`, no stdio argv, no readiness semantics, no capability matrix. Mason is a package-manager registry — it answers \"how do I install this binary\", never \"how do I speak to it\". A single-source design would have generated the half we could have guessed and none of the half that is hard. Hence two sources joined on `neovim.lspconfig`, a key that dangles ~3 % of the time, and `resolveBin` must implement mason's own template DSL plus ~12 install backends. Project-root resolution stays ours (`resolveProjectRoot`): no registry supplies it.\n\n### Capability is declared *and* learned (P-006)\n\nPer-`(language, intent)` capability is declared where known and **learned** from observed `MethodNotFound`/capability responses, persisted in Postgres fleet-wide so one agent's discovery is not re-paid by the next. Unsupported intents refuse loudly. This exists because \"supported\" and \"answers your intents\" are different predicates — Serena's own language table conflates them, and R-2 forbids us from doing so.\n\n### Readiness is per-intent and warmed at provision time (settled by D-003)\n\n`LanguageSpec.readinessStrategy ∈ progress-signal | settle-window | canary-query`, conservative by default, and **each strategy names the intent it certifies** — a canary firing `definition` certifies `definition` only. Provisioning issues one throwaway `references` per server as part of warmup, which converts D-003's measured ~27 s penalty from something the first unlucky agent pays into a one-time provisioning cost paid by nobody. An unproven server may never certify an empty result (P-007).\n\n### Coherence: pull-stat is correctness, push is optimisation (P-008)\n\nWI-40251's pull-stat check remains the *correctness* mechanism. Lock-release push invalidation and `didChangeWatchedFiles` are added as *optimisations* where servers support them, with debounced re-opens to prevent `didClose`/`didOpen` thrash. The ordering is deliberate: an optimisation that is absent or unsupported must degrade to correct-and-slower, never to fast-and-stale.\n\n### Resource governance sized against residency (P-009)\n\nRefcount plus idle-TTL LRU eviction of warm servers, cgroup memory caps through the task ledger, `processes:freeze` for pressure relief, and a warm-server ceiling with provision queueing. Sizing follows R-6's evidence: for rust the cost is the resident index rather than the load.\n\n### Licensing (P-010)\n\nFetch-at-runtime is the default and is now evidenced rather than assumed; GPL-family servers stay process-separated; any bundled exception requires a per-version THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES manifest. The bundling policy itself is owner/legal-gated.\n\n### Verification strategy\n\nTwo spikes are already done (P-001, P-002). The remaining evidence obligations are P-011's per-language acceptance canaries at provision time — failures *demote* a matrix cell rather than shipping a wrong answer — and P-012's replayed 1000-agent trace for the SLOs. P-015 measures our cold-open false-empty window against Serena/SolidLSP; note D-003 already rules out finding false-empties in the reference-build window specifically, since that query blocked and then returned the correct 192 sites. The benches are committed and parameterised (`lsp-saturation-bench-cli.ts`, `lsp-intent-warmth-cli.ts`) and are to be **extended, not re-forked**.\n\n### A note on reading the measurements\n\nD-002's absolute rates are for this 128-core box; the portable results are the *shapes* — the per-class knee and head-of-line blocking. rust-analyzer rests on a single probe and is not evidence it is faster than tsserver. Any \"~15 req/s per tsserver\" capacity figure is a **retracted** reading that describes one pathological symbol, not server capacity.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Plan items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-003, P-012 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-011, P-012 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004, P-012 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005, P-011, P-014 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-007, P-011 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-004, P-012 | tree |\n\nThis map preserves all nine source requirements. Each listed item contributes its authored responsibility; a scoped item completion does not certify other items or the whole requirement. P-004 proves the admission controller and its typed daemon/socket integration under D-010/D-011. P-012 retains the complete replayed 1000-agent trace and fleet SLO obligation. Tree means pinned current-build evidence, with no inference of deployment or shipment. R-8 still requires the independent owner/legal decision and complete provisioned-set license audit.\n\n## Items\n- **P-001** `done` SPIKE (falsifier): download a pinned mason-registry registry.json release, verify checksums, attempt the mechanical mapping onto LanguageSpec. Deliverable: mapped/unmappable field table + % coverage. If lossy, the consume-don't-author premise weakens and P-005 is re-scoped. — note: ← WI-40254 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` SPIKE (falsifier): saturation measurement — one warm tsserver + one rust-analyzer under simulated 100→1000-agent query traces (definition/references mix). Deliverable: p50/p95 latency vs concurrency, the knee, and the queue model P-004 implements. Decides whether replicas-by-shard are ever needed. — note: ← WI-40260 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Extract the LSP service tier: move server ownership out of the operator process into a managedSpawn-enrolled, cgroup-confined daemon; operator lsp.* facade talks RPC to it; keyed (language, projectRoot). Reuse-first: this is a RELOCATION of lsp-adapter.ts's server-owning half, not a rewrite. — note: ← WI-41086 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `blocked` Admission control: per-server bounded queue + backpressure, per-agent fairness, priority classes; queue depth as a registered state cell and health signal. — note: Local source/technical adequacy verified; final accepted4 whole-BAR disclosure awaits successful P012/WI41095 fleet oracle/F2/full-tail/SLO evidence. Checkpoint ffd66ad80299; mutationbindings23726..28; success dependency recorded.\n- **P-005** `todo` Tiered LanguageSpec registry: Tier-1 verified closed union (exhaustive Record, WI-40250 pattern); Tier-2 GENERATED from the pinned mason-registry release (purl → resolveBin/provision recipe), SHA-256-verified fetch-at-runtime provisioning, declared runtime prerequisites surfacing as unavailable-because. Promotion 2→1 via acceptance corpus pass. — note: ← WI-41088 released\n- **P-006** `done` Capability matrix per (language,intent): declared where known, LEARNED from observed MethodNotFound/capability responses, persisted in Postgres fleet-wide; unsupported intents refuse loudly (never render \"cannot\" as \"none\"). — note: ← WI-41089 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Readiness strategies generalized (extends WI-40224): LanguageSpec.readinessStrategy ∈ progress-signal | settle-window | canary-query, conservative default; an unproven server can never certify an empty. — note: ← WI-41090 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `todo` Coherence at scale: keep WI-40251 pull-stat as correctness; add lock-release push invalidation + workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles where servers support it; debounced re-opens to prevent didClose/didOpen thrash. — note: ← WI-41091 released\n- **P-009** `todo` Resource governance: refcount + idle-TTL LRU eviction of warm servers, cgroup memory caps via the task ledger, processes:freeze pressure relief, warm-server ceiling with provision queueing. — note: ← WI-41092 released\n- **P-010** `blocked` Licensing + notices pipeline: fetch-not-bundle default; per-version THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES manifest for any bundled exception; flag GPL/proprietary/licensed-runtime servers in the spec. Needs owner/legal sign-off on the bundling policy — engineer-flagged, not engineer-decided. — note: D-004 quiescence gate: no tree writes until WI-40086 terminal. Gate wi-40086-qualified-current-tip verified fired:false at 04:47Z.\n- **P-011** `todo` Acceptance canaries per provisioned server: auto-run a per-language micro-corpus (the prior plan's P-002 pattern) at provision time; failures demote the language's matrix cells rather than shipping wrong answers. — note: ← WI-41094 released\n- **P-012** `todo` Fleet-scale load test: replayed 1000-agent trace against the service tier; SLOs: p95 query latency, zero certified-false-empty, zero certified-stale answers. — note: ← WI-41095 released\n\n## Non-goals\n- Reimplementing any language server.\n- Adopting Serena (D-044/D-045 record why; its symbol-edit ideas port via WI-40242).\n- Bundling servers into the installer as the default path.\n\n\n## Phase — Tier-3 residue coverage (opened by D-001)\n\n- **P-014** `todo` Tier-3 hand-authored specs for the ~84 residue servers D-001 measured (18 Lua-function `cmd`, 42 with no lspconfig key, 9 dangling keys, plus absent-field residue). Prioritise by USAGE, not alphabet: typescript-language-server, jdtls, eslint/json/html/css/yaml/tailwind, ruby-lsp, csharp-language-server come first, because a Tier-2 generator provably misses them — our own first language is in this residue. Each entry ships with a P-011 acceptance canary. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n- **P-015** `done` Measure the COLD-OPEN false-empty window, ours vs Serena/SolidLSP, on the same repo and query. This is the one number that substantiates the \"our readiness contract is the field-leading half\" claim the WI-40244 research rests on — it is currently asserted from architecture reading, not measured. Owner-offered, never run. Deliverable: window in ms for each, per language, with the query trace. — note: ← WI-41097 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — P-001 MEASURED: \"consume, don't author\" survives but needs TWO pinned sources, and its 74.2% coverage is biased AWAY from the popular languages\nDate: 2026-08-21\nFalsifier run 2026-08-21 against mason-registry release `2026-08-21-imaginary-beer` (both published checksums verified: registry.json.zip d7de8cbc…, registry.json 0191398f…) joined against nvim-lspconfig `v2.11.0`. Scripts: /tmp/mason-spike/{analyze,join,join2}.mjs.\n\n#### Population\n590 packages in the registry; 325 carry category `LSP`; 215 distinct display languages; purl source types span 12 backends (github 155, npm 84, pypi 29, cargo 21, golang 9, generic 7, gem 6, openvsx 5, nuget 3, luarocks 3, opam 2, composer 1).\n\n#### What mason DOES give us, mechanically\n- provisioning recipe (purl + asset targets): 325/325 = 100%\n- licenses: 325/325 = 100% (needed for P-010)\n- an executable declaration: 319/325 = 98.2%\n- display languages: 312/325 = 96.0%\n\n#### What mason gives us of the PROTOCOL contract: ZERO\n- LSP `languageId` (the wire value): 0/325\n- stdio launch argv: 0/325\n- `requiresProgressSignal` / readiness semantics: 0/325\n- per-intent capability matrix: 0/325\n\nThis is the finding that matters. Mason is a PACKAGE MANAGER registry — it answers \"how do I install this binary\", never \"how do I speak to it\". Every field our LanguageSpec exists to carry is absent from it. A design that said \"generate LanguageSpec from mason\" would have generated the half we could have guessed and none of the half that is hard.\n\n#### The recovery path, and its real cost\nThe registry DECLARES a join key, `neovim.lspconfig`, and nvim-lspconfig configs carry `cmd`, `filetypes` and `root_markers`. Coverage:\n- key present: 283/325 = 87.1%\n- key RESOLVES to a real config file: 274/325 = 84.3% (9 keys dangle: ada-language-server, codeql, erlang-ls, haxe-language-server, omnisharp-mono, sourcery, tsc, vetur-vls, wc-language-server)\n- 42 packages carry no key at all\n\nBut a joined field is only useful if it is DATA. It is not always:\n- `cmd`: static table 252/274 (92.0%), Lua FUNCTION 18 (6.6%), absent 4\n- `filetypes`: static 263/274 (96.0%), function 0, absent 11\n- `root_markers`: static 221/274 (80.7%), absent 53\n\n**End-to-end derivable as pure data (mason bin + static cmd + static filetypes): 241/325 = 74.2%. Residue: 84 packages = 25.8%.**\n\n#### The sting — and the reason 74.2% must not be quoted unweighted\nThe 18 function-`cmd` entries are not the long tail. They are: typescript-language-server, tsgo, jdtls, eslint-lsp, json-lsp, html-lsp, css-lsp, yaml-language-server, tailwindcss-language-server, svelte-language-server, angular-language-server, astro-language-server, biome, oxlint, glint, ruby-lsp, csharp-language-server, powershell-editor-services. That is most of the web stack plus Java, Ruby and C#. `cmd` is a function precisely BECAUSE those servers need per-project resolution (ts_ls prefers a project-local `node_modules/.bin/typescript-language-server` over a global one) — i.e. the entries needing real logic are the entries with real users.\n\nOur OWN first language is in the residue: typescript-language-server. So a Tier-2 generator would have covered 74.2% of packages and NOT the one we already ship.\n\n#### Consequences for the plan\n1. P-005 is RE-SCOPED, not cancelled. Tier-2 generation is real and worth building for the ~241 data-derivable servers, but it is a TWO-SOURCE pipeline (mason for provisioning, nvim-lspconfig for protocol), joined on a key that dangles 3% of the time — not \"consume the mason registry\".\n2. A THIRD tier is required and was missing from the plan: hand-authored specs for the ~84 residue servers, prioritised by usage rather than by alphabet. **Filed as P-014** (note: the plan has no P-013 — plans:add-item allocated P-014 directly; an earlier draft of this decision cited P-013 and was wrong).\n3. `resolveBin` must implement mason's own template DSL (`{{ version | strip_prefix \"v\" }}`, `{{source.asset.bin}}`) plus ~12 install backends. 95 entries use `{{source.asset.bin}}` and 85 use the `npm:` scheme. This is real work the \"just consume it\" framing hid.\n4. `root_dir` is a Lua function in every sample inspected and is absent-or-static-markers-only in the data — project-root resolution stays OURS (`resolveProjectRoot`), and no registry supplies it.\n5. Licensing for P-010 is now measurable: of 325, MIT 203 / Apache-2.0 70, but 8 `proprietary` and ~27 GPL-family (incl. 2 AGPL, 1 LicenseRef-Qt-Commercial). Fetch-at-runtime remains the correct default and is now evidenced.\n\n#### Method caveat (stated so it is not read as uniform)\nStatic-vs-function classification is a line-anchored regex over the Lua source (`^\\s*<field>\\s*=\\s*({|function)`), not a Lua parse. The unmatched rows — cmd absent 4, filetypes absent 11, root_markers absent 53 — are measurement residue, not confirmed absences; a Lua-parse pass would move a handful of them. The headline 74.2% is therefore a FLOOR on data-derivability, and the 25.8% residue is a ceiling. `supported_platforms` is declared on only 4/325, so platform coverage must be read off `source.asset[].target`, not that field.\n\n### D-002 — P-002 verdict: the knee belongs to the QUERY CLASS, not the server — replicas-by-shard would not fix it; per-class admission (P-004) would\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMEASURED 2026-08-21 by `.papercusp/scratch/p002-saturation.mts` driving the REAL `lspQuery` path with the REAL `BENCH_PROBES` cursors. 20,769 requests total across tsserver + rust-analyzer, ladders 1→1000 concurrent, closed-loop with a FIXED request count per level (not a wall-clock cutoff — a cutoff discards the still-queued, i.e. slowest, requests, so p95 improves as the server degrades).\n\n#### The answer to the item's stated question\n**Replicas-by-shard are NOT needed, and would not have helped.** Sharding gives each replica the same repo and therefore the same expensive symbol; N replicas each still take ~18s for the query that hurts. The fix is admission control per QUERY CLASS (P-004), not more servers (P-003 stays a relocation, not a fan-out).\n\n#### What was measured\nCheap, index-hit classes scale essentially perfectly to the top of the plan's stated range:\n- tsserver `definition`, 1000-way concurrent: **8,077 req/s, p50 112.7ms, p95 140.7ms** — throughput still RISING at c=1000 (5,437/s at c=256), so there is no knee ≤1000.\n- rust-analyzer, 1000-way: 7,442 req/s, p95 131ms.\n- `references` on normally-used symbols: 655 req/s (`pinModuleState`) and 570 req/s (`PanelRegistry`) at c=64, p95 ~117ms.\n\nONE class collapses, and it is not the runtime:\n- `references` on `managedSetInterval` (used repo-wide): 1.24/s at c=1, 2.95/s at c=8, **3.28/s at c=64 with p50 18.5s / p95 21.2s**. Throughput plateaus from c≈8 — the knee for this class is c≈8 at ~3.3 req/s.\n\n#### The finding that changes the design: head-of-line blocking, measured at 538x\nThe SAME warm server does 8,077 definition/s alone, but **15.6 req/s** when one third of the trace is hot-symbol references (3-cursor 2:1 mix, c=1000, p95 166s, max 192s). One expensive class starved everything behind it on the single stdio pipe — a 538x aggregate collapse.\n\nTherefore P-004's queue model must be **per-class (method × symbol-cost), not a single per-server FIFO**. A plain FIFO reproduces exactly this: thousands of millisecond-cheap definitions stuck behind one 18s reference scan. Required with it: a per-class concurrency cap, a timeout with a TRUTHFUL degraded answer, and queue depth per class as the registered state cell.\n\n#### Correction recorded on purpose\nThe first (multi-cursor) reading looked like \"one warm tsserver saturates at ~15 req/s / is single-threaded-bound\", and I was about to report it. Controls falsified it: definition-only on one cursor reached 8,077/s — FASTER than rust-analyzer. The ceiling was never the runtime. Anyone citing a \"~15 req/s per tsserver\" capacity number from this work is citing the retracted reading.\n\n#### Two findings for other items\n- **P-007 (readiness): warmth is per-QUERY, not per-server.** The server answered `definition` in 2ms while the first `references` on `managedSetInterval` still cost 24,759ms. A readiness strategy that certifies \"the server is up and settled\" certifies something it has not established, and an unproven-for-this-query server can still emit a slow or empty answer.\n- **P-009 (resource governance): rust-analyzer holds 2,838 MB steady vs tsserver's 60–113 MB (~25–47x).** For rust the fleet constraint is MEMORY, not CPU — RSS grew only ~57MB going from 1 to 1000 concurrent, so it is the resident index, not the load, that costs.\n\n#### Correctness held throughout — the honest-degradation contract survives saturation\nAcross all 20,769 requests at up to 1000-way concurrency: **0 errors, 0 false-empties, every level completed**. Degradation was in latency only, never in truthfulness. This is a positive result for the never-render-cannot-as-none contract, and the baseline P-012's SLOs can now be written against.\n\n#### Known limits of this measurement — do not over-read it\n- Single-cursor levels repeat one identical query, so they measure BEST-CASE index-hit throughput; the server's own caches make repeats nearly free. Real heterogeneous traces will land between these and the mixed-trace number.\n- rust-analyzer has only ONE probe in the corpus (`rust-trait-implementations`), so its curve rests on a single cursor in a single crate and is NOT comparable to the 3-cursor TS trace. It is not evidence that rust-analyzer is faster than tsserver.\n- The absolute rates are for this 128-core box, unloaded-ish. The SHAPE (per-class knee, head-of-line blocking) is the portable result; the rates are not.\n\n### D-003 — P-007 ruling: readiness must be warmed PER-INTENT — the first `references` costs a one-time ~27s process-wide index build a definition-ready server has not paid\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMEASURED 2026-08-21 within a SINGLE tsserver lifetime (probe `.papercusp/scratch/p002-intent-warmth.mts`), which is what makes this a mechanism rather than a comparison across runs:\n\n| step | query | latency | sites |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `definition` cursor 0 — cold server | 5,184ms | 1 |\n| 2 | `definition` cursor 0 — repeat | **4ms** | 1 |\n| 3 | `definition` cursor 1 — NEW doc | 483ms | 1 |\n| 4 | `references` cursor 2 — FIRST references | **27,256ms** | 192 |\n| 5 | `references` cursor 2 — repeat | 721ms | 192 |\n| 6 | `references` cursor 1 — DIFFERENT doc | **80ms** | 8 |\n| 7 | `definition` cursor 2 — after the build | 2ms | 1 |\n\n#### The mechanism\nThe first `references` anywhere pays a **one-time, process-wide** reference-index build of ~27s. It is NOT per-symbol and NOT per-document: step 6 shows a different file answering in 80ms immediately afterwards. Step 7 shows `definition` was unaffected throughout — it was fast before the build and fast after.\n\n#### Why this changes P-007\nA readiness strategy that certifies the SERVER (\"up, settled, answering\") certifies something it has not established. At step 2 this server was, by any server-level test, demonstrably ready — 4ms answers — and was still 27 seconds away from being able to answer a `references`. So `readinessStrategy` must be evaluated **per (language, intent)**, and provisioning should issue one throwaway `references` per server as part of warmup. That converts a 27s penalty paid by whichever agent happens to ask first into a one-time provisioning cost paid by nobody.\n\nConcretely, for the P-005 spec: readiness is a per-intent property, and `progress-signal` / `settle-window` / `canary-query` each need to name WHICH intent they certify. A canary-query strategy that fires a `definition` certifies `definition` only.\n\n#### Bounds on this finding — do not over-read it\n- Measured on tsserver against this monorepo only. rust-analyzer was not probed this way; its cold-start profile differs (it holds a 2,838MB resident index, so its build is likely front-loaded into startup instead — that is a PREDICTION, not a measurement, and P-011's per-language canaries are where it should be checked).\n- The 27s is this repo's size, not a portable constant. The SHAPE — per-intent, one-time, global — is the portable part.\n\n#### One thing this rules OUT, which matters for P-015\nThroughout the 27s build the query BLOCKED and then returned the correct 192 sites. It did not return an empty answer, and it did not error. So this particular window is a LATENCY hazard, not a false-empty hazard — consistent with the D-002 ladders (0 false-empties in 20,769 requests). ScriptC 0.0.34 is a five-week-old experimental LLVM/C compiler with real Node API lowering and explicit QuickJS dynamic islands. The first Papercusp operator probe was not analyzable because the current program graph has 35 TypeScript errors, so the plan begins with evidence and a reusable parity substrate. Migration is staged by executable boundary: small shipped helpers, bounded services/workers, operator-facing CLIs, then the operator sidecar. Vite UI and Tauri/Rust stay unchanged. Every wave retains its Node artifact.\n\n**Next:** When implementation is authorized, start P-001 through P-004 only: pin toolchains, inventory all shipped entries, build the differential harness, and add parallel Linux/macOS/Windows shadow lanes. Do not activate any ScriptC artifact before the all-three parity decision is green.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2139951 — Run `scriptc coverage` on every executable shipped in the desktop sidecar and classify each statement/module as static, dynamic-island, unsupported, native-addon/FFI, or resource/packaging blocker. P… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139952 — Build one reusable differential-conformance harness that runs Node/esbuild and ScriptC artifacts with identical fixtures and compares stdout, stderr, exit code, files, IPC frames, HTTP behavior, sign… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139953 — Extend the desktop release matrix with parallel Linux/macOS/Windows ScriptC build+smoke lanes, an all-three parity verdict, per-platform provenance, and a fail-closed rule: no platform defaults to a … <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139954 — Pilot the dependency-light `git-ext-bridge` helper as a native executable, preserving the exact git remote-helper protocol, environment, signal, and error behavior; run Node-vs-native differential te… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139955 — Pilot packaged `project-history`, initially allowing an explicit dynamic island for YAML/npm dependencies; compare generated files byte-for-byte and report the static/dynamic split. <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139956 — Pilot read-only orchestrator bins (`assemble-prompt`, `get-plan-context`) and require deterministic output, error, path, and Unicode behavior across Node/native and Linux/macOS/Windows. <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139957 — Activate Wave 1 atomically for one release only after the three-platform parity verdict is green; keep version-matched Node artifacts installed and exercise rollback in each platform smoke suite. <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139958 — Migrate the event-loop sentinel worker through an explicit executable IPC contract; differential-test stdio/SSE framing, cancellation, error codes, TLS, and large-output backpressure. <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139960 — Pilot onboarding and tutorial-runner binaries; compare prompts, persisted state, subprocess launch, path quoting, terminal encoding, and resume semantics across all release OSes. <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139961 — Activate Wave 2 atomically only after the all-three parity gate and forced rollback pass; record coverage, dynamic-island surface, artifact size, startup, RSS, and divergences without allowing perfor… <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139962 — Migrate `ptool` behind the existing MCP transport contract; preserve account/model/carry flags and window… <!-- P-014 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139964 — Migrate mutating orchestrator bins (`invoke-once`, `run`) under crash-consistency and exactly-once differential tests, including PostgreSQL transactions, child processes, signals, and restart recover… <!-- P-015 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139965 — Activate Wave 3 atomically after all three release legs pass; retain a version-locked Node rollback and verify mixed old/new workspace state cannot create feature drift. <!-- P-016 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139966 — Make the real `serve.ts` program graph clean under ScriptC's compiler configuration, then capture complete coverage. The current probe stops before lowering on 35 type errors, so no whole-operator co… <!-- P-017 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139967 — Carve dynamic plugins, native addons, embedded PostgreSQL, ONNX/audio workers, and runtime-loaded resources behind explicit IPC/FFI/resource manifests so coverage is deterministic and unsupported beh… <!-- P-018 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139968 — Run the ScriptC operator as a shadow sidecar against representative read-only traffic, then full isolated stateful suites; compare endpoint/tool catalogs, routes, migrations, scheduling, plugins, rec… <!-- P-019 -->\n- [ ] WI-2139969 — Switch the operator default only in a release whose Linux/macOS/Windows builds all pass the same feature-parity manifest, differential suite, upgrade/rollback test, and soak; ship Node alongside for … <!-- P-020 -->\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Requirements\n\nP-001 must produce a reproducible, reviewable toolchain baseline for every supported release target. The baseline MUST pin the ScriptC compiler/runtime version, each native host/target toolchain version, source or distribution reference, license metadata, checksums, and the supported target triples (Linux x64, the macOS architectures actually shipped, and Windows x64).\n\nThe platform-owned build recipe MUST resolve only those pinned inputs, run from a clean checkout without undeclared host state, and emit a provenance bundle that names the exact inputs and commands used. Two clean runs for each target MUST reproduce byte-identical outputs or record an explicit, measured nondeterminism exception with its cause and guard.\n\nP-001 is complete only when the manifest, recipes, provenance records, and reproducibility evidence are versioned and consumable by P-002 (coverage), P-003 (differential conformance), and P-004 (the three-platform release matrix). Node/esbuild artifacts remain available as the rollback baseline, and no ScriptC artifact is eligible to become a platform default until the all-three parity gate is green.\n\n## Design\n\nUse one versioned machine-readable toolchain manifest plus platform-owned recipes. Each target entry carries the ScriptC pin, native compiler/linker/runtime pins, target triple, distribution/source locations, checksums, licenses, and environment assumptions; the recipes validate checksums before use and write a provenance record beside every artifact. Host bootstrap is separate from target compilation so a clean runner can rebuild without relying on a developer-installed compiler.\n\nRun Linux, macOS, and Windows jobs independently against the same manifest, retaining the existing Node/esbuild build for differential comparison and rollback. Feed the resulting provenance and artifact identities directly into the coverage, differential harness, and release-matrix work rather than introducing a second metadata system. The trade-off is a larger explicit manifest and deliberate pin updates, accepted in exchange for fail-closed reproducibility and auditable release evidence; performance optimizations never waive parity or provenance requirements.\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Foundation — measured compatibility and parity substrate\n\n- **P-001** `done` Pin ScriptC and its native target toolchains reproducibly; record compiler/runtime provenance, supported target triples, licenses, checksums, and a platform-owned build recipe for Linux x64, macOS architectures actually shipped, and Windows x64. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-2024456 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `todo` Run `scriptc coverage` on every executable shipped in the desktop sidecar and classify each statement/module as static, dynamic-island, unsupported, native-addon/FFI, or resource/packaging blocker. keep version-matched Node artifacts installed and exercise rollback in each platform smoke suite. blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Wave 2 — bounded services and workers\n\n- **P-009** `todo` Migrate the event-loop sentinel worker through an explicit executable IPC contract;
