compare prompts, persisted state, subprocess launch, path quoting, terminal encoding, and resume semantics across all release OSes. blocked-by: P-008\n- **P-012** `todo` Activate Wave 2 atomically only after the all-three parity gate and forced rollback pass; record coverage, dynamic-island surface, artifact size, startup, RSS, and divergences without allowing performance to waive correctness. blocked-by: P-009, P-010, P-011 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Wave 3 — operator-facing CLIs\n\n- **P-013** `todo` Migrate `ptool` behind the existing MCP transport contract; test every framing mode, JSON fidelity, large payload, timeout, signal, auth, and exit-code behavior on Linux/macOS/Windows. blocked-by: P-012 importance: high\n- **P-014** `todo` Migrate `psu` and launcher/PTY seams only after native PTY dependencies have an explicit ScriptC strategy (supported API, C FFI, or retained subprocess); preserve account/model/carry flags and window launching on every OS. blocked-by: P-012 importance: high\n- **P-015** `todo` Migrate mutating orchestrator bins (`invoke-once`, `run`) under crash-consistency and exactly-once differential tests, including PostgreSQL transactions, child processes, signals, and restart recovery. blocked-by: P-012 importance: high\n- **P-016** `todo` Activate Wave 3 atomically after all three release legs pass; retain a version-locked Node rollback and verify mixed old/new workspace state cannot create feature drift. blocked-by: P-013, P-014, P-015 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Final wave — operator sidecar\n\n- **P-017** `todo` Make the real `serve.ts` program graph clean under ScriptC's compiler configuration, then capture complete coverage. The current probe stops before lowering on 35 type errors, so no whole-operator coverage claim is valid until this gate is clean. blocked-by: P-016\n- **P-018** `todo` Carve dynamic plugins, native addons, embedded PostgreSQL, ONNX/audio workers, and runtime-loaded resources behind explicit IPC/FFI/resource manifests so coverage is deterministic and unsupported behavior cannot silently fall back. blocked-by: P-017\n- **P-019** `todo` Run the ScriptC operator as a shadow sidecar against representative read-only traffic, then full isolated stateful suites; compare endpoint/tool catalogs, routes, migrations, scheduling, plugins, recovery, observability, and resources on all three OSes. blocked-by: P-018\n- **P-020** `todo` Switch the operator default only in a release whose Linux/macOS/Windows builds all pass the same feature-parity manifest, differential suite, upgrade/rollback test, and soak; ship Node alongside for one rollback window and remove it only in a later gated plan. blocked-by: P-019\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Three-platform parity is a hard activation invariant\nDate: 2026-08-21\nA ScriptC replacement may be built and shadow-tested independently, but it cannot become the default on Linux, macOS, or Windows until all three supported release legs pass the same versioned behavior contract and feature/catalog manifest. If one leg fails, all three keep the Node implementation for that release. Builds still run in parallel; this is an enablement gate, not serial scheduling.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-008, P-012, P-016, P-020\n\n### D-002 — Node artifacts remain the rollback authority\nDate: 2026-08-21\nEvery migrated wave ships a version-matched Node/esbuild artifact until a later plan removes it. Each platform smoke suite must prove forced rollback, and runtime health must make fallback observable rather than silently creating an unknown mixed-engine state.\nRelated: P-004, P-008, P-012, P-016, P-020\n\n### D-003 — Static coverage and dynamic islands are explicit release evidence\nDate: 2026-08-21\nScriptC must never be described as statically compiling a component unless its versioned coverage report proves that claim. npm/any code may use `--dynamic` only through an enumerated dependency manifest; QuickJS shims, copied boundary semantics, unsupported Node builtins, native addons, and FFI bindings are part of the parity review and release provenance.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-006, P-010, P-013, P-014, P-017, P-018\n\n### D-004 — Migrate by executable boundary, not by arbitrary source files\nDate: 2026-08-21\nEach wave replaces a process or worker whose inputs, outputs, resources, and lifecycle can be differentially tested. Shared TypeScript libraries stay source-compatible and may be reached by Node and ScriptC simultaneously; no broad rewrite is justified merely to raise a coverage percentage.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-013, P-014, P-015\n\n### D-005 — Current operator probe is a preflight failure, not a coverage measurement\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMeasured with ScriptC 0.0.34 on 2026-08-20: `scriptc coverage apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts --dynamic` stopped before lowering with 35 TypeScript errors, including missing declarations and standing type mismatches. Therefore no static/dynamic percentage for the whole operator is currently valid; P-017 must establish a clean analyzable graph before a migration decision.\nRelated: P-002, P-017\n\n### D-006 — The web UI and Tauri shell are outside the compiler migration\nDate: 2026-08-21\nVite/browser TypeScript continues to ship as JavaScript in the platform webview, and the Tauri shell remains Rust. ScriptC targets packaged Node-side executables only. Feature parity covers the whole app behavior, but this plan does not replace the browser engine or rewrite existing Rust.\nRelated: P-001, P-020"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"security-analysis-routing-semgrep-codeql-joern-2026-08-21","title":"Security analysis routing: Semgrep / CodeQL / Joern as the D-001 security row","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Security analysis routing: Semgrep / CodeQL / Joern as the D-001 security row\nslug: security-analysis-routing-semgrep-codeql-joern-2026-08-21\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-21\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nFill the one deliberately-empty row of the ratified code-intelligence routing table:\n**security analysis**. Parent plan `code-intelligence-routing-lsp-gitnexus-2026-08-20`\nratified that table as D-001 and, in D-005, split the security engines out of it — because\nSemgrep, CodeQL and Joern are each a real adoption project, and bundling them forced a false\nchoice between rubber-stamping three large installs and stalling the LSP work behind them.\n\nThis plan is that follow-up. It is authored from Phase F of the parent, as D-005 required.\n\n## Why this is not just \"install a linter\"\n\nThe parent plan's own words: Joern is \"specialist, not a default turn tool\". Each engine has a\ndifferent cost centre — CodeQL wants a compiled database and minutes of build time, Semgrep is\nfast but rule-quality-bound, Joern is a CPG with a query language and a steep floor. Picking by\nenthusiasm rather than by measured fit is how a capability nobody uses gets installed.\n\n**Until this plan ships, security questions route to existing practice and SAY SO honestly,\nrather than claiming a capability that is not installed** (parent D-005). That honesty rail is\ninherited, not optional.\n\n## Inherited rails — settled by the parent plan, do not re-litigate\n\n- **PIN THE BINARY, NEVER `npx latest`** (parent D-040). A resolver that reaches the network at\n  call time is not reproducible, and an npm name is not proof of identity — the parent found\n  `code2prompt` on npm is a DIFFERENT project from the intended one, with no executable.\n  Provision to an operator-owned absolute path and assert `--version` EQUALS the pin.\n- **CALLER VALUES MUST NEVER REACH argv FLAG-SHAPED** (parent D-041). The readable, default way\n  to build argv — join the caller's values after `--flag` — makes the security property depend\n  on whether the engine's parser binds a leading-dash token as a VALUE or re-reads it as its own\n  OPTION. Commander and clap have each shipped both behaviours. Two independent defences:\n  refuse leading-dash patterns AND emit attached `--flag=value`. This matters more here than\n  anywhere in the parent plan: the whole point of a security engine is that its checks cannot be\n  disabled by the input it is scanning.\n- **CURATED FACADE ONLY; RAW BACKENDS NEVER IN A RECOMMENDATION POSITION** (parent D-042). The\n  guard at `packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/code-intel-routing-authority.ts` already\n  enforces this by POSITION, with false-positive controls; extend its `BANNED_ROUTES` rather\n  than writing a second guard.\n- **PROMPT WEIGHT IS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED** (parent D-007). Measured\n  2026-08-21: the catalog is at `tools=757 budget=1500 max=1498` — TWO chars of headroom on the\n  heaviest tool. A new facade must fit on arrival; there is no slack to borrow.\n- **CLAUDE.md IS ZERO-SUM** (parent D-043). ~112 chars of headroom against an 80,000-char\n  projection budget. Routing guidance lands in `/internal/docs` and the role playbooks; adding\n  to CLAUDE.md silently evicts another rule.\n- **AN ENGINE THAT ANSWERS OUTSIDE ITS ROW IS A DEFECT** (parent D-001). Security analysis is\n  not type truth, not topology, and not text search.\n\n## The failure mode this plan must design against\n\nThe parent plan's most expensive lesson was epistemic, not technical: `gitnexus.query` returns\nUNRANKED NOISE rather than an empty set, so a nonsense input yields ~20 confident-looking rows\nand its failure is indistinguishable from success (parent D-021). A security engine has the\nsame shape and far higher stakes — **a scanner that silently scans nothing reports CLEAN**,\nwhich is the most dangerous false answer available. Every intake below therefore requires a\nNEGATIVE CONTROL: a known-vulnerable fixture the engine MUST flag, exercised through the same\ninvocation path as the real scan. An engine that cannot produce a positive detection on demand\nis not installed, however green its output looks.\n\n## Now\n\nNot started. First real step is the owner scope gate (P-001): this plan should not install\nthree engines on its own judgment when D-005 explicitly framed engine selection as the decision\nworth separating out.\n\n\n## Phase A — Scope gate and falsifiable corpus\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Owner scope gate: ratify WHICH engines to adopt (Semgrep / CodeQL / Joern) against MEASURED fit, not enthusiasm. D-005 framed engine selection as the decision worth separating out, so do NOT install three engines on agent judgment. Deliverable: a cost/fit table (install footprint, per-scan latency, language coverage, rule-quality dependence, false-positive posture) plus a recommendation AND the honest do-nothing option. importance: urgent\n- **P-002** `todo` Freeze the security acceptance corpus WITH NEGATIVE CONTROLS: per language, a known-vulnerable fixture and the exact finding each engine must report, plus a clean twin that must NOT be flagged. Pin the baseline commit. This is the artifact that makes a CLEAN verdict falsifiable — without it, an engine that scans nothing is indistinguishable from an engine that found nothing. importance: urgent\n\n\n## Phase B — Bakeoff on the frozen corpus\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Semgrep bakeoff: run the frozen corpus, record detection rate against the known-vulnerable fixtures, false positives against the clean twins, per-scan latency and RSS. Record rule-provenance (which ruleset, pinned to which revision) — Semgrep is rule-quality-bound, so an unpinned ruleset makes the measurement unreproducible. importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` CodeQL bakeoff on the identical corpus. Measure the DATABASE BUILD cost explicitly (wall time, disk, whether it needs a working compile) — that cost, not query latency, is what decides whether CodeQL can ever be a turn-time tool here or is strictly a scheduled/CI engine. importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Joern bakeoff on the identical corpus. The parent plan already calls it \"specialist, not a default turn tool\" — so the question this item answers is narrow: is there a class of question (dataflow/taint across a CPG) that NEITHER Semgrep nor CodeQL answers acceptably here? If not, record that and drop it rather than adopting it for completeness.\n- **P-006** `todo` Record the backend selection as a plan Decision using REPRODUCED evidence, including the rejected alternatives and why. State the default explicitly: if no engine clears the bar, the honest outcome is that the D-001 security row stays unfilled and guidance keeps saying so. importance: high\n\n\n\n\n## Phase C — Integration behind a curated facade\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Provision the selected engine(s) PINNED to operator-owned absolute paths; assert --version EQUALS the pin at test time and resolve by explicit path only, never `command -v` and never `npx latest` (parent D-040 — an npm name is not proof of identity). importance: high\n- **P-008** `todo` argv safety per parent D-041, with HOSTILE-INPUT tests written FIRST: caller values must never reach argv flag-shaped. Two independent defences — refuse leading-dash patterns AND emit attached --flag=value. The specific thing to prove: a caller cannot disable the scan (or its severity floor, or its ruleset) through the values it passes. A test matrix of only well-formed inputs would go green on the vulnerable build. importance: urgent\n- **P-009** `todo` Build the read-only curated facade (mirroring lsp-facade.ts / packer-facade.ts: frozen op list, one entry point returning a typed answer for EVERY outcome including refusals, budget applied recording the PRE-CUT total). FLAGS-gated, default ON once verified, managedSpawn-enrolled. Measure prompt weight ON ARRIVAL — the catalog sits at max=1498 of a 1500 budget (parent D-007). importance: high\n- **P-010** `todo` NEGATIVE-CONTROL TEST IN CI: the engine must FLAG the known-vulnerable fixture through the REAL invocation path (not a unit-mocked one), and must NOT flag the clean twin. A scanner that silently scans nothing reports CLEAN, which is the most dangerous false answer available — this test is the only thing standing between that and a green build. importance: urgent\n\n\n\n\n## Phase D — Routing and adoption\n\n- **P-011** `todo` Fill the D-001 security row and extend BANNED_ROUTES in packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/code-intel-routing-authority.ts (do NOT write a second guard — parent D-042 established the position-not-presence design with false-positive controls). Guidance lands in /internal/docs and the role playbooks, NOT CLAUDE.md, which has ~112 chars of headroom (parent D-043). importance: high\n- **P-012** `todo` Author the acceptance rubric against as-built reality, get it vetted and INDEPENDENTLY graded by a non-implementer, publish the runbook, and only then ship. Include the honest statement of what the adopted engine does NOT cover, so the next agent does not read a partial capability as a complete one.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"serialize-and-slow-kopia-backups-2026-08-20","title":"Serialize Kopia backups and reduce hot-backup cadence","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Serialize Kopia backups and reduce hot-backup cadence\nslug: serialize-and-slow-kopia-backups-2026-08-20\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-10-01\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE + LIVE; plan remains READY only for the mandatory acceptance-review sequence. Code-truth audit #1 passed 4/4 with 17 citations. Acceptance rubric acceptance-serialize-and-slow-kopia-backups-2026-08-20 is active/current/complete (4 criteria, methodRef, drift markers, relevant test bindings). Fresh critique consult conv-mt309uz6-0000-5ebe1d11e6a74156944778167faa3d0a is awaiting responder su-1d899d11. After critique: emit current-revision meta-acceptance vetting scorecard, invoke shipped gate to launch/discover a non-implementer grader, await its complete grade, record author acceptance, and mark shipped. All source locks released; runtime idle; next backup 10:00.\n\n**Next:** Read consult conv-mt309uz6-0000-5ebe1d11e6a74156944778167faa3d0a; reconcile any critique, vet current rubric revision, drive independent grading + author acceptance, then set status shipped and end the continuation loop.\n\n## Goal\n\nPrevent backup-induced desktop freezes with the smallest durable change: one shared lock across hot, daily home/VM, and protected/manual Kopia snapshots; pressure-aware deferral for scheduled work; and a 30-minute hot cadence with a matching health threshold.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- At most one managed Kopia snapshot operation may run at a time across the hot, daily home/VM, and protected/manual entrypoints.\n- A scheduled hot backup must skip cleanly when the global lock is held or host memory/I/O full PSI is above the configured safety threshold; a protected/manual backup must wait for the same lock.\n- Lock ownership must be kernel-released on normal exit, command failure, signal, or process death; no stale lock file may wedge future backups.\n- The effective hot cadence must be 30 minutes, and production snapshot-staleness detection must allow one missed cycle plus runtime/jitter by using a 60-minute threshold.\n- Existing source selection, cold-source exclusion, repository format, retention, pre-snapshot hook, backup exit semantics, and restore behavior must remain unchanged.\n- Automated regression coverage must prove mutual exclusion, scheduled skip/defer behavior, protected/manual wait behavior, PSI parsing/threshold behavior, and failure cleanup.\n- Live verification must show the effective timer/threshold, no concurrent Kopia processes, and a successful guarded cycle without new Xorg slow-input warnings or sustained memory/I/O PSI regression.\n\n## Design\n\nIntroduce one tracked, reusable guard entrypoint in the existing backup/systemd surface. It opens a single per-user runtime lock and then either acquires it non-blocking for scheduled mode or waits for it in protected/manual mode before executing the supplied command. Scheduled mode reads Linux memory and I/O full PSI before starting and exits successfully with an explicit deferred result when either configured threshold is unsafe. The hot and daily home/VM scripts call the guard rather than maintaining independent locks; the documented protected/manual command uses wait mode. The timer override changes from 15 to 30 minutes and the healthcheck default from 30 to 60 minutes. This deliberately avoids a system-service migration and hard cgroup caps: serialization plus admission addresses the measured overlap incident with less privilege and operational change; stronger resource isolation remains a later escalation only if a single guarded run still breaches the pressure budget.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis deliberately does not migrate Kopia to a system service or add hard cgroup limits. Those remain escalation options only if a single serialized backup still breaches the desktop pressure budget. Preserve existing source filters, retention, repository format, and restore behavior.\n\n## Proposed decisions\n\n- Effective hot-backup cadence: 30 minutes instead of 15.\n- Snapshot staleness threshold: 60 minutes instead of 30, preserving one missed-cycle tolerance plus runtime/jitter.\n- Scheduled jobs skip when the global lock is held or host PSI is already unsafe; protected/manual jobs wait for the same lock.\n- Daily home/VM and hot backups must no longer own separate locks.\n\n## Verification contract\n\nAutomated tests must prove lock mutual exclusion, scheduled skip/defer behavior, protected/manual wait behavior, pressure-threshold parsing, and lock release after failure. Live verification must confirm the effective timer, healthcheck defaults, zero concurrent Kopia processes, and one successful guarded scheduled cycle without Xorg slow-input warnings or sustained memory/I/O PSI regression.\n\n## Phase - Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` importance:high Add a canonical shared Kopia guard with one global lock, scheduled pressure deferral, protected/manual wait mode, and automated tests for mutual exclusion, PSI parsing, and failure cleanup. — note: ← WI-40236 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` importance:high blocked-by:P-001 Wire the hot snapshot and daily home/VM snapshot paths through the shared guard, preserve their source/exit semantics, and document the guarded protected/manual entrypoint. — note: ← WI-40237 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` importance:high blocked-by:P-002 Change the effective hot-backup cadence from 15 to 30 minutes and the snapshot-staleness threshold from 30 to 60 minutes; update comments and healthcheck self-tests. — note: ← WI-40238 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` importance:high blocked-by:P-003 Install/reload the effective user configuration, run focused automated tests and shell self-tests, then verify one real guarded scheduled cycle has no Kopia overlap, stale-alert regression, Xorg slow-input warning, or sustained memory/I/O PSI breach. — note: ← WI-40239 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase - Post-incident dump churn\n\n- **P-005** `done` Canonicalize the live papercusp-db-backup writer in apps/operator/scripts/systemd and switch system-cluster plus oddsmith pg_dump directory archives from inner zlib compression to uncompressed output so outer Kopia zstd/content-defined chunking can deduplicate hourly rewrites without weakening the hourly RPO or pg_restore validation. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40561 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Extend the existing backup-health signal to monitor the backup filesystem independently of PGDATA, retain a measured history, and report ETA to the 2% admission floor rather than only ETA to full; add isolated self-test coverage for green, red, falling, recovering, and insufficient-history cases. blocked-by: P-005 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40562 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `todo` Install/reload the canonical writer, prove a real uncompressed dump is pg_restore-readable, and measure two consecutive post-change dump/snapshot cycles against the pre-change 6.3 GB upload baseline; close WI-39596 only if growth is bounded and the backup-volume detector is live. blocked-by: P-005, P-006 importance: urgent\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — All managed Kopia snapshots share one guard\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThe canonical contract is one per-user runtime flock for every managed Kopia snapshot. Hot scheduled work uses non-blocking acquisition plus memory/I/O full-PSI admission and defers cleanly; daily home/VM and protected/manual work wait for the same lock. The hot cadence is 30 minutes and snapshot staleness is 60 minutes. Direct raw protected/manual Kopia snapshot-create invocations are outside the supported path; use the guarded entrypoint. System-service migration and hard cgroup caps are deferred unless a single serialized run still violates the PSI/Xorg acceptance budget.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-002 — Concurrency acceptance counts managed snapshot-create operations, not process names\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThe live monitor's raw pgrep-by-name sample briefly reached two, but that metric counts any process named Kopia and does not establish two backup writers. The load-bearing writer audit for the finished-code run is: exactly one sudo command containing snapshot create, one guard started event, one guard finished rc=0 event, one snapshot-log run start, and one snapshot-log run end; current Kopia process count is zero. Therefore D-001 acceptance is defined as at most one managed snapshot-create operation. The identity of the brief second name-only process was not captured, so no stronger claim about it is made.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-003 — Preserve hourly database RPO; remove inner compression so Kopia can deduplicate rewrites\nDate: 2026-08-22\nLive writer evidence on 2026-08-22 distinguishes cadence from representation: /mnt/data/Backup/db-dumps was 35–36 GB; the first Kopia cycle after an hourly pg_dump -Fd -Z1 rewrite uploaded 6.3 GB, while the next unchanged 30-minute cycle uploaded 0 B. Therefore the 30-minute hot timer is not itself the hourly churn source. Keep the hourly database recovery-point objective and existing 30-minute guarded snapshot cadence. Change both system-cluster and oddsmith directory-format dumps to uncompressed pg_dump output; Kopia remains the single zstd compression layer, allowing content-defined chunking across rewrites. Acceptance requires a real pg_restore-readable artifact plus consecutive-cycle repository-growth measurement. Independently monitor the backup filesystem against the 2% admission floor.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-004 — Serialize database dump rewrites with managed Kopia snapshots on the existing guard\nDate: 2026-08-22\nAt 04:00 EDT on 2026-08-22, papercusp-db-backup.service and kopia-snapshots.service started six seconds apart. Because the DB unit did not participate in the shared guard, both writers ran together and I/O full avg10 rose to 52.41%; stopping only the scheduled snapshot reduced it to 10.19% immediately and 1.31% after decay while the DB dump continued. The canonical DB service therefore uses the existing kopia-backup-guard.sh in wait mode with label db-dump around papercusp-db-backup.sh. Wait mode preserves D-003's hourly RPO; holding the same lock prevents Kopia from snapshotting a dump rewrite or competing for disk bandwidth. This extends D-001's single serialization surface rather than adding another lock. The recurrence guard is packages/operator-core/lib/kopia-backup-guard.test.ts, which requires both the shared-guard route and the canonical uncompressed writer tail.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-005 — D-005 — Shared guard spans user and root maintenance identities\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe mixed-UID reproduction for EI-21144963086649202 disproves D-001's per-user runtime lock as a complete serialization contract: a user guard under /run/user/1000 and a root-launched guarded task under /run/user/0 entered concurrently. Preserve one guard and the existing scheduled-vs-wait semantics, but pin the production default to the host-shared /run/lock/papercusp-kopia-global.lock namespace. Create the lock with shared-write permissions so both the user systemd services and root maintenance can open the same inode; retain KOPIA_BACKUP_LOCK_PATH as the explicit test/deployment override. Add a mixed-UID regression proving a root-launched waiter blocks behind a user-launched holder.\n\n### D-006 — D-006 — Dedicated lock subdirectory avoids sticky-lock protected_regular denial\nDate: 2026-08-22\nFollow-up to D-005 from live default-path verification: this host has fs.protected_regular=2, so root cannot open a user-owned lock file directly in sticky /run/lock even when mode 0666. Use the dedicated non-sticky /run/lock/papercusp/kopia-global.lock path instead. The guard creates the subdirectory and lock under umask 000, yielding a shared-write directory/file for either user-systemd or root maintenance identity. Keep the explicit KOPIA_BACKUP_LOCK_PATH override for isolated tests. Acceptance remains bidirectional mixed-UID serialization on the actual default path.\n\n### D-007 — Phase the hourly dump after the hot snapshot source window\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\nMeasured: the six-hour KOPIA_BACKUP_GUARD read returned 65 rows and showed three hot sweeps stopped with `deferred-during-run reason=priority-waiter shared-guard handoff`. The complete `/mnt/backup/db-dumps` snapshot row ran 2026-09-30T23:30:08Z–23:37:23Z (7m15s); local dump runs were 25.9–47.8m. At 2026-10-01T00:45:12Z the healthcheck measured that source stale by 1h14 (last row start 23:30:08Z). The loaded hot timer fires at :00/:30 with up to 20s random delay; the DB timer was hourly at :00 with up to 90s random delay and 1m accuracy. The DB waiter is priority and the dump is non-restart-safe.\nSet the hourly DB timer to :10. Keep D-001's 30m hot cadence, 60m snapshot-staleness budget, and shared guard, plus D-003's hourly local RPO. The existing REQUIRED_SOURCES order puts `/mnt/backup/db-dumps` first: :00 hot runs then have at least 9m25s before the earliest :10 DB run, and a post-dump :30 waiter has at least 9m40s before the next earliest :10 run under the measured 47.8m dump duration; both windows exceed the measured 7m15s source capture. Guard this schedule/source-order contract in the timer regression test.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-008 — The local-only transcript tier is dumped outside the shared guard (amends D-004 for that tier)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-77ceb44f for WI-10004870.\n\nD-004 put the hourly db-dump under the shared Kopia guard for two reasons: (a) so Kopia never snapshots a dump mid-rewrite, and (b) so the dump and a snapshot do not compete for disk bandwidth (measured 2026-08-22: I/O full avg10 52.41% with both running).\n\nThe papercusp-transcript tier (~101G, ~25 min to dump) is excluded from every Kopia snapshot by .kopiaignore (ratified ruling, WI-2146225), so reason (a) cannot apply to it. Holding the lock through that phase blocked the hot sweep for ~25 min every 2.5h without protecting any snapshot.\n\nRuling: papercusp-db-backup.sh dumps every snapshotted tier under the shared guard as before, then asks kopia-backup-guard.sh to drop the lock early (request file at KOPIA_BACKUP_GUARD_RELEASE_PATH; the guard logs result=released-early). Only after that does it dump the due transcript tiers. The migration rendezvous and pg_dump-vs-pg_dump serialization are unchanged. D-001's Kopia-vs-Kopia serialization is unchanged; this ruling applies only to the db-dump label.\n\nReason (b) is knowingly relaxed for this tier. It stays open until measured: on the first transcript-due run on the new code (expected 21:10Z timer, 2026-10-01), record the I/O full avg10 during the overlap, plus the durations of the transcript dump and the hot sweep's db-dumps capture against their solo baselines (~25 min; 7m15s per D-007). If the overlap pushes I/O full avg10 to the D-004 level, or measurably slows the db-dumps capture, revert this tier to dumping under the lock, or gate its start on the guard's I/O admission, and record that here.\n\nGuards: backup-tier-split.test.ts (transcript tiers dumped after the release request), kopia-backup-guard.test.ts (early release hands the lock back; no request keeps the whole-lifetime hold). Both were proven falsifiable with copy-out mutants.\nRelated: P-007\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"sidestage-mobile-pagespeed-exceptional-2026-08-21","title":"Make SideStage mobile PageSpeed exceptional","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make SideStage mobile PageSpeed exceptional\nslug: sidestage-mobile-pagespeed-exceptional-2026-08-21\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-21\n---\n\n## Objective\nDiagnose and eliminate the causes of poor mobile PageSpeed performance on https://sidestage.papercusp.com/, deploy the verified fix through the canonical release pipeline, and rerun PageSpeed until the result is consistently exceptional.\n\n## Success criteria\n- Mobile Lighthouse/PageSpeed Performance score is at least 95 on three consecutive post-deploy runs.\n- FCP, LCP, TBT, CLS, and Speed Index are all in Lighthouse's green/good bands on those runs (FCP <= 1.8 s, LCP <= 2.5 s, TBT <= 200 ms, CLS <= 0.1, Speed Index <= 3.4 s).\n- Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO remain at least 95, with regressions fixed if this work causes any.\n- Relevant local tests/build checks pass; the fresh green checkpoint is rerun and the green pin is deployed.\n\n## Approach\nCapture a reproducible baseline and audit evidence; trace each costly request/task/layout shift to the code that produces it; prefer small reuse-first changes; add a recurrence guard in the project test framework; verify locally; release through git-sync -> checkpoint -> deploy; then run repeated public mobile PageSpeed tests and iterate on any remaining red/orange metric.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-21. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nState: active owner-directed remediation.\nNext: establish baseline and map the deployed URL to its canonical source and build path.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Phase — Execution\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Reproduce the mobile PageSpeed baseline and identify the concrete render/network/main-thread bottlenecks in the canonical SideStage implementation. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40330 dropped\n- **P-002** `todo` Implement the smallest durable performance fixes and add project-native regression coverage. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent\n- **P-003** `todo` Run focused tests, production build analysis, and local Lighthouse verification; iterate until thresholds are green. blocked-by: P-002 importance: urgent\n- **P-004** `todo` Drive git-sync, a fresh green checkpoint verdict, and deployment of the green pin; diagnose and repair any red gate encountered. blocked-by: P-003 importance: urgent\n- **P-005** `todo` Rerun public mobile PageSpeed at least three times; iterate through code, verification, and redeploy until all stated success criteria hold consistently. blocked-by: P-004 importance: urgent\n\n\n\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"state-plane-interest-and-hardening-2026-08-21","title":"State plane: interest profiles, delivery hardening, and earn-in discipline","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: State plane: interest profiles, delivery hardening, and earn-in discipline\nslug: state-plane-interest-and-hardening-2026-08-21\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n## Now\n\nstate: authored 2026-08-21 from the owner's state-plane audit conversation — adoption measured, delivery gaps identified, interest-tier design ratified [owner:Avi 2026-08-21 commissioned the plan; design content ratified in discussion].\nnext: owner review. Phase 0 items are independent and same-day sized; Phase 2 orient/leader-brief items must land atop fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21 (see D-005).\n\n## Background\n\nA 2026-08-21 audit of the unified agent state plane (cell-registry.ts + ~10 registered cells) measured its first two weeks live (2026-08-07 → 08-21, papercusp-workspace, harness_shared.tool_invocations):\n\n- state:read 2,467 calls / 328 distinct callers, near-zero errors — but 81% concentrated on the 3 gate cells. Core earns its keep; it is today a gate-triage plane wearing a general registry's badge.\n- state:subscribe 300 calls / 77 callers with 17% not_ok (unclassified). watch:create called directly only 14×/2 callers ever — the cell preset rescued predicate_watches (253 registrations, 250 fired/consumed) from the zero adoption measured at P-003 ship time.\n- facts dependsOn: 4 of 1,916 live facts (0.2%) — dormant, confounded by facts:assert rejecting ~41–49% of calls (EI-21067740598816833).\n- testing.* cells: 0 reads ever. Plane stamps: 2 doors. Fleet transition event keys observed at zero live awaiters while leaders poll on timers.\n\nDelivery gaps found: subscription fire payloads carry no reread handle (the one delivery surface without one); absent reads give no near-miss help (host.load / release.gate / bare gate.greenCheckpoint guesses observed in invocation data); caller-relative cells lack 'self' sugar (agent.goal at 14 calls / 2 callers); a workspace-scoped su session lists only 4 of ~10 cells although CLAUDE.md directs su agents at the gate cells; state:read's no-arg directory note contradicts state:subscribe for event-signalled cells (EI-21069242359753673, filed).\n\nDesign ratified in the audit conversation: cell VALUES stay pull-only; automatic delivery is verdicts + handles; role/state interest is delivered in three tiers — fold (ambient, no interrupt), suggest (ready-to-fire handle at a transition moment), auto-arm (reserved for contexts where the miss is catastrophic and already mandated).\n\n## Goal\n\nLive state reaches the agents who need it automatically — as handles, folds, and edge-triggered wakes, never ambient value copies — and every plane feature demonstrably earns its tenure.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- No ambient injection of cell VALUES into prompts or turns (D-001).\n- No second subscription mechanism and no new state store (existing D-038 axis-5 / P-004 discipline carries forward).\n- No fleet-METRIC content in any fold, brief, or delta this plan touches — that is fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21's exclusive scope (D-005).\n- The event catalog does not become a cell (D-004).\n\n## Phase 0 — Delivery fixes (independent, same-day sized)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Subscription fire payloads carry the plane handle: extend evalPredicateWatch's emitAwaitedEvent payload ({ observed, predicate }) with reread { tool: 'state:read', args: { cell, as } } for watches registered through state:subscribe — thread the cell id + subject into the watch row at registration so the fire site can name them (events/await/predicate-watch.ts + agent-tools/state/subscribe.ts). The wake is currently the only delivery surface that hands an agent a volatile value without its re-read handle. importance: high — note: ← WI-40245 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Absent-read aftercare: state:read on an unknown cell returns audience-scoped near-miss suggestions (fuzzy match over listCells(reader) only — never the unchecked registry, preserving P-019's non-oracle property) plus redirects for known non-cells (host.load / host.now → \"orient field, call nothing\"). Fix the no-arg directory note that points event-signalled cells at state:subscribe instead of events:await (absorbs EI-21069242359753673). — note: ← WI-40247 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` as:'self' sugar: caller-relative cells whose declared param is an agent identity accept the literal 'self' in state:read and state:subscribe, resolving to the caller's ownerId — the existing coord-tools convention applied to the plane. — note: ← WI-40248 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Classify state:subscribe's 17% not_ok (50/300): break down error_message/error_code in tool_invocations; separate teaching-refusals (absent cell, missing as, no-materiality) from real breakage; fix what is broken; give each refusal class a distinct error_code so the taxonomy is a single query next time. — note: ← WI-40249 completed (done)\n- **P-022** `done` Wake folds the delivery-time reading (implements D-007, supersedes P-001's handle-only scope): when a state:subscribe watch fires, the wake turn's prompt folds the subscribed cell's compact reading (headline + material path + hoisted unknowns, state:read shape) resolved at TURN-ASSEMBLY time, stamped with resolvedAt + the reread handle; resolver error or latency-budget breach degrades to the P-001 handle-only form, never delaying the wake. importance: high — note: ← WI-40246 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Earn-in for the dormant halves\n\n- **P-005** `done` Reach verification: probes (measurement sweep and/or CI) asserting each cell's docs-declared audiences resolve readable:true via canReadCell — enumerating via listCellsUnchecked, the sanctioned admin surface. Diagnose and fix the observed gap: a workspace-scoped su session lists 4 of ~10 cells while CLAUDE.md directs su agents at the gate cells (scoping bug, doc bug, or serving-process divergence — determine which). importance: high — note: ← WI-40261 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Fix facts:assert's ~41–49% call-rejection rate (schema-shape failures, EI-21067740598816833) — precondition for any dependsOn adoption push. — note: ← WI-40263 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Auto-derive dependsOn: run the transcription-detector matcher over facts:assert bodies; on a high-confidence cell-value match, return the corresponding dependsOn entry as an accept-in-one-call suggestion (attach-mode only after measured precision), disclosed in the result with a one-field strip. Precision-first per EI-10949. blocked-by: P-006 — note: ← WI-40266 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Tenure rule: a periodic adoption verdict for registered cells — 0 reads over a trailing window produces a cut-or-keep line (agent-plane-measurement-sweep as home); first subjects: testing.census.population, testing.coverage.floor. The admission rule (\"a read with 0 calls is never promoted\") gains its tenure counterpart. — note: ← WI-40269 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Federation: verify a real transport exists behind federation:'shareable' (source_hive / fed_ts path); wire it or flip declared-but-untransported cells to local — a declaration with no mechanism is contract theater. — note: ← WI-40273 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Interest profiles (relevance without interrupts)\n\n- **P-010** `done` Interest-profile registry: declared data co-located with (not widening) the cell registry — the transcription-detector precedent keeps CellSpec at its ratified axes. Rows { context: fleet-leader | fleet-member | plan-holder | item-holder, watch: cell id | event key, tier: fold | suggest | auto-arm, on?, of?, why }; a test asserts every referenced cell/event is registered so profiles cannot drift. importance: high — note: ← WI-40275 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Fold tier: coord:orient matches the caller's live contexts (leadership, membership, lane, held items — all already resolved by orient) against profiles and folds matching cells' headline + reread handle, under the facts-fold dispatch budget, audience-checked, materiality-aware. Same-surface coordination: fleet-spec-scoped-metrics P-007 adds its leader metrics fold to this file — this fold carries NO metric content and lands atop their shape (D-005). blocked-by: P-010 — note: ← WI-40291 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Poller dispatch dedupe: within one poll tick, due watches sharing (tool, canonical args hash) share one resolver dispatch — the scaling prerequisite for auto-arm fan-out across a fleet. — note: ← WI-40292 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Lifecycle binding: bound_to { kind, ref } on predicate_watches + event_awaits (migration via the atomic allocator, scripts/next-migration.mjs), with GC hooked into the exits that already exist — take-leadership demotion, fleet end, work_items release/complete, presence reap. Auto/suggested-armed rows die with the state that justified them. blocked-by: P-010 — note: ← WI-40313 completed (done)\n- **P-014** `done` Leader auto-arm: fleet:take-leadership and leader-side fleet:launch-on-plan arm the leader profile's standard set (fleet-member-dead / fleet-drained / fleet-context-critical / fleet-claim-released awaits + any profile poll cells), disclosed in the tool result with the cancel handle; per-agent cap; FLAGS entry, default ON. Mechanizes what the persona already mandates and agents demonstrably skip — no NEW interrupts are manufactured. blocked-by: P-012, P-013 — note: ← WI-40322 completed (done)\n- **P-015** `done` Zero-awaiters advisory: leaderBrief gains one advisory line when the fleet's transition keys sit at live_awaiters:0 (read from events:catalog) — \"you are monitoring blind\" + the arm handle. ADDITIVE to the leaderBrief snapshot fleet-spec-scoped-metrics P-005 hydrates; consumes events:catalog, never their metric kernel (D-005). blocked-by: P-010 — note: ← WI-40325 completed (done)\n- **P-016** `done` Suggest tier: fleet:join returns suggestedWatches[] (ready state:subscribe / events:await calls + why); work_items:claim on an item whose blocker maps to a profile entry (gate-blocked → gate-green await) returns the same shape. One call to accept; nothing armed silently. blocked-by: P-010 — note: ← WI-40341 completed (done)\n- **P-023** `done` Epoch-boundary orient injection (implements D-008): extend the ## Orientation (Route A) injection to all epoch boundaries — carry-respawn first prompt, cold loop wake, fleet kickoff, session start — resolving the DERIVABLE orient fold (assignments, held checkpoints, staleness warnings, announced gates, inbox summary, leader brief) at prompt-assembly time, deriving intent where the epoch knows it (kickoff = plan lane, carry = prior intent). coord:orient remains the re-orient verb. Coordinate with fleet-spec-scoped-metrics P-007 on the leader fold surface (D-005 additive rule applies). importance: high — note: ← WI-40279 completed (done)\n- **P-024** `done` Additional interest-profile contexts (extends P-010's row set): (a) blocked-item holders auto-armed on their named blocker's resolution (work-item-done:<blocker> / work-item-unblocked), lifecycle-bound to the blocked state; (b) claim holders notified on their own claim's release/reassignment (claim-released) so leader reclaims are never silent; (c) ask/escalation/consult requesters armed on the answer event (escalation-resolved, conversation-answered) — verify which verbs already wire this and close the rest; (d) leader profile gains rate-limit-paused / rate-limit-reset / fleet-admission-blocked; (e) plan-lane workers get a fold/notify (not wake) on decision_added for their plan. blocked-by: P-010 — note: ← WI-40343 completed (done)\n- **P-025** `done` Owner-as-context: the owner is an interest context too — fold the needs-human / owner-gated queue (parked walls, items awaiting owner decisions, pending ask-owner escalations) into the OWNER's own interactive surfaces on owner presence, instead of relying on agents re-broadcasting walls in status reports. Same fold/suggest tiering; no wake tier (the owner is not woken by machinery). [owner:Avi 2026-08-21 asked that everything discussed be covered; originally parked in-conversation] blocked-by: P-010 importance: low — note: WI-40379 done. Shipped typed owner-present interest rows and registry-driven plans:attention selection; 43/43 focused tests passed and scoped lint:tsc status=clean across P-025 plus leader-control exhaustiveness guard.\n- **P-027** `done` Widen the epoch-boundary orient fold's CONTENT to D-008's full list — P-023 delivered the DELIVERY MECHANISM only (it fixed the suppression; see D-015). renderOrientationLines() currently emits held + unansweredDirected + loopArmed. Still missing from P-023's own text: held CHECKPOINTS, staleness warnings, announced gates, a real inbox summary, and the leader brief. TWO CONSTRAINTS for whoever takes this: (1) ORIENTATION_BUDGET_CHARS is 600 and the composer DROPS lowest-priority lines under pressure, so ADDED lines change WHICH existing lines get dropped — re-check the priority order, do not just append. (2) The leader-brief half is NOT unilateral: it lands on fleet-spec-scoped-metrics P-007's surface under D-005's additive rule, so coordinate there rather than emitting it from this fold. — note: ← WI-40392 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Convergence and re-audit\n\n- **P-017** `done` Widen plane-stamp adoption: emit stampStatePlane blocks from additional doors whose payloads carry cell-backed volatile values (candidates: release:deploy op:status, routines:list green-checkpoint row, dev:build_status). Registering the missing cells where a door value has none is in scope; stamps stay registry-derived — no hand tables. — note: ← WI-40404 completed (done)\n- **P-018** `done` Re-audit: repeat the adoption measurement (reads by cell, subscribe fires + error taxonomy, dependsOn count, stamp door coverage, leader transition keys' live_awaiters) after Phases 0–2 land; grade against the coordination-state-feature-adoption uptake rubric; report deltas to the owner with a prune list per P-008. blocked-by: P-011, P-014, P-016 — note: ← WI-40413 completed (done)\n- **P-026** `done` Meta-layer earn-in + interest-machinery efficacy measurement (extends P-018's re-audit scope per D-006): (a) transcription-detector advisory fire rate AND heed rate (did the advised agent re-read?); (b) auto-armed wake action-rate (did the woken agent act on the armed interest, or ignore it — the EI-10949 signal-to-noise guard applied to wakes); (c) fold-tier render cost per orient vs. the shaper budget; (d) agent-plane-measurement-sweep utility (does anything consume its output?). The meta layer must earn tenure by the same rule as the cells it measures. — note: ← WI-40415 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Cell VALUES are never ambient-injected — automatic delivery is verdicts and handles only\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21\nRatified in the owner audit: an injected value is a transcription wearing system authority — the exact artifact the plane exists to kill (state-plane-stamp.ts's NO-VALUE-COPY rule, D-044's surprisal line, P-021's measured fold cost). Every automatic delivery surface this plan adds ships the reread HANDLE, a staleness/change VERDICT, or an edge-triggered wake — never an ambient copy of the value itself. Pull (state:read at the moment of acting) remains the only path a value travels into an agent's reasoning.\nRelated: P-001, P-011\n\n### D-002 — Interest ≠ interrupt: three delivery tiers, auto-arm initially leaders-only\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21\nRole/state interest is delivered at the cheapest tier that serves it: fold (ambient, rides orient, no interrupt) for most contexts; suggest (a ready-to-fire subscribe/await handle returned at the transition moment — join, claim) when a wake MAY be warranted; auto-arm (subscriptions armed without asking) ONLY where the miss is catastrophic and the behavior is already mandated — fleet leaders' transition-event monitoring, where the observed failure is leaders polling while the event keys sit at zero awaiters. Auto-arm manufactures no new interrupts; it mechanizes mandated ones. Widening auto-arm beyond leaders requires a new decision here.\nRelated: P-010, P-011, P-014, P-016\n\n### D-003 — Auto/suggested-armed subscriptions are lifecycle-bound and die with the state that justified them\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21\nEvery watch or await armed by the interest machinery carries bound_to { kind, ref } (fleet slug / claim / plan lane) and is GC'd on the binding's death: leadership demotion or transfer, fleet end, work-item release/complete, presence reap. Without this, role-derived subscriptions accumulate as stale pollers waking dead sessions — the mechanized version of coupling nobody decoupled. Hand-armed subscriptions (an agent's own state:subscribe) are untouched: they keep predicate_watches' existing per-row lifecycle. The binding is ALSO the wake's provenance: every fire of an auto/suggested-armed subscription names its bound_to justification in the wake payload (\"armed because you hold leadership of <fleet>\"), so an agent is never woken by machinery it cannot attribute — and can cancel what it can see.\nRelated: P-013, P-014, P-016\n\n### D-004 — Event discovery stays a directory (events:catalog + announcedGates), not a cell\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21\nA cell answers \"what is the value of X right now\" under a falsifiability contract; the event catalog is a directory browsed while deciding what to wait on — no headline to misread, no independent measurement to falsify it. events:catalog (44 machine families + live_awaiters + provenance) and the announcedGates orient fold (declared gates, scoped, latching) remain the discovery surfaces; the improvement lever is relevance-scoped folding of catalog content per interest profiles (e.g. the P-015 zero-awaiters advisory), never reifying the directory as a cell.\nRelated: P-015\n\n### D-005 — Boundary with fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21: metric content is exclusively theirs; this plan ships handles and watches, landing additively\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21\nfleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21 owns ALL fleet-metric content and contracts: the spec-scoped metric kernel (their P-002), burn-down (P-003), the leaderBrief canonical snapshot (P-005), the cursor-based fleetDelta (P-006), and the leader-orient metrics fold (P-007, their D-003). THIS plan adds no counts, no populations, no metric fields to any fold, brief, or delta — its orient fold (P-011) carries cell handles/gates only, and its leaderBrief line (P-015) is one additive advisory consuming events:catalog live_awaiters, never their kernel. On the shared files (coord:orient fold assembly, fleet:leader-brief), this plan's items land AFTER or rebase ATOP that plan's shape — their contract is never altered, only appended to. Their D-004 (snapshot vs delta separate contracts) and D-005 (populations never silently compared) are honored by construction since no metric population is touched.\nRelated: P-011, P-015\n\n### D-006 — Earn-in before build-out: the registry's admission rule gains a tenure counterpart\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMeasured two weeks in: 81% of reads are 3 gate cells; testing.* cells have 0 reads; facts dependsOn sits at 4 of 1,916 live facts. The plane's periphery must adopt or be cut before new plane surfaces are added: P-008's periodic 0-read verdict enforces tenure, and P-018's re-audit (graded against the coordination-state-feature-adoption uptake rubric) is the gate on any post-plan expansion. \"A read with 0 calls is never promoted\" now also means \"a cell with 0 reads does not keep its seat by default\".\nRelated: P-008, P-018\n\n### D-007 — Wake turns fold the DELIVERY-TIME reading — fire-time resolution is the transcription hazard, not injection itself\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 [owner:Avi 2026-08-21 — challenged handle-only wakes: \"why instruct them to do a read when we can just inject the read?\"]. Ratified: the anti-transcription rule locates the hazard at WHEN the value was resolved, not how it travels. Fire-time payloads go stale across the fire→delivery lag (a parked session boots, a respawn queues — minutes), so they stay trigger-evidence only. But a reading resolved at TURN-ASSEMBLY/delivery time is exactly as fresh as the agent's own first-action state:read, minus one full LLM round-trip — and by the plane's own stamp thesis (promotion measured at 1.7%; make the right data travel the only path), instructing that read is promotion where injection is the lazy path. RULE: a wake for a cell subscription folds the cell's COMPACT reading (headline + material path + hoisted unknowns — state:read shape, never the door's full payload), resolved at prompt assembly, stamped with resolvedAt + the reread handle; resolver error or latency-budget breach degrades to handle-only rather than delaying the wake. Act-time re-read still applies when acting long after delivery. This supersedes P-001's handle-only scope — P-022 implements; P-001's handle remains as the degraded/fallback form.\nRelated: P-001, P-022\n\n### D-008 — Epoch boundaries INJECT the derivable orient fold instead of instructing the call — derivable vs caller-parameterized is the split\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 [owner:Avi 2026-08-21 — \"same for new epochs … why not just automatically inject the orient?\"]. Partially built already: the server-side ## Orientation block (Route A) injects held work-items, unanswered directed messages, and wake-source state on presence transitions for hosts that inject it, and fleet kickoffs bake the plan binding into turn 1. Ratified: extend that coverage to ALL epoch boundaries (carry-respawn first prompt, cold loop wake, fleet kickoff, session start), resolved at prompt-assembly time. The split that decides injectability: DERIVABLE content (assignments, held checkpoints, staleness warnings, announced gates, inbox summary, leader brief) is injected; CALLER-PARAMETERIZED content (intent declaration, free-form memory query) stays with the coord:orient verb — noting that at specific epochs even intent is derivable (kickoff = the plan lane; carry-respawn = the carry doc's prior intent), so the injected fold should use it. coord:orient remains the RE-orient verb, not the boot ritual. P-023 implements.\nRelated: P-011, P-023\n\n### D-009 — A call handle the platform EMITS must be a call the target tool ACCEPTS — pinned by a test, not by care\nDate: 2026-08-21\nRULING (P-004, measured). Any surface that hands an agent a ready-made follow-up call — a `reread` handle, a `seeAlso` selector, an `awaitable`, an interest-profile row (P-010), an epoch-boundary orient fold (P-023) — MUST emit arguments that the named tool's real schema accepts, and that pairing must be pinned by a test that parses the EMITTED literal against the TARGET tool's schema. Neither half may move unilaterally.\n\nEVIDENCE. `dev:pipeline_position` and `release:checkpoint-run` have emitted `state:subscribe { cell: 'gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict' }` since 2026-08-02 (commits b11b506c, 6cc7e4d4), with the reason \"wait for the verdict to CHANGE instead of re-polling this tool\". `on` was a REQUIRED arg, so that suggested call was un-callable. From 2026-08-09 through 2026-08-19: 12 `state:subscribe` calls passing no `on`, from 11 DISTINCT agents, on exactly 1 cell — the one those handles name. All 12 rejected.\n\nWHY IT SURVIVED TEN DAYS, which is the transferable part: the refusal was `invalid_args`, which ATTRIBUTES THE FAULT TO THE CALLER. So one platform defect presented as eleven independent agent errors, each individually unremarkable, and nothing aggregated them. It surfaced only under a deliberate census of the tool's whole failure population. Corollary for every lane: a failure mode that blames the caller will not self-report, because each victim reasonably concludes they personally got it wrong.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR SCHEMAS. Requiredness is a claim about what every caller can supply. `on` was required because a predicate needs a comparator — but the dominant real intent (\"wake me when this moves\") had no comparator to give, so requiredness made the common case inexpressible and pushed callers to `ne` against the value's current reading, i.e. transcribing a volatile value into a watch and racing it. Before making an argument required, check what the platform's OWN emitted handles pass for it.\n\nGUARD. `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/state/emitted-subscribe-handles.test.ts` scans the agent-tools tree for emitted `state:subscribe` selectors and safeParses each against the live schema — with a positive control (the scan must find handles, so an empty scan cannot read as clean) and a negative control (a bad selector must be rejected, so the check cannot pass vacuously). Extend this pattern per handle-emitting surface rather than re-deriving it.\n\n### D-010 — The operator-scope sentinel is not a harness name: canReadCell admits '*' + role operator, and BOTH conditions are required\nDate: 2026-08-21\nP-005 asked whether the \"workspace-scoped su lists 4 of ~10 cells\" gap was a scoping bug, a doc bug, or serving-process divergence. VERDICT: a SCOPING BUG. The other two were tested and falsified, not merely set aside.\n\nMECHANISM. All six pipeline cells declare `visibility: { kind:'harness', ref:'papercusp' }` (OPERATOR_PIPELINE_VISIBILITY). `canReadCell`'s harness case was a bare `reader.harnessSlug === v.ref`. An operator-scope session does not present a slug — `http-projection` assigns `ctx.harnessSlug = '*'`. So the scope meaning \"every harness\" compared equal to NONE of them, and the sentinel that means maximum reach produced minimum reach.\n\nBLAST RADIUS (measured, tool_invocations, 24h): role `operator` + harnessSlug `'*'` = 358,755 calls across 418 DISTINCT agents. For every one of them all six cells read `absent`.\n\nTWO SYMPTOMS, ONE CAUSE. (a) `state:read` lists 4 of 10 and returns `absent` for the gate cells. (b) `stampStatePlane`'s `collect()` shares the same oracle, so it filtered every candidate out, returned null, and `dev:pipeline_position` emitted NO `plane` key at all — while CLAUDE.md tells agents that door \"HANDS YOU THE HANDLE\". (b) is the quieter failure: an unreadable cell at least answers a question you asked; a suppressed plane block removes the chance to ask.\n\nNO SECRECY WAS BEING ENFORCED. The same session denied the cell was served the identical values by `dev:pipeline_position` ungated, with a `subject` block naming which pipeline they describe. The gate was costing the re-read discipline the state plane exists to provide while protecting nothing.\n\nTHE RULE. `canReadCell` admits a harness-scoped cell when the reader matches the concrete ref OR presents the operator-scope sentinel AND holds role `operator`. BOTH conditions are required and neither alone is safe:\n  • Sentinel alone fails OPEN. `http-projection` sets `'*'` via a bare `if (!spawnCtx.harnessSlug)` fallback, so it means \"unset\", NOT \"operator\" — three call-site comments claim otherwise and the code does not. Treating it as authority is exactly the defaulted-audience failure D-016 names.\n  • Role alone re-opens EI-20709429494940822. `operator` sessions also run scoped to sidestage / scout-runtime / engineering, and those have a competing pipeline of their own to misread this one as. An operator-SCOPE reader has declared no competing harness, so there is nothing for it to confuse this with.\n\nFALSIFIED ALONG THE WAY (recorded so nobody re-runs them): serving-process divergence was disproved by blob comparison — `pipeline_position.ts` is byte-identical (d9a31224) in the deployed sha and staging, and contains `stampStatePlane` in both. The doc-bug reading was rejected because the values ARE served to that population by the sibling door.\n\nFOR OTHER LANES: `visibility` on a CELL is a real secrecy boundary (P-019 gates existence, so a refusal cannot be used to enumerate), unlike `agent_facts.audience_scope`, which is delivery relevance only. Do not widen a cell audience by analogy to facts. Any new harness-scoped cell inherits this rule automatically; do not hand-roll a second sentinel check — `cell-registry.ts`'s copy is deliberate (the module is dependency-free) and pinned against the canonical `isAllHarnessSentinel` by cell-registry-harness-sentinel.test.ts.\n\n### D-011 — facts:assert's 41% rejection rate is an ERGONOMIC failure, not a documentation drift — EI-21067740598816833's mechanism is falsified by its own test\nDate: 2026-08-21\nP-006 cites EI-21067740598816833, a Scout-generated idea proposing a nightly loop that clusters facts:assert rejections and AUTO-PATCHES the tool's schema description, on the premise that \"the description and the validator have drifted apart\". That idea states its own falsification condition: \"if diffing them against the schema shows the constraints ARE already documented (meaning agents ignore correct docs rather than lacking them), the loop mechanism is solving the wrong problem\".\n\nTHAT CONDITION IS MET. Do not build the loop.\n\nMEASURED (tool_invocations, workspace-scoped, 14d): 7,639 calls / 3,130 not_ok / 41.0% / 576 distinct agents. The rate is real — it is the mechanism that is wrong.\n\nTOP CLUSTERS (n / distinct agents) — 86% of all rejections:\n  858 / 135  body over the char cap (would be clipped)\n  676 / 149  volatile measurement must use ttlSec <= 900s\n  533 / 121  shareable fact requires a resolvable federation scope\n  385 / 192  measuredAt is only meaningful with subjectVolatile:true\n  248 / 117  settledBy is only meaningful for kind:'undecidable'\n\nEvery cluster carries 100+ DISTINCT agents (P-004's discriminator). 192 agents do not independently misread one field.\n\nTHE CONSTRAINTS ARE DOCUMENTED, in-line, where agents read them. Verbatim from assert.ts: subjectVolatile — \"Requires measuredAt; the fold renders an explicit SNAPSHOT marker and the TTL is limited to 15 minutes.\" measuredAt — \"Required with subjectVolatile:true and refused by the store otherwise.\" ttlSec (:308) — \"When subjectVolatile:true, ttlSec must be <=900 seconds (15 minutes); subjectVolatile:true also requires measuredAt.\" Plus the tool description (:185). Nothing has drifted. Auto-patching a correct description would have produced churn and zero improvement, and the rejection rate would have been read afterwards as proof the loop needed more cycles.\n\nTHE ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS. Three of the top clusters (ttlSec<=900, measuredAt-without-volatile, volatile-without-measuredAt = 1,146 calls) are ONE intent — \"this is a volatile snapshot\" — that the schema forces the caller to express across THREE co-varying fields, where any two-of-three is a hard refusal. The agent's intent is fully recoverable in two of those three cases; the tool refuses anyway and stores NOTHING.\n\nTHE RULE ADOPTED: normalize an intent that is UNAMBIGUOUS and deterministically repairable; keep refusing one that is ambiguous or whose repair would manufacture a falsehood.\n  • measuredAt present + subjectVolatile omitted -> INFER subjectVolatile:true, disclosed in the result. You do not stamp a sample time for a non-sample. Strictly safer than the alternative the error itself offers (\"omit the timestamp\"), because inferring keeps the SNAPSHOT marker and the short TTL rather than discarding the sample's provenance.\n  • subjectVolatile:true + ttlSec > 900 -> CLAMP to 900, disclosed. A shorter TTL is never a correctness hazard.\n  • subjectVolatile:true + measuredAt MISSING -> KEEP REFUSING. Defaulting to now() would stamp an unknown-age sample as fresh, which is precisely the lie measuredAt exists to prevent. A refusal is correct here even though it costs 44 agents.\n  • settledBy with the wrong kind, and measuredAt in the future -> KEEP REFUSING. Both are genuine semantic errors, not recoverable intent.\n\nGENERAL PRINCIPLE FOR OTHER LANES: a validator that can name the exact repair in its error message can usually perform it. Rejecting while telling the caller precisely what to change is a design smell whenever the repair is deterministic — the cost is not one round trip but a permanent tax on every agent that ever calls the tool, and it is invisible in aggregate because each victim reads it as their own mistake.\n\n### D-012 — A tenure verdict needs registration age AND an observable window — \"0 reads\" alone never justifies a cut, and P-008's own named subjects prove it\nDate: 2026-08-21\nP-008 says a cell with \"0 reads over a trailing window\" produces a cut-or-keep line, and names testing.census.population and testing.coverage.floor as first subjects. Implemented literally, that rule emits a FALSE CUT on both of them on its first run. Three measurements, all taken 2026-08-21:\n\n(1) REGISTRATION AGE. Both cells were introduced by commit 92db953012 on 2026-08-18T15:05:12Z — 3.0 days ago (`git show` confirms only `+ cell:` lines, no removals). Any trailing window of 14 or 30 days scores 11–27 days that PREDATE THEIR EXISTENCE as \"0 reads\". Youth is indistinguishable from dormancy unless the rule is told the difference.\n\n(2) THE WINDOW IS NOT OBSERVABLE FOR 30 DAYS. harness_shared.tool_invocations is pruned to 14 days — DEFAULT_RETENTION_TARGETS in telemetry-retention-action.ts:173 (`{ category: 'tool-invocations', retention_days: 14 }`), corroborated by the measured oldest row across all 479 tools: 2026-08-07T08:08Z (~14.3d). The admission rule's own doc (state-read-inventory-which-reads-become-cells.md:75) states \"a read with 0 calls IN 30 DAYS is never promoted\" and adds \"the table's retention is about 30 days, so calls_all == calls_30d for every row\". That parenthetical was measured 2026-07-27 and is NOW STALE: retention is 14d. A tenure counterpart that inherits the literal \"30 days\" would query 16 days of guaranteed-empty history and read the emptiness as evidence.\n\n(3) DIRECT READS ARE NOT THE ONLY DELIVERY PATH, so a low count can mean success. host.load is not a registered cell at all but has 2 state:read calls, and cell-suggest.ts:40 answers them with \"already in your coord:orient payload — call nothing.\" Symmetrically, dev:pipeline_position hands callers a `plane` block of ready re-read handles, and P-001's deriveCellReread folds a handle into subscription fires. Every one of those delivers a cell's VALUE without producing a state:read row. A cell whose value is being delivered by a better path is the design working, not a cell to cut.\n\nTHEREFORE, binding on P-008 and on any later adoption/tenure verdict:\n\n a. A cell is ELIGIBLE for a cut verdict only when its registration age >= the trailing window AND the window lies wholly inside observable telemetry. The window is clamped to observable retention (14d today), and the clamp is DISCLOSED in the emitted line rather than silently applied. A verdict that cannot say how much history it actually saw is not falsifiable.\n\n c. The verdict is a LINE — cut-CANDIDATE — never an automatic cut, matching P-007's suggestion-only, precision-first discipline (EI-10949). Reason (3) means a confident automatic cut is unsound in principle, not merely risky.\n\n d. Registration age needs a real source. Git archaeology over cell-registrations.ts works for a human but is the wrong dependency for a sweep; the population must instead come from the LIVE registry with a declared registration date on the spec. Grepping the file is independently disqualified: `cell: AGENT_GOAL_CELL_ID` (cell-registrations.ts:659) is registered through a constant, so a string-literal grep finds 9 of the 10 registered cells and silently undercounts the registry by 10%. Enumerate via the registry (the admin/inventory enumeration already allowlisted in cell-access-parity's CALL_SITE_ALLOWLIST), never via text.\n\n e. Read counts come from the SAME source the admission rule uses (state:read rows in tool_invocations). A second derivation of \"how adopted is this cell\" would drift from the admission rule it is the counterpart to — the axis-5 / D-038 violation the sweep header already refuses for the divergence numbers.\n\nMEASURED FIRST VERDICT, for the record (10 registered cells, state:read rows, full observable history): gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict 892 · gate.greenCheckpoint.candidate 608 · gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership 544 · deploy.3070.sha 145 · git.mainBehindStaging 76 · git.pipelinePosition 62 · host.memoryPressure 51 · agent.goal 14 · testing.census.population 0 · testing.coverage.floor 0. Under this decision the last two are `too-young` (3.0d < window), NOT cut-candidates — and they become genuinely assessable on 2026-09-01.\n\n### D-013 — P-009: no cell is shareable and nothing consumes CellSpec.federation — fail the variant closed behind a named transport gate rather than building a cross-hive cell transport for zero declared demand\nDate: 2026-08-21\nMEASURED BEFORE IMPLEMENTING (the P-008 lesson applied again — P-008 as written would have false-cut its own two named subjects; measuring first caught it).\n\nP-009 reads: \"verify a real transport exists behind federation:'shareable' (source_hive / fed_ts path); wire it or flip declared-but-untransported cells to local — a declaration with no mechanism is contract theater.\"\n\nBoth of the item's named remedies are inapplicable as written. The measurements:\n\n(1) ZERO cells declare shareable. All 10 registered cells declare `federation: { kind: 'local' }`.\n    Instrument: the LIVE registry (listCellsUnchecked() via the real cell-registrations-wiring\n    seam), NOT a grep — a string-literal grep of cell-registrations.ts undercounts, because\n    agent.goal registers its name through the AGENT_GOAL_CELL_ID constant. Probe:\n    /tmp/p009-federation-probe.ts. => \"flip declared-but-untransported cells to local\" is a\n    NO-OP: there are none to flip.\n\n(2) NOTHING CONSUMES CellSpec.federation. That rule is well-reasoned and becomes live again the\n    day a transport lands; deleting it would lose the design intent.\n  - Add one named, greppable constant (e.g. CELL_FEDERATION_TRANSPORT_AVAILABLE = false)\n    documenting that no transport consumes CellSpec.federation, and reject `shareable` while it\n    is false — with a message naming exactly what must exist first and pointing at this\n    decision. Flipping one constant re-arms the whole path.\n  - Recurrence guard: a test asserting (a) shareable is refused today, (b) the refusal message\n    names the requirement, and (c) every registered cell is local. (c) is what fails if someone\n    lands a shareable cell without wiring transport.\n\nThis converts an unstated assumption into a first-class, testable, dated fact: the absence of a\ntransport becomes something the code asserts rather than something a future author discovers by\nwatching a declaration do nothing.\n\n### D-014 — Interest profiles: watch is a discriminated union, `of` is a param list, cell refs are imported consts — and the rows are declared intent, NOT measured demand\nDate: 2026-08-21\nP-010 shipped as packages/operator-core/lib/interest-profiles.ts. Four rulings, each a deviation from the item's literal wording that later phases (P-023/P-024/P-025 consume this registry) must follow rather than re-litigate.\n\n1. `watch` IS A DISCRIMINATED UNION, NOT A BARE STRING.\nThe item said `watch: cell id | event key`. Implemented as `{kind:'cell', cell} | {kind:'event', family}` because the two validate against DIFFERENT registries (BUILTIN_CELLS vs EVENT_CATALOG). Given only the string \"release.gate\", a checker cannot tell a misspelled cell from a misspelled event family and must guess — which is exactly how a typo passes as \"probably the other kind\". The union is what makes the drift guard the item asks for actually decidable.\n\n2. `of` IS A STRING ARRAY OF CONTEXT FIELD NAMES, NOT A SCALAR.\nEvent families are parameterized and some need more than one param: `plan-item` is `plan-item:done:<slug>:<id>` with BOTH required. A scalar `of` cannot express that, and an unresolved key param is not a cosmetic gap — `buildKey` produces a key nothing ever emits, so the waiter sleeps forever and silently (the hazard predicate-watch.ts documents). The validator therefore requires one `of` entry per REQUIRED param. For a cell, `of` names the caller-relative subject (`as`), which several cells refuse to answer without.\n\n3. CELL REFERENCES ARE IMPORTED CONSTANTS, NEVER RETYPED LITERALS.\nRows use `GATE_VERDICT_CELL.cell`, not 'gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict'. This follows the rule AGENT_GOAL_CELL states in its own comment: a hand-typed id that drifts from the registry fails SILENTLY, because getCell returns undefined and the surface discloses nothing, forever. Importing the const moves that entire failure class to compile time and leaves the runtime test the one job the compiler cannot do — proving the spec is REGISTERED (in BUILTIN_CELLS), not merely defined.
