VALIDATION TAKES `rows`, SO FALSIFIABILITY NEEDS NO TREE MUTATION.\n`validateInterestProfiles(rows)` is exported taking its subject as an argument rather than reading INTEREST_PROFILES directly. The test runs the identical logic against deliberately-wrong LOCAL control rows, proving each rule can fail without mutating the real registry or any tracked file — which on this swept shared tree is the only safe way to prove a guard is falsifiable. Every rule PUSHES and rules are independent, never else-if chained (the P-009/D-013 lesson): a row violating several reports all of them, and a test asserts that.\n\n⚠ 5. HONESTY RAIL — THE ROWS ARE DECLARED INTENT, NOT MEASURED DEMAND.\nEvery `why` traces to an instruction the system ALREADY gives agents (the su persona's leader-monitor mandate, its member operating loop, CLAUDE.md's \"is my change live\" guidance). NO row is justified by observed reads, and this registry must not be cited downstream as evidence of demand. The measurement points the other way and is recorded in the module header so nobody re-derives it and concludes the opposite: across all retained telemetry only 13 distinct cell names are read via state:read; of the 5 unregistered names, 2 are deliberate probes and 1 is a truncated-name typo, leaving `host.load` (2 callers) and `release.gate` (1) over 14 days as the only genuine reaches for something unregistered. That is noise-level. Existing read volume is evidence about ADOPTION, not about whether any row here is wanted.\n\nVerification: 17/17 tests pass, 0 skipped (runId 1bd02fd7), including a calibration block asserting the registry is non-empty and references both watch kinds — without which every referential assertion passes vacuously against an empty array, the exact trap P-009 hit. build:typecheck scoped to the two new files reports errorsInRequestedFiles: 0 (the project's 88 other errors are a pre-existing operator-core baseline in unrelated files, none touched here).\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-015 — P-023: the orient fold dedups on CONTEXT GENERATION, not on owner — and every owner-preserving boundary must advance it\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21. Implements D-008. Ratified against code, not inference.\n\nWHAT D-008 ASSUMED vs WHAT IS TRUE. D-008 reads as \"the Route A injection is ABSENT at\nmost epoch boundaries; extend it to all four.\" Measured, the injection is PRESENT at\nthose boundaries and SUPPRESSED. Those need opposite fixes, so the framing matters.\n\nTHE DEFECT. `turn-start-orientation.ts` diffs against `harness_shared.coord_read_cursors`,\nwhose PK is (workspace_id, owner_id, surface) — verified by describe, no epoch column.\nBut what the fold dedups against is the agent's CONTEXT: the block is suppressed because\n\"you were already told\", which is only true while the context it was told into exists.\nWherever those diverge — owner id survives, context does not — the fold went silent for a\nsuccessor that had seen nothing. Worse, the suppression is ANTI-CORRELATED with need: a\ncarry-respawn or cold wake usually changes no orientation state at all (the process merely\nrestarted), which is exactly what the fingerprint reads as \"nothing to say\". The cleaner\nthe boundary preserved state, the more certain the successor was told nothing.\n\nTHE RULE (this is the reusable part). Every boundary is one of two kinds:\n  (a) NEW owner id — fresh session start, fleet kickoff. No cursor row ⇒ committed null ⇒\n      orientationUnchanged returns false ⇒ emits. Already correct by construction, and\n      pinned by the pre-existing test \"speaks in full on the FIRST turn\".\n  (b) OWNER PRESERVED, context discarded. The cursor carries across ⇒ MUST advance the\n      context generation, or it suppresses forever.\n(b) had exactly two instances. Compaction/carry-respawn already bumped\n`memory_session_epochs` (request-compaction.ts, compact-reprime.ts). The COLD WAKE never\ndid — verified: those were the only two bumpSessionEpoch call sites in the tree.\nANYONE ADDING A NEW OWNER-PRESERVING BOUNDARY MUST BUMP THE GENERATION.\n\nWHAT SHIPPED. (1) `fingerprintOrientation(state, epoch)` carries the generation, and\n`orientationUnchanged` compares it. (2) The cold-wake branch in wake-executor.ts advances\nthe generation — covering `mode:'reset'` AND `mode:'recycle'`, since ColdWakeDecision is\n`{ cold:true; mode:'reset'|'recycle' }` and both discard context.\n\nCROSS-LANE (memory-delivery-unification-2026-07-12 owns this counter; D-005 additive rule).\nOrientation now keys on the SAME generation the memory surfaced-ledger already dedups on,\nwith the SAME key (`session_id` = the owner id — that is what the turn-start memory port\nalready passes). This is deliberate: two context folds on one rail must not disagree about\nwhat a boundary is. It also fixes a SECOND bug in memory's own lane at no extra cost — a\ncold wake never reset its surfaced-ledger either, so a cold successor's whole memory pool\nstayed deduped against a context it never had.\n\nFAIL-OPEN POSTURE, STATED SO IT IS NOT \"FIXED\" LATER. epoch 0 = \"generation unknown\"\n(missing relation / failed read; `currentSessionEpoch` already answers 0 and caches it).\nThat reproduces the pre-P-023 dedup EXACTLY rather than emitting every turn — degradation\nis to the old behaviour, never to noise. A committed cursor written before the epoch key\nexisted lacks the field, compares unequal, and re-emits ONCE: intended migration.\nThe cold-wake bump is best-effort and runs FIRST in the branch (mirroring compact-reprime's\n\"the epoch bump deliberately happens FIRST\"); if a later guard drops that delivery the bump\nstill happened, which costs one redundant block — the safe direction.\n\nROUTE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: injecting the fold INTO session-recovery-brief. That endpoint\nis the compaction boundary and would have been the literal reading of \"at prompt-assembly\ntime\", but the carry brief it renders ALREADY carries held items + checkpoints, directives,\nwalls, facts, awaits and the fleet pointer. The fold's only marginal signal there is\nunanswered-directed, and once the generation invalidates the cursor that arrives on the\nsame turn via the rail that already fires. Duplicating a rich brief to deliver one line is\nthe wrong trade; the generation fix covers all four boundaries with no new rail.\nRelated: P-023, P-011\n\n### D-016 — P-011 is NOT blocked on fleet-spec-scoped-metrics P-007 — land additively and rebase; do not wait for a dormant lane\nDate: 2026-08-21\nDate: 2026-08-21 (su-0eea6)\n\nMEASURED, not assumed: fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21 is status 'ready' but DORMANT — its P-005 and P-007 are both `todo`, and `work_items:list { sourcePlanSlug: 'fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-2026-08-21', notTerminal: true }` returns ZERO rows, so the plan was never started and no agent holds any of it. (Checked 2026-08-21T20:2xZ.)\n\nTHE QUESTION THIS SETTLES. D-005 says this plan's items on the shared `coord:orient` fold assembly \"land AFTER or rebase ATOP that plan's shape — their contract is never altered, only appended to.\" Read as a hard dependency, P-011 blocks forever on a lane nobody is working. That reading is wrong: D-005 is a DISJUNCTION, and the operative constraint is the second clause — never ALTER their contract — not an ordering requirement.\n\nRULING.\n1. P-011 MAY land before fleet-spec P-007. It is not blocked-by.\n2. It must land as a SELF-CONTAINED, CLEARLY-NAMESPACED additive block that carries cell handles/gates ONLY — no counts, no populations, no metric fields (D-005's real constraint, unchanged).\n3. It must NOT introduce a general \"fold assembly\" abstraction that a later P-007 would have to conform to. Whoever lands fleet-spec P-007 later APPENDS; they are explicitly NOT required to accommodate P-011's block, and may rebase it.\n\nWHY RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT AS JUDGMENT: the natural reading of D-005 (\"land AFTER\") makes P-011 look blocked, and a later agent re-deriving that would defer it again — indefinitely, because the blocking lane has no owner to unblock it. It does not touch fleet-spec's D-003/D-004/D-005, and it grants this plan no claim on metric content.\n\nRelated: P-011, P-015, P-027, D-005\n\n### D-017 — A delivery-time cell read includes its falsifier — push may not strip the independent measurement\nDate: 2026-08-21\nD-007's compact delivery-time read is a projection of state:read, and therefore includes the cell's declared falsifier alongside headline, material lens, unknown hoist, and source qualifier. Omitting it gives an injected value system authority while removing the one independent measurement declared to kill a false reading. The wake fold renders falsifier field/value/kills on the measured path, and loudly marks drift or door truncation as UNFALSIFIED rather than manufacturing measured-null agreement. Implemented and regression-covered by WI-40312.\nRelated: P-022\n\n### D-018 — P-024 narrowly widens auto-arm to singular lifecycle edges; plan decisions remain fold/notify\nDate: 2026-08-21\nP-024 is the explicit D-002 widening beyond fleet leaders, but only for a caller’s singular, already-emitted lifecycle edge: (1) a blocked-item holder may be armed on the named blocker’s work-item:done:<blocker> and its own work-item:unblocked:<dependent> edge; (2) a claim holder may be armed on claim:released:<item>, including an atomic reassignment away from that holder; (3) a question/escalation/consult requester may be armed on the concrete answer key returned for that request. Every registration reuses event_awaits, is idempotent, carries an exact bound_to justification, exposes an events:cancel handle, and is retired when the state/request that justified it ends. This does not authorize generalized ambient interrupts, wildcard event families, or copied state values.\n\nThe leader profile may add fleet-admission-blocked:<fleet> because the catalog and emitter share that concrete subject. The rate-limit-paused/reset families require an emitter-defined <scope>; current emitters are gym-scoped and fleet leader control has only fleet.slug, so P-024 must not manufacture rate-limit:*:<fleet> keys. Those rows remain inapplicable until a real leader-relevant subject/emitter mapping exists.\n\nA plan decision is not an events:await family. Plan-lane workers receive decision_added through the existing coord plan-event fold/notification rail, filtered to their current plan and still non-waking. Do not widen CellSpec or invent an event key for it.\nRelated: P-024\n\n### D-019 — P-025 reuses plans:attention as the owner's interest fold; owner-surface watches are typed and never auto-arm\nDate: 2026-08-22\nP-025 adds an owner-present interest context and extends D-014's discriminated watch union with a typed owner-attention surface variant. This is an extension of the union pattern, not a bare string or a third delivery system. The canonical consumer is the existing plans:attention feed: it already supplies the global owner Inbox and the selected session's pending-question rail, and already unions needs-human work items, registered carry-note walls, open owner questions/escalations, and pending session gates. Profile rows classify queue/wall sources as fold and pending asks/escalations as suggest; an owner-surface row is forbidden from auto-arm, because opening/using the owner's interactive surface is the presence signal and machinery never wakes the owner. Runtime source selection must read these rows, while existing adapters, dedupe, SSE invalidation, and UI renderers remain the authority. No new store, cell, event family, polling loop, or copied queue is introduced.\nRelated: P-025\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"unshipped-plans-live-reconciliation-audit-2026-08-20","title":"Live reconciliation audit of unshipped plans","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-21","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Live reconciliation audit of unshipped plans\nslug: unshipped-plans-live-reconciliation-audit-2026-08-20\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-21\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n# Live reconciliation audit of unshipped plans\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-006 WIP route A. Seven evidence-safe lifecycle outcomes applied: four stale empty shells and one explicitly unapproved/replaced proposal superseded; validation-contract plan has all 17 items terminal, completion audit seq 2 current at f3203e9 with 34 resolving citations, and fresh 94/94 tests green. No live-owned target was changed. D-003 governs: classifier bands are triage only.\n\n**Next:** Finish the existing meta-rubric vetting consult conv-mt7jzqiq-0000-2e4b5eda4c474fbdb641a9abc4fb4460 (do not duplicate); then ship first-class-spec-clauses-and-prior-attempt-briefs-2026-08-20 expectedCurrent=ready. Continue evidence-safe closeouts, P-007 blocker revalidation, and P-008 regeneration.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase — Audit\n\n- **P-001** `done` Capture a fresh workspace-wide plan census and a complete live-ownership exclusion set without mutating or interrupting ongoing work. importance: high — note: ← WI-40157 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Recover and independently reproduce the prior audit method, then build a per-plan disposition manifest from current plan items, promoted work, audit/acceptance evidence, and blocker text. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-40163 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Revalidate proposed terminal, superseded, catalog-residue, and blocker classifications against live state; flag stale blockers and protect every actively owned plan. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-40165 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Publish a browser-viewable rerun report and machine-readable evidence tables comparing the prior audit with the fresh census; make no lifecycle transitions. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-40169 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — Routine and reconciliation\n\n- **P-005** `done` Implement the classifierRevision=2 unshipped-plan audit as a persistent manually invoked, read-only on-demand routine using the existing routine/system-action framework; it must publish evidence but never schedule itself or mutate plan lifecycle, blockers, claims, or ownership. importance: high — note: ← WI-40180 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Revalidate and apply only evidence-safe lifecycle transitions from the frozen disposition manifest, starting with explicit plan-level supersession and independently verifiable terminal closeout; re-read live ownership immediately before every mutation batch and skip all live-owned plans. importance: high — note: ← WI-41344 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Review the typed stale-hint and prose-only blocker bands against current canonical blocker sources; clear only blockers proven stale, preserve legitimate blockers with owner/source/next-action evidence, and never disturb live-owned work. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-41377 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Regenerate the audit manifest/report after cleanup, verify classifier invariants and live delivery, and leave every surviving nonterminal plan either protected ongoing work or backed by a current legitimate blocker and recheck condition. blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007 importance: high — note: ← WI-41381 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Audit routine is manual and read-only\nDate: 2026-08-21\nThe persistent audit surface is an on-demand routine, not a scheduled plan recurrence. It may census, classify, compare, and publish evidence, but it must never mutate plan lifecycle/status, blocker rows, claims, assignments, or ownership. Cleanup remains a separate evidence-gated workflow.\nRelated: P-005, P-008\n\n### D-002 — Live-owner exclusion is load-bearing\nDate: 2026-08-21\nImmediately before every lifecycle or blocker mutation batch, query current coordination/fleet ownership and exclude any plan tied to a live plan claim or a nonterminal work item held by a live agent. A frozen audit classification never overrides live ownership.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-003 — Classifier bands are triage inputs, not lifecycle authority\nDate: 2026-08-24\nThe classifierRevision=2 bands are useful for candidate selection but are never sufficient mutation evidence. The fixture heuristic matched live product plans that merely mention canaries/tests, and the empty-plan band contains ratified rubric instruments plus scheduled templates. P-006/P-007/P-008 may mutate only after a current plan-level read, linked nonterminal-work read, and immediate live-owner read prove the exact transition safe; ambiguous rows remain nonterminal and are recorded as exclusions.\n\n### D-004 — Classifier revision 3 requires blocker-shaped Now syntax; incidental vocabulary is not a blocker\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24. P-007 revalidated the current prose-only blocker band against the canonical item/work/gate writers and found a systematic false-positive class in revision 2: textSignals concatenated slug, title, Now state, and Now next, then treated any occurrence of words such as credential, human review, release gate, or owner review as a blocker. Current counterexamples include authoritative-account-routing (explicitly says P-005 is now unblocked but names credential/provider probes), design-simplification (names an agent-executable next item while merely recommending owner input), and abolish-human-review (product vocabulary in the title). Ruling: revision 3 derives prose blocker signals only from Now state/next and requires blocker-shaped syntax—blocked/waiting/gated, an explicit owner action/decision, or a credential/API-key need/missing/provide assertion. Slugs/titles and incidental measurement/product vocabulary are non-authoritative. Typed item/issue blockers remain the canonical higher-priority evidence. P-008 must regenerate the artifact with negative controls for the observed false positives and positive controls for real owner/external gates.\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"email","plan_slug":"gmail-respond-with-draft-2026-08-22","title":"Gmail message — respond with a draft","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-22","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Gmail message — respond with a draft\nslug: gmail-respond-with-draft-2026-08-22\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-22\nupdated: 2026-09-04\n---\n\n# Gmail message — respond with a draft\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Ready built-in template. Each inbound Gmail message creates one isolated event run.\n\n**Next:** Read the triggering message, draft a useful response, and save it to the originating Gmail thread.\n\n## Background\n\n`plan_run.inputs.trigger` carries only the routing envelope — the message itself is\ndeliberately NOT embedded there. Read it with `triggers:read-payload`, passing this\nrun's numeric id. The draft tool accepts only that same id; it resolves the recipient,\nthread, reply headers, and OAuth credential server-side. It creates a Gmail DRAFT and\nnever sends.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Draft a reply in the originating thread.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Each inbound Gmail message yields one draft reply saved to the thread it arrived on.\",\"constraints\":[\"Create a draft only; never send.\",\"Resolve recipient, thread and credential server-side from the trigger plan run.\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"P-001\",\"D-001\",\"D-002\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A run of this template leaves exactly one Gmail draft on the originating thread, created through gmail:create-draft with the run's planRunId.\",\"falsifier\":\"A run completes with no draft, creates a second draft for the same run, or sends the message instead of drafting it.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Fire a gmail message.received event through the binding engine, then read the run and the draft tool's recorded result.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"},\"replication\":\"Run packages/operator-core/lib/external-triggers/gmail-flagship.integration.test.ts.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Draft\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Call `triggers:read-payload` with `planRunId=payload.plan_run.runId` to read the inbound message, compose a concise response, then call `gmail:create-draft` with that same `planRunId` and the response text. Complete only after the tool reports `created:true` or `alreadyCreated:true`.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Draft creation is anchored to a trigger plan run; auto-send stays outside this tool\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe tool resolves every Gmail coordinate and credential from the durable trigger run. Its public input is only planRunId plus text. It has no send branch; automatic sending is a separate owner-authority dark-flag surface.\n\n### D-002 — The message is referenced, not embedded\nDate: 2026-09-04\nA plan run's inputs land in a federated work-item payload, so embedding the inbound email there would replicate the owner's private inbox to admitted hive members. The engine now passes the routing envelope only, and the agent pulls the message server-side by planRunId. Read and write both resolve from the owner-local trigger run.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-blender-goal-amendment-and-creation-rail","title":"Acceptance — Blender goal amendment and creation rail","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-22","owner":"su-13039d37-73c3-4644-87a9-c81c06458cb4","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — Blender goal amendment and creation rail\nslug: acceptance-blender-goal-amendment-and-creation-rail\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-22\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-13039d37-73c3-4644-87a9-c81c06458cb4\n---\n\n# Acceptance — Blender goal amendment and creation rail\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22","title":"External triggers v1 — Slack + Gmail event sources, trigger→plan bindings, offline-safe cursor reconcile, cupboard-ready packs","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-22","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: External triggers v1 — Slack + Gmail event sources, trigger→plan bindings, offline-safe cursor reconcile, cupboard-ready packs\nslug: external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-22\nupdated: 2026-08-28\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** All implementation items are terminal: P-001–P-012 and P-016–P-031 done, P-032 dropped. P-013 is the only open item, still needs-human.\n\nTHE GMAIL HALF IS NOW FULLY PROVEN (su-fef75d27, 2026-08-25T21:47Z, WI-40939) — the prior Now's instruction to \"bind it and verify\" is COMPLETE, do not redo it:\n- Binding 6364f44f armed on ext:gmail:message.received -> gmail-respond-with-draft-2026-08-22.\n- Drafting proven: plan run 973 produced real anchored Gmail draft r-7293350000959795948 (labels=[DRAFT], correct threadId + In-Reply-To); never sent; a second call returned alreadyCreated:true with the SAME id, so reprocess is idempotent.\n- EXTERNAL SMTP TRANSIT PROVEN, unaided: a genuinely external sender (Intro <hi@intro.co> -> avi@papercusp.com, thread 1a03aba9ea57716f) drove Pub/Sub -> poll -> ingest -> armed binding -> trigger run ef3f5836 succeeded -> plan run 974, with no owner action.\n- DESKTOP ACCEPTANCE PASSED 9/9 (6 positives + 3 negative controls, rc=0): /admin/triggers renders the armed binding, its plan, \"1 binding · 1 armed\", and the runs view's passed/total fractions. Probe preserved as a WI-40939 comment.\n\nONE GAP FOUND, deliberately not self-fixed: nothing EXECUTES the work items minted by trigger runs. Their admission column is null, so scheduler:get_next cannot see them; the oldest has sat in todo 7.1 days. Filed EI-21460610464031791. Wiring it means an agent auto-acts on arbitrary inbound email — an autonomy escalation — so it is an owner call: ask conv-mt974ba5.\n\n**Next:** NOTHING IS AGENT-ACTIONABLE ON P-013 — both remaining blockers are owner walls, so do not re-verify the Gmail legs above (they are closed with evidence): (1) the Slack half has no agent path at all and needs owner-supplied xapp- (connections:write) + xoxb- tokens plus allowed channel IDs per reference/slack-external-trigger-setup.mdx, and P-013 cannot CLOSE until a live Slack mention is demonstrated; (2) the executor decision awaits the owner on conv-mt974ba5 — if they answer \"manual/review\", the follow-up is small and additive (an ageing signal like \"N runs idle > 24h\" on the EXISTING runs view, which already renders 0/1 fractions — do NOT build a new visibility surface).\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-40724 — Flagship Slack binding: @papercusp mention → respond-in-thread plan template, verified E2E through the desktop app <!-- P-008 -->\n## Background\n\nPapercusp has a complete INTERNAL reactive spine (events:emit/await, watch:create, gate latching) but no EXTERNAL event source — nothing outside the box can start work. This plan adds TRIGGERS: outside events normalized into `ext:*` event keys, plus ONE new primitive — trigger BINDINGS (event + filter → launch a plan from a template / wake an agent) with an autonomy-gated ARM step and per-binding storm policy.\n\nConstraint 1 — no public ingress: Papercusp is a Tauri desktop product behind NAT. Both v1 adapters use OUTBOUND transports only: Slack Socket Mode (outbound WebSocket), Gmail Pub/Sub PULL.\n\nConstraint 2 — offline doctrine (owner requirement + research 2026-08-21): user desktops are often OFFLINE and users must not run always-on infrastructure. v1 needs NO hosted buffer because both sources are REPLAYABLE — the provider retains events; every adapter must be CURSOR-RECONCILING on connect:\n- Gmail: history.list walk from stored historyId (full-resync fallback when the cursor expires); the Pub/Sub doorbell is a latency optimization, never the source of truth. Gmail watch renewed ≤7 days by a durable routine.\n- Slack: Socket Mode while connected — envelope-ack correctness + event_id dedupe (Slack retries unacked envelopes 3x; the Feb-2026 Delayed Events toggle extends retries hourly for 24h); on cold-start/reconnect, reconcile via conversations.history, rate-limit aware (non-Marketplace apps drop to 1 req/min on that method from 2026-03) — cache locally, backfill only cold gaps.\nA hosted buffer (Svix Ingest polling endpoints / Hookdeck) becomes necessary only for NON-replayable sources — the generic-webhook trigger, explicitly OUT of v1 scope; direction to be recorded as a Decision when the owner picks.\n\nReuse-first: EXTENDS the existing event system — never a parallel trigger system. Credentials ride the OAuth-integration design (snapshots/oauth-integration: connect-button flow, ctx.oauth.token()). Shareability rides per-field share semantics (snapshots/share-semantics) + the generic cupboard install/resolve cores (cupboard-plan-rubric-recipe-sharing-2026-08-21 D-003: extracted, not forked).\n\nGovernance non-negotiables from day one: (1) installed ≠ armed — arming is a separate autonomy-gated step (plans:arm-schedule doctrine); an unarmed binding never fires. (2) Per-binding storm policy (coalesce / queue / drop + max-concurrent). (3) Email replies are Gmail DRAFTS by default; auto-send is an owner-armed escalation (outward-facing send — registered dark-flag category).\n\n## Requirements\n\n- External Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar, and approved social-provider activity is normalized into canonical `ext:<source>:<event>` envelopes with stable external ids, durable deduplication, redacted payloads, and cursor-based replay after disconnects; replayable v1 sources require no public ingress or always-on hosted buffer.\n- A plan is derived as triggered when it has a schedule, external-event binding, or declared manual-start inputs. All three sources launch through the existing plan/run and recurrence substrates rather than a parallel scheduler.\n- A binding is installed separately from being armed, targets exactly one plan or recipe, carries its filter, mapping, storm policy, and local-principal authority, and cannot fire before the explicit autonomy-gated arm step. Trigger execution is durable, idempotent, observable, and reconstructable from receipt through outcome.\n- Workflow packs are share-safe pure manifest data: declared inputs and OAuth scopes, snapshot-stripped credentials, N `plan | recipe` targets, N single-target bindings, and correlation-inheriting internal-event edges. Recipe mappings are deterministic and complete; plan targets alone may receive redacted payload context; Cupboard installs always land disarmed.\n- Credentials resolve from the installer's own Personal Vault / OAuth connection and never from provider payload identity, shared snapshots, plan prose, or agent-supplied secret values. The Gmail and Calendar lanes reuse one Google Workspace connection and perform explicit scope upgrades.\n- Provider-neutral `mail:*`, `calendar:*`, `chat:*`, and approved `social:*` capability verbs operate on canonical object ids. Reply-shaped writes accept content only and resolve addressee/thread server-side; create-shaped destinations must come from a trusted owner/contact channel and are echoed before the write.\n- Slack reconnects safely under burst and cold gaps; Gmail treats Pub/Sub as a doorbell and `history.list` as truth; Calendar uses `syncToken` polling and local upcoming-event timing. Gmail response workflows create drafts by default, while outward sends remain an explicit higher-authority action.\n- The desktop Workflows/Triggers surfaces expose derived one-time/triggered filters, attach/detach and arm/disarm controls, manual args, storm policy, source health, correlated run timelines, redacted payload inspection, plan progress, and outcome links without introducing a second activity ledger.\n- The shipped starter workflows and focused/live acceptance evidence demonstrate Slack thread response, inbound-email draft response, and meeting-prep delivery through the same manifest, binding, plan-run, and provider-adapter contracts.\n\n## Design\n\nThe implementation extends the existing event, plan-run, recurrence, OAuth, Personal Vault, and Cupboard cores. An outbound provider adapter reconciles its provider cursor, normalizes a canonical event, and writes the delivery ledger before `events:emit`. The binding engine matches armed rows, applies filters and storm policy, and launches the existing durable plan/recipe path. Event keys and the one-time/triggered classification are derived from live substrate state so stored copies cannot drift.\n\nBindings form the workflow graph rather than owning a pipeline: each binding invokes one stored target (`plan | recipe`), and internal `binding-run-completed` / `plan-completed` edges stitch bindings together while inheriting one correlation id. A UI \"call a tool\" target is stored as a one-step recipe. Plan targets may use the redacted payload as agent context; recipe targets use declared args plus complete type/field mapping, pinned authority, retry policy, and an Activity-visible dead-letter disposition. Declared plan outputs feed downstream mappings. This keeps chaining inspectable while avoiding a second steps orchestrator.\n\nSource credentials stay behind typed connection ids and field-level share metadata. OAuth fields are `secret`, non-shareable, and stripped from snapshots; top-level and inline provider/scopes must agree. The explicit local principal—not any identity named in inbound content—authorizes deterministic work. Installing a workflow copies and validates its graph and templates but returns `armed:false`; connecting, instantiating, reviewing, and arming remain separate transitions.\n\nSlack uses Socket Mode plus `conversations.history`, Gmail uses Pub/Sub pull plus `history.list`, and Calendar uses `events.list` plus `syncToken`; each treats provider replay as truth and local transport as a latency aid. The queue-free v1 is the deliberate offline tradeoff for replayable providers. A Papercusp-managed polling buffer is reserved for a future non-replayable webhook source rather than imposed on every desktop user now.\n\nAgent-facing writes converge on one provider-neutral capability seam over canonical datatypes. Provider adapters own threading, MIME/event encoding, cursor semantics, and idempotency; agents supply intent-level fields only. Reply destinations are non-composable and server-resolved, while create destinations are provenance-checked. Provider MCP/OpenAPI surfaces remain adapter inputs or lazy generic escape hatches, not prompt-heavy agent contracts.\n\nThe Workflows UI reads the same bindings, plan runs, delivery ledger, and activity records used by tools. Filters and badges are projections, the Triggers panel edits the canonical binding/arming state, and run detail reconstructs the correlated event→policy→target→outcome path. Starter packs reuse the generic manifest-only plugin loader and Cupboard installer, so sharing adds no parallel package or orchestration system.\n\n## Phase 1 — trigger core\n\n- **P-001** `done` Schema migrations (atomic allocator + .DRAFT flow): trigger_sources (kind, config, credential ref, status, cursor jsonb), trigger_bindings (event pattern, filter, action, armed, storm policy), trigger_deliveries ledger (dedupe key, emitted event key, outcome) — note: ← WI-40365 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Ingestion core: adapter payload → normalized `ext:<source>:<event>` via events:emit, delivery ledger + dedupe, event keys DERIVED (buildKey — never hand-catalogued) blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40416 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Binding engine: match armed bindings (filter) → action executor (launch plan from template with event payload as launch context; wake agent), storm-policy enforcement, durable execution (DBOS workflow / tier:durable routine — no bare setInterval) blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-40419 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Arming + admin surface: /admin/triggers pane (state in nuqs), autonomy-gated arm/disarm, per-binding storm-policy edit; FLAGS entry default-ON for the surface blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-40432 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Agent verbs: triggers:list/create/bind/arm/disarm/status with guidance (when/notWhen), wired via the agent-tools index blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-40642 completed (done)\n- **P-022** `done` Google Calendar WRITE path (D-012, owner approved 2026-08-23): calendar.events scope on the SAME Google Workspace OAuth source (D-010 pattern; consent upgrade documented), platform write verbs create/update/delete-event behind a typed contract + focused tests — so the calendar app (calendar-app-papercusp-2026-08-23) never owns OAuth (D-007). — note: ← WI-40886 completed (done)\n- **P-023** `done` Facebook trigger source (D-012, owner approved 2026-08-23): replay-safe Graph poll adapter → ext:facebook:* events validated against the canonical social-post datatype (D-004), riding the Meta OAuth provider from personal-vault-live-integrations-2026-08-23 P-004 (vault owns connection config); delivery ledger + dedupe + storm policy like the other sources; no standalone Facebook app. — note: ← WI-40922 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Slack lane\n\n- **P-006** `done` Slack adapter: Socket Mode client (app-level token), envelope-ack correctness under burst, event_id dedupe, Delayed Events toggle documented in setup, reconnect/backoff, cold-start conversations.history reconciliation (rate-limit aware), normalize mention/DM/slash-command → ext:slack:*, connection health visible (managed timer, schedule:inventory) blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-40690 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Slack connect flow: app manifest template + credential storage per the OAuth substrate pattern (secrets never in tree), setup doc blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40691 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Flagship Slack binding: @papercusp mention → respond-in-thread plan template, verified E2E through the desktop app blocked-by: P-006 — note: ← WI-40724 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Gmail lane\n\n- **P-009** `done` Google provisioning: OAuth scopes (gmail.readonly + gmail.compose), Pub/Sub topic + pull subscription (GCP credits), grant Gmail push service-account publisher, token storage via OAuth substrate — note: ← WI-40529 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Gmail adapter: users.watch + ≤7-day renewal as a durable routine, Pub/Sub PULL doorbell consumer, history.list cursor walk with full-resync fallback, normalize ext:gmail:message-received blocked-by: P-009 — note: ← WI-40673 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Flagship Gmail binding: filtered inbound email → respond-to-email plan template producing a Gmail DRAFT; auto-send ships dark (owner-authority flag, registered with reason) blocked-by: P-010 — note: ← WI-40737 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — shareability + acceptance\n\n- **P-012** `done` Trigger-pack shape: manifest with per-field share semantics (secrets stripped, OAuth scopes declared) riding the generic cupboard install/resolve cores; package the email-responder as the example pack blocked-by: P-011 — note: ← WI-40924 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `needs-human` E2E acceptance: live Slack mention launches a plan; live email produces a draft; both driven and verified through the desktop app (tauri-agent-tools); triggers docs page blocked-by: P-008 — note: ← WI-40939 needs-human\n- **P-016** `done` Plan-plane facet + filters: derive one-time vs TRIGGERED classification (has schedule, event binding, or declared manual-start inputs) server-side in the plans:list projection — NO stored kind column (derived-truth rule); filter chips in PlansPane + a facet in the /adv Create dock (nuqs parseAsStringEnum); trigger-source badge on plan rows blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-40743 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `done` Triggered-plans UI: Triggers tab in PlanPopupModal/PlanDetail (?ppv) — list/attach/detach triggers across the three sources (schedule | external event | manual), arm/disarm toggles (installed ≠ armed), last/next fire, storm-policy summary; manual-start dialog rendering declared plan-inputs args (rides the system/plan-inputs start gate); per D-003 mockups blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-40771 completed (done)\n- **P-018** `done` Triggered-runs visibility: per-plan Runs tab + global trigger-activity feed — each run row: fired-at, trigger source + cause summary (event payload one-liner / cron spec / manual actor+args), storm-policy disposition (ran | coalesced×N | queued | dropped | deduped | failed+reason), launched plan-instance link with live status + items progress + agents, duration, cost; run DETAIL adds full redacted payload, matched binding/filter, policy decision trace, timeline (received→matched→policy→launched→completed), and OUTCOME links (Gmail draft, Slack thread); extends the existing plan-run substrate (admin/plans RunDetailPanel) rather than a parallel runs system blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-40802 completed (done)\n- **P-021** `done` Real-world starter templates shipped WITH v1 (the owner-named trio): slack-thread-responder (responds to a user message in-thread), email-draft-responder (drafts a reply to an inbound email — never auto-sends), meeting-prep-brief (useful prep info before each meeting) — each a plan template with declared inputs, sensible default storm policy, and a cupboard-pack manifest (feeds P-012) blocked-by: P-008, P-011, P-020 importance: high — note: ← WI-40940 completed (done)\n- **P-024** `done` Workflows builder v1 (per D-013): evolve the Concept C flow surface — free target choice (any plan; further target kinds per the pending target-model decision), input-mapping step in the contextual inspector, filter + storm-policy editing in place; no separate canvas editor blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-40876 completed (done)\n- **P-025** `done` Rename Automations surface → Workflows (per D-013): tab, routes, nuqs keys, copy, tests — coordinated with automations-trigger-flow-production-2026-08-22 P-004 verification so the rename doesn't race that plan's close — note: ← WI-40877 completed (done)\n- **P-026** `done` Plan outputs (per D-017): optional output schema beside input_schema (datatype-registry-typed); output publication at plan-run completion (declared-but-unfilled fails loudly); plan-completed events carry outputs so chained bindings and the builder's mapping picker read upstream output schemas importance: high — note: ← WI-40878 completed (done)\n- **P-027** `done` Workflows tab landing — implement the Blend (per D-018): needs-you strip (rendered only when non-empty), agent composer hero with source-derived suggestion chips, active-now cards, all-workflows ledger table + full-ledger secondary view, slide-over detail sheet; supersedes the Concept C flow-row landing; visuals per the Workflows Builder canvas page 1 importance: high — note: ← WI-40879 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3b — Google Calendar lane\n\n- **P-019** `done` Google Calendar adapter: incremental sync via events.list + syncToken cursor (full-resync fallback on 410), calendar.readonly scope on the SAME Workspace OAuth as Gmail; local time-wheel emits ext:gcal:event-upcoming (configurable lead, default 15m) + ext:gcal:event-created/updated; NO ingress — poll + syncToken by design (Calendar push channels need a public webhook, excluded per offline doctrine) blocked-by: P-002, P-009 — note: ← WI-40643 completed (done)\n- **P-020** `done` Flagship Calendar binding: meeting-prep brief — ext:gcal:event-upcoming (events with guests) → prep-plan template that assembles attendees, recent Gmail threads with them (reuses the Gmail lane read path), event description/agenda + attached docs, prior meeting notes → delivers a concise brief via desktop notification + inbox message before the meeting blocked-by: P-003, P-019 — note: ← WI-40658 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 5 — provider-neutral capability verbs (D-019 / D-020)\n\n- **P-028** `done` Capability-verb substrate (D-019 Tier 1, D-020 rails): ONE shared seam that (a) resolves a canonical object id (email-message / calendar-event / chat-message) → its trigger_sources row, provider adapter and credential under the D-008 explicit local principal, never provider payload identity; (b) implements the ADDRESSEE-NON-COMPOSABLE rail as tested code, not convention — reply-shaped calls take TEXT ONLY and the server resolves recipient/thread/channel; (c) implements the create-shaped path where an agent-supplied addressee must originate from a trusted channel (owner chat instruction or a personal:search contact) and is REFUSED when lifted from inbound content, echoing resolved recipients back. Verb families P-029..P-031 all sit on this; a falsifiability probe must prove the refusal path actually fires (scripts/mutation-probe.sh, copy-out tier — never mutate the shared tree). importance: high — note: ← WI-40880 completed (done)\n- **P-029** `done` mail:* family over the canonical email-message datatype (D-019 Tier 1): mail:reply { messageId, text } — addressee/thread/headers server-resolved, agent supplies text only (D-020 rail 1); mail:draft; mail:send (create-shaped, trusted-channel addressee per D-020 rail 2, recipients echoed back); mail:search over the owner-granted vault. Correct threading is the adapter's job, not the agent's: Message-ID → In-Reply-To/References propagation, threadId, Re:-preserved subject, from-alias, base64url RFC-2822 encoding. Gmail is the first adapter; the verb names carry NO provider. Sends EXECUTE per D-020 — not draft-only. Per-tool guidance (when/notWhen/chaining) required, and mind the prompt-weight gate. blocked-by: P-028 importance: high — note: capability-verbs/mail.ts + tools mail:reply / mail:send. Adapter now shares ONE MIME encoder: buildGoogleGmailRawMessage + new sendGoogleGmailMessage + replySubjectFor (gmail-flagship's private replySubject fork removed). mail:search DROPPED as duplicate — personal:search already returns the externalId these verbs take. Live-provider E2E rides P-013.\n- **P-030** `done` calendar:* family over the canonical calendar-event datatype (D-019 Tier 1) — DELIVERS THE AGENT-FACING HALF OF P-022, not a parallel surface: calendar:propose (create-shaped — attendees must come from a trusted channel per D-020 rail 2, echoed back before write), calendar:update, calendar:search. Coordinate with P-022's write-path work so the scope/consent half and the verb half land as one thing. blocked-by: P-028 importance: high — note: capability-verbs/calendar.ts + tools calendar:propose / calendar:update, on new adapter primitives createGoogleCalendarEvent/updateGoogleCalendarEvent. Live E2E rides P-013 + the owner OAuth-client wall.\n- **P-031** `done` chat:* family over the canonical chat-message datatype (D-019 Tier 1): chat:reply { messageId, text } — channel/thread server-resolved, agent supplies text only (D-020 rail 1), generalizing today's slack:respond-in-thread { planRunId, text } off its plan-run binding so ad-hoc reply works; chat:post (create-shaped, trusted-channel destination); chat:search. Slack is the first adapter; verb names carry no provider so Teams/Discord land as adapters later. blocked-by: P-028 importance: high — note: capability-verbs/chat.ts + tools chat:reply / chat:post. chat:reply generalizes slack:respond-in-thread off planRunId to a canonical messageId, keeping the same text-only/server-resolved-destination guarantee. chat:search dropped as duplicate of personal:search. Live E2E rides P-013.\n- **P-032** `dropped` Tier-3 generic door (D-019) — NOT in the current build slice, recorded so it is not re-litigated: one http:call-shaped tool { connection, operationId, args } with credentials resolved by connection id and never placed in context, a per-connection operation ALLOWLIST, and explicit confirmation for non-idempotent verbs. OpenAPI specs are imported to POPULATE the allowlist + arg schemas, never to mint tools. Tier-2 companion policy: vendor MCP servers mount behind tools:find/tools:invoke (zero prompt weight until reached for) and are an adapter implementation detail, never the agent-facing contract. Promotion detector: code:run recipe auto-capture — repeated Tier-3 use promotes an operation to a Tier-1 verb. importance: high — note: D-019 governance marker only; explicitly outside the current build slice.\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(added via plans:add-decision)\n\n### D-001 — Voice/video direction: bet on Google Meet (owner call, 2026-08-21)\nDate: 2026-08-22\nOwner chose the Google Meet path for voice/video [owner: interactive dialog 2026-08-21], over LiveKit self-host / Amazon Chime SDK / spike-first, with the constraints on record at decision time:\n\n- Near-term (GA today): Meet REST API + Google Workspace Events API — meeting-lifecycle triggers via Pub/Sub, meeting creation, post-meeting transcripts/recordings. These ride the SAME Google OAuth substrate as the Gmail lane and should be the next trigger source after Gmail ships.\n- Live in-call participation requires the Meet Media API, which as of 2026-08 is DEVELOPER PREVIEW, CONSUME-ONLY (an app can receive audio/video streams + participant metadata but cannot inject audio — a bot can listen, not speak), and requires the Cloud project, OAuth principal, AND every conference participant to be enrolled in the preview program, plus in-meeting host/co-host consent.\n- Implications: (1) step 1 of the voice milestone is Developer Preview enrollment — an owner-side Google account action; (2) the shippable v1 of voice/video is a listen-only Meet notetaker + meeting-lifecycle triggers; (3) two-way voice via Meet is blocked on Google shipping send-side media / GA — revisit this decision at GA.\n\nVoice/video work is NOT in this plan's scope; this decision pins the roadmap so future lanes don't re-litigate the stack choice. Sources verified 2026-08-21: developers.google.com/workspace/meet/media-api/guides/overview (+ concepts), Workspace admin control page for Media API access.\n\n### D-002 — Offline buffer strategy: queue-free v1; Svix Ingest polling endpoints (Papercusp-managed) when the first non-replayable source lands\nDate: 2026-08-22\n[owner: interactive dialog 2026-08-21] v1 ships QUEUE-FREE — the Slack and Gmail adapters reconcile from the providers' own replay APIs on every connect (cursor doctrine in Background): Gmail history.list from historyId; Slack envelope-ack + event_id dedupe + Delayed Events toggle + rate-limit-aware conversations.history backfill for cold gaps. Users sign up for nothing and run nothing always-on.\n\nWhen the first NON-replayable source lands (the generic-webhook trigger — explicitly out of v1), adopt Svix Ingest + Polling Endpoints via ONE PAPERCUSP-MANAGED Svix org that auto-provisions a per-user source + polling endpoint (their AutoConfig token supports zero-dashboard provisioning) — users still sign up for nothing. Per-user Svix accounts (free tier: 50k msgs/mo, 30-day retention, no credit card) remain the self-hoster escape hatch.\n\nBasis (research 2026-08-21): Svix polling endpoints are purpose-built push→pull conversion behind NAT; Hookdeck is the runner-up (push/CLI-tunnel model, 3-day free retention); direct cloud queues (Pub/Sub, SQS) fail the easy-signup bar — each user would need their own cloud project.\n\n### D-003 — TRIGGERED plans: naming + unification of schedule / event / manual under one trigger model, with plan-plane filters and a Triggers UI\nDate: 2026-08-22\n[owner: interactive dialog 2026-08-21 — near-verbatim: \"repeated plans are badly named, they should be called triggered plans. the trigger could be a schedule, an external event or manually clicking start and supplying args via the ui. we also need to make a ui for that\"]\n\nModel: a plan is ONE-TIME or TRIGGERED. A triggered plan carries ≥1 trigger from three sources:\n1. SCHEDULE — cron recurrence; the existing plans:set-schedule / plans:arm-schedule surface becomes the time-trigger special case of the binding model.\n2. EXTERNAL EVENT — an ext:* event binding via this plan's binding engine (P-003).\n3. Post-v1 roadmap D-006 remains otherwise unchanged.\n\n### D-013 — Workflows — product name + builder route for trigger→action wiring (amends D-003 vocabulary)\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive AskUserQuestion dialog 2026-08-23 — picked \"Workflow\" naming and \"evolve Automations tab\" builder route]\n\nNAMING: the wired object (trigger → filter/storm-policy → target) and its shareable cupboard bundle are named WORKFLOW. Rationale: plans already ARE the multi-step orchestration substrate — steps live inside plans (agent-executed); the workflow is the wiring, so the wiring surface stays thin.\n\n### D-014 — Workflow packs: graph-shaped manifest, secrets stripped, cupboard installs land disarmed\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive AskUserQuestion dialog 2026-08-23 — \"Yes — record and add items\"]\n\nWorkflow packs (P-012/P-021) are GRAPH-shaped: the manifest holds N targets (plans today; further target kinds — tool calls / recipes — pending the target-model decision) + trigger bindings + internal event edges + declared inputs + default storm policy + declared OAuth scopes. Per-field share semantics; secrets ALWAYS stripped. v1 packs ship single-target (the P-021 trio) — the graph generality is schema-level from day one so it never needs retrofitting once packs exist in the wild. This decision WIDENS P-012's item scope in place (no item-text editor exists; this ref-pinned decision is the governing text).\n\nCupboard installs land DISARMED (installed ≠ armed): the install flow collects the installer's own credentials/channel ids via the pack's declared inputs before an explicit arm; nothing acts on the installer's accounts until armed.\nRelated: P-012, P-021\n\n### D-015 — Workflow target model: plan | recipe (tool = one-step recipe), determinism-scaled mapping, event-stitched chaining from day one\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive AskUserQuestion dialog 2026-08-23 — picked \"Two stored, three shown\" and \"Event-stitched from day one\"]\n\nTARGET KINDS — two stored, three shown: a binding's target ∈ {plan, recipe}. The builder UI presents three (\"run a plan\" | \"run a recipe\" | \"call a tool\"); \"call a tool\" is authored as a one-step recipe under the hood, inheriting recipe declared-args + authority semantics. No third stored kind.\n\nMAPPING RIGOR SCALES WITH DETERMINISM: a deterministic target (recipe, incl. one-step tool) REQUIRES complete arg mapping — no agent interprets for it; a plan target may additionally take the full redacted payload as agent context. Mapping ladder per the builder mockups: (1) auto type-match via the reflexive datatype registry (D-004), (2) explicit field mappings with live sample data, (3) payload-as-context — plan targets only.\n\nAUTHORITY + SAFETY for deterministic targets: authority pinned at attach time (recipe revision model), executing under the explicit local principal per D-008 — never provider payload identity; mapped payload fields are DATA only (no template eval of payload into command-like args); privileged tools stay out of the v1 bindable set.\n\nCHAINING — EVENT-STITCHED, from day one: a chain (trigger → recipe → plan → tool) is N single-target bindings wired by INTERNAL-EVENT edges. This adds internal events (binding-run-completed, plan-completed) as a binding source — a fourth source alongside D-003's schedule | external event | manual. No pipeline/steps orchestrator on the binding. Each fire carries a CORRELATION id threaded through the chain so the graph view and the Runs feed (P-018) reconstruct and render a multi-binding path as one workflow run.\n\nFAILURE SEMANTICS: deterministic targets get explicit retry policy + a dead-letter disposition surfaced in Activity; replay rides the offline-safe cursor reconcile. Plan targets self-recover via the agent.\n\nSCHEDULER REUSE: schedule-trigger → recipe is declared through the existing routines/recurrence substrate — never a third scheduler.\nRelated: P-024, P-018, P-012\n\n### D-016 — Workflow creation is agent-mediated: read-only graph view + workflow-agent chat (amends D-013's interaction model)\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive turn 2026-08-23 — near-verbatim: \"Lets go with option B but this view should be read only. We should add a workflow agent chat to the view and direct the user to chat with the agent to create the workflow instead of expecting the user to create the complicated workflow themselves.\"]\n\nVIEW: the workflow detail is mockup Option B — the reused dependency-graph pane (elkjs, D-005 of the work tab) renders the chain — and it is READ-ONLY. No direct-manipulation editing of nodes, mapping, filters or wiring in the graph or an inspector.\n\nCREATION/EDITING: a WORKFLOW AGENT CHAT panel sits beside the graph. The user describes intent in natural language; the agent composes and edits the bindings, mapping, filters and storm policy, and the graph re-renders as the agent works. Structural changes are agent-mediated end-to-end — the user is never expected to hand-assemble a chain.\n\nDIRECT CONTROLS that remain: lifecycle only — arm/disarm, pause, run-with-last-event.\n\nD-013's surface rulings stand (evolve the Workflows tab, flow rows, no separate canvas editor); this amends only its interaction model (inspector-based editing → agent-mediated chat). The Brainstorm tab's chat panels (BrainstormChat/BrainstormFull) are the in-app pattern for the chat surface.\n\n### D-017 — Plans gain OPTIONAL declared outputs — typed via the datatype registry, published at completion, carried on plan-completed events for chained mappings\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive turn 2026-08-23 — \"do plans have the concept of output? For this workflow thing to work as we designed, plans will need to have the option of outputs. outputs should be optional\"]\n\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23: plans have input_schema (harness_plans.input_schema jsonb + the system/plan-inputs start gate) but NO output concept anywhere in the plan substrate (repo-wide search; the only output_schema matches are tool-result plumbing in result-door / mcp-handler).\n\nMODEL: plans gain an OPTIONAL output schema declared beside input_schema, typed via the reflexive datatype registry (D-004) — no app-local shapes. A completing plan run PUBLISHES its output values; the plan-completed internal event (D-015's fourth binding source) carries them, so a chained binding maps typed upstream outputs → the next target's declared inputs, and the builder's mapping picker can read the upstream plan's output schema.\n\nOPTIONALITY composes with D-015's mapping-rigor rule ACROSS edges: a plan with no declared outputs can still chain into a PLAN target (payload/context rung); a DETERMINISTIC next step (recipe / tool) requires the upstream plan to declare outputs — no agent interprets for it.\n\nPUBLICATION: the executing agent fills declared outputs at plan-run completion; a declared-but-unfilled output fails the run loudly rather than silently chaining undefined values.\n\n### D-018 — Workflows tab landing is the BLEND — warn strip + agent composer hero + active-now cards + ledger table (supersedes D-013's flow-row landing)\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive AskUserQuestion dialog 2026-08-23 — reviewed four mocked directions (Ledger / Console / Studio / Blend) on the Workflows Builder canvas, picked \"Blend\"]\n\nThe Workflows tab LANDING composes three postures, each only where it earns its place:\n1. NEEDS-YOU STRIP (Console posture) — one compact warn strip at top, rendered ONLY when non-empty (expiring source auth, dead-letter runs, disarmed-after-failures), each entry with a one-click action.\n2. AGENT COMPOSER HERO (Studio posture) — the workflow agent's composer front and center (\"What should happen automatically?\") with suggestion chips derived from connected sources; creation-by-chat per D-016.\n3. ACTIVE-NOW CARDS — the few currently-hot workflows as gallery cards (mini-wiring pills, arm toggle, spend, last fire).\n4. ALL-WORKFLOWS LEDGER — dense table rows (wiring pills, 14d sparkline, last fired, spend, arm toggle) with \"Open full ledger\" as the expanded secondary view; row click = slide-over detail sheet; opening a workflow lands on the read-only graph + agent chat (D-016).\n\nFull Console and full Ledger remain as secondary views. DISCIPLINE: the Blend is the busiest of the four directions — restraint is a requirement; quiet states collapse (strip absent, nothing hot → composer + ledger only).\n\nSUPERSESSION: replaces the Concept-C flow-row LANDING ruling inside D-013. D-013's naming, no-separate-canvas, and evolve-in-place rulings stand, as do D-015/D-016/D-017. Mockups: the Workflows Builder canvas — page 1 (final), page 2 (direction record with motivations/tradeoffs).\n\n### D-019 — External-service integration model: three tiers, provider-neutral capability verbs keyed one-to-one to canonical datatypes, promotion from generic door to first-party verb\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive AskUserQuestion dialog 2026-08-23 — picked \"Decision + plan items\" and \"Me, this session\"; then near-verbatim follow-up turn: \"give calendar and slack/chat this same treatment\"]\n\nQuestion asked: how should agents reach external services — call the APIs directly, use the service's own MCP server, hand-write a tool wrapper per service, or build one generic wrapper pointed at any OpenAPI spec?\n\nRULING — three tiers, one promotion rule.\n\nTIER 1 (the front door; default for anything the owner uses regularly): provider-neutral, task-shaped capability verbs, ONE FAMILY PER CANONICAL DATATYPE. This makes the D-004 datatype registry the contract on the WRITE side, as it already is on the read side:\n- email-message  → mail:reply | mail:draft | mail:send | mail:search\n- calendar-event → calendar:propose | calendar:update | calendar:search\n- chat-message   → chat:reply | chat:post | chat:search\n- contact        → read-only via personal:search in v1 (no write family)\nNever provider-named (no gmail:* / slack:* / gcal:* in the agent-facing set). The provider resolves from the connected trigger_sources row + credential_ref under the D-008 explicit local principal. Consequence: adding Outlook / Teams / Fastmail later is an ADAPTER, not a new agent-facing surface — no new verbs to learn and no prompt-weight cost.\n\nTIER 2: vendor MCP servers are an ADAPTER IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL, never the agent-facing contract. Mount them behind tools:find / tools:invoke so they cost zero prompt weight until reached for. Where a Tier-1 verb exists, the vendor MCP is what the adapter calls — not what the agent calls.\n\nTIER 3: exactly ONE generic spec-driven door (http:call-shaped) for the long tail — { connection, operationId, args }; credentials resolved by connection id and NEVER placed in context; a per-connection operation ALLOWLIST; non-idempotent verbs require explicit confirmation. OpenAPI specs are imported to POPULATE that allowlist and its arg schemas, NOT to mint hundreds of tools.\n\nREJECTED, with reasons on record:\n- Agents calling provider APIs directly: the token would enter context → transcript → compaction summary → memory. Also bypasses the ownership pin, the audit ledger, idempotency, and Gmail's history.list cursor doctrine (which each agent would otherwise rediscover per session).\n- A generic OpenAPI driver as the DEFAULT surface: a spec describes TRANSPORT, not TASK. \"Reply to this email\" is users.messages.send taking a base64url RFC-2822 blob; correct threading additionally needs Message-ID → In-Reply-To/References propagation, threadId, Re:-preserved subject and the right from-alias — none of which the spec encodes, and the failure is SILENT (the mail sends, the thread breaks). Add: zero when/notWhen guidance (routing, not capability, is this repo's measured failure mode), specs far too large to sit in a prompt, and DELETE exactly as reachable as GET. It stays the Tier-3 escape hatch; it is not the front door.\n\nPROMOTION RULE — this is what makes the three tiers ONE system rather than three parallel ones: a new service starts at Tier 3; repeated real use promotes it to a Tier-1 verb. code:run's existing recipe auto-capture is the promotion detector; no new mechanism.\n\nCONSISTENCY WITH THE WORKFLOW PLANE: D-015 makes \"call a tool\" a one-step recipe, so these same Tier-1 verbs are what a binding targets. Chat plane and workflow plane therefore share ONE verb set — the D-016 workflow agent composes with exactly what a chat agent invokes. D-013/D-016 govern the builder UI and are untouched by this ruling.\n\n### D-020 — Outbound action safety: the addressee is never agent-composable from untrusted content; owner-asked sends execute\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: interactive AskUserQuestion dialog 2026-08-23 — picked \"Send when I ask\", over \"Draft-only, always\" and \"Owner-gated send\"]\n\nSEND AUTHORITY: the Tier-1 outbound verbs EXECUTE when the owner asks in chat — mail:send sends, chat:post posts, calendar:propose writes the invite. Draft-only is NOT the v1 posture. mail:draft stays available as an explicit choice, not as the forced path. The existing run-scoped tools (gmail:create-draft, slack:respond-in-thread) keep their own narrower contracts unchanged; this ruling governs the new provider-neutral family.\n\nTHE STRUCTURAL RAIL that makes that safe. Inbound message content is UNTRUSTED TEXT, so an agent that can both read and send mail/chat is prompt-injectable by anyone who can send the owner a message. The mitigation is structural and must never be prompt wording:\n\n(1) REPLY-SHAPED verbs — mail:reply, chat:reply. The addressee is ALWAYS server-resolved from a message/thread id. The agent supplies TEXT ONLY and cannot name or redirect the recipient, thread or channel, and cannot read the token. This is exactly the property gmail:create-draft and slack:respond-in-thread already hold today with { planRunId, text } (\"the server resolves recipient/thread/credential; callers cannot redirect the post or read the token\"). The ONLY change is that the reference becomes a canonical messageId rather than a planRunId — so ad-hoc \"reply to my email like this\" works outside a trigger-bound plan run, without giving up the guarantee. Preserving this property is a hard requirement on the implementation, not a preference.\n\n(2) CREATE-SHAPED verbs — mail:send to a fresh recipient, calendar:propose with new attendees. These genuinely take an agent-supplied addressee, so rail (1) cannot cover them. For these the addressee MUST originate from a TRUSTED channel: the owner's own chat instruction, or a contact resolved through personal:search (which is already default-deny behind a live owner grant). An addressee lifted out of inbound message content is REFUSED. Resolved recipients are echoed back on a create-shaped send so a wrong addressee is visible before it leaves.\n\n(3) NEVER template-eval inbound payload fields into command-like args. D-015 already rules this for deterministic workflow targets (\"mapped payload fields are DATA only\"); this extends the same rule to the chat plane.\n\nWhy this is the deciding constraint for D-018's ruling: a generic OpenAPI driver cannot hold property (1) at all — there, `to:` is just another field the agent fills in, so the recipient becomes composable from whatever the agent read. That single property, more than ergonomics or token cost, is why the front door is a capability verb and not a spec driver.\n\n### D-021 — P-025's rename covers the Automations UI SURFACE only — not the operator-core automation modules\nDate: 2026-08-23\nScope ruling for the D-013 \"one vocabulary end to end\" rename, recorded because the naive reading of D-013 is materially wrong and another lane could act on it.\n\nMEASUREMENT: a case-insensitive search for \"automation\" across apps/operator-vite/src, apps/operator/app, libs and packages/operator-core/lib returns 131 files. Renaming all 131 is NOT what D-013 asks for and would be actively harmful.\n\nIN SCOPE — the user-facing Automations surface and its URL/CSS/test vocabulary:\n- apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/: AdvAutomationsTab.tsx (+ .test.tsx), adv-automations.css, adv-automations.legibility.test.ts, automations-model.ts (+ .test.ts), AdvShell.tsx (+ .test.tsx)\n- apps/operator-vite/src/components/__tests__/adv-shell-logic.test.ts\n- apps/operator-vite/src/routes/adv/index.tsx (+ index.test.tsx)\n- apps/operator-vite/src/components/left-sidebar/AutomationPane.tsx (+ .test.tsx) and the label references in LeftSidebar.tsx / RailSection.tsx / left-sidebar.styles.ts\n- the adv tab id 'automations' -> 'workflows' (this IS URL state via the `tab` nuqs param, so it is a user-visible rename and correct to change), plus the nuqs keys autoView / autoFlowFilter / autoFilter / autoId / autoQ, and the pc-automations__* CSS class prefix.\n\nOUT OF SCOPE — deliberately left on the current names:\n- packages/operator-core/lib/automation/** (catalog.ts, pane-categories.ts, routine-classification.ts, ...). This is the BACKEND catalog module. It is consumed by surfaces beyond this tab, it is not user-facing vocabulary, and renaming it would turn a UI rename into a cross-package refactor with a much larger blast radius than the plan item scopes.\n- Every incidental prose use of \"automation\"/\"automated\" in tool descriptions, blueprints, SQL comments and docs. These are English, not the product surface's name.\n- libs/generic/tooldef, libs/papercusp/**, db migration files.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS FOR ANOTHER LANE: an agent picking up P-025 from its title alone would either (a) rename 131 files, or (b) rename only AdvAutomationsTab.tsx and leave the nuqs keys and CSS selectors on the old vocabulary — the half-done outcome D-013 explicitly rejects. The boundary above is the one that satisfies \"one vocabulary end to end\" for what the operator actually sees and types into a URL, without dragging the backend module along.\n\nCOORDINATION NOTE (time-bounded, verify before relying on it): automations-trigger-flow-production-2026-08-22 D-008 records that its P-004 verification runs against the CURRENT names. The holder of P-004 (su-23a46928) asked on 2026-08-23T07:48Z for the rename to be held ~20-30m while they cleared shared gate reds. Pre-rename baseline measured at 08:21Z: the six affected suites are 133/133 green (adv-shell-logic 32, AutomationPane 54, AdvShell 29, AdvAutomationsTab 7, adv-automations.legibility 5, automations-model 6). Any red after the rename is P-025's to fix, not P-004's.\nRelated: P-025\n\n### D-022 — D-021 AMENDED: the P-025 rename boundary must include 4 cross-component consumer sites, or the rename breaks navigation with GREEN tests\nDate: 2026-08-23\nD-021 fixed the P-025 Automations→Workflows boundary as the operator-vite UI surface, OUT-scoping packages/operator-core/lib/automation/** and \"incidental English\". The operator-core OUT-scope still holds; a naive D-013 read still wrongly renames 131 files.\n\nCORRECTION: D-021's IN-scope list was INCOMPLETE and its \"incidental English\" exclusion too vague to apply — it misleads in BOTH directions. A repo-wide identifier + vocabulary sweep at HEAD found five consumer sites outside the named files. Site 5 has NO test — verify by inspection or add coverage with the rename.\n\nMETHOD (reusable): a boundary drawn from the files that OWN an identifier misses the files that CONSUME it, and the misses are the dangerous half. TWO sweeps are needed: the IDENTIFIER sweep (grep each renamed symbol/key/literal repo-wide, then decide per hit \"same key or substring collision?\") found sites 1-4; only the VOCABULARY sweep (grep the user-facing word, sort into the three classes) found site 5.\n\n### D-023 — D-023: the P-025 CSS namespace rename must NOT be a blind global replace — 3 class suffixes collide and would silently merge two surfaces' styles\nDate: 2026-08-23\nD-013/D-021 call for renaming the operator-vite CSS namespace pc-automations__* → pc-workflows__*. Executed as a blind global find-and-replace, that is WRONG and silently breaks the visual design of BOTH surfaces. This decision fixes the method.\n\nWHY: the P-027 Blend landing (WorkflowsLanding.tsx + adv-workflows-landing.css) already SHIPPED using the pc-workflows__ namespace. So the rename does not move classes into an empty namespace — it merges them into an occupied one.\n\nMEASURED AT HEAD: 57 distinct pc-automations__ suffixes vs 29 distinct pc-workflows__ suffixes. Exactly THREE collide, and all three are rendered in both surfaces (not dead CSS):\n- chips — AdvAutomationsTab.tsx 1 use, WorkflowsLanding.tsx 1 use\n- empty — AdvAutomationsTab.tsx 8 uses, WorkflowsLanding.tsx 2 uses\n- masthead — AdvAutomationsTab.tsx 1 use, WorkflowsLanding.tsx 1 use\n\nALL THREE CONFLICT — the declarations are not compatible, so merging them changes rendering on both sides depending purely on stylesheet load order:\n- chips: automations is `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:3px` (no margin); landing is `display:flex; gap:8px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-top:11px`.\n- empty: automations is `padding:24px; text-align:center; font-size:13px`; landing is `margin:0; padding:18px; border:1px dashed var(--wfl-line); border-radius:11px; font-size:0.84rem`.\n- masthead: automations is `margin:0 0 18px` AND a member of a shared flex group with __viewbar/__filters/__panelhead; landing is its own `display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; flex-wrap:wrap`.\n\nTHE SILENT-BLEED MECHANISM (worse than the direct conflicts): the automations sheet carries DESCENDANT rules keyed on these classes — `.pc-automations__chips span { border, border-radius:999px, text-transform:capitalize, ... }`, `.pc-automations__masthead h1 { font-size: clamp(25px,2.4vw,36px) }`, `.pc-automations__masthead p { max-width:780px; ... }`. After a blind rename these start matching the LANDING's chip spans and masthead heading/paragraph, restyling elements that were never in scope. Nothing references them explicitly, so nothing points at the cause.\n\nNOTHING CATCHES THIS. A CSS class collision does not fail vitest — the components still render, the class strings still match, the tests assert text and roles. adv-automations.legibility.test.ts and the contrast lint check colour/contrast, not layout, spacing, borders or font-size. So the entire post-rename suite (339 tests / 13 suites per D-022) can be green with both surfaces visually wrong.\n\nRULING: in the same pass, rename the THREE colliding suffixes on the AUTOMATIONS side to distinct names, leaving the landing's existing pc-workflows__{chips,empty,masthead} untouched:\n- pc-automations__chips    → pc-workflows__row-chips\n- pc-automations__empty    → pc-workflows__list-empty\n- pc-automations__masthead → pc-workflows__tab-masthead\nand carry their descendant selectors with them (__chips span; __masthead h1; __masthead p; and __masthead's membership in the shared flex group at adv-automations.css:17-22). The other 54 suffixes rename 1:1 and are safe.\n\nWHY THE LANDING KEEPS ITS NAMES: it shipped first, its names are asserted by its own 19/19 green tests, and it is the surface D-018 defines. Moving the incoming tab's classes is the smaller, safer diff.\n\nDELIBERATELY NOT DONE: unifying the two designs by letting the merges stand. That may well be desirable — two surfaces of one feature arguably SHOULD share chip and empty-state styling — but it is a visual design decision under D-018, it needs rendered verification, and it must not be smuggled in as a side effect of a rename. If it is wanted, do it as its own change with screenshots.\n\nVERIFY: after the rename, grep that ZERO pc-automations__ tokens remain; re-run adv-automations.legibility.test.ts plus the landing's suite; and because no unit test covers layout, confirm both surfaces render correctly in the Tauri shell with tauri-agent-tools (screenshot/check) rather than trusting green suites.\n\nMETHOD (reusable): before ANY namespace-wide CSS rename, diff the two namespaces' distinct suffix SETS and treat the intersection as a blocker to resolve explicitly. `comm -12` over two sorted suffix lists answers it in one command. This is the third distinct hazard found in P-025 that green tests would not have caught — after the LearningTab deep-link keys and the WorkspacePulseTab/LeftSidebar copy sites in D-022.\n\n### D-024 — D-024: AutomationPane is OUT of the P-025 rename (D-021 was wrong in the narrowing direction too), and the final nuqs key mapping\nDate: 2026-08-23\nCompletes the P-025 boundary. That is CORRECT per D-013's \"one vocabulary end to end\" and is the intended breaking change; there are no users to migrate (alpha).\nLearningTab.tsx's useOpenArming() writes wfView/wfFilter after this mapping, and its ARMING_AUTOMATIONS_TAB constant's VALUE becomes 'workflows' — see D-022 for why its test stays green either way and must be checked by hand.\n\n### D-025 — Entity vocabulary: UI noun is WORKFLOW, code/type layer stays automation (settles what D-013 left open; scopes with D-021/D-024)\nDate: 2026-08-23\nSettles the question D-013 opened and D-021/D-024 narrowed but did not answer: D-013 renamed the SURFACE (Automations tab -> Workflows tab) and D-021 confirmed P-025's rename covers the UI surface only, but neither said whether the ENTITY the surface manages is also renamed. So the two views inside the SAME tab answered differently for the SAME objects: WorkflowsLanding said \"workflows\" throughout, while the legacy catalog/flow views in AdvWorkflowsTab said \"automations\" (31 user-visible strings). Filed as EI-21267944751813417.\n\nEVIDENCE this is one entity, not two (why this is a naming ruling and not a product choice): AdvWorkflowsTab.tsx does `const flows = useMemo(() => buildAutomationFlows(items), [items])` and then `const landingWorkflows = useMemo(() => flows.map(toLandingWorkflow), [flows])`. The landing's \"workflows\" ARE the catalog's \"automations\", just mapped. Same objects, two nouns, one tab.\n\nTHE RULING\n- USER-VISIBLE COPY = workflow. Every rendered string, aria-label, placeholder, toast, confirm label, dialog title and error message in the Workflows tab says workflow. The tab label, the h1 and the landing already said Workflows, so the legacy catalog view was the outlier and it moved.\n- CODE / TYPE LAYER = automation, unchanged. This is the D-021 boundary applied to the entity noun: AutomationItem, AutomationCatalog, AutomationRoutine, buildAutomation*, filterAutomationItems, CreateAutomationModal, AutomationDetail, AutomationRow, the queryName 'automation.catalog', the DOM ids create-automation-trigger-label / create-automation-plan-label, and the 'automation-plan' plan-slug generator all KEEP the automation noun. A model rename is deliberately out of scope, consistent with D-021's operator-core carve-out.\n\nACCEPTED CONSEQUENCE, stated so nobody 'fixes' it later: the UI says workflow while the code says automation. That divergence is INTENTIONAL.
