AdvWorkflowsTab 8/8, WorkflowsLanding 19/19, adv-workflows.legibility 5/5, lint:tsc:operator-vite scope=files status=clean. Residual sweep zero user-visible hits; all 10 code-layer identifiers confirmed surviving via positive control.\n\nNOTE ON LOCATION: a first copy of this ruling was recorded as automations-trigger-flow-production-2026-08-22#D-010 before I confirmed that D-013/D-021/D-024 live HERE rather than there. THIS decision is the authoritative one; that one has been rewritten as a pointer to it.\n\n### D-026 — Every trigger binding carries a storm cap; unbounded is not representable\nDate: 2026-08-26\nRULING (cross-lane — any lane touching external-trigger bindings follows this).\n\nAn external-trigger binding's storm_policy may no longer be uncapped. `parseStormPolicy` resolves an absent or null `maxRuns` to DEFAULT_STORM_MAX_RUNS (12 runs / 60s window) instead of to `null`, and `StormPolicy.maxRuns` is typed `number`, so unbounded is not expressible in the type. Writers persist BOTH halves, so a stored row states its own effective policy rather than depending on a reader applying the same default.\n\nWHAT THIS SUPERSEDES. The prior judgment was that mail bindings are safely unbounded because \"mail volume is bounded by how fast humans write\" (asserted in the P-023 CONTROL test, admin.integration.test.ts). That premise is FALSE: ingestion sets the burst rate, not authorship. On 2026-08-26T07:43:40Z a Gmail poller closed a 2h35m resync gap and binding 6364f44f minted 228 autonomous plan runs in 68s (~3.4/s) — each a real agent launch — until it was disarmed by hand at 07:46:05Z. 100 minted work-items had to be set to dropped. Evidence: EI-21500982767775449.\n\nTHE SHAPE TO RECOGNIZE. Both live bindings held storm_policy={\"windowSeconds\":60} — a rate window with nothing to rate-limit against. Half-specified config is more dangerous than absent config: the present field READS as rate limiting in every dump of the row, so the missing one is invisible. Wherever a policy pairs a threshold with a window, treat an absent threshold as a defect, not a default.\n\nTHE WRITER, not the surface. The incident shape came from routes/admin/external-triggers.ts, whose zod `.default(null)` / `.default(60)` manufactured a policy object for a caller who stated nothing. That also silently disabled the P-023 per-platform social default for every route-created binding, because createExternalTriggerBinding only reaches for a source default when `stormPolicy` is ABSENT. Those defaults are now `.optional()`, so silence stays distinguishable from a stated policy.\n\nWHY A DEFAULT AND NOT A REFUSAL. A write-boundary refusal protects rows written after it lands and leaves every already-stored row uncapped. The parse-layer default caps the two live bindings with no config edit, no rebind, and no lost history — which matters because there is NO triggers:update verb (confirmed via tools:find: bind/arm/disarm/status/list only), so the alternative was disarm+rebind, which mints a new binding id.\n\nOVERFLOW IS VISIBLE, NOT DROPPED: a throttled event is recorded as a `skipped` trigger_run carrying `external_trigger_storm_limit:<max>/<window>s`. A caller needing a higher rate states an explicit `maxRuns`.\n\nGUARD: admin.integration.test.ts — 'GUARD: no source kind can produce a binding with a window but no cap' asserts the shape is unreachable across gmail/gcal/slack/bluesky/reddit, for both a stated cap-less policy and caller silence.\n\n### D-027 — Flagship provider workflows use durable manual-review execution, not a permanently wakeable named agent\nDate: 2026-08-28\nDate: 2026-08-27\nUnder the owner's explicit AUTO shipment mandate, the unresolved executor fork is settled to the safer manual/review policy. The live stable-agent configuration (`execution: { appHarnessSlug: email, agentName: email-agent }`) has produced `target_unwakeable` and makes provider ingestion depend on a permanently resident named session. That is the wrong operational contract for a desktop product: external events must durably mint the plan run and its reviewable work-item even when no agent is present. The flagship Gmail and Slack bindings therefore omit `action.execution`; work enters the ordinary durable claim/review lane. Arming/disarming and provider writes remain direct operator controls. The existing run progress fraction remains authoritative, and WI-311141 adds an ageing/needs-review signal on that same runs view so unattended work is conspicuous. Each Slack mention creates one isolated event run.\n\n**Next:** Read the triggering mention, write a concise answer, and post it to the originating thread.\n\n## Background\n\n`plan_run.inputs.trigger` carries only the routing envelope — the mention itself is\ndeliberately NOT embedded there. Read it with `triggers:read-payload`, passing this\nrun's numeric id. The response tool accepts only that same id; it resolves the source,\nchannel, thread, and bot credential server-side so a worker cannot redirect the reply\nelsewhere.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Reply in the originating thread.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Each Slack mention yields one reply posted to the thread it was made in.\",\"constraints\":[\"Resolve channel, thread and bot credential server-side from the trigger plan run.\",\"Never post to a caller-supplied channel.\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"P-001\",\"D-001\",\"D-002\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A run of this template posts exactly one reply to the originating Slack thread through chat:reply with the run's planRunId.\",\"falsifier\":\"A run completes with no reply, posts a second reply for the same run, or posts outside the originating thread.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Fire a slack mention event through the binding engine, then read the run and the reply tool's recorded result.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"},\"replication\":\"Run packages/operator-core/lib/capability-verbs/chat.test.ts (chat:reply { planRunId } exactly-once).\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Respond\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Call `triggers:read-payload` with `planRunId=payload.plan_run.runId` to read the triggering mention, draft a concise response, then call `chat:reply` with that same `planRunId` and the response text (it posts through the source's installed chat package, cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10#D-019). Complete only after the tool reports `posted:true` or `alreadyPosted:true`.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Bind replies to a trigger plan run, never caller-supplied Slack coordinates\nDate: 2026-08-22\nThe reply tool resolves channel and thread from the durable trigger run. Its public input is only planRunId plus text, preventing arbitrary-channel posting and keeping credentials server-side.\n\n### D-002 — The mention is referenced, not embedded\nDate: 2026-09-04\nA plan run's inputs land in a federated work-item payload, so embedding the message text there would replicate private workspace content to admitted hive members. The engine now passes the routing envelope only, and the agent pulls the mention server-side by planRunId.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-automations-trigger-flow-production-2026-08-22","title":"Acceptance — Concept C Workflows causal Flows production surface","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-23","owner":"su-a13e8e21-465a-49ab-a4a2-e3518737961d","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — Concept C Workflows causal Flows production surface\nslug: acceptance-automations-trigger-flow-production-2026-08-22\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-a13e8e21-465a-49ab-a4a2-e3518737961d\n---\n\n# Acceptance — Concept C Workflows causal Flows production surface\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nREVISION 3, rewritten against external critique from su-deca6671 and su-cf1c8670 (both 2026-08-23, routed by hand because the consult router was down). What the owner is buying: the 'Needs you' inbox can be emptied in one gesture by an agent that finishes what it is genuinely entitled to finish, hands back everything else in a usable form, and can be stopped. Criteria trace to the plan's goal and to D-001 (full-resolve authority, fully audited), D-002 (central resolver + directed consults), D-003 (command strip, run and review in place).\n\nWHAT THE CRITICS CHANGED. Rev 1 -> 2: 'terminal actions go through the same server helpers the UI buttons use' was an implementation prescription, so it became PARITY OF OBSERVABLE EFFECTS; 'full-width band', 'visible.length' and 'SSE / no polling' were mechanism leaking into acceptance and moved to method; the coverage criterion could be passed by a resolver that SKIPPED EVERYTHING, so skip became enumerated; substantive DECISION SAFETY and CANCELLATION were missing entirely and became criteria. Rev 2 -> 3, all from the second critic: the skip loophole had a TWIN in 'failed-with-reason' (both are now constrained, with run-level thresholds, and the burden is on eligible items ending terminal-or-recommended); decision safety needed KNOWN-ORACLE fixtures, because a valid option id proves nothing about the choice being right; effect parity must cover EVERY terminal action kind rather than one sample, and must include authorization and idempotency among the compared effects; the cancellation criterion carried a recompute-from-rows sentence that was implementation detail, so the model now states convergence and the method keeps the test; and SNAPSHOT INTEGRITY was absent — the manifest must be frozen at start and the run single-flight, or a concurrent start acts twice and a later filter change silently widens the set.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data).
