Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"calendar-app-papercusp-2026-08-23","title":"Calendar app — standalone papercusp app (own harness) on triggers + two-way Google Calendar sync, web + desktop","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Calendar app — standalone papercusp app (own harness) on triggers + two-way Google Calendar sync, web + desktop\nslug: calendar-app-papercusp-2026-08-23\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-28\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-27. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nSpec triad written 2026-08-23 (WI-41054, closed) — all 7 items are promotable (specTriadMissing: null). CORRECTION to the previous ## Now line, which claimed the papercusp-agentic-webapp template was not yet visible to the live operator and that P-001 was gated on the stalled green checkpoint: that was WRONG and is retracted. It was inferred from a single `templates:list { q: \"agentic\" }` call returning 2 rows, without checking what `q` matches. The decisive reads: `templates:list { limit: 200 }` returns count: 18 (the 18th root IS live) and `templates:get-guide { template: \"papercusp-agentic-webapp\" }` returns ok:true with title \"Papercusp Official: Agentic Web App\". P-001 is NOT gated on the deploy — materialization can proceed now. (The green gate IS separately stalled — repair-staging-mismatch, 35 consecutive reds — but that is WI-40086, held live by su-ccd31f35 under D-028 as a sole-serializer lane; it is not this plan's blocker and must not be contested.)\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: P-001 — materialize the app from papercusp-agentic-webapp via templates:new-app into its own harness, walking the closure's decision points (domain: personal calendar; tenancy: both single-user-local and multi-user server; optional planes: data-sync yes, search later), then open the materialized PROTOCOL.md + GUIDE.md as the building context.)\n\n## Background\n[owner: 2026-08-23] The calendar becomes its own application built on top of papercusp (like oddsmith), using the trigger system, supporting a desktop app and a webapp version, and the BYOC cloud version of papercusp — with Google Calendar integration (the owner's \"add GCal to the calendar plan\" directive lands here; the superseded calendar-app-2026-07-06 had none). Today's only live calendar surface is the operator's ScheduledCalendarTab (scheduled-plans view) — a different concern, untouched. Platform boundaries settled elsewhere and binding here: canonical datatypes calendar-event/contact ride harness_shared.datatype_registry (external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22#D-004 — no app-local shapes); the Google Workspace OAuth source + GCal adapters are PLATFORM-owned (D-007/D-010 there — this app never re-implements OAuth or adapters); read-side GCal triggers (ext:gcal:*, syncToken incremental sync) are already built (P-019/P-020 there); write-side GCal (calendar.events) is an approved amendment to that plan; Personal Vault is the connection/config surface.\n\n## Requirements\nWhat must be TRUE when this plan is done. Each is falsifiable; P-007 is where they are demonstrated rather than asserted.\n\n**R-1 — The calendar is its own app, not an operator surface.** A `calendar` app exists as its OWN pot/harness with its own plan-capable Hive home, materialized from the `papercusp-agentic-webapp` app-template (never a hand-rolled scaffold), carrying the materialized PROTOCOL.md + GUIDE.md the template closure produces. Nothing about it lives inside `apps/operator`. The operator's existing ScheduledCalendarTab is a different concern and is untouched by this plan.\n\n**R-2 — Canonical datatypes, never app-local shapes.** Every event and contact the app persists, renders, or emits validates against the `calendar-event` and `contact` entries in `harness_shared.datatype_registry`, and the app's blueprint declares them under `dependencies.datatypes`. A private redefinition of either shape anywhere in the app is a defect, not a local convenience (external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22#D-004).\n\n**R-3 — The app contains no OAuth and no Google API client.** No token exchange, no refresh loop, no `googleapis` call site, no adapter re-implementation. The app consumes the PLATFORM-owned Google Workspace source and GCal adapters (external-triggers D-007/D-010; read side P-019/P-020; write side WI-40886 / D-012), and its connection + configuration surface is the Personal Vault. Grep-level falsifier: no OAuth endpoint constant and no Google API host string in the app tree.\n\n**R-4 — Google Calendar sync is genuinely two-way.** With a vault-configured Google source: (a) remote changes land in the local store via the `ext:gcal:*` binding stream using `syncToken` incremental cursor semantics — a steady-state poll does not re-list the calendar; (b) a local create / update / delete propagates to Google through the platform `calendar.events` write verbs; (c) a simultaneous edit on both sides resolves by ONE recorded, deterministic conflict policy, and the losing revision is preserved and inspectable rather than silently discarded; (d) the app is idempotent against its own echo — a write it originated, arriving back on the read stream, does not duplicate or re-fire triggers.\n\n**R-5 — The calendar is usable as a calendar.** Month, week, day and agenda views render on `papercusp-ui` registry primitives; create / edit / delete / move works against the local event store; and all user-meaningful view state (view mode, focused date, selected event id, filter set) lives in the URL via nuqs, so `ui:get_state` / `ui:dispatch` can drive every one of them. State an agent cannot see or set is state in the wrong place.\n\n**R-6 — Triggers do real work, through the one seam.** The app ships at least the meeting-prep automation (seeded from the external-triggers P-020 flagship) plus a scheduling/reschedule automation, and meeting-prep FIRES from a real upcoming calendar event end to end. Its judgment plane crosses into the app at exactly one typed `work_items` ⇄ typed-contract seam (`papercusp-ops-pots`) — never a bespoke in-app agent loop.\n\n**R-7 — One core, two chassis.** A single core (SPA + server + data layer + ops-pots plane) yields BOTH a web-host deployment artifact — which is also the BYOC workspace-host build — and a thin Tauri desktop wrapper around that same core. There is exactly one materialization in the tree; the desktop artifact adds a shell, not a second app. Divergence between the two targets beyond the shell is a defect (D-001).\n\n**R-8 — Acceptance is demonstrated on both chassis.** E2E passes for desktop (driven headlessly via `tauri-agent-tools`) and for web (browser), against a BYOC workspace-host profile, with the trigger firing live and the Google round-trip observed — not inferred from unit tests.\n\n## Design\nHow it gets built, and the trade-offs settled.\n\n**Chassis: web-first core, desktop as a wrapper (settled — D-001).** The alternative considered was materializing from `papercusp-agentic-desktop-app` and adding a web build later. Rejected: the BYOC workspace-host target is a web-host artifact, so a desktop-first core would have to grow a web-host path anyway, and the two would drift. Materializing from `papercusp-agentic-webapp` makes the web-host artifact the natural output and the Tauri shell the additive one — which is also papercusp's own pattern. Cost accepted: desktop-only affordances (native notifications, tray) arrive later and go in the shell, not the core.\n\n**Tenancy: both, decided once at the closure's decision point (P-001).** The app answers both single-user-local and multi-user-server, because the BYOC fork requires the server shape and the desktop wrapper requires the local shape. Rather than branching the code, tenancy is a data-layer + auth-seam configuration chosen at materialization; the UI and the store are written against whichever the seam reports. Optional planes: `data-sync` YES from the start (the GCal stream and the multi-viewer web target both need live invalidation); `search` deferred until there is enough event history to make it worth it.\n\n**Platform boundary: the app is a CONSUMER, never an integrator (R-3).** The GCal read side already exists as `ext:gcal:*` trigger bindings with syncToken cursor state held by the platform adapter; the write side lands as `calendar.events` verbs under WI-40886/D-012. The app therefore owns: a binding subscription, a projection from the canonical `calendar-event` shape into its store, and calls to the write verbs. It does NOT own: OAuth, token refresh, quota/backoff, or API pagination. This is the reuse-first rule applied at the largest seam in the plan — re-implementing any of it would fork a maintained platform surface.\n\n**Sync model: local store is the working set, Google is a replicated peer (P-004).** Reads apply remote deltas into the local store keyed by the platform's stable external id, carrying an `etag`/version and an origin marker so the app can recognize its own echo (R-4d). Writes go local-first, then to the write verbs, with the external id backfilled on ack — so the UI never blocks on a network round-trip. Default conflict policy: **remote-wins on field-level collision, local-queue-and-retry on a write that lost a race**, with the losing local revision retained as an inspectable superseded row rather than dropped. This default is the design position, not yet ratified — P-004 records the final policy as a `D-NNN` decision on this plan, and the retained-loser requirement (R-4c) holds whatever policy wins.\n\n**UI: registry primitives + URL state (P-003).** Views are composed from the `papercusp-ui` component registry via `design-phase:search_registry` before anything is hand-rolled; the four view modes are one component family over a shared date-range query rather than four independent screens. All view state is nuqs (`parseAsStringEnum` for view mode, a date string for focus, a short scalar for selection) per the repo's nuqs rule — this is what makes R-5's agent-drivability free rather than a retrofit. The superseded calendar-app-2026-07-06 D-001..D-004 view/editor contracts may inform the decomposition, but its `window.CalendarStore` storage contract does not apply: storage is the papercusp data layer.\n\n**Triggers: one seam (P-005).** Automations are declared as trigger bindings + plan templates shipped with the app, and every one of them crosses into judgment through `papercusp-ops-pots`' single typed `work_items` ⇄ contract seam. Meeting-prep is seeded from the external-triggers P-020 flagship rather than written fresh, so the app inherits a binding shape already proven against live Google data.\n\n**Sequencing and the real critical path.** P-001 is gated on the `papercusp-agentic-webapp` template being visible to `templates:new-app` on the LIVE operator — the template exists on staging but the green gate is stalled (WI-40086), so the deploy that publishes the 18th root has not landed. That is a pipeline blocker owned elsewhere, not a design question, and it does not block specification work: P-002's contracts are written against the canonical registry entries, which already exist. P-004 and P-005 fan out from P-002/P-003 and touch disjoint surfaces (sync adapter vs. trigger bindings), so they are genuinely parallel; P-006 packaging must not begin before P-003 settles the core's shape, or the \"one core\" invariant (R-7) is decided by accident.\n\n## Phase 1\n- **P-001** `dropped` Materialize the app from papercusp-agentic-webapp via templates:new-app into its own harness; walk the closure's decision points (domain: personal calendar; tenancy: both single-user-local and multi-user server — the BYOC fork; optional planes: data-sync yes, search later). — note: ← WI-41060 completed (dropped)\n- **P-002** `todo` Deterministic plane: calendar-event/contact store + typed-contract write gates; blueprint declares dependencies.datatypes on the canonical calendar-event + contact registry entries — never private redefinitions. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Calendar UI: month/week/day/agenda views on papercusp-ui primitives; CRUD on the local event store; URL state in nuqs. (The superseded plan's D-001..D-004 view/editor/storage contracts may inform the UI decomposition but the storage is the papercusp data layer, not window.CalendarStore.) blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` Google Calendar two-way sync: consume the platform read adapter stream (ext:gcal:* bindings + syncToken cursor semantics); write path through the platform calendar.events write verbs once the external-triggers amendment lands; conflict policy (remote wins vs local queue) recorded as a decision. blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-005** `todo` Trigger bindings + plan templates shipped with the app: meeting-prep (seeded from the external-triggers P-020 flagship), scheduling/reschedule automations; judgment plane through the ONE work_items⇄typed-contract seam. blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-006** `todo` Dual-target packaging: web-host deployment artifact (also the BYOC workspace-host build) + thin Tauri desktop wrapper around the same core — one core, never two divergent materializations. blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-007** `todo` Acceptance: E2E on both chassis (tauri-agent-tools for desktop, browser for web); trigger-driven meeting-prep fires live; vault-configured Google source used end-to-end; verify against a BYOC workspace-host profile. blocked-by: P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Dual-target shape: one core, two chassis (owner ruling 2026-08-23)\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: 2026-08-23, interactive choice \"One core, two chassis\"] The app ships ONE core (SPA + server + data layer + ops-pots plane) with TWO chassis artifacts: the web-host deployment (also the BYOC workspace-host build, per byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22 D-018 \"one web UI, N artifacts; the GUI never embeds the Server\") and a thin Tauri desktop wrapper. NOT two divergent materializations. Materialize from papercusp-agentic-webapp; the desktop wrapper follows papercusp's own pattern.\n\n### D-002 — Supersedes calendar-app-2026-07-06 (vanilla-JS plan, never built)\nDate: 2026-08-23\ncalendar-app-2026-07-06 (\"local web app for managing a calendar\" at ~/Calendar/calendar-app, vanilla JS window.CalendarStore contracts, fleet-lane decomposition) was authored 2026-07-06 and never built — verified 2026-08-23: nothing exists on disk at ~/Calendar/calendar-app and all 7 items are still todo. Per the owner's 2026-08-23 directive the calendar is instead its OWN papercusp app on the trigger system with Google Calendar integration — which the old plan lacked entirely (satisfying \"if google calendar integration isn't in the plan, add that to this plan\": it lands here, its successor). The old plan's D-001..D-004 UI/storage contracts may inform P-003's view decomposition.\n\n### D-003 — templates:new-app CONNECTION_CLOSED root-cause: single owner = su-30d307ac, routed under WI-41060\nDate: 2026-08-23\nBoth app lanes (email WI-41058, calendar WI-41060) are blocked on the same reproducible defect (EI-21107910194803524: templates:new-app dies mid-write with CONNECTION_CLOSED :6432, strands the pot, rollback does not fire on the connection path). To avoid duplicated root-causing, ONE owner: su-30d307ac owns root-cause + durable fix + compensation extension, working UNDER its held lane item WI-41060 — fleet claim-specs are plan-scoped and cannot admit the off-plan EI (WI-41054 refusal precedent), so evidence/fix state lands as comments on EI-21107910194803524 while the lane claim stays WI-41060. su-ebcf16d3 (email lane) does NOT duplicate root-cause work: re-claims WI-41058, verifies no email-side strand, contributes its evidence (PgBouncer backend pid 3974, WI-41058 checkpoint). BOTH materializes stay held until the fix is verified green; the fleet leader releases both. Supersedes the 20:59Z leader direction assigning root-cause to the email lane (that member carry-respawned and lease-released WI-41058; calendar member is live, strand-clean, corroborated 2/2, and volunteered — invitation to re-route was explicit in msg mt6awy5f).\n\n### D-004 — SUPERSEDES D-003: root-cause owner = su-ebcf16d3 under WI-41058 (accepted claim wins the race); su-30d307ac stands down, contributes evidence\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRace resolved. Before D-003's re-route was communicated to either member, email member su-ebcf16d3 re-claimed WI-41058 and formally ACCEPTED root-cause ownership under the original 20:59Z leader direction (\"Accepted: I own CONNECTION_CLOSED root-cause + durable fix under WI-41058 (claimed). Starting now.\" — ~21:15Z). Tie-break honors the accepted, claimed, directed assignment over the volunteered one: su-ebcf16d3 OWNS root-cause + durable fix + compensation extension for EI-21107910194803524, working under WI-41058. su-30d307ac STANDS DOWN on root-cause; contributes its independent corroboration (2/2 failures on slug 'calendar', strand-clean verification, new-app.ts:563-573 reading, dev:pg_health capture, and its two open questions: PgBouncer-vs-verb-connection-handling origin; whether both lanes' failures share one PgBouncer backend pid) as comments on EI-21107910194803524; holds the WI-41060 materialize parked on announced gate 'templates-new-app-fix-green'. The leader verifies the fix green, then emits the gate and releases BOTH materializes. D-003's routing mechanics still stand (plan-scoped claim-specs cannot admit the off-plan EI; work under the held lane item) — they now apply to WI-41058.\n\n### D-005 — P-001 materialize is gated on templates:new-app being DEPLOYED, not on its fix being green\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRULING (fleet leader, verified 2026-08-23T21:58Z) — canonical twin of the same decision on email-app-2026-08-23; both lanes are blocked by one cause.\n\nDo not retry templates:new-app until dev:pipeline_position reports deployed:true for packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/templates/new-app.ts.\n\nsu-30d307ac's diagnosis on WI-41060 was correct and its self-retraction was correct: the failure is specific to this compound verb's write path, not pool exhaustion. Mechanism: new-app.ts blocks 111-290s inside pot:create while the ambient workspace tx sits idle; Postgres kills it at idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (60s), surfacing a bare `write CONNECTION_CLOSED 127.0.0.1:6432`. Hence dev:pg_query succeeding immediately before and after, and dev:pg_health reading healthy at failure time.\n\nskipWorkspaceTx:true at new-app.ts:588 fixes exactly this — but at 21:58Z the path reads committedLocal:true, onStaging:true, inMain:FALSE, deployed:FALSE. :3070 runs release sha 9599c6ca without it. Gate stalled at 35 reds (verdictStale=writer-starved, abort=repair-staging-mismatch), owned live by WI-40086 / su-ccd31f35 under D-028 sole-serializer — not this lane's to contest, and release:checkpoint-run must not be fired.\n\nPRESERVED DECISION ANSWERS for the materialize when it unblocks (GUIDE order: tenancy fork FIRST, then domain, then the closure): tenancy = BOTH single-user-local (embedded PG) AND multi-user server, the BYOC fork; domain = personal calendar; optional planes = papercusp-data-sync YES, papercusp-search LATER (deferred until there is event history worth indexing); slug 'calendar'; parentDir /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace; kickoffBuilder FALSE — a GUIDE-seeded builder would double-place P-002..P-007 outside the fleet spawn graph.\n\nPRE-RETRY HYGIENE (required, from su-30d307ac's checkpoint): verify BOTH that /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/calendar is absent AND that harness_registry payload->'projects' has no {\"slug\":\"calendar\"} entry; if either is present, pot:obliterate { slug:'calendar', confirm:true } FIRST or slug_exists makes retry impossible. Attempt #1 stranded a pot row (obliterated); attempt #2's compensation succeeded. Current state verified clean: harness:status{slug:'calendar'} => not found.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"email-app-2026-08-23","title":"Email app — standalone papercusp app (own harness) on triggers + Gmail, web + desktop","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Email app — standalone papercusp app (own harness) on triggers + Gmail, web + desktop\nslug: email-app-2026-08-23\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SHIPPED 2026-08-25. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-shipped snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nOwner re-authorized direct implementation in AUTO mode on 2026-08-24. Prior fleet member is ended and holds no claims. The canonical seven-item plan is now owned by su-9613bc92; requirements and design are audited against the full source conversation.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is shipped. (Pre-shipped next, no longer actionable: Materialize the `email` app through `templates:new-app` only after verifying the live `skipWorkspaceTx` fix and ensuring no stranded `email` directory or harness registration exists. Then implement P-002 through P-007 in dependency order.)\n\n## Background\n\n[owner: 2026-08-23] Email becomes its own application built on top of papercusp (like Oddsmith), using the trigger system, supporting a desktop app and a webapp version, and the BYOC cloud version of papercusp. Canonical `email-message` and `contact` datatypes live in `harness_shared.datatype_registry`; the app reuses the platform-owned Google Workspace OAuth source, Gmail adapter (`users.watch`, Pub/Sub, `history.list` cursor), external trigger system, Personal Vault connection/config surface, and Papercusp UI/data planes rather than duplicating them. Gmail auto-send remains dark behind owner authority; normal agent output is a Gmail draft.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Deliver a standalone email product in its own Papercusp harness with one shared application core and both web and Tauri desktop chassis; the web artifact must also support the BYOC workspace-host deployment profile.\n- Persist and query email messages and contacts through the canonical registered datatypes with typed-contract write gates; do not create app-private duplicates of platform data contracts.\n- Provide a usable inbox: thread list, conversation view, search, compose, reply drafting, labels/triage, and URL-addressable view state.\n- Integrate through existing Personal Vault Google configuration, Gmail ingestion, and `ext:gmail:*` trigger bindings. Agent replies must create Gmail drafts; sending is forbidden by default and only available behind the registered owner-authority dark flag.\n- Ship reusable trigger bindings and plan templates for respond-to-email→draft plus triage and labeling automations. All judgment crosses the application boundary through exactly one typed `papercusp-ops-pots` seam.\n- Preserve offline/local usability for the desktop target and multi-user/server operation for web/BYOC.\n- Include project-native tests proving contracts, inbox flows, trigger-to-draft behavior, no-send enforcement, and both chassis builds. Acceptance requires focused tests plus E2E on web and desktop; live Gmail/BYOC checks must be reported honestly if external credentials are unavailable.\n\n## Design\n\nMaterialize from the official `papercusp-agentic-webapp` whole-app template because the product needs the web-host/data-layer/UI closure plus the single ops-pots judgment seam. Select domain `email`, tenancy `both` (single-user local and multi-user server), data-sync `yes`, search `yes`, and `kickoffBuilder:false`. Keep the generated SPA/server/data core canonical; add the standard thin Tauri shell around that same core instead of creating a second desktop implementation.\n\nThe deterministic plane owns canonical email/contact reads and typed writes. The integration plane consumes the already-built Gmail source and trigger events. The judgment plane may classify, triage, and draft, but cannot bypass typed commands or grant itself send authority. URL state uses `nuqs`; UI composition starts from registry/Papercusp UI primitives. The app ships starter plan templates and bindings as data, not a bespoke workflow runtime.\n\nMaterialization is guarded because four prior attempts exposed the idle-in-transaction failure class: the dispatcher held an ambient workspace transaction while `pot:create` ran long enough for Postgres to kill it. The durable fix is `skipWorkspaceTx:true` on `templates:new-app`. Before retrying, verify the target directory and harness registry are both clear; if not, use the supported pot cleanup verb. The temporary user-layer template bridge is removed after the canonical bundled template is live so it cannot shadow future updates.\n\n## Phase 1\n\n- **P-001** `done` Materialize the app from papercusp-agentic-webapp via templates:new-app into its own harness; walk the closure's decision points (domain: email; tenancy: both single-user-local and multi-user server; optional planes: data-sync yes, search yes — inbox search matters early). — note: ← WI-41058 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Deterministic plane: email-message/contact store + typed-contract write gates; blueprint declares dependencies.datatypes on the canonical email-message + contact registry entries. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-41411 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Inbox UI: thread list/conversation view/compose on papercusp-ui primitives over the ingested email-message store; URL state in nuqs. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-41412 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Gmail integration: consume ext:gmail:* trigger bindings + the vault-configured Google source for ingestion; agent-drafted replies land as Gmail DRAFTS via the platform verbs; auto-send stays behind the owner-authority dark flag. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-41413 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Trigger bindings + plan templates shipped with the app: respond-to-email→draft (seeded from external-triggers P-011 flagship + the P-021 starter trio), triage/label automations; judgment plane through the ONE seam. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-41414 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Dual-target packaging: web-host deployment artifact (also the BYOC workspace-host build) + thin Tauri desktop wrapper around the same core — one core, never two divergent materializations. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-41415 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Acceptance: E2E on both chassis; live inbound email → draft produced, driven through triggers; verify against a BYOC workspace-host profile. blocked-by: P-004, P-005, P-006 — note: ← WI-41416 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Dual-target shape: one core, two chassis (owner ruling 2026-08-23)\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: 2026-08-23, interactive choice \"One core, two chassis\"] Ship one core (SPA + server + data layer + ops-pots plane) with a web/BYOC host artifact and a thin Tauri wrapper. Do not create two divergent materializations.\n\n### D-002 — Supported user-template bridge unblocks the missing bundled root\nDate: 2026-08-23\nThe root template was installed into the documented per-workspace user template layer because it existed on staging but was not yet deployed. This is a temporary supported bridge, not a parallel scaffold. Remove it once the bundled template is live, or the user copy will shadow canonical updates.\n\n### D-003 — Materialization requires the live transaction fix and clean target\nDate: 2026-08-23\nPrior `templates:new-app` attempts failed when Postgres killed an idle ambient transaction during long `pot:create` work and stranded half-born pots. The durable fix is `skipWorkspaceTx:true` on the handler. Before retrying, confirm the target directory and harness registry contain no `email` residue; clean through the supported pot verb if needed. Unit-green alone is insufficient when the executing operator still serves an older build.\n\n### D-004 — Activation audit and ownership transfer (2026-08-24)\nDate: 2026-08-24\nThe activation audit re-read the complete owner directive and execution history in sessions `a88e70c4-9cb9-443f-b65e-c4c2e5988745` and `8e35f0d2-be14-4bd7-be1d-9c81b07d6b4c`, plus the live plan/work-item ledger. Requirements, scope, constraints, decisions, dependencies, sequencing, acceptance, and the materialization failure history are mapped above. The prior fleet member is ended with no claims; owner explicitly directed this session to implement the plan itself in AUTO mode from start to finish.\n\n### D-005 — Canonical unified app root supersedes the legacy agentic-web overlay\nDate: 2026-08-24\nWI-41156 intentionally retired the four legacy app roots and made their refs aliases of `papercusp-app`; this plan's requested `papercusp-agentic-webapp` ref therefore remains valid but now resolves to the unified parameterized root. For P-001, answer `target: both`, `agents: pots`, `domain: email`, `optional-planes: data-sync + search`; retain the plan's web tenancy `both` and thin shared-core Tauri decision. The temporary per-workspace legacy template installed under D-002 must be removed from the resolving layer before re-materialization because it shadows this canonical alias. Live inspection found the existing `apps/email` contains generated template artifacts only, with no harness row and no Git repository, so it is safe to clean and re-materialize through the official verb.\nRelated: P-001, P-006\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fleet-headcount-guarantee-2026-08-23","title":"Guarantee fleet headcount — close the refill loop, fix the wrong-pool reader, and LAND the instruments already built","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Guarantee fleet headcount — close the refill loop, fix the wrong-pool reader, and LAND the instruments already built\nslug: fleet-headcount-guarantee-2026-08-23\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** READY, not started. Written 2026-08-23 by su-c1dea4c8 (leader, nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820) on an interactive owner directive from Avi after the fleet ran at ~16 turn-taking members against an expected 30, and the leader reported the gap across several wakes instead of closing it.\n\n**The reframe that shaped this plan:** the instrument fixes mostly EXIST already. `fleet-lead-instrumentation-audit-2026-08-09` is COMPLETE (25/25 items, 13 decisions) and its own Now says *\"NOT YET DEPLOYED ... appear only after the next green+deploy.\"* WI-41005 is done and green and undeployed for the same reason. `fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21` has owner-approved scope but has not started because the execution route was never selected. So the dominant failure is DELIVERY, not diagnosis, and a 31st diagnosis plan would re-enact the exact failure. Phase 3 is therefore about landing built work; only Phase 2 is genuinely new capability.\n\n**Next:** Avi selects the execution route (this plan, or fold into `fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21`, whose pending route selection is the same open decision). P-001 is claimable immediately and is already held as WI-41067.\n\n## Background\n\nMeasured 2026-08-23T21:22Z on `harness_shared.coord_presence` for the drain fleet:\n\n| reading | count |\n|---|---|\n| roster rows | 59 |\n| heartbeat fresh (5m) | 34 |\n| active (15m) | 25 |\n| took a turn (5m) | **16** |\n| codex in-flight (instant) | 1 |\n\nThe dashboard showing \"<10 thinking\" was correct; the roster was the misleading surface. 34 processes alive, 16 taking turns — the difference is warm-dead sessions whose heartbeat keeps ticking after the session ends.\n\nFour independent defects turned that into an invisible, hours-long shortfall:\n\n1. **The leader read the wrong inference pool.** `fleet:capacity` has NO `fleet` parameter; with no args it falls through to a hardcoded legacy `BEE_PROVIDER` (claude). This fleet's members are codex. Bare call: claude, BLIND, 7/12 walled, diverged. Correct call: codex, MEASURED, healthy, no divergence. Opposite operational conclusions, same instant. `fleet:leader-brief`'s own remedy text tells the leader to run that bare call as its falsifier.\n2. **No target existed anywhere.** Every surface reported \"members: 57\"; none reported \"you are N below target.\" The number lived only in the owner's head, so nothing could alert on it.\n3. **Nothing refills.** Even once known, no mechanism restores headcount, and `fleet:respawn-member` fails CLOSED on unmanaged sessions (EI-21269964911840629), leaving a wedged member unrecoverable by anyone.\n4. **Counts without identities.** `fleet:leader-brief` truncates its member array at 12 of 57 even at `payloadTier:'full'` with a projection. You cannot respawn a member you cannot name.\n\n## Phase 1 — Stop misreporting who is working\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Fix `fleet:capacity` wrong-pool default: accept `fleet` (defaulting to caller's fleet), resolve provider from the fleet's MEMBERS, return per-provider readings when members span backends, and stamp `providerSource: explicit|fleet-members|legacy-default` so a defaulted reading can never be mistaken for a measurement of your own fleet. Tracked as WI-41067. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Correct `fleet:leader-brief`'s remedy text, which currently instructs leaders to run the bare wrong-pool falsifier. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `done` Report turn-taking liveness distinctly from process liveness: expose `roster` / `heartbeatFresh` / `activelyWorking` as separate named fields everywhere headcount is shown, so a warm-dead population can never read as healthy. importance: high — note: ← WI-41102 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Stop truncating member identities at 12 of N in leader-brief; a leader needs names to act, and the count alone is not actionable. importance: high — note: ← WI-41103 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Separate historical cumulative counters from live state in the brief summary — `admission_blocked` is non-decaying but sits beside live gauges, which invites (and caused) void before/after reasoning. — note: ← WI-41104 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Close the refill loop (new capability)\n\n- **P-006** `done` Make TARGET HEADCOUNT first-class fleet state, set at launch and readable by any surface — not leader memory, not a prompt convention. importance: high — note: ← WI-41145 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Automatic refill: when `activelyWorking < target`, respawn toward target clamped to the FLEET'S OWN pool headroom, emitting a fleet event on every refill and on refusal-with-reason. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-41146 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `todo` Fix respawn failing closed on unmanaged sessions (EI-21269964911840629) — today a wedged member on an unmanaged host has no recovery route available to its leader OR itself. blocked-by: P-007 importance: high\n- **P-009** `todo` Address context-death as the dominant attrition cause: members hit ~97% context and re-enter on cold wakes; pair a pre-death checkpoint with a recovery path that does not depend on the failing respawn lever.\n\n## Phase 3 — Deliver what is already built\n\n- **P-010** `todo` Land `fleet-lead-instrumentation-audit-2026-08-09` (25 items, complete 2026-08-09, undeployed since). Verify each instrument on :3070 rather than in-tree. importance: high\n- **P-011** `todo` Land WI-41005 (spurious `parked-awaiting-capability`), complete and green and undeployed behind the same gate. blocked-by: P-010\n- **P-012** `todo` Decide the delivery policy for fleet-health fixes blocked behind a long-held green gate: today a 35-red gate under a WI-40086 quiescence hold blocks every fleet-observability fix indefinitely, with no expedited lane. This is the root delivery constraint behind P-010 and P-011. importance: high\n\n## Phase 4 — Tooling friction hit while monitoring this fleet\n\n- **P-013** `todo` `fleet:invariant` rejected a description 3x with only \"too long — N over, trim to 500\" and no preview of what would be cut; each retry cost a full round-trip. Report the overage with the clipped tail, as `facts:assert` already does.\n- **P-014** `todo` `projection` pick/pipe is unusable against toon-rendered bodies: `pick` reports \"not JSON, skipped\", `pipe` then matches the whole rendering as ~3 lines and returns nothing useful. A no-match returning an EMPTY body reads exactly like a filter that worked.\n- **P-015** `todo` `loop:checkpoint` `checks` silently evicts carried rows at a 12-row cap under merge; this session lost 7 carried checks, one of which was the very correction that would have prevented the wrong-pool error hours earlier.\n- **P-016** `todo` Fact scopes at their 200-row cap evict ANOTHER agent's fact on every new key, with no pre-write warning unless `dryRun` is used. A leader recording findings quietly deletes peers' findings.\n- **P-017** `todo` Plan fragmentation: 30 non-archived plans match fleet/drain/capacity, several ready-but-unstarted and overlapping. Consolidate or supersede, so the next agent does not add a 31st.\n- **P-018** `todo` Plan dedup (`similar_exists`) matches on generic shared tokens and missed the real neighbors: creating this plan surfaced 5 candidates (fleet-messaging, traceability, Queen/Scout, 2x Blender), 2 of them shipped/superseded, while the two genuinely overlapping plans were found only by hand-written SQL. Dedup that surfaces false neighbors and hides true ones trains agents to reflex `force: true`. blocked-by: P-017\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Do NOT re-audit the instruments; deliver the completed audit instead\n\n`fleet-lead-instrumentation-audit-2026-08-09` is COMPLETE — 25 items done, 13 decisions recorded — and explicitly undeployed. Its recurring finding was \"MEASURE THE CLAIM BEFORE BUILDING: a symptom outlives its fix.\" Writing a fresh audit of the same instruments would reproduce precisely the failure it warned about. This plan therefore treats that work as an asset to LAND (P-010), and claims new ground only where no existing plan does: target headcount and automatic refill (Phase 2).\n\n### D-002 Target headcount is fleet state, never leader memory\n\nThe shortfall was invisible because the target existed only in the owner's head, so no tool could evaluate it. As an immediate stopgap a `fleet:invariant` (`target-headcount-30-actively-working`, critical) is registered on the drain fleet and evaluates on every `fleet:leader-brief` read, returning target/actively_working/shortfall/roster_rows as evidence. That is a per-fleet patch by one leader, NOT the fix: P-006 makes it a platform property so every fleet gets it without a leader remembering to register it.\n\n### D-003 The wrong-pool default is a correctness defect, not a usability nit\n\nA tool named `fleet:*` that cannot consult a fleet, and silently answers about a hardcoded legacy provider, produces confidently wrong operational verdicts — here, a leader telling members their pool was healthy on evidence from a pool they do not use. The remedy must make the provenance of the reading visible (`providerSource`), because the failure mode is not an error but a plausible answer to a question nobody asked.\n\n### D-004 Liveness must be reported as turn-taking, not heartbeat freshness\n\n34 heartbeat-fresh vs 16 turn-taking on one fleet at one instant. Any surface reporting a single \"members\" number without distinguishing these can show a healthy fleet that is doing nothing, which is what happened. This is already documented in the liveness semantics; the defect is that the leader-facing surfaces do not honor it.\n\n### D-005 — Execution route: this plan runs STANDALONE; fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21's unstarted scope folds into Phase 4\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDECIDED 2026-08-23T22:50Z by su-c1dea4c8 (leader, nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820) under AUTO mode, on the open route question this plan's own ## Now names. Disclosed to Avi; reversible on his word.\n\nRULING\n1. This plan RUNS STANDALONE. It is not folded into fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21.\n2. fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21's unstarted scope is ABSORBED into this plan's Phase 4 (tooling friction hit while monitoring this fleet). Do not start it as a separate lane.\n\nGROUNDS\n- This plan is ALREADY IN MOTION: P-001 is covered by WI-41067 and P-003 by WI-41102, both open. Folding a plan whose items already carry live covering work-items would orphan in-flight work for no gain.\n- fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21 has owner-approved scope and ZERO motion, stalled for the identical reason (its execution route was never selected). Two plans waiting on one unmade decision is the failure being corrected here.\n- The two scopes are the same lane: friction-remediation's subject is tooling friction, which Phase 4 already defines and holds items for. Absorption is the reuse-first move; a parallel plan would duplicate the surface.\n\nCORRECTION THIS SUPERSEDES\nThe prior leader reading that this plan was INERT (0 promoted work-items) was FALSE and is retracted. It rested on a source_plan_slug query, which is the wrong column: plan coverage is a work->plan_item edge, and source_plan_slug is populated only by the plans:start path, so hand-filed covering items read NULL. See owner-fact 13209 (dead-end slot). Promotion was never this plan's gate; the unmade route choice was. Do NOT hand-mint work-items for this plan's items on a source_plan_slug zero -- work_items:create {plan_item} will refuse with duplicate_plan_item where coverage already exists, and that refusal is the correct probe.\n\nFOR LANES PICKING UP FROM HERE\n- Read item state via plans:items {slug, harness:'papercusp'} and trust effectiveStatus (it folds coverage). Never source_plan_slug.\n- P-002 is blocked by P-001 (WI-41067, held). P-003 is WI-41102 (open). P-004..P-018 coverage is UNENUMERATED -- check before filing.\n- Phase 4 now owns the friction-remediation scope; file new tooling-friction items there rather than against the 08-21 plan.\n\n### D-006 — Refill must clamp to the fleet OWN provider measured headroom, not to an available flag\nDate: 2026-08-23\nMeasured 2026-08-23T23:33Z. 8/12 pool accounts are usageWalled with utilization7d=1.00; 4 of the 5 CODEX accounts (this fleet's provider) are hard-walled, the 5th at 0.92 and reading stale. Workspace activity fell from 138 agents/33,105 calls (21:00Z) to 27 agents/3,027 calls (23:00Z). RULING for every item in this plan: (1) A refill or headcount-guarantee mechanism MUST clamp to measured headroom of the fleet's OWN provider. An unclamped refill is how a 7-day quota was consumed in hours, and it is the mechanism that produced the outage this plan was written to prevent. (2) Headroom MUST be read from utilization7d + windowResetAt7d, NEVER from available/usageWalled alone: those are cached, and 11 of 12 rows carried readingStatus 'stale' at measurement time, one of them 136 minutes old with a failing probe. (3) A target-headcount that cannot be met from measured headroom must surface as a stated, owner-visible wall, never as silent under-fill: silent under-fill is indistinguishable from a healthy idle fleet, which is what made this outage invisible for ~2 hours.\n\n### D-007 — Headcount is the wrong control variable for quota exhaustion — burn rate is\nDate: 2026-08-23\nAMENDS the earlier decision of this date (refill must clamp to the fleet's own provider headroom). That ruling stands but is INCOMPLETE, and this trace shows why.\n\nTRACE 2026-08-23T23:40Z, harness_shared.tool_invocations grouped by coord_owner_id.\nPEAK 20:00-21:30Z: owners=133, median lifespan 2,321s, median 313 calls/owner, 49,495 calls, only 23 owners short-lived (<5 min).\nCONTROL 16:00-17:30Z: owners=129, median lifespan 463s, median 83 calls/owner, 21,792 calls, 41 short-lived.\nNew-owner birth rate per hour: 16:00=66, 17:00=44, 18:00=20, 19:00=7, 20:00=22, 21:00=49, 22:00=7, 23:00=10.\n\nWHAT THIS REFUTES: I hypothesised the 21:00Z peak was a runaway refill loop, which would have made unclamped refill the direct cause of the outage. It was not. Agent POPULATION was flat (133 vs 129 in the control) and the 21:00Z new-owner rate (49) was LOWER than 16:00Z (66). There was no spawn storm.\n\nWHAT ACTUALLY BURNED THE QUOTA: per-agent intensity. Median calls per owner rose 83 -> 313 (3.8x) and median lifespan 463s -> 2,321s (5x), for 2.3x the total calls at flat headcount.\n\nRULING: a headcount guarantee, and equally a headcount CLAMP, could not have prevented this outage and will not prevent the next one. Both multipliers of burn are (members x per-member throughput), and this plan governs only the first. Clamping spawns bounds how many agents exist; it does not bound what they spend. Any item in this plan that justifies itself by 'protecting capacity' must state which multiplier it governs, and no item may claim to prevent quota exhaustion on headcount control alone. The missing control — a burn-rate budget against the rolling 7-day window — is filed separately and is NOT in this plan's scope.\n\n### D-008 — Execution route selected under AUTO: keep this plan standalone, bound it against fleet-friction-remediation, promote rather than spawn\nDate: 2026-08-24\nPROVENANCE: selected by su-c1dea4c8 (leader, nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-20260820) under AUTO mode, 2026-08-24T01:45Z. This is a self-selected route DISCLOSED to Avi, NOT an owner directive. Avi's directive was to write the plan; the route was left open and AUTO authorizes me to close it. Reversible on his word.\n\nWHY IT NEEDED CLOSING: two ready plans -- this one and `fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21` (scope APPROVED 2026-08-21, version 34, never started) -- were BOTH gated on the identical sentence, \"Avi selects the execution route.\" Neither was blocked on scope. Waiting was itself the failure this plan diagnoses: delivery, not diagnosis.\n\n(1) WHICH PLAN -- keep `fleet-headcount-guarantee-2026-08-23` STANDALONE. Do NOT fold into fleet-friction-remediation.\nRationale: this plan is already in flight (P-001 held as WI-41067; P-003 covered by WI-41102) while friction-remediation has never started. Folding re-homes LIVE work into a STALLED container -- trading a moving thing for a parked one -- and yields a 31-item mega-plan that is worse for parallel claiming, not better. P-017's fragmentation concern is real but its remedy is a BOUNDARY, not a merger; merging two plans does not reduce 30 plans to a meaningful degree and costs the in-flight state.\n\n(2) THE BOUNDARY (this is the part other lanes must follow):\n- `fleet-headcount-guarantee-2026-08-23` OWNS: operational headcount, the refill loop, and landing already-built-but-undeployed instruments. Its Phases 1-3.\n- `fleet-friction-remediation-2026-08-21` OWNS: contract/result integrity, performance and scope, client guardrails, system proof and ship. Its Phases 1-2 and 4-5.\n- WHERE THEY COLLIDE on fleet truth: this plan's Phase 1 WINS; friction-remediation's Phase 3 (\"Fleet truth and recovery\") DEFERS to it and should cite this decision rather than re-deriving the same fixes. A lane finding itself implementing \"report who is actually working\" belongs to this plan regardless of which plan it claimed from.\n\n(3) WHO EXECUTES -- promote into the claimable pool; do NOT spawn a new fleet.\nAt decision time ~7 members were IDLE with ~34 claimable items available, and the codex pool read 5-of-12 serving with a capacity reading that is BLIND (no refresh path; `accounts:probe-capacity` probes Claude accounts only and takes no provider arg). Adding spawns into that would add contention and cost while the existing idle capacity is the actual unused resource. So: `plans:start` on both plans to promote items via the real promotion path, and let existing capacity pull them. The leader takes the delivery-critical Phase 3 (landing built work) directly, since it is a deploy/gate problem rather than a claimable coding lane.\n\n(4) SAME ROUTE ANSWERS FRICTION-REMEDIATION. Its Next reads \"Avi selects the execution route. After route selection, call plans:start, claim P-001 first...\" -- that selection is hereby made and is identical: plans:start, claim its P-001 first, open only disjoint lanes, respecting the boundary in (2).\n\n(5) FALSIFIER -- what would REVERSE this decision, stated up front so it is checkable rather than defended:\nIf, after promotion, the promoted items sit UNCLAIMED while members remain idle, then the bottleneck is claim-SPEC scope, not headcount or plan structure -- and the correct response is to WIDEN THE SPEC, not to spawn more agents and not to re-merge the plans. (The fleet has already refused claims with `fleet_scope_violation`, so a spec too narrow for these items is a live, not hypothetical, failure mode.) Conversely, if items are claimed promptly and still nothing deploys, the binding constraint is the green gate (P-012) and Phase 3 is the only phase that matters.\n\nNOT DETERMINED HERE: whether the 18 items' coverage is complete. Coverage is a work->plan_item EDGE and is NOT readable from `source_plan_slug` (that column is written only by the plans:start path, so hand-filed covering items read NULL). Do not infer uncovered items from a source_plan_slug zero.\nRelated: P-001, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-017\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fundraise-automation-2026-08-23","title":"Fundraise automation — agent-run investor outreach (the outreach system IS the demo)","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Fundraise automation — agent-run investor outreach (the outreach system IS the demo)\nslug: fundraise-automation-2026-08-23\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-23\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23 (owner-directed, AUTO). 9 of 15 items done; the rest are parked on owner data or named external gates, not silently skipped. Built and green (67 tests, changed files tsc-clean): the `pipeline-deal` registry datatype (generic-kind, no migration needed) carrying stages, tiers, warm path and the outreach-approval record — domain-neutral so sales/BD/hiring reuse it, with people and threads referencing canonical `contact`/`email-message`/`calendar-event` rather than investor-flavoured copies; `libs/papercusp/plugins/fundraise-pipeline/`, a 7-target/7-binding/1-edge trigger pack (research, first touch, reply classification, follow-up ladder, meeting prep, post-meeting, weekly review); `packages/operator-core/lib/fundraise/outreach-approval.ts`, the send-approval gate, which fails CLOSED and binds each approval to a specific draftRef so approval cannot transfer to regenerated content; `pipeline-tiering.ts`, the list rule with no way to represent a tier 3; and the runbook at /internal/docs/agent-insights/running-a-fundraise-on-the-product. THE PACK CANNOT SEND MAIL: it requests gmail.compose and deliberately no gmail.send, so every path ends at a draft — a property of the granted scopes rather than of the agent following instructions, guarded by a test that fails if anyone adds a send scope. Nothing here is armed: every binding ships disarmed and installation arms nothing.\n\n**Next:** OWNER, two things, neither blocked on engineering: (1) supply the actual target names (P-001) and your actual personal network for the intro graph (P-002) — the tiering machinery is built and tested, but no fund list was invented because fabricating fund theses is the worst failure available in this domain; (2) pass live Slack/Gmail acceptance (P-012), the one hard blocker, since every event-driven binding rides live Gmail/Calendar and it needs provider credentials plus a desktop session. P-010/P-011 additionally wait on the byoc-cloud-workspaces lane, and P-013's build-in-public cadence is a content decision. When those clear, arm in this order: install → seed and qualify the list → arm weekly-pipeline-review FIRST so the human review gate exists before the approval queue it governs → research-enrichment → first-touch-outreach → the event-driven reply and meeting bindings last, once drafts are landing and reading well.\n\n## Background\n\nSource: the fleet-leader session's investor-outreach recommendation (2026-08-23), which the owner asked to be written into a plan for review [owner directive, mid-turn 2026-08-23T21:10Z].\n\n**Core insight:** the outreach system IS the demo. A fundraise visibly run by our own agents on the trigger/workflow substrate is a pitch no deck can match — but only if the automation is good, because investors are the most spam-calibrated audience on earth; an automated email that feels automated is negative signal.\n\n**Design principles (standing, non-negotiable):**\n- Agents do ~95% of the work; a human fingerprint stays on every first touch.\n- Never fully unattended: auto-run research, drafting, scheduling, follow-up timing — keep a weekly owner review gate and owner approval on ALL first-touch sends. Drafts never auto-send.\n- Warm intros still dominate venture: the agents' first job is mapping the intro graph, not sending email.\n- A misfire into a Tier-1 partner's inbox is unrecoverable; an agent-run fundraise with the owner's judgment at the edges is impressive.\n\n**Substrate mapping (the flagship bindings are ~80% of a fundraise CRM already):** investor replies → Gmail trigger → classify (interested/pass/later) → update pipeline item → draft response (shipped respond-to-email pattern). No reply after N days → scheduled plan → follow-up draft. Meeting lands → ext:gcal:event-upcoming → meeting-prep brief retargeted at funds. Post-meeting → thank-you draft + materials + next-step item. Pipeline itself → plans plane: one plan per active conversation, Workflows tab as the CRM board, trigger-activity feed as the fundraise log. Container for the pack: the trigger-pack shape shipped as WI-40924.\n\n## Phase 1 — Target list + intro graph (research + drafting; zero spam risk, no gates)\n\n- **P-001** `needs-human` Build the tiered target list (~100–150 targets): Tier 1 = funds/angels with an explicit agent-infra thesis AND a warm path (human-approved everything); Tier 2 = thesis-matched cold (agent-drafted, owner-approved); there is NO Tier 3 — no spray. importance: high — note: Tiering rule BUILT + tested (pipeline-tiering.ts: tier1/tier2, no tier 3 representable, weak+unresearched dropped, assessList warnings). Needs owner: the actual target names — deliberately not fabricated.\n- **P-002** `blocked` Map the intro graph: which contacts in the owner's network touch which fund; draft the forwardable blurb for each connector. Research+drafting workflow only — nothing sends. — note: ← WI-41070 blocked\n- **P-003** `done` Fund-research enrichment step: per-fund brief (portfolio, partners' writing, likely objections) feeding cold-email personalization and meeting prep. — note: plan-fund-research.md + research-enrichment binding; quotes require URLs, weak match drops the target.\n\n## Phase 2 — Fundraise CRM on the existing substrate (~one-plan build on what exists)\n\n- **P-004** `done` Investor-pipeline datatype with stages + the send-approval gate, packaged as the fundraise trigger-pack (container: the WI-40924 trigger-pack shape). importance: high — note: pipeline-deal datatype registered (generic-kind, no migration) + outreach-approval.ts gate (fail-closed, draftRef-bound) + pack. 30 gate tests.\n- **P-005** `done` Binding: investor reply → Gmail trigger → classify (interested/pass/later) → update pipeline item → draft response. Drafts, never auto-send. blocked-by: P-004 — note: plan-classify-reply.md + investor-reply-to-pipeline binding; correlation is the filter, unmatched mail stops the run.\n- **P-006** `done` Binding: no reply after N days → scheduled plan (plans:set-schedule) → polite follow-up draft. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-41074 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Binding: meeting lands on calendar → ext:gcal:event-upcoming → meeting-prep brief retargeted at funds (partners, portfolio, likely objections). blocked-by: P-004 — note: plan-meeting-prep.md + meeting-to-investor-prep binding; adds pipeline history to the shipped prep pattern.\n- **P-008** `done` Binding: post-meeting → thank-you draft + materials + next-step item. blocked-by: P-004 — note: plan-post-meeting.md + internal plan-completed edge; defers execution past the real meeting end.\n- **P-009** `done` Pipeline surfaces: one plan per active investor conversation; the Workflows tab as the CRM board; the trigger-activity feed as the fundraise log. blocked-by: P-004 — note: Convention, not new UI: pipeline-deal is a work_item kind so existing surfaces carry the board. Documented in the runbook.\n\n## Phase 3 — Demo funnel (getting them to try it; gated on the cloud-workspaces lane)\n\n- **P-010** `blocked` Hosted sandbox spectator scenario: pre-seeded cloud workspace — watch a fleet triage a real inbox, watch a Slack mention become a running plan; 10-minute magic moment, nothing to configure. Never ask a VC to install a desktop app cold. External gate: byoc-cloud-workspaces lane must land first. — note: Gated on byoc-cloud-workspaces landing. Spectator content is real (briefs/board/draft history are genuine artifacts, not fixtures).\n- **P-011** `blocked` Own-fundraise workspace as the flagship demo: the pipeline board where the visiting investor IS a row — their fund, the research brief on them, the meeting prep the agent generated before the call. — note: Gated with P-010; the board it demos exists once the list is seeded.\n- **P-012** `blocked` Concierge tier for Tier-1 calls: connect their Gmail/Slack live on the call, arm one trigger, let them watch an email become a drafted reply. First-person magic beats spectator magic. — note: Gated on live Gmail/Slack acceptance — concierge tier arms a trigger on the call.\n- **P-013** `needs-human` Build-in-public cadence: short screen recordings of fleets working, posted on a schedule. (Note: this plan-local P-013 is unrelated to the external live-acceptance gate that happens to share the id in its own plan.) — note: Build-in-public cadence is an owner content decision; nothing to build.\n\n## Phase 4 — Outreach execution (gated on live Slack/Gmail acceptance + explicit owner go)\n\n- **P-014** `done` Cold-email format: one line of genuine agent-researched personalization + one inline link to a live artifact showing the workflow that produced that very email (pipeline board, research notes, draft history). \"This fundraise is being run by the product\" is the hook. blocked-by: P-005 — note: plan-first-touch.md: one sourced observation, one proof link, <150 words, omit-rather-than-estimate; agent writes approval state pending, never approved.\n- **P-015** `done` Standing send-approval + weekly review gate: owner approval on every first-touch send, weekly pipeline review. A policy that persists for the life of the fundraise, not a one-time setup. importance: high — note: plan-weekly-review.md (reports, never approves) + the enforced gate in outreach-approval.ts.\n\n## Open questions (for owner review)\n\n- Tier-1 list seed: who supplies the initial fund/angel names — owner brain-dump, or agent-proposed from public theses for owner curation?\n- N (follow-up delay) and the weekly-review slot: owner preferences.\n- Whether the own-fundraise demo workspace is the production workspace or a sanitized mirror (investor-visible data hygiene).\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"goal-live-holder-guarantee-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — goal live-holder guarantee enforced at the write boundary","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-23","owner":"su-dc9570ff-24ef-4888-8094-2a047d753607","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — goal live-holder guarantee enforced at the write boundary\nslug: goal-live-holder-guarantee-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-dc9570ff-24ef-4888-8094-2a047d753607\n---\n\n# Acceptance — goal live-holder guarantee enforced at the write boundary\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nGraded post-implementation per D-007 against the as-built system. Thesis under test: holder liveness is a PRECONDITION checked where goals are admitted, not a property observed later by a heartbeat/sweep. Criteria trace to the plan's goal and Decisions (D-001 one canonical read; D-008 read-time defaults + the load-bearing P-005-before-P-004 ordering; D-009 the narrowed pause premise) rather than to the shape of the diff.\n\nREVISION 2 (vetting, consult conv-mt64jg9o): rev 1 was authored and graded by the same agent, so it was self-attacked before external critique landed. Two changes. (a) covers-preexisting-goals was WEAK — it graded stored-shape unit tests, so it would have passed even if real rows disagreed with the defaults; its method now requires a census of live goal rows, which on 2026-08-23 returned 19 goals / 18 carrying no holder key / 0 explicit opt-outs, empirically confirming D-008's reasoning that a false default would have covered almost nothing. (b) refusal-is-actionable ADDED: rev 1 graded only that a refusal HAPPENS, never that the caller can act on it — a guarantee enforced by an unhelpful error is a guarantee people route around. KNOWN GAP, deliberately NOT a criterion: none of these grade the guarantee under CONCURRENCY (two claimants racing one goal). That is adjacent to what this plan promised rather than part of it, so it is filed as a separate finding instead of being smuggled in here to fail a ship on out-of-scope work.\n\nREVISION 3 (meta-vetting, criterion prefer-structured-check): seven of the eight criteria gain a kind:'tests' structured check, so their outcome is decided by a run rather than by the grader's prose. Measured before binding them: the 10-file union runs in 11.0s / 375 passed / 0 failed on current staging (box at load 98/128), against emit's 120s shared batched budget — a 9x margin, so this rubric does not inherit the WI-39848 class of ungradeable-by-budget acceptance card. covers-preexisting-goals deliberately keeps NO tests-check: its subject is the live goal population, and a unit-test binding there would restore the rev-1 defect. Nothing else about rev 2 changed — every criterion keeps its full method and replication drill.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"learning-loop-identity-consumption-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — learning loop: stable identity, non-rejecting fold-in-place, and visible consumption","status":"active","created":"2026-08-23","owner":"su-8fc3ac2e-1ddf-403f-848b-3b03ebae2276","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — learning loop: stable identity, non-rejecting fold-in-place, and visible consumption\nslug: learning-loop-identity-consumption-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-23\nowner: su-8fc3ac2e-1ddf-403f-848b-3b03ebae2276\n---\n\n# Acceptance — learning loop: stable identity, non-rejecting fold-in-place, and visible consumption\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nFinal post-implementation acceptance rubric for plan learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08. The plan must give observations and ideas a stable identity, make consumption visible, bound growth without deletion or refusal, and retain an explicit measured harm detector. Governing decisions: D-001; D-003 as amended by D-042; D-043; D-044; D-045.\n\nROLES (v4, per the su-13039d37 retraction of 2026-08-23T00:01Z, which supersedes the v3 role ruling): the implementer/proposer su-8fc3ac2e PROPOSES this rubric, EMITS the meta-acceptance attestation citing the resolved vetting consult conv-mt4x0uev-0000-de2d7070e0fd41da9e184be9f11abfaf (accepted post 76090 by su-13039d37, resolved 2026-08-22T23:59:24.588Z), and later records the implementer acceptance verdict — but NEVER grades acceptance. su-13039d37 is the EXTERNAL CRITIC only: it authored the vetting critique and must not attest or grade. su-08275 grades all eight criteria and emits the single coherent scorecard, superseding its v2 card. The D-043 ratifier (su-3771084b) and the v2 revision serializer (su-d16af7c0) must not grade. RATIONALE, VERIFIED AT THE WRITER: readVettingConsultCritique (packages/operator-core/lib/consult/get-feedback-core.ts:380) counts only consult posts whose author_id is NEITHER the emitter NOR the consult requester. su-8fc3ac2e is the requester of conv-mt4x0uev and su-13039d37 is the responder, so the critique counts for exactly one emitter — su-8fc3ac2e — and an attestation emitted by su-13039d37 would see zero critique posts and be refused. This clause REPLACES the v3 ROLES clause and the v2 GRADER INDEPENDENCE clause, which barred every named party from both attesting and grading and therefore admitted zero eligible actors — the deadlock filed as EI-21197705199224488.\n\nP-016 HONESTY: the advance commitment and the measured post-deploy outcome are separate criteria. The measured-outcome criterion remains unknown until the P-013 fold is deployed and at least seven full post-deploy days exist. UNKNOWN is the only honest pre-clock rating; it is not a pass and does not erase the open P-016/WI-40694 obligation.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"orchestration-surface-residue-drain-2026-08-23","title":"Drain the orchestration-surface residue — 35 fleet-filed defects on code:run, capability:bash*, recipes:*, result-door, functions.exec","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Drain the orchestration-surface residue — 35 fleet-filed defects on code:run, capability:bash*, recipes:*, result-door, functions.exec\nslug: orchestration-surface-residue-drain-2026-08-23\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-012 is done — every actionable item on this plan is now closed. 14 of 16 items terminal. D-009 records the consolidated 8-cluster map (cluster -> root cause -> survivor) plus the ruling that a frozen scope cannot be re-derived by re-running its own defining query. P-012's dedupe pass closed the last 3 filings that were still open and double-counting: EI-21253366598345158 (4th rg filing, survivor EI-21230696318029111) and the canonical timeout-unit pair EI-21244621935918273 + EI-21249688296844162, the latter as fixed-at-source/deploy-blocked (tooldef 92dc13e, proven by facade-types.test.ts:193, unobservable at runtime until the red gate greens).\n\n**Next:** Two items remain, neither actionable solo. P-001 is parked on two sibling EIs held by live peers (su-c8b7263b, su-93b72058) — do not override, re-ask, or re-wake them. P-014 is parked for Avi: per D-006 both halves of its premise are void, and the only residual ask is ONE independent grade, which a self-grade cannot satisfy. One deploy-gated action is carried on EI-21233638670808546: recipes:sweep { ids:['recover-exact-held-checkpoint-spill'] }, dryRun first. Nothing here contests the red green-checkpoint gate, which is peer-claimed on WI-40086.\n\n## Background\n\n`orchestration-runtime-unification-and-safe-output-2026-08-22` closed all 29 of its items `committed` and shipped the replacement execution engine. In parallel, 26 OTHER agents hit defects in those same surfaces while doing unrelated work (`found_during` names WI-40195, WI-40086, WI-40025, WI-40132, WI-40303, WI-40324, WI-40413, WI-40451, WI-40743, WI-40905, WI-40917, GRADE rubric fires, BYOC fleet leadership, self-compaction recovery).
