Also corrected that plan's ## Now, which read \"Plan complete\" and was falsified by the new open item.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The rg filings name the WRONG root cause — ripgrep was never installed; a PATH-only fix does nothing\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23. Established by direct probe, not inference.\n\nAll four rg filings (EI-21267507656500336, EI-21238315448439451, EI-21230696318029111, EI-21253366598345158) describe the cause as \"capability:bash confined shell PATH lacks rg\". That is WRONG, and acting on it would have produced a fix that changes nothing.\n\nMEASURED: there is NO standalone ripgrep binary anywhere on this host. A scan of ~/.cargo/bin, /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin, /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, ~/.local/bin and ~/.papercusp/bin found no rg; the identical scan found /usr/bin/git, so the instrument was sound and the absence is genuine. No ripgrep dpkg package is installed. `type rg` in an interactive shell reports 'rg is a function' — a shell FUNCTION Claude Code defines in the profile, which re-execs the claude binary with argv[0]=rg. The 342MB claude executable embeds ripgrep 14.1.1 (+pcre2); `( exec -a rg $CLAUDE --version )` prints it.\n\nReal cause: ripgrep exists on this host ONLY as an argv[0] dispatch inside the claude binary, reachable via a shell function. Shell functions are NOT exported into a scrubbed `bash -c` child, so every non-interactive caller (capability:bash, code:run, saved recipes, exec-sandbox) correctly failed while the same command worked when a human typed it. The PATH was never the variable.\n\nFIX APPLIED: an `rg` entry point at ~/.local/bin/rg that resolves the claude executable (CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, else the stable ~/.local/bin/claude symlink the installer repoints on upgrade) and `exec -a rg`s it, exiting 127 with a grep/gitnexus pointer if claude is absent. ~/.local/bin is ALREADY on the capability:bash augmented PATH (verified by probing the live tool), so NO operator code change was needed. Verified end-to-end through capability:bash: rg resolves, reports ripgrep 14.1.1, and a real search returned 2 matches against a grep -c control of 2.\n\nRESIDUE: the shim is a HOST file, not in git. It fixes this operator host and does not reproduce on a fresh machine. The durable in-repo half is tracked as P-017. CORRECTION: an earlier revision of this decision, and the three EI completions closed under it, cite \"P-016\" for that follow-up — plans:add-item assigns ids itself and issued P-017. P-016 does not exist on this plan; read P-017 wherever P-016 appears.\n\nGENERAL LESSON for the rest of this drain: a filing's stated root cause is a REPORTER'S HYPOTHESIS, not evidence. Four independent agents agreed on 'PATH lacks rg' and all four were wrong — agreement among reporters who share an assumption is not corroboration. Probe the mechanism before implementing any filing's proposed cause.\n\nRelated: P-002, P-017, orchestration-runtime-unification-and-safe-output-2026-08-22#D-016\n\n### D-002 — D-002: the bash_output/bash_kill \"lost liveness\" cluster is ONE cause — a worker-local JOBS map in a clustered operator — and the read/kill halves are already fixed at source, undeployed behind the red gate\nDate: 2026-08-23\nCORRECTION (19:1xZ, by the author): an earlier revision of this decision listed EI-21268587281908172 among the duplicate reproductions of the cause below. THAT WAS WRONG and is retracted. Its body reads `ptool reported UND_ERR_SOCKET other side closed` on a READ-ONLY status call — an undici socket error, not a worker-local JOBS miss. It is a DIFFERENT, still-unexplained failure and must not be dismissed as deploy-blocked. The three genuine duplicates are EI-21269047456975775, EI-21268717187555755 and EI-21268638266066878, each quoting tracking_lost_process_alive against a task identity-probed ALIVE.\n\nROOT CAUSE (measured, not inferred). The operator runs a MULTI-PROCESS pool: ~7 sibling `hono-host.mjs` workers forked from pid 303461 at 2026-08-23T17:14:58Z. `capability:bash { run_in_background }` records the job in the LAUNCHING worker's process-local `JOBS` Map (`bash-jobs.ts:470`, a bare `new Map()`), and the later `capability:bash_output` / `bash_kill` call is served by a DIFFERENT worker whose Map never had the entry. The lookup misses, the OS process is fine, and the tool reports lost liveness.\n\nDIRECT REPRODUCTION (twice, same connection, no restart):\n- direct foreground call -> worker 306077\n- background launch #1 -> worker 306089; launch #2 -> worker 306056 (the job printed its own parent: `BG-JOB worker=306056`)\n- read 30-60s later -> `ok:false reason:tracking_lost_process_alive`, pid CONFIRMED alive, log still growing.\n\nWHAT THIS REFUTES (each was a filing's or a reader's stated cause):\n- NOT an operator restart: the pool has been up since 17:14:58Z with NRestarts=0, and the newest filings' jobs launched 18:16:21Z and 18:20:36Z, inside that uptime.\n- NOT registry eviction: `pruneFinished()` filters `status !== 'running'`; running jobs are never evicted.\n- NOT a truncated-id mismatch: `cryptoRandomId()` is `randomUUID().slice(0,12)`, used as both the `JOBS.set` key and the returned `bash_id`; `getJob` is a plain `JOBS.get`.\n- NOT an import-specifier module split: every importer of `bash-jobs` uses the identical `'./bash-jobs'`.\n- `pinModuleState` CANNOT fix this. It pins to `globalThis` WITHIN one process; this is a cross-PROCESS split. Anyone reaching for the CLAUDE.md shared-lib-singleton rule will be led astray — bash-jobs.ts:452-455 already invokes that reasoning and calls the registry \"already a pinned singleton\", which is misleading.\n\nDISPOSITION — the running build is the CAUSE OF THE FILINGS, not the current source:\nEvery one was reproduced against `papercup-release` HEAD a2d69cef50 (all workers run `papercup-release/apps/operator/dist-host/hono-host.mjs`), the ~40h-stale build behind the red gate. Staging has moved on:\n- READ path: release returns `ok:false reason:'tracking_lost_process_alive'`; staging returns `ok:true, status:'running', recovered_from_ledger:true, tracking_lost:true` with pid/scope/log/output attached (blob diff release 481426b2 -> staging a4d38a8f). Introduced by 354cd78a95 (2026-08-22T04:12:51Z), which IS in staging and origin/main but NOT in the local `main` the release deploys from.\n- KILL path: release `bash_kill.ts` is 58 lines with NO ledger fallback (`getJob` miss -> `ok:false unknown_bash_id`, job never killed). Staging is 192 lines resolving `getTaskByBashJobId` and using the task-manager cgroup/pid rails — what can stop a surviving Chromium subtree.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR OTHER LANES: this one cause also explains the three duplicates named above. They are already fixed at source: deploy-blocked, not code-blocked, and must NOT be re-implemented.\n\nSTILL GENUINELY OPEN (fixed nowhere until this drain): `bash_output` AND `bash_kill` both rejected `bash_id` + `task_id` together (\"Pass exactly one of bash_id or task_id\", in BOTH release and staging) — EI-21240465530065342. capability:bash HANDS the caller both ids, so passing both back is the natural recovery call, and it sat on the very path agents must use while the read-path fix is undeployed. Fixed in this drain in both tools: at least one handle required; both-supplied resolves through the durable task_id; a bash_id naming a DIFFERENT job is refused as `handle_mismatch`, reading/killing NOTHING.\n\nRESIDUE RESOLVED: EI-21235407864966665 quotes reason `not_live`, which exists in `task-manager/control.ts:247`, NOT in either build of `bash_kill`. That refusal is BY DESIGN (D-010: a terminal/residue row is report-only), with the `reapTerminalResidue` opt-in (WI-37521) re-verifying via `countScopeProcesses` before reaping.\n\nSTANDING RULE (extends D-001): agreement among reporters is not corroboration when they share an assumption, and a symptom reproduced against :3070 is evidence about the DEPLOYED build only. Diff the release blob against staging FIRST — twice today that alone was the whole answer. And read each sibling's BODY before folding it into a cluster: three of these four matched, one did not.\n\n### D-003 — A result-door spill's byte offset is a LOCATOR, not a completeness promise — emit it always, name it per byte-stream\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRuling made under P-005 (WI-41032). Governs `packages/operator-core/lib/result-door.ts` and anything consuming a spill recovery cursor. **This SUPERSEDES the contract taken from EI-21185758364267344** (done), which is why it is recorded here rather than in a message.\n\n#### The two facts that were conflated\n\nA spill cursor carries two orthogonal facts about the JSON body:\n\n1. **WHERE the body starts** — a byte fact. Always knowable, always safe to state.\n2. **WHETHER the body is a complete population** — a semantic fact about what the tool serialized.\n\nThe previous rule withheld fact 1 whenever fact 2 was false (`result-door.ts:856`, guard `parsedJsonBody && !partialJsonBody`). EI-21185758364267344's actual complaint was that the cursor *promised exact spill bytes* while the body had stopped at an 11-of-22 record clipping marker — i.e. it objected to fact 2 being misstated. Removing the **locator** did not address that; it removed a true statement to stop a false one.\n\n#### Why the withholding actively caused harm\n\nWithholding the offset never stopped anyone parsing those bytes — it pushed them onto the only remaining strategy, \"start at the first `{`\". A manifest-bearing spill's first `{` is the **scratch-reference manifest at byte 31**, not the body. So the fallback returns a **well-formed but WRONG object**: a silent wrong answer where the previous state of the world gave a loud failure. That is strictly worse, and it is what EI-21208128396414381 and EI-21202588767992062 hit (the latter's \"non-JSON footer, jq Invalid numeric literal at line 3\" was not a footer at all — it parsed the manifest on line 2, then hit the `# result-door spill` HEADER on line 3).\n\n#### The second, independent defect: one offset, two byte streams\n\n`bodyByteOffset` was measured against the RAW on-disk file (manifest header included), but the cursor's own `next` instructs the caller to fetch the body via `capability:read`, and `read.ts:189-204` sets `bytes = parsed.payload` — stripping the manifest **before** `byte_offset` is applied. Following the cursor exactly therefore overshot by the ~450-byte manifest header and landed mid-body. That is EI-21239097430071791, and it is a defect of *naming*: a single unqualified field cannot be correct for two streams.\n\n#### The rule\n\n1. **Emit the locator for every valid JSON body**, including a tool-internally clipped one.\n2. **Name each offset for the stream it measures.** `bodyOffsetInPayload` (within `capability:read`'s `response.data`) and `bodyOffsetInFile` (within the raw file at `args.file_path`). Never reintroduce a bare, stream-agnostic `bodyByteOffset`.\n3. **Carry incompleteness as its own machine-readable field** — `bodyComplete: false` — never as the ABSENCE of another field. An absence is indistinguishable from \"this door emitted nothing\", so it cannot be branched on.\n4. The honesty wording on the partial path stays: the offset must never read as a promise that paging recovers omitted records.\n\n#### Generalization (apply beyond this file)\n\n**Never signal one fact by suppressing a different, true one.** A reader cannot distinguish a deliberate suppression from an absent capability, so suppression degrades into a guess — and a guess that happens to parse is worse than an error. If a value needs a caveat, ship the value *and* the caveat as separate named fields.\n\n#### Falsifiability\n\n`result-door-encoding-contract.test.ts` now keeps two permanent CONTROLS that reproduce the original defect: the file-relative offset applied to the payload stream must still `toThrow()`, and the first-brace fallback must still yield the manifest (`schemaVersion`, no `rows`). If either control ever starts succeeding, the two offsets have collapsed back into one and the guards have stopped discriminating.\n\n### D-004 — A test that pins an implementation's internal constant hides the defect that constant causes — assert the budget, not the rung\nDate: 2026-08-23\nCONTEXT. P-006 fixed `shapeCodeRunSummary` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/code/run.ts). Fixing it required CHANGING an existing passing assertion, which is normally the move that should stop an agent. Recording why it was correct here, because the general shape recurs.\n\nTHE ASSERTION. run.test.ts asserted `payload.summary.lines.every(line => line.length <= 360)`. 360 was not a contract. It was `CODE_RUN_SUMMARY_PROJECTION_STEPS[0].stringChars` — an internal rung constant of the projection ladder — copied into the test as a literal.\n\nWHY IT WAS ACTIVELY HARMFUL. The ladder returns the FIRST rung that fits the 3,500-char budget and then stops, so it never spends the remainder. Measured: a caller-bounded 5,000-char tail came back at 381 chars — 10.9% of the budget it was entitled to. The test asserted `<= 360` and PASSED on that. The assertion did not merely fail to catch the defect; it PINNED it, and would have failed on any fix. A green test stood guard over a 9x under-delivery for as long as the constant matched.\n\nTHE RULING. When a test asserts a bound, assert the bound the SYSTEM promises, derived from the same source the code reads — not the intermediate constant the implementation happens to use to reach it. Here: the summary must fit CODE_RUN_SUMMARY_CHAR_BUDGET, and must USE it (>75%). The constant is now exported so the test derives the number rather than restating it; a budget change moves both together and cannot drift. This is the derived-truth ladder (CLAUDE.md) applied to assertions: DERIVE the expected value, do not hand-maintain a second copy of it.\n\nTHE TELL, for reuse by other lanes. A bound-assertion whose literal equals an implementation constant is a review smell. Ask what the value would be if the code were CORRECT rather than merely current; if the assertion would fail on the fix, it is pinning the bug. The specific class to watch: a ladder/tier/rung that picks the first option that fits, with the fit measured against a budget the rungs know nothing about. That structure silently under-delivers by design, and any test written against a rung will certify it.\n\nCOROLLARY (applied here). Every assertion changed this way must be paired with a CONTROL proving the replacement can still fail — the pre-fix shape is reproduced in the test and asserted to violate the new assertions. Without that, \"I changed the test and it passed\" is indistinguishable from weakening it. P-006 added 2 controls plus a calibration case (a summary under budget must stay byte-identical), so the new assertions cannot pass vacuously.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-005 — A structural-error auto-resolution is NOT evidence for a filing whose symptom is not a telemetered error\nDate: 2026-08-23\nFINDING. P-007's two filings (EI-21163938645109933, EI-21164455886001541) arrived already terminal, closed by terminal_owner='structural-error-verifier' with the stock rationale: \"code:run has emitted no error in the deployed operator's telemetry for >=6h, so the structural error is fixed on the deployed sha.\" I reproduced both filed behaviours live on current source, unchanged, AFTER that close. Both auto-resolutions are false.\n\nWHY, STRUCTURALLY — this is the part that generalises. A code:run fieldMiss is an ADVISORY attached to a SUCCESSFUL call: the envelope is `ok: true` plus `fieldMissHelp`. It is never a telemetered error. So the verifier's evidence — absence of errors over a 6h window — is INCAPABLE of observing this class of filing. It did not get unlucky; its signal cannot bear on the claim, and it would have closed these two whether or not anyone fixed them. An auto-resolution of this shape is therefore indistinguishable from a no-op, while reading as a verified close.\n\nTHE RULING, for any lane that encounters one. Before treating a `structural-error-verifier` close as evidence, ask whether the filing's SYMPTOM is something that surfaces as a tool ERROR. If the symptom is an advisory, a wrong-but-successful value, noise, a shape complaint, or anything else the call reports with ok:true, the auto-resolution carries NO evidential weight — re-verify by reproduction before relying on it, and re-open if the behaviour persists. The verifier remains legitimate for its DESIGNED population: watchdog-filed structural errors that genuinely appear in telemetry.\n\nSCOPE OF THE CLAIM — deliberately bounded, do not inflate it. terminal_owner='structural-error-verifier' has closed 1255 items in this workspace (516 nit / 739 non-nit), 165 inside this drain's window, with 0 ever reopened. I VERIFIED EXACTLY TWO as false. The remaining 1253 are UNMEASURED. The correct statement is \"the premise is invalid for a subclass, and two closes in that subclass are proven false\", NOT \"1255 false closes\". Anyone quoting this decision must carry that boundary with it; the 0-reopen figure is the reason the population deserves a sampled audit, not the reason to condemn it wholesale.\n\nMETHOD NOTE, because it nearly cost me the finding. My first attempt to size the population returned a confident 0 for rows I already knew existed: engineer_issues has NO harness_slug column (it lives inside the payload jsonb) and its `scope` is not the harness slug, so my predicate silently matched nothing. A positive control on the two known ids exposed it. Size this population with terminal_owner='structural-error-verifier', not a LIKE against the rationale prose, and never accept a zero here without a control — the whole point of this decision is a mechanism that reports absence as if it were proof.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-006 — P-014's premise is void on both halves: no bespoke rubric is missing, and the grade it was meant to gate has already been passed\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-014 reads: \"Author the missing acceptance rubric for the orchestration plan and obtain an INDEPENDENT grade (a self-grade never satisfies the gate) so it can reach `shipped`.\" Both halves were checked against live state before doing any of the work, and both fail.\n\nHALF 1 — \"the missing acceptance rubric\" is a MISFILING, not a gap.\n`rubrics:list` returns 38 rubrics, of which FOUR carry characteristic `plan-acceptance`, all status active: plan-class-migration (5 criteria), plan-class-investigation (5), plan-class-feature-ship (6), plan-class-bugfix (5). The convention here is a SHARED plan-class rubric applied to a plan, not a bespoke rubric authored per plan. So there is nothing to author; authoring a fifth, plan-specific rubric would duplicate an existing surface and is exactly the reuse-first smell. (`rubrics:search` for the plan's own words returns count 0 — which is consistent with the shared-rubric convention, and is NOT evidence a bespoke one is required.)\n\nHALF 2 — the gate it was meant to open is ALREADY OPEN.\norchestration-runtime-unification-and-safe-output-2026-08-22 is frontmatter status `shipped`, with 29/29 items done (counts {done:29}, nonDone []). `forcedPast` is null, so it was not force-shipped past a rubric gate — it simply reached shipped without one. Therefore an acceptance grade can no longer gate anything on that plan; the only remaining value is a retrospective acceptance RECORD.\n\nWHY THIS IS NOT SOMETHING I CAN CLOSE AS DONE.\nThe one genuinely-missing artifact is an INDEPENDENT grade, and the item's own text rules out the only grade I can produce: a self-grade never satisfies it, and `blender:grade-idea` refuses a self-grade by construction. This drain is SOLO by explicit owner choice (Avi declined every fleet route), so I cannot spawn a grader, and conscripting a live peer mid-lane to perform a retrospective grade on an already-shipped plan is not worth a peer's context.\n\nDISPOSITION: P-014 → needs-human, with a small precise ask rather than a vague one. If an acceptance record is still wanted for that shipped plan, the ask is one grade against an EXISTING shared rubric — my read is `plan-class-feature-ship` (it shipped behavior changes across the tool runtime), with `plan-class-bugfix` the alternative if the grader reads the 29 items as defect repair. No authoring required. If no retrospective record is wanted, the item should be dropped rather than done — I have deliberately not made that call, because \"is a retrospective acceptance record worth having\" is a judgment about process value, not a fact I can verify.\nRelated: P-014\n\n### D-007 — functions.exec IS client-supplied (P-009 answered) — but \"resolved-by-D-017-disable\" is FALSE: the disable is deliberately unactivated, so the cluster dedupes to 3 live trackers rather than closing 11\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-009 ANSWERED — client-supplied, not editable. Per the chartered boundary map (/internal/docs/agent-insights/orchestration-runtime-boundary-and-reuse-map, authored by WI-40674 for the sibling plan's P-001), the ownership row reads verbatim: \"Codex functions.exec | Codex client | No | A sealed V8 isolate supplied by the client. It evaluates JavaScript outside this repository; `typeof process` is `undefined`. Papercusp cannot patch the isolate or account for bytes that remain entirely inside it.\" So no fix to this cluster can be authored in this workspace. Read, not re-derived, as P-009 instructed.\n\nBUT P-010'S PRESCRIBED CONCLUSION DOES NOT FOLLOW. P-010 says: \"If client-supplied, they are resolved-by-D-017-disable.\" That inference silently assumes the D-017 disable is IN FORCE. It is not, and this was checked three independent ways:\n(1) D-017's own text is conditional — the disable holds \"once three preconditions hold, AND NOT BEFORE\" (parity / steering / safety).\n(2) No enforcement exists in code. `libs/flags/src/types.ts` has no flag governing a native-code-exec disable (positive control: KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS greps fine in the same tree, so the instrument was not blind). A repo-wide search for functions.exec across packages/libs/apps/orchestrator/scripts finds it ONLY in dev/code_run_adoption.ts (telemetry), orchestration-benchmark-corpus.ts (the P-002 corpus + client-residue classifier), and run-script.ts (\"functions.exec compatibility helpers\"). There is no deny-list analogue to orchestrator/src/no-subagent-deny.ts.\n(3) DECISIVE, from the record rather than from absence: WI-40722 — the work-item that closed the sibling plan's P-026 \"Staged disable\" — carries completion evidence stating verbatim that \"the managed cross-client native script-execution disable REMAINS UNACTIVATED because the attributed P-020 safety window has not qualified\", with residue \"Activation remains intentionally deferred until an attributed P-020 window reports acceptance=qualified/action=advance with all hard invariant counts zero\" and notChecked \"Activating the native disable, explicitly forbidden by D-054 until qualification\". P-026 was closed as a TIMING DISPOSITION, not as a shipped disable.\n\nSo functions.exec is still live for managed agents today, and closing 10 open defect reports as \"resolved by a disable\" that is explicitly deferred would erase live evidence about a door that is still open — the exact under-evidenced close the drain contract forbids.\n\nTHE CLUSTER IS ALSO NOT ONE ROOT CAUSE. P-010 calls it \"all one suspected root cause\"; reading the summaries, it is three:\nA. Template-literal EAGER INTERPOLATION — the JS isolate expands ${...} / backticks / delimiters before exec_command sees them (EI-21189761275425673 SURVIVOR, plus EI-21221294126002583, EI-21203278260564343, EI-21197472621405959, EI-21177009672496283, EI-21166104872073167, EI-21198226293077464; EI-21165382168319956 already resolved).\nB. JS STRING QUOTING — an inner quote terminates the JavaScript string and the whole wrapper dies with a SyntaxError before any nested tool runs (EI-21171829542040618 SURVIVOR, plus EI-21202198335487407).\nC. SESSION-HANDLE LOSS — not an interpolation or quoting bug at all: the wrapper emitted only result.output, discarding the returned session_id after a 30s exec_command yield, so the remaining command could not be resumed (EI-21199204366845711, stands alone). This one is a CALLER-PATTERN defect, fixable by the caller today, and its own summary already records the correct pattern.\n\nRULING. Dedupe within each class only — 7 confirmed duplicates close against their class survivor. The 3 survivors stay LIVE, marked blocked on the D-017 activation gate (itself gated on a qualifying P-020 window), not closed. Net effect 11 filings → 3 trackers, with no live defect erased. Do NOT re-close these citing D-017 until an attributed P-020 window qualifies and the disable actually ships.\nRelated: P-009, P-010\n\n### D-008 — Recipe-corpus hygiene: never widen the sweep heuristic to reach one recipe; a stale one-off is not a bug\nDate: 2026-08-23\nSettled while disposing P-011's four stale-recipe filings. Two rules, both measured, that apply to ANY future recipe-hygiene or stale-recipe filing.\n\nRULE 1 — NEVER lower staleDays/raise maxRunCount to reach a specific recipe.\n`recipes:sweep` is criteria-only (status='active' AND run_count <= maxRunCount AND last_run_at < now()-staleDays); it has no id targeting. Measured on this corpus 2026-08-23: staleDays 30 (the default) => 0 candidates; staleDays 7 => 6,703; staleDays 1 => 9,544. The oldest last_run_at in the whole corpus is ~29 days, which is why the default matches nothing. So \"just lower staleDays a bit\" to retire one known-broken recipe silently retires 6,700-9,500 unrelated ones. If you need one specific recipe gone, use the targeted `ids` path (added under P-011; see RULE 3) — never the heuristic.\n\nRULE 2 — A never-reused stale recipe is NOT a defect worth repairing; the scheduled routine already owns it.\n`recipeHygieneTick` (packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/periodic-workflows.ts:1108, crontab '0 30 5 * * 0' = weekly Sun 05:30 UTC, default ON, kill-switch PAPERCUSP_RECIPE_HYGIENE=0) calls runRecipeHygieneOnce -> sweepRecipes with DEFAULT params. Any recipe with runCount <= 1 is therefore retired automatically once it crosses 30 days. Filing \"recipe X is stale against current result shapes\" for such a recipe, and then repairing its field reads, is work with no consumer. Close those as no-fix-warranted citing this decision plus the recipe's measured runCount, and say WHEN the routine will take it.\n  BUT the predicate is runCount <= 1, so a recipe with runCount >= 2 is NEVER swept by the routine no matter how old it gets. Check runCount before you claim automation covers it. That check is exactly what split P-011's four filings: EI-21242333311402679 (runCount 1) and EI-21158792512116462 (runCount 1) closed under this rule; EI-21233638670808546 (runCount 2) did not and needed the targeted retire.\n\nRULE 3 — a recipe with bindingSchema:null can never be made parameterisable in place.\nrecipes/revise.ts writes `script` only and never touches bindingSchema; code-recipes-store.ts:214 refuses a bindingSchema without a capabilityManifest; recipe-contract.ts:359-364 rejects non-empty bindings when schema===undefined (`binding_schema_required`). So \"repair the recipe by adding a binding\" is not reachable by any agent-facing verb — the honest dispositions are retire, or re-author as a new recipe with a contract. P-011 added `ids` to recipes:sweep (store + tool + 3 integration tests, lint:tsc clean, 23/23 green) to make the retire half expressible; it bypasses staleDays/maxRunCount but keeps status='active' and adds an explicit promoted_tool IS NULL rail, and reports every id it did not retire in `skipped` with a reason, so a typo'd id can never read as a successful no-op.\n\nMETHOD NOTE (why this decision exists at all): three of P-011's four assessed dispositions were wrong, and each was caught only by reading the writer instead of the label. The sweep plan died on the measured blast radius above; the \"add a binding\" plan died in recipe-contract.ts; and the \"presence result drift\" diagnosis was one field (`label`) that does not exist on the raw row at all — the raw key is `ownerLabel`, and `label` is only the TOON RENDERED column header. Reading a script against a rendered view rather than the raw object produces a field that was never there. Same wrong-depth class as recipes:get results[].recipe vs results[].runCount.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-009 — The consolidated cluster → root-cause → survivor map, and why a frozen scope cannot be re-derived by re-running its own defining query\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23. Closes P-012. The ONE place the drain's cluster mapping lives; references D-001..D-008 rather than restating them.\n\n#### The map — 8 clusters, 38 named filings\n\n| # | cluster | items | root cause | survivor / disposition |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `recipes:get` ReferenceError | P-001 | defect in a shipped tool | 3 filings. EI-21240252527666257 closed. EI-21244835029001612 + EI-21251761121852782 PEER-HELD (su-c8b7263b, su-93b72058) — deliberately NOT overridden or re-woken. |\n| 2 | `rg` unavailable to non-interactive callers | P-002, P-017 | **D-001** — ripgrep never installed; rg was an argv[0] dispatch via a shell FUNCTION, which a scrubbed `bash -c` child does not inherit. The filings' own \"PATH lacks rg\" cause was wrong. | 4 filings, class survivor **EI-21230696318029111** (earliest). 3 closed under D-001; the 4th (EI-21253366598345158) was still open and double-counting — closed here. Durable half = P-017. |\n| 3 | `bash_output` loses liveness | P-003 | **D-002** — worker-local JOBS-map locality | 3 filings, all done |\n| 4 | result-door spill unparseable | P-005 | **D-003** — a spill's byte offset is a LOCATOR, not a completeness promise | 5 filings done. 4 more share this cause but are OUT of frozen scope: sweep against D-003, don't re-investigate. |\n| 5 | `capability:bash.timeout` unit invisible | P-004 | Schema was already correct (ms `.describe()` since 2026-06-13, 44f738fe). Unit lost in **code:tools' facade RENDERING**, which projected field TYPES and dropped descriptions. | EI-21224388159140296 dropped/deprecated; canonical pair EI-21244621935918273 + EI-21249688296844162 closed here as FIXED AT SOURCE (tooldef 92dc13e, argDocs `@param` renderer), DEPLOY-BLOCKED. |\n| 6 | `code:run` clipping / false field-miss / 30s vs batch hint | P-006–P-008 | **D-004** — a test pinning an internal constant hides the defect that constant causes | 5 filings, all terminal |\n| 7 | `functions.exec` template literals | P-009, P-010 | **D-007** — client-supplied, but \"resolved-by-D-017-disable\" is not a valid close while that disable is unactivated | 11 → 3 live trackers. 7 duplicates closed against class survivors; EI-21199204366845711 closed separately (different root cause); **EI-21189761275425673** (class A) + **EI-21171829542040618** (class B) stay blocked on the D-017 gate — correct, not residue. |\n| 8 | stale saved recipes | P-011 | **D-008** — never widen the sweep heuristic to reach one recipe | 1 repaired, 2 dropped (recipeHygiene retires at 30d), EI-21233638670808546 BLOCKED carrying the drain's one deploy-gated action (`recipes:sweep { ids:['recover-exact-held-checkpoint-spill'] }`, dryRun first). |\n\nNon-cluster: P-013 (`## Now` corrected), P-014 (needs-human; **D-006** voids both halves of its premise), P-015 (WI-40973 routed to ox-alpha-omp-integration).\n\n#### What P-012 changed\n\nThree filings were confirmed duplicates/canonicals still sitting OPEN and double-counting. All three now `done`/committed: EI-21253366598345158, EI-21244621935918273, EI-21249688296844162. Every other named filing is terminal or deliberately non-terminal for a recorded reason (peer-held ×2, D-017-gated ×2, deploy-gated ×1).\n\n#### RULING: a frozen scope cannot be re-derived by re-running its own defining query\n\nReplaying \"36 open, non-observation work-items filed since 2026-08-22T12:00Z on the orchestration surfaces\" does NOT return the frozen set. Three independent reasons, all hit before getting it right:\n\n1. **\"open\" was evaluated AT the freeze instant** — items open then are terminal now; the predicate silently re-evaluates.\n2. **The window is open-ended forward** — 35 at freeze, ~80 by 22:4xZ, the excess being peers' filings made minutes ago. Closing one as a \"drain duplicate\" would destroy another agent's fresh work.\n3. **\"orchestration surfaces\" was a SEMANTIC judgement, not a column** — no predicate exists; reproducing the window without it returns the whole fleet's filings.\n\nA fourth trap is mechanical and silent: **`item_kind <> 'observation'` is NOT the observation filter.** Observations are `lane='observation'`; filtering on item_kind admitted hundreds of agents' end-of-turn notes into what looked like a residue list. Use `work_items:list { includeObservations:false }` or predicate on `lane`.\n\n**The reliable reconstruction is the plan's own item texts** — each P-NNN names its cluster's EIs (37), plus the 4th rg filing named only in D-001 = the 38 audited here. That set is stable because it was WRITTEN DOWN at freeze rather than re-measured. Generalisation: a scope defined by a live query is frozen only if you materialise the id list at freeze time; otherwise it is a moving target wearing a fixed number.\n\nRelated: D-001..D-004, D-006..D-008; P-001 (parked), P-014 (owner-gated).\n\n### D-010 — P-014 dropped: no retrospective acceptance record will be produced, because the grade can gate nothing and no artifact is missing\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24\nResolves the disposition D-006 deliberately left open. D-006 established that both halves of P-014's premise are void; it stopped short of deciding whether a retrospective acceptance record is worth having, calling that \"a judgment about process value, not a fact I can verify\", and routed it to the human. Under the owner's standing AUTO grant that judgment is mine to make and disclose, so I am making it rather than leaving the item parked indefinitely.\n\nDECISION: drop P-014. Do not author a rubric, do not obtain a retrospective grade.\n\nREASONING (all three must hold, and all three do):\n1. NOTHING IS MISSING. The convention here is a SHARED plan-class rubric applied to a plan, not a bespoke per-plan rubric. Four plan-acceptance rubrics exist and are active. Authoring a fifth, plan-specific one is the reuse-first smell — a new parallel surface duplicating an existing one.\n2. THE GRADE CAN GATE NOTHING. orchestration-runtime-unification-and-safe-output-2026-08-22 is already frontmatter `shipped`, 29/29 items done, with `forcedPast: null` — it was NOT force-shipped past a rubric gate; it simply reached shipped without one. A grade applied now is downstream of the only decision it could have informed.\n3. THE RECORD HAS NO CONSUMER. Nothing reads a retrospective acceptance grade on an already-shipped plan. Producing one costs a live peer's context (the only way to satisfy the independence requirement, since a self-grade never satisfies the gate and blender:grade-idea refuses one by construction) and returns a row nothing queries.\n\nWHAT THIS IS NOT. This is not a claim that acceptance rubrics are low value in general — applied BEFORE a plan ships, gating it, they do real work. The defect here is one of sequencing: P-014 asked for a gate artifact after the gate had already been passed. That is the generalizable lesson, and it is why the correct disposition is `dropped` rather than `done`: nothing was accomplished, and recording it as done would falsely assert that an acceptance record exists.\n\nREVERSIBILITY. D-006 preserves the complete analysis permanently, including the exact ask should anyone want it later: one grade against an existing shared rubric, `plan-class-feature-ship` being my read (`plan-class-bugfix` the alternative if a grader reads the 29 items as defect repair). Reopening costs one status flip. Nothing is destroyed by this drop.\n\nThis makes the plan 16/16 terminal: 15 done, 1 dropped.\nRelated: P-014\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"ox-alpha-omp-integration-2026-08-23","title":"Integrate Ox Alpha through OMP as an experimental Papercusp model tier","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Integrate Ox Alpha through OMP as an experimental Papercusp model tier\nslug: ox-alpha-omp-integration-2026-08-23\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-23\n---\n\n# Integrate Ox Alpha through OMP as an experimental Papercusp model tier\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001..P-003 are done: the ox-alpha tier is configured, model-tier context-window resolution is fixed for provider-qualified selectors, and a tracked non-confidential canary verified model selection + repository read. A FOURTH item was added 2026-08-23 and is open, so this plan is no longer complete: P-004 routes in the owner-asked `omp update` + canary re-verify (WI-40973, open and unassigned), which had been swept into orchestration-surface-residue-drain-2026-08-23 by a keyword match on \"canary\" and does not belong to that drain (its D-006-adjacent P-015 routes it here). Working canary recipe = `omp -p` one-shot with the coord extension. Known residue, harmless: dead 0-turn sessions 17128/17129 left by failed `psu --headless nohup` attempts.\n\n**Next:** P-004 — run `omp update`, then re-run the ox-alpha canary via the P-002 recipe and confirm model selection + repository read still pass on the upgraded CLI. Unassigned; WI-40973 tracks it.\n\n## Background\n\nOx Alpha is already present in OMP 17.3.5's bundled OpenRouter catalog and the current host has an OpenRouter credential. Papercusp accepts provider-qualified OMP model specs. The missing product work is to expose a reversible experimental tier and prove the tracked Papercusp tool path without sending confidential workspace content.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- The workspace model-tier menu contains exactly one tier named `ox-alpha` with backend `omp`, spec `openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha:max`, and a 400,000-token soft compaction limit.\n- Every pre-existing tier remains byte-for-byte equivalent in name, spec, backend semantics, guidance, and compaction limit; no default tier is replaced.\n- A post-write `config:tiers-get` resolves Ox Alpha to its advertised 1,048,576-token window and keeps the requested soft limit valid.\n- A tracked Papercusp OMP canary starts on Ox Alpha, lists repository paths without reading source content, calls at least one Papercusp read-only MCP tool, and reports the selected model.\n- Canary prompts and tool results contain no secrets, personal data, confidential source, or other sensitive workspace content.\n- The rollback is the exact pre-change tier array captured immediately before the write.\n\n## Design\n\nReuse the existing model-tier registry and OMP OpenRouter provider; add no provider adapter, model YAML, or parallel configuration surface. Immediately before mutation, read `config:tiers-get`, copy its stored tier rows, append one `ox-alpha` row, and pass the complete array to the replace-wholesale `config:tiers-set` API. Verify by re-reading the same registry.\n\nExercise the real tracked launch path with one bounded canary process as the system under test, not as a delegated implementation worker. Use the exact OMP selector and a non-confidential prompt limited to path listing plus a harmless Papercusp state/catalog read. Capture launch identity, model evidence, tool evidence, and terminal disposition. Keep the existing tier array as the one-call rollback payload.\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n## Phase 1 — Configure and verify\n\n- **P-001** `done` Append an experimental OMP model tier named ox-alpha using openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha:max while preserving the existing tier menu and defaults. importance: high blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-40914 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Run a tracked non-confidential Ox Alpha canary through Papercusp and verify model selection, repository read access, and at least one Papercusp MCP read call; record evidence and rollback. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: Canary green via one-shot omp -p on openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha:max; evidence WI-40915.\n- **P-003** `done` Fix model-tier context-window resolution for OMP catalog models so provider-qualified selectors retain safe compaction limits and UI/config round-trips preserve the resolved window. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-40918 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `todo` Run `omp update` to upgrade the OMP CLI, then re-run the ox-alpha tier canary (the P-002 recipe: `omp -p` one-shot with the coord extension) and confirm model selection + repository read still pass on the upgraded CLI. Owner-asked (Avi, 2026-08-23). Tracked as WI-40973. Routed here from orchestration-surface-residue-drain-2026-08-23 P-015: it matched that drain scope only on the word \"canary\" and is ox-alpha integration work, not orchestration residue.\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Ox Alpha remains experimental and non-confidential\nDate: 2026-08-23\nUse the existing OMP OpenRouter provider and exact selector openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha:max. Do not replace standard/deep defaults. Canary inputs must contain no repository source, secrets, personal data, or other confidential content because the anonymous Stealth provider terms permit retention and conflict on training use. Keep the existing model tiers as the immediate rollback.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"papercusp-agentic-webapp-template-2026-08-23","title":"papercusp-agentic-webapp — the agentic WEB app template (web twin of papercusp-agentic-desktop-app)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: papercusp-agentic-webapp — the agentic WEB app template (web twin of papercusp-agentic-desktop-app)\nslug: papercusp-agentic-webapp-template-2026-08-23\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-23\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001..P-005 DONE 2026-08-23 (su-945ad, owner-approved route: self). The papercusp-agentic-webapp root exists and is fully pinned: templates/papercusp-agentic-webapp/ (template.yaml + listing.json + GUIDE + checks + reference + vendored template-kit), machine twin AGENTIC_WEBAPP_TEMPLATE in @papercusp/template-kit, templates/README.md updated (six app roots). Evidence: kit suite 81/81 incl. the yaml↔twin/dir-census/GUIDE-lint pins; operator-core template guards 43/43; tsc clean; compose probe over the real 18-dir set green for all 6 app roots (see D-002 for the advisory tauri-shell affinity finding; D-003 for the new vendored-kit sync script scripts/sync-template-kit-vendored.mjs — run it after any canonical kit edit). Changes are in the staging tree awaiting git-sync + the green gate; live templates:list shows the 18th root after the next deploy.\n\n**Next:** P-006 (owner-gated): push the public templates mirror (npm run mirror:check → mirror:push) once the owner says go. Downstream: calendar-app-papercusp-2026-08-23 + email-app-2026-08-23 materialize FROM this template.\n\n## Background\n[owner: 2026-08-23] Create a papercusp agentic web-app template that mimics papercusp-agentic-desktop-app but uses papercusp-webapp as the base instead of the desktop template. The design is already anticipated by papercusp-webapp's template.yaml: \"an agentic web app layers papercusp-ops-pots onto this the way papercusp-agentic-desktop-app layers onto papercusp-desktop-app.\" This template is the materialization root for the upcoming email/calendar apps (see calendar-app-2026-08-23, email-app-2026-08-23). Reference structure: templates/papercusp-agentic-desktop-app/ (template.yaml, listing.json, GUIDE.md, checks/composition-integrity.test.ts, reference/, template-kit/).\n\n## Phase 1\n- **P-001** `done` Author templates/papercusp-agentic-webapp/: template.yaml (scope app, category app; requires papercusp-webapp@0.1.0 + papercusp-ops-pots@0.1.0 — webapp closure already brings web-host + data-layer + ui; composesWith data-sync/search; decisionPoints: domain + tenancy carried up + optional-planes; musts mirroring agentic-desktop: walk-decision-points, honor-closure-musts, mechanical-validation), listing.json, GUIDE.md adapted from agentic-desktop for the web-host chassis, reference/ worked example. — note: ← WI-40795 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Machine twin AGENTIC_WEBAPP_TEMPLATE in @papercusp/template-kit src/reference-templates.ts, suite-pinned yaml↔twin the same way the other app roots are. blocked-by: P-001 — note: AGENTIC_WEBAPP_TEMPLATE added to canonical reference-templates.ts + REFERENCE_TEMPLATES; suite-pinned (templates-dir.test.ts 7/7); tsc 0 errors\n- **P-003** `done` checks/composition-integrity.test.ts: composeTemplates closure resolves (pins consistent, exactly one root app scope) and the union of the closure's checks is the CI gate. blocked-by: P-001 — note: checks/composition-integrity.test.ts byte-identical to the other roots; compose probe over real 18-dir set: all 6 app roots compose OK, agentic-webapp union=11 checks\n- **P-004** `done` Register the new root everywhere the existing three app roots are registered (sidecar templates bundle papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/sidecar/templates/, any listing/manifest/census that enumerates app-scope roots); verify templates:list serves it and templates:get-guide returns the GUIDE. blocked-by: P-001 — note: sidecar bundling is build-time-generic (build-desktop-sidecar.sh copies all of templates/); listing.json in place; templates/README.md table + six-roots prose updated; live templates:list shows 18 after next deploy (release checkout serves its own tree). Public mirror = P-006\n- **P-005** `done` Acceptance: template-kit suite + composition checks green, scoped typecheck on touched packages; verify papercusp-ops-pots composes onto the web chassis with no desktop-only assumption (record any found as plan decisions); confirm the app-root count everywhere it is asserted (WI-36053 precedent: scope:\"app\" root counts are pinned in tests). blocked-by: P-002 — note: kit suite 81/81, operator-core cupboard guards 43/43 + template-docs-slugs 3/3, tsc clean, sync-script --check clean; ops-pots-on-web finding recorded as D-002 (advisory affinity absorption; composes fine)\n- **P-006** `done` Publish the new template to the PUBLIC templates mirror (Papercusp/templates): npm run mirror:check to measure drift, npm run mirror:push to apply+commit+push. Outward-facing (public repo) — owner go-ahead before pushing; the Cupboard official listings publish from that mirror, so until pushed the new root is local/bundled only. — note: Owner approved 2026-08-23; mirror:push landed 93ef437 on github.com/Papercusp/templates (18 dirs + 2 vendored pkgs, 0 extraneous)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Thin pure composition: papercusp-webapp + papercusp-ops-pots; no own components\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner: 2026-08-23, interactive approval] The agentic web-app root is a THIN PURE COMPOSITION exactly mirroring papercusp-agentic-desktop-app: requires papercusp-webapp@0.1.0 (whose closure brings papercusp-web-host + papercusp-data-layer + papercusp-ui) + papercusp-ops-pots@0.1.0 (judgment plane, the ONE work_items⇄typed-contract seam). No components of its own; an app built from it passes the UNION of the closure's checks. This was pre-anticipated by papercusp-webapp's own template.yaml (\"an agentic web app layers papercusp-ops-pots onto this the way papercusp-agentic-desktop-app layers onto papercusp-desktop-app\"). Machine twin AGENTIC_WEBAPP_TEMPLATE in @papercusp/template-kit, suite-pinned.\n\n### D-002 — In-repo affinity walk absorbs the tauri shell into the agentic-webapp group (pre-existing asymmetry; advisory-only)\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-005 finding, measured via a compose probe over the real 18-dir set (all 6 app roots compose OK; agentic-webapp: 9 members, 11-check union). The union for papercusp-agentic-webapp includes papercusp-tauri-desktop-shell:boot-e2e because EVERY data/ui/agentic aspect (data-layer, ui, ops-pots, data-sync, search) names papercusp-tauri-desktop-shell in composesWith (descriptive affinity, authored when all consumers were desktop apps) while NONE names papercusp-web-host — so the desktop groups never absorb the web chassis but web groups absorb the desktop shell. Harmless in practice: the in-repo unconfigured walk is advisory; a materialized app runs against its CHOSEN set (TEMPLATE_CHECKS_CONFIG composition.templateYamls), which excludes the tauri shell — the GUIDE already directs builders to config. Options if ever worth fixing (templates owner's call): add papercusp-web-host to those aspects' composesWith (symmetric noise both ways), or teach compositionGroup to skip shell-category templates outside the requires closure. Not changed here — 5 aspect templates + twins is out of this plan's scope.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-003 — Vendored template-kit copies are now DERIVED by scripts/sync-template-kit-vendored.mjs\nDate: 2026-08-23\nThe per-template vendored template-kit copies (required by template-bundle-integrity invariant 1: only <ref>/ is overlaid into a materialized app) were previously refreshed by hand and drifted (EI-20496357290097303). This plan added scripts/sync-template-kit-vendored.mjs: derives every vendored copy from canonical libs/generic/template-kit for exactly the templates whose checks IMPORT @papercusp/template-kit (import-shape matching, same four shapes as the guard's externalImportsOf — a bare substring match over-vendored 8 aspect templates on first run and was fixed + reverted in the same session), removes dev-harness files per isVendorDevOnly, deletes orphans, and offers --check. The byte-equality GUARD remains template-bundle-integrity.test.ts; the script is the matching writer. Run it after ANY canonical kit edit.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plan-visibility-revamp-2026-08-23","title":"Plan visibility revamp: sidebar dual timestamps, sidebar→detail dashboard, HUD weighted board","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Plan visibility revamp: sidebar dual timestamps, sidebar→detail dashboard, HUD weighted board\nslug: plan-visibility-revamp-2026-08-23\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-23\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — all 8 items done, verified, plan drained. Shipped: P-001 planWorkActivity.list resolver; P-002 PlansPane ✎/⚒ V1 timestamps; P-003..P-005 option-C plan dashboard + sidebar wiring; P-006 HUD H2 weighted board (weighted cols + rails + seg strip + hudpsort); P-007 enriched plan cards (avatars/liveCount/✎⚒/who-line/settled track); D-005 ALL plan clicks open the ?pdash takeover (harness-qualified encodeScopedRef), hudplanpop + PlanPopupModal removed. Evidence: 299 unit green (runIds 68e896ac + 2029ce3b), tsc clean in touched files, live tauri drives run2 + run5 CLEAN FULL PASS on 121 real cards incl. click→takeover→back and entityCardAges=0. Owner's desktop window reloaded; :3270 verified serving the P-007 css chunk.\n\n**Next:** Nothing — plan closed. Ships to :3070 automatically via git-sync → green gate (owner's own window runs the dev stack and is already fresh).\n\n## Background\n\nOwner asks 2026-08-23 [owner:aviynw]. The Plans face (apps/operator/app/_components/plans/PlansPane.tsx, op-chat middle pane) shows one ambiguous timestamp; owner wants BOTH last-edit (plan doc) and last-work (work-item progress), icon-coded. The all-plans view: owner picked mockup option C, with the EXISTING plan sidebar as the list — no new top-level tab; clicking a plan opens the option-C detail as an app-pane takeover. The HUD Plans tab (apps/operator/app/adv/hud/HudEntityColumns.tsx) is hard to navigate (5 equal columns, no agents on plan cards, filter-only navigation past 60 cards/column); owner picked fix H2 (weighted board). Reuse-first: plans.list, advRoster.list, plans.attention, planSessions.list all exist; the ONE new feed is per-plan last-work activity.\n\n## Phase 1 — data\n\n- **P-001** `done` planWorkActivity.list sync query: slug → last-work timestamp (max of GREATEST(updated_ts, last_progress_at) over harness_shared.work_items where source_plan_slug = slug), workspace-scoped; resolver entry in packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver + invalidation on work_items writes (table-to-query-names); unit tests. — note: ← WI-41008 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — sidebar timestamps (V1)\n\n- **P-002** `done` PlansPane rows: replace the single header ago with the V1 pair — ✎ plan.updated + ⚒ lastWorkAt (green-hot under 1h, dim em-dash when never worked), tooltips with full timestamp, isStale = max(edit, work); pure-helper + component tests. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-41009 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — plan detail page (option C)\n\n- **P-003** `done` PlanDashboard surface (option C right panel, full width of the app pane): header (bucket/title/slug, ✎/⚒ meta, progress bar, needs-you), Working-now session cards (planSessions.list joined with roster liveness/intents), Recent-activity feed, actions (Launch agent, open full plan editor, search transcripts); nuqs deep-linkable. — note: ← WI-41024 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Activity-feed data source: merged plan edits + work-item progress rows for one plan (small resolver reusing plan events + work_items reads); unit tests. — note: ← WI-41015 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Wire sidebar → detail: clicking a PlansPane row navigates the app pane to the PlanDashboard (popup retired on this path; back affordance; deep link preserved). blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-41029 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — HUD H2 weighted board\n\n- **P-006** `done` HUD Plans board layout: weighted columns (needs-you wide / working widest / blocked narrow), Ready + Done collapsed to expandable count rails, labeled segmented filter strip replacing the bare count chips, sort picker (default: last work). — note: WI-41033 committed: live-driven weighted board (run2+run5)\n- **P-007** `done` HUD plan cards enriched: agent avatars + live count (advRoster currentPlanSlug), ✎/⚒ times (planWorkActivity), who-is-doing-what line from roster intents. blocked-by: P-001, P-006 — note: ← WI-41038 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 5 — verification\n\n- **P-008** `done` Verification sweep: targeted vitest for every touched package (test:affected -- --changed-paths), lint:tsc where operator-core is touched, live drive of all three surfaces via tauri-agent-tools (agent-e2e §0–2) with evidence on the work items. blocked-by: P-002, P-005, P-007 — note: ← WI-41039 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Plan dashboard = mockup option C, reached from the EXISTING plan sidebar; no new top-level tab\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner:aviynw 2026-08-23, interactive] Of the four full-width mockup options (canvas cf9475c1 page 1; source apps/operator/docs/design/plans-mission-control-2026-08-23/), the owner picked OPTION C (split list + live detail) — with the twist that the LIST half is the existing op-chat plan sidebar (PlansPane), not a second list: clicking a plan in that sidebar opens the detail page. Consequences: no separate top-level /adv tab for the plan dashboard; mission-control options A/B/D are NOT being built.\nRelated: P-003, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Sidebar click opens the FULL option-C detail as an app-pane takeover; popup retired on this path\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner:aviynw 2026-08-23, interactive] The owner picked app-pane takeover and clarified: \"it shouldn't just open the detail page it should open what you showed me in option C\" — i.e. the full option-C surface (header with bucket/title/✎⚒ meta/progress/needs-you, Working-now session cards, Recent-activity feed, Launch-agent/open-plan/search-transcripts actions), full width of the app pane, deep-linkable, with a back affordance. PlanPopupModal is retired for this click path (it may remain mounted for other callers).\nRelated: P-003, P-005\n\n### D-003 — Sidebar rows show BOTH timestamps, V1 header pair; ⚒ = work-item progress; stale = max(edit, work)\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner:aviynw 2026-08-23, interactive] Rows show ✎ last plan edit (harness_plans.updated, already on PlanListRow) AND ⚒ last work (max work-item activity where source_plan_slug = plan, from GREATEST(updated_ts, last_progress_at) → new planWorkActivity.list sync map joined client-side like needsYouByPlan/liveByPlan). Placement = V1 compact header pair (canvas page 2), ⚒ green-hot under 1h, dim em-dash when never worked, hover tooltips with full timestamps. isStale switches to max(edit, work) so a worked-but-unedited plan no longer reads stale. Owner also said \"make the improvements in the plan row timestamps page\" — the page-2 treatment is the spec.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-004 — HUD Plans board fix = H2 weighted board (kanban kept, width follows attention)\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner:aviynw 2026-08-23, interactive] Of the three HUD fixes (canvas page 3), the owner picked H2: keep the five-column kanban but weight widths by attention (needs-you wide, working widest with rich cards, blocked narrow, Ready/Done collapsed to expandable count rails), replace the bare count chips with a labeled segmented filter strip, add a sort picker (default: last work), and put agents + ✎/⚒ times on plan cards. H1 (bands) and H3 (unified lanes) are not being built; H3 was rejected partly because it overlaps the new sidebar→detail dashboard. This revamps the Plans board that hud-session-launcher-and-board-tabs-2026-07-26 P-009 built.\nRelated: P-006, P-007\n\n### D-005 — Every plan CLICK opens option C (the ?pdash dashboard takeover) — the full-plan popup is retired on click paths\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[owner 2026-08-23 interactive, mid-turn: \"clicking a plan should open option C from the mockup not the full plan\"]. Scope: EVERY surface where a click resolves to a plan — PlansPane sidebar rows (P-005, already wired), the HUD Plans-tab cards, and the HUD Work-items-tab ask cards whose target is a plan (both re-routed under P-007, WI-41038). All write PLAN_DASHBOARD_PARAM ('pdash'); PlanDashboardHost at the SPA root renders the takeover. The HUD's 'hudplanpop' popup key + its PlanPopupModal mount are REMOVED, not just unwired. PlanPopupModal itself survives for its non-click writers (chat ref pills, 'pplan'). If the owner still sees the popup after this lands, they are on a stale deployed shell — verify via dev:pipeline_position, not by re-fixing.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"social-platform-integrations-2026-08-23","title":"Social platform integrations — social:* capability verbs + replay-safe trigger adapters for the major networks","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Social platform integrations — social:* capability verbs + replay-safe trigger adapters for the major networks\nslug: social-platform-integrations-2026-08-23\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nCOMPLETE to the limit of agent authority. 27 of 28 items are terminal. The only non-terminal item is P-020 (X/Twitter), PARKED per D-002 on an owner paid-tier purchase decision — do not start it.\n\nAll nine platform adapters are landed, tested and typecheck-clean: Bluesky, Mastodon, Reddit (Wave A); YouTube, Facebook Pages, Instagram, Threads (Wave B); LinkedIn, TikTok (Wave C). Lane green at close: 63 files / 1227 tests / 0 failures.\n\nThe registry now spans the full capability range, and both extremes were discovered by verification rather than assumed: LinkedIn (P-021) is WRITE-ONLY (read: null — both read scopes are partner-restricted), and TikTok (P-022) is READ-ONLY (write.verbs: [] — no comment surface exists at all, and unaudited posting is SELF_ONLY, which SocialVisibility cannot represent, so declaring `post` would silently downgrade every caller to invisible).\n\nWHAT REMAINS IS OWNER-GATED, NOT ENGINEERING. Per D-052 no lane may report step 6 (\"the reply lands on the platform\") as accepted; every wave's LIVE acceptance is owner-walled:\n1. Wave A credentials — a Bluesky app password, a Mastodon instance account, a Reddit app registration. The ONLY wall that is not a third-party review, so the cheapest path to a first live acceptance. Already asked (conv-mt5ivafv-0000-5c253f2cb15c482db5c974bc155d2874); do NOT re-ask.\n2. X/Twitter paid tier — blocks P-020.\n3. Meta app review (Facebook Pages / Instagram / Threads), TikTok Content Posting audit, LinkedIn partner review — multi-week identity/legal/business verification.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: OWNER DECISION, not agent work: supply Wave A credentials (wall 1) to unlock the first live acceptance run — the recipe is in the WI-41084 checkpoint and docs testing/social-platform-acceptance. No agent should start P-020 or claim any live acceptance until then.)\n\n## Background\n\n**This is not a new integration system.** Papercusp already has the whole spine; this plan fills the one hole in it and then repeats a landed pattern N times.\n\nWhat already exists (verified in tree, 2026-08-23):\n- `external-triggers/` core — `ingestion.ts` (adapter payload → `ext:<source>:<event>` via events:emit, delivery ledger, dedupe, payload VALIDATED against the canonical datatype's ajv schema), `binding-engine.ts` (armed binding → launch plan / wake agent, storm policy, durable execution), `source-store.ts`, `admin.ts`.\n- Agent verbs `triggers:create | bind | arm | disarm | list | status`, and `/admin/triggers` with the installed-is-not-armed gate.\n- Live adapters: `slack.ts` (Socket Mode), `google-gmail.ts`, `google-calendar.ts`, `facebook.ts`.\n- OAuth substrate `lib/oauth/` (`providers.ts`, `token.ts`, `storage-fs.ts`) with `google`, `facebook`, `github`, `claude` providers registered; tokens resolved server-side and never placed in agent context.\n- The canonical datatype `social-post` is ALREADY registered first-class + published in `harness_shared.datatype_registry` (id, text, url, media, author, replyToId, occurredAt), and `facebook.ts:308` already normalizes `ext:facebook:post` to it.\n\nThe hole: **`social-post` is the only canonical datatype with no Tier-1 verb family.** D-019 (external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22) rules one provider-neutral capability family per canonical datatype — `email-message` → `mail:*`, `calendar-event` → `calendar:*`, `chat-message` → `chat:*`. `social-post` has a READ path (Facebook ingestion) and no WRITE path at all. So this plan is exactly two things:\n\n1. **`social:*` — the fourth Tier-1 family**, sitting on the SAME capability-verb seam as mail/calendar/chat. Cross-plan hard dependency: external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22 **P-028** (capability-verb substrate: canonical-id → source row → adapter → credential resolution, plus the D-020 rails as tested code). We do not build a parallel seam; if P-028 is not landed when this plan starts, landing it is the first act.\n2. **N replay-safe trigger adapters**, one per platform, each a near-copy of the `facebook.ts` shape: outbound-only transport, cursor reconcile, dedupe, normalize to `social-post`, emit `ext:<platform>:*`.\n\n**Inherited constraints (not re-litigated here):**\n- D-002 offline doctrine — no public ingress. Papercusp is a Tauri desktop app behind NAT. Every adapter is OUTBOUND-only (poll+cursor, or an outbound WebSocket) and reconciles on connect. This is the dominant constraint on this plan, because social platforms are overwhelmingly webhook-push; see Open decision 2.\n- D-004 — no app-local post types. Everything normalizes to `social-post`; a payload failing its ajv schema is a delivery-ledger failure, never a silently-mutated shape. If a platform carries a field the canonical shape lacks, the fix is to widen the registry datatype once, not to fork a per-platform type.\n- D-019 — verbs are provider-neutral. There is no `twitter:post` / `instagram:reply` in the agent-facing set, ever. Adding a platform is an ADAPTER, costing zero new prompt weight.\n- D-020 — the addressee is never agent-composable from untrusted content. This binds harder here than for mail: a social feed is untrusted text authored by strangers by definition.\n- Installed is not armed. Every binding lands disarmed.\n\n**Scope boundary, stated so it cannot sprawl:** this plan owns platforms whose unit of content is a `social-post`. Discord, Telegram, Teams and WhatsApp are `chat-message` platforms and belong to `chat:*` (external-triggers P-031) as additional adapters — they are explicitly NOT in this plan, and a Discord outbound webhook poster already exists at `lib/integrations/outbound-webhook.ts`. Snapchat, Pinterest and Twitch are deferred: no compelling agent use-case named yet, and each carries app-review cost equal to a Wave C platform.\n\n**Why waves, and why they are provisional:** platforms differ by two orders of magnitude in acquisition cost — not in engineering difficulty. Bluesky is an afternoon; X is a purchase order; TikTok is a compliance project. The waves below sort by ACQUISITION cost (self-serve auth, free tier, no app review) so the substrate is proven on cheap platforms before any money or review cycle is spent. The per-platform facts driving that sort are stated in P-001's matrix and are unverified until P-001 runs.\n\n## Phase 0 — matrix, registry, conformance kit (the gate)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Verify the platform capability matrix against LIVE vendor docs and record it as the plan's first Decision: per platform capture auth mode (self-serve OAuth vs app review vs paid contract), required scopes, read transport (outbound WS / poll+cursor / webhook-only), whether the read path is REPLAYABLE from a cursor after an offline gap, write capabilities (post / reply / delete / media), rate limits and quota units, cost, and automation-policy restrictions. Every row cites the doc URL and the date read. Waves 1-3 below RE-SORT against this result rather than the reverse. importance: high — note: ← WI-40892 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Platform capability registry: one row per platform declaring the P-001 facts as data the code reads (auth mode, scopes, transport, supported verbs, limits, review status). This is CURATED tier-4 truth (it describes external services, so it cannot be derived from our code) and therefore must be ATTESTED: a probe records each declared capability against a live or recorded provider response, so a silently-revoked capability fails a test instead of failing a user. The `social:*` verbs and the UI both read this registry; nothing restates it in prose. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-40902 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Adapter conformance kit — ONE shared contract test suite every social adapter must pass, which is what makes N platforms tractable rather than N bespoke integrations: cursor reconcile across a simulated offline gap with zero loss and zero duplicate emission, replay dedupe via the delivery ledger, emitted payload validates against the `social-post` ajv schema, rate-limit backoff honours the platform's documented budget, credential never appears in adapter output or agent context, and connection health visible in schedule:inventory. Ships with the Facebook adapter retro-fitted as the first passing case. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-40903 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — the `social:*` capability family (D-019's fourth family)\n\n- **P-004** `done` Confirm or land the cross-plan dependency: external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22 P-028 (capability-verb substrate + D-020 rails as tested code). If P-028 is unlanded, coordinate with its holder rather than forking a second seam; `social:*` adds no substrate of its own. importance: high — note: WI-40907 done, committed authority\n- **P-005** `done` social:reply { postId, text } — reply-shaped per D-020 rail 1. The account, thread, parent post and credential are ALL server-resolved from the canonical post id; the agent supplies text only and cannot redirect the reply, address a different account, or read the token. This is the verb that makes an inbound-triggered social agent safe at all. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: WI-40909 done, committed authority\n- **P-006** `done` social:post { text, media?, accountId } — create-shaped per D-020 rail 2: the destination account MUST originate from a trusted channel (the owner's own chat instruction, or an account resolved from the connected-sources list) and is REFUSED when lifted from inbound content. Resolved account, audience/visibility and media are echoed back before publish. Publishing is public and irreversible, which is why Open decision 4 governs whether this executes on owner-ask or ships behind an owner-authority flag. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-40911 done\n- **P-007** `done` social:search and social:read over the owner-granted vault + connected sources — the read half of the family, so an agent can ground a reply in prior context without each adapter re-exposing a bespoke read path. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-40931 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` social:delete { postId } behind explicit confirmation, plus the non-idempotent-verb confirmation path shared with Tier-3. Deletion is included deliberately: an agent that can post and cannot retract is worse than one that can do neither. blocked-by: P-005 — note: ← WI-40935 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Falsifiability probe for the D-020 rails, per the mutation-probe discipline (copy-out tier, never mutating the shared tree): prove that an addressee lifted from inbound content is actually REFUSED and that social:reply cannot be redirected, by mutating the guard and confirming the test goes red. A rail that has never failed is a rail nobody has tested. blocked-by: P-005, P-006 importance: high — note: Rail-1 injection guard proven falsifiable by in-tree mutation probe (verdict=caught); 3 permanent controls + all-platform-branch injection test added. See D-010.\n- **P-010** `done` Per-tool guidance (when / notWhen / chaining) for the whole family, and check the prompt-weight gate before merge — the measured failure mode in this repo is routing, not capability. blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007 — note: ← WI-40943 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Wave A adapters: self-serve auth, free, no app review\n\n- **P-011** `done` Bluesky adapter (AT Protocol) — the reference social adapter and the first to run the P-003 kit end to end: app-password or OAuth auth, Jetstream/firehose as an OUTBOUND WebSocket (structurally the same shape as the landed Slack Socket Mode client, so the reconnect/backoff/dedupe pattern is reused not reinvented), cursor reconcile on connect, normalize to `ext:bluesky:post` / `:reply` / `:mention` → `social-post`, full read AND write so it exercises both halves of Phase 1. blocked-by: P-003, P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-40944 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Mastodon adapter — per-instance OAuth (dynamic client registration, since there is no single host), streaming API over an outbound connection with poll+cursor fallback, normalize to `ext:mastodon:*`, read + write. Second adapter deliberately chosen to prove the registry handles a MULTI-INSTANCE platform where the host is per-connection config. blocked-by: P-003, P-005 — note: ← WI-40947 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Reddit adapter — OAuth, poll+cursor over the free non-commercial tier (rate budget from P-001, and the commercial-use terms recorded on the registry row), normalize to `ext:reddit:post` / `:comment` / `:mention`, read + write. Third adapter, deliberately POLL-ONLY, to prove the poll path independently of the WebSocket path. blocked-by: P-003, P-005 — note: ← WI-40954 completed (done)\n- **P-014** `done` Wave A gate: all three adapters pass the P-003 conformance kit unmodified, and at least one full loop is verified through the desktop app — a live mention fires a binding, an agent drafts, the owner approves, the reply lands. Any conformance-kit change needed to accommodate a platform is a finding about the KIT and must be recorded, not quietly patched per-adapter. blocked-by: P-011, P-012, P-013 importance: high — note: ← WI-40957 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Wave B adapters: credentials or app identity we already hold\n\n- **P-015** `done` YouTube adapter — rides the SAME Google Workspace OAuth source as Gmail and Calendar (the D-010 one-credential-path pattern; a scope addition plus a documented consent upgrade, never a second credential path). Read via Data API poll+cursor for channel activity and comments; PubSubHubbub push is unusable without public ingress so it is explicitly not used. Write: comment replies, and video upload gated on the quota budget from P-001 (upload is quota-expensive enough that it needs its own storm policy). blocked-by: P-003, P-005 — note: ← WI-40968 completed (done)\n- **P-016** `done` Facebook Pages adapter — extends the LANDED `external-triggers/facebook.ts` from its current owner-authorized vault-read surface (profile, posts, photos) to Pages read and write, reusing the registered `facebook` OAuth provider. Requires additional scopes and Meta app review; the review dependency is tracked as work, not as a blocker discovered late. Retro-fit it onto the P-003 kit as part of this item. blocked-by: P-003, P-005, P-014 — note: ← WI-40970 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `done` Instagram adapter — Meta OAuth (Business/Creator account required), content-publishing plus comment read/write. Comment webhooks are unavailable to us without ingress, so this is poll+cursor; if polling cannot meet the latency the use-case needs, that is the concrete case that forces Open decision 2 rather than a hypothetical one. blocked-by: P-016 — note: ← WI-40991 completed (done)\n- **P-018** `done` Threads adapter — Meta OAuth, publishing and replies, normalize to `ext:threads:*`. If the kit does not hold, this plan should ship fewer platforms rather than more.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — D-001 — Scope boundary: this plan owns social-post platforms only; chat-message platforms are chat:* adapters\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — reversible; owner did not rule on scope]\n\nRULING. Nothing major is silently dropped — the excluded set is named above with its reason.\nRelated: P-005, P-011\n\n### D-002 — D-002 — X/Twitter is PARKED pending an owner cost authorization; every other platform proceeds\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — this is an owner-walled item, NOT an agent decision to spend]\n\nRULING.
