This appears in the plan's Waiting-on-owner list and in every status report until cleared.\nRelated: P-020\n\n### D-003 — D-003 — Poll-and-cursor everywhere in v1; the Svix ingest path is NOT adopted pre-emptively\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — reversible]\n\nRULING. Every social adapter in v1 uses an OUTBOUND-only transport: an outbound WebSocket where the platform offers one (Bluesky Jetstream, Mastodon streaming), otherwise poll plus a durable cursor. No adapter depends on inbound webhooks, and Papercusp stands up no public ingress and no hosted buffer for this plan.\n\nThis is the direct application of D-002 in external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22 (offline doctrine) to a class of source that is overwhelmingly webhook-push. That decision already ruled that when the first NON-REPLAYABLE source lands, Papercusp adopts Svix Ingest polling endpoints under one Papercusp-managed org. Social is arguably that moment: Meta, TikTok and LinkedIn-org events are push-only.\n\nI am NOT adopting Svix now, deliberately. The reason is evidentiary, not economic: every social platform's list endpoints are cursored, so polling is REPLAY-SAFE and satisfies the offline doctrine with zero new infrastructure and zero user signup. What polling costs is LATENCY, and I currently have no measurement of how much latency any real workflow can tolerate. Adopting a managed third-party ingest tier to solve an unmeasured problem is exactly the mitigation-before-diagnosis shape this repo treats as a defect.\n\nWHAT WOULD REVERSE THIS, stated in advance so the reversal is evidence-driven rather than a later wake's mood: P-017 (Instagram) is the first adapter where comment latency plausibly matters. If its measured poll latency cannot meet the comment-triage workflow's needs at a rate budget the platform permits, that measurement is the trigger to open the Svix decision — with a number attached, per D-002's own terms.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for the registry: every platform row carries its transport and its measured (not assumed) poll latency, so this decision can be re-judged from data.\nRelated: P-002, P-011, P-017\n\n### D-004 — D-004 — Publish posture: reply-shaped verbs execute on owner-ask; create-shaped public publishing ships behind an owner-authority flag\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — a REFINEMENT of D-020 in external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22, not a reversal of it]\n\nD-020 ruled that owner-asked sends EXECUTE, and rejected draft-only as the v1 posture. That ruling was made about mail and chat. I am applying it unchanged to `social:reply` and refining it for `social:post`.\n\nRULING (a): `social:reply` EXECUTES on owner-ask, exactly per D-020. The addressee, thread, parent post, account and credential are all server-resolved from a canonical post id; the agent supplies text only. The blast radius of a wrong reply is the existing thread — bounded, visible, and correctable by a follow-up. This is the same property `slack:respond-in-thread` already holds today.\n\nRULING (b): `social:post` — create-shaped public publishing — ships behind a REGISTERED owner-authority flag for its first release, default OFF, with a DARK_FLAGS_REVIEW_BY date. The resolved account, audience and media are echoed back before publish regardless of the flag.\n\nWHY this is not the parking-lot abuse the repo's dark-flag rule forbids. That rule exists to stop finished work being shipped dark 'to verify later', and it names three legitimate default-OFF categories. This is squarely the second: an outward-facing publish surface the owner must personally ratify. A public post differs from a mail send in kind, not degree — it is unbounded in audience, permanently indexable, attributable to the owner's identity, and not correctable by a follow-up message. Combined with the fact that inbound social content is untrusted text authored by strangers at volume with an incentive to manipulate, an agent that can autonomously publish to the owner's public identity on day one is not a feature I should hand myself while the owner is asleep.\n\nWHAT MAKES THIS HONEST rather than a punt: the flag is registered with its reason and a review-by date, the verb is fully built and fully tested behind it, and flipping it is a single owner decision on waking — not a hand-off of unfinished work. If the owner says publish freely, the flag flips and nothing else changes.\n\nRULING (c): no verb in this family ever template-evaluates an inbound payload field into an addressee, account, audience or destination. P-009 proves this by mutation probe rather than asserting it.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-009\n\n### D-005 — D-005 — Verified Wave A matrix; replay-safety is NOT uniform and collapses to the Gmail cursor contract; platform verification is JUST-IN-TIME per wave\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-001 result. Sources fetched and read 2026-08-23; each row cites where it came from.\n\nVERIFIED — WAVE A.\n\nBluesky / atproto (https://atproto.com/specs/event-stream):\n- Transport: CLIENT-INITIATED WebSocket upgrade, one-way server-to-client (\"Streams are currently one-way, with messages flowing from the server to the client\"). Outbound-only, so it satisfies the offline doctrine with no ingress.\n- Cursor: integer `cursor` query param against a monotonic `seq` on each message; gaps are legal (\"They may contain arbitrary gaps\").\n- Reconnect semantics are fully specified: omitted cursor starts live; a cursor AHEAD of current seq is an error (`FutureCursor`) and the server closes; a cursor INSIDE the window replays from >= seq then goes live; a cursor OLDER than the window yields an `#info` message saying it is too old and replay begins at the oldest retained seq; `cursor=0` replays the whole window.\n- REPLAY DEPTH IS BOUNDED AND QUALITATIVE: \"a reasonable time window (eg, hours or days)\", explicitly \"not to enable clients to roll all the way back to the beginning of the stream.\"\n- Framing: binary DRISL-CBOR, header+payload, `op`/`t`. A slow consumer gets a \"too slow\" error then disconnect. 429 with Retry-After is a documented HTTP-level failure.\n- NOT YET VERIFIED: the write path (createRecord / app.bsky.feed.post shape) and the app-password vs OAuth auth model — docs.bsky.app now 301s to bsky.network, which renders client-side and returned empty to fetch, and atproto.com/guides/applications 404s. Verify before P-011's write half; the read half is fully specified above and is unblocked.\n\nMastodon (https://docs.joinmastodon.org/methods/streaming/ and /methods/statuses/):\n- Transport: WebSocket (3.3.0+) at wss://<instance>/api/v1/streaming, or HTTP SSE. Streaming host may differ from the API host — discover via `configuration.urls.streaming`, do not assume.\n- NO REPLAY AT ALL. There is no cursor, since_id, or offset parameter on any streaming endpoint. A disconnection gap can ONLY be recovered through the REST timeline endpoints.\n- Scopes: user token + `read:statuses` (+ `read:notifications` for the user stream). 4.2.0 removed app-token access.\n- Write: `POST /api/v1/statuses`, reply via `in_reply_to_id`, `visibility` in {public, unlisted, private, direct}, scope `write:statuses`.\n- IDEMPOTENCY: an `Idempotency-Key` request header prevents duplicate submissions, retained up to 1 hour. Use it on every write; a retrying adapter without it double-posts.\n\nReddit (https://github.com/reddit-archive/reddit/wiki/API):\n- OAuth2, 60 requests/minute, with X-Ratelimit-Used / -Remaining / -Reset headers to steer backoff.\n- Mandatory User-Agent format `<platform>:<app ID>:<version> (by /u/<username>)`; generic agents are \"throttled heavily\" and the docs say \"NEVER lie about your user-agent.\"\n- Poll-only, batch-preferred.\n- NOT VERIFIED: current free-vs-commercial terms and whether an access agreement is required — the support-site article 403s to fetch. Treat commercial use as unresolved; it does not block a personal-account integration.\n\nTHE STRUCTURAL FINDING, which changes P-003. Replay-safety is not a property adapters either have or lack — there are three distinct classes: (a) bounded-window cursor replay (Bluesky), (b) no replay, REST backfill only (Mastodon), (c) poll-only with cursored listings (Reddit). But all three collapse to ONE contract: reconcile(cursor) that must handle a CURSOR-UNUSABLE outcome by falling back to a bounded REST backfill. That is structurally identical to what the Gmail lane already implements — history.list from a stored historyId with a full-resync fallback when the cursor expires. So the conformance kit does not invent a reconciliation model; it generalizes the landed one, and the Gmail adapter should be expressible in the same contract as a falsification check on the abstraction.\n\nRULING — verification is JUST-IN-TIME, at the head of each wave, not all up front. Wave B and C rows are deliberately NOT verified tonight. API pricing, scopes and review requirements are the fastest-moving facts this plan depends on; verifying TikTok's audit terms now for work that starts in weeks produces a stale row that must be re-verified anyway, and a stale row is worse than an absent one because it reads as known. Each wave's first item re-runs this verification for its own platforms. P-002's registry therefore carries a per-row `verifiedAt` and the code treats an unverified row as unusable rather than as permissive.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-006 — D-006 — The platform is a value RESOLVED FROM THE POST, never a caller argument; and read-verified never implies write-verified\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — P-004 result. Binding on every adapter lane, P-011 through P-019.]\n\nP-004 ASKED whether to coordinate with the holder of external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22 P-028 or fork a second seam. Neither: P-028 is already DONE. The substrate landed at packages/operator-core/lib/capability-verbs/ (resolve.ts, addressing.ts, mail.ts, chat.ts, calendar.ts). There is no holder to coordinate with. P-004 therefore became: extend that seam, and prove the D-020 rails survive the extension.\n\nRULING (a) — THE PLATFORM IS A RESOLVED VARIABLE, NOT A CONSTANT AND NOT AN ARGUMENT.\n\nmail.ts and chat.ts hardcode a single vault source (`doc.source !== 'gmail'`, `vaultSource: 'slack'`) because their canonical datatype has exactly one connected provider. `social-post` has ten, connected simultaneously. So social cannot copy that shape, and the two obvious alternatives are both wrong:\n\n  - A constant per verb (social:reply-bluesky, social:reply-mastodon) re-introduces the provider into the verb name, which is precisely what D-019 exists to prevent, and multiplies prompt weight by ten.\n  - A caller-supplied `platform` argument beside the post id is WORSE THAN A MISDIRECTED REPLY, and this is the part worth stating explicitly. It would let an injected payload choose WHICH OF THE OWNER'S IDENTITIES TO SPEAK AS. A wrong reply lands in the wrong thread and is correctable by a follow-up; a reply sent from the wrong ACCOUNT is not correctable at all, because the identity that spoke is not something a later message can retract.\n\nSo a social post is addressed by ONE opaque ref, `\"<platform>:<externalId>\"`, parsed at the seam. The platform half selects the credential; it is never trusted as an instruction. Adapters receive coordinates already derived from the stored document.\n\nMechanical detail that bit and is pinned by test: the ref splits on the FIRST colon only. An AT-URI is itself full of colons (at://did:plc:xyz/app.bsky.feed.post/3k), so a last-colon or split-all implementation truncates real Bluesky ids into ids that still LOOK valid and resolve to nothing.\n\nRULING (b) — READ-VERIFIED DOES NOT IMPLY WRITE-VERIFIED. This is now a registry field, not a note.\n\nD-005 recorded that Bluesky's write path is unread (docs.bsky.app 301s to a client-rendered host) while its event stream is exhaustively specified. That residue lived in a `notes` STRING, which no code can enforce — leaving the system one forgetful moment from issuing a guessed createRecord against the owner's real public identity. SocialPlatformRow.write now carries its own `verifiedAt`, and `assertSocialWriteAllowed` refuses a null. Measured, not asserted: bluesky read OK / write REFUSED (write-unverified); mastodon and reddit OK on both; all seven Wave B/C rows refused as unverified.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for P-011: the Bluesky INGEST adapter is unblocked and should be built now. Its write half stays refused by the registry until someone verifies the lexicon from a source that actually serves bytes. That is not a blocker to route around — it is the gate doing its job.\n\nRULING (c) — A REPLY NEVER WIDENS ITS PARENT'S AUDIENCE.\n\nA rail with no mail or chat equivalent, which is why it had to be invented rather than inherited: an email reply reaches the same recipients by construction, and a Slack thread reply inherits its channel. A social parent carries an INDEPENDENT audience setting, so replying `public` to a followers-only post republishes that post's content, quoted, to everyone — a disclosure the owner never authorized and cannot retract. It is easy to do by accident because `public` is every platform's default. `resolveReplyVisibility` permits match-or-narrow and refuses widening.\n\nSub-ruling, from a bug my own falsifiability control caught before it shipped: visibility normalization has THREE cases and collapsing any two is a leak. ABSENT (the platform has no per-post audience — Reddit, Bluesky) → public, because those posts genuinely are public and narrowing would make every Reddit reply `direct`, which is not safer but meaningless. UNRECOGNIZED LABEL (a future platform's) → direct. MALFORMED (present, not a string) → direct. The first implementation routed through `string()`, which coerces a non-string to '' and so made corrupt data indistinguishable from an absent field, landing it on `public` — the one guess that can leak.\n\nRULING (d) — NO SECOND MAPPING TABLE. The platform id IS the vault source name AND the trigger-source kind, and resolve.ts derives its social entries from the registry rather than restating the ten ids. A hand-maintained copy would drift silently in the worst possible way: an adapter that works and a credential that simply never resolves.\n\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-007 — D-007 — A create names its destination as ONE opaque token; own-timeline posting is a separate verb, never an omitted argument\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — P-006 result. Binding on every adapter lane, P-011 through P-019, and on any future own-timeline verb.]\n\nD-006 ruling (a) settled how a REPLY gets its platform: derived from the stored parent, never a caller argument. A CREATE has no parent, so P-006 had to answer the same question with that derivation unavailable.\n\nRULING (a) — THE DESTINATION IS ONE OPAQUE TOKEN, `\"<platform>:<destination>\"`, NOT A PLATFORM ARGUMENT BESIDE A DESTINATION.\n\nThe caller unavoidably names where a new post goes. That does NOT license re-admitting a free-standing `platform` argument, because a separate argument can be varied INDEPENDENTLY of the destination — which is exactly the failure D-006 forbids: choosing which of the owner's identities speaks. Carried inside one token, the platform half CANNOT disagree with the destination half, and rail 2 judges the token the caller actually named.\n\nThe first-colon split is now FACTORED (`splitPlatformToken`) and shared by `parseSocialPostRef` and `parseSocialDestinationRef`. This is D-006 ruling (d) one level down: the AT-URI rule is a single fact, and two hand-maintained copies would fail in the worst available way — one ref kind parsing correctly while the other truncates, both looking valid. Pinned by test, including that the post-ref refusal messages stayed byte-identical across the refactor.\n\nRULING (b) — OWN-TIMELINE PUBLISHING IS OUT OF SCOPE FOR `social:post`, AND MUST NOT BE ADDED AS AN OPTIONAL DESTINATION.\n\n`social:post` is the COMMUNITY/destination-addressed create. Posting to the owner's own timeline (Mastodon, Bluesky) is a different verb with a different risk profile — no third-party audience choice, but maximum identity exposure — and it needs its own item.\n\nThe tempting shortcut is to make `destination` optional and treat its absence as \"my own timeline\". That is REFUSED: it makes rail 2 inapplicable exactly when the argument is omitted, i.e. a gate that silently disables itself on the quiet path. `parseSocialDestinationRef` therefore refuses a trailing-colon token (`\"reddit:\"`), pinned by test, so rail 2 always has something to judge.\n\nRULING (c) — THE PUBLISH FLAG GATES THE OUTBOUND CALL ONLY, AND IS READ INSIDE THE SEAM.\n\nPer D-004(b) the resolved account and audience are echoed back \"regardless of the flag\", so the flag CANNOT short-circuit at the top. Order is: parse → rail 2 → registry write gate + credential → adapter lookup → flag. With publishing un-ratified the verb still returns the REAL resolution (the account that would have spoken) plus `withheld`, which is what the owner ratifies against — not a prediction of it.\n\nThe flag is read in `postToCanonicalSocialDestination`, NOT passed in as a `publish: boolean`. A caller-supplied boolean puts publish authority in the caller's hands and the next caller written is the one that forgets. There is exactly one decision point and no argument that bypasses it — pinned by a control that passes `publish: true` and still sends nothing. ADAPTERS MUST NOT ADD THEIR OWN PUBLISH GATES; the seam owns this.\n\nRULING (d) — `SocialWriteAdapter.post` IS OPTIONAL, AND ITS ABSENCE IS A DISTINCT ERROR FROM \"THE PLATFORM CANNOT POST\".\n\nThe registry already declares per-platform `write.verbs`, and `assertSocialWriteAllowed` refuses an unsupported verb BEFORE the adapter lookup. So a missing `post` method means \"the adapter has not implemented a verb its platform DOES declare\" — `social_post_adapter_verb_missing`, distinct from `social_post_adapter_missing`. Collapsing them would report an unwritten adapter method as a platform limitation and send the next agent to verify a lexicon that was never the problem.\n\nRULING (e) — POST AND REPLY IDEMPOTENCY KEYS OCCUPY DISJOINT SPACES.\n\nA post ref and a destination ref are both `\"<platform>:<tail>\"`, so a reply to `reddit:abc` and a post addressed to `reddit:abc` with identical text would otherwise hash identically, and an adapter deduping on the key would silently drop the second, genuinely different, write. Keys carry a verb-distinct prefix (`pc-social-` vs `pc-social-post-`); pinned by test.\n\nRelated: P-006, P-008, P-011, P-012, P-013\nRelated: P-006, P-008, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-019\n\n### D-008 — Post refs are MINTED server-side and round-trip-verified; no caller ever assembles one\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — P-007 result. Binding on every adapter lane P-011..P-019 and on any future social read surface.]\n\nD-007 ruling (a) made the post ref unforgeable at the PARSE end: one opaque `\"<platform>:<id>\"` token whose halves cannot disagree. P-007 found the rail was bolted to only one end of the bridge.\n\nTHE GAP, read from code rather than assumed. `searchPersonalDocuments` (personal-vault/store.ts:515-530) returns `source` and `externalId` as SEPARATE fields. It is the only read surface that existed. So every caller wanting to act on something it found had to CONCATENATE the two halves by hand — and `social:reply`'s own guidance instructed exactly that, telling agents to \"pass the returned canonical ref\" that `personal:search` does not return and never returned. The guidance described a mint that did not exist.\n\nHand-assembly is where the halves come apart, and every failure mode is silent because the resulting token is perfectly well-formed: transposing the halves, pairing one platform with another platform's id, or carrying a stale platform across a loop iteration all PARSE cleanly and address the wrong thing. A test in social-read.test.ts pins this — `mastodon:t3_abc123` (a Reddit fullname under Mastodon) parses without complaint.\n\nRULING (a) — EVERY REF AN AGENT RECEIVES IS MINTED SERVER-SIDE, FROM THE SAME ROW ITS ID CAME FROM. `social:search` returns a ready `postId` on every hit; `social:read` re-mints from the stored row rather than echoing the caller's token. Callers pass refs onward VERBATIM. Adapter lanes must not add a surface that returns a platform and an id as separate fields for a caller to join.\n\nRULING (b) — THE MINT IS SELF-CHECKING BY ROUND-TRIP, NOT BY VALIDATION. `mintSocialPostRef` formats the token, parses it back through the seam's own parser, and refuses unless it addresses exactly the row it was built from. A validation rule would be a second copy of the parser and would drift; a round-trip cannot be fooled by both copies drifting the same way. It also catches what a length or emptiness check cannot: a stored id with leading whitespace mints a token the parser trims into a DIFFERENT id, and that refuses here rather than resolving to the wrong post. Consequence for adapter lanes: an adapter that stores an `external_id` which does not survive trim-and-reparse produces posts that are findable but not addressable, and social:search will count them in `skipped` rather than return them.\n\nRULING (c) — READING AND WRITING ARE SEPARATELY EARNED; THE READ PATH USES THE READ GATE. `social:read`/`social:search` gate on `assertSocialPlatformUsable` (row-level verifiedAt), NEVER `assertSocialWriteAllowed`. These genuinely differ today: Bluesky's event stream is fully specified and readable while its createRecord shape is unread and write-refused. Using the write gate would refuse verified reads; using no gate would read from an unverified platform. Read results carry a `replyable` verdict resolved from the write rule itself, so an agent is told a post is unanswerable BEFORE it drafts a reply rather than after.\n\nRULING (d) — SCOPE NARROWING IS LOCAL AND AN EMPTY INTERSECTION IS AN EXPLICIT REFUSAL. Two authorization shapes were verified against `authorizePersonalAccess` before any code was written, and both obvious implementations are wrong. (i) Requesting NO scopes and searching what comes back: the authorizer returns `requested.length ? requested : granted` (authorization.ts:83) and the store applies NO scope filter for an empty array (store.ts:466) — so `social:search` would span Gmail, Calendar and Contacts, and would then MINT \"social post refs\" for emails. (ii) Requesting all ten platform scopes up front: an owner who granted only Bluesky gets `scope_not_granted`, a hard refusal of the entire call rather than a narrowing — unusable under every partial grant, which is the normal case. The construction is therefore: request nothing, take the granted set, intersect locally with the registry-derived social scopes, and refuse explicitly when the intersection is empty. Never fall through to an unscoped search. A platform filter may only narrow within the grant.\n\nRULING (e) — A DISCARDED MATCH IS REPORTED, NEVER SILENTLY DROPPED. Rows that cannot be minted are returned as counts by reason in `skipped`. A search that quietly discards matches is indistinguishable from one that found nothing, and that difference is exactly what an agent uses to conclude the owner never posted about something.\n\n### D-009 — A confirmation is only real if producing it required seeing what is being destroyed\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — P-008 result. Binding on every adapter lane P-011..P-019 and on any future non-idempotent or destructive verb.]\n\nRULING (a) — DELETE SHIPS, AND WITHHOLDING IT WOULD BE THE LESS SAFE CHOICE. reply and post are ADDITIVE and fail forgivingly: a duplicate reply is noise a follow-up corrects. Delete is SUBTRACTIVE and terminal — no undo, no trash on any Wave A platform. The instinct is to omit it as the dangerous one, and that instinct is backwards: the failure mode of the post verbs is a wrong public post under the owner's identity, and delete is precisely what remediates that. An agent that can post and cannot retract is worse than one that can do neither, because withholding delete does not remove the danger, it removes the recovery.\n\nRULING (b) — A BOOLEAN `confirm: true` IS NOT A CONFIRMATION, AND NEITHER IS ECHOING THE ID. This is the substance of P-008. An injected instruction can set a boolean exactly as easily as the owner can, so a boolean authenticates nothing; its only real effect is to make the caller feel careful, which is worse than no rail because it is mistaken for one. Re-passing the postId fails the same way one step later: the caller already holds it, so echoing it proves only that it can copy a string. Both wrong shapes are kept as permanent CONTROLS in social-delete.test.ts, each shown admitting inputs the real rail refuses.\n\nRULING (c) — THE CONFIRMATION IS DERIVED FROM THE POST'S OWN CONTENT, SO PRODUCING IT REQUIRES HAVING READ IT. `socialDeleteToken(ref, text)` is handed out by `social:read` and ONLY by `social:read`, and recomputed server-side at delete time from the row as it stands now. Three properties follow that a boolean cannot have: it cannot be REPLAYED onto another post (the token is a function of the post, so one post's token never matches another's — tested with identical text, the hardest case); it cannot be GUESSED from a ref (an agent that fabricated or transposed a postId without reading it cannot produce it, which is the wrong-target deletion this exists to stop); and it goes STALE if the post changed between read and delete, which correctly refuses because you are no longer deleting what you looked at. This is D-007 ruling (a) one domain over: bind the dangerous parameter to something the server derives, never to a value the caller can vary independently.\n\nRULING (d) — A MISMATCH MUST NOT ECHO THE EXPECTED TOKEN. Returning it on failure would turn the rail into a two-call oracle: guess once, read the expected value out of the error, spend it on the second call — confirming a post the caller never read, which is exactly the property (c) exists to guarantee. Pinned by test.\n\nRULING (e) — `deleted: false` IS A FIRST-CLASS OUTCOME AND MUST NEVER BE SMOOTHED INTO SUCCESS. Delete is the one verb whose RETRY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ITS SUCCESS: a second call on an already-gone post sees exactly what a successful first call left behind. So \"the platform reported nothing to delete\" is a different fact from \"I deleted it\", only the adapter can tell them apart, and an adapter that cannot must say so rather than return a success the caller will report to the owner as a deletion. Adapter lanes: implement `delete` to distinguish these, or do not implement it.\n\nRULING (f) — GATE ORDER, AND WHY IT IS THE SECURITY CONTENT. Parse → resolve from the owner's vault → CONFIRM → registry write gate for `delete` specifically → adapter. Confirmation precedes credential resolution for the same reason rail 2 refuses an injected destination before credential lookup: an unconfirmed delete must never reach a code path holding the owner's identity. Note also that resolution IS the authorization for the target — `resolveSocialPost` is scoped to (workspace, user), so this verb can only ever reach the owner's own posts, and a guessed id belonging to someone else is not refused but simply not found, which is the stronger property. Finally, the write gate is per-VERB: `write.verbs` is declared per platform and several platforms declare reply/post WITHOUT delete, so `assertSocialWriteAllowed(id, 'delete')` is a real refusal rather than a formality.\n\nRULING (g) — DELETE REUSES THE REPLY COORDINATE DERIVATION RATHER THAN ADDING ITS OWN. Deleting needs the same platform-native handle for a post that replying to it does. A second derivation would be a second copy of per-platform knowledge, and the way that copy fails is by deleting the wrong object — the worst available failure for this verb.\n\n### D-010 — A purity test is not a rail test: the security property is WHICH FIELDS are trusted, not the shape of the signature\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-009 (WI-40937) set out to prove the D-020 rails falsifiable for the social seam. D-020 lives on plan `external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22`, not on this plan — `social.ts:558` cites it correctly, and a lookup scoped to this plan returns nothing, which is a scoping artifact and not evidence of a stale citation.\n\nWHAT WAS ALREADY PROVEN, and should not be re-done: rail 2 (create-shaped addressee) is thoroughly pinned — `addressing.test.ts` and `addressing.integration.test.ts` carry refusal cases, a falsifiability control, a calibration case, a discrimination case, per-owner/per-workspace scoping, and an explicitly documented KNOWN LIMIT (an attacker who has genuinely corresponded with the owner is a `prior-correspondent` and is admitted). `social.ts:644` routes the create-shaped destination through `assertTrustedAddressee`, so social inherits all of it. Rail 1 was likewise pinned for MAIL, including \"IGNORES an address injected into the message body\".\n\nTHE GAP, and the ruling. Rail 1 for SOCIAL had only a purity check: `resolveSocialReplyCoordinates` is deterministic and `.length === 1`. That check is worth keeping but it CANNOT express the security claim, and the reason is general enough to state as a rule:\n\n  **A resolver that read `doc.text` or `doc.participants` would PASS the purity check unchanged.** It would still be deterministic, and it would still take exactly one argument. Purity is a property of the SIGNATURE; the rail is a property of WHICH FIELDS ARE TRUSTED. Only the second one is the security claim, and no amount of signature discipline implies it.\n\nThis was not theoretical. The in-tree mutation probe (tier 3, `git-sync:papercusp` held exclusive so no sweep could commit the mutant; tree verified byte-identical afterwards) changed exactly one line of the Mastodon branch to trust `participants[0]`. The purity test stayed GREEN. The new injection test and its control both went RED. `MUTATION_PROBE_RESULT verdict=caught expected=caught target=in-tree:lock-held baseline_exit=0 guard_exit=1`.\n\nOPERATIVE, binding on every later platform: `resolveSocialReplyCoordinates` derives coordinates from a DIFFERENT set of payload keys per platform branch, so each branch can regress alone and a green suite proves nothing about a branch it never exercised. The injection test therefore loops over every platform branch. **When a Wave B/C platform gains a coordinate branch (P-015..P-019), it MUST be added to that loop in the same change.** A branch absent from the loop is untested against the injection it exists to refuse — and, per the above, its purity is not a substitute.\n\nKept permanently as controls, because each one is a wrong implementation that LOOKS right: a resolver trusting `participants[0]`, and a resolver scraping an `@handle` out of the body. Plus a DISCRIMINATION case asserting the controls agree with the real resolver on a benign post and diverge only on the injected one — without it, a control could \"pass\" by being wrong about everything, which would prove nothing about the injected case specifically.\n\n### D-011 — A value the agent carries between two verbs shares ONE name across the seam, and the guidance is pinned to the live catalog\nDate: 2026-08-23\nSettled in P-010 (WI-40943) by finding the defect it prevents. Binds every remaining item that adds social surface — Wave A/B/C adapters (P-011..P-019) and the packs/templates/UI work (P-023..P-028).\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. social:read returned a field named `deleteToken`. social:delete took an arg named `confirmToken`, and its description and chaining both told the agent to pass \"the confirmToken that social:read returns\" — a field that did not exist under that name. Nothing was broken in either tool: each was internally consistent, both typechecked, both had passing tests. The defect lived only in the SEAM, and the two tools landed in separate plan items (P-007, P-008), so per-tool authorship could not have caught it. It surfaced only on reading the five verbs as a family — which is exactly what P-010 says the item is for (\"the measured failure mode in this repo is routing, not capability\").\n\nRULE 1 — one name across a carry seam. When an agent's job is to move a value from tool A's RESULT into tool B's ARG, A's field and B's arg share one name, and the guidance uses that same name. Two names means the agent must translate, and the guidance becomes the only place the mapping is written — so it silently rots into instructions for a field that does not exist. Fix the PRODUCER or the CONSUMER as the measurement dictates, not as taste dictates: here `confirmToken` appeared 8x across the delete path against `deleteToken`'s 2x, both in the producer, so the producer was renamed.\n\nRULE 2 — a cross-reference in guidance is code-describing metadata and gets pinned. Guidance that names another tool, or a field another module returns, is a second copy of a truth that file owns; the derived-truth-ladder says derive, pin, or attest. These are pinned: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/social/social-guidance-routes.test.ts` asserts every `family:verb` the social guidance routes to resolves in the LIVE projected catalog, and pins the confirmToken name on both sides (type-level on SocialPostView, runtime on delete's zod shape, plus the prose). New social surface keeps that green rather than working around it.\n\nRULE 3 — the pin carries its own controls. The test ships permanent broken-input controls proving it CAN go red (a dead route in a real family is caught; colon-shaped prose like \"reddit:r/rust\" is correctly tolerated) plus a calibration case over the real guidance. No shared-tree mutation is needed to demonstrate falsifiability, so there is no restore step and no git-sync sweep race — the pattern to copy for the remaining guard work on this plan.\n\nMEASURED, not assumed: prompt-weight gate clean at 800 tools, 0 over the 1500 budget / 1600 hard cap after these edits (social:post 1293, reply 1059, delete 963, read 790, search 776). tools-md-sync 57/57. The pin test 5/5.\n\n### D-012 — D-012 — Verifying a platform can silently retire a guard's only test subject; check the population before flipping\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRULING. When a registry row's verification state flips (read→verified, write→verified, blockedOn→cleared), the flip is not just a data edit: it can remove the ONLY live example of a gate branch, silently retiring that guard's coverage. Before flipping a row, MEASURE the population that reaches each affected branch; after flipping, re-measure. If the population goes to zero, the branch must be re-bound to a SYNTHETIC subject in the same change — never left vacant, and never \"fixed\" by deleting the failing tests.\n\nWHAT FORCED THIS (P-011, 2026-08-23). Bluesky's write path verified. Bluesky had been the sole live instance of read-verified-but-write-refused, so it was the standing example across SIX tests in FOUR files — social.test.ts, social-post.test.ts, social-read.test.ts, social-reply.test.ts — including two permanent CONTROLS. Measured after the flip: ZERO real rows reach assertSocialWriteAllowed's `write-unverified` branch (every Wave A row is write-verified; every other row is unverified+blockedOn and refuses earlier). That branch is the guard that stops a guessed write from reaching the owner's real public identity, and it would have become untested at exactly the moment Wave A started writing — i.e. it would have been rediscovered by a wrong post to a real account.\n\nTHE TELL, worth generalizing: one of the CONTROLS failed. Not because the guard regressed, but because its subject stopped discriminating — the deliberately-wrong implementation and the real one began agreeing about Bluesky. A control is only a control while the two still disagree about its subject. A control failing right after a state flip should be read as \"my subject went stale\", not \"the code broke\".\n\nMECHANISM ADOPTED:\n- `socialWriteRefusal(row, verb) -> SocialPlatformUnusableError | null` extracted from `assertSocialWriteAllowed` (which is now its throwing facade). Pure and row-taking, so the branch is exercisable against constructed rows forever.\n- `HALF_VERIFIED_ROW` lives at MODULE scope in social.test.ts, shared by the write-gate block and the bottom-of-file control, so a second copy cannot drift into being write-verified and disarm the control.\n- platform-registry.test.ts PINS the half-verified population as []. If a future platform lands in that state the pin fails — which is good news (real coverage returned), and the message says so.\n- Data-driven tests over listSocialPlatforms() auto-arm for any future half-verified row with no test edit.\n\nBINDING ON P-012 (Mastodon), P-013 (Reddit) and every Wave B/C verification: state the branch population before and after your flip, in the work-item. \"Tests still pass\" is not evidence here — the failure mode is tests that pass because the property became untestable.\n\nSECOND, INDEPENDENT CORRECTION recorded because it is the same family and recurred a third time this plan: a refusal REASON must be read from the gate's branch ORDER, not from the row's fields. I asserted LinkedIn refuses as 'owner-blocked' because its row carries `blockedOn`; it actually refuses as 'unverified', because `assertSocialPlatformUsable` tests verifiedAt/sources first and never reaches the blockedOn branch. The row's data predicts the wrong answer. Read the code that decides, not the data it decides about.\n\n### D-013 — A conformance harness whose page size exceeds the kit's test gap makes the gap check decorative\nDate: 2026-08-23\nBINDING ON EVERY REMAINING ADAPTER (P-013 Reddit next, and all of Wave B).\n\nMastodon's signature failure mode is paging a gap with `since_id` instead of `min_id`. The docs distinguish them precisely: `since_id` \"sets a lower bound on results\" and in practice returns the NEWEST page; `min_id` \"returns results immediately newer than this ID... paginates forward\". So with a 100-status gap and a 40-status page limit, a `since_id` implementation returns the newest 40, advances its marker past all 100, and the middle 60 are gone permanently.\n\nWhat makes this the dangerous class rather than an ordinary bug: it has NO symptom. It emits a full page of real events and reports a healthy `emitted` count. There is no error, no refusal, and none of the zero-events tell that catches Bluesky's cursor bug. Only an identity check on WHICH events arrived can see it.\n\nThe P-003 kit's `offline-gap-closed-exactly-once` check DOES catch it — it compares the ids published during the gap against the ids emitted. But ONLY when the gap spans more than one page. The kit publishes a 3-status gap, so a harness with a page size of 20 (or an unbounded fake that returns everything at once) exercises zero pagination and passes a broken adapter with a green tick.\n\nTHE RULE: every adapter's conformance harness MUST use a page size smaller than the kit's 3-status gap. `mastodon-adapter.test.ts` uses `PAGE_SIZE = 2`.\n\nThis generalizes past pagination. A conformance kit grades the adapter; the HARNESS decides which of the adapter's behaviours the kit can reach. A harness parameter chosen for convenience can silently place a real failure mode outside the kit's reach, and the resulting green is indistinguishable from a real one. When you write a harness, state for each check what would have to be true of your fake for that check to be incapable of failing.\n\nNOTED AGAINST P-011: Bluesky's harness returns the whole world in one page, so its pagination is never exercised. That is not a live defect — the Bluesky client is seq-filtered and does not paginate — but it means the Bluesky suite carries no evidence about paging behaviour, and should it ever grow a paged client, the harness must change with it.\n\n### D-014 — `path` reports which route closed the gap, not whether there was one — alert on backfillReason instead\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRESOLVES an ambiguity in the P-003 contract that Mastodon is the first platform to expose.\n\nTHE QUESTION. Mastodon's stream carries no cursor, so reconciliation is a REST re-read on every connect. What should `path` be on a pass that re-read REST and found nothing new? `live-only` (\"cursor accepted and the provider had nothing to replay\") is literally true of the REST call. `backfill` is true of the mechanism.\n\nTHE RULING: `backfill` + `backfillReason: 'no-replay-supported'`, on EVERY pass where a stored marker exists, including no-op passes. `MastodonAdapter.declarePath` implements this and `mastodon-adapter.test.ts` pins it.\n\nWHY. `live-only` asserts that stream replay was consulted and had nothing — a claim about a capability this platform does not have. An operator reading `live-only` would believe the stream is covering gaps when in fact only the REST re-read is. That is precisely the false comfort D-005 exists to prevent, restated one level up: the silent-loss bug is invisible because \"nothing was missed\" and \"we lost the gap\" both look like zero events, and a path field that overclaims re-creates that ambiguity in the one place built to resolve it.\n\nTHE COST, STATED. `path === 'backfill'` stops discriminating \"routine tick\" from \"we lost the stream\" on Mastodon — it is true 100% of the time there. An operator alerting on backfill RATE would see this platform permanently at 100%.\n\nTHE MITIGATION. That information has not been lost, it has moved. `backfillReason` already carries it, and the three values partition cleanly:\n  - `no-replay-supported` — STRUCTURAL. The platform has no cursor; this is the steady state and means nothing is wrong.\n  - `cursor-expired` / `cursor-rejected` — EXCEPTIONAL. A cursor existed and the provider refused it. Something was actually lost and recovered.\n\nSo: ALERT ON `backfillReason ∈ {cursor-expired, cursor-rejected}`, NEVER on `path === 'backfill'`. That predicate is meaningful across all three Wave A platforms; the path-based one fires forever on one of them and would be tuned out, taking the real signal with it.\n\nGENERAL FORM, for the remaining adapters: when a contract field's honest value on your platform is constant, do not pick a more \"informative\" neighbouring value to preserve the field's discriminating power. Report the honest constant and move the discrimination to the field that can carry it.\n\n### D-015 — Reddit's `before` walks FORWARD in time, and the response's own `before` field is never the forward marker\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRead from the writer (reddit-archive/reddit), not from the registry row or recall.\n\nMECHANISM. `ListingController.build_listing(self, num, after, reverse, count, ...)` takes NO `before` parameter — `before` is expressed as `after` + `reverse=True`. The builder walks from the anchor in the reverse direction and takes `num` items, so `before=X` returns the N items IMMEDIATELY NEWER than X (adjacent to the anchor), then re-orders them newest-first for display. That makes `before` a forward-in-time pagination cursor, structurally the same as Mastodon's `min_id` — the P-003 contract holds across a third platform without change.\n\nTHE TRAP, and it is the same shape as D-013's. The obvious design is to persist the response's own `data.before` as the next forward marker. It is documented as \"The fullname of the listing that follows before this page. null if there is no previous page\" — so on the newest page, which is exactly the page every poll fetches, it is NULL. The field is null precisely when you need it. The forward marker MUST therefore be derived from `children[0].data.name` (the newest item in the page), never from `data.before`.\n\nBINDING on the adapter: the persisted cursor is the newest fullname EMITTED, and the walk-continuation signal is \"the page came back full\". Those are two different facts and MUST NOT share a field — that is the P-012 `nextMinId` double-duty defect, which coincided on every page except the last.\n\nSTALE ANCHOR. Two distinct outcomes, both verified in source, neither of which is silent loss:\n  - anchor fullname does not resolve → `VByName.run` falls through to `set_error(errors.NO_THING_ID)`, the param becomes None, and the listing returns PAGE 1 (newest). That is RE-EMISSION, caught by dedupeKey.\n  - anchor resolves but is unviewable → `if after and not self.builder_obj.valid_after(after): ... self.abort403()`. That is a LOUD 403.\nSo a Reddit adapter can never silently lose a gap to a bad cursor, and the port models the 403 as an explicit anchor-rejection driving path:'backfill', backfillReason:'cursor-rejected'.\n\nlimit: `VLimit(param, default=25, max_limit=100)`, clamped `min(max(i, 1), self.max_limit)`. count: `max(int(count), 0)`, display-only, does not select items.\n\n### D-016 — Write idempotency is a PER-VERB property; the registry scalar means \"the weakest verb\", and Reddit is where that stopped agreeing\nDate: 2026-08-23\nFINDING. The Reddit row asserted `idempotency: 'none'` with the note \"No documented idempotency mechanism, so the adapter must carry its own write-dedupe guard.\" Read against the writer (`r2/r2/controllers/api.py`), that is wrong for two of the three verbs:\n\n  - reply (POST /api/comment) — nothing. No key, no header, no duplicate check. The guard is entirely ours. TRUE as stated.\n  - post (POST /api/submit) — for `kind: 'link'` there IS a real, server-side, DEFAULT-ON duplicate check. Its own docstring: \"If a link with the same URL has already been submitted to the specified subreddit an error will be returned unless `resubmit` is true.\" That is a genuine idempotency mechanism the note denied existed. `kind: 'self'` has no equivalent.\n  - delete (POST /api/del) — IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION: `was_deleted = thing._deleted`, set, commit, plus `if not thing: return` for an unresolvable id. Re-deleting succeeds as a no-op. No guard needed.\n\nTHIS IS NOT REDDIT-SPECIFIC. The Bluesky row already carries the same shape: it says `idempotency: 'none'` while its own adjacent comment explains that a client-supplied `rkey` \"is the hook a replay-safe adapter uses to make a retry land on the same record\". So the scalar understates TWO of the three Wave A platforms, and in both cases the real mechanism survives only in prose that no code can read.\n\nRULING — the scalar STAYS, and stays `'none'` for Reddit. Considered and rejected: widening `SocialWriteIdempotency` to name the mechanisms that exist ('header' | 'client-key' | 'server-duplicate-rejection' | …), or making it a per-verb map. Rejected because the field has exactly ONE consumer — a documentation guard in platform-registry.test.ts requiring `notes` whenever it is not 'header' — so it is documentation, not a behavioural switch, and a cross-cutting type change to landed P-002 work would buy no behaviour. Its job is to answer \"must a write path supply its own guard?\", and for that job the SAFE reading is the weakest verb's guarantee: over-guarding `delete` costs a wasted check, while trusting a mechanism that does not cover your verb double-posts publicly and cannot be withdrawn. This is rung 4 (CURATED) of the derived-truth ladder with its reason stated: the fact is a vendor's documented behaviour, derivable from none of our code and pinnable to nothing we build.\n\nBINDING on any Reddit write path:\n  1. Send `resubmit: false` on a link submission. Hardcoding `true` disables the only native mechanism this platform has — which is exactly the mistake the old note invited.\n  2. Treat the duplicate refusal as SUCCESS-EQUIVALENT for a retry and hand back the existing submission. Retrying loops forever against a refusal that can never change.\n  3. Do not guard `delete`, and do not report `deleted: true` from a bare /api/del: it is `@noresponse`, so the body is empty whether it removed something or resolved nothing. Confirm via /api/info (which reddit's own rules prefer as a batch endpoint) or return `deleted: false` WITH the reason — under-claiming, which `SocialDeleteOutcome` explicitly requires over a success the caller reads as \"I deleted it\".\n  4. Refuse a `t4_` parent on /api/comment. The endpoint routes on the PARENT'S TYPE: a message parent creates a private message under `privatemessages` scope. Here that means a legacy connection must be distinguishable from a fully-scoped one, which ALLOWED-placement gets for free and DEFAULT-placement destroys.\n\nTEST OBLIGATION for P-015: a control asserting `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_SCOPES` still equals exactly the original four, so a later well-meaning \"just add it to the list\" edit fails loudly instead of silently re-granting.\n\n### D-020 — YouTube quota is THREE non-fungible buckets, not one — so a storm cap is per-VERB, and P-015's \"upload is quota-expensive\" premise is wrong (the conclusion survives for a sharper reason)\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — reversible; owner did not rule on this]\n\nVERIFIED AGAINST LIVE VENDOR DOCS, read 2026-08-23, two independent pages agreeing with verbatim quotes:\n- developers.google.com/youtube/v3/getting-started — \"a default quota allocation of 100 `search.list` calls, 100 `videos.insert` calls, and 10,000 units per day combined for all other endpoints\"; \"A read operation ... usually costs 1 unit\"; \"A write operation that creates, updates, or deletes a resource usually costs `50` units.\"\n- developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos/insert — \"Quota impact: 100 calls per day. Without that control the wrong-bucket derivation passes every test that only checks a cap exists.\n\n### D-021 — YouTube's two read streams have DIFFERENT replay guarantees — comments have no time cursor at all, so the registry's per-platform `replay` field is wrong for youtube as written\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — reversible; owner did not rule on this]\n\nVERIFIED AGAINST LIVE VENDOR DOCS, read 2026-08-23:\n- developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/activities/list — `publishedAfter` (datetime, ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sZ`) \"specifies the earliest date and time that an activity could have occurred for that activity to be included in the API response.\" Not deprecated. This is worth stating once so P-016 through P-019 expect it rather than rediscovering it three more times.\n\n### D-022 — YouTube ships TWO read adapters, one per stream — the conformance kit is registry-independent (verified), so D-021's per-stream split costs the kit nothing\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\n[self-imposed under the owner's AUTO grant, 2026-08-23 — reversible; owner did not rule on this]\n\nFollows D-021, which established that YouTube's activities stream has a real time cursor (`publishedAfter`) while its comments stream has NO time filter at all, so the two streams cannot share one `replay` declaration.\n\nFINDING THAT UNBLOCKS IT, read off the code rather than assumed. `conformance.ts` contains ZERO references to `platform-registry` — grep count is 0, and its only imports are `../../datatype-payload-validation` and `./adapter-contract`. The margin exists solely to make the boundary INSTANT reachable and is the smallest representable step on purpose — widening it into a lag cushion would only move the same cliff further out while multiplying the re-read on every pass.\n\n### D-024 — Meta's own getting-started docs name TWO scopes that DO NOT EXIST — only the permissions reference is authoritative, and the failure would have surfaced only at owner-walled connect time\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23 by reading four live Meta pages against each other.\n\nTwo official Meta pages list DIFFERENT scope sets for the same Pages capability, and between them they name two permission strings that are not real:\n\n- `pages-api/getting-started` lists: `pages_manage_metadata`, `pages_manage_posts`, `pages_manage_read_engagement`, `pages_show_list`.\n- `pages-api/posts` lists: `pages_manage_engagement`, `pages_manage_posts`, `pages_read_engagement`, `pages_read_user_engagement`.\n\nChecked against the canonical `developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions` reference:\n- **`pages_manage_read_engagement` does not exist** — it is a conflation of `pages_manage_engagement` and `pages_read_engagement`.\n- **`pages_read_user_engagement` does not exist** — the real string is `pages_read_user_content`.\n\nTHE VERIFIED WAVE B FACEBOOK SCOPE SET (5 strings, each with its verbatim grant):\n- `pages_show_list` — \"allows your app to access the list of Pages a person manages\". Do not copy their scope lists out of a getting-started page either.\n\n### D-025 — Facebook Pages has NEITHER a storable cursor NOR a time filter, and /feed is RANKED — so replay is watermark-and-FILTER, never watermark-and-terminate (generalizes D-023)\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23 against `graph-api/results`, `graph-api/reference/page/feed/` and the comments edge reference.\n\nTHREE independent vendor facts converge on one design, and each alone would have been survivable:\n\n1. **Cursors must not be stored.** Verbatim: \"Don't store cursors. The placeholder was wrong, in the same way D-021 found the placeholder wrong for youtube. That is now twice; the registry's per-platform `replay` scalar is a guess until the wave's verification lands, and should be read as such for every unverified row.\n\nAPPLIES TO P-017/P-018: both are Graph API edges under the same paging contract. Verify their ordering guarantee explicitly rather than inheriting an assumption of chronology.\n\n### D-026 — Facebook Pages is THREE read streams on three edges, and comments have NO page-wide edge — so the comment stream is a per-post fan-out, not a poll\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23 against the Page node reference and the `/comments` edge reference.\n\nTHE EDGES, verbatim, and what each actually returns:\n- `feed` — \"any interactions with a Facebook Page including: posts and links published by this Page, visitors to this Page, and public posts in which the Page has been tagged.\" The BROADEST edge, and a mixed stream of three different event kinds. It also returns UNPUBLISHED posts: \"Published and unpublished posts will be returned when querying the `/{page-id}/feed` endpoint. Use the `is_published` field to return only published posts.\"\n- `posts` — \"This Page's own Posts, a derivative of the `/feed` edge.\"\n- `published_posts` — \"All published posts by this page.\"\n- `visitor_posts` — \"Shows all public Posts published by Page visitors on the Page.\"\n- `tagged` — \"The Photos, Videos, and Posts in which the Page has been tagged.\"\n\nTHE RULING, applying D-022 (one adapter per STREAM):\n1. **`published_posts`** is the Page-authored stream — and it is the right edge, not `feed`. Reading `feed` and filtering by `is_published` + author would re-implement, client-side and fallibly, a filter the vendor already applies server-side, while spending quota on rows we discard.\n2. **`visitor_posts`** is a genuinely DIFFERENT event (\"someone posted on my Page\"), not a variant of the first. Merging the two behind one adapter would force a caller to distinguish them from a `from` field — exactly the shape D-006 rejects for platform resolution.\n3. **per-post `/{post-id}/comments`** is the reply stream.\n\n**THERE IS NO PAGE-WIDE COMMENTS EDGE.** The `/comments` edge is \"common to multiple Graph API nodes\" — Album, Comment, Event, Link, Live Video, Photo, Post, Thread, User, Video. The Page node is NOT among them. So \"what did people say on my Page today\" is not one call: it is one call PER TRACKED POST. This is a structural difference from every platform in Wave A and from YouTube (D-021), where the comment stream was at least addressable in one request, and it is the fact that makes the comments adapter's cost scale with the number of posts under watch rather than with the number of comments.\n\nThat fan-out lands directly on the BUC budget, which scales with engaged users — so the two facts compound: a Page quiet enough to have a small budget is also a Page whose posts must still each be polled. The comments adapter therefore needs a bounded, explicitly-declared watch window over recent posts, not an unbounded per-post sweep.\n\nCOMMENT FILTER — the default UNDER-FETCHES. `filter` is an \"enum { toplevel, stream }\": `toplevel` — \"This is the default. It returns all top-level comments in chronological order\"; `stream` — \"All-level comments in `chronological` order\", described as useful \"for comment moderation tools.\" Taking the default silently drops every reply-to-a-reply. For a reply-triage integration that is the same silent-loss failure D-025 rules against, so the adapter sends `filter=stream` explicitly and never relies on the default.\n\n`can_comment` on an individual comment \"indicates whether it is possible to reply to that comment\" — consistent with YouTube's `canReply` (D-023 posture): an ABSENT `can_comment` still attempts, because refusing on absence turns a missing optional field into a dropped reply.\n\nSCOPE OF THIS ITEM (P-016): `published_posts` + comments + write ship now. `visitor_posts` is DECLARED in the registry as a known, verified, not-yet-implemented stream with this reason recorded — an omission stated on the surface a reader consults, rather than a stream that silently never fires.\n\n### D-027 — Reading comments with the WRONG token type returns EMPTY DATA, not an error — so the Page-token exchange is a correctness rail, and an unverified token must THROW rather than emit zero\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23 against the `/comments` edge reference and `pages-api/getting-started`.\n\nTHE MECHANISM. Facebook requires a **Page access token**, which is a different credential from the user access token that OAuth returns. It is obtained by a second hop: \"send a `GET` request to `/user_id/accounts` endpoint where `user_id` is your user ID\", authenticated with the user token; the response returns \"a short-lived Page access token\" per Page, along with each Page's `tasks` array (`ANALYZE`, `ADVERTISE`, `MODERATE`, `CREATE_CONTENT`).\n\nTHE TRAP, verbatim: `/comments` \"returns empty data\" on Album, Photo, Post, and Video **when read with a User access token.** Not an error. Not a 403. An empty `data` array — byte-identical to a post that genuinely has no comments.\n\nA second instance of the same shape: comment `id` values \"are withheld from apps using Page Public Content Access — To access the comment IDs for a Page post you must be able to perform the MODERATE task.\" So insufficient privilege degrades the payload silently rather than refusing the call.\n\nTHE RULING. **The token-type check is a correctness rail, not an auth detail, and the adapter must be unable to emit a zero it has not earned.** Concretely:\n- The comments adapter resolves and uses a PAGE token, obtained via the `/me/accounts` exchange, and records which Page id it was minted for.\n- Before trusting an empty comments result, the adapter must have positively established that it is holding a Page token for that Page and that the Page's `tasks` include `MODERATE`. If it cannot, an empty result is a THROWN error naming the missing precondition — never an emission of zero events, and never a silent advance of the watermark.\n- The watermark must not advance on an unverified empty read. Advancing it would convert one wrong-credential poll into permanent, unrecoverable loss of every comment in that window, because a watermark-and-rescan replay (D-025) never looks back past it.\n\nWHY THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS FACT IN WAVE B. Every other failure mode found in this verification announces itself: a bad scope fails the authorize call (D-024), a throttle returns code 80001, a ranked feed over-fetches. This one produces a well-formed, successful, plausible answer — \"no new comments\" — indefinitely, on a Page that may be receiving hundreds. It would be discovered not by any test, gate, or monitor, but by a human eventually noticing that the integration has never once fired. An adapter that cannot distinguish \"no comments\" from \"wrong credential\" is not observably working even when it is; that distinction has to be built in at the point the credential is resolved, because no downstream check can reconstruct it.\n\nGENERALIZATION for P-017/P-018 and any future platform: **when a vendor documents that insufficient privilege degrades to empty rather than erroring, an empty result stops being evidence of absence.** The adapter owes a positive precondition check before it is allowed to report zero. Look for this explicitly in each platform's verification rather than assuming an error will be raised.\n\n### D-028 — Meta's quota is DYNAMIC (4800 × engaged users/24h), the token type selects the regime, retrying a throttle EXTENDS the block, and no write verb has any idempotency mechanism\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23 against `graph-api/overview/rate-limiting` and the Page `/feed` publish reference.\n\nQUOTA IS A FUNCTION, NOT A CONSTANT. Verbatim: \"Calls within 24 hours = 4800 * Number of Engaged Users\", where the multiplier is \"the number of Users who engaged with the Page per 24 hours\", over a rolling 24-hour window. Every prior platform in this plan had a fixed budget (YouTube's three fixed buckets, D-020). Facebook's budget MOVES, and it moves with engagement — which means it is smallest exactly when a Page is quiet, and largest when a post goes viral. A storm cap derived from any constant is therefore wrong in both directions: too tight to serve a busy Page, too loose to be safe on a new one. The cap must be derived from the reported usage, not from a compiled-in number.\n\nTHE TOKEN TYPE SELECTS THE REGIME. Verbatim: \"requests made with application or user access tokens are subject to Platform Rate Limits, while requests made with system user or page access tokens are subject to Business Use Case Rate Limits\" — and \"If both Platform and Business Use Case rate limits can be applied to a request, BUC rate limits will be applied.\" Platform limits are a different formula entirely (200 × users per rolling HOUR). So the credential mix-up in D-027 does not merely return empty comments — it also silently relocates the adapter into a smaller, faster-cycling budget with a different error code. Both codes must be handled: **80001** (\"Page calls made with a Page or System User access token\") and **32** (\"Page calls made with a User access token\"). Treating only one as a throttle leaves the other to be misread as an unclassified failure.\n\nUSAGE IS REPORTED IN A HEADER, SO THE CAP CAN BE DERIVED. `X-Business-Use-Case-Usage` carries `business-id`, `call_count`, `estimated_time_to_regain_access`, `total_cputime`, `total_time`, `type` (value `pages` for Pages), `ads_api_access_tier`, and \"can return up to 32 objects in one call\". `call_count`/`total_cputime`/`total_time` are percentages of the allowance. Reading this header is how the adapter learns the budget it is actually operating under; ignoring it is how a dynamic quota gets treated as a static one.\n\n**RETRYING A THROTTLE MAKES IT WORSE.** Verbatim: \"Continuing to make calls will continue to increase your call count, which will increase the time before calls will be successful again.\" And the wait is reported, not guessed: `estimated_time_to_regain_access` is the \"Time, in minutes, until calls will not longer be throttled.\" No fixed duration is stated.\n\nThis inverts the usual retry posture. For every other platform in this plan, a rate-limit response is retryable-with-backoff and a retry is at worst wasted. Here a retry is actively HARMFUL — it extends the outage it is responding to. So 80001 and 32 are classified as **hold-until-a-stated-deadline**, not as retryable: on either code the adapter parks for the reported minutes and makes no further call. A generic exponential-backoff retry wrapper applied to Meta would deepen every throttle it touched, which is the kind of defect that looks like the platform being flaky rather than like our own retry loop being the cause.\n\nWRITE IDEMPOTENCY IS `none`, ON EVERY VERB. The Page `/feed` publish reference documents `actions`, `backdated_time`, `child_attachments`, `feed_targeting`, `link`, `message`, `object_attachment`, `place`, `published`, `scheduled_publish_time`, `tags`, `targeting`, `call_to_action` — and **no idempotency key, client token, request id, or dedup parameter of any kind.** A retried POST creates a duplicate public post. Per D-016 this is recorded per-verb rather than as a platform scalar, but here both verbs (post-create, comment-create) agree: `none`. This is what makes the retry ruling above load-bearing on the write path specifically — the one operation whose accidental repetition is publicly visible is also the one with no protection against it.\n\nTHE COMPENSATION — read-after-write, which makes D-008 cheap. Verbatim: \"This endpoint supports read-after-write and can immediately return any fields returned by read operations.\" The create response is `{\"id\":\"post-id\"}`, and requesting fields on the create call returns them in the same round trip. So D-008's requirement that a post ref be MINTED server-side and round-trip-verified costs ONE call here rather than a create-then-GET pair — and that verification is the only defense available against the duplicate-on-retry risk, since the platform offers none.\n\n### D-029 — A dynamic allowance is capped by anchoring to the formula's FLOOR, and rationing is kept separate from throttling\nDate: 2026-08-23\nGoverns every platform whose rate budget is not a constant — today facebook-pages (D-028), and by inheritance Instagram and Threads, which sit under the same Business Use Case regime.\n\nTHE FACT EVERYTHING ELSE FOLLOWS FROM. `X-Business-Use-Case-Usage` reports PERCENTAGES — \"a whole number expressing the percentage\" of the allowance. So a live observation tells you what FRACTION of the budget remains and never how big the budget is. There is therefore no observation, however fresh, that yields an absolute number to cap against. One absolute anchor is still required, and the only one the vendor commits to is its own formula evaluated at its smallest real input: 4800 x 1 engaged user = 4800 calls/24h. That is `SocialRateBudget.dynamicQuota.assumedDailyFloor`, and it is REQUIRED on the type — a dynamic quota that cannot be anchored cannot be derived, and should fail to compile rather than fall back.\n\nAnchoring low means the cap is understated whenever the Page is busier than one engaged user. That is the safe direction: overstating spends an allowance whose exhaustion trips a throttle that retrying EXTENDS.\n\nWHY THE CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT COULD NOT BE REUSED, which is the part worth carrying forward. `FALLBACK_MAX_RUNS = 12` is conservative against a per-minute budget that refills continuously, and reckless against a small daily one: 12 runs x 10 calls x 288 windows/day = 34,560 calls against a 4,800-call floor — a 7x overspend, presenting as a working cap right up until the day it stops the integration outright. A cap's safety is not a property of its size; it is a property of the budget it was calibrated against, and the two failure directions are indistinguishable from the number alone.\n\nTWO CONDITIONS THAT LOOK ALIKE AND ARE NOT. Both present as \"we are near the limit\" and they take opposite actions:\n- RATIONING (headroom low but nonzero) -> WIDEN THE WINDOW, cap stays 1. The integration keeps working more slowly. Holding here would silence a source that can still reply once an hour.\n- THROTTLED (the provider said so, or the allowance is spent) -> HOLD, launch nothing, schedule NO retry. Widening a window would still authorise the calls; on this platform those calls are themselves what extends the block.\nConflating them is the specific failure this split prevents.\n\nA HOLD IS NOT `maxRuns: 0`. Same run count, opposite meaning, and the accounting differs: `planCoalesceWithCap` returns held events in their own bucket rather than as `coalesced`, because \"coalesced\" asserts the events were folded into a run and under a hold no run exists. A hold also has no faithful STORED form — `parseStormPolicy` rejects a non-positive maxRuns, and the tempting repair (clamp to 1) would persist a standing licence to call built out of an instruction to stop — so `toBindingStormPolicy` REFUSES a held policy instead of choosing. A hold is acted on now; it is never written down.\n\nNO DURATION MAY BE INVENTED. Meta documents no fallback hold duration and documents that continuing to call extends the block, so an unstated duration crosses the vendor boundary as `null` and stays null. A default here would be a retry loop underneath a no-retry policy.\n\nORDERING: a declared `dynamicQuota` outranks `buckets` and `requestsPerMinute` on the same row, by construction. Checking a compiled-in constant first would let the stale number win over the field added to overrule it.\n\nThe vendor-specific translation stops at `facebookQuotaObservation`; what crosses into the storm-policy layer is `SocialQuotaObservation` — two facts any scaling-allowance platform can state. Instagram and Threads should reuse that seam rather than adding a second vendor conditional.\nRelated: P-016, P-017, P-018, P-023\n\n### D-030 — AMENDS D-029 — a declared BUCKET beats a dynamic quota for its own verb; the two describe different budgets, not competing estimates of one\nDate: 2026-08-23\nD-029 stated, unconditionally, that a declared `dynamicQuota` outranks `buckets` and `requestsPerMinute` on the same row. Instagram falsified the buckets half within the hour. This amends it; the rest of D-029 stands unchanged.\n\nWHY D-029 GOT IT WRONG. It was written with exactly one dynamic-quota platform in the registry (facebook-pages), which declares no buckets. With one example the two possible readings of \"outranks\" are indistinguishable:\n  (a) a MOVING budget outranks a STALE CONSTANT purporting to describe the same budget, and\n  (b) a dynamic quota outranks any bucket whatsoever.\n(a) is the reasoning I actually wrote down. (b) is the rule I actually implemented. Instagram is the case that separates them.\n\nWHAT INSTAGRAM STATES — two budgets at once, verified from its own pages:\n  1. A moving CALL budget: \"Calls within 24 hours = 4800 * Number of Impressions\", reported as percentages in X-Business-Use-Case-Usage under type `instagram`.\n  2. A fixed PUBLISHING cap: ~50 posts/24h, \"enforced on the POST /<IG_ID>/media_publish endpoint\".\nNeither can be spent on the other's behalf. A day of heavy comment reading does not consume publishing quota, and 50 publishes do not exhaust the call budget. They are non-fungible in exactly D-020's sense — which is the rule the unconditional form was overriding without noticing.\n\nTHE AMENDED RULE, per verb:\n  - A bucket that DECLARES this verb WINS. It is a hard cap on exactly this operation, and the dynamic quota says nothing about it.\n  - Every verb no bucket declares falls to the dynamic quota — and specifically NOT to `selectQuotaBucket`'s tightest-bucket fallback, which would cap a read against a publishing limit it never draws on. On Instagram that fallback would have derived ~5 runs/day for comment reading from a limit on publishing posts.\n  - With no dynamic quota present the tightest-bucket fallback is unchanged (YouTube's behaviour is untouched).\n\nTHE MEASURED DIFFERENCE, since \"the ordering changed\" understates it: for verb `post`, the old ordering derives 288 runs/day (one per 5-minute window, from the call budget); the amended one derives 50/day — landing exactly on the vendor's stated publishing cap, which is itself the evidence the derivation used the right budget.\n\nA CONTROL TEST NOW MODELS THE OLD RULE PERMANENTLY, so the amendment cannot silently regress into the version that was wrong. Writing that control also caught a second-order error worth recording: my first version compared `maxRuns` between the two orderings and FAILED, because both derive a cap of 1 — what a widened window changes is the RATE, not the cap. A control comparing the wrong dimension would have been vacuous while reading as strict. The lesson generalizes past this file: when two policies differ, assert on the quantity the mechanism actually moves, and let the test tell you when you have picked the wrong one.\n\nGENERAL FORM, for the next platform: when two limits disagree, first ask whether they describe the SAME budget. If they do, the more authoritative or more current one wins (D-024, D-029). If they describe DIFFERENT budgets, both are true and each governs what it actually meters — and picking one is not a resolution, it is a category error.\nRelated: P-016, P-017, P-018, P-023\n\n### D-031 — A FULL page under a hard result cap with no paging is evidence of possible LOSS, and the adapter must report it rather than succeed quietly\nDate: 2026-08-23\nInstagram's /{ig-media-id}/comments edge states, verbatim: \"Returns a maximum of 50 comments per query\", documents NO paging cursors anywhere, and states \"Comments cannot be filtered by timestamp\". It also guarantees ordering — \"Requests made using version 3.2+ will have results returned in reverse chronological order\".\n\nPut together, those four facts define a HARD CORRECTNESS BOUND, not a performance characteristic:\n\n  a newest-50 window with no way to ask for the 51st is CORRECT for an incremental\n  poll if and only if fewer than 50 new comments arrive between two consecutive polls.\n\nAbove that rate, the older unseen comments are not merely late — they are UNREACHABLE through this edge, forever. No retry, no backfill and no cursor recovers them, because the API offers no way to address them.\n\nWHY THIS NEEDS A RULE. The overflow is invisible from the result. A poll that returns 50 comments looks exactly like a healthy poll that happened to find 50. But there is a detectable signature: A FULL PAGE WHOSE OLDEST ITEM IS STILL NEWER THAN THE STORED WATERMARK means the window did not reach back to what we last saw, so at least one comment fell off the end. If the oldest item is at or older than the watermark, the window covered the gap and nothing was lost.\n\nTHE RULE: when a platform caps a result set and offers no paging, the adapter MUST compute that predicate on every pass and surface the overflow — as a reported outcome, not a log line. Emitting the 50 it can see and returning success is the failure mode: it produces an integration that silently degrades exactly when the account gets busy, which is precisely when the comments matter most.\n\nThis is the same family as D-027's Facebook finding (an under-privileged read returns EMPTY rather than erroring, so an empty result stops being evidence of absence) and it generalizes the pair into one principle: WHEN THE API CANNOT TELL YOU THAT SOMETHING IS MISSING, THE ADAPTER MUST DERIVE IT FROM WHAT IT CAN SEE. Both cases are places where \"the call succeeded\" and \"we have the data\" come apart, and both are invisible unless a specific predicate is computed on purpose.\n\nNOTE THE ORDERING CONTRAST, because inheriting the wrong half would be easy: on Pages the feed is RANKED, so an early-exit at the first below-watermark item is UNSOUND and the adapter must filter every item (D-025). On this Instagram edge reverse-chronological order IS documented, so newest-first is a real guarantee — which is what makes the newest-50 window meaningful in the first place, and what makes the overflow predicate computable. Same family of question, opposite answers, and both were verified rather than assumed.\n\nALSO NOTE WHERE THE FACT LIVES. The IG Media reference — the page a reader naturally starts from — documents the comments edge in ONE LINE and states none of this. Every fact above comes from the EDGE's own reference page. A registry row built from the parent node's reference would have been confidently wrong about ordering, the cap and the top-level-only default. The general lesson for P-018 and beyond: read the EDGE page, not just the node page, before writing down what an edge does.\nRelated: P-017, P-018, P-003\n\n### D-032 — A platform may be MEDIA-PRIMARY, and the generic post contract assumed otherwise\nDate: 2026-08-23\nFACT (verified 2026-08-23, Instagram content-publishing reference): `POST /{ig-id}/media` takes `image_url` or `video_url`; the caption is the optional half. There is no text-only Instagram feed post.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND INSTAGRAM. `SocialPostRequest` was `{ destination, text, visibility, idempotencyKey }` — text REQUIRED, media absent entirely. That shape is not neutral: it encodes the assumption that a post is text with optional decoration, which is true of every Wave A platform and of Facebook Pages, and exactly backwards on Instagram. The contract was written from four samples that happened to agree, and the agreement read as a general truth rather than as a property of those four.\n\nRULING.\n1. `SocialPostRequest.media?: readonly SocialPostMedia[]` is added, OPTIONAL. Optional is not timidity: a required field would strand every existing caller and every text-primary adapter in order to encode a fact about ONE platform. Same reasoning that made `lossRisk` optional on the reconcile result.\n2. The ASYMMETRY LIVES IN THE ADAPTER, NOT THE TYPE. A media-primary platform asserts its own requirement and refuses a text-only request with a message naming the reason. It must not degrade — posting a caption with a placeholder image would publish something nobody asked for to the operator's audience.\n3. A MULTI-MEDIA REQUEST IS REFUSED EXPLICITLY, never satisfied by taking the first item. Instagram supports carousels through a different construction (one container per child plus a CAROUSEL parent); posting only the first of two images would drop caller-supplied content while reporting success. Silent partial fulfilment is the failure mode being forbidden here, and it generalizes.\n\nFOR P-018 AND LATER WAVES: when adding a platform, ask whether its create is text-primary or media-primary BEFORE reusing a neighbour's adapter shape. The question now has a place to be answered in the contract instead of being discovered at the provider.\n\n### D-033 — A detection affordance is not idempotency, and its answer must be three-state\nDate: 2026-08-23\nFACT (verified 2026-08-23): Instagram publishes in two calls — `POST /{ig-id}/media` creates a container, `POST /{ig-id}/media_publish` publishes it — and the container carries its own `status_code`, readable at `GET /{ig-container-id}?fields=status_code`, with documented values EXPIRED | ERROR | FINISHED | IN_PROGRESS | PUBLISHED. Vendor polling guidance: \"once per minute, for no more than 5 minutes\". Neither verb has any idempotency mechanism (D-016 shape: a verified absence across the documented parameter lists, not an unknown).\n\nTHE TEMPTING WRONG READING, stated so it can be refused: \"the container tells us whether the publish happened, so the adapter can retry safely.\" It cannot. The probe answers a question the failed CALL could not — it does not make the write idempotent, and a retry gated on a stale or unreadable probe still duplicates a public post.\n\nRULING.\n1. AN AMBIGUOUS PUBLISH IS RESOLVED BY THE CONTAINER, NOT GUESSED, and the result is THREE-state, never a boolean with a default:\n   - PUBLISHED  → the post EXISTS; retry is UNSAFE.
