(This is the case Facebook Pages' single-call create cannot detect at all — it is what the extra call buys.)\n   - FINISHED   → ready and unpublished; nothing went out; a retry would be safe.\n   - ERROR/EXPIRED → terminal and unpublished; retrying THIS container cannot succeed.\n   - IN_PROGRESS, or a probe that itself failed → UNRESOLVED. Reported as null.\n2. NULL IS MANDATORY BECAUSE BOTH DEFAULTS ARE HARMFUL. Defaulting to \"retry safe\" duplicates a post; defaulting to \"unsafe\" silently drops one. There is no conservative direction, so the honest value is the absence of an answer — the same reasoning as `lossRisk` being set only on positive evidence.\n3. THE ADAPTER NEVER ACTS ON IT. `retrySafe: true` is reported to the caller and acted on by nobody in the adapter. The choice concerns the operator's public timeline and belongs to whoever owns that.\n4. A RESPONSE THAT ARRIVED BUT CARRIES NO ID IS AMBIGUOUS, NOT A FAILURE. It feels like a failure and treating it as one invites the duplicating retry; epistemically it is identical to a timeout.\n5. PROBE BEFORE PUBLISHING, not only after. Publishing an IN_PROGRESS container fails, and a failed publish IS the ambiguous state. The probe is affordable because the publishing cap \"is enforced on the POST /{ig-id}/media_publish endpoint\" — container creation and status polling spend call budget, never publishing quota (D-030's separation, put to work).\n\nGENERAL FORM for later platforms: when a provider offers a way to OBSERVE the outcome of an unacknowledged write, that is worth real cost — but classify it as detection, keep the adapter passive, and let the unresolved case stay unresolved.\n\n### D-034 — RETRACTION: D-024 fires on Instagram too — and a probe's scope bounds its claim\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRETRACTED CLAIM. Earlier this item I wrote into the instagram registry row: \"D-024 CHECK RAN AND PASSED HERE ... every scope string named by Instagram's tutorial pages WAS found in the permissions reference, unlike Facebook Pages where two named permissions did not exist at all. Same instrument, opposite outcome.\" That is now corrected in the row, and the correction is recorded here because the row is not addressable after the fact and because the same error is easy to repeat.\n\nWHAT FALSIFIED IT. Reading the `/replies` EDGE reference (for an unrelated reason — the reply target's semantics) found `page_read_engagement`, SINGULAR, listed among that edge's required permissions. The permissions reference has no such entry; the real permission is the plural `pages_read_engagement`. So Instagram's documentation DOES name a permission that does not exist. D-024 fires here exactly as it did for Facebook Pages.\n\nWHY THE CLAIM WAS WRONG WHILE THE MEASUREMENT WAS RIGHT — the part worth keeping. The probe covered the overview and tutorial pages. The conclusion was written about INSTAGRAM. Between measuring and writing, the scope silently widened from \"every string on the pages I read\" to \"every string Instagram names\", and the widened form is what a later reader inherits as fact. Nothing about the check was sloppy; the sentence was.\n\nTWO RULINGS.\n1. A D-024 SWEEP THAT READS ONLY TUTORIALS IS NOT A SWEEP. The edge pages carry the phantom permissions as well as the behavioural facts — this is D-031's \"read the edge page\" reaching the same conclusion down a second, independent path. Resolve every scope string against the permissions REFERENCE, and enumerate the strings from the EDGE pages the adapter actually calls, not from the getting-started page.\n2. A CLAIM MAY NOT BE QUANTIFIED BEYOND WHAT THE PROBE OBSERVED. When recording a verification result, state the scope IN the claim (\"on the N pages read\", \"for the endpoints this adapter calls\"). A NEGATIVE result — \"we looked and found nothing wrong\" — is the most dangerous kind to widen, because it reads as a property of the subject when it is a property of the search.\n\nPINNED: `instagram-write-adapter.test.ts` asserts the registry requests the plural and never the singular (positive AND negative, so an empty scopes list cannot pass it), and that the /replies edge is in the row's sources. `providers.test.ts` asserts the same on the live OAuth provider's allowed and default lists.\n\n### D-035 — D-035 Threads collapses post and reply into ONE write path; nested replies are addressable, unlike Instagram\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED on developers.facebook.com/docs/threads/retrieve-and-manage-replies/create-replies/ (2026-08-23).\n\nA Threads reply is created by the SAME two-step flow as a post: POST /{threads-user-id}/threads (container) then POST /{threads-user-id}/threads_publish with creation_id. The ONLY difference is one extra container parameter, reply_to_id.\n\nWHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN JUST CODED. Instagram's shapes are ASYMMETRIC — a reply is a single call (POST /{ig-comment-id}/replies) and a post is two (media + media_publish). P-017's write adapter is built around that split. Copying its structure to Threads would invent a distinction the vendor does not have, and would produce two code paths where one is correct. An adapter author reading only P-017 would almost certainly make that mistake, because the two platforms sit under one Meta app identity and one review.\n\nSECOND, AND A REAL CAPABILITY DIFFERENCE: Threads lets you reply to a REPLY. Verbatim: \"Use the reply_to_id parameter to reply to a specific reply under the root post.\" D-031 recorded that Instagram silently RE-PARENTS a reply-to-a-reply onto the top-level comment, so an adapter there cannot honour a nested parent and must not pretend to. Threads can. The two behaviours are opposite, and neither is inferable from the other.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR THE CODE: one publish path parameterised by an optional replyToId; the parent id is passed through verbatim rather than being normalised up to a root id.\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-036 — D-036 Replay CLASS and LOSS BOUND are independent axes — Threads and Instagram share a class and differ on loss\nDate: 2026-08-23\nThreads' media-level read edges (GET /{media-id}/replies, GET /{media-id}/conversation) document NO since/until filter and no usable since-marker, so closing a gap means re-reading from the newest entry and stopping CLIENT-SIDE at a stored watermark. That is exactly SocialReplayClass 'watermark-rescan' — the same class as Instagram comments and YouTube commentThreads.\n\nBUT THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE OPPOSITE, AND THE CLASS NAME DOES NOT CARRY IT. Instagram's edge is capped at \"a maximum of 50 comments per query\" with NO paging documented, which is what makes its rescan genuinely LOSSY: a full newest-50 page whose oldest item is still newer than the watermark proves comments fell off the end unreachably (D-031). Threads' edges are BOTH documented as paginated, both return paging.cursors.before/after, and NO cap phrase (\"maximum of N\") appears anywhere on the page. So the Threads rescan can page backwards until it reaches the watermark: cost grows with the gap, but nothing is lost.\n\nTHEREFORE the Threads read adapter must NEVER set lossRisk. The contract already says \"Absent means 'no evidence of loss'\", and here that absence is a positive, verified fact rather than an adapter that could not compute the predicate.\n\nWHY A DECISION AND NOT A CODE COMMENT. The registry's replay field is the thing a later reader consults to answer \"can this platform lose events?\", and for these two platforms it gives the SAME answer while the truth differs. Without this recorded, the natural inference — Threads is watermark-rescan, Instagram is watermark-rescan and is lossy, therefore Threads is lossy — is available, wrong, and would justify building a loss-reporting path that can only ever emit false positives. The class answers HOW a gap is closed; it does not answer WHETHER it can be.\n\nONE GUARD ON THE ARGUMENT: the provider cursor must NOT be persisted as a resume point across polls. The docs never state how to pass a cursor in a request (cursors appear only in sample responses), and an 'after' on a reverse-chronological list is a position within one result set, not a position in a stream — the same trap the registry already records against YouTube's pageToken. The persisted cursor stays a timestamp watermark.\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-037 — D-037 Threads documents NO throttle code and NO usage header — the absence is the verified fact, not a gap to fill from Instagram\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRead both candidate writers on 2026-08-23: the Threads troubleshooting page and the Threads section of graph-api/overview/rate-limiting.\n\nNEITHER documents a numeric throttle error code. The troubleshooting page carries only media-container statuses (EXPIRED, ERROR, FINISHED, IN_PROGRESS, PUBLISHED) and string error_message values (FAILED_DOWNLOADING_VIDEO, INVALID_BIT_RATE, ...). No 8000x code, no subcode.\n\nNEITHER documents a usage RESPONSE HEADER. There is no x-app-usage, no X-Business-Use-Case-Usage, and no threads-specific header. The overview instead routes budget-reading to an ENDPOINT: GET /{threads-user-id}/threads_publishing_limit, which returns ABSOLUTE figures (quota_usage/config, reply_quota_usage/reply_config, delete_*, location_search_*).\n\nTHIS IS A STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE FROM ITS TWO SIBLINGS, not a documentation gap. Facebook Pages and Instagram both report budget as a PERCENTAGE in a shared header and both have their own BUC code (80001/32 for Pages, 80002 for Instagram, each verified against the header's own documented type list). Threads reports budget as an absolute figure from a queryable endpoint and states no code at all. D-029's assumedDailyFloor exists precisely because a percentage header cannot tell you the denominator; on Threads that reasoning does not apply the same way, because the endpoint answers directly.\n\nSO THE REGISTRY ROW CARRIES NO throttleCodes AND NO budgetHeaders. Populating either by reading across from Instagram would be inherited-not-verified (D-005) with a sharp failure mode: an adapter watching for 80002 on a host that never emits it would treat every throttle as an unclassified error, and one parsing X-Business-Use-Case-Usage on graph.threads.net would read a header that is not there and conclude its budget was healthy. An empty field that is honestly empty is safer than a plausible one that is wrong.\n\nSTILL GENUINELY UNKNOWN and recorded as such: what Threads returns on throttle. The floor and the four per-profile buckets are documented, so rationing is possible without it; only the classification of a live throttle response is not.\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-038 — D-038 The owed Instagram floor cross-check is RESOLVED — 4800 stands; the minimum-10 clause is Threads-only\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-018's vendor read found Threads documents \"The minimum value for impressions is 10 (so if the impressions is less than 10 we default to 10)\", making its floor 4800 * 10 = 48,000 calls/24h. Instagram's registry row records assumedDailyFloor 4800 as \"the formula at one impression\". Since BOTH platforms state the identical formula sentence — \"Calls within 24 hours = 4800 * Number of Impressions\" — the obvious suspicion was that Instagram's figure was 10x too conservative and should be harmonised upward.\n\nCHECKED AGAINST THE WRITER RATHER THAN ACTED ON. Re-read graph-api/overview/rate-limiting, which carries BOTH products' sections on ONE page. The minimum-impressions sentence appears ONLY under Threads. The Instagram Platform section states the same 4800 formula with NO minimum clause of any kind.\n\nSO INSTAGRAM'S 4800 IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE CHANGED. Threads' floor is 48,000; Instagram's is 4,800; they differ by a documented clause, not by an error in either row.\n\nWHY THIS IS WORTH A DECISION. The error was available in the DANGEROUS direction. Raising Instagram's floor to 48,000 to 'match' would have made its assumed budget ten times more GENEROUS than documented — a rationing layer that permits ten times the calls the vendor allows, failing only under real load and looking correct in every test. The conservative-looking figure was the right one.\n\nTHE GENERAL RULE, which is D-005 pointed at a case it did not obviously cover: two products sharing one formula SENTENCE on one PAGE still differ in their CLAUSES. Co-location is not agreement. 'They document the same formula' licenses citing both, never inferring one's qualifiers from the other's.\nRelated: P-017, P-018\n\n### D-039 — D-039 Replying on Threads is gated by ROOT-POST OWNERSHIP or a review-heavy scope — v1 takes ownership and enforces it in code\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERBATIM from the create-replies page: \"To reply to a thread, you must meet one of the following permission requirements\" — \"You are the owner of the root thread post\" OR \"You have either the threads_keyword_search or the threads_manage_mentions permission.\"\n\nTHIS IS A SECOND, SEPARATE GATE from the capability scope. threads_manage_replies is still required (the permissions reference defines it as \"create a reply on behalf of a Threads profile, hide or unhide replies to a thread\"). The ownership rule governs WHICH threads may be replied to, and no amount of threads_manage_replies satisfies it for someone else's root post.\n\nTHE EARLIER READ HAD THIS WRONG. P-018's first checkpoint listed threads_keyword_search and threads_manage_mentions under 'Also exist, NOT needed', derived from the overview and the permissions reference. Both of those describe what the scopes MEAN; neither states that replying to an unowned post requires one. Only the create-replies endpoint page does — which is the third time in this one item that a load-bearing permission fact lived on an endpoint page and not in an overview (D-034, and the threads_read_replies omission).\n\nDECISION: v1 replies ONLY under root posts the connected profile owns, and requests NEITHER threads_keyword_search NOR threads_manage_mentions.\n\nWHY THAT IS THE RIGHT SCOPE AND NOT A DUCK. The read adapter ingests replies to OUR OWN media — that is what the media-level conversation edge is for — so every reply the write adapter is asked to make already sits under a root post we own. Ownership therefore satisfies the gate for the actual v1 workload, and requesting a mentions/keyword-search scope would be asking review for privilege the feature does not use, the same reasoning that excluded ads_management on Instagram and pages_manage_metadata on Pages.\n\nENFORCED, NOT ASSUMED. The adapter carries the owning user id and refuses a reply whose root post is not attributable to it, BEFORE the call goes out — the D-027 rail. This matters because Meta's habit under insufficient privilege on these surfaces is to omit or misbehave rather than refuse cleanly, so a runtime discovery would be ambiguous. If a later item genuinely needs to reply to unowned posts (a mentions-monitoring feature), that is a scope ADDITION and a review change, and it should be a deliberate decision rather than a silently widened adapter.\nRelated: P-018\n\n### D-040 — D-040 The client-side watermark was the third copy — extracted to social-watermark.ts, and the drift it had already accumulated is the argument\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-018 was about to write a THIRD private implementation of the same client-side watermark cursor. Facebook Pages has one (`FacebookWatermarkCursor` / `facebookIsNewAgainstWatermark` / `facebookAdvanceWatermark`) and Instagram has another (`InstagramWatermark` / `instagramIsNewAgainstWatermark` / `instagramAdvanceWatermark`). Two is a coincidence; three is a shared concern nobody had named.\n\nEXTRACTED to `social-watermark.ts` — `SocialWatermarkCursor`, `socialInstantMs`, `isSocialWatermarkCursor`, `socialIsNewAgainstWatermark`, `socialAdvanceWatermark` — and the Threads adapters use it. P-018 adds ZERO new copies.\n\nWHY THIS IS SAFE TO SHARE WHERE ALMOST NOTHING ELSE IN THIS PLAN IS. D-005 forbids reading a vendor FACT across platforms — a cadence, an error code, a cap, an ordering guarantee. This is not a vendor fact. It is OUR algorithm for the situation every `watermark-rescan` platform creates: no server-side time filter, so the client re-reads from the newest entry and stops at a stored mark. The module is therefore forbidden from ever growing a platform-specific branch; a platform needing different behaviour needs its own function and a recorded reason.\n\nTHE DRIFT IS THE EVIDENCE, and it is why this is a decision rather than a tidy-up. The two existing copies had ALREADY diverged in three ways after a few days:\n  (1) Facebook's guard requires the watermark to PARSE; Instagram's accepts any non-empty string. A mark that cannot be placed on a timeline excludes nothing, so the permissive version re-emits its whole window every pass while looking healthy. The extracted version takes Facebook's stricter reading — an unusable cursor degrades to a cold start, which is loud and bounded.\n  (2) On an unparseable instant Facebook's advance returns the cursor untouched; Instagram's returns `{watermark:'', seenAtWatermark:[]}`, a value that then fails Instagram's own guard. Harmless by luck, not by design. Extracted: leave the cursor untouched.\n  (3) The persisted field is named `boundaryIds` on one and `seenAtWatermark` on the other — two spellings of one storage contract.\n\nNOT MIGRATED IN THIS ITEM, DELIBERATELY, AND FILED RATHER THAN DROPPED. Both existing copies keep working and keep their tests. Migrating them would rename a PERSISTED cursor field on two completed adapters — invalidating every stored cursor, which presents as every watched source cold-starting at once — and that deserves its own verification rather than riding along at the end of an unrelated item. Filed as a follow-up with these three drift points recorded, so the finding survives as work rather than as a comment.\n\nTHE GENERAL POINT FOR THIS PLAN. The plan's central bet is that one abstraction serves N platforms, and the conformance kit was built to test that bet on the RECONCILE contract. The watermark shows the bet has a second surface nobody was watching: shared IMPLEMENTATION, as opposed to shared INTERFACE. The kit cannot detect duplication — three adapters can pass it perfectly with three copies of the same helper quietly drifting underneath. So duplication has to be caught by an author noticing they are writing something for the third time, which is what happened here and is not a mechanism anyone should rely on twice.\nRelated: P-016, P-017, P-018\n\n### D-041 — A shared-source scope addition pins its non-destructive mechanism in an executable assertion, never in prose\nDate: 2026-08-23\nWave B is the first wave that adds scopes to an OAuth source ALREADY CARRYING LANDED, WORKING TRIGGERS: YouTube (P-015) rides the same Google Workspace connection as Gmail and Calendar, on purpose (external-triggers D-010, one credential path). P-019 exists because that sharing creates a specific regression — \"a scope change on a shared OAuth source can force re-consent and silently break landed triggers\".\n\nWHAT P-019 FOUND. The mechanism that makes the upgrade safe is `include_granted_scopes=true` on the Google authorize URL: Google's incremental authorization returns a token carrying the UNION of old and new grants when it is set, and ONLY the newly requested scopes when it is not. That single parameter (providers.ts:273) was asserted by NO test anywhere, while platform-registry.ts's own youtube row leaned on it IN PROSE: \"`include_granted_scopes=true` is already set on buildAuthorizeUrl, so the upgraded token retains the landed Gmail and Calendar grants (D-019)\".\n\nDelete that one line and nothing goes red. The first YouTube consent then returns a youtube-only token; googleGrantedScopes() (personal-vault.ts:207-221) returns the STORED list whenever it is non-empty, falling back to GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_SCOPES only when nothing was stored — so a youtube-only grant is a non-empty list that omits every Gmail scope, and Gmail and Calendar compute a non-empty `missingScopes` and flip to needs-consent / connected:false. Landed, working triggers break, at an owner action nobody associates with the cause.\n\nTHE RULING. When a plan item adds scopes to an OAuth source that already carries landed triggers, the property that makes the addition non-destructive must be pinned by an EXECUTABLE assertion, not by prose in a registry row or a code comment. Prose that a reader must trust is not a guard: it documents the dependency without detecting its removal, and it reads as reassurance precisely where the failure is silent.\n\nTwo shapes count as the property, and both are now asserted for Google in wave-b-gate.test.ts:\n  1. the retention mechanism itself (the token keeps the prior grants), and\n  2. the DEFAULT request is unwidened (an owner who never enables the new capability sees no change to the consent screen, so no existing connection is re-prompted and no refusal can take the landed lanes down).\n\nSCOPE: binds every remaining item that touches a shared credential — P-021 (LinkedIn) and P-022 (TikTok) if either rides an existing source, and any later addition to the Google or Meta sources. It does NOT bind a platform that gets its own fresh credential path, which by construction cannot de-scope an existing one.\n\nNOTE ON THE CONTROL. providers.ts is an IMPORTED module, so the SUBJECT_DIR copy-out trick cannot redirect it at a mutated copy, and mutating it in the shared tree to prove the guard bites would race git-sync. The prescribed alternative for a module subject was used instead: a named predicate (`retainsPriorGrants`) shared by the assertion and a permanent control that rejects both the dropped parameter and a falsified 'false', plus a calibration case so a predicate that rejects everything cannot pass. This is an honest limit, recorded rather than papered over: half A's falsifiability rests on those in-file controls, not on a source mutation.\n\n### D-042 — A wave gate derives its subjects from source and registry, never a hand-maintained per-platform list\nDate: 2026-08-23\nP-014's Wave A gate proved each Wave A platform was run against the P-003 conformance kit by reading `${platform}-adapter.test.ts` — one file per platform name. That was COMPLETE for Wave A, because every Wave A platform had exactly one read adapter.\n\nIt silently stops being complete at Wave B. YouTube has activities AND comments; Facebook Pages has posts AND comments. A one-file-per-platform check finds the first, reports the platform covered, and cannot see that a SECOND adapter skipped the kit entirely. The check would still be green, and the reader would still believe the wave was gated.\n\nTHE RULING. A wave gate derives its subjects from the source or the registry; it never hand-maintains a per-platform list.\n\nApplied in wave-b-gate.test.ts as:\n  - ADAPTER MODULES are found by scanning for the SocialAdapter contract's own marker, `readonly platformId = '<id>'` — read adapters declare it, write adapters do not. This finds every read adapter regardless of what the file is called, which is the whole point: the failure being guarded against is an adapter that exists and is not kit-run, and a convention-based scan cannot see a file that breaks the convention.\n  - THE PLATFORM SET comes from `listSocialPlatformsByWave('B')`, so a Wave B platform added later is gated the day it is added rather than the day someone remembers to extend a literal.\n  - THE SCOPE PROPERTY (D-019: requestable but never presumed-granted) is re-derived from the registry's own auth.scopes. providers.test.ts already asserts this over a hand-maintained list of three escalating scopes; the registry-derived form is what makes it a WAVE gate rather than a spot check.\n\nThis is the derived-truth ladder applied to a gate's SUBJECT SET, not just to its assertions: a gate that hand-lists what it inspects is a second copy of a truth the source already owns, and it drifts the same way every other hand-maintained copy does — except that when a gate drifts it fails OPEN, reporting coverage it no longer has.\n\nMANDATORY POSITIVE CONTROLS. A derived subject set can come back EMPTY, and `it.each([])` is a silent pass — so every derived enumeration must be asserted non-empty (and, where a filter narrows it further, that filtered set asserted non-empty too) before anything is concluded from it. wave-b-gate.test.ts carries these at each derivation: the platform set, the scope set, the googleapis-scope subset, the module scan, and the kit source length. Without them a gate that measures nothing is indistinguishable from a gate that passes.\n\nSCOPE: binds the Wave C gate and any later wave gate. It does NOT require retrofitting P-014's Wave A gate, whose per-platform enumeration remains complete for its wave — but a Wave A platform gaining a second read adapter would invalidate it, so prefer the derived form if Wave A is ever touched.\n\n### D-043 — Trigger packs must not use the `schedule` binding source: it is declared in the SDK and consumed by nothing\nDate: 2026-08-23\nEstablished building P-026's scheduled-crosspost template, and binding on every pack this plan ships (P-025 and P-027 included).\n\n`{ kind: 'schedule', scheduleRef }` is a real member of `PluginTriggerPackSource` in `packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts:751` and of the published `papercusp-plugin.schema.json`. It has ZERO consumers: repo-wide, `scheduleRef` appears only in those two files plus their build artifacts (positive control: `payload-context`, a sibling field in the same union, appears in 10 source files). Neither `install-plugin-core.ts` nor `plugin-host-runtime.ts` reads it — both collect `sourceKinds` from `binding.source.kind === 'external'` only.\n\nThe trap is that it VALIDATES. `validateTriggerPackDeclaration` short-circuits with `if (binding.source.kind !== 'external') continue;` before the eventPattern and OAuth cross-checks, so a schedule-sourced binding passes cleanly and produces a pack that looks scheduled and can never fire. A template whose defining feature rides that is worse than one that says plainly where the cadence lives.\n\nRULING: use `kind: 'manual'` and name the real surface — `plans:set-schedule` then `plans:arm-schedule` (two steps; an unarmed schedule never fires) — in the pack's `## Now` and README. `starter-packs.test.ts` asserts the absence of `scheduleRef`, so a later \"fix\" that reintroduces it reds rather than shipping silently.\n\nThis does NOT say the schedule source is wrong to exist — only that declaring one today asserts a referent the system cannot resolve. If a consumer is ever built, this decision is what should be revisited.\n\n### D-044 — A pack's storm policy is PINNED to the P-023 registry derivation, and its default is the tightest platform in scope\nDate: 2026-08-23\nTwo rulings, both binding on any pack this plan ships (P-025's Cupboard trigger-packs especially).\n\n**(a) The default is the TIGHTEST derivation across the pack's scope, with per-binding overrides carrying each platform's own.** A `defaultStormPolicy` applies to every binding that does not override it, so it must be safe for the weakest budget it can reach. Measured `read` derivations across the comment-digest platforms differ by 30×: Reddit 30/300s, Threads 16/300s, YouTube 3/300s, Facebook Pages 1/300s, Instagram 1/300s. One averaged cap would be simultaneously too generous for Instagram and 30× too strict for Reddit. So the default is Facebook Pages'/Instagram's 1/300s and every richer platform carries an explicit per-binding `stormPolicy`. Scope for a pack with external bindings is the platforms it binds; for one whose binding is `manual` (crosspost) it is every platform its destinations may name, compared by runs-per-second.\n\n**(b) Those numbers are PINNED, not hand-maintained.** A manifest is static JSON and cannot import `socialStormPolicyFor()`, so every `maxRuns`/`windowSeconds` literal is a second copy of a number the registry derivation owns — exactly the drift the repo's derived-truth ladder forbids, and unfixable by deriving. Rung 2 (PIN) applies: `starter-packs.test.ts` recomputes each effective policy (`binding.stormPolicy ?? defaultStormPolicy`) from the registry and compares. A registry budget that changes now reds three manifests instead of leaving them quietly overstating what a platform tolerates.\n\nThe same rung covers the crosspost `destinations` pattern, which is a second copy of \"which rows declare the `post` verb with a verified write path\" (currently bluesky|mastodon|reddit|facebook-pages|instagram|threads; YouTube excluded because its row declares `reply` only).\n\nA pin is worthless if the thing it pins against is constant, so the test opens with a CALIBRATION asserting `socialStormPolicyFor` actually discriminates between platforms — otherwise every comparison would pass while measuring nothing. Falsifiability proven out-of-tree (`SOCIAL_STARTER_PACKS_DIR`) against 6 mutations, all caught.\n\n### D-045 — Social trigger packs declare no `oauthField` — no social platform in scope has a platform-wide OAuth provider to name\nDate: 2026-08-23\nBinding on every social pack, and the place P-021's shape is wrong for this wave.\n\nEach P-021 pack binds an `oauthField` to a provider (`google`, `slack`). No social platform in scope can do that honestly:\n\n- **Bluesky** — `app-password` mode; the registry records its scope list as EMPTY. The validator refuses an `oauth[]` entry with zero scopes, so there is nothing to declare.\n- **Mastodon** — `instance-oauth`: the client is registered PER INSTANCE, so no single provider id means \"Mastodon\".\n- **Reddit** — a self-serve OAuth app, not a platform-wide provider.\n- **Threads** — deliberately left unwired by P-018. A Threads-configured Meta app carries its own app id, secret and authorization host, distinct from Facebook's, and those endpoints were never verified. Declaring `provider: \"facebook\"` would assert a credential path that was examined and explicitly not built.\n\nThe failure this prevents is silent. `validateTriggerPackDeclaration` cross-checks only manifest-INTERNAL consistency (inline `oauth` vs `oauth[]`, scope-set equality); it never resolves `provider` against the OAuth provider registry, which holds four entries (github, google, facebook, claude). So a fabricated provider passes validation and fails only at an authorize call nobody can reach yet — the same shape as D-034's phantom scopes, one layer up. P-021's own `provider: 'slack'` is not in that registry either, which is how easy this is to do by pattern-matching.\n\nRULING: social packs declare no `oauth` block and no `oauthField`; bindings carry `sourceKind` only, and credentials are acquired through the trigger-source connection flow. Each README names the registry scopes that connection must carry, so the requirement is stated where a human acts on it rather than encoded as a referent the system cannot resolve.\n\nCorollary, asserted in `starter-packs.test.ts`: a pack that does not publish must carry NO write scope string anywhere in its manifest (the write-scope list is derived from the registry, with a positive control so an empty filter cannot pass vacuously). That is what makes mention-triage's \"never auto-publishes\" a structural property rather than a promise in its plan prose.\n\n### D-046 — Coalesced trigger deliveries are NOT agent-readable — a plan may not be written as if they were\nDate: 2026-08-23\nCaught in review of P-026's own comment-digest pack, one step before shipping it. Binding on P-025 and P-027, and on any plan template this system ships.\n\n`coalesce-with-cap` folds a window's events into one run, so the obvious plan instruction is \"read the comments coalesced into this run from the delivery ledger\". That capability does not exist. `harness_shared.trigger_deliveries` is written by `ingestion.ts` and exposed by NO agent verb: the `triggers:*` family is create / bind / arm / disarm / list / status, and the only other reference to the table outside ingestion is a plan run-enrichment integration test's fixture cleanup. A plan built on it validates, installs, reads plausibly, and strands the agent at run time.\n\nThe asymmetry that makes this dangerous: the run legitimately carries ONE event, so a plan that summarised only its own payload would also be wrong — a \"digest\" of one comment reported as a window. Both the naive fix and the naive failure look like working plans.\n\nRULING: reconstruct the window instead of reading it. `social:search` already accepts a `platforms` list and a `{ from, to }` datetime range, so a digest derives the range from the launching event's `occurredAt` minus the source's storm-policy `windowSeconds` and searches for it. Two limits must then be reported rather than hidden: `social:search` caps at 50 hits per call (hence `maxCommentsPerPlatform` max 50, and a full result means the window OVERFLOWED), and its `scopesSearched`/`skipped` say which platforms were actually covered — an unsearched platform and an empty one are different findings.\n\nCorollary, same neighbourhood, same cause: a `postId` is an OPAQUE token that `social:read` and `social:reply` refuse when the caller assembled it from a platform and an id. Every plan step that needs one takes it verbatim from `social:search`. Both P-026 packs originally hand-assembled `<platform>:<id>`; both were corrected.\n\nIf an agent-facing deliveries read is ever built, this decision is what should be revisited — the reconstruction is a workaround for a missing surface, not a preference.\n\n### D-047 — A trigger pack's plan.md must be a STRUCTURED plan template, and only the install path checks it — pack acceptance therefore requires a real install, never validation alone\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\nEstablished building P-025's seven per-platform packs. Binding on P-027 and on any future pack this plan or its successors ship.\n\nTHE GAP. `validateTriggerPackDeclaration` — the validator every pack test reaches for first — does NOT open a pack's `plan.md`. It checks manifest structure: binding ids, event-pattern prefixes, the oauth field/scope agreement, edge acyclicity. A pack whose plan is ordinary markdown passes it cleanly.\n\n`inspectTriggerPackForInstall` (`cupboard/install-plugin-core.ts:249-254`) does open it, runs `parsePlan(markdown)`, and throws `InstallPluginError: trigger-pack plan at <path> is not a structured plan template` (422) unless the result is non-legacy AND carries a `frontmatter.slug`. So the plan needs YAML frontmatter — `title` / `slug` / `status`, with `slug` matching the pack directory, because the installer reports `planTargets: [{ path, slug }]` off that frontmatter.\n\nHOW IT SURFACED, WHICH IS THE POINT. All seven packs were generated, validated green through the real validator (and its falsifiability confirmed by six in-memory mutations, all caught), and covered by a new 58-assertion suite that also passed. Every instrument said the packs were correct. They would have shipped, been installed by an owner, and failed at 422 — because not one of those instruments exercised the install path. The failure appeared only when a real-install case was added to `install-plugin-core.test.ts`, where all seven failed at once with the same error.\n\nThis is the same shape as D-046 (a plan step naming an unreachable capability) one level up: there, the manifest was schema-checked while the PROSE went unchecked; here, the manifest was schema-checked while the plan's STRUCTURE went unchecked. In both, the artifact that validates is not the artifact that runs.\n\nTHE RULE. A pack is not accepted on validation. Its acceptance must install it through `installPluginFromCupboardCore` against the real shipped directory, and assert the installer's own report — `targetCount`, `bindingCount`, `sourceKinds`, `planTargets`, `armed: false`, and that installing granted no capability. `install-plugin-core.test.ts` now carries such a case for all seven P-025 packs alongside the P-021 and P-026 ones.\n\nONE REFINEMENT ON HOW TO ASSERT IT. That case compares the installer's reported `bindingCount` against the manifest read off disk rather than against a literal in the test table. Those are different subjects — it checks that the INSTALLER counts what the manifest declares — so it is not tautological, and it avoids duplicating a number that `platform-packs.test.ts` already pins against the adapters. A literal there would have been a third copy of the same fact.\n\n### D-048 — D-045 REFINES for a per-platform pack: declare an oauthField exactly when the registry scopes are non-empty and wholly inside one registered provider's allowedScopes\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\nEstablished building P-025. Amends the SCOPE of D-045 without overturning it; binding on P-027 and any later per-platform pack.\n\nWHAT D-045 SAID, AND WHY IT WAS RIGHT WHERE IT WAS ESTABLISHED. D-045 ruled that social trigger packs declare no `oauthField`, because no social platform in scope has a platform-wide OAuth provider to name. It was established on P-026's packs, which are CROSS-platform: a pack spanning Bluesky and Mastodon, or five comment platforms, genuinely cannot name one provider for that scope, whatever any individual platform supports.\n\nWHY IT DOES NOT TRANSFER UNCHANGED. A P-025 pack spans exactly ONE platform, so the question D-045 answered (\"which single provider covers this multi-platform scope?\") is not the question being asked. Inheriting the conclusion across that change of shape is precisely the failure D-005 exists to prevent, and the failure this plan has now hit twice in the other direction (a P-021 manifest field, a P-019 per-platform gate) — an inherited shape is always correct for the wave that produced it.\n\nTHE RULE, RE-DERIVED FROM THE REGISTRY. A pack declares an `oauthField` exactly when the platform's `auth.scopes` are non-empty AND every one of them is contained in some registered provider's `allowedScopes`. The operator registers four providers (`github`, `google`, `facebook`, `claude`), and containment resolves as:\n\n- **youtube → `google`.** Its two registry scopes (`youtube.readonly`, `youtube.force-ssl`) are both members of `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_ALLOWED_SCOPES`.\n- **facebook-pages → `facebook`** and **instagram → `facebook`.** `FACEBOOK_ALLOWED_OAUTH_SCOPES` is the union of the Facebook, Pages and Instagram scope sets, so both platforms' lists are wholly inside it.\n- **bluesky → none.** `app-password` mode; the registry records its scope list as EMPTY, and the validator refuses an `oauth[]` entry with zero scopes.\n- **mastodon → none.** `instance-oauth`: the client is registered PER INSTANCE, so no single provider id can mean \"Mastodon\".\n- **reddit → none.** A self-serve OAuth app; this operator registers no Reddit provider.\n- **threads → none.** Its scopes are non-empty but were deliberately excluded from `FACEBOOK_ALLOWED_OAUTH_SCOPES` by P-018, because Threads authorizes against `graph.threads.net` under a separate app id and secret.\n\nTHE PROPERTY WORTH KEEPING. That single containment rule produces the correct answer for all seven WITHOUT a per-platform table, Threads included — the case a hand-written table is most likely to get wrong, because Threads looks like a Meta platform and its scopes are non-empty. `platform-packs.test.ts` implements the rule as one function and contains no `if (id === 'threads')` branch; the rule, not a list, is what knows. A future platform whose scopes are folded into a provider's allowed set gains its Connect button automatically, and one that is not silently keeps a plain credential field instead of a promise that would fail at consent time rather than at build time.\n\nRESIDUE, NAMED NOT SILENT. The P-021 packs declare provider `slack`, which is NOT among the four registered providers, and the validator never checks a provider string against the OAuth registry. That is a real pre-existing gap; it is out of P-025's lane and is recorded here so it is not rediscovered as a surprise.\n\n### D-049 — Platform packs bind one explicit event per binding and never a wildcard, because one platform's event name space is provider-controlled\nDate: 2026-08-23\nDate: 2026-08-23\nEstablished building P-025. Binding on any per-platform pack.\n\nTHE OPTION NOT TAKEN. `eventPattern` supports a wildcard: `keyMatchesPattern` (`events/await/pattern.ts:88`) macro-expands, compiles `*` to `.*`, and anchors the whole key, so `ext:bluesky:*` is legal and would match every event a platform emits. For a pack whose stated job is \"wire this platform up\", a single wildcard binding looks like the obviously right shape — it is shorter, and it cannot go stale when an adapter gains an event.\n\nWHY IT IS WRONG HERE, AND THE REASON IS NOT UNIFORM. Six of the seven platforms emit a CLOSED event set computed by a small function (`blueskyEventName` -> post|reply|mention, `redditEventName` -> post|comment, `threadsReplyEventName` -> post|reply, and so on). YouTube does not: `youtubeActivityEventName` returns `snippet.type` lowercased with an `'activity'` fallback, and `snippet.type` is a provider-controlled string (`upload`, `like`, `subscription`, `playlistItem`, …). So `ext:youtube:*` binds whatever YouTube decides to send.\n\nThat is not merely broad, it is actively harmful on exactly that platform. `normalizeYouTubeActivity` deliberately falls `title -> description -> ''` for `text`, because a `like` or a `subscription` carries neither and failing datatype validation would drop a well-formed provider response entirely. So a wildcard fires the plan on empty-text activities — against YouTube's `read` budget, which the registry derives as the TIGHTEST of any platform in scope at 3 runs per 300s. A handful of likes exhausts the window and starves the events the owner actually wanted.\n\nTHE RULE. One binding per event, each with an explicit `ext:<platform>:<event>` pattern, and no `*` in any platform pack. `platform-packs.test.ts` asserts the absence of the wildcard, and separately drives each adapter's real `*EventName` function to confirm every declared event is one the adapter can actually PRODUCE — a binding for an event nothing emits installs cleanly and then never fires, which is D-046's phantom in binding form rather than prose form.\n\nTHE SECOND REASON, WHICH WOULD HAVE JUSTIFIED IT ALONE. A binding is the unit of arm/disarm. Per-event bindings let an owner arm mentions without posts, or comments without uploads, from the triggers admin without editing the pack — which is what \"installable and shareable rather than hand-wired\" means in P-025's own terms. A single wildcard binding is all-or-nothing.\n\nWHERE CLOSURE IS AND IS NOT ASSERTED. For the six closed platforms the test also checks the converse — every name the adapters can emit HAS a binding — so a new adapter event reds the suite instead of being silently unhandled. For YouTube that check is deliberately skipped and marked `closed: false`, because the producible set there is what we can demonstrate, not what can arrive. Asserting closure over a provider-controlled name space would be asserting something we cannot know.\n\n### D-050 — Social cursor freshness is a FOUR-state verdict, never a nullable timestamp\nDate: 2026-08-23\nAny surface reporting how current a social source is MUST use socialCursorFreshness() (packages/operator-core/lib/external-triggers/social/cursor-freshness.ts) and render four states: synced | position-only | never-synced | unrecognized. Reading a timestamp field directly is forbidden.\n\nWHY. SocialReconcileResult.cursor is typed `unknown` because every adapter owns its cursor shape, and the eight that exist disagree on both the field name and on whether a cursor carries a time AT ALL:\n\n  watermark      + boundaryIds     - threads, facebook-pages, youtube-comments\n  watermark      + seenAtWatermark - instagram (same idea, drifted name; WI-41027)\n  publishedAfter + boundaryIds     - youtube-activities\n  minId          + lastEventAt?    - mastodon (time OPTIONAL)\n  seq            + lastEventAt?    - bluesky  (time OPTIONAL)\n  newestFullname                   - reddit   (NO time, by design)\n\nSo the natural implementation - read cursor.watermark, show \"last synced X ago\" - is correct for three platforms and silently null for the rest. Null renders as \"never synced\", which is indistinguishable from a dead integration. A perfectly healthy Reddit source, whose cursor is an opaque t3_ fullname, would have reported never-synced forever.\n\n`position-only` is the state that earns its keep: it asserts \"this cursor is advancing, and this platform cannot tell you when\" - a true statement neither synced nor never-synced can express, and the difference between a calm reading and a false alarm.\n\n`unrecognized` is reserved for a genuine defect: a cursor present that matches no known shape, or a known instant field holding an unparseable value. It must NOT be used for a timeless cursor.\n\nDRIFT GUARD. cursor-freshness.test.ts parses the real adapter interfaces out of the social dir and fails if any cursor field is unclassified, so a ninth cursor shape breaks the build instead of silently degrading the pane to never-synced. Proven falsifiable out-of-tree (SOCIAL_CURSOR_DIR): adding a TumblrCursor with an unclassified field failed two independent assertions.\n\nNOTE FOR READERS TODAY: nothing in production persists a social cursor yet - the only non-test caller of adapter.reconcile is the conformance kit - so every real social source currently reads never-synced. That is CORRECT, not a bug in the pane. The write path itself exists and works (updateExternalTriggerSourceSyncState, used by Slack); social is simply not wired to it.\nRelated: P-027\n\n### D-051 — A social binding's storm policy defaults to the platform's rate budget, never to unbounded\nDate: 2026-08-23\nWhen a trigger binding is attached to a source whose kind resolves to a social platform, the storm-policy fields default to that platform's computed budget (socialStormPolicyFor(row,'read') -> maxRuns / windowSeconds), surfaced through ExternalTriggerSourceAdminRow.social.rateBudget. Non-social sources keep the landed blank-means-unbounded default, untouched.\n\nWHY. The generic composer default is blank maxRuns = unbounded. On a metered platform that is not a neutral default, it is the wrong one in a way that stays invisible until it bites: an unbounded coalesce cap lets a single storm spend the whole quota day, after which the integration stops entirely until the quota rolls over. The owner attaching the binding has no way to know the right number, and the registry already does.\n\nThis composes with D-023 (a social binding defaults to coalesce-with-cap, never to unbounded) - that decision set the MODE at the store layer; this one sets the NUMBERS at the surface where a human chooses them, so the pane no longer offers a default the store would have to override.\n\nImplemented as stormDefaultsFor() in PlanTriggersPanel.tsx, applied both on dialog open and on source change. The composer additionally states the budget and its basis inline, plus two constraints that decide whether arming can work at all: the platform's owner-side wall (blockedOn - Meta app review, a TikTok audit) and whether its WRITE path is verified, since a reply/post action on an unverified write path is refused at run time.\nRelated: P-027\n\n### D-052 — D-052: acceptance is per-wave, and step 6 (\"the reply lands on the platform\") is owner-walled at EVERY wave — no lane may report it accepted\nDate: 2026-08-23\nBinding on every remaining platform lane (P-020 X, P-021 LinkedIn, P-022 TikTok) and on any future wave.\n\nTHE ACCEPTANCE LOOP, as P-028 states it, has seven steps: connect an account -> arm a binding -> a live inbound event launches a plan -> an agent drafts a reply -> the owner approves -> **the reply lands on the platform** -> the delivery ledger shows the trace.\n\nTHE RULING. Steps 1-5 and 7 are acceptable by an agent using fixtures and a simulated inbound event. **Step 6 is owner-walled at every wave and no amount of agent work clears it.** A lane may NOT report its platform, or its wave, as accepted on the strength of a simulated trace. Say \"code + simulated acceptance green; live acceptance blocked on <the specific wall>\" — never \"accepted\".\n\nTHE WALLS, derived from the platform registry (platform-registry.ts is authoritative; if this text ever disagrees with that file, the file wins):\n- Wave A (Bluesky, Mastodon, Reddit) — owner CREDENTIALS only: a Bluesky app password, a Mastodon instance account, a Reddit app registration. No external review. This is the cheapest wave to take live and the only one whose wall is not a third-party process.\n- Wave B (YouTube, Facebook Pages, Instagram, Threads) — YouTube needs the owner to approve the Google incremental-consent screen once; Facebook Pages / Instagram / Threads need META APP REVIEW (identity, legal and business verification, multi-week lead time).\n- Wave C (LinkedIn, TikTok, X) — LinkedIn partner review; TikTok audit (unaudited apps cannot direct-publish, so v1 targets the draft/inbox path); X paid-tier purchase authorization, a recurring cost outside agent authority under any mode (D-002).\n\nWHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A NOTE. The walls are invisible from inside a green test run: every adapter passes conformance, every surface renders, and the simulated trace completes end to end. A lane that measures only what it can run will conclude it is done. The registry already carries `blockedOn` per platform and the product renders it — a lane closing an item should read that field rather than infer readiness from a green suite.\n\nWHAT P-028 ACTUALLY VERIFIED (the honest scope of this item's close): both P-027 surfaces driven in a real Tauri shell with falsifiable `check` assertions plus a negative control — the social sources pane (all four D-050 cursor states, the sources=all|social nuqs filter, three distinct rate-budget bases) and the plan binding composer (SocialSourceNote, and D-051's storm-cap prefill re-deriving per selected platform). Fixtures were created through the real createOwnedExternalTriggerSource and deleted afterwards. The runbook is docs page `testing/social-platform-acceptance`, drift-anchored to the registry so a platform added later forces the page to be revisited.\nRelated: P-028, P-021, P-022, P-020\n\n### D-053 — A scope's PROSE never outranks the endpoint's own permissions table — and reply is not universal\nDate: 2026-08-23\nLinkedIn (P-021) falsified an assumption baked into the write contract since P-005: that every social platform can reply.\n\nTHE FACTS. LinkedIn's permissions reference (\"Getting Access\") lists the COMPLETE self-serve set — profile, email, w_member_social — and states \"Open Permissions are the only permissions that are available to all developers without special approval.\" The Posts API (POST /rest/posts) declares w_member_social, so POSTING is self-serve. The Comments API (POST /rest/socialActions/{urn}/comments) — the endpoint that actually creates a comment — declares w_member_social_feed, which is NOT in that set.\n\nTHE TRAP. w_member_social's own DESCRIPTION, in both the permissions reference and the Posts API table, reads \"Post, COMMENT and like posts on behalf of an authenticated member.\" So the scope's prose claims commenting while the commenting endpoint names a different scope.\n\nTHE RULING, extending D-030 (a bucket declaring a verb wins for that verb) one level up: the surface that DECLARES a verb wins for that verb. An endpoint's own permissions table outranks a scope description, because the table is what the authorization check reads. Reply therefore stays UNDECLARED for LinkedIn until a live call settles it, and the disagreement is recorded as contested in the row's notes rather than resolved by guessing. Declaring it on the strength of the prose would put a failing write on the owner's real public identity.\n\nCONSEQUENCES, all landed:\n- SocialWriteAdapter.reply became OPTIONAL, for the reason already stated on post/delete: a missing method is an ADAPTER gap, a missing registry verb is a PLATFORM limitation, and the two must stay separately reported. Requiring reply would force a throwing method that misreports the second as the first. SocialReplyCapableAdapter is the type a reply-implementing adapter returns, so callers keep static proof without ! assertions.\n- LinkedIn's reply refusal is now cased explicitly in resolveSocialReplyCoordinates. That seam runs BEFORE the write gate, so without the case the accurate reason was masked by \"no coordinate derivation for it YET\" — which would send a reader off to implement coordinates no scope would ever let them use.\n- Read is walled the same way: r_member_social is \"restricted ... available to approved users only\" and r_member_social_feed is \"granted to select developers only\". LinkedIn is the registry's first WRITE-ONLY platform.\n\nThis is D-034 firing a third time and in a third direction: not a phantom scope (Instagram) and not a missing one (Threads' threads_read_replies), but a scope whose DESCRIPTION overstates what it grants.\n\n### D-054 — blockedOn is a hard usability GATE, not a notes field — a partially-walled platform must not set it\nDate: 2026-08-23\nA near-miss worth recording, because the wrong version passed every unit test.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED. LinkedIn genuinely has owner-walled capabilities: reading anything, organization/page access, and a RECURRING 60-day re-authorisation (programmatic refresh tokens are partner-only, so an unattended connection stops working every 60 days until a human completes the browser flow). Describing those in the row's blockedOn was the natural move, and it was made.\n\nWHY IT WAS WRONG. assertSocialPlatformUsable THROWS on any row carrying blockedOn, before it ever reaches the write gate. So describing a PARTIAL wall there makes the WHOLE platform unusable — including the self-serve personal-posting path P-021 exists to deliver and had just verified. The adapter would have been unreachable at runtime while the suite stayed green. It was caught only because a sibling test asserted the refusal REASON ('unverified') and got 'owner-blocked' instead.\n\nTHE RULE. blockedOn means \"the platform cannot be used at all until the owner acts\". A row sets it only when what the row DECLARES is blocked. Walls on capabilities the row does not declare are already expressed structurally — read: null for a read wall, an absent verb for an unavailable one — and any remaining prose goes in policyNotes / auth.notes. platform-registry.test.ts now pins this both ways: a write-only row must explain itself in policyNotes, and assertSocialPlatformUsable('linkedin') must resolve.\n\nTHE GAP THIS EXPOSES, recorded rather than papered over: blockedOn is BOTH the hard usability gate AND the only owner-visible prose the admin pane renders (ExternalTriggerSocialAdminFacts has no policyNotes field). So a platform that is USABLE but carries an operational caveat has nowhere to tell the owner. LinkedIn's 60-day expiry is the first caveat to hit it and currently reaches no owner-facing surface. A separate advisory channel is the fix; it is pane work, not P-021.\n\nALSO SETTLED, both from derived systems reacting to LinkedIn becoming verified:\n- Trigger packs derive from platforms that are verified AND READABLE. A pack turns inbound events into plan runs and both shipped workflows (mention-triage, comment-digest) are read-built, so a write-only platform's pack could only be an empty shell — exactly the \"hollow row that reads as support\" D-002 already refused for X/Twitter. LinkedIn IS added to social-scheduled-crosspost, which is a write workflow it fully serves.\n- LinkedIn is the first platform whose REAL published budget (150 member requests/day) triggers storm-policy's window-widening branch; that branch existed from the start but had only synthetic coverage. The per-platform cap invariant was over-strict (it asserted the fixed 300s window unconditionally) and now permits a widened window only when the basis records windowWidened.\n\n### D-055 — CORRECTION to P-022's stated premise: unaudited TikTok clients CAN direct-publish — the real wall is SELF_ONLY visibility, and THAT is what makes `post` undeclarable. TikTok ships READ-ONLY, the mirror of LinkedIn\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23 against content-posting-api-get-started, content-sharing-guidelines, content-posting-api-reference-upload-video, content-posting-api-reference-get-video-status, tiktok-api-scopes, tiktok-api-v2-video-list and tiktok-api-v2-video-object.\n\nRETRACTION FIRST. P-022's item text says \"unaudited apps cannot direct-publish, so v1 targets the draft/inbox path\". That premise is FALSE, on two independent pages. Verbatim: an app \"can use this API in an unverified status, but all content uploaded via this endpoint will be restricted to private viewing mode.\" Unaudited clients may call Direct Post; nothing bars them from the endpoint.\n\nWHAT UNAUDITED ACTUALLY COSTS (content-sharing-guidelines, verbatim):\n- \"Unaudited API Clients can only post contents in `SELF_ONLY` viewership.\"\n- \"All user accounts using the API client to post must be set to private at the time of posting.\"\n- \"Unaudited API Clients can allow up to 5 users to post in a 24 hour window.\"\nThe restriction is on VISIBILITY and volume, not on endpoint access. The item's conclusion (do not ship direct posting in v1) survives; its reason does not, and the true reason is stronger.\n\nTHE RULING: `write.verbs: []`. TikTok is the registry's first READ-ONLY platform — the exact mirror of LinkedIn (P-021), which was its first write-only one. Neither TikTok write endpoint can honestly implement `post`:\n\n1. DIRECT POST is invisible. `SocialVisibility` is 'direct'|'followers'|'unlisted'|'public' and has NO self-only member; VISIBILITY_ALIASES even maps 'private' to 'followers'. So an unaudited direct post would silently DOWNGRADE every caller's requested visibility to invisible. The codebase throws SocialVisibilityWidened to prevent accidental WIDENING; this is that hazard's unguarded mirror. A reply nobody can see is worse than a refusal, because it reads as success.\n\n2. DRAFT/INBOX creates no post. `/v2/post/publish/inbox/video/init/` returns a `publish_id` and drops media in the creator's inbox; status reaches SEND_TO_USER_INBOX and only becomes PUBLISH_COMPLETE if a HUMAN opens the notification and finishes it in TikTok's editor. `SocialPostOutcome.externalId` is \"Platform id of the created post\" and `ref` exists \"so the caller can address it later\" — a publish_id is neither.\n\nREPLY AND DELETE DO NOT EXIST at this grant tier, with a positive control for the absence: the scopes reference is a complete table and DID return video.list, video.publish, video.upload and user.info.* — the instrument answered — and contains no comment scope and no delete scope. The Display API surface is user info + video list + video query only. (The Research API documents a comments query, but that is a separate vetted-researcher product.)\n\nNO CONTRACT CHANGE WAS NEEDED. `socialWriteRefusal` already refuses an undeclared verb with \"platform declares [], not 'post'\", which is the accurate report. Adding a `draft` verb for the inbox handoff was CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: nothing in the mention-triage or comment-digest workflows this plan exists to serve would ever call it, so it would be new surface with no caller.\n\nD-054 COMPLIANCE. The Content Posting audit is real owner-side work, but it walls capabilities this row does not DECLARE, so it must NOT be set as `blockedOn` — that would refuse the whole platform including the read path that works. It is recorded in `policyNotes` instead.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN. TikTok exposes no comment surface at all, so it can never serve mention-triage or comment-digest; its pack records new uploads and nothing else. If the owner ever completes the audit, SELF_ONLY lifts and `post` becomes declarable — the inbox path never does.\nRelated: P-022\n\n### D-056 — A BACKWARD-paging cursor is not a watermark: TikTok's cursor means \"posted BEFORE this instant\", so storing it inverts the read — and documented descending order is what licenses early termination (contrast D-025)\nDate: 2026-08-23\nVERIFIED 2026-08-23 against the v2 video-list reference.\n\nTHE VENDOR FACTS. `POST /v2/video/list/` takes `cursor` (int64) and `max_count` (int32, default 10, MAXIMUM 20) and returns `videos`, `cursor`, `has_more`. Verbatim: \"the cursor value is a UTC Unix timestamp in milli-seconds. You can pass in a customized timestamp to fetch the user's videos posted BEFORE the provided timestamp\", against a list \"sorted by create_time in descending order\".\n\nTHE TRAP. The obvious implementation — persist the returned cursor, send it back next pass — asks TikTok for everything OLDER than what we already have. It never returns a new item. And it does not fail: `has_more` stays true as it walks backward through the creator's history, so the adapter looks busy and healthy while emitting nothing new for as long as it runs. This is the same silent-success class the whole adapter contract was shaped around, arriving through a field that LOOKS like every other cursor in the registry.\n\nTHE RULING. TikTok's cursor is valid ONLY inside one pass. What crosses the pass boundary is OUR watermark, never sent to TikTok. Each pass: start with NO cursor (newest page), page backward via `response.cursor` while `has_more`, emit items with create_time > the watermark, and TERMINATE on the first item strictly below it.\n\nEARLY TERMINATION IS LICENSED HERE, AND D-025 IS WHY THAT NEEDS SAYING. D-025 FORBIDS \"stop at the first item older than the watermark\" for Facebook Pages, because its /feed is RANKED and an unseen item can sit behind a seen one. TikTok documents the opposite — descending create_time — and that ordering guarantee is the entire justification for the exit. The rule generalizes: an early exit is a claim about ORDERING, so it is legitimate exactly when the vendor documents the order and never merely because the data looked sorted. Recorded next to the code for the same reason: if TikTok ever drops that guarantee, this optimisation silently becomes D-025's bug.\n\nTERMINATE STRICTLY BELOW, NOT AT-OR-BELOW. `create_time` has one-SECOND resolution, so several videos routinely share the watermark second. Stopping at the first EQUAL item would drop its same-second siblings; a boundary-id set disambiguates which of them were already emitted.\n\nTWO UNIT TRAPS, both silent:\n1. `cursor` is MILLISECONDS and Video Object `create_time` is \"UTC Unix epoch (in seconds)\" — verified on the Video Object page. A 1000x slip throws nothing; it lands timestamps in 1970 or the year 56000, both of which compare cleanly and decide everything or nothing is new. Every crossing goes through named converters.\n2. The stored mark is an ISO string in a field called `watermark`, NOT the raw seconds, because `cursor-freshness.ts` derives the admin pane's \"last synced\" verdict from a small set of recognized field names. A bespoke numeric field is unrecognized, and the pane would report the platform NEVER SYNCED forever while it synced perfectly. Conforming costs one parse and no shared-code change.\n\nLOSS REPORTING. The page bound (maxPages) is OURS, not the vendor's, and hitting it with a watermark set IS unrecoverable loss: the watermark advances to the newest item emitted, so the next pass terminates even sooner and never reaches the skipped ones. That is reported as `lossRisk: capped-window-overflow` per D-031. Cold start is excluded — a bounded first read is intended, and reporting loss there would fire on every new connection and train readers to ignore the field. For scale: the default bound is 400 videos and TikTok documents a per-creator cap of roughly 15 posts/day, so it spans about four weeks of maximum-rate posting.\nRelated: P-022\n\n### D-057 — A test that needs \"an unverified platform\" must DERIVE it from the registry, never name one — the same exemplar has now moved three times as collateral damage from successful verifications\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRULING, binding on every lane in this plan and on anything later touching the social registry.\n\nTHE PATTERN. Several suites need an exemplar of a registry PROPERTY — \"a platform that is not verified\", \"a platform declaring no egress hosts\" — to prove a refusal path. Naming one reads well and rots silently: the moment that platform gets verified, which is the entire purpose of this plan, the test fails for a reason unrelated to what it tests.\n\nTHE EVIDENCE. The \"unverified platform\" exemplar has now moved THREE times, each time as fallout from a success, and each move left behind a comment explaining itself:\n- bluesky to linkedin (P-021)\n- linkedin to tiktok (P-021) — social-read.test.ts still carried the note \"tiktok, not linkedin: LinkedIn was this example until P-021 verified it\"\n- tiktok to whatever remains (P-022)\nP-022 hit five such sites at once across social.test.ts, social-read.test.ts, social-reply.test.ts and social-egress.test.ts. The tests were never wrong; they were pinned to an INSTANCE of a property instead of the property.\n\nTHE RULE. Ask the registry. `platform-exemplars.fixture.ts` exports `anUnverifiedPlatformId()` and `aNoEgressHostPlatformId()`, each deriving from `listSocialPlatforms()`. A suite says \"pick the unverified one\" and keeps testing the refusal for as long as a refusable row exists.\n\nWHAT HAPPENS WHEN NONE EXISTS is deliberately a LOUD FAILURE, not a skip. The fixture throws with a message saying the branch under test is no longer reachable from live data and needs a synthetic row — which is a real finding worth failing on, and is exactly the pattern `socialWriteRefusal` already documents for its own `write-unverified` branch (unreachable from real rows, so exercised synthetically). Silently skipping would let a refusal path quietly stop being tested at the moment it stopped being exercised.\n\nGENERALIZATION. This is the derived-truth ladder applied to test fixtures: a hardcoded platform id in a test is a second copy of a fact the registry owns. Prefer deriving; where a test genuinely needs a fixed subject, pin the PROPERTY it depends on rather than the id. The same smell appears wherever a test names a platform as an exemplar of a STATE (\"the write-only one\", \"the one with no cursor\") — those will move too.\nRelated: P-022\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: P-004 contract triage (D-025): papercusp/social-platform-integrations-2026-08-23 (\"Social platform integrations — social:* capability verbs + replay-safe trigger adapters fo\"): no plan update since 2026-08-26 (45 days idle), 27/28 items terminal, 0 open work-items sourced from it, and no ## Requirements bars to backfill a contract from; superseded in P-004 contract triage rather than given a fabricated contract. Forced by: su · su-f2a82 (`su-f2a82c74-67a6-4526-ac82-099159a51144`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"unified-app-template-2026-08-23","title":"Collapse the web/desktop app templates into one target-parameterised root","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Collapse the web/desktop app templates into one target-parameterised root\nslug: unified-app-template-2026-08-23\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-10-12\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** NOT COMPLETE — P-006 is the sole remaining blocked item. The six finished engineering items are code-truth audited and independently accepted: audit seq 1 at sha e5ac858c resolved 17/17 citations and verified 6/6 items; scorecard EI-21306988106058735 grades all six `unified-app-template-acceptance` criteria healthy (score10=10, missingKeys=[], fresh generation). D-009 records that verdict. It did NOT settle how `requires` picks a chassis, and `requires` is the hard half: `resolveRequiresClosure` (composition.ts:142) walks `requires` UNCONDITIONALLY, and `composeTemplates` (:228) errors if any pinned req is absent. So a single root CANNOT hard-require web-host OR tauri-desktop-shell.\n\nTHREE OPTIONS CONSIDERED:\n(a) `papercusp-app` requires neither chassis, and the `target` prompt tells the builder to add one. REJECTED: strictly worse than today — today `papercusp-webapp` hard-pins `papercusp-web-host`, so the chassis cannot be silently dropped. (a) makes a chassis-less app compose green.\n(b) Conditional requires (`when: {decisionPoint, equals}`). REJECTED: `requires` is evaluated with NO answers in hand (validateTemplateSet and the gym runner both call it registry-wide), so a conditional edge is unevaluable exactly where the closure is validated.\n(c) CHOSEN: extend the EXISTING `TemplateDecisionPoint` with an optional `selects` — the decision point that asks the question also names, per answer, the templates that join the composition.\n\n    decisionPoints:\n      - id: target\n        prompt: ...\n        selects:\n          arity: one-or-more\n          options:\n            - { value: desktop, templates: [{ id: papercusp-tauri-desktop-shell, version: 0.1.0 }] }\n            - { value: web,     templates: [{ id: papercusp-web-host,           version: 0.1.0 }] }\n\nWHY (c) IS THE SMALLEST EXTENSION: it is one more field on a surface that already exists and is already unioned per-template by `composeTemplates`; it directly implements the plan's own words (\"the `target` decision point SELECTS the chassis aspect\"); and it is checkable with NO answers, which is what killed (b).\n\nTHE STATIC GUARD (this is what replaces the lost hard pin): `composeTemplates` gains a selection-satisfaction rule evaluated structurally, no answers needed — for each selecting DP, count options whose templates are ALL present in the composition. If the DP has no empty option the axis is REQUIRED (>=1 satisfied); `arity:'one'` additionally caps non-empty satisfied options at 1. `target` has no empty option, so a chassis-less composition FAILS — the guarantee `requires` gave us is preserved, and `target: both` is expressed by satisfying two options.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR THE ANTI-DRIFT PIN: `normalized()` in templates-dir.test.ts compares decision points as `{id, prompt}` ONLY. Adding `selects` without widening that projection would leave the new field UNPINNED — yaml and TS could diverge silently. `normalized()` must carry `selects`, or this decision ships with a hole in its own guard.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Retirement = delete the four dirs + manifests; old refs survive as listing ALIASES, not as stub directories\nDate: 2026-08-24\nP-004 says \"retire as roots, keeping their refs resolving\". Two mechanisms were available; the choice is forced by an existing test.\n\nTHE FORCING CONSTRAINT: templates-dir.test.ts asserts `expect(dirs.sort()).toEqual([...known].sort())` — the set of directories under templates/ must EXACTLY equal the set of REFERENCE_TEMPLATES ids. So a retired root cannot keep a directory without also keeping a manifest, and keeping a manifest means it still enumerates in `templates:list` as a separate root — which is precisely what retiring it means to stop.\n\nTHEREFORE: the four dirs and their four reference manifests are DELETED, and the old refs resolve through an `aliases` field on the surviving root's listing.json, honoured by `resolveTemplate` in cupboard/template-store.ts (today: `templates.find(t => t.ref === key || t.id === key)`, :219). An alias hit resolves to `papercusp-app` and reports the alias it came in on, so `templates:new-app { template: 'papercusp-webapp' }` — the form live tool descriptions and in-flight materializes use — keeps working.\n\nSECOND-ORDER EFFECT, easy to miss: `guide-lint.ts` fails prose naming a template id that is not in the known set (:135). Every surviving template's GUIDE.md / reference README / checks README that names one of the four retired ids will FAIL the lint the moment their manifests go. Same for `composesWith` entries naming them (papercusp-web-host, papercusp-tauri-desktop-shell, papercusp-project-history, papercusp-release-pipeline, papercusp-ops-pots all do), which `validateTemplateSet` treats as registry rot when dangling.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-003 — `target: both` is ALLOWED — the tax is +1 check declaration, not a doubling\nDate: 2026-08-24\nP-005 measured the checks-union cost of `target: both` and the answer overturns the framing the template itself shipped with.\n\nMEASURED (via resolveSelection -> composeTemplates over REFERENCE_TEMPLATES):\n\n| selection | check declarations |\n|---|---|\n| `target: desktop, agents: none` | 4 |\n| `target: web, agents: none` | 4 |\n| `target: both, agents: none` | **5** |\n| `target: desktop, agents: pots` | 7 |\n| `target: both, agents: pots` | 8 |\n\nThree of the four declarations are SHARED and paid once either way (`papercusp-app:composition-integrity`, `papercusp-data-layer:components-integrated`, `papercusp-ui:components-integrated`). Each chassis contributes exactly ONE check — its `boot-e2e` — and that single check is the entire tax.\n\nRULING: `both` is allowed, and the existing gating (opt-in, never the default, `arity: one-or-more`, the `dual-target-is-opt-in` MUST) is sufficient in KIND. No new gate is needed. What was wrong was the DEGREE: the `target` prompt said \"the checks are what double\" and the MUST said it \"doubles the chassis check suites\". At the union level nothing doubles — the tax is +1 declaration (+25%). All three prose sites (the `target` prompt, the MUST rule in both `reference-templates.ts` and `templates/papercusp-app/template.yaml`, and `GUIDE.md` item 4) now state the measured numbers instead of an adjective.\n\nSCOPE OF THE CLAIM — any lane quoting this number must carry the caveat: it counts check DECLARATIONS, not seconds. The one declaration `both` adds is a build-the-app + boot-the-host + probe-health check, the most expensive kind there is, so wall clock grows by more than +25% and this measurement does not say by how much. A runtime figure requires materializing an app and running both suites; nobody should derive one from the count.\n\nPINNED, NOT PROSE: `templates/papercusp-app/checks/composition-integrity.test.ts` now asserts 4/4/5, the exact shared trio, and the exact two chassis checks, with failure output naming the drifted union — so a closure member that gains a check fails the pin and forces the three prose sites to be updated with it. Proven falsifiable in memory: +1 check on a chassis gives 4/5/6, +1 on the shared `ui` template gives 5/5/6.\n\nCONSEQUENT FIX (P-005 depended on it): that check file was executed by NO vitest config — `affected-tests.mjs` routes `templates/` to `@papercusp/template-kit`, whose include glob covered only `*.fixture.test.ts` siblings. Fourteen passing assertions ran nowhere, including the mechanical proofs behind three of the template's own `musts` (`thin-app-template`, `answer-target-first`, `agents-are-explicit`), each declaring `enforcedBy: \"composition-integrity\"`. That fact says NOTHING about whether mobile belongs there. `target` is an axis OVER A SHARED CLOSURE; the question is whether mobile has one to share.\n\nMEASURED (closures and component sets resolved from the manifests, not from memory):\n\n| | shares templates with desktop | shares COMPONENTS with desktop | with web | has papercusp-data-layer | has papercusp-ui |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `papercusp-android-app` | NONE | **NONE** | **NONE** | no | no |\n| `papercusp-iphone-app` | NONE | **NONE** | **NONE** | no | no |\n\nSet against what the two CURRENT `target` values share, the contrast is the whole decision:\n\n- `desktop` ∩ `web` = **7 shared components** — dock-workbench, embedded-pg-discovery, embedded-postgres-server, lexicon, papergrid, typed-contracts, ui-primitives.\n- desktop-only: hono-host, tauri-release-kit, tauri-shell. web-only: next-standalone-host.\n\nSo desktop and web differ by a CHASSIS and agree on everything else — that is precisely what makes one root able to serve both, and it is why `papercusp-app` can hard-require `papercusp-data-layer` + `papercusp-ui`.
