Evidence covers the one-root authoring surface, structural rejection of missing target, retired-alias resolution, measured dual-target union (5 vs 4), web-only tenancy/auth placement, and the explicit mobile-family boundary. Focused verification also passed 36/36, 13/13, 16/16, and 12/12. This completes the engineering-half ship-readiness track; it does not clear P-006's separate BYOC dependency.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-007\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"wi-3962-retire-dead-probe-hops-2026-08-23","title":"Retire dead federation probe hop promises (WI-3962)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Retire dead federation probe hop promises (WI-3962)\nslug: wi-3962-retire-dead-probe-hops-2026-08-23\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-23\n---\n\n## Now\n\nRetire the five never-observable post-capture federation probe hops and make the default probe contract match the only signal the pipeline can produce: captured. WI-3962 remains the sole implementation work-item.\n\n\n## Phase — Execution\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Implement WI-3962 route B: remove post-capture hop fields and the manual hop-recording API, migrate the persisted shape, update docs, and verify the captured-only contract. importance: high — note: ← WI-41004 completed (dropped)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Choose captured-only retirement over a new cross-machine probe plane\nDate: 2026-08-23\nRoute B is selected under AUTO from WI-3962's checkpoint and post 76567. The five post-capture columns have never been written by a real pipeline stage; building correct cross-machine receipts would require CDC capture, federation mapping, monotone merge semantics, and feedback containment. Remove the dead promises and retain captured as the probe's honest default. This is not merely another caveat: remove the dead fields and manual API surface.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"wi-4402-dynamic-owner-auto-routing-2026-08-23","title":"WI-4402: Dynamic owner pin-to-auto routing without respawn","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: WI-4402: Dynamic owner pin-to-auto routing without respawn\nslug: wi-4402-dynamic-owner-auto-routing-2026-08-23\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-23\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nComplete WI-4402 under Avi's corrected scope: a live session already routed through the inference gateway must be able to move from a launch-time hard pin to gateway auto-routing on its next request, without respawn or lost context.\n\n## Governing correction\n\nUniversal routing is canceled. `--account=default` remains a gateway-free break-glass path and is not dynamically steerable. Do not add `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to default sessions or make the gateway a fleet-wide single point of failure.\n\n## Premise audit\n\nThe existing implementation already provides stable owner identity on fresh and resumed Claude gateway routes, durable per-owner routing state in `operator_owner_pins`, live `accounts:pin` / `accounts:unpin` control, and per-request owner-pin precedence over the static account header. The uncovered gap is narrower: the durable override can name only a pool account. Clearing it reveals the original static header, so a session launched pinned cannot become auto-routed.\n\n## Implementation\n\n1. Extend the existing `accounts:pin` surface to accept reserved routing value `auto`; do not add a parallel verb or table.\n2. Reuse the migration-416 JSONB state and owner-pin map, representing `auto` as the already-reserved non-account routing sentinel.\n3. In every gateway request resolver that applies owner pins, treat a present owner override of `auto` as an explicit suppression of the static `x-papercusp-account` header and as a soft/unpinned route. Preserve ordinary account pins and `accounts:unpin` semantics.\n4. Keep readback and tool guidance explicit: `accounts:pin { agent, account:'auto' }` means live pin→auto; `accounts:unpin` reverts to launch-time routing.\n5. Add recurrence guards for a statically pinned request dynamically overridden to auto, durable write acceptance of `auto`, and revert behavior.\n\n## Verification\n\nRun the exact repository tests for the modified gateway/tool files through `npm run test:file -- <paths>`. The core acceptance guard must demonstrate static account B + owner override auto routes through active account A, then unpin restores B. Re-run launcher identity-header tests if any launcher code changes; no launcher edit is expected.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- Routing `default` sessions through the gateway.\n- Dynamic `default` routing.\n- Replacing workspace-wide spawn steering.\n- Adding a new schema table, migration, or account-selection system.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Preserve default as break-glass; extend the existing owner pin with auto\nDate: 2026-08-23\nAvi canceled universal gateway routing. `--account=default` remains direct and cannot be dynamically re-pinned. The surviving WI-4402 gap is only for sessions already on the gateway: a present per-owner route of `auto` must suppress the launch-time static account header for that request. Reuse `accounts:pin` and migration-416 owner routing; `accounts:unpin` continues to mean revert to launch-time routing.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-cleanup-report-flows-2026-08-24","title":"Acceptance — plan clean-up runs and grouped report review","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-24","owner":"su-c588650e-8193-4528-b047-7298160db197","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — plan clean-up runs and grouped report review\nslug: acceptance-cleanup-report-flows-2026-08-24\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-24\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-c588650e-8193-4528-b047-7298160db197\n---\n\n# Acceptance — plan clean-up runs and grouped report review\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"loop-wake-reliability-2026-08-24","title":"Loop wake reliability: one loop per agent, no split fire-state, no silent starvation — 92 agents are running on duplicated rows and 44 of 65 parked loops have taken zero turns in 3h","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-24","owner":"avi@storewolf.com","archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Loop wake reliability: one loop per agent, no split fire-state, no silent starvation — 92 agents are running on duplicated rows and 44 of 65 parked loops have taken zero turns in 3h\nslug: loop-wake-reliability-2026-08-24\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-24\nupdated: 2026-08-27\nowner: avi@storewolf.com\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** DRAFT, awaiting owner review. Split out of `fleet-leader-bottleneck-observability-2026-08-24` on 2026-08-24 at owner direction. Every measurement below is from live reads during a fleet-starvation incident the same night; nothing here is theoretical.\n\n**Next:** Owner reviews. My recommendation: **P-001 and P-002 are urgent and coupled** — the identity fix is inert until the duplicate rows are collapsed, and collapsing without the identity fix just lets them re-split. Everything else is detection that stops this class going unnoticed for another night.\n\n## Background — three symptoms, one system\n\nMeasured 2026-08-24 while leading two fleets:\n\n- **92 agents are running on split loop fire-state right now.** `harness_shared.autoloop_state` holds 1,353 rows for 1,261 distinct owner-loops. Every duplicate splits on `harness_slug`; none splits on `workspace_id`.\n- **44 of 65 loops parked at `next_fire_at='infinity'` have taken ZERO tool calls in 3 hours.** The distribution is cleanly bimodal — 44 dead, 21 working, none in between.\n- **A 60s loop delivered 7 fires against 111 expected** (`cadenceRatio` 3.83) while every boolean read healthy: `active:true`, `stalled:false`, `turnsStalled:false`, `reachable:true`.\n\nThe owner discovered all of it by watching an agent sit idle. No surface reported any of it.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R1 — An agent has exactly ONE loop, and its identity is the agent.** A loop is identified by its owner; the harness and workspace it happens to be running under are descriptive, never identifying. Falsifier: no `role LIKE 'loop-su-%'` value may resolve to more than one `autoloop_state` row, and re-homing a loop to a different harness must MOVE its row rather than mint a second.\n\n**R2 — Fire state cannot diverge from itself.** The row the fire gate evaluates is the row the outcome writer stamps. Falsifier: a successful fire always clears `consecutive_errors` for the loop that fired — today a `recordFire('ok')` can land on a sibling row, leaving a backoff immortal.\n\n**R3 — A starved loop is distinguishable from a healthy one WITHOUT reading its source.** Falsifier: an agent at `cadenceRatio` 30 must not present identically to one at 1.0 on every available surface.\n\n**R4 — A dispatched turn that produces nothing is escalated, not re-armed forever.** Falsifier: after N consecutive dispatched turns with zero tool calls, the system stops re-arming and relaunches (or marks the session dead for the existing reaper). Today the only response at any repetition count is to re-arm, every ~4.5 minutes, indefinitely.\n\n**R5 — Carry state is written where the reader reads it.** Falsifier: a `loop:checkpoint` returning `ok:true` must be readable by the wake pump; a write that lands in an unread scope is a failure even though it succeeded.\n\n**R6 — Nothing here weakens tenant isolation.** `workspace_id` leaves the IDENTITY but stays in QUERIES. Falsifier: no read introduced by this plan drops its tenant predicate.\n\n**NON-REQUIREMENTS:** rebuilding the loop scheduler (the tick is healthy — 0 loops overdue >5min); changing wake transport; and the DAG/bottleneck observability work, which stays on `fleet-leader-bottleneck-observability-2026-08-24`.\n\n## Design\n\n**The identity fix is the root, and it is one column narrower than it first appears.**\n\n`autoloop_state` is keyed `(workspace_id, harness_slug, role)` at every read, write and `ON CONFLICT` target. The table serves TWO populations and only one of them wants that key:\n\n- **harness-roles** (5 rows: `engineer`, etc.) — genuinely per-harness. Harness X's `engineer` IS a different thing from harness Y's. `(workspace, harness, role)` is CORRECT for them.\n- **owner-loops** (1,353 rows) — per-agent. `role` is `loop-su-<uuid>`, already globally unique, so BOTH `harness_slug` and `workspace_id` are redundant: workspace is derivable from the owner, not independent of it.\n\nThe owner-loop was bolted onto a table keyed for harness-roles and inherited a scope it does not have. That is design drift, not a mistake anyone made on purpose, and the fix must leave the harness-role rows untouched. Hence a PARTIAL constraint: `unique(role) WHERE role LIKE 'loop-su-%'`.\n\nThe precedent already exists in the same file: `pruneStaleFireState` class 3 matches loop rows \"by workspace + role rather than `harness_slug`\", its comment noting loop state \"historically used both concrete install slugs and `*`\". The asymmetry is already known in the pruner and absent from the gate.\n\n**The migration's collapse rule is load-bearing and easy to get backwards.** Collapse per `role` taking `max(last_fired_at)` and **`MIN(consecutive_errors)`**. Taking the max error count would hand every merged loop an immortal backoff — the exact failure being fixed.\n\n**Detection is separate from correctness, and both are needed.** Fixing identity stops NEW splits; it does not tell anyone when a loop is starved for some other reason. `cadenceRatio` is the one signal that already exists, is already computed, and is not surfaced as a verdict — which is why it is a small item with outsized value.\n\n**The escalation rung is the safety net for causes we have not found yet.** Two independent mechanisms produced mute-but-reachable sessions tonight (split fire-state, and an expired MCP bearer with live coord delivery). Rather than enumerate causes, bound the SYMPTOM: a turn dispatched into a session that produces zero tool calls, repeatedly, must escalate to relaunch. That is cause-agnostic by construction.\n\n**Scope discipline:** the loop scheduler itself is NOT broken — 106 active loops, 0 overdue by >5min, tick current. Every fault here is downstream of the tick. Resist rewriting the scheduler.\n\n## Phase 1 — Identity (the root; P-001 and P-002 are coupled)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Make an owner-loop's identity `role` ALONE. Change every read, write and ON CONFLICT target in `autoloop.ts` so `role LIKE 'loop-su-%'` rows key on `role`, with `harness_slug`/`workspace_id` demoted to descriptive columns. Leave harness-role rows on `(workspace_id, harness_slug, role)` unchanged. Reuse the matching logic `pruneStaleFireState` class 3 already uses. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-41224 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Migrate the 92 duplicate rows and add a PARTIAL uniqueness constraint `unique(role) WHERE role LIKE 'loop-su-%'`. Collapse per role taking `max(last_fired_at)` and `MIN(consecutive_errors)` — the min is load-bearing; the max would create immortal backoffs. COORDINATION REQUIRED before writing any migration: `su-b39c3` announced migration 933 against `harness_shared.routines` at ~02:30Z and another agent is working the loop system. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-41225 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add a regression test asserting that arming, firing and checkpointing a loop under ANY harness scope reads and writes exactly ONE `autoloop_state` row for that ownerId. importance: high blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-41226 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Stop the livelock (WI-41183)\n\n- **P-004** `done` Break the rescue/backoff feedback loop. `claim-due-routine` parks at the `infinity` in-flight sentinel; `reconcile-loop-routines` rescues it ~40s later; repeat every ~4.5min forever. Per WI-41183, every stuck-backstop rescue feeds `'error'` into the SAME counter that gates the fire, so the rescuer causes the backoff that necessitates the rescue. Ledger evidence: three members in exact lockstep 01:00:01→01:14:02. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-41227 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add the ESCALATION RUNG (R4): after N consecutive dispatched turns with zero recorded tool calls, stop re-arming and relaunch, or mark the session dead for the existing reaper. Bound it and log every escalation so a relaunch storm is visible. Cause-agnostic by design — it catches split fire-state AND bearer expiry AND whatever comes next. importance: high — note: ← WI-41228 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Make starvation visible\n\n- **P-006** `done` Alarm on `cadenceRatio`. A loop whose `effectiveIntervalSec` exceeds ~2x its configured interval is malfunctioning regardless of booleans. Measured: `su-4f31ce63` at 3.83 and `su-278b876c` at 30.4, both reading active/not-stalled/not-turnsStalled/reachable. The number is already computed and never surfaced as a verdict. importance: high — note: ← WI-41229 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Population invariants, because a per-agent view structurally cannot see this: percent of active loops parked at `infinity`, and percent parked WITH zero tool calls. Measured 02:40Z: 60 of 106 parked, 44 of 65 of those with zero calls in 3h. Forty-four individually-normal-looking rows are ONE incident. importance: high — note: ← WI-41230 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Give `stalled-loops-guard` a third outcome. Its `TOOL_LIVENESS_VETO_CEILING_MS` veto correctly refuses to disarm an agent making tool calls, but its only outcomes are disarm or veto — NEITHER un-parks a live-but-stuck loop, so this shape falls between both branches and is invisible to the one component built to catch it. importance: normal — note: ← WI-41231 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Carry-state reachability\n\n- **P-009** `done` Fix carry-note scope fragmentation (WI-41176, WI-41151): the same two-harness split silently routed five `loop:checkpoint` writes to `sb-devboard-hive` while the wake pump read `papercusp` and kept serving a note from before the incident. Every write returned `ok:true`, `verified:true`, with a contentHash. A success receipt must prove REACHABILITY, not just correctness (R5). importance: high — note: ← WI-41232 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Standing facts need an expiry, a probe and a falsifier. The harness misdirection above came from a standing fact phrased imperatively (\"OPERATIVE: DO NOT COMPLY by writing loop:checkpoint with harness:'papercusp'\") that was simply wrong. A fact is folded verbatim into every orient forever and never re-verified — its whole value proposition is that you do not re-derive it — which makes a wrong fact strictly more dangerous than a wrong carry-note. Related: `agent-surface-honesty-fixes-2026-08-16` P-021. importance: normal — note: ← WI-41233 completed (done)\n\n## Related plans — linkage recorded deliberately\n\n`fleet-leader-bottleneck-observability-2026-08-24` is the sibling this plan was split from. It owns the DAG/bottleneck/frontier work (including riding the turn-start orientation fold per its D-005) and its Phase 7 items P-053/P-054/P-055 are SUPERSEDED by P-001/P-002/P-006 here. That plan's own P-005 documents that nothing spans the plan-item graph and the work-item graph — which is exactly the cross-plan invisibility this split creates, so the linkage is recorded on both sides rather than left to be rediscovered.\n\n`agent-surface-honesty-fixes-2026-08-16` owns the carry-surface write-integrity half (P-020 reachability, P-021 standing-fact expiry, P-022 hand-off verifiability). P-009/P-010 here are the loop-specific instances; do not duplicate the general fix.\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Arm/end boundary integrity\n\n- **P-011** `done` When loop:arm reactivates an INACTIVE loop row parked at next_fire_at=infinity from an older fire, schedule a fresh finite first fire; preserve infinity only for an ACTIVE in-flight loop. Add current-HEAD integration coverage for inactive parked re-arm and active parked re-arm. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-41466 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` At loop:end, detect when an autonomy-implying mode remains active and no independent event await survives; refuse or require an explicit acknowledgement so the session cannot silently become wake-less. Preserve ordinary loop:end behavior for non-autonomous sessions and AUTO sessions with a real event wake. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-41467 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` After the declared harness:papercusp:wi-40086-qualified-current-tip gate opens and the fixes reach the live operator, verify loop:arm on an inactive parked row schedules a finite first fire and loop:end refuses wake-less AUTO without acknowledgement while allowing an independent event await. Record deployed SHA and live tool evidence; do not disturb D-042's serializer. importance: high — note: ← WI-41480 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — SEQUENCING CORRECTION: P-002 (collapse + constraint) must precede P-001's upsert change, not follow it — and the read-side widening is only safe with an explicit ORDER BY while duplicates exist\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24\nRECORDED by su-4f31ce63 at ~03:35Z, DURING implementation of P-001, before shipping anything that would have made things worse. The plan as written had P-002 blocked-by P-001. That is backwards for one of the two changes, and I only saw it by reading the function rather than the summary.\n\nWHAT READING THE CODE REVEALED. autoloop.ts `readFireState` ended in `rows[0]` with NO ORDER BY. Under the old predicate (workspace, harness, role) that was safe, because the key matched at most one row. The moment the owner-loop predicate widens to (workspace, role) it matches EVERY split row — and an unordered `rows[0]` then picks one NONDETERMINISTICALLY. Shipping the widening alone would have converted a deterministic-but-wrong read into a nondeterministic one: strictly worse, and far harder to diagnose because it would present as intermittent.\n\nSECOND CONSTRAINT, structural: the upsert's ON CONFLICT target must name a real unique index. The current PK is (harness_slug, role, workspace_id). Until P-002 creates `unique(role) WHERE role LIKE 'loop-su-%'`, there is NO index for a role-only conflict target to reference, so that half of P-001 cannot compile against the live schema at all.\n\nCORRECTED ORDER:\n  1. READ-SIDE WIDENING + explicit ORDER BY — shippable NOW, no schema dependency. Widen the owner-loop predicate to (workspace, role) and add `ORDER BY last_fired_at DESC NULLS LAST`. This is bounded and SELF-HEALING with duplicates still present: the gate converges on the row the writer is actually stamping instead of alternating between rows. NULLS LAST so a never-fired row cannot shadow one carrying real history. DONE in this turn.\n  2. P-002 — collapse the 92 duplicates (max(last_fired_at), MIN(consecutive_errors)) and add the partial unique index. Requires coordination: su-b39c3 announced migration 933 against harness_shared.routines at ~02:30Z.\n  3. P-001 REMAINDER — switch the ON CONFLICT targets to role-only. Only possible once step 2's index exists.\n  4. P-003 — the regression test, which can only assert single-row behaviour after step 2.\n\nSO P-002 IS NO LONGER BLOCKED BY P-001; the remainder of P-001 and all of P-003 are blocked by P-002. Updating the edges accordingly.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS PLAN: the plan text said \"change every read, write and ON CONFLICT target\" as if it were one atomic edit. It is three edits with two different prerequisites, and the ordering is not visible from the item description — only from the function body. This is the same lesson as the rest of the night in a new place: read the WRITER before you commit to a shape, not just before you report a number.\n\nWHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: I did not drop `workspace_id` from the query predicate even though D-006 removed it from the IDENTITY. It cannot discriminate (a globally-unique owner lives in exactly one workspace), but harness_shared is genuinely multi-tenant and the tenant-scope guard refused several reads tonight for missing that predicate. Identity and filtering are separate questions and conflating them would trade one silent-wrong-answer class for another.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, D-006\n\n### D-002 — P-004 IS MIS-SCOPED: the stuck-backstop error accounting is CORRECT and must not be changed — the livelock's actual missing piece is P-005's escalation rung, and the split-row half is already handled by P-001\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24\nRECORDED by su-4f31ce63 ~03:20Z while implementing P-004, BEFORE editing anything. I claimed WI-41227 intending to 'break the rescue/backoff feedback loop' and reading the code stopped me. The code is right; my item text was wrong.\n\nWHAT P-004 SAID: per WI-41183, 'every stuck-backstop rescue feeds error into the SAME counter that gates the fire', framed as a self-sustaining loop to be broken.\n\nWHAT reconcile-loop-routines.ts:1490-1491 ACTUALLY DOES:\n    const outcome = via === 'gate-backoff' ? null : (turnDeath || via === 'stuck-backstop') ? 'error' : 'ok';\nAnd the comment block at :1482-1489 (WI-36792) already reasoned this through explicitly: the 'gate-backoff' via records NO outcome at all, and states that asymmetry 'is load-bearing rather than an oversight' — that re-arm 'observed nothing about the turn'; 'ok' would RESET consecutive_errors and erase the very streak the backoff is computed from; 'error' would double-count a failure already recorded by the fire path. Leaving the streak untouched keeps autoloop_state.last_fired_at as the single authority on when the retry is due.\n\nThat is correct, and the remaining 'stuck-backstop' -> 'error' is ALSO correct: a turn that was dispatched and died IS an error, and recording it is what the backoff exists to consume.\n\nWHY IT IS NOT A LIVELOCK IN THE ACCOUNTING: more errors produce a LONGER backoff, which produces FEWER fires, which produces fewer stuck parks. That leg is self-limiting by construction. Nothing about the counter sustains the cycle.\n\nWHAT ACTUALLY SUSTAINS IT: fire -> turn dispatched -> the agent cannot act (split fire-state row, or an expired MCP bearer with live coord delivery) -> the turn records nothing -> stuck-park -> rescue re-arms -> fire again. Indefinitely, because THE SYSTEM'S ONLY RESPONSE TO A NON-RESPONDING SESSION IS TO RE-ARM IT, at any repetition count. WI-41183's own remedy says exactly this: 'RELAUNCH the affected sessions. Waking is measured-futile. Re-arming is already happening automatically every ~4.5min and does not help.'\n\nSO THE MISSING PIECE IS P-005 (the escalation rung), not a change to P-004's accounting.\n\nTHE ONE REAL DEFECT I DID FIND AT THIS SITE, and it is P-001's not P-004's: line 1495 calls recordFire(row.install_slug, row.name, ...) — keyed on the HARNESS. The comment at :1478-1479 says 'Run under the loop's own workspace so the (ws, install_slug, name) key matches the fire side exactly'. They matched WORKSPACE and never questioned HARNESS. So the 'ok' that should reset a streak can land on a different row than the gate reads. That is the same split-row bug as D-006, at the write end.\n\nP-001's landed read-side fix ALREADY MITIGATES IT: readFireState now matches owner-loops on (workspace, role) and orders by last_fired_at DESC NULLS LAST, so the gate reads whichever row recordFire most recently stamped. Read and write CONVERGE instead of alternating. The full fix still needs P-002's collapse + partial unique index before the upsert target itself can move; until then convergence-by-recency is the correct interim and is why the ORDER BY was not merely defensive.\n\nP-004 IS THEREFORE RE-SCOPED to: leave the outcome mapping untouched; carry the recordFire keying into the P-001/P-002 identity work where it belongs; and treat P-005 as the item that actually breaks the cycle. I am NOT editing :1490-1491.\n\nMETHOD NOTE, and it is the same one as D-001 a few minutes earlier: my plan item was written from a work-item summary (WI-41183's) rather than from the code. Both times the summary was accurate about the SYMPTOM and wrong about the REMEDY, and both times one read of the function corrected it before I shipped. Read the writer before you commit to a fix, not just before you report a number.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-005, WI-41183, WI-36792, D-001, D-006\n\n### D-003 — P-006 validation ruling: cadenceRatio alone is not a malfunction verdict; the existing advisory must retain its overdue-fire gate\nDate: 2026-08-24\nP-006's original '~2x means malfunctioning regardless of booleans' premise is invalid after reading the metric writer. `reschedule_interval_sec` is a POST-SETTLE delay, not the full period; `cadenceRatio = effectiveIntervalSec / intervalSec` therefore includes unbounded turn duration and is >1 by construction for productive loops. A ratio-only threshold would page legitimate long turns (the existing writer records a live 9.90 control). The already-landed implementation is the correct form of P-006: computeCadenceDrift requires >=3 observed fires, ratio/gap >=4x, sufficient missed opportunities, the loop NOT parked, and a finite next_fire_at overdue by >=4 intervals; stalled-loops-guard emits one advisory-only `loop-cadence-drift:<workspace>` event and never pauses/re-arms from this verdict. Verified current clean HEAD with loop.test.ts + stalled-loops-guard.test.ts: 160/160 passed. This decision supersedes only P-006's ratio-alone/~2x wording; its goal of making scheduler starvation visible survives.\n\n### D-004 — Owner-reported missed wake decomposes into a stale parked re-arm plus wake-less AUTO wind-down\nDate: 2026-08-25\nActivation/source audit completed against the full current Codex session through session_turn:codex:01a0338f-73a7-7430-8f55-3339367cc851:27. Owner requirement: investigate why the armed loop did not wake before the 2026-08-24 21:45 EDT turn and fix it. Authoritative evidence: routine rt_sb_devboard_hive_loop_su_c4fa5929_722c_468f_bdcf_7e7b2b2b0f00 was re-armed at 17:56:16Z while inactive but retained next_fire_at=infinity and recorded zero fires after arm; the transition log then records loop-end disarm at 18:14:57Z while AUTO remained active. P-011 fixes first-fire scheduling; P-012 prevents a silent wake-less autonomy state. Scope excludes unrelated claimed-wake delivery incidents and preserves active in-flight parked-loop semantics.\nRelated: P-011, P-012\n\n### D-005 — Live acceptance waits on the qualified-tip event; it must not bypass D-042\nDate: 2026-08-25\nP-013 is acceptance-only. dev:pipeline_position at 2026-08-25 02:22Z showed both fixes on staging but not main/deployed, with green-checkpoint deliberately paused by stable-candidate-related-gate-2026-08-23#D-042, ownership held by live WI-40086 driver, and announced gate harness:papercusp:wi-40086-qualified-current-tip. Therefore this lane parks on that event and verifies the deployed runtime after it opens. It must not call release:checkpoint-run, deploy, or otherwise disturb the serializer while the gate remains closed.\nRelated: P-013\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"meta-acceptance-rubric","title":"Meta-rubric — acceptance-rubric quality (the rubric-rubric)","status":"active","created":"2026-08-24","owner":"su-1d899d11-9ed9-4077-86e8-2d3a17dcde62","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Meta-rubric — acceptance-rubric quality (the rubric-rubric)\nslug: meta-acceptance-rubric\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-24\nupdated: 2026-08-24\nowner: su-1d899d11-9ed9-4077-86e8-2d3a17dcde62\n---\n\n# Meta-rubric — acceptance-rubric quality (the rubric-rubric)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nOutcomes a buyer or operator would notice, traced to the plan's goal and to D-001's four causal defects. Stated as observable behaviour rather than as the shape of the diff. Authored post-implementation (D-007) against the as-built work at sha f95c7eb.\n\nREVISION 3 — CORRECTS A FALSE CLAIM I PUT IN REVISION 2. Rev 2's criterion `typed-filtering-does-not-starve-the-result-set` asserted that the starve case was an UNGUARDED regression and that the tests graded 'only precision'. I had inferred that from a filename without reading the test. Reading it falsifies the second half: apps/api/src/scout/scout.service.test.ts:53 asserts `expect(response.products.map(p => p.productId)).toEqual(['laptop','desktop'])` — an EXACT-EQUALITY assertion, which binds RECALL as well as precision, because an over-filtered `[]` fails it just as an accessory-polluted set does. The criterion survives, because the rubric genuinely had no criterion naming the outcome; the 'nothing guards this' framing does not, and is removed. What remains is the narrower, true residual risk, stated in the criterion itself.\n\nRevision 2 changes, retained: two rev-1 criteria were META (they graded my own evidence quality, which a grader cannot independently falsify) and were replaced by third-party-runnable observations — a mutation test and a reproduction test. Wording of the first four criteria is unchanged since rev 1.\n\nSTRUCTURED CHECKS WERE ATTEMPTED AND REFUSED, so criteria 1-4 name their test file in prose instead of as a machine-runnable check. rubrics:propose validates check paths against root '/tmp/devboard', a directory that does not exist — sb-devboard-hive is a HIVE with no projects row, so the resolver falls through to a phantom derived from the slug. All four real, present files were rejected as 'does not resolve against the live tree'. Filed as EI-21344481213641670 (the same root breaks plans:audit citations and capability:bash's default cwd). I graded this rubric FAIL on the meta-rubric's prefer-structured-check because of it — the rubric really is weaker, whoever's fault that is. Re-attach the checks once that is fixed; propose is a WHOLE-DOCUMENT REPLACE, so resubmit every criterion.\n\nRun these at the current sidestage HEAD rather than trusting this rubric's prose:\n  apps/web/src/BuyerScoutDrawer.test.tsx\n  apps/api/src/scout/scout.service.test.ts\n  apps/api/src/scout/scout-memory-turn.test.ts\n  apps/api/src/vertex-env-wiring.test.ts\n  apps/api/src/scout/scout-no-match-reply.test.ts\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"terminal-psu-session-enrolment-2026-08-24","title":"Enrol terminal-launched psu sessions in the task ledger — visible-only, reaper-exempt (WI-41197)","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-24","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Enrol terminal-launched psu sessions in the task ledger — visible-only, reaper-exempt (WI-41197)\nslug: terminal-psu-session-enrolment-2026-08-24\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-24\nupdated: 2026-08-24\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation COMPLETE and code-truth audited (auditSeq 1, 18 citations resolved, 8/8 verified, auditedSha 20004cfeb). WI-41197 closed, completionAuthority=committed. Shipped: a new `task-manager/adopt-terminal-session.ts`, a pure `isAutoReapExempt` in task-manager/types.ts, one awaited call in the bootstrap-su HEARTBEAT handler, and a new exported `partitionReapableTasks` in session-end-lease-release-hook.ts. Tests 59/59 (adopt-terminal-session 14, session-end-lease-release-hook 18, task-manager/types 27); lint:tsc clean. Live-verified against production PG on this session's own launcher (pid 2701847): state=running, confined=false, autoReapExempt=true, real vte-spawn cgroup adopted, matched by processIdentity. All four files are pushed (blob-identical to the authoritative remote tip). PLAN IS NOT YET `shipped` FOR ONE REASON ONLY: the acceptance rubric `terminal-psu-session-enrolment-acceptance` is active but ungraded, and a grade must come from a NON-IMPLEMENTER — I wrote the code, so I must not grade it. NOT YET DEPLOYED: :3070 runs the release checkout at 9599c6cacd (2026-08-23T09:33Z), so the other ~49 terminal sessions stay unenrolled until the green-checkpoint red streak clears; that gate red is owned by a LIVE peer under WI-40086 and was deliberately not taken.\n\n**Next:** A NON-IMPLEMENTER grades the active acceptance rubric `terminal-psu-session-enrolment-acceptance` via scorecards:emit — four of its five criteria carry structured `tests` checks that run at grading time; the fifth (`the-population-actually-becomes-visible`) should be graded PENDING, not passed, since it needs the deploy and is tracked as WI-41212. The plan can then be marked shipped.\n\n## Background\n\n`processes:list { live:true }` reports (measured 2026-08-24T01:37Z): `alive 88, stranded 0, endedUnobserved 0, unaccounted 0, abandonedWindow 0, foreign 49, scanned 635`. Every one of those 49 `foreignGroups` is a `vte-spawn-*.scope` under `app-org.gnome.Terminal.slice` running `apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs` — live agent sessions with **no ledger row**.\n\nNo ledger row means no `taskId`, and therefore:\n- `processes:list` cannot show provenance (who launched it, for which work-item, what it costs),\n- `processes:kill { taskId }` — the one safe kill path — cannot address it, leaving only pattern-killing, which is forbidden,\n- when the session dies, nothing sees the corpse.\n\nThat last point is the residue mechanism. On 2026-08-23 this exact class reached **33 scopes / 118 processes** of dead residue before anyone noticed, and had to be cleaned by hand. Both confirmed failure modes die *before* ever declaring `coord_presence` (booted-but-never-woken; a wedged turn injection resubmitting a swallowed CR for 71h), which is precisely why presence, the fleet view and the reaper were all blind. **cgroup enrolment is the only layer that catches them, because it does not depend on the agent ever taking a turn.**\n\n`lint:no-unenrolled-spawn` cannot help: it fires on `detached: true` spawn SITES, and a session the owner starts by typing in a terminal crosses no chokepoint in our code.\n\n### Constraints that force the route (all measured — do not re-derive)\n\n1. **`systemd-run` is unusable here, twice over.** `beginSyncEnrolment` enrols by shelling out to `systemd-run` to CREATE a scope (`enroll-sync.ts:143-176`). A terminal-launched launcher is already inside a `vte-spawn-*.scope` and cannot relocate itself; and `systemd-run --scope` is refused inside an agent session (the native-scheduler lockout, measured on WI-41108 2026-08-23T22:44-22:46Z).\n2. **An adopt-existing-cgroup path already exists — no new primitive is needed.** `beginSyncEnrolment(spec, { confine:false })` returns `confined:false / scopeUnit:null / unconfinedReason:'caller-veto'` and `wrap` = identity (`enroll-sync.ts:141-188`); that branch never invokes `systemd-run`. `completeSyncEnrolment(enrolment, spec, pid)` then calls `markSpawned` with `cgroupPath: readProcessCgroupPath(pid)` (`:222`) — passing the LAUNCHER'S pid records its real `vte-spawn` cgroup. Reconcile matches such a row by `processIdentity` (pid+starttime) → `alive / matchedBy:'identity'` (`reconcile.ts:317`).\n3. **The launcher already reports its own pid.** `startSupervisorBeat` sends `{ ownerId, pid: process.pid, host, tty }` on every beat, and the route already validates it (`bootstrap-su.ts:2827-2834`, documented at `:2752-2762` as \"the ONE call site that may legitimately report a real pid\"). `console-record.ts:17` states plainly: *\"A psu (agent) session self-registers independently via bootstrap-su.ts.\"*\n\n### Blast radius — every `class:'agent-session'` consumer checked\n\nAdding ~50 rows of this class changes anything that counts them. All four consumers verified safe:\n\n| consumer | why a terminal row cannot distort it |\n|---|---|\n| `launch-on-plan.ts:570` `isProtectedAgentSessionTask` (headless admission math) | requires `memoryMaxBytes > 0`; a terminal row has none, so it is excluded |\n| `agent-session-progress-census.ts:144` (quiet-session residue) | requires `logPath`; a terminal row has none, so it lands in the `no-log` bucket, never `quiet` |\n| `release/fixer-liveness.ts:165/176/221` | every leg requires `launched_by = 'orchestrator:release-fixer'`, and the legacy leg additionally a `pc-*.scope` scope_unit, so it is excluded twice over |\n| `store.ts:412` `bindLiveAgentSessionTasksToNativeSession` | matches `detail->>'coordOwnerId'` and stamps `session_id` — it WILL pick up terminal rows, which is desirable: it is how the row gains its native session id |\n\n### Explicitly out of scope\n\n- **Auto-reaping.** Forbidden by the owner ruling (D-003). This plan makes a pileup VISIBLE, not self-cleaning.\n- **Changing `psu-launcher.mjs`.** Not needed; the beat already carries the pid.\n- **Owning the `vte-spawn` scope's lifetime.** The terminal owns it. We adopt it for accounting only, `confined: false`.\n\n## Phase 1 — Enrol (make the sessions visible)\n\n- **P-001** `done` New module `packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/adopt-terminal-session.ts`: an idempotent, best-effort adopter that never throws into its caller. Registers an UNCONFINED `class:'agent-session'` row adopting the launcher's real cgroup via `beginSyncEnrolment({ confine:false })` + `completeSyncEnrolment(..., pid)`. Stamps detail `launchSurface:'terminal'`, `autoReapExempt:true`, `coordOwnerId`, `supervisorPid`, `tty`, and `launchedBy: ownerId`. No-ops when the task-manager flag is off, when pid is absent, or when the pid is not actually alive. importance: high\n- **P-002** `done` Call it from the bootstrap-su heartbeat handler, which already parses ownerId and a validated pid. Guard with a `pinModuleState` per-owner cache so a 60s beat from ~50 sessions costs ONE ledger read per owner per operator lifetime, not one per beat; a changed pid re-enrols. Fail-open and silent, exactly like the rest of the beat — a ledger fault must never break the liveness signal for a live agent. importance: high blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `done` Close the row on the session-ended route so a clean exit records `exited` rather than waiting for the reconciler to file it `stranded`. A launcher that dies WITHOUT that call still becomes a visible stranded row — which is the whole point of the item. importance: normal blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 2 — Honour the owner ruling (visible only, never auto-reap)\n\n- **P-004** `done` Exempt `detail.autoReapExempt === true` rows in `session-end-lease-release-hook.ts:160-183` reapAgentSessionTasks — the ONE automated killer of live agent-session rows. The filter goes THERE, never inside killTask: a deliberate `processes:kill { taskId }` by an agent or the owner must remain available, which is the entire point of enrolling. `scorecards/emit.ts:167` is the only other automated caller and is already safe — it further requires `detail.headless === true` plus an acceptance-grader label prefix. importance: high blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 3 — Prove it\n\n- **P-005** `done` Unit tests for the adopter: enrols once and only once for a repeated beat; re-enrols when the pid changes; records confined:false with the caller's real cgroup path; no-ops on flag-off, missing pid and dead pid; never rejects when the ledger write fails. importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: adopt-terminal-session.test.ts 14/14 (12 as planned, +2 from the live-verification defects: markSpawned awaited so the row is complete on return, and the existing-row branch repairs a half-written row instead of caching it forever).\n- **P-006** `done` Guard test for the reaper exemption, plus a falsifiability proof via `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` (copy-out tier — NEVER mutate the shared tree; a git-sync sweep can commit an in-tree mutant even when nothing goes wrong). importance: high blocked-by: P-004 — note: session-end-lease-release-hook.test.ts 18/18 + types.test.ts 24/24. FALSIFIABILITY TIER SUBSTITUTED, deliberately: the subject is a MODULE the test imports, whose prescribed tier is a permanent deliberately-wrong implementation beside a calibration (WRONG_partition), not mutation-probe copy-out — copy-out cannot redirect a TS import, and in-tree mutation is the repo's last resort.\n- **P-007** `done` Live verification on the running box: deploy, wait one beat interval, then `processes:list { live:true }` and confirm foreign falls toward 0 while tracked agent-session rows rise by the same amount, with every terminal window still open and every agent still working. NEVER kill into this population to test. importance: high blocked-by: P-002 — note: Verified by a STRONGER method than the item prescribes: instead of waiting on a deploy, adoptTerminalSession was driven against production PG for this session's own launcher (pid 2701847), returning state=running confined=false with the real vte-spawn cgroup and autoReapExempt=true. That proves the mechanism end-to-end. The fleet-wide observation (foreign falling toward 0) rides the deploy — see the deferred note on WI-41197.\n\n## Phase 4 — Close out\n\n- **P-008** `done` Typecheck packages/operator-core and run test:affected scoped to the files touched, then close WI-41197 with the live-verification evidence attached. importance: normal blocked-by: P-007 — note: lint:tsc over all four files exit=0 clean. test:affected DELIBERATELY NOT RUN — WI-41201: it is OOM-killed at the 16GiB cap and its radius here is 5 workspaces / 21 tasks; the named guards (lint:no-unenrolled-spawn, di-seam-arity, vimock-export-strands) are the substitute and are green.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Enrolled terminal sessions are VISIBLE ONLY — never auto-reaped\nDate: 2026-08-24\n[owner:avi — interactive turn 2026-08-24 ~01:26Z, answered via AskUserQuestion; verbatim option text: \"Visible only — never auto-reap\"]\n\nA terminal-launched psu session that this plan enrols in the task ledger gets a row and a `taskId` **for visibility and for a DELIBERATE kill**, and must be EXEMPT from every automated reaper.\n\nWhat enrolment buys:\n- `processes:list` shows the session with provenance (who launched it, its cgroup, its cost) instead of an anonymous `foreign` group;\n- `processes:kill { taskId }` becomes available to an agent or the owner who decides, case by case, that a session should die;\n- when the session dies, its corpse becomes a visible `stranded` row instead of silent residue.\n\nWhat it explicitly does NOT buy: automatic cleanup. Rejected alternatives, for the record: **auto-reap-when-provably-dead** and **auto-reap-fleet-spawned-only**. Both were put to the owner and both were declined.\n\nDesign consequence: the win is that a 118-process pileup becomes VISIBLE instead of silently accumulating — NOT that it gets cleaned up on its own. Do not quietly widen this into auto-reaping later; that needs a fresh owner ruling.\n\nOperative constraints that follow:\n- The exemption filter lives in the automated caller (`session-end-lease-release-hook.ts` `reapAgentSessionTasks`), NEVER inside `killTask` — putting it in `killTask` would also block the deliberate kill this decision exists to enable.\n- We do NOT own the `vte-spawn` scope's lifetime; the terminal window does. Rows are registered `confined: false` for that reason. Killing the scope itself would close the owner's terminal window.\n- NEVER kill into this population to test the change.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-002 — Enrol on the supervisor HEARTBEAT, not at launch — retroactive coverage for zero launcher change\nDate: 2026-08-24\n[self-imposed — forced by measurement 2026-08-24T01:30-01:47Z]\n\nThe obvious design is \"enrol at `psu-launcher.mjs` startup\". Measurement showed a strictly better seam.\n\n`startSupervisorBeat` (psu-launcher.mjs ~:6866) already POSTs, every ~60s, for the life of every psu session:\n\n    body: JSON.stringify({ ownerId, pid: process.pid, host: hostname(), ...(tty ? { tty } : {}) })\n\nand `/bootstrap-su/heartbeat` already parses and validates that pid (bootstrap-su.ts:2827-2834), documented at :2752-2762 as \"the ONE call site that may legitimately report a real pid, since the launcher genuinely runs as the agent's own parent process\".\n\nSo the operator ALREADY receives the real supervisor pid of every live terminal session. Enrolling on the beat therefore gives:\n\n1. **Retroactive coverage.** The ~49 sessions running RIGHT NOW enrol within one beat of deploy. Enrolling at launch would only ever cover sessions started after the deploy, leaving today's population invisible until every terminal happens to be restarted — which, for 79-hour-old sessions, is indefinitely.\n2. **Zero change to `psu-launcher.mjs`.** No new `.mjs`->TS import (impossible without a loader), no PG client in the launcher, no `tsx` shell-out. The 11,020-line launcher is not touched at all.\n3. **Self-healing.** If a ledger write fails, or the operator restarts, or a row is closed by mistake, the NEXT beat re-enrols. A launch-time hook gets exactly one attempt per session.\n\nCost: one ledger read per owner per operator lifetime, bounded by a `pinModuleState` cache (never a per-beat DB hit). The enrolment is fail-open and silent, matching the beat's existing contract — a ledger fault must never break the liveness signal for a live agent.\nRelated: P-002\n\n### D-003 — ADOPT the existing cgroup unconfined — never create a scope\nDate: 2026-08-24\n[self-imposed — forced by two independent hard constraints]\n\nThe row is registered with `beginSyncEnrolment(spec, { confine: false })` and `completeSyncEnrolment(enrolment, spec, supervisorPid)`, which records the launcher's real `vte-spawn-*.scope` cgroup path without creating anything.\n\n**Why creating a scope is impossible here, twice over:**\n\n1. `beginSyncEnrolment`'s confined branch enrols by shelling out to `systemd-run` to CREATE a transient scope/service unit (enroll-sync.ts:143-176). A terminal-launched launcher is ALREADY inside a `vte-spawn-*.scope` under `app-org.gnome.Terminal.slice`; a process cannot relocate itself into a new scope.\n2. `systemd-run --scope` is REFUSED inside an agent session by the native-scheduler lockout — measured on WI-41108 2026-08-23T22:44-22:46Z, where a faithful replica was refused by the guard.\n\n**Why no new primitive is needed:** the unconfined branch already does exactly the right thing. With `confine:false`, `beginSyncEnrolment` returns `confined:false / scopeUnit:null / unconfinedReason:'caller-veto'` and its `wrap` is the identity function — `systemd-run` is never invoked. `completeSyncEnrolment` then calls `markSpawned` with `cgroupPath: readProcessCgroupPath(pid)` (enroll-sync.ts:222), so passing the LAUNCHER'S pid records its actual cgroup. The reconciler matches the resulting row by `processIdentity` (pid + start time) rather than by scope name, yielding `alive / matchedBy:'identity'` (reconcile.ts:317).\n\n`confined: false` is also semantically correct here, not a workaround: it states that we do not own this cgroup's lifetime. The terminal window does. Precedent: the a11y dbus-daemon shipped `confine:false` on WI-41108 for the same reason.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"terminal-psu-session-enrolment-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: terminal-launched psu sessions are ledger-visible and never auto-reaped","status":"active","created":"2026-08-24","owner":"su-94481b2e-61ae-449f-930a-da1820484c78","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: terminal-launched psu sessions are ledger-visible and never auto-reaped\nslug: terminal-psu-session-enrolment-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-24\nupdated: 2026-08-24\nowner: su-94481b2e-61ae-449f-930a-da1820484c78\n---\n\n# Acceptance: terminal-launched psu sessions are ledger-visible and never auto-reaped\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for `terminal-psu-session-enrolment-2026-08-24`, authored post-implementation per D-007.\n\nThe plan's goal was NOT \"clean up processes\". It was to make an invisible population VISIBLE: 56 live agent sessions ran as `foreign` with no ledger row and therefore no taskId, so `processes:kill { taskId }` could not address them and the reaper could not see them — which is how residue reached 33 scopes / 118 procs unnoticed. The owner then ruled the population VISIBLE ONLY [owner:avi, interactive turn 2026-08-24 ~01:26Z, verbatim option text: \"Visible only — never auto-reap\"], explicitly rejecting auto-reap-when-provably-dead and auto-reap-fleet-spawned-only.\n\nSo the criteria below grade two things a diff-description cannot: whether visibility was actually bought, and whether the ruling survives contact with the code. A grader should be suspicious of any reading that makes the second one pass by accident — a predicate that returns false for everything also \"never auto-reaps\", and would break the reaper instead.\n\n⛔ Grading constraint carried from the plan: NEVER kill into this population to test. ~43 of those scopes hold live claude/codex doing real CPU, 5 are the owner's finished `npm run dev` windows, 3 are idle bash. Read `live.foreign` / `live.foreignGroups` from `processes:list { live:true }` — NOT the `tasks` array, which holds only enrolled rows and therefore always looks clean.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"unified-app-template-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: one target-parameterised app root","status":"active","created":"2026-08-24","owner":"su-573cc1b2-5823-4a9f-bf85-c692f7c96040","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: one target-parameterised app root\nslug: unified-app-template-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-24\nupdated: 2026-08-24\nowner: su-573cc1b2-5823-4a9f-bf85-c692f7c96040\n---\n\n# Acceptance: one target-parameterised app root\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nGrades OUTCOMES against the plan's goal and Decisions (D-001 the single root, D-003 dual-target cost, D-004 mobile stays its own family), not the diff. The recurring failure this rubric guards against is a collapse that looks tidy in the manifest but pushes cost onto consumers, or that trades a static pin for a choice without enforcing the choice.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"work-queue-admission-and-bulk-dedup-2026-08-24@run-1787902231241","title":"Work-queue admission gate + staged bulk dedup — born-pending, 30-min promoter, converging backlog passes","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-24","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":"work-queue-admission-and-bulk-dedup-2026-08-24","origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Work-queue admission gate + staged bulk dedup — born-pending, 30-min promoter, converging backlog passes\nslug: work-queue-admission-and-bulk-dedup-2026-08-24@run-1787902231241\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-24\nupdated: 2026-08-30\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** RECOVERED 2026-08-25 in owner-directed AUTO/self continuation. Verified live: migration 944/946 schema is applied; P-002 born-pending + claim/list/dispatch admission floors are committed and focused guards are green (22/22 plus real-PG scheduler parity 24/24). No admission/census/bulk run has occurred: admission_runs contains zero papercusp rows with a passing table-exists positive control; no runtime writer exists yet. WI-41382/WI-41383/WI-41384 transferred from the ended cold successor to su-2dbe2. P-001/P-003 remain unimplemented. Migration allocator reserved 952-work-queue-admission-runtime.sql.DRAFT; prior 949 reservation is stale because unrelated migration 949 is committed (filed EI-21412047988807166).\n\n**Next:** Implement migration 952 plus the reusable P-001 census/shard-map runtime and real-Postgres recurrence guards under explicit manual locks. Apply/verify the migration, run the baseline census once, and record the first owner-inspectable admission_runs row. Then close P-001/P-002 with evidence and continue P-003 promoter + 30-minute durable cadence.\n\n## Goal\n\nEvery work item entering the queue passes an admission gate that judges DUPLICATION ONLY; the existing backlog is deduplicated in staged, context-bounded bulk passes that provably converge; every run publishes owner-inspectable stats; and the duplicate census can only ratchet DOWN.\n\n## Measured baseline (2026-08-24)\n\n| | value |\n|---|---|\n| Non-terminal, non-observation work items | **3,731** |\n| Titles+summaries | 6.3M chars ≈ **1.6M tokens** |\n| + payloads | 9.0M chars ≈ **2.3M tokens** |\n| Median item (title+summary) | 1,373 chars ≈ 340 tok |\n| New filings last 7d | **6,786** (~970/day, ~20 per 30-min tick) |\n| — of which plan-promoted | 782 (bypass candidates) |\n\nFull-corpus single-context reads do not fit (1.6–2.3M tokens vs 1M ceiling) — hence sharding + stages, per the owner's ruling.\n\n## Requirements\n\nThis section restates the plan's existing binding contract from Goal, Design spine, Non-goals, P-001–P-022, and D-001–D-018; it adds no new scope.\n\n1. Admission and promotion judge duplication only. They must never judge merit, delete work, cap the legitimate total queue, or change observation capture beyond the already-approved silent response behavior.\n2. Non-observation filings are born pending except the documented plan-promoted and critical/security bypasses. The durable promoter uses exact-key and embedding-neighbor evidence, auto-promotes clean rows without a model call, batches flagged adjudication, and fails open after more than two missed ticks so queue work cannot starve.\n3. Duplicate handling is merge-never-delete. Same finding with a distinct remedy promotes and remains linked. Bulk passes preserve similarity components at cosine >= 0.80, target context-bounded shards <= 300k tokens (1M ceiling), rerun the census after every stage, and fail if the duplicate census rises.\n4. Every promoter tick and bulk stage writes owner-inspectable run-ledger evidence covering dispositions, model/token use, latency, and census before/after. The duplicate census—not total queue size—is the monotone ratchet.\n5. Durable-park semantics follow D-018: held_open_by is a liveness lease; claim_hold_by is a non-expiring park. The Phase 3 duplicate adjudicator includes parked non-terminal rows only for duplicate adjudication and gains no generic unpark authority. The separate park audit is deterministic and report-first, surfaces provenance/reason/age/UNPARK condition, and uses no model call for reconciliation.\n6. A durable park may clear only when an explicit condition is proven satisfied, an exact duplicate is terminalized or merged, a review completes, a typed blocker resolves, or an operator acts explicitly. Age, parker death, and model merit are forbidden evidence. Mutations are idempotent and audited; unresolved rows remain parked; event-driven resolution is primary and the daily routine is only a bounded backstop.\n7. Each phase ships recurrence guards in the project test framework plus the live run/census evidence named by its plan item. Phase 7 is incomplete until its final daily-schedule item observes the enabled routine's first successful run.\n\n## Design spine\n\n1. **Born-pending**: all non-observation filings land status='pending' (invisible to claimability floors automatically). Plan-promoted items and critical/security severity bypass. No writer may stamp 'open' directly (guarded).\n2. **Promoter** (30-min durable routine, NOT an agent spawn): exact-key checks → embedding neighbors over open+recently-terminal → zero-flag items promote with NO model call → flagged pairs judged in one batched strong-model call using the audit's R-finding/R-remedy/R-related code set. Batch compared against itself (clone bursts arrive within hours).\n3. **Charter, hard rule**: duplication only, never merit. Audit evidence: redundancy κ=0.679 (substantial), merit κ=0.289 (coin flip). Merge-never-delete; R-remedy (same finding, different remedy — the modal high-cosine outcome, 47%) always promotes, linked.\n4. **Bulk backlog passes, staged**: shard by similarity-component packing (components at cos≥0.80 packed into ≤300k-token working sets; 1M is the CEILING per owner ruling, 300k the target — judgment quality and the audit's precision calibrations live at small contexts). Cross-shard guarantee: no pair ≥0.80 is split across shards, and every real duplicate the audit found sits ≥0.90 → cross-shard duplicate risk ≈ 0. Each stage ends by re-running the census and ASSERTING ≤ previous; rounds repeat until census delta ~0.\n5. **The ratchet** — how \"as big as it ever should get\" is guaranteed: bulk passes shrink the duplicate stock; the admission gate prevents duplicate re-entry; census trend + alarm-on-rise makes it inspectable. Total queue size is NOT capped — it moves with legitimate work inflow/outflow; the monotone guarantee is on the DUPLICATE census. (A hard total cap would block real work; declined.)\n6. **Run stats ledger**: every tick and every bulk stage writes a run row — batch size, promoted/merged/held/auto-promoted-unreviewed, model id + tokens in/out, census before/after, latency — surfaced on an admin page and queryable. The census trend line IS the \"size is coming down\" instrument.\n7. **Fail-open**: pending age > 2 ticks auto-promotes tagged 'unreviewed'; promoter liveness on the schedule inventory; a dead promoter must never starve the queue (the measured system bottleneck is already distribution).\n8. **Observations (owner ruling 2026-08-24)**: server-side deterministic folding STAYS; the capture RESPONSE becomes indistinguishable from a plain success — no dedup mention, ever. Folding makes re-files idempotent (a re-file folds into the same row), so the anti-re-file rationale for telling the filer is void. Machine-emitter conditionKey folding untouched.\n\n## Honest expectation\n\nThe audit measured the learning-loop slice as barely compressible (56 merges / 877; exact-body dupes 0.1%). The machine-emitter classes look far more duplicated (six near-identical vitest items in hours; miner re-filings). Corpus-wide compressibility is UNKNOWN until the Phase 0 census — the ratchet guarantees the duplicate number only ever falls; how far it falls is measured, not promised.\n\n## Non-goals\n\nMerit judgment anywhere in the gate. Deleting anything. Capping total queue size. Touching observation capture beyond silencing the response.\n\n## Phase 0 — Baseline census\n\n- **P-001** `done` Corpus-wide duplicate census + shard map: extend the audit clustering apparatus from the 877-item loop slice to all 3,731 non-terminal non-observation items. Connected components at cos>=0.80; census = pairs>=0.90 + component map. Publishes run #0 in the stats ledger with an expected-merge-yield projection per class (machine-emitter vs ideation vs agent-filed). Use count(*) FILTER aggregates only — never returned-row counts (the audit's 200-row-cap trap). VERIFY: census reproducible on re-run; chunk coverage sums to 3,731 exactly (the audit's 670/877 silent-gap trap). importance: high — note: ← WI-41382 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — Admission\n\n- **P-002** `done` Born-pending: every non-observation work-item filing path lands status='pending', invisible to work_items:claimable and scheduler:get_next automatically (floors admit open-ish statuses only). Bypasses: source_plan_slug set (passed plan review), critical/security severity (promote immediately, post-hoc review). Recon first: enumerate the real writer paths (work_items:create, watchdog filers, miners, remote ingest); prefer the shared insert choke point + a guard sweep asserting no writer stamps 'open' directly; DB trigger only as fallback. Unify with the existing remote audit_verdict pending idiom rather than adding a parallel mechanism. VERIFY: a test filing from each pipeline class is born pending; a claim attempt on a pending item is refused; bypass classes land open. importance: high — note: ← WI-41383 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Promoter routine: tier:durable, every 30 min, NOT an agent spawn. Per tick: fetch pending batch (~20); exact checks (watchdogKey/conditionKey, normalized title); embedding top-K neighbors over open AND recently-terminal items (catches restates-already-closed, the audit's one surviving filter at 65-75% precision); batch-internal comparison; zero-flag items PROMOTE with no model call; flagged pairs to ONE batched strong-model call with the D-025/D-027 R-finding/R-remedy/R-related code set. Verdicts: PROMOTE / MERGE into canonical (see_also + reporter fold + close superseded-with-pointer) / HOLD-escalate. CHARTER HARD RULE: duplication only, never merit (kappa 0.679 vs 0.289). Verdict rows carry model id + config. Check work_items:judge_redundancy / set_redundancy / promote tool semantics FIRST and extend rather than rebuild. VERIFY: replay the six vitest clones through the gate — one promotes, five merge; an R-remedy pair both promote, linked. importance: high — note: ← WI-41384 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Fail-open + liveness: pending age > 2 ticks auto-promotes tagged 'unreviewed' (target ~0 in steady state, alarmed if not); promoter registered on the schedule inventory with last-run alarm at 90 min; critical bypass verified live. The measured system bottleneck is distribution (greenlit plans sat 6 days unclaimed) — a dead promoter must never silently starve the queue. VERIFY: kill the promoter deliberately, confirm auto-promote engages and the alarm fires (falsifiability, not assumption). importance: high — note: ← WI-42166 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Stats ledger\n\n- **P-005** `done` [owner:Avi 2026-08-24] 'the agent should also include stats on all their runs inspectable by the user.' Run-ledger table (Postgres, migration via the atomic allocator): one row per promoter tick and per bulk stage — started/finished, batch size, promoted, merged, held, auto-promoted-unreviewed, model id, tokens in/out, census before/after, latency. Admin surface listing runs + the census trend line; sync via @papercusp/sync (useSyncQuery + notifySyncInvalidate), state in nuqs. Alarm when census RISES (the P-012 recurrence guard made concrete). VERIFY: every run visible in UI within one tick; alarm fires on an injected census rise. importance: high — note: ← WI-42184 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Bulk backlog passes\n\n- **P-006** `done` Staged converging dedup over the existing 3,731: shard by similarity-component packing (components at cos>=0.80 packed into <=300k-token working sets; 1M ceiling per owner ruling, 300k target for judgment quality and cost). Cross-shard guarantee: no pair >=0.80 split across shards; real duplicates live >=0.90 (audit-measured). Each stage: judge shards (same charter + code set as the promoter) -> execute merges -> re-run census -> ASSERT census <= previous (ratchet) -> next round until delta ~0. Stage rows land in the stats ledger. VERIFY: ratchet assertion demonstrably fails the stage on an injected rise; convergence reached and stated with the final census. — note: ← WI-42208 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Root-cause sweep\n\n- **P-007** `dropped` Weekly full-picture pass — the owner's 'see the whole picture, catch shared root causes' goal at 1/500th the cost of per-tick full reads: cluster digest (centroids + exemplar titles + counts, ~100-200k tokens; all 3,731 titles alone are ~128k tokens) read in one strong-model call; files umbrella shared-root-cause items THROUGH the admission gate like any other filing. VERIFY: first sweep produces a ranked digest; umbrella items land pending and pass promotion. blocked-by: P-006 — note: Split into hourly delta sweep + daily full digest per owner cadence ruling 2026-08-24. See decision.\n- **P-011** `done` HOURLY delta sweep (owner cadence ruling 2026-08-24): every hour, read the last hour's admitted items in full + last-24h titles + cluster-map summary (~40-50k tokens) in one model call; detect shared-root-cause BURSTS (differently-worded items from one cause — invisible to the pairwise promoter); file umbrella items THROUGH the admission gate; every run writes a stats-ledger row (tokens, umbrella yield). Runs from Phase 1 onward — reads only post-gate admissions, needs no bulk pass. VERIFY: inject a synthetic 5-item burst (distinct wording, one cause) and confirm the next sweep links them under one umbrella. importance: high — note: ← WI-42244 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` DAILY full digest (was weekly — owner raised cadence 2026-08-24): whole-corpus cluster digest (~150-200k tokens) read in one model call for slow-building cross-cutting patterns; umbrella items through the gate; stats-ledger row per run. BLOCKED by the first completed bulk stage (do not digest duplicate mass). Cadence dial stays open: raise to hourly only on stats-ledger evidence (umbrella yield lagging the delta sweep's detections). VERIFY: first run produces a ranked digest whose top clusters reconcile with the census. blocked-by: P-006 — note: ← WI-372136 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Observation capture response\n\n- **P-008** `done` [owner:Avi 2026-08-24, verbatim] 'it can be deduped deterministically on the server first too, thats okay, what i dont want is for the results to go back to the agent so the agent says hey maybe this is a duplicate let me spend time investigating.' Silence the capture response: keep the shipped server-side fold (P-013/14 of learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08) exactly as is; make the response indistinguishable from a plain success — no survivor id, no repeatCount, no HARD/SOFT, no dedup mention. This deliberately inverts that plan's P-015: folding makes re-files idempotent (they fold into the same row at zero corpus growth), so the anti-re-file rationale for telling the filer is void. Machine-emitter conditionKey folding untouched. Re-point the blocked P-016 before/after measurement at the new regime. VERIFY: capture response byte-shape identical between a folded and a fresh filing; a deliberate re-file folds into the same row. — note: ← WI-42255 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 6 — Backpressure (gated on loop restart)\n\n- **P-010** `done` Wire the producer governor to queue health: when the learning loop is un-paused, its tick admission must throttle on pending-queue depth + promoted→first-claim latency (from the P-005 ledger), not on budget alone. This was recommendation #1 of the post-audit review and was discussed as 'plugs in later — pending-queue depth is the signal the loop governor should throttle on', then dropped from the drafted plan (session-history audit gap, restored 2026-08-24). GATED: no-op while the producer stays owner-paused (no tick since 2026-08-22); the item activates when anyone restarts the loop, alongside the audit plan's P-010 provenance precondition. VERIFY: with the loop live, deep pending queue measurably reduces ideation admissions; drained queue restores them. — note: ← WI-42261 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 7 — Durable park observability and deterministic reconciliation\n\n- **P-017** `done` Establish the durable-park contract and live baseline. Re-read WI-42167, WI-5361, the hold writer/reaper, claimability writer, P-006 census writer, and current park population. Pin with focused tests that held_open_by is a liveness lease while claim_hold_by is a non-expiring durable park; confirm P-006 includes parked non-terminal rows. Record exact current counts and a reusable classification schema without mutating parks. importance: high — note: ← WI-42279 completed (done)\n- **P-018** `done` Separate active claims, hold-open leases, durable parks, and pending agent review across work_items:claimable, work_items:burn_down, fleet-leader/admin UI, and documentation. Surface parker, reason, parkedAt, age, and stated/missing/unresolved UNPARK condition while preserving storage/API compatibility. Add writer and rendering regression tests. importance: high blocked-by: P-017 — note: WI-42280 completed with committed authority: queueControl producers remain required; burn-down/TUI projections and canonical docs are verified. Tests: TS 63/63, dependent typecheck exit 0, Rust 714/714, fmt/clippy green.\n- **P-019** `done` Verify and harden P-006 integration for parked rows. Keep duplicate adjudication as P-006's only authority: parked rows remain in the census; exact duplicate merge/terminal dispositions preserve canonical occurrence/provenance and never grant generic model-based unpark authority. Add real-Postgres positive and negative controls without rebuilding the bulk dedup system. importance: high blocked-by: P-017 — note: ← WI-42281 completed (done)\n- **P-020** `done` Implement a separate deterministic report-first durable-park audit using existing routines, work_items:burn_down/claimability semantics, sync surfaces, and the existing run ledger where compatible. Emit exact counts, age buckets, reasons, condition status, missing metadata, and overdue review rows with no model call and no mutation in report-only mode. importance: high blocked-by: P-017 — note: ← WI-42282 completed (done)\n- **P-021** `done` Implement condition-aware reconciliation plus a one-time audit of the current durable-park population. Mutate only on deterministic evidence: explicit UNPARK condition satisfied, exact duplicate terminalized/merged, completed review, resolved typed blocker, or explicit operator action. Preserve WI-5361's no-boomerang invariant; forbid clear-by-age, dead parker, or model merit. Make every disposition idempotent and auditable; unresolved rows remain parked and reported. importance: high blocked-by: P-019, P-020 — note: ← WI-42283 completed (done)\n- **P-022** `done` Wire the park audit on a daily report-first cadence with event-driven condition resolution as the primary path and the schedule as a bounded backstop. Verify routine registration/arming, run-ledger/UI visibility, replay idempotency, negative controls, and a live current-population report. Complete the phase only after all tests pass and the enabled routine is observed producing its first successful run. importance: high blocked-by: P-018, P-021 — note: ← WI-42284 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 8 — Scheduled queue-control convergence\n\n- **P-023** `done` Recurring bulk queue-control census, cleanup, and liveness reconciliation: inventory active claims, liveness-bound hold-open leases, durable claim-hold parks, agent-review gates, and their overlaps; reclaim only genuinely orphaned claims; let eligible leases self-reap while preserving coexisting durable parks; require every retained park to carry a realistically reachable typed release condition, accountable owner/source, concrete re-evaluation trigger, and evidence; flag missing, ambiguous, orphaned, unreachable, or satisfied-still-parked conditions; reframe, terminalize, or escalate impossible conditions rather than hiding them forever; clear parks only through fingerprinted evidence-backed CAS with assignment/control-drift guards; persist exact before/after membership, per-row audit records, reconciliation artifact hashes, and recurrence health.
