This directly resolves WI-42484 and the live owner-directed Sol xhigh expansion blocker. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-42493 released\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Census metric CORRECTED before first use — count UNADJUDICATED pairs only, or the ratchet false-alarms on legitimate admissions\nDate: 2026-08-24\nSelf-audit finding, caught before Phase 0 ran. As drafted, the census was \"pairs >=0.90 corpus-wide\" and Phase 3 asserts it monotone non-increasing. But P-003 deliberately PROMOTES R-remedy pairs (same finding, different remedy — the modal high-cosine outcome, 47% in the audit), and a promoted R-remedy pair can sit >=0.90. So the raw pair count RISES through correct behaviour, the ratchet assertion fails a healthy stage, and the alarm cries wolf until someone mutes it — which kills the owner's guarantee at its first contact with reality.\n\n**CORRECTED DEFINITION, binding on P-001/P-005/P-006:** the census counts pairs >=0.90 **with no recorded adjudication**. Every promoter/bulk verdict (merge, R-remedy-keep, R-related) writes its adjudication (work_items:set_redundancy or equivalent), and adjudicated pairs leave the census permanently. Monotone non-increase is then genuinely guaranteed: merges remove pairs, adjudications retire pairs, and the admission gate ensures no pair enters unadjudicated above threshold. The alarm now means exactly one thing — un-judged duplication is accumulating — which is the recurrence the owner asked to be guaranteed against.\n\n### D-002 — Phase 3 is CONDITIONAL on Phase 0's projection — bulk passes are not run on faith\nDate: 2026-08-24\nThe audit measured the learning-loop slice as barely compressible (56 merges/877, 2 locally disposable; exact-body dupes 0.1%). If the corpus-wide census shows similarly low UNADJUDICATED duplication outside the machine-emitter classes, staged full-corpus passes are mostly spend without yield. RULING: P-006 executes at full breadth only if Phase 0 projects a material merge yield (working threshold: >150 unadjudicated pairs outside already-known clusters; tune at P-001 with the data in hand). Below that, Phase 3 shrinks to one targeted pass over the machine-emitter clone classes (the vitest×6 shape), which is where the observed duplication actually lives. The ratchet + admission gate still deliver the owner's guarantee either way — the gate, not the bulk pass, is what prevents re-growth.\n\n### D-003 — Stats ledger MUST include promoted→first-claim latency — the distribution instrument, and the future backpressure signal\nDate: 2026-08-24\nSession-history audit gap. The completed backlog audit's strongest operational finding was that DISTRIBUTION, not quality, is the live defect (four greenlit plans, six days, zero pickup; 482/487 corpus exits via ordinary work). This plan adds admission latency in front of that queue and, as drafted, measured everything about admission and nothing about pickup. Binding amendment to P-005: the ledger also records, per promoted item, time from promotion to first claim, surfaced as a trend beside the census. It is cheap (two timestamps already exist), it watches the one number the pending queue could plausibly worsen, and it is the exact signal the producer governor throttles on when the learning loop restarts (backpressure, P-009).\n\n### D-004 — P-007 (root-cause sweep) runs AFTER Phase 3 — a digest over an un-deduped corpus double-counts its own clusters\nDate: 2026-08-24\nOrdering was implicit and is now explicit: the weekly sweep reads the cluster digest, and before the bulk passes run, that digest carries the duplicate mass the passes exist to remove — umbrella items filed off it would inherit the double-counting. P-007 is blocked by P-006's first completed stage. (Its filings already route through the admission gate, so even a premature run cannot inject duplicates — this ordering is about signal quality, not safety.)\n\n### D-005 — Root-cause sweep cadence RAISED per owner — two-tier: hourly delta sweep + daily full digest (weekly retracted)\nDate: 2026-08-24\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-24, interactive] \"weekly sweep i thought we were going to run this like every hour\" — a correction of MY unbundling: the owner's original proposal had the full-picture function running with the frequent agent; I split it out and set weekly without flagging the change. Retracted.\n\n**RULING + DESIGN.** Root-cause detection runs HOURLY, structured two-tier so frequency lands where the information is:\n- **Hourly DELTA sweep** (~40-50k tokens/run): the last hour's admitted items in full + last-24h titles + the cluster-map summary. Its job is BURST detection — one broken migration firing 20 differently-worded items in an hour is invisible to the pairwise promoter (below cosine thresholds) and a weekly read catches it uselessly late. Starts with Phase 1; reads only post-gate admissions.\n- **DAILY full digest** (~150-200k tokens/run, was weekly): whole-corpus cluster digest for slow-building patterns. Blocked by the first completed bulk stage so it does not digest duplicate mass.\n\nHourly-FULL was considered and priced: ~3.6-5M tokens/day to re-read 3,731 mostly-unchanged items for a ~40-item hourly delta. The two-tier design delivers the hourly detection the owner wants at roughly a third of that, with sharper focus. The dial stays open: if the daily digest proves to lag real patterns, raising IT to hourly is a config change, and the stats ledger (tokens/run, umbrella-yield/run) is exactly the evidence to decide with.\n\nP-007 (weekly, single-tier) is dropped in favour of two successor items.\n\n### D-006 — Sharding implementation spec — components at ≥0.90 with ghost context for 0.85–0.90, because ≥0.80 components collapse into one giant shard (measured)\nDate: 2026-08-24\nOwner asked how sharding is implemented; specifying it exposed a defect in my own drafted mechanism, corrected here before Phase 0 builds it.\n\n**THE BUG.** P-001/P-006 said \"connected components at cos>=0.80 packed into shards\". Measured on the audit slice: **15.3% of ALL pairs sit >=0.80** (58,830 of 384,126 among 877 items). A similarity graph that dense is one giant connected component — the \"components\" would be a single mega-shard larger than the whole corpus budget, and the packing step would have nothing to pack. The 0.80 threshold is fine for an EDGE SCAN; it is unusable as the COMPONENT threshold.\n\n**CORRECTED STRUCTURE — three thresholds, three roles:**\n- **>=0.90 — component edges (hard guarantee).** Union-find over these. Audit evidence: every real merge lived >=0.90; at this threshold the slice gave 392 edges → 65 components + singletons — tractable, packable.\n- **0.85–0.90 — ghost context (soft guarantee).** A cross-shard pair in this band does NOT move shard membership; instead the neighbor's text is appended to the shard READ-ONLY (role='ghost', verdict authority stays with the item's home shard), capped at ~15% of shard budget, highest-cosine first. Evidence this band needs context-only treatment: no audit merge ever came from <0.90, and D-019/D-021 measured even 0.90–0.93 at 0.833 precision.\n- **<0.85 — unguarded by design.** Exact-body census measured 0.1% duplication; pairs this far apart are not duplicates on any instrument we ran.\n\n**PIPELINE (P-001 builds; P-006 consumes):**\n1. **Coverage + homogeneity check**: every corpus item has an embedding, one embedding_mode (audit slice: gemma-768, 100%; corpus-wide UNVERIFIED — items missing embeddings go to a text-only bucket handled by exact keys + trgm, never silently skipped).\n2. **Edge scan** at >=0.85, chunked (rn % N), count(*) FILTER aggregates only, per-chunk coverage assertion summing EXACTLY to corpus size (the 670/877 silent-gap trap). Edges persist to a table (dedup_edges: a, b, cos, trgm, band) — durable, resumable, and stage N+1 recomputes only rows whose canonical changed.\n3. **Union-find at >=0.90** → components (3,731 nodes; runs in-process, trivial).\n4. **Giant-component escape hatch**: any single component exceeding the shard token budget is split INTERNALLY by raising the threshold within it (0.92, 0.94, …) until sub-components fit; severed internal edges become ghost pairs. Without this, one dense cluster (the audit had a 27-member one) could still break packing.\n5. **Greedy bin-packing**: components sorted by size desc, packed to <=300k-token working sets (token estimate = (title+summary chars)/4; measured p50 1,373 chars/item); singletons fill remaining space nearest-centroid-first so near-but-below-threshold items tend to co-locate.\n6. **Ghost pass**: for each 0.85–0.90 edge crossing shard boundaries, append the smaller item as ghost, capped.\n7. **Persist shard_map(run_id, shard_id, item_id, role member|ghost) + a stats-ledger row**; assert Σ members = corpus size before any model call.\n\n**GUARANTEES, restated honestly:** no >=0.90 pair is ever split (hard, structural); 0.85–0.90 cross-shard pairs are visible as context (soft, capped); <0.85 uncompared across shards by design, with the measured evidence that nothing lives there. The promoter's per-item KNN path is separate and unaffected — new items aren't in dedup_edges until admitted.\n\n### D-007 — Shard size: 300k target ratified, 1M ceiling with an evidence gate — and the full implementation is owner-greenlit, solo\nDate: 2026-08-24\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-24, interactive] \"Okay fold this all into the plan and then implement it yourself now from start to finish\" — ratifies the design as it now stands (sharding spec, two-tier sweep cadence, 300k/1M shard sizing) and directs solo implementation by this session.\n\n**SHARD-SIZE RATIONALE, recorded so the 300k number is never read as arbitrary:**\n1. Marginal recall of a bigger shard is ~zero BY MEASUREMENT: >=0.90 pairs are never split (structural), 0.85-0.90 pairs are ghosted into view, and below 0.85 the audit found nothing (0.1% exact-body duplication, zero real merges).\n2. Every precision figure that authorizes automated merging (tier-A 0.833, filter precisions, kappa=0.679) was measured at SMALL context. At 1M the system would execute merges on uncalibrated precision — the exact out-of-scope-measurement error class D-033/D-036 retracted.\n3. Care-per-item collapses in mega-calls (audit: ~10 verification checks changed 3 of 40 scores); smaller shards bound retry blast radius and parallelize.\n4. What 1M saves is ghost overhead, capped at 15% by construction.\n\n**THE DIAL:** shard size is config. Raising toward the 1M ceiling requires stats-ledger evidence (per-shard precision spot-checks at 300k holding + material ghost volume) AND a raised spot-check rate on the first stage at the new size to rebuild the precision measurement at that scale. Owner was offered 1M-now and did not take it; this evidence gate is the standing rule.\n\n### D-008 — RECON REVERSAL — a synchronous admission dedup ALREADY EXISTS in _create-core.ts. The gap is not detection, it is that unresolved candidates are handed to the FILING AGENT\nDate: 2026-08-24\nRead `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/_create-core.ts` before writing the gate. It already implements most of what P-002/P-003 proposed to build, and building it again would have been the duplicate-work irony this whole plan exists to prevent.\n\n**WHAT ALREADY SHIPS, at filing time, synchronously:**\n- `admissionIdentity(title)` → a normalized `titleKey` (`harness/improvements/digest`), stamped into `payload.admissionIdentity`.\n- A LEXICAL leg (`findFulltextLexicalDupes`) and a SEMANTIC leg (embedding candidates), with a `dedupCoverage: { lexical, semantic, degraded }` verdict recorded on the row.\n- **Exact-identity auto-fold**: an exact normalized-title collision does NOT mint a new row — it calls `appendWorkItemOccurrence` on the first row (EI-20449994308545912, added because a rapid `items:[…]` batch outran embedding availability). This is fold-in-place for work items, already live.\n- Fail-CLOSED gates for two callers: `requireCompleteDedupCoverage` (DRAIN) and `goalDedupGate` (GOAL mode) refuse the create when a leg is down.\n\n**THE ACTUAL GAP — and it is exactly the owner's complaint.** For everything short of an exact title match, the semantic/lexical candidates come back to the CALLER as `similarOpen`, and resolving them is the filing agent's problem. That is verbatim what the owner ruled against on 2026-08-24: \"what i dont want is for the results to go back to the agent so the agent says hey maybe this is a duplicate let me spend time investigating.\" The detection is fine; the RESOLUTION is in the wrong place, on the wrong actor, at the wrong time.\n\n**RE-SCOPE, binding on P-002 and P-003:**\n- **P-002 shrinks.** Born-pending does NOT need a new dedup path — it needs (a) the `admission` column stamped at this existing choke point, and (b) `similarOpen` to STOP being returned to filing agents, becoming instead a durable candidate set the promoter consumes. The existing exact-identity fold stays exactly as is; it is already the behaviour the owner wants (silent, deterministic, server-side).\n- **P-003 shrinks and sharpens.** The promoter is not a from-scratch deduper: it resolves the candidate pairs `_create-core` ALREADY COMPUTES but currently delegates to the filer, asynchronously and in bulk, under the dup-only charter. Reuse `admissionIdentity`, `findFulltextLexicalDupes` and `appendWorkItemOccurrence` rather than writing new equivalents.\n- **The two fail-CLOSED callers (DRAIN, GOAL) keep their current behaviour.** They deliberately refuse rather than defer, they are narrow, and their callers are not the \"quick filing\" population the owner is protecting. Do not fold them into the pending path.\n\n**Why this is worth a decision rather than a code comment:** the plan as ratified told an implementer to build an admission gate. Without this, that implementer builds a second one beside the existing one — two dedup mechanisms disagreeing at the same seam, which is precisely the failure `ungraded-scope.ts` documents for \"ungraded\" (three surfaces, three numbers, all arithmetically right).\n\n### D-009 — admission is written at INSERT and by the promoter's DIRECT base-table write — never through the engineer_issues view's UPDATE path\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24. Settled while implementing P-002; binds P-003 (the promoter) and any later admission writer.\n\nFINDING THAT FORCED IT. harness_shared.work_items is the ONE base TABLE. Both\nharness_shared.engineer_issues and harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated are\nVIEWS over it, and engineer_issues carries an INSTEAD OF trigger\n(engineer_issues_view_dml) with a FIXED INSERT column list. Migration 944 added\nadmission/admitted_at/admitted_by to the base table only, so a named `admission` on an\nissue-family INSERT was silently DROPPED and the column just defaulted NULL — which\nisAdmitted() reads as ADMITTED. Net: the entire gate was a silent no-op for the whole\nissue family (bug/change/task) while appearing to work for features. Migration 946\ncloses it by appending the three columns to the view and to the trigger's INSERT.\n\nTHE RULING, three parts:\n\n1. BORN-ADMISSION RIDES IN THE INSERT, for BOTH families. Never a post-create UPDATE.\n   A create-then-demote sequence leaves the row admitted and claimable in the gap\n   between the two writes, which is exactly the race born-pending exists to close.\n\n2. MIGRATION 946 DELIBERATELY DID NOT EXTEND THE TRIGGER'S UPDATE BRANCH. The\n   engineer_issues view is a read/field-edit compatibility surface, not a lifecycle\n   writer — the same rationale under which it already REFUSES terminal transitions\n   (EI-20092514168581881). admission is promoter-owned lifecycle state. So an UPDATE\n   through the view leaves a stored admission untouched rather than round-tripping a\n   stale snapshot of it back over the promoter's write.\n   => P-003's promoter MUST write harness_shared.work_items DIRECTLY. If it updates\n   through engineer_issues instead, its verdict is silently discarded and every item\n   stays pending forever — a failure that looks like \"the promoter never ran\".\n\n3. A FILING PATH MAY ONLY MINT 'pending' OR 'auto'. Enforced by the type\n   `BornAdmission = 'pending' | 'auto'` rather than by convention: 'admitted' is the\n   promoter's verdict and 'unreviewed' is the fail-open watchdog's, and neither is\n   something a writer may assert about itself. admitted_at/admitted_by are stamped ONLY\n   for the non-pending case, so an unjudged item is distinguishable from one a\n   filing-time bypass already cleared.\n\nSCOPE CORRECTION CARRIED WITH IT: born-pending is UNIVERSAL for non-observation items,\nper WI-41383's own spec — not the narrower \"pending only when similar items were found\"\nrule an earlier working note had assumed. The bypasses to 'auto' are source_plan_slug\nset (already passed plan review) and critical/security severity (post-hoc review).\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-010 — dedup_edges.cos is COSINE-ONLY — the create-time prescreen persists its semantic leg there and nothing else\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24. Ruling for every lane that writes or reads `harness_shared.dedup_edges`.\n\nP-002 item d stops returning `similarOpen` to a filing agent on a SUCCESSFUL create and persists the candidates for the promoter instead (plan Now: \"the gap is NOT detection — it is that unresolved candidates are returned to the FILING AGENT\"). Implementing it exposed a metric collision worth ruling on once rather than per lane.\n\n`_create-core` merges THREE prescreen legs into one `similarOpen` array, and they do not share a metric:\n* the P-008 semantic guard — cosine in the migration-548 embedding space (`source` unset);\n* `findRecentLexicalDupes` — Jaccard word-overlap on titles (`source:'lexical-recent'`, EI-9940);\n* `findFulltextLexicalDupes` — full-text + title-token similarity (`source:'lexical-fulltext'`, EI-19298062354262754).\n\n`dedup_edges.cos` is NOT NULL and carries exactly one of those: cosine. P-001's census counts unadjudicated pairs at cos>=0.90 and unions sharding components at cos>=0.80. Writing a Jaccard or trigram score into that column would not degrade gracefully — it would read as a REAL cosine edge and move the corpus metric the whole plan is measured by, in the direction that manufactures duplicates.\n\nDECISION: the create-time writer (`agent-tools/work_items/dedup-edges.ts`) persists the SEMANTIC leg only, at cos>=0.85 (the table's documented floor), same-harness only (the PK is harness-scoped), ordered a<b, `trgm` from the candidate's `titleSimilarity` when the guard supplied one, `run_id='create-prescreen'` (a sentinel — the column has no FK, and an edge no census has touched should say so). Lexical candidates are DROPPED by that writer.\n\nNothing is lost by dropping them, and this is the part later lanes must not \"fix\": the lexical legs exist to cover the window BEFORE the async embed-backfill has indexed a fresh row. By the time the P-003 promoter ticks (30 min) the row is embedded, and the promoter recomputes top-K neighbours itself — so the prescreen write is a census CONTRIBUTION and an optimisation, never a correctness dependency. The lexical candidates also still ride into the occurrence ledger as evidence for issue-family filings.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for P-001: the census may find pre-existing `dedup_edges` rows stamped `run_id='create-prescreen'`. They are real cosine edges and count; a census pass may overwrite them with its own `run_id`.\nCONSEQUENCE for P-003: do NOT add a second metric axis to this table (a lexical score column, a nullable `cos`, a `metric` discriminator) to make lexical edges representable. If a lane finds it genuinely needs lexical pairs persisted, that is a NEW table or a new decision, not a widening of this one.\n\nFalsifiability control: `dedup-edges.test.ts` keeps a deliberately-wrong \"accept every candidate\" builder permanently in tree, so the cosine-only assertion proves it can fail on every run.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-011 — P-003 does NOT extend work_items:judge_redundancy / set_redundancy / promote — the names collide, the semantics are orthogonal\nDate: 2026-08-24\nDate: 2026-08-24. Corrects an instruction inside P-003's own text, so it is recorded rather than left for the next agent to re-derive (or to follow).\n\nP-003 says: \"Check work_items:judge_redundancy / set_redundancy / promote tool semantics FIRST and extend rather than rebuild.\" That instruction was written from the tool NAMES. Recon (2026-08-24) reads the implementations, and all three are about something else:\n\n* `work_items:set_redundancy` (decentralized-dispatch-scaling P-014, migration 195) — BOINC-style REPLICA redundancy: mark ONE high-stakes item to run INDEPENDENTLY on N Swarms. `redundancy` is an integer column meaning \"how many replicas\", not \"is this a duplicate of something\". Inert unless `PAPERCUSP_WORKITEM_REDUNDANCY=1`.\n* `work_items:judge_redundancy` — judges the REPLICAS of one item via `gym:judge` (the frozen Opus grader) and adopts the best RESULT. Its unit is a replica's output, never a pair of work-items. Needs ≥2 complete replicas of the SAME item.\n* `work_items:promote` — mints an F-FIX FEATURE so a filed bug/change gets a pipeline run (D-005). \"Promote\" here means bug→pipeline, not pending→admitted.\n* Siblings in the same family for completeness: `claim_replica`, `record_replica_result`, `redundancy_status`.\n\nSo the whole family answers \"did we run this ONE item enough times, and which run do we keep?\". P-003 answers \"are these TWO items the same work?\". Extending them would overload `redundancy` with a second meaning on a live column, make `judge_redundancy` return two incompatible verdict vocabularies, and — worst — silently redefine `promote`, a verb the pipeline already depends on.\n\nDECISION: P-003 builds its own promoter surface and does NOT touch the replica-redundancy family. What it DOES reuse (the reuse the plan item was reaching for, correctly, just aimed at the wrong names):\n* `admissionIdentity` (harness/improvements/digest) — the normalized title key, already the exact-duplicate test in `_create-core`;\n* `findSemanticDupes` / `findFulltextLexicalDupes` / `findRecentLexicalDupes` (agent-tools/work_items/*-dupe-guard) — the three prescreen legs, already budget-bounded and fail-open;\n* `appendWorkItemOccurrence` / `recordIssueOccurrence` (issue-occurrence-ledger) — the lossless \"preserve the report on the canonical\" primitive the coalesce path already uses;\n* `selectCanonicalIssue` + `decideIssueAdmissionCircuit` (issue-occurrence-ledger) — canonical selection and the burst circuit;\n* `harness_shared.dedup_edges` / `dedup_adjudications` / `admission_runs` (migration 944) as its substrate, with edges already contributed at create time (D-010).\n\nNAMING RULE that falls out: the promoter's verdicts must NOT be called \"redundancy\". Use the admission vocabulary migration 944 already declares — `pending` / `admitted` / `auto` / `unreviewed` — and the D-025/D-027 R-finding-merge / R-remedy-keep / R-related / distinct verdict set on `dedup_adjudications`, which is where a PAIR verdict belongs.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-012 — Inflow for this gate is LIVE at ~104/day (agent-review), not zero — you can tune the census threshold against real traffic today\nDate: 2026-08-24\nFiled from the `learning-loop-backlog-triage-2026-08-22` lane, which is where your Phase 1 (admission gate) and Phase 2 (census-rise alarm) came from: that plan's D-044 absorbed its P-011/P-012 into this plan. Nobody currently holds an item here, so this is recorded as a Decision rather than sent as a message — a message to an empty lane reaches no one.\n\n**THE PREMISE YOU MIGHT INHERIT, AND WHY IT IS WRONG.** The originating plan's D-043 deferred those two items on the reasoning that they \"exist to bound an inflow that is currently ZERO,\" and that building a gate for a paused producer means \"shipping untested control-flow against a workload that does not exist, and tuning a threshold with no live signal to tune against.\"\n\nHalf of that is right and half is wrong.\n\n**Right:** Scout/blender is genuinely stopped — 0 ticks in `harness_shared.scout_ticks` for 51.2 hours (last 2026-08-22 19:03Z), 0 ideas routed, owner-paused.\n\n**Wrong:** Scout is not the only producer. Measured 2026-08-24 off `scout_routed_ideas.routed_at`, workspace `papercusp-workspace`:\n\n| origin | last 24h | last 2d | all-time |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **agent-review** | **104** | **180** | 554 |\n| su-ideate | 1 | 3 | 224 |\n| scout | 0 | 0 | 1,623 |\n| drill / shadow-variant | 0 | 0 | 4 / 20 |\n\nThe `agent-review` rail filed 104 ideas in the last 24 hours while Scout sat at zero. The discrepancy surfaced arithmetically: the triaged corpus grew ~100 rows (877 → 969 → 980) across a window in which Scout provably routed nothing, which cannot happen at zero inflow.\n\n**WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THIS PLAN — two concrete consequences.**\n\n1. **You do NOT have to wait for a Scout restart to tune Phase 2's census-rise threshold.** There is live traffic to calibrate against right now, ~104/day, and it is one `GROUP BY origin` away. Tuning against real traffic beats picking a number and waiting for a producer that may stay paused indefinitely.\n\n2. **Scope the gate to the FILING PATH, not to the Scout tick** — which your P-002 (\"Born-pending: every non-observation work-item filing path lands…\") already does correctly, so this is corroboration rather than a change of direction. Stating it explicitly because the whole faucet discussion upstream was Scout-centric (\"the producer is paused\", \"the loop is off\"), and anyone reading that history could reasonably conclude that gating the Scout rail is sufficient. It is not: pausing Scout removed only part of the inflow, and a Scout-scoped gate would leave ~104 filings/day ungated.\n\n**Verify before acting on it — this is a volatile measurement.** `SELECT origin, count(*) FILTER (WHERE routed_at > (extract(epoch from now())-86400)*1000) FROM harness_shared.scout_routed_ideas WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' GROUP BY 1` re-answers it in one call, and the rate will have moved.\n\n### D-013 — Census runs pin the eligible corpus at start; canonical readback is scoped by pinned IDs, not mutable edge provenance\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThe first live P-001 run exposed a consistency defect: each rn%N chunk rebuilt eligibility from the live work_items table, while create-time prescreen writes are allowed to replace dedup_edges.run_id as the CURRENT value's provenance. Therefore neither per-chunk live membership nor run_id is a stable run boundary. Binding correction for P-001 and P-006: read the eligible corpus once; pin its ordered member IDs plus embedded/missing classification for every chunk, text-context read, stale-edge cleanup, census readback, and shard-map coverage assertion. Read the canonical dedup_edges values over those pinned endpoints after all chunks; run_id remains provenance only and MUST NOT define the result set. Per-chunk INSERT/UPDATE RETURNING counts are diagnostics, never the exact edge census. Add a real-Postgres regression that mutates an item's eligibility between chunks and still proves exact pinned membership/edge coverage and reproducibility.\n\n### D-014 — P-006 bulk execution is a durable on-demand system action, never a synchronous tool request\nDate: 2026-08-26\nThe writer-verified live baseline is 19,444 unadjudicated >=0.90 pairs across six ~300k-token shards. Even with bounded shard concurrency and <=200 verdicts per call, the run necessarily outlives the operator HTTP/proxy request ceiling. RULING: work_items:bulk_dedup only materializes a due-now one-shot routine targeting system:work-item-admission-bulk-dedup and returns the stable run/routine ids immediately. The background routines engine performs the model calls, batched ledger/link writes, merges, post-stage census, and transactional ratchet. The action is scheduling:'on-demand' and classified spend:'llm'. Completion authority is admission_runs rows under the returned run-id prefix, not the enqueue response. A failed or disconnected client must never be able to kill or misreport the corpus run.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-015 — P-011 hourly delta sweep is a durable one-call system action with typed umbrella linkage\nDate: 2026-08-26\nImplement P-011 by extending the existing routines + admission substrate: a standing tier:durable system:work-item-admission-delta-sweep action fires hourly at :07, offset from the 30-minute promoter. A tick reads all work items admitted in the last 60 minutes in full, last-24h admitted titles, and the latest completed census shard-map summary; if the last-hour set is nonempty it makes exactly one canonical learning-model call. Model context outside the last-hour set is read-only. A proposal is actionable only with >=3 distinct member IDs, all from that tick's last-hour set; unknown IDs, overlap, or incomplete typed-link coverage fail the run loudly. Each umbrella is filed through captureImprovement in harness scope so it is born pending and traverses the existing admission gate, never a parallel writer. Each contributing source gets a typed source --caused-by--> umbrella coord link. Stable server-derived watchdog identity makes replay/repeated detection converge. Every tick, including empty ticks, writes one admission_runs run_kind='delta-sweep' row with source counts, tokens, model provenance, umbrella yield, filed/canonical ids, and link counts. Verification injects five differently-worded admitted items with one shared cause and proves one pending umbrella plus five typed links, one complete ledger row, and replay with no second model call using real PostgreSQL.\n\n### D-016 — Unkeyed observation capture disposition is server-private; keyed emitters and explicit checks stay detailed\nDate: 2026-08-26\nOwner-directed P-008 supersedes learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08 P-015 for unkeyed `lane:observation` filings. After a successful write, the agent-facing tool returns the same `{ok:true}` bytes whether the server minted, HARD-folded, or SOFT-linked the filing. The durable fold, occurrence ledger, repeat/reporter state, and row/link writes are unchanged. `conditionKey`/server-keyed observations retain detailed coalesce metadata because machine emitters use it operationally; `checkDuplicatesOnly:true` also remains detailed because the caller explicitly requested an inspection. The old plan's P-016 before/after measurement must restart when this response-silent build deploys and use writer-side occurrence-versus-mint/fold counts plus re-file behavior, never caller-visible fold metadata.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-017 — P-010 throttles Scout ideator admission from the existing P-005 queue snapshot\nDate: 2026-08-26\nImplement P-010 by extending the existing Scout preflight and `readWorkItemAdmissionSnapshot`; do not add a parallel governor or metric store. The owner-pause check remains first, so a paused Scout performs no queue read and no cycle. When enabled, derive pressure from the P-005 writer's `pending` count and immutable `admitted_at -> first_claimed_at` p95. Missing/unavailable latency is neutral (fail-open), never zero. Thresholds reuse existing admission capacity/liveness constants: NORMAL at <= one 20-item promoter batch and p95 <= 90m (or no sample) preserves the configured budget; ELEVATED above 20 pending or 90m p95 caps `maxIdeators` at 3; DEEP above 40 pending or 180m p95 caps it at 1. Take the strongest of the two signals. Stamp the exact pressure decision on the Scout tick ledger. Thus a deep queue measurably reduces new ideation while a drained queue restores the original per-hive budget, with no new flag or default-off path. Live calibration at 2026-08-26 19:07 EDT, read through the P-005 writer definition, was pending=17, unreviewed=0, latencySampleSize=0; it is context, not a hardcoded baseline.\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-018 — Durable parks stay durable; visibility and deterministic reconciliation are a separate Phase 7 lane\nDate: 2026-08-26\nOwner ruling and source-conversation audit, 2026-08-26. Preserve both existing semantics: `held_open_by` is a liveness-bound hold-open lease; `claim_hold_by` is a durable do-not-self-select park that survives its parker and does not expire automatically. User-facing surfaces must distinguish active claims, leases, durable parks, and agent review. Never clear a durable park from age, parker death, or model merit judgment. P-006 already includes non-terminal parked rows in its corpus and retains authority only for duplicate adjudication; it must not become a generic unpark mechanism. Phase 7 adds a separate deterministic report-first park audit/reconciler, reusing claimability/burn-down, routines, sync/UI, and run-ledger surfaces. Report every park's provenance, reason, age, and stated/missing/unresolved UNPARK condition. Prefer event-driven condition resolution, with the daily audit as a bounded backstop. Mutations require deterministic evidence: explicit condition satisfied, exact duplicate terminalized/merged, completed review, resolved typed blocker, or explicit operator action. Every mutation is idempotent and audited; unresolved parks remain parked. Preserve WI-5361's no-boomerang invariant and storage/API compatibility.\nRelated: P-017, P-018, P-019, P-020, P-021, P-022\n\n### D-019 — P-010 separates workspace Scout identity from queue-health scope\nDate: 2026-08-26\nLive writer audit found that the workspace-scoped Scout's identity key (`workspaceId`) was being reused as `harness_slug`, masking the real pending queue. Bind the units explicitly: tick/single-flight identity and work-queue scope are separate values. When WORKSPACE_COORDINATION is ON, the one-per-workspace Scout reads queue health across the whole workspace (omit the harness predicate); when OFF, each legacy per-hive Scout filters by its real harness slug. The workspace sentinel must never be interpreted as a literal harness filter. Preserve the existing P-005 writer, pressure thresholds, fail-open policy, owner-pause ordering, and exact tick evidence. Acceptance must cover this topology seam in a production-entry test and show live deep pressure followed by a drained/normal restoration.\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-020 — Durable-park classification is multi-axis; loop continuation cannot self-protect dead-owner control state\nDate: 2026-08-27\nDate: 2026-08-26\n\nP-017 classifies each non-terminal work item on independent axes; no single `claimHold` bucket is authoritative:\n\n1. **Active-claim axis** — `taken_by`/`taken_at` describe current execution ownership only.\n2. **Hold-open lease axis** — `held_open_by`/`held_open_at`/`held_open_reason` describe a liveness-bound gate. A dead-owner sweep may lift this lease after grace; a live or briefly parked session keeps it.\n3. **Durable-park axis** — `_claimHold` with `claim_hold_by`/`claim_hold_at`/`claim_hold_reason` is a non-expiring do-not-self-select decision. It survives parker death and age, and can coexist with a hold-open lease; lifting the lease must preserve the durable park. Missing/unparseable `claim_hold_at` means age UNKNOWN, never inferred from item creation/update age.\n4. **Agent-review axis** — pending/revision-requested/completed agent review is independent of active claim, lease, and park state.\n5. **Duplicate-corpus axis** — P-006 includes parked non-terminal rows only for duplicate adjudication; inclusion grants no generic unpark authority.\n\nLiveness has two scopes. Fresh session evidence (presence, live spawn alias, or recent active turn) governs dead-owner loop retirement. The broader work-item holder set also includes an armed engine loop as same-owner continuation authority, protecting an in-flight claim between wakes. The armed loop must not be allowed to prove its own owner live inside the sweep that retires abandoned loops; that circularity left the dead-owner set empty and is guarded by WI-42279 tests.\n\nBaseline retained from P-017: 4,003 non-terminal non-observation rows; 52 active claims; 312 `_claimHold`; 7 hold-open leases; 307 durable parks; 2 rows with lease+park coexistence; 0 unattributed `_claimHold`; 461 pending review; 2 revision-requested. All 307 durable parks lacked parseable `claim_hold_at`, so their age remains unknown. Preserve D-018 and WI-5361: no age-, death-, or merit-based durable unpark; deterministic report-first reconciliation only.\n\n### D-021 — WI-42287 report-only census is independent of Phase 7 implementation coverage\nDate: 2026-08-27\nAuthoritative boundary from WI-42287's owner, 2026-08-27. WI-42287 is an independent, owner-directed one-time report-only census artifact (396 rows) under D-018. It edits no product paths, performs no unpark mutation, and does not supply or satisfy P-017 implementation coverage. It likewise does not replace P-020's durable report-first audit implementation. WI-42279 is the exclusive P-017 implementation/completion authority. Any coverage edge mapping WI-42287 to P-017 is a mapper/linkage artifact to correct separately, never evidence of shared implementation ownership. Related: P-017, P-020.\nRelated: P-017, P-020\n\n### D-022 — Durable parks must prove liveness, not only clearance safety\nDate: 2026-08-27\nOwner direction: a retained durable park is healthy only when its release condition is realistically reachable, has an accountable owner or authoritative source, and has a concrete re-evaluation trigger. The audit must flag missing, ambiguous, orphaned, impossible, or triggerless release conditions; a condition that can never realistically be met is permanent hidden backlog and therefore a defect. Preserve D-018's safety rule: age or parker death alone never clears a park. The remediation is explicit reconciliation, reframe/terminalize, or escalation—not blind expiry.\n\n### D-023 — The scheduled bulk step owns the complete claim/lease/park lifecycle\nDate: 2026-08-27\nOwner direction: recurring queue cleanup must cover the whole queue-control state machine, not only duplicate detection. Each scheduled run inventories active claims, hold-open leases, durable parks, agent-review gates, and overlaps; reclaims only proven orphan claims; preserves lease-vs-park semantics; evaluates every park's release-condition reachability, owner/source, trigger, and evidence; flags unreachable or already-satisfied conditions; and uses the evidence-matrix/fingerprint/assignment-guard/CAS/audit path for any clear. Impossible conditions are reframed, terminalized, or escalated rather than left as permanent hidden backlog. Age or parker death alone remains forbidden as a durable-park clear signal. P-023 is the recurring template lane, scheduled daily with overlap skipped and missed historical ticks skipped.\nRelated: P-023\n\n### D-024 — P-024/P-013: retire the stale P-008 total-seat ceiling while preserving governed batching\nDate: 2026-08-27\nP-013 of capless-adaptive-resource-governor-2026-08-26 is the governing direction: there is no configured or machine-derived upper capacity bound, and local worker/agent/queue/memory caps are removed. Therefore fleet:launch-on-plan's P-008 regression must assert the full live-member deficit as the requested cohort, not a 12-seat total ceiling. The launch executor may still use its 1+3 execution batches and stop opening later batches after a spawn failure; the exact retry set must include the failed and unattempted pre-pinned identities. Governed dispatch admission remains the only legitimate capacity clamp. This decision changes the test contract only; it does not bypass admission or authorize replay of legacy transactions.\nRelated: P-024\n\n### D-025 — The park audit's daily backstop is live; its event-driven half is gated on a typed-contract population that is currently zero\nDate: 2026-08-27\nDate: 2026-08-27 (P-022 implementation, su-c02023a0)\n\n**Measured, twice, by independent instruments.** Direct SQL over `harness_shared.work_items` and the audit engine's own first scheduled run (`sched-.routinesTick-2026-08-27T15:22:30.000Z-34`) agree exactly: 285 durable parks, 5 hold-open leases, 62 active claims. Release-condition health is `tracked: 0, unverified: 285, unreachable: 0, satisfied-still-parked: 0`. **Not one live park carries a complete typed `payload.claim_hold_release` contract**, so every park is missing the `trigger` (and owner/reachability/evidence) that `classifyDurableParkReleaseLiveness` needs. Unpark-condition prose splits `stated: 132, missing: 17, unresolved: 136`.\n\n**Consequence for P-022's wording.** P-022 asks for \"event-driven condition resolution as the primary path and the schedule as a bounded backstop\". The backstop half is now real: `work-item-durable-park-audit` is seeded ACTIVE, daily, report-only, registered in `BESPOKE_ACTIVE_SEEDS`, its action flipped from `scheduling:'on-demand'` to `'standing'`, and it has been observed producing a successful scheduled run. The event-driven half **cannot function today** — a subscriber keyed on the contract's `trigger` would subscribe to zero rows. Building it now would ship a mechanism with no population, which is the same \"implemented but never turned on\" failure this plan has already hit on P-004, P-011 and P-012.\n\n**Ruling.** The event-driven path is sequenced BEHIND typed-contract adoption, and the audit is the instrument that measures the gate opening: `releaseConditionHealth.statusCounts.tracked` rising off zero is the signal that an event path has anything to bind to. Until then the daily schedule carries 100% of re-evaluation, which is the bounded backstop doing exactly its job — not a gap to route around. Do not read \"schedule is the backstop\" as licence to treat the daily run as optional while the primary path is absent.\n\n**Two rails this does not weaken.** (1) D-018/D-022/D-023 stand: the scheduled row is report-only by construction — its payload carries no `mode`, so the action takes its audit branch and can never reach `runWorkItemDurableParkReconciliation`. A durable park is still never cleared by age, parker death, or model judgment; clears remain explicit decisions on the evidence-matrix/fingerprint/CAS path. (2) An event-driven path, when built, must FLAG for re-evaluation rather than auto-clear — D-022 makes reachability a reporting property, and prose-matching a park reason to a work-item id (65 of 285 reasons cite one) is not evidence a condition is satisfied.\n\n**Incidental repair, recorded because it is the same class.** `bespoke-active-seeds-check.test.ts` was RED on arrival: `work-item-admission-daily-digest` (P-012's routine) has a seed script whose writer defaults ACTIVE but was never added to `BESPOKE_ACTIVE_SEEDS`, so the guard that exists to catch un-seeded routines was itself failing. Fixed here because the guard asserts an exact registry match and P-022's own entry could not go green beside it. Its live routine row is still absent — that remains P-012's to seed.\n\n**Cron zone, since it is a live foot-gun.** Routine cron fields are evaluated in the operator's LOCAL zone, not UTC: `0 47 3 * * *` produced `next_fire_at 2026-08-28T07:47:00Z` (03:47 America/New_York). Reading a routine's cron hour as UTC is a silent 4-hour error when correlating a fire against a UTC ledger timestamp.\nRelated: P-022, P-023\n\n### D-026 — The delta sweep's codex failures were a clobbered credential, not exhausted quota — do NOT change LEARNING_MODEL_SPEC or route learning paths to Claude\nDate: 2026-08-27\nP-011's hourly delta sweep failed every fire with `codex-cli bridge: codex exited 1: ` and an EMPTY tail. That blank tail was read as \"all codex accounts are out of usage\", and the proposed remedy was to repoint the sweep at Claude. Both the diagnosis and the remedy were wrong. Recording this because the same blank error is visible to every lane and invites the same conclusion.\n\nMEASURED CAUSE\n`~/.codex/auth.json` (mtime 2026-08-27 10:35) was overwritten: 3864B `auth_mode:'chatgpt'` with OAuth `tokens{...}` became 314B `auth_mode:'apikey'` whose `OPENAI_API_KEY` is 259 chars of papercusp's own coord wake-delivery text (a `delivery-<n>.md` path plus \"1 duplicate queued wake was coalesced into this ONE delivery\"). codex rejects that bearer at the HTTP header layer — `failed to convert header to a str for header name 'authorization'` — and writes the error to its `--json` STDOUT stream. `codex-cli-bridge.ts` captured stderr only, so the cause never surfaced. Tracked as EI-21618978789879488.\n\nCONTROLLED PROOF — identical argv, same model `gpt-5.6-sol`, same `model_reasoning_effort=xhigh`, only CODEX_HOME varies:\n  ~/.codex                          -> websocket auth-header error, exit 1\n  aviynw4_codex.codex-cli           -> turn.completed, agent_message \"OK\", 3.5s\nSo `gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh` was working the entire time.\n\nRULINGS\n1. Do NOT change `LEARNING_MODEL_SPEC` (packages/operator-core/lib/learning/model-policy.ts) in response to codex failures. It is the canonical contract for ~20 model-bearing learning paths (scout, gym, transfer, replay, ablation, iq-battery, the admission promoter) and is pinned by model-policy.test.ts:259-261 and transfer/live-deps.test.ts. The model was never the failing variable.\n2. Do NOT route learning traffic to Claude as a codex-outage remedy. Measured pool: codex 2/5 available; Claude 5/7 usage-walled (aviynw3, avistorewolf.com, aviynw10, aviynw4 all at utilization7d 1.0; aviynw 0.95). Claude is the MORE exhausted provider. That move would have degraded ~20 paths and left the credential destroyed.\n3. Treat `available:true` on an account as a QUOTA statement only. Account availability never validates that a credential can authenticate, so the clobbered account advertised `available:true, usageWalled:false, headroomFraction:0.81` while being unable to make a single call, and the pool selected it ahead of four healthy homes indefinitely. `codex-home-diagnostics.ts` reports only `authExists`, and a clobbered file exists — existence is not validity.\n4. A provider-wide outage claim needs a per-credential control before it is believed. One healthy sibling credential falsifies \"the provider is out\" in a single command.\n\nREMEDIATION APPLIED\n- `accounts:set-session-override { excludeAccounts:['chatgpt-sub-cli'] }` — the existing steer knob, reversible in one call once the credential is restored. Verified end-to-end: POST :8788/v1/responses with model gpt-5.6-sol now returns `status:'completed'`, `output_text:'OK'`, `gateway_codex_cli:true`.\n- `codexCliFailureDetail()` in codex-cli-bridge.ts now harvests diagnostics from the `--json` stdout stream as well as stderr, so a non-zero exit can never again be reported with an empty tail. Covered by 27/27 passing tests including a fixture built from this incident's actual stdout.\n\nRESIDUE (open on EI-21618978789879488): what WROTE coord delivery text into a credential file is still unidentified. The whole-file shape flip says a full replace, not a field patch. Restoring the `chatgpt-sub-cli` account itself needs an owner-interactive `codex login`; its OAuth tokens are unrecoverable from disk (verified across all of deploy-credentials/ plus ~/.codex).\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-027 — Serialize same-root bulk recovery under two-account Codex capacity\nDate: 2026-08-28\nFor WI-42278/P-012 recovery, keep the existing stable runId and set shardConcurrency=1 while the Codex pool has only two serving accounts; do not enqueue another logical root. A rearm issued while the prior routineFire dedup workflow is still PENDING does not change that workflow's serialized payload, so wait for terminal/null deduplication_id and verify the newly minted routineFire input before proceeding. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for the plan that makes a ratified design reference binding on implementation. Authored AFTER implementation, against as-built reality.\n\nTHE GOAL: once a reviewer ratifies a design reference, implementing that surface owes CURRENT PASSING deterministic evidence at every required case — and no prose, mask, substitution or stale record may stand in for it. Exploration before ratification stays completely unconstrained.\n\nCriteria are OUTCOME-shaped, not task-shaped: each asks whether the shipped system HAS a property, not whether an item was worked. Traces to D-004 (only deterministic engine evidence counts), D-019 (one reference = one image = one environment), D-020 (indistinguishable captures are a fourth bypass class), D-021 (noise only measurable by real captures), D-023 (enforcement scoped to the render host the threshold was measured on).\n\nHOW TO READ THE BOUND CHECKS — this is the most important instruction here. Every criterion carries a structured tests-check, and scorecards:emit EXECUTES those files at grading time, refusing a pass-rating contradicted by a red one. That is a floor, NOT a verdict. A green file proves THE TESTS PASS; the criterion claims A PROPERTY. The gap between those is where this rubric can be graded wrongly, and it is not hypothetical: during this rubric's own vetting, the reviewer described a criterion of theirs graded DEGRADED with two green bound files, because one proved ordering, the other proved truncation, and NOTHING exercised their composition. A grader running bindings mechanically would have rated it healthy.\n\nSo every method below requires the grader to do one thing a green file structurally cannot do: STATE WHAT THE BOUND FILES DO NOT EXERCISE. Compare what each binding EXERCISES against what the criterion CLAIMS, and name the unexercised middle. Each driftMarkers additionally names the BINDING's own failure mode, not just the property's. And a bound file with no falsifiability control — no deliberately-wrong implementation it CATCHES — is worth less than it appears, because green-and-vacuous is indistinguishable from green-and-real; where a control is absent, say so and rate accordingly rather than assuming.\n\nKNOWN RESIDUE, DISCLOSED: EI-21414614584540571 — ignoredRegions is recorded onto evidence but never reaches the engine, so a reviewer-authored mask is inert. mask-not-a-bypass.test.ts pins that the engine never receives regions, which keeps it inert rather than latent. This is stated so a grader does not spend a round rediscovering it. It is deliberately NOT accompanied by any instruction about how to weigh it: that judgement is the grader's, governed by criterion 2's driftMarkers, which name 'ignoredRegions reaches the engine' as a drift condition. If the residue threatens the criterion, the rubric should say so through its markers, not through the author's request.\n\nVETTING: critiqued in consult conv-mt8nose4-0000-0a1aa1a65bef4c16a0a4cd29904c140b by su-9aa2b64c (routed below the relevance floor, so weighed as first-principles review). Their critique drove this revision: the three binding repairs above, the merge of two criteria on shared FAILURE MODE rather than shared topic, and deletion of the previous 'grade WITH it' instruction. One deliberate deviation is noted in criterion 5.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** Complete the evidence matrix and runtime verification tasks below, then have a non-implementing reviewer grade the rubric and ratify the result. The structured criteria in `template_data` remain canonical.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan `bulk-resolver-controls-and-run-lifecycle-2026-08-24`, authored post-implementation against as-built reality (audited sha `ac33925e`, auditSeq 1). Goal traced: visible/configurable/validated resolver launch settings for Inbox bulk resolve + Plans cleanup, with hardened run creation, manifest performance, liveness recovery, and deterministic cleanup execution. Decisions traced: D-001 (reuse existing launch vocabulary), D-002 (fixed execution invariants; configure only meaningful axes), D-003 (click-time settings snapshot on every run), D-004 (owner-bound heartbeats/writes; canonical `classifyRunLiveness`; UI must not duplicate the timeout rule).\n\n## Requirements\n\nThe acceptance record must make the following truths testable against the as-built implementation, without introducing new product behavior:\n\n- Both Inbox bulk-resolve and Plans cleanup expose validated model, effort, and account settings through the existing launch vocabulary; fresh, headless, and role-su remain fixed invariants.\n- Every run persists the validated click-time launch snapshot and uses that snapshot for reload, reporting, diagnostics, restart, and audit.\n- Resolver liveness and recovery are owner-bound end to end: stale prior owners cannot heartbeat, mutate outcomes, or settle a replacement; readers and UI derive staleness from the canonical classifier.\n- Inbox run creation and manifest generation are atomic and use one canonical action-map read while retaining locked just-in-time action revalidation.\n- Provable Plans cleanup findings execute deterministically before any LLM resolver launch; judgment work remains reviewable.\n- The evidence trail covers focused UI/core tests, real-Postgres integration (including migration 945), scoped typechecks, and the scoped affected run, with every residue item attributed to an external cause or marked unknown.\n\n## Design\n\nUse the six criteria in `template_data` as the sole rubric source. Build an evidence matrix keyed by `configurable-validated-launch`, `click-time-snapshot`, `owner-bound-liveness-recovery`, `atomic-manifest-performance`, `deterministic-cleanup-first`, and `verification-residue-honesty`:\n\n- For each key, cite the exact source/test files and the executed command or ledger result; do not infer a green criterion from a plan statement alone.\n- Run the smallest focused UI/core and real-Postgres falsifiers first, then the scoped typechecks and affected suite. Record command, result, and runtime/build identity in the acceptance work item and plan revision.\n- Grade each criterion `healthy`, `degraded`, `broken`, or `unknown`. A missing or stale probe is `unknown`, not green; a red result is retained with its root cause and whether it is plan-introduced.\n- Preserve D-001 through D-004: extend existing launch/configuration and run-authority surfaces, keep ownership and click-time semantics, and do not add a parallel catalog, selector, timeout rule, or persistence writer.\n- After the matrix is complete, route the evidence to a reviewer who did not implement the underlying plan. The reviewer may ratify the rubric; the proposer must not self-ratify.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Evidence matrix\n\n- **P-001** `done` Map each template_data criterion to exact source/test citations and the executed probe that can falsify it; include the audited implementation SHA ac33925e, decisions D-001 through D-004, and a checked/not-checked/residue record. importance: high — note: ← WI-1245890 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Runtime verification\n\n- **P-002** `done` Execute the smallest focused UI/core falsifiers and the real-Postgres integration checks (including migration 945), then run scoped typechecks and the scoped affected suite; record command, result, runtime/build identity, and any externally caused residue. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-1246677 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Independent grading\n\n- **P-003** `done` Have a non-implementing reviewer grade all six criteria healthy/degraded/broken/unknown from the evidence matrix, classify any residue as plan-introduced or external, and ratify or revise the acceptance rubric without self-ratification. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: Independent non-implementer grade complete at rubric revision 10: scorecard EI-21915300701189038 (supersedes EI-21909902857384208). 5 healthy / 1 degraded / 0 broken / 0 unknown; zero plan-introduced regressions; residue external. Re-measured at HEAD 0ecd21584c: 135 passed / 0 failed across all 9 cited files. Ratification deliberately NOT performed by the grader.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n\n### D-001 — P-002 scope verdict: target radius green; run-level reds are external drift\nDate: 2026-08-30\nMeasured: current staging HEAD is 4184805d39bfd25cb4c28be3f287eb006301d07c. The P-002 radius is the exact 17 paths in the affected command; every run-start blob at ef5bcbd106ad3710f42508be863ed9e67714fcee equals its current HEAD blob. The direct current-HEAD probes are green: seven unit/route/UI files, 87 tests plus 6 settings-control tests; two real-Postgres files, 32 plus 10 tests. The bulk-run integration exercises heartbeat_at from migration 945 (libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/945-bulk-run-heartbeat.sql). The durable affected task 0mtg00tc31tznp4s1r1 / run 4066957-bc46f8b8 reported AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT status=failed tasks=27 failed=3 with 11 failing files, but none overlap the 17-path radius; it also reported runStartHead ef5bcbd1 and reportHead 3d3a20f with 94 commits/165 changed files and two stale failing blobs. Therefore P-002 may treat the 11 reds as externally caused tree-drift residue, not plan-introduced regressions. The per-run marker says changedPaths=9 while the recovered wrapper command contains 17 paths; retain this provenance discrepancy as run instrumentation residue and do not call the affected run a clean green verdict. P-003 must grade from the radius-green evidence plus this explicitly disclosed external residue.\nRelated: P-002\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"bulk-resolver-external-contract-drift-2026-08-24","title":"External contract drift exposed by the bulk resolver affected run","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-25","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: External contract drift exposed by the bulk resolver affected run\nslug: bulk-resolver-external-contract-drift-2026-08-24\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-25\nupdated: 2026-08-30\n---\n## Goal\n\nRestore a current, evidence-backed acceptance verdict for `bulk-resolver-controls-and-run-lifecycle-2026-08-24` by repairing the external contract drift still reproduced from affected run `835484-75ab12f4`, clearing Cargo's disk-admission blocker, and re-running the complete declared acceptance checks without overstated causation.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Preserve the bulk-resolver implementation and decisions D-001 through D-004; these repairs are external residue, not feature redesign.\n- Update tests to the current ratified source contracts rather than reverting unrelated source changes.\n- Sync vendored template-kit files byte-for-byte from the canonical `libs/generic/template-kit` surface.\n- Reclaim only demonstrably safe local diagnostic/cache/temp storage; never delete a peer's uncommitted work.\n- Treat `AFFECTED_TESTS_LOAD_SUSPECT` as an advisory only. A red is externally attributed only with direct source/log/history evidence or a fresh passing reproduction.\n- Do not fire `release:checkpoint-run`; D-042's exact serializer retains that gate.\n\n## Design\n\nThe repair is test-first and source-preserving. For each reproduced contract failure, read the current writer/source commit and change the stale assertion or full-module mock to that committed contract; do not revert the production behavior. Mobile templates reuse the canonical `libs/generic/template-kit` bytes through a mechanical vendor sync, verified by the existing bundle-integrity test. Storage recovery uses only local diagnostic tables explicitly marked trimmable, disposable caches, and individually verified inactive temporary build artifacts; no canonical worktree, peer-held file, or unknown directory is removed. Verification runs the exact residue files, the acceptance rubric's declared files, and Cargo through their owning repository runners. The independent scorecard records `healthy`, `degraded`, `broken`, or `unknown` per criterion from those current results and corrects any earlier causal prose that exceeded the affected-run writer's contract.\n\n## Scope boundaries\n\nIn scope: the five reproduced test-contract drift classes, six drifted mobile-template vendor files, safe disk recovery sufficient for Cargo admission, Cargo verification, the independent scorecard, and corrections to the recovered plan's audit/completion wording. Out of scope: unrelated product changes, a duplicate green-checkpoint run, or changing the bulk-resolver feature itself unless a fresh acceptance check finds a genuine plan-radius regression.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Every reproduced residue file passes in a fresh scoped run.\n- The six mobile template-kit vendor files are byte-identical to canonical.\n- Cargo is actually spawned and exits green; an admission refusal is not a pass.\n- All nine acceptance-rubric check files pass on unchanged tested content.\n- The independent scorecard states only evidence the underlying writers/logs establish.\n- `WI-41456` closes with structured verification and the recovered feature plan receives an evidence-correct accept/reject verdict.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Drafted from the recovered session and fresh residue reproduction.\n\n**Next:** Complete the spec-triad blocker, start the plan, claim P-001, and repair sequentially in this session.\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract drift repairs\n\n- **P-001** `done` Update the LLM backend-selection test to the current authoritative Codex-model contract introduced outside the bulk-resolver plan. — note: ← WI-41471 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Complete the git-sync action test's full-module mock with the new exported byte-limit constants and verify threshold propagation. — note: ← WI-41472 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Align the coord:inbox and coord:presence contract tests with the later WI-41389/WI-41252 source decisions without widening the live schemas. — note: ← WI-41473 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Sync the Android and iPhone vendored template-kit files from `libs/generic/template-kit` and pass template-bundle integrity. — note: ← WI-41474 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Verification recovery\n\n- **P-005** `done` Reclaim safe local storage until Cargo admission succeeds, then run the selected desktop Cargo suite to a real terminal verdict. — note: ← WI-41475 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Re-run all prior residue plus the nine acceptance-rubric checks, correct the recovered plan's durable evidence, emit the independent scorecard, and close WI-41456. Repair their stale tests/vendored copies; do not roll those source contracts back to make this plan green.\n\n### D-002 — Advisory is not causation\n\n`AFFECTED_TESTS_LOAD_SUSPECT` and timeout signatures explain why a failure needs re-triage; they do not establish that load caused it. The acceptance record will distinguish direct causes, still-open failures, and unexercised lanes.\n\n### D-003 — Activation source audit preserved during live-schema mismatch\n\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThe complete plan-related sources were re-read before execution: current Codex session `01a03687-7819-7bc1-9660-bdfd02fa4619` turns 1–8 and recovered predecessor session `01a03582-4a29-7671-9231-8ddf8b614db9` turns 0–86. This Decision is the durable fallback mapping until the running operator refreshes.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"directed-pair-work-items-2026-08-25","title":"The Directed Pair — paired execution of substantive work items","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-25","owner":"aviynw@gmail.com","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: The Directed Pair — paired execution of substantive work items\nslug: directed-pair-work-items-2026-08-25\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-25\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: aviynw@gmail.com\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** 17 of 20 items terminal; P-007/P-008/P-009 blocked. The wall remains PURELY a deployment wall.\n\n**Ship-protocol progress.** Step 1 is not met until P-007 runs. Step 2 IS met for everything auditable: `plans:audit` seq 8 (2026-08-27T17:24Z, sha 065f1af9b9) covered all 17 terminal items — 42 citations checked and resolved, 14 code-verified, and 4 recorded `not-code` (the verification, runbook-authoring and adversarial-audit items, whose deliverable is a Decision or work-item findings rather than code). The three blocked items are correctly uncovered. Run by the takeover leader as a NON-implementer for 16 of the 17.\n\n**Steps 3–6 (rubric → vetting → grading → verdict) are DEFERRED ON PURPOSE.** The rubric is authored against as-built reality and any later edit invalidates its attestation; the plan's substance is the pilot, so a rubric written before P-007 runs would describe outcomes that do not exist and be invalidated by the run it judges.\n\n**Exclusion provenance RESOLVED.** The \"no cohort materialization before WI-41764 live tested=deployed / never inspect WI-40086\" boundary is backed by **D-034** as a lane-inherited plan Decision, binding regardless of authorship. D-034's owner-typed citation covers the fleet shape only, so the exclusions are Decision-authoritative rather than verified owner speech. They stand and remain uncrossed.\n\n**⚠ DEPLOYMENT BLOCKER RE-DIAGNOSED (17:47Z) — the earlier reading is superseded.** Not a global git-sync outage, and not owned by a live agent: `su-5fa940bc` has ENDED. Only the papercusp **superproject** leg is lock-starved (siblings sync normally each tick); `git-sync:papercusp` is held exclusive by an owner stamped a pid not running on this host, re-acquired every ~10min. Filed with evidence and a proposed fix as **WI-209800** (critical, open, unowned).\n\n**Next:** Nothing in this lane is executable until the superproject can commit — now tracked as **WI-209800**, which is unowned and needs either an owner decision or a claimant (do NOT fire `git-sync:run`: it dispatches the same `system:git-sync` action into the same starved lock check). Verify the freeze by BLOB ONLY (`git hash-object <path>` vs `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`) — `routines:list` git-sync health reports `synced` and `dev:pipeline_position` reports `committedLocal/deployed: true` while the tree is frozen. Once commits resume: (1) re-send the IDENTICAL completion payloads for WI-175665 and WI-139197, which sit at completionAuthority:'proposed' only because their blobs are uncommitted; (2) green the gate (WI-40086 lane) and deploy; (3) re-verify both WI-134439 defects and WI-139197 against the LIVE operator and close WI-134439; (4) unblock and run P-007, then P-008/P-009; (5) only then author the acceptance rubric against as-built reality, vet it, have a NON-implementer grade it, record the acceptance verdict, and ship.\n\n## Requirements\n\nShip the directed-pair pilot as a preregistered, auditable experiment without contaminating treatment assignment or grading. P-013 through P-015 may execute before the live gate; no real participant binding or pilot stamp is allowed until WI-41764 records status=passed, judgementPersisted=true, and identical testedSha/deployedSha. Execute only the D-032 exact 21-item A/B/C roster and never reroll seeds or substitute after arm disclosure. Each terminal outcome must carry complete assignment, claim-window, participant-cost, scorecard, and tripwire evidence; any missing or nonfinite coverage fails closed. Independent graders must not be participants and must remain blind to arm and treatment. The D-033 thresholds remain immutable until outcomes are collected. WI-40086 is outside scope.\n\n## Design\n\nReuse canonical work_items, scorecards, agent_usage_samples, pilot:assign, pilot:collect, and existing fleet/session rails. The execution pipeline is proof check -> freeze the cohort-wide participant roster -> eligibility re-read -> confirm:true materialization -> one isolated solo session for every A/B item or one isolated director plus implementer pair for every C item -> claim-window close on terminal completion -> push completion event -> blind grader scorecard -> push grade-ready event -> collection -> machine verdict -> P-008 policy encoding -> P-009 documentation. Cohort and item ids bind every stage. A/B claim windows contain one participant; C windows contain exactly two; no session may cross items or arms. Abort before the next stage on identity, eligibility, event, pricing, grading, or rollback mismatch. P-014 records the exact operational runbook and P-015 adversarially audits it before any real materialization.\n\n## Background\n\nOwner-initiated design exploration (2026-08-25, interactive session): every substantive work item is executed by a PAIR — a **director** that prompts the way a human owner would, and an **implementer** that structurally cannot act unless prompted (call-response by removed wake sources, not by politeness).\n\n**Design artifact (canonical visual spec, v2):** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/dafd1d07-da8a-4c60-a379-4de851468ce8 — source file `/home/marsh-office/.papercusp/artifacts/directed-pair.html` (deliberately outside the repo tree; republish via the Artifact tool from that path — pass the URL as `url` when updating from another session).\n\n**Research basis:** WI-41723 (survey of 2024–2026 literature; full citations in its completion record). Filter applied per the owner's caveat (much of the literature predates current-strength agents): capability findings DECAY as models improve; incentive/structural findings PERSIST; verification-difficulty findings STRENGTHEN (stronger generators produce subtler wrong claims). Prior art validating the shape: PairCoder (ASE'24 navigator/driver, arXiv:2409.05001); MAST (NeurIPS'25, arXiv:2503.13657 — verification failures ≈23.5% of multi-agent failures; +15.6% success from adding a verification step); Redwood AI-control trusted-monitoring protocols; process-beats-outcome supervision (arXiv:2305.20050). Current-model cautions driving the revisions: LLM-judge >50% error under bias stress (arXiv:2606.19544), self-preference bias (arXiv:2604.22891), Control Illusion — prompt hierarchies fail under conflict (arXiv:2502.15851), SWE-bench architecture-agnosticism (arXiv:2506.17208) + multi-agent token multipliers.\n\n### The v2 design (what the phases below implement)\n\n- **Director**: strongest model tier; holds the work item + completion authority; never edits. Issues MILESTONE-grain directives (not step-grain), each carrying pre-registered done-criteria. Verifies from the LEDGER (`testing:runs`, `dev:pipeline_position`, `capability:git` diff) — never from pasted output. 2-round rework cap per milestone, then fresh-context resample. Records cross-lane rulings as plan Decisions.\n- **Implementer**: parked between turns — only wake source is the director (no loop:arm, no scheduler pull, no AUTO). Load-bearing constraints TOOL-DENIED at launch (`work_items:complete`, `loop:arm`, `scheduler:get_next`), not persona-forbidden. Runs its full internal loop (edit/test/fix) within a milestone. Evidence replies carry ledger refs + decisions made + surprises. Authority via a system-prompt delegation clause scoped to the WI — provenance spoofing is banned.\n- **Pairing scope**: adaptive tier gate — trivial = solo; substantive = solo + ledger-checked review gate (pilot arm B); big/high-risk = paired. The threshold is empirical and re-measured on model upgrades.\n\n## Phase 1 — personas and rails\n\n- **P-001** `done` Author `directed-implementer` persona via blueprint:extend: call-response contract (wake → execute the milestone → evidence reply via coord:send → END TURN), scoped blocker resolution (fix what blocks the current milestone; implementer holds file locks via the automatic hook), coord wake/reply protocol, implementer-compaction recovery (the directive+evidence history is the carry document) blocked-by: P-001, P-002 — note: ← WI-41756 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Fleet spec `type` field: 'single' (default — today's fleet, unchanged) | 'paired'; See D-014.\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — the three-arm pilot\n\n- **P-005** `done` Build arm B — solo + review gate: a solo-agent variant with a forced, ledger-checked self-review step before work_items:complete (the cheap structural alternative that current SWE-bench skepticism predicts may capture most of the pair's value) — note: ← WI-41760 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Pilot design: ~20 substantive-tier items × 3 arms (A solo baseline / B solo+gate / C directed pair); assignment protocol; metrics = reopen rate, completion-integrity audit failures, wall-clock, token cost; grading rubric authored per the acceptance-rubric discipline blocked-by: P-004, P-005 — note: ← WI-41761 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `todo` Run the pilot; independent (non-implementer) grading via scorecards; record the verdict and per-tier deltas blocked-by: P-006 — note: Blocked — see D-041, updated 2026-08-27 after WI-41764's e2e probe was RUN (it is now done). Inspect participant binding, isolated session/pair launch, exact claim-window start/end, blind grader identity, cost attribution, push-event ordering/latching, rollback, and fail-closed evidence fields; reconcile P-015 findings into a concrete acceptance matrix and record exact corrections. Do not materialize a cohort or cross any D-034 exclusion. importance: high — note: ← WI-42427 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `done` Implement canonical pilot participant binding and role-dispatch receipts by extending the existing launch/session/claim/coord surfaces—no parallel roster system. Fresh launch must expose canonical ownerId+sessionId; after the run-owned claim, persist a server-issued binding receipt {receiptId,itemId,ownerId,sessionId,role,claimVersion,bindingIssuedAtMs}; dispatch must return a linked role/session receipt with dispatchedAtMs>=bindingIssuedAtMs. Add a cohort-wide validator for unique ownerIds/sessionIds, one-to-one provenance, distinct C roles, and no cross-item/arm/role reuse. Deliver a typed module plus focused launch/dispatch/binding tests; do not edit pilot-cohort.ts. No cohort materialization and never inspect WI-40086. importance: high — note: ← WI-42429 completed (done)\n- **P-018** `done` Implement a reusable atomic pilot-materialization core, isolated from pilot-cohort.ts until integration. In one PG transaction/CAS over the frozen 21 ids, require each expected row version, state=open, claimable/unblocked/unheld, exact frozen assignee, canonical binding receipts, and all seven pilot keys absent; any miss leaves zero visible stamps. Bind arm-B proof to the authoritative current deployed green SHA at confirm time and return the exact proof/current-pin receipt. Persist exact preimages; rollback must verify every touched row or return an explicit cohort-abort receipt. Add transaction/concurrency/current-pin/rollback recurrence tests. No cohort materialization and never inspect WI-40086. importance: high — note: ← WI-42430 completed (done)\n- **P-019** `done` Implement reusable pilot collection and push-fan-in guards, isolated from pilot-cohort.ts until integration. Enforce a prebound grader per item disjoint from every participant/operator/runbook author, opaque pre-reveal packet fingerprint, createdAt>=closedAt, exact returned card id, exactly one complete non-provisional audit-clean card, and typed duplicate/unbound/pre-terminal gaps. Tie cost windows to canonical binding+dispatch receipts and revalidate them at collection. Provide event-cap-aware completion and grading fan-in (21 exact receipts or 20+1 roots); scorecard events are wake hints only and durable ledger/card ids are evidence. Add focused grading/window/event tests.
