Remove caller-supplied identity/window trust, wire atomic confirm/current-pin proof receipts, canonical binding/dispatch verification, exact-card grading, durable 20+1 fan-in receipts, and conservative typed gaps. Run the full focused pilot + launch/dispatch/event/scorecard suites, scoped TSC/catalog/format checks, and an independent executable dry run; record the final implementation Decision/runbook correction. Keep pilot:assign confirm:true forbidden and D-032 unstamped until all guards pass plus WI-41764 is terminal with judgementPersisted and testedSha=deployedSha=current green deployed SHA. Never inspect WI-40086. blocked-by: P-017, P-018, P-019 importance: high — note: ← WI-42432 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — adopt and keep honest\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Encode the adaptive tier gate from pilot results (which tiers pair, which get arm B's gate); document the re-measurement trigger — re-run the 3-arm comparison on major model upgrades: pairing must re-earn its keep each generation blocked-by: P-007\n- **P-009** `todo` Fold outcomes into an agent-insights doc (docs:author) + final artifact update; generalize or retire per the verdict blocked-by: P-008\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Model pairing specifics: which cross-family combination for director vs implementer given current account-routing options — owner call at launch time.\n- If arm B's review gate wins, should it become a universal completion hook (mechanical gate on work_items:complete) rather than a persona behavior?\n- Milestone sizing heuristics: what bounds a milestone (expected turns? file count? risk?) — refine during the pilot.\n- Leadership inside a paired-type fleet (the pair-as-construct question itself was ANSWERED by D-008 [owner:2026-08-25]: a pair is a fleet TYPE): with N pairs in one fleet, do directors report to a fleet leader above them, or is one director dual-hatted as leader? Also: does the tier gate route ITEMS to differently-typed fleets, or does a paired fleet's claim spec admit only substantive+/big items? Settle in P-004/P-010.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Directives are milestone-grain, not step-grain\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThe director issues milestone-sized directives (a bounded deliverable with done-criteria), and the implementer runs its full internal edit/test/fix loop within the milestone. Per-step navigation (PairCoder-era driver/navigator) was capability compensation for 2024 models and adds only latency with current implementers. The director gates milestone boundaries and completion — the structural checks — not individual moves. Aging filter applied: capability findings decay; incentive findings persist. [owner-reviewed design conversation 2026-08-25; research WI-41723]\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-002 — Verification is ledger-grounded — pasted output is a claim, not evidence\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThe director verifies every milestone and the final completion from system-of-record surfaces it reads itself: testing:runs rows, dev:pipeline_position / gate cells, the actual diff via capability:git. It never accepts the implementer's rendering of results. Basis: MAST found deployed verifiers superficial; LLM-judge literature (2026, current models) shows >50% error under bias-inducing conditions and vulnerability to adversarial phrasing; the generation-verification gap literature shows stronger generators produce subtler wrong claims — so this ruling strengthens, not decays, as models improve.\nRelated: P-002, P-005\n\n### D-003 — Director authority comes from system-prompt delegation — provenance spoofing is banned\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThe implementer's launch context (genuinely system-level, authored by our infrastructure) carries one scoped grant: directives from director <sid> via coord are authoritative for WI-X, subordinate only to actual owner turns and standing safety rails. Re-stamping director messages as [owner:] is prohibited: it would poison compaction provenance (the WI-3532 manufactured-directive class, including false PERMISSION claims), and it leans on exactly the behavior instruction-hierarchy training is hardening against — an authority mechanism that weakens every model generation. Truthful stamp class instead: [director:<sid> for WI-X].\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-004 — Load-bearing implementer constraints are tool-denied at launch, never persona-only\nDate: 2026-08-25\nwork_items:complete, loop:arm, scheduler:get_next (minimum set) are removed from the implementer's toolset at launch, the same mechanism as NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY. Rationale: Control Illusion (arXiv:2502.15851) and successors show prompt hierarchies fail inconsistently under conflict, and smarter models are better at rationalizing around prose rules. Structure where possible; delegation prose only for what structure cannot express. The call-response mode itself already follows this principle (no wake sources = structural).\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-005 — Two failed rounds per milestone, then fresh-context resample\nDate: 2026-08-25\nAfter two failed rework rounds on one milestone, the director stops re-prompting the same implementer context and instead relaunches fresh (or switches approach / escalates). Grounds: anchoring is structural to autoregressive models — the failed attempt in context conditions the next one — and Redwood control evaluations found resampling among the best-performing protocols. MAST's step-repetition statistic (15.7%, its top single mode) is treated as era-bound corroboration, not the load-bearing justification.\nRelated: P-002\n\n### D-006 — Director gets the strongest model; implementer may be cheaper; cross-family preferred\nDate: 2026-08-25\nDecomposition, delegation, and judgment have the capability floor (delegation studies: ~0.85 with strong-tier orchestrators vs ~0.45 unusable at fast tier — 2025/26, current models), so never economize on the director; the implementer tier is free. Cross-model-family pairing preferred where operationally convenient: self-preference bias (judges favoring their own model's output, arXiv:2604.22891) means a same-model pair rubber-stamps more. Concrete family choice is an owner call at launch (account routing).\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-007 — The tier gate is adaptive and pairing must re-earn its keep each model generation\nDate: 2026-08-25\nPairing scope is an empirical dial, not a constant: trivial = solo; substantive = solo + ledger-checked review gate (arm B); big/high-risk = paired — with the thresholds set by a 3-arm pilot (~20 substantive items; metrics: reopen rate, completion-integrity audit failures, wall-clock, token cost) and RE-MEASURED on major model upgrades. Grounds: SWE-bench leaderboard analysis finds no architecture wins; solo agents keep improving, shrinking the band where a pair pays; the Agyn-skeptic reading suggests the structural feedback loop, not the second agent, may carry most of the value — arm B exists to test exactly that.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-008\n\n### D-008 — Pairs are a fleet TYPE — spec takes type:'single'|'paired', per-role launch params, auto-coupling\nDate: 2026-08-25\n[owner:2026-08-25] Four rulings, superseding P-004's open launch-shape question (which offered \"director launches implementer directly, or a 2-member fleet\"): (1) The pair is not a new construct — it is a TYPE of fleet: the fleet spec gains `type`. (2) `type:'single'` = today's fleet, unchanged and the default; `type:'paired'` = the directed-pair system. (3) Each director↔implementer pair is coupled at launch through the existing coupling system (coord:couple, declared with reason = the pair's work item) so each sees the other's working state in detail; decoupled at pair wind-down. (4) Launch options are TYPE-DRIVEN: the paired form accepts the full launch parameter set — model/effort, count, headless, account, carry — SEPARATELY for the directors group and the implementers group. Spawn announcements cover both role groups.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-009 — Launch options are CONDITIONAL on fleet type — the schema branches, it does not merge\nDate: 2026-08-25\n[owner:2026-08-25] Owner check made explicit what D-008 left implicit (\"type-driven\"). The launch option SHAPE is conditional on `type`, on every surface that offers a launch (tool schema, psu picker, launch UI): `type:'single'` presents today's FLAT parameter set (count, model/effort, headless, account, carry) completely unchanged — no per-role nesting, no new required fields, so existing callers and habits keep working; `type:'paired'` presents the SAME parameter set as two per-role groups, `directors: {...}` and `implementers: {...}`, so the roles can differ in every knob independently (a top-tier visible director beside cheaper headless implementers is the expected shape, per D-006). This is a BRANCH, not a superset: a launch whose option shape does not match its declared type is REJECTED with invalid_args naming the expected shape — never silently coerced, never a flat value quietly broadcast to both roles, because a silent coercion is how someone gets a fleet of directors running the implementer's model. Corollary for disclosure: the spawn announcement (account routing + model + carry, mandatory even under AUTO) covers BOTH role groups on a paired launch — one line per role, not a merged summary.\nRelated: P-010, P-011\n\n### D-010 — The pair's ENGAGEMENT is a plan item; the work items under it are the MILESTONES\nDate: 2026-08-25\n[owner:2026-08-25 \"what do you think about making the director/implementer pair work across an entire plan item instead of just a work item?\"] YES — adopted, and it refines D-001 rather than replacing it. Two distinct scales, named separately: ENGAGEMENT SCOPE = what the pair is assigned; MILESTONE GRAIN = what one directive covers.\n\nDEFAULT: engagement = a PLAN ITEM (P-NNN); milestones = the WORK ITEMS beneath it. The director claims the plan lane (coord:declare-intent { current_plan_slug, items:['P-NNN'] }), decomposes it, and MINTS each milestone as a real work item (work_items:create { plan_item:{ slug, item } } — the forward coverage edge already exists), hands it to the implementer, verifies from the ledger, and closes it. When every milestone is closed, the director flips the plan item.\n\nWHY (four gains, none requiring a new primitive): (1) The director's milestone decomposition — previously an ephemeral, private list inside one work item — becomes DURABLE and fleet-visible ledger rows; peers can see what the pair is doing without asking. (2) Pair setup cost (two sessions, coupling, delegation grant, context load) amortizes across several milestones instead of being repaid per work item; fixed overhead is the main economic objection to pairing (D-007). (3) The director accumulates context ACROSS milestones, so it catches cross-milestone drift — milestone 3 quietly undoing milestone 1's decision — which is precisely the inter-agent-misalignment/context-loss class that Cognition's argument warns about. (4) It uses existing primitives end to end: plan-lane claims, work→plan_item coverage edges, plan-item rollup as the completion gate.\n\nWORK-ITEM ENGAGEMENT REMAINS AVAILABLE, not deprecated: a standalone big/high-risk work item with no plan item above it is a legitimate engagement; there the milestones are ephemeral director-authored steps as in D-001. So engagement scope is 'plan-item' (default) | 'work-item', declared at launch and settled by what the pair was handed.\n\nCOSTS ACCEPTED: (a) Serialization — work items under one plan item that are genuinely independent could otherwise run in parallel across a fleet; the mitigation is that a paired fleet runs N pairs on DIFFERENT plan items, and a director may hand a genuinely-parallel plan item back for single-type routing rather than serialize it. (b) Larger blast radius per bad director — mitigated by D-002 (ledger verification) and D-005 (resample), and bounded by the plan item, which is a reviewed unit. (c) Longer implementer engagements compact more often — which makes D-005's fresh-context resample MORE valuable, not less; the directive+evidence history remains the carry document.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-004\n\n### D-011 — D-011 — Activation audit (recorded here: plans:audit has no `phase` arg on this build)\nDate: 2026-08-25\n[owner:2026-08-25 \"implement it yourself now from start to finish\"] supersedes the earlier \"keep as draft\" verdict; plan moves draft→active. (8) plan-item engagement → D-010, P-001/P-002/P-004.\n\nREJECTED ALTERNATIVES on record: provenance spoofing (D-003); persona-prose-only constraints (D-004); step-grain directives (D-001); merged option superset (D-009); pair as a distinct non-fleet construct (D-008); work-item-only engagement (D-010, retained as the secondary mode, not the default).\n\nOWNER CORRECTIONS incorporated: aging filter on the literature; conditional-not-merged launch options; plan-item engagement scope; keep the diagram in sync.\n\nOPEN QUESTIONS carried, not dropped: cross-family model pairing; arm-B-gate-as-universal-hook; milestone sizing heuristics; leadership inside a paired fleet + item routing across fleet types.\n\nPROMISED FOLLOW-UPS: pilot rubric + independent (non-implementer) grading at Phase 2; re-measurement trigger at Phase 3; agent-insights doc at P-009.\n\nGAPS FOUND AND REPAIRED THIS PASS: P-004 still offered the launch shape D-008 had settled (fixed, plan v15); a stale open question already answered by D-008 (replaced, v15); the type-conditional option contract was implicit (made explicit, D-009 + P-011, v16); the artifact lacked an engagement view (Fig 2 added, artifact v2.3).\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-012 — Pair count lives at the TOP level; per-role groups carry role knobs only, never `count`\nDate: 2026-08-25\nImplementation of P-011 surfaced an ambiguity in D-009 that the artifact's launch snippet had baked in: it showed `count` inside BOTH `directors:{…}` and `implementers:{…}`. Two independent counts can express `directors:{count:1}, implementers:{count:3}` — a fleet that is not pairs at all, which is precisely the shape the `paired` TYPE exists to guarantee against (D-008: \"N director↔implementer pairs\"; P-012 auto-couples each pair 1:1, which is undefined when the counts differ).\n\nRULING — for `type:'paired'`:\n- **`count` at the TOP level is the number of PAIRS.** One source of truth for N. A paired fleet of `count:3` has 3 directors, 3 implementers, 6 members, 3 couplings.\n- **The per-role groups carry ROLE knobs only**: `agent`, `model`, `effort`, `headless`, `account`, `carry`. Every one stays independent per role, which is the substance of D-009 (a top-tier visible director beside cheaper headless implementers).\n- **`count` inside a role group is REJECTED** with `invalid_args` pointing at top-level `count` — not silently ignored, and not honoured as a per-role override. Silently ignoring it is how someone believes they launched 1 director for 3 implementers and gets 3 pairs.\n\nThis NARROWS D-009, it does not overturn it: the option shape still BRANCHES on type and still never merges. What changes is that the branch's paired arm is `{ count, directors:{…}, implementers:{…} }` rather than two fully-symmetric groups.\n\nRejected alternative: keep `count` in both groups and validate they are equal. It preserves a pleasing symmetry but makes one field redundant-but-load-bearing, and adds a whole failure class (unequal counts) that the top-level form cannot express at all. Prefer the encoding where the invariant is unrepresentable over the one where it is merely checked.\n\nFollow-up: the artifact's Launch snippet (Fig-adjacent code block) showed the rejected shape and has been corrected to match.\n\n### D-013 — Implementer tool-denial is a server-side ROLE gate; --disallowedTools is defence-in-depth, not the rail\nDate: 2026-08-25\nP-003 said \"wired into the launch path the same way NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY is\". Located and read, that mechanism does NOT generalise to the implementer's denials, and adopting it verbatim would have produced a rail that looks enforced and is not.\n\nWHAT IS THERE (correcting the plan's own note — the module DOES exist; the recorded path was one directory too shallow):\n- `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/no-subagent-deny.ts` — `NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY = ['Task','Agent','Workflow']` + `noSubagentToolsDenyFlag()` → `--disallowedTools=…`.\n- Two sibling precedents in the same directory: `native-scheduler-deny.ts`, `owner-desktop-notify-deny.ts`.\n- `apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs` duplicates the rendered literal (plain node, cannot import TS); a lockstep test in `apps/operator/lib/psu-launcher.test.ts` pins the copies together.\n\nWHY IT DOES NOT TRANSFER: `--disallowedTools` is a CLIENT-side flag. The implementer's denials (`work_items:complete`, `loop:arm`, `scheduler:get_next`) are papercusp MCP tools, and `tools:invoke` dispatches any catalog tool SERVER-side. This is the only layer both paths pass through.\n2. **SECONDARY = `--disallowedTools`**, carrying the client-native tools (Task/Agent/Workflow already) and the mangled MCP names as belt-and-braces. Defence-in-depth, never the thing relied on.\n3. **VERIFY LIVE, both paths.** P-003 already demanded a live check; this widens it: the acceptance evidence must show the denial holding for a DIRECT call *and* for a `tools:invoke` of the same verb. The no-subagent module's own history is the argument — a `Task`-only deny silently became a no-op when the tool was renamed `Agent`, and nothing detected it until someone tested a real spawn.\n4. Follow the existing lockstep-test discipline if any literal has to be duplicated into plain-node launcher code.\n\n### D-014 — D-014: paired seats are INTERLEAVED and clamp to whole pairs, and the paired arm reuses the existing per-member override path\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThree settled choices in wiring `type:'paired'` into `fleet:launch-on-plan`.\n\n**1. Seat ordering is INTERLEAVED, not blocked.** Seat 2k is the DIRECTOR of pair k; seat 2k+1 is its IMPLEMENTER.\n\nThe obvious alternative is blocked (`d,d,…,i,i,…`). It is wrong here for one decisive reason: **launch waves get clamped routinely** — the capacity clamp, the host-memory clamp and `MAX_MEMBERS` all open fewer seats than requested, and this is normal operation, not an error path.\n\n- Interleaved, a truncated wave degrades to FEWER WHOLE PAIRS — a smaller version of what the caller asked for.\n- Blocked, it degrades to all-directors-and-no-implementers: every seat opens, `openCount` reports success, nothing can be coupled, and the fleet is silently useless.\n\nInterleaving also makes pair identity derivable from the seat index alone (`pairIndexOfSeat = floor(seat/2)`), which is exactly what P-012's auto-coupling consumes — no side table, and nothing to re-sync when a member is respawned into an existing seat.\n\n**2. An odd seat allowance opens one FEWER seat, never one half-pair.** `wholePairSeats()` rounds down. A lone director is not a degraded pair but a broken one: it has nobody to direct, and (per D-013) the implementer-side denials mean it cannot fall back to doing the work itself. The clamp is reported rather than silent — `pairing.pairs` vs `pairing.requestedPairs` on the result — because quietly opening `count-1` seats is how a clamp becomes a mystery.\n\n**3. The paired arm is expressed as the EXISTING `members: MemberSpec[]` per-member override list, not a second member-command path.** `expandPairedMembers()` turns the two resolved role slices into one member-spec array; the handler assigns it to `args.members` and translates `count` (pairs) into a seat target before `resolveSavedFleetLaunchSpec` runs.\n\nThis is the reuse-first choice and it buys correctness, not just brevity: the paired arm inherits the member>fleet>system precedence fold, launch-context composition, the attestation records and the saved-launch-spec round trip unchanged, and there remains exactly ONE place a member command is built — so the two arms cannot drift. Everything downstream (capacity clamp, headcount governor, `MAX_MEMBERS`, deficit math) keeps treating `args.count` as a seat target and needs no paired-awareness at all.\n\nConsequence: `members` may not be combined with `type:'paired'` — the override list IS how the split is expressed, so a caller-supplied one would silently overwrite half of every pair. That combination is refused with a repair rather than merged.\n\nA test pins the reuse claim itself: every knob `expandPairedMembers` emits must be a real `MemberSpec` field, because `memberSpecSchema` is `.strict()` and an invented knob would otherwise surface as an opaque refusal at launch time, far from its cause.\nRelated: P-011, P-012\n\n### D-015 — D-015 — An su-tier implementer cannot be tool-denied by ANY existing rail; the exemption's own rationale is the seam\nDate: 2026-08-26\nCORRECTS D-004 (which assumed `--disallowedTools`-style launch denial works) and COMPLETES D-013 (which correctly rejected the client-side rail but prescribed a server-side role gate that is ALSO bypassed). Verified in the code that writes it, not inferred:\n\n1. `spawn-mcp.ts:297-298` — verbatim: \"Dispatch capability is unchanged — isSuperuser still bypasses role gates; only the advertised list narrows.\" A `--role` on an su-spawned member narrows the ADVERTISED tools/list only. `tools:invoke { name:'work_items:complete' }` still dispatches server-side.\n\n2. `capability-envelope/policy.ts:178` — `if (ctx.isSuperuser || ctx.isPowerUser) return { withinEnvelope: true, applied: false }` returns BEFORE role is read and BEFORE the protected-glob loop. So ROLE_ENVELOPES/`denyCapabilities` — the D-013 prescription — never evaluates for an su-tier member.\n\n3. The implementer MUST be su-tier: `spawn-mcp.ts:283-285` says resolveAgentIdentity-gated tools (\"plans:promote, coord:*\") require the isSuperuser identity, and \"a plain signed spawn's ctx has none\". The call-response contract (D-001/D-003) is built on `coord:send` evidence replies, so demoting the implementer to a signed spawn removes the very channel the design runs on.\n\n4. Even if (1)-(3) were solved, the envelope's grain is WRONG for D-004. It matches CAPABILITY globs; `toolName` is passed into `evaluateCapabilityEnvelope` but is only interpolated into reason strings, never matched. `work_items:complete` and `scheduler:get_next` both declare `capability:'work_items:write'` — shared by 43 tools including `work_items:checkpoint`, `comment`, `claim`, `create`. Denying that capability to block `complete` strands the implementer's own progress-recording. `loop:arm` declares `routines:write` (7 tools).\n\nRULING — the exemption's stated rationale is the seam, and it does not cover this case. `policy.ts:12-14` justifies the superuser exemption as: \"supervised human sessions keep native-tool ergonomics; the policy is the safety net precisely where there is no human.\" A directed implementer is precisely a session with NO human — it is su-tier only as a side-effect of needing coord identity. So the correct fix is NOT to punch a hole in the exemption, but to recognise it keys on the wrong predicate for this population.\n\nTherefore P-003 is implemented as a SELF-IMPOSED, LAUNCH-DECLARED SESSION CONFINEMENT that binds independently of isSuperuser:\n- It can only ever NARROW; it holds no widening path (mirrors the dynamic-tool-confinement invariant, which reuses the same canonical matcher).\n- It is TOOL-NAME grain (D-004 names tools), so it is expressed as a `denyTools` glob list beside the existing capability dimensions rather than as a new parallel system.\n- It is declared by the launcher at spawn and travels with the session, so it cannot be edited by the confined agent (an agent that can lift its own denial has no denial).\n\nSCOPE HONESTY — this touches the capability-envelope enforcement seat, which `dynamic-tool-confinement.ts:20-23` classifies as a TCB edit (D-007, tier:'human'). It is disclosed as such rather than slipped in: the change is narrowing-only and adds no grant/mint path, which is the property that makes it safe to land, and it is the reason this decision is recorded BEFORE the edit rather than after.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for D-002: this strengthens rather than replaces ledger-grounded verification. Structure covers what structure can express; the director's independent ledger check remains the backstop for everything it cannot.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-016 — D-016 — The confinement seat is verified; declaring the confinement at launch belongs to P-004, and P-003's live-verification clause resolves with it\nDate: 2026-08-26\nTwo things settled while implementing P-003, recorded so neither is re-derived.\n\n1. THE SEAT IS THE DISPATCH STACK, AND IT COVERS INDIRECT DISPATCH. Verified, not assumed:\n   - `tools/invoke.ts:8` states it outright — the target \"runs server-side through the same dispatcher a direct call uses, so it is gated\" — and the handler is a pure delegator to `ctx.dispatchTool` (`:173`).\n   - `dispatch-stack.ts:281` consults the `checkCapabilityEnvelope` port as a dispatch STEP and short-circuits to `capability_denied` at `:301`.\n   Therefore a deny returned from `checkCapabilityEnvelopeImpl` binds a direct call and a `tools:invoke` call alike. This was the one fact that could have sunk D-015's design, which is why it was checked in the code rather than reasoned about.\n\n   The session confinement is wired FIRST in that port impl, ahead of `evaluateCapabilityEnvelope`, precisely so it is not reached by the `isSuperuser || isPowerUser` early return that made the role envelope unusable here.\n\n2. WHERE P-003 ENDS AND P-004 BEGINS. P-003 delivers the RAIL: the pure decision, the resolver seam, and the seat wiring. It cannot deliver its own last clause — \"verify the denial is effective in a LIVE session, not just configured\" — because nothing declares a confinement yet, and declaring one is a launch-time act: the confinement names the coupled director and the scoped work item, both of which come into existence at pair launch. That is P-004 (pairing mechanics within the paired-type fleet).\n\n   So P-004 inherits two concrete obligations, not a vague handoff:\n   a. Install the host resolver at boot via `setSessionConfinementResolver`, reading server-side state keyed by the calling session's own identity. The resolver must NEVER read a confinement out of the request args — a confinement the caller supplies is one the caller can omit.\n   b. Have the paired launch persist `directedImplementerConfinement({ directorSid, workItemId })` for the implementer session, then satisfy P-003's live clause by observing a real `capability_denied` on `work_items:complete` from a running implementer — including once through `tools:invoke`, since that is the bypass this whole line of work exists to close.\n\n   Until (a) lands, the gate is INERT by construction: no resolver ⇒ null ⇒ every session unconfined. That is the intended shipping state, not an unfinished edge — it is what makes landing the seat wiring safe ahead of the launch path.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-017 — The confinement keys on the coord identity — and must REFUSE population-shaped ids\nDate: 2026-08-26\nDate: 2026-08-26\nSettles D-016(a)'s open question — which server-side key the resolver reads — and records a hazard a naive implementation ships silently.\n\n1. THE KEY IS `resolveAgentIdentity(ctx).ownerId`. It is transport-resolved, not caller-supplied: for a superuser session the route folds the `Mcp-Session-Id` header (else the install-script `?client=` machine id) into `ctx.uiClientId`; for a spawned agent it is the HMAC-verified `client=` param, and `identity.ts` REFUSES to attribute an unverified one (EI-318 — the public catch-all never sets `sigVerifiedSpawn`, so a loopback `curl ...?client=` cannot forge an identity). That is exactly the property D-016(a) demands. The same primitive already gates `coord:*` and file locks, so the confined session, its lock owner, and its coord sender are one id by construction.\n   Never key on `ctx.runId` / `ctx.spawnId` — `identity.ts`'s own header forbids it: both regenerate on every MCP call.\n\n2. A CONFINEMENT MUST NEVER BE KEYED ON A TRANSPORT-ONLY ID — this is the hazard. `resolveAgentIdentity` returns the shared constant `SUPERUSER_FALLBACK_CLIENT_ID` (`'su-loopback'`) for ANY superuser session that arrives without a per-session client id, and `mcp-call-<pid>` for one-shot `mcp-call.mjs` invocations. Those name a POPULATION, not a session. A confinement stored under one would bind every client-less su session on the box — the owner's own interactive session and the pair's own director included — and it would do so silently, because a deny looks identical whether it was aimed at you or inherited.\n   So the guard runs on BOTH sides: `declareSessionConfinement` REFUSES to write under such a key (the bad row never exists), and the resolver REFUSES to apply one (defence in depth if a row arrives by another path). `isTransportOnlyIdentity()` already exists for the mirror-image hazard — it stops a transport fallback from taking CREDIT for a completion; here it stops one from taking BLAME for a confinement. Same predicate, opposite direction.\n\n3. THE STORE IS ITS OWN `operator_state` TABLE, NOT `session_briefs.control_state`. Mirrors the ratified sibling `operator_capability_envelopes` (D-010): one JSONB row per workspace, a sync module cache refreshed on local write plus a 60s `managedSetInterval`, so the dispatch hot path stays zero-await. Explicitly NOT `session_briefs.control_state`: that document is rewritten wholesale by other writers (`mode:set`, orient), and a security rail living inside a doc someone else replaces is a clobber-shaped fail-open.\n\n4. THE COLD-CACHE WINDOW IS CLOSED BY ORDERING, NOT BY THE CACHE. Fail-open on a cache miss is FORCED, not chosen: unconfined is the default for every session in the fleet, so failing closed on a miss would deny every dispatch on the box. The window is therefore closed causally — the launch path persists the confinement (which refreshes the in-process cache synchronously) BEFORE it spawns the implementer, so the row exists before the confined process does. Cross-process operators converge on the 60s refresh.\n\n5. THE RESOLVER INSTALLS ITSELF ON IMPORT, and the seat imports the store. A separate boot-time install step is a hazard here because this gate's failure mode is SILENT: no resolver ⇒ null ⇒ every session unconfined, with nothing thrown and nothing logged. Binding installation to the module the dispatcher already imports removes the \"boot path forgot to call it\" class entirely. `hasSessionConfinementResolver()` remains for the assertion.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-018 — The director-directive stamp uses the recognized `[peer:…]` prefix with a qualifier — refining D-003\nDate: 2026-08-26\nD-003 specified the truthful stamp class as `[director:<sid> for WI-X]`. The shipped persona uses `[peer:<director-sid> · director for WI-NNN]`, and that form is correct — this refines D-003 rather than departing from it, and the divergence should not be \"fixed\" back.\n\nReason: the compaction machinery and every later re-summarizer recognize a CLOSED four-tag set — `[owner:…]` · `[self-imposed]` · `[peer:<sid>]` · `[inferred]`. A `[director:…]` tag invented for this pair carries more specificity at the cost of being understood by the one mechanism the tag exists to survive. Since D-003's whole purpose is preventing attribution rot THROUGH compaction, a tag that compaction does not recognize defeats its own goal.\n\nThe resolution keeps both properties: the recognized prefix does the machine-legible work (a director is a peer, and demonstrably not an owner), and D-003's specificity rides as a trailing qualifier where a human reader and a re-summarizer both retain it.\n\nPinned by `packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/directed-implementer-persona-tool-claims.test.ts`, whose extraction control asserts the tag forms are not mistaken for tool names.\nRelated: P-001, P-004\n\n### D-019 — D-004's \"structure, not prose\" binds NEGATIVE constraints only — positive obligations stay persona-borne\nDate: 2026-08-26\nP-004's compaction-recovery contract is persona prose, not a launch rail. That looks like a violation of D-004 (\"load-bearing implementer constraints are tool-denied at launch, never persona-only\") and is not one. Recording the boundary, because the apparent conflict will otherwise be re-opened.\n\nD-004 governs constraints that PREVENT an action. A deny list is expressively capable of exactly one sentence — \"you may not call X\" — so every negative constraint that matters belongs there, and the reasoning behind D-004 (prompt hierarchies fail under conflict; smarter models rationalize around prose) applies at full force.\n\nThe compaction-recovery contract is a POSITIVE obligation: check whether you already replied, then either finish and reply or send a status. There is no denial that expresses it. The only nearby structural move — denying `session:request-compaction` — is strictly worse: it would strand a long milestone at the context wall rather than let it recover, converting a recoverable event into a dead session.\n\nSo the boundary is expressive, not a matter of confidence: negative → deny list (D-004 governs); positive → persona, pinned by a doc-claims test where the prose has a mechanically checkable premise. The compaction section's premise (\"you have no wake source of your own\") is exactly such a premise — it is true only while `loop:arm` is denied, so it is pinned in `directed-implementer-persona-tool-claims.test.ts` rather than trusted. That pin is the substitute for structure, and it is what keeps this from being \"persona-only\" in the sense D-004 forbids.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-020 — Arm B's self-review gate is OPT-IN per item, never a global default — enabling it globally would destroy the experiment it belongs to\nDate: 2026-08-26\nThe arm B mechanism (`packages/operator-core/lib/work-item-self-review.ts`) must be selected by pilot arm assignment and be INERT otherwise. Recording this before the wiring exists, because \"gate is built, gate is off\" is exactly the state in which a later agent flips it on to be helpful.\n\nTwo independent reasons, either sufficient:\n\n1. **It would destroy the measurement.** Arm A is the solo BASELINE and arm B is solo + this gate. A globally-forced self-review makes A and B the same arm, and the pilot (D-007) can no longer say what the gate is worth. The plan's whole purpose is to find out whether the cheap structural check captures most of the pair's value; a default-on gate answers that question by making it unaskable.\n\n2. **It would break every in-flight completion in the fleet.** `work_items:complete` is on the hot path for every agent here. A new required field turns every close into a refusal until every caller is updated — the required-field-strand class the repo already guards for (`lint:required-field-strands`), landing on the one verb the fleet cannot route around.\n\nThis is NOT the dark-flag anti-pattern. That rule governs FINISHED features parked behind a flag nobody flips; this is an experimental arm whose entire point is being applied to one arm and not the other. The right shape is an item-level arm assignment the pilot sets, not a global feature flag and not a `KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS` entry.\n\nNote the asymmetry when it does gate: `not-claimed` / `uncorroborated` / `stale-review` refuse, but `rubberStampRisk` and `yieldedChange` are MEASUREMENTS and must never refuse. A zero-findings review is a legitimate outcome and a data point; refusing it would teach agents to invent findings, which is worse than the rubber-stamping it was meant to catch — the same reason D-002's fourth refusal condition warns against punishing an honest `notVerified`.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-021 — Arm B's ENFORCEMENT wiring lands with the assignment protocol, not before it — with the exact spec, so it is not re-derived\nDate: 2026-08-26\nP-005 delivers arm B's mechanism (`packages/operator-core/lib/work-item-self-review.ts`, 27 tests green). The enforcement wiring into `work_items:complete` deliberately lands with the assignment protocol instead, and this records why plus exactly how, so the next agent writes it rather than re-deciding it.\n\n#### Why not now\nThe gate reads `payload.pilotArm === 'B'` (`itemIsArmB`, default false per D-020) and NOTHING sets that marker yet — the assignment protocol is P-006's by the plan's own text. So wiring it today ships an unexercisable path into the verb every agent in the fleet depends on: it could not be tested end-to-end, only unit-tested against a marker no real item carries. The field, the gate, and the trigger should land and be proven together.\n\nThe concrete risk is named in the repo's own guidance: recording a `selfReview` requires extending `CompletionRecordSchema` — a SHARED record type, not a local one — and `completion.verification` is documented as strict. That is the `lint:required-field-strands` class, landing on `work_items:complete`, which no agent can route around.\n\n#### The exact wiring (read before writing)\n1. **Field.** Extend `CompletionRecordSchema` with `selfReview?: { lookedAt?: string; findings?: string[]; changedAsResult?: string[] }`, and add `'selfReview'` to `COMPLETION_FIELDS` in `agent-tools/work_items/completion-coerce.ts` so a flat completion is still recognised. Keep it OPTIONAL — the record must stay valid for arms A and C.\n2. **Gate placement.** In `completeOne` (`agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts`), beside the `verificationCoverageError` block (~line 2040-2080). Follow that block's shape exactly: compute the gap, build the message, and `return { ok:false, id, error, selfReviewError }` BEFORE any state write — EI-20962416980274656 records why a late rejection there produced a non-atomic half-write (a recorded completion plus an open item, needing a second call).\n3. **Ledger.** `selfReviewLedgerQuery({ workspaceId: ctx.workspaceId, coordOwnerId: resolveAgentIdentity(ctx).ownerId, goalRef: it.id, sinceMs: <the item's takenAt> })`, rows mapped through `toSelfReviewLedgerRow`, then `judgeSelfReview`. `completeOne` is async and `getOrgPg` is already imported, so both are in scope. Do NOT re-write that SQL inline — its two non-obvious predicates are load-bearing and documented at the function.\n4. **Refuse on** `not-claimed` / `uncorroborated` / `stale-review`. **Never refuse on** `rubberStampRisk` or `yieldedChange` — they are pilot MEASUREMENTS (D-020), and refusing a zero-findings review teaches agents to invent findings, which is worse than the rubber-stamping it targets.\n5. **Cost.** The ledger query runs only for arm-B items, so the hot path is untouched for every other close.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-022 — D-007's metric list is power-inverted: at ~7 items/arm NO binary metric can fire, so the primary metric must be a continuous graded score and the pilot is a screening study\nDate: 2026-08-26\nDate: 2026-08-26\nMeasured against this harness's own ledger before designing the pilot, because D-007 names its metrics in an order that turns out to be worst-first. All rates: `harness_shared.work_items`, harness papercusp, lane <> 'observation', terminal rows, 14 days, n=3918. Each measured with a passing `positiveControlSql`.\n\n#### The measured base rates\n| signal | rate | instrument |\n|---|---|---|\n| reopened | **0.74%** | `payload ? 'reopenHistory'` |\n| authority = 'proposed' | **0.74%** | `authority` column |\n| verification.coverage present | **0.0%** | `_completionEvidence->'verification'->'coverage'` |\n| no completion evidence at all | 7.7% | `payload->'_completionEvidence' IS NULL` |\n| verifiedHow ∈ {unit, integration} | 23.1% | ditto |\n| addedTests = true | 29.0% | ditto |\n| filesChanged non-empty | **44.5%** | ditto — the highest-variance signal available |\n\n⚠ Two instrument corrections, both of which would have produced a confident wrong design:\n- **`requeue_count` is NOT a reopen count.** It is written only by the stale-claim reaper (`work-items-stale-claims.ts:552`) when an agent dies holding an item. Reading it as \"the work was wrong and came back\" measured abandonment and reported 0.33%. The real signal is `payload.reopenHistory` (`work-items.ts:3668`), and it is 0.74%.\n- **`completion_ref` is NULL on 100% of rows.** Evidence lives at `payload->'_completionEvidence'` for `done` closes and `terminal_completion_ref` for `dropped` closes; no route writes both. A single-surface read reports the other route's closes as evidence-free.\n\n#### The power computation (α=.05, two-sided, n=7/arm)\n- **Reopen rate:** expected events per arm = 0.052. **P(the entire 21-item pilot observes zero reopens) = 85.6%.** The headline metric returns 0/7, 0/7, 0/7 five times in six and carries no information.\n- **Best-variance binary** (filesChanged, 44.5%, closest to the 50% max-variance point): Fisher's exact power is **7.9%** for a +30pt effect and **25%** for a +50pt effect. 80% power at +30pt needs **n≈50/arm (150 items)** — 7× the specified pilot.\n- **Continuous per-item score:** n=7/arm reaches 79% power at Cohen d=1.6, 53% at d=1.2, 25% at d=0.8.\n\n#### The ruling\n1. **The PRIMARY metric is a continuous per-item graded score** from the acceptance rubric — every item yields one, so 21 items give 21 observations rather than 21 coin flips at p=0.007. This is the only metric family that can carry a decision at the specified size.\n2. **Reopen rate, authority='proposed', and coverage-present are reported as RAW COUNTS, never as rates, and never as the basis of a verdict.** A rate computed on an expected 0.05 events is not an estimate. They stay in the record as safety tripwires: any reopen at all in the pilot cohort is worth reading individually.\n3. **`verification.coverage` is not a metric.** At 0.0% it has no variance to measure.\n4. **The pilot is pre-registered as a SCREENING study.** It can rule a large effect IN; it cannot rule a moderate effect OUT. The decision rule in P-008 must be phrased as a cost-adjusted effect-size threshold, and a null result must be recorded as \"no large effect detected at n=7/arm\", never as \"pairing does not help\". This is the specific misreading the numbers above make near-certain if left unstated — at 7.9% power the experiment fails to fire even when the effect is real and large.\n5. **Do not silently enlarge the pilot to chase significance.** 150 items is not affordable here and D-007's ~20 is the right cost. The fix is the continuous metric plus honest interval reporting, not more items.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-023 — The pilot protocol: mechanical assignment, a grader blind to arm, and cost summed across BOTH agents — each closes a specific way the result would otherwise be fake\nDate: 2026-08-26\nDate: 2026-08-26\nP-006 ships the pilot's instruments; this records the protocol P-007 must run them under. Each rule below exists because breaking it produces a result that LOOKS like evidence and is not — which is worse than no pilot, because it would be acted on.\n\n#### 1. Assignment is mechanical, seeded, and reproducible\nUse `assignCohort(candidates, seed)` (`packages/operator-core/lib/pilot-arm-assignment.ts`). Never hand-pick an arm.\n- **Why:** the natural instinct is to give the scary item the pair. That is maximally correlated with difficulty, so arm C would carry the hard items and lose on every metric no matter how much pairing helped.\n- **`tier` is declared BEFORE assignment and before any outcome is known.** The module refuses to infer it: nothing in the row is a trustworthy a-priori difficulty signal (`severity` is filed for triage urgency, not effort). Only `substantive` enters the pilot — D-007 already rules trivial work solo and high-risk work paired.\n- Assignment is **permuted-block within stratum**, so arms stay balanced at every block boundary. This is what makes an early-stopped pilot still analysable, and these are real work items competing with real work, so an early stop is the likely outcome, not the exceptional one.\n- Candidates are **sorted by id** before blocking, so argument order cannot shift arms — otherwise \"re-run until the split looks right\" is arm-shopping with extra steps.\n- An item already carrying `payload.pilotArm` is **never reassigned**. Record the seed; `verifyAssignments` re-derives the plan and catches a hand-edited arm, which is otherwise invisible because an edited `pilotArm` looks exactly like a real one.\n\n#### 2. The grader is BLIND to the arm\nStrip `payload.pilotArm` (and `pilotSeed`/`pilotStratum`/`pilotBlockIndex`) from everything the grader sees.\n- **Why:** the pilot's hypothesis is that arm C produces better work. An unblinded grader who can see which items had a director will find that hypothesis confirmed. This is the cheapest protection the design has and it is worthless applied loosely.\n- The grader must also **not be the implementer** of the item being graded, per the plan-completion independent-grading discipline.\n- Grade from ARTIFACTS — diff, tests, item record, ledger — never from the closing agent's narrative about its own work (D-002).\n\n#### 3. Cost sums EVERY participating agent\n`ArmObservation.agentCostsUsd` is an ARRAY, deliberately: arm C carries two entries (director + implementer), arms A and B carry one.\n- **Why:** token cost is recorded per agent session (`agent_usage_samples`, `agent_loop_sessions`), never per work item, so attribution is by (agent, claim window). A collector that sums one agent per item reports the pair at roughly half price and inverts the entire cost-benefit question the pilot exists to answer. There is deliberately no single-agent shape to fall into by accident.\n\n#### 4. Arm B's gate activates by the marker, and only there\nStamping `pilotArm:'B'` is what arms the `work_items:complete` self-review gate. Arms A and C leave it inert (D-020). The gate refuses only `not-claimed`/`uncorroborated`/`stale-review` and never on `rubberStampRisk`/`yieldedChange` — enforced in `selfReviewRefusal()` and unit-tested, not left as prose.\n\n#### 5. Report per D-022\nPrimary = the continuous mean score from rubric `directed-pair-pilot-item-quality`. Rare binaries are raw counts; `countRareEvent` withholds a rate below 5 events so a 0/7 cannot be rendered as \"0%\". `buildPilotReport` derives its interpretation from the ACHIEVED n, so an early-stopped pilot cannot inherit the planned power claim.\nRelated: P-006, P-007\nRelated: P-006, P-007\n\n### D-024 — Completion evidence is split across THREE surfaces and no single read sees it all — the grading rubric was pointing at the wrong one, and would have scored every item at the floor\nDate: 2026-08-26\nDate: 2026-08-26\nFound by testing the rubric authored minutes earlier against a known-positive control instead of trusting it. Recording because the map is repo-wide, and because the failure it produces is invisible: it yields a clean, plausible, uniformly-bad score rather than an error.\n\n#### The measured map\n| field | where it actually is |\n|---|---|\n| summary, coverage, testsRun, testResult, verifiedHow, addedTests, filesChanged, treeStamp | `payload->'_completionEvidence'` |\n| **deferred, whatLanded, coordNotes** | **NOT on the row and NOT returned by `work_items:get`** — they live in the rendered completion BROADCAST (coord:thread / coord:feed on the emit), and coordNotes is separately harvested into the observation lane as its own row |\n| evidence for `dropped` closes | `terminal_completion_ref` — and no route writes both surfaces |\n| `completion_ref` | **NULL on 100% of rows.** Never read it. |\n\nVerified on WI-41761, whose completion passed four `deferred` entries and six `whatLanded` entries minutes before: `jsonb_object_keys(payload->'_completionEvidence')` returns exactly the eight verification keys and none of the narrative ones; `terminal_completion_ref` and `completion_ref` are both NULL.\n\n#### Why this nearly corrupted the pilot\nThe `residue-disclosed` criterion's method instructed the grader to \"read the completion's deferred, coordNotes, and verification.coverage fields\" — at `_completionEvidence`, where two of the three do not exist and the third (`coverage`) is present on ~0.0% of historical closes. A grader following that instruction literally would have found zero disclosed residue on **every** item and scored **every** item at the floor.\n\nThat is the worst possible failure for this rubric specifically: D-022 moved the pilot's primary metric to a continuous score precisely to escape a zero-variance measurement, and a criterion that scores identically everywhere reintroduces exactly that failure inside the new instrument. It would not have looked like a bug. It would have looked like a finding about how badly agents disclose residue.\n\n#### What changed\nThe rubric (`directed-pair-pilot-item-quality`) now carries the surface map in its description, a four-surface read in `residue-disclosed`'s method, an explicit calibration caveat that coverage-absence alone must not drive the score, an anti-drift marker telling the grader that scoring every item at the floor is itself evidence the read was wrong, and a replication drill that runs the read against a KNOWN-POSITIVE control first (WI-41761) and treats a miss there as invalidating any absence claim.\n\nIt also gained a general calibration step: grade 2–3 non-pilot closed items first and check both that scores VARY and that graders agree within a point. An instrument that cannot discriminate must be fixed before it is used, not discovered afterwards in the results.\n\n#### The transferable rule\nAn absence measured through one surface is a claim about the surface until a known-positive control proves the read works. This is the third instrument error on this plan — after `requeue_count` (the stale-claim reaper's counter, not a reopen) and `completion_ref` (NULL everywhere) — and all three produced confident, plausible, wrong numbers rather than errors.\nRelated: P-006, P-007\nRelated: P-006, P-007\n\n### D-025 — Arm B's corroboration ledger is blind to native review tools — the gate must not ship to real items until that is fixed\nDate: 2026-08-26\nDate: 2026-08-26\n\nEstablished while running WI-41764's end-to-end verification of the arm-B self-review gate. This governs P-007 (running the pilot) and any lane that would stamp a real item to arm B.\n\nTHE FINDING. `REVIEW_TOOLS` in work-item-self-review.ts lists only MCP names (capability:git, capability:read, code:review, lsp:query), and `judgeSelfReview` corroborates against harness_shared.tool_invocations, which records MCP tools ONLY. A review performed with native Read/Bash/Grep is therefore invisible to the gate, yields verdict `uncorroborated`, and REFUSES the close.\n\nEVIDENCE. This session performed a genuine review of complete.ts and work-item-self-review.ts via native Read + git diff/show/grep. tool_invocations across 18 distinct tools and ~114 calls: zero REVIEW_TOOLS rows. session_turn_parts over the same window: Read 3, Bash 7. Both with passing positive controls. An honest reviewer is refused.\n\nWHY IT IS A PILOT-KILLER, NOT JUST A BUG. Arm B exists to measure what a forced self-review step is worth. If corroboration keys on tool ROUTING rather than on reviewing, arm B measures which tools an agent habitually uses. capability:read shows 2060 calls across 98 distinct agents in 24h while native tools are structurally absent, so the pilot population splits by client/tool habit — a confound sitting directly on the experiment's central variable, and invisible in the results.\n\nTHE RULING. No item may be stamped to pilot arm B until BOTH hold: (1) the corroboration source counts native review — read session_turn_parts (workspace_id='default', owner = coord ownerId) alongside tool_invocations, or add a non-refusing verdict for 'no ledger visibility on this client'; and (2) the gate has been re-verified live against a DEPLOYED operator by repeating the WI-41768 fixture probe. Today the gate is also inert in production (deployed sha predates the gate commit by ~2 days) — see fact `arm-b-gate-inert-until-deployed`.\n\nThis refines D-021 rather than departing from it: D-021 deferred the wiring, and the wiring is correct as written. What is wrong is the ledger the wiring consults.\n\nDIRECTION NOTE. Prefer widening the corroboration source over relaxing the gate. Relaxing makes arm B weaker than designed; widening makes it measure the thing it was built to measure. The module's own comment already sets the tie-break: a false refusal on the hot path is far worse than a permissive pass.\n\n### D-026 — Arm-B corroboration reads both ledgers, widens EDITS symmetrically, excludes shell commands, and treats a blind ledger as non-refusing\nDate: 2026-08-26\nImplements D-025's preferred direction (a) for EI-21481919801123128. Four rulings, three of which go beyond the original fix sketch and bind any later work on this gate.\n\n**1. Two ledgers, normalized across three names.** `selfReviewLedgerQuery` now UNIONs `harness_shared.tool_invocations` with `harness_shared.session_turn_parts`. The same call wears three names — `capability:read` (invocations), `mcp__papercusp-su__capability_read` (turn-parts, client-mangled), and `Read` (native) — so `normalizeToolName` strips the `mcp__<server>__` segment before matching. The prior `:`→`_` fold alone matched none of the mangled forms; a widened tool list without this would have looked correct and still corroborated nothing.\n\n**2. EDIT_TOOLS was widened symmetrically, and this is load-bearing.** The sketch in EI-21481919801123128 named only the REVIEW side. Widening reviews alone would have been worse than the bug: a native-editing agent has no recorded edits, so `lastEditAtMs` returns undefined, the stale-review check can never fire, and arm B would corroborate reviews of states that were subsequently rewritten — for exactly the agents newly able to pass. `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit`/`NotebookEdit` are therefore in EDIT_TOOLS.\n\n**3. `Bash` is in NEITHER list, deliberately.** It is the highest-volume native tool (measured 124 calls to 19 `Read`s in one session) and it is arbitrary — `git diff` is a review, `npm test` is not, `ls` is neither. Admitting it to REVIEW_TOOLS would manufacture evidence, which the module docstring calls worse than having no gate. Admitting it to EDIT_TOOLS is the mirror defect: any command after a review would read as a later mutation and turn honest closes into `stale-review`. Discriminating by parsing the command text out of the part payload was considered and REJECTED — a shell-command regex on the completion hot path fails in both directions. The refusal message names the qualifying tools so a Bash-only reviewer can comply in one call.\n\n**4. New non-refusing verdict `unobservable`, distinct from `uncorroborated`.** An EMPTY ledger means the instrument is blind, not that the agent did nothing — and this is self-falsifying rather than a courtesy: reaching `work_items:complete` requires having made at least one call in the window, so zero rows is POSITIVE evidence of blindness. Refusing on it would let an ingestion outage convert arm B into a wall on the one verb no agent can route around. This is NOT a retreat to D-025's direction (b): (b) proposed relaxing INSTEAD of widening, which would leave arm B weaker than designed. With (1) landed, this floor fires only when both ledgers see nothing at all — a case where refusing is provably uninformative. `uncorroborated` (visible ledger, no read of the code) still refuses.\n\n**Performance is part of the ruling, not a footnote.** `session_turn_parts` is 2.37M rows with no index serving `(owner, ts)`; the gate's own predicate measured a Parallel Seq Scan, 5 workers, 222,576 buffers, 444ms. Migration **968** adds a partial index on `(owner, ts DESC) WHERE part_kind = 'tool_use'` — measured after: Index Scan, 49 buffers, 0.271ms. The `part_kind = 'tool_use'` literal in the query is what lets the planner use that partial index; do not relax it to an `IN (...)`. `workspace_id` is deliberately not a leading column — it is `'default'` on 2,373,429 of 2,373,429 rows, so it carries no selectivity.\n\n**Scoping asymmetry, accepted knowingly.** The turn-parts leg has no `goal_ref` column, so it is scoped by owner + window only — strictly more permissive than the invocations leg, in the same direction and for the same stated reason as the existing `goal_ref IS NULL` admission. Likewise a turn-parts row carries no `status`, so a native call that errored still counts as a review.\n\n### D-027 — P-007 is not deploy-only — the production collector/materializer remains deploy-independent work\nDate: 2026-08-26\nAudit on 2026-08-26 retracted plan Now revision 60's claim that P-007 was blocked only on deployment. WI-41761's committed P-006 completion evidence explicitly lists: 'The DB collector feeding pilot-metrics is deferred to P-007.' A production import search found no runtime caller of pilot-metrics.ts, and catalog search found no operational directed-pair pilot collector/assignment tool. Therefore the deploy gates only the live arm-B fixture probe and any real B-arm execution; it does not gate building and verifying the collector/materialization surface. Implement that runtime now, reuse existing work-item/scorecard/usage ledgers, and keep the existing safety rail: do not stamp a real item pilotArm='B' until WI-41764 passes against the deployed operator.\nRelated: P-006, P-007\n\n### D-028 — The P-007 runtime reuses canonical ledgers and fail-closes arm B on a tested=deployed proof\nDate: 2026-08-26\nWI-42259 closes D-027's deploy-independent runtime gap with two purpose-built tools over the existing stores — no parallel experiment database. `pilot:assign` is read-only unless confirm:true; it reuses assignCohort, requires explicit participant session + claim-window bindings (A/B: one solo; C: director + implementer), and verifies the persisted seed/stratum/block assignment. Any cohort containing a new B assignment is refused unless the terminal probe item records `payload.out.pilotArmBGateProbe = { status:'passed', testedSha, deployedSha, judgementPersisted:true }` with testedSha === deployedSha. A failed multi-item write removes every pilot key it added and reports incomplete rollback loudly. `pilot:collect` reuses work_items, scorecards and agent_usage_samples: it requires terminal items, complete post-assignment scorecards from a non-participant grader, fully priced per-session claim windows (two costs for C), and seed re-verification; missing evidence is a typed gap, never zero cost or a floor score. The report is built by the already-settled D-022 pilot-metrics module, so rare events remain raw counts and achieved-n controls the screening interpretation.\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n\n### D-029 — The seeded preview is an audit artifact, not permission to materialize stale candidates\nDate: 2026-08-27\nThe frozen 21-item, three-stratum cohort was previewed through staging `materializePilotCohort` with seed `directed-pair-work-items-2026-08-25:p007:preview-2026-08-27:v1` and `confirm:false`. This resolves D-029 attrition without hand substitution or arm shopping while preserving every still-eligible predeclared substantive v1 row.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-031 — Cohort v2 exact roster is frozen before arm assignment\nDate: 2026-08-27\nApplying D-030 to the frozen canonical windows produced this exact 21-row v2 roster, all re-read open + unassigned + unstamped immediately before this decision.
