Any arm-B data collected before this fix is deployed carries that confound and must not be read as a behavioural result.\n\nALSO RULED (defect 1, same item): a demonstrably stale native leg now yields `ledger-behind` rather than `uncorroborated`. `ledger-behind` still REFUSES — this is not a loosening. It swaps a false finding (\"the claim rests on prose alone\") and harmful advice (\"re-read the code\") for a correct transient one that names the real-time escape hatch. Do NOT \"improve\" this by ACCEPTING on lag: leg 2 always lags ~2min and prompt closes are the norm, so accepting would disable the gate for arm B entirely. The `NATIVE_LEDGER_LAG_CEILING_MS` bound is load-bearing for the opposite reason — a pure-MCP client emits no turn-parts ever, and without the ceiling it could hold the gate open indefinitely.\n\nSTATUS: implemented and unit-verified (92/92 in `work-item-self-review.test.ts` + `work-item-self-review-gate.test.ts`, scoped typecheck clean). NOT yet deployed — git-sync frozen (WI-144314) and the green gate red (WI-40086), both owned elsewhere. The pilot must not be read as measuring arm-B behaviour until this is live on :3070.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-044 — P-007 arm-B correctness prerequisites are satisfied; authoritative green-pin parity is the sole remaining gate\nDate: 2026-08-27\nDate: 2026-08-27\n\nD-042's arm-B correctness prerequisites are now satisfied. WI-249011 is done with completionAuthority=committed at git-sync commit fabd394409c936c39c048cdcf71dc61a55bd0bb2; both proof consumers accept canonical successful terminal state + payload.out and reject discard/nonterminal/top-level shapes, with 28/28 focused unit+PG tests and scoped typecheck green. Canonical WI-134439 is done with committed authority after live :3070 verification of both its ingest-lag and cross-item goal_ref defects. WI-139197 was already done. WI-41764 is terminal done and verify-reads payload.out.pilotArmBGateProbe={status:'passed',testedSha:'47226a9a6f934a368ba27edec5da08d461151bd8',deployedSha:same,judgementPersisted:true}; the patched production reader accepts that exact receipt. No live fixture was repeated.\n\nThe remaining D-037 predicate is not yet satisfied. A current path-scoped pipeline read says deployed SHA 47226a9a is executing and serving.startedSinceCodeChange=true, but the writer classifies deployOrigin='ahead-of-gate': the deployed SHA carries commits the last green pin does not. Therefore testedSha===deployedSha is true but testedSha===current authoritative green pin is not established. The green lane is held live by su-f0b8993d on WI-212675; per the single-fixer rule this lane sent the completed-prerequisite evidence once (coord-send-88840d9f1a4709e27dcdadd1e9041b7fad1491f8a3fbafe2d3257fcaeb381342) and will not enter or reread that gate lane.\n\nRULING: P-007 remains stored blocked and no pilot stamp / cohort materialization / pilot:assign confirm:true occurs until the held gate lane publishes a fresh authoritative green pin equal to WI-41764's tested/deployed SHA. On that exact transition, clear P-007's sticky block and execute the frozen D-032/D-036 protocol without reroll or fixture repetition. P-008 and P-009 remain transitively blocked on P-007.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"llm-agent-evaluation-validity-reliability-follow-on-2026-08-25","title":"Deferred follow-on: LLM/agent evaluation validity, reliability, production proof, and rollout","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-25","owner":"aviynw2@gmail.com","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Deferred follow-on: LLM/agent evaluation validity, reliability, production proof, and rollout\nslug: llm-agent-evaluation-validity-reliability-follow-on-2026-08-25\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-25\nupdated: 2026-08-28\nowner: aviynw2@gmail.com\n---\n\n# Deferred follow-on: LLM/agent evaluation validity, reliability, production proof, and rollout\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** PLACEMENT BLOCKED — P-001 is blocked because the predecessor plan is ready, not shipped, and its declared output values are absent. The start oracle requires compatibilityReportRef, validationContractVersion, evaluationTrialSchemaVersion, trajectoryContractVersion, and verificationEvidenceRef; none are currently published. The follow-on remains draft because its deferral attribution is unverified (WI-41690 / D-015), and the required owner/product decision has been typed on WI-41690 as needs-human. No fleet was created; do not invent inputs or retry the same launch.\n\n**Next:** After the product owner answers WI-41690 and the predecessor publishes all five declared outputs, re-read both plans, run the activation audit, then start P-001 via an independently led plan fleet.\n\n## Goal\n\nBuild empirically valid measurement, live reliability, production feedback, impartial external proof, reporting, and staged enforcement on top of the predecessor plan's fail-closed validation contracts and canonical evaluation evidence.\n\nThe finished follow-on must establish calibrated graders, uncertainty-aware comparisons, real fault and supervision canaries, multidimensional reliability and security, a privacy-safe production feedback loop, reproducible multi-seed external pilots, canonical reporting, and independently accepted enforcement.\n\n## Required predecessor outputs\n\nThis plan consumes, rather than duplicates:\n\n- The validated capability map and compatibility constraints.\n- The fail-closed inline validation assertion contract and transactional promotion behavior.\n- The versioned canonical `EvaluationTrial`/`EvidenceEnvelope` contract.\n- Full replayable trajectory and artifact evidence with compact-view and portable-export adapters.\n\nThe authoritative predecessor is `llm-agent-evaluation-measurement-integrity-2026-08-25`.\n\n## Existing surfaces to extend\n\n- Shared statistical inference in `@papercusp/bench-metrics`.\n- Typed rubrics, scorecards, evidence freshness, lineage, and release profiles.\n- Whole-Pot evaluation in `packages/operator-core/lib/pot-eval` and `@papercusp/eval-battery`.\n- External benchmarks, official graders, reproducibility cards, the Evaluation UI, and the gym/report firewall.\n- Existing trace and observation surfaces for privacy-aware production evaluation.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Shared statistical inference, reliability metrics, and paired causal comparisons.\n- Domain-specific judge meta-evaluation and calibration.\n- Live perturbation and supervision activation, broader internal corpora, and agent-security suites.\n- Privacy-aware production trace sampling and regression-case promotion.\n- Multi-seed external pilots, canonical reporting, independent acceptance, and staged enforcement.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- Reimplementing or weakening the predecessor's Phase 1 contracts.\n- Activating this plan before the predecessor is shipped and its outputs are current.\n- Replacing Papercusp's plan, rubric, scorecard, release-profile, or benchmark authority with a vendor platform.\n- Building a second evaluation database, dashboard, scheduler, or orchestration system.\n- Making an LLM judge the primary correctness oracle where deterministic outcomes exist.\n- Folding capability, reliability, safety, cost, and security into one opaque scalar.\n- Publishing performance claims before valid pilots complete.\n- Sending sensitive production content externally without a redaction and retention contract.\n\n## Phase 1 — Measurement validity and live reliability\n\n- **P-001** `blocked` Verify the predecessor plan is shipped; resolve its declared outputs; replay its assertion, canonical-envelope, and trajectory recurrence guards on current HEAD; record the accepted contract versions and compatibility constraints used by this follow-on. importance: urgent risk: moderate\n- **P-002** `todo` Consolidate statistical inference on `@papercusp/bench-metrics`: use task×seed pairing where possible; report pass@1, pass@k, pass^k/reliability, effect sizes, confidence intervals, paired bootstrap or McNemar results, coverage/infra denominators, and power-derived minimum sample sizes. Remove fixed-delta verdicts that can declare wins inside noise. blocked-by: P-001 → D-003, D-004 importance: urgent risk: moderate\n- **P-003** `todo` Build a judge meta-evaluation and calibration lane using a held-out, stratified expert-labelled corpus; measure agreement and uncertainty, false-positive/false-negative rates, rating indeterminacy, order/position/length/self-family bias, prompt and model sensitivity, adversarial robustness, and inter-rater disagreement. Pre-register domain-specific thresholds; keep any judge advisory until its current version passes. blocked-by: P-002 → D-002, D-003 importance: urgent risk: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Activate and verify the existing whole-Pot live rig: bind crash-recovery, requirements-shift, and multi-swarm injectors plus competent-off-brief and non-converging-churn supervision collectors; invalidate unapplied perturbations or collectors; expand the small seed set with versioned compositional stateful tasks and constrained user simulations; run positive-control canaries; and capture cost, token, coordination, collision, and lock metrics. blocked-by: P-002 → D-005, D-007 importance: urgent risk: high authority: owner\n- **P-005** `todo` Add a multidimensional reliability profile—capability, consistency, robustness, predictability, and safety—using repeated trials, semantic prompt paraphrases, tool/API/auth faults, schema and response-format changes, state drift, calibrated confidence/discrimination, policy compliance, and bounded error-severity measures. Keep every dimension visible. blocked-by: P-002 → D-003, D-004 importance: high risk: high\n- **P-006** `todo` Add executable adversarial-security adapters and curated corpora for prompt injection, tool poisoning, memory/context poisoning, privilege escalation, unauthorized action, exfiltration, jailbreaks, evaluation awareness, and reward hacking. Reuse AgentDojo and Promptfoo for execution; use Petri/Bloom-style generation only for independently reviewed candidate cases. blocked-by: P-001 → D-004, D-008 importance: high risk: high\n\n## Phase 2 — Production feedback and impartial proof\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Build the privacy-aware production evaluation flywheel on existing trace/observation surfaces: redact before persistence/export, sample traces, run code/model/human evaluators, route ambiguity and high cost, link user feedback, cluster failures, promote confirmed incidents into versioned offline regressions, and monitor freshness, saturation, drift, and the monitors themselves. blocked-by: P-003, P-005 → D-006, D-009 importance: high risk: critical authority: owner\n- **P-008** `todo` Run and independently audit impartial benchmark pilots: official third-party tasks and graders, matched model/task/environment/budget arms, reference reproduction, contamination/freshness checks, at least three seeds unless power analysis requires more, per-instance and infra accounting, confidence intervals, cost/Pareto reporting, immutable preregistration, and third-party re-grade export. blocked-by: P-004, P-005 → D-003, D-007 importance: urgent risk: high authority: owner\n- **P-009** `todo` Update the existing Evaluation UI and reports to read canonical evidence only and present capability, reliability, security, cost, and production signals separately; show uncertainty, coverage, invalid/no-op trials, judge calibration, caveats, provenance, and replay/export links. Refuse valid-looking deltas when comparison invariants fail. blocked-by: P-006, P-007, P-008 → D-004, D-007 importance: high risk: moderate\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification, enforcement, and closure\n\n- **P-010** `todo` Build and exercise the pre-enforcement verification package: compatibility and shadow recording; bounded canaries with positive controls; unit/property/mutation, PG, replay, and affected-suite tests; judge holdouts; production-redaction proof; external reference reproduction; schema compatibility; migration/rollback drills; operator runbooks; code-truth audit; acceptance-rubric vetting; and independent grading. Record an explicit accept/reject verdict before enforcement. blocked-by: P-009 → D-002, D-006, D-007 importance: urgent risk: critical authority: owner\n- **P-011** `todo` Only after acceptance, execute staged enforcement and closure: enable contract/statistical requirements by default; promote only calibrated judges; retain spend/privacy controls; broaden corpora and sampling while monitors remain green; retire legacy/fail-open paths and temporary flags after rollback proof; rerun the release verdict; and verify shipment evidence. blocked-by: P-010 → D-002, D-006, D-007 importance: urgent risk: high authority: owner\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. The predecessor output gate resolves current, replay-verified contract and evidence versions; stale or missing predecessor evidence blocks activation.\n2. All comparisons expose uncertainty, denominators, infra failures, and paired evidence; fixed thresholds alone cannot establish improvement.\n3. Every gating judge has a version-bound, independently labelled meta-eval with preregistered thresholds and confidence bounds; drifted judges remain advisory and surface `unknown`.\n4. Requested perturbations and supervision collectors record positive application evidence; unbound/no-op requests invalidate the trial.\n5. Reliability separately exposes consistency, robustness, predictability, safety, capability, cost, and severity; a good average cannot erase a critical failure.\n6. The security suite demonstrates attacks caught and healthy controls preserved, with uncertainty and reproducible cases.\n7. Production evaluation proves redaction before durable capture/export and promotes confirmed failures without leaking protected content.\n8. A full Pot canary and an impartial external comparison complete end to end with valid multi-seed evidence, reference reproduction, official grading, and replay instructions.\n9. Reports consume canonical evidence, refuse invalid comparisons, and keep evaluation dimensions separate.\n10. Focused, integration, mutation, affected-suite, live-canary, code-truth, and independently graded acceptance checks pass before enforcement or shipment.\n\n## Verification strategy\n\n- Replay the predecessor's current contract and evidence guards before follow-on work starts.\n- Unit/property tests for statistics, judge contracts, perturbation dispatch, privacy redaction, and report refusal.\n- Mutation probes proving new guards go red when removed.\n- PG and replay integrations for trial storage, score linkage, migrations, retries, and partial failure.\n- Judge meta-evals on frozen development and untouched holdout splits.\n- Bounded live canaries for every perturbation, supervision collector, scenario family, and production telemetry path.\n- External reference-arm reproduction and multi-seed comparisons under official graders.\n- `npm run test:affected`, relevant typechecks/lints, and a fresh release-gate verdict before enforcement.\n\n## Rollout\n\n1. **Predecessor gate:** resolve and replay the shipped Phase 1 outputs.\n2. **Shadow:** record trials and new statistics/calibration/reliability without ship impact.\n3. **Canary:** run perturbations, supervision, security, and privacy-filtered production sampling in bounded scopes.\n4. **Accept:** complete tests, drills, reference reproduction, rubric vetting, and independent grading.\n5. **Enforce:** enable only accepted, calibrated requirements by default.\n6. **Broaden:** expand corpora and sampling while freshness, cost, privacy, and false-positive monitors remain green.\n7. **Retire:** remove fail-open paths and temporary flags after compatibility, rollback, verdict, and shipment proof.\n\n## Risks and mitigations\n\n- **Stale predecessor contracts:** bind exact output versions and replay their guards before activation.\n- **Live-eval spend/runtime:** capacity preflight, per-run budgets, bounded concurrency, resumable trials, and early invalid-evidence aborts.\n- **Sensitive traces:** redact before write/export, minimize capture, restrict access, set retention, and disable external export until verified.\n- **Judge circularity/bias:** expert labels, heterogeneous holdouts, versioned calibration, bias perturbations, and deterministic floors.\n- **Contamination/saturation:** fresh/private holdouts, firewall, preregistration, freshness metadata, transcript review, and suite retirement.\n- **Metric gaming:** separate dimensions, paired failure metrics, mutation tests, official graders, and no report-on optimization.\n- **Migration breakage:** additive schemas, compatibility readers, idempotent backfill, shadow comparison, and rollback rehearsal.\n\n## Review questions preserved for resumption\n\n1. Production trace retention and raw-content policy.\n2. Domain-specific judge promotion thresholds and deterministic precedence.\n3. External-tool adapter boundaries.\n4. Internal-live-rig versus external-pilot sequencing.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — This plan is a deferred consumer of the Phase 1 predecessor\nDate: 2026-08-25\nThe predecessor owns contract integrity, canonical trial identity, and full-trajectory evidence. This follow-on consumes versioned outputs and does not duplicate that work.\n\n### D-002 — Deterministic outcome truth outranks model judgment\nDate: 2026-08-25\nExecutable tests, environment state, policy checks, artifact inspection, and independent human evidence gate where available. An LLM judge remains advisory until its exact version passes a domain-specific meta-eval and can never soften a deterministic failure.\n\n### D-003 — Report uncertainty and exploit pairing\nDate: 2026-08-25\nComparisons expose distributions and confidence, use matched task/scenario×seed pairs where possible, and distinguish capability from reliability. A point delta without uncertainty is descriptive only.\n\n### D-004 — Keep evaluation dimensions separate\nDate: 2026-08-25\nCapability, regression, consistency, robustness, predictability, safety/security, cost, and production quality stay separately visible. Composite summaries cannot hide a mandatory failure.\n\n### D-005 — An unapplied perturbation is invalid evidence\nDate: 2026-08-25\nA requested fault, environment change, or supervision collector must return verifiable application evidence. Missing bindings, no-ops, or ambiguity invalidate the trial.\n\n### D-006 — Privacy and spend are load-bearing constraints\nDate: 2026-08-25\nProduction capture is minimized and redacted before persistence/export. Live evaluation stays budgeted and resumable. Default-off sampling requires a registered privacy reason and graduation criteria.\n\n### D-007 — Separate built, validated, and proven states\nDate: 2026-08-25\nReports distinguish designed/built, bound, canary-validated, and production-proven evidence. No public claim precedes a valid pilot and reference reproduction.\n\n### D-008 — External tools are specialist adapters, not the control plane\nDate: 2026-08-25\nInspect supplies execution/logging; OpenTelemetry/OpenInference supplies telemetry interchange; Promptfoo/AgentDojo supplies adversarial execution; Petri/Bloom supplies candidate generation. Papercusp owns ratification, lineage, gating, and conclusions.\n\n### D-009 — Production failures become versioned regression evidence\nDate: 2026-08-25\nOnly privacy-safe, confirmed incidents are promoted; provenance, retention, and remediation state remain attached so production feedback cannot become an ungoverned data lake.\n\n## Research basis\n\n- Anthropic, “Demystifying evals for AI agents” (2026).\n- Harness-Bench (2026).\n- “Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability” and “Consistency as a Testable Property” (2026).\n- NeurIPS 2025 work on validating LLM judges under rating indeterminacy.\n- τ²-bench for compositional stateful tasks and constrained user simulation.\n- AgentDojo, Promptfoo, Inspect AI, OpenTelemetry GenAI/OpenInference, Petri, Bloom, and OpenAI production-eval guidance.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"memory-write-latency-2026-07-26-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: memory:remember write latency — cause attributed, cost bounded, class guarded","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-25","owner":"su-592946c2-a2c0-4291-8bbe-509173eee30c","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: memory:remember write latency — cause attributed, cost bounded, class guarded\nslug: memory-write-latency-2026-07-26-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-25\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-592946c2-a2c0-4291-8bbe-509173eee30c\n---\n\n# Acceptance: memory:remember write latency — cause attributed, cost bounded, class guarded\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. The plan's Goal is narrow and testable: a plan whose implementation and audit are COMPLETE must never be stranded un-shipped because an agent died — specifically the CREATOR, since grader recovery is pull-triggered by the creator retrying the ship. These criteria are outcomes (what must be TRUE), tracing to the Goal and requirements R1-R8, and to D-001's finding that the source conversation establishes exactly ONE actionable gap (grader FOLLOW-THROUGH), with vetting-consult expiry and grader SELECTION explicitly fenced as non-goals. Grade the OUTCOMES; do not credit a criterion merely because code exists for it.\n\nVETTING RECORD (2026-08-26). The consult router returned no_qualified_responder with reason embed_unavailable — the embedder could not measure similarity under host load, so this is cannot-measure, NOT measured-nothing, and no peer declined. Rather than rubber-stamp the resulting waiver I vetted my own three questions against the source.\n(A) COVERAGE GAP — I suspected a plan could be re-dispatched forever and never escalate, if the escalation clock reset on each dispatch. It cannot: stuckSinceMs is documented as when the plan first became eligible to be graded (NOT when the sweep first saw it), stuckForMs = nowMs - stuckSinceMs, and the escalation branch is evaluated BEFORE the redispatch-cooling guard. acceptance-grading-sweep.test.ts:194 pins exactly this ('escalation takes precedence over another re-dispatch'). No new criterion was needed; criterion 3's method now names this as its sharpest falsifier.\n(B) GRADEABILITY OF AN ABSENCE — accepted as a real weakness. Criterion 4 was stated as an absence, and absences are what graders most often rubber-stamp because nothing shows up to look at. Its method was rewritten from inspection into a four-part reachability check whose first part is type-level and cannot be waved through.\n(C) OVER-SPECIFICATION — criteria 2 and 3 were examined for merger and deliberately KEPT SEPARATE: they rest on different guards and fail differently. Criterion 2 is the grader-live guard (no duplicate grader while one is working); criterion 3 is the escalationExists guard plus minting idempotence (exactly one owner once hope of self-recovery is gone). Merging them would let a passing half mask a failing half.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data).
