Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"agent-in-flight-call-visibility-2026-08-26","title":"Agent in-flight call visibility — tell an idle member from one busy in a long call","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-26","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Agent in-flight call visibility — tell an idle member from one busy in a long call\nslug: agent-in-flight-call-visibility-2026-08-26\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-26\nupdated: 2026-08-26\n---\n## Goal\n\nA fleet leader must be able to answer one question about a member: **is it executing right now, or is it idle?** Today no instrument answers it, and the available signals actively mislead.\n\n**Originating incident (2026-08-26 ~20:26Z, fleet standalone-drain, EI-21548894457555139).** As leader I needed exactly this fact about member su-06d4c7f1. My first two conclusions were both wrong, in opposite directions. Each instrument answers a *different* question:\n\n- `coord:presence.sessionState` -> `parked`. That is the normal state BETWEEN turns, so it cannot separate idle from busy-in-a-long-call.\n- `loop:status.lastRealTurnAt` -> a turn happened minutes ago. \"A turn happened\" is not \"it picked up the work\".\n- `harness_shared.tool_invocations` -> written only when a call SETTLES. A member 20 minutes into one long call and a member doing nothing produce the SAME observable: no recent row.\n\nThe root cause is structural: **the ledger records completion, and nothing records commencement.** So `fleet:leader-brief` reported `dormant:true` and a `laneless-idle` bench suggestion for a member that was working hard.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation complete and VERIFIED; code-truth audit recorded (plans:audit auditSeq 1, auditedSha 881f2269, 12 citations, 4/4 verified).\n\nThe test:affected run for P-001's radius FINISHED. 11 red files, NONE attributable to this plan. Ten were already failing before this plan's first edit (~20:50Z), proven against the test_runs ledger (first-fail 2026-08-25T23:55Z..2026-08-26T20:02Z). The eleventh, apps/operator/lib/verify-tauri-headless-bind-retry.test.ts, was a genuine NEW red from a peer's 19:37Z change to scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh (commit 4581a3948d): it added a $NATIVE_TERMINAL reference inside write_and_launch_tauri() without adding it to the test probe's stand-in block, killing it under `set -u`. Repaired, and the diagnostic now names its own repair with a falsifiability control pinned against live bash. 16/16 green.\n\nRubric `acceptance-agent-in-flight-call-visibility-2026-08-26` is ACTIVE: 6 outcome criteria under plan-class-feature-ship, 4 bound to structured tests checks.\n\nBLOCKED at vetting — consult:get_feedback returns no_qualified_responder / reason `embed_unavailable` (twice). Cannot-measure, NOT measured-nothing; not licence to attest an unvetted rubric.\n\n⚠ RETRACTION (supersedes revision 10). Revision 10 blamed \"the host embedder over its 1200ms budget under load ~276\". WRONG, and unmeasured when I wrote it. Direct probe: the embed sidecar at :3384 is HEALTHY — POST /embed returns 200 with a valid 768-dim vector in 1.5-5.8ms, and papercup-dev-api has PAPERCUSP_EMBED_SIDECAR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3384 set. Neither a dead sidecar nor a missing config. The fault is client-side; the leading hypothesis is operator event-loop starvation under load (same family as the mcp_proxy_overloaded shedding), but that is NOT established and must not be repeated as fact.\n\nGate is HELD by a live holder, so the ten pre-existing reds are not mine; stood down per the one-fixer rule.\n\n**Next:** Retry consult:get_feedback vetting on a later wake. Do NOT diagnose it as a slow embedder — the sidecar measures healthy at ~2ms; the fault is client-side and unproven. Once a real vetting reply lands: improve the rubric, attest via scorecards:emit against meta-acceptance-rubric, ROUTE an INDEPENDENT grader (I am the implementer and may not grade it — routing is an obligation, not a stopping point), record my acceptance verdict, then plans:set-plan-status → shipped. Do NOT attest or ship while vetting is blocked.\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` In-flight call registry + per-call correlation id. New `packages/operator-core/lib/in-flight-calls.ts` (state via `pinModuleState`); additive OPTIONAL `callId` on `DispatchStartEvent` and the `recordInvocation` input; wire `PROJECTED_DEPS.onDispatchStart` -> begin and `recordInvocationImpl` -> end.\n- **P-002** `done` `fleet:leader-brief` gains exception-only `longCallInFlight: { ownerId, tool, ageSec }`, beside stalled/spinning/throttled/dormant. ALSO fix the misinformation this incident exposed: a member in a long call must stop reporting as `dormant` with a `laneless-idle` bench suggestion. Blocked-by P-001.\n- **P-003** `done` `coord:send` body sections gain structured `blockedOn: { kind:'process', taskId, logPath, startedAt }`, so a member can say what it is blocked on in a form a leader can act on rather than prose.\n- **P-004** `done` Close the enrolment gap: agent-launched verification runs must carry `featureId` so `processes:list` links process -> work-item. NOTE this is the item that actually covers the originating incident's deepest layer - that member's run was launched OUTSIDE the operator dispatch path, so no operator-side telemetry sees it regardless of when rows are written. — note: Implemented as its CORRECTED content per D-003, not as originally written. The original premise (missing process->work-item linkage) was false — task_ledger.work_item_id already exists and populates; verified live on this session's own three tasks. The real, fixable gap was that resolveBashTaskProvenance derived workItemId from the goal ref alone, so a fleet- or plan-scoped goal left the task unlinked while the agent held a claim. Fixed with an unambiguous-held-claim fallback (6/6 tests). The second half of the original premise — natively-launched runs are never enrolled at all — is NOT operator-fixable and is recorded in D-003 rather than left as an open item.\n\n## Context\n\nVerified during investigation, so no successor re-derives them:\n\n- **No migration is needed** for a `status='running'` row: `harness_shared.tool_invocations.status` is plain `text NOT NULL` with no CHECK constraint, `duration_ms` is nullable, and `'running'` is already this codebase's vocabulary (`action_executions_status_check`, `109-global-schemas-and-grants.sql:41`). Recorded because it is what makes the deferred D-002 option cheap if it is ever wanted.\n- **The dispatch seam already existed and stated this exact purpose.** `DispatchStartEvent` / `onDispatchStart` (`libs/generic/tooldef/src/dispatch-types.ts`, fired in `runDispatchStack` before any gate or handler step) documents itself as being for \"liveness that must be visible while a handler is still in flight, rather than only after it settles\". It existed, was already wired into the very object being edited, and was used only for a presence beat. Reading the comment beside the function saved an invasive multi-site patch to `_mcp-handler.ts`.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Correlate start and settle with an additive OPTIONAL callId, not a new ctx identity\nDate: 2026-08-26\n**Ruling.** A per-call `callId` is generated once in the dispatcher (`initExecution`) and handed to BOTH `onDispatchStart` and `recordInvocation` as an OPTIONAL field on each. Any lane needing to pair a call's beginning with its end uses this; do not invent a second correlation scheme.\n\n**Why it was needed at all.** Nothing in `UnifiedToolContext` identifies a single call: `runId`, `spawnId` and `parentSpawnId` are all SESSION-scoped. So an agent with two calls in flight at once produces two start events a host cannot tell apart, which makes \"this specific call is still running\" unrepresentable. Settling by `(ownerId, toolName)` instead is not a workaround — it actively mis-settles the concurrent-same-tool case, closing a running call's entry and reporting it as finished.\n\n**Why OPTIONAL is load-bearing, not timidity.** A REQUIRED field on a shared interface strands every existing call site (`npm run lint:required-field-strands` exists for exactly this). The value here is correlation for hosts that want it, not a new invariant every host must satisfy — a host that ignores `callId` is byte-identical to today. Do not tighten it without re-running that lint and having a reason beyond tidiness.\n\n**Not a UUID, deliberately.** A process-local counter behind a random prefix. The consumer is an in-process registry, so uniqueness WITHIN a process is the entire requirement; the prefix keeps two processes' ids distinct if one is ever persisted or compared across a port. `randomUUID()` would spend entropy per call on a hot path to buy a property nothing reads.\n\n### D-002 — P-001 ships the in-memory registry only; the status='running' DB row is deliberately NOT built\nDate: 2026-08-26\n**Ruling.** P-001 is the in-process registry alone. The second layer the pre-implementation design specified — inserting a `status='running'` row into `harness_shared.tool_invocations` once a call passes a threshold, then settling it — is deliberately NOT implemented. Do not add it as an incidental part of another lane; if it is ever wanted it is its own item with its own justification.\n\n**This reverses my own earlier design, and the reversal is the point.** The design file written before implementation specified both layers. Implementation surfaced three things that change the trade:\n\n1. **The sole consumer is in-process.** P-002 (`fleet:leader-brief`) is served by the same operator process every agent's MCP calls dispatch through, so the registry answers its question completely with no DB round-trip. The DB layer buys cross-process reach that no current consumer asks for.\n2. **It would put transient rows in a ledger.** `tool_invocations` is read as a record of what HAPPENED. A row that appears, means \"maybe running\", and later mutates or disappears is a different kind of object, and every consumer that counts or groups by `status` inherits it.\n3. **Its failure mode is the exact bug being fixed.** An operator crash mid-call orphans a `running` row that then asserts, durably and forever, that a call is executing. This plan exists because an instrument misreported what an agent was doing; a fix whose own failure mode is a permanent false \"still running\" is not obviously a net improvement.\n\n**What is given up, stated plainly:** the registry is process-local, so it does not span :3070 and :3170 and is empty after an operator restart. Both are acceptable — a call in flight across a restart dies with the restart, so there is nothing to report. A consumer must read an empty registry as \"nothing observed here\", never as \"every agent is idle\". That caveat is written into the module header.\n\n**The prerequisite fact survives the deferral:** no migration is needed if this is ever revisited (see Context) — `status` has no CHECK constraint and `'running'` is already the codebase's vocabulary.\n\n### D-003 — CORRECTION — P-004's premise was wrong: the process→work-item link already works; the real gap is narrower\nDate: 2026-08-26\n**Retraction.** P-004 was written as \"agent-launched verification runs must carry `featureId` so `processes:list` links process → work-item\", asserting a missing linkage. **That assertion was false and is withdrawn.** I wrote it from the originating incident without reading the code that writes the value.\n\n**Evidence.** `harness_shared.task_ledger` already has a first-class `work_item_id` column, populated at enrolment (`task-manager/store.ts`) and surfaced by `processes:list` (`task-manager/inventory.ts`). `capability/bash.ts` already derives it. Queried live: all three background tasks this session launched carry `work_item_id = EI-21548894457555139`. The linkage works.\n\n**What is actually broken — two distinct things the original wording collapsed:**\n\n1. **A run launched through the agent's NATIVE Bash tool is never enrolled at all.** Verified on the incident's own member: `su-06d4c7f1` has exactly ONE `task_ledger` row — its own `agent-session`, `work_item_id: null`. The `affected-tests` run I could only see through a raw process scan (pid 1371230) has no ledger row whatsoever. **The operator cannot fix this in code**: the process is spawned outside it, so nothing is there to enrol it. The remedy is routing — long jobs go through `capability:bash` — which is already the documented rule. NOT actionable as an operator change; recorded so nobody re-opens it as one.\n\n2. **The goal ref is only SOMETIMES a work-item id — and this one IS fixable, so it became P-004's real content.** `bash.ts` derived `workItemId` by regex-testing the goal ref against `^(WI|EI|F)-`. A fleet leader declares `fleet:<slug>`; a plan-bound agent declares `<plan>#P-NNN`. Both yield null, so those tasks land unlinked even while the agent holds a claim. My own tasks linked only because my goal ref happened to BE the item id — the very next fleet-scoped run would not have.\n\n**The fix, and its deliberate limit.** `resolveBashTaskProvenance` now falls back to the caller's held claim (via the existing `readHeldWorkItems`, the same reader the carry brief and orient's recovery fold use, so the surfaces cannot drift) — but ONLY when the claim is UNAMBIGUOUS. Several held items give no basis for choosing, and a fabricated association is worse than an absent one: absent reads as \"unknown\", wrong reads as fact and misattributes the run's cost and provenance. That is the rule this function's own doc comment already stated (\"never a fabricated work-item association\"); the fallback honours it rather than widening it.\n\n**Method note, since this is the second time it has paid off on this plan:** the claim \"X is missing\" is the one most worth checking against the writer before acting. Both times the mechanism already existed — `onDispatchStart` for P-001, `work_item_id` here — and both times a symptom-shaped search would not have found it.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"directed-pair-pilot-item-quality","title":"Directed-pair pilot — per-item delivered quality","status":"active","created":"2026-08-26","owner":"su-856c8310-4bc8-4bcf-b29b-670456bb03ba","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Directed-pair pilot — per-item delivered quality\nslug: directed-pair-pilot-item-quality\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-26\nupdated: 2026-08-26\nowner: su-856c8310-4bc8-4bcf-b29b-670456bb03ba\n---\n\n# Directed-pair pilot — per-item delivered quality\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`draft` ⇒ a proposed rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nThe PRIMARY measuring instrument for the 3-arm directed-pair pilot (plan directed-pair-work-items-2026-08-25, P-006/P-007).\n\nSCORING: every criterion is rated on the rubric's scale and the item's score is the MEAN across criteria, giving one continuous value per item. D-022 measured this harness and found the pilot's originally-specified metrics cannot fire at its size: reopens run 0.74%, so a 21-item pilot has an 85.6% chance of observing zero across all three arms, and the best-variance binary reaches only 7.9% Fisher power at n=7/arm. A continuous score is the only metric family that can carry a decision here.\n\n⚠ THE GRADER MUST BE BLIND TO THE ARM. Strip payload.pilotArm (and pilotSeed/pilotStratum/pilotBlockIndex) from everything the grader sees. The pilot's hypothesis is that the paired arm produces better work, and an unblinded grader who knows which items had a director will find that hypothesis confirmed. Blinding is the cheapest protection the design has and is worthless applied loosely.\n\n⚠ THE GRADER MUST NOT BE THE IMPLEMENTER of the item being graded.\n\nGrade from ARTIFACTS — diff, tests, item record, ledger — never from the closing agent's narrative about its own work (D-002: pasted output is a claim, not evidence).\n\n⚠ WHERE COMPLETION FIELDS ACTUALLY LIVE (measured 2026-08-26, three surfaces, none complete alone):\n• payload->'_completionEvidence' holds ONLY the narrowed verification set: summary, coverage, testsRun, testResult, verifiedHow, addedTests, filesChanged, treeStamp.\n• `deferred`, `whatLanded` and `coordNotes` are NOT persisted on the work-item row and do NOT come back from work_items:get. They exist in the rendered completion broadcast (coord:thread / coord:feed on the completion emit), and coordNotes is separately harvested into the observation lane as its own row.\n• `terminal_completion_ref` carries evidence for DROPPED closes; no route writes both surfaces.\n• completion_ref is NULL on 100% of rows — never read it.\nA grader who reads only _completionEvidence will find zero deferrals on every item and score every item at the floor. That is a wrong instrument producing zero variance, not a finding about the work.\n\nCALIBRATION: before grading the cohort, grade 2-3 already-closed non-pilot items and compare scores with the other grader. If scores do not vary across items, or graders disagree by more than one point, the instrument is not discriminating and must be fixed BEFORE it is used — a rubric that scores every competent close 4-5 reintroduces the exact power failure D-022 moved away from, in continuous clothing.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"external-triggers-v1-acceptance","title":"External triggers v1 — acceptance","status":"active","created":"2026-08-26","owner":"su-fef75d27-419c-4d06-8ba5-f8c295f6039f","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: External triggers v1 — acceptance\nslug: external-triggers-v1-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-26\nupdated: 2026-08-26\nowner: su-fef75d27-419c-4d06-8ba5-f8c295f6039f\n---\n\n# External triggers v1 — acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nAuthored 2026-08-26 against AS-BUILT reality after the per-item code-truth audit (auditSeq 5: 29/30 items audited, 28 verified, verifiedRatio 0.97; only owner-walled P-013 uncovered).\n\nWhat this rubric measures is whether external activity can durably and safely START WORK in Papercusp — not whether files exist. Criteria are outcomes traced to the plan's Requirements section and its Decisions, and are deliberately written so the ONE genuine gap is gradeable rather than glossed: the Gmail lane is proven end-to-end with live external evidence, and the Slack lane has never been demonstrated live because it is blocked on owner-supplied tokens (P-013). A grader who marks live-acceptance-evidence as fully met has not checked.\n\nGRADER NOTE (required by plan-class-feature-ship): spot-check the implementer's audit citations. The implementer authored the Gmail half and therefore may not grade this rubric. Two audit findings are recorded as false friends and are worth re-testing because each would have resolved while certifying nothing: sync-resolver/index.ts for P-016, and agent-tools/plans/runs.ts for P-018.\n\nCHECK-RUN EVIDENCE PRE-RUN FOR THE GRADER (2026-08-26T15:17:49Z, so the grader inherits evidence instead of re-deriving it): all 7 rubric check files were executed at settled HEAD. SIX ARE GREEN (vitest rc=0): ingestion, google-gmail, admin, binding-engine, google-workspace, gmail-flagship. ONE IS RED (rc=1): source-store.integration.test.ts — a KNOWN, FILED, deploy-window artifact, NOT a criterion failure. See criterion envelope-normalization-and-replay's method for why, and do not re-derive it as a fresh defect.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"machine-derived-capacity-profile-2026-08-26","title":"Capless adaptive resource governor","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-26","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Capless adaptive resource governor\nslug: machine-derived-capacity-profile-2026-08-26\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-26\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n# Capless adaptive resource governor\n\n## Objective\n\nReplace Papercusp's scattered fixed, machine-derived, and deployment-specific capacity ceilings with one capless feedback-control system. Resource-consuming demand is not rejected because a configured worker, queue, pool, agent, batch, or concurrency maximum was reached. Instead, every admission point asks one typed governor seam whether work should start now, remain durably pending, or receive priority treatment based on live system health.\n\nThe governor has no configured upper capacity bound. Its instantaneous admission window is controller state that expands while the system remains healthy, contracts when observed degradation appears, and probes upward again after recovery. CPU saturation may slow work naturally; it is not itself a reason to throttle. The plan preserves semantic, correctness, security, protocol, cost, and external-service policy constraints because those are not machine-capacity limits.\n\nThis plan replaces the earlier conservative capacity-profile direction in place. It reuses `@papercusp/resource-profile` for observation and platform normalization, but the new source of truth is a live governor contract rather than a table of derived caps.\n\n## Governing policy\n\n1. **No application capacity ceilings.** Remove fixed and machine-derived maxima for agents, workers, requests, pools, batches, queues, and comparable resource-sensitive execution. Do not replace `64` with a smarter static `192`.\n2. **Live admission, not pre-sizing.** Admit work according to current latency, forward progress, memory behavior, swap behavior, scheduler/event-loop delay, service waits, and resource failures.\n3. **No throttle from utilization alone.** High CPU, high resident memory, or a long durable backlog is acceptable while the system remains responsive and makes useful progress.\n4. **Pre-crash degradation is evidence.** The controller need not wait for OOM or a hard exception. Sustained latency inflation, memory PSI, working-set acceleration, major faults, swap thrashing, event-loop stalls, database waits, or collapsing throughput may trigger throttling when they are temporally attributable to admitted work.\n5. **No permanent ratchet.** Every contraction decays. The controller resumes upward probing after recovery and has no configured maximum to stop expansion.\n6. **Durable deferral, not rejection.** Work that should not start now remains in the canonical durable queue/work-item store rather than an unbounded resident-memory queue.\n7. **Protect judgment and recovery.** Monitoring, cancellation, completion/release, heartbeats, coordination, emergency recovery, and the governor's own control traffic are never throttled behind ordinary work.\n\n## What routes through the governor\n\nEvery operation that can increase concurrent resource residency must use the typed admission seam, including:\n\n- Agent, fleet member, PTY, subprocess, and worker starts.\n- MCP/HTTP request execution when it begins meaningful work.\n- Inference, embedding, model, tool-execution, and provider calls.\n- Database transactions/jobs, DBOS work, checkpoint work, and new connection demand.\n- P2P/sync transfers, indexing, cache fills, compaction, batches, CI/release jobs, and background routines.\n- Socket-heavy, disk-heavy, or memory-heavy operations whose concurrency can amplify pressure.\n\nPure metadata reads, health sampling, cancellation, completion, resource release, heartbeats, coordination, and recovery bypass admission. Cheap operations that cannot materially increase residency may be statically classified as bypass. The bypass list is explicit and linted; arbitrary callers cannot self-declare themselves exempt.\n\nA top-level admission carries an `AdmissionContext` through nested calls. Descendants declare incremental resource demand rather than being charged again for the entire request. This prevents both double-throttling and hidden fan-out.\n\n## One authority, distributed enforcement\n\nThe governor is one logical admission authority, not one synchronous network bottleneck:\n\n- A live control loop maintains global and per-resource/per-class controller state from machine and subsystem telemetry.\n- Hot-path consumers receive short-lived, revocable local admission leases or credits.\n- Local checks consume a lease without a round trip; lease exhaustion or invalidation asks the governor for a fresh decision.\n- Leases expire quickly, carry the telemetry generation and admission class, and cannot create a fixed maximum.\n- Cold/rare paths may call the governor directly.\n- When the governor is temporarily unreachable, existing work continues, control/recovery traffic passes, and new ordinary admissions freeze or use only still-valid leases. There is no fail-open overload burst.\n\nThis shape makes every start governable while keeping the decision plane observable, replaceable, and fast.\n\n## Live health model\n\nThe monitor uses current behavior rather than a machine-size lookup. Signals include:\n\n- End-to-end and per-stage p50/p95/p99 latency, deadline misses, completion rate, queue age, and forward-progress slope.\n- CPU pressure and scheduler/run-queue delay, event-loop lag, process stalls, and throughput per admitted unit. Raw CPU percentage is context only.\n- Working-set size and growth, effective memory availability, memory PSI, GC duration/frequency, major faults, swap-in/swap-out rate, swap-device latency, and estimated time to exhaustion.\n- Database acquisition latency, active/waiting connections, transaction latency, lock waits, refusal/errors, and embedded-versus-dedicated topology.\n- File-descriptor/socket/port usage and related wait/error signals.\n- Disk space, IO latency/queueing, network latency/throughput, and subsystem-specific saturation.\n- Provider 429s, quota headers, account health, and request latency.\n- The governor's own sampling delay and decision latency.\n\nSignals are normalized through `@papercusp/resource-profile` where it already models platform facts. Linux cgroup/container, macOS, Windows/job-object, packaged, desktop, and service deployments feed the same health schema.\n\n## Dynamic controller\n\nThe controller maintains an unbounded desired admission window and optional per-resource/per-class windows. These are ephemeral feedback state, never configured capacity caps.\n\nAt each control interval:\n\n1. Compare current health with rolling healthy baselines, declared service objectives, and recent admission changes.\n2. Attribute degradation to the most likely resource and workload class using temporal correlation, resource ownership, and downstream evidence.\n3. If health is stable or improving, increase admission and continue probing upward.\n4. If health degrades, reduce the responsible admission rate/window proportionally to severity.\n5. If severe degradation threatens forward progress, pause new admissions for the responsible class/resource while running work drains.\n6. Preserve control, recovery, cancellation, and release operations.\n7. After a stable recovery interval, expire the contraction and probe upward again.\n\nController changes record signal snapshots, baseline deltas, attribution, confidence, affected class/resource, previous/new state, and recovery condition. A low-confidence signal may slow the rate of upward probing but cannot permanently lower capacity. Health objectives, sampling periods, hysteresis, and ramp rates are control-stability parameters—not machine-capacity ceilings.\n\n## Physical constraints without duplicated caps\n\nOperating systems, databases, providers, and devices have real physical or contractual limits. Papercusp does not mirror them into guessed caps. It observes live availability and behavior.\n\nWhen a new operation cannot currently succeed—for example, no connection can be acquired or the machine is losing forward progress—the governor defers admission. This is an instantaneous feasibility decision, not a permanent concurrency maximum. The system continuously retries through controlled probing when health returns.\n\nThe monitor/recovery plane receives scheduling priority and minimal resource isolation so it remains able to throttle and recover. That protection is an availability invariant for the controller, not a capacity limit imposed on productive work.\n\n## Durable scheduling and fairness\n\nThe durable work-item/job substrate owns pending demand. The governor controls when work becomes resident/executing; it does not create a second in-memory queue.\n\nAdmission is work-conserving and fair across interactive, control, normal, and bulk classes. Priorities and weights determine ordering, not fixed quotas. Unused capacity is borrowable immediately. Starvation detectors raise a class's effective priority without reserving a permanent slice.\n\nCancellation and completion return resource observations immediately. Actual measured cost feeds subsequent decisions; cost hints are advisory and may not become hidden hard caps.\n\n## Failure containment\n\nThe live loop must remain safe when sensors, consumers, or the governor misbehave:\n\n- Out-of-process supervision detects a stalled governor or stale telemetry.\n- Lease generations invalidate stale decisions.\n- Admission contexts are idempotent across retry and cannot leak credits.\n- Controller oscillation, correlated retry storms, and contradictory sensors are detected and surfaced.\n- Severe health loss pauses new ordinary starts; it does not kill healthy running work unless a separate cancellation policy authorizes that.\n- Recovery always includes an upward probe; a transient incident cannot leave a permanent low-water mark.\n- Diagnostics show why work is running or deferred and which live evidence produced the current decision.\n\n## Registry and lint\n\nReplace the old capacity-limit registry with an admission inventory and enforcement registry. Each entry records:\n\n- Admission operation and typed class.\n- Resource dimensions it can increase.\n- Writer/start site and downstream fan-out.\n- Governor seam and context propagation path.\n- Bypass status and justification, if any.\n- Telemetry/feedback ownership.\n- Durable deferral behavior.\n- Cancellation/release accounting.\n- Migration and verification state.\n\nLint rejects new resource-consuming starts that bypass the seam, hidden local semaphores or concurrency maxima, static numeric capacity defaults, unbounded resident queues, missing context propagation, and unjustified bypasses. Semantic/security/protocol limits are annotated as non-capacity policy.\n\nThe existing audit baseline remains useful: 69 high-signal tunables, 355 limit-named environment surfaces, and 1,641 broad limit-like assignments are migration inputs. Each is re-read at its writer and classified as remove, convert to governor admission, retain as semantic/policy, physical upstream constraint, or false positive.\n\n## Subsystem migration\n\nMigration removes or neutralizes local capacity caps only after the corresponding start path is governed:\n\n1. Agent/fleet/PTY/swarm/scout/process starts and memory-heavy agent work.\n2. MCP/HTTP/operator execution, sockets, workers, queues, and transport fan-out.\n3. Inference, embedding, provider calls, batching, database/sidecar/checkpoint pools, and DBOS jobs.\n4. P2P/sync, indexing, cache fills, compaction, CI/release/test workers, and background routines.\n5. Development, systemd/service, packaged, Linux/macOS/Windows desktop, and container configurations.\n\nEach migration proves that demand remains durable, starts are observable and governable, nested fan-out propagates context, local caps are deleted rather than raised, and the governor can expand without an artificial ceiling.\n\n## Cross-machine validation\n\nExercise the governor on a small laptop, workstation, high-core/memory server, constrained container/cgroup, Linux, macOS, Windows, embedded/dedicated Postgres, and single/multi-worker topologies. Drive representative demand at 1, 10, 30, 100, 300, and beyond the previously configured ceilings.\n\nValidate:\n\n- CPU saturation slows work without unnecessary throttling when latency/progress remain healthy.\n- Memory growth, PSI, GC, major faults, and swap behavior cause smooth pre-crash contraction and recovery.\n- Service/resource-specific pressure throttles only attributable work.\n- Durable backlog does not inflate resident memory.\n- Local leases match centralized decisions and expire safely.\n- Controller loss, telemetry staleness, retry storms, oscillation, and nested fan-out are contained.\n- No static or machine-derived capacity ceiling stops upward probing.\n- Control/recovery traffic remains responsive throughout.\n\n## Rollout and rollback\n\nBegin in observe-only mode: compute decisions and compare them with current behavior without delaying work. Then govern one subsystem at a time, deleting its local caps only after admission, deferral, telemetry, and recovery are verified. Expand through bounded canaries and cross-machine stress/soak evidence.\n\nRollback restores the previous admission behavior for the affected subsystem while keeping durable demand and telemetry intact. It must not reinstate a scattered permanent cap as the long-term architecture. Emergency rollback may temporarily freeze admission or restore a known behavior, but the durable resolution is repair of the governor/control loop.\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- No fixed or machine-derived concurrency, worker, queue, pool, batch, or agent ceilings.\n- No central per-request RPC bottleneck.\n- No unbounded resident-memory queue.\n- No throttling from raw utilization alone.\n- No conversion of semantic, security, correctness, protocol, cost, or provider rules into capacity controls.\n- No implementation or `plans:start` action in WI-42311.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-27. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nReplace and activation-audit this plan under WI-42311. Return it to `ready` without calling `plans:start`, then complete WI-42311 with this plan reference.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Phase 1 — Admission and evidence contracts\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Inventory every resource-consuming admission site and every bypass across agents/fleets/PTYs/processes, MCP/HTTP/operator, inference/embedding/providers, DB/DBOS/checkpoint, P2P/sync/index/cache/compaction, CI/release/test, and background routines. Re-read each current cap/default writer from the 69 high-signal, 355 environment-surface, and 1,641 broad-candidate audit. Classify each as govern, explicit control/recovery bypass, semantic/policy, physical upstream constraint, or false positive. Acceptance: every start site names its residency dimensions, fan-out, durable source, telemetry, cancellation/release path, and current cap to delete; no conclusion comes from a name/count alone. importance: urgent\n- **P-002** `todo` Define the single typed Governor admission API and propagated AdmissionContext. A resource-consuming start requests admit/defer with class, resource dimensions, incremental cost hint, deadline, parent context, and idempotency key; the result is start-now, durably-deferred, or privileged bypass. Nested calls charge only incremental residency and cannot self-exempt. Acceptance: API/schema tests cover idempotent retry, nested fan-out, cancellation/release, bypass authorization, and compatibility adapters; no capacity maximum exists in the contract. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent\n- **P-003** `todo` Implement the shared live-health schema and out-of-process monitor using @papercusp/resource-profile for platform normalization. Sample latency/progress, CPU PSI/scheduler/event-loop delay, working set/growth, memory PSI, GC, faults, swap rate/latency, DB waits, FD/socket/port pressure, disk/network, provider feedback, and governor health across Linux/container, macOS, and Windows. Acceptance: timestamps/confidence/ownership are explicit; stale/missing/contradictory sensors are detectable; monitoring and recovery stay responsive during workload saturation. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Capless control loop\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Define health objectives, rolling healthy baselines, degradation detection, and causal attribution without static capacity thresholds. Raw CPU/RAM utilization cannot throttle by itself; sustained latency inflation, forward-progress loss, swap thrash, PSI/GC/fault evidence, service waits, or failures may throttle when temporally and topologically attributable to admitted work. Acceptance: deterministic fixtures distinguish healthy 100%-CPU operation from collapse, ordinary swap use from thrash, unrelated load from causal degradation, and low-confidence evidence from actionable evidence. blocked-by: P-003 importance: urgent\n- **P-005** `todo` Implement the capless controller: an unbounded desired admission window plus per-resource/per-class feedback state that increases while health is stable, contracts proportionally on attributable degradation, pauses responsible new starts on severe loss of progress, and always probes upward after recovery. No configured floor/ceiling or machine-derived maximum may stop expansion. Acceptance: simulations prove stable convergence, bounded oscillation, causal contraction, automatic recovery with no permanent ratchet, and no throttle from utilization alone. blocked-by: P-002, P-004 importance: urgent\n- **P-006** `todo` Implement short-lived, revocable distributed admission leases for hot paths so one logical governor does not become a per-request RPC bottleneck. Leases carry telemetry generation, resource/class scope, expiry, and remaining admission credit; cold paths may ask directly. Acceptance: local decisions match controller state, stale generations/expired leases cannot admit, governor loss freezes ordinary new admission while valid work/control traffic continues, and no lease encodes a permanent maximum. blocked-by: P-002, P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Integrate the governor with the canonical durable job/work-item substrate. Deferred demand remains durable and non-resident; admission pulls it when health permits rather than placing it in an unbounded in-memory queue or rejecting it. Acceptance: process restart and long deferral lose no work, queue depth does not scale resident memory, priority changes are honored, and completion/cancellation wakes the admission loop without polling. blocked-by: P-002, P-005 importance: urgent\n- **P-008** `todo` Implement end-to-end AdmissionContext propagation, actual-cost feedback, nested incremental resource claims, and exact release/cancellation accounting. Acceptance: retries are idempotent, fan-out cannot hide or double-count demand, leaked credits are detected/reclaimed, actual residency updates controller evidence, and a top-level request remains traceable through every governed descendant. blocked-by: P-002, P-006, P-007 importance: high\n- **P-009** `todo` Replace the capacity registry/lint with an admission/enforcement registry. Lint every resource-consuming start through the governor seam; reject hidden local semaphores or capacity maxima, static numeric capacity defaults, unjustified bypasses, missing context propagation/release, and unbounded resident queues. Encode work-conserving priority/fairness and protect monitor, cancellation, release, heartbeat, coordination, and recovery traffic without fixed productive-work quotas. Acceptance: positive/negative fixtures cover all classes and every bypass has an owner and rationale. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-008 importance: urgent\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Subsystem migrations\n\n- **P-010** `todo` Migrate agent, fleet, PTY, swarm, scout, process-spawn, and memory-heavy agent work to Governor.admit; remove their local worker/agent/queue/memory capacity ceilings rather than raising them. Acceptance: nested agent fan-out carries one AdmissionContext, demand stays durable, control traffic remains responsive, and load can grow beyond every former cap while health permits. blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009 importance: high\n- **P-011** `todo` Migrate MCP, HTTP, operator, transport, sockets, cluster workers, and request execution to the governor seam; remove development/systemd, packaged, per-worker, and queue concurrency caps. Acceptance: cheap metadata/control bypasses are explicit, meaningful work is governed before residency, no per-worker multiplication escape remains, and hot paths use leases without a central latency bottleneck. blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009 importance: high\n- **P-012** `todo` Migrate inference, embedding, provider calls, batching, database/sidecar/checkpoint pools, transactions, and DBOS jobs. Treat provider/database physical or contractual constraints as live feedback, not duplicated Papercusp caps. Acceptance: DB waits/refusals, provider 429s, model latency, memory/swap behavior, and completion feedback throttle only attributable classes; upward probing resumes; old pool/concurrency/batch defaults are removed or retained only as non-capacity policy with evidence. blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009 importance: high\n- **P-013** `todo` Migrate P2P/sync, indexing, cache fills, compaction, CI/release/test workers, and background routines; unify development, systemd/service, packaged, Linux/macOS/Windows desktop, and container configurations on the same governor/health/lease contracts. Acceptance: no deployment forks admission logic, former support-path caps are deleted after governance lands, and equivalent live inputs produce equivalent decisions across paths. blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Validation\n\n- **P-014** `todo` Run cross-machine, saturation, chaos, and controller-loss validation on laptop, workstation, high-core/memory server, constrained container, Linux/macOS/Windows, embedded/dedicated DB, and single/multi-worker topologies. Drive 1/10/30/100/300 and beyond former ceilings. Acceptance: healthy CPU saturation is unthrottled; latency/memory/swap/service degradation contracts smoothly before crash; durable backlog remains non-resident; leases/context/accounting stay correct; no static ceiling halts probing; recovery traffic stays responsive; controller automatically expands after recovery. blocked-by: P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013 importance: urgent\n\n## Phase 5 — Rollout and rollback\n\n- **P-015** `todo` Roll out observe-only decisions, then govern one subsystem at a time, deleting its local caps only after admission/deferral/telemetry/recovery evidence is green. Expand through canaries and soak, publish diagnostics/runbooks, and drill rollback that restores prior admission behavior without losing durable demand. Acceptance: all inventory rows have a final disposition, registry/lint prevent cap recurrence and bypasses, rollback works, temporary controls are removed, and the capless governor becomes the default across every deployment. blocked-by: P-014 importance: urgent\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Capacity is capless controller state, never a configured ceiling\nDate: 2026-08-27\nPapercusp must not configure or derive maximum agents, workers, queues, pools, batches, or concurrency from machine size. The governor may hold an instantaneous admission window so it can throttle, but that state has no upper bound, expands while health permits, contracts from live degradation, and is never a durable capacity ceiling.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-014\n\n### D-002 — Every resource-consuming start uses one typed admission seam\nDate: 2026-08-27\nAll operations capable of increasing concurrent resource residency must call Governor.admit directly or consume a valid governor lease before starting. This includes agent/process, MCP/request, model/provider, DB/job, transfer/index/cache/compaction, CI/release, and background work. Governance occurs at residency admission, not merely at API receipt.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-003 — Control and non-resident operations bypass explicitly\nDate: 2026-08-27\nHealth sampling, cancellation, completion/release, heartbeats, coordination, emergency recovery, and cheap metadata work that cannot materially increase residency bypass admission. Bypasses are registry-owned and linted; callers cannot self-declare exemption. This keeps the governor and recovery path live without routing meaningless operations through a bottleneck.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-009\n\n### D-004 — One logical governor uses distributed short-lived leases\nDate: 2026-08-27\nAdmission policy and live controller state have one logical authority, but high-volume enforcement is local through short-lived revocable leases. This avoids a central per-request RPC, preserves consistent decisions, and lets telemetry generation/expiry invalidate stale grants. Governor loss freezes new ordinary starts instead of failing open into an overload burst.\nRelated: P-002, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-005 — Throttle on measured health degradation, not utilization\nDate: 2026-08-27\nCPU saturation, high resident memory, swap use, or backlog size alone do not justify throttling. Sustained latency inflation, loss of forward progress, memory PSI/working-set acceleration, GC/major-fault/swap thrashing, service waits, or hard failures may contract admission when attributable to recent work. The controller can act before a crash; an OOM is not required evidence.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-014\n\n### D-006 — Every contraction expires and upward probing has no ceiling\nDate: 2026-08-27\nA throttling decision records evidence, attribution, confidence, and recovery condition. After stable recovery it decays and the governor probes upward again. Low-confidence evidence may slow probing but cannot create a permanent low-water mark. No floor/ceiling table or machine profile terminates growth.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-014, P-015\n\n### D-007 — Deferred demand stays durable and non-resident\nDate: 2026-08-27\nThe governor controls when durable work becomes resident; it does not reject demand or accumulate a second unbounded memory queue. Paused work remains in the canonical job/work-item substrate and is woken by health/release transitions. This is admission backpressure without data loss or a queue-cap policy.\nRelated: P-002, P-007, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-008 — AdmissionContext prevents hidden fan-out and double throttling\nDate: 2026-08-27\nA top-level admission context propagates across nested calls. Descendants declare only incremental resource demand, retries are idempotent, and releases/cancellations close exact claims. This makes all resource growth visible without charging a request repeatedly at every internal boundary.\nRelated: P-002, P-006, P-008\n\n### D-009 — Throttle the attributable resource and workload class\nDate: 2026-08-27\nA provider 429 contracts that provider/account lane; DB waits contract DB-heavy admission; memory/swap degradation contracts memory-heavy work. Unrelated work continues when healthy. Global contraction is reserved for machine-wide loss of forward progress, never inferred from a single subsystem's utilization.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-012, P-014\n\n### D-010 — Monitor and recovery availability outrank productive admission\nDate: 2026-08-27\nThe out-of-process governor, health sampling, cancellation, completion/release, coordination, and recovery plane receive priority and minimal isolation so the system can always observe and recover. This is a control-plane availability invariant, not a hard productive-work capacity quota.\nRelated: P-003, P-009, P-014\n\n### D-011 — Observe physical and contractual constraints; do not duplicate them\nDate: 2026-08-27\nOS, cgroup, database, provider, socket, disk, and device constraints remain real, but Papercusp does not mirror them into guessed caps. Live inability or degrading behavior defers the next admission, and controlled probing resumes when feasibility returns. Semantic, security, correctness, protocol, and cost policies remain separate fixed rules.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-004, P-012\n\n### D-012 — Admission registry and lint are the recurrence guard\nDate: 2026-08-27\nCI must reject resource-consuming starts that bypass Governor.admit/leases, hidden local semaphores and capacity maxima, static capacity defaults, unbounded resident queues, missing context/release accounting, and unjustified bypasses. Existing capacity literals are deleted or explicitly retained only as non-capacity policy/upstream constraints with writer evidence.\nRelated: P-001, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-015\n\n### D-013 — Observe first, then govern and delete caps subsystem by subsystem\nDate: 2026-08-27\nRollout begins with shadow decisions and diagnostics. A subsystem's local caps are removed only after its admission seam, durable deferral, telemetry, lease/context accounting, and recovery behavior are verified. Rollback restores prior admission behavior temporarily, never a second permanent cap architecture.\nRelated: P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-015\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"standalone-feature-backlog-drain-2026-08-26","title":"Drain the standalone (plan-less) papercusp feature backlog","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-26","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Drain the standalone (plan-less) papercusp feature backlog\nslug: standalone-feature-backlog-drain-2026-08-26\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-26\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nLeadership is now su-09889dff on fleet standalone-drain. D-016 restored the visible Codex fleet on account=default, model=gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh, warm carry; new members su-767af364 and su-b0344442 passed durable first-turn verification and are waiting on work-item:done:WI-3985. WI-662 is terminal. WI-3985 remains open/live-held by su-5c67a395 behind its declared capability gates. The remaining documented blocked residues are WI-4480, WI-3232, WI-3133, WI-5211, and WI-3130. Sentinel rev10 and the fixed 24-ID cohort are unchanged, with no currently claimable row. P-001/P-005 are restored to todo after the corrected duplicate-projection incident; D-003 remains binding.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Use the armed fleet transition watches and the workers' WI-3985 completion await, not status polling. When WI-3985 terminalizes, re-read its completion evidence, clear only proven-satisfied dependencies, and let rev10 place WI-4480 and WI-3133. Audit WI-4480's real macOS shortcut battery and WI-3133's lifecycle/fresh-install evidence plus armed schedule. Then re-evaluate WI-3232/WI-5211/WI-3130, rerun the exact fixed-cohort census, send final dispositions, and close order #10 only when every residue is honestly terminal or dependency-bound.)\n\n## Background\n\nThe plan items below are **LANES** — they exist to give the fleet its parallel width and to group the work narratively. They are NOT the units of work and must never be promoted (`plans:start` on this plan would double-mint rows against the existing work-items — exactly the defect filed as WI-42160). The authoritative units are the pinned work-items, pulled from the live ledger.\n\n### Pinned wave — pullable now (15)\n\n| lane | items |\n|---|---|\n| Desktop / UX surface | WI-4480, WI-3388, WI-4446 |\n| Runtime reliability | WI-3821, WI-3778, WI-3604 |\n| hive-git transport | WI-3583, WI-3641 |\n| Sandbox + capability envelope | WI-3786, WI-3627 |\n| Agent substrate | WI-1281, WI-662 |\n| Verdicts + batteries | WI-5394, WI-3921, WI-3964 |\n\n### Pinned but floor-held while `blocked` (4)\n\nWI-3232 (offline self-admit, owner-directed bug) · WI-3985 (mem0 federation) · WI-603 (HIVE_REKEY flag) · WI-609 (EXTERNAL_BENCH flag, carries a human blocker). Clearing a stale blocker on these is legitimate drain work for the leader.\n\n### EXCLUDED — rig-gated, cannot terminate on this box (5)\n\nWI-5211 (3-machine live fleet drill; also `_claimHold`) · WI-3133 (continuous Mac-VM E2E battery) · WI-3130 (native-arm64 macOS build toolchain) · WI-3629 and WI-1939 (p2p wiring both explicitly deferred to the P-305 rig). These stay open and are reported as residue at wind-down, not silently dropped.\n\n## Phase 1 — drain lanes\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Desktop / UX surface lane: WI-4480 (docs-search shortcut OFF by default + a real disable, shortcuts tested on all 3 platforms), WI-3388 (resizeable + collapsible native terminal dock), WI-4446 (beta release-history page). All three carry verbatim owner specs in their bodies — read them, do not paraphrase them away. importance: high — note: ← WI-267220 completed (dropped)\n- **P-002** `todo` Runtime reliability lane: WI-3821 (global admission control for agent-spawned heavy builds), WI-3778 (ensureSendSideWired re-resolve on SESSION_CLOSED), WI-3604 (sidecar boot must LOG + ASSERT its DHT universe — recurrence guard for the split-universe outage class). importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` hive-git transport lane: WI-3583 (live per-peer dial registry, device pubkey to swarm socket), WI-3641 (wire authorizeScopeRepoServe so scope-family repos serve over the papercusp/hive-git transport). importance: medium\n- **P-004** `todo` Sandbox + capability envelope lane: WI-3786 (wire the P-105 sandbox axes into the live foreign-work spawn path), WI-3627 (widen the foreign-session capability envelope beyond deny-all — marked owner-gated, and DRAIN/AUTO carries the owner's standing approval to pass that gate; disclose what you passed). importance: medium\n- **P-005** `todo` Agent substrate lane: WI-1281 (full/trimmed initial-context toggle in the SU launch selector), WI-662 (LAZY_SUBSTRATE_BOOT v2 — evict idle SHARED harnesses behind a swarm-presence keepalive). importance: medium — note: ← WI-267222 completed (dropped)\n- **P-006** `todo` Verdicts + batteries lane: WI-5394 (72h bridged-canary soak — the clock started 2026-07-18, so this is a READ-the-result-and-close, not a fresh soak), WI-3921 (M2 IDEATE-mode battery re-run), WI-3964 (su-ideate-learning-substrate implementation anchor). importance: medium\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 The claim spec is a static id-pin, not a property filter\n\nThe standing guidance is to steer a lane with a property filter and reserve `id in [...]` for a one-off wave. This drain IS that exception: the owner named a finite, already-enumerated set (the plan-less feature items), and the natural property filter — `plan IS NULL` — is unsafe here, because a `not`/`!=` leaf on a NULLABLE spec field silently drops rows in the SQL compiler. The pin is composed with a `kind` leaf so it is never an id-ONLY selector. No auto-inflow is wanted: a new plan-less item filed mid-drain is out of the owner's named scope.\n\n### D-002 Rig-gated items are excluded from the wave, not dropped\n\nFive items need hardware this box does not have (a Mac VM, a native-arm64 toolchain, the multi-machine P-305 rig). Pinning them would let members claim, fail, and release them repeatedly. They keep their state and their WI-42159 priorities and are reported as residue at wind-down.\n\n### D-003 Plan items are lanes; they are never promoted\n\n`plans:start` is forbidden on this plan. Promoting these six lane items would mint six new feature rows duplicating work-items that already exist — the double-mint defect filed as WI-42160 during the audit that produced this backlog.\n\n### D-004 — The drain wave was unclaimable at launch: 26 feature rows stranded at status='todo'\nDate: 2026-08-26\nFound during launch preflight, 2026-08-26T18:30Z. fleet:launch-on-plan refused with executableWidth 0 / featureFamily.claimable 0.\n\nROOT CAUSE, read in code: claimFloorsWhereSql (packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts:4798) defaults `states = opts.states ?? ['open']` and matches `AND status = ANY(${states}::text[])` — a RAW match with NO alias-fold. A feature/chunk row at the legacy `todo` status is therefore invisible to every feature-family self-select path, permanently and silently. The floor's own comment says so and warns that its previous 'no row sits at todo' claim was false in both halves.\n\nMEASURED (workspace papercusp-workspace, harness papercusp, item_kind IN feature,chunk): todo = 26, created 2026-06-21..2026-07-18; open = 286. 15 of the 26 were the entire pullable half of this drain's scope.\n\nTWO INSTRUMENT TRAPS on the same question, both survived: (1) harness_shared.work_items_claimable returns zero for every one of these rows, but it is hard-scoped to item_kind IN (bug,change,task) and structurally cannot answer for features — a verified-absence result that means nothing here. (2) status='todo' reads like ordinary un-picked backlog on every list surface. Neither says 'unclaimable'.\n\nACTION: all 26 flipped todo -> open (the canonical post-unification claimable status migration 638 intended). Verified after: todo = 0. This unstranded this drain's wave and 11 rows outside it. Reversible; titles, priorities and plan linkage untouched.\n\nRESIDUAL, NOT FIXED HERE: there is no recurrence guard. A writer regressing to 'todo' mints a silently-unclaimable row again with nothing failing loudly — 26 rows were invisible for over two months and no surface reported it, so the detector gap is a second defect. Wanted: a health-check asserting zero non-terminal feature-family rows outside CLAIM_STATES_ALLOWLIST, and/or write-path normalization rejecting 'todo' for item_kind IN (feature,chunk). Filing of the standalone bug row was refused by the DRAIN dedup gate (semantic leg unavailable) and must be retried.\n\n### D-005 — D: An empty block-reason is the detector for a STALE blocked item — audit blocked items before reporting them as residue\nDate: 2026-08-26\nRuling for this drain and any future one, established while auditing the 5 blocked items in the 19-item pinned wave.\n\n**Do not report a `blocked` item as residue until you have checked whether its blocker still exists.** Two of the five were not blocked at all:\n\n- **WI-603 \"Implement + flip HIVE_REKEY\" → done.** The work shipped 2026-06-29 under a RENAMED key: `HIVE_REKEY` → `FLAGS.POT_REKEY`. It is DEFAULT ON, absent from `KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS`/`DARK_FLAG_CASE`, owner-ratified, shipped in desktop alpha.2 (`libs/flags/src/types.ts:1521-1532`). The gate it waited on (2-machine K-CUT witness, WI-560/WI-559) was satisfied.\n- **WI-609 \"Build + flip EXTERNAL_BENCH\" → dropped.** Not blocked but VOID: the blueprint is RETIRED per WI-5646 (owner decision 2026-07-26); the registry says verbatim \"Do NOT flip ON\" and the P-009 pilot that was its graduation condition will never run (`libs/flags/src/types.ts:2993-2998`).\n\n**The detector: an EMPTY block reason.** Both stale items had a blank summary AND a null checkpoint. All three genuinely-blocked items carried real reasons, and the best-formed (WI-662) carried a STRUCTURED `externalBlockers: [{ref:'two-machine-federation-rig', kind:'runtime', status:'active'}]`. So: a blocked item with no recorded reason is not residue, it is an UNAUDITED item — treat empty-reason as a work signal, never as a status.\n\n**Why WI-603 evaded every prior already-fixed sweep: a RENAME defeats name-based absence checks.** The natural audit — grep the flag name in the registry — returns ZERO hits for `HIVE_REKEY`, and zero hits reads identically to \"never implemented\" when it actually meant \"renamed and shipped\". The stable identifier survived the rename: the runtime slug stayed `\"papercusp-hive-rekey\"` while the key changed. **When an absence check on a NAME returns zero, confirm the name still addresses the thing before believing the absence** — prefer the slug/string identifier over the symbol name.\n\nThis is the same false-zero family as this drain's earlier zero-match claim-spec incident, where three members read an empty claim result as a broken filter when it was the correct arithmetic answer to a drained pin. In both cases the instinct to \"repair\" the instrument was the error; in both cases the fix was to confirm what the zero actually measured.\n\n### D-006 — D: Claim spec rev 6 is MALFORMED — I authored it, and a member's zero-match escalation was correct where my \"drained wave\" ruling was not\nDate: 2026-08-26\n**Retraction first.** I ruled three times that `matchedByFilter=0` on `standalone-feature-drain-wave-wi42159` rev 6 was the correct arithmetic answer of a drained static pin, and broadcast a fleet-wide stand-down on that basis. On the fourth escalation, su-4f31a25e produced the falsifier I should have checked myself: **WI-4480 is pinned, `open`, unassigned, and `kind=feature`, so the filter must match at least one row — a zero is inconsistent.** They were right; my explanation was not.\n\n**The spec, read from `harness_shared.cup_claim_specs` (bee_id `fleet:standalone-drain`, revision 6, authored by su-b5f45c90 at 2026-08-26T18:37:38Z).** Its `view.filter.all` carries THREE clauses:\n\n1. `kind IN [\"feature\",\"chunk\"]`\n2. `id IN [19 pinned ids]` — WI-4480 among them\n3. `kind IN [\"feature\"]`  ← redundant duplicate of (1)\n\nClause 3 is a duplicate `kind` predicate layered on clause 1. Logically the intersection is non-empty (`feature` satisfies both), so a correct compiler should still match WI-4480. It does not.\n\n**What is established vs. what is not.** ESTABLISHED: the spec pins WI-4480; WI-4480 is open/unassigned/feature; `matchedByFilter` is nonetheless 0; and the filter contains a redundant duplicate `kind` clause that I introduced. NOT ESTABLISHED: that the duplicate clause is the *cause* — I verified the inconsistency, not the mechanism. Anyone picking this up should test the duplicate-`kind` hypothesis first but must not assume it.\n\n**Why the stand-down still stands, on corrected reasoning.** The outcome is unchanged but the reason is different from what I originally gave. A repaired spec surfaces exactly ONE additional row — WI-4480 — which requires live Tauri shortcut testing on all three platforms. No member of this fleet can run it. So repairing the spec converts \"no work\" into \"guaranteed-failing work\"; it does not unblock anyone. Members finishing held items should `loop:end`, which is what I asked for, for a reason I had wrong.\n\n**Likely bearing on the WI-4480 mystery.** This drain burned 8 disconfirmed hypotheses on why WI-4480 was \"never served\" despite being open and unclaimed. A pinning spec whose filter fails to match it is a strong candidate explanation, and it was sitting in a table I had not read. The earlier hunt searched behaviour; the answer was in the spec definition.\n\n**The process lesson.** Three members independently reported this and I overruled all three with the same confident framing, because a drained wave *was* the expected end-state and the zero was *consistent* with it. Consistency with an expected story is not verification of it. The cheap falsifier — does any pinned row still satisfy the filter — was available from the first report, and a member had to hold the line to the fourth escalation to get it checked. When several independent reporters contradict a leader's model, that is signal about the model, not repetition to be managed.\n\n### D-007 — D-007: WI-3388 closes on scoped evidence — the 31-failure affected-router red is a VERIFIED-unrelated shared-tree condition, owned elsewhere\nDate: 2026-08-26\nRULING (leader, standalone-drain): WI-3388's final `test:affected` red does NOT block its closure. su-06d4c7f1 reported 31 failures in @papercusp/operator-core::test:lane-stateful and characterised them as \"unrelated shared-tree\". I did NOT take that characterisation on trust — \"unrelated\" is exactly the claim that decides whether the item may close, so it was verified from the ledger before ruling.\n\nEVIDENCE THAT THE RED IS NOT WI-3388'S (testing:runs, status fail|error, 8h window):\n1. MECHANISM. The FLEET_TYPES reds — fleet_registry/{leave,join,headcount-target}.test.ts and fleet_registry/__tests__/create.test.ts — all carry `durationMs: 0`, `commitSha: null`, `branch: null`, with outputTail `[vitest] No \"FLEET_TYPES\" export is defined on the \"../../agent-fleets-store\" mock`. Duration zero + null sha means these died at COLLECTION, not at assertion: a `vi.mock` of agent-fleets-store no longer matching that module's export surface. That is export drift from another lane, and repo convention is explicit that a multi-file Vitest invocation aborting during collection must NOT be attributed to every requested path.\n2. IMPOSSIBILITY. WI-3388's three changed paths are native_terminal.rs (Rust), scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh (shell) and one new TS test. A Rust source file cannot alter a TypeScript module mock's export surface. There is no causal path from this item's diff to a FLEET_TYPES mock mismatch, scorecard semantics, persona projection or OAuth/docs.\n3. SCALE + PRE-EXISTENCE. The ledger holds 193 red rows in the 8h window (result truncated by limit), and `state:read gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict` returns 44 CONSECUTIVE REDS with assessment `red-stale` (verdictStale:true, mainBehindStaging:true). A 44-red streak is a long-standing tree condition that massively predates this run.\n4. INFRASTRUCTURE ARTIFACT. The member's own secondary observation is corroborated: several test-file-name-filter reds are downstream of `EEXIST /tmp/pc-heavy-ready/ready.mXINVK` — a pc-heavy readiness-file collision between concurrent heavy runs on the shared box, i.e. parallelism residue, not a code defect.\n\nWHAT IS GREEN AND IN SCOPE: dock-specific focused tests 2/2; mac VM 56/56 plus a real AppKit NSWindow+WKWebView dynamic-load roundtrip (250px initial, 0px collapsed, 1000px full, 400px reopen, 100px min, 500px max, 250px exact); live Linux X11 acceptance on Xvfb :90 (rail collapse unmapped Ghostty 321px, expand GUI 1280->1601, Show restored, drag persisted fraction .25->.3496 with Ghostty 321->448); lint:tsc:scripts and lint:tsc:operator clean.\n\nGATE DISPOSITION — NOT OURS TO FIX. `state:read gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership` returns `held` with assessment `held-live` (holderSessionState:'live', no duplicates, no expiry) and the explicit safe action \"Do not take it over.\" Per the one-fixer rule, this fleet sends its evidence once and stops: no claim, no fallback loop, no repeated gate reads. The shared red has a live owner and a second agent on it is waste, not diligence. This drain does NOT force, quarantine, or route around it.\n\nBINDING FOR THIS FLEET: an item whose OWN scoped verification is green may close over a shared-tree red that is verified-unrelated by mechanism, provided its completion evidence DISCLOSES the shared red honestly rather than claiming a full green — the same honest form accepted on WI-3778 (D-005), where the broad affected wrapper never reached a verdict and the completion said so. A completion that silently implies a full-suite green is re-opened by completion-integrity audit. Closure on scoped evidence is NOT a waiver of completion integrity; it is a scoping of what this item's evidence is allowed to claim.\n\n### D-008 — A zero claimable frontier while the pinned feature rows are live-held is drained arithmetic, not a spec defect\nDate: 2026-08-26\nDuring the 2026-08-26 fleet recovery, claim spec `standalone-feature-drain-wave-wi42159` revisions 8/9 returned `spec_matches_nothing` after WI-3232 and WI-3985 were claimed by live members. That zero is CORRECT: the static pin contains the authorized wave, and claimability excludes rows already held. Before changing the spec after a zero pull, read `fleet:assignments` and distinguish live-held from absent. If every in-scope nonterminal row is live-held, do not widen, do not duplicate either claim, and do not reinterpret a bug/other-feature backlog as part of this drain. Record the drained frontier and park on the feature-scoped `work-item:claimable` event; wake only if a held lane releases or a new row becomes claimable under the same spec.\nRelated: P-001, P-005\n\n### D-009 — WI-3232 offline-seed acceptance must use the seeded Server artifact, not GUI/base\nDate: 2026-08-27\nDate: 2026-08-27\n\nThe stale WI-3232 handoff named retained `papercusp-gui` 0.0.13 as the fresh-install acceptance artifact. A pristine VM proved that package boots the GUI/operator but contains no bundled seed, so `restoreHiveSeed` returns `ran:false` and the offline self-admit branch correctly does not run. Current canonical distribution tests deliberately exclude the multi-GB `seed/**/*` payload from GUI/base resources and include it in Server resources; the retained artifact source already contains the self-admit implementation. Therefore the GUI result is not evidence that the shipped self-admit code regressed—it is evidence that the acceptance targeted the wrong package role.\n\nRuling: exercise WI-3232 only against a current, fully finalized and audited seeded `papercusp-server` artifact on a pristine machine. Do not consume an archive while its writer still holds it. Verify package/PG/operator boot, offline local self-admission without GitHub or federation, checkout presence, and seeded plans/work-items. If the Server path is green, close WI-3232 with that evidence and mark the GUI handoff obsolete; if it is red, fix the actual Server packaging/bootstrap root cause and add a recurrence guard. This does not widen the feature-only drain or alter D-008's live-held zero-frontier rule.\n\nRelated: WI-3232, D-008.\n\n### D-010 — Fixed-cohort census is 24 features; count active-wave and rig residue separately\nDate: 2026-08-27\nCORRECTION / RETRACTION (2026-08-27 00:42 EDT): revision 17's Now block described only WI-3985 and WI-3232 and implied the drain could wind down after those two. That was incomplete. The authoritative cohort is the 24 standalone feature IDs in WI-42159's audit artifact. Current fleet claim spec standalone-feature-drain-wave-wi42159 rev 9 admits 19; D-002 excludes five rig/hardware-gated IDs but explicitly keeps them as wind-down residue. An exact work_items:burn_down read over all 24 IDs at 2026-08-27T04:42:26Z returned 15 lifecycle-terminal and 9 nonterminal: in-flight WI-3985; unclaimed WI-4480; blocked/parked WI-3232 and WI-662; plus excluded rig/hardware residue WI-3133, WI-5211, WI-3629, WI-1939, WI-3130. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nAuthored AFTER implementation, against as-built reality. The plan added two ADDITIVE knobs to the goal launch-settings layer, both found by trying to satisfy a concrete owner request and failing. So the acceptance question is not 'does the field exist' but 'does pinning it change the launch, and does NOT pinning it change nothing'.\n\nCriteria are OUTCOMES, each tracing to the goal or a recorded Decision (D-002 unpinned-means-unpinned, D-008/D-009 derive-from-launcher and independent role groups, D-011 one spelling of a vocabulary, D-016 closed-set extension).\n\nTwo anti-faking traps are deliberate, because both are cheap to fake: (1) READ-BACK IS NOT DELIVERY — a setting that reads back correctly proves serialization, not behaviour, so the headed criterion is satisfied only by an observation made from OUTSIDE the API response; (2) A GUARD THAT HAS NEVER FAILED IS UNTESTED — the paired criterion requires a control falsifier showing the assertion fails when the guard is removed.\n\nREVISION NOTE (revision 3). The required vetting consult returned `no_qualified_responder` — all three matched candidates were `ended` and revival failed to spawn — so no external critique was available. Rather than treat an unanswered consult as a pass, I acted on the two gaps I could establish myself. First: the original criteria graded each knob in ISOLATION and nothing graded how a goal pin composes with an explicit caller argument or with the other knob; that gap was real and evidenceable, so criterion 3 was widened from narrow inheritance into the single distinct outcome of PRECEDENCE AND COMPOSITION. Second: every criterion shipped with an EMPTY `driftMarkers`, which is the field the meta-rubric's falsifiability criterion reads; each now names what would make its evidence expire. Recorded because an unanswered vetting step is weaker evidence than an answered one, and a grader is entitled to know which criteria never faced an outside reader.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation acceptance rubric, authored against as-built reality after all three plan items reached terminal and the completion audit recorded 3/3 verified with 18 resolving citations (auditSeq 3, auditedSha 295b1d521aae).\n\nWhat the plan set out to do: collapse a two-valued launch knob ('full' | 'trimmed') to one, so that every agent launch path seeds a small core tool surface and reaches the rest of the ~550-tool catalog lazily through tools:find / tools:invoke, WITHOUT breaking callers who still pass the removed value.\n\nThe criteria are OUTCOMES, not tasks. Three things they are deliberately built to catch, because each is how THIS migration would fail quietly:\n\n(a) A mode can be removed in BEHAVIOUR while the prose that teaches it survives, and the prose is what the next agent believes. So 'docs-match-behaviour' is a first-class criterion, not a tidiness note.\n\n(b) The lazy-catalog claim is only really tested on a client with NO fallback. A Claude client can reach an unseeded tool via its own native ToolSearch even if ?tools= seeding were broken; a Codex client cannot — ?tools= is its only trim lever and it cannot materialize a client-side wrapper mid-session. So criterion 4 names that property (not the vendor) and requires evidence independent of the agent's own self-report, because an agent asserting 'my tool list was trimmed' is exactly the unverified claim this codebase makes you go read the writer for.\n\n(c) REVISION 2, and the reason this rubric changed before it was ever used: criterion 3 originally asked the grader to ENUMERATE launch paths and check each reaches the shared guard. Running my own replication step showed why that instrument is wrong — the plan's Acceptance section named five paths, and the code actually has nine call sites across five subsystems, including four HTTP endpoint routes nobody had listed. An enumerating check cannot fail on the path you forgot to enumerate, which is precisely the path most likely to bypass the guard. Criterion 3 is now a NEGATIVE check: the grader must search for an entry point that reaches psu WITHOUT passing either the normalizer or a schema-level literal boundary, and a pass requires that search to come back empty. I could not fully discharge that myself — see its method — so it is stated as the grader's job, not as a claim I have already settled.\n\nGrader: please spot-check the implementer's audit citations rather than taking the audit's verdicts on trust.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data).
