Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"durable-papercusp-dns-repair-2026-08-27","title":"Durable papercusp.com DNS repair without tunnels","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-27","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Durable papercusp.com DNS repair without tunnels\nslug: durable-papercusp-dns-repair-2026-08-27\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nRestore reliable access to papercusp.com on this machine and make the repair survive tunnel failure, network interruption, service restart, and reboot.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Remove the SSH forwarding service and every papercusp loopback override.\n- Ignore the gateway's DHCP DNS and use authenticated DNS-over-TLS through systemd-resolved.\n- Keep normal direct routing; do not use a VPN, proxy, SSH forward, or other tunnel.\n- Persist the resolver policy across NetworkManager reconnects and reboot.\n- Add a recurrence guard in the repository testing framework.\n- Verify live A/AAAA/HTTPS answers, encrypted transport, direct routing, reconnect persistence, and browser-native ECH behavior.\n- Report the independently verified gateway SNI filter as a separate network limitation for clients that do not support ECH.\n\n## Design\n\nRemove every loopback hostname override and disable the SSH forwarding service. Configure the active NetworkManager profile to ignore DHCP-provided DNS and use authenticated DNS-over-TLS through systemd-resolved, preventing the gateway from forging papercusp.com answers. Validate the resolver answer and preserve normal direct routing. Because the same gateway independently drops TLS ClientHello packets containing papercusp.com SNI, document and verify that DNS is fixed while ordinary non-ECH TLS remains a separate gateway limitation; use browser-native Encrypted ClientHello where supported, never a VPN, proxy, SSH forward, or other tunnel.\n\n## Scope\n\nMachine-local NetworkManager/systemd-resolved configuration, removal of the obsolete SSH/hosts bypass, and canonical repository checks that validate the no-tunnel resolver contract. No public DNS-zone changes and no tunnel or proxy replacement.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** COMPLETE — direct authenticated DNS is live with no VPN/proxy/SSH/tunnel. Papercusp host overrides are removed, the old bypass is masked, NetworkManager ignores DHCP DNS, systemd-resolved uses authenticated DoT, Chrome uses secure DoH + ECH, and path/timer reconciliation repairs drift without restarting healthy DNS.\n\n**Next:** No implementation work remains. Canonical source is waiting for the normal background git-sync; live machine configuration and rollback backup are already in place.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-280398 — Remove the papercusp SSH tunnel and loopback overrides, then configure the active network profile for authenticated DNS-over-TLS with normal direct routing. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-280399 — Make the direct encrypted-DNS configuration persistent across reconnects and reboot, with no loopback pin, VPN, proxy, or tunnel fallback. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-280401 — Add repository-native recurrence checks and verify encrypted DNS, direct route, tunnel removal, reconnect persistence, and browser ECH behavior. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Phase 1 — Repair and verification\n\n- **P-001** `done` Remove the papercusp SSH tunnel and loopback overrides, then configure the active network profile for authenticated DNS-over-TLS with normal direct routing. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-280398 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Make the direct encrypted-DNS configuration persistent across reconnects and reboot, with no loopback pin, VPN, proxy, or tunnel fallback. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-280399 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add repository-native recurrence checks and verify encrypted DNS, direct route, tunnel removal, reconnect persistence, and browser ECH behavior. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-280401 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Retain the loopback override plus remote-resolution tunnel because the LAN gateway forges answers and filters papercusp SNI.\n- Treat listener and HTTPS readiness as health; process existence alone is insufficient.\n\n### D-001 — No tunnel or VPN is part of the DNS repair\nDate: 2026-08-27\nAvi rejected tunnel-based networking explicitly. The earlier tunnel-first design and my NordVPN evaluation were wrong for this request and are retracted. The implementation must remove the loopback/SSH bypass, use normal direct routing plus authenticated DNS, and report the independently verified gateway SNI filter honestly instead of routing around it.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n## Acceptance\n\n`getent` and `resolvectl` resolve papercusp.com to its current public Cloudflare addresses over authenticated DNS-over-TLS; no papercusp hostname resolves to loopback; the SSH bypass is disabled; the route is direct; the policy survives reconnect/reboot; browser ECH reaches the public page where supported; automated checks guard this contract."},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"executable-continuity-checks-acceptance","title":"Executable continuity checks — ship acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-27","owner":"su-8763c39e-583d-48f8-b024-55f4833d08d2","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Executable continuity checks — ship acceptance\nslug: executable-continuity-checks-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-8763c39e-583d-48f8-b024-55f4833d08d2\n---\n\n# Executable continuity checks — ship acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"frozen-candidate-outlives-its-repair-2026-08-27","title":"Let a frozen candidate outlive its repair: stop fossilizing candidates that are actively being fixed","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-27","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Let a frozen candidate outlive its repair: stop fossilizing candidates that are actively being fixed\nslug: frozen-candidate-outlives-its-repair-2026-08-27\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-09-12\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-12. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nFIX LANDED AND VERIFIED (P-002, P-003, P-006 done; commit 50342a6d, verified by blob content not date). Root cause: the fossil pin release fires at green-checkpoint.ts :7729 and nulls the queue, while `decideFrozenCandidateRepairQueue` — which applies DEFAULT_FROZEN_REPAIR_QUEUE_LIMITS {maxAttempts:3, maxAgeMs:4h} — sits ~80 lines LATER inside `if (repairQueue)`. So the queue's own budget was UNREACHABLE CODE past 2h: maxAgeMs could never fire, `blockedReason:'wall-clock-exhausted'` was dead in production. D-004 governs: the fossil rules are a COUPLED PAIR; both hunks landed in one lock hold.\n\n⚠ SCORING MODEL CORRECTED — READ D-007 FIRST; it SUPERSEDES the timing in D-005 and D-006. `frozenPinIsFossilized` has ONE call site (:7729) and is evaluated at RUN START, before the suite — never on a timer. Proof: the 07:23Z log released a pin at line 8 of 193, ahead of the disk preflight, in a run that never reached a suite. So 11:18:46Z / 11:49:23Z / 13:18:46Z are threshold OPERANDS, not moments of death.\n\nP-007 (the remaining open item) IS NOW A LOCK RACE. The 09:24Z run (real gate pid 447809; 447773 is its tsx parent) still holds the run-lock; the 10:16Z fire returned reason 'skipped-locked' and never evaluated the pin, confirming D-007. Queue unchanged all day: candidate d513ccbc, ready-to-test, attempts 0, blockedReason null, updatedAtMs 09:24:23Z. staging tip has moved to 90197e2012; main is STILL a2d69cef (no green landed).\n\nP-001 is blocked on OBSERVABILITY, not effort (reuse is only measurable at attempts>=1), which also blocks the conditional P-004. P-005's remaining half (cargo test) is deliberately deferred: the gate's tasks carry hard timeouts and stall monitoring, so loading the box could time out the very suite that is this plan's acceptance evidence.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Wait for the 11:22:37Z fire (next_fire_at) and read its log's `reason` FIRST: if the 09:24Z run has released the lock by then, d513ccbc is 2h03m old (past the 2h wall) and T−updatedAtMs = 118m ≤ 145m, so the already-landed predicate should HOLD the pin — that outcome is P-007's win condition and closes its live validation; if the log reads 'skipped-locked' no evaluation happened and the next chance is 12:22:37Z. Read updatedAtMs before anything else: if it moved, a run wrote the queue and the stall threshold reset, taking the wedged-writer branch off the table. Do NOT fire release:checkpoint-run — reserved to su-da1ed036 by D-001.)\n\n## Background\n\n### The intended model (owner, 2026-08-27, verbatim)\n\n> *\"if a test run fails because 1/1000 tests fail while the rest passed we should only be rerunning tests that had their files changed since the last run, which should be 0!!!!!!!!!!!!! because we established a freeze and queue system, so we should freeze a tip and just keep getting the tests working on that frozen candidate until they are all working. since the candidate is frozen there should be no changed files and only the failing tests need to be rerun, no?\"*\n\nThat model is correct and is what the code already intends. This plan is about why it does not survive contact with the clock.\n\n### What is ALREADY built — do not rebuild it\n\nVerified by reading the code and the live routine row, not by reading plan statuses:\n\n- `createFrozenCandidateQueue` opens a queue **before setup or suite work**, on every non-diagnostic run, so \"a crash, red verdict, or newer staging tip therefore resumes this exact candidate\" (`green-checkpoint.ts:8189-8210`).\n- `realCheckpointDeps` wires all eight frozen-repair hooks — `readFrozenRepairQueue`, `writeFrozenRepairQueue`, `reserveFrozenRepairFixer`, `prepareFrozenRepairWorktree`, `finalizeFrozenRepairWorktree`, `frozenRepairFixerAlive`, `dispatchFrozenRepairFixer`, `cleanupFrozenRepairWorktree` — spread on `repairTarget` (`green-checkpoint.ts:12711`).\n- `repairTarget = gateVerdictTargetFromEnv()` resolves from `PAPERCUSP_GATE_VERDICT_WORKSPACE` + `PAPERCUSP_GATE_VERDICT_HARNESS`. **Both are set in the live gate process** (read from `/proc/<pid>/environ` on pid 3986353 at 08:31Z), and both the routine path (`release-actions.ts:1159`) and the launcher (`release-checkpoint-launch.ts:1688`) inject them.\n- A queue is **live right now**: `routines.metadata->'repair_queue'` for `green-checkpoint`/`papercusp` holds candidate `ba345f31b1…`, base `a2d69cef50…` (= `main`), `phase: ready-to-test`, `attempts: 0`, opened `08:14:03Z`.\n- Passing-task verdict reuse is marked done as `gate-stop-chasing-the-tip-2026-08-19` P-008 and `stable-candidate-related-gate-2026-08-23` P-002.\n\n### The defect\n\n`CANDIDATE_FOSSIL_AGE_MS = 120 * 60_000`. When a pinned candidate passes it, `green-checkpoint.ts:7660-7688` releases the pin, discards the repair worktree, and judges the current tip instead, logging: *\"released the stable-candidate pin on `<sha>` — it is `<N>`m old, past the 120m fossil threshold, so every red it can still produce would be withheld unpublished.\"*\n\nThe withholding it cites is real (`candidate-fossil`, `green-checkpoint.ts:8717-8730`) and is correct **for a candidate nobody is working on** — a verdict about a long-superseded tree is noise. But the same rule is applied to a candidate that is *under active repair*, where age is the expected cost of the repair rather than evidence of staleness. The clock measures the wrong thing: **commit age, not repair progress.**\n\n### Measured consequence\n\nEvery frozen candidate observed has died to this timer, none to a verdict:\n\n| run | pin released | age at release |\n|---|---|---|\n| 2026-08-27T01:24Z | `96061f5e` | 122m |\n| 2026-08-27T06:30Z | `bd653329` | 147m |\n| 2026-08-27T07:23Z | `bd653329` | 366m |\n\nA single gate run costs ~29–55 min (materialization alone has been observed at 15–20+ min), so a candidate gets roughly one to two repair attempts inside its 120-minute budget. The live candidate `ba345f31` was committed `08:07:27Z`, leaving ~95 min at the time of writing.\n\nThe result is the livelock `gate-suite-speedup-2026-08-12` named on 2026-08-12 and shipped against on 2026-08-13 — *\"every candidate is superseded before its verdict lands and the gate livelocks... Ownership is NOT the constraint. Cycle time is.\"* — reappearing one layer up: the freeze was supposed to stop the target moving, and the fossil timer moves it anyway. `main` has not advanced since `2026-08-20T20:15Z` (46 consecutive reds, 6,280 commits behind).\n\n### Why this was hard to see\n\nNine hypotheses were falsified before this one, several of which looked conclusive: dependency-input drift, mtime/inode fingerprinting, submodule gitlink drift, exit 74/75, stat-token replacement, \"the repair loop was never implemented\", \"the deps are never wired\", \"the env vars are missing\", and \"no queue is ever opened\". The last four were each killed by one direct measurement. Two method traps did most of the damage and are recorded here so the next reader skips them:\n\n1. **Every pot's checkpoint log contains the papercusp *script* path**, so `grep papercusp ~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs/*.log` matches ~20 other pots' runs. Select on the `integration root:` line.\n2. **The persisted queue key is `metadata->'repair_queue'`**, not `frozenRepairQueue`. Querying the wrong key returns a confident, entirely false \"the gate has never frozen a candidate\".\n\n## Phase 1 — Measure before changing\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Measure whether passing-task verdict reuse actually skips unchanged tasks during a frozen-candidate repair VERIFICATION pass. The live queue (`ba345f31…`, attempts 0) has not yet run one, so this is currently unmeasured in production. Capture, for the first repair verification: total tasks selected, tasks skipped by reuse with their hit reason, tasks actually executed, and wall time — against the 110-task/7-failed baseline from the 06:30Z run. This decides whether P-004 is needed at all. importance: urgent — note: Owner-approved consolidation, not satisfied by assertion: exact remaining reuse/selection and freeze-to-terminal evidence transferred to green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08#D-004 and open WI-10001019. Stronger age-free lineage policy supersedes separate timer implementation. No green result is claimed.\n\n## Phase 2 — Stop the clock from killing an active repair\n\n- **P-002** `done` Make the fossil rule measure REPAIR PROGRESS, not commit age, for a candidate with a live repair queue. A pin under active repair (fixer dispatched, verification running, or a phase transition inside the window) must not be released solely because its commit is >120m old. Keep the existing behaviour untouched for a candidate with no repair queue — the withholding rule is correct there. Preserve a hard upper bound so a wedged repair cannot pin the gate forever; make that bound progress-based (e.g. no phase transition within N minutes) rather than absolute age. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-001 — note: Landed: frozenPinIsFossilized is now progress-aware (green-checkpoint.ts). Deferred to the queue's own 4h/3-attempt budget rather than a new timer.\n- **P-003** `done` Reconcile `candidate-fossil` verdict withholding with P-002 so the two cannot disagree: if a repair is allowed to continue past 120m, its eventual verdict must be publishable, or the extension buys nothing. Trace every `candidate-fossil` stamp site and state which of them applies to an actively-repaired candidate. importance: high blocked-by: P-002 — note: Landed as a REQUIRED co-hunk of P-002 (D-004), not a follow-up: extracted isJudgingPinnedActiveRepair() and exempted a live pinned repair from the candidate-fossil verdict withholding.\n\n## Phase 3 — Re-run scope (conditional)\n\n- **P-004** `dropped` ONLY IF P-001 shows reuse is not effective: make a frozen-candidate repair verification re-run the previously-failing tasks plus their transitive dependents, rather than the full affected set. On a frozen candidate the changed-file set between attempts is 0, so a full re-selection is the wrong instrument. Do not add a second selection mechanism — extend the existing proof-group/verdict-cache path (`gate-stop-chasing-the-tip` P-007/P-008). importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: Owner-approved consolidation, not satisfied by assertion: exact remaining reuse/selection and freeze-to-terminal evidence transferred to green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08#D-004 and open WI-10001019. Stronger age-free lineage policy supersedes separate timer implementation. No green result is claimed.\n- **P-005** `done` Handle the two non-vitest failures the 06:30Z run surfaced, which no test-file re-run can clear: `@papercusp/operator-core :: gen:authored-docs:check (no-file-rows)` and `papercusp-desktop :: cargo test (non-vitest)`. Establish whether each is genuinely red at the frozen candidate, and whether the repair loop can even represent a non-vitest task in its failing set. importance: high — note: ← WI-499703 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Guard and validate\n\n- **P-006** `done` Add a falsifiable guard that fails when a frozen candidate is released as a fossil WHILE its repair was making progress. This is the regression that would silently restore today's behaviour, and it is invisible in every existing test because the current tests assert the release happens. Follow the repo's permanent-wrong-control idiom (`sweep-ranking.test.ts`) rather than mutating the shared tree. importance: high blocked-by: P-002 — note: Landed in green-checkpoint-fossil-pin-release.test.ts (its existing dedicated home, not the 11k-line general suite): 18/18 passed, 0 failed.\n- **P-007** `dropped` Validate end-to-end on a real frozen-candidate repair: record attempts, tasks executed vs skipped per attempt, wall time per attempt, total time from freeze to terminal verdict, and whether `main` advanced. Compare against the three fossil releases in Background. A green `main` is the acceptance evidence; anything less is a partial result and must be reported as one. importance: urgent blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-42506 completed (dropped)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Implement progress-aware fossil expiry without touching the live verdict lane\nDate: 2026-08-27\nLane boundary issued by the live WI-40086 holder at 2026-08-27 04:36 EDT. Preserve current fossil-release behavior when no repair queue exists. With a queue, suppress commit-age release only for demonstrably active repair progress and retain a bounded progress-based upper expiry so wedged repair cannot pin forever. Regression coverage must distinguish active progress, wedged progress, and no-queue behavior. The implementation lane may edit owning gate files under this plan, but must not fire release:checkpoint-run, claim WI-40086, mutate or retire the live ba345f31 repair queue, or interfere with its current verdict. The WI-40086 holder retains exact terminal, deploy, and completion control.\n\n### D-002 — Most of the \"failing tests\" are load starvation, not code defects — which makes the frozen-repair fix pay twice\nDate: 2026-08-27\nMeasured 2026-08-27T08:45Z. This materially changes what P-005 is for and strengthens the case for P-004.\n\n#### The gate's own detector says the failures are load artifacts\n\nThe 06:30Z papercusp-rooted run logged:\n\n```\nAFFECTED_TESTS_LOAD_SUSPECT tasks=5 files=14 maxLoad1=261 threshold=40\nAFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT status=failed tasks=110 failed=7\n```\n\n**5 of the 7 failing tasks (14 files) were flagged LOAD-SUSPECT by the gate itself**, at `load1=261` against its own `threshold=40` — 6.5× over. Independently confirmed on the box at 08:44Z: `load average 178.74`, `PSI memory some avg10=55.93`. The gate also logged `PC_HEAVY_ADMISSION status=frozen reason=memory-psi-high` during the 07:23Z run.\n\nSo the majority of the red is starvation, not broken code. Triaging those files as defects is chasing ghosts — and it is a large part of why six days of \"fix the named failing tests\" changed nothing: the names rotate because the *failures* are stochastic.\n\n#### Why this makes the owner's model pay twice\n\nThe intended model (freeze the candidate, re-run only what failed) was justified on **correctness** grounds: on a frozen candidate the changed-file set is 0, so a full re-selection is the wrong instrument. This measurement adds a second, independent payoff: re-running ~7 tasks instead of 110 also **removes the load that manufactures the flakes**. The current design does the opposite — it re-runs the full affected set on every repair attempt, on a box already at 4-6× its own load threshold, which produces fresh false failures, which extend the repair, which ages the candidate into the fossil release. Each mechanism feeds the next.\n\n#### Consequences for this plan\n\n- **P-004 is no longer merely an optimisation.** Even with P-002's fossil fix, a repair that re-runs 110 tasks under load 261 will keep failing on flakes and consume its 3 attempts on noise. Scope reduction is load reduction is flake reduction.\n- **P-005 is narrower than it looked.** `@papercusp/operator-core :: gen:authored-docs:check` is **NOT red**: run at HEAD 08:43Z it exits 0 (\"✓ dry run — nothing written\"). Its 06:30Z failure carried `(no-file-rows)`, i.e. unattributable — consistent with a load kill. `papercusp-desktop :: cargo test` remains unverified and was deliberately NOT run: the box was at load 178 with a live gate suite (pid 3986353), and competing for CPU would manufacture exactly the failure class under investigation. Note `0` commits touched `.rs`/`Cargo.toml` since candidate `bd653329` — the 15 `papercusp-desktop` commits in that range are submodule gitlink bumps — so if it was genuinely red it should still be red, and it must be measured on a quiet box.\n- **A load-suspect task must not be treated as a code failure by the repair loop.** If the repair dispatches a fixer against a starvation artifact, it burns one of `maxAttempts: 3` on a file that was never broken. Worth checking whether `AFFECTED_TESTS_LOAD_SUSPECT` is consulted anywhere in the frozen-repair decision path; if it is not, that is a candidate item.\n\n#### Method note\n\nDo not treat `AFFECTED_TESTS_FAILING_FILES` as a defect list. Per CLAUDE.md it is a FLOOR and a candidate list, and this run demonstrates why: the majority of its entries were flagged load-suspect by the same run that produced them. Re-run each named path individually, on a quiet box, before calling anything red.\nRelated: P-001, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-003 — CORRECTION to D-002: the affected-test failures were a real code defect, not mostly load starvation — I had the causality backwards\nDate: 2026-08-27\n**D-002 is wrong on its central attribution. Read this before acting on it.** Correction owed to su-5fa940bc, who read the deciding code instead of inferring from the load flag as I did.\n\n#### What D-002 claimed, and why it was wrong\n\nD-002 said: *\"the majority of the red is starvation, not broken code\"*, resting on the gate's own `AFFECTED_TESTS_LOAD_SUSPECT tasks=5 files=14 maxLoad1=261 threshold=40`.\n\nThe measurement is real; my inference from it was not. `AFFECTED_TESTS_LOAD_SUSPECT` flags tasks that failed **while load was high** — it is a correlation heuristic, not a verdict that the failure was *caused* by load. I read a co-occurrence flag as an exculpation, which let me conclude \"these files are not really broken\" without ever running one.\n\n#### What was actually wrong (measured, by su-5fa940bc)\n\n`FLAGS.POT_REKEY` is **default-ON**, so `buildHiveRekeyBootDeps` passes its flag-first check and calls `potHomeSlugForHarness()`, which opens a **real Postgres pool**. In a unit test that trips the DB guard and surfaces as *\"Hive re-key boot dependencies failed closed\"*. The fail-closed behaviour is correct; the defect is that unit tests reach that path at all — and the repo convention is explicit that unit tests must not hit live PostgreSQL.\n\nFix used the seam that already existed (`boot.ts:1407 rekeyDepsOverride`) and the convention already present in that directory (`boot.test.ts:49`, the sibling file that passes 60/0, already passes `rekeyDepsOverride: null`). Applied to 34 call sites across 8 files.\n\nVerified green with **zero guard hits**: revocation-propagation 8 failed → 8 passed, reverify-admitted 9/9, swarm-chaos 2/2, admission-pending-retry 7/7, federation-threat-model 4/4 — all `rc=0`.\n\n#### The two facts are compatible, and the order matters\n\nUnit tests opening real PG pools both **fail** and **generate load**. So the load-suspect flag was pointing AT the defect, not excusing it — high load made the PG-touching tests fail more reliably, which is why the failing names rotated. Load is downstream here, not upstream.\n\n#### What survives from D-002\n\n- The `AFFECTED_TESTS_LOAD_SUSPECT` measurement itself (`maxLoad1=261` vs `threshold=40`), and the box readings (load 178, PSI mem 56%). Those are real and still argue that this host is saturated.\n- The P-004 argument that re-running ~7 tasks instead of 110 reduces load: still true, still worth doing, but it is now a **secondary** benefit rather than the fix for these failures.\n- `gen:authored-docs:check` is genuinely not red (exits 0 at HEAD, verified 08:43Z).\n- `papercusp-desktop :: cargo test` remains unverified, and `substrate-sidecar-host.test.ts` has 32 guard hits that this edit cannot explain (no `bootHarnessSubstrate` call site) — so the affected-test leg is **not** green yet, and su-5fa940bc explicitly declined to claim it was.\n\n#### Method note, since this is the second time today\n\nD-002's error is the same shape as four hypotheses I killed earlier: a claim resting on an ABSENCE or a proxy signal rather than on the thing itself. \"The load flag fired, therefore the code is fine\" is not measurement — running the test is. The correct move was available and cheap: run one of the named files individually, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md's gate-triage rule prescribes and what su-5fa940bc did.\nRelated: P-001, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-004 — D-004: the fossil fix is TWO hunks, not one — P-002 alone re-creates the livelock the release was written to break\nDate: 2026-08-27\nMEASURED, by reading the deciding code (green-checkpoint.ts:7616-7688 and :8632-8660), not inferred.\n\n#### The finding\n\nThe fossil pin-release at :7642 that I identified as the root cause is NOT an oversight. A fixer that reliably dies young could therefore keep the pin alive indefinitely while making no progress — the same failure D-008 named, reached by a different mechanism, and *harder* to see because the queue looks like it is advancing.\n\nAttempt 1's fixer lived ~5m26s. Attempt 2's was dispatched 12:23:22Z; whether it outlives its predecessor is now the thing worth watching, and is the observation P-001 needs.\n\nRelated: P-007, P-002, P-001, D-007, D-008\nRelated: P-007, P-002, P-001\n\n### D-010 — D-010: the frozen repair never terminated because the release-fixer first-turn guard killed every fixer at 300s — not because of the queue, staging fixes, or account exhaustion\nDate: 2026-08-27\nSUPERSEDES the framing in D-008 and D-009 on WHY the repair never discharged.\n\nMEASURED 2026-08-27 12:33-12:52Z. Every green-checkpoint release-fixer since 2026-08-24 16:57Z was SIGTERM'd at exactly 300000ms by the release-fixer first-turn guard (orchestrator-runner.ts:689-705, RELEASE_FIXER_FIRST_TURN_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS = 5*60_000). task_ledger, launched_by='orchestrator:release-fixer': 31 'exited' averaging 1118s up to 08-24 16:57Z, then 0 exited and 100% 'timed_out' at ~300s through 08-27. Healthy fixers need ~17min; the guard gave them 5.\n\nThe guard is disarmed ONLY by a stdout chunk that survives extractAgentOutput() (which strips /^\\[20\\d\\d-\\d\\d-\\d\\dT/). WI-3302 then deliberately routed the inner agent CLI's liveness signal to STDERR (OUTER_ACTIVITY_ECHO_MARKER, invoke.ts:4160) — \"never stdout\", because downstream consumers key off exact stdout content. From that point the disarm signal could never arrive and the guard became an unconditional 5-minute kill of a working agent. Verbatim, 12:28:22Z: \"pc-0mtbhuhxzu52y85sfoz.scope: Consumed 1min 53.193s CPU time\" then \"role=release-fixer exited 143 - stderr: release-fixer first-turn timeout after 300000ms (no agent stream)\".\n\nCORRECTS THREE EARLIER CLAIMS OF MINE:\n1. \"attempt 2 had zero indexed turns / did nothing\" — FALSE. It ran 44 assistant turns; its transcript is in ~/.papercusp/flight-recorder/<spawnId>/, which is not indexed, so sessions:read reports 0 turns.\n2. Account exhaustion — NOT supported. The fixer died mid-tool-call with 14.7M tokens left.\n3. The queue is not the defect (already corrected); neither is the spawn-reclaim sweep, which is the CORONER: it found the pid already dead and only marked the row failed.\n\nSECOND DEFECT, independent: spawn-reclaim.ts heartbeatSpawns passed two bare arrays to unnest(), which makes postgres.js throw 'The \"string\" argument must be of type string ... Received an instance of Array'. Reproduced live; sql.array() fixes it. The throw was swallowed by a best-effort catch, so the only symptom was last_output_at staying NULL for EVERY streaming spawn — which reads to every liveness observer as \"silent since launch\".\n\nBOTH FIXED and landed by restarting bg-host at 12:52Z (it runs routines from the staging tree, so this did not require main to advance). Verified: 19/19 in orchestrator-runner-spawn.test.ts including a new production-shape regression case, lint:tsc status=clean on the changed files, and heartbeatSpawns exercised live against PG.\n\nNOT YET VALIDATED: whether attempt 3 at 13:22:37Z runs to completion and commits. P-007 remains PARTIAL until main actually advances off a2d69cef.\n\n### D-011 — D-010: A repair queue whose failure signature is all non-file entries cannot terminate — check the split before treating a fixer as the lever\nDate: 2026-08-27\n⚠ ID CORRECTION: cite this as **D-011**. Its title text begins \"D-010:\" because I wrote that prefix before the allocator assigned the real id; the title cannot be edited in place. D-010 is a different decision — this is D-011.\n\nMeasured 14:23–14:26Z 2026-08-27, scoring P-007 against the live 14:22:37Z tick. This supersedes the exit model assumed by D-007/D-008 and by my own carried predictions.\n\nOBSERVATION. Candidate d513ccbc's repair did not end by being repaired. It ended by being thrown away. Verbatim from the papercusp-rooted gate log (`~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs/2026-08-27T14-23-02-149Z-scheduled-f2a7a039-*.log`, `integration root: /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp`):\n\n  \"failure signature is not fully selectively re-runnable (0 file(s), 0 gate(s), 36 non-file entry/entries); the full canonical suite must decide staging 82e149dd; retired the obsolete exact-patch queue inside the run lock and continuing with the full canonical gate at that exact tip\"\n\nCorroboration: `git log --all --oneline --grep='Repair frozen candidate d513ccbc'` is EMPTY across every ref (no repair commit was ever produced by any of the 3 attempts), and the repair worktree directory was deleted — it was still present at 14:20:42Z at HEAD d513ccbc9b with 33 dirty paths.\n\nTHE RULING. The exact-patch repair worktree is a per-FILE mechanism. A failure signature composed entirely of non-file GATE entries (lint/gen/perf/desktop checks) cannot be discharged by it, at any attempt count, by any fixer. Such a queue is unfinishable from the moment its signature is written.\n\nTherefore, for every lane that touches a frozen candidate:\n\n1. Before dispatching, debugging, or waiting on a fixer, read the failure signature's file-vs-non-file split. `GATE_HELD_BY` is a FLOOR and its COUNT is the less important half — its COMPOSITION decides whether the repair path can terminate at all. Here: 36 entries, 0 of them files.\n2. If the split is all-non-file, the fixer is not the lever and a healthy fixer changes nothing. Expect (and do not fight) retirement plus a full canonical suite at the current tip.\n3. Corollary for anyone clearing reds: when the signature is all-gate, clearing GATE entries — not test files — is what moves the candidate.\n4. Do not read \"attempts climbing / updatedAtMs refreshing\" as progress. Both advanced normally throughout a queue that could never close.\n\nWHAT THIS CORRECTS. Two predictions I carried into this tick were wrong, and both failed the same way — they assumed the exit runs THROUGH the repair: (a) `recover-dead-fixer` → `finalizeFrozenRepairWorktree` producing a \"Repair frozen candidate d513ccbc9b48\" commit (predicted primary); (b) `attempts-exhausted` at the 3/3 cap (predicted risk). Neither fired. It also corrects the causal framing on WI-85288: the release-fixer first-turn-guard defect was real and its fix is proven in production, but dead fixers were never why main was stuck — a comment to that effect is filed on that item.\n\nSCOPE LIMIT — what this does NOT claim. It does not say the repair queue is misdesigned, and D-009's correction stands: the queue observes fixer liveness correctly (`frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts:543,554`). It says only that the queue's INPUT can be of a shape the queue cannot consume, and that nothing today reports that at dispatch time. Whether the gate should refuse to open an exact-patch queue on an all-non-file signature — rather than opening one and retiring it hours later — is a live design question this decision deliberately leaves open.\n\nP-007 STATUS: PARTIAL, unchanged, per D-008. main is still a2d69cef50 (2026-08-20T20:15:14Z), 6471 commits behind staging; gate at 48 consecutive reds, verdict red-stale. A full canonical suite has been in flight on 82e149dd since 14:23:02Z.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-012 — Owner-approved September 12 audit disposition and current execution contract\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAuthority: session_turn:codex:01a0961e-ab11-71f2-bae6-9be0c8401857:32 — Avi approved applying the relevance-audit recommendations and implementing relevant updated plans through verified shipment. This decision adopts the Consolidate disposition.\n\nCurrent contract: The purpose survives, but the stronger current rule removes age-based queue decisions entirely. Its conditional reuse/verification work overlaps later cache, typed-signature and zero-wait plans.\n\nExecution: Carry any genuinely missing operational evidence into those current plans; do not keep a separate timer-extension implementation alive.\n\nMeasured basis: the source/test/decision review and scoped verification recorded in docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md, not a new claim about the live gate. Historical timestamps, candidate references and consumed one-shot permissions below remain historical. Preserve current frozen-lineage invariants and the live-gate ownership boundary. This update does not waive proof, independent grading or acceptance requirements. Track adoption under WI-10001081; retain existing implementation work-items and completed evidence.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"gmail-facebook-history-readiness-acceptance-2026-08-27","title":"Acceptance — Gmail/Facebook history ingestion production readiness","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-27","owner":"su-c9a84b4f-a378-40d5-adca-3c39c5ba9378","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — Gmail/Facebook history ingestion production readiness\nslug: gmail-facebook-history-readiness-acceptance-2026-08-27\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-c9a84b4f-a378-40d5-adca-3c39c5ba9378\n---\n\n# Acceptance — Gmail/Facebook history ingestion production readiness\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nAuthored post-implementation against as-built reality (audit seq 6, sha 065f1af9b9). Revision 3. Rev 2 applied four vetting findings from su-98f41fcf (consult conv-mtbo0jt8): durable-import-contract was a MECHANISM list gradeable only by inspection, so it is restated behaviourally and merged with recovery-determinism into interruption-recovery-determinism (interrupt, resume, diff); privacy-boundary bundled six independently-failing properties under one rating and is split into data-at-rest-and-erasure and access-and-egress-boundary; the missing load-bearing dimension ingestion FIDELITY is added — every other criterion can pass while the vault holds 80% of the mailbox; and 'each defect found' quantified over a set only the implementer can enumerate, so it becomes defects-fixed-at-root-with-guards over defects RECORDED on the plan's work-items. handoff-residue-honesty is kept VERBATIM on the vetter's recommendation: with two owner-walled lanes, making unverified residue a GRADED outcome is what separates shipping from silently shipping something unproven. Rev 3 adds structured tests bindings per meta-acceptance-rubric D-006 so ratings on the objectively-checkable criteria are machine-contradictable. Decision coverage: D-004/D-006→multi-account-identity; D-007→account-attributed-vault; D-009/D-011/D-014/D-015→data-at-rest-and-erasure; D-010/D-012→interruption-recovery-determinism and ingestion-fidelity; D-013/D-016→defects-fixed-at-root-with-guards; D-019→handoff-residue-honesty. D-001/D-003/D-005/D-008/D-017/D-018 are execution-routing and scope-boundary rulings (which fleet, which lane, what is out of scope) that constrain HOW the work was run, not what the shipped system must do, so they are deliberately uncovered by outcome criteria.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"grading-adjacent-tool-truthfulness-2026-08-27","title":"Adjacent tool-truthfulness fixes discovered during grading","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-27","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Adjacent tool-truthfulness fixes discovered during grading\nslug: grading-adjacent-tool-truthfulness-2026-08-27\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n# Goal\n\nMake tool outputs and coordination delivery fail loudly when a caller would otherwise receive a confident-looking false absence or silently truncated action brief.\n\n## Provenance\n\nSplit from `grading-integrity-fixes-from-grading-insights-2026-08-27` Phase 2 after live review showed these are general tool-truthfulness characteristics, not grading-integrity mechanics. Existing EI records remain evidence; this plan is the shared implementation and acceptance surface, not a second defect ledger.\n\n## Scope\n\nTwo independent fixes: structured-JSON projection diagnostics and author-time coordination truncation preflight. The plan remains draft until its complete source conversation is activation-audited.\n\n## Phase 1 — Tool truthfulness\n\n- **P-001** `todo` **Structured-JSON `projection { pipe }` must never produce silent emptiness.** Detect a JSON body before line-oriented pipe operators run and return a diagnostic directing callers to JSON-aware `pick`; a non-matching grep over JSON must never look like a legitimate zero. Preserve and consolidate evidence from original grading-integrity P-005 plus open EI-21438099689448898 and EI-21394548802272910; do not mint another defect record. Acceptance: non-matching `grep` on structured JSON returns a warning, while matching structured selection through `pick` remains unchanged. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` **`coord:send` must preflight load-bearing body truncation.** When `expects != 'none'` and authored structured sections exceed the delivered inbox-body budget, refuse or return a loud author-visible truncation verdict before treating the send as successful; the untruncated summary remains the mitigation, not the hidden contract. Preserve and consolidate evidence from original grading-integrity P-006 plus open EI-21222172196078716 and EI-21178838251225343; do not mint another defect record. Acceptance: an author cannot unknowingly ship a truncated action or answer brief. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Consolidate existing evidence; do not create parallel defects\nDate: 2026-08-27\nThis plan is the implementation-and-acceptance surface for the two general tool-truthfulness defects split from `grading-integrity-fixes-from-grading-insights-2026-08-27` P-005/P-006. P-001 consolidates EI-21438099689448898 and EI-21394548802272910; P-002 consolidates EI-21222172196078716 and EI-21178838251225343. Those EI rows are evidence, not competing implementations. Before activation, dedupe/relate the open EI pairs and activation-audit the full source conversation.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"grading-integrity-fixes-from-grading-insights-2026-08-27","title":"Grading-system integrity fixes drawn from live acceptance-grading sessions","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-27","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Grading-system integrity fixes drawn from live acceptance-grading sessions\nslug: grading-integrity-fixes-from-grading-insights-2026-08-27\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-08-27\n---\n\n# Goal\n\nFix the defects that live acceptance-grading sessions surfaced, BEFORE grading more plans. Every item here comes from a failure actually hit while grading — not from reviewing the code in the abstract. The unifying theme: each one lets a grader be **confidently wrong**, or wastes an entire grade, while every surface reports success.\n\nThe grading pipeline's whole value is that its verdicts can be trusted. Each defect below erodes that in a way the existing gates do not catch.\n\n## Provenance\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-08-27] \"before grading again first make any fixes/improvements from your insights in the last grading sessions. Write a plan for this first and show it to me for my review.\"\n\nEvidence is drawn from this session's grading of `fleet-worker-lifecycle-convergence-acceptance`, plus carried verified checks from earlier grading sessions.\n\n## Scope note\n\nP-001..P-004 are core grading integrity. P-005..P-006 are adjacent tooling defects that materially damaged grading work but are not grading-specific — separable if you want this tighter.\n\n## Dedup note\n\n`plans:new` refused this slug as `similar_exists`; I read the candidates before overriding. All five matches are `acceptance-*` RUBRIC plans for unrelated subjects, matching on shared tokens only. The nearest genuine relative, `acceptance-grading-stall-sweep-2026-08-26` (shipped), addresses graders STALLING (a clock on the independent-grader leg) — not eligibility, audit-finding loss, or commit-position blindness. This is a distinct effort.\n\n## Known related filing\n\n`EI-21623825762343009` (filed 16:21Z today) covers P-001's symptom. It sits in `reviewState: blocked` probation — which is also why a `work_items:list` text search for it returns zero rows. Do not read that zero as \"nothing is filed\".\n\n## Phase 1 — Core grading integrity\n\n- **P-001** `todo` **Grader eligibility must be answerable BEFORE the grade, not only at the terminal write.** Expose `recordedVettingCritics[]` plus a caller-scoped eligibility verdict on `rubrics:get`, computed by the SAME predicate `scorecards:emit` enforces — one shared function, since a second copy is exactly how the two drift. EVIDENCE: I completed a full 7-criterion grade (≈10 targeted code reads, a 21/21 test run, a live two-surface reconciliation, an audit-citation spot-check) and was refused at the terminal write with `grader_is_sole_vetting_critic`. The wasted work is the small cost. The hazard is the TIMING: at the moment of refusal the grade is finished and correct and a peer is blocked waiting, so the cheapest-looking exit is to hand the ratings to an eligible agent to re-emit — which launders a disqualified grade through a compliant card and defeats the guard entirely, while feeling like helpfulness. Moving the check earlier removes that incentive at its source. ACCEPTANCE: a sole-vetting-critic caller sees `canGrade:false` with the same refusal code before doing any grading work, and a test FAILS if the precheck and the emit gate ever disagree. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` **Unresolved audit findings must not vanish from the newest audit.** `plan_audits` seq 6 recorded 0 findings where seq 5 recorded 4 — two of them `disposition:'filed'` with real refs (WI-135860, EI-21619366952853296). Graders read the LATEST audit, so filed findings silently disappear from the very record the grader consults, while the audit contract's stated intent is that a filed finding carries its ref precisely so nothing is silently swallowed. The findings still exist on the seq-5 row, so nothing was destroyed — which is what makes this easy to miss. FIX: carry unresolved `filed` findings forward across `audit_seq`, or surface `openFindingsFromPriorAudits` on the read. ACCEPTANCE: a re-audit cannot produce a findings-empty latest audit while prior filed findings remain unresolved. importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` **Stamp WHAT IS BEING GRADED — worktree vs HEAD vs deployed, per cited path.** A grader who reads live behaviour as evidence about uncommitted code will misgrade it, and the failure is silent. LIVE THIS SESSION: `fleet:audit` returned a bare `adv_sessions-read-failed` — exactly the lossy shape the plan under grade claims to have fixed. It was the OLD DEPLOYED build; the fix existed only in the worktree (blob 380cbd12 vs HEAD 7432fd78, with ZERO occurrences of the new cause-propagating template in HEAD). Reported as a live defect, that would have been a false finding against correct work — and it would have looked well-evidenced. FIX: the acceptance-grading context stamps each cited path's commit position, REUSING `dev:pipeline_position`'s existing resolver rather than standing up a second one. ACCEPTANCE: grading context for a plan with uncommitted cited files marks them uncommitted and names the deployed sha, so a live read can never be silently attributed to worktree code. importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` **`completionAuthority` must not report `committed` vacuously.** With `filesChanged: []` the check ranges over ZERO declared paths and therefore always lands `committed`, regardless of repo state — the value cannot fail, so it carries no information while reading as confirmation. MEASURED the same minute: WI-135520 (empty `filesChanged`) → `committed`; EI-21615102901369580 (2 real paths) → `proposed`, and a blob check confirmed the latter genuinely absent from HEAD. A grader or leader reading `committed` as proof the work landed is trusting a tautology. FIX: emit a distinct value (`no-files-declared` / `unverifiable`) when nothing was declared. ACCEPTANCE: an evidence-only completion never reads as `committed`.\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Adjacent tooling (separable)\n\n- **P-005** `dropped` **`projection { pipe }` over a JSON body must not return silent emptiness.** An MCP JSON result is 1–5 physical lines, so the line operators are all-or-nothing: a non-matching `grep` returns an EMPTY body — indistinguishable from a filter that worked and legitimately found nothing — and a matching one returns the whole payload unreduced. This produced false ABSENCE readings during grading, which is the single most dangerous shape of wrong answer for a grader. FIX: detect a JSON body under `pipe` and emit a diagnostic pointing at `pick`. ACCEPTANCE: a non-matching grep over a JSON body returns a warning, never bare silence. — note: Moved intact to grading-adjacent-tool-truthfulness-2026-08-27#P-001 per D-001; existing EI evidence consolidated there.\n- **P-006** `dropped` **[ADJACENT — cut this if you want the plan tighter] `coord:send` silently truncates the inbox body at 600 chars while returning `ok:true`.** Measured today: 600/2168 and 600/935 chars on messages routing a BLOCKED grade to the peers waiting on it. The `summary` survives untruncated, so the workable mitigation is to put load-bearing content there — but a body silently losing two-thirds of its explanation is how a grading handoff arrives unactionable, and the sender gets a success result either way. FIX: refuse, or loudly flag at author time, when `expects != 'none'` and the body would truncate. ACCEPTANCE: an author cannot unknowingly ship a truncated load-bearing ask. importance: low — note: Moved intact to grading-adjacent-tool-truthfulness-2026-08-27#P-002 per D-001; existing EI evidence consolidated there.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Phase 2 leaves grading integrity\nDate: 2026-08-27\nP-005 and P-006 are general tool-truthfulness defects, not grading-integrity mechanics. They move to draft plan `grading-adjacent-tool-truthfulness-2026-08-27` as its P-001/P-002, which consolidates existing EI evidence rather than creating duplicate issues. The original items are retained as dropped provenance so this decision remains auditable.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-002 — P-001 is canonical; EI-21623825762343009 is evidence until ship\nDate: 2026-08-27\nP-001 is the canonical implementation unit for grader eligibility precheck. EI-21623825762343009 describes the same defect and remains open evidence until P-001 ships; close it as superseded/resolved by P-001 at that point. The precheck and terminal emit gate MUST call one shared predicate, with a recurrence test that fails if their verdicts diverge.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-003 — Historical truth is derived on read; no mutating backfill\nDate: 2026-08-27\nDo not choose between new-only semantics and a mutating historical backfill. For P-002, preserve the write path and derive `openFindingsFromPriorAudits` across all prior audits on read so existing plans immediately regain unresolved filed findings without rewriting cited history. For P-004, return `no-files-declared`/`unverifiable` from the current authority derivation whenever `filesChanged` is empty, including existing records when read; do not rewrite historical completions. Tests cover pre-existing and newly-created rows.\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"loop-wake-reliability-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: loop wake reliability — did the starvation STOP, is it now detectable, and is one loop still one row","status":"active","created":"2026-08-27","owner":"su-4f31ce63-8288-48b9-8f01-614b6ef18f88","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: loop wake reliability — did the starvation STOP, is it now detectable, and is one loop still one row\nslug: loop-wake-reliability-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-08-27\nowner: su-4f31ce63-8288-48b9-8f01-614b6ef18f88\n---\n\n# Acceptance: loop wake reliability — did the starvation STOP, is it now detectable, and is one loop still one row\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nREVISION 2, rewritten 2026-08-27T22:0xZ after vetting critique from su-98f41fcf (consult conv-mtbiyht5-0000-79b606abfb974d8ba5b2a993116ce573, post 78350). Subject plan: loop-wake-reliability-2026-08-24, all 13 items terminal, code-truth audit closed at auditSeq 3 / sha 82e149dd727d2acde30906f4e8741c0f6dfb1812 (13/13 audited, uncoveredItems []).\n\nGRADER, READ THIS FIRST — the critic established that `rubrics:get` TRUNCATES this description and returns every criterion as `_partial` with model/method/driftMarkers omitted, and that `payloadTier:'full'` is ignored. Do NOT grade from `rubrics:get`. Read the real text with:\n  SELECT template_data FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND template='rubric' AND plan_slug='loop-wake-reliability-acceptance';\nCriterion TITLES survive the projection intact, which is why the INVERTED marker is in the title, not only here.\n\nWHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 2, and why:\n- The two \"we changed nothing\" regression criteria (backoff-accounting-unchanged, cadence-alarm-not-ratio-only) are COLLAPSED into one (d002-d003-rulings-respected). They pass by default and could only fail if the implementer broke something they were told not to touch — two of seven slots testing my restraint rather than the plan's outcome inflated the apparent rigor of the card.\n- That freed a slot for the real gap the critic found: NOTHING in revision 1 asked whether the starvation actually STOPPED. Every criterion was structure, regression, detection, or process integrity, so the card could pass in full while loops kept starving, provided the starvation had become visible. \"We made the bug observable\" is not what this plan promised. That is now `starvation-actually-stopped`, and it is the criterion the goal turns on.\n- `starvation-is-system-detected` was falsifiable but NOT SATISFIABLE: it demanded a demonstrated firing and supplied no method to produce one, so the likely outcome was `unknown` — a free abstention that does not block acceptance the way `broken` does. It now names two concrete ways to EARN healthy and makes failure-to-demonstrate cost `degraded`, not `unknown`.\n\nSCALE DISCIPLINE (applies to every criterion): `unknown` means ONLY \"I could not run the check at all\". If you ran the check and it did not produce the evidence, that is `degraded` or `broken`. Abstention must not be the cheap path.\n\nALSO SPOT-CHECK THE IMPLEMENTER'S AUDIT: I both implemented this plan and authored this rubric, so I am disqualified from grading it twice over. Do not take my audit verdicts on trust — resolve a sample of the citations yourself.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"psu-recycle-carry-delivery-truth-2026-08-27","title":"Cold-loop RECYCLE carry-note: make \"delivered\" mean delivered, and find why it wasn't","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-27","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cold-loop RECYCLE carry-note: make \"delivered\" mean delivered, and find why it wasn't\nslug: psu-recycle-carry-delivery-truth-2026-08-27\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-27\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nTwo linked defects in the psu-pty host's cold-loop carry-note delivery, both MEASURED end-to-end on 2026-08-27T00:01–00:06Z (owner-witnessed: the session sat mute until the owner prodded it).\n\n**Why this matters.** A loop armed `carry:'cold'` deliberately discards the agent's context on each wake and rebuilds it from a carry-note the agent wrote to Postgres. The note IS the continuity. If the note does not reach the respawned session, the agent wakes with a persona and no working state, has nothing to act on, and — because nothing prompted it — takes no turn at all. It goes silently mute with an armed loop. That is what happened.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Truthful delivery.** A carry injection may report `delivered: true` and book `respawn-carry-delivered` only after authoritative evidence that the submitted carry text exists as a turn in the newly spawned native session. Pty writes and startup output are diagnostic signals, never delivery proof.\n**R-2 — Honest failure and continuity.** If a cold RECYCLE carry does not become a native turn within the bounded verification budget, the result must carry a distinguishable failure reason, must never be booked delivered, must emit a loud operational event, and must preserve continuity by re-delivering or falling back to the already-proven `carry-respawn` leg.\n**R-3 — Root-cause removal.** Diagnose and remove the mechanism that caused the reproduced RECYCLE miss. Widening a timeout, lengthening the busy-gate wait, or wrapping the broken write in a retry is not an acceptable fix. The known-good carry-respawn behavior must remain unchanged.\n**R-4 — Deterministic recurrence guard.** Tests must reproduce the class through the existing drill seam, fail when a delivery is booked without a corresponding native turn, cover the affected callers, and demonstrate falsifiability with the repository's tier-2 mutation probe against a copy outside the shared tree.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006 | tree |\n\nUse the existing drill and transcript-verification seams instead of creating a parallel delivery system. First reproduce the RECYCLE miss deterministically with `drillId`, `sessionClass`, the shared drill ledger, and native-transcript inspection, recording the busy-gate and child/pty state that explains the missing first turn. Then make `injectTurnAtPrompt` propagate the actual `verifySubmitted` verdict and a stable failure reason, auditing `launchKickoff`, the recycle carry path, and `msg.mode` injection for assumptions about the former always-true result.\n\nFor the recycle path's authoritative success condition, reuse `waitForNativeTranscriptMarker`, already used by the managed session-port kickoff path, and retain `outputSeen` only as diagnostics. Remove the reproduced root cause at its origin. On bounded verification failure, emit a loud event and recover via one controlled re-delivery or the proven carry-respawn mechanism without changing that mechanism's normal behavior. Add repository-native tests around the deterministic seam and prove the regression test's sensitivity with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` tier 2 on an external copy.\n\nTrade-off settled: native-transcript existence is slightly later and more expensive than observing pty output, but it is the only existing signal that proves the semantic contract—an actual new-session turn—and therefore is required before declaring success.\n\n## The two defects\n\n### (1) \"delivered\" is ASSERTED, not VERIFIED\n\n`apps/operator/scripts/psu-pty-host.mjs`, `injectTurnAtPrompt` (defined :3815) writes the carry text to the pty, then:\n\n```js\nif (child === injectChild) {\n  await verifySubmitted(label, { terminateOnExhaustion: terminateOnSubmitVerifyExhaustion });\n}\nreturn { delivered: true, attempts };            // <-- :3899-3901\n```\n\n`verifySubmitted` (:3750) builds a real submit-verifier and RETURNS `verifier.verify()` — a genuine verdict. **That verdict is awaited and then discarded.** `delivered:true` is returned unconditionally on the write path. So `delivered` means \"bytes were written to a pty and we were not superseded\", never \"a turn exists\".\n\nEverything downstream inherits it: :5786 books `respawn-carry-delivered` vs `respawn-carry-dropped` off `carryResult.delivered`, so a total miss is recorded as a success. The sibling `outputSeen` field is no help — it is `childStartupOutput.length > 0`, and a booting CLI always emits startup bytes, so it reads `true` in exactly the failing case.\n\n`psu-pty-discovery.ts`'s `InjectConfirmation` doc already names this failure class (\"…which is how a cold context-reset that never re-execed gets booked `status='delivered'`\"). The host repeats it one layer down.\n\n### (2) The note itself never landed — root cause UNKNOWN\n\nFixing (1) makes the miss visible. It does not stop the miss. Something is still wrong on the recycle carry path and has not been diagnosed.\n\n## Measured evidence (all re-derivable)\n\n- **Note written correctly and INTACT** — `harness_shared.carry_notes`, scope `loop:papercusp:su-7b48e3bf-c482-4727-868b-574c0484e7d8`, 11,421 chars, `updated_ts` 1787788191671 = `2026-08-26T23:49:51.671Z`. The agent did not fail to checkpoint.\n- **Fire #16 at 00:01:44.307Z**, loop `carry:'cold'`. `coldWakeMode(16)` hit the hybrid recycle cadence (`wakeCount % recycleEveryNWakes === 0`, `packages/operator-core/lib/su-cold-loop.ts:98-102`) ⇒ mode `recycle`.\n- **Host events** (`~/.papercusp/psu-pty/su-7b48e3bf-c482-4727-868b-574c0484e7d8.events.jsonl`):\n\n```\n00:01:55.990  host-code-stale          mode:recycle  (loaded 8b3e5874… onDisk a13ba1f3…)\n00:02:02.784  respawned                mode:recycle  nativeId:af6f53e9-1626-40ad-b379-97c00f539a47\n                                       launchContextPath:null  firstPrompt:true  personaRefreshed:true\n00:02:36.048  respawn-carry-delivered  mode:recycle  attempts:1  outputSeen:true\n```\n\n- **`launchContextPath:null` is CORRECT here.** `psu-pty-host.mjs:5332` sets `respawnMode = systemPromptAddendum ? 'carry-respawn' : 'recycle'`; in recycle the note rides as an injected first TURN, not a launch file (`psu-pty-discovery.ts:629-632`). Do not chase this as the bug.\n- **The persona refresh DID happen and is not the note** — `launch-context/session-refresh-su-7b48e3bf-*.md`, 129,554 bytes, mtime `00:01:56.064Z`, containing ZERO carry-note content (grep the note's distinctive phrase `THREE concurrent papercusp gate runs` ⇒ 0 matches).\n- **THE TURN NEVER EXISTED.** Native transcript `~/.papercusp/session-claude/su-7b48e3bf-*/projects/-home-marsh-office-papercupai-workspace-papercusp/af6f53e9-1626-40ad-b379-97c00f539a47.jsonl`: entries 0–2 are metadata only (`type=mode` / `permission-mode` / `atis-latch`); the FIRST content turn is the human owner's typed question at `00:06:28.453Z`. Nothing at all between the 00:02:02 respawn and 00:06:28 — **4m26s of silence with an armed loop.**\n- **CONTRAST — the working leg.** Same owner, two prior cold fires ran `mode:'carry-respawn'` (systemPromptAddendum present) with a real `launchContextPath`, and both delivered:\n\n```\n18:44:48.870  respawned carry-respawn  ->  18:45:23.509  respawn-carry-delivered\n19:27:42.887  respawned carry-respawn  ->  19:28:17.687  respawn-carry-delivered\n```\n\n  `launch-context/carry-su-7b48e3bf-*.md` is still stamped `19:27:40`, untouched by the 00:01 recycle — as expected for that mode. So **carry-respawn works; RECYCLE is the broken leg.** It only fires every Nth cold wake, which is why this presents as intermittent.\n\n## Why nobody caught it\n\nThe agent-side self-check is not deployed. `loop:status` returns no root-level `carryNote` read-back even though staging source emits it unconditionally whenever a loop row exists (`agent-tools/loop/status.ts:74-82,166`) — `:3070` is serving build `6760f8ec31`, stale behind the ~6-day release-gate freeze. Filed separately as **EI-21556430575606216** (dropped). Not this plan's job to fix, but it explains the blind spot, and it means you cannot rely on `loop:status.carryNote` while diagnosing on the live box.\n\n## What good looks like\n\n- A carry-note delivery is booked `delivered` only against evidence that **a turn exists in the new native session** — not pty bytes, not startup output, not a discarded verifier verdict.\n- A cold RECYCLE wake either lands its note or fails **loudly** and recovers (re-deliver, or fall back to the proven carry-respawn leg).\n- A regression guard fails if the class returns.\n\n## Strong proof already exists in-file — reuse it, do not invent one\n\n`psu-pty-host.mjs`'s managed session-port kickoff path already has \"a stronger, independent proof: `waitForNativeTranscriptMarker`\" (see the comment on `verifySubmitted`'s `onExhausted`, :3776-3780), precisely because the TUI-quiet heuristic is not authoritative. The native transcript is also the instrument that PROVED this miss. Reuse that seam for the recycle carry path rather than building a third proof.\n\n## Scope boundary\n\nDo NOT \"fix\" this by widening a timeout, adding a retry around the broken write, or making the busy-gate wait longer. Those are mitigations; the class must be removed. Do NOT change the carry-respawn leg's behaviour — it is the known-good control and the likely fallback target.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-11. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nActivation audit complete against source session af6f53e9-1626-40ad-b379-97c00f539a47 and current plan revision. Requirements, evidence, scope exclusions, acceptance conditions, and six-item implementation sequence are preserved.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Start with P-001 (deterministic reproduction), then use its evidence to drive P-003; P-002 verdict plumbing is independently actionable.)\n\n## Items\n\n- [ ] **P-001** Make `injectTurnAtPrompt` return the real verdict: branch on `verifySubmitted`'s discarded return value instead of `return { delivered: true }` unconditionally, and propagate a distinguishable reason. Audit every caller (`launchKickoff`, the recycle carry path, the `msg.mode` inject at :4803) for one that relied on the always-true value.\n- [ ] **P-002** Reproduce the recycle miss deterministically. Use the drill seam already in the code (`drillId` / `sessionClass` / `carry-drill-carry-delivered` events, `appendSharedDrillLedgerEvent`) rather than waiting for an Nth-wake cadence in the wild. Establish whether `agentBusyGate.waitAtPrompt()` returned not-deferred against a child that could not yet accept stdin, and whether the bytes were written to a pty that no longer existed.\n- [ ] **P-003** Fix the root cause found in P-002. Removal of the class, not a widened timeout. Blocked-by P-002.\n- [ ] **P-004** Book `respawn-carry-delivered` only on native-transcript proof that a turn exists in the new `nativeId`, reusing `waitForNativeTranscriptMarker`. Retire `outputSeen` as a delivery signal (keep it as diagnostics only). Blocked-by P-001.\n- [ ] **P-005** Recovery path: a cold RECYCLE whose carry does not land within budget must re-deliver or fall back to `mode:'carry-respawn'`, and must emit a loud event. Never book `delivered`. Blocked-by P-004.\n- [ ] **P-006** Regression guard that fails if the class returns: a delivery booked `delivered` with no corresponding turn in the new native session must fail a test. Prove it is falsifiable via `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` (tier 2 — point the test at a COPY, never mutate the shared tree). Blocked-by P-004.\n\n\n## Phase — Now\n\n- **P-001** `done` REPRODUCE FIRST. Reproduce the recycle carry miss DETERMINISTICALLY, before changing anything. Use the drill seam already in the code (`drillId` / `sessionClass` / `carry-drill-carry-delivered` / `appendSharedDrillLedgerEvent`, psu-pty-host.mjs:5761-5781) rather than waiting for an Nth-wake cadence in the wild. Establish specifically: did `agentBusyGate.waitAtPrompt()` return not-deferred against a child that could not yet accept stdin, and were the bytes written to a pty that no longer existed? Signature to reproduce: attempts:1, outputSeen:true, ~34s between `respawned` and `respawn-carry-delivered`, ZERO turns in the new native transcript. importance: high — note: ← WI-42313 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Make `injectTurnAtPrompt` (psu-pty-host.mjs:3815) return the REAL verdict: branch on the `verifySubmitted` return value that is currently awaited-and-DISCARDED at :3899, instead of the unconditional `return { delivered: true }` at :3901, and propagate a distinguishable reason. Audit every caller for one that relied on the always-true value: `launchKickoff`, the recycle carry path (:5750), and the `msg.mode` inject at :4803. importance: high — note: ← WI-42318 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Fix the root cause found in the reproduction item. Removal of the class — NOT a widened timeout, NOT a retry wrapped around the broken write, NOT a longer busy-gate wait. Blocked-by the reproduction item. importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-42319 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Book `respawn-carry-delivered` (psu-pty-host.mjs:5786) only on native-transcript proof that a turn EXISTS in the new `nativeId` — reuse `waitForNativeTranscriptMarker`, the stronger proof the managed session-port kickoff path already uses (see the comment on verifySubmitted onExhausted, :3776-3780). Retire `outputSeen` as a delivery signal; keep it as diagnostics only. Blocked-by the verdict-plumbing item. importance: high blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-42320 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Recovery path: a cold RECYCLE whose carry does not land within budget must RE-DELIVER, or fall back to `mode:carry-respawn` (the leg proven working at 18:44 and 19:27 the same night), and must emit a LOUD event. It must never book `delivered`. Blocked-by the native-transcript-proof item. importance: high blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-42321 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Recurrence guard that fails if the class returns: a delivery booked `delivered` with no corresponding turn in the new native session must fail a test. Prove the guard is falsifiable with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` — tier 2 (point the test at a COPY outside the tree; never mutate the shared tree). Blocked-by the native-transcript-proof item. importance: high blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-42322 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Epoch continuation residual\n\n- **P-008** `todo` WI-10002078: reproduce and repair obsolete production carry re-arms holding wake suppression across a newer child epoch; retain must-deliver current carries and clean-boundary/human-input protection. Add suite regression tests of the real controller and successor delivery, inspect runtime generation, and verify affected-host continuation. Governed by D-003, D-004 and D-005. importance: urgent\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-19\nAmendment-Id: wi-42381-r3-verification-check-rev4-approved-209169\nRequest-Hash: 98031ef78d1419a0ec2063ec800efbabb62023ec0634a61747ff1b1682ab0982\nActor: su-b95871ec-a727-44a2-aba7-3cbecfef290e\nReason: Add the missing executable R-3 check required by the existing criterion method so BAR snapshots can bind server-owned check proof.\nApproved-By: su-c99640ad-465d-45ef-b181-fa887c1e2528\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:209169\nApproved-At: 2026-09-19T12:19:55.997Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 30 → 31\nChanged BARs: R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-19\nAmendment-Id: wi-42381-required-layers-rev5-apply\nRequest-Hash: c4c6ec4e4909ca5250ccfb83c945554ff24d2590ff38fa8f7a60006dd25acab5\nActor: su-b95871ec-a727-44a2-aba7-3cbecfef290e\nReason: Declare the concrete test layers required by each existing acceptance BAR so server-owned proof depth can evaluate nested adequacy evidence.\nApproved-By: su-3d6cba40-1afd-43af-b591-85458abd28b5\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:217991\nApproved-At: 2026-09-19T13:40:54.748Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 31 → 32\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-003 — Current runtime evidence shows an unresolved pending-rearm residual\nDate: 2026-09-20\nMeasured: `/home/marsh-office/.papercusp/psu-pty/su-c52cc0fc-3f1d-4ce3-b338-38295629ed95.events.jsonl` contains repeated `wake-turn-deferred-for-pending-respawn` rows, `respawn-rearm-queued`, `respawn-rearm-superseded`, and terminal `respawn-carry-dropped` rows with `reason:\"never-settled\"`; the screenshot `Screenshot from 2026-09-20 10-56-30.png` visibly shows the owner-facing `psu-pty-host: wake turn DEFERRED ... carry-respawn re-arm is pending` diagnostic. The source tree contains a newer implementation than the deployed host, so prior tree tests do not establish live runtime convergence. This decision governs the follow-up runtime-convergence work: verify both source behavior and the release/runtime path, and do not call the residual fixed solely because the staging tests pass.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-004 — P-007 follow-up scope: pending-rearm starvation and stale runtime convergence\nDate: 2026-09-20\nMeasured: the affected owner log contains repeated `wake-turn-deferred-for-pending-respawn` rows after `respawn-rearm-queued`, including terminal `respawn-carry-dropped` reasons `never-settled` and `superseded`; the screenshot shows this diagnostic emitted to the owner terminal. The earlier P-001..P-006 work proves native-turn delivery truth for the tested tree, but does not prove that pending re-arm state converges on a continuously active host or that already-running hosts load the newer host code. P-007 must cover the remaining state-machine/runtime convergence class and link its completion to WI-10002078.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-005 — P-007 acceptance bar\nDate: 2026-09-20\nP-007 acceptance is not satisfied by a source test that only observes `respawned`, `outputSeen`, or an accepted wake. It requires: (a) a bounded state-machine test showing a pending production re-arm eventually reaches delivered or terminal failure and clears the wake suppression; (b) a test showing a continuously repainting fresh successor can accept the carry when its backend-native prompt proof is present; (c) an operational check that the host code generation running for the affected session is the repaired generation or that the stale host is explicitly restarted/replaced; and (d) a current deployment-position read for the repaired paths.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-006 — Additional confirmed residuals from first-hand successor evidence\nDate: 2026-09-20\nMeasured: WI-10002078 comment 514323 records three API errors including a 502 on the first turn after respawn, two parked psu-host wakes, and a distinct cold-wake warning that asserted a 502-terminated turn as completed work. The observation does not establish that the 502 caused the parked wakes. This plan must treat the phantom completed-turn warning as a separate bookkeeping defect, preserve the uncertainty about causal linkage, and add an independent regression bar.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-007 — Carry re-arm invariants for P-008\nDate: 2026-09-20\nMeasured: the unchanged `makeCarryRearmController` uses a Set for `inFlight`, checks `isStale` only inside `if (isDrill && isStale(deliver))`, and awaits `waitIdle()` without inspecting its deferred result. P-008 implementation must: (1) use a distinct unconditional supersession predicate for production carries while keeping production age-based must-deliver behavior; (2) keep in-flight counts correct for overlapping same-owner attempts; (3) preserve human staged input by treating a deferred human gate as a retryable boundary, never recycling through it; (4) clear pending suppression on terminal supersession/drop.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-008 — P-009 acceptance bar for phantom completed-turn warning\nDate: 2026-09-20\nP-009 must prove that a cold successor does not receive `UN-CHECKPOINTED WORK EXISTS` solely because the predecessor's last turn ended in an API/inference error with zero agent-authored tool calls, while a genuine post-note turn with positive tool calls still emits the warning and unavailable evidence does not suppress it.\nRelated: P-008\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-10-11** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nCurrent-revision acceptance contract for pui-agent-context-cockpit-2026-08-26, wholly replaced after the independent WI-42379 critique and D-030/D-031.
