Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation definition-of-done, authored against as-built reality at tree sha 2d3106addae0b5d21d4b6bf09f6c53a541b95357 (completion audit seq 1: 48 citations checked, 15/15 items verified).\n\nThe outcome this plan owes is stated most plainly in D-067, and these criteria trace to it: 'future code regressions may legitimately make a candidate red, but release infrastructure must never again turn one red or one pre-verdict abort into an opaque multi-day freeze. Every scheduled attempt must end in a typed exact-candidate state; stale failures must never masquerade as the current verdict; dead/parked ownership and stranded pauses must self-heal; a real red must reach longest-proven-green-prefix salvage.' Permanent green was explicitly NOT the promise.\n\nTHREE THINGS THE GRADER MUST KNOW BEFORE GRADING, because they bound what any grade here can honestly mean:\n\n1. SCOPE OF THE EVIDENCE PLANE. Every criterion is written to be falsifiable from code and tests at the audited sha. That is deliberate and is the plan's most contested judgement, recorded as D-107: P-009 sat blocked five days and eight closer handoffs waiting on a live gate verdict, which is LIVE_GATE_OPS, while the repo contract says a held or red gate does not block non-final work and a plan item may require deployed main only when it names a deployed-only property. If you believe a criterion genuinely cannot be settled without a live run, say so IN that criterion's evidence rather than passing it on code alone.\n\n2. THE FIELD READING IS NOT GREEN, AND IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN OMITTED. At authoring time the papercusp green-checkpoint gate is red and held-live by su-c8e26e3b under WI-212675, titled 'Re-green current 50-red checkpoint and restore tested/deployed parity'. A 50-red streak is exactly the field shape D-067 was written about, so criterion `typed-terminal-state-and-salvage` must be graded against that reading, not around it. D-067's own distinction is between a legitimate red (permitted) and an OPAQUE freeze (forbidden): judge whether the current streak is typed, exact-candidate-attributed and owned, or opaque. Neither author nor grader may enter that lane to find out; it has a sole live owner.\n\n3. THE SALVAGE MECHANISM IS GRADED EXPLICITLY, NOT IMPLIED. An earlier revision of this rubric had seven criteria none of which named longest-proven-green-prefix salvage, even though D-067 names it as the recovery half of the guarantee and D-062/D-063/D-064 record that it had THREE independent suppressors (pre-verdict aborts, the repair queue returning terminal upstream of it, and a budget check whose error grew with the radius it existed to shrink). That was a hole a grader could have passed the plan through while the named mechanism stayed suppressed. It is closed by folding salvage into criterion 4, which now fails if salvage is unreachable.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan cloud-workspaces-guided-rail-2026-08-28, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. The plan rebuilt apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces as the owner-chosen guided rail: a persistent left rail carrying 01 Connect / 02 Configure / 03 Operate with per-step status, one stage on screen at a time, and Operate as the landing step once a workspace exists. Criteria trace to the plan's Goal, its ## Requirements (R1-R11) and its Decisions: D-002 (the roving-tabindex radiogroup contract extracted to ONE shared primitive rather than a fourth hand-rolled radiogroup), D-003 (the hosted session mounts inside the expanded host panel — a deliberate re-expression of a pinned invariant, not a drop), D-004 (Configure's empty state kept as a component-level guard while the user-facing invariant moves to the routing layer), D-005 (the narrow-width readability invariant re-expressed by the rail-collapse and type-floor tests). The heaviest criterion is C6: the redesign changes presentation and must not quietly relax any safety behaviour the pre-redesign suite pinned.\n\nREVISION 2 — what changed and why. Vetting via consult:get_feedback returned no_qualified_responder (three matching peers, all `ended`; revival refused because the top candidate reads live at the pty host), so the vetting questions were answered by self-review and the rubric was revised rather than left as first drafted. The substantive change is the live-verification criterion. As first written its only hard signal was the script's exit code, and its own driftMarker admitted the hole: 'a green run whose assertions all SKIPped'. That is not hypothetical — every such assertion is fixture-dependent, so a run against an empty install can SKIP its way to exit 0 and look identical to a real verification. The criterion now requires the grader to read the machine-readable CW_RAIL_RESULT coverage line and to REFUSE a pass when `exercised` does not name the data-dependent assertions. C6's method was also hardened from 'diff the suite' to a named, runnable procedure a non-implementer can execute without trusting the implementer.\n\nREVISION 3 — TWO CHANGES, BOTH RAISED BY THE INDEPENDENT GRADER, NEITHER OF THEM A WEAKENING.\n\n(1) A defect in the rubric itself, found the expensive way. C7 declared check: { kind:'tests', files:['scripts/verify-cloud-workspaces-rail.sh'] }. That path is correct as C7's human-run METHOD and invalid as an automated tests-check: scorecards:emit routes every RATED criterion's declared files through the Vitest router and refuses any file the run did not report on, and the router cannot report on a .sh (TEST_FILE_UNSUPPORTED_INPUT / NON_TEST). Because every criterion must be rated, no rating value skipped it — the rubric was UNGRADEABLE and the plan could never reach shipped. The grader hit this at emit time, after completing the entire grading. The obvious repair was to DROP C7's check block, and rubrics:propose correctly refused that as a silent loss of deterministic enforcement. So the check was REPOINTED instead, at a new real Vitest suite — apps/operator/lib/verify-cloud-workspaces-rail-contract.test.ts — which pins the script's contract: the exact CW_RAIL_RESULT printf format, the three data-dependent `exercised` tokens, the absence of any unguarded negative, the nonce+presence fusion inside settle(), read-only-ness asserted against COMMENT-STRIPPED source, and fail-on-failures. Those are precisely the properties C7's method previously asked every future grader to re-verify by hand. The suite was proven falsifiable by copy-out mutation probe (verdict=caught, tree byte-identical afterwards), following the repo's 26 existing verify-tauri-headless-*.test.ts guards. C7's model, method and driftMarkers are UNCHANGED from revision 2, so ratings produced against revision 2 remain valid. The class fix — validating routability at propose time so the cost lands on the author instead of a grader at ship time — is tracked as WI-369566.\n\n(2) C6 was made STRICTER, not looser, in response to its own degraded rating. The grader's C6 procedure surfaced two undeclared gaps. The first, a dropped narrow-width readability test, is now declared as D-005 and listed among the qualifying re-expressions. The second was not a paperwork gap at all: the redesign had introduced a <main> landmark at page.tsx nested inside the router's <main data-route-transition-page>, where the pre-redesign page had none, and the assertion that would have caught it was dropped in the rewrite. That was a real accessibility defect; it was FIXED (WI-370245), not declared away. C6's model and driftMarkers now name the landmark invariant explicitly so the class cannot return unpinned. Raising the bar and then meeting it is the intent; a grader should treat any criterion that got EASIER between revisions as the thing to scrutinise, and none did.\n\nKNOWN, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED MID-GRADE: the CW_RAIL_RESULT `exercised` field is derived from fixture preconditions rather than from assertions that actually reported PASS (the stronger grep_pass() derivation is defined and never called). Filed as EI-21680639474041670 rather than silently patched, so the grader's C7 evidence stays valid against the script it actually ran.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"learning-tab-improve-retain-clarity-2026-08-28-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — Learning tab: de-duplicate Improve vs Retain, unify the table chrome, clarify the loop section","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-28","owner":"su-21bb3977-f695-464c-a792-c3cc65dfb478","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — Learning tab: de-duplicate Improve vs Retain, unify the table chrome, clarify the loop section\nslug: learning-tab-improve-retain-clarity-2026-08-28-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-28\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-21bb3977-f695-464c-a792-c3cc65dfb478\n---\n\n# Acceptance — Learning tab: de-duplicate Improve vs Retain, unify the table chrome, clarify the loop section\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Treat the peer-review leg as UNAVAILABLE, not performed.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"nonblocking-test-materializer-2026-08-28","title":"Non-blocking test and materializer admission","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-28","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Non-blocking test and materializer admission\nslug: nonblocking-test-materializer-2026-08-28\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-28\nupdated: 2026-08-31\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** DRAFT — baseline captured; implementation route is self-executed under owner-directed AUTO mode.\n\n**Goal:** Let focused and broad test suites make honest progress without blocking release materialization, while preserving a trustworthy release verdict.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-361470 — Specify the parent/child AdmissionContext, idempotency, receipt lifecycle, demand accounting, and lock ordering for test and materializer paths. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-361471 — Implement a reusable governed test-process adapter by extending the existing resource-governor execution seam; queue durably under pressure, propagate context, and release/cancel on every exit path. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-361472 — Integrate affected-tests/test-files process starts with the adapter while retaining focused-lane routing and honest progress/terminal markers. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-361473 — Audit and narrow materializer locking to correctness-only target boundaries; prove no governor lease is held while waiting for a lock. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-361474 — Add unit tests for demand construction, queue/receipt lifecycle, cancellation, worker-exit classification, and no-false-green behavior. <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-361475 — Add integration/stress coverage for PSI backpressure, materializer contention, focused-lane coexistence, and measured actual-demand release. <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-361476 — Run the focused seam suite on settled HEAD, then the conservative broad sweep, and finally the fresh canonical root `npm test`; preserve complete logs and terminal markers. <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-361477 — Document rollout/rollback and record completion evidence; leave the capless-governor P-016/P-018 migration cross-reference for remaining subsystems. <!-- P-009 -->\n## Background\n\nThe forced canonical run acquired its ordinary slot while the materializer intent and writer locks were free, then encountered repeated memory-PSI freezes, Vitest worker exits, and load-suspect retries. The run was terminated through its own preemption monitor and is not a verdict. A bounded focused baseline passed the pc-heavy and resource-governor seam tests, but its provenance became unknown because HEAD moved during the run.\n\nThe materializer is the release/checkpoint preparation process: it creates an isolated pinned checkout and dependency generation. Its intent/writer locks are correctness fencing, not a host-wide capacity budget.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Route build/test residency through the existing capless Governor.admit contract with CPU, memory, disk, and process demand; persist a receipt under pressure and release measured actual demand.\n- Keep materializer correctness fencing narrow (target/release-root/dependency-generation), acquire it just in time, and never hold a governor lease while waiting on that lock.\n- Preserve the focused lane for `test:file` and explicit `--changed-paths` verification; broad diagnostic runs must support an explicit conservative worker/task envelope.\n- Treat PSI freezes as backpressure and worker exits/timeouts as red or undetermined evidence; never convert either into a green result.\n- Retain the final acceptance requirement: one fresh canonical root `npm test` with non-empty Vitest and Cargo execution evidence, exit 0, and no unhandled errors.\n- Do not bypass release-gate ownership or force a red gate; do not add a parallel admission system.\n\n## Design\n\nUse the existing resource-governor execution/queue seams and `testing:run` patterns. The test runner submits one parent `build`/`process` admission for each resident test process, propagates the typed AdmissionContext to children, and exact-releases or cancels the receipt on exit. The scheduler remains responsible for test correctness and progress markers; the governor is responsible for residency. The materializer continues to serialize only its target swap/copy boundary.\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline and contract\n\n- **P-001** `done` Record the forced baseline, exact logs, resource vector, and non-verdict disposition; publish the operator-facing runbook command for focused and conservative broad runs.\n- **P-002** `done` Specify the parent/child AdmissionContext, idempotency, receipt lifecycle, demand accounting, and lock ordering for test and materializer paths. — note: ← WI-361470 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Implementation\n\n- **P-003** `done` Implement a reusable governed test-process adapter by extending the existing resource-governor execution seam; queue durably under pressure, propagate context, and release/cancel on every exit path. — note: ← WI-361471 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Integrate affected-tests/test-files process starts with the adapter while retaining focused-lane routing and honest progress/terminal markers. — note: ← WI-361472 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Audit and narrow materializer locking to correctness-only target boundaries; prove no governor lease is held while waiting for a lock. — note: ← WI-361473 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Regression coverage\n\n- **P-006** `done` Add unit tests for demand construction, queue/receipt lifecycle, cancellation, worker-exit classification, and no-false-green behavior. — note: ← WI-361474 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Add integration/stress coverage for PSI backpressure, materializer contention, focused-lane coexistence, and measured actual-demand release. — note: ← WI-361475 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Validation and rollout\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Run the focused seam suite on settled HEAD, then the conservative broad sweep, and finally the fresh canonical root `npm test`; preserve complete logs and terminal markers. — note: ← WI-361476 released\n- **P-009** `done` Document rollout/rollback and record completion evidence; leave the capless-governor P-016/P-018 migration cross-reference for remaining subsystems. — note: ← WI-361477 completed (done)\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Focused tests never wait on the ordinary materializer slot domain.\n- A pressured broad run queues or runs conservatively and emits explicit progress; no worker-exit or timeout path can be read as passed.\n- Materializer correctness remains protected without a host-wide capacity semaphore.\n- All new tests pass, and the final canonical run exits 0 with non-empty Vitest and Cargo markers and no unhandled errors.\n\n## Decisions\n\n- The existing capless governor and testing:run execution seams are extended; no parallel governor or bespoke state store is introduced.\n- The forced canonical baseline is evidence of resource contention and an incomplete verdict, not proof of a source regression.\n\n### D-001 — Materializer exclusivity is DERIVED from the selector's `reused` verdict at every call site — never hardcoded\nDate: 2026-08-29\nThe whole-box `pc-heavy.sh --exclusive-all-slots` barrier is a correctness requirement ONLY when the dependency-generation selector had to PUBLISH a fresh generation on this run. A REUSED generation is immutable and content-addressed, so materialization only copies it into the caller's own private root — parallel-safe across pots. Every materializer call site must therefore compute `!selectedDependencyGeneration.reused` rather than splice the flag in unconditionally.\n\nThis restates D-033 (WI-42329) and extends it from one site to the CLASS, because applying it site-by-site is exactly how it was lost: D-033 landed on `setupTree` and the structurally identical `prepareFrozenRepairWorktree` kept the unconditional literal, silently, because nothing failed when it did.\n\nThe missed site was strictly worse than the one D-033 fixed: the frozen-repair path runs ONLY while the gate is already red, so a host-wide hold serialized every pot's hourly gate at the moment throughput matters most — the same shape D-033 measured (3 acquired / 16 starved-after-900s over 40 runs, `main` frozen 6 days).\n\n`reused` is advisory and degrades to `false`, so an absent or unparseable selector verdict keeps the CONSERVATIVE exclusive hold. Narrowing must never be reached by guessing.\n\nRecurrence is now guarded structurally rather than per-site: `green-checkpoint-real-deps.test.ts` asserts NO line in `green-checkpoint.ts` is a bare `\"--exclusive-all-slots\",` argv element, with a calibration floor so the scan cannot go vacuous.\n\nMeasured: grep -nE for a bare `\"--exclusive-all-slots\",` argv line in apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts — HEAD 44bd1318a3: 1 hit (line 13210, inside prepareFrozenRepairWorktree); post-fix working tree: 0.\nMeasured: grep -c for the conditional spread in the same file — HEAD: 1; post-fix: 2 (green-checkpoint.ts:13234 and :13802).\nMeasured: both call sites obtain `.reused` from the same selectPrewarmedDependencyGeneration (green-checkpoint.ts:12899-12988), so the value was already in scope at the missed site and simply unread.\nMeasured: testing:run over green-checkpoint-real-deps.test.ts + green-checkpoint-crash-result.test.ts + green-checkpoint-self-watchdog-result.test.ts — 158 passed / 0 failed (runId e1692960-f188-4d16-8fa1-7c760765b4c2).\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-002 — P-007 narrows to ONE gap: three of its four concerns are already covered, at the layer where they actually live\nDate: 2026-08-29\nP-007 was written as four integration/stress rigs (PSI backpressure, materializer contention, focused-lane coexistence, measured actual-demand release), sized at ~600-900 lines. A pre-implementation coverage audit shows THREE are already covered by live, behavioral, non-skipped tests. Writing the planned four rigs would have duplicated existing coverage rather than adding any.\n\nLoad-bearing correction: PSI freeze/thaw and lane admission do NOT live in the TypeScript resource-governor. They live in `scripts/pc-heavy.sh` (bash), whose guard suite is `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/pc-heavy.test.ts`. Anyone scoping this from the TS tree alone will conclude the coverage is missing. It is not — it is one directory over.\n\nMeasured: `wc -l apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/pc-heavy.test.ts` = 4123; `grep -cE 'it\\.skip|describe\\.skip|\\.skipIf'` over it = 0 (the only `skipIf` hit is a comment at :334), so every citation below is a live test.\n\nCOVERED (verified by reading the test BODIES, not the titles):\n\n1. PSI backpressure — pc-heavy.test.ts:2072 \"freezes lower-priority roots deterministically, preserves the release gate, and thaws one per quiet window\" drives the real freeze->thaw cycle with concurrent real processes. Measured: it writes a PSI value file and passes it as `PC_HEAVY_MEM_PSI_OVERRIDE_FILE`, the seam at pc-heavy.sh:455-467, whose own comment says the dynamic file is \"first for tests ... to model pressure -> recovery in one run\". Also :2205 (bounded-lease termination when pressure never recovers) and :1988 (PSI halves the memory budget).\n\n2. Materializer contention — Measured: pc-heavy.test.ts:358 (exclusive materialization drains a live holder), :495 (ordinary holders yield their whole child group), :1301 (no slot squatting during a drain), :1470 (concurrent exclusive materializers serialize rather than split the slot domain). D-001's derivation rule is separately pinned by green-checkpoint-real-deps.test.ts:2382 (D-033 reused-vs-fresh) and :3626-3765 (the P-005 guard, which documents its own falsifiability).\n\n3. Focused-lane coexistence — Measured: pc-heavy.test.ts:1357, :1417, :2045, :2257, :3510, :3552, :3603, :3651 cover focused test:file / scoped test:affected / scoped lint:tsc holding an independent bounded lane while exclusive materialization or the gate reserve clamps the ordinary pool.\n\nTHE ONE REAL GAP — measured actual-demand release:\n\nThe chain is sampler peak -> settle -> execution.finish(actualDemand) -> governor.release -> durable PG receipt. Both ENDS were covered and the MIDDLE was not. Measured: P-006's `governed-test-process.test.ts` injects a stub `executionApi` (:94-:160), so it never reaches a governor or a database; `queue.integration.test.ts:215` persists an exact actual-cost release but from a hand-supplied `{ databaseConnections: 3 }`, never a measurement.\n\nWhy it matters: the miss is SILENT by construction. `createGovernedProcessDemandSampler.stop()` settles as `memoryBytes: extra ?? peakRss ?? planned?.memoryBytes` (governed-test-process.mjs:280), so a run whose measurement failed writes the PLANNED RESERVATION into the receipt and is indistinguishable, in the durable row, from one that measured correctly. A governor learning reservations it invented is not learning anything.\n\nRESOLVED: closed by `packages/operator-core/lib/resource-governor/governed-test-process-demand.integration.test.ts` — 2 tests, real child process, real procfs sampling, real bridge/execution/governor, real Postgres receipt; only the DB connection is substituted. Measured: 2/2 passing; proven falsifiable by two in-tree mutation probes on different assertion families (drop `peakRss` from the sampler fallback -> caught; flip the worker-exit cancel branch to a release -> caught, with test 1 still passing so the two families are independently falsifiable). Both probes restored the tree byte-identical.\n\nRULING: P-007 is satisfied by the gap test above. Its coverage claims for (1)-(3) are discharged by citation, not by new rigs. P-008's focused seam suite should include pc-heavy.test.ts and green-checkpoint-real-deps.test.ts in its evidence set, since those are where three of P-007's four acceptance concerns are actually demonstrated.\n\n### D-003 — \"Settled HEAD\" is the wrong instrument for P-008 — the runner's three-state provenance verdict already supersedes it, and a READER must hash before acting on a read\nDate: 2026-08-29\nDate: 2026-08-29\nP-008 says \"run the focused seam suite on settled HEAD\", and Background explains why: the earlier focused baseline's \"provenance became unknown because HEAD moved during the run.\" That diagnosis names the wrong variable, and acting on it literally (freezing git-sync for the duration) would have frozen fleet-wide commits for nothing.\n\nVitest reads the WORKING TREE, not HEAD. git-sync commits the tree periodically while peers EDIT it continuously between commits. So a HEAD freeze gives a stable commit POINTER while the bytes under test drift underneath.\n\nBOTH halves were measured during run 1, in one window (p008-logs/drift-samples.tsv):\nMeasured: 02:17:02 HEAD moved ccab18efbd -> eaedbad5c6 while the 16-file tested surface hash held constant at b1a229a6185a. A HEAD move is therefore NOT sufficient to invalidate a run => freezing HEAD is NOT NECESSARY.\nMeasured: 02:17:32 and 02:18:02 the surface hash moved (b1a229a6185a -> 22d9153fed34 -> b39a8c7574ff) while HEAD held constant at eaedbad5c6. Content drifts with HEAD frozen => freezing HEAD is NOT SUFFICIENT.\nMeasured: the drifting file was scripts/affected-tests.mjs, three distinct blobs in ~4 minutes (b2d911c8 -> 8dbe2573 -> 1bcfd90b).\n\nTHE INSTRUMENT ALREADY EXISTS — do not build a new one.\nMeasured: scripts/test-files.mjs:1419 emits `head=<sha> uncommittedPaths=<n>/<m> provenance=<verdict>` on every TEST_FILE_RESULT line, and provenanceResultFields() resolves three states: 'drifted' (a tested path changed mid-run), 'unknown' (HEAD moved, or a path's state is unknowable), 'stamped' (clean).\nMeasured: its doc comment at test-files.mjs:1355-1366 already reasons this through more carefully than P-008's phrasing — a HEAD-only move is deliberately 'unknown' and explicitly \"NOT a clean bill\" because \"this runner measures only the named test files, not their import graph\"; and drift deliberately does NOT change the exit code, because turning a correct green red on a DIAGNOSTIC signal would make it a false-RED generator, citing 2026-08-12 when six consecutive gate reds were all stale tree churn and zero were standing defects.\n\nRULING for P-008 and P-009: quote the runner's own `provenance=` verdict as the provenance evidence. Do NOT hold locks:acquire_resource on git-sync to \"settle HEAD\" for a test run; it costs the whole fleet its commits and buys a weaker guarantee than the stamp you already get free. A `provenance=drifted` or `provenance=unknown` result is reported as such and NOT read as a clean verdict.\nMeasured: run 1a closed `status=passed head=ccab18efbd uncommittedPaths=0/8 provenance=stamped` because it finished ~02:16:30, before the 02:17:02 HEAD move; run 1b carried head=eaedbad5c6 uncommittedPaths=0/1 provenance=stamped. Both are attributable without any lock ever being taken.\n\nRESIDUAL GAP, stated so nobody reads the stamp as more than it is: the stamp covers the NAMED paths only, never their import graph. scripts/affected-tests.mjs — which runs 2 and 3 EXECUTE — is exactly such an unmeasured module, and it was the file drifting. Confirm it is byte-stable before launching a broad or canonical run; a run launched mid-rewrite of its own runner is not attributable to any version.\n\nTHE READER-SIDE HAZARD, which neither instrument catches and which nearly produced a fabricated defect report:\nMeasured: reading scripts/affected-tests.mjs with `sed -n '440,470p;525,555p'` DURING that rewrite returned a readMemAvailableMb() whose entire body was `process.exit(78)`, flatly contradicting its own doc comment (\"Returns null (not 0) when the reading is unavailable\"). It read as a serious stubbed-out-function defect and was one step from being filed as one.\nMeasured: the real body reads /proc/meminfo and returns null on failure; the observed text was a splice of two versions read while the file was rewritten under the reader.\nThe splice was SYNTACTICALLY COHERENT and told a plausible story, so nothing about it looked like corruption. The provenance stamps cannot help here — they describe the file the RUNNER executed, not the bytes a READER observed.\nRULE: before acting on, quoting, or filing anything from a source read on this tree, `git hash-object <file>` before and after the read. Two different hashes mean the read is attributable to no version and must be repeated. This is the cheap general defense against the whole class.\nRelated: P-008, P-009\n\n### D-004 — WI-361476 broad verification requires a fresh exact-HEAD, clean-file, pressure-safe release\nDate: 2026-08-30\nWI-361476 may launch its broad/canonical verification only after the fleet leader verifies the current staging HEAD, confirms the named runner/test files are clean and unlocked, and reads state:host.memoryPressure as ok. A prior release is void after any HEAD change, dirty/locked target, or pressure regression. While void, preserve the focused passing evidence, launch nothing, checkpoint, and compact; a cold successor requests a new bounded release from the new live state.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"own-tui-full-divorce-2026-08-24-corrective-acceptance","title":"Own TUI corrective agent-chat acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-28","owner":"su-829ffa14-57da-4930-9ab9-b95d3d6ad44d","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Own TUI corrective agent-chat acceptance\nslug: own-tui-full-divorce-2026-08-24-corrective-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-28\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-829ffa14-57da-4930-9ab9-b95d3d6ad44d\n---\n\n# Own TUI corrective agent-chat acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nRelease-gating acceptance for the verified Phase 6 own-TUI candidate: current interactive shell, canonical operator/store rendezvous, installed-binary native agent-chat journey, owned-loop substrate, parity evidence, and PSU/PUI command separation. Phase 7 remote/shared-substrate scope is preserved intact in pui-remote-shared-substrate-2026-08-28 under D-041.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"probe-staging-first-guard-2026-08-28","title":"PROBE — live falsifiability check of the staging-first activation guard (supersede after use)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-28","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: PROBE — live falsifiability check of the staging-first activation guard (supersede after use)\nslug: probe-staging-first-guard-2026-08-28\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-28\nupdated: 2026-08-28\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-28. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nThrowaway probe plan created by su-d086df30 on 2026-08-28 to prove the staging-first activation guard REFUSES a non-final main wait on the running server, not merely in unit tests. Supersede immediately after the probe.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Attempt activation and record the refusal.)\n\n## Background\n\nThis plan exists only to be rejected. P-001 deliberately gates a non-final implementation item on green main / :3070. P-002 and P-003 are the two forms the guard must still accept.\n\n## Phase 1 — Implementation\n\n## Phase 2 — Shipment\n\n- **P-002** `todo` Final shipment verification: once the gate is green, deploy main to :3070 and confirm the shipped build answers. importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Confirm auto-rollback on the deployed host. This is a deployed-only property because staging cannot exercise the release checkout's rollback path. importance: normal\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Release\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Implement the widget bridge and close it only after the green-checkpoint gate is green and main has deployed to :3070. importance: high — note: Probe positive-control step: this item existed only to be refused by the staging-first guard, which it was (staging_first_guard_failed / non_final_deployed_main_wait). Dropped so the re-audit can show the SAME plan passing once the offending non-final main wait is gone — proving the guard discriminates rather than refusing everything.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"pui-tui-tab-audit-2026-08-27-acceptance","title":"PUI/TUI 21-surface audit acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-28","owner":"su-26a92ed3-a953-4030-b8d7-8055c43bac72","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: PUI/TUI 21-surface audit acceptance\nslug: pui-tui-tab-audit-2026-08-27-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-28\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-26a92ed3-a953-4030-b8d7-8055c43bac72\n---\n\n# PUI/TUI 21-surface audit acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27","title":"Restore canonical test-suite startup and green end-to-end verdict","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-28","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Restore canonical test-suite startup and green end-to-end verdict\nslug: test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-28\nupdated: 2026-09-19\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-19. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nImplementation repairs are recorded; P-004 remains the shared authoritative verification/acceptance obligation. September 12 owner-approved audit reconciliation: D-028 and the current exact-lineage policy govern verification identity; old current-HEAD or hand-cut wording is historical while a frozen queue exists. The existing live gate/original tracker driver retains execution ownership. Actual Vitest/Cargo execution, truthful terminal outcome and the current evidence contract remain mandatory.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. Both were got wrong on this plan — by me, twice — and each wrong reading cost a run or a wrong root cause.\n\n**1. pc-heavy SIGSTOPs; it never uses the cgroup freezer. `cgroup.freeze` cannot observe a pc-heavy freeze.**\n\nMeasured: `grep -n 'kill -STOP\\|kill -CONT' scripts/pc-heavy.sh` → `:885 kill -STOP -- \"-${_preempt_child_pid}\"`, thaw at `:906` and `:1026` `kill -CONT`. I twice reported \"freeze/thaw is FALSIFIED, 476 cgroup.freeze files scanned\" and both reports were invalid on this basis; retracted 06:20Z. **The probe is `ps -o stat=` (T) or the emitted `PC_HEAVY_ADMISSION` records — never cgroup.freeze.**\n\n**2. `PC_HEAVY_MEM_PSI_MAX_FREEZE_SEC` is a KILL LEASE, not a stall bound.**\n\nMeasured: `sed -n '836,850p' scripts/pc-heavy.sh`. When `now - _psi_frozen_since >= _psi_max_freeze_sec` (`:506`, default 300) the code does NOT thaw and resume. It writes record `expired`, emits `expired memory-psi-high-timeout`, and sets `_expire_frozen=1`. The in-code comment states the intent directly: \"once that lease expires, terminate its process group and return an explicit undetermined result instead of leaving affected-tests suspended until its much later outer watchdog fires.\"\n\nConsequence for P-004: a PSI-stopped canonical run is counting down to TERMINATION WITH `undetermined`, not merely running slowly. Per D-006 `undetermined` is not a verdict, so such a run **cannot satisfy P-004** and must not be graded `fail` either. Recovery is the only other exit: PSI ≤ `_psi_recover` sustained for `_psi_recovery_sec` → `kill -CONT` (`:906`).\n\n**3. Elapsed time cannot tell you which is happening.** `:886` resets `_psi_frozen_since` on every `kill -STOP`, so a run CYCLING stop/thaw refreshes its lease each cycle and can stall far past 300s without ever expiring, while a continuously-frozen run dies at the cap. These are opposite outcomes with identical wall-clock signatures. Ruling this once, because 14 files were red and more than one is this shape.\n\nThe worked case: presence-contract.test.ts pinned EI-20231966513487176's removal of `ownerIds` from coord:presence. presence.ts then RE-ADDED `ownerIds` as the documented compatibility alias for the bounded `owners` selector — the exact parallel of the `ownerId` -> `owner` alias the same guard explicitly blesses — with mutual-exclusion validation and normalization to the canonical selector before lookup.\nMeasured: `TZ=UTC git log -1 --date=iso-strict-local -S'ownerIds: z' -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/presence.ts` => 2026-08-30T17:46:08+00:00 f1c460c2a3 (+28/-4); the guard test's own last touch was 2026-08-26T15:38:09+00:00 e59dabaa76. The code change is the NEWER and more complete expression of intent: schema entry (presence.ts:120), description in two places, validation (presence.ts:167-179), normalization (presence.ts:199).\n\nRULING: honor the newer contract and re-pin the guard to it. Concretely, `ownerIds` moves from the guard's removed-list to its alias assertions; `harness`, `plan`, `includeStale`, `include_stale` stay pinned removed.\n\nTHE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE OUTCOME: a guard in this state is usually already half-broken, and the failing half hides it. Here the schema assertion failed loudly while the guidance assertion PASSED FOR THE WRONG REASON — it only required the description to CONTAIN the string \"ownerIds\", which a sentence introducing it as a valid alias satisfies exactly as well as one naming it removed. Deleting the failing line would have shipped a guard that asserted nothing about this key in either direction, and it would have looked green. So the rule is: when you re-pin, STRENGTHEN the surviving assertions to the new contract (require the alias be documented AS an alias; require both `owners` and `ownerIds` to be declared, so the alias cannot be dropped silently either) and state in the file why the pin moved. A guard that goes green by losing a claim is worse than the red it replaced.\n\nBOUNDS: this ruling authorizes re-pinning a guard to a newer deliberate contract. It does NOT authorize bumping a ratchet/baseline guard to admit a newly-introduced offending site — for those (child-output-guard, pure-lane-unbounded-sync-spawn, undrained-stdout-exit-guard, tool-data-shape-ratchet) the correct fix remains fixing the SITE, and the baseline is shrink-only. Distinguish them by asking whether the code change was a considered contract change or an accidental new offender.\n\n### D-026 — Do NOT pull the Cargo percent-floor bypass: it is OFF the critical path, and drift-chasing gets a measurable stopping rule\nDate: 2026-08-31\nRULING (su-062dd71e, fleet leader). Two decisions, both prompted by su-respawn-c64c6507 escalating rather than self-authorizing — which was the correct call.\n\n1) THE CARGO BYPASS LEVER STAYS UNPULLED — for a scheduling reason, not a safety one, so the reasoning is falsifiable.\nPERCENT_FLOOR_BYPASS_GB (scripts/lib/cargo-result.mjs:151, added under EI-21901389541963783) would admit Cargo below the 128 GiB absolute floor. It is NOT pulled, because Cargo admission is a SECONDARY blocker: test:lane-pure is genuinely RED at HEAD 760d18be8f (14 of 18 attributed files, per-file TEST_FILE_RESULT stamps, executed=1 matched=1), so P-004 criterion (a) `exit 0` fails whether or not Cargo is admitted. Pulling a lever whose own comment requires \"verified, measured peak Cargo working-set data\" — against ~37 GB STEADY-STATE data explicitly not verified at peak — buys ZERO schedule and risks filling a filesystem at 95% used that also hosts the fleet and the owner-s two RUNNING VMs. Risk with no upside is not a trade.\nThis DEFERS, it does not foreclose. Revisit when lane-pure is green and the run is otherwise ready: at that point the bypass is the only thing between us and a verdict, the peak working set can be measured honestly, and the trade becomes real. EI-21901389541963783 is already needs-human and stays the owner-facing surface.\nMeasured: disk reclaim is a proven TREADMILL — 12.7 GiB freed from pure caches took free space 102.7 -> 115.4 GiB, and ten minutes later df read 98.3 GiB, BELOW the start. `docker volume prune` returned 0B against an advertised 11.73 GiB. df at 03:40:54Z: 91G free, 95%. The 128 GiB floor is unreachable by reclaim; nobody should spend further turns trying.\n\n2) LANE-PURE REDS ARE THE CRITICAL PATH, WITH A STOPPING RULE.\nThe 14 are repo-wide INVARIANT GUARDS reddened by drift from OTHER lanes (presence-contract: ownerIds is back in coord:presence-s declared schema; check-generic-independence: @papercusp/sync depends on private @papercusp/debounce-coalesce) — small, real, separately-owned regressions, not flakes. Fix forward, and file each against its owning lane so the drift is attributed rather than silently absorbed.\nTHE RISK THIS CREATES, NAMED: P-004 requires a canonical root run at exit 0, i.e. the WHOLE tree green, on a tree ~100 agents commit to continuously. That is a moving target, and grinding it indefinitely is the failure mode. STOPPING RULE: measure reds-fixed against new-reds-appearing across two consecutive cycles. If drift outpaces repair, STOP and escalate the CRITERION rather than grinding — do not quietly weaken it, which is the same goalpost-moving refused in (1).\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-027 — Lane reds are classified by failure LATENCY; the 2026-09-02 lane reds were real, and their owners have since fixed them\nDate: 2026-09-02\nSupersedes the working caveat that \"a red in a full-lane run is uninterpretable under fleet load\". (Run-7's starvation: 45s deadlines, ~46.7s waits.)\n- millisecond-scale failures with ZERO DbCallDeadlineError -> a REAL red at HEAD, load-independent. A 1ms assertion failure cannot be pool starvation.\nBefore accepting any \"this is unmeasurable under load\" caveat, ask which OBSERVABLE would discriminate; here it was milliseconds vs seconds, already in the log.\n\nWHAT THE RUN MEASURED (answers D-039 item 3: yes, still red — and NOT load-shaped).\nMeasured: lane test:lane-stateful, task 0mtjo6dkbji09o21l58, log .papercusp/scratch/bash-115d5a58-0a3.log (1,008,913 B). Marker `===EXIT_STATEFUL:1` at log line 8531. Totals: Test Files 4 failed | 2011 passed | 5 skipped (2020); Tests 11 failed | 31247 passed | 26 skipped | 3 todo (31287). DbCallDeadlineError 0; Unhandled Rejection 0; no failing assertion slower than 23ms (probe for /[0-9]+s$/ on failing lines returned empty).\n\nTwo false positives future readers will hit in this same log, both harmless: the 212 \"pool\" hits are the WORD inside test NAMES (\"account-pool snapshot\"), and all 4 \"ECONNREFUSED\" hits sit inside a PASSING test's name (\"...no real PG, no ECONNREFUSED console.warn\", green at 356ms).\n\nTHE WRAPPER EXIT CODE LIED. capability:bash reported exit_code 0 while the lane's own marker was 1. Read the in-log EXIT marker, never the outer wrapper code — same class as a `cmd | grep | head` pipeline whose trailing stage owns the exit status.\n\nTHE FOUR RED FILES WERE NOT THE GATE'S REDS. capacity.test.ts, coordination/messages.park.test.ts, coordination/messages.role-live-delivery.test.ts, __tests__/affected-tests-budgeted-scheduler.test.ts. The fixes are genuine mock repairs, not silencing: `git show | grep '^+' | grep -E '\\.skip|\\.only|\\.todo|xit\\(|xdescribe'` is empty across all three commits, and the capacity repair deliberately preserves the real poolVerdictByProvider because a `() => []` stub would make pool-snapshot assertions pass VACUOUSLY.\n\nBOUNDARY ON THIS EVIDENCE — do not overread it. C6 still needs a fresh full run from a PINNED worktree; this decision closes the question of what those 11 failures were, not the question of whether the lane is green.\n\n### D-028 — SUPERSEDES D-017 while a frozen repair queue exists: P-004 must test the existing repairHead, never recut from staging/current HEAD\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-07\n\nSUPERSEDES D-017 for every P-004 execution while a frozen green-checkpoint repair-queue row exists. The caller must not be trusted to select the SHA. Carry/checkpoint text directing selection of staging/current HEAD is a lineage violation, not merely advisory prose.\n\nTracked root-cause fix: EI-22577614615643288.\nRelated: P-004, D-009, D-017, D-024, frozen-candidate-stays-frozen-through-all-fixes-2026-09-03\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-029 — Acceptance criteria bind 1:1 to Requirements bars; R-5 and R-6 are uncovered and need new criteria\nDate: 2026-09-09\n[self-imposed, MEASURED 2026-09-09 by su-1f1d56da against the real seed builder — not inferred]\n\nCONTRACT (read from packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-seed.ts, buildAcceptanceBarSeed): the acceptance-BAR seed emits EXACTLY ONE criterion per Requirements bar (`criteria = requirements.bars.map(...)`), and `legacyCriterionMap` must map every R-N to every existing outcome criterion ONE-TO-ONE. Two criteria cannot share a bar: `existingByBar` is a Map keyed by barKey, so a duplicate silently collapses and one criterion's authored prose is LOST. Adopting WITHOUT legacyCriterionMap is worse — with no barHash on a legacy criterion the builder takes the `seeded` branch and replaces all six hand-authored criteria with auto-generated bar text. legacyCriterionMap is therefore the only path that preserves the graded identity, outcome, falsifier and METHOD.\n\nMEASURED COVERAGE of the six criteria at rubric rev 8 against R-1..R-6 (plan v58):\n- R-1 <- cargo-admission-reach (strong)\n- R-2 <- admission-policy-not-loosened AND reclaim-bounded-and-safe (the hard-floor half and the producer-owned-reclamation half of ONE bar)\n- R-3 <- named-reds-green-at-head AND sweep-residue-dispositioned (the 'fixed at its owning contract' half and the 'or proven transient' half of ONE bar)\n- R-4 <- canonical-verdict-trustworthy (strong)\n- R-5 (existing runner, shared-box admission controls, staging-only workflow, live-gate single-owner boundary preserved): NO criterion. C2 and C3 each cover roughly a quarter of it.\n- R-6 (partial-run evidence retained and reused only while valid; unchanged passing tasks reused, failed and dependency-changed tasks rerun): NO criterion. Nothing in the rubric grades evidence REUSE at all.\n\nRULING. The rubric is amended so each bar has exactly one criterion that genuinely grades it: merge the C2/C3 pair into one R-2 criterion and the C4/C5 pair into one R-3 criterion BY CONJUNCTION (both assertions preserved verbatim in the merged model and falsifier - a merge must not drop a guard), and author genuinely new criteria for R-5 and R-6. Only then is legacyCriterionMap an honest bijection.\n\nREJECTED ALTERNATIVE: forcing a bijection out of the six criteria as they stand (e.g. C3->R-5, C5->R-6). A dry run proved this PASSES - action legacy-backfill, rev 8->9, barSetHash null -> bfd89d8739c6. That is exactly why it is refused: the gate validates the bijection's SHAPE and never its MEANING, so it would stamp barSetHash certifying coverage of R-5 and R-6 that does not exist, and an independent grader reading barKey R-6 would grade partial-run evidence reuse against a criterion about sweep residue. This is the 'all items terminal is not a finished plan' failure wearing the bar contract's own badge.\n\nNOT REJECTED BY THIS DECISION: the plan's Requirements. R-1..R-6 are the plan's authentic six outcomes (v58 re-grammared the pre-existing numbered list; the outcomes were not invented). Requirements are not to be trimmed to fit the evidence that happens to exist.\n\nCOST ACKNOWLEDGED: this is a rubric edit, so it invalidates the vetting attestation and any independent grading. That cost is already sunk - the migration itself reports invalidatesPriorProof:true - and the plan carries a standing REJECT on C6 and cannot ship regardless, so this is the correct moment to batch revisions before requesting independent grading.\n\n### D-030 — SUPERSEDES D-029's remedy: decompose the two compound bars instead of merging criteria (8 bars, 8 criteria)\nDate: 2026-09-09\n[self-imposed, MEASURED 2026-09-09 by su-1f1d56da. Corrects D-029 the same hour it was written, before any lane acted on it.]\n\nD-029's DIAGNOSIS STANDS: the seed emits exactly one criterion per bar, legacyCriterionMap must be a strict bijection, the gate validates the bijection's SHAPE and never its MEANING, and R-5/R-6 are genuinely ungraded. Do not force a false 1:1.\n\nD-029's REMEDY IS WITHDRAWN. It prescribed merging C2+C3 into one R-2 criterion and C4+C5 into one R-3 criterion. Reading the full criterion bodies shows that merge would destroy deliberate design:\n- C4 grades its count as an explicit FLOOR ('a legitimately ADDED test must not fail this criterion'); C5 grades its counts as explicit EQUALITY ('a mismatch in EITHER direction falsifies it'). One merged criterion cannot hold both rules coherently.\n- C3 carries an explicit EVIDENCE SEPARATION clause forbidding reuse of C1's aggregate green, and grades four NAMED protective cases individually. C2 grades CONSTANTS, deliberately independent of whether admission currently passes.\n- C2 and C3 are the plan's two NEGATIVE guards. Collapsing two independent guards into one rating coarsens exactly the criteria whose whole value is separability.\n- An independent scorecard (EI-21876170289465633, su-129e288a) already grades C1-C5 PASS / C6 FAIL by these keys. Merging or renaming destroys that grading's referent; preserving the keys lets it be re-attested rather than re-derived.\n\nREQUIREMENTS ARE AUTHENTIC AND ARE NOT TO BE TRIMMED. plan_revisions seq 6 (su-2b2cea02, 2026-08-28 03:33Z) states requirements 1-5; seq 7 (same author, 04:17Z) deliberately ADDS requirement 6, partial-run evidence reuse. Plan v58 only re-grammared that list into R-N form. So R-5 and R-6 are the plan author's own requirements, not an artifact of the grammar repair, and folding or dropping either is out of bounds.\n\nRULING. Decompose the two COMPOUND bars into their already-separately-graded halves, and author one new criterion for each currently-ungraded requirement. Target shape, 8 bars to 8 criteria, every existing criterion preserved byte-for-byte with its key intact:\n  R-1 entrypoint reaches every selected task            <- cargo-admission-reach (existing)\n  R-2 hard free-space floor retained                    <- admission-policy-not-loosened (existing)\n  R-3 reclamation producer-owned, inactive, minimal     <- reclaim-bounded-and-safe (existing)\n  R-4 exposed failures fixed at their owning contract   <- named-reds-green-at-head (existing)\n  R-5 exposed rows dispositioned or proven transient    <- sweep-residue-dispositioned (existing)\n  R-6 verdict non-vacuous and HEAD-bound                <- canonical-verdict-trustworthy (existing)\n  R-7 runner and operational boundaries preserved       <- NEW criterion to author\n  R-8 partial-run evidence reused only while valid      <- NEW criterion to author\nOld R-2 and old R-3 are each compound ('retain a floor WHILE reclaiming only...'; 'fixed at its owning contract OR proven transient'), so splitting them is a faithful refinement into atomic bars, not a scope change. The Bar-to-work map is rewritten to match.\n\nACCEPTED COSTS, stated rather than hidden. (1) Bars renumber, so any external reference to 'requirement 5/6' by number must be re-read against the new list; the TEXT of every original requirement survives. (2) Eight criteria exceeds the '3-7 outcome criteria' guidance in rubrics:propose. That guidance is prose in the tool description and is NOT code-enforced (no max on the criteria array). It is knowingly departed from here because the 1:1 rule makes criteria count a DERIVED quantity: once the plan states eight atomic requirements, eight criteria is the only truthful count, and trimming to seven would mean declining to grade a requirement. That tension between a fixed criteria-count guideline and a bar-count-driven contract is worth raising against the contract's own design rather than absorbing silently.\n\n### D-031 — Proof-depth floors and structured checks for all 8 acceptance BARs (rubric rev 11)\nDate: 2026-09-09\nDate: 2026-09-09\nAuthor: su-1f1d56da (rubric author / implementer). All three are P-001 admission BARs and that file carries the matching describe blocks ('native-suite admission reclaim reaches its own producer output (P-001)'; 'cargo disk admission' + 'disk admission measures the mount Cargo writes to'; 'bounded inactive artifact reclaim' + 'isolated Cargo target cleanup').\n- R-4 -> tests: the six operator-core P-002 reds. THREE are confirmed verbatim by D-003 (unreachable-tier-mock-guard.test.ts, pot/wake-coherence.test.ts, inference-gateway/launch.test.ts); the other three (report-cargo-tests, affected-tests-tree-drift, affected-tests-budgeted-scheduler) are the remaining fully-qualified operator-core test paths named in the plan body. Every path was verified to resolve on disk. If one of these was NOT among the six named reds, the check is BROADER (stricter) than the BAR, never weaker — the safe direction for an acceptance bar.\n- R-7 -> tests: report-cargo-tests.test.ts + affected-tests-tree-drift.test.ts (affected-runner selection and failure labelling are what 'canonical runner preserved' means operationally).\n- R-8 -> tests: affected-tests-tree-drift.test.ts + affected-tests-budgeted-scheduler.test.ts (partial-run evidence retention and its invalidation on tree drift).\n- R-5 and R-6 -> {kind:'instrument', instrumentKey:'none'}, the SANCTIONED explicit-manual contract (evaluator :245). R-5 grades a written disposition/classification and R-6 grades a canonical root run's admissibility; neither is a vitest file set, and fabricating one would be a false check. The good ledger-backed evidence is to be RE-BOUND at spec revision 2. R-1 already has ledger-backed unit proof (bindings 3232/3233, adequacy.testLayer=unit, pathReachable=true), so correct-layer passes under this floor.\nApproved-By: su-000a4d8f-cb58-4327-aee1-b37c4f2a6e94\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:202661\nApproved-At: 2026-09-09T14:36:05.323Z\nRubric revision: 10 → 11\nSubject plan revision: 64 → 65\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-034 — The \"missing rubric\" ship blocker is a STALE-BUILD artifact; the real blocker is 8 ungraded BARs\nDate: 2026-09-11\nAny agent trying to ship this plan will read a ship-gate refusal that names the WRONG cause. Do not act on it without the A/B below.\n\n**What the gate says depends on which BUILD answers you.** Agent MCP calls are proxied to :3070, the RELEASE checkout, pinned to green `main`. `main` has not advanced since ~2026-09-06 (25 consecutive gate reds), so :3070 runs a build that predates the acceptance-gate fix by 5 days.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-11T19:32Z, identical `plans:get { slug, mode:'meta', shipReadiness:true }` issued against both ports in the same minute, only the build differing —\n- `curl 127.0.0.1:3070/api/health` → sha `e66be3c4ff` → `acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready: bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_author_verdict_missing`\n- `curl 127.0.0.1:3170/api/health` → sha `ef98790de6` (staging HEAD) → `acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready — 8 of 8 BAR(s) blocking, 0 clean: R-1: grading_missing; R-2: grading_missing; R-3: proof_inadequate, proof_missing, grading_missing; R-4: grading_missing; R-5: proof_inadequate, proof_missing, grading_missing; R-6: proof_inadequate, proof_missing, grading_missing; R-7: proof_inadequate, proof_stale, grading_missing; R-8: proof_inadequate, proof_stale, grading_missing; contract-level: bar_hash_mismatch, vetting_stale, author_verdict_missing`\n\n**`rubric_missing` is false and the code already knows it.** The rubric exists and resolves: `harness_shared.harness_plans` row `test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27-acceptance`, template='rubric', status='active', version 11; the subject plan pins it (`acceptance_bar_rubric_slug`='test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27-acceptance', `acceptance_bar_rubric_revision`=11, `acceptance_bar_epoch`=1, cohort='legacy-backfilled', seeded 2026-09-09T14:41:01Z by su-1f1d56da). The current build enumerates its 8 BARs (R-1..R-8), which is only possible if the rubric resolved.\n\nMeasured: `packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts` lines 705-730 and 762-770 carry the P-002/D-002 fix — a pinned-but-unresolved rubric must report `bar_snapshot_rubric_unresolved`, never `rubric_missing`, and an unresolved rubric has an UNKNOWN bar set, not an empty one. Its own comment names this exact symptom: \"measured together as `bar_set_empty, rubric_missing` against a rubric that was active with six criteria at the time.\" That fix landed 2026-09-07T19:03:30Z in 2b71df785eef7c2dd5658fbe1a3cf9fc381c47eb, one day AFTER the green pin :3070 still serves.\n\n**Consequence — the repair the stale refusal implies is wasted work.** It reads as \"seed or restore the plan's canonical acceptance rubric.\" The rubric and the seed both already exist; re-seeding accomplishes nothing and the refusal does not move. At least one agent (this one, via its own carry-note) already planned a full wake around that wrong repair.\n\n**The actual work to ship this plan**, from the current build: every one of the 8 BARs needs GRADING; R-3/R-5/R-6 need proof attached; R-7/R-8 carry stale proof; and at contract level the bar-set hash must be reconciled, vetting re-run (stale), and an author verdict recorded. The pre-epoch acceptance chain recorded in ## Now (independent card EI-21876170289465633, author REJECT EI-21876530880766219) does not satisfy the BAR contract — it predates the epoch and the plan revision has since moved to 65.\n\nProof for several BARs still bottoms out on P-004's green canonical root `npm test` (exit 0, non-empty Vitest and Cargo counts), which is not reachable while the tree is red. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for converge-frozen-candidate-by-fix-only-admission-2026-08-27, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality.\n\nWhat the plan actually is: two halves that must be graded differently. The FIRST half (P-001..P-006) is an OPERATION performed by hand on a live frozen candidate — blob-compare the verdict-named failing files, prove an admission set is fix-only, build the admission commit by git plumbing, advance the repair worktree, read the next verdict. Its evidence is artifacts (a commit sha, a worktree state, a verdict reading), not source paths; the completion audit records eight of the twelve terminal items as `not-code` for exactly this reason. The SECOND half (P-007..P-013) is durable engineering that must survive the operation: discoverability at the moment of failure, a shared-tree collision guard, the freeze-and-converge default's off switch and observability, and the salvage-reachability follow-on.\n\nWhy the criteria below are shaped the way they are. This plan's own history is the argument for them. A salvage defect on this exact code path survived a 15/15, 48-citation completion audit and a plan decision (D-108) asserting it was already fixed, because every assertion in front of it was an EXISTENCE assertion — 'the helper is defined', 'the partial-green code is present' — which passes against completely inert code. So criteria here ask whether a behaviour is REACHED, whether a switch is REACHABLE, and whether a claim is distinguishable from an inference; they deliberately do not ask whether code exists.\n\nOne criterion (live-gate-ownership-was-respected) grades process rather than product. It is here because the plan's terminal state depends on it: D-011 ruled P-006 out of this lane precisely because a second agent on a held gate is waste, and a plan that had greened main by duplicating another agent's live lane would have satisfied its goal by violating the rule that makes the goal safe to pursue.\n\nGrading note for whoever takes this: P-006 is expected to be non-terminal or externally owned at grading time. That is not an unfinished item to hold against the plan — it is the recorded consequence of D-011. Grade what this lane did with the constraint, not whether main is green.\n\nOUTCOME FLOOR — stated explicitly, because a grader who is not told will silently supply one. This rubric deliberately carries NO outcome floor. It does not ask whether convergence actually OCCURRED — whether any single candidate was observed to shrink across an admission round. That exclusion is deliberate and load-bearing: D-011 ruled P-006, the round that would demonstrate it, out of this lane, and P-005's own record states the before/after comparison CANNOT be made because the readings span different candidates and populations. So D-005's shrink property — the loop's only stopping condition — was not observed end-to-end on a single candidate by this lane. A passing card here certifies that the METHOD was built, made durable, honestly recorded, and pursued without crowding a held gate. It is NOT evidence that a frozen candidate converged, and no later reader may use it as that.\n\nREVISION NOTE (2026-08-29T18:52Z): incorporates a third-party vetting critique (su-4cecd7f8, comment on WI-769750 at 18:43Z) and one factual defect reported by grader su-062dd. Six criteria carry a VETTING AMENDMENT; the sharpest was that `freeze-and-converge-is-switchable-and-legible` checked only that the flag's READ SITE is reached, reproducing at the flag layer the exact existence-vs-effect error this rubric was built to prevent — and, separately, pointed at the wrong file for that read. Every criterion now carries its replication drill in the `replication` field as well. Neither peer wrote criterion text; su-4cecd7f8 deliberately did not read the item closures or audit citations.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation definition of done, authored against as-built reality, then REVISED after vetting critique from su-3ad55b09 (consult conv-mtdtfhx0). Provenance: code-truth audit seq 2 at tree sha 1880c066b79e65767b59527983a8d3fb5cd3919f — 23 citations checked, 11/11 items covered, 7 verified by code/test, 4 recorded not-code (P-001 ratification, P-004 issue re-scope, P-006 governance, P-010 validation run).\n\nWHAT THIS PLAN PROMISED: the gate must stop judging a moving target. A red candidate is frozen and repaired forward rather than re-cut at the tip; a verdict names exactly one tree; per-run triage becomes a shared machine-readable artifact; and the passing-task verdict cache is reused conservatively, both during repair verification and at the root `npm test` entry point.\n\nWHAT IT DID NOT PROMISE, and must not be graded on: a permanently green gate; reuse across DIFFERENT agent sessions (undemonstrated on purpose, tracked on WI-595883); and confirmation of the unstable-closure-hash hypothesis, which is still UNOBSERVED and has only ever been produced by a deliberately planted control — a grader must not record it as confirmed, nor fail a criterion for its absence.\n\nCHANGES MADE IN VETTING, so the grader can see what was challenged: (1) the old shared-triage criterion bundled two independent mechanisms and was the only one anchored to a work-item rather than a Decision — it is now NARROWED to queryable per-file outcomes, anchored to the new D-011, with its replication pinned to a concrete run group instead of 'a recent gate run' (an unpinned empty result was ambiguous between 'stamping is broken' and 'nothing was red', i.e. a zero that reads as a pass). Log-line trustworthiness is now explicitly OUT of contract per D-011. (2) The cross-run-reuse criterion was the most diff-restating of the set; it is re-cast as its OUTCOME — a reused verdict must be indistinguishable from having actually run the task — with the env-key specifics demoted to method, so a rename or relocation cannot fail a criterion the system did not regress. (3) A criterion was ADDED for the reviewer's strongest finding: every original guard pointed one way (do not chase the tip) and nothing guarded the symmetric failure of never catching up to it. (4) The two 'prove the instrument fires' criteria were merged, since they grade one shared epistemic property, which kept the set inside the 3-7 band.\n\nDECISION COVERAGE, inverted deliberately: D-001/D-002 -> criterion 1; the freeze-bound invariant -> criterion 2; P-002 -> criterion 3; D-011/P-003 -> criterion 4; D-005 -> criterion 5; D-007/D-008/D-009/D-010 -> criterion 6; P-009 -> criterion 7. Three Decisions intentionally have NO criterion: D-003 and D-006 are governance/retraction records with no shipped behaviour to observe, and D-004 is a time-bound coordination ruling for one release attempt rather than a lasting product guarantee.\n\nKNOWN UNCOVERED, disclosed rather than hidden: the reviewer raised a lower-confidence concurrency gap — that no criterion asserts a repair and an auto-refire cannot both be judging the same candidate. That invariant lives in the gate-singleton and in-flight-retriage machinery, which this plan did not author, so it is not graded here. A grader who believes it belongs in this plan should record that disagreement rather than invent evidence for it.\n\nGRADER OBLIGATION: spot-check at least three of the implementer audit citations at the audited sha before accepting any criterion as verified.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation acceptance rubric for green-main-fast-2026-08-25, authored against as-built reality on 2026-08-29 by su-062dd71e (P-012). REVISION 2, amended after third-party vetting by su-98f41fcf (consult conv-mtesuvr4-0000-3158b8b6d6df4922a0230b7bfe93af94).\n\nThe plan has TWO halves and the rubric grades both separately: Phase 1 is an OUTCOME (main green, pin deployed); Phase 2 is four STRUCTURAL reforms. The dominant acceptance risk, recorded repeatedly in the plan's own Decisions, is that Phase 2 certifies code that never runs: D-013 states plainly that a shipped plan can certify unreachable code, and D-020, D-021, D-038/D-039 and D-044 are four separate instances of it. C2 exists to make that failure mode gradeable rather than invisible, and it is the criterion a grader should spend the most evidence on.\n\n**`unknown` IS A FIRST-CLASS VERDICT — read this before grading anything.** Revision 1 of this rubric used a fail/partial/pass scale with no `unknown`, which was its most serious defect: at least three criteria here have honest no-verdict outcomes (C2 when execution cannot be established, C5 when no work-item commissioned an edit, C4 when no affected-tests run log exists in the window). A grader who cannot honestly say `unknown` will say `pass`, which is precisely the faking this rubric is built to prevent. If you cannot establish a criterion, record `unknown` with what you tried — never `pass`, and never `fail` either, since absence of evidence is not evidence of failure.\n\n**RELATIONSHIP TO THE CLASS RUBRIC.** plan-class-feature-ship already grades `audit-citations-spot-checked` generically. C6 here is deliberately NARROWER — it names D-044's specific missing→partial correction of P-008 — so grade C6 on that named verdict and let the class criterion carry the general spot-check, rather than filing the same finding twice across two cards.\n\nAUTHORSHIP/ELIGIBILITY: su-062dd71e authored this rubric and is INELIGIBLE to grade it. su-98f41fcf critiqued it and is ALSO ineligible — the vetting critic is refused at scorecards:emit and fails closed (EI-21623825762343009). Authored AFTER implementation, against as-built reality.\n\nThe plan's goal was not 'the services run somewhere else'. Its Phase 6 is titled 'Do not end up here again', so a migration that restored service but left the estate equally fragile, equally unmeasured, still paying the old provider, or MORE EXPOSED than the one it replaced would NOT satisfy it.\n\nGRADING NOTE. 24 of 26 items are live-infrastructure actions with no repository artifact, audited not-code BY DESIGN. Do NOT treat a `none` citation as a missing citation — treat it as a claim to falsify against live system state. Every criterion names a probe you can run yourself; prefer running it to reading the implementer's account. This desktop is NOT a valid witness for DNS or TLS (D-026) — witness those from a VM.\n\nPROVENANCE OF REVISION 3 — read this, because it is the honest history of a rubric written by the person it grades.\n\nRevision 1 had 7 criteria. The implementer identified a gap while submitting it for vetting (no criterion covered security exposure) and added `exposure-no-wider-than-source` before any grading occurred.\n\nRevision 3 folds two independent falsification passes:\n\n(a) The IMPLEMENTER attacked his own weakest criterion and found a real instrument defect, recorded as D-035: `systemctl show pc-estate-backup.service -p Result,ExecMainStatus` returns success/0 for a unit that has NEVER EXECUTED (measured on hetzner-restore-mesh, where ExecMainStartTimestamp is empty). The old drill would have scored a never-run backup healthy.\n\n(b) An INDEPENDENT REVIEWER with no history on this plan (su-d2d6b3a2, critique on WI-656761) returned 8 findings, executed 2 of the 8 drills live, and broke 5 criteria. All 8 findings were accepted. The two the author could not have found himself are worth naming: the decommission drill was structurally incapable of the pagination reconciliation its own PASS condition demanded, and — the significant one — NO criterion's rating was sensitive to the plan's own reason for existing. That produced the new criterion `recovery-survives-provider-loss`, which is EXPECTED TO RATE DEGRADED at ship time.\n\nThat last point is deliberate and the grader should weigh it as such: a criterion the author added knowing it currently fails is included precisely because the alternative — a rubric where everything passes — would have hidden the plan's central undischarged risk. The author explicitly did NOT build a quick mitigation first in order to grade himself healthy; that would be the reverse-engineering smell this rubric asks the grader to police.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revised 2026-08-29 after vetting consult conv-mtershv7-0000-e2aee61df144471cb9a52e25ccfc1587 (su-98f41fcf, posts 78866 + 78867).\n\nSCOPE, stated once so no criterion has to keep repeating it. This plan ships on its MECHANISM. Its one operational item (P-010) was dropped under ship-main-greening-plans-2026-08-29#D-019 as bounded and tested by #D-020, and its whole sequence — execute the current-tip qualification, verify exact green plus two Stable-C samples, emit generation 3, promote/deploy the green pin, verify live tested/deployed parity, restore the D-005 interval-backup mitigation, close residue — is routed UNPERFORMED to WI-835974 (originally WI-41495, which the P-010 drop cascade terminated — see C7). C7 is the floor that makes that explicit and is not optional: a grader who cannot verify C7 should fail the plan, not excuse it.\n\nLATENCY SCOPE. The plan's title promises FAST. End-to-end qualification latency is NOT graded here — it needs a live gate run, which belongs to WI-41495's lane and is unperformed. What IS graded, in C3, is the structural residue claim the speed rests on: that only O(1) publish/selection remains inside the serialized verdict slot. A shipped status is evidence about that residue and about nothing faster.\n\nAUTHORING LINT, recorded here rather than as an ungradeable criterion: C1-C6 are written about mechanism only and none of them asserts a live-gate outcome. That is a property of this fixed document, knowable at authoring time, so it is not something a grader can falsify — it does not belong in a criterion's method.\n\nTWO CARDS, TWO SCALES. This acceptance card grades on healthy/degraded/broken/unknown (the acceptance convention: 29 of 31 active acceptance rubrics in this workspace). The class card filed beside it, plan-class-feature-ship, grades on pass/partial/fail/unknown. The two scales are NOT comparable and the acceptance verdict must not average them; read each card on its own scale.\n\nCode-truth basis: plans:audit auditSeq 1, sha 808acac89a3b80f62bf4d0d4bf3f570fc2439ff1, 37 citations checked, 10 items audited, verifiedRatio 0.9 (the 0.1 is P-010, dropped by design).\n\nDRILL HYGIENE (applies to every replication drill in this rubric, stated once): (a) assert matched === the number of files requested BEFORE reading pass/fail — a route-error or a partial match reports no failures, which reads as green; a run that measured nothing is `unknown`, never healthy. (b) one file per testing:run call for load-bearing evidence — a multi-file Vitest invocation can abort during collection and that result must not be attributed to every requested path. (c) The implementer's counts below are HISTORY at sha 808acac89a, not the bar; the bar is the stated PASS CONDITION. (d) Line numbers are hints that rot on this swept tree — cite and search by SYMBOL. (e) The grader runs at current HEAD; HEAD is authoritative and a divergence from the historical count is a finding to report, not a failure by itself.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). REVISION 3 — final; attestation follows this revision because any later edit invalidates it.\n\nTHE TWO CHECKOUTS (every method below names its root; resolve paths only against these):\n  CALENDAR = /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/calendar\n  EMAIL    = /home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/email\nThey have a deliberately identical layout, so an unqualified path such as tests/native-package.e2e.test.ts exists in BOTH and silently resolves to whichever root you happen to be in. Never evaluate a criterion from an unnamed root.\n\nWHY NO CRITERION CARRIES A MACHINE-RUN check.tests, and what that costs:\n  • EI-21827847930833430 — FIXED by this plan's work. Three sites resolved the Cargo target dir independently; two asked cargo metadata, which honours the machine-wide [build] target-dir.\n  • EI-21825823418460682 — OPEN, NOT fixed here, and a genuinely different defect (revision 1 wrongly called them siblings, implying the second was repaired). plans:audit resolves a BARE citation path across checkouts, so a path can verify a different app than the item claims.\nA check that resolves to the wrong target does not merely fail to verify — it manufactures positive evidence for a claim nobody tested, silently, which is worse than no check. So the binding is declined while that defect is open. But declining does not remove the ambiguity, it MOVES it from the machine to the human grader, where it is invisible. That is why every method below names the absolute root and the exact command: the disambiguation is a step the author performed and handed over, not one the grader must improvise.\n\nGRADER ELIGIBILITY — correcting an earlier error in this file's history: su-98f41fcf disclosed that vetting disqualifies it from grading. su-ac7fc651 read the code (emit.ts:425-427) and showed the refusal fires only when critics.length === 1 && critics[0] === grader — literally SOLE critic. This rubric now has TWO vetting critics (su-98f41fcf and su-ac7fc651), so neither is the sole critic and neither is disqualified on that ground. The binding constraint is the ordinary one: the grader must not be the implementer/author, su-accf0e6a.\n\nORDERING: from 2026-08-31T00:00:00Z the ship gate refuses acceptance_rubric_vetted_after_grading if the attestation post-dates the independent grading. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it.
