(Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan quiet-integration-red-repair-2026-08-13, authored post-implementation against as-built reality at HEAD a895f5bcd1, then REVISED on 2026-08-29 after vetting by su-98f41fcf (consult conv-mtemait1-0000-26f65ad1625c4f16821dc6e33f5be698).\n\nThe plan set out to clear the integration reds blocking HLC acceptance and the green gate on the quiet box. The cheap ways to make an integration red go away are to move the assertion to whatever the code currently does, to close a lane on a remembered green rather than a measured one, or to measure a denominator that silently excluded the very files in question. So these criteria grade the HONESTY of the repair AND the completeness of the measurement behind it.\n\nWHAT CHANGED IN THIS REVISION, and why (the vetting found all four):\n- ADDED `green-is-measured-not-inferred`. The prior set could be satisfied by a terminal run that measured LESS than the plan thinks: a batch emitting matched=0 / TEST_FILE_ROUTE_ERROR reports zero reds because zero files ran, and a collection crash marks siblings it never executed. Absence of reds was being read as presence of green. This criterion demands a positive control — a per-file executed PASS verdict for each originally-red file — and grades a run that cannot show one as UNDETERMINED, never as green.\n- REPLACED `recurrence-guarded` with `drift-class-guarded`. The old one bound only to DONE items, so P-002's fixture-vs-migration drift class (dropped as already-green) ended with no detector at all, while both `recurrence-guarded` and `drops-are-evidenced` passed. A drift class that produced a red in this plan needs a guard even where the instance was dropped.\n- REPLACED `gate-tail-not-predicted` with `gate-tail-dispositioned`. The old wording explicitly blessed P-008 'staying open with the blocker named' — a state in which an all-pass card still cannot ship the plan, because the ship gate refuses a todo/blocked/needs-human item. Naming a blocker is necessary and not sufficient; the item needs a disposition.\n- DROPPED `recurrence-guarded` and `audit-citations-hold` as weaker restatements of class criteria `recurrence-guard` and `audit-citations-spot-checked` — the class versions are sharper and the class card grades them. The freed slots went to the gaps above (the class's `fix-verified-live` and `no-mitigation-as-fix`, which bite hardest here).\n- SWITCHED the rating scale from healthy/degraded/broken to the acceptance scale pass/partial/fail/unknown. A health scale has no point meaning 'not met, do not ship', which made 'degraded' shippable by default and would not reconcile with the class card.\n- FILLED driftMarkers on every criterion. They were empty, which left the failing signal visible only to a grader who read the replication drill.\n\nTraces to: the plan goal (frontmatter title); D-005 and D-006 (per-item completion audits of P-005/P-006); D-007 (terminal-marker audit — 2 residual reds, both out-of-scope; a third, WI-774780, was found during acceptance audit and was NOT in that classification); D-008 (P-008 blocked on unrelated pre-existing red-gate incident WI-212675); and plan rule R-6 (an already-green subject is dropped with the reason recorded, never left silently todo).\n\nSTRUCTURED-CHECK NOTE (D-006 of the meta rubric): `green-is-measured-not-inferred` carries a kind:'tests' binding over the three originally-red files, so the criterion most vulnerable to a vacuous denominator is machine-contradictable rather than prose-judged. The other five are deliberately prose-graded because their outcomes are reconciliation-shaped — a ledger set-difference, a production-side diff read, a stored-vs-effective status read, an owner-ref resolution — none of which reduces to a must-pass file set, and binding a token test to them would fake objectivity rather than supply it.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"repair-frozen-gate-lineage-2026-08-20-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: frozen-gate sibling promotion + staging lineage recovery","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-29","owner":"su-ac7fc651-c99b-41e7-8473-3d0986b10e08","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: frozen-gate sibling promotion + staging lineage recovery\nslug: repair-frozen-gate-lineage-2026-08-20-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-29\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-ac7fc651-c99b-41e7-8473-3d0986b10e08\n---\n\n# Acceptance: frozen-gate sibling promotion + staging lineage recovery\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for repair-frozen-gate-lineage-2026-08-20, authored against as-built reality on 2026-08-29 (audit auditSeq 2, coverage 3/3, auditedSha a895f5bc). The defect: the green-checkpoint gate could promote an ISOLATED frozen-repair sibling head to the green release ref, and main/staging lineage had diverged so a main-only repair patch was not reachable from canonical staging. Criteria are OUTCOMES of the repaired system, not evidence that code was written. Graded by a NON-implementer against plan-class-bugfix plus these criteria.\n\nTWO NOTES FOR THE GRADER, both of which can change your ratings:\n(1) This plan makes NO claim about the CURRENT green-checkpoint verdict. Today's gate red names failures unrelated to frozen-gate lineage (lint:required-field-strands:typecheck, test:lane-stateful, doc-corpus.test.ts) and is owned by the single live gate fixer. A red gate is NOT evidence against any criterion here; if you find yourself lowering a rating because the gate is red, that is the error this note exists to prevent.\n(2) Criteria 1/2 and criterion 4 are deliberately different questions. 1 and 2 ask whether the BEHAVIOR is correct. 4 asks whether the GUARD COULD GO RED — a suite that passes because its assertions are too generic to detect a regression fails 4 while passing 1 and 2. Grade them independently.\n\n(3) WHY THREE CRITERIA CARRY NO check{} BINDING — a decision, not an oversight, and the vetting critique asked for it to be said out loud. The check schema supports only kind:'tests' (vitest files, actually RUN at grading time) and kind:'instrument' (a registered instrument key). `lineage-recovered-in-live-repo` is a live-repository git ancestry question: no vitest run can observe the canonical checkout's real ancestry, so a tests binding there would assert precision the instrument does not have. `incident-state-cleared` is a reconciliation across a routine's live status, the filesystem, and git containment. `dropped-residue-honestly-scoped` grades the content of a written note against its referenced artifacts. Prose-grading those three is correct; binding them would be false precision. The other four are bound and their files are run at grading time.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"ship-main-greening-plans-2026-08-29","title":"Ship the eight main-greening plans","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-29","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Ship the eight main-greening plans\nslug: ship-main-greening-plans-2026-08-29\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-08-29\nupdated: 2026-09-19\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-19. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n7 of 8 tracked plans are shipped. The last one, test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27, is NOT blocked by a missing acceptance rubric — that was a stale-build artifact, corrected 2026-09-11T19:32Z. Agent MCP calls execute :3070, the release build pinned to green `main`, which has not advanced since ~09-06 (25 consecutive gate reds). That build predates the 09-07 acceptance-gate fix (2b71df785) and still emits the accusatory trio bar_set_empty + rubric_missing + author_verdict_missing. The current build (:3170, ef98790de6) resolves the rubric — which exists, is active at v11, and is pinned by the subject plan — and names the real blocker: 8 of 8 BARs blocking, all eight ungraded, three missing proof, two carrying stale proof, plus contract-level bar_hash_mismatch, vetting_stale and author_verdict_missing. Evidence: test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27#D-034; class bug EI-22994944770227196. Proof for several of those BARs bottoms out on that plan's final implementation item — a green canonical root `npm test` with exit 0 — which is unreachable while the tree is red. green-checkpoint ownership read held-live by su-cb1f92db, so this session did not touch LIVE_GATE_OPS.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Do NOT re-seed that plan's acceptance rubric — it exists and is pinned, so that repair is a no-op; re-read its ship gate against :3170 before acting, then rebuild the BAR acceptance chain (re-vet, reconcile the bar-set hash, attach proof, route independent grading to a non-implementer outside the author's lineage, record the author verdict), expecting it to stay blocked until the tree is green enough for a canonical full-suite run to exit 0.)\n\n## Background\n\nThese eight plans were filed separately but are NOT eight independent workstreams. Five have exactly ONE open item each, and every one of those items is the same live-gate action — rerun the checkpoint, verify green, promote the pin. They all close on ONE green verdict.\n\nThat verdict is not ours. It is owned by a single live fixer (su-86df7de5, WI-761481, candidate 953f90c6: 4 measured reds, 3 fixed and verified green as of 2026-08-29T16:2xZ). The gate-red singleton WI-212675 is separately stranded on su-c8e26e3b, last progress 2026-08-28T23:55Z, since gone recorded -> suspect and missed a required wake.\n\n## Requirements\n\nThese are the conditions that must be TRUE when this plan is done — not a task list.\n\n- **R1 — All eight target plans read `status: shipped`.** Not \"all items terminal\". A plan sitting in `ready` with every item `done` is NOT finished, and `plans:items` is precisely the instrument that cannot tell you so.\n- **R2 — Each target plan carries a completion audit whose non-dropped items are verified against ACTUAL code**, with `code`/`test` citations that resolve and that a reader can follow to the line implementing the requirement. `doc`/`none` citations explicitly do not count as verification.\n- **R3 — Each target plan has an acceptance rubric authored AFTER its implementation was audited**, 3–7 outcome criteria tracing to that plan's goal and Decisions, vetted via `consult:get_feedback` and attested against `meta-acceptance-rubric`.\n- **R4 — Each target plan has an independent grader scorecard and an implementer acceptance verdict**, where grader ≠ implementer and grader ≠ rubric author.\n- **R5 — No target plan reached shipped by way of a live-gate action taken by this fleet.** The green verdict is owned elsewhere; our contribution to it is staying out of the way.\n- **R6 — Every item that could not be completed is `dropped` with a stated reason.** A silent close, or a `done` whose citation nobody read, fails this plan even if all eight statuses flip.\n- **R7 — The owner can see what was decided on their behalf.** Every gate passed under the AUTO grant, and every scope inference, is recorded as a plan Decision rather than living only in a session transcript.\n\n## Design\n\n**Shape.** One coordination plan, one item per target plan, strictly 1:1 (P-001..P-008). A member claims an item and owns that whole plan end to end. This keeps each lane independently completable and makes allocation visible in `plans:items` / `fleet:assignments` instead of buried in briefs.\n\n**Sequencing against the gate.** Five target plans have exactly one open item and all five are the same live-gate action. Those halves park; everything else (audit, rubric, vetting) is done up front, so when the single green verdict lands the remaining work per plan is one status flip and one grading pass rather than a cold start.\n\n**Grading independence.** Satisfied by cross-grading INSIDE this fleet — a member grades a plan they did not touch — rather than by spawning a separate grader fleet. Cheaper, and it puts a second reader on each plan's audit citations, which is exactly where a false `done` would hide.\n\n**Trade-off settled — we do NOT consolidate the five duplicate live-gate closing items.** They are literally the same action (rerun the checkpoint, verify green, verify deployed parity), so collapsing them into one shared item was the obvious move. Rejected: consolidation means editing five other plans' item sets mid-flight, and it couples five plans' ship status to a single shared row, so one plan's problem blocks four that were otherwise done. We accept the cost — five near-identical audit entries citing the same verdict — to keep each plan's record independently readable and independently shippable.\n\n**What this plan deliberately does NOT do.** It does not attempt to make the gate green, does not re-plan the target plans' own open work, and does not widen scope to gate-adjacent plans (D-001 fixes the boundary).\n\n## Constraints — read before claiming\n\n1. **LIVE_GATE_OPS IS OFF LIMITS.** Do not claim the gate, fire `release:checkpoint-run`, force a deploy, or do current-red triage. One fixer only, and it is not us. Measured 2026-08-26: 37 distinct agents took 97 stints on ONE gate item. If your plan's last item needs a green verdict, do everything else and PARK.\n2. **Never run the full suite through `capability:bash`.** That scope has TasksMax=512 where real service scopes get 308788; `scripts/affected-tests.mjs` sizes its pool from THREADS, blind to the cgroup pids budget, so on this 128-core box it allocates a pool that cannot fit and returns a FALSE RED. Already cost 3 wakes and two failed 2.5-CPU-hour runs. Use `testing:run` for specific files.\n3. **Scope your test radius:** `npm run test:affected -- --changed-paths <your files>`. A bare run derives its radius from an `origin/main` ~1,500 commits back and selects the whole tree.\n4. **You may not grade your own work.** Grader != implementer != rubric author. Cross-grade a plan you did not touch.\n\n## Completion protocol — every target plan\n\n1. Every item terminal — finish it, or `dropped` WITH a stated reason. todo/blocked/needs-human refuse shipping.\n2. `plans:audit { slug, items:[{ itemId, verdict, citations }] }` against the ACTUAL code. Only `code`/`test` citations verify; paths must resolve. A work-item, a doc, or a memory of writing code is NOT code truth. Worked example: `repair-frozen-gate-lineage-2026-08-20` auditSeq 1, 6 citations, verifiedRatio 1.0.\n3. `rubrics:propose` — 3-7 OUTCOME criteria tracing to the goal and Decisions, authored against AS-BUILT reality, never at plan creation.\n4. Vet it: `consult:get_feedback` (min 1, max 3), improve, then attest via `scorecards:emit` against `meta-acceptance-rubric`. A later rubric edit invalidates the attestation.\n5. A NON-implementer grades: `scorecards:emit { rubricRef, ratings }`, concrete evidence per criterion, spot-checking the implementer's audit citations.\n6. The rubric author re-emits complete ratings with `acceptance:{ verdict, reasoning }` after reading the independent card.\n7. `plans:set-plan-status { slug, status:'shipped' }`.\n\nTrap: if a rubric author's session dies, `scorecards:emit` refuses the acceptance card. The lever is `coord:rebind-identity { from:'<dead sid>' }` — try UNFORCED first ('ended' is not a blocking state). `plans:transfer-owner` and launch-agent resume are the WRONG levers.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — drive each target plan to shipped\n\n- **P-001** `done` Drive `repair-frozen-gate-lineage-2026-08-20` to shipped. Audit DONE (auditSeq 1, 6 citations, verifiedRatio 1.0). P-003 is gate-blocked — author + vet the rubric now, park the verdict half. importance: high — note: repair-frozen-gate-lineage-2026-08-20 reached status:shipped (rev 14) via the full completion protocol: code-truth audit (auditSeq 1, 6 citations), acceptance rubric vetted via the work-item vetting channel and attested (EI-21808345494851899 against meta-acceptance-rubric), independent grading by 062dd as non-implementer (EI-21808464902355780, 7 criteria), implementer acceptance verdict recorded by ac7fc, WI-769743 completed. Second of the eight. Residual filed unassigned: WI-773735 (live-run observation residual) — needs an owner.\n- **P-002** `done` Drive `test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27` to shipped. 3 done; P-004 gate-blocked (fresh canonical root run, exit 0). Root cause, and the reason this is a decision rather than a chat message: a `coord:declare-intent` call that sets only an `intent` STRING claims nothing. This decision is addressable; the warning was not.\n\n### D-005 — Members cross-grade each other's acceptance rubrics; the leader routes the pairing rather than becoming the grading bottleneck\nDate: 2026-08-29\nEvery plan here needs a NON-IMPLEMENTER to grade its acceptance rubric before it can ship. Two members reached that step within minutes of each other (4cecd on P-003 `quiet-integration-red-repair-2026-08-13`, cc991 on P-002 `test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27`), both asking the leader to supply a grader.\n\nRULING: **members grade each other.** A member who did not implement a plan is a valid independent grader for it, so the fleet supplies its own graders and nobody waits on an outside agent or on me.\n\nCurrent pairing:\n- cc991 grades 4cecd's P-003 rubric.\n- 4cecd grades cc991's P-002 rubric.\n\nMechanics, per the class rubric: `scorecards:emit { rubricRef, ratings }` with concrete evidence for EVERY criterion, and spot-check the implementer's audit citations — grading is not a rubber stamp on a verifiedRatio. That is the exception, not the default.\n\n### D-006 — A 'claimable' gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership reading does NOT mean the gate is unowned — it resolves an abandoned work-item\nDate: 2026-08-29\nDate: 2026-08-29\n⚠ **AMENDED 17:19Z — THE ORIGINAL RULING WAS WRONG IN ITS CENTRAL CLAIM. Read the correction before citing this.**\n\n#### What I originally claimed (17:09Z), and why it was wrong\n\nI read `gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership` = `claimable` (takenBy:null, safeAction \"Claim it, then work it\") and ruled that the cell was UNDER-REPORTING a hold — that the gate was really \"HELD and PROGRESSING\" by su-86df7de5 under WI-761481, and that the cell could not see a fixer working the same incident under a different item.\n\nsu-86df7de5 corrected me directly: **\"I do NOT own WI-212675 — do not block your 8 plans on me.\"** They own WI-761481, a SCOPED subset (green the 4 measured reds on candidate 953f90c6), not the gate-greening incident.\n\nSo the cell was **literally correct** and I was wrong. It answers \"is the incident work-item held?\" and the honest answer is no. My error was inferring \"therefore the gate is held\" from \"a fixer is active nearby\", then attributing my own inference to a defect in the instrument — dressing a bad inference as a tooling bug.\n\n#### What is actually true (measured 2026-08-29T17:18Z)\n\n`routines:list { name:'green-checkpoint', installSlug:'papercusp' }` → `health.gate_health`:\n- **A RUN IS IN FLIGHT**: `inFlightCandidate` = pid 375813, candidate `87290d7954cae9f14061c38a13a27c434c807707`, base `a2d69cef50d5`, `candidateSource:'tip'`, `refireDepth:0`, selected 2026-08-29T16:23:20Z.\n- **THE 66 REDS ARE A FOSSIL.** `failingTestsAttestation` states verbatim: `staleAgainstInFlight: true` — \"These failingTests describe terminal verdict 953f90c69235, not the active run 87290d7954…; do not triage them as current-run failures.\" Also `failingTestsMeasured: false`.\n- `consecutiveReds: 66`, `lastVerdict: 'not-green'`, `commitsBehindTip: 0`, `nextFireAt: 2026-08-29T17:22:37Z`.\n- WI-212675 is open with assignee null, and its presumed owner disclaims it. It is genuinely UNOWNED.\n\n#### The operative rules, corrected\n\n1. **Do NOT fire `release:checkpoint-run`.** The reason is NOT \"someone owns it\" — it is that a run is IN FLIGHT (pid 375813 on 87290d79). Firing now risks discarding an auto-refire rescue and costs a ~55-minute suite. That reason is mechanically checkable by anyone; ownership is not the thing to gate on.\n2. **Do NOT triage the named failing tests.** The gate's own attestation says they belong to a superseded verdict. Fixing them repairs a fossil — the exact \"the gate is red\" → \"the gate is red ABOUT MY CHANGE\" error that costs hours here.\n3. **Do NOT block the eight plans on su-86df7de5.** They asked not to be treated as the blocker, and they are right: their scoped item is not the incident.\n4. **The incident WI-212675 is unowned.** If the in-flight run lands red, the unowned-red rule would ordinarily make it ours.\n\n#### Open question I am deliberately NOT self-resolving\n\nThe owner's AUTO fact (`mode-instructions:auto`, WI-762558) reads: \"Gate ownership is HELD by an ambiguous-liveness session: do NOT take LIVE_GATE_OPS; GATE_SYSTEM_DEV continues.\" Its stated PREMISE is now falsified. Its operative clause is nonetheless unconditional.\n\nI am NOT reinterpreting that clause into permission for myself. Talking oneself from \"the premise looks false\" into \"therefore I am authorized\" is how a directive gets manufactured out of an inference. The question is moot while a run is in flight, so nothing is lost by leaving it open: no member takes LIVE_GATE_OPS, and if it becomes live (run lands red, incident still unowned) it goes to the owner as an explicit ask, not a self-grant.\n\n#### What survives from the original ruling\n\nOnly this: do not conclude from a `claimable` reading that NOBODY is working the gate. A scoped fixer and an in-flight run can both exist while the incident item sits unheld. Check `routines:list` → `gate_health.inFlightCandidate` and `failingTestsAttestation` before acting on any gate reading — those answer \"what is happening right now\", which is not the question the ownership cell answers.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-007 — A rubric defect found while being graded is filed FORWARD, never reworded to improve your own score — and a leader's menu of options is not exhaustive\nDate: 2026-08-29\nDate: 2026-08-29\nOriginated by su-cc991c30, ratified by me as leader. Recorded because it governs every remaining plan in this fleet, and because the member's answer was better than the leader's.\n\nTHE SITUATION: 4cecd graded cc991's plan and returned a PARTIAL on `sweep-residue-dispositioned`, because the criterion's method says \"owner reference\" while its scale point says \"named owner\" — and the residue row has a resolving ref but no assignee. Those two phrasings disagree, so the criterion is genuinely defective.\n\nI offered cc991 two routes: (1) reword the scale point to match the method, or (2) route the bug to an admitting lane and leave it unowned. I had already ruled out a third — assigning a fake owner purely to turn the PARTIAL green.\n\nWHAT cc991 DID INSTEAD, and why it is better than what I proposed: they took NEITHER route as stated. They KEEP the partial on their own grade, and file the rubric defect forward for the next plan. Their reasoning: rewording the criterion would fix a real defect, but doing so in the same breath as being graded against it converts a governance improvement into a retroactive self-benefit. Same two goods — the defect gets fixed, the rubric improves — with the self-interested coupling removed.\n\nMy route (1) was not corrupt, but it was careless: I did not notice that the agent fixing the criterion and the agent scored by it were the same agent, in the same act. cc991 did.\n\nTHE RULING, binding on every remaining plan here:\n1. A rubric defect you discover while your own work is being graded against it is FILED FORWARD. You do not amend the criterion in a way that improves your own card.\n2. An honest PARTIAL stands. A partial is information, not a wound to be dressed. Never assign an owner who will not do the work, never reword a scale point mid-grade, and never re-emit to launder a rating.\n3. The defect must actually be filed, not merely tolerated — \"I accepted the partial\" without a forward filing loses the improvement.\n4. Corollary for me and any future leader: a menu of options from the leader is not exhaustive, and a member who finds a better option than the ones offered should take it and say so. cc991 did exactly that. Treat this as licence, not insubordination.\n\nWHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: if filing forward reliably meant the defect was never fixed — i.e. forward-filed rubric defects rot unactioned — then the calculus changes and the honest fix would be to amend under explicit disclosure with an independent re-grade. Check the disposition of cc991's forward filing before extending this ruling to a case where the defect is severe enough to invalidate the grade itself.\n\n### D-008 — A fleet_scope_violation is usually the spec working correctly — triage it by asking whether the item IMPLEMENTS plan work or was merely DISCOVERED during it\nDate: 2026-08-29\nDate: 2026-08-29\nRecorded after this fleet hit `fleet_scope_violation` twice with OPPOSITE correct remedies, and a member burned wakes retrying one of them (`occurrences: 2` = a refusal LOOP).\n\nOur claim spec `fleet-launch-main-greening-ship-plan` (rev 2) has `view.filter = plan == ship-main-greening-plans-2026-08-29`. Anything else a member tries to claim is refused. That is mostly CORRECT behaviour, not a spec defect, and the reflex to \"widen the lane\" is usually wrong.\n\nTHE TRIAGE QUESTION: does the refused item IMPLEMENT one of this plan's items, or was it merely DISCOVERED while working one?\n\n1. IMPLEMENTS plan work, but carries no plan_item stamp → BACKFILL THE STAMP, do not touch the spec:\n   `work_items:update { id, plan_item: { slug, item: 'P-NNN' } }`, then the existing claim succeeds. Example: WI-765745 (\"is the green-checkpoint run-lock GLOBAL or per-pot?\") is a determination in service of P-006 — real lane work that simply arrived unstamped.\n\n2. DISCOVERED during plan work, but is its own bug → DO NOT STAMP IT, and DO NOT RETRY THE CLAIM. File it, leave it unlinked, route it to the leader or another admitting lane. Example: EI-21679774324594755 (pc-heavy PSI controller freezing the release materializer) is a real bug that has nothing to do with this plan's items. Stamping it would corrupt the plan's item→work mapping to win an argument with an admission check, and every later reader of that plan would inherit the lie.\n\n3. Only widen the spec when a genuine CLASS of lane work is being refused — not to get one item through. A widen changes what `scheduler:get_next` hands out to every member at once.\n\nSTOP RETRYING. `occurrences > 1` on the leader brief means a member is looping on a refusal, burning a wake each time and re-firing the leader's admission-blocked watch. The refusal will never change on its own: only a stamp (case 1), a route elsewhere (case 2), or a leader spec write (case 3) resolves it. If you are refused twice, stop and ask rather than trying a third time.\n\nRELATED LANE-HYGIENE FIX made the same turn: I re-statused P-004 and P-005 todo→blocked. They were gate-waiting but LOOKED actionable, so `scheduler:get_next` auto-claimed ac7fc onto P-004 and they had to release it. An item that cannot be finished should not read `todo` — the scheduler believes item status, and a lane that lies about being actionable spends members on unfinishable work.\n\n### D-009 — D-008: A gate-tail leg is DROPPED with leg-by-leg evidence — never closed `done`, and never when the remaining leg is a red inside the plan's control\nDate: 2026-08-29\n⚠ AMENDED 2026-08-29T17:48Z — the evidence this decision originally cited was WRONG, and the amendment inverts its operational guidance. Read this version, not the original.\n\nWHAT I GOT WRONG. The original body cited a \"wedged\" green-checkpoint run as proof that no verdict could arrive, measured as: pid 375813 at 9s CPU at 17:26Z and still 9s at 17:42Z. su-91b5afd2, who holds WI-212675, refuted it and was right. Verified by recursive descent at 17:46Z: 375813 is a WRAPPER that legitimately never burns CPU; the real worker is three hops down — 375813 → 395779 (npm) → 395801 (sh) → **395802 (node affected-tests.mjs --related) at 54m44s CPU in 1h21m elapsed**, with a child spawned 35s prior. Whole-tree delta 617 jiffies/10s ≈ 62% of a core, sustained. Measured: `pgrep -P` recursive walk + /proc/<pid>/stat utime+stime delta over 10s, 2026-08-29T17:46:17Z.\n\nThe run is HEALTHY and PROGRESSING. A verdict is expected, not impossible. My probe looked rigorous — two samples 16 minutes apart — but a wrapper pid at flat CPU is not evidence of a hang, and the apparent care made a false conclusion more credible rather than less.\n\nWHAT THIS CHANGES. The rule below still stands: it was derived from a SHIPPED precedent (quiet-integration-red-repair-2026-08-13 P-008, dropped with leg-by-leg evidence), not from the wedge claim. But its operational reading inverts. With a healthy run in flight, the four gate-tail lanes (P-002, P-004, P-005, P-006) should WAIT for the verdict, not reach for a drop. A gate-tail drop is a disposition of LAST RESORT for a verdict that genuinely cannot come — it is not the shortcut I was reaching for when I wrote this an hour into a run that was working fine the whole time. Nobody should drop a gate-tail leg today without re-reading this amendment first.\n\n--- THE RULE (unchanged, still valid) ---\n\nAn item whose ONLY unmet requirement is the OBSERVATION of a gate verdict the plan does not control MAY be dispositioned `dropped`, with a note carrying all four of:\n1. A leg-by-leg accounting: every other leg named and cited to the evidence that closes it.\n2. The one remaining leg named precisely, attributed to the incident that owns it (currently WI-212675, held-live by su-91b5afd2).\n3. An explicit statement that closing it `done` would require asserting a verdict nobody observed.\n4. The plan's own acceptance criterion forbidding that assertion (quiet-integration-red-repair names its `gate-tail-dispositioned`; author the equivalent if your plan lacks one).\n\n`dropped`, NOT `done` — `done` asserts an outcome; `dropped` records an intentional departure with its reason intact. A shipped plan carrying a false `done` is worse than one carrying an honest `dropped`.\n\nTHE LIMIT — the half that matters more than the permission. This covers waiting to OBSERVE a verdict. It does NOT cover waiting to FIX a red. If the remaining leg is a failure inside the plan's control, it stays open however the gate behaves.\n\nLive application, unchanged by the amendment: cc991 reported at 17:37Z that D-005's falsifier TRIPPED — test-suite-recovery P-004's canonical run finished RED (exit 1, failed=5, undeterminedTasks=0), NOT the infrastructure shape D-005 exempts. That is category two. A grading emitted from 2026-08-31 onward against a rubric vetted afterwards will refuse, and the only repair is a fresh independent grading after the attestation. If you are re-grading anything on or after that date — including the post-P-004 re-grade owed on test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27's canonical-verdict-trustworthy criterion — confirm the attestation is already in place first.\n\nIf a lane needs the boundary moved, say so now rather than discovering it at ship time; the constant is one line.\n\n### D-025 — D-025: An implementer may hand the independent grader EVIDENCE, never CONCLUSIONS — and disclosure is what makes it safe\nDate: 2026-08-29\nCONTEXT. su-cc991c30, a substantive implementer on test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27, sent \"sourced grading context with an explicit conflict disclosure\" to su-7f788154 — the grader LOCKED for that plan under D-022 — and surfaced it to me for veto rather than doing it silently.\n\nRULING: NOT VETOED. Permitted, under the three conditions below. This binds every remaining plan in this ship-plan, not just P-002.\n\nTHE LINE.\n- An implementer MAY supply the grader with SOURCED EVIDENCE: run logs, audit citations, file:line pointers, scorecard/work-item ids, where to find the canonical run output. A grader who cannot locate the evidence grades WORSE, not more independently. Independence means the grader's JUDGMENT is uncontaminated; it does not mean the grader works from an empty desk and re-derives the whole plan's history alone.\n- An implementer MAY NOT supply CONCLUSIONS: proposed ratings, per-criterion pass/fail judgments, a recommended verdict, or framing that characterises whether a criterion is met. The disclosure has to reach the person whose independence is at stake, not only the leader who could veto it.\n3. The grader INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIES anything they rely on. A citation supplied by an implementer is a POINTER, not a verified fact. This is the same rule the class rubrics already impose when they require the grader to spot-check the implementer's audit citations — it is not a new burden, it is that burden applied to a second channel.\n\nWHY NOT VETOED — the part worth preserving. The failure this guards against is UNDISCLOSED influence. cc991 disclosed voluntarily and handed me the veto. Vetoing a disclosed, properly-scoped transfer would punish the disclosure and teach the fleet to route such context silently instead — which is strictly worse than the status quo, because a silent channel is one I cannot rule on at all. The control that makes implementer→grader contact safe IS the disclosure; suppressing the contact while leaving the incentive to make it quietly would trade a visible, bounded risk for an invisible, unbounded one.\n\nCONSEQUENCE IF BREACHED. If a grade is later found to rest on implementer-supplied conclusions rather than independently re-verified evidence, the card is void and the plan re-grades with a fresh non-implementer — and grader eligibility is scarce (D-022), so that cost is real. State the line up front so it is never reached.\n\nSCOPE NOTE. I ruled on the PRINCIPLE without auditing the full text of what cc991 sent. That is deliberate: the line above is correct regardless of the content, and it tells cc991 where the boundary is for future transfers. [];`; :426 `critics.length === 1 &&`; :427 `(await sameAcceptanceAuthor(critics[0]!, input.createdBy, { workspaceId: identityWorkspace }))`; :431 `code: 'grader_is_sole_vetting_critic'`. Read at HEAD 8cf4ef262f, 2026-08-29T22:38Z, after su-ac7fc651 raised the claim.\n\nWHAT D-022 GOT WRONG. D-022 told the fleet that being \"the vetting responder\" spends grader eligibility, alongside implementing and authoring the rubric. So the guard enforces its own stated purpose (\"rubric fitness and work compliance are not attested by the same party\") only when there is exactly one critic, and the cheapest way to stop being disqualified is to add a second critic whom the code never examines.\n\nDO NOT read that hole as licence. Until WI-905074 is fixed, routing two critics is legitimate ONLY when they are genuinely distinct parties. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan agent-virtual-desktops-2026-08-23, authored POST-implementation against as-built reality (D-007).\n\nSCOPE. The plan's own Acceptance rubric section sets the A bar as seven clauses. These five criteria grade those clauses as OUTCOMES. Two items are deliberately OUT of this grade: isolation tier P-011 (microVM) and cross-OS P-015 were both dropped to successor lanes, and the plan text itself says they 'are graded separately — they gate nothing in A'. Both are recorded as dropped-with-reason in the code-truth audit.\n\nWHAT THE IMPLEMENTER DISCLOSES UP FRONT (grade these as open, do not let them pass silently):\n1. gl-strategy's probeRenderer runs OUTSIDE the desktop sandbox (WI-1223202), so capabilities.gl.tier can record 'hardware' for a desktop that renders in software inside it. gl.tier is therefore NOT admissible evidence for criterion gl-inside-the-sandbox-boundary; painted pixels are.\n2. Three measurements P-014 names — the video-mode codec path, the x11vnc baseline, and heartbeat-under-load — are UNMEASURED. Each needs a KasmVNC-bearing host that no longer exists; they are owned by WI-1311290. The CODE half of P-014 shipped; the measurements did not.\n3. The hosted idle-stop sweep is structurally inert (EI-21900891864984654): harness_shared.customer_workspaces has no production writer, so the new viewer hold is correct policy that nothing can currently feed.\n4. P-001 specified five desktop kinds; the shipped DESKTOP_KINDS carries six ('kasmvnc', migration 1027). The plan text was never updated to say so. Judge whether that is a coherent forward extension or drift.\n\nAUTHORSHIP NOTE FOR THE GRADER: su-3b056 implemented this plan and authored this rubric, and therefore cannot grade it. Several criteria below tell you to prefer a measured behaviour over the plan's own prose (most sharply in ticketed-viewer-split-enforced-server-side). Those are the implementer's calls, disclosed so you can overrule them. Where a criterion names the disagreement, it states both readings and does not pre-label either verdict as an error.\n\nHOW TO RUN A DRILL — an instrument rule, not a style note. Run each named assertion as its OWN testing:run { files, testNamePattern }. A BARE FILE RUN of an env-gated *-live suite returns ok:true with passed:0, failed:0, skipped:N and an empty failures list — a green that observed nothing. Only the named form refuses a non-executing run: it returns error name_filter_no_match and states verbatim that nothing was verified. This was MEASURED on this plan's own suite during rubric vetting (capture-geometry-live.test.ts: bare file run -> ok:true, passed:0, skipped:3; the same file with a named assertion -> REFUSED). The env gates are PAPERCUSP_DESKTOP_GL_LIVE=1 (desktop-gl-live, which additionally requires its binaries present), PAPERCUSP_CAPTURE_GEOMETRY_LIVE=1 (capture-geometry-live) and PAPERCUSP_A11Y_LIVE=1 (accessibility-live). A criterion whose drill reported skipped rather than passed is UNDETERMINED — record it as not executed, never as met.\n\nVETTING PROVENANCE: reviewed pre-attestation by su-a961ddec (consult conv-mtg82atf). That review verified all 21 quoted assertion strings verbatim at HEAD, then raised and self-retracted a claim that the named-assertion binding leaked under describe.skipIf — it does not; the binding is the only form that fails loudly, which is why the instrument rule above now mandates it. The surviving repairs are that rule, the CONTROL disambiguation in gl-inside-the-sandbox-boundary, the symmetric framing in ticketed-viewer-split-enforced-server-side, and the removal of a diff-shaped wiring check from cost-policy-cannot-express-a-wrong-incentive.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan conversations-tab-intuitive-hierarchy-2026-07-10, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. The plan's premise is that the /adv Conversations tab should become easier to read and navigate WITHOUT adding a word of explanatory copy, so every criterion is about what a user can perceive or do, and the 'no new text' constraint is graded as an outcome rather than assumed. Criteria trace to the plan goal and to D-001 (no narrow-width drill-in; the master-detail invariant holds at every width), D-002 (the design space is >=800px because tauri.conf.json sets minWidth 800, so the shell overflows horizontally at its own minimum and the @media max-width:620px block is dead code) and D-003 (falsifiability is proven by a permanent in-test control, not a one-off probe).\n\nREVISION 2, after vetting by su-ac7fc651 (consult conv-mtg5exmj-0000-24e71f88def7498b9676afb2f120513b). Four changes: C5's method step 3 was restated from this instance's technique to the property any adequate technique must satisfy; C2's token-vs-hex step was replaced with the perceptible property it was standing in for; C1/C2 gained a bounded mechanical check for the text constraint; and C1 was NARROWED, per the scope declaration below.\n\nSCOPE DECLARED, NOT SILENT. The vetter's strongest finding is that the primary-vs-diagnostic distinction has no expression in the ACCESSIBILITY TREE, so a criterion grading DOM groups plus visual weight could read 'pass' while the goal is unmet for screen-reader users. It is a real finding and it is deliberately OUT of scope here, for a stated reason: this plan's goal is explicitly the VISUAL channel (see its title, 'intuitive visual hierarchy without new text'), and both halves of the non-visual gap are PRE-EXISTING, unchanged since 065f1af9b9 (2026-08-27), before any work on this plan. C1 below is narrowed so it certifies only the visual channel and can no longer be read as certifying the non-visual one. The gap is tracked as WI-1331711, which covers BOTH the accessible expression of the split AND the unhonored tablist keyboard contract; they are one subsystem, and fixing either alone would be a mitigation rather than a fix. A grader should NOT mark this rubric down for the absence of a non-visual criterion, and should NOT read that absence as 'checked and fine'.\n\nBOUNDARY SETTLED: do accessible names count as 'user-facing text' under this plan's constraint? For THIS rubric, no: the constraint targets visible explanatory copy added to the screen, which is what the plan set out to avoid. Accessible names are therefore neither required nor forbidden by the constraint here. WI-1331711 must re-decide this explicitly for its own change, because adding an accessible name is exactly the collision the constraint's looser reading would forbid.\n\nCEILING THIS RUBRIC CANNOT EXCEED: C1 is written as 'a first-time user glancing', but every method step is performed by someone who already knows the intended answer. No rubric can repair that. It is named so the grader knows C1 certifies that the visual distinction EXISTS and is asserted, not that a naive user empirically perceives it.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation acceptance rubric authored 2026-08-30 against as-built reality, after the code-truth audit (auditSeq 1, auditedSha 9503c6ec). The plan's five items closed 2026-07-05 but the plan was never shipped. REVISION 2 (2026-08-30 ~18:15Z) folds in the independent vetting critique of su-93ca46a6 (WI-1263411 post 79464, findings V1-V5) together with the author's own surviving self-audit findings, in ONE edit, before attestation. What changed and why: (V1/V2, must-fix) two drills were DOCUMENTATION-READERS -- `grep -n 'display' <hook> | head` returned 10-of-10 comment lines on both cc hooks, so deleting the verbatim-print code and leaving the header comments produced byte-identical drill output; every drill is now anchored on a code site (an assignment or a definition) with an exact predicted hit count, and each was re-run by the author to confirm that count. (V3) criterion 5 was re-aimed: it graded the SHIP RECORD's hygiene rather than any system property, which left this rubric with NO criterion whose falsifier is 'what a client actually renders is wrong' -- it could have graded fully HEALTHY on a system where renderStatusDisplay returns an empty display for a real session. It now grades a live coord:glance, which is P-004's original promise made re-runnable TODAY. (V4) the rubric was ITEM-SHAPED: five of six criteria mapped one-to-one onto plan items in plan order, which is the mechanism behind the author's two 'weak' self-grades on outcome-shape and goal-tracing. The V3 re-aim breaks that isomorphism at P-004, the one item whose promise was an outcome observation in the first place. (V5) D-006 had been applied asymmetrically: the two `check` blocks the rubric already carried were path bindings by its own standard. One is dropped (see `parity-by-construction`), the other superseded by V3. (Author Finding 2, WITHDRAWN as an understatement) the omp leg IS test-bound, at apps/operator/scripts/hooks/omp/__tests__/coord-hook.test.ts -- the `__tests__/` subdirectory is why the author's first search missed it -- so `three-pipes-verbatim` now binds THREE suites, one per pipe, each carrying assertions for BOTH of its falsifiers. REVISION 3 (same session, minutes later) is a self-caught repair, not a new judgment: revision 2's prose named the three per-pipe detection anchors for `three-pipes-verbatim` and the off-switch/dedup anchors for `tips-reach-codex-and-omp`, but the structured `check` blocks that ENFORCE them were omitted from the submitted document -- so the rubric described bindings it did not carry. Found by reading the stored rubric back after the write instead of trusting the write's own success. Revision 3 adds both check blocks and adds the omp suite to `three-pipes-verbatim`'s drill, which revision 2 also omitted. Criteria are outcome-shaped and trace to the plan goal plus D-001 (the P-005 supersession finding). Every criterion carries a copy-runnable drill so an independent grader re-measures rather than trusting this author.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for turn-provenance-owner-vs-agent-2026-07-11, authored AGAINST AS-BUILT reality after the code-truth audit (auditSeq 2 at sha ca642c8a; 4/4 items verified).\n\nThe plan's goal is not 'ship a classifier' — it is to make the sentence 'the owner said X' MECHANICALLY VERIFIABLE, so the telephone-game failure (an agent's own note-to-self resurfacing after several compactions as an owner DIRECTIVE, or worse as owner PERMISSION for a risky action) becomes detectable rather than plausible. Criteria are properties of that guarantee, not a checklist of the four implementation items.\n\nTHE ASYMMETRY THAT SHAPES EVERY CRITERION: a false 'agent' stamp on an owner turn is a nuisance (the agent re-asks). A false 'OWNER' stamp on a machine turn manufactures authority out of nothing. Because D-004 makes absence-of-evidence an AFFIRMATIVE owner stamp, every gap in this system drains toward the dangerous direction by default. C2, C3, C4 and C5 exist to grade that direction specifically.\n\nREVISION HISTORY THE GRADER SHOULD READ AS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE SUBJECT, NOT AS APOLOGY. Revision 1 said the classifier had five paths; it has six — the omitted one, machine-surface, is precisely the guard that keeps un-enrollable CLI surfaces out of the OWNER default. Revision 2 (this one) followed an independent vetting that read the code rather than my description of it and found a criterion asserting a FALSE property: the old C4 claimed 'expiry cannot flip a verdict'. It could, in the dangerous direction — an expired ledger row demoted an envelope-carrying turn to unverified-claim (safe) while promoting an envelope-less one to affirmative OWNER, because the liveness predicate was applied INSIDE the hash find. That defect is now fixed (plan D-006) and the criterion is replaced by the invariant that would have caught it. Both corrections point the same way: on this subject the important path is the one that is easiest to overlook, because it is the exception rather than the rule. Grade accordingly — prefer the branch you have not thought about.\n\nGRADER CONSTRAINT: must be neither an implementer on this plan nor this rubric's author. The author implemented the D-005 GC fix and the D-006 classifier fix and therefore cannot grade. Evidence is required per criterion — a card with bare verdicts is void (fleet rotation ruling, 2026-08-30).\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"agent-economy-flywheel-2026-08-30","title":"Agent Economy Flywheel — capability marketplace, outcome-verified billing, DAO + license-as-membership","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-30","owner":"aviynw3@gmail.com","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Agent Economy Flywheel — capability marketplace, outcome-verified billing, DAO + license-as-membership\nslug: agent-economy-flywheel-2026-08-30\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-10-11\nowner: aviynw3@gmail.com\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-08, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_work_contract_missing, bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted. Next repair: Accept the mapped clause: plans:get-specs, then plans:set-specs with lifecycleStatus:\"active\", expectedRevision set to its current revision, and every other field unchanged (keep the sourceBar pin and acceptanceRef; omitting either rides the prior value forward). That provenance-only promotion carries the bound proof and work-item contracts forward: confirm the result reports evidenceCarriedForward > 0 on a clause that had proof. If it is absent, another field changed and the proof must be re-bound at the new revision. Do NOT re-prove or amend the rubric on this code: the proof is not stale, the clause was never accepted. (R-27). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nAvi resumed remaining DAO work in AUTO on 2026-10-08, route self. su-38c4b8ff holds P-007/P-016..P-020/P-039 and operational follow-ups WI-10004824/WI-10004808. Existing audit/accounting work remains complete; implementation begins with finishing the persona-refresh funding gate, then shared paid-tool dispatch enforcement, per-turn identity metering, statements/splits, two-peer testnet verification and a mainnet cutover proposal. Real company/bank/accountant inputs remain explicit external prerequisites.\n\n**Next:** su-38c4b8ff completes WI-10004280/P-016 restart funding check and tests, then advances the remaining claimed technical items.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10004279 — Identity per-use offer: list an identity release with a per-use offer through the existing doors (publish-listing + `cupboard:publish-offer`), no new offer type. `skuRef` = the identity release; `met… <!-- P-015 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004280 — Activation gate: activating a priced identity layer through any door (launch, switch, rebind, restart) requires a funded channel or prepaid credits for its offer, else a typed refusal. Free identitie… <!-- P-016 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004281 — Inference metering interception: while a priced identity is applied, reserve a per-turn ceiling with `cupboard:meter-invocation op:reserve` before the turn, and settle the actual billed cost from `ag… <!-- P-017 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004282 — Itemized statement: extend the per-use commerce dashboard (D-062, micros) with per-identity lines for buyer and seller: inference cost, markup, DAO take, component splits. Add the mandatory listing s… <!-- P-018 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004283 — Component split down the dependency tree: the split manifest has one `component` share today. Divide it among the authors in the identity's exact dependency closure (identities-v1 P-006), integer-ato… <!-- P-019 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004284 — Two-peer paid-identity journey: a seller peer publishes a priced identity; a buyer peer funds a testnet channel, activates the identity and runs turns; receipts and vouchers settle on testnet through… <!-- P-020 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004285 — Mainnet cutover proposal (D-007 point 4): after the two-peer testnet journey (P-020) passes, su-b48451ff prepares a mainnet cutover for Avi's approval: the chain and stablecoin, the capital to fund t… <!-- P-039 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004286 — Legal scaffolding brief for counsel: entity options (WY DAO LLC vs UNA vs foundation), CLA draft, license-as-membership term sheet (free tier, revenue threshold, membership clause, version-pinning pr… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004287 — E1 shadow metering, identity-first (rescoped 2026-09-30): author a markup sheet over identity classes; generate per-org monthly \"what this would have cost\" statements from agent_usage_samples_identit… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004288 — E2 outbound paid pilot: publish 2–3 Papercusp capabilities as paid endpoints (candidates: papercusp-engineer as identity #1, rubric-grading-as-a-service, headless UI-verification); list on Bazaar + A… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004289 — E3 humans-loop pilot: minimal claim surface routing real needs_human items (route:'market'); one external human (not Avi) claims, completes, passes rubric grading; manual payout. GO = loop completes … <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004290 — Listing pipeline, rescoped 2026-09-30: the catalog and publish/listing doors exist (DAO P-008, cupboard/publish-listing.ts, cupboard:publish-* doors, blueprint listings). Remaining: the identity as t… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004291 — Per-use enforcement at the tools:invoke chokepoint, rescoped 2026-09-30 (an earlier v2 of this refresh wrongly proposed dropping it): when an agent calls an installed per-use Cupboard item, the dispa… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004292 — Discovery citizenship: publish the catalog via .well-known + ERC-8004 registration; ingest external x402/Bazaar endpoints into tools:find so papercusp agents can discover + pay third-party capabiliti… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004293 — Security vetting pipeline for third-party listings (prompt-injection review of descriptions/results, permission scoping, sandboxed probe runs, listing-time lint refusing kernel-contradicting identiti… <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004294 — Outcome-priced tiers: listings may offer refund-on-failed-grading or pay-on-shipped-evidence pricing, the optional premium tier over D-005's default; exportable audit trail (invocation → work-item → … <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004295 — Contributor payouts: retroactive, adoption- and outcome-weighted distribution from the DAO treasury (DAO P-034 Safe) to capability authors, computed from the same ledger and the per-author component … <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004296 — DAO charter v1, rescoped 2026-09-30: the governance machinery is built (DAO P-001 admission policy, P-003 quorum reducer, P-023/P-024 Safe treasury and bridge, P-037 admission certificates). Remainin… <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004297 — License-as-membership rollout: relicense under CLA'd terms; enforcement via network access (marketplace listing, federation, gateway) rather than litigation <!-- P-013 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004298 — Humans marketplace v1: standing Designated-Human roles (retainers) + task routing; DAO membership in good standing as the employer-accountability rail; disclosure, escrow, fiat payout defaults <!-- P-014 -->\n## What changed in the 2026-09-30 refresh\n\n1. **New Phase A (P-015..P-020): per-use identity billing.** Charge for use of identities published to the Cupboard, on the DAO plan's rails. It adds no payment system of its own. This is the concrete next build.\n2. **Rescoped items the DAO plan already delivered**, in whole or part: D-001, P-003, P-006, P-007, P-009, P-011, P-012. No item is dropped. Each names the as-built code it now reuses. They stay `todo` here; a rescope takes effect only when Avi approves.\n3. **Folded in the three owner ideation addenda of 2026-08-30** as proposed D-005 and D-006: identity is the top-level SKU; three rings (kernel, identity, instance); identity pricing is an inference markup while in the identity. Owner basis verified in owner-typed turns 17, 20 and 23 of session b72752ed (agent summaries: memories 5141d513, a5b30a79, f121f80e).\n\n## As-built inventory (what exists now)\n\nRails from shared-pot-dao-cupboard-v1-2026-09-04 (every item below is done):\n- **Per-use offers (P-028).** `cupboard:publish-offer` accepts `pricingModel:'per-use'` with `unitPriceMicros`, `meterUnit`, `priceVersion` and `splitManifestHash`, keyed by `skuRef` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/cupboard/publish-offer.ts). Stripe checkout refuses per-use; per-use routes to the microcharge path.\n- **Microcharge protocol (P-020).** Signed usage receipt plus cumulative voucher, bound to payer, seller/host, release, nonce, quantity, price version and split hash. Escrow is reserved before execution (p2p/microcharge.ts).\n- **Metering interception (P-031).** `cupboard:meter-invocation { op: reserve | settle | usage }` (agent-tools/cupboard/meter-invocation.ts, cupboard/metered-invocation-door-io.ts, p2p/metered-invocation.ts). It is an explicit door the serving code must call; nothing at the tools:invoke chokepoint calls it automatically. Also the BYOC honor path (p2p/byoc-execution.ts, used by delegated spawns in p2p/delegated-spawn-honor.ts): inference and tools run on the customer's or host's own credentials, with budget reservation/commit and privacy-preserving metering.\n- **Funding.** P-029 wallet binding (`cupboard:bind-wallet`); P-030 Stripe-funded prepaid credits; P-032 payment channels on the pilot L2 through an x402-style EVM adapter, testnet first.\n- **Settlement.** P-033 batch settlement (p2p/evm-settlement.ts). P-034 revenue split and DAO treasury (p2p/revenue-settlement.ts): an immutable per-release split manifest with shares creator, host, component, dao, reserve, tax, operating; a Safe with Zodiac Roles v2. P-035 ledger bridge. P-036 two-peer convergence and double-spend.\n- **D-062.** Per-use money is bigint micros and is never rounded into the minor-unit ledger. Receipts, settlement proofs and revenue splits roll up separately in micros, on the per-use commerce dashboard.\n- **Governance and catalog.** P-001/P-003 signed admission policy and quorum reducer; P-023/P-024 Safe treasury and on-chain bridge; P-037 admission certificates enforced at every execution door; P-008 the eleven-kind catalog with SKU, visibility and immutable releases.\n\nIdentity substrate from identities-v1-2026-08-30:\n- Identities are blueprint packages with immutable releases, installable from the Cupboard (cupboard/blueprint-release.ts, `cupboard:install-blueprint`), with publisher attestation (cupboard/identity-attestation.ts, D-124).\n- The kernel/identity/instance layering is live: the sealed kernel renders last and outranks identity and instance layers.\n- **P-009 / WI-2143750, per-identity usage attribution.** View `harness_shared.agent_usage_samples_identity_attribution` joins every inference sample (tokens, cache tokens, `cost_usd`) to the applied identity (`identity_specification_revision`, `identity_state_revision`, `identity_stack_refs`). `tool_invocations_identity_attribution` does the same for tool calls. Migrations 1149 and 1177 keep it correct across carry-respawns. identities-v1 said \"no billing in this plan\".\n\n**The gap (DAO plan D-065):** no identity install or launch path calls the meter. The attribution exists and the rails exist; nothing connects them.\n\n## Background\n\nFour interlocking ideas from the 2026-08-30 session, ordered by dependency:\n\n1. **Capability marketplace** — meter + charge for the things agents USE: tools, skills, recipes, blueprints, rubrics/graders, templates, memory/context packs, sandboxes, and (as one more listing type) humans. At drafting time Papercusp had the four marketplace mechanisms in production, unbilled: catalog (~550-tool registry + dormant `templates-marketplace`/`rubrics-marketplace` flags), discovery (`tools:find`), dispatch chokepoint (`tools:invoke`), metering ledger (`tool_invocations`). Since then the DAO plan built the billed Cupboard catalog and per-use rails (see the inventory above).\n2. **Outcome-verified billing** — the differentiator nobody in the scan has: bill/refund keyed to whether the invocation contributed to verified work (completion-integrity evidence + graded rubrics), vs. the industry's raw per-call metering.\n3. **Agents-hire-humans surface** — `needs_human` items are an organic job feed; strongest product is standing ROLES (fractional Designated Human / oversight retainers). Prior art: Payman.\n4. **DAO + license-as-membership** — commercial use above a revenue threshold requires membership; dues/rev-share fund the treasury; membership carries evidence-backed reputation-weighted governance. The DAO is the credibly-neutral registry root that corporate-owned stacks (Coinbase, OKX) cannot be.\n\nOwner addenda (2026-08-30): the marketplace's top-level SKU is a scoped agent identity: a signed, versioned package bundling persona, deny-by-default tool grants, skills, recipes, rubrics, knowledge packs, engine and autonomy defaults, installable in one click. Its track record accrues to the identity. Components stay individually sellable beneath it, with revenue splitting down its dependency tree. Pricing: metered as an inference markup while in that identity, not per tool call and not as a salary.\n\nCompetitive scan (2026-08-30, sources in session transcript): x402 rails at 165M+ txns / $50M volume / 480k agents, free facilitator — adopt, never build. Namespace layer contested by ERC-8004 (mainnet Jan 2026), OWASP ANS, IETF DNS-AID, MCP Registry — adopt/publish to all, invent nothing. 20k+ MCP servers, &lt;5% earn revenue, &lt;$50k/day global agent-tool payments — the economy hasn't started; early, not late.\n\n## Strategy (proposed — becomes D-001..D-006 on ratification)\n\n- **D-001 (proposed; largely settled by the DAO plan) Adopt rails:** the DAO plan adopted x402-style cumulative vouchers on a pilot L2 and stablecoin (its D-014/D-018), with Stripe for fiat top-ups (its P-030/P-038). This plan adds no rail.\n- **D-002 (proposed) Adopt namespace:** publish capabilities via `.well-known`, register via ERC-8004, list on x402 Bazaar / Agentic.Market. No proprietary naming system.\n- **D-003 (proposed) Build the white space only:** outcome-verified billing on the evidence ledger; the identity as the top listing type in one cross-category catalog; the DAO as neutral governance root (its machinery now exists).\n- **D-004 (proposed) Evidence before build:** Phase 1 experiments gate Phase 2+, and identity shadow statements (P-003) gate live identity charging (P-017). Rep-only governance at first; no transferable token without counsel.\n- **D-005 (proposed; owner addendum #3) Identity pricing is an inference markup while in that identity:** bill = inference at billed cost (after prompt cache) + identity markup % + DAO take, itemized. The markup splits down the identity's dependency tree to component authors. Attribute the whole session while the identity is applied; never split kernel from identity tokens inside one context window. Zero charge while idle. Per-accepted-outcome piecework stays an optional premium tier (P-010). Guardrails against token farming: an itemized invoice, burn knobs (persona size, effort, loop cadence) declared and diffed as listing metadata, and a mandatory cost-per-accepted-outcome listing stat.\n- **D-006 (proposed; owner addenda #1 and #2) Identity is the top-level SKU, in three rings:** sealed kernel > identity > instance. The kernel is monotonic: an identity may add duties, never remove them. Lint refuses kernel-contradicting identities at listing time; the kernel renders authoritatively at run time. identities-v1 built the layering; what remains is the listing-time lint (P-009) and papercusp-engineer as identity #1 (P-004).\n\n## Requirements\n\nAcceptance bars written at activation (2026-09-30, su-b48451ff) from the owner turns mapped in the activation audit. One observable outcome per bar. Every open plan item has at least one bar, and no bar spans two items. Ratified 2026-09-30 by Avi's approval of the refreshed plan (owner dialog, session 6a87256d).]\n\nThe marketplace's top-level SKU is a scoped agent identity: a signed, versioned package of persona, deny-by-default tool grants, skills, recipes, rubrics, knowledge packs, and engine and autonomy defaults, installable in one click. Use it; do not add a second registry.\nRelated: P-017, P-018, P-016\n\n### D-010 — Meter placement is the shared dispatch seat; app-credential calls carry no identity markup; assumptions (1)-(3) verified in code\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self su-b48451ff 2026-09-30, second reply on consult conv-muo94c08-0000-b503bab10bc84b88a0a3d6712da646e7 from su-77431d9c (external-app-access-to-workspaces P-001 author), plus my own code reads.]\n\n1. P-007 placement: 'the tools:invoke chokepoint' in P-007's text means the shared dispatch seat every transport passes (projected-tool-deps.ts PROJECTED_DEPS / the kernel seat), not the tools:invoke wrapper. Never key a meter on the tools:invoke wrapper's outer ctx.principal (requirePrincipal:false, a synthesized transport principal). Key on the target-bound ctx, or on serverAudit.identityLaunchRecord (D-009 point 7).\n3. Reserve/settle must stay off the synchronous request path: reserve once per turn (P-017's per-turn ceiling), settle after, and batch vouchers for on-chain settlement. A per-call synchronous channel round trip would cap throughput (relay bench: about 1,000 req/s per connector, hard refusal past 32 in-flight).\n5. Assumptions (1)-(3) were not vouched for by either consult reply, so I verified them in code. Measured: (1) packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/cupboard/publish-offer.ts:16-50 accepts pricingModel 'per-use' and requires unitPriceMicros/meterUnit/priceVersion/splitManifestHash; (2) packages/operator-core/lib/p2p/revenue-settlement.ts:5-7 RevenueShare includes 'dao' in bps, :69-90 assigns the rounding remainder to the DAO; (3) packages/operator-core/lib/p2p/microcharge.ts:93 reserveMicrocharge / :118 settleMicrocharge on CumulativePaymentVoucher, packages/operator-core/lib/p2p/metered-invocation.ts:224 openMeteredInvocation / :316 closeMeteredInvocation.\nRelated: P-007, P-017, P-015\n\n### D-011 — Identity funding binding (skuRef -> channelId) lives in local Postgres; the hosted Cupboard stays the authority on channel state\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self su-b48451ff 2026-09-30, from code reads; governs P-016 and P-017.]\n\nMeasured (repo papercusp):\n- Hosted payment channels are principal-scoped escrow. The channel row has no seller, offer or release column (apps/operator-public/src/payment-channel-store.ts PaymentChannelRow).\n- The hosted metered door takes channelId and offerId on every call (apps/operator-public/src/routes/metered-usage.ts POST /commerce/metered-invocations). Which channel pays for which identity is therefore the buyer's routing choice, not a fact the hosted side holds.\n- The per-use checkout preflight already returns channel.channelId together with channel.releaseRef (packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/commerce-door-gate-io.ts PerUseCheckoutPreflightOk), but nothing stores that pair.\n- No operator code opens channels or reads prepaid balances today (only metered-invocation-door-io.ts reads channel usage).\n- Deploying the prod Cupboard worker is owner-authorized (memory b94fecea), so a hosted binding would put a deploy wall in front of P-016 and P-017.\n\nRuling:\n1. The binding (workspace, hosted principal, identity skuRef) -> channelId is stored in a new local table written through the cupboard doors. It is written in two ways: when a per-use checkout preflight returns an identity-release releaseRef, and by an explicit bind door that first confirms the channel through the hosted owner-only GET /commerce/payment-channels/:channelId.\n2. The hosted Cupboard remains the authority on funds. The activation gate re-reads the channel (GET /commerce/payment-channels/:channelId) and the prepaid balance (GET /commerce/prepaid-credits/balance) on every activation. A closed, failed or exhausted channel, or credits with debt, refuses the next activation. A stored binding alone never counts as funding.\n3. Prepaid credits need no binding; they are a balance of the principal.\n4. P-017 reads the same binding to choose the channelId for the per-turn markup meter.\n5. Fail closed only for Cupboard-installed identity releases. When their offer or funding cannot be read, the gate refuses with a typed identity-pricing-unverifiable code. Local layers and the kernel are never priced and never gated.\nRelated: P-016, P-017\n\n### D-012 — P-016 restart and rebind doors: a refused priced layer is dropped from the refreshed render, never kept by fail-soft; priced ancestors count\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self su-b48451ff 2026-09-30, from code reads; governs P-016. Point 1 revised 17:00Z the same day: both restart callers persist `stack: artifact.stack`, so keeping the old stack in the record would desynchronise it from the stored artifact.]\n\nMeasured (repo papercusp):\n- The restart door is the SU persona refresh (packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-mcp/bootstrap-su-persona-refresh.ts) and the codex home repair (endpoint-route/routes/adv/sessions.ts, around the rebuildSuLaunchArtifact call). Both rebuild the launch artifact, neither provisions, and both persist the rebuilt artifact's stack on the launch record.\n- The pty host keeps the INHERITED render when a refresh fails (apps/operator/scripts/psu-pty-host.mjs, refresh fallback). A refresh that only throws on an unfunded layer would therefore leave the priced identity active after a restart, which defeats 'revocation stops the next activation'.\n- coord:rebind-identity does not recompile the launch artifact (agent-tools/coordination/rebind-identity.ts reads launch_spec fleet only). Its next activation happens at the restart door.\n- The first gate resolved only each stack entry's own file. A local layer that extends an installed priced identity loaded the priced layer without being gated.\n\nRuling:\n1. Restart doors call one shared helper, rebuildSuLaunchArtifactFunded (packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/identity-activation-restart.ts). It rebuilds, admits the stack, and on refusal rebuilds once more with the refused stack entries removed. The refreshed render carries no unfunded priced layer. The caller persists that artifact as it does today, so the refused entries also leave the launch record: a detach. They come back only through a re-attach, which is the gated switch door. The response reports identityActivationRefusal and removedLayerRefs.\n2. If removing stack entries cannot cure a refusal (for example, a priced layer that arrives only through a derived fleet or mode layer), the helper throws IdentityActivationRefusedError. The caller answers with a typed refusal and must not fall back to the inherited render. The codex repair's pinned-prompt recovery path admits the record's stack before reusing the prior bytes, and refuses (402) instead of degrading them.\n3. Gating walks each stack entry's full extends chain. A priced installed identity reached as an ancestor is charged and refused under the stack entry that pulled it in (layerRef = that stack entry).\n4. Launch, switch (attach/switch/rollback) and restart are the gated doors. Rebind is covered through restart. Detach never activates a layer and is never gated.\nRelated: P-016, D-011\n\n### D-013 — Pre-mainnet ledger and transparency phase (owner rulings 2026-09-30)\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-30, AskUserQuestion answers in session su-e77d337d, owner directive #1057 part 2; write-up ~/.papercusp/artifacts/dao-launch-and-auditable-banking-2026-09-30.md, WI-10004323]\n1. DAO features for the open-source launch: a tamper-evident (hash-chained, on-chain anchored) ledger and a public transparency report. Treasury spend proposals and contributor bounties were offered and NOT selected.\n2. Report cadence: Avi asked \"why monthly, shouldnt that be generated like every hour?\" Ruling: a LIVE layer refreshed hourly with the ledger root anchored hourly, plus a signed monthly statement that makes fiat numbers final after Stripe/bank/chain reconciliation (card settlement lags days and refunds can reverse sales weeks later, so hourly fiat numbers are labelled provisional).\n3. Entity: operating company now (owns Stripe, bank accounts, taxes); DAO legal wrapper added before mainnet to own the Safe.\n4. Placement: a new phase in THIS plan, before the mainnet cutover (P-039). The phase is held for Avi's review: its root items are needs-human until he approves; nothing in it starts before then.\n\n### D-014 — Owner approved the pre-mainnet ledger/transparency phase and the Stripe-verifiability additions\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-01, directive #1121, session 6027fde3 turn after the D-013 recap] Verbatim: \"I approve all but what technologies will we be using to back this?\"\nReading (recorded by su-eeace879, stated back to Avi in the same turn): approves (a) the D-013 phase P-040..P-045 held for his review, and (b) the three additions offered to make Stripe revenue publicly checkable, because a hash chain anchored on chain proves the ledger was not altered but not that it matches what Stripe collected: (1) salted per-payment commitments in the anchored Merkle root, with customer inclusion receipts and an open verifier; (2) the DAO 10% share moved on chain to the Safe so Safe receipts can be cross-checked against reported revenue (already an invariant in P-043/P-044); (3) independent attestation of the Stripe side: a monthly accountant sign-off anchored on chain, plus a research spike on zkTLS proofs of Stripe API responses (maturity unevaluated).\nThe technology stack is PROPOSED by su-eeace879 in the same turn, not yet an owner ruling. P-045 remains owner work (company, bank accounts, Stripe live mode, Safe signers).\n\n### D-015 — Build route for Phase B: su-eeace879 builds it itself, in AUTO mode\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-01, directive #1127] Verbatim: \"okay, this looks good.  put yourself on auto mode and you build this all yourself now\". Given after the provenance split (prior research vs new, unresearched suggestions) in directive #1125's answer, so \"this looks good\" accepts the proposed stack including the new items.
