Test mode and testnet only; mainnet stays behind P-039.\n\n### D-016 — Bill-grade shadow statements count only cost_source='provider' rows\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self su-b48451ff 2026-10-01, from WI-10004493] D-005 prices identities on \"billed cost\". The only cost_source values any usage writer assigns are 'estimated' and 'provider' (libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/usage-sample-pg.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/interactive-usage/ingest-claude-transcripts.ts). The shadow markup sheet had billGradeCostSources = ['billed'], a value no writer emits, so no statement could ever be bill-grade.\n\nRULING: \"billed cost\" in D-005 means cost_source='provider' (the provider reported the charge). 'estimated' rows are list-price estimates from token counts and stay non-bill-grade. Applied in packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/shadow-metering.ts (SHADOW_MARKUP_SHEET_VERSION e1-2026-10-01), pinned by a test that fails if the sheet names a source no writer assigns.\n\nCAVEAT [inferred]: provider-reported cost on subscription-seat traffic may itself be notional (flat-fee seats). September had only 158 provider rows ($1,298.51) against ~$278k estimated, so bill-grade coverage is near zero today. That is the P-003 GO-signal gap tracked on WI-10004494, not a reason to count estimates as billed. Stored estimates are also frozen at write-time prices; see the bug filed alongside this Decision.\n\n### D-017 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: wi10004521-r27-r37-apply\nRequest-Hash: 933a9f6e3200e67413d80e247ce6d0f53385794c82aef6c54f190e9fd1624e6a\nActor: su-b48451ff-a428-4deb-b138-f41d782bc5e6\nReason: Add R-27..R-37 for Phase B items P-039..P-048 (D-013/D-014/D-015), drafted by su-b48451ff and wording-checked by su-eeace879 on WI-10004521; approved by su-ce16248e (thread-post:1152432).\nApproved-By: su-ce16248e-063e-44a9-8a16-e4f658ad61c7\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1152432\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T03:26:36.945Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 61 → 62\nChanged BARs: R-27, R-28, R-29, R-30, R-31, R-32, R-33, R-34, R-35, R-36, R-37\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-018 — Estimated usage cost is re-priced in place under a derived price-table version, not priced at read time (WI-10004517)\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self su-b48451ff 2026-10-01] Context: agent_usage_samples.cost_usd (cost_source='estimated') was computed once at write time from @papercusp/model-pricing and never revisited. The table changed at least 9 times in September, so a month mixed price regimes, and rows unpriced at write time (3,343 in September, mostly gpt-6-*) stayed NULL after their model gained a price.\n\nDecision: (b) re-price in place. (1) @papercusp/model-pricing derives PRICE_TABLE_VERSION from the table's content (a hash), so any price edit changes the version without a hand bump. (2) agent_usage_samples gains price_table_version (migrations 1280 column, 1281 index); all three writers stamp it on every non-provider row. (3) repriceUsageSamples (operator-core lib/interactive-usage/reprice-usage-samples.ts) re-derives cost_usd/cost_source for every non-provider row whose stamp differs from the running version, using the SAME costFromTokens over a reconstruction of each writer's TokenUsage from the stored columns, then stamps it. The interactive ingester prices through that same reconstruction, so writer and repricer agree by construction. It runs after each interactive-usage-ingest tick (extends that routine; no new routine). Provider-reported cost is never touched. (4) Shadow statements report their cost basis (running version, stale rows, unpriced rows) and are not bill-grade while any row is stale or unpriced.\n\nWhy not (a) read-time pricing: 85 non-test source files read cost_usd. Pricing only in the shadow reader would leave every other spend surface on frozen prices, and a SQL re-implementation of costFromTokens (long-context tiers, cache-write tiers, unpriced conditions) would be a second formula that drifts. A stored estimate is a derived value, not an observation, so re-deriving it rewrites no history; the price history stays in git.\n\nAccepted cost: after a price change the repricer rewrites up to ~1.3M rows, bounded per tick (default 200k).\n\n### D-019 — Repricing keeps tier-unknown cache-write rows at the 5-minute floor, marked as a lower bound (never re-derived to NULL)\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed su-b48451ff 2026-10-01, WI-10004517; refines D-018]\n\nEvidence: a read-only dry pass of the D-018 repricer over 57,410 sampled live agent_usage_samples rows found 582 priced rows it would have turned into NULL (in-sample $3.9k; opus-4-7 $1,796 to $0.03, opus-5 471 rows, opus-4-8, sonnet-4-6). Cause: about 8.5k interactive Anthropic rows from Jun to Sep have cache writes but NULL 5m/1h split columns (written before the split existed). costFromTokens now refuses an unknown TTL tier (\"do not guess a price\"), so re-deriving them nulls them. A distinguishing test on 3,000 random such rows showed the old writer stored exactly the 5-minute-rate cost under today's table: opus-4-7 254/254, opus-4-8 133/133, sonnet-4-6 171/171, opus-5 2,300/2,315. So those values are FLOORS, not guesses.\n\nRuling: priceStoredUsageSample (used by both the ingester and the repricer) prices a tier-unknown row at the 5-minute floor when the model is priced, keeps cost_source='estimated' (so the four spend reports that sum 'estimated' do not lose the history), and records usage_provenance.costBound='lower'. A known split later clears the bound and replaces the floor with the exact price. A floor is never bill-grade (billGradeCostSources is ['provider']), and shadow statements report lower-bound samples in their cost basis.\n\nAlso found: claude-opus-5-5 tier-unknown rows sit above even today's upper bound, because the cache-read rate was corrected (0.4 to 0.2/M). The floor re-derive corrects them; nulling would have hidden them.\n\n### D-020 — Unknown-tier floor covers the long-context tier, lives in model-pricing, and the price stamp covers the pricing rules (extends D-019)\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self su-b48451ff 2026-10-01, WI-10004517] Context: the D-019 dry run (57,479 live stale rows) left two problems. (1) A model with a long-context tier (gpt-6-astra/sol/luna, gpt-6.1-sol since 2026-09-23; gpt-5.4 since 2026-10-01) makes costFromTokens refuse any aggregate row, because an aggregate has no request size. 312 gpt-6-astra interactive aggregates priced before 2026-09-23 would be nulled; they are stored at exactly the standard-context price (row 120573: 10x0.36671 + 50x0.009444 + 1x7.333632 = 11.472932). Another 402 priced gpt-5.4 aggregates (104 interactive, 298 jsonl) would be nulled the same way, and 3,448 gpt-6 aggregates are already NULL. (2) PRICE_TABLE_VERSION hashes only the table. The deployed ingester has already stamped 601 gpt-6-astra aggregates with the current version and NULL cost, so a rule change such as D-019 never reaches rows stamped before it.\n\nRuling:\n(a) An unknown tier is priced at its cheapest rate and marked as a lower bound. This covers the long-context tier of an aggregate (input and output multipliers capped at 1) as well as D-019's cache-write TTL. Unknown model, unreported cache writes, and an inconsistent tier breakdown still refuse.\n(b) The floor lives in @papercusp/model-pricing: costFromTokens(model, usage, { unknownTier: 'floor' }) returns bound:'lower'. The default stays 'refuse', so gateway/billing callers are unchanged. Every agent_usage_samples writer (interactive ingester via priceStoredUsageSample, agent-usage-telemetry 'headers', orchestrator usage-sample-pg 'jsonl') and the repricer use floor mode and persist usage_provenance.costBound.\n(c) PRICE_TABLE_VERSION hashes the table plus PRICING_RULES_REVISION. Bump that revision whenever costFromTokens's derivation of a given usage changes, so every stamped row is re-derived the same way a price change does.\n\nAlternatives rejected: keep nulling aggregates (it erases cost the writer measured); price the long tier (an overstatement); a separate rules-version column (every writer and reader would need a second comparison).\n\n### D-021 — Phase B tech-choice vetting: EAS attest() on Base Sepolia, RFC 9162 Merkle log as a generic lib, viem, OpenTimestamps deferred, Coinbase Business for live fiat-to-USDC\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed per D-015; researched by su-eeace879 2026-10-01 ~05:00Z, WI-10004598] Audit-style vetting of the five choices D-015 named as unresearched. Test mode / testnet only; mainnet stays behind P-039.\n\n1. Hourly anchor: EAS on Base Sepolia -- ADOPT WITH CONDITIONS. EAS is an OP-stack predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000021 (SchemaRegistry 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000020) on Base Sepolia (v1.2.0) and Base mainnet (v1.0.1; re-verify the ABI at P-039). Use attest() under one registered NON-revocable schema (bytes32 logRoot, uint64 treeSize, uint64 windowStart, uint64 windowEnd, string logId), NOT bare timestamp(bytes32): timestamp() reverts AlreadyTimestamped on identical data, so a quiet hour with an unchanged root would fail, while attest() lets every hour leave a record (the missed-hour alert checks for that record); attest() puts treeSize and the window on chain, so verify-anchor needs only a public RPC (getAttestation); attestations are enumerable by schema + attester from Attested event logs, so anyone can audit the cadence. Conditions: a dedicated anchor key holding gas only (never a Safe signer); the attester address is published in the P-044 report; self-hosters set their own key/chain through the open-core hook. Rejected: own contract (reuse the audited predeploy); bare timestamp() (above).\n\n2. Merkle format: RFC 6962 -> use RFC 9162 sec 2.1 -- ADOPT. RFC 9162 (Dec 2021) obsoletes 6962; the tree hashing is identical (SHA-256, 0x00 leaf / 0x01 node prefixes) and 9162 adds the inclusion- and consistency-proof verification algorithms 6962 never specified. Leaf encoding is ours (domain-tagged canonical bytes), not CT TransItem. Implement as a new zero-dependency domain-free lib libs/generic/merkle-log (tree hash, inclusion + consistency proofs) tested against the RFC 9162 example tree and the transparency-dev/merkle reference vectors; the P-046 open-source verifier bundles it. Publish consistency proofs between successive hourly roots so a verifier can prove the log only appended between anchors. Not reused: p2p/artifact-package.ts merkleRoot (a content address with a ROOT_TAG||count finalizer and no proofs; changing it would break published listing addresses).\n\n3. EVM client: viem -- ADOPT. Already resolvable in the tree (2.56.3, declared by apps/operator-public); upstream 2.56.9 (2026-09-24); MIT, maintained by wevm, Base Sepolia chain definitions built in. Do NOT add @ethereum-attestation-service/eas-sdk (it brings ethers v6, a second EVM client); call EAS/SchemaRegistry through viem with a minimal ABI fragment verified against sepolia.basescan.org. Condition: declare viem in packages/operator-core/package.json instead of relying on the hoist.\n\n4. OpenTimestamps -- NOT ADOPTED NOW. The JS library (npm opentimestamps 0.4.9, Jan 2021; old name javascript-opentimestamps deprecated) has had no release in ~5 years and one maintainer; Bitcoin confirmation puts hours of latency on a complete proof; full verification needs a Bitcoin block-header source, a second chain dependency for the verifier. The public calendars are alive (v0.7.1, free). Revisit as an optional secondary backend for self-hosters who want key-less anchoring: the open-core anchor hook is an interface so a second backend needs no caller changes.\n\n5. Fiat-to-USDC: Circle / Coinbase -- TESTNET ROUTE ADOPTED; LIVE ROUTE RECOMMENDED, OWNER-GATED. Test mode uses Circle testnet USDC on Base Sepolia 0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e (faucet.circle.com, 20 USDC per 2h; CDP faucet for gas). Live: Coinbase Business (bank-linked, USDC on Base, payouts API) is recommended over Circle Mint, which targets institutions (KYB, typically seven-figure monthly volume) and does not fit a pre-revenue company. Opening that account is Avi's work under P-045; no code depends on the live route before P-039. Base mainnet USDC 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, to re-verify at cutover.\n\nSources: github.com/ethereum-attestation-service/eas-contracts (deployments); sepolia.basescan.org/address/0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000021 (verified source incl. timestamp/AlreadyTimestamped); rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162 and rfc6962; github.com/wevm/viem + npm; opentimestamps.org, npm opentimestamps; developers.circle.com/stablecoins/usdc-contract-addresses, developers.circle.com/circle-mint, coinbase.com/blog (Coinbase Business payments), docs.base.org/tools/network-faucets.\n\n### D-022 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: amend-c3af56b970d93e67fcc706f7\nRequest-Hash: 43359b07328771aeabfc0cc6f3c9088a66564ee36c722f9ba50873a275c61136\nActor: su-b48451ff-a428-4deb-b138-f41d782bc5e6\nReason: WI-10004521: apply rubric-vetting fixes F1-F5 (consult conv-muozymlo-0000-fdc7f0743e9b475da5cf8a64eec71933, answer post 1152470)\nApproved-By: su-6fa7fadb-61fe-454a-9503-f4a18c083762\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1152640\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T05:28:15.025Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 69 → 70\nChanged BARs: R-28, R-29, R-30, R-31, R-32, R-33, R-34\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-023 — Money-journal producers: Stripe balance-transaction import + chain-transfer mapper; P-043's reconciliation run drives the import (P-042)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; WI-10004635]\n\nContext: R-30 is falsified by any money movement that is not a balanced journal entry carrying its external reference. Stripe webhook payloads (invoice.paid, checkout, refund, dispute) do not carry the balance-transaction id or the processing fee. Producers are also split across stores: hosted billing and cupboard commerce run in operator-core/PG; prepaid credits and treasury run in operator-public/D1.\n\nDecision:\n1. Stripe: the journal's Stripe producer is the account's balance-transaction list (GET /v1/balance_transactions, expand data.source + data.source.invoice). It is the authoritative ledger of every Stripe money movement, whichever checkout created it. Each BT maps to exactly one entry: entryId stripe-bt:<id>, externalRef stripe-balance-transaction, idempotent. Mapping: charge/payment -> customer-payment (fee = bt.fee, tax from the expanded invoice, DAO share + refund provision by configured basis points on gross minus tax), or credit-purchase when the charge metadata carries purpose 'prepaid-credits'; refund/payment_refund -> refund; dispute adjustment (negative) -> chargeback with the dispute fee; stripe_fee/tax_fee -> provider-payment; payout -> skipped (Stripe balance to bank stays inside 'operating'); anything else -> reported as unmapped, never silently dropped.\n2. Chain: a treasury Safe transfer maps to a dao-transfer entry keyed by its chain tx hash.\n3. Driver: P-043's scheduled reconciliation run imports first and then reconciles: journal vs the internal commerce ledger vs Stripe vs the bank feed. P-042 ships the producers and their tests; P-043 schedules them. Bank-feed producers (tax remittance, provider payments by bank) arrive with P-043's bank feed.\nRejected: posting from each webhook handler (no BT id or fee in the payload, and each needs a Stripe fetch anyway); a per-producer journal hook in D1 (the journal is PG).\n\n### D-024 — Anchor log format: per-workspace RFC 9162 log of chain links, one attest() per completed hour, open-core AnchorBackend hook (P-041)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; refines D-021; WI-10004660]\nConsumed by P-044 (report shows latest anchored root), P-046 (receipt verifier bundles the proof check), and P-047 (attestation hash anchored beside a root).\n1. Leaves: every row of harness_shared.ledger_chain_links (P-040) becomes one leaf of a per-workspace append-only RFC 9162 Merkle log (libs/generic/merkle-log). Leaf hash = leafHash('papercusp.ledger-anchor/v1/leaf\\n' + canonicalJson({entryHash, seq, streamId})). New links are appended in (streamId, seq) order at each tick. The log never reorders or rewrites.\n2. Cadence: once per completed UTC hour, publish { logId, logRoot, treeSize, windowStart, windowEnd } through an AnchorBackend. After missed hours, one anchor covers the gap (windowStart = previous windowEnd). Each stored anchor also keeps a consistency proof from the previous anchor's tree size.\n3. Open-core hook: AnchorBackend.publish / AnchorReader.read. The hosted backend is EAS attest() on Base Sepolia under the D-021 schema. A self-hosted install configures its own key and RPC through the same hook; no Papercusp service sits in the path.\n4. Proof: buildInclusionBundle returns a self-contained JSON bundle: link, optional entry, leafIndex, treeSize, logRoot, audit path, and anchor receipt (backend, chainId, attestation UID, tx, attester). It is proven against the EARLIEST anchor covering the leaf. verifyInclusionBundle recomputes entry digest, link hash, leaf hash and inclusion, then reads the attestation from public chain data and checks root, size, logId and the pinned attester.\n5. Missed hour: when the last completed hour (20-minute grace) has no anchor, the operator files ONE deduplicated alert (stable watchdogKey per workspace). A failed publication writes nothing, so it surfaces as a missed hour.\n6. Scope gap: the Cupboard D1 commerce and treasury chains (operator-public) are not in ledger_chain_links. Feeding them into the log is a follow-up work-item, not silently omitted.\n\n### D-025 — Reconciliation engine, deduped break items, and a fail-closed DAO-transfer gate pushed to the Worker (P-043)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; refines D-023 §3]\nContext: R-31 is falsified by a DAO transfer that executes while an invariant is broken, and by one break filing a new work item every hour. The journal and the Stripe import live in operator-core/PG. Prepaid credits, treasury transfers and the DAO-transfer door (POST /commerce/payment-channels/:channelId/settlements/:batchId/treasury) live in operator-public/D1.\nDecision:\n1. Engine: a pure module cupboard/reconciliation.ts evaluates named invariants over a source snapshot. Three are mandated: credit-reserve-covers-outstanding-credits (journal customer-credit-reserve >= outstanding prepaid credits, available+reserved, from D1); dao-payable-equals-accrued-minus-transferred (journal dao-payable == DAO share accrued in the commerce ledger minus DAO transfers seen on chain); safe-balance-equals-receipts-minus-approved-spends (on-chain Safe token balance == on-chain receipts minus approved spends). Three are matching checks: journal-matches-stripe, journal-matches-bank, journal-matches-chain (every external movement has exactly one journal entry, and every journal entry's external ref exists at its source, compared by amount). Each verdict is one of ok | broken | unknown (source failed) | not-configured (no such source configured; never treated as a pass, and the gate ignores it only because no transfer can use that rail).\n2. Modes: 'provisional' runs hourly over the open month; 'final' runs once after month close over the closed month and treats not-configured mandated sources as unknown.\n3. Breaks: PG reconciliation_runs plus reconciliation_breaks with a unique open-row index on (workspace, invariant). A NEW break opens exactly one work item (bug, the invariant + evidence). A break still present on a later run only bumps last_seen. Resolution stamps resolved_at and comments on the item. A later break opens a new item.\n4. Gate: DAO transfers are paused while any break is open, or any mandated invariant is unknown. operator-core pushes {open:boolean, reasons, runId, at} after every run to an HMAC-authenticated operator-public route (PUT /commerce/treasury/transfer-gate, secret RECONCILIATION_GATE_SECRET, ±5 min). D1 stores it in treasury_transfer_gate. The treasury route refuses 409 transfers_paused when the gate is closed, absent, or older than 3 h (fail-closed: a reconciliation that cannot report must not leave transfers running). An operator-only GET /commerce/treasury/reconciliation-inputs serves outstanding credits and routed DAO transfers under the same HMAC.\n5. Driver: a DBOS workflow imports Stripe balance transactions first (D-023 §3), then reconciles, persists, files or resolves items, and pushes the gate. It runs hourly, plus the final run on day 1 of each month. A cupboard:reconciliation tool gives status and a manual run.\n6. Bank feed: an interface only (BankFeedSource). No bank is connected; connecting one needs owner credentials, so journal-matches-bank is not-configured until then.\nRejected: running the reconciliation inside the Worker (the journal is PG); a GitHub-operator bearer for machine calls (needs a human token on the host); pausing only on the three named invariants (an unmatched external movement means the journal those invariants read is itself wrong).\nRelated: P-043\n\n### D-026 — Transfer gate shape: per-workspace D1 rows, a treasuryReconciled flag, monotonic pushes, final-run breaks, and the gate as the last precondition before money moves (refines D-025 §3-4, P-043)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; WI-10004681]\nContext: D-025 §4 named one gate row and four refusal states (closed, absent, stale). Building it surfaced five gaps. (a) The operator reconciles every workspace that has a journal, but one Worker owns one treasury. (b) A workspace whose run never read the Worker's credits and DAO transfers evaluates the treasury invariants as not-configured, and D-025 §1 says the gate ignores not-configured; that run could open a gate for a treasury it never looked at. (c) Pushes travel over the network, so a delayed push from an earlier run could overwrite a later closed gate. (d) A gate dated in the future would never go stale. (e) Breaks are keyed per invariant, not per period, so next month's clean provisional run would resolve a break a final run opened for the closed month.\nDecision:\n1. D1 table treasury_transfer_gate holds one row per workspace (migration 040). The var RECONCILIATION_GATE_WORKSPACE names the workspace whose gate governs this Worker's DAO transfers. Unset means no workspace vouches for the treasury, and every DAO transfer is refused.\n2. Each push carries treasuryReconciled: true only when that run read the Worker's reconciliation inputs and evaluated the treasury invariants. The door refuses a gate without it (code treasury-not-reconciled).\n3. A push replaces the stored row only when its atMs is not older than the stored atMs (ON CONFLICT ... WHERE excluded.at_ms >= at_ms). The Worker answers applied:false for an ignored push.\n4. The Worker refuses a push whose atMs is more than 5 minutes ahead of its clock (the signature tolerance).\n5. A break opened by a final run stays open through provisional runs. Only a later final run resolves it.\n6. The door checks the gate after every deterministic refusal (auth, config 503s, batch_not_final, reconciliation_failed, safe_deployment_unrecorded, routing_refused) and immediately before the first transfer is submitted. Those refusals keep their own codes, and nothing moves while the gate is closed. Refusal: 409 {error:'transfers_paused', code, detail} with code in no-governing-workspace | never-reported | break-open | treasury-not-reconciled | stale.\nRejected: one global gate row (a workspace with no treasury inputs would govern it); checking the gate before the adapter and config checks (an unconfigured deployment would report transfers_paused instead of the 503 that names the missing setting); signing the request URL's pathname rather than the fixed route path (a proxy prefix would break verification with no security gain, since the method and route are already bound into the MAC).\nEvidence: apps/operator-public/src/__tests__/reconciliation-routes.test.ts (7) and treasury.test.ts (12, incl. every paused code); packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/reconciliation.test.ts (final-run break rule).\nRelated: P-043\nRelated: P-043\n\n### D-027 — Cupboard D1 chains join the anchor log through a signed Worker link feed unioned with pgAnchorLinkFeed (closes D-024 §6, WI-10004676)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; refines D-024 §6; WI-10004676]\nContext: D-024 §6 left the Worker's D1 hash chains (commerce.ledger, commerce.event-log, commerce.prepaid-credits, treasury.transfers, treasury.safe-deployment-records) out of the anchor log. Two options: (a) the operator pulls the Worker's chain links and anchors them in the existing per-workspace log; (b) the Worker anchors its own log through the AnchorBackend hook. Option (b) would put an EAS signing key and a second log inside the Worker. Option (a) reuses the anchor log, the EAS backend, the inclusion bundles and the P-043 operator-to-Worker HMAC channel.\nDecision: option (a).\n1. Worker route: GET /commerce/ledger-chain/links, signed with the D-025 §4 HMAC (RECONCILIATION_GATE_SECRET). It returns { workspaceId: RECONCILIATION_GATE_WORKSPACE, links: [{ streamId, seq, entryHash }], nextCursor } in (stream_id, seq) order, paged by an opaque cursor. The signed path includes the query string, so a captured signature cannot fetch a different page. No secret: 503. No governing workspace: an empty page with workspaceId null.\n2. Leaf identity is unchanged: D1 links keep their own stream ids, so a verifier recomputes them from the Worker's /admin/ledger-chain/:stream/export with the same @papercusp/hash-chain rules. Bundles for D1 leaves carry no entry (the entry lives in D1).\n3. Workspace binding: D1 links belong only to the operator's treasury workspace (PAPERCUSP_RECONCILIATION_TREASURY_WORKSPACE, defaulting to the Stripe journal workspace), which must equal the Worker's RECONCILIATION_GATE_WORKSPACE. A mismatch yields no D1 links and a reported error, never links filed under the wrong log. The treasury workspace is anchored even when PG holds no links for it.\n4. Union: unionAnchorLinkFeed(primary, secondaries) concatenates links. Two sources claiming the same streamId is a hard error for that tick (leaf keys would collide). A secondary source's fetch failure is reported and that tick anchors the primary's links only; the D1 links join at the next successful tick. D-024 promises no per-window completeness, and leaves are never reordered, so a late join is sound.\n5. A Worker outage is visible: the anchor pass result carries feedErrors per workspace, and cupboard:ledger-anchor-run returns them.\nTests: the Worker route's signature, paging and workspace cases; the feed client's paging, signed query and workspace mismatch; the union's collision and degraded-secondary cases; the anchor pass appending D1 links as leaves.\n\n### D-028 — Transparency report: pure journal-derived report, hourly live push and EIP-191-signed monthly statement served by the Cupboard Worker (P-044)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; builds on D-024 (anchor log), D-025 (reconciliation), D-027 (Worker link feed). Amended 2026-10-01 to match the build (WI-10004751).]\n1. One pure function, buildTransparencyReport(entries, period, extras) in cupboard/transparency-report.ts, derives every money figure from money-journal entries (P-042), never from a second source. Revenue by stream = net credits to `revenue`, grouped by movement kind. Accounts = the period's trial balance per account, including dao-payable (the DAO's share). DAO transfers = `dao-transfer` entries with their chain-tx hash. All cents are integers. Tests pin report totals == trialBalance totals over the same entries.\n2. Treasury balance is reported only when measured; otherwise {status:'not-measured', reason}. It is never inferred from the journal. Until WI-10004708 reads the Safe on chain, every report says not-measured (TREASURY_NOT_MEASURED).\n3. Live layer: rebuilt on every ledger-anchor tick (DBOS, every 15 minutes), in a separate step right after the anchor pass, so `latestAnchor` is the root just published or the newest stored one. Period = the open UTC month; the report carries provisional:true. The push body is {workspaceId, month, generatedAtMs, report, statementStatus}, sent over the reconciliation HMAC to PUT TRANSPARENCY_LIVE_PATH (/commerce/transparency/live). The Worker keeps one row per workspace and never replaces it with an older generatedAtMs. Public read: GET /transparency/:workspaceId (live report, statement status, statement index). cupboard:ledger-anchor-run with confirm:true runs the same pass.\n4. Monthly statement: built only from the closed month's FINAL reconciliation run. It covers exactly that month, carries provisional:false, the run id and its verdicts, entriesRoot (sha256 over the period entries' digests), and latestAnchor = the FIRST stored anchored root whose window ends at or after the month end. That root commits to every chain link through the month close, including the money-journal stream; pinning the first one (never the newest) makes the statement reproducible. The digest is sha256(canonicalJson(statement)), signed with EIP-191 by the anchor key (the D-021 attester key), in cupboard/transparency-statement.ts, so anyone can recover the signer. PUT TRANSPARENCY_STATEMENT_PATH: the Worker checks digest and signature, then stores it immutably (first publication wins; an identical push is a no-op; a different digest is refused 409). Public read: GET /transparency/:workspaceId/statements/:month.\n5. The statement is withheld when the final run has ANY invariant 'broken' or a MANDATED invariant 'unknown' ('not-configured' is not a failure). statementStatus is one of: published (digest), pending (no final run for the closed month, no anchored root covering the month end, no signing key, or the Worker unreachable), withheld (withheldBy names the invariants; detail names the open breaks), none (no month has closed with journal activity). Each tick re-derives a published statement; a different digest is drift: reported in statementStatus.detail and filed once per (workspace, month) as a bug. The published statement stands.\n6. No new operator PG table: the Worker D1 copy is the published record (migration 042_transparency.sql), and the operator can recompute any statement from the journal. Code: transparency-publish.ts (pass core, no DB imports), transparency-runtime.ts (PG / key-file / work-item defaults).\n\n### D-029 — Per-payment receipts: salted commitments on a stripe.payment-receipts hash chain, proven by the D-024 inclusion bundle, verified offline (P-046)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; builds on D-023 (Stripe balance-transaction import), D-024 (anchor log + inclusion bundle), P-040 (hash chains)]\n1. Commitment: for each Stripe balance transaction, commitment = SHA-256('papercusp.payment-receipt/v1\\n' + salt + '\\n' + canonicalJson({amount, created, currency, fee, id})), salt = 32 random bytes (hex). The salt makes a low-entropy amount unguessable from the commitment, so totals stay public while individual payments stay private.\n2. Storage: harness_shared.payment_receipts (workspace_id, balance_transaction_id, receipt_seq, salt, commitment, amount, fee, currency, stripe_created, source_id, source_customer, recorded_at). One row per balance transaction, idempotent on (workspace_id, balance_transaction_id). The salt is confidential: only the receipt holder gets it.\n3. Chain: a new hash-chain stream 'stripe.payment-receipts' (LedgerSource over payment_receipts in receipt_seq order, entry = { commitment } only). witnessLedgerAfterAppend links each new row into ledger_chain_links, so the existing pg feed puts it in the hourly anchor log (D-024) with no new anchoring code. Neither the chain table nor the log ever holds a plaintext amount.\n4. Producer: the reconciliation pass's Stripe import (runReconciliationPass) records a receipt for every balance transaction it lists, whether the journal maps, skips or flags it, because the receipt commits to what Stripe reported.\n5. Receipt: { format:'papercusp.payment-receipt', version:1, transaction:{id, amount, currency, fee, created}, salt, commitment, bundle } where bundle is the D-024 AnchorInclusionBundle for the receipt's chain link with entry {commitment}. Before the covering hour is anchored the issuer answers not-yet-anchored.\n6. Verifier: verifyPaymentReceipt(receipt, reader, {expectedAttester}) recomputes the commitment from transaction + salt, requires it to equal bundle.entry.commitment and the link's stream to be 'stripe.payment-receipts', then runs verifyInclusionBundle against the public chain (easAnchorReader over a public RPC). The module imports no PG code, and a CLI (verify-payment-receipt) wraps it so anyone can check a receipt with only the receipt file and an RPC URL.\n7. Delivery: operator tool cupboard:payment-receipt { balanceTransactionId } issues a receipt; the signed-in customer fetches receipts for their own charges through the hosted-billing API (matched on the charge's Stripe customer).\nRelated: P-046\n\n### D-030 — P-048 zkTLS verdict: NO-GO for Phase B; Stripe-side assurance comes from P-047 plus Stripe's own verified-metrics profile; revisit on named triggers\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; research spike WI-10004806, sources on that item]\n\nQuestion (P-048): can zkTLS / TLS-notarization give a third-party-verifiable proof that a Stripe API response (balance or payout totals) said what we publish, without revealing the API key or customer data?\n\nFindings:\n1. Maturity. TLSNotary, the open base layer, is v0.1.0-alpha.15 (May 2026, pre-release), TLS 1.2 only. api.stripe.com still accepts TLS 1.2, so it would work today. The project removed its notary server from the repo in alpha.13; notary.pse.dev is development-only with no SLA. Production use means running or paying for a notary/verifier.\n2. Trust. A portable proof is only as good as a notary that is independent of the prover, because prover + notary collusion forges anything. Running our own notary proves nothing. Every hosted option moves trust to a vendor or to TEE hardware: Reclaim (proxy attestors, now two TEE attestors per IACR 2026/2187), Opacity (TLSNotary + SGX + EigenLayer slashing), vlayer (Intel TDX notaries), Primus/zkPass (proxy or MPC). Proxy mode also assumes an honest network path (BGP hijack risk).\n3. Claim gaps specific to our use. (a) Account binding: GET /v1/balance does not name the account, so a prover could prove another Stripe account's numbers. Binding needs /v1/account in the same session plus a public statement of which account id is ours, which only an outside party (the P-047 accountant, or Stripe itself) can give. (b) Completeness: monthly totals need every page of /v1/balance_transactions (last page has_more:false) or a Reporting API CSV, so many notarized sessions per month. (c) livemode must be revealed or test-mode numbers pass. (d) It proves Stripe said it, not that revenue is genuine (wash payments). (e) The secret key travels in the Authorization header: selective disclosure can redact it, and a restricted read-only key bounds the exposure.\n4. Cost. Software is open source and roughly 1-2 s (proxy) to 4-16 s (MPC) per small request. The real cost is an independent notary operator (no published pricing) and owning a pre-1.0 Rust/WASM prover pinned to one protocol version.\n\nDecision:\n- NO-GO for Phase B. zkTLS would swap trust in our report for trust in a notary vendor or TEE, and it still needs the outside account binding that P-047 provides anyway.\n- Stripe-side assurance for Phase B = P-047 (accountant monthly sign-off, hash anchored on chain) plus Stripe's own verified-metrics profile (profile.stripe.com, Stripe as first-party attester, no key handed to anyone), linked from the transparency report once Stripe is in live mode (P-045). That link is filed as an owned follow-up.\n- Revisit when ANY of these holds: TLSNotary ships a stable 1.0 (or TLS 1.3 support) AND an independent notary network we do not control offers terms; a customer, auditor or regulator asks for a cryptographic Stripe-side proof; Stripe offers a signed balance/payout statement API.\n- If revisited, the shape is: one notarized session per month over /v1/account + every /v1/balance_transactions page with a restricted read-only key, Authorization header redacted, livemode and account id revealed, attestation hash anchored beside that month's root (same slot as P-047).\n\n### D-031 — P-047 statement attestations: a public attestation record chained on transparency.statement-attestations, bound to the signed statement digest (and so to its month root), proven by the D-024 bundle\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; builds on D-024 (anchor log + inclusion bundle), D-028 (signed monthly statement); WI-10004816]\n1. Record (public, unsalted): { format:\"papercusp.statement-attestation\", version:1, workspaceId, month, statementDigest, monthRoot:{logId,treeSize,logRoot,ref}, documentSha256, attestor:{name,firm|null}, attestedOn:\"YYYY-MM-DD\", scope }. scope is a non-empty subset of stripe-balance-transactions, stripe-payouts, bank-feed; P-047 asks for all three, but a subset is allowed until a bank account exists (P-045) and the verifier reports which were attested. The document itself (the accountant's signed PDF) is never stored, only its SHA-256.\n2. Binding: at record time the month's statement must be published on the Cupboard Worker and its digest must equal statementDigest; monthRoot is copied from that statement's report.latestAnchor (the root covering month end, D-028). Because the statement digest covers latestAnchor, the attestation is bound to the month root through the statement, not by a second claim. A month with no published statement refuses (statement-not-published); a digest mismatch refuses (statement-digest-mismatch).\n3. Storage + anchoring: harness_shared.statement_attestations (append-only, unique per workspace+month+documentSha256; a corrected attestation is a new row, never an edit). The record itself is the chain entry on stream transparency.statement-attestations, so the hourly anchor run (D-024) commits it to a later root of the same log. \"Alongside that month's root\" = same log, later root: the verifier checks bundle.logId == monthRoot.logId and bundle.treeSize >= monthRoot.treeSize; the D-024 consistency proofs between successive anchors already show the later root extends the month root.\n4. Proof + verification: proof = { attestation, bundle } with bundle.entry = the record. verifyStatementAttestation checks format, entry equality, stream, same-log/later-root, optional document SHA-256, then verifyInclusionBundle against public chain data. Pure module, no Postgres, so a public verifier can import it.\n5. Surface: operator tool cupboard:statement-attestation { op: record | proof | list }. Showing attestation status on the public transparency page is a follow-up.\n6. Out of scope: engaging the outside accountant (owner work, alongside P-045).\n\n### D-032 — Independent DAO accrual: journal FINAL settlement claims and take the accrual from the Worker's allocations (P-043 residue WI-10004709)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed su-eeace879, AUTO per D-015; refines D-025 §1]\nContext: dao-payable-equals-accrued-minus-transferred fell back to the journal's own dao-payable credits as the accrual, so it only checked the transfer leg. WI-10004709 proposed passing the DAO share of FINAL settlement batches as the accrual. Measured: nothing journals a settlement claim. dao-payable is credited only by Stripe customer-payments (and by usage-settlement, which has no production caller), while every DAO transfer is drawn from a settlement batch's dao allocation and IS journaled (debit dao-payable). Passing the settlement accrual alone would therefore break the invariant on the first final batch, and the break would be real: the journal lacks the EVM rail's revenue and DAO accrual.\nDecision:\n1. GET /commerce/treasury/reconciliation-inputs also serves every FINAL settlement batch as {batchId, chainId, claimTransactionHash, claimMicros, daoMicros, finalizedAtMs}, oldest first.\n2. The treasury workspace's run imports each one as a customer-payment entry keyed chain-tx:<chainId>:<claimTxHash>: grossCents = cents(claimMicros), daoCents = cents(daoMicros), no fee, tax or refund provision; occurredAt = finalizedAtMs (finality is when the money counts, acceptance line 14). journal-matches-chain lists these claims as inflows beside the DAO transfers.\n3. The accrual is composed per rail: journal dao-payable credits on non-chain entries (Stripe and bank rails, which their matching checks tie to those sources) plus the Worker's DAO allocation of final batches finalized before the period end, each rounded to cents per batch exactly as the import rounds it. A missing, duplicated, mis-split or hand-posted chain-rail accrual now breaks the invariant.\n4. A final batch that later goes disputed or refunded leaves the listing while its journal entry stays: the invariant breaks until a reversing entry is posted. That is intended.\nRejected: passing the settlement accrual as the whole accrual (breaks on every Stripe DAO credit and on every final batch); recomputing the Stripe rail's DAO share from Stripe (needs full history each run, and the import already uses the same policy).\nRelated: P-043, WI-10004709, D-025\n\n### D-033 — P-019 component authorship binds exact dependency pins in the existing split manifest\nDate: 2026-10-08\n[self-imposed under Avi AUTO/self scope; implementation unit WI-10004283, remaining integration still open.] Measured: packages/operator-core/lib/p2p/revenue-settlement.ts had one component allocation and canonical split/receipt hashes; evm-settlement.ts:203 passes that manifest to settleRevenue and hosted treasury.ts:385 rechecks receipts through reconcileSettlement. Reuse these surfaces. Extend the manifest with componentDependencies entries {packageKind,ref,revision,contentHash,author}; the identity-release producer must supply the exact verified dependency closure (exclude the identity root, which receives creator share), never reconstruct it from current mutable source. Each unique dependency has one unit; coalesce units by author, distribute component micros by largest remainder with deterministic code-unit author ordering, and retain the existing DAO allocation/rounding. The receipt includes componentAllocationsMicros and reconciliation re-derives every author amount, refusing missing, extra or tampered recipients even if the sum is unchanged. Manifest hash binds dependency versions, hashes and authors. Old manifests without componentDependencies retain their existing digest and behavior. This settles the arithmetic unit only; published identity offer binding, exact-closure author resolution, Worker wire persistence and payout/statement use must still be integrated before P-019 closes.\nRelated: P-019, P-017, P-018\n\n### D-034 — P-019 reuses priceVersion for exact component pins and the retained release for attribution\nDate: 2026-10-08\nDate: 2026-10-08\n[turn:self] Self-imposed within Avi AUTO/self scope. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for capless-inference-gateway-2026-08-28, authored against as-built reality after implementation. The plan's goal is that inference admission stops being governed by numeric productive-capacity maxima and starts being governed by measured physical contracts with causal attribution, behind a durable queue, with work-conserving priority, one canonical state model, a drilled rollback, and continued upward probing after recovery. These seven criteria are the plan-specific OUTCOMES; the shared invariants (tests landed with the feature, no unregistered dark ship, live through the gate, docs updated, audit citations spot-checked) come from classRef plan-class-feature-ship and are not restated here. Grading class chosen in D-019 (the plan carries 19 decisions, D-001..D-019, plus D-020 added during vetting).\n\nGRADER NOTE: P-014 and P-015 were implemented by su-b5211 (the rubric author), so criteria 3, 6 and 7 are where an independent read is worth the most; treat every implementer claim below as a pointer to a probe, never as evidence.\n\nONE AGGREGATION RULE, applying to ALL SEVEN criteria (this replaces three per-criterion caveats that would have drifted apart, and makes `unknown` mean the same thing everywhere): a criterion with ANY leg unmeasured or unresolved is capped at `partial`; `pass` requires EVERY leg measured; a leg that CONTRADICTS another leg of the same criterion is `fail` regardless of the rest. The point of running several probes is that runtime can disagree with source, and that disagreement must never be averaged away.\n\nREVISION 3 — rewritten twice under independent vetting (su-98f41fcf and su-ac7fc651, consults conv-mtf439en and conv-mtf4h4uz). Recorded because these were concessions, not polish. Revision 2 fixed: C3's 'record the live ratio as PENDING' (not a value emit accepts, and it let C3 reach a full pass with its only production-measured leg excused) became a rating cap; C1 gained an explicit aggregation rule, now generalised above; all criteria gained structured `check` bindings where every one had been check:null; the header ratingScale was aligned off the schema's placeholder healthy/degraded/broken/unknown, which has no 'do not ship' point. Revision 3 fixes a COVERAGE gap neither I nor the first critic saw: all six criteria were SAFETY properties (nothing binds, nothing rejects, nothing misrepresents, nothing reinstates, nothing inflates) while the plan's goal also commits to a LIVENESS property — contractions expire AND upward probing resumes. A lane that contracts on a real fault, expires the fault on schedule, and then sits at the contracted value forever passed all six. C7 exists to fail that. Vetting also surfaced a live production defect in P-013's deliverable, now fixed and recorded as D-020; see C4.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nSUCCESSOR to the retired rubric email-calendar-web-desktop-ship-2026-08-27-acceptance. Authored by the implementer (su-accf0e6a). REVISION 2 — revised after independent vetting, which found three defects in revision 1: its re-affirmation exemption was keyed on the wrong variable, the non-movement check it relied on fails OPEN, and criterion 1 credited a read-API round trip as evidence for a claim about a WEB UI.\n\nWHY A SUCCESSOR EXISTS. This plan shipped at 2026-08-30T00:04Z on a complete independent grading by su-799a2f56 (scorecard EI-21833310247310216, superseding EI-21832584701743975) that rated `web-apps-real-data` PARTIALLY-MET against that rubric's own drift marker — 'partially-met if one app is demonstrated and the other is not'. Email was substantially demonstrated; Calendar was not. Rather than leave a known evidence gap standing inside a shipped record, this session returned the plan to `ready` at 2026-08-30T02:03Z, closed the Calendar gap under plan platform-to-app-data-producer-2026-08-30 item P-008, and is re-grading. The original rubric could not be re-activated: proposeRubric pins a retired acceptance rubric's status (rubrics.ts:1569-1572) and ratifyRubric refuses acceptance-kind rubrics outright (rubrics.ts:1856-1862), because the platform's ruling is that reopening a closed acceptance contract needs a successor, not a content upsert. That ruling is recorded as D-018 on platform-to-app-data-producer-2026-08-30. The retired rubric is untouched and stands as the record of what was accepted at 00:04Z.\n\nTHE THREE CHECKOUTS (every method below names its root; resolve paths only against these):\n  CALENDAR = /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/calendar\n  EMAIL    = /home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/email\n  PLATFORM = /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp\nThey have a deliberately identical layout, so an unqualified path such as tests/native-package.e2e.test.ts exists in BOTH app roots and silently resolves to whichever root you happen to be in. Never evaluate a criterion from an unnamed root.\n\nRECORD THE IDENTITY BEFORE YOU RATE ANYTHING. Before rating any criterion, paste into your card, for EACH of the three roots, the output of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `git rev-parse HEAD`. A criterion evaluated from a root you did not record grades `unknown`, never `met`. Two evidence rules follow: (a) `git blame` and commit SUBJECTS are NOT evidence in these repositories and must not be cited — git-sync sweeps the tree on a schedule under one identity and labels commits with whatever agent context was current, so blame names the wrong author and the subject describes the sweeping agent's intent rather than the diff; (b) when a criterion claims a specific file carries a specific change, establish it by BLOB IDENTITY (`git rev-parse <sha>:<path>`) or by reading the file's current content — never by a commit message that mentions it.\n\nTHE RE-AFFIRMATION RULE, AND WHY REVISION 1'S VERSION WAS WRONG. Revision 1 keyed its exemption on WHICH CRITERION FAILED LAST TIME: `safety-limits-hold` was singled out for a mandatory re-read because it previously came back not-met. That is the wrong variable. The load-bearing property is not the prior verdict, it is WHAT THE EVIDENCE DEPENDS ON. Keyed the old way, the rubric demanded fresh work on the criterion that had failed while permitting re-affirmation of the LEAST re-affirmable one — `web-apps-real-data`, whose evidence is a live round trip against live sidecars, a live credential and Google's own API, which no git check can attest at all. That is backwards. THE CORRECT RULE, which this revision uses: a criterion may be RE-AFFIRMED only if its evidence is a pure function of the source tree AND the identity comparison below returns identical. Any criterion whose evidence depends on something outside the source tree — a live service, a credential, a build product, a database, an external API, a human having done something — is EXEMPT from re-affirmation and must be graded on current evidence or rated `unknown`.\n\nWHY THE NON-MOVEMENT CHECK IS GONE. Revision 1 asked you to run `TZ=UTC git log --since=2026-08-29T23:00:00Z --oneline -- tests/ packages/core/src/ apps/` in each app root and re-affirm if it returned nothing. Do NOT run that check. It fails OPEN, which is the worst property a gate can have, and it misses at least: lockfiles and toolchain pins (Cargo.lock, package-lock.json, rust-toolchain.toml) that change what a build produces from unchanged source; THE PLATFORM REPO, which by construction is the thing that moved in this re-grade; generated and build output no source path covers; live external state no git command can see (the OAuth token, API quota, the sidecars, Google itself); and uncommitted working-tree state — and on this swept tree a clean `git status` means the sweeper ran, not that nothing changed. Its `--since` form is independently unreliable: git renders committer dates in each commit's OWN recorded offset, so a wall-clock UTC stamp silently compares against local-offset timestamps. A path-and-time scan that returns clean is indistinguishable from one that looked in the wrong places.\n\nWHAT REPLACES IT: AN IDENTITY COMPARISON THAT FAILS CLOSED. Ask an identity question, not a time-and-path question. For each app the identity is (a) the commit SHA the graded artifact was BUILT FROM and (b) digests of the files determining what that source builds into — Cargo.lock, package-lock.json, and rust-toolchain.toml where present. Re-affirmation is permitted only when the prior card RECORDS that identity and it compares identical to the identity you record now. If the prior identity is unrecorded or unresolvable, the comparison FAILS CLOSED: re-affirmation is unavailable, and you either grade from current evidence or rate `unknown`. Both are acceptable; say which you did.\n  BEFORE YOU RELY ON THIS GATE, SHOW IT REFUSING ONCE. Point the comparison at an identity you know differs — any earlier commit reachable in that app's history will do — and record that it reports a mismatch. A gate nobody has seen refuse is not a gate. If it does not refuse, say so and treat re-affirmation as unavailable throughout.\n  EXPECT IT TO FAIL CLOSED HERE. The prior card (EI-21833310247310216) was written before any rubric asked for identity, so it may well not record a built-from SHA. Check rather than assume — but if it does not, that is the gate working, not an obstacle to route around. This revision records the current identity so the NEXT re-grade has something to compare against.\n\nWHAT THIS SUCCESSOR ASKS OF YOU. Criterion `web-apps-real-data` is graded FROM SCRATCH on current evidence: it is the only thing that changed and the Calendar half is the whole point of this re-grade. For the other five, apply the re-affirmation rule above per criterion, and state for each which path you took — graded fresh, or re-affirmed on an identity comparison you record. A re-affirmation whose identity comparison you did not perform is not a grading, and I would rather read `unknown` than a rating you did not establish.\n\nA NOTE ON COST, NOT A DIRECTION. Criteria 2 and 5 drive two native cargo builds that must run SEQUENTIALLY and take tens of minutes. That is a fact about the work, not an instruction about where to spend it. How you allocate effort — and whether an expensive re-run or an honest `unknown` is the better answer for a given criterion — is your call, not mine.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — spec-scoped fleet metrics","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-30","owner":"su-384b4ce5-5f34-4e2a-bc08-418593a0fcf1","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — spec-scoped fleet metrics\nslug: fleet-spec-scoped-metrics-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-384b4ce5-5f34-4e2a-bc08-418593a0fcf1\n---\n\n# Acceptance — spec-scoped fleet metrics\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01.
