Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"incremental-test-proof-reuse-2026-08-30","title":"Incremental tests reuse prior passing proofs until related inputs change","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-30","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Incremental tests reuse prior passing proofs until related inputs change\nslug: incremental-test-proof-reuse-2026-08-30\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-08-30\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation and current-tree verification are complete, committed at 33466aadb986, and their completion authority is settled. The shipment item is active. The live green-checkpoint lane is held by su-86df7de5; its older in-flight candidate excludes this commit. The owner received the commit and fresh-verdict/deploy requirement once. Per gate exclusivity, this session is not duplicating checkpoint, red-triage, deploy, or monitoring operations.\n\n**Next:** Gate owner returns the fresh green/deployed identity containing 33466aadb; self then records shipment evidence, completes the shipment item, runs the completion audit, closes the plan, and ends the AUTO loop.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-1030244 — Reproduce the current no-reuse behavior with a bounded two-run gate-shaped harness; record which identity/closure components move and pin the acceptance matrix against WI-1024071 evidence. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-1030245 — Implement the correctness-preserving separation: keep last-green for selection/certification, remove selection-base drift from cross-run proof identity, and derive ordinary-task related inputs from w… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-1030246 — Add regression and recurrence coverage for unchanged-hit/no-spawn, unrelated root/script hit, related workspace/dependency/runner/config miss, whole-tree guard miss, and all existing fail-closed case… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-1030247 — Run focused cache, affected-selection, and green-checkpoint recurrence suites plus the relevant typecheck/current-build verification; diagnose and repair every regression introduced by this plan. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-1030248 — Use git-sync for the commit hop, obtain a fresh green-checkpoint verdict that contains the implementation commit, trigger deployment of that green pin, and verify :3070 serves the same candidate. Thi… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-1030250 — Run the completion audit, update the plan Now block to the shipped evidence, complete WI-1024071 with structured verification, and end AUTO continuation. <!-- P-006 -->\n## Background\n\nWI-1024071 reports a checkpoint run with 0 cache hits and 123 misses after a long red streak. Source inspection refines the brief's base-only hypothesis:\n\n- Last-green is correctly the selection/certification base.\n- A stable cross-run passing-verdict group already stores clean whole-task passes.\n- Cross-run gate configuration drops the selection base, but the child-environment identity still hashes `AFFECTED_BASE`, so base movement evicts byte-identical proofs.\n- Ordinary-task provenance currently includes every tracked root file plus all of `scripts/` and `libs/test-config/`, so unrelated root/script churn evicts every ordinary task.\n- Repo-wide guards intentionally bind the whole tree; integration/external-state tasks intentionally remain non-reusable.\n- The zero-hit run also changed `scripts/affected-tests.mjs`, a genuine runner input. The repair will not fabricate reuse for that run; it makes future relatedness precise.\n\nThis extends the existing cache, related-test graph, atomic store, and diagnostics. It does not add a second cache or change checkpoint certification.\n\n## Scope and invariants\n\n1. Selection/certification remains relative to last green; proof reuse is a separate content-addressed decision.\n2. Reuse only clean, complete, first-pass whole-task passes with matching task, command, relevant environment/configuration, implementation version, and related-input contents.\n3. Ordinary-task related inputs are its workspace, transitive local dependencies, task/runtime configuration, package-resolution inputs, and the actual transitive shared runner/config module graph—not blanket root/scripts globs.\n4. Repo-wide guards stay whole-tree-bound. Integration/external-state tasks and incomplete/unreadable provenance always execute.\n5. Any related path byte, mode, symlink target, membership, command, relevant environment/config, or policy change forces execution.\n6. Selection-base drift alone does not evict a cross-run proof.\n7. Cache faults stay loud and fail toward running tests, never false green.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- **R-001 — Incremental reuse:** A task with a clean prior whole-task pass must be skipped on a later invocation when every related input is identical, even if the checkpoint selection base or run identity changed.\n- **R-002 — Related-change invalidation:** Any change to the task workspace, a transitive local dependency, the executed command/script, an actual shared runner/config input, package-resolution input, relevant environment/configuration, or cache implementation version must execute the task again.\n- **R-003 — Unrelated-change stability:** An unrelated tracked root document or unrelated script must not invalidate an ordinary workspace task.\n- **R-004 — Fail-closed boundaries:** Repo-wide guards remain bound to the whole tracked tree; integration/external-state tasks, targeted retries, failures, absorbed passes, and incomplete/corrupt provenance are never reusable.\n- **R-005 — Honest observability:** The run summary must identify cross-run hits/misses and actionable invalidation reasons without claiming that the selection base itself is a task input.\n- **R-006 — Shipment:** Focused recurrence tests pass, a fresh green checkpoint includes the fix, and :3070 serves that green candidate.\n\n## Design\n\nThe existing affected-test runner remains the sole selector and cache consumer. It continues deriving the affected task set from last-green for certification. For each selected ordinary task, it constructs a cross-run proof identity from the existing command/environment/config/version components plus a content hash of a derived related-input manifest.\n\nThe manifest reuses the current workspace dependency closure and the existing fail-wide import-graph machinery. It contains the selected workspace and transitive local workspaces; package-manager resolution files; task-owned config; and the transitive static module/data inputs actually used by `scripts/affected-tests.mjs` and shared test configuration. It no longer includes every root file or every script merely because of directory location. A graph hole, unreadable path, unscanned submodule, or empty manifest yields a miss.\n\nThe per-run proof keeps its run/base boundary. For ordinary reusable workspace tasks, the runner removes `AFFECTED_BASE` from the real child environment, making selection-base drift structurally incapable of changing the task; their stable cross-run proof therefore has no base input to ignore. Repo-wide guards and integration/external tasks retain the base in their real environment and identity, forwarded bases are resolved to immutable SHAs, and unresolved base-dependent provenance executes instead of reusing. The atomic cache format and clean-pass admission rules remain unchanged; repo-wide guards also keep the existing whole-tree manifest.\n\nTrade-off: exact relatedness requires a small import-graph walk, but that cost is bounded and far below re-running large test tasks. The safety bias stays toward extra execution whenever the graph is uncertain.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- Two gate-shaped invocations over byte-identical related inputs, with different run groups and `AFFECTED_BASE` values, run the task once; invocation two reports a cross-run hit and spawns no task.\n- Changing an unrelated root document or unrelated `scripts/` file preserves an ordinary-task hit.\n- Changing the workspace, transitive workspace dependency, actual runner/config module, package-resolution input, command, relevant environment/config, or implementation version forces a miss.\n- A repo-wide guard still misses for any tracked-tree change.\n- Failed, absorbed, targeted-retry, integration/external, legacy/corrupt, or incomplete-provenance cases execute.\n- Focused tests plus a bounded real two-run recurrence pass on canonical staging.\n- The containing staging commit is included in a fresh green checkpoint and deployed :3070 equals that green candidate.\n\n## Prior art reused\n\n- `scripts/lib/passing-task-verdict-cache.mjs`: identity, content proof, atomic store, diagnostics.\n- `scripts/affected-tests.mjs`: sole production lookup/store consumer.\n- `scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs`: existing fail-wide static import graph.\n- Existing recurrence suites in operator-core and release.\n- Shipped `stable-candidate-related-gate-2026-08-23`, `gate-stop-chasing-the-tip-2026-08-19`, WI-38446, and WI-572013.\n\nThe similar plans are shipped/superseded, or the ready file-selection plan has every item done; this is a new evidence-driven regression repair, not a fork of active work.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Evidence\n\n- **P-001** `done` Reproduce the current no-reuse behavior with a bounded two-run gate-shaped harness; record which identity/closure components move and pin the acceptance matrix against WI-1024071 evidence. importance: high — note: ← WI-1030244 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Repair\n\n- **P-002** `done` Implement the correctness-preserving separation: keep last-green for selection/certification, remove selection-base drift from cross-run proof identity, and derive ordinary-task related inputs from workspace/transitive deps plus actual shared runner/config inputs while keeping fail-wide categories. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-1030245 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add regression and recurrence coverage for unchanged-hit/no-spawn, unrelated root/script hit, related workspace/dependency/runner/config miss, whole-tree guard miss, and all existing fail-closed cases. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-1030246 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification\n\n- **P-004** `done` Run focused cache, affected-selection, and green-checkpoint recurrence suites plus the relevant typecheck/current-build verification; diagnose and repair every regression introduced by this plan. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-1030247 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Ship\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Use git-sync for the commit hop, obtain a fresh green-checkpoint verdict that contains the implementation commit, trigger deployment of that green pin, and verify :3070 serves the same candidate. This item explicitly requires deployed main because shipment identity cannot be proven on staging. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-1030248 released\n- **P-006** `todo` Run the completion audit, update the plan Now block to the shipped evidence, complete WI-1024071 with structured verification, and end AUTO continuation. blocked-by: P-005\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Separate certification base from reuse proof\n\nCheckpoint selection/certification keeps last-green. Cross-run reuse ignores selection-base drift and relies on task-specific related-input content.\n\n### D-002 — Narrow ordinary provenance; preserve fail-wide categories\n\nOrdinary tasks use a derived related-input set. Repo-wide guards keep the whole tree and graph/enumeration uncertainty stays a miss.\n\n### D-003 — Execute production wiring twice for acceptance\n\nIdentity unit tests are insufficient. Closure requires a bounded two-invocation recurrence proving first execution, second skip, unrelated-change hit, and related-change miss through the real consumer.\n\n### D-004 — Base relevance is task-shaped, not global\nDate: 2026-08-30\nMeasured: a two-invocation GREEN_CHECKPOINT=1 probe reached the stable fallback and missed only because changedKeys=[AFFECTED_BASE], proving gate cross-run reuse is live. Source census found AFFECTED_BASE consumers in affected-tests plus base-aware guard scripts, and green-checkpoint supplies lastReady as a full SHA. RULING: do not remove AFFECTED_BASE from the generic identity. Ordinary reusable workspace tasks will have AFFECTED_BASE removed from their REAL child environment, making selection base structurally irrelevant to what they execute. Repo-wide guards and integration/external tasks retain it; forwardBase argv is resolved to an immutable commit when possible, and base-dependent provenance fails closed when it cannot be resolved. This reconciles D-001 with the counterexample that some guards genuinely test base..HEAD.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-005 — Cross-run proof identity is related-input identity, never inherited process identity\nDate: 2026-08-30\nOwner correction 2026-08-30: WI-1024071 exists to ensure a task that already passed is NOT rerun unless its task definition or related files changed since that proof. Governing identity components are task key; command/argv/cwd/package script text; static proof policy; proof implementation version; and dependencyHash over the task's related workspace/dependency/runner/test-config closure. The inherited process environment (agent/session, PATH, credentials, gate/load/admission/preemption/wrapper state, including all future variables) is ambient caller state and MUST NOT participate in cross-run identity. A task that intentionally needs an environment value must declare it into a task-owned command/config/related-input surface; ambient inheritance cannot invalidate every green task. Acceptance: unrelated file change + arbitrary caller-environment drift => identity-match hit and no task spawn; related workspace/dependency/runner/test-config change => dependency-closure-changed miss and execution. Green checkpoint/deployment is separate shipment work and is not the objective or closure criterion of WI-1024071.\n\n## Source audit\n\nCanonical owner turns: `session_turn:claude:77a3c032-6f64-4c8a-862f-0a18d208670a:30`, `session_turn:claude:77a3c032-6f64-4c8a-862f-0a18d208670a:56`, and `session_turn:codex:01a050a3-3177-7671-8999-46b3880a3ca3:1`. WI-1024071 was read in full.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plans-list-windowing-cardinality-fix-2026-08-30","title":"plans.list cardinality windowing — bound the default feed without breaking bucket-tab browse or slug reachability","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-30","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: plans.list cardinality windowing — bound the default feed without breaking bucket-tab browse or slug reachability\nslug: plans-list-windowing-cardinality-fix-2026-08-30\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-08-30\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Phase 1-2 (P-001/P-002/P-003) shipped — see D-005. plans:get + PlanGetResult now surface title/status/startStatus; PlanDashboard.tsx fetches its own plan via usePlan(slug,{live:true}) instead of .find()-ing a shared list, closing a real correctness bug independent of windowing. Verified: 0 typecheck errors on the 4 touched files, 32/32 tests passing. Root cause of the ORIGINAL cardinality trigger (D-001/D-002/D-003: organic growth, no housekeeping shortcut, naive row limit would break bucket-tab browse) is diagnosed but Phase 3-5 (P-004..P-009 — scoping the default feed + lazy per-bucket fetch for PlanRail/PlansListPanel) is deliberately deferred as separate, larger-blast-radius follow-up work.\n\n**Next:** Next claimant: pick up P-004 (design the includeFinished/status-set filter arg for plans:list, default usePlanList() to exclude terminal statuses) as the entry point into the remaining Phase 3-5 windowing work. No blocker from Phase 1-2.\n\n## Background\n\n### The detector and the item that filed this plan\n`packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/sync-read-audit.ts`'s `SYNC_READ_ALLOWLIST['plans.list']` entry (maxBytes 720_000) already documents, from its own prior measurements: *\"the only axis left is CARDINALITY (windowing/pagination), which is a design question, not a cut... THAT BREACH IS THE WINDOWING TRIGGER, NOT ANOTHER RAISE.\"* EI-21869958222942655 (bug, major) reproduced the crossed trigger live: `plans.list` at `{}` returned `data.length=1540`, ~1176 KiB, breaching both the detector's row (>1000) and byte (256 KiB dev / 720 KB prod-allowlist) thresholds. The item's own filed fix direction: *\"bound rows on the wire and preserve search/browse reachability; do not merely silence the detector or raise the ceiling.\"*\n\n### Measured row composition (dev:pg_query, live, 2026-08-30)\n```\nworkspace_id=papercusp-workspace, harness_slug=papercusp:\n  total                              1523\n  active_non_instance (archived=false AND template_slug IS NULL)   1424\n  terminal status (shipped OR superseded)                          953   (62.6% of total!)\n```\nThe dominant term is **terminal-status rows** (953 of 1523, i.e. plans whose lifecycle bucket is `shipped` or `rejected`/superseded per `bucketOf()` in `apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-api.ts`). Excluding just those two statuses from the DEFAULT fetch would cut the shared feed to ~570 rows (~412 KB at the measured ~723 B/row — safely under the 720KB ceiling with real headroom), and matches the exact same \"drop the buckets nobody needs by default\" pattern `PlansPane` already implements CLIENT-SIDE (its `showFinished` toggle, default false — see `ACTIVE_BUCKETS` in `PlansPane.tsx`).\n\n### Why a naive server-side row `limit` (e.g. `limit:500, order:'updated'`) is WRONG here\n`usePlanList()` (`apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-api.ts`) is a SHARED cache key deliberately used by ~12 call sites (P-001: collapsing 3 distinct arg shapes into one superset query to avoid redundant ~1.5MB-per-cold-wave fetches — see the doc comment above `usePlanList`). Two of those consumers are genuine **full-corpus, all-lifecycle-bucket browse UIs**, not incidental:\n- `apps/operator/app/admin/plans/PlanRail.tsx` (737 lines) — the admin `/admin/plans` rail, with `PlanBucketTabs` (Draft/Ready/Running/Shipped/Superseded) as a first-class navigation surface. Client-side substring search over title/slug, UNIONED with `searchHitSlugs` from `usePlanSearch(q)` (an ALREADY-EXISTING independent server-side search query, `plans.search` — see below).\n- `apps/operator/app/adv/create/use-create-data.ts` → `usePlanListMaps()` → `apps/operator/app/adv/create/PlansListPanel.tsx`, which renders the SAME `PlanBucketTabs` component for the Create-tab's plan browser. Same client search + `usePlanSearch` union pattern.\n\nA recency-capped `limit` on the shared query would silently truncate BOTH of these bucket-tab UIs' \"Shipped\"/\"Superseded\" tabs to only the most-recently-touched plans, hiding the rest of the historical archive from pure browsing — that IS the \"silently break reachability\" outcome the filed item explicitly warns against, on two separate first-class product surfaces, not an edge case.\n\n### Search reachability is ALREADY solved — do not rebuild it\n`apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-api.ts`'s `usePlanSearch(query)` hook already exists, hits an INDEPENDENT server-side query (`plans.search`, presumably backed by the `harness_plans_search_idx` GIN `_search` tsvector index — confirm at implementation time) and is `enabled` only when `query.length > 0`. It is NOT gated by `plans.list`'s cardinality at all. `PlanRail` (via `PlansClient.tsx`'s `railSearchHits = usePlanSearch(q)`) and `PlansListPanel` both already union its hits (`searchHitSlugs`) into their rendered rows. **Typed-search reachability for a specific plan is therefore unaffected by any windowing of the default (no-query) fetch** — this materially de-risks the whole effort: the remaining problem is PURELY \"pure bucket-tab browsing with no search text typed\", not general findability.\n\n### Two independent correctness risks found during the consumer audit (must be fixed regardless of the windowing decision)\n1. **`apps/operator/app/_components/plans/PlanDashboard.tsx`** (`?pdash=<slug>` deep link) does `usePlanList({}).data.plans.find(p => p.slug === planSlug)` against the SAME shared cache — it does its OWN plan lookup by `.find()` rather than a targeted fetch. If `planSlug` names an old shipped plan not present in a bounded window, this silently renders \"plan not found\" for a valid deep link. A targeted single-plan fetch already exists (`usePlan(slug, {live:true, harnessSlug})` → `plans.get`), BUT `PlanGetResult` (same file, ~line 466) does **not** currently expose `title`/`status`/`startStatus` as top-level fields (only nested `frontmatter?: Record<string,unknown>` and `now`) — `bucketOf()` needs `Pick<PlanListRow,'status'|'startStatus'>`, which `plans.get`'s current response shape cannot supply directly. This needs either a small resolver/type extension (surface those two fields alongside `frontmatter`) or deriving them from `frontmatter.status` + a `now`-adjacent equivalent of `startStatus` (verify how `op_status`→`startStatus` is currently only computed in `plans:list`'s row-shaping, likely `list-shape.ts` — check whether `plans:get` already returns raw `op_status` under a different key before assuming a schema change is needed).\n2. **`apps/operator/app/adv/create/use-create-data.ts`**'s `usePlanListMaps()` builds `harnessByPlan`/`planBucketBySlug`/`planMetaBySlug` maps from the same shared list, consumed by `MainViewPanel.tsx` (`maps.harnessByPlan.get(plan)` to resolve a linked-work-item's plan's harness) and `PreviewPanel.tsx` (same pattern). Same reachability risk as (1) for a work item that references an older/shipped plan.\n\n## Phase 1 — extend `plans.get` / `PlanGetResult` / `usePlan` for safe targeted lookups\n- **P-001** `done` Determine how `startStatus` (`op_status`-derived) is computed for `plans:list` rows (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/list-shape.ts` or wherever `PlanIndexRow`→list-row shaping happens) and whether `plans:get`'s underlying `callPlansRead('get', ...)` already has access to the same source column (`op_status`) — if so this is a resolver/type change only (surface it), not new plumbing. importance: high\n- **P-002** `done` Add `title`, `status`, `startStatus` to `PlanGetResult` (`apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-api.ts`) and the `plans.get` resolver/tool response so a single-plan fetch is sufficient for any consumer that only needs list-row-equivalent fields (not the full raw markdown body). blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 2 — decouple PlanDashboard (ship independently of windowing; fixes a real bug today)\n- **P-003** `done` Switch `PlanDashboard.tsx`'s plan-row lookup from `usePlanList({}).data.plans.find(...)` to `usePlan(planSlug, {live:true, harnessSlug})`, deriving `bucket` from the now-exposed `status`/`startStatus` fields. Verify `PlanDashboard.test.tsx` still passes and add a case for a plan NOT present in a small/bounded list. blocked-by: P-002\n\n## Phase 3 — lazy per-bucket fetch for the two full-browse bucket-tab UIs\n- **P-004** `todo` Design the exact arg shape for \"exclude terminal statuses\" on `plans:list`/`plans.list` resolver (e.g. a boolean `includeFinished` default `true` for back-compat with every non-UI caller, or reuse/extend the existing `status` single-value filter into a set). Default the SHARED `usePlanList()` cache to `includeFinished:false` (or equivalent), cutting the steady-state feed to ~570 rows / ~412 KB. importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Give `PlanRail`/`PlansClient.tsx` an on-demand fetch that ADDS shipped+superseded rows (a SEPARATE query, not merged into the shared base cache) triggered when the user selects the Shipped or Superseded bucket tab — so those tabs still show the COMPLETE historical set, not a recency-truncated one. blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `todo` Apply the identical lazy-fetch pattern to `PlansListPanel.tsx` / `use-create-data.ts`'s Create-tab bucket tabs (same `PlanBucketTabs` component, same requirement). blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Phase 4 — the remaining correctness risk (use-create-data.ts slug maps)\n- **P-007** `todo` Audit `MainViewPanel.tsx`/`PreviewPanel.tsx`'s consumption of `harnessByPlan`/`planBucketBySlug` for a plan not present in the now-bounded default list; fall back to a targeted `usePlan()`-style fetch when the lookup misses, mirroring the Phase 2 fix. blocked-by: P-003, P-004\n\n## Phase 5 — verification + re-measurement\n- **P-008** `todo` Update `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/sync-read-audit.ts`'s `plans.list`/`plans.byHive` allowlist entries with fresh live-measured before/after byte counts once the default fetch is scoped (lower `maxBytes` to reflect the new steady state, or remove the entries entirely if under the 250KB default — follow this file's own documented convention of citing exact measured numbers, 0-row-loss verification, and a stated re-review trigger). blocked-by: P-005, P-006\n- **P-009** `todo` Regression suite: `apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-list-superset-filter.test.ts`, `PlanDashboard.test.tsx`, `PlansPane.test.tsx`, `PlanRail`/`PlansClient` bucket-tab tests, `use-create-data.test.tsx`, `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/list.status-limit.test.ts`, plus a live before/after row-count + byte measurement on :3170 for `plans.list` at `{}` and the exact superset args `usePlanList` sends. blocked-by: P-008\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Row growth is organic; no housekeeping shortcut exists (measured)\n\nDirect query against `harness_shared.harness_plans` (workspace `papercusp-workspace`, harness `papercusp`) shows 1424 of 1523 rows are `archived=false AND template_slug IS NULL` — i.e. genuinely active, non-instance, authored plans. The `coord.plans` precedent (WI-7256, pruning finished `@run-` scheduled-instance snapshots) does not apply: instance rows are a small minority here (well under 100 of 1523). Any fix must reduce genuinely-wanted-by-default row count, which is why this requires the lazy per-bucket design in Phase 3 rather than a data-hygiene cut.\n\nMeasured: `dev:pg_query` against `harness_shared.harness_plans`, 2026-08-30 (see Background section for the exact query and counts).\n\n### D-002 — A naive row-limit on the shared `usePlanList()` cache is rejected\n\n`PlanRail.tsx` and `PlansListPanel.tsx` (via `use-create-data.ts`) both render `PlanBucketTabs` (Draft/Ready/Running/Shipped/Superseded) as first-class browse surfaces over the FULL shared list. A recency-capped `limit` would silently truncate the Shipped/Superseded tabs on both surfaces — a real product regression on two distinct pages, which the originating item's fix direction (\"preserve search/browse reachability\") explicitly rules out. The correct design is lazy on-demand fetch of terminal-status rows only when a terminal bucket tab is actually selected (Phase 3), not a blanket cap.\n\nMeasured: direct source read of `PlanRail.tsx` (737 lines, `PlanBucketTabs` prop `plans={sorted}` over the full shared list) and `PlansListPanel.tsx:207` (`<PlanBucketTabs plans={maps.visiblePlans} .../>`), 2026-08-30.\n\n### D-003 — Search reachability does not need to be rebuilt\n\n`usePlanSearch(query)` (`apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-api.ts:1449`) already runs an independent server-side `plans.search` query, gated only on `query.length > 0`, entirely decoupled from `plans.list`'s cardinality. Both `PlanRail` (via `PlansClient.tsx`'s `railSearchHits`) and `PlansListPanel` already union its hits into their rendered rows. Windowing the default (no-query) fetch therefore does not regress typed-search findability for any plan, including ones outside the default window — only pure bucket-tab scrolling with no search text is affected, and only for the two terminal buckets, addressed by Phase 3's lazy fetch.\n\nMeasured: direct source read of `usePlanSearch` (`plans-api.ts:1449-1458`) and its call sites (`PlansClient.tsx:670`, `PlansListPanel.tsx`), 2026-08-30.\n\n### D-004 — P-001 finding: plans:get's `get.ts` response has no top-level status/startStatus/title today\nDate: 2026-08-30\nTraced `plans:get`'s implementation (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/get.ts`, the `base` object built ~line 872-895) — this is the SAME tool backing both the agent-facing MCP surface and the admin HTTP/sync-resolver `plans.get` (via `callPlansRead('get', {mode:'full'})`, confirmed by `usePlan()`'s own doc comment in `plans-api.ts`). Today `base` returns `frontmatter` (raw parsed frontmatter — has `.title`/`.status` as AUTHORED strings), `now`, `contentHash`, `version`, `promotePolicy`, `forcedPast`, `sectionIndex`, `counts` — but no top-level `status`/`startStatus`/`title`, and critically NOT the DAG/opStatus-reconciled `startStatus` that `bucketOf()` needs to distinguish the 'running' bucket (started-but-not-shipped) from 'ready' (approved-not-started).\n\n`list.ts:721` shows the pattern already used for `plans:list` rows: `startStatus: reconcileStartStatus(row.opStatus, status)` (import from `./plan-start-state`). `source.ts:181/289` confirms `PlanRow.opStatus` is read from the `op_status` column already selected in the underlying list queries.\n\nRemaining work for P-001/P-002: confirm whether `get.ts`'s own row-fetch (the plan-content read this file uses, distinct from `listPlanIndexRows`) ALSO selects `op_status` — if yes, add `title: parsed.frontmatter.title ?? null`, `status: parsed.frontmatter.status ?? null`, `startStatus: reconcileStartStatus(row.opStatus, status)` to the `base` object (additive, safe for every existing `plans:get` consumer since new fields are ignored by old callers) and mirror the 3 fields onto `PlanGetResult` in `apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-api.ts`. If `op_status` is NOT already selected by get.ts's row fetch, the change also needs to add it to that SELECT (check the query around wherever `row` is constructed for this file, likely a `getPlanContentsBySlugs`-style call from `./source`).\n\nDeliberately stopped here (context budget) rather than rush an edit to `plans:get`, which is a heavily-shared, widely-consumed tool — the next wake should verify the row-fetch query, land the 3-field addition, add/extend a get.ts test asserting the new fields, then proceed to P-003 (switch PlanDashboard.tsx off its `.find()`-based lookup).\n\n### D-005 — Phase 1-2 (P-001/P-002/P-003) shipped independently of Phase 3-5 windowing\nDate: 2026-08-30\nEI-21869958222942655's original bug report conflated two distinct concerns: (a) a real windowing/cardinality concern for the DEFAULT plans.list feed (Phase 3-5, P-004..P-009 — wider blast radius, needs lazy per-bucket fetch for PlanRail/PlansListPanel's Shipped/Superseded bucket tabs; still deferred, still todo), and (b) PlanDashboard.tsx's independent correctness bug: a `.find()`-based single-plan lookup against a shared, potentially-windowed list, silently broken regardless of whether windowing ever ships.\n\nP-001/P-002/P-003 close concern (b): `plans:get`'s resolver (get.ts) and `PlanGetResult` (plans-api.ts) now surface `title`/`status`/`startStatus` using the same `op_status` source column list-shape.ts already reads (resolver-only change, confirmed no new plumbing needed — resolves P-001's open question). `PlanDashboard.tsx` now fetches its own plan via `usePlan(slug,{live:true})` instead of `.find()`-ing a shared list, so it can never silently miss a plan that a windowed/bounded list omits.\n\nMeasured: `apps/operator/app/admin/plans/plans-api.ts` — `PlanGetResult` interface (line ~570) now has `title?`, `status?`, `startStatus?` fields added directly after `legacy: boolean;`.\nMeasured: `build:typecheck { project: \"packages/operator-core\", files: [\"plans-api.ts\",\"PlanDashboard.tsx\",\"PlanDashboard.test.tsx\",\"get.ts\"] }` → errorCount: 0 for the 4 filtered files (project totalErrorCount: 155, all in unrelated pre-existing files).\nMeasured: `testing:run { files: [\"apps/operator/app/_components/plans/PlanDashboard.test.tsx\",\"apps/operator/app/admin/plans/usePlan.test.tsx\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/plans-entries.test.ts\"] }` → passed: 32, failed: 0, skipped: 0 across all 3 files.\n\nTracked via work-item EI-21869958222942655 (papercusp). P-004..P-009 remain open, untouched, and claimable as a separate follow-up scope — they are NOT blocked by this decision and do not need the same fix pattern.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"platform-to-app-data-producer-2026-08-30-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: canonical Google-backed rows reach the Email and Calendar app stores through one producer","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-30","owner":"su-accf0e6a-4c70-4f42-bd97-ad55c5bf69d9","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: canonical Google-backed rows reach the Email and Calendar app stores through one producer\nslug: platform-to-app-data-producer-2026-08-30-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-accf0e6a-4c70-4f42-bd97-ad55c5bf69d9\n---\n\n# Acceptance: canonical Google-backed rows reach the Email and Calendar app stores through one producer\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan platform-to-app-data-producer-2026-08-30, authored after implementation against as-built reality by the implementer (su-accf0e6a). REVISION 2 — revised after independent vetting, which found that a criterion graded the MECHANISM this implementation happens to use rather than the OUTCOME the plan promised, and that one of the owner's four answers had no criterion attached at all. What changed: the freshness criterion now grades an observable outcome and is renamed; a new criterion grades whether the backfill actually drained the corpus; a skipped control now rates `unknown` rather than `partially-met`; every criterion carries an explicit falsifier; and identity is now a recorded observation rather than prose.\n\nTHE TEST EVERY CRITERION HERE MUST PASS — APPLY IT AS YOU READ THEM. Could a DIFFERENT, correct implementation fully achieve this plan's goal and still FAIL this criterion? If yes, the criterion grades my implementation rather than the plan's outcome. Say so in your grading. That is a defect in this rubric and I want it reported, not worked around.\n\nTHE ONE CHECKOUT. Unless a criterion says otherwise, every path below is repo-relative to PLATFORM = /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp. Three plan items (P-002, P-009, P-012) land in SEPARATE git repositories — EMAIL = /home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/email and CALENDAR = /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/calendar — and any criterion that reaches into one names it explicitly. Never evaluate a criterion from an unnamed root: the two app checkouts have deliberately similar layouts.\n\nRECORD THE IDENTITY BEFORE YOU RATE ANYTHING. Identity is an observation, not a preamble. Before rating any criterion, paste into your card, for EACH of the three roots above, the output of `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and `git rev-parse HEAD`. A criterion evaluated from a root you did not record grades `unknown`, never `met`. Two evidence rules follow: (a) `git blame` and commit SUBJECTS are NOT evidence in this repository and must not be cited — git-sync sweeps the whole tree on a schedule under one identity and labels commits with whatever agent context was current, so blame names the wrong author and the subject describes the sweeping agent's intent rather than the diff; (b) when a criterion claims a specific file carries a specific change, establish it by BLOB IDENTITY (`git rev-parse <sha>:<path>` compared against `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`) or by reading the file's current content — never by a commit message that mentions it.\n\nWHAT THE LIVE EVIDENCE IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT A FUNCTION OF. The strongest evidence in this plan is an integration test that talks to two RUNNING sidecars over HTTP, using a signing secret from an environment file, against app databases other processes also write. Its result is therefore NOT a pure function of the source tree: the same three checkouts can produce a pass now and a failure in an hour with no commit in between. So record every live result together with the identity it was earned against — the three HEAD shas above, the wall-clock time of the run, and which sidecars were up (`systemctl --user is-active papercusp-email-sidecar papercusp-calendar-sidecar`). Any later re-affirmation of this rubric must understand that NO source-tree check can attest a live round trip; re-affirming a live result because the code did not move is a category error.\n\nTHE LIVE EVIDENCE AND HOW TO RUN IT. To run anything marked LIVE:\n  cd PLATFORM && set -a && . ~/.papercusp/app-producer.env && set +a && npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/app-data-producer/live-app-round-trip.integration.test.ts\nThe sidecars are systemd user units papercusp-email-sidecar (:8791) and papercusp-calendar-sidecar (:8792).\n\nWHY THE LIVE TEST'S TWO CONTROLS ARE PART OF CRITERION 1 RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE. A green live test can be green for two wrong reasons and neither is visible in a passing run. If the apps were in LOCAL_MODE every caller would be accepted as a fixed owner and the suite would pass while proving nothing; and if the test could not SKIP when unconfigured it would red the shared gate for every peer with no sidecar. So criterion 1 is met only when you have SEEN the test pass configured, skip unconfigured, and fail on a deliberately wrong signing secret. A grader who runs only the happy path has not graded it.\n\nRATING VOCABULARY — `unknown` AND `partially-met` ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. `partially-met` is a claim ABOUT THE SUBJECT: it says the thing works in part, and you may only say that if you measured it. `unknown` says NO MEASUREMENT WAS MADE. When you skip a control, do not run a step, or cannot establish a root, the honest rating is `unknown`. Collapsing that into `partially-met` destroys the distinction exactly where it matters and biases toward the pass, because `partially-met` reads as \"mostly there\" when the truth is \"not established\". I would rather read `unknown` with a reason than a rating you did not establish.\n\nEVERY CRITERION CARRIES A FALSIFIER. Each criterion ends with a FALSIFIER naming the artifact that would have to exist and the observation that would have to differ for a not-met. If you are rating a criterion `met` because you read the code and agreed with it, and you cannot point at the falsifier's artifact, the criterion has not been graded — rate it `unknown` and say the falsifier could not be exercised.\n\nA WARNING ABOUT COUNTS. Do not compare a producer-side delivered-row count against an app-side stored-row count and read the difference as a shortfall. The canonical corpus currently holds roughly two rows per provider entity (a separate ingest defect, filed as EI-21854534787220439) and both apps upsert by provider id, so the correct app-side target is the DISTINCT external_id count, not the delivered count. The corpus is LIVE and moving: measure it, never cite a count carried in from an earlier note.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"restore-brainstorm-under-more-2026-08-30","title":"Restore Brainstorm under More","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-30","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Restore Brainstorm under More\nslug: restore-brainstorm-under-more-2026-08-30\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-08-30\n---\n\n## Now\n\nRestore the existing Brainstorm workspace as a secondary `/adv` tab under More, preserving Quick Panel access and repairing existing `?tab=brainstorm` links.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-1008447 — Restore Brainstorm as a per-pot secondary `/adv` tab under More by reusing the existing `BrainstormFull`, repairing routing/deep links, and preserving Quick Panel access. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-1008448 — Update focused navigation/rendering tests and verify the restored Brainstorm path end to end. <!-- P-002 -->\n## Background\n\nBrainstorm was deliberately removed from `/adv` on 2026-07-13 and moved into the Quick Panel. The implementation remained intact, but current in-app CTAs and global-search results still emit `?tab=brainstorm`, which now falls back to Overview. Reuse `BrainstormFull`; do not fork the feature.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- A single-pot `/adv?slug=<pot>&tab=brainstorm` deep link must render the existing complete Brainstorm workspace instead of falling back to Overview.\n- Brainstorm must remain absent from the primary strip and appear exactly once in the searchable More menu.\n- Quick Panel Brainstorm access and persisted brainstorm data must remain unchanged.\n- All existing in-app links that emit `tab=brainstorm` must land on the restored surface.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing `AdvShell` tab registry and `AdvMoreMenu` grouping rather than introducing a new navigation or brainstorming surface. Lazy-load the canonical `BrainstormFull` from the current per-harness panel, classify it as per-pot so All Pots scope hides it, and place it before Plans in a renamed `Create & Build` More group. This trades a small additional route bundle for restored discoverability while retaining the Quick Panel as the fast global doorway.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Re-register `brainstorm` as a per-pot `AdvTabId`.\n- Place it first in the More menu’s renamed `Create & Build` group, immediately before Plans.\n- Render the existing `BrainstormFull` in the current Vite `/adv` panel.\n- Preserve the Quick Panel Brainstorm tab unchanged.\n- Restore legacy/deep-link and shortcut behavior where appropriate.\n- Update focused unit and navigation coverage.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- `?slug=<pot>&tab=brainstorm` renders Brainstorm rather than Overview.\n- Brainstorm is not a primary strip tab and appears in exactly one More-menu group.\n- The surface is hidden in All Pots scope, like other per-pot tabs.\n- Existing welcome and search links land on the restored surface.\n- Focused tests pass.\n\n## Phase 1 — Restore and verify\n- **P-001** `done` Restore Brainstorm as a per-pot secondary `/adv` tab under More by reusing the existing `BrainstormFull`, repairing routing/deep links, and preserving Quick Panel access. importance: high — note: ← WI-1008447 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Update focused navigation/rendering tests and verify the restored Brainstorm path end to end. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-1008448 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Reuse BrainstormFull and preserve both entry points\nDate: 2026-08-30\nMeasured: `apps/operator/app/quick-panel/page.tsx` already lazy-loads the complete `BrainstormFull` surface, while `apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvShell.tsx` removed only the `/adv` tab id and redirects old deep links to Overview. Restore the same component as a per-pot secondary tab under More; keep the Quick Panel entry unchanged. Place Brainstorm before Plans in a renamed `Create & Build` group so idea capture precedes planning without occupying the primary strip.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: canonical test-suite startup restored and its verdict trustworthy","status":"active","created":"2026-08-30","owner":"su-cc991c30-1aab-4f3f-8fd2-8e9031da84e2","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: canonical test-suite startup restored and its verdict trustworthy\nslug: test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-09-09\nowner: su-cc991c30-1aab-4f3f-8fd2-8e9031da84e2\n---\n\n# Acceptance: canonical test-suite startup restored and its verdict trustworthy\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27, authored against AS-BUILT reality on 2026-08-29 after the completion audit (auditSeq 5, 3/3 items verified, verifiedRatio 1.0, 10 citations checked).\n\nThe plan's goal is 'make the canonical root npm test start reliably and finish with a clean verdict on the canonical staging tree'. Note the goal has TWO halves — STARTING reliably (admission) and a CLEAN VERDICT (execution). The plan's own history shows these fail independently and for unrelated reasons, so the criteria below keep them separate rather than collapsing them into one green/red.\n\nWHAT 'RELIABLY' MEANS HERE (operationalised, so a grader does not have to guess): it is REACH + POLICY, not repetition. C1 (the admission guard can reclaim its OWN producer output), C2 (that reach was not bought by loosening the policy) and C3 (reclamation stays bounded, producer-owned and safe) together constitute 'reliably'. There is deliberately NO repeat-runs condition anywhere in this rubric — no criterion requires N consecutive green runs — because the plan's observed failures were STRUCTURAL (a candidate set that could not reach debug/, assertions stale against a deliberately retired contract), not flaky. A grader must not read 'reliably' as demanding a repeat count this rubric does not ask for, nor treat a single green run as failing to establish it.\n\nTwo criteria are deliberately NEGATIVE (C2, C3): the cheapest way to make this plan look done is to lower the admission constants until the host is let in, which D-002 explicitly forbids. A rubric that only asked 'does Cargo start now' would score that cheat full marks.\n\nEVIDENCE DISJOINTNESS: criterion OVERLAP is acceptable (two criteria may both bear on the admission guard); shared EVIDENCE is not. C1 consumes the aggregate green of report-cargo-tests.test.ts; C3 therefore grades on individually-named protective cases within that file and may not be satisfied by the same aggregate.\n\nGrader note: C6 is expected to FAIL at authoring time. P-004 is open, and a rubric written so that everything passes on the day it is written is not measuring anything.\n\nAMENDED 2026-08-30 (first amendment) following an independent vetting critique (su-98f41fcf, conv-mteztuoq), which found four defects in the authoring revision: C6's fail and partial regions overlapped on a plausible outcome; C6's 'undetermined' point was unreachable by construction because it still named a premise this rubric's own CORRECTION had retracted; C1 and C4 hardcoded an exact pass total that would auto-fail on a legitimately added test; and C3's evidence was not separated from C1's. All four are repaired. C5's scale was checked by the critic against live state and deliberately left unchanged — its 'partial' was returning a TRUE reading, and rewording a scale point because it returns a grade the author dislikes is grading the rubric to the artifact.\n\nAMENDED AGAIN 2026-08-30 (second amendment, C6 only) — SELF-CORRECTION. The first amendment rewrote C6's scale WITHOUT first reading this plan's own Decisions, and thereby contradicted three of them. D-006 rules that ANY canonical red whose failing instrument produced no finding grades 'undetermined', not fail (exit status alone is not a finding); the first amendment had narrowed 'undetermined' to resource limits only, pushing a no-finding red into 'fail' and reintroducing the exact gap D-006 was written to close. D-005 rules that an exit 1 with ZERO failed counts whose only failing signal is a boundedPgReadTxn:acquire deadline is infrastructure exhaustion rather than a test red, and that P-004 may close on such a run; the first amendment's flat 'non-zero exit' fail clause contradicted that outright. D-007 (fleet leader, 02:00Z) rules that P-004's run MUST execute from a worktree pinned to a fixed sha, because the canonical run takes ~50 minutes in the live CWD that git-sync commits continuously — run 3 absorbed 35 commits across 122 files and reported failures against code that was never broken — so a live-tree run's reds do not settle P-004 and its exit code does not satisfy the clause. C6 now encodes all three, with an explicit precedence order, so the grader applies them in sequence rather than reconciling them ad hoc. C1-C5 are unchanged by this second amendment.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"unified-web-portal-2026-08-29","title":"Unified web UI — the app.papercusp.com portal across BYOC cloud workspaces, email, calendar, and desktop streaming","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-30","owner":"aviynw3@gmail.com","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Unified web UI — the app.papercusp.com portal across BYOC cloud workspaces, email, calendar, and desktop streaming\nslug: unified-web-portal-2026-08-29\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-10-22\nowner: aviynw3@gmail.com\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** 2026-10-13: su-bf6bd owns P-031/WI-2001281 under fleet byoc-cloud-carry-1013; AUTO and 60s warm loop registered. 45/52 done; seven remain. September R7/r31 READY checkpoint is stale: WI-40472 dropped under D-338. Leader audit requires reuse cloud-cross-feature's existing GCP lifecycle receipts, adding only portal Tauri/private-Git evidence. Current target/org/workspace/DesktopSession/auth-state and original Git-source/scope still need recovery. P-105/P-106/P-109/P-110 precede P-107, then P-015 audit/rubric/grade/ship. Preserve their complete c… <!-- P-099 -->\n- [ ] WI-1931051 — Add contract, render, navigation, bulk-functionality, responsive, and browser acceptance coverage for Direction B; build both affected products, deploy the Portal backend through its supported handof… <!-- P-100 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981742 — Restore the existing operator Accounts-first LeftSidebar beside Papercup Chat when the operator is embedded by the cloud portal, while leaving focused Plans/Inbox routes chromeless. <!-- P-101 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981743 — Filter the embedded `/adv` tab presentation to exactly Overview, HUD, Learning, and Work (`harnesses`), preserving canonical tab IDs and ordinary non-embedded tab navigation. <!-- P-102 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981744 — Add regression coverage for embedded Accounts rail composition and the four-tab allowlist, then run focused portal and operator suites. <!-- P-103 -->\n## Background\n\nWhat exists today, and what this plan adds:\n\n- **BYOC cloud workspaces** — `byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22` (papercusp): local provisioning, GCP/AWS/Azure parity, hosted control plane, browser terminal/file access, and the one-SPA/three-artifact distribution split. This plan is the umbrella that closes its `app.papercusp.com` destination: it consumes the existing BYOC provider/identity/routing work, adds the missing browser transport/sync/production-delivery substrate, and composes that canonical operator SPA into the wider email/calendar/desktop portal without forking it.\n- **Email app** — harness `email`, materialized from the `papercusp-agentic-webapp` template into `.papercusp/apps/email` (WI-41058; plans `email-app-2026-08-23`, shipped via `email-calendar-web-desktop-ship-2026-08-27`). Gmail flows (respond-with-draft), embedded PG, data-sync + search planes, single-user-local AND multi-user-server tenancy.\n- **Calendar app** — harness `calendar` (WI-41060; meeting-prep plans; shipped via the same ship plan). Materialize was resumed on gate `templates-new-app-fix-green`; binding to be re-verified at activation.\n- **Desktop streaming** — the DesktopSession substrate (`agent-virtual-desktops-2026-08-23`) + the Cloud Workspaces embedded pane (`cloud-workspaces-embedded-pane-visual-polish-2026-08-29`): streaming a (cloud) workspace desktop into a browser pane. Per owner ruling on WI-982048, BYOC cloud desktops are agent sandbox desktops.\n\n**The gap:** each product has its own UI, but a customer has no single place to sign in, see their workspaces, read mail, check the calendar, and watch/drive a streamed desktop. This plan delivers that portal: one auth session, one shell (nav + workspace switcher + app launcher + notifications), with the three app surfaces and the BYOC management surface composed inside it.\n\n## Scope and non-goals\n\n**In scope:** the hosted web portal (working name app.papercusp.com): auth + account/session; the unifying shell (nav, workspace switcher, launcher, notification/badge plumbing); embedded or composed surfaces for email, calendar, and desktop streaming; the BYOC workspace-management surface (list / provision / connect / start-stop / backups) driving the BYOC control plane; responsive behavior down to tablet width.\n\n**Non-goals:** replacing the operator desktop (Tauri) UI; re-implementing app internals (the portal COMPOSES the existing apps — reuse-first, no forks); the marketing site (papercusp.com is its own pot); native mobile.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- **R-001** One signed-in web portal (app.papercusp.com) unifying Mail, Calendar, Desktop streaming, and BYOC workspace management — plus a Papercusp operator surface — as ONE experience while each app keeps its canonical implementation and tenancy boundary [owner 2026-08-29/30].\n- **R-002** Hybrid shell architecture: persistent app rail (Option B) with the Mission Control dashboard (Option A) as Home — D-009.\n- **R-003** Light AND dark themes with easy switching; ONE shared token system across portal + email + calendar apps; the theme propagates to every embedded surface — D-011 [owner 2026-08-30].\n- **R-004** Compose the existing canonical apps/SPA — never fork or re-implement (reuse-first; the BYOC integration map governs reuse boundaries).\n- **R-005** Web-ready transports: desktop keeps endpoint-IPC routing; the browser obeys the six-connection origin budget via one per-origin scheduler [owner 2026-08-29] — see \"Web-readiness architecture\".\n- **R-006** Scaffold from the papercusp-agentic-webapp template into its own harness; the portal carries an embedded agent/copilot plane — D-010.\n- **R-007** Hosted multi-tenant correctness: tenant isolation, revocation bounds, and the assembled BYOC acceptance gates per \"Web-readiness acceptance criteria\".\n- **R-008** Responsive to tablet width; native mobile out of scope.\n\nProvenance + full audit trail: \"Owner requirements and technical source audit\" below, and Decisions D-009–D-011.\n\n## Design\n\n- **Shell:** left app rail (Home, Mail, Calendar, Desktops, Workspaces, Papercusp, Settings) + slim top bar (workspace switcher, global search, notifications, account). Home renders the Mission Control dashboard (Inbox / Today / Desktops / Workspaces / Notifications cards). Mockups: design canvas \"Papercusp Portal\" (WI-1026732; sources under .papercusp scratch, re-seedable); the Session Stage stream HUD (quality/latency chips, keyboard/clipboard/fullscreen/disconnect) carries into the Desktops viewer.\n- **Composition:** the portal is a template-materialized shell; each surface is composed per the P-004 integration contract (embedded pane / in-shell module / hand-off, decided per surface). The Papercusp surface reuses the cloud-workspaces embedded operator pane seam; the canonical operator SPA is composed, never forked — \"Web-readiness architecture\" governs transports and budgets.\n- **Theming:** one DTCG-sourced token package generating semantic CSS vars — defined on :root (light), overridden under [data-theme=\"dark\"] and @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) guarded by :root:not([data-theme=\"light\"]) (3-state light/dark/system). The portal owns the switch (persisted per account) and propagates it over the P-004 contract; per-app accents are a thin override layer; the package + dark block are upstreamed into the papercusp-agentic-webapp template — D-011.\n- **Data/transport:** one domain/query/mutation contract with transport selected once at the boundary — endpoint IPC on desktop, budgeted HTTP/SSE in the browser under the per-origin scheduler.\n- **Auth:** per P-003 (open): one portal account; Google OAuth attachment for mail/calendar; hosted identity/org/workspace stack per BYOC P-069–P-088.\n\n## Owner requirements and technical source audit\n\nOwner turn, 2026-08-29: make the app web-ready and integrate it with the BYOC plan; keep desktop routing through IPC; handle the browser's historical six-concurrent-request HTTP limit gracefully.\n\nAudited before this revision:\n\n- BYOC revision 584 / hash `83d170b4d8a291f1e36b7f66d488c3cf6c28389d6f0627b12dbc8b0078ba44a0`: every numbered item 001–089 with status/dependencies, all numbered decisions 001–193, and complete bodies for the web/transport/auth/routing/supersession decisions.\n- Governing BYOC decisions: D-001, D-004–D-005, D-008–D-011, D-015, D-017–D-018, D-022, D-025, D-030, D-051–D-052, D-063–D-071, D-075, D-127, D-141–D-143, D-146, D-154, D-159, and D-182.\n- Current desktop transport: `installDesktopIpcPolyfills` transparently routes same-origin `/api/*` fetch and EventSource traffic through Tauri endpoint IPC. `HarnessSyncProvider` starts connection-capped and raises to the measured IPC profile only after `endpoint_ipc_status().client === 'connected'`.\n- Current browser transport: native HTTP/SSE. Sync reads share `CONNECTION_CAPPED_MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 2`, but mutations, auth/control fetches, finite streams, and other EventSources do not share one origin-wide budget.\n- Prior work: `drop-sync-batcher-2026-07-25` shipped the per-query FIFO gate; `no-http-anywhere-2026-07-28` closed desktop transport escape doors but retains an open server-parallelism lane; `arrow-zero-copy-sync-reads-2026-07-26` was superseded after Arrow lost on real nested payloads.\n- Sync writers: the client metric accepts `tsMs`, but the live SSE route drops `SyncEvent.ts` (EI-21843904371852669); bridged invalidations use a 90s leading-only dedupe window; the 180s drift sweep is repair-only; the existing live audit budgets resolver compute at 150ms and payload at 250KB.\n\nBefore activation, re-read the complete source conversations for both this portal draft and the BYOC plan, then re-audit every BYOC revision newer than 584. This is a reviewable draft, not authorization to execute from a stale snapshot.\n\n## Web-readiness architecture\n\nThe unified portal may be a template-materialized shell per P-002, but the BYOC operator surface remains the existing canonical SPA. The portal composes that surface; it does not scaffold or fork a replacement. Page components use one domain/query/mutation contract, with transport selected once at the boundary.\n\n### Desktop IPC invariants\n\n- Keep `window.fetch` and `window.EventSource` routed through `@papercusp/desktop-ipc` → Tauri → the multiplexed endpoint-IPC channel for the local operator document.\n- Do not make desktop pages select HTTP themselves. A required-IPC failure stays loud; ambiguous non-idempotent writes are never replayed.\n- Select the concurrency profile from the proven IPC client state, not from shell presence. Connected IPC keeps its separately measured high-concurrency profile.\n- A credential-free remote HTTPS document loaded in the thin shell remains a browser client of the Server origin that served it; it must not route through a different local operator's IPC bridge.\n\n### Browser HTTP/SSE and the six-connection budget\n\nCorrectness assumes only six HTTP/1.1 connections per origin:\n\n1. One long-lived connection for a consolidated control SSE stream.\n2. One connection reserved exclusively for auth, mutation, cancel, navigation, or another direct user interaction.\n3. One unallocated recovery/navigation slot so an unclassified or recovery call cannot starve.\n4. At most three admitted finite requests in the remaining space, with background sync work capped at two. Every additional same-origin long-lived stream dynamically shrinks the finite limit.\n5. HTTP/2/3 can raise a measured throughput cap, but never removes priority, queue bounds, cancellation, or server-cost limits.\n\nOne shared per-origin scheduler—not one gate per hook—extends the existing sync gate. It supplies:\n\n- `interactive-control`, `foreground-read`, `background-sync`, and `bulk` classes;\n- a reserved interactive lane that background work cannot consume;\n- FIFO within a class, bounded waiters, cancellation on unmount, and shedding/coalescing of superseded background work;\n- no transparent replay of unsafe mutations after an ambiguous failure;\n- active-stream registration plus in-flight, queued, queue-wait, request-time, outcome, byte, and negotiated-protocol metrics;\n- multi-tab coordination: one elected control-stream owner shares events through `BroadcastChannel`, hidden tabs pause background work, and leases expire when a tab disappears. If coordination is unavailable, each tab uses the conservative profile rather than optimistic fan-out.\n\nBulk files and browser PTY/desktop streams are registered separately and follow the BYOC connection-profile/reverse-connector contract. They cannot consume the portal control origin's reserved interactive capacity.\n\n### Sync correctness and performance\n\n- Preserve `SyncEvent.ts` as `tsMs` through the SSE route. Measure server resolve, scheduler wait, request/transfer, parse/cache, React commit, and update-to-screen as separate intervals.\n- Replace leading-only 90s suppression with immediate-first plus bounded trailing-latest coalescing. Intermediate burst states may collapse, but the final version must always push within the freshness budget; the 180s sweep remains a fault-repair backstop.\n- Retain Last-Event-ID replay and delta version/checksum guards. Reconnect and cross-tab stream-leader transfer must converge without a polling storm.\n- Apply the existing `sync-read-audit` 150ms compute / 250KB payload ceilings and query-health guards. Fix staged resolver work, projection shape, windowing, duplicate keys, and shared-cache/server parallelism before selecting a new query engine.\n- Consume rather than duplicate the open server-parallelism lane in `no-http-anywhere-2026-07-28` / WI-6616. Re-measure after its shared-cache result lands.\n- A narrow incremental-maintenance pilot may target representative BYOC relational views only behind the existing `@papercusp/sync` contract. It proceeds only if it beats the optimized current path on p95 update-to-screen, CPU, memory, and correctness; a losing pilot closes with evidence and does not restore Zero app-wide.\n\n## BYOC integration map\n\n| BYOC range | Portal treatment |\n| --- | --- |\n| P-001–P-006 | Consume provider/topology/threat/workflow/test foundations; do not redefine them. |\n| P-007–P-012 | Reuse the canonical Cloud Workspaces page plus GCP provider/storage/connectivity behavior. |\n| P-013–P-017 | Preserve connection manager, psu selector, native-launch tickets, native auth, and remote GUI parity; browser fallbacks are explicit capabilities. |\n| P-018–P-025 | GCP E2E, chaos/recovery, private-beta, image, backup, cost, soak, and orphan gates are prerequisites for the first GCP portal cut; destructive provider work is not duplicated. |\n| P-026–P-035 | Keep AWS/Azure code behind the same provider-neutral UI. D-154's deferred live canaries remain successor gates, not implied parity. |\n| P-036–P-045 | Carry hosted control-plane deployment, browser terminal/file, migration, security, and multi-tenant outcomes into this plan, preserving their later decisions. |\n| P-046–P-048 | Consume initialization/credential delivery, transport capabilities, and the one-SPA/three-artifact distribution split. |\n| P-049–P-056 | Reuse vm-release and supply-chain artifacts; the portal/browser never embeds Server/runtime payloads. |\n| P-057–P-058 | Platform plan-promotion/admission fixes remain infrastructure; no portal duplication. |\n| P-059 | Re-home the deferred app.papercusp.com deployment as this plan's production-delivery lane. |\n| P-060–P-068 | Honor D-127 supersession by P-069–P-088. P-068's never-run assembled acceptance remains an explicit release gate. |\n| P-069–P-088 | Consume hosted profile, WorkOS, sessions, identity/org/workspace schema, Principal/permissions, RLS, lifecycle, entitlements, governance, and attack-harness units; verify them through assembled-system acceptance. |\n| P-089 | Reuse the redesigned canonical page and fail-closed action client; do not fork it. |\n\nD-154 remains binding: the first live cut is GCP. This plan resumes the hosted/browser work deferred from that cut without rewriting the provider sequence. AWS/Azure live parity is carried forward until their real-account canaries exist.\n\n## Web-readiness acceptance criteria\n\n1. The canonical operator SPA and domain contracts pass in a normal browser and Tauri; page code does not fork its data model by runtime.\n2. Tauri same-origin fetch/EventSource remains on endpoint IPC, connected IPC retains its measured profile, native psu/terminal behavior is intact, and required-IPC failure is loud.\n3. Under a deterministic six-connection HTTP/1.1 origin, a cold BYOC page plus control SSE and an active finite stream cannot starve login, lifecycle mutation, cancel, or navigation. Background work never occupies the reserved interactive lane.\n4. Scheduler metrics expose streams, in-flight/queued work and queue wait by priority. No waiter is unbounded; stale background work is cancelled/shed; unsafe writes are not automatically replayed.\n5. Multiple tabs use one control event spine per origin and converge after owner-tab loss. Hidden tabs do not multiply standing connections or background waves.\n6. The server timestamp reaches the client metric. Commit → event, refetch, parse/cache, and paint are measured separately.\n7. Repeated same-key writes inside the former 90s window deliver the final state within 2s in the normal path. The 180s sweep is tested only as recovery.\n8. Representative BYOC views meet resolver p95 ≤150ms where the existing budget applies, payload ≤250KB unless explicitly allowlisted, warm update-to-screen p95 ≤1s, and no accepted tail above 2s without a named external dependency and approved exception.\n9. Hosted auth/RLS/CSRF/HTTP/SSE/WS/PTY/file/MCP/direct-SQL tests prove Tenant A cannot enumerate, subscribe to, route to, or mutate Tenant B. Revocation closes access within D-069's 60s bound.\n10. Browser terminal/file/desktop flows use the D-143 reverse connector and scoped tickets without public VM operator, Postgres, or MCP ports. Bulk transfer does not consume reserved portal control capacity.\n11. A real GCP workspace can be provisioned, initialized, connected, used from browser and desktop, stopped/started, backed up/restored, upgraded/repaired, and destroyed with zero billable orphan residue, reusing BYOC evidence rather than repeating destructive steps gratuitously.\n12. app.papercusp.com negotiates HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, but the same build passes the forced HTTP/1.1 cap test. Production has a reproducible artifact, exact SHA, CSP/TLS/cache/SSE/WS ingress, telemetry, canary, rollback, and disaster-recovery evidence.\n13. BYOC's assembled tenant-isolation gate actually runs; the hosted authorization/RLS unit-test slice is not substitute acceptance.\n14. Email, calendar, desktop streaming, and BYOC workspace management remain one portal experience while each underlying app keeps its canonical implementation and tenancy boundary.\n15. AWS/Azure remain visible and capability-correct in the shared surface, while live parity claims remain deferred until their successor real-account canaries run.\n\n## Risks and rollout gates\n\n- A global wrapper could throttle IPC: profile selection must use proven transport capability and both profiles get regression tests.\n- Long-lived responses can hold finite slots: streams register separately and finite requests have total deadlines.\n- A per-tab gate cannot protect a per-origin pool: cross-tab stream ownership and leases are required, with conservative fallback.\n- HTTP/2 can hide HTTP/1 regressions: retain a six-socket fixture.\n- Removing dedupe can restore storms: preserve source-aware coalescing and measure event/refetch rate under sustained writes.\n- Transport tuning can hide slow resolvers: scheduler wait, request, resolve, transfer, and paint stay separate.\n- BYOC changes concurrently: re-audit later decisions before activation and before any cross-plan completion claim.\n- Hosted unit green can masquerade as acceptance: BYOC decision D-182 blocks that misrepresentation and the assembled tenant-isolation gate must run.\n\nRollout order: contract/baseline → origin scheduler + stream spine under forced HTTP/1.1 → sync correctness/performance → hosted auth/routing/PTY/file in two-tenant staging → real GCP Stage-A/Stage-B E2E + soak → app.papercusp.com canary + exercised rollback → code-truth audit and independent graded acceptance.\n\n## Phase 0 — Owner decisions (gate to activation)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Pick the portal design This navigation task is independent of the live GCP P-031 gate. importance: high — note: ← WI-2146954 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n(recorded via plans:add-decision as they are made — none yet; P-001..P-004 will produce the first ones)\n\n### D-001 — Desktop endpoint IPC is a hard runtime invariant\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: Supported Tauri operator documents keep same-origin `/api/*` fetch and EventSource traffic transparently on `@papercusp/desktop-ipc` through the multiplexed Tauri endpoint-IPC channel. Page code does not select HTTP for desktop. A required-IPC failure remains loud, and an ambiguous non-idempotent write is never replayed. A remote HTTPS document displayed by a thin shell remains a browser client of the origin that served it and may not borrow a different local operator's IPC bridge. The higher concurrency profile is selected only after the IPC client reports connected and is benchmarked separately from browser transport.\n\nMeasured: 2026-08-30 source/code audit found `installDesktopIpcPolyfills` wraps same-origin fetch and EventSource, while `HarnessSyncProvider` raises its cap only after `endpoint_ipc_status().client === 'connected'`; owner source turn `session_turn:codex:01a05076-7bde-7ab0-a5e7-1ef96fa32565:11` explicitly requires keeping desktop IPC. This extends, rather than forks, the existing no-HTTP transport boundary.\nRelated: P-016, P-017, P-019, P-025, P-029\n\n### D-002 — HTTP/1.1 six-connection correctness is the browser baseline\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: Browser correctness assumes a six-connection HTTP/1.1 origin even when production negotiates HTTP/2 or HTTP/3. The conservative allocation is one consolidated control SSE connection, one slot reserved exclusively for auth/mutation/cancel/navigation or another direct interaction, one unallocated recovery/navigation slot, and at most three admitted finite calls; background work may occupy at most two. Every additional same-origin standing stream reduces finite admission dynamically. HTTP/2/3 may increase a measured throughput cap but cannot remove priority, bounds, cancellation, or server-cost controls.\n\nMeasured: 2026-08-30 source/code audit confirmed browser traffic uses native HTTP/SSE and the existing `CONNECTION_CAPPED_MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 2` protects sync reads only—not all origin traffic or streams. The six-connection failure mode is an explicit owner constraint in `session_turn:codex:01a05076-7bde-7ab0-a5e7-1ef96fa32565:11`.\nRelated: P-017, P-018, P-019, P-020, P-021, P-029\n\n### D-003 — One per-origin scheduler owns browser finite-request admission\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: Extend the existing generic sync concurrency gate into one process-pinned, per-origin scheduler rather than adding gates per hook or app. Every finite same-origin browser call—sync reads and prefetch, auth/session, mutations, lifecycle actions, shell reads, and remaining raw fetch clients—must enter it. It provides `interactive-control`, `foreground-read`, `background-sync`, and `bulk` classes; a background-proof interactive reservation; FIFO within class; bounded waiters; unmount cancellation; stale-background shedding/coalescing; total deadlines; active-stream registration; and class/outcome/wait/byte/protocol metrics. Multi-tab control-stream ownership is coordinated with leases and `BroadcastChannel`; coordination failure uses the conservative profile.\n\nMeasured: 2026-08-30 code audit found one existing per-query FIFO gate in `@papercusp/sync`, but no origin-wide admission surface covering auth, mutations, finite streams, raw clients, or extra EventSources. This decision reuses that gate and the BYOC transport-capability/reverse-connector seams.\nRelated: P-016, P-018, P-019, P-020, P-021, P-029\n\n### D-004 — Push freshness delivers the final state and preserves stage timing\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: The normal push path must deliver the final version of repeated same-key writes, not merely the first version of a burst. Preserve `SyncEvent.ts` through SSE as `tsMs`; measure commit/event receipt, scheduler wait, resolver work, transfer, parse/cache, React commit, and update-to-screen separately. Replace the 90-second leading-only bridge suppression with source-aware immediate-first plus bounded trailing-latest coalescing. Intermediate burst states may collapse, but the final state must arrive within two seconds in the normal path. The 180-second sweep remains repair-only, with Last-Event-ID replay and delta checksum/version guards preserved.\n\nMeasured: 2026-08-30 writer/call-path audit found the client latency metric accepts `tsMs`, the live SSE route omits `SyncEvent.ts`, bridged invalidations suppress repeat keys for 90 seconds, and the 180-second sweep repairs drift. Source turns 6–10 asked for actual push latency and established that resolver recomputation—not socket fanout—dominates current warm/tail behavior.\nRelated: P-017, P-022, P-023, P-024, P-029\n\n### D-005 — The portal consumes canonical BYOC lineage and ships GCP first\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: `byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22` remains the canonical provider, topology, identity, routing, lifecycle, supply-chain, and hosted-control-plane authority. This portal composes the existing BYOC operator SPA and its domain contracts; it does not scaffold or fork a replacement. The portal consumes all P-001–P-089 outcomes and later supersessions, re-homes the deferred `app.papercusp.com` delivery lane, and reuses valid destructive evidence. Per BYOC D-154, the first live portal cut is GCP. AWS/Azure remain visible and capability-correct, but no live-parity claim is made until their real-account successor canaries run.\n\nMeasured: 2026-08-30 plan audit read BYOC revision 584 / hash `83d170b4d8a291f1e36b7f66d488c3cf6c28389d6f0627b12dbc8b0078ba44a0`, all 89 items and 193 decisions; the plan names `app.papercusp.com` as a destination and retains GCP-first/deferred-provider sequencing. Owner source turns `session_turn:claude:02378061-2db6-47e9-82ea-2989dead4ec4:0` and `session_turn:codex:01a05076-7bde-7ab0-a5e7-1ef96fa32565:11` require one unified portal integrated with that work.\nRelated: P-012, P-013, P-025, P-026, P-027, P-028, P-030, P-031\n\n### D-006 — Hosted browser access is control-plane-only and tenant-scoped\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: The hosted BYOC surface uses the canonical static SPA in the hosted control-plane-only profile. It requires fixed-scope hydration, validated WorkOS sessions, a dedicated non-owner RLS role, exact-origin CSRF/CORS, tenant-aware authenticated HTTP/SSE, fail-closed capability fallbacks, and short-lived single-use reverse-connector tickets bound to user, organization, workspace, host, resource/action, transport, and session. It must not expose local default-user identity, loopback/public routes, process-global workspace selection, desktop bridge APIs, local process/file routes, reusable host bearers, or public VM operator/Postgres/MCP ports.\n\nMeasured: 2026-08-30 BYOC revision-584 audit traced the hosted profile, Principal/permission/RLS lineage and the outbound reverse-connector decision (`byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-143`). This decision composes those existing seams into the portal rather than creating a parallel auth or routing system.\n\nTopology rationale: P-025 intentionally converges six prerequisite domains—portal decisions, scheduler/stream/freshness, and resolver performance—because hosted exposure is the security integration boundary; splitting it would permit partial browser enablement without the whole fail-closed contract.\nRelated: P-025, P-026, P-027, P-028, P-030\n\n### D-007 — Query-engine change is a measured narrow pilot, never app-wide Zero\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: First bring representative portal/BYOC named queries inside the existing 150 ms compute and 250 KB payload budgets by correcting staged resolver work, projections, windows, duplicate keys, and shared-cache/server parallelism, consuming the open WI-6616 result from `no-http-anywhere-2026-07-28`. Only if material tails remain may a narrow incremental-maintenance pilot run behind the existing `@papercusp/sync` contract. Adopt it only on measured p95 update-to-screen, CPU, memory, and correctness wins; otherwise close the pilot with evidence.
