Extends D-009's rail composition.\n\n### D-016 — P-004 app-integration contract: in-shell module is the DEFAULT; embedded pane only where an independent runtime is required; no subdomain hand-off for any rail surface\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDate: 2026-08-30. Resolves P-004. Decided by su-0d5049ee under owner-directed AUTO mode, NOT by an owner dialog — unlike D-009/D-010/D-011/D-013. Flagged plainly so the owner can override cheaply; a Decision is addressable after delivery, which is why this is recorded here rather than in a message.\n\nTHE RULE, per surface:\n\n| Rail surface | Contract | Why |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Home (Mission Control) | in-shell module | native shell content; renders from the shared data layer |\n| Workspaces (BYOC Cloud Workspaces) | in-shell module composing the CANONICAL page | P-089 \"reuse the redesigned canonical page and fail-closed action client; do not fork it\" |\n| Mail | in-shell module | P-008 requires unified badge counts in the shell |\n| Calendar | in-shell module | P-009 requires today/next-meeting data feeding the Home surface |\n| Papercusp (operator app) | embedded pane, via the cloud-workspaces embedded operator pane seam | P-091, verbatim: \"never a second embed path\" |\n| Desktops | embedded pane + separately registered stream transport | see the companion decision on the desktop-stream transport |\n| Settings | in-shell module | native shell content |\n\nWHY SUBDOMAIN HAND-OFF IS REJECTED FOR EVERY RAIL SURFACE. It is not merely less convenient, it breaks four things this plan has already committed to:\n1. Theme propagation. The Design section states the portal \"owns the switch (persisted per account) and propagates it over the P-004 contract\". A cross-origin document cannot inherit the semantic CSS vars; it would need a bespoke postMessage theme channel, i.e. a second theming path, contradicting D-011's single shared token package.\n2. The unified notification model. P-011 requires one notification center and badge model spanning email, calendar, desktops and workspace events. Cross-origin surfaces cannot feed one badge model without inventing a second aggregation transport.\n3. Session/account continuity. P-003's single portal account plus per-app Google OAuth attachment implies one session context, not a hand-off per surface.\n4. Shell chrome. A hand-off leaves the rail and top bar behind, which is the whole of D-009's App Dock shell.\nHand-off remains correct ONLY for genuinely external destinations that were never portal surfaces (for example a cloud provider's own console). It is not an option in the rail.\n\nWHY IN-SHELL MODULE IS THE DEFAULT RATHER THAN IFRAME-EVERYWHERE. The binding constraint is the browser connection budget in \"Web-readiness architecture\": correctness assumes six HTTP/1.1 connections per origin, with one consolidated control SSE, one reserved interactive slot, one recovery slot, and at most three admitted finite requests — and explicitly, \"every additional same-origin long-lived stream dynamically shrinks the finite limit\". Each same-origin iframe that opens its own SSE consumes budget the shared scheduler cannot see or arbitrate, because the architecture mandates \"one shared per-origin scheduler — not one gate per hook\". In-shell modules share the ONE control stream and the ONE scheduler, which is the only composition that keeps that budget analysable. Cross-origin iframes would each get their own budget but reintroduce every problem in the paragraph above.\n\nTHE COST, STATED HONESTLY: in-shell modules bind Mail and Calendar into the portal's build and release cadence, so a surface can no longer ship independently. That is a real loss and the strongest argument for hand-off. It is accepted because P-008/P-009 require the shell to aggregate their DATA (badge counts, next-meeting), which already forces a shared data contract; once the data layer is shared, an independent UI deployment buys much less than it costs.\n\nTHE ONE GENUINELY OPEN CALL, flagged for the owner: Mail and Calendar are the least-constrained rows. They are separately materialized apps, and the plan does not state their contract the way P-089 states Workspaces' and P-091 states Papercusp's. I chose in-shell module from the P-008/P-009 data requirements alone. If the owner wants them shipping on independent cadences, the alternative is an embedded pane (NOT hand-off — hand-off still fails all four points above), and only those two rows change; the rest of this decision stands unaltered.\n\nMeasured: plan sections read at 2026-08-30T05:30Z via plans:get on this slug, version 61, contentHash b6afcafd0c6a — \"Web-readiness architecture\" (six-connection budget; one shared per-origin scheduler; \"the portal composes that surface; it does not scaffold or fork a replacement\"), \"Design\" (composition + theming + one domain/query/mutation contract), \"BYOC integration map\" (P-089 do-not-fork), \"Phase 2 — App surfaces\" (P-008/P-009/P-010/P-011/P-091 texts quoted above).\nRelated: P-004, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-091\n\n### D-017 — P-004 desktop-stream embed transport: split the surface — viewer chrome is an in-shell module, the stream is a separately registered transport outside the portal control origin's connection budget\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDate: 2026-08-30. Resolves the second half of P-004 (\"the desktop-stream embed transport (reuse the DesktopSession/embedded-pane seam)\"). Companion to D-016. Decided by su-0d5049ee under owner-directed AUTO mode, not by an owner dialog.\n\nTHE SPLIT, which is the whole decision: the Desktops surface is ONE rail item but TWO transports, and conflating them is the failure mode this decision exists to prevent.\n\n1. VIEWER CHROME — in-shell module, per D-016's default. The rail item, the Session Stage stream HUD (quality/latency chips, keyboard/clipboard/fullscreen/disconnect), the full-screen toggle, the reconnect UI, and the desktop LIST all live in the shell document. They consume the shared per-origin scheduler and the single consolidated control SSE like every other surface, so they inherit theming (D-011) and feed the unified notification/badge model (P-011) with no second path.\n\n2. THE MEDIA/INPUT STREAM ITSELF — a separately REGISTERED transport following the BYOC connection-profile / reverse-connector contract, and explicitly NOT accounted against the portal control origin's six-connection budget. \"Web-readiness architecture\" is unambiguous: \"Bulk files and browser PTY/desktop streams are registered separately and follow the BYOC connection-profile/reverse-connector contract. They cannot consume the portal control origin's reserved interactive capacity.\"\n\nWHY THE SPLIT IS FORCED, not stylistic. A desktop stream is a long-lived, high-throughput connection. The budget model in \"Web-readiness architecture\" allows six HTTP/1.1 connections per origin and states that \"every additional same-origin long-lived stream dynamically shrinks the finite limit\". A stream admitted as an ordinary same-origin request would therefore consume the finite pool that the interactive and recovery lanes depend on, and — worse — would do so invisibly to the one shared scheduler that is supposed to arbitrate it. Two concurrent desktop panes would exhaust the budget outright. Registering the stream separately is what keeps the control origin's reserved interactive capacity provably intact, which is the property the whole scheduler design rests on.\n\nREUSE, NOT A SECOND EMBED PATH. The pane uses the SAME DesktopSession / embedded-pane seam that P-091 pins for the Papercusp surface, whose instruction is verbatim \"never a second embed path\". One embed seam serves both the operator-app pane and the desktop viewer; a bespoke desktop-only embed would fork it. Concretely this means the Desktops viewer is an embedded pane in D-016's taxonomy, and its distinguishing feature versus the Papercusp pane is only which transport its content registers, not a different embedding mechanism.\n\nRECONNECT SEMANTICS ARE SEPARATE AND MUST NOT BE CONFLATED. The control SSE's Last-Event-ID replay and delta version/checksum guards belong to the control stream. The desktop stream has its own reconnect lifecycle under the connection-profile contract. P-010's \"reconnect semantics\" refers to the latter; a reconnecting desktop stream must not trigger control-stream reconnection, and a control-stream reconnect must not tear down a healthy desktop stream. Implementations should assert this independence rather than assume it.\n\nCAPABILITY DECLARATION, NOT SILENT DEGRADATION. BYOC P-013–P-017 requires preserving \"connection manager, psu selector, native-launch tickets, native auth, and remote GUI parity\", and states that \"browser fallbacks are explicit capabilities\". The browser desktop viewer therefore DECLARES its capability set (clipboard, keyboard passthrough, audio, resolution/scaling, file transfer) and shows what is unavailable in-browser, rather than silently presenting a degraded stream as parity with the native path.\n\nMULTI-TAB. The elected control-stream owner / BroadcastChannel model in \"Web-readiness architecture\" governs the CONTROL stream only. It must not be extended to multiplex a desktop stream across tabs — a stream is bound to the pane that opened it. Where coordination is unavailable, the conservative profile applies, per the same section.\n\nMeasured: plan sections read at 2026-08-30T05:30Z via plans:get on this slug, version 61, contentHash b6afcafd0c6a — \"Web-readiness architecture\" (streams registered separately; cannot consume reserved interactive capacity; six-connection budget; BroadcastChannel control-stream election), \"Design\" (Session Stage stream HUD carries into the Desktops viewer), \"Phase 2 — App surfaces\" (P-010 and P-091 texts), \"BYOC integration map\" (P-013–P-017 browser fallbacks as explicit capabilities).\nRelated: P-004, P-010, P-091\n\n### D-018 — Latest owner execution route: su-cf372 implements directly; D-010's earlier session-route clause is superseded\nDate: 2026-08-30\nDecision: Owner source turn `session_turn:codex:01a050ba-0ac5-7221-aa4a-8d7efda7f183:19` explicitly directs this current session (`su-cf372db2-1b1a-4b60-b143-f6aa1f94c3a6`) to enter AUTO mode and implement the plan itself from start to finish. Contrasted against the loopback tier documented at apps/portal/apps/host/src/workspace-hosts.ts:180-207.\nRelated: P-026, P-012\n\n### D-027 — P-026 ticket handling: route-label validation, an audience allowlist of one, and a rebuilt success body — the three things the portal adds that upstream cannot\nDate: 2026-08-31\nAll seven of P-026's required binding dimensions are ALREADY bound upstream by `HostedConnectorTicketBinding` — user→userId, organization→organizationId, workspace→customerWorkspaceId, host→hostId, resource/action→audience, transport→transport, session→hostedSessionId — and single-use + short-lived are `consumeTicket` plus the 60s default session TTL. Three rulings, and one gap recorded rather than papered over.\n\n1. EXPORT AND RELINQUISHMENT ARE ONE RESULT, NOT TWO STEPS.\n`exportLocalAuthority` returns `{ bundle, next }` together, and the route persists `next` BEFORE returning the bundle. The tempting shape — mint the bundle, keep local authoritative \"until the import succeeds\" — IS the two-master window this item exists to close: between those two moments, two processes both legitimately claim the account. A signature that handed back only a bundle would let a caller emit a transferable copy and never record that it had, re-introducing the same bug one layer up. If the relinquish write fails, the caller gets an error and NO bundle; that is the safe direction.\n\n2. THERE IS NO HOSTED→LOCAL DIRECTION, AND ITS ABSENCE IS ENFORCED.\nThe watermark's `sourceProfile` is typed as the literal `\"local\"`, and `parseAuthorityBundle` refuses anything else with `authority_bundle_wrong_direction`. Not merely unbuilt: a hosted account's state is tenant-scoped and RLS-bound upstream, so emitting it into an unauthenticated local process would be an exfiltration path wearing a feature's clothes. An unbuilt route gets built by the next person who wants one; a refusal by shape does not.\n\n3. THE WATERMARK HASHES THE PAYLOAD, NEVER ITSELF.\n`contentHash` is sha256 over a key-sorted canonicalization of the payload only. Canonical ordering is load-bearing: `JSON.stringify` preserves insertion order, so an honest round-trip that rebuilt the object differently would read as tampering — a false alarm that teaches operators to ignore the real one. A hash over its own container would also force the verifier to re-derive which fields to exclude, which is exactly where this check usually goes wrong.\n\nRefusals, all of which have tests: replay of a spent export; a SECOND, different export onto an account that already holds authority (the multi-master refusal); an altered payload; the wrong identity in either direction. A re-offer of the export ALREADY in force is an idempotent no-op rather than a refusal, because that is what a retried upload looks like and refusing it would push operators toward clearing the ledger to get unstuck — the one action that genuinely re-enables replay.\n\n⚠ ACCEPTED GAP: THE SPENT-EXPORT LEDGER IS PER-ACCOUNT. `runtime.serviceFor(ownerId)` builds one store per owner, so `consumedExportIds` is owner-scoped and ONE bundle can be imported into TWO DIFFERENT hosted accounts. This is inherent to an offline bundle with no pre-declared target — the exporting local side does not know which hosted account will receive it, so nothing in the bundle can bind one. The invariant P-027 actually names (no local/hosted multi-master) still holds absolutely, because the local side relinquished before the bundle existed. Verified by apps/portal/tests/authority-handoff.test.ts (15) + authority-handoff-routes.test.ts (5, a real export→import through the host).\nRelated: P-027\nRelated: P-027\n\n### D-031 — P-027 provider parity: AWS/Azure stay VISIBLE but are refused at the seam, because upstream's own delegation adapters are unavailable — and the portal's table is pinned to that fact\nDate: 2026-08-31\nDate: 2026-08-31\nAcceptance criterion 15 asks that \"AWS/Azure remain visible and capability-correct in the shared surface, while live parity claims remain deferred\". Before this item the Workspaces connect form offered three plain `<option>` values — Google Cloud, AWS, Azure — with no annotation. That is a parity claim made BY OMISSION, which is why it needed an explicit negative rather than merely no positive.\n\nRULING, three parts:\n\n1. THE CAPABILITY IS UPSTREAM'S FACT, NOT THE PORTAL'S POLICY. The hosted plane wires provider delegation adapters in `productionProviderDelegationAdapters()`: GCP gets a real `verify()`, while AWS and Azure both get an adapter whose `verify()` unconditionally throws `hosted_provider_delegation_<provider>_adapter_unavailable`. THE SEAM REFUSES BEFORE FORWARDING. `postWorkspaceHostCommand` rejects the CONNECTION leg for a deferred provider (`workspace_host_provider_parity_deferred`) and for an unrecognised one (`workspace_host_provider_unknown`), without contacting the control plane. The gate is scoped to `connection` only: a provision call names a connection already vetted at connect time, so re-gating it would refuse legitimate work on a live provider.\n\n3. ENFORCEMENT IS SERVER-SIDE; THE UI IS THE COURTESY HALF. The form generates its options from the capability table (so a provider cannot reach the UI without declaring its parity), labels deferred ones \"— not yet available\", shows the reason, and disables submit. Do NOT ship via the D-043 bookkeeping path; audit #20 already replaced its stale `dropped` verdicts with not-code (P-015), partial (P-028), missing (P-029–P-031).\nRelated: P-015, P-028, P-029, P-030, P-031\n\n### D-046 — The P-028 cut-over gate is --check-env WITH reference resolution, not name presence\nDate: 2026-09-02\nSupersedes the operating caveat that `--check-env` exit 0 could not be trusted as the cut-over gate (D-037/D-044: never publish a half-configured profile behind app.papercusp.com).\n\n**The defect** (filed by su-0c710c57 as WI-2141402, confirmed independently in code): `check_env` tested `[[ -n \"${!name:-}\" ]]` over all seven REQUIRED_NAMES. Four of those names hold a REFERENCE — the name of a secret to look up — so `set` meant only that a pointer string was present. Nothing dereferences the refs at boot either. So filling the single owner-provided literal (WORKOS_CLIENT_ID) would have flipped the gate to exit 0 with the WorkOS secrets still absent, and the unit would have started clean and passed /api/health while failing every real request. The wall clearing was exactly the moment the gate silently became wrong.\n\n**The ruling.** The cut-over gate is now: three literals SET *and* four `*_REF` references RESOLVING against the encrypted store, dereferenced through `resolveHostedSecretRef` — the same resolver the runtime uses at point of use, so the gate cannot drift from the runtime. Two resolving and two not is the calibration: a gate failing everything would be indistinguishable from a broken gate.\n- `--render-only` → exit 0 (staged cut-over untouched).\n- `testing:run hosted-check-refs.test.ts` → 7 passed / 0 failed. `lint:tsc --files=<both>` → status=clean.\n\nOutstanding wall is exactly WORKOS_CLIENT_ID (literal), WORKOS_API_KEY and WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET.\n\n### D-047 — --check-env now rejects unfilled placeholder literals; D-046's \"sufficient gate\" ruling holds only because of it\nDate: 2026-09-02\nD-046 ruled `deploy-hosted-control-plane.sh --check-env` the SUFFICIENT gate for the app.papercusp.com cut-over, and the armed cut-over procedure fires on its exit 0. Any future literal added to LITERAL_NAMES inherits this check; if one is ever added that can legitimately hold a `your-`/`your_`-prefixed value, narrow `is_unfilled_placeholder` rather than deleting it.\n\nRecurrence guard: `apps/operator/lib/hosted-control-plane-placeholder-guard.test.ts` (24 assertions, executes the predicate rather than text-matching it). Falsifiability proven with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh --fake-destructive`: MUTANT CAUGHT, tree integrity verified byte-identical. Filed and fixed as WI-2141667.\n\nOperational consequence for whoever runs the cut-over: exit 0 is now trustworthy on its own. Remediating WORKOS_CLIENT_ID means uncomment AND fill with the real ID from the WorkOS dashboard — uncommenting alone now fails the gate loudly with a PLACEHOLDER row instead of passing it quietly.\nRelated: P-028\n\n### D-048 — Hosted boot FAILS FAST on an unresolvable secret ref, and the cut-over gate dereferences exactly what the runtime dereferences — no more (extends D-046)\nDate: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02. Extends D-046 (which fixed the gate); closes the two halves of WI-2141402 that D-046 left open, both named in the filing's own proposed fix (its items 2 and 3).\n\n**Half 1 — the gate is a PROCEDURE, so it cannot be the only defence.** D-046 makes `--check-env` exit 0 sufficient, but nothing enforced it: an operator could `--install-only` then `systemctl start` without running it, and the encrypted store can change between gate and start. `createHostedRuntime` resolved exactly ONE of the four references at boot (the session cookie secret); the WorkOS API key and cookie password were resolved per sign-in inside the provider, and the webhook secret per webhook through a thunk. So a profile whose refs were SET with secrets ABSENT started clean, passed /api/health, and first failed on live traffic against app.papercusp.com — which su-54215254 and su-0c710c57 both recorded as worse than a refusal to start.\n\n**Ruling:** `createHostedRuntime` now runs a boot preflight that dereferences every reference the runtime uses, before assembling anything. Resolved values are DISCARDED (only the cookie secret is returned, which composition needed anyway), so point-of-use resolution still picks up a rotated secret — the preflight adds a start-time gate, it does not cache. Failure is `hosted_runtime_secret_ref_unresolved:<ENV_NAME>`; an unrecognised resolver error collapses to a bare `resolution_error`, because a DB connection failure's message can embed a connection string with its password (same discipline as hosted-check-refs.ts `classifyFailure`).\n\n**Half 2 — the gate had the SAME defect inverted, and it was live.** `WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY_REF` carries the `_REF` suffix but is never dereferenced: `createWorkOsWebhookRoute` passes it to the receipt store, which records it verbatim as provenance. It is a signing-key IDENTIFIER, not a secret reference. D-046's gate put it in `OPTIONAL_REF_NAMES` and resolved it, so setting it to its natural value would have turned a CORRECTLY configured deployment red and blocked a cut-over with no failing component to point at. **Ruling:** it is reported as a label (`set  label_not_dereferenced`) and never gates.\n\nBoth halves are one defect class — the gate's predicate and the runtime's predicate drifting apart — and neither is visible from one side alone. So the two lists are now PINNED to each other (derived-truth ladder rung 2): `HOSTED_RUNTIME_RESOLVED_SECRET_REFS` in hosted-runtime.ts is the single source, and doc-claims/hosted-cutover-gate-ref-set.test.ts fails if the script's `REF_NAMES` diverges from it in either direction, or if a label reaches the resolver entrypoint.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-02T15:33-15:41Z on this tree.\n- packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-runtime.ts:210 (pre-fix) resolved ONLY hostedSessionCookieSecretRef at boot; :241 `signatureKeyRef: () => configuration.workosWebhookSignatureKeyRef` is passed unresolved, and packages/operator-core/lib/auth/hosted/workos-webhook-intake.ts:316,326 writes it verbatim via safeExternalRef into webhook_event_receipts.signature_key_ref. `grep -rn signatureKeyRef` over packages+apps returns no resolver call site.\n- Live A/B with the label set to a realistic `workos-webhook-key-2026-08`: pre-fix gate -> `WORKOS_WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY_REF UNRESOLVED resolution_error` (false RED); current gate -> `set label_not_dereferenced`. Live `--check-env` otherwise byte-identical and still exit 1 on the two genuinely-missing WorkOS secrets; `--render-only` still exit 0.\n- Falsifiability of the new pin proven WITHOUT mutating the tree: `scripts/mutation-probe.sh --against-commit HEAD --fake-destructive` -> `verdict=caught` (current 3 passed, historical 2 failed, calibration passed on both snapshots, tree byte-identical).\n- The boot preflight's falsifier is the previously COMMITTED assertion it replaces: HEAD's hosted-runtime.test.ts:55 asserted `resolveSecret` was called exactly once and threw `unexpected eager secret read` on any other ref; the new test asserts 4.\n- Tests: 11 hosted files green (run 26a4e9fe, exit 0), incl. hosted-auth-runtime.bundle-cone; re-run green after the type fix (run 0c894238). `lint:tsc --files=` status=clean on BOTH legs (operator + operator-core) at 15:41:22Z, run last. `lint:tests` clean.\n\n**Explicit residue (NOT done, deliberately):** `hosted-auth-runtime.ts` — the narrow portal composition — still resolves per-request with no boot preflight. It has no in-repo production caller (it is consumed by the portal's esbuild prebundle, which must not inherit operator-state-pg, EI-22091008218242870), and it is not what the systemd unit boots, so it is outside the P-028 cut-over path this rules on. A portal lane that boots it should decide separately.\n\n### D-049 — D-049: the cut-over gate's LITERAL leg is pinned too, and the closure is against readHostedRuntimeConfiguration itself — not a second list\nDate: 2026-09-02\nExtends D-048 (which pinned only the REFERENCE leg) and closes WI-2141766, raised by su-54215254 against D-048.\n\n#### 1. The undetermined question is SETTLED: exporting a literal-names list from hosted-runtime.ts cannot disturb the portal prebundle cone.\n\nsu-54215254 flagged this as explicitly undetermined and it decided WHERE the list could live. It is a non-issue, and the reason is directional:\n\nMeasured 2026-09-02T16:04Z, walking the same static relative-import graph `hosted-auth-runtime.bundle-cone.test.ts` walks:\n- `hosted-auth-runtime.ts` cone = **21 modules**, heavy-substrate modules reachable = **0**, and `hosted-runtime.ts` is **NOT in it**.\n- `hosted-runtime.ts` cone = **3,893 modules**, and it reaches all four FORBIDDEN modules directly (`routes/index.ts`, `sync-sse.ts`, `operator-state-pg.ts`, `integration-credentials.ts`).\n\n`hosted-runtime.ts` is the HEAVY module; the portal-prebundled entry does not import it. Adding an export to it therefore cannot change the cone — nothing in those 21 modules imports it. Re-measured after the export landed: still 21 modules / 0 heavy, and `hosted-auth-runtime.bundle-cone.test.ts` passes (1 test).\n\nThe constraint binds only in the REVERSE direction: nothing inside that 21-module cone may import the list. The doc-claims TEST imports it, and tests are not in the portal bundle. Precedent: `HOSTED_RUNTIME_RESOLVED_SECRET_REFS` is already imported from `hosted-runtime.ts` by that same test under D-048, with the cone green throughout.\n\n**Ruling: the literal-names list lives in `hosted-runtime.ts`, beside the reference list.**\n\n#### 2. Declined su-54215254's rung-1 proposal (\"have readHostedRuntimeConfiguration derive its own reads from the list\"), and pinned harder instead.\n\nTheir filing preferred rung 1 (DERIVE) over rung 2 (PIN). I did not take it, because here it TRADES DOWN: `readHostedRuntimeConfiguration` returns the typed `HostedRuntimeConfiguration` interface, and assembling that object by iterating a name list cannot be expressed without an assertion cast, so a field rename would stop being a compile error. Deriving would buy drift-safety by SPENDING type-safety.\n\nWhat landed keeps both:\n- `HOSTED_RUNTIME_LITERAL_CONFIGURATION` and `HOSTED_RUNTIME_OPTIONAL_LABELS` are `as const satisfies readonly { field: keyof HostedRuntimeConfiguration; env: string }[]`, so a renamed FIELD is a compile error (what rung 1 would have given up).\n- The ENV-name half — which no type can check — is closed in `hosted-cutover-gate-ref-set.test.ts` by EXERCISING the reader rather than re-reading it: supply exactly the catalogued names and it must succeed and produce exactly the catalogued fields; drop each in turn and it must refuse, naming that one.\n\nThis is strictly stronger than the list-vs-list pin WI-2141766 asked for. A list-vs-list pin cannot tell \"agrees with the runtime\" from \"agrees with a stale copy of the runtime\". The closure can, because the runtime is what answers — so a NEW required name fails the gate test even if someone updates both the catalogue and the script.\n\n#### 3. The controls are permanent, because the assertion is a claim ABOUT a checker.\n\nA broken closure check would pass its own assertion silently. So the test carries one deliberately-wrong input per branch, permanently (the repo's prescribed tier-1 pattern for a module subject): a catalogue missing a required name → `incomplete:` (the false-GREEN direction, WI-2141402); a catalogue carrying a name the reader does not require → `not required:` (the false-RED direction, D-048); and a deliberately-wrong READER returning an uncatalogued field → `field set:` (invisible to the other two branches).\n\nMeasured: `packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/hosted-cutover-gate-ref-set.test.ts` 7/7 pass; 17 hosted files / 140 tests pass; `npm run lint:tsc -- --files=…` → `LINT_TSC_RESULT … exit=0 status=clean`. Falsifiability of the two SCRIPT-side legs proven with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh --fake-destructive` against a copy outside the tree (the test's subject path is env-overridable): dropping `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` from LITERAL_NAMES → `verdict=caught`; adding `\"${LITERAL_NAMES[@]}\"` to the resolver call → `verdict=caught`. Both runs verified the tracked file byte-identical afterwards.\n\n#### 4. The generalisation, which is the part worth carrying.\n\nD-048 said a gate is a predicate claiming to predict a runtime predicate, and both directions drift. WI-2141766 is the correction to how I ACTED on that: I pinned the leg that had failed and declared the class closed, when the gate's surface was a script with THREE arrays and I had pinned one. **When you build a drift-pin, enumerate the whole surface it is meant to cover before calling the class closed — otherwise you have MOVED the drift, not stopped it.** And prefer pinning to the BEHAVIOUR (exercise the function) over pinning to another LIST, because only the first can tell agreement from stale agreement.\nRelated: P-028\n\n### D-050 — Keep P-029 blocked on measured public TLS timeout\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured 2026-09-04T23:26:01Z: `curl -4 -I --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 12 --http1.1 https://app.papercusp.com/health` reaches TCP but exits 28 with SSL connection timeout before any HTTP status. Local hosted origin :3880/health remains 200. Therefore P-029's hosted AuthKit/storage-state and HTTP/1.1 acceptance cannot proceed yet; preserve the sticky blocked status and re-probe on the bounded loop. Clear this decision only after public TLS returns HTTP and authenticated sign-in can begin.\nRelated: P-029\n\n### D-051 — P-029 TLS timeout is a box-local SNI filter, not a public outage\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured correction: the in-box `curl -4 -I --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 12 --http1.1 https://app.papercusp.com/health` and `openssl s_client` hang only when SNI is `app.papercusp.com`; the same Cloudflare IP (172.67.145.145) completes TLS 1.3 for SNI `www.cloudflare.com`. A server-side fetch through `https://r.jina.ai/https://app.papercusp.com/api/hosted/auth/session` reaches the public endpoint and returns HTTP 401 `session_cookie_missing`, proving external HTTPS is live. Prior reports treating the local timeout as an external TLS outage are retracted. P-029's remaining blocker is an authenticated Playwright storage-state / credentialed runner; do not clear the plan block until that state exists and hosted acceptance runs. The `papercusp-com.pages.dev` alias returns HTTP 200 for the marketing shell but does not expose the hosted API routes, so it is not itself an acceptance origin.\nRelated: P-029\n\n### D-052 — Accept WorkOS callbacks with an absent nonce only behind state, browser binding, and PKCE\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured: 2026-09-05 live WorkOS Staging AuthKit exchange for the dedicated P-029 password user returned a sealed authenticated session with matching sid, verified email, and Password method, but its access-token claims omitted nonce and amr even though beginSignIn supplied claimNonce. The current provider rejects any absent nonce as invalid_callback, making every real hosted password sign-in fail after the callback. Decision: keep rejecting a present nonce that differs from expectedNonce; tolerate an absent nonce only in exchangeCallback after the route has already consumed signed single-use state, matched the browser-binding digest, and the WorkOS exchange has validated the exact PKCE verifier. This is compatibility with observed provider behavior, not a general nonce bypass. Add regression tests for absent acceptance and present mismatch rejection.\nRelated: P-029\n\n### D-053 — Enforce the hosted browser query vocabulary at the shared sync provider\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured 2026-09-05 on the real app.papercusp.com P-029 path: the hosted route intentionally admits only workspaceHosts.control, which completed successfully over HTTP/1.1, while eight local-shell useSyncQuery consumers produced 24 deterministic 400s after retries and made the zero-transport-failures gate fail. Keep the server allowlist narrow. In hosted mode, pass the exact allowed query names into the existing shared SyncProvider so disallowed hooks are disabled, manual invalidation is inert, and prefetch is skipped before any request. Local mode remains unrestricted. This preserves the unified component tree without widening the credentialed hosted API surface or weakening P-029's failure assertion.\nRelated: P-029\n\n### D-054 — Hosted offline replay acceptance must deterministically sever the physical SSE stream\nDate: 2026-09-05\nChrome CDP offline emulation is not evidence that an already-established EventSource socket has transitioned: the socket can remain open until the 15s heartbeat or 30s zombie detector, longer than P-029's 10s disconnect observation. The hosted acceptance keeps real network offline mode but also drives the production visibility-pause path (its 5-minute timer is already compressed by the test) to close the physical control stream deterministically. It emits one invalidation only while the browser is both offline and physically disconnected, restores network and visibility, then still requires reconnectCount to advance and the named invalidation counter to increase by exactly one. This changes the outage trigger, not the replay/zero-loss/zero-duplication criterion.\n\n### D-055 — Cross-tab physical-owner changes must carry the SSE resume cursor\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-029 measured one offline workspaceHosts.control invalidation arriving twice after a visibility-driven owner pause/resume. The hosted endpoint correctly replays events newer than its supplied cursor, but createCrossTabControlStream destroyed the physical ResilientEventSource—and its tracked lastEventId—without copying that cursor into the wrapper; the replacement therefore connected without a cursor and the hosted route replayed from zero, including the already-seen seed plus the offline event. Extend the existing resilient EventSource with an initialLastEventId option and make the cross-tab wrapper capture the outgoing source cursor, seed every replacement owner source with it, and clear it only when the URL truly changes. Preserve the exact +1 live assertion.\n\n### D-056 — The unconditional steering rail is first-paint shell, while its panel bodies stay lazy\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-029 LayoutShift attribution measured 0.605 of total CLS 0.714 when the route root moved from x=360 to x=744 after the 384px LeftSidebar lazy chunk mounted; the header then contributed another 0.098 reflow. D-017's accepted one-frame tradeoff applies only to the flag-gated OperatorChatSidebar, whose presence was historically unknowable before mount. LeftSidebar is first-class unconditional chrome on every eligible non-embedded route, so its fixed rail shell and reservation must mount in the root's first React commit. Import LeftSidebar eagerly; preserve lazy imports for Accounts/Papercup/Pulse/Conversations panel bodies so the content cost remains deferred. Guard the root import against regression to lazy().\n\n### D-057 — Hosted acceptance owns its document origin and forbids edge-injected third-party scripts\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-029's hosted browser necessarily loads from its exact configured HTTPS origin; declare only that origin in the spec-local egress allowlist. Keep the shared foreign-origin detector strict for every other host. The live edge currently injects Cloudflare Web Analytics from static.cloudflareinsights.com, which the portal CSP blocks but the egress sensor correctly observes. Prevent the transform at the source by adding Cache-Control no-transform to the already no-store dynamic SPA shell; do not allowlist the analytics host or weaken CSP. Guard both the hosted response header and the spec-local exact-origin declaration.\n\n### D-058 — After parity, converge browser and Tauri on one shared UI with native capability adapters and shared themes\nDate: 2026-09-05\nOwner direction: Avi's 2026-09-05 conversation (session_turn:codex:01a0739c-4e96-7be2-a97f-5a79420ecdd2:1 and :3) asks to add the shared-web-UI destination to this plan and continue in AUTO through shipped status. This is a target architecture and queued implementation work, not a claim that current token or screen parity is complete.\n\nAfter the existing parity/real-host acceptance, use one frontend source and shared screens, navigation, components, and themes for the browser and the Tauri desktop shell. Preserve supported local operation by packaging the shared UI with the desktop's local services; loading the public hosted URL must not become a prerequisite for local/offline use.\n\nKeep implementation differences behind typed capability adapters: (1) files, terminals, and local agents use desktop native/local services versus authorized remote workspace APIs or browser-granted access; (2) tray, global shortcuts, native windows, and updater use OS integrations versus available browser equivalents; (3) local/offline operation uses packaged UI/local services versus browser caching and reachable services; (4) native credential storage, authentication, and IPC coexist with web sessions, HTTPS, WebSockets, and SSE. Capability differences must not require forked screen implementations or silently remove working desktop behavior.\n\nExtend D-011/D-013 and the existing shared token surface: make Blue Frost an ordinary selectable theme shared by browser and desktop, retain light/dark/system behavior, and audit actual imports/token ownership before claiming both apps already use one system. Reuse existing theme/token generators and adapters rather than adding parallel registries or a new app scaffold.\n\nSequence the added consolidation and theme work after P-031; then verify the same shared UI in a real browser and the maintained isolated Tauri harness, including native integrations, local/offline operation, auth/transport, and theme propagation. P-015 final audit, one batched as-built rubric revision, independent grading, verdict, and shipment must cover the extended plan; D-044/D-045's real-evidence and no-force-ship requirements remain binding.\nRelated: P-031, P-090, P-015\n\n### D-059 — Web More navigation mirrors desktop secondary groups and keeps existing surface routes\nDate: 2026-09-05\nOwner requirement: session_turn:codex:01a0739c-4e96-7be2-a97f-5a79420ecdd2:13 asks for the desktop More tabs in a new web More button. Measured: desktop AdvShell owns SECONDARY_TAB_GROUPS; all destinations already exist in the portal registry, with plans→create, calendar→scheduled, and settings→adv-settings to distinguish other portal apps. Implementation P-108 extracts the existing secondary metadata into operator-ui and consumes it in both shells. Web secondary entries move into a searchable More popover; primary apps and utility destinations retain their existing routes. The trigger reflects the active secondary section; state uses the existing URL panel slot; keyboard selection, Escape/outside dismissal and focus return use the registered Popover + cmdk controls. Theme colors use portal tokens. P-108 is independent of the GCP READY window and is required before P-015 final shipment.\nRelated: P-108, P-015\n\n### D-060 — Portal-only settings belong inside the canonical Personalization and Papercup sections\nDate: 2026-09-06\nOwner ruling from session_turn:codex:01a07464-6460-7621-988f-a61cfe951f70:34: the portal Settings page must not prepend a separate portal-only card. The portal theme control belongs inside the canonical Personalization section, and the portal's default Ask Papercup agent control belongs inside the canonical Papercup agent section with the other Papercup settings. Compose both through a typed optional host-capability/extension seam so the shared settings routes remain one tree and desktop/non-portal runtimes omit unavailable portal controls cleanly. Each control and each theme preference has one visible instance and one state owner. This supersedes D-009 only where it placed PortalSettingsCard above SettingsLayout; D-009's parity, persistence, and native-settings goals remain binding.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-06 source read found portal/packages/ui/src/shell.tsx AppSurface renders PortalSettingsCard before EmbeddedPane and that card owns ThemeSwitcher plus AgentSettingsSurface; papercusp/apps/operator/app/settings/personalization/page.tsx already owns the Theme section, while papercusp/apps/operator/app/settings/operator/page.tsx and settings/layout.tsx own the Papercup agent section/navigation. design-phase.search_registry returned control.theme/ThemeSwitcher; the P-109 UI IR passed design-phase.validate_spec and design-phase.lint_spec with zero issues.\nRelated: P-105, P-106, P-107, P-109\n\n### D-061 — Keep the original desktop app available beside the portal-wrapped Tauri app until measured cutover\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDate: 2026-09-06\nOwner direction: session_turn:codex:01a07742-4316-7e83-8cf7-30d541f4e2a4:30 requires maintaining the original desktop app so it remains usable while the portal-wrapped Tauri app is proven.\n\nMeasured: papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json currently defines the original `Papercusp GUI` identity `com.papercusp.gui`. The existing `nightly` channel already proves the reusable side-by-side mechanism: `tauri.nightly.conf.json` gives it a distinct product name and `com.papercusp.gui.nightly` identity; `bin/release.config.ts`, `bin/lib/gen-latest-manifest.sh`, and `test/nightly-channel-identity.test.js` couple the identity overlay to a distinct channel data home and updater feed, refuse identity/stamp drift, and require Debian coexistence without conflicts or replacement.\n\nDecision:\n1. The current original desktop app remains the stable/classic application during this migration. Its bundle id, executable/product identity, data home, updater root, release artifacts, and working local/offline behavior must not be replaced by the portal-wrapped build. It continues receiving critical compatibility/security fixes and its existing release/tests remain maintained.\n2. The portal-wrapped Tauri app ships first as a separate side-by-side preview channel by extending the existing desktop channel registry and identity-overlay machinery. It receives its own visible product name/icon, bundle identifier, executable/package identity, data home, updater feed, release manifest, and install records. The intended channel id is `portal` unless a code-truth constraint requires another single-segment id; do not hand-roll a parallel release system.\n3. Both applications reuse the existing native Rust/sidecar services and typed capability adapters where compatible, but their UI entrypoints, persisted app state, updater feeds, and install identities remain isolated. Shared backend code is not permission to point both running apps at one mutable UI state directory. Any data import from classic to portal preview is explicit, copy-based, versioned, reversible, and never deletes or upgrades the classic source in place.\n4. Shipping this plan means the portal-wrapped preview is installable and verified alongside the still-usable original desktop app. It does not authorize overwriting, uninstalling, auto-migrating, or redirecting the original app. A later cutover requires a new explicit decision based on measured parity, co-install and upgrade tests, local/offline and native-capability coverage, sustained dogfood/soak evidence, rollback, and recovery from the classic app.\n5. P-107 acceptance must exercise both apps installed together: distinct OS identities/icons/processes/data homes/updater feeds; original-app smoke remains green; preview uses the shared portal UI plus native adapters; neither launch/update corrupts or captures the other; rollback leaves classic usable. P-015 final audit/rubric/grade must treat coexistence and no-replacement as ship requirements.\nRelated: P-105, P-106, P-107, P-109\nRelated: P-105, P-106, P-107, P-109\n\n### D-062 — Avi selects visual desktop concept B for the portal\nDate: 2026-09-07\n[turn:self] Avi selected the desktop mockup: 'For the desktop mockups lets go with option B'. The accepted visual reference is scratchpad/visual-desktop-mockups-2026-09-07/b-workspace.png, with the B workspace and empty/disconnected states in the existing index.html/ui-ir.json. Implement the large selected desktop viewer with a compact desktop roster and activity alongside it, explicit Watch/Take control, release/Escape, fullscreen and responsive empty/error/connection states. Use real existing desktop-session/agent state; illustrative mockup names, screenshots and activity are not production data.\n\nReuse HostedDesktopViewer, OperateStage/DesktopSurface, HostedWorkspaceSession and the registered UI components/portal semantic tokens. This authorizes the B integration in the existing portal desktop surface under WI-2001281/P-031; it does not authorize a separate gallery/dock design or change the cloud/desktop credential protocol. Source-level implementation and focused verification may progress while the separately approved G5 initialization runs. P-031 still requires actual remote/browser/Tauri acceptance and cannot close from a static screenshot. P-105/P-107 later consume the selected design and its runtime evidence.\nRelated: P-031, P-105, P-107\n\n### D-063 — Reuse exact cross-feature GCP bootstrap receipts without treating them as hosted/native parity\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[turn:self] Leader audit coord-send-c1e89bafd34c1ea30b26f6e57ef91f0ad8546f8c315a621d312c39e69c2ad4ab directs P-031 to reuse cross-feature GCP lifecycle evidence and add Tauri/private-Git legs. Measured: current WI-40472 is dropped under D-338, so the September saved R7 READY window is stale. Read retained /mnt/backup/cloud-e2e-workspace-host-20261010r5/provider-acceptance files: clean-room-report.json SHA256938fdc006543fe9db699fd21c17fa04f68f84519bae661ee96de3f80bd013538; cli-exit-receipt.json1927b06f31148b79634fdb088ae3b2e9d7511771d7c60a61d05ea6c3b44c5c01 (passed=true); original-task-ledger-authoritative-receipt.json8ea0a8a4c4ba37611e8b702aef7dd43be41906543c8eb005aec69455785b6c9b; iap-rule-cleanup.jsonc47bbf663b28e2582fa0478e7f7a7fa75cd70e78ff84d5d3ad711e9feb88f8cf; post-run-eight-kind-census.json5952b3e312b4b6a092bff4d543b8754356915248251013369ec45d967f049b1a (verdict=PASS). Predecessor coord-send-1f4b85321e1fe8f1ea56f6f8c6695087f2fc5a0573962f29b9f3edd04ba25a3a reports agentRuntimesInstalled=false and agentRuntimesVerified=false. Reuse these exact bootstrap/teardown receipts in P-031/P-015, preserve their frozen source/artifact scope, and do not promote them to current hosted/agent/Tauri/Git acceptance. Current hosted target and auth-state remain to be recovered with the cross-feature owner. Exclude double-fixture-receipt.json from provider proof (providerRun:false). No requirement waived, no duplicate lifecycle spend authorized by this bookkeeping decision.\nRelated: P-031, P-015\n\n### D-064 — Owner: run the real GCP portal/Tauri E2E on avi-test with the saved GitHub token\nDate: 2026-10-20\nQuestion asked: how should agents do the real GCP end-to-end run that portal P-031 (+P-105/106/107/109/110/P-015) and carrier P-001/P-002 wait on? Owner chose verbatim: \"Use avi-test (Recommended)\" — option text: \"Agents run it on the existing avi-test hosted workspace, using the GitHub token already saved in Papercusp. If a browser sign-in is needed, they send you one link. Real GCP VM costs apply for the length of the run.\" This answers the human blocker cloud-e2e:existing-host-git-source-scope-choices on WI-10007610: target = existing avi-test hosted workspace; Git route = GitHub token already saved in Papercusp; scope = still wanted. Dialog answers are not indexed by sessions:search (EI-13472), so this Decision is the durable record.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"voice-public-release-acceptance-2026-08-29","title":"Acceptance: voice recovery and current-generation public-release readiness","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-30","owner":"su-09c95811-a8d2-488b-8951-a753ebe89e8a","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: voice recovery and current-generation public-release readiness\nslug: voice-public-release-acceptance-2026-08-29\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-09c95811-a8d2-488b-8951-a753ebe89e8a\n---\n\n# Acceptance: voice recovery and current-generation public-release readiness\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan voice-recovery-current-generation-readiness-2026-08-27, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality at HEAD 7f603e9541.\n\nWhat the plan set out to do: take local voice from a broken state (EI-21656634210912167 — Whisper ExecStart missing, 63,496+ restart attempts; Kokoro vanishing between checks) to a state where the voice feature set is fit for a PUBLIC RELEASE, under seven recorded Decisions.\n\nThe criteria are outcome criteria, each tracing to the plan goal and to a specific Decision. They deliberately do NOT reward unit-test green on its own: D-004 states plainly that unit tests and health endpoints are necessary but insufficient, and that the verdict must rest on capability-level live endpoint evidence plus current-generation deployment identity.\n\nCRITERION NUMBERING: C1 local-first-capability · C2 single-lifecycle-owner · C3 honest-failure · C4 wake-gate-on-real-stt · C5 generation-green-and-current · C6 conversational-control · C7 residue-dispositioned.\n\n=== RATING SCALE, including the fourth value ===\nfail | partial | pass | not-measured.\n`not-measured` means THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT MEASURE IT — zero evidence was produced, as distinct from evidence of a defect. It NEVER counts as pass, it is NEVER a polite fail, and anything not-measured MUST be carried into C7's residue list by name.\n\nA criterion's stored rating holds ONE value, so a criterion can be PARTIAL or PASS on its falsifiable half while a NAMED SUB-CLAIM inside it was never measured at all. C1 and C3 both have that shape on this host. C7(f) therefore collects BOTH whole criteria rated not-measured AND every individually-named unmeasured sub-claim — see C7(f). Without that, the exact thing the fourth rating was added to make visible would be dropped by the mechanism built to collect it.\n\nThis matters most for the class the repo's own gate-triage rule already governs: a test batch reporting matched=0 or TEST_FILE_ROUTE_ERROR is UNDETERMINED — never red, never green, never 'fixed'. Zero files measured is not a failing measurement.\n\n=== REVISION HISTORY ===\nRev 2 added C6 (conversational-control): the first revision graded provisioning, engines, wake, currency and residue, but nothing graded barge-in, self-echo, or single-session ownership.\n\nRev 3 repaired three blockers from independent vetting: C2 measured the wrong surface (it asserted the legacy unit must be ABSENT and prescribed `systemctl --user list-units`, which does not list a disabled inactive unit at all — the implementer drew exactly that wrong inference, stated publicly that the unit was 'genuinely retired', and retracted it); C3 was unfalsifiable by its own method (its marker forbids silent cloud substitution but its method was two GETs on a health endpoint, which reports declared state and can never observe runtime routing); and C7 was circular (it told the grader to verify residue against a completion record that this grade itself produces).\n\nRev 4 repaired six findings from a second vetting pass, five of them criteria that could not express or reach their own verdicts: the missing `not-measured` rating (load-bearing in C3 and C5); C4 having no FAIL for a MISSED wake; C1's PARTIAL being unreachable and its method having become stricter than its own markers, contradicting C3; C3's egress watch being a SAMPLER, so its 'not contacted' marker could not be falsified by its own instrument; C2 naming a restart-count baseline it never supplied; and C2 stating a call-site fact incorrectly.\n\nRev 5 repairs two findings from a third vetting pass, both in C7, and both of the same family as everything above — a check that cannot fail on the thing it exists to catch:\n(1) C7(a) prescribed 'work_items:get must show them still open'. Both cited rows ARE open, so that check passes whether or not the citation is correct — the criterion could not fail on its own miscitation, because the error would sit in the criterion's DESCRIPTION rather than in the grader's disposition. It now verifies the PROPERTY D-007 actually designates (origin='remote', unassigned, not terminalizable from this node), which is falsifiable.\n(2) C7(f) collected criteria RATED not-measured, but C1 and C3 place not-measured on a HALF while the criterion overall rates partial or pass — so on this host those halves were guaranteed to be dropped by the collector built for them.\n\nThe generalisable lesson, which by rev 5 has now produced an error in EVERY participant — the implementer twice, the first reviewer, and the vetting reviewer — is one shape: a real probe, correctly executed, whose SCOPE was narrower than the conclusion drawn from it. Most recently the vetter read WI-7117 and WI-4470 by TITLE, concluded they were not federation residue, and was wrong: D-007 designates them by the `origin` column, not by subject matter, and both rows do carry origin='remote' with no assignee. The structural defect they found was real even though the premise they found it from was not — which is itself the argument for fixing the check rather than the citation.\n\nThe rubric-level form of the test that has now found eleven defects: for each criterion, ask whether its METHOD can produce every verdict its DRIFT MARKERS describe, and whether it can FAIL if its own stated premises are wrong.\n\nGrader note on scope: this rubric grades whether the VOICE feature set is releasable and whether residue is honestly dispositioned. It does not grade the workspace-wide green-checkpoint gate, a separate shared surface owned by another agent at grading time — but C7 requires that dependency to be stated rather than hidden.\n\nGrader eligibility: anyone who posted on this rubric's vetting thread is disqualified from grading it — scorecards:emit refuses with grader_is_sole_vetting_critic, and it refuses AFTER the grade is complete rather than prechecking, so confirm eligibility before spending the work.\n\nREV 6 (2026-08-30) — INSTRUMENT REPAIR under plan Decision D-008, authored AFTER an independent grade REJECTED this plan. Two defects in the rubric itself: C6 returned a FALSE PASS (it graded WIRING, a structural proxy for a temporal property, and passed a guard that could never fire), and C4 was UNPASSABLE by construction (its marker demanded a system property its method and scope limit excluded). C6's repair is mandatory and stands alone; C4's system-level claim is RELOCATED to C6, where the method now drives the real capture->dispatch path and can fail on the exact line that failed C4. The bar moves STRICTER: post-repair C6 is a test the product FAILED yesterday and passes only because of a fix landed today. Disclosed here per D-008 condition 4 so any later reader prices the edit correctly rather than reading it as housekeeping.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"workflow-popup-searchable-targets-2026-08-30-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: New Workflow popup searchable plans and truthful trigger targets","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-30","owner":"su-bd63a6bc-9628-4cb2-8fca-7226fc59e3a7","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: New Workflow popup searchable plans and truthful trigger targets\nslug: workflow-popup-searchable-targets-2026-08-30-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-30\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-bd63a6bc-9628-4cb2-8fca-7226fc59e3a7\n---\n\n# Acceptance: New Workflow popup searchable plans and truthful trigger targets\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nREVISION 3, incorporating a second independent vetting critique — su-a961ddec on consult conv-mth52g5f, 2026-08-31T11:39:42Z, verdict REVISE-THEN-ATTEST — plus that critic's own same-hour CORRECTION (11:45Z) after su-69bd68f9 re-derived their measurement and found it overstated. Revision 2's history is preserved below.\n\nWHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 3. Two load-bearing edits, both to the RUBRIC'S BINDINGS. No test file is touched.\n\n(1) `silent-return-to-zero-is-detectable` was VACUOUS AS BOUND, and the vetting spot-check did not close it. The criterion bound exactly two assertions — the L119 pre-fix control and the L125 calibration — and BOTH are self-contained local replicas whose subject is the test file, not `acceptance-grader-select.ts`. Measured consequence: revert the shipped D-001 fix (put `assignee` back into computeGraderExclusions) and both stay GREEN, so the criterion rated PASS with the defect fully reintroduced. The control was asserting a property of Postgres plus a fixture — \"a table without column X rejects a SELECT of X\" — which is true forever, independent of the fix. This revision ties the criterion to the real subject by making line 137 its REQUIRED calibration, so the graded pair is {mutant fails, REAL SHIPPED subject passes}. That is the repo's own stated falsifiability discipline for an imported module: a deliberately-wrong control PLUS a calibration the real subject must pass.\n\nSEVERITY, CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. The first critique said a revert reddens only line 137. It reddens FOUR assertions — every one that invokes the real subject throws on the bad column. su-69bd68f9 caught this by re-deriving the claim instead of taking it on trust while holding their grading card. So: the SUITE is not blind to a revert and the shipped P-005 guard is doing its job. What was decorative is this criterion's BINDING — the rubric pointed it at the only two assertions in the file that cannot fail. That is a defect in the rubric, repaired here; it is NOT a defect in the code, and the integration test is deliberately left alone. Deriving the mutant from the shipped query instead of hand-copying it remains worthwhile HARDENING (it removes a replica that can silently drift out of sync) but is optional, is not a repair, and is filed as a separate follow-up rather than folded into this revision.\n\nDISCLOSED CONSEQUENCE FOR `non-overlapping`, stated rather than hidden by the file split. With L137 as crit 5's required calibration, crit 3 and crit 5 now SHARE a deciding assertion. They do not share a question: crit 3 grades whether the happy path yields a usable NON-EMPTY implementer set; crit 5 grades whether the guard PAIR is falsifiable — mutant red, real subject green. Before this edit they were non-overlapping only because crit 5 could not go red from anything except an edit to itself, which is co-rating with nothing, not independence. A grader must judge `non-overlapping` against this disclosure, not against the file layout.\n\n(2) `cascade-reaches-a-live-responder` CERTIFIED ITS OWN REFERENCE MEASUREMENT. `Expect >= 1` is satisfied by the very observation the criterion was authored from: a grader \"reproducing\" it could open conv-mth4i7ql — the row already named in the method — and rate pass. That is not re-verification, and n=1 cannot separate \"the mechanism works\" from \"the mechanism fired once while I was watching it.\" The threshold is now MOVING; see the criterion.\n\n(3) INSTRUMENT RUNG, stated because rung 4 by default is what the derived-truth ladder forbids. The two live-database criteria keep instrumentKey 'none', but now SAY WHY: no registered state cell exists over the consult_state cascade count, and a `dev:pg_query` probe is explicitly non-persistable (indirect/meta surfaces are rejected), so a state cell is the actual lever and building it is a follow-up item, not a blocker on this acceptance. Rung 4 WITH a stated reason is legitimate; rung 4 by default is not.\n\nWHAT REVISION 2 ESTABLISHED, retained. Rev 2 incorporated su-2db1b4e6's critique (WI-1713111 comment, 11:35:57Z, DO NOT ATTEST AS WRITTEN). It dropped and SPLIT the original `cascade-executes-for-real`, which read \"a real acceptance-grading round reaches a responder and is recorded\" — satisfied by a round that measures nothing, the exact instrument-that-measured-nothing failure this plan exists to eliminate, reappearing one level up in the plan's own acceptance evidence. That critic measured that \"reached a responder and was recorded\" is FABRICABLE by the consult ledger: 34 consult_state rows in this workspace are closed_answered with a non-null responder_id and wakes_used = 0 (WI-1713046, positive-controlled 34/34 vs 0/46 on genuine rows). It is now two criteria with a non-fabricable predicate: `cascade-reaches-a-live-responder` (earned) and `cascade-completes-a-grading` (NOT earned — blocked by WI-1699998, recorded honestly rather than absorbed by loose wording). Rev 2 also made `role-gate-admits-the-roles-that-exist` require BOTH directions (as worded it was passed by a gate admitting everything unconditionally — the mirror of the bug just fixed); outcome-ified `discovery-completes-against-the-real-schema` (\"valid\" was satisfied by a query merely not throwing, which an empty result also achieves); and made `exclusions-cannot-reach-across-workspaces` NAME its tables, because sibling tables here disagree about which workspace_id they populate — consult_state stores this pot's rows under 'papercusp-workspace' while event_awaits stores every row under 'default', so a workspace-scoped predicate against the wrong table returns a clean, confidence-inspiring zero from a fully-populated table.\n\nRATING SCALE SEMANTICS. `unknown` is NOT a pass — it means the evidence to decide was not obtained, and it is non-passing for the acceptance verdict. `partial` is likewise non-passing. Only `pass` is passing. The implementer owns the passing bar and must state, in the acceptance reasoning, why any non-pass rating is or is not acceptable to ship over.\n\nThe plan's goal has two halves — find why discovery fails, and prove a real cascade round runs. The first is thoroughly met (two stacked defects, both root-caused). The second is carried by the split C1 pair and is honestly contested; see those two criteria.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-plan-dashboard-mission-control-2026-08-31","title":"Acceptance: PlanDashboard direction-A mission-control revamp","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-31","owner":"su-0d840a60-af11-4570-87e3-fbdb70c2e58d","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: PlanDashboard direction-A mission-control revamp\nslug: acceptance-plan-dashboard-mission-control-2026-08-31\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-0d840a60-af11-4570-87e3-fbdb70c2e58d\n---\n\n# Acceptance: PlanDashboard direction-A mission-control revamp\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for the direction-A (mission control) PlanDashboard revamp the owner picked from the 3-direction canvas (D-001): plan substance (Now + grouped items) as the left column, telemetry (working-now, decisions, noise-collapsed activity) as a 400px right rail, segmented progress band in the header. All data from existing reads (plans.get full mode + planActivity.list) — no new resolvers. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for the PUI remote + shared substrate continuation. Two halves are graded: (a) REMOTE PARITY — a pui running against a remote operator is selected, authorized, and installed on the same rails a remote psu is; and (b) SHARED SUBSTRATE — pui consumes psu's canonical sources rather than a forked client-side duplicate. Criteria trace to the plan's goal and to D-001..D-005, not to the diff.\n\nREVISION 4. Corrects a SAFETY DEFECT I introduced in revision 3: that revision's primary method for shared-option-sources-single-source instructed the grader to 'add a SENTINEL value to the canonical registry'. On this shared box (~85 live agents, git-sync committing the whole tree on a short cadence) that is a shared-tree mutation that can be swept into a commit — the exact sweep race the project guide forbids, and which the guide notes a cleanup trap cannot fix. The vetting REASONING behind the sentinel was correct and is retained (a search for a duplicate is never run against a known-duplicated tree, so it has no demonstrated power to fire); only the unsafe prescribed ACTION is replaced, with a hermetic fixture-level control plus structural evidence. Rev 4 changes that one method and this description; the other five criteria are unchanged from rev 3.\n\nVETTED TWICE: su-a961ddec (consult conv-mtgi5khp) and a late second critique from su-3b0568df, incorporated on its merits rather than discarded on the technicality that the consult had closed. Every concrete weakness from both was accepted.\n\nACCEPTANCE BAR, FIXED IN ADVANCE so it cannot be rationalized afterwards: every criterion `pass` EXCEPT install-freshness-residual-honest, which may be `partial` — and only on the D-004-sanctioned ground that the freshness verdict is unproven, never on the ground that the residual was lost. Any `fail` blocks acceptance.\n\nON `unknown` — READ THIS BEFORE ACCEPTING ONE (EI-21924434989535557). The gate cannot distinguish 'unknown because the property is genuinely unestablished' from 'unknown because the grader was DENIED THE INSTRUMENT', and both look identical on a card; the cheap path for an implementer is to wave the second through, which silently converts a rubric's strongest criterion into its weakest. So: an `unknown` the grader could have resolved by reading BLOCKS acceptance. An `unknown` where the grader states the instrument was unavailable or withheld is a GRADER-CAPABILITY GAP, not evidence of the property — it must be recorded as such and re-graded by someone holding the instrument, never silently accepted. Note that acceptance graders auto-launched in role `judge` cannot call dev:pg_query or routines:list, so any criterion needing live re-measurement is ungradeable by that role.\n\nTWO DELIBERATE COLLISIONS WITH THIS RUBRIC'S CLASS — stated because a grader would otherwise resolve them silently:\n1. `pui-loop-prompt-canonical` vs the class's FLAG DEFAULTS ENABLED. D-001 keeps activation SEPARATE: the owned loop ships OFF on purpose. Do NOT mark the class flag criterion broken for that.\n2. `install-freshness-residual-honest` vs the class's LIVE THROUGH THE PIPELINE. The plan's sole deployed-only property is precisely what did not go live. Consistent, not contradictory, under D-004 — say which reading you applied.\n\nGRADING IS PROSPECTIVE. D-056 accepted P-003's ITEM-level code truth on the current build; that is not the plan acceptance verdict. D-058 retracts D-056's closing '6 of 7 shipped' clause — item terminality is not a shipped plan.\n\nAUDIT PROVENANCE: completion audit at auditSeq 4 (auditedSha d70b6e04a5). auditSeq 3 cited five doc comments and format! message strings as kind:'code' under P-001/P-004; the independent grader's spot-check caught it BEFORE any grade, and auditSeq 4 re-cites enforcement and demotes documentation to kind:'doc'. Bound test files verified green and NON-VACUOUS 2026-08-31T00:39Z: executed=6 matched=6 passed, skippedTests=0.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data).
