Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nREVISION 5 — the ships-on-without-a-flag criterion now has a behavioral render binding. Revision 4's grep proved identifier presence but not that the render obeyed chatTurns and carried no structured check. Rev 5 adds a focused close/unmount/reopen test plus a positive-control flags-catalog absence guard. Focused local result: SessionChatModal.test.tsx 150 passed / 0 failed.\n\nDefinition-of-done for chat-popup-turn-rail-2026-08-31, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. Goal: a reader opening a session popup can see what happened in the session without asking, and jump straight to an answer past the tool-chip wall.\n\nREVISION 4 — driven by independent acceptance grading (EI-21986741094464185, grader su-09a15767), which returned 5 healthy / 1 degraded / 1 BROKEN against rev 3. Every finding was accepted after the implementer re-verified it directly rather than on report. Rev 4 makes three repairs:\n\n(a) THE LIVE OVERCLAIM (was BROKEN). Rev 3's own text below, plus D-007, the plan's ## Now and WI-1813289, all said five Tauri boots PROVED three legs. Measured: scripts/verify-turn-rail.sh holds nine numbered assertions at :140-:235 and the run exits 1 at :137 — BEFORE the first one. Assertions executed: 0 of 9. See D-009, which records the retraction and the rule it sets.\n\n(b) A FALSE CLAUSE IN `degrades-not-disappears` (was DEGRADED). Rev 3 asserted the rail 'gives way last'. TURNS_NARROW_MEDIA_QUERY is 1000px, so the real order is Fleet 1400 -> Orders 1180 -> TURNS 1000 -> Activity 860: third of four. The source comment at SessionChatModal.tsx:341 claimed the same wrong thing twenty lines above the constant that falsifies it; the comment is fixed too.\n\n(c) `live-scope-declared-honestly` WAS UNDER-SCOPED, which is how (a) passed rev 3. It audited whether the record named the legs the implementer had CHOSEN to name — never whether that list was COMPLETE against the harness's own assertions. It now requires the record to state the last line reached and the assertions-run count.\n\nREV 4 ALSO CLOSED TWO REAL COVERAGE GAPS the grading found, rather than writing criteria that excuse them. The audit cited SessionChatModal.test.tsx for the P-003 precedence rule and ChatConversation.test.tsx for the P-005 reverse binding; both citations resolved but neither file contained a single reference to its subject. Both rules were pure logic inlined inside components where no test could reach them without mounting the whole popup. Both are now extracted into session-turn-index.ts (resolveFocusPrecedence, pickTopMessageIndex) and directly tested — 13 new cases, 19 -> 32 in that file, 224 -> 237 across the four chat files. Criterion 1 is broadened to cover the property those rules actually serve.\n\nREAD BEFORE GRADING — the live-verification scope, stated per D-009. Five Tauri boots ran and ZERO of the verifier's nine assertions executed; the run died at :137 on a data-availability blocker (no candidate scope had a popup transcript containing user turns, so the rail correctly rendered zero rows and there was never a row to click). Five boots is one failure repeated five times, not five pieces of evidence. What the failure-path diagnostic dump does honestly support: the empty state is correct against a real assistant-only transcript (rolesInPopup {assistant:9}, rows:0) — genuine, live, load-bearing. It also reported railZone:true and density 'rail' at 1280px, which are real DOM readings but BARE PRESENCE/ATTRIBUTE CHECKS; rev 3 cited railZone:true as corroboration of the D-002 sibling invariant and that citation is WITHDRAWN, because presence does not establish siblinghood and this rubric's own method forbids resting that invariant on a bare check. Everything else is jsdom tests plus a mutation-probe-falsifiable CSS SOURCE guard — a substitution, not an equivalent. The gap is P-008 (dropped, with reason) and WI-1813289, whose unverified list is now the complete nine.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"coord-derived-fields-measurement-2026-09-14","title":"Coord derived-fields post-ship measurement (2-week window, P-009 of coord-derived-fields-2026-08-31)","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-31","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Coord derived-fields post-ship measurement (2-week window, P-009 of coord-derived-fields-2026-08-31)\nslug: coord-derived-fields-measurement-2026-09-14\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-08-31\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nMeasure the coord-derived-fields ship (2026-08-31) after its 2-week window and judge by VALUES, not fill (parent D-001: only after this window does a remove-vs-keep question for blockedOn become askable). Three readings:\n\n1. `why` fill rate split authored vs derived — `fieldProvenance.why` marks derivation ('goal-stamp-derived'); machine senders excluded; pre-ship baseline 1,635/2,755 hand-authored sends omitted `why` (parent D-002).\n2. Authored `blockedOn` adoption now that it is rendered/taught/awaitable — pre-ship baseline 67/38,343 sections/14d with zero render sites (parent D-003).\n3. The `coord:computed-provenance-check` aggregate from the scout coord-health lane (parent D-004; `loadCoordProvenanceCheck` in `packages/operator-core/lib/scout/coord-health-lane.ts`).\n\nRecord the reading as a Decision on plan `coord-derived-fields-2026-08-31` and surface it to the owner.\n\n(Deliberate scheduled follow-up of coord-derived-fields-2026-08-31 — the similar_exists match IS the parent; this plan exists so the parent can ship while the measurement fires on its own one-shot schedule.)\n\n## Now\n\nScheduled one-shot for 2026-09-14 (parent P-009). On fire: run the three measurements, judge by values, record + notify.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Measure and judge\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Run the three measurements over the 2-week window (why fill split authored-vs-derived per fieldProvenance; authored blockedOn adoption vs the 67/38,343 D-003 baseline; the coord:computed-provenance-check aggregate). Judge by VALUES not fill; record the verdict as a Decision on plan coord-derived-fields-2026-08-31 and notify the owner.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"delegated-spawn-responder-build-provenance-2026-08-31","title":"Delegated spawn receipts identify the honoring host build and expose honest skew","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-31","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Delegated spawn receipts identify the honoring host build and expose honest skew\nslug: delegated-spawn-responder-build-provenance-2026-08-31\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-08-31\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001, P-002, and P-003 are complete and committed. Current hosts append bounded responder-build markers to delegated-spawn honored/refusal receipts; outcome resolution and p2p:trace expose current/legacy/unknown evidence and same/skew/unknown comparison, with SHA skew explicitly not implying chronology. Focused unit verification passed 34/34; the two-peer federation integration passed 2/2 after updating its first-turn/receipt fixture; scoped TypeScript, formatting, and diff checks are clean.\n\n**Next:** No remaining work on this plan; preserve the committed evidence and use p2p:trace for mixed-version delegated-spawn diagnosis.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-1858859 — Add a bounded responder-build marker derived from getBuildInfo() to every delegated-spawn honored/refusal receipt detail, with a parser and current/legacy/unknown tests. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-1858861 — Compose the responder build marker into the existing delegated-spawn outcome and p2p:trace surfaces; expose same-build, different-build(skew), and unknown without claiming chronology. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-1858862 — Run focused unit/integration/type checks, verify the changed files and mixed-version behavior, update the plan Now block, and complete EI-19330215508907244 with structured evidence. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Background\n\nThe 2026-08-02 incident was caused by a remote rig honoring a delegated spawn with an installed sidecar that predated the detector being tested. `p2p:trace` now receives federated honored/refusal receipts and is the proven cross-machine debugging surface, but those receipts identify the responder account/device—not the code bytes that made the decision.\n\nCurrent code already provides the reusable primitives: `getBuildInfo()` resolves the loaded operator's baked SHA/version; `emitP2pReceipt()` is the one federated response channel; `resolveDelegatedSpawnOutcome()` and `p2p:trace` already compose the requester-side verdict. The plan extends those seams. It does not add a new host registry, updater, or bespoke status reader.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- Every delegated-spawn refusal or honored receipt emitted by a current host MUST carry a bounded, machine-readable responder build marker derived from `getBuildInfo()`.\n- A missing or unknown marker MUST remain explicit legacy/unknown evidence; it MUST NOT render as current or healthy.\n- `p2p:trace` MUST expose the responder build and an honest comparison against the tracing operator: same, different (skew), or unknown. Different SHA is skew, not automatically older/stale because ancestry is not proven.\n- Existing receipt wire/database schemas MUST remain unchanged; the marker rides the existing signed `detail` payload for mixed-version compatibility.\n- Tests MUST cover current, legacy, unknown, same-build, and different-build cases plus the real honor/refusal orchestration paths.\n\n## Design\n\nUse one pure helper in the P2P receipt module to format and parse a versioned marker such as `[responder-build sha=<safe-sha> version=<safe-version>]`. The formatter reads `getBuildInfo()` at emit time, caps values to the existing safe-value policy, and emits `unknown` when the loaded artifact cannot prove its SHA. The parser treats absent, malformed, and unknown markers as an explicit `unknown` state and preserves the original detail. Delegated-spawn honor/refusal paths append the marker through the existing `emitP2pReceipt` call; `p2p:trace` parses it and compares the responder SHA with the local `getBuildInfo()` SHA. No new DB columns, migrations, network calls, updater, or host-dossier registry are introduced.\n\n## Scope and acceptance\n\n- Every delegated-spawn refusal or honored receipt emitted by a current host carries a bounded, machine-readable responder build marker derived from `getBuildInfo()`.\n- A missing/unknown marker remains explicit legacy/unknown evidence; it never renders as current.\n- `p2p:trace` exposes the responder build and an honest comparison against the tracing operator: same, different, or unknown. A different SHA is called skew, not automatically older/stale because ancestry is not proven.\n- Existing receipt wire/database schemas remain unchanged; the marker rides the existing signed `detail` payload for mixed-version compatibility.\n- Tests cover current, legacy, unknown, same-build, and different-build cases plus the real honor/refusal orchestration paths.\n\n## Exclusions\n\n- Do not reopen shipped plan `learning-pot-scope-gate-2026-08-30`.\n- Do not adopt `unified-web-portal-2026-08-29` or WI-1659159.\n- Do not create a second host-dossier/update system. Server update manifests, pollers, external hand-placed-install staleness checks, `/api/desktop/version`, and sidecar provenance already cover those separate layers.\n- Do not claim that SHA inequality proves chronological staleness without an ancestry/time measurement.\n\n## Phase 1 — Receipt contract\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add a bounded responder-build marker derived from getBuildInfo() to every delegated-spawn honored/refusal receipt detail, with a parser and current/legacy/unknown tests. — note: ← WI-1858859 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Compose the responder build marker into the existing delegated-spawn outcome and p2p:trace surfaces; expose same-build, different-build(skew), and unknown without claiming chronology. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-1858861 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Run focused unit/integration/type checks, verify the changed files and mixed-version behavior, update the plan Now block, and complete EI-19330215508907244 with structured evidence. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-1858862 completed (done)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"deterministic-plan-state-derivation-2026-08-31","title":"Deterministic plan-state derivation — close the plan-drift gaps","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-08-31","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Deterministic plan-state derivation — close the plan-drift gaps\nslug: deterministic-plan-state-derivation-2026-08-31\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-08-31\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** All six plan items are complete: blocker reflection, read-time Now-pointer derivation, lifecycle/freshness derivation, the authorial drain transition, the bounded historical sweep, and the acceptance re-measurement. Activation audit #1 and completion audit #2 are recorded with resolved source/code citations.\n\nCurrent acceptance readings are explicitly time-scoped because the live corpus continues to change: the original Background cohorts are 45→42 for blocked linked items still reading todo, 98→76 for raw terminal next-pointer references, and 196→134 for active/ready plans whose item graphs are fully terminal. The sweep remains intentionally capped and convergent; its residue is not claimed fixed.\n\nThe plan is ready, not shipped. Shipping remains a separate gate requiring a plan-specific acceptance rubric and independent grading; no shipped status is asserted.\n\n**Next:** Author the plan-specific acceptance rubric and obtain independent grading before any shipment decision; keep the sweep running under its bounded cadence.\n\n## Background\n\nOwner question [owner:aviyn 2026-08-31]: \"Our plans seem to be drifting from the current state a lot, is there any way we can increase the amount that plans get automatically updated deterministically by the system as our state changes?\"\n\nFollow-up [owner:aviyn 2026-08-31]: \"Should we use our rules engine for this?\" — answered per-track below; the engine is a PURE matcher (sync `when`/`args`, no I/O), which is what decides where a rule fits and where an action is required.\n\n### What is already deterministic (do NOT rebuild)\n\nThe plan-item <-> work-item axis is well covered and must be left alone:\n\n- `effectiveStatus` is derived from the blocked-by graph, never stored (`@papercusp/plan-parser`).\n- `reflect-rules.ts` mirrors work-item lifecycle ONTO the plan item by firing the real `plans:set-status` (gets the plan lock, revision capture, plan-event emit for free).\n- `reconcile-linked-work-items.ts` is the reverse mirror for plan-item -> work-item.\n- `lane-sync-rule.ts` re-syncs the lane inline off `plans:set-item-blocked-by`.\n- `plan-item-orphan-reconcile` sweeps every 15 min as the backstop.\n\n### Measured drift (papercusp harness, active/ready, non-archived, non-rubric)\n\n| class | count |\n|---|---|\n| active plans | 404 |\n| plan `active` with EVERY item terminal | 196 |\n| `## Now` next-pointer naming an already-terminal item | 98 |\n| plan row untouched > 7d / > 30d | 323 / 214 |\n| linked plan-item/work-item pairs | 553 |\n| blocked work-items linked to an active-plan item | 65 |\n| ...carrying a real external blocker | 64 |\n| ...whose plan item still reads `todo` | 45 |\n\n### A hypothesis that was TESTED AND FALSIFIED — do not retry it\n\nInitial theory: the production `plans:start` -> promote.ts path writes no `payload.plan_item` stamp (only the `source_plan_slug`/`source_plan_item_ids` columns), so `reflect-rules.ts` — which resolves ONLY the payload stamp via `stampOf()` — silently never fires for plan-started items.\n\nFalsified by measurement: 552 of 553 linked pairs DO carry the payload stamp, and only 12 (2.2%) are work-item-done-with-item-not-done. The completion-reflection direction is ~98% clean and needs no new mechanism. `reflect-rules.ts` resolving only the payload stamp remains a latent fragility worth noting, but it is NOT the live drift source.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Blocker reflection must ship BOTH directions; the clear direction needs a new attribution guard\nDate: 2026-08-31\nFINDING (2026-08-31, while implementing P-001).\n\nMeasured: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/set-status.ts:123-128` — `onlyIfNotBlocked` is described as 'SKIP an item already `blocked`/`needs-human` instead of weakening its explicit gate (reported `skipped:\"blocked_guard\"`, ok:true)'.\nMeasured: `packages/operator-core/lib/plan-items/reflect-rules.ts:115` `setStatusArgs()` sets `onlyIfNotBlocked: true` at line 128 — unconditionally, for every reflection that uses it.\nMeasured: `reflect-rules.ts:183` rule `plan-item-reflect:set-state` fires `plans:set-status` with those same args; `reflectedStatus('open')` returns `todo`.\n\nCONSEQUENCE, pre-existing: a work-item going `blocked` -> `open` maps to plan status `todo`, fires, and is then silently skipped because the plan item is blocked. A plan item parked BY reflection can never be un-parked BY reflection. The skip reports ok:true, so nothing surfaces it.\n\nMeasured: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/set_blocker.ts:266` parks via internal `setWorkItemStateWithAliasInfo(input.id, strictHumanAsk ? 'needs-human' : 'blocked', ...)` and `:275` un-parks via `setWorkItemStateWithAliasInfo(input.id, 'open', ...)` — both bypass the `work_items:set_state` TOOL, so neither emits the tool-invocation event the reaction engine matches. This is why no reflection fires in either direction today.\n\nMeasured (SQL, papercusp workspace/harness, active+ready non-archived non-rubric plans): 65 blocked work-items linked to a plan item; 64 carry a non-null `payload->'externalBlockers'`; 17 have plan item `blocked`, 2 `needs-human`, 45 `todo`.\n\nWHY THIS GOVERNS P-001: shipping only the blocker-SET direction would park ~45 more plan items with no automatic route back to `todo`, worsening the drift this plan exists to reduce. The CLEAR direction is load-bearing, not a nicety.\n\nTHE FORK. A correct clear must distinguish a block THIS reflection set from a block set for another reason (a deliberate gate recorded on the plan, or a sibling work-item still blocked). Passing `onlyIfNotBlocked: false` unconditionally would let one work-item's blocker clearing wipe such a gate.\n\nOPTIONS:\n  (a) ATTRIBUTED CLEAR (recommended) — add a set-status guard that clears only when the plan item's current block is attributable to this reflection AND no OTHER linked work-item is still blocked/needs-human. Conservative: an unattributable block stays put, with the existing claim-time contradiction hint and the periodic sweep as backstop. Cost: one new guard in set-status.ts.\n  (b) UNCONDITIONAL CLEAR — pass `onlyIfNotBlocked: false` on the clear direction. Simplest, but an automated cascade can clear a deliberately-set plan gate. Not recommended.\n  (c) SET-ONLY — ship only the blocked direction. Rejected: strictly worsens the measured problem, per the paragraph above.\n\nAlso in scope of (a): the pre-existing `set-state` asymmetry is the same bug reached by a different event, and should be fixed by the same guard.\n\nSTATUS: implementation paused pending a choice among (a)/(b)/(c). Nothing has been written to `reflect-rules.ts`.\n\n### D-002 — Use the rules engine for reflection and transition; use read-time derivation for stored-copy drift\nDate: 2026-08-31\nOwner question [turn 2026-08-31]: whether the rules engine should be used for this work. Ruling, per track, with the engine's actual contract as the deciding constraint.\n\nMeasured: `libs/generic/rules/src/types.ts` module docstring — 'The engine is a PURE matcher: it decides WHAT should fire and returns it; the consumer FIRES it. (rules-engine D-002: dispatch/durability/loop-protection are the consumer's concern.)'\nMeasured: same file — `Predicate<E> = (event: E) => boolean` and `ArgsTemplate<E> = Record<string, unknown> | ((event: E) => Record<string, unknown>)`. Both SYNC: no I/O is possible in `when` or `args`.\nMeasured: `packages/operator-core/lib/events/registry.ts:101` — `matchReactions` is documented '(pure)'.\nMeasured: `packages/operator-core/lib/plan-items/reflect-rules.ts` module header — 'the rules matcher is pure/sync — no I/O — which is exactly why convert stamps the payload in addition to the `implements` edge'.\n\nRULING BY TRACK:\n\nP-001 (blocker reflection) — YES, the rules engine, and it is the natural home. `reflect-rules.ts` is already a rules-engine module and this is a fourth rule beside its three. Measured: `work_items/set_blocker.ts:317-324` returns `{ ok, id, changed, workItem, activeBlockers, ... }` post-transition, so the pure/sync matcher has the stamp and the direction without I/O. This also follows the architecture note in `lane-sync-rule.ts`: a reaction hangs off the TRIGGER TOOL, never a hardcoded call inside the tool's implementation, so the whole plan-item <-> work-item lifecycle stays ONE mechanism inspectable in `events:graph`.\n\nP-002 (`## Now` pointer) — NO. A rule would react to change by firing a WRITE that refreshes a stored copy. That is rung 3 of the derived-truth ladder (ATTEST/reconcile a second copy) when rung 1 (DERIVE) is available. The pointer has no reason to be stored: computed at read time from the item graph it cannot drift, has no window in which it is wrong, and has nothing to fail. Using the engine here would build a reconciler for a copy we should instead delete. Per CLAUDE.md's ladder: take the FIRST rung that fits.\n\nP-003 / P-004 (plan lifecycle) — SPLIT. The VERDICT ('is every item terminal') is read-time derivation, same argument as P-002. The TRANSITION ('stop sitting active') is the rules engine, because a real trigger event exists: `plans:set-status` making the last item terminal. But the matcher cannot ask 'was that the last non-terminal item?' — that is I/O — so the rule must fire an ACTION that does the read and decides, which is exactly the shape `plan-items/reconcile-rule.ts` already uses.\n\nP-005 (sweep) — NOT the rules engine, and this is the general limit worth stating: a reaction rule only ever fixes the FUTURE. It fires on an event, so pre-existing drift (the measured 196 plans, 98 pointers, 45 items) is invisible to it. Every reflection mechanism here is therefore PAIRED with a periodic sweep as backstop — `lane-sync-rule` with `plan-item-orphan-reconcile`, and P-004 with P-005. Treat rule-plus-sweep as the unit, not the rule alone.\n\nGENERAL RULE for future work on this plan: use the rules engine when a real state CHANGE must propagate as a side effect and a trigger tool event exists to hang it on. Use read-time derivation when the problem is that a value is stored at all. Reaching for a rule to keep a redundant copy fresh is the smell.\n\n### D-003 — The derived next-pointer supersedes stored prose only when EVERY plan item that prose names is terminal\nDate: 2026-08-31\nBinding on P-002 (the read-time derivation) and on P-005 (the sweep backstop), which must not rewrite what the read layer deliberately preserves.\n\nTHE RULE. At read time the item graph is the authority on *which item is next*, but it is NOT the authority on the author's `next:` prose in general. The derived pointer replaces the stored one when, and only when, **every plan item the stored prose names is already terminal** — i.e. it directs the reader at nothing live. Five dispositions fall out, and all five are reported:\n\n- `superseded` — every named item terminal; derived pointer leads, stored line kept verbatim beneath it (prepend-only, like terminal-now-stamp).\n- `ratified` — at least one named item is live; stored prose passes through UNCHANGED.\n- `unverifiable` — the prose names no item of this plan; the graph has no jurisdiction (e.g. \"run the acceptance grading, then ship\" on a drained plan).\n- `filled` — there was no stored pointer; the derived one fills the gap.\n- `abstained` — the plan has no items; the graph is silent. Explicitly NOT the same as `drained`.\n\nWHY NOT SIMPLY ALWAYS RETURN THE DERIVED POINTER. It destroys information a derivation cannot invent. \"P-001 first: it is the smallest change and the highest-value\" carries RATIONALE; the graph can produce the id and never the reason. An author may also deliberately pick a lower-ranked live item, which the graph cannot call wrong.\n\nWHY NOT THE OPPOSITE WIDENING (\"any named item is terminal\"). It would catch more, and destroy far more: \"P-001 landed; pick up P-002\" is the most common shape a Now block takes, and it names a terminal item by design.\n\nMeasured: `npx tsx` running `reconcileNowNext` over all 1,499 papercusp `harness_plans` rows with a structured item list (dumped from `harness_shared.harness_plans`, 2026-08-31): superseded 208 (89 on plans whose status is still live) · ratified 107 · unverifiable 587 · filled 97 · abstained 500. Two safety invariants held at exactly 0 across all 1,499: the derived pointer never named a terminal item, and no stored text was ever dropped from the returned value.\n\nTHE RESIDUAL, AND HOW IT IS HANDLED. The universal rule leaves one gap, found by running the code over the corpus rather than by reasoning about it: a pointer whose DIRECTIVE is stale but which also mentions a live item survives as `ratified` — measured on `silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01` (\"Start P-015 …\" where P-015 had shipped). That is handled by APPENDING a caution, never by replacing, using the existing write-time classifier `detectNowItemContradictions`, which already separates \"start P-015\" from \"P-015 landed\". It fires on 22 of 1,499 rows (1.5%). Append-only means a false positive costs a line of prose and never a real instruction.\n\nFOR P-005. The sweep may rewrite the stored bytes ONLY for the `superseded` population. `ratified`, `unverifiable` and `abstained` prose is off limits — a sweep that \"fixes\" those would destroy exactly the curated rationale this decision exists to protect. `filled` is a judgement call the sweep should leave to a human or to the read layer, since writing a derived pointer into the file re-creates the stored copy P-002 exists to remove.\nRelated: P-002, P-005\n\n### D-004 — The lifecycle overlay reports, never repairs — and freshness reports only signals with a real writer\nDate: 2026-08-31\nBinding on P-004, P-005, P-006 and any surface rendering the derived `lifecycle` field.\n\n**1. The derivation REPORTS; it never rewrites `status`.** `plans:get` returns `lifecycle` beside `status`, never instead of it, and `lifecycle.disposition` says whether they agree. Same discipline as D-003 one level up: replacing a hand-written label would destroy authorial intent (a plan deliberately parked in `draft`), and the evidence does not support that authority.\n\n**2. The graph contradicts the label in exactly TWO cases.** (a) `draft`/`ready`/`active` over a graph whose every item is terminal — the headline drift class. (b) `shipped` over a graph with live items — the ship gate refuses live items, so this means the graph moved after the ship, or the gate was forced past. `superseded` is NEVER contradicted: it means deliberate abandonment mid-flight, so live items are its correct shape, and flagging them would manufacture drift out of the one status whose whole meaning is \"we stopped\".\n\n**3. A drained graph is NOT a finished plan, and the contradiction text says so out loud.** All-items-terminal is evidence about IMPLEMENTATION only. Shipping needs a code-truth audit and independent grading that no item status can evidence, so the verdict tops out at `implementation-complete` / `awaiting-acceptance` and there is deliberately NO `accepted` verdict. P-004 inherits this: it may move a drained plan toward awaiting-acceptance and must NEVER auto-`shipped`.\n\n**4. An itemless plan ABSTAINS.** A derivation reading \"no live items\" as \"finished\" would declare every itemless plan complete on its first run. `no-items` and `abstained` are distinct values for exactly this reason.\n\n**5. A drained plan is never `stalled`, however cold.** \"Finished and untouched\" is not \"unfinished and abandoned\"; reporting the first as the second sends a reader to restart work already done.\n\n**6. FRESHNESS REPORTS ONLY SIGNALS WITH A REAL WRITER.** P-003 asked for three activity signals; only two exist. `harness_shared.plan_items.updated_at` looks exactly like a per-item transition stamp and is not one — the index is rebuilt by DELETE+INSERT on every plan write, so every row of a plan carries the plan's write time. Publishing it as `lastItemTransitionAt` would emit one timestamp twice under two names, the second promising a granularity nothing measures: the very defect class this plan exists to remove. No per-item transition history exists (`plan_revisions` stores content snapshots, not item edges). Item transitions are therefore covered IMPLICITLY by the plan write they cause; `sources` names each measured signal; an unreadable signal reports as `unmeasured`, never defaulted. **A future agent wanting per-item transition times must ADD a real writer, not re-point at this column.**\n\n**7. Refined drift measurement, superseding P-005's approximate figure.** P-005 cites \"the 196 already-drifted plans\". Precisely defined — non-archived, status draft/ready/active, every structured item terminal — the real figure is **227 live plans**. P-005/P-006 should use 227 as the baseline and can re-run the same module for acceptance evidence.\n\n---\n\n**Measured (2026-08-31):**\n- `plans/plan-index-rows.ts:92,108` — `DELETE FROM harness_shared.plan_items` then `INSERT INTO`, matching its own header. Confirmed live: grouping `harness_plans` joined to `plan_items` gives `min(i.updated_at) = max(i.updated_at) = p.updated_at` on every row returned.\n- `harness_plans.updated_at` checked for the bulk-touch failure mode before being trusted: 1,572 papercusp plans spread 0–103 days, 810 older than 30 days, no single day above 87 rows — it tracks real writes, not a sweep.\n- Behavioural run of the shipped modules over all **1,483** papercusp plans with an item array (`/tmp/p003-corpus-run.mjs`): verdicts implementation-complete 716 / no-items 487 / active 157 / stalled 106 / awaiting-acceptance 17; dispositions agreed 749 / abstained 487 / contradicted 247, of which **227 on still-live plans** (point 7). 487 itemless plans (33%) abstained (point 4). 757 plans are ≥30 days idle but only 106 are `stalled` (point 5). Five safety invariants all **0**: stalled-on-drained, itemless-judged, superseded-contradicted, live-contradicted-with-live-items, negative-idle.\n- The acceptance lookup index-scans ONLY because of the redundant-looking `NULLIF(template_data->>'subjectPlan','') IS NOT NULL` conjunct, which lets Postgres prove the query implies the partial unique index predicate. `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` without it: Seq Scan, 726 buffers, 6.07ms — on EVERY plan read. With it: Index Scan, 8 buffers, 0.12ms. Pinned by a source-text test.\n- End-to-end on staging `:3170`: `plans:get` returns `lifecycle` for this plan (verdict `active`, `agreed`) and, for `outage-must-not-be-silent-2026-08-02`, `status: active` → verdict `implementation-complete`, disposition `contradicted` (10 done, 1 dropped, idle 28d).\n\n### D-005 — P-004 adds `awaiting-acceptance` to the stored vocabulary, and writes it only on the authorial act that drains the graph\nDate: 2026-08-31\nDate: 2026-08-31\nBinding on P-004 and P-005. Resolves the apparent conflict between D-004 point 1 (\"the derivation REPORTS; it never rewrites `status`\") and D-004 point 3 (\"P-004 may move a drained plan toward awaiting-acceptance\").\n\n**1. The two are not in conflict, because they are different authorities.** D-004 point 1 governs the READ-TIME OVERLAY: `plans:get` renders a verdict for a plan nobody asked to change, so relabelling there would silently rewrite 227 historical plans on a mere read, and its warrant is only \"I derived something\". P-004 is a WRITE fired by an author's own `plans:set-status` call — the act that MAKES the graph drained. The warrant is the author's edit, not the derivation, and the write is confined to the plan they just edited. A read must not repair; a write triggered by the repairing act may.\n\n**2. The state had to be added; it did not exist.** There was no value meaning \"implementation landed, acceptance not yet done\". P-004's own text names \"the awaiting-acceptance state\", so creating it is inside P-004, not scope creep.\n\n**3. Why not reuse the existing operational axis.** Reuse-first required checking `op_status` (started/paused/done) first, and it does not fit: `clearStartedForTerminalPlan` already writes `op_status='done'` to mean LIFECYCLE-TERMINAL, and `reconcileStartStatus` heals toward it on that premise; reusing it for \"drained but not shipped\" puts two meanings in one column — the defect class this plan removes. It is also insufficient alone: `bucketOf` tests `startStatus` BEFORE `status`, so clearing op_status files a drained plan under **Ready**, which reads as *not started yet* — a different false statement, not a fix.\n\n**4. WHY A STORED COPY IS ADMISSIBLE HERE, when this plan exists to delete stored copies.** The test is not \"is it derived?\" but \"can the stored value contradict the graph without anyone noticing?\". `active` vs `awaiting-acceptance` encodes EXACTLY ONE graph fact — is any item non-terminal — so the mapping is total and invertible from the graph, and P-003's reconciler reports any divergence on every read. `draft` is the opposite: its difference from `ready` encodes authorial intent the graph cannot see, which is why a rule may never write or overwrite it. That asymmetry, not the mere fact of being stored, is what makes one safe and the other not.\n\n**5. The rule is symmetric, and classifies from scratch.** Following `lane-sync-rule.ts`'s construction rather than special-casing a direction: drained && stored in {ready, active} -> `awaiting-acceptance`; not-drained && stored = `awaiting-acceptance` -> `ready`. Reopening an item therefore un-does the transition, so the rule cannot strand a plan in a state its own graph refutes.\n\n**6. Four statuses are deliberately untouched.** `draft` (authorial intent, point 4) · `shipped` and `superseded` (terminal; moving off them would resurrect a closed plan) · and `awaiting-acceptance` is NEVER auto-advanced to `shipped`, per D-004 point 3 — the ship gate requires a code-truth audit, a vetted rubric and independent grading, and auto-shipping would forge exactly that evidence. The rule can start the acceptance path; it can never conclude it.\n\n**7. `active` is legacy** — accepted as a SOURCE of the transition, never written as a target.\n\n**8. For P-005.** The sweep may move the same two edges on the already-drifted population, under the same exclusions. Kills the 98 stale pointers structurally. importance: high — note: ← WI-1744270 completed (done)\n\n- **P-003** `done` Derive a plan `lifecycle` verdict on every plan read — `active` / `implementation-complete` / `awaiting-acceptance` / `stalled` — computed from item statuses plus the acceptance-gate state, so `status` alone stops being the field readers trust. Read-only: no writes to any plan. Also surface a `freshness` signal (last item transition, last linked work-item transition, last plan write) so a 30-day-cold plan cannot read as live. importance: high — note: Landed as WI-1761223 (completionAuthority: committed). derivePlanLifecycle + reconcilePlanLifecycle in @papercusp/plan-parser, signal gathering in plans/plan-lifecycle-derivation.ts, read-time overlay in plans:get. 148 tests, 4 guards green, whole-corpus run over 1,483 plans with five safety invariants at 0, and end-to-end verification on staging :3170. Jurisdiction recorded as D-004.\n\n## Phase 3 — Act on the derived verdict\n\n- **P-004** `done` Transition plans off `active` once every item is terminal, via the rules engine: a rule on `plans:set-status` fires an ACTION (the matcher is pure/sync and cannot ask \"was that the last non-terminal item?\" — that is I/O) which re-reads the plan and moves it to the awaiting-acceptance state. NEVER auto-`shipped`: the ship gate requires a code-truth audit, a vetted acceptance rubric, and independent grading, and auto-shipping would forge exactly that evidence. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-1814841 completed (done)\n\n- **P-005** `done` Add the periodic sweep backstop for P-004, since a reaction rule only ever fixes the FUTURE — the 196 already-drifted plans need a pass. Mirrors the existing rule-for-immediacy + sweep-for-backstop pairing (`lane-sync-rule` + `plan-item-orphan-reconcile`). Consider registering the already-built, already-tested, currently-UNARMED `unshipped-plans-audit` (absence of a routine row verified with a positive control) as the reporting half rather than writing a new sweep. blocked-by: P-004 importance: medium — note: ← WI-1827049 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Verification\n\n- **P-006** `done` Re-run the drift measurement queries from Background after P-001..P-005 land and record before/after counts as completion evidence. The 45 / 98 / 196 figures are the acceptance signal; each must be driven to a stated number, not asserted as \"fixed\". blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-1835165 completed (done)\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"federation-scope-branding-2026-08-31","title":"Brand federated hive scope so a local slug cannot be passed where canonical shared state is meant","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-31","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Brand federated hive scope so a local slug cannot be passed where canonical shared state is meant\nslug: federation-scope-branding-2026-08-31\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-08-31\n---\n\n## Now\n\nStart at **P-001 (WI-6312)**. It is the keystone: introducing the branded scope type at the `pot_members` write seam is what makes the local-vs-canonical mix-up *unrepresentable* rather than merely audited. Every other item is either blocked by it or becomes mechanical once it lands.\n\nDo NOT start at the umbrella (EI-21949920919847957) and do NOT start with the audit items — an audit before the type exists produces a list that rots while the tree moves under it.\n\n## Background\n\nFederated hive scope is passed as a bare `string`. A **local** pot slug and the **canonical** (owner) hive slug are therefore the same type, so passing one where the other is meant is invisible to the compiler and silent at runtime. The failure mode is not an error — it is an empty result set: a joiner reads its local namespace, finds zero rows, and reports \"no members\" rather than \"wrong scope\". That is why these six items keep being rediscovered separately.\n\nVerified at HEAD on 2026-08-31 (su-996d0712, checkpoint on EI-21949920919847957):\n\n- Branding infrastructure is genuinely **absent**: a repo-wide search for `__brand`, `Brand<`, `Opaque<` returns exactly one hit — `EpochKey` in `sync/hyperbee/hive-epoch-crypto.ts:30`. The premise is accurate and not already-fixed.\n- All six contributing work-items were confirmed still `open` by `work_items:get` — not assumed from the digest.\n\n## Phase 1 — make the mix-up unrepresentable\n\n- **P-001** `todo` WI-6312 — introduce the branded federated-scope type and apply it at the `pot_members` WRITE seam and its single-row readers (`getHiveMember`, `loadHiveMemberDevicePubkeys`, `upsertHiveMember`, `addRevokedHivePubkeys`), which currently take an unbranded string scope. KEYSTONE — land this before anything else. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` WI-6318 — carry the branded type across EVERY `hiveScoped` reader; the defect is not limited to `pot_members`. Includes `pot:report`, which refuses a legitimate joiner on BOTH gates. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` WI-6319 — audit the remaining hive-home-grained readers on NON-tool-arg paths: services, routines, projection helpers, sync-resolver and UI. This sweep only pays off once the type exists. blocked-by: P-002\n\n## Phase 2 — the concrete bugs the type makes impossible\n\n- **P-004** `todo` EI-18778409692069309 — a joiner reads `pot_members`/revocations under its LOCAL slug while projections write under the CANONICAL (owner) slug, so a fed-b node silently sees zero rows. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-005** `todo` WI-6311 — `reconcileOwnedHiveEpochKeys` enumerates `pots.pot_home_slug` (LOCAL) to drive EPOCH-KEY reads that are projected under federated scope. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-006** `todo` WI-6216 — a federated pot harness ingests into TWO different local workspaces on the same node. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 The umbrella is superseded by this plan, not closed on its merits\n\nEI-21949920919847957 is a `system:work-item-admission-daily-digest` aggregate over the six items above. It is retired by pointing at this plan. Its premise is TRUE at HEAD, so it must not be recorded as refuted or superseded-by-a-fix; the honest disposition is that the work is real and now lives here, decomposed and ordered.\n\n### D-002 A digest aggregate is plan-shaped exactly when its members are still open\n\nThe fleet leader initially ruled the opposite and retracted it (coord 2026-08-31T12:14Z). The distinguishing test is step 1 of the digest-triage recipe: read the members' STATE. Members already terminal or superseded means the aggregate is an audit of a stale claim and closes in one sitting. Members still OPEN and describing inter-dependent code work across subsystems means it is plan-shaped and decomposes. Ten aggregates sharing the first outcome do not make it the class.\n\n### D-003 Start at the write seam, not the audit\n\nBranding the write seam first makes the invalid state unrepresentable; auditing first only enumerates instances of a bug the type system will shortly prevent, and that list goes stale as the tree moves under it.\n\n### D-004 Created past the plan dedup guard, deliberately\n\n`plans:new` refused with `similar_exists` naming five overlapping plans. All five were read before forcing. `federation-release-hardening-relaunch-2026-07-01` is the only non-terminal candidate and is finished on its merits — all 13 briefs done, release min-bar met, no open release-critical code blocker; its remaining `Next` is an owner-gated Hetzner billing wall plus a post-release backlog, none of which is a scope-type refactor. `shared-hive-federation-2026-06-08` and `shared-hive-p2p-release-readiness-2026-07-03` are `shipped`; `fleet-federation-reanchor-2026-06-06` and the acceptance plan are `superseded`. Those plans re-keyed federation identity and proved out rigs; none of them introduces a branded scope TYPE, which is this plan's whole subject. Note for whoever revisits this: `search:semantic` does not cover plans, so the refusal above was the only plan-aware dedup that ran.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"gate-speed-round-2-2026-08-31-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: gate speed round 2 — did the gate actually get faster, and is every number honest?","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-31","owner":"su-86df7de5-1f35-42e8-a5fb-621b171313fc","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: gate speed round 2 — did the gate actually get faster, and is every number honest?\nslug: gate-speed-round-2-2026-08-31-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-86df7de5-1f35-42e8-a5fb-621b171313fc\n---\n\n# Acceptance: gate speed round 2 — did the gate actually get faster, and is every number honest?\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hud-plan-card-density-2026-08-31-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — HUD Plans board: compact two-line plan cards","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-31","owner":"su-7e441b25-2bbd-40f5-b241-cbea306cdbcc","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — HUD Plans board: compact two-line plan cards\nslug: hud-plan-card-density-2026-08-31-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-02\nowner: su-7e441b25-2bbd-40f5-b241-cbea306cdbcc\n---\n\n# Acceptance — HUD Plans board: compact two-line plan cards\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nAuthored AFTER implementation against as-built reality, then REVISED against an independent critique (su-08f9a6d0, WI-1743279 comment 79879, findings F1-F7). The plan's goal was one thing: make the HUD Plans board's plan cards dense enough to scan a column of plans instead of three, WITHOUT the board quietly losing information or dragging the other boards along with it. The criteria split along the two ways this fails — failing to deliver the density (1, 5), or delivering it by discarding facts and surfaces nobody agreed to lose (2, 3, 4, 7) — plus one that grades the evidence itself (6), because on this surface the cheapest way to be wrong is to cite an instrument that cannot fail.\n\nWHAT THE CRITIQUE CHANGED, so a grader can see what was conceded rather than argued away. (F5b) Criterion 1 was entirely unbound on the argument that its PIXEL half is unmeasurable in jsdom; the reviewer pointed out its own model names a DOM regression (a row creeping back) that is perfectly visible there and already asserted — so criterion 1 is now bound for that half and prose-only for the pixel half. (F5a) The `instrument` binding kind was never addressed; it is addressed explicitly in criteria 1 and 5 now. (F1) Criterion 3's bar accepted a control over ONE non-plan card kind, which a `card.plan ?? card.goal` widening would have walked straight through; it now requires one case per kind that actually flows through EntityCardBody. (F2) Criterion 2's population was the rubric author's own prose in D-001, and under-enumerated; it is now defined as a CODE DERIVATION the grader performs. (F3/F4/F6) D-002's absent-not-hidden ruling, the card's degraded-data branches, and its greyscale/colour-only encoding had no covering criterion at all — criterion 7 is new and covers them. (F7) Criteria 1, 5 and 6 read the same artifact and could triple-count one defect; the division of labour is now stated in criterion 6.\n\nWHY 1 AND 5 KEEP AN UNBOUND HALF. jsdom has no layout engine: getBoundingClientRect, offsetHeight, scrollWidth and clientWidth are all 0 (the reviewer probed this rather than accepting it, and confirmed getComputedStyle DOES resolve — the cascade works, only layout is absent). A tests binding for a HEIGHT or an OVERFLOW assertion would therefore pass unconditionally, which is worse than no binding because it would read as rigor. No `instrument` binding exists for headless-rig geometry either; if one is ever registered, both criteria should take it. Their instrument is the live rig, named inline in each replication drill.\n\nGrader: you are NOT the implementer. Spot-check the audit's citations (plans:audit seq 2) rather than taking the notes at face value.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hud-session-display-names-2026-08-31-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: HUD session cards carry the terminal title's information, and a human-given name reaches every surface at once","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-31","owner":"su-b2572cce-ba13-46a2-95ca-ece01f722f91","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: HUD session cards carry the terminal title's information, and a human-given name reaches every surface at once\nslug: hud-session-display-names-2026-08-31-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-b2572cce-ba13-46a2-95ca-ece01f722f91\n---\n\n# Acceptance: HUD session cards carry the terminal title's information, and a human-given name reaches every surface at once\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01.
