(Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan hud-session-display-names-2026-08-31, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. The plan's goal was that a HUD session card stop being an opaque short id and instead carry what the OS terminal title already carries, plus let a human name a session once and have that name appear everywhere the session is represented. The criteria below are OUTCOMES, each tracing to the plan's Requirements (R1-R10) and its four owner Decisions; none restates an implementation step.\n\nREVISION NOTE (rev 2): the criterion `identity-added-never-replaced` was widened and renamed to `naming-never-costs-findability` to cover R7. Rev 1 left R7 (the board's search box matches a manual name) with no criterion of its own, so the rubric could not have failed if search had silently stopped matching manual names - a hole in a stated requirement. The independent grader ratified this fix and the reasoning: rendering a name and MATCHING it are separate code paths, so the author's original judgement that R7 was \"subsidiary\" was wrong, while folding it into criterion 2 rather than adding an eighth was right, because R2 and R7 are two halves of one user-facing outcome.\n\nREVISION NOTE (rev 3): STRUCTURED CHECK BINDINGS ADDED. Rev 2 was entirely prose-only across all seven criteria while the plan had in fact shipped a full unit suite - exactly the under-binding the meta-rubric's `prefer-structured-check` (D-006) names. Six criteria now carry check:{kind:'tests'} bound to the files whose assertions actually decide them, so scorecards:emit RUNS those files at grading time and a pass-rating that a failing test contradicts is refused rather than accepted on prose. Each bound criterion's method names the SPECIFIC assertion that would go red for that criterion's own drift marker - path binding alone is not detection binding.\n\nREVISION NOTE (rev 4 - FINAL, wording only): criterion 4's TITLE was literally false about the code and is corrected. It read \"both coord:glance and adv-roster call it\", but adv-roster does NOT call the display-name resolver: it imports and calls `sessionObjective` only (adv-roster.ts:34, :805) and deliberately hands over the LAYERS, with display-name resolution sitting one layer out in hud-board-model.ts (:1464). That layering is not a defect - it is precisely what this criterion's own method REQUIRES, since a consumer handed a pre-resolved string is how a second copy of the chain grows back. The old wording would have sent a future reader grepping adv-roster for sessionDisplayName, finding it absent, and reading a correct design as a regression. Found by the independent grader (su-c44f0e35) during grading and verified against source before the fix. NO criterion's meaning, method, drift markers, or check bindings changed in rev 4 - only that one title string and this note, so the independent scorecard EI-21974551854982626 filed against rev 3 grades the identical substance.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"learning-pot-scope-gate-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — a per-pot learning gate that actually refuses, and controls that do not lie about it","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-31","owner":"su-8c2ebfa6-8e13-4ed1-8d06-7e3fca2f2ced","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — a per-pot learning gate that actually refuses, and controls that do not lie about it\nslug: learning-pot-scope-gate-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-8c2ebfa6-8e13-4ed1-8d06-7e3fca2f2ced\n---\n\n# Acceptance — a per-pot learning gate that actually refuses, and controls that do not lie about it\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for learning-pot-scope-gate-2026-08-30, authored against as-built reality after implementation.\n\nThe plan's goal was NOT \"add a switch to the Learning tab\". It was a REAL per-pot gate — one that refuses work at the engine seams — plus the two surfaces that drive it. So these criteria are written as outcomes about REFUSAL and about TRUTHFULNESS OF CONTROLS, not about widgets existing.\n\nThe recurring failure this plan kept running into, across D-005 through D-011, is one shape: a control that appears to change something it cannot durably change. The chip popover was the only home for per-lane switches, so the rail could not collapse (D-008). The scout ceiling is workspace-wide, so a per-pot switch for it would silently change every pot (D-009). The `blender:<pot>` governor row is rewritten from the pot's budget CONFIG after every scout cycle, so an arm/budget write there is reverted by the next tick (D-011). Three separate instances of the same lie. Criteria 5-7 exist to grade whether the shipped surfaces refuse to tell it.\n\nREVISION 2 — revised after third-party vetting (consult conv-mth0qwa0, critique by su-a961ddec): criterion 6 restated from an ungradeable design principle into a round-trip durability outcome; checks kept BOUND with permanent wrong-implementation controls added rather than unbound; criterion 8 added after confirming no ratified design reference exists for this surface.\n\nREVISION 3 — revised again after INDEPENDENT GRADING (card EI-21960348160674773, su-45497fc3, a non-implementer with no prior history on this work). That grader rated 7 healthy / 1 degraded and found four defects in THIS RUBRIC, not in the implementation. All four are fixed here:\n\n (1) CRITERION 8 CARRIED A FALSE LIVE CLAIM, now struck. I had written that all 28 pots are \"switched off with nothing armed\" and that the rail must therefore render ZERO active chips today. The first half is true; the second is not. I re-measured independently rather than taking the correction on trust: 28 pots are gated off, but SEVEN of them (calendar, email, papercusp, phone-app, portal, stonebrook-android-20260821, thornbury-iphone-20260821) still have an armed lane and therefore still render as ACTIVE chips — the same seven the grader named. Those seven are CORRECT by design: D-008 established that arming a lane on a switched-off pot is meaningful, because it pre-stages what switching the pot back on restores, and learning-pot-rail.test.ts:218 deliberately keeps them. So the code was right and my criterion's premise was wrong: it conflated \"all switched off\" with \"all switched off AND nothing armed\". A future grader following the old method literally would have observed seven chips and graded BROKEN against correct code. The graded bound is now a pure code property, and the live check is stated as a procedure with that trap named.\n\n (2) CRITERION 2 WAS BOUND TO A FILE THAT COULD NOT DETECT ITS OWN DRIFT. It bound only learning-governor/core.test.ts, which asserts the verdict-layer analogue (an unresolved potEnabled PARAMETER) and never the row-to-boolean step — so flipping potScopeEnabled to `row?.enabled === true` would have left it green. packages/operator-core/lib/learning/pot-gate/core.test.ts, which asserts the absent-row property directly, is now bound (verified present, 9/9 green).\n\n (3) CRITERION 3's ONE LOAD-BEARING JOIN WAS ASSERTED NOWHERE. The picker opening the drawer for a chipless pot — the thing that makes P-052's rail collapse legal rather than a silent stranding — had no test at all, so deleting the wiring would have stranded exactly the population P-052 buries with every bound check still green. FIXED AS CODE, not by re-pointing a binding: three assertions added to LearningPotPicker.test.tsx driving the REAL useOpenPotDrawer (never a mock of it) and observing the nuqs `lpot` write, plus a positive control that every listed pot exposes the affordance. LearningPotRail.test.tsx is also now bound here.\n\n (4) CRITERION 6 COULD NOT DETECT A RE-ADDED BUDGET SECTION. Its bound page.test.tsx had zero references to budget / CONFIG_SECTIONS / section. Two assertions added there: a stale `?section=budget` normalizes to scout and the retired editor's placeholder is absent, plus a POSITIVE CONTROL that `?section=` is genuinely read — without which the first passes vacuously on a page that ignores the parameter entirely. (The grader initially proposed binding the live .sh verifier instead, then retracted that itself after measuring TEST_FILE_ROUTE_ERROR — a shell script cannot back a kind:'tests' check.)\n\nGRADER NOTE — I cannot grade this. I implemented P-012, P-052 and P-013 and authored this rubric. Audit seq 3 recorded 44 citations across 14 items at verifiedRatio 1.0; that is a claim to spot-check, not a finding.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"phone-app-2026-08-30-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — Phone app v1 (browser-first call rails, papercusp agent on the line)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-31","owner":"su-9cf69310-a10e-498e-8d1e-18e46b15a4a0","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — Phone app v1 (browser-first call rails, papercusp agent on the line)\nslug: phone-app-2026-08-30-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-9cf69310-a10e-498e-8d1e-18e46b15a4a0\n---\n\n# Acceptance — Phone app v1 (browser-first call rails, papercusp agent on the line)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nRubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan phone-app-2026-08-30, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality: a browser-first v1 in which the papercusp agent answers real WebRTC calls, with the PSTN edge deliberately deferred under D-016. Six outcome criteria trace to the plan's Background goal (Shape 2 — our own agent worker inside papercusp, self-hosted media plane, one room per call, call data in the app's Postgres) and to Decisions D-015 (latency), D-016 (PSTN deferral), D-018 (phone surfaces belong to the suite app, never the operator rail) and D-019 (Deepgram Aura is the pinned shipping TTS vendor). The shared repo invariants — tests landed with the feature, flags on by default, gate green, docs updated, and the grader's spot-check of the implementer's audit citations — are NOT restated here; they come from classRef plan-class-feature-ship and must be graded from it.\n\nHOW TO WEIGH THE RATINGS. C1 (agent-holds-a-real-spoken-call) and C4 (guest-can-join-a-scheduled-call-with-no-account) are SHIP-BLOCKING: anything below `pass` on either blocks the ship until addressed. C6 (pstn-deferral-is-recorded-and-claimable) is the honesty gate — it decides whether a deliberately-deferred scope was recorded truthfully, and a `fail` there blocks regardless of how well the code scores. C2, C3 and C5 may land `partial` with a stated reason without blocking, provided the reason is recorded.\n⚠ `unknown` IS NOT A SOFT PASS. On a ship-blocking criterion, `unknown` counts as NOT MET and blocks exactly as `fail` does — it means the grader could not establish the outcome, which is precisely the state this gate exists to catch. Several methods below can legitimately land `unknown` (an unreadable /proc/<pid>/environ, a declined re-measurement, an unavailable Postgres arm); say which and why, and never round one up.\n\nGRADER ORIENTATION. The phone app and portal are SEPARATE git repos, symlinked into the workspace root: /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/phone-app and .../portal (real paths under ~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/). Running services: portal :3801, sidecar :8793, livekit-server :7890, livekit-sip, papercusp-phone-worker.service. ⚠ The portal is a `next dev` that compiles each route on demand — give a first curl a LONG timeout, because a short one returns 000, which reads exactly like the service being down. ⚠ For any BROWSER check of the guest page use the `verdict` skill: it is a plain Next route on :3801. Do NOT use the Tauri harness (that is for the operator app only), and never point a browser at :3055/:3070 — a PreToolUse hook blocks it, and a grader who does not know this will report a blocked probe as a failed one. The implementer (su-9cf69310) is also this rubric's author, so the ratings must come from someone who is neither.\n\nSTANDING RAILS — do not \"fix\" these while grading: the worker's resolveAgentName() deliberately returns \"\" so LiveKit AUTOMATIC dispatch is preserved; PHONE_TTS_VENDOR=deepgram must stay pinned (D-019 — removing it makes the worker refuse to start); no phone surface may be added to the operator app (D-018).\n\nREVISION HISTORY. r2 (pre-attestation): fixed a method that told the grader to grep for a literal \"DO-NOT-RE-ADD\" string that does not exist in the tree. r3 (this one), from an independent vetting critique by su-3b0568df: the critique found that in C1 and C3 the drift markers named a marquee failure that NO method step would turn red on — a grader could execute every step faithfully and rate `pass` on a mute agent or on a silently-skipped Postgres arm. Every criterion has now been re-passed against the question \"which method step turns RED if exactly this drift marker were true?\", positive and negative controls were added where the answer was none, line-number pins were demoted to hints (a moved line read as a deleted marker — the false-FAIL direction), and the weighting rules above were added because `unknown` previously had no stated cost.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"scheduling-and-liveness-source-of-truth-2026-08-31","title":"One scheduler (DBOS) and one liveness oracle — make the right call discoverable","status":"draft","created":"2026-08-31","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: One scheduler (DBOS) and one liveness oracle — make the right call discoverable\nslug: scheduling-and-liveness-source-of-truth-2026-08-31\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-01\n---\n\n## Now\nTwo source-of-truth defects, both surfaced 2026-08-31 [owner:Avi 2026-08-31]. Neither\nis a missing capability — in both cases the correct call already exists and nothing\nroutes the agent to it.\n\n**1. Liveness.** An agent answered \"which sessions are running?\" with\n`harness_shared.adv_sessions WHERE ended_at IS NULL`. That is not the liveness oracle.\nWhen the host died at 01:32 UTC the operator was SIGKILLed, so every session that died\nwith it never wrote `ended_at` — the rows became zombies and the agent reported 44\nrunning agents when the truth was ~12 runtimes / 3 live. The owner caught it from the\napp's own \"agents running\" dropdown. `coord:presence` → `sessionState` is documented as\nTHE verdict from one shared oracle; nothing pointed the agent at it.\n\n**2. Scheduling.** The same agent called DBOS-backed routine rows \"cron\", because\n`harness_shared.routines` stores `trigger_kind='cron'` plus a cron EXPRESSION, fired by\nthe durable `routinesTickImpl` in `lib/dbos/routines-workflow.ts`. Separately, three REAL\nUnix crontab entries exist (oddsmith paper feed `*/15`, error-triage ingest `*/14`,\nerror-triage autofix `17 */3` — the last spawns a headless autonomous agent). Those sit\noutside DBOS, invisible to routines pause/status/liveness. Owner rule: all scheduling is\nDBOS, never cron.\n\n## Background\nThe mechanism to fix (1) already exists — `dev:pg_query` emits \"ⓘ a tool covers this\nread\" advisories (observed firing for `coord_event_log` → coord:feed, and for\n`adv_sessions` → sessions:search). It has no rule for the liveness question, and its\nexisting adv_sessions hint points at sessions:search, which answers a different question\nentirely — so the one advisory that did fire actively pointed away from the right call.\n\nThe native-scheduler PreToolUse guard already enforces (2) for agents, blocking\n`crontab`/`at`/`systemd-run` creation. The three existing entries predate or bypassed it.\nThat guard also over-blocks read-only `crontab -l` (EI-21934170410740770), which is what\nmakes the violation hard to audit in the first place.\n\n## Phase 1 — liveness discoverability\n- **P-001** `done` Add a dev:pg_query advisory: a query touching harness_shared.adv_sessions with an ended_at IS NULL/IS NOT NULL predicate warns that this is NOT the liveness oracle, names coord:presence sessionState, and states that ended_at goes unwritten when the operator dies uncleanly — note: ← WI-1447231 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `todo` Correct the EXISTING adv_sessions advisory, which currently routes to sessions:search — right table, wrong question\n- **P-003** `todo` Add a tool-routing pair: \"which agent sessions are running right now\" -> coord:presence (sessionState) / fleet:assignments, NOT a raw adv_sessions ended_at query\n- **P-004** `todo` Guard test proving P-001 is falsifiable: a zombie-row fixture must produce the advisory, and a query without the predicate must not blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 2 — one scheduler\n- **P-005** `todo` Migrate the three oddsmith Unix crontab entries onto DBOS routines so they are visible to routines pause/status/liveness; remove the crontab lines only after the routine rows are observed firing — note: ← WI-1447249 released\n- **P-006** `todo` Persist the standing rule to shared memory and the agent-facing docs: all recurring work is a DBOS routine or blueprint schedule, never a Unix cron; include the trigger_kind='cron' terminology trap that caused the owner miscommunication\n- **P-007** `todo` Fix the native-scheduler guard's read-only over-block (EI-21934170410740770) so `crontab -l` audits work — that false negative hides exactly the violations P-005 removes\n\n## Decisions\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"spawn-door-governor-migration-2026-08-31","title":"Migrate the second agent-spawn door onto the governor admission seam","status":"ready","created":"2026-08-31","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Migrate the second agent-spawn door onto the governor admission seam\nslug: spawn-door-governor-migration-2026-08-31\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-08-31\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ACTIVE TAKEOVER (2026-08-31). P-001–P-003 done; WI-1723509 settled. Activation audits #2 and #3 are recorded, with #3 covering revision 35 after D-014 acceptance repair. P-004 is the sole actionable item and now explicitly covers all 8 callers, live-traffic baselines, silent-door no-traffic verdicts, code-truth checks, and post-migration receipt agreement. Current tenant query: 55 spawns in 7d, 0 governor_observation receipts, positive control 6,951 lifetime rows; the observe-only receipt writer has not yet reached the release plane. The live gate lane is held by another live agent; this session sent evidence once and does not operate or monitor LIVE_GATE_OPS. Downstream P-005–P-013/P-040 remain dependency-ordered.\n\n**Next:** On the 15-minute blocked cadence, run the positive-controlled receipt-count query; when receipts > 0, restore 60s cadence, execute P-004 under D-013/D-014, then proceed through the sequential migration chain.\n\n## Mission\n\nMake `spawnAgentInHarness` cross the same admission seam every other launch path crosses, and make the enforcement scan able to SEE it if it ever stops. Today it does neither, while its own header at `operator-spawn.ts:771` claims to be \"the ONE chokepoint every launch path funnels through\".\n\n## Parent and reuse\n\nAncestor: `unify-agent-spawn-chokepoint-2026-06-06` (SHIPPED 2026-06-10, 18/18 items done and code-verified). That plan built the chokepoint, the brain admission, the single ceiling and the no-raw-spawn guard, and closed stating \"One chokepoint, brain admission, one ceiling, class-gated durability, interactive floor, and the no-raw-spawn guard are all live.\"\n\nThis plan does NOT re-open it and does not dispute it. It records that the shipped claim was true of what the guard MEASURED, and that the measurement had a blind spot: the real child start (`console-spawn.ts:1599`) sits outside every `RESOURCE_GOVERNOR_INVENTORY` path prefix, so a whole door was never in scope to be checked. The gap surfaced three months later, from a different plan's independent acceptance grader — which is why P-001 fixes the DETECTOR before anything else. Reuse `spawnGovernedAgentProcess` rather than building a second seam; the ancestor's guard is extended, never forked.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- The criterion's lead invariant is \"there is exactly one governor admission seam\". A resident increase must do one of exactly three things: cross `Governor.admit`, hold a validated local lease, or carry an explicit `BYPASS_REGISTRY` entry.\n- `spawnAgentInHarness` (`packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/operator-spawn.ts`) does none of the three.\n- This is a MIGRATION, not a design problem. `spawnGovernedAgentProcess` (`packages/operator-core/lib/resource-governor/spawn-execution.ts`) is the real seam — admissionClass `agent`, lease held across the child's whole lifetime, exact-release on exit, cancel on a throwing spawn — and is already wired into `agent-tools/capability/launch-agent.ts:96` and `agent-tools/fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts:45`, with tests. The pattern to copy exists and is proven.\n- Behaviour today is capless and non-rejecting: the door enforces its own `effectiveSpawnCeiling`, which after WI-586538 resolves to the governor's LIVE adaptive window on a seed-sourced host and a deliberate user throttle otherwise, and over-ceiling spawns QUEUE on the D-004 wake key rather than being rejected. So this is partial, not fail: wrong seam in CODE, no lease, no receipt.\n\n## Risk — why this is staged and not one commit\n\nThis path spawns the fleet's own recovery machinery: wake executors, supervision relaunches, spawn-relaunch. A LEAKED lease here starves every future spawn fleet-wide; a BLOCKING admit delays the very wakes that recover a wedged fleet. WI-590490 explicitly prescribes P-018's methodology — observe-only first, then one caller at a time behind a canary. That prescription is carried into the items below and is not negotiable without a Decision recording why.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Changing what the governor's adaptive window computes. This plan changes WHICH code path asks it, never the answer.\n- Removing `effectiveSpawnCeiling` before the seam demonstrably holds the lease (P-012 only).\n\n## Work breakdown\n\n### Phase 1 — Fix the detector first\n\n- **P-001** `done` Widen the `RESOURCE_GOVERNOR_INVENTORY` path prefixes to cover the real child-start path. The actual spawn is `dbos/orchestrator-runner.spawnInvokeOnce` -> `console-spawn.ts:1599 spawn(spawnBin, spawnArgs)`, and `console-spawn.ts`, `dbos/orchestrator-runner.ts` and `harness-invoke-once.ts` sit outside EVERY inventory prefix, so they are never scanned. Prove the fix with the grader's own mechanical demonstration: an identical violating source returns `['resource-start-outside-admission']` from `inspectGovernorSource` but `[]` from `scanInventory` when placed at an uncovered path — after P-001 both must agree. — note: ← WI-1707283 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Pin the coverage with a guard test asserting each of the 8 spawn-door files (`operator-spawn.ts` + the 7 callers) resolves inside a scanned prefix, so a future path move re-opens the blind spot loudly instead of silently. Blocked by P-001. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-1711192 completed (done)\n\n### Phase 2 — Observe before binding\n\n- **P-003** `done` Emit a governor admission RECEIPT from `spawnAgentInHarness` in observe-only mode: record the admission decision that WOULD have been made, bind nothing, reject nothing. Ship flag-ON per repo policy — observe-only is safe by construction. Blocked by P-001. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-1723509 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `todo` Baseline from live observe-only data before any caller binds: spawn rate, burst shape, worst-case wait, and per-caller distribution across all 8 callers for doors with live traffic. For each silent caller, record an explicit no-traffic verdict naming the observation window, verify by code truth that the caller crosses `spawnAgentInHarness` and the receipt path, and after that caller's migration require post-migration receipt agreement before advancing; never treat an empty/all-unknown sample or zero divergence as evidence that migration is safe. Blocked by P-003. blocked-by: P-003\n\n### Phase 3 — Migrate one caller at a time, recovery machinery LAST\n\nEach item: migrate that caller onto `spawnGovernedAgentProcess`, canary it, verify lease acquire/release pairing under a forced-throw spawn, then proceed. Ordered by blast radius, least first.\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Migrate `agent-tools/operator/converse.ts:708`. Blocked by P-004. blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `todo` Migrate `agent-tools/fleet/place_batch.ts:578`. Blocked by P-005. blocked-by: P-005\n- **P-007** `todo` Migrate `papercup/papercup-deep-delegate-deps.ts:152`. Blocked by P-006. blocked-by: P-006\n- **P-008** `todo` Migrate `p2p/offer-executor-prod-deps.ts:94`. Blocked by P-007. blocked-by: P-007\n- **P-009** `todo` Migrate `fleet/spawn-relaunch.ts:90` — recovery machinery begins here. Blocked by P-008. blocked-by: P-008\n- **P-010** `todo` Migrate `fleet/supervision.ts:175`. Blocked by P-009. blocked-by: P-009\n- **P-011** `todo` Migrate `events/await/wake-executor-fresh-context.ts:92` — the riskiest; a blocking admit here delays the wake that recovers a wedged fleet. Blocked by P-010. blocked-by: P-010\n\n### Phase 4 — Collapse the second door\n\n- **P-012** `todo` Migrate `spawnAgentInHarness` itself onto `spawnGovernedAgentProcess` and retire the parallel `effectiveSpawnCeiling` ceiling once the seam provably holds the lease. Correct the `operator-spawn.ts:771` header, which has been claiming sole-chokepoint status it did not have. Blocked by P-011. blocked-by: P-040\n- **P-013** `todo` Lease-leak soak + rollback drill. A leaked lease starves every future spawn, so the acceptance bar is: forced-throw spawn, killed child, and operator restart each leave zero orphaned leases. Blocked by P-012. blocked-by: P-012\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Migrate one caller at a time, recovery machinery LAST\n\n- **P-040** `todo` Migrate `iq-battery/bee-instance.ts:270` — the EIGHTH caller, found by census in D-012 and named by no earlier item. Same terms as every other caller: migrate onto `spawnGovernedAgentProcess`, canary it, verify lease acquire/release pairing under a forced-throw spawn. Acceptance ALSO includes deleting its `EXPECTED_COVERAGE_GAPS` ratchet entry in `spawn-door-coverage.test.ts` (the exact-set-equality assertion fails until that entry is removed, which is the intended closing signal). Must land BEFORE P-012: retiring the parallel `effectiveSpawnCeiling` path while this door is unmigrated is exactly the silent-bypass class this plan exists to close. Blocked by P-011. blocked-by: P-011\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Mechanism: route the chokepoint, not the seven callers\nDate: 2026-08-31\nOwner-dialog answer at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:19 chose \"Route the chokepoint (Recommended)\" over the filed brief's prescription. spawnAgentInHarness IS the chokepoint all seven callers funnel through (~1000 lines: role validation, factory-role guard, brief-placeholder backstop, gateway env, hydration, spawn-tree recording). Rewriting the seven callers onto spawnGovernedAgentProcess would duplicate or bypass all of it. Routing the chokepoint itself governs all seven at once; caller-side work reduces to threading `parent` AdmissionContext for attribution. Binds P-012; P-005..P-011 are attribution-threading, not re-implementation.\n\n### D-002 — The lease does not replace live OS measurement — it adds reservation and attribution\nDate: 2026-08-31\nOwner challenged the premise at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:21: \"WHY DOES IT NEED A TICKET, CANT THE LIVE SYSTEM RESOURCES JUST BE FIGURED OUT ON DEMAND... EVERYTHING IS A PROCESS AND HAS BUILT IN OS TRACKING\". Verified answer at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:23: resource-governor/live-health.ts ALREADY samples OS-native signals (PSI cpu some avg60, PSI memory some/full avg60, /proc/stat procs_running+procs_blocked, /proc/meminfo swap) and that measurement is the PRIMARY signal driving the adaptive window. The lease adds exactly two things /proc cannot: (1) THE BLIND WINDOW — a spawn authorized but not yet started burns nothing measurable, so N concurrent deciders each read an idle box and all launch; measurement is a trailing indicator, the reservation is what makes concurrent deciders see each other. Not hypothetical: operator-spawn.ts:694 documents the ceiling-overshoot race (P-039) that forced admitSpawn to take a PG advisory lock. (2) ATTRIBUTION — /proc shows a process burning a core but not which launch commissioned it; AdmissionContext.parent carries that. CONSTRAINT ON THIS PLAN: the migration must not replace the adaptive live-health window with a static cap. P-012 retires effectiveSpawnCeiling only once the seam provably holds the lease.\n\n### D-003 — Recovery-path spawns: observe-only first, recovery callers last, no blocking admit that can deadlock the repair crew\nDate: 2026-08-31\nOPEN QUESTION REPAIRED. The source conversation left this unanswered: it was asked at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:19 (\"How should recovery-path spawns behave?\"), the owner replied \"i dont understand what this does please explain it simply\", the plain-language reframing at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:21 was answered with the ticket question instead, and the conversation then moved to status at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:24. No owner ruling exists. RESOLVED HERE under AUTO mode [turn:160086aa-4a1b-493b-908c-e18eefeedf02@2026-08-31T11:18Z] and DISCLOSED to the owner rather than blocking on it. THE RISK: this door spawns the fleet's own repair crew (wake executors, supervision relaunches). A blocking admit during a pile-up holds the repair crew at the door exactly when it is needed — a self-feeding jam (box jammed -> repair crew held -> box stays jammed). RULING: (a) P-003 ships observe-only — record the admission decision that WOULD have been made, bind nothing, reject nothing; (b) P-004 measures the worst-case wait a real admit would have imposed on a recovery wake from that live data, and THAT number gates Phase 3; (c) the three recovery-path callers migrate LAST in the DAG (P-009 spawn-relaunch, P-010 supervision, P-011 wake-executor-fresh-context) and never with an admit that can block indefinitely; (d) per the governor plan's D-004, bypasses are registry-owned and lint-enforced — a caller cannot self-exempt, so any recovery exemption requires an explicit BYPASS_REGISTRY row with a reason, not an inline escape.\n\n### D-004 — Admission ordering: admitSpawn before any lease; the lease wraps only the child start\nDate: 2026-08-31\nDesign constraint established during investigation (checkpointed on WI-590490 at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:18). ORDERING IS A LEAK RISK: admitSpawn must run BEFORE any governor lease is taken. If the governor admitted first and admitSpawn then returned over_cap or duplicate, the lease must be explicitly cancelled or it LEAKS — and the governor plan's D-035 names a leaked lease here as starving every future spawn. Taking the lease only around the actual child start makes the leak structurally impossible rather than defended-against. Binds P-012 and is the acceptance bar for P-013 (forced-throw spawn, killed child, and operator restart must each leave zero orphaned leases).\n\n### D-005 — Migrated callers must normalize the admission-failure THROW\nDate: 2026-08-31\nLoad-bearing standing fact read at session_turn:claude:28d773ab-5c4d-4f81-9cb4-da07f10d0f9c:10 (fact key fleet-launch-admission-failure-shape): spawnGovernedAgentProcess THROWS on admission failure, and fleet:launch-on-plan currently lets that throw reject Promise.all before per-member classification. Any caller migrated under P-005..P-011, and the chokepoint itself under P-012, must NORMALIZE that throw into the caller's existing result shape rather than inherit the Promise.all-rejection shape. A migration that propagates the raw throw is not done.\n\n### D-006 — P-001 measured: the plan's own child-start arrow is wrong; the real gap is one file, not three\nDate: 2026-08-31\nMEASURED at current HEAD with an out-of-tree probe importing the scanner (inspectGovernorSource + BYPASS_REGISTRY + RESOURCE_GOVERNOR_INVENTORY) and running it against the candidate files. No tree mutation. Results:\n\n- packages/operator-core/lib/console-spawn.ts -> [\"resource-start-outside-admission\"], bypassRegistered=FALSE, covered by no active lane. THIS IS THE ONLY REAL UNDISPOSITIONED FINDING.\n- packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-runner.ts -> [\"resource-start-outside-admission\"], bypassRegistered=TRUE already, covered by no active lane. Its BYPASS_REGISTRY row (scanner :1433) is therefore INERT today: it dispositions a path nothing scans. Widening makes the existing row live; no new row needed.\n- packages/operator-core/lib/harness-invoke-once.ts -> [] (ZERO codes). It contributes NOTHING and is in the plan item text in error; it only exports resolveSpawnBackendModel.\n- packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/operator-spawn.ts -> [] and IS already covered, re-confirming the checkpoint correction that lib/fleet/ is an existing prefix.\n\nCORRECTION TO THE PLAN PREMISE (P-001 text and the WI-590490 checkpoint both assert it): the chain \"dbos/orchestrator-runner.spawnInvokeOnce -> console-spawn.ts:1599 spawn(spawnBin, spawnArgs)\" DOES NOT EXIST. orchestrator-runner.ts contains no reference to console-spawn at all (grep for console-spawn/consoleSpawn/spawnConsole in that file returns nothing) and calls node:child_process spawn directly at its own :18 import. They are SIBLING doors, not a chain: spawnInvokeOnce is the headless DBOS agent chokepoint; console-spawn owns the visible-terminal and headless primitives.\n\nWHAT console-spawn.ts ACTUALLY IS: the low-level spawn primitive that GOVERNED callers wrap. resource-governor/spawn-execution.ts imports SpawnChildExit/SpawnConsoleResult from it (:3) — i.e. spawnGovernedAgentProcess admits, then calls this primitive as its spawnProcess(context). Its importers are capability/launch-agent.ts (the lane's own governed site), fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts, goals/start.ts, capability/terminal.ts, harness/routines/fleet-headcount-action.ts, goals/goal-auto-start.ts, terminal-spawn.ts.\n\nRULING for P-001: (1) widen the agent-process-memory lane with the two exact file paths console-spawn.ts and dbos/orchestrator-runner.ts (exact-file entries, the style the P-015 lane already uses); do NOT add harness-invoke-once.ts. Not armed; arming waits until the writer is tested.\n\n### D-010 — Observation rows sample ADMITTED spawns, never spawn ATTEMPTS — P-004's denominator rule\nDate: 2026-08-31\n⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-31, same session, before any consumer relied on it. The durable protection\nis the widened guard, which now fails on any NEW uncovered door, not the count itself.\nRelated: P-002, P-012\n\n### D-013 — P-004's baseline query is VETTED and must obey three rules: unknown excluded from the denominator, nulls never coerced to 0, tenant-scoped\nDate: 2026-08-31\nP-004 produces the number D-003 gates Phase 3 on. An unscoped baseline mixes other tenants' spawns\n    into the Phase-3 gate number.\n\nVETTED QUERY:\n\nWITH obs AS (\n  SELECT\n    governor_observation->'door'->>'caller'                 AS caller,\n    governor_observation->'door'->>'outcome'                AS door_outcome,\n    governor_observation->'governor'->>'wouldAdmit'         AS would_admit,\n    (governor_observation->'governor'->>'estimatedWaitMs')::numeric AS est_wait_ms,\n    (governor_observation->'governor'->>'classQueueDepth')::numeric AS queue_depth,\n    CASE jsonb_typeof(governor_observation->'divergedFromGovernor')\n      WHEN 'boolean' THEN (governor_observation->>'divergedFromGovernor')::boolean\n      ELSE NULL END                                         AS diverged\n  FROM harness_shared.spawned_agents\n  WHERE workspace_id = 'papercusp-workspace'\n    AND harness_slug = 'papercusp'\n    AND governor_observation IS NOT NULL\n    AND started_at > now() - interval '24 hours'\n)\nSELECT\n  COALESCE(caller, '(attribution-unavailable)')                       AS caller,\n  count(*)                                                            AS spawns,\n  count(*) FILTER (WHERE door_outcome = 'admitted')                   AS admitted,\n  count(*) FILTER (WHERE door_outcome = 'over_cap')                   AS refused_over_cap,\n  count(*) FILTER (WHERE would_admit <> 'unknown')                    AS opinionated_sample,\n  count(*) FILTER (WHERE diverged IS TRUE)                            AS diverged_true,\n  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE diverged IS TRUE)\n    / NULLIF(count(*) FILTER (WHERE would_admit <> 'unknown'), 0), 1) AS diverged_pct_of_opinionated,\n  count(*) FILTER (WHERE est_wait_ms IS NOT NULL)                     AS wait_samples,\n  max(est_wait_ms)                                                    AS worst_wait_ms,\n  percentile_disc(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY est_wait_ms)\n    FILTER (WHERE est_wait_ms IS NOT NULL)                            AS p95_wait_ms,\n  max(queue_depth)                                                    AS max_queue_depth\nFROM obs\nGROUP BY ROLLUP (COALESCE(caller, '(attribution-unavailable)'))\nORDER BY spawns DESC NULLS LAST;\n\nREADING IT. `caller` groups on the descriptive D-011 label; all EIGHT labels are\nthreaded (measured: grep of `spawnCaller:` returns exactly the eight door labels).\nThe D-003 gate number is `worst_wait_ms` restricted to the recovery-path callers\n— `fleet/spawn-relaunch`, `fleet/supervision`,\n`events/await/wake-executor-fresh-context` — since that is the wait a blocking\nadmit would impose on the wake that recovers a wedged fleet.\n\nACCEPTANCE PRECONDITION: `opinionated_sample` must be large enough to mean\nanything, and `wait_samples` must be non-zero, before any number here is quoted\nas the Phase-3 gate. A NULL is the query telling you it has no opinion — report\nthat as \"not yet measurable\", never as a pass.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-014 — D-014: The live spawn population collapsed ~85% and is now single-caller dominated — P-004's baseline cannot deliver per-caller divergence evidence for 7 of the 8 doors\nDate: 2026-08-31\nP-004 says \"baseline from live observe-only data ... spawn rate, burst shape, and per-caller attribution\", and P-005..P-011 + P-040 each gate their caller's migration on that evidence. Do NOT read a silent door's zero rows as \"safe to migrate\". Zero observations is absence of evidence about that door, not evidence it never spawns; a door quiet for a week can fire during an incident, which is exactly when a wrong admission decision is most expensive.\n\nRULING for whoever executes P-004 onward: P-004's acceptance is re-scoped to what the traffic can actually support — (a) a real baseline for the door(s) that carry live traffic, and (b) an explicit, recorded NO-TRAFFIC verdict for every door with zero observations in the window, naming the window length. A silent door's migration must then gate on something the sample can supply — code-truth review of its admission path plus the observe-only receipt agreeing with the governor decision on the first N live spawns AFTER migration — never on a divergence statistic that cannot exist. Whoever re-scopes P-004 should state the observation window explicitly rather than waiting for a sample size that will not arrive.\n\nThis decision rests on measurement taken while P-003 is committed and on staging but NOT deployed (blockedOn: gate), so ZERO receipts exist yet; it constrains what P-004 can conclude once they do, and does not itself require deployed data.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-040\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"unified-responder-selection-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — one generic responder-selection mechanism consumed by both the critique consult and acceptance grading","status":"superseded","created":"2026-08-31","owner":"su-302e07bf-eb9f-4eba-a768-247fe2047d93","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — one generic responder-selection mechanism consumed by both the critique consult and acceptance grading\nslug: unified-responder-selection-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-08-31\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-302e07bf-eb9f-4eba-a768-247fe2047d93\n---\n\n# Acceptance — one generic responder-selection mechanism consumed by both the critique consult and acceptance grading\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.)\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation definition-of-done for unified-responder-selection-critique-and-grading-2026-08-30, authored against AS-BUILT reality after all 7 items landed and the code-truth audit passed 7/7 (auditSeq 1, sha ada8f4e6ee, 23 citations resolved, 0 unverified).\n\nThe plan's goal was NOT \"add a second grader\". It was to make ONE mechanism own responder selection so the critique consult and acceptance grading cannot drift apart (D-001, owner ruling), then to prove the independence properties the system already relied on still hold once n went from exactly-1 to min:1/max:2.\n\nREVISION 2 — changed by the vetting critique (consult conv-mtghcszj-0000-4660332c6d174834ae2ebf5c603f3d8b), which is why this text differs from what was first proposed:\n- Criterion 1 was asserting that both consumers IMPORT the shared module. The critique's central finding: \"imports are not parity — a consumer can import the shared selector and then re-sort, filter or truncate its result and still satisfy every word of that criterion while drifting exactly as D-001 feared.\" The criterion now demands the DIFFERENTIAL, and a new test (selection-parity.test.ts) was WRITTEN to make it bindable rather than the criterion merely reworded.\n- Criterion 6 was partly self-serving (I wrote the guards and the criterion grading them). Its method now demands an ARTIFACT — a committed control asserted to fail — and names scripts/mutation-probe.sh, so a grader who wrote none of it verifies mechanically instead of stylistically.\n- Criterion 6 gained the missing clause: when Docker is absent the correct rating is `unknown`, never `healthy` by default and never `broken`, so an environment gap cannot silently read as either.\n- Vacuous-pass coverage (raised by the first responder, who declined on capacity but left the prior): a selector that never selects anyone satisfies parity trivially, since two empty lists are always equal. Positive controls are now demanded explicitly.\n\nTwo notes for the grader, because they are where a shallow pass would go wrong:\n- Five criteria carry structured `tests` checks that are RUN at grading time. Green is necessary but NOT sufficient — the criteria ask whether guards are FALSIFIABLE and whether invariants hold MENU-WIDE, which a green suite cannot answer. Read the named cases.\n- D-007/D-008 require a CONTROL PAIR for every rule: the identical fixture with the condition inverted must produce the opposite outcome. A guard without one is untested rather than passing.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for capacity-signal-clarity-and-fleet-capacity-repair-2026-09-01, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. The plan came out of an incident whose defining error was reading a POLICY VERDICT as a MEASUREMENT: a pacing projection rendered as a capacity wall, and the fleet's own strength meter reporting 3/50 against ~37 live members. D-001 settled that quota was never the binding constraint, so no leg was permitted to remedy the shortfall by lowering headcount or throttling; the shortfall had to be treated as a control-plane and signal-clarity defect. These seven criteria grade the OUTCOMES that follow from that framing. They deliberately do not restate the plan-class-bugfix invariants (root cause, recurrence guard, live verification, mitigation labelling, citation spot-checks) — the class rubric grades those, and the grader applies both.\n\nCoverage of the plan's Decisions, stated so a gap is visible rather than assumed: D-002 → criteria 1 and 3; D-003 → criterion 2; D-004 → criteria 3 and 4; D-005 → criterion 5; D-006 → criterion 7; D-001's prohibition (no leg may remedy by lowering headcount or throttling) → criterion 6, which grades the SHAPE of the remedy, not only its correctness. D-007 records that P-001 reached production through the inference gateway, which runs from the tree and bypasses the release pipeline; criterion 1 is the only criterion with live production evidence available, and its replication drill uses it.\n\nSix of the seven criteria carry a structured tests binding per the meta-rubric's prefer-structured-check, so a pass-rating a failing run contradicts is refused at emit. Criterion 7 deliberately carries none: it grades an ABSENCE (work correctly not done) and no test can assert that a defect does not exist. That is the one place fuzzy judgment is the honest instrument, and its method is written to make the judgement falsifiable instead.\n\nTwo criteria carry a binding that covers only PART of what they grade: criterion 1 (payload half bound; the P-006 doc and the P-013 out-of-band delivery are not) and criterion 6 (park and launch halves bound; the park -> loop:end seam and the D-001 absence half are not). Each names its own uncovered half in a BINDING SCOPE paragraph rather than implying total coverage, so a green run is not sufficient evidence for either. Item coverage: P-013's outcome lands OUTSIDE the codebase, so no code-truth citation and no test binding can ever reach it; it is graded as a declared sub-claim of criterion 1 rather than left ungraded.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-capacity-signal-clarity-and-fleet-capacity-repair-2026-09-01-r2","title":"Acceptance: capacity signal clarity + fleet capacity repair (2026-09-01)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-01","owner":"su-dba4a849-ff14-45ee-95f2-8bc3eb1f22c2","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: capacity signal clarity + fleet capacity repair (2026-09-01)\nslug: acceptance-capacity-signal-clarity-and-fleet-capacity-repair-2026-09-01-r2\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-01\nupdated: 2026-09-01\nowner: su-dba4a849-ff14-45ee-95f2-8bc3eb1f22c2\n---\n\n# Acceptance: capacity signal clarity + fleet capacity repair (2026-09-01)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-01. Azure is outside v1 (aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10… <!-- P-031 -->\n## Product shaping\n\nAudience: Avi and customer teams operating hosted or BYOC workspaces.\nProblem: D-154/D-169 preserved launch-cut work, but this draft still describes already-delivered hosting and Stripe test setup as absent and duplicates the focused AWS lane.\nOutcome: finish the retained hosted customer-account, Azure, external review and commercial gates with traceable current-build proof and an independent ship verdict.\nNon-goals: reopen the shipped GCP launch; create another AWS canary, billing stack, portal or orchestration system; treat a prepared packet, mock, test subscription, or missing external approval as a completed live gate.\nSource turns: session_turn:claude:a48e15ad-d6dc-47d7-bbdf-1449d14f6162:16; session_turn:codex:01a06df4-18c2-7f10-9f58-8a540718609c:11; session_turn:codex:01a06de2-4374-7d50-9cf5-d5474b4cc431:6; session_turn:claude:9de76438-7f9c-4844-a6a8-cf6e02a31df5:6, :10, :17.\nScenarios: a hosted customer runs an ordinary workspace through the sealed customer-content boundary; Tenant A's overlapping object ids never grant access to Tenant B; an Azure operator installs the generated IAM policy then proves lifecycle and cleanup in an authorized subscription; an independent tester and legal reviewer issue actual findings/dispositions; an approved live paid offer completes payment, usage, cancellation and cleanup.\nAssumptions: app.papercusp.com hosting and Stripe TEST subscriptions already exist; only focused successor evidence may settle transferred AWS/commercial work. Azure subscription access, external review authority and live billing configuration must be checked rather than inferred.\nOpen prerequisites: hosted acceptance receipts, Azure subscription/delegation and allowed spend, external tester/legal reviewer, approved live commercial offer and live-mode credentials. Preparation proceeds under AUTO; absent credentials or third-party sign-off cannot be fabricated.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Hosted workspace operation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The existing hosted control plane operates an ordinary authorized customer workspace end to end through the approved confidential boundary, with exact artifact/runtime identity and retained-data teardown receipts.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The existing hosted control plane operates an ordinary authorized customer workspace end to end through the approved confidential boundary, with exact artifact/runtime identity and retained-data teardown receipts.\",\"falsifier\":\"A health response alone, mock journey, missing initialized workspace, mismatch between operation receipt and serving artifact/runtime identity, or unreconciled hosted-control-plane workspace resource remains fails. R-7 judges relay confidentiality; R-4 judges the Azure provider census.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Reuse unified-web-portal P-031 and cloud-cross-feature shipment receipts; add only missing hosted customer-operation evidence. Inspect connect/provision/initialize/operation/cleanup receipts and their serving artifact. Confirm staging/current-build acceptance before final-release shipment. Match each hosted operation/cleanup receipt artifact id with the servingRuntimes observation for that exact runtime. Store an immutable connect/provision/initialize/operation/cleanup manifest and resource disposition on P-001; a health response alone is insufficient. Missing observations are unknown and cannot pass.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Hosted tenant isolation and independent security acceptance.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Two deliberately overlapping tenants cannot enumerate, subscribe to, route to or mutate each other's HTTP/SSE/WS/PTY/files/MCP/SQL resources. WorkOS session refresh, revocation/role change, RLS owner bypass/transaction context, CSRF/CORS/cookies, webhook ordering, onboarding rollback, entitlements, support-grant expiry and secret canaries have positive and negative assembled evidence plus independent security review.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Two deliberately overlapping tenants cannot enumerate, subscribe to, route to or mutate each other's HTTP/SSE/WS/PTY/files/MCP/SQL resources. WorkOS session refresh, revocation/role change, RLS owner bypass/transaction context, CSRF/CORS/cookies, webhook ordering, onboarding rollback, entitlements, support-grant expiry and secret canaries have positive and negative assembled evidence plus independent security review.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any cross-tenant success, untested required attack surface, persistent revoked access, missing positive authorized control or absent independent reviewer fails.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inventory every P-002 attack surface against existing native tests; run an assembled current-build two-tenant acceptance with authorized positive controls and adversarial negative cases. Record per-surface proof, exact runtime and independent review findings; component tests alone are insufficient. Fixed census: HTTP, SSE, WS, PTY, files, MCP, direct SQL/RLS owner bypass and transaction context, WorkOS refresh/revocation/role change, CSRF, CORS, cookies, webhook ordering, onboarding rollback, entitlements, support-grant scope/expiry and secret canaries. Partition each as checked/notChecked/notApplicable with positive/negative controls and residue; pin the manifest as an immutable P-002 thread post. The bound assembled Hono/PostgreSQL integration file covers overlapping HTTP/SSE/MCP/direct SQL isolation, socket replay, WS/PTY/files/MCP tickets and rotation, persisted-session revocation with a surviving tenant, and scoped expiring support grants. Those are the tree partition only; simulated provider delegation cannot satisfy live-provider or independent-review clauses. Unchecked required entries prevent pass.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-two-tenant-acceptance.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Azure IAM and image preparation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Prepare the retained Azure IAM/image work without duplicating AWS.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Customer-run Azure policy is generated from the existing preflight action population, validates its customer scope, contains no wildcard actions or credentials, and documents image-gallery/marketplace prerequisites.\",\"falsifier\":\"A hand-copied action list, broader wildcard grant, invalid scope, secret material or a claimed live publication without receipt fails.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Extend existing Azure connection/preflight tests to prove generated scope/action constraints, refusal cases and no secret material; inspect the maintained compute-gallery release path and record remaining publishing prerequisites. azure-connection.test.ts 'covers preflight permissions exactly, with subscription and resource-group scope boundaries' diffs generated Actions+DataActions against AZURE_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS and asserts no wildcards/secrets paths. Invalid scope cases require throws. 'returns fresh non-secret JSON and refuses secret-shaped input' builds valid JSON, plants clientSecret:'forbidden' requiring refusal, and proves surviving fresh output. Native mutation test_runs 21179705 (wildcard Actions), 21179703 (resourceGroup validator bypass),21179687 (remove secret-input isolation) fail those assertions with baseline/copy-baseline and machine descriptors. These are detector evidence, not Azure publication. The image prerequisite guide requires separate committed-file review lineage; builder tests alone do not satisfy that clause.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/azure-connection.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/azure-compute-gallery-release.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Live Azure lifecycle and zero orphan gate.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"An authorized real Azure subscription proves connect/preflight/provision/initialize/operation/recovery/destroy, retained-data disposition and provider-read zero-orphan inventory with positive controls; P-031 judges the preserved Azure gate.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An authorized real Azure subscription proves connect/preflight/provision/initialize/operation/recovery/destroy, retained-data disposition and provider-read zero-orphan inventory with positive controls; P-031 judges the preserved Azure gate.\",\"falsifier\":\"Mocks, absent subscription credentials, missing lifecycle legs, an unobserved resource kind, or any orphan fails.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Once authorized subscription/delegation and spend exist, use the maintained Azure adapter and compute-gallery image release, run the real canary, and attach operation ids, runtime/image identity, backup/restore data controls and provider-read resource census. No Azure verdict is inferred from AWS or GCP. Pin the P-004/P-031 manifest as immutable work-item posts with subscription/operation ids, image/runtime, restore marker and provider-read resource-kind census plus positive controls. Absent authorization/unperformed lifecycle is unknown and prevents pass; observed orphan, uncovered resource kind in a claimed census, or fixture evidence presented as live is fail.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — External penetration test and legal privacy review.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"An external penetration tester and authorized legal/privacy reviewer issue an actual scoped report and sign-off; material findings are fixed and independently rechecked or explicitly remain blockers.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"An external penetration tester and authorized legal/privacy reviewer issue an actual scoped report and sign-off; material findings are fixed and independently rechecked or explicitly remain blockers.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An agent-authored scope packet, internal security tests, unsigned legal notes or outstanding material findings fail.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Prepare a scope/evidence packet from current hosted topology, customer-content threat model, isolation matrix, logging/retention/support controls and cleanup evidence. Obtain the third-party reports and signed legal/privacy disposition; record identities, dates, scope and recheck evidence.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Commercial live billing gate.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The focused monetization successor supplies an approved paid offer and verified live payment to provisioning, usage accounting, cancellation and resource/billing closure, reusing shipped Stripe TEST rollout and existing accounting/entitlements.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The focused monetization successor supplies an approved paid offer and verified live payment to provisioning, usage accounting, cancellation and resource/billing closure, reusing shipped Stripe TEST rollout and existing accounting/entitlements.\",\"falsifier\":\"A test subscription, unapproved offer/live activation, duplicate billing stack, inaccurate retained-resource costs, or missing real charge/cancellation/cleanup receipt fails.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read papercusp-monetization-2026-09-04 and cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03 receipts. Reuse their accounting/budget/entitlement/Stripe paths, verify approved live configuration without exposing secrets, then record real payment and lifecycle/usage/cancellation/cleanup proof. TEST-mode evidence is preparation only. P-008 consumes the focused successor's immutable approved-offer/live-payment/usage/cancellation/resource-and-billing-closure manifest, recording mode/provider ids without secrets. Missing approval/live config or unperformed payment is unknown and prevents pass; test-mode evidence presented as live, inaccurate accounting, a duplicate stack or completed cancellation leaving obligations is fail.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Customer content stays customer controlled.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Preserve D-001 and parent D-295 confidential customer-local execution.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"With customer-controlled ingress as the default, customer-held keys and independently verified endpoint identity protect customer content across gateway, relay, persistence, logs and telemetry throughout authorized connect/reconnect/revocation and vendor-outage customer-local operation by refusing any relay that lacks an established customer-sealed channel.\",\"falsifier\":\"A recoverable negative content marker, vendor-readable relay, revoked connection success, or customer-local work failing solely because the vendor is unavailable fails. Forwarding content before the independently verified customer-sealed channel is established, or defaulting to vendor-controlled readable ingress, fails.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Reuse the completed confidentiality correction ledger and rerun affected maintained marker, sealed-channel and vendor-outage tests on the assembled current build. Preserve browser delivery/trust/key-custody limits; no TLS/base64-only substitute. Sealed-channel tests positively deliver authenticated frames, reject mismatched keys before any frame and hold frames for async verification; marker integration supplies readable-relay negative and endpoint-delivery positive controls; outage integration operates through customer-controlled ingress. hosted-workspace-connector.test.ts 'closes old-generation streams on rotation and the current generation on revocation' requires stale-ticket refusal and authenticate(revokedBearer)===null. hosted-connector-client.test.ts positively reconnects after ordinary close but 'NEVER reconnects after a revoked close' keeps one socket and emits revoked terminal state after timers. These tree checks do not prove every live/default configuration: pin selected ingress/trust/key-custody configuration and complete content-carrier census on P-009 before pass.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/byoc-sealed-channel.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-relay-content-marker.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-byoc-vendor-outage.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-workspace-connector.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-connector-client.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002 | live |\n| R-3 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-031 | live |\n| R-5 | P-007 | live |\n| R-6 | P-008 | live |\n| R-7 | P-009 | tree |\n\nReuse the existing workspace-host adapters, preflight action constants, scoped identity/revocation/sealed channel, compute-gallery release, accounting/entitlements and plan/rubric/results ledger. Adjacent fleets own AWS and portal journeys. Current-build acceptance is the implementation plane; final-release evidence is required only for final operation/shipment. Every live prerequisite is guarded by its item; shaping or activation never certifies an unmet prerequisite.\n\n## Background\n\nD-154 restricted the initial launch to GCP and deferred AWS, Azure, the hosted control plane, and billing. D-169 then recorded the mechanical consequence: `plans:set-plan-status -> shipped` refuses a plan holding any `todo`/`blocked`/`needs-human` item, so the only vocabulary for \"deliberately not done in this cut\" is `dropped` + a note. That is correct, but it puts real, valid, unbuilt work inside the dropped items of a plan about to ship — where nothing indexes it as outstanding.\n\nThe most consequential single item is P-068, the hosted customer-account acceptance gate: overlapping-name multi-org signup, WorkOS session refresh/logout/revocation and role-change propagation, cross-tenant HTTP/SSE/WS/PTY/file/MCP/direct-SQL object-id attacks, RLS owner-bypass and transaction-context tests, CSRF/CORS/cookie-domain checks, webhook ordering, onboarding rollback, entitlements, support-grant expiry, and secret canaries — plus an INDEPENDENT SECURITY REVIEW and positive evidence that Tenant A cannot enumerate, route to, subscribe to, or mutate Tenant B resources.\n\nThe underlying isolation surface was in fact delivered and independently verified in the same audit: `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on 7 hosted/customer tables (978-hosted-customer-rls.sql) and on the 6 `workspace_host_*` tables (979-workspace-host-tenant-rls.sql), both applied 2026-08-26; `withTenantContext` using transaction-local `set_config`; and a deliberately overlapping two-tenant attack harness. All carry unit and integration coverage. What has NEVER run is an assembled acceptance pass over the whole hosted surface, or an independent review of it. That distinction is the reason this item must not be treated as covered by its component tests.\n\n## Phase 1 — Hosted control plane\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Deploy and operate the hosted control plane at app.papercusp.com (carries P-059 of the BYOC plan). The portal hosting/DNS already exist; remaining work is operating customer workspaces through the approved boundary and reusing unified-web-portal P-031 receipts. importance: high blocked-by: P-009 — note: ← WI-6554700010009860 released\n- **P-002** `blocked` Run the hosted customer-account acceptance gate, including the independent security review and positive cross-tenant isolation evidence (carries P-068 of the BYOC plan). Cannot begin before the control plane it audits exists. importance: high blocked-by: P-001, P-009\n\n## Phase 2 — Multi-cloud\n\n- **P-003** `dropped` Live AWS canary transferred to aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01 P-012/WI-10005036 per D-003 and D-004; not abandoned and not claimed complete here. AWS successor remains sole proof lane. importance: normal\n- **P-004** `dropped` Live Azure canary with zero-orphan proof (carries P-035). Owner-walled: no Azure subscription or credentials exist in this workspace. importance: normal — note: ← WI-6554700010009862 dropped\n- **P-005** `dropped` Former multi-cloud Gate 5 transferred: AWS readiness is judged by aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01, Azure readiness remains P-031, hosted customer acceptance remains P-002. Superseded duplicate per D-004, not a passed gate. importance: normal\n- **P-006** `dropped` Azure customer-run least-privilege IAM template generated from existing AZURE_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS, scope validation and negative tests, plus compute-gallery/marketplace image setup and remaining publication prerequisites. AWS IAM is already carried by aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01 P-013/WI-10005037; do not duplicate it. Authorable without Azure live credentials. importance: normal — note: ← WI-6554700010009843 dropped\n\n## Phase 3 — Commercial and external review\n\n- **P-007** `dropped` External penetration test and legal/privacy sign-off (carries P-043). Owner-walled: requires procuring an external vendor and a legal review; an agent can prepare scope and evidence but cannot obtain either. importance: normal — note: ← WI-6554700010009863 dropped\n- **P-008** `dropped` Post-beta commercial billing (carries P-067). Stripe TEST subscriptions have shipped in cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03. Reuse the focused papercusp-monetization-2026-09-04 successor for the approved paid offer and live billing activation/proof; no parallel implementation. Live-mode configuration/charge/outcome remain required. importance: low — note: ← WI-6554700010009864 dropped\n\n\n## Phase — Hosted customer-content boundary\n\n- **P-009** `done` Implement the hosted confidentiality correction approved by byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-295; reuse the existing finding WI-2144452. Reuse authenticated transport/identity infrastructure and preserve D-143 binding, generation, revocation and scoped authorization, while replacing or refusing the vendor-readable PTY/file/content relay for the strong customer-data promise. Use customer-controlled ingress by default; any vendor-relayed content must use an established end-to-end transport with independently verified endpoint identity and customer-held keys. Specify browser application delivery, trust anchors, key custody/recovery, revocation and limits against an active vendor; vendor-served JavaScript plus TLS/base64 is not sufficient. Keep customer plans/work items/prompts, transcripts, source, model I/O and diagnostic content out of vendor storage/log/telemetry. Add negative content-marker tests across gateway, relay, persistence and logs, plus positive authorized connection/reconnect/revocation tests, in an isolated current-build assembled system; no hosted DNS/deployment prerequisite for implementation. The agent loop and content remain customer-local and work during a vendor outage. Complete before hosted deployment/acceptance; this does not pull hosted, AWS/Azure or billing into the GCP launch cut. importance: high — note: Hosted confidentiality correction completed by hosted-byoc-confidentiality-correction-2026-10-02 P-001..P-009; parent WI-2144452 done. Assembled BYOC 5-plane marker harness passed with zero recoverable markers, test run 20601379 and current spec evidence 23056/23057. Positive sealed-channel and vendor-outage proofs reside on completed WI-10005596/WI-10005597.\n\n\n## Phase — Gates\n\n- **P-031** `dropped` Azure multi-cloud readiness gate, split out of P-005 per D-003: Azure is judged ready once the live Azure canary (P-004) lands with zero-orphan proof. Azure is outside v1 (aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01#D-004), so this gate no longer holds AWS or GCP readiness. blocked-by: P-004 — note: Dropped per byoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01#D-006 — owner-dialog ruling by Avi [turn:c42f7bc8@2026-10-15T13:12:47.818Z] under directive #1901: Azure (P-004/P-006/P-031) dropped for now, moves to a future plan; pentest+legal (P-007) dropped for now with a prep package owed; live commercial billing (P-008) out — billing stays Stripe TEST.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Hosted deployment requires the approved customer-content boundary; GCP launch scope stays separate\nDate: 2026-09-04\nAvi approved the six-part BYOC architecture review in session_turn:codex:01a06df4-18c2-7f10-9f58-8a540718609c:11, adopting the review at :10. This carrier remains deferred and draft; adding an implementation gate does not activate hosted deployment, AWS/Azure live parity or billing, and does not change their existing external prerequisites. The customer-local agent loop, Postgres/SPA, Cupboard content and locally cached config/model assets remain as ruled in the main plan.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-005, P-009\n\n### D-002 — Commercial billing has a focused hosted-first monetization draft; preserve this carrier's launch gates\nDate: 2026-09-04\nAvi requested a current plan incorporating the September 4 monetization review in session_turn:codex:01a06de2-4374-7d50-9cf5-d5474b4cc431:6. The detailed commercial proposal is papercusp-monetization-2026-09-04 (draft; WI-2144496). That successor covers pricing, metering, budget admission, manually invoiced pilots and subsequent Stripe automation for the commercial work carried here as P-008. Keep P-008 traceable here, but implement the commercial stack only through that focused successor once activated; do not create a parallel billing implementation. This update is planning authorization only: final prices, license choice, billing activation, deployment and prospect outreach remain unapproved. All existing carrier item statuses and D-001 confidentiality requirements remain; main BYOC D-295 stays the architectural authority. The successor consumes this carrier's hosted deployment, customer-account security acceptance and confidentiality correction plus portal acceptance before paid hosted launch, while preserving the existing GCP cut. The separate agent-economy draft is not activated or superseded.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-003 — AWS lanes carried by aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01; Gate 5 no longer waits on the Azure canary for AWS readiness\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, executing aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01 P-014 (owner directive #1223); v1 scope per aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01#D-004 = [owner:Avi 2026-10-01, directive #1232] \"lets also make part of v1. aws support, both papercusp cloud and byoc cloud, and also support bring your own cloud for google\"; Azure stays out of v1].\n\nRULING:\n- P-003 (live AWS canary, carries P-030) is CARRIED by aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01 P-012 (live real-account canary in 413781344298: connect -> preflight -> provision -> initialise -> SSM -> stop/start -> snapshot/restore -> destroy, zero-orphan tagged inventory). P-003 closes when that item closes, citing its evidence; nobody should build a second AWS canary here.\n- The AWS part of P-006 (IAM templates, least-privilege policy) is CARRIED by aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01 P-013. P-006 stays open here for the Azure templates and any marketplace-image follow-up.\n- P-005 (Gate 5) is rescoped so AWS readiness no longer waits on the Azure canary: its blocked-by becomes [P-003, P-002] (AWS canary + hosted customer acceptance). The Azure half of the gate moves to a new item blocked by P-004, so the Azure requirement is preserved, not dropped.\n\nWHY: the AWS lane is now active v1 work on its own plan, while Azure is still owner-walled (P-004 needs-human, no subscription). Keeping Gate 5 tied to Azure would block AWS readiness indefinitely.\n\n### D-004 — Fleet carry replaces the passive register; remove transferred AWS duplicates and stale hosting/billing walls\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAvi renewed end-to-end carry under AUTO in session_turn:claude:9de76438-7f9c-4844-a6a8-cf6e02a31df5:6 and :10, and requested supersession audit at :17. Leader audit report /reports?sel=rpt_7bbcd3a4-8019-4463-bdbc-281789776924 and leader turn :20 direct dropping carrier P-003/P-005 and narrowing P-006 to Azure. Preserve D-001/D-295 confidentiality, the Azure P-004/P-031 obligation, P-002 security acceptance and D-002 commercial successor. Supersession is transfer, not a passed canary or abandoned work. Local Azure probe found no az executable, no AZURE_/ARM_ env names and no ~/.azure/azureProfile.json; this is a local credential-route finding, not proof about all stored provider connections. No new live spend, publication or third-party clearance is implied by those observations.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-031\n\n### D-005 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: byoc-carrier-vetting-repair-20261013-r2\nRequest-Hash: 6cf0408ae31de5e041c7620d073718336d3545c7d24cd8dcd702c41806e05128\nActor: su-61c39eff-e943-44d4-be3f-519f3989fb0d\nReason: Reconcile independent critique thread-post:1178445: decision lineage, fixed tenant census/partial detector coverage, exact Azure mutation controls, explicit missing-evidence outcomes, hosted/Azure/content partitions and D-001 default ingress/refusal guard. Preserve all seven mandatory outcomes and live Azure/external/legal/commercial gates.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-5193b26d-7e48-4ba6-a480-45402f56f6b9\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1178474\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T07:37:11.784Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 16 → 17\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-6, R-7\n\n### D-006 — Owner scope ruling: drop Azure, drop pentest/legal (prep package owed), hosted control plane authorized, live billing out\nDate: 2026-10-15\nSource: OWNER-DIALOG answers typed by Avi [turn:c42f7bc8@2026-10-15T13:12:47.818Z] (verdict owner-dialog), session su-6ccd68f6, under owner directive #1901 (\"carry all these plans to shipped status yourself now\").\n\n1.
