The root `PlanDashboardHost` full-pane takeover does not mount on `/plans`, so it can never cover the split.\n- **R-3 The desktop chat sidebar is unchanged.** In the default `stack` layout both panes produce the same layout as before this plan: no new layout box (the column wrapper is `display: contents`), same DOM order and ids, and every pre-existing `InboxPane.test.tsx` / `PlansPane.test.tsx` case passes without modification.\n- **R-4 Selection stays URL-owned.** `?opcis` (inbox) and `?pdash` (plans) remain the only selection state in both layouts; a portal deep link `?app=inbox&item=<id>` or `?app=plans&plan=<harness::slug>` opens the face with that item / plan already selected in the aside, forwarded by the portal shell through `portalEmbedHref` extra params.\n- **R-5 Narrow fallback.** At 900px and below the split collapses to one column: with a selection the detail fills the page and a \"Back to list\" control clears the selection; without a selection the list fills the page.\n- **R-6 Bulk flows untouched.** `InboxBulkStrip` / `PlansCleanupStrip` behaviour and their persisted runs are unchanged, and split mode introduces no new data reads — the aside renders exactly what the row click already opened.\n- **R-7 Accessibility holds in both layouts.** A row's `aria-controls` resolves to the detail element `inbox-expanded-<id>` in stack and split mode; when the detail is passively removed in split mode keyboard focus lands on the surviving row or the aside landmark, never on `<body>`.\n- **R-8 Evidence.** Vitest cases cover stack-unchanged, split-renders-aside, selection-moves-detail and narrow-back; verdict captures of :3081 at 1800×1000 and 900×1000 show R-1/R-2/R-5 live; the plan ships only after the per-item code-truth audit and an independently graded acceptance rubric.\n\n## Design (Route 1)\n\n- Both panes gain `layout?: \"stack\" | \"split\"` (default `stack`). Every existing child is wrapped in `<div className=\"op-inbox__column\">` / `<div className=\"plans-pane__column\">`; in stack mode that wrapper is `display: contents` (zero layout change), in split mode the root becomes `display:grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(380px, 37%) minmax(0,1fr)` (Plans: 41%) with the column as a flex column and a new `<aside className=\"…__aside\">` on the right.\n- Inbox aside: the existing `InboxExpandedDetail` + `OtherDetail` (+ `WorkItemDiscussion` when `?opcid` targets it) for `selectedItem` (already computed from `?opcis`); rows in split mode do NOT render the inline detail; empty state \"Select an item to read and answer it here\". `aria-controls` keeps pointing at `inbox-expanded-<id>`, which now lives in the aside.\n- Plans aside: `PlanDashboard` (lazy, `Suspense`) driven by the same `?pdash=<harness>::<slug>` param the row click already sets (`decodeScopedRef`), `onBack` clears the param; selected row gets `is-selected`; empty state \"Select a plan to open its dashboard here\". `__root.tsx` must NOT mount the full-pane `PlanDashboardHost` takeover on `/plans` (route-aware skip via `useRouterState` pathname), otherwise the takeover covers the split.\n- Narrow (`@media (max-width: 900px)`): grid collapses to one column; with a selection the column hides and the aside fills the page with a \"Back to list\" button (the mockup's narrow state), without one the aside hides.\n- Deep links: `portalEmbedHref(href, theme, extra?)` (packages/operator-core/lib/portal-embed.ts, imported by the portal) gains an optional extra-params map; the portal shell reads `?plan=` / `?item=` (nuqs) and forwards them as `pdash` / `opcis` into the iframe src for the plans / inbox kinds. The board's link shapes `?app=plans&plan=<ref>` and `?app=inbox&item=<id>` then work end to end.\n- Verification: tests beside the components (Vitest, jsdom) + live capture of :3081 at 1800×1000 and 900×1000 with verdict; refresh the audit page's shipped captures.\n\n## Phase 1 — Operator: split layout in the panes\n\n- **P-001** `done` InboxPane `layout=\"split\"`: column wrapper, aside with the selected item's detail/discussion, no inline detail in split, empty state, narrow back button; CSS in inbox-pane.css; InboxPane.test.tsx cases (stack unchanged; split renders aside; selection moves detail). importance: high — note: ← WI-2140895 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` PlansPane `layout=\"split\"`: column wrapper, aside rendering PlanDashboard from `?pdash`, `is-selected` row, empty state, narrow back button; CSS in plans-pane.css; PlansPane.test.tsx cases. importance: high — note: PlansPane layout=\"split\" + plans-pane.css + split cases; 29/29 green 2026-09-02T04:3xZ\n- **P-003** `done` operator-vite `/plans` + `/inbox` routes pass `layout=\"split\"`; `__root.tsx` skips `PlanDashboardHost` on `/plans`; route tests assert the prop and the skip. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 — note: ← WI-2140918 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Portal: deep links\n\n- **P-004** `done` `portalEmbedHref` extra params (+ test in portal-embed.test.ts); portal shell reads `?plan`/`?item` and forwards `pdash`/`opcis` for the plans/inbox embeds (+ shell-ui test); rebuild + restart papercusp-cloud-portal.service via the portal's `npm run build` (scripts/build-standalone.mjs → copy-standalone) and verify :3801/:3081 serve the new build. — note: ← WI-2140919 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification and closure\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Operator change live for the portal: `dev:pipeline_position` on the edited files, gate green, :3070 serving it; verdict captures of :3081 `?app=inbox` and `?app=plans` at 1800×1000 and 900×1000 showing list + detail and the narrow fallback; refresh docs/mockups/portal-work-plans-inbox-shipped-*.png; per-item code-truth audit (`plans:audit`). blocked-by: P-003, P-004 — note: ← WI-2140920 blocked (1 external blocker)\n- **P-006** `todo` Acceptance rubric (`rubrics:propose`, kind acceptance) vetted via `consult:get_feedback { policy:'rubric-vetting' }`, independent non-lineage grader, implementer verdict, `plans:set-plan-status shipped`. blocked-by: P-005\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Route 1 — add a split (list + detail) mode to the existing panes behind the portal's full-page routes; keep the iframe embed; do not rebuild native portal surfaces\nDate: 2026-09-01\nContext: the owner-chosen Direction B mockup (docs/mockups/portal-work-plans-inbox.html, chosen [turn:codex:01a059a6-4246-7590-8f29-5c9ae5856183@2026-08-31T17:23:16-04]) is list + detail; the shipped portal faces are single-column because unified-web-portal-2026-08-29 P-098/P-099 framed the chat-sidebar panes unchanged.\n\nMeasured: apps/operator-vite/src/routes/plans.tsx:15-22 and routes/inbox.tsx:15-22 render `<PlansPane />` / `<InboxPane />` inside `.portal-focused-work-surface` with no layout prop; apps/operator/app/globals.css:140-155 only supplies the flex/height chain; apps/operator/app/_components/inbox/InboxPane.tsx:1053-1058 renders OtherDetail INLINE under the selected row; apps/operator/app/_components/plans/PlansPane.tsx:814-816 sets `?pdash` and apps/operator-vite/src/routes/__root.tsx:327 mounts PlanDashboardHost as a full-pane takeover; the portal's packages/contracts/src/index.ts:287-288 registers both as mount:\"embedded-pane\".\n\nDecision: implement the split INSIDE the existing panes as an opt-in `layout=\"split\"` prop used only by the two full-page routes — a column wrapper (display:contents in stack mode so the desktop sidebar is byte-for-byte unchanged in layout) plus a right-hand aside that hosts the SAME detail components (OtherDetail/WorkItemDiscussion; lazy PlanDashboard) driven by the SAME URL params (`opcis`, `pdash`). The root takeover host is skipped on /plans. Deep links are forwarded by the portal (`?plan`/`?item` → `pdash`/`opcis`) through `portalEmbedHref`.\n\nRejected: Route 2 — native portal surfaces rebuilt in the Next app from the board's IR spec. It duplicates the readers and the bulk-run/review flows the embed carried over for free, and the board itself recommended composition. Also rejected: making the split the panes' default — the chat sidebar is ~360px and must keep its stack.\n\nInvariants for every lane: InboxBulkStrip / PlansCleanupStrip behaviour and their persisted runs are untouched (owner requirement, same turn as above); selection stays URL-owned (nuqs); no new data reads — the aside renders what the row click already opened.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"resource-governor-admission-ledger-2026-09-01","title":"Resource-governor admission ledger — remove receipts from work-items","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Resource-governor admission ledger — remove receipts from work-items\nslug: resource-governor-admission-ledger-2026-09-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-01\nupdated: 2026-10-08\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-005/P-007 are held by successor su-455545e0 in owner-directed AUTO. Read current WI-2092046/WI-2092048 checkpoints for dependency evidence and the active completion-wake registration. D-012/D-013 correct the inherited dual-write explanation: the cutover store creates new identities only in the ledger and settles existing legacy receipts. The focused real-PG regression passed (run b2e62f84), and source-conversation re-audit #10 preserved the original durable-only scope and direct implementation route. P-004 remains completed on staging; prior deploy-independent verification and completion audit #9 remain recorded. Only the destructive retirement step requires proof of every actual deployed writer. The release owner has warned that a repair-lineage deployment can omit the governor paths, so a changed SHA alone is insufficient. LIVE_GATE_OPS stays with WI-212675's live holder; this plan continues through one exact completion await without a periodic monitor.\n\n**Next:** On WI-212675 completion or new readiness evidence, verify every active admission-writer runtime and its loaded code, serialize the fresh-watermark seal, reconcile all governed workspaces to zero legacy activity, execute D-009's atomic migration/source retirement, then finish P-007 changed-tree verification, independent grading, audit and verified shipment.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2092040 — Pin the current admission call graph, receipt-id assumptions, migration/boot ordering, legacy writer lifetimes, and reusable Postgres ledger primitives; record the final schema and cutover design as … <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-2092041 — Allocate and author the migration-owned dedicated resource-governor admission ledger, identity/queue/lease indexes, retention fields, and active legacy snapshot/backfill shape; verify schema migratio… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2092042 — Refactor the existing PostgreSQL admission queue store to persist new receipts solely in the dedicated ledger with opaque non-WI identities while preserving AdmissionDriver, DurableAdmissionRecord, q… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-2092044 — Implement the rolling cutover for already-live legacy work-item receipts without duplicate execution: new writes ledger-only, exact legacy settlement compatibility, liveness-safe reconciliation, and … <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-2092046 — Move retention and queue census to the dedicated ledger, remove all legacy payload.resource_governor rows from work_items once safe, and retire work-item-specific receipt GC, claim/goal/carry/fleet e… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-2092047 — Add focused unit and real-PostgreSQL integration recurrence coverage for identity races, state transitions, leases, expiration/abandonment, cancellation, supersession, restart recovery, rolling cutov… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-2092048 — Run current-tree acceptance: migration-wide integration coverage, targeted governor suites, explicit affected-test routing/run, final routed typecheck after the last edit, live staging canaries/censu… <!-- P-007 -->\n## Goal\n\nResource-governor admissions remain durable, idempotent, cancellable, lease-owned, restart-safe, and observable, but never mint or mutate work-items. Agent, process, embedding, and inference admissions use the same existing governor seam backed by a dedicated canonical ledger.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. New admissions must never allocate a work-item identity, insert or update harness_shared.work_items, emit work-item lifecycle events, or participate in work-item claims, assignments, plans, federation, completion, or retention.\n2. Admission persistence must remain durable and fail-closed: a caller receives no accepted receipt unless the canonical record is committed. Workspace + namespace + idempotency key is unique under races.\n3. The existing queued → eligible → leased → running → completed/cancelled/superseded/expired state machine, decision generation/evidence, demand/context metadata, cancellation, result references, lease ownership/CAS, expiry, and abandonment semantics must remain intact.\n4. Agent, process, embedding, and inference admissions must use the same ledger-backed Governor seam with no per-class persistence fork.\n5. A rolling cutover must allow receipts created before deployment to settle exactly once without admitting new work-items or duplicating execution. Compatibility must have a measurable zero-population removal condition.\n6. Queue census, controller inputs, status reads, reconciliation, and terminal retention must read the dedicated ledger and remain bounded/selective under the historical admission rate.\n7. Completion requires zero payload.resource_governor rows in work_items, removal of obsolete receipt-specific work-item machinery, and recurrence tests that fail if either boundary regresses.\n8. Database behavior must be verified against real PostgreSQL migrations and concurrency semantics; final type checking occurs after the last source or test edit.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing resource-governor subsystem at its persistence seam rather than adding another governor. Create one PostgreSQL-canonical harness_shared.resource_governor_admissions table owned by migrations. Each row has a dedicated opaque receipt identity, workspace scope, the existing versioned DurableAdmissionRecord as the single canonical record, and timestamps. Selective unique/expression indexes cover workspace+namespace+idempotencyKey and workspace+namespace+state+age; lease-owner/expiry access is indexed only where the measured queries require it. The table carries no work-item kind, status, assignee, plan, completion, federation, or claim fields and fires no work-item triggers.\n\nPgWorkItemAdmissionQueueStore is replaced by a ledger-backed implementation behind the unchanged DurableAdmissionQueueStore/AdmissionDriver contracts. New identities use a non-WI prefix with collision-resistant generation; receiptId remains opaque to callers. The controller, drainer, status cells, execution wrappers, and agent/process/embedding/inference integrations continue consuming the same typed governor interfaces.\n\nCutover is single-write: after the code flip, new admissions write only the ledger. A bounded legacy adapter recognizes already-existing WI-prefixed receipts and routes only their lookup/settlement to the old row so live pre-cutover leases can finish. It never creates or copies new legacy receipts and is removed after a fresh census proves zero live legacy rows; terminal legacy history is deleted under the existing short retention rule. This avoids dual-write divergence while preserving exactly-once execution during a rolling restart.\n\nRetention and reconciliation move with the store. Once legacy activity is zero, delete remaining governor receipt rows and the old partial indexes, remove receipt-specific work-item GC/exclusions/guards, and retain a structural test scanning production governor code for work_items/next_work_item_id use. Integration tests exercise the real migration, identity race, all state transitions, legacy settlement, restart/expiry, and high-volume bounded queue queries.\n\n## Background\n\nThe resource governor currently writes one harness_shared.work_items row per admission with item_kind='task' and payload.resource_governor. Source comments now classify these rows as ephemeral local queue state and explicitly not work. The mismatch has caused queue pollution, claim/goal/carry/fleet special cases, generic lifecycle corruption, and a prior high-volume database incident. The original reuse-first rationale—reuse the canonical durable substrate rather than create an in-memory queue—remains valid at the Governor API and PostgreSQL layers, but not at the work-item entity boundary.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Add a migration-owned PostgreSQL admission ledger and selective identity/queue/lease indexes.\n- Reuse the existing AdmissionDriver, DurableAdmissionRecord, controller, drainer, state cells, and callers.\n- Give new receipts an opaque non-WI identity.\n- Cut all new governor persistence over to the ledger.\n- Preserve already-live legacy receipt settlement during the rolling cutover, then remove the compatibility path after the legacy population reaches zero or is reconciled safely.\n- Remove legacy payload.resource_governor rows from work_items and retire work-item-specific receipt GC/exclusions once no longer needed.\n- Cover agent, process, embedding, and inference admission classes plus restart, expiry, cancellation, supersession, dedupe, and corruption boundaries.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- No interim work-queue filter or presentation-only stopgap.\n- No second governor API, controller, scheduler, or in-memory queue; this is a persistence backend correction.\n- Schema through an atomically allocated migration .DRAFT, never runtime DDL.\n- New durable state is PostgreSQL-canonical.\n- Generic work-item verbs must never be part of the new receipt lifecycle.\n- Shared-tree edits use explicit manual file locks; git-sync owns commit/push.\n- Tests use the repository's canonical Vitest unit/integration frameworks and real PostgreSQL semantics where the database contract matters.\n- Typecheck runs last over the final complete changed-file set.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- A current-tree source scan and integration test prove no production governor enqueue path writes harness_shared.work_items or allocates next_work_item_id.\n- New admissions for all four live classes persist and settle solely through the dedicated ledger.\n- Identity uniqueness, lease CAS, reconciliation, cancellation, supersession, and restart recovery remain correct.\n- A rolling cutover test proves legacy receipts can settle without duplicating execution while all new writes use the ledger.\n- The canonical work queue contains zero governor admission receipts after migration cleanup.\n- Targeted tests, migration-wide integration coverage, affected tests, and final routed typecheck are green.\n\n## Phase 1 — Durable persistence boundary\n\n- **P-001** `done` Pin the current admission call graph, receipt-id assumptions, migration/boot ordering, legacy writer lifetimes, and reusable Postgres ledger primitives; record the final schema and cutover design as plan Decisions before editing production code. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-2092040 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Allocate and author the migration-owned dedicated resource-governor admission ledger, identity/queue/lease indexes, retention fields, and active legacy snapshot/backfill shape; verify schema migration behavior against real PostgreSQL. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2092041 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Refactor the existing PostgreSQL admission queue store to persist new receipts solely in the dedicated ledger with opaque non-WI identities while preserving AdmissionDriver, DurableAdmissionRecord, queue selection, lease CAS, cancellation, supersession, and reconciliation semantics. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-2092042 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Implement the rolling cutover for already-live legacy work-item receipts without duplicate execution: new writes ledger-only, exact legacy settlement compatibility, liveness-safe reconciliation, and a bounded path to zero legacy active receipts. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-2092044 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `todo` Move retention and queue census to the dedicated ledger, remove all legacy payload.resource_governor rows from work_items once safe, and retire work-item-specific receipt GC, claim/goal/carry/fleet exclusions, mutation guards, indexes, and comments whose only purpose was the old representation. importance: high blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-2092046 released\n- **P-006** `done` Add focused unit and real-PostgreSQL integration recurrence coverage for identity races, state transitions, leases, expiration/abandonment, cancellation, supersession, restart recovery, rolling cutover, all four live admission classes, and the invariant that governor enqueue never writes or allocates work-items. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-2092047 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `todo` Run current-tree acceptance: migration-wide integration coverage, targeted governor suites, explicit affected-test routing/run, final routed typecheck after the last edit, live staging canaries/census, per-item code-truth audit, independent acceptance grading, and ship the plan. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Durable correction only; no interim queue-hiding layer\nDate: 2026-09-01\nOwner directive, 2026-09-01: Avi explicitly selected the durable solution, said the workspace can wait for implementation, rejected a stopgap, enabled AUTO, and selected direct self-implementation. Therefore this plan will not add a temporary list/search/UI exclusion as a deliverable. Existing safety exclusions remain only until the underlying work-item receipt representation is removed.\nRelated: P-001, P-005, P-007\n\n### D-002 — Correct the persistence entity, reuse the governor\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/resource-governor/queue.ts owns the current DurableAdmissionRecord/AdmissionDriver state machine and writes payload.resource_governor into harness_shared.work_items; receipt-gc.ts and scheduler/goal/carry code explicitly classify those rows as local telemetry, not work. Decision: retain and extend the existing Governor API, controller, drainer, state cells, record schema, and caller seams, but move canonical persistence to one dedicated PostgreSQL admission ledger. This is not a second governor or queueing system; it is the correct backing entity for the existing one.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-005\n\n### D-003 — New admission identities are opaque and never WI-prefixed\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: QueueReceipt.receiptId and store interfaces type the receipt identity as string, while the current Pg store alone chooses harness_shared.next_work_item_id(). Decision: the ledger owns a distinct opaque admission-receipt identity; no new receipt allocates a work-item id or claims item_kind='task'. Callers must treat receiptId as opaque, and tests pin that boundary.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-006\n\n### D-004 — Rolling compatibility settles legacy receipts but never accepts new legacy writes\nDate: 2026-09-01\nThe shared staging runtime can carry already-live agent/process leases across a code rollout. Decision: after cutover, all new admissions write only the dedicated ledger. A bounded compatibility path may resolve and settle receipts that already exist in work_items, keyed by their legacy identity and protected against duplicate execution. It is migration plumbing with an explicit zero-population removal condition, not a permanent dual-write or alternative store.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-005 — The migration finishes only when work_items contains no governor receipts\nDate: 2026-09-01\nTerminal retention alone is not completion. The durable boundary is complete only when legacy active receipts have settled or been safely reconciled, payload.resource_governor rows are absent from the canonical work ledger, the old partial indexes/GC/writer are removed, and production source contains no admission enqueue path targeting work_items. Defensive corruption checks may remain only where they protect historical input during the same bounded cutover.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-006 — Exact ledger schema, cross-version cutover guard, and compatibility removal sequence\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: the stable call graph is Governor → WorkItemAdmissionQueueDriver → DurableAdmissionQueueStore. Production PostgreSQL stores are instantiated only by resource-governor/execution.ts (long-lived per-process and dedicated one-shot runtimes), inference-gateway/durable-admission.ts, and the periodic reconciler; callers, QueueReceipt, AdmissionContext, the controller, and drainer carry receiptId only as string. The WI identity assumption is confined to PgWorkItemAdmissionQueueStore, MemoryAdmissionQueueStore test identities, one QueueReceipt comment, work-item release protection/exclusions, receipt GC, migration 986 indexes, and receipt-shaped tests. Live source inspection also found EI-219699 adding ended-owner reclamation and queue census in queue.ts; that behavior is required but its SQL must move to the ledger/store seam.\n\nSchema: add exactly one canonical table, harness_shared.resource_governor_admissions. Its base columns are workspace_id text, receipt_id text DEFAULT ('RG-' || gen_random_uuid()::text), record jsonb, and created_at timestamptz. receipt_id is checked as RG-UUID and the primary key is (workspace_id, receipt_id). Generated stored projections derived only from record — schema_version, namespace, idempotency_key, admission_class, state, priority, coalesce_key, enqueued_at_ms, updated_at_ms, deadline_at_ms, lease_owner, and lease_expires_at_ms — keep DurableAdmissionRecord the single canonical state while making constraints and indexes selective. Checks pin schemaVersion=1, required nonempty identity/class fields, the eight state values, monotone nonnegative timestamps/generation, and lease fields for leased/running rows. Unique (workspace_id, namespace, idempotency_key) is the race arbiter. Partial indexes cover active queue selection/coalescing, active lease expiry/owner reconciliation, queued deadline/abandonment, and terminal retention; no work-item, plan, claim, federation, assignment, completion, or harness issue columns/triggers exist.\n\nIdentity and transactions: new receipts use database-generated RG-UUID identities and never call next_work_item_id(). Reuse boundedOrgTxn plus the existing sorted advisory identity/coalesce locks. Enqueue marks a per-workspace cutover latch in the existing operator_settings KV (reuse-first; no second control table), checks ledger and legacy identity under the same transaction, and inserts only the ledger. A temporary BEFORE INSERT guard on work_items rejects payload.resource_governor inserts once that latch is set, so an old process cannot create a new legacy receipt after the first ledger writer commits. Existing legacy UPDATE settlement remains allowed.\n\nRolling order: (1) additive migration creates the ledger, projections/indexes, and dormant guard; boot/gate migration apply precedes background startup and normally precedes request serving, while failure keeps background work withheld. (2) new store code sets the latch and single-writes ledger; WI-prefixed receipts route only to a bounded legacy adapter. RG receipts never touch work_items. (3) find/cancel checks both stores and refuses a contradictory duplicate; receipt-targeted transitions route by prefix; reconcile/census/ended-owner reclaim union ledger plus pre-cutover legacy until the legacy active count is zero. (4) after a fresh positive-control census proves the latch exists, ledger writes advance, and no new legacy created_at exceeds cutover, delete terminal legacy rows, drop migration-986 indexes/legacy GC and work-item exclusions/guards, remove the adapter and temporary insert trigger, and retain structural + real-PG recurrence tests.\n\nLegacy lifetime: release deployment replaces admission-serving hosts/sidecars, but already-running one-shot operations and 24h agent/process leases may settle afterward. Therefore no bulk deletion of active legacy rows is allowed; settlement is compare-and-set by receiptId + leaseId + owner, explicit ended-owner reclamation may shorten the window, and the compatibility removal condition is measured zero active legacy rows plus zero total payload.resource_governor rows after terminal deletion.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-007 — Rolling overlap rejects collisions, not every old-binary admission\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: after the first staging ledger writer set the workspace latch, three testing:run calls from still-resident operator tool hosts failed with SQLSTATE 23514 even though their identities did not collide with a ledger row. Restarting the embed sidecar did not change the result, proving the global workspace guard crossed independently deployed operator planes. Decision: correct D-006's fail-closed scope. During rolling overlap, an old binary may continue creating a bounded legacy WI receipt when no ledger identity or active coalesce peer conflicts. The trigger rejects only an identity already present in resource_governor_admissions or an active cross-store coalesce collision; shared advisory locks keep those checks ordered. New-code writers remain ledger-only and the composite store continues exact legacy settlement. A separate explicit legacy-writers-retired watermark—not the first-ledger-write latch—must precede terminal deletion and adapter removal. This preserves availability during staging/main overlap without permitting duplicate execution.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-008 — Final legacy deletion is a parked, globally guarded contract migration\nDate: 2026-09-01\nP-005a and migration 1076 must first be committed, applied, and running on every admission-writer plane. Only after markLegacyWritersRetired() has serialized the per-workspace edge and a fresh census reports zero non-terminal legacy receipts may migration 1077 be armed. Migration 1077 remains `.sql.DRAFT` until then and fails closed unless every governed workspace has the retired marker, every legacy workspace has a positive ledger/cutover control, every remaining legacy row is a valid terminal state, and no row is newer than its marker; it holds the work_items table lock across proof and deletion. At that edge the deployed P-005a compatibility reader tolerates zero rows and does not require the legacy indexes/trigger for correctness, so 1077 deletes terminal telemetry rows and drops only the representation-specific indexes/trigger/function. P-006/P-007 must treat an armed 1077 before those proofs as a regression, not a shortcut. Related: P-005, P-006, P-007.\n\n### D-009 — Arm migration 1077 and remove compatibility source in one phase\nDate: 2026-09-01\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/1077-resource-governor-work-item-receipt-retirement.sql.DRAFT` is the only 1077 filename; `packages/operator-core/lib/resource-governor/execution.ts`, `packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/durable-admission.ts`, and `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/periodic-workflows.ts` still instantiate `PgAdmissionCutoverQueueStore`; and `packages/operator-core/lib/resource-governor/admission-ledger-removal-contract.test.ts` passes 3/3 while pinning both phases. Decision: migration 1077 may be renamed to armed `.sql` only in the same source change that swaps every production writer to `PgAdmissionLedgerQueueStore`, deletes the composite/tool compatibility files, and removes every listed work-item exclusion, release guard, storage alarm exemption, and schema-reference artifact. Before that edge the test requires compatibility to remain; after it the test forbids partial cleanup. This implements D-008's database gate as an atomic source contract and governs P-005 through P-007.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-010 — Retirement edge remains closed until a fresh zero-legacy census\nDate: 2026-09-01\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: the scoped papercusp database has 14,668 legacy payload.resource_governor work_items rows (574 non-terminal; newest created_ts=1788281874039), 131,128 ledger rows (30,012 active), only the ledger cutover latch, and no legacy-writers-retired marker. Migrations 1062, 1067, and 1076 are applied; migration 1077 is still parked as .sql.DRAFT. The three production writer callers still instantiate PgAdmissionCutoverQueueStore. Decision: P-005 stays blocked. Do not delete legacy rows, retire compatibility, arm 1077, or remove the cutover store until every writer plane is proven ledger-only, the serialized retirement marker is present, and a fresh census proves zero non-terminal legacy receipts after the live gate owner produces a fresh promotion. This durable decision supersedes any expired short-TTL blocker fact and governs P-005 through P-007.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-011 — P-006 recurrence coverage closes ahead of the P-005 retirement edge\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: 2026-09-01T23:25Z — the ported recurrence integrations use PgAdmissionLedgerQueueStore over test/_admission-ledger-fixture.ts with no work-item allocator: admission-ledger-store.integration.test.ts 23/23 (testing:run 4ab8faf2), p018-rollback-drill.integration.test.ts 4/4 (f0638ad9), governed-test-process-demand.integration.test.ts 2/2 (f43d7eda), p017-profile-matrix.integration.test.ts 72/72 (5a31b402); final routed lint:tsc was clean at23:25:14Z, head5be66dc690. P-006 is complete ahead of P-005: porting this coverage never arms1077, deletes compatibility or purges legacy rows. D-009/D-010 remain unchanged. P-007 cites the ledger suites and fixture for P-006.\n\nCorrection measured 2026-09-05: the previous instruction to delete every remaining test FILE containing PgWorkItemAdmissionQueueStore was overbroad. packages/operator-core/lib/resource-governor/queue.test.ts mixes legacy PostgreSQL cases with shared WorkItemAdmissionQueueDriver tests: stable receipt identity/restart/conflicting replay at:440+, persistence failure, lease/cancel/coalesce behavior, child/parent release feedback, and reconciliation sharing/rejection handling at:689-773. These shared-driver checks must survive the retirement. Remove or port only legacy-store-specific test cases and fixtures; delete whole files only when all their behavior is exclusively the retired store/tool. Keep admission-ledger-removal-contract.test.ts itself: it is the ongoing post-retirement source guard, not disposable legacy coverage. Inspect mixed work-items-release-request.integration.test.ts similarly before pruning it. queue-signal-origin.test.ts is specifically tied to the old work_items insert and must be considered in the final obsolete-test cleanup.\n\nAlso measured: receipt-gc.ts:1-66 already performs bounded terminal retention exclusively against resource_governor_admissions, and periodic-workflows.ts:1967-1989 invokes it. Preserve that ledger GC implementation, its schedule and tests. Retirement removes obsolete WORK-ITEM-specific receipt machinery; it must not remove ledger retention. The final D-009 edit changes the periodic reconciler from composite to ledger-only while keeping terminal GC.\n\nThese corrections preserve the original accepted recurrence/retention requirements. They do not reopen P-006, move the retirement edge earlier, or permit deletion before the all-writer and census preconditions.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-012 — P-005 is gated by the cutover seal's deployed-only precondition, not by P-004 and not by \"the deploy\" generically\nDate: 2026-09-03\nCorrection recorded in D-013 on 2026-09-05: the earlier dual-write explanation was wrong. PgAdmissionCutoverQueueStore.enqueue delegates to PgAdmissionLedgerQueueStore.enqueue. New identities INSERT only into resource_governor_admissions. The work_items UPDATE supersedes an existing legacy coalesce peer; it does not create a legacy receipt. Old independently running binaries can still create legacy receipts during the rolling overlap.\n\nP-004 implementation and its non-final acceptance use staging/current-build and are complete. P-004 has no deployed-main prerequisite; do not reopen it or repeat its completed verification. The narrow retirement prerequisite below belongs to P-005's destructive final compatibility-removal step.\n\nP-005 deployed-only property: every independently executing admission-writer process sharing the governed database creates new identities in the ledger. Staging/current-build cannot prove this property because it cannot establish the loaded write path of a separate deployed process that may still create legacy work_items rows. A cutover-capable build satisfies the new-admission predicate while retaining bounded settlement of existing legacy identities. This is the only release-plane dependency; implementation and ordinary acceptance remain on staging/current-build.\n\nMeasured: source enqueue chain at admission-cutover-store.ts:281-283 and admission-ledger-store.ts:252-313, with adapter at :150-219; focused real-PG test b2e62f84 on 2026-09-05 passed. The first successor runtime inventory and git show comparison identified release build 6e898b6cf8 using PgWorkItemAdmissionQueueStore, while the gateway and staging build identities use the cutover store. The 2026-09-05 namespace census still found recent legacy admissions. These are dated observations, not perpetual state: re-verify actual running writers at the retirement edge.\n\nOnce the writer predicate holds, serialize the retirement marker with the fresh watermark, reconcile active legacy receipts to terminal, verify the positive-controlled zero-active census for every governed workspace, and perform D-009's atomic migration 1077/source retirement. Then finish post-change P-007 acceptance and independent grading. No cleanup, marker or migration arm is justified merely by a staging commit. Preserve the live gate owner's exclusive LIVE_GATE_OPS lane.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-007\n\n### D-013 — Correct D-012: the cutover store creates new receipts only in the ledger; retirement still requires deployed writer proof\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured: 2026-09-05 source read of packages/operator-core/lib/resource-governor/admission-cutover-store.ts:150-154 documents and implements an adapter with no insert method; :281-283 delegates enqueue to this.ledger.enqueue. admission-ledger-store.ts:252-313 returns an existing legacy receipt with created:false and INSERTs new identities only into harness_shared.resource_governor_admissions. The legacy UPDATE at admission-cutover-store.ts:196 operates on already-selected active coalesce peers and sets them superseded; it does not create a legacy admission. Existing integration coverage at admission-cutover-store.integration.test.ts:127-204 proves modern admissions produce RG receipts while work_items contains only the older writer's receipts.\n\nCorrection: D-012's assertion that the CURRENT composite cutover store is a dual-write design that creates legacy rows until the seal is false. New legacy rows require an independently running old writer. Do not treat this.legacy compatibility support, a work_items UPDATE, or the presence of PgAdmissionCutoverQueueStore as proof that a process creates new legacy receipts.\n\nThe safety precondition survives: prove every independent running admission-writer plane uses the ledger enqueue path, then serialize the retirement marker, reconcile legacy receipts to terminal and establish the fresh positive-controlled zero-active census, then perform D-009's atomic migration/source retirement. A running cutover build can satisfy the new-writer predicate while retaining compatibility to settle old identities. No seal, deletion, source retirement or gate operation is authorized by this correction alone. The live gate lane remains with its holder.\nRelated: P-005, P-007\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"session-followup-fixes-2026-09-01","title":"Session follow-up fixes: provenance search and affected guards","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-01","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Session follow-up fixes: provenance search and affected guards\nslug: session-followup-fixes-2026-09-01\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-01\nupdated: 2026-09-01\n---\n## Now\n\nImplement and verify both open follow-ups from session 2c61fbc1, then close their work-items with committed-quality evidence.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-1994990 — Reproduce EI-21985285171148762 after indexing delay, identify whether AskUserQuestion answers are persisted/queryable, implement the smallest durable fix in sessions:search, and add regression covera… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-1994996 — Fix EI-21874072892843451 so AFFECTED_GUARD output preserves workspace/package execution context and consumers cannot run guards at repository root; add regression coverage. <!-- P-002 -->\n## Background\n\nThe recovered session's primary hooks-installation change is complete. Two direct follow-ups remain open: EI-21985285171148762 (AskUserQuestion owner-dialog provenance lookup) and EI-21874072892843451 (AFFECTED_GUARD workspace-aware execution).\n\n## Requirements\n\n- AskUserQuestion answers persisted in a session transcript must be discoverable through the documented owner-dialog/provenance search path after normal indexing; if they are not persisted, the search contract and guidance must state that limitation explicitly.\n- AFFECTED_GUARD results must preserve the workspace/package context required to execute each guard, and supported consumers must not invoke package-local scripts from the repository root.\n- Each fix must include regression coverage exercising the failure direction and focused verification evidence sufficient for terminal work-item closure.\n\n## Design\n\n- Reproduce the provenance issue against a fresh dialog answer after the normal indexing window, then trace the writer and reader. Extend the existing session transcript indexing/search path at the narrowest seam; do not create a parallel provenance store.\n- Extend affected-tests output or consumer handling to carry a structured workspace plus script command (or an equivalent unambiguous runnable representation), and test package-local and root-declared guards while preserving compatibility where practical.\n- Verify each independent item before closing it.\n\n## Phase 1 — Provenance search\n\n- **P-001** `done` Reproduce EI-21985285171148762 after indexing delay, identify whether AskUserQuestion answers are persisted/queryable, implement the smallest durable fix in sessions:search, and add regression coverage. importance: high — note: ← WI-1994990 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Affected guard execution\n\n- **P-002** `done` Fix EI-21874072892843451 so AFFECTED_GUARD output preserves workspace/package execution context and consumers cannot run guards at repository root; add regression coverage. importance: high — note: ← WI-1994996 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n- The two fixes are independent and touch disjoint source areas; each requires regression coverage.\n- Reproduce the provenance gap before choosing a persistence or query fix; do not infer absence from a zero search result.\n- Preserve workspace/package context for every affected guard and make the output directly runnable or structurally consumable.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"silent-halt-owner-rails-acceptance-2026-09-01","title":"Acceptance: silent-halt detection and the owner rail — an agent that stops must be noticed, and the notice must reach someone who can act","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-01","owner":"su-55a5bada-badc-413e-a69e-6e012f6af6f9","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: silent-halt detection and the owner rail — an agent that stops must be noticed, and the notice must reach someone who can act\nslug: silent-halt-owner-rails-acceptance-2026-09-01\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-01\nupdated: 2026-09-02\nowner: su-55a5bada-badc-413e-a69e-6e012f6af6f9\n---\n\n# Acceptance: silent-halt detection and the owner rail — an agent that stops must be noticed, and the notice must reach someone who can act\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation acceptance rubric for plan silent-halt-detection-and-owner-rails-2026-08-08, authored against as-built reality on 2026-09-01. Rev 2 batches the vetting critique (WI-2140767 comment by su-4342525e, 23:09Z) with the author's own meta-rubric pass: symbol/test-title anchors instead of line numbers; structured check:{kind:'tests'} bindings with the DETECTOR assertion named for every bound criterion; C4's probe replaced because lastFiredAt is the instrument this plan's own D-008 declares invalid (claim ≠ fire); C5(c) replaced by the three concrete prohibitions D-005–D-010 actually make; 2×2 thresholds spelled out; numeric floor on C3. SCOPE NOTE — P-004 (checkpoint-harvest title synthesis, 41/41 tests) is a side deliverable of the plan's instrument lane, not an outcome of the silent-halt goal: it is verified by the plans:audit citation on P-004 (grader spot-checks that citation like any other) and is deliberately NOT a criterion here. The plan's goal: every path that silences an agent session pages the OWNER at the silencing instant (D-001), through a rail verified to the pg_notify seam (D-002); the declared-fact drift on agent_fleets.control_state that had turned the halt rescue into a noise source is reconciled fail-safe (D-003, D-012); the rescue is re-enabled under owner authority and actually executing (D-004); no duplicate detector or validator was built — every premise reversal is a measured Decision (D-005–D-010); and the one genuine owner-policy fork is carried as explicit residue rather than silently dropped (D-011). Grade each criterion pass / partial / fail / unknown with the probe named in its method. 'unknown' — never pass — when a probe could not be run, and for ANY testing:run criterion when the router reports TEST_FILE_ROUTE_ERROR or matched=0 (a zero-file batch exits green). GRADER SPOT-CHECKS (class rubric + vetting): (i) testing:run runs the WORKING TREE — before attributing a green to the audited tree, record `git status --porcelain <cited files>` and compare `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` with the blob SHAs the plans:audit stored (auditSeq 2, sha 09b284bd…); a dirty cited file is evidence about the tree, not the candidate; (ii) spot-check at least two audit citations, one of them on the D-008 write path (harness/routines/claim.ts branches; dbos/routines-workflow.ts advance-then-fire order) since that Decision is the plan's load-bearing premise reversal; (iii) before grading, confirm the ship gate sees this rubric — plans:get { slug, shipReadiness:true } — the lifecycle projection reported acceptance.rubricRef null at 23:03Z while rubrics:get showed rev 1 active (projection lag); note what you saw.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"typed-blocker-staging-first-2026-09-01","title":"Enforce staging-first execution for typed blockers","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Enforce staging-first execution for typed blockers\nslug: typed-blocker-staging-first-2026-09-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-01\nupdated: 2026-09-01\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft; implementation and focused verification are present in the canonical staging tree.\n\n**Next:** Activation-audit the owner conversation, start this plan, verify commit authority, and close the implementation item.\n\n## Background\n\nStaging/current-build is the implementation and non-final acceptance plane. Main/:3070/green-checkpoint is the promotion and final-shipment plane. The existing plans:audit guard catches release-plane waits in plan prose, but direct work_items:set_blocker calls could still create a live-dependency gate blocker on ordinary implementation work. That converted a promotion-only condition into a hard development stop.\n\n## Phase 1 — Direct blocker admission\n\n- **P-001** `done` Reuse the existing staging-first classifier at work_items:set_blocker. Reject main/:3070/green-checkpoint/green-pin/production blockers for ordinary implementation items and direct callers to staging/current-build.\n- **P-002** `done` Preserve valid exceptions for actual gate-repair/re-green items, final shipment/promotion/rollback/migration-ordering work, and a named deployed-only property with a concrete staging limitation.\n\n## Phase 2 — Regression and delivery\n\n- **P-003** `done` Add tests for ordinary rejection, gate-repair allowance, deployed-only allowance, and staging-only runtime/deploy blockers.\n- **P-004** `todo` Verify focused tests, scoped TypeScript, staging commit authority, and terminal work-item evidence.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Main-green is promotion-only by default\n\nMain-green, deployed :3070, and live green-checkpoint status are not prerequisites for ordinary implementation or non-final verification. A typed blocker may wait on them only for final/release-plane work or a concrete deployed-only property that staging cannot exercise.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse one policy seam\n\nThe direct blocker writer calls the existing staging-first classifier; no parallel release-plane classifier is introduced.\n\n### D-003 — Separate fact-plane lane\n\nEI-19406121468813407 remains independent fact-cap fairness work and is not part of this plan; it is available for handoff.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"work-queue-resolution-improvement-2026-08-31","title":"Work-queue resolution reliability and efficacy follow-up","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-01","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Work-queue resolution reliability and efficacy follow-up\nslug: work-queue-resolution-improvement-2026-08-31\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-01\nupdated: 2026-09-01\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** DRAFT — follow-up to the shipped work-queue admission/bulk-dedup plan. Planning and verification scope only; no learning-loop settings or schedules are changed.\n\n**Objective:** Preserve the healthy 30-minute admission safety path, make run reporting truthful, make historical bulk dedup resumable, and measure duplicate-removal quality directly.\n\n**Scope:** admission ledger/reporting; census and ratchet attribution; bulk-stage execution; delta sweep and daily digest reliability; fail-open review debt; durable-park metadata; tests, staging canaries, and runbooks.\n\n**Out of scope:** enabling/disabling/rearming/retuning learning loops; clearing parks by age or parker death; unrelated queue cleanup; force-deploying past a red gate.\n\n**Audit baseline (papercusp-workspace / papercusp, 2026-08-31):**\n\n| Run family | Rows | Writer-recorded result | Effect |\n|---|---:|---|---|\n| Promoter ticks | 387 | 173 promoter complete, 20 promoter failed, 194 fail-open complete | 440 normal admissions, 13 confirmed merges, 178 fail-open admissions |\n| Bulk stages | 8 | 2 complete, 5 failed, 1 running | 3,270 judged pairs in completed stages; 0 merges; 60 holds |\n| Census scans | 14 | 12 complete, 1 failed, 1 running | Rebuilt duplicate corpus/shard maps |\n| Delta sweeps | 106 | 88 complete, 18 failed | 43 umbrellas, 144 source links |\n| Daily digests | 14 | 2 complete, 5 blocked, 7 failed | 36 umbrellas, 480 links across successful runs |\n| Durable-park audits | 11 | 10 report-only complete, 1 explicit reconcile complete | Latest audit saw 1,922 parks; reconcile promoted 20 |\n\nThe normal admission path was healthy at measurement: one pending item, about 11 minutes old; 453 promoter-admitted, 167 fail-open unreviewed, and 560 filing-time auto rows. The 1,902 adjudications were 14 r-finding-merge, 1,730 r-related, 154 distinct, and 4 r-remedy-keep.\n\nThe final successful bulk stage reviewed 1,500 pairs, all r-related, and merged none. Its census movement from 20,645 to 18,789 is not proof that 1,856 duplicates were removed. The durable-park held total of 6,952 is a sum of repeated snapshots, not a unique-row count.\n\n**Target outcome:** an audit can answer from the ledger which runs completed, failed, blocked, or remain running; which unique rows/pairs changed; what was rolled back; why a run stopped; and whether confirmed merges meet a quality threshold.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-1979604 — Define and implement writer-recorded run-status classification in the owner-facing report; separate complete, failed, blocked, and running, and label unique rows versus repeated snapshots. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-1979605 — Add explicit attempted/successful/rolled-back/unchanged counters and preserve failure/blocked reasons in the admission ledger projection. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981683 — Add model/account preflight, canary execution, shard checkpoints, idempotent replay, stale-running recovery, and structured transport/protocol failure classification; verify with a staging rerun. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981684 — Create a labeled candidate-pair evaluation set and ratify a merge precision/preservation threshold before enabling destructive bulk merges; report recall and canonical selection. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981687 — Make dependency gates explicit, bound digest prompts/responses, preserve validated partial results, retry transient failures, and make umbrella filing/linking idempotent. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981689 — Give unreviewed admissions a durable re-review state, age SLO, retry owner, and alert; measure re-reviewed, still-open, and terminal outcomes. <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981692 — Require owner/source, reachable release condition, re-evaluation trigger, and evidence for each new park; report unique population and metadata completeness while preserving explicit reconciliation. <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-1981693 — Add focused tests, run a staging canary, and publish a before/after report with unique rows changed, confirmed merges, quality results, failures, and rollback evidence. Do not change learning-loop se… <!-- P-008 -->\n## Background\n\nThe shipped plan delivered born-pending admission, the 30-minute promoter, fail-open liveness, census/sharding, bulk stages, delta sweep, daily digest, durable-park audit, and a stats ledger. This is the evidence-driven follow-up for the gap between mechanical operation and demonstrated cleanup efficacy.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Owner-facing run reports MUST distinguish complete, failed, blocked, and running states using writer-recorded status.\n2. Metrics MUST identify unique rows, pair verdicts, or repeated snapshots and expose attempted, successful, rolled-back, and unchanged outcomes.\n3. Bulk cleanup MUST be resumable, idempotent, provider-aware, and auditable at shard and pair level.\n4. Destructive merges MUST have a labeled precision/preservation gate; a falling census alone MUST NOT count as cleanup.\n5. Delta/digest jobs MUST preserve validated progress, handle dependency gates, bound model payloads, and replay safely.\n6. Fail-open admissions MUST remain liveness-safe while acquiring a measurable re-review path.\n7. Durable parks MUST carry accountable ownership, reachable release conditions, triggers, and evidence.\n8. Verification MUST include focused tests, a staging canary, and a causal before/after report.\n9. This work MUST NOT alter learning-loop settings or schedules.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing admission ledger, census, deduplication, routine-action, and work-item surfaces rather than creating parallel systems. Keep the 30-minute promoter and independent fail-open guard separate. Add status/counter fields at existing ledger writers, shard checkpoints and idempotency keys for bulk replay, and a labeled evaluation gate before destructive merges. Make umbrella writes idempotent, model fail-open review debt as lifecycle metadata, and require park accountability. Roll out on staging first.\n\n## Phase 1 — Truthful run and queue reporting\n\nNormalize owner-facing projections around writer-recorded status (complete, failed, blocked, running), not finished_at alone. Label counters as unique rows, pair verdicts, or repeated snapshots. Add attempted, successful, rolled-back, and unchanged fields and preserve failure/blocked reasons.\n- **P-001** `done` Define and implement writer-recorded run-status classification in the owner-facing report; separate complete, failed, blocked, and running, and label unique rows versus repeated snapshots. importance: high — note: ← WI-1979604 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Add explicit attempted/successful/rolled-back/unchanged counters and preserve failure/blocked reasons in the admission ledger projection. importance: high — note: ← WI-1979605 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Reliable, resumable bulk execution\n\nAdd model/account preflight, a small canary, shard-level checkpoints, idempotent replay, stale-running recovery, and structured transport/protocol classification. Never re-send an oversized batch or discard successful shards. Record the actual model and account route. Run a controlled staging rerun before production cleanup.\n- **P-003** `done` Add model/account preflight, canary execution, shard checkpoints, idempotent replay, stale-running recovery, and structured transport/protocol failure classification; verify with a staging rerun. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-1981683 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Direct efficacy and precision measurement\n\nCreate a labeled candidate-pair set before rerun. Track duplicate-only precision, non-duplicate preservation, merge count, canonical selection, adjudication coverage, and estimated recall. Require a ratified merge-quality threshold (proposed default: at least 98% precision on labeled auto-merge pairs) before destructive merges. Keep r-related, distinct, r-remedy-keep, and r-finding-merge separate.\n- **P-004** `done` Create a labeled candidate-pair evaluation set and ratify a merge precision/preservation threshold before enabling destructive bulk merges; report recall and canonical selection. blocked-by: P-003 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-1981684 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Delta sweep and digest reliability\n\nMake dependency gates explicit and event-driven where possible. Bound digest prompt/response sizes, preserve validated partial results, retry transient failures, and make umbrella filing/linking idempotent. Report successful, blocked, and failed runs separately with coverage/link checks.\n- **P-005** `done` Make dependency gates explicit, bound digest prompts/responses, preserve validated partial results, retry transient failures, and make umbrella filing/linking idempotent. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-1981687 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Fail-open review debt\n\nRetain fail-open admission so a dead promoter cannot starve the queue, but give unreviewed rows a durable re-review state, age SLO, retry owner, and alert. Measure re-reviewed, still-open, and terminal outcomes. Fail-open is temporary admission, not a final review decision.\n- **P-006** `done` Give unreviewed admissions a durable re-review state, age SLO, retry owner, and alert; measure re-reviewed, still-open, and terminal outcomes. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-1981689 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 6 — Durable-park accountability\n\nRequire each new park to carry an accountable owner/source, reachable release condition, concrete re-evaluation trigger, and evidence. Report unique park population and metadata completeness. Keep reconciliation explicit and decision-backed; never clear solely due to age or parker death.\n- **P-007** `done` Require owner/source, reachable release condition, re-evaluation trigger, and evidence for each new park; report unique population and metadata completeness while preserving explicit reconciliation. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-1981692 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 7 — Verification and rollout\n\nAdd tests for status classification, census causal attribution, resumable stages, retry bounds, digest gating, fail-open re-review, and park metadata. Verify on staging with a canary corpus, then publish a before/after report containing unique rows changed, confirmed merges, quality results, failures, and rollback evidence. Do not alter learning-loop configuration.\n- **P-008** `done` Add focused tests, run a staging canary, and publish a before/after report with unique rows changed, confirmed merges, quality results, failures, and rollback evidence. Do not change learning-loop settings. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-1981693 completed (done)\n\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Reports distinguish complete, failed, blocked, and running; completed cannot include failures or blocks.\n- No stale running bulk stage remains without an owner, recovery action, or explicit disposition.\n- Each rerun records actual model/account, shard coverage, retries, protocol failures, writes, rollbacks, and pair outcomes.\n- Destructive merge is gated by the labeled precision/preservation threshold.\n- Census before/after includes a causal write delta; a census decrease alone is never reported as duplicates removed.\n- Digest/delta reports expose success, blocked, and failure counts and pass idempotent replay/coverage tests.\n- Unreviewed rows have a measurable re-review path and age/terminal outcomes.\n- Park reports use unique populations and show owner/condition/trigger/evidence completeness.\n- Focused tests and a staging canary pass; no learning-loop setting changes occur.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Keep this follow-up separate from learning-loop work\n\nThe owner redirected the audit to the work-queue bulk resolver. This plan does not enable, disable, rearm, or retune learning loops.\n\n### D-002 — Status truth comes from the writer-recorded state\n\nA non-null finished_at is insufficient because failed and blocked actions also finish. Use detail.status, with running as the fallback where appropriate.\n\n### D-003 — Census movement is not a cleanup KPI by itself\n\nThe census counts unadjudicated high-similarity pairs and can change with corpus/edge activity. A cleanup claim requires a causal stage write delta plus adjudication outcomes.\n\n### D-004 — Destructive merges require a quality gate\n\nAn r-finding-merge terminalizes a duplicate row. Do not enable a new bulk rollout until the labeled precision and preservation checks pass.\n\n### D-005 — Fail-open is a liveness safety valve, not final review\n\nUnreviewed rows remain claimable by design, but must be tracked as review debt and revisited.\n\n### D-006 — Durable parks release only by stated condition\n\nAge, parker death, or model opinion is not sufficient to clear a durable park.\n\n### D-007 — Ratified v1 merge-quality gate and independent label boundary\nDate: 2026-09-01\nMeasured: `harness_shared.dedup_adjudications` in papercusp-workspace/papercusp has 1,902 rows; every `judged_by` value is a model id and zero rows carry `labelSource` or `reviewedBy` evidence. The existing verdicts are therefore predictions, not independent ground truth.\n\nThe v1 merge-quality gate uses a versioned, frozen, independently labeled pair corpus in source. It does not insert labels into `dedup_adjudications`, because any row there permanently retires a production pair from the census. Gate reports extend the existing `admission_runs` stage envelope; no parallel run ledger or label table is introduced.\n\nFor every non-empty bulk root, the same model, duplication-only prompt, parser, and deterministic canonical selector used for production must first replay the labeled corpus. Destructive persistence remains fail-closed unless all of these pass: 100% adjudication coverage; at least 98% duplicate-only precision; 100% non-duplicate preservation; at least 90% duplicate recall (anti-vacuity); and 100% canonical-selection accuracy. The corpus must contain at least 8 merge-positive and 12 non-merge cases across distinct, r-related, and r-remedy-keep. Metrics and thresholds are persisted with the dataset version/hash, model, served account, verdict counts, and failure reasons. Empty/no-pair canaries may bypass the model replay because no destructive write is reachable.\n\nAny dataset, prompt, model, or threshold change invalidates the prior gate result and requires a fresh replay. A failed, incomplete, stale, or absent result blocks merges before `persistAdmissionPlan`; it is never converted to a hold or fail-open merge.\nRelated: P-004\nRatified: Avi via owner-directed AUTO on 2026-09-01\nRelated: P-004\n\n## Verification notes\n\nSource writers inspected: packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-admission-promoter.ts; work-items-admission-bulk-dedup.ts; work-items-admission-census.ts; work-items-admission-delta-sweep.ts; work-items-admission-daily-digest.ts; work-items-durable-park-audit.ts; and the corresponding routine actions. Live evidence came from harness_shared.admission_runs, harness_shared.dedup_adjudications, and harness_shared.work_items.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-effort-scoped-continuity-2026-09-02","title":"Acceptance — effort-scoped continuity: was the mechanism built and verified, and does the card say plainly what it could not measure?","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-02","owner":"su-abb373d6-a2a1-4f96-85e0-4e2641bc42ac","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — effort-scoped continuity: was the mechanism built and verified, and does the card say plainly what it could not measure?\nslug: acceptance-effort-scoped-continuity-2026-09-02\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-09-02\nowner: su-abb373d6-a2a1-4f96-85e0-4e2641bc42ac\n---\n\n# Acceptance — effort-scoped continuity: was the mechanism built and verified, and does the card say plainly what it could not measure?\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nREVISION 3. Rewritten against TWO independent vettings: su-d939052a on conv-mtkhxemi (2026-09-02T19:39Z) and su-55a5bada on WI-2142352 post 80933 (2026-09-02T20:03Z). Their findings became plan decisions D-015 and D-016. Five defects were real and are fixed here.\n\nFROM THE FIRST VETTING (D-015). (1) THE TITLES OVERCLAIMED: revision 1 asked behavioural questions while offering only code and tests as evidence. A criterion asking whether the mechanism WORKED ON THE POPULATION cannot be graded now and must be rated `unknown`; one asking whether it was BUILT AND VERIFIED can be graded now, and deploying adds nothing to it. Criteria 1-6 are therefore phrased as the mechanism questions they actually test, and the behavioural question is made explicit and UNMEASURED in criterion 7 — rather than keeping behavioural titles over code evidence, which is the trap itself. (2) THE SELF-AUDIT WAS SELF-SERVING: it could pass by disclosure while other criteria read `healthy` on absent evidence. Criterion 7 now has teeth over the rest of the card. (3) UNBOUNDED ABSENCES ARE UNGRADEABLE: a grader can only report what their search did not find, which is a statement about the search. Criteria 5 and 6 name the LOCI where the absence must hold, each with a positive control proving the file was read.\n\nFROM THE SECOND VETTING (D-016), which corroborated the deploy position from its own independent measurements rather than from this plan's record. (4) A BLOB CITATION IS BLIND TO DEPLOYMENT STATE BY CONSTRUCTION, so a criterion graded on cited blobs cannot distinguish 'the remedy landed' from 'the remedy is in force'. D-015 fixed the rating vocabulary but did not require the card to say WHERE the graded code is. EVERY criterion graded without live behavioural evidence must therefore record the DEPLOYMENT POSITION of its cited paths — one dev:pipeline_position read per cited path — as part of its evidence. The same structural hole was found on an unrelated plan's rubric two hours earlier (silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01-acceptance, WI-2142322 post 80916), making it a condition of the tree rather than a quirk of this plan. (5) NO CARRY-COVERAGE NUMERAL APPEARS ON THIS CARD, not even as a forbidden example: D-014 already forbade reporting it as this plan's delta, and the residual risk is a grader IMPORTING it as a baseline precisely because it would be the only number in view.\n\nRE-GRADE TRIGGER — NAMED HERE, NOT IN A SIDE NOTE, because unnamed 'graded pre-deploy' silently becomes 'graded'. THIS CARD'S VERDICT IS PROVISIONAL. Criteria 1-6 can today be graded only against code and tests. They are RE-GRADED once the green-checkpoint gate greens and this change actually deploys, riding the same trigger as the owed post-deploy re-measure on WI-2142309.\n\nGRADER CONTEXT: the implementation is COMMITTED AND ON STAGING BUT NOT DEPLOYED (:3070 runs the release checkout; the gate is red at ~99 consecutive reds, verdict stale, ownership held elsewhere on WI-212675). Per D-014 the plan's live-adoption metrics are structurally zero and must NOT be read as the mechanism failing; per D-015 they must NOT be read as the mechanism working either. Grade criteria 1-6 against CODE AND TESTS, which is the evidence that exists and is sufficient for the questions they now ask — and record the deployment position alongside.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for frozen-candidate-freeze-actually-holds-2026-09-02, authored AFTER implementation against as-built code. The goal is not 'add a hold branch' — it is that a frozen red candidate stops being thrown away whenever the auto-fixer cannot be dispatched, that the hold is OWNED and BOUNDED and STILL CONVERGING, that its state is legible without log archaeology, and — the point of all of it — that frozen candidates actually get RESUMED. Three predecessor plans shipped 33 done items with zero acceptance rubrics while the resume counter sat at zero (20 retirements / 0 resumes in a day) and nobody noticed.\n\n⚠ GRADING PRECONDITION, applies to EVERY criterion graded from a LIVE reading: record the BUILD IDENTITY of the writer (observedRuntimeSha / deployBuildIdentity / deployed sha), not just the values. Repair-queue and gate_health rows are written by the RUNNING gate, and on this box the deployed operator serves the GREEN release checkout — which, while the gate is red, can faithfully report PRE-FIX code indefinitely. The subject under test IS the gate, so this is circular by construction: a live reading that looks wrong is either (i) pre-fix code still deployed — evidence the fix has not SHIPPED, not that it is wrong — or (ii) post-fix code and a real regression. The values alone cannot separate those two, and they demand opposite responses. A criterion graded green against code predating the fix is the most expensive false pass available on this plan.\n\nGRADING ORDER: criterion `freeze-state-and-reason-are-a-read` is graded FIRST. `a-held-freeze-always-has-a-live-owner` depends on it — if the freeze's state and owner are not readable, that criterion is UNMEASURED, never pass, because a grader who can read nothing finds no orphaned freeze and would otherwise score it green on absence of evidence.\n\nREV 2 (self-vetting): the field criterion could not FAIL — its method let an unmet precondition score as pass; now requires `unknown`. The hold criterion covered 'the queue survives' but not 'still re-verified against repairHead'. The bound criterion did not require the bound to exceed the stall window it gates.\nREV 3: bound every objectively-checkable criterion to the tests that decide it (meta-rubric D-006).\nREV 4 (vetting, su-d939052a): ownership de-pinned from module names to the observable orphan signature; field criterion moved onto `candidateSource`, measurable without waiting; hold and bound MERGED into one criterion that discriminates a transient wall from a dead end through the same predicate; added the affirmative resumes>0 criterion that six negative guards were all missing.\nREV 5 (vetting, su-55a5bada, contesting rev 4's own fix): (1) the affirmative criterion as written REINTRODUCED the same hole mirrored — resumes==0 cannot distinguish 'never resumes' from 'nothing needed resuming' — so it now grades a RATIO with an explicit denominator (freezes_opened / resumes_attempted / resumes_completed), yielding a defined verdict in every world instead of only lucky ones, with freezes_opened>0 AND resumes_attempted==0 as a HARD FAIL because that is literally the 20/0 signature. (2) it must not depend on production traffic — a forced positive control is required, since a criterion satisfiable only when the right failure happens to occur is a wish about traffic, not a property of the system. (3) the build-identity precondition above. (4) the 4-depends-on-5 grading order above.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-lateral-fleet-coordination-2026-09-02","title":"Acceptance — lateral fleet coordination: the star topology question answered, and the one surviving change bought inside the owner's context budget","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-02","owner":"su-d341b62f-08fb-497b-8191-ccfcd5673078","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"remote","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — lateral fleet coordination: the star topology question answered, and the one surviving change bought inside the owner's context budget\nslug: acceptance-lateral-fleet-coordination-2026-09-02\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-09-02\nowner: su-d341b62f-08fb-497b-8191-ccfcd5673078\n---\n\n# Acceptance — lateral fleet coordination: the star topology question answered, and the one surviving change bought inside the owner's context budget\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nThe plan asked whether the leader-hub messaging star is a defect and, if so, what to do about it. Its answer turned out to be NO (D-001, D-003), which makes this plan unusual to grade: most of its value is in what it correctly did NOT build, and a grader who only looks for shipped code will mis-score it. The criteria below therefore trace to what the plan PROMISED — settle the question, and let nothing through that spends member context budget without earning it — rather than to the one diff that landed. D-001 is the binding constraint throughout: the owner ruled that low fleet-wide message volume is deliberate, that member context budget is the thing being protected, and that new lateral traffic is defensible only where a specific message prevents more context cost than it creates. Graded by a NON-implementer, alongside the plan-class-feature-ship invariants.\n\nREV 2 incorporated two independent vettings (consult conv-mtkg9obc-0000-d6cadb80b9974f4d8977bc0bb59f6014). Reviewer 1 (su-d939052a) found a title/method disagreement on the cost criterion and an uncontrolled delegated measurement; reviewer 2 (su-93c2dec6) adjudicated the first as a RETITLE (declining the decisiveness leg as post-hoc causal reconstruction — the least reliable thing a rubric can ask for), hardened the positive control with two further clauses, and raised the two-plane (staging vs serving) hazard. The criterion formerly keyed `cost-constraint-actually-bound-the-outcome` was renamed accordingly — its old key claimed causation the method never tested.\n\nREV 3 closes the gap the meta-rubric's `prefer-structured-check` names: the two code-bound criteria were prose-only while a test file with permanent wrong-implementation controls already decides them, so both now carry a `kind:'tests'` structured check that scorecards:emit RUNS at grading time. The three record-bound criteria stay prose because no test decides them.\n\nSTANDING RULE FOR EVERY CRITERION BELOW: a measurement that cannot be made is `unknown` — never pass, never fail. Repo-relative paths are qualified with their checkout (`papercusp/...`) because ~50 sibling checkouts share this workspace and a bare path fails every same-repo probe exactly like a fabricated one.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data).
