Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nAuthored against as-built reality after all six items reached terminal state, then revised twice — once on my own review, once on vetting feedback from su-d939052a (consult conv-mtjodm72). The plan's claim is that the root volume's dominant reclaimable consumer was gateway_payload_blobs TOAST bloat (60.59 GiB of TOAST over 0.78 GiB of live payload) rather than the VM images the prior record blamed, that reclaiming it returns more headroom than the volume needs, and that the failure class is then guarded so it cannot silently recur. These criteria grade that claim as an OUTCOME. They trace to the plan goal and to D-001 (VM images out of scope), D-002 (reclaim under a lock_timeout guard), D-003 (the PG16 cluster is unreferenced but deliberately not reclaimed) and D-004 (the bloat is already re-accumulating, so the reclaim is a mitigation and the detector is the load-bearing fix).\n\nTHREE THINGS A GRADER SHOULD REFUSE TO ACCEPT. (1) A `df` percentage as evidence for criterion 1: the gate's admission decision is a specific code composition, and running it differs from reading a percentage. (2) Any framing that treats the reclaim as having SOLVED the problem — D-004 measures the TOAST relation regrowing at ~0.8 GiB/hour, so a completion reading as 'fixed' rather than 'mitigated, with a guard that fires in time' has misdescribed the outcome. (3) For criterion 7, the PRESENCE of a disclosure sentence as evidence the caveat is still true — that is the author witnessing their own write. Each of the four residues must be independently re-verified at grading time.\n\nCLASS CHOICES, MADE DELIBERATELY. Criterion 3 is violatable rather than settle-once: its subject is partly a RECORD, and a record can drift back — any future writer can re-file the VM-images diagnosis, so the property must keep holding, not merely have held once. Criterion 7 is violatable for the same reason: the requirement is that the record STAYS honest, so a later edit stripping a caveat should falsify it permanently. Criterion 4 alone is settle-once, because it grades a single completed action that cannot un-happen.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nSCOPE FOR THE GRADER. This plan (a) extracted Overview/HUD/Work/Learning into first-class cloud-portal rail destinations, (b) moved steering + Papercup chat into OUTER-shell sidebars framing chromeless operator pane routes (/portal-panes/steering, /portal-panes/chat), (c) retired the single 'Papercusp' rail destination via a forward-only migration that DELETES persisted rows, (d) unified favicon + rail mark behind one constant, (e) rebuilt and redeployed the portal standalone. It spans TWO independent git repositories, so plans:audit code-verifies only the papercusp-side items; portal-side items are recorded not-code with alternative evidence.\n\nREAD THIS BEFORE RATING: an all-pass is FORECLOSED by design. Criterion 2's drift markers require the known soft-404 sidebars to be rated a shortfall rather than excused as disclosed, so while EI-22126055661840542 is open, criterion 2 cannot be rated pass by this rubric's own terms. That is intended. Plan Decision D-002 records the conscious choice to ship with that rated non-pass, with measured evidence that the fix requires a different service's release gate (red across 89 consecutive runs, already claim-held under WI-212675). Do NOT soften criterion 2 to produce an all-pass; rate it on its merits and expect the acceptance verdict to carry the shortfall.\n\nRevision 5, after independent vetting by TWO reviewers (su-d939052a, su-a961ddec; consult conv-mtjntdhc). Reviewer 1 fixes: a process-originated observable for 'actually serving'; an additive-only disclosure criterion closing a relocation loophole; an outcome-shaped brand title; a new migration data-safety criterion. Reviewer 2 fixes: criterion 1's method no longer asserts GLOBAL zero-occurrence of the brand name (which manufactured a false failure on legitimate uses like document.title); criterion 5 also rates the CROSS-SERVICE build dependency; this description exists; criterion 6 is marked violatable; and methodRef is set. Reviewer 2's contest — that the soft-404 collides with criterion 1's 'routes nowhere' — was checked and CONCEDED by its author: `ls apps/operator-vite/src/routes/portal-panes/` is exactly chat.tsx and steering.tsx, so the failing routes are the SIDEBARS, not any rail surface.\n\nBINDING NOTE: criterion 3 carries a structured tests check with named detectors (verified green, 9/9, both paths resolve). The other six are deliberately prose-only for a stated structural reason — criteria 1/4/6 are decided by portal-repo tests whose paths cannot resolve against this repo's citation root (binding them would be a path that does not resolve, itself a drift marker), and criteria 2/5 are decided by observations of a LIVE two-service deployment that no unit test can make. Rollback/recovery for the standalone portal redeploy is an EXPLICIT CUT recorded as plan Decision D-001.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). P-011 is rated `missing` — revised DOWN from `partial` on direct code truth after two peers independently corroborated that coord:dispatch reaches only the retired mug tier. P-008 is `missing`. P-010 is `dropped` as superseded, so the headline must not read as if six verbs were retired. One item (WI-7421) is closed with zero completion evidence on any surface (EI-22173645305713341), and one (WI-37365) was closed 'committed' on evidence its own author retracted as FALSE (EI-22175397357614106).\n\nA `pass` on every criterion is evidence you have not checked, not evidence the plan is good.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan facts-require-explicit-expiry-2026-09-02, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality, then REVISED once following vetting (consult conv-mtkdsrjq, su-d939052a). Grade OUTCOMES, not the presence of code.\n\nSCOPE IS DELIBERATELY NARROWED TO THE WRITE BOUNDARY. The plan's original goal read 'no fact may be written with a lifetime nobody chose'. Vetting established that this rubric cannot honestly certify that goal, because expiry is not the only way a fact dies: at the per-scope cap a routine peer assert EVICTS live facts regardless of the expiry their author explicitly chose (measured 2026-09-02 ~17:31Z — one assert evicted 16 workspace facts; two confirmed gone with expiresAt 2026-09-08, six days of chosen life left; the cap refuses eviction only for confidence:'verified' victims). That is the same defect class relocated from the write boundary to the cap. It is NOT this plan's to fix and was filed as EI-22172733057985514, which has since been INVESTIGATED and CLOSED: the eviction itself is real, but the half of that report claiming the evicted fact's author is never notified is DISPROVEN - notifyEvictedFactOwners() (agent-facts/notify-evicted.ts, awaited from assertFact at store.ts:2122) informs them and orient surfaces factEvictionDisclosures, so the residual is a DISCLOSED override of a chosen lifetime, not silent loss. So this rubric certifies the WRITE BOUNDARY explicitly, and criterion 7 grades whether that residual is named honestly rather than papered over.\n\nNOTE FOR THE GRADER: do NOT grade criterion 1 by the kind=NULL share. That was the plan's own stated acceptance test and it is falsified AS AN INSTRUMENT (a compliant ttlSec write stays kind=NULL forever, so it would read a correct implementation as a failure) — see D-001/D-003. Criterion 6 makes that a property you RUN rather than a claim you believe.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nALL SIX ITEMS TERMINAL, PLAN DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED — see D-003. Implementation landed and is code-truth audited (plans:audit completion seq 3, auditedSha 96c9def1, 5 of 6 items verified; the rubric item is not-code by construction). Independent grading by su-1899608f, outside the implementer lineage, against rubric rev 5: bespoke card EI-22174370371911157 = 3 healthy / 3 unknown / 0 broken; class card EI-22174565974510550 (plan-class-feature-ship) = 4 pass, gate-green-shipped FAIL, docs PARTIAL. Implementer acceptance verdict EI-22174803419780885 = REJECT, meaning NOT-YET-VALIDATED rather than defective. Every code-truth criterion passed: the capacity preflight derives its provider and fails open; one predicate discriminates a transient wall from a genuine dead end, bounded and still converging; freeze state and reason are a read that fails closed and reaches prose. All three unknowns share ONE cause — the DEPLOYED gate is sha 6e898b6cf8, which predates this plan's fixes, so the mechanism the plan exists to build has never executed in production. A freeze was held during grading (candidate 1f43e05a, repairHead ef0d2c06 advanced past it, attempts=1, opened 16:07:28Z) carrying NO freezeAndConverge disposition and NO frozen-repair-convergence condition item, because the shipped code is not the running code. The forced positive control IS satisfied and was re-verified independently by the grader (green-checkpoint.test.ts:1558 drives freeze then repair then resume, end to end). Blocked on DEPLOY, not on code: gate red at 99, main behind staging, WI-212675 held by su-a7410503.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Do NOT ship on code truth alone (D-003). Wait for main to go green and fast-forward to a staging commit carrying this plan's fixes, confirm the gate writing the readings reports THAT sha rather than the pre-fix 6e898b6cf8, then count ONE real freeze-to-resume (resumes_completed >= 1, naming candidate, run, and what it converged from) with no run re-cutting at tip while a red freeze was open — then supersede EI-22174803419780885 with an accept card and ship. Follow-up work-item: WI-2142105. Do NOT revise the rubric to make the unknowns gradeable; that un-counts both independent cards and the meta-attestation.)\n\n## Background\n\n### What the owner was told, and what was actually true\n\nThree plans were marked `shipped`. Every one carries the same lifecycle verdict — *\"no acceptance rubric is active — the validation path has not begun. Implementation landing is not the same as a finished plan.\"*\n\n| plan | status | items | rubric |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `gate-stop-chasing-the-tip-2026-08-19` | shipped | 11 done | **none** |\n| `converge-frozen-candidate-by-fix-only-admission-2026-08-27` | shipped | 12 done, 1 dropped | **none** |\n| `frozen-candidate-compliance-enforcement-2026-08-30` | shipped | 10 done | **none** |\n\n33 implementation items, zero independent validation. This is exactly the failure the project conventions lead with: **\"ALL ITEMS TERMINAL IS NOT A FINISHED PLAN.\"** The agents were not lying — they shipped implementation. \"Shipped\" here meant \"every item is done\", not \"the system demonstrably works\".\n\n### The evidence that would have caught it was blocked by the bug itself\n\n`frozen-candidate-outlives-its-repair-2026-08-27` is still `draft`, 3 of 7 items live, last activity 4 days ago. Its **P-001 is `blocked`**, and its own note says why:\n\n> *\"Blocked on OBSERVABILITY, not on effort: reuse-vs-skip is only measurable during a repair RE-verification (attempts >= 1, after a fixer has run).\"*\n\nA repair re-verification requires `attempts >= 1`. Attempts only increment when a fixer is actually dispatched. The dispatch has been failing the capacity preflight and retiring the queue at `attempts === 0` — so the measurement that would have exposed the defect was gated behind the defect. That is why days of work could look finished: nobody ever observed a frozen candidate being resumed, because it never was.\n\n### Root cause, measured 2026-09-02\n\n**Layer 1 — the gate could not see where the fixer runs.** `checkFixerProviderCapacity()` resolved its provider as `process.env.PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_FIXER_PROVIDER || \"codex\"` — a hand-maintained literal whose own comment conceded it (*\"the fixer's backend is NAMED here rather than derived\"*). A derived-truth-ladder violation at rung 4 where rung 1 was available. Consequence: when the owner moved `release-fixer` to `claude-opus-5:xhigh` on `claude-code`, the preflight kept measuring the weekly-exhausted codex pool. A config-only switch was a silent no-op — config and gate disagreeing, gate winning, nothing reported.\n\n**Layer 2 — the retire predicate conflates two different claims.** At the `dispatch-fixer` decision, a capacity hold on a queue that is `awaiting-fixer` / `attempts === 0` / unassigned is treated as *\"structurally unable to resolve this frozen candidate\"*, so the queue is retired and the run falls through to the staging tip. But \"the AUTO-FIXER cannot be dispatched\" is not \"this queue is unreachable-green\": agents and humans converge onto frozen candidates routinely, and the adjacent WI-2141347 branch already handles a repairHead an agent converged — so the code demonstrably knows agent convergence happens; it just does not count it as a reason to keep the freeze. Retiring re-admits the whole fleet sweep at the next tip, which is precisely the treadmill D-007 diagnosed.\n\n**Layer 3 — it fails silently.** The only evidence that freeze-and-converge had been off for an entire day was grepping run logs. No gate surface reports it.\n\n### Why the failing count is not monotonic\n\nEach re-cut at tip re-admits every commit landed since. The 14:27Z run reports `commitsBehindTip=22`, `rangeFilesChanged=36`. Per-run the suite is overwhelmingly green (40,654 tests passed, 3 failed), so this is a convergence problem, not a quality problem: a tiny failing set never reaches zero because the candidate moves underneath it.\n\n## Phase 1 — make the freeze hold\n\n- **P-001** `done` Derive the release-fixer's provider from the agent-config row the dispatch actually launches on, instead of a hardcoded `\"codex\"` literal. Precedence env-override > derived > old literal; fail OPEN on every unknown so an unreadable config can never masquerade as a measured wall. — note: landed; resolveReleaseFixerProvider() in green-checkpoint.ts, 5 regression tests, existing preflight tests still green, lint:tsc clean.\n- **P-002** `done` Stop retiring a zero-attempt frozen queue on a TRANSIENT provider-capacity hold. Hold the freeze and keep testing repairHead so agent/human convergence still advances the candidate, bounded so a queue nobody converges cannot pin the gate forever. Retire only on genuine unreachable-green. — note: ← WI-2141797 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` When the freeze is held with no dispatchable fixer, ROUTE the repair to agents rather than leaving it unowned: file/refresh one unassigned convergence work-item naming the frozen candidate, its failing set, and the converge call — so agents fix the frozen candidate instead of fixing at tip. — note: ← WI-2141805 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Surface freeze-and-converge state and its REASON on the gate surfaces (release:deploy status / gate_health), so \"the freeze is currently OFF because X\" is a read, not archaeology across run logs. — note: ← WI-2141798 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Regression tests for P-002/P-003/P-004, including the falsifier that matters: a capacity-held zero-attempt queue must SURVIVE the run rather than be retired. — note: Regression tests landed with each item rather than as a trailing batch. The named falsifier exists and is exercised: green-checkpoint.test.ts 'HOLDS a STALLED zero-attempt queue when the measured wall OUTLASTS the stall window' is the exact twin of the pre-existing retire test (identical 16-min queue and moved tip; only the wall length differs), asserting the queue SURVIVES the run — plus its bound, 'the convergence hold is BOUNDED'. Also: 15/15 frozen-repair-agent-routing (incl. the ACTIONABLE_CONDITIONS opt-in guard + a near-miss control), 11/11 freeze-disposition (incl. a positive control), P-003/P-004 negative controls on the fresh-hold and retire paths. Totals 16:47Z: 503/503 green-checkpoint.test.ts, 92/92 queue, lint:tsc clean.\n\n## Phase 2 — validation this plan must not skip\n\n- **P-006** `done` Author the post-implementation acceptance rubric against as-built reality, vet it, and route it to a NON-implementer grader. This is the step all three predecessor plans omitted, and omitting it is why the owner was told the system worked while it had never once resumed a frozen candidate. — note: ← WI-2141879 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — \"The auto-fixer cannot be dispatched\" is NOT \"this queue is unreachable-green\"\nDate: 2026-09-02\nRULING, binding on any lane that touches the frozen repair queue: a measured provider-capacity wall on a zero-attempt queue is a statement about the AUTO-FIXER's availability, not about the candidate's reachability. Retire a frozen queue only on genuine unreachable-green.\n\nWhy this needed a ruling rather than just a fix: the two claims were conflated in one predicate, and the conflation was invisible because both produce the same immediate action (retire). Measured 2026-09-02: the fixer's provider was walled for six days, so every queue stalled after 15 minutes, retired, and re-cut at tip — 20 retirements and 0 resumes in one day, with freeze-and-converge silently off fleet-wide. Retiring bought nothing (the next queue hit the same wall 15 minutes later) and cost the entire convergence property.\n\nAgents and humans converge onto frozen candidates routinely, and the code already knew this — the WI-2141347 converged-repairHead branch exists precisely to test a head one of them advanced. It simply did not count agent convergence as a reason to KEEP the freeze.\n\nCONSEQUENCES other lanes must honour:\n- Do not treat a capacity hold as license to retire. `release:repair-queue { op:'retire' }` remains correct only for provable unreachable-green (fixer dead AND fixes absent from the frozen candidate, verified per path by blob comparison).\n- Fix reds ON the frozen lineage via `op:'converge'`, not at tip. Fixing at tip is the behaviour this plan removes.\n- A held freeze is not a stalled gate. It is the mechanism working, and the convergence work is the repair path.\n\n### D-002 — A held freeze is BOUNDED, and the bound is measured from the queue's own opening\nDate: 2026-09-02\nRULING, the counterweight to D-001: holding a frozen candidate because the auto-fixer is walled must never become an unbounded hold. A freeze nobody converges is a WEDGED gate, which is strictly worse than the re-cut treadmill D-001 removes — the treadmill at least produced verdicts.\n\nThe bound is FROZEN_REPAIR_CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MS (4h), and two properties of it are binding, not incidental:\n\n1. MEASURED FROM openedAtMs, never refreshed per tick. A deadline recomputed from 'now' on each run is not a bound at all — it renews forever and reads as one. The hold compares (now - queue.openedAtMs) against the window.\n\n2. MATERIALLY LONGER than the zero-attempt stall window it gates (4h vs 15min, a ~16x ratio). This direction is the easy one to get wrong silently: a convergence window shorter than or comparable to the stall window makes the hold branch unreachable in production while every unit test still passes on its fixture. Anyone tuning either constant must preserve the ordering, or the hold becomes dead code that looks alive.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for other lanes: a queue that has been held for its full window and still has no convergence IS retired, and that retire is correct — do not read it as the D-001 defect recurring. The distinguishing evidence is the queue's age against the hold window, which the freeze disposition now records as a read rather than leaving to log archaeology.\n\n### D-003 — D-003: This plan does not ship on code truth alone — it ships when ONE real freeze→resume is counted on the DEPLOYED fix\nDate: 2026-09-02\nRULING (binds anyone who later picks this plan up, including a future me): do NOT flip this plan to `shipped` on the strength of its implementation being complete and audited. All six items are terminal and every code-truth criterion graded healthy, and that is still not sufficient here.\n\nWHY, specifically. Independent grading by su-1899608f (outside the implementer lineage) produced two cards against rev 5: bespoke EI-22174370371911157 = 3 healthy / 3 unknown / 0 broken, and class plan-class-feature-ship EI-22174565974510550 = 4 pass, gate-green-shipped FAIL, docs PARTIAL. The implementer acceptance verdict EI-22174803419780885 is REJECT, meaning NOT-YET-VALIDATED rather than defective.\n\nEvery one of the three unknowns has the SAME cause: the deployed gate is 6e898b6cf8, which does not contain P-002/P-003/P-004. The mechanism this plan exists to build has never executed. A freeze was held while grading (candidate 1f43e05a, repairHead ef0d2c06 advanced past it, attempts=1, opened 2026-09-02T16:07:28Z) carrying NO freezeAndConverge disposition and NO frozen-repair-convergence:* condition item — because the shipped code is not the running code.\n\nThe trap this closes: the plan's own Background records that three predecessor plans shipped 33 done items while the resume counter sat at zero and nobody noticed. Shipping THIS plan with its affirmative criterion unmeasured would be the fourth instance of that failure, distinguished only by having better paperwork. The rubric's stated goal is not \"add a hold branch\" but that frozen candidates actually get RESUMED. Note also that the criterion's HARD FAIL condition (freezes_opened>0 AND resumes_attempted==0) is TRUE of the deployed system today; it is spared only because that system predates the fix — which argues for waiting, not for shipping.\n\nSHIP CONDITIONS, falsifiable and needing no judgement:\n1. main goes green and fast-forwards to a staging commit containing these fixes;\n2. the gate writing the readings reports THAT sha, not 6e898b6cf8;\n3. ONE real freeze→resume is counted — resumes_completed >= 1, naming the candidate, the run, and what it converged from;\n4. no completed run re-cut at tip while a red freeze was open.\nThen supersede EI-22174803419780885 with an `accept` card and ship. Follow-up work-item: WI-2142105.\n\nDO NOT instead: revise the rubric to make the unknowns gradeable (that un-counts both independent cards and the meta-attestation), force:{reason} past the gate (force waives only the four code-truth checks and never the acceptance verdict), or re-grade with a lineage-disqualified grader.\n\nMeasured: `state:read { cell:'gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict' }` at 2026-09-02T17:31Z returned 99 consecutive reds, assessment red-current, verdictStale false, mainBehindStaging true. Deployed sha 6e898b6cf8 and the absent freeze disposition were measured by the independent grader and recorded verbatim in EI-22174370371911157. plans:audit completion seq 3 (auditedSha 96c9def1) records P-006 not-code with 5/6 items verified.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-004 — Owner-approved September 12 audit disposition and current execution contract\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAuthority: session_turn:codex:01a0961e-ab11-71f2-bae6-9be0c8401857:32 — Avi approved applying the relevance-audit recommendations and implementing relevant updated plans through verified shipment. This decision adopts the Revise disposition.\n\nCurrent contract: Transient provider unavailability must not mean abandoning a candidate. However, the later age-free invariant supersedes some bounded-hold wording, and its no-active-rubric argument does not prove predecessors lacked validation.\n\nExecution: Retain the capacity-hold behavior; correct the rationale and old bounds, refresh stale citations, and obtain the explicitly required live freeze/resume evidence.\n\nMeasured basis: the source/test/decision review and scoped verification recorded in docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md, not a new claim about the live gate. Historical timestamps, candidate references and consumed one-shot permissions below remain historical. Preserve current frozen-lineage invariants and the live-gate ownership boundary. This update does not waive proof, independent grading or acceptance requirements. Track adoption under WI-10001081; retain existing implementation work-items and completed evidence.\n\n### D-005 — D-003's premise is half stale and its blocker has MOVED, not cleared — the fix IS deployed, and the deployed mechanism opens freezes that nothing resumes. Still do not ship.\nDate: 2026-09-15\nDate: 2026-09-15\nAuthority: [self-imposed] by su-a604a73a while carrying ship-main-greening-program-2026-09-15 (its D-001 records the owner mandate). This does NOT waive D-003, which binds 'anyone who later picks this plan up'. It corrects D-003's factual premise and re-states, on measurement, why this plan still must not ship.\n\nWHAT CHANGED. D-003 asks for 'resumes_completed >= 1'.\nMeasured: grep -rl --include=*.ts over packages/ libs/ apps/ (node_modules excluded), 2026-09-15 -> resumes_completed 0 files, resumesCompleted 0 files, resumes_attempted 0 files; in the SAME invocation, positive controls admissionRounds 7 files, shrinkPerRound 7, freezeAndConverge 18, awaiting-fixer 41. A controlled absence over that scope, not an empty grep.\nThe code's actual instrument is lastResumeRunStartedAtMs ('when verification begins at the admitted repair head').\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/release/frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts:489 and :2097. Measure THAT, not the name D-003 used.\n\nLIVE FROZEN CANDIDATE 4071fc66d1689a0c8942e9b6a1ca111e59763139, opened 2026-09-15T15:52:14Z.\nMeasured: routines:list { name:'green-checkpoint', installSlug:'papercusp' } -> health.gate_health.freezeAndConverge + .convergence:\n- lastResumeRunStartedAtMs null · lastAdmittedAtMs null · fixerSpawnedAtMs null\n- attempts 1 · convergence.phase 'ready-to-verify' · ownership.phase 'awaiting-fixer' · fixerSpawnId null\n- reason 'frozen repair fixer dispatch did not return a spawn for 7798bcdf; queue remains unassigned for retry'\n- shrinkPerRound failingCount 1 -> 4 -> 2, shrinkTotal -1, converging FALSE, consecutiveReds 33\nMeasured: harness_shared.frozen_repair_edit_ledger GROUP BY candidate -> 6 distinct frozen candidates since 2026-09-06, 734 ledgered edits (9aa9e788 alone 617 edits by 69 agents).\nSo freezes DO open, repeatedly, on the deployed build, and nothing resumes them. D-003's HARD FAIL shape (freezes_opened > 0 AND resumes_attempted == 0) holds against e66be3c4.\n\nREAD admissionRounds CORRECTLY — it cost me three reversals in one session. It is NOT a count of admissions.\nMeasured: frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts:2725 and :2747 — `admissionRounds: rounds.length` where `const rounds = queue.convergenceRounds ?? []`, documented 'Recorded red rounds. 0 means none observed under this build, NOT a stalled cycle.' A reader taking admissionRounds:3 as 'three admissions happened' will conclude the resume loop works; it does not. A null latency stamp likewise means NOT STAMPED (a Pick<> backfill helper covers those four stamps), which is why the verdict above also rests on converging:false and the awaiting-fixer phase, not on nulls alone.\n\nSCOPE LIMITS — do not overstate this Decision:\n1. SHIP CONDITION 1 is NOT fully verified. Only ONE mechanism constant (FROZEN_REPAIR_CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MS, 3 occurrences, positive-control checked) was confirmed in the deployed build. P-002/P-003/P-004 were NOT each blob-checked against e66be3c4.\n2. 'Zero resumes EVER' is NOT established. A retire clears the queue row, so prior cycles' stamps are gone. The evidence is the LIVE queue plus the code's own comments recording '20 retirements, 0 resumes' for 2026-09-02.\n3. SHIP CONDITION 4 (no completed run re-cut at tip while a red freeze was open) was NOT checked at all.\n\nRULING: D-003 stands and this plan does NOT ship. What changed is the BLOCKER, not the verdict — no longer 'waiting for a deploy that never came' (it came) but 'the deployed mechanism opens freezes and nothing resumes them', whose visible symptom is a repair queue wedged at awaiting-fixer with a null fixerSpawnId across 33 consecutive reds. Whoever picks this up should measure lastResumeRunStartedAtMs on a live queue and treat the fixer-dispatch stall as what stands between this plan and ship condition 3.\nNOTE: the acceptance-verdict seat is not a permanent dead end.
