A superseding card is still required to clear a standing reject.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"mac-desktop-e2e-recurring-battery-2026-09-02","title":"Recurring Mac desktop E2E battery — headless-safe regression runs + a rig-testability detector","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-02","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Recurring Mac desktop E2E battery — headless-safe regression runs + a rig-testability detector\nslug: mac-desktop-e2e-recurring-battery-2026-09-02\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-09-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\nEach fire runs the headless-safe Mac E2E battery against the Mac VM\n(`ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-mac -p 2222 aviweiss@127.0.0.1`) and records a verdict per\ndimension. Scripts live at `papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-*.sh` and are already committed —\ndo NOT \"promote\" them from `~/.papercusp/mac-e2e-scripts-handoff/`, which is a July leftover.\n\n**Verdict grammar (D-009): exit 0 = PASS, 1 = FAIL, 2 = VOID.** A VOID is NOT a pass and NOT\na failure — it means the run *could not have failed honestly*, so it must never be quoted as\ngreen. Treat a VOID as an alert about the RIG, and a FAIL as an alert about the APP.\n\n## Background\n\nWI-3133 carries a standing directive to keep the Mac app under thorough end-to-end testing.\nThe 2026-07-05 \"ALL GREEN\" pass was taken when the VM had a console (Aqua) login session.\nIt no longer does, and nothing noticed for 10 days (`~/.papercusp/logs/gui.log` last written\n2026-08-23T03:56:01Z).\n\n**Why this battery excludes the GUI dimensions.** `open <app>` requires an Aqua session.\nThe VM currently sits at `loginwindow` with `/dev/console` owned by `root` and `who` empty,\nso launchd refuses with `OSLaunchdErrorDomain Code=125`. Every GUI-dependent assertion is\ntherefore unsatisfiable, and the two scripts that depend on it now VOID instead of reporting\na misleading FAIL.\n\n**Why `mac-vm-fresh-install-e2e.sh` is NOT on this schedule.** It is destructive by design\n(`rm -rf` of `/Applications/Papercusp*.app`, including the bundle the `com.papercusp.server`\nLaunchDaemon executes) and its final proof is a GUI `open`. It now aborts safely via control\nC0 before deleting anything, but a destructive script does not belong on an unattended\ncadence. Run it attended, only once a console session exists.\n\n## Phase 1 — the battery (executed each fire)\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Non-destructive health: run `papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-health.sh --json`. PASS requires `status:\"healthy\"` with `ssh_ok`, `operator_pid_alive`, `operator_port_listening`, `qmp_running` all true and `qemu_fd_exhausted:false`. Note `guest_kernel_panic` is a RECENCY flag, not a presence flag (writer at `mac-vm-health.sh:279-284`) — a set `guest_panic_epoch` alongside `false` is normal and means the newest panic predates operator start.\n- **P-002** `todo` Log scan: run `papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-log-scan.sh`. PASS requires zero Rust panics (section A) and zero macOS crash reports for papercusp-desktop (section D). Section B lists residual ERROR lines with no time bound, so old rotated-log hits are expected — judge B by whether anything is NEW since the last fire, not by emptiness.\n- **P-003** `todo` Rig-testability control: run `papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-relaunch-verify.sh`. exit 0 = the GUI relaunch dimension genuinely passed; exit 2 = VOID, the rig has no Aqua session and the GUI dimension is untestable — that is the detector, so surface it rather than filing it as an app regression; exit 1 = a real WI-3139-class relaunch failure, escalate. Safe to schedule: it voids BEFORE any teardown and carries a `trap` that restores the Server daemon.\n- **P-004** `todo` Record the run: append the three verdicts to WI-3133 (`work_items:comment`). If P-003 VOIDs, refresh the rig-testability blocker rather than opening a duplicate. If P-001 or P-002 FAILs, file a bug with the evidence attached.\n\n## Phase 2 — restore full coverage (not part of a fire)\n\n- **P-005** `blocked` Restore a console (Aqua) session on the Mac VM so the GUI dimensions become testable again. Auto-login is already configured (`autoLoginUser=aviweiss`, `/etc/kcpassword` present dated Jun 11, FileVault off, no `DisableFDEAutoLogin`) yet the VM booted to `loginwindow`. Two unfalsified candidates: a stale `/etc/kcpassword`, or auto-login suppressed by the panic-recovery boot. The cheap falsifier is a guest reboot; if it lands at `loginwindow` again, re-encoding `kcpassword` needs the account password, which is genuinely owner-gated.\n- **P-006** `todo` Once P-005 clears, run `mac-vm-fresh-install-e2e.sh` ATTENDED (destructive) and restore the full 5-dimension pass. blocked-by: P-005\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 The battery is scoped to headless-SAFE scripts only\nA destructive script (`mac-vm-fresh-install-e2e.sh`) must not run on an unattended cadence,\neven now that it aborts safely — a control that prevents damage is not a licence to schedule\ndamage. It stays attended-only.\n\n### D-002 A VOID is a rig alert, never a green and never an app regression\nScheduling a verification whose environment can silently stop supporting it is how the GUI\ndimension died unnoticed for 10 days. The battery therefore keeps a script that can VOID,\nspecifically so the unrunnable state is reported every fire instead of being invisible.\nReading a VOID as a PASS, or filing it as an app bug, both defeat the purpose.\n\n### D-003 — P-003's \"safe to schedule\" claim is HALF TRUE — it voids before teardown only on an UNTESTABLE rig; on a testable one it really does restart the daemon\nDate: 2026-09-02\nP-003 currently reads: \"Safe to schedule: it voids BEFORE any teardown and carries a `trap` that restores the Server daemon.\"\n\nThat is true only of the **exit-2 branch**. Measured evidence contradicts it as an unconditional claim.\n\n**Measured:** su-0300ecfc's VM `gateway.log`, reported in coord-send-a30339b13894c2c2ce5f4f508a23cb5c955353b90881f56519dd0cd45e5055ee — a 12:01Z run of `papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-relaunch-verify.sh` produced `SIGTERM 12:01:25Z` on `com.papercusp.server`, with `launchd run 3 up 12:02:50Z`. That is ~85s of daemon downtime, mid-drill, on a rig another agent held.\n\n**The actual semantics:**\n- Rig has NO Aqua session → exit 2 (VOID), returns *before* teardown. Genuinely safe. This is the case the plan text describes.\n- Rig IS GUI-testable → proceeds to a REAL relaunch: stops the daemon, verifies, and relies on the `trap` to restore it. The trap works — the daemon came back — but the outage is real and is disruptive to any concurrent holder.\n\nSo \"safe to schedule\" is a property of the RIG STATE at fire time, not of the script. The script cannot know in advance which branch it will take, and the branch it takes on a *healthy* rig is the disruptive one. Phrased the way it was, the claim is most wrong exactly when the rig is most usable.\n\n**Consequences for scheduling:**\n1. This battery must not fire while another agent holds VM custody. It is not self-limiting.\n2. A rig-custody check belongs BEFORE P-003 in the fire sequence, not as an assumption in the prose. Until that exists, custody deconfliction is manual and the armed schedule is a standing hazard.\n3. `plans:arm-schedule` is autonomy-gated while `plans:disarm-schedule` is not, so the asymmetry favors disarming early when custody is uncertain — a disarm is cheap to *do* and expensive to *undo*, which is the opposite of the usual reversibility intuition and is worth stating explicitly so a successor does not disarm casually.\n\nDo NOT quote P-003's \"safe to schedule\" sentence as authority for firing this battery against a live rig. Fix the sentence when P-003 is next edited.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-004 — Schedule DISARMED 15:41Z at the rig holder's request — and the source shows the headless branch is genuinely safe, which reopens what caused the 12:01Z restart\nDate: 2026-09-02\nSharpens D-003 with a reading of the actual script, and records the disarm. **Do not re-arm without reading this.**\n\n**Measured** — `papercusp-desktop/bin/mac-vm-relaunch-verify.sh`, read 2026-09-02T15:42Z:\n- The Aqua check (control C1) runs FIRST. Source comment: \"Run FIRST, before any teardown.\"\n- No Aqua session → `void(...)` → `emit_verdict` → `exit 2`, printing \"Nothing was torn down.\"\n- `restore_server()` opens with `[ \"$TORE_DOWN\" = \"1\" ] || return 0`, and `TORE_DOWN=1` is set only INSIDE the relaunch loop — which the C1 void path never reaches.\n\nSo on a headless VM the EXIT trap no-ops and **no `launchctl kickstart` is ever issued**. D-003's ordering claim is confirmed, and the void branch is safe in the strong sense: not merely \"restores afterwards\" but \"never touches the daemon at all\".\n\n**Disarm:** `plans:disarm-schedule` run 2026-09-02T15:41Z. su-0300ecfc reported the VM has NO Aqua session and that they are NOT releasing custody, then explicitly asked for the disarm. Executed immediately rather than at the announced 17:45Z trigger: their answer already settled the trigger condition, and deferring only added the risk that this session died first and the disarm never happened. The authored schedule is kept; `plans:arm-schedule` is autonomy-gated, so re-arming is a deliberate act.\n\n**The open question this exposes — worth more than the disarm.** Given the above, the two readings of the 12:01Z incident are no longer equivalent:\n1. The VM HAD an Aqua session at 12:01Z and has since lost it → C1 passed, teardown was real, this script caused the SIGTERM. Benign; the disarm is the right fix.\n2. The VM was headless at 12:01Z too → this script tore down nothing, and **something else** sent `SIGTERM 12:01:25Z` to `com.papercusp.server`. In that case the disarm protects against nothing and the real cause is still live.\n\nDiscriminator, on the VM's own log around 12:01:25Z: the C1 void line (\"no Aqua (GUI login) session\") ⇒ case 2; teardown/`[restore] kickstart issued` lines ⇒ case 1. Asked su-0300ecfc to check (coord-send-e77b7fcabd17aa9d13a003150cf48e5fd844e7442e47a9c37780ea412ad67e73); unresolved here because reading it requires touching the held rig.\n\nUntil that is settled, do NOT record \"the 12:01Z daemon restart was caused by this battery\" as established. It is the leading hypothesis, not a measurement — and treating it as settled is how a fix removes the suspect instead of the cause.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-005 — RESOLVED: the 12:01Z daemon restart was a build #7 redeploy, NOT this battery — D-003's conclusion survives but the evidence it cited is retracted\nDate: 2026-09-02\nCloses the open question D-004 raised. **Read this before citing D-003.**\n\n**Measured:** su-0300ecfc, the rig holder, reported 2026-09-02T15:45Z (coord, re WI-2039873): \"SOLVED the 12:01Z restart: it was a build #7 app REDEPLOY from my own lane, not P-003 and not an unknown actor.\"\n\nSo of D-004's two cases it is **case 2** — `mac-vm-relaunch-verify.sh` tore down nothing — but with a benign, identified cause rather than a lurking one. There is no unexplained SIGTERM source still armed on that VM. That was the live risk D-004 existed to surface, and it is closed.\n\n**What this retracts.** D-003 cited the 12:01Z incident as measured proof that P-003 performs a real teardown. That attribution came from the original incident report and is now withdrawn at the source: this battery did not cause it. Any reading of D-003 as \"P-003 has been observed restarting a daemon in the wild\" is WRONG — it has not.\n\n**What survives, and why.** D-003's actual conclusion is unchanged, because it does not depend on that incident. It rests on the script's own control flow, read directly (D-004's Measured block): C1 runs before any teardown; the no-Aqua path exits 2 with `TORE_DOWN` never set, so `restore_server` no-ops and nothing is touched; the Aqua-present path proceeds to a genuine quit/relaunch of both apps. \"Safe to schedule\" therefore remains a property of rig state, not of the script. That was always the load-bearing argument; the incident was corroboration, and it turned out to be corroboration of something else.\n\n**Net effect on the plan:** none of the P-003 guidance changes. The distinction worth preserving is epistemic — a decision whose conclusion is right for reasons that are partly wrong is exactly the kind that misleads later, because the retracted half keeps getting quoted as precedent.\n\n**The schedule stays DISARMED.** Not because of the restart risk, which is now understood, but because su-0300ecfc still holds VM custody, is not releasing it, and asked for the disarm. Re-arm when custody is released — `plans:arm-schedule`, autonomy-gated.\nRelated: P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"memory-vector-entity-index-split-2026-09-02","title":"Stop semantic memory recall from ordering over an HNSW index that is 91% entity vectors","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-02","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Stop semantic memory recall from ordering over an HNSW index that is 91% entity vectors\nslug: memory-vector-entity-index-split-2026-09-02\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-09-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001, P-002 and P-003 are done. Migration 1093 is applied live (fence_seq 512, submodule libs/papercusp e196ba52); the memory-only partial HNSW indexes exist on all four memory_vec_* tables. P-004 has landed the query half in libs/generic/memory/src/canonical-store.ts search(): a new vecKindCond() emits `v.row_kind = '<kind>'` on the VEC side while the pre-existing `c.` payload predicate is RETAINED as a free drift backstop (D-007 — both clauses, measured identical plan and buffer counts, so keeping `c.` costs nothing and stops a mirror drift from becoming a correctness bug).\n\nMEASURED on the SQL search() actually emits (captured from the store, not hand-written), live DB, topK=12, user_id='harness:papercusp', production GUC hnsw.iterative_scan=relaxed_order: before = full _hnsw_idx / 16,621 index rows / 104,629 buffers; after = partial _hnsw_memory_idx / 39 rows / 814 buffers. All shared-hit, so ~128x is real work avoided. The entity path does not regress.\n\n⚠ That is ONE point in the parameter space. P-005 owns the real proof and its item text is explicit that a single EXPLAIN proves nothing — the plan is parameter-selected, so sparse/median/dense × topK 5/12/100 × memory- and entity-derived query vectors remains UNMEASURED.\n\nWI-2141379 is held and not yet closed: the unit surface is green (215/215 across canonical-store, backend, mem0-backend, reembed, temporal-lite), build:typecheck 0 errors, mutation-probe verdict=caught, 3 guards clean. The full `test:affected --changed-paths` run is queued behind the shared admission mutex under fleet load.\n\n**Next:** Triage the queued test:affected result (read AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT status=, never the exit code), then close WI-2141379, which auto-unblocks P-005 and P-007. Then P-005: the three-regime × three-topK × two-vector-kind measurement matrix, reusing the scratch DB p002_hnsw_probe.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2141376 — Choose the discriminator mechanism and record it as D-003: (a) denormalize `row_kind` onto each `memory_vec_*` table plus a PARTIAL HNSW index per kind, or (b) split into separate memory/entity vec t… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-2141377 — Confirm the expected win before building: with a memory-only index of 5,917 vectors that is ~41% matches for the densest user, the walk should fall from ~22,362 candidates to order tens. Validate on … <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2141378 — Allocate the migration via `node scripts/next-migration.mjs`, write it at the returned `.DRAFT` path, arm it only once tested. Include the discriminator column, its backfill, the partial HNSW indexes… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-2141379 — Update `canonical-store.ts` `search()` so the planner can use the partial index: push the discriminator onto the vec-table side (`v.`) rather than relying on the joined `c.` predicate. Keep the exist… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-2141380 — Re-measure in ALL THREE regimes — sparse user (~1 row), median (~27-40), dense (2,511) — at topK 5 / 12 / 100, with BOTH a memory-derived and an entity-derived query vector. A single EXPLAIN proves n… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-2141381 — Confirm the fleet-wide effect from `pg_stat_statements` after deploy: buffers/call and rows/call for the memory variant (baseline 5,438 buffers, 8.62 rows/call, mean 18.62ms, max 48,672ms). Rows/call… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-2141382 — Verify recall QUALITY is unchanged: the partial index must not alter which memories are returned, only how fast they are found. Compare result sets before and after for a fixed set of query vectors a… <!-- P-007 -->\n## Background\n\n`canonical-store.ts` `search()` builds one query per `storeKind`, and the two kinds are **disjoint by construction**: memory recall filters `NOT (payload ? 'entityType')`, entity recall filters `payload ? 'entityType'`. `pg_stat_statements` confirms they are two separate normalized statements that never mix. Despite being disjoint populations with disjoint queries, they share one table and one HNSW index — so each kind's queries pay to traverse the other kind's vectors.\n\n`memory_canonical` already carries `row_kind` as `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload ? 'entityType') STORED`, with a partial index `WHERE row_kind='memory'`. That discriminator was never propagated to the vec tables — which is exactly where the HNSW ordering happens.\n\nScope note: `memory_vec_harrier` is the live table, but the same shape exists for `memory_vec_openai` / `memory_vec_local` / `memory_vec_gemma` (`CanonicalStoreConfig.vecTable`). The fix must be uniform across them or explicitly scoped to the active one.\n\n## Phase 1 — Design\n\n## Requirements\n\nWhat must be TRUE when this is done. Each is measurable against the baseline recorded on WI-1706004.\n\n1. **Memory recall no longer orders over an entity-dominated index.** A semantic memory recall must not rank against a neighbour set that is ~91% rows it will immediately discard.\n2. **The walk terminates on sufficiency, not on budget.** Today both observed walks stop just past `hnsw.max_scan_tuples`=20000 — exhaustion, not success. After the change, a typical recall must fill its limit without approaching that cap.\n3. **rows/call rises toward topK.** Baseline is 8.62 rows/call against a production topK of 5–20; the shortfall is the under-fill caused by (2).\n4. **buffers/call falls materially from the 5,438 baseline, and the latency tail collapses.** Mean 18.62 ms with a **max of 48,672 ms** is a slow-tail distribution, not a uniformly slow query — the tail is the thing to kill.\n5. **Recall results are unchanged.** Same memories, same order, for a fixed set of query vectors and users. This is a performance change; any change in returned rows is a defect, not a win.\n6. **No regime is traded for another.** The win must hold across sparse (~1 row), median (~27–40) and dense (2,511) users at topK 5/12/100, with both memory-derived and entity-derived query vectors. This requirement exists because the falsified fix in D-001 looked like a 4.5× win when measured in one regime only.\n7. **The discriminator stays correct on the write path.** New and updated rows must not drift between the vec table and canonical, or the partial index silently loses rows.\n\n- **P-001** `done` Choose the discriminator mechanism and record it as D-003: (a) denormalize `row_kind` onto each `memory_vec_*` table plus a PARTIAL HNSW index per kind, or (b) split into separate memory/entity vec tables. Weigh backfill cost, write-path maintenance (trigger vs application write), and how `CanonicalStoreConfig.vecTable` is selected. importance: high\n## Design\n\n**The fix changes the index the planner orders over — not the WHERE clause.** That direction is already settled by D-001: the obvious sargable predicate swap is falsified, because handing the planner `row_kind='memory'` flips it *into* the HNSW path where the walk is expensive (90,958 buffers vs 28,794 on the dense user). Rewriting predicates alone therefore helps the pre-filter regime and harms the HNSW regime, which is why requirement 6 is stated as a non-trade.\n\nMechanism, in order:\n\n- **Partition the vector index by row kind.** Two candidates remain open and are decided in P-001 as D-003: (a) denormalize `row_kind` onto each `memory_vec_*` table plus a PARTIAL HNSW index per kind, or (b) split into separate memory/entity vec tables. The choice turns on backfill cost, write-path maintenance (trigger vs application write), and how `CanonicalStoreConfig.vecTable` is selected — not on query shape, which is identical either way.\n- **Put the discriminator on the vec-table side.** The query is post-filter *by construction*: `runVectorSearch` sets `hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order`, ordering is on `v.`, and every predicate sits on the joined `c.`. A partial index is only usable if the discriminator is available on `v.` (P-004).\n- **Migration-only.** `hypopg` is not installed and CLAUDE.md forbids runtime DDL on the shared database, so the index change is allocated via `scripts/next-migration.mjs`, written at the returned `.DRAFT` path, and armed only after testing (P-003).\n- **Price it before building it.** A memory-only index holds 5,917 vectors and is ~41% matches for the densest user, so the walk should fall from ~22,362 candidates to order tens. P-002 validates that on a scratch database before any migration is allocated.\n\n**Trade-off accepted:** two partial indexes cost more write-time maintenance and more disk than one combined index, and the discriminator must be kept correct on the write path (requirement 7). That cost is accepted because entity rows outnumber real memories roughly 10:1 in the vector table, and today *every one* of 2.24M memory recalls pays for them.\n\n## Phase 2 — Implement\n\n- **P-002** `done` Confirm the expected win before building: with a memory-only index of 5,917 vectors that is ~41% matches for the densest user, the walk should fall from ~22,362 candidates to order tens. Validate on a scratch or throwaway database — hypopg is NOT installed and CLAUDE.md forbids runtime DDL on the shared database. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2141377 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Prove behaviour\n\n- **P-003** `done` Allocate the migration via `node scripts/next-migration.mjs`, write it at the returned `.DRAFT` path, arm it only once tested. Include the discriminator column, its backfill, the partial HNSW indexes, and maintenance of the discriminator on the write path. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-2141378 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Update `canonical-store.ts` `search()` so the planner can use the partial index: push the discriminator onto the vec-table side (`v.`) rather than relying on the joined `c.` predicate. Keep the existing `runVectorSearch` iterative-scan setup unless P-005 shows it is no longer needed. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-2141379 completed (done)\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Confirm the fleet-wide effect from `pg_stat_statements` after deploy: buffers/call and rows/call for the memory variant (baseline 5,438 buffers, 8.62 rows/call, mean 18.62ms, max 48,672ms). Rows/call should rise toward topK as the `max_scan_tuples` exhaustion stops. blocked-by: P-005\n## Decisions\n\n- **P-005** `done` Re-measure in ALL THREE regimes — sparse user (~1 row), median (~27-40), dense (2,511) — at topK 5 / 12 / 100, with BOTH a memory-derived and an entity-derived query vector. A single EXPLAIN proves nothing here; the parameters select the plan. Record before/after buffers and HNSW candidates walked. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-2141380 completed (done)\n### D-001 — The sargable predicate swap is falsified; do not ship it\n\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nThe obvious one-line fix — replace `NOT (c.payload ? 'entityType')` with the stored `c.row_kind = 'memory'` and `c.user_id` — was measured in two regimes and is **regime-dependent, not a fix**:\n\n- median user (40 memories), topK=12: **0.895ms vs 4.077ms, 4.5x FASTER** (it avoids the per-row jsonb detoast), identical buffers.\n- dense user (2,511), topK=100: **90,958 buffers / 208.7ms vs 28,794 / 162.1ms, 3.2x WORSE.** A sargable predicate flips the planner off the Hash-Join plan onto `memory_vec_harrier_hnsw_idx`, where the iterative scan walks 22,974 candidates.\n\nMeasured: same query vector and topK for each pair, under `BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order`.\n\nThe detoast saving is real and worth keeping as a secondary cleanup, but it must ride ON TOP of the index fix, never instead of it — shipped alone on the strength of the median-user win it would regress the tail this plan exists to remove.\n\n- **P-007** `done` Verify recall QUALITY is unchanged: the partial index must not alter which memories are returned, only how fast they are found. Compare result sets before and after for a fixed set of query vectors and users. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-2141382 completed (done)\n\n### D-002 — The cause is index composition, not sargability, topK, or a seq scan\n\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nThree candidate causes were tested and eliminated:\n\n- **Seq Scan on `memory_canonical`** — the framing WI-1706004 inherited from `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN)`. No measured plan ever seq-scans that table; GENERIC_PLAN cannot use `memory_canonical_user_id_idx` because it plans without parameter values. The item was right to refuse to design off it.\n- **topK** — production topK is 5-20 (`canonical-store.ts:607` defaults 5; `mem0-backend.ts:580` passes the caller's limit, capped at 20). The blow-up reproduces at topK=5.\n- **the per-user filter** — free on its own: 16 candidates walked, 819 buffers.\n\nControl, same vector / user / topK, varying only the filter set: none gives 12 walked / 758 buffers; user only gives 16 walked / 819 buffers; user plus entity-exclusion gives **22,362 walked / 133,756 buffers**. The cause is that memory recall orders over an index whose nearest neighbours are 91% rows it must discard.\n\n### D-003 — (pending P-001) discriminator mechanism\n\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nTo be recorded when P-001 lands: partial-index-on-denormalized-column vs table split, with the reasoning. Placeholder so the choice is recorded as a decision rather than an implementation detail discovered later in a diff.\n\n### D-004 — Discriminator mechanism: denormalized row_kind per vec table, maintained by a TRIGGER\nDate: 2026-09-02\nTake option (a): denormalize `row_kind` onto each `memory_vec_*` table plus a PARTIAL HNSW index per kind. Reject option (b) (separate memory/entity vec tables). Maintain the column with a DATABASE TRIGGER, not an application write.\n\nMeasured: `libs/generic/memory/src/vec-write.ts:32-37` (VEC_TABLE is a fixed 4-entry mode->table lookup: openai/local/gemma/harrier); `:75-79` (vecUpsertSql writes ONLY `(memory_id, vector, embedded_at)`); `libs/generic/memory/src/canonical-store.ts:73` (CanonicalStoreConfig.vecTable is a 4-literal union); four in-repo vec INSERT sites — `vec-write.ts:76`, `canonical-store.ts:597`, `canonical-store.ts:896`, `reembed.ts:154`; trigger precedent on this schema — `sql/506-pot-rename-slice2-expand.sql:274` (`memory_feedback_pot_hive_sync_trg BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE`) and `sql/587-memory-federation-slug-stamp.sql:54` (`stamp_memory_federation_slug()`).\n\n**Why not (b) — separate tables.** The vec table is selected by a FIXED one-dimensional mode->table lookup (`VEC_TABLE`, and the mirror at `mem0-client.ts:579-586`), and `CanonicalStoreConfig.vecTable` is a union of exactly those four literals. Splitting by kind makes the lookup two-dimensional (mode x kind = 8 tables) and changes a widely-referenced type. `activeVecTable()` exists to answer \"which table does recall read?\" for the federated backfill (EI-10405); under (b) that question no longer has a single answer. That is a large blast radius for a change whose entire purpose is index selectivity, and it buys nothing (a) does not: a partial index already gives the planner a kind-pure structure to order over.\n\n**Why the column cannot be GENERATED.** `memory_canonical` solves the same problem with `row_kind GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload ? 'entityType') STORED` plus `memory_canonical_row_kind_memory_idx WHERE row_kind='memory'`, and (a) deliberately mirrors that proven pattern. But the mirror is imperfect and that matters: a generated column may only reference columns in its OWN row, and `payload` lives in `memory_canonical`, not in `memory_vec_*`. So the vec-side discriminator needs an explicit maintenance mechanism.\n\n**Why a trigger, not an application write.** Four independent in-repo INSERT sites write these tables, and NONE has the kind in scope — every one writes `(memory_id, vector, embedded_at)` only. An application-maintained column would have to be correct at all four, and at every future writer, forever. This subsystem already documents what a stale denormalized value costs here: `vec-write.ts:61-64` warns that a wrong `MODE_DIMS` entry makes the width guard return false rather than throw, so \"a mode left at the wrong width simply stops writing vectors — no error, no log, and semantic recall for that mode quietly degrades to nothing.\" A drifted `row_kind` has exactly that shape, and it is worse: it puts a real memory on the wrong side of the partial index, so the row silently disappears from recall. That is a CORRECTNESS regression produced by a performance fix, which Requirement 5 forbids outright. A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger stamping `NEW.row_kind` from `memory_canonical` by `memory_id` cannot drift, and matches the two existing stamping triggers on this schema.\n\n**Open risk to resolve in P-003, not hand-waved here:** ordering. A vec row inserted before its canonical row exists has no kind to read. P-003 must state the trigger's behaviour in that case (reject, or stamp NULL and exclude from both partial indexes until corrected) and confirm against the actual insert ordering in `canonical-store.ts` and mem0's add() path. Whichever is chosen, a NULL-kind row must be visible as a defect rather than silently unindexed — the same silent-degradation failure this decision exists to avoid.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-005 — P-002 CONFIRMS the partial-index win — 25,338 candidates to 23 — but ONLY on the HNSW-selected path; at topK=100 the planner uses Hash Join and the change is neutral\nDate: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nThe expected win is CONFIRMED, on a calibrated offline rig, in the regime that produced the incident. Proceed to P-003/P-004. But the win is regime-bounded and the bound must survive into the implementation, because D-001 was falsified for exactly the sin of generalising one regime.\n\nMeasured: `libs/generic/memory/src/canonical-store.ts:636` — the recall SQL builds `WHERE NOT (c.payload ? 'entityType') AND c.state != 'archived' AND c.payload->>'user_id' = $n ... ORDER BY v.vector <=> $1::vector LIMIT $2`, with the store-kind clause from `storeKindCond()` at `:301-304` (`NOT (payload ? 'entityType')`) and per-filter conds built as `c.payload->>'<key>' = $n`. So the user scope and the entity exclusion are BOTH payload expressions, not the indexed `c.user_id` / `c.row_kind` columns. All arms below were run with those predicates pasted verbatim.\n\nMeasured (rig): throwaway database `p002_hnsw_probe`, local PG 18.4 + pgvector 0.8.2 — no DDL on the shared database, no production writes. Fidelity verified rather than assumed: 66,234 vectors / 5,929 memory / 60,305 entity / 1024 dims / 202 archived, densest user `harness:papercusp` at 2,523; production canon is 66,235 rows and only ONE lacks a vector, so the copy is effectively the whole table. Real payloads copied (20MB). Method mirrors WI-1706004: BEGIN READ ONLY + SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order + EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS).\n\nCALIBRATION FIRST. The rig was NOT trusted until arm A reproduced the known incident. Three earlier probe choices failed to reproduce it and were discarded, which is the substance of this decision: the pathology is selected by the QUERY VECTOR, not by the user or topK alone. A probe drawn from the target user's own stored memories sits in its own cluster and is satisfied within ~12 candidates (800 buffers, 18.8ms) — that reproduces the plan's OTHER control (\"user filter alone walks 16 candidates / 819 buffers\"), not the incident. Only an ENTITY-DERIVED probe — whose neighbourhood is the 91% entity population — reproduces it:\n\n  arm A, topK=12, entity-derived probe: Index Scan using vec_hnsw_all, rows=25,338 candidates walked, 147,178 buffers, 453.6ms\n  the documented incident:                                            22,362 candidates,        133,756 buffers, 484ms\n\nSame regime, same magnitude. The rig is calibrated.\n\nRESULT, same probe / user / topK, changing only the index and which side carries the discriminator:\n\n  A (today)                 25,338 candidates   147,178 buffers   453.6 ms\n  B (D-004 partial index)        23 candidates     1,172 buffers    27.1 ms\n  ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n                              1,102x fewer          126x fewer      16.7x faster\n\nThe plan predicted the walk should fall \"to order tens\". Measured: 23. B reaches 12 results from 23 candidates because the user filter still discards a few (0.52 rows/loop) — the partial index makes the walk kind-pure, so nearly every candidate is a real memory.\n\nTHE BOUND — do not drop it. At topK=100 the planner does NOT choose HNSW at all in either arm; it picks a Hash Join over a Seq Scan of the vec table, and the two arms are indistinguishable (28,608 buffers both; 107.2ms vs 106.0ms). The partial index therefore neither helps nor harms there. Likewise for a SPARSE user (1 memory) the planner abandons HNSW for a btree path on `canon_payload_user_idx` and finishes in ~1ms in both arms. So the change is a large win on the HNSW-selected path and NEUTRAL elsewhere — it is not a universal speedup, and P-005's three-regime sweep must confirm neutrality rather than assume it.\n\nSECONDARY, independent of any query plan: the partial index is 28MB against 399MB for the full index — a 14x storage reduction, and it builds in 2s against 56s.\n\nINCIDENTAL FINDING for P-003. Measured: zero vec rows currently lack a canonical row (`SELECT count(*) FROM memory_vec_harrier v LEFT JOIN memory_canonical c ON c.id=v.memory_id WHERE c.id IS NULL` = 0). D-004 defers to P-003 the trigger's behaviour when a vec row is inserted before its canonical row; that hazard is real but presently unrealised, so P-003 is specifying a guard against a future writer, not repairing existing data.\n\nMETHOD WARNING worth carrying: the first baseline attempt used the indexed `c.user_id` / `c.row_kind` columns instead of the payload expressions. That is silently the D-001 variant, which is already falsified — an unfaithful baseline can make the fix look good by measuring the fix against itself. Paste production's predicates from source; do not paraphrase them.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-006 — Only a MEMORY-side partial HNSW index is built; D-004's open ordering risk is closed, and a second drift path it missed is closed by a propagation trigger\nDate: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02\nSettled while implementing P-003 (migration 1093). Four rulings P-004/P-005/P-007 must follow.\n\n#### 1. ONE partial index, memory side only — not \"one per kind\"\n\nD-004 sketched \"a PARTIAL HNSW index per kind\". P-003 builds only\n`memory_vec_<mode>_hnsw_memory_idx ... WHERE row_kind='memory'` and RETAINS the existing\nfull `memory_vec_<mode>_hnsw_idx`.\n\nMeasured: `memory_vec_harrier` = 808 MB total / 444 MB indexes / 5,472 kB heap (1024-dim\nvectors are TOASTed out of line), 66,262 rows of which 60,331 are entities. An entity\npartial index would rebuild ~400 MB of what the full index already holds, and the runner\nwraps each migration in a transaction (`lint-migrations.test.ts` fails the gate on\nexplicit transaction control) so `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` is unavailable — it would\nhold a write lock throughout, for no gain, since the retained full index already serves\nentity and unfiltered queries. The memory index measured 28 MB, built in 1.4 s.\n\nP-004: recall must push `row_kind='memory'` onto the VEC table; a predicate on the joined\n`memory_canonical` cannot select this index. P-005/P-007: there is no entity partial index.\n\n#### 2. D-004's open ordering risk is CLOSED — the trigger RAISES, never stamps NULL\n\nD-004 deferred: what does the trigger do for a vec row inserted before its canonical row?\nAnswer: that row cannot exist. Measured — every `memory_vec_*` has `FOREIGN KEY\n(memory_id) REFERENCES memory_canonical(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` with NO `DEFERRABLE`\n(`dev:pg_query describe harness_shared.memory_vec_gemma`), so it is enforced at end of\nstatement; and `canonical-store.ts:590` orders writes explicitly — \"Upsert canonical\nfirst (vec table FKs to it), then vec row.\"\n\nSo `stamp_memory_vec_row_kind()` raises with `ERRCODE='foreign_key_violation'` naming the\nmemory_id and table. That satisfies D-004's \"visible as a defect rather than silently\nunindexed\" more strongly than NULL-stamping: the state is unreachable, not merely\nobservable. The trigger also ALWAYS overwrites a caller-supplied value, mirroring\n`memory_canonical.row_kind`'s \"cannot be set by a writer\". Both verified on a faithful\n66,262-row probe (an insert passing `row_kind='entity'` for a memory row stored 'memory').\n\n#### 3. A SECOND drift path D-004 did not cover, closed structurally\n\n`memory_canonical.row_kind` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (CASE WHEN payload ? 'entityType'\nTHEN 'entity' ELSE 'memory' END) STORED`, so a canonical payload UPDATE can flip the kind\nwithout touching `memory_vec_*`. Measured across all three payload writers:\n`updatePayload` (:923) and `invalidate` (:947) both carry `AND NOT (payload ?\n'entityType')`, and `payload || patch` can only ADD keys, so entity->memory is\nimpossible — but the mem0 text-update at :890 merges an arbitrary payload UNGUARDED, so\nmemory->entity IS reachable. Leaving that to call-site guards is the same \"correct at all\nfour sites, forever\" fragility D-004 rejected for inserts, so 1093 adds\n`propagate_memory_row_kind()` (`AFTER UPDATE OF payload ... WHEN OLD.row_kind IS DISTINCT\nFROM NEW.row_kind`). Verified by running the exact :890 shape against a memory row.\n\n#### 4. The defect is CORRECTNESS, not only latency — P-007 should widen\n\nCalibrated probe: real schema, real 66,262 rows, production's `SET LOCAL\nhnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order` (`canonical-store.ts:456/519`), entity-derived query\nvector (P-002: the pathology is selected by the QUERY VECTOR). Arm A reproduced P-002's\nbaseline within 0.4% (25,430 candidates vs 25,338), so the rig is calibrated, not a\nsecond copy of the fix. Against EXACT brute-force ground truth (12 true nearest memories):\n\n| arm | candidates | buffers | time | returned | CORRECT |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| A: predicate on joined canonical, full index (today) | 25,430 | 97,077 | 160.0 ms | 11 of 12 | 2 of 12 |\n| B: predicate on vec table, partial index (1093+P-004) | 12 | 893 | 4.1 ms | 12 of 12 | 11 of 12 |\n\nArm A does not merely walk further — it returns the WRONG memories, and silently returns\n11 where 12 were asked, because `relaxed_order` gives up at `hnsw.max_scan_tuples` after\nspending its budget on entity vectors. 17% recall accuracy today vs 92% after.\n\n⚠ Bound: ONE probe vector, pathological entity-adjacent regime, on a rig. Evidence FOR\nthe change, NOT a discharge of P-007 — P-007 still owns recall quality across D-005's\nthree regimes (sparse/median/dense) and at topK=100, where D-005 measured the change as\nNEUTRAL because the planner picks a Hash Join.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-007 — search() carries BOTH discriminators: v.row_kind buys the index, the c. predicate stays as a free drift backstop\nDate: 2026-09-02\nP-004's item text says to push the discriminator onto the vec side \"rather than relying on the joined `c.` predicate\", which reads as REPLACE. Implemented as ADD instead — both clauses are emitted. Recording it because P-005/P-007 will measure against this SQL shape, and because a later reader \"simplifying\" the apparent redundancy would silently undo P-004.\n\nWHY BOTH:\n\n1. The `v.row_kind` clause is what buys the index, and only it can. A predicate on the JOINED canonical row cannot be applied until AFTER the approximate index scan has picked its candidates, so `storeKindCond('c.', …)` alone forces the full `memory_vec_*_hnsw_idx` (~91% entity vectors).\n\n2. Retaining the `c.` clause is FREE — not a judgement call, a measurement. Vec-only and both-clauses produce the SAME plan and the SAME buffer counts. There is no performance argument for dropping it.\n\n3. It is the drift backstop. `memory_canonical.payload` stays the source of truth for what a row IS; `memory_vec_*.row_kind` is a trigger-maintained denormalized mirror (migration 1093). If the mirror ever drifted, a false `row_kind='memory'` would be caught by the retained `c.` predicate instead of leaking an entity row into memory recall. Drift therefore degrades SPEED, never CORRECTNESS. This directly answers the drift risk D-004 raised and D-006 extended.\n\nMeasured: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of the SQL canonical-store.ts search() ACTUALLY emits (captured from the store with a fake pool, not hand-written — the real query also carries a validity clause `(c.invalid_at IS NULL OR c.invalid_at > now())` that a hand-written approximation omits), live papercusp DB, topK=12, user_id='harness:papercusp', under the production GUC `SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order`:\n\n  before (c. only)  -> Index Scan using memory_vec_harrier_hnsw_idx, 16,621 index rows, 104,629 buffers\n  after  (v. + c.)  -> Index Scan using memory_vec_harrier_hnsw_memory_idx, 39 index rows, 814 buffers\n\nAll buffers were `shared hit` on both arms, so the ~128x reduction is real work avoided, not an I/O-caching artifact. Execution times (191ms -> 8.3ms) are reported only as corroboration: a first run of either arm pays HNSW first-touch cost, and reversing arm order flipped the timings while buffer counts stayed identical, so buffers are the honest metric here and timing is not.\n\nENTITY PATH: pushing `v.row_kind='entity'` does not regress it. No partial entity index exists (D-006 deliberately declined one), so it keeps using the full index — but the filter now applies before the join, cutting canonical lookups (18 loops/72 buffers -> 12 loops/48 buffers).\n\nGuarded by five assertions in libs/generic/memory/src/canonical-store.test.ts, including one that fails if the clause is expressed as `c.row_kind` — which would typecheck, keep every result correct, and silently give the index back, since `row_kind` exists on `memory_canonical` too. Proved falsifiable: scripts/mutation-probe.sh removing the `vecKindCond('v.', …)` line -> `verdict=caught`, 4 failed / 85 passed, tree restored byte-identical.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-007\n\n### D-008 — P-005 VERDICT: the fix is a DENSE-USER fix and its size is set by where the query vector lands, not by topK; never a regression inside the production envelope (topK<=20), and D-005's \"topK=100 is neutral\" is corrected to ~0.8x\nDate: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nP-005 measured the full parameter space on the GENUINELY-EMITTED SQL (captured by running the real `search()` against a fake pool, not hand-written), both arms differing by exactly one conjunct, verified by diff. Every cell was run twice with the arm ORDER REVERSED; buffers reproduced to within 6 blocks, so the comparison is order-independent and cache-artifact-free (rail: compare BUFFERS, not wall-time).\n\nMeasured: `git diff c34f5e1 HEAD -- src/canonical-store.ts` in libs/generic/memory = one code delta, `vecKindCond('v.', storeKind)` prepended to `conds`. Rig: /tmp/p005/{capture-sql.mts,run-matrix.py,sweep-topk.py,sweep-synth.py}; arms BEFORE=pre-P-004 emitted SQL, AFTER=current, under `BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order` on live `papercusp`.\n\n**1. It is a DENSE-USER fix. Sparse and median users are byte-identically neutral.**\n- sparse (`harness:all`, 1 row): 47 buffers BEFORE and AFTER, at every topK, both vector kinds.\n- median (`hive:lane7hive`, 27 rows): 395 buffers BEFORE and AFTER, likewise.\nNeither regime uses ANY vector index: the planner fetches the user's rows via `memory_canonical_user_id_idx` (an EXPRESSION index on `(payload ->> 'user_id')`) and sorts. The partial HNSW index is simply not on their path — no win, and no risk either.\n- dense (`harness:papercusp`, 2,426 rows) is where the whole effect lives.\n\n**2. The win's SIZE is set by where the query vector lands relative to the memory manifold — not by topK.** Dense user, topK=5/8/20, BEFORE→AFTER buffers:\n- memory+40% noise (a near-paraphrase of a stored memory): 635→639, 696→698, 951→945 = **1.0x, neutral**\n- blend(memory+entity): 3,491→729, 3,552→788, 3,798→1,007 = **3.8-4.8x**\n- random unit vector: 50,151→904, 64,648→966, 118,397→1,195 = **55-99x**\n- entity-derived: 132,382→1,008, 133,721→1,048, 136,101→1,259 = **108-131x**\nThis is the important refinement. A query that closely paraphrases an existing memory was ALREADY fast — both arms find memory neighbours immediately. The fix buys nothing there and everything in the tail, which is exactly the case that hurt: a query matching no memory well is the one that previously walked the entire entity population. Do not describe the win as \"entity-derived queries only\"; describe it as \"queries that land away from the memory cluster\", which is most real recall traffic that returns poor matches.\n\n**3. Inside the production envelope the win is universal and there is NO regression.** `memory:search` hard-caps limit at 20 (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/memory/search.ts:136`, `.max(20)`, default 8 at :173); `canonical-store.search()` defaults topK=5. Over topK 5/8/12/16/20 the dense+entity ratio is 131x/128x/118x/114x/108x and the dense+memory ratio is 1.0x. Worst observed cell inside the envelope is exactly neutral. This CLOSES D-001's failure mode — the fix is not regime-dependent in the harmful direction.\n\n**4. Above the envelope the win decays but persists: 24→102x, 32→61x, 50→48x, 75→38x.** BEFORE saturates from topK>=16 at 22,808 candidates / 136,101 buffers — the iterative scan exhausting its budget over the whole memory population.\n\n**5. CORRECTION to D-005.** D-005 predicted that at topK=100 the planner uses a Hash Join and \"the change is neutral\". Measured on the real emitted SQL it is NOT neutral: both arms abandon HNSW, but BEFORE plans a serial Hash Join at 29,037 buffers / 120.7ms while AFTER plans a PARALLEL Nested Loop at 38,605 buffers / 104.5ms — **~0.8x on buffers (worse) though ~13% better on wall time.** This is real and reproduced in both arm orders. It is NOT a production concern, because topK=100 is structurally unreachable through `memory:search` (cap 20); it matters only if a future caller bypasses that cap or the cap is raised. Anyone raising that cap must re-measure this cell first.\n\nConsequences for the remaining items:\n- P-007 (recall QUALITY) should compare result sets on the DENSE user with a far-from-memory query vector; sparse/median cannot distinguish the arms at all (identical plans), so they are a weak control, and a near-paraphrase vector is likewise uninformative.\n- P-006 (`pg_stat_statements` after deploy) should expect the fleet-wide mean to move much less than 118x: the effect is confined to dense-user recalls whose query lands away from the memory cluster, so the improvement will show in the TAIL (max/stddev of buffers per call), not in the mean. A flat mean is NOT evidence the fix failed.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-009 — P-007 VERDICT: recall quality is not merely preserved, it is substantially IMPROVED; the one apparent semantic divergence is a benign top-K tie-break, and the arms are semantically equivalent in 35/36 cells\nDate: 2026-09-02\nDate: 2026-09-02\n\nP-007 widened D-006 §4's single-vector rig probe to the full space, on the LIVE database, against EXACT brute-force ground truth. D-006 §4 explicitly required this (\"Evidence FOR the change, NOT a discharge of P-007\").\n\nMeasured: /tmp/p005/p007-quality.py — 36 cells = 3 regimes (sparse `harness:all`, median `hive:lane7hive`, dense `harness:papercusp`) x topK {5,12,100} x 4 query-vector kinds (memory-derived, entity-derived, blend, random-unit). Ground truth per cell computed in the same READ ONLY transaction with `SET LOCAL enable_indexscan=off; enable_bitmapscan=off; enable_indexonlyscan=off`, forcing the seq-scan+sort plan and therefore exact ordering. Arms are the pre-P-004 and current GENUINELY-EMITTED SQL.\n\n**1. Zero regressions; large improvements.** In all 36 cells `after_recall >= before_recall`. Dense regime, recall vs exact ground truth, BEFORE→AFTER:\n- topK=5: entity-derived 20.0%→60.0%, random-unit 20.0%→100.0%, blend 80.0%→80.0%, memory-derived 100%→100%\n- topK=12: entity-derived 16.7%→83.3%, random-unit 25.0%→91.7%, blend 91.7%→100.0%, memory-derived 100%→100%\n- topK=100: 100%→100% for all four (both arms abandon HNSW here for an exact non-vector plan, per D-008 §5)\nSparse and median are 100% in BOTH arms at every topK — those regimes never use a vector index at all (D-008 §1), so there is nothing to approximate and they cannot distinguish the arms.\n\n**2. The framing in P-007's item text needed correcting, and the correction matters.** The item asks to confirm the index \"must not alter which memories are returned\". Taken literally that is an arm-vs-arm comparison, and it would have FAILED here — the arms genuinely do return different memories in the dense regime. The correct reading, established only by the third (ground-truth) leg, is that the OLD arm was returning the WRONG memories and the new one is closer to correct. An arm-vs-arm check cannot distinguish \"unchanged\" from \"both equally wrong\", and on this path it would have reported a regression where there is a ~5x accuracy improvement. Any future change to an approximate index on this path must be measured with all three legs.\n\n**3. The single flagged divergence is BENIGN — a top-K tie-break, not a semantic difference.** 35 of 36 cells had the two arms' EXACT ground-truth sets identical, which is the positive proof that the two SQL forms MEAN the same thing and differ only in index approximation. The one exception (dense/topK=12/blend) was investigated: ranks 12 and 13 have IDENTICAL scores (0.6725766247328414), so which row survives `LIMIT 12` is arbitrary. Each arm is individually deterministic (identical ORDER across 3 consecutive runs); they break the tie differently because their scan orders differ. This is inherent to `ORDER BY <distance> LIMIT k` over tied values, predates this change, and is not introduced by it.\n\nConsequence for P-006 and for any future regression test on this path: a recall test that asserts exact id-set equality at the top-K boundary WILL flake on ties. Compare on score at the boundary, or compare set-equality only above the last tied score.\n\nConsequence for P-006 specifically, compounding D-008: the deployed effect includes a CORRECTNESS improvement, not only a latency one. `pg_stat_statements` measures neither — rows/call will rise toward topK as the `max_scan_tuples` exhaustion stops (which P-006's item text already predicts), and that rise is the observable proxy for the recall improvement measured here.\nRelated: P-006, P-007\n\n## Measurement protocol (binding for this plan)\n\nAny performance claim about this query MUST state which regime it sampled and MUST hold `hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order` in the session, because `runVectorSearch` sets it and `dev:pg_query` cannot (single-statement). Use psql. Two probes in this investigation were biased and each produced a confidently wrong reading — the first drew its query vector from a memory row and reported no bug at all; the second measured the falsified fix as a 4.5x win. Report buffers AND HNSW candidates walked, not execution time alone.\n\n## Out of scope\n\nFingerprint coverage, fusion floors, rerank thresholds and BM25 packaging — all settled in the shipped plan `semantic-search-fingerprint-coverage-2026-08-03`. This plan changes only which vectors the memory query orders over.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"portal-work-two-pane-2026-09-01-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — Portal Plans + Inbox restored to the ratified Direction B list + detail (two-pane) layout","status":"active","created":"2026-09-02","owner":"su-38293ac0-699e-4a7e-a066-c80ac84e163e","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — Portal Plans + Inbox restored to the ratified Direction B list + detail (two-pane) layout\nslug: portal-work-two-pane-2026-09-01-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-09-02\nowner: su-38293ac0-699e-4a7e-a066-c80ac84e163e\n---\n\n# Acceptance — Portal Plans + Inbox restored to the ratified Direction B list + detail (two-pane) layout\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for portal-work-two-pane-2026-09-01, authored against as-built reality after P-001..P-004 landed. The plan's goal is that the portal's Plans and Inbox faces present the owner-ratified Direction B layout (list + detail) instead of the single-column embeds that unified-web-portal-2026-08-29 P-098/P-099 shipped. D-001 chose Route 1 to get there: add an opt-in `layout=\"split\"` INSIDE the existing panes, used only by the two full-page routes, reusing the same detail components and the same URL params — explicitly NOT rebuilding native portal surfaces, and explicitly NOT making split the default (the ~360px chat sidebar must keep its stack).\n\nThese criteria therefore grade OUTCOMES, not the route taken: whether the two faces actually present list + detail, whether that happened without regressing the stack rendering or the bulk/cleanup flows D-001 named as invariants, and whether it is real on the live portal rather than only in tests.\n\nTwo notes for the grader. (1) Criterion `live-on-portal-both-viewports` is the plan's P-005 deliverable and was gate-blocked at authoring time — the operator release gate has been red for 89 consecutive runs, so a `fail`/`unknown` there may reflect the gate rather than the implementation; check `dev:pipeline_position` before attributing it to this work. (2) Where a criterion carries a `tests` binding those files are RUN at grading time, so a pass rating there is machine-contradicted if they fail; the two unbound criteria are unbound deliberately because a CSS media query and a live portal frame are not provable by a unit test, and binding them to one would have made the rubric look more rigorous than it is.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"scratch-wi4287-guardprobe-1788386348313","title":"WI-4287 guard probe (throwaway)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-02","owner":"su-d939052a-4d66-4910-b8f6-a5a38720a029","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: WI-4287 guard probe (throwaway)\nslug: scratch-wi4287-guardprobe-1788386348313\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-10-13\nowner: su-d939052a-4d66-4910-b8f6-a5a38720a029\n---\n\n# WI-4287 guard probe (throwaway)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`draft` ⇒ a proposed rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nA shared standard for a system characteristic — its criteria grade structured observations.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"standing-facts-expiry-audit-2026-09-02","title":"Audit every standing fact: correct expiry and kind across the whole live corpus","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-02","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Audit every standing fact: correct expiry and kind across the whole live corpus\nslug: standing-facts-expiry-audit-2026-09-02\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-09-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\nAuditing all **8,426** current standing facts (`harness_shared.agent_facts` where `retracted_at IS NULL AND superseded_at IS NULL`). Every fact gets an explicit recorded verdict on two axes — **expiry** and **kind** — and the verdicts are applied by direct UPDATE.\n\nDriving work-item: **WI-2141854**. Ledger + shards under `tmp/facts-expiry-audit/`; the durable decision record is committed to `docs/audits/`.\n\n## Background\n\n`facts:assert` defaults `ttlSec` to 7 days when the caller omits it. Agents omitted it almost universally, so the corpus is on a 7-day fuse regardless of whether a fact states a durable invariant or a passing observation.\n\nMeasured population (2026-09-02): 36,850 rows in `agent_facts`; **8,426** current + unretracted (the audit surface), of which 3,379 already lapsed, 4,858 live with a finite expiry, 189 live-permanent. Excluded: 25,980 superseded, 2,929 retracted (2,345 of those machine-EVICTED by the cap).\n\nKind distribution across the audit surface: 5,415 unset, 2,477 `conclusion`, 450 `convention`, 63 `undecidable`, 21 `assumption`.\n\n**1,399 live facts expire within 7 days** — the same fuse is still burning, which is why the owner extended the audit to unexpired facts.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 The audit surface is current + unretracted rows, and only those\n\nA fold serves rows matching `superseded_at IS NULL AND retracted_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()` (`liveFactPredicate`, `agent-facts/store.ts`). So:\n\n- **superseded** rows are a prior VERSION of a key whose current version exists elsewhere in the chain. They are never folded whatever their expiry; unexpiring one would resurrect a value that was deliberately corrected. Excluded.\n- **retracted** rows were removed by a decision (`facts:retract`) or by the cap sweep (`evicted_at IS NOT NULL`). Neither is an expiry lapse. Excluded — but the 2,345 machine-evicted rows are a real, separate restoration problem, filed as their own work-item rather than folded into this one.\n\n### D-002 Unexpiring is an UPDATE on the same row, never a re-assert\n\n`facts:assert` supersedes the row: new version, `created_by` rewritten to the restoring agent, `created_at` reset, TTL capped at 90d. That destroys the authorship and assertion-time provenance an audit exists to preserve, and would stamp ~8,000 facts as authored by this session. Restoration is therefore a direct `UPDATE ... SET expires_at` on the existing row (`scripts/facts-expiry-audit.mjs`), leaving author, assertion time and version chain intact. `expires_at = 'infinity'` is the permanent sentinel (`FACT_PERMANENT_EXPIRY`), already used by 189 live conventions.\n\n### D-003 REJECTED criterion: \"owner-scoped fact whose session has no presence row is unreachable\"\n\nTempting and wrong. 4,155 of 4,262 owner-scoped facts have no `coord_presence` row, which reads as \"the addressee is dead, so restoring is a no-op\" — it would have disposed of half the corpus in one move. Corroborating against a second instrument killed it: **2,100 of those ownerIds have an `agent_activity` row and 527 were active within 2 days.** Presence rows are reaped on a TTL, so their absence is not a liveness verdict. Facts are judged on the durability of what they CLAIM, never on whether their addressee is currently awake.\n\n### D-004 Two axes per fact, judged independently\n\n**Expiry** — `permanent` (`infinity`) · `extend:<days>` · `leave` (already correct, whether that means correctly lapsed or correctly short-lived).\n\n**Kind** — `convention` only where the claim is genuinely NORMATIVE (\"we do X here\", \"never do Y\", \"X is the canonical way\"). A durable FINDING about how the system behaves is a `conclusion`, not a convention. This distinction is load-bearing: conventions take no cap seat and default to permanent, so mass-converting durable conclusions into conventions would quietly disable the per-scope cap.\n\n### D-005 Restore strictly — a restored fact spends every future agent's context\n\nFolds are bounded per selector and the per-scope cap is 200, so a restored fact does not merely reappear, it COMPETES with live facts for a seat every agent pays for on every wake. A fact earns permanence only if it is (a) still true, (b) durable — an invariant, convention, settled do-not-repeat, or hard-won tool/API semantics — and (c) worth a seat. Point-in-time readings, in-flight status, session/mode-bound coordination state and shipped-and-done conditions stay expired.\n\n### D-006 Machine-generated ephemera is judged as a CLASS, on content, with sampled verification\n\n`launch-provenance` (3,010 rows) and `mode-instructions:*` (384) are each written by one code path and are homogeneous by construction. Both are session/mode-bound by their own text (\"...report milestones to them while live\"; \"retracted when the mode is turned off\"). They are judged as classes against sampled bodies and a measured homogeneity check — not row by row, and not by asserting homogeneity without measuring it. That leaves **5,033 heterogeneous facts** requiring genuine per-fact judgment.\n\n### D-007 — The kind axis is convention-only; an undeclared modality is left undeclared\nDate: 2026-09-02\n5,415 of the 8,426 audited facts carry no `kind`. The temptation is to backfill them all as `conclusion`. Do not: `store.ts` states the rule explicitly — \"Omit = not declared (never rewritten to 'conclusion' — a modality nobody stated is not one)\". Mass-backfilling would manufacture a modality thousands of authors never declared, which is the same class of error as manufacturing an owner directive from an agent's own note.\n\nSo the kind axis of this audit answers exactly the question the owner asked — *should this actually be kind:convention?* — and nothing else:\n\n- **PROMOTE to `convention`** where the claim is genuinely NORMATIVE and durable: \"we do X here\", \"never do Y\", \"X is the canonical way\". A convention takes no cap seat and defaults to permanent, which is correct for a standing rule.\n- **DEMOTE a mislabelled `convention` to `conclusion`** where an existing convention is really a finding, a measurement or a status. This one matters: a mislabelled convention is cap-exempt and permanent, so it is a free seat taken under false pretences.\n- **LEAVE everything else's kind untouched**, including unset.\n\nThe corollary is that a durable FINDING is not promoted to convention just to win permanence. Permanence is the expiry axis's job (`expires_at = 'infinity'`), and the two axes are decided independently — conflating them would quietly disable the per-scope cap for every fact this audit restores.\n\n## Phase 1 — instrument and criteria\n\n- **P-001** `done` Dump the full 8,426-row audit surface into reviewable shards; verify the dump count against the live population. — note: 8,427 rows dumped to ~/.papercusp/facts-expiry-audit (moved out of tmp/ — git-sync sweeps the tree and the working set is 16MB). 26 shards of 200.\n- **P-002** `done` Measure homogeneity of the launch-provenance and mode-instructions classes; record the class verdicts with sampled evidence (D-006). — note: Measured: launch-provenance 2995/3010 on-template, mode-instructions 399/400. 16 off-template rows pulled out for individual review. 396 mode-instructions extended to 90d where the agent_modes row still stands.\n- **P-003** `done` Write the per-fact verdict rubric that the classification pass applies verbatim. — note: RUBRIC.md written with the two-axis procedure, reason-token vocabulary, worked calibration examples from shard-001, and the two traps that already bit this audit.\n\n## Phase 2 — classify every fact\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Classify the 1,806 high-blast-radius facts (workspace, harness, role scope) — these fold for every agent. blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-005** `todo` Classify the 3,227 lower-blast-radius facts (work_item scope, owner-scope residual). blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-006** `todo` Validate the merged ledger: every id in the population judged exactly once, no id outside it. blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Phase 3 — apply and verify\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Apply the expiry verdicts in one transaction (dry-run first). blocked-by: P-006\n- **P-008** `todo` Apply the kind verdicts (convention promotions/demotions). blocked-by: P-006\n- **P-009** `todo` Verify post-state against the ledger; record the durable audit record. blocked-by: P-007\n- **P-010** `done` File the machine-eviction restoration problem (2,345 cap-evicted rows) as its own work-item (D-001). — note: Filed as WI-2141921 (bug, major): 2,345 of the 2,929 retracted rows were machine-EVICTED by the cap, not deliberately retracted. Separate remedy, and it compounds with this bug — the cap ranks victims by remaining TTL fraction, so null-ttlSec facts age into evictability fast.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"unified-voice-turn-contract-router-2026-08-31-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — unified voice-turn contract + policy router (server-selected authority, fresh filtered vault context, transport-preserving adapters, continuity/linking, executor parity, verified docs)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-02","owner":"su-8eea06bc-d647-4c99-aaaf-6c6ff325e982","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — unified voice-turn contract + policy router (server-selected authority, fresh filtered vault context, transport-preserving adapters, continuity/linking, executor parity, verified docs)\nslug: unified-voice-turn-contract-router-2026-08-31-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-02\nupdated: 2026-09-02\nowner: su-8eea06bc-d647-4c99-aaaf-6c6ff325e982\n---\n\n# Acceptance — unified voice-turn contract + policy router (server-selected authority, fresh filtered vault context, transport-preserving adapters, continuity/linking, executor parity, verified docs)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan unified-voice-turn-contract-router-2026-08-31, authored 2026-09-02 against the as-built tree (HEAD 6731386a; voice files blob-identical to audited sha aebfba81). Six OUTCOME criteria trace to requirements R1–R8 and decisions D-001..D-007. RUBRIC-WIDE EVIDENCE RULE: every suite or typecheck offered as evidence cites its testing:run runId (ONE file per call) or, for the external phone-app / chat-protocol checkouts, the log path of the run; an unsourced \"it passed\" rates 'unknown', never 'pass'. Structured checks PARTITION the in-tree files so one red file fails one criterion: C1 router unit; C2 both projection files; C3 adapter unit; C4 router integration + router unit (the unit file is shared with C1 BY DESIGN: its 'isolates a $kind principal in a restricted call conversation' and 'L4 counterexample' cases are the only in-tree falsifiers of BOTH C1's policy-elevation marker and C4's guest-isolation marker — graders read different assertions from the same run); C5 chat-protocol voice.test.ts + adapter integration; C6 prose-only (typecheck, external suites, spec ledger, docs — no in-tree Vitest file decides these). Phone-worker evidence lives in the external phone-app checkout (/home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/phone-app) and is MANDATORY manual evidence (with log path) where a criterion names it; a check.files list is deliberately partial wherever the criterion says so.
