Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for memory-fold-pollution-and-cap-eviction-2026-09-02, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality.\n\nThree defects in the agent-facts memory system:\n(1) POLLUTION — system:burn-governor wrote 14 per-account `account-burn` facts, occupying 11 of the 12 fold lines an agent sees, so the fold represented one writer instead of the workspace.\n(2) DESTRUCTION — the per-scope cap enforced backpressure by EVICTING another author's row (26-47 evictions/24h per contended scope, 16-17 authors).\n(3) SILENCE — the fold showed 12 lines of a several-hundred-fact population with no indication it was a slice.\n\nEvery criterion is an OUTCOME of the running system, not a description of work performed.\n\nRATING SCALE: 0/1/2/3 plus the bare value `unknown`. Use `unknown` when the evidence did not settle a criterion — explicitly preferred over inferring a pass from 'the tests are green' or a fail from 'I could not reproduce it'.\n\n⚠⚠ HAZARD 0 — WRONG DOOR. READ THIS BEFORE OBSERVING ANYTHING LIVE. This change is committed and on staging but NOT deployed: verified 2026-09-03T00:05Z, dev:pipeline_position for store.ts reports committedLocal true, onStaging true, inMain FALSE, deployed FALSE, with the serving release's code dated 2026-09-01T03:23Z — about 45 hours behind the tree, and the gate is red at 100 consecutive reds with its repair queue held by another agent. CONSEQUENCE: the DEPLOYED operator still runs the OLD code, so probing it shows the OLD ceiling of 200, the OLD evict-a-stranger behaviour, and the OLD 14-fact fold monopoly — the exact INVERSE of what six of these seven criteria assert. A grader who probes the deployed door will rate those criteria 0 on evidence that is perfectly correct about the running system and perfectly wrong about the change. So: grade every runtime observation against the INTEGRATION TESTS and/or STAGING (:3170), never the deployed operator, and confirm deploy position yourself first with dev:pipeline_position { path: 'packages/operator-core/lib/agent-facts/store.ts' }. If you cannot reach a door carrying the change, record `unknown` — never a fail. Only defects-cannot-silently-return is door-independent, being test-based. (Found by the vetting reviewer, whose lane's standing lesson is that a contract must be probed on BOTH doors; independently verified before adoption.)\n\n⚠ HAZARD 1 — CLIPPING. Because the old 200 ceiling is still enforced on the deployed door, any live ordinary count there is pinned at exactly 200: a number that reads like demand but IS the old cap.\n\n⚠ HAZARD 2 — PREDICATE WIDTH. Counting 'live facts' as merely (superseded_at IS NULL AND retracted_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()) reads 495 workspace / 370 harness; the population the cap ACTUALLY enforces reads 198 / 200. The difference is source_hive IS NULL, the wall:/dead-end:/guard-rail: exemptions, kind <> 'convention', and the subjectVolatile split. The reviewer and I disagreed 2.5x on this before comparing predicates — and store.ts:305-308 documents the right method twelve lines above the constant.\n\nDECISION COVERAGE (the meta-rubric's invert test): D-001 → burn-signal-not-traded-away. D-002 → fold-represents-many-authors. D-003 → cap-refuses-never-destroys. D-004's three sub-rulings → cap-refuses-never-destroys (partition rule + re-assert-never-refused + decoupled volatile bound) and ceiling-is-demand-grounded (the demand-grounded ceiling). D-005 → refusal-is-actionable. D-006 → fold-discloses-its-own-bound. P-003's durable-guard deliverable → defects-cannot-silently-return.\n\nREVISION HISTORY (all pre-grading; no card existed at any edit). r2 self-vetting: added ceiling-is-demand-grounded (D-004's ceiling half was ungraded); rewrote two criteria gradeable from source strings. r3: measured the live cap population, found it clipped at the old 200, hardened the ceiling criterion. r4: adopted four findings from the external vetting consult (conv-mtkqsiv5, su-93c2dec6) — removed an author-attested /tmp evidence path; replaced a TTL constant read that provably could not see its own named failure; deleted a live headroom threshold that would have flipped on ordinary growth rather than regression; and graded the previously-ungraded volatile ceiling. r5: the same reviewer, having retracted their own headroom measurement, found the WRONG-DOOR hazard above — the sharpest finding in the set, because it would have made an honest grader confidently wrong on six criteria at once. Every runtime method now names its door.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"main-green-status-visible-2026-09-03-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: every high-level main-greening fact is a readable state cell (main-green-status-visible-2026-09-03)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-03","owner":"su-4342525e-2b14-4780-bf1b-3b413480030d","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: every high-level main-greening fact is a readable state cell (main-green-status-visible-2026-09-03)\nslug: main-green-status-visible-2026-09-03-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-03\nupdated: 2026-09-03\nowner: su-4342525e-2b14-4780-bf1b-3b413480030d\n---\n\n# Acceptance: every high-level main-greening fact is a readable state cell (main-green-status-visible-2026-09-03)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan main-green-status-visible-2026-09-03, authored against as-built reality at 0310db47 after the completion audit (auditSeq 1, 13/13 verified, 53 citations). Goal [owner:Avi 2026-09-03 ~04:13Z verbatim]: 'EVERY HIGH LEVEL THING AGENTS NEED TO KNOW WHAT THE MAIN GREENING STATUS IS SHOULD BE VISIBLE LIKE THE TEST SUITE PROGRESS AND THE LINT PROGRESS AND ANYTHING ELSE' — as readable state cells, with the question set derived from real session history (D-001) and its coverage made falsifiable by a committed test (D-003 §4). Six outcome criteria, each tracing to the goal and a Decision, each carrying a tests check binding; the bound files are DISJOINT across criteria so the tests instrument discriminates (a detector that lives in a file bound under another criterion is cited by name in the method instead). REVISION 3 folds the vetting critique from consult conv-mtlvyvdu-0000-c1066113be7d4357b186563dbe9feb83 (su-44c8a3b5): three diff-restatement fragments excised (C3/C4/C6), D-005 §4 surfaced in C3's title, C1's future-tense clause moved into its binding, the unresolvable-cell gap added to C6, C2/C6 split on the SURFACE axis. Author caveat: mutation proofs were run only where the bound file carries its own falsifier (C1 non-vacuity pins, C2 defect-shaped controls, C4 rename falsifier); for C3/C5/C6 the grader should judge detector adequacy from the named assertions.\n\nWHERE TO READ THE CELLS LIVE: the :3070 operator runs the RELEASE checkout and main has not fast-forwarded since these cells were registered, so state:read there answers `absent` for the new cells. Read them on the STAGING operator until main promotes: `node scripts/mcp-call.mjs state:read --json-file <args.json> --client <your-su-id> --port 3170` (verified 18:58Z: freezeDisposition=converging with reason, convergence=no-attempts, retriage=no-refire, ownerBrief.attestations present on :3170; absent on :3070). The class criterion gate-green-shipped is judged on the gate: candidate 761d0a85ac is under a full canonical suite (run 7f876d2d). Grader must be outside the author's lineage (su-4342525e-2b14-4780-bf1b-3b413480030d) and must not be the vetting critic.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"role-model-one-answer-2026-09-03","title":"Switching a role's model should be one edit: one resolver, explicit-wins, backend rides with the model, and you can see the answer","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-03","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Switching a role's model should be one edit: one resolver, explicit-wins, backend rides with the model, and you can see the answer\nslug: role-model-one-answer-2026-09-03\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-03\nupdated: 2026-09-03\n---\n\n## Now\n\nMake \"what model does this role run on?\" a ONE-EDIT, ONE-ANSWER question. Today it is assembled from three disagreeing sources, the backend is guessed by regexing the model's NAME, and there is no way to see the resolved answer before a spawn dies.\n\nWorking order: **P-002 then P-005 first** — together they are most of the value and they fix the live incident. P-001 is the refactor that makes the rest cheap.\n\n## Background\n\n### The incident\n\nNine consecutive release-fixers (2026-09-03, 00:32:57Z to 01:27:40Z) spawned `backend=codex model=gpt-5.6-sol toolCalls=0`, each dying instantly on `\"You've hit your usage limit ... try again at Sep 6th, 2026 10:26 PM\"`. The gate's repair arm was inert for hours and it looked like infrastructure failure.\n\nIt was not. BOTH relevant settings were already correct:\n\n- `roleBackends['release-fixer'] = 'claude-code'`\n- `models['release-fixer'] = 'claude-opus-5:xhigh'`\n\nMeasured by stubbing the fire seam (`setLaunchBlueprintFire`) and calling the real entry point with no spawn:\n\n```\nfireLaunchBlueprintForEvent('green-checkpoint:red', { installSlug:'papercusp', workspaceId:'papercusp-workspace' })\n->  CAPTURED_ROLE: \"release-fixer\"\n    SPAWN_BACKEND: \"claude-code\"        <- correct, and ignored\n    SPAWN_MODEL:   \"gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh\"  <- tier menu, resolved earlier in the SAME function\n```\n\nThe spawn body ships SELF-CONTRADICTORY and nothing complains. The model wins because the backend is inferred from it.\n\n### Three sources of truth\n\n1. TIER MENU (`cfg.tiers`) — roles inherit a spec via model-FAMILY math (`specFamilyKey`) with floor/ceiling clamps in `resolveTierSpec` / `resolveRoleOwnModelSpec`. Every row is currently `gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh` / `codex`.\n2. PER-ROLE MODEL (`cfg.models[role]`) — never consulted by the launch path.\n3. PER-ROLE BACKEND (`cfg.roleBackends[role]`) — set, then lost, because backend is derived from the model string.\n\n`resolveRoleOwnModelSpec`'s own docstring documents the losing behaviour as intent: \"The invoke route resolves the backend from that model spec, so cross-provider tiers such as `gpt-5.5:high` can move the role onto Codex.\"\n\n### The configured intent that is currently inert\n\nAll eight per-role models are already set, and they encode a deliberate split that has never taken effect:\n\n| role | models[role] | roleBackends[role] |\n|---|---|---|\n| mug | sol:xhigh | claude-code |\n| kettle | sol:xhigh | claude-code |\n| scanner | sol:xhigh | claude-code |\n| release-manager | sol:xhigh | claude-code |\n| doc-steward | claude-opus-5:xhigh | claude-code |\n| content-fixer | claude-opus-5:xhigh | claude-code |\n| release-fixer | claude-opus-5:xhigh | claude-code |\n| merge-resolver | claude-opus-5:xhigh | claude-code |\n\nNote `roleBackends` is itself inconsistent with `models` for the four `sol:xhigh` roles — a contradiction the system currently resolves silently instead of refusing (P-005).\n\n### A second, independent precedence trap\n\n`effectiveTierConfig` does NOT merge `tierCeilings` — it is `sessionCeilings ?? workspace?.tierCeilings`. Owner-steering already holds a non-empty `{cup:'standard', mug:'max'}`, so anything written to `cfg.tierCeilings` is silently discarded. Same failure shape: a correct-looking write with no effect and no warning.\n\n### Why no config-only fix is both capable and surgical (measured)\n\nAdding a Claude tier row shifts the family FLOOR for every role whose committed default is in that family. Measured blast radius with `tierCeilings['release-fixer']` pointed at the new row:\n\n| candidate row | roles changed |\n|---|---|\n| claude-opus-5:xhigh | 8 — every launch role comes off GPT |\n| claude-sonnet-5:high | 3 — release-fixer, plus cup and queen |\n| claude-haiku-4-5:high | 1 — surgical, but Haiku 4.5 is likely too weak to repair failing tests |\n\nRoles default to opus (the 8) or sonnet (cup/queen), so haiku is the only collision-free family. CAPABLE + SURGICAL IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH CONFIGURATION. That is the design defect, stated as a measurement.\n\n## Phase 1 — make the answer single, explicit, and visible\n\n- **P-001** `done` Introduce ONE resolver `resolveRoleLaunch(role, { cfg, steering }) -> { model, backend, source, why }` as the single seam every launch path calls. Today the answer is assembled across launch-blueprint.ts, model-tiers.ts, agent-config.ts, owner-steering.ts and the /invoke route. `source` names which rule won (per-role | tier-menu | committed-default) so the readout in P-004 and the refusal in P-005 derive from the same computation, not a second copy of it.\n- **P-002** `done` EXPLICIT PER-ROLE WINS: an explicit `cfg.models[role]` is the answer, and family/floor/ceiling math gets no vote over it. Activates the eight already-configured per-role models exactly as set. Deliberately changes WI-4640 precedence — record a Decision. importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` BACKEND RIDES WITH THE MODEL, never parsed from its name. Tier rows already carry a `backend` field and the catalog knows each model's provider; deriving a CLI choice by regexing `gpt-` out of a string is the mechanism that silently ate `roleBackends`. `roleBackends[role]` becomes the fallback used only when no per-role model is set. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-004** `done` MAKE IT VISIBLE: \"what will each role launch as?\" as a readable state cell plus a line in the agent-config surface, rendering `{ role, model, backend, source }` straight from P-001's resolver. Diagnosing this incident required hand-writing a tsx probe against an internal test seam; had the resolved pair been visible it was a 30-second read. importance: high\n- **P-005** `done` CONTRADICTION IS AN ERROR: refuse (or loudly warn) at compose time when an explicit backend disagrees with the backend implied by the model, instead of silently dropping one. The nine dead fixers each shipped a body asserting both claude-code and a GPT model. importance: high\n- **P-006** `done` Fix the `effectiveTierConfig` ceilings trap: merge `tierCeilings` (session over workspace, per key) rather than whole-object replace, or make the discard explicit and reported. Same silent-write class as the main bug.\n- **P-007** `done` Tests + end-to-end verification: unit cover for explicit-wins, backend-with-model, and the contradiction refusal; then re-run the fire-seam probe and confirm the release-fixer composes model=claude-opus-5:xhigh + backend=claude-code consistently, and that the four sol:xhigh roles still resolve to their configured GPT models. blocked-by: P-002\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — An explicit per-role models[role] OUTRANKS the tier menu — deliberately narrowing WI-4640's model-spec-wins order\nDate: 2026-09-03\nRULING (cross-lane — every launch path and anyone reasoning about WI-4640 precedence must follow it).\n\nAn EXPLICIT per-role `cfg.models[role]` is the answer for that role's launch model. The tier menu's family/floor/ceiling math gets no vote over it. Precedence, strongest first:\n\n1. a caller/bench-set `bodyExtra.spawnModel` (unchanged — an explicit per-launch pin still wins)\n2. `cfg.models[role]` (NEW)\n3. the tier menu via `resolveRoleOwnModelSpec(role, effectiveTierConfig(cfg, steering))`\n4. the role's committed default\n\nWHY. Specific beats general, and `models[role]` is the most specific statement an owner can make about a role. Before this, `models[role]` was never read on the launch path at all — only the tier menu was — so a correctly-set per-role model was silently inert with no warning.\n\nWHAT THIS NARROWS. WI-4640 established that a cross-provider tier spec may move a role onto another backend, and `resolveRoleOwnModelSpec`'s docstring states it: \"The invoke route resolves the backend from that model spec, so cross-provider tiers such as `gpt-5.5:high` can move the role onto Codex instead of being applied to the Claude CLI.\" That remains TRUE for roles with no explicit per-role model — the tier menu still steers them, and the no-regression test asserts it. This decision only says the tier menu cannot override an owner's explicit per-role pin.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/launch-blueprint.ts:790-812 (the spawnModel block now prefers `cfg?.models?.[target.role]?.trim()`). Verified end-to-end by stubbing the fire seam and calling the real entry point with no spawn — BEFORE: `model=gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh, backend=claude-code` (self-contradictory); AFTER: `model=claude-opus-5:xhigh, backend=claude-code` (consistent). Command: `npx tsx -e \"…setLaunchBlueprintFire(capture); fireLaunchBlueprintForEvent('green-checkpoint:red', {installSlug:'papercusp', workspaceId:'papercusp-workspace'})\"`.\n\nMeasured: `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/launch-blueprint.test.ts` → 37/37 passed (3 new: explicit-wins; caller-set still wins over explicit; no-per-role-model tier resolution unregressed).\n\nCOST OF THE OLD ORDER, for anyone tempted to revert it. On 2026-09-03 between 00:32:57Z and 01:27:40Z, nine consecutive release-fixers spawned `backend=codex model=gpt-5.6-sol toolCalls=0` and died instantly on \"You've hit your usage limit ... try again at Sep 6th, 2026 10:26 PM\", leaving the release gate's repair arm inert for hours. Throughout, BOTH `models['release-fixer']='claude-opus-5:xhigh'` AND `roleBackends['release-fixer']='claude-code'` were already set correctly. Because the backend is derived from the model spec downstream, losing the model here silently lost the backend too, and the spawn body shipped asserting both `claude-code` and a GPT model with nothing complaining. Four agents spent hours on it across WI-2142846 and WI-2143057; the diagnosis required hand-writing a probe against an internal test seam because the resolved pair is not visible anywhere (which is what P-004 fixes).\n\nSCOPE LIMIT / KNOWN GAP. This decision does NOT fix backend inference. `inferBackendFromModelSpec` (harness-invoke-once.ts:122) still parses the backend out of the model NAME, and measurably returns `undefined` for both `sol:xhigh` and `claude-opus-5:xhigh` while returning `codex` for `gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh` — so a GPT model whose name lacks a `gpt-` prefix falls through to `roleBackends` and could hand a GPT model to the Claude CLI. P-003 (backend rides with the model) and P-005 (a contradiction refuses instead of silently dropping one) close that; until they land, keep `models[role]` and `roleBackends[role]` mutually consistent.\nRelated: P-002\n\n### D-002 — D-002: backend rides with a CHOSEN model; a committed default still inherits the host command\nDate: 2026-09-03\nP-003 says \"backend rides with the model, never parsed from its name\". Implementing it exposed a boundary the item did not name, and getting it wrong would have been a fleet-wide regression.\n\nRULING — the backend precedence, in `resolveRoleLaunch` (packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/role-launch.ts):\n1. `tier-row`      — the winning tier row's own `backend` field.\n2. `model-catalog` / `model-shape` — but ONLY when the model was CHOSEN (`source` is `per-role` or `tier-menu`).\n3. forced `codex`  — a Codex-only spec pins codex even over an explicit `roleBackends`.\n4. `role-backends` — `cfg.roleBackends[role]`, the fallback when no model was chosen.\n5. `inherit`       — nothing pins it; the host's `AGENT_CMD` wins.\n\nWHY 2 IS RESTRICTED TO A CHOSEN MODEL. A COMMITTED DEFAULT (`ROLE_MODEL_DEFAULTS`) is a code-level floor, not an owner statement about this role's CLI. Deriving a backend from it would silently overrule an operator running `AGENT_CMD='omp -p'` for every role that merely has a committed spec — and `inferBackendFromModelSpec`'s docstring records that Claude/OMP aliases inheriting the configured command is deliberate, with only Codex forcing a swap (WI-4640; kettle@papercusp was hard-downed 2026-07-16 by a claude binary handed `--model gpt-5.6-luna`).\n\nMeasured: three launch-blueprint tests went red on the first implementation precisely here — `spawnBackend` became `'claude-code'` where the contract says it must stay unset and fall through to the route's own resolution. They are the falsifier for this decision, not incidental churn.\n\nCONTRADICTION IS REPORTED, NEVER RESOLVED SILENTLY. A `roleBackends[role]` the resolved model overrules is returned on `conflict` (never dropped, never applied), surfaced as a `[backend-conflict]` warn at compose time, as `conflicts[]` on `config:role-launch`, as the `agent.roleLaunch` cell's headline, and as a red line in the /settings/agent \"Launches as\" column.\n\nMeasured (live config, read-only probe 2026-09-03T02:53Z): all 8 configured roles — content-fixer, doc-steward, kettle, merge-resolver, mug, release-fixer, release-manager, scanner — resolve model `claude-opus-5:xhigh`, backend `claude-code`, source `per-role`, conflicts 0.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"role-model-one-answer-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: switching a role's model is one edit with one answer","status":"active","created":"2026-09-03","owner":"su-4342525e-2b14-4780-bf1b-3b413480030d","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: switching a role's model is one edit with one answer\nslug: role-model-one-answer-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-03\nupdated: 2026-09-03\nowner: su-4342525e-2b14-4780-bf1b-3b413480030d\n---\n\n# Acceptance: switching a role's model is one edit with one answer\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan role-model-one-answer-2026-09-03, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. The plan's goal: make \"what model does this role run on?\" a ONE-EDIT, ONE-ANSWER question. Before it, the answer was assembled from three disagreeing sources, the backend was guessed by regexing the model's NAME, and there was no way to see the resolved answer before a spawn died. Criteria are OUTCOMES of the shipped system, not a restatement of the seven items. Governing rulings: D-001 (an explicit per-role models[role] outranks the tier menu) and D-002 (backend rides with a CHOSEN model; a committed default still inherits the host command).\n\nREVISION HISTORY — both revisions came from applying meta-acceptance-rubric criterion prefer-structured-check honestly to my own rubric, before requesting any independent grading. REV 2 repaired three criteria whose bound test files resolved and passed but whose assertions could not go red for the criterion's own drift marker (criterion 6's real falsifier lives in role-launch.test.ts, not model-tiers.test.ts; criterion 2's structural detector is launch-blueprint.test.ts's readAgentConfig call-count; criterion 5 rested on a registration census that would stay green if the surface rendered garbage). REV 3 closes the two gaps rev 2 could only DECLARE, by shipping the missing detector: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/config/role-launch.test.ts (6 tests, added 2026-09-03) exercises the config:role-launch handler and asserts the conflict REACHES conflicts[]/verdict, that a MATCHING pair does not (cry-wolf control), that an inherited backend is reported as undetermined rather than as a conflict, and that every row carries model + backend + source together. Criteria 4 and 5 are now bound to it.\n\nREMAINING PROSE-GRADED SCOPE, stated rather than implied: the agent-config ROUTE projection and the Tauri \"Launches as\" UI column still have no committed test. Both render the same resolveRoleLaunch output the now-bound tool renders, so the drift risk is the same shape, but a grader must confirm them by inspection plus a headless drive rather than by a green run.\n\nGrader note: every criterion carries driftMarkers naming the concrete broken state — grade by trying to MAKE those true against the real tree, not by confirming the implementer's citations read plausibly. The implementer's code-truth audit (auditSeq 1, sha 05b8686, 25 citations, 7/7 implemented) is available to spot-check; the class rubric requires that spot-check.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"storewolf-central-server-cloud-deployment-2026-09-03","title":"storewolf-central-server — revival + portable cloud deployment (GCP first)","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-03","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: storewolf-central-server — revival + portable cloud deployment (GCP first)\nslug: storewolf-central-server-cloud-deployment-2026-09-03\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-03\nupdated: 2026-09-07\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** D-040 applied: 25/30 items are done, four noncritical requirements are explicitly dropped/deferred, and only P-027 remains active. The existing GCE `storewolf` VM is now running a controlled non-live test runtime: mongod active, storewolf@All READY on :8000 with `live:false` and a real DB connection, wolfcastle active on :4000, both app units disabled across reboot, and systemd NeedDaemonReload=no. A persistent local SSH tunnel exposes the new `/healthz` endpoint at http://localhost:18081/healthz; its live response currently reports ok=true, mode=All, databaseConnected=true, serviceCount=55. The local StoreWolfServer on :9000 remains the only live production writer and Cloudflare ingress is unchanged. Focused Vitest coverage is green (2 files, 6 tests). The legacy Marko login routes were disabled in source in 2025 and remain a separately filed pre-existing UI issue (EI-22565257600378004), not a cloud-runtime failure.\n\n**Next:** Avi opens http://localhost:18081/healthz and confirms the cloud test result; after that feedback, P-027 either proceeds through the guarded stop-old/start-new production cutover or stays in non-live test mode.\n\n## Background\n\nstorewolf-central-server is a Node.js monolith-of-services: `Server.js` boots a `ServiceManager` that scans `Services/*/` and exposes each over one Express app at `POST /services/<Service>/<endpoint>`. Production ran as two systemd units on one host (`sw-central`, `sw-transformer`), `WorkingDirectory=/home/prod/subarch/central`, user `prod`.\n\nFull dependency inventory: `~/storewolf-deploy-dependency-inventory.md`. Condensed:\n\n**Four repos, three runtimes.** storewolf-central-server (+38 submodules) · Storewolf-Libs (npm `file:` path dep) · wolfcastle (Deno service, port 4000) · castle (the Deno *framework* wolfcastle is built on). Runtimes: Node 22 LTS, Deno, Python 3.\n\n**The castle relationship is commonly misremembered.** castle is NOT superseded by wolfcastle — `wolfcastle/app.ts` lines 1–2 import `Util` and `Server` from `castle/mod.ts`; 26 `from \"castle/...\"` imports total. wolfcastle = thin `app.ts` + Sheets/Datasheets services; ALL infrastructure (Server, Listener, ServiceLoader, Authenticator, Gateway, Guard, Validator, Crypt, PubSubber, Queing) lives in castle. castle *was* also a runnable server once (its `deno.json` still has `dev`/`app` tasks), so wolfcastle superseded it **as the deployed service** but not **as the library**. The name collision is compounded by storewolf's route to wolfcastle literally being `/castle/`.\n\n**Datastores.** MongoDB 141 GB at `/mnt/data/db` — 101 collections, ALL inside the `admin` database (leads 37.8M docs, advertiser_suggestedBidsAndExpressions 86.7M, sourceFromAsinAssociations 9.7M). Plus per-service SQLite, LMDB, and `/dev/shm` shared-memory maps.\n\n**Co-location is a hard constraint.** 21 of ~40 services run as child processes on offset ports, communicate over `localhost` HTTP, and share memory via `/dev/shm` (`SharedMap.js`, `mmap-object`). This is why the compute target is a VM, not containers.\n\n**Ingress is already portable.** cloudflared tunnel (`~/.cloudflared/storewolf-prod.yml`) publishes prod/dev.storewolf.com → `http://localhost:80`. Works identically on GCE, EC2, Hetzner or a laptop — no cloud LB, no DNS cutover, no cert migration.\n\n## Phase 0 — Preserve (nothing is safe until this is done)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Push all unpushed commits in storewolf-central-server (5 commits, 41 files, 8466 insertions) and Storewolf-Libs (2 commits) to their existing private remotes\n- **P-002** `done` Back up castle and wolfcastle to new PRIVATE repos under the aviynw account — both had dead remotes (github.castle.com has no DNS record at all)\n- **P-003** `done` Cold-backup the 141 GB MongoDB dbPath to /mnt/backup (mongod stopped; verified by file count + byte size) importance: high — note: BACKUP_OK 2026-09-02T20:19:30-04:00 — 560 files / 150521474556 bytes exact match both sides, rsync exit 0 in 943s, mongod restarted by trap and verified active+listening\n- **P-004** `done` Restore-drill the backup: point a throwaway mongod at the copy and count a collection — a backup is not a backup until read back blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-2142934 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Offsite copy of the mongo backup — /mnt/backup is the SAME MACHINE, so current state survives disk failure but not host loss, fire or theft blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-2143724 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `dropped` Rotate the credentials now sitting in private GitHub repos: storewolf config.jsonc (38 secret / 9 credentials / 6 token / 2 password keys), wolfcastle .vscode/launch.json (CastleKey, CastleAuth), wolfcastle users.json (admin hash + bearer tokens) — note: Owner explicitly accepts the existing credential exposure; rotation is optional follow-up, not a cloud shipment gate (D-040). Existing WI-2143725 preserves the deferred work.\n- **P-007** `dropped` Re-encrypt config.jsonc and its 8 plaintext siblings; add them to .packerignore so they cannot enter an image build — note: Owner waived re-encryption as a shipment requirement (D-040). The completed .packerignore/image-exclusion half remains in force.\n\n## Phase 1 — Establish ground truth\n\n- **P-008** `done` Capture the live host config into version control: full /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/avi.storewolf.com (contains the /castle/ route absent from BOTH repo nginx backups), cloudflared yml, systemd units, crontabs, real runtime versions — note: CAPTURED + COMMITTED + PUSHED (b8aa8ee, verified on remote by independent re-fetch). deploy/host-config/ holds the full 282-line avi.storewolf.com vhost incl. the /castle/ → 127.0.0.1:4000/services/ route absent from both repo backups, cloudflared ingress yml (credentials .json deliberately excluded), mongod+nginx units, and live runtime versions (Ubuntu 24.04.4, node v25.9.0, python 3.14.7, mongod 8.0.20, nginx 1.24.0). Secret-swept with a positive control proving the sweep fires.\n- **P-009** `done` Settle which branch is canonical. Local prod=2024-10, origin/prod=2025-02, newest work is old_node_fetch=2026-08 and is NOT an ancestor of origin/prod. The revival target must be an explicit decision, not an accident — note: Settled by D-007: old_node_fetch (4c0482f, 2026-08-15) is the canonical revival branch; origin/prod's 8 divergent commits are NOT merged. The item asked for an explicit decision rather than an accident, and D-007 is that decision, with the measurement that forced it: `git rev-list --left-right --count old_node_fetch...origin/prod` => 512/8, and neither branch is an ancestor of the other (both descend from merge-base 295d209), which is why \"newest branch\" could not settle it alone. Flipped on a re-read of D-007's own text, not from memory of having decided it. Everything downstream already builds on this: deploy/provision.sh pins a SHA per D-007 rather than tracking a branch.\n- **P-010** `done` Fix Services/EbayAds — it has a gitlink on disk but NO url in .gitmodules, which breaks clone AND silently aborts `git submodule foreach`/`status` mid-scan — note: FIXED + falsified. Scope was LARGER than the item stated: 40 gitlinks vs 37 declared paths — THREE unmapped, not one (Services/EbayAds, mmap-object, claude-cowork-linux). Recovered each real URL from its own .git/config remote and added all three to .gitmodules. Before: `git submodule status` emitted 'fatal: no submodule mapping found ... Services/EbayAds' and aborted mid-scan around Services/Easyship. After: exit 0, 0 fatal lines, all 40 enumerated, unmapped=0.\n- **P-011** `dropped` Relieve /mnt/data disk pressure (97% full, 293G free). The 2.0 TB swapfile on the data volume is the largest reclaimable item and its I/O contends with the DB; sdb is entirely free — note: Local disk maintenance is not a prerequisite for the already-provisioned GCE deployment; deferred to WI-2143726. No data deletion or swap action authorized (D-040).\n- **P-012** `done` Verify the dead-dependency findings before they enter an image: mmap-object, gm, lmdbx, shm-typed-array, shared-memory-datastructures, cbor-x, msgpackr all showed 0 direct requires — note: VERIFIED, and the item earned its place: one of the seven was a FALSE POSITIVE. msgpackr is NOT dead — required at Storewolf-Libs/SharedArray.js:4, which is reachable from Services/DataStore/DataStore.js and Services/Synchronizer/Synchronizer.js. Confirmed unused (0 direct requires): gm, shared-memory-datastructures, cbor-x. Already removed + install-verified by peer su-877a3c6e under WI-2142915: mmap-object, lmdbx, shm-typed-array, node-postal, ems.\n- **P-013** `done` Confirm whether AWS S3/SNS/SQS (SDK v2 AND v3 both present) and Postgres (PostgresReadStore in Storewolf-Libs) are live — each would be an additional provisioned dependency — note: BOTH CONFIRMED LIVE — each is a real provisioned dependency for any target host. AWS: aws-sdk v2 in Services/Advertiser/Advertiser.js, plus @aws-sdk/client-s3/sns/sqs v3 in Services/Amazoner/Amazoner.js and Amazoner_back.js (v2 and v3 genuinely coexist, as the item suspected). Postgres: Storewolf-Libs/PostgresReadStore.js, reached via Store.js/SharedMap.js and Services/DataStore/DataStore.js.\n\n## Phase 2 — Local bring-up (the revival, and the acceptance test)\n\n- **P-014** `done` Stand up the four repos + 38 submodules on this box: node 22, deno, python3, and the native-module toolchain (node-gyp, make, g++, libpostal) blocked-by: P-009 — note: toolchain verified (node22/deno/python3/make/g++/node-gyp); submodules 37/40 registered; castle deno-check clean, wolfcastle runs; libpostal proven UNNEEDED\n- **P-015** `done` Bring up castle + wolfcastle on :4000 and prove the Sheets/Datasheets path end to end: storewolf Communicator.crun → nginx /castle/ → wolfcastle :4000/services/ blocked-by: P-014 — note: ← WI-2143408 completed (done)\n- **P-016** `done` Boot storewolf `central` mode against the restored MongoDB and confirm the 21 child processes come up on their offset ports blocked-by: P-014 — note: ← WI-2143409 completed (done)\n- **P-017** `dropped` Upgrade the mongodb driver off the EOL pinned 3.7.3 — as its OWN verified step, not bundled into the migration blocked-by: P-016 — note: MongoDB driver modernization is deferred to WI-10000343 after the live local debug checkout is settled; self-hosted GCE Mongo does not require it (D-040).\n- **P-018** `done` Record the working bring-up as an executable script — this becomes the Packer provisioner, so it must be reproducible rather than remembered blocked-by: P-015, P-016 — note: ← WI-2142973 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Golden image\n\n- **P-019** `done` Author a Packer manifest producing an immutable, versioned VM image from P-018's provisioner blocked-by: P-018 — note: immutable versioned image produced + verified: deploy/packer/build/qemu-storewolf-0-1-0-20260903/storewolf-0-1-0-20260903.qcow2 (40GiB virtual / 6.78GiB actual), qemu-img check 'No errors were found on the image', plus packer-manifest.json carrying image_version 0.1.0, node_major 22, deno_version 2.5.6\n- **P-020** `done` CI/build access to 38 private storewolf/* submodule repos (deploy key or PAT) plus vendoring the Storewolf-Libs `file:../` path dep, which does not survive a naive build context blocked-by: P-019 — note: ← WI-2142999 completed (done)\n- **P-021** `done` Size and trim the image: libpostal ~1.8 GB trained data (ONE call site, Services/Easyship), Chrome ~400 MB, Python ML stack ~1 GB. Decide bundle-vs-split with real numbers, not estimates blocked-by: P-019 — note: MEASURED, and the item's headline premise was obsolete. DECISION: BUNDLE, do not split. Real numbers: node_modules 1.5G · .git 1.3G (excluded via .packerignore) · puppeteer/Chrome cache 581M · heaviest packages geoip-lite 154M, googleapis 115M, aws-sdk 101M, @cloudflare 98M, nodejs-polars gnu+musl 74M each, @pagefind 66M, wrangler 49M. Chrome STAYS: puppeteer has 7 real call sites (MarketplaceStuff x2, StateManager/CentralState_Avi, DellOrders, +3). Trimmable now: the nodejs-polars musl build (74M) is dead weight on a glibc host (ldd = GLIBC 2.39), and .git (1.3G) is already excluded. Net image payload ~2.1G, which does not justify a split-image architecture.\n- **P-022** `done` Boot the image LOCALLY (or on a scratch instance) and re-run P-015/P-016 against it — retire \"can we reproduce it\" before taking on \"can we move clouds\" blocked-by: P-019 — note: Verified on the rebuilt image (20260904, 7.3GB): 12 passed / 0 failed. P-016 — storewolf reached READY (Ready PID: 1402), bound :8000, mongo connect resolved. P-015 — wolfcastle :4000, castle resolved a real endpoint, nginx proxies byte-identically. Harness now durable at deploy/verify-image.sh.</note>\n<parameter name=\"rationale\">P-022 asked whether the golden image can actually reproduce the running system, before taking on \"can we move clouds\". Answered yes, by measurement rather than inference. The first boot found three real defects (WI-2143804: Storewolf-Libs module resolution; mongo socket EACCES masked into a ~27.8h silent hang; dangling /mnt/data symlinks causing lmdb ENOENT), all three are fixed in deploy/provision.sh, and the rebuilt image passes 12/12. P-015 was deliberately re-measured on THIS image rather than inherited from the pre-D4 build. Acceptance follows D-022: the criterion is the app's own \"Ready PID:\" line, never a child-process count — a healthy image forks zer…\n\n## Phase 4 — Cloud deploy (GCP first, provider-neutral)\n\n- **P-023** `done` Provision one GCE VM sized for the workload, with a persistent disk for the mongo dbPath, SQLite and LMDB paths blocked-by: P-022 — note: ← WI-2143929 completed (done)\n- **P-024** `done` Decide the MongoDB target: self-hosted on the same VM (keeps `admin`-as-app-database working, no driver forcing) vs Atlas (portable, but restricts `admin` and forces the P-017 driver upgrade) blocked-by: P-017 — note: Decided in D-024: self-hosted mongod 8.0 on the same GCE VM. Managed MongoDB is structurally excluded — all 11 service call sites are .db('admin'), Database.js cannot emit an Atlas SRV/replica-set URI, and the 141G backup is a raw WiredTiger dbpath no managed service ingests.</note>\n<parameter name=\"rationale\">P-024 asked for a decision, and the decision is recorded with its measurements in D-024. Three independent measured constraints make managed MongoDB infeasible without an application rewrite rather than merely more expensive: every service selects .db('admin') (managed services reserve admin for the control plane); lib/Database.js:24-31 hardcodes a single-host mongodb:// URI with no SRV/replicaSet/authSource support; and /mnt/backup/mongo-dbpath-2026-09-02 is a raw WiredTiger dbpath (534 files, 0 BSON dumps) that only a self-hosted mongod can consume, which also keeps P-025 a file copy rather than a 141G dump/restore over the wire. Supporting: source mongod is 8.0.20 and the ima…\n- **P-025** `done` Migrate the 141 GB dataset to the chosen target and verify collection counts against the source blocked-by: P-023, P-024 — note: ← WI-2143948 completed (done)\n- **P-026** `done` Move the secret envelope: STOREWOLFPASSWORD + STOREWOLFKEY into GCP Secret Manager; the encrypted-config mechanism itself is already provider-portable and needs no change blocked-by: P-023 — note: ← WI-2143983 completed (done)\n- **P-027** `needs-human` Point the existing cloudflared tunnel at the new host — no cloud LB, no DNS change, no cert work blocked-by: P-023 — note: Cloud test runtime is green; waiting for Avi to open http://localhost:18081/healthz and confirm the observed result before the deliberate production cutover required by D-033 and the plan Now section.\n- **P-028** `done` Verify egress: BrightData proxy config plus scraper egress identity against a cloud NAT IP blocked-by: P-023 — note: ← WI-2144009 completed (done)\n- **P-029** `done` Document the AWS/Azure delta so provider-neutrality is a demonstrated property rather than a claim — note: Accepted on existing verified implementation evidence under D-040; external-repo commit authority is no longer a completion gate.\n\n## Out of scope (deliberately)\n\n- Repo hygiene: the 1.3 GB `.git` for 622 tracked files, the `undefined/` directory with 36 tracked files, `SIOGHKSDLJASFHSAKGJ/`, `claude-cowork-linux/`, and the random-named root files. Real debt, not on the critical path, and touching 622 tracked files mid-migration destroys the ability to diff.\n- Rewriting or modernizing services during the move. Change hosts OR change code, never both — otherwise every failure has two candidate causes.\n- Splitting services across hosts/containers. Blocked by the `/dev/shm` + localhost coupling; would be a rewrite, not a repackaging.\n- Rewriting git history to purge committed secrets. Rotation (P-006) addresses the live risk; history rewrite across 40 repos is a separate project.\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Cloud deploy (GCP first)\n\n- **P-030** `done` Extend the P-026 boot-time Secret Manager fetch per D-035/D-036: materialize production config_avi_prod.jsonc and GlobalConfig.js beside Server.js at /opt/storewolf with atomic 0600 root:root writes and post-write assertions; guarantee DEBUGDIR, CACHEDIR and GCPATH plus the cwd-relative Debug target; add non-transacting regression coverage and verify on the stopped/disabled VM without starting StoreWolf, wolfcastle, or changing cloudflared ingress. blocked-by: P-026 importance: high — note: Accepted on existing implementation and live GCE boot verification under D-040; external-repo commit authority is no longer a completion gate.\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Developer Git checkout on GCE\n\n- **P-031** `done` Commit and push the complete current Storewolf repository graph (storewolf-central-server, every reachable submodule/gitlink, Storewolf-Libs, castle, and wolfcastle); install a persistent GitHub SSH credential on the GCE storewolf VM; clone/pull the repositories into the required /home/marsh-office sibling layout; install dependencies; and verify that `cd ~/storewolf-central-server && node Server.js -p 9000 -c config_Avi_debug.jsonc --mode AllNOLIVE` starts with live=false and a real MongoDB connection. Preserve the existing /opt image deployment and never pass -l during acceptance. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000593 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Compute target is ONE container-free VM, not containers\nDate: 2026-09-03\nDate: 2026-09-02\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-02] ruling, and it is independently forced by the code.\n\n21 of ~40 services run as child processes on offset ports from base 3000, communicate over localhost HTTP, and share memory through /dev/shm. Splitting them across containers or pods would require --ipc=host, --network=host and volume mounts for every SQLite/LMDB path — at which point the container boundary buys nothing while costing the build.\n\nMeasured: Storewolf-Libs/SharedMap.js and SharedMapMultiKey.js use the mmap-object native addon (has binding.gyp, compiled at install); lib/Communicator.js routes inter-service calls to http://localhost; config.modes defines the deployable service sets (central=40, sw-wills=15, sw-avis=11, will-dev=19, advertiser=1).\n\nThis is the case where lift-and-shift is the correct engineering answer rather than the lazy one. Reproducibility is still enforced, just at the VM-image layer (Packer) instead of the container layer — the same immutable-versioned-artifact discipline, one level down. Refs P-017, P-024.\nRelated: P-017, P-024\n\n### D-006 — First mongo backup goes to local sda1 via stop-mongod filesystem copy\nDate: 2026-09-03\nDate: 2026-09-02\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-02] chose the target (inspect sda/sdb then use one) and the method (stop mongod, filesystem copy) from an explicit option set.\n\nThe data had FOUR independent protections missing simultaneously: single disk (one 7.3T NVMe, no RAID), 97% full (293G free, itself a corruption risk), not a replica set (rs.status() throws — standalone node), and no backup scheduled or recent (no cron, no systemd timer; the only mongodump trace is ~/mongodumpArchive.log last written 2025-11-23, whose companion ~/mongodumpArchivecd is 0 bytes — a typo'd filename, so no archive exists).\n\nTarget verified virgin before any write: sda1 and sdb1 each carry a DOS/MBR partition typed 82 Linux swap but with NO swap signature, NO filesystem signature (wipefs -n empty), first 4KB all zeros, no fstab entry, not swap-active. Refs P-003, P-004, P-005.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-007 — D-007: old_node_fetch is the canonical revival branch; origin/prod's 8 divergent commits are NOT merged\nDate: 2026-09-03\nP-009 asked which branch the revival targets. Both halves of that are wrong, and acting on it would take the machine down. This decision overrides the item text.\n\n**It is live, not idle.** Measured: `swapon --show` => `/mnt/data/swapfile file 2T 163.1G -2`. Measured: `free -h` => Mem total 251Gi, used 172Gi, free 37Gi, available 78Gi.\n\n`swapoff` must fault every in-use page back into RAM before it returns. That is 163 GB demanded on a host with 37 GB free and 78 GB available — the kernel would OOM-kill its way through the process table to try to satisfy it. This box runs ~100 concurrent agent sessions plus mongod plus the owner's own StoreWolfServer, so the blast radius is the entire fleet and the owner's live work. A swapfile cannot be shrunk in place either: the only path is swapoff → recreate smaller → swapon, and step one is the fatal one. There is no safe version of this while the host is memory-pressured.\n\n**It is not even the biggest target.** Measured: `du -sh /mnt/data/*` => Backup 2.3T, swapfile 2.0T, back 547G, offload 520G, papercusp-backups 450G, transformerDB 383G, papercusp-audit-inputs 263G, Debug 174G. `/mnt/data/Backup` is LARGER than the swapfile and, unlike swap, is not load-bearing for a running kernel.\n\n**Ruling.** The swapfile is out of scope for P-011 permanently — not \"later\", not \"with care\". Reclamation must come from the data directories, and those are the owner's to authorize: three of the four biggest (Backup, back, offload) are named like backups, and this is a plan whose Phase 0 exists to PRESERVE data. Deleting 2.3 TB called \"Backup\" during a data-preservation project is precisely the irreversible mistake this plan is meant to avoid, so it does not happen on agent judgment.\n\n**Also note the swapfile is doing real work.** 163 GB resident in swap on a 251 GB box means the working set genuinely exceeds RAM. The item's secondary claim — that swap I/O \"contends with the DB\" — is plausible and is an argument for MOVING swap to a different spindle, not for deleting it. The plan already notes sdb is free; relocating the swapfile to sdb (create there, swapon the new one, only then swapoff the old, in that order, so capacity is never negative) is the shape of a safe fix and is the only swap change that should ever be attempted.\n\nConsequence: P-011 cannot be closed by reclaiming swap. It needs either an owner decision on the data directories or the sdb relocation above.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-009 — D-009: P-007 re-encryption must FOLLOW P-006 rotation, not precede it — encrypting leaked values protects nothing\nDate: 2026-09-03\nPhase 0 lists P-006 (rotate) and P-007 (re-encrypt) as siblings, and P-007 reads as the immediately actionable one. Reversed: re-encrypting first is security theatre, and doing it first actively wastes the rotation.\n\n**The exposure is already off-box, in history.** Measured: `git rev-parse origin/old_node_fetch:config.jsonc` => `3c557d92bad1276f73c69569c8517c7904705a1b`, byte-identical to the local HEAD blob. Measured on that PUSHED blob: 0 `ciphertext` nodes, 59 secret-shaped keys, 34 non-empty secret values of 8+ chars. Remote: `git@github.com:aviynw/storewolf-central-server.git`. Seven sibling config*.jsonc are tracked and pushed alongside it.\n\nRe-encrypting the working copy produces a new commit whose *parent* still contains the cleartext. Anyone with repo access — now or from any existing clone or fork — reads the old blob directly. So encryption changes nothing about the credentials that have already left the building. The only control that actually invalidates them is issuing new ones, which is P-006 and requires the owner.\n\n**Doing P-007 first is worse than merely useless.** Encrypt now and you produce ciphertext wrapping values that are known-compromised, which reads as \"secured\" in every later review while the live credentials remain the leaked ones. Then rotation lands and you must decrypt, replace and re-encrypt anyway — the work is redone, and in between the repo carries a false all-clear.\n\n**Ordering.** P-006 (owner issues new credentials) → write the new values in → P-007 (`encrypt_config.sh`) → verify 0 plaintext secret values remain. P-007 is therefore blocked on P-006, not merely adjacent to it.\n\n**What was safely done now.** The half of P-007 with no dependency on rotation: `.packerignore` added, excluding all 8 config*.jsonc plus GlobalConfig*.js, .env*, node_modules, .git, and the two non-service submodules. This is the durable fix for the stated risk that they \"cannot enter an image build\" — and it also encodes the right pattern, that configuration is injected at DEPLOY time from a secret manager rather than baked into an image that every instance, snapshot and export inherits.\n\n**Not attempted deliberately, and why.** (a) Re-encryption rewrites files the owner's live `StoreWolfServer` (pid 3231091, started 20:29:17, cwd = this repo) depends on. (b) `.gitignore` does not untrack an already-tracked file; making it effective needs `git rm --cached`, which would remove config*.jsonc from the repo the deployment currently reads its configuration from. Neither is an agent's unilateral call while the owner is mid-revival.\n\nContext (WI-2142940): `decrypt_config.sh` appears to have been run twice, which clobbered the encrypted backup, so `validation.secret` is now literally `valid` and the master password currently decrypts nothing — any non-empty value satisfies startup. The crypto path is dormant until `encrypt_config.sh` runs again, which is the P-007 step above.\nRelated: P-006, P-007\n\n### D-010 — Tunnel ingress is remotely-managed: ship no local ingress yml, and cut over by UUID exclusivity\nDate: 2026-09-03\nThe GCP image must NOT install a cloudflared ingress yml, and cutover must never run the same tunnel UUID on two hosts at once.\n\nEVIDENCE (two independent instruments):\n1. With neither, cloudflared pulls ingress from the Cloudflare API. Control: the papercupai-api connector (pid 209525) on the same host DOES pass --config, which is what a locally-configured tunnel looks like.\n2. An out-of-band change — su-877a3c6e repointed prod+dev via the CF API at 2026-09-03T00:34Z and deploy/host-config/cloudflared/storewolf-prod.yml did not change. Running that UUID on the GCP host while the old host still runs it makes Cloudflare load-balance across both connectors, so traffic lands on the old box at random. Cutover is stop-old-then-start-new, never an overlap. Booting it proves the count is right and the mechanism is not. This governs P-018's provisioner and therefore P-019/P-022.\n\n#### The parent does not spawn anything\nMeasured: ServiceManager/ServiceManager.js:49-56 — addChildService() only calls\ncommunicator.addChild(service, 'http://localhost:' + (Number(this.port) + Number(config.portOffset)) + '/services/' + service)\nand returns { isChild: true }. No spawn, no fork. `spawn` IS imported (line 15) and `this.childProcesses = []` IS declared (line 45), but neither is ever used. The call site comment states the contract outright: \"If this is a child service assume it is already running in it's own process.\"\n\n#### 21 services, 4 processes\nMeasured from config.jsonc `services` (21 entries with child:true), grouped by portOffset:\n  +1  Transformer\n  +2  DellCom\n  +5  Advertiser, Easyship, Amazoner, MarketplaceStuff, BrightData\n  +6  Hubx, Amazon, Fedex, Agent, Ebay, Telegram, Email, Boilerplate, Sheets,\n      Datasheets, Synchronizer, SQLExamples, Scorer, Swing\nOnly FOUR distinct offsets. Services sharing an offset share one child process.\n\n#### Confirmed by running it\nMeasured 2026-09-03: `node Server.js -c <cfg> -m central -p 19000 --noweb` (read-only; no -l, no --dbwrite).\n- MongoClient connected over the unix socket mongodb://%2Ftmp%2Fmongodb-27017.sock\n- \"Main Request Routing Server Started on Port: 19000\"; GET :19000/services/ -> HTTP 200\n- exactly 21 \"added as child service\" lines, names matching the static list above\n- 19001 / 19002 / 19005 / 19006: NO listener on any of them\nSo the parent comes up fully and registers 21 child URLs pointing at ports nothing is serving. Static prediction and runtime agree exactly.\n\n#### Consequences for the image\n1. provision.sh must install FIVE units, not one: the parent (`-m central -p <base>`) plus four children, each `-s <csv of that offset's services> --parent <base> -p <base+offset>`. A single-unit image comes up \"healthy\" with all 21 child services dead.\n2. Child services fail OPEN, not loud — the parent logs \"added as child service\" whether or not anything is listening, so nothing in the boot output distinguishes a correct bring-up from a broken one. Health-check the offset ports explicitly.\n3. `-s` is the child's service selector (\"csv of services to enable\", Server.js printHelp) and `--parent <port>` marks it a child.\n\n#### Second, independent blocker for the same lane\nNo config in the tree can boot central mode. The image must ship a config that satisfies BOTH halves; none exists yet.\nRelated: P-016, P-018, P-019, P-022\n\n### D-013 — D-013: CORRECTS D-012 — the first P-016 boot used `-m central`, which is a silent no-op; central mode is 17 in-process + 21 child = 38 services, now genuinely verified via `--mode`\nDate: 2026-09-03\nAmends D-012. The bundle self-labels non-reproducible and refuses to be mistaken for a promotable artifact, so this cannot leak into a release by accident.\n2. **Release stays gated** on two things, in order: the owner committing package.json/package-lock.json, then `REF` in provision.sh:24 being bumped to a sha that CONTAINS the fix. Bumping the pin is not optional cleanup — a release built at b8aa8ee fails npm install by construction.\n3. Reading a script's *prose description in a plan* is not reading the script. Four sub-rulings, all reuse-first:\n\n**1. Reuse the existing bucket, do not mint a new one.**\n`gs://papercusp-estate-backups-active-alcove-504205-q3` already exists in the D-011 project (US multi-region, STANDARD default). The storewolf snapshot goes under a new `storewolf-mongo/<snapshot-name>/` prefix beside the existing `daily/` and `tools/` prefixes.\nMeasured: `gcloud storage ls` returned exactly those two prefixes before this work; bucket describe returned location US multi-region, default_storage_class STANDARD.\n\n**2. COLDLINE via lifecycle, not via upload flag.**\n`gcloud storage rsync` has NO `--storage-class` flag (measured: `gcloud storage rsync --help` lists only --delete-unmatched-destination-objects / --recursive / --exclude among the relevant flags). Setting the class at upload time via `cp --storage-class` also DISABLES parallel composite upload — gcloud warns explicitly. So the upload runs at the bucket default and a lifecycle rule ages `storewolf-mongo/` into COLDLINE at age 1 day.\nThe bucket's two pre-existing `daily/` rules were preserved verbatim; the update was verified to return 3 rules, not 1.\nCost: ~140GB COLDLINE US multi-region ≈ $0.98/month.\n\n**3. NO lifecycle delete rule on this prefix.**\nThe `daily/` prefix deletes at 45 days. This prefix deliberately does not. A disaster-recovery snapshot that is refreshed rarely must not silently expire — an offsite backup that has aged out looks like protection while providing none. Retention here is an explicit human decision, not a timer.\n\n**4. A read ACL, not sudo-gcloud.**\nThe .wt files are `mongodb:mongodb 0600`. Running gcloud under sudo writes ROOT-OWNED files into the invoking user's gcloud config (measured: my first test upload created a root-owned file under ~/.config/gcloud/logs/2026.09.03/ — repaired). That would break the owner's later non-root gcloud use. Instead the script grants an additive, reversible POSIX ACL (`setfacl -R -m u:$USER:rX`) and runs gcloud unprivileged. Undo: `sudo setfacl -R -b <snapshot-dir>`.\n\n**Deliverable:** `/home/marsh-office/storewolf-mongo-backup-offsite.sh`, a companion to the existing `storewolf-mongo-backup.sh` (same log/verify/STATUS conventions). It REFUSES to run unless the local backup declared `BACKUP_OK` — replicating a corrupt backup offsite is worse than having none. It verifies by object count + total bytes, the same check the local backup uses, and writes a manifest object beside the data so a future restorer can verify without access to this host.\n\nNote it lives in $HOME beside its sibling, NOT in the storewolf repo: this is host DR operations, not VM provisioning. Putting it in deploy/ would have mixed the two.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-019 — D-019 — The qemu builder MUST set cpu_model = \"host\": MongoDB needs AVX, and packer's default qemu64 model does not have it\nDate: 2026-09-03\nDate: 2026-09-03\n\nThe first real `packer build` of the image FAILED at the acceptance-check step. This decision records the cause so the fix is not later \"cleaned up\" as a stray tuning knob.\n\n**Measured**, from the build log (task 0mtm4mx1f1mt7ptaj6y, failed after 5m32s):\n```\n==> FATAL: MongoDB 8.x is not installed\n/tmp/script_7848.sh: line 11: 4787 Illegal instruction (core dumped) mongod --version\nBuild errored: Script exited with non-zero exit status: 132.\n```\n\n**The message was wrong.** mongod was installed AND enabled — the check on the immediately preceding line (`systemctl is-enabled mongod`) had just passed. Exit 132 = 128 + 4 = SIGILL. MongoDB 5.0+ is compiled to require AVX; the binary dies on the first instruction that uses it.\n\n**Root cause: no `-cpu` flag.** Packer's qemu builder passes no `-cpu` argument unless `cpu_model` is set, so QEMU falls back to the `qemu64` model, which does not advertise AVX. Measured from the live build's process line: `qemu-system-x86_64 -name storewolf-... -machine type=pc,accel=kvm ... -smp 4 -boot c` — no `-cpu` anywhere. The host itself has the feature (`grep -w 'avx\\|avx2' /proc/cpuinfo` → `avx avx2`), so nothing on the host revealed the gap.\n\n**Two fixes landed, because this was also a DETECTOR failure:**\n\n1. `cpu_model = \"host\"` on the qemu source. Verified: `packer validate` exits 0 with \"The configuration is valid.\", confirming the field is supported by packer-plugin-qemu v1.1.6.\n2. The acceptance check now separates \"absent\" from \"present but cannot execute\": it captures `mongod --version` output and exit code, reports a non-zero exit as an EXECUTION failure explicitly stating \"this is NOT a missing install\", and special-cases 132 with the AVX/cpu_model explanation. A probe that names the wrong cause is worse than one that fails loudly — this one would have sent the next reader to reinstall a database that was already correctly installed.\n\n**Constraint this places on later work:** `cpu_model = \"host\"` makes the image's CPU baseline that of the BUILD host. That is the correct trade here (the D-011 GCP target has AVX), but it means an image built on a host with a newer instruction set than the deployment target could fail the same way in the opposite direction. If image portability across heterogeneous hardware ever becomes a requirement, replace \"host\" with an explicit named model that includes AVX (e.g. `Skylake-Client` or `Haswell`) rather than reverting to the default.\nRelated: P-018, P-022\n\n### D-020 — D-020 — P-006's credential rotation is owner-gated by CAPABILITY, not by permission: measured breakdown of what only Avi can rotate\nDate: 2026-09-03\nDate: 2026-09-03\n\nThe playbook requires exhausting the privilege I already hold before reporting a credential wall (on this box `sudo -n` is NOPASSWD: ALL). I did that check for P-006. The wall survives it — but it is narrower and far more actionable than \"rotate the credentials\" implied, so this records the measured breakdown rather than the vague blocker.\n\n**Measured** — distinct secret-bearing KEY NAMES in `storewolf-central-server/config.jsonc`, extracted by name only (values deliberately not read): 32 distinct names.\n\n**Genuinely owner-gated — requires signing into a third-party console. No amount of local privilege substitutes:**\n- Amazon Selling Partner API — `SELLING_PARTNER_APP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `sellerAppSellerSecret`, `sellerRefreshTokenNA`\n- AWS IAM — `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `iamUserAccessKey`, `iamUserSecretAccessKey`\n- Amazon Product Advertising API — `productAdvertisingAccessKey`, `productAdvertisingSecretKey`\n- eBay — `ebay_auth`\n- Generic OAuth clients — `clientSecret`, `client_secret`, `refreshToken`, `refresh_token`, `accessToken`\n\n**NOT owner-gated — I can rotate these, and they should NOT be reported as blocked:**\n- The GCP service account (`private_key_id`, `privateKey`, `auth_uri`, `token_uri`, `auth_provider_x509_cert_url` — a service-account JSON). This project is `active-alcove-504205-q3` and I hold `super@papercusp.com` on it, so `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create/delete` rotates it without the owner.\n- Self-issued application secrets: `avi_token`, `cacheToken`, `liveLeadsToken`, `basicAuth`, plus wolfcastle's `CastleKey` / `CastleAuth` and `users.json` (admin hash + bearer tokens). These are values the system issues to ITSELF; nothing external validates them, so rotating them is a local edit plus a restart.\n\n**Why I did not rotate the second group now, despite being able to.**\n1. The service races the mount and strands its own data.** provision.sh enables mongod at boot with `dbPath=/mnt/data/db`, and systemd starts it long before google-startup-scripts runs the mount. mongod initialised its dbPath on the BOOT disk; the mount then covered /mnt/data, removing the live data directory from under a running process. Circular wait.** The mount script RUNS AS google-startup-scripts.service and starts mongod. Ordering mongod after that unit makes systemd wait for mongod before the unit it waits on can finish. Measured: `systemctl list-jobs` showed `google-startup-scripts.service start running` beside `mongod.service start waiting`; an interactive `systemctl start mongod` hung past 50s; the startup script never reached its final log line. `RequiresMountsFor=/mnt/data` alone expresses the real dependency and does not reference the unit currently executing. P-025 replaces it wholesale with the real 141 GB WiredTiger dbpath.\n\n**Why this nearly shipped green.** The natural check is `systemctl is-active mongod` plus `ls /mnt/data`, and immediately after provisioning both look correct — the directories present are the image's on the wrong disk, and the active service is seconds from failing. A `df -h /mnt/data` in the same window reads /dev/root and then /dev/sdb a minute later. All three instruments are racy in exactly that window, so a single sample of any of them is a coin flip.
