Dev host `df -h /mnt/data` = 7.3T total / 6.9T used / 398G available / 95%; `swapon --show --bytes` = 246,384,852,992 bytes live (~229 GiB); `free -h` = 10 GiB free / 58 GiB available. `/dev/sdb` is NOT entirely free: it has an MBR (`PTTYPE=dos`) and a 1.3T partition with no filesystem signature/mount. `ss -ltnp :9000` = StoreWolfServer pid 134537, cwd `/home/marsh-office/storewolf-central-server`; package.json and package-lock.json are modified. GCE witness: zero active storewolf@ units, wolfcastle inactive, zero StoreWolfServer processes.\n\n**Shipment residue (do not force/drop):**\n1. P-006 — Avi must issue third-party replacements in Amazon SP-API/AWS/Product Advertising/eBay/OAuth provider consoles unavailable to this session. D-030 also requires STOREWOLFKEY and STOREWOLFPASSWORD to become different values.\n2. P-007 — remains blocked on P-006 by D-009; encrypting known-leaked values first is false security and must not be used to make the plan look complete.\n3. P-011 — needs Avi to identify/authorize data to remove or explicitly authorize a new layout after inventorying `/dev/sdb`. The item text's 'sdb entirely free' premise is retracted. Swap deletion remains forbidden by D-008; the current pressure makes it even less safe.\n4. P-017 — needs Avi's live :9000 debug session to end and the in-flight package.json/package-lock.json changes to be settled before driver edits/npm install. Do not edit or install into the live checkout.\n5. P-027 — needs a new explicit owner cutover decision replacing D-033. Until then, StoreWolf/wolfcastle stay disabled+stopped and Cloudflare ingress remains untouched.\n\nP-020, P-029 and P-030 are complete. P-029/P-030 source changes are verified on disk/live but still await the external StoreWolf repository's owner-managed commit; Papercusp git-sync does not manage that checkout, and this session must not manually commit a shared tree containing Avi's unrelated changes. The plan cannot truthfully enter shipped while any residue above remains.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-011, P-017, P-027, P-029, P-030\n\n### D-040 — Owner waives credential exposure as a shipment gate and authorizes route-A cloud test activation\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-06\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-06, session_turn:codex:01a07974-9901-75b3-bd71-21e68e711445:7] Owner directed: \"unblock it i dont care about the leaked credentials this is not important stuff.\" [owner:Avi 2026-09-06, session_turn:codex:01a07974-9901-75b3-bd71-21e68e711445:10] Owner then selected route A and asked to be told when and how it is testable.\n\nRuling:\n1. P-006 credential rotation and P-007 re-encryption are no longer shipment gates. The owner accepts the present exposure for this non-sensitive project. Keep the already-implemented .packerignore/image-exclusion controls; do not expose secret values in logs or reports. Rotation/encryption may happen later but cannot block cloud testing or shipment.\n2. P-011 local-disk cleanup and P-017 MongoDB-driver modernization are maintenance work, not prerequisites for the already-built self-hosted-GCE deployment. Preserve their durable follow-ups; do not delete backup/data directories and do not modify the live local checkout merely to make this plan green.\n3. P-029 and P-030 are accepted on their existing verified implementation evidence. Their owner-managed external-repository commit remains desirable but lack of commit authority is not a reason to misstate completed implementation as incomplete.\n4. This decision supersedes D-033 only for a controlled, non-live GCP test activation. Start Storewolf without -l / with STOREWOLF_LIVE=0, keep cloudflared production ingress unchanged, and expose the test through an operator-local SSH tunnel. This creates no second live marketplace writer. A later production cutover still requires stop-old-then-start-new and separate verification; never overlap the same tunnel UUID or two live writers.\n\nMeasured before ruling execution: GCE instance storewolf is RUNNING at reserved IP 34.173.157.14; mongod and nginx are active; runtime config and Secret Manager env files exist with verified modes; storewolf@All and wolfcastle are disabled/inactive; /etc/storewolf/All.env is the only missing prerequisite for the existing non-live acceptance path. Local StoreWolfServer remains listening on :9000.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-011, P-017, P-027, P-029, P-030\n\n### D-041 — GCE developer checkout uses full Git commit/push/pull and a persistent VM SSH key\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-07\n\nOwner-directed requirements:\n- [turn:01a07d37@2026-09-07T19:27:04.981Z] The GCE host must support the exact interactive command `cd ~/storewolf-central-server && node Server.js -p 9000 -c config_Avi_debug.jsonc --mode AllNOLIVE` with the complete dependency closure.\n- [turn:01a07d37@2026-09-07T19:37:22.988Z] Transfer is full Git history through commit, push, and pull/clone; copying source files is rejected.\n- [turn:01a07d37@2026-09-07T19:41:38.031Z] A persistent GitHub SSH private key may be stored on the VM for simpler direct pulls.\n\nMeasured: local repository inspection on 2026-09-07 found `storewolf-central-server` on `old_node_fetch` tracking `origin/old_node_fetch`, 40 declared submodules, sibling Git repositories Storewolf-Libs/castle/wolfcastle, and the requested config pair tracked. GCE inspection found `/home/marsh-office/storewolf-central-server` absent, `/opt/storewolf` not a Git checkout, Git installed, and port 9000 free.\n\nBinding implementation:\n1. Review and commit intentional current changes in each owning repository before pushing. Never leave a superproject gitlink pointing at a commit absent from its declared reachable remote.\n2. Clone the superproject and every submodule recursively from GitHub, with Storewolf-Libs, castle, and wolfcastle as sibling Git repositories under `/home/marsh-office`. No source-file copy/rsync may substitute for Git transfer.\n3. Install the existing GitHub SSH credential as `/home/marsh-office/.ssh/id_ed25519` mode 0600, its public key mode 0644, and a verified github.com host key. Do not emit private key material in logs. Owner accepts that this broad key carries the same private-repository authority on the VM as on the source host.\n4. Preserve `/opt/storewolf` and the controlled :8000 test runtime. Acceptance uses :9000 without `-l`; health must report `mode=AllNOLIVE`, `live=false`, and `databaseConnected=true`.\n5. Future updates are normal Git pulls on the VM, not image-bundle copying.\nRelated: P-031\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"work-item-claim-floors-batch-rewrite-2026-09-03","title":"work_item_claim_floors: batch/set-based rewrite (buffer cost)","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-03","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: work_item_claim_floors: batch/set-based rewrite (buffer cost)\nslug: work-item-claim-floors-batch-rewrite-2026-09-03\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-03\nupdated: 2026-09-03\n---\n\n## Now\nState: Diagnosed, not yet designed/implemented. `harness_shared.work_items_claimable` / `work_item_claim_floors(...)` costs ~130 shared buffers per row across ~84,087 open papercusp rows (~10.9-11M buffers total) to answer the authoritative \"what's claimable\" read. Root cause is architectural: `work_item_claim_floors` delegates through a chain of ~20 wrapper functions (`_v22` -> `_v21` -> ... -> `_v1`), each adding one more per-row EXISTS/JOIN floor check (reserved-plan-lane, blocked-dep, needsOwnerAction, etc.), evaluated once per candidate row rather than batched. Migration 1100 (mark the functions PARALLEL SAFE) and 1101 (fix a seq-scan in the blocked-dep branch) both landed correctly and are verified live, but neither reduces the underlying per-row cost — 1100 only bought ~1.7x headroom via parallelism (2.86s vs the 5,000ms statement_timeout ceiling), which regresses as open-row count grows (already 84K+) or under parallel-worker contention on this heavily-loaded box. A partial/expression index on the floor predicate is NOT viable: `work_item_claim_floors` is STABLE (it reads mutable tables — plan claims, deps, etc.), and Postgres requires IMMUTABLE for an index expression. Full EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) evidence lives on EI-22201349964242175's checkpoint.\nNext: P-001 — design + prototype a set-based (batch) rewrite of ONE floor branch as a LEFT JOIN/CTE evaluated once across the whole candidate set instead of per-row, and measure its buffer cost against the current per-row cost for that one branch.\n\n## Background\nFollow-up chain: EI-21553706255036686 (work_items_claimable blew the 5s statement_timeout deterministically at 12,933ms / 11.4M buffers) -> migration 1100 (mark all 8 `work_item_claim_floors*` functions PARALLEL SAFE; planner metadata only) dropped it to 2,859ms via a 5-worker parallel plan, same row count, but buffer traffic UNCHANGED at ~11M (EI-21553706255036686 closed on the timeout, with EI-22201349964242175 filed for the residual) -> migration 1101 (fix a real seq-scan in the blocked-dep branch's nested EXISTS, 267,508 buffers -> 3) verified correct but empirically NOT the dominant cost: that branch only fires when `work_item_deps.blocked_ref` matches a row's feature_id, true for only 1,484 of 84K+ candidates system-wide.\n\nThree EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) probes on EI-22201349964242175 isolated the real cost:\n- Full aggregate (`SELECT count(*) FROM work_items_claimable WHERE harness_slug='papercusp'`): Filter (incl. `cardinality(work_item_claim_floors(...)) = 0`) costs 10,955,326 buffers across ~84,130 candidate rows.\n- Same candidates, filter WITHOUT the floors() call (just the cheap jsonb lane/needsOwnerAction checks): 70,123 buffers, 146ms.\n- ONE direct `work_item_claim_floors(...)` call for a real row: 154 buffers, 4.9ms (~130/row average; 154 x 84,130 ~= 13M ~= the observed 10.96M).\n\nThe cheap jsonb pre-filters only exclude 16,013 of ~84K candidates, so reordering predicates (raising the function's `procost`) cannot meaningfully cut the cost — most rows genuinely need real floor evaluation. This is death-by-many-small-checks, not a single missing index: no ONE migration fixes it. The durable fix is re-architecting the v1..v22 delegation chain from per-row scalar EXISTS calls into set-based batch evaluation (LEFT JOINs / a single CTE per floor type, computed once across the whole candidate set) -- a much larger effort than either of the two migrations already shipped, requiring careful behavioral-equivalence verification across every floor in the chain before it can replace the current implementation.\n\nAlso flagged but not investigated: the blocked-dep branch hardcodes `d.workspace_id = 'default'` regardless of the caller's actual `p_workspace_id`, even though 160,346 of 160,427 papercusp work_items are `workspace_id='papercusp-workspace'`. Matching still works today because blocked_ref/blocker_ref values appear globally-unique feature_ids, but this looks like a pre-existing scoping oddity (a prior peer's memory flagged a similar pattern in `work_item_is_blocked()`) that deserves independent verification -- not necessarily related to the perf problem.\n\n## Phase 1 — Investigate + prototype\n- **P-001** `todo` Design + prototype a set-based rewrite for ONE floor branch (pilot — pick the cheapest/most isolated, e.g. the jsonb lane/needsOwnerAction pre-filter or the blocked-dep branch) as a LEFT JOIN/CTE evaluated once over the full candidate set instead of a per-row scalar call; measure its buffer cost against the current per-row cost for that one branch via EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS). — note: ← EI-22201349964242175 released\n- **P-002** `todo` Build a behavioral-equivalence harness: for every open papercusp work_item, compare the OLD per-row `work_item_claim_floors(...)` verdict against the NEW batch-evaluated verdict and assert they are identical before trusting any rewritten branch. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Investigate the `d.workspace_id = 'default'` hardcoding in the blocked-dep floor branch (flagged during EI-22201349964242175's diagnosis, not verified) -- determine whether it is a real scoping bug independent of this perf work, and whether `work_item_is_blocked()` shares the same pattern.\n\n## Phase 2 — Extend + ship\n- **P-004** `todo` Extend the pilot's set-based pattern across the remaining floor branches in the v1..v22 delegation chain, one at a time, each gated green by the P-002 equivalence harness before merging. blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-005** `todo` Ship the rewritten work_items_claimable/work_item_claim_floors via a migration; re-measure the aggregate with EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS); confirm it drops well under the 5,000ms statement_timeout with real margin (not just parallelism headroom); close EI-22201349964242175 citing the new measurement. blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Per-row scalar floor evaluation is the buffer cost; partial/expression index is not viable\nDate: 2026-09-03\nwork_item_claim_floors(...) is STABLE (it reads harness_plans/plan_item_claims/work_item_deps etc., which mutate), not IMMUTABLE. Postgres requires IMMUTABLE for a functional/partial index expression, so the \"partial/expression index\" fix floated in EI-22201349964242175's original filing is NOT implementable as described — it would need a denormalized/trigger-maintained column instead, which is itself a design decision this plan should make explicitly in P-001 rather than assume. The only durable path is set-based (batch) re-evaluation of the v1..v22 delegation chain: LEFT JOIN/CTE floors computed once over the whole candidate set instead of a per-row scalar function call.\n\nMeasured: EI-22201349964242175's checkpoint records three EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) probes (2026-09-03T02:53:49Z) — full aggregate 10,955,326 buffers/~84,130 rows; same candidates without the floors() call 70,123 buffers/146ms; one direct floors() call 154 buffers/4.9ms (~130/row average, consistent with the aggregate). The cheap jsonb lane/needsOwnerAction pre-filter excludes only 16,013 of ~84K candidates, so raising the function's procost to reorder predicates cannot meaningfully cut the cost — most rows genuinely require real floor evaluation.\nRelated: P-001, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-design-to-code-coverage-seam-2026-09-02","title":"Acceptance: the coverage seam — is completion evidence actually falsifiable, and do the instruments actually gate?","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-04","owner":"su-318d21e2-9fd2-40ca-b79c-f5d34f6f9767","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: the coverage seam — is completion evidence actually falsifiable, and do the instruments actually gate?\nslug: acceptance-design-to-code-coverage-seam-2026-09-02\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-04\nowner: su-318d21e2-9fd2-40ca-b79c-f5d34f6f9767\n---\n\n# Acceptance: the coverage seam — is completion evidence actually falsifiable, and do the instruments actually gate?\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nThis plan's goal was to join design→code traceability and ACTIVATE the code→test measurement already built. Its animating claim, stated as D-008, is that a check which cannot fail is decoration — and worse than nothing, because it consumes the attention a real check would have earned.\n\nSo these criteria deliberately do NOT ask 'was each item implemented' (the completion audit already answers that, with 59 resolved citations). They ask the harder question the plan exists to answer: can the mechanisms it shipped FAIL, and do they fail in the safe direction? A grader who only confirms the code exists has re-run the audit rather than graded the plan.\n\nREVISION 2 — WHAT INDEPENDENT VETTING CHANGED. This rubric was vetted by su-a961ddec, who RAN three of the drills rather than reading them and found that criterion C2's drill produced a FALSE FAIL on correct code: it grepped the inner symbol `deriveDraftSpecClauses`, which legitimately has no external caller, while the seam actually crosses at the exported wrapper `persistDerivedDraftClauses`. That is the mirror of D-008 and the more dangerous half of it — a check that fails SPURIOUSLY teaches the grader to override the drill, disarming it for the case where it is right. Re-verifying that report, the author found the SAME defect class in two further drills, including one the vetter had proposed as the fix: a `Measured:` literal that three of the six cited Decisions do not use (they write 'Measured;' and 'Measured before'), and a `judgePatchCoverage` grep that HITS a comment in `qodo-cover-loop.ts:9` explaining why that wiring was rejected. All three are corrected below, and every drill in this revision was EXECUTED against the live tree before being written down.\n\nGRADER ORIENTATION. The highest-value check is `instruments-refuse-rather-than-decorate`: trace, in source, whether each shipped gate has any path from 'could not measure' to a passing exit. That property is what distinguishes this plan from an elaborate no-op, and it is cheap to falsify — one wrong branch and the criterion fails. Per the class rubric, also spot-check the implementer's audit citations rather than taking them on trust. Where a drill's CORRECT outcome is an empty or surprising result, the drill says so explicitly — read that note before recording a failure.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-design-to-code-coverage-seam-2026-09-02-runtime","title":"Acceptance: falsifiable completion evidence and persistent code→test attribution","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-04","owner":"su-6bcf6fd9-20c3-459a-a553-f8c602677cf0","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: falsifiable completion evidence and persistent code→test attribution\nslug: acceptance-design-to-code-coverage-seam-2026-09-02-runtime\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-04\nowner: su-6bcf6fd9-20c3-459a-a553-f8c602677cf0\n---\n\n# Acceptance: falsifiable completion evidence and persistent code→test attribution\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). D-008 reconciles the later Papercusp-only resume direction in session_turn:claude:8b243b44-d9d8-497c-babc-e5af36d6592e:0 with the explicit IQ-battery and improvement-implement pauses retained in turn 13. Those reserved lanes remain paused. P-012 stays blocked on production lifecycle integration tracked by EI-24932377195872399 and exact-generation independent release evidence. The goal remains one evidence-backed experiment and one promotion authority for every learning change.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2144596 — Define the single learning contract for candidates, experiments, evidence, decisions, activation, rollback, actor attribution, pot scope, and delayed outcomes. Default observations, policy updates, lens weights, and feedback to the owning pot; expose workspace rollups separately; require explicit provenance a… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144604 — Build a reproducible baseline/challenger battery with development, sealed acceptance holdout, and fresh monitoring tasks. Pin task, model, prompt, rubric, code, evaluator, exposure, randomization, re… <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144605 — Compare the current Gym optimizer, a simple trace-reflection baseline, and GEPA under matched task splits, models, exposure, and total spend; select based on measured quality, regression, uncertainty… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144606 — Migrate Scout, Gym, calibration, transfer, regret, and Red Queen outputs into the common candidate/evidence/decision lifecycle; retire alternate promotion and reward writers only after parity evidenc… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-2144607 — Re-run the Blender release rubric and both provenance-isolated drills against a current generation after the owner lifts the pause; require complete scorecards, independent criterion review, freshnes… <!-- P-012 -->\n## Background\n\nThe current Blender surface has reactive capture, Scout generation, Gym optimization, calibration, transfer, regret mining, and Red Queen drills. The existing experiment/eval-battery and learning-governor surfaces are valuable reuse points. The audit found an automatic Gym promotion path that can bypass optimizer gates, missing deterministic regression signals in the default adapter, an invalid confidence claim in the release metric, incomplete local spend accounting, grade-over-outcome reward credit, and ambiguous pot versus workspace ownership.\n\nGrading currently has three distinct layers that must not be conflated:\n- individual routed ideas are graded through `blender:grade-idea`;\n- automated success metrics and standard release scorecards assess the pipeline;\n- plan acceptance uses a separate independent grading cascade.\nThe plan must name the reviewer and authority for each layer.\n\n## Requirements\n\nWhen this redesign is complete, every candidate change has one immutable candidate-version record that names its parent, variant, task/model/prompt/rubric/code and evaluator hashes, evidence receipts, gate results, actor attribution, pot scope, spend settlement, uncertainty, and rollback target. Promotion is possible only from that complete record and its single authoritative verdict; an earlier opinion, a positive dev-anchor delta, or a missing measurement cannot activate it.\n\nRequired evaluator and probe signals are explicit `pass`, `fail`, or `not-measured` values with task coverage and artifact references. Missing required evidence is inconclusive and cannot be treated as a pass. Release statistics report a valid confidence bound for nonzero errors and distinguish historical improvement from the literal release bar. Every spend attempt is reserved and settled, including proposer calls, partial evaluation, cancellation, and failure, with requested, reserved, used, and unsettled amounts visible.\n\nReviewer provenance is complete and independent: individual ideas record the resolved human/agent/Mug attribution and retain the D-012 no-self-grade guard; standard Blender scorecards have a named non-author, non-implementer substantive steward or judge; the integrity auditor records evidence completeness separately; plan acceptance retains the relevance-selected cascade of up to two independent graders. Pot-owned observations and policy updates never silently become workspace-wide or cross-pot learning.\n\nA reproducible baseline/challenger battery covers development, sealed acceptance holdout, and fresh monitoring tasks with pinned task, model, prompt, rubric, code, evaluator, exposure, randomization, repeat, and cost receipts. Scout, Gym, calibration, transfer, regret, and Red Queen outputs converge on the common lifecycle, and release re-certification includes complete scorecards, independent review, freshness, provenance-isolated drills, and reproducible rollback. D-008 records the later Papercusp-only resume direction. IQ-battery and improvement-implement remain paused under the retained owner controls.\n\nThe following records backfill the existing acceptance requirements; they do not certify completed work.\n\n**R-1 — Production learning decisions use one complete lifecycle.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Make the pre-release decision and evaluation core evidence-backed before release.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a06e1b-74f7-73a2-8ecc-ffe0e85a82f1:10\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0ffa1-cf31-7e23-a0ab-f064cc924f61:6\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Scout, Gym, calibration, transfer, regret and Red Queen production outputs use one immutable candidate/evidence/decision contract. Activation consumes its complete current-parent verdict and captured rollback target. Alternate writers retire only after source-artifact and evidence-kind parity with zero backlog. Every spend attempt is reserved and settled, including proposer calls, failure, partial evaluation and cancellation; missing measurements prevent acceptance.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A producer output bypasses the common contract; a failed or unmeasured candidate activates; a source artifact is lost; a legacy writer is retired with missing parity or backlog; incurred spend lacks a settlement.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"scout\",\n      \"gym\",\n      \"calibration\",\n      \"transfer\",\n      \"regret\",\n      \"red-queen\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\n      \"pass\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise actual production writer and activation boundaries with private fixtures and pinned candidates. Inspect stored source identities, hashes, spend, verdict and rollback. Try missing evidence, rejected gates, stale parent, partial failure and legacy backlog. Pure adapter tests alone cannot satisfy migration.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/experiment/contract.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/experiment/lifecycle-adapter.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/gym/__tests__/promotion-gate.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Learning effectiveness and review remain independently evidenced.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Make grading ownership explicit and choose the optimizer using demonstrated outcomes.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a06e1b-74f7-73a2-8ecc-ffe0e85a82f1:10\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0ffa1-cf31-7e23-a0ab-f064cc924f61:6\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Required evaluator signals carry pass/fail/not-measured coverage and artifacts. Nonzero-error confidence bounds are valid. Matured artifact-grouped outcomes determine effectiveness, pot-owned feedback stays local without explicit transfer, and matched baseline/challenger, reflection and GEPA comparisons pin exposure, sealed holdout, randomization, repeats and complete cost. Idea reviews preserve no-self-grade; release review records independent substantive reviewer attribution distinct from integrity auditing.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Missing evidence passes; confidence is overstated; a failed matured artifact earns success because of a grade; cross-pot learning lacks transfer provenance; optimizer comparison omits matched controls; substantive review comes from the author or lacks attribution.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"evaluator\",\n      \"statistics\",\n      \"reward\",\n      \"pot-scope\",\n      \"battery\",\n      \"optimizer-comparison\",\n      \"reviewer-provenance\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\n      \"pass\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Reconcile immutable battery receipts and matured reward records to pinned task/model/prompt/rubric/code/evaluator hashes and actual exposure. Reproduce nonzero-error statistics and absent signals. Inspect reviewer matrix and real attribution/refusal paths. Treat historical status labels as evidence to inspect, never independent efficacy proof.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Exact-generation public release is independently certified.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Complete original release acceptance before declaring the program shipped.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a06e1b-74f7-73a2-8ecc-ffe0e85a82f1:10\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0ffa1-cf31-7e23-a0ab-f064cc924f61:6\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Public release requires complete fresh Blender release scorecards on one identified current artifact/generation, independent substantive criterion review, both provenance-isolated drills, and reproducible rollback. Final shipment evidence names the exact shipped artifact and serving runtimes; current-build proof alone cannot establish shipment. IQ-battery and improvement-implement remain paused under the explicit retained controls.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Release is claimed with an unknown generation, stale or incomplete scorecard, author review, either missing drill, unverified rollback, no exact shipped artifact, or either reserved lane re-enabled.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"release-rubric\",\n      \"provenance-isolated-drill-1\",\n      \"provenance-isolated-drill-2\",\n      \"rollback\",\n      \"artifact-runtime-provenance\",\n      \"retained-pauses\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"deployed\",\n    \"evidenceRuntime\": \"bg-host\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\n      \"pass\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"After producer integration, pin current bg-host generation and exact artifact/runtime identity. Obtain independent fresh substantive Blender release grading, execute both existing drills within approved budgets, preserve their fixture/source provenance and demonstrate rollback. Verify release-operator shipment separately from bg-host source binding and retain receipts. No unknown measurement may become pass.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing experiment/types.ts, experiment/run-core.ts, learning-governor, change-ledger, and work-item provenance seams. A candidate writer creates an immutable version envelope; the evaluator attaches typed evidence and receipts; the governor reserves and settles spend; a single decision function compares against the current parent and emits the only promotion verdict; activation and rollback consume that verdict atomically. Alternate positive-anchor promotion and reward writers are removed after parity evidence.\n\nKeep reviewer selection and attribution in a separate provenance layer. `blender:grade-idea` resolves the actor according to the source surface and refuses self-grade; release-card review requires an independent substantive steward or judge while the integrity auditor emits a distinct completeness result; plan-acceptance cards use the existing independent two-grader cascade. Store observations, weights, and feedback under the owning pot and expose workspace rollups with explicit transfer provenance.\n\nUse the existing eval-battery to run matched baseline/challenger cohorts, sealed holdouts, and fresh monitoring tasks. Persist hashes, randomization, exposure, repeats, costs, confidence calculations, and delayed/right-censored outcomes in the common evidence record. Final release re-certification follows actual producer migration and parity; D-008 resolves the historical blanket pause while reserved pauses remain binding.\n\n### Bar-to-work\n\n| Bar | Plan items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-005, P-011 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003, P-004, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-012 | deployed |\n\nProducer migration requires tests of actual writer and activation boundaries; direct pure-adapter fixtures alone cannot satisfy R-1. R-3 is final shipment verification on the identified background-host generation and exact shipped artifact; independent work proceeds on current-build evidence.\n\n## Phase 1 — Make evidence and authority trustworthy\n\n- **P-001** `done` Define the single learning contract for candidates, experiments, evidence, decisions, activation, rollback, actor attribution, pot scope, and delayed outcomes. Final acceptance blocked by owned producer-integration gap EI-24932377195872399 plus unproven generation parity/fresh rubric+drill evidence; not shipped.\n\n## Decisions\n\n- The owner pause on self-improvement routines remains in force throughout this plan.\n- Existing experiment/eval-battery, governor, change-ledger, and provenance surfaces are the default extension points.\n- A candidate cannot activate from an earlier opinion, a partial signal, or an alternate acceptance formula.\n\n### D-001 — Reviewer matrix — three grading regimes, their reviewer rules, and the provenance recorded for each\nDate: 2026-09-04\nSpecifies P-006. Three regimes, each with its own reviewer rule — do not collapse them.\n\nREGIME 1 — INDIVIDUAL SCOUT IDEAS (`blender:grade-idea`).\nReviewer is the CALLER, derived from ctx, never caller-supplied. `deriveGradedBy`: role `mug` yields `auto-grader`; else the resolved `ctx.ownerId`; else the literal `owner`, reserved for an unidentifiable human surface so autonomous grades cannot take the owner's sovereign slot. Self-grading is REFUSED before the ledger write when `scout_routed_ideas.created_by === caller ownerId` (`applied:false`, `reason:'no-self-grade'`): a self-grade would pollute lens weights (C-5), ideator priming (C-4) and the P-005 grade-to-revise wake.\n\nGUARD-SCOPE RULING (load-bearing). The guard is caller-attributed and FAILS OPEN by design: `resolveCallerOwnerId` returns null when `resolveAgentIdentity` throws, and a null caller skips the comparison. One unattributable ctx therefore produces BOTH effects at once — attribution falls back to the literal `owner` AND the no-self-grade comparison is skipped. Source-verified; the deployed-path RATE of unattributable ctx is NOT. P-006's \"verify it in the deployed path\" is discharged only by measuring that rate on live invocations, not by re-reading source.\n\nREGIME 2 — STANDARD BLENDER RELEASE SCORECARDS.\nSubstantive criterion review requires a NAMED reviewer who is neither the card's author nor the subject's implementer, recorded as kind `substantive`. The grading-integrity auditor is a SEPARATE role that does NOT satisfy it: per P-013 (D-004, goal-mode-design-intent-hardening-2026-08-16) a terminal card stays `gradingAudit.state:'pending'` until a NON-AUTHOR auditor grades it against the `grading-integrity` meta-rubric — ONE level only (the audit card is never itself stamped pending), TERMINAL cards only, dispatch limit 50. It establishes evidence COMPLETENESS, is recorded `integrity-audit` never `substantive`, and alone leaves substantive review outstanding.\n\nREGIME 3 — PLAN ACCEPTANCE CARDS.\nRetain the relevance-selected cascade (unified-responder-selection-critique-and-grading-2026-08-30, D-001/D-003/D-005): min 1 / max 2 — grader 2 woken only after grader 1 replies, declines or expires, HOLDING grader 1's card. Eligibility refuses `grader_in_implementer_lineage` (implementer = `rubric.createdBy ?? rubric.proposedBy` plus principal implementers, via `areAcceptanceLineageRelated`); selection excludes plan participants, rubric author, shipper. Below the floor it makes a declared BEST-AVAILABLE minimum-fill pick, and says so.\n\nINDEPENDENCE RULING (load-bearing, D-003 [owner]). Only the FIRST card is an independent sample; the carried card anchors grader 2, so the second grading is a REVIEW of the first. Nothing downstream may call the pair two independent gradings; grader 2's agreement is not corroboration. Read Requirements' \"up to two independent graders\" as \"one independent grader plus an anchored reviewing grader\" — the authority read selects exactly ONE independent card.\n\nRECORDED FOR EVERY REVIEW, ALL REGIMES. (1) reviewer identity; (2) role — `owner` | `<ownerId>` | `auto-grader` | named steward/judge | integrity auditor; (3) selection route — caller-derived, cascade position k/menuSize with above-floor or minimum-fill noted, or audit dispatch; (4) the rubric REVISION reviewed against; (5) kind — `substantive` or `integrity-audit`. Kind is NOT inferable from identity; store it explicitly.\n\nDANGLING REF REPAIRED. P-006's `decisionRefs:['D-012']` does not resolve here: this plan parsed zero decisions before this one, so `missingRefs` returns empty and nothing flags it. The referent is the BINDING owner decision of 2026-07-10 cited inline in grade-idea.ts. D-NNN ids are plan-local and five unrelated plans carry their own D-012, so cite it as grade-idea.ts's D-012, never a bare \"D-012\".\n\nMeasured 2026-09-04; paths under packages/operator-core/lib/.\n- agent-tools/scout/grade-idea.ts:55-58 `deriveGradedBy` (L56 mug->auto-grader; L58 `return ownerId || 'owner'`).\n- grade-idea.ts:427 `D-012 (owner 2026-07-10, BINDING)`; L435 `const callerOwnerId = ctx?.ownerId ?? null`; L439 `reason: 'no-self-grade'`.\n- grade-idea.ts:571-575 `resolveCallerOwnerId` catch -> `return null` (fail-open); L411 `deriveGradedBy(ctx)` + L599 `runGradeIdea(args,{role,ownerId})` — ONE ownerId feeds both attribution and guard.\n- consult/grading-cascade.ts:7-8 min1/max2 cascade; L178 \"...two independent gradings\"; L195 wake copy \"a REVIEW of it, not a blind second sample\".\n- agent-tools/scorecards/grader-eligibility.ts:36,282 `grader_in_implementer_lineage`; L230 implementer resolution.\n- acceptance-grading-authority.ts:305 `complete.find((c) => c.acceptance == null)`; L307 `no_independent_card`.\n- grading-integrity.ts:21 `GRADING_INTEGRITY_RUBRIC_REF`; L28 `GRADING_AUDIT_DISPATCH_LIMIT = 50`.\n- NOT measured: deployed-path rate of unattributable ctx; whether a named steward/judge role exists in code (Regime 2). Both stated unverified above.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-002 — Deployed-path measurement of the Regime-1 no-self-grade guard — clean where evaluable, structurally blind on 42% of graded rows\nDate: 2026-09-04\nDischarges the \"verify it in the deployed path\" requirement that D-001 left explicitly NOT measured for P-006 Regime 1. D-001's body sits at the 5000-char cap, so this lands as its own decision; read the two together.\n\nFINDING 1 — CLEAN WHERE EVALUABLE. Of 607 graded rows, 353 (58%) carry a known originator and ZERO are self-grades. Non-vacuous: the comparison actually ran on all 353.\n\nFINDING 2 — STRUCTURALLY UNEVALUABLE ON 254 ROWS (42%), and the boundary is exactly origin='scout'. Every scout-origin graded row has created_by NULL (254/254); every other origin has it populated (su-ideate 241, agent-review 88, shadow-variant 20, drill 4 — zero nulls). The guard compares scout_routed_ideas.created_by === caller ownerId, so a NULL originator skips the comparison for the same reason a null caller does. \"Zero self-grades\" is therefore an observation about 58% of the ledger, never a property of all of it.\n\nFINDING 3 — THE FAIL-OPEN RATE IS BOUNDED, NOT ZERO. deriveGradedBy returns `ownerId || 'owner'`, so a fail-open resolveCallerOwnerId and a genuine human owner grade write the SAME literal `owner`. 250/607 rows (41%) carry it. 41% is thus the UPPER BOUND on unattributable-ctx grades, and the two cases are not separable after the fact. On 79 rows BOTH legs are blind (graded_by='owner' AND created_by IS NULL).\n\nRULING. Regime 1's guard is sound where evaluable and must NOT be described as verified end-to-end. Any claim that self-grading \"cannot happen\" is unsupported for scout-origin ideas. Two follow-ups, neither blocking P-006: (a) write created_by on scout-origin rows, or record explicitly that scout-origin ideas have no gradeable creator, so the 42% is a declared category rather than a silent skip; (b) distinguish fail-open from genuine-owner at write time (a distinct label or an attribution-failed flag), so the 41% stops being unsplittable.\n\nCORRECTION (self). An earlier in-session reading of this same question reported 335 graded rows, 155 owner-label rows, and \"every row carrying an originator\". All three were WRONG — re-measured: 607, 250, and 254 rows with a NULL originator. The third error was the load-bearing one: it asserted the very blind spot Finding 2 establishes does exist. Nothing downstream consumed those figures (they never reached D-001 or a peer), and they are corrected here so the measured numbers are the ones on the record.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-04, dev:pg_query over harness_shared.scout_routed_ideas WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND graded_by IS NOT NULL (positive control passed, 1 row). Totals — graded 607; self_grades 0; created_by NULL 254; graded_by='owner' 250; 'auto-grader' 16; resolved ownerId 341; graded before 2026-07-10 (grade-idea.ts D-012) 0; first grade 2026-07-14T00:42:02Z, last 2026-09-01T07:35:38Z. GROUP BY origin — scout 254 graded / 254 null-creator / 79 doubly-blind; su-ideate 241/0; agent-review 88/0; shadow-variant 20/0; drill 4/0.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-003 — P-007 reward dimensions are artifact-grouped and outcome-matured\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-007 uses a separated reward report with six explicit dimensions: reviewer preference, artifact delivery, measured effectiveness, regressions, cost, and uncertainty. The report groups routed provenance by routedRef before attribution; one fused artifact contributes one unit of mass split across its distinct source lenses, so source rows cannot multiply success or cost. Reviewer grades remain a prioritization signal only. Effectiveness is populated only by a matured outcome; pending and right-censored outcomes remain visible and are excluded from matured means. The existing computeLensOutcomes API remains byte-compatible during migration, while getScoutRewardReport is the new live routed-ledger seam. Measured: npm --workspace @papercusp/operator-core test -- lib/scout/reward.test.ts lib/scout/outcome-feedback.test.ts lib/scout/routed-ledger.test.ts --run => 52 tests passed (5 reward, 38 outcome-feedback, 9 routed-ledger); source paths packages/operator-core/lib/scout/reward.ts and routed-ledger.ts were read at implementation.\nRelated: P-007, P-009, P-011\n\n### D-004 — P-009 batteries pin identity and isolate cohorts\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-009 extends the existing experiment:run seam with a pure ReproducibleBattery specification. Every battery pins task, model, prompt, rubric, code, evaluator, baseline arm, exposure, fixed-seed randomization, repeats, and optional budget. Development, sealed-acceptance, and fresh-monitoring cohorts require non-empty, disjoint case ids; holdout cases must carry sealed=true and monitoring cases fresh=true. planReproducibleBattery deterministically expands arm × case × repeat cells, while toRunExperimentInput maps one cohort to the existing dry-run request without spend. Cost receipts validate requested/reserved/used/unsettled amounts, receipt-cell uniqueness, cohort membership, and governor bounds; missing receipts remain unmeasured rather than zero-cost.\n\nMeasured: npm --workspace @papercusp/operator-core test -- lib/experiment/battery.test.ts lib/experiment/run-core.test.ts lib/experiment/contract.test.ts --run => 28 tests passed. Source read: packages/operator-core/lib/experiment/battery.ts and packages/operator-core/lib/experiment/run-core.ts.\nRelated: P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-005 — P-010 matched optimizer comparison uses uncertainty-adjusted sealed holdout selection\nDate: 2026-09-05\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-010 extends the P-009 battery contract with a pure comparison seam for the current Gym optimizer, a simple trace-reflection baseline, and GEPA. Every method must carry identical task split coverage (development, sealed-acceptance, fresh-monitoring), task/model/prompt/rubric/code/evaluator pins, fixed randomization seed, repeats, exposure, and per-method spend cap. Selection reads only the sealed-acceptance split: measured regressions are hard failures, missing regression or uncertainty evidence is an inconclusive gap, and a challenger must clear Gym's quality upper bound with its own lower bound. Actual cost remains explicit, bounded by the matched cap and the existing 3x cost ceiling by default, and breaks equal-quality ties. No paid optimizer or paused background routine is invoked by this seam; adapters can supply recorded runs later.\n\nMeasured: npm --workspace @papercusp/operator-core test -- lib/experiment/optimizer-comparison.test.ts lib/experiment/battery.test.ts lib/experiment/run-core.test.ts lib/experiment/contract.test.ts --run => 36 tests passed. Full operator-core typecheck reached the compiler with no P-010 diagnostics; the current red result is from unrelated peer files fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts and plans/audit.test.ts.\nRelated: P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-006 — P-011 routes six producer outputs through one validated lifecycle before legacy retirement\nDate: 2026-09-05\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-011 adds pure adapters for Scout, Gym, calibration, transfer, regret, and Red Queen outputs into the existing LearningContract shape. Each adapter preserves candidate identity, experiment pins, typed evidence with coverage and artifact references, governor spend reservation/settlement, one decision authority, optional activation, and matured/pending outcomes. Accepted contracts fail closed when any evidence is failed, not measured, or incomplete. Legacy promotion and reward writers are retained until evaluateLifecycleParity confirms every legacy artifact reference and required evidence kind are represented; canRetireLegacyWriter also requires the legacy backlog to be zero. No source writer is silently removed and no paused learning routine is invoked.\n\nMeasured: npm --workspace @papercusp/operator-core test -- lib/experiment/lifecycle-adapter.test.ts lib/experiment/contract.test.ts lib/learning-governor/spend.test.ts --run => 37 tests passed. Full operator-core typecheck had no P-011 diagnostics; current red files are unrelated peer edits.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-007 — P-012 is owner-gated, not stalled — the pause is independently corroborated and the unblock condition is one owner action\nDate: 2026-09-05\nDate: 2026-09-05. Governs P-012 (work-item WI-2144607).\n\nVERDICT: P-012 is NOT executable now, and the only action that would make it executable is explicitly forbidden by this plan's ## Now. Correct status is `needs-human`, not `todo`. This is a GATE, not a stall — do not re-claim it as actionable work, and do not re-derive the investigation below.\n\nWHY — measured, and NOT taken on trust from this plan's own ## Now:\nP-012 requires re-running the release rubric and both provenance-isolated drills \"against a current generation\". Every producer of a generation is an owner-paused self-improvement routine.\n\nMeasured: `routines:list { rollup:true }` at 2026-09-05T01:16Z → group `self-improvement` (\"Gym/scout/blueprint-singleton learning loops + the improvement pipeline\"): count 34, activeCount 0, pausedCount 26, mostRecentFire 2026-09-01T22:52:02.638Z (>3 days cold).\n\nMeasured: `routines:list { group:'self-improvement' }` → the pause rows carry OWNER attribution in their own `paused.reason`, and none self-resumes (`autoResumesAt:null, finite:false` on every one):\n- gym-cycle, improvement-triage, improvement-implement, improvement-human-digest — \"Owner-directed pause 2026-08-22 while scheduled LLM/background spend is inventoried and public-release defaults are redesigned\"\n- improvement-watchdog, improvement-invalid-args-miner — \"Owner-directed pause of all learning loops on 2026-08-24\"\n\nThat is the load-bearing point: the pause is corroborated INDEPENDENTLY of the ## Now prose, by the routine records themselves. A stored plan claim would not have been sufficient.\n\nDELIBERATELY NOT MEASURED: whether a \"current generation\" is a stored row anywhere. `dev:pg_query { describe:'*generation*' }` returned 0 relations — which is evidence for neither side, so I am not resting on it. The argument does not need it: every PRODUCER has been stopped for 3+ days, so a *current* generation cannot exist regardless of how generations are stored.\n\nA false-negative worth recording: `routines:list { q:'blender' }` returns ZERO rows. The routines are named gym/scout/improvement-*, never \"blender\". Searching the filer's vocabulary would have concluded \"no such routines exist\"; searching the CLASS (the routine group) found all 34. Do not re-run the vocabulary search and read its zero as an answer.\n\nTHE UNBLOCK CONDITION, stated precisely so the owner's decision is one step and not an investigation:\n1. Owner lifts the pause on install `papercusp`, group `self-improvement` (`routines:group-set` for the group, or `routines:set` per routine). 26 rows are paused; all are `finite:false`, so nothing resumes on its own and no amount of waiting changes this.\n2. Let the loops produce one current generation.\n3. THEN P-012 runs as written: release rubric + both provenance-isolated drills, requiring complete scorecards, independent criterion review, freshness, and a reproducible rollback before public release.\n\nWHY AUTO/DRAIN DOES NOT WAIVE THIS: an AUTO grant lets an agent pass approval gates on its own judgment. This is not an approval gate. It is (a) an unmet factual precondition and (b) a prohibition on the only act that would meet it. Re-arming autonomous background learning loops is fleet-autonomy escalation — a residual owner-wall AUTO does not cover — and this plan's ## Now forbids it independently: \"no item in this plan may resume or re-arm them without a later owner decision.\" Closing P-012 as `done` would therefore be a false completion, and dropping it would discard a real pre-release requirement.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-008 — P-012's blanket owner-pause gate has a later release direction; actual provenance and producer integration now block acceptance\nDate: 2026-10-03\n[turn:self] [self-imposed interpretation of later recorded authority; not a new owner decision] Updates D-007's current applicability without asserting GO or waiving acceptance evidence.\n\nSOURCE AUTHORITY: orders:get #1111 returned the literal owner instruction to re-enable learning/dreaming/bulk review for papercusp only. Its machine-returned sourceTurnRef is 8b243b44-d9d8-497c-babc-e5af36d6592e:5ce14383c25c9c81b6f719a51f13987c7e3d6acbb39b2442769b2f557c9f2b0c; sessionRef8b243b44-d9d8-497c-babc-e5af36d6592e. WI-10004483 and that directive's disposition record explicit IQ-battery/improvement-implement exceptions. Those pauses remain binding. This loop-origin turn records the source read and interpretation, never substitutes for an owner-typed turn.\n\nMeasured Oct3: routines:list {installSlug:'papercusp',group:'self-improvement'} shows approved gym-cycle/triage/watchdog producers active with recent fires; improvement-implement stays inactive/indefinitely paused. No routine/control was changed here. Active/lastFired is scheduler evidence, not completed-generation or quality proof; the Sept5 blanket-pause premise is obsolete.\n\nGeneration semantics: scout/generation-watermark.ts readBgHostActiveEnterMs/readRunningGeneration derive generation from runtime start and boot/source identity, not a learning routine's output. blender:success-metrics {harnessSlug:'papercusp',watermarkRef:'bg-host-restart'} returned hostStartedAt2026-10-03T04:08:00Z, bootHeadSha14842e6873..., querying deployedSha d740fc3802, scoutCodeHash:null and staleHost:true. The writer defines staleHost as not-proven-fresh, so this does NOT prove broken host code; it prevents an unqualified generation-parity PASS.\n\nSeparate prerequisite: P-011's stored completion is pure-library proof. Scoped production-source searches across packages, libs, apps and scripts find the six common lifecycle adapters/parity guards/validator only at their own definitions, and tests use handcrafted input. Owned EI-24932377195872399 investigates and repairs production wiring before P-011 is treated as migrated. Existing Gym immutable-verdict policy is separate and must remain intact; reuse the implemented adapters/contract/ledger rather than create a parallel lifecycle.\n\nP-012 remains incomplete and blocked. Prerequisites are actual producer integration, exact artifact/generation provenance, fresh complete rubric evidence, both provenance-isolated drills, independent substantive review and reproducible rollback. Current instrument UNKNOWNs for error/diversity/reconciliation remain UNKNOWN. No paid cycle, drill, self-grade, release-gate action or shipment occurred. This material dependency/decision change requires a fresh activation audit of the complete source conversation before further plan activation/execution.\nRelated: P-011, P-012\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"blender-release-readiness","title":"Blender public-release readiness","status":"active","created":"2026-09-04","owner":"su-respawn-6d9ff0dad81028899a3642dd5017ec60","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"remote","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Blender public-release readiness\nslug: blender-release-readiness\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-04\nowner: su-respawn-6d9ff0dad81028899a3642dd5017ec60\n---\n\n# Blender public-release readiness\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** The Mug ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting this plan to `active`\n(rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nGO/NO-GO testing gate for shipping the blender learning pipeline (scout ideation → routing → grading → learning) to the public. [owner:Avi 2026-07-13] directed its creation, and [owner:Avi 2026-07-13] directed it be IMPROVED as it is used for grading. Every criterion is a defect class the 2026-07-12/13 hardening session PROVED can rot silently — and each carries a copy-runnable replication drill, because a bar you cannot re-run on demand is 'it worked yesterday', not a release gate. Complements su-ideation-health (ongoing su-ideate loop health); this rubric is the release-scoped judgment over the whole blender pipeline. Created/authored by su-eb9b7ae3; v1 revision re-proposed by su-f69a7 folding in su-eb9b7ae3's scorecard-#1 grading deltas, ratified by su-eb9b7ae3 per WI-4497. Each criterion's model ends with a machine-readable [instrumentKey: <blender:success-metrics key | none>] mapping bar→instrument (WI-4504/P-003 health badges consume this; it is data, not tribal knowledge). TOKEN FORMAT (pinned, deterministic, per eb9b7 ask): the token is exactly `[instrumentKey: <key>]` as the LAST token in each criterion's model field, where <key> is a lowercase blender:success-metrics criterion key matching /[a-z0-9-]+/ or the literal `none`; consumers parse /\\[instrumentKey:\\s*([a-z0-9-]+|none)\\]\\s*$/ against the model string. V2 (2026-07-16, rubric-system-hardening-2026-07-14 P-008): + generation-parity criterion (consumes the P-002 watermark window, P-003 gradedGeneration scorecard stamp, and P-007 runningGeneration echo); grading-coverage floor (eligible-stale==0) on grading-loop-closure; lens-diversity >=4 distinct/7d bar on multi-lens-routing; capacity-storm red-path clause on e2e-drill (P-006 drill mode); releaseGating:true (arms the P-004 staleness watchdog — a >6h complete-scorecard gap on this rubric now pages) and a structured grading window on every criterion (P-001 resolveCriterionWindow). V2 proposed AND ratified by su-f8714 under the explicit owner AUTO grant [owner:Avi 2026-07-16 'put yourself on auto mode and continue with the rubric hardening plan until it is complete'] — proposer==ratifier is disclosed per D-012, not concealed. V2->V3 (2026-08-16, blender-loop-repair-and-opus5-xhigh-2026-08-16 P-008 / WI-39480): added error-tick-rate, auto-adopt-liveness, and outcome-provenance -- three defect classes the 2026-08-16 audit found LIVE and invisible to the graded rubric (journald-only degradations; the WI-5414 auto-adopt sweep dead since it shipped behind manual button-clicks; 600/746 outcomes copied from 4 frozen niche verdicts while the gym was disabled). Each carries its incident as the red-path calibration. V3->V4 (2026-09-04, EI-19370536181527310): added fitness-signal-is-real as an explicit graded criterion bound to the existing programmatic bar, so corpus reality is no longer grader-discretionary.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"code-intelligence-routing-lsp-gitnexus-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: code-intelligence routing, shared LSP, GitNexus hardening, and packers","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-04","owner":"su-382bc062-3709-4d40-a18d-cf6ad761a235","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: code-intelligence routing, shared LSP, GitNexus hardening, and packers\nslug: code-intelligence-routing-lsp-gitnexus-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-04\nowner: su-382bc062-3709-4d40-a18d-cf6ad761a235\n---\n\n# Acceptance: code-intelligence routing, shared LSP, GitNexus hardening, and packers\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric).
