Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"desktop-health-per-bridge-correlation-2026-09-04","title":"Desktop health per-bridge correlation","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-04","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Desktop health per-bridge correlation\nslug: desktop-health-per-bridge-correlation-2026-09-04\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-04\n---\n## Now\n\nImplemented and verified under the already-claimed fleet item `EI-19357343092509867`. This draft is the required design record; it was not launched and did not change the selected fleet-member route.\n\n## Background\n\nMultiple Tauri desktop bridges can be live under one HOME. Each bridge owns a webview and a mutable runtime API target, but `desktop-health.ts` previously checked all bridge evals against one global `desktop-build-target.json`, then combined that global IPC/API result with an arbitrary successful bridge eval. Signals from different desktops could therefore manufacture either an UP or DOWN verdict.\n\nExisting substrate extended:\n\n- `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/dev_bridge.rs` already serves an authenticated per-process `/health` response.\n- `crate::SELECTED_API_PORT` is the authoritative live API target and changes when the environment switcher retargets the desktop.\n- `endpoint-ipc.<port>.json` is the existing per-port IPC discovery surface.\n- Existing singleton-based exported helpers remain for compatibility; the desktop-health recurring probe now uses strict per-port helpers.\n\nSource audit: full originating session `claude:923c2bb2-63d2-490d-a5a0-1ff6d9381ce3` turns 0–7, current item/checkpoint, and current Rust/TypeScript writers were read on 2026-09-04. No additional owner constraint exists beyond the per-bridge fix and normal evidence-backed drain completion.\n\n## Design\n\n1. Extend the bridge's authenticated `/health` JSON with `selected_api_port`, loaded at request time from `SELECTED_API_PORT`; bump the bridge protocol version because the HTTP response shape changes.\n2. Have desktop-health request `/health` for each live bridge and parse only a finite TCP port.\n3. For each bridge independently, evaluate one tuple: bridge eval, selected API port, strict `endpoint-ipc.<port>.json` connectability, and API round-trip to that same port.\n4. Aggregate tuple outcomes only after each tuple is complete. Any healthy complete tuple makes the desktop UP. A bridge with healthy eval but unavailable/legacy target metadata abstains from target checks and prevents a false DOWN. The desktop is DOWN only when every bridge-local possibility is conclusively unhealthy.\n5. Never fall back to the last-writer-wins singleton in the new per-bridge path. Retain existing singleton helpers for unrelated compatibility callers/tests.\n\n## Acceptance evidence\n\n- PASS — `/health` reports the bridge's current selected API port, with Rust regression coverage for the JSON contract.\n- PASS — desktop-health evaluates IPC and API status using the port learned from each specific bridge.\n- PASS — a passing eval from bridge A cannot combine with healthy IPC/API from bridge B to produce UP.\n- PASS — one fully healthy bridge keeps the aggregate UP even when another bridge is unhealthy.\n- PASS — missing legacy bridge target metadata abstains explicitly and does not create a false DOWN.\n- PASS — focused tests: 47/47 desktop-health, 114/114 service-health, and 1/1 Rust response-contract test; scoped TypeScript formatting and Rust formatting pass. Package typecheck remains blocked only by the unrelated pre-existing TS1308 in `agent-tools/plans/with-plan-lock.ts`; a filtered compiler run emitted no desktop-health diagnostics.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Reuse the authenticated bridge health endpoint\n\nNo new discovery file or singleton is introduced.\n\n### D-002 — Read the live atomic at request time\n\nPersisted startup configuration is not authoritative after an environment switch.\n\n### D-003 — Use strict per-port lookup in the recurring probe\n\nFalling back to the global singleton would recreate the reported bug.\n\n### D-004 — Preserve compatibility exports\n\nExisting singleton-based helpers remain available while the recurring health probe moves to bridge-local correlation.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"green-main-system-audit-and-red-streak-elimination-2026-09-04","title":"Green-main system audit: eliminate multi-day red streaks and make recovery bounded","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-04","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Green-main system audit: eliminate multi-day red streaks and make recovery bounded\nslug: green-main-system-audit-and-red-streak-elimination-2026-09-04\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-19\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-19. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nOwner-directed full-system audit is beginning while the existing frozen candidate/repair-head greening lane remains intact. The exact dependency publisher completed successfully; the subsequent ordinary run exposed a separate pre-test checkpoint-permission defect, now under repair. This audit must not bypass the frozen lineage with tip convergence, queue retirement, a manual checkpoint run, or force deployment.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Background\n\nThe owner reports approximately fifteen days without a fresh green and observes that repeated fixes and multiple plans over the last two weeks have not restored continuous greening. The audit treats that as a hypothesis to prove from primary run, verdict, main, deploy, plan, work-item, and source-code records—not as a metric whose name is self-explanatory.\n\nPlan-aware dedup surfaced the shipped `gate-audit-hardening-2026-08-31` and `gate-verdict-liveness-and-repair-reliability-2026-08-31` plans plus three superseded acceptance templates. This is deliberately a new audit because it evaluates whether those completed changes worked in production and why the red/no-verdict interval continued afterward; reopening one would mix historical implementation with its independent outcome audit.\n\n## Scope\n\nEnd-to-end: candidate selection and freezing; exact repair admission; dependency generation and cache publication; scheduler and run-lock behavior; test/lint execution; verdict persistence; promotion to main; deployment to :3070; ownership, recovery, and observability; and the plans/changes intended to improve those stages during the last two weeks.\n\nPreserve the currently ratified frozen lineage while auditing it. Do not use a manual checkpoint run, converge to staging tip, retire the active repair queue, or force-deploy around a red/inconclusive gate.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nThe final audit must (1) reconstruct the actual chronology from writers and ledgers; (2) classify every material delay/failure by originating mechanism rather than symptom; (3) map recent plan promises to code, tests, and live behavior; (4) state which parts of the core design are sound, which need redesign, and why; (5) evaluate whether the latest frozen-lineage plan is sufficient; (6) define measurable steady-state and incident-recovery targets consistent with no more than a few consecutive reds; and (7) register every substantive residual fix with a recurrence guard and verification path.\n\n## Phase 1 — Live critical path and evidence freeze\n- **P-001** `todo` Preserve and finish the current frozen lineage: validate the exact publisher selector/token; diagnose and durably fix every pre-test setup failure; admit only exact verified repair paths; resume only the ordinary scheduler; and capture promotion/:3070 evidence without tip convergence, queue retirement, manual checkpoint-run, or force-deploy. importance: urgent\n- **P-002** `done` Freeze a live audit baseline from writer-owned surfaces: canonical repair queue, gate ownership, routine control, run/verdict ledger, remote main, green pin, deployed process, and their provenance/units. Record unknown or stale values explicitly rather than treating counters as current verdicts. importance: high — note: ← WI-2144526 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Fifteen-day history and plan inventory\n- **P-003** `done` Inventory every green-main, checkpoint, release-recovery, frozen-candidate, dependency-generation, gate-observability, and fixer-reliability plan/decision/work-item changed in the owner-reported fifteen-day interval; deduplicate aliases and preserve supersession relationships. importance: high — note: ← WI-2144527 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Reconstruct the checkpoint/run chronology from primary ledgers: candidate and repair-head lineage, start/end/outcome, whether a suite actually ran, originating failure class, ownership transitions, promotion/main/deploy movements, and elapsed recovery intervals. Read each metric/status writer before interpreting it. importance: high — note: ← WI-2144528 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Map each material promise from the recent plans to the exact implementation, regression coverage, deployed/runtime version, and observed outcome; distinguish implemented-but-not-deployed, deployed-but-not-exercised, detector-only, mitigation-only, and genuinely preventive changes. blocked-by: P-003, P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-2144981 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Architecture and failure-mode audit\n- **P-006** `todo` Audit candidate selection, quiet-cut eligibility, frozen-candidate semantics, repair-queue state machine, exact path/hunk admission, and every known un-freezing path. Evaluate correctness, forward progress, concurrent-edit containment, and whether the model is comprehensible enough to operate safely. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Audit dependency input identity, generation publication, reuse, retention, selector/token leases, materialization, permissions, cleanup, and concurrency. Classify which failures can prevent tests from starting and verify each has a bounded recovery plus a recurrence detector. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n- **P-008** `todo` Audit scheduler cadence, pause/resume serialization, run locks, stale-run replacement, ownership/fixer succession, event wakes, and autonomous recovery. Determine whether any single dead process, stale lease, or missing event can leave the gate unjudged for hours or days. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n- **P-009** `todo` Audit suite selection/execution, test and lint result authority, inconclusive-versus-red classification, verdict persistence, green-pin promotion, remote main movement, deploy trigger/rollback, and live-process certification. Prove where a successful code fix can still fail to produce a new green. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n- **P-010** `todo` Audit observability and control: status-cell semantics, stale counters, run-phase/progress signals, failure taxonomy, alarms, repair ownership, operator guidance, and measurable SLOs. Identify false-green, false-red, false-owned, and silent-no-verdict states. blocked-by: P-004, P-005 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Design verdict and remediation program\n- **P-011** `todo` Evaluate the latest frozen-candidate plan against the historical failure taxonomy and architecture audit: state exactly what it prevents, what it merely makes visible, what it leaves untouched, and whether completing it is sufficient to restore and sustain green main. blocked-by: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010 importance: high\n- **P-012** `todo` Issue the core-design verdict per subsystem—keep, simplify, replace, or redesign—with explicit invariants and tradeoffs. Define operational targets for verdict freshness, consecutive-red/no-verdict bounds, time to owner pickup, time to first test, repair convergence, promotion, and deployment. blocked-by: P-011 importance: high\n- **P-013** `todo` Register and rank every residual substantive fix as plan items/work-items with root cause, recurrence guard, verification path, dependencies, and migration/cutover plan. Prefer extensions of existing surfaces over parallel systems. blocked-by: P-012 importance: high\n- **P-014** `todo` Publish the thorough owner-facing audit: chronology, failure taxonomy, recent-plan scorecard, current-plan sufficiency verdict, core-design assessment, target-state architecture, prioritized roadmap, and live greening status. Independently re-check every load-bearing number/status against its writer before delivery. blocked-by: P-001, P-013 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The fifteen-day ledger must be read as events, not runs; candidate churn is the dominant red-amplifier\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured: `harness_shared.pipeline_events`, scoped to workspace `papercusp-workspace`, install `papercusp`, after the last verdict-green row (`advanced` at 2026-08-20T20:55:17.536Z, candidate `a2d69cef50d5`) contains 500 `green_checkpoint` event rows: 101 verdict-red (`not-green`), 69 typed no-verdict rows, 231 skip rows, 96 `decision-pending` rows, and 3 promotion-failed rows. These are EVENT rows, not 500 runs: one fire may emit several. The 101 red verdict rows name 98 distinct candidate SHAs and 59 distinct failing-test sets; only three reds reused a candidate. Therefore the historical system overwhelmingly judged a moving target. A `consecutiveReds` headline cannot be interpreted as repeated failures of one repair, and any audit/alert must separately report candidate identity, terminal verdict class, and no-verdict/skip volume.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-010\n\n### D-002 — A gate-system plan is not effective when code-truth ships but the live controller remains on an older build\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured: `gate-verdict-liveness-and-repair-reliability-2026-08-31` is marked shipped (final update 2026-09-01T16:58:30Z), yet the post-finalization release-fixer ledger has 27 launches: 25 failed and 2 done. `dev:service_health` at 2026-09-04T20:41Z reports the routine bg-host alive but code-drifted (`loadedSha=47fba77388`, current source `f49702d62a...`); `release:deploy` reports the deployed operator at `6e898b6c...`. The related `frozen-candidate-freeze-actually-holds-2026-09-02` plan correctly remains awaiting-acceptance because its own live mechanism has never executed on the deployed build. Ruling: for code that operates the gate/control plane, unit/code-truth/staging acceptance is necessary but not sufficient. Activation on the real scheduler/controller plus at least one correlated live cycle is a blocking acceptance criterion, or the plan must say implemented-not-live rather than shipped.\nRelated: P-003, P-005, P-008, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-003 — Preserve immutable qualification semantics; redesign the orchestration and self-hosting boundary\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured basis: the current frozen queue remains exact (`candidate=1f43e05a...`, `repairHead=21f03de7...`, phase `ready-to-verify`), and its exact dependency publisher completed with a stable 58-tree manifest and immutable selector. Those are sound invariants: immutable candidate, explicit repair lineage, fail-closed dependencies, atomic promotion. The failure surface is the orchestration around them: `green-checkpoint.ts` is 18,498 lines and changed in 174 commits since 2026-08-20; `release-actions.ts` is 5,654 lines/85 commits; queue state is split across routine JSON, pipeline events, host-local refs/files, work-items, and processes; live control-plane versions diverge. Provisional ruling pending the remaining audit: do not rewrite the whole gate or abandon frozen qualification. Replace the implicit/multi-store orchestration with one durable, run-correlated qualification transaction and an independently refreshable controller; keep the existing immutable artifacts and exact-admission primitives as components.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-012\n\n### D-004 — The 800k context request is resolved control work, not a green-main audit deliverable\nDate: 2026-09-04\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured: owner turn session_turn:codex:01a06de1-b991-7a30-b9b0-87f296f4ca02:5 requested an 800k Papercusp context limit; the exact session-row override reached 800,000 at turn :14, then the current watchdog re-derived the safe soft ceiling as 682,000 from the measured 828,400 effective rollout window at turn :16. The earlier 400k hard-limit assertion at turn :7 was explicitly retracted at turn :11. EI-22361738882260478 is terminal with focused verification. Ruling: preserve the verified 682k safety limit; treat the context-control defect as resolved and outside this plan's product scope, while retaining it in the activation audit because it shared the owner's source request.\nRelated: P-002, P-014\nRelated: P-002, P-014\n\n### D-005 — A frozen repair verdict must bind to repairHead, never the immutable base candidate\nDate: 2026-09-04\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured: the ordinary run selected and fully exercised repairHead 21f03de7a31267d226430af098bbc861ea74cabe, then emitted `candidate-fossil` at 2026-09-04T21:41:24Z and published no code verdict. The queue simultaneously held candidate 1f43e05ae7a88ebed626c84ff254a0b1508937d6 and repairHead 21f03de7a31267d226430af098bbc861ea74cabe. In the exact judged blob, `isJudgingPinnedActiveRepair` compared the judged SHA to `repairQueue.candidate`, while verification targets `repairQueue.repairHead`; therefore every lineage with at least one admitted fix necessarily missed the D-004 fossil exemption. This re-created the coupled livelock that frozen-candidate-outlives-its-repair-2026-08-27#D-004 explicitly prohibited.\n\nRuling: the active pinned identity at verdict time is repairHead. The immutable base remains lineage ancestry and must not authorize a stale verdict after repairHead moves. Consume the queue as one typed object so tests can cover base != head, head match, base mismatch, unrelated stale candidate, and blocked queue. The two-file source fix passed 6/6 focused tests, 514/514 full green-checkpoint tests, file-scoped operator tsc, Prettier, and diff-check. It is not accepted into frozen lineage until git-sync commits the final shared-file blob and an independent review confirms any co-resident gateFireId change.\nRelated: P-001, P-005, P-006, P-008, P-011\nRelated: P-001, P-005, P-006, P-008, P-011\n\n### D-006 — Refresh: release-fixer dispatch rows are not successful repairs\nDate: 2026-09-04\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured: a tenant-scoped query of harness_shared.spawned_agents for workspace_id='papercusp-workspace', harness_slug='papercusp', started_at >= 2026-08-31T16:58:30Z (the finalization time of gate-verdict-liveness-and-repair-reliability-2026-08-31), selecting the release-fixer role/brief, returns 42 launches: 39 status=failed (all 39 carry error_message and 19 have non-zero exits) and 3 status=done. The install-scoped pipeline_events ledger independently has 42 kind='release_fixer' rows with status='ok'; the writer records dispatch-event insertion, not child repair success. Earlier D-002's 27 launches / 25 failed / 2 done was a point-in-time snapshot at 20:41Z and is superseded for the current audit report, not evidence that the underlying history was fabricated.\n\nRuling: report the current writer-backed 42/39/3 outcome and keep process success separate from dispatch acknowledgment. The high failure ratio remains a live survivability concern; loaded-controller drift and provider/launcher mechanisms still require the subsystem audit.\nRelated: P-005, P-009, P-010, P-014\nRelated: P-005, P-009, P-010, P-014\n\n### D-007 — D-013 — Terminal ordinary run confirms frozen 1f43 lineage remains the only admission target\nDate: 2026-09-04\nMeasured 2026-09-04 23:09–23:16Z from release:deploy status, the retained service log, and the staging (:3170) repair-queue reader. The ordinary controller is idle (`checkpointRunInFlight.active=false`, `checkpoint.state=idle`, `verdictPending=false`); the run's terminal marker is `__GREEN_CHECKPOINT_SYSTEMD_TERMINAL__` with exit status 137, and its embedded verdict is `advanced:false`, `green:false`, `reason:not-green` for repairHead 21f03de7 (runId 1a79485f-310d-47b2-a996-a038d021289f). The staging queue still reads frozenCandidate 1f43e05ae7a88ebed626c84ff254a0b1508937d6, repairHead 21f03de7a31267d226430af098bbc861ea74cabe, phase ready-to-verify. Historical evidence remains that 1f43 passed 3254 test files / 47749 tests while only @papercusp/web and lint:tsc:workspaces held the full gate red. Therefore all repair work and any future exact admission stay on the 1f43 frozen lineage; the 26-file tip retriage is explicitly non-authoritative. No manual checkpoint-run, queue retirement/convergence, or force-deploy is permitted. This governs P-001 and P-004.\nRelated: P-001, P-004\n\n### D-008 — Capacity skips must requeue the ordinary verifier, without weakening admission\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured: harness_shared.pipeline_events row 363464 (2026-09-05T00:25:55Z) recorded green_checkpoint status=skipped-memory-budget with scopes=3, committedG=120, requestG=40, budgetG=125; routines:list then showed the next fire at the next hourly cron and no fresh verdict. Decision: treat an over-budget refusal as a safe transient capacity outcome. Reuse the existing TRANSIENT_ABORT_REQUEUE_MINS (10-minute) forward-only, active-row, pause-aware update so capacity is retried promptly. Keep the memory admission guard enabled; never lower the cap, bypass it, or start a manual checkpoint as the remedy. The recurrence test must prove both refusal (no child launch) and requeue guards.\nRelated: P-001, P-004, P-008\n\n### D-009 — The frozen base remains immutable while admitted repairHead advances\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured: release:repair-queue at 2026-09-05T01:36Z reports frozenCandidate=candidate=1f43e05ae7a88ebed626c84ff254a0b1508937d6 and repairHead=2e2c105b4b95cba2ae48d0b4b8b9e8c7f5111731. Its admission ledger records 1f43 → 7cd37 → 2c8ab → 21f03 → 043358 → 2e2c, each with path-exact source/blobs. Measured: pipeline_events 340507/340508 show 1f43's 3,254 test files and 47,749 tests passed, while @papercusp/web and lint:tsc:workspaces failed, so “full suite passed” was too broad. Decision: candidate/frozenCandidate is the immutable full-gate base; repairHead is the only mutable admitted descendant. Legacy event rows that put 21f03 in the generic candidate field describe the judged repairHead from the pre-identity writer and do not prove the frozen base moved. No candidate replacement or tip convergence is authorized.\nRelated: P-001, P-004, P-006\n\n### D-010 — Owner-approved September 12 audit disposition and current execution contract\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAuthority: session_turn:codex:01a0961e-ab11-71f2-bae6-9be0c8401857:32 — Avi approved applying the relevance-audit recommendations and implementing relevant updated plans through verified shipment. This decision adopts the Revise disposition.\n\nCurrent contract: The architecture and promise-to-implementation audit remains relevant. Its fixed fifteen-day window and live-candidate baseline are historical; carrying those as current instructions would misdirect work.\n\nExecution: Update the audit scope/baseline to this reconciled portfolio and carry only evidence-backed residuals. Keep source/runtime/observed-outcome distinctions and avoid another open-ended inventory loop.\n\nMeasured basis: the source/test/decision review and scoped verification recorded in docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md, not a new claim about the live gate. Historical timestamps, candidate references and consumed one-shot permissions below remain historical. Preserve current frozen-lineage invariants and the live-gate ownership boundary. This update does not waive proof, independent grading or acceptance requirements. Track adoption under WI-10001081; retain existing implementation work-items and completed evidence.\n\n### D-011 — Absorb the legacy deploy-trigger checklist into current deploy/observability verification\nDate: 2026-09-12\nOwner-approved consolidation: session_turn:codex:01a0961e-ab11-71f2-bae6-9be0c8401857:32. deploy-trigger-and-gate-unblock-2026-06-21's unparsed legacy P-001/P-002/P-003 tooling is retained as implemented source history. Its P-004 quarantine-op proposal was deliberately not built and is not revived. Any remaining P-005 instruction alignment and P-006 watchdog verification belong to this plan's P-009/P-010 current deploy/observability review and resulting owned residuals. Current contract: trigger ships an eligible already-certified green pin subject to in-flight, pause and certification checks; the latest candidate may be red without invalidating that prior green pin. Force remains explicit, audited and owner-gated. Measured basis: current deploy launch/handler source and85passing deploy-launch tests in the relevance audit. Preserve original history and shipped validation; no new deployment claim.\nRelated: P-009, P-010\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-09-19** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: Owner-approved consolidation D-019. P-020 now carries the evidence-backed re-baselined audit; this source plan is superseded by the owner-approved single-tracker consolidation. D-016/D-017 select customer-owned OpenRouter keys, explicit Qwen3 Coder/Sonnet 4.6 model choices, required ZDR, no provider-credit/API resale, a $50 customer-funded inference cap and the existing $500/30-day assisted one-repository offer. The canonical offer is updated; WI-10005829's D-009 human blocker is cleared and its state reopened. Stripe signup and the cloud/BYOC TEST dashboard rollout are shipped. Real buyer consent/payment/outcomes, measured economics, selected-runtime qualification, security and exact final release acceptance remain open; no paid launch or master shipment is asserted.\n\n**Next:** WI-10005829: reconcile the current source/activation audit and acceptance criteria with D-016/D-017, then qualify the customer-key runtime and onboard real consenting pilot buyers using the existing billing, budget and hosting seams.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10005858 — Define the paid pilot offer and buyer hypothesis: small engineering teams/agencies with one recurring repository-maintenance workflow, an explicit deliverable, customer acceptance criteria, included … <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005859 — Audit current hosted readiness and reuse boundaries against the named portal/BYOC/carrier plans and D-295. Map every needed component to its existing owner/item; verify assumptions about WorkOS, curr… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005860 — Build the pilot unit-economics and price sheet from measured compute, persistent storage/IP, egress, model/cache usage, payment fees and support effort. Separate subscription margin and consumption m… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005861 — Extend existing usage/cost telemetry into an org/workspace-attributed commercial ledger and clear usage statement. Keep estimates distinct from provider-billed amounts, identify every billable event … <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005862 — Implement prepaid/allowance and budget protection on the existing entitlement/accounting seam: atomic reservations before parallel work, settlement/release, scoped limits, warning thresholds and safe… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005863 — Assemble GCP-hosted provisioning, measured readiness, adaptive resource admission, scale-up/drain/idle-stop, restart/restore and verified teardown using the existing cloud/runtime owners' work. Consu… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005864 — Qualify OpenRouter through the existing customer-runtime/provider seams (D-009): reusable first-class execution, curated model/effort/tool metadata and current fee-inclusive price data; customer-supp… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005865 — Establish assisted-pilot purchase and entitlement operations: reviewed monthly quote, manual invoice/payment confirmation, versioned staff/private-beta assignment, finite usage allowance, suspension/… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005866 — Run the assembled pilot-readiness gate using the existing hosted confidentiality/customer-account security acceptance in carrier P-001/P-002/P-009 and portal acceptance. Verify payment/assignment -> … <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005867 — Launch the assisted hosted pilot only after P-009 and verified final release identity/promotion. Offer it to a small design-partner cohort using the agreed quote; target three unrelated paying organi… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005868 — Evaluate the pilot after the agreed observation window (initial proposal: 30 days). Record paid organizations, repeat usage, customer-accepted outcomes, rework/human intervention, onboarding time, re… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005869 — If P-011 supports expansion, implement self-service billing on the existing organization entitlement boundary: one Stripe customer per org, Checkout/portal, signed idempotent webhooks, order-independ… <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005870 — Reconcile the useful self-managed source and free/paid boundary with the existing owner-selected ELv2 product/permissive-library release (open-source-release-2026-09-29 D-003/D-016; monetization D-01… <!-- P-013 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005871 — After P-013 approval, release the curated core with install/upgrade/backup/export documentation, a sample workflow, supported-extension interfaces and clear community-versus-paid support. Prefer a cl… <!-- P-014 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005872 — Design managed-BYOC packaging over the existing adapters and D-295: scoped auditable grants, customer-local data/execution, updates/recovery, budget scope and responsibility matrix, cloud-direct bill… <!-- P-015 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005873 — After hosted pilot learning supports the offer, productize managed BYOC by integrating existing cloud/carrier delivery and the shared entitlement/budget/accounting components. Acceptance: a real cust… <!-- P-016 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005874 — Evaluate and specify the strongest next paid extension from pilot evidence: management of existing local/self-hosted installations, agency client workspaces and cost allocation, maintained workflow p… <!-- P-017 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005875 — Close commercialization planning/delivery milestones with an auditable disposition for every offer: shipped and measured, rejected by evidence, or carried to an explicitly owned successor. Reconcile … <!-- P-018 -->\n## Objective\n\nBuild a sustainable business around a useful self-managed Papercusp core. Start with the D-016/D-017 assisted repository-maintenance pilot on the existing customer-owned runtime/key route, with transparent costs and controlled spending. Preserve fully hosted service and managed BYOC as separately qualified commercial offers, charging for operation and management while customer-direct bills remain separate. Develop enterprise support and maintained workflows without making a marketplace or GPU-hosting business a launch prerequisite.\n\nThe first-week objective is a paid-pilot-ready offer and, if readiness gates and a real buyer permit, a paid assisted pilot. One week is an experiment target, not a production-readiness guarantee. The existing source-available publication, broad self-service billing and multi-cloud expansion have separate evidence gates. Reuse open-source-release-2026-09-29 and its selected ELv2 product license; verify remaining sample-workflow and independent acceptance evidence.\n\n## Product shaping\n\nAudience: a small engineering team or agency with one active TypeScript/JavaScript repository, a named maintainer and a reproducible acceptance command. This buyer/workflow is a hypothesis until unrelated customers pay and accept comparable work.\n\nProblem: recurring maintenance requires narrow changes, reproducible evidence and clear limits on spending and staff intervention. The first offer sells a bounded maintenance service with customer-controlled model access.\n\nOutcome: under D-016/D-017, prepare a $500, 30-day, one-organization/one-repository assisted pilot: one setup session, four independently reviewable weekly deliveries, up to two staff support hours, next-business-day response, no SLA and no automatic renewal. Each maintainer accepts the agreed behavior and test evidence. No-change work counts only with explicit customer acceptance. Cancellation stops future work; undelivered weekly service is refundable pro rata at $125 per portion, with tax/processor treatment disclosed before payment.\n\nExecution and spending: start on the existing local/customer-cloud runtime. The customer owns a dedicated revocable OpenRouter workspace key, funds inference and infrastructure directly, and selects qwen/qwen3-coder by default or anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 explicitly. Require request-level provider.zdr=true, account/key prompt-logging and training exclusions, eligible fallback endpoints and declared subprocessors. No silent premium/model substitution, API-access resale, model markup or automatic top-up. Default inference limit is $50 per 30-day pilot, versioned with any explicit customer change in the existing entitlement/budget and provider-key seams. Exhaustion checkpoints and stops new spending.\n\nCloud launch boundary: cloud-portal-public-release-2026-10-13#D-002 now owns the 14-day public cloud trial, self-service subscription management and live billing. That cloud launch no longer waits for this separate assisted-pilot cohort. Reuse its assigned delivery and evidence; do not duplicate implementation. The repository-maintenance service and self-managed/BYOC/extension offers keep their separate acceptance obligations.\n\nScope boundaries: managed inference, a new billing stack, marketplace/DAO/x402/outcome billing and GPU hosting are outside this first offer. The existing hosted-cloud, public core, managed-BYOC and commercial-extension work remains in P-001..P-018 and its existing owners. Hosted Papercusp cloud is conditional on its own measured cost, security/readiness and release evidence. D-010/D-011/D-012/D-013/D-015, ELv2 wording, the independent cloud subscription lane and customer-content boundaries remain binding.\n\nSource turns: session_turn:claude:2cb6bb4e-17ec-4bd5-8363-676a0e4d9a38:0/:10/:17/:21/:23/:24/:25/:29; session_turn:codex:01a06de2-4374-7d50-9cf5-d5474b4cc431:1/:6/:17/:22; session_turn:codex:01a10027-cabd-70f1-b00b-3d060273bda7:5/:8; session_turn:codex:01a135d1-cc74-7180-ae13-70e2990bdec4:9. D-016/D-017 record the delegated first-pilot choices. The later delegation is readable as a file-backed owner candidate; preserve that reported provenance instead of fabricating an origin stamp. The original direct-self AUTO grant and governing decisions remain the execution authority.\n\nScenarios: (1) an eligible consenting maintainer receives one bounded patch/draft PR with exact source and before/after checks; (2) no qualified ZDR endpoint, revoked key or exhausted allowance stops new spending visibly; (3) cancellation stops future work without implying deletion of customer resources; (4) real Stripe LIVE payment is collected only after merchant/payout/tax readiness is verified; (5) three unrelated paying organizations are observed for 30 days before the continue/reprice/narrow/stop decision.\n\nOpen acceptance: measured contribution margin of at least 50%, genuine buyer consent/payment/runtime/key/account-policy readiness, accepted deliveries, cohort outcomes, independent security and exact shipped release proof. Fixture/source tests establish their named source behavior only. Neither the policy decision nor a tree-ready offer closes those gates. R-1..R-18 and their evidence planes, falsifiers and BAR-to-work map remain intact; the current MONETIZATION spec evidence methods bind the selected D-016/D-017 parameters.\n\n## Source and existing-plan reconciliation\n\n- Source discussion: session_turn:claude:2cb6bb4e-17ec-4bd5-8363-676a0e4d9a38, 2026-09-02. Owner turns 0 and 10 establish monetization/open-source exploration and discussion before implementation; 17 requests managed BYOC provisioning; 21 explicitly chooses fully hosted v1 and BYOC planning; 23-25 narrow one open-weight model and compare GLM 5.3 with Kimi K3; 29 requests automatic provisioning and shutdown.\n- Original private memo: /home/marsh-office/papercusp-monetization-options-2026-09-02.md. Its BYOC-first checklist and restrictive-license recommendation are historical proposals, not the current launch order or a license decision.\n- Current review and plan request: session_turn:codex:01a06de2-4374-7d50-9cf5-d5474b4cc431; owner request :6. This focused successor follows the carrier's instruction to split activated commercial work into its own plan.\n\n## Product and pricing proposal\n\n| Offer | Customer value | Pricing shape | Timing |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Community, self-managed | Useful runnable source-available core, local agents, owned data, documented extension points | No platform service fee under the selected ELv2 product license; customer buys infrastructure/model access | Separate curated release |\n| Assisted repository maintenance | One repository, four weekly reviewable deliveries, setup and bounded support | $500 for 30 days, no automatic renewal; customer-direct infrastructure and OpenRouter inference | Selected first pilot, D-016/D-017 |\n| Papercusp Cloud | Ready workspace, managed provisioning/updates/recovery, observability and support | Monthly team/workspace platform fee, explicit compute usage and explicit inference usage; optional finite included credit | After its measured readiness/security/release gates |\n| Managed BYOC | Same management in customer's cloud, scoped permissions, spend visibility | Management subscription with stated included environments/capacity/support; cloud charged directly to customer | After hosted pilot learning |\n| Enterprise | Private deployment support, organization policy, audit/retention controls and service commitments | Annual support/management or commercial-feature contract | Qualified demand; no invented readiness claims |\n| Maintained workflows | A maintained repeatable job with setup, integrations and quality evaluation | Setup fee plus recurring maintenance/service fee, with usage clearly allocated | One workflow in the pilot; broader catalog later |\n\nUse a team/workspace fee as the main base, including collaborators where economical. Human seats alone do not measure autonomous fleet load. Unlimited inference, unbounded compute and undefined support are not included. A finite allowance is permitted and shown in money with an understandable compute/model rate breakdown. Keep billing prices/versioned entitlements in data, not hard-coded fleet-capacity constants.\n\nDo not charge merely for raising a customer's spending ceiling. Basic spending controls are included in every offer where Papercusp manages consumption. Premiums buy demonstrable management, scale, reserved availability, additional managed environments or support. Avoid a percentage of cloud spend or raw agent-hours as the sole management fee; neither rewards efficient work. Do not invoice raw accepted-work-item counts in v1.\n\nD-017 selects the $500/30-day finite service offer; P-003 measures its payment fees, labor/support and contribution margin before quoting. The target is at least 50% contribution margin for the service scope. If measured costs fail it, agree a narrower scope before quoting. Inference and infrastructure are customer-direct under D-016; provider prices are not a Papercusp tariff. Other prices in the old memo remain historical proposals. Use subscription revenue, metered revenue, cloud/model costs, support labor and payment fees separately; distinguish markup from gross margin. BYOC removes customer compute from our invoice, not our control-plane, support or security costs.\n\nThe selected pilot is a finite 30-day service purchase through the existing Stripe/invoice and versioned entitlement seams. Verify actual LIVE merchant/payout/tax configuration before collection; the $1 TEST offers do not establish this sale. The customer funds its dedicated OpenRouter key directly, with a default $50 hard stop and no automatic top-up or overage. Cancellation refunds undelivered weekly service pro rata under the disclosed terms. Later recurring/self-service expansion follows validated pricing and pilot evidence.\n\n## Requirements\n\nThese acceptance outcomes preserve the existing P-001 through P-018 scope and D-009/D-011. The recorded e2e layer supplies runtime-test provenance only; source tests never establish rights clearance or independent publication/installation, whose genuine proof remains required by R-14.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-14 — Verified public core release.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Deliver the remaining monetization plan scope directly under AUTO.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a10027-cabd-70f1-b00b-3d060273bda7:8\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An independently installed published self-managed core completes the sample workflow with customer-provided model access and verified upgrade/backup/export, supported-extension and community-versus-paid support boundaries without a compulsory cloud account.\",\"falsifier\":\"Published links fail, clean installation or upgrade/export/backup fails, or the promised self-managed core requires a compulsory cloud account.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-014\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Verify public repository/package/docs identities and links, perform an independent clean installation and sample workflow, and retain supported-extension/support-boundary/upgrade/export proof. The recorded e2e layer provides runtime-test provenance; fixture e2e or source tests alone never establish these genuine operational outcomes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-15 — Reviewable managed-BYOC contract.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Deliver the remaining monetization plan scope directly under AUTO.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a10027-cabd-70f1-b00b-3d060273bda7:8\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The GCP-first managed-BYOC design states scoped permissions, trust and operational responsibilities, customer-direct cloud costs and the separate management price.\",\"falsifier\":\"The contract double-bills cloud spend, has unbounded IAM access, duplicates provisioning or omits revocation/export/offboarding and budget scope.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-015\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the existing adapters and D-295; review the commercial/technical contract against IAM, recovery, key/retention, management costs and provider-specific follow-on boundaries.\\nVerification obligation: review the complete commercial/technical contract against the existing adapters and D-295, IAM, recovery, key/retention, management cost and provider-specific follow-on boundaries. The recorded e2e layer supplies runtime-test provenance only; contract review never establishes the real customer-owned GCP canary required by R-16.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-16 — Verified customer-owned BYOC.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Deliver the remaining monetization plan scope directly under AUTO.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a10027-cabd-70f1-b00b-3d060273bda7:8\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A real customer-owned GCP account completes the agreed managed-BYOC lifecycle with correct separate management billing and resource disposition.\",\"falsifier\":\"Customer-owned connect/provision/work/scale/revoke/offboard fails, privacy guarantees fail or customer cloud costs are billed again as Papercusp consumption.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-016\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"After learning from the approved first-pilot route (local/customer-cloud per D-016/D-017, preserving P-009/P-011/P-015 sequencing) supports the offer, run the customer-owned GCP canary with scoped grants and verify management invoice, resource obligations, export/revocation/offboarding. The recorded e2e layer provides runtime-test provenance; fixture e2e or source tests alone never establish these genuine operational outcomes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-17 — Selected next paid experiment.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Deliver the remaining monetization plan scope directly under AUTO.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a10027-cabd-70f1-b00b-3d060273bda7:8\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Pilot evidence produces a ranked commercial extension decision with a bounded buyer/value/cost experiment and success/stop criteria.\",\"falsifier\":\"A candidate disappears without disposition or a new product is built without evidence, budget and a bounded delivery decision.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-017\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Compare existing-install management, agency allocation, maintained workflows, enterprise support and reserved capacity against actual pilot demand; record build/defer decisions and assign the chosen delivery successor.\\nVerification obligation: the ranked extension decision must use actual pilot demand, record build/defer choices and name the chosen delivery successor. The recorded e2e layer provides runtime-test provenance; fixture e2e or source tests alone never establish these genuine operational outcomes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | live |\n| R-7 | P-007 | live |\n| R-8 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-009 | live |\n| R-10 | P-010 | live |\n| R-11 | P-011 | live |\n| R-12 | P-012 | live |\n| R-13 | P-013 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-014 | live |\n| R-15 | P-015 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-016 | live |\n| R-17 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-018 | live |\n\n\n\nReuse org-scoped HostedEntitlementSet/bundles/assignments, telemetry and model-pricing, the resource governor, DBOS operations, workspace-host provider adapters, signed runtime/image pipelines, backup/restore and resource obligation records. Audit actual call paths and live acceptance; a schema field or completed plan item is not proof that the assembled product works.\n\nKeep platform control metadata separate from customer-authored plans/work items, source, prompts, transcripts, model I/O and diagnostic content. D-295 and carrier D-001/P-009 are binding for the customer-content guarantee. Vendor control services receive allowlisted metadata only. The customer runtime remains usable during a vendor outage; do not introduce a per-model-call dependency on the vendor control plane. Define trusted browser/application delivery, endpoint identity, customer-held keys, revocation and recovery before claiming vendor-unreadable content. Standard vendor-operated VM/root access alone cannot justify that claim. Fully hosted and BYOC trust models must be stated accurately; any incompatible change to the approved promise must be resolved explicitly, never hidden by a pricing decision.\n\nOpenRouter is the production model-access route (D-009), replacing the former GLM 5.3/Kimi K3 single-model proposal. Retain BYOK and existing provider choices; do not operate GPUs or resell consumer subscriptions. Qualify a curated model allowlist with complete Papercusp jobs, tool calls, retries, vision behavior and human correction. Token rates alone do not establish cost per successful job. Read current OpenRouter provider pricing, purchase fees, rate/credit limits and production terms before quoting. Define customer-owned versus Papercusp-owned account/key responsibilities and funded-credit exposure explicitly; BYOK is not a promise of zero OpenRouter fees. Reuse provider-reported cost/cost details for reconciliation and per-key limits as an additional backstop beneath atomic local reservations. OpenRouter and upstream model providers are declared third parties; apply supported zero-data-retention controls and exclude endpoints that cannot meet the selected policy. Customer content stays in the authorized runtime/provider path; invoicing must not centralize plaintext prompts in vendor control services. Until managed-inference capacity, permissions and privacy-compatible accounting are verified, offer customer-supplied OpenRouter keys and label managed inference unavailable.\n\nUse measured workload classes and queue/host health for admission and scaling. API-model agent processes, browser/build jobs and GPU inference have different requirements; do not promise a universal agents-per-VM number. Idle shutdown requires no active jobs and a recoverable checkpoint; no viewer activity alone is insufficient. Include hysteresis, startup readiness and draining so scaling does not interrupt work.\n\nThe runtime budget ledger must reserve exposure before admitting concurrent model/compute work, settle against observed billable use and release unused reservations. Handle retries, cache read/write accounting, estimated versus provider-billed costs, maximum request exposure, storage obligations and billing lag. Customer-controlled infrastructure cannot honestly promise a cap on unrelated cloud spending. Define the scope of the cap and residual storage/IP charges. At exhaustion, stop new spend and checkpoint/drain safely; retain/export data according to the disclosed retention policy.\n\n## Phase 1 — Offer, reuse and unit economics\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Define the paid pilot offer and buyer hypothesis: small engineering teams/agencies with one recurring repository-maintenance workflow, an explicit deliverable, customer acceptance criteria, included support, duration and cancellation terms. Prepare a demonstration and interview/quote materials; do not assume this segment or a dollar price is validated. Acceptance: one reviewable offer, a measurable workflow and recorded pricing/segment hypotheses. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005858 released\n- **P-002** `todo` Audit current hosted readiness and reuse boundaries against the named portal/BYOC/carrier plans and D-295. Map every needed component to its existing owner/item; verify assumptions about WorkOS, current-build runtime configuration, customer-content access, credentials, teardown and recovery. Define hosted versus BYOC trust/operating responsibility and external prerequisites. Acceptance: an evidence-linked gap/dependency matrix, no duplicated cloud lane, and a threat model that preserves the approved privacy constraints. importance: high blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Build the pilot unit-economics and price sheet from measured compute, persistent storage/IP, egress, model/cache usage, payment fees and support effort. Separate subscription margin and consumption margin; set numeric target margins and experiment thresholds before quoting. Specify finite credits, billing units, rounding, cancellation, overage/top-up choices and BYOK behavior. Acceptance: reproducible cost examples for idle, normal, heavy and burst workloads plus a concrete proposed quote. importance: high blocked-by: P-001, P-002\n\n## Phase 2 — Bounded, operable hosted service\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Extend existing usage/cost telemetry into an org/workspace-attributed commercial ledger and clear usage statement. Keep estimates distinct from provider-billed amounts, identify every billable event and deduplicate retry/replay events. Support monthly rollups, forecasts and traceable adjustments without customer-content leakage. Acceptance: fixture and integration reconciliation for compute, storage/egress, cached/uncached model use, duplicate events and cross-org separation. importance: high blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-005** `todo` Implement prepaid/allowance and budget protection on the existing entitlement/accounting seam: atomic reservations before parallel work, settlement/release, scoped limits, warning thresholds and safe exhaustion behavior. No silent top-up or unbounded debt. Acceptance: concurrent requests, crash/retry, streaming cancellation, delayed billing and restart cannot bypass the admitted-spend policy; residual retained-resource costs are visible and bounded by documented policy. importance: high blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `todo` Assemble GCP-hosted provisioning, measured readiness, adaptive resource admission, scale-up/drain/idle-stop, restart/restore and verified teardown using the existing cloud/runtime owners' work. Consume D-295 identity/fencing/backup proofs and resource obligations. Acceptance: ordinary create/use/stop/resume/destroy, mixed workloads, active-job protection, stuck operations and orphan cleanup work on current build; provider success alone never marks a workspace ready. importance: high blocked-by: P-002, P-005\n- **P-007** `todo` Qualify OpenRouter through the existing customer-runtime/provider seams (D-009): reusable first-class execution, curated model/effort/tool metadata and current fee-inclusive price data; customer-supplied keys and explicit managed-key ownership/limits/retention policy. Benchmark representative completed jobs against a baseline for quality, retries, vision and total cost. Acceptance: real agent sessions and provider-reported accounting reconcile, key/limit/exhaustion behavior is verified, supported models and third-party data handling are explicit; no GPU hosting, consumer-subscription resale or vendor-readable prompt relay is required. Managed inference activates only with verified commercial capacity, allowed production use and compatible metering. importance: high blocked-by: P-002, P-004, P-005\n- **P-008** `todo` Establish assisted-pilot purchase and entitlement operations: reviewed monthly quote, manual invoice/payment confirmation, versioned staff/private-beta assignment, finite usage allowance, suspension/cancellation and customer-readable statements. Acceptance: authorized operator can provision only the agreed org entitlement, reconcile payment/usage, correct an invoice and end renewal without deleting retained customer data. Payment prerequisites must be verified; manual handling is documented. importance: high blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005\n- **P-009** `todo` Run the assembled pilot-readiness gate using the existing hosted confidentiality/customer-account security acceptance in carrier P-001/P-002/P-009 and portal acceptance. Verify payment/assignment -> usable workspace -> OpenRouter/BYOK job -> correct usage -> budget stop -> resume -> cancellation/export/retention/teardown, plus overlapping two-tenant IDs, revocation, content-marker leakage tests and vendor outage. Acceptance: focused tests and customer journeys pass on a pinned current build; independent security findings are resolved or explicitly block real customer use. importance: high blocked-by: P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n## Phase 3 — Paid learning, then self-service\n\n- **P-010** `todo` Launch the assisted hosted pilot only after P-009 and verified final release identity/promotion. Offer it to a small design-partner cohort using the agreed quote; target three unrelated paying organizations as an experiment, not a forecast. Record customer acceptance and support commitments. Acceptance: real payment and a customer-approved completed workflow; unmet sales targets remain open evidence, never fabricated closure. importance: high blocked-by: P-001, P-003, P-009\n- **P-011** `todo` Evaluate the pilot after the agreed observation window (initial proposal: 30 days). Record paid organizations, repeat usage, customer-accepted outcomes, rework/human intervention, onboarding time, reliability, actual cost, margins and support effort. Compare with thresholds set in P-003 and make a dated continue/reprice/narrow/stop decision. Acceptance: reconciled evidence and a decision; do not confuse a paid trial with proven retention or outcome counts with comparable units. importance: high blocked-by: P-010\n- **P-012** `todo` Reuse cloud-portal-public-release-2026-10-13#D-002 and its existing public cloud self-service delivery (14-day trial, subscription management and verified live billing); the cloud offer does not wait for assisted-pilot P-008..P-011. Reconcile its commercial evidence on the existing organization entitlement boundary: one Stripe customer per org, Checkout/portal, signed idempotent webhooks, order-independent subscription state, renewal/failure/grace/cancel/refund handling and meter reconciliation. Publish the validated pricing/usage experience in the existing portal/site. Acceptance: duplicate/out-of-order events, failure recovery, cross-org access and end-to-end purchase/cancel cases pass; free allowances, overages and retained-resource costs are visible. importance: normal\n\n## Phase 4 — Useful self-managed source on the existing release track\n\n- **P-013** `todo` Reconcile the useful self-managed source and free/paid boundary with the existing owner-selected ELv2 product/permissive-library release (open-source-release-2026-09-29 D-003/D-016; monetization D-012). Reuse its curated public export and rights/compatibility/contribution/closed-set decisions. Audit exact current Rust/npm/native/image/model artifacts, notices/source obligations, contributor rights, embedded secrets/customer data and history. Acceptance: current reviewed license matrix and manifest, usable core demo and release decision are linked and verified; ELv2 is labeled source-available, no second repo or replacement license is invented, and missing independent/public artifact evidence has an accountable owner. importance: high blocked-by: P-001, P-002\n- **P-014** `todo` After P-013 approval, release the curated core with install/upgrade/backup/export documentation, a sample workflow, supported-extension interfaces and clear community-versus-paid support. Prefer a clean public export where internal history is unsuitable. Explain hosted benefits accurately and provide an optional path to paid management. Acceptance: independent clean installation completes the sample workflow using customer-provided model access, secrets/history checks pass, and published repository/package/docs links resolve. No compulsory cloud account for the promised self-managed core. importance: normal blocked-by: P-013\n\n## Phase 5 — Managed BYOC and commercial extensions\n\n- **P-015** `todo` Design managed-BYOC packaging over the existing adapters and D-295: scoped auditable grants, customer-local data/execution, updates/recovery, budget scope and responsibility matrix, cloud-direct billing plus a management subscription. Define GCP-first acceptance and preserve AWS/Azure canaries as existing follow-on lanes. Acceptance: a technical/commercial design with IAM/permissions, revocation/export/offboarding and costs stated; no duplicate provisioning/control plane. This design can proceed before the hosted pilot finishes. importance: normal blocked-by: P-002, P-003\n- **P-016** `todo` After hosted pilot learning supports the offer, productize managed BYOC by integrating existing cloud/carrier delivery and the shared entitlement/budget/accounting components. Acceptance: a real customer-owned GCP account completes connect/provision/work/scale/revoke/offboard with proof of resource disposition, privacy guarantees and a correct separate management invoice; customer cloud charges are not double-billed. AWS/Azure GA requires their own existing live canaries, not a checkbox here. importance: normal blocked-by: P-009, P-011, P-015\n- **P-017** `todo` Evaluate and specify the strongest next paid extension from pilot evidence: management of existing local/self-hosted installations, agency client workspaces and cost allocation, maintained workflow packages, enterprise/private-operation support, or reserved execution capacity. Define buyer/value/cost, privacy/support promises, a cheap paid experiment and success/stop criteria for each retained candidate; create a separate bounded delivery plan only for the selected next experiment. Acceptance: ranked evidence and explicit build/defer decisions; marketplace take-rate and outcome billing remain in the economy plan. importance: normal blocked-by: P-011\n- **P-018** `todo` Close commercialization planning/delivery milestones with an auditable disposition for every offer: shipped and measured, rejected by evidence, or carried to an explicitly owned successor. Reconcile the BYOC billing carrier and this plan without silently dropping unfinished work. Acceptance: final offer/license matrix, pricing basis, verified release identities, operating runbook, pilot results and accountable remaining scope; do not mark the entire plan shipped merely because one pilot starts. importance: normal blocked-by: P-012, P-014, P-016, P-017\n\n## Milestones, sequencing and verification\n\nM1: a concrete offer and measurable cost/pricing hypothesis (P-001..P-003).\nM2: a technically ready selected customer-key assisted pilot, with hosted-cloud readiness separately qualified (P-004..P-009), including payment/entitlement operations without requiring full Stripe automation.\nM3: real paid learning and a go/reprice/narrow/stop decision (P-010..P-011).\nM4: useful OSS release (P-013..P-014), independently gated and able to progress alongside commercial readiness.\nM5: public cloud self-service follows cloud-portal-public-release-2026-10-13#D-002 on its own launch path (P-012); managed-BYOC expansion retains its separate learning and customer-account gates (P-015..P-016).\nM6: next-offer experiment and final accountable disposition (P-017..P-018).\n\nThe initial week may complete discovery, pricing, manual billing preparation and safe current-build validation. It does not promise to close external security review, new credentials, a customer's buying cycle, a GPU inference service or public-repo curation within seven days. The executor records actual critical-path estimates after P-002.\n\nAll product tests ship in the project's test framework. Ordinary implementation/acceptance uses staging or an isolated current build. Only final promotion/shipment checks use green main/deployed identity; obey the single-owner LIVE_GATE_OPS contract and do not create a second gate monitor. A paid launch requires the hosted security and confidentiality gates, not just unit tests. No new fleet is launched by this plan draft.\n\nPilot measurement definitions: a paying organization means a real settled payment from an external organization; repeat usage means a distinct later customer-requested run; successful output requires recorded customer acceptance for the agreed job; cost distinguishes provider-billed, allocated infrastructure/support, estimated and list-equivalent values. Never present internal list-equivalent token spend as an invoice or a unit-cost baseline.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Hosted first; preserve existing cloud scope\nDate: 2026-09-04\nOwner direction from source turn 21 is fully hosted v1 with BYOC planned next. The old memo's BYOC-first checklist is superseded for this commercial proposal. This does not activate the separate BYOC GCP plan's deferred hosted or multi-cloud lanes. Their existing owners and D-295 obligations remain authoritative.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-009, P-015, P-016\n\n### D-002 — Planning authorization and draft boundaries\nDate: 2026-09-04\nCurrent owner turn :6 requests plan authoring and a summary. This plan records recommendations for review; it is not a product execution approval, a final license choice, a sales/publish instruction or a fleet launch. Preserve all such choices as proposed until selected. Before activation, re-read the complete source conversation, reconcile later corrections and record the activation audit.\nRelated: P-001, P-010, P-013, P-014\n\n### D-003 — Transparent platform, compute and inference with bounded allowances\nDate: 2026-09-04\nRecommended pricing separates platform value, measured compute/storage/egress and model consumption. Finite included credits are allowed; unlimited consumption is not. Basic budget controls are universal and atomic admission/settlement enforces the defined cap. Higher spending ceilings alone are not a paid feature; raw agent-hours or accepted-task counts are not the v1 invoice unit. Price/rate/budget policy is versioned data, not hard-coded capacity defaults.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-008, P-012\n\n### D-004 — Pilot learning precedes full billing automation\nDate: 2026-09-04\nA monthly manually invoiced platform subscription plus bounded usage and existing staff entitlements can validate the offer. Stripe automation is subsequent productization, not proof of demand. Target a small paid cohort and repeat customer work; record a continue/reprice/narrow/stop decision and carry any resulting changes explicitly. Specific dollar prices and target margins are set in P-003, not inherited from speculative memo anchors.\nRelated: P-003, P-008, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-005 — API-model support and privacy-compatible operations\nDate: 2026-09-04\nGLM 5.3 is the initial candidate via a production API with BYOK supported. Qualify real job economics before declaring it cheapest/easiest. Do not operate GPUs or resell consumer coding-plan quotas in this launch. D-295 customer-local execution and allowlisted control metadata remain binding; billing must not insert a vendor-readable per-call prompt proxy. Hosted root access and browser/key trust must be addressed before making strong confidentiality claims.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-006, P-007, P-009, P-015\n\n### D-006 — Useful OSS, with license choice still open\nDate: 2026-09-04\nRecommended direction is a useful open-source core, paid operation/management and clearly separated commercial additions. Apache-2.0 is the initial candidate for owned core code after release-artifact compatibility/rights review. AGPL permits commercial hosting and does not automatically reach every unrelated service; FSL permits internal self-hosting and is source-available until its per-version conversion, so its noncompete clause does not itself sell ordinary enterprise internal-use licenses. Enterprise revenue must buy actual support, management, contractual commitments or commercial capabilities. Library-only publication is insufficient to demonstrate Papercusp.\nRelated: P-013, P-014, P-017\n\n### D-007 — Correct cost and readiness assumptions\nDate: 2026-09-04\nThe measured zero-idle value in desktop-egress-accounting.ts is desktop streaming egress, not total hosting cost. Running VMs and retained disks/IPs/control-plane/support still have costs. BYOC data residency alone is not vendor-unreadability. A billing schema seam, plan completion count or provider resource-success event does not prove customer readiness. Verify current writer semantics, assembled behavior and actual costs before pricing or claiming launch.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-006, P-009\n\n### D-008 — Reuse the carrier; no parallel commercial stack\nDate: 2026-09-04\nThe commercial-billing item in byoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01 and its original BYOC-plan source remain traceable carrier references. This plan supplies their detailed commercial execution specification after activation. The carrier remains draft and does not launch wholesale. Cloud/privacy/portal components stay with their existing plans. The agent-economy draft remains independent and unratified; no marketplace, DAO, x402 or output-billing commitment is inferred here.\nRelated: P-002, P-008, P-012, P-015, P-018\n\n### D-009 — OpenRouter replaces the single supported open-weight model (owner ruling)\nDate: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29\nSource: [owner:Avi 2026-09-29 interactive, directive #918] verbatim: \"- Launch with one open-weight model, comparing GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3.\" - scrap this we'll use open-router for this.\n\nRuling: the v1 plan no longer standardizes on one open-weight model (GLM 5.3 vs Kimi K3, source turns 23-25 of session claude:2cb6bb4e). Model access for the paid offer goes through OpenRouter. This supersedes the GLM 5.3 portions of D-005, the P-007 qualification target, the Z.ai rate evidence source, and the 'single open-weight model/GLM-vs-Kimi economics' coverage line. D-005's other constraints (no GPU operation, no consumer-plan resale, BYOK support, truthful confidentiality claims) are unchanged by this ruling.\n\nNot decided by this ruling (open, pending Avi's review of the WI-10003888 audit): which models are allowed and at what customer price, whether hosted workspaces use a Papercusp OpenRouter account with per-workspace keys vs customer-supplied OpenRouter keys, ZDR enforcement defaults, and how OpenRouter's Terms (reselling clause 7(4), non-transferable credits 4.4) shape the inference charge.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-007, P-009, D-003, D-005\n\n### D-010 — P-012 Stripe self-service machinery is being built early (test mode) under stripe-subscription-signup-2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-01 directive #1102] asked to build the Stripe subscription signup UI and backend now, in parallel, before the system is ready. The implementation lives in plan stripe-subscription-signup-2026-10-01 and is the P-012 machinery (one Stripe customer per org, Checkout/portal, signed idempotent order-independent webhooks, subscription state) — not a parallel stack (D-008). D-004 is respected for activation: live-mode charging stays behind a default-OFF owner-authority flag and prices stay with P-003; meter reconciliation plugs into the entitlement seam later. P-012 remains blocked for live launch.\n\n### D-011 — Owner authorizes direct AUTO execution of remaining commercialization scope; preserve cloud subscription lane\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: session_turn:codex:01a10027-cabd-70f1-b00b-3d060273bda7:8, read in full in this session. This supersedes D-002's planning-only posture for the remaining scope. Route is this session implementing directly, without a new fleet or client-native subagents. This is a delegated product decision, not a claim of production acceptance.\n\nRuling: launch the first paid pilot with each customer's own OpenRouter account and a dedicated revocable workspace key, held in the existing customer-runtime secret store. The customer funds OpenRouter directly. Papercusp charges for its software/service/hosting only: no resale of OpenRouter API access, credit transfer, model markup, consumer-plan resale, automatic provider top-up or unapproved overage. Papercusp-managed inference is outside this first-pilot route and does not block customer-key implementation; it requires a separate documented provider-authorized commercial arrangement before offering it.\n\nModel policy: default qwen/qwen3-coder for bounded repository-maintenance work. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 is the explicit customer-selected premium option; no automatic premium escalation or model substitution. These exact model ids are present in the live OpenRouter catalog and declare tool support. This is the initial allowlist, not a benchmark/ranking claim; each must pass the existing task, cost and runtime qualification before a paid delivery. Deprecated or unavailable ids fail visibly. Provider prices belong to the customer's OpenRouter bill; no invented Papercusp per-token tariff.\n\nPrivacy: require provider.zdr=true on every customer-content request and the account/key retention settings to exclude prompt/chat logging and model-training use. ZDR applies to fallback routes too; no relaxation or non-ZDR fallback. If no qualified endpoint exists, stop that request. Source/prompts/transcripts/model I/O stay in the customer execution boundary and go directly to the selected OpenRouter endpoint; central billing gets only allowlisted control/usage metadata. Disclose OpenRouter and the selected endpoint as subprocessors; ZDR is a routing policy, not a promise of zero operator access or complete hosted confidentiality. Existing P-009 security/consent/tenant/key-revocation requirements remain mandatory.\n\nDefault pilot inference budget: $50 per 30-day pilot, customer-funded, with a hard stop and no automatic top-up. A customer may explicitly lower/increase it before work; the agreed limit is versioned in the existing budget/entitlement seam and dedicated provider-key limit. Exhaustion checkpoints and stops new spending.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-13 official https://openrouter.ai/terms says credits are non-transferable (4.4) and prohibits reselling API access (Restrictions); https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/zdr documents provider.zdr=true and no eligible non-ZDR endpoints; https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models returned both selected exact ids with tools support. Current pilot doc already specifies customer-key inference; this extends that existing offer. OpenRouter BYOK-upstream-provider keys are a separate concept from ownership of the customer's OpenRouter account.\n\nResolves D-009's first-pilot ownership/models/customer-inference-price/ZDR/terms choices. It does not close production, genuine customer, payment, security or final-release evidence.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-007, P-009\n\n### D-017 — Avi-delegated pilot offer: $500 for 30 days, bounded delivery and genuine acceptance\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAuthority: Avi delegated the remaining monetization decisions in this session. Extend the existing assisted-repository-maintenance-pilot offer rather than creating another pricing/billing system.\n\nRuling: select the existing $500 price hypothesis as the first paid-pilot offer: one organization, one repository, 30 days, one setup session and four weekly independently reviewable maintenance patches/draft PRs, with up to two staff support hours, next-business-day response and no SLA. No automatic renewal. Customer maintainer acceptance against the agreed test/behavior is required for each delivery; no-change investigation counts only when explicitly accepted.\n\nUse Papercusp LLC as the merchant/service counterparty through the existing Stripe seam; actual live merchant/payout/tax configuration must be verified before collection. The $1 Stripe TEST offers remain test offers and are never substituted for this price. Start on the existing local/customer-cloud execution route so the customer pays infrastructure and OpenRouter directly. Hosted Papercusp cloud may be offered only after its current security/readiness, measured cost and release requirements pass; the first customer-key pilot does not depend on selling managed inference or subsidized hosting.\n\nThe $500 covers the finite platform/service scope. Inference is separate and customer-direct under the model/budget ruling. Infrastructure is customer-direct on BYOC; any Papercusp-hosted resource charge must be itemized from measured cost/rates and explicitly funded/capped. No unlimited allowance, automatic top-up or debt. Target >=50% contribution margin for the platform/service scope after payment fees and measured labor/support; this is an experiment target, not a measured result. If measured P-003 costs fail the target, reduce the agreed scope before quoting; do not silently alter price or broaden spend.\n\nCancellation: stop future work on request; no automatic renewal. Refund undelivered weekly service portions pro rata ($125 each). Disclose tax and any processor refund-fee treatment before payment; incurred customer-direct provider/cloud usage is the customer's bill. Cancellation is not authorization to delete customer data/resources; use existing export/offboarding and resource-disposition proofs. Do not promise a public license/security guarantee that P-015/P-009 has not cleared.\n\nPilot evidence: recruit three unrelated paying organizations, observe each for 30 days, record authorized real Stripe LIVE payment, customer-owned runtime/key/model readiness, customer-approved comparable jobs, support/rework/time/cost and repeat-use intent. P-011 records continue/reprice/narrow/stop after that measured evidence; no fabricated or staff/test payments as demand proof. Price selection is complete; buyer onboarding and real payment are execution evidence, not another owner pricing decision. Do not mark the master plan shipped before its required genuine paid/security/final-release acceptance passes.\n\nMeasured: existing apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs/commercialization/assisted-repository-maintenance-pilot.mdx offers $500/$1000 hypotheses, one repository/four weekly deliveries/two support hours/no renewal; docs/evidence/cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03.json identifies Papercusp LLC TEST billing and excludes real commercial acceptance.
