Genuine customer/cash/security/rights/runtime/30day/public/BYOC/final acceptance remains mandatory.\nApproved-By: su-3a921a08-73ae-4534-8406-427a8ddcbea9\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1181527\nApproved-At: 2026-10-14T19:19:38.031Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 36 → 37\nChanged BARs: R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-022 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: monetization-requirements-reprojection-20261014-r9-p37\nRequest-Hash: 132941764f60d2aeb91672bb6bec7bb280e3f970a3ffe6b18cf35c08def6bc3c\nActor: su-dae9d804-7887-4fc2-b09f-d62f9430b5ba\nReason: Repair represented stale Requirements method/check blocks from current canonical rubric without changing BAR meaning; EI-25984284061088637\nApproval: not required — every change is additive ()\nRubric revision: 9 → 10\nSubject plan revision: 37 → 38\nChanged BARs: \nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, R-13, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18\n\n## Evidence sources and claims to revalidate\n\nOriginal discussion and private memo are historical sources, not current deployment attestations. Official sources checked during the 2026-09-04 review:\n- Z.ai model rates: https://docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing (revalidate before quotes; token rates do not prove job cost).\n- GCP stopped-instance retained-resource charges: https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/reference/rest/v1/instances/stop\n- FSL internal-use rights: https://github.com/getsentry/fsl.software/blob/main/FSL-1.1-ALv2.template.md\n- AGPL scope and commercial use: https://opensource.org/license/agpl-3.0\n- Open Source Definition: https://opensource.org/osd\n- Packaging comparisons, not demand evidence: https://trigger.dev/pricing/ and https://supabase.com/pricing\n\nCurrent source seams inspected in the review: packages/operator-core/lib/auth/hosted-entitlement-schema.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/desktop-egress-accounting.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/hosted-lifecycle-reconcile-action.ts and its seed. Recovery scheduling has source implementation now; runtime deployment and complete lifecycle behavior still require P-002/P-006 evidence. No old missing-caller claim is carried forward as current fact.\n\n## Requirement coverage and unresolved choices\n\nHosted-first/monthly billing: P-001/P-003/P-008/P-010; automatic provisioning/scale-down and capacity uncertainty: P-005/P-006; OpenRouter execution, provider fees, BYOK/managed-key policy and completed-job economics (D-009): P-007; managed BYOC and separate charging: P-015/P-016; useful open-source release/license compatibility: P-013/P-014; paid partners and first-week target: P-001/P-010/P-011; truthful costs and corrected license claims: D-006/D-007; self-managed upgrades/agencies/workflows/enterprise/reserved capacity: P-017; marketplace/output billing: explicit deferred scope in D-008; actual verification and operating handoff: P-009/P-018.\n\nSettled first-pilot choices: D-016/D-017 customer-owned runtime/OpenRouter key, the two explicit model ids, required ZDR and logging/training exclusions, $50 customer-funded inference limit, and $500/30-day finite service with no renewal. D-011/D-013 preserve direct-self AUTO and the independent cloud/subscription lane. The activation audit is refreshed against current source after this semantic reconciliation; no operational or shipment verdict is implied.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plan-popup-fullscreen-control-2026-09-04","title":"Shared plan popup: theme parity, fullscreen, outline, and complete P/D navigation","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-04","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Shared plan popup: theme parity, fullscreen, outline, and complete P/D navigation\nslug: plan-popup-fullscreen-control-2026-09-04\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** The expanded shared-component plan is reviewed and owner-approved for direct implementation in this session, including the Papercusp design-phase registry workflow. The full source conversation has been recovered after compaction; no product, route, or scope questions remain open.\n\n**Next:** Record the activation audit against this repaired revision, start the plan, and execute P-002 through P-007 in dependency order.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2146690 — Add an accessible fullscreen toggle to `apps/operator/app/_components/plans/PlanPopupModal.tsx` that fullscreenes the entire plan dialog (header, tabs and content) through the browser Fullscreen API.… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146691 — Search the component registry, define the popup/fullscreen/outline/detail-action UI IR, validate and lint it, and pin keyboard, responsive, URL-state, and theme behavior. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146692 — Add focused failing regression tests for shared host theme inheritance, fullscreen/restore, all P/D dashboard drill-ins, target cleanup, and outline reachability. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146693 — Replace hard-coded Vditor and outline colors with resolved semantic theme behavior and live theme updates in the canonical shared MarkdownPreview/PlanEditor path. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146694 — Make every PlanDashboard P-item and D-decision open the canonical full-plan view at its exact anchor, while preserving a separate linked-work-item action. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146695 — Redesign the shared outline navigation with hierarchy, semantic tokens, active and focus states, P/D enrichment, and responsive behavior. <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146696 — Run focused component suites and typechecks, build the shared surface, and verify light/dark/system themes, fullscreen, keyboard use, and linked/unlinked P/D detail paths in both the staging desktop/… <!-- P-007 -->\n## Background\n\nPlan popups provide plan content, sessions, tabs and close controls inside a modal. The hosted portal and desktop/operator already share this implementation: `packages/operator-ui/src/surfaces/index.tsx` is a composition facade that imports the canonical `PlansPane`, which reaches `PlanDashboard`, `PlanPopupModal`, `PlanDetail`, `PlanEditor`, and `MarkdownPreview` under `apps/operator/app`. There is no duplicated portal copy of the plan UI.\n\nThe remaining defects are within that shared tree. `MarkdownPreview` forces dark Vditor colors even when the host resolves light, PlanPopupModal has no fullscreen control, its outline is a fixed dark rail, PlanDashboard makes only linked P-items interactive, and unlinked P-items plus all D-decisions are inert.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Theme parity.** The popup, document body, syntax treatment, outline, controls, loading states, and errors inherit the active host theme in both applications, including explicit light/dark changes and system-preference changes.\n\n**R-2 — Fullscreen.** An accessible maximize/restore control fullscreenes the complete dialog. It preserves dirty-edit protection, tabs, scroll position, Escape/external exit state, and focus restoration.\n\n**R-3 — Useful outline.** The outline has a labeled navigation header, readable hierarchy, semantic colors, hover/focus/current-section states, independent sticky scrolling, and a compact responsive form. It remains keyboard accessible and scrolls the inner plan container.\n\n**R-4 — Every P/D entry opens full detail.** Every PlanDashboard plan item and decision exposes an explicit detail action. P-items open the canonical full plan at their exact P-anchor; linked work items retain a separate work-item action. Decisions open the same full plan at the exact D-anchor. URL state is deep-linkable and stale targets clear on close.\n\n**R-5 — One shared implementation.** All changes land in the canonical shared plan components. The operator-ui facade remains composition only; no desktop-specific or portal-specific fork is added.\n\n**R-6 — Both hosts verified.** Focused component tests cover theme switching, fullscreen, outline navigation, linked and unlinked P-items, D-decisions, target cleanup, and keyboard semantics. Browser verification covers the staging desktop/operator and the `:3081` portal.\n\n## Design\n\nUse the Papercusp design path when approved: `design-phase.search_registry` for existing dialog, fullscreen, navigation-rail, and detail-action primitives; express the selected layout as UI IR; run `design-phase.validate_spec` and `design-phase.lint_spec` before implementation.\n\nReuse `PlanPopupModal → PlanDetail → PlanEditor → MarkdownPreview`. Extend URL-owned target state so PlanDashboard can open the full document at a P- or D-anchor through the existing `scrollPlanTarget` helper. A linked P-item gets two distinct affordances: “View plan item” and “Open work item.”\n\nResolve Vditor's light/dark mode from the host root attribute and system media query, subscribe to the existing theme-change mechanisms, and replace hard-coded `#19232A`, `#aaa`, and `#232E37` presentation with semantic tokens.\n\nFullscreen uses the browser Fullscreen API on the complete PlanPopupModal content element, as already decided in D-002. State follows `fullscreenchange`, and the existing Modal wrap/content contracts preserve sizing, close, focus, and dirty-state behavior.\n\nThe outline stays in the shared MarkdownPreview/PlanEditor layer. Enrich the rendered navigation after parsing so section headings and P/D anchors are clearly distinguished, while the full-detail drill-in remains the canonical plan document rather than a second detail renderer.\n\n## Phase 1 — Shared plan-popup upgrade\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add an accessible fullscreen toggle to `apps/operator/app/_components/plans/PlanPopupModal.tsx` that fullscreenes the entire plan dialog (header, tabs and content) through the browser Fullscreen API. Reuse existing fullscreen icon/button conventions; update the label/icon from Fullscreen to Exit fullscreen from fullscreenchange state; disable with an explanatory tooltip when unavailable; preserve close, dirty-edit confirmation, URL-backed tab state and sessions tab. Add focused tests for enter, exit, external/Escape exit, unsupported API and existing popup behavior. importance: high blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-2146690 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Search the component registry, define the popup/fullscreen/outline/detail-action UI IR, validate and lint it, and pin keyboard, responsive, URL-state, and theme behavior. importance: high — note: ← WI-2146691 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add focused failing regression tests for shared host theme inheritance, fullscreen/restore, all P/D dashboard drill-ins, target cleanup, and outline reachability. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-2146692 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Replace hard-coded Vditor and outline colors with resolved semantic theme behavior and live theme updates in the canonical shared MarkdownPreview/PlanEditor path. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-2146693 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Make every PlanDashboard P-item and D-decision open the canonical full-plan view at its exact anchor, while preserving a separate linked-work-item action. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-2146694 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Redesign the shared outline navigation with hierarchy, semantic tokens, active and focus states, P/D enrichment, and responsive behavior. blocked-by: P-004, P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-2146695 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Run focused component suites and typechecks, build the shared surface, and verify light/dark/system themes, fullscreen, keyboard use, and linked/unlinked P/D detail paths in both the staging desktop/operator and `:3081` portal. blocked-by: P-001, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-2146696 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Defer implementation\nDate: 2026-09-04\nAvi explicitly asked to disregard implementation and write the fullscreen request to a plan. This records the historical authorization state that was in force on 2026-09-04; D-003 supersedes it after the later owner directive.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-002 — Fullscreen target is the complete plan dialog\nDate: 2026-09-04\nWhen implemented, the target is the modal content element containing the plan popup header and body, not only the scrollable plan body. This keeps the title, tabs, close control and reading surface together. The browser Fullscreen API is the primary web mechanism; desktop-specific window fullscreen behavior is outside this item.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-003 — The 2026-09-05 owner directive reopens and broadens the work\nDate: 2026-09-05\nAvi explicitly requested the fullscreen button plus correct theme inheritance, a redesigned outline, and full-detail access for every plan item and decision. This supersedes D-001's defer instruction. Execution still follows the normal plan-review and route-selection gate.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-004 — The plan UI remains one shared implementation\nDate: 2026-09-05\nThe portal and desktop/operator already share the canonical plan components. `packages/operator-ui/src/surfaces/index.tsx` is a host facade, not a second implementation. This work extends the shared components and adds no host-specific copy.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-005 — Full detail is the canonical plan at an exact anchor\nDate: 2026-09-05\nA P-item or D-decision opens PlanPopupModal/PlanDetail at its exact identifier through URL-owned state and `scrollPlanTarget`. This preserves surrounding context, editing, status, evidence, and cross-references. A linked work item remains separately available rather than replacing plan-item detail with feature detail.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-006 — Direct implementation and design-phase workflow approved [turn:01a072c2-188a-7d40-b73b-fcfe5f9dce06@2026-09-05T20:23:46.626Z]\nDate: 2026-09-05\nAfter receiving the complete expanded-plan summary, recommended self-implementation route, design-phase registry workflow, and available fleet alternatives [turn:01a072c2-188a-7d40-b73b-fcfe5f9dce06@2026-09-05T19:01:48.893Z], Avi directed this session to continue where it left off [turn:01a072c2-188a-7d40-b73b-fcfe5f9dce06@2026-09-05T20:23:46.626Z]. That continuation approves direct implementation in this session and use of `design-phase.search_registry`, `design-phase.validate_spec`, and `design-phase.lint_spec` without another route or plan prompt.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n## Out of scope\n\nDesktop window-level fullscreen APIs, a second plan/detail renderer, a portal-only or desktop-only component fork, changes to unrelated WorkItemPopupModal behavior, and redesign of plan authoring semantics.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"portal-universal-bar-and-agent-roster-2026-08-31-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — portal universal bar, agent roster, Ask Papercup, and LiveKit voice parity","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-04","owner":"su-ff91e268-bf1a-4f97-9e51-93857bd54827","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — portal universal bar, agent roster, Ask Papercup, and LiveKit voice parity\nslug: portal-universal-bar-and-agent-roster-2026-08-31-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-04\nupdated: 2026-09-04\nowner: su-ff91e268-bf1a-4f97-9e51-93857bd54827\n---\n\n# Acceptance — portal universal bar, agent roster, Ask Papercup, and LiveKit voice parity\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nThe plan exists because EI-20185455308799001 was terminalized TWICE from a single zero snapshot while the leader-required criterion was lifecycle root cause: the closer's own narration was the only thing standing between a hollow close and committed authority. The definition of done is therefore not 'an evaluator exists' but 'the deciding path now refuses the specific closes that motivated it, refuses nothing honest, and cannot be talked out of it by a declaration'. Grade the outcomes below, not the diff. A grader should spot-check the implementer's audit citations (plans:audit auditSeq 2, auditedSha 28484a53) rather than take them on trust; every cited path resolves in the committed tree. Evidence baseline: testing:run over terminal-criteria.test.ts + complete.test.ts at 2026-09-05T10:23Z returned 376 passed / 0 failed (78 + 298).\n\nFILE-PATH CONVENTION FOR EVERY REPLICATION DRILL BELOW: every named test block lives in packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/terminal-criteria.test.ts UNLESS the drill explicitly gives a different path. This is stated because rev 3 did not state it and a grader following the drills literally searched complete.test.ts, which contains ZERO terminalCriteria references — an empty grep that reads exactly like the absence the drill exists to detect.\n\nSTATED LIMITATION, DELIBERATE AND OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS GRADING: the outcome that matters most in the long run — whether enforcement actually reduces hollow closes in the field — is NOT a criterion here, because it is unmeasurable today. The gate is committed but not deployed (dev:pipeline_position on complete.ts: deployed false; the running operator's code is as-of 2026-09-01 against a 2026-09-05 commit), so every close in the population was judged by the OLD path. Do not read the absence of a field-efficacy criterion as an oversight, and do not let a grader pass or fail this plan on speculation about it. The measurement to run once deployed: compare the rate of committed bug/change closes whose sole verifiedHow is a forbidden mode, before vs after the deploy watermark; the criteria below are the necessary conditions for that measurement to be worth taking at all.\n\nREVISION HISTORY. Rev 3: the author graded this rubric against meta-acceptance-rubric before requesting grading and repaired two findings — criterion 7 led with a check readable from the diff alone rather than the outcome it protects, and D-014 (whole-string matching, which keeps 16 qualified honest closes out of the failure set) had gradeable consequences with no covering criterion. Rev 4: an independent grader (su-95fb613c) found that criterion 2's drill sent them to the wrong test file; on inspection the defect was broader than the one instance they hit — FIVE drills named a test block without naming its file — so all five are now explicit rather than just the reported one.\n\nSECOND STATED LIMITATION, ADDED REV 5 (vetting finding F1; ruled in D-019). The forbidden-evidence-mode conjunct adjudicates a SELF-REPORTED label: a closer who would have written verifiedHow:'already-passing' can write 'unit' instead and that conjunct passes. This is NOT the field-efficacy question above — relabelling-resistance is an in-process property and IS gradeable today — so it is named here rather than left for a grader to discover.\nScope it correctly before grading anything on it. The two criteria are ANDed and only ONE of them is self-reported: durable-change resolves the declared paths against real Git blob identity taken from the SERVER tree stamp (durableChangeRating, packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/terminal-criteria.ts), so relabelling CANNOT manufacture a fix out of nothing — a close that landed no durable change still fails whatever label it carries. The residual gap is real but narrower than 'the gate passes them': a close that DID land a durable change but INFLATES its verification label.\nNo criterion grades that, deliberately. The natural cross-check — corroborating the claimed mode against addedTests — was designed and then killed by measurement on this very plan: addedTests is empty across all 851 closes in the population (recorded in the shipped comment in terminal-criteria.ts, alongside a filler-token stoplist killed the same way). A criterion demanding relabelling-resistance would therefore grade the gate against a corroborating field that does not exist in the data, and the only way to pass it would be to build the cross-check on a population of zero — the exact error this plan already caught twice, imported into the acceptance instrument itself, where it would be graded green by whoever built the dead code. Do not read the absence of a relabelling criterion as an oversight; grade criterion 1's 'rejects THAT incident' as bounded by the stated label, with durable-change as the non-self-reported half that holds regardless.\n\nRev 5: folded the three findings from the independent vetting critique (su-respawn-4787beb0, not in the author's lineage, implemented none of this). F3 exposed a gap in the WORK, not just the rubric — there was no way to switch enforcement off without a revert — so an owner-flippable default-ON kill-switch was BUILT (D-018) and is graded by the new eighth criterion. F2 (criterion 1 is n=1, all four payloads from one incident) is repaired with a held-out admit case. F1 (nothing grades relabelling-resistance) is ruled a stated limitation rather than a criterion, with the measured reason recorded in D-019.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan portal-operator-proxy-budget-2026-09-05 (bug EI-22460658078754511), authored against the as-built PORTAL tree — the sibling checkout at ~/papercupai-workspace/portal (HEAD ff24ba99 plus this plan's edits to the portal host's operator-origin, operator-sync and operator-passthrough modules and its new operator-proxy-budget test). Portal files are named BY MODULE below, never as papercusp-relative paths; the papercusp harness holds no code for this fix. Root cause, measured 2026-09-05 22:50Z: the portal host's operatorFetch aborted every FORWARDED operator read at a 2.5s header budget (OPERATOR_TIMEOUT_MS, meant for the self-hiding workspace-stats readout) while the browser's sync client (DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS in @papercusp/sync) waits 20s; under fleet load the operator's tail crossed 2.5s on 3 of 120 concurrent reads (max 3.3s, p90 7ms) and every one reached the page as a fabricated 502 with no journal line. D-001 fixes the forwarded-leg budget at 30s (above the client, equal to the blanket passthrough's header budget; the browser's own abort signal remains the real deadline). Grader: spot-check the implementer's plans:audit citations against the portal tree, run the two portal test files there (from the portal root: npx vitest run operator-proxy-budget operator-passthrough), and drive :3081 yourself (curl burst + verdict) for the live criterion — the release under test must contain OPERATOR_PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS (grep the served release directory that the portal runtime's `current` symlink points to).\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Goal: every desktop ADV tab the portal still lacked (health, prs, insights, conversations, settings, docs, history, git, stats, testing, plans/create, calendar/scheduled, frames, evals) plus the /coord dashboard is reachable from the portal rail and renders the desktop body, honouring D-004 (dedicated rail entries, never a restored tab strip, never hidden tabs), D-005 (calendar tab is 'scheduled'/\"Scheduled\") and D-006 ('create'/\"Create\", 'adv-settings'/\"ADV Settings\"). Every criterion names the goal clause or Decision it enforces. REV 2 (self-vetted against meta-acceptance-rubric): rev-1 'deep-links' merged into 'body-renders-live' (a strict special case: the deep-link collapse is one of that criterion's own failure modes); structured test bindings added where a papercusp test decides the outcome; a failure-mode criterion added covering the pre-existing rail kinds, the unknown-kind fallback, create-without-plan, and previous-release chunk continuity across the deploy. REV 3: bindings corrected to the assertions that actually detect each drift — the empty embed tab strip is pinned by adv-shell-logic.test.ts ('renders NO Papercusp tab strip inside a cloud embed'), not the registry test; the registry test's 'renames only the kinds whose ADV id the portal already uses (D-005 / D-006)' and 'gives a surface exactly the pot bar the operator gives its tab' assertions are now bound on naming-decisions and pot-scope-parity. Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan `progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05`, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality (audited at 5d11e99627, auditSeq 5), and REVISED at revision 2 from an independent vetting critique (consult conv-mtojdqwy-0000-15e6540f598a4175ac762ab0070a87f2, 2026-09-05). Builds on class `plan-class-feature-ship` — the class already carries goal-outcomes-met, tests-ship-with-feature, flag-on-default, gate-green-shipped, docs-updated and audit-citations-spot-checked, so nothing below restates them. The seven criteria here are the plan-SPECIFIC commitments, each tracing to a numbered Decision.\n\nGRADER, READ THIS FIRST — a mechanic that has refused complete cards before: rate ONLY the seven bespoke keys below. A card keyed with class criteria (`goal-outcomes-met`, `audit-citations-spot-checked`, …) is REFUSED at emit with 'unexpected criterion key(s)' — the expected key set is the bespoke criteria, never a union with the class. Assess the class criteria in your card's `body` instead. Note also that this plan is `status: draft` with all five items `done`: all-items-terminal is not a shipped plan, and `plans:items` cannot tell you it isn't.\n\nThe plan's goal was a CONSUMPTION fix, not a new signal (D-002): release:trace could recommend `checkpoint:await` off an aging run-lock snapshot, leaving the operator to interpret raw lane heartbeats and exposing two symmetric harms — killing healthy work, or waiting passively on a wedged producer. The shipped answer is a pure certificate consumed at the recommendation site.\n\nTWO THINGS THE GRADER MUST NOT LET ME OFF ON. (1) The plan declared a single falsifier — one false `stalled` on a progressing run — and it did not fire, but it also could not have: D-012/D-014 established that the stall branch was structurally unreachable for the runs sampled (164 samples, all `unknown`; exercised=1, liveHeartbeat=0, cacheDescribedRun=0). D-015 later proved the branch IS reachable by chaining the real producer in a test. So the certificate is proven REACHABLE and CORRECT-GIVEN-ITS-INPUT; it is NOT proven CALIBRATED. (2) Consequently BOTH DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS (600_000) and DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_TRUST_MS (300_000) remain declared judgements (D-007), and `thresholds-disposition-recorded` exists to make that gradeable rather than quietly inherited. `falsifier-reported-with-its-scope` binds the same gap forward, onto YOUR card and the ship note — artifacts that did not exist when this rubric was written.\n\nSTRUCTURED CHECKS (D-006 / P-011), added at revision 3: five of the seven criteria carry a kind:'tests' binding that scorecards:emit RUNS at grading time, so a `pass` those suites contradict is refused at emit — await-only-on-progressing and retriage-interlock-unconditional bind release-trace.test.ts; ambiguity-never-stalls and no-parallel-monitor bind release-trace-progress.test.ts; producer-to-certifier-seam-tested binds git-pipeline-position.test.ts. The remaining two — falsifier-reported-with-its-scope and thresholds-disposition-recorded — are marked instrumentKey:'none' DELIBERATELY: both grade what the shipped RECORD says, which no test can assert, and the meta-rubric explicitly preserves fuzzy judgment criteria exactly where the outcome is not objectively checkable. Their bar is the replication drill plus, for the falsifier criterion, the forward obligation on your own evidence string.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-pui-tui-next-wave-2026-09-05","title":"Acceptance BAR — PUI/TUI next wave — close-out of the 2 unshipped plans, session-lifecycle hardening, and the owner-prioritised improvement slate","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-d694b5df-c6c9-4deb-b84e-07b9a1b2df69","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — PUI/TUI next wave — close-out of the 2 unshipped plans, session-lifecycle hardening, and the owner-prioritised improvement slate\nslug: acceptance-pui-tui-next-wave-2026-09-05\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-06\nowner: su-d694b5df-c6c9-4deb-b84e-07b9a1b2df69\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — PUI/TUI next wave — close-out of the 2 unshipped plans, session-lifecycle hardening, and the owner-prioritised improvement slate\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for the plan, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. REVISION 2 — rewritten from the rubric-vetting critique on consults conv-mtnopemt-0000-ada2e2eb2bc94d6db881e17142995213 (post 83695) and conv-mtnp3nlc-0000-93f9ab1b906c41749c1b93fb1af586d5 (post 83700). This revision RAISES the bar above what revision 1 had already been graded against, so some criteria are expected to read `unknown` until the additional observations are collected. That is intentional: the rubric is the definition of done, not a description of what happened to get measured.\n\nWHAT THE CRITIQUE CHANGED, so a grader can see the reasoning rather than re-derive it:\n(1) SOUNDNESS HOLE, now fixed: never-starved graded COUNT PARITY, and 0 == 0 satisfies parity — a window in which the stream emitted nothing was a clean PASS, and fanout-actually-reduced did not catch it either because a zero baseline makes dropPct 0/0. Both criteria now carry a baseline-liveness conjunct that makes such a reading VOID rather than pass-or-fail.\n(2) never-starved graded CARDINALITY, not identity: a filter that dropped one real event and duplicated another passed count parity unchanged. It now compares by event identity.\n(3) replay-not-narrowed is RETIRED as a standalone criterion. Both halves of it were satisfied by construction — unfiltered replay is the default, and 'a recorded decision' was discharged by the author commenting on their own choice. Its real value is its interaction with starvation across a growth-triggered reconnect, so it is folded into never-starved as an OBSERVATION.\n(4) The measurement models the wrong topology: three independent long-lived connections, where production is ONE elected socket with follower tabs plus reconnects. The reconnect path is folded into never-starved; the follower path becomes its own criterion.\n(5) instrument-falsifiable is bound PER READING rather than to 'the instrument' as one global object, and now names the isolation property a control must have.\n\nCLASS CHOICE, stated because it is arguable: originating work-item WI-7331 is filed as a `change`/defect, which would suggest plan-class-bugfix. I took the stricter plan-class-feature-ship because the class should track the RISK SURFACE of what shipped, not the filing kind of the ticket: this introduces a new wire contract, changes what every connected client receives, and touches the cross-tab socket-election path. Bugfix is for changes whose blast radius is bounded by the defect; this one's is bounded by the client population. Note the consequence — the feature-ship class requires the grader to spot-check the implementer's audit citations.\n\nTHE CENTRAL RISK THIS RUBRIC POLICES: the failure mode is SILENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A filter that drops nothing is a no-op that every unit test still passes. A filter that drops too much starves a client into stale UI, which users report as 'the page is wrong sometimes', not as a filter bug. Criteria are written so BOTH failures are detectable, and no criterion may be satisfied by the implementation's own unit assertions alone where a live observation is what is actually claimed.\n\nACCEPTED WITHOUT A CRITERION, recorded rather than left silent (plan decision D-006): the declared interest set is GROW-ONLY for the life of a connection, so filtering benefit decays with connection age and mount count, and a long-lived connection eventually crosses MAX_DECLARED_QUERY_NAMES and reverts to full fan-out. Unbounded growth is accepted for now with the cap as its backstop; what is NOT accepted is that the reversion be invisible, which is why cap-crossing observability is folded into fails-open-on-ambiguity.\n\nREVISION 3 adds STRUCTURED CHECKS (kind:'tests') to the four criteria whose outcome is deterministically checkable, so they are CHECKED rather than attested: fails-open-on-ambiguity, single-wire-contract, sockets-not-multiplied and union-covers-followers each bind the Vitest files that must PASS at grading time. The remaining three — fanout-actually-reduced, instrument-falsifiable and never-starved — are deliberately left unbound: each grades a LIVE OBSERVATION against a shared event stream (or a mutation-probe control), which no must-pass unit file can stand in for. Binding them to a unit suite would be the exact substitution this rubric's central risk warns against — a green suite standing in for a measurement that was never taken.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-tool-contract-class-sizing-non-vacuous-guard-2026-09-05","title":"Acceptance — tool-contract class sizing, and a regression guard that cannot pass vacuously","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-4b4fd2ae-6a75-4331-8e6c-954fb9d0e313","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — tool-contract class sizing, and a regression guard that cannot pass vacuously\nslug: acceptance-tool-contract-class-sizing-non-vacuous-guard-2026-09-05\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\nowner: su-4b4fd2ae-6a75-4331-8e6c-954fb9d0e313\n---\n\n# Acceptance — tool-contract class sizing, and a regression guard that cannot pass vacuously\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for tool-contract-class-sizing-and-non-vacuous-guard-2026-09-05, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality. The six criteria are the plan's own Design Bars R-1..R-6 (see its '## Requirements' section and its 'Design Bar -> work map'), one criterion each, checkable against the tree without reading the item list. R-3, R-4 and R-5 carry a STRUCTURED CHECK bound to the guard's own test file, so a pass-rating on any of them that the run contradicts is refused at emit — a rubric about a guard that cannot pass vacuously should not itself be gradeable on prose alone.\n\nWHY THIS PLAN EXISTS — stated carefully, because the obvious framing is FALSE. The parent plan ratified a hazard (its D-008): that a zod schema ending in .refine/.preprocess loses .shape, so a catalog-wide per-argument guard would iterate nothing and pass green while citing coverage. Two things then turned out to be untrue. (1) The MECHANISM is dead: at zod 4.4.3 .refine/.superRefine KEEP .shape (parent D-011, D-012; this plan's D-004). (2) The parent's own P-009 guard was measured NOT VACUOUS — 854/854 tools scanned, 0 dropped — because it reads the projected JSON Schema and never consults the zod shape at all (parent D-010). So this plan is NOT 'the fix for a vacuous parent guard'. What remained genuinely open, and what this plan did, is three things: size the defect class re-runnably, measure which wrappers actually hide the shape and on how many live tools, and build a REDIRECT contract guard whose floors come from that measurement rather than from item text — and prove it can fail. The vacuity HAZARD is real and worth guarding against; the claim that it had already occurred in the parent is not.\n\nGRADER NOTES — three corrections are already on the record; expect to find them, and grade their HANDLING rather than re-filing them as fresh defects. (a) The implementer (this rubric's author) reported '29/29 green' for the guard test. FALSE and retracted: the file has 12 tests and had 12 at the implementer's own commit 4f78f2ecfe, so it was wrong-when-written, not drift. Caught by su-ce26a18a, independently re-found by you in phase A, corrected in plans:audit auditSeq 4. The P-004 verdict is unaffected — only the count was false. (b) Revision 1 of THIS rubric asserted in its description that the parent's P-009 guard 'was VACUOUS', and its R-6 criterion told you to confirm that finding on the parent. That was the same error a second time — a claim inherited rather than re-derived — self-caught before any grading card was emitted, by reading parent D-010 instead of trusting the framing. Revision 2 corrected the description and R-6. (c) Your phase-A finding that P-001's citation was stale (test cited @b011b833 while the same path resolved @aeffb115 under P-004/P-005 in the same audit, because P-001's entry carried forward from audit #3) was accepted and fixed: plans:audit auditSeq 5 re-resolves P-001 ONLY at staging 53c92ba8c2318b67, verdicts unchanged, 0 uncovered items. The blob shas were re-derived locally rather than taken from the report.\n\nBASELINE THE AUTHOR MEASURED (2026-09-05T15:43Z, staging 53c92ba8c2, clean tree, uncommitted=0): the guard test runs 12 passed / 0 skipped, exit 0, and its live scan reports toolsInspected=817 argsInspected=4178 toolsWithRedirects=28 declarations=129 issues=0. Note this sits ABOVE the pinned floors of 26/122 — that gap is the shrink-only design working as intended, not drift to be scored as a defect.\n\nGRADING MECHANICS (revision 5, from the vetting critique): (1) The grader rates THESE SIX bespoke keys ONLY. A card that also keys the `plan-class-bugfix` class criteria (root-cause-named, recurrence-guard, …) is REFUSED at emit with 'unexpected criterion key(s)' — the class criteria must still be ASSESSED, in the card's `body` prose. (2) Revision 5 folds in the rubric-vetting critique (consult conv-mtojm7y8, responder su-44c8a3b5, post 95053) and grader su-034c7943's R-4 correction, batched into ONE bump so a peer card is not un-counted. (3) The vetter's own eligibility to GRADE this rubric was spent by answering the vetting consult (grader_is_sole_vetting_critic); the grading is routed elsewhere. (4) The vetter tried to construct a vacuity attack against R-3 and could not: both denominators are floored, `zero-accepted-keys` is a real issue kind raised as an error, declarations are counted per tool, and the detector controls including the negative calibration case are held permanently.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-tool-contract-repair-2026-09-05","title":"Acceptance: tool contract repair (71-filing invalid_args class)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-9f0de75b-b0a0-4452-906e-5b44204d65f7","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: tool contract repair (71-filing invalid_args class)\nslug: acceptance-tool-contract-repair-2026-09-05\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-06\nowner: su-9f0de75b-b0a0-4452-906e-5b44204d65f7\n---\n\n# Acceptance: tool contract repair (71-filing invalid_args class)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). So 'call the tool and see whether it still rejects the bad key' measures the wrong build and fails in BOTH directions: a landed fix reads as still-broken, and an unlanded one can read as fixed. Verify against PARSED CURRENT SOURCE in the staging tree, or POST to :3170 explicitly. A criterion graded by a bare :3070 call is not graded.\n\nSecond caveat: this plan was executed by a fleet and its work was SPLIT. su-8d170842 took the harness/scope-key cluster under WI-2145930; this lane took the argRedirect alias/rename and work_items clusters. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation definition-of-done, authored against as-built reality after P-001/P-002/P-003 landed. Grades OUTCOMES, not whether code was written. The plan's premise is that a large ungraded filing population (agent-review) had no consumer; each criterion asks whether that is now false.\n\nACCEPTANCE PLANE (revision 2, added at the independent grader's request before grading — su-85ae1b7c, 2026-09-05T21:33Z; recorded as plan D-004). Revision 1 said \"the serving system\" and \"production triage\", which the grader correctly read as requiring behaviour observable only on deployed main. That is unearnable here and not what these criteria are for: the standing convention is that the CURRENT BUILD (working tree / staging :3170) is the implementation and acceptance plane, and green main / :3070 is reserved for final promotion. So every criterion below is graded against the current build. A change that is correct on the current build but not yet promoted is DEPLOY LAG, which is the pipeline's state and not a defect of this plan; it does not reduce any rating.\n\nWhat that does NOT excuse: the failure modes these criteria actually target are all observable on the current build. An inert code path — a module that exists and passes unit tests but that no call site invokes — is a FAIL on the current build and stays a fail. Aggregation that deletes or hides member filings is a fail on the current build. A rail that hard-codes an origin literal is a fail on the current build. Deploy lag excuses only the absence of production ROW COUNTS, never the absence of an invocation, a divert, a citation, or a per-origin cap.\n\naggregation-is-additive traces directly to D-001. staleness-screen-is-reached is the criterion most likely to fail on an inert-but-tested code path, so grade it by execution on the current build (a positive control that actually diverts), not by presence.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nComposite release-gating rubric for the auto-loop product AS IT EXISTS AFTER the 2026-08-09 Mug/Cup/Kettle retirement (plan retire-mug-kettle-su-only-2026-08-09 D-001; the `papercusp-mug-kettle-system` flag is DELETED, not default-OFF, and cup:spawn / kettle:* / curation:state-of-pot REFUSE): the Blender self-learning leg plus capacity admission, owner controls, and release parity. Composes (does not duplicate) the leg rubric blender-release-readiness. Origin: EI-12461/EI-12455; owner directive [owner:Avi turn f362a778@2026-07-16T20:31:59Z].\n\nCRITERIA REMOVED 2026-09-05 (WI-2145252) — they grade a subsystem that no longer runs, and a mandatory component that CANNOT be graded is not a strict gate, it is a permanently-red one. That is the standard already set one level up by apps/operator/lib/release/release-profile.ts (AUTOLOOP_COMPONENT_RUBRIC_REFS, WI-5379, 7 -> 4 component rubrics); this applies it one level DOWN, to the criteria inside the composite:\n  placement-throughput (instrument pot-throughput-ticks) · cup-execution-health (mug-dispatched-cup-spawns) · kettle-supervision-health (kettle-autoloop-state) · e2e-loop-closure (e2e-traversal-trace)\n\ne2e-loop-closure was NOT named in the filing and was removed on the SAME standard after independent measurement: its traversal is defined as pot_placements row -> Mug-dispatched cup spawn -> kettle scorecard -> blender ledger, and harness_shared.pot_placements has ZERO rows in the last 30 days (newest 2026-07-19T13:03Z) while child_role=cup spawns stopped 2026-08-17T19:02Z. Leaving it would have left the rubric ungradeable, i.e. a non-fix.\n\nSurvivors were verified live before being kept: capacity-admission reads scout_ticks (639 rows in 30d, newest 2026-09-05T04:02Z — Scout survives the retirement per D-001) and accounts:status; owner-controls needs only READ verbs, and pot:get-steering / pot:status / autoloop:status are live (pot:set-steering is retired, which the criterion already forbids invoking); blender-leg-health defers to the live blender-release-readiness rubric; release-parity reads deployed-generation state.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"feature-change-reconciliation-and-zero-state-clarity-2026-09-05","title":"Feature/change reconciliation and unambiguous zero-claimability semantics","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-05","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Feature/change reconciliation and unambiguous zero-claimability semantics\nslug: feature-change-reconciliation-and-zero-state-clarity-2026-09-05\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-30\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-09-26, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_method_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing. Next repair: Fill the BAR METHOD/check contract before vetting or grading. (R-1). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nP-001 through P-004 are complete. Avi explicitly resumed the canonical non-P2P feature/change drain under D-015.
