The existing WI-2034624 regression explicitly requires fail-closed wait for untyped live members.\n\nAuthority: D-015 assigns fleet liveness, replacement, blockers, and terminal verification to the leader; owner explicitly designated this successor as leader.\nRelated: P-005, WI-10000745, WI-2034624\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-017 — Reject audit #14’s stale four-shard residue; live aggregates require fresh authoritative assignments\nDate: 2026-09-08\nDate: 2026-09-08\nRULING: Audit #14's statement that P-004 shards 44, 47, 49, and 50 are live/open is rejected as a stale-input false alarm. P-005 must regenerate the 50-row assignment snapshot from the authoritative work-item ledger before running the aggregate and must not call an untimestamped repository artifact a live read. A live aggregate needs a capture timestamp plus source identity; absent that freshness proof, its row-state verdict is UNKNOWN and cannot reopen terminal evidence.\n\nMeasured: direct `work_items:get` reads at 2026-09-08T14:14Z report WI-2146837, WI-2146841, WI-2146842, and WI-2146843 all `done`, committed, with fresh artifact content and no reopen lifecycle event. The consumed file `scratchpad/feature-change-reconciliation-and-zero-state-clarity-2026-09-05-p004-validation-live-assignments.json` was last committed 2026-09-07T10:22:14-04:00, has only a `rows` array, and retains the old 46-done/4-open snapshot. Detector repair is filed as EI-22703147954431247.\n\nAuthority: D-015 forbids reopening the terminal P-004 cohort; P-005 requires fresh exact populations and complete audit evidence.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, EI-22703147954431247\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-018 — Interpret scheduler windDown by reason/paused fields, not as fleet control state\nDate: 2026-09-08\nCode-truth ruling after owner resume: scheduler:get_next's fleetScopedMiss sets windDown:true for an ACTIVE fleet whenever the scoped claim path has no claimable row and no survivor/divergence exception. A real fleet pause is a distinct preflight branch: readFleetPauseState requires registry controlState='winding-down', and only that branch adds paused:true plus the winding-down error. Therefore reason='all_matches_gated' with claimable=0 means an active, floor-gated pool—not a stale pause or resume-control defect. Retract prior leader messages/findings that inferred pause divergence from windDown alone. Report a resume mismatch only with a current response carrying paused:true/code fleet_winding_down after active fleet state; otherwise park on the returned claimability filter and do not re-author the spec.\n\n### D-019 — Treat creation-time claimable events as edge hints; duplicate admission remains authoritative\nDate: 2026-09-08\nDate: 2026-09-08\nRULING: WI-10000818 is not a revision-19 spec failure and does not justify a fleet resume/spec mutation. Its creation-time `work-item:claimable` event is an edge hint: the emitter guards assignee/state/claim-hold/plan-lane, but duplicate admission is a separate scheduler floor. `scheduler:get_next` remains authoritative and correctly refuses the row while `admissionPending` is present. Members must not claim by id, re-file, or keep escalating this unchanged state; park on the existing claimability watch and pull again only after the promoter changes admission. A later scheduler miss with unchanged `admissionPending` is no delta.\n\nMeasured: `work_items:get` at 2026-09-08T21:02Z showed WI-10000818 open and unassigned. Peer `work_items:observe` evidence reported `gated:true` with `admissionPending` duplicate screening. Source reads of `work-items.ts` showed create always calls `emitWorkItemCreatedEvent`; `work-items-events.ts` showed the claimable co-fire does not evaluate duplicate admission; `work-items.ts::observeWorkItem` and `scheduler/get-next.ts` showed duplicate admission is evaluated separately and exposed as the `admission_pending` floor. The shared explanation in `work-items-admission.ts` assigns clearing to the durable promoter and describes the existing-row remedies.\n\nThis decision supersedes every message that inferred `windDown:true` meant fleet control was winding down; D-018 already governs that separate field interpretation.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-020 — Observation-lane claimable wakes are emitter-floor defects, not revision-19 scheduler divergence\nDate: 2026-09-09\nRULING: EI-22689325784232956 is correctly excluded by the scheduler's unconditional observation-lane floor even though revision 19's authored view filter matches its kind/change, harness, and non-P2P plan. `work_items:observe available:true` is tuple/by-id availability, not proof that opportunistic scheduler self-selection may serve the row. The release wake is a detector false positive: `emitWorkItemClaimableEvent` checks assignee, claimable state, claim-hold, duplicate admission, and plan-lane blockage, but does not apply `observationLaneExclusionSql`; the scheduler candidate path does apply it as `ok_observation`, and comments explicitly say observation rows are not work-queue material. Therefore do not mutate revision 19, claim the observation by id, infer scheduler divergence, or infer fleet drain from this wake. Treat this exact item/reason as reconciled after one authoritative pull and retain the scoped await; future repeats are no delta. The separately suggested concurrency explanation is also false: the writer calls `readClaimConcurrency` with the individual caller's ownerId, so WI-10000742 held by the leader cannot consume another member's maxConcurrentClaims slot.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-09 live `work_items:observe` reported EI-22689325784232956 open, unassigned, payload.lane='observation', source plan papercup-owner-reports-and-ledger-recovery-2026-09-09 P-007. `scheduler:get_claim_spec` returned revision 19 unchanged with kind in {feature,change}, non-P2P exclusions, and maxConcurrentClaims=1. Source reads: packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts::observationLaneExclusionSql returns lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation' and declares the floor unconditional; packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/get-next.ts applies it as ok_observation; packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-events.ts::emitWorkItemClaimableEvent omits that floor; packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scheduler/get_next.ts and scheduler/claim-spec-store.ts pass the individual caller ownerId/cupId into readClaimConcurrency. Canonical detector bug: EI-22773307703217310; consolidate same-incident filings there rather than minting more duplicates.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-021 — Plan-owner release wakes may legitimately re-miss for generic fleet members\nDate: 2026-09-09\nRULING: WI-10000890 is not a revision-19 scheduler mismatch and is not a second D-020 observation-floor reproduction. Its P-003 external blocker cleared and emitted the broad `work-item:claimable` edge, but P-003 already carried a live plan-item claim held by su-116734b2-b2f7-4315-8a9d-1f19376a7ef5. The shared `reservedPlanLaneExclusionSql` deliberately excludes a plan-linked candidate from every other claimant while allowing the lane owner; the same owner then claimed WI-10000890. A global edge can therefore be actionable for its rightful owner while generic fleet watchers correctly re-miss. One authoritative pull is the expected reconciliation; no spec mutation, by-id claim, or bug filing follows. D-020 stays narrow to unconditional floors the emitter could apply before emitting (specifically observation lane); do not consolidate claimant-relative plan-reservation wakes into that detector defect.\n\nMeasured: `plan_items:status` at 2026-09-09T09:02Z reported use-existing-router-for-review-requests-2026-09-08#P-003 effective todo, disposition claimed-pooled, live claim/holder su-116734b2-b2f7-4315-8a9d-1f19376a7ef5, and implementing WI-10000890. Concurrent `work_items:observe` reported WI-10000890 claimed by that same owner at 09:01:18Z and available=false. Source read: packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts::reservedPlanLaneExclusionSql includes live plan-item claims held by another owner, and the predicate is shared by feature- and issue-family claim paths. Retract messages/findings that called this a scheduler divergence, a plan-readiness bug, or D-020 reproduction; owners of EI-22773726428715145 / EI-22773789433985971 should correct or terminalize those false-premise filings.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-022 — Revision-19 concurrency is per member, not a fleet-wide single slot\nDate: 2026-09-09\nRULING: Revision 19's `limits.maxConcurrentClaims: 1` caps each member's own held work-items. It is not a fleet-wide semaphore. A leader's leadership work-item therefore cannot consume another member's claim slot. On a scheduler miss, read the caller-specific concurrency diagnosis and its `heldIds`; do not infer fleet starvation from the aggregate assignment count or ask an unrelated holder to release.\n\nMeasured: `scheduler:get_claim_spec` returned fleet revision 19 with maxConcurrentClaims=1. A simultaneous `fleet:assignments` read showed leader su-62f84751 holding WI-10000742 while reporting member su-08c9879 held zero claims. Source: `agent-tools/scheduler/get_next.ts` calls `readClaimConcurrency` with `cupId: args.ownerId`; `scheduler/claim-spec-store.ts::getActiveClaimsForBee` filters `taken_by` to that exact cup id. The fleet-scope concurrency regression suite asserts the same owner-local verdict.\n\nThis does not change D-019/D-021: a claimable edge may still legitimately re-miss for admission or claimant-relative reasons. It only corrects the claim-cap explanation.\nRelated: P-005\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-023 — Mixed-family misses: feature rows are withheld by stop-the-line even when observe reports available\nDate: 2026-09-09\nDate: 2026-09-09\nRULING: WI-10000864 is not evidence of a revision-19 filter or claim-path mismatch. It matches revision 19's `kind in {feature,change}` and non-P2P view and `work_items:observe` reports it open, unassigned, and `available:true`; that availability is the tuple/by-id contract, not proof that opportunistic self-selection may bypass every scheduler floor. The row is feature-family. `claimFloorsWhereSql` composes `stopTheLineExclusionSql(sql, 'feature-consolidated')`, whose feature branch is exactly `NOT activeRedStreak` with no per-row exemption. Therefore, while the papercusp `gate-red-streak:` condition remains open past 24 hours, every feature-family row—including plan-promoted WI-10000864—is withheld from scheduler self-select. P-001 itself is healthy: todo, pooled/unclaimed, and has no blockers.\n\nThe current scheduler envelope's `reason:'all_matches_gated'`, `matchedByFilter`, `stopTheLine`, `observationLane`, and `claimable` values describe the issue-family diagnostic only. `families.feature:null` is deliberate and `basis:'partial-family'` is the required qualifier: `scheduler:get_next` invokes `diagnoseFleetScopeFeatureFamilyMatch` only when the issue-family breakdown has `matchedByFilter===0`; with a large nonzero issue-family match set, no feature-family count is run. Do not use those issue counts to size or classify feature rows, and do not treat a transient unmeasured response as a standing defect when a later response restores partial measurement.\n\nOperational consequence: preserve scheduler authority. Do not claim WI-10000864 by id, mutate revision 19, or call the lane drained. Wait for the existing red-gate owner to produce direct deployed/green proof; the condition bridge should then settle the red-streak item and lift the feature floor automatically. Only if a fresh scheduler pull still misses after verified green may the stale condition or feature claim path be investigated.\n\nMeasured: `scheduler:get_claim_spec` at 2026-09-09T13:12Z returned revision 19 with the exact feature/change non-P2P filter. `work_items:observe` and `plan_items:status` at 13:09Z showed WI-10000864 feature/open/unassigned, P-001 todo/pooled/no blockers. Source reads at current staging HEAD 765418ba63bf: `packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts::claimFloorsWhereSql`, `packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-admission.ts::stopTheLineExclusionSql`, `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scheduler/get_next.ts` lines 1872-1982, and `packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/fleet-scope-admission.ts` lines 1590-1658 and 2121-2171. This extends D-018/D-020/D-021/D-022; none of those authorize by-id bypass.\nRelated: P-005\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-024 — P-005 deployed-only exception is limited to live cooperative-respawn readiness\nDate: 2026-09-09\nDate: 2026-09-09\nRULING: P-005's deployed-only property is narrowly limited to the live cooperative-respawn canary required by D-016: a replacement member must be persisted into the already-running fleet governor's `probeOwnerIds` and then appear in that same fleet's typed `workerReadyMemberIds`. Staging/current-build cannot exercise this property because the canonical fleet, its running member terminals, launch transaction, and governor state live in the deployed operator process; changing or testing staging source does not mutate or prove behavior in that existing live runtime.\n\nAll non-final implementation and acceptance remain on staging/current-build: source inspection, focused unit/integration tests, typecheck, claimability/corpus checks, and plan audit must proceed there and must not wait on main. Only after those checks pass and the relevant source is deployed may the leader run one cooperative replacement against a freshly reverified idle/no-claim/no-lock legacy member. The live canary is final shipment evidence, not a prerequisite for unrelated implementation. Preserve the one-live-gate-owner rule: while LIVE_GATE_OPS ownership is held, the leader waits for direct deployment proof and does not inspect, re-run, mutate, or shadow-monitor the current gate.\n\nMeasured: P-005 and WI-2146349 require final live paused/readiness evidence; D-016 binds the canary to `fleet:respawn-member` and the existing governor probe cohort. WI-10000745's checkpoint records source committed to staging but absent from deployed main at its last verified read, and explicitly forbids canary execution before deployed parity. Current non-final source/focused-test evidence remains valid independently of deployment.\nRelated: P-005\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-025 — Current activation-audit rubric conflict is deployed schema skew, not invalid persisted data\nDate: 2026-09-09\nDate: 2026-09-09\nRULING AND RETRACTION: The leader initially diagnosed `plans:audit`'s `bar_rubric_conflict: active acceptance rubric has invalid template_data` as malformed persisted rubric data. That diagnosis was wrong and is withdrawn. The exact stored template_data parses successfully against the current staging `rubricTemplateDataSchema`. The deployed operator at e66be3c4ff7b rejects exactly the top-level `subjectHarnessSlug` field, which current staging recognizes and constrains. `rubrics:get` consequently reports the backing rubric as unprojectable and the deployed `plans:audit` cannot seed/refresh BARs. This is D-016/D-024 deployment parity, not a data-repair authorization.\n\nDo not rewrite, strip, re-propose, or re-ratify the valid rubric to fit stale deployed code; that would destroy current schema evidence and change an already-started BAR contract. Continue every staging/current-build P-005 check that does not require the live runtime. After the live gate owner provides direct deployed parity, rerun `rubrics:get` and `plans:audit {phase:'activation'}`; success must replace the currently stale audit pointer.\n\nMeasured: `plans:get-template-data` returned rubric plan revision 7 with `subjectHarnessSlug:'papercusp'` and eight criteria. A current-staging TS parse at HEAD 765418ba63bf returned success. The same payload parsed against read-only deployed release HEAD e66be3c4ff7b returned one error only: unrecognized key `subjectHarnessSlug`. Source diff shows current staging added that field to `rubricTemplateDataSchema`.\nRelated: P-005\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-026 — The new non-P2P feature fleet preserves existing SELF-route plan authority\nDate: 2026-09-26\nAffects: coordination-metadata-friction-reduction-2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-26. Avi directed a 10-member headless ChatGPT 6 Sol high fleet on non-P2P features. This broad feature-drain direction does NOT silently revoke coordination-metadata-friction-reduction-2026-09-07#D-001, where Avi approved SELF implementation by su-59b85ff1. During the new fleet's first claims, member su-respawn-9b39ebc351e95e74a7db75c3e327daa3 discovered WI-10000551/P-004 under that SELF-only plan, released it without edits and alerted the leader. The leader set scheduler claim spec on fleet nonp2p-feature-drain-sol-high-10-2026-09-26 to revision 3, preserving the prior non-P2P feature-only dynamic filter and adding exclusion of plan=coordination-metadata-friction-reduction-2026-09-07. The setter's whole-family preview reported same matched population before/after (45), so this guards FUTURE reopening rather than disposing work; P-004 stays for its original SELF route or explicit owner reroute. Fleet members must inspect other governing route decisions before implementing; release + report any conflict. Do not count such protected rows as fleet drain residue.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-027 — The feature fleet excludes previously approved solo routes and live gate operations\nDate: 2026-09-26\nAffects: backend-audit-diagnosis-before-repair-2026-09-13, cupboard-release-pipeline-content-trust-2026-09-16, portable-identity-packages-2026-09-26, hud-orders-instant-load-2026-09-13, pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-26. Avi's direction to run a ten-member non-P2P feature fleet does not rescind earlier route-A approvals. Fleet members encountered and released claims whose governing authority reserves execution to a different solo session: backend-audit-diagnosis-before-repair-2026-09-13#D-001, cupboard-release-pipeline-content-trust-2026-09-16#D-006, portable-identity-packages-2026-09-26 ## Now, hud-orders-instant-load-2026-09-13#D-001, and pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07#D-031. The PUI proposal WI-10003251 lacks a structured source-plan slug, so it requires an explicit id exclusion. Current-red gate operations WI-10002995 and WI-10002996 were also admitted despite a live exclusive fixer; they remain outside this fleet's lane. Leader claim-spec revision 6 excludes those five plan slugs and three explicit work-item ids, preserving the existing non-P2P and coordination-metadata exclusions. This is a placement boundary, not a disposition of the work: the original solo owners and gate owner retain their routes. Before editing any newly claimed feature, members must read governing plan decisions and release/report any further conflict. Do not clear claim holds or count these protected items as fleet drain residue without an explicit owner route change.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-028 — Run a five-member gpt-6.1-sol:xhigh non-P2P feature-only drain\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\nRULING: The owner explicitly directed this session to lead a fleet of up to five gpt-6.1-sol agents at xhigh effort on a non-P2P feature drain. This run narrows D-015 from feature+change to open feature rows only, while preserving the canonical shared non-P2P P2P/federation/transport fence. Launch five headless Codex members through inference-gateway account:auto with warm carry. Members self-pull one feature at a time through the fleet claim spec and must verify implementation in the project test suite before structured terminal completion. The leader owns lane preview before launch, liveness/replacement, blocker resolution, gate ownership compliance, and a positive-control-backed zero-state census before declaring the drain complete.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts buildFleetKindClaimSpec composes view.fence='p2p-lane' whenever the fleet slug contains 'nonp2p', and applies the fleet claim spec before member terminals open. plans:items read at 2026-09-30 reports P-005 todo and unclaimed. fleet:status reports the prior D-015 fleet is winding-down with a non-live leader, so this run uses a fresh fleet rather than mutating that historical lane.\nRelated: P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"nonp2p-owner-blocker-audit-2026-09-05","title":"Audit and clear non-P2P owner/capability residue","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-05","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Audit and clear non-P2P owner/capability residue\nslug: nonp2p-owner-blocker-audit-2026-09-05\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n\n# Audit and clear non-P2P owner/capability residue\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2146360 — Freeze the live target set from D-096 post 94965: audit every needs-human-owner and needs-human-capability row against current lifecycle, typed blocker/capability policy, checkpoint, evidence, and ac… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146361 — For every audited row whose alleged owner/capability wall is satisfiable by this superuser session under AUTO, remove the stale blocker or perform the missing in-scope action, then verify and close/r… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2146362 — Re-run the exact cohort classifier, publish an exact one-by-one list for every surviving genuine external blocker with its current reason, required action, and next responsible party, and close the p… <!-- P-003 -->\n## Background\n\nAvi asked for a live audit of every D-096 bug represented as blocked on the owner, immediate self-unblocking wherever possible, and an exact one-by-one list of any genuine external residue. This is deliberately separate from the frozen rev3 acceptance snapshot.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Every owner/capability wall is revalidated.** Every row in the D-096 `needs-human-owner` and `needs-human-capability` categories is joined to its current lifecycle state and read through the existing typed capability policy plus its actual evidence; a historical label alone never counts as a live wall.\n\n**R-2 — Every satisfiable wall is removed with proof.** For each row whose required action is within this superuser session's authority and available capabilities, perform the action or remove the stale gate, verify the result, and record a per-row evidence-backed terminal or corrected disposition; no bulk clear is allowed.\n\n**R-3 — Every genuine survivor is actionable one by one.** Publish the exact remaining ids, current blocker, evidence, required next action, and responsible external party, together with before/after counts and a fresh classifier run.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Plan items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002 | live |\n| R-3 | P-003 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Audit, clear, and report\n\n- **P-001** `done` Freeze the live target set from D-096 post 94965: audit every needs-human-owner and needs-human-capability row against current lifecycle, typed blocker/capability policy, checkpoint, evidence, and actual external dependency; deduplicate rows that have already become terminal. importance: high — note: ← WI-2146360 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` For every audited row whose alleged owner/capability wall is satisfiable by this superuser session under AUTO, remove the stale blocker or perform the missing in-scope action, then verify and close/reclassify the item with per-row evidence; never bulk-clear, touch WI-212675 LIVE_GATE_OPS, revise the rev3 rubric, mutate rev5, restaff, or touch D-058/D-059 receipts. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2146361 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Re-run the exact cohort classifier, publish an exact one-by-one list for every surviving genuine external blocker with its current reason, required action, and next responsible party, and close the post-snapshot audit with before/after counts and verification evidence. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-2146362 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Post-snapshot cleanup is separate from the frozen acceptance record\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured 2026-09-05: nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08 is awaiting independent acceptance against rubric revision 3; D-096 and WI-2140570 post 94965 freeze a 2026-09-05T15:06:30.482Z residue snapshot. This owner-directed audit is a NEW post-snapshot effort: lifecycle progress after that timestamp is expected and must not revise rubric rev3, rewrite D-096, or add items to the already completion-audited plan. Scope is exactly the manifest's 70 needs-human-owner plus 7 needs-human-capability rows, reconciled against current state. Reuse the existing typed owner-capability policy (`requiresOwnerCapability`) and live work-item evidence; a label alone is not an owner wall. Self-clear every satisfiable row with per-item evidence. Preserve real external capability walls and report them one by one. Protected exclusions remain: no WI-212675 LIVE_GATE_OPS, no D-058/D-059 receipt mutation, no claim-spec rev5 change, no restaffing, and no bulk lifecycle rewrite.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-002 — AUTO resolves five product-direction gates; two remain protected\nDate: 2026-09-05\nMeasured against the seven live product-decision blocker records in the D-096 owner/capability target set. Under the current owner-directed AUTO grant, the following decisions are made now. (1) EI-44: the owner inbox defaults to live owner decisions/capability gates across all plans, including shipped plans; those cards sort ahead of general attention work. (2) WI-39302: adopt the already-working SPICE endpoint 127.0.0.1:5930 as the supported Mac VM remote-view path and close the QXL Apple Screen Sharing path as won't-fix; a future virtual-display experiment may reopen separately. (3) WI-41690: ratify direct implementation of the predecessor measurement-integrity plan now; keep the follow-on deferred until the predecessor publishes its five required output values. (4) WI-5457: failed or timed-out completeSpawn exits automatically enter superviseCrash, clean cancellation never does, and existing restart strategy plus intensity limits bound retries. (5) WI-3049: fail closed on non-canonical epoch-wrap authors at read/write; do not destructively clean or re-grant historical keys without verified peer-VM identity. These five product-decision refs are clearable. Two are not: WI-5784 remains behind the explicit Scout pause through its 2026-09-08 review edge, and WI-636615's 61-file dirty tree stays untouched under the anti-footgun rail until Avi chooses keep/commit/discard at file granularity.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"operator-chat-sidebar-revival-2026-07-13-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: the revived OperatorChatSidebar is the primary chat surface with current Pot Health, cards, voice, and a dark native dock","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-b44f1d59-e309-44f6-aa98-4cd7ebc1c866","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: the revived OperatorChatSidebar is the primary chat surface with current Pot Health, cards, voice, and a dark native dock\nslug: operator-chat-sidebar-revival-2026-07-13-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\nowner: su-b44f1d59-e309-44f6-aa98-4cd7ebc1c866\n---\n\n# Acceptance: the revived OperatorChatSidebar is the primary chat surface with current Pot Health, cards, voice, and a dark native dock\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nPost-implementation definition-of-done for operator-chat-sidebar-revival-2026-07-13 against the current as-built tree. Revision 3 folds in D-008 and the later shipped Pot Health design authority retire-mug-kettle-su-only-2026-08-09#D-032. Every stable Vitest-checkable outcome is bound to a detector; the conditionally live ask-choice integration run and the Rust dock check remain explicit manual evidence rather than unsound structured bindings.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05","title":"Portal (:3081) — continuous design iteration across every rail tab","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-05","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Portal (:3081) — continuous design iteration across every rail tab\nslug: portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-08\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation, deploy and evidence are COMPLETE and verified (release YxRyV_UAA…-098fe40a live, sourceRootDigest 8d35ca25cc6f independently recomputed). CORRECTED 2026-09-08T00:19Z per D-017: the prior text of this block was WRONG about what blocks ship. (1) INDEPENDENT RE-GRADE — DONE. WI-10000577 closed 21:06Z by su-000a4d8f; card EI-22638284550937659 rates R-1/R-2/R-3 all healthy against rubric revision 5. Vetting attestation EI-22577324999589644 is current and the author acceptance verdict EI-22642447291323971 (accept) is already recorded. (2) THE ACTUAL WALL is bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing on R-1, R-2 and R-3: rubrics:get via :3170 shows requiredTestLayers null on all three, and acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts:243 raises it at phase 'ship' for every role:'outcome' BAR with empty layers. D-017 rules that a requiredTestLayers amendment is MANDATORY and authorized, narrowed strictly to declaring those layers — no prose re-authoring, no re-propose, no re-seed. Declare all three in ONE `criteria` transaction: requiredTestLayers is a BAR-meaning field, so per-criterion patches would walk the revision 6/7/8 and each bump voids the card pinned to the one before. (3) THE REVISION PIN is real but SECONDARY and self-inflicted: recording D-017 through the agent MCP route (:9071 -> :3070, build e66be3c4ff) bumped the plan without running synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision, which per D-016 exists only on :3170. Every plan write for this plan MUST go through :3170 (scripts/mcp-call.mjs --port 3170) until that synchronizer deploys; a :3070 write re-opens this gap each time. (4) READ EVERY GATE VERDICT THROUGH :3170. :3070 reports the misleading bar_snapshot_proof_uncertain for this identical state; all three acceptance-gate files blob-differ between the builds.\n\n**Next:** su-872eeb6b has TAKEN THE SEAT (confirmed 00:17Z). Seat-bound sequence, in order: rubrics:amend { dryRun:true } via :3170 -> capture the server approval JSON to a FILE (never retyped; EI-22562050692029127 is this rubric failing that exact step on a 62-char nextBarHash where 64 is required) -> outside-lineage reviewer posts those exact bytes via work_items:comment -> apply with approvalRef -> re-vet -> independent re-grade against revision 6 (su-000a4d8f notified their rev-5 card will be voided) -> author acceptance verdict -> plans:set-plan-status shipped. Make EVERY intended revision BEFORE requesting the re-grade. su-336850c4 (WI-10000646) drives the non-seat-bound half and holds no plan items.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Every scoped Portal surface receives a complete visual design pass.** Audit the rail and top bar, native surfaces, side panes, embedded operator seam, and cross-cutting responsive/accessibility behavior represented by P-001 through P-010. Exercise light and dark themes at 1440×900 and 1280×800 when the live surface supports those viewports; rank findings and track each adopted defect through its implementing plan item.\n\n**R-2 — Adopted changes remain truthful, contained, responsive, and state-safe.** At the target viewports, content must not clip or overflow its host surface; enabled, disabled, loading, empty, transient, and status treatments must describe the real actionable state in both themes. Acceptance must avoid destructive or outward actions and restore the pre-pass theme, current app, pane, call, dialog, and verdict state.\n\n**R-3 — Every adopted change has current-source and live-release evidence.** Verify each change with Portal typecheck, affected project tests, a successful guarded build/handoff of the rebuilt release, and inspected before/after or equivalent live screenshots recorded under `.papercusp/reports/portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05/`.\n\n## Design\n\nThe existing phase items are the implementation units; acceptance BARs project onto them rather than introducing a second work breakdown.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010 | live |\n| R-3 | P-011 | deployed |\n\n## Background\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-05] Directive verbatim: \"put yourself on auto mode and continuously iterate on all the tabs in our http://127.0.0.1:3081/ app and make design improvements\". No scope limits, no tab priority, no visual direction given — design judgment is the agent's, disclosed per change.\n\nMechanics (verified 2026-09-05): source edits land in the portal checkout; `npm run build` (scripts/build-standalone.mjs, takes the `git-sync:portal` lock) publishes a new release under `.portal-runtime/portal/releases/` and repoints `current`; the running server resolves `current` ONCE at start, so a release goes live only after `apps/operator/scripts/systemd/deploy-cloud-portal.sh --handoff` (papercusp repo) / a unit restart. Tokens: `app/tokens.css` is GENERATED from the DTCG source (`tokens.base.json` via `generate-tokens.mjs`) — never hand-edit. Shell: `packages/ui/src/shell.tsx` (2.8k lines) + `app/globals.css` (2.4k lines, heavily annotated — read the comment above a rule before changing it). Other agents commit to this tree daily — file locks arbitrate.\n\n## Phase 1 — audit\n\n- **P-001** `done` Baseline visual audit: screenshot every rail tab (light + dark; 1440×900 and 1280×800) via verdict against :3081, record a ranked findings list as plan decisions/Now, and file each concrete defect as a work-item under this plan. importance: high — note: ← WI-2146962 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — shell + native surfaces (iterate; one finding per loop wake)\n\n- **P-002** `done` Rail + top bar: overflow affordance for the 36-item rail (visible scroll cue / grouping), dim/disabled-state semantics, label wrapping, density of the collapsed side-pane strips, status chips, theme control. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000116 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Home (Mission Control): promo banner weight, metric-card empty states, notification list rhythm, empty-space use, responsive grid. — note: ← WI-2147062 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Mail surface design pass. — note: su-49c21c66 2026-09-06T00:21Z: LIVE on release jOs-sQ47JI9_CeUeKQxgy-20260906001850099 (:3081, handoff 00:19:23Z) — verdict js at 1440×900: 200 .thread-card, 0 overflowing, 0 clipped, .thread-list scrollWidth==clientWidth (389/389), 0 undecoded-entity snippets (was 583/389 + 62 overflowing). Fixes: email packages/ui/src/styles.css .thread-line/.thread-meta align-self:stretch+min-width:0, .thread-card align-items:stretch (host button{align-items:center} override), .thread-list overflow:hidden auto; guard email/tests/thread-rows-fill-the-card.test.ts 4/4; screenshots /tmp/design-after-mail-{light,dark}.png\n- **P-005** `done` Calendar surface design pass. — note: ← WI-2147155 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Phone surface design pass. — note: ← WI-2147610 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Workspaces surface design pass. — note: ← WI-10000284 done\n- **P-008** `done` Side panes (Accounts dock, Papercup chat, launched sessions, notification center, app launcher ⌘K, agent roster, process popover) design pass. — note: WI-10000302 completion is fully recorded but its terminal state is temporarily blocked by EI-22550369431560084 (live-UI artifact resolver checks deployed release rather than canonical staging). P-008 itself is complete and live-accepted on immutable Portal release PnRju1EfKfM0bo192lRnM; durable evidence is .papercusp/reports/portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05/side-panes-pass-2026-09-06.md.\n\n## Phase 3 — embedded operator tabs\n\n- **P-009** `done` Embedded-pane seam for the framed operator tabs (Desktops, Plans, Inbox, Overview, HUD, Work, Learning, Workflow Editor, Brainstorm, Health, PRs, Insights, Conversations, ADV Settings, Docs, History, Git, Stats, Tests, Create, Scheduled, Frames, Evaluation, Coordination, Cloud, Cupboard, DEV, Support, Settings): loading/unconfigured states, theme handoff, frame chrome, pot bar; defects INSIDE the framed operator page are filed against the operator (apps/operator-vite) and fixed there when portal-visible. — note: HUD conversation popup controls are complete and live (WI-2147225, D-005). The broader embedded-tab audit and separate Decisions query defect WI-2147274 remain; this item is not fully complete.\n\n## Phase 4 — cross-cutting\n\n- **P-010** `done` Responsive (≤1280 wide, ≤768 tall) + accessibility pass across the shell: focus rings, contrast against tokens, keyboard reach of the hidden rail items, reduced-motion. — note: ← WI-10000317 done\n- **P-011** `done` Verification harness: every change verified by `npm run typecheck` + affected vitest + a verdict screenshot of the rebuilt release; keep a before/after screenshot pair per change under `.papercusp/reports/portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05/`. — note: ← WI-10000327 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Composed surfaces size themselves against the HOST box (container queries), never the viewport\nDate: 2026-09-05\nEvery module surface the portal composes (Mail, Calendar, Phone, Workspaces) renders inside `.surface`, which is already `container: portal-surface / inline-size`. Inside the portal the viewport and the surface diverge by 176px with both docks collapsed and by ~770px with both expanded, so a package's `@media (max-width: …)` breakpoint asks about a box the surface does not live in and answers wrong in the direction that clips.\n\nMeasured 2026-09-05 on :3081 at 1440×900: `.calendar-shell` 1264px wide, `.workspace` 704px holding a `header.toolbar` of scrollWidth 996 and a `.month-grid` with `min-width: 740px` — the calendar package's `@media (max-width: 1380px)` compact layout never engaged because the VIEWPORT was 1440. Result: view switcher clipped to one letter, Saturday column half-hidden behind an unsignposted horizontal scroll.\n\nRuling: (1) a composed surface expresses width breakpoints as unnamed `@container (max-width: …)` queries so the nearest inline-size container — the portal's `.surface`, or the app's own document — decides; (2) the standalone app makes its document a container (`html { container-type: inline-size }` in calendar `app/globals.css`); (3) base styles must survive the narrowest realistic host box without a breakpoint (toolbar `flex-wrap: wrap`, grids sized by `minmax(<floor>, 1fr)` with `min-width: 0`, not a hard px minimum). Guarded by calendar `tests/responsive-rules-follow-the-host-box.test.ts`. The email package's 960/720/480 viewport breakpoints have the same defect and are the next candidate (P-004 second pass).\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-010\n\n### D-002 — Rail overflow (P-002) is deferred to a peer's in-flight 'More sections' change; re-audit after it lands\nDate: 2026-09-05\nThe #1 audit finding — `.rail-apps` 399px tall vs 1590px of content at 1440×900, 23 of 30 app tabs scrolled out of view behind a 22px scroll-fade — was found already being addressed by an uncommitted peer change in the portal tree at 2026-09-05T22:44Z local 18:44 (new `packages/ui/src/more-sections.tsx` + `shell.tsx` / `shell-model.ts` diffs: the operator's `ADV_MORE_GROUPS` rendered as a searchable cmdk popover behind one rail item, `panel=more`). No live lock holder at 22:50Z (`locks:queue` empty). This plan does NOT contest it. Sub-findings the popover does not by itself address, to verify on re-audit: the bottom fade greys whichever row sits under it (the Inbox row read as disabled — it is not); a scrolled rail clips its top row with no top cue; 'Papercup Chat' is the only two-line label; at 1280×800 the compressed rail crams badges over icons.\nRelated: P-002\n\n### D-003 — Promos are dismissible per account via one <html data-dismissed> attribute; the desktop-CTA bar itself stays ON by default and off Home\nDate: 2026-09-06\nThe Mail/Calendar/framed-tab desktop-CTA bar (owner ask WI-1254479) and Mission Control's TUI callout each get a × that hides them PER ACCOUNT (P-003). Mechanism, chosen for no first-paint flash and no hydration diff: `UserPreferencesSchema.dismissed` (OPTIONAL — absent IS 'nothing hidden', keeps the authority-handoff payload hash stable), mirrored to localStorage `portal-dismissed`; app/layout.tsx runs PORTAL_DISMISSED_BOOTSTRAP (single-sourced in @portal/contracts) to stamp `<html data-dismissed=\"id id\">` before paint; the shell re-stamps from /api/preferences on load and on each × (packages/ui/src/dismissals.ts); packages/ui/src/promo-dismissals.css hides from the attribute alone. React never owns the attribute. RULING for later lanes: the desktop download is NOT duplicated onto the Home card — tests/shell-ui.test.tsx pins the owner ask that the CTA appears on exactly Mail/Calendar/framed tabs, and a Home-card button broke it; the only Home appearance is the quiet `.tui-callout-compact` footer row, and only after the card is dismissed. Measured: verdict on :3081 release GF4m…234503 at 2026-09-05T23:54Z — click × → .tui-callout display none, .tui-callout-compact flex, html.dataset.dismissed='desktop-cta tui-callout', reload keeps it hidden, GET /api/preferences.dismissed = both ids; restored to [] afterwards.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-004 — Mail thread rows: a line inside the centred column-flex card must be stretched before its children can truncate\nDate: 2026-09-06\nemail/packages/ui/src/styles.css: `.email-shell .thread-card` is `display:flex; flex-direction:column` with `align-items:center`, so every child line is a centred fit-content box — `min-width:0` + ellipsis on the <strong> inside `.thread-line` had nothing to shrink against. Fix (P-004 follow-up): `.email-shell .thread-line, .email-shell .thread-meta { align-self:stretch; min-width:0 }`. Any future line added to the card needs the same. Measured: verdict on :3081 release GF4m…234503 at 2026-09-05T23:56Z — .thread-line scrollWidth 477 in a 373px .thread-card (align-items:center, flex-direction:column), <strong> width 414 with min-width:0/flex:1 1 auto/nowrap/overflow:hidden already applied; 120 of 200 cards overflowing, .thread-list 583/389.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-005 — HUD conversation popup controls belong to the panel they toggle\nDate: 2026-09-06\nOwner continuation request (2026-09-06, session 6278c564-a66c-471f-8b69-e32297a1aafc turn 6, repeated in this session) makes the HUD conversation popup the next design priority. Implement as WI-2147225: expanded Orders, Activity, Fleet each show one consistent collapse control in their header; collapsed panels leave a labeled edge strip in their original position. Use the existing PanelToggleButton and panel content, preserving URL state, deferred panel data mounting, overlay behavior, and window/display maximize. Keep the conversation header for identity/status and window actions. Verify light/dark and narrow/wide interaction and geometry in the current build. This supersedes earlier placement of Orders on the conversation left toolbar. Remaining portal findings stay under the existing plan.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-006 — Desktop readiness requires observed and desired serving state\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDecision: an observed host state of running/degraded is provider state, not by itself proof that the host can serve a desktop. Desktop-launch affordances must reuse the existing running/degraded vocabulary for both axes: the observed state must be serving and, when a desired state is supplied, the desired state must also be serving. A missing desired state preserves compatibility with the older projection. When these axes disagree, the disabled explanation names the reconciliation transition rather than advertising a usable desktop. This governs P-007 and future workspace-to-desktop entry points.\n\nMeasured: on live :3081, p018-canary-20260905-r7 showed observed=running, desired=provisioning, terminal repair=succeeded, and CANNOT SERVE while Open desktop remained enabled. After the change, the same unmocked card was disabled with title “The desktop is unavailable while this workspace is reconciling (running → provisioning).” Final source readback confirmed hostCanOpenDesktop checks both axes and the CTA consumes its single desktopReady result; focused Vitest was 47/47 and Portal typecheck had 0 errors.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-007 — Host controls own geometry, focus, and motion against mounted primitive cascades\nDate: 2026-09-06\nMeasured: on the rebuilt :3081 document, apps/operator/app/_primitives.css loaded after Portal CSS and its zero-specificity `:where(button, .pc-btn)` baseline contributed min-height 26px plus 4px 10px padding to `.rail-unpin`. The nominal 20px control computed as 22x26px; at 1280x768 and 1440x900 the primary rail button's center hit-tested to Unpin, and the same later baseline restored 120ms transitions under reduced motion. After host-local min-size/padding, focus-outline, and reduced-motion declarations, the production-cascade browser suite passed 5/5 at 1280x768 and 390x768. Decision: when mounted native surfaces bring shared zero-specificity primitives into the Portal document, an exact-size host-owned icon control must explicitly own its min-size/padding, visible focus indicator, and reduced-motion override. Its browser regression must load the real later cascade and use real pointer/keyboard hit testing; do not clone or rescope the shared primitive sheet to solve a local control contract.\nRelated: P-010, P-011\n\n### D-008 — P-010 guards must measure the composed host cascade and shared chat seam\nDate: 2026-09-06\nMeasured in the current Portal source and rebuilt live release n1RY3Pvr1DwJA5nl_lJvU-20260906225252809-1256025-41f9cfc4: mounted Operator primitives load after Portal CSS, so host-owned controls must explicitly own geometry, focus, motion, and state colors; the Portal's PapercupChat renderer now uses shared pc-chat classes and custom-property mapping, so retired ask-turn/formatAskText selectors are not valid contrast evidence. Keep the production-cascade Playwright guard and the three-theme shared-chat token guard as the recurrence checks. Evidence: .papercusp/reports/portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05/responsive-accessibility-pass-2026-09-06.md; focused Vitest 241/241; Playwright 5/5.\nRelated: P-010, P-011\n\n### D-009 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-07\nAmendment-Id: 58a7a7935d8ea15db0d9c81e451911d7ccdde12e593654d31aa1714c1255d715\nRequest-Hash: e9f7115e7b4a49c331761e639ca805c57c8d7bef3bf48a9527d82c95cbd53c87\nActor: su-49e81510-13a1-45b8-a584-6f9edbaf182d\nReason: Replace legacy seeded BAR prose with the final as-built outcomes, methods, replication drills, scopes, and runnable host/release checks before independent grading.\nApproved-By: su-96533dc7-ef1c-4059-8d85-2f54290c3572\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:199591\nApproved-At: 2026-09-07T01:50:04.012Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 46 → 47\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-07\nAmendment-Id: portal-v5-critique-199637-20260907\nRequest-Hash: 1386dcecfe15a22a9dbde6078ae5bd229c6dfca7a3ab9c2a5ad662904e2ca514\nActor: su-49e81510-13a1-45b8-a584-6f9edbaf182d\nReason: Apply independent critique WI-2146962#199637: separate coverage, visual/state quality and provenance; replace the arbitrary image count with an exact matrix; remove wrong-subject checks and make manual proof partitions explicit.\nApproved-By: su-96533dc7-ef1c-4059-8d85-2f54290c3572\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:199649\nApproved-At: 2026-09-07T02:43:25.239Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 47 → 48\nChanged BARs: R-1\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-011 — Phone's disabled-state witness is unobtainable under rubric rev 5's own procedure — it needs an author disposition, not another capture attempt\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-07\nActor: su-872eeb6b-06e7-4f37-84a6-b3955700a650 (driver, WI-2146962)\n\nFINDING (factual reading of the live rubric, not a verdict).\n\nR-2 requires that \"enabled/disabled/loading/empty/transient/status treatments describe the real actionable state\", and its evidencePlane is `live`. But R-2's own replication drill states verbatim: \"Missing, unexercised or wrong-target cases remain unknown; do not send/call/launch/resolve as part of acceptance.\"\n\nPortal's Phone surface only disables controls during call connection/ending, pending incoming/screening writes, or saving an invite. Every one of those is a send/call/launch/resolve. So the single action class that would produce the disabled state is the action class the rubric forbids. The witness is not merely un-captured — it is UNREACHABLE by any procedure the rubric permits.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR OTHER LANES: do not treat this as an implementer omission, and do not attempt to close it with another capture run. `phone-disabled.png` shows an ENABLED form and is explicitly insufficient; re-shooting it changes nothing. Manufacturing the state with a browser fixture does not close it either, because R-2's method says fixtures \"prove only their named clauses; fixtures are not live evidence\".\n\nRESOLUTION IS THE RUBRIC AUTHOR'S (su-ca863adf-6074-40a3-84c3-ed9c4606da11), and is one of exactly three:\n  (a) accept the absence with a recorded reason, scoping Phone's disabled state out of R-2;\n  (b) amend R-2 to admit a clearly-labelled browser fixture for this one clause (an amendment needs independent approval, per the D-009/D-010 protocol);\n  (c) rate R-2 degraded on this basis and ship or reject on that.\n\nThe driver is NOT choosing among these and has not substituted for the author. Recorded so the question stops being rediscovered as a capture task.\n\n### D-012 — Rebuilding for R-3 changes DEPENDENCIES, not just source — so the existing bounded-source-comparison argument does not by itself justify reusing the gallery across the new release\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-07\nActor: su-872eeb6b-06e7-4f37-84a6-b3955700a650 (driver, WI-2146962)\n\nWHAT THE DRIFT ACTUALLY IS. Exactly four tracked files postdate the running release Jk8vf6ox...051125119. NONE is an adopted UI/design change for P-001..P-011: two are dependency pins, two are build tooling and its own test.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-07T13:57Z, in the portal checkout (a symlink to .papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/portal), HEAD 6090a4d, git status --porcelain = 0 lines. Enumerated with `git ls-files` + `stat -c %Y` against build epoch 1788757885 (2026-09-07T05:11:25Z) -> exactly 4 files: package.json 05:20:43Z, package-lock.json 05:29:31Z, tests/build-standalone.test.ts 10:30:47Z, scripts/build-standalone.mjs 10:33:50Z. POSITIVE CONTROL (files in the 10 min BEFORE the cutoff) returned packages/ui/src/shell-model.ts and shell.tsx and tests/preference-refresh.test.ts at 05:07:06-07Z plus tsconfig.json at 05:11:25Z, proving the scan was live rather than trivially empty.\nMeasured: `git show 0719d39 -- package.json` = +9/-0 adding overrides { lodash-es 4.18.1, @excalidraw/excalidraw>nanoid 3.3.18, @excalidraw/mermaid-to-excalidraw>nanoid 5.1.16 }. `git show 6090a4d --stat` = scripts/build-standalone.mjs +159/-45 and tests/build-standalone.test.ts +25/-? only.\nMeasured: the added functions in build-standalone.mjs are hasValidGitEntry, findCoordinationDomain, pathWithin, sourceManifestLockGroups — git-sync leasing and source-manifest locking. `grep -rl sourceRootDigest` in the portal tree resolves to scripts/release-source-digest.mjs, scripts/copy-standalone.mjs, scripts/standalone-runtime.mjs (+ its .d.mts and test) — none touched by 6090a4d, so release-identity semantics are unaffected by the builder change.\n\nROOT CAUSE of the manifest half: the overrides were declared at 05:20Z but NEVER INSTALLED.\nMeasured: at 14:00Z node_modules was dated 2026-09-04T15:25:18Z and `require('lodash-es/package.json').version` returned 4.17.21. After `npm ci --prefix <portal>` at 14:01:35Z (exit 0, \"added 758 packages\"): lodash-es 4.18.1, nanoid 3.3.18. So the recorded limit \"does not establish that the new dependency manifests were built\" was literally true — they were not present on disk at all.\n\nTHE TENSION THIS DECISION SETTLES. Verification-contract step 4 says \"A fresh build is needed only if the promised source is not represented by the inspected artifact\", which alone argues NO rebuild is required: the promised UI source IS represented.\nMeasured: sha256 of packages/ui/src/shell.tsx = c3868dc7..., shell-model.ts = 8d43b027..., tests/preference-refresh.test.ts = a5dd21ae... — byte-identical to the three .sources[].sha256 recorded in preference-race-provenance.json, and their mtimes 05:07:06-07Z precede the 05:11:25Z build.\nBut R-3's own driftMarker says \"The release sourceRootDigest does not match committed Portal source\", which is currently TRUE (provenance.json itself records rootDigestMatches:false). Method and bar disagree.\n\nRULING. Resolve it by rebuilding, because that removes the ambiguity instead of arguing the mismatch is benign. BUT the rebuild carries a cost that must not be papered over:\n\nTHE EVIDENCE-REUSE HAZARD. The precedent used for the previous correction release was a BOUNDED SOURCE COMPARISON — \"only shell.tsx differs, therefore unaffected gallery observations may be reused.\" That inference holds only while DEPENDENCIES are constant. This rebuild changes them (lodash-es 4.17.21 -> 4.18.1; nanoid 3.3.3 -> 5.1.16/3.3.18 under excalidraw). Source equality therefore NO LONGER implies artifact equality, and the 188 preserved gallery slots cannot be carried across this release on the source-comparison argument alone.\n\nCONSEQUENTLY, for the post-rebuild release the grader must require BOTH:\n  (i) the affected-source comparison as before, AND\n  (ii) positive re-verification that rendering did not change under the new dependency versions — at minimum the 16 current interaction cases plus a bounded visual spot-check on surfaces that actually consume the bumped packages.\nAn (i)-only claim is insufficient for this release and must not be accepted as equivalent to the earlier one.\n\nIf that re-verification proves too costly, the honest alternative is to NOT rebuild and instead have the author rule explicitly that the four non-adopted files are out of R-3's scope — but that ruling is the author's, and it must be recorded rather than assumed.\n\n### D-013 — D-011 is WRONG and is superseded: R-2's disabled-state proof is reachable, so the rubric must NOT be amended\nDate: 2026-09-07\nSUPERSEDES D-011. Recorded by su-872eeb6b, acceptance-author successor (audited coord:rebind-identity from the warm-dead su-ca863adf, 2026-09-07T14:35Z).\n\nD-011 CLAIMED R-2's disabled-state witness is UNREACHABLE: \"R-2 wants a live truthful disabled state; R-2's drill forbids send/call/launch/resolve, and only those produce it.\"\n\nIT IS WRONG. R-2 demands source-reading plus a visible explanation, NOT a call-induced state. \"no desktop launch or call\" is a CONSTRAINT ON THE METHOD, not proof the state is unobtainable — the drill excludes launching/calling BECAUSE the proof is source-plus-explanation. D-011 read the method as a contradiction.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-07T14:43Z — acceptance-matrix-2026-09-07.json stateCases[1] verbatim:\n  {\"state\":\"disabled\",\"surface\":\"workspaces-and-phone\",\"proof\":\"read source decision and visible unavailable explanation; no desktop launch or call\"}\nMeasured: 2026-09-07T14:49Z — same file, stateCases[5], corroborating the source-reading method:\n  {\"state\":\"status\",\"surface\":\"workspaces-home-phone\",\"proof\":\"compare displayed claim to its source fields and read disabled/reconciling/unavailable explanations\"}\n  (\"workspaces-and-phone\" is a surface GROUP; the matrix defines 7 stateCases and no registry keyed by that string.)\n\nCONSEQUENCE 1 — DO NOT AMEND THE RUBRIC. The dead author spent ~13h (its carry-note) on a rubrics:amend needing an outside-lineage approver who never posted. An amendment also invalidates BOTH the meta-attestation AND every independent grading, forcing re-vet + re-grade. The case is satisfiable as written. Keep revision 5.\n\nCONSEQUENCE 2 — ACCEPT-WITH-REASON WAS NEVER AVAILABLE.\nMeasured: 2026-09-07T14:42Z — packages/operator-core/lib/plan-acceptance-gate.ts, refusal `acceptance_bar_not_met` (lines 1195-1225) verbatim: \"Every mandatory outcome needs a current pass-equivalent rating; a disclosure criterion or the rubric author's acceptance verdict cannot substitute for the outcome.\"\nMeasured: 2026-09-07T14:41Z — rubrics:get rev 5: r-1/r-2/r-3 each mandatory:true, passRatings:[\"healthy\"].\nMeasured: 2026-09-07T14:43Z — same gate file lines ~839/~887: rubric-family checks are \"NOT waivable by `force` (D-005)\".\n=> A degraded r-2 blocks ship regardless of the author's verdict, and force cannot clear it.\n\n=> ONLY ROUTE: make r-2 HONESTLY HEALTHY by supplying the evidence the matrix asks for.\n\nTHE ACTUAL GAP.
