Create invite\", i.e. the ENABLED scheduled view. The disabled case was NEVER CAPTURED — not captured-and-found-unreachable. Grader card EI-22577547772880485 names exactly this, plus a second gap: the Process capture froze the loading overlay instead of a post-refresh panel. The WORKSPACES half is already proven there (\"disabled Workspace actions with state-specific explanations\").\n\nSOURCE DECISION TO CITE (satisfies half 1 of stateCases[1]; no call, no launch).\nMeasured: 2026-09-07T14:50Z — packages/ui/src/voice-session.tsx (real path /home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/portal):\n  - `portalVoiceCapture(state)` (~lines 122-131) IS the disabled decision: returns `{can:false, reason}` with state-specific reasons — \"Voice is unavailable\", \"The microphone is unavailable\", \"Voice is reconnecting\", \"Voice is disconnected\", \"Voice is not connected yet\" — and `{can:true}` only when phase===\"live\".\n  - `portalVoiceStatus(state)` (~lines 99-111) IS the visible explanation: \"Voice service unavailable — retry, or type instead\"; \"Microphone unavailable — allow access, or type instead\".\n  - Its docstring records this was fixed FOR truthfulness (\"'Voice unavailable' was dead copy kept green by a hand-built fixture\"; a control that cannot act \"says so instead of accepting the press and discarding it\") — the R-2 property itself.\n\nWORK IMPLIED: (i) cite portalVoiceCapture/portalVoiceStatus as the source decision; (ii) capture the VISIBLE unavailable explanation for the workspaces-and-phone group; (iii) re-capture Process settled post-refresh, not mid-overlay.\n\nD-011's PROHIBITION, HALF LIFTED: \"do not re-shoot phone-disabled.png\" is LIFTED — re-shooting is REQUIRED for (ii). The rest STANDS: no real call, no desktop launch (stateCases[6] also forbids call/send/decision/verdict mutation).\n\nMETHOD CAUTION: /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/portal is a SYMLINK; `find`/`grep -r` do NOT descend it without -L and return a silent FALSE ABSENCE that reads like \"this code does not exist\". It caused two wrong conclusions here before a positive control caught it. Search the resolved real path, always with a positive control.\n\n### D-014 — Portal guarded build fingerprints linked out-of-root deps but no longer locks them\nDate: 2026-09-07\nCONTEXT. r-3 requires the published sourceRootDigest to be tied to current COMMITTED Portal source, which requires a guarded build to actually COMPLETE. Six attempts were made 2026-09-07; runs 1-5 all failed the same way, never exceeding ~2.8k of 16.6k manifest paths before their unrenewable lock TTL expired.\n\nMEASURED CAUSE. The build exclusively locked its whole fingerprint manifest, of which 98.3% are linked out-of-root dependencies reached through node_modules symlinks into the shared papercusp monorepo. At the hardcoded chunk size of 50 that is 333 sequential lock acquisitions against a repo ~86 agents edit continuously.\n\nDECISION. Linked out-of-root dependencies are FINGERPRINTED but NOT LOCKED. sourceManifestLockGroups routes them to the existing `unclaimable` path (fingerprinted for drift detection, not locked). Locked set 16,640 -> 285 (6 chunks); manifest unchanged.\n\nWHY THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN r-3. (1) The fingerprint scope is UNCHANGED, so drift in a linked dependency is still DETECTED. (2) assertSourceFingerprintUnchanged already treated a linked-dep move as NON-FATAL (only `rootMoved` throws). Because that drift was already tolerated, holding those locks could never change a build verdict; they were pure cost. r-3's bar is committed PORTAL source, which is exactly the in-root set still locked.\n\nSUPERSEDES the prior in-code rationale that a linked package 'must be claimed with a path relative to its own coordination domain rather than dropped from the proof window'. The traversal-path crash guard that rationale also protected is RETAINED and still tested.\n\nMeasured (all at the real build root /home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/portal, 2026-09-07 17:05-17:17Z):\n- Measured: node -e fingerprintReleaseSource(<real root>) -> TOTAL_MANIFEST 16640, linked-dep 16356 (98.3%), chunks_at_50 = 333 (pre-fix lock set).\n- Measured: same probe post-fix -> manifest 16642 unchanged, linked (NOT locked) 16357, in-root (LOCKED) 285 => 6 chunks; positive control 'in-root has package.json' true; negative control 'in-root has any ../' false.\n- Measured: run6's own build log at 17:16:38Z printed LOCKSET_INROOT_OF_MANIFEST=286/16644 from the committed tree at HEAD c39537f1 — the fix verified in the tree actually being built, not only in a probe.\n- Measured: npx vitest run tests/build-standalone.test.ts tests/source-integrity.test.ts -> VITEST_EXIT=0, 24/24 tests, 2 files passed.\n- Measured: npm run typecheck -> TYPECHECK_RESULT status=clean exit=0 errors=0 files=2433.\n- Measured: tests/source-integrity.test.ts:40 'records linked out-of-root files but keeps them out of rootDigest'; its header comment states 'linked-only drift is tolerated with a warning, in-root drift is refused' — pre-existing corroboration authored by someone else.\n- Measured: scripts/build-standalone.mjs sourceManifestLockGroups now calls isLinkedDependencyPath(filePath) -> unclaimable.push + continue, before any domain resolution.\n- Measured: probing via the papercupai-workspace/portal SYMLINK instead of the real root reports 297 paths / 0 linked operator-core entries, because the dependency symlink's relative 7-level target climbs above /home/ from that path. Re-measure only at the real root.\n\nTracked on EI-22621887684452494.\n\nSTATUS: code + tests green and the fix is confirmed live in the built tree; run6 (task 0mtri4akbtj28da1hrk) is the first build on it. A green BUILD_EXIT=0 is what closes it.\n\n### D-015 — rubric_revision_mismatch here is a STALE SUBJECT-REVISION PIN — repair by pin-sync, never by re-authoring the rubric\nDate: 2026-09-07\nMEASURED 2026-09-07T20:00-20:15Z at primary source. This decision was WRONG TWICE before settling; both corrections are kept visible so no reader inherits a retracted claim.\n\nTHE CAUSE OF THE MISMATCH (VERIFIED). acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts fires bar_snapshot_rubric_revision_mismatch on a three-clause OR. Only the THIRD clause fires here:\n- plan.rubricSlug === rubric.rubricId OK\n- plan.rubricRevision (5) === rubric.revision (5) OK\n- rubric.barContract.subjectPlanRevision (49) !== plan.revision FIRES\nMeasured: harness_plans - subject version 58, rubric version 5, pinned subjectPlanRevision 49, barSetHash b66435fc2b705ea5 on BOTH sides (full-string equality, not a prefix).\n\nWHY THE PIN IS STALE (VERIFIED - settled cause). The BAR-neutral synchronizer is NOT DEPLOYED. Measured: dev:pipeline_position on with-plan-lock.ts (marker synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision) returns committedLocal:true, onStaging:true, inMain:false, deployed:false; the serving build is e66be3c4ff and blockedOn:'gate' (green-checkpoint red, 6 consecutive, phase awaiting-fixer). Agent tool calls execute against :3070, the release checkout, so plan writes ran on a runtime that does not contain the synchronizer. No guard failed - the code was never there.\nThis independently reproduces the root cause already recorded on EI-22582809406076435 (closed 06:39Z today): 'the deployed runtime predates the committed BAR-neutral subject revision synchronizer'. The durable fix and its regression already landed under EI-22458390497775173 and WI-10000058; they are waiting on the gate, not on new code.\n\nRETRACTED CLAIM #1: that any BAR-neutral plan write repairs the pin automatically. FALSIFIED by experiment - two consecutive body-only writes (add-decision 58->59, set-now 59->60, neither setting templateData) left the pin at 49 both times.\nRETRACTED CLAIM #2: that the silent false came from the previousBody-vs-nextBody fingerprint check. Wrong - superseded by the deployment finding above. A scratch probe replaying every reachable guard passed all of them (requirements parse R-1/R-2/R-3, mappings parse, fingerprint f03057538061baf1 non-null, revisions agree, schema parses, barSetHash equal, 3 BAR criteria, rebuild ok), which is consistent with code that simply never executed.\n\nWHAT IS SAFE, AND WHAT IS STILL FORBIDDEN (VERIFIED, unchanged).\nMeasured: plan-acceptance-gate.ts:1020 pins a card with s.rubricRevision === rubric.revision. Cards and the vetting attestation pin to the RUBRIC revision (5), so SUBJECT-plan edits do NOT un-count an independent card. The in-flight re-grade on WI-10000577 may be emitted against revision 5 regardless of plan edits.\nMeasured: the synchronizer's UPDATE sets only template_data + origin, with `version` solely in the WHERE clause, and passes preserveExistingBars:true. A pin advance does not move the rubric revision.\nSTILL FORBIDDEN: re-authoring, re-proposing, amending or re-seeding the rubric. Those bump the rubric revision and destroy BOTH the vetting attestation and any independent card.\n\nHOW THIS GETS REPAIRED. Preferred: let the deploy land - the fix is already on staging, so the pin advances on the next body-only write once the runtime carries the synchronizer. The gate is red and owned (gateOwnership hold-blocked), so gate work belongs to its single owner, not to this lane.\nFallback with precedent: EI-22582809406076435 applied an exact-CAS one-row pin repair (dev:pg_mutate, dryRun then commit) guarded on exact subject/rubric/version/barSetHash, advancing subjectPlanRevision one step at a time and verifying acceptance-snapshot complete=true with zero problems afterwards. Its H1-vs-H2 distinguishing test is satisfied here for H1 (stale bookkeeping): rubric revision and both barSetHash values are byte-identical.\nDo NOT hand-force the pin as a first move, and never with a fabricated previousBody. The source fingerprint is deliberately stricter than barSetHash and also covers Bar-to-work MAP edges, so equal hashes alone do not prove BAR-neutrality; the map plausibly changed as P-001..P-011 completed. The pin blocks nothing until the independent card and the acceptance verdict land.\n\n### D-016 — D-016: the D-015 pin synchronizer runs only on :3170 — the earlier body-only-write falsification was build-confounded\nDate: 2026-09-07\nD-015 concluded the BAR-neutral subject-revision synchronizer was 'not deployed', and recorded that two body-only plan writes FAILED to advance barContract.subjectPlanRevision (stuck at 49). That falsification was measured against the WRONG BUILD and must not be inherited.\n\nMEASURED 2026-09-07T20:55Z, by content not ancestry:\n  git show <ref>:packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/with-plan-lock.ts | grep -c synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision\n  6370b7fa98 (serving :3170) => 2\n  e66be3c4ff (serving :3070 and :9071) => 0\n  staging => 2\n\nAgent MCP calls route :9071 -> :3070, so every prior test of the synchronizer executed a build that does not contain it. The writes were not neutral-and-ineffective; the code never ran. This is the repo's documented :3170-vs-:3070 trap in its third costume today: it does not present as 'my edit is not live', it presents as 'a well-written guard is inexplicably returning false'.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR THE PIN REPAIR: an exact-CAS dev:pg_mutate row repair is NOT required and should not be the first move. Route a plan write through :3170 (scripts/mcp-call.mjs --port 3170) and the shipped synchronizer performs the repair as designed. Reserve the audited DB mitigation (precedent EI-22582809406076435) for the case where :3170 is genuinely unavailable.\n\nSTANDING RULE: before concluding that code behaved subtly wrong, prove the code is RUNNING on the endpoint you are exercising. A health-sha check (curl :3170 :3070 :9071 /api/health) plus a content grep costs two commands and settles it. Note also that a coord broadcast declaring :3170 DOWN was stale by ~20 minutes when re-measured here - verify a liveness claim before you route around it.\n\n### D-017 — The ship wall is bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing, not the revision pin — a requiredTestLayers amendment is mandatory and authorized, and the blanket no-amend rule is narrowed\nDate: 2026-09-08\nDate: 2026-09-07 (recorded by su-336850c4, owner-directed takeover of the dead su-4c6126e7 lane).\n\nTHE SHIP WALL IS NOT WHAT ## Now AND D-015 SAY IT IS. Both describe the blocker as a stale barContract.subjectPlanRevision pin. MEASURED 2026-09-08T00:08-00:11Z, it is not.\n\n1. THE VERDICT YOU READ DEPENDS ON WHICH BUILD ANSWERS. Agent MCP calls route :9071 -> :3070, health sha e66be3c4ff. :3170 serves 7e8e135e6a (== staging on these files). Blob-compared, ALL THREE acceptance-gate files differ between them:\n   acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts   e66be3c4ff e74a066b0f  vs staging 1e68c01e0e\n   acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts e66be3c4ff 2242848917  vs staging c7f3e23905\n   plan-acceptance-gate.ts               e66be3c4ff b28021e642  vs staging 5224e76632\n   :3070 refuses with the vague `bar_snapshot_proof_uncertain`. :3170 refuses with `3 of 3 BAR(s) blocking, 0 clean: R-1/R-2/R-3 bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing`. This is D-016's :3170-vs-:3070 trap in its FOURTH costume today: not 'my edit is not live' but 'the gate names the wrong blocker'.\n\n2. THE REAL BLOCKER, MEASURED AT PRIMARY SOURCE. rubrics:get via :3170 on rev 5: r-1, r-2 and r-3 each carry `requiredTestLayers: null`. acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts:243 raises bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing at phase 'ship' for EVERY role:'outcome' BAR with empty requiredTestLayers. The pin is NOT the wall and repairing it ships nothing.\n\n3. THE BLANKET 'NEVER AMEND' IS NOW UNSHIPPABLE AND IS NARROWED. ## Now and D-013 forbid any rubrics:amend because it voids the vetting attestation and the independent card. That was correct guidance against CASUAL re-authoring, but as an absolute it makes this plan PERMANENTLY unshippable: acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts:606 states the only repair is `Declare requiredTestLayers through rubrics:amend AND bind evidence carrying a matching details.adequacy.testLayer`, and requiredTestLayers is in BAR_MEANING_FIELDS by name, so the revision necessarily moves to 6 and cards pinned at 5 go stale (evaluator:255 bar_snapshot_grading_stale).\n   RULING: a requiredTestLayers amendment is MANDATORY and is hereby authorized for this plan. The prohibition is narrowed to what it was actually protecting: no re-authoring of BAR PROSE, no re-proposing, no re-seeding, no amendment beyond declaring requiredTestLayers. Everything else in D-013 stands.\n   This is fully analysed on EI-22643649562847906 (open, unassigned, filed 22:31Z) which reached the same conclusion independently and REFUTED the migration-gap hypothesis; do not re-derive it.\n\n4. THE AMENDMENT COSTS A RE-CEREMONY. BATCH IT. Revision 6 invalidates BOTH the vetting attestation EI-22577324999589644 AND the independent card EI-22638284550937659 (all three criteria healthy, emitted 21:06Z by su-000a4d8f). Sequence, in order: dry-run -> outside-lineage approval receipt -> apply -> re-vet -> independent re-grade -> author acceptance verdict -> ship. Make EVERY intended revision before requesting the re-grade; a second amendment un-counts the new card too.\n\n5. DO NOT HAND-TRANSCRIBE THE APPROVAL RECEIPT. This rubric ALREADY failed this exact step once: EI-22562050692029127 (2026-09-07 00:54Z) failed `acceptance_bar_approval_invalid_receipt`, and the settled cause was an R-3 nextBarHash of 62 chars where acceptanceBarApprovalSchema requires /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/ — hand-transcription damage, NOT a validator defect. Route rubrics:amend { dryRun:true } through :3170, capture the server's approval JSON to a FILE, and have the outside-lineage reviewer post those exact bytes via work_items:comment. Reviewer identity and timestamp are read from the authenticated post and must never be supplied by the caller.\n\nPROVENANCE. The directive to drive this plan to completion is [owner:Avi 2026-09-07 ~20:03 EDT, interactive turn]: 'continue where they left off ... if they were working on a plan pickup the whole plan not just the work item'. The owner did NOT rule on rubrics:amend in that turn; clauses 3-5 above are [self-imposed], derived from the code and measurements cited, not from owner speech. su-872eeb6b's park on 'Avi's ruling at conv-mtrth4n8' predates all of it.\n\n### D-018 — RETRACTED: D-017 clause 1 is refuted by measurement — declaring requiredTestLayers makes the BAR strictly worse, not shippable\nDate: 2026-09-08\nRETRACTION of my own D-017 clause 1, issued by its author (su-336850c4). Reported by seat holder su-872eeb6b via pre-flight measurement on :3170 and then INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED BY ME IN CODE before recording. Do not act on D-017 clause 1.\n\nWHAT D-017 CLAUSE 1 SAID (wrong): amend the acceptance rubric to declare narrowed `requiredTestLayers` on R-1/R-2/R-3, clearing `bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing`.\n\nWHY IT IS WRONG (two independent mechanisms, both read in the tree):\n\n1. DECLARING LAYERS INVERTS THE RATING, IT DOES NOT SATISFY IT. In `computeAdequacy`, `correct-layer` is `not-applicable` only while `requiredTestLayers.length === 0`. Once layers are declared, `present` is populated ONLY from evidence rows where `typeof details.testLayer === 'string'`. The current evidence cohort carries `testLayer=null` on all 20 clauses, so `present` stays empty, `missing` = every required layer, and the rating is `fail` — i.e. the refusal moves from `proof_depth_missing` to `proof_inadequate`. Strictly worse, and it spends both the vetting attestation and the independent card to get there.\n\n2. THE AMEND RE-REVISIONS EVERY CLAUSE, SO PRE-BINDING CANNOT DODGE IT. The projection loop calls `setSpecClause` for EVERY clause, not only changed ones; `unchangedBar` selects which VALUES are written, never whether the write happens. So all 20 clauses go 5 -> 6 and every existing evidence binding is staled. Real price of the D-017 path is therefore the amend PLUS 20 evidence re-bindings.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy.ts:715-773 (`requiredTestLayers.length === 0` -> not-applicable; else `missing.length` -> rating 'fail', populated only from string `details.testLayer`); packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-amendment.ts:370-385 (`const unchangedBar = clause.source_bar_hash === criterion.barHash`, inside a `for (const clause of clauses)` loop that calls `setSpecClause` unconditionally).\n\nUNVERIFIED LEAD, NOT A RULING — the seat holder owns whether to pursue it. `requiredProofFloor` (same file, lines 379-388) returns floor 'none' WITHOUT any declared layer, via `clause.behaviorClass === 'non-automated' && clause.requiredTestLayers.length === 0`, and separately via `classRef === 'plan-class-investigation' && requiredTestLayers.length === 0`. That inverts the search direction: the lever for a manual/operational criterion may be behaviorClass with layers left EMPTY, not layers declared. I have NOT established (a) the current behaviorClass of R-1/R-2/R-3 or this plan's classRef, (b) whether behaviorClass is reachable through any legal surface — `acceptance-bar-amendment.ts` passes `behaviorClass: clause.behavior_class` through UNCHANGED, so `rubrics:amend` appears unable to set it, or (c) whether floor 'none' alone clears the ship refusal. Treat all three as open.\n\nPROCESS NOTE, so this class of error is cheaper next time: D-017 was authored from a refusal CODE plus a repair HINT, without reading the evaluator that produces the code. The hint named the symptom's field and I inferred the lever from it. On any BAR refusal, read the rating function before ruling — the repair hint names what is missing, never what will be accepted.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"portal-parity-2026-09-03-acceptance","title":"Portal parity with the papercusp app — acceptance (docks, split-pane, native surfaces styled, deep-link isolation, API passthrough, release continuity)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-e8071b9d-b6aa-4d2b-ba3f-05de514f9d7b","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Portal parity with the papercusp app — acceptance (docks, split-pane, native surfaces styled, deep-link isolation, API passthrough, release continuity)\nslug: portal-parity-2026-09-03-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\nowner: su-e8071b9d-b6aa-4d2b-ba3f-05de514f9d7b\n---\n\n# Portal parity with the papercusp app — acceptance (docks, split-pane, native surfaces styled, deep-link isolation, API passthrough, release continuity)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition of done for portal-parity-with-papercusp-2026-09-03, authored against the as-built :3081 releases of 2026-09-05. FINAL RELEASE: rH0tRkeuFOCkOtrTlk2XN-20260905165030111-1567760-871ad125 (readlink …/.portal-runtime/portal/current), served by papercusp-cloud-portal.service since ExecMainStartTimestamp 2026-09-05 12:51:29 EDT = 16:51:29Z. :3081 is the PORTAL host, not the operator — verdict (headless Chromium) is the correct instrument here; the operator-port ban covers :3055/:3070/:3170 only. Every criterion is an OUTCOME a non-implementer can observe on http://127.0.0.1:3081 with verdict (poll `.rail-item` count > 4 before clicking a rail entry) or by running the named tests, per D-004 (acceptance is a rendered screenshot, not a character count) and D-006 (suite-wide green by file count). Evidence dir: ~/.papercusp/evidence/portal-parity-2026-09-03/ — evidence is stated as a PROPERTY (a capture newer than the service start), never as a filename set, so the grader's own captures on the final release count. Portal checkout (separate git root): ~/papercupai-workspace/portal (symlink to ~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/portal) — its tests run with `npx vitest run <file>` from that checkout. TEST BINDINGS: the two papercusp-repo guards are bound as structured checks (runnable via testing:run); the portal tests are NAMED per criterion with their detecting assertion but stay prose-bound, because the running operator build refuses sibling-checkout check paths (measured 15:47Z on rubrics:propose: 'portal/tests/… does not resolve against the live tree') — the grader runs them from the portal checkout and cites the named assertion, not the file's pass count. Rev 2 = the author's self-vet: detecting assertions named per criterion, D-005 and D-008 §1 coverage added, no two criteria share an instrument. Rev 3 = the rubric-vetting consult critique (su-44c8a3b5, conv-mtojflez-0000-db15534eb01b4ffcbbefa0f40dd1b8ee) applied: the '≥70% of innerHeight' magic number replaced by the model's own property; the '*-v3.png' evidence SET replaced by the per-tab newer-than-service-start property; the pinned asset hash replaced by a chunk DERIVED at grading time from the releases' own-assets manifests, with the retention tolerance stated; the toast observable pinned to [data-sonner-toast] with its three detecting tests named; final release id updated. Rev 4 = the EI-22439758558949990 fix folded in: c3 gains the Vditor editor-mount probe (the /vditor/* passthrough that was 404 before), and the final release id is updated to rH0tRkeu (service start 16:51:29Z). The default-drift HALF of EI-22439758558949990 (REST returns default prompt/preferences while the sync read returns empty, so the settings form seeds empty) is fixed in code (packages/operator-core/lib/operator-config-defaults.ts shared by the REST route and sync-resolver) and unit-verified (5/5), but its live activation is on the OPERATOR :3070 whose green-checkpoint is stalled — so it is STAGED, not live, at grading time, with no user-data loss; it is not a rubric criterion (no criterion asserts the operator-config seed value) and is dispositioned on the bug + in the acceptance reasoning. Graders rate the 7 keys below only.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05","title":"Progress-certified release:trace verdict for active checkpoint candidates (merge of the two held 2026-08-14 filings)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-05","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Progress-certified release:trace verdict for active checkpoint candidates (merge of the two held 2026-08-14 filings)\nslug: progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-19\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-19. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nALL 5 ITEMS TERMINAL (5 done, 0 dropped) and the feature IS LIVE IN PRODUCTION.\n\n⚠ CORRECTION [self-imposed] [turn:self], measured 2026-09-16: the prior State block ended \"NOTHING is wired into production: release-trace.ts is untouched and the verdict is computed nowhere but its own test.\" That was written 2026-09-05 when only P-001 was done, and it has been FALSE since P-002 landed. It is corrected here rather than left to be inherited — a stale not-yet-wired claim reads exactly like a live one and is the kind of sentence a successor acts on.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/release-trace.ts:17 imports certifyCheckpointProgress from ./release-trace-progress; :832 calls it (`const cert: ProgressCertificate = certifyCheckpointProgress(run, nowMs)`); :1182 calls it again for the retriage-window interlock. The pure module (packages/operator-core/lib/release-trace-progress.ts:168) is unchanged and still returns { verdict: progressing|stalled|unknown, basis, evidenceAgeMs, evidenceAgeSource, liveAuthority, inRetriageWindow, detail }.\n\nShipped ON, not dark: FLAGS.RELEASE_TRACE_PROGRESS_CERTIFICATE is default-ON and pinned by libs/flags/src/production-defaults.test.ts:920 (\"stays default-ON and never goes dark\"), so it is not an override-only flip and not parked in KNOWN_DARK_FLAGS.\n\nThe design invariants recorded on 09-05 still hold and are unaffected by this correction: every D-003 ambiguity yields unknown rather than stalled; D-005 is structural (a cache-backed reading past the trust window supports no verdict, and even inside it can never support stalled, because a stale snapshot of an advancing run and a live snapshot of a wedged one are the same bytes); verdictWrittenAtMs is checked before any staleness rule; D-007 records both numeric thresholds as declared judgements with named falsifiers.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Implementation is DONE — what remains is the acceptance chain, per ship-main-greening-program-2026-09-15 D-005, which measured this as the most expensive remaining plan.\n\nBlocking right now: shipReadiness = acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready (bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty, bar_snapshot_rubric_revision_mismatch) — no BARs declared.\n\nOrder: (1) activation conversation audit against the source conversation, verifying any owner-approval turn is genuinely owner-typed before relying on it (a loop-fire replay reads exactly like owner speech and cannot support one); (2) draft->ready; (3) acceptance-BAR legacy backfill; (4) rubric revision 3->4; (5) re-vet with archive_floor:2, or an archived critique of a DIFFERENT rubric can be served as persuasive vetting-shaped prose; (6) FRESH independent grade from outside the author's lineage — ROUTE it via work_items:create { assign_to } to a live peer, never launch one (a self-launched grader is refused grader_in_implementer_lineage) and never file it unassigned (born-pending strands it ~30-60min); (7) re-emit the acceptance verdict; (8) ship.\n\nBatch every intended rubric revision BEFORE requesting the independent grade — a later edit un-counts the card.)\n\n## Background\n\nEI-20446991238274520 (kind `change`, severity `major`, filed by su-d4b9a5af during a `drain-control-plane-resilience-2026-08-13` IDEATE pass, lens `risk-first`) asks for a \"progress certificate\" on `release:trace` so `nextVerb` awaits only a demonstrably-progressing checkpoint run, rather than recommending `checkpoint:await` from an aging run-lock snapshot.\n\nBoth risks it names are real and already documented in this tree:\n- **Duplicate/replacement runs that kill healthy work** — CLAUDE.md's hard rule against firing a manual `release:checkpoint-run` into a re-triage window, and the EI-11667 \"replace-storm\" that starves the gate of every verdict.\n- **Passive waits on a wedged producer** — the playbook's \"a wait is only OK while the blocker is visibly progressing\".\n\n### What was measured (2026-09-05)\n\nGreps over `packages/ libs/ apps/ scripts/`:\n\n- `capturedBytes` → **0 hits.** `affectedTask` / `laneHeartbeat` / `lane_heartbeat` → **0 hits.** The recipe the filing says the operator must invoke, `distill-stalled-checkpoint-process-and-log-evidence` → **0 hits.**\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/release-trace.ts` is 1058 lines and contains **zero** references to `progressAtMs`, `advancing`, `stalled`, or `health`.\n- `gate.checkpointRunInFlight` ALREADY carries `progressAtMs`, `elapsedSec`, `startedAtMs`, `currentPhase`, `activeSource` (`run-lock` | `process-authority` | absent⇒cache), `candidateSource`, `inRetriageWindow`, `asOfAgeMs`.\n- `progress_at` / `current_phase` are emitted at three real sites in `release-checkpoint-launch.ts` (1499/1543, 1620), backed by `readRunPhase` over the run-lock dir — a populated field, not a dead one.\n- `release/checkpoint-run.ts:1805` already tells agents in prose to \"Judge liveness from current_phase + progress_at\" — the interpretation burden this plan retires.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — `checkpoint:await` only on a certified `progressing` run.** No path may recommend the passive wait for a checkpoint run it has not certified as advancing: `progressing` is NECESSARY for the await, not merely preferred (D-002, D-008). `stalled` and `unknown` must reach distinct, differently-WORDED recommendations, so an operator reading the verb never has to open a field to learn which case they are in (D-003, D-005, D-008).\n\n**R-2 — Ambiguous or aged evidence yields `unknown`, never `stalled`.** `progressAtMs === startedAtMs` is equally the shape of a run that has just started and of one that never advanced, so it may never produce `stalled` on its own (D-003). Evidence age CAPS the verdict rather than annotating it (D-005). The asymmetry is the safety property of the whole feature: a false `stalled` invites an operator to kill or replace healthy work, while an over-cautious `unknown` costs only a second look.\n\n**R-3 — The re-triage interlock holds on every path, INCLUDING with the steering flag OFF.** No verdict path may recommend a manual `release:checkpoint-run` inside the auto-refire re-triage window, because firing one discards a live rescue and costs a full suite (D-004). It is keyed on the VERB in `safeNextVerb` rather than on any branch, so a verdict path added later cannot route around it (D-010), and it is deliberately NOT gated by `RELEASE_TRACE_PROGRESS_CERTIFICATE` — gating a SAFETY interlock behind a STEERING kill-switch would let that switch silently re-arm a footgun (P-005).\n\n**R-4 — A REAL producer is proven able to reach the stall branch.** A suite that hand-builds `ProgressCertificateInput` proves the branch is correct GIVEN such an input but can never prove a producer emits one; the deciding gate `cachedDescribesNow` sits on the other side of that seam and was untested by construction (D-015). Acceptance requires a test that chains the real `mapCheckpointRunInFlight` into `certifyCheckpointProgress`, covering BOTH the reaching case and the identity-gate suppression that mechanically explains the P-004 zero (D-014).\n\n**R-5 — The certificate EXTENDS release:trace on existing signal — no parallel monitor, no persisted history.** It is assembled from run-lock, process, and affected-task heartbeat data already read (D-001); it persists no reading history (D-013 closed the retrospective-backfill route on two measured defeating conditions); and it stands up no second surface answering \"is the gate progressing\". The certifier stays pure — `nowMs` is a REQUIRED parameter, with no clock, fs, or db read — and the flag resolves at the io seam rather than inside the module.\n\n**R-6 — Both uncalibrated thresholds have a STATED disposition in the shipped record.** `DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS` (600_000) and `DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_TRUST_MS` (300_000) ship as declared JUDGEMENTS rather than measurements (D-007), and P-004 did not calibrate them (D-014); D-015 settled REACHABILITY only, which is not calibration. The shipped record must either name the measurement that calibrated them, or state plainly that they remain declared judgements AND name what would calibrate them. Silence on either constant is a defect, and the 300_000 trust window is the one most often dropped.\n\n**R-7 — The declared falsifier is reported WITH its reach.** The plan staked itself on one falsifier: a single false `stalled` on a progressing run (P-004). It did not fire — and could not have, because the stall branch was structurally unreachable for the runs sampled (164 samples, all verdict `unknown`; exercised=1, liveHeartbeat=0, cacheDescribedRun=0) (D-012, D-014). `falseStalls=0` is therefore a measurement of REACH, not of correctness, and every artifact reporting it — including the independent grading card and the ship note — must carry that limitation beside it, or it is a false clean bill.\n\n## Design\n\nAuthored post-implementation against as-built reality (2026-09-15), so this records the design that SHIPPED rather than one proposed ahead of it. Symbols are named instead of line numbers deliberately: this plan's own rubric cites line offsets from 2026-09-05 that have since moved, and a line number is a derived fact that rots silently.\n\n- **The certifier is a pure function.** `certifyCheckpointProgress` in `packages/operator-core/lib/release-trace-progress.ts` maps an already-assembled reading to `{ verdict: progressing|stalled|unknown, basis, evidenceAgeMs, evidenceAgeSource, liveAuthority, inRetriageWindow, detail }`. `nowMs` is a REQUIRED parameter rather than a defaulted `Date.now()`, and the module carries no imports at all, so it cannot reach a clock, filesystem or database even accidentally (R-5). Purity is what makes the verdict falsifiable without booting a gate.\n- **The producer is existing signal, not a new monitor.** `mapCheckpointRunInFlight` in `packages/operator-core/lib/git-pipeline-position.ts` assembles the certifier's input from run-lock, process-authority and heartbeat fields that `gate.checkpointRunInFlight` already carried (`progressAtMs`, `startedAtMs`, `currentPhase`, `activeSource`, `inRetriageWindow`, `asOfAgeMs`). No table, migration, routine or timer was added, and no reading history is persisted — D-013 closed the retrospective-backfill route on two measured defeating conditions (R-5).\n- **The consumption seam is the recommendation site.** In `packages/operator-core/lib/release-trace.ts`, `progressGatedAwait` is the only producer of the `checkpoint:await` recommendation on candidate-active paths, so `progressing` is necessary for the passive wait; `stalled` and `unknown` route to distinct, differently-worded verbs keyed off `basis`, which is why eight bases exist rather than one catch-all (R-1, R-2).\n- **The interlock is keyed on the VERB, not on a branch.** `safeNextVerb` withholds a manual `release:checkpoint-run` whenever `inRetriageWindow` is set, so a verdict path added later cannot route around it (D-010). It deliberately does not read `RELEASE_TRACE_PROGRESS_CERTIFICATE`: that flag exists for one carried risk (an uncalibrated threshold), while the interlock reads a window-membership fact no threshold enters — gating a SAFETY interlock behind a STEERING kill-switch would let the switch silently re-arm a footgun (R-3).\n- **The flag resolves at the io seam.** `RELEASE_TRACE_PROGRESS_CERTIFICATE` is resolved in `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release/trace.ts` and passed in, rather than read inside the certifier — which is what keeps the certifier pure (R-5). Code default ON, not dark.\n- **Two constants ship as declared judgements.** `DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS` (600_000) and `DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_TRUST_MS` (300_000) are labelled in-source as judgements, not measurements (D-007). P-004 was named as what would calibrate them and did not: D-014 records the stall path never executing on live data, and D-015 settled REACHABILITY only. The calibrating observation remains unmade — a HEALTHY checkpoint run quiet for longer than the threshold — because papercusp gate runs finish in ~17s (R-6, R-7).\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003, P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-004 | tree |\n\nEvery bar is `tree`-plane, and that is a deliberate judgement rather than a convenience. Five of the seven acceptance criteria bind test files that run at grading time; the remaining two grade what the shipped RECORD states, which no live gate observation can settle either. Nothing in this plan's acceptance requires watching a real checkpoint run — D-014 established that live sampling could not reach the stall branch at all, and D-015 closed it with a chained producer test. Declaring a `live` plane here would invent a blocker the plan does not have.\n\n## Phase 1 — the typed verdict\n\n- **P-001** `done` Write a PURE verdict function (new `packages/operator-core/lib/release-trace-progress.ts`) mapping existing `checkpointRunInFlight` fields to `{ verdict: 'progressing'|'stalled'|'unknown', evidenceAgeMs, basis }`, with unit tests covering every D-003 ambiguity case FIRST. Pure and separately testable so the verdict is falsifiable without booting a gate. importance: high — note: ← WI-2145760 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Wire P-001's verdict into `release-trace.ts` so `nextVerb` recommends `checkpoint:await` ONLY on `progressing`; `stalled` and `unknown` route to distinct, differently-worded recommendations per D-003/D-005. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2145774 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Honour the re-triage interlock (D-004): assert by test that no verdict path can recommend a manual `release:checkpoint-run` while `inRetriageWindow` is set. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2145801 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Run the filing's own cheap experiment as a SHADOW computation over real traces — emit the verdict without letting it change `nextVerb` — and record whether it ever labels a progressing run stalled. That single false-stalled is the filing's declared falsifier. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-2145843 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Only after P-004 reports clean, let the verdict steer `nextVerb`, behind the standard flag discipline (code default ON, verified live). blocked-by: P-004 — note: Certificate steers nextVerb behind FLAGS.RELEASE_TRACE_PROGRESS_CERTIFICATE (default ON, not dark); D-004 interlock deliberately ungated. 7 new tests green, lint:tsc clean.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 Build on the substrate that exists, not the substrate the filing names\n\nThe filing asks for a certificate \"assembled from existing run-lock, process, and affected-task heartbeat data: per-lane last elapsed/capturedBytes\".\n\nMeasured 2026-09-05: `capturedBytes` and every lane/affected-task-heartbeat symbol return ZERO hits across `packages/ libs/ apps/`, and the recipe it names returns zero hits too.\n\nThis is not a defect in the filing — it was authored in an IDEATE pass, where naming a plausible substrate is normal, and catching it is exactly what a design gate is for. But an implementer who takes those names as given will either build per-lane telemetry first (far larger than the filing scopes) or invent fields and report a certificate assembled from them.\n\n**Ruling:** the certificate is assembled from `gate.checkpointRunInFlight`, which already carries `progressAtMs`, `elapsedSec`, `startedAtMs`, `currentPhase`, `activeSource`, `candidateSource`, `inRetriageWindow`, `asOfAgeMs`. No new telemetry is in scope. Per-lane granularity, if ever wanted, is a separate filing against the probe.\n\n### D-002 The gap is real, and it is a CONSUMPTION gap rather than a missing signal\n\n`release-trace.ts` references none of `progressAtMs`, `advancing`, `stalled`, `health`. The signal already exists on the object `release:trace` reads; it simply never reads it. Meanwhile `release/checkpoint-run.ts:1805` instructs every agent to interpret `current_phase` + `progress_at` individually — the burden the filing correctly wants to retire.\n\nThis keeps the change small and inside the filing's own \"extend the existing release:trace surface (do not add a parallel monitor)\" constraint.\n\n### D-003 `progressAtMs === startedAtMs` is AMBIGUOUS — never emit `stalled` from it alone\n\n`progressAtMs` falls back to `startedAtMs` when progress was not measured, at three sites (`git-pipeline-stats.ts:1156`, `:1205`, `events/await/checkpoint-verified-wait.ts:68`). The equality means EITHER \"started, no progress yet\" OR \"never measured, start time substituted\". Those demand opposite responses, and `progressAtMs <= startedAtMs ⇒ stalled` collapses them into the alarming one.\n\nNot hypothetical: EI-22129511435526580 already fixed one instance at the stats layer, and its comment names the outcome — a run \"deep in the affected-test sweep, log mtime seconds old\" reported as \"stuck materializing for 53 minutes\", \"the exact false-positive-for-a-stall / false-negative-for-a-real-wedge failure mode\".\n\n**Ruling:** `unknown` is a first-class verdict, not a tidiness fallback. `stalled` requires POSITIVE evidence of non-advance — a `progressAtMs` that is measured (distinguishable from the placeholder), fresh enough to trust, and older than a phase-aware threshold. Where the inputs cannot separate the two readings the verdict is `unknown`, and `nextVerb` must say what to check rather than assert either state. A false `stalled` is the expensive direction: it invites a manual run that discards live work.\n\n### D-004 No verdict path may recommend a manual run inside the re-triage window\n\n`checkpointRunInFlight.inRetriageWindow` is marker-backed and readable on cron-fired runs. CLAUDE.md is unambiguous that firing a manual run into that window \"discards the rescue and costs a full suite\". A `stalled` verdict is the state most likely to tempt a caller into firing one, so the interlock is asserted by test (P-003), not left to recommendation wording.\n\n### D-005 Evidence age is part of the verdict, not a footnote beside it\n\nWhen `activeSource` is absent the reading is cache-backed and `asOfAgeMs` \"can be arbitrarily large (measured: 7h)\"; the field's own documentation says to treat an old cache-backed reading \"as a HINT, not a measurement, in EITHER direction\". A verdict computed from a 7-hour-old snapshot and rendered with the confidence of a live run-lock read would be the identical class of error this plan exists to prevent, one layer up.\n\n**Ruling:** the verdict carries `evidenceAgeMs` and its `basis`, and an age past the trust threshold caps the verdict at `unknown` regardless of the underlying numbers.\n\n### D-006 This plan IS the ordered merge; that is why it was created over a similarity refusal\n\n`plans:new` refused this slug as `similar_exists` at 0.924 against `progress-certified-release-trace-for-active-checkpoint-candi-2026-08-14`, and 0.881 against `active-checkpoint-truth-capsule-on-release-trace-2026-08-14`. Both are `superseded`, both sit at REVISION HOLD (steward-graded 3/5, 2026-08-16), and neither is pickable.\n\nTheir own `now.next` fields order this merge: the two \"are ONE mechanism and must merge into ONE filing\"; the progress-certified plan \"holds the BETTER mechanism text ... carry that text into the merge; do not deprecate it\"; and \"originator su-d4b9a5af is no longer running — whoever picks this up owns the merge.\"\n\n**Ruling:** `force: true` was justified not by a clean search but by that explicit instruction — the merge they order exists in no live plan, so continuing either held plan in place would leave the other un-merged. Both are recorded here as superseded-by-merge. The mechanism text was carried forward, not deprecated, per the ruling.\n\n**Explicit scope exclusion, from the capsule plan's ruling:** candidate identity with authoritative-vs-inferred provenance, and a per-path containment falsifier, have **already shipped** — verified independently 2026-09-05 by reading `candidateSource` (`retriage-marker` | `in-flight-candidate` | `run-probe`) and the containment leg in `git-pipeline-position.ts`. Re-proposing them \"grades 3 again\". This plan is therefore scoped to the release:trace-side capsule plus the progress certificate ONLY.\n\n### D-007 — Both verdict thresholds are declared JUDGEMENTS, not measurements — P-004 is what calibrates them\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-001 ships two numeric thresholds it cannot justify from data: `DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS = 600_000` (heartbeat age past which a live-authority reading is called `stalled`) and `DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_TRUST_MS = 300_000` (cache age past which a non-live reading supports no verdict at all).\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/release-trace-progress.ts — both constants are exported with doc comments stating they are judgements, and `certifyCheckpointProgress` takes a `ProgressCertificateOptions` override for each, so no caller is forced onto the default.\n\nRULING: nobody may cite either default as a measured property of green-checkpoint runs, in a doc, a comment, a work-item, or a downstream decision. They are placeholders chosen so the module can exist and be tested; this plan already carries the reason a wrong value is expensive (D-003: too low a stall threshold re-manufactures the false stall that costs a full suite).\n\nEach names its own falsifier, so calibration is a measurement and not another judgement:\n- stall threshold — a run observed HEALTHY with a heartbeat gap wider than 600s means the value is too low.\n- evidence trust — a cache-backed reading older than 300s that still tracked the live run means the value is too conservative; one younger than 300s that did not means it is too generous.\n\nThat is exactly the shadow computation P-004 already specifies (emit the verdict over real traces without acting on it). So P-004 is not merely a safety gate before P-005 wires the verdict into `nextVerb` — it is also the only thing that can turn these two numbers from judgements into measurements, and it should record the observed distributions when it runs.\n\nThis is recorded as a decision rather than left in the code comment because the failure it guards against is downstream: a later reader quoting \"the 10-minute stall threshold\" as if it described the system is the same class of error as this plan's sibling, `machine-enforced-terminal-criteria-2026-09-05` D-022 — a real number read as a property of a population nobody measured.</body>\nRelated: P-001, P-004\n\n### D-008 — `progressing` is NECESSARY for the await, not sufficient; and `unknown` routes on WHO answered\nDate: 2026-09-05\nP-002 was specified as \"recommend `checkpoint:await` ONLY on `progressing`\". Implementing it surfaced two cases the literal rule answers badly. Both are recorded here because other lanes will read the routing and because P-003/P-004 assert against it.\n\n**1. `verdict-published` is `progressing`, but must NOT await.**\nP-001 classifies a run that has published its verdict and continued into re-triage/salvage as `progressing` — correctly: the run is healthy, and its overdue-looking elapsed time is salvage, not a wedge. But the thing a `checkpoint:await` would wait for HAS ALREADY ARRIVED. Awaiting it is waiting on the past.\n\nRuling: \"only on progressing\" is a NECESSARY condition for the await, never a sufficient one. `verdict-published` routes to `state:read { cell: 'gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict' }` — read the verdict that exists rather than await one that already came. This NARROWS the await; it does not widen it, so it cannot violate the P-002 constraint it refines.\n\n**2. `unknown` splits on `liveAuthority`, not on basis alone.**\nThe first cut routed every `unknown` to `dev:pipeline_position` (\"the reading is the problem — get a better one\"). That is wrong for half the population and the failure is silent: when a LIVE authority (run-lock / process-authority) already answered and still could not certify advancement, a re-read cannot supply a heartbeat that was never emitted. The recommendation would be a loop dressed as an action — the reader re-reads, gets the identical certificate, and re-reads again.\n\nRuling: `unknown` routes on WHO answered.\n- live authority answered → `processes:list`. This reading is the best the interface can produce; measure the producer instead.\n- no live authority → `dev:pipeline_position`. The READING is the limitation and a live re-read genuinely fixes it.\n\n`stalled` also routes to `processes:list` (a stall is a claim about the PRODUCER), but with a materially different claim in its reason: `stalled` asserts non-advancement, live-authority `unknown` explicitly asserts that neither health NOR a wedge was established. Same verb, different claim — collapsing the two sentences is the D-003-class error one level up.\n\n**Verified, not assumed:** `progress-unmeasured` is NOT the common shape. `git-pipeline-position.ts` writes `progressAtMs = active && cachedDescribesNow ? cachedRun.progressAtMs : undefined`, so an absent heartbeat means the cached run reading does not describe now — a genuinely low-information case, not the healthy default. Read from the writer before assuming this routing over-triggers.\n\n**Falsifiability measured, not argued:** an in-tree mutation probe under a file lock neutralized the gate (`cert.verdict === 'progressing'` → `true`); 6 of the 8 new cases failed (MUTANT CAUGHT, tree verified byte-identical afterwards). The suite also carries a control asserting the fixture DOES recommend `release:checkpoint-run` once the in-flight run is removed — without it, every \"did not recommend the forbidden verb\" assertion could pass for reasons unrelated to P-002.\n\n### D-009 — Measurement backing D-008's claim about absent heartbeats\nDate: 2026-09-05\nD-008 asserts that an absent `progressAtMs` is a low-information case rather than the healthy default, and that claim decides whether its `unknown` -> `processes:list` routing over-triggers in production. Recording the measurement separately so the claim is falsifiable rather than resting on another decision.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-05, `grep -n \"progressAtMs\" packages/operator-core/lib/git-pipeline-position.ts` — read from the WRITER, not inferred from the field's name or its optionality:\n- git-pipeline-position.ts:4464 — `const progressAtMs = active && cachedDescribesNow ? cachedRun!.progressAtMs : undefined;`\n- git-pipeline-position.ts:4537 — `...(progressAtMs !== undefined ? { progressAtMs } : {})`\n\nSo the field is omitted exactly when the run is inactive OR the cached run reading does not describe now. It is NOT omitted from ordinary healthy live readings, which is what would have made the routing fire on the common path.\n\nFalsifier: if a later change emits `progressAtMs` only on a narrower branch (or drops it), the `unknown`/`progress-unmeasured` route becomes the common case and D-008's second ruling needs re-deciding.
