So the process-authority probe identified the run within seconds.\"* Only ONE of the two is a gate observation.\n\nThe `13:08:47.624Z` row's witness cgroup is\n`/…/papercusp.slice/papercusp-agent.slice/papercusp-agent-session.slice/pc-0mto01yca3te9v41hud--agent.scope`,\nwhich matches the analyzer's `AGENT_SCOPE = /\\/papercusp\\.slice\\//` and is EXCLUDED as agent contamination — an agent session burning CPU, not the green-checkpoint gate. Only `13:27:28.564Z` (`/…/app.slice/run-u583750.scope`, outside the slice) is the gate, and only it was corroborated against the gate's own checkpoint log.\n\nWhat changes and what does not:\n- **D-012's MECHANISM is unaffected.** The cache-identity gate co-nulls `candidate`/`currentPhase`/`progressAtMs` while `startedAtMs` survives; that shape is structural and holds for any active-run reading regardless of whose process is running. Both rows exhibit it and both remain valid evidence *for that claim*.\n- **The GATE-population evidence narrows from 2 observations to 1.** Any sentence of the form \"both live samples of the gate…\" overstates it.\n- **D-012's ruling is untouched and reinforced** — the corrected count is one gate sample, zero heartbeats.\n\n#### 3. A sharper statement of the falsifier's reach than the closure recorded\n\nAll **164** rows returned verdict `unknown` (basis: 162 `no-run`, 2 `progress-unmeasured`). Zero `progressing`, zero `stalled`. So `falseStalls=0` is true but vacuous in the strongest available sense: not \"tested and never false-stalled\" but **\"never reached a branch that could have false-stalled\"**. Report it only that way (D-012 §1).\n\nDistinct and not to be pooled with the above: a separate live `:3170` trace did show `progressAtMs` present at ~91s age, so the `progressing` branch does execute on production data. That observation is not part of this series. Likewise D-015 settled REACHABILITY of the producer→certifier stall path via the seam test and settled nothing about CALIBRATION; `DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS` (600,000) and `DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_TRUST_MS` (300,000) remain declared judgements this series did not calibrate.\n\nMeasured: `wc -l .papercusp/scratch/p004-samples.jsonl` = 164; `jq -r '.verdict' | sort | uniq -c` = `164 unknown`; `jq -r '.basis' | sort | uniq -c` = `162 no-run, 2 progress-unmeasured`; rows with `reading.progressAtMs != null` = 0; rows with `reading.startedAtMs != null` = 2; advancing witness outside `/papercusp\\.slice/` = 1, inside = 1; exclusion regex at `.papercusp/scratch/p004-analyze.mts:109`; ignore rule at `.gitignore:178`; refusal emitted by `packages/operator-core/lib/plan-acceptance-gate.ts:484-497` via `evaluateEphemeralDeliverableDurability`.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-017 — Owner-approved September 12 audit disposition and current execution contract\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAuthority: session_turn:codex:01a0961e-ab11-71f2-bae6-9be0c8401857:32 — Avi approved applying the relevance-audit recommendations and implementing relevant updated plans through verified shipment. This decision adopts the Keep disposition.\n\nCurrent contract: The current certificate correctly treats absent/equal-fallback/stale-cache signals as unknown and preserves the retriage interlock. It replaces the two older overlapping trace proposals.\n\nExecution: Finish the recorded acceptance chain and retain the published limits: the ten-minute stall threshold is judgment, not a newly proven production calibration.\n\nMeasured basis: the source/test/decision review and scoped verification recorded in docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md, not a new claim about the live gate. Historical timestamps, candidate references and consumed one-shot permissions below remain historical. Preserve current frozen-lineage invariants and the live-gate ownership boundary. This update does not waive proof, independent grading or acceptance requirements. Track adoption under WI-10001081; retain existing implementation work-items and completed evidence.\n\n### D-018 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-17\nAmendment-Id: p016-variant-a-checks-only-r6-r7-rev4to5\nRequest-Hash: a80c4578109cb1712a1aa82fba778dc5604528495cb719232f08ec49eaeeb7fc\nActor: su-a604a73a-08f7-4699-a4c1-05506614e161\nReason: P-016 variant A (checks-only): bind the manual instrument contract to the two corpus-inspection BARs R-6/R-7 so neither is unfalsifiable. Out-of-lineage approval by su-4dbc7355 (thread-post:205154). Ruling ship-main-greening-program-2026-09-15#D-007.\nApproved-By: su-4dbc7355-3bfa-4308-b4d8-e5223e782644\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:205154\nApproved-At: 2026-09-17T03:29:17.811Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 30 → 31\nChanged BARs: R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-019 — SHIP-TIME GATE: the ship note must report P-004's falsifier WITH its reach — relocated here from acceptance criterion R-7, which could not bind it\nDate: 2026-09-17\nDate: 2026-09-17\nRecorded by su-a604a73a at 2026-09-17T05:0xZ, BEFORE amending rubric `acceptance-progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05` R-7 `falsifier-reported-with-its-scope`, so the obligation is never unheld for even one revision.\n\n#### Why this moved\n\nIndependent vetting critic su-a961ddec (consult conv-mu4zj5mc, post 205222) found that R-7's subject-side half names an artifact that DOES NOT EXIST at rating time. Per the documented completion sequence, independent grading is step 5, the implementer's acceptance verdict step 6, and `plans:set-plan-status shipped` step 7. R-7 required the grader to \"confirm the ship note / plan status write carries the same caveat\" — an artifact written strictly AFTER the card that must rate it.\n\nThe consequence is not pedantic: a grader who cannot observe the ship note has NO correct rating available. `fail` blames the subject for the sequence; `pass` asserts the unobserved. The scale has `unknown`, but R-7 forecloses it — \"Silence in either place is a `fail`, not an omission to be waived.\" I verified this text directly in template_data rather than taking the critique's word for it.\n\nAn acceptance criterion cannot bind an artifact that postdates acceptance. So the obligation is RELOCATED, not dropped.\n\n#### THE GATE (binding on whoever ships this plan, including a future me)\n\nBefore `plans:set-plan-status { slug:'progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05', status:'shipped' }`, the ship note MUST state the falsifier's result WITH its reach. Concretely, it may not report `falseStalls=0` (or \"no false stalls\") without, in the same passage, recording that this measures REACH and not correctness, and carrying the figures that establish it: 164 samples, all verdict `unknown`, exercised=1, liveHeartbeat=0, cacheDescribedRun=0.\n\nRationale, unchanged from R-7's model and still true: the stall branch was structurally unreachable for the runs sampled (D-012/D-014), so `falseStalls=0` is \"never reached a branch that could have false-stalled\", NOT \"tested and never false-stalled\". Reporting it bare is a false clean bill.\n\nAlso carried, and NOT to be read as settled by D-015: DEFAULT_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS (600_000) and DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_TRUST_MS (300_000) remain declared judgements this series did not calibrate. D-015 settled REACHABILITY only. Reachability is not calibration.\n\n#### What R-7 keeps\n\nR-7 retains the reach-vs-correctness substance and a mechanically checkable obligation on the grading card — the one forward artifact that DOES exist at rating time. Its ship-note half lives here now.\n\n### D-020 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-17\nAmendment-Id: 27bb6edbb36b6f56031448e85f7d06317adb3947023e47a4b79d41b6f562fc1e\nRequest-Hash: 133563e5ec0b1a9755b30769cff9554998cb47a80aac93571bd18af2af297aa4\nActor: su-a604a73a-08f7-4699-a4c1-05506614e161\nReason: R-7 falsifiability defect found by independent critic su-a961ddec: the bound check cannot falsify its own driftMarker; the forward obligation in method (b) is withdrawn to grader discipline. Authorized by ship-main-greening-program-2026-09-15#D-010.\nApproved-By: su-a961ddec-7f2e-4250-8927-d935aecfad61\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:205230\nApproved-At: 2026-09-17T08:00:05.064Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 32 → 33\nChanged BARs: R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-021 — P-016 cannot ship without an R-7 BAR amendment; that amendment invalidates the current proof bindings and the in-flight independent grade\nDate: 2026-09-17\nRULING (2026-09-17, su-a604a73a). Binds the P-016 ship lane and anyone holding a grade against this rubric.\n\nMEASURED FACTS\n1. The acceptance rubric WAS vetted. Attestation EI-23496206381768205 exists at rev 9 with a criteriaHash matching current exactly. The reading that 'vetting was never done' is FALSE and has already misdirected one peer.\n2. Its grade-the-grader audit RAN and returned a SUBSTANTIVE verdict: EI-23496651720186270 (auditor role-024c55b9, 08:29:13Z), 3 of 6 FAIL - terminal-re-rate, re-runnable-evidence, degenerate-distribution. gradingAudit.state='failed' here means 'judged and rejected', NOT an infrastructure miss ('pending' is the infrastructure miss).\n3. The root defect is in the ARTIFACT, confirmed by me directly from harness_shared.harness_plans rather than taken on the audit's word: criterion R-7 (falsifier-reported-with-its-scope) at rev 9 has method (b) 'no paraphrase-quality judgement is involved' - a PRESENCE check where quoting verbatim satisfies the bar - while its driftMarkers still penalize 'the grader's own evidence ... merely quoting the rubric or a Decision instead of restating the limitation' and still carry 'a ship note that reports the falsifier without its reach', an obligation D-019 relocated to the ship gate. A grader reading driftMarkers fails a card method passes.\n\nRULING\n(a) P-016 CANNOT honestly reach satisfied vetting while that contradiction stands. Re-attesting without fixing it reproduces the same audit failure; attesting honestly records a rubric defect, which is not a passing vetting either. The amendment is unavoidable, not optional.\n(b) The amendment is NOT free and must not be fired casually. rubrics:amend dryRun classifies a driftMarkers edit as kinds:['bar-meaning'], fields:['falsifier'], approvalRequired:true. Measured blast radius: rubric rev 9->10, subject plan rev 33->34, 10 invalidatedProofRefs, invalidatedScorecardIds EI-22438862127500981 + EI-23365757672694634, authorVerdictBecomesStale:true, reboundWorkItemIds WI-10001488, nextRepair bar_snapshot_proof_stale ('Bind proof to the new spec revisions, then refresh vetting and independent grading').\n(c) My initial framing - that aligning driftMarkers to the already-authoritative model+method 'does not move the operative bar' - is WITHDRAWN. The mechanism classifies a falsifier edit as bar-meaning, and that classification governs over my semantic reading of it.\n(d) SEQUENCING, binding on this lane. The amendment requires an OUTSIDE-LINEAGE approver; I authored the rubric, so I cannot self-approve. Order: route approval -> amend to rev 10 -> re-bind the 10 invalidated proof refs -> re-derive (never copy-forward) the vetting attestation against rev 10 -> grading audit -> refreshed independent grade -> acceptance verdict -> ship.\n(e) The in-flight independent grade by su-5115b977 (7 bespoke criteria, 5 pass / 2 partial / 0 fail, parked on WI-10001714) WILL be un-counted by the revision bump. Their caveat is adopted as binding: a verbatim re-emit is honest only for criteria whose text did not move. R-7 is the criterion being amended, so R-7 MUST be re-graded against rev 10; the other six may be re-emitted verbatim.\n\nWHY RECORDED HERE, NOT IN A MESSAGE\nTwo agents have now independently reached a wrong diagnosis of this rubric's vetting state from a refusal string alone, and a coord message is not addressable after delivery. Cite this decision rather than paraphrasing it.\n\nNOT ESTABLISHED (do not read as settled): whether the amendment, once landed, actually clears the audit - the acceptance-grading-sweep is owner-paused and the auto-dispatch fix (EI-23414612968722239) is in main but NOT deployed, so a fresh attestation may sit pending. That is a separate blocker and does not change (a).\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"psu-session-port-durable-repair-2026-09-05","title":"Make psu session ports consistent, recoverable, and verifiable","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-05","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make psu session ports consistent, recoverable, and verifiable\nslug: psu-session-port-durable-repair-2026-09-05\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-20\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** DRAFT for owner review. Investigation WI-2146697 is complete apart from recording and checking this plan. No implementation, activation, agent launch, session migration, or deployment is authorized by this plan's creation.\n**Next:** Review this repair design and select an execution route. Before activation, audit the complete owner conversation and the authority-continuity requirement behind WI-214387, record plans:audit, then execute the dependency order below.\n**Stop condition:** The supported Claude-to-Codex/OMP port matrix passes, failures recover without losing history or duplicating an owner, and an approved release has passed the ordinary gate and shipped.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Canonical destination.** Inspect, prepare, bootstrap, and launch resolve one identical concrete backend/model/effort/provider/account/context contract; aliases, defaults, provider prefixes, and denied models cannot drift between stages.\n\n**R-002 — Safe complete payload.** The ported seed is complete enough to continue work, strips unsafe provider-specific thinking/signatures and secrets, preserves inert tool relationships, discloses omissions, and hashes every semantic byte including the current instruction.\n\n**R-003 — Atomic recoverable lifecycle.** A logical port attempt produces at most one target, retrying a lost response returns the same receipt, failed/expired attempts remain diagnosable and retryable, and no target home or binding is silently overwritten.\n\n**R-004 — Single continuing owner.** The target continues the source coordination identity and valid operational state without parallel execution, duplicate claims, lost fleet/loop/mode/await state, or resurrected expired locks.\n\n**R-005 — Exactly-once kickoff and native proof.** The current instruction is delivered once, ordinary fresh kickoff is suppressed for a port, and delivery is accepted only after exact target-native transcript persistence is proven.\n\n**R-006 — Bounded repair and truthful diagnostics.** Expiry/crash cleanup is bounded and restart-safe; typed errors preserve the failing stage and cause without leaking payloads or credentials.\n\n**R-007 — Recurrence guard.** Repository tests exercise the integrated launcher → inspect/prepare → bootstrap → PTY → native-delivery path and fail when destination, payload, authority, retry, or proof contracts regress.\n\n**R-008 — Real user-path acceptance.** Synthetic tracked Claude history ports successfully to supported Codex/OMP targets, resumes natively afterward, preserves the source history, and reaches the installed psu path through the normal gated release.\n\n**R-009 — Guarded router backend failover.** The router reuses the session-port primitive only for an authoritative provider-wall verdict, only at an idle turn boundary, under explicit cross-provider-egress policy, with compatible target selection and one attempt per wall generation.\n\n**R-010 — No silent oscillation.** Ambiguous health, pacing projections, generic errors, latency, and in-flight work never trigger a switch; target-wall and no-target outcomes are explicit, restart recovery is deterministic, and failback is deliberate rather than automatic ping-pong.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-002 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-004 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-006 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-007 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-008 | P-008 | live |\n| R-009 | P-009 | deployed |\n| R-010 | P-010 | live |\n\nThe detailed architecture, evidence corrections, acceptance matrix, sequencing, and rollout constraints remain in the sections below.\n\n## Background and scope\n\nThe owner reported that resuming Claude native session 5414d1c5-81a7-439d-bcb7-bb85b0f2430c (ADV 22525) into Codex's backend-default choice prepares port 74e90915-9cdc-4ee2-b015-ff44d65e8179, then aborts with \"prepared target codex/default does not match bootstrap codex/gpt-5.6-sol\". They requested a thorough audit of the functionality, followed by a durable repair plan.\n\nThe exact row was read during the initial investigation: target_model=NULL, source hash matching the disclosed archive, no target ADV row, error=NULL. Preparation succeeded; target bootstrap rejected the inconsistent model representation. September 1 commit ab908874a5 added resolveCodexModel to bootstrap without applying the same policy to port inspection/preparation.\n\nThis is a follow-up to shipped plan psu-cross-backend-session-port-2026-07-14, not a reimplementation of its original scope. That plan's July authority-isolation decisions were followed by WI-214387, whose August repair preserves the source coordination owner. Preserve that continuation intent and make its transfer atomic; do not silently restore the earlier blanket refusal of claim/loop-bearing sources.\n\nSupported scope remains tracked plain Claude SU -> Codex or OMP within the same workspace and supported host topology. Native same-backend resume/fork must remain correct. Reverse ports, untracked imports, cross-workspace transfers, and new backend support are excluded. Existing native transcripts are never rewritten or deleted by this repair.\n\n## Evidence and corrections\n\nEvidence source: current staging implementation, original plan decisions, WI-214387 and WI-4943 records, bounded incident-row reads, actual exported-function probes with synthetic data, and the existing test framework. No provider call or real session launch was made for this investigation.\n\n- F01, reproduced: omitted Codex model remains null in sessionPortRequestBody, but freshSuBootstrapBody resolves it to gpt-5.6-sol. Provider-qualified openai/gpt-5.6-sol:high also differs from the bare bootstrap model. Explicit gpt-5.6-sol and sol:high agree. Sources: apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs resolveResumeTarget/sessionPortRequestBody/freshSuBootstrapBody; endpoint-route/routes/adv/sessions.ts resolveSessionPortInspection; bootstrap-su.ts model resolver and prepared-target comparison.\n- F02, reproduced: a port with an explicit or inherited kickoff retains it through sessionPortTargetArgs and finalizeFreshSuArgs while bootstrap returns sessionPortKickoffFile. hostThroughPty immediately rejects both with \"plain kickoff and managed kickoff file are mutually exclusive\". Preparation has already occurred by then.\n- F03, reproduced in preparation service: expired-date prepared, pending, and delivered rows are returned as reusable. Failed/expired rows permanently reject the same semantic input. currentInstruction is absent from the idempotency key; changing it leaves the rendered hash unchanged. Source: session-port/service.ts and render.ts.\n- F04, proven call ordering; fault-injection regression still required: bootstrap's row.status !== prepared check precedes generic claimAgentLaunch replay lookup. Once a successful first bootstrap made the row pending, a lost-response retry rejects before reaching its cached response.\n- F05, code-level concurrency defect; production incidence NOT established: bootstrap claims use per-request random keys; target reservation occurs after fallible home creation. transitionSessionPort permits pending -> pending and can replace target_adv_session_id. Two requests can pass the earlier state/owner reads before either creates a target. Reproduce with real disposable-Postgres barriers before declaring a measured duplicate.\n- F06, reproduced with the actual readManagedKickoffFile function and an in-memory fake filesystem: changed seed bytes retaining the checksum marker are accepted although their digest differs. Both bootstrap and native-transcript lookup use substring presence. The delivery endpoint accepts a client boolean/hash/path without independently reading the target user turn. renderSessionPortSeed hashes the history frame but appends the current instruction afterward.\n- F07, code-level partial-commit defect: delivered/failed session_ports transition, ADV projection update, artifact unlink, and telemetry are separate operations. The ADV writer returns a boolean that delivery does not require to be true. Status reconciliation checks only the port row. A partial failure can report delivered while leaving a target hidden or cleanup incomplete.\n- F08, reproduced synthetic data: adapter exports thinking as text; the original plan D-005 says to drop it. The exact incident archive contained 59 thinking blocks / 71,622 characters. Narratives over 16,000 characters truncate with an inline marker but no warning/count and may still advertise full fidelity. Tool result association loses call IDs. Top-level Claude attachment records are grouped as synthetic rather than classified for meaningful content vs bookkeeping.\n- F09, reproduced synthetic data: JSON api_key values, Slack tokens, and PEM material passed the port scrubber unchanged; earlier probes also covered AWS/JWT patterns. Reuse the maintained shared sensitive-text primitives and extend their missing cases with high-confidence fixtures. No actual credential leak from this aborted launch was established; the earlier critical labels exceeded the evidence.\n- F10, budget/summary risks: buildContextBudget DOES reserve 8,000-15,000 tokens plus runtime overhead. The defect is not absence of reserves. The final complete seed/current instruction is not counted or bound as one object; inspection omits live plan text and other bootstrap overlays; OMP's actual default/provider/local context can resolve later. Summary chunks split at fixed character offsets and independent per-chunk output limits do not guarantee a global fit. These require boundary fixtures; they did not cause this particular small-enough port rejection.\n- F11, continuity: resolveSuInstructionRuntime ALREADY reads durable modes, so claiming all modes are lost is incorrect. However port args clear fleet/harness-related launch context, base rendering uses those empty fields, and the seed still falsely says no source owner/claims/loops/modes carried. The generic live-owner conflict is checked late; no atomic cross-backend handoff joins source reservation, native wake/resume, and target creation.\n- F12, expiry/diagnostics: the incident seed remained 0600 on disk and the row remained prepared after its stated expiry at the historical read. Physical cleanup is attached to daily telemetry retention. Bootstrap rejection did not record its original error. Broad 404-to-upgrade remapping can mislabel source-not-found as protocol skew.\n- F13, home relocation detail: rekeyCodexHome only renames the temporary UUID home; its config log_dir was rendered as an absolute temporary path and numeric ADV hook ID was unavailable before allocation. Runtime environment can supply the ADV id, so universal hook failure is NOT established. Materialize using the final target identity or repair all managed path/identity fields in place before launch.\n\nVerification on September 5:\n- Full suite: npx vitest run packages/operator-core/lib/session-port packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/__tests__/bootstrap-su.test.ts apps/operator/lib/psu-launcher.test.ts apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host.integration.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/model-context-budget.test.ts\n- Result: 14 files, 962 tests passed, no skips, exit 0, 115.58s. These existing tests pass despite the reproduced failures, demonstrating missing cross-boundary cases.\n- Additional stdin Node/tsx probes used real exported functions; checksum-reader tamper probe used injected filesystem functions and synthetic bytes. They are diagnostic evidence, not shipped regression tests.\n- Full live CLI canaries, real DB concurrency injection, and a production-wide incident rate were NOT measured. The earlier small port-row census mixed controlled acceptance attempts with user attempts and must not be presented as a reliability percentage.\n\n## Durable design\n\n### One resolved launch contract\n\nExtend SessionPortTarget/SessionPortContractSummary and existing launch helpers. Retain a displayable requested selector separately from resolved backend, model, effort, provider, account policy, effective context window, context size, launch-context digest, source identity, and stable prompt inputs. Both inspection and bootstrap consume the same resolver, including plan context and backend policy. Exclude volatile observation timestamps from semantic hashes.\n\nResolve defaults/aliases/provider prefixes and deny-listed models BEFORE source export, summaries, artifacts, or target rows. Validate account compatibility without exposing credentials. Explicit routing fails closed. The preview displays the concrete destination; the client launches the returned prepared destination, not a second reconstruction from picker state. A changed route or material prompt/window change requires a fresh review/fit, not silent substitution.\n\n### Complete bounded content, with honest fidelity\n\nReuse sensitive-text.ts and current adapter/render/fit modules. Drop foreign thinking/signatures and executable provider objects per the established content contract. Keep tool relations as local inert identifiers, not executable calls. Classify meaningful text attachments; declare binary/unsupported omissions and truncations explicitly. Reject ambiguous/unrecoverable source graphs with a useful error.\n\nCompute a digest and byte length over the entire canonical payload, including the current instruction; place the digest receipt outside the hashed payload. Define the exact treatment of the verified turn-origin prefix and CRLF before persistence comparisons. Check bytes at preparation, bootstrap, PTY read, and target-user-turn proof. Checksum-marker substring presence alone is insufficient.\n\nBudget the exact final payload with the same target context and runtime reserves as launch. Mark estimation honestly; use supported backend token counters where available and tested conservative bounds otherwise. Split summaries on conversation/tool-group boundaries, allocate a global output budget, pass output limits to the maintained summarizer, sanitize its output, and fail clearly if even the latest required group cannot fit. Never silently drop content to make a test green.\n\n### Retryable, exclusively owned attempts\n\nReuse session_ports, ADV rows, and the existing agent-launch idempotency ledger. Separate a logical request fingerprint (including currentInstruction and material launch-context inputs) from an attempt key. Retransmitting one active attempt returns its same receipt; an explicit retry of a failed/expired attempt creates a linked new attempt using the same valid source. A delivered request resolves to its existing target or requires an explicit new continuation decision; it must not attempt a second bootstrap with an already-consumed token.\n\nAcquire one transactionally fenced port/source reservation before creating any target home. Extend existing acquireAdvSessionResume row-lock/lease semantics to arbitrate native resume, port, and wake through the same ownership rule. Only prepared -> pending can bind a target. Repeating pending is idempotent only for the same target/attempt; it cannot reassign target IDs. Validate replay authorization and immutable request digest, then return a committed bootstrap receipt before rejecting its already-progressed state.\n\nAllocate or reserve the final hidden target ADV id before writing identity-bearing configuration, so CODEX_HOME paths, hooks, log_dir and later native resume agree. On failure, retain a typed attempt error and clean only that attempt's resources. Do not erase history to recover a bad bootstrap.\n\n### Operational continuity and delivery\n\nKeep one coordination owner with a new native conversation. Read current fleet membership/role, modes, loop configuration, plan/harness, facts and valid claims from their registries. Preserve those bindings; update native/session/home pointers and wake routing under the reservation. Expired/released locks are not resurrected. Ensure one executable host owns that coordination identity throughout the transfer.\n\nCheck a live source before preparation/egress. A live source requires an explicit supported orderly handoff or a clear stop-source instruction, never a second process using its identity. Failed handoff leaves the original session recoverable; recovery must not reset shared owner authority. The old native transcript stays intact, and its later resume cannot become a concurrent second owner.\n\nThere is exactly one port kickoff channel. currentInstruction is included once in the canonical managed seed; suppress ordinary fresh kickoff generation and explicitly honor no-kickoff semantics without silently omitting the imported context.\n\nDecode the target backend's native JSONL and verify the full exact imported user turn bound to this attempt/native id. The server must verify that evidence or a defined authenticated host attestation, rather than trusting arbitrary proof fields. Commit port/ADV delivery visibility atomically. Artifact cleanup is retried independently after commit; a cleanup error or lost acknowledgement must not kill a verified usable target.\n\n### Expiry, recovery and observability\n\nEnforce expiry at prepare/status/bootstrap, regardless of janitor cadence. Bound unattended artifact cleanup to expiry plus a documented short grace (proposed 120 seconds while the operator is running), with startup recovery after downtime. Extend the existing session lifecycle/retention machinery with a due-only bounded sweep; do not run the whole daily telemetry prune every minute or introduce a parallel service.\n\nTrack attempt cleanup for failed/delivered as well as expired rows. Never infer that an expired pending target never ran: verify actual native persistence before ending it. A watchdog detects stale pending attempts and incomplete delivery projections using the same predicate as the lifecycle. Record typed stage/cause and safe recovery instructions without tokens, seed text or raw secrets. Preserve the initiating failure when cleanup later runs.\n\n## Acceptance matrix\n\n| Area | Required proof |\n| --- | --- |\n| Target resolution | Codex omitted/default, bare id, alias, provider prefix, each supported effort and denied model; OMP explicit/default and account-compatible routed model. Inspect, prepared record, bootstrap, config and actual native model agree. |\n| Source | Live and canonical archived Claude; archive after live-file deletion; source hash change between inspect/prepare; branch/compaction fixtures; meaningful text/binary attachments. Source native bytes unchanged. |\n| Content | Thinking/signatures excluded; high-confidence secret fixtures scrubbed before artifact/summarizer; local inert tool links retained; every loss appears in preview/final receipt. |\n| Integrity | Changed history, changed current instruction, retained marker, partial JSONL, wrong native file/session/role, wrong receipt/token, symlink, permission widening and expired artifact all fail without authorizing a target. |\n| Budget | UTF-8/multilingual and exact boundary payloads including kickoff/framing; tiny window; huge recent group; multi-chunk summary; empty/oversized/aborted summarizer; changed plan context/window requires re-fit. |\n| Retry/race | Real disposable-PG tests for concurrent same/different request keys, timeout before/after each commit, server restart, preparation conflict, failed/expired retry, and replay after delivery. Exactly one target/active owner. |\n| Continuity | Plain, plan-bound, fleet member/leader, AUTO/DRAIN/loop and valid-claim source states survive as appropriate. Live-source transfer and native-resume race are fenced. Failure rollback preserves authority; no peer state reset. |\n| Delivery/cleanup | Explicit/env/absent kickoff and no-kickoff behavior; slow startup; partial paste; exact user-turn persistence; lost POST response; projection write failure; unlink failure; child exit races; expiry and startup janitor recovery. |\n| Real user journey | Synthetic tracked Claude fixture -> Codex and OMP using default and explicit choices, interactive and headless where supported; verify actual target model, native history, owner/claims, current instruction exactly once, then native resume. No production source repurposed as canary. |\n\n## Implementation sequencing\n\nThe P-items below are deliberately serialized because most touch the same launcher, bootstrap, service and tests. Parallel execution is not assumed. No code changes occur until the owner approves implementation and chooses the execution route.\n\n## Review and rollout\n\nUse current staging/build for implementation and acceptance. Native CLI canaries use synthetic history and explicit authorized account/model routing. Keep delivered older ports natively resumable. Version the changed preparation/content semantics and refuse incompatible prepared artifacts with an actionable retry path; never degrade to an empty fresh target.\n\nBefore final shipment, run the focused matrix plus repository-required checks and the affected suite. Follow normal git-sync -> green checkpoint -> deploy. LIVE_GATE_OPS ownership must be checked before any gate action; coordinate with its single owner instead of creating a competing monitor. No forced red deploy.\n\nUpdate the canonical PostgreSQL-owned docs through docs:author, and record a superseding decision for the old authority-isolation statements once approved. Do not hand-edit generated docs or historical migration files merely to change comments; record the current schema/protocol contract in maintained docs and any genuinely needed forward migration.\n\n## Explicit limits and open decisions\n\nNo implementation approved yet. On activation, confirm the supported behavior for an actively running source: recommended default is refuse before preparation and offer orderly handoff, never implicit takeover. Confirm whether oversized single recent groups may be summarized or must fail with actionable guidance; default is clear failure until the user chooses reduced fidelity. These are design choices recorded for review, not reasons to pause this investigation.\n\nThe exact account/model chosen for future canaries is a launch-time owner choice; no provider spend or new agents were authorized for this planning task. Existing safe routing defaults and denied-model policy remain in force.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Resolve and protect the payload\n\n- **P-001** `done` P1 canonical destination and preview contract (F01,F10,F12). Extend existing SessionPortTarget/summary and launch resolvers to canonicalize Codex default/alias/provider prefix/effort and OMP default/provider/account before preparation. Use identical stable plan/launch-context/prompt inputs and effective context across inspect and bootstrap. Return the resolved destination to the launcher; do not reconstruct from picker state. Add table-driven regressions for null, bare id, aliases, provider prefixes, denied ids, route compatibility and changed-context refusal. Acceptance: the exact owner default-model failure and provider-prefix variant pass end to end through inspect -> prepare -> bootstrap with no weakening of destination checks. importance: high — note: ← WI-10001989 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` P2 complete safe portable payload (F03,F06,F08,F09,F10). Reuse sensitive-text primitives, drop thinking/signatures, preserve inert local tool relationships, classify attachments, and disclose all truncation/omission. Hash and budget the complete canonical seed including currentInstruction; specify provenance-prefix/newline normalization and version the changed transform contract. Fit atomic conversation/tool groups and globally budget bounded summarizer chunks/outputs. Add adversarial content and exact-boundary tests. Acceptance: no synthetic secret/foreign thinking escapes before artifact or summarizer, altered payload cannot retain validity, oversized content has an honest actionable outcome. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001994 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Own one recoverable attempt\n\n- **P-003** `done` P3 atomic preparation/bootstrap/retry lifecycle (F03,F04,F05,F13). Extend existing session_ports and agent-launch replay/resume reservation surfaces, with any needed forward migration. Include currentInstruction and material launch inputs in logical identity; distinguish retransmission from a linked new failed/expired retry. Reserve port/source and final hidden target ADV identity transactionally before home creation. Bind prepared -> pending once; same-state idempotence cannot change target. Authenticated exact-request replay returns the existing bootstrap receipt before progressed-state rejection. Materialize final-home paths/hooks/log_dir consistently. Acceptance: disposable-PG concurrency/barrier and lost-response tests prove one target, no mutated binding, no permanent retry dead end and no home overwrite. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001996 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `todo` P4 same-owner operational handoff (F11). Preserve WI-214387's coordination-owner continuity; extend the existing resume reservation/lease so native resume, wake and cross-backend port cannot run the owner concurrently. Load fleet membership/leadership, current registry modes, scope and valid claims before render; preserve native history and update only native/home/wake pointers. Refuse active-source conflicts before prepare/egress unless an explicit orderly handoff is supported. Rollback restores prior recoverability without clearing owner/peer authority; never resurrect expired locks. Acceptance: plain/plan/fleet leader/member/AUTO/DRAIN/loop/claim fixtures and transfer-failure/native-resume races prove one executing owner with consistent prompt/env/registry state. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Prove delivery and recovery\n\n- **P-005** `todo` P5 one kickoff and exact native delivery proof (F02,F06,F07). Consume explicit/env currentInstruction once in the managed seed; suppress ordinary fresh kickoff for a port. Define no-kickoff behavior explicitly. Parse exact target backend user-turn records and verify full canonical payload digest/length plus attempt/native binding; validate proof server-side or through a defined authenticated target-host attestation. Commit port/ADV visibility atomically; post-commit cleanup is separately recoverable. Lost acknowledgement reconciles the whole delivery, and cleanup failure does not kill a verified usable target. Acceptance: plain/env/absent kickoff, retained-marker corruption, wrong-role/file/session, partial JSONL, slow startup, child-exit and lost-response tests. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` P6 bounded expiry/crash repair and diagnostics (F07,F12). Enforce TTL at prepare/status/bootstrap; extend existing session lifecycle/retention machinery with bounded due-only cleanup, proposed <=120s grace while running and startup recovery after downtime. Reconcile all terminal cleanup residue and incomplete ADV projections, verify native persistence before ending an expired pending target, and preserve original typed failure stage/cause. Distinguish source-not-found, routing, protocol, integrity, fit, persistence and cleanup errors; no credentials or payload in telemetry. Acceptance: fake-time and disposable-PG crash-at-every-stage tests, failed unlink recovery, expired retry recovery, detector assertion and unchanged source history. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Acceptance and rollout\n\n- **P-007** `todo` P7 adversarial regression matrix and contract/docs reconciliation. Add the Acceptance matrix to the repository's Vitest/framework tests, including real disposable-PG races and an integrated launcher -> inspect/prepare -> bootstrap -> PTY -> delivery path. Ensure fixtures use actual native record shapes and assert history/current instruction/model/authority rather than marker presence. Record the approved superseding authority decision and update PostgreSQL-owned docs through docs:author. Keep historical migration files immutable unless a new forward migration is actually needed. Acceptance: focused suite and required affected checks pass; injected defects demonstrably fail their recurrence guards; no reliance on the old 962-green baseline alone. blocked-by: P-006 importance: high\n- **P-008** `todo` P8 live synthetic acceptance and normal shipment. After execution/canary authorization, use synthetic tracked Claude history to verify Codex and OMP default and explicit models, supported interactive/headless routes, current instruction exactly once, native persistence, real effective model, one owner and subsequent native resume. Exercise interrupted/retried delivery using fixture sessions. Preserve existing delivered native ports and reject incompatible old prepared transforms with linked retry guidance. Validate in current staging first; final shipment alone requires green main/deployment proof. Respect LIVE_GATE_OPS ownership, git-sync and the normal green-checkpoint/deploy pipeline; never force past red. Acceptance: recorded transcripts' hashes, model/session/owner identities, fixture cleanup, exact deployed revision and all required cases evidenced. blocked-by: P-007 importance: high\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Guarded router failover\n\n- **P-009** `todo` P9 router backend-failover contract and implementation. Reuse the proven session-port primitive rather than adding a parallel transcript copier. Trigger only from the router's authoritative provider-wall verdict, only at an idle turn boundary with no in-flight model/tool work, and only under an explicit workspace cross-provider-egress policy. Resolve a compatible target backend/model/account through the canonical launch policy; preserve the existing coordination owner, claims, fleet/loop/modes/awaits and recorded lineage; emit a durable failover decision/event. Add a one-attempt-per-wall-generation circuit breaker and refuse generic errors, latency, rate pacing, unknown health, or target-capability mismatch. Acceptance: provider-wall fixtures port exactly once; every non-wall or ambiguous signal stays on the original backend; no duplicate owner or parallel execution is created. blocked-by: P-008 importance: high\n- **P-010** `todo` P10 router failover recovery, anti-ping-pong, and live acceptance. Add deterministic target-walled/no-compatible-target behavior, bounded retry after a new wall generation, explicit operator diagnostics, and a deliberate/manual failback path rather than automatic backend oscillation. Test Claude→Codex and Codex→supported-target policy directionality, cross-provider disclosure/opt-in, restart recovery, repeated wall notifications, interrupted ports, and subsequent native resume. Run a synthetic current-build journey and normal gated shipment; verify the installed router and psu launcher share the same port contract and that the target's first successful turn preserves the source work state exactly once. blocked-by: P-009 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Reuse session ports for guarded cross-backend router failover\nDate: 2026-09-19\nOwner-directed on 2026-09-19 (session_turn:codex:01a0bb4d-713f-72d2-bc9a-2bbd2d09e353:11): execute route A and assess router reuse. The router will reuse the same repaired session-port primitive only after its end-to-end contract is proven. Automatic switching is allowed solely from an authoritative provider-wall verdict, at an idle turn boundary, under explicit cross-provider-egress policy. Generic errors, latency, pacing projections, unknown health, and in-flight turns never trigger a switch. The source coordination identity and operational state continue on the target; one wall generation can produce at most one port attempt, and failback is deliberate rather than an automatic ping-pong loop.\nRelated: P-009, P-010\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"session-popup-compaction-and-contrast-2026-08-02-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: session chat popup — compacted bottom panel, anchored mode dropdowns, sectional contrast, and the owner-owed decision shelf","status":"active","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-8a2ad6cf-a3a8-414a-801e-bcb310c569fe","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: session chat popup — compacted bottom panel, anchored mode dropdowns, sectional contrast, and the owner-owed decision shelf\nslug: session-popup-compaction-and-contrast-2026-08-02-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\nowner: su-8a2ad6cf-a3a8-414a-801e-bcb310c569fe\n---\n\n# Acceptance: session chat popup — compacted bottom panel, anchored mode dropdowns, sectional contrast, and the owner-owed decision shelf\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan shared-pot-dao-cupboard-v1-2026-09-04, authored against the as-built tree (audit pass #2 auditSeq 5, sha 8039844b, 167 citations, 26 items; passes #3–#4 (auditSeq 6–7) add P-013 with 5 code/test citations and re-audit P-004/P-012 at current blobs — 27/27 audited: 25 implemented, 2 dropped). Goal: shared-pot DAO governance (plan admission enforced fail-closed at every lifecycle door, governance rounds + voting reducer, federation, onchain bridge) and Cupboard commerce v1 (listings/catalog, publish chain with private artifacts, entitlement-checked install, provider-neutral commerce ledger with Stripe as first adapter, commerce doors), validated by a shadow pilot.\n\nDISCLOSURES (grade AGAINST these, not around them):\n(a) D-045 §4 SEAM SET — P-015 distribution, P-018 revenue-settlement, P-020 microcharge, P-021 payment-channel, P-022 evm-settlement, P-023 treasury-controls, P-024 onchain-governance-bridge are implemented + unit-tested with NO production consumer in this plan; consumer = the follow-on pilot-network activation plan (Safe treasury + L2 channel need owner-held credentials/capital). P-019 is test-only.\n(b) D-048 PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY — no ledger→delivery entitlement bridge exists (ledger Entitlement has no releaseRef; projectEntitlements has no production caller) and the production install door resolves no release chain / distribution / apply (install-door-gate-io.ts loadReleaseChain null, resolveDistribution null, apply throws). A PAID install is unreachable in production by construction; v1 claims journeys verified THROUGH the door handlers via configure() seams (configureCommerceIo, configureInstallDoorSources) whose defaults are the production honest-but-empty readers. WI-2146431 (major) filed, open, post-v1.\n(c) STRIPE WALL [inferred from WI-2145113#completion, not an owner directive] — STRIPE_SECRET_KEY / STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET are installed in no operator-public deployment (webhook route answers 503 until `wrangler secret put`); NO live Stripe call was made; purchase is driven from real signed webhook bytes through the adapter's own HMAC verification.\n(d) No wrangler build/deploy of apps/operator-public was performed in this plan; Worker routes are verified under the fake-d1 / sqlite-d1 harness.\n(e) ORG PURCHASES FAIL CLOSED — hosted + local share one rule (authorizeOrgActor, D-049) and loadOrganizations returns an empty Map (no org writer), so only INDIVIDUAL buyers complete checkout (D-046/D-047 §1). WI-2146425 (403-code org-existence oracle) is unreachable in v1, post-v1.\n(f) P-017 durable metering (recordSpendDurable) is still uncalled; prepareByocExecution is wired on the production honor path.\n(g) P-013 SHADOW MODE + PILOT VERDICT (D-050) — optional `mode` ('shadow'|'enforce') on PlanAdmissionPolicy, default 'enforce', signed inside the canonical policy bytes; shadow evaluates through the SAME assertPlanAdmission path, admits, and records the would-be refusal to a fail-open sink seam. The pilot (WI-2145116: 14 tests / 6 legs, 5-member synthetic cohort, metrics artifact packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/p013-shadow-governance-pilot.metrics.json with 10 legs) measured that enforcement CANNOT be activated in production: configurePlanAdmissionCertificateSource has zero non-test callers (definition site only), so with governance.planAdmission set and mode enforce ALL 7 lifecycle doors refuse missing-certificate (leg enforce-production-wiring 7/7 refused; shadow-production-wiring 7/7 admitted; enforce-with-bridge 7/7 admitted). Enforcement activation stays OFF per the item text and D-050; the certificate producer is P-004/P-005 scope, filed as WI-2146499 (major), follow-on plan. Pilot actors are synthetic (no users exist). Cupboard legs (submission/review/publish/browse/purchase/refund/delivery/install) are measured by CITATION to their owning committed suites (CUPBOARD_LEG_COVERAGE in the pilot file), not re-driven — a disclosed scope-down from the leader brief.\n(h) Open deferred residue: no production site builds a PRIVATE ReleaseGateInput yet; update/rollback is re-driven only at the install gate (install-door-gate.test.ts), not through the door handler; entitled-install success bytes are install-io's own suite's subject.\n(i) Dropped with reason: P-014 (pilot-conditional extras), P-026 (provider adapters deferred by D-024).\n(j) Decisions D-045..D-050 post-date activation audit #3 (plan rev 89); the completion audit is the as-built truth.\n(k) Findings filed from this plan: WI-2146431 (major), WI-2146499 (major, certificate producer), WI-2146425 (minor), WI-2146263 (detector proposal, dropped by the admission promoter).\n(l) SHIP-GATE WAIVER, DISCLOSED IN ADVANCE — plans:get shipReadiness (current tree) refuses requirement_unrealized: activation mappings M-011/M-012 (storage options) and M-020 (owner's carry-to-shipped directive) name the DROPPED items P-026 and P-014 among their targets; a dropped item can carry no code/test citation (the realization judge keeps the ordinary evidence rule for dropped targets), and activation coverage is additive by design (re-audit refused activation_coverage_regression on removing the targets). The requirements ARE realized by the remaining targets (P-025/P-027 + D-024/D-025 for storage; every other item done through the completion protocol for M-020). The ship write will therefore pass force:{ reason } waiving ONLY this code-truth check; the waiver is recorded permanently on the plan with who/why. Nothing rubric-side (vetting, independent grading, implementer verdict) is waived. Grader: treat this as a disclosed process limitation, and fail criterion code-truth-audit-spot-check only if a SAMPLED citation does not resolve.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — silent wrong answers: did the remedies land as mechanical guarantees that can fail and are actually in force, and were the plan's own refuted specs handled honestly?","status":"active","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-c2957604-71a1-4c5e-9c01-9d9a9d6f9e47","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — silent wrong answers: did the remedies land as mechanical guarantees that can fail and are actually in force, and were the plan's own refuted specs handled honestly?\nslug: silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01-acceptance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\nowner: su-c2957604-71a1-4c5e-9c01-9d9a9d6f9e47\n---\n\n# Acceptance — silent wrong answers: did the remedies land as mechanical guarantees that can fail and are actually in force, and were the plan's own refuted specs handled honestly?\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for silent-wrong-answers-2026-08-01, authored post-implementation against as-built reality. The plan targets ONE defect class in seven places: a tool returning a well-formed, plausible result carrying no signal it is wrong. Two properties make this plan unusual and both are graded here: (1) it is ordered by MECHANICAL STRENGTH, with doc/prompt last and 'explicitly not relied upon'; (2) a majority of its own item specs turned out to be instances of the target class and were refuted by measurement (D-001, D-003, D-106, D-110, D-111, D-112, D-113, D-114), making 'dropped with the measurement recorded' the honest terminal state rather than a failure. The class rubric plan-class-bugfix supplies the generic invariants; these five criteria cover what is specific to this plan.\n\nREVISION HISTORY. Rev 2 repaired what reviewer 1 (su-d939052a) found: rev 1 REPRODUCED THE TARGET CLASS AT THE GRADING LAYER, since four of five criteria were satisfiable without opening the tree and a plan record written by the implementer is itself a well-formed plausible artifact carrying no signal it is wrong. Rev 3 repairs what reviewer 2 (su-55a5bada) found, and both findings are gaps neither the author nor reviewer 1 named: (i) a cited blob proves code EXISTS, never that it is IN FORCE — a guard can be correct, falsifiable, and NOT DEPLOYED, so criterion 1 was blind to deployment; (ii) criterion 4 drew its denominator from its numerator (quantifying only over instances the implementer noticed AND recorded), so an uncaught instance was invisible by construction and the criterion could not fail. Grade against the durable record, the current tree, AND the live surface — never against this description.\n\nNON-GOAL: LIVE_GATE_OPS (the current gate verdict, gate control-plane actions, checkpoint/deploy/force operations) is explicitly excluded from this rubric; do not infer its status from missing evidence.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"spend-attribution-2026-09-04-acceptance","title":"Acceptance: goal-spend readouts name the population they measured","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-05","owner":"su-de91d1a7-8a50-4a66-8cd9-384226b9a7df","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: goal-spend readouts name the population they measured\nslug: spend-attribution-2026-09-04-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\nowner: su-de91d1a7-8a50-4a66-8cd9-384226b9a7df\n---\n\n# Acceptance: goal-spend readouts name the population they measured\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nAuthored post-implementation against as-built reality. READ THIS FIRST, grader: the plan's TITLE promises closing an 89% attribution gap, and that is NOT what shipped. D-005/D-006/D-007 ruled out both fix branches on measured evidence, so what landed is narrower: every readout of goal spend NAMES the population it measured, and a diagnostic lineage scope reports its measured overlap with the pot scope instead of being summable against it. Grade against that as-built commitment, not the title. Criterion 5 exists so 'we labelled the number honestly' can never be graded as 'we fixed attribution'; criterion 6 exists so honest labelling cannot pass while the signal itself got no better.\n\nVETTING LINEAGE. Rev 1 was critiqued in consult conv-mtnpd8zn, rev 2 in conv-mtnpi9zz, both by su-44c8a3b5 (lineage-external). THIS revision 3 IS the improvement those critiques asked for. Rev 2 had added the structured checks and CONTROL cases; revision 3 repairs what survived that pass:\n(a) Criterion 1 was a DEMONSTRATED false pass — its model said 'EVERY surface' while its method grepped only the two files the implementer edited. packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/goals.ts:117 emits spentCents bare on GoalSummaryRowBase, the row every sync client receives, outside both greps. The method is now population-scoped and names that surface explicitly so a grader must classify it rather than miss it. I verified this claim in the source before accepting it.\n(b) Criterion 3 now covers the SECOND, independently-written provenance allowlist at sync-resolver/goals.ts:333-340, which can drift from budgetSpendScope.\n(c) Criterion 5's burden is INVERTED (and its key renamed to match its new meaning): it no longer grades the absence of a false claim — a self-discharging negative that a grader who reads nothing passes identically to one who reads everything — but the PRESENCE of an explicit residual statement, and it names its harness so an out-of-hive grader can actually run the drill. The previous drill returned harness_forbidden for exactly the lineage-external graders this gate requires.\n(d) Criterion 6 is NEW and answers 'does the bar let relabelling pass as fixing?'. All five previous criteria pass on a system where the lineage scope is inert. This one can FAIL while the code is written perfectly.\n\nTWO CLASS-CRITERION NOTES, so they are rated rather than guessed. flag-on-default: this change ships NO feature flag — it is a labelling and diagnostic-scope change with no gated surface — so rate that criterion not-applicable/unknown, never fail-for-absence. gate-green-shipped: the change is committed and contained in candidate 771cee3d, but the green-checkpoint gate is red and held by another live agent (WI-212675, 113 consecutive reds, verdict a stale candidate-fossil), so promotion is outside this plan's control; grade it against observed pipeline state, as a fact about the pipeline rather than a defect in this work.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). design iteration\nslug: portal-inbox-design-2026-09-05\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-05\nupdated: 2026-09-05\n---\n# Cloud portal inbox and page design iteration\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation in progress under AUTO mode.\n\n**Next:** Complete P-001, then continue through the portal page sweep in P-002.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2145069 — Inspect the portal inbox route and improve the main content state when a sidebar item is selected, including hierarchy, spacing, selected affordances, and responsive behavior. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-2145070 — Review every portal page for the same visual system and implement the highest-value design refinements that fit the existing patterns. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2145071 — Run focused checks and browser-level verification against the local portal, then record the iteration results and next improvement target. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Requirements\n\n- When a sidebar item is selected in the inbox, the main content must make the selected context immediately clear through hierarchy, spacing, and a visible selected affordance.\n- Portal pages should share a coherent visual system for layout, typography, color, focus, and responsive behavior.\n- Design changes must preserve existing interactions and be verified against the local portal build.\n\n## Design\n\n- Reuse the portal's existing components and tokens, tightening the selected sidebar row and inbox content relationship rather than introducing a parallel navigation pattern.\n- Give the selected inbox view a clear header, supporting metadata, and an intentional empty/loading state while keeping the two-pane layout readable at narrow widths.\n- Sweep the remaining routes for the highest-impact inconsistencies and apply small, reversible refinements that reinforce the same visual language.\n\n## Background\n\nThe cloud portal's inbox is the primary work surface. Selecting an item in the sidebar should establish a strong visual connection to the main content, and the rest of the portal should feel like the same product as users move between pages.\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n## Phase 1 — Inbox selected state\n\n- **P-001** `done` Inspect the portal inbox route and improve the main content state when a sidebar item is selected, including hierarchy, spacing, selected affordances, and responsive behavior. importance: high — note: ← WI-2145069 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Portal-wide visual sweep\n\n- **P-002** `done` Review every portal page for the same visual system and implement the highest-value design refinements that fit the existing patterns. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-2145070 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification and next iteration\n\n- **P-003** `done` Run focused checks and browser-level verification against the local portal, then record the iteration results and next improvement target. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-2145071 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\nThe inbox selected state is the first concrete iteration; subsequent page improvements should reuse the same portal visual language and remain verified on the local build.\n\n### D-001 — Target the Mail app for the visible portal Inbox\nDate: 2026-09-05\nThe visible cloud portal Inbox is the Mail app surface composed from the email workspace (`@email/ui`), where the selected sidebar item is a thread and the main surface is the conversation pane. The operator Resolution Inbox is a separate embedded surface and is outside this first pass.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-byoc-delivery-acceleration-2026-09-06","title":"Acceptance BAR — BYOC delivery acceleration: earlier failure detection, resumable releases and reliable agent control","status":"active","created":"2026-09-06","owner":"su-c86de2dd-45a1-4e86-8b17-c07c4a096f7f","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — BYOC delivery acceleration: earlier failure detection, resumable releases and reliable agent control\nslug: acceptance-byoc-delivery-acceleration-2026-09-06\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-06\nupdated: 2026-10-20\nowner: su-c86de2dd-45a1-4e86-8b17-c07c4a096f7f\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — BYOC delivery acceleration: earlier failure detection, resumable releases and reliable agent control\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for gate-latency-selection-and-retry-policy-2026-09-06, authored against the as-built code on the staging checkout (plans:audit #2, 6/6 items verified with code/test citations). GOAL (plan Background): the scheduled gate run e70cd139 spent ~2h28m because (a) the 0.5 over-threshold rule widened a correct 3849/6493 related selection to the FULL 6493-file suite, (b) static import closure over-selects through hub modules, (c) a 34-minute retry pass re-ran 36 deterministic reds unconditionally, and (d) a 21-minute setup stretch could not be attributed to a phase. D-001 (recorded from the P-006 replay) rules that flake signatures are read from the vitest failure report only, attributed per file, and a broad red re-runs just the signature-bearing files. RETRY ENV SEMANTICS (unchanged contract, narrowed scope): AFFECTED_RETRY_FAILED=1 is set by the green-checkpoint and auto-enabled by interactive runs only when load1 per core exceeds 1.0 (an explicit 0/1 always wins); it still means 'a failed workspace gets one retry' — the decision layer only narrows WHAT is re-run (small red ≤ RETRY_SMALL_RED_FILES=3 files: the whole failed set; broad red with attributable signatures: the signature-bearing files only; broad deterministic red: skipped with AFFECTED_RETRY_SKIPPED reason=), and AFFECTED_RETRY_FAILED=0 disables every retry. SCOPE OF ACCEPTANCE (plan ## Now): every item is accepted on the staging checkout / current build; these paths are deliberately NOT admitted onto the frozen candidate 50ed2739 lineage and are judged by the first post-green tip cut — the class criterion gate-green-shipped and the criterion first-post-green-run-latency are therefore graded against that tip cut, not the frozen lineage, and rate `unknown` (never pass) until such a run exists; the author's acceptance verdict states whether it is conditional on them. LOG LOCATION: 21 installs share ~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs — the papercusp run is the scheduled log whose `integration root:` line ends in /papercupai-workspace/papercusp. VETTING RECORD: consult conv-mtpc76id-0000-fa27aa52e58446429468eb0d5534f0d2 (routed 04:54Z to su-44c8a3b5, below floor) expired unanswered at 05:23Z with 0 posts; re-route conv-mtpehthj-0000-ef6164a0055e48d999742b5f4dcae20b (05:58Z, excluding the expired responder and the designated grader) returned no_qualified_responder / no_live_responder; revision 2 is the author's self-vetting against meta-acceptance-rubric rev 5 (structured test bindings added, retry-env semantics stated, latency outcome added). Portal files are named BY MODULE below, never as papercusp-relative paths; the papercusp harness holds no code for this fix (its .papercusp/reports/portal-deep-link-tab-step-2026-09-06/ holds the evidence, two screenshots and probe.sh). Root cause, measured 2026-09-06 ~00:10Z: the shell's operator bridge (operatorDeepLinkTargets + useOperatorDeepLink) treated step/tab/host as pinned targets for EVERY app kind and wrote null for them on mount, clobbering the mounted page's own nuqs selector — so ?app=dev&tab=pg opened DEV on its default tab and ?app=cloud&step=connect opened Cloud on 03 Operate, while the desktop honours both. D-003 keeps `desktops` as the ONE deliberate pin (step=operate&tab=desktops) and makes every other kind defer step/tab/host to its mounted page; D-004 registers tab as owned by desktops+cloud+dev and step/host by desktops+cloud in SURFACE_PARAM_OWNERS, so a selection survives hops among owners and clears on any other hop (Home). Deployed 00:41Z as portal release zsbDNiN5utSCRh2AV2Xdk-20260906004051562 (the `current` symlink under ~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/.portal-runtime/portal/). Grader: spot-check the implementer's plans:audit #2 citations in the portal tree (the shell module's operatorDeepLinkTargets and SURFACE_PARAM_OWNERS symbols; the portal-deep-links and surface-param-isolation tests under the portal's tests directory), run those two test files there, and drive :3081 yourself with verdict (the daemon is per-session — start your own; the served release must carry the minified owners literal, grep it as in criterion 1).\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data).
