Exercise exact-credential and Unix-identity failures, stale/changed inputs, interrupted build/publicat… <!-- P-009 -->\n## Problem and measured evidence\n\nThe BYOC critical path repeatedly discovers a prerequisite during initialization, followed by a full build/package/sign/publish/repair cycle before the next check. During the 48-hour review window the scoped operation ledger recorded provision 5 succeeded/1 failed, initialization 0 succeeded/7 failed, repair 7 succeeded, and destroy 5 succeeded. These are operation statuses, not completed customer journeys. The exact status/finished_at writer was read in packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/observability-store.ts.\n\nR28's successful coherent pin-to-package span was about 43 elapsed minutes (21:08:10–21:51:17 UTC on September 6). Package/sign/audits alone took about 17 minutes (21:34:18–21:51:17) for a 2,009,027,839-byte bundle. These are one-run elapsed observations, not CPU attribution or a statistically established baseline.\n\nObserved failure classes: immutable Git credential consumption modified/deleted material or reached ambient helpers; a delivered Codex identity was revoked while a different controller identity worked; agent cwd/process-group behavior failed under the real identity; repeated runtime installs exhausted storage; an incoherent source/gitlink pin could print failure while exiting zero. Existing fixes and regression tests cover these classes, but cheap preflight did not stop them early enough in the release path.\n\nControl-plane evidence: work_items:get through code:run exceeded 25-second and outer 60-second deadlines (EI-22553216430265813). A critical-continuation write waited 20,116 ms behind another write and was explicitly not forwarded (trace7613d1f3-cb23-48b2-9107-4c285e719f88). Large, historical checkpoint bodies and mixed result envelopes required repeated recovery reads. Some projection misses were caller mistakes; this plan must not relabel them as a missing projection mechanism.\n\nReport and main evidence: /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/reports/byoc-progress-2026-09-06.md; WI-40472; EI-22540056603732931; r28 publication/evidence logs. Additional examples: EI-22547693786563362 (false-success pin helper, now fixed), EI-22551425269737147 (safe restart refusal on git-sync barrier), EI-22551870229115553 (heredoc arrow misclassified as shell redirection).\n\n## Outcomes\n\n1. Known credential, identity, storage and source-pin defects fail before a paid-host mutation or expensive release cycle.\n2. An interrupted release resumes from the last verified stage, with immutable inputs and one-use operation IDs preserved.\n3. Small control reads and unrelated critical writes remain responsive; cancellation and mutation receipts are unambiguous.\n4. Agents resume from concise current evidence while preserving every authorization, spent identifier and open commitment.\n5. Cache reuse reduces repeated preparation time while preserving trust, freshness, customer isolation and offline operation.\n6. Progress is reported as verified customer-acceptance milestones with measured queue/compute/recovery time.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Exact-path readiness.** Known credential, identity, storage and source-pin defects fail before any paid-host mutation or expensive release cycle.\n\n**R-002 — Resumable release integrity.** Interrupted releases resume from the last verified stage with immutable inputs and one-use operation IDs preserved.\n\n**R-003 — Responsive control plane.** Small control reads and unrelated critical writes remain responsive, with explicit unavailable evidence and unambiguous mutation receipts.\n\n**R-004 — Concise recovery.** Agents resume from authoritative current evidence without losing authorizations, spent identifiers or open commitments.\n\n**R-005 — Trusted artifact reuse.** Cache reuse reduces repeated preparation time while enforcing complete input identity, freshness, isolation and offline operation.\n\n**R-006 — Evidence-backed acceptance.** Progress reports distinguish build, publication, bootstrap, initialization, user acceptance, soak, cleanup and final shipment using authoritative receipts.\n\n- Extend existing release scripts/CLIs, the task/DBOS and operation journals, resource governor, result envelopes, work-item checkpoints and carry system. This plan adds no parallel workflow engine, secret store, queue service or memory system.\n- Preserve the fixed Claude/Codex/OMP gate; exact credential-generation immutability and repository scope; signatures, vulnerability/identity audits, current source provenance, customer-local execution, access isolation, one-use operation IDs and honest unknown outcomes.\n- Preserve the 1-hour real-deployment soak (D-013, replacing the literal 24-hour soak), teardown/eight-kind census, billing commitments and final green-release requirement. This acceleration plan does not reduce BYOC acceptance.\n- Respect the capless feedback-governor model. Proposed latency targets below are acceptance criteria, not static concurrency/pool limits. Raising timeouts, queue limits or resource caps is not an accepted durable fix.\n- Separate an already-fixed-but-not-deployed case from an unimplemented defect. Reproduce on current build before editing; coordinate any rollout through the existing owner. LIVE_GATE_OPS remains exclusively with its registered owner.\n- Keep the current GCP alpha/deferred-hosted/AWS/Azure scope. Existing D-298 ordering is retained; dependency changes need an explicit reviewed decision.\n- New behavior affecting agent instructions must follow the existing persona render/edit runbook and canonical source path. No generated prompt copies are edited.\n\n## Design\n\nThe implementation composes the existing release/task/operation journals, credential and identity probes, work-item read projection, MCP governor admission, carry receipts, artifact-boundary cache and milestone views. Each wave adds a narrow adapter or guard at the existing seam, records a verifiable receipt, and keeps the accepted dependency graph authoritative. Baseline evidence gates edits; independent read-path and write-path lanes may proceed only after P-001 and remain disjoint under file locks. Resume and reuse consume the same immutable source/gitlink/policy identity and operation ledger, while reporting derives milestones from those receipts rather than authored summaries.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-002 | P-005, P-009 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-003, P-004, P-009 | tree |\n| R-004 | P-007, P-009 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-006, P-009 | tree |\n| R-006 | P-008, P-009 | deployed |\n\n## Reuse and ownership\n\nBYOC plan byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22 retains P-309/P-314 content and artifact boundaries; this plan owns orchestration/cache integration and does not create duplicate implementation lanes for those requirements.\n- agent-tooling-token-efficiency-2026-06-25 and tool-call-batching-wrappers-2026-06-21 are shipped. Reuse their composites, schemas and instrumentation; do not reopen finished items.\n- mcp-proxy-reconnect-herd-2026-08-25 and agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02 are shipped. This plan concerns demonstrated continuation/read-path residue, not reimplementation of those mechanisms.\n- agent-managed-compaction-2026-07-01 contains existing carry work. Check its current work-item ownership before changing shared files and extend its mechanisms.\n- Existing dispatch-level result-projection/apply.ts already implements projection and miss disclosure. Respect its distinction between absent data and pre-projection truncation. Existing trimmed-contract.ts requires a covered/exempt decision for payload shapers.\n- Current work_items/get.ts already contains a shared call deadline and cache. Its deadline tests exist. Trace queue wait, handler execution, enrichment, serialization and deployed version before proposing a fix.\n- Relevant existing files include packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/get.ts and its tests, apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.ts and tests, apps/operator/lib/release/workspace-host-publication-manifest-cli.ts, scripts/publish-workspace-host-artifacts.mjs, the desktop sidecar build/audit scripts, and the existing workspace-host initialization/canary/credential modules.\n\n## Overlap review\n\nReviewed the three plans returned by the creation dedup gate. goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 already owns unfinished-request tracking, stale-carry reconciliation, brief delivery, compression fidelity and context freshness. Reuse that plan's P-005 through P-011; this new plan only integrates and verifies BYOC release/task/operation receipts against that work. It does not implement a competing carry or agent-behavior system.\n\nbyoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01 owns hosted deployment, multi-cloud and commercial deferrals; those outcomes remain out of scope here. coord-delivery-residual-gaps-2026-07-11 has built its deafness/enrollment/advisory work and is awaiting acceptance; it is a reuse point, not a new implementation lane.\n\nThis is a distinct plan for measured delivery feedback, exact-path preflight, release resumption/caching and control-tool performance. Its cross-plan carry dependency is explicit. Existing artifact/content work stays with the BYOC plan.\n\n## Execution waves\n\nWave 1: establish the bounded baseline/reuse map, then run independent early-preflight and tool read/write reliability lanes. Shared proxy files stay in one implementation lane under file locks.\n\nWave 2: integrate the preflight with resumable release execution; then connect concise carry/receipts and measured artifact reuse.\n\nWave 3: integrate truthful milestones/dependencies and run the end-to-end failure/recovery and performance comparison. Implementation lanes must prove their own behavior before the combined comparison.\n\nDo not add agents to a serialized critical path merely to increase headcount. Parallel execution is permitted only for independent work with explicit dependency edges and disjoint file claims.\n\n## Proposed acceptance targets\n\n- Preflight: every seeded known failure class is rejected before any provider mutation; a valid fixture passes using the exact selected artifact, identity and credential generation. No secret material appears in logs, task bodies or reports.\n- Tool reads: for a defined representative replay cohort, 1–10 item summary reads target p95 ≤2 seconds end to end, while unavailable/timeout responses preserve the distinction from an empty result. Detailed history is explicitly requested and paged.\n- Critical writes: a slow completion on an unrelated work item cannot consume another session's entire continuation deadline. Same-entity ordering, conflict checks and audit/forwarding receipts remain correct.\n- Resume: interrupt at every stage, including response-loss after a provider accepted a request; resume performs zero duplicate mutations or redundant already-verified artifact builds.\n- Carry: at least 50% fewer routine coordination/carry bytes in the replay cohort, with zero loss of ownership, approvals, current task/operation identity, spent IDs, walls and evidence references.\n- Artifact reuse: demonstrate at least 30% reduction in repeated preparation elapsed time for identical pinned inputs in a controlled comparison. This is a proposed target, not a promised speedup; every required trust/freshness check must still pass.\n- Reporting: build, publication, bootstrap, full agent initialization, DesktopSession/user acceptance, soak, cleanup and final shipment are individually evidence-backed. A green build alone cannot advance the later stages.\n\n## Validation method\n\nUse existing test frameworks and current-build acceptance surfaces. Run the existing fixed regressions as the starting control; add integration tests only where the cross-stage mechanism is missing. Exercise real Git credential behavior and actual Unix identity boundaries where possible; do not replace them with mocked booleans.\n\nCapture per-stage elapsed time, queue wait, handler/enrichment/serialization time, retries, recomputation, tool calls and injected bytes using existing task/tool telemetry. Compare equivalent source/artifact/credential conditions; document policy/tool/database versions and resource-governor admission. Do not infer CPU saturation from load or assign a whole-two-day time share from one sample.\n\nPasses require both failure controls and a positive path. A timeout or missing artifact is unavailable evidence, not success. Do not rerun a spent cloud operation to improve the benchmark. Use isolated current-build fixtures for destructive failure drills; reserve final green-main verification for shipment.\n\n## Review decisions\n\nThe proposed order is preflight and control-tool reliability first, resumable execution and concise carry second, artifact optimization and combined acceptance third. The exact tool latency and speedup targets should be confirmed against the baseline; any proposed change to these targets must be explicit in the review record.\n\nOwner authorization is recorded in D-002. This is a new cross-surface remediation plan prompted by fresh September 6 evidence; existing shipped mechanisms remain dependencies and reuse points. Activation must start only genuine residual work after current-build validation, without duplicating already-completed fixes.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline and reuse\n\n- **P-001** `done` Validate the observed slow/failing paths on current build and create a bounded baseline using existing task/tool/operation telemetry. Acceptance: kill/restart between every stage and lose a response after provider acceptance; resumption executes zero duplicate provider mutations and does not redo an already-verified immutable artifact stage; false-success exit/marker mismatches fail closed; the existing positive BYOC journey uses this maintained path. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000403 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Add measured content-addressed reuse to the existing release stages. Their full UID/storage/paid-host matrix, provider response-loss integrity, global latency/write receipts, native warm/cold pickup and context targets remain unverified; canonical manual:none acceptance checks and all evidence gaps remain unchanged. This plan remains draft; no items are promoted or started before that review. It creates no additional acceptance gate for the already-authorized BYOC shipment mission. Existing BYOC requirements and AUTO continuity remain intact. Generic brief/request/carry/freshness work belongs to goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06; this plan integrates BYOC receipts and verifies the result. Existing BYOC content/artifact implementation stays in its current plan. Revalidate current-build residuals and shared-file ownership before activation; do not reopen shipped tooling plans or duplicate already-owned fixes. Numeric latency/reuse/carry targets are proposed acceptance criteria for review, not hard resource/concurrency settings or guaranteed forecasts.\nRelated: P-001, P-007, P-009\n\n### D-002 — Owner authorization supersedes review-only hold\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDate: 2026-09-06\nAvi's current owner directive explicitly authorizes implementation of this plan now, from start to finish, in this session. This supersedes D-001's review-only hold while preserving its scope boundaries: no extra BYOC shipment gate, reuse existing release/coordination/carry/artifact surfaces, retain credential, signature, audit, secret-isolation, dependency-ordering, soak, cleanup and final-green requirements, and do not duplicate work already owned by the existing BYOC and agent-briefs plans. The nine plan items may be activated in dependency order; numeric targets remain measured acceptance criteria, not static limits.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-003 — External implementation and acceptance evidence are hard gates, not prose dependencies\nDate: 2026-09-07\nRuling: BYOC P-006 and P-007 may be promoted with the plan, but must remain non-claimable until the external implementation they adapt is either terminal-success with evidence or explicitly handed off by an authenticated source-plan owner. Dialog answers are not indexed by sessions:search (EI-13472), so this Decision is the durable record.\n\n### D-014 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: amend-bbdb0863e5fedbacf2e839d0\nRequest-Hash: cb0def48b34a4a17b03e3de769062753e1493afcd1dd5d80057980b79d1d7f35\nActor: su-1622829b-5b04-4074-a03a-90f8eb5e24ca\nReason: Owner decision byoc-delivery-acceleration-2026-09-06#D-013 (2026-10-20): R-006 requires a 1-hour real-deployment soak instead of the literal 24-hour soak. Revised per outside-lineage objection thread-post:1192014 / 1192008: model, method and driftMarkers all state the 1-hour soak; plan bullets amended at plan v62/v63 to cite D-013; check files unchanged.\nApproved-By: su-49853576-c6fe-40f6-bd2a-0ece61034494\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1192031\nApproved-At: 2026-10-20T17:29:38.800Z\nRubric revision: 10 → 11\nSubject plan revision: 63 → 64\nChanged BARs: R-006\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-015 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: amend-19d682ec991f8cc06d8168ae\nRequest-Hash: 4f13a6cebd02f86133048727b0585393b780e874dce121c98fa91a79b6d2e84e\nActor: su-1622829b-5b04-4074-a03a-90f8eb5e24ca\nReason: Vetting consult conv-mvgzrsjy (su-1edc0b07, post 1192086) attested rev 11 and asked for non-hash method precision before grading: name the authoritative ledger/receipt stages, require a QUALIFYING soak under the workspace-host soak policy, and cite the new 59-minute floor controls. Nothing here is startable until the parent plan ships and the owner activates this plan. Every item traces to a parent decision: D-053 (Hyperdrive deferred), D-054 (wallet attestation follow-up), D-055 (commerce off the hive log in v1), D-056 (GitHub's role), D-057 (hive log retention).\n\n**Next:** Owner: activate this plan after shared-pot-dao-cupboard-v1-2026-09-04 ships; the parent's P-043 retention model is the prerequisite for every item here.\n\n## Background\n\nThe parent plan settled, on 2026-09-06, that the hive peer log (Hypercore over Hyperswarm) is authoritative for governance and distribution only; commerce facts live behind the Worker plus chain finality (D-055). The owner adopted Hyperdrive/Hyperblobs over the existing swarm as the direction for artifact bytes but kept it deferred (D-053). GitHub is permitted for identity, key proofs and public mirrors, never for governance state, the commerce record or money (D-056). The dev-box hive store measured 46 GB with no retention (D-057, WI-2147374); the parent's P-043 owns the retention model and must land before any of the items below add new kinds to the log.\n\n## Phase 1 — Bytes and availability (D-053)\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Hyperdrive/Hyperblobs provider adapter behind the ArtifactStore seam: one core per artifact, publisher seeds, buyers replicate over existing swarm connections; providerId + opaque locator per D-035/D-040; the P-025 Merkle root remains the only content address; private releases stay client-side encrypted (D-022). Must respect the per-kind retention model from the parent's P-043. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Hosted Node pin node that joins the hive swarm and seeds published cores for availability (Workers cannot join a swarm); permitted under D-052; owner-gated deploy like the parent's P-038. blocked-by: P-001 importance: normal\n\n## Phase 2 — Identity (D-054, D-056)\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Wallet-binding proof published in the identity gist beside the device key, and a federated attestation on the hive member record, so a seller peer can verify a buyer's wallet binding without the Worker (the D-054 follow-up). Free-tier GitHub suffices; peers verify with their own token. importance: normal\n\n## Phase 3 — Discoverability and federation (D-055, D-056)\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Public catalog repo mirror of signed listing manifests (a Homebrew-tap style GitHub repo) for discoverability and web browsing; the hive log stays authoritative for listings; the mirror is derived, never written by hand. importance: low\n- **P-005** `todo` Federated commerce-event and settlement-proof stream on the hive peer log with sparse replication and epoch rotation designed in from the start, for when surviving without the Worker becomes a requirement (reverses the v1 choice in D-055 deliberately, with the retention model in place). blocked-by: P-001 importance: low — note: Design bound by D-002: no per-call receipts on the log — one superseding cumulative voucher per channel plus one per-epoch usage summary with a Merkle root; receipts kept locally by both parties and pruned after the dispute window.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — This plan is a container for deferred work, not a commitment\nDate: 2026-09-06\nItems here were recommendations the owner chose to defer on 2026-09-06 (parent D-053: \"yes lets go with this, but we'll keep this deferred\"). Recording them as todo items in the parent plan would block its ship gate; recording them only in prose would lose them. This plan holds them with their parent-decision provenance until the owner activates it.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Receipts never ride a federated log per call: the per-epoch rollup design that binds P-005 (owner challenge 2026-09-06 01:09Z)\nDate: 2026-09-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-06 01:09Z interactive, verbatim] \"the hyperswam log stores every receipt from every user.  that would be gigantic!!!! look how many tool calls we make alone on this machine\". The leader withdrew per-call receipts on the log at 01:11Z (dev box, measured 01:10Z: 333,463 tool calls/24h, 1,908,969/7d, 431 distinct agents/24h, 15 GB invocation ledger) and replaced it with the rollup below; parent D-055 then took ALL commerce off the hive log for v1, so this design binds only if P-005 is activated.\n\nDesign (binding for P-005): a receipt is exchanged over the direct buyer↔seller swarm connection, signed by both sides, and kept LOCALLY by both parties until the channel settles and the dispute window closes; then it is pruned. The federated stream carries only (a) channel open/close, (b) ONE cumulative voucher row per channel that supersedes the previous row — parent D-014: the latest voucher is the whole balance, receipts are evidence not state — and (c) ONE usage summary per settlement epoch holding call count, total and a Merkle root over that epoch's receipts. The Merkle root makes pruning safe: either party proves one receipt's inclusion in a claimed total without anyone storing the receipts (the same trick as the parent's P-025 content address). Storage scales with open channels × settlement epochs, never with calls: at the dev box's rate a third of a million rows a day becomes a few hundred. Prerequisites: the parent's P-043 retention model (sparse replication + epoch rotation) and the parent's storage tier table (the decision recorded beside D-058 on 2026-09-06). Any per-call kind proposed for the log fails review.\nRelated: P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"desktop-release-shared-project-history-2026-09-06","title":"Publish desktop release for Linux, Windows, and macOS with shared project history","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Publish desktop release for Linux, Windows, and macOS with shared project history\nslug: desktop-release-shared-project-history-2026-09-06\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-06\nupdated: 2026-09-18\n---\n\n## Now\nConnect the shared Project History system to Papercusp release documentation, then cut, verify, and publish the next desktop release.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000248 — Integrate and verify shared Project History on the release page with focused regression tests. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000249 — Freeze the release source and build verified Linux, Windows, and macOS GUI and Server artifacts. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000250 — Publish platform builds and release documentation; verify public downloads, updater feed, and history interactions. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Scope and acceptance\nUse the existing release:cut, uploader, release registry, and history publisher. Preserve the permanent updater address; publish artifacts before the update manifest. Build Linux, Windows, and macOS GUI and Server artifacts from one immutable commit using the existing channel. Verify provenance, identity scrubbing, signing, platform builds, public downloads and the updater feed. Reuse the shared Project History v2 assembler and ProjectHistoryView through a thin release adapter, scoped to each release's recorded plan/work-item set. Preserve downloads and readable static detail links. Keep source edits in canonical staging under locks; the maintained cutter may prepare its dedicated isolated build checkout. Leave commits and pushes to git-sync.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Published desktop builds.** Release 0.0.19 alpha provides Linux, Windows and macOS GUI and Server downloads from one verified green source, with matching version/provenance and valid updater signatures.\n\n**R-2 — Shared release history.** The release page opens the generalized Project History v2 model in ProjectHistoryView, exposing recorded plans, completed work items and verification evidence while excluding later completions from older releases.\n\n**R-3 — Reliable public access.** Public files pass identity gates; downloads and static detail links remain usable without JavaScript, and shared plan dialogs work from self-hosted assets. Public readback verifies uploaded bytes before reporting publication success.\n\n## Design\nExtend record-release-cli with a thin adapter from hydrated release records to the shared plan-parser Project History v2 assembler. Attach only release-listed work items, preserve unplanned work in an explicit group, and do not infer landed commits from tree stamps. Bundle ProjectHistoryView with esbuild for static hosting; mount one shared viewer per selected release from generated JSON, retaining static fallback details. Extend the existing publisher to upload and verify the shared viewer assets before index.html. Exercise schema, release membership, redaction, empty data, fallback navigation and browser interactions. R1/source-composition approval and formal audit remain unwaived; nothing published.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-022 — Compose D021 dependency and installer repairs through the existing pinned native-source seam\nDate: 2026-09-09\nMeasured: 2026-09-09 fire148, papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/windows-source-repair.js admits only src-tauri/src/*.rs and verifies that subtree; build-windows-cross.sh applies it before copying the frozen release Cargo.toml/lock. Owner composition answer and full source/activation review remain required.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-023 — Separate immutable extraction failure from a pinned post-start permissions witness\nDate: 2026-09-09\nMeasured: 2026-09-09 fire164 strict fullmode verdict failed only PostgreSQL0744->0755; packaged/installed GUI and Server files/directories and all runtime bytes matched. Retain /tmp/p002-d021-installed-continuation164/verdict.json unchanged and never recolor it. Check all bytes, membership, links and full permissions including rw/specialbits/directories. UI/stability, full formal source/activation review, applicable green evidence and Avi-only R1 remain required; this decision neither answers R1 nor authorizes mixed-source publication.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-024 — Keep native acceptance phases and recurring guest-crash evidence separate; do not repeat failed CPU-profile treatments\nDate: 2026-09-12\nMeasured September12: functional2 mouse navigation at15:15:58UTC positively displayed WORKSPACE PULSE and SPAWN ACCOUNT POOL in the exact installed eddbd6e7 GUI. Subsequent preflight found PID2320 absent. Prior passes remain historical evidence after a reboot, not a current-boot liveness claim. P003 remains after P002; no LIVE_GATE_OPS.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-025 — Avi answers R-1: rebuild 0.0.19 from green main e66be3c4, artifacts only, all three platforms\nDate: 2026-09-15\nThe owner-only R-1 source-composition approval that D-024 recorded as \"required and unanswered\" is now ANSWERED. Owner Avi, interactive turn 2026-09-15 (verbatim ask: \"cut a new release of our windows linux and mac builds off of the latest green main... Continue getting 0.0.19 built and released\"), then three explicit dialog answers:\n\n1. SOURCE (R-1 approved): rebuild 0.0.19 from GREEN MAIN e66be3c4ff7b00d91d44334d7299464af47b7aeb. This satisfies R-1's \"one verified green source\" and matches the standing owner directive of 2026-08-13 (\"the cuts should only come from the latest main gate not from staging\"). Avi was told before answering that e66be3c4 is 9 days old and 2,933 commits behind staging, and chose it anyway. Staging was offered and declined.\n\n2. REBUILD AUTHORIZATION (D-024 fence lifted, NARROWLY): Avi selected \"Rebuild artifacts only\". D-024's \"No new installer/rebuild to replace completed phase evidence\" is lifted SOLELY to re-produce the release binaries, which no longer exist. It is NOT lifted for the completed Windows native acceptance phases: native148 / repack154 / finalize155 remain terminalPASS and MUST NOT be rerun or rebuilt (EI-22799680200953558). No config reset, no baseline restoration, no process kills, no signal work. All prior receipts, dumps and crash evidence stay preserved.\n\n3. PLATFORM SCOPE: all three — Linux, Windows and macOS (GUI + Server roles), with zig and llvm-lipo to be installed first so the macOS universal binary can be produced.\n\nWHY A REBUILD IS NECESSARY AT ALL (the fact that inverted this lane):\nMeasured 2026-09-15T16:2xZ by su-4163e120: all 7 artifact paths named by the surviving receipt /tmp/p002-linux-mac-configured-email-audits.json are ABSENT from disk. The Linux three were under /mnt/data/cargo-target/.papercusp-target-slots/dev2/release/bundle/ (a rotating target slot, since reclaimed) and the macOS four under /tmp/papercusp-relcut-0019-alpha-e66-current/ (also reclaimed). No 0.0.19 binary exists anywhere under /tmp (maxdepth 4) or /mnt/data/offload, where the newest artifacts are 0.0.18. The RECEIPTS survive (2678B and 5333B) and /tmp still holds 1028 p002-* entries, so /tmp was not wiped wholesale — the binaries specifically were reclaimed, with /mnt/data at 100% capacity. D-024's fence was written to protect completed-phase evidence while those binaries existed; the evidence survives and the binaries do not, so P-003 publication is impossible without re-producing them.\n\nALSO ESTABLISHED, correcting a blocker prior holders could not clear:\nR-1's exact wording was reported unlocatable by su-5115b977 and su-3b77bc46, who searched the Decisions section and the rubrics. It is in neither. It is in this plan's ## Requirements section: \"R-1 — Published desktop builds. Release 0.0.19 alpha provides Linux, Windows and macOS GUI and Server downloads from one verified green source, with matching version/provenance and valid updater signatures.\" Future readers: look in ## Requirements, not Decisions.\n\nSEPARATE AND STILL OPEN (not waived by this decision): the acceptance rubric for this plan does not exist (rubrics:list { subjectPlan } returns count 0), so bar_snapshot_rubric_missing / bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty continue to block plans:set-plan-status → shipped. That blocks marking the PLAN shipped; it does not block cutting or publishing artifacts. Authoring that rubric remains agent-actionable.\n\nRelated: P-002, P-003, D-016 (cut only an exact committed source), D-024 (the fence this narrowly lifts).\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-026 — The operator History route reads Postgres directly and serves PAGES; the committed-artifact CLI path is unchanged\nDate: 2026-09-16\nThe operator's `GET /api/harness/:slug/project-history` no longer shells out to `papercusp project-history generate`. It now uses a `ProjectHistoryProvider` backed directly by Postgres plus one grep-scoped `git log`, and it serves a PAGE (`?limit`/`?offset`, default 20, hard cap 100) with a `page:{count,total,offset,limit,hasMore}` block instead of the whole archive.\n\nWHY, with the measurements that forced it:\n\n1. The old route could never load at all on `papercusp`. The CLI shells a bare `ptool` once per plan/work-item read and walks the entire commit graph with `--name-only`: ~290s against a 90s child budget and a 120s route watchdog. No budget bump fixes that shape — the operator OWNS the database it was spawning hundreds of subprocesses to reconstruct.\n\n2. PAGINATION IS PART OF THE FIX, NOT A SEPARATE NICETY, and this is the part worth carrying to other lanes. The obvious remedy — a durable cache plus out-of-band generation — is unbuildable here, and one query says so: `papercusp` holds 1,882 plans carrying 36MB of plan markdown plus 27MB of items/decisions BEFORE work items and commits, i.e. a ~63MB JSON document. A latency fix (cache, precompute, background job) PRESERVES the payload; when the payload is the defect it converts a timeout into a hang and moves the failure somewhere harder to see. The tab would still be broken and it would have looked like the fix landed.\n\n3. Rubric-template plans (`template='rubric'`) and archived plans are excluded AT THE READ. Acceptance rubrics are plan-BACKED for storage only — the grading instrument, not delivered work. Seventeen of them polluting a published archive is what EI-20475585438015488 had to clean by hand; excluding them at the read stops it recurring.\n\nWHAT DID NOT CHANGE, deliberately — this is the cross-lane part:\n- `papercusp project-history generate` (the CLI) and the `system:project-history-refresh` routine KEEP the committed-artifact path exactly as it is. That implementation is correct for ITS consumer: a hive's public repo, which must build with no operator and no database. Only the operator route switched to direct PG.\n- `assembleProjectHistory` is untouched as the single definition of what a v2 document IS. The route supplies its documented I/O boundary rather than reimplementing it — notably, it does NOT duplicate the WI-39831 loud-refusal invariant (a provider resolving 0 work items for N referenced ids must fail, never degrade to evidence-free plan-ledger stubs).\n\nSEPARATE, SHARED FIX in `libs/generic/plan-parser`: `generateProjectHistory` called `parsePlan` INSIDE a `.filter()` callback, re-parsing each plan's markdown once per work item carrying `planSlugs`. Measured on a real 20-plan page: one parse per plan for the whole page = 87ms, while the filter did 20 x 139 = 2,780 parses ~ 12.1s. `referencedWorkItems` now returns `{ slug, ids }` so the slug it already parses is reused. The derivation is byte-identical, so no value can differ; every consumer benefits, including the CLI path above. Page latency went from 15.1s to 1.05s for 20 plans, and the curve is now flat in page size rather than superlinear.\n\nGENERALISABLE: when the plan is 'make the slow thing faster', measure the PAYLOAD's size before building the machinery. Cost of asking here was one query (~200ms); cost of not asking would have been the whole cache implementation plus a false completion report at the end of it.\n\n### D-027 — A build-gate config fix cannot be hand-propagated into a frozen release root — it must travel by commit\nDate: 2026-09-18\nDate: 2026-09-18. Measured this turn, read-only. [self-imposed ruling — NOT an owner directive.]\n\nCONTEXT. The 0.0.21-alpha cut (22:05Z, sourceSha 0df65de9) ran ~65min and was refused by the assembled-bundle GITLEAKS gate before any platform leg, so no artifacts exist. The finding is a VERIFIED FALSE POSITIVE on vendor bytes: generic-api-key matching `secretStream,this.signature=new ` in minified serve.mjs — the jws package's SignStream constructor (node_modules/jws/lib/sign-stream.js), where minification removes the separator so the detector reads an identifier+assignment as a key/value pair. No credential is on that line. Fix authored in the SHARED tree at papercusp/papercusp-desktop/bin/release-gitleaks.toml: one [[rules.allowlists]] block, condition=AND, targetRules=[generic-api-key], paths=[serve.mjs], regexTarget=\"match\" (deliberately NOT \"line\" — per that file's own comment at :111-114, allowlisting the multi-megabyte generated LINE would blanket-exempt it and hide a real credential).\n\nFALSIFIABILITY PROVEN, and this is the load-bearing result rather than the green: a synthetic probe OUTSIDE the tree showed (A) the jws expression alone => exit 0 suppressed, and (B) the same expression PLUS a real-looking api_key => exit 1 STILL CAUGHT. A full re-scan of both real roots with the edited config then returned sidecar exit=0 and resources exit=0. Suppressing the alarm and blinding the gate are indistinguishable from the exit code alone; only (B) tells them apart.\n\nTHE RULING. The obvious shortcut — copy the fixed config into the frozen papercusp-relcut-0020 root and re-fire immediately — is REFUSED BY THE CUTTER, measured, and must not be retried:\n1. release-local.sh:2118 reads `--config \"$ORCHESTRATOR_HERE/release-gitleaks.toml\"`, and ORCHESTRATOR_HERE (:114) is the running script's OWN directory. So the cut executes the FROZEN ROOT's copy; a shared-tree-only fix is inert for a relcut cut. That premise is real.\n2. But resolveCutRoot (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release/cut.ts:369-374) refuses ANY dirty worktree with `root_not_clean`. Under reuseSeedVersion the ONLY tolerated dirt is release-local.sh's own version-field rewrites in RELEASE_RESUME_VERSION_PATHS, validated byte-exactly against expectedVersionFile (:185-198); any other path fails as `desktop status contains non-cutter path`. A copied-in bin/release-gitleaks.toml hits exactly that.\n3. Advancing the submodule gitlink instead does not help: validateReleaseResumeResidue accepts ` M papercusp-desktop` only WITH desktopHeadMatches=true (:171-174), i.e. only when the gitlink still matches the frozen superproject.\n\nSo the frozen root must BE a committed sha. That is the provenance guarantee the cleanliness check exists to hold, not an incidental nicety — and it applies to build-gate config exactly as to shipped source, even though this file is never bundled and changes zero shipped bytes. The argument that gate config is exempt because it does not ship is CORRECT about bytes and IRRELEVANT to the mechanism.\n\nTHE SANCTIONED ROUTE (also the standing source policy: cut only from the latest green main): let git-sync commit the shared-tree fix, let the superproject gitlink bump ride with it, let green-checkpoint FF main, then re-point/re-prepare papercusp-relcut-0020 at that new green main and fire with the NEW sourceSha. dev:pipeline_position for the path reports blockedOn='committed' with dirtyUncommitted=true — commit is the single lever. Helpfully, the relcut's desktop submodule origin is the LOCAL shared checkout (/home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercusp/papercusp-desktop), not GitHub, so propagation needs no remote round-trip; and the green gate cuts its candidate from LOCAL staging and never fetches, so a blocked push to the submodule's protected main does not stall this.\n\nDO NOT, in a hurry: copy the config into the relcut root; broaden the allowlist to regexTarget=\"line\"; patch audit-release-bundle.py (it is correct, and separately verified); or edit src-tauri/sidecar, which is regenerated build output (release-local.sh:2101) so an edit there is erased by the next staging step and the identical gate refuses again ~65min later.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06","title":"Reliable agent briefs and long-horizon context: delivery, continuity and measured behavior","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: \"Reliable agent briefs and long-horizon context: delivery, continuity and measured behavior\"\nslug: goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-06\nupdated: 2026-10-10\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-10, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_stale. Next repair: Re-prove the current spec revision; superseded proof does not cover it. (R-11). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nExisting goal-agent behavior plan expanded with Avi's generic portfolio/lifecycle directive and six audit-derived items (P-021–P-026). The plan now covers concurrent multi-plan stewardship, independent current-window grading, trusted spend control, coordination/recovery efficiency, explicit GOAL work-container selection, and terminal closure evidence. Original continuity/history work and acceptance obligations remain in scope.\n\n**Next:** Re-run the activation audit for the materially expanded scope, then use the plan as the single generic goal-agent behavior program: complete baseline/effect measurement, implement the six added behavior controls, and certify selection → delegated execution → verification → independent regrade → owner report.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000447 — Reconcile the complete source conversation, current source/runtime generations, stopped-goal constraints, existing work-item ownership and both systems' intended contracts. Preserve controlled reprod… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000448 — Record a complete baseline against the current GOAL rubric and independent system delivery/history checks. Pin actual subject/window/generation and consumed payloads; retain a comparable baseline for… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000449 — Preserve each unfinished owner request across acknowledgements, interruptions, handoffs and compaction. Reuse WI-10000319. A request clears only through a matching substantive delivered answer, expli… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000450 — Reconcile current specs, decisions, checkpoints, retractions and stop conditions before using older carry summaries. Account for actual outer-envelope content, keep omitted obligations recoverable, avoid suppress… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000452 — Connect the existing bounded descendant-history compiler to production plan reads, plan launch/context bundles and plan-scoped leader context using WI-10000321. Combine the plan's own history with re… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000453 — Complete goal-level history and injection now, superseding the earlier P-020 deferral as directed by Avi. Include the goal's own history, related plans and their items, plus directly attached items; … <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000454 — Complete capture-to-compression fidelity at work-item, plan and goal levels. Reuse checkpoint learned/learnedLevel, effort threads and the shared extractor/advisory. Reuse WI-2142387 for new-post notification, then extend relevant plan/goal changes through existing event/generation and delivery… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000456 — Strengthen supervisory follow-through using the existing agenda: expose the next applicable prioritization, delegation, verification or reporting action and test its canonical effect. Preserve curren… <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000457 — Verify the existing diagnostic-tripwire repair EI-22512669283419131 through the full consuming stop path. Exercise unmeasured estimates, genuinely measured breaches, agent-supplied external metrics, … <!-- P-013 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000458 — Integrate the registered system and supervisory repairs, verify all required production consumers and final delivery paths, and record each root cause, recurrence guard and outcome. Preserve earlier … <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000459 — Run matched system and agent-effect measurements after integration, using the two active goal-mode-e2e performance criteria plus the complete current rubric. Capture exact consumed context, equivalen… <!-- P-014 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000460 — Obtain independent acceptance of system correctness and the measured behavior report, audit all required outcomes, and verify containing deployment for this cycle and the retained original brief plan… <!-- P-004 -->\n## Source and scope\n\nThis scope retains the original continuous grading mandate and adds the owner-directed delivery, request continuity and complete hierarchical-history repairs. Source conversations and constraints are recorded below.\n\n## Objective\n\nMake the brief/task-list system reliably deliver correct, current obligations, and make long-horizon context carry the relevant history of a work item, plan or goal into the actual consumer. Then measure whether the improved system helps agents resume correctly and complete the intended supervisory cycle.\n\nAssess two things separately: system correctness from canonical source through final delivered payload, and agent behavior after verified exposure. A passing compiler test does not establish delivery; delivery does not establish agent follow-through; observed follow-through without matched controls does not establish causation.\n\n## The five promised improvements\n\n| Original point | Concrete outcome | Tasks |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| 1. Preserve unanswered owner requests | Acknowledgements do not clear the requested deliverable; recovery retains it until a matching delivered answer, cancellation or supersession. | P-005, P-011 |\n| 2. Prefer current evidence to stale carry | Current specs, decisions, corrections, completions and stop conditions govern continuation; old contradictory notes are marked superseded. | P-006, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011 |\n| 3. Strengthen supervisory follow-through | The next applicable prioritization, delegation, verification or reporting obligation is delivered and evaluated against its actual effect. | P-007, P-012, P-014 |\n| 4. Verify the tripwire repair end to end | Diagnostic estimates cannot masquerade as measured spend or trigger an unmeasured shutdown; genuine measured breaches still work. | P-013 |\n| 5. Measure whether the changes help | Matched, explicitly exposed runs measure lost obligations, repeated investigation, correct resumptions, verified work and recovery cost. | P-002, P-014, P-004 |\n\n## Verified baseline and gaps\n\nCurrent-build focused runs 2ef2c7da-5790-4c12-911a-7b63ed9c3162 and bed5aa77-1a8a-4515-8870-87f9731c4bae passed. They exercise obligation evaluation, providers, reminders, history compilation and existing read/render seams. They do not cover the full failure cases below. Controlled probes and source evidence are recorded on WI-10000243 comments 199493 and 199500 and the linked fixes. No field failure rate or new behavioral improvement has been established.\n\n| Finding | Required repair or preservation | Existing record |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Any later assistant message sets continuation answered=true. | Separate acknowledgement/response presence from resolved owner-request state and verified delivery. | WI-10000319 |\n| The outer orientation can discard a provider-generated due task and recovery link while the inner receipt says delivered. | Compute the final sink receipt after every budget/shaping stage and retain a bounded recovery route for omitted duties. | WI-10000320 |\n| The cursor stages an omitted obligation's generation, suppressing it on the next unchanged warm turn. | Advance seen/delivered state only for delivered material; reconcile later delivery, genuine clears, cancellation and context resets without endless repeats. | WI-10000320 |\n| Failed goal/plan identity discovery can become an empty automatic agenda. | Keep unreadable scope explicitly unknown with recovery information; never invent no-demand or satisfaction. | WI-10000320 |\n| The promised complete-agenda recovery reference points to a reader that lacks that complete shared projection. | Extend the existing read surface and prove the exact emitted recovery reference resolves. | WI-10000320 |\n| Work-item/ancestor history returns current specs, decisions and corrections with omission refs. | Preserve this working behavior, scope discipline and member cost. | Live reads of WI-10000243 and WI-2147072 |\n| The plan descendant-history compiler has no production read/injection caller. | Connect the shared compiler to actual plan-level read, launch and leader consumers, with bounded integration proof. | WI-10000321 |\n| Full goal-level history was deferred. | Complete goal own-history plus descendant plan/item history under the new owner instruction; do not leave an admitted but unused goal rung. | This plan P-009; supersedes the deferral in effort-scoped-continuity P-020 |\n| New history after claim needs reliable delivery. | Reuse the existing new-post task and integrate meaningful history changes with generation/cursor recovery. | WI-2142387 |\n| Coarser history relies on recorded outcomes, causes, corrected premises and residue. | Verify capture and compression together; preserve missing/unknown information rather than inventing structure. | Existing effort-thread and prior-attempt-rungs surfaces |\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Subject and exposure.** Each sampled run has an evidence record containing its goal, holder, observation window, source generation and instruction exposure.\n\n**R-2 — Stopped-goal constraints.** A stopped goal remains stopped throughout the bounded probe.\n\n**R-3 — Honest conduct grading.** Each criterion without an observed opportunity is reported as unknown or idle.\n\n**R-4 — Matched behavioral effect.** Each claimed behavioral effect cites matched opportunity windows with explicit instruction generations.\n\n**R-5 — Causal correction.** Each verified correction includes a passing recurrence guard for the original observed failure.\n\n**R-6 — Independent acceptance.** Each final acceptance verdict cites a reviewer outside the implementer's lineage.\n\n**R-7 — Existing grading surfaces.** Each submitted run verdict contains every current GOAL criterion on the canonical scorecard surface.\n\n**R-8 — Separate shipment verification.** Each original-plan shipment claim cites a deployed generation containing the feature.\n\n**R-9 — Owner-request continuity.** A request remains unresolved across acknowledgements, interrupted replies, handoffs and compaction until a matching substantive answer is delivered, or the request is explicitly cancelled or superseded. A later unrelated answer or machine wake cannot resolve it.\n\n**R-10 — Current authority and corrections.** Every delivered continuation identifies its source generations and preserves applicable current specs, decisions, retractions, verified completions, ownership and stop conditions ahead of stale summaries. Contradictory or unreadable evidence remains explicit until recovered. Fresh pushed context counts as a read.\n\n**R-11 — Final delivery and cursor integrity.** Final sink receipts describe what survived the complete rendering/transport budget. An omitted obligation cannot become seen or satisfied. Its bounded recovery path remains available, and a later eligible delivery is not suppressed by an unseen generation. Genuine no-change and already-delivered warm turns remain deduplicated.\n\n**R-12 — Unknown scope and usable recovery.** Failed scope/provider/history reads are distinguishable from measured no-demand and empty history. The named recovery action resolves the relevant full evidence through an existing read surface. Agent, fleet-leader and GUI consumers use the same canonical status and honest sink-specific delivery state.\n\n**R-13 — Complete hierarchical history.** A plan-level consumer receives its own history plus relevant child-item history. A goal-level consumer receives its own history, related plans and their child items, and directly attached work items. Shared paths deduplicate; unrelated objects remain excluded; missing or unreadable relationships are disclosed. Production delivery is required, not only an exported compiler.\n\n**R-14 — Bounded capture and compression.** Learned information is written at the level where the work occurs. Fixed per-consumer budgets admit nearer material first and reduce detail by depth, preserving authority, corrected premises and unfinished residue with exact drill-down refs. Missing extracted fields remain unknown or explicitly omitted. Cost does not grow without bound as descendants grow.\n\n**R-15 — History freshness across time.** New relevant posts, decisions, spec revisions and corrections after claim can refresh the consumer through existing event/generation mechanisms. Failed or truncated reads do not advance unseen generations. Warm dedup, cold starts, handoffs, late changes and cancellation preserve correctness without repeated full-history injection.\n\n**R-16 — Role-correct supervisory progress.** Applicable next actions preserve prioritization, delegation, verification, reporting, current-task continuation, peer ownership and justified waits. No artificial launch, read, new-item or self-implementation quota is introduced.\n\n**R-17 — Safe measurement and stop semantics.** Diagnostic estimates never acquire authoritative measurement provenance. Full-path tests distinguish unmeasured values, genuinely measured breaches, legitimate agent-supplied external metrics, stale data and attribution failure. A recorded stop keeps its true cause and historical goals are not revived for testing.\n\n**R-18 — Complete evidence and accountable residue.** Every required system outcome has a final-output or integration proof at the appropriate plane, and every claimed behavioral effect has matched live exposure evidence. Unknowns, regressions, omitted sources, costs and any remaining work retain explicit records and owners. The plan cannot close with the required goal or plan integration left deferred.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-014 | live |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-013 | live |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-004, P-014 | live |\n| R-4 | P-002, P-004, P-014 | live |\n| R-5 | P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004, P-014 | live |\n| R-7 | P-002, P-003, P-004, P-014 | live |\n| R-8 | P-004 | live |\n| R-9 | P-005, P-011 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-006, P-008, P-009, P-011 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-008, P-009 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-003, P-010 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-012, P-014 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-013 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-003, P-004, P-014 | live |\n\n### Reuse the existing mechanisms\n\nExtend agent-obligations, agent-obligation-reader/providers/reminders, turn-start-orientation and the existing read cursor. Keep canonical report, launch and independent-verification authorities; do not create a competing task queue, scheduler, report store or grading system.\n\nExtend carry-doc/carry-brief and existing request, thread and delivery records for unresolved owner commitments. Do not treat mere chronological assistant output or a keyword in prose as proof that a request was fulfilled.\n\nExtend prior-attempt-context, containment-tree, effort-thread, prior-attempt-rungs, claim-time-enrichment and plans:context-bundle for history. Preserve the already-working work_items:get/claim ancestor path. Use authoritative item-to-plan, item-to-goal and plan-to-goal edges; prose similarity never invents membership.\n\n### Brief delivery\n\nCompile the canonical agenda once for the scope/generation. Project load-bearing actions first, then account for every outer-envelope and transport limit before declaring delivery. Reserve a compact, truthful recovery indication when the full obligation cannot fit. Stage cursor evidence for the actual final payload; keep unseen obligations recoverable without hot-looping.\n\nRepresent failed identity discovery separately from a known absent goal/plan. Preserve provider unknowns, direct-message priority and current-task continuation. Expose the complete shared agenda through the existing recovery reader, and verify the emitted reference with the same owner/plan/goal scope. The GUI may have a different display budget but must not claim the agent saw material its final sink dropped.\n\nKeep the existing contracted ceilings, including the small turn-start envelope and distinct leader budget. Raising a ceiling or disabling dedup alone is not a fix. Measure optional-read latency; fail softly with an honest unknown rather than blocking a turn or guessing clear.\n\n### Long-horizon capture, reads and injection\n\nWork-item consumers retain their own history and relevant parent authority. Plan consumers receive bounded own-plus-child history. Goal consumers receive bounded own-plus-plan-plus-item history, including direct goal items, without duplicate descendants.\n\nWire the compiled result into existing canonical full reads and the actual plan/goal launch and leader/holder context paths. Match the scope to the role: a member claim remains ancestor-only; a leader/goal reader may receive the bounded descendant rollup. Show generation, omissions and a working detail reference. Initial/cold delivery may carry fuller context; subsequent warm turns use meaningful change detection.\n\nCapture at the most specific applicable work level through existing learned/learnedLevel and effort-thread paths. Verify that the shared extraction/advisory can preserve observed outcomes, causes, corrected premises and residue through depth reduction. Do not require agents to maintain a new transcript, fabricate fields, or copy the same note to every level.\n\nReuse WI-2142387 and existing event/cursor mechanisms for new relevant history after claim. Test changes that land after a carry snapshot and before the successor acts. Preserve retractions and current stop instructions through truncation and raw-ref recovery.\n\n### Independent system and behavior checks\n\nSystem tests use controlled scope/read failures, crowded payloads, final receipts and cursors, actual production readers, duplicate edges, deep/large hierarchies and wrong-subject controls. They do not require judging an LLM's choices.\n\nBehavior measurements begin only with a pinned subject/window and the exact serialized context consumed. Use current goal-mode-e2e, including task-brief-effectiveness and long-horizon-context-effectiveness. Record all current criterion keys; never hardcode the old 27-key rubric. Measure legitimate opportunities, justified deviations, missing exposure, completed verified cycles, lost requests, repeated work, stale decisions, false interventions and recovery cost separately.\n\nThe initial finite GOAL observation retains the previous bounded probe: use goals:start for a fresh scoped subject, with only the starter's holder and one scoped member. No historical killed goal is resumed. The probe may read its own portfolio/mode/brief, deliver one complete report and update only its own terminal state. It may not create further pots/apps/fleets/agents/plans/work-items, edit files or change other goals. Both sessions stand down after the first evidenced report, at a forbidden action, or after the existing ten-minute no-progress limit. Default system account and warm carry remain the defaults; record the actual model and generation. A nominal budget with missing attribution is not claimed as a reliable hard cap.\n\nMatched baseline, brief-only and reminder/enforcement arms run only in authorized isolated conditions with equivalent workload, model, resources and opportunities. Never disable safeguards on live work or manufacture a causal conclusion from unmatched historical scores. If the observations are inconclusive, report them as such and continue the owned next step.\n\n## Contract constraints retained\n\n- The original continuous grading/improvement mission remains, along with original-plan verified shipment. This document expands the first cycle; it does not erase either obligation.\n- Re-read actual stop records and budget/control constraints for the selected subject. WI-2146681 preserves the historical incident; EI-22512669283419131 already contains the narrow write-path repair.\n- Use writer-backed units, populations and source/runtime generations. Agent-origin conduct is separate from hook activity; a stored artifact or inner receipt is separate from delivered evidence.\n- Capture a reproducing system baseline before a code repair. A complete LLM behavior study is not a prerequisite to fixing a directly reproduced system defect.\n- Independent reviewers must be eligible and outside the implementer's lineage. The grading runbook repair EI-22529179403686857 is already recorded; verify rather than duplicate it.\n- Source work stays in canonical staging under the effective lock mode. This session's separately registered WI-10000288 gate responsibility is not replaced by this plan. Other live owners remain exclusive; ordinary implementation and acceptance can proceed on the current build.\n- Final shipment requires exact containing-deployment evidence. A code fix, focused green suite, accepted plan or proposed deployment is not shipment.\n- Previous approval 199440 on WI-10000271 pinned an older plan/rubric revision. It cannot authorize this expanded acceptance contract without a fresh preservation review. This resolves multi-sentence spec-quality rejection without removing any acceptance obligation.\nApproved-By: su-c5c2c2a4-b541-40a9-9b0d-3b0396a28419\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:199960\nApproved-At: 2026-09-07T07:19:14.852Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 31 → 32\nChanged BARs: R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-007 — Repo-file measurement must not promote opaque fingerprint attestations\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-07\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/bind-spec-evidence.ts currently accepts repo-files measurement alongside non-null fixture/rubric/environment fingerprints, while packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-evidence-store.ts recomputes only sourcePaths/testPaths and then prefers that reduced server tuple.\nDecision: repo-files measurement establishes source/test currentness only. The binder must reject non-null fixtureFingerprint, rubricFingerprint, or environmentFingerprint alongside measurement. Existing mixed rows remain append-only history and must be superseded by corrected bindings. Reads may merge supplied comparisons for diagnostic transparency, but any applicable non-repository dimension remains explicitly partially-server-measured and aggregate unknown; it must never be promoted to fully server-measured freshness. This preserves the no-self-attestation security boundary while removing the silently unreachable input state.\nRelated: P-006\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-008 — Spec-test adequacy uses canonical scenario and one-to-one causal-pair contracts\nDate: 2026-09-08\nDate: 2026-09-08\nMeasured: WI-10000674 independently reproduced a false PASS in packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy.ts: any required-layer row, any successful mutation/counterexample, and any successful execution can satisfy the current rubric even when R-10/R-13 acceptance-method cases and R-5 failure-to-recurrence pairing are absent. Current accepted specs expose immutable falsifier JSON and evidence bindings expose immutable details JSON plus durable testRunId/coverageEvidenceRef.\nDecision: extend those existing surfaces instead of creating a parallel manifest system. A spec falsifier may declare sorted stable requiredScenarios and causalPairing:'one-to-one'; both are covered by the immutable spec content hash. Bound evidence declares adequacy.scenarioIds and adequacy.causalPairIds. The evaluator must require every canonical scenario to be covered by a successful ledger-backed binding, and for one-to-one clauses require exactly one successful counterexample/mutation binding and exactly one successful repaired binding per pair ID, with no unpaired negative, recurrence, or multi-pair row. Missing obligations fail; malformed stored metadata remains unknown/fail-closed. Binding validation rejects malformed/duplicate IDs before persistence.\nRationale: this makes the exact acceptance method machine-checkable while reusing canonical spec revisions, immutable evidence bindings, repository measurement, execution ledgers and the existing eight adequacy ratings. P-009 will revise R-10/R-13/R-5 with their current method-derived obligations and rebind fresh measured proof before any new card can pass.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-009 — R-5 keeps exactly five causal pairs and satisfies both layers with a real-Postgres recurrence\nDate: 2026-09-08\nMeasured: acceptance rubric acceptance-goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06@6 R-5 explicitly requires integration and unit, and the exact evaluator on AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-009@4 returned correct-layer:fail because all five repaired pair rows were unit-level. The four historical ledger rows encode exactly five original failures: reader, kickoff, holder, goals:get context, and goals:get raw-ref recovery.\nDecision: R-5's canonical falsifier will enumerate those five stable failure scenarios and retain causalPairing:'one-to-one'. Exactly five negative-to-recurrence pairs are required. The missing-goal-history-reader pair replays through the stronger real-PostgreSQL plan/goal consumer test; the other four replay through their exact unit consumer paths. This satisfies the rubric's integration+unit layer contract without inventing a sixth historical failure or duplicating a recurrence.\nRationale: the acceptance method requires the original counterexample to fail and the corrected production path to pass; it does not require the negative and recurrence legs to use the same test layer. The real-PostgreSQL consumer is a direct execution of the repaired reader through the production graph, so it is the strongest recurrence for that pair.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-010 — R16 distinguishes held-task completion from independent plan acceptance\nDate: 2026-09-14\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/llm-testing/scenarios/su/S33-goal-agenda.ts tells the continue subject to run the already-held task's named verification, then seek independent review; its prohibited regex nevertheless classifies every refused work_items:complete as out-of-scope/self-grade. No original R16 boundary, requirement or independent acceptance obligation is weakened.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-011 — Fold September 20 full-history audit into the generic goal-agent behavior scope\nDate: 2026-09-21\nAvi asked to turn the existing goal-agent/multi-plan-launch work into a generic goal-agent behavior improvement plan and fold in any additional findings from the full audit. The audit report `rpt_c02c1887-f292-48f3-bdd3-2940011d31c3` is authoritative for these additions: preserve delegation and claim-rail behavior; require a separate evaluator with a fresh current window; do not count placement as progress until terminal completion evidence and regrading exist; repair trustworthy goal spend attribution/control before long unattended runs; and reduce coordination/recovery treadmill so the steward spends more effort on frontier selection, delegated closure, and evidence synthesis. The resulting plan must also explicitly exercise multiple plans/pots/fleets concurrently with distinct ownership, no portfolio-loop clobbering, and complete selection→execution→verification→regrade closure.\nRelated: P-012, P-014\n\n### D-012 — P-026: a per-plan CLOSURE gate, derived from the acceptance gate, replaces the administrative-status terminal predicate\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22\nItem: P-026\nActor: su-ae3c4989-e86a-4ce3-bb2e-a3c357c8bd21\n\n#### CORRECTION to this decision's first draft\n\nThe first draft claimed \"nothing reads back whether the delegated execution actually closed\". The absence lint flagged it, I probed it, and it is FALSE as written. `independentVerificationObligation` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-obligation-providers.ts:687) already reads `evaluatePlanAcceptanceGate` and already classifies every gate code through an exhaustive `GATE_CODE_OWNERSHIP` map. The corrected, narrower claim is measured below.\n\n#### Measured (read this turn)\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-obligation-reader.ts:655-659 — the default `planSlugs` dependency is `getSessionBrief({ ownerId })` then `brief?.currentPlanSlug ? [brief.currentPlanSlug] : []`. The acceptance obligation is raised for EXACTLY ONE plan: the one the agent declared itself on. A GOAL holder that DELEGATES plan X never declares itself on X (the fleet leader does), so no independent-verification obligation is ever raised against the holder for X.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/goal-launch-settings.ts, the `terminal` const in `compileGoalPlanPlacement` — terminality comes from administrative status alone: `status in {done, shipped, superseded} OR (items non-empty AND every item in {done, dropped})`.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-obligation-providers.ts:~379 — `planPlacementObligation` filters `applicablePlans` to `placement.state !== 'terminal'`, then clears on placement consistency. Its `clearsWhen.summary` states it verbatim: \"every non-terminal goal worklist plan has a consistent independently led placement and its launch boundary is admissible\".\n\nThe two compose into the defect: the ONLY obligation a holder carries for a delegated plan is the placement one, which clears on placement and then drops the plan entirely once its items read done/dropped. Closure is unobserved for every delegated worklist plan.\n\nMeasured population, 2026-09-22, `harness_shared.harness_plans` WHERE harness_slug='papercusp' AND archived IS NOT TRUE — plans satisfying the item-status leg while NOT shipped and NOT superseded: **258** (awaiting-acceptance 205 of 206, draft 39 of 134, ready 13 of 125, active 1 of 262). `awaiting-acceptance` means exactly \"implementation complete, acceptance NOT granted\".\n\n#### Decision\n\n1. **DERIVE from the acceptance layer; build no second oracle.** `evaluatePlanAcceptanceGate` already adjudicates item completion, the code-truth audit, spec proof, rubric vetting, independent (non-implementer) grading and the implementer's acceptance verdict.\n\n2. **Widen the acceptance obligation to the delegated worklist.** `planSlugs` becomes the UNION of `currentPlanSlug` and the goal worklist's non-closed plan slugs, so a holder carries an independent-verification obligation for work it delegated. The existing `.slice(0, 8)` at agent-obligation-reader.ts:179 is the cost bound; no new cap is invented.\n\n3. **New pure fold `resolvePlanClosure` in packages/operator-core/lib/goals/plan-closure.ts**, four legs mapped from `PlanAcceptanceGateCode`: `terminalEvidence` (`plan_items_unfinished`), `verificationReadBack` (`acceptance_unaudited`, `audit_coverage_stale`, `audit_citations_unresolved`, `requirement_unrealized`, `spec_proof_stale`, `spec_clause_unproven`), `independentRegrade` (`acceptance_ungraded`, `self_graded_only`, `acceptance_bar_not_met`, `acceptance_rejected`, rubric-vetting codes), `measuredReport` (`acceptance_not_recorded` + the parse in 6).\n\n4. **FOUR-VALUED, and `unknown` never collapses to `closed`.** `closed | open | partial | unknown`. The measurement-failure codes (`acceptance_lineage_unreadable`, `spec_coverage_unavailable`, `design_evidence_unavailable`, `acceptance_rubric_revision_unreadable`) and an unreadable gate force `unknown`, never reported as progress. This is P-026's \"preserve partial/unknown outcomes instead of declaring success from claims or placement\".\n\n5. **`compileGoalPlanPlacement` stops deciding terminality alone.** It takes a `closure` input; `state === 'terminal'` requires the three EVIDENCE legs. An administratively-complete but unevidenced plan gets the new state `awaiting-closure` with repair action `close-plan`, stays in the worklist, and names its own next verb. `planPlacementObligation` clears on closure, not placement; `partial`/`unknown` closure yields obligation status `unknown`, never `satisfied`.\n\n6. **The measured report is structured.** `PLAN_CLOSURE_REPORT_FIELDS = ['effect','cost','uncertainty','residue']`, parsed from the implementer's recorded acceptance `reasoning` using the heading-parse discipline `goal-owner-report.ts` already uses. No new store.\n\n#### Consequence for other lanes\n\nA GOAL holder may no longer count a plan done because its items are done/dropped. Any lane reading `GoalPlanPlacement.state` must handle `awaiting-closure`; letting it fall through to `terminal` re-introduces this defect.\n\n### D-013 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-23\nAmendment-Id: af2b162bfb0c815c9d709421f9940a4271506e1ce2533a20326d88bd4295c1c3\nRequest-Hash: 7bc245a48e26ef967eaae57e529dca9104057399dac97d58066fd6bebdc52607\nActor: su-ae3c4989-e86a-4ce3-bb2e-a3c357c8bd21\nReason: P-004 acceptance contract: bind a structured verification check to all 18 acceptance criteria so every bar names the artifact that falsifies it, replacing prose-only silence. 11 tree/integration bars get kind:tests bindings whose files are BOTH linked by an existing spec_evidence_binding for this plan AND were run green in this session (709 tests, 0 failed, per-file attribution, collectionFailed:false on every file). The 7 live-plane bars whose proof is deployment-generation containment, reviewer-lineage inspection, a scorecard census or a matched behavioral A/B get the explicit manual declaration kind:instrument/instrumentKey:none rather than an invented test path. Criteria are re-sent verbatim with exactly one added field each, so no method, model, barKey or barHash changes.\nApproved-By: su-77b3a99d-e271-43fc-9ab1-7daf214767b8\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1141086\nApproved-At: 2026-09-23T01:42:40.199Z\nRubric revision: 7 → 8\nSubject plan revision: 73 → 74\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-014 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-26\nAmendment-Id: goal-agent-p004-r15-r16-apply-20260926-post1147969\nRequest-Hash: 5667b3c982784a6da09f8443757afff073ad74fad31246a5a23507b35dc406e7\nActor: su-e45b5e9c-2bb1-4cf1-a2cf-e485806f7e98\nReason: Resume independently critiqued R-15/R-16 correction from thread-post:1147759; verify preview currency before outside approval.\nApproved-By: su-6980f429-03ca-4459-b818-38c97278f9c0\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1147969\nApproved-At: 2026-09-26T23:57:38.057Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 76 → 77\nChanged BARs: R-15, R-16\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-015 — P-004 is in owner scope (#574/#717); the \"owner-paused\" label was self-imposed\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27.
