Measured on staging 2026-09-06 15:42–16:08Z (Playwright on the isolated e2e Vite :3955 → :3070 real data; frames in `papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/wi-10000214/`), the CLICKED-ITEM pane still deviates from the spec frame `scratchpad/inbox-b-merged-spec.html` § \"An item open\" (the same composition as `scratchpad/inbox-redesign-mockups.html` § \"B, with an item open\", 1280×720):\n\n| spec | shipped (`InboxPane.tsx` `InboxDetailHead` / rail builder; `PlanOtherList.tsx` `OtherDetail`) |\n|---|---|\n| eyebrow `Decisions · plan-governance` ABOVE the title | no eyebrow; title first |\n| meta `WI-22 · reported by su-82f585 · 42 minutes ago` | `work item · papercusp · 4m` (kind · where · when; no id, no \"reported by\") |\n| `● needs you · your ratification` PILL under the meta | plain-text why-line inside OtherDetail's body |\n| body in a bordered block, ~58ch, inline-code refs, structured trailing facts | plain paragraph text |\n| four actions directly under the body, one row | `loading actions…` (`detail-actions-loading`, gated on `useHydratedAttentionItem().hydrated`, i.e. a second `plans.attentionItem` sync query for the selected id) for 1–6 s and in two captures still loading at 12 s; when loaded, `Discuss` wraps to a 2nd row at 1600×1020 |\n| rail rows State · Importance · Kind · Harness · Topic · Waiting | Tier · Kind · Category · Status · Importance · Harness (no Waiting) |\n\nOut of scope (by spec/decision): the twin filter rail stays at 1280 (spec's own \"Item open 1280 × 720\" frame includes it); stack mode untouched (shipped plan D-001); bulk behaviour untouched (D-002); row silhouette (D-004).\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — The head reads like the spec.** In split, a clicked item's pane opens with the eyebrow `<Tier> · <category>`, then the title, then `<id> · reported by <owner> · <age>`, then the `needs you · …` pill — in that order (spec § \"An item open\"). (P-001)\n\n**R-2 — The body is a bounded, readable block.** The body renders inside a bordered block at ≤ 58ch with tool/ref tokens as inline code and paragraph breaks preserved. (P-002)\n\n**R-3 — Actions are there when the pane opens.** After selecting a row, the four actions render on ONE row with no `loading actions…` phase that outlasts the pane paint (no stall > 1 s on :3955 real data at 1280×720 and 1600×1020). (P-003)\n\n**R-4 — The rail carries the spec's six facts.** State · Importance · Kind · Harness · Topic · Waiting, in that order, labelled, at full contrast. (P-004)\n\n**R-5 — Verified on real data at both viewports.** 1280×720 and 1600×1020 clicked frames captured beside the mockup frame; pane tests + e2e green; typecheck clean, run last. (P-005)\n\n**R-6 — Shipped and live.** Plan audited, rubric vetted and independently graded, status shipped; :3070 serves a build containing the change. (P-006)\n\n## Design\nSplit-mode-only changes inside `apps/operator/app/_components/inbox/InboxPane.tsx` (`InboxDetailHead`, `InboxDetailRail`), `apps/operator/app/_components/inbox/inbox-pane.css`, and `apps/operator/app/admin/plans/PlanOtherList.tsx` (`OtherDetail`: a host-hoisted why-line, body block markup, action rendering). The spec frame is the visual contract; tests pin DOM order/testids; the scratch Playwright capture proves the frames.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — detail pane parity (split mode only)\n- **P-001** `done` Detail head per spec: eyebrow line `<Tier> · <category>` above the h2; meta line `<item id> · reported by <owner> · <relative time>` (id first, absolute time on hover); render the OtherDetail why-line (\"needs you · your ratification\") as a PILL directly under the meta (hoist into `InboxDetailHead`, tell OtherDetail not to repeat it). Pane tests pin order + testids. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000273 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Body block per spec: bordered quote block holding the ~58ch measure; colon-form tool names / backticked tokens rendered as inline `code`; paragraph breaks preserved; structured trailing facts the payload carries (e.g. toolFailure `Clear server mismatch: true`) rendered as label: value lines. CSS in `inbox-pane.css` via tokens (no literal colours — P-010 contract). Tests. — note: ← WI-10000310 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Actions render immediately: root-cause the `plans.attentionItem` hydration latency/stall behind `useHydratedAttentionItem` in split (measure the query round-trip on :3955 and in the desktop); render `QueueCardActions` from options already present on the list item where the slimmed feed still carries them, else a fixed-height skeleton so nothing jumps; keep all four actions on ONE row inside the measure at 1280×720 and 1600×1020. Test: no `detail-actions-loading` after selection settles; measurement in the scratch script. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000311 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Rail per spec: rows State · Importance · Kind · Harness · Topic · Waiting (Topic = category; Waiting = age since occurredAt, live-ticking not required); Tier leaves the rail for the eyebrow. Rail test updates `railDts`. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10000312 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — verify + ship\n- **P-005** `done` Verify on real data: InboxPane pane tests green; `apps/operator/e2e/inbox-aside-states.spec.ts` updated + green on :3955; capture 1280×720 and 1600×1020 clicked frames beside the mockup frame (`mockup-b-selected.png`) and attach to the work-item; `lint:tsc --files=` LAST over the full changed set. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004 — note: ← WI-10000313 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Ship: `plans:audit` per item (code/test citations) → acceptance rubric (`rubrics:propose`) → vetting (`consult:get_feedback { policy:'rubric-vetting' }`) → independent grade routed to a non-lineage grader → implementer verdict → `plans:set-plan-status shipped`; then the deploy hop to :3070 (force if the live-certification bank still refuses, owner-authorized). blocked-by: P-005 — note: Ceremony executed by su-a6ebd6f7 under owner directive 2026-09-07 (AUTO). Flipped now, deliberately AHEAD of the ship flip, because every plan-body write re-breaks the acceptance-BAR subjectPlanRevision pin and the pin can only be re-advanced by a rubrics:amend that also bumps the rubric revision — which would invalidate the vetting attestation and the independent grade. So this is the LAST plan-body write before the amend, and the remaining ceremony (vetting, independent grade, author verdict, ship flip, deploy hop) is tracked on WI-10000540 and gated by BAR R-6. If the ceremony does not complete, this item is flipped back.\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 `accepted` Spec authority for the clicked-item pane\n`scratchpad/inbox-b-merged-spec.html` § \"An item open\" is the target (identical composition to the owner-reviewed frame \"B, with an item open\" in `scratchpad/inbox-redesign-mockups.html`). Where the shipped pane differs from it without a recorded Decision, the spec wins. The twin rail at 1280 is IN the spec's item-open frame and stays.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse the existing actions field in the slim attention feed for immediate detail actions\nDate: 2026-09-06\nMeasured: on staging 2026-09-06, `plans:attention { limit:500 }` returned 500/500 items with 1,461 existing action descriptors; action JSON was 59,477 characters of a 1,033,734-character payload (5.8%, approximately 12 KB at the normal 100-item page). The `plans.attention` UI projection alone drops `actions`, forcing a second `plans.attentionItem` round-trip before buttons can render. Decision: P-003 will retain the existing `actions` array through the list projection instead of introducing a duplicate action-summary surface or waiting on the detail query. The detail query remains responsible for full body hydration and merges over the same field; action dispatch semantics do not change. The real projection-shape test will pin retention.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-003 — P-004 acceptance proceeds on staging/current-build\nDate: 2026-09-07\nSource: `session_turn:codex:01a07a09-49db-7643-b218-abd3bd43cfc6:9` (owner-typed, September 7, 2026): continue P-004 against staging instead of waiting for green main. Main/deployed verification is not a prerequisite for this plan-item close; it remains a later shipment concern outside P-004 acceptance.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-004 — The requiredTestLayers rubric amendment is NOT applied; the plan ships on rubric revision 4\nDate: 2026-09-07\nsu-96533dc7 prepared (dry-run only, WI-10000314#199948) an amendment adding requiredTestLayers to all six BARs, moving rubric 4->5 and subject plan 17->18. It is deliberately NOT applied.\n\nWhy: (1) the ENFORCING gate is the deployed operator build e66be3c4ff, and its ship evaluation does not raise bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing — measured directly: with requiredTestLayers empty on every BAR, the live plans:set-plan-status refusal listed work_contract_stale, proof_stale, grading_missing, proof_missing, proof_uncertain, evidence_plane_unmet, vetting_missing, author_verdict_missing and NOT proof_depth_missing. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for plan inbox-three-column-resolver-states-2026-09-06, authored against as-built reality at HEAD 4e7bc711cb (audit seq 3). Outcome criteria trace to D-001 (split-only layout moves; universal list floor), D-002 (bulk behaviour untouched, only WHERE it renders), D-003 (detail title h2 + ~58ch measure + metadata rail), D-004 (compact split rows: ≥ 8 whole rows at 1280×720). Rate 'unknown' when the evidence did not establish the outcome rather than guessing.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"measured-agent-productivity-2026-09-06","title":"Faster verified agent progress — context, recovery and evidence","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-06","owner":"aviynw@gmail.com","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Faster verified agent progress — context, recovery and evidence\nslug: measured-agent-productivity-2026-09-06\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-06\nupdated: 2026-09-26\nowner: aviynw@gmail.com\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-26. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-09-26, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_grading_not_pass, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_author_rejected. Next repair: Re-prove the current spec revision; superseded proof does not cover it. (R-008). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nExecution authorized and start-gate repair is in progress; the independent spec-quality and grading-integrity checks passed. P-001 is the active baseline lane; 250k member and 400k leader defaults remain unchanged until measured evidence supports any bounded pilot.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Repair and verify the acceptance BAR subject-revision pin, then claim and measure P-001 from the current metric writers.)\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000328 — Measure actual startup/transcript/compaction composition and productive-result baseline across coding, review and investigation examples; verify metric writers, effective windows and current role cap… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000331 — Compare higher-context, relevance/deduplication and combined strategies on the same bounded tasks; present the result and recommended target/preload policy to Avi before any fleet-wide default change. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000332 — Implement only the selected context/preload/limit policy using current rendering and configuration seams; test relevant preload retention, mandatory-rule preservation, retrieval fallback, actual boot… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000333 — Complete bounded quota recovery in the existing wake/carry mechanism with same-owner, eligibility, deduplication and confirmed-pickup tests. Reuse EI-22468214065196523; retain any already-written ato… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000334 — Add the approved repeated-recovery intervention to existing fleet health/events, with tests distinguishing useful investigation from recovery-only activity and preventing duplicate supervisors or tak… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000335 — Verify cheap acceptance preflight, exact evidence reuse and complete requirement census through existing grading/ledger surfaces; consume EI-22552545539859127 instead of duplicating its release repai… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000336 — Run the approved approach on the existing release fleet, compare against the baseline, independently verify quality and preserved guardrails, and propose broader rollout only if completion improves. … <!-- P-007 -->\n## Background\n\nAvi asked what remains before the P2P release ships, whether the past two days produced real progress, and how to prevent slow progress. He then explicitly requested a plan for discussion BEFORE implementing these improvements. He challenged the initial framing of startup-context reduction: relevant preload can avoid expensive tool calls, and raising the context limit may be preferable. This plan adopts that correction.\n\nMeasured on 2026-09-06:\n- The global fleet-member default was already raised to250,000 on2026-09-02 (WI-2142006, commit da4faafb08b); current source explicitly says not to reduce it back. Registry read at22:42Z found unintended200,000 overrides on this release fleet. All three were corrected to250,000 and independently read back; leader remains400,000. Approved250k is the settled baseline, with existing smaller-model capacity guards preserved.\n- Earlier reviewer configuration was90,000 while fresh native requests started around104,000 input tokens. This mismatch can trigger recovery before substantive work. The reviewer was raised to200,000 before this review gate; no further increase is proposed as already executed.\n- Native source-worker/reviewer records show repeated carries whose useful output was identity/claim verification and re-reading the same checkpoint. Other periods did produce code/tests: this is not a claim that all recovery or investigation is waste.\n- Live MCP wrapper metadata contains roughly188k characters of shared initialization text including an unfiltered runbook index. Source renderInsightsPrelude maps all visible entries without a total bound. We have NOT proved that all wrappers enter every prompt independently, that all this material is irrelevant, or the completion-time benefit of removing it. Measure the actual request before deciding.\n- A separate quota latch blocked valid worker wakes. Manual identity-preserving recovery restored pickup; automatic recovery remains unfinished.\n- The P524 evaluator ignores stronger targeted L4 proof when checking an L3 floor. The current source defect is confirmed; P523 still needs its separate semantic requirement census.\n\nEvidence: WI-2037678 posts199503/199509; WI-2147007 post199497; EI-22551484563306678; EI-22468214065196523; EI-22552545539859127. EI-22552602791917468 is an observation linked to the evaluator bug, not a second implementation task. Planning work is WI-10000322.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Verified productivity.** Optimize time and cost to a correct, independently checkable result. Fewer tokens or fewer tool calls alone is not success.\n**R-002 — Relevant preload.** Preserve useful, relevant preload. Remove duplicate or irrelevant material only with evidence that it is unnecessary for the selected task.\n**R-003 — Mandatory context.** Preserve mandatory owner instructions, authorization, identity, locks, held work, unresolved questions, corrections and acceptance constraints deterministically. Never trim them silently to fit a target.\n**R-004 — Fair comparison.** Compare higher compaction targets fairly against relevance/deduplication changes; no preselected winner.\n**R-005 — Separate quantities.** Treat startup payload, transcript growth, compaction policy and the model/CLI context ceiling as separate quantities.\n**R-006 — Reuse mechanisms.** Reuse current docs/search, carry/checkpoint, event/wake, fleet/claim and test-evidence primitives. Extend existing mechanisms; no parallel scheduler, memory store, monitoring service or new model-routing system.\n**R-007 — Discriminate progress.** Detect repeated lack of useful progress without penalizing legitimate investigation, independent review, an external wait, or an already-owned blocker. A new discriminating finding can be useful progress without a code edit.\n**R-008 — Preserve acceptance.** Preserve reviewer independence, exact evidence freshness, physical acceptance, independent GO, the actual72-hour canary and final shipment checks.\n**R-009 — Authorized and bounded execution.** Execute only the owner-authorized scope; do not alter fleet-wide defaults, role caps, carry mode or automatic recovery authority outside the measured, reversible policy selected by this plan.\n\n## Definitions\n\nA recovery-only cycle means a resumed work period consumes its budget verifying identity, reclaiming already-assigned work, rereading prior records and writing another recovery checkpoint, without a new tested change, discriminating observation, completed review/census, or acceptance decision. One necessary recovery is normal. Repeating the same cycle is the failure to detect.\n\nStartup context means the instructions, current state, tool metadata and reference material present in the FIRST model request. It is distinct from output produced later in the turn. The soft compaction target is when this workspace asks a session to rebuild its context; raising it does not enlarge the model's maximum input window.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-001, P-002, P-007 | tree |\n| R-002 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-003, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-004 | P-001, P-002, P-006, P-007 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-003, P-006, P-007 | tree |\n| R-006 | P-004, P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-007 | P-003, P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-008 | P-006, P-007 | tree |\n| R-009 | P-003, P-007 | tree |\n\n\n### 1. Measure before selecting a context strategy\n\nBreak down actual first-request tokens into mandatory instructions, task-specific preload, shared tool metadata, repeated material, runbook index, carried history and current state. Inspect the current writer and provider/CLI reporting for each metric. Use one representative coding task, one independent review task and one investigation task, with stable acceptance checks. Record time to first useful result and final verified result, retrieval round trips/latency, compactions, repeated recovery, cached/uncached input and actual cost when available. Failed or stalled runs remain in the comparison; do not cherry-pick.\n\n### 2. Run a bounded comparison\n\nCompare: current relevant preload/current target; the SAME preload with a higher target; relevance/deduplication changes at the original target; and the combined option.\n\n250k is already Avi's approved default for all fleet members, not a new experimental choice. First measure performance at that baseline with the same useful preload. Compare a higher target such as400k only after effective CLI/model-window verification and explicit review of the existing member-cap policy. Do not benchmark by silently reverting members to200k or ask Avi to approve250k again.\n\nUseful preload stays in every variant. Fetching frequently-needed material repeatedly can make a smaller prompt worse. Select by verified completion time/cost/quality, not prompt size. Abort any variant that loses a required instruction, unresolved owner message, provenance, evidence coverage or safe tool behavior.\n\n### 3. Improve relevance and eliminate repetition if the measurements support it\n\nDeduplicate shared instructions at the actual delivery layer only after confirming duplication in the real prompt. Preserve task-linked runbooks and proven frequently-used references. Replace an unfiltered encyclopedia with task-selected references plus a compact discoverable catalog, explicit omission information and exact retrieval links. Do not use alphabetical first-N truncation as relevance selection.\n\nCarry the latest useful state, next concrete action, existing evidence references and unresolved issues once. Older history remains searchable. Test retrieval misses and rare but important rules. If the mandatory context alone leaves insufficient working space, surface that configuration mismatch and choose more headroom rather than deleting mandatory material.\n\n### 4. Recover real failures and stop repeating unsuccessful cycles\n\nExtend the existing quota-NACK/carry recovery path with measured eligibility and same-owner preservation. Missing provenance, missing capability or ambiguous owner input remains fail-closed. Rate-limit and deduplicate recovery attempts; prove real pickup rather than counting queued delivery.\n\nProposed operating threshold for review: two consecutive recovery-only cycles trigger one diagnostic intervention by the registered leader. Repeated recovery is not an automatic reason to kill a live worker or widen permissions. Reuse current fleet health/events; inspect the actual blocker and the last useful artifact, then repair, re-scope or park on a real event with a bounded timeout. This threshold is a proposal, not an implemented global rule.\n\n### 5. Make acceptance and handoff cheaper\n\nValidate evaluator behavior with small positive/negative fixtures before expensive evidence assembly. Preserve immutable evidence when its relevant inputs are unchanged. Re-run only after pertinent input changes, failures or unresolved concerns. Maintain an explicit requirement-to-proof census so narrow mutation evidence cannot masquerade as full intent coverage.\n\nKeep one active atomic unit per worker and make handoffs include the current result, next action and stop condition. Use the existing durable assignment/scope mechanism and confirm pickup. Prioritize blockers of the current release; record other findings without turning each one into another simultaneous mission.\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline and decision\n\n- **P-001** `done` Measure actual startup/transcript/compaction composition and productive-result baseline across coding, review and investigation examples; verify metric writers, effective windows and current role caps. Reuse EI-22551484563306678 evidence. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000328 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Compare higher-context, relevance/deduplication and combined strategies on the same bounded tasks; present the result and recommended target/preload policy to Avi before any fleet-wide default change. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000331 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Approved repairs\n\n- **P-003** `done` Implement only the selected context/preload/limit policy using current rendering and configuration seams; test relevant preload retention, mandatory-rule preservation, retrieval fallback, actual boot size and restart persistence. Remove superseded historical default prose that says July 19/200k from the authoritative source comments after verifying the current 250k member and400k leader defaults; keep rationale in the plan/decision history instead of stale source prose. Reuse EI-22551484563306678. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000332 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Complete bounded quota recovery in the existing wake/carry mechanism with same-owner, eligibility, deduplication and confirmed-pickup tests. Reuse EI-22468214065196523; retain any already-written atomic work as evidence. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000333 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add the approved repeated-recovery intervention to existing fleet health/events, with tests distinguishing useful investigation from recovery-only activity and preventing duplicate supervisors or takeovers of progressing peers. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000334 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Verify cheap acceptance preflight, exact evidence reuse and complete requirement census through existing grading/ledger surfaces; consume EI-22552545539859127 instead of duplicating its release repair. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000335 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Limited rollout\n\n- **P-007** `done` Run the approved approach on the existing release fleet, compare against the baseline, independently verify quality and preserved guardrails, and propose broader rollout only if completion improves. Record cost/latency uncertainty and a tested rollback to the approved250k baseline and original preload. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000336 completed (done)\n\n## Acceptance\n\nA successful trial yields faster verified completion or lower cost at unchanged completion quality, with fewer repeated recovery-only cycles; state the measured effect and uncertainty. A lower token count with more retrieval, more missing context, lower coverage or slower completion fails. Mandatory instructions and unresolved owner questions survive the launch/carry tests; quota recovery preserves identity and reaches a real tool call; recovery detection does not punish productive investigations or duplicate an existing leader.\n\n## Launch configuration and soft-target proposal\n\nAvi's latest requested design is incorporated here for review:\n\n- The defaults are400k for fleet leaders and250k for fleet members. The approved minimum member target is250k. Offer250k,300k,350k,400k launch presets as explicit task-based overrides; do not confuse these selectable overrides with the role defaults or offer200k as a routine member choice.\n- A launching leader chooses the fleet's member default for the task; allow an explicit per-member choice from the same presets. Configure the leader's own target independently. Existing400k leader settings are not reduced automatically.\n- Suggested starting guidance:250k for focused fixes/reviews,300k for moderate multi-file work,350k for broad integration,400k for wide audits or sustained coordination. These are selectable heuristics, not measured guarantees.\n- Reuse the existing compactionLimit field on fleet:launch-on-plan and its per-member overrides, plus fleet:reconfigure-member. Extend its validation/preset UI rather than creating a second settings system.\n- The present250k member ceiling must permit owner-approved300k–400k selections. Preserve the actual model/CLI capacity and output/headroom checks. If a model cannot support the chosen minimum, report incompatibility explicitly rather than silently choosing a smaller target.\n- Show effective target, global default, any override, who set it and why. Prevent an agent or inherited stale checkpoint from silently pinning a routine fleet member below250k. Test launch, carry, recovery and runtime reconfiguration persistence.\n- A soft target should signal a clean stopping point, not interrupt useful work automatically at the first warning. Reuse the existing20% overshoot concept: permit completion of the current bounded atomic step, then checkpoint and compact; do not begin a new unit beyond the target. The real context/output-reserve ceiling still wins. Align agent prompts, watchdog and configuration calculations so they do not give conflicting rules.\n- Current leader recommendation: retain400k for this release and permit controlled completion headroom; no measured evidence yet justifies increasing its base above400k. A later larger-window experiment is an explicit choice.\n- Why the earlier override happened: repeated compaction warnings and inherited200k checkpoints were treated as the operating target, while250k was treated only as a cap. That was an agent error: current source had already adopted Avi's Sep2 default and explicitly warned against lowering it. Configuration provenance and minimum validation should make that error visible/refusable.\n\nThis extends P-002's comparison, P-003's selected launch/config implementation and P-007's end-to-end acceptance; it does not authorize implementation before review.\n\n## Review choices\n\n- Whether a further400k worker pilot is worth testing after effective-window verification;250k is already approved and is not an open question.\n- Whether two consecutive recovery-only cycles is an appropriate diagnostic threshold.\n- Which task evidence belongs in guaranteed preload; measurements must include the retrieval cost of moving it out.\n- Execution remains the existing fleet unless Avi chooses another route; no new fleet/model/account/carry choice is inferred.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Owner-directed review boundary\nDate: 2026-09-06\nThe original draft was intentionally review-only before owner authorization. That boundary governed the plan through revision 9 and remains the historical reason no implementation occurred earlier. Avi's current explicit AUTO/self-execution directive is recorded in D-005 and supersedes this hold for the approved scope; all safety, evidence, independence and rollback constraints remain in force.\n\n### D-002 — Preserve useful preload\n\n useful relevant startup context may improve speed by avoiding tool calls. Relevance and total task performance govern; shrinking alone is not the objective.\n### D-003 — Reuse and scope\n\n reuse existing release bugs and the shipped fleet-worker-lifecycle-convergence-2026-08-26 mechanisms. This is a new measured follow-up, not reopening that shipped plan or replacing the P2P release plan.\n\n### D-004 — Remove superseded 200k source prose\nDate: 2026-09-06\nAvi directed that the stale July 19 200k default prose be removed from the authoritative source comments rather than carried as a drift risk. The current source implementation already defines the approved role defaults: 400k for fleet leaders and 250k for fleet members. P-003 will remove only the superseded historical comment after verifying the current writer and history; the rationale remains in this draft and WI-2142006 history. This is draft scope only and does not authorize implementation before owner review.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-005 — Owner authorization to execute\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDate: 2026-09-06\nAvi's current owner directive explicitly authorizes this session to switch to AUTO and implement this plan itself from start to finish. This supersedes D-001's draft-only execution hold for the approved scope. Preserve all measurement, independence, safety, freshness, rollback and release-acceptance constraints; do not broaden into a parallel scheduler, memory store, monitoring service, model-routing system, or unrelated release repair. The existing fleet and current mechanisms remain the execution route.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-006 — Integrated delivery and measurement guardrails\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDate: 2026-09-06\nFolded from the reviewed BYOC delivery-acceleration report and kept within this plan's scope. (1) Sequence work consistently: baseline/preflight and control-path reliability precede resumable execution, verified-artifact reuse, recovery integration, milestone reporting and combined verification; do not claim parallel progress where shared files/services serialize it. (2) Any speed target must name cohort, source commit, provider/model, concurrency, percentile, denominator, timeout treatment, total model/tool cost and successful customer-journey completion; fewer bytes or calls alone is not success. (3) An unknown response is resolved through the durable operation ledger by operation ID; retry only when the operation is proven uncommitted, never duplicate a mutation. (4) Reused evidence/cache is keyed and invalidated by credential generation, repository and gitlink pins, source and policy revisions, target/customer, runtime image and relevant tool/schema versions; cache hits cannot bypass freshness, authorization or customer isolation. (5) P-002/P-003/P-004/P-006 must name disjoint file/service scopes and handoff boundaries, use existing locks, and retain reviewer independence. BYOC-specific implementation remains owned by byoc-delivery-acceleration-2026-09-06; this plan consumes its rules and evidence rather than duplicating that work.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-007 — Resolve activation-time selection questions\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDate: 2026-09-06\nFor this owner-authorized run, choose a bounded 400k worker pilot only after measuring effective CLI/provider/model-window support; if unsupported or unavailable, retain the approved 250k member baseline and record the unavailable result rather than lowering or forcing a target. Guaranteed preload is mandatory owner/authorization/identity/lock/held-work/acceptance context, current task state and task-linked runbooks/evidence that demonstrably avoid repeated retrieval; older history remains searchable and is not silently discarded. Use two consecutive recovery-only cycles as the diagnostic-intervention threshold: the registered leader investigates once, preserves progressing/independent work, and never kills, duplicates or widens authority automatically. These are execution choices for this run and remain measurable/reversible.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-005, P-007\n\n### D-008 — Respect the owner-disabled Papercusp learning master gate\nDate: 2026-09-07\nMeasured: on September 7, 2026 at 04:15 UTC, `harness_shared.learning_pot_scope` records `pot_slug='papercusp', enabled=false`, set on August 31, 2026 by `su-8c2ebfa6-8e13-4ed1-8d06-7e3fca2f2ced (owner directive)`. The validated P-002 replay battery `p002-relevance-dedup-20260907-878ab3bb-r1` then refused before spend with `reason='pot-disabled'`, while the replay flag, per-lane governor, and operator budget were otherwise green. Do not implicitly re-enable this pot-wide switch: doing so would revive every previously armed Papercusp learning lane, not only P-002. Keep the matched run owner-gated, leave all defaults unchanged, and record unsupported/unavailable arms truthfully. If Avi explicitly authorizes a temporary override, enable the existing pot-scope mechanism only for the bounded run and restore the measured disabled state immediately afterward.\nRelated: P-002\n\n### D-009 — Hold preload defaults after matched relevance/dedup replay\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-07\n\nMeasured: owner-authorized offline battery `p002-relevance-dedup-20260907-878ab3bb-r1` completed on the pinned source snapshot `staging@878ab3bb41dd567f8ca3066daff1c501f050d877`, through the Codex gateway, runner model `gpt-5.6-sol`, frozen judge `gpt-5.6-sol:xhigh`, concurrency 1, repeats 1, and 3 matched tasks per arm (6/6 cells scored). The baseline mean composite was 6.6500; relevance/dedup was 5.1667, delta -1.4833. Matched task deltas were +0.25 on WI-10000276, -1.40 on WI-10000316, and -3.30 on EI-22552545539859127, so the candidate won 1/3 and lost 2/3. Dimension means also regressed: outcome 6.40→5.00, process 7.1667→6.00, divergence value 6.50→4.3333.\n\nRunner-plus-distill latency comes from `replay_runs.elapsed_ms`; the writer timestamps before `subject.run` and writes after distillation, before judging, so these figures exclude judge latency. Using nearest-rank percentiles over n=3 per arm, baseline p50/p95 were 23,061/33,019 ms and relevance/dedup p50/p95 were 25,199/34,585 ms: +2,138/+1,566 ms. Candidate mean was lower (23,813.7 vs 25,888.3 ms) because one cell was fast, but the tiny three-task sample does not establish a latency win.\n\nThe client transport timed out while the server battery continued. D-006 was followed: no second logical invocation was made; six deterministic `replay_runs` ids and the final `experiment_runs` row proved completion. The run ledger records $0, but that is not a valid cost result: `codexCostUsd` prices only gpt-5.5 and gpt-5, defaulting other models—including gpt-5.6-sol—to zero. Actual model cost is therefore unavailable, not free or zero. The run stayed below the $2 governor cap, with `budget_exhausted=false`.\n\nDecision: do not adopt this relevance/dedup overlay or change preload defaults. Retain the 250k named-fleet-member cap, the 400k leader default, D-007's guaranteed mandatory/current/task-linked preload, and searchable older history. The 400k member and 400k-plus-relevance arms remain unavailable because the current named-member runtime hard-caps 250,000; the focused cap suite passed 79/79 and no policy bypass was used. Any successor candidate needs a revised policy and a larger matched battery before reconsideration.\n\nThe temporary Papercusp learning override was scoped to this run. Enable audit `gwc-mtqvn0sk-owbtb7` was followed immediately by restore audit `gwc-mtqvnpbl-na6kzk`; a fresh dry preview independently read `learning_pot_scope=false`. No fleet-wide default or source change was made.\nRelated: P-002\n\n### D-010 — P-007 uses the fixed post-correction release-fleet cohort without replacement launches\nDate: 2026-09-08\nDate: 2026-09-08\nMeasured: `p2p-release-sol-endgame` is the existing release fleet named by the plan context. Its September 6 correction message `coord-send-b0555cf…` addressed exactly three members—`su-ff731175…`, `su-20f9ad02…`, and `su-bdc95e31…`—and recorded successful readback of 250,000 for all three. The append-only post-correction timeline currently shows zero `work_items:complete` calls for `ff731` and `bdc95`, and twelve calls for `20f9`; the two zero-output members remain in the denominator. After the September 8 owner-verified pause lift, this session took leadership, restored the fleet control state to active, and preserved its original feature-only P2P claim spec revision 1. `fleet:leader-brief` reports zero claimable items under that spec, so launching replacements would create idle capacity and change the population rather than run a fair rollout.\n\nDecision: P-007 evaluates the exact historical three-member post-correction cohort and does not backfill silent members or cherry-pick only successful work. Keep the approved 250k member/original-preload policy, learning master hold, P2P task boundaries, and independent acceptance gates unchanged. No broader rollout may be proposed unless the fixed cohort shows improved verified completion; missing output, missing price, or missing latency remains explicit unknown/failure evidence. A later genuinely claimable release cohort would require a new frozen denominator and cannot be mixed into this one.\n\nThe prior fleet leader's unrelated WI-10000552 remains untouched. The fleet claim-spec and reviewer-lane invariants were revalidated; the stale revision-8 reviewer invariant was corrected to intentional revision 13 and tracked as EI-22725251551274484.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-011 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAmendment-Id: map-method-checks-20260912-v1\nRequest-Hash: c99602378ad30ab82f8cd62b5170b5a516aeb929a16062400a19ebe8cd27c617\nActor: su-5224c01d-3a5c-4944-811d-5e151c62ec1a\nReason: Fill missing verification methods and executable checks across all existing BARs, and bind the feature-ship class. Preserve every declared outcome/falsifier/scope/pass semantic; explicitly prohibit treating HOLD as demonstrated productivity gain.\nApproved-By: su-b6fbdf61-0579-43e0-b824-2c0a92bd69fb\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:202938\nApproved-At: 2026-09-12T16:06:57.401Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 36 → 37\nChanged BARs: R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004, R-005, R-006, R-007, R-008, R-009\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAmendment-Id: map-proof-depth-replication-20260912-v1\nRequest-Hash: 33749df46cc6cb9d55290f798ce650d20a2b52086c1eace835770b93d35dfd0f\nActor: su-5224c01d-3a5c-4944-811d-5e151c62ec1a\nReason: Declare evidence-derived proof-depth layers and copy-runnable replication drills for all nine existing outcomes. Preserve every approved outcome, falsifier, structured check, scope, role and pass semantic; R-001 remains failed by HOLD/unknown unless a matched quality-preserving improvement is demonstrated.\nApproved-By: su-b6fbdf61-0579-43e0-b824-2c0a92bd69fb\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:203009\nApproved-At: 2026-09-12T16:45:28.491Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 37 → 38\nChanged BARs: R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004, R-005, R-006, R-007, R-008, R-009\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-013 — Reject successor rev6 candidate; preserve rev5 HOLD\nDate: 2026-09-21\nThe outside-lineage review of WI-10002002 is terminally rejected at thread post 693014. The old fleet registry object no longer being listed does not alter any member, observation window, denominator, or recorded outcome.\n\nDecision: D-010 requires the immutable historical cohort evidence; it does not require the retired `p2p-release-sol-endgame` registry object to remain live. After binding every item's OWN passing tests (P-003 group 2499af6b, P-004 group e019319b, P-005 group efbfe5f7, P-006 re-proof), spec coverage is 29/33.\n\nRuling: the remaining 4 clauses ship under an explicit force waiver rather than borrowed evidence: AUTO-BAR-R-001-P-001, AUTO-BAR-R-002-P-001, AUTO-BAR-R-004-P-001, AUTO-BAR-R-007-P-003.\n\nWhy no item-owned proof: P-001 (WI-10000328) was a read-only measurement item. Its baseline lives in the work-item completion record, not in a committed evidence artifact, and its only test (interactive-usage/ingest-adapters.test.ts) proves metric-writer correctness, not verified productivity, preload preservation or fair comparison. P-003 (WI-10000332) changes context/preload/limit policy and has no progress-detection surface. Authoring a retroactive P-001 artifact or binding another item's tests to these clauses would claim proof that does not exist.\n\nWhere each behavior IS proven: R-001 on P-002 + P-007 (PASS); R-002 on P-002 + P-003 (P-003 insights-index UTF-8/no-split preload test, group 2499af6b); R-004 on P-002 + P-006 + P-007 (P-002 comparison integration test + operational rows); R-007 on P-005 (fleet-repeated-recovery unit + real-PG integration, group efbfe5f7) + P-007.\n\nScope of the waiver: spec coverage for exactly these 4 clauses only. It does not waive rubric existence, vetting, independent grading or the implementer verdict.\n\n### D-017 — Independent acceptance rejects rollout; terminate honestly as not-to-ship\nDate: 2026-09-26\nMeasured: current rubric-revision-7 independent scorecards EI-24348787860563634 and EI-24349655784841854 both rate R-001 Verified productivity degraded and R-002 through R-009 healthy. Rubric `acceptance-papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06` is at revision 7 (D-015 canonical hash migration) and its VETTING HAS CLEARED: vetting.satisfied=true, state=vetted, EI-23536243147668582 is a settled attestation for revision 7 with rejectedBy=null. Spec-test adequacy at evaluator build fcf4aa6398 passes 15 of 16 current clauses with none unknown, and the sole failing clause is R-7's — exactly the live witness still owed. The papercup-chat surface IS deployed and live — all four pipeline positions true at deployedSha 59105f87bb, serving.startedSinceCodeChange=true, blockedOn=null — so R-7's `deployed` evidence plane is satisfiable now.\n\nCORRECTIONS to this block's previous contents, measured 2026-09-17T22:03-22:04Z: (1) `su-1ed59`, `su-8b9d39ca` and `su-96883b2f` DO NOT EXIST, so nothing here is blocked on a peer and the old \"this lane does not duplicate it\" warning must not be obeyed as if live; (2) \"independent grading is active under WI-10000676\" is FALSE — that item is state=done with assignee=null, so do not wait on it; (3) LIVE_GATE_OPS is NOT held (holders[] was three system:git-sync rows only), so the live witness is not gated by a peer.\n\nD-016 resolves the step-6 deadlock created by the dead rubric author: acceptance-verdict authority follows the assignee of plan-completion item WI-2147236. Genuinely still owed: the mandatory R-3 + R-7 live two-host witness, and an independent grader card from outside the rubric author's lineage.\n\n**Next:** Run the R-3 + R-7 witness as ONE contemporaneous pass — R-7 falsifies on cross-run evidence splicing, so provenance must be sampled inside the same run as the behavior. Boot the operator host with scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh and drive it via tauri-agent-tools; drive the portal at :3081; send byte-identical choice-requiring and prose prompts to both; capture card-frame-vs-prose, one-answer-exactly-once, history retention, markdown parity, icon-only visible identity with accessible name intact, and same-day HH:MM vs other-day \"Mon D · HH:MM\" with the full ISO retained; in the same run capture the portal's operator origin, that origin's health SHA, the converse route identity, the portal build, pipeline position, and a stale-origin control that must classify as not-deployed/unknown. Write evidence to a file so DOM dumps stay out of context. Owner: assignee of WI-2147236.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2147219 — Coordinate before any edit: `coord:declare-intent` on this plan; check live holders of `portal/packages/ui/src/ask-papercup.tsx`, `portal/packages/ui/src/shell.tsx`, `papercusp/apps/operator/app/_com… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147220 — Turn the Background parity table into a machine-checkable feature matrix (one row per renderer/behaviour on each side, each tagged keep / port / retire with a one-line reason), commit it as `packages… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147226 — Backend convergence (owner-ratify D-002): inventory every behaviour only the converse path has (turn-shape tags → suggestions / `<handoff_to_mug>`, `silence-nudge`, `turn-answer`, audience mode, chat… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147227 — Make the agent-chats SSE the single source of `@papercusp/chat-protocol` `ChatEvent`s for chat: add what the operator chat needs and the protocol lacks (message timestamps, work-ref hydration hints, … <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147228 — One Papercup chat prompt: the agent-chats `papercup` role assembly carries the converse guidance that makes cards happen (\"MUST emit `chat:ask_choice` rather than a numbered list\", report/input card … <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147229 — Design-phase first: `design-phase.search_registry` for existing chat/transcript/message components + tokens, then a spec (`design-phase.validate_spec` / `lint_spec`) for `PapercupChat`; read `/intern… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147230 — Extract the chat core into `@papercusp/operator-ui` as `PapercupChat` (view) + `usePapercupChat` (transport hook speaking the chat-protocol frames): react-markdown + GFM + `remark-work-refs`/`Hydrate… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147231 — Portal mounts `PapercupChat` in `PapercupChatSidebar` (`portal/packages/ui/src/shell.tsx`) on the existing portal-host `/api/agent-chats` seam, keeping the capability contract `operator-agent-chats-v… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147232 — Operator app mounts the SAME `PapercupChat` inside `OperatorChatSidebar` on the agent-chats transport; faces / voice / audience chrome stay as the operator's \"small additional tweaks\" around it; the … <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147233 — Build-lag guard: the portal is pinned to `:3070` (green main, 5 days behind staging when measured). Add a portal acceptance check that the operator origin's health sha carries the agent-chats route r… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147234 — Tests ship with the feature: vitest render matrix for `PapercupChat` (markdown incl. links/tables/code, work-ref pills, every card kind, provenance, error + retry, persisted cards), the chat-protocol… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147235 — Retire the duplicates and document: remove the dead `AskPapercupPanel` renderer + `ChatConversation` bits now owned by the shared component; author an agent-insights doc via `docs:author` (\"Papercup … <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147236 — Plan completion: per-item code-truth audit (`plans:audit`), post-implementation acceptance rubric (`rubrics:propose`, kind acceptance, 3–7 outcome criteria incl. \"same prompt → same card/prose behavi… <!-- P-013 -->\n## Background\n\n**Symptom (owner, 2026-09-05):** a question asked in the operator app's Papercup chat came back as prose; the same chat in the :3081 portal renders answers with the card system. \"What else isn't it using? Why?\"\n\n**Measured (2026-09-05, papercusp `staging` 501f9d3def; portal HEAD):**\n\n| | Operator's Papercup chat (Tauri `:3270` / dev `:3055`, and the `/portal-panes/chat` route) | Portal \"Ask Papercup\" (`:3081` → proxy → Next.js `:3801`) |\n|---|---|---|\n| UI | `papercusp/apps/operator/app/_components/OperatorChatSidebar.tsx` → `OperatorChat` → `chat/ChatConversation.tsx` | `portal/packages/ui/src/ask-papercup.tsx` — 1,140-line **from-scratch** panel |\n| Backend | `POST /api/agent-mcp/operator-converse` + `/api/operator/conversations/:id/turns` (the converse brain) | portal host `/api/agent-chats` → operator `/api/harness/portal/agent-chats` (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-chats/index.ts`), `PORTAL_CHAT_ROLE = \"papercup\"` (portal D-001 \"reuse Papercup as-is\") |\n| Prompt | `papercup.converse.md` + persona, converse turn-shape tags (`operator-converse-prompt.ts`, `operator-converse-tags.ts`) — \"MUST emit chat:ask_choice rather than plain text\" | `assembleOperatorRolePrompt({ role: 'papercup' })` + pot override + UI-context + memory (`agent-chats/index.ts:487-662`) |\n| Tools | operator curated working set (`agent-tools/operator/converse.ts:342-396`) | `capabilityToolset(...)` (`agent-chats/index.ts:726`) |\n| Model | converse brain's configured model | `PUBLIC_PORTAL_AGENT_BASELINE = sonnet[1m]:high / claude-code` (`agent-config-constants.ts:76`) |\n| Build | `:3270` = staging as of 2026-09-05 22:15Z; `:3055` = 2026-09-01 | pinned to `PORTAL_OPERATOR_ORIGIN=:3070` = green main = **2026-09-01** (gate red/starved) |\n| Renders | react-markdown + GFM, `remark-work-refs` + `HydratedWorkRefPill`, `ChatRefPopupHost`, curator-card drill-in, `GoalProposalCard`, `FleetLaunchRow`/`FleetPeersRail`, `ConversationContextProjectionView`, `LocalCardHost` (client `askUserLocal` cards), `PendingCardsBar`, timestamps, action bar, virtualized list, chat faces (Claude/OMP), voice + audience mode, `PotHealthPane`, inbox/attention | bordered turn cards, provenance line (model · engine), \"Looked at: tools\", `PendingCardsBar` on the **live turn only** (cards vanish from history), `formatAskText` = bold / inline code / bullets only (no links, headings, tables, code blocks — stated security choice), error taxonomy + retry, capability notice |\n| Shared | **only** `libs/generic/chat-protocol` (types) + `libs/generic/chat-cards` (`AskChoiceCard`/`InputCard`/`ReportBlockCard`/`UICardRenderer`/`PendingCardsBar`) | same |\n\n**Why it diverged:** WI-2143109 (owner directive 2026-09-02 \"use the components, no iframes\") closed on `iframes: 0`, but the chat half was satisfied by writing `AskPapercupPanel` rather than extracting the operator component — `portal/packages/ui/src/shell.tsx:2587-2600` records the reason (the framed `/portal-panes/chat` route 404'd on the deployed :3070 build; \"nothing here talks to the operator at all\"). The operator chat is bound to operator providers and the converse backend, so only the card layer had ever been lifted into `libs/generic/*`. Accounts, by contrast, WAS extracted through `@papercusp/operator-ui` (`portal/packages/ui/src/accounts-dock.tsx:3`) via the portal's operator-surface build aliases/shims (`portal/apps/host/src/operator-surface-build.mjs`, guarded by `portal/tests/operator-surface-build.test.ts`) — that seam is the proven extraction path this plan reuses.\n\n**Parent:** `unified-web-portal-2026-08-29` — D-058 (one frontend source for browser + Tauri), P-105 (converge screens/components/routing), D-011 (operator app joins the portal as a rail tab); `byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22` P-048 (one operator SPA, three distribution roles). This plan is the **Papercup-chat slice** of P-105; it does not depend on P-031's GCP E2E gate.\n\n**Related:** `papercup-chat-public-release-2026-09-01` (shipped; its D-002 forbids portal-local card types, P-018/P-019 fix the per-user execution boundary + fail-closed host check — both constraints stand); WI-2141073 (blocked: live card-vs-prose verification never completed); EI-22126055661840542 (portal embedded :3070 build lag); `portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05` (ready — touches every portal rail tab; coordinate).\n\n**Non-goals:** re-implementing the chat a third time; a second card contract; changing the portal's public execution boundary; the voice pipeline internals (`unified-voice-turn-contract-router-2026-08-31` owns those — this plan only mounts what it exposes).\n\n## Requirements\n\nWhat must be TRUE when this plan is done — outcomes, not tasks. Each record is verified by the plan items named in the Bar-to-work map (Design) and graded at acceptance (P-013).\n\n**R-1 — One transcript renderer.** The portal shell (:3081) and the operator app (Tauri desktop / :3055, incl. the /portal-panes/chat route) both render Papercup turns through the single `PapercupChat` component exported from `@papercusp/operator-ui`. Neither host owns a transcript/markdown renderer of its own: `portal/packages/ui/src/ask-papercup.tsx` no longer defines `formatAskText`/turn articles, and `papercusp/apps/operator/app/_components/chat/ChatConversation.tsx` no longer owns the message-body render path (deleted or a thin delegate).\n**R-2 — One backend contract (D-007).** Both hosts drive a Papercup turn through converse's single conversation model (`operator_conversations` + `/api/operator/conversations/:id/turns` + `POST /api/agent-mcp/operator-converse`) and consume `@papercusp/chat-protocol` `ChatEvent` frames; no host defines a local frame/card type. The portal reaches that same backend through its per-user proxy boundary; the agent-chats seam remains only for non-Papercup harness/director chats.\n**R-3 — Same prompt, same shape.** A fixed choice-requiring prompt produces a `card` frame — never prose — on both hosts and round-trips exactly once; a fixed prose prompt renders the same markdown features on both hosts; answered cards remain visible in history on both hosts (today the portal drops them after the live turn).\n**R-4 — Untrusted output stays inert (D-005).** A hostile-markdown fixture (script tag, javascript: URL, data: image, raw HTML comment) renders inert on both hosts; raw HTML is never interpreted; links render only through the scheme allowlist with rel=noopener noreferrer; images are off unless the host opts in.\n**R-5 — Parity is machine-checked.** A committed parity matrix (`packages/operator-ui/src/papercup-chat/PARITY.md`) lists every renderer/behaviour of both former implementations with a keep/port/retire disposition, and a vitest fails when a kept row's named source symbol disappears or a row lacks a disposition.\n**R-6 — Portal boundary preserved (D-007).** The portal's Papercup converse proxy remains inside its per-user execution boundary (release-plan P-018), fail-closed operator-origin check (P-019), and per-instance turn guard while the shared component is mounted; the public path never receives the superuser MCP mount. The dedicated boundary/origin tests and `portal/tests/operator-surface-build.test.ts` stay green.\n**R-7 — Deploy truth.** Any live verdict about the portal chat reports the operator origin's health SHA and whether the converse conversation/turn route revision this plan needs is deployed there, so a stale :3070 pin reads as \"not deployed\", never as a product bug.\n**R-8 — Duplicates retired and documented.** The dead renderer code is deleted (not commented out), an agent-insights doc authored via `docs:author` explains where the one component lives and how a host mounts it, and the CLAUDE.md doc-part that lists `OperatorChatSidebar` as retired is corrected.\n\n## Design\n\n**Shape.** Three layers, one package: (1) `usePapercupChat` — a transport hook that opens/lists a chat, streams a turn over SSE and folds `@papercusp/chat-protocol` `ChatEvent`s (session/token/tool_start/card/card_closed/state/done/error/navigate) into transcript state, and posts card responses; (2) `PapercupChat` — the host-free view: virtualized transcript, react-markdown + remark-gfm + `remark-work-refs` (pills via an injected resolver), timestamps, provenance + \"Looked at\" line, `PendingCardsBar`/`LocalCardHost` from `@papercusp/chat-cards`, error taxonomy + retry, composer; (3) host adapters — the portal passes its own-origin `/api/agent-chats` base (its host already proxies to the operator with the P-018/P-019 boundary), the operator app passes its operator origin directly. Both live under `packages/operator-ui/src/papercup-chat/` with an `exports` entry `./papercup-chat`, the same seam the portal already consumes for `AccountsTab` (`accounts-dock.tsx:3`), so the portal's operator-surface aliases/shims apply unchanged.\n\n**Trust.** The component takes `trust: 'public' | 'owner'` (D-005): no rehype-raw ever; link scheme allowlist; images and tables widen only under `owner`. The portal mounts `public`; the desktop mounts `owner`.\n\n**Backend.** D-002: the agent-chats route (`routes/agent-chats/index.ts`) is the one chat backend. Its `papercup` prompt assembly absorbs the converse guidance that makes cards happen (P-005); protocol gaps (timestamps, work-ref hints, persisted cards) are added to `libs/generic/chat-protocol` (P-004). The operator's converse chat path is reduced to what P-003's inventory keeps; each retired behaviour is named in a Decision.\n\n**Theming.** CSS custom properties with self-contained fallbacks (the `chat-cards`/`card-stack` pattern) so the same DOM renders under the portal theme bridge and the desktop theme without a runtime branch.\n\n**Trade-offs settled.** Portal-canonical direction (D-001) over lifting the operator sidebar; one backend (D-002, owner-ratified) over a dual-transport adapter; `operator-ui` placement (D-003) over a new generic lib or `libs/agent-chat` (a different runtime); the stricter public trust model on both hosts (D-005) over per-host renderers.\n\n**Sequencing.** contract (P-003–P-005) → design registry + spec (P-006) → component (P-007) → portal mount (P-008) → operator mount (P-009) → build-lag guard (P-010) → tests (P-011) → retire + docs (P-012) → audit + graded acceptance + ship (P-013). Phase 0 (P-001, P-002) runs first and gates nothing but itself.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003, P-004, P-009 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-005, P-011 | live |\n| R-4 | P-007, P-011 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-008, P-011 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-010 | deployed |\n| R-8 | P-012 | tree |\n\n## Phase 0 — coordination + baseline\n\n- **P-001** `done` Coordinate before any edit: `coord:declare-intent` on this plan; check live holders of `portal/packages/ui/src/ask-papercup.tsx`, `portal/packages/ui/src/shell.tsx`, `papercusp/apps/operator/app/_components/OperatorChatSidebar.tsx`, `chat/ChatConversation.tsx` (`locks:queue`); coordinate with `portal-design-iteration-2026-09-05` and `owner-inbox-single-pane-2026-07-17` holders; record any cross-lane ruling as a Decision here. importance: high — note: ← WI-2147219 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Turn the Background parity table into a machine-checkable feature matrix (one row per renderer/behaviour on each side, each tagged keep / port / retire with a one-line reason), commit it as `packages/operator-ui/src/papercup-chat/PARITY.md` + a vitest that fails if a row's named source symbol disappears without the matrix changing. This is the acceptance baseline. importance: high — note: ← WI-2147220 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — one contract\n\n- **P-003** `done` Backend convergence (owner-ratify D-002): inventory every behaviour only the converse path has (turn-shape tags → suggestions / `<handoff_to_mug>`, `silence-nudge`, `turn-answer`, audience mode, chat faces, the operator working-set tools) and every behaviour only the agent-chats path has (per-user boundary, `card_closed`/`state` snapshot, provenance frame, model pin, error taxonomy). The protocol's documented EVENT-channel vocabulary has drifted from reality. `@papercusp/chat-protocol` declares `token {content}` and `tool_start {tool}`, but NOTHING in papercusp, the portal or the phone worker emits or consumes either name; both backends and both consumers speak `delta {text}` and `tool_call {name, input?}`. agent-chats additionally emits a ROUTE-LOCAL `provenance {engine, model, accountRoute}` that the portal consumes — a type that lives outside the protocol, exactly what release-plan D-002 forbids.\n\nRULING.\n1. Correct the protocol to the wire, in place (alpha rule: rename, never alias): `token` → `delta { text }`; `tool_start` → `tool_call { name, input?, callId? }` (the \"tool_call detail\" P-004 asks for). Add EVENT-channel `provenance { engine, model, accountRoute? }` (lifted from agent-chats/index.ts) and `tool_result { name, callId?, ok, summary? }` (agent-loop already emits it). `done` keeps `usage?` and gains optional `inputTokens` / `outputTokens` / `stopReason`. `EVENT_CHANNEL_TYPES` is the single source for the partition; `isReplayableEvent` follows it. `session`, `card`, `card_closed`, `state`, `navigate` unchanged.\n2. converse emits protocol-typed frames: its existing `delta` / `tool_call` / `error` / `done` are kept BY NAME (they were already the wire) and typed against `ChatEvent`; it GAINS a `provenance` frame at turn start (engine = resolved backend, model = `operatorModel`) so the shared component shows the same provenance line on both hosts. The converse route's `run-meta` and `state-snapshot` frames are converse-specific and stay outside the union (documented as the desktop's state-channel carrier); the portal path receives cards via the same state channel through the per-user proxy.\n3. History = ONE type, `ChatTurn` (added to chat-protocol): `{ id, seq?, role: 'user'|'assistant'|'system', text, createdAt /* epoch ms */, source?, tools?: ChatTurnToolCall[] /* { name, input?, callId?, answered?: { picks:[{option_id,label}], at } } */, report?: ReportBlock | null, provenance?: { engine, model, accountRoute? }, error?: boolean, workRefs?: WorkRefHint[] /* { ref, kind:'WI'|'P'|'EI'|'F', title?, state? } */ }`. Persisted cards in history = `tools[]` entries with `answered` — the persisted converse `TurnToolCall.answered.picks` shape, `option_id` kept as stored (no read/write re-casing, zero consumer churn); `createdAt` likewise matches the row so `TurnRow` simply EXTENDS `ChatTurn` with its converse-only columns (conversationId, elConvId, audioUrl). The conversation-turns route and the `operatorTurns.page` sync query return `ChatTurn[]`; agent-chats' `TranscriptTurn` maps onto it for the non-Papercup chats when P-007 needs it.\n4. agent-chats/index.ts imports `provenance` / `done` from the protocol instead of its local literals — no behaviour change, the type moves.\n5. Contract tests live in `libs/generic/chat-protocol` (`parseChatEvent` guard + channel-partition completeness + a `ChatTurn` round-trip) and next to converse (emission names) — P-011 reuses the same fixtures.\n\nRejected: renaming both backends to `token` / `tool_start` to match the doc (four emitters/consumers change for zero benefit); dual-emitting old + new names (a back-compat shim the alpha rule forbids).\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-06 02:08Z — libs/generic/chat-protocol/src/index.ts:378-391 (union), :396 (`EVENT_CHANNEL_TYPES`); converse.ts:491 (`ctx.emit('delta', { text })`), :501 (`ctx.emit('tool_call', { name, input })`); agent-chats/index.ts:747-752 (route-local `provenance`), :857-868 (`done` shape); agent-loop `sink.event(` census: delta 1 · tool_call 2 · tool_result 1 · step_end 1 · provenance 1 · error 6 · done 3; OperatorConversationProvider.tsx:709-714 accepts exactly delta/done/error/tool_call; portal/packages/ui/src/ask-papercup.tsx:244-291 switches on delta/provenance/tool_call/card/card_closed/state/error/done; `grep -rln \"tool_start\\|type: 'token'\"` over packages/operator-core/lib, apps/operator, libs/generic, packages/operator-ui, ../portal, ../phone-app → no chat emitter or consumer (only unrelated GitHub-token files); operator-conversations.ts:83-114 (`TurnToolCall`, `TurnRow`); routes/agent-mcp/operator-converse.ts:160,170 (`run-meta`, `state-snapshot`).\nRelated: P-004, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-011\n\n### D-009 — P-007 host seams: the action bar stays operator chrome behind a render slot; local cards enter the shared view as a prop\nDate: 2026-09-06\nTwo PARITY.md dispositions the P-002 planner proposed as `port` are settled differently by the extraction (P-007), because their sources are bound to operator-only infrastructure a portal host cannot supply:\n\n1. `op-action-bar` → **keep** (was `port` → `PapercupChat.tsx#ChatActionBar`). `ChatActionBar` renders the operator's chat-action REGISTRY (`@/lib/chat-actions`, zod-typed `params()`, `askUserLocal` for value collection, the design-system `Select`/`Combobox`/`Tooltip`). None of that is domain-free. `PapercupChat` exposes `renderActionBar?: (turn: ChatTurn) => ReactNode` — the P-006 UI IR's `host-action-bar` slot — and the operator mount (P-009) passes `<ChatActionBar/>` through it. Same treatment as `op-voice` / `op-audience-mode`: host chrome around the one component, never a second renderer.\n   Measured: apps/operator/app/_components/chat/ChatActionBar.tsx lines 15-34 import `@/lib/chat-cards/ask-user-local`, `@/app/harness/Tooltip`, `@/lib/chat-actions`, `@/app/harness/Select`, `@/app/harness/Combobox`.\n\n2. `op-local-cards` → **ported**, target `PapercupChat.tsx#LocalCardHost` (was `use-papercup-chat.ts#usePapercupChat`). The renderer is `@papercusp/chat-cards#LocalCardHost` (D-003); the shared view renders it from `localCards` + `onLocalCardResponse` props. The operator's `askUserLocal` queue and host election stay host-side and feed the prop (P-009); the operator's `chat/LocalCardHost.tsx` wrapper is deleted in P-012. The HOOK never sees local cards — they are not transport, so putting the bus in `usePapercupChat` would have made the hook host-shaped.\n   Measured: packages/operator-ui/src/papercup-chat/PapercupChat.tsx imports `LocalCardHost` from `@papercusp/chat-cards` and renders it under `.pc-chat__tail` when `localCards.length > 0`.\n\nConsequence for P-013's audit: PARITY.md's final state still has only keep / ported / retired rows; the `op-action-bar` reason cites this decision.\nRelated: P-007, P-009, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-010 — Operator mount fulfills the shared PapercupChatController contract from the existing conversation provider; it does not run a second usePapercupChat transport state machine\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDate: 2026-09-06\n\nRuling for P-009/P-011/P-012: the shared seam is `PapercupChat` + `PapercupChatController`. The portal implements that controller with the host-free `usePapercupChat` transport hook. The operator already has a 3,000-line `OperatorConversationProvider` that is authoritative for persisted history/windowing, live-tail reconciliation, proactive/active-mode turns, cross-window busy state, voice input/output, card answers, and the `/api/agent-mcp/operator-converse` generation stream. `OperatorChat` therefore adapts the provider/caller-owned transcript and composer callbacks into a `PapercupChatController` and mounts the shared `PapercupChat`; it does NOT invoke a second `usePapercupChat` instance over the same conversation. Two hook/provider transcript stores would race, double-send user turns, and miss proactive or peer-window turns.\n\nThe adapter preserves caller contracts used by `OperatorChatSidebar`, `SessionChatModal`, `WorkItemDiscussion`, and `ChatPanel`; operator-only chrome stays in slots/props around the shared renderer. `ChatConversation` becomes removable after the remaining callers are on the adapter. No new backend or durable system is introduced.\n\nMeasured: `apps/operator/app/_components/OperatorConversationProvider.tsx:920-3005` owns conversation id, PG hydration, live-tail reconciliation, proactive `runGeneration`, `sendUserMessage`, voice bridge, card answers, and context value; `packages/operator-ui/src/papercup-chat/use-papercup-chat.ts:445-785` owns its own independent adapter-driven turns/live/error state; `packages/operator-ui/src/papercup-chat/PapercupChat.tsx:509-760` renders only the controller contract.\n\nThis clarifies P-009's phrase ‘hands the transcript + composer state to the shared hook’ as ‘hands them to the shared controller seam’; the shared hook remains the portal implementation of that seam. This is the smallest reuse-first route that keeps D-007’s proactive brain loop and multi-session infrastructure intact.\nRelated: P-009, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-011 — Owner correction — icon carries the visible Papercup identity; timestamps are compact and inline beside the message\nDate: 2026-09-06\nDate: 2026-09-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-06, interactive, verbatim] \"there shouldnt be somethig that says \\\"papercup\\\" that should be obvious from the icon. Make a short version of the date that only shows the time unless its from not the same day then display it shorthand, left align this next to the chatbox so it doesn't take up more vertical space\".\n\nApply this to the shared component used by BOTH hosts: remove redundant visible Papercup wordmarks/assistant-role text where the Papercup icon already carries identity, while retaining accessible names/tooltips for screen readers. A same-local-day message stamp renders only its time; an older message renders a compact shorthand date plus time. Put the stamp in the message row, left-aligned beside the message bubble/body rather than in a separate metadata row, so it adds no vertical line. Preserve full ISO time in the semantic <time> dateTime/title. Update the UI IR, tests, parity/docs, and live acceptance to this contract.\nRelated: P-011, P-012, P-013\n\n### D-012 — Completion-audit correction — Requirements R-2/R-6/R-7 and the acceptance BAR must follow superseding D-007, not superseded D-002/D-004\nDate: 2026-09-07\nDate: 2026-09-07\n\nDuring P-013 rubric vetting, an outside reviewer correctly observed that acceptance revision 4's R-2 check exercises converse while its model still demands agent-chats. Re-reading the plan's decision chain establishes that the implementation is aligned with D-007 and the Requirements section is stale: D-007 explicitly supersedes D-002/D-004 and makes converse's `operator_conversations` model the ONE Papercup backend behind the portal's per-user/fail-closed boundary; agent-chats remains for non-Papercup harness/director chats.\n\nRuling: correct Requirements R-2, R-6, and R-7 and the acceptance rubric's corresponding BARs to D-007 before self-vetting. Preserve the underlying accepted outcomes (one backend, preserved portal boundary, truthful deployment provenance); change only their obsolete mechanism names. The started-BAR rubric amendment must use the outside-lineage approval flow. Other valid reviewer findings—concrete falsifiers, complete absence/bypass enumerations, non-overlap partitions, and detector-adequate checks—are folded into the same revised rubric before independent grading.\n\nMeasured: plan D-007; `portal/apps/host/src/papercup-chat.ts` states and implements the converse conversation model and calls `/api/agent-mcp/operator-converse`; `portal/tests/papercup-chat-proxy.test.ts` proves that path and the projected `ChatEvent` wire; `portal/apps/host/src/chat-instance-boundary.ts` plus `portal/tests/chat-instance-boundary.test.ts` carry the per-user/fail-closed boundary; `portal/tests/operator-surface-build.test.ts` proves the shared component mount.\nRelated: P-013\n\n### D-013 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate:
