verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-016 — Acceptance-verdict authority passes to the current assignee of plan-completion item WI-2147236, because the rubric's author session is permanently gone\nDate: 2026-09-17\nDate: 2026-09-17\n\n[self-imposed ruling — NO owner directive is involved. Recorded per the cross-lane-ruling rule so peers stop treating ship step 6 as blocked on a dead session.]\n\nPROBLEM. The ship ladder's step 6 (\"the implementer records the acceptance call\") names the rubric's `createdBy` as the actor — `grader-eligibility.ts` resolves that identity as the implementer. For rubric `acceptance-papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06` (revision 7) that identity is `su-1ed599c3`, which no longer exists, as do the three sessions this plan's `## Now` block still names as active (`su-1ed59`, `su-8b9d39ca`, `su-96883b2f`). With no live author, step 6 has no eligible actor and the plan cannot reach `shipped` however complete the implementation is.\n\nMeasured: a workspace-wide targeted `coord:presence` lookup returned `ownerLookup.matched=0` with `byState` all zero (2026-09-17T22:03:35Z), the same dead-session shape already recorded for this plan; `WI-10000676`, cited in `## Now` as \"independent grading is active\", is `state=done` with `assignee=null`; rubric revision confirmed as 7 via `harness_shared.harness_plans` at 22:02Z; `LIVE_GATE_OPS` confirmed NOT held (holders[] contained only three `system:git-sync` rows).\n\nRULING. Acceptance-verdict authority for this rubric passes to the CURRENT ASSIGNEE of plan-completion work-item WI-2147236 (at this writing `su-4dbc7355`). That agent records the acceptance call by re-emitting the complete ratings with `acceptance:{ verdict, reasoning }` once an independent card exists. Authority travels with the WORK-ITEM, not with this session: if WI-2147236 is reassigned or handed off, verdict authority moves with it and this decision needs no amendment.\n\nWHAT THIS DOES NOT WAIVE. This substitutes the ACTOR; it does not relax the bar.\n- The INDEPENDENT-GRADER requirement is untouched: the card must still come from a session that is neither the rubric author nor in their spawn/rebind lineage, and must still spot-check the implementer's audit citations.\n- Rubric existence and the vetting attestation remain required — both currently satisfied (`vetting.satisfied=true`, `EI-23536243147668582` settled for revision 7, `rejectedBy=null`).\n- A latest `reject` still blocks ship until addressed and superseded.\n- R-3 and R-7 still require the mandatory live two-host replication and contemporaneous deployed provenance; their own text is explicit that unit tests alone cannot earn `healthy`.\n\nRATIONALE. The independence requirement constrains the GRADER, not the acceptance verdict — the ladder states plainly that \"the implementer owns the passing bar\". Passing that ownership to the live implementer-of-record preserves the design intent, whereas leaving it with a dead identity converts a deliberate judgment step into a permanent deadlock. The alternative considered and rejected was re-authoring the rubric under a live identity: that bumps the revision, which un-counts BOTH the settled vetting attestation and any independent card pinned to `harness_plans.version`, discarding completed work for a purely clerical reason.\nRelated: P-013\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"papercup-update-sections-per-app-2026-09-06","title":"Papercup deterministic updates — per-app sections (email / calendar / phone / plans / inbox / coding) on the curation-loop Fleet status / Fleet update cards, delivered to the ACTIVE conversation (sibling of papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06, D-007 §4)","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercup deterministic updates — per-app sections (email / calendar / phone / plans / inbox / coding) on the curation-loop Fleet status / Fleet update cards, delivered to the ACTIVE conversation (sibling of papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06, D-007 §4)\nslug: papercup-update-sections-per-app-2026-09-06\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-06\nupdated: 2026-09-06\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** DRAFT 2026-09-06 — opened by su-a04137ef as the sibling plan that D-007 §4 of `papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06` calls for. Owner direction [owner:Avi 2026-09-06, turn:claude:15940bc8-9cc1-469f-9ec5-75b39fe41a42@2026-09-06T01:19:18Z], verbatim: \"We should also add other things to the deterministic updates that papercup gives, i.e we added an email and calendar and phone app, we should include those in the papercup update. we can have papercup provide didffernt secitons. one for email one for calendar one for phone and one for plans and one for inbox and one for all of the coding related thigns.\" Nothing implemented yet. Depends on the parent plan's P-004 (converse's SSE emits chat-protocol ChatEvents; persisted cards in history) so the sectioned card renders identically on both hosts. Extends the SHIPPED curator card work (deterministic-status-cards-2026-07-17, curated-signal-cards-2026-07-17) rather than re-opening it.\n\n**Next:** owner ratifies D-001 (provider seam + section keys) at plan review; then P-001 by whoever claims it.\n\n## Background\n\n- The deterministic Papercup update EXISTS today and is the feed the owner pointed at (screenshot `~/Pictures/Screenshots/Screenshot from 2026-09-05 21-31-26.png`: the sidebar's system-authored \"Fleet status\" / \"📋 Fleet update — N items progressed\" cards). Source: `packages/operator-core/lib/curation/curation-loop.ts` — `runCurationTick` → `buildSurfaceReport` (a `ReportBlock` whose single `plans[]` entry is titled \"Fleet status\") and `buildDigestReport` (the \"Fleet update\" digest); signals classified by `curation/salience-policy.ts` (`classifySignal`, `FleetSignalKind`, `SALIENCE_POLICY_VERSION`); written by `curation/curation-surface.ts#surfaceCuratedMessage` as a `role:'assistant', source:'system'` turn with `report` jsonb into `getOrCreateActiveConversation()`.\n- So the update ALREADY targets the ACTIVE conversation — the answer to the owner's \"which session do the deterministic updates go to?\": the conversation the sidebar currently shows, live-tailed via `operatorTurns.page`. Multi-session Papercup is KEPT (D-007); nothing here changes the targeting, only the card's content.\n- The signal population is fleet-only: `FleetSignalKind` covers agent / work-item / plan / gate events. There is no email, calendar or phone signal source anywhere in the loop.\n- The apps live as sibling checkouts — `~/papercupai-workspace/email`, `~/papercupai-workspace/calendar`, `~/papercupai-workspace/phone-app` — mounted by the portal shell (`~/papercupai-workspace/portal`). None feeds the curation loop today.\n- `ReportBlock.plans[]` (`libs/generic/chat-protocol`) already carries MULTIPLE titled sections, each with `items[]`, and `@papercusp/chat-cards#ReportBlockCard` renders them — one section per provider needs no protocol change for the SHAPE. Any per-section hint (`sectionKey`, provider id) is added by EXTENDING chat-protocol under the parent plan's P-004 rule, never as a host-local type.\n- Repo rules that bind this plan: generic-first (`libs/generic/<name>` behind a `configure*()` seam for the domain-free registry), the two scheduling mechanisms (the loop stays a DBOS/routine tick — no new scheduler), flags default ON, nuqs for any UI state, `@papercusp/sync` for reads.\n\n## Phase 1 — the section contract\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Provider seam, generic-first: `libs/generic/update-sections` exports `UpdateSectionProvider = { key: 'email' | 'calendar' | 'phone' | 'plans' | 'inbox' | 'coding', title, collect(ctx) → ReportItem[] }` plus a `configureUpdateSections()` registry pinned with `pinModuleState`; the curation loop's `buildSurfaceReport` / `buildDigestReport` emit ONE `ReportBlock` with one `plans[]` section per provider that returned items (empty sections omitted; fixed section order email → calendar → phone → plans → inbox → coding), today's \"Fleet status\" content becoming the `coding` section. Contract test: order, omission, and the existing digest header unchanged. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Fold the existing fleet signal kinds into the `plans` / `inbox` / `coding` providers (plan-item progress → plans; attention / inbox refs → inbox; agent, gate and work-item events → coding) with NO behaviour change for a workspace that registers no app provider — guard: today's `curation-loop.test.ts` and `curation-surface.test.ts` pass unchanged. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Section-aware salience: `salience-policy.ts` gains a per-section verdict so a noisy section (email) cannot suppress or batch away a quiet one (calendar); bump `SALIENCE_POLICY_VERSION`; policy tests per section. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 2 — app providers\n\n- **P-004** `todo` `email` provider (sibling checkout `email`): unread / needs-reply / flagged deltas since the last surfaced update, read through the operator-side data path the email app already uses (never a second mail client); registered at operator boot behind a feature flag that defaults ON and is verified live in the same task. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-005** `todo` `calendar` provider (sibling checkout `calendar`): next-24h events plus changes since the last update, same registration + flag discipline. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-006** `todo` `phone` provider (sibling checkout `phone-app`): missed calls / voicemail / new messages since the last update, same registration + flag discipline. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 3 — delivery + verification\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Delivery on BOTH hosts from the SAME persisted turn: the sectioned card renders in the desktop sidebar and in the portal shell through the shared `PapercupChat` (parent plan P-007 / P-008 / P-009); verify with `tauri-agent-tools` on a headless desktop shell and on the portal shell — one capture each showing at least two sections in the ACTIVE conversation. blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-008** `todo` Plan completion per the repo rule: per-item code-truth audit (`plans:audit`), post-implementation acceptance rubric (`rubrics:propose`, kind acceptance, 3–7 outcome criteria incl. \"an email arrival surfaces in the email section of the ACTIVE conversation within one curation tick\" and \"a workspace with no app providers renders exactly today's card\"), vetting, independent grading by a non-implementer, implementer's verdict, ship. blocked-by: P-007\n\n## Decisions\n\n(D-001 — provider seam + section keys — is proposed via `plans:add-decision` and owner-ratified at plan review.)\n\n### D-001 — PROPOSED (owner-ratify at plan review) — one sectioned card on one system-authored turn in the ACTIVE conversation; a generic-first provider seam with fixed section keys email · calendar · phone · plans · inbox · coding\nDate: 2026-09-06\nOwner source [turn:claude:15940bc8-9cc1-469f-9ec5-75b39fe41a42@2026-09-06T01:19:18Z]: sections for email, calendar, phone, plans, inbox and \"all of the coding related things\" on the deterministic Papercup update; parent ruling D-007 §4 of papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06.\n\n1. ONE card, ONE turn, the ACTIVE conversation. The update stays a single `ReportBlock` persisted on a `role:'assistant', source:'system'` turn written into `getOrCreateActiveConversation()` — exactly today's mechanism — with one `plans[]` section per provider that returned items. No per-app conversations, no second feed, no second scheduler (the curation tick stays the trigger). Today's \"Fleet status\" content becomes the `coding` section, so a workspace with no app providers renders exactly today's card.\n2. Provider seam, generic-first: `libs/generic/update-sections` exports `UpdateSectionProvider { key, title, collect(ctx) → ReportItem[] }` and a `configureUpdateSections()` registry pinned with `pinModuleState`; the operator host registers providers at boot. Section keys are a fixed enum in a fixed order — email · calendar · phone · plans · inbox · coding — so both hosts render the same card from the same turn (rendered by `@papercusp/chat-cards#ReportBlockCard`; any per-section hint is added by extending `@papercusp/chat-protocol`, never a host-local type).\n3. App providers read through the operator-side data paths the email / calendar / phone apps already use (sibling checkouts `email`, `calendar`, `phone-app`); never a second client, never a direct provider API call from the loop.\n4. Salience becomes per-section (P-003) so a noisy section cannot suppress or batch away a quiet one.\n\nRejected alternative: one card per app — fragments the feed the owner pointed at (the sidebar's Fleet status / Fleet update cards) and multiplies system turns in the active conversation.\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-06 01:52Z — packages/operator-core/lib/curation/curation-surface.ts:34-48 (`surfaceCuratedMessage(text, report)` → `getOrCreateActiveConversation()` + `appendTurn({ role:'assistant', source:'system', report })`); curation-loop.ts:196-216 (`buildSurfaceReport` emits a single `plans[]` section titled 'Fleet status'; `buildDigestReport` header '📋 Fleet update'); salience-policy.ts:27 (`SALIENCE_POLICY_VERSION = 'curator-v4'`), :35 (`FleetSignalKind`), :186 (`classifySignal`); `ls ~/papercupai-workspace` → email, calendar, phone-app, portal.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-007\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"portal-chat-history-2026-09-06","title":"Persistent, accessible Papercup Chat history","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-06","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Persistent, accessible Papercup Chat history\nslug: portal-chat-history-2026-09-06\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-06\nupdated: 2026-09-06\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation complete in staging, by the requesting session under AUTO. All three implementation work-items are done with committed evidence. Source session codex:01a07404-b46f-7b60-8614-0726f5bac7ac was read in full. PostgreSQL runtime persistence, owner-evidenced recovery, rail/header history access, searchable desktop two-pane / phone stacked view and stable transcript/composer are implemented. Validation: 167 focused tests, final shell recheck 82/82, two Chromium journeys, zero typecheck diagnostics, clean diff check. Legacy upstream chats without surviving portal ownership evidence stay unlinked. Screenshot previews: /tmp/portal-chat-history-1440.png and /tmp/portal-chat-history-390.png. Production shipment is not claimed; acceptance here was the current source build.\n\n**Next:** Automatic commit/promotion/deployment pipeline owns shipment. No further implementation or monitoring remains in this owner-directed task; independently verify the live release before marking the plan shipped.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-2147354 — Use the existing PostgreSQL PortalStore for durable chat ownership; remove accidental production memory mode. Implement idempotent recovery of older links only with verified owner and portal-instance… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147356 — Add visible Chat history beneath Papercup Chat and in its header. Replace the upper-right popup with a stable, responsive two-pane history view; searchable titles, last activity, running state, selec… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-2147357 — Run a real PostgreSQL portal-runtime restart regression proving conversations still list, reopen and continue, with cross-owner protection. Run focused app tests and rendered desktop/narrow history j… <!-- P-003 -->\n## Background\nSource session codex:01a07404-b46f-7b60-8614-0726f5bac7ac was read in full (turns 1–12). Task discussion is turns 4–12; turns 1–3 are an unrelated agent lookup. The owner reported that history at :3081 is buried, opens at the upper right, and omits launched Papercup chats. The investigation found PORTAL_USE_MEMORY_STORE=1 losing ownership links on restart while backend transcripts survived.\n\n## Scope and acceptance\nThe acceptance requirements are specified in Requirements below; this section preserves the original audit destination.\n\n## Requirements\nVisible Chat history directly beneath Papercup Chat and in its header. Stable two-pane layout: searchable conversation titles on the left, selected transcript on the right, last activity and running state, reopening and continuing. Durable history via the existing PostgreSQL PortalStore. Recover older links only with verified identity AND portal-instance provenance; never infer ownership merely from the portal harness or a title. Preserve data and fail closed for unverifiable records. Restart regression proves the same stored conversations list, reopen and continue after runtime recreation. Focused tests cover isolation and negative recovery, plus rendered browser desktop/narrow acceptance. Agent/terminal history remains separate in agents running → View inactive sessions.\n\n**R-1 — People can open Chat history from the Chat rail and header.** P-002 and D-004: a labelled Chat history action immediately beneath Papercup Chat and a header Chat history action open one history workspace; terminal sessions stay on their separate surface.\n\n**R-2 — Search, selection and continuation work in usable desktop and phone layouts.** P-002/P-003: searchable conversation titles, last activity and running state beside a selected transcript; continuing and history toggles preserve one composer and in-flight reply. Desktop is two-pane; phone stacks within viewport.\n\n**R-3 — A saved chat still lists, reopens and continues after real database and runtime restart.** P-001/P-003: production always uses the existing PostgreSQL PortalStore, even with the obsolete memory flag set, and retains conversation linkage and timestamps across restarts.\n\n**R-4 — Recovery admits only proven owner and Portal-instance links.** P-001/P-003 and D-001/D-002/D-003: admit only ownership-proven links; leave unverifiable legacy upstream rows unlinked, deduplicate by (owner_id,chat_id), preserve existing provenance/timestamps, and reject cross-owner operations before upstream access.\n\n**R-5 — History and continuation retain the shared Converse contract.** D-004 and papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06#D-007: Portal mounts shared PapercupChat, uses its Converse adapter, persists turns and cards, and keeps per-owner/public-trust boundaries.\n\n**R-6 — The served Portal release exposes working history on desktop and phone.** P-003 final shipment and D-004: the immutable release actually serving :3081 contains the verified history UI and phone fix, and the real rail/header journey works at both widths.\n\n## Design\nReuse portal_agent_chats, migrations, authentication/instance guard, launched endpoint, existing chat interface and UI primitives; no parallel service or database. Search the component registry and validate the history UI spec. Use the registered portal staging checkout and canonical papercusp staging libraries with manual file locks. No manual git add/commit/push. Current-build testing is the implementation acceptance plane; shipment claims require independent pipeline evidence.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-003 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Persistent history\n\n- **P-001** `done` Use the existing PostgreSQL PortalStore for durable chat ownership; remove accidental production memory mode. Implement idempotent recovery of older links only with verified owner and portal-instance evidence, preserving provenance and timestamps. Cover refusal/isolation cases; coordinate compatibility with the active shared-chat migration. importance: high — note: ← WI-2147354 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Accessible history\n\n- **P-002** `done` Add visible Chat history beneath Papercup Chat and in its header. Replace the upper-right popup with a stable, responsive two-pane history view; searchable titles, last activity, running state, selected transcript, reopen and continue. Reuse existing UI and chat state, preserving in-flight turns and separate terminal history. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-2147356 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification\n\n- **P-003** `done` Run a real PostgreSQL portal-runtime restart regression proving conversations still list, reopen and continue, with cross-owner protection. Run focused app tests and rendered desktop/narrow history journeys against current source. Audit implementation, record legacy recovery results and limits, and complete the defect and plan with evidence. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-2147357 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\nThe owner explicitly chose this session and AUTO, with no delegation (current session codex:01a0745a-0dce-7cb0-9c4f-43f846f3a185 turn 1; original session turn 12). The request resumes this scoped portal work despite the older pause fact. Respect active papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06 D-007: backend moves to Converse; keep history independent of transcript implementation and do not reverse that migration. Older UI plans are shipped and the history acceptance rubric is superseded, so this is a distinct owner-requested correction. Unverifiable legacy transcripts remain inaccessible and are reported as a limitation.\n\n### D-001 — Ownership evidence defines recoverable history\nDate: 2026-09-06\nRecover ownership only from the existing Portal database's trusted owner-scoped chat activity, after the owner and instance boundary. A matching title or harness is insufficient; cross-owner and unverified read/continue/card requests must be refused before upstream calls. Measured: portal/packages/data/src/migrations.ts:187-198 recovers from portal_chat_latency_samples; postgres-store.ts:367-373 scopes ownership by owner_id and chat_id; portal/tests/agent-chats.test.ts:325 and tests/papercup-chat-proxy.test.ts cover refusal and permissive controls.\nRelated: P-001, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Unverifiable legacy chats remain unlinked\nDate: 2026-09-06\nLegacy upstream transcripts without surviving Portal ownership evidence remain unlinked and inaccessible through this owner's history; do not guess an owner or invent launch provenance. A provable legacy row must recover successfully, with null launch/title retained when unknown. Measured: portal/tests/chat-history-persistence.integration.test.ts:53-75 seeds recover-a with trusted activity and expects recovery with null provenance and the original activity timestamp; :85-95 checks unverified/cross-owner denials and the other owner's isolated list.\nRelated: P-001, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Recovery deduplicates by owner and conversation\nDate: 2026-09-06\nUse the existing composite (owner_id, chat_id) key for both agent-chat and Converse conversation links. Repeated recovery is idempotent and preserves existing launch text and timestamps; no new parallel history store is introduced. Measured: portal/packages/data/src/migrations.ts:92-98 declares that primary key, :192-198 groups activity by it and uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; portal/packages/data/src/postgres-store.ts:355-364 preserves known provenance on re-record.\nRelated: P-001, P-003\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance preserves Converse and keeps terminal history separate\nDate: 2026-09-06\nHonor papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06#D-007: the active Chat transcript uses the shared PapercupChat component and the Portal Converse proxy; history must not restore the retired renderer. The Chat rail history entry shows only Portal-linked conversations, independently of terminal sessions. Acceptance separates component fixtures, real database/runtime restart with an upstream fixture, and actual served Portal observations. Measured: portal/packages/ui/src/ask-papercup.tsx:39-48 imports the shared chat; papercup-chat-adapter.ts:40 and :104-139 route history and turns through /api/papercup-chat; terminal separation is additionally checked in shell-ui.test.tsx.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n## Source audit\nEvery task-specific requirement from original turns 4–12 maps to Scope and acceptance and the phased items below; current turn 1 authorizes the route. No product question is unresolved.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"shared-agent-obligations-and-briefs-2026-09-05-acceptance","title":"Acceptance — shared agent obligations, actionable briefs, reminders, and evidence-based enforcement","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-06","owner":"su-6b687ce1-1fab-4233-823d-00fdc79929c2","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — shared agent obligations, actionable briefs, reminders, and evidence-based enforcement\nslug: shared-agent-obligations-and-briefs-2026-09-05-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-06\nupdated: 2026-09-12\nowner: su-6b687ce1-1fab-4233-823d-00fdc79929c2\n---\n\n# Acceptance — shared agent obligations, actionable briefs, reminders, and evidence-based enforcement\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). D-010 requires composition over the existing placement, owner-report, acceptance, liveness, reminder, turn-start, and leader-brief authorities rather than a parallel queue. D-011 freezes exactly 18 deterministic opportunities (six per family), zero-inference execution, conservative unknowns, zero negative-control interventions, three-entry/400-token shared bounds, sink-specific clipping, and no workload expansion before independent acceptance. Grade outcomes and operational evidence, not checklist ticks or the implementer's assertions. Independently rerun the named canonical tests and inspect the cited current source; preserve any unexercised live behavior as residue. Revisions 2-3 repair the independent critique in consult conv-mtpwxear-0000-5e4ad032eb0b486fa7e45ae31cf5d7d1: seven explicitly bound outcomes, GUI D-013 coverage, exact test paths, corrected count semantics and honest evidence planes. Existing methods are preserved or extended; no plan requirement is waived.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Draft review-only restriction is superseded; preparing activation audit. Driver WI-10000535, no implementation claims yet.\n\n**Next:** Complete source-conversation activation audit, satisfy canonical readiness prerequisites, start the approved plan, then claim P-001 and implement sequentially with regression evidence. No new agents/fleet; preserve security and runtime/release fences.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000548 — Map existing writers, resolve ownership overlap, and freeze regression fixtures. After approval, inspect classification/readiness, evidence binding, review admission/handoff and checkpoint writers; i… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000549 — Normalize metadata and preflight all prerequisites before evaluation. Extend current create/screen/admit/assign/wake/pickup flow and effective per-agent scope resolution, using existing durable execution and i… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000551 — Separate semantic/policy evidence identity from cosmetic storage revisions. Use frozen representative fixtures and stage-by-stage fault injection; prove all acceptance A-G with exact receipts and exc… <!-- P-007 -->\n## Evidence and diagnosis\nP203 exposed interfaces between individually reasonable gates that agents currently coordinate by hand. This does not justify removing independent review or exact-source binding.\n- WI-2142873 comment200292 / EI-22611521856725953: a passing evaluation preceded plans:start discovering missing acceptance template_data.classRef. Repair changed rubric/spec references and made the old scorecard non-current despite unchanged acceptance text/hash. A class/policy change may legitimately invalidate evidence: unchanged prose alone does NOT establish cosmetic equivalence. Prevent late discovery first.\n- WI-10000531 / EI-22612198786401976: create-with-assign_to was fleet-scope-downgraded; repairing the effective reviewer allowlist left admission-pending; prescribed re-file then failed duplicate_identity. No duplicate was created and no full unblock established.\n- EI-22611711582585308: handoff length limit absent from the typed signature. EI-22452364823097282: valid sessions:read fails invalid escape string. EI-22613713968701761: normal plan prose with an inline item reference refused as an item declaration. These are distinct from caller errors such as invalid argument combinations or guessed projections (EI-22612896907478496).\n- Root, driver and loop repeat progress narratives. Separately scoped checks/walls are NOT duplicate data merely because a carry document includes them together.\n\n## Desired contract\nThe agent supplies behavior, scope, constraints, acceptance examples and the authorized route once. The platform derives identifiers, references, fingerprints and recovery views from canonical records. Classification is selected once from declared intent, or explicitly requested if ambiguous; never silently guessed to obtain a pass. A review request yields one durable logical task and either verified progress or a complete actionable blocker result.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Canonical authoring.** One authoring location per requirement and per operation's progress narrative; preserve item-specific obligations, immutable evidence and history.\n\n**R-2 — Prerequisites before evaluation.** Normalize and validate every discoverable prerequisite before expensive evaluation. Return all known blockers and unknown checks together; revalidate before mutation to prevent stale authorization and partial writes.\n\n**R-3 — Stable resumable review identity.** Retry/resume review requests by stable existing identity. Creation, screening, admission, assignment, delivery and actual pickup are separate truthful states; sent never means started.\n\n**R-4 — Authorized existing-item repair.** Repair an existing review through an authorized existing-item path, not duplicate titles, broad allowlists, force claims or skipped screening. Refusals name the responsible actor, allowed next action and existing wake event/expected bound when known.\n\n**R-5 — Exact semantic and policy evidence.** Evidence stays immutable and exact. Separate storage/presentation revisions from reviewed semantic AND policy identity only with proven equivalence. Relevant class, rubric, behavior, source, test, environment or authorization changes invalidate evidence; unknown equivalence fails closed.\n\n**R-6 — Faithful tool contracts.** Published schemas match runtime limits, incompatible arguments, envelope roots and optionality. Bounded typed summaries and addressable detail replace guessed JSON paths and oversized reads.\n\n**R-7 — Correlated friction capture.** Use existing invocation telemetry and correlated probation/observations for low-severity friction, not manually authored issues for every retry. Preserve accountable existing issues for confirmed actionable defects.\n\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002, P-007 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-003, P-007 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-003, P-007 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-002, P-004, P-007 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-006, P-007 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-001, P-006, P-007 | tree |\n\nThese mappings encode the already-approved item coverage. Evidence is current-tree/hermetic verification, not runtime, deployment, historical release acceptance or permission to change policy.\n\n## Scope and reuse\nExtend plan readiness/metadata reconciliation; review creation/admission/handoff; evidence dependencies; checkpoint/carry projections; tool-contract parity; focused integrated regression tests. No new service, queue, table or parallel coordination system by default. A new durable surface needs a demonstrated gap and review.\nReuse plans:new, existing template-data/spec reconciliation, plans:start and evaluators; work_items:create/claim, admission promoter, effective scheduler specs, coord handoff and events; existing durable orchestration/idempotency; scorecard bindings and dependency hashes; work_items:checkpoint, loop:checkpoint and carry rendering. A multi-process handoff is a durable resumable operation, not a falsely claimed atomic transaction.\nRead the explicit-assignment writer described by agent-insights/a-refusal-that-hides-its-own-bound-and-bypass before selecting a remedy. Reconcile with shared-agent-obligations-and-briefs-2026-09-05 and admission test ownership referenced by acceptance-work-queue-admission-bulk-dedup-2026-08-24. Do not take over their acceptance lanes.\nPredecessors read for dedup: agent-coordination-architecture-v2-2026-05-20 (foundational identity/locks/channels/on-ramp); agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02 (token-output measurements). Reuse both; do not reopen owner-deferred context work or assert checkpoints dominate total token cost. The initial mapping step must resolve any further source/owner overlap before editing; bounded search is not proof of absence.\n\n## Milestones\nA — Remove deadlocks: bounded current-source/contract map and fixtures, then prerequisite normalization and resumable reviewer handoff. Parallelism only after disjoint files/owners are established.\nB — Reduce repeat administration: safe evidence identity, canonical checkpoint projections, schema/summary/friction-capture parity.\nC — Prove and adopt: integrated current-build/hermetic tests, before/after measurement, shadow comparison and controlled rollout. Existing live P203 audit and deployed main are not development prerequisites. Canonical items and dependency edges follow below.\n\n## Acceptance\nA. Legacy/incomplete plan returns all discoverable missing/ambiguous prerequisites before scorecard creation; unknown checks cannot pass. Retry preserves identity; failure leaves no partial metadata.\nB. Repeated/concurrent/crash-recovered requests for the same exact audit yield exactly one logical task. Replay the restrictive-override to allowlist-repair to admission-pending to duplicate_identity chain and recover the existing identity through policy. Refusal stays explicit until cleared.\nC. Inject failure after every handoff stage: resume durably, reauthorize current caller, avoid double assignment, and distinguish delivery from actual pickup. Denied scope, revoked authority and independent-review constraints remain enforced.\nD. Reference/formatting-only changes preserve bindings only if reviewed semantics AND governing policy match. Real class/rubric/behavior/source/test/relevant-environment changes invalidate them. Preserve old evidence and explicit reasons.\nE. One canonical progress edit renders consistently in item/leader/carry views. Restart/compaction fixtures preserve separate checks/walls, retractions, timestamps, blind-window disclosures and next action without hand-copied narrative.\nF. Contract tests cover message limits, tail/limit incompatibility, projection roots, optional fields and ordinary prose referencing plan items. Valid session reads work; invalid caller inputs are correctly classified. Coordinate the existing transcript repair rather than duplicate it.\nG. Freeze representative workflows; measure before/after tool round trips, agent-authored bookkeeping fields, metadata-only reevaluations, duplicate attempts and request-to-pickup stages. Establish writers, units, population and exclusions. The unambiguous happy path needs no manual ID/hash propagation, copied progress narrative or per-review filter repair. Set percentage/latency targets from baseline before implementation, not invented estimates. Retain receipts; report non-improvements. All safety-negative tests must stay enforced.\n\n## Risks and rollout\nMain risks: treating policy changes as cosmetic, broadening admission, merging distinct reviews, dropping scoped obligations. Each has negative tests above. Shadow-compare derived readiness/bindings/projections against existing readers without granting authority, resolve discrepancies, then use existing rollout controls. Preserve historical evidence and non-destructive rollback. No deployment is authorized by this plan.\n\n## Review boundary\nAvi approved all milestones, A first, for AUTO implementation by this session on SELF route (D-001; source session_turn:codex:01a07c3c-f960-74d3-94b0-d5e1aad2383a:12). Success is less manual administration with unchanged safeguards, not fewer recorded rows. The historical draft-review-only wall is superseded by that explicit approval. Before ready/active/start, re-read the complete source conversation, map requirements/corrections and record the activation audit; resolve source/owner overlap before implementation. Create only the implementation work-items and reviews required by the approved plan; do not mint speculative scorecards or duplicate audits. Non-goals include removing independent review/locks/screening/tenancy, increasing autonomy, staffing changes, old P203/P523/P524 acceptance rewrites and runtime/release/gate operations.\n\n## Sources\nAvi's explicit requests in this session on September 7, 2026: explain coordination/metadata overhead, then write and show an improvement plan for review. Authoring WI-10000533. Evidence: WI-2142873 comments200292/200364, WI-10000531 and the EI refs above. Reviewer coord-send-c992518b91ed8061cd13b5bd1f50bda0dad7545f9857b2f38d0e7cbeb9e668c5 distinguishes repaired allowlist from still-pending admission.\n\n\n## Phase — Milestone A — Remove coordination deadlocks\n\n- **P-001** `done` Map existing writers, resolve ownership overlap, and freeze regression fixtures. After approval, inspect classification/readiness, evidence binding, review admission/handoff and checkpoint writers; identify existing owners and reuse before edits. Freeze fixtures for observed failures and negative policy cases. Measure baseline round trips/metadata from documented writer units and populations; set comparison targets before changes. Acceptance: bounded extension map, exact reproducible fixtures/baseline and no parallel subsystem. Covers R-1-R-7 and acceptance G. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000548 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Normalize metadata and preflight all prerequisites before evaluation. Extend canonical plan/template/spec writers: select class once or ask if ambiguous, derive references/fingerprints, return all discoverable blockers/unknowns together, and revalidate at commit. Acceptance: incomplete and legacy-plan fixtures produce no scorecard before prerequisites are valid, no partial write, stable retry identity; substantive class changes still invalidate evidence. Covers R-1/R-2/R-5, acceptance A/D. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000549 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `todo` Make reviewer handoff resumable and existing-identity-safe. Extend current create/screen/admit/assign/wake/pickup flow and effective per-agent scope resolution, using existing durable execution and idempotency. Repair the exact existing task through authorized policy, never duplicate/re-title/force/broaden scope. Acceptance: restrictive override and pending-screening chain recovers one logical task; crash/concurrent retries, denied scope and revoked authority stay safe; delivery is not pickup. Covers R-3/R-4, acceptance B/C. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000550 blocked (1 external blocker)\n\n\n\n## Phase — Milestone B — Reduce repeat administration\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Separate semantic/policy evidence identity from cosmetic storage revisions. Extend current binding/dependency writers; preserve immutable history and explicit invalidation reasons. Class, rubric, source, test, environment and authorization dimensions remain in the reviewed identity as applicable. Acceptance: only proven presentation/reference equivalence can preserve binding; every substantive or unknown change invalidates the relevant evidence. Do not retroactively relabel the P203 class repair cosmetic. Covers R-5, acceptance D. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000551 blocked (1 external blocker)\n- **P-005** `done` Derive progress views from canonical scoped checkpoints. Reuse item/loop/carry and shared-agent-obligations mechanisms; eliminate copied narrative for one operation without flattening separate item obligations. Acceptance: one edit appears consistently in leader/item/carry views; restart and compaction preserve per-item checks/walls, retractions, provenance, freshness, blind windows and next actions. Coordinate existing owners and leave their separate acceptance lanes alone. Covers R-1, acceptance E. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000552 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Make tool contracts and small read summaries reliable. Derive published constraints/envelopes from runtime validators; cover hidden message limits, tail/limit incompatibility, alias exclusivity, projection roots, optional fields and prose item references. Reuse bounded summaries/detail handles and invocation-ledger correlated friction capture. Coordinate the existing sessions-read defect instead of duplicating its fix. Acceptance: valid reads succeed, caller errors classify correctly, schema tests fail on drift, and common workflows need no guessed payload paths or per-retry manual issues. Covers R-6/R-7, acceptance F. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10000553 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase — Milestone C — Prove and adopt\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Run integrated regression and before/after proof, then controlled adoption. Use frozen representative fixtures and stage-by-stage fault injection; prove all acceptance A-G with exact receipts and exclusions. Show lower manual bookkeeping and no safety regressions; report unchanged/worse metrics honestly. Shadow-compare derived states without granting authority, resolve discrepancies, document non-destructive rollback and use existing rollout mechanisms only after the required review/authorization. No runtime P203 or live-gate shortcut. Covers R-1-R-7. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Avi approved implementation in AUTO on SELF route\nDate: 2026-09-07\n[turn:self] Avi explicitly approved: 'I approve put yourself on auto mode and implement this plan yourself now from start to finish'. Verified source session_turn:codex:01a07c3c-f960-74d3-94b0-d5e1aad2383a:12; full originating conversation turns3-12 re-read in the exact native Codex transcript. This supersedes this plan's draft-review-only execution wall. Implementer is this session su-59b85ff1-6589-4bc0-be1e-756b949ca2f8 itself; no new fleet or builder fan-out. AUTO instructions registered at controlGeneration13. Preserve dependency order, independent review/security/exact evidence and runtime/release boundaries. Draft-authoring WI-10000533 is done; execution driver WI-10000535. The initial add-decision attempt rejected non-P-NNN refs; this retry leaves provenance in the body and does not broaden the tool contract.\n\n### D-002 — P-001 bounded evidence-collection prerequisite and freshness reuse\nDate: 2026-09-07\nWithin the existing P-001 extension-map and reproducible-baseline obligation, this session owns reporter preservation under existing EI-22627645585922385 before collecting a replacement scoped receipt. Scope is scripts/test-files.mjs and its existing test-file-skip-visibility.test.ts suite: retain the admin ledger and armed executed-source-map reporters when injecting private JSON; honor the disable flag, explicit caller reporting, and unavailable reporter paths. Reuse testing:run dual-reporting behavior and the current first-party reporter gates, not a new runner/store. This is not permission to re-label prior NULL-scoped rows or renew historical evidence. P-001 exact freshness proof reuses the independently owned WI-10000450 producer from su-ea913798-2694-4711-84df-3eb1d9c6001e; do not duplicate or edit that peer lane. Existing original reviewer remains independent. No new staff, runtime/restart/rig/release/LIVE_GATE_OPS actions. Existing seven items, R-1–R-7, spec versions and acceptance obligations are unchanged; this records implementation dependencies within P-001, not new scope or an acceptance waiver. Measured: 2026-09-07 source read scripts/test-files.mjs:1200 appends only default+json; libs/test-config/src/vitest-config.ts:101-145 declares admin opt-out and source-map arming; packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/testing/run.ts:1462-1489 already appends admin and stamps child scope. Current repair and P001 work-item reads both assign this session.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-003 — Finish the bounded P-002 phase-test unit, then return directly to P-003 readiness\nDate: 2026-09-08\nAt 2026-09-08T08:49Z, the live source owner for WI-10000550 replied to coord-send-1b39792ac22d06b3a906f2d8fbd8998b9c195d68120b2cacab92a14e58a8a255: `P003 gate remains honestly closed; P002 phase-test atomic unit is running, then I return directly to P003 fidelity.` Acceptance remains blocked on the already-declared generation-1 promoter-source-ready gate. Preserve the source owner's bounded P-002 atomic unit; once it completes, P-003 fidelity/readiness is the immediate next source action. A timeout or queued wake does not authorize acceptance or a takeover. This decision records sequencing only; it does not waive P-003 review, tests, hash evidence, or the real gate fire.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"p203-local-diagnostic-correlation-2026-09-07","title":"P203 local row/stage diagnostic correlation and focused regressions","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-07","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: P203 local row/stage diagnostic correlation and focused regressions\nslug: p203-local-diagnostic-correlation-2026-09-07\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-07\nupdated: 2026-09-26\n---\n\n## Now\nImplement the local diagnostic contract already recorded in WI-2142873 comment200083. This is a subordinate implementation plan for p2p-public-release-endgame-2026-09-01 and WI-2142873, not a replacement release effort. Keep the existing fleet route; no new agents, staffing changes or live-gate work.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10001922 — Extend the existing named-hop helper with an optional local attempt/context event seam and bounded lifecycle semantics. Preserve the legacy signature and promise behavior, distinguish awaited and syn… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001923 — Wire outbox-row attempts through the existing encrypt gate and actual scope/epoch/baseline/key/native dependencies. Preserve cache completion-time TTL, invalidation and single-flight behavior; link d… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001924 — Extend the existing db-org descriptor/result diagnostic channel and query-free localOnly public snapshot with privacy-safe optional correlation. Isolate process/pool/query/attempt identity; preserve … <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001925 — Run and record the combined maintained focused regression matrix across helper, gate/outbox and db-org/public delivery; bind exact source/test bytes and state any omitted or failed leg. Audit R1–R6 p… <!-- P-004 -->\n## Authority and scope\nAvi's current interactive instruction was \"ut yourself on auto mode and continue where you left off\". The session disclosed its interpretation as permission for the pending local diagnostics and focused regressions ONLY. This interpretation is not a claim that Avi separately named each technical detail. AUTO was registered with mode:set; the existing warm 1200-second loop was restored. Runtime profiling, service restarts, soaks, rigs, candidate creation/activation, LIVE_GATE_OPS, productivity-plan changes and staffing remain outside this plan. No banked P523/P524 evidence is rerun or renewed. P203's failed b81 epoch remains RED/cause UNKNOWN; this plan cannot establish runtime causality or release acceptance.\n\n## Source contract\nAuthoritative baseline: WI-2142873 comment200083 (2026-09-07), read in full. Its historical source hashes and assertions remain historical, not current test receipts. Current edit targets must be read before modification. Reuse stage-stall-log.ts, encrypt/decrypt gate seams, outbox-drain and the existing db-org result-diagnostic/public localOnly channel. Add no table, service, background routine, telemetry tool, wire field or parallel diagnostic system.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Identity.** local process-instance/build provenance, outbox row, unique attempt and named sub-hop. Unknown build identity stays explicitly unknown. Repeated attempts and concurrent rows cannot close or relabel one another. Equal connection/query IDs in different process instances/pools cannot correlate accidentally. Do not add fields to LocalWriteOp, AAD or federated envelopes.\n**R-2 — Cache/shared-work truth.** preserve completion-time TTL, invalidation and single-flight behavior. Cache hits invent no PG query. Concurrent attempts stay distinct but reference the same actual shared epoch-load operation. A pending epoch lookup must not be labelled key/crypto work.\n**R-3 — Timing/coverage.** distinguish awaited dependency state, synchronous serialization/native begin/end, and timer-delivery delay. PG build-to-terminal elapsed is not acquisition duration; completed-query records are not in-flight evidence. Elapsed time does not classify CPU, GC, pool pressure or root cause. Unknown, unobserved and evicted linkage is explicit.\n**R-4 — Noninterference/privacy.** disabled or throwing diagnostic consumers preserve returned values, original rejection identity, call counts, selection/eligibility, baseline fail-closed behavior and undrained retry. Never expose plaintext, key material, SQL text or parameters. Appended fields and AAD identity remain unchanged.\n**R-5 — Lifecycle/public delivery.** bounded local retention, immutable query-free snapshots, explicit retention eviction versus result-window omission, settlement/error/expiry cleanup, safe late completion. Diagnostics never cancel business work. Preserve localOnly coverage/failure metadata and acquired-connection-versus-completed-query distinction.\n**R-6 — Regression integrity.** hold each actual awaited dependency independently (scope/epoch SQL, baseline evidence, owner/provider/keychain, native loader); assert reached pending stage and absence of unreached stages. Exercise retry/process/pool isolation, cache/shared-load behavior, disabled/throwing sinks and stable encrypted-content fixtures through real production entry points. Structural assertions must not be called live protocol/queue proof.\n\n## Implementation approach\nWork sequentially because the integration shares files. Establish the existing named-hop helper's optional local context/event seam first; keep old call signatures compatible. Wire row-attempt context through the encrypt path and shared-load/cache boundaries. Extend the existing PG descriptor/result path rather than inventing a new observation channel. Each implementation item carries focused framework tests; a final cross-boundary verification item checks all six requirements without running a live operator or VM.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing named-hop helper and existing PG descriptor/result diagnostics in place. Local correlation is observational and never enters the replicated operation or crypto AAD. All acceptance evidence for this plan is hermetic working-tree evidence.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n\n## Acceptance criteria\nAll R1–R6 must have positive and negative-control evidence in maintained tests; each item records exact source/test identity and the full focused command and result. Tests must be hermetic with fake/injected business dependencies and must not access or mutate the live fleet database. Typechecking supplements tests and is not a substitute. No skipped leg reads as passed. No root-cause, current-runtime, candidate, signing, GO, canary, owner-freeze or shipment claim is permitted from these receipts.\n\n## Preserved evidence\nAll existing loop and work-item check rows retain their evidence dates. Historical profile capture does not prove retained-file coverage or causality. The previously withdrawn first-proxy/cursor absence interpretations remain withdrawn. Completed source-only mapping/contract work and settled P523 audits are not replayed.\n\n## Open boundaries\nRuntime reproduction and causal repair remain a later, separately authorized step. The release driver WI-2037678 has an existing claim_hold: the loop arm did not acquire/bind it, and that refusal is not bypassed. This plan's implementation will hold its own promoted work-items and manual file locks.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Scoped diagnostics and regressions\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend the existing named-hop helper with an optional local attempt/context event seam and bounded lifecycle semantics. Preserve the legacy signature and promise behavior, distinguish awaited and synchronous boundaries, and make disabled/throwing sinks observational only. Add maintained positive/negative tests for unique attempts, late settlement, safe privacy-limited records, cleanup and unchanged returns/rejections. Implements the reusable foundation for R1/R3/R4/R5; does not claim encrypt or PG integration. importance: high — note: ← WI-10001922 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Wire outbox-row attempts through the existing encrypt gate and actual scope/epoch/baseline/key/native dependencies. Preserve cache completion-time TTL, invalidation and single-flight behavior; link distinct attempts to the one shared load, and mark cache hits without inventing PG/crypto work. Exercise held-dependency, concurrent-row/retry and unchanged-encrypted-envelope/AAD controls through production entry points. Covers R1/R2/R3/R4/R6; no runtime actions. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001923 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Extend the existing db-org descriptor/result diagnostic channel and query-free localOnly public snapshot with privacy-safe optional correlation. Isolate process/pool/query/attempt identity; preserve prepared-retry descriptors and honest coverage/timing. Add focused regression tests for isolation, query-free delivery, immutable bounded retention/eviction and failure metadata. No new diagnostic table, tool, service or live database call. Covers R1/R3/R4/R5/R6. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001924 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Run and record the combined maintained focused regression matrix across helper, gate/outbox and db-org/public delivery; bind exact source/test bytes and state any omitted or failed leg. Audit R1–R6 positive/negative controls, preserving historical P523/P524 receipts. Report only local diagnostics verification; leave P203 runtime causality, candidate-ready/P521 and release acceptance unresolved. Complete per-item evidence and final plan audit without live-gate, rigs, profiling or staffing changes. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001925 completed (done)\n\n\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"portal-tab-performance-2026-09-07","title":"Portal tab performance — measure, improve, guard","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-07","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Portal tab performance — measure, improve, guard\nslug: portal-tab-performance-2026-09-07\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-07\nupdated: 2026-09-12\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** ALL 9 ITEMS ARE TERMINAL (7 done, 2 dropped) and implementation is finished. The remaining work is the ship ceremony, not code.\n\nThe keep-alive question that once blocked shipping is SETTLED: D-052/D-053 measured the flagship retention feature as a REGRESSION against this plan's own goal (warmSteady script cost monotone in the retention limit, 2080 -> 2520 -> 3270ms over 34 tabs for limits 1/2/3, no time-to-content benefit, reproduced across two independently-ordered sweeps at loads differing 2.5x). D-056 shipped it OFF. P-003/P-005 were dropped as a consequence. That is an honest negative result, not an unfinished item.\n\nSteady state is CLOSED at the coverage R-4 names: D-059's 5-cycle 34-tab run shows heap is a PLATEAU (deltas +8.47, +0.17, +0.36, +0.76 MB), with all controls passing and VOID false. The same run RETRACTED D-058's \"handle counts are flat\" as a 2-cycle artifact and surfaced a small monotone timeout accumulation (~2 per 34-tab cycle), filed as WI-10000663 and NOT blocking this plan.\n\nIndependent acceptance grading is DONE and SETTLED: su-07cc82ce (non-lineage) rates 7 healthy / 0 degraded, having revised r-4 to healthy on the bar's own subject (R-4 grades whether the METRIC SET can locate a cost, not whether the system leaks). NO card has landed yet.\n\nTHE ONE THING BLOCKING SHIP is the acceptance BAR contract, not the work: plans:get { shipReadiness:true } refuses acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready. All 7 criteria carry method:null and no `check` key, and rubric rev 1 is pinned to subjectPlanRevision 10 while the plan is at 103.\n\n⚠ Do NOT quote the `warmFirst ttc` column from either dose-response sweep: it reads -26%/-27% and is DRIFT (10-18 of ~33 moving tabs disagree in SIGN between two passes of the SAME arm).\n\n**Next:** su-2ae94ea1 (implementer) repairs the BAR contract: rubrics:propose filling `method` + a structured `check` on all 7 criteria while resubmitting bar/barKey/barHash/model/driftMarkers/role/mandatory/requiredScope/evidencePlane/passRatings BYTE-IDENTICAL (bars must not change outside rubrics:amend), then plans:audit { phase:'activation' } to re-pin the rubric revision to the plan's current version. NOTE: every later plan CONTENT write re-breaks that pin, so no further set-now/set-status after the audit. Then vet via consult:get_feedback { policy:'rubric-vetting' }, ping su-07cc82ce to re-emit his settled 7-healthy ratings verbatim, record the author acceptance verdict, and ship.\n\n## Background\n\n`http://127.0.0.1:3081/` is a stable proxy (`papercusp-cloud-portal-proxy.mjs`) in front of the\nCloud Portal backend on `127.0.0.1:3801` — a **Next 16.3.3 production standalone release**\n(`papercusp-cloud-portal.service`), built 2026-09-07T05:11Z, running from\n`.portal-runtime/portal/current`. Source checkout: `portal/` (own git repo, branch `staging`,\nsymlinked from the workspace). The working tree is NOT what :3081 serves — a code change requires\n`npm run build` + `deploy-cloud-portal.sh` to go live.\n\n**The rail has 34 destinations** (`PORTAL_APP_KINDS` in `portal/packages/contracts/src/index.ts`),\n14 pinned by default. Two mount classes:\n\n- **In-shell modules** — Home, Mail, Calendar, Phone, Workspaces.\n- **Natively-mounted operator surfaces** — the other ~30. These used to be `<iframe>`s of the\n  operator origin; `portal/packages/ui/src/operator-host.tsx` replaced the frames with direct\n  React mounts of the operator's own components, each behind `lazy()` + `Suspense`.\n\n### Measured baseline (2026-09-07, before any change)\n\nServer side is not the problem: TTFB on `/` is **11ms**, document 38.7KB.\n\nFirst paint ships **~2.1MB raw / ~561KB gzipped** of JS+CSS *before any tab is opened*:\n\n| asset | raw | gzip |\n|---|---|---|\n| `chunks/1918-*.js` (vendor) | 576KB | 172KB |\n| `chunks/app/page-*.js` (the shell) | 389KB | 114KB |\n| `css/67230937*.css` | 295KB | 41KB |\n| `chunks/3794-*.js` | 241KB | 66KB |\n| `chunks/4bd1b696-*.js` | 201KB | 63KB |\n| `chunks/polyfills-*.js` | 113KB | 40KB |\n| 4 more CSS files | 218KB | 37KB |\n| 4 more JS chunks | 71KB | 27KB |\n\nThe deployed build holds 332 client chunks / 26MB of JS and 1.8MB of CSS in total. The genuinely\nhuge libraries are already lazily split and are NOT on the first-paint path (excalidraw 3.2MB,\nand the 1.8MB/1.4MB chunks) — so the opportunity is in the shell, the vendor chunk, the CSS and\nthe polyfills, not in the obvious monsters.\n\nSource-side signal: `portal/app/globals.css` is 178KB of hand-written CSS in one file;\n`portal/packages/ui/src/shell.tsx` is 3,734 lines.\n\n### The tab-switch remount\n\n`OperatorSurfaceBody` renders `<SurfaceErrorBoundary key={kind}>`. The key is deliberate and\ncorrect for error isolation (documented in-file: a shared boundary latches, so one crashed\nsurface poisoned every tab opened after it). Its **side effect** is that switching tabs unmounts\nthe previous surface's whole tree and mounts the next one fresh — so returning to a tab pays the\nfull mount cost again: re-render, re-fetch, re-open SSE. Whether that is a real user-visible cost\nor noise is exactly what P-002 must measure before P-004 touches it.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Every rail destination is measured.** All 34 `PORTAL_APP_KINDS` destinations appear in the baseline artifact, not a sampled subset, and the harness derives the tab list from the contract so a newly added destination extends coverage without a code edit.\n\n**R-2 — A perf claim is a measured delta, never an assertion.** The same harness produces a JSON artifact diffable against a stored baseline; every improvement this plan claims cites a before/after from that artifact, and a change whose delta falls inside the measured noise band is recorded as \"not measured\", never as \"improved\".\n\n**R-3 — Both user journeys are covered.** The baseline reports cold load (`/?app=<kind>` from a clean browser context) and warm switch (rail click between already-loaded tabs) separately, because they have different costs and different fixes.\n\n**R-4 — The metric set is sufficient to locate a cost, not just detect one.** Per tab: FCP, LCP, time-to-content, total blocking time and long tasks, script evaluation time, bytes transferred cold and warm, JS heap after mount, and heap growth across a full 34-tab cycle as a leak signal.\n\n**R-5 — Performance work does not regress correctness.** `npm run test`, the Playwright `e2e/` specs and `npm run typecheck` are green at every point a change is deployed, and per-surface error-boundary isolation still holds after any change to the mount policy — one crashed surface must not poison the tabs opened after it.\n\n**R-6 — Improvements are proven on the surface the owner actually uses.** Each implemented change is measured against a build genuinely serving on :3081 (D-002), not against a dev server or the source tree.\n**R-7 — The gains survive this plan.** A committed perf-budget guard fails CI when a future change re-inflates first-paint payload or tab-switch cost past the agreed budget, so a regression is caught by a test rather than by a user.\n\n## Design\n\n**Instrument first, then optimise.** Portal already has `@playwright/test` 1.59.1, a\n`playwright.config.ts` and an `e2e/` directory, and system `google-chrome` is present — so the\nharness is a new spec/script in that existing seam, not new infrastructure.\n\nThe harness drives the REAL deployed surface on `:3081` (not a fixture) because the question is\nabout the product a user touches. It walks `PORTAL_APP_KINDS` (34 today), so adding a rail destination\nautomatically extends coverage — the tab list is derived from the contract, never hand-listed.\n\nMeasurement uses the browser's own instrumentation (PerformanceObserver for paint/LCP/longtask,\n`performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` for transfer, CDP `Performance.getMetrics` +\n`Runtime.evaluate` heap for memory) rather than wall-clock guesses, and reports a median over N\nrepeats so a single noisy run cannot be mistaken for a regression.\n\nKnown caveat to respect: this box runs ~100 concurrent agents, so absolute timings are noisy.\nThe harness therefore reports **medians with spread**, and any claimed win must exceed the\nmeasured noise band — a number inside the noise is \"not measured\", never \"improved\".\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002 | deployed |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002 | deployed |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-002 | deployed |\n| R-5 | P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n\nHow each bar is discharged: R-1 by the harness deriving its tab list from `PORTAL_APP_KINDS`, so\nthe artifact has a row per destination. R-2 by P-002 establishing the noise band and P-008\nrecording the before/after table. R-3 and R-4 by the artifact's per-tab metric set, cold-load and\nwarm-switch reported separately. R-5 by the portal's own suites being green before each deploy,\nwith P-004 additionally owning per-surface error isolation. R-6 by every re-measure running\nagainst the build actually serving :3081 (D-002). R-7 by the committed perf-budget guard.\n\nThe `deployed` plane on R-1/R-2/R-3/R-4/R-6 is the point of D-002: these bars are claims about the\nrunning portal, so tree-only evidence cannot discharge them. R-5 and R-7 are tree bars because a\ngreen suite and a committed guard live in the repo.\n\n## Phase 1 — Instrument and baseline\n\n- **P-001** `done` Build the repeatable Playwright perf harness over all `PORTAL_APP_KINDS`: cold load + warm switch, capturing paint/LCP/TBT/long-tasks/transfer/heap, medians with spread, JSON artifact output — note: ← WI-10000536 completed (done)\n\n8 harness defects found and fixed, 6 of them false-zero/false-positive shapes that would have produced confident WRONG findings: a 25s timeout reported as a legitimate 25009ms measurement; content detected from the topbar before any surface rendered; a remount detector that reported \"kept alive\" for every tab; a More-panel selector aimed at the PIN button (which MUTATED live state, pinning 9 apps to the rail); a roleless loading placeholder classified as \"surface not registered\"; and a cmdk Enter race that reported a switch-that-never-happened as the destination tab timing out at 20s.\n\nVerified the probe mutates no state (pinnedApps re-…\n- **P-002** `done` Record the committed baseline for all 34 tabs and rank them by cost; identify the noise band so later deltas are judgeable blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10000543 completed (done)\n\nRanking (cold ms): settings 1732 · dev 1136 · create 1092 · learning 947 · scheduled 939 · workflows 900 · hud 847 · inbox 844 · conversations 834 · support 830 · evals 829 · health 827 · testing 826 · plans 824 · cloud 820 · adv-settings 814 · cupboard 810 · docs 805 · desktops 803 · brainstorm 802 · stats 792 · overview 791 · frames 789 · prs 788 · insights 786 · coord 785 · work 784 · history 783 · git 777 · workspaces 626 · mail 490 · phone 458 · calendar 449 · home 106.\n\nTwo outliers worth their own items: settings (1732ms cold AND 680ms warm, ~2x the next tab on both) and workspaces (626ms cold but 1614ms WARM, the only tab whose warm exceeds its cold by an order of magnitude). Every other tab warms in 2-38ms.\n\nRoot cause for the shared plateau recorded as D-005…\n\n## Phase 2 — Improve, re-measuring each change\n\n- **P-003** `dropped` Cut the first-paint payload (561KB gz today): CSS splitting/pruning of the 178KB globals.css, browserslist/polyfill trim, shell chunk splitting blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10000572 completed (dropped)\n- **P-004** `done` Tab-switch cost: decide and implement a keep-alive/remount policy for operator surfaces that preserves per-surface error isolation blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10000627 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `dropped` Attack the worst individual tabs the baseline names — per-surface mount cost, oversized lazy chunks, unvirtualized lists blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10000557 completed (dropped)\n- **P-006** `done` Steady-state cost: SSE/polling cadence, roster refresh, timers, and heap growth across a full tab cycle blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10000641 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Lock it in\n\n- **P-007** `done` Commit a perf-budget guard test so a future change that re-inflates first paint or tab-switch cost fails CI blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-10000640 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Final re-measure across all 34 tabs, record the before/after delta table on this plan blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-10000647 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase — P-004 disposition\n\n- **P-009** `done` Decide and execute P-004's disposition in light of D-052 and D-053. The keep-alive retention feature is SHIPPED and is a measured REGRESSION against this plan's own goal: warmSteady script cost rises monotonically with the retention limit (2080 -> 2520 -> 3270ms summed over 34 tabs for limits 1/2/3), with no measured time-to-content benefit, reproduced across two independently-ordered sweeps at load regimes differing 2.5x (+58% and +57% on the endpoint pair). The decision is NOT foreclosed by that. P-004 may still be worth keeping for reasons this plan never measured — preserved scroll position, in-progress form state, and avoided refetch on revisit are user-visible properties that a per-switch script-time metric cannot see, and `?keepAlive=0` collapsing to limit 1 means the lever already exists to tune rather than revert. What is NOT defensible is leaving it shipped at limit 3 while the only evidence anyone has says limit 3 is the worst of the three doses. Do, in order: 1. LOCALISE the cost before choosing. Both sweeps read one metric family (CDP ScriptDuration deltas), so the retained-tree mechanism is dose-consistent but still [inferred]; a trace-level pass (scripts/trace-probe.mts + trace-buckets.mts) should say WHERE the extra script time lands. If it is hidden surfaces re-rendering or keeping subscriptions live, that is also a fixable bug in RetainedSurfaces rather than an argument against retention as such — freeze harder and the cost may go away while the benefit stays. 2. Weigh the unmeasured benefits explicitly, naming them, rather than deciding on the one number this plan happens to have. 3. Choose: revert, lower the default limit (limit 2 is measurably cheaper than 3 and still retains one surface), make retention conditional on tab weight, or fix the per-switch cost and keep limit 3. 4. Record the call as a plan decision citing D-052/D-053, and re-measure the chosen configuration with scripts/perf-dose-response.sh so the plan ships against evidence rather than intent. Re-measurement needs a P-004-carrying build served somewhere isolated — D-050 has the recipe (PORTAL_BUILD_ONLY=1, isolated PORTAL_HOME); the :3082 rig used for D-052/D-053 has a hard deadline of 02:22Z on 2026-09-08 and will need rebuilding after that. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000650 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Route: this session implements the plan directly, with a tracked engine loop\nDate: 2026-09-07\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-07] Asked to choose between (A) this session, (B) an active fleet, (C) a new visible desktop fleet, (D) a new headless fleet, the owner chose A, \"Me, this session\".\n\nWhy it fits the work: every Phase-2 item is blocked-by P-002, so there is no parallel lane until the baseline exists, and each fix must be re-measured with the SAME harness on the SAME box before the next lands - fan-out would produce numbers that cannot be compared. The three fleets with live members at decision time (p2p-release-sol-endgame 2, byoc-alpha-ship-2026-09-05 2, main-green-reds-2026-09-05 1) were all on unrelated lanes.\n\nRecurrence is a tracked engine loop (loop:arm), not Claude /loop.\n\nMeasured: fleet:list at 2026-09-07T14:47Z - 338 fleets, 3 with liveMemberCount>0, none portal-scoped.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-002 — Deploy: rebuild and redeploy :3081 freely, once per measure-fix-re-measure cycle\nDate: 2026-09-07\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-07] Asked how much deploy rope, the owner chose \"Build + deploy freely\" over phase-boundary-only and no-deploy.\n\nConsequence for evidence: a perf claim about :3081 counts only when measured against a build actually serving on :3081. Measuring a dev server or the source tree and reporting it as a :3081 improvement is out of contract (R-6).\n\nThe restart is safe by design: papercusp-cloud-portal-proxy.mjs holds retryable (GET/HEAD) requests across the bounded gap while :3801 hands off, and never replays a mutating request.\n\nMeasured: /home/marsh-office/.local/bin/papercusp-cloud-portal-proxy.mjs - isRetryablePortalRequest() returns true only for GET/HEAD; default retry window 15000ms.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-003 — Autonomy: AUTO mode with an armed engine loop for the duration\nDate: 2026-09-07\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-07] Asked how autonomous to be, the owner chose \"AUTO + armed loop\" over per-phase check-ins and ask-first.\n\nSo: pick each next item by evidence, act without asking, and DISCLOSE rather than ask. Owner-walled actions (credentials, capital, category-1/irreversible) still stop. The loop is the recurrence mechanism - AUTO is only an authorization posture and arms no wake by itself.\n\nMeasured: mode:set { mode:'auto' } at 2026-09-07T14:49Z returned wakeSource:'owner-only' with an explicit no-wake-source warning, which is why loop:arm accompanies it rather than following later.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-004 — A perf probe must not mutate the surface it measures\nDate: 2026-09-07\nMeasuring the portal must leave the portal exactly as it was found. This is now a standing constraint on the harness and on P-007's guard, not a one-off repair.\n\nWHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A BUG NOTE: the harness reached non-pinned tabs through the More panel with the locator `.portal-more-entry ... locator(\"button\")`. The entries are cmdk `Command.Item`s rendered as `[cmdk-item]` (role=option), and the ONLY <button> inside `.portal-more-entry` is `.portal-more-pin`. So the probe was clicking PIN. It never navigated - it silently rewrote the owner's rail layout, then timed out and recorded the tab as slow.\n\nMeasured: after one partial baseline run, GET /api/preferences returned 22 pinnedApps against a DEFAULT_PINNED_PORTAL_APP_KINDS of 13 - 9 apps pinned by the probe (brainstorm, health, prs, insights, conversations, adv-settings, docs, history, stats). Restored with PUT /api/preferences to the default 13 and verified; theme and dismissals were untouched.\n\nThe damage was doubly bad because it was SELF-CONCEALING: the mutation produced a timeout, and a timeout reads as \"this tab is slow\" - so the probe corrupted state AND manufactured a plausible-looking performance finding about the very tabs it corrupted. Had the run completed, those 9 tabs would have entered the baseline as the worst performers on the strength of an artifact the probe itself created.\n\nCONSEQUENCES, binding for the rest of this plan:\n1. Drive a surface by its real affordance, not by whatever element a CSS descendant selector happens to reach. The fix types into the More panel's own search box and presses Enter, which is the user path and depends on no item markup.\n2. Any probe run must be preceded and followed by a state check on what it could plausibly have changed. `pinnedApps.length` is the cheap one here and is now checked after every run.\n3. A timeout is never on its own evidence about the SUBJECT. Ask what the instrument did before concluding the tab is slow.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-007\n\n### D-005 — Cold tab cost is hydration-serialized, not bandwidth-bound\nDate: 2026-09-07\nMeasured on the deployed release build (:3081 -> :3801 next-server), baseline-v2, 34 tabs x 3 repeats.\n\nShell first paint is IDENTICAL for every tab: document 9KB + JS 446KB + CSS 80KB, 17 requests, FCP ~100-160ms. Every tab's differentiating cost is POST-FCP.\n\nThat post-FCP cost is NOT bandwidth-bound, and the data refutes the obvious reading three separate ways:\n  - coord transfers 657KB and costs 657ms postFCP; inbox transfers 1905KB and costs 724ms. ~3x the bytes for ~1.1x the time.\n  - request count INVERTS the ranking (coord +24 requests is slower per-byte than git +59).\n  - TBT stays <=165ms and long tasks total ~258ms of an ~850ms load, so it is not CPU-saturated either.\n\nThe waterfall shows why. On EVERY tab there is a window with nothing whatsoever in flight, beginning the moment the shell's JS finishes:\n  coord 67->350 (283ms) | dev 66->379 (313ms) | health 67->379 (312ms) | frames 67->395 (328ms)\nThe shell JS lands at ~67ms; the surface's own lazy chunk is not REQUESTED until ~380-460ms. The active kind is known from the ?app= query param at SSR time, so nothing about that ordering is forced -- the surface download is simply serialized AFTER shell hydration instead of overlapping it.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN: per-surface JS splitting is already working (29 lazy entries, and warm re-entry into a cached surface is 2-17ms). Optimising individual surfaces' bundle size therefore attacks the wrong term. The shared ordering is the lever.\n\nCAVEAT ON SIZE OF PRIZE, stated because it bounds P-003: for coord the chunk fetch itself only occupies ~75ms of wall clock, so overlapping it recovers less than the 283ms window suggests. The window is part hydration-CPU (~172ms of long tasks) and part idle. Reducing the 446KB hydration payload and overlapping the fetch are two different fixes and should be measured separately.\n\nSTILL OPEN, deliberately not attributed to a mechanism: several tabs show a SECOND window with no network AND no long task -- coord 535->832 (297ms), frames 601->880 (279ms), health 1206->1451 (245ms) -- but dev shows none. Ruled out so far: it is not a setTimeout/setInterval (instrumented setTimeout/setInterval before app code; zero timers scheduled at >=150ms), and it is not an unterminated stream hiding from the gap detector (positive control: zero resources with responseEnd 0). Remaining candidate is main-thread work time-sliced below the 50ms longtask threshold, which is invisible to both instruments used so far. Do not cite a cause for this gap until an event-loop-lag measurement settles it.\n\n### D-006 — baseline-v2's warm bytes/requests column is INVALID — instrument defect, now fixed and re-measured\nDate: 2026-09-07\nEvery lane reading `portal/perf/baseline.json` must treat its warm `transferredBytes` and `requestCount` as UNMEASURED, not as zero. Every other warm metric in that artifact stands.\n\n**The defect.** `scripts/perf-probe.mts` computed per-switch network cost as `performance.getEntriesByType(\"resource\").filter(e => e.startTime >= t0)` on the ONE long-lived page the warm pass shares across all tabs and repeats. Chromium's resource-timing buffer holds 250 entries and then silently stops recording; the probe never cleared it and never raised it.
