Build the e2e proof.\n\nSEQUENCING: prove the full chain (bind → evaluate → verdict pass → scorecards:emit terminal → gate accepts) on ONE cheap l3 clause BEFORE mass-producing evidence for nine. The details contract is exacting — details.adequacy.{testLayer,pathReachable,oracleIndependent,fixtureCalibrated,falsifiable,collected,skipped,executed,outcome,targeted,coverageRungs,scenarioIds,causalPairIds} — and a wrong shape degrades silently to 'unknown' rather than erroring.\n\nTOOL GOTCHAS (each cost a round trip): `limit` on plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy caps the EVIDENCE SET not rows (limit:1 → {ok:false,error:'evidence_selection_hit_limit'}, no rows key); an unprojected call truncates rows and its marker misreported 'totalCount 5' when the true count was 9, so always pass a projection and read `count`/`verdicts`; clauses resolve through planItemIds:['P-007'] — workItemIds:['WI-10000429'] returns count 0; plans:get-spec-evidence returns rows under key `evidence`, not `rows`.\n\n### D-015 — PUI-FILE-CONTEXT: implement the composer @ picker rather than drop it; pin PUBLIC_RELEASE_UX affordances against the code\nDate: 2026-09-11\n**Owner ruling [owner:Avi 2026-09-11] [turn:self], recorded because it governs P-007's scope and the shipped doc.**\n\n#### The finding that prompted it\n`apps/tui/PUBLIC_RELEASE_UX.md:315-319` (repeated in the acceptance table at `:384`) promises: \"When the composer is focused, @ opens a project-scoped file/attachment picker… Cross-project and unreadable paths are refused with the reason; PUI never falls back to a similarly named file.\"\n\nNone of it is implemented.\n\n**Measured: 2026-09-11, scope = the ENTIRE `apps/tui` tree (51 `.rs` files under `apps/tui/src`, plus `build.rs` and `apps/tui/tests/*.rs`), not one module:**\n- `grep -rn \"Char('@')\\|'@' =>\\|== '@'\" apps/tui/` -> 0 matches\n- `grep -rn \"'@'\\|\\\"@\\\"\\|b'@'\" apps/tui/src/` -> 0 matches (no `@` character in the TUI source at all)\n- `grep -rn \"attachments\\|Attachment\" apps/tui/src/*.rs` -> 0 matches (no composer attachment state)\n- `grep -rn \"Cross-project\\|cross-project\" apps/tui/` -> 0 matches outside PUBLIC_RELEASE_UX.md itself\n- The only 3 files matching `attachment` (`transcript.rs:17`, `brain_view.rs:154`, `client.rs:1036`) concern session RE-attachment — unrelated to files.\n- Modules that DO mention \"picker\" (`session_config.rs`, `models.rs`, `workbench.rs`, …) are the model/mode/account/session pickers documented elsewhere.\n\n⚠ The scope is stated deliberately. Earlier in the same session a `find -maxdepth 4` produced a convincing FALSE absence (the claude-agent-sdk, installed one level deeper), so this absence was established by searching the whole tree twice rather than by one bounded grep. A bounded search's empty result is not an absence.\n\nP-007's clause **PUI-FILE-CONTEXT@4** (falsifier: *\"picker attaches content from an unselected project or needs native UI\"*) therefore had nothing to exercise — unprovable because the behaviour does not exist, not because a test was missing.\n\n#### The ruling\nPresented three options (implement / drop the clause and retract the doc promise / defer to a later item). Avi chose **implement the picker**, as documented — including the cross-project + unreadable refusal WITH reason and no similar-name fallback, since that refusal IS the clause's falsifier rather than polish. Tracked as **WI-10001039**.\n\nAvi separately approved **pinning the acceptance table**: a doc-claims test (`packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/`) asserting every keyboard affordance PUBLIC_RELEASE_UX.md promises has a matching key handler in `apps/tui`, so a promise with no implementation fails the build.\n\n#### Why the pin, and why it is a plan-level decision\nThis is the SECOND documented-but-unimplemented affordance found in this plan (EI-22982452433293308 was the first). Two independent instances make PUBLIC_RELEASE_UX.md a prose surface asserting code truth with no divergence check — precisely what the derived-truth ladder says to DERIVE, PIN, or ATTEST rather than hand-maintain. Without the pin, later plan items keep discovering these one clause at a time during acceptance, which is the expensive moment to find them.\n\n**Consequence for other lanes:** do not treat PUBLIC_RELEASE_UX.md as evidence that a behaviour exists. Check the affordance against the Rust source before writing a clause test or reporting an item complete. THE LIFECYCLE LIVES IN THE BINARY. `pui self install|update|rollback|uninstall|status` implements versioned releases under $PUI_HOME (default $XDG_DATA_HOME/pui): immutable `releases/<version>-<sha12>/`, `current` + `previous` links, `~/.local/bin/pui` -> current. CLAUSE EVIDENCE (D-014): release-acceptance.integration.test.ts. A journey must wait for the canonical projection (DB settled, then 'saving…' gone) before the next key, as a person would; a DB-only wait races the UI.\n\n### D-021 — PUI Claude default-mode approvals: auto-allow only server-advertised read-only SU tools (host capability_* family excluded); writes keep asking with a session-scoped remembered choice; tools:invoke is a write\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23 [self-imposed under AUTO, su-091ad703; D-011 solo route; disclosed, not asked]. Governs WI-10002759 and P-012's native-question journey (PUI_INSTALLED_NATIVE_QUESTION_ACCEPTANCE, Linux x86_64 x Claude cell).\n\nMEASURED (2026-09-23 16:20-16:40Z, reading HEAD): su-session-claude-engine.ts launches PUI Claude runtimes with permissionMode 'default' + settingSources user/project/local; every one of those settings files is empty on this box, so EVERY papercusp-su MCP call reaches canUseTool -> su-session-native-cards.ts handleClaude -> an Approve/Decline owner card. FOUND WHILE MEASURING: tools:invoke is registered under capability agent_tools:read with no explicit effect, so it is advertised readOnlyHint:true although it dispatches ANY tool (capability:bash included) - wrong for replay safety and for any annotation-keyed approval.\n\nDECISION:\n1. The PUI Claude engine auto-allows a papercusp-su tool ONLY when the connected server advertises it readOnly, it is not in the host capability_* family (host file/code reads keep native approval parity), and the SDK did not attach matchedAskRule (a user ask rule always wins). Everything else keeps the owner card. Unknown or newly listed tools ask (fail-closed).\n2. tools:invoke becomes effect 'write' with an argument-sensitive effectForCall that returns the target's own effect, matching code:run's contract, so its advertised annotation is truthful.\n3. The approval card gains the PUBLIC_RELEASE_UX 'broader remembered permission' secondary choice whenever the SDK supplies allow suggestions. It is applied with destination 'session' only (a PUI card never writes settings files) and its label names the exact rule and that lifetime.\n4. The directive-disposition loop is NOT changed: PUI turns are owner turns and the SU dispositioning them is correct psu semantics.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: SU bookkeeping WRITES (orders_disposition, declare-intent, checkpoints) still ask once in default mode; the owner can remember them for the session. That is native Claude Code default-mode parity. The acceptance journeys must therefore answer an approval card when one appears instead of assuming none will.\n\nOPEN (owner, non-blocking): whether coordination-state writes (coord:write, work_items:write, plans:write) should be auto-allowed in default mode is a security-posture broadening I did not take; it is recorded here for the owner, not decided.\n\n### D-022 — Allow the owner directive bookkeeping write without a native approval card\nDate: 2026-09-23\n[self-imposed] [turn:self] WI-10002759 measured an installed PUI real-Claude turn reaching `mcp__papercusp-su__orders_disposition` after a normal owner message and parking on its native approval card, so the turn/composer never settles. Root cause: PUI's `canUseTool` auto-allows only advertised read-only SU tools; `orders_disposition` is advertised as a write, so it falls through to the card handler. Ruling: In PUI default prompt mode, auto-allow only the exact `orders_disposition` tool advertised by the `papercusp-su` server as writable, and only when no user ask rule matched. Preserve approval cards for every other write, all host capability tools, unknown servers/tools, and any call matched by a user ask rule. This narrows the D-021 open scope to the required SU-owned directive bookkeeping operation; it does not authorize a blanket MCP or write-tool bypass.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-023 — The task-reaper's managed-residue class spares a no-row scope that a live out-of-scope parent still holds\nDate: 2026-09-24\nDate: 2026-09-24 [self-imposed under AUTO, su-091ad703; D-011 solo route; disclosed, not asked]. The same applies to any isolated-store operator on this box (e.g. VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB desktops).\n\nRULING: 'Managed residue' means a no-row scope that NOBODY holds. `systemd-run --scope` execs the payload in the process its spawner forked, so a scope's root stays the spawner's child while the spawner lives, and is reparented to the user manager (…/init.scope) or pid 1 once the spawner dies. decideReaps now spares a no-row candidate when readScopeHolder finds a live parent outside the scope that is not init.scope, and also when the holder is unmeasurable (unmeasurable never authorizes a kill). It is folded into the hosted session key only when it is not psu, so every existing psu key is unchanged.\nThe remote pui gets NO PUI_OPERATOR from the controller. Like remote psu, it uses the host's own default operator selection. Measured live on avi-test: 'op http://127.0.0.1:3070' with the host's store pg-eb6b47745e43, which is not this box's pg-30bc975dfc43.\n`pui --connect` ALWAYS means a remote host: the pui picker has no 'this computer' entry, and --connect=local or a cancelled pick is refused. There is no hand-back-to-local contract, because psu passes the remote exit status through, so no status value is unambiguous. A pui launched with PAPERCUSP_PSU_CONNECTION_FORWARDED=1 refuses --connect. PUI finds the controller as `psu` on PATH, so a missing psu is refused with a hint.\n\nWhy not a local PUI on a forwarded remote operator: it would need a remote-operator token and an HTTP/SSE path that hosted workspaces lack (WI-10002873), and it would fork transport logic that psu maintains. 'Like our psu utility' rules out that second copy.\n\nEvidence (P-017 done 06:10Z, adequacy 3/3 on work item WI-10002893):\n- P017-PUI-HANDOFF: cargo 1115/0/17; remote-connect-handoff.integration 4/4 (test_runs 19248742); counterexample on the pre-P-017 binary, 3 red.\n- P017-CONTROLLER-PROGRAM: 21/21 (test_runs 19245767); counterexample on blob 97c4ca28cb, 4 red.\n- P017-REMOTE-LIVE: hermetic relay e2e 2/2 (test_runs 19248752), which on the old controller runs psu on the workspace; plus the live avi-test journey (WI-10002893#1143048).\nThe gcp-iap-ssh kind was not exercised live.\nRelated: P-017\n\n### D-026 — PUI public artifacts use Apache-2.0 and the existing Papercusp copyright line\nDate: 2026-09-24\nDate: 2026-09-24\nRULING: PUI, pui-companion and pui-companion-proto are distributed under Apache-2.0. Source: WI-10003295 (filed by su-f4481f51, measured: r8 and r9 bin/pui exit 127 in stock ubuntu:24.04 because cpal/rodio put libasound.so.2 in DT_NEEDED). Authority: D-031 (3), the bounded usability pass, whose route [owner:Avi 2026-09-26] was 'You, this session'.\n\nRULING: the main `pui` binary no longer links cpal or rodio. All device I/O (PTT capture, stream capture, device listing, Player playback, and the operator-voice-bus mic and mix playback) moves into a sibling binary, `pui-audio`, built from the same crate and shipped in the archive's bin/. pui drives it over stdin/stdout with a length-prefixed frame protocol. pui keeps its existing public voice API (CaptureSession, StreamCapture, Player, start_mic, start_playback, list_devices) as thin proxies, so callers do not change, and pure DSP/WAV code stays in pui. If pui-audio cannot start (exit 127, missing libasound2), voice reports a named, remediable error ('voice needs ALSA: install libasound2') and nothing else in pui is affected.\n\nREJECTED: (a) bundling libasound.so.2 (adds LGPL-2.1 distribution obligations beyond D-026, and a bundled copy cannot find the host's PipeWire ALSA plugin on non-Debian layouts); (b) static alsa-lib (duplicates alsa state when the host plugin loads the shared lib; LGPL relinking); (c) removing DT_NEEDED and binding lazily (requires dropping full RELRO/BIND_NOW hardening; fragile); (d) building the public release without voice (a product-scope cut the owner did not choose).\n\nRECURRENCE GUARD: the release stage gains a stock-container smoke (ubuntu:24.04 and debian:stable-slim, no libasound2) that runs install.sh, `pui --version`, `pui doctor` and `psu`, and refuses the candidate on any failure. [] <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000612 — Add the billing-export descriptor to existing GCP connection config and implement a public BigQuery API reader using existing Google auth/transport. Cover gross/credits/net, empty and malformed resul… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000613 — Extend hosted-lifecycle reconciliation with a bounded due-spend sweep that atomically read-modify-writes `cost_signals`, preserves prior evidence/deferral history, deduplicates retries, and exposes c… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000614 — Run focused/affected tests and typechecks, prove the existing durable routine invokes the path, and reconcile R4/R5 only if supported export config/data exists; otherwise record the exact external bl… <!-- P-004 -->\n## Background\n\nD-274 persists `spendSettlement.reconcileAfter` so teardown can proceed before delayed billing settles, but no production reader revisits that obligation and no supported provider-cost producer exists. R4/R5 forensic evidence proves exact sub-cent charges exist; it does not settle the persisted rows.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Use only the supported provider cost surface.** GCP production reads use Cloud Billing export through the public BigQuery API, never the private Console `BillingData` GraphQL endpoint.\n\n**R-002 — Reuse the existing connection and credential seams.** Store a typed, non-secret billing-export descriptor on the existing workspace-host connection; reuse its cloud credential and Google auth transport.\n\n**R-003 — Preserve exact accounting and conservative safety gates.** Preserve exact gross, credits, net micros and currency. Keep existing integer-cents budget gates conservative; never round spend down or equate net-zero-after-credit with zero gross usage.\n\n**R-004 — Reconcile the retained ledger atomically and idempotently.** Reconcile the surviving host row by atomic, idempotent read-modify-write of the whole `cost_signals` array. Preserve every prior signal and the original deferral history.\n\n**R-005 — Extend the existing durable routine.** Extend the existing durable `hosted-lifecycle-reconcile` routine. Add no credential store, spend-obligation table, or second scheduler.\n\n**R-006 — Keep unavailable or unstable settlement explicit and retryable.** Missing config, permission, data, or finality stays explicit and retryable. Empty rows are not zero, and one observation is not automatically final.\n\n**R-007 — Do not manufacture live R4/R5 settlement.** The live billing account currently exposes no BigQuery dataset. R4/R5 remain unsettled until a supported producer is configured and returns authoritative data.\n\n**R-008 — Preserve the independent BYOC authority walls.** This work never mints credentials, replays lifecycle operations, tears down R7, or opens the G6/r31 gate.\n\n## Design\n\nAdd a provider-neutral exact spend observation and settlement history. Add a GCP BigQuery-export adapter with validated table identity, parameterized project/run-label filters, bounded query bytes, and typed retry/absence outcomes. Extend hosted lifecycle reconciliation to scan due deferrals, resolve each retained host's existing connection, call the adapter, and converge the matching signal without losing unrelated entries.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-002 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-004 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-006 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-007 | P-004 | live |\n| R-008 | P-004 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — exact settlement contract\n\n- **P-001** `done` Define exact-micros/currency spend observations, conservative cents derivation, and settlement-history/finality semantics; update validators and unit tests. [importance: high] — note: ← WI-10000611 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Supported GCP producer\n\n- **P-002** `done` Add the billing-export descriptor to existing GCP connection config and implement a public BigQuery API reader using existing Google auth/transport. Add integration tests for unrelated-signal preservation and convergence. [importance: high] [blocked-by: P-003] — note: Verified in WI-10000662; independent audits WI-10000670 passed. WI-10000614 is retained as a superseded evidence record. Supported billing export remains missing; no settlement claimed.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Public BigQuery export, not Console internals\n\nMeasured: the current account has no accessible BigQuery datasets and exact R4/R5 data came only from a private Console endpoint. Official Google docs identify BigQuery export as the supported detailed-cost surface with labels, cost, credits, currency, latency, and evolving schema.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse existing product seams\n\nUse the existing provider config, cloud credential reference, workspace-host row, and hosted-lifecycle routine. The similarly named shipped spend-attribution plan addressed labeling/attribution honesty, not provider settlement, so it is prior art rather than an implementation home.\n\n### D-003 — Exact accounting differs from budget safety\n\nMicros plus currency are the accounting source. Existing cents gates consume conservative rounded-up values. Gross and credits remain separate.\n\n### D-004 — No false settlement\n\nA missing/empty/late query cannot close an obligation. Exact adequacy card EI-22728973201597463 passed independent audit EI-22729270661168973. Terminal close for WI-10000756 was accepted with committed authority after current-proof reevaluation. Work resumed under verified lift coord-send-73502856b21dff7c420e9f6f072460c1ee8f8bda3ed73c832562dbb37d59f8dc; self route and warm60s work loop restored.\n\n**Next:** Implement P-005 independent canary census and bounded versioned migration/exception rollout policy, then finalize the original desktop repair AUTO-BAR/report closeout in WI-10000723.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000753 — Add a typed design-approval binding through existing reference/plan/work-item surfaces. Choose the exact binding seam after inspecting current APIs; preserve original approved artifact and scope. Add… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000754 — Extend existing UI acceptance scaffolding with real navigation, clean/deep-link/persisted/back-forward entry contracts; reproduce the original desktop bug as a negative control. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000755 — Extend current render evidence with an explicit state/viewport/theme matrix, structural checks and side-by-side review. Label fixtures and real service acceptance separately. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000756 — Bind completion and shipment to every current design requirement and build/reference fingerprint, using existing evidence gates; prevent missing-registration and first-result shortcuts. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000757 — Independently grade the desktop repair as the pilot, exercise negative controls, define historical migration/exception handling, then propose the bounded enforcement rollout and concise author guidan… <!-- P-005 -->\n## Goal\n\nMake an approved UI design a traceable acceptance obligation spanning the user's actual navigation, implementation, rendered states and shipped build.\n\n## Background\n\nDesktop option B was selected in unified-web-portal-2026-08-29#D-062. The viewer was implemented within an expanded cloud host row, while the Desktops navigation selected no row. Existing component tests passed. The original plan and checked desktop work-item scopes had no registered visual-reference artifacts, so their visual gate was not applicable. A separate existing gate aggregation weakness returned the first applicable result; focused hardening is authored under the repair plan and must be verified independently.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Approval binds a specific artifact and scope.** A design approval records immutable artifact/hash/revision, approval provenance, implementing plan items, target route, required state/viewport/theme cases and any explicitly agreed adaptations. Approval cannot silently replace the reference with the current implementation. Exploratory concepts remain unconstrained.\n\n**R-2 — The actual user journey is tested.** Each accepted UI deliverable has a browser-level entry test through the real shell/navigation with a clean URL and persisted/direct-link/back-forward variants. A unit test mounting the target component alone does not discharge the entry obligation.\n\n**R-3 — Every relevant visual state has evidence.** Use controlled ready/empty/loading/disconnected/error states at agreed desktop/narrow sizes; record real-state acceptance separately. Verify geometry and interaction availability. Pixel thresholds apply only to commensurable captures; illustrative content never proves live connectivity. Show the approved reference and actual render side by side for review.\n\n**R-4 — Completion and shipment enforce current evidence.** Use all bound design references and required cases. Missing registration, missing proof, wrong target, stale source/build/reference revisions, invalid captures and failed checks each remain distinct blocking outcomes when the contract applies. A passing unrelated item cannot hide a failed requirement. Any exception is explicit, reasoned, versioned and reviewed; no silent dark flag or baseline refresh.\n\n**R-5 — Rollout has demonstrated negative controls.** Tests must catch the original empty-host entry defect, a correct component behind the wrong route, missing approved-reference registration, passing-plan/failing-item aggregation, stale build evidence, missing responsive state and a placeholder mislabeled as a working desktop. Document historical migration and limited exceptions before expanding enforcement; do not infer UI scope by fragile keyword matching.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing design-phase ratification/evidence verbs, work-item payload/plan binding, first-class spec clauses and existing acceptance gates. Reuse current Playwright/Vitest test frameworks and test-run ledger. Prefer typed requirements over prompt-only reminders. Avoid a parallel design table, service or new screenshot comparator. A DOM/geometry contract covers structure and entry; calibrated image comparison covers commensurable appearance; actual runtime journeys cover function. These are separate proof obligations.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Bind the contract\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add a typed design-approval binding through existing reference/plan/work-item surfaces. Choose the exact binding seam after inspecting current APIs; preserve original approved artifact and scope. Add missing/malformed/replaced-reference negative tests. — note: ← WI-10000753 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Prove what the user sees\n\n- **P-002** `done` Extend existing UI acceptance scaffolding with real navigation, clean/deep-link/persisted/back-forward entry contracts; reproduce the original desktop bug as a negative control. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10000754 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Extend current render evidence with an explicit state/viewport/theme matrix, structural checks and side-by-side review. Label fixtures and real service acceptance separately. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10000755 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Enforce and calibrate\n\n- **P-004** `done` Bind completion and shipment to every current design requirement and build/reference fingerprint, using existing evidence gates; prevent missing-registration and first-result shortcuts. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 — note: ← WI-10000756 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `todo` Independently grade the desktop repair as the pilot, exercise negative controls, define historical migration/exception handling, then propose the bounded enforcement rollout and concise author guidance. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-10000757 released\n\n## Scope and approval\n\nAvi reviewed the plan summary and approved start-to-finish implementation on 2026-09-08, designating the desktop option-B repair as the first canary (D-001). Activation must audit the complete source conversation and finalize exact acceptance clauses before implementation. Execute incrementally through the existing design-reference, spec-clause, evidence, test-run and acceptance stores. No cloud provisioning, credential changes, or claim that the separately gated connected-cloud desktop session is ready is part of this program.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Desktop option-B repair is the first enforcement canary\nDate: 2026-09-08\nAffects: desktop-design-fidelity-repair-2026-09-08\nAvi directed full implementation and designated the desktop design repair as the first canary. P-001 through P-004 must use the original broken Desktops entry as the negative control and the repaired option-B portal journey as the positive control; each stage must distinguish them before it advances. P-005 performs the formal independent canary grade, migration/exception decision, and bounded rollout recommendation. Reuse the existing durable desktop evidence and build identities rather than regenerating the implementation. This canary validates design binding, navigation, state/viewport evidence, and completion enforcement; it does not claim the separately gated connected-cloud desktop session is ready. Authority: session_turn:codex:01a0811d-70b9-7b00-bb2b-888f1ab88b91:12, building on session_turn:codex:01a07fff-cb14-77a3-ad93-908761cb4b82:10 and :16.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-002 — Bound rollout at explicit ratification; preserve historical obligations\nDate: 2026-09-08\nP-005 will extend the existing approval/ratification and enforceability surfaces. Explicit adoption outside the exact desktop option-B canary requires a versioned, byte-pinned rollout policy and an independently accepted review of that policy/census. The policy lists exact harness/feature/plan/item/route cohorts; scope never comes from titles or keywords. Historical references with no approval keep their existing host-calibration policy; existing adopted obligations are not weakened. Historical adoption is an explicit new approved revision. Temporary exceptions only defer new adoption for named cohorts, with owner, review provenance and expiry; they never waive an already-adopted failed proof or assert connectivity. The initial shipped recommendation is canary-only, with wider cohorts enabled only after their complete policy and independent review qualify. Existing cloud initialization/credential approvals remain outside this visual repair.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-09\nAmendment-Id: design-proof-layers-20260909-repair\nRequest-Hash: 63103d1f2183a16702a2e504501f00785a51a3068006ec5cfe16f9001c2bcbc9\nActor: su-3fd66acf-912c-44b2-9e13-3edaebd910fb\nReason: Declare executable methods and required proof layers matching the existing design acceptance outcomes without weakening reference, rollout, or live evidence obligations.\nApproved-By: su-372556ab-1320-4f14-b705-043f1d18c68a\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:202199\nApproved-At: 2026-09-09T03:47:14.582Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 8 → 9\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08","title":"Green gate: zero-wait convergence — event-driven re-judge, working auto-fixer, no full-gate fallthrough on repair rounds","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-08","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Green gate: zero-wait convergence — event-driven re-judge, working auto-fixer, no full-gate fallthrough on repair rounds\nslug: green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-08\nupdated: 2026-09-19\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-19. Never force.)\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000855 — Event-driven re-judge on admit: emit on `admit confirm`, bg-host handler fires the frozen-queue resume run immediately; in-flight run → `retestRequested` self-refire (R1, R7). <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000856 — Fixer auto-dispatch actually spawns: verify WI-10000758 live in bg-host, fix EI-22722785825237733 snapshot-matcher skip, fixer admission rides P-001 (R2). <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000857 — No full-gate fallthrough on repair rounds: widened selector → widened related radius + signature kinds; full gate only for post-suite-leg reds (R3). <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000858 — Run lint/check legs concurrently with the test sweep (R4). <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000859 — gen:*:check self-heal via the paired gen:* writer + hunk-exact admission of the artifact (R5). <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000860 — Admission pre-check at repairHead+patch with `admission-does-not-fix` / `admission-imports-red` refusals (R6). <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000861 — Latency instrumentation in gate_health + doc-claims test pinning the no-cron-wait repair path (R7). <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000862 — Lockfile-drift auto-convergence on the frozen lineage: when the `--ensure-ref` prewarm misses (`dependency-prewarm-missing`, exit 74) and the ONLY manifest delta between repairHead and the live integ… <!-- P-008 -->\n## Background\n`main` has been red since 2026-09-06 16:04Z. The frozen candidate 9aa9e788 is under freeze-and-converge (see the frozen-candidate plan's decisions); 12+ manual admission rounds; the failing count went 35→9→16→30→30→30→30→32→28→28→27→24.\n\nEach round costs ~1 h because: (1) the re-judge only happens on the hourly cron tick (:22); (2) the selective retest (`affectedTestsAtRef`, green-checkpoint.ts ~L977–988) FALLS THROUGH to the FULL gate (~55 min) whenever the selector widens (hub-package or gitlink admissions) or a task cannot be narrowed; (3) `post-suite-leg`/`workspace-task` signature kinds (frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts ~L50–66) are re-measured only by the full gate.\n\nThe auto-fixer (release-fixer, dispatched on a red against the failure signature) fired 0× in 15 reds: \"dispatch returned no spawn\" (green-checkpoint.ts ~L11848). WI-10000758 (wiring) landed 2026-09-08; EI-22722785825237733 (snapshot-matcher skip) is open.\n\nOwner directive [owner:Avi 2026-09-08T23:26Z, verbatim]: \"MAKE SURE YOU GET RID OF THE WAITING. ANY WAITING TIME DOING NOTHING IS RETARTED THERE SHOULD BE LIKE 0 OF THAT\".\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Zero idle wait.** A repair-queue admission (`release:repair-queue admit confirm`) triggers the re-judge of the frozen lineage IMMEDIATELY (event-driven); the :22 cron tick is never on the repair path's critical path.\n\n**R-2 — Fixer auto-dispatch, admission-triggered re-judge.** A red dispatches the fixer immediately and a fixer's admission triggers R-1 — a normal red converges with no human round.\n\n**R-3 — No full-gate fallthrough on repair rounds.** A repair round re-measures ONLY the signature kinds + the admitted paths' related test radius. The FULL gate is never the fallback on a repair round: a widened selector runs the widened related radius, still not the whole tree; only a `post-suite-leg` red may trigger a full gate.\n\n**R-4 — Lint/check legs concurrent with the test sweep.** Lint/check legs (gen:client-docs:check, gen:tool-catalog:check, lint:migration-forward-compat, typecheck-ratchet, …) run CONCURRENTLY with the test sweep, not after it.\n\n**R-5 — gen:*:check legs self-heal safely.** On a generated-artifact check failure, run the paired writer in the frozen verification tree, rerun the check and admit only its proved exact delta. Report success only after regeneration, recheck and admission all succeed. Regeneration failure, failed recheck, absent/unprovable delta, failed probe or refused admission stays a typed named failure or inconclusive outcome with no false green or unverified publication.\n\n**R-6 — Admission pre-check.** Before publishing, measure the signature test-file entries and admitted test files at the built repairHead-plus-patch commit. Refuse measured no-fix/imported-red results and runner/setup failures. The sole automatic unmeasured exception is D-002's checkpoint-tree-busy path, explicitly recorded for the authoritative re-judge; deliberate opt-out requires skipPrecheck plus a reason. An unmeasured result never counts as passing.\n\n**R-7 — Named bounded waits + latency metrics.** Every remaining wait is a bounded, NAMED wait on an event with a watchdog; `gate_health` reports admit→verdict, red→fixer-spawn and fix→admit latencies so idle time is measurable, not anecdotal.\n\n## Design\n- Event seam: `admit confirm` (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release/repair-queue.ts) emits `gate:repair-admitted:<candidate>`; a bg-host handler fires a green-checkpoint RESUME run of the frozen queue immediately under the existing run-lock singleton. If a run is in flight, set `retestRequested` on the queue row so the finishing run re-fires itself (the same self-refire path re-triage uses) instead of parking until cron.\n- Retest scope (R3): in the `affectedTestsAtRef` fall-through, replace \"run FULL gate\" with \"run `affected-tests --changed-paths <admitted> --related` even when widened, plus every `test-file`/`lint-leg`/`workspace-task`/`seed` entry of the signature\"; reserve the full gate for `post-suite-leg`.\n- Concurrency (R4): the lint legs are read-only on the checkpoint tree and CPU-light — run them beside the vitest sweep (green-checkpoint.ts ~L15103–15135 lint legs; perf/delta gates ~L12816/L12928 stay post-suite).\n- Self-heal (R5): registry-driven map `gen:X:check` → `gen:X` in NON_TEST_GATE_SCRIPTS; the regenerated path is admitted via the existing hunk-exact admission so provenance stays ledgered.\n- Pre-check (R6): reuse `runTestsAtRef` against a throwaway ref = repairHead + the admission hunks; refusal codes `admission-does-not-fix` / `admission-imports-red` naming the files.\n- Instrumentation (R7): three timestamps on the queue row; a doc-claims test pins \"no cron wait on the repair path\" by asserting the emitter→handler wiring.\n- Code sites: apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/release/frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release/repair-queue.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/release/green-checkpoint-schedule.ts; scripts/affected-tests.mjs.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-008 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-008 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006, P-009 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007, P-008 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — kill the waits\n- **P-001** `done` Event-driven re-judge on admit: emit on `admit confirm`, bg-host handler fires the frozen-queue resume run immediately; in-flight run → `retestRequested` self-refire (R1, R7). importance: high — note: ← WI-10000855 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Fixer auto-dispatch actually spawns: verify WI-10000758 live in bg-host, fix EI-22722785825237733 snapshot-matcher skip, fixer admission rides P-001 (R2). importance: high — note: ← WI-10000856 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` No full-gate fallthrough on repair rounds: widened selector → widened related radius + signature kinds; full gate only for post-suite-leg reds (R3). importance: high — note: ← WI-10000857 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Run lint/check legs concurrently with the test sweep (R4). — note: Verified on disk 2026-09-10T22:45Z: 5 `P-004:` tests in green-checkpoint-real-deps.test.ts (lines 1977–2712) + overlap wiring in green-checkpoint.ts (:365, :17848); prior holder's run 5/5 focused, 634/634 combined, operator typecheck clean; adequacy card AUTO-BAR-R-4-P-004@4 pass.\n- **P-005** `done` gen:*:check self-heal via the paired gen:* writer + hunk-exact admission of the artifact (R5). — note: R5 implemented: apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint-gen-check-self-heal.ts (+13 tests) wired into green-checkpoint.ts verify-repair red branch — paired gen:* writer runs in the frozen verification tree, re-check, then hunk-exact admission of only the writer delta onto repairHead (actor gate, D-001). testing:run 12b0d161 40/40; LINT_TSC_RESULT status=clean 00:00:09Z head a7ca49bf7f.\n- **P-006** `done` Admission pre-check at repairHead+patch with `admission-does-not-fix` / `admission-imports-red` refusals (R6). blocked-by: P-003 — note: R6 shipped: admit door is two-phase (build dryRun → measure signature/admitted test files at the built commit in the gate's checkpoint tree → publish); refuses admission-does-not-fix / admission-imports-red; runner root canonicalized to the main worktree (:3170 runs from the papercusp-staging linked worktree, which setup-release-checkout refuses).\n- **P-007** `done` Latency instrumentation in gate_health + doc-claims test pinning the no-cron-wait repair path (R7). blocked-by: P-001 — note: R7 landed: repairLatency clocks (fixerSpawnedAtMs/lastAdmittedAtMs/lastVerdictAtMs) on FrozenRepairQueueDiagnostic + gate_health, doc-claims pin gate-repair-latency-no-cron-wait; tests green, lint:tsc clean LAST (23:16Z)\n- **P-008** `done` Lockfile-drift auto-convergence on the frozen lineage: when the `--ensure-ref` prewarm misses (`dependency-prewarm-missing`, exit 74) and the ONLY manifest delta between repairHead and the live integration tree is lockfile blobs equal to staging's, the resume path auto-admits those paths whole-blob onto repairHead (actor=gate, ledgered reason) and re-prewarms — reusing the live generation; any other delta stays a typed miss and raises a stall alert instead of a silent `inconclusive`. Fixes EI-22752586902645795 (R-1, R-2, R-7). importance: high — note: lockfile-only drift between repairHead and staging is auto-admitted onto the frozen repairHead via the admission door; non-lockfile drift refuses loudly (LOCKFILE_DRIFT_NOT_CONVERGEABLE). 10/10 unit, lint:tsc clean (WI-10000862)\n- **P-009** `done` Reconcile R-6's precheck failure policy: a runner/setup failure must refuse publication with a typed actionable outcome; preserve D-002's explicit checkpoint-tree-busy defer-and-record exception and the deliberate skipPrecheck+reason opt-out. Add a recurrence test distinguishing busy from failed runner, prove failed/unmeasured execution cannot masquerade as a passed precheck, and update exact evidence/acceptance bindings. importance: high — note: Clear stale blocked gate after settled implementation and evidence; WI-10001088 has persisted exact adequacy plus causal-evidence v2 completion.\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n(none yet — awaiting owner review)\n\n### D-001 — Candidate-derived generated artifacts never transit canonical staging\nDate: 2026-09-09\nP-005's paired-writer repair must execute inside the frozen candidate/repair verification path and admit only its proved generated-artifact delta onto repairHead. A live gate fixer must not generate against exact-e07 in a disposable snapshot, copy that blob into canonical staging, wait for git-sync, or use wholeBlob admission: that makes staging's catalog candidate-derived rather than tip-derived and widens provenance. Until P-005 lands, an existing admission door that requires staging/captured hunks has no safe manual equivalent for this generated artifact; keep the current candidate held rather than mutating staging or synthesizing commits.\n\n### D-002 — R6 admission pre-check runs on confirmed admits at the built (unpublished) commit; fail-closed on a red result, fail-open-and-loud when the checkpoint tree is busy; explicit skipPrecheck opt-out\nDate: 2026-09-11\nP-006 design (su-ad21c897, 2026-09-11T00:06Z). The admit door (release:repair-queue op:admit, confirm:true) builds and PROVES the admission commit unpublished (admitPathsOntoRepairHead dryRun:true), runs the frozen signature's `test-file` entries plus any admitted test files at that commit, and only then publishes. Refusals: `admission-imports-red` — an admitted test file outside the signature fails at the built commit; `admission-does-not-fix` — the signature consists ONLY of test-file entries and none of them pass at the built commit (when the signature carries other kinds — lint-leg, workspace-task, post-suite-leg, seed — a test run cannot prove 'fixes nothing', so only imports-red applies). Unmeasured files never count as passing. The checkpoint tree is the gate's own instrument: when a gate run holds it, the pre-check does not run and the admission is ACCEPTED with a loud `precheck:{ran:false, reason:'checkpoint-tree-busy'}` marker — the R-1 event-driven re-judge measures it; a fail-closed door here would stall every fixer admission for the length of a gate run and defeat R-1/R-2. Opt-out for a deliberate wide admission: `skipPrecheck:true` + `precheckReason` (recorded on the ledger entry and the result). Dry-run admits report the population they WOULD run without running it. Pure evaluation lives in packages/operator-core/lib/release/admission-fix-precheck.ts behind a runner seam so the verdict logic is unit-testable independent of the tree.\n\n### D-003 — Owner-approved September 12 audit disposition and current execution contract\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAuthority: session_turn:codex:01a0961e-ab11-71f2-bae6-9be0c8401857:32 — Avi approved applying the relevance-audit recommendations and implementing relevant updated plans through verified shipment. This decision adopts the Revise disposition.\n\nCurrent contract: Event-triggered repair verification, scoped retesting and latency visibility remain high-value. R5/R6 prose overstates the implemented exceptions, and P-007's plan/WI completion evidence is inconsistent.\n\nExecution: Clarify the exact contracts, repair evidence/grade debt and test the actual operational loop. The current owner's redundant-refire defect means this cannot yet be called operationally solved.\n\nMeasured basis: the source/test/decision review and scoped verification recorded in docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md, not a new claim about the live gate. Preserve its residuals here: predecessor P-001's executed-versus-reused task evidence and P-004's conditional cache/selection gap map to this plan R-1/R-3 and existing conservative proof-cache tests; predecessor P-007's real freeze-to-terminal outcome maps to R-7 and final shared operational acceptance. This is a transfer, not a claim that those observations already passed. WI-10001019 carries closure/evidence work; the single live gate owner supplies operational evidence. Measured basis: completed relevance audit and its exact snapshots/test runs in docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md.\n\n\n### D-005 — Owner-approved R5/R6 contract reconciliation preserves exact proof and distinguishes busy from failed execution\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAuthority: session_turn:codex:01a0961e-ab11-71f2-bae6-9be0c8401857:32. Update current spec/rubric proof bindings after the final implementation.\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-12\nAmendment-Id: zero-wait-acceptance-methods-checks-r5-r6-v1\nRequest-Hash: b25c5f30b72bf9a9e41883d02ab0ef188988b9d3440ac183e38e188f64b793bf\nActor: su-bfcb867a-6027-45be-a703-be2854bdc24e\nReason: Align the acceptance BAR contract with plan revision 28, D-003 through D-005, and bind executable checks before final grading.\nApproved-By: su-b6fbdf61-0579-43e0-b824-2c0a92bd69fb\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:203214\nApproved-At: 2026-09-12T19:58:55.779Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 28 → 29\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-15\nAmendment-Id: 6fdb5e6de47edc22ccc907471afc63dc1449b7b55c1ca5f26a4d58c320223699\nRequest-Hash: 03add48b0ed779419414befcd7c79852829714b83cd6ec1a8b538a41d342254a\nActor: su-a604a73a-08f7-4699-a4c1-05506614e161\nReason: P-012 of ship-main-greening-program-2026-09-15: declare requiredTestLayers [unit] on tree-plane bars R-2..R-6 so acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot can rate proof depth (clears bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing); no prose/meaning change to the bars beyond the proof-layer floor. Approved by outside-lineage reviewer su-8ee7575e (thread-post:204756).\nApproved-By: su-8ee7575e-152d-4557-874c-62e4fe036ed9\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:204756\nApproved-At: 2026-09-15T17:30:35.292Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 33 → 34\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-008 — R-4's concurrency requirement is scoped to REPAIR ROUNDS; an initial candidate run deliberately keeps the suite-first barrier\nDate: 2026-09-16\n#### Ruling\n\nR-4 (\"Lint/check legs concurrent with the test sweep\") governs **repair rounds only**. On an INITIAL candidate run the gate deliberately preserves the suite-first barrier, and that is correct behaviour, not a violation of R-4.\n\nThe acceptance rubric's R-4 criterion is amended to say so explicitly at revision 7. R-1 historical timing remains contested and must be graded truthfully.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6)\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 36 → 37\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plan-popup-full-window-control-2026-09-08","title":"Plan popup full-window control","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-08","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Plan popup full-window control\nslug: plan-popup-full-window-control-2026-09-08\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-08\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n## Now\n\nAdd a distinct full-window control next to the existing full-screen control in the shared plan popup.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000690 — Validate the full-window/full-screen interaction spec against the design registry and existing SessionChatModal/GoalDetailPanel precedent. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000698 — Implement the distinct full-window and full-screen controls in shared PlanPopupModal, with focused regression coverage. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000699 — Run focused plan-popup tests and the repository affected-test gate; record verified desktop/cloud parity from the shared mount path. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Background\n\nPlanPopupModal is shared by the desktop app and cloud portal. It already carries a private isWindowExpanded fallback, while SessionChatModal and GoalDetailPanel use the reusable usePopupMaximize hook for an explicit full-window/full-screen pair. The registry search returned only the generic primary action, so the closest approved local precedent is the existing popup toolbar pair.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Adjacent controls.** Show a separate Full window button directly beside Full screen.\n\n**R-2 — Window semantics.** Full window fills the application or browser viewport without entering OS/browser fullscreen.\n\n**R-3 — Screen semantics.** Full screen retains true display fullscreen behavior rather than becoming an alias for Full window.\n\n**R-4 — Host parity.** Both controls work in desktop and cloud through the shared PlanPopupModal.\n\n**R-5 — Accessible states.** Use distinct accessible labels, tooltips, pressed states, and matching restore icons.\n\n**R-6 — Safe cleanup.** Escape and close restore the popup without leaving display or URL state stranded.\n\n**R-7 — Regression safety.** Preserve plan tabs, dirty-edit close confirmation, provenance, and plan-target cleanup.\n\n## Design\n\nReuse usePopupMaximize with a plan-specific query parameter and the established Maximize2/Minimize2 full-window pair plus Maximize/Minimize full-screen pair. Reuse the existing popup control styling and Tooltip primitive.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Shared popup controls\n\n- **P-001** `done` Validate the full-window/full-screen interaction spec against the design registry and existing SessionChatModal/GoalDetailPanel precedent. — note: ← WI-10000690 completed (done)\n- across local + ElevenLabs","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-08","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cloud portal voice — desktop-parity controls, then public-release readiness across local + ElevenLabs\nslug: portal-voice-parity-and-release-2026-09-08\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-08\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\nP-001 — port the desktop voice control into the portal top bar, driven by an\nengine-agnostic portal voice-mode state machine (LiveKit as engine #1).\n\n## Why\n\nThe cloud portal (`portal/packages/ui/src/voice-session.tsx`, rendered from\n`portal/packages/ui/src/shell.tsx`) grew its own voice controls as a row of\nplain TEXT buttons — \"Mute Papercup\", \"Hold to talk\", \"Retry voice\", \"Check\nmicrophone\", \"Enable audio\" — plus a \"Start voice chat\" text button, all bound\ndirectly to a LiveKit room. The desktop operator app has a designed ICON\ncontrol: a round orb with status glyphs, a live mic-level ring, animated\nlistening/speaking/thinking states, a mode label, and a gear settings link\n(`papercusp/apps/operator/app/_components/voice/VoiceButton.tsx` + the\n`.pc-voice-*` rules in `papercusp/apps/operator/app/globals.css`).\n\nOwner directives, 2026-09-08, recorded verbatim in D-001..D-004 below: use the\ndesktop buttons with the icons, keep them in the top bar, make the search bar\ntake voice, and then get cloud voice to public release supporting BOTH the\ndesktop's local engine AND ElevenLabs.\n\n## Background — what desktop and portal actually share (verified in code)\n\n`papercusp/libs/generic/chat-protocol/src/voice.ts` (VOICE_PROTOCOL_VERSION 1)\nis already the shared boundary. Its own header: \"the shared boundary between\nPapercup owner voice, Phone/LiveKit, and any future voice transport ... Media\nstays transport-specific; turn identity, authority, conversation linkage,\nexecutor selection, and emitted events do not.\" It declares\n`VOICE_TRANSPORTS = ['papercup-local', 'papercup-hosted', 'phone-livekit']` and\n`papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/voice-turn-router.ts` routes all three,\nresolving principal/authority/capabilities server-side.\n\nDesktop and portal are therefore NOT rival systems at the turn layer. They\ndiverge strictly below the microphone:\n\n- Desktop = `papercup-local`/`papercup-hosted`: Web Speech API + local\n  VAD/whisper capture (`energy-vad-capture.ts`, `stt-voicemode.ts`,\n  `f32-to-wav.ts`, `ptt-capture.ts`), an ElevenLabs Conv-AI / Realtime\n  full-agent mode that owns the mic (`micOwnedByFullAgent`), and cross-surface\n  leader election (`voice-leader.ts`).\n- Portal = `phone-livekit` ONLY: one LiveKit room per chat, the agent worker\n  owning VAD/endpointing/turn-detection/barge-in/STT. The browser component is\n  deliberately a thin transport seam that declines to \"grow a second browser\n  voice stack\". Turns return over the loopback-only `external-turns` bridge\n  (`operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-chats/external-turns.ts`).\n\nThe portal holds ONE of three sanctioned transports and is missing the other\ntwo. Closing that gap is the release work.\n\n## Prior art to reuse, not rebuild\n\n`on-desktop-direct-lan-voice-2026-07-14` (draft; all phases done, owner residue\noutstanding) already built the LOCAL engine as a device-authed streamed\nendpoint: `POST /api/device/voice/turn` (device-JWT, SSE) running\nwhisper -> papercup brain -> per-sentence kokoro TTS, with warmup and a\n`mobileVoiceMode: off | desktop-local | auto` dispatch that keeps ElevenLabs\nbyte-compatible and lets EL win when configured. The cloud work should reach\nthat surface rather than grow a third local stack.\n\n## Approach\n\nThe desktop `VoiceButton` renders a `VoiceState` and never learns which engine\nproduced it. That is what makes the button port a down-payment on the release\nprogram instead of a re-skin to be thrown away: give the portal its own\n`voice-mode` state machine with the same state shape, back it with LiveKit\nfirst, and the local + ElevenLabs engines plug in underneath without the UI\nchanging again.\n\n\n## Requirements\n\nEach is stated so a grader can decide it from the built artifact, not from intent.\n\n**R-1 — The portal's voice control is the desktop control.** The portal top bar renders the desktop orb (`.pc-voice-btn`) with its status glyph, mic-level ring, and the animated listening, speaking, thinking and connecting glyphs; and the portal no longer renders the text-label buttons \"Mute Papercup\", \"Hold to talk\", \"Retry voice\", \"Check microphone\", \"Enable audio\", or the \"Start voice chat\" text button. (D-001)\n\n**R-2 — The control lives in the top bar.** It renders inside the portal `.topbar`, beside the search bar, and not in a dock, panel or drawer. (D-001)\n\n**R-3 — The mode cycle is the desktop's.** Clicking cycles off to push-to-talk to always-on and wraps back to off; holding the button and holding the backtick key both force-listen in every mode. (D-002)\n\n**R-4 — Always-on holds the microphone open.** While always-on is selected, capture is published continuously with no control held down, rather than push-to-talk under a different label. (D-002)\n\n**R-5 — Always-on cannot leave a microphone open silently.** Continuous capture does not begin without explicit consent, a visible indicator states that it is running, and it is torn down on chat change, on tab hide via visibilitychange, and on disconnect, with a test exercising each of those three teardown paths. (D-002)\n\n**R-6 — The search bar takes voice.** A microphone control renders inside the top-bar search input, and is absent rather than merely disabled where the browser exposes no capture path. (D-003)\n\n**R-7 — Search voice speaks to Ask Papercup and leaves the box empty.** Using the search microphone opens a Papercup voice chat carrying the spoken question, the search query value is unchanged, and the rail and notification rows are not filtered by what was spoken. (D-003)\n\n**R-8 — The control is engine-agnostic.** The voice control renders from a VoiceState value and contains no LiveKit import, type or branch; the LiveKit adapter is reachable only through the engine interface, so a second engine can be added without editing the control. (D-004)\n\n**R-9 — The existing voice room did not regress.** Push-to-talk, output mute that silences Papercup and never the microphone, retry, microphone-permission recovery and autoplay recovery all still work, and the accessible status still names the device each control governs.\n\n**R-10 — Phase 2 is complete with the desktop-local voice boundary intact.** Phase 2 reached its recorded terminal disposition with the desktop-local security boundary intact. P-007 is intentionally dropped under D-011, so the hosted multi-tenant portal does not expose `/api/device/voice/turn` or the desktop whisper→brain→kokoro path. P-008 through P-010 are complete: hosted voice uses the server-brokered ElevenLabs and LiveKit engines, the owner-visible engine picker and availability-aware Auto policy are shipped, and the public-release safeguards are verified against the hosted portal.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\nThe evidence plane is chosen for what can actually decide the requirement. The two\nrequirements that assert something about a REAL microphone are `live` on purpose: a\njsdom test can prove the state machine intends to publish continuously, but it cannot\nprove a browser held the microphone open, and claiming otherwise would be exactly the\nfalse verification this column exists to prevent.\n\n| BAR | Items | Evidence |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | live |\n| R-5 | P-003 | live |\n| R-6 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-001, P-005 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Desktop-parity voice controls in the portal top bar\n\n- **P-001** `done` Portal voice-mode state machine: a `voice-mode` module in portal/packages/ui/src exposing the desktop VoiceState shape (status off|connecting|idle|listening|speaking|paused; mode off|push-to-talk|always-on; supported, audioReceiving, awaitingResponse, processingTranscript) behind an ENGINE interface. LiveKit (phone-livekit) is engine #1, adapting the existing openPortalVoiceSession handle. Extend tests/voice-session.test.ts and tests/shell-ui.test.tsx rather than adding a new harness. importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Public-release readiness across local + ElevenLabs (D-005)\n\n- **P-006** `done` RELEASE SURVEY (entry point; output is an evidenced design, not code): audit the ElevenLabs path the desktop uses (fullAgentEngine=elevenlabs-conv and its prefs), the local path already shipped by on-desktop-direct-lan-voice-2026-07-14 (POST /api/device/voice/turn, device-JWT, SSE, whisper->brain->kokoro, warmup, mobileVoiceMode dispatch), and what a hosted multi-tenant browser can actually reach of each. importance: high — note: ← WI-10000806 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `dropped` Reach the LOCAL engine from the cloud portal, reusing /api/device/voice/turn rather than growing a third local stack.
