No shipment.\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Portal voice controls are the desktop icon controls, in the top bar\nDate: 2026-09-08\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-08] \"another agent added papercup voice buttons to our cloud button. but we should use the same buttons that we were using in our desktop app with the icons. We should keep them on the top bar though since the cloud portal has the serach bar.\"\n\nThe portal's text-label voice buttons (Mute Papercup / Hold to talk / Retry voice / Check microphone / Enable audio, plus the \"Start voice chat\" text button) are REPLACED by the desktop operator's icon control: the .pc-voice-btn orb with status glyphs, live mic-level ring, animated listening/speaking/thinking glyphs, mode label, gear settings link, and the compact icon session row. They stay in the portal TOP BAR, not in a dock or panel, because the top bar is where the portal's search bar already lives.\n\nDo not re-derive a bespoke portal voice button. Port the desktop shape.\n\n### D-002 — Full desktop parity including always-on mode\nDate: 2026-09-08\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-08, answering an explicit options prompt] Owner chose \"Full parity incl. always-on\" over an icons-only re-skin.\n\nThe orb CYCLES Off -> push-to-talk -> Always-on exactly as the desktop does. Always-on is NEW portal behaviour: it keeps the microphone published continuously to the room rather than only while held. Hold-the-button and hold-backtick remain force-listen in every mode.\n\nBecause always-on means a continuously open microphone in a browser tab, it carries obligations the desktop's own implementation already discharges: explicit consent, a visible always-on indicator, and reliable teardown on chat change / tab hide / disconnect. Those are acceptance conditions, not follow-ups.\n\n### D-003 — The search-bar mic speaks straight to Ask Papercup; it does not dictate into the box\nDate: 2026-09-08\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-08] \"the cloud portal has the serach bar. That should be able to take in voice too I'm not sure if we added that yet.\"\n\nAnswering the options prompt, the owner chose \"Speak straight to Ask Papercup\" over dictating into the field: the mic in the portal search input opens a Papercup voice chat carrying the spoken question, and the SEARCH BOX ITSELF STAYS EMPTY. It is a shortcut into the voice room, not a dictation aid, so voice does not filter the rail/notification rows.\n\nVerified 2026-09-08: no search-bar voice existed anywhere — not in the portal, and not in the desktop's GlobalSearchDialog either. The owner's \"I'm not sure if we added that yet\" resolves to NOT ADDED.\n\n### D-004 — Portal voice is engine-agnostic: one state machine, three transports beneath it\nDate: 2026-09-08\n[self-imposed, from the owner's release directive] The desktop VoiceButton renders a VoiceState and never learns which engine produced it. The portal MUST adopt that same split rather than binding the orb to LiveKit.\n\nConcretely: the portal gets its own voice-mode state machine exposing the desktop's VoiceState shape, with LiveKit (phone-livekit) as engine #1, so the local and ElevenLabs engines plug in underneath without the UI changing again. Binding the new orb directly to LiveKit would make the button work throwaway the moment the release program lands, which is why this is a decision and not a preference.\n\nThis honours the existing shared boundary: chat-protocol/src/voice.ts already declares VOICE_TRANSPORTS = ['papercup-local','papercup-hosted','phone-livekit'] and voice-turn-router.ts already routes all three. The portal is missing two of the three; it is not on a rival system.\n\n### D-005 — Cloud voice ships supporting BOTH the desktop local engine and ElevenLabs\nDate: 2026-09-08\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-08] \"AFTER YOU FIX THE BUTTONS TAKE CHARGE OF GETTING OUR VOICE FEATURES IN OUR CLOUD VERSION READY FOR PUBLIC RELEASE IT SHOULD SUPPORT BOTH THE LOCAL VERSION WE HAD IN THE DESKTOP APP AS WELL AS ELEVEN LABS\"\n\nTwo directives in one: (a) SEQUENCE — the button work lands FIRST, the release program follows; (b) SCOPE — cloud voice at public-release quality must support the desktop's local engine AND ElevenLabs, not one or the other.\n\nReuse, do not rebuild: plan on-desktop-direct-lan-voice-2026-07-14 already shipped the local engine as POST /api/device/voice/turn (device-JWT, SSE, whisper -> papercup brain -> per-sentence kokoro TTS) with warmup and a mobileVoiceMode: off | desktop-local | auto dispatch that keeps ElevenLabs byte-compatible and lets EL win when configured. The cloud path should reach that surface rather than grow a third local stack.\n\n\"Take charge\" is an ownership grant over the program, not a licence to skip the route/approach gate on the large pieces.\n\n### D-006 — D-006: the orb's `disabled` tracks `supported` alone; \"do not invite a press you will discard\" moves to the COPY\nDate: 2026-09-08\nRULING. `PortalVoiceControlView`'s orb button sets `disabled={!state.supported}` and MUST NOT derive `disabled` from `portalVoiceCanCapture`. The property the old portal expressed through that attribute — a control must not invite a press it will discard — is preserved, but relocated to the control's COPY.\n\nWHY THE ATTRIBUTE CANNOT CARRY IT ANY MORE. The old surface had a dedicated \"Hold to talk\" button whose only action was capture, so `disabled = !canCapture` was exactly right. The orb has TWO actions on one element (D-001): click cycles off -> push-to-talk -> always-on, hold does PTT. `portalVoiceCanCapture` is false in `off`, `connecting`, `reconnecting` and `disconnected`. Disabling the orb there would disable the CYCLE in precisely the states where the cycle is the only thing the viewer can usefully do — and once P-004/D-003 removes the separate \"Start voice chat\" text button, choosing a mode IS starting voice, so a `status: \"off\"` orb that is `disabled` makes voice unstartable. It would also strand a viewer mid-reconnect with no way to turn voice off.\n\nMeasured: packages/ui/src/voice-control.tsx:140 `disabled={!state.supported}`; the two press channels at :141-145 (`onClick={onCycleMode}` + `onPointerDown/Up/Cancel/Leave -> onPushToTalk`). The capture gate itself is at packages/ui/src/voice-session.tsx:493 — `if (!sessionRef.current || !portalVoiceCanCapture(state).can) return;` — so a hold that arrives in a non-capturing state is already refused by the handler, not by the DOM.\n\nWHAT CARRIES THE PROPERTY INSTEAD. In every state where `portalVoiceCanCapture(state).can` is false, NEITHER the status line NOR the control title may invite a hold. Both are checked over the whole state census in tests/a-muted-speaker-is-not-a-silent-microphone.test.tsx.\n\nLIVE BUG THIS EXPOSED, now in scope for P-002. `portalVoiceControlTitle` (voice-mode.ts:260-267) returns \"Voice: <mode> (click to cycle, hold the button or ` to talk)\" for every supported, non-connecting state that does not need consent — including `status: \"off\"`, `\"reconnecting\"` and `\"disconnected\"`, where `pushToTalk` drops the press. That is the same false-invitation defect the status line was fixed for (\"Voice ready — hold to talk\" while idle), surviving in the tooltip. The title must name the click action alone when capture is impossible.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR PHASE 2 (P-007/P-008, D-005). Engines added under the seam report `PortalVoiceStatus`, and a new non-capturing status inherits this rule for free: it must not appear in copy that invites a hold. A new engine does not get to re-decide the orb's `disabled` derivation.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-007 — Release survey (P-006): only SERVER-BROKERED voice engines are hosted-reachable; the desktop-local pipeline is LAN+device-JWT by construction and must not be ported\nDate: 2026-09-08\nThree voice engines exist. They differ by WHERE the media brain runs, and that alone decides what a hosted multi-tenant browser can reach.\n\n1) PORTAL / LIVEKIT — shipped, engine #1. REACHABLE.\nMeasured: portal/packages/ui/src/voice-session.tsx:6-9 — \"a thin LiveKit transport seam… turn-taking, barge-in, and speech recognition remain owned by the LiveKit agent worker\" (server-side, not in the browser).\nMeasured: portal/apps/host/src/api.ts:119-121 — \"call MEDIA goes browser<->LiveKit directly over WebRTC and never transits the portal… instead of paying a proxy hop per audio frame (D-015)\".\nMeasured: the portal host mints NO LiveKit token of its own — `git grep -nE \"voice/(session|token|start)|createToken|AccessToken|roomName|agentDispatch\" -- apps/host/src` returns nothing (exit 1). It PROXIES /api/phone/* to the Phone sidecar (api.ts:136-138), which owns the call binding server-side and later appends trusted LiveKit transcript turns.\n\n2) ELEVENLABS CONV — desktop today. REACHABLE IN PRINCIPLE, not yet from the portal.\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-mcp/operator-elevenlabs-bootstrap.ts:21-24 mints a conversation token SERVER-SIDE against api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/conversation/token using the `xi-api-key` header; :55-68 gates it on prefs.fullAgentEngine==='elevenlabs-conv' AND prefs.elevenLabsAgentId AND readElevenLabsKey().\nSo the secret never reaches the browser and media is browser<->EL — the shape a hosted browser CAN use. Two gaps: the mint route lives on the OPERATOR (/api/agent-mcp/…), not the portal host; and its cooldown + in-flight dedup are keyed by agentId alone (:10-12, :75-94), i.e. per-AGENT, not per-tenant.\n\n3) DESKTOP-LOCAL whisper -> brain -> kokoro. NOT REACHABLE. Do not port it.\nMeasured: routes/device/voice-turn.ts:3-24 — \"the phone is a thin audio client and the DESKTOP does STT + brain + TTS, all local\"; POST /device/voice/turn + /device/voice/warmup, SSE, `auth: DEVICE_AUTH` (routes/device/voice.ts:20-47, devicePrincipal -> workspaceId + ownerId).\nMeasured: voice-node/local-whisper-service.ts:2-21 — whisper is an operator-managed CHILD PROCESS spawned on a dedicated LOCAL port (default 2022), health-gated, reaped on operator exit. voice-node/kokoro-local.ts:2 — kokoro TTS runs IN-PROCESS inside the operator.\nBoth halves are therefore bound to ONE user's desktop operator process. There is nothing for a hosted multi-tenant browser to address. It is reachable only by a device on that LAN holding a device JWT — which is precisely what prefs.mobileVoiceMode ('auto' | 'off' | 'desktop-local', voice-prefs.ts:228-238) selects for a PHONE.\n\nCONSEQUENCES, binding on P-007..P-010:\n(a) Do NOT design a hosted browser path onto /api/device/voice/turn. Making it hosted-reachable means exposing a user's desktop STT/TTS to the internet — a different and much larger product/security decision, not a port. If anyone wants it, it comes back to the owner as its own proposal.\n(b) The hosted-reachable set is exactly the server-brokered engines: LiveKit (shipped) and ElevenLabs Conv (needs a portal-side mint boundary plus per-TENANT key isolation and cooldown, not per-agentId).\n(c) Copy the existing precedent rather than inventing one: the sidecar-proxy boundary where only control-plane JSON crosses the portal and media goes direct (api.ts:119-121, 136-138). An EL engine for the portal should take that shape.\n(d) This is an ADD, not a re-architecture: the Phase 1 seam already declares the vocabulary — portal/packages/ui/src/voice-mode.ts:350, `PortalVoiceTransport = \"phone-livekit\" | \"papercup-local\" | \"papercup-hosted\"` — so ElevenLabs enters as another transport under the existing engine-agnostic state machine (D-004), with the orb/copy layer untouched.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-008 — P-008: ElevenLabs' portal transport id is the EXISTING `papercup-hosted` — do not mint a fourth name; and the EL key is a PLATFORM secret in host env, not a per-tenant vault entry (no vault exists)\nDate: 2026-09-08\nDate: 2026-09-08\n\nTwo P-008 design questions that P-009/P-010 must not re-decide differently.\n\n=== 1. TRANSPORT ID: EL is `papercup-hosted`, already ===\n\nD-007(d) said EL \"enters as another transport\". Read literally that invites a fourth id. It must NOT be minted, for two measured reasons.\n\nMEASURED — the contract is closed and validating:\nlibs/generic/chat-protocol/src/voice.ts:16 — `VOICE_TRANSPORTS = ['papercup-local', 'papercup-hosted', 'phone-livekit'] as const`. There is no ElevenLabs member.\nvoice.ts:279 — `const transport = enumValue(raw.transport, VOICE_TRANSPORTS)`, and :285 returns `null` for the WHOLE envelope when transport is unknown. So a turn stamped with an invented id does not degrade — it is silently DROPPED by the parser. The portal comment at packages/ui/src/voice-mode.ts:346-350 (\"so the portal never invents a fourth name for a transport the server already knows\") is therefore load-bearing, not stylistic.\n\nMEASURED — the desktop ALREADY calls ElevenLabs `papercup-hosted`:\npackages/operator-core/lib/voice-node/operator-voice-session.ts header:1-5 — \"Operator voice session host — ONE shared ElevenLabs/operator session\"; the module owns the single EL WebSocket (:6-8, elPongMessage / `ev.type==='user_transcript'` / `this.elConversationId`).\nThat same module, at :445-450, stamps its EL turns `transport: 'papercup-hosted', executor: 'papercup-hosted'`.\n\nSo the id question was never open. `papercup-hosted` IS the ElevenLabs transport in this system; P-008's own words — \"the desktop existing byte-compatible session-init and mode dispatch as the reference\" — resolve to reusing it. The portal today implements only `phone-livekit`, so the `papercup-hosted` slot is free and semantically exact.\n\nBINDING: P-009's engine-selection surface maps the user-visible \"ElevenLabs\" choice onto transport `papercup-hosted`. It does NOT add a contract member, and it does not surface the raw transport id as the user-facing label — engine NAME and transport ID are different vocabularies and only the latter is contract-bound.\n\n=== 2. KEY CUSTODY: platform env secret, per-TENANT mint boundary ===\n\nP-008 requires EL keys never reach a tree file or the browser bundle. The obvious reading — a per-tenant BYO key — is not implementable now:\nMEASURED — \"Personal Vault\" appears in portal DECISIONS.md:76 and blueprints/README.md:10 as a CONCEPT only; `grep -rn -i vault` over the portal's *.ts/*.tsx returns no implementation. There is no encrypted per-tenant secret store to put a tenant's EL key in, and inventing one inside P-008 would be a second durable surface smuggled into a voice item.\n\nDECIDED: the portal holds ONE platform-owned EL key in host process env (never DB, never tree, never bundle), exactly as the desktop holds one via `readElevenLabsKey()`. Per-TENANT isolation is enforced at the MINT BOUNDARY, not by key partitioning — which is the gap D-007(b) actually named (\"per-TENANT key isolation and cooldown, not per-agentId\").\n\nConcretely, the portal mint differs from the desktop reference (operator-elevenlabs-bootstrap.ts) on exactly three axes, and these are the P-008 acceptance surface:\n(a) AUTH — desktop is `auth: 'public'` (:52), sound for a single-user desktop, unsafe hosted. Portal mint requires the WorkOS identity and fails closed.\n(b) COOLDOWN + IN-FLIGHT DEDUP — desktop keys both by agentId alone (:12 `el-mint:${agentId}`, :88 `inFlight.get(agentId)`). On a multi-tenant host that is a CROSS-TENANT COUPLING: one tenant's mint would rate-limit another's, and a shared in-flight promise would hand tenant A's token to tenant B. Portal keys both by tenant.\n(c) RESPONSE SHAPE stays byte-compatible: `{ conversationToken, agentId }`.\n\nA per-tenant BYO EL key remains a legitimate future item; it is deliberately NOT P-008, and when it arrives it changes only where the key is READ, not the mint boundary above.\n\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-009 — D-009 — P-009 ships the selection MECHANISM without a `local` choice; absence of a preference key means auto\nDate: 2026-09-08\nP-009 as written asks for \"one owner-visible choice across off / local / ElevenLabs / LiveKit\". It ships WITHOUT `local`. Three consequences below are binding on P-010.\n\nWHY `local` IS EXCLUDED. `local` means transport `papercup-local` — the desktop's whisper→brain→kokoro pipeline — reached from a hosted multi-tenant browser. That is exactly P-007, which D-007 refuted on its premise: reaching it from a hosted browser means exposing a user's desktop STT/TTS to the internet. P-007 is `needs-human` and the question is open with the owner (conv-mtt2q2q3-0000-5fcd4c08d76c4a9c8a6709f6641ef1a7); my recommendation there was server-brokered only. So shipping a `local` entry now would do one of two bad things: render a control that cannot work, or pre-empt an owner SECURITY decision by making the exposure selectable. Neither is P-009's call to make.\n\nMeasured 2026-09-08T21:08Z (scope: the ENTIRE ~/papercupai-workspace/portal checkout, all *.ts/*.tsx/*.sql/*.json excluding node_modules, via `grep -rl` so the result is one line per file and cannot be truncated by a line cap): the string `papercup-local` occurs in exactly ONE file, packages/ui/src/voice-mode.ts, and there only inside the `PortalVoiceTransport` type-union declaration — i.e. the transport id is NAMED but has no implementation. Zero files reference `device/voice/turn`, `deviceVoice`, `kokoro` or `whisper`. The sole engine implementing the seam is packages/ui/src/voice-elevenlabs.ts, whose transport is ELEVENLABS_TRANSPORT. So \"there is no portal-reachable local engine\" is a measured absence over the whole checkout, not an inference from one module.\n\nThis is a SCOPE decision, not a redesign. The choice enum, the auto policy and the resolver are all written so `local` is an additive entry: add it to PORTAL_VOICE_ENGINE_CHOICES, add its availability flag, and give it a rung in the auto ladder. Nothing about the mechanism has to change when P-007 is answered. If the owner answers \"server-brokered only\", `local` never arrives and P-009 is already complete as shipped.\n\nDECISION 1 — THE CHOICE SET IS `auto | off | elevenlabs | livekit`. `auto` is a first-class stored value, not the absence of a value. A user who has deliberately chosen auto and a user who has never touched the setting are the same behaviour but must stay distinguishable, because only the second may be silently re-pointed when a new engine (`local`) is added later.\n\nDECISION 2 — THE PREFERENCE KEY IS OPTIONAL, NOT DEFAULTED, AND ABSENT MEANS AUTO. `voiceEngine` is added to UserPreferencesSchema as `.optional()`, NOT `.default(\"auto\")`. This follows a constraint the portal already documents in that same schema: the `dismissed` field carries the comment that it is deliberately optional-not-defaulted so \"the authority-handoff payload hash stays byte-stable for accounts that never touched it\", and `pinnedApps` likewise treats absent as materially different from empty. [inferred, from those two in-file comments rather than from a test I ran] a `.default()` would add a key to every existing account's parsed preferences and change that hash for accounts that never opened voice settings, which risks the P-027 local→hosted authority handoff. Absent is normalised to `auto` at the RESOLVER, never at the parser. Recheck if this ever needs to be load-bearing: assert that parseUserPreferences({}) returns an object with no `voiceEngine` key.\n\nDECISION 3 — AN EXPLICIT CHOICE OF AN UNCONFIGURED ENGINE RESOLVES TO UNSUPPORTED, NOT TO A SILENT FALLBACK. If a user explicitly picks ElevenLabs on a portal where no EL key is configured, the resolver returns unsupported and names that engine; it does NOT quietly hand them LiveKit. Only `auto` walks the ladder. This exists so P-010's \"failure copy that names the engine that failed\" has something true to say — a silent substitution makes that requirement unimplementable, because by the time the UI reports a failure it no longer knows which engine the user asked for. The auto ladder mirrors the desktop, minus the excluded rung: ElevenLabs when configured, else LiveKit when configured, else off.\n\n### D-010 — D-NNN: the portal voice control drops the Off/PTT/On WORD and carries the mode in the ICON — a deliberate divergence from the desktop reference\nDate: 2026-09-09\nRULING. The portal's `PortalVoiceControlView` renders NO visible text in any persistent mode. The mode is carried by the orb's icon (mic-off / mic / mic-with-waves, swapped by the `.pc-voice-btn--mode-*` class) plus the existing per-mode border. Only TRANSIENT states (speaking / thinking / processing / listening / connecting) render a glyph child. This DIVERGES from D-001/D-002's \"the markup and class names are deliberately the desktop's\" and that divergence is intentional.\n\nWHY. D-001/D-002 made the portal a faithful port of the desktop's `VoiceButton.tsx`. The port was faithful, and that was the defect:\n\nMeasured: `apps/operator/app/_components/voice/VoiceButton.tsx:357` — `content = <span className=\"pc-voice-btn-label\">{MODE_LABEL[vs.mode]}</span>;` with `MODE_LABEL = { 'off': 'Off', 'push-to-talk': 'PTT', 'always-on': 'On' }` (VoiceButton.tsx:54-58).\nMeasured: the portal reproduced it at `portal/packages/ui/src/voice-control.tsx:129` (pre-change).\nMeasured live 2026-09-09T03:4xZ, verdict snapshot of :3081 — `@e44 - button \"Voice mode — off\": \"Off\"`, DOM class `pc-voice-btn pc-voice-btn--mode-off pc-voice-btn--status-off`, textContent `\"Off\"`.\n\nSo the control commissioned to REPLACE a row of text-label buttons was itself labelled in text. Fidelity to a reference that labels itself in words reproduces the thing the plan existed to remove. The owner reported it directly (\"the voice buttons still have a lot of buttons with text, not icons\").\n\nTHE WORD WAS NEVER LOAD-BEARING. Measured: `portal/app/globals.css` already dropped `.pc-voice-btn-label` entirely under `@media (max-width: 760px)` and put nothing in its place, with the in-file comment \"the orb is the control, the label is commentary, and the accessible name carries the mode regardless\". A control whose mode survives losing its label at one width never needed the label at any width. The mode remains stated by `portalVoiceControlLabel` (accessible name), `portalVoiceControlTitle` (tooltip), the sr-only `role=\"status\"` line, and the per-mode border.\n\nTHE HALF THAT IS NOT FREE. Measured: the base `.pc-voice-btn-icon` mask is ONE mic silhouette shared by every mode. Deleting the label alone would therefore make `off` and `always-on` differ by border colour only — a dead microphone that looks like a live one, strictly worse than the text it replaced. So the icon MUST differentiate, and does: `off` (and `is-unsupported`) take a slashed mic; `always-on` takes a mic with radiating arcs; `push-to-talk` keeps the base mic. Removing the label without the per-mode masks is a REGRESSION, not a partial fix — do not do one without the other.\n\nBINDING ON P-010 and any later engine-picker or settings surface: a persistent state in this control is an icon. Words belong in the accessible name, the tooltip and the sr-only status line, never in the button face.\n\nGUARD: `portal/tests/a-mode-is-an-icon-not-a-word.test.tsx` (11 cases) pins both halves — no visible text in any persistent mode, no `pc-voice-btn-label` in the markup, distinct accessible names per mode, and three pairwise-distinct icon masks. It carries a permanent wrong-implementation control, because every assertion in it is an ABSENCE check and an absence check passes just as happily when the detector is broken.\n\nOPEN, NOT RULED HERE: the DESKTOP still renders `Off`/`PTT`/`On` (VoiceButton.tsx:357). Parity now points the other way — the desktop should follow the portal. That is a papercusp-repo change behind the green gate, outside this plan's portal scope, and it is the owner's call whether the desktop changes too. Raised to the owner 2026-09-09; not actioned unilaterally.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-011 — P-007 security disposition: the desktop-local engine remains local-only; hosted voice is server-brokered\nDate: 2026-09-09\nOwner-directed AUTO continuation authorized completing the remaining P-007 disposition. DECIDED: do not expose `/api/device/voice/turn` or the desktop whisper→brain→kokoro pipeline to the hosted multi-tenant portal. The desktop-local engine remains reachable only through its existing LAN + device-JWT boundary. The cloud portal's hosted-reachable engines are the two server-brokered paths already delivered: LiveKit and ElevenLabs; in the owner-visible picker, LiveKit is the safe local/Papercup fallback when ElevenLabs is absent.\n\nMeasured: D-007's complete source survey found `routes/device/voice-turn.ts` executes STT + brain + TTS on the desktop; `local-whisper-service.ts` binds Whisper to an operator-managed local child process; `kokoro-local.ts` runs TTS in the operator; and `routes/device/voice.ts` exposes the path only through DEVICE_AUTH. P-007 itself records the incompatible hosted boundary: WorkOS sessions + multi-tenant RLS. The current plan contains no owner-approved trust or relay design that would change those measured boundaries.\n\nRationale: bridging that endpoint would not be a port; it would create an Internet-facing remote-execution/media path into a user's desktop and require a separately designed trust, discovery, consent, revocation, NAT/relay, tenant-isolation, and abuse-control system. Inventing that system here would violate both reuse-first and the portal's fail-closed tenancy model.\n\nP-007 is therefore terminal as intentionally not implemented, not unfinished. A future owner-approved remote-desktop voice product may reopen the idea as its own security plan; it must not be smuggled into this release. This disposition ratifies D-007 and D-009 rather than changing the shipped engine-selection mechanism.\nRelated: P-007, P-006, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: add portal tests and verify live work-ref hydration. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000898 — Freshly measure chat-history and plans-tab latency, explicitly falsify or confirm candidate mechanisms, fix the measured root cause plus any false outage taxonomy, and add a recurrence guard. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000114 — Re-read and complete WI-10000114 / portal-chat-history-2026-09-06 acceptance and shipment against current source and the latency result; do not redo settled implementation. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000657 — Re-read and complete WI-10000657 / portal-tab-performance-2026-09-07 acceptance using current source and current acceptance machinery; resolve the stale subject-harness evidence issue honestly. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000663 — Complete WI-10000663: identify the owner of monotone portal timeout handles, durably clear the leak, and add a detector. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] EI-22652615103627575 — Complete EI-22652615103627575: serve and record real portal release provenance so performance comparisons cannot certify null==null. <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] EI-22689325784232956 — Complete EI-22689325784232956 with a durable guard that prevents carried verified rows from authorizing code at an unverified enforcement layer. — note: → EI-22689325784232956 <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10000906 — Reconcile peer-owned WI-10000656 without contesting a progressing claim: obtain its current disposition, help only with new discriminating evidence, and take over solely if the lane becomes stranded.… <!-- P-008 -->\n## Background\n\nThe recovered session left a completed-but-unverified shared report renderer, an authenticated portal link-hydration gap, fresh latency diagnosis for chat history and plans, and five older ledger items. WI-10000848 is now verified and closed; this plan owns the residue that remains.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Split renderer trust from brain authority.** Preserve D-007's public converse/tool boundary; renderer trust and brain/tool trust remain separate decisions.\n\n**R-2 — Authenticate renderer widening.** Give authenticated/local portal viewers work-item hydration only through a server- or shell-owned trust value; never accept a browser-supplied privilege flag.\n\n**R-3 — Diagnose current latency contrastively.** Measure chat-history/plans latency now; WI-2141694's K=0 result rejects portal self-saturation as a premise, so every candidate mechanism must be distinguished by a falsifiable observable.\n\n**R-4 — Reconcile ledger truth.** Re-read existing plans and work-items from current source and ledger state; never fabricate evidence or repeat already-settled implementation.\n\n**R-5 — Preserve peer ownership.** Do not contest WI-10000656 while its live peer claim is progressing; coordinate once and take over only if the lane becomes stranded.\n\n**R-6 — Ship recurrence guards.** Every behavior change includes a regression in the owning repository and focused verification.\n\n## Design\n\nUse the existing shared Papercup renderer, portal session classification, work-item ledger, plan acceptance surfaces, timer/provenance probes, and carry verification mechanisms. Add no parallel subsystem.\n\nTrust is split deliberately: the portal host proxy continues to send public trust to converse, while the UI renderer derives its trust from the authenticated/local shell context. This enables safe ref hydration without exposing owner MCP/tool authority.\n\nLatency work begins with request-stage timings and current traces, then changes only the measured bottleneck and the timeout taxonomy that misreports latency as unreachability.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | live |\n| R-4 | P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-008 | live |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-002, P-005, P-006, P-007 | tree |\n\nR-1 and R-2 are discharged by source and tests that keep the portal brain public while deriving the renderer's trust from shell-owned session state. R-3 needs live request-stage timing because the symptom is latency in a running portal. R-4 is ledger/source reconciliation. R-5 reads the live peer claim before any action. R-6 is discharged by committed tests or deterministic guards in each behavior-changing lane.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nThe plan is complete when P-001 through P-006 are terminal with tests and root-cause evidence, P-007 records the peer-owned item's terminal disposition or an evidence-backed takeover, and both affected portal plans have a current, honest acceptance/ship disposition.\n\n## Phase 1 — Owner-reported Papercup behavior\n\n- **P-001** `done` Derive Papercup report-renderer trust from the authenticated/local portal viewer while preserving the public converse/tool boundary; add portal tests and verify live work-ref hydration. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-10000897 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `dropped` Freshly measure chat-history and plans-tab latency, explicitly falsify or confirm candidate mechanisms, fix the measured root cause plus any false outage taxonomy, and add a recurrence guard. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-10000898 completed (dropped)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Reconcile affected plan acceptance\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Re-read and complete WI-10000114 / portal-chat-history-2026-09-06 acceptance and shipment against current source and the latency result; do not redo settled implementation. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Re-read and complete WI-10000657 / portal-tab-performance-2026-09-07 acceptance using current source and current acceptance machinery; resolve the stale subject-harness evidence issue honestly. importance: high\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Finish carried implementation defects\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Complete WI-10000663: identify the owner of monotone portal timeout handles, durably clear the leak, and add a detector. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` Complete EI-22652615103627575: serve and record real portal release provenance so performance comparisons cannot certify null==null. blocked-by: P-004\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Verification integrity\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Complete EI-22689325784232956 with a durable guard that prevents carried verified rows from authorizing code at an unverified enforcement layer. — note: ← EI-22689325784232956 released\n- **P-008** `todo` Reconcile peer-owned WI-10000656 without contesting a progressing claim: obtain its current disposition, help only with new discriminating evidence, and take over solely if the lane becomes stranded. — note: ← WI-10000906 released\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Split renderer trust from converse/tool authority\nDate: 2026-09-09\nMeasured: packages/operator-ui/src/papercup-chat/PARITY.md:78 defines the public/owner converse toolset split, and PARITY.md:120 defines work-ref pills as public=inert and owner=render. Portal packages/ui/src/shell.tsx already distinguishes local and authenticated session views, while portal packages/ui/src/ask-papercup.tsx hardcodes renderer hostTrust=\"public\" and apps/host/src/papercup-chat.ts separately hardcodes public converse trust. Decision: preserve public trust for the host proxy/converse/tool plane; derive only the shared UI renderer trust from shell-owned authenticated/local state. Never accept a viewer-supplied trust flag.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-002 — Reject portal self-saturation as the latency premise\nDate: 2026-09-09\nMeasured: WI-2141694's current checkpoint records K=0 portal-held sockets with a positive-control socket census, and the item is dropped. Decision: do not reuse the prior six-socket/self-saturation hypothesis. P-002 must start from current request-stage timings and a contrastive diagnosis; connection contention remains only one rival hypothesis until newly measured.\nRelated: P-002\n\n### D-003 — Preserve the live retained-surface claim\nDate: 2026-09-09\nMeasured: work_items:get on WI-10000656 at 2026-09-09T06:48Z reported assignee su-6cd4d159-ab71-4bd5-a2c1-85ce3ed40369 and a later checkpoint describing current trace results. Decision: do not claim or edit that lane while the holder is live/progressing. Send useful evidence once; take over only after a fresh liveness/progress check proves the lane stranded.\nRelated: P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"review-verification-efficiency-2026-09-09","title":"Review and verification efficiency — retain judgment, automate bookkeeping","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-09","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Review and verification efficiency — retain judgment, automate bookkeeping\nslug: review-verification-efficiency-2026-09-09\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-09\nupdated: 2026-09-30\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Seven plan items are complete; P-008 is claimed by replacement fleet member under WI-10000985. Its settled staging HEAD 4d2cb4be matrix passed all 12 files (834 assertions, zero skips) with harness-scoped runs 19721300/01 and 19721306–15; bindings 14337–14348 were measured current and superseded stale binding 13412 is retracted. LIVE_GATE_OPS is separate.\n\n**Next:** P-008 holder keeps R-10 UNKNOWN unless an immutable matched baseline and inventory can be recovered or an independently reviewed BAR action resolves the gap; fleet leader places independent rev4 meta-vetting, then refresh product grading and final typecheck before author verdict. Deployed certification requires a distinct gate-owner receipt.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10000978 — Map exact current call paths, prior-plan deliverables, governing decisions, source/receipt baseline and remaining gaps for R-1 through R-10. Prove stale/partial/false/self-reviewed evidence refuses. Typecheck after final edits, update canonical runbooks, co… <!-- P-008 -->\n## Background\n\nEvidence: scratchpad/plan-throughput-verification-audit-2026-09-09.md (WI-10000908). The audit did not establish a general slowdown. It established false completion formatting rejections, concentrated expensive test/fixture retries and long acceptance/reviewer tails. Preserve that distinction; no blanket test reduction or invented saving percentage.\nSource: codex session 01a0852a-448b-72a1-8fc0-80941826f408, originating turn 1 through SELF/AUTO authorization turn 22 (2026-09-09T15:29:21.420Z). Owner follow-up explicitly requires existing-router recruitment and waking. Native transcript is recoverable when sessions:read fails (EI-22798764355689052).\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Reviewer routing and independence.** Reviewer selection, wake/pickup, independence, decline/expiry replacement and bounded fallback use the existing consult router. Reuse use-existing-router-for-review-requests-2026-09-08; do not duplicate its implementation. Verify current implementation, acceptance and runtime independently; diagnose the observed rubric-read disagreement rather than assuming the rubric is absent. Respect live peer claims.\n\n**R-2 — Structured causal evidence.** Explicit causal evidence contains hypothesis, alternative, test procedure, predicted observation under each, actual observation and evidence references. Eliminate mandatory English sentence grammar. Preserve historical records, causal honesty and truthful already-fixed/investigation dispositions; structural validity does not prove causal truth.\n\n**R-3 — Versioned completion contract.** Expose the entire applicable completion contract together from the same versioned definition the running validator uses. Return all unmet requirements together through existing read/validation surfaces. Validation-only calls do not mutate or close work; no substantive guard is bypassed.\n\n**R-4 — Durable evidence references.** Capture machine-known test/evidence facts once, then use durable references across work-items, specs, audits and acceptance. Reuse agent-work-efficiency-2026-09-08 evidence bundles, recovery, resume packets and repetition advisories. Do not retype recorded commands, outcomes, SHAs, IDs or canonical requirement text. Unknown, failed, skipped, partial, stale or wrong-subject evidence never becomes passing proof.\n\n**R-5 — Scorecard acceptance by reference.** The rubric author may accept/reject an exact independent scorecard by ID plus reasoning without transcribing its complete ratings. Preserve the original independent card and persist the source relationship. Reject wrong rubric/revision/subject, nonterminal/retracted/stale cards, unauthorized authors and prohibited lineage. Retain the separate author judgment.\n\n**R-6 — Relevant reuse and proportionate scrutiny.** Reuse unchanged item audits, relevant test receipts and vetted criteria/templates with original provenance. Invalidate only on relevant criterion/code/dependency/environment/method/promise changes, not unrelated global HEAD or status/formatting changes. Use reviewed reusable acceptance criteria and one independent product-focused review for ordinary work; additional rubric/meta/grading scrutiny is for material new criteria, disputed evidence, high-risk work or accountable sampling. Never reduce independence merely to compensate for broken reviewer staffing.\n\n**R-7 — Deterministic bookkeeping.** Derive mechanical status, counts, next actions and notifications from authoritative writes. Remove duplicate completion FYIs, copied results and unchanged checkpoint rewrites. Preserve new decisions, blockers, rationale and non-derivable successor context. Extend existing state/event/checkpoint surfaces, using push instead of agent polling.\n\n**R-8 — Focused and recoverable testing.** Keep focused regressions, integration/persistence checks and representative live user journeys. Improve expensive fixture isolation and failed-scenario reruns/recovery through existing testing surfaces. Never rerun a matrix solely to recover evidence; retain full final coverage where the release promise needs it. Distinguish infrastructure/fixture failure from product failure.\n\n**R-9 — Acceptance and delivery separation.** Separate current-build implementation acceptance from final deployed-only certification. Keep explicit delivery properties, the shared green gate and one live gate fixer. No force past red without owner approval. Non-final implementation proceeds independently of deployment.\n\n**R-10 — Measurable efficiency without monitoring sprawl.** Compare representative before/after workflows using existing ledgers: mechanical submissions/calls, acceptance wait, false rejections, justified reruns and escaped/reopened defects, with unfinished-plan age and measurement limitations. No unbounded new monitoring program; no equating aggregate test-file duration to elapsed plan time.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-007 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-007 | live |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004, P-008 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-007, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-10 | P-001, P-008 | tree |\n\nExtend existing completion records and handlers, scorecards, rubric/criterion identity, audit carry-forward, test evidence bundles, plan-state derivation and canonical guidance. No parallel router, scheduler, service or evidence store. Read applicable design/testing/performance and persona edit-path docs before corresponding edits. Hold plan-linked work and automatic per-edit locks; preserve dirty peer changes and leave commits to git-sync. Pin baseline source/receipts before edits. Prove guards with permanent negative controls or copy-out mutants, never temporary regressions in shared source.\n\nAlready-shipped functionality receives explicit reuse evidence, not duplicated implementation. Coordinate a peer-owned gap once with its exact owner and continue independent work. Acceptance/runtime faults do not authorize weakening the contract. Report implemented, accepted, committed, promoted and executing separately.\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline and completion contract\n\n- **P-001** `done` Map exact current call paths, prior-plan deliverables, governing decisions, source/receipt baseline and remaining gaps for R-1 through R-10. Record a bounded reuse/change inventory and representative before-workflow counts. — note: ← WI-10000978 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement explicit causal prediction/observation evidence and shared versioned full completion-requirement/validation feedback in existing surfaces. Preserve historical reads, truthful dispositions and every substantive close guard. Add handler/schema positive and negative controls. Depends on P-001. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10000979 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Remove duplicated evidence work\n\n- **P-003** `done` Implement author acceptance/rejection by exact independent scorecard reference without ratings transcription. Retain persistence, provenance, authorization, lineage and current-subject/revision checks; verify real handler behavior. Depends on P-001. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10000980 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Complete safe criterion/template vetting and relevant-evidence reuse on existing audit/rubric/test identities. Scope invalidation to actual dependencies; preserve material/high-risk/disputed scrutiny. Prove unchanged reuse and changed-input refusal. Depends on P-002 and P-003. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 — note: ← WI-10000981 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Remove remaining mechanical evidence/status/notification duplication using existing evidence bundles, resume packets, authoritative state and events. Update canonical guidance after reading its edit-path runbook; preserve judgment and successor context. Depends on P-002, P-003 and P-004. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004 — note: ← WI-10000982 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Targeted verification and reviewer delivery\n\n- **P-006** `done` Verify and improve failed-scenario reruns, evidence recovery and expensive fixture isolation in the existing testing path. Distinguish infrastructure from product failures and preserve final coverage. Address actual P-001 gaps, not a speculative rewrite. Depends on P-001. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10000983 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Integrate with the existing reviewer-router rollout and settle reproducible in-scope acceptance lookup defects. Demonstrate eligible-reviewer wake/pickup and decline/expiry behavior through the existing lifecycle. Verify the executing build via authorized delivery, respecting live gate ownership. Depends on P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005 and P-006. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 — note: ← WI-10000984 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `todo` Run representative end-to-end workflows and compare mechanical cost against P-001. Prove stale/partial/false/self-reviewed evidence refuses. Typecheck after final edits, update canonical runbooks, complete code-truth audit, independent rubric vetting/grading, author verdict, plan shipment and truthful live-delivery verification. Close WI-10000964 and end this task loop only when all required work is complete. Depends on P-007. blocked-by: P-007 — note: ← WI-10000985 released\n\n## Acceptance BAR\n\n- R-1: Existing router selects eligible independent reviewers, wakes them, records actual pickup/outcome and advances decline/expiry without duplicate chains or altered review subjects. No parallel staffing system or self-review loophole.\n- R-2: Explicit causal evidence is accepted without sentence-template repair; incomplete records return all applicable unmet requirements without closing work. Caller discovery and runtime share the contract version.\n- R-3: Recorded tests can be bound/recovered and independent scorecards accepted by reference without transcription or unnecessary test processes. Wrong/stale/partial/skipped/retracted/prohibited-lineage evidence refuses with specific reasons.\n- R-4: Unchanged audits/criteria/templates retain original evidence provenance; relevant changes require new proof or judgment and unrelated bookkeeping does not. Material/high-risk/disputed work retains independent scrutiny.\n- R-5: Representative before/after workflows have fewer mechanical submissions/calls without removing required product checks. State/notifications stay honest; current-build acceptance and runtime delivery are separately demonstrated.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Owner authorization and SELF route\nDate: 2026-09-09\nAvi authorized a durable plan and SELF/AUTO implementation from start to finish at session_turn:codex:01a0852a-448b-72a1-8fc0-80941826f408:22. No implementation fleet. Required independent review is routed through existing machinery; the author does not self-certify.\n\n### D-002 — Preserve substance, simplify mechanics\nDate: 2026-09-09\nNo blanket test reduction or unsupported general-slowdown claim. Optimize evidence entry, staffing, applicability checking and bookkeeping; preserve causal reasoning, real user outcomes, reviewer independence and final release properties. Existing carry-forward/evidence/router work is reused.\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance and delivery remain distinct\nDate: 2026-09-09\nCurrent-build evidence is the default implementation plane. Claims that everyday agents encounter the new contract/router require executing-build evidence. Exactly one live gate operator; AUTO is not force-past-red permission. Pending delivery remains pending without reopening accepted implementation.\n\n### D-004 — Coverage fields ride the TERMINAL AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT verdict only; non-verdict statuses deliberately carry none\nDate: 2026-09-11\nRULING (P-006 / R-8 sub-req 5). `scripts/affected-tests.mjs` now appends `testsExecuted=N testsSkipped=M coverageUnreadableTasks=K` to `AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT`. Those fields appear ONLY on the terminal verdict emitted by `resultLine()` — the `status=passed` / `status=failed` line. `status=refused`, `status=aborted` and `status=dry-run` are emitted from hardcoded strings and deliberately carry NO coverage fields.\n\nWHY, and why this is not a gap to \"fix later\":\n1. The dangerous reading the tally exists to remove is \"status=passed while nothing executed\". A non-verdict status already self-declares that it decided nothing, so it cannot be mistaken for a green. Stamping coverage there would add noise, not safety.\n2. Several non-verdict lines are emitted ABOVE the point where the tally can be declared at all. The counters block states the constraint directly: these are module-level `let`s and \"a closure over these `let`s is a TDZ throw until this point\" (scripts/affected-tests.mjs, `readTerminalCounters` comment). A pre-launch refusal (`refuseOnTaskBudget`) and the early `no-affected-workspaces` / `all-excluded` / `no-test-script` exits all run before it. Making the fields universal would mean hoisting live state above its own declaration — the exact hazard that block was written to prevent.\n3. A run that never entered the run loop measured nothing. `testsExecuted=0` there would be a measured-looking zero for tasks that never started — the same bounded-measurement-as-confident-number defect the three-state tally exists to avoid.\n\nCONSUMER CONTRACT (what other lanes must follow):\n- Read coverage fields only after checking `status` is `passed` or `failed`. Requiring them unconditionally is a defect in the CONSUMER.\n- `REQUIRED_MARKER_FIELDS` in affected-tests-result-line.test.ts is the \"present on EVERY path\" set. The coverage fields MUST NOT be added to it; doing so asserts a promise the code correctly does not keep, and would red-pin the gate on every refused run.\n- Appending stays the compatibility contract: the prefix through `undeterminedTasks=` is byte-identical, green-checkpoint.ts matches the line whole (`SUITE_REFUSAL_LINE_RE`) and all readers tokenise `k=v`, so trailing fields reach existing parsers inert.\n\nMeasured: `node scripts/affected-tests.mjs --changed-paths .gitignore` (2026-09-11T12:02Z, HEAD bb945b55ab + this change) emitted:\n`AFFECTED_TESTS_RESULT status=passed tasks=4 failed=0 quarantinedFailed=0 timedOutTasks=0 undeterminedTasks=0 testsExecuted=0 testsSkipped=0 coverageUnreadableTasks=4`\n— all 4 tasks are repo-wide lint/invariant guards, not vitest, so they are reported UNREADABLE rather than as a measured zero. That is the three-state behaviour working, not a defect.\n\nMeasured (the false red this scoping removes): asserting the coverage fields on ANY marker line failed at affected-tests-coverage-accounting.test.ts:205 with `expected undefined to be defined` while the same source passed the `foldTaskCoverage` / `formatCoverageFields` containment checks — i.e. the wiring was present and the spawned run had returned a non-verdict line under concurrent load. Load-correlated, and on the gate's own suite.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-005 — Freshness checks must identify the evaluator, not the unrelated Scout background host\nDate: 2026-09-12\nMeasured: current-tree P003 integration at 53edba367e failed stale_host_generation although its scorecard evaluator was the newly launched test process. packages/operator-core/lib/scout/generation-watermark.ts:readRunningGeneration explicitly reads papercup-bg-host.service and compares that separate process boot HEAD with the querying build; it is Scout telemetry, not evidence of evaluator staleness. The defect EI-23074025929199961 originated when emit.ts promoted that advisory flag into a universal write refusal (EI-22964903794871049). Restore this Scout field to disclosed telemetry. Keep evaluator identity enforcement in the existing validateSpecTestAdequacyReplay path, which reruns the exact pinned evaluator, refuses build mismatch, missing identity, mismatched clause or contradicted pass, and writes no card. No new generation system and no restart requirement after unrelated global HEAD changes. Regression controls must distinguish a stale Scout with a current evaluator (may emit) from actual pinned evaluator drift (must refuse). This corrects instrument scope; reviewer independence, causal proof, and current evidence remain mandatory.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-007\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-13\nAmendment-Id: review-verification-p007-method-checks-v1\nRequest-Hash: c95aeb54e6e79b49398a4580484c80fef36a3a7a14211ca1cd1b922696a7f20d\nActor: su-97fccf61-e827-47ed-b670-751d6675a8a9\nReason: Bind concrete METHOD and structured checks to all ten predeclared acceptance BARs before vetting and grading; preserve BAR keys, provenance, scope, and pass semantics.\nApproved-By: su-cce35fc4-bc66-4193-b6a7-b7676fde310b\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:203586\nApproved-At: 2026-09-13T04:56:22.862Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 18 → 19\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-27\nAmendment-Id: p008-rev4-approved-1147976-20260927\nRequest-Hash: 5fcfd8bcfd326a701273fa238318f5d2666c87d55bcd6fdb2babd0a709b51284\nActor: su-respawn-866cd52e6c366185ce35a260c4bcdf65\nReason: Independent meta-vetting found generic falsifiers and missing R-8 coverage accounting plus R-9 content-containment/R-10 bounded-population detectors. Preserve all ten predeclared outcomes and planes while repairing verification and synchronizing the subject-plan revision.\nApproved-By: su-60554620-6afc-466e-932f-4c8a9d1319fd\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1147976\nApproved-At: 2026-09-27T00:05:46.092Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 23 → 24\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n## Measurement and reversal\n\nRecord exact source/test/environment identity, requested/executed coverage, durable receipts and observed stage boundaries. Measure eliminated mechanical steps plus actual scenario outcomes, not raw test counts. Reopened/escaped defects and unfinished-plan age guard the comparison. Any rollout control reuses existing settings; do not park finished functionality disabled. Reversal must preserve historical evidence and must never accept invalid claims.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"storewolf-cloudinary-to-cloudflare-r2-2026-09-09","title":"Storewolf product images: Cloudinary to Cloudflare R2 migration","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-09","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Storewolf product images: Cloudinary to Cloudflare R2 migration\nslug: storewolf-cloudinary-to-cloudflare-r2-2026-09-09\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-09\nupdated: 2026-09-09\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** Partial migration implemented in the local Storewolf checkout. R2 has 38,518 usable images; three damaged processed images were recovered from RAW. All21 tests pass, and16 sample export rows produced103 public HTTPS image downloads matching local bytes. Source changes are local and uncommitted; no application process was started or live marketplace listings changed. Verification artifacts: /home/marsh-office/storewolf-central-server/Debug/MarketplaceStuff/r2-migration-verification.json and r2-migration-sample-exports.csv. The manifest/content-addressing redesign remains withdrawn.\n\n**Next:** P-001 retains recovery of2,874 primary-photo references without known local originals and one empty OptiPlex awards image. Existing credentials for both Cloudinary accounts returned401 on authenticated resource reads. Locate another archive or restore Cloudinary access before completing recovery; unresolved references retain their original URLs. Source delivery also remains unverified: this external checkout is not covered by the available Papercusp git-sync scope, and manual commits are prohibited by the workspace instructions. Plan acceptance remains unshipped; the stale free-tier BAR must be aligned to Avi's later paid-account approval (session_turn:codex:01a08443-d840-7df2-849d-083477e215e6:26). rubrics:amend dry-run currently rejects its retained model/bar alias, filed as EI-22760310501189890. No additional spending permission is needed for the already-approved R2 storage.\n\n## Scope\n\nReplace Cloudinary with Cloudflare R2 while keeping the existing product-image folders, filenames, stored product data and export structure. Use the existing processed files under /mnt/data/Debug/MarketplaceStuff/Images/RAW_TRANSFORMED (approximately 3.05 GB), plus existing local main-image files needed by the exports. Proposed public hostname: images.storewolf.com.\n\nNo new manifest, content-hash naming system, catalog migration, deduplication framework, worker redesign, broad historical recovery, site redesign, or production-server migration. Preserve existing main/alternate/custom-photo selection and order. Report missing files encountered during upload; do not invent substitutes or silently claim they were uploaded.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Public R2 images.** Existing selected local product images are served as valid anonymous HTTPS image downloads from Cloudflare R2.\n\n**R-2 — Minimal export swap.** Generated marketplace image fields point to corresponding R2 files while preserving existing photo selection, ordering and non-image export values.\n\n**R-3 — Future uploads.** The existing product-image preparation flow uploads usable images to R2 without calling Cloudinary.\n\n**R-4 — Approved hosting cost.** The image upload uses the existing R2 account at its published Standard rates without activating paid add-on services; Avi approved the disclosed approximately $0.05/month incremental image storage after the existing account was measured above the shared free tier.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Work items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-003 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001 | live |\n\n## Necessary implementation\n\n1. Add a small R2 upload/public-URL helper using the already-installed AWS S3 SDK and environment configuration. Upload existing usable processed files under their current relative folder/filename paths. Keep originals on disk; skip/report empty or invalid files. One simple repeatable upload command is enough.\n2. Point getTransformedUrl and the active main-image export fields to the matching R2 object paths. Replace the executable store-wolf-to-dimvj15xq account substitutions. Handle the known legacy URL/filename forms in this helper; use the existing image-detail generation methods where current filenames need refreshing. Do not create a second catalog or rewrite source Google Sheets. Include necessary product-source/main/custom-image upload callers only.\n3. Replace Cloudinary upload calls on the normal image path with R2 uploads. Cloudinary currently also resizes images; R2 only stores files. Reuse existing processed bytes for migration, and use local Sharp processing for future images while retaining the current c_mfit,w_1600 behavior. Keep existing public method names where that avoids caller changes. All preparation remains before synchronous export-column evaluation.\n\n## Files expected to change\n\n- Services/MarketplaceStuff/MarketplaceStuff.js: URL and upload helpers, small integration changes.\n- Services/MarketplaceStuff/Config.js: active main/alternate/custom image fields and Cloudinary account substitutions.\n- One small shared R2 helper and a thin one-off upload command if existing entrypoints are unsuitable for the bulk copy.\n- package.json/owning lockfile only as needed to declare Sharp directly; reuse existing @aws-sdk/client-s3.\n- Focused .vitest.ts tests. Touch other existing image callers only when necessary for this provider swap; no worker architecture changes.\n- Protected environment configuration for R2 account, bucket, upload credentials and public base URL; secrets remain outside Git.\n\n## Phase 1 — Minimal swap\n\n- **P-001** `needs-human` Establish R2 access, check existing account usage, configure the image bucket/public hostname, and upload existing valid processed/main-image files preserving their paths. Record actual failed or missing files. — note: 38518 usable images uploaded; remaining recovery needs another archive or restored Cloudinary access for2874 primary references and one empty image. Both authenticated Cloudinary resource checks401. Evidence on WI-10000878; no complete migration claimed.\n- **P-002** `done` Make the small shared upload/URL replacement in the current code and export fields; preserve image selection, stored data, filenames and synchronous export behavior. Reuse local processing for future uploads. — note: ← WI-10000879 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Test URL mapping and upload calls, generate representative eBay/other affected export rows in isolation, and verify their URLs return actual images anonymously over HTTPS. Enable the change only after upload/public verification. Do not submit or revise live marketplace listings. — note: ← WI-10000880 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `dropped` Superseded by P-001/P-003; separate manifest/pilot-and-bulk framework withdrawn at Avi's request.\n- **P-005** `dropped` Superseded by minimal P-002; broad integration/refactor lane withdrawn.\n- **P-006** `dropped` Superseded by focused P-003; broad migration acceptance framework withdrawn.\n- **P-007** `dropped` Superseded by P-003; separate rollout program withdrawn.\n\n## Verification and practical limits\n\nUse focused tests in the existing Vitest framework for legacy ID/full-URL conversion, URL encoding, main and custom photo selection, and successful/failed uploads. Check an actual generated file and download its image URLs without authentication. Do not call generateUploads with its default shared-data reset merely to test. Preserve existing local images so failed uploads can be retried.\n\nThe earlier read-only checks found the storewolf.com zone accessible and no DNS record at images.storewolf.com, but the inspected token's R2 bucket-list call returned 403. R2 subscription status, usable object-upload credentials and account usage are not yet established. A cached Wrangler login has no r2 scope in its recorded scopes; it does not establish R2 access either.\n\nR2 Standard includes 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A and 10 million Class B operations monthly, and free direct-download bandwidth. The processed archive alone is approximately 3.05 GB. Check account usage and additional main-image size before upload; do not upload the 8 GB original archive as a second copy. No paid Cloudflare Images or Worker service. R2 overages remain billable, so zero cost depends on remaining within the account-wide allowance. Source: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/ .\n\nExisting detail references sometimes contain old version filenames and some main/custom originals may be unavailable. Resolve straightforward known forms using existing files; any remaining recovery work is an explicit gap to discuss, not a reason to expand this swap into a new system. Reverting code would restore the previous behavior but cannot revive the shutdown Cloudinary account; preserve uploaded R2 files during any correction.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-desktop-terminal-closure-recovery-2026-09-12","title":"Acceptance BAR — September 12 desktop terminal incident and PTY recovery","status":"active","created":"2026-09-12","owner":"su-d2b8e9e5-f655-4e4c-ab16-bbe63bf5c65a","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — September 12 desktop terminal incident and PTY recovery\nslug: acceptance-desktop-terminal-closure-recovery-2026-09-12\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-12\nupdated: 2026-09-12\nowner: su-d2b8e9e5-f655-4e4c-ab16-bbe63bf5c65a\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — September 12 desktop terminal incident and PTY recovery\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). GNOME terminal server died by SIGKILL at 17:56:05Z. Sender remains unknown.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Durable terminal repair.** Identify and durably fix the originating cause of all desktop terminals closing, with a regression guard.\n**R-2 — Exact desktop recovery.** Restore every original agent active on the real desktop during 2026-09-12T15:01:02Z through 18:01:02Z using psu --resume, including older launches active in that window. Preserve native conversation, identity, account, model, fleet and carry; exclude headless-only sessions and prevent duplicate writers. Record each recovery outcome and unresolved residue.\n**R-3 — Durable deferral repair.** After closure/recovery, investigate and durably repair reported psu-pty-host deferred errors. Establish any relationship to closure from evidence.\n**R-4 — Verification.** Verify fixes with repository regression tests and restoration with concrete window, process and native-session evidence.\n\n## Design\nUse journal kill evidence, authoritative session/activity history and managed host records. Distinguish actual observed exits from reaper notice timestamps. Extend existing terminal/PTY lifecycle code and guarded exact-session capability:launch-agent recovery backed by psu --resume. Use manual locks for source edits and staging/current-build tests. Do not enter unrelated live release operations. One incident work-item WI-10001085 owns execution; this plan records the sequence and acceptance.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | live |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n\n## Acceptance criteria\nClosure: kill origin evidenced, originating defect durably repaired, recurrence test passes. Recovery: each in-scope session has a verified visible original-session resume or explicit actionable failure. Deferrals: event reasons are interpreted through their writer; regression tests demonstrate false deferral fixed while preserving real owner-input protection.\n\n## Work\n- **P-001** `todo` Investigate and durably fix mass desktop terminal closure.\n- **P-002** `todo` Resume original desktop agents from the three-hour census and verify identities and windows. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Investigate and durably repair psu-pty-host deferred errors. blocked-by: P-002\n\n## Decisions\nUse direct execution in this session, as requested incident work.
