The plan-start consult confirmed the design must key compatibility on exact embedding-space identity and explicitly map legacy rows. Deployed plans:start advanced the subject to revision 13 but its stale runtime omitted the revision record and BAR-pin synchronization; current staging already contains the durable fixes. No product files have been edited yet.\n\n**Next:** Repair the revision spine and BAR snapshot via this recorded Now write plus activation re-audit, rerun plans:start to promote P-001, then claim and implement P-001 in this session.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10001128 — Define and validate versioned embedding profiles by extending EMBEDDER_DIM_SPECS with immutable profile id, model revision policy, distance metric, normalization, and document/query recipe identity. … <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001129 — Thread exact profiles through ResolvedEmbedder, query-embedder provenance, canonical memory store configuration, writes, reads, score conversion, and profile-aware re-embedding. Keep current APIs com… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001130 — Evolve shared prose backfill and query paths from width/mode-only compatibility to exact profile identity without discarding current vectors merely to rename them. Preserve independent live-catalog w… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001131 — Implement resumable side-by-side memory profile migration from canonical text with explicit source/target profiles, coverage verification, atomic serving-profile selection semantics, and retention of… <!-- P-004 -->\n## Background\n\nThe application generates document and query vectors; PostgreSQL/pgvector stores them and computes the selected distance at query time. Width equality is necessary but insufficient: vectors from two model revisions or preprocessing recipes may be the same width and still occupy incompatible spaces. The current system already separates embedder output declarations from database storage declarations and verifies live pgvector widths; that independence must remain. It also already separates canonical memory text from per-model vector tables and tags shared prose vectors with an embedder mode.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Independent desired and actual state.** Embedder output configuration and database storage facts remain independently declared; tests and live-catalog validation must detect disagreement without deriving either side from the other.\n\n**R-2 — Complete versioned identity.** Every production embedding profile jointly identifies its immutable profile id, model, revision policy, output dimensions, distance metric, normalization, and document/query processing recipes; equal width alone never establishes compatibility.\n\n**R-3 — End-to-end profile binding.** Every resolved embedder and stored-vector path changed by this plan carries an exact profile identity, and query selection uses that same identity; a mismatch fails closed or degrades to lexical results rather than comparing foreign vectors.\n\n**R-4 — Closed pgvector metric mapping.** A profile metric compiles only through a closed, injection-safe mapping to its pgvector distance operator, score conversion, and matching index operator class. PostgreSQL receives the application-generated query vector and performs ranking; it never generates embeddings.\n\n**R-5 — Backward-compatible current data.** Existing compatible vectors remain usable without recomputation merely to add versioned identity; new writes carry exact profile identity immediately and legacy compatibility is explicit and test-covered.\n\n**R-6 — Side-by-side memory migration.** Canonical text and profile-specific vector storage allow a target memory profile to be built resumably while the current profile remains serving; coverage is verified before query embedder and storage selection switch together, and the previous profile remains retained for rollback.\n\n**R-7 — Prose safety remains independent.** Shared prose vectors gain exact profile identity while retaining their existing single-column resumable backfill and the actual-database live-width checks; a model, revision, or recipe change cannot masquerade as a compatible mode-only vector.\n\n**R-8 — Verification.** Focused unit and integration tests cover profile validation, all metric/operator mappings, current cosine behavior, profile mismatch rejection, existing-data compatibility, re-embedding coverage, coordinated selection, and rollback retention.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n\nExtend the existing `EMBEDDER_DIM_SPECS` declaration rather than creating a parallel configuration system. Profile identity is immutable and versioned; changing any space-defining field requires a new profile id. Keep storage facts in an independent storage registry and assert compatibility between the two. Thread profile metadata through `ResolvedEmbedder`, query-embedder provenance, canonical memory store configuration, and prose backfill/query filters. Current per-mode memory tables become explicit profile storage bindings; adding a future revision requires a new binding/table, allowing old and new profiles to coexist. Distance SQL is generated only from a closed enum.\n\nThe initial rollout must not recompute vectors merely to rename their identity: current vectors are associated with their declared current profile through an additive/backward-compatible migration or equivalent compatibility mapping. New writes use the exact profile immediately.\n\n## Scope boundaries\n\n- Do not replace pgvector.\n- Do not derive database width from embedder configuration.\n- Do not expose arbitrary SQL operators or identifiers from user input.\n- Do not silently switch the live embedding model or run a production-wide re-embed as part of this code change.\n- Do not edit generated schema projections by hand; add canonical SQL migrations and regenerate through the repository workflow when required.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nThe implementation is complete when current embedders have validated versioned profiles; memory and shared prose writes/reads select compatible profile and metric semantics; profile-aware side-by-side memory migration is resumable and coverage-verifiable; actual database width checks remain independent; focused tests pass; and the plan completion audit cites the exact code, tests, and migration evidence.\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract\n\n- **P-001** `done` Define and validate versioned embedding profiles by extending EMBEDDER_DIM_SPECS with immutable profile id, model revision policy, distance metric, normalization, and document/query recipe identity. Add an independent storage-profile registry and tests proving profile fields are complete, ids are unique/versioned, metrics compile only through the closed pgvector mapping, and storage compatibility is checked rather than derived. importance: high — note: ← WI-10001128 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Runtime binding\n\n- **P-002** `done` Thread exact profiles through ResolvedEmbedder, query-embedder provenance, canonical memory store configuration, writes, reads, score conversion, and profile-aware re-embedding. Keep current APIs compatible where practical, reject mismatched vectors, and test every supported comparison metric plus current cosine behavior. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001129 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Stored identity\n\n- **P-003** `done` Evolve shared prose backfill and query paths from width/mode-only compatibility to exact profile identity without discarding current vectors merely to rename them. Preserve independent live-catalog width validation, update the canonical migration/schema sources only, and add mismatch and legacy-data integration coverage. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001130 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Safe migration and verification\n\n- **P-004** `done` Implement resumable side-by-side memory profile migration from canonical text with explicit source/target profiles, coverage verification, atomic serving-profile selection semantics, and retention of the previous profile for rollback. Run focused and affected tests, audit code/migration coverage, and close the plan with exact evidence. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001131 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Independent desired and actual state remain separate\nDate: 2026-09-12\nDate: 2026-09-12\n\nKeep embedder output declarations independent from database storage declarations. Configuration states what an embedder is expected to emit; storage specs and live catalog reads state what PostgreSQL actually accepts. Compatibility tests join them and fail on skew. Deriving storage width from embedder configuration would hide an unapplied migration.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/search/prose-vector-dims.ts currently makes this separation explicit and prose-vector-dims.integration.test.ts plus embed-backfill.ts check live catalog widths.\nRelated: P-001, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Profile identity covers the full embedding space contract\nDate: 2026-09-12\nDate: 2026-09-12\n\nA compatible embedding is identified by a versioned profile, not by width or mode alone. The profile covers model, revision policy, dimensions, metric, normalization, and document/query processing recipes. Any space-defining change requires a new profile identity. Query generation and stored-vector selection must use the same profile; unknown or mismatched identity fails closed.\n\nMeasured: current code already records target dimensions in EMBEDDER_DIM_SPECS, uses distinct memory_vec_<mode> tables, and stores embedding_mode on shared prose tables, but it does not jointly version all space-defining fields.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Metric is a closed profile property, not arbitrary SQL\nDate: 2026-09-12\nDate: 2026-09-12\n\nThe profile's comparison metric compiles through a closed mapping to pgvector distance operator, score conversion, and index operator class. Current profiles remain cosine. No caller may interpolate an arbitrary operator or identifier. The storage declaration independently records its index metric and tests require it to match the emitting profile.\n\nMeasured: CanonicalVectorStore and all audited prose search paths currently hard-code cosine `<=>`; memory vector migrations build `vector_cosine_ops` HNSW indexes.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-004 — Reuse per-profile memory tables for side-by-side migration\nDate: 2026-09-12\nDate: 2026-09-12\n\nCanonical memory text remains stored once while old and new profile vectors coexist in separate profile-bound vector tables. Re-embedding builds the target from canonical text without deleting the serving profile, coverage is verified before selection changes, and the prior binding remains available for rollback. Shared prose columns retain their existing resumable convergent backfill in this plan but gain exact profile identity; replacing them with a polymorphic global vector store would be a larger parallel system and is out of scope.\n\nMeasured: canonical-store.ts and reembed.ts already separate canonical text from per-mode tables and fill a target table without deleting the source.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-005 — Applied migration drift is reconciled by immutable successor evidence\nDate: 2026-09-13\nDate: 2026-09-13\n\nMigration history and deploy safety are reconciled with a successor, not by pretending applied bytes changed. Migration 1154 remains recorded at its actually applied SHA 6c34b901; the canonical 1154 file retains the lock-bounded correction so environments that have not reached it never execute the unsafe monolithic transaction. Migration 1155 is the immutable, idempotent successor that re-applies the corrected end state to databases that already ran 1154. Therefore db:check_drift may continue to flag 1154's historical executable difference; closure is established by 1155's matching ledger SHA plus live catalog/view verification, not by erasing that historical signal.\n\nMeasured: db:migrations at 2026-09-13T07:54Z recorded 1155 at SHA f3c151822fb0b11c7c1a9459bad80195e5041944dae7e0daf6ebc4c0394afc8d; direct information_schema reads returned all 17 profile columns and all four compatibility-view projections present. Current 1154 file SHA is b48510177581764476ac602958e6ec26b5ef45d8ac6614d64662dd1647bc8bc8, while its applied ledger SHA remains 6c34b9014272387faa172be6c8bc4946e586f809746b4cb64a2f0ff361fd5dcd.\nRelated: P-003\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-006 — Internal-only P-003 clauses use targeted L4 counterexamples when no census surface exists\nDate: 2026-09-13\nThe coverage census remains authoritative: never hand-assert coverageRungs and never attach an unrelated coverage_evidence row. For P-003, the live census contains 2,059 current Papercusp surfaces, eight with view-computed meets_l3=true, but zero rows with source_file; the positive-controlled search for operator-core search sources returned no rows. Therefore no current declared surface can reverse-map the internal prose-vector implementation. Each P-003 clause must instead carry independently executed, ledger-backed targeted counterexample/mutation proof; plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy treats that genuine L4 proof as satisfying the L3 floor. The two mutationRequired VP clauses still require targeted L4. The independent tester's blocking critique is work-item comment 203730.\n\nMeasured: direct reads of harness_shared.testing_surface_depth and its writer in libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/846-coverage-census-tables.sql established the population and meets_l3 semantics; packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy.ts lines 639-648 define targeted counterexample/mutation as L4 and L3-or-stronger.\nRelated: P-003\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-14\nAmendment-Id: p003-acceptance-rev5-method-checks-20260913\nRequest-Hash: c8592a002882f02c430dc9ade8c3db8de4e45c51560e3a9141de6ed9dc163e7d\nActor: su-9b0bab35-0020-4599-93fb-283ca0bd8458\nReason: Apply outside-lineage critique WI-10001181/comment 203763: partition R-3/R-7, make R-8 evidence-only, add D-005/D-006 failure semantics, and bind detection-capable structured checks.\nApproved-By: su-71f3b6b4-47ca-49a2-9e3a-3612fa109652\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:204237\nApproved-At: 2026-09-14T01:17:00.624Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 20 → 21\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-fleet-launch-admission-clarity-2026-09-13","title":"Acceptance BAR — Fleet launch clarity — queue screening, launch, and verified pickup","status":"active","created":"2026-09-13","owner":"su-a910ea42-c995-483e-b5f5-bd46da5de524","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Fleet launch clarity — queue screening, launch, and verified pickup\nslug: acceptance-fleet-launch-admission-clarity-2026-09-13\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-13\nupdated: 2026-09-13\nowner: su-a910ea42-c995-483e-b5f5-bd46da5de524\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Fleet launch clarity — queue screening, launch, and verified pickup\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Evidence: docs/audits/backend-reliability-2026-09-13-evidence.json. Original audit WI-10001230. Its measurements are historical snapshots from September 13, not assertions about the runtime at implementation time.\n\nOwner requirements, in sequence: (1) write a plan to fix already diagnosed issues and continue diagnosis of unresolved matters; (2) for every implemented fix, write behavioral regression tests and add them to the suite preventing regressions reaching main; (3) correction: before any implementation, finish ALL diagnosis. This plan implements that ordering literally. A known source defect is not permission to fix it while another diagnostic question remains open.\n\nPrior-art lookup found existing coordination, loop-wake, fleet-reliability and gate-reliability plans. P-001 must resolve exact overlap and current owners before execution; reuse their implemented fixes, tests, and authoritative decisions. Do not reopen retired nursery-tier work or duplicate a live peer's lane. Relevant known plans include coord-dispatch-reliability-2026-06-21, fleet-reliability-verification-2026-07-10, fleet-reliability-verification-acceptance-2026-09-03, gate-verdict-liveness-and-repair-reliability-2026-08-31 and loop-wake-reliability-2026-08-24. These are references, not unexamined authorities about current behavior.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Diagnosis before implementation.** Every audit finding and explicitly recorded audit follow-up must receive a complete diagnostic disposition before ANY repair code, new production instrumentation, configuration adjustment, deployment, or live recovery operation under this plan. Insufficient evidence or an external blocker keeps the barrier closed; it cannot be renamed done to unlock repairs. Independent diagnostic lanes may run in parallel only after the execution route is chosen.\n\n**R-2 — Complete evidence and traceability.** Account for F01-F18 with initiating cause, affected scope/builds, alternative hypothesis, distinguishing procedure, expected and actual observations, evidence references, intended behavior, proposed smallest fix, and acceptance tests. Preserve source-fixed versus runtime-resolved, retrieved versus delivered, dispatch versus business outcome, and queued versus running distinctions. Every scoped newly discovered root-cause issue inherits the same diagnostic and test requirements.\n\n**R-3 — Behavioral regression tests on every fix.** Every implemented correction must include or extend a regression test in the project's maintained test suite that fails on the demonstrated defect/fault-injected baseline and passes with the fix. Cover success, relevant failure and boundary paths; preserve human-input and active-turn safety. A typecheck, source grep, screenshot, ad-hoc script, or optimistic mock is not sufficient behavioral proof. Previously implemented fixes are reused and their tests extended or adopted only after verifying that they catch the audited behavior.\n\n**R-4 — Tests actually gate main.** Each fix's required tests must be selected and executed by the real green-checkpoint promotion command for relevant source, test, fixture, configuration and submodule changes. Required-suite failure, zero execution, missing test prerequisites, silent skips, exclusion, or stale/wrong-candidate evidence must not permit promotion. A post-deployment canary supplements but cannot replace this pre-main gate.\n\n**R-5 — Safe, evidence-based remediation.** No production crash/load tests, arbitrary session interruption, unapproved provider/account change, blanket queue activation, force-deploy past a red verdict, weakened safety guard, or timeout/concurrency increase without a demonstrated cause. Reuse existing scheduler, delivery, retrieval, incident, state and backup mechanisms. Read-only production diagnosis and non-mutating source inspection are allowed in Phase 1; run existing diagnostic probes only against explicitly disposable fixtures when they write, inject, crash or restore.\n\n**R-6 — Proven rollout and closure.** Distinguish diagnosis complete, fix verified on current build, admitted to green main, and confirmed in the affected running component. Do not call an existing process repaired merely because a different build passed. Close the effort only with an F01-F18 disposition matrix, executed regression/gate evidence, applicable runtime witnesses, and explicit residual risks accepted by the owner.\n\n## Design\n\n### Two phases and a hard barrier\n\nPhase 1 performs diagnosis only. P-011 consolidates the diagnostic record. P-012 is an explicit complete-diagnosis review and authorization-provenance barrier, not an elapsed-time or status-count heuristic; D-001 records the owner's standing SELF/AUTO approval, so the review must not request the same permission again. P-013 and every later item are implementation or rollout work and depend on that barrier. No early known-fix exception is allowed.\n\nIf further diagnosis genuinely requires new production instrumentation or other implementation, describe the smallest needed experiment and ask for a specific exception; do not quietly add instrumentation during Phase 1. Prefer existing telemetry, direct read-only source/ledger inspection and disposable offline experiments. A blocked diagnostic item remains blocked and prevents P-012 from opening.\n\n### Diagnostic disposition protocol\n\nEach finding ends as one of: confirmed cause with reproducible evidence and proposed remedy; intentional behavior demonstrated with its governing contract and non-defect control; already fixed demonstrated on the relevant subject with regression evidence; or refuted with a falsifying observation. An unresolved/blocked finding is not complete. An incident's unavailable historical actor may remain unknowable only when the causal class and safety implications have been independently bounded and the owner explicitly accepts that residual at P-012. Merely failing to reproduce is not a refutation.\n\nFor timing/performance questions, P-011 records concrete service objectives, workload population, budgets and thresholds BEFORE implementation. Do not choose a favorable threshold after seeing the repaired result. Representative production evidence informs objectives; deterministic isolated tests enforce behavioral guarantees without flaky dependence on shared-host load.\n\n### Existing test/promotion wiring\n\nVerified during drafting: package.json exposes ordinary test:affected and an opt-in test:affected:integration. scripts/affected-tests.mjs only includes each workspace's generic test:integration when --integration is passed. It already has focused mandatory integration task entries, including prose-vector-dims and resource-governor-queue; extend that existing selection mechanism for the confirmed reliability contracts instead of adding an unrelated runner or merely creating ignored *.integration.test.ts files. Re-read the real gate command when executing because configuration can change.\n\nUse maintained Vitest suites in packages/operator-core and apps/operator, shared isolated PostgreSQL fixtures/migrations, and existing PTY integration fixtures. Add focused required integration targets to workspace scripts and the existing affected task registry where needed. Required acceptance tests must not rely on live provider billing, real owner sessions, ambient production credentials or the shared production database. Full real-world canaries/restore witnesses run separately with exact subject identity; they do not replace gate tests.\n\nFor EACH fix record: finding -> changed source -> test file/case -> failing baseline witness -> passing fix witness -> affected-selection paths -> gate task/run/candidate -> applicable runtime proof. Validate this mapping mechanically using existing coverage/acceptance evidence where possible, not an unmaintained parallel spreadsheet.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-011, P-012 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-013, P-014, P-015, P-016, P-017, P-018, P-019, P-020, P-021, P-022, P-023 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-008, P-013, P-023, P-024 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-009, P-010, P-012, P-024 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-011, P-023, P-024, P-025 | deployed |\n\nR-6 alone needs deployed evidence: promotion lineage, actual long-lived host generation and destination/runtime behavior cannot be certified solely by staging tests. Trace due-list inclusion, workspace/tier/pause policy, tick liveness, pre-claim admission, durable queue and native turn confirmation; compare other affected loop identities using bounded cohort coverage. Diagnose why zero-fire overdue loops escape the current detector (computeTurnsStalled returns false below minimum fire count). Required regressions: fresh arm to first fire and actual next turn; sustained admission pressure; empty/dead executor recovery; rearm after pause; restart; no false healthy at zero fires; preserved authority and human-input safety; duplicate scheduling never duplicates a turn. Fix root cause and detector through existing routines/loop surfaces, with real maintained tests selected by main. Carry-specific replacement remains the other agent's plan; coordinate overlap without taking it over.\nRelated: P-006, P-019, P-021, P-023, P-024\n\n### D-005 — Independent grading-integrity audit rejects current spec-quality card\nDate: 2026-09-14\nMeasured: plans:evaluate-spec-quality recomputed exact specSetHash 33071e61e09bee7785422be5b735b7024c53d0718025c5e41273f74d13ff21c9 with pass:8; plans:get-specs payloadTier full returned the complete 67-row current set split active:10, exempt:15, draft:42; scorecards:list on the exact subject returned only EI-23207223300694459.\n\nIndependent audit EI-23207802912043197 settles EI-23207223300694459 gradingAudit=failed. Draft pending conversation audit.\n**Next:** Activate, implement, test, then return to BYOC.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10001257 — Clarify plan-versus-ad-hoc launcher routing and scope queue-screening refusals/remedies, including accurate explicit-assignment guidance. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001258 — Expose registration/spawn/first-turn/task-claim distinctions in existing launch reporting with unknown-safe evidence. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001259 — Add regression tests for this failed workflow and honest launch reporting; update the current engineering runbook; run focused verification. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Launcher routing.** Existing-plan fleets use fleet:launch-on-plan; fixed ad-hoc briefs use capability:launch-agent. Avoid manually assembling the existing-plan workflow.\n**R-2 — Scoped queue screening.** Duplicate screening blocks automatic queue claims, not agent launch. Explain supported explicit assignment with authority caveats; do not weaken dependencies, locks, security, credentials or resource admission.\n**R-3 — Honest launch evidence.** Distinguish registration, process spawn, verified first turns and claimed tasks. Missing observations are unknown; spawn success must not read as agents working.\n**R-4 — Regression coverage.** Regression-test the observed immediate-headless-fleet request with pending queue work and unverified first turns; no invented wait or false running claim.\n**R-5 — Reuse and authority.** Reuse current tools, admission predicates, launch verification and docs. No new launcher/service/scheduler/capacity setting. Implement personally on canonical staging with locks and tests.\n**R-6 — Return to BYOC.** After focused implementation and verification, resume the existing BYOC plan through exact G7/R7 readiness, canary, 24h soak and verified shipment. No duplicate helpers or held LIVE_GATE_OPS.\n\n## Design\nImprove current launcher tool routing guidance and work-items-admission diagnostics. Add a small derived evidence summary to existing verification/result surfaces, preserving compatibility fields and unknowns. Update the existing engineering runbook rather than broad prompt duplication. Admission/authorization predicates stay unchanged.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-003 | live |\n\n## Implementation\n- **P-001** `done` Clarify plan-versus-ad-hoc launcher routing and scope queue-screening refusals/remedies, including accurate explicit-assignment guidance. — note: ← WI-10001257 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Expose registration/spawn/first-turn/task-claim distinctions in existing launch reporting with unknown-safe evidence. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10001258 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Add regression tests for this failed workflow and honest launch reporting; update the current engineering runbook; run focused verification. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10001259 completed (done)\n\n## Acceptance\nTool guidance names fleet:launch-on-plan for existing-plan fleets and capability:launch-agent for ad-hoc briefs. Queue-pending diagnostics explicitly scope the refusal and do not require a launch delay. Deterministic tests cover pending unassigned work, explicit-assignment caveats, unverified spawn, verified first turn and unknown task claims. Existing authority and dependency predicates remain unchanged. Tests pass and completion audit cites actual source/test evidence. No claim of deployed shipment before final release evidence.\n\n## Decisions\n- **D-001** Owner chose self implementation in AUTO; then resume BYOC. This interruption does not clear its credential gate.\n- **D-002** Reuse existing mechanisms; no new launcher or relaxed safeguards.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"managed-agent-capability-contract-and-native-cutover-2026-09-13","title":"Managed agent capability contract — native cutover, job continuity, offline recovery, preserved TUI UX","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Managed agent capability contract — native cutover, job continuity, offline recovery, preserved TUI UX\nslug: managed-agent-capability-contract-and-native-cutover-2026-09-13\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-13\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-22, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_rubric_unresolved. Next repair: Retry the acceptance-rubric read, or re-route to a process that can see it — the subject PINS a rubric this read could not resolve, so its absence here is UNMEASURED, not established. Do NOT amend or re-seed the rubric on this evidence: as far as this read knows it is intact, and amending it would destroy any in-flight grading card.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nReopened by D-034 (owner #1732, 2026-10-12): extend managed replacement to Codex and OMP, prove agents do equal work on real Papercusp plans (R-17), then turn native tools off per family (R-18). Phase 5 is P-023..P-031; P-015/P-016 now wait on it. Phase 4's P-020 (WI-10007984, held by su-faee16ea) has had no progress since 2026-10-10 21:42Z. Plan is a draft: its activation audit and acceptance-rubric amendment for R-15..R-19 are owed before start.\n\n**Next:** Run the activation audit over the #1732 source turns; amend the acceptance rubric for R-15..R-19; re-route P-020's stale claim; start P-023 (measure Codex/OMP native tool surfaces).\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10001157 — Verify current owners, inherited decisions, tool shapes and launcher paths; implement the complete test-backed capability disposition inventory, precise reuse sites and gap classification. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001162 — Implement start-once managed Bash that yields its durable job at the response deadline; preserve execution deadline, abort/kill, permitted full logs and structured terminal/running results. Test fast… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001163 — Close inventoried PTY/script lifecycle gaps: resize, completion events/wakes, restart/reattachment truth, explicit kernel state/media and nested authorization. Reuse task-manager/orchestration and pr… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001164 — Implement locally authorized bounded native recovery on existing launch surfaces, scoped capabilities, expiry/banner, offline audit/reconciliation and resume reset. Prove operator-unreachable recover… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001165 — Integrate one capability policy into Claude/Codex/OMP launch/resume/wake, cover aliases/nested execution/overrides, preserve sandbox/access policy and gate each restriction on proven replacement qual… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001166 — Connect or complete required file/patch/read/network/browser/state/question/media adapters; retain native UX and correct canonical-store distinctions; preload essentials and document exclusions. No d… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001167 — Add per-family/client acceptance and adoption telemetry, teaching denials, version-change checks, canary and rollback through existing controls. Prove managed positives/native bypass refusals before … <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001168 — Run and repair the isolated real-client parity matrix: launch/resume/wake, jobs/PTY/output, scripts/media/cancel, sandbox, offline recovery and restart windows. Enable verified managed defaults only … <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001169 — Update canonical runbooks/prompts, code-truth audit each item, author/vet as-built rubric, obtain existing eligible independent reviewer grading, record acceptance, verify deployed controls and mark … <!-- P-009 -->\n## Background\n\nAvi requested this plan and self implementation from start to finish in the current conversation, after accepting the recommendation: enforce Papercusp execution and shared-state authority, preserve useful native interfaces rather than rebuild every TUI feature.\n\nHistorical source: codex session 01a08777-040e-7e03-9562-cfbf1f73c9e1 on September 12, 2026, turns 3-11 and 22-27. Full original JSONL answer at line 970 was read; it extends beyond the 8k transcript-index cap. Managed Bash literally runs Bash; missing dedicated verbs do not establish a native-only capability. Operational differences are environment, permissions, stream/PTY semantics, deadlines, completion notifications, discovery and transport overhead, and recovery during operator/MCP outages. Native clients cap their own outputs but those bytes do not uniformly cross Papercusp's result door. We control managed output behavior, which is an advantage, not a reason for an unrestricted second backend.\n\nPrior work read: agent-capability-confinement-2026-06-13 and orchestration-runtime-unification-and-safe-output-2026-08-22 are shipped. Reuse their executors, policies, task ledger, output references and launch integrations; do not reopen completed items or assume shipped means this broader contract is proven. Dedup candidates capability-metadata-contract-2026-05-31 and pui-tui-remediation-and-consolidation-2026-08-27 are also shipped and cover different deliverables.\n\n## Product shaping — Phase 5 (D-034)\n\n**Audience.** Avi, and every agent the fleet runs on Claude, Codex and OMP.\n\n**Problem.** Native client tools run outside Papercusp's managed authority and outside its output bounds. Measured over 24h on 2026-10-12, Codex's native code-mode `exec` carried ~96% of all tool-output bytes: 143k Codex results, 1,067 MB, 33.6 GB re-read volume, against 8k Claude results, 20 MB, 0.85 GB. Papercusp's ~6 KB result cap and spill-to-file bound Claude's calls to Papercusp tools but not Codex's native `exec`. Every managed restriction lists only Claude as a client, and every cutover stage is off.\n\n**Outcome.** Claude, Codex and OMP agents do their work through Papercusp tools. Native tool calls are turned off family by family once proven. Agents finish real Papercusp plan work at least as well as they did with native tools, at no higher token cost.\n\n**Non-goals.** Rebuilding client TUI presentation (rendering, panels and navigation stay). The D-010 offline-recovery path. Trial agents working in the canonical shared tree. Model, provider or effort changes.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner directive #1732 (2026-10-12, Claude session su-8cec8a78), recorded in D-034. Context questions #1729, #1730 and #1731 in the same session. D-032/D-033's cutover exclusion is superseded by D-034.\n\n**Scenarios.**\n- SC-P5-1: after cutover, a Codex agent cannot call the native shell. It runs the command through capability:bash and gets a bounded result with a full-output reference.\n- SC-P5-2: a Codex agent runs a two-minute multi-tool script. The managed scripting path completes it without a 45-second wall and returns a bounded result.\n- SC-P5-3: an OMP fleet member and an OMP su session both lack native write/edit after cutover, and both edit through capability:edit under file locks.\n- SC-P5-4: matched native and managed-only Codex agents get the same completed plan item at its pre-implementation commit in isolated checkouts. Both are graded by that item's own tests, and success and token cost are compared.\n- SC-P5-5: a codex-cli upgrade changes a feature switch. The version check refuses that family's restriction until re-validated, and the native tool stays on.\n- SC-P5-6: a canary family's success rate drops. One-step rollback restores the native tool for that family.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Complete capability disposition.** Record a test-backed disposition for shell/SSH/interpreters, jobs/PTY, script orchestration/kernels, reads/list/search/LSP, edit/write/patch/notebook, HTTP/search/browser/computer, delegation, schedules/monitors/wakes, tasks/plans/goals, memory/checkpoint/resume/rewind, questions/approvals, images/artifacts/skills/discovery and pure TUI presentation. Each is managed execution, managed-backed native interface, deliberately retained interface with explicit boundary, or a precise unsupported gap. Discovery-only hiding is not security.\n\n**R-2 — Preserve command continuity.** Start each command once. Fast completion returns terminal output; exceeding the response window returns the SAME durable running job and full-output reference before MCP expiry without killing/restarting it. Separate execution deadline, response deadline, abort and explicit kill. Preserve exit truth and whole-tree cleanup, no double execution or orphaning. Completion remains observable through carry/restart.\n\n**R-3 — Bounded context, recoverable permitted output.** Preserve complete permitted output outside context with useful bounded previews, exact range/tail/filter retrieval and truthful truncation/retention/write-failure metadata. Preserve Unicode; specify streams and binary capture rather than falsely promise byte equivalence. Credentials stay redacted/access-controlled. Preload essential tools, avoid repeated discovery and measure context bytes separately from RPC counts; exclude native bytes from managed-output claims.\n\n**R-4 — PTY and script replacement quality.** Support managed PTY input, resize, incremental output, exit/cancel/cleanup, and reattachment or explicit unrecoverable restart outcomes. Preserve script authorized nested calls, branching/fan-out, cancellation, truthful uncertain writes, required explicit kernel state and media. Never silently replace persistent/multimodal workflows with stateless/text-only ones. Complete normal completion-wake behavior through existing events/task ownership.\n\n**R-5 — Documented recovery exclusion.** No locally authorized native recovery path ships; the software-rooted substitute proven forgeable in D-007/D-008 is absent and unreachable, not merely unbuilt. Canonical documentation records the absence as a deliberate owner-directed exclusion citing D-010, so a reader cannot mistake it for an oversight and rebuild it. Capability gaps whose only closure route was the dropped path carry an explicit unsupported/documented-exclusion disposition rather than an open gap, with no implementation item stripped to reach zero. Resurrection under a weaker authority root is out of scope.\n\n**R-6 — Enforced policy across clients and lifecycle.** Claude/Codex/OMP managed launch, resume and wake use one policy with version-validated adapters. Cover aliases, shell/interpreter/script nesting, file/network/computer paths and override arguments. Preserve sandbox/credentials/network controls; a managed tool name does not confer confinement. Unknown controls or unproven removal produce explicit unsupported/denied truth, never a false managed guarantee.\n\n**R-7 — Preserve UX and correct canonical state.** Keep native rendering/navigation/diffs/images/skills/discovery and useful plan/question panels when their operations use managed authority. Distinguish session tasks from shared work/plans/goals, durable memory from scratch context, transcript resume from filesystem rewind, HTTP fetch from browser/search, and exact-string edit from multi-file patch. Retained reads/provider/media paths have explicit access/output policies or honestly stated exclusions.\n\n**R-8 — Evidence-gated cutover and actual shipment.** Activate each restriction only after replacement, offline recovery and per-client launch/resume/wake acceptance pass with positive/negative controls. Test version drift, output recovery, jobs/PTY, cancellation, scripts/media, sandbox and nested bypass paths. Canary/rollback reuse existing config and telemetry. Finish code-truth audit, post-implementation rubric/vetting, independent eligible non-lineage grading, author acceptance, deployed-control verification and shipped plan status. Do not silently drop unmet outcomes.\n\n**R-9 — Native feature retention until admitted cutover.** For every family and client whose cutover has not been admitted under R-18, native features remain available and usable. Acceptance observations alone never activate replacement restrictions, cutover stages or wider authority. Native TUI rendering, panels and navigation stay after cutover (D-034 supersedes the D-032/D-033 cutover exclusion).\n\n**R-10 — Persistent managed execution.** An authorized persistent managed kernel session preserves owner-scoped state across permitted calls, bounds recoverable output and media, and exposes cancellation, whole-process cleanup and truthful restart outcomes.\n\n**R-11 — Managed browser parity.** An authorized managed browser session returns the DOM state reached by permitted navigation.\n\n**R-12 — Client integration ahead of cutover.** Each required installed Claude, Codex and OMP journey continues its exact session through the version-aware managed interface.\n\n**R-13 — Reconciled lifecycle parity.** Each declared jobs/PTY, patch/notebook, read/network/media and question/permission boundary exhibits its specified managed semantics, and the canonical capability inventory matches measured source/runtime behavior with paired positive and refusal controls.\n\n**R-14 — Final acceptance record integrity.** Each final parity claim resolves to its exact independently graded evidence record.\n\n**R-15 — Codex and OMP replacement coverage.** Every native tool exposed by the installed Codex and OMP clients maps to a managed replacement, or to an explicit retained/unsupported disposition, in the version-pinned inventory. Codex surfaces include code-mode exec, shell/unified exec and stdin, apply_patch, image view, web/browser/computer use, multi-agent, sleep, plan panel, image generation, apps and skills. Each replacement's gaps are closed or named, for example code:run's 45 s timeout and 20,000-char script limit against Codex exec.\n\n**R-16 — Enforceable off-switch per client.** Each client has a version-validated, host-composable way to turn a native tool off for a launch: Claude's deny list; Codex's Papercusp-generated config.toml feature switches; OMP's allow-list composed for su, role and fleet launches. A turned-off tool is provably absent (negative control: the model cannot call it), Papercusp tools still work, and a client version change re-validates before any restriction applies.\n\n**R-17 — Equal work on real Papercusp plans.** Agents restricted to managed tools complete real Papercusp plan work as effectively as native-tool agents of the same client and model.\n- **Replay trial:** completed plan items replayed from their pre-implementation commit in isolated checkouts, graded by the item's own tests or acceptance, as matched native vs managed-only runs per client.\n- **Live pilot:** managed-only agents on open plan items through the normal claim/verify/complete flow.\n- **Pass (default, fixed before the first run):** on at least 30 replayed items per client, managed-only success no more than 5 points below native, and median tokens per completed item no higher than native.\n- **Reported:** tokens, wall time, tool calls, errors/retries and refusals.\n\n**R-18 — Staged cutover with rollback.** A native tool is turned off per family per client only after that family passes R-16's negative control, the real-client parity matrix and R-17. Canary first, then default. Telemetry records bypass attempts and teaching denials. A one-step rollback through the existing controls is drilled. Verified on the deployed build. Native TUI rendering stays.\n\n**R-19 — Agents taught the managed tools.** Client overlays and shared prompts teach the managed replacement for each turned-off native tool within the launch-prose budget. Guidance for removed tools is deleted. The shared per-result cap statement is accurate for every client.\n\n\n## Design\n\n**Active continuation boundary (Avi, 2026-10-09):** Phase 4 fills and verifies managed replacements while retaining all native TUI features. R-9 through R-14 govern new work; historical cutover enablement and dropped P-004 offline recovery are not revived. Extend existing tool/policy/task/test surfaces; no parallel platform.\n\nOne machine-readable capability disposition contract feeds existing launch controls, guidance and acceptance tests. Extend existing libraries, policy registries and services; no parallel permission system, scheduler, store or orchestration backend. Retain native-looking facades when they call managed authority; disable independent backends per capability after parity. Human-owned unmanaged terminals remain outside managed enrollment.\n\nCommand execution has two clocks: a bounded response window and an independently declared execution deadline. Reuse task/job ownership and log capture. Return terminal output if it finishes; otherwise yield that existing job's durable handle. Completion events/wakes and cancellation use existing task-manager primitives, with idempotent delivery/readback, not new polling loops.\n\nRecovery is checked and recorded locally before contacting the operator, using protected launcher configuration and existing local audit patterns. A failed operator cannot be required to authorize its own recovery. Preserve existing security authority; no broad permanent overrides.\n\n### Capability disposition matrix\n\n| family | existing managed authority / counterpart | interface policy |\n| shell, SSH, interpreter | capability:bash | managed backend after parity |\n| jobs, output, stop, PTY | bash_output/bash_kill, pty_*, task-manager | managed lifecycle, familiar terminal interface |\n| scripting, kernels | code:run, recipes/orchestrate, managed language execution | explicit state/media; no bypass runtime |\n| reads, list, grep/glob, LSP | capability:read/list, governed rg, lsp:query | managed access/output or explicit retained exception |\n| writes, patches, notebooks | capability:edit/write, lsp:apply, required patch/notebook adapters | preserve efficient edit semantics and locks |\n| HTTP, search, browser, computer | capability:fetch/computer and approved provider/browser integrations | separate access/output contracts |\n| delegation | capability:launch-agent, fleet, coord | enrolled identity and managed lifecycle |\n| schedule, monitor, wake | scheduled plans, loop, watch, events | canonical durable scheduling |\n| tasks, plans, goals | tasks versus work_items/plans/goals | retain panels, correct canonical stores |\n| memory, checkpoint, resume, rewind | memory/facts, work-item/session recovery | explicit distinct semantics |\n| questions, approvals | owner Inbox/coord plus genuine client permission checks | native dialog may remain a frontend |\n| images, artifacts, skills, discovery, TUI | existing integrations | retain useful UX, govern side effects |\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-008 | live |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-006, P-008 | live |\n| R-4 | P-003, P-008 | live |\n| R-5 | P-004, P-008 | live |\n| R-6 | P-005, P-007, P-008 | live |\n| R-7 | P-006, P-008 | live |\n| R-8 | P-007, P-008, P-009 | deployed |\n| R-9 | P-014, P-015, P-020 | live |\n| R-10 | P-017 | live |\n| R-11 | P-018 | live |\n| R-12 | P-020 | live |\n| R-13 | P-019 | live |\n| R-14 | P-015, P-016 | deployed |\n| R-15 | P-023, P-026 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-024, P-025, P-027 | live |\n| R-17 | P-028, P-029 | live |\n| R-18 | P-031 | deployed |\n| R-19 | P-030 | tree |\n\n### Verification and rollout\n\nUse focused hermetic tests and isolated real clients/current-build services. Never stop the live owner operator merely to simulate an outage. Preserve unrelated dirty-tree changes. Cite exact tested versions and subjects. Keep an unready capability explicitly unready until its gaps are fixed in this plan; restriction itself is not proof of parity. Final deployment requires deployed-only evidence because launch/recovery controls must reach the shipped artifact; earlier implementation/acceptance uses staging.\n\n## Phase 1 — inventory and replacements\n\n- **P-001** `done` Verify current owners, inherited decisions, tool shapes and launcher paths; implement the complete test-backed capability disposition inventory, precise reuse sites and gap classification. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-10001157 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement start-once managed Bash that yields its durable job at the response deadline; preserve execution deadline, abort/kill, permitted full logs and structured terminal/running results. Test fast completion, yield, explicit timeout, cancellation, output recovery and no double execution. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-10001162 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Close inventoried PTY/script lifecycle gaps: resize, completion events/wakes, restart/reattachment truth, explicit kernel state/media and nested authorization. Reuse task-manager/orchestration and prove actual lifecycle behavior. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001163 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `dropped` Implement locally authorized bounded native recovery on existing launch surfaces, scoped capabilities, expiry/banner, offline audit/reconciliation and resume reset. Prove operator-unreachable recovery in isolation. blocked-by: P-001 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-10001164 dropped\n\n## Phase 2 — policy and interfaces\n\n- **P-005** `done` Integrate one capability policy into Claude/Codex/OMP launch/resume/wake, cover aliases/nested execution/overrides, preserve sandbox/access policy and gate each restriction on proven replacement quality. blocked-by: P-003, P-004 importance: urgent — note: ← WI-10001165 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Connect or complete required file/patch/read/network/browser/state/question/media adapters; retain native UX and correct canonical-store distinctions; preload essentials and document exclusions. No duplicate stores or false equivalence. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001166 completed (done)\n\nWhat changed: the prior note said none of this item's gaps could close until P-004 cleared. D-010 RETIRED that feature and dropped P-004, so there is no P-004 gate on anything. Verified individually rather than as a blanket unblock: P-006's only blockedBy is P-001 (done). P-005 was the sole item directly gated on P-004 and is likewise unblocked. P-007 is NOT unblocked by D-010 — its blockedBy is [P-005, P-006], neither of which is P-004.\n\nRemaining residue on this item is acceptance-shaped and jointly owned with P-007/P-008 per D-009; it closes through P-008's real-client parity matrix, not through further adapter work here. Preserve native-looking tools/panels backed by managed authority and pure presentation/discovery. Never weaken credential/sandbox policy for native inheritance or claim byte identity where redaction/decoding/interleaving changes it.\n\n### D-004 — Reuse; recovery and parity before cutover\n\nDate: 2026-09-13\n\nExtend shipped capability/orchestration and existing task/result/launch/policy stores. Distinguish truncation from loss, retention and redaction. Account native bytes separately until they actually cross managed handling.\n\n### D-006 — Represent managed PTY screen state as a standard MCP embedded resource\nDate: 2026-09-13\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/capability/pty.ts returned a custom {type:'pty'} block by casting it to TextContent; libs/generic/tooldef/src/wire.ts and the live MCP result validator accept only standard MCP content variants, and the staging capability:pty_read_screen call was rejected at content[0].type. Decision: expose ANSI screen state as a standard embedded resource (`type:'resource'`) with MIME `application/x-papercusp-pty-screen+ansi`; encode durable task id and cols/rows in its papercusp URI and preserve structured metadata in top-level `_meta.pty`. This keeps the screen a distinct non-text result-door-accounted medium while remaining interoperable with Codex/MCP clients. Custom protocol variants must not be introduced by type casts.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-007 — Offline recovery authority requires an external hardware owner signature\nDate: 2026-09-13\nDate: 2026-09-13. Measured: independent review EI-23185135982484883 reproduced recoveryAuthorizationEligibility={ok:true} from a managed agent using env -i systemd-run --user --pty, and `sudo -n -l` on this workstation reports `(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL`. Therefore environment markers, process ancestry, TTY shape, same-UID file modes, PAM/polkit, the installed superuser token, or any other machine-local software secret/prompt cannot establish human-owner provenance; they remain defense-in-depth only. Decision: a recovery grant is authoritative only when its exact normalized capability (grant id, argv, cwd, reason, issue/expiry/runtime/use and terminal binding) carries a signature from a pinned external or hardware-backed owner key whose signing operation requires FIDO user presence and user verification. Verify that SSHSIG proof before persistence and again at redemption. The interactive terminal confirmation is UX, never the authority. Preserve one-use atomic consumption, exact argv, expiry/runtime/process-group kill, loud banner, external append-only audit/reconciliation and ordinary resume reset. Add the scrubbed systemd pseudo-TTY exploit as the required negative regression. This replaces the rejected local HMAC/TTY/ancestry-as-authority design without weakening its secondary controls.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-008 — The recovery owner-key pin must be rooted outside managed-agent mutation authority\nDate: 2026-09-13\nDate: 2026-09-13\nMeasured: a software-only ordinary Ed25519 key wrapped in the OpenSSH `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com` wire format, with signer-chosen flags 0x05, was accepted by the real `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen -Y verify` as a good ED25519-SK UP+UV signature. On this workstation, managed agents also have NOPASSWD root and can replace same-machine home or system files. Independent reviewer WI-10001225 therefore rejected a local public-key file plus claimed SSHSIG flags as the P-004 authority root. Decision: D-007's pinned external/hardware owner signature is acceptable only when the trust anchor is outside managed-agent mutation authority. A locally replaceable pin, file-mode check, SK algorithm label, or UP/UV bits alone is insufficient. The implementation must either verify enrollment attestation against an external immutable trust root or bind the owner public key/fingerprint through another non-replaceable external authority; absent that root, authorization fails closed before grant persistence. Existing terminal/env/ancestry checks and local HMAC remain defense-in-depth only.\nRelated: P-004\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-009 — A capability gap is co-owned by every contributing item — do NOT strip an implementation item to reach zero gaps\nDate: 2026-09-18\nDate: 2026-09-18\n\nMeasured in libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/managed-capability-contract.ts: `owningPlanItems` consistently names EVERY plan item that must contribute to closing a gap, not only the item that finally accepts it. Evidence across the whole registry, not a sample: line 568 ['P-004','P-008']; line 331 ['P-005','P-007','P-008']; lines 122/384/422/470 ['P-005','P-007','P-008']; line 668 ['P-003','P-006','P-008']. In every one of these an IMPLEMENTATION item co-owns a gap whose falsifier is real-client acceptance.\n\nDecision: P-006 co-owning its 8 acceptance-shaped gaps is CORRECT BY CONVENTION, not a mis-attribution. Re-owning those gaps from P-006 to P-007/P-008 so that P-006 'reaches zero gaps' is goalpost-moving and is REFUSED. A gap closes when its acceptance lands, and the implementation item stays named on it until then.\n\nConsequence for P-006: it cannot and should not reach zero gaps from the tree plane alone. Its own adapter deliverable being complete is the correct terminal state for the implementation half; the residue is owned jointly and is blocked behind the needs-human P-004 hardware-key gate (D-007/D-008). Report the wall; do not manufacture registry edits to clear it.\n\nThis RETRACTS a self-imposed direction I was carrying (a 'patch-notebook precedent' of re-owning gaps), which this convention evidence falsifies. Recorded because a carry-note was actively steering the next agent toward the harmful sweep.\n\n### D-010 — Owner drops the hardware-rooted recovery feature; P-004 is retired and the chain unfreezes without it\nDate: 2026-09-18\nDate: 2026-09-18\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-18] OWNER DIRECTIVE, given interactively (turn-provenance: OWNER) in answer to a direct question about how to resolve the P-004 wall. Verbatim option chosen: \"Drop the recovery feature\". Presented alternatives were: already own a hardware key / buy one (~$30-60) / drop the feature / investigate the cost of dropping it first. The owner chose to drop.\n\nWHY THE WALL EXISTED: D-007 and D-008 established that the locally-authorized recovery path in P-004 cannot be trusted without an authority root outside this machine's mutation reach. Measured: a software-only Ed25519 key wrapped in sk-ssh-ed25519 wire format with signer-chosen flags 0x05 was accepted by the real /usr/bin/ssh-keygen -Y verify as a genuine hardware-backed ED25519-SK UP+UV signature, and managed agents on this workstation hold NOPASSWD root. Independent reviewer WI-10001225 rejected a local public-key file plus claimed SSHSIG flags as an authority root. So the only sound implementation required an EXTERNAL hardware security key enrolled by the human owner.\n\nDECISION: the owner judges the emergency-recovery capability not worth a hardware purchase. P-004 is therefore RETIRED (dropped, not deferred) rather than remaining needs-human indefinitely. The plan proceeds WITHOUT a locally-authorized native recovery path.\n\nCONSEQUENCES that implementing agents must honour:\n1. Do NOT resurrect P-004 under a weaker root. The forgeability result in D-007/D-008 is unchanged by this decision; dropping the feature is sound precisely BECAUSE no weaker substitute is acceptable. Shipping a software-rooted recovery path would be security theatre and is explicitly out of scope, not merely unbuilt.\n2. Items blocked solely on P-004 (P-005, P-006, P-008, P-009, and P-007 insofar as P-004 is one of its two blockers) unblock on this decision. Re-verify each item's remaining blockers individually; do not assume a blanket unblock.\n3. Capability gaps whose owningPlanItems name P-004 (e.g. the entry co-owned ['P-004','P-008'] in libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/managed-capability-contract.ts) need re-dispositioning: a gap whose ONLY route to closure was the dropped recovery path becomes an UNSUPPORTED/documented-exclusion, not an open gap. D-009 still governs and forbids stripping an implementation item from a gap merely to reach zero.\n4. The absence of a native recovery path must be DOCUMENTED as a deliberate exclusion in the canonical runbooks under P-009, with this decision cited, so a future reader does not read it as an oversight and rebuild it.\n\nDisclosure: recorded by su-a8686 under AUTO; the ruling itself is the owner's, not the agent's.\n\n### D-011 — Repair poisoned spec evidence by recorded retraction, never by bumping a revision to shed it\nDate: 2026-09-18\nDate: 2026-09-18. MEASURED, not inferred.\n\nRULING: on this plan, a malformed spec-evidence binding is repaired by a RECORDED RETRACTION, never by bumping a bar/spec revision to shed it.\n\nWHY THIS NEEDED RULING: bindings are append-only and the evaluator scans every row for the (spec, revision) cohort, so one bad row permanently blocks the clause. spec_revision is the only partitioning dimension, and carryUnchangedBarEvidenceBindings (acceptance-bar-amendment.ts:505-567) deliberately does NOT carry evidence for a bar whose hash moved. An agent stuck on a poisoned clause therefore has a working escape: edit the bar text, get a new revision, and the failing rows stop counting.\n\nThat escape is legitimate ONLY when the bar genuinely changed meaning - which is exactly what the carry-forward comment says it is for (\"a bar whose hash moved has genuinely different meaning and its proof must be re-run\"). Using it to launder an authoring error is gate-evasion: it produces a green verdict without ever confronting the bad evidence.\n\nBINDING ON EVERY LANE OF THIS PLAN:\n1. Do NOT amend a bar/spec whose text you do not otherwise need to change, for the purpose of clearing failing evidence.\n2. An authoring error in bound evidence is repaired by retracting it with a stated reason, once the retraction path exists.\n3. Until that path exists, a clause poisoned by an authoring error is BLOCKED on the platform fix - record it, do not route around it.\n\nCONCRETE APPLICATION: CAP-CONTRACT-P005-ONE-LIFECYCLE-POLICY@1 carries two malformed bindings (b6d7006c/testRunId 18384809 collected=false executed=false; 58e012b3 currentness=stale server-measured). Its clause text is NOT the problem and will not be amended to clear them.\n\n### D-012 — P-006 retention is a DERIVED census over a required native-surface→family mapping, not prose\nDate: 2026-09-21\nDate: 2026-09-21. MEASURED, not inferred.\n\nWHAT THIS RULES. The active P-006 clause CAP-CONTRACT-P006-UNPROVEN-RETAINED@1 reads: \"Every native capability family lacking a semantically equivalent managed adapter remains explicitly retained or unsupported instead of being disabled.\" As of this ruling that sentence was UNFALSIFIABLE in code, for one measured reason: a restriction in MANAGED_CAPABILITY_RESTRICTIONS (managed-capability-policy.ts:190) declares which native NAMES it denies but not which capability FAMILY those names belong to — the `family` field exists only on the `managed-cutover` authority variant (line 150), so all six `owner-mandate` restrictions (no-subagent-fanout, no-native-tool-search, no-owner-desktop-notify, no-native-scheduler, no-os-scheduler-shell, no-native-scheduler-skills) name no family at all. With six of seven restrictions unmapped, no query can answer \"is family X disabled?\", so \"every family\" cannot be checked. This is the code-side half of the open gap `presentation-action-authority-parity` (managed-capability-contract.ts:706, \"not yet exhaustively mapped\").\n\nTHE RULING, binding on every lane that touches the restriction table:\n\n1. `familyScope` is REQUIRED on EVERY restriction, both authority kinds. It is `{ kind:'contract-family', family }` for a family in MANAGED_CAPABILITY_FAMILY_IDS, or `{ kind:'outside-r1-taxonomy', note }` for a native surface the R-1 taxonomy genuinely does not cover (no-owner-desktop-notify is the one shipped instance — desktop notification is not one of the 13 families). Declaring it outside the taxonomy is a claim that must be stated, never a silent omission.\n\n2. `family` is REMOVED from the `managed-cutover` authority variant — it now lives only on `familyScope`. Restating it in two places is the duplication this module was created to delete. A `managed-cutover` restriction whose familyScope is NOT `contract-family` is MALFORMED: it is reported by the census and withheld by resolveCapabilityPolicy (fail-safe: it can never apply), rather than silently applying with an unknown family.\n\n3. RETENTION IS DERIVED, NEVER HAND-SET (derived-truth ladder rung 1). `capabilityRetentionCensus()` computes, for every id in MANAGED_CAPABILITY_FAMILY_IDS — the id list, not the disposition array, so a family added without a disposition is a VIOLATION rather than a silent omission — an outcome of `managed-cutover-eligible` (disposition is managed and cutoverReady), `unsupported` (disposition `unsupported-gap`), or `retained` (everything else), plus the exact set of (client, surface, audience) contexts in which that family is actually disabled, and by which restriction under which authority. Outcome is computed from the contract; it is not a second hand-maintained field.\n\n4. THE INVARIANT: a family whose outcome is `retained` or `unsupported` may be disabled ONLY under an `owner-mandate` authority. An owner mandate is a prohibition with no managed replacement to prove — the owner ruled the native capability out regardless of what we ship — so it is the one legitimate disabler of an unreplaced surface, and it must SAY so by naming its family. Any other disablement of a retained/unsupported family is a census violation. Note the census measures the resolved DECISION, not the table: a restriction that is withheld in every context disables nothing.\n\n5. SCOPE — what this ruling does NOT do. It does not close `persistent-kernel-lifecycle` (contract line 205) or `presentation-action-authority-parity` (line 706). Per D-009 both stay open, co-owned with P-008, until real-client acceptance. `script-orchestration-kernels` remains an explicit `unsupported-gap`, and the census asserts the honest consequence: nothing may disable it. Declaring a persistent language kernel implemented in order to zero a gap would be exactly the false equivalence P-006's item text forbids.\n\nCONSUMERS. P-007 (client-facing denial teaching text) and P-008 (measured-evidence readiness) read `capabilityRetentionCensus()` rather than re-deriving family membership; P-008 drives it through the existing injectable `readiness` seam, which now also accepts injected dispositions so both sides of the gate are provable without waiting for a real cutover.\n\n### D-013 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-21\nAmendment-Id: b790e2164fdd36bd6962d0e6b40dc99f816fe043d417e804de3eff83b7816d12\nRequest-Hash: 0d0cec4ab1db0d3e2d47b88c701e6c18adb8f963d6d24365f4f2f063976e3277\nActor: su-091ad703-d98f-4ccb-a20f-ea02d02e9f75\nReason: P-009 ship gate: bind the structured tests check + requiredTestLayers on all 8 seeded BARs (seeded empty; gate blocked on check_missing + proof_depth_missing).\nApproved-By: su-638ae8aa-ba1e-47a7-b96c-53216e41ae0b\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:778103\nApproved-At: 2026-09-21T12:07:53.018Z\nRubric revision: 11 → 12\nSubject plan revision: 26 → 27\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-014 — Evidence-plane resolution for the acceptance BARs, and R-5 is a bar-authorship repair because D-010 dropped the feature it demands\nDate: 2026-09-21\nDate: 2026-09-21. MEASURED, not inferred. Recorded by su-091ad703 under AUTO; the D-010 half restates the owner's ruling, the rest is the plan author's.\n\nWHY THIS NEEDED RULING. The ship gate raises TWO independent obligations per BAR and they are easy to conflate, which cost a full wake to untangle. (a) ADEQUACY (bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate) is computed PER CLAUSE and OR'd across a bar's mapped clauses, and it does NOT filter evidence by plane (the comment at packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts ~line 933 says filtering would drop the tree row; WI-10000275 fixed that). (b) EVIDENCE PLANE (bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts:281) needs at least ONE current binding whose details.evidencePlane equals the bar's declared plane, and is skipped only when the bar declares 'tree'.\n\nRULING 1 — WHAT 'live' AND 'deployed' MEAN ON THIS PLAN. 'live' is a real operational probe against a RUNNING operator, and 'deployed' is the same against the released green build on :3070. Measured this day: :3070 serves sha 91a5dba579 and its release checkout carries ONLY managed-capability-contract.ts and managed-capability-policy.ts (dated Sep 18); :3170 serves sha b0cf2c4564 and DOES carry the P-008 matrix/adoption/retention code. dev:pipeline_position on managed-capability-matrix.ts reports committedLocal true, onStaging false, inMain false, deployed false, blockedOn 'gate'. CONSEQUENCE: R-8's 'deployed' evidence is genuinely UNOBTAINABLE until the gate greens and the deploy lands — that is exactly P-009's 'verify deployed controls' clause, not a paperwork gap.\n\nRULING 2 — NEVER RELABEL TREE EVIDENCE. A vitest run is tree-plane. Writing evidencePlane 'live' or 'deployed' onto one, or amending a bar's plane DOWN to match the evidence on hand, both produce a green gate over a claim nobody tested. Both are forbidden on this plan. The live bindings recorded here (7879, 7880, 7881, 7882, 7883) cite actual observations of running systems with their shas, task ids and returned values, and each states what it does NOT claim.\n\nRULING 3 — PARK PLANE EVIDENCE ON A DIFFERENT CLAUSE FROM THE ADEQUACY PROOF. Because adequacy is per-clause, an operational binding carrying no testRunIds flips its clause off 'pass'. Measured: bindings 7877/7878 cleared evidence_plane_unmet on R-2/R-3 and simultaneously RE-RAISED proof_inadequate on them. They were retracted and re-bound verbatim to the P-002 clauses (7879/7880), after which R-2 and R-3 fell to grading_missing alone. Bind adequacy on one mapped clause and the plane observation on another.\n\nRULING 4 — R-5 IS A BAR-AUTHORSHIP REPAIR, NOT AN EVIDENCE HUNT. R-5 reads 'Independent bounded recovery. Locally authorized recovery launches work without operator/MCP...'. D-010 (owner Avi, 2026-09-18) DROPPED that feature and retired P-004, and D-010 point 1 states that shipping a software-rooted substitute would be security theatre and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE. So NO honest evidence can ever satisfy R-5 as written, and manufacturing some would assert a capability the owner deliberately declined. The repair is to re-author R-5 against as-built reality — that the absence of a locally-authorized recovery path is a deliberate, documented exclusion citing D-010, and that no weaker substitute shipped — and to set its plane to where that truth lives (tree). model and requiredTestLayers are BAR-MEANING fields, so this needs an outside-lineage approval exactly as D-013 did. Until then R-5 legitimately reads proof_missing; that is the gate working, not a defect.\n\nRULING 5 — D-010 POINT 4 IS STILL OPEN AND IS P-009'S. The absence of the native recovery path must be documented as a deliberate exclusion in the canonical runbooks, citing D-010, so a future reader does not read it as an oversight and rebuild it. Not yet done.\n\nSTATE AT THIS RULING, from the authoritative refusal of plans:set-plan-status{shipped}: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-6, R-7 = grading_missing ALONE; R-8 = evidence_plane_unmet + grading_missing; R-5 = proof_inadequate + proof_missing + evidence_plane_unmet + grading_missing; contract-level = vetting_missing + author_verdict_missing. Grading is NOT yet reachable: grader recruitment fires only on acceptance_ungraded / self_graded_only, and this refusal is acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready, which does NOT recruit. Do not recruit or wake a peer for these repairs.\n\n### D-015 — A bar amendment's invalidatedProofRefs is the WHOLE-snapshot set, not what drops — unchanged bars carry forward\nDate: 2026-09-21\nDate: 2026-09-21. MEASURED, not inferred. Recorded by su-091ad703 under AUTO.\n\nWHY THIS NEEDED RULING. A `rubrics:amend { dryRun:true }` on R-5's `model` returns `changedBars:['R-5']` but ALSO an `invalidatedProofRefs` array of 38 entries whose text plainly belongs to OTHER bars (R-1, R-7, R-8, the matrix-integration bar). Read at face value that says: amending one bar destroys the evidence of all eight, undoing the 6-of-8 grading-only state at a stroke.
