Treat it as the option doc's claim until someone reads the evaluator.\nThe ruling does NOT depend on it: the documented prohibition and the measured counting-path fact are each independently sufficient.\n\n=== THE RULING ===\n(a) The gap STAYS OPEN at that call site. It fails CLOSED (the bar stays stuck) rather than open, which is the safe direction.\n(b) DO NOT set includeRetracted:true in defaultReadEvidence, or in any gate/evaluator/counting read.\n(c) The ONLY D-011-compatible closure is a SEPARATE audit-scoped read feeding the cohort fingerprint ALONE, whose rows are provably unable to reach activeEvidence/currentEvidence/staleEvidence/proofState/supersededEvidence — shipping with a guard test that FAILS if a retracted row ever reaches the counting set. A real change with its own test burden, not a flag flip, and NOT in scope for WI-10002341.\n(d) The code comment is amended in place to carry this reasoning, so the trap is disarmed at the call site rather than only in a decision a reader may never open.\n\n=== HOW I NEARLY GOT THIS WRONG, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ===\nMy first probe was a single grep for 'includeRetracted' over the snapshot file. It hit :1607, which I took to be inside defaultReadEvidence (starting :1538), and I briefly concluded the gap was ALREADY CLOSED and the comment merely stale. Reading the function showed :1607 is in defaultReadScorecards — a different function where the flag is correct. One grep spanning two adjacent functions produced a confident wrong answer in each direction available: first 'already fixed', then nearly 'fix it this way'. The correct dispositions for those two call sites are OPPOSITE. Open the function; never trust a line number's neighbourhood.\n\n### D-032 — Avi: preserve native TUI features while assessing replacement-gap work\nDate: 2026-10-09\nOwner-typed directive 2026-10-09 in Codex session su-a4f4c443-54c6-4962-bdfb-bd9035645999: \"I dont want to disable any of the native tui features yet, but are any agents currently working on filling these remaining gaps?\"\n\nDo not enable new native TUI replacement cutover restrictions or disable native features based on the shipped-plan marker. Replacement-gap implementation and acceptance must remain separable from cutover enablement. This turn requests an ownership/status answer; it does not authorize launching agents or starting new implementation. The same constraint is recorded as workspace fact owner-native-tui-gap-work-no-disable-2026-10-09.\n\n### D-033 — Avi authorizes AUTO and self implementation of remaining parity; native cutover stays excluded\nDate: 2026-10-09\nOwner source session_turn:codex:01a120cc-9151-7bd2-a57b-4210357ea289:12: \"okay put yourself on auto mode and take on the remaining work yourself now\". Earlier owner source turn 8 retains native TUI features. AUTO is registered for su-a4f4c443-54c6-4962-bdfb-bd9035645999 and WI-10007761 drives the personal implementation loop.\n\nPhase 4 P-014..P-020 fills and verifies genuine replacement gaps under new R-9..R-14, using existing tools, policies, task/output stores and tests. Route A means this session implements; no implementation fan-out. Native TUI disabling, rollout-stage activation, and revival of dropped P-004 offline recovery remain excluded. Coordinate with su-d2ae94c8-6225-41a3-9e5d-f230f72064d3 on existing PUI compatibility evidence; do not duplicate that lane.\nRelated: P-014, P-015, P-016, P-017, P-018, P-019, P-020\n\n### D-034 — Avi (#1732): extend managed replacement to Codex and OMP, prove equal work on real plans, then turn native tools off — supersedes the cutover exclusion in D-032/D-033\nDate: 2026-10-12\nOwner-typed directive #1732, 2026-10-12 ~15:50Z, in Claude session su-8cec8a78 (turn-provenance OWNER interactive): \"lets expand our tools to replace native call functionality to both codex and omp and then lets setup some tests to make sure that agents are able to do all the same work effectively that they normally would.  For the tests lets give them real papercusp plans to work on.  If we turn off the native ttive functionality and get agents to use our tools that should solve a lot of the problems.  Fold all that into the plan.\"\n\nWhat this changes:\n1. Cutover is back in scope. D-032 (\"I dont want to disable any of the native tui features yet\") and D-033 (\"native cutover stays excluded\") are superseded on that point. R-9 and R-12 are amended so they no longer forbid cutover; they now hold native tools available only until a family's cutover is admitted under R-18.\n2. Scope widens from Claude to Codex and OMP. Measured 2026-10-12: every entry in MANAGED_CAPABILITY_RESTRICTIONS lists clients ['claude'], and managed-capability-policy.ts records codex: 'none' (no host-composable restriction surface) and omp: 'allow-list-cut'. codex-cli 0.162.1 does expose per-feature switches in config.toml (shell_tool, unified_exec, view_image, multi_agent, browser_use, computer_use, sleep_tool, code_mode_host and others, from `codex features list`). Papercusp generates each Codex session's config.toml, so a Codex off-switch is buildable. Whether each switch actually removes its tool is [inferred] until P-022's negative controls run.\n3. Cutover is gated on evidence that agents still do the same work. Per client and family, a native tool is turned off only after (a) a verified off-switch with a negative control, (b) the real-client parity matrix and (c) an effectiveness trial in which agents work on real Papercusp plans, all pass. The trial (R-17) replays completed plan items from their pre-implementation commits in isolated checkouts, graded by each item's own tests. It compares matched native vs managed-only runs, then runs a live pilot on open plan items.\n\nInterpretation, disclosed: \"native ttive functionality\" is read as native tool calls (the owner's preceding sentence: \"replace native call functionality\"). Native TUI rendering, panels and navigation remain, since managed tools render inside the client TUI. The owner can redirect.\n\nUnchanged: the D-010 offline-recovery exclusion, single-live-gate-owner coordination, and no destructive shared-tree operations. Trial agents never work in the canonical shared tree.\n\nWhy (session context, su-8cec8a78, 2026-10-12): Codex code-mode exec output is ~96% of tool-output bytes (24h: 143k Codex results, 1,067 MB, 33.6 GB re-read volume; Claude 8k results, 20 MB, 0.85 GB). Papercusp's door cap (~6 KB plus spill-to-file) bounds Claude's calls to Papercusp tools but not Codex's native exec. Evidence: WI-6554700010008932 posts 1176283, 1176300, 1176316.\n\nMeasured: libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/managed-capability-policy.ts:135-137 (omp: 'allow-list-cut', codex: 'none'); restrictions at :231, :251, :278, :297, :324, :356, :374 each declare clients: ['claude']; SHIPPED_CUTOVER_STAGING = {} at :611. `codex features list` on codex-cli 0.162.1 (2026-10-12 15:52Z) lists shell_tool, unified_exec, view_image, multi_agent, browser_use, computer_use, sleep_tool, code_mode_host and image_generation as stable and enabled.\n\n### D-035 — Avi authorizes AUTO shipment drive and headless GPT-6.1 xhigh implementation fleet\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAffects: pui-chat-first-ux-2026-09-28, pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07, bash-substitution-reachable-ceiling-2026-08-01\n[turn:self] Avi explicitly directs: \"put yourself on auto mode and carry these remaining plans to shipped status. If the work can be parrelized launch a fleet of headless chatgpt 6.1 xhigh agents to help you\". This supersedes prior self-only implementation-route restrictions (including D-033 and the earlier builder interpretation in the October 12 summary) for the remaining native-tool/PUI shipment scope. Lead via existing WI-10003472; parallelize only independent work under claims, DAG ordering and locks. Use Codex agent backend, installed gpt-6.1-sol model, xhigh effort, headless terminals, default system account and warm carry unless Avi redirects. Acceptance gates, matched native/managed trial models, version-pinned removal proof, native TUI rendering, and staged rollback remain requirements. This authorizes implementation resources and an end-to-end ship drive; it does not authorize force deployment through red tests.\nRelated: P-020, P-023, P-024, P-025, P-026, P-027, P-028, P-029, P-030, P-031\n\n## Exclusions and unresolved questions\n\nNo replacement of all TUI presentation, parallel scheduler/store/permission system, permanent recovery agent, uncontrolled native escape, implementation fleet, or destructive shared-tree operations. Resolve version-specific controls, remaining adapters and PTY/script gaps from actual source/tests. Do not silently reduce requirements. Residuals: verifyRepairHead selects cumulative admissions every round; failing short-circuit gate batches re-emit passed and unmeasured ids.\n\n## Compatibility and ownership\nThe complete docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md was read. Retain corrected architecture, not historical operational recipes.\n\n| Authority | Boundary |\n| --- | --- |\n| frozen-candidate-stays-frozen-through-all-fixes-2026-09-03 D-004/D-010/D-011/D-014 | exact repairHead, admitted fixes only, no tip recut/age escape, head-bound CAS |\n| green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08 R-1/R-3/R-7 D-003..D-006 | reuse event rejudge, typed routing, artifact healing, fail-closed precheck and latency; do not duplicate acceptance |\n| gate-verdict-liveness-and-repair-reliability-2026-08-31 P-011/D-009 | existing guarded selection base and final canonical aggregate |\n| stable-candidate-related-gate-2026-08-23; gate-latency-selection-and-retry-policy-2026-09-06 | fail-wide related selection, execution/coexecution safeguards |\n| EI-23170536217137589 / su-c1a8406e-57a4-4859-859a-fef5b254828a | peer owns affected-tests and passing-task-cache implementation/types/tests; no overlapping edits; require legitimate semantic invalidation |\n| WI-762558/WI-332753 / su-c7b7f864-27ce-4053-b90e-ea9eb638e21d | peer replied to coord-send-8cae50a6c220b8dc59e85fe0c39d907120d327177d34bf0ca06b76e76ae7db35: evidence-only, no source overlap; preserve single exact-lineage aggregate |\n| LIVE_GATE_OPS | existing owner retains gate/queue/deploy/run; this lane is source development only, no parallel monitor |\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Measured frontier.** Per-task measurement removes genuine passes from failure frontier, never unknown/crashed/unexecuted entries.\n**R-2 — Incremental covered radius.** Subsequent repair selects remaining failures plus related radius of new admissions only after a candidate/head-bound complete coverage receipt and continuous ledger prove prior coverage. Missing, malformed, capped, legacy or incomplete proof falls back to cumulative radius.\n**R-3 — Semantic validity.** Semantic inputs (membership/setup/assertions/result interpretation) still invalidate; scheduler/transport noise does not. Reuse existing peer-owned cache, no second cache.\n**R-4 — Exact lineage.** All runners execute exact repairHead; superseded evidence never certifies newer head. Selective success is not final aggregate/promotion proof.\n**R-5 — Honest explanation.** Explain delta/cumulative reason. Newly affected regressions may increase failures; no cosmetic monotonic counters.\n**R-6 — Verified personal implementation.** Implement personally, locked canonical staging, preserve peers, executable recurrence guards and real verification; distinguish source-complete from operational green.\n\n## Design\nExtend targeted result types with optional exact per-entry outcomes and run the whole bounded batch. Validate ids/coverage/status before shrinking; legacy aggregate-only results stay conservative. Failed coexecution remains failed even if individual diagnostic retries pass.\nExtend existing queue with one optional versioned selective-coverage receipt, minted after complete selective measurement, bound to candidate and measured head and persisted through head-checked CAS. Superseded verdict cannot overwrite newer coverage. Prove continuous admission chain from receipt head to current repairHead, derive new paths and pass them to existing affectedTestsAtRef at exact current head. Gaps/unknown/capped history use cumulative admittedPathsOf. Outstanding signature always runs. No new table/cache/service/loop. Final canonical gate unchanged.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-004 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Implementation\n- **P-001** `done` Reconcile source conversation and plan/peer boundaries; missing/malformed/gapped/capped receipts fail wider.\nA-3: Throw, missing/duplicate/foreign outcome, NOT CHECKED or failed-group/individual-pass cannot mint false coverage or erase unresolved obligations.\nA-4: Concurrent admission preserves newer head/phase/ledger; no tip reads; existing selective-success-to-full-gate test passes.\nA-5: Focused current-build verification and precise source identity; final operational green remains separate; no proxy claim of peer cache completion.\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Complement, do not supersede\nAuthority session_turn:codex:01a096c5-6f98-7623-a4c2-74baae3a2aa0:73, :80, :82. Related regressions may grow work. No skip/quarantine/force-green or weaker final gate.\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-14\nAmendment-Id: convergence-final-methods-v3-approved\nRequest-Hash: 9ffc85606b130f9e193582b268a4d3eb5a0de7162ed2ba3b132a8ed8b77e4a99\nActor: su-d2b8e9e5-f655-4e4c-ab16-bbe63bf5c65a\nReason: Apply the exact independently approved method amendment; keep original outcomes and final green gate intact.\nApproved-By: su-c7b7f864-27ce-4053-b90e-ea9eb638e21d\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:204202\nApproved-At: 2026-09-14T00:12:34.522Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 6 → 7\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-14\nAmendment-Id: convergence-r3-real-detector-v1\nRequest-Hash: 2ea4f7da98579d9d93c463c7091c3381deafdc4ae42f32e1f0a8b9d5ed51b18a\nActor: su-d2b8e9e5-f655-4e4c-ab16-bbe63bf5c65a\nReason: Bind actual cache semantic-invalidation detector per independent vetting finding; preserve original R3 outcome and layers.\nApproved-By: su-c7b7f864-27ce-4053-b90e-ea9eb638e21d\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:204249\nApproved-At: 2026-09-14T01:32:56.399Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 7 → 8\nChanged BARs: R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-005 — Correct precursor routing through append-only activation mapping supersession\nDate: 2026-09-14\nIndependent reviewer approved coord-send-b3a409ad89fb50e54317f6f907fe2fc65ec7e4148f9f7f8dd1eea00f9305d1a6 after re-reading source session_turn:codex:01a096c5-6f98-7623-a4c2-74baae3a2aa0:80 and :82. Exact revision-6 AUTO-BAR-R-6-P-001/P-004 records are internally inconsistent: lifecycleStatus=exempt, requiredEvidence=[manual], requiredTestLayers=[], mutationRequired=false, and their justification says the clause is not product runtime behavior, but behaviorClass=happy-path. The current code contract makes this classification load-bearing: validExplicitExemption requires exempt + non-automated + non-empty justification/provenance; automatedProofRequired and requiredProofFloor use non-automated to waive invented automated depth.\n\nApproved correction: author may create revision 7 for only these two clauses, changing behaviorClass to non-automated. Source read confirmed packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-quality.ts validExplicitExemption and packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts automatedProofRequired use behaviorClass=non-automated as the relevant switch.\n\nRelated: P-001, P-004\nRelated: P-001, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"retrieval-soft-budget-hard-deadline-2026-09-13","title":"Retrieval: warn after 1.2 seconds, retain results until a 10-second deadline, reduce latency, then reassess GitNexus","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Retrieval: warn after 1.2 seconds, retain results until a 10-second deadline, reduce latency, then reassess GitNexus\nslug: retrieval-soft-budget-hard-deadline-2026-09-13\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-13\nupdated: 2026-09-13\n---\n\n## Now\n\nState: APPROVED by Avi on2026-09-13, current source conversation turn51. AUTO enabled by owner direction, self execution required, tracked warm work loop armed. Source-conversation activation audit is in progress; implementation follows activation. Authoring item WI-10001229 is complete. Preserve the self route; do not spawn agents.\n\nNext: approve, audit the full source conversation, activate through plans:start, execute the ordered items, verify, and deliver the revised recommendation. Drafting changed no product code or runtime setting.\n\n## Owner request and order\n\nAvi requested: (1) write and implement the agreed slow-warning versus hard-timeout policy from start to finish; (2) investigate why retrieval exceeds1.2s and ideally eliminate those overruns; (3) only after(1) and(2) complete, return to GitNexus and recommend based on the new findings and previous decisions. Licensing is excluded at Avi's request. This is not authorization to install alternatives or replace the code-intelligence stack.\n\n## Outcome\n\nUseful retrieval completing within a reasonable time reaches agents, while1200ms remains a performance target. A10000ms end-to-end ceiling prevents indefinite waiting. Slow successes trigger investigation rather than automatic result loss. The larger hard deadline is not a performance fix: identify and correct measured latency causes, then deliver the GitNexus recommendation.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Slow successes remain usable.** [P-001/P-002/P-003/P-004/P-005]: Retain1200ms as the query-embedding soft performance target. A response after it but before the shared hard deadline is accepted and observed as slow-success, not discarded. Distinguish slowness, genuine errors, user cancellation and hard timeout.\n\n**R-2 — One end-to-end hard deadline.** [P-001/P-002/P-003]: Scope10000ms as ONE end-to-end hard deadline for automatic retrieval. Inventory embedding, search, rerank, corpus, parent injection and client bounds; the current2000ms outer race must not pre-empt the policy. Propagate remaining time; never renew ten seconds per stage. Other shared-library callers retain behavior unless explicitly migrated and tested.\n\n**R-3 — Safe partial results survive.** [P-002/P-003]: At deadline preserve completed safe results, explicitly label incomplete/timed-out/unavailable legs, and apply normal relevance, scope, provenance, dedup and output-budget filters. Never treat timeout as proof of no relevant memory or complete coverage. A genuine unrecoverable error can fail immediately.\n\n**R-4 — Cancellation preserves consumer ownership.** [P-002/P-003]: Propagate hard-deadline and caller cancellation through transport-backed embeddings, search and governed queued work. No orphan work or late delivery. Shared coalesced work still needed by another caller must not be cancelled by a single consumer.\n\n**R-5 — Performance warnings remain actionable.** [P-002/P-004/P-005]: Extend existing per-caller latency accounting/watchdogs, not a parallel telemetry service. Keep softTargetMs separate from hardDeadlineMs; slow-success continues to alarm appropriately. Record sufficient stage, queue/cache and endpoint context for causal diagnosis without duplicate-warning floods.\n\n**R-6 — Deadline and cancellation regressions are tested.** [P-003/P-006]: Framework tests with deterministic clocks must retain valid semantic results at1500/3000/9000ms; bound a hung leg near10000ms; retain completed lexical results when semantic work hangs; prevent additive nested deadlines; verify error/cancel/partial rendering and consumer-safe coalescing. Cover turn-start, mid-turn and actual facade call paths. Do not use long sleeps or flaky wall-clock unit assertions.\n\n**R-7 — Latency causes are distinguished.** [P-004]: Attribute queue wait, durable admission, embedder acquisition, model execution, SQL/highlighting, rerank and parent overhead separately. Use identical-input interleaved controls, representative body lengths/concurrency, uncached and cached runs, PID/build/endpoint stamps and sufficient samples. Process-local rings are not fleet statistics. A warm process or fast cache hit does not prove novel-query performance.\n\n**R-8 — Measured latency causes are corrected.** [P-004/P-005/P-006]: Implement narrowly justified performance corrections after a distinguishing experiment identifies cause. Verify before/after latency and1200ms breach rate, with uncached demand and background indexing fairness. Preserve vector-space compatibility and retrieval correctness. The aspiration is to stay under1200ms, not an unearned universal guarantee. If residual misses remain, record their rate/circumstances/cause and accountable follow-up. Raising timeouts, disabling semantic retrieval or relying on a cache is not a demonstrated root-cause fix. GPU/provider install, model changes, new services or invasive host changes require an explicit design/authority checkpoint.\n\n**R-9 — Index freshness has a separate disposition.** [P-004/P-005/P-007]: Keep the growing session embedding backlog as a separate freshness investigation; use eligible/current-vector writer semantics and measured indexing versus arrival rate. The specific original decision turns have gemma parent vectors, so global68% coverage alone does not establish why they were not selected. Do not perform a broad historical rebuild or change embedding models under this draft; record actionable residue rather than drop it.\n\n**R-10 — GitNexus reassessment follows verified retrieval work.** [P-007]: Only after timeout-policy and latency work passes acceptance, reassess GitNexus. Start from prior owner-approved decisions and actual agent-log evidence. Distinguish code graph navigation from compiler truth, operational history and runtime tests. Separate delivered-pointer utilization failure from retrieval defects. Do not impose tool-call quotas, weaken green-checkpoint baseline tests, or install a competing graph without a separately approved decision.\n\n## Existing evidence\n\nSnapshots from2026-09-13, not current-state promises: injected warnings reported query embed exceeded1200ms. corpus-recall-io contains a2000ms enclosing race. One worker(pid773035 of a16-worker cluster) reported250 midturn embeds with57 timeouts and p50=3ms. Three uncached gemma-query probes returned1948/235/810ms; the first observed saturation, but different inputs do not causally separate queue time from inference. Configured production units pointed to3384; that sidecar was warm, workers alive, execution CPU. CPU-only metadata is not proof of the bottleneck.\n\nCoverage samples20:52:45→22:22:26UTC: session_turn eligible+3592 versus current embeddings+512. Recent periodic sweeps embedded64 turns and64 chunks while exhausting200s budget. Existing alarms reported backlog-growth/recent-coverage breaches; two scheduled coverage samples were shed. Initial detection is working; durable response and throughput still need checking.\n\nAutomatic excerpt retrieval explicitly selects session_turn and work_item, not plan decisions. A relevant historical GitNexus pointer was nevertheless injected, and the agent did not follow it before recommending alternatives. Preserve both facts.\n\n## Design\n\nSeparate the soft performance target from a single absolute retrieval deadline. Share remaining-time and cancellation state through the existing search/injection seams; preserve already-completed safe candidates rather than restarting work at timeout. Extend existing telemetry to retain the1200ms target. Attribute latency before optimizing. Requirement-to-item mentions above describe contributing work; the table below assigns final outcome evidence to the item that can actually prove it, so preparatory tasks are not blocked on downstream implementation.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Work items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-003, P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-004 | live |\n| R-8 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-004 | live |\n| R-10 | P-007 | live |\n\n## Reuse and likely source scope\n\nReuse libs/generic/search/src/hybrid.ts and embed-latency.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/memory/corpus-recall-io.ts, injection.ts, recall-stats.ts, corpus-coverage-gate.ts; agent-mcp/turn-start-memory.ts and mid-turn-context.ts; existing embed-sidecar/resource-governor/backfill/watchdog surfaces and framework tests. No parallel memory system, graph engine, queue, metrics store or bespoke new tool family. The exact edit set follows the P-001 caller audit and file locks.\n\n## Historical authority and source trail\n\n- code-intelligence-routing-lsp-gitnexus-2026-08-20#D-001: GitNexus for call chains/impact/topology; official LSP for compiler-resolved symbol truth; rg for exact working-tree text.\n- Same plan#D-002: Avi dropped Serena. Official pinned language servers behind a thin Papercusp adapter won on reuse, read-only boundaries, Node/Rust operations, code:run parity and one shared fleet instance. Remains governing unless new evidence supports proposing revision.\n- Original comparison: codex:01a01fbc-6171-7d02-b205-8a3faeb65a8f turns3-6 on2026-08-20. Its Codebase-Memory and CodeGraphContext are distinct from colbymchenry/codegraph.\n- Explicit owner choice: claude:5ba8194a-9964-42d5-ade2-7699a0120deb turns28-34; turn34 says fold insights into plan and drop Serena. Plan decision dated2026-08-21UTC; conversation was August20 evening in NewYork.\n- docs/evidence/gitnexus-agent-log-audit-2026-09-12.md and WI-10001115: scheduler navigation, verification chain and design consumer, with index miss/crash/staleness controls and no measured whole-task savings.\n- EI-20018643059506852/EI-21742473853140433: closed prior timeout investigations retained a residual tail or accepted a healthy snapshot. Re-read completion before assuming cause fixed.\n- EI-23084905907473824: sessions:read invalid-escape failure. Bounded exact session_turns reads via code:run/dev:pg_query recovered source; never invent omitted transcript text.\n- Present conversation: owner asked to find prior technology decisions; diagnose failed context utilization and degraded retrieval; prefer warnings for reasonable latency and hard cutoff around10s; then explicitly ordered implementation, latency diagnosis and deferred GitNexus recommendation. Before activation resolve this native session, read full relevant turns, map requirements/corrections/rejections to R1-R10, and record plans:audit phase activation.\n\n## Scope, safety and delivery\n\nCanonical staging only, assigned work-items and manual locks before every edit. Preserve unrelated dirty changes; background git-sync owns commits/push. Use focused tests and staging/current-build acceptance during implementation. Final promotion/deployed claims require actual evidence. Read live gate ownership before any gate action; do not duplicate a held live-gate lane or force past red. Do not babysit asynchronous shipment without an actionable owned next step.\n\nNo global timeout expansion, new retrieval corpus, direct graph rollout, licensing work, manual commits, release-tree edits, suppressed quality/scope filters, or unbounded re-embedding. Avi approved AUTO self execution in source turn51. Source-conversation activation audit and normal claims/locks remain mandatory before implementation.\n\n## Required final evidence\n\nDeliver changed policy and current-build/deployed states separately; deterministic tests and live partial/cancellation delivery proof; before/after performance with cache/concurrency/sample qualifiers; named latency cause and explicit residual; independent backlog disposition; and a revised GitNexus recommendation that explains which prior premises changed. Passing mocks or a successful cached query alone are insufficient.\n\n## Phase 1 — Deadline policy and verification\n- **P-001** `todo` Audit the complete source conversation before activation; map R1-R10 and governing decisions. Trace inner/outer deadlines and every turn-start/mid-turn caller; baseline current behavior and safe partial-result/cancellation seams. Record design and per-caller migration boundary. Acceptance: activation audit recorded, exact deadline chain and test population enumerated, existing caller behavior protected. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Implement1200ms slow-warning semantics and one10000ms end-to-end retrieval deadline through existing shared seams. Preserve completed results at hard deadline and truthful partial provenance; propagate cancellation safely; retain strict soft-target telemetry/watchdogs. Acceptance: slow successes are deliverable, no inner2s cutoff pre-empts, no multiplied phase budgets or orphan queued work. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Add deterministic framework coverage for1500/3000/9000ms semantic success,10000ms hung work, partial lexical preservation, nested-budget propagation, caller cancellation, coalesced consumers, genuine errors, warning telemetry and actual injection/facade paths. Run focused suites and current-build delivery controls; repair failures before completing policy work. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Latency cause and remediation\n- **P-004** `todo` Investigate why1200ms is exceeded: controlled cached/uncached same-input probes with stage timing, queue/admission/inference/SQL/rerank attribution, fresh and warm workers, representative lengths and concurrency. Full plan closure follows the final recommendation item, not this technical acceptance item. Acceptance: no unverified green/deployed claim; remaining latency/freshness scope explicitly dispositioned. blocked-by: P-003, P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` After policy and latency acceptance, return to GitNexus. Test final selection is a superset of baseline for positive, stale, invalid, graph-unavail… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001409 — Complete requirement coverage and per-item code-truth audit; run focused/unit/integration/behavioral acceptance, independently grade the current acceptance rubric, record implementer verdict, verify … <!-- P-009 -->\n## Background\nThe completed empirical audit WI-10001115 and revised assessment WI-10001260 are docs/evidence/gitnexus-agent-log-audit-2026-09-12.md and docs/evidence/gitnexus-revised-assessment-2026-09-13.md. Read actual source turns before activation; no recalled paraphrase substitutes.\n\n## Scope and non-goals\nImplement the existing facade/guidance, failure/coverage semantics, selective adoption, consumer evidence and additive test-selection integration; execute an isolated bounded comparison. Extend existing code-intelligence, behavior/eval, BAR/rubric/evidence and affected-tests mechanisms, not a parallel graph service or validator.\nDo not unconditionally replace GitNexus, introduce Serena, install duplicate coordination/hooks, weaken baseline tests, make unrelated promotions depend on a live graph, or use raw gitnexus.query as a recommendation. Do not change account routing or cold carry on predicted scarcity. Backend changes are conditional on measured correctness/reliability/total-work benefit. Licensing is excluded per Avi's request. Preserve the unfinished retrieval-soft-budget-hard-deadline-2026-09-13 plan/WI-10001232 independently; its implementation and post-fix acceptance are not secretly closed by this plan. This newly directed plan takes execution priority.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Preserve question-specific authority.** GitNexus/graph:query supplies topology; official LSP supplies compiler semantics; rg supplies current text; ast-grep syntax; packers post-retrieval. Existing guidance overrides and code:run access are reused. Serena remains excluded.\n**R-2 — Actionable, truthful guidance.** Correct context/impact guidance directing agents into refused raw query paths or promising every consumer/exact current source. Use known-symbol and shared-helper-change triggers, show appropriate fallback, and test generated runtime artifact parity.\n**R-3 — Truthful failure and coverage.** Separate graph edges, file-level links, limited output, stale revisions, missing/unindexed symbols and backend failures. Empty/non-truncated/fresh results must not claim source completeness without independent proof. LSP degraded results must not silently become exhaustive references. Diagnose named failures against current code and exact indexed revisions before choosing repairs.\n**R-4 — Reliable existing backend.** Reproduce and root-cause the known-symbol omission plus graph refresh/restart/crash classes relevant to selective adoption; ship guards and verified fixes or choose a measured passing upgrade. Preserve existing full-rebuild policy until a candidate passes its failure fixture. No restart-only closure.\n**R-5 — Selective agent adoption.** Integrate bounded graph evidence at known-symbol navigation and shared-code impact decisions through existing routing/eval surfaces. Avoid per-grep/per-read/per-turn graph tax. Test both appropriate uses and legitimate text/log/runtime nonuses through the actual supported agent tooling.\n**R-6 — Consumer evidence in existing BAR/rubric.** Attach index/source revision, resolved consumers, source corroboration, checked/unchecked behavior, evidence/tests and fallback to the existing acceptance method. Neither a graph invocation nor zero callers satisfies the outcome. Mandatory failure/unknown stays nonpassing.\n**R-7 — Additive affected tests.** Extend current affected-test selection with corroborated, snapshot-bound graph dependency suggestions. Baseline selection remains a subset of final selection; invalid/stale/unavailable graph evidence cannot remove tests or silently pass mandatory evidence. No live graph dependency for unrelated green runs.\n**R-8 — Bounded comparative evidence.** Compare baseline LSP/rg, installed GitNexus, one pinned candidate GitNexus upgrade and Codebase-Memory on frozen scheduler/fingerprint/consumer/route plus ambiguity/re-export/edit/delete/refresh-failure fixtures. Preserve same-task/source/model/account comparability and cold/warm/cache distinctions. Measure correct task conclusions, missed consumers, context/tokens, wall time, indexing/update/recovery and resource cost. Follow @papercusp/bench-metrics fairness/attribution, not unverified README savings. CodeGraph only if a named gap warrants it; CodeGraphContext/SCIP are not additional default installs.\n**R-9 — Evidence-based backend disposition.** Explicit keep/upgrade/replace decision under the same correctness/reliability bar. No claimed alternative win when unsupported; no second permanent stack. Changes to backend/index policy require regression guards, safe rollback and non-destructive isolated validation.\n**R-10 — End-to-end delivery.** Focused tests, current-build user/tool journey, complete requirement coverage, per-item code-truth audit, independent acceptance grading and implementer verdict, then final deployed/packaged evidence as applicable. Distinguish working-tree result, committed result and shipped result. No manual git commit/push; respect sole live-gate owner; no force-deploy past red without Avi's explicit approval.\n\n## Design\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| Bar | Work items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-005 | live |\n| R-9 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-009 | deployed |\n\n### Reuse and likely source surfaces\nExisting bridge libs/papercusp/plugins/gitnexus-bridge/index.ts + generated index.cjs/tests; packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/{contracts,gitnexus-facade,lsp-facade,lsp-adapter,code-intel-bench,acceptance-corpus}; existing agent-tools graph/lsp handlers; existing hook/routing/eval registry; existing plans spec/consumer evidence; scripts/affected-tests.mjs and existing selection tests; existing isolated vendoring and testing mechanisms. Resolve exact paths from code before edits; do not make optional candidates unconditional dependencies.\n### Verification principles\nOutcomes are fixed here; implementer supplies discriminating METHOD/evidence after implementation. Include positive controls, negative/error cases, scope and revision stamps. Complete a comparison even when the correct conclusion is keep/no demonstrated challenger benefit, but do not call an unavailable required arm tested. Any unresolvable required comparison must remain explicit nonpassing residue rather than self-waived success.\n\n## Dependencies and sequence\nPreparation and corrected runtime guidance first; baseline/failure fixtures before backend repairs or comparisons. Reliability repairs and measured backend disposition precede reliance-sensitive rollout. Consumer evidence before additive test selection. Final acceptance after the complete ordered implementation. Single executor, file locks for every edit; independent reviewers may grade but never implement a hidden fleet.\n\n## Risks and rollback\nShared index mutations or installing a package in shared node_modules can disrupt peers. Use existing isolated vendor/benchmark paths and managed resource admission; never mutate the serving index for a drill. Read/backup before destructive data changes. Preserve prior backend pin and index policy until replacement is verified. Existing graph errors may stem from index/parser/resolver rather than staleness; controlled source/index controls distinguish them. Until then no fleet/member/drain claim; do NOT re-launch the plan fleet from the goal-placement prompt.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001: Execute in this session\nAvi selected route A. This Codex session implements and verifies the work directly; no fleet or sub-agent route is used.\n\n### D-002: Fix the work, then hide the remaining latency\nServer work is first because prefetch alone would merely move a multi-second defect off the click path. Prefetch is still required because an actually instant interaction needs the exact query result in the shared React Query cache before the rail mounts.\n\n### D-003: Preserve event-driven freshness\nThe existing producer-side, owner-scoped agentOrders invalidations remain authoritative. The change may reuse the client query cache but must not introduce an unbounded or long-TTL stale snapshot.\n\n### D-004 — Goal fleet placement of P-003 stood down; plan stays protected-solo (D-001/D-027)\nDate: 2026-10-02\n2026-10-02 14:14Z, goal steward su-9ec5d030 (goal work-on-everything-fresh-grading-and-improvement-60d3a8).
