The placement prompt re-firing on an owner-walled item is a classifier defect, filed separately; it is not a reason to re-launch.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"latest-agent-frameworks-tools-research-2026-09-14","title":"Latest agent frameworks and tools — borrow/adapt landscape","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-14","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Latest agent frameworks and tools — borrow/adapt landscape\nslug: latest-agent-frameworks-tools-research-2026-09-14\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-14\nupdated: 2026-09-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Approved research. Establish the workspace's prior-review baseline, scan current releases and source, then publish a cited report and decision matrix.\n\n**Next action:** Inventory prior Papercusp framework/tool evaluations and normalize the candidate universe before external release research.\n\n## Background\n\nThe owner requested thorough online research into the latest agent frameworks and related tools, specifically asking whether anything released in the last few months contains ideas or code Papercusp has not yet examined. The approved route is this Codex session, open-source-first, producing a detailed report plus decision matrix.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Current release window.** Cover releases or materially new capabilities announced from 2026-06-01 through 2026-09-14, while allowing older projects with a newly relevant release.\n\n**R-2 — Complete adjacent-tool scope.** Cover agent runtimes/orchestration, coding-agent infrastructure, memory/context, interoperability and tool protocols, evaluation/observability, browser/computer use, and sandbox/execution systems.\n\n**R-3 — Evidence-backed novelty.** Establish “not looked at yet” from current workspace plans, reports, work-items, code dependencies, and relevant session records; do not infer novelty merely from one grep.\n\n**R-4 — Primary-source grounding.** Prefer official release notes, documentation, repositories, commits/tags, and papers; use secondary sources for discovery and triangulation.\n\n**R-5 — Code and license inspection.** Inspect source architecture, representative implementation files, release history, and license for the strongest candidates, not only marketing pages.\n\n**R-6 — Reuse classification.** Separate borrowable code, transferable design ideas, hosted-product-only ideas, and watchlist items.\n\n**R-7 — Actionable recommendations.** For each recommended candidate, name the precise mechanism, why it fits Papercusp, likely integration seam, license/provenance constraints, expected benefit, cost/risk, and a falsifiable next probe.\n\n**R-8 — Durable artifact.** Deliver a self-contained cited report plus a compact ranked decision matrix in the canonical repository.\n\n**R-9 — Evidence boundaries.** State the research cutoff, uncertainty, conflicts, inaccessible sources, and other material limitations explicitly.\n\n## Design\n\nThe survey uses four evidence passes:\n\n1. Workspace baseline: plans, reports, dependencies, benchmarks, issues/work-items, and session history.\n2. Discovery census: official project/release channels and reputable ecosystem roundups to avoid incumbent-only bias.\n3. Candidate deep dives: primary documentation, release history, source architecture, representative implementation files, license, and project vitality.\n4. Comparative synthesis: novelty versus Papercusp, reuse fit, duplication risk, implementation seam, and recommendation confidence.\n\nCandidates are classified as **borrow now**, **prototype**, **watch**, **already covered/no new action**, or **reject**, with sourced facts kept distinct from analytical judgments.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-004 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline and census\n- **P-001** `done` Build the complete workspace prior-review baseline and candidate census: enumerate frameworks/tools already assessed, implemented, benchmarked, or explicitly rejected; define novelty criteria and a June–September 2026 release inventory. importance: high — note: ← WI-10001418 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Primary-source deep dives\n- **P-002** `done` Research the strongest novel candidates from official docs, release notes, repositories, commits/tags, papers, and licenses; inspect representative source architecture and record precise transferable mechanisms. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001429 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Comparative recommendations\n- **P-003** `done` Compare candidates against current Papercusp mechanisms and rank borrow now, prototype, watch, already covered/no action, or reject; include integration seams, benefits, risks, licenses, and falsifiable probes. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001430 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Artifact and quality audit\n- **P-004** `done` Author the self-contained cited report and decision matrix, verify every material citation and release date, audit completeness against the owner request, and close with explicit limitations and next actions. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001431 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n- D-001 — Scope is open-source-first. Proprietary tools may appear when they expose a distinctive transferable mechanism, but code-borrow recommendations require inspectable source and a compatible license.\n- D-002 — The main artifact is a detailed report with an embedded ranked decision matrix.\n- D-003 — Execution route is this Codex session; no fleet or sub-agent fan-out.\n\n### D-001 — Open-source-first scope\nDate: 2026-09-14\nPrioritize inspectable open-source agent frameworks and adjacent tools. Include proprietary products only when they expose a distinctive transferable mechanism; code-borrow recommendations require inspectable source and a compatible license.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Detailed report plus decision matrix\nDate: 2026-09-14\nPublish one self-contained, heavily cited research report with an embedded compact matrix that ranks each candidate and makes next actions explicit.\nRelated: P-003, P-004\n\n### D-003 — Self execution route\nDate: 2026-09-14\nThe current Codex session executes the research directly. No fleet or client-native sub-agent fan-out is used.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"managed-carry-lifecycle-enforcement-2026-09-13","title":"Managed carry lifecycle — enforce correct handoff and resumed work","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Managed carry lifecycle — enforce correct handoff and resumed work\nslug: managed-carry-lifecycle-enforcement-2026-09-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-14\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-006 remains unfinished and needs a route decision; WI-10001395 has the current checkpoint. Oct22 self-session continuation verified existing implementation, fixed test-fixture isolation/readiness/current-contract errors, and refreshed focused evidence. Rubric rev3 remains unvetted; old rev2 card failed independent audit. All seven current BAR hashes match authenticated prior amendment approval204649, but this is not current vetting or acceptance. No new agents, independent grades, deployed drill, force deploy or live-gate intervention were launched. Exact route conflict: non-audit scorecard emission auto-launches independent auditors, while R7 requires a disposable managed Codex session; kickoff forbids additional agents.\n\n**Next:** Finish the current host-fixture verification and report it; Avi/coordinator resolves the no-new-agents constraint before independent vetting/acceptance and the deployed disposable-session drill can proceed.\n\n## Background\nAudit artifacts: docs/audits/backend-reliability-2026-09-13.md and backend-reliability-2026-09-13-evidence.json. Relevant F02/F03/F04/F06/F09/F15 concern busy boundaries, false completion, failed recovery, host skew, provenance and delivery. Agent su-b81649b7-e17e-43a4-afcb-b7ded6027164 has a recorded SIGHUP at September 14 00:27:53 UTC and repeated carry nonce da5fbf51d387663b across native sessions. Stale-rearm and late-shutdown attribution remain hypotheses. Current agent su-6eeda0f9-9087-43b2-b27d-e3856a7cf256 promised continuation at 01:01:47 UTC; its next owner prompt found no armed loop. A missing recurring loop alone does not explain a failed one-shot carry. Read exact request, receipt, native-event and first-turn evidence. Owner quotation of another agent's addressed carry is not itself proof of misdelivery.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Evidence before repair.** Each diagnosed failure has a source-grounded causal account, a distinguishing reproduction and explicit remaining historical uncertainty.\n\n**R-2 — Managed continuity enforcement.** A managed carry request validates recipient-owned durable checkpoint and continuation authority before ending the predecessor, with an explicit pending or refusal result if prerequisites cannot be established.\n\n**R-3 — Idempotent lifecycle.** Duplicate or superseded requests and delayed callbacks cannot repeat a settled carry or retire its live successor.\n\n**R-4 — Truthful continuation.** Queued, submitted and native-turn-started outcomes remain distinct while a failed or deferred operation remains actionable.\n\n**R-5 — Protected boundaries.** Carry preserves active work, human-staged input, owner-selected route and permission boundaries while missing prerequisites leave the predecessor intact.\n\n**R-6 — Regression selection.** Behavioral regressions distinguish defect from repair and are selected by the normal promotion suite.\n\n**R-7 — Verified shipment.** The plan reaches shipped only after code-truth audit and independent acceptance grading with exact-runtime carry-and-resume evidence and honest older-host adoption status.\n\n## Design\nExtend existing request-compaction, checkpoint/flush gates, loop continuation, carry marker/outcome, PTY rearm/dedup and native-session evidence; no parallel scheduler or prose-only compliance scheme. Inspect actual client interception before changing it. Bind owner/request identity and predecessor generation to settlement; invalidate stale retries and fence child callbacks. Autonomous work must retain a durable wake, but one-shot carry owns its first prompt independently of a recurring loop. Use isolated non-human PTY fixtures, never peer terminals. No broad restart, forced red deploy, timeout inflation or safety-guard disablement. Staging is implementation acceptance; deployed identity matters for final shipment.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-006 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Diagnosis\n- **P-001** `done` Recover source conversation and exact request/receipt/native timeline for both owners; inspect existing incidents; distinguish stale rearm, native bypass, parent teardown and missing wake; record cause and uncertainty before repairs. importance: high — note: ← WI-10001264 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Enforcement\n- **P-002** `done` Enforce managed carry checkpoint/authority and continuation prerequisites at existing request/flush/client seams; preserve route and explicit pending/refused outcomes; add behavioral regressions. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001278 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Repair proven retry/supersession and child-lifecycle races with identity-scoped settlement and callback fencing; test duplicate, delayed, failed and superseded requests. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001279 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Complete truthful delivery and failed-carry recovery through existing outcomes/ledgers, including first-turn proof and stable actionable non-convergence. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001290 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Verify and ship\n- **P-005** `done` Run focused unit/integration and disposable PTY carry-and-resume tests with negative controls; verify promotion selection and supported client/host coverage. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-10001296 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `needs-human` Perform code-truth audit, rubric vetting and independent grading; verify normal green promotion and exact-runtime shipment; mark shipped and close driving item only when every acceptance bar is satisfied. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: Local preparation and test-fixture repairs performed in current continuation. Acceptance route requires Avi/coordinator resolution: kickoff forbids additional agents, while scorecards:emit automatically dispatches new independent auditors and R7 replication requires a disposable managed Codex drill session. Preserve independent acceptance and exact deployed proof; no new agents launched and no gate bypass. See WI-10001395 current checkpoint for verified results and remaining own-test finalization.\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Session preservation and hook runtime\n\n- **P-007** `done` Preserve tracked Codex sessions across provider-error recurrence: remove unconditional provider-alarm ended_at/wake/claim cleanup, add class-specific park/backoff/recovery behavior, and retain explicit lifecycle termination only for confirmed process death, owner close, or irrecoverable corruption. importance: urgent — note: ← WI-10001919 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Repair precompact-managed-carry hook module resolution from ~/.papercusp/hooks/cc so Node launched outside the repository resolves the canonical operator-core runtime or emits a bounded diagnostic; add external-cwd regression coverage. importance: high — note: ← WI-10001917 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Run focused watchdog and hook tests plus affected verification; inspect staging/deployed positions and record completion evidence. importance: high — note: ← WI-10001918 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Explicit SELF and AUTO\nOwner turn session_turn:codex:01a09d53-bfbf-71d0-b849-79f63df8c570:20 authorizes this session implementing from start to finish. No subagent implementation or fleet launch. Use an existing non-implementer for independent review.\n\n### D-002 — Scoped diagnosis first\nDo not activate the broader audit repairs by implication. Diagnose this carry slice before fixes, preserving uncertain historical attribution. Existing shipped substrate plans are dependencies/prior art, not reopened claims.\n\n### D-003 — Honest completion and safe execution\nManual file locks and claimed work precede edits. Maintain durable checkpoints and the armed warm engine loop. A request ACK, local pass or child-only restart is not shipped evidence.\n\n### D-004 — Diagnosed boundaries and smallest enforcement seam\nDate: 2026-09-14\nAffects: backend-audit-diagnosis-before-repair-2026-09-13\nMeasured: owner/source transcript session_turn:codex:01a09d53-bfbf-71d0-b849-79f63df8c570:1-27 plus local Codex rollout event 2026-09-14T01:05:47.648Z; target owner host ledger /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/psu-pty/su-b81649b7-e17e-43a4-afcb-b7ded6027164.events.jsonl; current apps/operator/scripts/psu-pty-host.mjs and packages/operator-core/lib/role-codex-home.ts; official OpenAI Codex config/hook docs. Decision: treat two causal classes separately. (1) Managed request for su-6eeda queued at 01:01:30, busy-gate expired at 01:04:30 (max quiet 144ms vs 1500ms), but Codex performed an in-process native type:compacted boundary at 01:05:47 on the same native session before the managed host cut; the next control state had no loop. Codex model_auto_compact_token_limit is a trigger, not a disable, and current managed homes do not intercept PreCompact/PostCompact. The existing synchronous Codex PreCompact hook is the smallest reuse seam: route automatic native compaction to session:request-compaction and veto the native cut, preserving its flush/brief/authority/host path and explicit refusal/pending result. (2) Original su-b816 received the same self-compaction nonce in native sessions 01a09d41 and 01a09d4f. The later thread was created without a corresponding host terminal event, and its active turn died when Codex shut down the prior thread. Current host source permits a second LIVE host to take over the same owner socket instead of refusing; independent host-local retry/dedup state can therefore replay a carry and a later host teardown can kill the apparent successor. Fail closed on live duplicate host startup before unlink/spawn, and add generation/lifecycle regressions. Retraction: the earlier assertion that one stale makeCarryRearmController callback alone replayed the nonce and its delayed shutdown directly propagated is not proven; exact historical launcher/signal sender remains unresolved. What survives: duplicate nonce across native sessions, SIGHUP end, no accepted shutdown, same-process prior-thread shutdown timing, and unsafe duplicate-host takeover in current source.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n\n### D-005 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-14\nAmendment-Id: managed-carry-p006-method-checks-v1\nRequest-Hash: ce1e778c1ba4c76179faf38bd538ed5ce9a710a62a7020bcc8356e056d60204c\nActor: su-c77f160e-1bd4-4436-9090-bb0360873809\nReason: Bind the independently reviewed as-built METHOD, structured check, replication drill and required proof layer for every predeclared managed-carry BAR before grading.\nApproved-By: su-219d4df8-b6db-459c-ab03-4a36436615fd\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:204649\nApproved-At: 2026-09-14T13:38:39.893Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 14 → 15\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"postgresql-evidence-traversal-2026-09-14","title":"PostgreSQL-first evidence traversal over existing project relationships","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: PostgreSQL-first evidence traversal over existing project relationships\nslug: postgresql-evidence-traversal-2026-09-14\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-14\nupdated: 2026-09-14\n---\n\n# PostgreSQL-first evidence traversal\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-14. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nState: draft — proposal for Avi's review only.\nNext: review this scope and acceptance criteria. Do not activate, promote, assign execution work, launch agents, migrate or deploy.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Objective and source request\nAvi asked to (1) choose real relationship questions and map existing links, (2) use bounded traversal through existing reads, joins first and recursion only where needed, (3) return revisions/evidence/missing links explicitly, (4) use current hybrid search to discover unknown starting IDs, and (5) consider AGE or another backend only after measuring a limitation. Deliver one bounded evidence-bearing read for each selected question, reducing agent-side lookup chains while retaining PostgreSQL and existing authorities.\n\nResearch: docs/reports/postgresql-mem0-graph-follow-up-2026-09-14.md; WI-10001291. Design review: WI-10001305. Respect effort-scoped-continuity-2026-09-02 D-007/D-008/D-009/D-010: containment/history already exists and must not be recreated.\n\n## Initial questions\nDecision/specification to implementing work-item to recorded code/revision and verification evidence; what is transitively blocked by a work-item; which recorded decision or correction explains the current approach. Choose at least three representative real cases, including missing evidence, an orphan item, a direct-goal item and linked plan descendants. Not every evidence or dependency relation is containment.\n\n## Scope and non-goals\nRead-only query functionality over existing records. No external graph database, AGE installation, memory migration, universal nodes/edges store, unrestricted SQL tool, inferred authority/permissions, automatic implementation from history, or eager transcript concatenation. No change to canonical domain writers. A missing relationship is disclosed, never manufactured as verified. Keep member-versus-leader budgets and routing intact.\n\n## Reuse map\nUse work_item_deps through its canonical reader for operational dependencies; coord_links and work_items:links for descriptive relationships; plan_items/plan_decisions and immutable specification/evidence bindings; containment-tree.ts for goal/plan/item membership; prior-attempt-context.ts for collection, authority ordering, compression, omissions, fingerprints and raw-ref recovery; current hybrid search and scoped identity resolution for seed discovery.\n\nCandidate code areas: packages/operator-core/lib/containment-tree.ts, prior-attempt-context.ts, work-item-blocking.ts, agent-tools/work_items/links.ts, agent-tools/plans/get.ts, agent-tools/plans/spec-evidence-store.ts and existing search source registry. Inspect governing decisions and locks before editing; this map does not require changing every file.\n\n## Proposed design\nAn existing typed read interface receives scope, start object or discovery query, intent and limits. Resolve known IDs directly. For prose-only inputs, obtain a bounded candidate set from current hybrid search, preserve original identifiers and expose ambiguity. Compose existing domain readers with SQL joins. Use recursive SQL only for variable-length relationships; preserve cycle handling, access scope and cancellation.\n\nReturn start identity, path steps, source kind/ref/revision or fingerprint, verification state, current-versus-historical classification, missing links, unavailable sources, omitted records and actionable raw-source recovery. A record marked done is not sufficient proof that behavior was verified. Use the existing evidence contract.\n\nBound execution as well as output: depth, visited objects/edges, seeds, SQL timeout, source fan-out, records/bytes and recovery refs. A final LIMIT is not an execution bound. Apply scope restrictions at every hop and on recovery. A cap or cycle must not look like complete absence.\n\nChoose the smallest existing API extension during the contract step. A new table/verb or materially different backend requires a documented reuse analysis and a separate review; do not quietly broaden this plan.\n\n## Work items (not promoted)\n- **P-001** `todo` — Select at least three real question fixtures, capture current answer/evidence, lookup chain, latency and missing-data behavior, and freeze the comparison before implementation.\n- **P-002** `todo` — Map relationships and specify the smallest existing-reader extension, response/recovery contract and explicit execution budgets; distinguish containment history from dependency/evidence traversal. · blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` — Implement bounded direct/recursive traversal behind the selected existing read interface; reuse authority/scoping semantics and report cancellation, cycles, caps and unavailable sources. · blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` — Connect current hybrid search for seed discovery only when exact identity is unknown, preserving ambiguity, identifiers and tenant constraints. · blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-005** `todo` — Integrate evidence/revision/fingerprint reporting and exact raw-source recovery without duplicating history stores or inflating member context; expose one representative read workflow. · blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `todo` — Add and run project-framework tests for fixed chains, cycles, high fan-out, missing/deleted/corrected sources, stale evidence, scope leakage, unknown IDs, mixed goal attachments and recovery. Compare frozen baseline at equal correctness/completeness. · blocked-by: P-005\n- **P-007** `todo` — Demonstrate selected questions on current-build/staging, document measured value and residual gaps, and present acceptance evidence; reconsider another backend only after a concrete measured limitation and separate approval. · blocked-by: P-006\n\n## Acceptance criteria\nEach known-seed question has a single bounded read returning the recorded chain or an explicit missing/unavailable explanation. Every conclusion exposes its source and revision/evidence status; no fabricated link or promoted authority.\n\nScope tests deny unauthorized access at seed, hop and recovery. Cycles/caps report partial coverage. Degraded reads never assert complete absence. Corrections/deletions are respected; retained history is labeled and remains governed by existing retention/access policies.\n\nAt equal correctness/completeness, agent lookup calls decrease on target multi-call cases and p95 end-to-end latency does not regress against the recorded baseline. Absolute execution budgets are fixed in the contract step before implementation. Existing member-claim and plan/goal-history tests remain green. Feature tests ship with implementation; typecheck alone is insufficient.\n\nImplementation acceptance uses current-build/staging. Final promotion/shipment is separate; do not claim deployment from local tests.\n\n## Risks\nAbsent links: separate capture gaps from query gaps. Generic graph abstractions: preserve each domain's writer/read authority. Recursive fan-out: bound work and expose omissions. Stale caches: start without new caching; use source versions/fingerprints if needed. Semantic ambiguity: return candidates or uncertainty. Existing history overlap: extend, do not fork. Serving/source drift: acceptance must exercise the actual intended consumer, not only a helper.\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — PostgreSQL first\nDate: 2026-09-14\nUse existing relational records and bounded joins/recursion. A graph-shaped question does not authorize a graph database.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse continuity and relationship machinery\nDate: 2026-09-14\nReuse existing compiler authority, omission and recovery contracts; keep non-containment relations explicit.\n\n### D-003 — Discovery is not evidence\nDate: 2026-09-14\nSearch finds seeds. Only permitted recorded links and evidence substantiate conclusions; inferred links cannot become authority without the existing verification workflow.\n\n### D-004 — Draft only\nDate: 2026-09-14\nAvi requested a proposal and summary, not implementation. Keep draft until review approval and execution-route choice. Audit the complete source conversation and record activation audit before any later activation; none is claimed now.\n\n### D-005 — Superseded by the owner-requested consolidated plan\nDate: 2026-09-14\nOwner explicitly requested consolidation on 2026-09-14, then personal AUTO execution to shipped. Successor: scoped-evidence-and-continuity-2026-09-14. The successor preservation map was read back and maps this plan's seven items to its 12 consolidated units; original decisions remain retained here. This is transfer of unimplemented requirements, not completion or abandonment. Execute the successor only.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-09-14** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: Owner explicitly authorized consolidation and superseding originals. Their unfinished requirements remain intact in scoped-evidence-and-continuity-2026-09-14 with complete item/decision mapping; waive only the unfinished-items supersede refusal, not implementation or shipment acceptance. Forced by: su · su-c8ca9 (`su-c8ca9c94-3080-4bdb-bdcb-9d7fc6a62a48`).\n<!-- papercusp:forced-past:v1: -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"scoped-continuity-quality-and-temporal-reads-2026-09-14","title":"Scoped continuity quality and time-aware history reads","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Scoped continuity quality and time-aware history reads\nslug: scoped-continuity-quality-and-temporal-reads-2026-09-14\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-14\nupdated: 2026-09-14\n---\n\n# Scoped continuity quality and time-aware history reads\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-14. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nState: draft — owner review only; implementation is not authorized.\nNext: review improvement scope, time semantics and acceptance criteria. Do not activate, promote work, launch agents, migrate or deploy.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded.\n\n## Objective\nImprove how useful evidence survives work-item, plan and goal context boundaries, and enable bounded time-aware reads through the existing PostgreSQL continuity surfaces. Preserve correct-level writing, canonical authority, fixed member/leader budgets, source recovery and explicit uncertainty.\n\n## Source request and governing context\nOwner requested the six Research insights for improving this system recommendations from docs/reports/scoped-continuity-design-review-2026-09-14.md as a plan, and asked whether time-based reading exists and whether it should. Preserve every recommendation: semantic survival at each depth; selective capture improvements; task-relevant detail; immutable versus current-object recovery; incremental refresh/delta delivery; and correct resumed actions after repeated context boundaries.\n\nReuse effort-scoped-continuity-2026-09-02 D-007/D-008/D-009/D-010. They establish scope-matched writes, bounded leader rollups, no copying/promoting lessons, and feedback before costly semantic extraction. Related draft postgresql-evidence-traversal-2026-09-14 addresses relationship-query ergonomics; coordinate shared files/contracts rather than duplicate work. Prior review WI-10001305; this planning investigation WI-10001313.\n\n## Verified baseline\nCurrent source already provides append-only scoped lessons, bounded checkpoint journals, containment resolution, prior-attempt compilation, depth-based field selection, protected authority/residue, omissions, fingerprints and raw recovery. Records carry at timestamps and are ordered by authority/scope before recency. The checked collector and plan/goal rollup entry points do not expose a unified since/until/as-of read contract.\n\nGoal history is an append-only audit projection with bounded pages. Plan revisions have sequence, timestamp and stored snapshots. memory:search separately supports as_of validity filtering over memory_canonical. That is not a historical goal/plan/work-item snapshot, transaction-time reconstruction, or proof of past containment membership. Current containment reads current relationships. Retention-bounded journals cannot reproduce discarded source text.\n\nA prior review found serving-generation mismatch EI-23210960729184724. Verify the actual consuming build as acceptance evidence; do not operate another agent's live release-gate lane.\n\n## Scope and non-goals\nExtend current capture feedback, compiler, source readers and existing plan/goal/work-item read interfaces. Time is another selection dimension, not a new database. No graph database, global memory blob, compulsory new checkpoint form, universal event store, copying lessons between levels, silent budget increases, automatic permission rewriting or uncontrolled recursion. No fabricated old history or retention-policy expansion without separate review.\n\n## Proposed temporal reads\nNames below specify behavior, not already-existing API arguments. Final schema names must extend the current typed read interface.\n\nCURRENT CONTEXT: keep today's default bounded briefing with protected current authority and unresolved residue; existing callers do not change.\n\nCHANGES SINCE: newly recorded, updated, corrected, retracted or deleted evidence since a scope-bound cursor or explicit timestamp. Prefer durable per-source progress to a wall-clock-only resume marker. Include descendant changes even when the parent plan text is unchanged.\n\nWINDOW/TIMELINE: select records in a half-open interval [from,to), with chronological ordering, deterministic tie-breaking and bounded keyset paging. Recorded time is the initial basis. Domain-event/effective time is selectable only when a source actually records it; unknown times stay unknown.\n\nHISTORICAL AS-OF: reconstruct retained evidence/versions and relationships as known by cutoff T. Exclude facts learned later, later corrections, current summaries and current membership masquerading as historical state. Return exact, partial or unsupported coverage per source family. Never imply an exact past snapshot from mutable current rows.\n\nVALID-ON: an optional separate dimension answering which retained facts apply at domain time T. Reuse memory validity semantics where appropriate. It is NOT the same as known-at: a policy effective September 7 but recorded September 9 must yield different answers to those questions.\n\nExamples: what changed in this goal since the agent's last read; decisions recorded September 7–10, 2026; evidence known on September 7 before a later correction; a constraint effective on September 7 but learned later.\n\n## Time, authority and completeness contract\nNormalize timestamps to UTC; preserve original timezone/provenance where relevant. Require an offset or a declared input timezone and define date-only boundaries. Test DST, equal timestamps, clock skew, late arrival and replay. No missing timestamp may be silently invented as epoch/current time.\n\nApply time selection during source collection and descendant admission, BEFORE recency/child/record/byte caps. Filtering today's already-capped brief cannot correctly answer an older interval. Bound execution work as well as output, and expose omissions/unknown source coverage.\n\nOpaque cursors are bound to workspace, subject, query filters, mode and policy version. Use existing durable source positions/watermarks or a minimal equivalent; a single maximum timestamp can miss late events. Page replay is idempotent. Include retained tombstones/edits. If history retention invalidates a cursor, require a fresh snapshot or return an explicit gap rather than silently skipping it.\n\nCURRENT and SINCE reads may carry older still-binding decisions/safety constraints as a separately labeled baseline, never pretend they occurred in the requested window. Historical evidence does not authorize current action: present-day execution permissions remain separate from past approvals.\n\nFor a historical plan/goal view, declare whether membership is historical-at-cutoff or current. Exact historical membership requires retained link versions/events. If those do not exist, label the limitation; do not silently use today's tree.\n\nEvery answer carries source kind/ref/revision or hash, recorded time, effective time where present, scope, selection policy, historical/current status, partial/truncated/unavailable coverage and exact recovery instructions. Recovery uses the same time/scope semantics. Current-object refs and immutable snapshot refs are distinct.\n\n## Six research-derived improvements\nSEMANTIC SURVIVAL: paired fixtures at work-item, plan and goal levels must preserve corrections, blockers, permission limits, evidence and non-keyword phrasing; test meaning and action, not just strings.\n\nSELECTIVE CAPTURE: measure current extractor/advisory results first. Where consequential notes still lose meaning, add a bounded source-grounded fallback with optional structured fields and exact supporting spans. Never invent a root cause or mandate extra note-writing ceremony.\n\nTASK-RELEVANT RESOLUTION: preserve the fixed budget and protected corrections/residue; allocate more detail to an explicitly relevant deep child by shrinking ordinary irrelevant detail or targeted drill-down. Preserve member/leader boundaries.\n\nIMMUTABLE RECOVERY: reuse source revisions/hashes for critical evidence; do not promise recovery of discarded journal content. Clearly distinguish a source as it is now from the version used by a prior brief.\n\nINCREMENTAL REFRESH: key cache/summary validity on true dependencies, membership, time selection and policy, not only the plan revision. Send a delta only when the consumer has the right base; otherwise send a fresh bounded snapshot. Late corrections invalidate derived results. Avoid unnecessary model refresh on unchanged scopes.\n\nRESUMED-ACTION EVALUATION: exercise work-item -> plan -> goal -> compaction -> resume across repeated boundaries and time-scoped updates. Measure total foreground/background/retrieval cost and correct actions.\n\n## Reuse map\nPrimary candidates: packages/operator-core/lib/prior-attempt-context.ts, prior-attempt-rungs.ts, containment-tree.ts, effort-thread.ts, work-item-checkpoint.ts, carry-note.ts; existing plans/get and revisions readers, fleet/leader-brief and goal readers/startup; packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/goals/history.ts and get.ts; spec/evidence revision stores, retained audit/sync events and existing plan-attribution enrichment. Inspect actual writers/clock units and governing decisions before changing a source. This map does not authorize editing every file.\n\n## Work items (not promoted)\n- **P-001** `todo` — Inventory current source/time/retention/capture/reader capabilities and freeze representative continuity/time questions across the three scopes, including missing history and negative cases; measure semantic loss, query cost and current behavior.\n- **P-002** `todo` — Define the smallest existing-interface contract: time modes and clock mapping, scope/membership, cursor and snapshot semantics, coverage/recovery, source/model budgets and supported versus partial historical cases. · blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` — Reuse or minimally extend immutable source/version reads and scoped source-progress tracking needed for recovery and temporal reads; preserve deletion/retention boundaries. Return material schema or retention changes for separate review before mutation. · blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` — Implement bounded recorded-time window and changes-since reads, stable paging, late-change/tombstone handling and filter-before-cap selection; retain current-context behavior. · blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-005** `todo` — Implement as-of reconstruction only for genuinely supported retained source versions/membership, with explicit partial/unsupported responses elsewhere; distinguish valid-on and prevent future-evidence leakage. · blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `todo` — Improve capture only where baseline evidence warrants: measure existing feedback, then selectively add provenance-grounded extraction with optional fields, deterministic fallback and bounded model spend. · blocked-by: P-005\n- **P-007** `todo` — Add task-relevant detail allocation and exact source expansion within existing authority/residue/context budgets; evaluate semantic survival, not merely larger output. · blocked-by: P-006\n- **P-008** `todo` — Refine source-dependent refresh and base-validated deltas, including time/membership policy in fingerprints; unchanged scopes must not cause unnecessary model work. · blocked-by: P-007\n- **P-009** `todo` — Run deterministic/real-PostgreSQL and blinded semantic tests for permissions, negation, correction, time boundaries, late events, moved membership, retention gaps, races, scope isolation, stale summaries, recovery, omissions and cache invalidation. · blocked-by: P-008\n- **P-010** `todo` — Exercise real consuming agents through repeated compaction/resume and time-scoped reads on current-build/staging; compare total cost and correct action to the frozen baseline, disclose residual limits and verify deployed generation separately before claiming shipment. · blocked-by: P-009\n\n## Acceptance criteria\nAll six research recommendations remain covered. Scope-matched writes, member/leader boundaries and protected authority/residue are preserved. Critical corrections, restrictions, evidence and unresolved work survive tested compression depths. No global memory store, required note form or unconditional new model call.\n\nWindow/since fixtures return the expected scoped events, including older in-window descendants that today's cap would exclude and late-recorded corrections. Equal-time records page without loss or duplication under the documented cursor/snapshot policy. Retention gaps and read failures are explicit.\n\nAs-of fixtures exclude later knowledge and use retained historical revisions/membership when available. Unsupported history is labeled. Known-at and valid-on deliberately differ in late-arrival fixtures. A historical approval never grants present authority.\n\nSemantic extractions retain source support and uncertainty. Summary/delta updates check the base and source identity; invalidated summaries do not remain silently current. Existing member/leader and recovery tests stay green.\n\nFix absolute latency/cost ceilings and non-inferiority margins from the baseline before intervention. Compare equivalent evidence/model budgets, and report ingestion/extraction, refresh, retrieval and foreground costs separately. A cheaper but incorrect continuation fails.\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Extend the existing system\nDate: 2026-09-14\nReuse PostgreSQL, scoped threads, compiler and source/version machinery. This is a follow-on to shipped continuity work, not a replacement; coordinate overlap with the SQL evidence-traversal draft.\n\n### D-002 — Time-aware reads are in scope\nDate: 2026-09-14\nAdd changes-since and interval reads first; provide as-of only to the extent retained evidence supports it. Apply temporal selection before bounded admission.\n\n### D-003 — Known-at differs from valid-on\nDate: 2026-09-14\nSeparate recorded time from effective time. Memory validity filtering alone does not reconstruct historical system knowledge or containment.\n\n### D-004 — Historical completeness is evidence-bound\nDate: 2026-09-14\nNever invent discarded history, silently extend retention or present current rows as an exact past snapshot. Report per-source coverage and distinguish current versus immutable recovery.\n\n### D-005 — Selective and measurable\nDate: 2026-09-14\nMeasure capture and semantic survival before adding model work; preserve authority and test correct resumed action at bounded total cost.\n\n### D-006 — Draft only\nDate: 2026-09-14\nOwner asked for a reviewable plan, not execution. Obtain review approval and execution-route choice, audit the full source conversation and record activation audit before any later activation.\n\n### D-007 — Superseded by the owner-requested consolidated plan\nDate: 2026-09-14\nOwner explicitly requested consolidation on 2026-09-14, then personal AUTO execution to shipped. Successor: scoped-evidence-and-continuity-2026-09-14. The successor preservation map was read back and maps this plan's ten items and six research/temporal requirements into the consolidated units; original decisions remain retained here. This is transfer of unimplemented requirements, not completion or abandonment. Execute the successor only.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-09-14** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. Reason: Owner explicitly authorized consolidation and superseding originals. Their unfinished requirements remain intact in scoped-evidence-and-continuity-2026-09-14 with complete item/decision mapping; waive only the unfinished-items supersede refusal, not implementation or shipment acceptance. \"outcome\": \"Affected output refreshes; wrong-base deltas become bounded snapshots and unchanged scopes avoid extra work.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-7\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n    \"SC-004\",\n        \"SC-005\",\n        \"SC-008\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Bounded PostgreSQL evidence with exact recovery.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Bounded PostgreSQL evidence with exact recovery\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a09da9-d069-7443-a3fd-b254b8c9125a:26\",\n Named new test files are planned project-suite acceptance files, not claims that they exist or pass today; exact check selection is reviewed against the inventory before implementation.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-012 | live |\n\nKeep the existing serial dependencies. agents retrieve trustworthy recorded evidence across work-items, plans and goals through bounded PostgreSQL reads, and carry the important meaning through long-running work without losing corrections, permissions, verification or outstanding commitments. Reduce unnecessary lookup chains and repeated context while preserving original source recovery and explicit uncertainty.\n\n## Existing authority and reuse\nRespect effort-scoped-continuity-2026-09-02 D-007/D-008/D-009/D-010: write at the insight's level; append durable effort lessons rather than copy/promote them; bounded leader rollups differ from member reads; measure capture/advisory results before adding expensive extraction.\n\nReuse work_item_deps through its canonical domain reader; coord_links and work_items:links for descriptive typed links; plan_items/plan_decisions; immutable spec/evidence bindings; containment-tree.ts for membership; prior-attempt-context.ts and prior-attempt-rungs.ts for collection, authority ordering, compression, omissions, fingerprints and recovery; effort-thread.ts and checkpoint/journal writers; existing hybrid search, source attribution/enrichment, plan revisions and goal audit history. Non-containment dependency/evidence links must not be forced into the containment hierarchy.\n\nCandidate areas: packages/operator-core/lib/prior-attempt-context.ts, prior-attempt-rungs.ts, containment-tree.ts, effort-thread.ts, work-item-checkpoint.ts, carry-note.ts, work-item-blocking.ts, agent-tools/work_items/links.ts, agent-tools/plans/get.ts, agent-tools/plans/revisions.ts, spec/evidence stores, fleet/leader-brief.ts and goal consumers; packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/goals/history.ts and get.ts; existing search registry and attribution enrichment. Inspect current source/decisions, register each execution item and take enforced file locks before edits.\n\n## Required query families\n1. Decision or specification -> implementing work-item -> recorded code/revision -> verification evidence. A done label alone is not verification.\n2. Transitive operational blockers through the canonical dependency semantics.\n3. Recorded decision/correction explaining the current approach.\n4. Current scope history, changes since a prior read, a chronological interval, and supported historical reconstruction.\n\nFreeze at least three real project questions plus cases for orphan work-items, direct-goal items, plan descendants, ambiguous search seeds, missing evidence and unauthorized similarly named records. Distinguish capture gaps from inconvenient readers. Never fabricate a missing relationship.\n\n## Shared request and response contract\nExtend the smallest existing typed read interfaces. A known start ID is resolved directly; a prose start uses a bounded candidate set from existing hybrid search, preserving original identifiers and ambiguity. Prefer normal joins; use recursion only for variable-length paths. A new table/verb/backend requires explicit reuse analysis and may not silently expand this plan.\n\nResponses identify starting objects, path steps, source kind/ref/revision or fingerprint, recorded time and effective/event time where present, verification status, current/historical classification, membership basis, partial coverage, unavailable sources, cycles/caps, omissions and actionable raw-source recovery. Recovery uses the same scope/time policy. Keep current-object references distinct from immutable snapshots.\n\nBound execution AND output: query deadline/cancellation, seed count, visited nodes/edges, depth, source fan-out, rows/bytes and recovery refs. A final LIMIT alone is not a work bound. Apply tenant/harness restrictions at seed, each hop, source collection and recovery. Preserve current member/leader budgets and protected authority/residue.\n\n## Temporal semantics\nCURRENT: existing bounded briefing remains default, with current authority and unresolved residue.\nSINCE: newly recorded/changed/corrected/retracted/deleted evidence since a scope-bound cursor or explicit instant, including descendant changes without parent markdown changes. Prefer durable source positions over wall-clock-only progress.\nWINDOW: select records in [from,to), chronological order with stable tie-breaks and bounded keyset paging. Recorded-time is initial basis; event/valid time is used only where actually recorded.\nKNOWN-AT / HISTORICAL AS-OF: retained source versions and relationship membership as known by cutoff T. Exclude later knowledge, corrections, present-day summaries or membership masquerading as past evidence. Report exact/partial/unsupported coverage by source family.\nVALID-ON: optional separate axis for facts applying at domain time T; not equivalent to known-at. A policy effective September 7 but recorded September 9 yields intentionally different answers.\n\nNormalize to UTC; require an offset or explicit timezone, define date-only boundaries and preserve original timezone/provenance when meaningful. Test DST, equal times, clock skew, replay and late arrival. Missing timestamps stay unknown.\n\nFilter sources/descendants by time BEFORE recent-child/record/byte caps. Filtering today's 24-child/16-record sample cannot answer an older interval correctly. Cursors bind workspace, subject, mode, filters and policy version; replay is idempotent, and retention-invalid cursors return a gap/fresh-snapshot requirement. Retained edits/tombstones and late events must not be lost behind a single max timestamp.\n\nCurrent/since answers may retain older binding decisions as a separately labeled baseline, never as in-window events. Historical evidence cannot grant current permission. Historical membership requires retained membership history; if only today's edges exist, disclose that limitation rather than claim an exact past tree.\n\n## Continuity quality requirements\nMeasure semantic survival through work-item -> plan -> goal compression: corrections, blockers, permission limits, verification and non-keyword lessons must survive the tested cases. Preserve exact source evidence and uncertainty.\n\nMeasure existing extractor/advisory effectiveness before changing capture. Add source-grounded semantic extraction only where consequential loss warrants it, with optional fields, exact source spans, deterministic fallback and explicit model cost. No mandatory new form, invented root cause or unconditional extra model call.\n\nAllow task-relevant deep-child detail within the fixed budget by reducing ordinary irrelevant detail or targeted drill-down; depth is not the only relevance signal. Do not weaken protected corrections/residue or member/leader boundaries.\n\nReuse immutable revisions/hashes for critical evidence. Retention-bounded journals are not infinite archives. Source/version support determines recovery claims.\n\nCaches/derived summaries depend on actual source versions, membership and temporal/query policy, not just parent plan revision. Start without new caches unless measured need; any delta requires the consumer's correct base, otherwise return a fresh bounded snapshot. Late corrections invalidate relevant derived output. Unchanged scopes avoid unnecessary model refresh.\n\nEvaluate actual resumed actions across repeated boundaries, not only string presence. Count ingestion/extraction, refresh, retrieval, foreground inference and repeated-work costs.\n\n## Non-goals and safeguards\nNo external graph database, AGE installation, universal graph/event store, global memory blob, wholesale memory migration, unrestricted SQL, copying lessons between levels, authority inferred from similarity, automated permissions rewriting, uncontrolled recursion, eager transcript concatenation or silently raised budgets. Preserve canonical domain writers. No fabricated historical completeness. Material retention expansion, destructive migrations, new outward data transfer or a materially different backend requires separate authority; use explicit partial/unsupported behavior instead of quietly widening scope.\n\nMem0 remains an optional derived-memory candidate, not a dependency or replacement for authoritative history. Source-grounded extraction/classification/feedback/synthesis may be compared if existing mechanisms demonstrably fail; Platform-only features, user-only Dream scope and managed-data transfer are not assumed available in OSS. Additional ranking/decay experiments remain optional, not hidden critical-path commitments.\n\n## Workstreams and items\n### Shared foundation\n- **P-001** `todo` — Inventory existing capabilities, source clocks/versions/retention and actual serving paths; freeze real relationship/time/continuity fixtures with correct answers, lookup costs, semantic-loss baseline and negative cases. Record any source/runtime mismatch as a scoped follow-up without taking over another live gate.\n- **P-002** `todo` — Specify the smallest shared reader/response/recovery contract, authority and scope checks, membership/time/cursor semantics, supported history matrix and bounded execution/model budgets. Freeze comparison margins before intervention. · blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` — Reuse or minimally extend immutable source/version reads and scoped source-progress tracking for exact recovery and temporal selection. Preserve retention/deletion boundaries and disclose coverage gaps; no unapproved retention/schema expansion. · blocked-by: P-002\n### Evidence and time retrieval\n- **P-004** `todo` — Implement bounded joins/recursive traversal through canonical dependency/evidence/relationship readers, with cancellation, cycles, high-fan-out limits, source revisions, evidence state and missing/unavailable links explicit. · blocked-by: P-003\n- **P-005** `todo` — Integrate current hybrid search only for unknown starting identities; preserve original identifiers/ambiguity and provide an existing-interface read workflow with exact source recovery. · blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-006** `todo` — Implement bounded recorded-time interval and changes-since reads, stable paging/cursors, late-event/tombstone handling and filter-before-cap descendant/source admission; preserve default current reads. · blocked-by: P-005\n- **P-007** `todo` — Implement known-at historical reads for retained source/membership families that genuinely support them; explicit partial/unsupported answers elsewhere. Keep valid-on distinct and exclude future knowledge/current authority leakage. · blocked-by: P-006\n### Continuity quality\n- **P-008** `todo` — Improve capture only where baseline warrants: evaluate existing feedback, selectively extract important missing lessons with source support and optional fields, bounded spend/fallback, no invented root causes. · blocked-by: P-007\n- **P-009** `todo` — Add task-relevant depth/detail allocation or exact targeted expansion within fixed authority/residue/context budgets; verify semantic survival and unchanged member/leader scope. · blocked-by: P-008\n- **P-010** `todo` — Refine source-dependent refresh and base-validated deltas only where needed; fingerprints include membership/time/query policy and source changes; do not refresh unchanged scopes unnecessarily. · blocked-by: P-009\n### Shared acceptance and shipment\n- **P-011** `todo` — Add/run project-framework deterministic, real-PostgreSQL and blinded semantic checks across both workstreams: missing/changed/deleted sources, false premises/negation, permissions, temporal edges/DST/equal times, late events, moved membership, retention gaps, races, cycles, caps, scope isolation and raw recovery. no final LIMIT-only work bound or unknown-as-empty result.\nAC-05: Window/since fixtures include expected older in-window descendants and late-recorded updates/corrections; equal-time paging has no loss/duplication under the documented cursor/snapshot contract.\nAC-06: Known-at excludes later knowledge and uses retained historical revisions/membership where supported; A spill file preserves output already produced; it does not by itself avoid upstream database/network/CPU work or full-result memory assembly. Streaming helps memory but still needs scheduling, cancellation and resource controls. Do not globally delete LIMIT, timeout, safety or access-control checks.\n\nRead evidence: packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts documents the 2,000 LIST ceiling as protection against repeated live-sync reassembly/serialization, not virtualized rendering. Its countWorkItems/countWorkItemsByState and listAllWorkItemsForFileExport demonstrate already-existing intent-specific alternatives. Generic result-door/output-envelope and tooldef projection mechanisms already distinguish some output loss from recoverable spills; extend them rather than add a parallel protocol.\n\nMeasured logged-call evidence through 2026-09-14T01:18Z: August 24–September 6 had 135 general burn-down calls by 36 attributed agents; September 7+ had 41 burn-down calls, 40 exact cohorts and one general call. This is ONE consumer's usage/exposure, not a generic cap-hit rate. Successful work_items:list/export counts are also not cap-hit counts. The current invocation writer records arguments/status/timing/size/reference, not a reliable generic source-cap outcome; some internal calls are outside that ledger. Exact generic frequency and avoidable recovery cost remain unmeasured and are explicit work in this plan.\n\nConfirmed cross-surface failure patterns are documented in agent-insights/a-fetch-cap-becomes-a-ceiling-on-a-count, agent-insights/spilled-is-not-omitted-recoverability-in-result-envelopes, and agent-insights/measuring-payload-tier-forced-truncation-and-door-spill. The existing corpus-accurate-counts-and-facets-2026-08-21 plan is shipped; preserve/reuse its implementations and tests. capless-adaptive-resource-governor-2026-08-26 governs resource admission and must not be contradicted by a new arbitrary global capacity ceiling.\n\n## Scope and boundary\n\nAll first-party read/list/search/report/export surfaces and their shared source/projection/transport primitives are in the INVENTORY. Remediation is explicitly classified per surface, not blanket removal. Include work items, plans, sessions/history, facts/memory, coordination/fleet reads, metrics and available connector wrappers. For third-party/provider limits the plan requires truthful capability/continuation handling, not promises of access the provider cannot supply. Security, authorization, retention, cost policy and privacy limits remain enforced and distinct from size limits. This plan does not change work-item admission, issue identity or auto-cleanup policy; the separate work-queue plan owns those.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Agents and engineers using first-party read, list, search, metrics, history and export tools.\",\n  \"problem\": \"A bounded source read can silently become the full population for a count or audit, while a spill only preserves the produced subset.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Complete authorized requests remain complete across bounded pages or resumable jobs; exact calculations cover the full predicate and unfinished work has explicit continuation.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Work-item admission, duplicate identity, judging and cleanup policy belong to work-queue-judging-and-cleanup-2026-09-14.\",\n    \"No weakening authorization, privacy, retention, external-provider boundaries or the existing adaptive resource governor.\",\n    \"No unbounded in-memory corpus loading or replacement platform subsystem.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:10\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:13\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:17\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:20\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:24\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:26\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Cover generic platform source limits, retain resource-bounded processing and remove arbitrary total-coverage ceilings.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:17\",\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:20\",\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:24\",\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a09d5a-0ce5-73f3-bb92-05743a73dcb3:26\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"observed-fact\",\n      \"text\": \"The canonical draft has 8 unstarted items and no first-class clauses; interrupt midway, assert INCOMPLETE and a valid checkpoint, resume and compare exact sorted IDs/count/hash to an independent oracle.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/export.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/burn_down.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n| Intent | Source strategy | Delivery |\n|---|---|---|\n| Exact summary or existence | Full-predicate aggregate or targeted existence query | Small result with exactness and scope |\n| Interactive browse | Bounded projected page | Stable continuation plus exact/unknown total |\n| Complete audit/export | Managed streaming batches | Manifest-backed file/reference and resume status |\n| Best-match search | Declared top-K/approximate retrieval | Ranked matches and coverage limitations |\n| Policy/provider constrained | Honor the actual boundary | Explicit unavailable/partial and permitted alternative |\n\nShared protocol belongs in existing output-envelope/result-door/tooldef surfaces; per-source continuation belongs in the owning adapter. Never reconstruct restricted data through an alternate surface. Storage retention and authorization are not truncation defects. The inventory determines the smallest code changes rather than assuming every tool uses the work-items 2,000 limit.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Plan items | Evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-006, P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-001, P-005, P-008 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-007, P-008 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-007 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Census and contract\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Audit generic source-limit owners/call sites and predecessor work; establish resource rationale and observed friction baseline with coverage gaps; classify the complete enumerated population and assign each limit a disposition. Covers R-1/R-7/R-8. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Define and test the shared completeness/exactness/stage/recoverability/continuation contract in existing envelopes and source adapters, including externally imposed and security/retention bounds.
