Test mutable datasets and provider-specific continuation boundaries. Covers R-4/R-6/R-9. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Extend existing full exporters/managed traversal jobs with streaming batches, manifests, hashes, checkpoint/resume/cancel and authorized retrieval; prove full recovery beyond source/output caps with bounded resource use. Covers R-5/R-8/R-9. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` Instrument source/projection/transport outcomes and linked recovery effort in the existing telemetry/state surfaces; separate measured cap hits from ordinary pages, spills, usage and missing coverage. Produce a generic frequency/friction report, including internal consumers. Covers R-7. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n\n## Phase 3 — Acceptance and rollout\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Independently verify large-corpus exactness, complete traversal/manifests, oversized records, permissions, concurrent mutations, outage/replay/cancellation and resource behavior; reuse existing corpus-accuracy tests and publish all unchecked/excluded surfaces. Covers R-1 through R-10. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 importance: high\n- **P-008** `todo` After plan/route approval, roll out verified changes by consumer group, document recovery behavior and measure generic cap encounters, exact-answer success, memory/latency and avoidable extra calls against baseline. Preserve safe rollback and report unresolved provider/policy limits; do not claim zero friction from absent instrumentation. Covers R-7/R-8/R-9/R-10. blocked-by: P-007 importance: high\n\n## Acceptance\n\n**Owner-clarification regression (R-11/P-007):** For a known authorized 100,000-record fixture, exact aggregation must return 100,000 and complete traversal/export must retrieve every expected ID exactly once across multiple resource-bounded batch sizes, including 2,000. Pause partway, verify INCOMPLETE plus a usable checkpoint, and resume to the complete matching manifest. A fixed total cutoff or presenting the partial subset as complete fails acceptance. Batch size is never a source-coverage ceiling.\n\nFor each inventoried surface, retain or remove its limit with explicit rationale and source evidence. Exact summaries must match an independent oracle above the old cap and be invariant to page size. Complete access must enumerate exactly the authorized snapshot/cohort with no missing/duplicated IDs and full retrievable evidence, or report an explicit supported limitation. Resource-bounded tests must not turn a complete request into unbounded memory/work. The final report includes a directly measured generic cap-hit rate, telemetry coverage and recovery cost; it never treats usage/exposure as cap hits. Runtime knobs are tuned from measured latency/memory/cost, not invented capacity targets.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Keep per-request safeguards, remove inaccessible population ceilings\n\nOwner-directed clarification: REMOVE arbitrary source-coverage caps; do not merely retain them with warnings or increase their numeric value. RETAIN bounded, resumable processing: batches, streaming, resource-aware pacing and checkpoints. Resource constraints govern execution, not the completeness or scope of the request. Counts cover the complete scope; interrupted traversal remains INCOMPLETE with a concrete continuation. Existing authorization, retention and truly external provider constraints remain distinct and explicit. This is a plan amendment, not implementation or activation approval.\n\n### D-002 — Output spill and source completeness are independent\n\nA recoverable spill guarantees recovery of the produced payload only. Manifest/scope evidence establishes whether the requested source population was completely processed.\n\n### D-003 — Generic policy, separate work-queue application\n\nThis plan owns generic limits and queue metric access. The separate queue plan consumes its exact-summary/complete-export contract while owning domain admission, identity, judgments and cleanup. No duplicate implementation of generic transport/pagination in that plan. Other queue repairs may proceed independently after their own approval.\n\n### D-004 — Draft is not execution authority\n\nBefore activation, read the complete source conversation, map all requirements/corrections to this plan, record canonical activation audit, obtain Avi's plan and execution-route choice, and only then start. No fleet/model/account/carry choice is implicit in writing this plan.\n\n### D-005 — Plan-overlap review\n\nThe creation guard suggested rate-limit-layer-v2-2026-06-05. Its canonical Now section was read: shipped, 23 completed items, inference capacity/admission scope. This new owner-requested source-completeness effort is distinct, retains the governor, and does not reopen that plan.\n\n### D-006 — Execute approved portfolio assignment without changing product scope\nDate: 2026-10-15\nExecution authority is now provided by Avi's owner-typed portfolio directive session_turn:codex:01a13d6d-a7d4-7ad2-8c54-ebc7e7326525:38 and this exact-plan kickoff: one existing headless gpt-6.1-sol:xhigh session, account auto, warm carry, no additional agents. This supersedes the prior draft-only execution hold in D-004 and Now, not the original requirements. Repair preparation, activation and admission using supported tools before implementation; preserve non-author/independent acceptance, credential/owner-only boundaries, live claims and release-gate ownership. Preparation work-item WI-6554700010014344 records source/ownership proof. Measured: plans:get v5/v6 and plans:get-specs returned 8 todo items and no clauses; fleet:assignments exact plan returned no other owner; indexed adv_sessions exact plan query returned this owner only (44188).\nRelated: P-001, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-007 — Activation waits for authenticated historical product-source evidence\nDate: 2026-10-15\nThe source text remains readable and is not classified as fabricated, but current activation provenance is unresolved. Measured: plans:audit activation dryRun returned item_provenance_missing / derived_source_not_owner_backed for P-001–P-008. sessions:search on source turn26 returned unknown/unenrolled-origin; a same-scope source read confirmed original mapped turns10,13,17,20,24,26 are all unenrolled-origin with no currently retained session prompt stamps. A positive-control-backed owner_directives read for the original author returned no captured directives. The hook-only sessions:record-prompt-origin carrier explicitly refuses model-authored historical stamps. Do not relabel the original requirements as agent-added, map portfolio execution authority as new product requirements, or bypass the gate. Resume when authenticated source provenance is restored from genuine retained evidence or Avi reaffirms the existing product scope in an authenticated owner turn. D-006 execution authorization remains valid; this is an evidence prerequisite, not a renewed route/permission request. Independent spec-quality and P-007 acceptance remain required after activation preparation.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-008 — Correct the provenance wall using explicit planner-authored item declarations\nDate: 2026-10-15\nCorrection to D-007: unverified historical owner origin is real, but requiring authenticated reaffirmation as the only activation path was too strong. The live plans:audit contract explicitly permits agent-added item declarations with reasons. P-001–P-008 are the legacy planner-authored decomposition of existing R-1–R-11, so declare that truth without claiming owner-backed derivation or changing requirement intent. Measured: activation dry-run with explicit reasons passed at plan v12; owner0/derived0/agent-added8/unresolved0, seven source refs resolved. No original requirement is newly attributed to Avi, no portfolio authorization is used as new product requirements and no gate is bypassed. Supersedes D-007's owner-only stop; its source-origin evidence remains valid. Continue canonical activation and independent gates with the provenance distinction preserved.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-009 — Independent review is the remaining admission boundary under the no-agent constraint\nDate: 2026-10-15\nPreparation has passed the current-build structural spec-quality evaluator, not independent grading. Measured: operator-api route3170 at build3972e21dc6 contains the current evaluator; 27active clauses/8items pass with specSetHash4036adf4b5a048e813c7bf8e41dbe8cea62412632daa33fddb362d4145317dd4 and wouldBlock:[]. The terminal standard-rubric scorecard must receive a settled NON-AUTHOR grading-integrity audit before plans:start. Source scorecards/emit.ts:3889–3905 triggers the independent-audit dispatcher for any newly created non-audit card, including provisional cards, with fresh-judge fallback documented at3954; therefore no scorecard emission is safe under this exact kickoff's no additional/helper agents constraint. Do not self-audit, disable review, weaken the contract or issue a terminal/provisional card to route around it. Next permitted external action is a coordinator/owner resolution providing a compliant independent review route without this session launching helpers, or explicitly authorizing the platform's required independent-review recruitment. Product P-001–P-008 remain unstarted; prepare nothing else that bypasses admission.\nRelated: P-001, P-007\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"storewolf-architecture-interview-audit-2026-09-14","title":"Storewolf architecture audit, diagrams and interview guide","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Storewolf architecture audit, diagrams and interview guide\nslug: storewolf-architecture-interview-audit-2026-09-14\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-14\nupdated: 2026-09-14\n---\n## Now\nOwner approved direct solo AUTO execution. WI-10001433 holds audit and deliverable work.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Architecture audit.** Inventory the current Storewolf runtime, service boundaries, communication, persistence, deployment, auth, reliability, scaling and tests with code evidence and qualified uncertainties.\n\n**R-2 — Diagram.** Deliver checked component and workflow diagrams with source-backed edges and explicit external boundaries.\n\n**R-3 — Interview guide.** Deliver a truthful 90-second pitch, deeper walkthrough and likely follow-up answers without inventing personal contribution or throughput.\n\n**R-4 — Scope discipline.** Work directly on the approved old_node_fetch checkout as a read-only subject; preserve dirty files, never start services or mutate production, and save only report deliverables in the canonical Papercusp tree with locks.\n\n## Scope\nSubject: /home/marsh-office/storewolf-central-server. Storewolf is not registered as a managed harness and will not be added to one. Papercusp plan and work item are tracking only.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\nMajor claims and diagram edges cite source. Census distinguishes defined versus configured services. Risks state conditions and consequences. Diagram syntax and local file links are verified. Runtime deployment state is not claimed from historical snapshots.\n\n## Phase 1 — Audit and deliver\n- **P-001** `todo` Audit source, trace workflows, assess risks and deliver checked diagrams plus interview guide. Tracked by WI-10001433. — note: ← WI-10001433 released\n\n## Decisions\nDirect solo AUTO route approved. No fixes or production actions. Existing uncommitted changes are part of the audit snapshot."},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"work-queue-judging-and-cleanup-2026-09-14","title":"Work queue integrity and automatic judging plus evidence-backed cleanup","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Work queue integrity and automatic judging plus evidence-backed cleanup\nslug: work-queue-judging-and-cleanup-2026-09-14\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-14\nupdated: 2026-09-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** DRAFT FOR AVI'S REVIEW. No activation, implementation, live disposition, schedule/flag change, credential rerouting or fleet launch is authorized by drafting. Execution route, rollout authority and model/account/carry are unselected. Audit task: WI-10001252.\n\n**Objective:** Reduce genuine unresolved work and unnecessary report duplication through coherent intake, reliable admission, automatic judging PLUS safe automatic cleanup, and honest evidence-backed progress metrics.\n\n**Proposed approach:** Extend the existing admission/promoter/bulk/adjudication/lifecycle pipeline. Every eligible judgment reaches a validated, idempotent apply step and a verified outcome; ambiguous/protected cases remain visible for review. Begin with high-evidence repeated tool-error classes, then reconcile the full authorized backlog without discarding distinct obligations.\n\n**Separate source-limit plan:** source-limit-complete-access-2026-09-14 owns generic exact-summary/page/export/telemetry infrastructure, including queue read consumers. This plan consumes those contracts and owns DOMAIN identities, admission, cleanup and lifecycle flow. Intake and judgment work can proceed independently after approval. Full production reconciliation/measurement requires verified complete-access primitives from that plan or already-existing equivalent verified capabilities; do not copy generic code into a parallel queue reader.\n\n## Evidence and prior work\n\nAudit report: docs/audits/bug-queue-growth-audit-2026-09-13.md. Frozen 2026-09-14T00:55:51.702418Z inventory: 1,549 Papercusp and 166 other-project nonterminal non-observation bug rows. These are report rows, not an independently adjudicated unique-defect total. Recent drain closures are substantial; do not infer fleet failure from raw count alone.\n\nFindings to reverify at implementation: capture-core's bug path can omit admission, which is accepted as legacy NULL; unchanged tool failures split canonical identity on serving build changes; wrapped invalid_input/invalid_args messages reproduce structural misclassification; semantic screening can be unavailable; admission judging has frequently failed on measured usage limits while fail-open continues; historical completed bulk stages recorded zero merged rows despite decreasing candidate-pair counts. A disposition verdict is not proof of successful mutation. Prior exact counts/percentages are frozen evidence, never a future status claim.\n\nReuse the shipped work-queue-admission-and-bulk-dedup-2026-08-24, shipped change-queue-readiness-and-cleanup-parity-2026-09-05, implementation-complete/awaiting-acceptance work-queue-resolution-improvement-2026-08-31, and the existing work-queue-bulk-dedup-health rubric. Completed EI-22458055788060997 added shared live-row/evidence merge safeguards; preserve them. The original admission plan D-023 already covers claim/lease/park lifecycle cleanup. This plan is a new owner-directed integration/outcome effort, not a second implementation of those mechanisms. P-001 checks current code, deployed generation, tests, relevant decisions and live ownership before placing work.\n\n## Scope\n\nGeneric work-item domain behavior across supported kinds, scoped by the existing workspace/harness/policy system. Papercusp is the initial production pilot; no blanket cleanup of unrelated projects. Preserve the current non-P2P drain fleet's scope and leader. Do not change worker models or headcount, introduce another queue/cleanup daemon, perform P2P redesign, broadly approve pending work, weaken existing completion/claim guards or hard-delete records.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Coherent problem and occurrence identity.** Distinguish durable unresolved problem identity from report occurrence, build/version and reporter evidence. Unrelated deploys must not create a new canonical unresolved problem when the evidence describes the same root and remedy. Preserve different causes/remedies and explicit post-fix regression lineage. Coalesce concurrent reporters atomically and preserve producer aliases/redirects through merges. Merely stripping a build suffix or grouping same-text errors is insufficient.\n\n**R-2 — Correct error attribution.** Normalize nested tool wrappers while preserving the underlying tool/code/contract/location. A caller error does not become a structural bug because it passed through tools:invoke/code:run. Repeated failures prove recurrence, not necessarily product-defect validity. Preserve real infrastructure/transient/caller/schema/product distinctions and actionable follow-up without one incident per tool/build manifestation.\n\n**R-3 — Complete admission and readiness coverage.** Enumerate direct create, capture, watchdog, imports, plan promotion and observation-to-work promotion. Every newly runnable row receives an attributable pending, admitted or documented justified bypass state from one shared contract. Restrict legacy NULL to genuine legacy provenance. Duplicate judgment, current reproduction/existence, implementation readiness and human review are separate axes. Uncertain/degraded reports remain visible review debt with an accountable next step.\n\n**R-4 — Automatic judgment plus application.** Extend the existing pipeline to support retain/admit, duplicate merge, already-fixed closure, authoritative obsolete/superseded closure, reclassification, eligible recovered-alarm closure and defer/escalate. For approved safe classes, perform cleanup automatically after validation; do not stop at a report or require a human per eligible row. Existing merge application is reused, not falsely treated as absent. Every judgment records applied/no-change/deferred/invalidated/failed/rolled-back outcome and actual changed IDs.\n\n**R-5 — Sufficient evidence and explicit authority.** Similarity/title, age, missing recent reports, dead parker or model confidence alone cannot authorize cleanup. Same finding plus same remedy and preserved obligations permit duplicate consolidation. Already-fixed needs current positive evidence covering the remaining requirement. Obsolete/superseded needs an explicit authoritative retirement/replacement with no orphan obligation. Recovered alarms need a positive healthy probe and evidence the detector still runs. Misclassification preserves history and routes to the correct workload. Uncertain, protected, human-owned policy or product-value decisions defer.\n\n**R-6 — Race safety and recoverability.** Re-read current row/version, evidence, scope/origin, canonical survivor, active claims, hold-open leases, durable parks, review state, dependency graph and both reference directions at apply time. On drift, invalidate and rejudge; never force past the guard. Reuse canonical lifecycle writers, per-candidate idempotency and CAS with audited before-images. Preserve evidence/comments/occurrences/IDs/redirects/obligations. Implement/test per-action and per-batch undo with conflict detection, respecting later legitimate edits. Use the existing backup snapshot/restore mechanism before historical mutation stages. No hard-delete cleanup.\n\n**R-7 — Reliable judgment and apply execution.** Reuse managed routines/DBOS steps, durable bulk checkpoints, single ownership and the existing resource governor. Distinguish quota, transport, protocol, database and guard failures; bound retries and recover interrupted steps without repeating committed work. Keep model/account behavior within approved routing. Track last successful judge and last successful apply, not just last fire. A judge outage must never grant merge/closure authority; any existing work-availability fail-open remains explicitly unreviewed debt with re-review and cannot authorize cleanup. Do not starve valid emergency work or silently hide pending reports.\n\n**R-8 — Historical and incremental coverage.** Initial reconciliation covers the whole authorized nonterminal population through complete traversal and a stable cohort manifest, including no-similarity-signal records. Start with high-evidence clusters and use verified yield/quality to pace expansion. Incremental runs rejudge changed/new evidence rather than repeatedly rescan unchanged rows. Retain distinct cases and report every deferred/excluded/not-checked row. Reuse existing orphan/lease/park/review reconciliation; durable parks clear only on proven release predicates, not age/death, and unreachable or contested conditions escalate.\n\n**R-9 — Honest workload and throughput.** Distinguish occurrences, report rows, canonical problems, unverified/review debt, ready/active/blocked/human-only/out-of-lane stock, verified code fixes, cleanup exits and regressions. Reclassification must not hide the original workload. Extend existing lifecycle/audit writers to retain dated admissions/promotions, kind/lane/scope changes, closure/merge/reopen events needed for stock-flow reconciliation. Declare older-history gaps and membership attribution limits. Use the separate generic-source plan for complete counts, not capped lists. Pair decisions/census drops, applied cleanup and delivered fixes are different units.\n\n**R-10 — Independent safety and production outcome proof.** Test complete producer coverage, identity/wrapper regressions, distinct-root controls, wrong merges, false fixed/obsolete closes, detector blindness, source/build mismatch, live claims/parks, changed refs, concurrent applies, crash/replay and undo. Require an independent review plus a production canary with actual eligible mutations and after-state/undo evidence. New autonomous disposition authority starts in shadow until approved and proven; after enablement, approved safe cleanup is unattended. Maintain a stop switch that halts cleanup application without losing intake or stopping the drain.\n\n## Automatic disposition matrix\n\n| Judgment | Required basis | Result after policy approval |\n|---|---|---|\n| Distinct current work | Remaining problem/readiness evidence | Retain/admit; do not merge |\n| Duplicate | Same finding and remedy; preserved unique evidence/obligations; stable survivor | Merge, retain redirects/occurrences and reference integrity |\n| Already fixed | Current positive verification covering every remaining obligation | Close with verified evidence and implementation provenance |\n| Obsolete/superseded | Explicit retirement/replacement authority; no orphan obligation | Close with non-fix disposition and replacement link |\n| Misclassified | Underlying typed cause and justified target kind | Reclassify preserving history and workload accounting |\n| Recovered alarm | Positive health and detector-liveness coverage under existing eligible-source policy | Close alarm with recovery evidence, not by silence |\n| Uncertain/protected/drift/policy choice | Evidence or authority insufficient | Defer/escalate with reason and next action; no disposal |\n\n## Architecture and reuse\n\nUse capture-core, invocation-friction, tool-error-classifier, issue-occurrence-ledger, existing condition/admission identities, work-items admission predicates, promoter/census/adjudications/admission_runs, shared merge snapshots and guard validators, bulk checkpoints, lifecycle auto-close and durable-park reconciler. Extend the existing queue-health/rubric/notification surfaces. A common eligibility/apply contract covers online and historical paths. Any new durable surface requires evidence no existing owner fits.\n\nThe judge produces evidence-linked candidate actions against a snapshot; a deterministic validator authorizes only allowed actions on unchanged live state; canonical writers apply atomically/idempotently; verification checks preserved invariants and writes the causal outcome. Unknown is a first-class retained result. A failed apply cannot be reported as cleanup. Notifications summarize the recoverable batch, not every repeated occurrence.\n\n## Phase 1 — Reconcile and define\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Reverify the audit premises against current source/runtime and predecessor tests/decisions; enumerate producer and lifecycle owners, resolve live-work overlaps, freeze a pilot cohort and baseline, and finalize the evidence/authority/disposition matrix with source-plan interface mapping. Covers R-1 through R-10. importance: high\n\n## Phase 2 — Stop avoidable intake\n\n- **P-002** `todo` Repair nested error attribution and stable problem-versus-occurrence identity, with atomic coalescing, survivor aliases, per-build evidence and genuine regression lineage. Include identical-timeout/different-build and wrapped caller-error fixtures plus distinct-root controls. Covers R-1/R-2. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Unify admission/readiness stamps across all enumerated create/capture/watchdog/import/promotion paths; preserve justified bypasses and genuine legacy behavior while making degraded/unreviewed debt explicit and re-reviewable. Covers R-3/R-7. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n\n## Phase 3 — Judge and clean automatically\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Extend existing judgment and shared live-row guards with the approved disposition matrix, full current evidence, claim/hold/park/origin/review/reference protection and causal outcome records. Never count a proposal as an applied mutation. Covers R-4/R-5/R-6. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003 importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Implement guarded idempotent application for the additional cleanup dispositions through existing lifecycle writers, with audited before-images, per-action/batch conflict-safe undo, snapshot/restore integration and exact after-state verification. Preserve distinct obligations and later changes. Covers R-4/R-5/R-6. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` Integrate judging plus cleanup into existing managed recurring/bulk runners, with checkpointed stages, single ownership, authorized account/model handling, measured failure classes, debt alerts and separate judge/apply liveness. Fail-open never authorizes cleanup. Covers R-7/R-8/R-10. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Add dated domain lifecycle/stock-flow reconciliation and clear owner/fleet reporting for occurrences, review debt, work states, verified fixes, cleanup exits and regressions; consume the generic complete-summary/export contract. Cover no-signal backlog and existing park/lease reconciliation without duplicating their implementation. Covers R-8/R-9. blocked-by: P-003, P-005 importance: high\n\n## Phase 4 — Prove and enable\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Independently run adversarial safety/producer/identity/readiness/counting tests and crash/replay/undo drills. Verify full cohort access and generic-source-plan acceptance for required read paths, or explicitly proven equivalent existing primitives; wire that dependency before rollout. Produce no false disposal in the agreed safety battery and exact obligation/row accounting. Covers R-1 through R-10. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007 importance: high\n- **P-009** `todo` After explicit cleanup-policy approval and independent acceptance, snapshot and execute a small production canary with actual eligible mutations and tested undo; complete staged manifest-backed historical reconciliation, then enable unattended incremental judging plus cleanup only within approved scope. Record every retained/merged/fixed/obsolete/reclassified/deferred/excluded case. Covers R-4/R-6/R-7/R-8/R-10. blocked-by: P-008 importance: high\n- **P-010** `todo` Verify seven-day outcomes: exact stock/flow reconciliation, validated arrivals plus regressions versus verified fixes, actual cleanup yield, review-debt age, recurrence and false-disposal rates. If genuine defects still grow, name the measured producers/blockers and accountable follow-ups rather than weakening admission/evidence. Record final deployed lineage and operator runbook. Covers R-7/R-8/R-9/R-10. blocked-by: P-009 importance: high\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. All enumerated runnable producer routes stamp attributable admission or approved bypass; none silently mint unexplained legacy NULL. Uncertainty remains visible.\n2. Identical unresolved root/remedy across unrelated builds and concurrent reporters stays one canonical problem with preserved occurrences; genuine distinct roots/regressions remain separate. Wrapped caller errors classify correctly.\n3. Every automatic disposition meets the approved evidence/authority matrix and records an applied or non-applied outcome. Protected/changed rows, absent evidence and dead detectors cannot produce false closes.\n4. Crash/retry/undo preserves exactly-once effects, row versions, evidence, redirects, both reference directions and subsequent legitimate work; historical stages have recoverable snapshots and manifests.\n5. Independent production canary proves actual eligible cleanup and safety, not only code presence, smoke-test success, a judgment count or a lower candidate-pair census. Failed or blocked judges/actuators are reported distinctly.\n6. The initial authorized cohort is fully accounted for, including no-signal survivors and every deferred/excluded case. Complete-access proof is not derived from a capped response.\n7. Seven-day report reconciles dated stock/flow and separately reports verified fixes, cleanup, reclassifications and regressions with explicit coverage. Fewer report rows alone is not success. False disposal in the agreed adversarial suite is zero; observed production error triggers containment/undo/review rather than hidden reclassification.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — A successor, not a duplicate implementation\n\nPreviously returned overlap plans were read and are shipped/superseded. Preserve the existing shared merge/lifecycle safeguards and verified work. P-001 links continuing implementation where it exists; this new owner-requested plan owns newly measured gaps and integrated automatic outcomes.\n\n### D-002 — Judging plus cleanup is one governed pipeline\n\nAutomatic duplicate application already exists in part. Extend it to the listed evidence-backed lifecycle dispositions and prove actual outcomes; do not add a separate queue/daemon or pretend a model decision itself changed state.\n\n### D-003 — No metric-driven or merit-based disposal\n\nDo not merge merely by title/similarity, close by age/silence, clear parks by dead ownership, or relabel reports to make counts fall. Distinct remedies and human policy/value choices remain protected. Retain/defer is valid.\n\n### D-004 — Plan split and cross-plan dependency\n\nsource-limit-complete-access-2026-09-14 owns generic complete-access/count/export changes and cap telemetry. This plan owns domain intake/judgment/cleanup and dated lifecycle flows. P-008 requires verified complete read access before P-009, while intake fixes need not wait on unrelated generic adapters. Encode exact cross-plan dependencies at activation; no duplicate generic implementation.\n\n### D-005 — Review and enablement gates\n\nThis is a draft, not authority to execute. Before activation reread the full source conversation, map requirements/corrections, record activation audit, obtain Avi's approval and execution-route choice. Before production cleanup enablement, explicitly approve scopes/actions/routing and pass independent safety/canary/undo verification. Once enabled, eligible actions run automatically without a human per row. No schedule, fleet, account, model or cleanup flag is changed by authoring this plan.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"portal","plan_slug":"acceptance-portal-session-search-parity-2026-09-14","title":"Acceptance BAR — Portal session-search parity in Agents Running and universal search","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-14","owner":"su-52501ad8-65b2-40ad-a0b9-823cd1478be3","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Portal session-search parity in Agents Running and universal search\nslug: acceptance-portal-session-search-parity-2026-09-14\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-14\nupdated: 2026-09-19\nowner: su-52501ad8-65b2-40ad-a0b9-823cd1478be3\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Portal session-search parity in Agents Running and universal search\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"context-cost-detector-2026-09-15","title":"Context-cost detectors: make advertised-surface growth impossible to ship silently","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Context-cost detectors: make advertised-surface growth impossible to ship silently\nslug: context-cost-detector-2026-09-15\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-15\nupdated: 2026-09-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** The psu Claude seed regression (EI-23319364088969722) is FIXED and VERIFIED — 432,714 B -> 113,588 B on the wire (-73.7%, ~-116K tokens/turn), live on next `psu` launch. Two detectors shipped with it (name ratchet + wire-byte budget), both verified to actually fire via `test:affected`. DRAFT pending owner review: what remains is generalizing the detector beyond the one seed it currently guards.\n\n**Next:** Owner review of Phase 2. Then P-004 — extend the budget instrument to argSchema bytes catalog-wide (EI-23345472964244980), so per-tool schema growth is governed the way promptWeight already is.\n\n## Background\n\nOn 2026-09-11 psu Claude sessions went from ~151K to ~317K tokens of context on EVERY turn. Root cause chain:\n\n1. Claude Code defers tool schemas — it advertises names up front and fetches full JSON schemas on demand. **That deferral is implemented BY the ToolSearch tool.**\n2. psu denies ToolSearch by owner directive (one call measured +67,045 tokens, bypassing `applyResultDoor`'s ~1,500-token cap — a ~45x overshoot).\n3. Denying it silently also removed deferral, so every ADVERTISED tool began shipping its full argSchema every turn.\n4. That exposed a latent problem: the Claude seed was DERIVED from the weak-model OMP spine (48) + Claude extras (16) = 64 names = 432,714 B ~= 157K tokens. The model best able to drive `tools:invoke` was receiving the largest up-front surface.\n\n**Why nobody caught it for four days** — this is what the detectors must address:\n\n- Each of the 64 seed names was added individually, with genuine demand evidence, and each was individually defensible. **Nothing ever measured the aggregate.** Per-item justification with no total is not a budget, and it drifts in one direction only.\n- The existing weight instrument measures the WRONG HALF. `npm run tool-weight` / `tool-guidance-budget.ts` govern promptWeight (description + guidance, 1,500 chars/tool). Cost is dominated by argSchema, which they do not look at: `coord:send` is ~1.2K of guidance and 39,254 B of schema. A tool sits inside the prompt-weight budget and still costs 30-40 KB per turn.\n- There was no signal on first-turn size at all.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- R1. Growth in the ADVERTISED surface must fail a build, not be noticed by a human weeks later.\n- R2. The detector must catch BOTH doors: more names seeded, and a seeded tool's schema growing with no seed change.\n- R3. Detectors must be validated against the incident they were built for. A detector that cannot reproduce the known 09-11 step is not evidence, however principled it looks.\n- R4. Every guard needs a falsifiability control and a plausibility FLOOR. Every assertion here is an upper bound, and an upper bound is satisfied trivially by a broken instrument.\n- R5. No capability may be removed to buy bytes. Unseeded must mean one `tools:find`/`tools:invoke` round-trip, never unreachable.\n- R6. Budgets are raised only with a fresh measurement recorded beside the constant — a deliberate per-turn cost decision, never a quiet append.\n\n## Design\n\n**Substrate: the tools/list WIRE payload.** Deterministic, causal, zero-noise, measurable in-repo from the same projected catalog the server renders (`packages/agent-mcp/src/server.ts:758` builds each entry as `{name, description, inputSchema: sanitizeToolSchema(advertised)}`). `listAllProjectedTools()` from `@papercusp/tooldef` is the in-repo equivalent, already trusted by `tool-guidance-budget.ts`.\n\n**Rejected substrate: `harness_shared.agent_usage_samples`.** The natural place to watch first-turn size CANNOT see this class: `turn_count` is NULL and rows are periodic CUMULATIVE snapshots, and the population mixes every anthropic session in the workspace. The best available proxy (first sample where `cache_read_tokens=0` -> `input + cache_creation`) was validated against the known 09-11 step and FAILED: n=1-5 boots/day, medians swinging 82K / 770K / 104K, no visible step. A threshold alarm there would have fired all through August and still missed the real event. Do not rebuild it.\n\n**Two doors, two guards, each verified to fire under `test:affected`:**\n\n| door | guard | selected when |\n|---|---|---|\n| seed gains a name | `CLAUDE_MINIMAL_SEED_MAX_NAMES` ratchet (`apps/operator/lib/psu-launcher.test.ts`) | a `psu-launcher.mjs` edit selects `apps/operator` |\n| a seeded tool's schema grows | `claude-seed-wire-budget.test.ts` (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/`) | a tool-definition edit selects `operator-core` (`test:lane-pure`/`test:lane-stateful`) |\n\n**Instrument caveat, recorded so it cannot mislead:** the in-repo projection reads ~20% LOW versus the wire (90,869 B vs 113,588 B for the same 31 names) because it skips the server's late entity-enum/sanitize passes. Compare in-repo numbers to in-repo numbers only.\n\n## Phase 1 — shipped 2026-09-15\n\n- **P-001** `done` Give Claude its own minimal seed: `CLAUDE_MINIMAL_SEED_TOOL_NAMES` (31 names) replaces the derived spine+extras (64), behind a `PAPERCUSP_CLAUDE_FULL_SEED` escape hatch that restores the old seed byte-identically. `ompCoreToolNames` untouched. Measured 432,714 B -> 113,588 B.\n- **P-002** `done` Ratchet the seed size: `CLAUDE_MINIMAL_SEED_MAX_NAMES` + regrowth guard, heavy-denylist guard, reachability guard, MCP-name-shape guard, and a falsifiability CONTROL.\n- **P-003** `done` Wire-byte budget guard measuring projected argSchema bytes, with a plausibility floor, a vacuous-catalog floor, a name-resolution guard, and a CONTROL proving it fires.\n\n## Phase 2 — remaining coverage\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Extend the budget instrument to argSchema bytes catalog-wide (EI-23345472964244980): a second tier in `tool-guidance-budget.ts` expressed in WIRE BYTES, with the same soft-ratchet / hard-cap / grandfather shape promptWeight already uses. importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Make `npm run tool-weight` report BOTH halves (promptWeight and argSchema bytes), so an author trimming a tool sees which half is actually heavy. Today it reports the half that usually is not.\n- **P-006** `todo` Give the OMP/codex seed (`OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES`, 48 names) a wire budget too. Those models cannot drive `tools:invoke`, so the remedy there is likely a per-tool schema cap rather than a smaller seed. blocked-by: P-004\n- **P-007** `todo` Quantify and decide the non-papercusp tool blocks (claude natives, claude-in-chrome). `PAPERCUSP_TOOLS` scopes only the papercusp-su server, so these are outside its reach entirely; per D-003 a deny flag does NOT reclaim an MCP server's bytes. importance: high\n- **P-008** `todo` Decide whether a first-turn size signal is worth building on a CORRECT substrate (per-turn telemetry that does not exist today), or whether the build-time guards above are sufficient. Default assumption: sufficient.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 The detector is a build-time guard, not a runtime alarm\n\nMeasured: the runtime substrate cannot support one. `agent_usage_samples` is cumulative-snapshot shaped and its population is contaminated; the proxy failed validation against the known 09-11 regression (n=1-5 boots/day, medians 82K/770K/104K, no step). The wire payload is deterministic and causal, so the signal belongs at the source. A guard that fails a build has no threshold to tune and no false-positive rate.\n\n### D-002 Unseeding is the preferred remedy, not schema-shrinking\n\nA seeded tool is paid for on EVERY turn of EVERY session, forever; an unseeded one costs a single `tools:find`/`tools:invoke` round-trip. This inverts only because ToolSearch is denied — so papercusp's OWN discovery (`tools:find` searches the full ~900-tool catalog and activates matches) is what makes the trim safe, and it is unaffected by the ToolSearch deny. That is the specific difference from the EI-9011 / WI-37534 cuts that hurt.\n\n### D-003 An `mcp__*` entry in `--disallowedTools` buys ZERO bytes\n\nMEASURED, not inferred: in the 2026-09-15 capture `mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate` was denied by the identical token and its schema stayed in the body verbatim. Denying a NATIVE tool DOES strip its schema (denying `Artifact` moved a captured body 871,924 -> 822,141 B). To drop an MCP server's schemas you must stop LOADING the server. Do not propose a deny flag as a way to shrink an MCP block.\n\n### D-004 — Drop claude-in-chrome from AGENT sessions via psu-scoped --strict-mcp-config, not by touching the owner's config\nDate: 2026-09-15\n[owner:aviynw8 2026-09-15] Owner directive, given interactively after being shown the fork: \"disable the claude-in-chrome tool blocks\", resolved to the psu-scoped lever.\n\nMEASURED CONTEXT. claude-in-chrome costs ~26,029 B / 22 tools (~9.5K tokens per turn) — a CARRIED figure from a predecessor's captured wire body, NOT independently re-measured; that instrument read ~12% lower than this session's live tools/list on the same 64-name seed (380,207 vs 432,714 B), so treat it as order-of-magnitude until a fresh capture confirms it.\n\nWHY NOT A DENY FLAG. Settled by D-003: an `mcp__*` entry in --disallowedTools reclaims ZERO bytes (measured — `mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate` was denied and its schema stayed in the body verbatim). To drop an MCP server's schemas you must stop LOADING the server.\n\nWHY NOT THE USER-LEVEL KEY. `~/.claude.json` carries `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled: true` + `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled: true`, and the CLI auto-attaches the server from there — psu passes no --chrome and no --mcp-config (argv verified on three live psu sessions). Flipping that key WOULD work and is one line, but it is the owner's PERSONAL Claude Code config: it would disable Chrome automation for their own interactive sessions, not just agents. Rejected for blast radius.\n\nDECISION. Add `--mcp-config <papercusp-su only>` + `--strict-mcp-config` to the psu CLAUDE SU launch (suLaunchArgs). Strict mode loads ONLY the named servers, so chrome and every other user-level server drop for AGENT sessions while the owner's own client is untouched. This deliberately narrows the D-005 \"su keeps its FULL toolkit — every user server loads\" choice to agents only; D-005's other half (no --mcp-config because it would DOUBLE the user-level papercusp-su) does not apply under strict mode, which ignores user-level servers rather than merging them.\n\nMANDATORY PRE-SHIP VERIFICATION — this is the risky half and must not be skipped. Under strict mode the user-level papercusp-su is NO LONGER loaded, so the supplied config must fully define it or psu sessions lose papercusp entirely. Two specific hazards: (1) the user-level URL relies on `${PAPERCUSP_SID}` env-expansion — if --mcp-config files do not env-expand, the launcher must write a per-session file with the SID already resolved (precedent: writeOmpSessionConfigDirAsync does exactly this for omp), or every write lands under an anonymous `mcp-call-*` identity (EI-8509); (2) the bearer token must be carried. Verify on a throwaway `claude -p` through the :9074 capture tap and confirm from the CAPTURED BODY — not a model self-report (the NATIVE_TOOL_SEARCH_DENY_FLAG docblock's standard) — that papercusp-su tools are present AND no `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` schema remains. The same capture yields the verified byte saving that replaces the carried 26,029 B estimate.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-005 — SUPERSEDES D-004 — drop claude-in-chrome with the CLI's own --no-chrome flag; --strict-mcp-config was both ineffective and dangerous\nDate: 2026-09-15\nD-004 is SUPERSEDED. Read this instead; do not implement D-004's plan.\n\nSHIPPED: `NO_CHROME_FLAG = \"--no-chrome\"` threaded into all three psu claude paths in psu-launcher.mjs (the sites already carrying NATIVE_DEADWEIGHT_DENY_FLAG: role, suLaunchArgs, resume). Verified from the BUILT argv rather than the source — suLaunchArgs('claude') ends [..., NATIVE_DEADWEIGHT_DENY_FLAG, \"--no-chrome\"]; omp and codex branches untouched. Tests 804/0 after updating the pinned argv arrays; lint:tsc clean on both legs.\n\nWHY D-004 WAS WRONG, on both counts:\n\n(a) INEFFECTIVE. claude-in-chrome is NOT a configured MCP server. `claude mcp list` returns ONLY papercusp-su; the CLI attaches Chrome from the paired extension (`claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled` + `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` in ~/.claude.json). `--strict-mcp-config` filters CONFIGURED servers, so it could never have removed chrome — it would have changed nothing about the 22 tools / 28,499 B it was aimed at.\n\n(b) DANGEROUS. Strict mode ALSO stops loading the user-level papercusp-su, which every psu session depends on — psu deliberately passes no --mcp-config precisely BECAUSE that server is user-level (see suLaunchArgs' comment and D-005 of the identities plan). So it risked stranding the entire papercusp surface to fix nothing, with the SID-env-expansion and bearer hazards D-004 itself flagged as \"the risky half\".\n\nWHAT ACTUALLY WORKS: `--no-chrome` is a first-class CLI switch — \"Disable Claude in Chrome integration\" (verified in `claude --help`, Claude Code 2.1.268). It is per-launch, so it satisfies the owner's real constraint exactly: AGENT sessions lose Chrome, the owner's own interactive sessions keep it. No config of the owner's is touched, and none of strict mode's blast radius applies.\n\nUNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: D-003 stands — an `mcp__*` entry in --disallowedTools reclaims ZERO bytes (measured: `mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate` was denied and its schema stayed in the captured body verbatim). And the user-level toggle remains correctly rejected for blast radius.\n\nPROCESS LESSON, recorded because it is the third instance in one session: the correct lever was already written down in the CLI's own `--help`, and I designed two wrong ones before reading it. The same thing happened earlier with the disk-space-alarm docblock and the ToolSearch-deny docblock — each already contained the answer being re-derived. Read the help/docblock of the thing you are about to engineer around BEFORE designing around it.\n\nALSO RECORDED so nobody re-measures: chrome = 22 tools / 28,499 B of a 113-tool captured wire body (papercusp-su 397,655 B, natives 59,280 B), ~10.4K tokens per turn. And a `claude -p` probe through the :9074 tap returned PROBE_OK but wrote NO new capture (11 files before, 11 after) — it did not route through the proxy, so that run was a model self-report and was discarded rather than cited as evidence.\nRelated: P-007\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"reports-library-2026-09-15","title":"Reports library — a built-in home for owner-facing audits/reports with publish, browse and search","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Reports library — a built-in home for owner-facing audits/reports with publish, browse and search\nslug: reports-library-2026-09-15\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-15\nupdated: 2026-10-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Reports remains UNSHIPPED. WI-6554700010013549 preparation repaired four independent clauses to revision2, added eleven Conformance falsifiers copied exactly from rubric7, and a source-backed nine-scenario Product shaping brief (ready-for-review; semantic acceptance unmeasured). Current3170 activation preview passes; exact quality hash ffc67a5ebce49e482b57d3b5eae5ec69776271edad5c6b5f66ab05829f345802 still fails only canonical R2/R11 coupling. Clean committed384986 tests92PASS (ledger21247377/21247378); initial working-tree pass remains drifted. Canonical rubric7/BAR set preserved. WI10007208 remains live-owned by su-f146f0a3 for acceptance/final artifact; no independent reviewer or release-gate operation launched.\n\n**Next:** su-f146f0a3 on WI10007208 reconciles exact native/realPG/model receipts and current rubric7 vetting; preparation WI-6554700010013549 is blocked at outside-lineage R2/R11 atomization/review under Avi's no-more-agents boundary. Resolve that route boundary before a review launch, then repair only through canonical rubrics tools and fresh exact quality/activation evidence; preserve immutable proof and final-release-only R11.\n\n## Background\n\n**The ask** [owner:Avi, Codex session su-fc0a87ca, 2026-09-14 11:46]: \"We're creating a lot of audits/reports … meant to be read by me, not necessarily about our system, unlike runbooks … make this report/audit functionality a built in papercusp feature and provide a tab where users can search and browse through all prior audits.\"\n\n**What exists today (measured 2026-09-15):**\n- `harness_shared.harness_text_artifacts` (`harness_slug, rel_path, content, updated_at, workspace_id`) behind `packages/operator-core/lib/text-artifacts.ts` and the `artifacts:save` tool (`packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/artifacts/save.ts`). A raw generated-text store: no title/summary/subject/visibility/lineage, keyed by pot + path. Not searchable as a first-class corpus.\n- `harness_shared.pot_reports` — **a moderation table** (`reporter_github_user_id`, `target_kind/ref`, `report_reason`, `status open`; writer `lib/hive-reports-store.ts`). Same word, unrelated concept. The new relation must not collide with it.\n- Harness docs (`harness_docs` / `/internal/docs`) — pot-scoped, code-drift + regeneration semantics; correct home for runbooks/knowledge, wrong home for a deliverable written FOR a person ABOUT something possibly outside the pot.\n- Chat report cards: `coord:send { report: ReportBlock }` renders a 📋 card (`apps/operator/app/_components/chat/ReportBlockCard.tsx`) — an ephemeral, inbox-only report surface.\n- Audit-mode verdicts, plan acceptance scorecards/verdicts, curation state-of-pot outputs — all \"reports for Avi\" living in messages, plan decisions, or scorecard rows.\n- claude.ai Artifacts — account-scoped, deletable, un-indexed, invisible to every papercusp read path (insight doc: *an artifact is a rendering, never a deliverable's only home*).\n- Search: hybrid lexical+semantic engine in `libs/generic/search` (legs/hybrid), source kinds registered in `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/search/sources.ts` (e.g. `session_turn`, `work_item`, docs); embeddings per `lib/search/prose-vector-dims.ts`; coverage gate in `lib/search/coverage-gate.ts`.\n- UI: operator-vite, TanStack file routes (`apps/operator-vite/src/routes/*.tsx`, `routes/admin/*.tsx`, generated `routeTree.gen.ts`); all data via `@papercusp/sync` (`useSyncQuery` + resolver entries in `packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts`, `notifySyncInvalidate` after writes); markdown+mermaid rendering exists in `apps/operator/app/_components/MarkdownEditor.tsx`.\n\n**The two design points carried from the earlier discussion:** (1) a report can be *created in* one pot, be *about* something else entirely, and be *private to the owner* — origin, subject and visibility are three separate fields, never one pot assignment doing all three jobs; (2) the browse tab is only valuable if there is ONE write path agents reliably use — capture is the hard problem, not the tab.\n\n## Product shaping\n\nThis retrospective brief maps the recorded owner request and existing plan decisions to user scenarios. It changes no accepted requirement, implementation route or evidence boundary. Preserve per-run evidence and distinguish local/current-build proof from final deployed proof.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Storage — one new relation, not a fourth text store\nMigration (number from `node scripts/next-migration.mjs --name report-library --intent …`, written at the `.DRAFT` path, armed when tested): `harness_shared.report_library` —\n`workspace_id, report_id (ulid, pk with workspace_id), title, summary, body_md, kind (audit|review|analysis|postmortem|status-digest|proposal|other), subject_kind, subject_ref, subject_label, origin_harness_slug, author_owner_id, author_session_ref, visibility (owner|pot|workspace), supersedes_report_id, lineage_id (root report_id, self for a root), source (agent|backfill|adapter:<name>), tags text[], published_at, updated_at, retired_at` + indexes on `(workspace_id, published_at desc)`, `(workspace_id, lineage_id, published_at desc)`, `(workspace_id, subject_kind, subject_ref)`, and a trigram/tsvector index on `title||summary` for the lexical leg. Chunk embeddings in `harness_shared.report_library_chunks (workspace_id, report_id, chunk_idx, text, embedding)` following the `doc_sections.embedding` convention (`prose-vector-dims.ts`). Body inline (text): reports are documents, not blobs; `harness_text_artifacts` stays what it is. Name avoids `pot_reports` (moderation) and `telemetry_reports`.\n\n### Store + tools\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/report-library.ts` — `publishReport`, `getReport`, `listReports` (filters + lineage collapse), `retireReport`, `visibleTo(callerCtx)` predicate used by every read; no module-scoped state.\n- Tool group `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/reports/`: `publish.ts`, `get.ts`, `list.ts`, `search.ts`, `retire.ts`, imported from `agent-tools/index.ts`, each with `guidance { when, notWhen, chaining }` kept light (`npm run tool-weight`). `reports:publish` stamps origin from ctx (never caller-supplied), validates size/kind/subject, computes `lineage_id` from `supersedes`, writes chunks + embeddings (async, non-blocking on the write), emits `report:published:<id>` (registered in `events:catalog`), calls `notifySyncInvalidate`.\n\n### Search\nRegister `report` in `agent-tools/search/sources.ts` (lexical over title/summary/body, semantic over chunks); `scope.ts` accepts `report`; coverage gate learns the new corpus. Embedder reused from `search/embedder.ts`.\n\n### Sync + UI (operator-vite)\n- Resolvers `reports.list` (filters, cursor) and `reports.get` in `sync-resolver/index.ts`; `notifySyncInvalidate('reports')` after publish/retire.\n- Route `apps/operator-vite/src/routes/reports.tsx` (top-level, sibling of `plans.tsx`; owner-facing, so NOT under `/admin`) + nav entry (the `settings-nav-route-coverage` test enforces registration). nuqs keys: `kind`, `subject`, `pot`, `vis`, `q`, `tag`, `since`, `sel` (report id), `hist` (lineage open). Reader reuses the existing markdown+mermaid renderer in read-only mode; metadata strip; supersedes prev/next; \"copy as markdown\".\n- Design-phase check first: `design-phase.search_registry` for list/reader/filter-bar components before hand-rolling anything; tokens from the DTCG set.\n\n### Capture\n- Persona rule (edit the authored `su.md` practice tile, regenerate its derived part via the existing `gen:su-decomposition` writer, then verify a fresh sealed Codex AUTO launch-context render via `composeSuStackSource` and `renderSuPlaybook`; see D-025).\n- Adapters: audit-mode wind-down → `reports:publish { kind:'audit', subject: the audited program }`; acceptance verdict (`scorecards:emit { acceptance }`) → `kind:'review'`, subject the plan; `coord:send { report }` → persisted as `status-digest` with the ReportBlock rendered to markdown (card keeps working; the library is the durable copy).\n- Turn-end detector: extend the existing turn-end observation harvest to flag an unpublished report-shaped turn (heading + ≥ N chars + audit/report/review title) — files an observation, never blocks.\n- Backfill: a one-shot `scripts/backfill-reports.mts` that reads the named turns from the session-turn store and publishes them with `source:'backfill'` and the original session ref as `author_session_ref`.\n\n### Non-goals (this plan)\nNo comments/annotations on reports, no export-to-PDF, no per-report ACL beyond the three visibilities, no editing a published body (publish a superseding report instead), no federation egress (reports stay hive-private; `shareable` can come later).\n\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-003, P-008 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006, P-008 | live |\n| R-5 | P-009, P-010 | live |\n| R-6 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-002, P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014 | live |\n| R-9 | P-006, P-010 | live |\n| R-10 | P-002, P-003, P-008, P-009, P-010 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-004 | live |\n| R-12 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-004 | live |\n| R-16 | P-004 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Storage + tools\n- **P-001** `done` Migration `report_library` + `report_library_chunks` via the atomic allocator; tests. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-10007245 completed (done)\n- **P-013** `done` Turn-end detector for unpublished report-shaped turns → observation (never blocking); test with a fixture turn. blocked-by: P-011 — note: ← WI-10007262 completed (done)\n- **P-014** `done` Backfill script + run: the Storewolf architecture and transformer-service audits from session su-fc0a87ca (and any other named audits Avi lists) published with `source:'backfill'`. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-10007276 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 5 — Acceptance + ship\n- **P-015** `todo` Per-item code-truth audit (`plans:audit` with code/test citations), acceptance rubric proposed + vetted, independent non-lineage grader, implementer verdict, `plans:set-plan-status shipped`. blocked-by: P-010 blocked-by: P-012 blocked-by: P-014\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Origin, subject and visibility are three independent fields\nDate: 2026-09-15\nA report is CREATED IN one pot (origin: harness_slug + author ownerId + session ref, server-stamped), is ABOUT something that may be entirely outside that pot (subject: typed kind + ref + label, incl. `external` for things like storewolf/transformer-service), and is SHOWN TO a chosen audience (visibility: owner | pot | workspace, default owner). No single pot assignment does all three jobs — that is exactly the semantics harness docs lack (docs are pot-scoped by construction). Carried from the 2026-09-14 Codex discussion [owner:Avi framing; agent proposal], adopted here as the core schema rule.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Own relation `harness_shared.report_library`; do not overload text_artifacts, docs, or pot_reports\nDate: 2026-09-15\nMeasured 2026-09-15: `harness_text_artifacts` is (harness_slug, rel_path, content, updated_at, workspace_id) — no title/summary/subject/visibility/lineage, so every report field would have to be smuggled into rel_path or a side table. `harness_shared.pot_reports` is the moderation table (reporter_github_user_id, target_kind/ref, report_reason, status) — same word, unrelated concept; the new name must not collide with it (hence `report_library`, not `reports`). Harness docs carry code-drift/regeneration semantics that are wrong for a deliverable written for a person. Reuse-first still holds for everything AROUND the row: embedder, hybrid search legs, coverage gate, sync-resolver, markdown+mermaid renderer, ReportBlock cards are all reused, not re-implemented.\nRelated: P-001, P-005, P-006, P-009\n\n### D-003 — Capture is the load-bearing half — the tab is empty without one write path\nDate: 2026-09-15\nThe Storewolf and transformer-service audits from the very session that asked for this feature exist only as chat text: the information was produced, nobody routed it. So the plan treats capture as a first-class phase, not a follow-up: (a) a persona rule that owner-facing deliverables go through `reports:publish`; (b) adapters that auto-publish the report-shaped outputs the system ALREADY produces (audit-mode verdicts, acceptance verdicts, `coord:send { report }` cards); (c) a turn-end detector that files an observation (never blocks) when a report-shaped turn ends unpublished; (d) a one-time backfill of the known audits. A browse tab shipped without Phase 4 would be judged a failure of this plan even with every UI item done.\nRelated: P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014\n\n### D-004 — Supersedes lineage instead of in-place edits; retire is soft\nDate: 2026-09-15\nAudits get redone. A re-done audit is published with `supersedes: <prior id>`; `lineage_id` is the root report's id; the list collapses to latest-per-lineage with history one click away. A published body is never edited in place (publish a superseding report) and never deleted (`retired_at`), so a citation to a report id stays resolvable forever.\nRelated: P-002, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-005 — Reports are a registered search source, not a tab-local search\nDate: 2026-09-15\nRegister `report` in `agent-tools/search/sources.ts` + `scope.ts` so the Reports tab's search box and `search:semantic` / `search:fulltext { scope:['report'] }` read ONE corpus; chunk embeddings computed on publish via the existing embedder and reported through the existing coverage gate, so a thin/unembedded index says so instead of silently returning nothing.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-006 — Top-level /reports route in operator-vite, all state in nuqs, existing renderer reused\nDate: 2026-09-15\nOwner-facing, so a top-level `routes/reports.tsx` sibling of `plans.tsx` — not under `/admin`. Every filter, the selected report and the lineage-open state live in the URL via nuqs (`kind, subject, pot, vis, q, tag, since, sel, hist`) so agents can drive the tab through ui:get_state / ui:dispatch. Data only via @papercusp/sync (`reports.list` / `reports.get` resolvers + notifySyncInvalidate on publish/retire). The reader reuses the markdown+mermaid renderer already in the tree (read-only mode) rather than a new one; a design-phase registry check precedes any new component.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-007 — Visibility is enforced at the store read, per caller; owner default\nDate: 2026-09-15\n`visibleTo(callerCtx)` is one predicate every read path (tools, sync resolvers) goes through: an agent sees `workspace` reports, `pot` reports of its own pot, and its own authored reports; `owner` reports are visible only to the human owner (UI) and their author. Default visibility is `owner` because the ask is reports 'meant to be read by me'. No per-report ACL beyond the three levels in this plan.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-009\n\n### D-008 — Flag `reportsLibrary` ships default ON\nDate: 2026-09-15\nPer the flags policy: finished work sets the code default ON and is verified live in the same task. Nothing here is irreversible, outward-facing, or security-bearing, so it is not a dark-flag candidate.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-009 — Route A (in-session implementation) chosen by the owner; the two open design questions take their proposed defaults\nDate: 2026-09-15\n[owner:Avi, interactive turn 2026-09-15, reply \"A\" to the route question] The owner approved the plan and chose route A — this su session (su-4dbc7355) implements it directly, no fleet. The plan moves draft → active.\n\nThe two questions raised alongside the summary went unanswered in that reply, so each takes the default I recommended, recorded here so a later reader sees they were CHOSEN rather than overlooked, and both are cheap to reverse:\n- Default visibility stays `owner` (private to the owner). Rationale: the ask was reports \"meant to be read by me\". Changing the default later is a one-line change plus a backfill UPDATE; per-report visibility is settable at publish regardless.\n- P-014 backfill scope stays the two audits named in the plan (Storewolf architecture + transformer-service, session su-fc0a87ca). The backfill script takes a list, so adding more later is an argument, not a rewrite.\n\nIf the owner answers either question differently while the work is in flight, amend this decision rather than silently switching.\nRelated: P-004, P-009, P-014\n\n### D-010 — Agent sessions never hold owner authority on the reports:* surface — the UI lane owns the human-owner path\nDate: 2026-09-15\n`resolveViewer()` in `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/reports/_shared.ts` hardcodes `isOwner: false` for EVERY caller of the agent tool group, including superuser and power-user sessions.\n\nWhy: `ReportViewer.isOwner` means *the human owner*, and it is a total bypass — `visibleTo` returns `sql\\`TRUE\\`` for it. Essentially every caller of the agent surface is an agent, so honouring an agent's superuser flag here would make `owner` visibility mean nothing at all: the least-visible tier would be readable by any su session in the workspace.\n\nWHAT THIS BINDS ON THE UI LANE (P-006/P-007): the Reports tab is the human owner's surface and MUST construct its own viewer with `isOwner: true` rather than reusing `resolveViewer`. If the UI composes the agent-side helper, the owner will silently NOT see their own `owner`-visibility reports (they would see only workspace-visible ones plus anything they authored) — a missing-data bug that looks like an empty library, not like a permission error.\n\nNote the one case that already works without the bypass: an author can always read back its own `owner`-visibility report, because `visibleTo` grants `author_owner_id = <viewer>` unconditionally.\n\nMeasured: `visibleTo()` at packages/operator-core/lib/report-library.ts returns `sql\\`TRUE\\`` when `viewer.isOwner`; `resolveViewer()` returns `{ isOwner: false, ownerId, potSlug }`. Pinned by reports.test.ts — 'never claims owner authority for an agent session', which passes `isSuperuser:true, isPowerUser:true` and asserts the viewer handed to the store still has `isOwner:false`.\nRelated: P-003, P-006\n\n### D-011 — reports:retire is author-only — write authority is deliberately narrower than the R-7 read matrix\nDate: 2026-09-15\nR-7 governs who may READ a report. It says nothing about who may retire one, and reusing it as the write rule would let any agent in a pot retire a peer's `pot`-visible report, or any agent at all retire a `workspace`-visible one.\n\n`reports:retire` therefore applies its own narrower rule: you may retire a report you AUTHORED (`origin.author_owner_id === ctx.ownerId`). The check is two-stage so it cannot be used to probe which report ids exist:\n  1. resolve through the store's viewer gate — not visible => `not_found` (the same answer reports:get gives);\n  2. only then compare authorship — visible but not yours => `not_author`.\n\nRetirement stays SOFT regardless: the row keeps its body and still resolves by id, so a citation never breaks (R-3). There is no hard delete anywhere in the group.\n\nThe intended alternative for a non-author who thinks a report is wrong is `reports:publish { supersedes }`, which corrects it while keeping the correction visible as history — a better outcome than withdrawal in almost every case.\n\nOPEN FOR A LATER LANE: this grants no override to the human owner (who today acts through the UI, not this tool group). If the Reports tab needs an owner-retires-anything action, it is a deliberate widening to decide there, not an oversight here.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/reports/retire.ts stages the checks in that order; pinned by reports.test.ts — 'refuses not_author for a VISIBLE report the caller did not write' asserts `retireReport` is NOT called, and 'an invisible report is not_found' asserts the same.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-012 — Reports reuse shared chunk registry and server-bound search source\nDate: 2026-10-07\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/search/chunks/registry.ts provides shared text_chunks storage, automatic sweep/coverage registration; migration 1166's report_library_chunks has no updated_at and has no writer in current source. P-005 uses existing text_chunks with a report surface rather than introducing a dedicated adapter/migration. Publish synchronizes and embeds this report's chunks; existing background sync/sweep recovers failed indexing. The unused legacy table remains untouched. Search sources compose store visibleTo at SQL reads; tool handlers bind ReportViewer exclusively from ctx, never args or the author-filter bag. Direct internal registry consumers default to workspace-visible reports. This keeps generic search types domain-neutral.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-013 — Capture adapters reuse author-scoped report publication keys and series tags\nDate: 2026-10-07\nMeasured current report-library.ts publish path always INSERTs a new row and exposes no request identity. P-012 requires idempotency per capture source. Extend the existing report_library row with optional request_key, unique within workspace+author. Expose request_key on reports:publish for the same retry-safe path used by adapters; same key with changed content is a structured conflict rather than a silent different report. Daily editions keep separate lineages; corrections alone supersede. Reuse existing tags for series browsing at /reports?tag=<tag>, newest first, and return exact-edition /reports?sel=<id> citations. Source-derived capture keys bind the event/run ref and author rather than caller-supplied provenance. No new publisher/table/system is introduced.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-014 — Native operation retries share a host-verified publication namespace\nDate: 2026-10-08\nMeasured operation-agent-placement.ts generates a fresh agent_launch_owner_id for each attempt, so D-013 author-scoped keys cannot deduplicate a retry across workers. Extend the existing report_library request-key index with an optional server-only request_scope. Ordinary publication stays workspace+author scoped. Native workers derive a stable operation scope from the host-applied operation binding after checking the canonical work-item pin and current claim; unavailable or mismatched binding is refused. Actual author/session provenance remains that of the original immutable report. Reuse operation-worker-binding admission and existing report_library publisher; no separate publication table or service.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-015 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-08\nAmendment-Id: reports-bar-contracts-4375-v3\nRequest-Hash: 3f8ef826b93fe3505e0fbef1e61b157664bc09d85d2c71e491381e4b7fc65a5d\nActor: su-4375e570-0ffb-4d0f-8652-9d23635c5fe9\nReason: Complete missing methods/checks and name their measured unit/integration layers for existing BARs. its P-001 belongs to the live gate owner), then run P-006..P… <!-- P-020 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001492 — Ship test-suite-recovery-2026-08-27: P-004 canonical exact-repairHead run once the gate is green (D-028), then rebuild the 8-BAR acceptance chain (re-vet, hash reconcile, proof, independent grading, … <!-- P-021 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001493 — Ship the original tracker ship-main-greening-plans-2026-08-29: after P-021, reconcile P-002 against the consolidated child mapping, then complete its own audit/rubric/independent grading and author verdict <!-- P-022 -->\n## Background\n\nThe Sep-12 relevance audit (docs/evidence/main-greening-plan-relevance-audit-2026-09-12.md, committed b95853141c) classified 35 main-greening plans as Keep / Revise / Consolidate / Historical / Redesign-draft and its dispositions were adopted as Decisions on four plans the same day. Ten plans remain non-shipped (most all-items-terminal but never carried through the two-family completion gate). The owner directed AUTO and asked that every one be carried to `status: shipped` under that audit. This program is the tracker: one item per plan, plus the adoption tracker and the one defect the audit filed.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Truthful terminal disposition and residual accounting for all ten plans.** The ten plans in D-001 have their owner-approved D-019 dispositions truthfully recorded: three non-consolidated plans are shipped through their own code-truth audit, vetted rubric, outside-lineage grade and author verdict without force waiver; seven source plans are superseded into this program with exact residual carriers and no claim of independent shipment. The four dropped carrier acceptance chains P-012, P-015, P-021 and P-022 are explicitly not achieved, and any remaining substantive residual or unmatched work-item must be accounted for before this program can ship.\n\n**R-2 — Sep-12 dispositions are applied, not merely recorded.** Every Revise/Consolidate disposition in the audit's primary table is reflected on its plan record (Decision present AND item/Now prose reconciled with it), and adoption tracker WI-10001081 is completed with the per-plan verification listed.\n\n**R-3 — Independent grading outside author lineage.** Every acceptance scorecard counted toward a ship was emitted by a grader who is neither the rubric author nor in the author's spawn/rebind lineage, recruited from a live session rather than launched by the author.\n\n**R-4 — Every live-gate action followed exclusive ownership and exact lineage.** Every LIVE_GATE_OPS action by an agent associated with this program, including actions under another goal_ref, was performed only by the registered live gate holder for that exact condition or a platform-authorized fixer delegate within its assigned scope; it targeted the exact candidate/repairHead, did not compete with another live controller, and carried the required authorization and red-test acknowledgements for any force deploy. The original zero-call R-4 promise failed and remains disclosed in D-050/D-051; this replacement can pass only on positive historical proof of the actual single-owner safety invariant.\n\n**R-5 — The audit-filed defect is fixed with a behavior-sensitive guard.** EI-23072663469449933 is closed with a test that fails when the wrapper stops persisting the clean first-pass task verdict, replacing the stale exact-string assertion.\n\n**R-6 — The system-audit plan is re-baselined before its audits run.** green-main-system-audit-and-red-streak-elimination-2026-09-04 carries a recorded re-baseline per its D-010 (reconciled portfolio, evidence-backed residuals only, its P-001 left to the live gate owner) before P-006..P-010 execute.\n\n**R-7 — Whole-blob repair admissions preserve the source cohort.** Every whole-blob admission to this program's frozen repair lineage after D-045 used one pinned sourceCommit, included every differing importing test and imported module from that same commit before a validating precheck, and left the accepted repairHead without stale source-cohort members.\n\n**R-8 — The accepted green pin reached the serving release.** The exact frozen candidate and repairHead accepted under P-031 reached a green main pin and were served by the :3070 release operator, with the deployment record, greenPinSha, deployedSha, and observed health SHA agreeing on that lineage without a force waiver.\n\n## Design\n\nThe program is a tracker: each item carries one plan through the two-family completion gate (per-item code-truth audit, vetted rubric, independent grade, author verdict). It does NOT waive D-003: only the plan's own owner/grader chain can discharge its second clause, on evidence.\n\n### D-005 — RE-SEQUENCED: P-016 is the MOST expensive plan, not the closest to shipping\nDate: 2026-09-15\nMeasured 2026-09-15T22:1xZ by su-a604a73a. This CORRECTS a carry-note claim that survived several wakes ('P-016 remains the closest to shipping') and would send a successor to spend its effort in exactly the wrong place.\n\nMEASURED COST OF P-016 (progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05). Its full remaining chain is: activation conversation audit -> status draft->ready -> acceptance-BAR legacy backfill -> rubric revision 3->4 -> re-vet -> FRESH independent non-lineage grade -> re-emitted acceptance verdict -> ship. Every hop is forced, none is skippable:\n- plans:set-plan-status { status:'ready' } refuses conversation_audit_required, so it cannot leave draft without plans:audit { phase:'activation' }.\n- While status is 'draft', acceptance-bar-migration.ts:65 selects action 'seed-strict', forcing backfilled:false, which makes acceptance-bar-seed.ts:477 refuse the legacyCriterionMap this pre-BAR rubric requires. Confirmed by dry run: reason 'drafts receive the durable epoch marker and strict BAR seeding'.\n- acceptance-bar-seed.ts:829 computes rubricChanged from a stableJson comparison of template_data. A backfill necessarily writes barContract + barKey pins, so the rubric bumps 3->4 and UN-COUNTS all three cards pinned at rev 3: EI-22437423788282955 (vetting), EI-22438862127500981 (independent grading, su-95fb613c), EI-23365757672694634 (acceptance verdict). force waives only code-truth checks, never vetting or independent grading.\n\nMEASURED COST OF P-013/P-014: acceptance_bar_epoch IS NULL for gate-ownership-condition-singleton-2026-08-03 and gate-ownership-followup-2026-08-08, so they are excluded from BAR coverage entirely.
