If P-016's backfill IS performed, perform it BEFORE requesting any grading, never after - grading a revision that is going to bump is the specific waste this decision exists to prevent.\n\nTWO RETRACTIONS folded in, so neither is re-derived: (a) 'legacyCriterionMap is disqualified because a half-seeded contract already exists' is FALSE - that rubric's template_data.barContract IS NULL; the earlier check read harness_plans' acceptance_bar_* columns, a different object. (b) 'adding the ## Requirements section may have caused the conflict, so removing it may be the repair' is FALSE - the seeder refused with bar_requirements_missing BEFORE that edit and the plan was already epoch 1; removing it would only revert to that refusal.\nRelated: P-012, P-013, P-014, P-016\n\n### D-006 — Amend-vs-disclose on a defective acceptance rubric turns on whether a COUNTED artifact is pinned to the current revision\nDate: 2026-09-16\n#### The question this settles\n\nAn independent vetting critic finds a criterion whose `check` cannot falsify its own `driftMarker` — delete the behaviour and the bound tests stay green. Do we AMEND the rubric (bumping the revision) or DISCLOSE the defect and ship?\n\nThis arose twice in one wake with OPPOSITE correct answers, which is why it needs a recorded ruling rather than a habit.\n\n#### RULING\n\nThe deciding fact is whether any COUNTED artifact is currently pinned to the rubric's revision. Vetting critiques and scorecards pin to `(revision, criteriaHash)`, so any bump un-counts them.\n\n**(a) A counted artifact EXISTS → DISCLOSE.** Amending forfeits real, independently-produced work that must then be re-done. Rate the defective criterion honestly (`weak`/`fail`) in the meta-acceptance attestation, state the gap INSIDE the criterion's own `method` so the grader is instructed by the rubric itself rather than by a side-channel message, and record it. Do not inflate the rating to get a clean sheet.\n\n*Precedent — P-013 / `acceptance-gate-ownership-condition-singleton-2026-08-03` rev 8:* su-4dbc7355 held a FINISHED independent 6/6 acceptance card and two critics' critiques were pinned; the grader asked in writing to freeze. R-2 `bridge-settles-on-resolve` has `check.files` omitting the very integration file its method names, and `rubrics:amend` cannot reach `check`. Disclosed, `falsifiable-with-evidence` rated **weak**, `non-overlapping` rated **weak**. Shipped on disclosure, not on a clean sheet.\n\n**(b) NO counted artifact exists → AMEND.** It costs exactly one re-vet cycle and forfeits nothing. Shipping criteria that cannot fail is precisely the defect class this program exists to remove; a rubric whose gate cannot fire is indistinguishable from one that passed.\n\n*Precedent — P-014 / `acceptance-gate-ownership-followup-2026-08-08` rev 1:* su-28ebd65f's critique (WI-10001544 post 204823) found TWO blocking instrument defects — criterion 1 `workspace-fail-closed` (the adoption half is untested: delete the `findConditionKeyHolder` call and both check files stay green) and criterion 5 `pointer-through-checked-accessor` (its central D-014 property is asserted in `cell-read.test.ts:1263`, which is NOT in `check.files`). There is NO attestation and NO grading card on that rubric, so amending voids nothing. Amend to rev 2, batching ALL findings including the D-002(b) traceability gap, then re-vet once.\n\n#### COROLLARY — the trap, and it caught this program for hours\n\n\"Do not bump the rubric revision\" is a constraint inherited from case (a). It does NOT transfer to a rubric with nothing counted, and honouring it there ships an unfalsifiable gate **for free**. A constraint inherited from a premise that does not hold must be RE-DERIVED, not carried as a standing rule. Check for the counted artifact before honouring the freeze.\n\n#### MECHANISM NOTES (measured, not inferred)\n\n- `rubrics:amend` **cannot modify `check`**. A `check.files` defect therefore requires `rubrics:propose` (a new revision); there is no in-place repair.\n- `rubrics:propose` is refused by the orphaned-contract guard (`rubric-loss-guard.ts:429-431`) ONLY when the **SUBJECT PLAN's** `adoptionEpoch > 0` — not the rubric's own epoch. Measured in `harness_plans`: `gate-ownership-condition-singleton-2026-08-03` and `gate-ownership-followup-2026-08-08` both carry `acceptance_bar_epoch NULL` ⇒ propose is AVAILABLE for both; `progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05` carries `acceptance_bar_epoch 1` / cohort `post-epoch` ⇒ which is exactly why P-016 alone is deadlocked (EI-23376469015732685). So the P-016 deadlock does NOT generalize to this program's other plans, and must not be cited as a reason to avoid amending them.\n- Batch every intended change into ONE revision before requesting critique or grading. A piecemeal amendment re-invalidates each time.\n\n### D-007 — P-016's acceptance chain was COMPLETE at rubric rev 3 and my own rev-4 backfill invalidated it — so the rubric gets exactly ONE more amendment (checks-only), then the chain is rebuilt in order\nDate: 2026-09-17\nMeasured: 2026-09-17T03:1xZ by su-a604a73a via rubrics:amend { dryRun:true } preview, scorecards:list, and packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts:78-89,248-258.\n\n#### The finding that reframes this lane\n\nP-016 (progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05) ALREADY HAD a complete acceptance chain at rubric revision 3: vetting attestation EI-22437423788282955 current at rev 3, an independent grade EI-22438862127500981 by su-95fb613c (outside my lineage) rating all seven pass at rev 3, and an author ACCEPT verdict on 2026-09-15. scorecards:list shows both stored cards pinned to rubricRevision 3.\n\nThe rubric is now at revision 4. My own acceptance-BAR legacy backfill made that 3->4 move, and it invalidated the entire chain. That is the sole reason vetting.state now reads 'unvetted' and all seven bars read grading_stale. Nothing about the plan's implementation regressed — 5/5 items are terminal and the feature is live in production.\n\n#### RULING 1 — exactly one more amendment, then stop touching the rubric\n\nEvery rubric revision bump un-counts the vetting attestation, the independent grade, and the author verdict pinned to the prior revision. The chain must therefore be rebuilt STRICTLY AFTER the final revision exists: amend -> re-vet -> bind proof -> independent grade -> author verdict -> ship. An amendment made after the grade lands spends a scarce non-lineage grader for nothing, which is exactly what the 3->4 move already cost once.\n\n#### RULING 2 — the amendment is checks-only (variant A), not the wider proof-depth variant\n\nTwo candidate payloads were dry-run against the live contract:\n- A (bind check to the 2 unbound criteria): changedBars 2.\n- B (A plus requiredTestLayers:['unit'] on the 5 test-bound bars): changedBars 7.\n\nBoth returned IDENTICAL readiness on every other axis — approvalRequired:true, revisionMovement rubric 4->5 / subject 30->31, invalidatedScorecardIds 2, invalidatedProofRefs 0, authorVerdictBecomesStale:true, and nextRepair bar_snapshot_proof_stale. B therefore churns five extra bar hashes and arms a proof-adequacy check for no measured readiness gain. A is adopted. If bar_snapshot_proof_depth_missing genuinely survives proof binding, it is addressed THEN with evidence, not pre-emptively on a guess.\n\n#### RULING 3 — instrument:'none' is a faithful migration here, not a dodge\n\nR-6 (thresholds-disposition-recorded) and R-7 (falsifier-reported-with-its-scope) are corpus-inspection criteria. Both ALREADY carry the legacy criterion-level instrumentKey:'none'; the evaluator reads bar.check, which is null, so bar_snapshot_check_missing fires and both bars are structurally unfalsifiable. The amendment promotes the author's existing declaration to the generalized check:{kind:'instrument',instrumentKey:'none'} form — evaluator:249-252 names this the explicit manual contract, and automatedProofRequired() at :78-89 defers to the projection's instrument declaration precisely so a manual BAR is not held to an automated proof floor. Their methods already state concrete falsifying observations ('a single unqualified occurrence fails this criterion'), so falsifiability lives in the method the grader executes. Binding a fabricated tests-check instead would be WORSE: it would look automated while R-7's forward obligation went unchecked.\n\n#### RULING 4 — the amendment requires an OUTSIDE-LINEAGE approval, which must be ROUTED\n\nThe preview returns approvalRequired:true with an acceptance-bar-amendment-approval payload. An unvetted rubric is not an unpinned one.\nRelated: P-016\n\n### D-008 — barHash, not contentHash, decides whether a revision bump invalidates evidence — a barSetHash-only move is collateral and the identical evidence re-binds soundly\nDate: 2026-09-17\nAffects: green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08, progress-certified-release-trace-2026-09-05\nDate: 2026-09-17\nMeasured: plans:get-specs { harness:'papercusp', slug:'green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08', specIds:['R6-P009-PRECHECK-RUNNER-FAIL-CLOSED'], includeHistory:true } comparing revision 6 against revision 7, plus plans:get-spec-evidence on the same clause (currentness { current:0, stale:22 }). Leaving them undone strands the plan permanently, and there is nobody to hand them back to.\n\nThe third-party critique must still come from an agent who is neither the emitter NOR the dead author — the existing `scorecards:emit` predicate is unchanged by the author's death, and inheriting the emit seat does not relax it.\n\n#### RULING 2 — inheriting the chain does NOT make you eligible to grade\n\nThis is the trap, and it is silent. `grader-eligibility.ts` resolves the IMPLEMENTER as the rubric's `createdBy` and refuses a grader in that author's lineage. Re-binding all 151 ahead of time resets a clock that expires again before it is used — freshen the evidence immediately before grading instead, and use `specAdequacy.evidenceRefs` to name the exact current cohort rather than deleting history.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-013 — P-012 splits into 8 re-bindable tree clauses and 2 live-plane clauses that no test can satisfy — and its proof_stale is NOT the cohort artifact that R6-P009's was\nDate: 2026-09-17\nDate: 2026-09-17\nMeasured: 2026-09-17T13:1xZ by su-a604a73a via plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy (whole plan, classRef plan-class-feature-ship), plans:get-spec-evidence currentness aggregates, and plans:get-specs sourceBar.evidencePlane.\n\n#### The false lead this kills\n\nEarlier the same wake I resolved R6-P009 by discovering its `freshness` block was pure SUPERSEDED HISTORY in the default evaluation cohort: 31 bindings / 5 current, and narrowing `evidenceRefs` to its 3 distinct current refs returned verdict=pass, wouldBlock=[] with NO writes. It is kept because P-031 has churned through 5 holders and the 6th reads contextPressure=critical, so a live leader holding an armed fleet:claim-released watch is the only thing standing between another release and another multi-hour orphan window.\n\nDECISION 3 — the holder is NOT contested and NOT monitored. su-cfa16b20 is live and progressing on P-031. Per the claim rule a live peer's claim is coordinated with, never taken; per anti-babysitting the leader does not watch them work. One expects:'none' note was sent about the checkpoint-cap/context-pressure risk, and that is the whole of the interaction.\n\n⚠ KNOWN DEGRADATION disclosed with this decision: the new leader's own wake path is degraded (loop:status reachability warning — 'this process is alive in a terminal we cannot inject; wakes PARK as inbox-only until it exits'). Wakes are DEFERRED, not lost — they fire when the process exits, as demonstrated by this session being woken after its 14:06Z death — but a catcher that wakes late is a weaker guarantee than the armed watches imply. Anyone who needs a fast catch should not rely solely on this leader.\n\n### D-047 — WI-10002525 is RETRACTED: empty-SHA freshness rows were not the exact-pin certifier; P-031 waits on a live specialized certification already bound to 80521d598f\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23\n\nCORRECTS the external-blocker diagnosis placed on P-031 by the seventh holder and closes WI-10002525 as dropped.\n\nMeasured 2026-09-23T01:50Z: systemd unit papercup-live-release-certification was active/running with PID 3652899, started 20:00:11 EDT. /tmp/papercup-live-release-certification.log showed the release trigger's specialized run rebuilt clean HEAD 80521d598f (dirty-files=0), closed its certified-source window at build end at HEAD 80521d598f/dirty=0, classified content-matrix as PASS-971 under the existing documented downgrade, and was actively running from-repo. The verdict bank also contains historical specialized rows with nonempty certification_target_sha values.\n\nRULING: sampled rows with certification_target_sha:'' were ordinary hourly freshness records and cannot establish that the specialized writer lost its target. The prior 'permanently fail-closed for any green pin' root-cause claim is false and must not enter P-040 or acceptance. No source edit is warranted from it. P-031 remains blocked only on the demonstrably progressing exact-pin run and the automatic subsequent :3070 deploy. Preserve D-039/D-042: no manual checkpoint-run, queue retirement, tip convergence, or force-deploy.\nRelated: P-031, P-040\n\n### D-048 — R-4 must NOT be remapped or reworded to clear the ship gate — it was contradicted in letter and disclosed in D-039; the independent grader decides, not the implementer\nDate: 2026-09-23\nCONTEXT: plans:set-plan-status shipped refuses acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready (6/6 BARs blocking). R-4 additionally carries bar_snapshot_mapping_dropped_only, and the gate's own nextRepair invites 'Map the outstanding BAR to a live replacement item or amend the BAR'. I was one step from mapping R-4 onto P-031 (a live done item whose contract states the same constraint almost verbatim). I am recording why that would have been wrong.\n\nMEASUREMENT: harness_shared.tool_invocations, harness=papercusp, since 2026-09-15 — 56 forbidden-op rows overall (checkpoint-run 43 all ok; repair-queue retire 4 ok; deploy force 3 ok). Filtered to sessions known to belong to this program: EXACTLY 2, both su-14342fa6 (this program's registered fleet leader), both release:checkpoint-run status=ok, both goal_ref=WI-10001493, at 2026-09-22 04:46:13Z and 04:48:04Z.\n\nR-4's falsifier fires on 'contradicted'. It was contradicted.\n\nBUT NOT CONCEALED: D-039 already records, in the leader's own words, that 'the manual run bought ~34min by violating P-031 in letter... the deviation is disclosed not buried'. And D-041 explains the dropped carriers: P-021/P-022's subject plans were superseded into this program on 2026-09-19, so their acceptance chains could not legitimately complete. Both decisions are sound; neither is challenged here.\n\nRULING: mapping_dropped_only is a TRUE CONSEQUENCE of a legitimate drop, not a bookkeeping defect to paper over. Remapping R-4 to a live carrier would make a disclosed breach read as a clean pass, which is exactly the goalpost-moving the two-family acceptance gate exists to prevent — and it would be done by an implementer on their own plan. So: R-4 is carried FORWARD AS WRITTEN into independent grading, with D-039 and this decision as the evidence the grader rates it against. If R-4 is to be amended to record the disclosed exception, that goes through the outside-lineage amendment path (precedent WI-10001779, R-1 rev 8->9), never by the implementer's own hand.\n\nThis decision does not assert the plan should fail. It asserts that the judgement is the independent grader's to make on complete information.\n\n### D-049 — R-4 was breached THREE times, not two, and R-1 is unsatisfiable as written after D-019; repair is a disclosed, outside-approved BAR amendment, never a remap-to-pass\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23. Recorded by su-e3d58938 (holder of WI-10002581 since 04:09Z, handed over by su-2bee6ccf).\n\nMEASURED 2026-09-23 ~04:20Z (harness_shared.tool_invocations, workspace papercusp-workspace, invoked_at >= 2026-09-15, goal_ref a work-item of this plan):\n1. UNDISCLOSED: 2026-09-17 21:12:47.524Z. su-a604a73a (the program's then-driver and rubric author) ran release:deploy op=force with confirm:true, status ok, goal_ref WI-10001488 (P-016). The reason was recovering the critical fleet outage EI-23538941588991674: deployed build 987162bae3 denied every MCP tool for 14 agents. Its two ok calls at 21:11:35Z and 21:12:23Z carried no confirm, so they were dry-run previews, and two more calls were invalid-input. No Decision in this plan mentions this deploy, and the Now block's 'R-4/D-037/D-039 continue to bind: ... no force-deploy' reads as if none happened.\n2. DISCLOSED in D-039: 2026-09-22 04:46:13.654Z and 04:48:04.817Z. su-14342fa6 ran release:checkpoint-run, status ok, goal_ref WI-10001493, under D-038's suspension.\nNo repair-queue retire is attributed to the program. The prior holder's '2 attributed rows' count (WI-10002581 checkpoint, 03:53Z) was therefore incomplete.\n\nR-1 IS ALSO UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN. R-1 requires all ten D-001 plans at status shipped. Live: 3 shipped (gate-ownership-condition-singleton-2026-08-03, gate-ownership-followup-2026-08-08, frozen-candidate-carry-and-launch-fail-closed-2026-09-07) and 7 superseded by the owner-approved D-019 consolidation. Three of the seven carry a supersede-only forced_past (supersede_items_unfinished). Their carrier items: P-016, P-017 and P-020 are done; P-012, P-015, P-021 and P-022 were dropped (D-040/D-041). So four subject plans' own acceptance chains were never completed. D-026 (09-22) amended R-1's wording but kept 'ten plans shipped'.\n\nRULING ON THE REPAIR:\n(a) No remap-to-pass. The plan body's Bar-to-work map already lists P-031 for R-4, but mapping an outcome BAR that asserts 'the gate is never touched' onto a live carrier would present a breach as a pass.\n(b) R-4 becomes role:'disclosure' (mandatory:false, passRatings:[], coversBarKeys:['R-1']). It states all three breaches with timestamps, actors, goal_refs and reasons. It keeps a live carrier (P-031) so its proof can be bound.\n(c) R-1 is re-based to the D-019 dispositions actually recorded. The four dropped acceptance chains are named explicitly in its condition, not hidden.\n(d) Both changes go through ONE rubrics:amend transaction, approved by an authenticated outside-lineage reviewer (precedent: D-024/D-025/D-026). Then, in order: bind proof, vet, get an independent grade via set-plan-status recruitment, and record the author verdict.\nThe implementer does not decide this alone: the reviewer who approves the amendment, and then the grader, each see this Decision. If the approval is refused, R-4 stays an outcome, grades broken, and the plan does not ship. That result is then reported to Avi as a finding.\n\n### D-050 — Correct the R-4 gate-action census and keep BAR amendment outside-lineage reviewed\nDate: 2026-09-25\nDate: 2026-09-25\nMeasured: 2026-09-25 01:52 UTC, read-only SQL on harness_shared.tool_invocations and frozen_repair_edit_ledger; writer at packages/operator-core/lib/projected-tool-deps.ts:867 stamps invoked_at at dispatch settlement. Scope: workspace papercusp-workspace, invoked_at >= 2026-09-15, agents = DISTINCT coord_owner_id with any goal_ref matching a work item whose source_plan_slug is this program. The agent-cohort definition deliberately includes those agents' OTHER goal_refs, as R-4 says \"or its agents\"; actor membership alone does not prove an unrelated call was directed by this program.\n\nCORRECTION to D-049 and WI-10002581 comment 1141244: the \"three breaches\" account is incomplete. Outside-lineage reviewer su-091ad703 refused both draft amendments in comment 1141348. In the measured cohort there are 8 status-ok release:checkpoint-run calls (2 plan-goal by su-14342fa6 at 2026-09-22 04:46:13/04:48:04Z; 6 other-goal by su-7dc2f158 and su-c99640ad on 2026-09-21). There are 28 status-ok release:repair-queue admit calls with confirm:true (18 plan-goal: 12 by su-14342fa6, 4 by su-4aba3409, 2 by su-3340afad; 10 other-goal by su-a604a73a on 2026-09-16). These are confirmed INVOCATIONS, not a claim that every admission published: R6 can return precheck-running before publication. There are 2 status-ok release:deploy calls with confirm:true: force by su-a604a73a at 2026-09-17 21:12:47Z for WI-10001488, and trigger by su-cfa16b20 at 2026-09-23 00:04:16Z for WI-2144525. Thus 38 effect-capable calls appear in this cohort, versus the earlier packet's three. No retire or converge invocation appeared in this scoped result.\n\nSeparate from those 38: 22 status-ok admit calls without confirm and 7 status-ok deploy force/trigger calls without confirm are dry-run previews by the current tool contracts; they do not by themselves prove publication or deployment. The same cohort also has 4 invalid-input admit previews, 1 invalid-input confirmed admit, and 2 invalid-input force previews. It has 132 status-ok and 2 error release:repair-queue record-edit calls. The edit-ledger writer at packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release/repair-queue.ts:697 persists attribution hunks without moving repairHead; 120 rows in frozen_repair_edit_ledger match the agent cohort (ledger ids 902..4732, non-contiguous). Work-item identity is NULL on those ledger rows, so the counts are actor-attributed, not proof of a program-directed queue admission. Any disclosure must name this separate category rather than silently treating it as either no action or a published repair.\n\nRULING: R-4's existing abstention outcome is contradicted. D-019 owner-approved consolidation also leaves R-1's \"all ten shipped\" condition impossible: 3 are shipped and 7 intentionally superseded. No BAR has been amended and no approval has been granted. Prepare full proposed R-4/R-1 condition, method and falsifier texts plus dry-run args for outside-lineage review; do not remap an outcome to a pass or apply without authenticated reviewer approval. A reviewer may reject the proposal, in which case this plan remains unshipped.\nRelated: P-016, P-017, P-020, P-021, P-022, P-031\n\n### D-051 — Outside reviewer rejects a nonblocking R-4 conversion; owner must decide the exact acceptance deviation\nDate: 2026-09-25\nDate: 2026-09-25\nAuthority: authenticated outside-lineage review by su-bce45d81-6ee6-47f8-bb83-fd8a803cd261, WI-10002581 thread post 1143954 at 2026-09-25 02:02:54Z. It reviewed the exact census in post 1143952, full proposed rubrics:amend dry-run args in post 1143953, and D-050.\n\nRULING: NOT APPROVED. The corrected 38 effect-capable invocation census is materially more complete, and D-019 supports describing seven source plans as superseded rather than shipped. But active rev12 R-4 is a mandatory outcome promising this program's sessions would not run checkpoints, mutate/retire the repair queue, or force deploy. D-050 establishes that promise was contradicted. Changing R-4 to role=disclosure, mandatory=false, passRatings=[] removes a KNOWN FAILED outcome from the ship floor. D-019 authorized single-tracker consolidation, not waiver of this no-live-gate-action condition. An agent-authored disclosure Decision cannot supply the missing owner risk acceptance. Reviewer says keep R-4 mandatory and broken/awaiting-acceptance, or obtain an explicit owner decision naming this exact waiver and its shipment consequence before proposing a nonblocking replacement. Their independent rubrics:amend dry-run timed out, so no fresh reviewer CAS/hash equivalence was attested.\n\nThe proposed amendment has NOT been applied. Current rubric remains rev12, R-4 mandatory. Next action is an answerable owner choice: (a) keep R-4 mandatory and leave this program unshipped; (b) explicitly waive R-4's mandatory outcome with the recorded gate actions disclosed, then independently re-review a fresh amendment and complete every other acceptance family; or (c) supersede the program as unshipped with a written learning. No force-ship or silent re-map.\nRelated: P-016, P-017, P-020, P-021, P-022, P-031\n\n### D-052 — Owner directs R-4 replacement around actual live-gate ownership, with historical action audit before grading\nDate: 2026-09-25\nDate: 2026-09-25\nAuthority: Avraham, interactive owner turn: \"do as you recommend\" following the recommendation to replace R-4's blanket program-membership ban with an ownership-based acceptance rule and to audit every historical gate action first.\n\nDecision: preserve the platform's exact-one-live-fixer invariant. R-4 as authored in D-001 is an overbroad lifetime zero-call rule tied to program membership, not to who held the live gate lane. It was self-imposed by an agent while another agent held the gate, not an owner instruction to ban every future program-associated gate owner. Correct the acceptance criterion to grade actual authority and isolation: for each action coupled to the current verdict, the caller must be the registered live gate holder at that time, the candidate/repair lineage must be exact, competing action must not exist, and exceptional force deploys must carry the required owner authorization and audit receipt. Preserve the literal old R-4 failure and the full action census as historical disclosure; never present it as an original-rule pass.\n\nSequence: (1) reconstruct historical gate ownership and exact action outcome for the recorded calls; distinguish confirmed tool invocation from published admission/deploy and actor cohort from plan goal_ref. (2) if the evidence proves nonowner or unapproved force action, the replacement outcome fails unless the owner explicitly accepts that specific deviation; missing history remains unknown. (3) prepare an exact R-4/R-1 amendment and obtain outside-lineage review. (4) only after approval, apply, bind proof, vet, grade independently, record verdict, and attempt shipment. This decision authorizes the redesign work, not a passing grade or a force waiver. No LIVE_GATE_OPS current-run work is assigned by it.\nRelated: P-031\n\n### D-053 — Historical R-4 owner proof is mixed; positive authority and outcome required for every action\nDate: 2026-09-25\nDate: 2026-09-25\nMeasured: read-only historical audit of harness_shared.tool_invocations writer (projected-tool-deps.ts:867), coord_event_log claim/intent messages, coord_links, work_items, owner_directives, and repair-queue/checkpoint-run source. This is historical evidence, not a read or takeover of the CURRENT live gate.\n\nOriginal R-4's zero-call promise is falsified (D-050). For the proposed owner-based replacement, positive ownership and effect proof is MIXED and incomplete:\n- 2026-09-16 22:02-22:20Z: ten confirmed admit invocations by su-a604a73a under non-program gate item WI-10001674. Coord claim event at 21:46Z and his explicit release at 22:39Z bracket these calls. Each admission's publication/outcome still needs its own ledger proof.\n- 2026-09-22 04:46:13/04:48:04Z: two checkpoint-run invocations by su-14342fa6. work_items:create at 04:46:01Z created WI-10002334 with assign_to:self before both calls; its body and call reasons record an unowned gate and dead fixer, with repairHead e1068622. The second call pins requiredAncestorSha. Tool status=ok proves dispatch, not the terminal run verdict or absence of competing holder.\n- 2026-09-17 21:12:47Z: su-a604a73a called release:deploy op=force confirm:true for green pin 59105f87, citing critical outage EI-23538941588991674. He explicitly released WI-10001674 at 2026-09-16 22:39Z. Bounded coord claim events and tool claim/create rows before the force call show no later gate claim by him, and the owner_directives table yielded no matching deploy/outage/force signoff in that date window. These bounded absences do not prove no approval existed elsewhere; they mean the new criterion's positive authorization receipt is NOT YET ESTABLISHED.\n- 2026-09-22 04:05-04:30Z: five confirmed admits by su-14342fa6 preceded his WI-10002334 gate claim; WI-10002322 explicitly described source repairs only. Several admit call reasons describe precheck retries and the 04:30 call says PUBLISH, but tool status alone does not prove which attempts moved repairHead. Exact owner/outcome evidence is still required for all 28 confirmed admits, eight checkpoint calls, and two confirmed deploy calls in D-050's full cohort.\n\nDecision for review: replace cohort-membership abstention with a mandatory, falsifiable criterion checking exact-time registered live owner or delegated fixer, exact candidate/repair lineage, no competing control-plane action, and required force-deploy owner authorization/acknowledged-red-test receipt. Preserve the old R-4 literal failure in D-050/D-051 and grade missing positive proof UNKNOWN, never healthy. This owner-directed correction (D-052) is not a pass finding. Outside-lineage reviewer must assess the exact amended text before apply; if any historical nonowner or unapproved action is confirmed, the corrected outcome fails.\nRelated: P-031\n\n### D-054 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-25\nAmendment-Id: amend-86a75aa4dd0e87f6cceb6312\nRequest-Hash: df344c5391360053d80767244b9aae3314fbd92f6ad3afd35b3d202dc9c6e8fc\nActor: su-da3149e7-884d-403f-81cd-4f4548b27e64\nReason: Owner-directed D-052 corrects R-4's cohort-based zero-call rule to the actual single-owner safety invariant; D-053 records historical proof gaps and old breach, so no passing verdict is presumed.\nApproved-By: su-bce45d81-6ee6-47f8-bb83-fd8a803cd261\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1144474\nApproved-At: 2026-09-25T03:34:07.876Z\nRubric revision: 12 → 13\nSubject plan revision: 188 → 189\nChanged BARs: R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-055 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-25\nAmendment-Id: amend-7af83091f7f0b56f22553822\nRequest-Hash: 3b80cafbfc88fcf092cd8452ee8d208d6b11dd1b5361a5065c274a7322b072eb\nActor: su-da3149e7-884d-403f-81cd-4f4548b27e64\nReason: Owner-approved D-019 consolidation superseded seven D-001 subject plans; correct R-1's impossible all-ten-shipped wording while preserving exact residual and dropped-chain accountability.\nApproved-By: su-bce45d81-6ee6-47f8-bb83-fd8a803cd261\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1144666\nApproved-At: 2026-09-25T03:44:28.205Z\nRubric revision: 13 → 14\nSubject plan revision: 191 → 192\nChanged BARs: R-1\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-056 — Close rev15 rubric coverage gaps without presuming a pass\nDate: 2026-09-25\nDate: 2026-09-25\nMeasured: outside-lineage rev15 holistic critique on WI-10002581 posts 1144751 and corrected 1144752; Current six BARs do not directly test either outcome. The active R-5 check is instrument:none although packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/affected-tests-passing-verdict-cache.test.ts:390-415 executes the callback.\nRuling: propose mandatory R-7 for D-045 cohort integrity and mandatory R-8 for P-031 exact serving lineage, mapped to P-031. Clarify current ledger BARs on staging-operator, R-5 on the tree with its canonical test bound, and R-8 on release-operator; make R-2/R-3/R-5/R-6 falsifiers specific. These are a proposal until the exact rubrics:amend delta receives authenticated outside-lineage approval. The old R-4 zero-call breach and missing historical owner/force-signoff receipts remain disclosed and block a healthy R-4 grade. No BAR is passed and no shipment is implied.\nRelated: P-019, P-031\n\n### D-057 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-25\nAmendment-Id: amend-97cb42835e308f33be89e47b\nRequest-Hash: 6f1302b1a9ea8d831fa8499b82278b7f39f76a6659bd714aeed3d1f331e30249\nActor: su-da3149e7-884d-403f-81cd-4f4548b27e64\nReason: Address outside-lineage R-5 detector objection in post1144818 with verified real persist-path artifact and bypass-write mutation test; preserve eight mandatory outcomes and R-4 historical unknown boundary.\nApproved-By: su-bce45d81-6ee6-47f8-bb83-fd8a803cd261\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1144842\nApproved-At: 2026-09-25T04:53:42.121Z\nRubric revision: 15 → 16\nSubject plan revision: 197 → 198\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-058 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-25\nAmendment-Id: amend-a8e1fb87c2c22ab21d00a97a\nRequest-Hash: 14ea40fe0c85a3108c66298b19829f612979729ecca1633f4cd8667170b8a9c3\nActor: su-da3149e7-884d-403f-81cd-4f4548b27e64\nReason: Correct R-5 after independent review post1145146: retain truthful unit layer, replace the invalid historical runtime-CAUGHT demand with same-commit false-positive evidence and current real-path artifact/bypass-write guard.\nApproved-By: su-bce45d81-6ee6-47f8-bb83-fd8a803cd261\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1145191\nApproved-At: 2026-09-25T05:56:24.310Z\nRubric revision: 16 → 17\nSubject plan revision: 198 → 199\nChanged BARs: R-5\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-059 — R-7 historical admission #19 stays FAILED — no waiver [owner:Avraham 2026-09-26]\nDate: 2026-09-26\nOwner answered the AskUserQuestion 'R-7 admission' in session su-7256202c (turn stamped OWNER interactive, directive #555 context) with: \"Keep R-7 failed\". Bot audit CLEAN (no exfil; only optional Gemini egress, kept off). Key: the runner (auto-apply-runner.js) already patches the console apply script via regex-replace in buildInjection(), so the dedupe hook + company-Set inject the same way — wellfound-auto-apply.js stays 100% upstream on disk; ALL changes live in the runner. Bot uses channel:'chrome' (system Chrome) so no chromium download.\nNext: verify background install (task 0mu35gubn1pbf1xk4o7), then P-002.\n\n## Background\nWI-10001445 (Avraham Weiss job applications). Canonical tracker: ~/Downloads/AI_Agent_Job_Applications.json (~2,414 records, 2.8MB). Resume: ~/Downloads/Avraham_Weiss_SWE_Papercusp_Clera.pdf. Prior assets: .papercusp/scratch/{wf-decrypt.py (decrypts Wellfound cookies from live Chrome keyring), dedupe-set.mjs, wf-cdp.mjs, wf-login2.mjs}. Bot: Playwright wrapper injecting a console apply script into wellfound.com/jobs; human-paced 60-150s; DataDome-aware; 50/day cap.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-001 — Cross-platform company dedupe.** Never double-apply across platforms: dedupe by COMPANY against the canonical tracker BEFORE sending.\n**R-002 — Canonical write-back.** Record every submitted application to the canonical tracker (platform 'wellfound'); re-read the file before every append because peers write it too.\n**R-003 — Authorized role and compensation filter.** Only SWE roles, remote, salary >= $150k; keep the $150k default and do not pass MIN_SALARY_K without a fresh owner authorization.\n**R-004 — Upstream source preservation.** Keep wellfound-auto-apply.js unmodified on disk; all integration changes belong in auto-apply-runner.js.\n**R-005 — Safe demographic defaults.** Leave demographic questions blank unless required; keep relocate permissive.\n**R-006 — Dry-run before live submit.** Dry-run verification must prove dedupe, salary filtering, form behavior, and no phantom applies before any live submit.\n**R-007 — Owner-gated live execution.** No future live run or scheduled applying occurs until Avi explicitly authorizes it; when authorized, apply one-at-a-time and monitor DataDome/errors.\n\n## Design\n- Dedupe hook: in buildInjection(), inject window.__DEDUPE_HAS_COMPANY (normalized-company Set from the canonical tracker) beside window.__APPLY_CONFIG, AND inject a ~4-line guard at top of fillAndSubmit(company,title) via .replace('async function fillAndSubmit(company, title) {', ...) that skips + closes the panel when company is already in the Set.\n- Write-back: beside logApplication(pendingJob) (LIVE only), re-read canonical JSON then append a normalized record; add company to the in-memory Set.\n- Salary floor: inject MIN_SALARY + a floor in job selection, and/or a Wellfound salary URL param.\n- Auth: seed .wellfound-chrome-profile from wf-decrypt.py cookies. Fallback: `node auto-apply-runner.js wellfound login`.\n- Durable location: ~/wellfound-autoapply (outside repo tree; node_modules must NOT enter shared tree).\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-003, P-008 | live |\n| R-002 | P-004, P-008, P-009 | live |\n| R-003 | P-005, P-008, P-009 | live |\n| R-004 | P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-002, P-006, P-008 | live |\n| R-006 | P-008 | live |\n| R-007 | P-009 | live |\n\n## Phase 1\n- **P-001** `done` Re-clone bot to ~/wellfound-autoapply and npm install (playwright + stealth; channel:'chrome' = no chromium download) — note: ← WI-10001891 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Extract CV from resume PDF; populate .env (US SWE identity, contact, links, skills, highlights) — note: ← WI-10001892 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Wire dedupe: __DEDUPE_HAS_COMPANY Set from canonical tracker + fillAndSubmit guard via buildInjection() — note: ← WI-10001894 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Wire write-back to canonical JSON (re-read before append) + intra-run Set update — note: ← WI-10001895 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add $150k salary floor and US remote SWE search URL/filters — note: ← WI-10001896 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Demographic-blank default; keep relocate permissive — note: ← WI-10001897 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Seed .wellfound-chrome-profile from decrypted cookies; verify logged-in — note: ← WI-10001898 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Dry-run: verify dedupe fires, salary floor, forms fill, no phantom applies — note: ← WI-10001899 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Live run: apply one-at-a-time to SWE >=150k remote roles, record each, monitor DataDome/errors — note: ← WI-10001900 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 Use upstream apply code unchanged; inject dedupe via the runner\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-15 turn] \"cant we just use their code exactly and just hook in a dedupe step instead of copy pasting\". wellfound-auto-apply.js stays byte-for-byte upstream; dedupe hook + company-Set injected via auto-apply-runner.js buildInjection() (already regex-patches the script). Same captcha/pacing/selectors, our dedupe, minimal surface, upstream-pullable.\n\n### D-002 Dedupe key is COMPANY across platforms\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-14] \"lets not apply the same company twice even if on different platforms.\" Bot's own seen-Set (job.href) + Wellfound \"Applied\" stamp handle same-platform; our hook adds cross-platform company dedupe against the canonical tracker. Company via getCompany() (\"Apply to <X>\"), normalized (lowercase, strip Inc/LLC/punctuation).\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"sb-devboard-hive","plan_slug":"acceptance-hn-email-apply-automation-2026-09-15","title":"Acceptance BAR — HN Who-Is-Hiring email apply: extract addresses, compose tailored emails, send under review","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-15","owner":"su-4e3cf07d-acc9-4dbe-8385-0860203aa7ee","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — HN Who-Is-Hiring email apply: extract addresses, compose tailored emails, send under review\nslug: acceptance-hn-email-apply-automation-2026-09-15\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-15\nupdated: 2026-09-16\nowner: su-4e3cf07d-acc9-4dbe-8385-0860203aa7ee\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — HN Who-Is-Hiring email apply: extract addresses, compose tailored emails, send under review\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). All implementation items terminal; plan at awaiting-acceptance, bars unweakened (D-016/D-021). R-1/R-3/R-4 can only be proven on the DEPLOYED Worker, which still serves the 2026-09-26 build (POST /github/webhook = 404 identical to a control path, re-measured 03:06Z). Open owner question: conversation conv-mupnp1e7-0000-3a021b95edf74a519102dd82b0bfac6a (A deploy Worker bundle / B rescope the 3 bars to tree plane / C drop live GitHub leg), plus WI-10004856 (register GitHub App, owner-only). The leader yielded its session slot to the goal holder; there is currently NO live fleet leader.\n\n**Next:** Relaunched leader: fleet:take-leadership, then events:await the conversation:answered key above, and on the owner's answer run the matching path per the WI-10004858 checkpoint (A deploy per WI-10004875; B rubrics:amend + re-vet + rebind; C drop live leg), then plans:audit per item, plans:set-plan-status shipped, implementer verdict.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10001646 — Worker pins content at publish: for self-describing kinds, resolve the repo's default-branch head, fetch `git/trees/<sha>?recursive=1` filtered to `<listing_ref>/`, compute a canonical tree digest (s… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001647 — Install verifies the pin: replace tip-clone with fetch-by-SHA (`git init` + `fetch --depth 1 origin <sha>` + checkout) in the shared `install-self-describing-core` deps, recompute the tree digest of … <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001648 — Worker re-scans what it pins: lift `scanIdentityLeaks` + `sensitive-text` into a generic lib with no node-only imports (they are pattern scanners), run it in the Worker over the fetched `<ref>/` byte… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001649 — Versioned re-publish: a publish of the same (repo, kind, ref) at a new SHA creates a new listing version and resets `review_status` to pending, instead of today's dedup-return of the old row (which m… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001650 — OWNER-GATED: register a \"Papercusp Cupboard\" GitHub App (permissions: contents:read, checks:write, metadata:read; webhook: push). Install `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GITHUB_APP_WEBHOO… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001651 — Worker webhook `/github/webhook`: verify the HMAC; on `push` to a repo holding an active listing, fetch `<ref>/` at the pushed SHA with the installation token, run the P-003 scan + schema validation,… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001652 — Spike then land: server-side static script analysis for `recipe` using tooldef `checkScript` (`libs/generic/tooldef/src/code-orchestration/parse-check.ts`, TypeScript-AST based). Spike whether the Ty… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001653 — Review approves a SHA: `/admin/listings/:id/review` records `approved_commit_sha`; the admin review surface shows the diff of `<ref>/` against the previously approved SHA. An approval of a drifted ro… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001654 — First-party mirrors (Papercusp/recipes, goals, plans, rubrics, templates-mirror): add `.github/workflows/cupboard-verify.yml` running the same scan + schema validation + `checkScript` on every PR/pus… <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001655 — Optional provenance for third-party repos: publish a REUSABLE workflow `Papercusp/cupboard-actions/.github/workflows/verify.yml` that emits a GitHub artifact attestation (Sigstore) binding the `<ref>… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001656 — Route the self-describing kinds through the existing release gate: each publish core builds the release manifest, ships the package bytes to R2 as the ORIGIN via `prepareReleaseForPublish`, and the W… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-10001657 — Acceptance — hostile-publisher scenario as a committed integration test: publish a clean recipe, approve it, force-push a dirty script to the mirror, attempt install → refused `content-address-mismat… <!-- P-012 -->\n## Background\n\nWhat the pipeline does TODAY, measured, not remembered:\n\n- **The Worker verifies WHO, never WHAT.** `POST /listings` (`listings.ts:696-745`) calls `GET /repos/:owner/:name` with the publisher's own token, refuses a private repo, checks `repo.id === github_repository_id`, derives `publisher_permission` — then stores `github_url` + `listing_ref`. It never fetches a byte of the repo's content. The `indexer.ts` header states it plainly: \"Cupboard server has no GitHub app credentials yet\".\n- **Human review exists and approves a POINTER.** `REVIEW_POLICY_KINDS` (`db.ts:121`) = knowledge-pack, blueprint, app, rubric, plan, recipe, goal — every instruction-carrying kind lands `pending` until an operator approves via `POST /admin/listings/:id/review`. But the row holds no commit SHA and no digest, so what the reviewer approved and what a later installer receives are unrelated by construction.\n- **Install takes the branch tip.** `gitCloneShallow` = `git clone --depth 1 -- url dest` (`install-io.ts:32`), then `<clone>/<listing_ref>/` is parsed and copied. No commit pin, no digest check, at all 8 install-io call sites (goal, recipe, plan, rubric, template, blueprint, bundle-app, plugin). Whoever controls the mirror repo controls every future install, after review.\n- **Identity scrubbing is client-only.** `identity-scrub.ts` runs in operator-core before `writeFileSync`; the Worker cannot tell whether it ran. `authorityUnresolved` on a recipe is the PUBLISHER's static analyzer's self-report, \"surfaced to the installer, never a blocker\".\n- **A content-addressed hosted path already exists and the self-describing kinds skip it.** `publish-release-gate.ts` (Merkle-root recomputation via `validatePublishableRelease`), migration 018's `release_content_hash / release_manifest_digest / release_signature` columns, the R2 `ARTIFACTS` bucket, and P-045's release-mirror route whose stated invariant is \"the mirror can only ever publish bytes that already passed the hosted publish path\". `publishListingToCupboard` runs the gate only `if (release)` — plans, goals, recipes, rubrics, templates never send it.\n- **The first-party mirror repos are unprotected.** Papercusp/recipes, goals, plans: no `.github/`, no branch protection, force-push allowed on recipes and plans. A force-push does not purge history: dirty commit `3afccdd` in Papercusp/goals stayed fetchable by SHA after the branch moved.\n\nGoverning rulings inherited from `shared-pot-dao-cupboard-v1-2026-09-04`: **D-055** (facts behind the Worker; hive log authoritative for governance + distribution only) and **D-056** (GitHub = identity, key proofs, Release mirror — never governance/commerce/money). This plan keeps the Worker as the content authority and uses GitHub only as identity, mirror, and a verification/provenance SIGNAL. Adjacent, not overlapping: `cupboard-p2p-follow-ups-2026-09-06` P-004 (a derived catalog mirror of signed manifests) consumes the pins this plan produces.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — An install is a version, not a pointer.** The bytes an operator approved are the bytes every later install receives, verified by digest at install time; a mismatch refuses.\n\n**R-2 — Scrub on the client, verify on the server.** Identity scrubbing stays local (the identity must never leave the publisher's machine), and the Worker independently re-scans the bytes it catalogs so a bypassed or stale client scrubber cannot publish a leak.\n\n**R-3 — No check that matters against a hostile publisher runs anywhere the publisher controls.** Not on their machine, not in a workflow file in their repo.\n\n**R-4 — Content drift after approval is detected and never silently served.** A push to a listed repo after approval marks the listing as drifted and re-enters review; the pin never auto-advances.\n\n**R-5 — First-party mirror repos are protected.** CI verification on every PR/push, required status check, no force-push, linear history.\n\n**R-6 — GitHub stays identity + mirror + provenance signal; the Worker stays the authority.** Attestations from GitHub are an optional trust badge the Worker verifies, never a substitute for its own pin and scan (D-055/D-056).\n\n## Design\n\n### The mechanism, before and after\n\nBefore: `client scrubs → client pushes tip → Worker stores URL → operator approves URL → installer clones tip`. Every arrow after the first trusts the previous hop; the last arrow trusts a branch that can move.\n\nAfter: `client scrubs → client pushes → Worker fetches <ref>/ at the pushed SHA, re-scans, computes tree digest, stores (sha, digest) → operator approves THAT sha (diff shown) → installer fetches THAT sha, recomputes digest, refuses on mismatch`. A GitHub App webhook on `push` re-runs the Worker-side scan at the new tip, posts a Check Run, and flags drift; it never advances the pin. Phase 4 moves the ORIGIN of bytes to R2 through the existing release gate, at which point GitHub is purely the mirror P-045 already assumes it is.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-011, P-012 | deployed |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-005, P-006, P-007 | deployed |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-006, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-5 | P-009 | live |\n| R-6 | P-010, P-011 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Make the pointer a version (no new infrastructure, no owner gate)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Worker pins content at publish: for self-describing kinds, resolve the repo's default-branch head, fetch `git/trees/<sha>?recursive=1` filtered to `<listing_ref>/`, compute a canonical tree digest (sorted path + blob sha), store `pinned_commit_sha` + `pinned_tree_digest` (worker migration 028). This is the server-side half of R-2 — a verifier, never a launderer (D-005). blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10001648 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Versioned re-publish: a publish of the same (repo, kind, ref) at a new SHA creates a new listing version and resets `review_status` to pending, instead of today's dedup-return of the old row (which makes a legitimate update impossible and a malicious one invisible). blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10001649 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Eyes on the mirror: a GitHub App on OUR infrastructure\n\n- **P-005** `dropped` OWNER-GATED: register a \"Papercusp Cupboard\" GitHub App (permissions: contents:read, checks:write, metadata:read; webhook: push). An approval of a drifted row re-pins to the reviewed SHA. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-10004625 done\n\n## Phase 3 — GitHub Actions where GitHub Actions is trustworthy\n\n- **P-009** `done` First-party mirrors (Papercusp/recipes, goals, plans, rubrics, templates-mirror): add `.github/workflows/cupboard-verify.yml` running the same scan + schema validation + `checkScript` on every PR/push; enable branch protection with that check required, linear history, force-push and deletion disabled. Install prefers R2 by content hash, GitHub as fallback with the P-002 digest check. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10001656 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` Acceptance — hostile-publisher scenario as a committed integration test: publish a clean recipe, approve it, force-push a dirty script to the mirror, attempt install → refused `content-address-mismatch`; publish with the client scrubber bypassed and an identity in the body → Worker 422 `identity_leak`; push after approval → row marked drift, install still serves the approved bytes. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-006 — note: ← WI-10001657 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Two adversaries, two different answers\n\n\"Scrubbing\" and \"malicious code\" are different threats with opposite trust directions. Identity/secret scrubbing protects the PUBLISHER from themselves — it must run locally, because a server-side scrubber would have to receive the secret in order to remove it. Malicious content protects the INSTALLER from the publisher — nothing run on the publisher's machine can help, because a hostile publisher skips `cupboard:publish-*` and pushes whatever they like. So: scrub client-side, VERIFY server-side, and PIN so that what was verified is what installs.\n\n### D-002 — What \"a plugin that runs on GitHub's servers\" can and cannot do\n\nThree different things hide in that phrase. (a) A GitHub Actions workflow in the PUBLISHER's repo runs on GitHub's servers but from a file the publisher edits — worthless against a hostile publisher, excellent as a merge gate for the FIRST-PARTY mirror repos we control (P-009). (b) A GitHub App is a webhook receiver + installation token that runs on OUR Worker: the publisher controls nothing in the check path. This is the \"remote server\" the question asks for (P-005/P-006). (c) A reusable workflow emitting a Sigstore artifact attestation binds a digest to a specific workflow ref and commit — a real provenance signal the Worker can verify, and the only Actions-based mechanism that is meaningful for third-party repos (P-010). The App is the load-bearing piece; Actions are the fast-feedback and provenance layers around it.\n\n### D-003 — The Worker is the content authority and fetches the bytes itself\n\nThe Worker already holds the publisher's token and already calls GitHub for repo metadata; fetching `<ref>/` at a SHA is one more call. It records what IT computed (SHA, tree digest, scan verdict), never what the client reports. Inherits D-055/D-056 of `shared-pot-dao-cupboard-v1-2026-09-04`: GitHub is identity + mirror, the Worker is the authority.\n\n### D-004 — Reuse the release gate; do not build a second content-address system\n\n`publish-release-gate.ts`, `validatePublishableRelease`, the migration-018 release columns, the R2 artifact store and the P-045 mirror are the content-addressed path this plan's end state needs. Phase 1's SHA/tree-digest pin is the minimal fix that needs no byte upload; Phase 4 converges on the existing gate rather than keeping two identity schemes.\n\n### D-005 — Verify, never launder, on the server\n\nA server-side check REFUSES a package that fails; it never rewrites one. Rewriting identity out of a duty body or a recipe script would publish something that reads or runs differently from what its title claims (the same ruling `identity-scrub.ts` and `recipe-export.ts` already make). The Worker's scan is a gate with a named refusal, not a sanitizer.\n\n### D-006 — Owner approved the plan; route A (su-c68e6e76 implements); recipe publishing (WI-10001553 step E) HOLDS until P-001/P-002 land\nDate: 2026-09-16\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-16 turn:self] Via AskUserQuestion: \"A. Approve — I do it myself\" and \"Hold until P-001/P-002 land\". Consequences: (1) activation audit → plans:start → Phase 1 in this session's lineage; (2) Papercusp/recipes stays EMPTY until the Worker pins content at publish and install verifies the pin — the first recipe listings must be versions, not pointers; (3) P-005 (GitHub App registration) remains owner-gated and is the only Phase 2 item an agent cannot do. Fleet routes were declined.\n\n### D-007 — Binding in-tree mutation evidence so freshness passes, and what meets_l3 actually requires\nDate: 2026-09-16\nSettled while closing P-002; applies to ANY plan item graded under plan-class-feature-ship, so other lanes should follow it rather than re-deriving.\n\n**1. A raw `testing:run` counterexample row is PERMANENTLY source-stale and will fail `freshness`.**\n`spec-test-adequacy` rates freshness `fail` if ANY bound row has `currentness.overall === 'stale'` (spec-test-adequacy.ts:1426). A tier-3 in-tree mutation probe records its counterexample row while the MUTANT is on disk, so that row's stored `sourceFingerprint` is the mutant's and can never match the restored tree. This is inherent to in-tree mutation probing, NOT a defect in the proof. Binding those raw rows deadlocks the clause: `falsifiability` demands a mutation/counterexample row (:1067) while `freshness` rejects the only one you have.\n\n**2. The resolution: re-bind the SAME durable run through `plans:bind-spec-evidence` with `measurement`, not `sourceFingerprint`.**\n`measurement: { schemaVersion:1, kind:'repo-files', sourcePaths:[...], testPaths:[...] }` makes the server measure the fingerprints and RECOMPUTE them from the canonical checkout on later reads, so the row reads `currentness=current, currentnessProvenance=server-measured`. Keep `testRunId` pointing at the original durable run so the raw measurement stays auditable. This is honest because the probe restored the source byte-identical, so the measured file set IS the baseline the probe certified. Verified: both P-002 clauses went `fail → pass` with `wouldBlock: []`.\n⚠ Pass `measurement` OR `sourceFingerprint`, never both, and omit `testFingerprint` (server-computed under measurement).\n\n**3. Do NOT try to satisfy `falsifiability` with an attested boolean.** `details.adequacy.falsifiable: true` alone rates `unknown`, and the evaluator says so explicitly: \"Binder-attested falsifiable=true ... is insufficient to demonstrate red capability\". Measured red capability is required. The system correctly refuses the shortcut.\n\n**4. `meets_l3` turns on fuzzer-vs-authored, NOT human-vs-agent.** The rung label (\"a test a machine did not write\") reads as if it excludes agent-written tests, which would make the L3 risk floor unsatisfiable for all agent work. The authoritative definition is migration 846: `meets_l3 = bool_or(verdict='pass' AND generated=false AND evidence_kind IN ('traffic','file-coverage'))`, and the column comment scopes `generated` to \"TRUE when the test was machine-generated (fuzz harness, crawler) ... without it, a fuzzer would satisfy the very criterion that exists to require human understanding of intended behaviour\". `generated=false` is therefore correct for a hand-authored intent test, agent-written or not. Note `generated=false` is the ONLY thing separating L3 from L1 (identical evidence_kind filter), which confirms the axis is authored-vs-generated.\n\n**5. Attest `coverageRungs` at the rung you actually measured.** For P-002 I claimed l1+l3 and deliberately NOT l4: l4 is `mutation_score >= 0.6` over a population, and two hand-picked targeted mutants is not a mutation score. The risk floor only needs l3.\n\n**6. Adequacy metadata must be nested under `details.adequacy.*`.** Flat `details.falsifiable` is accepted, persisted, and silently inert — the binder rejects the flat form for exactly this reason.\n\n### D-008 — P-009 live mirror population and protection limits\nDate: 2026-09-19\nMeasured 2026-09-19 against the Papercusp GitHub organization: the extant first-party content mirrors are Papercusp/recipes (public), Papercusp/goals (private, empty), Papercusp/plans (public), and Papercusp/templates (public; this is the documented templates mirror and contains rubric payloads). There is no Papercusp/rubrics or Papercusp/templates-mirror repository (gh repo view and org repo listing both return no such repository). Added and merged a dependency-free .github/workflows/cupboard-verify.yml plus .github/cupboard-verify.mjs to all four extant mirrors. The verifier scans published listing/payload bytes for identity/secret material, validates listing schemas and required payload files, and checks recipe script delimiter balance. Branch protection is live on recipes, plans, and templates: required cupboard-verify (strict), required_linear_history=true, allow_force_pushes=false, allow_deletions=false. GitHub rejects branch protection on private Papercusp/goals with HTTP 403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro; its workflow is live and passing, but protection remains unavailable until the repository visibility/plan changes. The stale five-name requirement is therefore not silently treated as satisfied; P-009 remains open for the missing-repository and private-protection residue.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-009 — P-006/P-007 build against a fake GitHub; P-005 gates only LIVE enablement\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[fleet-leader su-dd32ef9d, 2026-10-01, AUTO] P-005 (register the \"Papercusp Cupboard\" GitHub App + mint key/webhook secret) is genuinely owner-only: the App manifest flow needs a logged-in GitHub browser click and the private key is only shown once to that user. MEASURED (scratch harness .papercusp/scratch/p007-spike: Worker entry importing tooldef parse-check checkScript; wrangler 4.86.0, compat_date 2025-09-01, flags [nodejs_compat], typescript = @typescript/typescript6@6.0.2). (1) SIZE: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` = 10859 KiB raw / 1740 KiB gzip — under the 3 MB free and 10 MB paid compressed limits. (2) VANILLA BUILD FAILS: TypeScript init throws `ReferenceError: __filename is not defined` (typescript.js getNodeSystem -> isFileSystemCaseSensitive) because the Worker bundle is ESM with no CJS `__filename`. (3) THE FAILURE IS SILENT: parse-check.ts ensureParseCheckReady() caches the half-initialised module as `{}` (`m.default ?? m`), so every later checkScript silently takes the REGEX FALLBACK — measured: hasParseErrors:true and the destructured call `const {coord}=tools; coord.send()` is MISSED (refs [plans:get, workItems.list] only; calls []). That is exactly the evasion class authority analysis exists to catch, so a Worker that 'works' in this state under-reports authority. (4) FIX: wrangler.toml `[define] __filename = \"\\\"/typescript.js\\\"\"`, `__dirname = \"\\\"/\\\"\"` -> verified A/B by wrangler's own hot reload on the config change: TS initialises, hasParseErrors:false, refs include coord.send, calls[] fully resolved with literal args; cold dynamic import 363 ms, checkScript 11 ms first / 0-1 ms warm. Dynamic import is lazy under esbuild so no cost at Worker global startup. RULING: (a) land checkScript IN the Worker (content-pin.ts seam, kind==='recipe', over the blob text already fetched for the P-003 scan) — no Container/Queue consumer. (b) Harden ensureParseCheckReady to THROW when the loaded module lacks createSourceFile, so a failed init can never degrade silently to regex; the Worker maps that throw to a refusal/unresolved=true, never to authorityUnresolved=false. (c) Recurrence guards: a vitest asserting wrangler.toml carries the __filename/__dirname defines, and one asserting ensureParseCheckReady rejects on a broken module. The independent grader and the outside-lineage approval reviewer can still reject this; their verdict governs.\nMeasured: apps/operator-public/src/routes/github-webhook.ts:88 returns 503 app_not_configured when any of GITHUB_APP_ID / GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY / GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent, and apps/operator-public/src/__tests__/github-webhook.test.ts:278 pins it ('fails closed with 503 app_not_configured when %s is absent') — reviewer 2's count of zero fail-closed cases was wrong. hostile-publisher.test.ts has exactly four it() blocks (L264, L280, L305, L319), mapped R-1, R-3, R-2, R-4 in rev 4. Not deployed: the Worker ships by manual `wrangler deploy` (apps/operator-public/package.json deploy script); this plan makes no deployed-plane claim (D-009).\n\n### D-016 — RETRACTION of D-015's plane downgrade: keep R-1/R-3/R-4 on the deployed plane; resubmit only the non-weakening edits\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[fleet-leader su-dd32ef9d, AUTO] The outside-lineage reviewer objected (WI-10004858 post 1153439) to the rev3->4 amendment previewed in thread-post:1153435. I ACCEPT points 1, 2 and 4 and RETRACT the parts of D-015 they hit.\nFALSE PREMISE (mine): D-015 and the amendment reason said the Worker is 'not deployed, D-009' and used that to move R-1/R-3/R-4 from deployed to tree. D-009 says no such thing; it only gates the GitHub App (P-005). I never measured whether the operator-public Worker is deployed or what code it serves, so I had no basis to claim 'not deployed'. Moving the plane lowers what 'healthy' means for 3 of 6 mandatory bars (a green unit test against a fake GitHub would then suffice) while requiredScope still said deployed, so each criterion also contradicted itself. Retracted.\nTHE R-5 DEFECT is real: my numbered-marker RATING BASIS said 'rate from the bound proof of the named test files and mutation-probe rows', but R-5 has no test files (instrument check, method names the gh api outputs). R-5 keeps its own method's basis.\nWHAT SURVIVES (reviewer accepted): per-bar TEST MAP text, numbered BROKEN-if falsifier markers, the scope-limit disclosure that the live GitHub leg is unproven, and the R-2/R-6 edits.\nPLAN: resubmit rev4 WITHOUT any plane change (R-1/R-3/R-4 stay deployed), R-5 rating basis fixed. THEN MEASURE what the deployed plane actually has: whether the operator-public Worker is deployed, which commit it serves, and whether an install against it can be recorded as deployed-plane evidence for R-1. Open consequence to disclose: if R-3/R-4 genuinely require the live webhook leg, they cannot rate healthy until WI-10004856 lands, and D-014 unblocks the item gate but NOT the acceptance gate. That is an honest outcome, not one to paper over; if the deployed Worker's publish-time scan and install-time pin check satisfy R-3/R-4's outcome without the App, say so with deployed evidence. D-015's other findings stand.\n\n### D-017 — MEASURED deployed plane (2026-10-01): cupboard.papercusp.com serves the 2026-09-26 build, which predates this plan; no unilateral deploy from the shared tree. R-1/R-3/R-4 stay deployed and cannot rate healthy until the Worker bundle ships\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[fleet-leader su-dd32ef9d, AUTO, measured] Executes the MEASURE step of D-016.\nMeasured: `curl -X POST https://cupboard.papercusp.com/github/webhook` -> http=404 size=13, byte-identical to a control `curl -X POST .../github/webhook-nonexistent-ctl` -> 404; in-tree apps/operator-public/src/routes/github-webhook.ts:88 registers `route.post('/github/webhook')` and returns 503 `app_not_configured` when GITHUB_APP_ID / GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY / GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET are absent (pinned by github-webhook.test.ts:278). So the serving Worker does not contain the route.\nMEASUREMENTS (read-only, 13:45-13:55Z): (1) The Worker IS deployed and live: GET https://cupboard.papercusp.com/listings -> 200, 30 listings; `wrangler deployments list` (OAuth login, d1/workers write scopes) shows the newest deployment created 2026-09-26T22:13Z, version a4839b71-4f92-4cd6-aefb-431ef2b687b1. (2) It predates this plan's code: the POST/control pair above; listing rows carry no `verified_by` field and `pinned_commit_sha` is null on all 30 listings. (3) Remote D1 (`wrangler d1 execute papercusp-cupboard --remote`, sqlite_master) lacks transparency_live / transparency_statements / transparency_attestations / treasury_transfer_gate, so migrations 040/042/043 are unapplied and 038/039/041 (additive ADD COLUMNs on harnesses) are very likely unapplied. The first GET /github/webhook 404 I saw was a method mismatch (route is POST-only) and is NOT evidence; the POST/control pair is.\nBLAST RADIUS (`git log --since=2026-09-26T22:13Z` over apps/operator-public/src + migrations): 9 migrations (035-043) and 26 non-test source files. This plan owns roughly 038/039/041 plus content-pin, attestation, github-app, github-webhook and the listings/self-describing-artifacts edits. The rest belongs to other plans: treasury-store / transfer-gate / routes/treasury (owner capital gate P-034 of agent-economy-flywheel), ledger-chain, commerce stores, transparency, identity surface (035-037, 040, 042, 043).\nRULING (best default, disclosed): I do NOT run `wrangler deploy` or `d1 execute --remote` from the shared tree for this plan. A deploy cannot be scoped to this plan's files or migrations, and it would ship another plan's unreleased payment-rail and transparency code plus irreversible D1 migrations to a live public marketplace on its behalf. That is a release decision for the Worker bundle as a whole, not an acceptance-ceremony step. wrangler is authenticated on this box, so this is a sequencing/ownership call, not a capability gap.\nCONSEQUENCES: (a) R-1/R-3/R-4 stay evidencePlane 'deployed' (D-016) and rate on deployed reality: until the bundle ships, R-1 (pin + install-time digest check) is NOT observable on the deployed plane; R-3/R-4 additionally need the GitHub App (WI-10004856) for their live leg. (b) The ship gate stays closed on those bars. Not papered over. (c) Tracked by a needs-human release work-item (named in WI-10004858's checkpoint) listing the bundle, the migration list and the remote-state check that must precede it. (d) Everything not dependent on the deploy proceeds: the rev4 amendment (no plane changes), R-5 gh-api evidence, the final-sweep audit.\n\n### D-018 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: amend-3ce3d73f632de5aa14bdd7c2\nRequest-Hash: d01e7a90a258c9c1994f105d1247428bd4f7a5b0c718f82e64794febf5062646\nActor: su-dd32ef9d-2329-4f7b-9cfd-a5f685c1062a\nReason: Fold in the outside-lineage reviewer's accepted points (WI-10004858 post 1153439) and D-015/D-016/D-017: numbered BROKEN-if falsifier markers that name the tests which make each observable (replacing the tautological template), deployed-plane probes + explicit rating rules for R-1/R-3/R-4, the unproven-live-GitHub-leg scope limit on R-3/R-4 (WI-10004856), and R-5 rated on its own method basis (gh api outputs) with a matching replication. NO evidencePlane, requiredScope or check change: R-1/R-3/R-4 stay on the deployed plane (retracts the rev3->4 plane downgrade previewed in thread-post:1153435).\nApproved-By: su-98d8df9a-b7ec-42a2-bf94-f299c21dcade\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1153523\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T13:55:36.879Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 54 → 55\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-019 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: amend-d1cded3b9c36c6291ba83208\nRequest-Hash: a68a6b1bffc84212629aa137b02f72a716df223f5cd45b08680a0a5a41fbe323\nActor: su-dd32ef9d-2329-4f7b-9cfd-a5f685c1062a\nReason: Rev 5: fold in the rev-4 vetting critique (conv-mupln3n4, post 1153532). R-1 gets its OWN deployed check (the hostile-mirror install replayed against the deployed Worker; no version endpoint exists) and a RATING line (healthy only with the plan's Worker bundle deployed AND the hostile install refused; a Worker predating the plan = broken as in rev 4, digest-mismatched install succeeds = broken, unreachable host = unknown), and marker (6) no longer probes the webhook/verified_by (those are R-3/R-4/R-6 outcomes). R-3 model gains its missing subject. All edits tighten; no evidencePlane, requiredScope or check change (D-016).\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-00f5d2c5-2e4b-4b47-861d-e1e1f91941d6\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1153554\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T14:07:39.077Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 55 → 56\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-020 — Rev-5 AUTO-BAR clauses accepted (provenance-only promotion); proof is re-bound after the WI-10004701 final sweep; deployed/live-plane bars stay gated\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[fleet-leader su-dd32ef9d, AUTO, measured] Sequence so far: rubric rev 5 applied 14:25Z (approvalRef thread-post:1153554), meta attestation scorecard EI-24787562111894260 grading-audit PASSED 14:30Z (audit EI-24787710868482134), after which the ship gate's contract codes moved off vetting to bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted. Executed the gate's own repair: plans:set-specs lifecycleStatus:active for all 14 draft AUTO-BAR-R-N-P-xxx clauses at their current revision (expectedRevision echoed; behavior/falsifier/acceptanceRef/sourceBar echoed unchanged). Result: every clause advanced one revision; AUTO-BAR-R-6-P-010 carried its 4 bound proofs forward (evidenceCarriedForward=4); the other 13 had none to carry, as expected.\nWhy all 14, not one per bar: the gate named R-1 first, and per-bar 'mapped clause' is not documented as 'any one'; accepting every mapped clause costs nothing and cannot weaken a bar (the clauses are the bars' own derived text).\nRemaining gate codes, read from the ship refusal after acceptance: proof_missing/proof_inadequate on R-1..R-6 (R-6 only inadequate: proof is bound, adequacy not yet passed), evidence_plane_unmet on R-1/R-3/R-4 (deployed) and R-5 (live), grading_missing on all six, author_verdict_missing.\nNEXT ORDER: (1) wait for the member's WI-10004701 final sweep (it rebinds stale rows; re-binding AUTO-BAR proof before it ends would be redone); (2) bind one proven clause per bar by reusing the sweep's fresh test_runs (plans:bind-spec-evidence fromTestRun); (3) adequacy evaluation + cards; (4) R-5 live-plane gh-api measurement; (5) R-1/R-3/R-4 deployed-plane stays unmet until the Worker bundle ships (WI-10004875, owner/release decision, D-017); the bars are NOT weakened (D-016).\nNothing here is an owner directive; it is my own sequencing.\n\n### D-021 — Deploy preflight measured; no unilateral Worker deploy; correction: grading_missing is independent acceptance grading, not adequacy audits\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [fleet-leader su-dd32ef9d, AUTO, measured 15:5xZ]\n\nRETRACTION (mine, 15:48Z checkpoint + turn report): I said R-2/R-5/R-6 were blocked at ship only by bar_snapshot_grading_missing and that it would clear when their spec-test-adequacy grading audits landed. WRONG. Those audits pass quickly (R-5 card EI-24792183665548953 audit passed 15:46:33Z). bar_snapshot_grading_missing is the INDEPENDENT acceptance-rubric grading (a non-implementer), which set-plan-status recruits only once the refusal reads acceptance_ungraded; it cannot clear while R-1/R-3/R-4 carry proof_inadequate / evidence_plane_unmet / proof_missing. So the single critical path to ship is R-1/R-3/R-4 on the deployed plane.\n\nPREFLIGHT for the Worker deploy (all read-only, measured): (1) apps/operator-public has 0 uncommitted files; last commit 9d037f63cc 14:48Z. (2) wrangler is authenticated (OAuth) on this box; last production deployment a4839b71 on 2026-09-26T22:13Z authored by the account owner. (3) remote D1 papercusp-cupboard d1_migrations ends at 034_versioned_publish; harnesses lacks approved_commit_sha (038) and verified_by (041), so 035-043 are cleanly pending, no partial state. (4) wrangler deploy --dry-run builds the bundle. (5) rollback = wrangler rollback to a4839b71, code only; D1 migrations are not reversible.\n\nRULING: no unilateral deploy yet. Reasons: the account's Workers Paid status is UNVERIFIED and the bundle needs it (P-007 in-Worker TypeScript parse, ~360ms cold CPU; on a free plan the live Worker could start failing requests), the bundle applies 9 irreversible migrations including other plans' treasury/ledger/transparency tables, and the owner personally operates this deploy. Re-asked on the human coord channel with a one-word answer (A deploy / B rescope R-1,R-3,R-4 to tree / C drop live leg). Default if still unanswered: bars stay unweakened (D-016), plan stays awaiting-acceptance.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"gmail-oauth-system-browser-2026-09-05-acceptance","title":"Gmail OAuth system-browser repair acceptance","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-17","owner":"su-6446a52e-32ea-4299-96db-2a92010799ad","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Gmail OAuth system-browser repair acceptance\nslug: gmail-oauth-system-browser-2026-09-05-acceptance\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-17\nupdated: 2026-09-17\nowner: su-6446a52e-32ea-4299-96db-2a92010799ad\n---\n\n# Gmail OAuth system-browser repair acceptance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric).
