Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hn-ack-triage-2026-09-18","title":"HN application acknowledgements — measure the reply-worthy population under a scoped Gmail grant","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-18","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: HN application acknowledgements — measure the reply-worthy population under a scoped Gmail grant\nslug: hn-ack-triage-2026-09-18\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-18\nupdated: 2026-09-18\npersonalScopes: personal:mail\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft, inert. This plan declares exactly one Personal Vault scope — `personal:mail` — and nothing in it can read anything until the owner previews and approves that grant in Settings → Personal Vault.\n\n**Next:** Owner approves the grant, then P-001–P-004 run *as a plan run* (the grant only authorizes a plan-run session — see D-001).\n\n⚠ **This plan does not send mail, and must not be extended to.** See D-003.\n\n## Background\n\nThe owner's HN outreach lane (WI-10001783) has sent job applications and received a body of automated acknowledgement email in reply. A prior session announced an isolation of how many of those acknowledgements come from a human and actually invite a response — and never finished it. The resulting figure (\"~3 of 857\") is **unsourced** and must not be quoted or planned around; re-deriving it honestly is this plan's entire purpose.\n\nThat measurement needs read access to the owner's synced mailbox, which is default-deny. This plan exists because a plan-template grant is the only owner-facing way to open it.\n\n## Phase 1 — Measure\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Confirm the grant is live from inside the plan run: call `personal:search` with scope `personal:mail` and assert `allowed: true`. If it refuses, STOP and report the refusal reason verbatim — never fall back to a direct SQL read of `harness_shared.personal_documents`, which is the open bypass defect WI-10001796.\n- **P-002** `todo` Derive the acknowledgement population: count messages that are replies to the outreach sends, partitioned by automated-noreply vs human-addressable sender. Report counts together with the query that produced them, so the number is falsifiable. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Within the human-addressable partition, isolate the ones that ask a question or request an action. Quote the distinguishing signal per message; do not infer intent from subject line alone. blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` Deliver the measurement to the owner as counts plus per-message evidence, and STOP. Recommend nothing about sending. blocked-by: P-003\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The grant authorizes a plan RUN, not an interactive agent session\nDate: 2026-09-18\n`authorizePersonalAccess` derives a `plan-template` principal *only* from `ctx.planRunSessionId`, which the plan-agent runner supplies as `?plan_run=<sessionId>` on the MCP URL and which resolves through `harness_shared.plan_runs`. An ordinary interactive session has no `plan_runs` row, so it is never covered by this grant no matter who approves it. The Phase 1 work must therefore execute as an actual plan run of this plan. Approving this grant does NOT hand any interactive agent session access to the mailbox.\n\n### D-002 — Scope is `personal:mail` alone, and this plan does not reuse an existing grant\nDate: 2026-09-18\nA live `plan-template` grant already exists for `meeting-prep-brief-2026-08-22` carrying gmail + calendar + contacts. Running this work under that principal would launder consent the owner gave for meeting preparation into job-application processing. This plan declares its own narrower scope and stands or falls on its own approval.\n\n### D-003 — Measuring is in scope; replying is NOT, pending verified owner authority\nDate: 2026-09-18\nThere is a verified standing owner instruction (2026-09-16, interactive): do not answer recruiters on Avi's behalf. WI-10001783's body asserts a 2026-09-17 turn superseded it for acknowledgement replies, but that assertion is agent-authored, is flagged UNVERIFIED OWNER ATTRIBUTION on the item's own checkpoint, and could not be located in the session transcript index on either the verbatim or the semantic leg. An unverified supersession must not serve as permission for an outward-facing irreversible act — mail sent as the owner cannot be unsent. This plan therefore measures and reports only; sending stays walled until the owner states it in their own words.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22","title":"Acceptance BAR — BYOC cloud workspaces — local provisioning, GCP first, AWS/Azure parity, then app.papercusp.com","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-19","owner":"su-02bcfdcc-6da5-445c-8b3d-5d81b66010f2","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — BYOC cloud workspaces — local provisioning, GCP first, AWS/Azure parity, then app.papercusp.com\nslug: acceptance-byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-19\nupdated: 2026-10-02\nowner: su-02bcfdcc-6da5-445c-8b3d-5d81b66010f2\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — BYOC cloud workspaces — local provisioning, GCP first, AWS/Azure parity, then app.papercusp.com\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Reproduce the raw MCP envelope contract from the result-format implementation and the interrupted session evidence.\n2. Update `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/precompact-managed-carry.mjs` to pin `_meta.format=json` and accept structured results as defense in depth.\n3. Extend `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/precompact-managed-carry.test.ts` with request-shape and structured-result regression cases.\n4. Run focused Vitest plus relevant type/lint/install-path checks and record evidence on WI-10001961.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-001 | live |\n| R-002 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-004 | P-004 | deployed |\n\n- **P-001** `done` document the measured interruption chain and root-cause correction — note: Session transcript and live source evidence establish the hook veto/turn_aborted chain; no human interrupt evidence.\n- **P-002** `done` pin JSON result negotiation and support structured MCP result envelopes — note: Pinned params._meta.format=json and added structuredContent parsing defense-in-depth.\n- **P-003** `done` add and run regression tests for all managed carry result classes — note: Regression tests cover JSON text, structured result, refusal, malformed output, and transport failure.\n- **P-004** `done` verify installation/projection and complete WI-10001961 with structured evidence — note: Official installer published the source hook to the active shared Codex hook path; source and installed SHA-256 match.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"desktop-release-0-0-21-alpha-2026-09-19","title":"Ship Papercusp desktop 0.0.21-alpha","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-19","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Ship Papercusp desktop 0.0.21-alpha\nslug: desktop-release-0-0-21-alpha-2026-09-19\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-19\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Superseded under D-001: 0.0.21-alpha was historically published 2026-09-21 and all 7 artifacts were withdrawn 2026-10-06 under open-source-release-2026-09-29#D-032. Current public latest offers 0.0.25; history retains 0.0.21 with no artifacts; 7 retired artifact paths return 404. P-001 remains done; P-002..005 dropped; acceptance rubric retired. Withdrawal regression tests: 5 passed, 0 failed (testRunId 21251148).\n\n**Next:** No execution remains on this superseded release plan; preserve withdrawal and historical evidence. Future release work belongs to its independently authorized current release plan.\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Exact release identity.** Cut desktop version 0.0.21-alpha from an exact clean superproject SHA; do not treat source tags or nightly tags as published artifacts.\n\n**R-002 — Durable blocker resolution.** Resolve the current assembled-bundle gitleaks failure and any seed/cut blocker with a narrow, tested fix; preserve fail-closed identity and credential gates.\n\n**R-003 — Parallel platform builds.** Launch Linux, macOS, and Windows legs in parallel; each leg must complete its own smoke verification before publication.\n\n**R-004 — Two-surface publication.** Publish updater artifacts plus latest.json to R2, then publish release history; verify both public surfaces byte-for-byte or by their canonical verification scripts.\n\n**R-005 — Honest closure.** Record exact source SHA, artifact names, sizes, hashes, publish URLs, and observed live version.\n\n## Design\n\nUse the maintained release path: exact-SHA isolated cut checkout, release:cut orchestration, per-platform smoke gates, bin/upload-release.sh for updater bytes, and bin/publish-release-history.sh for human/update-history pages. Never manually mutate release tags or bypass red gates without a measured owner-walled necessity.\n\n- **P-001** `done` Diagnose and durably fix the current release cut blocker; run focused regression tests. — note: ← WI-10001909 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `dropped` Reconcile the green checkpoint and exact source SHA; create or select a clean isolated cut checkout. — note: D-001: Historical 0.0.21-alpha shipment was withdrawn under open-source-release-2026-09-29#D-032; repeating these execution/publication steps would restore withdrawn downloads. Preserve original evidence; no new acceptance pass.\n- **P-003** `dropped` Cut 0.0.21-alpha with Linux, macOS, and Windows legs in parallel and capture artifact manifest. — note: D-001: Historical 0.0.21-alpha shipment was withdrawn under open-source-release-2026-09-29#D-032; repeating these execution/publication steps would restore withdrawn downloads. Preserve original evidence; no new acceptance pass.\n- **P-004** `dropped` Smoke-verify each platform artifact and publish updater bytes plus latest.json to R2. — note: D-001: Historical 0.0.21-alpha shipment was withdrawn under open-source-release-2026-09-29#D-032; repeating these execution/publication steps would restore withdrawn downloads. Preserve original evidence; no new acceptance pass.\n- **P-005** `dropped` Publish and verify release-history surfaces; record hashes, URLs, and final shipment evidence. — note: D-001: Historical 0.0.21-alpha shipment was withdrawn under open-source-release-2026-09-29#D-032; repeating these execution/publication steps would restore withdrawn downloads. Preserve original evidence; no new acceptance pass.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-001 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-002 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-004 | P-004, P-005 | live |\n| R-005 | P-005 | live |\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- 0.0.21-alpha latest.json is live and advertises all shipped platforms.\n- release-history history.json contains desktop-v0.0.21-alpha.\n- Per-platform artifacts have smoke evidence and matching published hashes.\n- The green checkpoint and deploy position are recorded where applicable.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Preserve D-032 withdrawal; reconcile the historical release without re-cutting\nDate: 2026-10-15\nMeasured 2026-10-15 during owner-authorized exact-plan execution (WI-6554700010014311): current plan has no other live claims or declared owner; native adv_sessions has only this session 44175 on this plan; exact acceptance payload.planSlug query has only this session's reconciliation item. WI-10001909 records original publication at 2026-09-21T04:21:54.729Z with a documented owner-directed Linux VM smoke exception. The release registry writer stores version 0.0.21 and channel alpha separately; registry read confirms historical source b5e2b1fbccf06ed45dba11589d9ee7619f3d3662, publication time, and all 7 registry artifacts withdrawn under open-source-release-2026-09-29#D-032 at 2026-10-06T12:14:55Z.\n\nGoverning decision D-032 explicitly withdraws all superseded 0.0.8–0.0.24 distributed artifacts, preserves history entries, and archives objects. Re-running P-002..P-005 as new publication would reverse that decision. Preserve P-001's historical completion and retire the stale remaining execution steps as dropped, then supersede this obsolete plan via supported lifecycle tools. This is a lifecycle reconciliation, not a new successful acceptance grade. Do not restore latest.json to 0.0.21, rebuild, upload, bypass independent acceptance, or touch the held LIVE_GATE_OPS lane (WI-10006055). Original requirements and historical evidence remain intact.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hn-outreach-800-target-completion-2026-09-19","title":"Complete the 800-target HN outreach campaign","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-19","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Complete the 800-target HN outreach campaign\nslug: hn-outreach-800-target-completion-2026-09-19\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-19\nupdated: 2026-09-19\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Reconcile the full campaign.** Treat the harvested 787-row post-liveness queue as the campaign population; classify every row into sent, eligible-to-compose/send, duplicate, bounced/quarantined, excluded by the post or peer coverage, or unresolved with explicit evidence. Do not silently treat the current 221-row sender queue as the whole campaign.\n\n**R-002 — Repair and regenerate safely.** Fix the shared generic composer defect that emits the obsolete three-line signature, add a real selfcheck that guards signature parity, then regenerate only unsent eligible drafts without changing the record of already-sent mail.\n\n**R-003 — Preserve irreversible-send gates.** Every live send must pass the real instruction extractor, routing exclusions, quality gate, exact dedup census, bounce/quarantine checks, approved style, exclusive sender lock, 90-second minimum pacing, 400/day cap, and circuit breaker. Never bypass a gate to increase volume.\n\n**R-004 — Continue autonomously to a terminal census.** Keep AUTO and the tracked loop active until every campaign row is terminally partitioned and every eligible gated message has either been accepted or recorded as an explicit transport failure requiring reconciliation.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing extractor → routing-table → deterministic composer → quality gate → review decisions → guarded run-live pipeline. Reuse the existing sendqueue, tracker, dedup, bounce, pacing, and journal surfaces; add no parallel sender or policy store. First fix the shared signature constructor and guard it in compose.selfcheck. Then enrich unresolved historical target identities from cached HN post headers using the existing conservative company-name rules, feed only reliable identities through the real instruction/routing path, compose and gate unsent rows, rebuild the queue atomically, and let run-live deliver only the exact eligible census.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-002 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | live |\n| R-004 | P-003, P-004 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Root-cause repair\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Fix the shared generic signature constructor, add a recurrence selfcheck, and prove already-sent draft records remain byte-identical.\n\n## Phase 2 — Full inventory recovery\n\n- **P-002** `todo` Recover reliable company identities and instruction/routing records for the unresolved historical target rows, preserving exclusions and quarantines.\n- **P-003** `todo` Compose and quality-gate every newly eligible unsent row, rebuild the guarded sender queue, and produce an exact full-population partition.\n\n## Phase 3 — Autonomous delivery\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Run the guarded sender continuously at the approved pace until the exact census is empty, reconcile failures, and close with durable ledger evidence.\n\n## Acceptance\n\nThe campaign is complete only when a machine-readable census partitions the full harvested population without residue, the composer and sender selfchecks pass, no already-sent draft changed, and the guarded sender reports no remaining eligible row.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-a-results-envelope-must-never-report-ok-true-while-an-item-i-2026-09-20","title":"Acceptance BAR — A No implementation, activation, fleet launch, or plan start is authorized by this draft.\n\n**Next:** Owner reviews the scope and either approves revisions or authorizes activation and implementation planning.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10002373 — Audit the current acceptance gate, rubric authority resolver, obligation provider, and plan status transition surfaces; identify the exact extension points and existing Work on Everything branches. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002374 — Implement generic idempotent creation/reconciliation of a high-priority plan-acceptance obligation for `acceptance_ungraded` and `bar_snapshot_grading_missing`. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002375 — Implement rubric-driven independent versus owner-authorized grading, including recruitment and wake of the required independent grader. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002376 — Enforce the acceptance state machine: scorecard emitted, all bars satisfied, and explicit `shipped` transition are all required. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002377 — Define and expose the live shared-provider counts for active plan-execution agents, actionable plans awaiting delegation, plans awaiting acceptance, and active drain fleets. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002378 — Update the plan-agent brief to use live counts and the acceptance-first delegation priority order, including idle/no-work reporting and no idle spawning. <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002379 — Add focused, integration, and regression coverage for generic routing, rubric authority, grader wake/recruitment, acceptance persistence, explicit shipment, live counts, and priority ordering; remove… <!-- P-007 -->\n## Background\n\nAcceptance routing and plan-agent delegation must be platform behavior shared by every plan. Existing acceptance-grading work addressed narrower failure modes, including independent-grader stalls and a grading cascade that did not execute. This plan generalizes the desired behavior across all plans and removes any dependency on Work on Everything-specific exceptions.\n\nThe system should use the existing shared obligation provider, canonical plan reads, and canonical fleet assignments as the sources of truth. Prompts and briefs must not embed stale counts or goal-specific routing rules.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Generic acceptance obligation creation.** When any plan reaches `awaiting-acceptance` and its gate reports a grader-gap code (`acceptance_ungraded` or `self_graded_only`), automatically create or reconcile a high-priority plan-acceptance obligation for that plan, ranked as grader work. Author-repair gate codes — including `acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready`, the gate code through which the bar-snapshot condition `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` surfaces — rank as upstream author work and must NOT recruit a grader.\n\n**R-2 — Rubric-controlled grader authority.** The plan's rubric determines whether the obligation requires an independent grader or permits owner-authorized grading. Routing is behaviourally generic: two plans with identical rubric authority produce the same routing decision whatever their goal identity — a Work on Everything relationship being one instance, not the rule.\n\n**R-3 — Independent grader recruitment and wake.** When the rubric requires independence, the obligation provider recruits and wakes the required independent grader, with idempotent behavior when the obligation or grader is already active.\n\n**R-4 — Acceptance is a guarded state, not an implied shipment.** A plan remains in `awaiting-acceptance` until the required grader emits the scorecard, all acceptance bars are satisfied, and the plan is explicitly moved to `shipped`. A scorecard or passing bars alone must not auto-ship the plan.\n\n**R-5 — Live plan-agent counts in the brief.** The plan-agent brief receives live values for active plan-execution agents, actionable plans awaiting delegation, plans awaiting acceptance, and active drain fleets. Values come from the shared obligation provider plus canonical `fleet:assignments` and plan reads taken at decision time; prompt literals and stale cached counts are not authoritative.\n\n**R-6 — Acceptance-first delegation policy.** Over real plan and agent state, the plan-agent brief produces the correct DIRECTED NEXT ACTION, not merely prose that mentions one. When a plan is awaiting acceptance, the directed action is to finish that acceptance flow first, even though every delegation precondition holds simultaneously. When that acceptance is settled and actionable plans exist with no live plan-execution agents, the same brief directs selecting the next plan and launching or attaching a plan fleet. When no actionable plans exist, it directs reporting idle or no work rather than spawning idle agents. The priority order is acceptance first, next actionable plan delegation second, idle reporting third.\n\n**R-7 — Regression coverage defends the product, and no parallel path survives.** Every behaviour these bars promise is defended by a committed test that fails when the PRODUCT is broken, not merely when this rubric's own registry is edited: removing gate-triggered obligation routing, rubric-controlled grader authority, grader wake and recruitment, acceptance-state persistence, the explicit-shipment guard, live count sourcing, or the delegation priority order from the implementation causes at least one committed test to fail. No Work on Everything-only implementation path remains in the acceptance-routing decision, and no second, parallel obligation system is introduced: every raised acceptance obligation, grader-gap and author-repair alike, is produced by the one shared obligation provider.\n\n**R-8 — Acceptance-gate non-silence, split by gate class.** A plan that reaches `awaiting-acceptance` always progresses to a terminal disposition without an operator noticing a stall. Where the gate reports a grader gap (`acceptance_ungraded`, `self_graded_only`), the obligation is raised, an eligible independent grader is recruited and picks the work up, a scorecard is emitted against the active rubric, and the plan ends in `shipped` or an explicit non-ship disposition. Where the gate instead reports author repair, that repair is raised as an OWNED obligation against the author under the same non-silence guarantee — never left as a refusal that only a human or a passing agent would notice. No gate disposition leaves a plan with neither a recruited grader nor a raised author obligation.\n\n## Design\n\n### Reuse and boundaries\n\nExtend the shared obligation provider and existing plan/fleet read surfaces rather than adding a parallel goal-specific coordinator, prompt counter, or bespoke Work on Everything route. The acceptance gate remains the source of the triggering facts; the obligation provider owns durable obligation creation and grader recruitment/wake; plan status transitions remain explicit and authoritative.\n\n### Acceptance routing flow\n\n1. Observe a plan in `awaiting-acceptance` with gate findings.\n2. If either `acceptance_ungraded` or `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` is present, upsert one high-priority plan-acceptance obligation keyed to the plan and acceptance context.\n3. Resolve grader authority from the plan's rubric.\n4. For independent grading, recruit or wake the required independent grader; for owner-authorized grading, route to the authorized owner path.\n5. Accept the plan only after the required scorecard and all bars are present and passing.\n6. Require an explicit transition to `shipped`; keep the plan in acceptance otherwise.\n\n### Live delegation brief flow\n\n1. Read live plan-agent and fleet state from canonical provider surfaces.\n2. Compute the acceptance frontier before selecting any new actionable plan.\n3. If acceptance work exists, complete or dispatch that flow before new plan execution.\n4. Otherwise, if live plan-execution agents are zero and an actionable plan exists, select the next plan and launch or attach a plan fleet.\n5. If no actionable plan exists, report idle/no work and do not spawn.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-003 | live |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005, P-006 | live |\n| R-6 | P-006 | live |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-002, P-003, P-004, P-007 | live |\n\n## Non-goals\n\n- Do not create a second obligation system or a second fleet-count source.\n- Do not auto-ship plans from a scorecard or a passing bar snapshot.\n- Do not spawn agents when no actionable plan exists.\n- Do not preserve Work on Everything-specific routing when the generic platform path covers the same behavior.\n- Do not activate or implement this plan as part of drafting it.\n\n## Phase 1 — Acceptance routing foundation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit the current acceptance gate, rubric authority resolver, obligation provider, and plan status transition surfaces; identify the exact extension points and existing Work on Everything branches. importance: high — note: ← WI-10002373 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement generic idempotent creation/reconciliation of a high-priority plan-acceptance obligation for `acceptance_ungraded` and `bar_snapshot_grading_missing`. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: Implemented and shipped via WI-10002374 (completionAuthority=committed). The isDelegable/isActionable split landed in packages/operator-core/lib/agent-obligation-providers.ts; both AUTO-BAR spec clauses graded verdict=pass with wouldBlock=[], terminal scorecards EI-23955177761842821 (R-1) and EI-23955178980387630 (R-3) emitted, and both grading audits settled state=passed via the relevance router.\n- **P-003** `done` Implement rubric-driven independent versus owner-authorized grading, including recruitment and wake of the required independent grader. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: Both acceptance bars implemented and verified. R-2 (rubric-driven grading authority, tree plane) landed earlier; R-3 (independent-grader pickup confirmed from the grader's own LATER activity, live plane) landed this turn as a separate seam per D-011 — inbox-wake.ts untouched. Evidence: 81/81 tests (runId bb3a31c5), live probe 6/6 PASS against the real database with the production reader, typecheck status=clean. Findings + two traps recorded as D-012.\n- **P-004** `done` Enforce the acceptance state machine: scorecard emitted, all bars satisfied, and explicit `shipped` transition are all required. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: R-4 (plane: tree) satisfied and now GUARDED by a new paired-control test, 6/6 green, lint:tsc status=clean. Detail in rationale.\n\nWHAT I FOUND (code truth, read before asserting): all three conditions the item names are already enforced, and the one R-4 isolates was UNGUARDED. Two independent mechanisms make `shipped` unreachable by evidence alone, and the guard pins BOTH because either alone is a silent hole: (1) the derivation is report-only - reconcilePlanLifecycle (libs/generic/plan-parser/src/lifecycle.ts:515) returns a `disposition` about a stored status and never returns or rewrites one, so a drained plan with a satisfied acceptance signal is REPORTED agreed-upon, never promoted; (2) the write is gated on an explicit request - shouldEvaluateAcceptanceGate (agent-tools/plans/set-plan-status.ts:266) arms the acceptance gate exactly when a caller names status:'shipped', wh…\n\n## Phase 2 — Live delegation brief\n\n- **P-005** `done` Define and expose the live shared-provider counts for active plan-execution agents, actionable plans awaiting delegation, plans awaiting acceptance, and active drain fleets. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-006** `done` Update the plan-agent brief to use live counts and the acceptance-first delegation priority order, including idle/no-work reporting and no idle spawning. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: R-5 and R-6 both satisfied on the `live` plane. Findings recorded as D-014 — read it before P-007.\n\nSHIPPED: context-bundle.ts (the plan-agent launch seed) gained a DELEGATION POSTURE block. `renderDelegationPostureBlock` is pure/exported (modelled on the existing renderInputsBlock), renders the four counts through `renderDelegationCount`, and states the priority order acceptance-first / delegation-second / idle-third. `buildPlanContextBundle` reads `readDelegationCounts` in the render pass via an injectable `readDelegation` seam. The block sits ABOVE the plan body on purpose: the plan text is what most reads as 'go do this'.\n\nR-5 evidence: the live probe brackets the render with two provider reads and compares all four counts only when the bracketing reads agree (the counts are live in a busy workspace, so a naive read-render-compare would falsely falsify a correct implementation — and on the first run one count genuinely DID move mid-probe). Final run: agents 9/9/9, delegation 139/1…\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification and migration\n\n- **P-007** `done` Add focused, integration, and regression coverage for generic routing, rubric authority, grader wake/recruitment, acceptance persistence, explicit shipment, live counts, and priority ordering; remove obsolete Work on Everything-only routing. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002379 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n- **D-001 — Platform behavior is generic.** Acceptance-grader obligation routing and plan-agent delegation are platform capabilities for every plan; Work on Everything must not receive a special implementation branch.\n- **D-002 — The rubric is the authority boundary.** The plan's rubric determines independent versus owner-authorized grading; callers do not infer authority from goal identity.\n- **D-003 — Acceptance requires explicit shipment.** The plan remains in `awaiting-acceptance` until the required scorecard exists, every acceptance bar passes, and a separate explicit transition moves the plan to `shipped`.\n- **D-004 — Canonical live reads are mandatory.** Brief counts come from the shared obligation provider and canonical plan/fleet assignment reads at decision time; prompt literals and stale cached counts are not authoritative.\n- **D-005 — No idle fan-out.** Agent launch is conditional on a live zero-agent count plus at least one actionable plan, and is subordinate to any outstanding acceptance flow.\n\n### D-001 — Platform behavior is generic\nDate: 2026-09-22\nAcceptance-grader obligation routing and plan-agent delegation are platform capabilities for every plan; Work on Everything must not receive a special implementation branch.\n\n### D-002 — The rubric is the authority boundary\nDate: 2026-09-22\nThe plan rubric determines independent versus owner-authorized grading; callers do not infer authority from goal identity.\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance requires explicit shipment\nDate: 2026-09-22\nThe plan remains in awaiting-acceptance until the required scorecard exists, every acceptance bar passes, and a separate explicit transition moves the plan to shipped.\n\n### D-004 — Canonical live reads are mandatory\nDate: 2026-09-22\nBrief counts come from the shared obligation provider and canonical plan/fleet assignment reads at decision time; prompt literals and stale cached counts are not authoritative.\n\n### D-005 — No idle fan-out\nDate: 2026-09-22\nAgent launch is conditional on a live zero-agent count plus at least one actionable plan, and is subordinate to any outstanding acceptance flow.\n\n### D-006 — P-001 audit: the generalization gap is MISSING workspace-scoped plan discovery, not a Work-on-Everything branch to delete\nDate: 2026-09-22\n⚠⚠ **ITEM 2's RULING IS RETRACTED — SEE D-008 BEFORE ACTING ON THIS DECISION.** A workspace-wide acceptance scanner (`acceptance-grading-sweep`, a system routine seeded ACTIVE) already exists; D-008 carries the measurement and the revised P-002 scope. Item 2's *evidence* stands (the OBLIGATION path really is session-scoped); only the inference 'therefore nothing scans the workspace' was wrong. Items 1, 3 and 5 are unaffected; item 4 is de-escalated by D-008.\n\n**Measurement scope (binds every claim).** Static code-truth over TypeScript under `packages/`, `libs/`, `apps/`, excluding node_modules/dist, at 2026-09-22T07:1xZ. NOT measured: runtime behaviour, orchestrator/sidecar trees, non-TS surfaces. Absences are asserted AT THIS SCOPE and no wider.\n\n#### 1. No Work-on-Everything BEHAVIOURAL branches in this path (STANDS)\n`Measured:` grep -rn -i for workOnEverything / work-on-everything / work_on_everything / 'work on everything' over `agent-obligation-providers.ts`, `acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts`, `agent-tools/plans/**` -> **0 behavioural hits**. Only 2 matches, both provenance doc-comments: `agent-tools/plans/get-properties.ts:3` and `set-property.ts:3`.\n`Measured (POSITIVE CONTROL):` same pattern vs `launch-agent.ts` -> **1 hit at :87**. The instrument works, so the zero is a real absence.\n`Falsifier:` a WoE-conditional spelled differently (goal-slug compare, flag, DB-driven branch) would NOT be caught. If P-002 finds one, amend this.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for R-2/R-7: nothing WoE-specific to delete here, so consult Q(1) is answered NO at this scope. R-7's 'remove WoE-only paths' is a NO-OP for this path — do not manufacture a deletion to satisfy it. (WoE identifiers DO appear in ~116 files repo-wide, overwhelmingly cupboard/goal-install surface this plan does not touch.)\n\n#### 2. ⚠ RETRACTED RULING — evidence stands, inference does not (see D-008)\n`Measured (STANDS):` `agent-obligation-reader.ts` is the sole production assembly path for the OBLIGATION AGENDA (4 call sites). Its default discovery dep (~:600) returns `brief?.currentPlanSlug ? [brief.currentPlanSlug] : []`, and all four call sites narrow to <=1 plan or disable acceptance reads:\n- `coordination/tools/orient.ts:3519` — no override -> default dep\n- `turn-start-orientation.ts:1985` — no override -> default dep\n- `fleet/leader-brief.ts:4831` — `planSlugs: leaderPlanSlug ? [leaderPlanSlug] : []`\n- `fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts:2692` — `planSlugs: []`\nSo the OBLIGATION plane is session-scoped. **RETRACTED:** the further claim that 'nothing scans the workspace for plans awaiting acceptance', and the ruling that P-002 should ADD workspace-scoped discovery. The `acceptance-grading-sweep` routine already does that scan. D-008 supersedes.\n\nSTILL VALID: `independentVerificationObligation` (`agent-obligation-providers.ts:618`) is already generic, `priority:'high'`, and idempotent via `episode: ${code}:${rubricId}:${sourceGeneration}` (:705) — REUSE it; do not author a second obligation family.\n\n#### 3. `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` is real but UNCLASSIFIED (STANDS, and is worse than stated)\n`Measured:` grep in `agent-obligation-providers.ts` -> **0 hits**, though declared at `acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts:89` and handled at `plan-acceptance-gate.ts:557`. There `GRADER_GAP_CODES = {acceptance_ungraded, self_graded_only}`; `AUTHOR_REPAIR_CODES` holds 14; this code is in neither, so it falls to `status:'blocked'` — nobody's actionable work — although R-1 names it as a trigger. D-008 shows it is absent from all THREE copies of that set, so it reaches neither the obligation agenda nor the sweep. Highest-value fix in P-002.\n\n#### 4. `.slice(0, 8)` cap (STANDS as fact; DE-ESCALATED by D-008)\n`Measured:` `agent-obligation-reader.ts:161` -> `[...new Set(...)].slice(0, 8)` with no truncation marker (grepped the file — none). Unreachable today (max input 1). Since D-008 removes the reason discovery would widen here, this is hygiene, not a correctness blocker.\n\n#### 5. Bearing on consult Q(2) — acceptance-first starvation (STANDS)\nThe obligation plane cannot starve delegation today (one plan per agent). Note the sweep has its OWN bound — `ACCEPTANCE_GRADING_SWEEP_MAX_PER_TICK = 10` — which is the existing answer to R-6's starvation worry and should be reasoned about rather than reinvented. Consult `conv-mucaemon-...` (latency 'proceed') has no post yet; this records the evidence so a later answer refines a written position.\n\n### D-007 — The grader-gap code set is DUPLICATED in two files — P-002 must update both, and should collapse them to one exported constant\nDate: 2026-09-22\nSecond P-001 finding, separated from D-006 because it is an independent ruling that changes P-002's diff.\n\n**Measurement scope.** Static code-truth over TypeScript in `packages/` at 2026-09-22T07:1xZ, node_modules/dist excluded.\n\n#### The duplication\n`Measured:` the same classification exists as two independent, hand-maintained literals:\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-obligation-providers.ts` -> `const GRADER_GAP_CODES = new Set<PlanAcceptanceGateCode>(['acceptance_ungraded', 'self_graded_only'])`\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/set-plan-status.ts:289` -> `export const ACCEPTANCE_GRADER_GATE_CODES = new Set(['acceptance_ungraded', 'self_graded_only'])`\n\nIdentical membership, different names, no shared source. One decides whether an obligation is `due` vs `blocked`; the other decides whether a ship refusal recruits a grader. They are the same question asked twice.\n\n#### Why this matters NOW\nD-006 item 3 requires adding `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` to the grader-gap classification. Adding it to only ONE copy makes the two surfaces disagree: the gate would recruit a grader while the obligation agenda still reports the plan as `blocked`/nobody's-work, or the reverse. That disagreement is invisible to a typecheck (both remain well-typed) and invisible to a test that exercises only one surface.\n\n#### RULING for P-002\n1. Add `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` to BOTH sets in the same change, OR\n2. Preferred, and the repo's stated discipline (derived-truth ladder rung 1, DERIVE): collapse to ONE exported constant beside `PlanAcceptanceGateCode` in `plan-acceptance-gate.ts` and import it at both sites, so the classification cannot drift again.\nOption 2 is strictly better and is a small diff; take it unless something concrete blocks it, and say so if you don't.\n3. Whichever is taken, add a test that asserts the two consumers agree on the SAME code set — the recurrence guard. Without it, the next code added to one copy re-opens this silently.\n\n#### Incidental finding on R-4 (informs P-004's scope)\n`Measured:` `set-plan-status.ts` already refuses ship on `if (!gate.satisfied)` (~:435, error `gate.code ?? 'acceptance_gate_failed'`), and the ship path is gate-guarded (~:266, :396-:400). `Measured:` grep for a production `status:'shipped'` write triggered by scorecard emission -> none; the hits are a suggestion STRING (`acceptance-drain-filing.ts:235`), LLM-test fixtures, the gate's own proof record (`plan-acceptance-gate.ts:1447`), a cleanup dispatcher, and a type literal.\n\nSo R-4's stated hazard ('a scorecard or passing bars alone must not auto-ship') appears ALREADY satisfied by the existing guard. P-004 should therefore be scoped as REGRESSION COVERAGE proving the invariant holds (and that `force:{reason}` is the only bypass, recorded via `forcedPast`), not as building new enforcement. `Falsifier:` I grepped for the write rather than tracing every caller; if P-004 finds a path that reaches `shipped` without the gate, amend this and treat it as a real defect.\n\n### D-008 — RETRACTION of D-006 item 2 — a workspace-wide acceptance scanner ALREADY EXISTS; P-002 shrinks to a 3-site code-set fix\nDate: 2026-09-22\n**This retracts the load-bearing claim in D-006 item 2. Read this before acting on D-006.** D-006 asserted 'nothing scans the workspace for plans awaiting acceptance' and ruled P-002 as ADDING workspace-scoped discovery. That is WRONG. D-006 flagged this exact possibility as residue ('P-002 must confirm before building a second scanner'); the check fired and refuted it.\n\n**Measurement scope.** Static code-truth over TypeScript in `packages/` at 2026-09-22T07:2xZ, node_modules/dist excluded.\n\n#### What actually exists\n`Measured:` `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/acceptance-grading-sweep-action.ts` is a registered SYSTEM ROUTINE (`register-system-actions.ts:620`), seeded **ACTIVE by default** (`seed-acceptance-grading-sweep-routine.ts:46`, tier `ephemeral`). Its own comment (:105): *\"Deliberately NOT workspace-scoped to the routine's ALS context: one sweep serves every workspace's plans, so the workspace travels on the row.\"*\n\n`Measured:` its SQL (~:120-152) scans `harness_shared.harness_plans` WHERE `archived = FALSE AND status NOT IN ('shipped','superseded')`, joined to an acceptance rubric (`template_data->>'kind' = 'acceptance'`) and a `plan_audits` completion audit, ordered oldest-gradeable-first under a LIMIT, then filtered through `isHarnessInScope` (work-scope-policy P-007).\n\n`Measured:` per row it decides `skip | dispatch | escalate` (`acceptance-grading-sweep.ts`), capped at `ACCEPTANCE_GRADING_SWEEP_MAX_PER_TICK = 10` actionable decisions per tick so a stalled backlog cannot fan out into a launch storm.\n\nSo the workspace-wide discovery R-1 presumes missing is BUILT, ACTIVE, BOUNDED, and harness-scoped. **Do not build a second scanner.**\n\n#### What the real gap is (narrower, and better)\nTwo parallel mechanisms exist and they are NOT the same thing:\n- the **sweep** discovers stalled plans workspace-wide and DISPATCHES A GRADER;\n- the **obligation agenda** (D-006 item 2's evidence, which stands) surfaces acceptance as an agent-visible OBLIGATION, and is session-scoped to the reading agent's own declared plan.\n\nD-006's finding that the obligation path is session-scoped remains CORRECT and measured. What was wrong was the inference that therefore nothing scans the workspace. R-1 asks for an obligation, not a dispatch, so the residual gap is that the sweep's workspace-wide knowledge is never projected onto the obligation plane.\n\n#### The actual high-value defect: the trigger code set is duplicated THREE ways and all three omit R-1's named code\n`Measured:` three hand-maintained copies of 'the codes meaning this plan waits on a GRADER', all three exactly `['acceptance_ungraded', 'self_graded_only']`:\n1. `agent-obligation-providers.ts:589` `GRADER_GAP_CODES` — **unpinned**\n2. `agent-tools/plans/set-plan-status.ts:289` `ACCEPTANCE_GRADER_GATE_CODES` — exported as the pin anchor\n3. `acceptance-grading-sweep.ts` `ACCEPTANCE_GRADING_STALL_GATE_CODES` — pinned to (2)\n\n`Measured:` an anti-drift guard ALREADY exists between (2) and (3) — `acceptance-grading-sweep.test.ts:68` regex-matches the exported literal out of `set-plan-status.ts` source and fails if it is renamed, un-exported or reshaped. Copy (1) is outside that pin.\n\n`Measured:` `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` — which R-1 names explicitly as a trigger — is absent from ALL THREE. So today that refusal reaches neither the obligation agenda (falls to `status:'blocked'`) nor the sweep (`not-a-grader-gap` → skip). A plan stalled on exactly that code is invisible to BOTH mechanisms. This is the single highest-value fix in P-002.\n\n#### REVISED P-002 scope (supersedes D-006's ruling)\n1. Add `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` to all three copies in ONE change; extend the existing pin test to cover copy (1) too, so the three cannot drift again. Prefer collapsing to one exported constant beside `PlanAcceptanceGateCode` in `plan-acceptance-gate.ts` — but note the sweep deliberately keeps a literal for a stated **zero-runtime-dep** reason, so if collapsing would add a runtime import to the sweep, KEEP the literal and widen the pin instead. D-007's 'collapse' preference is downgraded to 'collapse only if it does not violate that constraint'.\n2. Project the sweep's workspace-wide result onto the obligation plane rather than re-deriving it, if R-1's obligation requirement is to be met generically.\n3. D-006 item 4 (`agent-obligation-reader.ts:161` `.slice(0, 8)`) is DE-ESCALATED: since discovery is not widening there, the cap stays unreachable. Leave it, or add the truncation marker as hygiene — it is no longer a P-002 correctness blocker.\n\n### D-009 — R-1 is PARTLY UNSAFE AS WRITTEN: bar_snapshot_grading_missing must NOT become a grader-gap code — classify it as author-repair instead\nDate: 2026-09-22\nThis corrects the fix D-006 item 3 and D-008 both recommended. Implementing them literally would have shipped a regression. Recording it before any lane acts.\n\n**Measurement scope.** Static code-truth over `packages/operator-core/lib` at 2026-09-22T07:3xZ.\n\n#### The exclusion is DELIBERATE and documented\n`Measured:` `acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts:154-158` states it outright:\n> *\"this refusal does not recruit a grader, and nothing said so. Recruitment fires only for ACCEPTANCE_GRADER_GATE_CODES ({acceptance_ungraded, self_graded_only}) — **deliberately, so a malformed rubric cannot spawn agents**. It took the live plane to find it, which is the argument for\nkeeping R-5/R-6 on the `live` evidence plane rather than relaxing them to `tree`.\n\n### D-015 — P-007/R-7: falsifiability is proven by in-tree mutation probes, because copy-out CANNOT reach a statically-imported module subject\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22\n\nRecords how R-7's coverage claim was actually established, and corrects a carried instruction that\nwould have produced NO evidence at all had it been followed literally.\n\n**Measurement scope.** Seven mutation probes (`scripts/mutation-probe.sh`) run 2026-09-22 12:43-12:58Z\nagainst the COMMITTED tree, plus a baseline run of all seven named test files whose router banner\nreported `uncommittedPaths=0/7 provenance=stamped` — i.e. the committed blobs are what ran, not a\ndirty working tree.\n\n#### 1. The carried instruction was inapplicable, not merely conservative\n\nMy predecessor's carry-note said, emphatically: \"Use the probe's COPY-OUT tier (the default) — NEVER\nthe in-tree mutation shape, because git-sync can sweep a mutant into a commit.\" The HAZARD is real and\nwell-documented. The PRESCRIPTION is not executable here.\n\nCopy-out works by mutating a copy outside the tree and pointing the test at it via `{}`. That requires\nthe test to take its subject as a PATH. That is the probe's own documented false-`survived` trap,\nand the natural next move from it is to WEAKEN a correct guard. So following the note would not have\nyielded weaker evidence; it would have yielded INVERTED evidence.\n\nCLAUDE.md's own tier table already routes a module-import subject away from copy-out. Its answer is a\npermanent paired control — which these tests DO carry, and which is necessary but not sufficient here:\na paired control proves the ASSERTION discriminates between two fixtures; it cannot prove that reverting\nthe PRODUCTION module turns the test red, because an injected-dep test may never touch production code\nat all. R-7's behavior is exactly that second claim, so the in-tree tier is what it requires.\n\n**Mitigation actually held** (not assumed): a `locks:acquire` file lock on all six subjects for the whole\nrun, heartbeated across it — git-sync excludes actively file-locked paths from its staging pathspecs.\nEvery probe printed `tree integrity: VERIFIED ... byte-identical to its pre-probe state`, and\n`git status --porcelain` over all six subjects was empty afterwards. The runner also aborts the entire\nrun on exit 3 (restore failed) rather than continuing into the next mutation.\n\n#### 2. Result: 7 of 7 mutants CAUGHT\n\nR-1 obligation-providers - R-2 grading-authority - R-3 grader-pickup - R-4 set-plan-status -\nR-5a delegation-counts - R-5b context-bundle (counts baked to a literal) - R-6 context-bundle\n(idle directive turned into a launch directive). Each subject, mutation and verdict is recorded as DATA\nin `packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-test-coverage.ts`, not as prose.\n\n#### 3. Why the map stores a VERDICT and not just a path\n\nR-7 does not say a test exists per bar; it says a test that FAILS ON REVERSION exists per bar. That is a\ncounterfactual, so it is unreadable from the test's source and cannot be recovered by any naming\nconvention. `validateBarTestCoverage` therefore treats a bar whose probe verdict is `survived` or\n`not-probed` as UNCOVERED — identical to having no test at all. CONTROL C in the guard pins precisely\nthat distinction, and is the control that would catch a future maintainer \"fixing\" the guard into the\nweaker exists-a-test reading.\n\n#### 4. Scope stated honestly\n\nBars R-1 and R-2 each also carry a P-001 spec whose subject is the AUDIT ARTIFACT (that the audit cites a\nresolvable seam), not runtime behavior. There is nothing in code to revert for those, so they are verified\nby `plans:audit` citation resolution, not by a probed test. The map covers each bar via the spec whose\nbehavior is executable — the same bar-scoped granularity R-7's own falsifier uses (\"a bar in this plan's\nset has no committed test\"). Anyone reading the map as per-SPEC coverage would be reading it wrong.\n\n### D-016 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-22\nAmendment-Id: 61dbb39f0e97b543de5404f699a32656eadf9a8f812441ee59a1c7b07d8e368d\nRequest-Hash: cfc086465112208622dbae451489ae1ad7943b3a142088a9c5d5427b7f9c7368\nActor: su-ae3c4989-e86a-4ce3-bb2e-a3c357c8bd21\nReason: Bars authored pre-implementation: method/check/requiredTestLayers empty, ship gate reports method_missing + check_missing + proof_depth_missing on all 7. Binds each bar to its committed test with a measured mutation verdict and declares unit proof depth.\nApproved-By: su-cecee8ca-952a-463c-bd06-ef584b4d0acd\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1059788\nApproved-At: 2026-09-22T14:58:58.467Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 31 → 32\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-017 — requiredTestLayers is per-criterion — R-3/R-5/R-6 keep evidence plane `live`; revision 4 rides one `criteria` amend\nDate: 2026-09-22\n**Question (left open by the rubric-vetting reviewer, consult conv-mucua50r post 1079617).** D-016's amendment declared unit proof depth UNIFORMLY across all 7 bars, while R-3/R-5/R-6 carry `requiredScope:['live']`. The reviewer could not determine whether `rubrics:amend` sets `requiredTestLayers` per bar or set-wide, and stated that if it is set-wide then R-3/R-5/R-6 \"cannot keep `live` and be provable\", so dropping them to `tree` would be \"the only consistent option the machinery offers\". That would have weakened three bars.\n\n**RULING 1 — `requiredTestLayers` is PER CRITERION. R-3/R-5/R-6 KEEP evidence plane `live`.** Dropping them to `tree` is NOT required and must not be done. Evidence, read directly from the writer:\n- `plans/rubric-template.ts:439` declares `requiredTestLayers` INSIDE `requirementAcceptanceSchema` — a per-criterion `.strict()` object, beside `requiredScope`, `evidencePlane`, `passRatings`, `mandatory`, `role`, `coversBarKeys`.\n- `plans/rubric-template.ts:512` re-exports it as `requirementAcceptanceSchema.shape.requiredTestLayers`, described as 'acceptance-kind only: required proof layers, such as integration or e2e; BAR amendment required to change'.\n- `rubrics/propose.ts:303-311` reads `criterion.requiredTestLayers` inside `args.criteria.forEach((criterion, index) => ...)`, as one of the per-criterion `barFields`.\n\nThe uniform declaration in D-016 was therefore a MODELLING choice, not a constraint the machinery imposed. Revision 4 declares proof depth per criterion and leaves the three `live` planes intact.\n\n**RULING 2 — revision 4 must ride the `criteria` COMPLETE replacement set, in ONE amend.** `rubrics/amend.ts:165-170` refuses `criteria` combined with `criterion`, `criterionClass`, or `criterionEvidencePlane` ('criteria is the complete replacement set'). Its own description: 'replace the COMPLETE criterion set through the atomic BAR amendment transaction. Use this when adding a BAR or binding structured checks across the set; read rubrics:get first and resubmit every stored criterion.' This is independently why the batching requirement already on WI-10002442 is correct: any bar-text change invalidates the same 15 proof refs, so all of them ride one transaction.\n\n**RULING 3 — the approval is dryRun-FIRST, not author-first.** `rubrics/amend.ts:179`: 'For a started BAR meaning change, use `dryRun:true`, store the returned approval on the work item, send the reviewer a pointer, then apply `approvalRef:\"thread-post:<id>\"`.' The reviewer approves the payload the dry run EMITS; they do not hand-author approval JSON in advance.\n\n### D-018 — evidencePlane/requiredTestLayers coherence is NOT machine-enforced — a `live` label proves nothing; D-017 is not licence to keep one\nDate: 2026-09-22\n**Addendum to D-017, raised by the rubric-vetting reviewer (consult conv-mucua50r post 1082173) and then MEASURED.**\n\nD-017 ruled that the machinery does not FORCE dropping R-3/R-5/R-6 to `tree`. It did NOT rule that those bars ARE live-evidenced, and D-017 must not be read as licence to keep a `live` label. This decision records the complement.\n\n**RULING — `evidencePlane` and `requiredTestLayers` are decorative unless the author makes them true.** `requiredTestLayers` is `z.array(z.string().trim().min(1)).min(1).max(50).optional()` (rubric-template.ts:439) — a FREE-FORM string array. There is no enum, no value validation, and NO coupling to `evidencePlane` anywhere. The ':513' phrase 'such as integration or e2e' is a `describe()` string: documentation, not a constraint. Nothing will ever refuse a bar declaring `evidencePlane:'live'` + `requiredTestLayers:['integration']` whose `check.files` are the same unit tests it always had.\n\n**MEASURED on this plan's own rubric (revision 3), with positive controls:**\n- r-3 `plane=live layers=[unit] check=[acceptance-grader-pickup.test.ts]`; r-5 `plane=live layers=[unit] check=[delegation-counts.test.ts, delegation-posture-brief.test.ts]`; r-6 `plane=live layers=[unit] check=[delegation-posture-brief.test.ts]`.\n- Integration tests referencing this plan's subjects (`readDelegationCounts`, `classifyGraderPickup`, `delegation-posture`): **0**.\n- Live/DB surface (`withHarnessAdminClient|getHarnessAdminUrl|testcontainers|PGlite|pg_`) in all three bound files: **0 hits**, across 202/307/354 lines.\n- Positive controls so those zeros are a real absence and not a broken instrument: 957 `*.integration.test.ts` exist in operator-core, and the same symbol pattern without the file filter returns 5 files.\n\n**CONSEQUENCE — relabelling is FORBIDDEN as a repair.** Changing `requiredTestLayers` from `['unit']` to `['integration']` while `check.files` stay on mocked unit tests does not fix the defect; it HIDES it, and is strictly worse than leaving the contradiction visible. The only thing that closes the gap is the CHECK BINDING moving off pure unit tests. A revision-4 relabel was authored and has been WITHDRAWN on this basis.\n\n**Ordering this imposes:** the committed integration tests must land and be bound BEFORE the amend, not after — otherwise the bar asserting D-014's cold-start fail-open (52 on first read, 51 thereafter) is bound to a mocked unit test that cannot catch that class by construction, leaving the bar unfalsifiable by its own check. Binding first preserves the single-amend batching (the 15 proof refs are still paid exactly once).\n\n### D-019 — R-8 (composite) must split by GATE CLASS — as first drafted it was unpassable because R-1 requires the state R-8 called a falsification\nDate: 2026-09-22\n**Raised by the rubric-vetting reviewer (consult conv-mucua50r post 1084850), with a live instance. Recorded as a decision at their request because a consult post is not addressable later.**\n\n#### The contradiction\nMy first R-8 draft was falsified if a plan in `awaiting-acceptance` could sit with 'no recruited grader'. But R-1 REQUIRES exactly that for author-repair codes: gate codes that are author repair — `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` among them — 'rank as upstream author work and must NOT recruit a grader'. So for every author-repair disposition, R-1 mandates precisely the state R-8 declared a falsification. **R-8 could never pass while R-1 holds** — an unsatisfiable bar, the mirror image of the unfalsifiable bar withdrawn in D-018.\n\n#### Live instance (not hypothetical)\nPlan `managed-agent-capability-contract-and-native-cutover-2026-09-13` is `awaiting-acceptance` now. `plans:set-plan-status{shipped}` refuses on `R-4: bar_snapshot_grading_not_pass` — the same author-repair class — and the recruiter fires only on `{acceptance_ungraded, self_graded_only}`, so it refuses WITHOUT recruiting. It has sat there and moved only because agents kept noticing.\n\n**The real defect it exposes is not the absent grader — that is correct, the rubric is not gradeable yet. It is that the author-repair path is SILENT:** nothing raises an owned obligation, so the stall can only be found by a human or a passing agent.\n\n#### RULING — adopt the class-split R-8\n> A plan that reaches `awaiting-acceptance` always progresses to a terminal disposition without an operator noticing a stall. Where the gate reports a grader gap (`acceptance_ungraded`, `self_graded_only`), the obligation is raised, an eligible independent grader is recruited and picks the work up, a scorecard is emitted against the active rubric, and the plan ends in `shipped` or an explicit non-ship disposition. Where the gate instead reports author repair, that repair is raised as an OWNED obligation against the author under the same non-silence guarantee — never left as a refusal that only a human or a passing agent would notice. No gate disposition leaves a plan with neither a recruited grader nor a raised author obligation.\n\n> **Falsifier:** falsified if any gate disposition can leave a plan in `awaiting-acceptance` with neither a recruited grader nor a raised owned author-repair obligation; or if reaching a terminal disposition requires an operator to notice a stall.\n\nThis preserves the no-human-notices property, keeps R-1's must-not-recruit rule intact, and makes the bar reachable. R-8 is an ADDED bar and must ride the SAME amend as the six changed bars (a later addition re-invalidates all 15 proof refs).\n\n### D-020 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-22\nAmendment-Id: de9fd0874620d287129a68891eed0d5bb23344f32fd856a449d74bd050cf4f40\nRequest-Hash: 7d39ab6485c35e11dac1028456905af969692521153702bff033e7235813d59f\nActor: su-ae3c4989-e86a-4ce3-bb2e-a3c357c8bd21\nReason: Revision 4 — ONE batched BAR amendment repairing six defects found by the rubric-vetting reviewer (consult conv-mucua50r, su-091ad703) and by my own code-truth audit, plus the added composite bar ruled in plan Decision D-019. Batched because any bar-moving amend invalidates the same 15 proof refs and the independent scorecard; paying that cost exactly once is the point (D-017 ruling 2).\n\n1. R-3/R-5/R-6 — evidence plane STAYS `live` (D-017 ruling 1) and requiredTestLayers becomes ['integration'], but only because check.files MOVE onto committed live integration tests that exercise the real subjects against real Postgres: acceptance-grader-pickup-live (6/6), delegation-counts-live (4/4), plan-agent-brief-posture-live (4/4). D-018 forbids relabelling without moving the binding — a relabel HIDES the defect. R-5 binds both the provider test and the brief test because its bar promises both that the counts are live and that the brief receives them.\n2. R-6 bar text — restated so the grammatical subject is the DECISION produced over real state, not 'The brief instructs: …'. The old form was satisfiable by a string assertion over prompt text.\n3. R-7 — RESOLVED BY REPAIR, NOT DELETION. Its defect was self-reference: its check bound acceptance-bar-test-coverage.test.ts, whose subject is THIS rubric's own bar-to-test map, and its mutation mutated the registry rather than the product, so it could go healthy on a system that does not work. It now states an observable consequence about the PRODUCT (removing a delivered behaviour must fail a committed test) and its binding moves onto the product tests. Its second sentence also takes up the plan Non-goal 'do not create a second obligation system', which no rev-3 bar covered.\n4. R-2 second sentence — stops grading code STRUCTURE (absence of Work-on-Everything branches) and states behavioural indistinguishability instead.\n5. R-8 — ADDED; its text is plan Decision D-019's RULING verbatim, with D-019's falsifier as driftMarkers. It rides THIS amend because a later addition re-invalidates all 15 proof refs a second time (D-019). Its barProvenance is honestly `legacy-backfilled`, NOT `pre-implementation`: it was authored after implementation from D-019, and the provenance enum offers only those two — claiming predeclaration would be false.\n6. R-1 bar text — it named `bar_snapshot_grading_missing` as though it were a gate code. It is not a PlanAcceptanceGateCode; it is a bar-snapshot condition surfacing via `acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready`, which GATE_CODE_OWNERSHIP maps to 'author', never 'grader'. The bar now names the real grader-gap set {acceptance_ungraded, self_graded_only} and states the author-repair class explicitly. Repaired by FIXING THE BAR TEXT, not by widening recruitment — a deliberate comment in agent-obligation-providers.ts records that widening it would make a rendered user promise a lie.\n\nThe subject plan's Requirements and Bar-to-work map were updated to match (plan revision 42) before this amend, so the plan document and the rubric state the same bars.\n\nConsequence accepted: 15 proof refs and scorecard EI-23979736358691557 are invalidated; nextRepair bar_snapshot_proof_stale — proofs re-measured and re-bound, vetting refreshed, then independent re-grading.\n\nREVIEW ROUND 2 (su-091ad703, WI-10002442 post 1140492) — two bar-text fixes folded in, so only R-2 and R-5 move again: (a) R-5 still dropped both of D-004's capitalised clauses, keeping only \"not a stale prompt constant\"; it now says reads are taken AT DECISION TIME and stale cached counts are not authoritative. (b) R-2 stated indistinguishability for the Work-on-Everything INSTANCE only; D-002's class is that callers never infer authority from GOAL IDENTITY, so it is generalised with WoE named as one instance. Their two other findings (R-5's D-014 case is vacuous against a warm cache and a null work-scope policy; R-6's idle state has no case) are TEST content, move no hash, and land before proof re-binding.\nApproved-By: su-091ad703-d98f-4ccb-a20f-ea02d02e9f75\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1140536\nApproved-At: 2026-09-22T19:58:24.880Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 44 → 45\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-codex-carry-respawn-transcript-continuity-2026-09-21","title":"Acceptance BAR — Preserve visible conversation continuity across Codex carry-respawn","status":"active","created":"2026-09-21","owner":"su-2d5053f6-2652-4b39-a45d-d50e4cefdb6a","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Preserve visible conversation continuity across Codex carry-respawn\nslug: acceptance-codex-carry-respawn-transcript-continuity-2026-09-21\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-21\nupdated: 2026-09-21\nowner: su-2d5053f6-2652-4b39-a45d-d50e4cefdb6a\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Preserve visible conversation continuity across Codex carry-respawn\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21","title":"Acceptance: two-class turn-start memory with hybrid owner-directive capture","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-21","owner":"su-c03852cb-8576-425b-9cd9-b4441bc9dbe8","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance: two-class turn-start memory with hybrid owner-directive capture\nslug: acceptance-turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-21\nupdated: 2026-09-24\nowner: su-c03852cb-8576-425b-9cd9-b4441bc9dbe8\n---\n\n# Acceptance: two-class turn-start memory with hybrid owner-directive capture\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24.
