Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"codex-carry-respawn-transcript-continuity-2026-09-21","title":"Preserve visible conversation continuity across Codex carry-respawn","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Preserve visible conversation continuity across Codex carry-respawn\nslug: codex-carry-respawn-transcript-continuity-2026-09-21\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-21\nupdated: 2026-09-21\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Preserve predecessor history.** When a Codex carry-respawn replaces a predecessor native thread, the owner must be able to view the predecessor turns from the successor session surface without the system claiming that data was deleted.\n\n**R-002 — Keep native-session safety.** The successor must remain a fresh Codex native thread; do not reuse the predecessor rollout or reintroduce active-writer/session-id collisions.\n\n**R-003 — Make the transition explicit.** The visible transcript must include a clear, non-user-authored continuation marker linking the successor to its predecessor and explaining that the old turns remain available.\n\n**R-004 — Preserve ordinary resume behavior.** A normal Codex resume with no carry-respawn must remain unchanged, and separate sessions must not be merged merely because they share a workspace or owner.\n\n**R-005 — Regression coverage.** Tests must cover carry successor lineage/marker generation, predecessor-history retrieval or rendering, and the existing queued PreCompact fail-closed behavior.\n\n**R-006 — Verification.** Run the focused operator/TUI tests and the affected test command; record root cause, changed files, and observed results.\n\n## Design\n\nThe carry launcher will persist a bounded predecessor reference alongside the carry document, expose successor/predecessor lineage through the existing session/transcript read surface, and have the TUI/session browser render the predecessor transcript as an explicitly labeled continuation section. The host will continue rotating native Codex threads and the precompact hook will continue vetoing native compaction. If the predecessor transcript cannot be resolved, the successor remains usable and the UI reports the missing-history state rather than silently showing an empty conversation.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-001 | P-001, P-002 | live |\n| R-002 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-002, P-003 | live |\n| R-004 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-006 | P-004 | tree |\n\n- **P-001** `done` Trace the Codex carry-launch, transcript resolver, and session-browser render seams; confirm the smallest reusable lineage surface. — note: ← WI-10002184 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `todo` Add durable predecessor-to-successor lineage metadata and a bounded, labeled predecessor transcript projection.\n- **P-003** `todo` Add regression tests for fresh-thread safety, lineage rendering, missing predecessor history, and ordinary resume isolation.\n- **P-004** `todo` Run focused tests and the affected suite; complete only with observed evidence.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- A carry successor still launches as a fresh Codex native thread.\n- The successor surface visibly links to and can show the predecessor history.\n- No predecessor turns are mislabeled as owner turns authored in the successor.\n- A normal resume remains unchanged.\n- Focused and affected tests pass.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Use Codex native fork for carry successors\nDate: 2026-09-21\nMeasured in the launcher seam and local Codex CLI help: `codex fork <SESSION_ID>` creates a separate native thread from the predecessor, while the existing carry path stripped all resume/fork subcommands and launched a blank thread. Carry-respawn will therefore resolve the newest persisted rollout in CODEX_HOME, invoke native `fork <id>` when available, and fall back to the existing fresh-thread path when no safe predecessor rollout exists. The managed carry marker remains in the successor first turn and a cut-scoped lineage sidecar records predecessor id/path without changing ordinary resume behavior.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"desktop-release-incremental-resume-2026-09-21","title":"Make desktop release cuts incrementally resumable","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make desktop release cuts incrementally resumable\nslug: desktop-release-incremental-resume-2026-09-21\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-21\nupdated: 2026-10-16\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Phase 1 orchestration and phase receipts are both complete and verified. Receipt coverage spans linux + windows + mac at start/prepare/commit plus the manifest stage — every release stage holding the four prerequisites a sound receipt requires. arm64/android are deliberately excluded (D-007): they hold none of prerequisites 1-3, so covering them means BUILDING those prerequisites, which is WI-10002472 and not part of this plan. Evidence: desktop shell suite 669/669 exit 0, journal suite 44/44, content-identity selftest ALL PASS, and three copy-out mutation probes all verdict=caught with the shared tree byte-identical after each. ⛔ Owner directive #96 is open and UNCHANGED by any of this: the 0.0.22-alpha cut stays PAUSED — no release:cut run/tag/upload. Everything in this plan is tooling that proceeds fully while the cut is paused, so none of it is waiting on the owner.\n\n**Next:** P-003 — persist reusable stage outputs and transactional seed manifests, plus the sparse-holder fallback. Its blocker is now cleared, so claim it next; then P-004 (fault-injection and resume tests for interruption after every phase, and stale-receipt rejection), which depends on P-003. Both are ordinary implementation work needing no owner decision. Only once both land is this plan eligible for the ship sequence: per-item code-truth audit → acceptance rubric authored against as-built reality → rubric vetting → independent non-implementer grading → the implementer's acceptance call → plans:set-plan-status shipped.\n\n## Background\n\nThe 0.0.21-alpha cut completed, but earlier retries rebuilt expensive stages because the manual release:cut path did not always create/pass managed journal IDs, seed state could be lost with an isolated worktree, and compressed package outputs were not reusable across retries. This plan makes every release phase independently resumable while preserving exact source, toolchain, and policy identity.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Durable operation identity.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Every release cut creates or resumes a durable operation journal keyed by source SHA, release version, and requested target platforms; retries can discover the prior operation without relying on an ephemeral worktree or shell process.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Existing engineering requirement from the canonical plan, preserved verbatim; not a new owner requirement.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Every release cut creates or resumes a durable operation journal keyed by source SHA, release version, and requested target platforms; retries can discover the prior operation without relying on an ephemeral worktree or shell process.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A retry discovers a different operation for the same source/version/platform tuple, or reuses one across changed source/gitlink/version/platform identity.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run test:file on the operation and journal suites; inspect persisted operation identity and restart discovery wiring in release-cut-operation/release-cut tools. Exercise same-identity retry and changed source/gitlink/version/platform negative controls.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/release-cut-operation.test.ts\",\n        \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Verified phase receipts.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Each release phase writes an atomic receipt containing its inputs, output paths and hashes, source/gitlink identity, toolchain/policy identity, and completion state; resume skips a phase only when its receipt still validates.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Existing engineering requirement from the canonical plan, preserved verbatim; not a new owner requirement.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Each release phase writes an atomic receipt containing its inputs, output paths and hashes, source/gitlink identity, toolchain/policy identity, and completion state; resume skips a phase only when its receipt still validates.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A phase skips work using an invalid, expired or mismatched receipt, or accepts output bytes different from the committed digest.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the Vitest journal and real-Postgres task ledger tests and the desktop Node shell suite. Inspect each linux/windows/mac/manifest start, prepare and commit consumer; compare actual output bytes to persisted digest and exercise stale, missing and corrupted controls.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/store.integration.test.ts\",\n        \"papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Reusable stage cache.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Cargo, sidecar, seed, package, compression, provenance, and manifest outputs are cached by content and policy identity, with transactional seed manifests and a proven sparse-to-full fallback when sparse holders cannot boot.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Existing engineering requirement from the canonical plan, preserved verbatim; not a new owner requirement.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Cargo, sidecar, seed, package, compression, provenance, and manifest outputs are cached by content and policy identity, with transactional seed manifests and a proven sparse-to-full fallback when sparse holders cannot boot.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Changed compression content/policy still hits the same cache identity, a failed staged seed replaces the prior seed, or a sparse refusal ships stale/seedless instead of retrying once and failing closed.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run cut-seed-cli Vitest tests, desktop Node release-local suite, and release-content-identity.selftest.sh. Verify transactional publication with rollback, sparse refusal/full-cut fallback, committed output comparison and zstd/xz producer plus knob invalidation. Reuse native Cargo and sidecar caches; no parallel cache system.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/cut-seed-cli.test.ts\",\n        \"papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Resume regression guard.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Fault-injection tests interrupt after every phase and prove a retry starts at the next valid phase, rejects stale or mismatched receipts, and never silently republishes an unverified artifact.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Existing engineering requirement from the canonical plan, preserved verbatim; not a new owner requirement.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Fault-injection tests interrupt after every phase and prove a retry starts at the next valid phase, rejects stale or mismatched receipts, and never silently republishes an unverified artifact.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An injected interruption after a supported phase causes a retry to replay committed work, skip unverified work, accept stale/mismatched receipts, or publish without validated manifest outputs.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run phase-boundary interruption/restart tests against the real Postgres receipt store and canonical shell prepare/commit consumers using disposable outputs. Cover linux/windows/mac/manifest per D-007, stale identity, downstream invalidation and no-unverified-publish. No actual release cut or upload is needed or authorized.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/store.integration.test.ts\",\n        \"papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Architecture\n\nUse the existing managed release journal as the control plane and extend the manual release:cut entrypoint to allocate operation and phase IDs on every invocation. Store receipts and reusable outputs in a durable cache keyed by source SHA/version plus toolchain and policy fingerprints. Validate receipts before reuse; invalidate only the affected phase and downstream dependents. Record compression policy (including xz preset) in provenance.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Durable orchestration\n\n- **P-001** `done` Thread operation and phase journal IDs through manual release:cut; persist source/version/platform identity and restart discovery. — note: REOPENED on code-truth evidence (measured 2026-09-22T18:55Z, positive-controlled). P-001 claims \"thread operation and phase journal IDs through manual release:cut ... and restart discovery\". No such code exists: grep -rlE \"phase[_-]?journal|cut[_-]?operation|operation[_-]?journal|restartDiscovery\" across packages, apps, libs and papercusp-desktop returns ZERO files, while the positive control (preflightCut) returns 4 — the instrument works, so the absence is real. release-cut-launch.ts has 0 occurrences of journal/operationId/receipt, and there is no cut_phase/cut_operation/release_cut migration. The done status propagated from linked WI-10002143, whose actual deliverable was \"Re-cut 0.0.21-alpha with macOS and Windows legs\" (landed: owner-identity-env.ts, gate-release-site.ts, record-release-cli.ts, publish-release-history.sh) — that touches \"persist source/version/platform identity\" at best, and not the journal or restart discovery at all. Left done, this item would have been audite…\n- **P-002** `done` Add atomic phase receipts with input/output hashes, toolchain and policy fingerprints, and receipt validation/invalidation rules. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10002458 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Persist reusable stage outputs and transactional seed manifests, add sparse-holder fallback, and key compressed package reuse by input hash plus compression policy. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10002488 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Add fault-injection and resume tests for interruption after every phase, stale receipt rejection, downstream invalidation, and no-unverified-publish behavior. blocked-by: P-003 — note: ← WI-6554700010016226 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Keep the existing managed release journal and extend it; do not introduce a parallel orchestration system.\n- Default alpha retries to reuse verified outputs, while recording any policy change (such as a faster xz preset) in provenance.\n\n### D-001 — 0.0.21-alpha release source advances ce28a91f -> 9ccdf21e to scrub an owner-name literal from the shipped sidecar\nDate: 2026-09-22\nRULING (2026-09-22T04:30Z, su-ebc93). The pinned release source ce28a91fd2e5827f0b1ce598c6342ae66fb0846d CANNOT produce shippable bytes and has been advanced to 9ccdf21e2dc4f01c56e398598edd769de59666a9. Any lane quoting the old sha for 0.0.21-alpha is now stale.\n\n#### Why\nThe linux leg failed the WI-4419 identity scan:\n  'ASSEMBLED BUNDLE CARRIES SENSITIVE IDENTITY - MUST NOT SHIP (1 file): src-tauri/sidecar/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/su.md'\nThat file carried the owner's first name as a literal ('When Avi issues an owner directive ...'), so every installed desktop would have shipped the owner's identity. The scan is correct to refuse.\n\nThis is a REGRESSION, not long-standing: 0.0.20's tree has 0 occurrences; the literal entered 2026-09-21T16:17:27Z in a0e582dd, ~12h before the cut.\n\n#### Why the source had to move (no cheaper option exists)\n- The sidecar assembles from PAPERCUSP_ROOT=\"${PAPERCUSP_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/libs/papercusp}\" -> the CUT TREE's own submodule, so fixing only the canonical tree does not reach the build.\n- Overriding PAPERCUSP_ROOT to the canonical tree would build from different source than the pinned release source: a provenance lie. Rejected.\n- release-local.sh:453-460 sets BUILD_SHA=<short>-dirty when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty in EITHER the desktop tree OR the superproject. libs/papercusp is a superproject submodule, so an UNCOMMITTED fix there poisons BUILD_SHA.\n- PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DIRTY=1 is NOT an escape: the ship-gate asserts gitDirty==false on every channel including alpha, so a dirty cut yields only unshippable bytes (release-local.sh:480-493).\nTherefore the fix must be COMMITTED in the cut tree, which necessarily moves the gitlink and the sourceSha.\n\n#### What was done, and the scope bound\nCherry-picked ONLY d589fe1d (su.md, +1/-1) onto the pinned submodule a268c83e -> 3d0ddd99, then committed that single gitlink advance -> superproject 9ccdf21e.\nDELIBERATELY NOT taken: the wider a268c83e..ff621c0c range (6 commits, 9 files) which also carries NEW DB migration 1189 (owner-directive-capture) and orchestrator changes (su-stack.ts, su-decomposition.ts). Those are unrelated to the gate failure and must not ride an alpha release cut unvalidated.\nAlso not needed: the sibling fix to su-collaborator/prompts/collaboration-stance.md. That file does not carry the literal at this pin (the line arrived later); verified with a positive control. It IS fixed in canonical for the fleet.\n\n#### Verification\nCut tree blueprint prompts: 0 occurrences of the literal (positive control: 3 files still match 'owner directive', so the grep is sound). Submodule clean, superproject clean, desktop clean, 4.5G seed still staged.\n\n#### Consequence for other lanes\nThe tag desktop-v0.0.21-alpha was pinned to ce28a91f and must be re-pinned to 9ccdf21e before the legs can run. Use sourceSha 9ccdf21e2dc4f01c56e398598edd769de59666a9 for every remaining leg (linux/mac/windows), handoff and publish.\n\n### D-002 — OWNER AUTHORIZED moving the published desktop-v0.0.21-alpha tag to the corrected source\nDate: 2026-09-22\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-22] [turn:self]\n\nOWNER DECISION, given in a direct interactive turn in response to an explicit AskUserQuestion. The owner selected 'Move the tag'.\n\nQuestion put to the owner (verbatim intent): the published tag desktop-v0.0.21-alpha is pinned to source ce28a91f, which contains the owner-name leak the WI-4419 ship-gate refuses; the corrected source is already on origin; how should the tag be resolved so the legs can run?\n\nOwner chose: RE-PIN desktop-v0.0.21-alpha to the corrected source, keeping the 0.0.21-alpha version identity. Options explicitly declined by that choice: shipping as 0.0.22-alpha; delete-then-recreate as two steps; 'something else'.\n\n#### What this authorizes, precisely\nA rewrite of an ALREADY-PUBLISHED tag on the public repo github.com/Papercusp/papercup. This is normally refused by design - release-local.sh states 'Fail-closed: LOCAL-only cuts never mutate origin. A missing/mismatched remote pin is a precondition failure, not an invitation for the cutter to force-push', and release:cut op:'prepare-tag' is a CREATE-ONLY lease that cannot move an existing ref. The owner's explicit choice is the authorization that permits deviating from that default; it is NOT a licence to force-push anything else.\n\n#### Scope bound - this authorization does NOT extend to\n- Creating a GitHub Release or uploading artifacts (artifacts stay LOCAL; op:prepare-tag reports githubRelease:false, artifactUpload:false).\n- Pushing arbitrary commits to the public repo. The corrected source must already BE on origin; the tag moves onto an existing public commit, it does not publish a new one.\n- Publishing a reduced platform scope. FAIL CLOSED on three platforms per EI-23847426944518507.\n\n#### Consequence\nSupersedes the blocker recorded on the WI-10002143 checkpoint at 04:35Z. The release keeps the 0.0.21-alpha identity. The tag must land on an ORIGIN commit whose libs/papercusp gitlink contains the su.md scrub (d589fe1d, present in origin/main at ff621c0c, verified 0 occurrences). The purely-local cut commit 9ccdf21e is NOT on origin and therefore is NOT a valid tag target.\n\n### D-003 — P-002 is a receipt-COVERAGE task on the existing journal, not a new receipt mechanism\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22\nRULING (2026-09-22T19:35Z, su-ebc93). Any lane reading P-002 as 'build phase receipts' is working from a wrong premise and would ship a SECOND journal beside a working one.\n\n#### Measured: all four demands already exist and are wired\nMeasured: `grep -nE 'toolchain|rustc|fingerprint|policy' papercusp-desktop/bin/release-local.sh` → identity builder at 816-868 emits `toolchain: { rustc: command('rustc'), cargo, node, npm, tauriCli }` (838-844) and `policy: { files: <sha256 of 7 policy files>, allowIncompleteRoles, skipProvenanceParity, skipMigrationLint, skipMigrationBootsmoke, skipBuildset, allowUnverifiedSubmodule }` (852-860), inside `identity = { schemaVersion: 2, platform: 'linux-x86_64', … }`.\nMeasured: `grep -nE '^export (async )?(function|const|type|interface) ' scripts/lib/release-task-journal.ts` → `releaseStageInputHash:101`, `releaseTaskStageContentIdentity:106`, `releaseTaskStageInputHash:131`, `releaseStageRequestIdentity:139`, `assertReleaseTaskIdentity:185`, `inspectReleaseTaskStage:305`, `beginReleaseTaskStage:312`, `settleReleaseTaskStage:400`.\nMeasured: `sed -n '975,1030p' papercusp-desktop/bin/release-local.sh` → the commit at 990-995 passes evidence refs `build-provenance:sha256:$provenance_sha` (the OUTPUT hash, sha256sum'd at 989), `source-gitlink:$PROVENANCE_SOURCE_GIT_HEAD`, `artifact-set:hash-signature-verified`, `audit-reuse-expires:$RELEASE_TASK_REUSE_EXPIRES_AT`.\nMeasured: same range → three enforced invalidation rules: `release_task_verify_linux_artifacts` verifies bytes BEFORE commit and fails closed (979-983); `release_task_linux_outputs_absent` → `refuse … artifact-set:confirmed-absent` then re-mints an attempt (1019-1029); `release_task_audit_reuse_expiry` returns non-zero unless identity-scan evidence is fresh (985-988), and `settleReleaseTaskStage` (scripts/lib/release-task-journal.ts:445-455) throws unless that expiry is in the future. Atomicity is cursor-CAS with 12 retries (400-412).\n\n#### Measured: the real gap is COVERAGE\nMeasured: `grep -oE 'release_task_(journal_call (commit|refuse|begin)|begin_stage) +release\\.[a-z.]+' papercusp-desktop/bin/release-local.sh | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u` → exactly TWO stage names: `release.build.linux`, `release.manifest`.\nMeasured: `grep -oE 'RELEASE_TASK_[A-Z_]*IDENTITY' … | sort -u` → only `RELEASE_TASK_BUILD_IDENTITY`, `RELEASE_TASK_MANIFEST_IDENTITY`.\nMeasured: the builder is `release_task_linux_content_identity()` (line 771) and hardcodes `platform: 'linux-x86_64'` (line 825). The mac leg (mac sidecar handling ~2575), the windows leg (windows toolchain verification ~1429) and upload/publish (38 matches for `upload|publish`) carry NO receipts — so an interrupted cut resumes only those two phases and redoes the rest.\n\n#### Ruling\nP-002 is implemented by GENERALIZING the existing builder to a per-platform identity and adding begin/commit/refuse pairs for the remaining phases through the SAME `release_task_journal_call`. No new table, no second journal: `harness_shared.task_ledger.detail.release` stays canonical.\n\n#### Consequence for P-004\nP-004's 'interruption after every phase' is unreachable until this coverage lands, which is why P-003/P-004 sit blocked behind P-002.\n\n#### Method note\nThis is the SECOND time on this plan that a keyword grep scoped to ONE file reported a capability absent while it existed under different vocabulary elsewhere (the first cost P-001 a wrong 'greenfield' framing). The check that caught it both times: grep the CONSUMER (release-local.sh), not just the library.\n\n### D-004 — P-002 leg order is driven by receipt PREREQUISITES, not artifact family — linux-aarch64 is NOT next; windows/mac are\nDate: 2026-09-22\nRULING (2026-09-22T20:05Z, su-ebc93). Any lane resuming P-002 from the prior carry-note's \"start with linux-aarch64 — same artifact family as the proven linux trio, so the verify/absent/expiry helpers are directly modelled\" is working from a WRONG premise. Artifact family (deb/appimage) is the cheap part. The linux receipt trio depends on three prerequisites that aarch64 does not have.\n\n#### Measured (papercusp-desktop/bin/release-local.sh)\n1. **No per-leg build provenance.** The linux commit evidence is `build-provenance:sha256:<sha>` (:918), and `release_task_linux_outputs_absent` gates on `[[ -f \"$bundle/build-provenance.json\" ]]` (:854). Emissions exist for linux (`emit_linux_build_provenance` :2247/:2324/:2762), windows (inline in build-windows-on-vm.sh, per the EI-8914 note at :2828) and mac (`emit-build-provenance.sh` :2854). grep for any arm64 emission returns NOTHING. With no provenance file there is no output hash to commit and `outputs_absent` cannot distinguish absent from complete.\n2. **No reuse landing.** `grep -oE 'PAPERCUSP_REUSE_[A-Z0-9_]+|\\b(LINUX|WIN|MAC|ARM64|ANDROID)_REUSE\\b'` counts PAPERCUSP_REUSE_LINUX=12, _MAC=10, _WIN=9, MAC_REUSE=8, LINUX_REUSE=6, WIN_REUSE=5 — and ZERO for arm64/android. The journal's `reuse`/`reconcile` actions have nowhere to land on a leg with no reuse variable.\n3. **No cardinality assertion.** `assert_reused_provenance` is ALREADY leg-parameterized (`:2171` — `$2 = leg label`) and is called for linux (:2290), windows (:2377) and mac (:2453). Never for arm64.\n\n#### Consequence for the plan\nWiring aarch64 first means BUILDING those three prerequisites first — a materially larger job than \"model it on the linux trio\", and one that would be discovered halfway through the receipt work. **Windows and mac each have all three today** and are therefore the correct next legs. aarch64 and android need a prerequisite pass before they are journallable at all.\n\n#### Two defects found by this same check (being fixed under P-002)\n- `:2430` the arm64 `ARTIFACTS+=` is DEAD CODE — `ARTIFACTS=()` at :2746 resets the array afterwards, so only the :2772 append survives. arm64 is the only leg that appends before the reset.\n- `:2772` arm64 is the ONLY leg with no `_found` guard (cf. `linux_found` :2754, `win_found` :2782, `mac_found` :2816, each of which fails the cut on an empty glob). `WITH_ARM64=1` can therefore collect ZERO arm64 artifacts and let the cut proceed, publishing a release that advertises arm64 support with no arm64 bytes.\n\n#### Method note\nThis is the THIRD consecutive P-00x item whose \"greenfield/ready\" framing was wrong, and the third time a cheap pre-implementation probe caught it (P-001 and P-002 both via grepping the CONSUMER rather than the library; see EI-23992721572397275). The generalizable rule here is narrower and worth carrying: a leg is ready for a receipt when its PREREQUISITES exist (provenance emission, reuse landing, cardinality assert), never when its artifact TYPE resembles one that is already wired.\n\n### D-005 — CORRECTION to D-004: windows HAS all receipt prerequisites and is the next leg — the blocker I recorded came from a stale comment\nDate: 2026-09-22\nRULING (2026-09-22T20:25Z, su-ebc93). **This supersedes the windows half of D-004 and the first version of WI-10002471. Do not act on either.** D-004's arm64/android findings STAND; only its windows claim is retracted.\n\n#### What I got wrong\nI recorded that windows \"has prerequisites 1-3 but fails a 4th — it never surfaces the role set it built, decided inside build-windows-on-vm.sh (gui-only server-side)\", and on that basis REMOVED windows from the leg registry rather than wire it.\n\n**`bin/build-windows-on-vm.sh` DOES NOT EXIST** (`ls` → \"No such file or directory\"). I was quoting a stale comment in release-local.sh that describes a deleted VM-based producer. The real producer is `bin/build-windows-cross.sh` (native cargo-xwin + Inno-under-wine), selected as `WIN_PRODUCER=\"$ORCHESTRATOR_HERE/build-windows-cross.sh\"`. My supporting grep returned \"0 files\" truthfully but answered the wrong question — I searched for a `WIN_BUILT_ROLES`-shaped variable when the leg just uses `PAPERCUSP_BUILD_ROLES` directly.\n\n#### Measured (bin/build-windows-cross.sh)\n- `:194` `ROLES=\"${PAPERCUSP_BUILD_ROLES:-gui server}\"` — builds EXACTLY the requested roles, defaulting to BOTH. No gui-only narrowing anywhere.\n- `:597` `for role in $ROLES`; gui → \"Papercusp GUI\", server → \"Papercusp Server\".\n- `:594` hard-fails a role that produces no `${app_name}_${VERSION}_x64-setup.exe`.\n- `:826` `[[ -f \"$SETUP_EXE.sig\" ]] || fail \"tauri signer produced no .sig\"` — every installer is signed or the leg fails.\n- `:764` emits `build-provenance.json` via the snapshotted emit-build-provenance.sh.\n\nSo the expected artifact set IS derivable — **one signed setup.exe per role in PAPERCUSP_BUILD_ROLES** — the same derivation linux's `expected_debs` already uses. Windows has all four prerequisites and needs no new reporting mechanism.\n\n#### Ruling\nWindows is the NEXT leg to wire, and the work is just its two predicates plus registry rows — not the reporting-mechanism change WI-10002471 originally proposed. `release_task_windows_outputs_absent` must count setup.exe files (fixed, one per role) and must NOT count `*-setup-N.bin` DiskSpan slices, whose count is variable and which `papercusp_normalize_spanned_server` replaces with a single zip at collection time.\n\n#### Method note — the same error a third time, now in its most expensive form\nD-004 itself warned that an absence claim is scoped to the vocabulary and file set it searched. I then made exactly that error in the act of writing the warning: I read a COMMENT describing the producer instead of the producer. Comments are hand-maintained metadata about code (derived-truth-ladder rung 4) and drift silently; the file even contradicted itself, claiming gui-only in one place and gui+server in another. The operational rule: **when a comment names a file, stat the file before believing the sentence.** The stale comment and the registry's wrong justification have both been corrected in-tree so the next reader does not inherit the trap.\n\n### D-006 — The mac receipt is blocked on its own BEST-EFFORT provenance — making that emission fatal is prerequisite work inside P-002, not a separate concern\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22 RULING (2026-09-22T20:50Z, su-ebc93), after the windows leg landed. Any lane picking up \"wire the next leg\" should read this first: mac looks like a copy of windows and is not.\n\n#### Measured in the producer, not in comments about it\n`papercusp-desktop/bin/build-mac-cross.sh` EXISTS (42KB) and has three of the four prerequisites outright: `:155` `ROLES=\"${PAPERCUSP_BUILD_ROLES:-gui server}\"`; `:230` `OUT_BUNDLE=\"${PAPERCUSP_MAC_OUT:-$SRC_TAURI/target/$MAC_BUILD_TARGET/release/bundle}\"` which IS the dir release-local collects from (`MAC_OUT=\"$ROOT/src-tauri/target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle\"`); `:704` `PROV_ARTIFACTS+=(\"$OUT_BUNDLE/dmg/${product}_${VERSION}_${DMG_ARCH}.dmg\" \"$OUT_BUNDLE/macos/$product.app.tar.gz\")` per role; and `PAPERCUSP_REUSE_MAC` + an `assert_reused_provenance … mac` label already exist.\n\n#### The blocker: prerequisite 1 is OPTIONAL for mac, and it is the one the mac receipt most depends on\n`build-mac-cross.sh:727-737` emits provenance under `if [[ -x … && ${#PROV_ARTIFACTS[@]} -gt 0 ]]` and ends `|| echo \"WARN: provenance emit failed (non-fatal)\"`. release-local's own mac block says the same thing in prose: \"Best-effort: a provenance hiccup must never fail a good release.\" So a mac build can SUCCEED with no build-provenance.json.\n\nThat is not merely untidy, and it is worse for mac than it would be for any other leg, because of the **unversioned `.app.tar.gz`**. Tauri emits it with no version in the name, so a version-scoped count CANNOT distinguish a current updater bundle from a prior cut's — which the existing code openly concedes by falling back to a cross-count assertion (`_mac_tgz_n > _mac_dmg_n` ⇒ contaminated) and by noting the set \"rides the pre-collection clean (fresh path) / P-005 verification (reuse)\". The only instrument that can actually tell a stale tgz from a current one is the per-artifact sha256 in build-provenance.json. So for mac, provenance is not corroboration — it is THE expected-set oracle.\n\n#### Ruling\n1. **Wiring mac REQUIRES making its provenance emission fatal** (both in `build-mac-cross.sh` and in release-local's mac collection block). Until then a mac receipt is unsound in a specific way: the leg's completeness predicate would have to treat \"no provenance\" as retryable-absent, so a COMPLETE mac build whose emit warned would be rebuilt, and — on a committed receipt — would hard-fail the cut as \"committed but absent\". Fail-closed, never a false receipt, but also never resumable. Treat the fatal-emit change as part of P-002's mac increment, not as a follow-up.\n2. **This does not weaken the windows leg that just landed.** Windows does not share the defect: its producer hard-fails a role yielding no installer (`:594`), hard-fails a missing `.sig` (`:826`), and its installers are all version-scoped, so its expected set is countable without provenance and provenance is corroboration.\n3. **arm64/android stay OUT** — D-004's finding stands, tracked as WI-10002472.\n4. **P-002's stated leg list is therefore reduced deliberately, not abandoned**: windows DONE; mac requires the fatal-emit change above; linux-aarch64 + android ruled out by D-004. Record that departure on the item rather than silently shipping a shorter list.\n\n#### Method note (why this decision exists at all)\nD-005 was the cost of concluding a leg's capability from a comment naming a deleted file. This time the producer was read first and the comments were checked against it — and a SECOND stale copy of that same dead reference turned up in release-local's mac block (\"the Windows leg records build-provenance.json (inline in build-windows-on-vm.sh)\"), corrected in the same pass.\n\n### D-007 — P-002 is COMPLETE at linux+windows+mac+manifest: every stage holding the four receipt prerequisites is journalled, and arm64/android are excluded on a re-verified basis\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22 RULING (2026-09-22T21:05Z, su-ebc93), after the mac leg landed. This closes P-002's scope question, which D-003/D-004 left implicit: \"coverage\" needed a defined END, or the item could be read as unfinished forever because two legs exist that will never carry a receipt.\n\n#### Measured (this turn, against the current tree)\n- `for p in start prepare commit; do grep -oE \"release_task_leg_$p +[a-z0-9-]+\" papercusp-desktop/bin/release-local.sh | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u; done` -> **linux, mac, windows at ALL THREE phases** (was linux+windows).\n- Measured: `papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/release-content-identity.js:32-39` listed `linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, windows-x86_64, darwin-aarch64, darwin-x86_64, android` — **no universal entry**, while `release-local.sh` pins `MAC_BUILD_TARGET=universal-apple-darwin` and `MAC_OUT=$ROOT/src-tauri/target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle`, and `build-mac-cross.sh:158` sets `DMG_ARCH=\"universal-apple-darwin\"`. `darwin-universal` was ADDED to that list.\n- Measured: `papercusp-desktop/bin/build-mac-cross.sh:727` guarded the emit with `[[ -x … && ${#PROV_ARTIFACTS[@]} -gt 0 ]]` and ended `|| echo \"WARN: provenance emit failed (non-fatal)\"`; the `release-local.sh` mac collection block ended `|| echo \"WARNING: mac build-provenance.json emit failed (non-fatal)\"`. Both are now fatal.\n- Measured: `build-mac-cross.sh:469` (`[[ -f \"$tgz.sig\" ]] || fail`) and `:606` (`[[ -s \"$dmg.sig\" ]] || fail`) — the producer hard-fails without EITHER signature, which is what makes \"one signed dmg + one signed updater bundle per role\" the expected set rather than a guess.\n- Measured: `bash bin/lib/release-content-identity.selftest.sh` -> ALL PASS; `node --test test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js` -> 44 pass / 0 fail (was 36); `npm --prefix papercusp-desktop run test:shell` -> `tests 669 / pass 669 / fail 0`, exit 0.\n\n#### The prerequisite that had to be MADE true, not found true\nD-006 recorded mac as blocked on its own best-effort provenance. That was correct, and it is now fixed at both producers. Two silent-skip conditions went with it: the `-x` test on the emitter (it is invoked via `bash`, so the exec bit never gated execution — testing it only ever skipped the emit on a checkout that would have worked) and an empty `PROV_ARTIFACTS`.\n\nThis mattered because mac's provenance is an ORACLE, not a cross-check. Tauri leaves `<Product>.app.tar.gz` UNVERSIONED, so no count or filename can separate this cut's updater bundle from a prior cut's; the per-artifact sha256 is the only instrument that can. Linux (`release-local.sh` `emit_linux_build_provenance`) and Windows (`build-windows-cross.sh:764`) have always emitted fatally under `set -euo pipefail` — mac was the lone best-effort leg, i.e. the leg that could least afford to be.\n\n#### Platform key: darwin-universal, and NOT either existing darwin key\nD-006 carried `darwin-universal` as a placeholder and explicitly said do not guess it. Per the measurement above, neither existing darwin key describes a universal binary. Reusing a thin-arch key would make a universal receipt interchangeable with a single-arch one shipping different bytes. The platform is the receipt NAMESPACE; the selftest only requires that unknown keys are refused and that two keys never collide, both of which still hold.\n\n#### The scope ruling\nThe registry comment in `release-local.sh` states the four prerequisites a leg needs before a receipt is sound (a build-provenance emission; a reuse variable; an `assert_reused_provenance` label; a knowable EXPECTED artifact set). **linux, windows, mac and the manifest stage have all four and are journalled. arm64 and android have none of 1-3.**\n\nThat exclusion is RE-VERIFIED this turn by direct read, not inherited from D-004. Measured: the arm64 leg at `release-local.sh:2702` is a bare `for role in $PAPERCUSP_BUILD_ROLES` loop around `tauri build --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, with no `emit-build-provenance.sh` call, no `PAPERCUSP_REUSE_*` variable, and no `assert_reused_provenance` label. Giving it a receipt would not be wiring — it would mean BUILDING those three prerequisites first, which is its own change, tracked by WI-10002472. A receipt that passes on bytes nothing can verify is worse than no receipt: it is a false guarantee.\n\n**Therefore P-002 is done.** A lane that reads \"receipt coverage\" as \"every leg including arm64/android\" is working from a scope this decision closes; that work is real but it is NOT P-002.\n\n#### Falsifiability\nThree mutation probes, all `verdict=caught`, each followed by `tree integrity: VERIFIED — byte-identical` (copy-out; the shared tree was never mutated): dropping the mac cross-count contamination rule; deleting the `[mac]=RELEASE_TASK_MAC` registry row; and restoring the exact pre-P-002 non-fatal `|| echo \"WARN: provenance emit failed (non-fatal)\"` line.\n\n### D-008 — P-003 is FOUR clauses with four different dispositions — one is already built, one is a parity port, two are real gaps\nDate: 2026-09-22\nRULING (2026-09-22T22:20Z, su-ebc93). Any lane reading P-003's one-line text as a single unit of work will build a second seed-transaction layer beside a working one — D-003's failure exactly. P-003 is more exposed to it than P-002, because its four clauses have four DIFFERENT dispositions.\n\n#### The authoritative requirement is R-3, not the item one-liner\n\nMeasured from the plan body this turn: **R-3** — \"Cargo, sidecar, seed, package, compression, provenance, and manifest outputs are cached by content and policy identity, with transactional seed manifests and a proven sparse-to-full fallback when sparse holders cannot boot.\" Design adds: \"Record compression policy (including xz preset) in provenance.\" **R-2** demands receipts carry \"output paths and hashes\". Judge done-ness against those, not the item text.\n\n#### Clause 2 — \"transactional seed manifests\": ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. Do not rebuild.\n\n`withSeedOutput` (apps/operator/lib/release/cut-seed-cli.ts:1152-1188) mkdtemps a sibling transaction dir, builds into `next/`, then `rename(outDir -> previous/)` + `rename(next/ -> outDir)` with rollback and an AggregateError preserving the prior seed. The manifest write (:1541) happens INSIDE staging, BEFORE the swap — so the presence of `manifest.json` already implies a completed publication. Contract comment (:1149): \"a failed cut must preserve the entire prior seed, including its manifest and epoch keys.\" Cite it; do not re-add it. If a future change moves any manifest/epoch-key write AFTER the rename, this clause reopens.\n\n#### Clause 3 — \"sparse-holder fallback\": EXISTS, in the SIBLING producer. A parity port.\n\nThe proven sparse-to-full fallback is `papercusp-desktop/bin/ensure-release-seed.sh` — :230 \"The cut is a function so the P-014 sparse fallback below can re-run it verbatim\", :266 \"P-014 (D-012) — the sparse fallback. cut-seed-cli now REFUSES --sparse when it cannot [append a head snapshot]\". `release-local.sh` does NOT call it: it carries its own `cut_release_seed()` (:1985-2084) duplicating the cut with NO fallback. Its `seed_reuse=auto` (:2030) takes the FRESH path whenever no committed corestore exists, then hard-fails on a busy box — the EI-17143 drain/fd-lock failure its own comment (:2017-2028) describes.\n\nSame shape as P-002's mac fix: the mechanism is not in dispute and needs no design argument; one producer is out of parity with its proven sibling. Port it — or better, converge the duplicate onto `ensure-release-seed.sh`, which closes the clause by construction.\n\n#### Clause 1 — \"persist reusable stage outputs\": REAL GAP. Evidence refs are write-only.\n\nAll five evidence-ref sites in release-local.sh (:1134, :1136, :1170, :1369, :1370) are `--evidence` WRITES. Nothing reads one back, so no reuse decision is checked against what the receipt committed:\n\n- Build legs commit `artifact-set:hash-signature-verified` — a LABEL — plus `build-provenance:sha256:<sha>`, which digests ONE file in the bundle, never the artifact set's paths and hashes. On a `reuse` hit `release_task_verify_<leg>_artifacts` re-derives everything from the CURRENT tree (cardinality + provenance + signature), so a different-but-internally-consistent artifact set passes.\n- The manifest stage is closer but still open: `release_task_manifest_output_digest` (:1333) computes a real output digest and commits it as `manifest-receipt:sha256:<d>` — then `release_task_commit_manifest_stage` returns early on `action=reuse` (:1352), so the stored digest is never compared.\n\nTwo-sided fix, and the second side is what matters: persist output paths+hashes AND verify them on reuse. Persisting alone reproduces the manifest stage's existing half-measure.\n\n#### Clause 4 — \"key compressed package reuse by input hash PLUS compression policy\": REAL GAP.\n\n`release_task_content_identity` (release-local.sh:791-813) passes 14 `PAPERCUSP_REUSE_*` policy vars into bin/lib/release-content-identity.js (signer, roles, tauri CLI, host, channel, rustflags, channel config, 6 skip/allow flags). **None is a compression policy.** Two real ones exist, both tunable:\n\n- `stage-source-tree.sh:385` `zstd_level=\"${PAPERCUSP_SOURCE_ZSTD_LEVEL:-6}\"`, applied at :421 as `zstd -T0 \"-${zstd_level}\" --long=27` — the `source.tar.zst` package.\n- `repack-deb-xz.sh:104` `xz -9 \"-T${XZ_THREADS}\" \"--memlimit-compress=${XZ_MEMORY_LIMIT}\"` — the xz preset Design names explicitly.\n\nChange any and the reuse key is byte-identical, so a package compressed under one policy satisfies a request for another. Search trap: \"compression\" appears exactly ONCE in release-local.sh, in an unrelated comment — a keyword grep reads as \"already handled\".\n\n#### Order (by prerequisite)\n\n1. **Clause 4** — self-contained, and the one a keyword search hides.\n2. **Clause 1** — core of R-2/R-3: persist output paths+hashes and CHECK them on reuse.\n3. **Clause 3** — parity port.\n4. **Clause 2** — no code; cite `withSeedOutput`.\n\n### D-009 — CORRECTION to D-008: the sparse fallback is PORTED into release-local.sh, not converged onto ensure-release-seed.sh — that script ships seedless on failure\nDate: 2026-09-22\nRULING (2026-09-22T22:55Z, su-ebc93). This revises ONE clause of D-008 on measurement made after it was written. D-008's clause-3 analysis stands; only its closing preference does not.\n\n#### What D-008 got ahead of the evidence\n\nD-008 said of clause 3: \"Port it — or better, converge the duplicate onto `ensure-release-seed.sh`, which closes the clause by construction.\" I wrote that having read the fallback's LOCATION but not that script's FAILURE CONTRACT. Reading it changes the answer.\n\n#### Measured: converging would widen what a release may publish\n\n`ensure-release-seed.sh:299-310`, on a failed cut:\n\n- `seed_usable` → `log \"a usable committed seed is still present — continuing the build with it\"; exit 0` — it proceeds on the STALE committed seed;\n- otherwise, unless `PAPERCUSP_SEED_REQUIRED=1`, `log \"WARN: no usable seed after a failed cut — bundle ships seedless (cold-join)\"; exit 0`.\n\nBoth exit **0**. That tolerance is correct for the dev-bundle path it serves, and wrong for a release cut: calling that script from `release-local.sh` would silently make \"ships a stale seed\" and \"ships seedless\" successful outcomes of a RELEASE, which is a policy change well outside P-003 and one nobody reviewed — least of all while owner directive #96 has the cut paused.\n\nConvergence is therefore not the cheaper option; it is a different, unrequested decision wearing the costume of de-duplication. The duplication D-008 objected to is real, but the two call sites genuinely differ in failure posture, which is exactly when a shared helper is the wrong shape.\n\n#### What landed instead\n\nThe P-014/D-012 recovery is ported verbatim in behaviour (`release-local.sh`): the cut becomes a function so the fallback can re-run it with a different flag set; a refused `--sparse` retries ONCE as a full cut; `--no-force-backfill` is used only when the refused attempt's log proves its refresh completed. The release posture is kept EXPLICIT and opposite to the sibling's: both attempts failing returns 1 and aborts the cut — it never falls back to the stale committed seed and never ships seedless.\n\nThe two decisions are split out as pure predicates (`release_seed_sparse_refused`, `release_seed_fallback_args`) because the cut itself shells out to `npx tsx` inside a subshell; logic left inline with it is reachable only by running a real seed cut, which is why the sibling's fallback has never had a test. Both are now covered, and both are proven falsifiable by copy-out mutation probes.\n\n#### Standing consequence\n\nThe duplicate cut in `release-local.sh` is now DELIBERATE, not an oversight — do not \"clean it up\" by routing it through `ensure-release-seed.sh` without first deciding, explicitly, whether a release may ship a stale or seedless bundle. A regression guard asserts the release posture directly (it requires the refusal string and, after stripping comments, rejects any seedless/cold-join tolerance inside `cut_release_seed`).\n\n\n## Conformance\n\nExecutable regression bindings for the existing R-1 through R-4, added during P-003 closure on 2026-10-16. These bindings preserve the original requirement scope; R-4 is completed by P-004 before plan acceptance. Node tests use the desktop package runner; Vitest files use test:file.\n\n```conformance\n{\n  \"footprint\": {\n    \"paths\": [\n      \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.mts\",\n      \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.test.ts\",\n      \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release-cut*\",\n      \"papercusp-desktop/bin/release-local.sh\",\n      \"papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/release-content-identity*\",\n      \"papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js\",\n      \"apps/operator/lib/release/cut-seed-cli*\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"requirements\": {\n    \"R-1\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"release-resume-regression\",\n          \"stage\": \"implementation\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"Operation discovery or source/version/gitlink binding is lost across a recreated release context.\",\n          \"check\": {\n            \"kind\": \"tests\",\n            \"files\": [\n              \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.test.ts\"\n            ]\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-2\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"release-resume-regression\",\n          \"stage\": \"implementation\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"A phase reuses missing, corrupted, changed or expired outputs, or skips comparing its committed receipt digest.\",\n          \"check\": {\n            \"kind\": \"tests\",\n            \"files\": [\n              \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.test.ts\",\n              \"papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js\"\n            ]\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-3\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"release-resume-regression\",\n          \"stage\": \"implementation\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"Seed replacement loses the prior committed seed on failure, sparse refusal does not retry safely, or output/compression policy identity fails to invalidate reuse.\",\n          \"check\": {\n            \"kind\": \"tests\",\n            \"files\": [\n              \"apps/operator/lib/release/cut-seed-cli.test.ts\",\n              \"papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js\"\n            ]\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-4\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"release-resume-regression\",\n          \"stage\": \"implementation\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"Interruption changes the next valid phase, replays a spent request, accepts stale receipt bytes, or permits an unverified manifest.\",\n          \"check\": {\n            \"kind\": \"tests\",\n            \"files\": [\n              \"scripts/lib/release-task-journal.test.ts\",\n              \"papercusp-desktop/test/release-local-linux-reuse.test.js\"\n            ]\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"deterministic-tool-definition-delivery-2026-09-21","title":"Deterministic tool-definition delivery: derive WHICH tools are advertised and HOW MUCH schema each one ships from measured demand x measured bytes, instead of hand-maintained seed lists","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-21","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Deterministic tool-definition delivery: derive WHICH tools are advertised and HOW MUCH schema each one ships from measured demand x measured bytes, instead of hand-maintained seed lists\nslug: deterministic-tool-definition-delivery-2026-09-21\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-21\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nReplace the hand-maintained agent tool-seed lists with ONE deterministic function that decides, per tool and per agent kind, **how that tool's definition is sent**: full schema, compact schema, or not advertised at all (deferred to `tools:find` / `tools:invoke`). The inputs are measured demand and measured wire bytes under an explicit per-agent byte budget; the output is a generated artifact with a build-time drift check.\n\nThis is the owner's question, asked twice and never answered, made executable:\n\n> \"its also relevant how mcuh we gain by the shortining and the frequency. The right approach is some function of 'how frequently used' + 'how much is gained by trimming' do you think we should turn that into a deterministic fucntion that determies how tool definitions are sent?\"\n> -- [owner:Avi 2026-09-21], codex thread 01a0c4bb-9c14-7cf0-be63-3cd768915e83 ordinals 1256 and 1265 (the thread's last agentMessage is ordinal 1246, so both turns died unanswered when the session carry-respawned).\n\nThe answer is **yes**, with two corrections the plan encodes as Decisions: the frequency numerator must be DISTINCT CALLERS rather than call count, and the decision must not be binary -- a middle \"compact schema\" tier is what makes the trade-off solvable rather than a forced choice between 30 KB/turn and one round-trip.\n\n## Why now\n\n- **The current mechanism is hand-maintained metadata that describes code** -- exactly the rung-4 CURATED case the derived-truth ladder says to move to rung 1. `CLAUDE_MINIMAL_SEED_TOOL_NAMES` (31 names), `OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES`, `CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES` and their ratchets/budgets are all hand-curated lists in `apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs`, each entry justified in a docstring by measured numbers that were true on the day someone measured them.\n- **The known failure mode of that shape is documented in the code itself.** EI-23319364088969722: \"every one of those 64 names was added individually, each with real demand evidence and each individually defensible. NOTHING EVER MEASURED THE AGGREGATE.\" The seed reached 432,714 B on the wire (~157K tokens on EVERY turn of EVERY psu Claude session) one defensible append at a time. None of them CHOOSES the list. So the hand curation still has to be re-done by a human every time demand moves, and between those passes the list is stale by construction.\n- **It is measurably stale right now.** Over 14 days in papercusp-workspace (1,780,234 calls, 460 distinct tools, 3,189 distinct callers), several of the highest-breadth tools are NOT advertised to Claude while lower-breadth ones are. `improvements:capture` reaches 870 distinct callers and is deferred; `coord:send` 578; `locks:acquire` 422 is seeded. They were cut on BYTES alone -- the right instinct applied with only one of the two terms the owner named.\n- **Denying ToolSearch removed the escape valve.** Claude's native schema deferral is implemented BY ToolSearch; psu denies ToolSearch by owner directive, so every advertised tool ships its FULL argSchema on every turn. Today there are three hand lists with a drift guard asserting they stay DISJOINT. budgetBytes })` -> a per-agent map of tool -> `full | compact | deferred` -> a GENERATED data module -> `claudeSeedToolNames()` / `ompCoreToolNames()` in the launcher -> `PAPERCUSP_TOOLS` on the MCP url -> the server's `tools/list` projection.\n\nNothing in that path consults a hand-written list, and every input is committed, so the output is reproducible from a checkout with no database.\n\n### Reuse and implementation seams\n\nThe cost instruments already exist and are reused rather than reinvented: `advertisedWireBytes`, `serializedInputSchemaBytes`, `namedToolSchemaBytes`, `namedToolWeights` and `promptWeight` in `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/tool-guidance-budget.ts`, over `listAllProjectedTools()` from `@papercusp/tooldef` (`libs/generic/tooldef`). The compact-schema reducer is domain-free and therefore starts in `libs/generic/tooldef` behind the generic-first rule, not inside `operator-core/lib` to be extracted later.\n\nThe routing-table floor is READ from `apps/operator/lib/seed-mandate-coverage.ts`, which already derives the promoted set from the generated bash->tool routing table; it is not re-listed. `$defs`/`$ref` structure is preserved through compaction rather than inlined, because `$defs` is exactly what keeps duplicated sub-schemas out of the byte budget (`schema-ref-inline.ts` documents the opposite direction for discovery renderers only).\n\nThe existing aggregate guards (`claude-seed-wire-budget.test.ts`, `omp-seed-wire-budget.test.ts`, `tool-schema-byte-budget.test.ts`) are re-pointed at the derived seed rather than removed: they remain the ceiling the derivation must respect, which keeps a bad generation a build failure rather than a launch failure. `PAPERCUSP_CLAUDE_FULL_SEED` and `PAPERCUSP_OMP_TOOLS_EXCLUDE` keep working unchanged, so the instant revert is still one env var.\n\nThe launcher is dependency-free by design, so the generated artifact is a plain data module it can import with no build step.\n\n### Actual-session continuation candidate (D-058 / P-015)\n\nThe initial generated seed remains reproduced from committed demand, catalog bytes, floors and the unchanged 100000-byte budget. The proposed continued-session exception derives membership and original FULL definitions only from canonical tools actually invoked by this workspace and stable owner, using the existing invocation ledger, workspace-qualified surface key and tools/list_changed notification. Activation or discovery alone never promotes detail. Authorization and confinement filter the current catalog before projection; retired or unauthorized names create no definition or permission. No new store, ranking, decay, eviction policy or fourth tier is introduced. This history-derived layer is default ON after independent contract approval; the curated PAPERCUSP_CLAUDE_FULL_SEED escape hatch remains default OFF. Continued-session definition bytes may grow beyond the initial-seed budget and must be measured and disclosed separately.\n\nP-015 must prove real client notification and received FULL definitions after direct and nested invocation, reconnect, memory reset, workspace/owner isolation and retryable restoration failure. Both existing SUT provider loops must mirror actual-use promotion and retain per-request exact definition manifests in the existing persisted raw transcript. The static FULL control remains unchanged. New arm identities, complete five-scenario replication, model/scenario/artifact/config pins and unchanged R-6/R-9 decision rules must be preregistered before any new LLM measurements. D-049/D-053/D-056 remain adverse history and failed rows are never retried.
