Host promotion remains unwired until source scope and canonical BAR review; this is not R6 acceptance.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — The demand numerator is DISTINCT CALLERS, not call count\nDate: 2026-09-21\nThe owner said \"how frequently used\". Call COUNT is the wrong operationalisation of that: it is dominated by loop and heartbeat tools (activity:report 622,195 calls over 14d; coord:glance 124,692) which are fired by machinery, not chosen by a model deciding what to do next. DISTINCT CALLERS measures BREADTH OF NEED -- how many independent agents ever had to reach for this tool -- which is exactly what an up-front advertisement buys. Ratio on the same window: activity:report is 622k calls / 2,677 callers (233 calls per caller, a loop) vs work_items:get 38,706 / 1,044 (37, genuine breadth). The policy function therefore takes callers as the numerator and records calls only as a tiebreak.\n\n### D-002 — Three delivery tiers, not binary seed membership\nDate: 2026-09-21\nToday the decision is binary: a tool is advertised with its FULL argSchema (coord:send = 39,254 B on every turn of every session) or it is invisible to the model and costs a tools:find round-trip. That forced choice is why the 2026-09-15 cut had to drop seven high-demand heavies. Adding a COMPACT tier -- argSchema reduced to the machine-critical skeleton (property names, types, required set, enums, numeric/length bounds, oneOf discriminators) with prose descriptions and examples stripped -- makes the trade-off continuous. The policy resolves each tool to FULL | COMPACT | DEFERRED. This is also what makes the owner's two terms combine into one function rather than compete: high demand + high bytes now resolves to COMPACT instead of losing to a budget.\n\n### D-003 — The generator reads a FROZEN, COMMITTED demand snapshot -- never the live DB\nDate: 2026-09-21\nThe generated seed must be reproducible offline, in CI, and from any checkout, and its diff must be reviewable. A generator that queries harness_shared.tool_invocations at build time produces a different answer every run, cannot run in the green-checkpoint checkout, and makes the drift --check meaningless. So demand is captured into a committed JSON snapshot by a separate, explicitly-run refresh command; the generator is a pure function of (catalog, snapshot, budget, floors). Refreshing the snapshot is a reviewable diff that shows exactly which tools moved.\n\n### D-004 — Floors bypass the score but may only choose a CHEAPER TIER, never be dropped\nDate: 2026-09-21\nFour classes of tool must be advertised regardless of measured demand, because their absence does not degrade gracefully: (1) REACHABILITY FLOOR -- tools:find and tools:invoke, without which the entire deferred catalog is unreachable; (2) ROUTING-TABLE MANDATE -- names the generated bash->tool table promotes, already machine-checked by seed-mandate-coverage; (3) SILENT-HALT LIFECYCLE -- session:request-compaction, loop:status, coord:declare-intent and friends, whose absence HALTS or strands rather than slows; (4) PROSE MANDATE -- duties stated in root CLAUDE.md that no machine guard covers. A floor guarantees a tool is at least COMPACT. It does NOT guarantee FULL: the policy may still resolve a floor tool to COMPACT when bytes demand it. This keeps the budget binding without letting it break a mandate.\n\n### D-005 — One derivation for claude, codex and omp; agent kind is a PARAMETER\nDate: 2026-09-21\nOwner directive [Avi 2026-09-21]: \"lets make omp claude and codex use the same tool list in trimmed mode\". Today there are three hand lists (OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES, CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES, CLAUDE_MINIMAL_SEED_TOOL_NAMES) plus a drift guard asserting two of them stay DISJOINT -- a rule that only exists because they are separate lists. resolveToolDelivery takes agentKind and varies only its BUDGET and its FLOOR SET; the ranking and the tier assignment are identical. Divergence between agents becomes a data difference with a stated reason, not three lists that drift independently.\n\n### D-006 — Guidance tiering is IN SCOPE -- the owner asked for it directly\nDate: 2026-09-21\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-21] thread 01a0c4bb ordinal 1122, verbatim: \"when we provide tools are we providing the full guidance as well?  What if we provided two tiers?  one with full guidance and one with partial guidance?  how verbose is the guidance can it be shortened without losing information?\". So the delivery decision covers BOTH halves of a tool definition, not just argSchema: a resolved tier fixes (a) how much SCHEMA ships and (b) how much GUIDANCE ships. The two halves have different cost profiles and must be measured separately -- promptWeight() governs description+guidance at a 1,500-char budget while argSchema is unbudgeted per-tool beyond SCHEMA_BYTE_BUDGET, and coord:send is the canonical split (~1.2 KB of guidance against 39,254 B of schema). A tier is therefore a PAIR (schemaDetail, guidanceDetail), and the FULL/COMPACT/DEFERRED names in D-002 refer to that pair. The owner's last question (\"can it be shortened without losing information?\") is an acceptance condition, not rhetoric: the compaction must be lossless for machine-critical content and is tested as such.\n\n### D-007 — The Aug-20 26-tool list is the BASELINE the derivation is sanity-checked against\nDate: 2026-09-21\nCORRECTED 2026-09-21 -- THE 26-TOOL FIGURE IS WRONG, AND IT WAS REPORTED TO THE OWNER AS FACT.\n\nThe owner's directive [owner:Avi 2026-09-21, thread 01a0c4bb ord 1083/1091] was: \"get the tool list we had at '- Aug. 20: 19 OMP-core tools + 7 Claude extras = 26 tools.' lets make omp claude and codex use the same tool list in trimmed mode.  lets base it off these 26 plus any other you think we should add based on usage frequency\". That directive rests on a number the PRIOR SESSION produced in its own answer at ord 1246 and never verified against the code.\n\nMEASURED: at the last Aug-20 commit (84829ccc, 2026-08-20T23:23:39Z) the advertised set was OMP_CORE_MCP_TOOL_NAMES = 43 names and CLAUDE_SEED_EXTRA_TOOL_NAMES = 18 names, i.e. 61 advertised to Claude, not 26. MEASURED SEED HISTORY (apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs, one commit sampled per day, arrays parsed with a hyphen-aware tool-name regex and calibrated against three independently-known values the prior analysis got RIGHT -- Sep-11 = 48+16 = 64, Sep-15 minimal = 31, current OMP core = 49): Jul-07 omp 34 · Aug-10 43+14 = 57 · Aug-12 through Aug-23 43+18 = 61 · Aug-24 44+18 = 62 · Aug-26 45+17 = 62 · Aug-27 46+17 = 63 · Sep-11 48+16 = 64 · Sep-15 minimal seed 31 · Sep-19 onward omp 49, claude 31.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ARITHMETIC. The prior session used the 26 figure to tell the owner \"the seed had grown from about 26 tools to 64\" and presented seed growth as roughly co-equal with the ToolSearch-deny in causing the regression. On the measured numbers the seed went 61 -> 64 between Aug 20 and Sep 11, a 5% change. So seed growth is NOT what made the context explode recently: the step-change was essentially ENTIRELY the 2026-09-11 --disallowedTools=ToolSearch launch flag, which removed native schema deferral and made an already-large seed arrive inline on every turn. The prior session's own ord-1246 text actually says this (\"The decisive step-change was the Sept. 11 ToolSearch-deny change\") -- the 26 figure contradicted its own conclusion and nobody noticed.\n\nWHAT THE DECISION IS NOW. There is no 26-name list to base anything on. The baseline control is the MEASURED Aug-20 61-name set, recovered from commit 84829ccc and committed with the demand snapshot. P-012 emits the generator's diff against THAT set. The owner's intent -- start from a known-good working set and justify every addition by usage frequency -- is preserved exactly; only the false starting number is replaced. The owner has been told.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-008 — Agent COMPREHENSION is an acceptance condition, not an assumption\nDate: 2026-09-21\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-21] thread 01a0c4bb ordinal 1195, verbatim: \"will agents handle this well or will it confuse them?\". A compacted schema that saves bytes but causes malformed calls is a regression, and byte measurements cannot detect it. The prior session's own research (ord 1246) flagged the same risk from the outside: \"Weaker/local models may find deeply indirect schemas harder to use even if the client accepts them.\" So shipping requires behavioural evidence alongside byte evidence -- an llm-test run (npm --prefix apps/operator run llm-test) exercising real calls against COMPACT-tier definitions, plus the invalid-args rate for affected tools read from tool_invocations before and after. A byte win with a comprehension regression does not ship.\n\n### D-009 — The unified trimmed-mode budget is 100,000 B for claude, codex AND omp — unify DOWN, not up\nDate: 2026-09-21\nOwner directive [Avi 2026-09-21] was \"lets make omp claude and codex use the same tool list in trimmed mode\" (D-005). That leaves one number undecided: WHICH budget the unified list is cut against. The three live ceilings disagreed — CLAUDE_SEED_WIRE_BYTE_BUDGET = 100,000 B (claude-seed-wire-budget.test.ts), the OMP spine's D-001 ceiling = 262,144 B (omp-seed-wire-budget.test.ts), and codex had no measured ceiling at all.\n\nRULING: all three take 100,000 B, the TIGHTEST of the three. Unifying up to OMP's 262,144 B would have been the conservative-looking choice and is the wrong one: it would nearly triple Claude's advertised wire payload to solve a problem that the COMPACT tier already solves.\n\nMEASURED JUSTIFICATION (npm run gen:tool-delivery -- --report, 2026-09-21T22:56Z, catalog 899 tools, demand snapshot captured 22:40:11Z):\n  claude/codex/omp, all identical: 43 FULL + 47 COMPACT = 90 advertised, 809 deferred, 99,898 B of 100,000 B, overrun 0.\n\nCompare the hand-maintained list this replaces: CLAUDE_MINIMAL_SEED_TOOL_NAMES is 31 names whose own docstring totals ~106,873 B (2,873 + 54,396 + 18,072 + 31,532). So the derivation advertises ~2.9x as many tools (90 vs 31) for ~7,000 FEWER bytes. That is D-002 paying out exactly as argued: once a schema can ship without its prose, the budget stops being a zero-sum fight between heavyweights, and matching OMP down to Claude's ceiling costs OMP nothing it was actually using.\n\nCONSEQUENCE for P-008: CLAUDE_MINIMAL_SEED_MAX_NAMES = 31 is now actively WRONG as a ratchet — the derivation legitimately produces 90 names, and a name-count ceiling was only ever a proxy for the byte budget it now measures directly. Retire it rather than raising it, and record that the binding constraint is bytes.\n\nThe three budgets are still spelled out PER KIND in TRIMMED_BUDGET_BYTES rather than collapsed to a single constant, so a future divergence has to be a visible data edit carrying its own reason — not a code change nobody reviews.\n\n### D-010 — The Aug-20 baseline is a FLOOR, not merely a comparison — and at COMPACT it costs 93,769 B, so it fits\nDate: 2026-09-21\nP-012's baseline diff was authored as a REPORT and immediately became a FINDING, which is the strongest argument for having built it.\n\nWHAT THE FIRST DIFF MEASURED (npm run gen:tool-delivery -- --report, 2026-09-21T23:58Z, baseline commit 84829ccc, catalog 899, demand snapshot 22:40:11Z): kept 41, added 49, DROPPED 20 of the 61 owner-directed Aug-20 names. The dropped set was not marginal. It was the ENTIRE work-item lifecycle (work_items:create / claim_next / complete / release / set_state / update / checkpoint), the ENTIRE plan-authoring surface (plans:new / plans:items / plans:set-status / plans:set-now / plans:add-decision), plus coord:send, improvements:capture, facts:assert, facts:retract, loop:checkpoint, events:await, fleet:launch-on-plan and search:fulltext.\n\nWHY THEY LOST, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED. Not low demand -- improvements:capture has 863 distinct callers, the second-highest in the whole catalog, and coord:send has 577. They lost on VALUE DENSITY because they are the heaviest schemas in the catalog: coord:send is 32,612 B at FULL, work_items:complete 25,257 B, work_items:checkpoint 24,125 B. Against a 100,000 B budget, three of them would eat 82% of it.\n\nWHAT THE DIRECTIVE ACTUALLY SAID. D-007 quotes the owner verbatim: \"lets base it off these plus any other you think we should add based on usage frequency\". \"Base it off these PLUS any other\" is a FLOOR statement -- keep this set, then add. Leaving the baseline as a mere input to a ranking makes it droppable, and a ranking duly dropped a third of it. That is the defect: not the ranking, but the baseline's lack of standing.\n\nRULING: the Aug-20 61-name union becomes a fifth FLOOR TIER, 'owner-baseline', in apps/operator/lib/tool-delivery-floors.ts -- DERIVED from the committed measurement of commit 84829ccc, never re-listed by hand. Floors guarantee >= COMPACT and never FULL (D-004), which is exactly what makes this affordable.\n\nMEASURED AFFORDABILITY, and the number that settles it: the WHOLE 61-name baseline at COMPACT is 93,769 B of the 100,000 B budget (41 kept = 30,066 B, 20 dropped = 63,703 B), leaving 6,231 B for demand-ranked additions. So the owner's directive was never in tension with D-009's budget -- it was in tension with the FULL tier, and the COMPACT tier introduced by D-002 is precisely what dissolves that tension. Restoring the same 20 names at FULL would have cost 163,601 B and been genuinely unaffordable; this is the concrete payoff of three-way admission over all-or-nothing.\n\nCONSEQUENCE, stated plainly because it is a real trade: the resolved map gets SMALLER in name count than the unfloored 90 and carries fewer names at FULL. That is the correct direction. A seat spent on a name the owner never asked for, while a name they explicitly named is deferred, is the ranking optimising the wrong objective.\n\nWHAT I CHECKED AND DID NOT CONCLUDE -- recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it. The first diff also showed activity:report (2,644 callers, 618,956 calls) as the single highest-ranked admission, which looks like D-001's stated fix failing: D-001 moved the numerator from CALLS to CALLERS specifically to stop ranking loop machinery, and named activity:report as the canonical example. I tried to quantify a 'machinery' class by calls-per-caller and the heuristic DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE -- at a >20 ratio it also catches tools:find (52), state:read (131), capability:bash (45), facts:list (218) and locks:acquire (28), all of which are genuinely model-chosen tools that agents simply call often. Only activity:report (234), accounts:status (8,371), coord:emit (27) and locks:check_command (122) look machinery-shaped, and together they are a few KB of a 99,898 B budget. So the machinery critique is NOT supported by a measurement and is explicitly NOT part of this ruling. The owner-baseline floor fixes the observed harm without needing it.\n\n### D-011 — COMPACT ships a SUMMARY, not silence — and P-010's specified 'partial' projection is a MEASURED near-no-op\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-21\n\nP-010 was written to add a PARTIAL-GUIDANCE tier: keep `when`, drop `notWhen`/`chaining`. Built and measured against the live catalog it SAVES 0.8%. Recording the negative result, because the next reader will otherwise re-propose it.\n\nMEASURED (npm run gen:tool-delivery -- --report, catalog=899):\n  GUIDANCE_BYTES full=334,797 partial=332,013 summary=114,971 compact=0\n  savedByPartial=2,784 (0.8%)   savedBySummary=219,826 (65.7%)\n  GUIDANCE_LOSS reducedNotWhen=13 reducedChaining=5 railsRetained=0\n  GUIDANCE_SHAPE tools=899 explicitDescription=886 composedFromGuidance=13\n\nROOT CAUSE, verified in code not inferred: `describeFromGuidance()` (libs/generic/tooldef/src/define-tool.ts) composes a description from when/notWhen/chaining ONLY for tools that omit an explicit `description`. 886 of 899 declare one. On the MCP wire — where `description` is a tool's single prose field — there are almost no guidance sections to drop. A projection that reduces only COMPOSED descriptions cannot cut a catalog that is 98.6% not composed. `partial` is retained as a measured exported projection (it is what makes the 0.8% falsifiable) but is NOT what the delivery tier uses.\n\nTHE LARGER FINDING. COMPACT shipped `description: ''`. Under D-010's floor the map was full=4 / compact=67 — so 67 of 71 ADVERTISED tools reached the model as a bare name plus a schema. A prose-less tool still occupies a budget seat while being unidentifiable: the same failure as the 2026-05-21 'Tool X' placeholder incident, where the brain confabulated rather than call tools it could not distinguish.\n\nRULING: COMPACT = compact schema + SUMMARY prose. `summaryGuidanceDescription()` keeps one lead sentence PLUS every hard refusal/safety clause, wherever it appears. Rails are never traded for the lead: a summary that fits by dropping 'this is irreversible' is not a cheaper tier, it is a more dangerous one.\n\nTHE CAP IS A MEASUREMENT. SUMMARY_LEAD_MAX_CHARS=100 is the LARGEST cap fitting D-009's 100,000 B budget, per the SUMMARY_CAP_SWEEP instrument added to scripts/gen-tool-delivery.ts, which re-prices the catalog and re-resolves the map per candidate:\n  cap=0   full=4 compact=67 spent=100,000 FITS  <- but 67 ship NO prose\n  cap=80  full=2 compact=61 spent= 99,962 FITS\n  cap=100 full=0 compact=63 spent= 99,996 FITS  <- CHOSEN\n  cap=120 full=0 compact=62 spent=100,293 OVERRUN\n  cap=200 full=0 compact=62 spent=101,254 OVERRUN\nAn earlier draft named cap=200; it overruns by 1,254 B and is SUPERSEDED. Re-run the sweep after a catalog change rather than hand-editing the constant.\n\nTHE TRADE, stated because it is real: pricing prose in costs 8 advertised seats (71 -> 63), and `full` drops to 0 because no spare density remains to buy upgrades. Both are the right direction. A COMPACT tool is still fully CALLABLE — compaction removes prose, never contract — so the loss is prose depth, not capability; an empty description instead makes a seated tool unidentifiable, and the 8 tools losing a seat stay reachable via `tools:find`. VERIFIED after regeneration: full=0 compact=63 deferred=836 spent=99,996 overrun=0, TOOL_DELIVERY_BASELINE kept=61 of 61 dropped=0 — D-010's owner-baseline mandate fully satisfied at the chosen cap.\n\nLOCKSTEP IS THE LOAD-BEARING INVARIANT. compactWireBytes (measurement) and applyCompactTier (delivery) must project the description identically. If delivery ships prose that measurement priced at zero, every spentBytes and the budget itself become a fiction — and it fails SILENTLY, because every 'compact < full' assertion still passes. Pinned by a reconciliation test in tool-allowlist.test.ts that serializes the DELIVERED listing and asserts its byte length equals compactWireBytes(...).compact, keeping the old empty-description behaviour permanently as a control that must NOT reconcile. Verified 51/51 across the three touched suites.\n\nANSWER TO THE OWNER'S QUESTION ('how verbose is the guidance, can it be shortened without losing information?'): shortened yes, without losing information NO — and the loss is stated, not assured. 65.7% of prose bytes removed catalog-wide. Lost: every sentence after the first, except hard rails. Kept: the selection signal and all safety text. `partialGuidanceLoss()` reports the per-tool loss set so the trade is arguable from numbers.\n\nCONSEQUENCES: P-011 must measure comprehension against THIS final tier (cap=100), never the P-006 interim prose-less one. P-009 must document the negative partial result beside the shipped summary tier, so the 0.8% is not rediscovered.\nRelated: P-010, P-011, P-009\n\n### D-012 — P-011's specified instrument (llm-test --target su) CANNOT measure D-008 — it delivers a hand-authored catalog\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22\n\nMeasured: 2026-09-22T00:45Z, working tree at staging.\n  (a) `grep -n 'export function buildCatalog' packages/operator-core/lib/llm-testing/targets/su-catalog.ts` -> line 833: `export function buildCatalog(entries: ReadonlyArray<SuCatalogEntry> = SU_CATALOG): BuiltCatalog`. Body (834-846) iterates `entries` only; no catalog/projection import.\n  (b) `grep -rlE 'tools_compact|applyCompactTier|compactInputSchema|parseCompactToolNames' --include=*.ts packages/operator-core/lib/llm-testing apps/operator/bin` -> ZERO files.\n  (c) POSITIVE CONTROL, same pattern, wider root -> 6 files: _mcp-host.ts, tool-allowlist.ts, psu-launcher.mjs, claude-integration.ts, claude-seed-wire-budget.test.ts, dist-host/hono-host.mjs. So (b)'s empty result is a real absence, not a broken instrument.\n  (d) `npm run gen:tool-delivery -- --report` -> GUIDANCE_LOSS ... toolsLeftProseless=0; GUIDANCE_DELIVERED compactTools=63 composedAmongCompact=0 tier=summary proseBytes=5489.\n\nP-011 as authored says: \"run npm --prefix apps/operator run llm-test against a session wired to COMPACT-tier definitions and record pass/fail per scenario\". Per (a)+(b)+(c) it does not do that: the su target's Anthropic `tools` array is built from SU_CATALOG, a HAND-AUTHORED constant in su-catalog.ts (see the literal entries for agent_tools:list / tools:find / tools:invoke at 525-548).\n\nCONSEQUENCE: a green `llm-test --target su` run says NOTHING about whether the compact/summary projection confuses a model, because that harness never delivers the projection. Recording it as P-011 evidence would be a VACUOUS GREEN -- the failure class the repo guide names (an instrument that measured none of the space, whose clean result is indistinguishable from a real pass). D-008 is a SHIP BLOCKER, so satisfying it that way would ship the plan on evidence that cannot fail.\n\nRULING -- P-011 is satisfied only by evidence that touches the delivered tier:\n1. STRUCTURAL (strongest, already in hand): compact-schema-catalog.test.ts proves that for EVERY tool in the live catalog the compact projection preserves the callable contract -- required set, type, enum/const, bounds, oneOf/anyOf, $defs. A proof over the whole population, not a sample: any argument object valid under COMPACT is valid under FULL. This retires the 'can a caller still form a VALID call' half of D-008.\n2. RESIDUAL RISK structure cannot cover: prose guides tool SELECTION and field VALUES, not shape. D-011 mitigates it -- COMPACT ships a capped summary plus every hard rail, and per (d) toolsLeftProseless=0, so no shipping tool is prose-free.\n3. BEHAVIOURAL: any real-model probe MUST be fed the actual resolved compact-tier definitions. `buildCatalog`'s `entries` parameter (a) is the existing seam; do NOT fork a parallel harness.\n4. PRODUCTION TELEMETRY: pre-change invalid_input/invalid_args baseline captured = 889,080 calls / 4,320 invalid = 0.4859% over 7d (workspace papercusp-workspace, invoked_at >= now()-7d -- the column is invoked_at, NOT created_at). Post-deploy comparison against it is the durable regression detector.\n\nDo NOT record a bare `llm-test --target su` pass as P-011 evidence.\n\n### D-013 — A spec-adequacy refusal from :3070 is BUILD-SCOPED evidence, not a cause — re-evaluate against :3170 before believing its attribution\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22. Measured, not inferred.\n\nAgent MCP calls execute against :3070, the RELEASE checkout. On 2026-09-22T02:34Z :3070 served sha=91a5dba579, whose spec-test-adequacy.ts blob is ef98dabbc46f281485b8f06f031a92261e625677 and contains ZERO occurrences of `executableEvidenceGaps` and `mutationInCohortNotExecutable`. The working tree, `staging` and `main` all carry blob a0ba2531161dd0260beb5f090c64d06f792d6a97, where both symbols are present (2 and 6). Extraction positive-control passed (71,905 bytes extracted), so the zeros are genuine absence and not a broken instrument.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: the deployed evaluator predates the EI-23756870948948211 population-split fix. That fix's own in-code comment records that the previous version asserted ONE untested cause — \"outside the current grading cohort\" — when the far more common real case was a row sitting INSIDE the cohort failing isSuccessfulExecutableEvidence. So :3070 emits a confidently-worded but WRONG cause. Re-evaluated against :3170 (sha=8be0640bd0, verified to carry the fix before use), the SAME payload produced a materially different verdict: falsifiability PASSED and two entirely different criteria (oracle-independence, execution-integrity) surfaced.\n\nRULING for every lane on this plan: do NOT take a :3070 spec-adequacy refusal's named cause as fact. Verify the deployed build carries the relevant evaluator code (blob/symbol check against the judged sha), and re-run the identical payload through `node scripts/mcp-call.mjs <verb> --json-file <args> --client <su-id> --port 3170` before acting on the attribution. This is the documented A/B (\"a deployed refusal can be stale while staging accepts the same request\"); it is stricter, not weaker, so it is not gate-evasion.\n\nSECOND RULING: the prefix \"evaluator capability unavailable on build sha=X\" remains the known MISLABEL for missing/insufficient evidence (EI-23894975926884293) and is NOT a deploy or capability outage — it appeared byte-identically on two different builds. Do not re-open that hunt. The genuinely build-scoped part is the CAUSE NAMED AFTER it, which is what this decision governs.\n\nRETRACTED BY THIS DECISION: the prior working claim on this plan that AUTO-BAR-R-3-P-010@3 was blocked on missing `evidenceKind:'mutation'` evidence requiring scripts/mutation-probe.sh. The clause revision itself records mutation_required=false, required_evidence=['tree'], required_test_layers=[]; and the evaluator passes falsifiability on a qualifying COUNTEREXAMPLE. Running that probe would have mutated shared source under a lock, racing git-sync, to produce evidence the clause never required.\n\n### D-014 — D-008's comprehension gate FIRED: the COMPACT tier measures a pass-rate drop, so the plan CANNOT ship on byte evidence alone\nDate: 2026-09-22\nDate: 2026-09-22. MEASURED, not inferred. The P-011 A/B ran all 45 su llm-test scenarios twice against the SAME harness, varying ONE knob (toolDefinitionTier: 'full' vs 'compact') via the su-compact-catalog projection built for D-012. Logs /tmp/p011-ab-{full,compact}.log, summary /tmp/p011-ab-summary.txt, driver .papercusp/scratch/run-p011-ab.sh.\n\nRESULT\n  control (FULL definitions):  40 passed / 5 failed / 0 errored\n  compact (COMPACT definitions): 33 passed / 10 failed / 2 errored\n\nSix scenarios regressed pass -> fail: su-S08-compact-read, su-S16-code-run-batch-write, su-S20-overview-not-for-single (x2 runs), su-S33-agenda-achieved, su-S33-agenda-delegate. One (su-S28-ideate-pass-closes-loop) went failed -> errored.\n\nTHE TWO 'errored' RUNS ARE NOT COMPREHENSION FAILURES AND MUST NOT BE COUNTED AS SUCH. Both are self-labelled by the harness as infrastructure: one produced `cost=$0.0000 turns=0` with `judge[meta]: the system under test produced no usable output (no turns were produced). This is an environment/SUT-health failure, not an operator behavioral finding` (consistent with the account-capacity shed broadcast during the run); the other is `judge[meta]: the external judge did not complete (judgeRun ... did not complete within 120000ms)`, explicitly `an evaluation-infrastructure failure, not an operator behavioral finding`. Excluding both, the evaluable comparison is 40/45 = 88.9% control vs 33/43 = 76.7% compact.\n\nONE FAILURE IS DIRECTLY THE PREDICTED FAILURE MODE, and it appears ONLY in the compact arm: `judge[conventionAdherence]: improvements:capture was invoked with a top-level 'lens' field rather than the required nested ideation:{ lens } structure`. That is a malformed CALL caused by a lost nesting contract - precisely what D-008 was written to catch and precisely what a byte measurement cannot see.\n\nRULING. AUTO-BAR-R-6-P-011 requires that an llm-test run against COMPACT-tier definitions PASSES PER SCENARIO. It does not. Under D-008 a comprehension regression blocks ship regardless of byte savings, so this plan CANNOT be marked shipped on the strength of its (substantial, real) byte results: wire 1,599,477 -> 649,761 B (-59.4%) and guidance 334,797 -> 81,030 B (-75.8%), all 61 Aug-20 baseline names kept with 2 added inside the 100,000 B budget. The savings are not in doubt; their behavioural cost is.\n\nWHAT THIS DECISION DOES NOT YET ESTABLISH. n=1 per scenario with LLM judges is noisy, and the control arm itself failed 5 runs across 3 scenarios, none of which are the six that regressed - a pattern as consistent with run-to-run variance as with a systematic effect. So this records a BLOCK, not a root cause. The next step is replication of the regressed subset in both arms; a confirmed regression then needs the cause localised to the schema half (compactInputSchema) or the prose half (summaryGuidanceDescription), because D-011 already measured those separately and they are independently tunable (the SUMMARY_CAP_SWEEP shows cap=100 fits at 99,996 B while cap=120 overruns, so there is real headroom to trade).\n\nDo NOT read the byte results as invalidated, and do NOT re-run the baseline: it was captured before the tier change went live, which is the only thing that makes it a baseline.\n\n### D-015 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-22\nAmendment-Id: 12003dad5adece37a1779a1120400eadf1fa07afcf97fd1d17ce0f98d8543125\nRequest-Hash: d4830a6b92b612f7e1a9a2c77ff35493cfc68209b9f7c5343ac4a99269b8f378\nActor: su-77b3a99d-e271-43fc-9ab1-7daf214767b8\nReason: Bind the verification contract (structured check + concrete falsifiers + proof depth) to all 7 bars. I am rejecting it, for three reasons:\n1. **Nothing is gained.** The compact tier is ALREADY LIVE (D-018). \"Plan shipped\" is a paperwork state here, not a product state. Weakening my own acceptance bar would buy a status flag and cost the only durable pressure on an unvalidated live configuration.\n2. **The author weakening their own gate to pass it is the smell the whole two-family evidence design exists to prevent.** I authored the bar, I own the plan, and I would be the one relaxing it immediately before requesting independent grading. Even with sound reasoning, that is the move a grader should refuse, so I should not make it.\n3. **The obligation is dated and owned.** WI-10002398 carries the 2026-09-29 discharge with three named outcomes: bar satisfied, an owner decision to HOLD recorded, or the config REVERTED via PAPERCUSP_CLAUDE_FULL_SEED=1 (a path already covered by a committed test). A blocked ship gate is a WEAKER consequence than that item, not a stronger one — so blocking costs nothing that the obligation was not already carrying.\n\n#### WHAT THIS MEANS CONCRETELY\nThe plan does NOT ship today, and that is the correct outcome rather than a failure. R-6 clears when the incident obligation is discharged: complete the shipping-seed A/B to a rung-verified result and bind it with coverageRungs.l3, or record an owner HOLD, or revert. Every OTHER bar is now proven or about to be — 17 of 19 adequacy specs pass, and R-9 clears as soon as the spec-test-adequacy fix (EI-23958122348412546) deploys.\n\n#### THE GENERALISABLE FINDING, worth more than this plan\nAn \"incident obligation\" and a \"ship gate\" are DIFFERENT instruments with OPPOSITE failure modes — a ship gate makes inaction safe, an incident obligation makes inaction unsafe — and the bar contract can only express the first. Authoring the second INSIDE the first silently converts it back into the first. If incident obligations are worth having as a class, they need their own surface (a dated obligation that does NOT block ship but escalates on expiry), not prose inside a mandatory bar. Two SEMANTICALLY IDENTICAL tools swept over N duplicated sub-schemas — one using `$defs`+`$ref`, one fully inlined.\n\n      N | byte sav% | tok sav%\n    ----+-----------+---------\n      1 |     -6.9% |    -2.8%\n      2 |     38.3% |    16.2%\n      4 |     62.6% |    37.0%\n      8 |     75.2% |    55.2%\n     16 |     81.5% |    68.2%\n\nMarginal cost per additional duplicate: **30.0 tok/dup referenced vs 207.0 tok/dup inlined (ratio 0.145)**.\n\n#### WHY A SWEEP AND NOT A SINGLE N\nA single N cannot separate the hypotheses — any one gap is explicable as a tokenizer artifact. Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Broad evidence sample.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Audit a larger stratified sample of review and grading records across independent acceptance grading, author-acceptance cards, rubric vetting, grading-integrity reviews, and ordinary code reviews.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"The audit must measure usefulness by review type rather than infer it from aggregate counts.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\"Record exclusions and coverage limits.\"]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A reproducible live report contains the defined strata, sample frame, exclusions, and coverage limits for all five review types.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any required stratum, exclusion, or coverage limit is absent or cannot be re-run from the recorded report.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\"independent acceptance grading\", \"author-acceptance cards\", \"rubric vetting\", \"grading-integrity reviews\", \"ordinary code reviews\"],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"live\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"manual\"],\n    \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read the published audit report and re-run its canonical census and bounded sample queries against the live Papercusp stores.\",\n    \"check\": {\"kind\": \"instrument\", \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"},\n    \"replication\": \"Open report rpt_fa10ea78-fa47-42b8-9b14-12464897c4fb, replay its census and sample queries, and compare stratum membership, exclusions, and limits.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-002 — Usefulness classification.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Classify sampled records as substantive catch, useful confirmation, ceremony/redundancy, stale or invalidated, or inconclusive with explicit numerator and denominator definitions.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"A usefulness decision is only auditable when each category has a stated denominator.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\"Compute rates separately for each review stratum.\"]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The live audit report assigns every sampled record exactly one usefulness class and publishes per-stratum numerators, denominators, and rates.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A sampled record is unclassified, multiply classified, or a reported rate lacks an explicit numerator or denominator.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\"sampled records\", \"per-stratum rates\"],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"live\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"manual\"],\n    \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Re-read the report's classification table and recompute each per-stratum rate from its recorded numerator and denominator.\",\n    \"check\": {\"kind\": \"instrument\", \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"},\n    \"replication\": \"Replay the report's classification query, count each category by stratum, and compare the recomputed rates with the published values.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-003 — Outcome traceability.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Trace each sampled rating through rubric criterion and revision, evidence, remediation or disregard, linked work item, completion, and available tree or code evidence.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"A rating is useful only when its claimed outcome can be followed to an owned disposition and verified impact.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\"Separate rubric linkage from verified implementation impact.\"]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Every traced sample has a criterion and revision, evidence reference, disposition status, linked work item where applicable, completion status, and an explicit implementation-impact verdict.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any traced sample stops before disposition or conflates rubric linkage with verified implementation impact.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\"criterion and revision\", \"evidence\", \"remediation/disregard\", \"linked work item\", \"completion\", \"tree/code evidence\"],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"live\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"manual\"],\n    \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Follow representative scorecards through the canonical scorecard, work-item, completion, and tree evidence readers.\",\n    \"check\": {\"kind\": \"instrument\", \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"},\n    \"replication\": \"Select the report's representative samples, read each cited scorecard and linked work item, and record where the chain ends or is verified.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-004 — Ceremony reduction without disabling grading.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Keep review and grading enabled for every plan while identifying the smallest changes that remove duplicate, stale, or decision-neutral ceremony.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"The measured problem is low-value ceremony, not the existence of grading.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\"Do not disable grading or mutate global pipeline policy.\"]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The tree contains passing regression coverage for poor-rating disposition, grading-integrity settlement, and current-revision acceptance authority, and the report states that grading remains enabled.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any guardrail test fails, or the proposed change disables grading or changes global pipeline policy.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\"poor-rating disposition\", \"grading-integrity settlement\", \"current-revision acceptance authority\"],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"unit\"],\n    \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the focused Vitest guard suite and inspect the canonical scorecard and acceptance writers for always-on grading and no global-policy mutation.\",\n    \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/observation-types.test.ts\", \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scorecards/emit.grading-audit.test.ts\", \"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-grading-authority.test.ts\"]},\n    \"replication\": \"Run npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/observation-types.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scorecards/emit.grading-audit.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-grading-authority.test.ts and inspect the scorecard emit and acceptance authority sources.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-005 — Durable measurement and rollout.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Define recurrence guards, rollout stages, and a post-change measurement window for useful-finding rate, repeated grades, stale invalidations, unlinked poor ratings, tool calls, and elapsed or tool time.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"The change is only useful if it reduces ceremony without reducing substantive findings.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\"Record the measurement window and keep pipeline policy unchanged.\"]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A live measurement plan names the pre/post windows, all required metrics, rollout stages, and recurrence guards with owners.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any required metric, window, rollout stage, recurrence guard, or owner is missing.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\"useful-finding rate\", \"repeated grades\", \"stale invalidations\", \"unlinked poor ratings\", \"tool calls\", \"elapsed/tool time\"],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"live\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"manual\"],\n    \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read the recorded measurement window and rerun its metric queries at the end of the window.\",\n    \"check\": {\"kind\": \"instrument\", \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"},\n    \"replication\": \"Record the start watermark, execute the post-change window queries at close, and compare every metric with the baseline using the same denominators.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Findings\n\nThe expanded read-only audit used the canonical scorecard/work-item stores and a stratified 80-row acceptance sample, with targeted strata for poor cards with and without dispositions, clean cards, superseding/retracted cards, and author-acceptance cards. It did not mutate the review pipeline.\n\n- The broad scorecard census from 2026-06-01 onward contains 5,803 rubric scorecards: 602 acceptance-named, 1,661 grading-integrity, and 3,540 other rubric families. The acceptance per-rating analysis contains 593 cards because nine acceptance-named rows have no usable ratings map.\n- In the 593-card acceptance analysis, 161 cards contain at least one poor rating; those cards contain 311 poor rating rows. A targeted sample confirmed both real catches and ceremony patterns: some poor ratings name concrete remediation or disregard, while many otherwise complete-looking cards do not.\n- Only 15 of the 161 poor acceptance cards carry a per-rating remediation/disregard field. Thirty-seven have an author-acceptance verdict; 124 are independent poor cards. One hundred fourteen poor cards have neither a rating-level disposition nor an author verdict. This is the clearest effectiveness gap.\n- Coord links do not solve this by themselves: the sampled poor cards commonly have topic/tag links, but those links do not prove that a remediation work item exists, was completed, or changed the relevant code/outcome.\n- The grading-integrity family is different: it has 1,662 cards and 532 poor cards, but rating-level remediation/disregard is intentionally not the right disposition mechanism for that family; its structural audit stamp and re-grade flow are the relevant controls.\n- The audit confirmed useful review cases already present in the earlier census (Learning-tab, gateway-kernel, capless-governor) and found repeated/superseding cards, author-accepted poor outcomes, and stale/revision-sensitive records that can create ceremony. The current telemetry still cannot prove a code diff caused a particular rubric outcome for every card.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | P-001 | live |\n| R-002 | P-002 | live |\n| R-003 | P-003 | live |\n| R-004 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-005 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Audit\n\n- **P-001** `done` Build the population and stratified sample, with separate strata for independent acceptance grades, author-acceptance cards, rubric vetting, grading-integrity reviews, and ordinary code reviews. Record exclusions and coverage limits. — note: ← WI-10002183 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Inspect the sampled records and classify usefulness, ceremony, staleness, invalidation, and inconclusive evidence using a written rubric. Compute per-stratum rates. — note: ← WI-10002194 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Trace sampled outcomes from rubric criterion and revision through evidence, remediation/disregard, linked work items, completion, and available tree/code evidence. Separate rubric linkage from verified implementation impact. — note: ← WI-10002195 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Improvement design\n\n- **P-004** `done` Draft the smallest implementation changes that preserve grading for every plan while reducing duplicate/re-stale ceremony, making contract/revision identity visible, and surfacing remediation/disregard at grading time. — note: ← WI-10002187 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Define regression tests, ledger guards, rollout stages, and a post-change measurement window. Record the draft plan and audit report for owner review; do not mutate pipeline policy in this plan. — note: ← WI-10002188 completed (done)\n\n## Proposed guardrails\n\n1. Keep independent grading and rubric vetting enabled for every plan.\n2. Add an acceptance-specific poor-rating disposition gate: each poor outcome must name a remediation work item or an explicit disregard rationale. An author-acceptance verdict alone should not erase an unaddressed poor outcome.\n3. Make the tuple `plan revision + rubric revision + criteria hash + evidence fingerprint` the one current grade. A new card should supersede the old one only when evidence or contract meaning changed.\n4. Freeze the plan/rubric contract while grading. If it changes, invalidate the in-flight grade once and re-route to one fresh grade, rather than allowing repeated ceremony.\n5. Emit a compact classification record for each completed review: substantive catch, useful confirmation, ceremony/redundant, stale/invalidated, or inconclusive.\n6. Measure useful-finding rate, poor-outcome disposition rate, repeated/superseding grade rate, stale invalidation rate, acceptance calls, tool time, and end-to-end delay before and after rollout.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- The audit report includes population, sample frame, classification rubric, rates by review type, evidence coverage, and limitations.\n- Every proposed improvement maps to an observed failure mode and a recurrence guard.\n- The plan remains ready for owner review; no implementation begins until approved.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10002183 — Build the population and stratified sample, with separate strata for independent acceptance grades, author-acceptance cards, rubric vetting, grading-integrity reviews, and ordinary code reviews. Reco… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002194 — Inspect the sampled records and classify usefulness, ceremony, staleness, invalidation, and inconclusive evidence using a written rubric. Compute per-stratum rates. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002195 — Trace sampled outcomes from rubric criterion and revision through evidence, remediation/disregard, linked work items, completion, and available tree/code evidence. Separate rubric linkage from verifi… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002187 — Draft the smallest implementation changes that preserve grading for every plan while reducing duplicate/re-stale ceremony, making contract/revision identity visible, and surfacing remediation/disrega… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002188 — Define regression tests, ledger guards, rollout stages, and a post-change measurement window. Record the draft plan and audit report for owner review; do not mutate pipeline policy in this plan. <!-- P-005 -->\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-21\nAmendment-Id: wi-10002182-bar-contract-repair-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: d4a13b5e7c30c5714196e599ec4bd4d8a2a70236b7e4ac4da5231e665c498e83\nActor: su-0e3c7f17-8bc8-473d-899f-8271d393a565\nReason: Apply independently approved acceptance BAR contract with explicit method, structured check, replication proof, evidence plane, and grading fields.\nApproved-By: su-bb42b259-63f0-4824-9af4-2ff1ac60acca\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:815671\nApproved-At: 2026-09-21T16:21:39.898Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 14 → 15\nChanged BARs: R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004, R-005\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — Independent acceptance rejected on degraded BAR evidence\nDate: 2026-09-21\nDate: 2026-09-21\nDecision: The author acceptance verdict is REJECT for the current independent grade. Independent card EI-23891057698252715 (rubric rev2, plan rev15) rates all five BARs degraded (score10=5); grading-integrity audit EI-23890203007055294 and meta attestation EI-23889903543509546 are current/passed. Author verdict card EI-23892225418061097 adopts the independent ratings and records the concrete residue: fresh bounded replication, complete per-row usefulness classification and outcome traceability, current source/test fingerprints, and named post-change measurement values/thresholds. Ship readiness remains false; do not call plans:set-plan-status shipped until fresh evidence is bound and a later independent grade supports acceptance.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR evidence must be evidenceKind='test'; manual report bindings can never reach currentness=current\nDate: 2026-09-22\nROOT CAUSE of the three stuck BARs — evidence KIND, not evidence quality.\n\nComplete binding census (harness_shared.spec_evidence_bindings, 27 rows, sums exactly):\n| spec | kind | n | testRunId | newest | currentness |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| R-001 | manual | 5 | 0 | 8021 | unknown |\n| R-001 | coverage-census | 2 | 0 | 8007 | unknown |\n| R-002 | manual | 7 | 0 | 8022 | unknown |\n| R-003 | manual | 7 | 0 | 8023 | unknown |\n| R-004 | test | 2 | 0 | 7997 | **current** |\n| R-005 | test | 2 | 0 | 7998 | **current** |\n| R-005 | manual | 1 | 0 | 8024 | unknown |\n| R-005 | operational | 1 | 0 | 8010 | unknown |\n5+2+7+7+2+2+1+1 = 27 (reconciles to the full binding population)\n\nTHE DISCRIMINATOR IS evidenceKind. Every binding reading currentness.overall='current' is evidenceKind='test' (7997, 7998). Every 'manual'/'coverage-census'/'operational' binding reads 'unknown', because its sourceFingerprint is 'report:rpt_<uuid>' — a published prose report the currentness resolver cannot check against the tree — so dimensions.source='unknown' and overall degrades to 'unknown'.\nNOT the discriminator: test_run_id is NULL on ALL 27 rows, including the two current ones.\n\nCONSEQUENCE: R-001, R-002 and R-003 have SEVEN bindings each and ZERO test-kind bindings. Those three criteria could not be rated healthy no matter how good the underlying analysis was. su-0e3c7f17 re-bound the same three criteria 21 times (ids 8003..8023), each landing 'unknown' with staleReasons EMPTY, so nothing told it why — then died polling scorecards:list for a verdict that could not move.\n\nR-004 and R-005 are already satisfied on this axis (current test bindings 7997/7998).\n\nFIX: R-001/R-002/R-003 need committed TESTS asserting their invariants, bound evidenceKind='test' — not another report.\n\nEVIDENCE: harness_shared.spec_evidence_bindings GROUP BY spec_id, evidence_kind WHERE plan_slug='review-grading-effectiveness-improvement-2026-09-21'; plans:get-spec-evidence showing currentness.dimensions.source='unknown' with staleReasons=[] on 8021/8022/8023/8024.\n\n### D-004 — CORRECTS D-003 — BAR evidence currentness turns on RECOMPUTABLE tree-anchored fingerprints, not evidenceKind\nDate: 2026-09-22\nCORRECTION OF D-003 — the discriminator is RECOMPUTABILITY, not evidenceKind.\n\nD-003 claimed \"evidenceKind='test' is the sole discriminator for currentness='current'\". That is WRONG and I am retracting it before anyone acts on it. Falsifying evidence: bindings 7995 (R-004) and 7996 (R-005) are evidenceKind='test', naming the SAME three test files as 7997/7998, and they still read currentness='unknown'. Kind=test is necessary-looking but not sufficient.\n\nTHE ACTUAL MECHANISM, read from the source (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-evidence-store.ts):\n\n  function compareFingerprint(stored, current) {\n    if (stored === null) return 'not-applicable';\n    if (current == null) return 'unknown';        // <-- this branch\n    return stored === current ? 'current' : 'stale';\n  }\n  overall = staleReasons.length ? 'stale' : guardedUnknownReasons.length ? 'unknown' : 'current'\n\n'unknown' does NOT mean \"the evidence is poor\". It means THE READER COULD NOT RECOMPUTE A CURRENT FINGERPRINT TO COMPARE THE STORED ONE AGAINST. The stored side is fine; the current side is null.\n\nA current fingerprint is only recomputable when the binding is anchored to something the system can re-measure from the live tree:\n  - fingerprintRepoFileSet(repoRoot, declaredPaths) -> 'sha256-file-set-v1:<digest>' — hashes REAL repo file paths (rejects non-files, paths outside root, escaping symlinks)\n  - the work-item-set path -> 'sha256-work-item-set-v1:<digest>'\n\nObserved, consistent with exactly that:\n  - 7997/7998: source AND test fingerprints both 'sha256-file-set-v1:...' -> recomputable -> current\n  - 7995/7996: source is a BARE hex (no scheme prefix), test_fingerprint NULL -> not recomputable -> unknown\n  - every manual/coverage-census/operational binding on R-001/R-002/R-003: source_fingerprint = 'report:rpt_<uuid>' -> nothing to recompute -> unknown\n\nWHY THE CORRECTION MATTERS PRACTICALLY: acting on D-003 as written, an agent would author tests, bind them evidenceKind='test' with hand-supplied fingerprints, and land ANOTHER 'unknown' — reproducing 7995/7996 exactly. The rule to follow is: bind evidence whose evidence_ref names REAL TREE FILE PATHS and let the measurement path compute both fingerprints. Never hand-author a fingerprint value.\n\nALSO NOTE: test_run_id is NULL on all four of 7995-7998, including the two current ones, so a missing testRunId is not implicated either way.\n\n[self-imposed] Measured 2026-09-22 by reading the resolver source plus the four binding rows. Supersedes D-003's discriminator claim; D-003's binding CENSUS (27 rows, the per-spec table) remains accurate and is not retracted.\n\n### D-005 — Evidence currentness turns on a stored re-measurable measurement — retracting D-003 and correcting D-004\nDate: 2026-09-22\nMEASURED CORRECTION. D-003 (\"evidenceKind='test' is the sole discriminator for currentness=current\") is RETRACTED as false, and D-004's supporting claim is corrected. Anyone acting on either would rejoin the loop that consumed su-0e3c7f17.\n\nFALSIFIERS (plans:get-spec-evidence, 2026-09-22): bindings 7995/7996 are evidenceKind='test' and read UNKNOWN. Binding 7997 is evidenceKind='test' AND server-measured, and reads STALE. So kind predicts nothing. Across all 27 live bindings on this plan: 24 unknown, 3 stale, ZERO current. The carry-note claim that \"R-004/R-005 already have current bindings (7997/7998) and need nothing\" was therefore FALSE — they are stale, not current.\n\nTHE ACTUAL DISCRIMINATOR is whether the binding stored a re-measurable `details.currentMeasurement` (schemaVersion 1, kind 'repo-files', repo-relative sourcePaths/testPaths). With one, the server re-hashes those files at read time (fingerprintRepoFileSet -> sha256-file-set-v1, spec-evidence-store.ts) and returns current|stale with provenance='server-measured'. Without one it returns unknown, unknownReasons=['source-current-fingerprint-not-supplied'], provenance='not-supplied'. A hand-written sourceFingerprint STRING in sha256-file-set-v1 shape does NOT make a binding measurable — 7997 carries one and is still judged by re-measurement, not by the string.\n\nOPERATIVE RULE: never hand-author a fingerprint value and never bind a prose report ref (report:rpt_<uuid> cannot be recomputed). Pass `measurement` and let the server hash the tree.\n\nCHURN COROLLARY (new, and the reason 7997 went stale within hours): a measurement anchored to a high-churn implementation file yields a permanently-stale reading that a grader cannot distinguish from weak evidence. Measured over 7 days in this tree: rubrics.ts 7 commits (last 06:00Z today), emit.ts 5, acceptance-grading-authority.ts 0; the corresponding test files 2, 0, 1. Anchor on the low-churn artifact that PINS the contract (the test, and the writer the method was derived from) and treat staleness on a genuinely-churning subject as a true re-verify signal, not noise. Do not silently drop a real subject file from a measurement just to obtain a prettier reading.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-bash-substitution-reachable-ceiling-2026-08-01","title":"Acceptance — bash substitution reachable ceiling: corrected denominator, published ceiling, cheap compliance, honest adoption verdict","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-22","owner":"su-e8f7f7d3-8970-4e90-a6de-7551587b1559","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance — bash substitution reachable ceiling: corrected denominator, published ceiling, cheap compliance, honest adoption verdict\nslug: acceptance-bash-substitution-reachable-ceiling-2026-08-01\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-22\nupdated: 2026-09-22\nowner: su-e8f7f7d3-8970-4e90-a6de-7551587b1559\n---\n\n# Acceptance — bash substitution reachable ceiling: corrected denominator, published ceiling, cheap compliance, honest adoption verdict\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"agent-throughput-waste-reduction-2026-09-23","title":"Cut agent wall-clock and moot work without weakening any gate: supersede cascade, early BAR drift, reliable wakes, how-to handoff","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cut agent wall-clock and moot work without weakening any gate: supersede cascade, early BAR drift, reliable wakes, how-to handoff\nslug: agent-throughput-waste-reduction-2026-09-23\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-23\nupdated: 2026-09-23\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-23. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\nDraft. Written from the WI-10002598 audit of ship-main-greening-program-2026-09-15 (09-15 to 09-23) and of su-e3d58938's three carry epochs.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: P-001 (supersede cascade), the largest measured waste.)\n\n## Why (measured 2026-09-23, harness_shared.tool_invocations + session_turn_parts)\nThe ship-main-greening program has taken 8 days. 13 agents made 11,854 MCP calls under program goal_refs, over 111 distinct active hours. Native Edit/Read/Bash (~60% of tool use) is not in this ledger, so these counts are floors.\n\n1. **Moot work, about 29% of program calls.** Three items were eventually dropped: P-022 (1,840 calls), P-012 (984) and P-021 (650). The owner-approved D-019 had superseded their subject plans on 09-19. P-022 still drew 1,840 calls on 09-21 and 09-22, before D-040/D-041 noticed on 09-22. Nothing flags a carrier item when its subject plan is superseded.\n2. **Acceptance drift surfaced at ship time, 4 days late.** R-1 required ten plans shipped; D-019 made that impossible on 09-19, but it surfaced only at the 09-23 ship attempt. D-026 (09-22) re-worded R-1 and kept the impossible clause. There were 106 rubrics:amend calls, the rubric is at rev 12, and some amendments invalidated evidence already collected (D-007).\n3. **Dark holders.** Across the 13 agents: 78 h active, 52 h in 232 short idle gaps, 222 h in stretches over an hour. On 09-23 the program leader went dark twice in an hour. Its cold-loop fires parked with 'no injectable psu host' although loop:arm had reported rewakeGuaranteed:true (EI-24023838400909760), so another agent had to backstop it. P-031 changed hands 5+ times.\n4. **No-op wakes.** In su-e3d58938's chain (4h15m: about 106 min active, 153 min idle), 3 of 7 inbox-wake turns had nothing to act on: an auto-resolved alert for an item it had closed, a todo->todo plan event, and a message already handled.\n5. **Rediscovery at handoff.** tools:find was called 415 times. The prior WI-10002581 holder concluded 'no BAR amendment verb exists' after 3 tools:find calls, although this same program had used rubrics:amend in D-024/D-025/D-026.\n6. **Carry ceremony and failed calls.** Coordination/carry was 24% of calls: loop:checkpoint 486 and work_items:checkpoint 395, which duplicate each other; coord:send 651; session:request-compaction 122; coord:orient 131 (15 min of tool time). There were 1,016 failed calls (8.6%): invalid_input 322, handler_error 297, checkpoint_merge_would_evict_rows 94, authorization_denied 46, and 29+ SQL column guesses.\n\n## Is the time useful?\nPartly. Useful: the gate-lane fixes (P-031), the completed ships, and integrity findings. D-049, for example, found an undisclosed force-deploy. Not useful: items 1, 3, 4 and 5 above, plus the retry share of item 6. Together that is roughly a third of calls and most of the idle wall-clock.\n\n## Non-negotiables\nNo gate is removed or weakened: acceptance BARs, independent grading, outside-lineage amendment approval, locks, the single-fixer gate rule and provenance all stay. Every item only adds early detection or removes waste, and ships a Vitest guard in the owning package.\n\n## Phase 1 — Stop moot work early\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Supersede cascade: when a plan is superseded or consolidated (plans:set-plan-status superseded, or a consolidation Decision), find every non-terminal item in other plans whose deliverable is shipping or accepting that plan (a \"Ship <slug>\" carrier). Park it out of claim_next with a pointer to the superseding decision, notify its holder, and raise a repair obligation on the carrier plan. Guard (Vitest): superseding plan X parks a todo/wip item in plan Y that carries X, and leaves unrelated items claimable. Baseline: P-022 drew 1,840 calls after D-019 made it moot. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n- **P-002** `dropped` Early BAR drift: re-evaluate acceptance-BAR contract readiness whenever a Decision is added, an item is dropped or superseded, or a plan named in a BAR model changes status, not only at ship. Surface the blocking codes (mapping_dropped_only, BAR models naming superseded plans) in the plan Now/orient and on the carrier item. Reuse acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot; no second evaluator. Guard: dropping the last live carrier of a BAR yields mapping_dropped_only in live readiness on the same write. Baseline: R-1 impossible from 09-19 but found 09-23. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Keep holders awake and informed\n\n- **P-003** `dropped` Reliable wakes: a cold-loop fire that parks with \"no injectable psu host\" falls back to the inbox-wake injection path that reaches the session. loop:arm and loop:checkpoint stop reporting rewakeGuaranteed:true when the owner's last fire parked. Tracks EI-24023838400909760 and EI-21431587306904888. Guard: a fixture whose last fire parked gets rewakeGuaranteed:false plus a fallback delivery. Baseline: program leader dark twice in one hour on 09-23, needing a backstop agent. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n- **P-004** `dropped` No-op wake suppression: an inbox-wake the recipient cannot act on is delivered to the inbox without starting a turn. Covers an auto-resolved alert for an item the recipient itself closed, a plan event with no state change (todo->todo), and a message already read. Anything directed with expects action/answer, and every owner directive, still wakes. Guard: the three observed shapes are suppressed and directed asks still wake. Baseline: 3 of 7 inbox-wake turns in su-e3d58938 were no-ops. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n- **P-005** `dropped` How-to handoff: when a work item changes holder, the prior-attempt brief lists the mutating verbs that succeeded on the item's plan, from tool_invocations and plan Decisions (for example, rubrics:amend was used in D-024/D-025/D-026). Extend the existing priorAttemptBrief; no new surface. Guard: the brief for a released item on a plan with a prior rubrics:amend names it. Baseline: the prior WI-10002581 holder concluded no amendment verb existed; tools:find was called 415 times. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Route overlaps and measure\n\n- **P-006** `dropped` Route the overlaps to coordination-metadata-friction-reduction-2026-09-07 instead of duplicating them. Carry-ceremony duplication (loop:checkpoint 486 plus work_items:checkpoint 395) goes to its P-005; the failed-call classes (invalid_input 322, handler_error 297, checkpoint_merge_would_evict_rows 94, SQL column guesses 29+) go to its P-006. Attach the WI-10002598 evidence there and get both items a live holder or a recorded disposition. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n- **P-007** `dropped` Plan efficiency read: one call returning, per plan, calls by activity category, effort on items that ended dropped, active vs idle wall-clock of its holders, failed calls by class, and holder changes. Extend plans:get mode:'meta' or register a state cell; no bespoke tool. Guard: a fixture plan returns category counts matching the tool_invocations rows it was seeded with. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n- **P-008** `dropped` Before/after proof: run the P-007 read on the next two plans that ship after P-001 to P-005 land, compare against the WI-10002598 baseline (moot share, failed-call share, dark-holder stalls, no-op wakes), and re-run the acceptance-gate regression fixtures to show no refusal was weakened. Report to Avi with numbers. importance: high — note: Moved to review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (D-004): P-001->P-030, P-002->P-031, P-003->P-033, P-004->P-034, P-005->P-035, P-007+P-008->P-032; P-006 is covered by its P-017/P-022/P-025.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — CORRECTION: 106 was rubrics:amend CALLS, not amendments; and overlap map with review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23. Recorded by su-e3d58938.\n\nRETRACTION. My 04:34Z report to Avi said the criteria were 'reworded 106 times'. That is wrong. Measured (tool_invocations, goal_ref in program items): 106 rubrics:amend CALLS, of which 16 applied amendments across 6 rubrics (7 on acceptance-ship-main-greening-program-2026-09-15), 66 dryRun previews, and 44 failed (41%). The 'Why' figure '106 rubrics:amend calls' stands as calls only. The same number in review-system-rework-reduction's report (106 amendments across 57 plans fleet-wide in 7 days) is a different population, so the match is a coincidence.\n\nOVERLAP with review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23 (26 items, independently corroborated by su-ae3c4989, directives #247/#254):\n- Not covered there, kept here: P-001 supersede cascade; P-002 BAR meaning drift after owner scope decisions (their P-003/P-004 cover incompleteness at seeding and vetting order, not later drift); P-005 how-to handoff; P-007 per-plan efficiency read.\n- Same subsystem, design together: P-003 here (cold-loop fire parks and the session goes dark, with a false rewakeGuaranteed) vs their P-013 (wake storms to dead sessions) and P-024 (loops firing while parked on an owner await). P-004 here (no-op wakes) vs their P-012/P-021 (status-reporter volume) and P-026 (wake text truncation).\n- P-006 here is RE-TARGETED. Failed-call classes go to their P-017/P-022 (measured per-tool failure rate; all invalid fields named in one refusal). Carry duplication goes to their P-025 (loop:checkpoint partial update). Both are live; coordination-metadata-friction-reduction-2026-09-07 has been idle for 14 days.\n- Adopted from theirs for WI-10002581 now: amend -> vet -> bind -> grade (their P-004). Expect recruitment starvation (their P-014) and silent consults (their P-015: 304 of 309 expired). The prior holder's consult to su-ce0b634c went unanswered, which fits their P-015.\n\n## Acceptance waiver\n\n_This plan reached a terminal status without fully satisfying its lifecycle gate. Each entry records an explicit, reasoned waiver — what was skipped, and why — so the exception stays visible to anyone who later treats this plan as evidence that the work was verified._\n\n- **2026-09-23** — shipped past `supersede_items_unfinished`. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nSTAND-DOWN 2026-10-01 (leader su-8d81e077): nothing agent-actionable remains. P-005 -> P-009 -> P-010 are OWNER-GATED on D-073 (paid S-I0 pilot cap fork: A amend D-017 cap + more paid inference | B retire/rescope R-4 as unproven, keep EI-24363753174870397 open [leader recommends B] | C leave blocked); typed ask coord:ask-owner conv-muppe3sk-0000-af77c94a4cd64133969ae02809cc87d2, asked once, unanswered; no paid request made, no bar changed. P-006 (WI-10002840, open/unassigned) is evidence-limited: durable startup-cache-evidence/v1 journal is live (D-075/D-076, gateway commit 7b1b94ea); R-10 stays UNKNOWN until a natural >=10 same-scope cohort appears in the journal (largest seen: 3); the terminated D-074 cohort must not be relaunched.
