Measure 5m/1h creation anatomy and gaps by cohort, then compare current 1h behavior with 1h stable-prefix/5m c… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002853 — Improve internal read-cache effectiveness only on proven expensive misses. Instrument existing cachedRead invalidation/expiry/key and build-cost reasons; select work-item detail and inbox candidates … <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002864 — Extend existing cache/usage/launch-cost health surfaces with cohort-aware regression detection. Add minimum-volume and coverage checks, unknown/stale-telemetry states, cold-fork startup cost and imme… <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10003179 — Accept the integrated change and verify final shipment. Run affected tests plus the focused ingestion/pricing/cache-policy/launcher/freshness suites; replay the fixed audit fixtures and run the bound… <!-- P-010 -->\n## Background\n\nAudit: WI-10002736, full report in comment 1142259 (2026-09-23), plus the final owner-facing report in this session. Planning work: WI-10002737. This plan addresses measured inefficiency and accounting defects; it does not assume caching is broken everywhere.\n\nFixed interactive-ledger windows ending 2026-09-23 14:00 UTC: Claude token reuse 96.77% over 24h and 96.31% over 7d; OpenAI 94.19% and 92.34%. These are INGESTION-time windows, not precise request-time trends. Independent actual-time Codex check: 1,404 available transcripts of 1,471 selected; 38,871 deduplicated nonzero-input usage events; 12,283,560,995 input tokens, 11,551,360,000 reused, 94.04%. Sixty-seven source files were unavailable and are explicitly excluded. Live gateway independently reported 94.6% token reuse; its 99.35% request-hit figure only means some cached prefix was present.\n\nOf 732,200,995 uncached tokens in that checked Codex cohort, 576,321,733 (78.71%) were in the first TWO LIFETIME nonzero-input requests of forked sessions within the window. Ninety-six forks consumed over 1M uncached tokens and immediately compacted. Sample: 691,102 input/0 cached; 690,650/2,816; compaction; 90,205/7,936; 90,825/89,856. These establish cold inherited-context processing; the precise provider miss cause remains unisolated. The 576M figure is an opportunity concentration, not promised savings.\n\nConfirmed defects: incremental Codex parsing resets model to gpt-5.5; ingestion records Date.now() rather than request time and omits account/trigger/turn attribution; Claude 1h writes are priced as 1.25x instead of 2x; Codex writes would be double-counted when nonzero. Observed Codex writes were zero, so the last defect did not change this audit's rates. Internal cachedRead snapshot: 51.67% immediate serves including stale-while-refresh, plans 99.5%, inbox 10.8%, work-item list 49.9%, work-item detail 0/50. That is one process over about 29 minutes, not a fleet-wide or historical verdict.\n\nExisting work to reuse: gateway-cache-plane-shared-prefix-ttl-2026-07-19 already implemented retention, stable-prefix splitting and provider-aware policy; P-003 was dropped and P-007 remains todo. agent-launch-context-cost-2026-09-18 is shipped, including default-on tool deferral and launch-cost tooling. cache-expensive-tool-reads-2026-06-22 and round2 are shipped. Do not rebuild these mechanisms or treat stale TODO prose inside a completed item as proof the implementation is missing.\n\nLinked findings: EI-24062060178983964 (Codex model attribution), EI-24061911155747454 (telemetry attribution), EI-24062569394101059 (write pricing/normalization), EI-24062495416991274 (fork/carry cold context). Each remains the existing defect record; link completion evidence and plan coverage to it. New scope warrants this remediation plan because the older cache-policy rollout does not cover these accounting and Codex lifecycle defects.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Correct token and model accounting.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Every supported ingestion path preserves the actual model across chunks and process restarts; unknown stays unknown. Input/read/write quantities are disjoint and reconcile to provider-reported totals. Duplicate usage notifications and zero-input reset events do not inflate request counts or spend.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The normalized usage ledger reconciles each supported source event to disjoint uncached, cache-read, cache-write and output totals with its observed model across chunk and restart boundaries.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any cross-chunk model drift, duplicate/reset overcount, or input/read/write reconciliation mismatch fails.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run incremental, restart, model-switch, unknown-model, duplicate cumulative usage, zero-reset and nonzero-write fixtures; compare all stored counters to provider source totals and a deliberately wrong reset-to-default parser.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/interactive-usage/ingest-adapters.test.ts\",\n        \"libs/generic/model-pricing/src/index.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Explainable, bounded measurements.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The existing usage ledger/reporting surfaces expose event time separately from ingestion time, measurement coverage, actual account when observed, model/transport, session and predecessor lineage, trigger, idle gap, compaction and cold/steady classification, and source provenance. Missing values never become inferred facts or zeros. Preserve both token-hit and request-hit definitions.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The existing usage ledger preserves request-event time, ingestion time and available account/trigger/lineage provenance with explicit coverage for every new ingested sample.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A replay duplicates a sample, parser state advances without samples or any unavailable account/trigger/time is fabricated.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run real-Postgres ingestion twice, interrupt the atomic watermark/state transaction, resume, and compare event IDs, timestamps, provenance and counts; verify unavailable fields remain unknown.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/interactive-usage/ingest-claude-transcripts.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Correct costs and honest history.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Price actual 5m/1h cache-write tiers, resolve model-specific rates from verified current references, and distinguish API-equivalent estimates from subscription billing. Backfill only reproducible source ranges; preserve original evidence/provenance and explicitly mark unrecoverable historical rows.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Source-backed historical corrections and estimates reconcile exactly to the observed model and 5m/1h write tier while preserving originals and unrecoverable-range disclosure.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A repeated backfill changes totals twice, overwrites unsupported history or prices an observed1h write at the5m rate.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Dry-run the archived audit fixtures, snapshot the bounded source rows, apply and repeat the correction in isolated Postgres; compare before/after totals, model attribution and tiered price arithmetic.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/interactive-usage/ingest-claude-transcripts.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Lower fork/carry cost without losing work.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Eliminate avoidable processing of oversized inherited history before immediate compaction while preserving necessary task knowledge, source-session access, lineage, authority, pending directives, claims, and active-writer safety. Include preparatory compaction and all successor/parent requests in cost comparisons. Proposed initial target: at least 50% less uncached input in the first two successor requests and at least 25% less uncached input per matched completed task; quality must meet R-8. Targets are proposed acceptance bars, not measurements or guaranteed savings.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The affected matched fork workload meets the adopted50percent first-two-request and25percent completed-task uncached-input reduction bars without losing required continuity facts.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Either reduction target is missed, preparatory compaction is excluded or any required carried fact/directive/authority is lost.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Replay oversized fork fixtures and compare the selected treatment with the current fork control; include preparation and retry costs; use the pre-registered paired live comparison and retain the95percent uncertainty interval and quality outcomes.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/scripts/psu-recovery.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/cache-efficiency.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Stable reusable context with bounded growth.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Keep invariant instructions/tools stable and changing state after the reusable prefix where the transport permits. Preserve tool discovery and required instructions. Reduce repeated material using existing context assembly and output shaping; do not pad prompts to manufacture a higher hit rate.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Reusable launch context remains stable across equivalent cohorts while required instructions and tool discovery survive bounded-context reductions.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Equivalent stable prefixes differ unexpectedly, required instructions disappear or deferred tools become unreachable.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Compare normalized rendered instruction/tool prefixes across cohort launches and run existing launch-cost and tool-deferral guards together with continuity fixtures; report total-token change and reject padded prompts.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/cache-policy.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/launch-cost-metrics.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Evidence-based TTL policy.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Retention changes are provider/model/transport aware, respect explicit caller settings and cache-marker budgets, and optimize measured total cost. Existing 1h policy remains until a mixed-TTL candidate demonstrates benefit for the measured workload. Do not inject public-API-only controls into subscription transports.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The selected TTL policy reduces measured input cost or retains the current policy when no candidate wins while honoring every supported provider/transport/caller constraint.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A candidate increases measured cost, violates caller TTL or marker order/budget, or sends unsupported controls on the subscription transport.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run shared gateway/proxy policy fixtures for1h-stable plus5m-tail, explicit settings, all-deferred tools, full marker budget and subscription transport; compare actual-tier costs and latency on matched cadence traces.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/cache-policy.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/lib/cache-proxy/proxy.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Useful internal caches with correct freshness.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Attribute misses to cold key, expiry, invalidation, bypass and other actual causes before narrowing invalidation. Inventory the schema and equivalent request identities before adding columns or constraints. Do not introduce a second usage ledger, cache service, scheduler, or dashboard. A new durable surface requires a recorded explanation of why extension cannot fit.\n\nAccounting contract: Anthropic total input = uncached + cache read + cache creation, retaining the creation tier split. OpenAI inclusive input must have read AND reported creation subtracted before storing uncached input. Keep absent write fields unknown rather than converting them to a measured zero. Parser state and byte watermark commit atomically; a model change within a file updates that state, a sparse fork resolves its lineage when possible, and otherwise remains unknown. Replaying a committed range is idempotent. Reconcile at request granularity or with an explicitly documented aggregate mapping.\n\nTelemetry contract: distinguish request event time, ingestion time, transport and source. Use existing provider request IDs or deterministic source-file/byte-range identity where needed; do not invent an unbounded payload store. Record bounded, versioned fingerprints of stable instructions/tools and routing decisions without prompt bodies or credentials. An account/trigger correlation may be marked derived only when its source is reliable; a launch-time pin is not proof of the actual serving account. Time-series and dashboards disclose incomplete coverage and separate forks, warm continuations, compactions and small/large prompts.\n\nFork/carry design: inspect mintCarryRespawnArgs/latestCodexRollout and the live Codex fork/compaction contract. Compare (a) unchanged full fork control, (b) preserving an identical useful prefix with unnecessary carry mutations removed, (c) compacting once before forking, and (d) a fresh bounded carry with addressable source-session recovery when continuity tests permit. Select the smallest supported change on measurements; do not hand-edit native rollout internals or blindly replace every fork with a fresh session. A cache-key/account/prefix change is a hypothesis until a distinguishing comparison establishes it. Keep active predecessor writer locks and per-cut carry delivery intact.\n\nTTL design: a candidate may use 1h stable-prefix markers followed by 5m conversation markers, provided measured cadence justifies it. Preserve Anthropic's marker limit and long-before-short ordering, deferred-tool compatibility and caller TTL intent. Maintain OpenAI generation-specific controls and the subscription exception. Measure rewrite eligibility separately from actual cache hits; a missing boundary split is not automatically a miss. Extend shared policy so gateway/default proxy cannot drift.\n\nInternal cache design: add miss-reason/build-cost counters to the existing primitive, then optimize the expensive proven cases. Candidate item-detail invalidation uses existing per-row tags only after dependencies/trigger coverage are proved; inbox needs recipient-relevant generations including broadcasts and visibility changes. Lists retain invalidation on membership/order changes. Retain hard-TTL and listener health safeguards. No global TTL widening, blanket table-tag removal, or L2 expansion merely to improve the percentage.\n\nExperiment discipline: reuse original audit fixtures, existing launch-cost tools and task-quality suites. Begin with offline replays; use live requests only for properties replays cannot establish. Pre-register matched workload strata, model/transport/account conditions, sample size, paired uncertainty calculation, total inference budget and stop conditions before live execution. Budget is part of implementation, not authorization to run now. Count compaction preparation and failed/retried work. Stop on continuity/security failure, projected budget exhaustion or >10% p95 first-useful-response regression against the matched control. Start with 30 matched fork cases per arm across small/large history, idle gaps and relevant transports; expand only if uncertainty prevents a decision, within the registered cap.\n\nPerformance acceptance: R-4's 50% startup and 25% end-to-end uncached reduction targets apply to the affected matched fork workload, not the entire fleet. Require the paired 95% interval to support an improvement, no required continuity-fixture loss, and no reproducible task-quality regression. A failed target is an open/retuned experiment with its evidence, never a successful close by renaming the metric. TTL needs lower measured input cost without unacceptable latency/quality loss; retain the prior policy if it loses. Internal cache changes need a measured reduction in rebuild work or read latency plus full freshness/isolation tests, not an arbitrary fleet-wide hit-rate target.\n\nEach acceptance bar below names its primary evidence-owning implementation item; supporting investigation, guards and integration work remain required through the dependency graph and item text. P-004 and P-009 additionally own distinct diagnostic and detector contracts. This avoids pretending the same projected outcome is an independent contract for several steps; no outcome or test obligation is removed.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-010 | deployed |\n| R-10 | P-006 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Make accounting trustworthy\n\n- **P-001** `done` Repair canonical usage parsing and write pricing. Feature changes are enabled by default after successful acceptance; no unregistered dark feature counts as shipped. blocked-by: P-009 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Outcome and scope\n\n[owner:Avi] Requested a plan based on WI-10002736. [proposed] Optimize correct, efficient completed work; a cache percentage is diagnostic, not the objective. Scope includes LLM prompt caching, usage accounting, fork/carry behavior and measured internal cachedRead opportunities. It excludes a replacement inference gateway/cache service, blanket account pinning, provider/model migration, unrelated embedding/result caches, and unrelated release repair. No implementation or autonomy grant is implied by drafting this plan.\n\n### D-002 — Sequence and reuse\n\n[proposed] Land accounting fixes with their tests first; prepare independent internal-cache measurements while shared ingestion edits serialize. P-004 need not wait for historical backfill to inspect the fork mechanism; P-005 comparisons use P-003's reconciled cohort. P-007 and P-008 can proceed independently when their prerequisites hold, but P-005/P-006 share launcher/context files and should be sequenced if their lock sets overlap. Do not spawn agents or choose an execution route until that work is requested/authorized. Every new finding uses existing work-item links instead of a duplicate queue.\n\n### D-003 — Retention is a cost decision\n\n[audit evidence] Current Claude policy already upgrades omitted TTLs to 1h; actual 1h writes were observed. [proposed] Retain it until a measured alternative wins. A nonzero 5m-write share is not a defect; this intentionally replaces the old rollout plan's '5m share ~0%' as the optimization criterion for NEW changes. Reconcile that older plan's remaining acceptance item explicitly during implementation. Public OpenAI API caching guidance cannot be applied unchanged to ChatGPT-subscription transport.\n\n### D-004 — Proposed measurable targets and evidence limits\n\n[proposed] Target at least 50% lower first-two-request uncached input and 25% lower uncached input per matched completed task in the affected fork cohort; no reproducible quality loss or >10% p95 first-useful-response regression. These thresholds require review before activation and are not projected savings from the audit. If they prove infeasible, record the measured limit and revise the plan openly rather than lowering a test silently. Missing source files and unknown model/account fields remain explicit; no backfill guesses.\n\n### D-005 — Safe integration and verification\n\n[proposed] Additive telemetry changes first; backup and dry-run before historical data rewrites. No cache reuse across an authorization or tenant boundary. Use existing kill switches and deterministic fallback paths during bounded experiments; preserve old behavior on continuity or correctness failure. Keep rollout reversible, and attach regression tests to every confirmed defect rather than closing on a manual probe.\n\n### D-006 — Execution approved and startup sharing added\n\n[owner:Avi, source session turn 14] AUTO is authorized; this session implements the plan itself through shipped status. This covers tracked files only; the stale path is therefore not in any tracked source and must live in PG-stored rubric/plan text I did not locate.\n\nRoot cause of D-074's irrecoverable cohort: request-stage telemetry timelines live only in a process-local recent array evicted beyond 256 rows (about 10 min on a busy fleet), and no durable store held first-request prefix fingerprints, so a ten-launch cohort could not be joined afterwards. That is a detector/evidence-retention defect, not evidence the requests did not happen.\n\nChange (staged in working tree): request-stage-telemetry.ts adds startup-cache-evidence/v1: startupCacheEvidenceRecord(timeline) emits only when ownerId is set AND previousObservedRequestGapMs===null (first request per owner); formatStartupCacheEvidenceLine / parseStartupCacheEvidenceLine map a journal line to StartupCacheEvidence for assessStartupCacheSharing (availableAt/expiresAt stay null: no provider eligibility source is observable); GatewayRequestTelemetry takes an onStartupEvidence option invoked inside complete() under try/catch so a throwing sink never fails a request. gateway.ts (~2279) wires the sink to log('info', line), i.e. journald, the zero-migration durable sink. Lines carry requestId, provider, model, transport, serving account, tools/instructions fingerprints, native correlation ids and cache read/write/input tokens only: hashes and byte counts, no prompt text.\n\nStill open: (1) the gateway journals only after a restart onto a build containing this change (dev:restart target gateway, after git-sync commits it). (2) The R-10 live ten-launch verdict needs a NATURAL cohort of >=10 same-scope launches to appear in the journal: logs:read unit papercup-inference-gateway grep 'startup-cache-evidence/v1' -> parseStartupCacheEvidenceLine -> assessStartupCacheSharing. Never relaunch the terminated D-074 cohort and do not manufacture a second one. (3) Peer BAR proof on gateway.ts under plan anthropic-credits-gateway-2026-09-30 is source-stale by this 4-line edit; those holders were notified once. (4) The stale R-10 check path (packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/cache-efficiency.test.ts) is absent from tracked files and from the sourceBar-pinned spec AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-006 rev 3 projection; real fixtures are request-stage-telemetry.test.ts 'ten-agent startup sharing evidence (R-10)' and cache-policy.test.ts. Amending rubric text would invalidate its attestation, so the fix is deferred to the BAR-readiness repair (R-1).\n\n### D-076 — Deployed gateway now journals startup-cache-evidence/v1 on real traffic; R-10 cohort verdict stays UNKNOWN\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [turn:self, owner-directed AUTO; P-006 / WI-10002840]. No BAR, cap or acceptance target changes; R-10 is NOT closed; no provider-sharing or savings claim is made; D-073 stays escalated and no paid P-005 request is made.\n\nMeasured: (a) dev:restart target gateway (confirm+authorize, gate_collision clear, nextFire 162s) moved MainPID 3247443 -> 3656143; /healthz answered ok:true accountId aviynw2 ~15s later (the restart tool's own 7.8s readiness probe returned 'unknown probe failure' first, then the listener came up). (b) journalctl --user -u papercup-inference-gateway --since -6m, grep startup-cache-evidence/v1, parsed as JSON: 41 rows, 0 unparseable; fields present: schema, requestId, ownerId, provider, protocol, transport, model, authorizationScope, tools{sha256,bytes,hashedBytes}, instructions{sha256,bytes,hashedBytes}, native{sessionId,threadId}, startedAt, finalizedAt, inputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, reuse, outcome, finalStatus. reuse: 29 partial-hit / 11 zero-read / 1 unobserved; outcome: 34 ok / 6 cancelled / 1 client-error. Both claude (anthropic-messages) and codex (openai-responses) providers emit. (c) Largest same (provider,model,authorizationScope,tools-hash,instructions-hash) group = 2 rows; no >=10 same-scope cohort exists yet, so the R-10 ten-agent startup-sharing verdict remains UNKNOWN, not verified. (d) git status of the 3 gateway files was clean at check time; a peer (su-839dcda5, anthropic-credits-gateway) asked after the restart to hold it while it ran in-tree gateway.ts mutation probes; whether a mutant was loaded at 15:43Z is UNDETERMINED and was asked of that peer; the loaded process still emitted the new evidence lines.\n\nConsequence: the recurrence guard for D-074 evidence loss is now live in the deployed gateway; the missing ingredient for R-10 is a natural or deliberately launched >=10 cohort of identical-prefix, same-scope sessions, which the current D-073 stop does not allow us to buy.\n\n### D-077 — R-10 cohort key is (scope,model,tools hash,stable system blocks) gated on messages<=3, not whole-instructions; verdict stays UNKNOWN; no safe reduction landed\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [turn:self, owner-directed AUTO; P-006 / WI-10002840]. No BAR, cap or acceptance target changes; R-10 is NOT closed; no provider-sharing or savings claim; D-073 stays escalated; no paid request.\n\nMeasured (gateway MainPID 2481885, startup-cache-evidence/v1 layout rows; 72 unique journal rows, 42 with layout; scripts: .papercusp/scratch/r10-union.mts):\n1. FIRST-IN-RING != STARTUP. 36 of 42 layout rows are mid-conversation (messages 5..260) first seen after a gateway restart; only 3 owners produced true startups (messages<=2 plus a tool-less preflight request each: tools 0, ~3KB, uncached).\n2. SAME-FORM PAIR (opus, 8s apart: b11a0afe, 7d5affe9): identical tools sha (88 tools/74 deferred/433464B) and identical stable system blocks 95B+82B+182633B, breakpoints on system 1,2 + last message. Startup1 in=2 read=4557 write=129117; startup2 in=2 read=71027 write=62667 => 53.1% of startup2 prompt tokens were cache reads. Unshared write ~62.7k tokens = system block 4 (14.5KB, same size, per-owner hash) + first user message (~140KB single text block, per-owner hash).\n3. DIFFERENT FORM (95c6c914, sonnet, tools sha differs 88/33/153395B, block4 36.8KB): read=0 write=161118 -- cannot share (model differs; tools prefix differs). Cache is per model+prefix.\n4. TOOLS ARRAY IS NEARLY SESSION-UNIQUE mid-conversation: 27 distinct tools sha over 42 layout rows, max 4 owners per sha (deferred tool loading mutates the array), so a cohort must key on the tools sha.\n5. The old key (whole instructions sha) is the wrong cohort key: the last system block is per-owner, so the largest group was 2-3 and 'no >=10 cohort' (D-076) understated the stable-prefix cohort size.\n\nDecision: (a) code fix landed: assessStartupPrefixCohorts + parseStartupPrefixRowLine in request-stage-telemetry.ts (key=scope,model,transport,tools sha+bytes,system blocks up to the last breakpointed one; counts only outcome ok, tools>0, messages<=3; never promises reads/writes; verdict cohort-present|cohort-too-small, sharingVerified always false), tests 56/56 incl. 5 new. (b) R-10 live ten-agent verdict stays UNKNOWN: n=2 same-form startups, need >=10 same-key startups from natural fleet launches; the evidence journal + this assessor now make that a read, not a re-derivation. D-073 gate unchanged. (c) NO-CHANGE decision for context reduction in this item: the only material unshared spans are the per-owner first user message (single ~140KB text block; provider caches at content-block granularity so a shared leading part inside one block cannot be hit) and system block 4; reducing/reordering them needs CLI request construction or a gateway body split that is NOT proven safe here -> filed as follow-up (see WI note), not implemented. Telemetry additions themselves add no prompt tokens.\n\nGuard: request-stage-telemetry.test.ts 'R-10 startup PREFIX cohorts from the journal layout (D-077)' fails if the key reverts to whole-instructions, if mid-conversation or tool-less rows count as startups, or if a stable-block/tools/model change fails to split cohorts.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-078 — D-077 premise corrected: message-0 block 0 (138KB) IS shared across 22/24 owners; the unshared obstacle is the per-owner system tail block that precedes it\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [turn:self, owner-directed AUTO; P-006 / WI-10005042 / WI-10002840]. No BAR, cap or acceptance target changes; R-10 NOT closed; no provider-sharing or savings claim; D-073 unchanged; no paid request. CORRECTION of D-077 item (c)/WI-10005042 premise ('first user message is a SINGLE per-owner ~140KB block').\n\nMeasured (gateway MainPID 3899576 restarted 20:13Z, segments telemetry live; 28 unique startup-cache-evidence/v1 rows, 24 with layout; scripts .papercusp/scratch/r10-groups.mts, r10-segments.mts):\n1. msg0 block 0 = 138107 bytes, sha16 1264dfecdb3d3db3, byte-identical across 22 of 24 owners (and across persona forms); one more at 138064B. msg0 is 2+ blocks: block 0 shared, block 1 per-owner 0.7-3KB. So layout.messages.first.segments is null BY DESIGN (the block holds a single <system-reminder>); option (1) 'split the first block at <system-reminder> boundaries' is moot.\n2. The real obstacle is ORDER: system[3] (12-28KB, per-owner) sits BEFORE message 0 in the provider prefix, so msg0 block 0 can only ever be written as part of an owner-unique prefix. Largest same-key cohort (opus, tools sha 0c871fa9, system[0..2] identical, 5 owners): system[3] 5/5 distinct; cache reads 71027 tokens (tools+system[0..2]) for 3 of 5, writes 114-134K tokens/owner.\n3. Fragmentation: 14 distinct tools shas and 17 distinct system[2] over 24 rows (deferred tool loading + persona forms) — sharing is same-form AND same-tools only; largest same-key group is 5 mid-conversation owners, so R-10 ten-agent verdict stays UNKNOWN.\n\nDecision: (a) no safe context reduction landed; telemetry only (adds no prompt tokens). (b) Remaining upside (UNCALIBRATED estimate): moving the per-owner system tail after msg0 block 0 plus a breakpoint on block 0 would let each same-form same-tools startup after the first READ ~35-40K tokens instead of WRITE them. That is a launch/carry composer change that moves persona/carry text from system to the user turn (authority semantics) — NOT proven safe, NOT implemented; needs its own design + byte-equality fixture + quality fixture before any experiment. (c) WI-10005042 stays the accountable follow-up, re-scoped to this finding.\n\nGuard: request-stage-telemetry.test.ts covers splitAtSystemReminders + segments null/non-null cases (57/57 at 20:11Z).\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-079 — D-078 design answer: relocate the per-owner system tail in the GATEWAY (stateless, default OFF) — authority semantics + R1\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[turn:self, owner-directed AUTO; WI-10005042 / P-006]. No BAR, cap or acceptance target changes; R-10 NOT closed; no savings claim; D-073 unchanged; NO paid request made.\n\nDESIGN DECISION answering D-078 (b): the per-owner system tail is relocated by the GATEWAY, not by a launcher/composer change.\n1. The gateway already splits the psu system block at PSU_CACHE_BOUNDARY (P-004): stable half = system[2], volatile tail = system[3] (launch brief + mode/precedence + carry doc, 12-28KB). The new pure fn relocateSystemTailToFirstUserTurn (cache-policy.ts) is chained AFTER that split and moves the tail into messages[0].content right behind block 0 (the 138KB block measured byte-identical across 22/24 owners), wrapped in a <system-reminder> that declares it carries system authority; it adds a breakpoint on block 0 when the 4-marker budget and ttl order allow. Why not the composer: the launcher cannot emit a user-turn block (Claude Code owns message 0), and a gateway rewrite is one pure function provable offline and killable by env.\n2. R1 (binding): relocation is STATELESS — it depends only on request-body shape, NEVER on turn number or breakpoint budget. If it did, turn 1 and turn 2 of one conversation would lay the prefix out differently and the whole conversation cache would be rewritten at the transition. Only the breakpoint ADD is budget-gated. Any caller that gates the move on budget/turn violates this decision.\n3. Authority semantics: the move changes no ENFORCED permission (kernel: identity text is never an input to authority; the INSTRUCTION-PRECEDENCE verdict is computed from the mode registry and enforced at dispatch). Whether the MODEL weights relocated text like system text is a QUALITY question that no offline test can answer.\n4. Therefore DEFAULT OFF (env PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_RELOCATE_SYSTEM_TAIL=1 arms it; relocateSystemTailEnabled). This is the deliberate exception to D-016 ship-ON: a quality-unproven authority-semantics change. It flips ON only after a bounded D-073-gated experiment compares same-form startups with/without relocation on cache read/write tokens AND on behaviour (mode/loop/carry compliance); that needs explicit paid-inference authorization and is NOT started.\nEvidence shipped: cache-policy-relocate-tail.test.ts (23 tests: byte-equality, prefix identity across 5 owners with a no-relocation CONTROL, R1 turn/budget, breakpoint/ttl order, 7 fail-to-no-op cases, idempotence). Uncalibrated upside stays ~35-40K tokens read instead of written per same-form same-tools startup after the first; tools-sha fragmentation (41 distinct / 132 rows) still caps the cohort.\nRelated: P-006, D-078\n\n### D-080 — Goal 60d3a8 restores independent cache leader with one member\nDate: 2026-10-10\nMeasured 2026-10-10T21:08Z through goals:get, fleet:assignments(snapshot) and plans:items(actionable): goal active; owner settings maxAgents=6, maxPerFleet=3, intendedParallelPlanFleets=1; cache fleet has no live agents; P-006 is actionable; P-005 links a blocked work-item and retained paid-experiment cap decision. Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for fleet-reliability-verification-2026-07-10, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality (completion audit #1, sha 95173602ab, 32 citations, 12 items audited).\n\nHOW THESE CRITERIA WERE DERIVED.When first authored, the plan carried no Decisions. It now carries D-001 and D-002 (both 2026-09-03) and D-003 and D-004 (2026-09-23, residual disclosures). They are derived instead from the plan's own five phase headings — Detection + integrity invariants, Watch/wake primitives, Leader ergonomics, Deploy vintage, Self-checking verification substrate — one criterion per phase, plus a sixth that carries the audit's two adverse findings. A grader should treat the phase headings as the goal statement this plan never wrote down.\n\n⚠ THE AUDIT FOUND TWO ITEMS OVERSTATING WHAT LANDED, both in Phase 5, and criterion `phase-5-substrate-gap-not-overclaimed` exists to keep them visible. P-010: probe:emit's stamping and loud refusal are real, but the claimed acked round trip with per-hop receipts is not — federation-probe.ts declares PROBE_HOPS = ['captured'] as const, a single hop, and both probe tools explicitly disclaim drain, replication, merge, member-guard and projection. A probe failure therefore cannot name its hop, which was the item's central purpose. P-011: the canary substrate, the scheduled sweep and ONE wired canary landed, but the item's \"every standing gate\" generalization did not, and there is no checkpoint-walker canary. Neither is a regression and neither is hidden — the code documents its own scope accurately in both cases. The gap is between the plan items, which are marked done, and the code.\n\n⚠ THE WORK-ITEM TRAIL IS NOT USABLE AS EVIDENCE HERE. Of the 12 linked work-items only three carry any filesChanged; the other nine record \"completed passed\" with no files. A grader spot-checking via work-items will find almost nothing. Use the audit's recorded paths, which all resolve.\n\nMechanical bindings were run green BEFORE being bound: 11 files, 214 passed, 0 failed, at 2026-09-03T01:32Z.\n\nRevision 2 (2026-09-23, su-07b72cf6, successor vetter, conv-mudgoqh7 by su-dd13ad54): corrected the stale no-Decisions premise; c5 rebound to the real P-009 stamp test and the merge stall test, with its method scoped to drain+merge (P-012 residual disclosed as D-003); c2 gains plan-item-lane-guard.test.ts and the P-005 awaiter-count leg; c4 gains a live runtime_vintage leg (off-box bundles deferred as D-004); c1's drill uses a /tmp schema copy, not the shared tree; c6 traces to D-001 through D-004 and carries a structured check. Not applied: 'bar == model', because bar is a read-time projection of model for acceptance rubrics (packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts:541).\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nDefinition-of-done for github-bridge-hive-egress-2026-07-02, authored AFTER implementation against as-built reality (completion audit #1, sha 405654dba4, 27 citations, 9/9 items code-verified).\n\nSCOPE BOUNDARY THE GRADER MUST HOLD. This plan's own Now block declares an unscheduled LATER PHASE: \"live 2-machine bridged-hive verify before flipping any real hive's mode to 'bridged'\". Phase 1 completeness is therefore NOT plan completeness, and no criterion here may be read as clearing that gate. The bridge has never been exercised against two real machines. Criterion `later-phase-and-decisions-not-overclaimed` exists specifically to fail a ship that papers over this.\n\nPATH DRIFT WARNING. Every item in the plan text cites `sync/hive-git/…`. That directory was renamed: the code is at `packages/operator-core/lib/sync/pot-git/`, the mode type is `PotGitMode` (plan says `HiveGitMode`), and the ingress domain constant is `papercusp-pot-git-github-origin-v1`. A grader spot-checking the audit from the item text alone will get a false 'missing' on all nine items. Check the audit's recorded paths, which resolve.\n\nThe governing design decisions D-001, D-002 and D-003 are all still marked PROPOSED (\"owner may amend\") and were drafted and built under AUTO. That is disclosed, not hidden, and the plan's Next line asks the owner to review them. It is a live acceptance consideration, not a defect.\n\nMechanical bindings were run green BEFORE being bound: 11 files, 132 passed, 0 failed (unit 88, integration 44) at 2026-09-03T01:22Z.\n\nRevision 2 (2026-09-23, su-07b72cf6, successor vetter): merged single-writer-preserved-no-new-election and no-new-scheduler-and-flag-honestly-defaulted into single-writer-and-scheduler-reused-flag-default-on (perfectly coupled at file granularity; vet conv-mudgoo6v F1), bound the flag half to libs/flags/src/production-defaults.test.ts, and added canonical-ref-set-egressed-is-staging-only-and-disclosed for the release-channel half of D-001/S-2 (F2). F3 (split the later-phase criterion) deferred: the acceptance cap is 7 criteria.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"goal-brief-to-claimed-plan-work-2026-09-23","title":"Goal brief to claimed plan work — selection, delivery and bounded follow-through","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-23","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Goal brief to claimed plan work — selection, delivery and bounded follow-through\nslug: goal-brief-to-claimed-plan-work-2026-09-23\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-23\nupdated: 2026-10-10\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-10, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_stale, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_author_rejected. Next repair: Re-prove the current spec revision; superseded proof does not cover it. (R-2). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nOwner-approved implementation, route:self: Aviyn instructed this session to fold the scope-aware planning refinements into this plan and carry it to shipped status (session_turn:codex:01a0cc77-3037-7e73-8666-6074aa95e250:38). WI-10002619 is the non-code program driver; substantive code work is tracked on the plan's implementing items. AUTO and the tracked work loop are active. Next: complete the source-conversation activation audit, then implement personally.\n\nPrimary outcome: an evidenced goal-local planning need becomes an appropriate started plan with an independently led fleet and actual member claims, while suitable existing Blender plans are adopted rather than duplicated. Scope, budget, admission and legitimate no-new-plan decisions remain explicit. P-006 is completed rubric-authoring history; P-008 covers the newly approved gap-review policy change.\n\n**Next:** Vet the current acceptance-rubric criteria BEFORE binding proof or emitting adequacy cards (amend → vet → attest → bind → cards → grade): a vetting critique usually becomes an amendment, and proof bound first must then be re-bound.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10002624 — Pin the baseline and replay the actual shared brief path for goal versus fleet leader. Resolve selected/delivered payload, scope, worklist revision, current-build generation and action effects; disti… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002625 — Implement outcome-derived planning-needed and standing-frontier obligations in the existing providers/readers. Detect uncovered needs even with a nonempty worklist; prioritize staffing suitable exist… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002626 — Harden eligible-plan materialization through the existing launch transaction and claim rails. Test independent initial leader, lease, positive plan filter, actual worker pickup and no duplicate fleet… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002627 — Verify and repair actual goal brief delivery across first turn, warm turn, cold wake and compaction using the shared fleet-leader path. Preserve current generation, stable obligation identity and omi… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002628 — Add bounded effect-based progress tracking and exhaustive refusal-to-action mapping in existing obligation/watchdog/reminder mechanisms. Populate placement age/deadline, exclude genuinely blocked/in-… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002629 — When authoritative budget and normal admission permit, run two matched current-build trials and independent grade: goal-local need -> new necessary plan -> execution, and Blender proposal -> existing… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002630 — Update the canonical GOAL-mode planning/IDEATE contract and existing gap-review recording/rubric surfaces to the approved scope-aware policy. Blender and goal holders can both plan within scope; requ… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002631 — Connect goal-local recurring findings and verified outcomes to Blender's existing routed-idea/goal-evidence/outcome feedback surfaces. Preserve original proposal/plan/goal attribution during adoption… <!-- P-009 -->\n## Background and evidence\n\n- WI-10002601 registers this design/rubric unit under WI-10002557.\n- shared-agent-obligations-and-briefs-2026-09-05 is SHIPPED (2026-09-12; nine terminal implementation items).\n- goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 already contains completed P-021/P-024/P-025/P-026 work for portfolio breadth, recovery, container selection and closure. Reuse those implementations. Its P-004 final acceptance is explicitly OWNER-PAUSED pending review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23. This plan DOES NOT lift or route around that pause.\n- generic-acceptance-routing-and-live-plan-agent-brief-2026-09-20 is awaiting-acceptance. Its old Now prose still says draft; use canonical lifecycle rather than that stale prose.\n- Frozen trial: su-6aab097a, 2026-09-23T01:59:40.260Z–03:42:00Z. Base card EI-24025141569545679; stewardship card EI-24025333199380204. No verified new plan-worker launch. The only known worklist plan had shipped on September21, so no new launch was owed for THAT plan. No proven instance of an ignored eligible launch instruction has been established.\n- Source gap: agent-obligation-providers.ts planPlacementObligation filters terminal plans and returns not-applicable when none remain. agent-obligation-reader.ts builds placement/report/acceptance/directive/wait obligations, not a standing-frontier-selection obligation. This does not implement the rubric's empty/terminal-only -> frontier duty.\n- Source gap: placement provider accepts ageMs, but the reader does not populate it; placement changeSignal has an event but no progress deadline, unlike reporting. This shared path does not currently establish a bounded claim-progress deadline. Check other watchdogs before adding any enforcement.\n- Source defect: launch refusals other than goal_budget_exceeded are described as headcount in planPlacementObligation. In particular, unknown priced spend must never produce advice to free agents or raise ceilings.\n- Known execution barriers are tracked: legacy worklist schema EI-23806538522165636 (source repair done; do not repeat); liveness WI-10002562; spend WI-1074208; fail-closed launch guard WI-10002052 (done).\n- Historical brief delivery is NOT proven from formatter/source tests or a missing transcript search hit. Required evidence must join the actual source generation, selected agenda, delivered content and ensuing effect.\n\n## Scope and non-goals\n\nExtend the existing obligation provider/reader/renderer, GoalPortfolioBrief placement compiler, canonical launch transaction, fleet claims, and event_awaits reminders. Do not introduce a parallel goal checklist, scheduler, execution ledger, per-turn supervisor swarm, or alternate launch tool.\n\nKeep owner worklist order/CAS, cross-goal ownership boundaries, independent initial plan leadership, native nonimplementation by the GOAL holder, and the unchanged 50000-cent weekly budget. No fabricated pot links, no estimated-cost promotion to authoritative spend, no budget bypass, no forced admission, no repeated launch after refusal without diagnosis, and no reopening shipped plans for test demand.\n\nGoal and all applicable descendants remain GPT-6 Sol xhigh with the persisted account/carry/capacity settings. Existing GPT-6 Sol/Luna catalog work is reused; regression checks prevent model-family drift. Do not activate Scout or other owner-paused work.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Complete, scoped planning-need selection.** An active standing goal must identify uncovered outcomes, recurring failures, ineffective current approaches and missing executable work—not infer planning need solely from an empty queue. Its shared brief emits a justified adopt/revise/create-and-start/drain/route/no-new-plan obligation. Empty or terminal-only worklists trigger a scoped gap/frontier review. Existing eligible plans are adopted, not duplicated; other-goal-owned work is routed away.\n\n**R-2 — Eligible plans reach real execution.** A currently eligible plan must reach an independently led plan fleet, positive plan/plan_item filter, valid delegated lease and actual member claim within two completed eligible decision opportunities after actionable delivery, or expose a current typed blocker with advancing accountable repair. Already-started plans recover their lane rather than creating another plan. This is the primary acceptance bar.\n\n**R-3 — Brief delivery is observable and current.** Goal and fleet leader consume the same obligation engine with role-appropriate actions. A source-generation/worklist-revision -> selected obligation -> delivered/non-omitted brief -> decision -> effect trace survives warm turns, cold restart and compaction. Omitted/stale/unmeasured input cannot be reported as ignored by the agent.\n\n**R-4 — Stalls cause bounded corrective action.** Derive no-progress age from canonical effects and completed eligible opportunities, not heartbeat, reads or repeated launches. A live long call, pause, admission restriction, authoritative budget refusal or no demand must not trigger duplicate launches. Diagnose the first refusal; choose another feasible independent lane when permitted. Stop/reassign/escalate through existing authority when the bounded repair makes no progress.\n\n**R-5 — Budget, liveness and legacy goals retain correct semantics.** Unknown spend stays unknown and blocks billable launches. Refusal copy and recommended action match the exact refusal discriminant. Verified tool activity and true silence are distinguished by the existing liveness repair. Legacy worklist values/version are preserved through the existing schema repair.\n\n**R-6 — Rubric judges needed planning and delivery, not output quotas.** Preserve the already-ratified five criterion improvements and their keys/checks/scales. Replace the remaining unconditional goal-agent idea-production requirement with evidence of a meaningful scoped gap review: existing plans sufficient is valid, while an evidenced planning need left unaddressed is not. Proposal grades and plan counts cannot satisfy execution demand. Partial repair credit requires fresh causal progress. Historical cards retain their original revisions and instructions.\n\n**R-7 — Behavioral change is measured with both planning origins.** After deterministic guards pass and budget permits, run two independent fresh current-build GOAL trials with matched baseline scenarios: one discovers an uncovered need and creates/starts/executes a necessary goal-local plan without a Blender proposal; the other adopts and executes an appropriate Blender plan without cloning it. Each must prove independent member claims and at least one organic end-to-end terminal/verification/feedback/report trace. Also exercise existing-plans-sufficient, terminal/no-demand, blocked-budget, missing-delivery and cross-goal negative controls. Record model/effort, workload, source generation, exact brief exposure, plan/proposal provenance, effects, cost and residual unknowns. No claim of improvement from formatter tests, plan counts, all-terminal trials or unmatched averages.\n\n**R-8 — Scope separates planning responsibilities.** Blender may generate workspace-level/cross-goal proposals and a goal agent may independently generate plans for its own goal. Both use existing proposal/plan rails. New opportunities do not confer authority over another goal or permit cloning a suitable existing plan. Planning is normally the organizing route; bare work-items remain the exception for self-contained work.\n\n**R-9 — Execution-first priority and meaningful gap review.** When suitable executable plans lack workers, staff or repair those lanes before another discretionary ideation pass. When existing plans do not cover the goal's needs, plan the gap. Record a periodic or trigger-driven gap review with evidence and one of the typed dispositions; a reasoned no-new-plan result is valid. No minimum new-idea/feature count and no records fabricated merely to satisfy a quota. Necessary planning, existing-plan progress, owner instructions and genuine blockers determine priority.\n\n**R-10 — Feedback retains scope and origin.** Goal-local recurring problems and observed outcomes feed Blender's broader learning; Blender proposals are routed to the appropriate goal holder. Preserve original proposal IDs, plan refs, goal attribution and amendment/adoption history on existing evidence/routed-idea/outcome surfaces. One accountable execution owner remains visible; feedback or refinement must not silently fork another plan.\n\n## Design\n\n### Existing mechanisms to extend\n\n1. Selection: GoalPortfolioBrief plus existing goal outcomes/history and scoped frontier/scheduler readers. Derive planning needs from uncovered outcomes and failures, not only queue emptiness. Use the shared provider/reader for scope-aware gap review and prioritize existing executable plans before discretionary ideation.\n2. Delivery: existing agenda projection and orientation/fleet-leader receipt paths, not a new prompt file. Add stable evidence references to existing retained payload/event surfaces only where a measured gap requires them.\n3. Execution: existing compileGoalPlanPlacement and fleet:launch-on-plan transaction. Surface its exact admissible arguments. Verify lease/filter/member claim from canonical records. GOAL chooses scope/width; a separate agent leads and workers implement.\n4. Progress: reuse existing goal-fleet watchdog/cohort and event_awaits. Populate effect age/deadline only from the responsible operation. One accountable reminder, no duplicate polling supervisor.\n5. Refusals: exhaustive typed mapping, especially goal_budget_unmeasurable versus exceeded/headcount/admission. Never infer permission from absence of measurement.\n6. Grading: replace unconditional new-idea production with meaningful scoped gap review; keep necessary planning, materialization, drain work and end-to-end closure distinct. Use the existing non-compensating stewardship rollup and explicit critical unknowns. Do not make another grading layer.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003, P-007 | live |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-004, P-007 | live |\n| R-4 | P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003, P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006, P-008 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | live |\n| R-8 | P-002, P-008, P-009 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-002, P-005, P-008 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-009, P-007 | live |\n\nLive means a pinned current-build/staging experiment with genuine delivered inputs and claimed work. Green main is required only for final shipment, not ordinary implementation. Existing P-004's paused acceptance remains separate.\n\n### Verification scenarios\n\nPositive: empty/terminal-only worklist discovers an eligible existing plan; unplanned multi-step work is planned once; eligible already-started plan gets a fleet; launch produces real member claim; failed launch is diagnosed; two independent eligible plans use permitted parallel capacity; warm/cold delivery preserves the actionable obligation; broken-leg repair progresses to closure.\n\nNegative: shipped plan produces no launch; legitimate no-demand remains a cheap no-op; missing/stale/omitted brief yields unknown/system attribution; other-goal ownership prevents adoption; unmeasurable/over-budget launch is refused without cap edits; full capacity and admission restrictions do not spawn storms; existing live leader/worker is not duplicated; live long-running tool does not look dead; silent ended holder is recovered through the permitted path.\n\nAdditional required cases: necessary goal-local plan creation with no Blender proposal; adoption of a suitable Blender plan without cloning; sufficient existing plans with a reasoned no-new-plan review; execution-first priority when an eligible plan lacks workers; both-origin feedback preserving proposal/plan/goal identity.\n\nCounterexamples that MUST not pass the revised rubric: thirteen proposal grades with eligible plan left unclaimed; launch receipts with zero worker claims; a busy drain presented as a plan fleet; repeated partial scores supported only by status reads; all-terminal workload used to certify plan-launch behavior.\n\n## Phase 1 — Reconcile and extend selection\n\n- **P-001** `done` Pin the baseline and replay the actual shared brief path for goal versus fleet leader. Resolve selected/delivered payload, scope, worklist revision, current-build generation and action effects; distinguish historical unknowns from causal findings. Reuse stored tests/evidence, do not rerun them merely for ceremony. importance: high — note: ← WI-10002624 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement outcome-derived planning-needed and standing-frontier obligations in the existing providers/readers. Detect uncovered needs even with a nonempty worklist; prioritize staffing suitable existing plans before discretionary ideation. Emit explicit adopt/revise/create-start/drain/route/no-new-plan actions, with scope/ownership/CAS/stop guards and justified sufficient-existing-plan results. Add canonical positive/negative demand tests. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002625 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Convert brief actions into claimed plan work\n\n- **P-003** `done` Harden eligible-plan materialization through the existing launch transaction and claim rails. Test independent initial leader, lease, positive plan filter, actual worker pickup and no duplicate fleet/plan. Reuse EI-23806538522165636 and existing completed placement work; fix only demonstrated remaining gaps. Deterministic development need not wait for billable-trial budget measurement. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002626 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Verify and repair actual goal brief delivery across first turn, warm turn, cold wake and compaction using the shared fleet-leader path. Preserve current generation, stable obligation identity and omitted-entry receipts; make evidence linkage sufficient to distinguish selection, delivery and agent follow-through. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002627 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Add bounded effect-based progress tracking and exhaustive refusal-to-action mapping in existing obligation/watchdog/reminder mechanisms. Populate placement age/deadline, exclude genuinely blocked/in-flight windows, diagnose before retry, and retain one accountable repair/wake. Link WI-10002562 and WI-1074208 rather than bypassing or duplicating them. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002628 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Grade and demonstrate the changed behavior\n\n- **P-006** `done` Ratify and validate the five targeted criterion improvements on the existing goal-mode-e2e and work-on-everything-stewardship-health rubrics. Preserve unchanged keys/checks/scales, prior card history and model settings. Exercise the listed pass/fail/unknown counterexamples; attach exact resulting rubric revisions and review once. importance: high — note: Completed within authoring unit WI-10002601. Rubric changes active after independent review. This item completion does not activate the draft implementation plan or resume prior program P004.\n- **P-007** `done` When authoritative budget and normal admission permit, run two matched current-build trials and independent grade: goal-local need -> new necessary plan -> execution, and Blender proposal -> existing plan adoption -> execution without duplication. Prove brief -> independent leader/filter/lease -> member claim -> terminal evidence -> verification -> origin-preserving feedback -> report. Include existing-plans-sufficient and no-demand/blocked/missing-delivery controls. Report actual cost and uncertainty. Final shipment follows normal green promotion/deploy with the established live-gate owner. Entry to the billable trials requires current, passing P-009 implementation unit/integration and attribution/mutation evidence, reviewed acceptance methods, permitted real workload subjects, authoritative budget and normal admission. P-009 final R-10 live certification is deliberately not a prerequisite: these trials produce its required organic traces. Keep P-009 nonterminal until those traces satisfy R-10 and the final independent grade; deterministic proof cannot replace them. D-010 separates implementation readiness from final certification. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-008 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002629 completed (done)\n\n- **P-008** `done` Update the canonical GOAL-mode planning/IDEATE contract and existing gap-review recording/rubric surfaces to the approved scope-aware policy. Blender and goal holders can both plan within scope; require meaningful review and necessary-plan follow-through, not a minimum new-feature count. Extend existing pass/evidence records to express supported dispositions and preserve model inheritance. Verify actual rendered/delivered mode text and rubric counterexamples; obtain only the normal independent ratification for changed standard rubrics. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002630 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Connect goal-local recurring findings and verified outcomes to Blender's existing routed-idea/goal-evidence/outcome feedback surfaces. Preserve original proposal/plan/goal attribution during adoption, revision and cross-goal routing; no new parallel ledger. Test both-origin feedback and duplicate-prevention behavior end-to-end at the current build. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10002631 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Primary unit of success\nThe unit is an eligible plan with independently led workers actually claiming and completing its work. Selection, launch and reporting are intermediate steps.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse and ownership\nThis follow-up adds missing frontier/delivery/progress coverage; it does not duplicate the shipped brief system or completed generic GOAL behavior work. Existing accounting/liveness items keep their normal owners/admission. The old behavior-program P-004 acceptance pause remains in force.\n\n### D-003 — Causal discipline\nCurrent source exposes gaps, but the frozen trial has no proved ignored actionable eligible-plan brief. The all-terminal plan and budget/liveness barriers are material confounds. New tests must establish positive demand and delivered opportunity before grading agent noncompliance.\n\n### D-004 — Safe autonomy\nNo budget or authority broadening, no fabricated spend, no new telemetry-only subject launch, no forced admission or red-gate deployment. Source and deterministic tests may proceed independently of blocked billable trials after implementation is activated.\n\n### D-005 — Scope-aware planning, not an exclusive plan author\nThe scope division is workspace-level synthesis for Blender and goal-local planning for each goal holder. Both may originate plans. Reuse or refine suitable existing work, keep one accountable execution owner, and route other-goal work instead of appropriating it. This supersedes the earlier suggestion that the goal agent should primarily be only a consumer of Blender plans. Sources: session_turn:codex:01a0cc77-3037-7e73-8666-6074aa95e250:33, :35, :37, :38.\n\n### D-006 — Priority and review evidence replace production quotas\nStaff suitable executable plans first; identify and plan genuinely uncovered needs when required. A meaningful goal-gap review may conclude existing plans are sufficient. Do not require a new feature filing every reporting cycle. Penalize evidenced neglected planning/execution opportunities, not a lack of manufactured output. Keep original scorecards historical. Sources: session_turn:codex:01a0cc77-3037-7e73-8666-6074aa95e250:35, :37, :38.\n\n### D-007 — One proposal lineage and both-origin acceptance\nReuse existing goal/plan/proposal links and feedback records for local and Blender-origin work. The matched acceptance cases must exercise both necessary local plan creation and nonduplicating adoption of a Blender plan, plus valid no-new-plan controls. Source: session_turn:codex:01a0cc77-3037-7e73-8666-6074aa95e250:37, :38.\n\n### D-008 — Implementation route and terminal condition\nAviyn explicitly selected this session to implement through shipped status. Root performs source implementation; independent agents are used only for scoped testing/review where required, on GPT-6 Sol xhigh. AUTO/work loop is registered. The old behavior-program P-004 pause is not lifted, and no budget, admission, cross-goal ownership or red-gate bypass is authorized. Source: session_turn:codex:01a0cc77-3037-7e73-8666-6074aa95e250:38.\n\n### D-009 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-26\nAmendment-Id: su9399-bar-checks-20260926-r3\nRequest-Hash: b4d0115158395ed9eed1f9b57786f0956c28b016dc2a70b9e634f0f9b95c318f\nActor: su-9399b875-0b9f-43da-b711-be029097ea2b\nReason: WI-10003253: repair ship-blocking missing checks and proof depth using existing clauses' layer unions, and replace generic falsifiers with already-authored method observations. Preserve outcome text, scope planes, mandatory flags and pass ratings. R7 manual instrument still requires behavioral evidence. Runtime remains undeclared pending preview investigation; methods pin :3170 per existing Design.\nApproved-By: su-616d29e6-b6fb-43c2-ba5c-9d8ff30c096f\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1147354\nApproved-At: 2026-09-26T19:08:28.197Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 13 → 14\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-010 — Separate implementation readiness from live certification; preserve R10 live bar\nDate: 2026-09-27\nMeasured 2026-09-27: plans:items returns P007 unresolvedBlockers=[P009]. Active AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-009@3 and rubric revision4 R10 method require both P007 organic terminal traces; WI10002629 checkpoint confirms no trials executed. This is a circular terminal-certification dependency, tracked EI-24385390926942125. Ruling: never close P009 from deterministic proof alone, relabel integration as live behavioral evidence, or fabricate P007 traces. Repair the sequencing by distinguishing P009 tested implementation readiness from its final live certification; P007 must eventually be eligible after the former so it can produce the latter. Of 109 goalPlacementTurnEnd rows, 0 carry governor open/restricted. observeGoalPlacementAdmission (packages/operator-core/lib/goal-placement-turn-receipts.ts) sets governor only from a fresh resource-governor.state snapshot whose admission.state is non-null and that carries an evidenceRef. admissionEligibility returns null for governor 'unknown', so eligibleAtOffer is always null and qualifyGoalPlacementTurn records nothing. Posted as WI-10003903 #1152301.\n2. [code] The only writer of resource-governor.state is system-health publishGovernorStateSnapshot (packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/compute.ts). Its own comment says it publishes the queue census only, with no controller or recovery decision, so admission.state is always null.\n3. [code] No agent-class admission decision exists to publish. Placement launches (agent-tools/fleet_registry/launch-on-plan.ts, agent-tools/capability/launch-agent.ts) go through spawnGovernedAgentProcess -> beginGovernedExecution (resource-governor/execution.ts). Governor.admit always enqueues a durable receipt, and the caller immediately takes a TARGETED lease on its own receipt (queue.ts leaseReceipt). No controller is consulted. The paced queue drainer (resource-governor/queue-drainer.ts) is exported from index.ts and nothing else. spawn-door-governor-migration-2026-08-31 records the governor as observe-only for agent spawns: P-003 is done, and the binding migration P-005..P-012 is todo.\n\nOPTIONS\n(a) Publish an authoritative agent-class admission into resource-governor.state. REJECTED for this plan: there is no decision to publish until spawn-door-governor binds a controller (its P-012). A published 'open' with no deciding authority would be fabricated evidence.\n(b) Treat a governor 'unknown' as non-voiding when planReason=ready and attempts=none. REJECTED: it lets missing evidence add debt in general, including the future state where a controller does bind and only its snapshot is stale.\n(c) CHOSEN: the governor leg reads the authority that actually binds agent admission.\n\nRULING\n1. A fresh snapshot with a published admission state still wins, unchanged: 'restricted' when paused or when 'agent' is in constrainedClasses, else 'open', with the snapshot's evidenceRef.\n2. Otherwise the leg consults one exported declaration beside the governed agent door: AGENT_ADMISSION_GOVERNOR_BINDING in resource-governor/spawn-execution.ts, value 'observe-only'. While it reads 'observe-only', the governor cannot restrict an agent launch, so the leg reads 'open' with evidenceRef 'governor:agent:observe-only'.\n3. PIN: a spawn-execution test asserts the behavior the declaration claims. While the declaration reads 'observe-only', spawnGovernedAgentProcess admits and leases its own receipt in the same call, with no drainer wait. When spawn-door-governor makes the door wait on a controller, that test fails and forces the declaration to 'binding'. With 'binding', an absent or stale snapshot yields 'unknown' again (fail-closed to unmeasured, never to open).\n4. Out of scope, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: launch-on-plan's capacity clamp (dispatchBudget) and the budget pause are separate doors. They are not read by the governor leg. A launch they refuse or clamp still shows up through the attempts leg (a receipt), and a goal budget pause is the 'pause' condition already in the clause.\n\nCONSEQUENCE\nNew turn-end rows can carry governor 'open', so eligibleAtOffer and eligibleAtCompletion become measurable for a ready plan with no in-flight attempt. Progress and stalled cursor rows may start appearing mid-arm. If it still reads gitnexus in-progress, premise 1 is wrong.\n\n### D-037 — R-3 oracle: a native session's owner is resolved from TWO independent witnesses (activation span, per-owner CLI transcript location); the receipt row's owner is never a witness\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed: su-32d1b8df under owner directives #908/#938. Recorded BEFORE the probe edit and before any probe run that uses it. Independent view requested from su-4f968faa (coord 16:19Z, 'view, not ruling'); if it identifies a flaw this decision is amended or reversed. Amends only how docs/evidence/goal-brief-r3-live-probe-2026-09-29.mts resolves a session's owner; the clause, the falsifier rule and D-034/D-035/D-036 are unchanged.]\n\nWHY\n1. [observed 16:13Z] The R-3 live probe fails r3-no-omitted-or-foreign-counted-as-delivered on activity 6512596 and 6512617, both 'foreign owner/workspace'. They are holder su-ce50c06d's confirmed deliveries in native session 59ad5d69, at 15:10Z.\n2. [observed] The probe's ONLY identity witness is harness_shared.session_identity_activation_spans. It has no row for 59ad5d69, 4c6d5262 or 33de8c90. su-ce50c06d's applied activation events at 14:35, 14:55 and 15:09Z all name the stale native id 9b1e7cb7 while the CLI ran 33de8c90 and then 59ad5d69. That recording defect is WI-10004917; the fix is in the tree and awaits the bg-host restart.\n3. [observed] The CLI writes its transcript under the owner's own config directory: ~/.papercusp/session-claude/su-ce50c06d-.../projects/*/59ad5d69-....jsonl, and likewise 4c6d5262 and 33de8c90. su-2e6fb313's 64436191 sits under su-2e6fb313, which agrees with its activation span. The receipt module neither writes nor reads that location.\n4. Treating a session with no span as foreign is a conservative stand-in, not the clause. The clause falsifies a FOREIGN-session payload, and 59ad5d69 is provably the receipt owner's own session. Keeping a single witness converts a defect in the identity recorder into a false falsification of the receipt logic under test.\n\nDECISION\nA. identityOf(nativeSessionId) collects owners from two witnesses: (i) DISTINCT owner_id in session_identity_activation_spans; (ii) the <owner> directory of every ~/.papercusp/session-claude/<owner>/projects/*/<nativeSessionId>.jsonl. The session resolves iff the union is exactly one owner. Two or more owners means a conflict, and zero means unresolved; both stay null, so the row is counted FOREIGN exactly as today.\nB. Workspace: from the span when one exists; otherwise the single DISTINCT workspace_id across that owner's session_identity_activation_events. Anything other than exactly one stays null, which reads as foreign.\nC. The receipt row's owner_id/session_id are NEVER a witness. observations.identityWitnesses records per session which witnesses answered and what each said, so a grader can audit every resolution.\nD. New counterexample R3_COUNTEREXAMPLE=forged-owner rotates each confirmed delivery's owner to a different owner. It must exit 1 with 'foreign owner/workspace' on every delivered row, including the transcript-only ones; that proves the second witness does not echo the row. count-not-applicable must still exit 1.\n\nCONSEQUENCES\n- 6512596/6512617 become judgeable. The session-boundary leg still needs a second complete chain for ONE owner in a different native session; nothing is credited across owners.\n- Rejected: B (open the window at the fix deploy and list pre-fix rows as residual unknowns). It discards real evidence instead of measuring it, and it requires two fresh chains. Rejected: C (leave R-3 red). The red is an artefact of the recorder bug, not of the clause.\n- No activation span is backfilled for any session, and no holder is messaged.\n\n### D-038 — R-3 oracle: a holder's fleet works a plan iff its claim spec targets that plan (D-033 binding), not iff its slug resembles the plan slug\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed: su-32d1b8df under owner directives #908/#938. In that case, record it here and on WI-10004975.\n\n### D-040 — R-3 oracle: D-037 witness (ii) also reads the ingested transcript store, so a pruned host transcript file does not turn a resolved session into 'foreign'\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02 [self-imposed: su-32d1b8df under owner directives #908/#938. [observed 12:40Z 10-02] The R-3 probe regressed from 2/3 to 1/3. r3-no-omitted-or-foreign-counted-as-delivered now fails on activity 6512596/6512617 (holder su-ce50c06d, native 59ad5d69-3227-4b4c-81cd-9bc53bda187b, 2026-10-01 15:10Z) with 'foreign owner/workspace'. Both passed at 00:16Z (r3-main-0017.json).\n2. [observed 12:44Z] The cause is pruning, not a change in identity. That session has no activation span (it was transcript-only under D-037), and ~/.papercusp/session-claude/su-ce50c06d-20e3-4945-86b7-a0d3b72b8550/projects/*/59ad5d69-....jsonl no longer exists, although the owner dir does. su-4f968faa's D-037 review predicted this ('a pruned file falls back to foreign').\n3. [observed 12:44Z] harness_shared.session_turn_parts still holds the session: 205 parts, owner su-ce50c06d-20e3-4945-86b7-a0d3b72b8550, source_kind claude, workspace_id 'default', 15:06-15:19Z 10-01. Retention is 14 days.\n4. [observed, read from code] The ingester takes a Claude transcript's owner from the same path D-037 witness (ii) reads: packages/operator-core/lib/search/session-ingest.ts FILE_ADAPTERS[claude].meta matches /\\/session-claude\\/([^/]+)\\// on ~/.papercusp/session-claude/<ownerDir>/projects/<cwd>/<session>.jsonl. The one override, ingestFileNow({ owner }), is passed the session's own launch identity, which is the same root D-037 already discloses as a residual.\n\nDECISION\n(1) Witness (ii) = the owners named by the on-disk per-owner transcript path UNION the owner that session_turn_parts recorded for that native session (source_kind 'claude'). It is one witness read at two times (probe time and ingest time), not a third witness.\n(2) The D-037 resolution rule is unchanged. If the on-disk and ingested readings disagree (for example a psu --fork seed copy under a different owner dir), the session names more than one owner and stays unresolved, so it counts as foreign. A session pruned from both the disk and the store still falls back to foreign.\n\nWhy: the D-037 witness is a fact about where the CLI wrote the transcript. Prove ordinary bug candidate screening, stale dupl… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002765 — Add typed declared work outcome to nested completion evidence; persist/project through work_items:complete/get, keep legacy unknown, extend exact completion_stats with outcome counts and honest label… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002766 — After P-001 and P-002, run current-build tests and scoped canary, record outcome, coverage, limitations, and release position without historical mass mutation. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Attributable intake.** New non-observation improvement captures are born with pending admission or an existing recorded urgent/assigned bypass. Judge failure uses bounded fail-open and never loses a filing.\n\n**R-2 — Duplicate and freshness screen.** Existing file-time candidates, stale-evidence verdict and build evidence reach the promoter before a bug self-pull. Search degradation stays explicit.\n\n**R-3 — Honest outcome accounting.** Extend payload._completionEvidence with a typed declared outcome for new durable change versus verified-existing, duplicate, invalid/expected and other no-new-change closure. Missing legacy outcome is unknown; authority=committed remains evidence sufficiency. A scoped canary proves current-build behavior without mass backfill; fleet rev7 and worker ceiling remain intact.\n\n## Design\n\nReuse work_items.admission/admitted_by, dedupCandidates/dedupVerdict/freshnessEnvelope, current promoter/fail-open runner, and _completionEvidence.
