Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-13, after item-dropped): bar_snapshot_rubric_revision_mismatch, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_mapping_dropped_only. Next repair: Before mutating BAR state, run dev:pipeline_position { path: \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/with-plan-lock.ts\", marker: \"synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision\" } to distinguish a stale serving build from a live guard. If the synchronizer is not deployed, land/redeploy it first; otherwise re-seed or amend atomically so subject and rubric revision pins agree.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nAll nine outcomes remain open. P-007/WI-10002829 has a fresh packaged release GUI with private staging discovery. Native popup results for the pinned visible plan are 5767ms, 2457ms and 2919ms, each over the unchanged 1500ms budget. The latest run splits 2919ms into 449ms detail mount, 1447ms request-to-parsed-response, 24ms data-state update, about 637ms further content readiness and about 170ms preview render. Source phase tests pass; no ten-run acceptance or shipment claim. Native discovery bug EI-24161953656319715 is resolved. One stage restart took roughly 11 CPU-active minutes; root-cause item EI-24165259633128552 is assigned. Other plan outcomes and rubric amendment 1142917 remain open; evidence and limits are in docs/evidence/papercusp-performance-remediation-2026-09-23.md.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: This session continues P-007: pin goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 on the same named native build, locate the measured request and mount costs in existing paths, make a durable improvement with project tests, then repeat native acceptance; continue the remaining independent P-001 through P-008 lanes and final P-009 shipment. The held live gate lane remains excluded.)\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10002823 — Restore and guard the existing backend performance producer; reuse EI-22365947616851657. Trace the watchdog collector/flag/persistence path without manually inserting a sample that hides the problem.… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002824 — Reuse and verify EI-24045346484356708 and EI-24022555028936462 in the affected runtime. Preserve indexed primary search plus bounded literal fallback and actual hook request compatibility. Validate c… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002825 — Use the saved bg-host CPU profiles to fix local Git spawn cost and inspector observer overhead. Extend the existing spawner sidecar with cancellation/progress acknowledgment as required; never strip … <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002826 — Profile the recursive lineage query and memory lexical ranking with representative inputs, bounded EXPLAIN ANALYZE and candidate counts. Reuse existing identity edges and retrieval admission. Test an… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002827 — Remove repeated full attention-feed construction from counts/refs and profile slow coordination/orientation stages. Extend current cachedRead/single-flight and derived-read surfaces, preserve invalid… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002828 — Diagnose memory admission and embedding phase deadlines, including missing lock-table fallback. Budget work end-to-end across queue, embed, lexical and render phases; coalesce identical work and canc… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002829 — Repair the recorded plan-popup regression and missing Web Vitals in the existing packaged Tauri/WDIO suite. Instrument data retrieval, Vditor preparation and render phases; verify multiple cold/warm … <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002830 — Resolve gateway/proxy failures and portal watchdog notification timeouts; quantify repeated migration/ref-announcement/ingest work and historical account polling. Preserve backup migration rendezvous… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002831 — Publish the comparative verification report after P-001 through P-008 have evidence or accountable dispositions. Run relevant regression suites and native acceptance, repeat fixed-window telemetry un… <!-- P-009 -->\n## Summary and priorities\n\nThe goal is faster app interactions and agent operations with unchanged correctness and useful recall. Audit numbers are historical baselines from September 23 around 22:00 UTC, not assertions about the runtime at implementation time. Refresh the specific behavior before changing it; another lane may already have fixed or deployed it.\n\n| Wave | Items | Work | Result |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 — Establish control | P-001, P-002 | Restore the existing performance-history producer; verify the staged search and hook-schema fixes in their actual serving processes | Trustworthy baseline, indexed search, accepted hook payloads |\n| 2 — Remove expensive work | P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006 | Cancellation-safe background spawning, low-overhead profiling, lineage/lexical query optimization, shared attention reads, bounded context retrieval | Shorter waits without weakening lineage, counts, recall, cancellation or lock safety |\n| 3 — Prove user-facing improvement | P-007, P-008, P-009 | Native popup/load budgets; gateway, proxy, portal and repeated-background-work diagnosis; comparative verification and shipment | Repeatable desktop responsiveness, explained failures and measured end-to-end results |\n\nP-001 and P-002 are the first implementation priority and can prepare independently. Waves express delivery order, not artificial start gates: profiling, fixture preparation and independent UI work may proceed before another lane ships. Each source lane verifies in staging/current-build. Only P-009 is an all-lanes integration barrier. This document does not launch parallel agents or select a future implementation fleet.\n\n### Proposed measurable targets\n\nThese are proposed engineering acceptance targets for named representative workloads, not measured outcomes or guaranteed speedups. P-001 freezes the corpus, request mix, concurrency, build and measurement definitions. If that validation shows a proposed target is inappropriate, record the evidence and revise it before optimization; never silently relax it after a miss.\n\n| Surface | Audit evidence | Proposed target |\n|---|---|---|\n| Session-search DB execution | 4.975 s mean in one short interval; not p95 | p95 <= 1 s on the representative search corpus; indexed primary plan and bounded literal fill; recall fixtures unchanged |\n| Identity-lineage DB execution | 2.163 s mean in one short interval; not p95 | p95 <= 500 ms on representative candidate sets, including cyclic and consult-lineage cases |\n| Attention count/reference server resolve | Warning maxima 4.45 s / 6.49 s; not p95 | Warm-cache p95 <= 250 ms; cold-build p95 <= 1 s on the representative workspace; exact counts and correct invalidation |\n| Agent orientation end-to-end | Stored p95 46.126 s | p95 <= 5 s for the frozen normal request profile; all required obligations and facts preserved |\n| Background main-loop responsiveness | Profile trigger p95 951 ms, plus substantial spawn/profiler frames | p95 <= 100 ms for representative normal multi-repo activity; report worst stalls and profiler-on/off overhead separately |\n| Useful context delivery | 2 s prompt deadline repeatedly reached | At least 95% of eligible normal-workload turns receive context within the existing 2 s deadline; retrieval quality matches the frozen baseline |\n| Native desktop | Popup 1.798–4.364 s against 1.5 s budget | Existing budgets: popup <= 1.5 s, FCP <= 3 s, LCP <= 4 s; expected metrics present |\n| Producer health | Backend history latest Aug 24 | Samples arrive at the configured cadence; alarm after two missed expected samples; injected producer/write failures detected |\n\nEligible context turns exclude intentionally disabled or inapplicable recall, but admission shedding and deadline omissions count as delivery failures. UI timings, server resolver timings, DB execution and end-to-end calls stay separate. Historical means/maxima in this table must not be used as a like-for-like comparison to the proposed p95 goals.\n\n## Background\n\nAvi requested a thorough performance audit using logs and a plan for fixing the findings, and approved route A during the audit. Avi then requested a written improvement plan and summary [turn:self]. Evidence was gathered on 2026-09-23: six-hour route/tool telemetry; service journals with windows up to 24 hours; current pg_stat_statements deltas and EXPLAIN; saved CPU profiles; desktop WDIO results; and current staging/release source. The report names every measured population, bounded window and unresolved cause.\n\nThe September 4 application-performance plan and July 26 database-performance plan are shipped. This follow-on plan reuses their infrastructure and existing fixes rather than reopening completed scope. EI-24045346484356708 (session search) and EI-24022555028936462 (hook schema) are done in the ledger but their old behavior appears in the measured runtime. EI-22365947616851657 already tracks stale performance history. desktop-performance-suite-2026-07-20 provides the existing native verification path.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Trustworthy measurements.** The existing backend performance series records fresh, timestamped samples; a stopped or failing producer is explicitly detected. Before/after evidence identifies build, host, sample bounds and metric definitions; missing data remains unknown.\n\n**R-2 — Existing fixes reach the affected runtime.** Live session search stops using the unbounded substring OR scan while preserving tested recall, and actual hook payloads containing glance_stale are accepted. Existing fixes are reused; source completion is distinguished from runtime verification.\n\n**R-3 — Responsive background execution.** Git execution preserves cancellation and lock lifetime without putting expensive process-launch work on the busy background loop. Diagnostic profiling has measured and bounded observer overhead and does not amplify the stalls being measured.\n\n**R-4 — Bounded database work.** Identity-lineage and memory lexical retrieval are profiled and optimized where the measured costs originate while preserving lineage exclusion, scope and retrieval semantics. Comparable plans and timings establish improvement; index additions alone do not constitute acceptance.\n\n**R-5 — Fast attention and context reads.** Attention counts/refs reuse efficient shared aggregation, and coordination reads avoid repeated expensive work. Before/after cold/warm and concurrent measurements cover the observed slow routes while preserving exact counts and invalidation semantics.\n\n**R-6 — Useful memory within its deadline.** Memory injection can deliver useful recall within its prompt deadline under representative concurrency, with bounded upstream work, truthful degraded states and cancellation/coalescing. Increasing the deadline or dropping recall is not an acceptable substitute for an evidenced fix.\n\n**R-7 — Desktop budgets hold.** The existing packaged-desktop suite measures plan popup at or below 1500ms, FCP at or below 3000ms and LCP at or below 4000ms on the accepted build and scenario. Expected metrics are recorded, and missing values cannot silently pass.\n\n**R-8 — Secondary performance leads are resolved with evidence.** Gateway/proxy failures, portal watchdog timeouts, repeated failing background work, migration rendezvous waits, historical polling and expensive diagnostic scans receive confirmed causes or explicitly justified non-defect dispositions. Backup, security and correctness invariants remain intact.\n\n**R-9 — Verified outcome.** A final comparable before/after report accounts for every finding, all regression tests and known limitations, and separately verifies shipment where required. No universal speedup or fixed-runtime claim is made from source tests alone.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend existing mechanisms; the work mapping below defines acceptance ownership.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002 | live |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-008 | live |\n| R-9 | P-009 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Measurement and existing corrections\n\n- **P-001** `done` Restore and guard the existing backend performance producer; reuse EI-22365947616851657. Trace the watchdog collector/flag/persistence path without manually inserting a sample that hides the problem. Establish fixed-window baselines for tools/routes, query costs, loop delays and desktop results. Test producer silence and persistence failure detection. Importance: high. — note: ← WI-10002823 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Reuse and verify EI-24045346484356708 and EI-24022555028936462 in the affected runtime. Preserve indexed primary search plus bounded literal fallback and actual hook request compatibility. Validate current source tests and live behavior. Any shipment work first reads LIVE_GATE_OPS ownership and follows its existing owner; do not create a second gate fixer. Importance: high. — note: ← WI-10002824 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Measured blocking and repeated work\n\n- **P-003** `done` Use the saved bg-host CPU profiles to fix local Git spawn cost and inspector observer overhead. Extend the existing spawner sidecar with cancellation/progress acknowledgment as required; never strip AbortSignal to force sidecar routing. Benchmark spawn latency and event-loop delay, test child termination before lock release, and distinguish profiler cost from application cost. Smaller samples are exploratory. Use repeated windows to detect jitter, without load-generating against production merely to fill a sample.\n4. **Test invariants first.** Each implementation lands with meaningful regression tests in the existing suite. Search: literal/no-match recall and ordering. Lineage: ancestor, alias, consult source and cycle rules. Spawning: cancellation, timeout, child exit before lock release. Verify queue recovery, lack of accumulating obsolete work, bounded memory growth and no change in correctness/error rates. This is a targeted regression soak, not proof against every leak.\n7. **Publish evidence and ship separately.** P-009 compares all proposed targets to measurements and gives each finding a fixed, disproven or explicitly deferred disposition with an owner/reference. No unresolved requirement is silently treated as passed. Use existing release ownership for final promotion/deployment, then recheck the affected serving behavior. No live peer claim is taken over.\n- **F1/F2:** verify installation/runtime correction first; a source patch already marked done is not a new implementation task.\n- **F3/F4:** medium-risk cancellation and diagnostic changes require child-lifecycle tests and measured observer cost. Never bypass AbortSignal or disable safeguards.\n- **F5/F6/F7/F10:** query/cache/recall changes require correctness fixtures and realistic population sizes. Do not interpret kill success or admission terminal as OS-exit proof. Do not kill a live shared sidecar merely because one client connection fails. Recovery should first revoke the original connection generation and join its pending exec in the still-live server; use kernel containment cleanup only after the exact server incarnation is confirmed dead. Bind execution to the preflight server/connection generation to reject reconnect races before spawn. Missing/failed observation must retain the lease. Ambiguous mutation outcomes must not be retried locally. Mutating signal-bearing Git stays local until disconnection-before-admission/PID, server death, generation mismatch and no-duplicate-mutation cases are verified.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-002 — P-003 warm profiler policy uses existing gate and monitor tick; bounds are explicit\nDate: 2026-09-24\nMeasured before choosing: saved runs 19280662/19281929 and evidence doc 10:55/11:13 sections show 100Hz overlap retains useful stacks and avoids recurring V8 map reconstruction (~0.05ms warm start versus 81–144ms ordinary start), with ~0.81% idle CPU and ~5.4% loaded CPU observed in short fixtures. Node25.9 installed v8.startCpuProfile and public docs expose no sample-limit option. Extend existing lag monitor/capture seam with one warm recorder and no additional recurring timer/service/flag. Use100Hz; rotate successor anchor before retiring predecessor on monitor ticks; retain at most2 anchors plus1 foreground. Gate false/error, monitor stop, unsafe p95, and overdue maintenance revoke/disconnect the recorder and cancel its foreground. Do not serialize overdue anchor just to discard it. Gate reads stay single-flight, and pending/stale reads cannot keep recording indefinitely. Artifact cadence/retention remain existing settings. Distinguish startup/rotation/capture observer cost from app frames. Rotation is a SOFT bound: main-thread stall can delay cleanup; never claim a hard native-memory or duration cap. Real product-path lifecycle/fidelity and sustained-overhead verification are required before claiming acceptance. This policy is source work, not a production performance or shipment claim.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-003 — Staging cutover completes guarded target migrations before stopping the ready host\nDate: 2026-09-24\nMeasured: 2026-09-24 source host-bootstrap.ts waitForBootMigrationGate applies migrations on request-only startup; db-boot-migrate.ts applyPendingMigrationsNow accepts an exact sqlDir and preserves backup rendezvous, reservation, preapply lint, deployed-code and destructive-snapshot guards. Existing green-checkpoint.ts ensureMigrationsCurrent already reuses this seam for a pinned candidate. EI-24180022773715880 observed the old staging API stopped before pending1223 could cross a backup-held rendezvous. Extend existing staging-sync under its checkout flock: after target lint and host bundle preparation, run applyPendingMigrationsNow against that target before requesting dev:restart. Refuse cutover on null/failed results. Do not add a raw runner, disable the backup lock, or rely on an idle-lock observation. After all pinned migrations are applied, the existing no-pending boot path handles a backup that begins between preflight and restart without executing new files unlocked. EI-24180437038891110's peer-owned migration lint is complementary, not the availability fix. Verify ordering/failure with project shell tests and the post-preflight backup race with real PostgreSQL.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-004 — Browser PTY agent traffic uses the stable MCP proxy; request callbacks stay on the source runtime\nDate: 2026-09-26\nMeasured: P-007 native popup runs r71-r80 on staging build c6679b912a and PID 2765610 passed 6/10 under 1500ms. Of the 9 generations created between 06:39 and 11:51 local, only 2 are papercusp's full tree: v1-314312cb at 06:39 (95 sources, 20.7 GiB) and v1-c328f2c6 at 11:51 (95 sources, 21.6 GiB). Each followed a real root package-lock.json commit (git log: 09:03 16123e093f and 11:33 832a0d9115; the 06:39 one has an earlier input). The other 7 are pot trees of 0.1 to 1.1 GiB. So the generation key is not churning. The cost is one full ~21 GiB ext4-to-XFS copy (no reflink across filesystems) per papercusp lockfile change, plus each materialization into ext4 checkouts. The claim 'nine ~17 GB generations in 5 h' in P-012's text and in the owner-facing summary was wrong. P-012 importance is effectively normal, not high. The durable fix is unchanged in shape: build the new generation as a reflink clone of the previous papercusp generation on the same XFS store, then copy only the changed package dirs. Validate exactness with the existing tree manifest.\n\n### D-012 — P-013: expensive aggregate list targets get a longer, still-bounded bridged coalesce window\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Measured by su-fa4c1948 (WI-10004929 checkpoint 19:10Z). One SSE subscriber on :3070 for 180 s received 51 workItems.summary + 51 workItems.byHarness bare invalidations (median gap ~2 s) during 199 work_items writes. Cause: invalidation-bus emitBridgedTarget/flushBridge pass maxStalenessMs = bridgeCoalesceWindowMs (hard-capped at 2 s) alongside the 90 s minSleepMs, so under sustained writes each of the 5 bridged sources emits a trailing event about every 2 s and every open Work Items panel re-fetches summary + page about every 3.5 s. Ruling: keep the bus-wide 2 s default and its bounded-staleness invariant. Add an opt-in host policy that gives specific EXPENSIVE aggregate list targets (workItems.summary, workItems.byHarness) a longer trailing window, 10 s, with a hard library maximum of 15 s. Staleness stays bounded, so the final write is never hidden for more than 10 s, and per-panel refetch drops from about 1 per 3.5 s to at most 1 per 10 s per source. Rejected: raising the global cap (it weakens freshness for cheap queries); client-side debounce only (it leaves N clients x 5 sources unbounded). Libs/generic/sync is a submodule: lock the provider and consumer halves together (EI-24804034237477602).\n\n### D-013 — Correction: P-015(b) premise — WI-10003469 shipped a TTL fix, not a delta fix, and it IS live\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Correction by su-fa4c1948 of its own 19:05Z finding, which was recorded on WI-10005005 and in the P-015(b) text (\"verify its delta fix is actually live\"). FALSE PREMISE: WI-10003469 never added delta or prefix storage. Its fix (packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/payload-spool.ts, DEFAULT_PAYLOAD_SPOOL_TTL_MS, comment at lines 57-74) shortened the UNREFERENCED-payload TTL from 2 h to 2 min, so a row is written and deleted within one 15-min checkpoint cycle. That removes the full-page images from the GC DELETE and the VACUUM visibility pass, which were 91% of that table's WAL. It was never meant to shrink per-insert bytes. MEASURED 19:23Z (census of all 101 live rows, all tenants): median expires_at - created_at = 120.0 s; oldest unreferenced row 138 s; 8 pinned; avg body 734 kB; relpersistence 'p'. So the TTL fix is live and working as designed. The ~426 kB WAL per insert (79 inserts/60 s, ~12% of cluster WAL at 19:05Z) is the expected cost of storing a ~700 kB body, not evidence of a broken fix. What remains open for (b) is a NEW design choice, not a verification. Options, all unimplemented: (1) make the table UNLOGGED, which writes no WAL; rows survive a clean restart but are truncated on crash recovery; this needs the gateway owner's ruling on whether the 30-min durable lease must survive a PG crash. (2) Chunked content-addressed storage, since about 95% of each body repeats the previous turn's. (3) Skip spooling on the synchronous path. Recorded so no one chases a nonexistent delta path.\n\n### D-014 — P-015(e) not adopted: keep wal_compression=pglz (measured A/B says zstd stores MORE WAL here)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Ruling by su-fa4c1948 while carrying P-015. Measured: libs/generic/resource-profile/src/index.ts:417-423 (databaseTuningToSettings) records WI-10003444's live A/B on this cluster (2026-09-27, exact per-image ratio from pg_waldump -b). Full-page images were stored at 0.431 of raw with pglz, 0.449 with zstd and 0.512 with lz4. Embedded PG 18.3 is built without lz4/zstd and refuses them with a FATAL at startup. The live value (pg_settings 19:27Z: wal_compression=pglz, sourcefile /etc/postgresql/18/main/conf.d/10-papercusp-autotune.conf) is generated from that profile, so a hand ALTER SYSTEM would also fight the generator. The (e) premise, that zstd reduces write amplification, is contradicted by measurement, so (e) is not adopted and the setting stays pglz. Reversible: revisit only if P-017's CPU attribution shows WAL-compression CPU among the top consumers. zstd's advantage is speed, not ratio, and would then need a per-host capability probe so embedded builds keep pglz. This narrows P-015's scope by one sub-item; the other sub-items (a, b per D-013, c, d, f) remain.\n\n### D-015 — P-015(c) satisfied by the existing price_table_version gate (steady-state re-pricing writes nothing)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Ruling by su-fa4c1948 while carrying P-015.\n\nMeasured [observed 19:22:36-19:23:36Z, 60 s pg_stat_user_tables + pg_stat_statements delta]: harness_shared.agent_usage_samples n_tup_upd 3,332,895 -> 3,332,895 (zero), and the reprice UPDATE's call count stayed at 579. The \"3.3M updates across 655k rows\" in the P-015(c) text is the CUMULATIVE counter since the 2026-09-29 stats reset, not a rate. The 579 reprice calls (2.88M rows, 7.2 GB WAL total) are the WI-10004517 backfill, which has completed.\n\nCode (re-read 19:26Z): packages/operator-core/lib/interactive-usage/reprice-usage-samples.ts:196-197 selects only `cost_source IS DISTINCT FROM 'provider' AND (price_table_version IS NULL OR < v OR > v)`, which uses the partial index from migration 1280-agent-usage-price-table-version.sql. Rows already at the current version are never touched, so steady-state writes are zero.\n\nRuling: no code change for (c). It is satisfied by the existing version gate.\n\nResidual, accepted: each future price-table version bump re-stamps every non-provider row once (~655k rows at ~2.5 kB WAL each, ~1.6 GB per bump). It is episodic, not steady-state. Skipping rows whose cost is unchanged at a bump would need the version stamp moved off the row, which is not justified at the current bump frequency. Re-open only if bumps become frequent.\n\n### D-016 — P-015 re-ranked by measured WAL share; (a) gets no session_turns redesign; (b) is the dominant lever\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Measured by su-fa4c1948 (WI-10005005).\n\nCumulative pg_stat_statements since the 2026-09-29 reset, as a share of top-level statement WAL [observed 19:43Z]:\n- (b) gateway_payload_blobs INSERT 27.2% (65 GB, 177k calls, ~396 kB/row), plus its GC DELETE 4.3% (10 GB) = 31.5%.\n- resource_governor_admissions UPDATE 10.4% + INSERT 4.7% = 15.1% (WI-10003465, su-360fb18f).\n- adv_sessions SET launch_spec 4.3% (WI-10004843, su-f35e5c5a).\n- (a) session_turns: embedding UPDATE 4.1%; owner backfill 3.4%; chunked_at 0.9%; inserts ~0.7%.\n- (c) re-pricing 2.3% (finished backfill, D-015); (d) last_surfaced_at bump 2.2% (fixed by migration 1312).\n\nSteady-state windows [observed]. 120 s at 19:36:26Z: cluster WAL 2.0 MB/s; session_turns embedding UPDATE 63 calls / 8.4 MB (~3.5%); the owner backfill and chunked_at UPDATE wrote ZERO. 90 s at 19:39:16Z: 94% of WAL attributed to statements; one session_turns bulk INSERT burst took 26% of the window (11,949 FPIs), but that statement totals only 279 MB cumulatively.\n\nFalse premise in the P-015(a) text: \"~3 s and ~6.6 MB WAL per session_turns insert\" was the owner-repair UPDATE (3,221 ms, 2.54 MB per call; backfillSessionOwners in packages/operator-core/lib/search/session-ingest.ts already has an IS DISTINCT FROM guard). It was a one-off repair burst, not an insert cost. None of session_turns' 194,981 updates was HOT. Each post-insert UPDATE changes an indexed column (text_embedding -> HNSW; owner -> owner_ts_idx; chunked_at -> session_turns_unchunked_idx predicate), so HOT is impossible by design.\n\nRuling for (a): no session_turns schema redesign now. Moving embeddings to a side table, or embedding before insert, would save only the GIN/btree re-insert plus the heap copy on the embedding UPDATE. The HNSW insert remains. That is roughly 1-2% of cluster WAL, below the cost of a search-reader refactor. Re-open if the steady-state embedding UPDATE share rises above ~10%.\n\nRuling for the order of the remaining work: (b) comes first. WI-10003469 shipped the 2-minute TTL (D-013), not a fix for the per-row WAL. Every turn still writes its full ~400-680 kB body to logged storage, and that item's own title records that 95% of those bytes repeat the previous turn's body. Durable options for (b), to be evaluated against the blob readers (ref_count>0 rows): content-delta/prefix storage, an UNLOGGED spool for unreferenced rows, or not spooling bodies that are never referenced. Checkpoint cadence is not a lever: checkpoint_timeout is already 900 s, and 162 of 191 checkpoints were timed.\n\n### D-017 — P-015(b): store gateway spool bodies as content-defined chunks + zstd (durability unchanged)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Ruling by su-fa4c1948 (WI-10005005).\n\nMeasured [observed 19:52Z, .papercusp/scratch/p015/cdc-probe.mts, read-only over all 120 live spool rows spanning 730 s]: raw bodies 78.3 MB (avg 652 kB); pglz TOAST stores 42.8 MB. Whole-body zstd would store 26.9 MB (-37%). Content-defined chunking (gear hash, avg 8 kB) + zstd per NEW chunk stores 6.6 MB (-84%); median turn is 95.7% duplicate chunks, p90 is a cold/new conversation (100% new). Also observed: no production code calls spool.read() (only tests), so nothing reads the bodies back today.\n\nRuling:\n1. New table harness_shared.gateway_payload_chunks (workspace_id, chunk_hash bytea[32], zstd bytes, raw_length, last_ref_at). Logged, written in the SAME transaction as the manifest, so D-004 durability (capless-inference-gateway-2026-08-28) is unchanged.\n2. gateway_payload_blobs stays the receipt-facing identity: key = sha256 of the whole body, ref_count, TTL, pinned grace and sweep rules are unchanged. A chunked row carries chunk_hashes bytea[] and empty bytes. get() reassembles, decompresses and re-verifies the sha256; any missing chunk reads as not-found.\n3. Chunk liveness: a chunk is kept while ANY manifest row references it, plus a 30-minute grace since last_ref_at so an idle conversation's next turn still dedupes. A writer refreshes last_ref_at only when it is older than half the grace, so a hot conversation updates almost no chunk rows. last_ref_at is deliberately NOT indexed (refreshes stay HOT); fillfactor 80.\n4. The chunk sweep runs after the manifest sweep, row/byte bounded, and re-checks last_ref_at under READ COMMITTED so a concurrent writer's refresh wins.\n5. The chunker is domain-free and goes in @papercusp/artifact-registry (libs/generic), the lib that already owns content addressing.\n\nNot adopted: UNLOGGED (D-013 option) and skipping the spool for synchronous requests. Both change D-004's crash-durability contract, which belongs to the gateway design owner; chunking reaches -84% without touching it.\n\nAcceptance: pg_stat_statements wal_bytes/turn for the spool statements over a 60-120 s delta window before vs after, plus TOAST growth; the integration test proves round-trip, dedupe across turns, and chunk GC safety.\n\n### D-018 — P-012: a ctime-only (or inode-only) record mismatch is reused only after a content comparison\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Ruling by su-fa4c1948 (WI-10004927).\n\nMeasured [observed 07:06-07:33Z, checkpoint WI-10004927 07:33Z]: the live P-012 incremental copy kept 0 of 208,196 files (copied_bytes 8.67 GB) because its trust key is an exact match over all 10 record fields, including ctime. On this host, papercusp-staging.current hard-links the canonical node_modules (setup-release-checkout default NODE_MODULES_COPY_MODE=hardlink), and every staging refresh changes nlink on about 208k inodes, so the kernel bumps their ctime about every 11-12 min. Same source, 21 min apart: 231,363/231,363 rows matched on content fields and inode; only 23,167 matched with ctime.\n\nRuling:\n1. Keep the exact 10-field match (with the racy-window floor) as the fast path.\n2. A regular file whose (path, type, mode, uid, gid, size, mtime) equals a predecessor record but whose ctime or inode differs is a CANDIDATE. It is kept only if sha256(live file) equals sha256(seed file), the reflinked predecessor copy. Otherwise it is copied. This keeps the in-place same-size/same-mtime rewrite guard (the 'caught by ctime' test), because the rewrite changes content and fails the comparison.\n3. Do NOT drop ctime from the key without a content check, and do NOT add nlink to the key: a link churn and a rewrite can coincide, and staging's create-then-remove leaves nlink unchanged.\n4. Rejected: changing staging to copy mode (canonical is ext4 with no reflink, so a 17 GB copy per refresh is worse); storing per-file digests at capture time (reads the whole source every generation even when nothing changed; candidate-only hashing reads only mismatched files).\n\nCost: reads, never writes, the candidate bytes twice (live ext4, mostly page-cached, plus the XFS seed), instead of writing about 8.7 GB and losing reflink sharing on a 97%-full /mnt/data. INCREMENTAL gains a verified=N field.\n\n### D-019 — Correction: D-018 premise — the 07:09Z kept=0 came from a cross-repository predecessor; rank predecessors by tree overlap\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Correction by su-fa4c1948 of its own D-018 premise, plus a ruling (WI-10004927).\n\nFALSE PREMISE in D-018: it says the 07:09Z nightly generation v1-0c9806da kept 0 of 208,196 files BECAUSE the trust key includes ctime. That was wrong for that run. Measured 08:10Z: v1-0c9806da's predecessor was v1-25b8ea9c, a 7-tree generation from a DIFFERENT repository (trees apps/desktop, libs/hive-app-seam, packages/template-checks; none exist in papercusp). Against its root node_modules .source-records (41,444 rows), 0 of 207,877 papercusp regular files match on path+inode and 8 match on path+size+mtime. kept=0 was decided by the cross-repo pick, independent of ctime. Papercusp's own previous generation v1-5a60f206 (01:45Z, 95 trees) was available and skipped.\n\nRoot cause: dependency_generation_find_reusable_predecessor (apps/operator/bin/release/dependency-generation.sh) ranks candidates only by created time among generations with the same closure fingerprint and scope. The closure fingerprint is the same for every repo running this script version, and /mnt/data/papercusp-dependency-generations is shared by every pot's gate (95-, 37-, 10-, 8-, 7-, 5-, 2- and 1-tree generations seen today). So the newest generation from ANY repo wins.\n\nWhat survives: D-018 is still needed. The ctime-churn measurement (same source 21 min apart: 208,196 rows differ in ctime only) shows a same-repo predecessor would also have kept ~0 without content verification. Both fixes are required.\n\nRuling: predecessor selection ranks compatible candidates by (1) exact tree matches (rel+fingerprint) with the current before-manifest, (2) shared tree rels, (3) created time. A candidate with zero shared rels is never selected. This uses data the script already has (before_manifest and each candidate's .tree-manifest). There is no new marker field, so existing generations stay eligible.\n\n### D-020 — P-011 separates recorded integration layer from actual live evidence plane\nDate: 2026-10-02\nMeasured: libs/test-config/src/execution-details.ts:14–27, read 2026-10-02 09:02Z: executable ledger layers are unit/integration/e2e/llm/browser. packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy.ts:1464–1529, read09:01Z: requiredTestLayers compares recorded testLayer; :1566–1591 separately enforces exact live/deployed requiredEvidence tokens against current evidencePlane. P011@1 put live in requiredTestLayers and omitted an explicit live plane. WI-10005390 appended PERF-OCT1-P011-MEMORY@2, fingerprint6059e251ea51a61458afd5075a8190a60e1f1139d28c55784b4ff12d2c624010: integration layer plus live evidence plane, identical behavior/falsifier/resource and functionality requirements. Private R2/R24/cache proofs remain scoped; none is promoted to actual live acceptance. Existing suite spec-test-adequacy.test.ts ledger20502898:105PASS/0FAIL/0SKIP, including the live-plane guard which rejects tree proof and stale live proof. Retained-owner distinctions, live/current-build measurement, R8/R9, independent acceptance and shipment remain open. This is declaration repair preserving source-backed requirements, not fulfillment or a scope relaxation.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-021 — A child work-item has no scoped-contribution close: it closes on its WHOLE resolved clause set or stays open\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource-verified 2026-10-03 ~05:25Z by su-fa4c1948 (independent contract review requested by su-7db4f, msg coord-send-d618eb60…; covers WI-10004890#1156774 and WI-10005816).\n\nMechanism: work_items:complete enforces EVERY clause in the item's resolved behavior contract — all explicit work_item_spec_revision_edges (any namespace) PLUS the clauses owned by its stamped sourcePlanItemIds. Each clause is graded whole by evaluateSpecTestAdequacy. Evidence is filtered to this item's own bindings (workItemIds:[id]), but the clause's obligations (layers, falsifiability, disclosed gaps) are never partitioned per contributor. The only non-enforcing exits are: no enforced clauses (applicable:false), a clause with proof floor 'none', a non-eligible (report-only) plan namespace, and the non-code kind exit — which itself refuses an item that changed source or submits executable proof.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts:3619 calls specTestAdequacyCompletionGate; packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/spec-test-adequacy-gate.ts:471 resolveWorkItemBehaviorContract, :500 enforcedClausesOf(contract) -> every eligible clause, :510-525 non-code kind refuses on source changes or executable-proof submission, :617 evidence read scoped workItemIds:[input.workItem.id]; packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/behavior-contract-resolver.ts:214 all edges for the item, :224 stamp namespace back-compat leg, :243 clauses of stamp.planItemIds. Read at staging working tree 2026-10-03 ~05:20Z. No grep hit for any scoped-contribution / partial-clause close construct in packages/operator-core/lib.\n\nRuling for this plan:\n1. WI-10005816 (and any other P-011 child stamped to P-011 or edged to PERF-OCT1-P011-MEMORY@2) stays OPEN (wip/blocked) until the full P-011 clause passes on its own bindings. A scoped baseline is checkpoint/progress evidence, not a terminal close.\n2. If a real scoped deliverable must close on its own, the only legitimate route is a plan-contract change: give that scope its own plan item and clause, and have the child stamped and edged ONLY to that clause, recorded as a Decision with activation re-audit and derived-item provenance. P-011's clause and its live-plane requirement stay unchanged.\n3. Not allowed: re-kinding to task, retracting or not creating edges, or dropping bindings to escape the full clause. Each of these weakens acceptance to buy a close.\n\n### D-022 — Closeout: every open item disposed on 2026-10-13 measurements; papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12 is now the governing performance plan\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13. Ruling by su-982534a7 under papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12 P-011 (WI-6554700010009311), owner directive #1744 (AUTO).\n\nThis plan has been idle since 2026-10-03. The 2026-10-12 audit (papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12) re-measured the system and is now the governing performance plan. Every open item here is disposed below from measurements taken 2026-10-13 04:50-05:12Z. pg_stat_statements has accumulated since 2026-10-09 13:43Z. Deltas are same-window samples.\n\nContext that applies to several items: :3070 (papercusp-dev-api) has served d740fc3802 since 2026-10-02 12:05Z. bg-host and staging :3170 (dcdf6b4e30) run current staging. A fix that is \"live on bg-host/staging\" is therefore not yet on :3070. The green-checkpoint gate is held by another live agent and is not this lane.\n\n- P-006 (WI-10002828) memory admission and embed deadlines: done in substance. Its checkpoint records the root cause fixed (turn-start recall now goes through withOptionalMemoryAdmission), R6 adequacy PASS, test_run 20375704. The item stayed blocked only on this plan's acceptance bars, which this ruling retires. Disposition: dropped with that evidence. No defect remains open.\n- P-008 (WI-10002830) gateway/proxy failures and the Oct 1 long UPDATE: the owner-map repair is verified on its item. The historical UPDATE's wait mechanism could not be reproduced, and the item's own later sweeps did not reproduce it either. Today's dominant UPDATE is the tool_invocations metadata backfill (queryid 4452249180979902157, mean 1,156 ms, max 342 s). Its fix (WI-6554700010008556, bounded window) is live on bg-host and staging and reaches :3070 with the next deploy. Disposition: dropped. The live part is tracked by the done fix plus the pending deploy.\n- P-010 (WI-10004889) global plan-item coverage scan: the fix is in the tree (ordered stamp read matching work_items_plan_item_stamp_idx, plus planItemRefs/planSlug-filtered paths). Matched same-window A/B, 05:04:17-05:07:18Z: fixed statement 2801009152787240793 (bg-host) 5 calls, 250 ms/call; old unordered statement -2442231371504820178, 4 calls at 2,707 ms/call. pg_stat_activity attributes every old call to the :3070 workers (pcusp:org-admin:p3152231/p1282542/p2282359) and the fixed one to bg-host p2604638. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) of the fixed read: index scan, 8,708 rows, 274 ms. Disposition: dropped as complete in source. The remaining 2.7 s calls disappear when :3070 is deployed.\n- P-011 (WI-10004890) service memory attribution: measured at process level. :3070 runs 6 cluster workers at 1.8-3.1 GB RSS each (cgroup anon 16.0 GB) plus a 0.85 GB primary. Workers are 25-86 min old, consistent with the 3,200 MB watchdog recycle. bg-host is 4.9 GB and staging 2.0 GB. The per-worker growth is exactly WI-10004801 (blocked on the :3070 deploy of its reader-narrowing fixes). Disposition: dropped here; the residue is WI-10004801.\n- P-012 (WI-10004927) dependency-generation full copies: D-018/D-019 code is verified on its item (91/91, mutants caught). Live, papercusp generations now carry a predecessor and arrive about 4-5 per day (14:06, 19:15 and 00:00 local on 10-12/13), against 9 in 5 h on 10-01. Per-generation IO bytes were not re-measured, because the INCREMENTAL lines go to the gate run's stderr and no retained log was found. Disposition: dropped with that gap stated.\n- P-016 unowned reliability failures of 10-01: not reproducible now. Every named pot's green-checkpoint shows lastVerdict green (calendar, readinglist, hello-world-hive and panda-gallery observed today; quartermaster and papercusp-public-site on 10-06). presence-transition-sweep and legacy-needs-human-reconcile fired at 04:54-04:55Z today with no error, and dead-citation-sweep's item is done. Both routine failures were lock_timeout. The contention class is tracked by WI-6554700010009563 (advisory-lock round trips). Disposition: dropped. The three EIs get this evidence as a comment.\n- P-017 steady-state service CPU: from the P-002 cgroup samples over the last 5 h, bg-host averages 0.17 cores (1.2-1.6 on 10-01, so resolved). The :3070 service cgroup averages 3.96 cores. A 30 s per-process delta puts about 2.4 cores in its 6 workers (0.29-0.59 core each) and 0.03 in the primary. CPU is not the contended resource now (papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12#D-006). Disposition: dropped. Worker cost is tied to WI-10004801's recycle loop and is re-measured after the :3070 deploy.\n- P-009 (WI-10002831) final comparative verification report: this ruling plus the closeout report published under WI-6554700010009311 replace it. Independent final acceptance of this plan's bars is retired with the plan, and acceptance of performance work now runs through papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12's rubric. Disposition: dropped.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23","title":"Cut acceptance-review rework: stable proof identity, shift-left contract + vetting, emit-ready evaluator, pipeline alarms","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-23","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cut acceptance-review rework: stable proof identity, shift-left contract + vetting, emit-ready evaluator, pipeline alarms\nslug: review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-23\nupdated: 2026-10-21\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-06, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_stale, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_author_verdict_missing. Next repair: Re-prove the current spec revision; superseded proof does not cover it. (R-1). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nImplementation: 41 of 42 items complete; P-037 (the R-8 canary) remains, pending the owner's scope answer (conv-muf025gh). D-019 promoted all 31 AUTO-BAR clauses from draft to active; earlier proof bindings are stranded at the old clause revisions and must be rebound at the current ones. Rubric rev 2 vetting is attested (EI-24113548637312007, integrity audit pending). The ship gate refuses acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready until each BAR has one fully proven clause at its current revision. Once P-001, P-002, P-018 and P-019 land: (a) ask su-c03852cb (holder of the canary, turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21, D-002 §4 and that plan's D-12… <!-- P-037 -->\n## Goal\nPlan acceptance should finish in about one proof cycle instead of three, with every existing check kept: independent audits, rubric vetting, attestation and grading. Agents also stop spending time on work a scope decision made moot, on wakes that never land or have nothing to act on, and on retrying refused calls.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Proof survives unrelated amendments.** An amendment that adds, removes or edits one BAR leaves proof bound to every unchanged clause valid. The amend dry run lists carried vs invalidated proof and the cards to re-emit. When a bound TEST or SOURCE path moves, only that binding is re-measured, and one weak binding no longer fails a clause that has a sufficient one.\n\n**R-2 — The contract is complete and vetted before proof is bound.** Starting a plan refuses a BAR that lacks a method, a structured check, or test layers its check files can satisfy. Binding evidence against an unvetted rubric revision warns.\n\n**R-3 — Review tools succeed on the first well-formed call.** A card the evaluator emits passes audit unchanged. Review reads are compact by default. A refusal names every invalid field at once. A long coord message is chunked, not cut. rubrics:amend returns a receipt instead of timing out.\n\n**R-4 — Agents stop spending turns on noise, dead wakes and moot work.** git-sync is never silent or starved and never sweeps a locked file. Status-hook volume drops. A wake to a dead or parked session revives it or falls back to the inbox path. A wake with nothing actionable costs no turn. One carried check can change without re-sending the rest. A new holder sees which mutating verbs already worked on the item's plan. A directive recorded by another live session cannot be closed silently, and a closed one can be reopened.\n\n**R-5 — Review recruitment is pulled, and the existing backlog drains.** An unanswered vetting or grading consult becomes a pullable review work item. The existing awaiting-acceptance backlog is classified and swept.\n\n**R-6 — Scope writes propagate, and the gain is measurable.** Superseding, consolidating or dropping parks the carrier items the change made moot and re-evaluates BAR readiness. One read reports per-plan efficiency, so before and after can be compared.\n\n**R-7 — No check is removed.** Independent audit, rubric vetting, attestation, grading and every existing refusal code keep firing. Every item ships with a Vitest guard in the canonical suite.\n\n**R-8 — The canary shows the gain, and paused lanes resume.** The canary plan turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21 (D-002 §4) closes its next BARs with single-digit tool calls per BAR and no re-measurement caused by an unrelated peer commit. The lanes Avi paused until this plan lands are told to resume.\n\n**R-9 — Ship-path friction is legible at the moment it costs.** A ship refusal names the phase that blocks and that phase's codes per BAR. An amendment dry run shows the readiness change it would cause, including manual BARs it would flip to automated proof. An edit to a bound proof source names, at the edit, the clauses it staled and the one call that re-measures them.\n\n**R-10 — Proof metadata is judged once, at bind, and a recorded run binds itself.** A binding the current adequacy rule would fail on targeting is refused at bind with the accepted targets named. Each adequacy card records the evaluator revision that graded it, so a rule change re-evaluates the stored runs mechanically and asks for a new audit only where a verdict changes. A recorded test run binds as proof by its id, with its paths, attribution and commit derived from the run.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing surfaces. Add no new table, service or flag unless an item states why none fits. R-1 and R-2 are handled in `acceptance-bar-amendment.ts`, `rubrics.ts` and the spec-evidence binders. R-3 is handled in the evaluator, the tool-contract refusal layer and coord:send. R-4 is handled in the git-sync routine, the hook scripts, the wake pump and cold-loop fire, loop:checkpoint, the priorAttemptBrief on work_items, and the orders verbs. R-5 is handled in the consult router. R-6 is handled in plans:set-plan-status and plans:get mode:'meta'. The execution route is recorded in D-006.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-018, P-019 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-005, P-007, P-008 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-009, P-012, P-013, P-024, P-025, P-035, P-036 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-014, P-016 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-030, P-032 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-037 | live |\n| R-9 | P-038, P-039, P-040 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-043, P-044 | tree |\n\n## Evidence\nFull report: `docs/evidence/review-system-time-audit-2026-09-23.md` (queries in `.papercusp/scratch/codex-review-audit{,2,3,4}.sql`).\n- Plan codex-gateway-live-model-catalog: 199 min of acceptance; model 105, tool 58, idle 32. Targets: a proof-binding discard rate below 20%, acceptance wall-clock at most half of today's per-plan median, and no check removed.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Two independent audits merged: proof-churn (su-1bb6850b) and review-recruitment (su-ae3c4989) are different bottlenecks, both real\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23\nActor: su-ae3c4989-e86a-4ce3-bb2e-a3c357c8bd21\nAuthority: [owner:Avi 2026-09-23, directive #254] \"Update the referenced plan and report by integrating your own findings and recommendations\"\n\nTwo agents audited the review system within MINUTES of each other without coordinating: this plan was created 03:58:49Z; su-ae3c4989 filed escalation mudku06s at 04:02:12Z from a separate session, separate queries, separate subject plan. That independence is what makes the overlaps evidence rather than shared assumption (CLAUDE.md: corroboration requires independent EVIDENCE, not independent recall).\n\nMeasured: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED\n- rubrics:amend failure 32.3% (250/773, 7d) — reproduces su-1bb6850b's ~32% exactly, from a different session and query.\n- Input-shape refusals: ~790 (their review-tool scope) vs 782 invalid_input across 29 tools (su-ae3c4989's whole session). Different populations, same defect class.\n- Hook noise: their 622 failed activity:report calls (glance_stale key) vs su-ae3c4989's volume measure — activity:report 6,326 + coord:glance 3,610, both call_origin='hook' = 63.6% of that session's 15,612 MCP calls. Their finding is the FAILURE half, this one is the VOLUME half; P-012 should fix both.\n- \"Rubric seeded incomplete at plan creation\" (P-003) is confirmed downstream on an unrelated plan: goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 has SEVEN bars that simultaneously declare check={kind:'instrument',instrumentKey:'none'} (the documented \"explicitly manual criterion\") AND a non-empty requiredTestLayers of llm/e2e/integration. A bar cannot be both. That contradiction is exactly what a seed not requiring complete method/check/layers produces, and it is currently blocking that plan.\n\nMeasured: NOT REPRODUCED — flagged, not disputed\nThe headline \"59% of 4,428 proof bindings thrown away\" could not be reproduced cleanly. Independent count over the same 7-day window: 4,288 bindings (close enough — window edge), of which 1,210 retracted = 28.2%. The remaining ~31% is presumably superseded-by-amendment, but the join needed to measure that fans out across duplicate spec_id rows per plan item and returned an untrustworthy 50,714. DIRECTION strongly confirmed; the NUMBER is unverified. su-1bb6850b should publish the exact query so the figure is re-runnable — it is the headline number for Phase 1 and it should not rest on one unshown measurement.\n\nDecision: the two audits are COMPLEMENTARY, not competing, and this plan absorbs both rather than forking.\n- su-1bb6850b owns the PROOF-CHURN axis (P-001..P-013): why bound evidence is destroyed and re-made. Their clause-fingerprint root cause (acceptance-bar-amendment.ts:439,558) is a genuine code-level mechanism and is strictly better work than the procedural workaround su-ae3c4989 was carrying (\"batch every rubric revision before binding\"). Phase 1 stands as authored.\n- su-ae3c4989 contributes the RECRUITMENT axis (P-014..P-016), which this plan did not measure at all: 309 consults expired in 7 days with 304 at exchanges_used=0, a ~1% live-peer answer rate, and a resulting 208-plan awaiting-acceptance backlog at median age 68 days. P-004 reorders vetting so a critique costs less; it does not make a critique ARRIVE.\n- P-013 and P-015 are NOT duplicates and must not be merged: P-013 re-homes DEAD sessions; the 304 silent consults went to LIVE sessions that never prioritized the inbox. Collapsing them would leave the larger population unfixed while looking addressed.\n\nRuling for any agent picking this up: do not weaken a bar to make it passable. The correct resolution of a manual-vs-llm-layer contradiction is real llm-layer evidence or an explicit non-automated re-declaration WITH justification — never silently dropping the layer to clear the gate. The requiredProofFloor='none' exemption (spec-test-adequacy.ts:742 and the downgrade at ~:1656) is the sanctioned route for genuinely non-code work and fires only on behaviorClass==='non-automated' AND requiredTestLayers empty; reaching it by deleting a layer that was deliberately authored is gaming the gate, not satisfying it.\nRelated: P-014, P-015, P-016, P-017\n\n### D-002 — Third independent audit merged: the proof-churn mechanism reproduced on a second plan; P-002's carry-forward already ships; turn-start-memory's remaining 24 BARs are this plan's canary\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23 [self-imposed; su-c03852cb, author of the third audit]. Written from [turn:self], acting on an owner directive verified owner-typed at [turn:51c7850d@2026-09-23T04:16:00.033Z], verbatim: \"okay integrate your findings into both the plan and report\".\n\nMeasured: [turn:self], 04:24-04:28Z, first-hand. `grep -n barSetHash packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-amendment.ts` -> 439, 558 write `barSetHash: data.barSetHash` into each projected clause. `grep -rn 'carryUnchangedBarEvidenceBindings|shouldCarryBarEvidence'` -> defs at acceptance-bar-amendment.ts:593,648; sole call site rubrics.ts:4341-4347; read :580-699. `grep -rn 'author-attested booleans cannot establish'` -> packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy.ts:1408. Report: docs/evidence/review-system-time-audit-2026-09-23.md, \"Third audit, independent\".\n\n#### 1. A second CASE of the proof-churn mechanism, not a second recall of it\n\nSubject plan `turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21` (26 BARs, 36.7h old), different agent and queries, no coordination. MEASURED: 737 evidence bindings created and 345 retracted (47%); 476 binding refs record RE-BOUND/RE-RUN/RE-PROBED/RE-MEASURED; 55 clauses produced 389 clause revisions over 10 rubric revisions, by 6 distinct binders. The rev 9 -> 10 amendment changed ONLY bar R-4, yet every AUTO-BAR clause got a new revision in the same transaction at 03:33:31Z — root cause 1, reproduced.\n\n#### 2. P-002 is a VERIFY task, not a BUILD task\n\nCarry-forward for an unchanged BAR ALREADY SHIPS (see Measured above): the carry runs inside the amendment transaction and is counted as `evidenceCarriedForward`. It preserves observed_at/created_by, recomputes binding_fingerprint over the new revision, refuses retracted rows, and requires the contract edge at the new revision. It landed as `acceptance-machinery-seam-fixes-2026-09-16` P-008. Observed before the source was read: R-11's bindings at the new revision carry created_at = the amendment txn (03:33:31Z) while keeping observed_at = the original measurement (2026-09-22 19:26-19:41Z).\n\nRULING: whoever claims P-002 verifies the existing carry and reports what it does NOT cover; do not re-implement it. The residue is the identity half — P-001 — alone. Improvement 1's row in the report has been corrected accordingly.\n\n#### 3. The pairs, so neither half ships alone\n\n- P-001 <-> P-018. P-001 stabilises clause identity ACROSS RUBRIC AMENDMENTS; P-018 stabilises proof ACROSS UNRELATED PEER COMMITS to the measured files. INDEPENDENT decay mechanisms that stack — fixing one leaves the livelock half-armed. On `turn-start-memory-two-class` the carry (item 2) worked and the proof still died, because R-11's three measured files were rewritten by a peer's refactor after measurement (su.md 00:17Z, papercusp-files.ts 02:31Z, owner-directive-prompt-render.test.ts 03:13Z, against proof observed 2026-09-22T19:26-19:41Z).\n- P-011 <-> P-018. P-011 re-measures when a bound TEST file's fingerprint moves; P-018 covers the measured SOURCE files, the dominant staleness cause on the second plan.\n- P-007 <-> P-019. Compact review reads must NAME the dragging binding ids or the any-drags refusal stays unactionable. Adequacy is judged over all live bindings at the current revision under an any-drags rule: one under-attested row fails the clause however strong its neighbour. R-11 only went clean after 13 superseded rows were retracted BY HAND — so part of the 59%/47% discarded-binding headline is bookkeeping, not re-proof, and supersede-on-bind lowers it for the right reason.\n\n#### 4. CANARY CONTRACT — this plan's acceptance test already exists\n\nGoverning owner ruling, addressable rather than paraphrased: `plans:get { slug: 'turn-start-memory-two-class-2026-09-21', decisionId: 'D-124' }` carries the owner's verbatim words and their turn ref. Effect: that plan is PAUSED at 2 of 26 BARs clean, and its remaining 24 BARs are the acceptance test for THIS plan.\n\nMEASURED BASELINE, from repairing R-11 by hand: ~20 tool calls, 2 mutation-probe executions, 3 binding cycles, 13 retractions, plus hand reverse-engineering of spec-test-adequacy.ts (the rule that an executable proof needs a real test_run_id is stated nowhere a caller sees it — only at the line cited in Measured).\n\nTARGET once P-001, P-002, P-018 and P-019 land: single-digit tool calls per BAR, no source reading to learn the rule, no re-measurement caused by an unrelated peer commit. Recipe checkpointed on WI-10002415. su-c03852cb holds the canary and will report a NEGATIVE result as a negative result.\n\n#### 5. Measurement caveat\n\nThe third audit counts MCP calls only; su-1bb6850b's numbers are transcript-timed. Theirs is the better time attribution, this one the better artifact count — 47% vs 59% corroborates the direction, not the number.\n\n### D-003 — Measured at clause granularity: the churn is the rubric-wide set hash, not carry ineligibility. su-ae3c4989's changedBarKeys candidate AND the premise behind it are both falsified\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23 [self-imposed; su-c03852cb, written from [turn:self]]. FALSIFIED: \"changedBarKeys contains every bar on a rubric-wide re-key\"\n\nBy construction: `rubric-loss-guard.ts:467-481` diffs PER CRITERION over ACCEPTANCE_BAR_MEANING_FIELDS (`rubric-loss-guard.ts:289-301`) — that list contains `barHash` but NOT `barSetHash` — and `rubrics.ts:3825-3827` keeps only kinds added|removed|meaning. [self-imposed; su-96de869c, implementer of P-024 / WI-10002651.] No owner turn; open to reversal by the fleet leader.\n\n**Clause.** RSR-P-024-A@2 reads \"No loop fire is delivered while the session is parked on an await.\"\n\n**Measured root cause** (su-77b3a99d, event_awaits + routine_loop_transitions, 2026-09-23). loop-fire.ts Guard 4 already withholds fires while a blocking await is open, but only until LOOP_AWAIT_SUPPRESSION_MAX_QUIET_MS (30 min) after the await's CREATION. After that the guard lifted outright: quiet 01:46-02:16Z, then 8 full loop turns by 04:22Z while the owner-answer await stayed open until 09:12Z.\n\n**Ruling.** The 30-min bound exists so a stuck-forever await (emitter bug, cancelled without cleanup, no expiresTs) cannot silence a loop permanently. Deleting it would meet the clause's letter but remove a safety check, which R-7 forbids. So the bound stays, and after it the loop gets ONE liveness fire per LOOP_AWAIT_HEARTBEAT_MS (60 min), measured from the last fire actually DELIVERED during this await (routines.metadata.last_delivered_at, stamped by incrementLoopFireCount). The await's own deadline still caps everything, so its fallback wake is never silenced. An unknown or pre-await delivery time keeps the old ceiling, and a failed read fails open.\n\n**Effect on the incident timeline.** The replay test gives >=7 fires under the old ceiling and <=3 under the new one, spaced at least one heartbeat apart.\n\n**What 'satisfied' means for the grader.** Between the 30-min bound and the await's resolution or deadline, fires are withheld except one per heartbeat. A fire every tick after 30 min is the falsifier. A report whose fingerprint equals that phase's last sent fingerprint is skipped, with two due-flags that count as a change of state: (1) PRE: lease renewal due, 600s since the last pre report (PAPERCUSP_ACTIVITY_KEEPALIVE_SEC). activity:report is the only liveness source for activity-mode plan-item claims (plan-items/activity-claim-renewal.ts renews on each report; lease >=20m), so suppressing identical reports forever would let a live agent that repeats one call lose its claims. 600s is half the lease. (2) POST: coordination fold due, 60s since the last post report (PAPERCUSP_ACTIVITY_POST_FOLD_DUE_SEC, equal to GLANCE_MAX_AGE_SEC). The post report also carries the inbox/glance fold (hook_bundle), so suppressing identical posts without a bound would delay directed-message delivery indefinitely. The existing interval gates stay (R-7).\n\n**Consequence.** Two identical consecutive states inside the due window emit one report, not two. A second identical report is only sent once the lease or fold is due, and that report exists to renew or fold, not to re-announce the state. If the leader reads the clause as forbidding these keepalives, the alternative is a clause revision, not removing them: without them claims lapse and inbox delivery stalls.\n\n### D-015 — R-10 added: two rework sources from a peer's friction report (Avi #375) that no item covers become P-043 and P-044; final certification runs once, after the last code lands\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDate: 2026-09-23. D-040 shortened the AFTER window to one UTC day but kept every other D-035/D-037 term, including step 6's per-side floors (>=200 tree BARs across >=15 plans, >=75 live BARs across >=8 plans, no plan above 40%). Rev-8 vetting (consult conv-muij3v6q-0000-92c372663aaa4788a896a969128f2efc, posts 1146717 and 1146719) measured the closed AFTER enrollment with the step-1 rule: tree 14 BARs across 3 plans (largest plan 8/14 = 57%), live 1 BAR across 1 plan, deployed 0. Under unchanged floors R-8 is UNKNOWN by construction, so the plan could never ship on it. That contradicts the owner's answer. Reviewer 1 also found the R-8 model still names a fourteen-day after window.\n\nRuling.\n1. BEFORE side unchanged: the frozen 2026-09-08..2026-09-22 census of 362 BARs and its floors stand.\n2. AFTER side: the step-6 population and concentration floors are replaced by a minimum cohort per primary plane of >=10 enrolled BARs across >=3 plans. Three plans is the least that supports a whole-plan bootstrap interval. An AFTER plane below the minimum is reported UNKNOWN for that plane and excluded from the improvement grade. If no primary plane qualifies, improvement = UNKNOWN. On the enrollment already measured, tree qualifies and live does not.\n3. Concentration: the 40% cap is replaced on the AFTER side by a leave-largest-plan-out check. Recompute the standardized gain without the AFTER plane's largest plan. If that gain is below 30% or changes sign, the rating is capped at degraded.\n4. Unchanged: the >=80% outcome-coverage and >=80% closed-BAR call-trace floors per graded plane; the healthy thresholds (>=30% lower standardized proof-work calls per completed BAR with a whole-plan bootstrap 95% interval excluding zero gain, completion no more than 5 points lower, p90 calls no more than 10% higher, no rise in retractions per BAR or failed adequacy); the step-7 paused-lane resumption half.\n5. Disclosure: the R-8 rating states the AFTER n, plan count and largest-plan share per plane, the leave-one-out result, and that this is a low-power one-day comparison, not the powered estimate D-035 asked for.\n6. D-037's anti-cherry-picking rule stands: no window extension and no floor change after AFTER outcomes are inspected.\n\nWhy this default. It keeps every robustness check that can be computed at this size (bootstrap interval, leave-one-out, coverage floors) and drops only the floors a one-day window cannot meet by construction. Alternatives not taken: keep the floors (R-8 permanently UNKNOWN, the plan unshippable, contradicting D-040) or extend AFTER back to 14 days (reverses D-040). Do not substitute keyword/name similarity or another unverified caller boolean as proof, or force arbitrary new scenario IDs on every legacy clause.\nAcceptance for this repair: reproduce same-specId/same-file/current-binding/measured-failed-case controls where an unrelated mentions case cannot prove publish-via-gateway; retain a genuinely aligned publishing positive control, explicit-scenario controls and existing case-identity guards.
