Follow each repository's release automation and liv… <!-- P-016 -->\n## Background\n\nStorewolf Central Server needs LLM-powered product processing using Papercusp. Avi initially asked whether to adopt Oddsmith's development-pot/ops-pot separation. The discussion established a stronger requirement: every Storewolf AI business operation, including extraction, classification, comparison, and longer research, uses the same durable work-item path. Lower latency must come from improving that path, not bypassing queueing, dispatch, recovery, or audit.\n\nStorewolf also needs a focused worker configuration instead of an unrelated full SU persona/tool surface, an enforceable model policy, and one concrete application call meaning 'run this task on this version of this blueprint'. Blueprints remain reusable definitions; plan runs/work items remain execution instances. Their execution contract must be unified, without merging these distinct responsibilities into one object or building another queue.\n\n### Source conversation and decisions to preserve\n\nCanonical source: codex session 01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840, owner su-f77cd8e4-c619-449e-b4aa-97f3fe93e5dd. Owner turns were re-read through sessions:read/search while drafting. The complete conversation, including assistant proposals and corrections, must be re-read and mapped in the activation audit; this draft is not an activation audit.\n\n| Source turn | Requirement / correction | Recorded here |\n|---|---|---|\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:1 | Use Papercusp for Storewolf LLM work; consider development and ops pots; reuse Oddsmith | R-1, R-2, D-001, P-002, P-010 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:9 | Simple extraction/classification/comparison should use work items too | R-1, D-001 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:11 | Reduce work-item overhead while retaining reliability | R-8, R-11, D-001, P-013 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:13 | Explain/enforce specific model selection; inspect Oddsmith and diagram it | R-5, R-12, P-008, P-015 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:16 | Focused Storewolf identity, initial prompt, tools; avoid full SU worker configuration | R-4, D-002, P-006 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:20 | Unify blueprint and work-item execution more tightly | R-3, R-6, D-003, P-003, P-004 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:23 | Concrete low-level task flow and diagram | R-12, Design task flow, P-015 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:25 | Mermaid alone was not viewable; deliver an actual image | R-12, diagram source links, P-015 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:27 | One final app call: run this task on this blueprint | R-2, proposed API, P-005, P-011 |\n| session_turn:codex:01a0cf1b-7831-7013-9361-1d74617eb840:30 | Write a plan and provide summary for review | P-001; draft only |\n\nThe unrelated context-limit request was already completed (682000 tokens) and creates no product requirement. Superseded proposal: direct gateway calls from Storewolf for short tasks. Gateway calls remain internal to governed work-item execution, never a separate application bypass. The conceptual API below and strict model/specification binding are proposed work, not existing guarantees.\n\n### Evidence from the source trace\n\n- Oddsmith's libs/hive-app-seam/src/work-items.ts submits generic task items with payload.domainKind, blueprintId and input. apps/desktop/src/lib/harness-ops-wiring.ts binds this to oddsmith-ops and bet-analysis. Its older blueprints describe specialist analyst/director/researcher prompts, models and outputs.\n- The checked Oddsmith apps/desktop/bin/serve.ts:390 does not pass fetchCompleted to the projector; apps/desktop/src/lib/projector-wiring.ts:112 defaults that port to an empty source. The legacy client also expects payloads in list results, whereas Papercusp's endpoint-route/routes/harness/work-items.ts slimListRow sets payload:null. Source-only gaps, not a certified current production outage: EI-24071453294746068.\n- The current app-agent template retains role-local tools/capabilities declarations rejected by the current blueprint validator. Migrate the existing template to the current authorities: EI-24071653209916702.\n- Current AgenticPlanExecutionTarget contains appHarnessSlug and agentName. launchPlanRuns is a host-injected interface, not a turnkey authenticated remote client. scheduler model_fit is currently neutral in the traced implementation. The gateway has a model-substitution path, so an executor model setting does not establish strict model compliance.\n- Reuse identities-v1-2026-08-30 and accept-identities-v1-m1-2026-09-04. The former is awaiting acceptance at draft time; do not claim the composition program is shipped or take over its owners' work. Re-check exact revision/acceptance compatibility at activation.\n\n## Scope\n\nIn scope: the smallest shared blueprint-to-work-item execution binding; a concrete authenticated submission/status/result interface and thin JS client; a focused Storewolf runtime identity and enforced permissions; exact/preferred model policy; reliable dispatch, completion and ingestion; one real Storewolf pilot; current template repair and cross-boundary compatibility tests; measured overhead reduction; reviewable documentation and images.\n\nProposed topology: register the existing Storewolf repository for development management and create/reuse a separate storewolf-ops runtime pot. This wraps the existing application and its business data; it does not replace its service architecture. Resolve the supported existing-repository import/registration route, exact slugs, canonical checkout and Git automation rules before editing; do not relocate the repository or silently enroll it into Papercusp's Git workflow.\n\nProposed pilot: product-spec extraction on representative, versioned Storewolf product inputs. Prove a dependent two-step workflow using the same machinery. Classification, comparison and research are supported operation shapes; implementing every domain workflow is not required for this first delivery.\n\nOut of scope: rewriting Central Server; migrating its business database; rebuilding identities/composition; replacing the scheduler/queue; a full Oddsmith trading-system migration; autonomous marketplace/order/price writes; external identity publishing; unapproved schedules, fleets, or production side effects. Fix shared seam/template defects required for this integration; attach narrowly scoped follow-ups for broader Oddsmith migration rather than silently expanding the plan.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — One durable AI execution path.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Every Storewolf AI business operation enters canonical plan/work-item execution before any model or agent work. One-step and multi-step tasks share durable acceptance, backpressure, assignment, failure states and results. No application direct-inference exception is introduced.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every supported Storewolf AI operation has a committed canonical work item before its first model request.\",\"falsifier\":\"An extraction, classification, comparison or research request reaches inference without a durable item.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Submit each operation against an instrumented gateway stub, trace work-item commit before inference, and compare the ledger to the request population.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — One concrete application call.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"An authenticated Storewolf client submits a versioned blueprint reference, immutable inputs and idempotency key, receives durable run/work-item identifiers, and reads status/results or reconciles completion notifications. Callers do not rebuild prompts, choose session IDs or wire queues per request.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Repeated submission with the same blueprint version, inputs and key returns one durable run and its retrievable result.\",\"falsifier\":\"A replay creates a second run or a conflicting input is accepted under the old key.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Exercise authenticated client submit, concurrent replay, conflict and status/result reads through the app boundary.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Versioned executable contract.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Each run/item pins a resolved blueprint/specification revision, input/output contracts and execution requirements with provenance, reusing the existing composition artifact. Retry semantics are stable across blueprint edits; current authorization/revocation remains enforced and cannot be frozen away by a pin.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A resumed item uses its original pinned specification revision while current revoked grants remain denied.\",\"falsifier\":\"Editing a blueprint changes an in-flight task or a revoked capability still works.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inspect persisted spec revision and retry outputs after source edits, then revoke a permission and attempt the restricted action.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Focused, confined Storewolf worker.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A worker has a Storewolf-specific prompt/identity, required tools, explicitly enforced role/principal limits and scoped queue access. An unrelated or incompatible SU/worker cannot execute this item simply by claiming it. Hiding tools or adding prompt instructions alone is insufficient; native/client tools and privileged transport bypasses are included in the boundary tests.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Only an applied Storewolf worker with the required allowed capabilities can execute Storewolf items.\",\"falsifier\":\"An SU or worker with a wrong identity, denied tool or missing applied revision completes the item.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Attempt wrong-role claim, forbidden MCP/native/shell access and valid restricted-worker execution; inspect authorization receipts.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Enforced model policy.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"An operation can require an exact model or declare a bounded allowed set/preference. Exact mode never succeeds after an unauthorized substitution; unavailable capacity remains waiting or fails retryably within deadlines. Record requested and actual model, effort/backend and account attribution without exposing credentials. Unknown model evidence cannot count as exact-model success.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An exact-model task cannot complete successfully when actual model evidence is different or unknown.\",\"falsifier\":\"Gateway substitution or missing model metadata still produces a compliant success.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Use gateway integration scenarios for exact, allowed and preferred modes, induced substitution, no capacity and missing response metadata.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — One orchestration lifecycle.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Blueprint execution requirements and plan dependency edges govern the same durable work items. No app-local queue, independent blueprint executor ledger, duplicate workflow cursor or hidden per-task agent fan-out is introduced. A model turn need not become a separate top-level work item.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"One-step and dependent blueprint runs advance through the same canonical work-item ledger and dependency edges.\",\"falsifier\":\"A step advances through a separate queue or a blocked descendant starts early.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inspect promotion and dispatch records for one-step and two-step fixtures, including replay and prerequisite completion.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Durable, idempotent acceptance.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Acknowledgement follows committed persistence, independent of worker wake success. Concurrent duplicate submissions recover one execution identity; the same key with different inputs/specification is rejected. Source snapshots and submission intent survive application restarts.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The app returns accepted only after durable persistence and concurrent identical submissions reuse one run identity.\",\"falsifier\":\"Acknowledgement precedes commit or concurrent replay mints two work items.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inject a crash after commit/before acknowledgement, then replay concurrently and compare durable identities.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Recoverable bounded execution.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Persist attempts/ownership and meaningful progress. Worker loss, lost wakes, transient gateway failures, cancellation, deadlines and late/stale completion are handled visibly using existing mechanisms, with bounded retries and no duplicate result application. Do not promise exactly-once provider execution.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A worker crash leaves its item recoverable without applying a result twice.\",\"falsifier\":\"A lost wake strands the item or a stale worker overwrites recovery.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Fault-inject loss at assignment, wake, inference and completion, then verify bounded recovery and stale-attempt rejection.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Validated durable completion and application.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Output and successful completion become durable consistently; schema/acceptance/model-policy failures are explicit. Notifications are replayable hints over stored truth. Storewolf validates input revision and business rules and atomically records application/receipt so duplicates do not repeat effects.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A valid result is applied once to the product revision named by the request.\",\"falsifier\":\"A duplicate delivery repeats effects or a stale result updates a newer product revision.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Replay notifications and crash between app reads and writes while checking the result receipt and product revision.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Existing surfaces and compatibility.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Extend pot-app-seam, canonical promotion/dispatch, identity composition, capability enforcement and the gateway. Repair the starter's current validation drift and cover the real app-to-platform payload contract. Do not treat historical Oddsmith docs as proof of current execution or regress existing consumers.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The current specialized app-agent template validates and app/server result transport retrieves completed payloads.\",\"falsifier\":\"Role-local legacy fields fail validation or a payload-stripped list silently drops a result.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run blueprint validation and a cross-boundary client/server round trip using the actual detail/event result surface.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-11 — Measured overhead improvement.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Instrument submission, persistence, ready-to-dispatch delay, deliberate queue wait, model time and result ingestion separately. Establish a reproducible baseline and explicit budget before optimizing; show the final comparison. Reuse compiled configuration and compatible warm capacity without weakening durability, isolation, revocation or model enforcement.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The canonical Storewolf task path meets the frozen P-002 latency and throughput budget while all reliability checks pass.\",\"falsifier\":\"A measured p95 phase exceeds the approved budget or an optimization weakens durability or confinement.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Compare p50/p95/p99 and throughput under identical recorded workloads before/after changes and rerun the failure matrix.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-12 — Reviewable flow and verification.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Deliver a runnable Storewolf example, low-level walkthrough, accessible SVG/PNG diagram, lifecycle/failure documentation and framework-integrated tests. Clearly distinguish implemented, proposed, locally verified and shipped behavior.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The runnable Storewolf example and accessible PNG/SVG accurately describe the verified task lifecycle.\",\"falsifier\":\"The example fails or the diagram depicts an unimplemented step as shipped.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Execute the example on current build, open both image files and compare each numbered step with trace and code evidence.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-13 — Controlled delivery.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Normal implementation and acceptance run on staging/current build. Final shipment verifies deployed application/platform compatibility and one approved non-dangerous pilot. Respect live gate ownership and existing release automation; no forced red deployment or marketplace mutation is implicit.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The deployed integration runs a non-dangerous Storewolf pilot with recorded revisions and recovery evidence.\",\"falsifier\":\"The integration exists only on staging or the deployed pilot cannot be reproduced safely.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"deployed\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"e2e\"],\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Verify deployed Papercusp and Storewolf build revisions, run a bounded extraction pilot, inspect committed result/application and execute rollback proof.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Objects and ownership\n\n| Object | Responsibility |\n|---|---|\n| Blueprint / identity sources | Reusable worker behavior, operation constraints, schemas and acceptance declarations |\n| Resolved agent/execution specification | Versioned composition and input closure with provenance; refer to it rather than copy full prompts into each work item |\n| Plan template / run | Single operation or dependent steps, immutable input/provenance, replay identity |\n| Work item / attempt | Durable assignment, execution ownership, progress, retries, result and evidence |\n| Agent session | Compatible restricted executor; session replacement does not replace durable task identity |\n| Storewolf application | Business validation, product-version checks, database effects and application receipts |\n\nDo not introduce a new profile registry, task table or dispatcher if one field/reference on these existing surfaces suffices. Capture any genuinely necessary new durable surface and the rejected reuse alternatives before implementation.\n\n### Proposed app-facing API\n\nIllustrative interface for review, NOT a currently callable SDK:\n\n```js\nconst run = await papercusp.tasks.submit({\n  blueprint: 'storewolf-extract-specs@1.0.0',\n  input: { productId: '123', productRevision: 17, title: 'Example laptop', description: '...' },\n  idempotencyKey: 'product:123:rev:17:extract-specs:v1'\n});\n// Accepted after durable persistence, even if dispatch is temporarily unavailable:\n// { runId, workItemIds, status: 'queued' }\n```\n\nThe final public method/route name is an implementation decision in P-005, recorded before code, and must extend the existing app seam rather than claim this pseudocode already exists. Installation binds an allowed operation/blueprint version to its plan template, ops-pot and eligible execution configuration. The authenticated service identity determines scope; client-supplied owner/model headers never grant authority. Add scoped status/result retrieval and reconnect reconciliation through existing detail/event surfaces; do not rely on payload-stripped list responses.\n\nCurrent reuse point: templates/papercusp-ops-pots/pot-app-seam/src/index.ts PlanRunDraft already carries templateSlug, input, provenance, execution {appHarnessSlug,agentName}, and dedupeKey. Its launchPlanRuns currently treats failed wake as failed launch even after promotion: preserve the committed receipt and expose acceptance separately from dispatch state. Bind the blueprint reference and immutable resolved artifact here and in canonical promotion/dispatch. Inspect callers and compatibility before changing this contract.\n\n### Low-level task flow\n\n1. Install/register the blueprint and focused Storewolf identity; resolve/pin the specification and provision permitted tools. Use existing blueprint/identity authoring and supported existing-repo management verbs.\n2. Start/reuse a compatible restricted worker, adopt its stable name and verify the applied identity/configuration. Installation/worker preparation is reused across tasks.\n3. Storewolf persists a pending submission alongside the product/job operation and snapshots/version-addresses inputs. Reuse existing persistence/outbox mechanisms where suitable.\n4. The authenticated interface validates operation permissions, input schema, size and idempotency identity; atomically create/recover the canonical run/items and persist the resolved specification reference.\n5. Return a durable accepted receipt. Dispatch availability is a separate state. Retries after lost acknowledgement return the same execution; conflicting reuse of a key is rejected.\n6. Dispatch only actionable unblocked items to a compatible worker; durably record assignment/attempt ownership before required wake. Check current permission state in addition to the pinned operation requirements.\n7. The worker reads the authoritative item, immutable inputs and contract. It uses only permitted tools, checkpoints progress and calls the gateway inside this governed execution.\n8. The gateway enforces model/fallback policy and reports actual execution metadata. Unavailable exact-model capacity is a visible queued/retryable state with deadline, not a hidden downgrade.\n9. The worker submits structured output and execution evidence. The shared completion boundary validates schemas, acceptance and model compliance and commits result/completion consistently. Stale/cancelled ownership cannot overwrite a newer attempt.\n10. Notify from committed state. Storewolf retrieves the durable result, verifies product revision and business constraints, and atomically applies it with a receipt. Reconnect reconciliation recovers lost notifications.\n\n### Reliability boundaries\n\n| Failure | Required behavior |\n|---|---|\n| Lost request acknowledgement | Same idempotency key recovers the same run/item IDs |\n| Concurrent duplicate request | Unique durable identity, no duplicated application effect |\n| Changed input with reused key | Explicit conflict; never return an unrelated prior result |\n| Worker absent / wake lost / crash | Work remains visible; recovery reuses canonical ownership and wake machinery |\n| Gateway timeout / rate limit | Bounded attempt/retry with attribution and explicit state |\n| Required model unavailable or substituted | No compliant-success claim; wait or fail according to policy |\n| Blueprint edited during a run | Pinned run semantics persist; current revocation still restricts authority |\n| Invalid or incomplete model output | Explicit failed validation or bounded retry |\n| Cancelled/expired/stale worker submits | Reject or retain as non-applicable evidence; no late business application |\n| Lost completion notification | Durable result remains readable and reconciliation discovers it |\n| Product changed since submission | Do not apply stale output to the new revision; record/requeue under policy |\n| Storewolf crashes while applying result | Transactional effect+receipt or equivalent existing idempotent mechanism |\n\nAt-least-once inference attempts may occur after ambiguous provider response/crash. Record that possibility and usage; the required business invariant is one application of an accepted result to the correct input revision. No unbounded retries, silent baseline substitution, permanent event-only sleep, or success acknowledgement before durable storage.\n\n### Worker and model configuration\n\nAuthor Storewolf domain behavior as an identity/role on the existing blueprint substrate. roles[].prompt/stack selects instructions; dependencies.tools declares imports; the current role/principal capability system enforces authority. Verify permissions for MCP, client-native tools, network/file access and shell-based bypasses. A task input is untrusted data and cannot rewrite identity, models or grants.\n\nExact model / allowed-set / preferred modes must be explicit and versioned. Pinning an account is not pinning a model. Reuse the gateway's request-policy/attribution surfaces; prevent prohibited substitution before inference and verify returned execution evidence before successful completion. Separate worker reasoning model from a task's optional subordinate model calls if the operation uses both; specify which calls are constrained.\n\n### Performance and observation\n\nMeasure end-to-end requests through the real canonical persistence/dispatch path using deterministic provider stubs for load tests and a small actual-model pilot separately. Record workload, machine/build versions, payload sizes, concurrency, throughput and p50/p95/p99 for each phase. Distinguish intended backpressure/queue wait from avoidable dispatch work. P-002 records provisional budgets and P-013 verifies them before acceptance; do not invent current latency figures.\n\nResolve/validate compiled configuration once per revision where safe; cache with revocation-aware invalidation, reuse compatible worker capacity, batch independent storage operations and remove measured polling/redundant setup. Bound job-specific context and isolate product inputs across warm tasks. Performance changes must pass the same durability and confinement tests.\n\n### Visual artifact\n\nExisting reviewed-discussion diagram source: /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/artifacts/storewolf-task-flow.svg ; raster: /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/artifacts/storewolf-task-flow.png. Both were rendered and visually checked under WI-10002767. They are local artifacts, not published URLs. Preserve both paths and update the diagram to final implemented semantics in P-015; deliver a PNG/SVG link, not Mermaid alone.\n\n### Dependency rationale\n\nDraft review intentionally leaves no executable ready items before P-001. After P-002, registration (P-017) and execution-contract work (P-003) can proceed independently; worker configuration needs both. Model-policy work is independent of the client transport after the contract is fixed. Integration depends on submission and completion contracts, not on redundant transitive edges. Template compatibility work and integrated tests/performance converge at the real pilot (P-014). Tests and performance have independent readiness after app integration, subject to actual file locks. The remaining sequential path represents real contract/persistence boundaries and the final verification order, not assumed need for a fleet; same-file work must be serialized. P-017 was added after dependency review specifically to avoid launching a worker before its pot exists.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-004, P-005, P-011, P-012 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-005, P-011, P-014 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003, P-007, P-009, P-012 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006, P-007, P-012, P-017 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-008, P-009, P-012, P-014 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004, P-007, P-012 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-005, P-011, P-012 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-007, P-008, P-009, P-012 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-009, P-011, P-012 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-002, P-003, P-004, P-010, P-012, P-017 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-002, P-005, P-007, P-013 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-012, P-014, P-015 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-016 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Review and baseline\n\n- **P-001** `done` Avi reviews this draft: scope and two-pot proposal; product-spec extraction as the initial pilot; dedicated restricted worker; strict/allowed model policy; one blueprint-based submit API; execution route for implementation. Generic infrastructure continues only in blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23; do not execute these promoted application-scoped items.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Preserve reliability for short and long tasks\nDate: 2026-09-23\nOwner-directed principle from turns 9 and 11: all Storewolf AI business operations use durable work items. The earlier direct-call shortcut is superseded. Reduce avoidable queue/dispatch overhead without bypassing the reliability contract.\n\n### D-002 — Worker identity, tools, authority and model are separate\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDraft recommendation responding to turn 16: create focused Storewolf identity/role configuration, bind it to real restricted execution and current authorization, and route only its work to compatible workers. Merely renaming or reprompting an SU does not provide confinement. Exact queue exclusivity and tool denial must be tested.\n\n### D-003 — Reuse definitions and execution substrate\nDate: 2026-09-23\nDraft recommendation responding to turns 20 and 27: bind a versioned blueprint/resolved specification to canonical plan/work-item executions. Extend identities-v1, pot-app-seam, promotion/dispatch, completion and gateway policy. Keep definition, run/item and session separate; introduce no parallel registry/queue or orphan blueprint executor.\n\n### D-004 — One application-facing submission\nDate: 2026-09-23\nThe target application experience is one submit call with blueprint version, input and idempotency key. The authenticated connection supplies Storewolf scope and installation supplies execution binding. tasks.submit is illustrative naming pending P-005, not an assertion of an existing endpoint. Durable acceptance and successful dispatch are distinct.\n\n### D-005 — Preserve application ownership and delivery scope\nDate: 2026-09-23\nProposed Storewolf development/ops separation leaves Central Server's architecture, business database and effect validation in the application. The worker reads and proposes under a restricted role. Product-spec extraction is the proposed first pilot; dangerous business actions and a full Oddsmith migration are excluded.\n\n### D-006 — Draft authorization only\nDate: 2026-09-23\nAvi requested a plan and review summary. Authoring and validating this draft are authorized; execution route, activation, provisioning and implementation are not chosen by this request. The current authoring session is solo; that does not preselect the implementation route. After approval, re-read the full source conversation, repair omissions and record plans:audit before activation.\n\n### D-007 — Distinct integration effort over identities-v1\nDate: 2026-09-23\nThe plan-store duplicate check identified identities-v1-2026-08-30. Its current Design and revision 303 were read: it owns blueprint/identity composition, immutable resolved artifacts, activation, authority and capability-provider contracts, and is awaiting independent acceptance. This new plan consumes those mechanisms and owns Storewolf's application-facing blueprint task submission, the binding from work items to that artifact, task-specific model compliance, durable application ingestion and performance proof. It does not reimplement the compiler, identity schema, activation or policy engine, and does not alter the existing plan's scope/status. P-003/P-006/P-007 must extend or consume the owned public contracts and coordinate any genuinely necessary foundation change under that existing lane. A separate Storewolf integration plan is appropriate because its application/runtime lifecycle and acceptance are distinct.\n\n## Review choices and open questions\n\n- Confirm the proposed first pilot: extraction of structured specs from a versioned product snapshot. The architecture also supports classification/comparison and multi-step research without a separate runtime.\n- Select initial model/effort/account policy and intended production deployment connectivity during contract setup. The strict-model capability is in scope; no concrete provider/model or account has been selected in this discussion.\n- Confirm final development/runtime pot slugs and the existing Storewolf repository's management route; do not duplicate an existing registration or change its Git workflow by assumption.\n- Choose implementation route when approving execution, using only then-available self/fleet routes. No fleet is launched by this draft.\n- Final API spelling, precise retry/deadline/concurrency values and performance budgets are recorded engineering decisions after P-002 baseline; material product tradeoffs return to Avi for review.\n\n## Verification and activation notes\n\nEvery feature/fix item includes its own relevant framework tests; P-012 covers system-wide failure boundaries rather than deferring all tests to the end. Use current-build/staging for ordinary acceptance, reserving deployed evidence for P-016. No test, metric, migration, production integration or strict-model guarantee is claimed to have passed by this draft.\n\nBefore activation, use sessions:search/read on the full source conversation including assistant corrections and later review turns; map every requirement, constraint, rejection, dependency and promise to R/P/D references, repair omissions, record plans:audit, and only then start. This draft's source table and diagram are review aids, not substitutes for that activation audit.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23","title":"Acceptance BAR — Generic blueprint execution, automation and durability","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-24","owner":"su-f77cd8e4-c619-449e-b4aa-97f3fe93e5dd","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Generic blueprint execution, automation and durability\nslug: acceptance-blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-24\nupdated: 2026-10-06\nowner: su-f77cd8e4-c619-449e-b4aa-97f3fe93e5dd\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Generic blueprint execution, automation and durability\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"su-mode-contract-identity-unification-2026-09-24","title":"Unify SU mode definitions and supplied resources in agent identity bundles","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-24","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Unify SU mode definitions and supplied resources in agent identity bundles\nslug: su-mode-contract-identity-unification-2026-09-24\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-24\nupdated: 2026-10-08\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** 2026-09-30T05:50Z (su-b0451bbf): 9/10 items done. For P-008 (WI-10002965), 6 of 7 spec clauses pass: R-5, R-6, R-7, R-9, R-10 and identity-native-applied-revision-proof (evaluator 05:19Z, after binds 16364/16365). R-8 (J3, deployed + rollback-resumed SU identity pins, WI-10003584) has no evidence yet. It needs a :3070 build carrying the current P-008 blobs. :3070 serves main 9a9473af, which lacks all 5. The frozen gate lineage (candidate 5ec99902, repairHead 5955f82b) also carries older blobs: role-launch-spec, package-recipe-resources, compile-packages, turn-start-memory and psu-launcher.mjs all differ from HEAD. Its promotion therefore does not make J3 eligible; one more candidate cycle is needed after it converges. Peer su-c0b38c83 owns the gate lane (WI-10004029 / WI-10004151).\n\n**Next:** When deploy.3070.sha changes, compare the 5 P-008 blobs (deployedSha vs HEAD). If they all match, run J3 on :3070 and bind R-8. Then complete P-008, run the per-item completion audit, get independent BAR grading, and ship.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10002907 — Before activation audit the full owner conversation and trace every correction into this plan. Prepare acceptance rubric/BAR/spec requirements through normal gates. Census fixed prompt sources, gener… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002957 — Extend the existing trusted manifest/compiler/resolver seams for one component model covering fixed content, generated context declarations and resource/operational contributions. Generate mode catal… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002958 — Package SU and reusable specialist content as selectable compositions; add GOAL/GRADE/TEST components and supported axes alongside existing modes. Reconcile canonical clauses and combination behavior… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002959 — Bind mode/registry-contract readers, bootstrap, orientation, peer messages, native hooks and context declarations to one selected component/resolver model. Preserve existing buildLeaderBrief, goal ki… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002960 — Connect selected resource/operational declarations through existing compileBlueprintWithPackages/provisionBlueprintPackages, recipe/rubric/knowledge/capability consumers and launch resolvers. Extend … <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002961 — Bind identity content and defaults through the existing SU role/fleet/goal adapters and generated compatibility views. Preserve current role-principal/tool-allowlist/quota, assignment/resource-profil… <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002962 — Connect psu and GUI to the installed identity catalog with one Identity picker and SU default, compatible installed choices, origin/version, pagination and explicit invalid entries. Add optional comp… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002963 — Use current launch-spec/identity-management/session-activation and host carry/recovery paths to retain pinned selections across launch/resume/update/rollback; extend only missing propagation seams. K… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002964 — Add real-suite guards for single-definition/catalog parity, fixed/generated context composition, refresh and omission/failure behavior, optional host integrations, graph limits, supported resource/op… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10002965 — Verify native current-build/deployed SU and generic identity delivery, including combined fixed/generated content, observed non-prompt resource/configuration use, CLI/GUI selection, relevant mode ena… <!-- P-008 -->\n## Motivation and intended result\n\nThe owner's objective is one composition system for the material and configuration supplied to agents. Everything reusable supplied to SU should be bundlable in agent identities, including the declarations that obtain current task/operational context. Fixed instructions and generated context must compose through the same path; their source and refresh behavior are component metadata, not separate agent concepts or parallel prompt systems.\n\nA component may contain a document, render current data through a declared provider/template, reference a resource such as knowledge/rubrics/recipes, or contribute operational configuration such as model defaults and tool requirements. These forms share composition, dependency resolution, versioning, validation and provenance. Their consumers still apply their concrete semantics: reading a model name in a prompt does not select the model, and bundling a recipe does not execute it.\n\nSU is a named default composition. Its fleet and goal machinery is an optional integration carried by the components that need it. Fleet assignment and goal launch-slot fields are not universal prerequisites for identities. Other identities can declare different context requirements or run without any SU fleet/work-item/goal integration.\n\nAgents retain ReAct execution: observe the task and tool results, decide the next action, call a tool, and repeat. A component changes the information/resources/settings supplied to that loop; no mandatory workflow spine or finite-state reasoning graph is introduced.\n\n## Vocabulary and product model\n\n| User-facing concept | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| Component / facet | A reusable blueprint contribution: instructions, generated context, resources, operational declarations, or a composition of those contributions. Source, refresh, inclusion and merge policy describe how it is consumed. |\n| Named identity | A saved, validated composition with a name and description; SU is the default. Saved compositions reuse the existing blueprint library and Cupboard distribution. |\n| Effective identity | The resolved, version-pinned component selection for a session. At a given turn the system also records which generated context and operational settings were actually supplied. |\n| Modes and optional customization | Controls that select applicable components through supported activation rules; they do not constitute a second instruction-authoring system. |\n\nSlots are composition rules for compatibility, ordering and cardinality. A component claims supported slots; changing the platform's slot vocabulary requires defined semantics and tests. Slot metadata need not appear in the ordinary launch flow.\n\nThe source of content does not create another top-level identity type. A markdown document and a current-goal rendering can both be stackable context contributions. A component can bundle both. The package pins the source/provider/template and its refresh policy; current values are resolved when needed and can change without creating a new authored identity version.\n\nPapercusp-specific assignment, launch-slot, responsibility-routing and permission consumers are described in the SU integration section. They are optional host bindings, not mandatory columns that every identity author or launch user must supply. Concrete membership/claim facts remain in their authoritative stores and may be rendered through a selected component.\n\nA complete ReAct identity is launchable when its declared required dependencies/inputs and runtime compatibility resolve. It does not need a workItem/spine graph. Abstract components remain discoverable in the library/editor without being presented as complete agent choices.\n\n## Observed starting point and confidence\n\n- Current source has four mode identity documents: AUTO, IDEATE, DRAIN and AUDIT; cold-auto shares AUTO. GOAL, GRADE and TEST currently use registry contracts without their own mode documents.\n- modes/registry.ts independently authors behavioral contract prose consumed by mode:get/set and coord:orient. Existing mode blueprints deliver another definition through stack composition. The IDEATE blueprint lacks the registry's GOAL-local review/delegated-build exception.\n- psu's interactive picker intentionally offers only the su role. The launch code already accepts an explicit stack or roles[].stack, and a separate identity library discovers local, installed (including Cupboard) and built-in sources.\n- Slots are currently a platform vocabulary; identity files cannot invent arbitrary slot semantics. The loader handles inheritance and rejects cycles/exclusive conflicts. This inspection did not establish a sufficient depth/size bound on every dependency path; the compiler work must verify and bound those inputs.\n- The SU launch artifact compiler handles source, prompt and runtime state. Resource bundle resolution/provisioning has a separate existing boundary. Current mode prompt attachment is not proof that arbitrary non-prompt bundles reach the SU consumer.\n- role is overloaded. Source inspection traced persona/model configuration, signed authorization, advertised tool catalogs, fleet/work assignments, goal launch-function settings, workflow participants, responsibility addressing, tool guidance/quotas and unrelated routine/protocol keys. The detailed inspection remains in the appendix.\n- In SU bearer sessions, a role label can narrow advertised tools while authenticated isSuperuser supplies authority. In role-scoped sessions the signed role participates in capability lookup and tool allowlists. Neither 'role is only persona' nor 'role is always permission' accurately describes current code.\n- These are source findings from the recorded inspection, not proof of actual live IDEATE delivery, configured grant values, all installed third-party packages, or production use of every legacy path.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — One composition path and complete coverage.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The owner asked for one reusable identity composition path for all SU inputs.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every reusable SU contribution, including generated task/operational context, is declared through the identity composition path. Enumerate source, consumer, inclusion/refresh policy and provenance. Fixed text and provider-rendered text are stackable contributions in the same pipeline. The package declares how live values are supplied; it does not export live session data or credentials as reusable assets.\",\"falsifier\":\"A required fixed or generated component bypasses the manifest resolver, lacks source/refresh provenance, or silently uses stale or missing live data.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inspect the resolved component graph and delivered input receipts for fixed and generated fixture components; run both resolution and current-value refresh checks.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/hive-local-blueprint.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — One definition per behavior.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The owner asked to eliminate two separately authored mode behavior definitions.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Mode and specialist behavior is authored once in identity packages. Mode tools, orientation, prompts and recovery consume that definition. Remove independently maintained registry contracts, prompt/addendum copies and redundant selection maps after their consumers migrate. Generated compatibility views may remain.\",\"falsifier\":\"A mode tool or delivered prompt still selects a separately authored registry behavior after its identity definition changes.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Change a fixture definition and compare mode:get/set and live identity resolution; assert obsolete registry prose is not selected.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/mode/set.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Derived mode catalog.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The runtime needs a generated, validated mode catalog with protected authority.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Trusted identity manifests supply mode ids, descriptions, definition references, axes, implications, subject requirements and supported activation/launch metadata. Generate and validate runtime catalog/types/discovery from those declarations. Enforced policy implementations stay code-backed; untrusted package metadata cannot create authority.\",\"falsifier\":\"An untrusted manifest can change enforced authority, or generated discovery/activation disagrees with the trusted manifest.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Exercise catalog generation with valid and malicious manifests; compare runtime activation and authorization decisions.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/mode/set.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Correct component and mode composition.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The owner needs finite, correct composition of multiple modes and components.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Add GOAL, GRADE and TEST components and distinct supported mode axes; retain AUTO/cold-auto exclusivity and legal overlays. Reconcile GOAL+IDEATE, GOAL+GRADE and GRADE+TEST according to existing owner decisions. Fixed/generated context and operational declarations compose deterministically; input order cannot silently drop a component or defeat its merge policy.\",\"falsifier\":\"A legal mode combination loses a component, an incompatible exclusive claim is accepted, or implications produce an unauthorized mode.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run a combination matrix through the identity compiler and mode activation; assert explicit conflict and authority outcomes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/hive-local-blueprint.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Actual resource and operational effects with ReAct.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Blueprints must contribute usable resources and settings while SU remains ReAct.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Bundled knowledge, rubrics, callable recipes, tool/provider requirements, model defaults and supported plan/goal/datatype/event/rule resources reach their existing consumers. Merely rendering their names as prompt text is insufficient. The agent still selects actions through its ReAct loop; a composed identity can launch without a workflow graph.\",\"falsifier\":\"A declared resource or model/tool setting appears only in prose, fails to reach its typed consumer, or ReAct launch requires a workflow spine.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Resolve a bundled fixture and observe resource consumers and launch settings; perform a multi-turn ReAct action choice without a workflow graph.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/install-blueprint-core.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Consistent resolution, preserved briefs and observable delivery.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The owner requires existing fleet and goal briefs and delivery effects to survive identity migration.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"CLI/GUI launch, mode:get/set/list, orientation, peer changes, native hooks, live attach/detach and resume consume the same component selection model. Existing fleet-leader, goal kickoff/portfolio/obligation and turn-start/carry/orient composers remain canonical. Identity bindings reuse them at their existing lifecycle points and preserve eligibility, source snapshot sharing, budgets, diagnostics, unknowns, reminders/progress effects, cursors and acknowledgements. Requested, prepared, applied and failed states stay distinct. A single composition model does not require collapsing distinct sinks into one text/template format.\",\"falsifier\":\"A selected fleet/goal component replaces its current composer or changes diagnostics, source scope, sink budget, cursor, ACK, reminder or progress behavior without an explicit accepted reason.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Compare before/after composer outputs and delivery receipts on identical fixtures; exercise mode attach, orientation and resume.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/leader-brief.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Reproducible definitions with current context.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Identity revisions must stay pinned while current operational context refreshes.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Pin package/document/provider/template revisions and component selection. Fresh launch, warm/cold recovery and relevant SU fleet/goal replacement paths preserve these pins while refreshing declared live values from current sources. Record resolved input snapshots/provenance for historical replay; never substitute a historical snapshot for a required fresh read. New live values need not create a new identity package version.\",\"falsifier\":\"A pinned session silently adopts v2, required current values remain stale, or an activation failure is reported as Applied.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Install two fixture revisions, relaunch and resume sessions, compare pinned definition and fresh source receipts, then inject activation failure.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/blueprint-release.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Verified migration.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The owner approved verified migration through normal shipment.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Reconcile old clauses and untracked context injectors with authority/source evidence, retaining intentional corrections and historical records. Verify actual component delivery, resource use, operational settings, negative cases and rollback before independent acceptance and normal deployment. Source-only findings remain labelled as such.\",\"falsifier\":\"A migrated path has no real-suite/native delivery proof, or final deployed delivery differs from the approved pinned selection.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Use the test ledger, current-build native launch, applied revision receipts and deployed run to verify distinct source, test, live and deployment planes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/su-persona-identity-receipt.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/lib/psu-resume-lifecycle.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — One identity selection and scalable composition.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The owner wants one installed identity picker with SU as the default.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"CLI and GUI offer SU by default and discover eligible installed identities through the existing catalog with pagination. Abstract components remain discoverable in the library/editor. Preview/customize the selected composition and save it as a named identity in the same library; never enumerate every possible combination. Broken/incompatible entries remain visible with a reason.\",\"falsifier\":\"A compatible installed identity is absent from CLI/GUI, SU is not the default, invalid entries lack reasons, or composition preview and launched spec disagree.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Exercise built-in and Cupboard-installed fixtures through CLI and GUI selection, pagination, preview and saved composition; compare launch spec.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/psu-launcher.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/lib/psu-launcher-fork.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Generic core with optional domain integrations.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The generic identity core must not force SU-specific assignment or launch fields.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Assignment, fleet, goal and launch-slot machinery is required only by selected components that use it. An unrelated identity must launch, compose and refresh declared context without SU assignment/launch-slot fields or work-item state. Preserve existing SU membership, resource settings, authenticated capabilities, quotas, addressing and history through scoped adapters; composing a prompt cannot silently change those records.\",\"falsifier\":\"A generic identity is rejected for missing SU fields, or composing identity text changes SU permissions, membership, quotas or responsibility routing.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run generic and SU launch fixtures through the same resolver; assert no SU fields required for the generic path and unchanged role-policy decisions for SU.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/role-launch-spec.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/identity-management.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Single authoring and compilation path\n\nUse existing blueprint manifests, slots, inheritance, bundle references, library/Cupboard installation and the compiled specification. Do not create a second identity database, second mode runner or separate preset format. A named identity is an existing package declaring a complete composition.\n\nThe resolution flow is: named identity + selected/applicable components -> validate and pin one composition -> load fixed content, resolve declared current content, and resolve resource/configuration declarations through their consumers -> deliver/apply the effective inputs -> record what was supplied. The agent then uses its normal ReAct loop. Active modes or host assignments may select components where that integration is present; they are not prerequisites for the generic composition engine.\n\nPackage reusable platform instructions and context-producing declarations as well as optional resources, retaining existing sealed precedence. 'Bundlable' and 'overridable by an arbitrary publisher' are different properties. Extend existing descriptor/compiler input and resolver seams where needed. Store credential references through the existing configuration system; never copy credentials into a distributable bundle.\n\nWhy: the user can distribute, inspect and reproduce the inputs of an SU agent while runtime information stays fresh and protected content keeps its intended precedence.\n\n### One component system for fixed content, current content and operational declarations\n\nA component may contribute any supported combination of:\n\n- Fixed content: for example the SU instructions or how to lead a fleet.\n- Current content: a declared provider/template reads the relevant source and renders the current goal, task, facts or fleet description.\n- Referenced resources: for example an installed knowledge pack, rubric or callable recipe.\n- Operational declarations: for example default model settings or required tool/provider references.\n\nThese are contributions within the same composition model, not four separate identity systems. Share component identity, dependencies, selection, provenance and merge/validation machinery. Attach source, inclusion and refresh metadata where appropriate. Keep type validation at consumer boundaries: the renderer consumes text, the launcher applies model settings, and the existing tool/resource providers consume their declarations.\n\nConcrete integration: a fleet-leadership component references its leadership document and the EXISTING buildLeaderBrief/fleet:leader-brief and applicable orientation integration, retaining the existing output shaping, eligibility and budget rules. A GOAL component references the existing kickoff/portfolio/obligation composers at their existing lifecycle points. It may also declare relevant resource/default references. The component selects existing producers; it does not query a few raw fleet tables and rebuild a summary. A summarization identity can instead provide instructions and a document/language input, requiring no fleet assignment, GOAL row or launch-slot key.\n\nGenerated content references its existing producer and inclusion/refresh policy through the current orientation/brief/host services. Extend their registration/selection seams only where required; do not add a second refresh/caching scheduler. Generated content preserves the existing inclusion/refresh policy it uses. Legacy allow/deny fixtures retain behavior. |\n| Responsibility routing | A message addressed to a registered responsibility reaches the correct scoped holder after persona/identity changes; history remains attributable. |\n| Version pinning | After installing v2, a v1-pinned session retains v1 component/provider/template definitions until explicit upgrade while refreshing required current source values. Replay can show the original input snapshot; rollback respects current authority. |\n| Delivery failure | A staged change, refused dependency or failed host injection cannot be reported as Applied; prior usable state and concrete failure are visible. |\n| Dependency graph | Cycles, missing versions, repeated ancestors, incompatible slots and depth/size expansion are handled deterministically with actionable origin paths. |\n| Lifecycle and ship | Fresh turn, warm turn, cold carry, resumed/replacement holder and deployed session consume the expected revision; tests/source render alone cannot stand in for live delivery. |\n\nUse canonical unit/integration/native host tests appropriate to each component, scoped source/type checks and recorded test/evidence ledgers. Prepare independent acceptance criteria before execution; do not fill gaps with self-authored pass claims. Runtime trials use controlled existing/test sessions where possible and observe existing budget/admission limits. Record cleanup and ensure no test leaks live mode or leadership state.\n\nPromotion follows the normal shared-tree commit, test gate and deploy process. Respect single ownership of live gate operations; never force deployment past a red gate. Final shipment requires the deployed identity consumers, not merely a local test result.\n\n## Design choices, alternatives and risks\n\n- Retaining registry contracts plus blueprints would retain measured IDEATE drift. Removing independent authorship while generating required lookup data resolves that source problem without removing runtime control.\n- Keeping both a role-persona picker and identity picker makes the user choose the agent twice. One named identity selection with optional facets matches the actual composition model; assignment and permission details remain inspectable internally.\n- Treating every identity facet as a standalone agent or enumerating all compositions would make the picker unusable. Show complete named choices and resolve selected parts on demand.\n- Letting packages invent arbitrary slot semantics makes composition and authority unpredictable. Extend a defined platform vocabulary with compatibility tests; allow reusable package authors to claim validated slots.\n- Requiring all identity blueprints to have a workflow spine contradicts the owner's ReAct architecture. Reuse non-workflow identity compilation and validate resources separately from action selection.\n- Creating separate prompt-composition systems for reusable text and current context would reproduce hidden injectors and drift. Use one component pipeline; source/refresh metadata explains how each contribution is obtained.\n- Treating SU assignments and launch slots as universal identity fields would force unrelated agents into Papercusp fleet concepts. Keep those as optional declared integrations.\n- Exporting live session values/credentials as reusable assets would create stale or sensitive bundles. Package their approved provider/template declarations and refresh policies; resolve values under the existing session authority.\n- The highest migration risks are hidden old consumers, contradictory text, privilege/claim changes from renamed fields, mixed versions on restart and missing resource consumers. The census, clause matrix, policy parity tests, pinned artifacts and native delivery evidence address these specific risks.\n\n## Scope and review boundary\n\nThis draft covers one generic identity component model for fixed/generated content and resource/configuration declarations, proves it through the SU/mode integration and a generic identity fixture, and migrates the installed identity launcher plus directly coupled SU adapters. Refactors to unrelated workflow engines, p2p systems, memory programs or operational incidents are out of scope. The source audit also excludes general authorization/role-gate replacement, new context refresh/caching infrastructure, replacement package/version/activation stores, and implementing every unused resource-kind enum. Only changes necessary to reference or adapt those current systems for the selected identities belong here.\n\nThe role inspection is source-backed but not exhaustive deployment proof.
