Refusing it would leave a pot permanently unable to install any identity over a dead administrator binding.\n\n2. **Readmitting a detached receipt.** P-006 'detached' was designed for user-edited memory/docs: releasing a resource whose content changed after install detaches the receipt, and the next prepare refuses 'package resource was edited; explicit review is required'. An ADOPTED resource (disposition 'unowned', never written by us) also lands 'detached' on release, so reinstalling an identity after uninstall over a reused administrator binding was refused forever. preparePackageResource now restarts a 'detached' receipt (as it does a 'deleted' one) when every external ref is disposition 'unowned', OR when the driver declares `readmitsChanged: true`. The pot-binding driver opts in (its create() already refuses any usable foreign choice, so re-admission cannot clobber an administrator's decision); the doc and memory drivers do NOT, so a user-edited doc still refuses 'changed' (package-doc-resources.integration.test.ts).\n\n3. **Rule:** kind-specific readmission belongs in the resource DRIVER (`readmitsChanged`), never in callers of preparePackageResource.\n\nFalsifiers: cupboard/blueprint-install-journal.integration.test.ts (retired foreign replaced; admin reused/re-pointed binding kept and re-bindable after admin removal), blueprint/package-doc-resources.integration.test.ts ('changed' refusal preserved).\n\n### D-037 — D-037 Bundled package content travels inside the identity release (vendored, clone-first, retained closure is the installed tier)\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; AUTO #894, P-020] Finding (code reading, to be proven by the P-020 integration test): a Cupboard identity that bundles a recipe/rule/rubric/knowledge-pack cannot install into a clean destination. install-blueprint-core resolves bundles through deps.resolvePackage, which defaults to resolveLocalBlueprintPackage (the INSTALLER's own recipe/rule/pack stores), and the launch compile (compileLaunchSpecificationArtifact -> compileBlueprintWithPackages) resolves them the same way. The signed release already pins every bundled package with its bytes, and commitBlueprintRelease retains them in .releases/<id>/<hash>/closure.json; its only reader (blueprint-release.ts readArchive) serves prompt maps and rollback, never package resolution.\nMeasured 2026-09-30 ~11:00Z: grep -rn 'closure.json' over packages/operator-core/lib (all non-test .ts) -> blueprint-release.ts only (readArchive + the commit writer); grep 'resolvePackage' in install-blueprint-core.ts/install-blueprint-io.ts -> production install passes none (defaults to resolveLocalBlueprintPackage); recipe/rule roots = env bundled dir + in-repo fallback + user subdir only.\n\nRuling:\n1. A blueprint repo VENDORS each bundled package as a self-describing dir at <blueprint dir>/packages/<kind>/<ref>/ (the same manifest+listing layout the local stores read).\n2. servedBlueprintSource (the one seam publish and install share) resolves bundled packages CLONE-FIRST from that dir, then the host stores, exactly as cloneFirstResolveExtends does for parents. The publisher signs the hash the installer recomputes by construction; a vendored package altered after signing changes its pin and is refused by the existing signed-manifest check.\n3. The retained closure.json of each ACTIVE installed release is the destination's installed-package tier: resolveLocalBlueprintPackage falls back to it when the host stores have no package of the requested ref/version. Host stores keep precedence when they hold the exact requested version, so nothing already installed is shadowed.\n4. No new store, no copy into the user package dirs (that would outlive uninstall and make the identity's content organic). Uninstall/rollback of the release removes/replaces the tier with the release, so bundled content follows the release lifecycle already journaled by P-014.\n\n### D-038 — P-020 finding: the launch compiler resolves identity grants over the same provider kinds as install (tool+recipe); destination recipe-provider conformance has no product surface yet\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; su-415552e6 under AUTO owner directive #894] Found by the P-020 integration test (cupboard/third-party-portability.integration.test.ts), read from source.\n\n1. **Measured defect, fixed.** Install (`capabilityGrantDepsForPot`, INSTALL_PROVIDER_KINDS) and the runtime grant policy (`readIdentityGrantPolicy`) resolve `tool` AND `recipe` providers for `grants.requires/optional`. The launch compiler's default resolver in blueprint/compile-packages.ts called `getPotCapabilityProviderBinding` with no `providerKinds`, which defaults to tools only. So an identity whose required class is served by a recipe provider installed, then failed every launch with `required capability class has no active pot provider binding`. Fix: new agent-identities/grant-provider-kinds.ts exports IDENTITY_GRANT_PROVIDER_KINDS = ['tool','recipe']; the compiler and install use it. identity-grants-port.ts keeps its identical literal for now: editing it would stale 8 peer proofs on other plans for a cosmetic change. Falsifier: the P-020 launch/attach case fails with the compiler line removed.\n\n2. **Three consents, in order, all artifact-bound.** A clean destination installs a third-party identity with a recipe-provided class through: class-contract consent (P-021) → destination conformance → recipe-provider consent (D-019, `capability_recipe_provider_consent_required`) → identity consent (D-034). No consent was merged or skipped.\n\n3. **Ceiling narrowing at inspection.** `narrowIdentityCapabilities` intersects exact sets; a pot ceiling is a glob envelope. The destination inspection narrows the provider's declared needs through `identityCeilingRefusal` first, as `resolvePackageSinkRecipeWearer` does at runtime.\n\n4. **Gap, owned follow-up.** No product tool records a RECIPE-provider conformance run at a destination: `classes:validate` validates tool providers only, and the only callers of `inspectIdentityRecipeClassProvider` are tests. For an identity that vendors its own recipe provider this is also circular: the recipe is not in the destination's stores until install, and install needs the passing binding first. The P-020 proof runs the real inspector and `recordProviderConformance` against the real destination registry, with a saved-recipe adapter that serves the release's pinned recipe bytes. That substitution is named in the test header. The product surface (for example, conformance of a self-provided vendored recipe inside install, from the verified closure, before the consent seat) is filed as a follow-up work item. It is not claimed as done by P-020.\n\n### D-039 — P-005 design: eight first-party platform classes as a code catalog; builtin provider contributions keep their shape and name class@major + verb; the binder validates first-party output against the class schema\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; su-415552e6 under AUTO owner directive #894]\n\n**Inventory (measured 2026-09-30 12:3xZ).** 16 builtin provider contributions across 10 builtin blueprints (`su`, `su.practice`, `su.fleet-leader`, `su.mode-{audit,auto,drain,goal,grade,ideate,test}`) name 8 internal function-path producers, which violates D-003 (never a function path). All 8 are produced IN-PROCESS by 4 consumers: `turn-start-orientation.ts` (su/su.practice/su.mode-goal bind), `agent-tools/coordination/tools/orient.ts`, `agent-tools/goals/start.ts`, and `agent-tools/fleet/leader-brief.ts`. The workspace `capability_class_registry` holds 0 rows. Third-party identities already use the class form (`inputKind capability-provider`, `producerRef == ref == class@major`, P-004/P-010/P-020). **Estimate:** 0 new runtime adapters (the producers are already in-process), 8 class contracts, 1 binder resolution path, 10 blueprint edits, and fixture updates in about 22 test files. Conformance is per-call output validation plus one committed conformance/regression suite, with no DB conformance rows (see below).\n\n**Classes.** A code catalog `FIRST_PARTY_CONTEXT_CLASSES` (orchestrator blueprint module) is the single source (derive rung). Each entry has an id, version `1.0.0`, one verb, an output kind of text or json, an output JSON Schema, and `providerRef first-party:<module>:<export>`:\n`papercusp.mode-state@1 read` (json) · `papercusp.current-assignment@1 read` (json) · `papercusp.coord-orientation@1 compose` (json) · `papercusp.fleet-leader-brief@1 read` (json) · `papercusp.turn-start-orientation@1 render` (text) · `papercusp.goal-kickoff@1 render` (text) · `papercusp.goal-portfolio@1 render` (text) · `papercusp.agent-obligations@1 render` (text).\n\n**Why not the P-004 capability-provider form.** Rerouting these outputs to `capability-provider`/`resource` would change their compiled input kinds and sinks (prompt text and operational settings would become JSON resources). It would also force pot-scoped compile resolution, which the root-su turn-start bind does not have. P-005 forbids that semantic change. So purpose, inputKind, refresh, ref and availability stay byte-identical, `producerRef` becomes the class@major, and a `verb` is added.\n\n**Schema (D-003 enforcement).** Every provider contribution's `producerRef` must be a `class@major` and must name its contract `verb`. Function paths are refused at parse. `capability-provider` keeps `producerRef == ref`.\n\n**Binder.** A setting or prompt-file provider contribution resolves its producerRef in the first-party catalog. An unknown class, a verb mismatch, or a text/json kind mismatch against the inputKind throws, because no in-process producer exists for it. Each produced value is validated against the class output schema (`compileJsonSchema`). A required mismatch throws `output refused: schema-mismatch`. An optional mismatch becomes an omitted receipt with `errorRef capability-output:schema-mismatch`, mirroring D-013. First-party output has no 16 KiB cap: host budgets (orientation char budget, the sink evaluator) still govern delivery. Receipts carry `classRef` (the exact `papercusp.<x>@1.0.0`) and `providerRef`.\n\n**Publication boundary.** The namespace `papercusp` is platform-reserved. The P-021 class-contract import refuses it as `platform-shadow` even when the destination holds no rows. First-party classes are NOT seeded into the per-workspace DB registry: that would mean runtime seeding in every workspace for a tier that is code. Making them bindable by third-party identities through pot bindings (P-004 path) is not in P-005. P-012 may add catalog-backed `classes:list/get` discoverability if its grant classes need it.\n\n**Semantics preserved.** Delivered bytes, setting values, omissions, receipt statuses and outputRevisions are unchanged. outputRevision is `sha256(value)` and is independent of producerRef. Only the metadata changes: resolved-input and receipt `producerRef` (function path -> class@major), plus added classRef/providerRef. A one-time launch-spec revision change is expected. Regression: a golden file of (identity, contributionId, status, outputRevision) captured from the PRE-migration binder for fixed inputs, asserted equal after migration. A per-class conformance test runs representative first-party values through the schema, and a mutation probe shows the schema check fails a malformed value.\n\nRelated: P-005, P-012, P-004, D-003, D-013, D-015\n\n### D-040 — P-012 design: grants are exact class@version refs; a governed wearer's tools/list is its kernel-admitted set at launch, re-announced on attach; launch refuses a required need above the ceiling; one grant tool-reach function\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; su-415552e6 under AUTO owner directive #894]\n\n**Inventory (read from source 2026-09-30 ~13:10Z).** Already built: class pins -> exact tool grants (`resolveIdentityGrantEnvelope`, capability-envelope/blueprint-envelopes.ts:122); the shared ceiling predicate (`identityGrantToolFailure`, :80); install refusal (`validateIdentityInstallGrants`); per-call kernel enforcement with `capability_unsatisfied` (`checkIdentityGrantKernel`, reached from projected-tool-deps.ts:720); the grant-bearing role launch receipt (bootstrap-role.ts:611). Gaps found:\n1. `GrantsSchema.requires/optional` accept any string (orchestrator blueprint/schema.ts:1217). An identity can declare a tool id as a need, which then fails late as `provider-unbound`.\n2. The wearer's VISIBLE surface ignores grants. `resolveVisibleToolListings` (transport/_mcp-host.ts:2946) applies role/manifest/principal/app/seed filters only. A governed wearer on a trimmed seed cannot see class tools the seed lacks, and cannot reach them either, because `tools:find` and `tools:invoke` are themselves outside its grants. It also sees seed tools the kernel will deny. Nothing re-announces the surface when an attach changes the applied identity.\n3. Launch never evaluates the ceiling. The compiler (blueprint/compile-packages.ts:358) refuses only an UNBOUND required class, so a required need above the current ceiling launches a session whose every call is denied.\n4. [inferred, probe = a unit test of resolveIdentityGrantEnvelope with a recipe-kind pin] Runtime treats a recipe provider's `verbBindings` values (recipe ids) as tool names (blueprint-envelopes.ts:182). Install instead admits the recipe's inspected tool reach (identity-grants-port.ts:472). If so, a recipe-provided grant class closes the whole runtime envelope with `tool-unavailable`.\n\n**Decision.**\n(a) Needs are classes. A grant ref must be an exact `class@version` (the registry's CAPABILITY_CLASS_ID_PATTERN + CAPABILITY_CLASS_VERSION_PATTERN, mirrored in the orchestrator schema). A tool-id-shaped ref is refused at parse, and the message names the rule.\n(b) Launch. For a governed wearer, tools/list lists exactly the names the identity kernel admits. It evaluates them by calling the SAME `checkIdentityGrantKernel` per listed name, with one state read and a per-listing memoized policy read, so there is no second decision path. The claim-timing check is stubbed, because it narrows WHEN, not WHAT. The admitted set replaces the `?tools=` seed for that session. Recovery-only states list only the recovery door. Ungoverned sessions are byte-unchanged.\n(c) Attach. After each tools/call on a connection that has listed, a throttled recheck (at most one per 5s per session) compares the identity surface key: applied specificationRevision, launch row id:xmin, and control generation. On a change it recomputes the admitted set and fires `notifications/tools/list_changed` when the set differs. Visibility converges on the first call after an attach. Authority never depends on visibility: the kernel stays exact per call.\n(d) Explicit refusal. The launch compiler evaluates each pinned grant class's tool reach against the current pot/role ceiling with `identityGrantToolFailure`, through an injectable policy reader. A required class above the ceiling refuses the compile (`input-invalid`, naming class, tool and cause). An optional one is not pinned: under the existing envelope rule, an optional class absent at compilation cannot acquire authority later. Install refusal and per-call denial are unchanged.\n(e) One grant tool-reach function, used by install, compile and runtime: `verbBindings` values for a tool provider, and the inspected recipe pins' `toolNames` for a recipe provider (D-019). Gap 4's probe decides whether this changes runtime behaviour; if it does, that change is the fix.\n\n**Non-goal.** A blueprint OPERATION's `policy.requiredTools` is an accepted-operation worker ceiling, not an identity need. It stays tool-named, and the kernel already intersects it.\n\n**Falsifiers (P-012 tests).** Schema refuses `work_items:claim` in grants.requires. tools/list for a governed wearer whose trimmed seed lacks the class tool lists that tool and omits an ungranted seed tool. The attach recheck fires list_changed exactly once when the applied revision changes the admitted set. Compile refuses a required class whose tool is outside the ceiling. The recipe-provider envelope admits the recipe's reach.\n\n### D-041 — P-012 refinement of D-040(b)/(d): unresolved identity states do not narrow the listing; an unreadable ceiling does not refuse a compile\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; su-415552e6 under AUTO owner directive #894]\n\nAmends D-040 in two places, found while implementing it.\n\n1. **(b) Recovery-only states.** D-040 said recovery-only states list only the recovery door. Implemented instead: only a GOVERNED resolution narrows tools/list. An unresolved one keeps the listing unchanged; the kernel still denies every call except the door. Unresolved means stale-artifact, no-launch-record, policy-unavailable, identity-recovery, revoked, or authority unavailable. WHY: those states are routinely transient at connect time. A carry-respawn successor lists its tools 2-5s before its first turn converges the activation (EI-23703586803892464), and ungoverned sessions hit them too. A client that ignores list_changed would then be stuck with a one-tool surface for the whole session. Narrowing would buy no authority, because the kernel stays exact per call.\n2. **(d) Unreadable ceiling.** The compile refuses only on a DEFINITE outside-ceiling or tool-unavailable verdict for a required class's reach. If the ceiling cannot be read (unregistered target, ambiguous role, store down), the compile is not refused. Otherwise preview/install compiles without a registered pot or role would break, and the per-call kernel still denies what it cannot vouch for. Role comes from the launch (role-launch-spec passes input.role).\n\nCode: capability-envelope/identity-tool-surface.ts (resolveIdentityToolSurface, recheckListedIdentitySurface), transport/_mcp-host.ts (identityAdmittedListings, withIdentitySurfaceRecheck), blueprint/compile-packages.ts (refuseRequiredGrantsAboveCeiling). Install now also uses grantProviderToolReach (D-040(e): one reach function).\n\n### D-042 — P-017 finding: identity install must claim bundled event keys and run the async-rule install check; otherwise a third-party async hook is inert in a clean destination\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; su-415552e6 under AUTO owner directive #894] Found while mapping AUTO-BAR-R-8-P-017 (\"both hook modes ... without registry pre-seeding\") to the P-020 journey, whose listing still reads hooks.async: []. Read from source; to be proven by extending cupboard/third-party-portability.integration.test.ts.\n\n**Observed (code reading, [inferred] until the test runs).** (1) `checkAsyncRuleInstall` (agent-identities/identity-async-rules.ts:236, D-027 §1: an async rule installs only when `on` is ONE active catalogued key and `fire` is a valid class verb) is called ONLY by standalone rule install (cupboard/install-rule-io.ts:35). Identity install (cupboard/install-blueprint-core.ts, install-blueprint-io.ts, blueprint-install-journal.ts, blueprint-release.ts) never calls it; 0 matches. (2) A standalone Cupboard event install CLAIMS its key (install-event-io.ts defaultSeedRegistry -> claimEventKey, D-026, contributor stamped from the install via registryInputFromPackage). Identity install never claims a BUNDLED event package's key. (3) Migrations seed no event keys (1170-event-key-registry.sql), so a clean destination's registry is empty. Net: an identity that bundles its own event package plus an async rule installs, and wearing it writes subscription rows (session-package-resources.ts:216 -> replaceIdentityRuleSubscriptions). But the key is uncatalogued, so the fire-time re-check refuses. The hook is silently inert, and D-027 §1's 'a bad rule fails before a wearer attaches it' does not hold for identities.\n\n**Decision.** 1. Identity install claims every bundled `event` package key through the SAME path as a standalone event install (`registryInputFromPackage` + `claimEventKey`, contributor = the install's observed listing@version). It runs as a P-006 journal resource of the release: uninstall releases a key only this release claimed, and a key held by core/plugin/another listing is left untouched and reported (D-026). 2. After the bundled keys are claimed and class contracts/provider bindings resolve, identity install runs `checkAsyncRuleInstall` for every bundled async rule and refuses BEFORE activation (typed code, e.g. `async_rule_not_installable`, naming rule + reason). 3. The P-017 acceptance journey adds an event package and an async rule firing the third party's own class verb. It asserts the listing/consent surface, the claimed key, per-wearer subscription rows at launch and attach, a reaction planned per wearer, refusal of an async rule on an uncatalogued key, and uninstall releasing the claimed key and cancelling subscriptions.\n\n**Scope guard.** Implementation lives in cupboard/ install + journal code. It does NOT touch role-launch-spec.ts, blueprint/compile-packages.ts, orchestrator blueprint/schema.ts or agent-identities/source.ts, which are held for su-b0451bbf's gate cut until they release them (by 17:00Z at the latest).\n\n### D-043 — P-008 deferred to follow-up WI-10004263 under D-011; acceptance BAR R-4 leaves this plan's rubric in the batched amend\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; su-415552e6 under AUTO owner directive #894] D-011 left the call to the implementer: before final closure, either finish optional P-008 or explicitly defer it to an owned follow-up. It is deferred.\n\n**Why.** Measured by reading source on 2026-09-30, P-008 is a design project, not an add-on:\n(1) memory writes carry no worn-identity stamp (agent-tools/memory/remember.ts);\n(2) harness_shared.knowledge_pack_candidates is fleet-global, and autoAdoptPendingCandidates promotes EVERY pending row into fleet-lessons, so identity candidates would need target/workspace columns (a migration), workspace-scoped listing, and a sweep exclusion to stay un-promoted;\n(3) materializeCandidateIntoPack writes only into fleet-lessons, and an installed third-party pack is an immutable release closure (D-037), so the adoption target needs its own rules.\nFinishing it would put a migration and a change to the memory write path on the critical path of a plan whose core acceptance (P-017) does not depend on it (D-011).\n\n**What changes.**\n(a) P-008 is set dropped, with this decision as the note.\n(b) Follow-up **WI-10004263** (papercusp feature queue, linked `relates` to WI-10003317) carries the measured design notes and the R-4 outcome as its acceptance.\n(c) The acceptance rubric's R-4 ('Reviewed learning feedback') is removed in the ONE batched rubric amendment that already has to land before re-vetting (vetting post 1151122), because a deferred item cannot be accepted by this plan. No other BAR changes meaning because of this decision.\nRelated: P-008, P-017, D-011\n\n### D-044 — P-017 as built: amends D-042 on the event-key contributor, the ownership stamp, rollback, and a one-line launch-compiler edit made with the file holder's approval\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[self-imposed; su-415552e6 under AUTO owner directive #894] Amends D-042. Everything below was read from source after implementation. Test evidence: cupboard/third-party-portability.integration.test.ts passed 5/5 at 14:37Z (TEST_FILE_RESULT status=passed).\n\n**As built (differs from D-042's text).**\n1. **Contributor.** A bundled key's registry contributor is `cupboard:blueprint:<blueprintId>` (`bundledEventKeyContributor`, blueprint/package-event-key-resources.ts). D-042 said listing@version. The key follows the listing, not one release, so a newer release of the same listing refreshes its own claim instead of colliding with it. A key held by any other contributor is refused with `event-key-held` and never taken over.\n2. **Ownership stamp.** Each claim stamps `created_by = cupboard:install-blueprint#<writeKey>` in the claiming transaction (`eventKeyWriteStamp`). Recovery and deletion act only on a row that carries this exact operation's stamp. A refresh re-stamps the row, so the earlier release's cleanup finds it changed and leaves it. Deletion locks the row (FOR UPDATE) and removes it only if the fingerprint and stamp are unchanged.\n3. **Resource kind.** The key is a workspace-wide P-006 journal resource of kind `event-key`: one resource however many pots install the release. A rollback that would re-create a released key refuses (`event key ... was released; reinstall the release to claim it again`) instead of re-claiming it silently.\n4. **Async-rule check.** `checkAsyncRuleInstall` runs for every bundled async rule before activation (cupboard/install-blueprint-io.ts). Keys the SAME release is claiming count as catalogued (`claimingKeys`). A refusal is 422 `async_rule_not_installable` with every refusal listed (install-blueprint-core.ts). An install path with no checker configured refuses with 500 `async_rule_checker_unavailable`. It never skips the check.\n5. **Consent.** `event` joins `recipe` and `rubric` as shared content in identity install consent (`SHARED_CONTENT_KINDS`, cupboard/identity-install-consent.ts). A claimed key is workspace-visible, so it is consented, not package-private.\n\n**Scope-guard amendment.** D-042 said this work would not touch blueprint/compile-packages.ts. It needed one line: the launch compiler's event branch now resolves `resolveInstalledEvent(request.ref, only('event'))`, so a vendored event resolves from <repo>/packages/event/ (D-037). Before the edit, a vendored event was unresolvable at launch. su-b0451bbf holds that file for their gate cut and approved this exact line (coord msg muo7acxk). I confirmed it was done (muo7c2ot). No other line of their held files (role-launch-spec.ts, orchestrator blueprint/schema.ts, agent-identities/source.ts) was touched.\n\n**Fixture lesson.** The first run of the journey was 4/5. The grant-policy reader in the fixture returned `bindings: []`, but production `readIdentityGrantPolicy` reads the pot's live bindings. So a second install saw a bound requirement with no current binding and failed with a false `capability_unsatisfied`/`provider-changed` (identity-grants-port.ts:458-465). The fixture now reads live bindings through `getPotCapabilityProviderBinding` with provider kinds ['tool','recipe'], the same kinds install resolves (D-038). Rule: a fixture that stands in for a policy reader must read the same live state production reads. A constant empty set there manufactures refusals.\nRelated: P-017, P-006, P-020\n\n### D-045 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-09-30\nAmendment-Id: pip-rubric-amend-rev2-to-rev3-1151277\nRequest-Hash: b2947e771de5c062f3a1158b4e29e0a867c3564f0473f6d3658cf0b0ea776817\nActor: su-415552e6-9f99-46c7-b29c-3a757e67cc62\nReason: Batched rev2->rev3 amend answering rubric-vetting post 1151122 (su-b42d4f67): R-4 removed (P-008 dropped, D-043); R-10 split from R-5 (P-011 fail-closed deny); R-11 split from R-6 (P-018 exactly-once per wearer); one atomic pass floor per bar with numbered BROKEN markers; per-bar scope map (token -> file + it() title); check files rebound to the files carrying each case. Measured: remember.ts:314 stamps writer session/workspace but no worn identity; knowledge-packs/candidates.ts:220 caps all pending rows globally, :275 lists globally, :500 writes only fleet-lessons, and :928 sweeps pending rows. Implement server-derived worn-identity provenance in memory metadata; an explicit proposal operation on knowledge_packs:candidates checks that the caller authored the memory, targets a recorded worn identity, and leaves visibility unchanged. Extend the existing candidate table with optional workspace/identity/target-pack fields, scoped dedup+cap+listing, and exclude identity candidates from the automatic fleet sweep. Existing decide_candidate deliberately adopts into a locally authored vendored pack and bumps its patch, or refuses installed/builtin targets, preserving D-037 immutable closure. Keep the existing fleet queue behavior. Source acceptance: real-PG tests for proposal, workspace isolation, sweep skip, local adoption/version bump, immutable refusal, dismissal, and unchanged memory metadata; focused existing suites remain green. No new tool, store, service, or schedule. All work remains one owned finite feature, WI-10004263.\n\n### D-048 — Identity memory proposals use the existing write-capable decision tool\nDate: 2026-10-01\nWI-10004263 implementation refinement to D-047: action:'propose' lives on knowledge_packs:decide_candidate (memory:write), while knowledge_packs:candidates remains a read-only workspace-scoped listing. This preserves the current capability boundary, introduces no new verb, and leaves memory visibility unchanged. Identity adoption serializes access to the authored target pack across workspaces, restores authored files on write errors, updates the bundle pin, and removes the previous local attestation so the next publish can attest changed content. Installed/builtin closure refusal remains unchanged.\nMeasured: read packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/knowledge_packs/decide_candidate.ts (propose schema and memory:write), knowledge-packs/identity-learning.ts (writer/worn-at-write checks), candidates.ts (target lock, file rollback, pin update) in canonical staging on 2026-10-01. The pre-fix real-PG regression observed a source write error return pack_write_failed with the manifest nevertheless advanced from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1; identity-learning.integration.test.ts now guards rollback and retry. P-002 worker/sibling parity is done with committed WI-10003150 evidence: worker suite 23/23, Mac launcher 4/4, and real Mac snapshot-fold worker execution/cleanup pass. Remaining P-004/P-006 work is blocked on current-build packaged-candidate/peer acceptance and independent grading-integrity for spec-quality scorecard EI-26018911173204868.\n\n**Next:** Route independent grading-integrity for scorecard EI-26018911173204868, then retry plans:start. Continue P-004 packaged-candidate/peer lifecycle evidence and P-006 matrix acceptance; keep final-release and real P2P shipment claims separate.\n\n## Background\nAvi observed agents waiting for green main despite available staging and asked for infrastructure that lets them always test current code before promotion. Prior staging-first guidance and runtime-wait plans are shipped; this effort fills execution and discoverability gaps. Current :3170 is a request-serving operator, not a separate full background/federation system. The headless Tauri verifier already snapshots code and can create an isolated database. The Mac rig composer omits sibling workers (WI-10003150); current staging source freshness repair WI-10003374 is owned elsewhere. No duplicate LIVE_GATE_OPS or desktop release cutter.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Agents testing Papercusp changes before promotion.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Agents wait for green main even when current code can exercise the property; the staging API alone does not execute every runtime.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Agents select and prepare a maintained current-build route with measured provenance, private mutable state and verified cleanup/restoration.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Replacing CI or creating a separate development worktree.\",\n    \"Weakening final-candidate, independent GO or 72-hour P2P release conditions.\",\n    \"Claiming staging proof verifies an actual production shipment.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:14\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:16\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:20\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:22\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:23\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:25\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:29\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:32\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:34\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:37\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:40\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Cover all supported pre-release functional test classes on current code instead of requiring main promotion.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a0dfc7-e76d-78b1-90be-b64946073316:40\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"observed-fact\",\n      \"text\": \"The serving-runtimes registry separates the staging API, background runner, desktop, peer and packaged-candidate routes.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"code:packages/operator-core/lib/serving-runtimes.ts\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"product-choice\",\n      \"text\": \"Reuse maintained runtime runners and keep final-release acceptance separate.\",\n      \"material\": true,\n      \"resolved\": true,\n      \"decisionRef\": \"D-001\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"scenarios\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-001\",\n      \"title\": \"Test current API behavior\",\n      \"kind\": \"normal\",\n      \"trigger\": \"An agent changes API behavior.\",\n      \"action\": \"Select the containing staging build and verify its loaded source before exercising it.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Attributed API evidence is available before main promotion.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-3\",\n        \"R-4\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-002\",\n      \"title\": \"Run mutable background and migration tests\",\n      \"kind\": \"normal\",\n      \"trigger\": \"An agent needs background or migration behavior.\",\n      \"action\": \"Prepare the disposable private runtime with distinct DB, workspace, device, network/service ports and IPC identity.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Test writes stay inside the owned test runtime.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-5\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-003\",\n      \"title\": \"Reject an incomplete peer payload\",\n      \"kind\": \"failure\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A native or peer test is missing a required worker, valid hash or host prerequisite.\",\n      \"action\": \"Run the existing launcher preflight before activation.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"The invalid candidate is refused before modifying the target.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-2\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-004\",\n      \"title\": \"Restore after success or failure\",\n      \"kind\": \"recovery\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A mutable run finishes or fails.\",\n      \"action\": \"Teardown owned resources and compare the pre/post baseline.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Cleanup and restoration receipts account for the complete owned lifecycle.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-6\",\n        \"R-7\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-005\",\n      \"title\": \"Preserve the shipment boundary\",\n      \"kind\": \"boundary\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A claim concerns what actually shipped or a physical multi-machine property.\",\n      \"action\": \"Use the exact release artifact or distinct real peers required by that property.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Current-build evidence does not impersonate final-release or physical-peer acceptance.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-4\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  \"considerations\": [\n    {\n      \"category\": \"Shared state and concurrent custody\",\n      \"disposition\": \"covered\",\n      \"reason\": \"File/resource locks protect peer custody; mutable runners isolate state and verify cleanup.\",\n      \"scenarioIds\": [\n        \"SC-002\",\n        \"SC-003\",\n        \"SC-004\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"category\": \"Hardware and credentials\",\n      \"disposition\": \"covered\",\n      \"reason\": \"The capability matrix requires explicit prerequisites and unmeasured external cases.\",\n      \"scenarioIds\": [\n        \"SC-003\",\n        \"SC-005\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Runnable current-build coverage.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Every supported pre-release test class has a maintained staging execution route; main promotion must not be a prerequisite.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The capability matrix enumerates unit/integration, API, background/federation, migration, desktop/native, multi-machine P2P/Git and candidate install/upgrade, with executable routes and explicit resource/credential prerequisites.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A supported functional test can only proceed after main promotion, or an uncovered runtime is reported ready.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Inspect the capability matrix against serving-runtimes and actual runner contracts; execute each declared preflight and verify current source identity. Run registry/runtime selection tests; require explicit residue for unsupported hardware or missing credentials.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/serving-runtimes.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Faithful and isolated execution.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Test runtime payloads and ownership must match exercised behavior without mutating shared live state accidentally.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A transported current-build payload exposes each required emitted worker and sibling asset with a valid content hash.\",\"falsifier\":\"An incomplete payload is admitted, a test reaches live data/identity unexpectedly, or runtime identity is unmeasured.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\",\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run worker recipe/launcher failure injection, execute emitted worker under plain Node, and validate actual child environment/isolation and cleanup on fresh current-build instances. Inspect migration backup/restore before shared-rig use.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/worker-scripts-bundled.test.ts\",\"papercusp-desktop/test/mac-vm-health.test.js\",\"apps/operator/lib/verify-tauri-headless-isolated-db.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.e2e.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Private mutable runtime.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Mutable/full-background current-build tests must not write through live database, identity or IPC ownership.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each mutable/full-background test child uses a database, workspace identity, device (keychain) identity, network/service ports and IPC endpoints distinct from the live host.\",\"falsifier\":\"A current-build child starts with the live database URL, workspace identity, device keychain identity, network/service port or IPC endpoint.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inspect actual launched child environment, HOME/keychain and device pubkey, database, network/service-port and IPC bindings; prove a child write sentinel never appears in the live workspace.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/verify-tauri-headless-isolated-db.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.e2e.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Restorable test lifecycle.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Current-build test runs must prove cleanup and restoration, not only startup isolation.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each mutable/full-background test run emits a teardown receipt proving its owned resources are gone.\",\"falsifier\":\"A test exits while its owned child process, database or IPC endpoint remains without a cleanup receipt.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run success and failure-path children, verify process, database and IPC cleanup against their owned-resource census, and retain teardown receipts.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.e2e.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Restored test baseline.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Current-build test runs must restore any prior state they change and retain evidence of restoration.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each mutable/full-background test run emits a restoration receipt matching its prior-state baseline.\",\"falsifier\":\"A test exits with a changed baseline or without a restoration receipt.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Compare success and failure-path pre/post baseline fingerprints; inspect protected rig backup and restoration evidence.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.e2e.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Agents choose execution before waiting.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Agents must discover concrete maintained staging test routes before parking on main.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Existing test/runtime tools, wait guards and canonical prompt projection name the proper runner, prerequisites, provenance and evidence scope, preserving only explicit final-release exceptions.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A generic main wait is admitted despite available current-build work, or staging proof is presented as actual production shipment proof.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise runtime resolution and wait guards for API, background, desktop and multi-machine cases including unknown and final-release negative controls; verify canonical rendered guidance.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-runtime-wait-guard.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/desktop-install/__tests__/papercusp-files.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Verified behavior and durable evidence.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Deliver measured readiness and preserve the P2P final-candidate, independent GO and72h requirements.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Every supported test route has attributed current-build execution evidence, explicit unmeasured external cases, and a separate final-release evidence boundary.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A route is declared universally usable without its real runtime evidence, or existing P2P ship conditions are weakened.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\",\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Review and replay the complete capability matrix on actual matching runtimes; verify source/hash, data isolation and teardown receipts. Physical/multi-host acceptance must run on real distinct peers; no mock or unit-only substitution. Account for every row and residue before independent review.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/worker-scripts-bundled.test.ts\",\n        \"papercusp-desktop/test/mac-vm-health.test.js\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.integration.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/staging-test-environments.e2e.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\nExtend serving-runtimes, acceptance-runtime-wait-guard, testing tools, verify-tauri-headless.sh, bundle-host-common.sh and current rig composer/launcher. Search the existing deployment-driver/runner contracts before adding any durable surface. Keep edits in canonical staging; generated build snapshots outside source are allowed, no alternate development worktree needed. Reuse WI-10003150 for worker parity and coordinate with WI-10003374 rather than duplicating its owner. Isolated runtime ownership must not start a second writer against live DB/identity. Candidate packaging can be tested before promotion; verification of actual production shipment remains a distinct final step.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-006 | live |\n| R-2 | P-002 | live |\n| R-3 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006 | live |\n| R-5 | P-003 | live |\n| R-6 | P-004 | live |\n| R-7 | P-004 | live |\n\nP-001 owns the capability matrix audit and its own first-class spec. P-003/P-004 also have distinct item-specific specs. This map assigns each BAR to the item that discharges it, avoiding duplicated projected behavior across items. The integration and e2e files exist and exercise registry isolation and local rig payload; real background-child, peer, installer and cleanup assertions must be extended during P-003/P-004/P-006. Existing paths are test contracts, not claims of live acceptance.\n\n## Work\n- **P-001** `done` Audit supported test classes and existing execution routes; record source, runtime ownership, data isolation, required platform/credentials, and exact verification contract. No vague all-staging claim. — note: ← WI-10003384 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Repair worker/sibling-asset parity across host, packaged desktop and rig bundles, including rig transport and atomic launcher validation, with recurrence tests. Reuse WI-10003150. — note: Worker parity repaired and verified locally plus on the real Mac rig; WI-10003150 committed completion authority.\n- **P-003** `done` Extend existing isolated current-build runner for uncovered background/federation/migration runtime cases, with distinct database/identity/IPC ownership and cleanup. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10003392 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `todo` Connect current-build peer and packaged-candidate routes to the same provenance/isolation contract; verify prerequisites and lifecycle without requiring main promotion. blocked-by: P-001, P-002\n- **P-005** `done` Extend existing tools and canonical agent guidance to select runnable current-build routes and reject unjustified main waits while preserving legitimate final-release verification. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10003391 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `todo` Run framework and real-runtime acceptance across the explicit capability matrix; record remaining externally dependent cases honestly and complete the plan's ship review. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Scope and reuse\nOwner request is pre-release testing without green-main waits; it does not make staging evidence proof of an actual production shipment. This plan owns current-staging runtime preparation and agent execution routing; reuse their maintained artifacts without reopening their scoped tasks.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"host-memory-reduction-2026-09-27","title":"Host memory reduction: stop the tower thrashing on 251 GB","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-27","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Host memory reduction: stop the tower thrashing on 251 GB\nslug: host-memory-reduction-2026-09-27\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-27\nupdated: 2026-09-28\n---\n\n## Findings (measured 2026-09-27 01:00-01:40Z; WI-10003390)\n\nAt the incident: MemAvailable 13/251 GB, PSI memory full 50%, swap in/out 100-800 MB/s, load 349.\n\n| Consumer | RAM | Swap | Note |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Kernel slab, unreclaimable | 30 GB | - | 18.3 GB is kmalloc-8k from AppArmor aa_get_buffer (CVE-2026-45884, per-cpu hold underflow; exec-heavy workloads). Stopping processes does NOT free it. |\n| Kernel page tables | 14.5 GB | - | 10.7 GB is postgres: 63 GiB shared_buffers on 4 KB pages (huge_pages=try, only 618 hugepages reserved), about 580 backends each mapping it |\n| Postgres | 72 GB | 0 | shared_buffers 63 GiB pinned (MemorySwapMax=0), max_connections 512, many idle pool connections |\n| Concurrent operator-core typechecks | 7-13+ GB each | | 4 ran at once via pc-heavy (preempt-run path). This was the trigger. |\n| Operator hono-host procs (28) | 21 GB | 7.6 GB | one canonical-tree process 9.2 GB; glibc malloc arena ~1.3 GB per worker (memory 626a56e7) |\n| qemu VMs | 12 GB | 36 GB | Mac 32 GB + Win 16 GB configured, running for days |\n| Other node (179) | 13 GB | 14 GB | embed-sidecar 5.1 GB; lane-a-fed installed GUI sidecars 4.9 GB |\n| Other services | ~3 GB | ~23 GB | StoreWolfServer 4 GB, typesense 2.5, appflowy, openobserve, kokoro TTS 1.4 GB, docker rig-a/b 6.6 GB, plane/chatwoot/outline stacks |\n| VS Code / Chrome / GNOME | 8 GB | 20 GB | |\n| Agents themselves (claude 24 + codex 157 procs) | ~14 GB total | | NOT the problem |\n\nFalsified: unread socket queues (about 200 KB total); leaked tracefs instances (0); page cache pinning dying memcgs (drop_caches did not change them); stopping leaked test scopes frees slab (no change).\n\n## Items\n- **P-001** `todo` Reboot into the installed kernel 7.0.0-34 (default GRUB entry; NVIDIA 580 DKMS module already built for it). This reclaims the ~23 GB leaked slab and clears the 171 GB swap residue. Verify: kmalloc-8k active objects stay flat under exec load for 1 h. Owner-gated: stops every agent. Only likely, not verified, that 7.0 contains the CVE-2026-45884 fix; the patch landed in apparmor-next Jan 2026.\n- **P-002** `done` Postgres on huge pages: vm.nr_hugepages sized to shared_buffers plus huge_pages=on removes ~10 GB page tables. Right-size shared_buffers from pg_buffercache/hit-ratio evidence (candidate 63 to 24-32 GiB). Cut idle backends (pooling / lower pool sizes / max_connections). Needs a restart window. — note: D-021: page tables fixed by the reboot (D-002); huge_pages=on + shared_buffers 32 GiB already in place (peer lane WI-10002573); idle-backend trimming measured at ~0.1 GB reclaimable, so no change.\n- **P-003** `done` pc-heavy admission reserves memory for jobs already admitted (budget x admitted, not instantaneous MemAvailable, which ignores their future growth), closes the preempt-run bypass, and caps each admitted compile with a cgroup memory.high. — note: ← WI-10003409 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Same typecheck with far less memory: one shared incremental typecheck service (tsgo watch/LSP) answers `lint:tsc --files` for all agents instead of N full 8-13 GB compiles; plus project references so a file edit checks only its subgraph. — note: ← WI-10003404 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Operator memory: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX / jemalloc for hono-host workers; identify the 9.2 GB canonical-tree process; consolidate redundant operator instances. — note: ← WI-10003419 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `blocked` VMs on demand: stop the Mac/Win VMs when no rig job needs them (start on demand), or lower their RAM with a balloon. — note: Windows VM already inactive+disabled. Mac VM (papercusp-vm-mac.service, 32.6 GB resident + 8.4 GB reclaimable cache) is NOT idle: the P-203 fold is live (watchdog cursor 5b00878b at position 7824153, advancing, 04:05Z). D-001 approves idle-stop only when no rig job needs it. Unblocks when the fold finishes: then stop it, `systemctl --user disable` the boot auto-start, and make the rig entrypoints (vm-preflight.sh candidate) start it on demand. Detail: WI-10003412 checkpoint.\n- **P-007** `dropped` Idle services: owner decides which of StoreWolf/typesense/appflowy/plane/chatwoot/outline/openobserve/kokoro/rig containers/lane-a-fed GUI must stay resident; the rest get socket-activated or stopped. — note: Owner decision D-005 (2026-09-27): leave all idle services running. Measured 04:10Z: 91 Docker containers total 3.8 GiB, kokoro 0.2 GiB, StoreWolf not running — ~4 GiB of 251, not worth breaking something in use.\n- **P-008** `done` Leaked test fixtures: kopia-backup-guard.test.ts and pc-heavy.test.ts left infinite `sleep 0.1` loops running 20 days (9 scopes, about 10 forks/s each, feeding the AppArmor leak). Fix the teardown, and add a reaper for stale vitest run-u scopes. — note: ← WI-10003416 done\n- **P-009** `done` Swap policy: a 2 TB swapfile on the busy data drive lets the box thrash for minutes instead of shedding load. Prefer freezing heavy jobs over thrashing (PSI-driven), and consider zram / a smaller swap. — note: ← WI-10003441 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Leak alarm: alert on kmalloc-8k / SUnreclaim / nr_dying_descendants growth so a kernel leak surfaces in days, not weeks. — note: ← WI-10003418 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Durable reductions\n\n- **P-011** `done` build:typecheck on the shared service: route build:typecheck { project, files } (scopeToFiles) through the P-004 tsgo service instead of a fresh --incremental false compile. Measured 2026-09-27: 322 calls in 7 days, 280 on operator-core, 64 agents, 17.9 s avg, each a ~13 GB whole-project compile (about 40/day). Needs parity for its structured result (errors/byFile/otherErrors/syntaxBroken/semanticCheckIncomplete) and a CLI fallback, exactly as lint:tsc has. importance: high — note: ← WI-10003415 completed (done)\n- **P-012** `done` gitnexus-reindex: same fresh code graph (embeddings on) at a fraction of the memory. The hourly `system:gitnexus-reindex` full analyze (packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/gitnexus-reindex-action.ts) now peaks 19-24 GB per run (its P-004 heap cap was sized from a measured 10.4 GiB peak) and runs 90-166 min (the file documents 3,133 s full / 2,343 s steady tick). 11 of the last 15 runs failed (165-min timeout, exit 134, killed); each failure leaves incrementalInProgress set, which forces the next run into a full rebuild, so a ~20 GB process is resident about half of every day while the index stays stale. Find where the time and memory went (graph growth, embedding-cache restore, parse caches, 8 GB LBUG buffer pool, 16-worker pool) and fix it so a run completes inside its budget at a lower peak. Evidence in the gitnexus-reindex decision. importance: high — note: ← WI-10003426 done\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Owner choices 2026-09-27: no reboot yet; su executes the plan itself; VMs + federation install may be idle-stopped\nDate: 2026-09-27\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-27, AskUserQuestion answers] (1) Reboot into 7.0.0-34 = \"Not yet\". Do NOT reboot; P-001 stays deferred until the owner says so. The leak keeps growing at ~3 GB/day at the measured rate. (2) Plan approved; route = \"Approve — you do it\": su-5b9cde39 (and its carry successors) implements the items itself, one at a time, verifying each. No fleet. (3) Idle-stop approved ONLY for: the Mac + Windows VMs (papercusp-vm-mac.service, papercup-vm-win.service), to become start-on-demand when a rig job needs them; and the federation test install (~/.papercusp-lane-a-fed, two sidecars ~5 GB). NOT approved for idle-stop: the Restart/StoreWolf services (StoreWolf, typesense, AppFlowy/Plane/Chatwoot/Outline/OpenObserve stacks) and kokoro TTS. Leave those resident. Still honour \"without killing any agents\" (#686): freeze/serialize agent-launched jobs, never kill agents.\n\n### D-002 — Post-reboot corrections: P-003 premise falsified, P-002 page tables fixed by the reboot, P-001 still open (GRUB pins 6.17)\nDate: 2026-09-27\nMeasured: 2026-09-27 02:45-02:55Z, su-5b9cde39, after the owner's 02:07Z reboot.\n\n1. P-001 is NOT done. The reboot came back on 6.17.0-40-generic because /etc/default/grub has GRUB_DEFAULT=saved + GRUB_SAVEDEFAULT=true and `grub-editenv list` saved_entry pins the 6.17.0-40 advanced entry. 7.0.0-34 is only the top menu entry. The earlier claim that it was the GRUB default was wrong. The AppArmor/kmalloc-8k slab leak will rebuild. Switching kernels needs a one-shot `sudo grub-reboot` plus a reboot, and is owner-gated.\n\n2. P-002 page-table half is DONE by the reboot. All 34000 hugepages from /etc/sysctl.d/60-papercusp-hugepages.conf were reserved at boot, postgres huge_pages=try holds ~33k, and PageTables went from 14.5 GB to 1.8 GB. Remaining P-002 scope: huge_pages=on so a silent 4 KB fallback becomes a startup error, plus the shared_buffers right-sizing question.\n\n3. P-003's premise is FALSIFIED. (a) scripts/pc-heavy.sh _mem_clamp_slots caps the TOTAL slot count at MemAvailable/12GiB. Admitted-but-still-small jobs barely lower MemAvailable, so it already reserves for their growth. (b) --pc-heavy-internal-preempt-run is spawned at pc-heavy.sh:3346 after admission; it is how an admitted preemptible job runs, not a bypass. What actually let 4 compiles freeze the box: the real compile peak (13+ GB) is above the 12 GiB/slot budget, and 30 GB of leaked slab eroded the base. P-003 is rescoped to 'derive the per-slot budget from the measured compile peak'; the bigger lever is P-004 (shrink the compile itself), which owner question #698 is driving.\n\n### D-003 — P-004 route: shared tsgo API service for scoped lint:tsc; warm --incremental and --checkers are dead ends\nDate: 2026-09-27\nMeasured 2026-09-27 03:20-03:25Z (WI-10003404 checkpoint; scripts in .papercusp/scratch/tsc-mem/).\n\nBaseline: one operator-core compile = 17,712 files, 13.4 GB peak, 29 s, and every `lint:tsc --files=<one file>` pays it, so N concurrent agents = N x 13 GB.\n\nRejected, with evidence:\n- Warm tsgo --incremental (scratch tsbuildinfo): three runs all re-checked the whole program (6.54M types every time), 13.0-13.9 GB and 24-27 s check time. tsgo 7.0.2's --incremental --noEmit gives no win here.\n- --checkers 2: 11.8 GB / 45 s (-1.6 GB at 1.5x the time). --checkers 1: 10.4 GB / 92 s. GOMEMLIMIT=4GiB: 11.6 GB / 176 s (the memory is live, not GC slack).\n- Splitting a tests project that consumes src through project references: about 13 -> 6 GB per compile, but it is still N x 6 GB under concurrency and a large tsconfig/emit restructure. Deprioritized.\n\nChosen: one long-lived tsgo API server (typescript@7.0.2 `unstable/sync`: API.updateSnapshot + program.getSemanticDiagnostics(file)) answers SCOPED gate runs (--files / --mine) for every agent. Measured: project load 2.5 s / 3.6 GB; 20 error files checked in 0.95 s with 0 mismatches against a fresh --incremental false compile; 137 clean files in 2.7 s with 0 diagnostics; snapshot update + recheck after an edit 31 + 89 ms; a full-tree invalidateAll snapshot costs 0.95 s, so every request re-reads the whole tree and change detection is complete by construction (this is the answer to EI-487's staleness objection). Resident memory stays around 4-5 GB and is bounded by one full check (11.5 GB measured) no matter how many agents ask.\n\nScope: bare / --update / green-checkpoint runs keep the CLI full compile (the API's full-program pass took 71 s against the CLI's 24 s). The scoped path checks the named files plus the cause-aware widening candidates (files that textually reference a type name a named file exports), computed over all program files. When the service is unreachable it falls back to the CLI, and says so.\n\n### D-004 — P-004 scope correction: the service serves --files only; --mine stays on the full compile, and guidance now steers to --files\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27\nCorrects D-003's \"answers SCOPED gate runs (--files / --mine)\". Measured/read 2026-09-27 03:55Z, su-5b9cde39.\n\n--mine cannot be served. Its verdict (scripts/lib/tsc-baseline-gate.mjs decidePerFile, EI-18766822535373909) also fails on an error in ANY file absent from the baseline, anywhere in the program, because git-sync commits a caller's own new file within minutes and git status cannot prove it isn't theirs. The baseline covers ~105 of ~17,700 operator-core files, so that verdict depends on checking essentially the whole program. The API's full-program pass is slower than the CLI (71 s vs 29 s, D-003), so serving --mine would cost more and preserve nothing. tscServiceEligibility already refuses it ('not a --files run'); that stays.\n\nInstead, the recommendation moves. build:typecheck's guidance (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/build/typecheck.ts notWhen + chaining) told agents to finish with `npm run lint:tsc -- --mine`, which is a 12.7 GiB compile per call. It now says `--files=<same files>`, which CLAUDE.md already prescribes and the service answers with a ~0.5 GiB caller.\n\nServed-path A/B (lint:tsc --files=packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/managed-spawn.ts): service 12.3 s wall, caller peak 525 MiB, one shared service 4.3-4.9 GiB, status=clean; PAPERCUSP_TSC_SERVICE=0 CLI 51.0 s incl. pc-heavy queue, caller peak 12.7 GiB, status=clean.\n\n### D-005 — Owner answers 2026-09-27 04:1xZ: one-shot GRUB into 7.0.0-34 (owner reboots later); idle services stay running\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-27, AskUserQuestion answers, owner-dialog turn ref [turn:dc449344@2026-09-27T04:45:03.326Z]]\n\n1. Kernel (P-001) = \"Set it; I'll reboot later\". su sets a one-shot `sudo grub-reboot` for 'gnulinux-advanced-776fcdae-...>gnulinux-7.0.0-34-generic-advanced-776fcdae-...'. The owner chooses when to reboot; su does NOT reboot. Verified before acting: /boot/grub/grub.cfg:23-27 sets boot_once=true when next_entry is set, and savedefault (L48-51) writes only when boot_once is empty. So the one-shot boot does NOT overwrite saved_entry (still 6.17.0-40), and the following reboot returns to 6.17 unless 7.0 is made the default. vmlinuz/initrd 7.0.0-34 and the nvidia DKMS modules for 7.0.0-34 are present. After the owner reboots: verify `uname -r`, the kmalloc-8k slab trend, and the NVIDIA driver; then propose `grub-set-default` to make 7.0 permanent.\n\n2. Idle services (P-007) = \"Leave them running\". Measured 04:10Z: 91 Docker containers total 3.8 GiB (bytebot 0.9 GiB), kokoro 0.2 GiB, StoreWolf not running. Not worth the breakage risk; P-007 dropped with no change.\nRelated: P-001, P-007\n\n### D-006 — P-008 route: the test router names, stops and bounds its own systemd scope; no separate stale-scope sweep\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27. Measured 05:08-05:20Z, su-5b9cde39. [self-imposed design ruling]\n\nCAUSE (observed, not reproduced): scripts/test-files.mjs launched every captured Vitest child as `systemd-run --user --scope --collect <cmd>`. That gave an ANONYMOUS run-uNNN.scope with no RuntimeMaxSec, and nothing ever stopped it. Fixtures spawned `detached: true` sit in their own process group, so the router's process-group watchdog SIGKILL never reached them. The sibling scope also escapes the caller's cgroup, so a caller deadline (capability:bash RuntimeMaxSec, pc-heavy) cannot reach it either. The router's systemd launcher landed 2026-09-06, and the 9 leaked scopes were ~19 days old on 2026-09-27, which fits. The literal `while :; do sleep 0.1; done` loops were rewritten out of kopia-backup-guard.test.ts / pc-heavy.test.ts on 2026-09-06, but the class remains: pc-heavy.test.ts still has ~8 `while :; do sleep 1; done` holders and kopia-backup-guard.test.ts:388 has `while :; do sleep 0.05; done`.\n\nFIX (in scripts/test-files.mjs): (1) the scope gets a unique name, papercusp-test-<pid>-<ms36>-<seq>.scope. (2) On the child's `exit`, and at the watchdog SIGKILL stage and on parent SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, the router runs `systemctl --user stop --no-block <unit>`, which kills the whole cgroup. It first reads TasksCurrent and prints `TEST_FILE_LEAKED_PROCESSES scope=... tasks=N reason=... files=[...]` when anything was still resident, so a leaking test file is NAMED in its own run output. (3) `--property=RuntimeMaxSec=<watchdogMax + killGrace + 30 min>` makes systemd reap the scope when the router itself is dead (SIGKILL, OOM). The slack keeps it looser than the router's own watchdog, because a pc-heavy freeze can stall the router's timers while systemd's clock keeps running.\n\nWHY NOT A SWEEP REAPER: an anonymous run-u scope cannot be attributed. Other `systemd-run --scope` users create the same names, so a sweep would have to kill by heuristic (age + process shape), which repo rules forbid (never kill by name or pattern). A named, bounded scope makes systemd the reaper, and that survives the router's death with no extra process.\n\nNOT CHANGED: testing:run already runs the router inside a bounded managed task scope (PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_GROUP + PAPERCUSP_TASK_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS) and the router correctly opens no nested scope there. Bounding the fixture loops inside the two test files is left as optional hardening, because the scope stop covers every test file.\n\nEVIDENCE: test-file-router.test.ts 113/113 green (new seam tests for exit, timeout, setsid-never-stops, and stopTestScope parsing). New test-file-router-scope-reap.integration.test.ts passes on real systemd 255: a setsid'd straggler holding the stdout pipe dies and the run settles in <300 ms. Falsifiability control (.papercusp/scratch/p008-scope-reap-control.mts, stop disabled): the run did NOT settle in 6 s and the straggler stayed alive. lint:tsc --files over all three files: status=clean on both the scripts and operator-core legs.\n\n### D-007 — P-010 route: alarm on SUnreclaim slope + nr_dying_descendants from a per-boot PG sample series; no per-cache (root-only, and the leaking cache name re-randomises per boot)\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27. Measured 05:24-05:31Z, su-5b9cde39. [self-imposed design ruling]\n\nWHAT IS READABLE: as the operator's user, /proc/meminfo (SUnreclaim, Slab), /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.stat (nr_dying_descendants), /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and /proc/uptime are readable. /proc/slabinfo and /sys/kernel/slab/* are root-only (-r--------). So the per-cache kmalloc-8k count is NOT available to an unprivileged alarm.\n\nWHY SUnreclaim, NOT A CACHE NAME: the leaking cache changes name every boot. Pre-reboot the leak lived in kmalloc-rnd-03-8k (~18 GB). At 05:30Z this boot (6.17.0-40 still, booted 02:07Z) kmalloc-rnd-03-8k is 4 MB and plain kmalloc-8k is 366 MB (46,792 objects), about 2.6 GB/day, which matches the ~3.5 GB/day leak. CONFIG_RANDOM_KMALLOC_CACHES re-randomises which of kmalloc-8k / kmalloc-rnd-NN-8k a call site uses per boot, so an alarm keyed on a cache name would silently miss it. SUnreclaim is the aggregate that contains every one of them.\n\nROUTE: a new in-process periodic check 'kernel-leak-watchdog' (10 min, host scope, fireOnArm) samples SUnreclaim, Slab and nr_dying_descendants into a new table harness_shared.host_kernel_memory_samples (migration 1234), keyed (boot_id, 10-min bucket) so the :3070 and :3170 operators on one host write one row, and a reboot starts a new series. It escalates via openEscalation (severity advisory, dedupKind 'kernel-memory-leak', one subject per boot per signal) when:\n  (a) SUnreclaim least-squares slope >= 1.5 GiB/day over the trailing 24 h of this boot, excluding the first 6 h after boot (warm-up: SUnreclaim went 3.3 GB at 02:45Z to 4.78 GB at 05:30Z while kmalloc-8k was still small), with >= 12 h of span and >= 12 samples; or\n  (b) SUnreclaim >= 10% of MemTotal (25 GiB here; the pre-reboot state was 29.9 GiB); or\n  (c) nr_dying_descendants >= 1000 AND its slope >= 500/day over the same window (pre-reboot plateau ~1,900; 278 -> 316 in ~6 min at 05:24-05:30Z, so the absolute floor stops normal churn from alarming).\nThe escalation body carries the numbers plus triage (sudo slabinfo top caches, cgroup.stat, the known 6.17 AppArmor instance and its P-001 fix). The known leak (~2.6-3.5 GB/day) trips (a) within about a day of warm-up ending.\n\nTHRESHOLDS ARE PROVISIONAL: calibrated from one boot's samples. Re-check once the table has a few days of data on 7.0.0-34 (the expected flat baseline): SELECT boot_id, min(sampled_at), max(sampled_at), min(sunreclaim_bytes), max(sunreclaim_bytes), max(dying_descendants) FROM harness_shared.host_kernel_memory_samples GROUP BY 1.\n\nNOT DONE: no sudo from the operator to read slabinfo (the shipped desktop cannot assume it; the escalation tells a human to run it). No feature flag, following the pg-tuning-drift precedent; openEscalation's dedup bounds the noise.\n\n### D-008 — P-005 findings + first route: duplicate spawner sidecars come from a timer race in the adoption probe; fix the probe, then bg-host / arenas / worker count\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27. Measured 05:40-05:50Z, su-5b9cde39. [self-imposed design ruling]\n\nMEASURED (anon RSS from /proc/<pid>/status RssAnon; unit from /proc/<pid>/cgroup):\n- papercusp-bg-host.service (canonical tree): 4.98 GB, ~8 min after its restart. No MALLOC_ARENA_MAX. Probably the plan text's '9.2 GB canonical-tree process' [inferred].\n- papercup-embed-sidecar.service: 4.62 GB.\n- papercusp-dev-api.service (:3070): primary 760 MB + 6 cluster workers (PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER_WORKERS=6) at 910-980 MB each, about 6.4 GB. MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 is already set.\n- papercusp-staging-api (:3170): 729 MB. No MALLOC_ARENA_MAX.\n- A tsx bin/hono-host.ts in a GNOME-terminal (vte-spawn) scope: 2.29 GB. Human-launched, out of scope.\n- Operator-spawned sidecars (processes:list class=sidecar): the bg-host's spawner sidecar at 1.94 GB plus its health monitor at 0.75 GB. :3070 had TWO spawner sidecars: 503775, spawned 04:30:39Z by worker 226804, and 799120, spawned 04:42:54Z by worker 226790.
