Applied live 13:35Z by pg-autotune --apply --huge-pages (reload, no restart)\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27. su-5b9cde39, measured 13:14:53-13:35:14Z. [measured unless tagged; setting choice self-imposed within the owner-approved plan route]\n\nA/B: .papercusp/scratch/walcomp-ab.sh on the native PG 18 cluster, windows off/pglz/lz4/zstd/off, 240 s each, switched by ALTER SYSTEM + reload. Output .papercusp/scratch/walcomp-ab-1316.tsv plus per-window pg_waldump --stats files. The EXIT trap reset it: 'EXIT: wal_compression reset -> off', and pg_settings then read 'off default'.\n\nMETRIC: per-window WAL totals are unusable because the load drifts 10x between windows. The closing off window hit a checkpoint and wrote 1,148 MB in 240 s, 91% images, against 112 MB in the lz4 window. The exact ratio comes from pg_waldump -b (--bkp-details) over each window's LSN range: stored = sum(8192 - hole - 'compression saved'), raw = sum(8192 - hole). Positive control: the off window's raw sum (209.5 MB) equals --stats FPI bytes (209,536,400), and pglz stored equals its --stats FPI bytes (177.8 MB).\n- pglz: 77,836 images, 412.7 MB raw -> 177.8 MB stored = 0.431\n- zstd: 17,242 images, 99.2 MB -> 44.6 MB = 0.449\n- lz4: 19,594 images, 119.2 MB -> 61.0 MB = 0.512\n- Images as a share of WAL bytes with compression off: 77.4% (window 1) and 91.4% (window 5).\nCPU: the pg cgroup CPU deltas (696 / 858 / 547 / 536 / 574 s per window) track load, not method; compressing ~640 MB with pglz is seconds of CPU [inferred], below the noise.\n\nRULING: pglz everywhere, set in databaseTuningToSettings next to checkpoint_timeout (libs/generic/resource-profile/src/index.ts, plus a test in index.test.ts). Why not zstd or lz4 natively: they compress no better here, and embedded PG 18.3 refuses both with a FATAL at startup (fact embedded-pg-rejects-lz4-wal-compression-2026-09-27; its HINT lists pglz, on, off). A native-only branch would bet boot on the embeddedPg classification, which has been wrong before (EI-2403).\n\nAPPLIED: `npx tsx scripts/pg-autotune.ts --apply --huge-pages`. The flag is required: a bare --apply regenerates the drop-in WITHOUT huge_pages = on, which silently loses huge pages for the 32 GB shared_buffers at the next restart. The drop-in diff was exactly the wal_compression line. Reload only (postmaster start 2026-09-27 00:19:38-04 unchanged). Live: wal_compression = pglz from conf.d/10-papercusp-autotune.conf; huge_pages on.\n\nTESTS: resource-profile index.test.ts 225/225 (new test: pglz for embedded and native, reloadable). Consumers green: pg-tuning-drift 27, in-process-periodic 21, apps/operator/bin/serve 103, embedded-pg-discovery 9.\n\nNEXT PROBE: re-run the per-relation WAL census, and a --stats pass over one checkpoint cycle, after both this change and the receipt-GC drain. Expected: FPI bytes per image ~0.43 of raw, and total WAL/h down ~40-50% at equal load [inferred].\n\n### D-033 — P-012: jemalloc (LD_PRELOAD) is not a memory lever for gitnexus analyze\nDate: 2026-09-27\nDate: 2026-09-27\nVERDICT on the pre-registered rule: jemalloc (LD_PRELOAD) does NOT lower gitnexus analyze PEAK memory, so analyzeEnv stays unchanged. The 4 GiB LBUG buffer pool is also rejected (it raises the peak). A secondary time-weighted comparison is running; see below.\n\nFixture and method (.papercusp/scratch/gitnexus-ab.sh): the repo's tracked files incl. submodules, 35,200 files; routine argv with --embeddings 0 and the analyzeEnv defaults; systemd scope MemoryMax=24G; one override per arm. [measured unless tagged]\n\nRound 1 (.papercusp/scratch/gitnexus-ab.tsv) is not usable. Its base arm overlapped the 15:38Z production reindex, and reclaim swapped 5.8 GiB of it out, which lowers cgroup memory.peak (memory.peak also counts page cache).\n\nRound 2 (.papercusp/scratch/gitnexus-ab2.tsv) used a 2 s sampler of cgroup memory.stat anon + memory.swap.current:\n- pool4g (LBUG pool 4 GiB) 16:55-17:49Z: 3,244 s, exit 0, anon peak 15,696 MiB, anon+swap peak 15,977, swap.peak 8,740.\n- base 17:49-18:48Z: 3,511 s, exit 0, anon peak 13,036, anon+swap peak 13,627, swap.peak 4,591.\n- jemalloc 18:48-19:34Z: 2,805 s, exit 0, anon peak 13,882, anon+swap peak 13,884, swap.peak 2,833.\n\nReading: jemalloc's peak is 1.9% above base on anon+swap and 6.5% above on anon alone. The rule required at least 10% below base (<= 12,264 MiB), so it fails. pool4g is 17% above base on anon+swap and 20% on anon, so it fails too. anon+swap over-counts swap-cache pages under swap churn (cgroup-v2: swapcached is charged to both memory and swap). The anon-only column has no such bias and gives the same ranking, so that bias cannot rescue either lever. n=1 per arm.\n\nSecondary observations:\n- jemalloc's 2 s series (.papercusp/scratch/gnxab-jemalloc-series.tsv, net = anon + swap - swapcached) peaks once, 13.9 GiB at 19:02Z during the graph phase. Otherwise it sits at median 8.0 GiB, p90 9.0 GiB, and exceeds 10 GiB in 0.9% of samples, because jemalloc returns freed pages.\n- jemalloc ran faster in both rounds: 2,493 vs 3,015 s, then 2,805 vs 3,511 s (17-20%). Every arm overlapped some production reindex, so this is suggestive, not clean.\n\nOPEN, added after round 2 [self-imposed; not part of the pre-registered rule]: peak sets the scope cap and admission, but host pressure depends on how long memory stays resident. Round 3 re-runs base with the same 2 s series (task 0muk8itl5nsr3x318s9, started 19:51:58Z, .papercusp/scratch/gitnexus-ab3.tsv + gnxab-base-series-1951.tsv). If base's median net is at least 25% above jemalloc's 8.0 GiB, record jemalloc as a residency lever in a new decision and wire it. Otherwise this verdict stands unchanged. A 2 s series also runs on the 19:35Z production tick (.papercusp/scratch/gnx-prod-1935-series.tsv) for a production baseline profile.\n\n### D-034 — Gateway payload spool: unreferenced retention 2 h -> 2 min, and a dedupe HEAD renews expiry (WI-10003469, lever D)\nDate: 2026-09-28\nContext [measured 2026-09-28 10:46Z, pg_waldump --stats=record over 300 MB / ~9 min]: pg_toast_3867601117 (TOAST of harness_shared.gateway_payload_blobs) is 48% of all WAL. Of that: Heap/INSERT (the body bytes) is 7%, Heap/DELETE is 41% and Heap2/VISIBLE is 50%, both almost entirely full-page images. A row lived about 2 h unreferenced, so the GC DELETE and VACUUM each touched every page for the first time since the last checkpoint (checkpoint_timeout 15 min, data_checksums on).\n\nAlso measured: nothing reads a spooled body back, and execution is synchronous inside the request (the gateway.ts SCOPE LIMIT comment above the retain() call).\n\nMeasured: at 2026-09-28T10:48Z I ran `grep -rn --include=*.ts --include=*.mts --include=*.tsx -E \"(payloadSpool|spool)\\??\\.read\\(\"` over packages/ apps/ libs/ bin/ scripts/, excluding node_modules, dist and .test. files. It found 0 hits. The positive control, the same search for `payloadSpool.spool(`, found 1 (gateway.ts spoolRequestBodyForAdmission). The direct-table users of gateway_payload_blobs are backup/src/hook.ts (a table list), frame-bootstrap.ts (a comment) and index-manifest.ts (index DDL). None selects `bytes`. FALSIFIER: a future async-detach executor that calls spool.read(payloadRef). It still reads a PINNED row, and this change does not affect pinned rows.\n\nRuling: DEFAULT_PAYLOAD_SPOOL_TTL_MS = 2 min (was 2 h). PgGatewayPayloadStore.head(), the dedupe path of putContentAddressed, now UPDATEs last_accessed_at and expires_at = GREATEST(expires_at, now+ttl), so the sweep's READ COMMITTED re-check spares a row a retry just deduped onto until its retain() lands.\n\nNOT changed: capless-inference-gateway D-004 (pre-acceptance spool, pinned by ref_count while a receipt names it), the pinned/abandoned branch (pinnedGraceMs 2 h keyed on last_accessed_at), legacy grace, and the sweep SQL.\n\nRejected for now: (a) content-defined chunking and (b) app-side zstd. Both shrink only the 7% insert share. (c) Skipping the spool on the sync path would reverse D-004 and re-enable the maxQueued 429 cap.\n\nVerify after deploy: re-run .papercusp/scratch/wal-census.sh (MB=300) plus pg_waldump --stats=record --relation on the TOAST filenode. Expected [inferred]: the spool TOAST WAL share falls from ~48% to <15%.\n\nVERIFIED 2026-09-28 14:47Z (WI-10003469) [measured]. Live on :8788 since 11:46:18Z. Window = checkpoint redo 80E/1CC12C30 (14:21:24Z) to 80E/5083E000, 828 MB over ~26 min, all rows written >2.5 h after the deploy (.papercusp/scratch/wal-remeasure-1469b.out). Spool TOAST = 165.2 MB = 20.1% of WAL (was 48.2%), ~6.3 MB/min (was ~16 MB/min). FPI is 12.5% of the spool's WAL (was ~91%). By record type: INSERT + INSERT+INIT 83%, DELETE 9%, VISIBLE 7% (was 7 / 41 / 50). The mechanism is confirmed. The fact's falsifier (share >25% or still FPI-dominated) did not fire.\nThe inferred <15% target was MISSED. The 9-min baseline window under-sampled inserts: the post-fix INSERT rate (~5.5 MB/min) matches the pre-fix population average (870 MB over 2 h = ~7 MB/min at 11:46Z). So the '7% insert share' premise above does not hold after the fix. The body bytes are now the spool's WAL. Chunk dedupe (a) is the remaining spool lever, at ~17% of WAL; it is not taken now (see WI-10003469 close note).\n\n### D-035 — WI-10003444: evicted the 3 dependency generations held ONLY by pins from checkouts already offloaded off root (58.3 GB), under the store's publish lock; bytes archived on /mnt/data. Root 96 -> 193 GB free. The store was NOT the net grower (9 generations then and now); the durable class fix is WI-10003695\nDate: 2026-09-28\nDate: 2026-09-28. su-5b9cde39, 15:05-15:30Z. [measured unless tagged]\n\nCONTEXT: root (nvme0n1p2 ext4) at 95% / 96 GB free at 14:50Z; infra disk alert firing.\n\n1. pui-mut scratch offload (.papercusp/scratch/offload-pui-mut.sh, log offload-pui-mut.log): 41,490 files / 35,058,729,862 bytes verified equal, now a symlink to /mnt/data/offload/root-disk/<same abs path>. EXIT=0 15:09:29Z.\n\n2. Retracts my own carry-note premise that '4 new generations today' were the grower: D-029 counted 9 generations at 09-27 12:00Z and there were 9 at 15:10Z today. Retention (RETAIN_COUNT=2 + pinned + leased; hourly at :50 via sessionDirGc -> dependencyGenerationRetentionTick, plus every consumer's apply_retention) prunes as many as are built; it pruned d1616 at ~15:19Z when the gate checkout moved to d3bb. Root free swings +/-15 GB within minutes: a checkout materialization is a full 20 GB copy (ext4 cannot reflink; cp -a --reflink=auto falls back), then the old copy is deleted. A 20 s sample at 15:13Z: nvme0n1p2 wrote 1,388 MiB, top writer the cp from v1-d3bb41de. The installer build (ISCC, xz -9) writes to /tmp, which is on nvme1n1.\n\n3. EVICTION (.papercusp/scratch/depgen-evict-offloaded.sh, log depgen-evict-offloaded.log, EXIT=0). Targets: v1-ba36afa4 (pinned only by papercusp-relcut-0022 -> /mnt/data/offload), v1-d92c4371 (only /home/marsh-office/p2p-e9f-candidate -> /mnt/backup/offload/WI-2146953), v1-edf76ace (only papercai-workspace/papercusp-relcut-0021 -> /mnt/data/offload). No process had a cwd in any of them; their node_modules are independent copies on other filesystems, so the generation only saved them a rebuild. Under the publish lock (15:20:19Z, <1 s) the script re-verified per identity that every pin's checkout realpath is on another st_dev and that no lease names it, then removed 5 input selectors via the retention path's own dependency_generation_remove_input_selectors_for_identity_locked (an exact-id consumer now sees an ordinary miss, not the invalid-token trap), removed 4 pins, and renamed each generation to .offload-<id> (same fs, atomic). After the lock it rsynced each to /mnt/data/offload/root-disk/<store path>/<id>, verified file count and apparent bytes equal (303,075 / 19,548,587,729; 289,251 / 19,223,387,536; 303,075 / 19,548,559,248), then removed the source. A README there states it is an ARCHIVE: the v2 tokens are dev:inode-bound (D-029) and will not validate as a store.\n\nVERIFIED AFTER: `dependency-generation.sh --integration <repo> --select-inputs-from <repo>` rc=0 -> v1-d3bb41de, token v2:68929d51. Store: 5 generations (70456 nightly-release, 89f1 legacy papercup-checkpoint, 9f13 relcut-0022-green/admission-precheck/live-certification, abef relcut-0023-win, d3bb gate + shared tree). df: 193 GB free, 90% (15:29:55Z). The infra-liveness condition cleared at ~15:30Z.\n\nDURABLE: WI-10003695 (filed, unassigned): retention should stop honouring a same-host pin whose checkout realpath is on another st_dev AND whose marker is older than N days; the sibling loop also re-pins symlinked siblings by their resolved target. The larger lever [inferred]: /mnt/data is XFS reflink=1, so the store plus the checkpoint/release checkouts on /mnt/data would turn every 20 GB materialization into a reflink clone and take those write storms off root (D-029 route b: an empty store).\n\n### D-036 — WI-10003444: the persistent root-disk grower is release-cut output that nothing prunes (wh-release-rNN cut dirs, relcut checkouts), not the depgen store. Band-aid: move finished cut dirs r52-r59 (~135 GB) to /mnt/data with symlinks; durable fix filed as WI-10003700\nDate: 2026-09-28\nDate: 2026-09-28. su-5b9cde39, measured 15:46-16:00Z. [measured unless tagged]\n\nSERIES: .papercusp/scratch/rootfree-1516.tsv, 1/min. Free space was 193.4 GB at 15:30Z, 176.4 GB at 15:35Z, then about flat (171.9-176.2 GB) through 15:55Z.\n\nDU DIFF: root-du-1455.txt.raw vs root-du-1548.mb, counting only keys present in both.\n- in-tree papercusp dir: -109.5 G (my offloads plus D-035).\n- papercusp-relcut-0023-win: +14.9 G, an active 0.0.23 Windows desktop cut.\n- /var/lib/docker: +20.4 G. This is 3 local-rig containers pcusp-rig-a/b/c at 7.36 GB each, started ~15:28Z. They are transient and account for the 15:30-15:35 drop.\n\nPERSISTENT GROWER: workspace-host cut work dirs ~/.papercusp/wh-release-rNN are 17-20 GB each and are never pruned. r57-r60 were created 09-28 08:02-09:12Z (~68 GB). Adding relcut-0023-win (29 GB) explains most of the -3.3 GB/h trend since 09-27. The depgen store is not the net grower (EI-24518238811166805 correction).\n\nACTION: finished, idle cut dirs r52-r59 are being moved to /mnt/data/offload/root-disk/<abs path>, with a symlink left at each original path. All logs read CUT_EXIT=0 except r58, which failed. This follows the owner's offload convention (#638, WI-10003337); r48/r50/r51 were moved the same way on 09-26. r60 (the newest) stays. Script .papercusp/scratch/offload-wh-release.sh verifies file count and apparent bytes for each dir before swapping in the symlink. Its in-use check is .papercusp/scratch/dir-in-use.py, because `lsof +D` and bfs -lname both reported a live cwd as idle (positive control). Nothing in the cut dirs is bound to an inode (checked the CLI; unlike the depgen tokens of D-029).\n\nDURABLE [proposed, not decided]: WI-10003700 (major, unassigned). After a verified publish, prune source/, sidecar/ and extracted/ (89% of each dir), and default the work root to /mnt/data behind a free-space floor.\n\nSIDE NOTE for #687/#688 (memory): the Windows VM papercup-vm-win.service is disabled but was started on demand at 09:56Z for the Windows cut and holds 16.7 GB. Docker holds 16.7 GiB across 99 running containers, 13.6 GiB of it the active rig. Idle-stop for the VMs remains P-006.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"pui-rev10-reproof-2026-09-27","title":"Re-prove PUI public-release spec clauses at their current revision (after acceptance rubric rev8/rev9 amendments)","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-27","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Re-prove PUI public-release spec clauses at their current revision (after acceptance rubric rev8/rev9 amendments)\nslug: pui-rev10-reproof-2026-09-27\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-27\nupdated: 2026-09-27\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nGet every spec clause of parent plan `pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07` (harness papercusp) to PASS `plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy` at its CURRENT revision, so the parent's ship gate stops refusing `acceptance_bar_contract_not_ready` and `plans:set-plan-status shipped` can recruit the independent grader. Mandate: owner directive #724 (Avi, 2026-09-27: finish getting the PUI/TUI plans shipped). Coordinating work-items: WI-10003472, WI-10003500 (held by su-f08bc8c5).\n\n## Context\n\nAcceptance rubric `acceptance-pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07` went to revision 8 (16:30Z) adding requiredTestLayers to every BAR, which re-projected all clauses to revision 10; all 57 governing clauses now FAIL adequacy because every prior binding pinned revision 9 or 7 (only 16 clauses had rev-9 proof at all). A further amendment is in outside-lineage review: R-15 moves from 'e2e' (unrecordable by the test ledger) to a manual-provenance instrument check. When it applies, the R-15 clause and possibly R-01/R-05/R-13/R-14 clauses re-project to a newer revision.\n\nrequiredTestLayers: R-03 = unit + integration; R-15 = manual-provenance (after the pending amendment); every other BAR = integration. PUI-*/P017-* clauses: use the layer the evaluator row demands.\n\n**Always use the revision the evaluator reports for a clause at bind time — never a hard-coded number.** Prove R-01/R-05/R-13/R-14 clauses LAST in your item and re-read their revision just before binding.\n\n## Procedure (every item)\n\n1. Read each clause's PRIOR bindings for the exact test path, test name and sourcePaths to reuse: `dev:pg_query` → `SELECT id, spec_id, spec_revision, work_item_id, evidence_kind, evidence_ref, details FROM harness_shared.spec_evidence_bindings WHERE workspace_id='papercusp-workspace' AND plan_slug='pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07' AND spec_id IN (...) ORDER BY spec_id, created_at DESC`. The clause's work_item_id comes from here (or from the evaluator row).\n2. Re-run the suite ONCE per work item with every clause bound: `testing:run { files:[<test file>], harness:'papercusp', evidence:{ workItemId, planSlug:'pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07', bindings:[{ specId, specRevision:<current>, testPath, sourcePaths, testLayer, scenarioIds:[<exact test name>] }] } }`. This stores a re-run recipe, so later `testing:run { remeasureEvidence }` works.\n3. Adequacy attestation: a ledger row alone yields only outcome/executed/testLayer. Re-bind with the ledger form `plans:bind-spec-evidence { slug:'pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07', harness:'papercusp', binding:{ workItemId, specId, specRevision, fromTestRun:<test_runs.id>, evidenceKind:'test', details:{ adequacy:{ testLayer, pathReachable:true, oracleIndependent:true, falsifiable:true, targeted:'<lower-cased specId>' }, pathReachability:'<why the test reaches the real path>', observations:'<oracle justification>' } }, supersedeAtRevision:true }`. Only attest what you verified by reading the test.\n4. Falsifiability: prove the test can fail with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` (copy-out mode or --fake-destructive; NEVER an in-tree mutation), with `--test 'npm run test:file -- <path>'` and PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_HARNESS=papercusp so the caught-mutant run lands in the ledger; bind it with evidenceKind:'mutation' and details.adequacy.targeted = the lower-cased specId (a string, not true). A counterexample binding is acceptable where a mutation is impractical.\n5. Risk floor (plan-class-risk-floor needs l3): bind a hand-built coverage-census row: `binding:{ workItemId, specId, specRevision, evidenceKind:'coverage-census', evidenceRef:'<test path>', measurement:{ schemaVersion:1, kind:'repo-files', sourcePaths, testPaths }, details:{ census:{ checked, notChecked, notApplicable, residue:[] }, adequacy:{ outcome:'passed', executed:true, testLayer, targeted:'<lower-cased specId>', coverageRungs:{...} } } }`. Model it on a recent live census row (e.g. PERF-P-001 in spec_evidence_bindings) and confirm with the evaluator.\n6. Loop `plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy { slug:'pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07', harness:'papercusp', classRef:'plan-class-feature-ship', specIds:[<one>] }` until every clause in your item PASSES; fix the named criterion rather than re-running blindly (summary output trims to the first row — pass one specId for full ratings).\n7. Checkpoint your work-item with per-clause PASS/FAIL and binding ids, then complete it with evidence. Do NOT call plans:set-plan-status on the parent plan and do NOT emit scorecards on its acceptance rubric — su-f08bc8c5 owns shipping, and grading must come from a non-implementer.\n\nDo not edit product source to make a test pass; a genuine failure is a finding — file it and report it to su-f08bc8c5 via coord:send.\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` agent-chat-pty clauses (25) — suite agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts. Clauses: AUTO-BAR-R-01-P-004, AUTO-BAR-R-02-P-004, AUTO-BAR-R-02-P-009, AUTO-BAR-R-03-P-006, AUTO-BAR-R-03-P-008, AUTO-BAR-R-04-P-008, AUTO-BAR-R-04-P-010, AUTO-BAR-R-05-P-007, AUTO-BAR-R-06-P-009, AUTO-BAR-R-07-P-002, AUTO-BAR-R-07-P-008, AUTO-BAR-R-08-P-010, AUTO-BAR-R-09-P-010, AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-006, PUI-APPROVAL-ALLOW, PUI-APPROVAL-DENY, PUI-BASELINE, PUI-COMMANDS, PUI-EDITOR-COPY, PUI-EDITOR-HISTORY, PUI-EDITOR-UNDO, PUI-FILE-CONTEXT, PUI-QUESTION, PUI-TOOLS-DIFF, PUI-USAGE. R-03 clauses also need a unit-layer binding. Add npm run preview:check (drift vs a fresh export) and preview:push (re-export, re-… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10003659 — OWNER REVIEW (needs-human): Avi browses Papercusp/papercusp-preview and approves its contents, or lists removals (feeds back into the P-001 exclude list). <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10003660 — OWNER-GATED, OUTWARD-FACING: general per-person access via `npm run share-source -- add|remove|list <github-user>` (read permission only; refuses any repo but Papercusp/papercusp-preview). First reci… <!-- P-006 -->\n## Goal\nGive invited individuals (first: dhh and steipete, both GitHub handles verified 2026-09-28) read access to Papercusp's source through a private, per-person revocable channel, at the PUBLIC-SAFE level: exactly the tree every desktop installer already ships as sidecar/source.tar.zst (D-003, D-004). No repository is made public; no one is added to Papercusp/papercup or its 6 private submodule repos.\n\n## Context\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-28] asked how to provide the source \"via a private link not by making a git repository public\", and chose **Private repo + invite** in the follow-up dialog. Part of the \"get DHH to try papercusp\" thread (owner directive #784).\n\n## Facts measured 2026-09-28\n- Papercusp/papercup: PRIVATE, 5.27 GiB pack, 29,990 tracked files, 38 submodules (all Papercusp/*, none nested deeper).\n- Tracked non-product debris at top level: .papercusp (1,651 files), _retired (820), .tmp-vitest-wi1347 (528), .agent-tmp (528), scratchpad (197), .tmp (189), .tmp-tsx / .tmp-content-fixer / .tmp-claude / .tsx-tmp (~137 each), shared-pot-release-testing (116), scratch (15), .papercusp-artifacts (13), .claude (8); docs/briefs (6), docs/plans (27).\n- No LICENSE at the repo root. No gitleaks config. gitleaks + trufflehog are installed (~/.local/bin).\n- Reuse precedent: scripts/templates-mirror-sync.mjs (canonical tree -> Papercusp/templates mirror; drift check by default, --push to apply).\n- Papercusp/papercusp-preview does not exist yet.\n\n## Scope\nIn: snapshot export script, fail-closed secret/internal-content gate, NOTICE + START-HERE, private preview repo + push + re-sync, owner review, held invite.\nOut: making anything public; access to the real repo or any submodule repo; git history; the outreach message itself (separate thread).\n\n## Acceptance\n- A single-commit private repo whose tree is the product source at ONE recorded superproject SHA (plus per-submodule SHAs in MANIFEST.json), with every excluded path absent.\n- gitleaks + trufflehog clean on the exact pushed tree; internal-identifier denylist clean.\n- Re-sync is one command with a drift check; the gate re-runs on every push.\n- No invite is sent without an explicit owner go.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Selection parity with the installer cut.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Share at the public-safe level: exactly what the desktop installer already ships as sidecar/source.tar.zst, reusing its selection instead of a second list.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"For a pinned commit, the exported file set equals the tracked files that the shared stage-source-tree selection admits, with node_modules absent.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A file the installer selection excludes appears in the export, or the export and stage-source-tree.sh compute their selection from different lists.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the export tests against a synthetic superproject with a submodule: they compare the export listing to the shared selection library output and assert excluded and node_modules paths are absent.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts\"\n      ],\n      \"cases\": [\n        {\n          \"file\": \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts\",\n          \"testName\": \"ships every selected tracked file, including the submodule contents\"\n        },\n        {\n          \"file\": \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts\",\n          \"testName\": \"drops every excluded class, node_modules at any depth, and all git metadata\"\n        },\n        {\n          \"file\": \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts\",\n          \"testName\": \"retains the exact eligible bytes from both internal documentation roots\"\n        },\n        {\n          \"file\": \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts\",\n          \"testName\": \"equals the installer selection over the same clean commit, minus node_modules\"\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Fail-closed content gate.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"No secret or internal content reaches the preview repo; reuse the release gate.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The gate refuses to publish when audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir, gitleaks or trufflehog reports any finding in the exported tree, and passes a clean tree.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A tree containing a planted credential passes the gate, or a scanner that cannot run is treated as clean.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the gate tests: a planted-secret fixture must be refused, a clean fixture must pass, and a missing scanner binary must refuse rather than pass.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-gate.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Pinned history-free snapshot.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Snapshot of the source at one commit, no git history.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Each export writes MANIFEST.json naming the superproject SHA and every submodule SHA it exported, and the export directory contains no .git entry.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"MANIFEST.json omits a submodule, names a SHA other than the gitlink, or the export carries git metadata; or an unresolvable gitlink is silently skipped.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the export tests: they assert MANIFEST SHAs match the fixture gitlinks, no .git exists in the output, and an unresolvable gitlink makes the export refuse.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Evaluation notice.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Recipients get the source for evaluation with a map of where things live.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The export root contains NOTICE restricting use to evaluation and START-HERE.md describing how to find and run the code.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Either file is missing from an export or NOTICE lacks the evaluation-only terms.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the export tests: they assert NOTICE and START-HERE.md exist at the export root with the evaluation-only wording.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — One-command re-sync with drift check.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Reusable script with one-command re-sync for future updates.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"preview:check reports drift when the remote tree differs from a fresh export and reports clean when they match, and preview:push publishes a single gated commit.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A differing remote reads clean, or push publishes without running the gate.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the sync tests against a local bare repository standing in for GitHub: drift and no-drift cases, and a push that must invoke the gate first.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-sync.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Per-person revocable read access.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"A general add/remove-a-person command, not DHH-specific; nobody added without an owner go.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"share-source add, remove and list act only on Papercusp/papercusp-preview with read permission, and refuse any other repository or permission.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The command can target another repository, grant more than read, or add a collaborator without an explicit confirm flag.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the share-source tests with a stubbed gh: they assert the exact API calls, read-only permission, the refusal for other repos, and dry-run without confirm.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/share-source-cli.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Items | Evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004 | live |\n| R-6 | P-006 | live |\n\n## Open questions\n- RESOLVED (D-003/D-004): which docs/ ship is exactly what stage-source-tree.sh's allowlist + audit-release-bundle.py FORBIDDEN_PATH ship today (docs/plans, briefs, .papercusp excluded) — the preview never diverges from the installer cut.\n- Invite timing relative to the stability / first-run fixes — owner call at the invite step.\n\n## Phase 1 — Export\n\n- **P-001** `done` Write scripts/source-preview-export.mjs (a second mirror target beside scripts/templates-mirror-sync.mjs) that REUSES the release cut instead of re-implementing it: the papercusp-desktop/bin/stage-source-tree.sh selection (allowlist + EXCLUDES + identity scrub via audit-release-bundle.py --source-leakers/--scrub-text) over a clean checkout at ONE pinned superproject SHA with submodules at their gitlinks, WITHOUT node_modules; MANIFEST.json (superproject SHA, per-submodule SHAs, file count). Factor the shared selection into one place so the installer tarball and the preview repo cannot diverge. Vitest tests: selection parity with stage-source-tree, node_modules absent, refusal on unresolvable gitlink. importance: high — note: Done under WI-10003639. Landed as scripts/source-preview.mjs (export|gate|check|push; npm run preview:*), not source-preview-export.mjs. Selection is shared with the installer: papercusp-desktop/bin/stage-source-tree.sh is invoked for selection+scrub, so the tarball and preview cannot diverge. node_modules excluded; MANIFEST.json records superproject + per-submodule SHAs + file count. Tests: packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-export.test.ts 9/9 (parity, no node_modules, unresolvable-gitlink refusal).\n- **P-002** `done` Author NOTICE (evaluation-only, no redistribution, per-recipient id) and START-HERE.md (one-page map: what Papercusp is, how to run it, where the core lives); the export script injects both into the snapshot root. — note: Done under WI-10003639. NOTICE (evaluation-only, no redistribution) + START-HERE.md generated by startHereText() in scripts/source-preview.mjs and injected at the snapshot root. Per-recipient id: the repo is one shared snapshot; per-person identity lives in the share-source access list (scripts/share-source.mjs), per D-004.\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Content gate\n\n- **P-003** `done` Gate: papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir over the exported tree (the SAME fail-closed gate the installer passes), plus gitleaks + trufflehog in directory mode as additional detectors. Any finding blocks publishing; a vendor key is accepted only via BENIGN_ERE (no second list, WI-10003577). Planted-secret positive control in the tests. importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: Done under WI-10003639. runGate(): audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir (fail-closed) + gitleaks + trufflehog in dir mode; any finding blocks. Extra-detector false positives accepted only via scripts/source-preview-allowlist.json keyed by exact sha256+rule+path with mandatory reason (D-005); never exempts the audit leg. Planted-secret positive controls in source-preview-gate.test.ts 14/14. Real tree main@09e39c5d: all 4 legs clean, exit 0.\n\n## Phase 3 — Publish\n\n- **P-004** `done` Create PRIVATE repo Papercusp/papercusp-preview with NO collaborators; push the gated snapshot as a single commit. Add npm run preview:check (drift vs a fresh export) and preview:push (re-export, re-gate, push). Record the pushed commit + MANIFEST superproject SHA on this plan. importance: high blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003 — note: ← WI-10003658 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Owner gates\n\n- **P-005** `needs-human` OWNER REVIEW (needs-human): Avi browses Papercusp/papercusp-preview and approves its contents, or lists removals (feeds back into the P-001 exclude list). importance: high blocked-by: P-004 — note: Owner review: Avi browses https://github.com/Papercusp/papercusp-preview (private; only org accounts aviynw/papercupai have access) and approves the contents or names changes. P-006 invites stay held until an explicit go.\n- **P-006** `todo` OWNER-GATED, OUTWARD-FACING: general per-person access via `npm run share-source -- add|remove|list <github-user>` (read permission only; refuses any repo but Papercusp/papercusp-preview). First recipients dhh and steipete, each only on an explicit owner go. Revocation = remove. blocked-by: P-005\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Share a flattened, scanned snapshot via a separate private repo + held read-only invite\nDate: 2026-09-28\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-28] chose \"Private repo + invite\" over an email-locked Cloudflare Access link, both, or waiting. Consequences: (1) never invite DHH to Papercusp/papercup or its 38 submodule repos — full 5.27 GiB history, internal plans/briefs and any once-committed secret would ship; (2) the preview is history-free, so only the exported tree needs secret scanning; (3) the invite is held behind explicit owner approval.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse the release source-tree pipeline — no second exporter, no second secret list\nDate: 2026-09-28\n[self-imposed, from code read 2026-09-28] papercusp-desktop/bin/stage-source-tree.sh (WI-3308; header says DEFAULT-ON since 2026-07-07, opt-out PAPERCUSP_STAGE_SOURCE=0) already stages the monorepo source into every desktop installer as sidecar/source.tar.zst, and papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-release-bundle.py already gates it (paths + identity literals + CREDENTIAL_ERE; --scan-dir for an assembled tree; third-party keys accepted ONLY via BENIGN_ERE, \"never a second list\" per WI-10003577). Therefore: P-001 derives its include/exclude and identity scrub from stage-source-tree.sh (minus node_modules, plus the flat submodule export), not from a fresh hand list; P-003 runs audit-release-bundle.py --scan-dir over the exported tree as the canonical gate, with gitleaks + trufflehog as additional detectors — never a parallel denylist. Corollary for the owner: anyone holding a desktop installer built with source staging ON already holds a copy of the source; verify on a current installer before treating the preview repo as the first disclosure.\n\n### D-003 — What the release already ships: a public-safe source cut + a sealed full-pot seed — share at one consistent level, never a scrubbed copy beside an unscrubbed channel\nDate: 2026-09-28\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-28] [turn:164d4d35@2026-09-28T08:46:36.318Z] (verbatim, dialog answer): \"PAPERCUSP IS ITSELF A DOGFOODED POT INSIDE PAPERCUSP AND WE ARE BUNDLING IT INSIDE THE RELEASE ... ITS SECURITY THEATER IF WE SCRUB IT FROM GITHUB AND THEN SHARE IT ON THE POT ... DID WE [already scrub]? IF SO CAN WE USE THE SAME THING FOR GITHUB?\" Also: make this general (not DHH-specific); share with OpenClaw's creator too (GitHub steipete, verified).\n\nMEASURED from code 2026-09-28 (su-aeffc7d0): the desktop release ships TWO copies of the source.\n(1) sidecar/source.tar.zst — papercusp-desktop/bin/stage-source-tree.sh, an ALLOWLIST + identity scrub, gated by papercusp-desktop/bin/audit-release-bundle.py FORBIDDEN_PATH (vcs .git, .papercusp*, docs/plans, agent-briefs, .claude/.harness, pi-sessions transcripts, scratch/tmp, .env*, credential files/dirs, dev systemd units, internal build-infra docs, test files, ...) plus CREDENTIAL_ERE and identity literals. Readable by ANYONE holding an installer. This is the existing public-safe cut.\n(2) the pot seed — apps/operator/lib/release/cut-seed-cli.ts: a depth-1 (no history) git bundle of Papercusp/papercup HEAD sealed under the pot epoch key (via=epoch; only an ADMITTED member can unwrap) plus the pot corestore shipped as ciphertext + merkle trees + public keys (seed-provider-corestore.ts header). Identity-redacted (SEED_EXCLUDED_TABLES, emails -> [email], build identity literals, hostname neutralization, seed-identity-guard) but NOT content-scrubbed: plans, work items etc. are the pot's content by design.\n\nCONSEQUENCES: (a) Avi is right — the scrub exists and is reusable; P-001's custom exporter and P-003's custom gate are superseded by reusing stage-source-tree.sh + audit-release-bundle.py. (b) Exposure must be chosen per person at ONE level: PUBLIC-SAFE (the source.tar.zst tree; what any installer holder has) or INSIDER (pot admission = HEAD + plans/work items/live state; GitHub read on the 7 private repos = tracked plans/.papercusp + FULL 5.27 GiB history, never secret-scanned). Scrubbing one channel while opening another at insider level is theatre. (c) Supersedes D-001's 'flattened scanned snapshot' framing; the D-001 rule 'never invite to the real repos' stands only if the public-safe level is chosen.\n\n### D-004 — Public-safe level for external source sharing; share tool is general, per person\nDate: 2026-09-28\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-28] [turn:self] chose \"Public-safe cut (Recommended)\" in the level dialog, and said earlier \"i want this to be general, i want to share this with some other people as well\" (DHH + the OpenClaw creator, GitHub steipete). So: recipients get read on ONE private repo holding the release source cut (same selection + scrub + gate as sidecar/source.tar.zst); the add/remove tool is recipient-agnostic; no one outside the team is added to Papercusp/papercup or its private submodules, and no pot invite is issued for this purpose. Route: implemented by su-aeffc7d0 in-session (owner chose \"Me, this session\").\n\n### D-005 — Extra-detector false positives are allowlisted by exact secret fingerprint, never by a second secret rule\nDate: 2026-09-28\nThe gate runs audit-release-bundle.py (both legs) plus gitleaks and trufflehog. On the first real cut (Papercusp/papercup@09e39c5d) both audit legs were clean; gitleaks raised 27 and trufflehog 10 findings, every one reviewed as a false positive or public-by-design value (git SHAs and sha256 digests in evidence docs, test-literal credentials, jwt.io example JWT, Chatwoot widget token, PostHog phc_ ingest key, plan slugs matched by UnifyID, minified Storybook code, the canonical-hive DISCOVERY token).\n\nRuling: those reviewed values live in scripts/source-preview-allowlist.json, one entry per (detector, rule, path, sha256 of the matched value) with a mandatory reason. The raw secret never leaves the gate — only its SHA-256 is compared and printed. A changed or new value in the same file is a new finding and refuses. The audit's own BENIGN_ERE stays the single vendor-key exemption list; the allowlist never exempts the audit. New candidates come from `npm run preview:gate -- <dir> --json <file>` and are reviewed before being added.\n\nRejected: path- or rule-level exemptions (a later real secret in the same file would pass); a second benign regex list beside BENIGN_ERE (two lists drift — D-002).\n\nPinned by packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-gate.test.ts (exact-value acceptance; a rotated value in the same path refuses; entries without a reason or with a short digest are rejected; the shipped file is valid and duplicate-free).\n\n### D-006 — Drift means the preview's CONTENT differs — not that the source repo has a newer commit\nDate: 2026-09-28\npreview:check and preview:push compare a comparable tree: the preview's root tree with MANIFEST.json dropped and the source commit that NOTICE and START-HERE.md name replaced by a placeholder (comparableTree in scripts/source-preview.mjs, via ls-tree/mktree on the root tree only).\n\nWhy: the first implementation compared full trees. Because MANIFEST.json, NOTICE and START-HERE.md embed the source commit, every superproject commit read as drift — and git-sync commits the shared tree every few minutes — so preview:check could essentially never report in sync, and each preview:push would publish a manifest-only churn commit to the reviewer.\n\nWhat still counts as drift: any shipped file changing, a NOTICE or START-HERE.md text change (including the copyright year), and a hand edit on the preview repo. When content is unchanged, check reports in sync naming both commits (the preview's snapshot commit and the fresh export's), and push skips.\n\nPinned by packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-sync.test.ts: a commit touching only a dropped path stays in sync and pushes nothing; a shipped-file change is drift and a confirmed re-push replaces the preview with one new orphan commit; a hand edit of NOTICE on the preview is drift.\n\n### D-007 — The preview's guide is README.md and links the releases page (owner directive #795)\nDate: 2026-09-28\nSource: owner directive #795 [turn:e029259f@2026-09-28T14:04:06.122Z], owner-typed: \"In the readme link to the releases page and explain how the source code is actually bundled in the release and why\".\n\n- START-HERE.md (P-002) is renamed README.md: GitHub renders only README.*, so START-HERE.md was never shown on the repo page (gh api .../readme returned 404).\n- README.md links the live releases page, ${PAPERCUSP_UPDATE_BASE_URL}/index.html. That value is deployment state (it is baked into shipped apps and must never rotate), so it is NOT committed to this repo: releasesPageUrl(env) reads the environment only, the CLI fills it from ~/.papercusp/release-host.env (the same file papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/release-host.sh loads), and the export refuses (exit 2) without it rather than publish a README with no download link.\n- README.md adds 'How this source ships inside every release' (sidecar/source.tar.zst: the same allowlisted and audited cut plus node_modules, extracted on first boot to a writable dir, run by the dev :3270 and local :3055 environments on the bundled node) and 'Why the release carries its own source' (an install can edit and run its own source without cloning or a toolchain; writable because the install dir is read-only; one archive because tauri's resource copy is slow over GBs of small files and breaks node_modules/.bin symlinks).\n- Correction: only the Papercusp SERVER installer carries source.tar.zst; the GUI installer ships only sidecar/spa. The README says so instead of 'every desktop installer'.\n\nMeasured: papercusp-desktop/bin/stage-source-tree.sh:1-31 (header: ONE resource sidecar/source.tar.zst, extracted on FIRST BOOT to a WRITABLE dir; install dir read-only; tauri copy slow; .bin symlinks survive tar not tauri copy). papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:7096-7107 (dev_source_dir = shared_state_dir/dev-source, or /home/papercup/.papercusp/dev-source via WSL) and :7360-7374 (PAPERCUSP_SOURCE_ARCHIVE = sidecar/source.tar.zst, PAPERCUSP_DEV_SOURCE_DIR). tauri.server.conf.json bundle.resources = ['sidecar/**/*','resources/*','seed/**/*']; tauri.conf.json (Papercusp GUI) = ['sidecar/spa/**/*'] (python3 json read, 2026-09-28). curl ${PAPERCUSP_UPDATE_BASE_URL}/index.html → 200, <title>Papercusp releases</title>, versions 0.0.7–0.0.22-alpha.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"drill-p004-r6-20260928","title":"THROWAWAY drill rubric (P-004 R-6, D-020/D-025): the drill plan states its purpose","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-28","owner":"su-25eb2e26-6180-4d2d-a021-e93f854b2db0","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: THROWAWAY drill rubric (P-004 R-6, D-020/D-025): the drill plan states its purpose\nslug: drill-p004-r6-20260928\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-28\nupdated: 2026-09-28\nowner: su-25eb2e26-6180-4d2d-a021-e93f854b2db0\n---\n\n# THROWAWAY drill rubric (P-004 R-6, D-020/D-025): the drill plan states its purpose\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"drill-p004-r6-20260928-2026-09-28","title":"THROWAWAY drill plan for goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 P-004 R-6 (D-020/D-025) — will be dropped, never shipped","status":"superseded","created":"2026-09-28","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: THROWAWAY drill plan for goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 P-004 R-6 (D-020/D-025) — will be dropped, never shipped\nslug: drill-p004-r6-20260928-2026-09-28\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-09-28\nupdated: 2026-09-28\n---\n\n# THROWAWAY drill plan for goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 P-004 R-6 (D-020/D-025) — will be dropped, never shipped\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-09-28. Governing rulings live on goal-agent-behavior-feedback-2026-09-06 (D-020, D-025).\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"pui-chat-first-ux-2026-09-28","title":"PUI chat-first UX: make `pui` something a person would choose over Claude Code / Codex","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-28","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: \"PUI chat-first UX: make `pui` something a person would choose over Claude Code / Codex\"\nslug: pui-chat-first-ux-2026-09-28\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-28\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Resumed 2026-10-15 on the existing SELF/AUTO lane. Avi accepted R-05 on build 33287a0d19 in D-037; the Oct 2 rejection is superseded. P-006 remains open for fresh measured BAR proof/calibration and independent product grading, not another usability sign-off. Native lock-protocol WI-6554700010009522 and exact-r14 review WI-10003414 are done. The focused wrap-aware native approval matcher and bounded Codex RPC receipt diagnostics now pass 42 canonical helper tests (run f8a229b5-743a-40f6-82cf-e624e2e645b5); this is helper proof only. Latest retained exact 6a0 full acceptance is still refused. No new candidate is published.\n\n**Next:** su-7534ff62 will finish focused native approval/effect/restart verification and Codex transport diagnosis, then refresh current BAR evidence and independent product grading before closing P-006; public publication retains Avi’s candidate-specific approval gate.\n\n## Evidence: what a fresh `pui` launch shows (captured 2026-09-28 ~06:59Z, su-f08bc8c5, 160x42, /mnt/data/tmp/pui-frame-1.txt)\n\n1. **The first message fails.** The chat pane says \"SU session · starting · reconnecting\", \"reconciliation: failed-orphaned\" and \"Session did not become ready. Draft retained; reconnect to retry.\" The composer says \"Message not accepted — draft retained\". The backend lists adv_sessions 31362 (su-00058bae, claude) as su_session_state=running, so the UI and the backend disagree.\n2. **Chat is a 78-column box, not the product.** The screen holds zellij chrome (tab bar plus two lines of keybinding tips), an 8-tab operator bar (Overview, Agent Chat, Inbox (285), Plans, Fleet, Sessions, Pots, Docs), a 73/83 fleet Presence list of other agents' sessions, and an unrelated bash shell pane on the right.\n3. **Internal jargon is shown to the user:** adv 31362, seq 1, chat a2e9c861-882, reconciliation: failed-orphaned, stream gap, pot papercusp, role operator, store pg-a9c7b890119f, op http://127.0.0.1:9071, and a \"usage in unknown / out unknown / cost unknown / context unknown\" row.\n4. **Status is duplicated and not actionable:** header and composer both say \"not ready\", neither says why or what to do, and the hint row lists Ctrl+X/R/K/F/E actions that do not apply to a failed start.\n5. **A garbled title:** \"MY FOCUS AND:\".\n\nNot a duplicate of the shipped plan pui-su-session-runtime-correction-2026-08-27, which made PUI HOST SU sessions; this one is about whether the interface is usable and competitive.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-01 — Chat is the whole screen.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783: people must be able to use pui instead of Claude Code / Codex\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A bare `pui` launch in a directory opens the workbench with that directory's chat as the focused main pane and the workbench boards beside it, and `pui --solo` opens that chat alone, full screen, with no multiplexer chrome, operator tab bar, fleet presence list or shell pane (D-020 Effect 3).\",\"falsifier\":\"A bare `pui` launch opens without the chat as the focused main pane or without a workbench board pane beside it, or a captured frame of `pui --solo` contains zellij chrome, the operator tab bar, a presence list or a shell pane.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Launch the installed/current-build `pui` in an isolated PTY with a fresh HOME, capture the first settled frame, and assert its regions; compare against a `claude` launch frame.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/pui-default-chat-layout.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-02 — The first message works.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783, plus the live repro: the first message in a default pui launch failed with 'Session did not become ready'\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"On a fresh HOME, typing a message into a default `pui` launch produces a streamed reply in the same transcript within a bounded time, and the UI session state agrees with the backend session state.\",\"falsifier\":\"A default launch shows 'Session did not become ready' or 'Message not accepted' while the backend session is running, or no reply streams within the bound.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Real-PTY launch of `pui` with a fresh HOME against a real engine; type a greeting; assert a streamed reply appears and the UI state matches adv_sessions.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/pui-default-chat-first-message.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-03 — No internal jargon on the chat surface.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783: the interface must be usable by people who would otherwise use Claude Code / Codex\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The default chat screen shows only model, directory, context use and cost (the last two only when known); internal ids, reconciliation states, store/pot/role names and operator URLs appear only in `pui doctor` or an explicit details view, and a failed start is explained in one sentence with one next action.\",\"falsifier\":\"A default chat frame contains an adv id, a reconciliation state, a store/pot/role name, an operator URL, or an 'unknown' usage row.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Capture default-chat frames in the ready and failed-start states and scan them for the forbidden token classes; open `pui doctor` and confirm the diagnostics are there.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/pui-default-chat-layout.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-04 — Transcript and composer parity.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783: pui must match what people get from Claude Code / Codex\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"In the default chat, streaming markdown, inline collapsible tool calls, file diffs, inline permission prompts, slash commands, @file mentions, input history, Esc to interrupt, multi-line input and clean scrollback/copy all work.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any listed interaction is missing or broken in a real-PTY session of the default chat.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Drive each listed interaction through a real-PTY `pui` session and assert on captured frames.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/pui-chat-parity.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-05 — Judged against the real alternatives.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783: YOU EXPECT PEOPLE TO USE THIS INSTEAD OF CLAUDE/CODEX\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A recorded side-by-side run of `pui`, Claude Code and Codex CLI on the same five tasks (greeting, read-and-explain a file, edit a file, run tests, resume a session) shows `pui` at least as usable on each; the 'P-032 head-to-head' section of docs/evidence/pui-parity-checklist-2026-10-05.md grades every row of the parity battery against stock Claude Code and Codex (D-020 Effects 2, 5); and Avi signs off on that review before any further PUI candidate is published.\",\"falsifier\":\"The review is missing, shows `pui` worse on any task without a follow-up item, or lacks Avi's sign-off while a new PUI candidate is published.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"manual-provenance\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the captured side-by-side frames and the review write-up, check each task's comparison, and find Avi's sign-off turn.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-06 — A chat runs the right identity for where it was started.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783: pui must behave like Claude Code / Codex for people using it outside this workspace\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner:Avi 2026-09-28 (directive #783, session claude:1f398e7c)\",\"D-004\",\"D-005\",\"D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Outside every registered checkout a `pui` chat runs the chosen CLI's own identity (its own preset prompt, no Papercusp MCP servers, no psu hooks) for Claude, Codex and OMP; inside a registered checkout it runs the SU identity with its rails.\",\"falsifier\":\"A chat launched outside every registered checkout carries the SU playbook, a papercusp-su MCP server or psu hooks, or a chat launched inside a registered checkout lacks the SU identity.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Tests in agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts: 'P-001: bare `pui` opens one full-screen chat ...' asserts the Claude engine's identity outside a checkout is { prompt: 'preset:claude_code', mcpServers: [], strictMcp: true, hooksOff: true }; 'P-016: a <backend> chat runs <backend>'s own identity outside every checkout and the SU identity inside one' runs for codex and omp and asserts both halves.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-07 — Leaving pui ends its engine unless detached, and a relaunch resumes.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783: pui must behave like Claude Code / Codex, which leave nothing running after exit and resume a conversation\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner:Avi 2026-09-28 (directive #783, session claude:1f398e7c)\",\"D-007\",\"D-008\",\"D-009\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Ending the session, /exit and a killed pui all end its engine (a killed pui once its client lease lapses); /detach keeps the engine running and resuming reattaches to it; a relaunch in the same directory resumes the latest resumable conversation from its transcript.\",\"falsifier\":\"A native engine process outlives an ended, exited or killed pui past its client lease, /detach does not keep it running, or a relaunch in the directory does not resume the latest conversation.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Tests in agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts: 'P-009 END: ending the session from PUI ends it and leaves no native engine process', 'P-009 QUIT: /exit ends the engine, says so, and a relaunch resumes the conversation from its transcript', 'P-009 LEASE: a pui killed outright leaves an engine that ends once its client lease lapses', 'P-009 DETACH: /detach keeps the engine running past its lease, and resuming reattaches to it'. Real engine: the P-005 review test's resume task (frames 05a-relaunch .. 05-resume-recall).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-08 — Tool calls, questions and approvals render cleanly.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi #783: the transcript must read like Claude Code / Codex, not like internal machinery\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner:Avi 2026-09-28 (directive #783, session claude:1f398e7c)\",\"D-003\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Tool rows and approval cards name tools in human words (no raw MCP ids or JSON), a tool call renders above the answer it produced, redraws leave no stale characters, a skipped question renders as a neutral skipped row and the agent continues, and an answered approval card collapses to one row at once.\",\"falsifier\":\"A tool row or approval card shows a raw MCP id (mcp__...) or JSON, a tool call renders below its answer, a redraw leaves stale characters, a skipped question renders as a failure or stops the agent, or an answered approval card stays expanded.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Tests in agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts: 'P-013: a tool call renders above the answer it produced'; 'P-011: tool previews, an approval card and the session picker redraw over prior content with no stale characters'; 'P-014: Esc on a $route question card renders a neutral skipped row and the agent continues' (direct and wrapped routes); 'P-015: an answered approval card collapses to one Approved row at once and a held Approve key cannot answer the next card'. Approval headlines (P-008) are asserted wherever an approval card is read: NATIVE_APPROVAL_HEADLINE ('Allow Update(calc.js)?') and SU_APPROVAL_HEADLINE ('Allow papercusp-su · <verb words> (MCP)?'), including the P-005 review test's approval frames.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nThe default `pui` entrypoint becomes the chat itself: one ratatui full-screen view bound to one SU session for the cwd, driven directly (no zellij layout). The existing operator boards and multi-pane workbench stay available behind `pui workbench`. Diagnostic detail moves out of the chat into `pui doctor` and a details toggle. The first-message failure (P-002) is fixed at its root before any layout work is judged, because a chat that cannot answer makes every other comparison moot.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-01 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-02 | P-002, P-012 | tree |\n| R-03 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-04 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-05 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-06 | P-007, P-016 | tree |\n| R-07 | P-009, P-010 | tree |\n| R-08 | P-008, P-011, P-013, P-014, P-015 | tree |\n\nTree evidence means real launches of the installed/current-build `pui` in an isolated terminal with captured frames, plus the automated tests that guard them.\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` Default `pui` = full-screen, single-session chat in the cwd (Claude Code / Codex parity). No zellij chrome, operator tab bar, fleet presence or shell pane. The boards move behind `pui workbench`, and chat does not depend on zellij. — note: ← WI-10003630 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` The first message must work. Root-cause why session 31362 never became ready in the UI while the backend reports running, and fix it. Recurrence guard: a real-launch acceptance test (fresh HOME, default `pui`, type a message, streamed answer within a bounded time) that runs in the release gate. — note: ← WI-10003622 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Remove internal jargon from the chat surface. Status line = model · cwd · context % · cost (only when known); errors = one plain sentence with cause and next action. Diagnostics move to `pui doctor` / a details toggle. — note: ← WI-10003637 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Transcript and composer parity with Claude Code: streaming markdown, inline tool calls with collapsible output, file diffs, permission prompts inline, slash commands, @file mentions, input history, Esc to interrupt, multi-line input, and clean scrollback/copy. — note: ← WI-10003876 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Side-by-side review against Claude Code and Codex CLI on the same five tasks (greeting, read-and-explain a file, edit a file, run tests, resume a session), with captured frames; findings become items here. — note: ← WI-10003881 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `todo` Release gate: P-032 (public release of the PUI) and any new PUI candidate publication wait on P-001 to P-005, plus Avi's sign-off on the side-by-side review. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-015, P-032 — note: ← WI-10004161 blocker cleared\n\n\n## Phase — Items\n\n- **P-007** `done` Default chat agent is a coding assistant for the launch directory, not the workspace superuser. P-005 evidence (/mnt/data/tmp/p005/pui/01-greeting*.txt, 03-edit.txt, 2026-09-29): to 'hi' the PUI replied 'Hi Avi! I'm oriented — no open directives assigned to this session, no active work-items, and no armed loop. There are a few owner directives sitting on ended sessions…', then raised a question card about taking over workspace work and called coord_orient / work_items_claimable against harness 'pot-verify' (unrelated to the cwd). Claude Code answered 'Hi! What are we working on today?' in 2s (/mnt/data/tmp/p005/claude/01-greeting.txt). Done when: in a fresh directory, 'hi' gets a short greeting with no Papercusp vocabulary, and read/edit/run-tests prompts act on the cwd without workspace-orientation tool calls. importance: high — note: ← WI-10003921 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Tool rows and permission prompts use human names and summaries, never raw MCP ids or raw JSON. P-005 evidence (/mnt/data/tmp/p005/pui/03-edit.txt): the PUI shows '⚙ mcp__papercusp-su__coord_orient ✗' with the raw JSON arguments, and asks 'Allow mcp__papercusp-su__work_items_claimable?' above a JSON block. Claude Code shows 'Update(calc.js) ⎿ Added 2 lines, removed 2 lines' with the diff, 'Read 1 file (ctrl+o to expand)', and names MCP tools as 'papercusp-su — Plans:Get Tool: (MCP)' with a one-line description. Done when: every tool row and approval card in the default chat shows a readable name and a one-line summary, with the raw arguments only behind the details toggle. importance: high — note: Readable tool rows + approval cards (tool_display.rs, su-session-approval-display.ts), raw args behind Ctrl+R via CardSpec.details; seen in P-005 frame 03-edit-approval-1. WI-10003921.\n- **P-009** `done` A PUI chat's engine must not outlive its client unattended.
