Only then re-ask Avi for R-05 (P-006). blocked-by: P-024, P-025, P-026, P-027, P-028, P-029, P-030, P-031 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006633 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n- Release hold recorded as pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07#D-040.\n\n### D-001 — P-002 root cause: the SU engine runtime is process-local; recover it client-side, make clustered operators route to its owner\nDate: 2026-09-28\nMeasured 2026-09-28 on session 31362 (see WI-10003622 checkpoint): the launching :3070 cluster worker died ~50s after launch (memory-watchdog recycle + respawn crash-loop on the pre-bootstrap EADDRINUSE check, already fixed on staging in 1ae55c476b but not yet on main). Every later request got a REHYDRATED descriptor-only host (executorAttached:false, reconciliation reattach/live_pid, cached at rehydrate time and false once the engine exited). Nothing acted on that verdict, so the PUI waited its full 60s for a ready event no process could emit.\n\nRuling: (1) The PUI owns recovery for a pending first turn. On a detached restored runtime it calls the existing exact-resume attach path (launch-su attach_adv_session_id -> launchAttachedSuSession) at most once, re-polls the snapshot every 3s while waiting, and fails an unresumable draft immediately with the host's reason. It never waits out the deadline in silence (apps/tui/src/main.rs detached_runtime / recover_detached_runtime). (2) Clustered operators (PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER>1, the dev box's :3070) are NOT safe for per-process session runtimes, whether SU session hosts or capability PTYs. That is one class, tracked on WI-10003626: route those requests to the process that owns the runtime. Installed builds run single-process by default (resolveClusterWorkers), so (1) alone covers users; (2) is required for anyone on a clustered host. (3) The recurrence guard is the real-launch test pui-default-chat-first-message.integration.test.ts plus the detached-runtime unit test.\n\n### D-002 — R-01..R-04 real-PTY checks live in agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts as named P-00N tests\nDate: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner #783].\nThe requirement blocks name per-bar test files (pui-default-chat-layout.integration.test.ts for R-03, pui-chat-parity.integration.test.ts for R-04) that do not exist.\nThe real-PTY harness (scripted Claude engine via vi.mock, in-process operator, PuiPane) lives inside packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts and cannot be imported by a second test file (importing a test file re-registers its ~60 tests; the vi.mock factories are file-scoped).\nSo P-001..P-004 are proven by tests named \"P-001: ...\", \"P-002: ...\", \"P-003: ...\", \"P-004: ...\" in that file (run with --testNamePattern=P-00[1234]: ).\nBefore this plan ships, amend the R-01..R-04 requirement check files to point at agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts (one bar amendment for all four), so the acceptance grader measures the tests that exist.\n\n### D-003 — The release gate (P-006) also waits on the P-005 findings P-007..P-015\nDate: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner directives #783 and #724].\nThe P-005 side-by-side review (WI-10003881, comment 1150395) found that the PUI in a fresh directory cannot resume a conversation (P-010), sometimes never delivers the first message (P-012), leaks workspace-superuser vocabulary into every reply (P-007), shows raw JSON in tool rows and approval cards (P-008), leaves stale characters on redraw (P-011), and keeps its engine running after /exit (P-009).\nP-006 as written waited only on P-001..P-005 plus Avi's sign-off. Signing off with these open would ship exactly the interface #783 objected to.\nRuling: P-006 is blocked by P-007..P-015 as well. Avi's sign-off on the review is requested only once those are done and a re-run of the P-005 review test passes all five tasks in a fresh directory.\n\n### D-004 — P-007: outside a project checkout the PUI chat runs Claude Code's own identity, with no psu hooks and no Papercusp MCP\nDate: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner #783 'YOU EXPECT PEOPLE TO USE THIS INSTEAD OF CLAUDE/CODEX'].\n\nMeasured: a PUI launch goes through bootstrap-su and startClaudeSuEngine, which runs the full su playbook as a custom system prompt (su-session-claude-engine.ts systemPrompt {type:'custom'}), loads the per-session CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with settingSources ['user','project','local'] (the whole psu hook set: SessionStart orientation, UserPromptSubmit provenance + memory injection, PostToolBatch midturn context, work-item nudges), and the papercusp-su MCP server whose instructions tell the model to coord:orient. The memory-injection hook alone took 17s on a P-012 first turn (p012-real3.log). That is why 'hi' in a fresh directory returns orientation talk.\n\nRuling:\n(1) Scope rule: when the launch cwd is NOT inside the bound harness's repository root (resolveHarnessRepoRoot), the Claude engine runs identity 'coding-assistant'. Inside a registered checkout it keeps the su identity, because the PreToolUse lock arbitration, secrets guard and migration guards are data rails on a shared tree.\n(2) 'coding-assistant' for Claude: systemPrompt {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code'} (Claude Code's own prompt, dynamic sections included, so no 'exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections'); settings.disableAllHooks=true; strictMcpConfig with no MCP servers (no Papercusp tools, no Papercusp server instructions). Auth settings, permission cards (canUseTool), the native session, presence and the engine supervisor beat are unchanged.\n(3) The rule is recomputed from the same inputs (cwd + harness) on resume, so a resumed chat keeps its identity without new persisted state.\n(4) Codex/OMP (startSuRpcEngine, AGENTS.md in CODEX_HOME) get the same rule in a follow-up; Codex is usage-limited until 2026-10-03 so it cannot be verified live now.\nRejected: an su_role addendum (the su kernel and hooks would still inject the vocabulary); disabling the hooks everywhere (drops the lock rails in the shared tree).\nDone evidence for P-007: engine unit test on the SDK options per identity; attached-launch test for the scope rule; real-engine check that 'hi' in a fresh directory gets a short greeting with no Papercusp vocabulary and no mcp__papercusp tool calls.\n\n### D-005 — P-007 scope rule: SU identity inside ANY registered checkout; an unreadable registry keeps SU\nDate: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; refines D-004].\n\nD-004 said 'outside the bound harness's repository root'. Implemented instead (su-session-attached-launch.ts claudeEngineIdentityForCwd): the Claude chat keeps the SU identity when its directory (realpath) is inside ANY registered harness checkout path in the launch workspace's registry, and is 'coding-assistant' otherwise. Reason: the lock/secrets/migration rails protect every shared checkout, not only the bound harness's; a chat opened in another registered checkout would otherwise run hook-free over peers' files. Measured: the live registry has 90 paths, none a broad parent (shortest are specific dirs such as /tmp/gym), so fresh user directories still resolve to coding-assistant. If the registry cannot be read, or the launch has no cwd, the identity stays 'su': dropping the rails needs positive evidence. Containment uses realpath (symlinked hives count as inside) and rejects name-prefix siblings. Same rule on resume from the saved boot cwd.\n\nTests: su-session-attached-launch.test.ts 'engine identity scope rule' (root, subdir, symlink, prefix sibling, parent, unregistered; launch fresh vs checkout; registry failure; resume).\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-006 — P-007: a coding-assistant chat loads the user's personal CLAUDE.md; the psu persona still never does\nDate: 2026-09-29\nDate: 2026-09-29. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; refines D-004]. Measured: every per-session CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is a symlink mirror of ~/.claude that deliberately skips the personal-memory entries CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.local.md (interactive-claude-config.ts PERSONAL_MEMORY_ENTRIES, psu-isolation P-002 / D-001), so a PUI chat running Claude Code's own identity ignored the user's global instructions, unlike stock `claude`. Ruling: interactive-claude-config.ts exports syncPersonalClaudeMemory(configDir, include, home). startClaudeSuEngine calls it on every real-engine start and resume with include = (identity === 'coding-assistant'): it links exactly those entries that exist in <home>/.claude, and for the su identity it removes only symlinks pointing at those files (a real file in the config dir is left alone), so a session whose identity changes on resume never keeps personal memory under the psu persona. The psu isolation rule (D-001 of psu-isolation P-002) is unchanged for every su-identity session. Scripted-engine launches (options.query set) make no change, the same gate as persistDefaultClaudeAuthSettings. Tests: interactive-claude-config.test.ts 'pui-chat-first-ux P-007'.\n\n### D-007 — P-009: every quit path ends the engine explicitly; /detach opts out; a durable lease covers a client that dies\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner #1010/#783]. Two layers. (1) Client, immediate: pui records its quit plan every event (App::su_session_exit) and, after the terminal is restored, sends the typed `end` command (reason 'client exited', 3 s timeout) on /exit, Ctrl+C, q and any quit key; SIGHUP/SIGTERM/SIGINT become Event::Terminate -> the same quit, with a 5 s hard-exit watchdog and a second signal exiting at once. The plan is refreshed per event and run from main after `run` returns, because a closed terminal makes the next draw fail with EIO and `run` returns early. `/detach` instead POSTs .../su-session/detach and quits; the engine keeps running until the next attach clears the detach. (2) Server, bounded backstop: adv_sessions.su_client_lease_until (migration 1247), renewed every 10 s by whichever cluster worker serves the SSE stream, enforced by the engine's owning worker on the DB clock; an unrenewed lease (TTL 30 s) ends the engine as unattended. This covers SIGKILL and crashes. Consequence accepted: a second pui attached to the same chat sees its session end when the first quits, and resumes it from the transcript, the same as two terminals cannot share one `claude` process. Rejected: lease-only (engine lingers ~30 s after /exit, and the P-005 picker showed it as PARKED), and in-process subscriber counting (wrong under PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER_WORKERS=6).\n\n### D-008 — P-009: the workbench resumes its restored chat when that chat's engine ended\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner #1010/#783]. Measured: after P-009 every pui quit ends the engine, so the restored chat's session reads EndedArchived. The workbench's startup adoption (apps/tui app.rs, SuSessionInventory arm, P-010 of the attached-session work) adopted only Attached non-terminal rows and never respawned an ended one. So a workbench reopened after a normal quit showed 'No messages yet' for a conversation that had a full transcript. This red the PTY tests 'first exact draft ... and reopens' and 'PUI-TASK ... survives restart' (.papercusp/scratch/pty-composer2.log). Ruling: the adoption also takes an EndedArchived row for the chat the workbench restored, when that row has a native session id; that attach resumes the engine from its transcript, exactly as picking the chat in Sessions does. FailedOrphaned, Pending and RuntimeReplaced rows still never adopt; adoption still fires at most once per advSessionId per client and only for the restored chat. Chat-first is unaffected: it opens a fresh conversation and resumes only through /resume. Pinned by app.rs unit test su_inventory_resumes_the_restored_chat_after_its_engine_ended.\n\n### D-009 — P-009: the default chat is the live one, else the latest resumable ended one in this directory\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner #1010/#783]. Refines D-008. Measured: with D-008's adoption arm in place, the PTY cases 'first exact draft ... and reopens' and 'PUI-TASK ... survives restart' still showed 'No messages yet' / 'session new' on reopen, with ONE launch-su and no resume. Cause: startup picks the chat in apps/tui main.rs default_operator_chat, which accepted only Attached && !terminal rows; after P-009 every normal quit leaves the chat EndedArchived, so no chat was selected, agent_chat_id stayed None, and the adoption arm (which requires the selected chat) never ran. Ending a session does not archive the agent chat. Ruling: default_operator_chat ranks candidates. A live chat (Attached, non-terminal, or an SU-class chat with no inventory row) ranks above an EndedArchived chat with a native session id; recency breaks ties within a rank. FailedOrphaned, Pending, and ended rows with no native id are never the default. The P-010 exact-directory rule applies to both ranks. Consequence: bare `pui` (or the workbench) reopened in the same directory after /exit resumes that directory's last conversation, as it did before P-009 when the engine stayed alive; a fresh directory still opens a new chat. Unit tests: main.rs default_operator_chat_keeps_an_ended_chat_that_can_resume and the updated default_operator_chat_uses_live_binding_and_excludes_terminal_runtime (a live chat outranks a newer ended one; with no live chat the resumable ended chat is chosen; one with no native id is history only).\n\n### D-010 — P-016: a new PUI chat runs on the operator's configured engine unless the owner picks one\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner #1010/#783]. Measured (p009-rerun3.log, P-016 PTY): with agent-config backend=codex, bare `pui` showed 'Claude · <dir>' and dispatched to Claude. Only the session-setup panel (app.rs open_session_setup) honoured `GET /api/agent-config` effectiveBackend; decide_su_dispatch and the status line fell from su_backend straight to PUI_DEFAULT_SU_BACKEND (Claude). Ruling: SuDispatchInputs gains configured_backend = App::configured_su_backend() (effectiveBackend codex|omp|claude-code; unknown -> None). Precedence: attached session > owner pick > the conversation's ended backend > loaded SU conversation (pick, else configured, else Claude) > no conversation (configured, else Claude). The status line, the continued-session open and the setup panel use the same order, so the label always names the engine the first message runs on. Claude stays the fallback when the read has not landed or the value is unmapped. Unit tests: su_session.rs a_new_conversation_runs_on_the_configured_backend_below_every_explicit_choice; app.rs a_configured_codex_or_omp_backend_names_and_opens_a_new_chat; PTY P-016 cases.\nRelated: P-016\n\n### D-011 — WI-10004158: an omitted launch account follows an OMP gateway model to auto; an explicit account is never rewritten\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30. Author: su-f08bc8c5 [self-imposed under AUTO; mandate owner #1010/#783]. Measured (p016-rerun5.log): bare `pui` on OMP on this box always failed to start. PUI sent account 'default' even when the owner chose none; resolveOmpSessionModel (psu-launcher.mjs) takes ~/.omp/agent/config.yml modelRoles.default (here papercusp-gateway/claude-sonnet-4-6) and refuses any papercusp-gateway/* model on the default/system route. Stock `omp` with the same config runs that model through the gateway. Ruling: (1) PUI sends only an account the owner chose (app.rs su_session_launch_options: account = chat_account). (2) launch-su resolves an OMITTED account with agent-launch-core defaultLaunchAccountFor: for agent omp, the effective model (PAPERCUSP_OMP_MODEL_SELECTOR, else the requested model, else the OMP native default, the same precedence as su-session-rpc-engine) matching papercusp-gateway/ gives 'auto'; everything else keeps defaultLaunchAccount() = 'default' (D-014 unchanged: the argv always carries --account). (3) An explicit account, 'default' included, is never rewritten; its refusal now renders as '<engine> could not start: <reason>' instead of a retry prompt (WI-10004158 UX half). Known residue: the session-setup panel still pre-fills an explicit 'default' (app.rs open_session_setup), so starting from that panel without changing the account on a gateway-default OMP config shows the refusal sentence rather than routing to auto. Before, Claude and pui tasks always logged taskCompleted:true, and pui's resume recall falsely passed. Known harness gap for P-032: probe 21 (@ mention) must clear the composer first; Claude's frame typed '@cal' after a leftover '/model'.\n\n### D-024 — P-030 shape: bare pui = per-launch chat workbench; `pui --solo` = chat only; `pui chat` stays the desktop dock\nDate: 2026-10-06\nBare `pui` opens its own pid-keyed zellij session `pui-chat-<launcher pid>`. It never attaches to an existing session, so a stale pui-wb or another terminal's chat cannot take a launch over, and a leftover whose launcher died is swept by the reaper's dead-owner rule. Layout: the chat (`pui --solo`) is the focused main pane at 65%. Beside it in one stack sit `pui hud` (expanded; the one reactive launch owner), `pui wake-pane`, `pui network-pane` and the work shell. Alt+z zooms the focused pane (collapse or restore the side panes). A launch narrower than 120 columns starts zoomed. Exiting the chat stops the session, and the launcher prints the conversation into the real terminal's scrollback. The solo chat is used whenever zellij cannot run: `--solo`, inside a zellij pane, a non-TTY launch, no zellij on PATH, or an operator identity that does not resolve (the solo chat owns setup). P-030's text named `pui chat` / `pui --solo` for chat-only, but `pui chat` is already the desktop-docked native terminal surface (run_chat_dock), so only `--solo` takes that role; changing `pui chat` would break the desktop dock. Chat-surface PTY tests and the parity battery run `pui --solo` (the battery takes `--pui-workbench` for bare-pui frames). [self-imposed under owner:Avi #1356 AUTO; P-030 text cites #1277/#1276]\n\n### D-025 — P-026 shape: the chosen model rides on the next owner turn; each engine applies it before that turn\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356; the P-026 text is from #1276 'how can I switch models?'] Chosen: no new command type. The su-session owner_turn command (libs/generic/chat-protocol/src/su-session.ts) gains an optional `model` (a spec, model[:effort]). Omitted means keep the current model. P-026 says the pick applies 'from the next turn', which is exactly a property of the next owner turn, so this reuses the existing command, receipt and delivery path instead of adding a parallel one. Per engine (each adapter's controls.ownerTurn gains `model?`): (1) Claude (su-session-claude-engine.ts): before input.write, if the spec differs from the current one, await sdk.setModel(model) and, for an effort suffix, sdk.applyFlagSettings({ effortLevel }). Both are streaming-input SDK methods (sdk.d.ts); ClaudeEngineQuery's Pick<Query,...> gains them. (2) Codex (su-session-codex-adapter.ts): pass model / effort on that turn's turn/start (verify against the app-server schema before building). (3) OMP: send the RPC set_model before the prompt (verify against the OMP RPC). After a successful apply the host snapshot's `model` is updated, so the footer and /status show the engine's real model, not the PUI's guess. PUI (apps/tui): /model opens the existing session_config model picker (PickerAxis, tiers from /api/agent-config for the chat's backend), current model marked; Enter stores a pending model that is sent with the next owner_turn. The footer shows the snapshot model, plus 'next turn: X' while one is pending. Launch flags `pui --model <spec>` and `pui --account <auto|default|name>` (D-023 adds --account) set the create-session model/account fields that already exist. Rejected: a separate set_model command. It needs its own receipt, refusal and replay handling, and between the switch and the next turn there is nothing for it to do. Guard: a PTY test switches the model with /model, sends a turn, and asserts the scripted engine received the new model for that turn and the footer names it; unit tests for the protocol field and each adapter.\n\n### D-026 — P-027 G-6: /approvals and Shift+Tab pick an approvals mode that rides on the next owner turn, like D-025's model\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356; '/approvals (permission mode)' is P-027 text from #1276]\n\nChosen: the su-session owner_turn command gains an optional `approvals` with one of three engine-neutral values. Omitted keeps the current mode. The engine applies it before the turn, so a refused switch refuses that turn (code approvals_switch_refused), the same contract as D-025's model.\n- `ask`: ask before edits and commands. Claude: sdk.setPermissionMode('default'). Codex: turn/start approvalPolicy 'untrusted' + sandboxPolicy {type:'workspaceWrite'}.\n- `auto-edit`: make edits without asking; ask before other commands. Claude: 'acceptEdits'. Codex: 'on-request' + workspaceWrite (Codex's own default, and what PUI launches Codex with today).\n- `read-only`: look and plan, change nothing. Claude: 'plan'. Codex: 'on-request' + {type:'readOnly'}.\nVerified 2026-10-06 against `codex app-server generate-json-schema` (codex-cli 0.160.1): TurnStartParams.approvalPolicy and .sandboxPolicy exist and apply 'for this turn and subsequent turns'. That 'untrusted' also asks before apply_patch edits is [inferred] from codex-rs, not probed live.\n- OMP has no approval-mode RPC (PUI installs always-ask callbacks), so an OMP engine refuses `approvals` and PUI says '/approvals is not available for OMP'.\n- Ruled out: full access / bypassPermissions. PUI launches never set allowDangerouslySkipPermissions, and D-021/D-022 keep tool approval with the owner through cards.\n\nThe host descriptor gains optional `approvals`, published after a successful switch (host.updateApprovals, like updateModel). The initial value is the launch mode: Claude 'ask', Codex 'auto-edit', OMP omitted.\n\nPUI: `/approvals` opens a three-row picker with one-line descriptions and the current mode marked; Shift+Tab in the composer cycles to the next mode. Either stores a pending mode that is sent with the next owner turn (`· next turn: <mode>` until then). /status shows the mode.\n\nRejected: a separate set_approvals command. It would need its own receipt, refusal and replay handling, and between the switch and the next turn there is nothing for it to do (the D-025 reasoning).\n\nGuard: unit tests for the host validation, each engine's sent parameters, and the PUI picker, cycle and send.\n\n### D-027 — P-025 adds /backend: the only route to Codex or OMP in chat-first pui\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356; 'Verified against the P-001-style frames for Claude, Codex and OMP' is P-025 text]\n\nFound while running the P-025 engine legs. Since P-027, chat-first Esc stays in the message box. The backend picker's only key, `b`, works only outside the box. A bare `pui` user could therefore never start a Codex or OMP conversation. The engine is not chosen by `--model` either: main.rs opens the SU session with `agent:` = picked backend, then the operator's configured backend, then Claude.\n\nChosen: a `/backend` composer command (apps/tui/src/chat_commands.rs SlashKind::Backend) that opens the existing backend picker (app.rs open_backend_picker). It adds no new picker and no new launch flag. A bound conversation still shows every row disabled with 'Open a new conversation to change it' (/clear). Rejected: a `pui --backend` launch flag. It would not help someone already inside pui, and stock Claude Code and Codex have no engine to pick, so there is no parity text for it.\n\nGuards: chat_commands::tests::backend_is_reachable_from_the_menu; app::tests::chat_first_backend_command_picks_the_engine_for_a_new_conversation. The parity battery takes `--pui-backend claude|codex|omp` and drives /backend, and `--probes 10,11,12,13` runs only selected rows.\n\n### D-028 — P-028: one approval prompt for every engine — 1 Yes / 2 Yes, don't ask again / 3 No (stop, tell it what to do), Claude Code keys\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356; the item text is P-028 from #1276]\n\nStock frames (default permission mode, recorded 2026-10-06 with the new p005 driver flag `--stock-args`; saved at ~/.papercusp/evidence/pui-parity-2026-10-05/p028-stock/):\n- Claude Code 2.1.289 (`--permission-mode default`): full-width rule, 'Edit file' / 'calc.js', numbered diff between dashed rules, 'Do you want to make this edit to calc.js?', `❯ 1. Yes` / `2. Yes, and switch to accept edits (...) for this session (shift+tab)` / `3. No`, footer 'Esc to cancel · Tab to amend'.\n- Codex 0.160.1 (`-s read-only -a on-request`; the CLI no longer accepts `-a untrusted`, the app-server schema still does, so D-026 stands): 'Would you like to run the following command?', reason, `$ cmd`, `› 1. Yes, proceed (y)` / `2. Yes, and don't ask again for commands that start with ... (p)` / `3. No, and tell Codex what to do differently (esc)`, 'Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel'.\n\nChosen contract (server su-session-native-cards.ts + pui):\n1. Every tool-approval card carries `approval: { title, question }` beside the existing prompt, and its options have stable ids `yes`, `always` (only when the engine can remember the choice), `no`. pui recognises an approval card by that field, not by parsing 'Allow X?'.\n2. Labels: '1. Yes'; '2. Yes, and don't ask again for <what> this session'; '3. No, and tell <Claude|Codex|OMP> what to do instead'.\n3. `always` per engine: Claude = its allow-rule suggestions or its acceptEdits mode suggestion, re-scoped to the session (D-021: never a settings file); Codex = decision `acceptForSession`; OMP has no remember option natively (it calls ui.select with Approve/Deny), so pui remembers it for this runtime: an edit-type tool by name, a command tool by its exact request text.\n4. `no` rejects AND stops the turn so the owner types what to do next, the way Codex's option 3 and Claude Code's Esc do: Claude deny with interrupt:true, Codex decision `cancel`, OMP 'Deny' then abort. Esc on an approval card is `no`.\n5. Keys (Claude Code's): 1/2/3 pick at once, up/down + Enter, Esc = No, Shift+Tab = option 2 when shown, Ctrl+R raw details. Rendering: a full-width rule, the title, the change between dashed rules (the diff is shown only here while the card is open, P-020), the question, the numbered rows with a ❯ marker on the highlighted row, footer 'Enter to select · ↑↓ to move · Esc to cancel'. After No the composer is focused with the hint 'Tell <engine> what to do instead'.\nNot taken: Claude's 'Tab to amend' (attach a note to Yes/No). Option 3 plus the next message covers the item text; revisit only if P-032 grades it a gap.\n\n### D-029 — P-029 shape: two new su-session events, `usage` and `plan`, fed by each engine's native data; pui renders footer, /status and a todo checklist from them\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356; the P-029 text is from #1276]\n\nFound before building: the su-session protocol (libs/generic/chat-protocol/src/su-session.ts) has no usage or context event. All three adapters declare `context` unsupported and Claude also declares `usage` unsupported, so pui's footer and /status can only say 'context unknown'. P-029 therefore needs protocol work first, not just rendering.\n\nChosen: two new event types on the existing event stream (no new transport, no polling).\n- `usage` {turnId?, contextTokens?, contextWindow?, inputTokens?, outputTokens?, costUsd?}. Every field optional; a field the engine cannot know is omitted, never guessed. costUsd is the running session total, not a per-turn delta.\n- `plan` {turnId?, items:[{text, status: pending|in_progress|completed}]}. Each event replaces the whole list.\n\nSources, each read from the installed engine, not assumed:\n- Claude (claude-agent-sdk sdk.d.ts): context = the last assistant message's input + cache_read + cache_creation + output tokens; window = result.modelUsage[model].contextWindow; cost = result.total_cost_usd (already a running total per the SDK doc, so read the latest, never sum). Plan = the TodoWrite tool's input.todos [{content, status}].\n- Codex app-server 0.160.1 (`codex app-server generate-json-schema`): `thread/tokenUsage/updated` {tokenUsage:{last.totalTokens, total, modelContextWindow}} gives context and window; Codex reports no cost, so costUsd is omitted. Plan = `turn/plan/updated` {plan:[{step, status: pending|inProgress|completed}]}.\n- OMP (~/.papercusp/bin/omp): every assistant `message_end` carries message.usage {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens, cost.total}; context = that message's totalTokens, cost = the sum over the session (same as OMP's own get_session_stats); window = get_state's model.contextWindow. OMP has no plan tool wired here, so `plan` stays unsupported for OMP.\n\nEach adapter flips its `usage` / `context` capability to supported only for the fields it actually fills.\n\npui (apps/tui): the idle footer reads `<model> · <approvals> · N% context left · $cost` (cost only when known). From 80% used it turns to a warning ('Context 85% full: /compact'). /status gains context used/window and cost. The working line gains the token count (G-2). The latest `plan` renders as a checklist above the input (☐ pending, ◐ in progress, ☑ done), hidden once every item is done and the turn has ended.\n\nRejected: polling a stats RPC from pui (adds a request per tick and a second source of truth); computing context in pui from transcript text (guesses tokens).\n\n### D-030 — P-010 tightening: a PUI that knows its directory never lands on a chat whose directory is unknown\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356; found fixing WI-10006533]\n\nObserved: back-to-back pui launches in different fresh directories (p005 driver legs) were refused on their first message, 'The conversation is already bound to a different engine or project'. Measured: the failed legs created no chat; the five passing legs each created one (pot-verify agent_chats 07:57-08:31Z). Both failures started while the previous leg's session was still shutting down (Codex adv 34915 ended 08:35:57, the Claude leg started 08:35:29; Claude adv 34885 ended 07:57:52, just before the OMP leg).\n\nMechanism in the code: probe_su_session_inventory drops any chat whose snapshot request fails (`.ok()`), and default_operator_chat ranked an su-session chat with NO inventory row as live (2) with no directory check. A row with cwd None was also eligible from any directory ('older operators'). So a launch in project B took project A's chat as its agent_chat_id, chat-first quick start (which needs agent_chat_id None) was skipped, and the first send asked the operator to bind A's chat to B's engine. With the same engine it would have silently joined A's conversation, which P-010 forbids. [inferred] The dropped snapshot is the teardown window answering 404 su_session_not_attached; not probed live.\n\nChosen: default_operator_chat follows session_in_directory's own rule. When the PUI's launch directory is known, a chat whose directory is unknown (no inventory row, or a row with no cwd) is not eligible as the default. A PUI with no known directory keeps the old ranking (nothing to scope by). Cost accepted: if a same-directory chat's snapshot fails transiently at startup, that launch starts a new conversation instead of landing on it; /resume still lists it. Rejected: retrying the snapshot probe (narrows the window, leaves the cross-project bind possible on any probe failure).\n\n### D-031 — P-029 wire shape: usage and plan ride the session descriptor (host.updateUsage / updatePlan), not new event types; pui tolerates unknown event types\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356]. Amends the wire shape in D-029; D-029's sources, fields, and pui rendering stand unchanged.\n\nFound before building [observed in source]: every installed pui ends its event stream on a frame it cannot decode. apps/tui/src/su_session.rs SuSessionEvent is a closed serde enum (tag=type, no fallback), and apps/tui/src/main.rs ~L6606-6636 turns a decode Err into SuSessionStreamError, which marks the session FailedOrphaned and fails the pending turn. So an operator that starts emitting new `usage`/`plan` event types would break every pui already installed (including ~/.cargo/bin/pui and any published candidate) on its first turn. Per-client filtering is no fix: pui marks any sequence gap as stale ('stream gap; reconnecting', app.rs apply_su_session_event).\n\nChosen: `usage` {contextTokens?, contextWindow?, inputTokens?, outputTokens?, costUsd?} and `plan` {items:[{text, status: pending|in_progress|completed}]} become OPTIONAL fields on SuSessionDescriptor, published through the existing `session` event by two new host methods, updateUsage (merges fields, emits only on change) and updatePlan (replaces the list), exactly as updateModel/updateApprovals already do. Old clients ignore the unknown descriptor fields (pui's descriptor struct has no deny_unknown_fields; validateDescriptor checks identity only). Bonus: a reconnect snapshot carries the latest usage and plan, so a resumed pui shows them immediately.\n\nClass fix in the same change: pui decodes an event whose `type` it does not know as Unknown{envelope}, which advances the sequence and is otherwise ignored, so a future protocol addition cannot break newer pui builds the same way.\n\nRejected: new event types (breaks installed pui); operator-side filtering by declared client capability (creates sequence gaps pui reports as stale); a protocolVersion bump (pui refuses a mismatched version outright, same break).\n\n### D-032 — P-032 result: fix the model picker, the @ popup redraw and Codex context % before re-asking Avi for R-05\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO, owner:Avi #1356]\n\nP-032 (WI-10006633) graded all 25 parity rows (docs/evidence/pui-parity-checklist-2026-10-05.md, 'P-032 head-to-head'). Claude engine: 22 level or ahead, row 12 behind, row 23 open, row 25 out of scope. Codex engine: rows 18/19/22 not yet level; row 7 is a box-config confound (this box's AGENTS.md lock rule), not pui.\n\nChosen: P-006 (re-ask Avi for R-05) waits until these are fixed and installed:\n- WI-10006652 /model lists server routing tiers with internal '[owner …]' notes; nothing settable on Codex. A missing model switch was one of Avi's 2026-10-02 rejection reasons (#1276), so asking with this picker invites the same rejection.\n- WI-10006651 @ popup not drawn after a cleared paste.\n- WI-10006653 Codex engine shows no context % until resume.\n- WI-10006646 (stray [ede_diagnostic] line on Esc/exit) fixed in tree; must be live on the operator pui talks to.\nNot blocking R-05 (filed, owned): WI-10006644 (5 s send bound on a stalled operator), WI-10006654 (unconfirmed resume-picker glitch), WI-10006626 (usage-limit line has no next step).\n\nRejected: asking Avi now with the gaps listed. The bar is 'as user friendly as the claude and codex tui' [owner 2026-10-02 #1276], and row 12 is a known miss on that bar.\n\n### D-033 — Bare pui shows the workbench panes at every width; the chat always shows an Alt+z hint\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, directive #1469, AskUserQuestion answer 'Always show + hint (Recommended)'] Supersedes the P-030 implementer choice to start zoomed (side panes hidden) below CHAT_WORKBENCH_MIN_SIDE_COLS=120. That choice hid every pane on Avi's 92-column terminal with no on-screen signal, so he concluded the panes were never restored (#1276/#1277). Rule now: bare `pui` never auto-hides the panes because of terminal width, and the workbench chat pane always shows a visible 'Alt+z' hint for hiding/showing them. Tracked as WI-10006739.\n\n### D-034 — Workbench side panes get a compact narrow render mode instead of 'Terminal too small'\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, dialog answer 'Compact side panes (Recommended)' + 'You (Recommended)', session su-210901d4] The bare-pui workbench keeps chat + side column (D-033). Each side pane (hud, wake, network, work) must render a condensed view down to ~28x10 instead of the global MIN_COLS=80/MIN_ROWS=20 'Terminal too small' block (apps/tui/src/ui.rs). PTY tests must assert real side-pane content at 92x26 and 200x50. Tracked as WI-10006754.\n\n### D-035 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-06\nAmendment-Id: amend-ee2490d43cb503b893d13d96\nRequest-Hash: 920e6efa9cef1469e27049a8cee4870d47f64690c1fcf3afdae3dfe508aeb55b\nActor: su-caaa53ba-fb38-44e0-a1b4-996a55267afc\nReason: Rev 9 per D-020 (pui-chat-first-ux): R-01 reworded to Effect (3) (bare pui = workbench with the chat as focused main pane; pui --solo = full-screen chat), citing the P-030 test; R-05 adds the P-032 parity checklist (Effects 2, 5) and declares its check manual (vetter post 1160161 defect a: the sign-off is human provenance). Grading audit EI-25245827981907644 failed rev 8 on R-01 vs D-020. Plan R-01/R-05 prose mirrored at plan rev 126. Review fix (thread-post:1160308, su-c11a3c22): every drill names the renamed 'P-001: `pui --solo`' test; R-01's drill also runs both P-030 tests; R-01 adds D-033 (owner #1469, narrow terminal keeps the panes and shows an Alt+z hint).\nApproved-By: su-c11a3c22-0344-4063-9608-36e526a81ad2\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1160327\nApproved-At: 2026-10-06T17:46:20.223Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 126 → 127\nChanged BARs: R-01, R-05\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-036 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-06\nAmendment-Id: amend-72b847a3971445db4c081322\nRequest-Hash: 3ba25fd1627abcb34f375f8fb65b5442ffbee63c6fff407c1bbe3afa3c7be23d\nActor: su-caaa53ba-fb38-44e0-a1b4-996a55267afc\nReason: Rev 10 per rev-9 vetting conv-muwz2if3 (posts 1160348 su-9b00a661, 1160351 su-b76ab845). Blocking: R-02 binds the shipped P-024 test and adds the D-021/D-022 never-silent floor (working line at once, status text within 5 s, hung operator errors within 5 s); R-04 binds the shipped P-018 test and adds D-019 (wheel scrolls, drag copies). Fold-ins: R-01 drift and method add D-034 (no 'Terminal too small'); sourceRefs add D-019..D-024, D-033, D-034, D-018 and owner #1060/#1276/#1277/#1469; P-001 failure attribution stated on the five bars that share it. Not changed: post 1160351's defect 3 is not present in rev 9, where R-01..R-04, R-06, R-07 already bind check.files to agent-chat-pty.integration.test.ts (rubrics:get rev 9).\nApproved-By: su-1cef92cb-3eae-4877-976c-b627a5b8f8ee\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1160360\nApproved-At: 2026-10-06T17:59:34.040Z\nRubric revision: 9 → 10\nSubject plan revision: 127 → 128\nChanged BARs: R-01, R-02, R-04, R-05\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-037 — Avi accepts PUI chat for R-05 on build 33287a0d19 (\"Good enough, ship it\")\nDate: 2026-10-07\nDate: 2026-10-07 ~00:43Z. Source: [owner:Avi 2026-10-07, interactive AskUserQuestion dialog in session su-caaa53ba-fb38-44e0-a1b4-996a55267afc]. Channel switch from the unanswered conv-muwr86ss-0000-4ec79793288745799f32e3701d60863d.\n\nQuestion shown (verbatim): \"Avi, the pui on this machine is now the current build (33287a0d19). Running `pui` in a terminal opens straight into one full-screen chat. Since your 2026-10-02 rejection, the first message now gets through reliably, tool calls show above the answer they produced, and an answered approval card shrinks to one line. Esc skips a question, and /exit plus /resume pick the conversation back up. After trying it, is pui's chat good enough to ship (R-05)?\"\n\nOwner answer (verbatim option selected): \"Good enough, ship it\".\n\nCandidate: installed ~/.cargo/bin/pui 0.1.0 (33287a0d19), binarySha256 6531c790a8d483c61d65a1b2abdcfc223c11582f1538281bee3e533ba9b3c82a, sourceDirty false (~/.papercusp/pui-install.json); git diff 33287a0d19..HEAD -- apps/tui is empty at 00:41Z. It includes the WI-10006770 Codex label fix (66d1b75935).\n\nEffect: R-05 (P-005 side-by-side review / P-006 owner sign-off) is accepted by the owner. This supersedes the 2026-10-02 rejection (D-018). Under D-041 R-12's study requirement is gone, so this approval is the only owner gate. Remaining ship steps (agent-owned): fresh as-committed PTY proof + mutation probes for the TUI clauses (batch 4, WI-10006717), per-item audit, rubric vetting attestation, independent grading, implementer acceptance, then plans:set-plan-status shipped. Release plan pui-first-party-public-release-2026-09-07 D-040's hold lifts once this plan ships.\n"},{"harness_slug":"recipe-app","plan_slug":"acceptance-recipe-app-crud-2026-09-28","title":"Acceptance BAR — Recipe app v1 — recipe CRUD (desktop)","status":"active","created":"2026-09-28","owner":"su-5df021e8-26ac-4fa1-b2e5-30478c077d9c","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Recipe app v1 — recipe CRUD (desktop)\nslug: acceptance-recipe-app-crud-2026-09-28\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-09-28\nupdated: 2026-09-28\nowner: su-5df021e8-26ac-4fa1-b2e5-30478c077d9c\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Recipe app v1 — recipe CRUD (desktop)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). V1 = recipe CRUD on the papercusp-app desktop template.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Template chassis boots.**\n```requirement\n{\n \"intent\": {\n  \"request\": \"start from the papercusp-app template, target desktop\"\n },\n \"acceptance\": {\n  \"condition\": \"A headless boot of the recipe-app desktop shell reaches a rendered webview backed by its embedded Postgres.\",\n  \"falsifier\": \"The headless boot exits or times out before a rendered webview.\",\n  \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n   \"integration\"\n  ]\n },\n \"verification\": {\n  \"method\": \"Run the boot integration test (headless Tauri boot).\",\n  \"check\": {\n   \"kind\": \"tests\",\n   \"files\": [\n    \"tests/boot.integration.test.ts\"\n   ]\n  }\n }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Recipes persist.**\n```requirement\n{\n \"intent\": {\n  \"request\": \"recipe CRUD data layer\"\n },\n \"acceptance\": {\n  \"condition\": \"A recipe saved through the typed write path is returned unchanged by the recipe read query after the sidecar restarts.\",\n  \"falsifier\": \"The read query returns a missing or altered recipe after restart.\",\n  \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n   \"unit\"\n  ]\n },\n \"verification\": {\n  \"method\": \"Run the recipe data-layer tests against the embedded Postgres.\",\n  \"check\": {\n   \"kind\": \"tests\",\n   \"files\": [\n    \"tests/recipes.data.test.ts\"\n   ]\n  }\n }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Recipe list shows saved recipes.**\n```requirement\n{\n \"intent\": {\n  \"request\": \"recipe list screen\"\n },\n \"acceptance\": {\n  \"condition\": \"Every saved recipe appears as an entry in the recipe list screen, which updates live without a reload.\",\n  \"falsifier\": \"A saved recipe is absent from the list or appears only after a reload.\",\n  \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n   \"unit\"\n  ]\n },\n \"verification\": {\n  \"method\": \"Run the list view tests with a sync-backed fixture.\",\n  \"check\": {\n   \"kind\": \"tests\",\n   \"files\": [\n    \"tests/ui/recipe-list.test.tsx\"\n   ]\n  }\n }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Recipe editor saves fields.**\n```requirement\n{\n \"intent\": {\n  \"request\": \"recipe editor create/edit\"\n },\n \"acceptance\": {\n  \"condition\": \"Submitting the recipe editor with valid fields stores a recipe with exactly those fields.\",\n  \"falsifier\": \"The stored recipe differs from the submitted fields or the submit is rejected.\",\n  \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n   \"unit\"\n  ]\n },\n \"verification\": {\n  \"method\": \"Run the editor tests.\",\n  \"check\": {\n   \"kind\": \"tests\",\n   \"files\": [\n    \"tests/ui/recipe-editor.test.tsx\"\n   ]\n  }\n }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Recipe detail and delete.**\n```requirement\n{\n \"intent\": {\n  \"request\": \"recipe detail view and delete\"\n },\n \"acceptance\": {\n  \"condition\": \"Confirming delete on a recipe detail view removes that recipe from storage and from the list.\",\n  \"falsifier\": \"The recipe remains in storage or the list after a confirmed delete.\",\n  \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n   \"unit\"\n  ]\n },\n \"verification\": {\n  \"method\": \"Run the detail view tests.\",\n  \"check\": {\n   \"kind\": \"tests\",\n   \"files\": [\n    \"tests/ui/recipe-detail.test.tsx\"\n   ]\n  }\n }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — End-to-end CRUD.**\n```requirement\n{\n \"intent\": {\n  \"request\": \"working recipe app\"\n },\n \"acceptance\": {\n  \"condition\": \"A headless end-to-end run of the full recipe lifecycle exits with zero failed steps.\",\n  \"falsifier\": \"Any step of the headless end-to-end run fails.\",\n  \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n   \"e2e\"\n  ]\n },\n \"verification\": {\n  \"method\": \"Run the headless Tauri end-to-end test.\",\n  \"check\": {\n   \"kind\": \"tests\",\n   \"files\": [\n    \"tests/e2e/recipe-crud.e2e.test.ts\"\n   ]\n  }\n }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nApp is materialized from papercusp-app (target: desktop) into harness recipe-app. P-001 bootstraps the chassis; P-002 owns schema + typed writes; P-003/P-004/P-005 are disjoint UI slices (list, editor, detail) that fan out in parallel; P-006 is the end-to-end acceptance pass.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"desktop-perf-measure-candidate-build-2026-09-29","title":"Desktop-perf gate: attribute by build identity, then measure the candidate's own build (or demote to a trend monitor)","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-29","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Desktop-perf gate: attribute by build identity, then measure the candidate's own build (or demote to a trend monitor)\nslug: desktop-perf-measure-candidate-build-2026-09-29\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-29\nupdated: 2026-09-29\n---\n\n## Context\n- Producer: packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/desktop-perf-scheduled-run.ts, scheduled in packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/periodic-workflows.ts (crontab `0 40 2,10,18 * * *`). Spawns `npm run test:all` in tools/perf-test/wdio; wdio.conf.ts picks the newest-mtime packaged GUI binary under the cargo target dir.\n- Attribution today: perf-report.ts `recordBinaryIdentity` stamps `build:packaged-binary-mtime-ms`; desktop-perf-gate.ts `binaryPredatesBaseline` compares it to main's newest commit time and demotes to warn (UNATTRIBUTABLE) when the build predates main.\n- Measures are numeric-only rows; `desktop_perf_runs` has `git_sha` (checkout HEAD at run time, NOT the binary's source) and no build-identity column.\n- The binary bakes `PAPERCUSP_BUILD_SHA` (build.rs / main.rs), and release builds emit build-provenance.json with `buildSha` next to the artifacts. ⚠ its top-level `gitHead` is the papercusp-desktop SUBMODULE head, not the superproject sha.\n\n## Items\n- **P-001** `todo` Record the measured binary's build identity on every desktop_perf_run: migration adds `build_sha text NULL`; wdio reads the identity (build-provenance.json `buildSha`, else unknown — never the checkout HEAD); ingest + recordDesktopPerfRun carry it; readers expose it. Tests in each layer's framework.\n- **P-002** `todo` Gate attributes by identity (blocked-by P-001): build_sha resolves to the judged candidate → attributable (today's budget logic); build_sha is contained in the baseline but is not the candidate → warn, pre-existing; build_sha unknown → current mtime fallback. Tests in the desktop-perf-gate tests.\n- **P-003** `todo` Measure the cost of a packaged Linux release build from an isolated checkout at a fixed sha (cold and warm cargo target), plus wdio suite time, and whether it contends on the shared cargo target lock. Record the numbers as evidence on the item.\n- **P-004** `todo` Apply D-002 to P-003's numbers and implement the chosen branch (blocked-by P-003, P-002).\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** draft; umbrella WI-10003824 held by su-4cdad80d. P-001 finding [observed 2026-09-29 04:55Z]: (a) no build-provenance.json exists next to the deb bundle under /mnt/data/cargo-target/release/bundle/deb/ (release provenance lives with release artifacts, not the cargo target); (b) `npm run build` = papercusp-desktop/bin/build-deb-repacked.sh never exports PAPERCUSP_BUILD_SHA, so a locally built packaged binary bakes an EMPTY sha; (c) the binary has no CLI flag that prints its identity. So P-001 must include the build path writing a build-identity file beside the bundle (sha + builtAt + source), with wdio reading it; binaries without that file (e.g. the 0.0.20 release deb) stay `unknown` and keep the mtime fallback per D-001.\n\n**Next:** P-001: define the identity-file contract, make build-deb-repacked.sh export PAPERCUSP_BUILD_SHA and write it, add build_sha to desktop_perf_runs (migration via the allocator), carry it through perf-report.ts, the ingest route and recordDesktopPerfRun, with tests at each layer.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Attribute desktop-perf runs by build identity before changing what gets built\nDate: 2026-09-29\n[self-imposed, su-4cdad80d 2026-09-29] Both branches of the D-002 fork need to know which source the measured binary was built from; today only its file mtime is known, and time attribution misreads any rebuild that is not the candidate as the candidate. So P-001 and P-002 (record build_sha; gate classifies attributable / pre-existing-on-baseline / unknown) land first, and the mtime rule stays as the fallback for runs with no identity. A build identity is recorded only from the artifact's own provenance, never from the checkout HEAD at run time (that is git_sha, a different fact).\n\n### D-002 — Fork criterion: the gate builds and measures the candidate only if it is cheap and lock-free; otherwise desktop-perf becomes a trend monitor\nDate: 2026-09-29\n[self-imposed default under AUTO, su-4cdad80d 2026-09-29; the owner may overrule] Written criterion applied to P-003's measurements: if a WARM isolated packaged Linux build plus the wdio suite adds at most 15 minutes to a green-checkpoint round AND does not serialize on the shared cargo target-dir lock with other builds on the box, the green-checkpoint builds the candidate in its checkout tree and measures it (desktop-perf keeps blocking authority, now provably about the candidate). Otherwise desktop-perf is demoted to a trend monitor: the producer rebuilds main three times a day for trend data and files regressions as work-items, and the gate stops presenting it as a promotion leg. Rationale: gate rounds are about an hour, and a gate that stalls on a cargo lock is worse than one that warns honestly.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"psu-cloud-connector-liveness-multi-signin-2026-09-29","title":"psu cloud workspaces: connector liveness (connector_unavailable) + multiple cloud sign-ins","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-09-29","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: psu cloud workspaces: connector liveness (connector_unavailable) + multiple cloud sign-ins\nslug: psu-cloud-connector-liveness-multi-signin-2026-09-29\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-09-29\nupdated: 2026-10-13\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** [2026-10-13 acceptance carry, WI-6554700010009749] All 10 original implementation items remain terminal; the plan is draft/archived and has not shipped. Current focused 7-file suites passed 243 tests with zero skips; ledger run refs are stored on WI-6554700010009749. Rubric rev6 is unvetted: consult conv-mv66s3uj-0000-ccca41ed9342493b823d06378cc5f1d0 post1178215 requires separating R-9/R-11 and R-13/R-6/R-8 falsifiers and an R-17 identity positive control. Existing automated proof is inadequate/stale; fresh R-9 live idle reconnect, R-12 deployed version/digest/watchdog, and R-13 live second-organization approvals are still unbound. No current implementation regression was measured in those focused suites.\n\n**Next:** Audit the recovered owner source and Product shaping; prepare one final as-built rubric amendment with outside-lineage review. Finish WI-6554700010009801's identity positive control once EI-23241836994497967's existing owner supplies a qualified maintained native-edit protocol. Bind current adequate evidence on each declared plane, re-vet and independently grade the final rubric, obtain the implementer verdict, then verify final shipment. Continue independent preparation while the native edit protocol repair progresses; do not bypass it or take another agent's live gate lane.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience:** People using their installed psu to connect to Papercusp cloud workspaces, including Avi on avi-test and people with accounts in several organizations.\n\n**Problem:** Avi's psu attach to avi-test closed with connector_unavailable and suggested resuming a shell that had never bound. A first cloud sign-in also hid the path to another sign-in, and another organization on the same portal replaced the first profile.\n\n**Outcome:** The connector and relay detect a silent link and recover it; the picker reports reachability honestly. Selecting a supported Papercusp cloud workspace opens psu's normal agent screen there. The machine's service starts psu, while agents run as the workspace account. One install holds several portal+organization+user profiles and always offers another cloud sign-in, with organization-labelled workspace entries.\n\n**Non-goals:** Add a customer-level service login (option A), install psu for use inside the customer's ordinary shell, retain a shell as the supported cloud psu experience (option C), add extra support for other portals, or change the separate BYOC shipment.\n\n**Source turns:** session_turn:claude:9a0d17e2-f149-4503-b140-cd615282fc2d:0 contains both original requests; :11 approves this-session execution, immediate avi-test restart/re-enrollment despite ending running sessions, and the several-accounts/organizations interpretation (D-001). session_turn:claude:213b514d-6fd0-41eb-83d2-2118b33a84ac:5 reports the interim shell failure; :8 and :9 request an explanation of A/B/C; :10 is the explanation, not owner authorization. Owner directive #1069 stores the literal B choice and is recorded by D-002; its sourceTurnRef/sessionRef are null, so no canonical owner session-turn for that choice is asserted. D-003..D-006 record subsequent acceptance amendments and the machine-level own-session scope clarification.\n\n**Scenarios:**\n1. After avi-test has had no terminal session for more than 25 minutes, Avi uses the installed psu to connect and gets a psu agent session whose agent runs as the workspace account. The method also records clean exit; R-11 owns the teardown acceptance condition.\n2. A connector stops answering pings or receives no inbound frames: relay/client contracts detect the failure, replace or detach the link, and stale heartbeats neither advertise reachability nor mint a terminal ticket. An attach with no bound shell offers no resume hint; recovery within the bounded wait attaches successfully.\n3. A person signs in to organization A, then B on app.papercusp.com. The first profile remains, the picker still offers another sign-in, entries name their organizations, and live portal approvals/control-plane workspace lists establish that both real sign-ins work.\n4. A supported cloud terminal request carries program psu and allowlisted argv. The host and launcher enforce the same restrictions; hosted-customer mode does not ask for identity, fleet, or an installer. Exiting psu ends the relay session without starting a shell.\n\n**Constraints and acceptance:** Preserve D-002's service/agent identity boundary and argv restrictions and D-005's one-customer-machine session boundary. Verification uses registered project tests for tree contracts and actual installed/live/deployed evidence for R-9/R-12/R-13. Earlier proof is a historical reference, not fresh operational proof. Missing second-organization approval is never replaced with fixture evidence or claimed as completed.\n\n## Diagnosis (measured 2026-09-29 ~17:00Z, su-2806a0fc)\n\n**Issue 1 — `psu --connect=app.papercusp.com/ws-3daf37098c8096b5d9e0ac72` → `closed (connector_unavailable)`**\n\nObserved:\n1. psu got a session ticket (DB row `papercusp_auth.hosted_workspace_connectors` for ws-3daf… = active/websocket/gen 16), then the relay broker on the hosted control plane (:3880, `hosted-workspace-session.ts` attachBrowser) found NO live connector socket for that binding and closed 4411 `connector_unavailable`.\n2. The avi-test VM (release 0.0.21-p318r60, `papercusp-workspace.service` up 1d7h) holds exactly one TCP connection to Cloudflare (104.21.73.140:443): ESTABLISHED, handshake-sized traffic only (3.2 KB out / 3.8 KB in), silent in BOTH directions for ~1h50m (since ~15:16Z). The tower's :3880 has no matching origin connection. The VM thinks it is connected; the control plane has no connector. Half-open link.\n3. Nothing can notice it: no WebSocket ping/pong on the connector on either side (`hosted-connector-client.ts`, `apps/operator/bin/hosted-handler.ts`), Node TCP keepalive off, the VM egresses via Cloud NAT on default timeouts (20-min idle mapping drop), and Cloudflare drops idle WebSockets after ~100s. The VM client reconnects only on a `close` event it never receives.\n4. The cloud's `reachable` flag (`/api/hosted/cli/workspaces`) and the terminal-ticket gate read only the DB row state. `heartbeat_at` is written once at registration and never again (the WebSocket client never calls `/heartbeat`), so the cloud said \"reachable\" and psu printed \"connected to …\" for a machine with no live link.\n5. psu's failure text says \"Your shell stays alive on the machine … --connect-session=… to resume\" even though the relay refused before any shell was opened. That text is misleading.\n\n[inferred] Which hop dropped the idle connection is not established (Cloudflare edge idle close vs. Cloud NAT mapping expiry). The fix below covers both. The portal's chat to avi-test uses the same connector, so it is down right now too.\n\n**Issue 2 — no place to add a second cloud sign-in**\n\nObserved in `apps/operator/scripts/psu-connection-front-controller.mjs`:\n- The picker offers \"Papercusp cloud — sign in\" ONLY when no cloud sign-in exists (`pickerChoices`: `if (!signedIn)`).\n- A cloud sign-in profile is keyed by portal host alone (`app.papercusp.com`), so a second `--connect-login` to the same portal REPLACES the first profile and revokes its token (`hostedLogin`).\n- A CLI token is bound to one organization (the approver's active org). So a person can hold one account/org per portal at a time. PUI hands every sign-in to psu (`apps/tui/src/remote_connect.rs`), so it has the same gap.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — The relay drops a connector that stops answering pings.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Find out why psu --connect to avi-test closed with connector_unavailable, and get it working.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner:Avi 2026-09-29 (order #928, session claude:9a0d17e2)\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The relay broker terminates a connector socket that misses the pong for its ping.\",\"falsifier\":\"A connector that stops answering pings is still attached after the next ping interval.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run hosted-workspace-session.test.ts. It writes `heartbeat_at` on attach and on pong, and `reachable` plus the terminal-ticket gate require a fresh heartbeat. The workspace-host client (`hosted-connector-client.ts`) pings on its own cadence and replaces a socket that has been silent for about 75s.\n2. **Truthful psu attach errors.** A 4411/4412 before a shell binds means the machine's link is down. psu waits briefly, retries with a fresh ticket, and never offers a resume hint for a shell that never existed.\n3. **Several cloud sign-ins.** A cloud profile's identity is portal + organization + user. The picker always offers another sign-in, and entries carry the organization name the control plane returns.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-005 | live |\n| R-10 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-010 | deployed |\n| R-13 | P-004 | live |\n| R-14 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-008 | tree |\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` Control-plane connector heartbeat + truthful reachability. In the relay broker: WebSocket ping every 30s, terminate a connector (or browser) that misses its pong. The pings keep the Cloudflare and NAT idle timers alive and detect dead sockets. The broker records liveness (`heartbeat_at` on attach, then throttled on pong). `reachable` and the terminal-ticket gate require a fresh heartbeat. Works with the already-deployed r60 hosts because `ws` auto-answers pings. Goes live when `papercusp-hosted-control-plane.service` restarts (it runs from the canonical tree). Tests: `hosted-workspace-session.test.ts`, `routes/hosted-cli/index.test.ts`. — note: ← WI-10003908 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Workspace-host connector watchdog. The VM client sends its own pings, and terminates + reconnects when no inbound frame arrives for ~75s, catching the half-open case from the VM side. Ships with the next workspace-host release cut; NOT live on avi-test until that machine upgrades. Tests: `hosted-connector-client.test.ts`. — note: ← WI-10003911 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` psu attach failures tell the truth. Map 4411/4412 to \"the workspace machine's link to Papercusp cloud is down / reconnecting\". Offer \"resume with --connect-session\" only when a shell actually bound. Retry the attach briefly while the machine reconnects. Tests: `psu-connection-front-controller.test.ts`. — note: ← WI-10003909 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Several cloud sign-ins at once. Connect, list and logout work with several profiles. The control plane returns the organization's display name with the token and the workspace list, so picker entries are labelled. An older host that does not know the kind refuses it (unknown kinds are already rejected), so the client falls back. importance: high — note: Implemented and unit-tested (WI-10003949 checkpoint; test runs 2026-09-30 18:29-18:45Z all green, lint:tsc clean). Live proof on avi-test is P-010.\n- **P-008** `done` psu launcher hosted-customer mode (apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs): under PAPERCUSP_PSU_HOSTED_CUSTOMER=1 refuse every non-allowlisted flag and turn off the identity, fleet and backend-install prompts (defense in depth for D-002 rule 1-2). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010009801 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` psu front controller (apps/operator/scripts/psu-connection-front-controller.mjs): psu --connect to a hosted workspace asks for kind 'psu' with the forwarded argv and types nothing; when the control plane or host refuses the kind, fall back to the interim shell line. Tests for both paths. importance: high — note: Implemented and unit-tested (WI-10003949 checkpoint; test runs 2026-09-30 18:29-18:45Z all green, lint:tsc clean). Live proof on avi-test is P-010.\n- **P-010** `done` Ship and prove: cut a VM release carrying the host change, upgrade avi-test, run psu --connect against it live (claude agent runs as the workspace account; refused flags are refused; exit ends the session), then tell Avi psu works on avi-test and close WI-10003949 and orders #1028/#1034. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004405 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Owner route + scope choices (2026-09-29)\nDate: 2026-09-29\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-29, AskUserQuestion answers] (1) Route: this su session implements all items itself (route A). (2) avi-test: restart/re-enroll its connector NOW (P-005 first), accepting that live shells/agent sessions on that machine end. (3) 'Auth to multiple Papercusp workspaces' means several accounts/organizations on app.papercusp.com at once: one profile per portal+organization+user, an always-present 'Sign in to another Papercusp cloud account or organization' picker entry, organization-labelled entries. Other portals need no extra work beyond what already exists.\n\n### D-002 — psu to a Papercusp cloud workspace is option B: the machine's Papercusp service starts psu in the customer's terminal; agents run as the workspace account\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-30, directive #1069, answering conv-muobiq1g after a side-by-side explanation of A/B/C: \"B\"]. Recorded by su-be77f2f5. Related: WI-10003949, orders #1028/#1034; byoc plan D-417, D-421, D-423, D-424, D-442.\n\nRuling: when psu --connect targets a Papercusp-hosted workspace, the workspace host opens a new relay terminal kind whose only process is psu, started by the host service (uid papercusp). psu runs its agent CLI as the customer workspace account through the D-424 identity wrapper. The customer gets psu's normal screen; there is no `psu` command inside the workspace account's own shell.\n\nSecurity requirements (from the read-only review, WI-10003949 comments 1151388/1151389/1151391):\n1. The host builds psu's argv and env. Customer argv is ALLOWLISTED (not denylisted): agent, model, effort, label, no-picker, and resume/fork limited to the customer's own sessions. Refused: --launch-context, --set-claude-token/--clear-claude-token, --recovery-*, --owner-id, --identity-revision, --launched-by, --session-id, --fleet*, --harness, --workspace, --user.\n2. psu runs non-interactive for identity, fleet and backend install (the install prompt would run a third-party installer as the service user); the customer toolchain is the D-423 root-owned one.\n3. When psu exits, the relay session ends. There is never a service-user shell fallback.\n4. psu's own launcher refuses the same flags in hosted-customer mode (defense in depth).\n5. An older control plane or host without the new kind falls back to the interim shell (WI-10003949 interim fix), never to a service-user process.\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: amend-b1b1bbdd4818cd79ea386434\nRequest-Hash: 4ee485d7f7544539e5bbf454ca42f29700761074dc4a0de019569bb5303e0262\nActor: su-2806a0fc-efc7-4cc8-840c-97d6648d714d\nReason: Option B (D-002) changed what P-010 delivers, so the BARs are brought in line with it. R-2 now also covers the terminal route refusing a stale-heartbeat workspace (409 workspace_not_reachable, no ticket). R-9 is re-scoped to the D-002 outcome: the owner's installed psu gets a psu agent session on avi-test after a long idle, the agent runs as the workspace account, and the session ends with psu. New: R-10 (D-002 argv allowlist), R-11 (psu exit ends the session, no shell fallback), R-12 (the connector watchdog is deployed on avi-test), R-13 (two organizations' sign-ins, live, owner-assisted).\nApproved-By: su-8089ee86-fd4d-47cb-bf26-2066d20368cd\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1153615\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T14:54:38.348Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 39 → 40\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: amend-336a93e18b20d611f7700e70\nRequest-Hash: 65daada14b3a1c2ad41dcaddfc473a58b7a6267bc3bbd3364c3c5d51109785fb\nActor: su-2806a0fc-efc7-4cc8-840c-97d6648d714d\nReason: Spec-quality on rev 4 found compound BAR models (R-9, R-10, R-13) and plan items P-007, P-008 and P-009 with no BAR. R-10 is split: it now covers only the host allowlist (P-006), and the control-plane refusal (R-14, P-007), psu's own hosted-customer refusal (R-15, P-008) and the front controller asking for psu (R-16, P-009) become their own BARs. R-9 and R-13 are restated as one sentence each with the same meaning. R-12's method drops a wrong note: runtime_release read r62b because avi-test was moved back to r62b on 2026-10-01 13:37Z for P-318 acceptance, not because the field is stale.\nApproved-By: su-cf7e4c17-2b6a-493c-ae91-3d35c3159c8a\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1153630\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T15:06:46.417Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 46 → 47\nChanged BARs: R-9, R-10, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-005 — D-002 rule 1: a customer's own sessions are every session on its hosted machine\nDate: 2026-10-01\nClarifies D-002 security requirement 1 (\"resume/fork limited to the customer's own sessions\"). It does not change the owner's choice of B. The scope of that limit is the hosted machine. [self-imposed clarification, su-2806a0fc, from rubric vetting post 1153633 item 1 on conv-mupo5ijv; not an owner ruling]\n\nWhy the machine is the right scope (code at HEAD, read 2026-10-01):\n1. One hosted machine serves exactly one customer workspace. Its operator scopes to the binding's single customerWorkspaceId (packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-workspace-host-runtime.ts, the \"serves exactly one workspace\" block). A host-started psu reaches only that machine's own operator (PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_URL = localOperatorOrigin in hosted-psu-session.ts), so a --resume or --fork id can only find that workspace's sessions.\n2. No agent session on that machine runs as anyone but the customer workspace account. Chat and converse spawns go through the process-wide D-421 transform, and psu sessions, fresh or resumed, go through the PTY host's D-424 identity stage; installHostedCustomerAgentIdentity installs both (hosted-agent-identity.ts). The PTY host refuses rather than run an agent as the service user (apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host-agent-identity.test.ts, 'propagates a staging refusal instead of spawning as the service user'). So there is no service-user agent session to resume, and a resumed session's agent runs as the customer account like any other launch.\n\nConsequence: the D-002 allowlist admits --resume, --resume=<id>, --fork and --fork-session with a plain session id, with no per-session owner check. R-10's method cites this decision. Revisit if a hosted machine ever serves more than one workspace or runs an agent outside the customer account.\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: amend-55bcbb01096b4977d3933eef\nRequest-Hash: c618510e38504ed0f7ae9ba920fa2d3852a86829c7b8509d76b30caa051a73ca\nActor: su-2806a0fc-efc7-4cc8-840c-97d6648d714d\nReason: Answers rubric vetting post 1153633 on conv-mupo5ijv. New R-17 (P-008) grades D-002 rule 2, which had no BAR: psu in hosted-customer mode never prompts for identity, fleet or a backend install, bound to new launcher tests with positive controls. R-10's method cites D-005, which records that D-002 rule 1's 'customer's own sessions' scope is the hosted machine. R-12's method now compares the release build record's bundle sha256 with the installed runtime_release.bundleSha256 and names the record of whatever release avi-test runs (r63 only as an example). R-1, R-3, R-6, R-7 and R-8 now name their tests.\nApproved-By: su-4226499d-90b8-49f5-ab35-e614e7118018\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1153691\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T15:38:36.042Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 70 → 71\nChanged BARs: R-17\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: psu-cloud-acceptance-rev7-apply-20261013-0de3f\nRequest-Hash: e29c2b4dce300423ac40782b701b1ec12c625e74511557225f9b95e64ebb5c3a\nActor: su-0de3fbb4-be3c-4265-af56-dbf896b85b76\nReason: Consult post1178215 found shared falsifiers: R13 overlaps R6/R8 and R9 overlaps R11. Separate live observables while preserving D001/D002, keep complete R12 version/digest/watchdog contract, and require the additive R17 identity positive control before attestation. Its code is pending qualified native edit protocol repair.\nApproved-By: su-fd16708d-6c66-4257-8a4c-b71c61d2b085\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1178333\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T05:44:48.605Z\nRubric revision: 6 → 7\nSubject plan revision: 78 → 79\nChanged BARs: R-9, R-13\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"shared-vector-search-libraries-2026-09-29","title":"Move reusable vector-search machinery into shared libraries: embedding-space safety, coverage gate + benchmark, calibrated near-duplicate check, embedding backfill engine","status":"ready","created":"2026-09-29","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Move reusable vector-search machinery into shared libraries: embedding-space safety, coverage gate + benchmark, calibrated near-duplicate check, embedding backfill engine\nslug: shared-vector-search-libraries-2026-09-29\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-09-29\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-11, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nP-002..P-006 done with committed authority (P-002 WI-10004271 and P-004 WI-10004273 closed 2026-10-01 04:2xZ; every AUTO-BAR/SPEC card audited pass).
