Parity test on a fixture database: same rows embedded, same o… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004276 — For each library touched: README section, BORROWABLE.md regenerated (npm run gen:borrowable), lint:generic-first clean (no papercusp imports inside libs/generic), and a fixture-host test proving each… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004277 — Finish per the plan-completion runbook: acceptance rubric authored after implementation, vetted, per-item code-truth audit, independent grading, implementer verdict, then plans:set-plan-status shippe… <!-- P-008 -->\n## Goal\n\nMove the rest of papercusp's reusable vector-search machinery into shared libraries (@papercusp/search, @papercusp/search-core) so other projects can use it, with papercusp keeping only its configuration and wiring. [owner:Avi 2026-09-29 interactive: asked for vector search functionality that \"should belong in a shared library we can use not just in papercusp but across other projects as well\"; then selected all four candidates below, as a separate follow-up plan.]\n\n## Scope (owner-selected 2026-09-29)\n\n1. **Embedding-space safety**: never compare vectors from different embedding models. Model/space label columns (embedding_mode, embedding_profile), the query-side filter (`proseProfileSql` in `agent-tools/search/sources.ts`), width/profile compatibility (`search/prose-vector-dims.ts`), and the stored-row self-check (`search/embed-space-self-check.ts`).\n2. **Coverage gate + benchmark**: `search/coverage-gate.ts` (search tells callers when the vector index is near-empty) into @papercusp/search; the D-016 retrieval benchmark (`memory/bench/turn-truncation-width-cli.ts`) into @papercusp/search-core, which already has `recallAtK` / `evaluateRelevance`.\n3. **Calibrated near-duplicate check**: the corpus-relative cut (95th percentile over 256 random background pairs) exists only in `agent-tools/plans/semantic-dedup.ts`; the work-item guard (`work_items/semantic-dupe-guard.ts`) uses separate logic.\n4. **Embedding backfill engine**: `search/embed-backfill.ts` (1,950 lines), coupled today to papercusp's embed admission, sidecar embedder and resource profile.\n\nNot in scope: the embedder cascade and the sidecar process (desktop-specific). Chunking itself is generic-rag-chunking-2026-09-29 (D-010 there puts it in @papercusp/search).\n\n## Relationships\n- generic-rag-chunking-2026-09-29: its P-001 and this plan's P-003 generalize the SAME benchmark instrument. Build it once, in @papercusp/search-core, whichever item starts first; the other reuses it. Its P-006 (chunk-aware leg) takes the embedding-space filter as an injected parameter so it doesn't wait on this plan's P-001.\n- search-unify-hybrid-engine-2026-07-20 and WI-10609 (moving work items, docs and the plans duplicate check onto runHybridSearch) touch the same files; check their state before P-004.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Embedding-space safety\n\n- **P-001** `done` Move embedding-space safety into @papercusp/search behind a configure seam where the host supplies its accepted models and vector width: the label-column convention (embedding_mode, embedding_profile), the query-side space filter builder (proseProfileSql, agent-tools/search/sources.ts), storage compatibility checks (prose-vector-dims.ts: validateProseStorageCompatibility and the resolve*ProfileSelection functions), and the stored-row self-check (embed-space-self-check.ts) with the embedder injected. Papercusp keeps its constants (PROSE_VECTOR_DIMS=768, PROSE_ELIGIBLE_MODES). All existing callers switch to the library; parity tests on current behavior first. — note: ← WI-10004270 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Coverage gate and benchmark\n\n- **P-002** `done` Coverage gate into @papercusp/search: search/coverage-gate.ts plus the embed-coverage measure it reads, with the host supplying its sources (table, vector column, label column). The hybrid engine can then report a near-empty vector leg to callers instead of answering confidently. — note: ← WI-10004271 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Retrieval benchmark into @papercusp/search-core. Per D-002 the harness already lives there (libs/generic/search-core/src/retrieval-bench.ts, built on recallAtK) and both bench CLIs call it. Remaining: move the width-sweep loop in memory/bench/turn-truncation-width-cli.ts (rank-based MRR and recall@1 of the true parent among distractors, probe-offset control) into search-core as a library function with the embedder and corpus injected, plus a parity test on a deterministic fixture embedder; chunking-bench-cli.ts keeps its path and flags. — note: ← WI-10004272 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Near-duplicate check\n\n- **P-004** `done` Calibrated near-duplicate check into @papercusp/search: extract the corpus-relative cut from agent-tools/plans/semantic-dedup.ts (quantile 0.95 over 256 background pairs) as a library function taking candidates, a background sampler and the quantile; move plans:new onto it with a parity test. Then read work_items/semantic-dupe-guard.ts, compare the two approaches on real filings (false merges vs missed duplicates), and record whether the work-item guard adopts the library check. Check WI-10609 first to avoid colliding with its migration of the same files. — note: ← WI-10004273 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Backfill engine\n\n- **P-005** `done` Design the backfill-engine seam before moving code: split search/embed-backfill.ts into a generic sweep (select rows whose vector is missing or in the wrong embedding space; batch-embed with per-row fallback on batch failure; cap oversized input; write vector plus label; round-robin across targets within a time budget) and papercusp hooks (the TARGETS list, embed admission, the sidecar embedder, resource profile). Record the seam as a decision. — note: ← WI-10004274 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Extract the backfill engine into @papercusp/search per the recorded seam; papercusp's embed-backfill.ts shrinks to its targets and hooks. Parity test on a fixture database: same rows embedded, same order, same per-target stats before and after. Watch the live sweep for one day after landing (embedded counts per target, no new errors). blocked-by: P-001, P-005 — note: ← WI-10004275 done\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Finish\n\n- **P-007** `done` For each library touched: README section, BORROWABLE.md regenerated (npm run gen:borrowable), lint:generic-first clean (no papercusp imports inside libs/generic), and a fixture-host test proving each extracted piece works with no papercusp code. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-006 — note: ← WI-10004276 done\n- **P-008** `todo` Finish per the plan-completion runbook: acceptance rubric authored after implementation, vetted, per-item code-truth audit, independent grading, implementer verdict, then plans:set-plan-status shipped. blocked-by: P-007\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Embedding-space filter output unchanged.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Move embedding-space safety into a shared library without changing which rows papercusp search can match.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:292f5b71-e70c-4185-8c3e-1554fd184e72:32\",\"session_turn:claude:292f5b71-e70c-4185-8c3e-1554fd184e72:34\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For every pinned case, covering each search source's mode and profile inputs, the library's embedding-space filter configured with papercusp's accepted models and vector width yields the SQL predicate and bind values of every pre-move papercusp embedding-space filter for that source.\",\"falsifier\":\"A pinned case yields a predicate or bind value that differs from its pin, or a pre-move papercusp embedding-space filter or a search source has no pinned case.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run packages/operator-core/lib/search/embedding-space-parity.test.ts. The generic sweep owns selection, embedding, the input cap, writes and the round-robin; papercusp supplies targets, embedder, admission, resource profile and storage width\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #970]. su-e8708a1c, P-005 (WI-10004274). P-006 implements it. Source: packages/operator-core/lib/search/embed-backfill.ts (backfillTable, runBackfillSweep, inspectBackfillTarget).\n\nGENERIC SWEEP. New module libs/generic/search/src/backfill/. It imports nothing from papercusp.\n1. Target shape. BackfillTarget and BackfillStats move unchanged.\n2. Select rows whose vector is missing or in the wrong embedding space. These move: stalePredicateSql, eligiblePredicateSql, activeRecipeVersion, BASELINE_RECIPE_VERSION, and the SELECT. The SELECT keeps its shape: stale AND eligible, the target's ORDER BY, LIMIT batchSize, OFFSET failedSoFar. recentPredicateSql and settledPredicateSql move too (P-002's coverage gate reads them). Label-column names (<embedCol>_mode, _profile, _recipe) come from P-001's convention, so P-006 stays blocked-by P-001.\n3. Batch-embed with per-row fallback on batch failure. Moves unchanged. The batch is sent in chunks of 16 (config batchChunkSize). The first failing or short chunk stops batching for that batch. Rows without a batch vector take the per-row path. Per-row timeout is config rowTimeoutMs (90000); the batch timeout is a host hook, batchTimeoutMs(n).\n4. Cap oversized input. The engine takes config maxInputChars and truncates each body to that many characters before it embeds. Every TARGETS bodySql already caps free text with left(..., 2000) (EI-12967's test) and papercusp sets maxInputChars to the embedder's per-text limit, so parity holds; a host target without a left() cap can no longer retry an oversized row forever. The left() caps stay in bodySql as part of each target's text recipe.\n5. Write vector plus label. The UPDATE moves unchanged. It is keyed on keyCols and guarded by the same stale predicate. It sets the vector and, when the columns exist, _mode, _profile and _recipe. The host supplies the label values.\n6. Round-robin across targets within a time budget. runBackfillSweep's loop moves: rotate by sweepCounter mod target count, skip targets that are absent or width-skewed, give each live target one batch per round, and mark a target drained when a call embeds 0 rows or it reaches maxRowsPerTarget. The loop ends at the budget (config budgetMs, papercusp 200000). The single-flight latch and its stale takeover (latchStaleMs, 1 h) live on a sweeper instance, createBackfillSweeper(...) -> run(opts), lastResult(), resetForTest(), which papercusp pins with pinModuleState; the library holds no module state.\n7. Infrastructure checks. These move: the pgvector-extension check, target inspection (column presence and live typmod) and the embedder-resolution deadline (config resolveTimeoutMs, 60000). The width verdict is a host hook.\n8. Logging: an injected logger (default console) keeps today's [embed-backfill] lines; width-skew errors take a host hint.\n\nPAPERCUSP HOOKS. These stay in embed-backfill.ts, which shrinks to targets and hooks.\n9. The TARGETS list and chunkStoreBackfillTarget (built from the CHUNK_STORES registry), passed to the sweeper as a getter.\n10. Embed admission and the embedders: resolveBackfillEmbedder, the admission-governed OpenAI embedder (daily cap, 429 penalties), the sidecar embedders and resolveBatchEmbed. The hook is resolveEmbedder() -> { mode, dims, profile?, embed, embedMany? } or disabled.\n11. The resource profile: batchSize = getResourceProfile().embedBatchSize, the per-sweep row cap, and the sidecar batch timeout (sidecarBatchTimeoutMs).\n12. Storage compatibility: PROSE_VECTOR_DIMS = 768, fitsProseColumns, computeProseColumnWidthSkew and resolveProseProfileSelection. P-001 moves their generic halves into @papercusp/search. The sweeper receives them as acceptsWidth(dims), widthSkew(...) and resolveProfileSelection(mode, profile).\n13. The SQL client: getOrgPg().sql, passed as getSql().\n14. Everything around the sweep: runEmbedBackfillOnce (doc-sections sync, chunk tick, memory_vec refill), battery policy, _runSweepLogged, the DBOS workflow.\n\nCALLERS. runBackfillSweep keeps its name and signature in papercusp as a delegate to the pinned sweeper, so its callers do not change. backfillTable moves to the library with an options object replacing the positional mode, spaceAware, embedMany and opts arguments. Its callers move in P-006; no positional alias.\n\nPARITY CONTRACT (R-9). P-006 must preserve these exactly: the SELECT, the chunk size and the break on the first failure, the per-row fallback, the guarded UPDATE, the rotation, the drain rules and the stats. P-005 commits the pre-move golden. packages/operator-core/lib/search/embed-backfill-parity.integration.test.ts runs one runBackfillSweep on a fresh PostgreSQL. It seeds three targets with missing and wrong-space vectors and pins each embedded body in embed order plus per-target stats. P-006 keeps it green unchanged and adds a direct run through the library sweeper with papercusp's TARGETS and hooks.\n\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-006, D-002\n\n### D-005 — R-8: semantic-dupe-guard does NOT adopt the library near-duplicate check; it keeps its fixed threshold and title co-signal. The library check is adopted by plans:new only (R-7)\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDate: 2026-09-30 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #970]. su-e8708a1c, P-004 (WI-10004273).\n\nCOMPARISON (committed): docs/evidence/shared-vector-search-libraries-2026-09-29/p004-dupe-guard-comparison.json, written 2026-09-30T17:30Z by packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/near-duplicate-guard-compare-cli.ts. It runs the REAL guard decision (findSemanticDupes, blob db2c994a) and the REAL library check (checkNearDuplicates, libs/generic/search/src/near-duplicate.ts blob dba89366) through the comparison module (blob 1433daf1; unit tests near-duplicate-guard-compare.test.ts, run 20287058 6/6). Population: 864 labelled historical pairs over 493 real work-item filings (0 skipped); each filing's candidate pool is the corpus that was open when it was filed (pool size min 32,539, median 79,015, max 122,871).\n\nRESULTS (133 real duplicates, 581 distinct pairs; the remaining 150 labelled pairs are related/remedy-keep and are counted in the file, not here):\n| approach | missed duplicates | false merges |\n| current guard (fixed cosine threshold + title co-signal) | 64/133 | 32/581 |\n| library calibrated cut alone (quantile 0.95; cut p05 0.652, p50 0.736, p95 0.805) | 25/133 | 251/581 |\n| hybrid: library cut inside the guard's co-signal | 62/133 | 33/581 |\n\nDECISION. The guard keeps its current check. The library cut alone finds 39 more duplicates but falsely merges 219 more distinct filings (43% of distinct pairs vs 5.5%); a false merge refuses a legitimate filing, which is worse than a missed duplicate for a create-time guard. The hybrid is within noise of the current guard (2 fewer misses, 1 more false merge) and would add a background calibration sample to every create call for no measured gain. So there is nothing to adopt. plans:new still adopts the library check (R-7), where both the corpus and the error trade-off differ.\n\nCAVEATS (recorded in the file): labels are the admission promoter's model adjudications (dedup_adjudications), not human judgments, and that population was pre-selected by cosine >= 0.85, a shared title key or a shared condition key, so it over-represents high-cosine pairs for all three approaches. Vectors are today's stored vectors (title + first 2000 body chars), not the create-time title+summary embedding. Applies D-018 rule 3.\n\nMeasured:\n- 2026-10-06T05:05Z: the D-018 bound (2026-10-06T05:00Z) has passed and portable-identity-packages-2026-09-26 has not shipped (awaiting-acceptance).\n- WI-10004265 and WI-10003305 (the portable-identity carry items) are open with assignee null (read 05:05Z), so rule 3's \"coordinate with the portable-identity holder\" has no counterparty and nobody can decline.\n- 04:01-04:10Z: 20 live portable-identity bindings (9 specs) cite packages/operator-core/lib/capability-class-registry-store.ts. 5 of those specs already fail freshness (AUTO-BAR-R-3-P-014, R-7-P-015, R-8-P-017, PORTABLE-P-016, PORTABLE-P-020). 4 currently pass and will go stale when the file changes: AUTO-BAR-R-2-P-021, AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-013, AUTO-BAR-R-6-P-018, PORTABLE-P-012.\n\nRuling:\n1. The messages keep their text except that the index message drops the index name (no test asserts it).\n2. P-008/R-11 is untouched (D-020 governs it).\nRelated: P-001, D-007, D-008, D-018\n\n### D-022 — P-008 R-11: window 2 is VALID and FAILED — session_turns and session_turn_chunks missed the progress rule; the bottleneck is the sweep's sequential non-HOT row writes, not the embedder; fix the write path, then window 3\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed under AUTO; owner directive #1413] su-ea145858, ~15:40Z. Window 2 per D-020.\n\n1. [measured] Snapshots: T0 2026-10-05T15:07:01.108Z (sha256 029e38f3...), Tcut 2026-10-06T14:57:07.754Z (6ee22b59...), T1 2026-10-06T15:07:07.882Z (0222b0d8...), all in .papercusp/scratch/rag-carry/r11-p008-w2-{t0,tcut,t1}-*.json.gz. `npx tsx scripts/r11-window-snapshot.mts evaluate <T0> <Tcut> <T1>` -> verdict 'failed', reason 'At least one retained cohort missed its progress rule' (r11-p008-w2-evaluate.json). Clause 1 holds on every target (session_turns T0 stale 22 -> 22 embedded; work_items 2 -> 2). Clause 2 fails on two targets: session_turns 36,211 of 61,487 in-window rows embedded at T1 (25,276 still stale); session_turn_chunks 29,882 of 33,243 (3,361 stale). The other 12 targets embedded every retained in-window row.\n\n2. [measured] Not void (D-015): all three capture units active, NRestarts 0, and each matches journald exactly over [T0, T1) (r11-w2-parity-window.mjs, a streaming port of r11-w2-parity.mjs, because the unfiltered capture outgrew readFileSync): filtered bg 1,455/1,455, unfiltered bg 903,931/903,931, sidecar 281/281. The host system journal has 0 'Suppressed ... user@1000' notices in the window. bg-host had 28 invocations in the window; D-015 says an engine-serving restart does not void. Receipts: r11-p008-w2-t1-checks.out, r11-p008-w2-t1-hashes.txt. Not yet run: the rev5 error-format/rate parse. It cannot turn this window healthy.\n\n3. [measured] Where the miss is: every in-window session_turns row from before 2026-10-06T04:00Z was embedded. From 04:00Z, 40-75% of each hour's rows were still stale at T1. From ~01:30Z most drains ended 'budget expired with work remaining' (e.g. '1 round(s) in 223s (budget 200s) · drained 1/14 target(s)'), and about a quarter to a third of the 5-minute ticks were shed or skipped (loop-shed, latch held). The sweep never stopped; it fell behind.\n\n4. [measured] The bottleneck is the write, not the embedder. The embed sidecar (CPUWeight 1500, 8-core quota, concurrency 6) averaged 22% of one core over its 5h43m uptime. pg_stat_statements: the sweep's per-row `UPDATE harness_shared.session_turns SET text_embedding ...` ran 82,170 times at mean 291.7 ms, max 62.4 s (23,969 s total); the session_turn_chunks UPDATE averages 64.3 ms; the session_turns stale-row SELECT averages 873 ms. session_turns (1.43M rows, 1.48 GB heap) carries 12 indexes, including a 5.5 GB HNSW on text_embedding, a 1.5 GB trigram GIN on lower(text) and a 684 MB tsv GIN, plus trigger session_turn_windows_sync_trg; only 686 of 111,735 updates were HOT. Every embedding write is non-HOT, so it re-inserts the row into all 12 indexes, re-trigramming the whole turn text. gin_pending_list_limit is 4MB, so some writers also pay a pending-list flush (the 62 s max is most likely that). libs/generic/search/src/backfill/backfill-table.ts (lines ~219-238) issues these writes one at a time, so session_turns throughput is capped near 3 rows/s before any other target gets time.\n\n5. [inferred] The same write path existed before the move (the library kept the per-row guarded UPDATE), so the move did not create this. R-11's pre-registered rule still counts it, and D-010 forbids a silent falsifier change. R-11 is therefore not met, and the rubric is not amended.\n\n6. Next (in order): (a) fix the write throughput in the library sweep (bounded-concurrency guarded writes; then measure and, if needed, a larger GIN pending list) under work item WI-10006735, with tests and a before/after measurement; (b) run window 3 per D-015/D-020: fresh capture units, passing preflight, T0, Tcut/T1 timers, T0 receipt on WI-10004277. No T0 is chosen on outcome. (c) Window-2 capture units are stopped now that T1 is taken; their files stay as evidence.\n\nCorrection (same turn): the first version of this decision cited the work item as 'WI-10006682 [filed this turn]' before it was filed. That id was a placeholder and never existed; the filed item is WI-10006735.\nRelated: P-008, D-010, D-015, D-017, D-020\n\n### D-023 — Correction to D-022: the sweep's session_turns writes are slow because they wait on row locks held by bulk UPDATEs, not because each write is expensive; the fix is a non-blocking guarded write, not write concurrency\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed under AUTO; owner directive #1413] su-ea145858, ~16:05Z. Corrects D-022's mechanism (D-022's window-2 verdict, VALID and FAILED, stands).\n\nRETRACTED from D-022: 'the bottleneck is the sweep's sequential non-HOT row writes' read as 'each write costs ~292 ms'. The 292 ms was a pg_stat_statements MEAN, and it is dominated by waits.\n\nMeasured:\n1. Probe .papercusp/scratch/rag-ea145/wi10006735-write-probe.mts (papercusp's own sweeper config, session_turns only; guarded UPDATEs deferred via a SQL proxy, then replayed against the live pool). 6 batches x 128 newest stale rows, 15:53:56-15:54:14Z, load 71-75. Per-write latency p50 9-12 ms, p90 24-65 ms in every batch. Batches with no lock waits: 66 and 46 rows/s at concurrency 1, 341/94/82 rows/s at 4/8/8. Batch 0 (concurrency 1): 6 of 128 writes hit the pool's 15 s lock_timeout ('canceling statement due to lock timeout'), so 99 s wall and 1.23 rows/s. Embedding 128 rows took 1.3-2.4 s per batch. Output: .papercusp/scratch/rag-ea145/wi10006735-write-probe.out.\n2. pg_stat_statements (cumulative): sweep UPDATE 88,937 calls, mean 271.7 ms, max 62.4 s, total 24,167 s. At ~10 ms of real work per row that is ~900 s of work and ~23,000 s of waiting. Bulk writers on the same rows: turn-origin reclassify UPDATE (session-ingest.ts ~2096) 13 calls, 65,000 rows (5,000 per statement), mean 47.8 s, max 183.5 s; owner backfill UPDATE (~1852) 3,258 calls, mean 369 ms, max 165.6 s; chunked_at UPDATE mean 71.7 ms, max 32.8 s; retention DELETE mean 9.8 s.\n\n[inferred, being checked] The writes wait on row locks held by these multi-second bulk statements. A 15-minute 1 s sampler of blocked session_turns writes and their blockers is running (task 0muwv7uo2w0kf5e3g07, output .papercusp/scratch/rag-ea145/wi10006735-lock-sampler.out, until 16:17Z).\n\nDecision:\n1. WI-10006735's fix is a guarded write that does not wait on a row lock (skip rows another writer holds: they stay stale, are counted, and offset the next SELECT like a failure), in libs/generic/search/src/backfill/backfill-table.ts, with tests there. Bounded write concurrency is not needed: serial writes at ~10 ms already exceed peak ingest, and the embedder (~60 rows/s) is the next ceiling.\n2. The 5,000-row reclassify statement is a separate defect (it stalls every session_turns writer for up to 3 minutes) and is filed separately.\n3. Editing backfill-table.ts stales 17 live bindings on 7 specs of this plan (R-9-P-006, R-10-P-006, R-11-P-008 test row, R-12-P-007, R-14-P-006, SPEC-P-005-SEAM-DECISION, SPEC-P-006-SWEEP-THROUGH-LIBRARY). They are re-measured after the fix lands, before window 3's evaluation.\n4. R-11 window 3 (D-015/D-020 protocol) starts at the first T0 after the fix is deployed to bg-host.\n\n### D-024 — P-008 R-11: window 3 started at T0 2026-10-06T18:05:00.165Z with the write-path fixes loaded; Tcut 2026-10-07T17:55Z, T1 2026-10-07T18:05Z\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed under AUTO; owner directive #1413] su-ea145858, ~18:08Z. Follows D-022 (window 2 valid and failed) and D-023 (mechanism: sweep session_turns writes waited on row locks held by bulk UPDATEs).\n\nPrerequisites, all loaded before T0 (measured):\n- Sweep write path made non-blocking (SKIP LOCKED guarded write), WI-10006735.\n- session_turns bulk writers fixed: WI-10006752 (reclassify batch) and WI-10006788 (catalogue-bump non-HOT rewrite; migration 1405 applied 17:40:41Z). Both closed with committed authority.\n- bg-host (papercusp-bg-host.service) MainPID 338825, InvocationID 2e98c3ccb6c74dcdbe966e8f9e85f145, started 17:36:41Z, NRestarts 0; :3271 health sha fa130511d7; dist-host/hono-host.mjs sha256 0f738f11...ceafa2 carries the libs/generic/search backfill engine markers.\n- After-fix backlog: session_turns stale 16,135 (17:53:41Z) -> 15,824 (17:58:37Z), a net drain of about 60/min.\n\nWindow 3 (frozen at T0, same procedure and committed baselines as window 2):\n- T0 snapshot r11-p008-w3-t0-20261006.json.gz, capturedAt 2026-10-06T18:05:00.165Z, sha256 c948dd7f4be2080f85119c9624426460171590df6ce46d596d3423b6d30b348b. Non-empty T0 stale cohorts: harness_escalations 6, operator_turns 2, session_turns 15,371, work_items 12.\n- Tcut 2026-10-07T17:55:00Z (timer r11-p008-tcut-1791309900), T1 2026-10-07T18:05:00Z (timer r11-p008-t1-1791309900); both active.\n- Capture units r11-p008-w3-{bg-capture,bg-all-capture,sidecar-capture-anchored}-20261006 active since 18:01:03Z, NRestarts 0; cursor parity 6/6, 858/858, 1/1 at 18:07Z.\n- Baselines unchanged: r11-bg-host-embed-backfill-journal.txt 7d408b8e..., r11-baseline-embed-sidecar-journal.txt 80b0165a..., r11-window-analysis.json f3173c8d... (last commit bc4829289a).\n- Full T0 receipt: WI-10004277 thread post 1160377.\n\nRule: evaluate only at or after T1 with `scripts/r11-window-snapshot.mts evaluate T0 Tcut T1`, then bind the verdict truthfully. Window history: window 1 void (D-020), window 2 valid and failed (D-022). No outcome-based change to the window is allowed after this record.\n\n### D-025 — R-11 window 3 is incomplete; preserve frozen evidence and preflight a replacement\nDate: 2026-10-09\n[self-imposed under AUTO #1413] Measured 2026-10-09T20:13Z by reading D-024 and .papercusp/scratch/rag-carry/r11-p008-w3-service-evidence-20261009.json, archive and retirement receipts. Server WI receipt records exactT0 and all runtime/capture/baseline details beforeT1.\nRelated: P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"ship-verification-plans-and-measure-2026-09-29","title":"Ship the remaining review/verification-improvement plans, then measure them against target numbers","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-29","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Ship the remaining review/verification-improvement plans, then measure them against target numbers\nslug: ship-verification-plans-and-measure-2026-09-29\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-29\nupdated: 2026-10-16\n---\n\n## Goal\nOwner directive #907 [owner:Avi 2026-09-29, interactive]: \"1. get the remaining plans shipped and make sure none of the remaining items were supersceded. 2. After that Let's take the measurements, and just not compre to previous because we don'y have those numbers, we can still compare to what we think in ideal realistically acheivable number is, so let's do that.\"\n\n## Product shaping\n- Audience: Avi, reviewing whether the existing verification improvements shipped and achieved realistic operating targets.\n- Problem: six named plans have incomplete acceptance or measurement state, while the before-baseline is unavailable.\n- Outcome: check supersession against actual implementation; ship each still-applicable plan through its normal independent acceptance gate; then publish existing-ledger measurements against the approved M-1..M-8 table.\n- Non-goals: new product features, generic backlog work, a new monitoring program, SQL shipping, bypassed acceptance, or reconstructed before-baselines.\n- Source turns: session_turn:claude:7701176b-bbfd-4c1b-a78f-393268d16046:9, :10 and :11; D-001/D-002 preserve the approved route, targets and sequence. The 2026-10-15 kickoff renews execution authority only.\n- Scenarios: a dropped item names a replacement, so verify that replacement in source/tests before disposition; a plan already shipped, so verify its canonical evidence rather than rebuild it; Next repair: Retry the acceptance-rubric read, or re-route to a process that can see it — the subject PINS a rubric this read could not resolve, so its absence here is UNMEASURED, not established. Do NOT amend or re-seed the rubric on this evidence: as far as this read knows it is intact, and amending it would destroy any in-flight grading card.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nINTERIM COST MODEL (2026-10-02, infra only, no LLM tokens; all measured on real GCP VMs). Target (#1064/#1068): 20 -> ~2 USD per assigned agent-month. An assigned agent is active 43% of the time (D-017); idle agents are parked with no process (D-018/D-025). NORMAL agent work (replayed Claude+Codex) MEETS the target on spot: e2-custom-16-32768 2.81 USD per active agent-month = 1.21 per assigned (D-020); c4a-highcpu-16 ARM 2.56 = 1.10 (D-027, cheapest, CPU-bound at ~83 active); c4a-standard-16 2.86 (D-024); t2d 3.95 dropped. Plus the per-workspace Server, 6-9 USD/month (D-022, ~0.15 per agent at 50 agents) => ~1.3-1.4 USD per assigned agent-month, ~14x below 20. On-demand ~2.9 (7x). HEAVY real work (full monorepo typechecks) does NOT yet: 3.3-4.4 per assigned agent-month (D-021/D-023); the cost is the typecheck, not the agent (60% of CPU), so the lever is a shared typecheck/test service. SPOT is viable (D-026): a reclaim costs 3-4 min host downtime and only the in-flight turn, and the drill is now scripts/agent-capacity/vm/reclaim-drill.sh. But hosted workspace hosts are on-demand-only with no reclaim recovery (WI-10005210), so the spot numbers are lab-only until that ships.\n\n**Next:** 1) WI-10005210: spot scheduling option + start-on-TERMINATED + per-session --resume in packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/gcp-provider.ts (makes the spot rows reachable). 2) WI-10005184: pc-heavy memory-capped heavy-job admission by default on agent hosts. 3) Shared typecheck/test service design (heavy-work lever, D-021). Waiting: S1 p2p cold join / WI-10005107 / WI-10004786 on su-3ee17's D-120 soak; WI-10005070 / WI-10004885 on the 0.0.28-alpha cut.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10004370 — Test-project safety rails: labels, teardown-sweep registration, project budget alert, verified deletion after every run. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004371 — Workload corpus: two representative open-source repos plus an everyday task set; measure commit-to-convergence delay. <!-- P-527 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004395 — S7 [D-008]: the p2p daemon's own CPU and RAM per cloud peer, folded into the capacity numbers (free anytime; private-VM bring-up with the as-cut .deb allowed, never shared). <!-- P-528 -->\n## Why\n- [owner:Avi 2026-09-30 #1062] \"a user only running 1 agent at a time will have very different requirements from someone running 50+\"; users must be told how many Claude/Codex agents a machine supports.\n- [owner:Avi 2026-09-30 #1063] \"lets not guess, lets test with real gcp instances\".\n- [owner:Avi 2026-09-30 #1064] \"$1000 a month for 50 agents is too expensive we need to figure out away ro reduce that by 10x\".\n- The earlier size guide (~1.5 working agents per CPU core; X-Large 32 CPU/128 GB for ~50 agents at ~$1,249/month) was an ESTIMATE from our own dev box, which also runs our full test suite, so it likely overstates a typical user [inferred]. Google's list price for that machine is ~$790/month, so a 10x cut cannot come from margin; it must come from cost.\n\n## Target\n- A hosted setup where 50 agents under a defined everyday workload cost the customer roughly $100-125/month, i.e. Google cost at or below ~$60-80/month [inferred from #1064; confirm with owner].\n- Machine capacity = most agents it runs while (a) agents' commands take at most 1.3x as long as with one agent, (b) nothing is killed for lack of memory, (c) Papercusp's API stays under 500 ms p95 [proposed thresholds].\n\n## Product shaping\n\n### Audience, problem, and outcome\n\nAvi is building Papercusp-hosted AI-agent workspaces for trial and paying customers. A customer returning after inactivity needs their own repositories, database, artifacts, credentials, and resumable agent sessions, not merely a running machine. Keeping a large VM running for every idle customer wastes compute, while treating customer disks as disposable loses data.\n\nThe outcome is an ordinary-cloud-VM pool with durable customer identity and storage, automatic wake/placement, bounded spending, and a traceable cost/pricing model. Compute may stop or be replaced; the customer workspace and its retained storage do not. The customer sees one workspace and a clear starting/ready/failed state.\n\n### Source turns and authorization\n\nOwner sources include the prior request about reconnecting idle customers to their unique data (session_turn:codex:01a13e49-263d-74e2-8148-661e5fe915ef:95), the real-VM correction (current continuation owner turns), the instruction to write the hybrid pool into this plan, and the explicit instruction: “Okay write this all into a detailed plan and then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped status.” D-058 governs the working pricing shape; D-061/D-062 distinguish the existing cluster from a fresh trial; D-063 governs measured capacity inputs; D-064 removes microVMs from the baseline.\n\nThe latest instruction authorizes this session to detail, implement, test, and ship the extension under AUTO. Earlier “shaping only / await approval” wording is superseded for this owner-directed scope. It does not authorize arbitrary customer price activation, unrelated platform changes, or bypassing release/security controls.\n\n### Scenarios and walkthrough\n\n1. New trial: the existing hosted signup/provisioning door creates a customer identity and encrypted durable data allocation, selects an eligible ordinary VM, initializes the tenant, and returns ready only after tenant identity, storage, and connector readiness agree.\n2. Idle return: activity stops; the controller checkpoints agent state, flushes database/filesystem writes, drains the runtime, and stops compute. Retained data continues to incur storage cost. On return, concurrent wake requests converge on one durable operation; the original VM is preferred where viable, otherwise a compatible same-provider/same-zone replacement reattaches the same tenant volume.\n3. Saturated pool: no safe VM is available. The request queues visibly; a budget- and quota-admitted ordinary VM is provisioned through the existing provider workflow. No customer is placed onto a draining, stale, incompatible, already-owned, or unauthenticated host.\n4. Host loss: the controller fences the old host and proves exclusive storage ownership before the replacement writes. It restores checkpoints and reconnects only after the expected tenant data marker and runtime readiness pass. Ambiguous detach or provider outcomes remain pending rather than risking two database writers.\n5. Paid use: the same mechanism uses explicit paid entitlements/reservations. Upgrading changes policy, not workspace identity or disk contents.\n6. Cloud comparison: GCP and AWS use their existing adapters. Provider and zone constraints follow the data volume; a GCP disk is never presented as directly attachable to AWS. A cross-cloud move is an explicit copy/restore migration with verification and rollback.\n7. Rollout: internal disposable canaries prove wake, idle, failure, data integrity, isolation, cleanup, and cost accounting before an external trial is enrolled. “Shipped” requires the exact deployed artifact and a passing current runtime journey, not a green unit test alone.\n\n### Non-goals and explicit limits\n\nMicroVMs, nested virtualization, a new cloud SDK layer, a second scheduler, silent migration of existing customers, public price changes, charging customers from experimental estimates, GPU hosting, and automatic cross-cloud live disk moves are out of scope. No trial is advertised as live until its end-to-end release criteria pass. Scaleway is a prospective credits/provider option; this work does not claim a production Scaleway adapter exists.\n\n### Isolation and storage decisions\n\nLaunch the ordinary-VM pool with one active customer tenancy per VM, enforced by durable exclusive assignment and host generation fencing. This reuses the existing dedicated-host security boundary. Sharing a VM kernel between unrelated customer code is a separate security qualification; containers alone are not asserted to prove that qualification. Warm hosts are unassigned and attested clean. A previously assigned host is ineligible for another customer until tenant runtime, disks, credentials, mounts and connector enrollment are removed and the boot environment is reimaged/attested. Default to retirement if clean-state proof is unavailable.\n\nThe customer workspace retains stable data identity. The data binding includes provider/account/project, region/zone, volume identity, encryption policy and host/controller generation. OS/boot disks are replaceable; swap is scratch; the tenant database and working filesystem are durable. Object storage holds backups/artifacts and is not treated as a live PostgreSQL filesystem. Trial database allowance is 256 GiB per D-062; OS 32 GiB and swap 256 GiB remain benchmark/profile inputs, not a mandate to preallocate that scratch capacity for every customer. Existing-cluster 384/512 GiB sizing remains separate.\n\n## Hybrid pool implementation design\n\n### Reuse map\n\nExtend @papercusp/deployment-driver workspace-host domain/types and existing provider registry, not DeploymentDriver's retired ephemeral frame abstraction. Reuse gcp-provider.ts/aws-provider.ts, provisioning-runner.ts, lifecycle-runner.ts, their DBOS workflows and operation idempotency/fencing. Reuse workspace_hosts, workspace_host_resources, customer_workspaces, hosted-lifecycle-store/policy, connector enrollment, resource obligations, and the existing cost model/price evidence. Extend existing persisted metadata/columns only after checking their constraints and tenancy model; any necessary new durable relation needs an explicit reuse justification.\n\n### Placement, reservations, and queueing\n\nThe placement function consumes authenticated customer identity, required VM profile, data affinity, entitlement, fresh host health, active assignments and pending reservations. It first reuses the customer's own healthy compatible host, then a clean unassigned warm host, otherwise returns an explainable queue/provision decision. Stable tie-breaking makes retries deterministic. Resource accounting includes reservations, not only running sessions. A transaction plus the existing controller fence admits one tenant lease per host and one writer for a data volume. The pure selector is not itself a reservation; the caller must atomically re-read and commit before any provider action.\n\nRequired filters: exact tenancy/account boundary, provider and zone compatibility, architecture/runtime/image compatibility, sufficient measured CPU/RAM/storage, healthy non-stale observation, not draining/reclaimed/quarantined, no conflicting assignment/reservation, and proven clean state for a new customer. No unknown health or price observation is promoted to healthy/free.\n\n### Lifecycle and reconnect state machine\n\nReuse existing queued/running/terminal lifecycle operations. The customer-facing journey distinguishes queued, starting, reconnecting, ready and recoverable failure. One idempotency key binds wake requests to customer, host generation, desired revision and durable operation. Wake resumes the existing stopped VM when safe; replacement allocates a new host identity while retaining workspace/data identity. Sequence: lease -> fence old writer -> stop/flush -> verify detach -> attach expected volume -> mount by verified device/UUID -> validate tenant marker -> restore runtime/checkpoints -> enroll tenant connector -> publish ready. Persist each phase through existing operation/resource checkpoints; retry only transient errors, reconcile ambiguous provider actions, and cap recovery attempts. Never mount a wrong/blank disk or use empty initialization to repair an existing customer.\n\n### Policies and autoscaling\n\nTrial and paid entitlements are server-owned, validated policies. Bound concurrent agents, CPU/RAM, durable storage, scratch space, job duration, idle time, allowed provider/region and monthly spend. Defaults come from measured capacity and existing catalog costs, with evidence dates. No caller may increase its own quota through labels or request metadata. Paid reservations have explicit capacity and cost ownership. Admission is fair across eligible customers, with deterministic ordering and aging.\n\nScale out from queued admitted demand and VM-profile fit; maintain an explicitly budgeted warm floor, default zero until a latency/cost canary justifies otherwise. Scale in only clean unassigned hosts or safely drained idle tenancies; active work/viewers and in-flight lifecycle actions hold shutdown. Cooldowns and pending provisioning count toward desired capacity. Spot is opt-in only after reclaim recovery and on-demand fallback pass for that exact workload/profile. No new recurring loop: extend the existing durable lifecycle workflow/routine.\n\n### Costs and pricing\n\nReport infrastructure cost separately from LLM tokens and customer price. Allocate actual compute duration, retained storage, provisioned IOPS/throughput, OS/swap, backups, object storage, network/egress, control-plane Server, and warm/idle capacity. Preserve unallocated overhead explicitly so the sum reconciles to the pool bill; unknown rates are unknown, never zero. Costs use currency, provider, region, measurement time, source and capacity evidence. D-063 achieved concurrency replaces nominal-slot assumptions. Show 1-agent and 50-agent examples, trial and paid, on-demand and qualified spot, with active-duty and pool-utilization sensitivities. Startup credits are a temporary discount, not the steady-state unit economics. The working commercial model is a workspace base fee plus agent fee; metered busy-hours is the comparison. Price activation needs a separately explicit commercial configuration, not automatic selection of a margin or amount.\n\n### Backups, recovery, observability, and rollout\n\nReuse provider snapshots and existing resource/cost/audit ledgers. A snapshot succeeds only after provider confirmation; database-consistent recovery additionally needs PostgreSQL backup/WAL guarantees. Targets for internal canary acceptance: acknowledged live-disk writes survive stop/start and same-zone replacement; an idle wake reaches ready within a measured 120-second target, recorded as a target until observed; backup recovery target RPO <=24h and RTO <=60min must be demonstrated before promised to customers. Keep deletion/retention and backup costs explicit.\n\nEmit bounded control metadata and counters for queue age, placement refusal, lease contention, start/wake time, disk-identity failure, recovery, stranded resources and allocated cost. Prompts, source, database contents and secrets stay in the tenant data plane. Reuse existing metrics/audit surfaces; high-frequency operational series do not go to PostHog. Unknown readiness blocks customer enrollment.\n\nRoll out in sequence: pure contract tests -> real isolated-DB concurrency/RLS tests -> provider adapter tests -> current-build disposable real-VM drill -> internal customer canary -> exact green artifact promotion/deploy -> final live journey and rollback proof. Keep the old dedicated-host route as rollback; never roll back tenant data by resetting compute.\n\n### Verification and shipment evidence\n\nEach implementation item must cite project-native tests, its changed source, and current-build acceptance. Required adversarial cases include duplicate wakes, reservation races, cross-tenant/cross-zone disks, stale health/fences, active viewers, saturated budget, provider timeout after success, failed detach, lost host, missing backup, reimage failure and cleanup after partial provisioning. Test fakes validate policy and replay; they cannot substitute for real provider drill evidence.\n\nFinal shipment evidence must name the exact commit/artifact, installed runtime identity, exercised customer journey, data marker/hash before and after replacement, isolation assertions, cost reconciliation and provider-confirmed canary teardown. A held live release gate has one driver; this lane continues independent implementation and asks that driver once for the final promotion evidence if needed. Do not mark this extension or the overall historical benchmark plan shipped merely because its shaping text exists.\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\nThis section records the maintained surfaces Cover replay, concurrent admission, stale observations/quotes, zero-controller placeholders, pending/retained resource accounting, refusal fairness, active work/viewer holds and failed-provider residue. Default warm floor is zero. Pooled GCP/AWS signup quotes, admits and enqueues on-demand consistently until profile-bound reclaim recovery is qualified; direct unqualified spot and existing spot inventory refuse. Replay at scale through a fake model server returning the recorded replies with the recorded delays, so real claude/codex CLIs and real tool commands run on the VM without spending AI-account quota. Check replay against a small real-agent run first.\n- Measure per run: CPU, memory, memory-pressure stalls, out-of-memory kills, disk IO, per-command slowdown vs 1 agent, Papercusp API latency, cost per hour.\n- Safety: every VM labeled and registered for the teardown sweep (leak history WI-10002413, WI-10002906), budget alert on the project, verified deletion after each run.\n\n## Cost levers to measure (none assumed)\n1. True per-agent footprint by workload profile.\n2. Fix Codex idle CPU spin (EI-21417256075155406; ~0.27 core per idle Codex session measured 2026-09-30) and re-measure.\n3. Spot VMs (reclaimable with ~30 s notice, much cheaper than on-demand) plus automatic agent resume after a reclaim.\n4. Machine families: e2 vs t2d (AMD) vs ARM (t2a/c4a).\n5. More agents per GB: zram memory compression, freezing idle agents.\n6. Leaner stack: desktop off when nobody is looking; trim the 3.4 GB Papercusp baseline.\n7. Shared hosts: several customers' agents on one bigger machine with strong isolation (gVisor/Firecracker): feasibility, density, security outline.\n8. Committed-use discounts on the pool (pricing math only).\n\n## Design\n\nThree pieces, all kept in the repo so the benchmark can be re-run: (1) a test-project safety layer (labels, budget alert, teardown sweep); (2) a load driver that launches N real Claude/Codex CLIs on a GCP VM, either doing real Papercusp backlog work (live run, changes landed on hand-merged branches per D-005) or replaying recorded sessions through a fake model server (size ramps); (3) a metrics collector (CPU, memory, pressure stalls, out-of-memory kills, per-command slowdown) whose run records feed the capacity table and the cost model.\n\nThe hybrid-pool baseline is a fleet of ordinary, real cloud VMs, not microVMs. A provider-neutral scheduler places tenant workloads on general-purpose, memory-optimized, or CPU-optimized VMs; drains and replaces hosts without losing durable tenant state; and scales a warm pool from queue and utilization signals. Tenant isolation is enforced with tenant-scoped processes or containers, OS permissions, network policy, IAM boundaries, and resource quotas. MicroVMs remain an optional future isolation tier only if measured threat-model or noisy-neighbor requirements justify the added complexity. The su builds the load driver and runs the baseline; whether to hand the lever experiments to a fleet is decided after the baseline.\n\n### D-002 — GCP spend cap: $200 across all test runs\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-30, AskUserQuestion answer] \"Up to $200 (Recommended)\". Enforce with a project budget alert and per-run teardown verification; ask the owner before exceeding it.\n\n### D-003 — Target: 10x is about the CUSTOMER price\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-30, AskUserQuestion answer] \"Customer price (Recommended)\": 50 agents should cost the customer about $100-125/month, so Google cost for them must be about $60-80/month or less. P-012 grades every lever combination against this.\n\n### D-004 — Workload: real Papercusp work landing through p2p git, plus replay for the size ramps\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-30, AskUserQuestion answers] asked \"Can we have them do real papercusp work?\" then, offered live+replay, \"We have a p2p git system that should be almost ready, can we use that?\". Ruling: (1) a group of our own agents does real backlog items on a test machine and lands changes through the p2p git system; this also calibrates the replay; (2) the 1-to-64-agent ramps replay recorded Papercusp sessions (worst-case heavy profile) plus a typical customer repo (normal profile). [self-imposed] If p2p git is not ready when P-017 runs, those agents work on branches the su merges, so capacity measurement is not blocked on the p2p release (plan p2p-public-release-endgame-2026-09-01: 30 done, 6 blocked, 1 todo on 2026-09-30).\n\n### D-005 — p2p git cannot carry the live run today; use hand-merged branches, and offer a GCP machine as a join test for the p2p team\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[peer:su-3ee17, p2p endgame fleet leader, coord msgs muoeaxcp/muoeaxdn/muoeayaa 2026-09-30 17:44Z] in reply to the su asking whether a GCP machine can join the papercusp hive for D-004.\n\n(1) Not today. Proven: two-machine p2p git on the small test hive hello-world-3-pot (tower + Mac VM), via the 0.0.25 exact-artifact drill; the 0.0.26 drill is running (started 17:33Z, result ~19:00Z). Not proven: a fresh machine joining the papercusp hive and its commits reaching papercusp staging. Evidence against, as they reported it: at 17:29Z the Mac VM logged 'papercusp: pot-git NOT CONVERGED WITH THE POT: local v3379 < announced v3642 (137m without local progress)'. They could not determine whether a remote peer's commit gets into the tower's staging tree (tower hiveGit.mode is 'bridged', path never exercised).\n(2) The P-521 independent GO and P-401 release GO/NO-GO are still open; no ETA, not today. No verified join runbook for the papercusp hive (docs/plans/WI-3505-cold-join-canary-playbook.md is marked historical).\n(3) A GCP machine would help them later as a third-machine cold join on hello-world-3-pot (not the papercusp hive), after the drill releases the rig lock (~19:00Z); they will message the su to schedule. They say this is recorded as a decision on p2p-public-release-endgame-2026-09-01 (not re-read by the su).\n\nRuling for this plan: D-004's fallback applies. P-018 lands test-machine work on branches the su merges. A new item offers one of our test machines to the p2p team for the hello-world-3-pot join, which also tells us when P-018 can switch to p2p git.\n\n### D-006 — The cloud test is also a live test of p2p git; do not wait for p2p to be ready\nDate: 2026-09-30\n[owner:Avi 2026-09-30 #1072] \"we can make this cloud test also a test of the p2p system. we dont need to need to wait for it to be ready before we use it to test the cloud system\". Supersedes the D-005 ruling (hand-merged branches as the default). Test machines join through p2p git in two stages: stage 1 (P-522) a GCP VM cold-joins the small test hive hello-world-3-pot, per su-3ee17 D-100 on p2p-public-release-endgame-2026-09-01; stage 2 (P-018) a GCP VM joins the papercusp hive and its agents' commits must reach staging through the tower's bridged hive-git. 'Real staggered its starts' was tested and falsified.\n\nRuling for every ramp and the capacity model (P-012): (1) the capacity inputs are per-agent CPU-seconds per hour and the per-agent memory.peak distribution; (2) concurrent memory is reported as slice anon p95 over a long --duration-sec window, net of the slice's t0 baseline, never a single 5 s max; (3) each phase starts from its t0 baseline recorded in the output; (4) load-driver refuses a CLI version mismatch unless --allow-version-mismatch is passed.\n\n### D-010 — P-005 ramps replay an interleaved session list; the 03:19Z sorted-order ramp results are void\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self 2026-10-01 04:25Z] load-driver assigned slot s on pass k to sessions[(s+k) % len] over a list sorted by id (claude-* before codex-*, exc before mea). Known benign residual: 3 recordings diverge on one tool exit status (environment PATH/files), LLM exchanges served exact; the table reports toolDiverged per step.\n\n### D-011 — P-005 Codex rows include the skills-watcher wake storm; P-006 re-measures with the skills roots created\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self, su-9dfd3, measured 2026-10-01 04:35-05:05Z; EI-21417256075155406]\n\nFinding: Codex 0.159.x's skills watcher watches each skills root, and for a MISSING root it watches the nearest existing ancestor with an inotify mask that includes IN_OPEN. On the P-005 VMs none of /etc/codex/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.codex/skills exist, and running Codex replays on cap-p005-s4 hold watches on $HOME (ino 8002d) and /etc (ino 2a). Every process start opens /etc/ld.so.cache and every git command opens ~/.gitconfig, so each such open wakes EVERY Codex session on the VM; tokio then fans the wake across one worker thread per vCPU. Codex CPU therefore grows with (Codex sessions x VM-wide exec rate), roughly quadratically in N.\n\nEvidence: on the 128-core tower, an idle Codex proc did 13,862 inotify reads in 3s; creating the empty roots moved the watches within 10s and dropped 4 idle procs from 5.3-6.2% to 0.1% CPU each (same procs, back-to-back 20s /proc deltas). Host-wide Codex CPU went ~19.6 -> ~5.6 cores (confounded by load drift, indicative only).\n\nRuling:\n1. The running P-005 ramps are NOT patched: they are the as-shipped baseline, and the table must label the Codex and mixed rows 'Codex with skills-watcher wakes (as shipped, no /etc/codex/skills)'.\n2. P-006 re-measures Codex with scripts/agent-capacity/vm/bootstrap-agent-vm.sh CODEX_SKILL_ROOTS=create (now the default; 'leave' reproduces the baseline). Method: claude CLI (sonnet) headless, fresh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, through the local gateway. Turn 1 reads two source files (4 API calls, ~55-65k context tokens incl. cache). LIVE = one stream-json process, wait, turn 2. RESUME = process A runs turn 1 and exits, wait, process B `--resume <id>` runs turn 2. Separate work dirs per mode (runs r2, r3, gap400).\n\nTurn-2 usage (cache_creation / cache_read, tokens): gap 20s r2 live 1267/32210, resume 1351/25669; r3 live 1303/31361, resume 1178/29435; gap 400s live 1358/25725, resume 1346/29402. All cache writes are ephemeral_1h, so Claude Code (OAuth accounts via our gateway) caches with a 1-hour TTL: a park under 1 h re-sends nothing extra in EITHER mode, and a park over 1 h re-writes the full context in BOTH modes. Keeping the process alive buys zero tokens.\n\nRetracted: run 1 (shared work dir, both modes concurrent) showed a live turn-2 miss (cw 25954 / cr 4742). It did not reproduce in 3 isolated runs; treat it as an artifact of that run, not a property of live processes.\n\nWake latency (spawn or send -> first assistant event): resume 2.3 / 3.2 / 4.4 / 11.1 s vs live 1.4-2.3 s, so resume adds ~1-9 s per wake (n=4, tower, idle). Memory: an idle live headless Claude CLI holds 213-216 MB RSS (tower PSS median for interactive sessions 173 MB, Codex 17 MB, P-529). Decision: process-free parking is a pure win for Claude agents on RAM-bound shapes (e2-highcpu, dense hosts): ~215 MB freed per parked agent for a few seconds of wake latency and no token cost. Codex parking saves little (17 MB). Still open: resume latency under VM load (measure on a lever VM) and Codex resume (`codex exec resume`). Related: P-014, P-016, P-529\n\n### D-019 — P-005 final: e2-standard-16 holds 64 active mixed agents (6.30 USD/active agent-month on-demand, 3.86 spot); with the 0.43 duty cycle that is ~1.66 USD per assigned agent-month on spot, before per-workspace Server overhead\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self, su-9dfd3, measured; final pull 10:35Z PULL_RC=0 TABLE_RC=0, all 4 VMs; data ~/.cache/agent-capacity/p005-ovl, table capacity-table-final.md; overlay workdirs per D-014, working Codex sandbox per D-012, interleaved list per D-010]. Related: P-005, P-007, P-014, P-016, P-528, D-014, D-017, D-018\n\n### D-020 — Cost lever (P-007/P-016): spot e2-custom-16-32768 is the cheapest measured shape at ~2.8 USD per active agent-month (1.2 per assigned agent-month); 16 vCPUs saturate at ~16 runs/min, so capacity must be read from achieved concurrency, not slot count\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self, su-9dfd3, measured 09:50-11:19Z; WI-10004749; data ~/.cache/agent-capacity/lever, table capacity-table-lever.md; same mixed-normal interleaved list, overlay workdirs and Codex sandbox as D-019; both VMs spot, torn down verified 11:14Z and 11:21Z].\n\nPer ramp step (runs/min = replayed sessions completed per minute; achieved = mean sessions in flight):\n- e2-highcpu-16 (16 GB): n32 12.2 runs/min, achieved 31.8; n48 15.4, 47.3, slowdown 0.73 OK; n64 SATURATED, 2 failed + 2 OOM kills, achieved 50.3. Spot is viable for agent hosts: a reclaim costs ~3-4 min of host downtime plus each session's in-flight turn; with termination action STOP no transcript or workspace data is lost.\n2. Detect a reclaim in the guest (the metadata preempted flag) or from the preempted operation, not from instance status. On the flag, agents have ~30 s to checkpoint and fsync.\n3. Recovery automation is not built in the hosted provider: start the stopped host as soon as it reaches TERMINATED, then --resume each interrupted session. That is WI-10005210, together with spot provisioning (the hosted insert sets no scheduling block today).\n4. (c) Existing hosts stay on-demand until recreated (D-028.4).\n\n### D-030 — pc-heavy per-slot memory reserve is derived from a per-host job-peak ledger: max + 10%, only after a full day of data\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self, su-9dfd3, 2026-10-02, WI-10005184 slices 1-2; measured, not owner-directed]\n\nRULING: pc-heavy admission budgets memory per slot from this host's own measured job peaks instead of the fixed 14 GiB, with three rails.\n1. MEASURE: the preemptible monitor sums RssAnon over the job's own process tree (/proc children walk from the setsid leader, NOT `ps -s`, which cost ~0.64 s CPU per call on this ~10k-process box) and appends one row per job to <PC_HEAVY_DIR>/job-peaks.tsv. anon_mib is the budgeting number (VmRSS double-counts shared file pages).\n2. STATISTIC = MAX (+10%, ceil GiB, clamp [1,64]) over the last 100 jobs that ran >= 3 samples. For the slice-4 spot VM ramp, either pre-seed the ledger from a prior run or set PC_HEAVY_MEM_PER_SLOT_MIN_SPAN_SEC=0 deliberately and say so in the result.\n\n### D-031 — Heavy-job admission rollout: capacity rigs stay per-arm; hosted hosts get a node preload + pc-heavy in the customer toolchain via a fixed agent env\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self, su-9dfd3, 2026-10-02, WI-10005184 slice 3; AUTO judgment, not owner-directed]\n\nRULING 1 — GCP capacity VMs are experiment rigs, not production hosts. Capacity planning uses >= 48 agents per e2-standard-16 under this workload, not 40.\n\n### D-041 — P-015: swap (zram or disk) is not a capacity lever under the hosted config; the p64+ limit is pc-heavy admission throughput\nDate: 2026-10-02\nMeasured 2026-10-02 on cap-p015 (e2-custom-16-26624, 16 vCPU / 25.4 GiB, on-demand), WI-10005392. The packed Server price is the measured D-045 packing; the floor assumes Servers fill spare RAM on agent hosts [inferred].\n\n### D-047 — Shared multi-tenant host: fixed loopback services get a per-tenant port by listener uid (WI-10005481)\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self 2026-10-02 21:40Z] Ruling for every fixed-port loopback service a Server runs (inference gateway :8788, packaged MCP proxy :9071, and the same rule for later ones such as the voice WS walks in WI-10005586).\n\n1. A Server never adopts a listener another Linux uid owns. Ownership comes from the kernel's LISTEN-socket uid (/proc/net/tcp{,6}), not from a health probe, since a healthy answer says nothing about whose it is.\n2. If the DEFAULT port is held by another uid, this tenant moves to its own port: rangeBase + (uid % span), walking forward inside the range past ports another uid holds (gateway 23800-24799, MCP proxy 24800-25799, both below the 32768 ephemeral range). The port depends only on the uid and the census, so every process of one tenant and every restart lands on the same port.\n3. The decision is written into the env vars every client reads (PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_PORT, PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_PORT, and PAPERCUSP_MCP_PROXY_BASE when unset) at the top of runBootstrap, before anything can spawn an agent. Spawned agents inherit it. This reuses the existing env contract instead of adding a new config surface.\n4. An EXPLICITLY configured port held by another uid is never moved silently. It is reported as explicit-foreign and the supervisor refuses to adopt it (gateway outcome refused-foreign).\n5. Hosts without /proc (macOS, Windows) keep the pre-fix behaviour. That is a named residual, not a guarantee.\n\nWhy not a network namespace per tenant: it needs root or user namespaces on every install path, while the port rule works for the unprivileged per-user .deb service today. Defense in depth (the gateway and proxy refusing foreign-uid loopback peers via loopback-peer-trust.ts) is a follow-up. It closes the boot-race window where an agent spawned before the pin could still carry the default port.\n\nCode: packages/operator-core/lib/process-supervision/tenant-loopback-port.ts (+ test), gateway-sidecar-spawn.ts, apps/operator/bin/host-bootstrap.ts.\n\n### D-048 — Health probes never count as embed-sidecar activity; any idle-reclaim mechanism must exclude its own probes (P-532b root cause)\nDate: 2026-10-03\n[self, su-9dfd3, measured 2026-10-02 on cap-p532b]\n\nP-532 (cap-p532, 1 tenant, sidecar default ON) showed NO idle exit in 45 min, although the same .deb's 5-min idle exit worked locally. P-532b re-ran with a measurement-only NODE_OPTIONS fetch-wrapping preload that logged the JS stack of every /embed POST. Observed: once the doc-vector backfill drained, the ONLY periodic caller was service-health `runServiceHealthTick -> probeEmbedSidecar`, which POSTs /embed every 60 s (bypassCache every 5 min). The sidecar counted that as activity, so its idle timer never expired.\n\nRuling:\n1. A probe identifies itself with EMBED_SIDECAR_PROBE_HEADER (`x-papercusp-health-probe`). The sidecar serves it (still counted in-flight, so it cannot exit mid-request) but never refreshes lastActivityAt.\n2. An idle exit is a designed state, not an outage: embedSidecarIdleByDesign() + lastExitIdle in the spawn module make the probe read 'not running (idle by design)' after an idle exit, while a crash still reads DOWN.\n3. General rule for any future idle-reclaim lever (sidecars, pooled workers, parked sessions): health/liveness probes must be distinguishable from work and excluded from the activity clock, or the lever silently never reclaims. Trace callers on the real host before guessing from code.\n\nTests: packages/operator-core/lib/service-health-embed-sidecar-probe-idle.test.ts (real probe against the real server) + idle-exit test, 17/17; mutation probes M4/M5 CAUGHT; service-health.test 140/140; behavioural strands exit 0. Live confirmation is P-532c (3 tenants, fresh .deb) under WI-10005630.\n\n### D-049 — Peer-uid trust on loopback stays policy-gated; every multi-tenant host must run with the policy on (WI-10005688)\nDate: 2026-10-03\n[self, su-9dfd3, 2026-10-03]\n\nThe inference gateway (WI-10003621) and now the MCP proxy (WI-10005688) refuse a loopback caller whose uid is not the service uid, but only when loopbackPeerUidPolicyActive(): vm-release profile, a hosted workspace host (PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_WORKSPACE_ROOT / connector bearer), or PAPERCUSP_LOOPBACK_PEER_UID_POLICY=service-only.\n\nNot turned on for every Linux host. Measured: reading /proc/net/tcp + tcp6 on this dev box (4,969 sockets, 752 KB) costs 17.6 ms per read, paid synchronously per new connection on the gateway's and proxy's event loops.\n\nRuling: any host that runs more than one tenant's Server (the D-045/D-046 shared pool, or any future packaged multi-tenant install) must start every Server with the policy on. Hosted workspace hosts already do (workspace-host-bootstrap writes PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_WORKSPACE_ROOT). The sidecar idle exit fires (first at 04:06Z, 10 min after the last real embed at 03:56Z), but the sidecar came back about every 10 min for the rest of the run with ZERO real embeds (8-10 starts per tenant, embtrace shows no /embed or /rerank call before any of them). Restarts land on 5-min wall-clock boundaries, which is the embed backfill sweep's DBOS cadence.\n\nRoot cause [observed in code + trace]: each sweep calls resolveEmbedder() and resolveBatchEmbed(mode) BEFORE it knows whether any row needs embedding. Both resolved the sidecar URL via resolveProcessSidecarUrl -> ensureEmbedSidecar, which spawns the child when it is down. So a drained Server respawned its ~2 GB sidecar every sweep, kept it 5 min until the idle exit, and repeated.\n\nDecision: building an embedder for a BACKGROUND caller is side-effect-free. New buildDeferredSidecarAwareEmbedder (embed-sidecar-wiring.ts) defers resolution to the first embed call. The backfill's buildLocal/Gemma/Harrier use it. resolveBatchEmbed decides batch capability with processSidecarConfigured() (no ensure) and resolves the URL per batch; a batch with no sidecar throws, and the drain falls back to per-row (same outcome as the old null). Interactive callers keep the EAGER builder on purpose: the query-embedder warm-up exists to pay the spawn before a user waits.\n\nGuards: embed-sidecar-deferred-build.test.ts and embed-backfill-deferred-sidecar.test.ts (70/70 with the existing wiring + backfill suites, runId 1ac0f102), plus mutation probes.\n\nConsequence for P-532/P-012: with the sidecar down, a tenant measured 2.13 GiB memory.current vs the 3.24 GiB in-process control (P-011), i.e. 1.11 GiB saved per idle Server [measured, 3 tenants; different machine type, so it is a caveat]. Peak while the sidecar is up was 4.4-4.9 GiB (+1.2-1.7 GiB over in-process). The saving only holds if the sidecar actually stays down, so it needs one more live run (P-532d) to confirm that it does.\n\n### D-051 — Resolving the MEMORY embedder is side-effect-free too: configure.ts resolveEmbedder uses the deferred builder (extends D-050; P-532f root cause)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self, su-9dfd3, observed] P-532f (cap-p532f, .deb with D-050 + WI-10005962): after the backfill drained, pct2/pct3 sidecars idle-exited and then restarted at 05:30:0x and 05:40:0x with ZERO real embeds; each start lands 0.1-0.4 s after the 10-min embed-backfill tick's drain line. Scope kept tight: buildEmbedderForMode stays eager (sole caller reembed.ts embeds immediately), and the interactive QUERY embedder (agent-tools/search/embedder.ts) stays eager per D-050. The executing agent should record current alignment and any integration gaps on WI-6554700010016277 and continue the existing lane through verification and shipment.\n\nThis records Avi's clarification of the existing required approach; it does not establish that the integrated design or the under-$20/month result has already passed.\nRelated: P-544, P-537, P-538, P-539, P-540, P-541, P-542\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"chatgpt-gpt-6-1-sol-support-2026-09-30","title":"Add ChatGPT GPT-6.1 Sol support","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-30","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Add ChatGPT GPT-6.1 Sol support\nslug: chatgpt-gpt-6-1-sol-support-2026-09-30\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-30\nupdated: 2026-09-30\n---\n\n## Goal\nSupport explicit gpt-6.1-sol selection and discovery in existing Codex launch and inference surfaces.\n\n## Scope\nUse the official model id and reasoning efforts through max. Extend the existing gateway fallback catalog, shared launch-window resolver, and canonical model-pricing table with official metadata. Preserve current model defaults and the headless GPT-6 Luna max bug-fleet selection.\n\n## Work\n1. Inspect existing seams and official metadata — complete.\n2. Implement metadata and regression tests under WI-10004267 — in progress.\n3. Run focused suites and verify current-build discovery — pending.\n\n## Acceptance\nExplicit selection preserves model and effort. Discovery includes the model. Extended-window policy and correct standard/cache/long-context pricing apply. Existing regression suites pass.\n\n## Sources\nAvi's current-session directives request AUTO, a non-P2P bug-drain GPT-6 Luna max fleet, HEADLESS members, and GPT-6.1 Sol support. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol documents the id, supported efforts, 1,050,000 provider context, $2 input/$0.10 cache read/$2.50 cache write/$10 output per MTok, with long-context premium above 272K.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation and live picker verification complete under WI-10004267. Existing gateway fallback catalog, native selector/effort preservation, extended-window policy, role budgets, and canonical pricing include GPT-6.1 Sol. Operator-core focused suite passed 205 tests and pricing suite passed 43. Coordinated gateway restart recovered HTTP 200. Live auto catalog, native app-server model/list, and actual Codex /model UI list gpt-6.1-sol (UI entry 9, GPT-6.1-Sol current). Active defaults preserved. Independent headless-launch mirror race is assigned to su-6f42e on WI-10004303.\n\n**Next:** No model-support edits remain; fleet leader continues HEADLESS GPT-6 Luna max nonp2p bug-drain supervision and verifies the separately owned launcher correction.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"embedding-candidates-benchmark-2026-09-30","title":"Measure mDenseOn and Perplexity candidate retrieval models","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-30","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Measure mDenseOn and Perplexity candidate retrieval models\nslug: embedding-candidates-benchmark-2026-09-30\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-30\nupdated: 2026-09-30\n---\n\n## Goal\nCompare mDenseOn and Perplexity with current Harrier and Gemma on frozen memory/prose fixtures. Owner authorized AUTO and direct continuation of Codex 01a0f2ed-2d87-7de0-a7b1-9100da8a29ef.\n\n## Scope\nReuse embedder-eval-cli and paired-leg-report. Add only missing candidate loader/import support and conventional tests. Each model has separate vectors. No production settings, models or indexes change. mDenseOn Python measurements are experimental, not claimed as sidecar-compatible.\n\n## Work\nClaimed WI-10004305: inspect inference contracts, add tested candidate support, run isolated memory/prose comparisons, record quality/uncertainty/timing/asset size. This single work item owns the whole benchmark; no fleet.\n\n## Acceptance\nResults for four models over complete fixtures, or actual compatibility failures explicitly reported. Paired uncertainty and runtime differences govern recommendations.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Measured candidate comparison | WI-10004305 | tree |\n\n\n## Phase 2 — ONNX, sidecar and live hybrid validation\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Audit phase-one fairness and freeze a reproducible phase-two evaluation contract: source/fixture identity, balanced held-out queries, no candidate tuning on held-out labels, controlled repeated serial latency, explicit sample/power limits. Pass when these guards are tested in the conventional suite. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Export pinned mDenseOn to ONNX using maintained Optimum tooling; implement the shared worker-backed CLS/query-document adapter. Pass when tokenizer and vectors agree with the frozen Python reference across short/long/batched inputs and no untrained truncation is used. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Extend the existing sidecar model/builder seam for the isolated candidate, preserving model/space identity and cache accounting. Pass when real HTTP, native client, batches, failure paths and worker isolation run against the actual exported graph. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Exercise production lexical-plus-semantic hybrid through an isolated candidate index and read-only live corpus snapshot; compare current Gemma/Harrier controls with mDenseOn on balanced fresh held-out queries and serial repeated warm timing. Pass when actual hybrid calls complete and guard false-positive admission, scope isolation and index-space separation. blocked-by: P-001, P-003 importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Re-grade robustness/fairness and retain source artifacts, exact commands, runtime/version/fixture fingerprints, per-query outcomes and paired uncertainty. Recommend adoption only if this evidence supports it; no production preference switch or re-embedding is part of validation. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Benchmark verdict: mDenseOn warrants a Gemma integration trial; no Harrier replacement established\nDate: 2026-09-30\nEvidence: eight full model/dataset passes over frozen v1 fixtures. Memory: 114 docs, 150 queries (120 answerable); prose: 2029 docs, 134 queries (122 answerable). MRR@10 memory/prose: Gemma .8805/.3492; Harrier .9293/.3715; mDenseOn .9294/.4260; Perplexity .9103/.4242. Paired mDenseOn-minus-Gemma MRR gains: memory .0489 CI [.0117,.0878], prose .0768 CI [.0111,.1421]. Both intervals exclude zero; prose benefit is concentrated in exact identifiers. Against Harrier, mDenseOn intervals include zero on both fixtures; those comparisons are underpowered, not proof of equivalence. Perplexity exact-identifier memory loss against Harrier is significant (delta -.0931 CI [-.1788,-.0217]). Recommendation: prioritize mDenseOn ONNX/sidecar and hybrid integration evaluation before changing Gemma; no current evidence warrants replacing Harrier. This benchmark did not mutate production settings or indexes. mDenseOn ran Python Sentence Transformers CPU fp32; other legs used Transformers.js CPU fp32 weights, Perplexity selecting pooler_output_int8. Prose mean query inference ms: Gemma 27.5, Harrier 151.2, mDenseOn 47.6, Perplexity 63.2. Timings are single runs with differing runtimes; not controlled latency distributions. Loaded uncompressed model/tokenizer assets GB: Gemma 1.2565, Harrier 2.4104, mDenseOn 1.2622, Perplexity 2.4129; these are not built desktop bundle sizes. No multilingual or live hybrid acceptance was claimed. Conventional verification: 693 memory library tests plus 16 candidate/paired tests passed. Reused embedder-eval-cli, existing frozen fixtures, paired-leg-report and the maintained generic ONNX loader; added only missing experimental candidate adapters and fingerprint/order-validated external vector import. Source reports: .papercusp/bench-reports/candidates-2026-09-30-memory-comparison.json; prose-comparison.json; assets.json; per-model reports and mdenseon-vectors.json in the same directory. Raw command logs /tmp/candidates-2026-09-30-{gemma,harrier,pplx,mdenseon}.log. Owned incidental transport follow-up EI-24361961451337184 remains open; using the green operator URL was a coordination mitigation, not a staging-service repair.\n\n### D-002 — Phase-two validation contract and fairness limits\nDate: 2026-09-30\nOwner source: session_turn:codex:01a0f2ff-e5eb-7cd1-be8c-6007ee6450cc:17. Continue directly in this AUTO session. Audit robustness, export mDenseOn ONNX, validate the real sidecar and actual production hybrid path. Source evidence: packages/operator-core/lib/memory/configure.ts:688 constructs HybridBackend(LexicalLegBackend(mem0),mem0); hybrid means lexical plus one semantic model. The earlier wording about Gemma as a live hybrid companion did not establish a two-semantic-model fusion and must not be used as the validation architecture. Phase-one 709 checks were implementation regressions; quality estimates came from 120 memory and 122 prose answerable queries, 90 of the latter exact identifiers. Phase-two guards: pin model and export/library versions; compare ONNX tokenization/vectors with the frozen Python reference at native 768 dimensions; include varied lengths, batches, query/document prompts, cache accounting and error paths. Use an isolated candidate sidecar and independently identified vector/index space, never silently label mDenseOn vectors as Gemma in a live store. Live canonical snapshots may be read; writes belong only to a uniquely named benchmark schema. Build a fresh balanced held-out query set independently of model rankings; freeze calibration/test partition before evaluation, use the same lexical/fusion policy, and report class-level uncertainty plus false-positive admission. Warm models first, run serial repeated timing rounds with rotated model order and p50/p95; single-run averages and asset bytes must not be sold as tail latency or complete application bundle size. Runtime parity and sample power are acceptance limits, not proof of multilingual/general superiority. Production model preference changes, global re-embedding and deployment past a release gate are outside this validation request. Reuse existing export tooling, worker, sidecar, canonical-store, HybridBackend, fixtures and paired stats rather than parallel services.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"goal-brief-r3-probe-fixture-2026-09-30","title":"Goal-brief R-3 live-probe fixture — two trivial items for a goal holder to place","status":"draft","created":"2026-09-30","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Goal-brief R-3 live-probe fixture — two trivial items for a goal holder to place\nslug: goal-brief-r3-probe-fixture-2026-09-30\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-09-30\nupdated: 2026-09-30\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Fixture for the goal-brief R-3 live probe (WI-10003903). Evidence pack for the grader: papercusp/.papercusp/scratch/phase6-grader-pack/README.md (+ plan.md, audits-12-17.json, citations.md).\n\nDISCLOSURES (grade AGAINST these, not around them):\n(a) STRIPE WALL — P-038 is needs-human: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY / STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET are installed in NO operator-public deployment (07:01Z `wrangler secret list` = IP_HASH_PEPPER only); the hosted purchase path answers 503 until the owner runs `wrangler secret put`.
