The settlement STATE MACHINE and the policy gates are what is proven; the live rail's own behaviour is not.\n(c) D-055 AUTHORITY PLACEMENT — commerce facts live behind the Worker (D1) + local ledger, finality on chain; the hive log carries governance + distribution only. P-036 therefore proves convergence of the P2P event stream between two real peers and adjudicates the double-spend at the escrow authority (Worker+chain posture), not on the hive log.\n(d) D-062 MONEY PRECISION — per-use money is bigint micros and is never rounded into the ledger's integer minor units; usage receipts/settlement proofs/revenue splits roll up separately (perUseRollup). template and inspect the instance's promoted items, blocker edges and the run's settlement.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | Reuse the maintained Rust/Android/binding checks and existing automatic native executi… <!-- P-016 -->\n## Background\n\nThe existing app is Kotlin/Jetpack Compose with a shared Rust core and UniFFI bindings in the managed papercup-rust-mobile repository. Reuse that app, its /api/device/* server routes, signing identity, release scripts, provenance manifest format, store collateral, and mobile templates/checks.\n\nEvidence read in this session:\n- Android UI/shared-client source history last changed on 2026-08-13; later August work mainly improved packaging, template checks, and release tooling. September commits include bookkeeping and token-kit updates. Dates do not establish current functional compatibility.\n- android-public-release-readiness-2026-08-11 is shipped as a readiness campaign. Its D-006/D-007 approved the exact Android 0.1.0 candidate for controlled non-public validation, retained public NO-GO, and recorded no upload. This does not establish a public release.\n- Current source targets compileSdk/targetSdk 36, minSdk 24, removes inherited advertising/attribution permissions, disables Firebase Analytics collection, and requires HTTPS for release pairing. Google's current target-API policy read on 2026-10-01 requires API 36 for new phone apps and updates.\n- Public privacy and support URLs returned HTTP 200 with the intended mobile content. The public Play listing for com.papercuspai.operator.mobile returned HTTP 404; private-track status remains unknown without Play Console.\n- Local release metadata still reports 0.1.0/versionCode 1 while current default debug metadata reports versionCode 100. The authoritative Android release provenance JSON and generated candidate record were absent. Existing local outputs are not a current candidate.\n- The mobile client already uses /api/device/*; the current platform still supplies device pairing, chat, plans, attention, monitoring, sync, push, and voice routes. Full compatibility has not been exercised in this assessment.\n- The mobile repository's GitHub workflow is workflow_dispatch-only. Its Android verification needs an automatic, owned execution path.\n\nSource references: android/app/build.gradle.kts; android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml; crates/papercup-core/src/client.rs and types.rs; Android screens; tools/build-scripts/build-android.sh and android-release-provenance.sh; tools/tests; store/RELEASE-CANDIDATE.md, DATA-SAFETY.md, PRIVACY-POLICY.md and LISTING.md; .github/workflows/ci.yml; packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device; packages/operator-core/lib/device-monitoring.ts; papercusp-desktop/bin/release-local.sh and upload-mobile-release.sh.\n\nPublic references: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878 ; https://papercusp.com/mobile/privacy ; https://papercusp.com/mobile/support .\n\n## Scope\n\nDeliver a maintained Android companion compatible with the supported current Papercusp desktop/operator release, followed by an explicitly approved Google Play public rollout. Public release means the signed, tested artifact is available through the intended public track and installs successfully on a physical phone; a plan marked shipped, a local APK, an R2 upload, or a closed-track upload alone is insufficient.\n\nInclude current companion flows: QR/manual pairing; workspace and pot selection; operator conversation and supported role selection; plans and item states; attention/approvals; running agents and fleet monitoring; diagnostics; push notifications; desktop-local and cloud voice; reconnection and credential revocation.\n\nInventory relevant platform changes since the August baseline, including authentication, workspace/harness scope, conversation behavior, status/approval semantics, remote/mesh transport, voice transports, and newly exposed companion functions. Account for every relevant change as implemented, already compatible, or explicitly excluded with rationale and Avi's approval when that exclusion changes the promised scope. Full desktop feature replication is not presumed; existing companion behavior is the starting point.\n\nExclude iOS delivery, a new mobile scaffold, replacement of the shared operator runtime, a new parallel synchronization/agent-orchestration system, and unrelated desktop feature work. If the compatibility census establishes a new requirement outside this scope, record the decision and seek approval before expanding.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Current-platform change census.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A source-backed inventory covers relevant changes since the August baseline, identifies exact mobile and server revisions and supported desktop versions, and assigns each compatibility gap or scope decision to a plan item.\",\"rationale\":\"Derived from Avi's public-release and latest-platform-compatibility request.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a2-0749-7f00-b7ed-d3e1f5880f3c:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A source-backed inventory assigns every relevant compatibility gap or scope decision since the August baseline to a plan item.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any one numbered observation holds: (1) a relevant platform change, current consumer, compatibility gap or unsupported scope exclusion is missing from the census or has no accountable disposition; (2) the inventory omits a relevant change since the August baseline; (3) the inventory does not identify the exact mobile and server revisions; (4) the inventory does not identify the supported desktop versions.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read current mobile/server git histories and the exact API/UI producers since August; enumerate companion contracts/features against their current consumers, assign a disposition and P-item, and independently reconcile inventory residue. Retain source revisions and evidence references.\\nEvidence artifact: the source-backed current-platform census with exact mobile/server/support revisions and accountable residue. Healthy requires this current artifact on the declared evidence plane; tree tests cannot substitute for a promised physical-phone, Play Console or public-install observation.\\nVerification conditions (sub-assertions moved out of the bar so the bar states one outcome; the grader rates each condition, and any failed condition prevents healthy): (a) the inventory covers each relevant change since the August baseline; (b) it identifies the exact mobile and server revisions; (c) it identifies the supported desktop versions.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"},\"replication\":\"Reproduce against the exact current source/spec/candidate/runtime identities and retain failed and passing observations; historical evidence or a different candidate cannot satisfy this requirement.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Wire and authentication compatibility.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The shared mobile core, generated bindings, request/response/error envelopes, token rotation/revocation, workspace scope, synchronization, and streaming behavior match the current device API; contract regressions fail maintained tests.\",\"rationale\":\"Derived from Avi's public-release and latest-platform-compatibility request.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a2-0749-7f00-b7ed-d3e1f5880f3c:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each supported device API operation returns a contract-correct mobile result in every declared scenario.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any one numbered observation holds:\\n(1) A maintained test fails to detect a shared-mobile-core regression against the current device API.\\n(2) Generated bindings do not match the current Rust/device contract.\\n(3) A supported request, response or error envelope is decoded or produced incorrectly.\\n(4) Token rotation or revocation fails its maintained boundary tests.\\n(5) Workspace scope is crossed or a supported synchronization scenario fails.\\n(6) A supported streaming scenario fails, hides an error or cannot recover.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked in the independent mobile repository and replay sanitized current /api/device response/error/token fixtures through crates/papercup-core/tests/client_test.rs. Exercise mismatched schemas, token revocation/rotation, workspace scoping and streaming failure cases; require meaningful matched tests and zero relevant ignores.\\nVerification conditions (sub-assertions moved out of the bar so the bar states one outcome; the grader rates each condition, and any failed condition prevents healthy): (a) the declared scenarios are request, response, error, binding, authentication, workspace, synchronization and streaming; (b) maintained tests detect a regression in each operation's result.\\nRating basis: the model and unchanged original intent remain the pass floor; rate every numbered falsifier independently, and any observed falsifier prevents healthy.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"cargo\",\"manifestPath\":\"papercup-rust-mobile/Cargo.toml\",\"sourceFiles\":[\"papercup-rust-mobile/crates/papercup-core/src/client.rs\",\"papercup-rust-mobile/crates/papercup-core/tests/client_test.rs\"]},\"replication\":\"Reproduce against the exact current source/spec/candidate/runtime identities and retain failed and passing observations; historical evidence or a different candidate cannot satisfy this requirement.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Companion feature correctness.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Chat, plans, attention/approvals, agent/fleet monitoring, workspace/pot selection, and diagnostics work against the supported current operator, render current states accurately, and do not silently hide failures or report unmeasured status as healthy.\",\"rationale\":\"Derived from Avi's public-release and latest-platform-compatibility request.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a2-0749-7f00-b7ed-d3e1f5880f3c:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each in-scope companion journey shows the supported current operator's actual state.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any one numbered observation holds: (1) an in-scope companion journey fails, shows stale/wrong state or hides an error as a healthy/empty result; (2) any in-scope journey (chat, plans, attention/approvals, agent/fleet monitoring, workspace/pot selection, diagnostics) is missing from the evaluated set; (3) a journey does not work against the supported current operator; (4) a current state renders inaccurately; (5) a failure is silently hidden; (6) unmeasured status is reported as healthy.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Drive the signed Android UI against a supported current-build operator and then the intended shipped counterpart. Send/receive chat, inspect plans/current item states, attention/approvals, workspace/pot selection, running agents/fleets and diagnostics; compare visible values with the underlying current writers and exercise missing/error data. Retain exact artifact/runtime identities, screenshots and maintained regression-test evidence.\\nEvidence artifact: the exact signed APK hash and native companion-journey evidence bundle, with operator runtime identity and writer comparisons. Healthy requires this current artifact on the declared evidence plane; tree tests cannot substitute for a promised physical-phone, Play Console or public-install observation.\\nVerification conditions (sub-assertions moved out of the bar so the bar states one outcome; the grader rates each condition, and any failed condition prevents healthy): (a) the journeys are chat, plans, attention/approvals, agent/fleet monitoring, workspace/pot selection and diagnostics; (b) each journey works against the supported current operator; (c) current states render accurately; (d) failures are never silently hidden; (e) unmeasured status is never reported as healthy.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"},\"replication\":\"Reproduce against the exact current source/spec/candidate/runtime identities and retain failed and passing observations; historical evidence or a different candidate cannot satisfy this requirement.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Secure remote access.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Release pairing and authenticated requests use the declared encrypted transport, preserve credentials in platform-protected storage, reject revoked/invalid tokens correctly, and recover over supported Wi-Fi/cellular/mesh/tunnel routes without weakening the release cleartext policy.\",\"rationale\":\"Derived from Avi's public-release and latest-platform-compatibility request.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a2-0749-7f00-b7ed-d3e1f5880f3c:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every supported release route satisfies the declared device-security contract.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any one numbered observation holds: (1) the release accepts an insecure/replayed pairing payload, leaks credentials, crosses workspace scope, accepts a revoked token or cannot recover through a promised remote route; (2) traffic does not use the declared encrypted transport; (3) credentials persist outside platform-protected storage; (4) a revoked or invalid token is not rejected correctly; (5) a connection does not recover over a supported Wi-Fi, cellular, mesh or tunnel route; (6) the release cleartext policy is weakened.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Fresh-pair with valid QR/manual payloads, deny invalid/replayed/HTTP release payloads, revoke/rotate the device token, switch workspaces and move a physical phone between Wi-Fi/cellular and supported secure remote routes. Inspect platform credential storage and sanitized transport/log evidence; reproduce reconnection and deny cross-workspace access.\\nEvidence artifact: the exact signed APK hash and sanitized physical-phone encrypted-route, token/storage and off-LAN reconnection matrix. Healthy requires this current artifact on the declared evidence plane; tree tests cannot substitute for a promised physical-phone, Play Console or public-install observation.\\nVerification conditions (sub-assertions moved out of the bar so the bar states one outcome; the grader rates each condition, and any failed condition prevents healthy): (a) traffic uses the declared encrypted transport; (b) credentials persist in platform-protected storage; (c) revoked or invalid tokens are rejected correctly; (d) connections recover over the supported Wi-Fi, cellular, mesh and tunnel routes; (e) the release cleartext policy is not weakened.\\nBar scope (moved out of the bar so it states one outcome): the device-security contract covers both release pairing and every authenticated request; the grader rates pairing and authenticated requests separately on every supported route, and a failure of either prevents healthy.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"},\"replication\":\"Reproduce against the exact current source/spec/candidate/runtime identities and retain failed and passing observations; historical evidence or a different candidate cannot satisfy this requirement.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Voice and notifications.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Desktop-local and opt-in cloud voice complete actual turns with recording/playback cleanup; push registration, delivery and deep links work in relevant foreground/background/terminated states with permission denial handled. Optional wake-word behavior is accurately disclosed and must not leave a broken advertised control.\",\"rationale\":\"Derived from Avi's public-release and latest-platform-compatibility request.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a2-0749-7f00-b7ed-d3e1f5880f3c:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each declared voice or push journey meets its documented acceptance contract.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any one numbered observation holds:\\n(1) A declared desktop-local or opt-in cloud voice mode cannot complete an actual turn.\\n(2) Recording, playback, cancellation or background transition leaves capture/session resources active.\\n(3) Push registration or delivery fails in a required foreground, background or terminated state.\\n(4) A notification deep link opens the wrong or inaccessible journey.\\n(5) Microphone or notification permission denial is mishandled or cloud-voice consent is bypassed.\\n(6) Optional wake-word behavior is inaccurately disclosed or an advertised wake-word control is broken.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run actual desktop-local and consented cloud voice turns and observe capture/transcript/playback/cancellation; revoke consent and repeat. Register/deliver FCM notifications and follow deep links in foreground/background/terminated states; deny microphone/notification permissions and check resource cleanup. Retain release-artifact identity, audio/notification evidence and maintained native tests.\\nEvidence artifact: the exact signed APK hash and actual voice-turn/consent/cleanup plus FCM delivery/deep-link/permission-state evidence. Healthy requires this current artifact on the declared evidence plane; tree tests cannot substitute for a promised physical-phone, Play Console or public-install observation.\\nVerification conditions (sub-assertions moved out of the bar so the bar states one outcome; the grader rates each condition, and any failed condition prevents healthy): (a) the declared journeys are desktop-local voice, opt-in cloud voice, wake-word disclosure, and push registration/delivery/deep-link; (b) each journey's acceptance contract covers its actual turn or delivery, consent, permission denial, and resource cleanup, and every journey x dimension pair is rated.\\nRating basis: the model and unchanged original intent remain the pass floor; rate every numbered falsifier independently, and any observed falsifier prevents healthy.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"},\"replication\":\"Reproduce against the exact current source/spec/candidate/runtime identities and retain failed and passing observations; historical evidence or a different candidate cannot satisfy this requirement.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Repeatable automatic verification.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The existing build/check surfaces run Rust tests, binding checks, Android unit tests, relevant instrumentation, release lint, manifest/privacy checks and provenance guards automatically on meaningful changes through an owned CI/local-gate path. Prefer existing typed contracts, role/permission semantics, monitoring readers, template check manifests, release scripts and artifact registry; do not introduce new tables, tools, services, polling systems or scaffold unless a documented search establishes why no maintained surface fits.\n\nFirst resolve the mobile harness, its canonical managed staging checkout, branch, lock mode and file-claim namespace. The existing sibling repository was read as evidence; that read does not authorize editing a non-canonical worktree. Register implementation work and acquire file claims before edits. Leave commits/pushes to the managed git-sync pipeline.\n\nBuild a compatibility matrix with feature/contract, August behavior, current writer/server route, mobile consumer, required change, test and owning P-item. Test real server envelopes and authentication boundaries, not only happy-path mocks; save sanitized fixtures in the project's normal suite. Existing pairing/token data is never written into evidence or logs.\n\nPre-release implementation acceptance uses staging/current-build with a valid encrypted route for the signed release app. For server changes, consult dev:pipeline_position with the correct testClass and execute its currentBuildTestRoute; a route gap must be prepared, not treated as a runnable runtime. Final compatibility verifies the exact supported deployed desktop/operator version because public users will pair to that shipped version. This is the final release stage, not a prerequisite for preparatory work.\n\nLIVE_GATE_OPS has one owner. Before any live gate action, read its ownership; if held, request any needed final-release evidence once and continue independent app work. No parallel fixer/monitor or repeated gate reads by a non-owner.\n\nMaintain one source-bound candidate identity throughout QA, upload and rollout. Any source or artifact change invalidates affected acceptance and requires a new candidate plus the necessary rechecks. Preserve Android upgrade ordering independently of desktop release labels: verify every previously distributed/Play version code before selecting the next one.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-004, P-006 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003, P-009 | live |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-009 | live |\n| R-5 | P-005, P-009 | live |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-007, P-011 | live |\n| R-9 | P-009 | live |\n| R-10 | P-010, P-011 | live |\n| R-11 | P-012, P-013 | deployed |\n| R-12 | P-014 | deployed |\n| R-13 | P-015 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline and compatibility\n\n- **P-001** `done` Reconcile current mobile/server source, canonical mobile harness/checkout and locking, old release decisions, existing artifacts, signing/toolchain availability, Play account/package history, and every relevant platform change since August. Source: docs/evidence/android-byoc-cloud-compatibility-2026-10-06.md §4 gap list G1-G9 and §5. Owner basis: directives #1484 and #1487 [owner:Avi 2026-10-06].\n\nModel:\n1. The base URL is opaque to the client. The Rust client keeps calling <serverUrl>/api/device/<route>. Desktop: serverUrl = LAN or own-tunnel URL. Cloud: serverUrl = https://app.papercusp.com/api/workspaces/<workspaceId>. No cloud branch in the client. The shared crate's base_url() must accept a path prefix and normalise a trailing slash. Android EndpointSecurity.kt must accept an https URL with a path (m1 adds that test in P-004). The client accepts pair baseUrls kind 'relay'.\n2. Portal device-http relay plane, a sibling of app-http in hosted-app-relay.ts: /api/workspaces/<id>/device/* -> connector -> VM /api/device/*. Default-deny allowlist derived from external-ingress-paths.ts (not copied). Authorization is forwarded only when device-JWT shaped. /device/pair needs no bearer. The deny-only ingress marker is stamped on every forward. The relay carries the WebSocket Upgrade for /api/device/voice. A 401 from the VM passes through unchanged.\n3. Pairing on cloud: portal Remote access -> Pair phone calls the VM's mint-pair-token over operator-http. On a hosted VM the advertised serverUrl is the portal relay URL. The QR payload shape is unchanged apart from the URL value and the added machine Noise key.\n4. Auth stays on the VM. The VM issues and verifies the device JWT; revocation and rotation stay there. The portal does shape checks only.\n5. workspace_offline is its own error, never Unauthorized (Unauthorized forces a re-pair on Android and would wipe valid credentials).\n6. Required amendment (su-b9f6deac): on a byoc workspace every device-http content frame is sealed end to end with the existing Noise XX channel (byoc-sealed-channel.ts). The phone is the initiator. The machine's static Noise public key travels in the pair QR; the phone's static key is registered when the pair is redeemed. The relay refuses plaintext byoc device content (hosted-byoc-confidentiality-correction D-003), classified in HOSTED_RELAY_FRAME_REGISTRY. The client seals whenever the pair payload carries a machine Noise key. Use a maintained Noise library in the shared Rust core, with cross-implementation test vectors against byoc-sealed-channel.ts.\n7. Device relay frames respect the 512 KiB relay frame cap (G9): voice and turn bodies fit under it or are chunked. This is an acceptance check on the relay work.\n\nOwnership: the shared BYOC Rust layer (URL prefix, workspace_offline mapping, sealed-channel initiator) is P-015 in this plan. The Swift DesktopVoiceSession side belongs to su-d34a76e0 (iOS half of WI-10006857). Applies to P-003 (WI-10004770) and the P-007 listing copy.\n\n### D-017 — Cloud device relay path is /api/workspaces/<id>/api/device/<route> (corrects D-013 #2 wording)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, m2 su-deb0a62a under owner AUTO; correction of D-013 #2's path wording so it satisfies D-013 #1]\n\nD-013 #1 keeps the client unchanged: the shared Rust client (papercup-rust-mobile crates/papercup-core/src/client.rs) always requests <base_url>/api/device/<route>, and the cloud base URL is <portal>/api/workspaces/<id>. So the phone sends /api/workspaces/<id>/api/device/<route>. D-013 #2's literal '/api/workspaces/<id>/device/*' would never match it, and every cloud call would 404.\n\nRuling: the portal device-http relay matches /api/workspaces/<id>/api/device/<route> and carries it to the machine's /api/device/<route>. Measured 22:26Z: secret-stream 6.9.1 uses noise-curve-ed 2.1.0 (Ed25519 DH via crypto_scalarmult_ed25519), not X25519, so a stock snow initiator will not interoperate; a custom Ed25519 DH resolver (reuse candidate: hypercore-protocol-rs) is required. That work lives in papercup-rust-mobile crates/papercup-core, disjoint from m2 operator files, and is shared with the iOS lane. Ruling: it is WI-10006994 (child of WI-10006956), owned by m1 su-a64f40ce, started once P-002 closes. m2 keeps server side: (c3), the pair-route key-equality follow-up, and the end-to-end hosted pairing test, which consumes WI-10006994. UniFFI changes follow iphone-public-release#D-015(1) advance notice.\n\n### D-019 — BYOC phones reach the workspace through a sealed WebSocket ingress at /api/workspaces/<id>/api/device/sealed (completes D-013 #6)\nDate: 2026-10-07\nDate: 2026-10-07\n[self-imposed, m2 su-deb0a62a under owner AUTO; owner basis directives #1484/#1487; implements D-013 #6]\n\nObserved 2026-10-07T01:00Z: apps/operator/bin/hosted-handler.ts routes /api/workspaces/:id/api/device/* to handleHostedDeviceRelay, which returns 403 byoc_plaintext_relay_refused for EVERY byoc workspace (hosted-app-relay.ts ~line 773). The WebSocket upgrade accepts only connector and browser (user-session ticket) roles. So no route carries a phone's sealed packets to a byoc workspace, although the broker (openAppChannel sealed:true) and the host (sealed device-http responder, pair key binding) both support it.\n\nRuling: add a phone-facing sealed ingress on the portal.\n1. Transport: WebSocket upgrade at <portal>/api/workspaces/<id>/api/device/sealed (base URL stays opaque per D-013 #1; the client derives it as <serverUrl>/api/device/sealed). No ticket and no bearer at the portal: the phone is unauthenticated to the portal by design, and auth stays on the VM inside the sealed channel (D-013 #4).\n2. The portal opens broker.openAppChannel(connector, handlers, 'device-http', { sealed: true }) and relays only sealed.packet frames (byoc-sealed-channel.ts wire shape) in both directions. Any other frame closes the socket with 4403 byoc_plaintext_relay_refused.\n3. Offline workspace: the upgrade is refused with HTTP 503 workspace_offline + retry-after (never 401, D-013 #5).\n4. Inside the channel the phone is the Noise XX initiator pinned to the QR machine key, then sends the existing http.request / http.body / http.end frames; it receives http.response / http.body / http.end / http.error. The host enforces the phone allowlist and the device-JWT binding; the VM verifies the JWT.\n5. Every http.body chunk carries at most 256 KiB raw so each sealed packet stays under the 512 KiB frame cap (D-013 #7).\n6. Non-byoc (papercusp-hosted) workspaces keep the plain HTTP relay; the client seals only when the pair payload carries a machine Noise key (D-013 #6).\nOwnership: portal ingress + its integration tests are WI-10006956 (m2). The Rust client transport is WI-10006994 (m1); the iOS side follows iphone-public-release D-014/D-015.\n\n### D-020 — P-015 large device uploads reuse HTTP body/end frames inside Noise (device plane only)\nDate: 2026-10-07\n[self-imposed under owner AUTO; implements D-013 #7 and ANDROID-P-015-FRAME-CAP]\nMeasured: hosted-operator-http.ts request() rejected inline decoded bodies above HOSTED_OPERATOR_HTTP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES (512 KiB); existing http.body response frames already chunked at HOSTED_OPERATOR_HTTP_BODY_CHUNK_BYTES (48 KiB). The first assembled D-019 run passed transport/security tests but only demonstrated large response chunking, not required large uploads.\nDecision: extend the EXISTING OperatorHttpChannel with opt-in device-only upload assembly. Phone sends http.request {requestId,method,path,headers,bodyChunked:true}, ordered http.body {requestId,data:canonical base64} fragments <=48 KiB decoded, then http.end {requestId}. All frames are separately Noise-sealed. Inline <=512 KiB stays unchanged. App/operator planes do not admit client body/end. Assembly is bounded to 32 MiB total (supports existing 15 MiB audio encoded in JSON), shares the channel in-flight cap, times out on the header budget, and is discarded on abort/close. Route policy runs before buffering; device key/JWT header and pair-body policies still run before the complete request reaches the VM. Runtime host and Rust phone must both include this extension; m2 owns host implementation, m1 owns client emission. No new table/tool/config/parallel protocol was introduced; reuse is http.request/body/end and OperatorHttpChannel.\nRelated: P-015\n\n### D-021 — Key-advertising Papercusp-hosted phones use the same sealed device ingress as BYOC\nDate: 2026-10-07\nDate: 2026-10-07\n[self-imposed m2 su-deb0a62a under fleet AUTO; implements D-013 #3/#6 and repairs EI-25301141794178113]\nMeasured: pair.ts machineNoiseKeyFor(hostedDeviceRelayBaseUrl(...)) advertises/requires Noise for both hosting classes; hosted-workspace-host-runtime.ts loads the shared machine key whenever PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_CONNECTOR_BEARER is configured. hosted-handler.ts and attachSealedDeviceSocket currently gate device/sealed to byoc; HostedWorkspaceSessionBroker.openAppChannel also drops sealed:true on papercusp. Before activation, read the complete source conversation using sessions:search/sessions:read, map corrections/constraints/rejected alternatives/dependencies/acceptance requirements, record plans:audit phase activation with itemProvenance, and repair any omissions.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01","title":"AWS cloud workspaces at feature parity with GCP in the cloud portal","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: AWS cloud workspaces at feature parity with GCP in the cloud portal\nslug: aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nA cloud portal user can connect their own AWS account and create, reach, stop/start, back up/restore and remove a Papercusp cloud workspace on AWS exactly as they can on Google Cloud today, in both the local (desktop) and hosted (portal) control planes. AWS shows as live in the portal, and a live run in the real AWS account proves the whole lifecycle with zero leftover resources.\n\n## Source\n\n- [owner:aviynw 2026-10-01, directive #1221] \"What's left to do to support amazon aws like we are supporting google GCP for our cloud portal?\"\n- [owner:aviynw 2026-10-01, directive #1223] \"Write a plan for supporting AWS and acheiving feature parity with GCP then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped status yourself now.\"\n- [owner:aviynw 2026-10-01, directive #1224] \"are you sure the aws account isnt in this workspace yet? if so tell me what you need from me to auth it\" — answer: the account exists (413781344298, IAM Identity Center profile `papercusp-byoc`); only the SSO session had expired, and the owner was given a device-login code.\n\n## Context (measured 2026-10-01, read-only audit)\n\nAWS was deliberately deferred by byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-154 (\"For the initial launch let's just get GPC working\"), recorded as dropped per #D-169 and carried in byoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01 (P-003 AWS canary, P-005 Gate 5, P-006 IAM templates/marketplace images). This plan takes over those AWS items.\n\nAlready written but unused outside tests (packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/):\n- `aws-provider.ts` — `AwsWorkspaceHostProvider` (EC2 instances, EBS volumes, snapshots) behind an injected `AwsWorkspaceHostSdkClient` seam. Only test fakes implement the seam.\n- `aws-connection.ts` / `aws-connection-profile.ts` — credential sources (local SSO profile / assume-role; hosted customer-role with external ID; hosted OIDC), permission action list, transport profiles (`aws-ssm-ssh` default).\n- `hosted-provider-delegation.ts` — AWS onboarding record + CloudFormation JSON template.\n- `aws-ami-release.ts` — AMI release module, no caller.\n\nNot wired:\n- No `@aws-sdk/*` dependency anywhere; no real EC2/SSM/STS client.\n- `lib/dbos/bootstrap.ts:319` registers only the `'gcp'` provider factory.\n- `endpoint-route/routes/workspace-hosts/connection.ts` rejects any target other than `gcp` (lines 100, 238, 271).\n- `endpoint-route/hosted-runtime.ts:285` — the AWS hosted delegation `verify()` always throws `hosted_provider_delegation_aws_adapter_unavailable`.\n- GCP-only with no AWS twin: IAP connector enrollment / credential delivery / initialization operations (`gcp-iap-*`), `cloud-workspaces/gcp-preflight.ts`, `gcp-safety.ts`, `soak-gcp.ts`, GCP-shaped cleanup obligations and inventory, GCP image-family release CLI, `psu --connect` kind `gcp-iap` only (WI-10002874).\n- Portal (`portal/` checkout): `PORTAL_PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES.aws.parity = 'deferred'` (packages/contracts/src/index.ts), the seam refuses AWS connections (apps/host/src/workspace-hosts.ts:261-266), and the first-workspace form is Google-only (packages/ui/src/workspaces.tsx).\n\n## Scope\n\nIn: AWS bring-your-own-cloud for both control planes (local desktop and hosted portal), every lifecycle verb GCP supports, setup/permission templates, safety rails, live canary, portal parity flip.\nOut: the Papercusp-hosted option (we run the machine in our own cloud) stays GCP-only; Azure stays deferred (carrier plan P-004); an AWS Marketplace listing is out unless an item below proves it is needed for parity.\n\n## Design\n\n- AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 modular clients (EC2, SSM, STS, Pricing, IAM simulate) implement `AwsWorkspaceHostSdkClient`; credentials come from the existing `planAwsSdkCredentialProvider` plan.\n- Reachability uses SSM Session Manager (`aws-ssm-ssh`) the way GCP uses IAP: no public IP, no inbound security-group rules.\n- Generalise, don't fork: where a GCP-only module carries provider-neutral logic (initialization operations, credential delivery, safety, soak, cleanup obligations), lift the neutral part behind the provider seam and add the AWS half.\n\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-012 | live |\n| R-10 | P-015 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-016 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-017 | live |\n| R-13 | P-012 | live |\n| R-14 | P-012 | live |\n| R-15 | P-012 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Foundations\n\n- **P-001** `done` Record the AWS identity model as a plan decision, mirroring byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-397 (per-org GCP service accounts, one instance per sign-up, allowlist until live-verified): Papercusp acts in a customer AWS account only by role-chaining control-plane principal -> that organization's own per-org IAM role in the Papercusp control-plane account -> the customer's role, whose trust policy names only that per-org role ARN and an org-scoped ExternalId. The control-plane principal may assume only roles under the per-org path. Same one-instance-per-sign-up cap and allowlist as GCP. importance: high — note: P-001 = D-001 recorded (WI-10005026); P-014 = carrier D-003 + P-005 rescope + P-031 (WI-10005038).\n- **P-002** `done` Real `AwsWorkspaceHostSdkClient` over AWS SDK v3 modular clients (EC2, SSM, STS, Pricing; IAM policy simulation for preflight), with credentials from `planAwsSdkCredentialProvider` for every source in aws-connection.ts (local SSO profile, local assume-role, hosted customer-role with ExternalId, hosted OIDC). Idempotent client tokens, waiter-based state waits honouring AbortSignal, and no credential material in argv/logs/evidence. Vitest coverage with an SDK mock; dependencies added via npm run install:safe. importance: high — note: WI-10005012 closed done 22:03Z with 5 audited spec-test-adequacy cards.\n- **P-003** `done` Production wiring: `createConfiguredAwsWorkspaceHostProvider`, register the 'aws' factory in lib/dbos/bootstrap.ts beside 'gcp', and extend provisioning-runner inventory and cloud-resource-obligations teardown to AWS resource kinds (instance, EBS volume, snapshot, security group, instance profile) so recovery, inventory and cleanup work for AWS hosts. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005027 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Connect and reach\n\n- **P-004** `done` Connection route parity: routes/workspace-hosts/connection.ts accepts target 'aws' (account ID, region, credential source, role ARN + ExternalId ref) for create/validate/update, with AWS preflight equivalent to cloud-workspaces/gcp-preflight.ts (identity check, permission simulation against AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS, region/VPC/subnet and SSM availability) and the same refusal vocabulary. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005028 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Reach and initialise an AWS host the way GCP does through IAP: SSM Session Manager transport (`aws-ssm-ssh`) with an instance profile carrying AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, no public IP and no inbound rules; connector enrollment, scoped credential delivery and initialization operations generalised from the gcp-iap-* modules behind the transport seam, with the AWS half implemented and tested. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005029 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` AWS workspace image: wire aws-ami-release.ts into a release CLI equivalent to apps/operator/lib/release/gcp-image-family-release-cli.ts so each workspace-host release publishes an AMI (with SSM agent) in the supported regions, and the provider's image catalog resolves it. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005030 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Safety and hosted\n\n- **P-007** `done` AWS safety rails and soak, generalised from gcp-safety.ts and soak-gcp.ts: per-connection instance cap (one per sign-up for hosted), tag-scoped ownership, orphan detection and zero-orphan teardown, cost estimate before create, and a soak runner that exercises the lifecycle repeatedly. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005031 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Hosted delegation for AWS: replace the always-throwing AWS adapter in endpoint-route/hosted-runtime.ts productionProviderDelegationAdapters with a real verify() (STS role chain per the identity decision, ExternalId check, evidence ref) and revoke(); hosted onboarding creates the per-org IAM role and serves the customer CloudFormation template from hosted-provider-delegation.ts. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005032 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` psu --connect parity: add an AWS connection kind (SSM-based) beside gcp-iap so an operator can open a session on an AWS workspace host from the CLI. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005033 completed (done)\n- **P-015** `done` AWS on Papercusp Cloud (v1, [owner:Avi 2026-10-01 directive #1232], D-004): hosted placement where Papercusp's own AWS account pays (the AWS twin of papercusp-hosted-workspaces on GCP): network, instance profile, AMI from P-006, one-per-sign-up cap from P-007, cost accounting matching GCP hosting, selectable from app.papercusp.com. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed ruling under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Extends byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-397 (owner chose 'Per-org accounts (Recommended)' for GCP; owner turn: 'we wat to ensure each sign up is only able to spin up a single instance').\n\nRULING:\n- Hosted control plane: Papercusp acts in a customer AWS account only by role-chaining: control-plane principal -> that organization's own per-org IAM role in the Papercusp control-plane account (path /papercusp/orgs/) -> the customer's role. The customer role's trust policy names only that per-org role ARN and requires an org-scoped ExternalId (confused-deputy protection). The control-plane principal's own policy allows sts:AssumeRole only on the per-org path, so it cannot reach a customer account directly.\n- Local (desktop) control plane: the operator's own credentials (SSO profile or assume-role) as already modelled in aws-connection.ts; no Papercusp principal involved.\n- Same limits as GCP: one instance per hosted sign-up, allowlist until live-verified.\n\nWHY: it is the direct AWS analogue of the owner's GCP choice, so a customer gets the same isolation guarantee on either cloud, and a leaked control-plane credential cannot act in any customer account without also passing that org's own role.\n\n### D-002 — Execution route: this su session implements the plan itself; AWS SDK v3 modular clients, not a hand-rolled SigV4 client\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed, AUTO].\n\nROUTE: implemented by this session (route A), not a fleet. Measured: the workspace fact account-burn (system:burn-governor, 2026-10-01 19:11Z) reports 16 of 17 inference accounts burning, most at a provider-measured 7-day wall, so a parallel fleet would stall on capacity.\n\nSDK: use the maintained AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 modular clients (@aws-sdk/client-ec2, client-ssm, client-sts, client-pricing, client-iam, credential-providers) behind the existing AwsWorkspaceHostSdkClient seam. GCP uses a hand-written REST client, but repo guidance prefers a maintained library over rolling our own, and SigV4 signing, SSO token refresh and role chaining are exactly the parts not worth re-implementing.\n\n### D-003 — Peer-consult findings folded into existing items (no new items)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. The pre-P-006 catalog filtered the shared (ExecutableUsers:self) query by tag:papercusp:managed, so a customer account saw zero Papercusp releases.\n\nRULING: (1) aws-sdk-client.ts listImages keeps the owned query (Owners:self + tag:papercusp:managed, provenance from tags). (2) Shared releases are queried with Owners:<trusted publisher accounts> + name papercusp-workspace-host-* (no tag filter), and each result is re-checked client-side: OwnerId must be a trusted publisher, the Description must parse via parseAwsAmiReleaseDescription, and the Name must equal AWS_AMI_NAME_PREFIX + that version. 'lists shared release AMIs by publisher, release name and Description provenance — never by tag' (imitation from another owner, name/description mismatch and staging candidate all excluded); test_runs 20452755 aws-ami-release-cli.test.ts 7/7 and 20452756 gcp-image-family-release-cli.test.ts 21/21; lint:tsc operator + operator-core status=clean 2026-10-01T22:49Z.\n\n### D-006 — P-007 safety parity scope: generalise what GCP runs in production; disclose the unwired preflight instead of duplicating it\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02.
