Soak: provider-dispatched soak seams (soak-seams.ts) with an AWS instance read (DescribeInstances of the registered instance) and an aws-ssm-ssh reach probe that enrolls no host key; standing health targets gcp and aws.\n\n### D-007 — AWS org ExternalId is derived from the organization; revoke acts through the verified-delegation gate\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Applies D-001 in P-008.\n1. ExternalId: organizationExternalId(org) = pcx- + sha256(\"papercusp-aws-external-id-v1:\" + org)[0:40], referenced as resolver://aws-external-id/<org>. Server-derived, never customer-chosen, unique per organization, stable across rotations. Not a secret (AWS documents ExternalId as a confused-deputy guard); the per-org principal remains the primary isolation, so no new secret store is introduced. The customer CloudFormation template prefills it as the ExternalId parameter Default.\n2. verify() walks the real chain (control plane -> per-org role -> customer role with ExternalId) and checks account + role, and additionally proves the customer role REFUSES the per-org role without the ExternalId; a trust policy missing the condition is marked invalid.\n3. revoke() records the revocation like GCP; it does not edit IAM, because rotation revokes the old generation after the new one verifies and both normally name the same customer role. Revocation takes effect where credentials are composed: a hosted AWS connection composes a provider only while its delegation is verified (aws-configured-provider), mirroring resolveHostedGcpAuth.\n4. Per-org role: /papercusp/orgs/pco-<sha256(org)[0:24]> (same digest as the GCP per-org account), trusting only PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_AWS_CONTROL_PLANE_PRINCIPAL_ARN, inline policy allowing sts:AssumeRole only on role/PapercuspWorkspaceHost-* (the template-created name).\n\n### D-008 — P-010 includes the hosted first-workspace server path for AWS bring-your-own-cloud\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. MEASURED: packages/operator-core/lib/auth/hosted/first-workspace.ts refuses any byoc configuration whose provider is not 'gcp' (provider_not_supported, line 320), and gcpFirstWorkspaceDesiredSpec throws for non-GCP records. So flipping the portal's AWS capability to live (P-010) would offer a form the server always refuses. RULING: 1. P-010 opens the server path too. A byoc request may name configuration {provider:'aws', accountId, region?, source:{environment:'hosted', method:'customer-role'}}. The server derives roleArn = arn:aws:iam::<accountId>:role/PapercuspWorkspaceHost-<accountId> (the role the served CloudFormation template creates) and, through bindDelegationToOrganization (P-008), the trusted principal and ExternalId; any caller-supplied roleArn, principal or ExternalId is discarded. OIDC stays refused. 2. Region is optional, validated against the AWS region pattern, default us-east-1. It shapes only the desired spec, never the delegation, so the template digest is unchanged. 3. awsFirstWorkspaceDesiredSpec mirrors the GCP one: account scope, region, zone <region>a, an instance size equivalent to e2-standard-4, encrypted 100 GiB data volume, cloud credential = the delegation credentialRef. 4. Image: the GCP first workspace pins a public Ubuntu 24.04 image; the AWS twin resolves Canonical's Ubuntu 24.04 SSM public parameter for the chosen region through a first-workspace dependency (public parameters resolve to the same AMI id in every account of a region). 5. The portal sends only accountId, region and displayName; it renders the returned CloudFormation template with a quick-create link and plain-language steps, the AWS twin of gcpGrantCommands.\n\n### D-009 — D-009 — The customer's CloudFormation stack builds the AWS host's network, instance profile, KMS key and launch template; amends D-008 points 2 and 4\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. MEASURED: aws-provider.ts readSettings refuses a desired spec without provider.vpcId, subnetId, securityGroupIds, instanceProfileArn, launchTemplateId and kmsKeyArn, and launches with AssociatePublicIpAddress:false. The GCP twin passes network {mode:'managed'} and the GCP provider builds VPC + subnet + Cloud Router + Cloud NAT itself. The hosted AWS delegation template (hosted-provider-delegation.ts awsTemplate) creates only the IAM role. So an AWS first workspace built from account + region alone fails at plan time. Also measured: the client calls DescribeSecurityGroups, GetConsoleOutput, GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota, GetProducts and SimulatePrincipalPolicy as the customer role, none of which AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS grants. RULING: 1. The hosted customer-role CloudFormation template also creates, in the region the customer chose: a VPC, a public subnet with an internet gateway and a NAT gateway, a private subnet routed through the NAT for the host, a security group with no inbound rules, an instance role carrying AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore with its instance profile, a customer KMS key (alias/papercusp-workspace-host) whose key policy lets the workspace-host role use it for EBS, and a launch template requiring IMDSv2. Every resource carries the tag papercusp:workspace-host=<accountId>. This is the AWS twin of the GCP managed network; the NAT gateway is the one standing cost the customer pays (about 32 USD per month plus data), disclosed in the portal steps. Not building it in the provider keeps iam:CreateRole out of Papercusp's role. 2. Region becomes part of the AWS delegation configuration (amends D-008 point 2): it is validated, defaults to us-east-1, and the template carries a CloudFormation Rule that refuses to deploy in any other region, so the template digest changes with region and a replay naming a different region is a delegation_conflict, never a silent move. 3. After verification the server discovers the stack's resources through the verified customer role by tag and fixed name (DescribeSubnets, DescribeSecurityGroups, DescribeLaunchTemplates, iam:GetInstanceProfile, kms:DescribeKey on the alias); missing or unfinished resources answer delegation_pending with the template, because the stack is still being created. No new SDK package is needed. 4. Image (amends D-008 point 4): the newest available Canonical Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 gp3 AMI (owner 099720109477) found with ec2:DescribeImages through the same role, so the lookup runs in the customer's own account and region and needs no ssm:GetParameter grant. 5. AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS gains ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups, ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplates, ec2:GetConsoleOutput, servicequotas:GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota, pricing:GetProducts and iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy, the calls the client already makes. 6. Instance size m6i.xlarge (4 vCPU, 16 GiB, the e2-standard-4 equivalent), 100 GiB encrypted gp3 data volume. Consequence: P-008 and P-004 evidence fingerprints over hosted-provider-delegation.ts and aws-connection.ts go stale and need re-proof at the re-settle step; P-013's docs describe this template.\n\n### D-010 — P-010 replaces the CloudFormation quick-create link with a downloaded template + region-scoped create-stack link\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. FINDING: a CloudFormation quick-create link (console #/stacks/quickcreate?templateURL=...) only accepts a template hosted at an Amazon S3 URL. The AWS first-workspace template is generated per organization (role name per account, ExternalId per organization, region Rule per request; D-007/D-009), so there is no stable S3 object to point at, and publishing per-organization templates to a Papercusp bucket would add a new durable surface (bucket, lifecycle, access policy) for a convenience. RULING: the portal (portal/packages/ui/src/workspaces.tsx awsHostStackSteps + AwsHostStackInstructions) gives the customer, all derived from the template the server returned: (1) a download of that exact template as papercusp-workspace-host.json (a data: URL, so nothing hosted), (2) a link to CloudFormation's create-stack page already in the chosen region, with plain-language steps (Upload a template file, stack name papercusp-workspace-host, leave the prefilled ExternalId, acknowledge named IAM, wait for CREATE_COMPLETE, press Check again), (3) the equivalent aws cloudformation deploy command with CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM and the region, (4) account, region, role ARN and ExternalId shown for recognition, (5) a cost note (NAT gateway about US$33/month plus data in us-east-1, KMS key US$1/month). This meets the P-010 clause 'CloudFormation quick-create link and plain-language steps' in substance (one link into the right console page plus steps); a one-click quick-create is deferred until there is a reason to host per-organization templates in S3. Revisit if the live canary (P-012) shows the upload step is a real drop-off.\n\n### D-011 — P-013 scope: a customer-run AWS setup template for the desktop path, a download route, and one public Cloud workspaces page for both providers\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223].\n\nMEASURED: (1) The hosted path already generates both providers' least-privilege templates from code: hosted-provider-delegation.ts gcpTemplate (custom role from GCP_WORKSPACE_HOST_REQUIRED_PERMISSIONS) and awsTemplate (CloudFormation role with Action = AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS plus the D-009 host stack), delivered by the portal since P-010. (2) The desktop/local AWS path has no template: the connection route (routes/workspace-hosts/connection.ts) asks for vpcId, subnetId, securityGroupIds, launchTemplateId, instanceProfileArn, kmsKeyArn and an optional roleArn that the customer would have to build by hand, while the GCP provider builds its network itself. (3) The customer-facing docs site (apps/papercusp-docs, bundled into the portal at /docs) has no cloud-workspaces page for either provider; the only GCP setup guidance is in-product.\n\nRULING:\n1. New aws-customer-setup-template.ts builds a CloudFormation template for the customer-run (desktop) path: a role PapercuspWorkspaceHostOperator-<account> whose only policy is AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS, trusting a principal the customer names (default: their own account root, so only principals they allow can assume it), plus hostedAwsHostStackFragment for network, instance profile, KMS key and launch template. Outputs map one-to-one onto the connection form fields (OperatorRoleArn, VpcId, PrivateSubnetId, SecurityGroupId, LaunchTemplateId, InstanceProfileArn, KmsKeyArn); the image still comes from the image catalog.\n2. hosted-provider-delegation.ts is NOT edited (P-010 evidence is bound to it); the role resource is a small deliberate duplicate.\n3. GET /workspace-hosts/aws-setup-template?accountId&region[&principalArn] returns it as a download, loopback-only, beside the other workspace-host routes, so the desktop Cloud Workspaces surface (P-011) can link it.\n4. apps/papercusp-docs gets one Cloud workspaces page covering Google Cloud and AWS, through app.papercusp.com and from the desktop app, describing permissions by service. A doc-claims test pins that page to the code: every service prefix in AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS and every template output it names must exist.\n5. Marketplace images are out of scope: parity does not require them (GCP ships its image through a shared image, AWS through shared AMIs per D-005).\n6. Stack name collision: the local template reuses the hosted fragment's per-account names, so an account already connected through app.papercusp.com in the same region should reuse that stack's outputs. The docs say so.\n\n### D-012 — Spec AWSP-P-013-cfn-policy-parity targets the hosted Papercusp role template; the desktop setup template's role needs no ExternalId\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223].\n\nMEASURED: spec AWSP-P-013-cfn-policy-parity rev 2 says 'the customer-facing AWS CloudFormation template for the Papercusp role grants exactly the actions in AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS, requires the customer's ExternalId in the trust policy, and the published AWS setup guide references that template.' Two customer-facing AWS templates now exist: (a) the hosted template, hosted-provider-delegation.ts awsTemplate, whose role is assumed by Papercusp's own per-organization principal with Condition StringEquals sts:ExternalId (D-007); (b) the desktop setup template, aws-customer-setup-template.ts (D-011), whose role is assumed by a principal inside the customer's own account (default: the account root).\n\nRULING:\n1. 'The Papercusp role' is (a), the role Papercusp itself assumes. The spec clause is evidenced against the hosted template plus the docs page's 'From app.papercusp.com' AWS steps, which show the ExternalId and the 'Download the setup file' link. A new doc-claims case in packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/cloud-workspaces-docs.test.ts pins all three claims together: the hosted role's policy actions equal AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS, its trust statement carries the sts:ExternalId condition, and the page's app.papercusp.com AWS steps name the ExternalId and the download.\n2. Template (b) deliberately carries no ExternalId. AWS defines ExternalId as a confused-deputy guard for a THIRD party assuming a role in your account; the desktop role is assumed only by principals the customer already controls in their own account, so an ExternalId would add a value the customer must copy without adding protection. Its least-privilege property is still tested (exact action set, principal confined to the customer's account).\n3. The spec text is not amended: read this way it already matches the as-built system, and amending it would invalidate nothing but add churn.\n\n### D-013 — AWS host bootstrap is pushed over SSM Run Command after the data volume attaches, not embedded in EC2 UserData; status reports via an EC2 console marker\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Governs WI-10005172 (prerequisite for P-012).\n\nMEASURED [turn:self] (scratch probe .papercusp/scratch/wi10005172-bootstrap-size.mts running renderWorkspaceHostProvisionBootstrap with agent runtimes + hosted connector): the realistic host bootstrap is 52,678 bytes raw and 14,840 bytes gzip -9. EC2 UserData is capped at 16 KiB raw. So the GCP shape (bootstrap embedded in instance startup metadata, 256 KB limit) does not port: raw does not fit at all, and gzip leaves ~1.5 KB before the durable-disk mount preamble is added. Any bootstrap growth would break AWS provisioning silently at RunInstances.\n\nALSO MEASURED: the AWS data volume is created and attached as separate steps AFTER run-instance (aws-provider.ts create-data-volume -> run-instance -> attach-data-volume), so a first-boot script cannot rely on the volume being present, and must identify it by volume id (/dev/disk/by-id/nvme-Amazon_Elastic_Block_Store_vol<hex>), never by guessing, because the mount step runs mkfs on an unformatted device.\n\nRULING:\n1. Delivery: a new AWS apply step after attach-data-volume pushes the bootstrap with SSM Run Command (AWS-RunShellScript). The pushed payload is gzip+base64 of [durable-disk mount for the exact attached volume id] + [controller bootstrap]; a short wrapper decodes it, verifies its sha256, installs it, and starts it as a transient systemd unit so it outlives the Run Command. The step waits for the instance to be SSM-online first (DescribeInstanceInformation). The renderer refuses an encoded payload over a stated ceiling with an error naming it, instead of failing inside AWS.\n2. The durable-disk mount script is shared with GCP: durableFilesystemStartupScript moves out of gcp-provider.ts into a provider-neutral renderer parameterized by device path and wait budget; GCP output stays byte-identical.\n3. Status channel 'ec2-console-output' is added to WORKSPACE_HOST_BOOTSTRAP_STATUS_CHANNELS: report_status writes a marker line to /dev/console; the controller reads GetConsoleOutput (already used for host-key pinning; ec2:GetConsoleOutput is already granted) and parses the LAST marker. resolveAwsSsmOperationsForHost passes this source like GCP passes guest attributes.\n4. Permissions: ssm:SendCommand and ssm:GetCommandInvocation join AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS; the hosted and desktop CloudFormation templates derive from that list, so they follow automatically.\n5. Boot semantics deliberately differ from GCP: the bootstrap runs once per provision and once per repair, not on every boot. The mount script writes fstab entries (nofail), which is what must survive a reboot. GCP's every-boot rerun is itself tracked as a defect (WI-10004242).\n6. Repair consumes the lifecycle-rendered script by re-pushing it over SSM after the repair action.\n\nREJECTED: gzip-only UserData (1.5 KB headroom, measured); a per-organization S3 object with a presigned URL (new bucket, lifecycle, two new SDK dependencies, and a URL that expires with the role session); a Parameter Store parameter (8 KB advanced tier).\n\n### D-014 — P011 independent review preserves current-reader provenance boundary\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self-imposed; turn:self] Measured 2026-10-02 during leader WI-10005203 independent review. WI10005035 closed committed with native artifact2db00a78de92bac3f3619b1f6a648d99b179b1c8155476926121e8afdd23b7a6 and binding20818. Independent raw3/source6 hash comparisons and saved PNG review passed. Same unscoped exact AWSP-P-011-desktop-aws-option@2 input produces PASS/no wouldBlock on3070 evaluatorf52b2457ba, but UNKNOWN/freshness on3271 evaluator3508acc28e. Current-reader bindings20710(run20476441) and20780(run20477833) report test-run-worktree-not-clean;20818 remainsCURRENT. Source packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-evidence-store.ts940-1015 and its conventional dirty/clean classifier tests170-240 establish why: declared file hashes do not pin undeclared dependencies of a dirty test run. Preserve the older PASS as dated evidence and reconcile unit/mutation run provenance against the current maintained reader before claiming root current-build L3. Reuse existing native evidence; no native replay, new acceptance target, actual AWS lifecycle claim or final shipment claim. This records the measured acceptance boundary without changing AWSP-P011 clause@2. Existing member0da received the exact comparison and reconciliation request9db4360a/fef9a7da.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-015 — Every portal workspace gets the D-401 bring-up, BYOC included, and a hosted provision retry carries it too\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Governs P-016 (and P-015 for AWS).\n\nMEASURED [turn:self]: canary host host-0f9b1ba8db30d143becc130a (portal BYOC, project pc-byoc-canary-1002) provisioned successfully at 06:43:51Z (r5), but its customer workspace ws-0f9b1ba8db30d143becc130a is still state='provisioning', the host has bootstrap_version=null, and health is degraded (controller-reach: no ED25519 host key enrolled, because host keys are enrolled only by initialize). Code reading: (1) first-workspace.ts passes bringUp only when hosting === 'papercusp' (comment: 'the customer's own cloud is left as they provisioned it'); hosted-bring-up.ts header says 'an ordinary provision (BYOC, the loopback route, the canary) still ends at the machine'. (2) The hosted browser surface exposes only connection/provision/action; initialize is bg-host loopback only. (3) The hosted provision route (hosted-browser.ts localProvisionRoute.startProvisioning) never sets bringUp, so a RETRY of any failed hosted first provision (WI-10005307 made retries possible) also ends at the bare machine, Papercusp-hosted included.\n\nWHY D-401 did not already cover this: D-401 answered the owner dialog for 'Use Papercusp's cloud' only; portal BYOC had been dropped (predecessor P-044/P-059) and was revived here by P-016. D-401 rule 3 ('never a silent forever-provisioning') is violated by portal BYOC today, and a portal BYOC customer has no controller of their own and no initialize route, so without this the workspace can never become usable.\n\nRULING:\n1. The first-workspace door requests the bring-up for every GCP host it admits, Papercusp-hosted or BYOC. Mechanically the two are identical: both run through a per-org delegation, neither VM holds a service account (gcpFirstWorkspaceDesiredSpec), and only the project differs.\n2. The hosted provision route derives a bring-up SERVER-SIDE when the host it provisions (already authorized as the one bound to the selected customer workspace) is a GCP host and that customer workspace is still 'provisioning'. Never for a workspace that is active/suspended/deleted: re-initializing a used host is not this route's job, and the bring-up's empty-source initialize must never run against a host that already serves a workspace.\n3. AWS portal workspaces (BYOC and P-015 Papercusp-hosted) need the same bring-up over SSM; hostedBringUpInitialization is GCP-only today, so AWS bring-up is P-015/P-012 scope and is filed as its own work item. Until it lands an AWS portal workspace stays 'provisioning' after its machine is built; that is a known, tracked gap, not an accepted behavior.\n4. Requested agents stay PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_BRING_UP_AGENTS (omp); D-250 holds (customers connect their own agent accounts).\n\nAlternative rejected: exposing initialize on the hosted browser surface for the customer to press. It adds a customer-facing step the owner ruled out in D-401 ('no manual step') and a new hosted route to secure.\n\n### D-016 — Hosted provision enqueues via the DBOS client; a provisioned-but-not-brought-up portal host recovers through repair, not a provision retry\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02. Actor: su-4d390264 [self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Refines D-015.\n\nMEASURED [turn:self]: (1) Canary retry r6 (prov-0f9b1ba8db30d143becc130a-r6, posted 07:13Z after the control plane restarted with D-015) reached its DBOS workflow with NO bringUp and NO actorId. dbos.workflow_status inputs for r2..r6 all lack actorId; the original first-workspace provision has it. Cause: the hosted control plane runs no DBOS, so the browser provision route's provisioningAvailable() was false and provision.ts forwarded the RAW request body to the controller's loopback /api/workspace-hosts/provision on bg-host. The server-derived fields (actor, D-015 bring-up) were added only in the local startProvisioning wrapper, which never ran. (2) r6 then ended ERROR with WorkspaceHostControllerFenceError and no operation row: beginWorkspaceHostOperation admits a same-revision provision only as the host's FIRST operation, and r5's provision had SUCCEEDED. (3) readHostedBringUpBinding (used by bringUpHostedHostAgain after repair/upgrade) keys only on an unrevoked connector enrollment, which only the bring-up creates.\n\nRULES: (a) The hosted browser provision route gets the same DBOS-client enqueuer as first-workspace (HostedBrowserRouteDependencies.provisioning; hosted-runtime.ts builds ONE client for both), so a hosted provision is enqueued with its actor and bring-up intact; raw-body forwarding remains only for processes with neither DBOS nor an enqueuer. Implemented 07:25Z with tests (hosted-browser.test.ts). (b) The provision fence is unchanged: a provision retry is a recovery only for a FAILED first provision. (c) A portal host whose provision succeeded but whose bring-up never completed (the canary's state, and the state any bring-up-stage failure leaves) recovers through `repair`: readHostedBringUpBinding falls back to the customer_workspaces binding (kind='hosted', workspace_host_id = host) ONLY while that workspace is 'provisioning', so an empty-source initialize can never run against a workspace that already serves. Tracked as its own work-item. (d) The canary is brought up through rule (c); if repair is not reachable from the hosted action route, destroy the host and re-onboard through first-workspace instead.\n\n### D-017 — P-015 design: AWS on Papercusp Cloud is the hosted customer-role chain with Papercusp's hosting account as the 'customer', confined per host by AWS tag conditions\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223] Decided 2026-10-02 by su-4d390264 while starting P-015.\n\n1. **Hosting account.** One AWS account holds every Papercusp-hosted AWS host: `PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_AWS_WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT_ID`, one region `us-east-1` (`PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_AWS_LOCATION`), so it mirrors GCP's single hosting project and single zone (hosted-gcp-hosting.ts).\n2. **Same infrastructure stack as BYOC.** Papercusp applies the D-009 host-infrastructure stack (VPC, private subnet, security groups, instance profile, launch template, KMS key; hosted-aws-host-stack.ts) ONCE in the hosting account. The server finds it through the same discovery (hosted-aws-host-discovery.ts). No second network model.\n3. **Per-organization hosting role, confined by AWS.** Each organization gets its own role in the hosting account, named with the customer-role prefix (`PapercuspWorkspaceHost-pco-<digest>`), so the existing per-org chain policy (`role/PapercuspWorkspaceHost-*` in any account) already lets the organization's control-plane role assume it and nothing upstream changes. Its trust policy names only that organization's own control-plane role (D-001) and requires the organization's ExternalId (D-007). Its permissions are the workspace-host client's own action list (AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS, already pinned to the SDK commands the client sends), each action classified once in a typed map, so a new action cannot compile unclassified. The classes: describe/quota/pricing calls are unconditional. Every call on an existing machine, disk, snapshot or session requires `aws:ResourceTag/papercusp:host-id` = the reserved host. Creates require `aws:RequestTag/papercusp:host-id` = the reserved host. Tags can only be written at creation. A restore may read only this host's snapshots. iam:PassRole covers only the stack's instance role, passed to EC2. KMS is pinned to the stack key's alias. So AWS itself refuses a change to another tenant's machine even if Papercusp's code named it. The policy is rewritten when a host is reserved, as GCP rewrites its name conditions.\n4. **Papercusp creates it, never the customer.** The control plane writes the hosting role through a hosting-admin role in the hosting account (`PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_AWS_HOSTING_ADMIN_ROLE_ARN`; when unset the hosting account is the control-plane account and the control plane writes it directly). This is the AWS twin of ensurePapercuspHostingGrant. The customer grants nothing, and the browser names nothing: account, region, role and host are all server-derived, exactly as D-399 requires for GCP.\n5. **No new credential source.** The delegation records `{ provider:'aws', accountId:<hosting>, region, source:{ environment:'hosted', method:'customer-role', roleArn:<hosting role>, trustedPrincipalArn, externalIdRef }, papercuspHosted:{ hostId } }`. Credential resolution, verification (including the ExternalId-enforcement probe), provisioning, discovery and the SSM bring-up (WI-10005354: the tunnel runs as the connection's own SDK credentials) are the customer-role code paths unchanged. Additions: the adapter checks that a `papercuspHosted` record names the hosting account and the organization's own hosting role, and the BYOC binding refuses a browser-supplied `papercuspHosted`.\n6. **Selection.** `hosting:'papercusp'` gains a `provider` field (`'gcp'` default, `'aws'`). The one-per-sign-up cap and the hosted bring-up apply unchanged. Cost accounting reuses whatever GCP hosting records, keyed by provider.\n7. **Live proof** needs AWS access to the hosting account, the same wall P-012 sits behind; the code and tests ship regardless.\n\nRejected: a shared Papercusp-wide hosting role with app-level host checks (one bug crosses tenants; D-399 requires the cloud to enforce it); a stack per organization (CloudFormation and VPC quotas, slow first sign-up); a new `papercusp-hosted` credential-source method (it would fork every customer-role code path for no isolation gain).\n\nMeasured: hosted-aws-auth.ts organizationRoleChainPolicy grants sts:AssumeRole on `arn:<p>:iam::*:role/PapercuspWorkspaceHost-*`; aws-provider.ts tags every instance, volume and snapshot with AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_MANAGED_TAG_KEYS.hostId (`papercusp:host-id`) via TagSpecifications at creation (RunInstances instance+volume, CreateVolume, CreateSnapshot), and no standalone CreateTags call exists in aws-sdk-client.ts.\n\n### D-018 — P-015 cost accounting: AWS hosted reuses GCP hosting's per-host attribution; an unconfigured AWS hosting account is a distinct non-retryable refusal\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1223] Decided by su-4d390264 at P-015 step 5. Refines D-017 rule 6.\n\nMEASURED [turn:self]: GCP hosting records no provider-specific cost ledger. Its accounting is (a) managed labels papercusp-managed / papercusp-host-id / papercusp-workspace-id on instance, disk and snapshot (gcp-safety.ts GCP_WORKSPACE_HOST_MANAGED_LABEL_KEYS), which Cloud Billing export attributes per host; (b) the provider price estimate in the safety preflight, which for GCP is confidence 'unknown', hourlyAmount 0 (gcp-api-client.ts estimatePrice); (c) the provider-agnostic Stripe organization subscription. admitHostedLifecycleJob (workspace_host_operations.estimated_cost_cents keyed by provider_target) has no production caller.\n\nRULING: AWS hosted cost accounting is the same three things, unchanged: (a) AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_MANAGED_TAG_KEYS carries the same three identities as tags written only at creation (hosting policy TagOnlyAtCreation); (b) the AWS Price List estimate (aws-sdk-client.ts estimatePrice, real on-demand compute + EBS figures) runs under the hosting role, which keeps pricing:GetProducts in its Observe statement; (c) Stripe, unchanged. Pinned by hosted-aws-hosting.test.ts 'keeps cost accounting at GCP parity'. One AWS-only ops step: AWS cost-allocation tags must be ACTIVATED in the hosting account's payer (Billing console or ce:UpdateCostAllocationTagsStatus) before papercusp:host-id / papercusp:workspace-id appear in Cost Explorer; GCP labels need no activation. That step needs AWS access to the hosting account, the same wall as P-012 and D-017 rule 7.\n\nAlso: a deployment without PAPERCUSP_HOSTED_AWS_WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT_ID now throws HostedAwsHostingUnconfiguredError, which first-workspace maps to papercusp_cloud_provider_unavailable (503, retryable:false, nothing recorded) instead of delegation_source_unavailable (retryable), so a person who picks AWS is told to choose Google Cloud rather than to keep retrying.\n\nRejected: wiring admitHostedLifecycleJob into hosted provisioning for AWS only (GCP does not use it; that would be new accounting, not parity).\nRelated: P-015\n\n### D-019 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-02\nAmendment-Id: amend-81fa4f0c0d7bfe5198e0fbd8\nRequest-Hash: 6290ce1e25d2de8ab3fad7b0beddab039c112d2c5e9f5906c90fc88c417c8b9a\nActor: su-4d390264-fc3c-4875-a655-a71b0afcd6ef\nReason: Add BARs R-10 (P-015 AWS on Papercusp Cloud), R-11 (P-016 GCP bring-your-own-cloud portal workspace activates) and R-12 (P-017 J5 outage continuity). These three items were added to the plan after rubric revision 1 was authored (owner directive #1232 put P-015/P-016 in v1 scope per D-004; P-017 moved in from byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22#D-445), so the acceptance bar did not yet cover them. Existing R-1..R-9 are unchanged.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-4765bb1b-9000-4373-a3ba-7a01d70ac4a4\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1155439\nApproved-At: 2026-10-02T10:45:24.464Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 66 → 67\nChanged BARs: R-10, R-11, R-12\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-020 — R-9 live AWS canary scope: eight numbered parts, a three-kind per-host census with positive controls, reboot descoped\nDate: 2026-10-02\nSource: acceptance-rubric vetting conv-muque0el (posts 1155446, 1155448), applied in rubric rev 3 [self-imposed, AUTO]. Measured in source 2026-10-02.\n\n1. R-9 enumerates the canary as numbered parts, one evidence ref each; any missing part prevents healthy: (1) connect + preflight; (2) provision + initialise over SSM; (3) stop/start with the connector heartbeat back; (4) snapshot, then restore onto a new instance with the original terminated, data written before and read after; (5) AMI upgrade to the shipped release plus rollback by a second upgrade, naming both AMI ids; (6) revoke the delegation, observe the provider refuse to act while revoked, then reconnect and act again; (7) a 60-minute soak with connector heartbeats and no service restart (parity with the GCP soak); (8) destroy + census. ExternalId rotation is not a part: D-007 derives the ExternalId from the organization, and it is stable across rotations (hosted-aws-identity.ts).\n2. Census kinds = instance, volume, snapshot. These are every resource the AWS client creates per host (RunInstances, CreateVolume, CreateSnapshot in aws-sdk-client.ts; it creates no security group, Elastic IP, ENI beyond the instance's own, SSM association or AMI) and they equal AWS_WORKSPACE_HOST_CENSUS_RESOURCE_KINDS (aws-safety.ts). Security group, instance profile, KMS key and launch template belong to the customer's CloudFormation stack (D-009); AMIs come from the release pipeline (aws-ami-production.ts). Both are out of the per-host census by design, and R-9 says so.\n3. The census must carry POSITIVE CONTROLS: a non-zero control count taken with the same filter shape, and proof the torn-down hosts existed (their create or restore operations succeeded before destroy). A vacuous zero is not clean. A destroy operation that ends failed after deleting everything passes only on a clean census plus a filed work-item for the failure.\n4. Reboot is descoped from R-9, mirroring sibling byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22 D-447: hosted boot re-runs the bootstrap and restarts papercusp-workspace about 3 minutes after boot (WI-10004242), and AWS hosts run the same bootstrap.\n5. Spend reconciliation for the canary window is not a part. Per-host cost attribution is graded on the tree plane (R-10, D-018), and AWS billing data lags the run by hours, so a spend part could not be graded at run time.\n6. Release identity is bytes: receipts pin the AMI id and the bundle sha256 (workspace_hosts.runtime_release.bundleSha256) the host ran. Receipts are point-in-time; a host re-pinned later does not fail the bar.\n7. R-6 is narrowed to the tree plane (cap refusal + the teardown call plan over those three kinds); its live proof is R-9's census.\n\n### D-021 — Rubric rev 3: R-10/R-11 narrowed to their seams, J5 (R-12) proven on GCP only, new live R-13 for the normal-path agent task on AWS\nDate: 2026-10-02\nSource: acceptance-rubric vetting conv-muque0el (posts 1155446, 1155448) [self-imposed, AUTO].\n\n1. R-10 and R-11 stated live product outcomes on tree-plane checks. Narrowed to what their tests prove: R-10 = the hosted-AWS placement selects the configured hosting account, emits the host-id and workspace-id tags, and refuses an unconfigured hosting account; R-11 = bring-up activates a portal workspace on a customer GCP project after provision success, retry included. P-016's live portal run (WI-10005297) is cited as supplementary evidence only. Each scope item names its describe/it block so a spot-check is a lookup (also done for R-2).\n2. R-12 (J5 outage continuity, moved here from the sibling plan by its D-445) is proven on a GCP host only. The drill blocks the host's egress with a GCP VPC firewall rule on the host network; there is no AWS mechanism (a security-group or NACL block) yet. R-12 therefore names the GCP host and claims no AWS coverage and no product-path release (the drill releases a gated test agent). The AWS drill is a filed follow-up, not part of this plan's bar.\n3. New live BAR R-13 (P-012): one Claude task and one OMP task on an AWS host, released through the product path (portal / connector, not SSH exec), each with its own task receipt and verified output. A readiness or marker probe does not satisfy it. This closes the gap that made the sibling plan's R-5 ungradable: parity of use, not only of provisioning.\n4. Live bars R-9, R-12 and R-13 use check {kind:'instrument', instrumentKey:'none'}: missing, stale or documentary-only output rates unknown or broken, the grader reconciles every operation id against workspace_host_operations and every task receipt against the release task ledger, and any vitest file is supplementary.\n\nMeasured: outage-drill receipt docs/evidence/j5-outage-drill-2026-10-02.json config = {project pc-byoc-canary-1002, network pc-host-19ff2a97befd83b51d2306fd-324ccce1-net, ruleName pc-j5-outage-drill-…}; Re-check whether any of those parts call AssumeRole under root before relying on it.\n\n### D-026 — P-012 part 5 images: two AMI releases from ONE bake. A = r62b bundle (0.0.21-p318r62b), B = r63 bundle (0.0.21-p318r63, the shipped release)\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 [turn:self].\n\n1. Part 5 needs two distinct papercusp-shaped AMIs. Lifecycle upgrade takes a target image, and rollbackImage defaults to the image the host is recorded as running (packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/lifecycle-runner.ts effectiveRollbackImage). A stock AMI would exercise a host shape we never ship.\n2. An AWS release names its AMI papercusp-workspace-host-<artifact.image.version> (aws-ami-release.ts). bootc-image-release-request-cli forces image.version to the server bundle's publication-manifest version. So one bake can yield two distinct releases by pointing release-input.json publicationManifest at two different trusted bundle publications. Measured 22:1xZ: ~/.papercusp/wh-release-r62b/publication/manifest.json has version 0.0.21-p318r62b with trustReport.trusted=true. r63 is 0.0.21-p318r63.\n3. Ruling: release A first (bake + r62b), then B (bake + r63) with deprecatePreviousAt. Each version gets its own clean-room run, because the clean-room report binds image.id@version. The canary provisions on A, upgrades to B (the shipped release), then rolls back with a second upgrade to A. Both AMI ids go on WI-10005036.\n4. Rejected: cutting a new r64 bundle (~55 min of release-cut per the r63 log, and no added coverage) and keeping a transient clean-room AMI as A (unencrypted and never released through the gate).\n5. Residue: both AMIs carry the same OS bytes, so part 5 proves the upgrade/rollback MECHANISM and the AMI-identity swap, not an OS-content change. The controller-pinned bundle installed by Initialize is independent of the AMI either way.\n\n### D-027 — bootc trust gate: a fixed finding in an RPM-owned file is vendor-pending (reported, not denied) only when the bake proves no newer RPM exists\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 on measured evidence; implementation tracked as WI-10005719.\n\n1. Evidence (measured 22:50-22:55Z on bake p012-aws-bake-20261002t213107z): GRYPE_ACTIONABLE_CRIT_HIGH_WITH_FIX=123 (rpm 14, go-module 109) under the D-289 filter; the prior bake had 102 under the same filter. Every flagged /usr Go binary is owned by an installed RPM (rpm -qf in the built image: skopeo-1.22.2-4.el9, podman-5.8.5-2.el9, google-guest-agent-20260921.00-g1.el9). `dnf -q --refresh check-update` in the built image exited 0, so the configured repos hold nothing newer. 69 findings sit in /sysroot/ostree/repo/objects: base-image copies of binaries the Containerfile dnf upgrade replaced in /usr (e.g. skopeo go1.26.3 object vs /usr/bin/skopeo go1.26.5). artifact-trust.ts has a single deny threshold and no waiver. As built, no CentOS Stream bootc image can pass while the vendor lags upstream Go fixes, and none ever has.\n\n2. Ruling: a fixed Critical/High finding remains ACTIONABLE (denied) unless BOTH hold: (a) the finding's file is owned by an installed RPM, recorded at bake time (syft ownership relationship or an rpm -qf census), and (b) the bake recorded `dnf check-update` exit 0 against the same repos in the built image. Such a finding is classified vendorPending: excluded from the deny population, but counted and listed in the trust report and the supply-chain summary, never dropped silently. The bake fails closed when check-update exits 100 (updates available) or errors, so a fix the vendor HAS shipped can never be classified pending.\n\n3. Anything papercusp builds or installs outside RPM (/opt/papercusp, bundled node/pip/go binaries) stays fully actionable, unchanged.\n\n4. The stale /sysroot/ostree/repo objects are NOT covered by this ruling (no installed RPM owns them). DEFERRED until the phase-4 AWS disk is inspected: if they do not ship, or are unreachable from the deployed commit, exclude them by evidence. If they ship, remove them at build time. Either way, a separate decision.\n\n5. Mirrored exactly in release-supply-chain.sh and bootc-image-release-request-cli.ts (the D-289 pattern), with focused tests and a mutation probe on each copy.\n\nRejected: zero tolerance on vendor binaries (unpassable, which pushes releases toward unrecorded force-ships); rebuilding vendor binaries (forks the distro); a free-form waiver list (hand-maintained, drifts, and could hide a fix the vendor already shipped).\n\n### D-028 — D-027 refinement: what counts as vendor-owned, and where ownership comes from\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 while implementing D-027 (WI-10005719).\n\n1. Ownership comes from the attested SBOM itself, not a separate rpm -qf census: syft records each INSTALLED rpm at the rpm database (/usr/share/rpm/rpmdb.sqlite on the bootc image) with its files in metadata.files. Measured on bake p012-aws-bake-20261002t213107z: 39,807 owned paths, including /usr/bin/skopeo and /usr/bin/podman; no ostree object is owned.\n2. A finding is vendor-owned when its artifact IS an installed rpm (type rpm, every location in the rpmdb), or when every location path is owned by an installed rpm. D-027 (a) said \"file owned by an installed RPM\"; rpm-type findings (14 on this bake: openssl, gnupg2, libcap, libevent, sqlite-libs, python3-urllib3, in redhat:distro) are the package itself, so the same rule applies to them. An .rpm ARCHIVE lying in the image is type rpm but not located in the rpmdb, so it neither counts as installed nor vouches for the files it lists.\n3. Only Critical/High findings are reclassified, the same population the gate denies.\n4. (b) is recorded as vendor-updates.json {digest, verdict, containerExit, checkUpdateExit, enabledRepos, availablePackages}. The release gate (TS) accepts it only for the bake digest, with containerExit 0, checkUpdateExit 0, >=1 enabled repo and >=1000 available packages under its OWN floor (a dnf with no repos also exits 0). A record for another digest refuses outright. If the summary records a vendorPending count and the TS derivation disagrees, the release refuses (copies-disagree guard).\n5. Effect on this bake: 123 actionable -> 54 vendor-pending + 69 actionable, all 69 in /sysroot/ostree/repo/objects (still governed by D-027 item 4).\n\n### D-029 — D-029: ostree-object findings are relocated to their live path, or classified stale base objects (resolves D-027 item 4)\nDate: 2026-10-02\nDate: 2026-10-02\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 on measured evidence (WI-10005719, comment 23:2xZ; /mnt/data/papercusp-bake/wi10005719/ostree-reachability.log).\n\n1. Evidence: the rendered AWS disk (bake aws-20261002t213107z, partition 4 mounted read-only) holds all 5 flagged objects in /ostree/repo/objects. Against deployed commit c8d482d2: 4 (00ed9dec, 0d38a080, 4fc5d859, 9eeca1cb; 49 findings) are NOT in the deployed tree. They are old podman/skopeo/quadlet/rootlessport copies held only by retained container layer refs. 1 (83de1547; 20 findings) IS deployed: /usr/bin/toolbox, a live base binary syft located at the object because the base layer hardlinks the live path to it.\n2. Ruling: the supply-chain step probes the image at the released digest (same container as the D-027 dnf check). For each fixed Crit/High finding located at /sysroot/ostree/repo/objects/xx/<62hex>.file it finds every file outside /sysroot with identical content (size-filtered sha256). A live copy RELOCATES the finding to that path, and D-027/D-028 ownership applies there. No live copy makes it a STALE BASE OBJECT: excluded from the deny population, counted (GRYPE_STALE_BASE_OBJECTS) and listed (stale-base-objects.json). It is not on any PATH and not in the deployed tree, and the build already ships the newer copy.\n3. Fail-closed: the probe counts only when the container exits 0, emits its end marker, and gives every object a verdict. Otherwise nothing is relocated or stale. The release gate (TS) uses ostree-objects.json only for the bake digest and only when complete, and cross-checks the summary count.\n4. Rejected: removing the objects at build time (they are base-layer content; a derived-layer whiteout does not remove the retained layer refs on disk) and pruning layer refs post-install (breaks incremental upgrades).\n\n### D-030 — Corrects D-026: on the bootc model each AMI release needs its OWN bake with that release baked in (--release-root/--release-version); one OS-only bake cannot yield releases A and B\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 on measured evidence (WI-10005761).\n\n1. D-026 item 2 was a false premise. It is true only of the LABEL: bootc-image-release-request-cli sets image.version from the publication manifest. It is not true of the image CONTENT. On hostModel bootc-image the bootstrap never installs a release; it requires /opt/papercusp/releases/<version> to exist in the booted image (libs/generic/deployment-driver/src/workspace-host-bootstrap.ts, the 'not present in the booted image' die). infra/images/bootc/bake-cloud-images.sh bakes a release in only with --release-root DIR --release-version V (workspace-host.Containerfile RELEASE_DIR block).\n2. Measured 2026-10-03 00:58Z: clean rooms A5 (r62b) and B2 (r63) on bake aws-20261002t213107z passed harden-os (WI-10005754 fixed) and both died at install-runtime: 'release 0.0.21-p318r62b is not present in the booted image'. bake.log has 0 '--release-root' hits: that bake is OS-only (D-024). Teardown clean.\n3. Ruling: bake twice, A = --release-root <extracted r62b vm-release tree> --release-version 0.0.21-p318r62b, B = the same for r63. Each bake gets its own supply-chain, secret-scan and trust report, then its own clean room, request and publish. Part 5 then also proves an image-content change (two different release trees), which removes D-026 item 5's residue.\n4. Detector gap: the request CLI must refuse pairing a bake that does not carry the publication's release version, before any clean-room spend (WI-10005761).\n5. Unchanged from D-026: A first, then B with deprecatePreviousAt; the canary provisions on A, upgrades to B (the shipped release r63), and rolls back to A.\n\n### D-031 — R-13 rescoped to GCP's proven level of agent use; product-path task dispatch moves to WI-10005792 because no GCP customer-cloud host has it either\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, under owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 [turn:self] on measured evidence; amends D-021 item 3.\n\n1. Evidence (03:00-03:10Z): routes/workspace-hosts/ has 12 routes (action, agent-credentials, audit, aws-setup-template, byoc-client-key, canary, connection, credential-lifecycle, desktop-pack, initialize, provision, soak) and none dispatches an agent task; canary is fixed-agent-initialization readiness. Consult conv-mursuxqd: reviewer 1 (post 1156649) found no product dispatch path; reviewer 2 (post 1156659) showed one exists (blueprint:submit over hosted-app-relay.ts; also launch-su via the portal owner-plane relay and the relay-carried psu session) but it has run only against a relay-linked local install, an isolated install and Papercusp-hosted avi-test, never a customer-cloud host. GCP's record: the P-318 desktop-BYOC canary proved credentials + readiness; the P-016 portal BYOC canary (WI-10005297) proved provision/bring-up/stop/start/snapshot/destroy with no agent task; the J5 drill (R-12) ran a gated agent task controller-pushed over IAP SSH.\n2. So D-021's R-13 (product-path task with a per-task receipt) asked for more than GCP has. That is new capability, not parity, which is what #1223 asked for. It moves to WI-10005792 (assigned su-4d390264), cross-cloud, with its preconditions (relay-linking a bg-host-provisioned host, WI-10004446 key mint, per-task backend choice).\n3. R-13 (rubric rev 4) becomes: on the AWS canary host running the shipped release, for EACH of Claude and OMP: (a) the agent-credential bundle for that slot is delivered through POST /workspace-hosts/:hostId/agent-credentials (Claude from a real source; OMP as the credential-free 'absent' slot it is by contract, since it runs on the host's local inference, D-230); (b) the fixed-agent-initialization canary (requestedAgents claude+omp) records a ready agent-verification receipt for that kind that agent-credential admission accepts (Claude: live-inference or authenticated-account; OMP: authenticated-account only, agent-credential-admission.ts isReadyAgentVerificationEvidence); (c) one gated agent task (outage-drill.ts agentTaskPrompt/gateReleaseCommand: the agent reads a secret released through a gate FIFO and writes sha256(secret)) completes with output equal to the expected digest. (a) and (b) cite operation ids reconciled against workspace_host_operations; (c) runs through outage-drill-cli.ts --cloud aws over SSM, with no egress block, and is labelled controller-pushed. The bar does not claim product-path dispatch.\n4. Why keep (c) although it runs over SSM: it is the only code that proves an agent finishes real work on the host with output that cannot be produced from the prompt, and it is what GCP proved (R-12). (a)+(b) alone are the readiness probe D-021 rejected.\n5. Falsified if: either kind lacks (a), (b) or a (c) digest match; the (c) secret appears in the prompt or a file name; or the evidence claims product-path dispatch.\n\nMeasured: ls packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/workspace-hosts/ (12 non-test routes, 03:00Z); grep -nE \"task_ledger|receipt\" outage-drill.ts outage-drill-cli.ts = 0 hits; agent-credential-admission.ts:156,184 (omp may not use live-inference); agent-credential-source-selector.ts:77 (absent valid only for omp); hosted-bring-up.ts:50 (omp verifies against local inference).\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-032 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-03\nAmendment-Id: amend-fddbf55682bdf3e0ce69de8a\nRequest-Hash: f80343575365cfaa14470159c38253d69adf7e91c96d5ddb3f300f65cda8e7f7\nActor: su-4d390264-fc3c-4875-a655-a71b0afcd6ef\nReason: D-031: R-13 rescoped to GCP's proven level of agent use\nApproved-By: su-003ee5ae-bedb-4bce-83e6-c64d6235f3f0\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1156675\nApproved-At: 2026-10-03T03:10:25.499Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 91 → 92\nChanged BARs: R-13\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-033 — R-13 gated task (c) is Claude-only; OMP keeps (a)+(b) with its local-inference receipt; OMP tool work moves to WI-10005804 (amends D-031 item 3)\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, under owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 [turn:self] on measured evidence; amends D-031 item 3.\n\n1. Parity evidence [observed]: before WI-10005796, outage-drill.ts (blob at 61ea9e254d) invoked only `<cli> -p <prompt> --allowedTools Bash,Write`, i.e. Claude. GCP's J5 drill (R-12) therefore proved a gated task for Claude and never for OMP. D-031 item 3 required part (c) for OMP as well, which asked for more than GCP has, the same over-reach D-031 itself corrected.\n2. Capability evidence [observed, 03:16-03:27Z, WI-10005804]: with the host-identical OMP agent home (only ~/.omp/agent/models.yml from WORKSPACE_HOST_AGENT_HOME_OMP_LOCAL_MODELS_YML, env -i, local ollama serving WORKSPACE_HOST_OMP_LOCAL_MODEL qwen2.5-coder:0.5b, argv from agentTaskInvocation('omp')), omp returns a final answer without issuing a tool call: 1/1 direct task and 3/3 gated tasks fail; ollama logs exactly one chat completion per run. So no customer-cloud host, GCP or AWS, can run an OMP tool-using task today. That is a cross-cloud product defect (WI-10005804), not an AWS parity gap.\n3. D-031's (b) wording for OMP was also wrong: it cited agent-credential admission (authenticated-account only for omp). A credential-free OMP slot proves readiness by local inference, and the canary evidence validator derives the allowed kinds from the probe table (workspaceHostAgentAllowedVerificationKinds, workspace-host-agent-authentication.ts): Claude live-inference, OMP local-inference. GCP's canary recorded exactly claude=live-inference / omp=local-inference.\n4. R-13 (rubric rev 6) becomes: on the AWS canary host running the shipped release, (a) for each of Claude and OMP the agent-credential bundle for that slot is delivered through POST /workspace-hosts/:hostId/agent-credentials (Claude from a real source; OMP as the credential-free absent slot); (b) the fixed-agent-initialization canary (requestedAgents claude+omp) records a ready agent-verification receipt for each kind that the canary evidence validator accepts (Claude live-inference, OMP local-inference); (c) one gated Claude task through outage-drill-cli.ts --cloud aws --mode task (agentTaskPrompt/gateReleaseCommand, no egress block, labelled controller-pushed over SSM) completes with output equal to the expected digest. (a) and (b) cite operation ids reconciled against workspace_host_operations.\n5. The OMP gated-task mode built in WI-10005796 stays: it is the instrument WI-10005804's recurrence guard needs.\n6. Decided by su-4d390264 on measured evidence (WI-10005910). Supersedes the self-imposed 'no image-content edits until the canary' rule: the chain3 images cannot run the release, so new bakes are required regardless.\n\n1. Evidence [observed 07:36Z]: chain3 clean room A (r62b) passed configure-service's install (WI-10005830 fixed and closed) and died at the papercusp-workspace.service restart. rocksdb-native@3.15.1's prebuild needs GLIBCXX_3.4.30; EL9 ships libstdc++ 11.5 (up to 3.4.29).\n2. Only rocksdb-native exceeds EL9 today (objdump over bin/node + 11 .node files), but any future prebuild or source-built addon can raise the floor again.\n3. Measured alternatives (.papercusp/scratch/wi10005910/load-probe.sh, /mnt/data/papercusp-bake/wi-glibcxx/): (a) built image A (EL9) reproduces GLIBCXX_3.4.30 in ~20 s (the control); (b) centos-bootc:stream10 + libatomic (glibc 2.39, libstdc++ 14.4.1) loads 11/11 addons; (c) every Containerfile package resolves on stream10 + EPEL 10 + the Google el10 repo except zlib, which EL10 provides as zlib-ng-compat; (d) bundling a newer libstdc++ in the release is rejected: the build host's copy needs GLIBC_2.38 (> 2.34), and a portable glibc-2.17 build (conda-forge) adds an unpackaged third-party binary invisible to the RPM SBOM/grype gate and needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH on every process that runs the release's node.\n4. Ruling: the base becomes quay.io/centos-bootc/centos-bootc:stream10 for the multi-cloud image (AWS, and the GCP/Azure renders of the same Containerfile). Changes: Containerfile FROM/ARG; Google repo el9 -> el10; zlib -> zlib-ng-compat; WORKSPACE_HOST_BOOTC_BASE_IMAGE (bootstrap bootc-base-image check); the supply-chain gate's vendor-kernel CPE rule generalised from .el9 to .el<N> (release-request CLI + release-supply-chain.sh mirror) with tests. Tool-only skopeo containers and the historical p30x probes keep stream9.\n5. This class then fails in minutes at bake time instead of ~1h later in a clean room. Covered by the bake test harness.\n6. Then rebake A (r62b) and B (r63) per D-030, run clean rooms, publish, and resume the canary (WI-10005036).\n\n### D-036 — Corrects D-035 item 'packages resolve': the Google el10 repo needs the v10 signing key; D-035's feasibility probe ran with gpgcheck=0\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, under owner directive #1223]. That probe (.papercusp/scratch/wi10005910/feasibility.sh) wrote the repo with gpgcheck=0, so it never exercised signature verification.\n2. Evidence [observed 08:29Z]: chain4 try 1 bake A died at STEP 17/35: 'Key import failed (code 3). Failing package is: google-guest-agent ... el10', 'Error: GPG check FAILED'. Probe (.papercusp/scratch/wi10005910/gce-gpg-probe.sh, log /mnt/data/papercusp-bake/wi-glibcxx/gce-gpg-probe.log): EL10 rpm (sequoia, DEFAULT crypto policy) rejects rpm-package-key.gpg (F09C394C3E1BA8D5: 'Policy rejected non-revocation signature ... requiring second pre-image resistance', i.e. SHA-1). rpm-package-key-v10.gpg ('Google Cloud v10 RPM Package Signing Key v1', b64936f9) installs google-guest-agent, google-compute-engine and google-compute-engine-oslogin with gpgcheck=1; all three are RSA/SHA256 signed by 3156c631b64936f9.\n3. Decision: the Containerfile's Google repo uses gpgkey=rpm-package-key-v10.gpg only, gpgcheck=1 unchanged. Do NOT weaken to gpgcheck=0 or a crypto-policy downgrade.\n4. Lesson: a feasibility probe must mirror the real config's verification settings; a relaxed probe proves less than it reads.\n\n### D-037 — AWS restore and upgrade are unimplemented in the provider; implement them (WI-10005971) before canary parts 4-5; parts 1-3 proceed on current code\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, under owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 [turn:self] on measured evidence.\n\n1. Evidence [observed 11:50Z]: packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/aws-provider.ts declares lifecycle { restore: false, upgrade: false } with the constraint 'Restore and in-place image upgrades are not yet supported', and plan() throws for both actions. No wrapper (aws-configured-provider.ts) or test adds them; no plan item or open work-item implemented them. GCP implements both (gcp-provider.ts planRestore, planUpgrade).\n2. Consequence: P-012 parts (4) and (5) cannot pass on the product path, so R-9 cannot be met, and GCP parity (the plan goal) is short two lifecycle actions. The plan text assumed them; it never scheduled them. This is a planning omission, not a descope.\n3. Resolution: implement AWS restore (data volume from snapshot + new instance from the desired AMI + attach + SSM bootstrap) and upgrade (recreate the instance from the target AMI keeping the data volume; rollback is a second upgrade), mirroring GCP's step, resource and checkpoint semantics; flip the descriptor flags; unit tests in aws-provider.test.ts. Tracked as WI-10005971 (bug, assigned su-4d390264), linked blocks WI-10005036. The AMIs need no rebake (the provider runs on the controller); bg-host :3271 must be reloaded onto the fix before parts 4-5, and the canary's contractApproval reportRef (aws-provider.test.ts test run) is re-pinned to a run that includes the new cases.\n4. Sequencing: canary parts 1-3 run on current code as soon as AMI A publishes; parts 4-5 wait for WI-10005971; parts 6-8 follow.\n\n### D-038 — AWS restore/upgrade design (WI-10005971): RunInstances names ImageId+InstanceType; upgrade is destructive-LAST replacement; host registry is latest-row-per-identity\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, under owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 [turn:self] from code reading; implements D-037.\n\n1. Finding [observed in code, 12:05Z]: AwsRunInstancesInput carries no ImageId and no InstanceType, and the customer stack's launch template sets only MetadataOptions (aws-customer-setup-template.ts; setup-template.served.json LaunchTemplateData keys = [MetadataOptions]). So desired.image and desired.size never reach EC2, and canary part 2 (provision) would fail at RunInstances. Not yet observed live; the fake client in aws-provider.test.ts accepts any input. Fix: run requests set ImageId = desired.image.id (ami- format checked) and InstanceType = desired.size, for provision, restore and upgrade.\n2. Restore = provision of request.desired (a distinct hostId) whose data volume is CreateVolume{SnapshotId}. The snapshot must be target aws, belong to the source host, be completed, and carry the managed host tag (mirrors GCP's READY + assertManagedHostResource).\n3. Upgrade keeps the old instance until the new one works (destructive LAST), unlike GCP's delete-first, because an AWS data volume is attached after launch and the bootstrap is pushed over SSM, so a one-step rollback cannot rebuild a host: stop old -> detach data volume -> run new (target AMI, same launch settings from the host's recorded desired spec + connection) -> attach -> bootstrap -> terminate old. detach is destructive:true, so a run-instance failure is stranded-by-failure and its precomputed rollback re-attaches the volume to the old instance and starts it. Rollback by a second upgrade (canary part 5) is the ordinary path.\n4. The lifecycle runner passes the host's recorded desired spec on the upgrade plan request (new optional WorkspaceHostPlanRequest.upgrade.desired; GCP ignores it).\n5. Registry: an AWS replacement gets a NEW instance id, so the old id stays applied on its provision-era row. readWorkspaceHostDestroyTarget therefore registers an identity iff its LATEST row (updated_at) is applied/unchanged, and the lifecycle runner observes the live set (plan-order checkpoint overlay), not the start-of-turn list. GCP's same-name recreate is unaffected (its latest row is the re-insert).\n6. Residue: a failure after run-instance applied (attach/bootstrap) fails the op with the old instance stopped and detached; recovery is a repair or second upgrade, which refuses an ambiguous instance set rather than guessing. To be filed as a follow-up.\n\n### D-039 — P-012 part 8 census: the canary snapshot is deleted as a recorded customer teardown step, because no lifecycle path deletes a workspace-host snapshot on either cloud (WI-10005987)\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, under owner directive #1223]. Decided by su-4d390264 [turn:self] from code reading; refines D-020 items 2-3 for part 8.\n\n1. Finding [observed in code, 12:57Z]: LIFECYCLE_ACTIONS = start|stop|restart|repair|snapshot|upgrade|restore. Neither gcp-provider.ts nor aws-provider.ts plans any snapshot deletion, and AWS planDestroy only CREATES a snapshot for a non-discard disposition. The only DeleteSnapshot call in the tree is AMI production. Workspace-host snapshots are therefore customer-retained on BOTH clouds. This is not an AWS parity gap; it is a product gap for both, filed as WI-10005987.\n2. Consequence: canary part 4's snapshot (tagged to host A) outlives the destroys of A and B, so a census of all three D-020 kinds cannot reach zero through the product alone.\n3. Rule: part 8 destroys host B through the product (discard). The driver then deletes the canary snapshot(s) as an explicit customer step (aws ec2 delete-snapshot through the operator-role session, the same permission the connection grants). It records the ids and the delete responses, and only then runs the census over instance, volume and snapshot. The census keeps snapshots in scope with positive controls (D-020 item 3): a non-zero pre-destroy count under the same tag filter, plus the provision (A) and restore (B) operations that succeeded.\n4. The grader should read the snapshot deletion as customer teardown of retained backups, not as the product's destroy removing them; R-9 part 8 is healthy on a zero census with this step recorded.\n\n### D-040 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-03\nAmendment-Id: aws-parity-rubric-rev7-r6-r9-r13\nRequest-Hash: 1d729ab9e52773a980e511bac4788f79548a64f9a86581f2774b23abf70b194e\nActor: su-4d390264-fc3c-4875-a655-a71b0afcd6ef\nReason: Rev 6 vetting (consult conv-musf7mm6, two concurring outside-lineage reviewers): R-6 named a snapshot teardown no lifecycle path performs (D-039) and its check file exercised neither clause, so it now binds provision.test.ts + aws-provider.test.ts over instances and volumes; R-9 part (8) names the discard disposition and the recorded customer delete-snapshot step; R-13's model drops its rationale sentence (moved to method) and its method names the real credential-delivery evidence.\nApproved-By: su-df2c1cbd-8d0c-4c9e-aaa0-261bfa1e6ff4\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1157451\nApproved-At: 2026-10-03T13:42:46.124Z\nRubric revision: 6 → 7\nSubject plan revision: 105 → 106\nChanged BARs: R-6, R-9, R-13\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-041 — Acceptance rubric rev 7: R-6 covers instances and volumes only, R-9 part 8 names the discard disposition and the customer snapshot delete, R-13 model is one outcome sentence\nDate: 2026-10-03\nDate: 2026-10-03\nSource: [self-imposed, AUTO, under owner directive #1223].\nDecided by su-4d390264 on the rev 6 vetting consult conv-musf7mm6 (two concurring outside-lineage reviewers, su-dd6a0ba4 and su-0c1c998d).\nDecision turn: [turn:f9d4ca4f@2026-10-03T13:42:46.605Z]\nOutside approval: su-df2c1cbd, thread-post:1157451, on preview thread-post:1157447 (WI-10005036).
