Cover shell/navigation, workspace/… <!-- P-016 -->\n## Background\n\nAvi asked for a live tutorial for users of app.papercusp.com, requested a thorough online search of suitable libraries, and then asked to save the findings as a plan and show a detailed summary. The proposed product is a persistent “Guide me” panel that teaches users while they perform real work in the app.\n\nOwner source references:\n- session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1 — “I think we need to create something that gives users of our cloud app at app.papercusp.com a live tutorial, how can we do that?”\n- session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:4 — “do a thorugh online search what other libraries should we use for this?”\n- session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:8 — “write this into a plan and show me the detailed summary”\n- session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:7 — the library research report; agent-authored recommendations, not owner ratification.\n\nRelated existing work: agent-first-onboarding-2026-07-03. The plan-aware duplicate check also returned hive-frame-desktops-live-view-2026-06-06, byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22, and unified-web-portal-2026-08-29. Their source bodies and tutorial-related items were reviewed: they own desktop streaming, provider/workspace lifecycle onboarding, and portal composition; this is a distinct instructional feature, consuming those capabilities rather than replacing them. Reuse its curriculum and tutorial-pack machinery where they fit. The browser cloud tutorial has a distinct target surface; do not transplant the desktop PTY-based Onboarding Console or reactivate that plan’s release lane.\n\n## Scope\n\nApproved product direction: the tutorial is the first product experience immediately after authenticated account creation and teaches the full product, not only Cloud setup (D-023). It must be available before a cloud connection, machine selection, payment or AI/microphone permission, including newly created accounts with a preassigned workspace. Returning users retain deliberate resume/Help/replay and exit controls. The full scope, measured product inventory and proposed acceptance/work mapping are recorded in D-024 and WI-10004837#comment:1161175; D-025 authorizes the minimal portal entry/mount/authenticated-progress seam and exactly one independent BAR reviewer. The preserving full-product amendment is now applied as rubric revision 10 and plan revision 103 using authenticated approval thread-post:1162484 of preview thread-post:1162450; P-014/P-015/P-016 and P-013 are the registered SELF implementation lanes. This authorizes only the minimal existing-portal seam, not a portal rewrite.\n\nThe existing “Get your first agent running” journey remains one curriculum module, preserving D-005's GCP-first connection/configuration, reviewed costs, explicit provisioning or selection of a usable existing workspace, chosen model/account, read-only tools-checklist task and inspected correlated result. Existing connections/workspaces enter at the first incomplete step; later approved beginner/prepared-workspace behavior is retained. Completed module proof remains valid for its original scope, not full-product/account-first acceptance.\n\nIn scope:\n- A persistent full-product guide with contextual highlighting, truthful explanations and safe interaction across the actual authenticated shell and product routes, plus Help for starting/replaying the correct curriculum version. Cover account/workspace/permissions, shell navigation/search/notifications/settings, Papercup Chat and agent/session/result/desktops work, plans/inbox/work coordination, knowledge/engineering/learning surfaces, Mail/Calendar/Phone, Cloud/BYOC and billing. Derive the exhaustive permitted-feature census from the maintained rail registry plus non-rail capabilities; explicitly explain unavailable or permission-gated capabilities rather than silently omitting them. The detailed family map and proposed detectors are in WI-10004837#comment:1161175.\n- Extend the existing authenticated progress machinery for account/org-level orientation before a workspace exists, without fabricating a workspace identity; workspace-dependent modules retain the existing isolated scope. Assess the actual store/writer before adding any durable surface.\n- Pause, resume, skip, restart, already-completed step recognition, and recovery from failed or delayed actions.\n- Progress associated with the signed-in tenant/user, workspace, lesson identity and lesson version.\n- Contextual AI questions grounded in the approved lesson content and minimal authorized app state, using the existing agent backend.\n- Opt-in spoken questions, spoken lesson guidance and authorized help answers, with mute/stop/replay, text fallback and lifecycle/scope cancellation, through the existing two-tier voice agent and tutorial-only voice profile (D-022, superseding D-012's no-microphone scope). Tutorial voice is available to all users, including free users, using Papercusp's protected ElevenLabs account. Voice never advances a domain step. P-012 waits on voice-two-tier-elevenlabs-agent-2026-10-06 P-010/P-011 and the P-013 billing dependency.\n- A billing explanation and Help entry derived from the actual billing implementation (P-013), including Papercusp versus cloud-provider charges, subscription/invoice/receipt controls, payment failure and an explicit test-mode disclosure when applicable; the tutorial initiates no charge.\n- Consent-aware tutorial analytics and maintained automated plus manual accessibility verification.\n\nOutside the first release:\n- A no-code lesson authoring system, narrated video, a new agent orchestration backend, and a different frontend framework. The former exclusion of tutorials for every feature is explicitly superseded by D-023's full-product direction; the proposed enforceable coverage census is recorded in D-024.\n- General autonomous UI control, automatic credentials/provisioning/spending, destructive actions, and a default session-replay rollout.\n- A commercial tour SaaS or additional CopilotKit/AI SDK/database/state/positioning library without a concrete gap in reused surfaces.\n\n## Requirements\n\nAvi approved direct AUTO implementation of this plan. These contracts preserve the reviewed outcomes and make their verification explicit; planned test files are implementation deliverables, not claims that tests already exist or passed.\n\n**R-1 — Complete first lesson.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"A signed-in user can complete the reviewed first-agent journey in the actual cloud-app surface and inspect a successful task result; users with existing connections/workspaces enter at the first incomplete step.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:17\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The authenticated first-agent lesson reaches an inspected successful task result for both new-user and existing-workspace entry paths.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The new-user or existing-workspace journey cannot reach an inspected successful task result, or a click advances the lesson without domain success. An existing-workspace user is not entered at the first incomplete step.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"new signed-in user\",\n      \"existing workspace\",\n      \"first-agent task result\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\",\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the journey integration suite and the Playwright cloud-tutorial journey against the maintained current-build runtime, using actual authenticated controls and observed workspace/agent/task state; inspect a successful task result and the corresponding lesson state. The structured requirements check verifies implementation coverage; the required automated layers are separately bound to the exact Vitest and recorded Playwright runs, and the grader must inspect those actual verdicts. The requirements check result is shared across R-1/R-6/R-12/R-13 and is not evidence for this BAR alone.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"requirements\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Usable guide.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The guide explains and highlights the current action while the real app remains usable; missing or late targets are handled without breaking the app, and exit cleans up the overlay.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:17\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The guide provides usable, recoverable explanations and highlighting of the current action throughout target waiting and complete exit cleanup.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The guide blocks required controls, fails to recover a missing target, or leaves an overlay/listener after exit. The guide does not explain and highlight the current action.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"guide controls\",\n      \"dynamic targets\",\n      \"exit cleanup\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Render the guide with real product components and late/missing target fixtures; exercise form interaction, pause/exit and remount; assert target interaction remains usable and overlays/listeners are cleaned up.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-guide.integration.test.tsx\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Confirmed progression.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Steps advance on confirmed authorized domain state rather than a Next-button click or target appearance; failed or delayed actions stay incomplete and offer an actionable recovery.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:17\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A lesson step reaches confirmed completion through its authorized domain action with actionable recovery for failed or delayed attempts.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A click or DOM target alone advances a step, or a failed/pending domain operation is treated as success. A failed or delayed step offers no actionable recovery.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"connection state\",\n      \"workspace readiness\",\n      \"agent/task success\",\n      \"failed or delayed actions\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Drive the lesson controller with controlled sequences of clicked/pending/failed/succeeded domain observations and assert that only confirmed success advances each corresponding step.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-lesson.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — User-controlled lifecycle.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The user can pause, resume, skip, restart and replay the lesson from Help, with sensible focus restoration and recognition of completed prerequisites.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:17\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The user can pause, resume, skip, restart and replay the lesson from Help, with sensible focus restoration and recognition of completed prerequisites.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any lifecycle action loses the intended lesson position, ignores existing prerequisites, or leaves focus trapped. A supported pause, resume, skip, restart or replay action cannot be reached from Help.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"pause/resume\",\n      \"skip/replay\",\n      \"precompleted prerequisites\",\n      \"focus restoration\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise pause/resume/skip/restart/replay from Help in the controller and guide suites, including already-completed prerequisites and focus restoration after exit.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-lesson.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-guide.integration.test.tsx\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Durable isolated progress.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Progress survives refresh and later sessions, is isolated by tenant/user/workspace/lesson/version, handles concurrent updates and lesson-version changes, and does not replay product side effects.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:17\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Progress survives refresh and later sessions, is isolated by tenant/user/workspace/lesson/version, handles concurrent updates and lesson-version changes, and does not replay product side effects.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Progress leaks between scopes, cannot restore after refresh, is corrupted by concurrent updates/version changes, or causes a repeated product side effect. Sign-out or session expiry exposes another user's progress or causes resumption to replay a product side effect.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"tenant/user/workspace isolation\",\n      \"refresh/later-session resume\",\n      \"concurrent updates\",\n      \"lesson versions\",\n      \"idempotency\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Use isolated database fixtures and authenticated request contexts for two tenants/users/workspaces; persist and reload progress, issue concurrent updates and version changes, and verify no cross-scope data or product-action replay.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-progress.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Accessible real interaction.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Keyboard and screen-reader users can follow the guide, operate highlighted forms and nested dialogs, and exit/resume; zoom, reduced motion and smaller viewports preserve task completion.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:17\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The lesson remains completable under each specified accessibility setting.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A user cannot operate a highlighted form/dialog, leave/resume the guide, or understand the current step with the tested accessibility settings.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"keyboard\",\n      \"nested dialogs\",\n      \"screen reader\",\n      \"zoom and smaller viewports\",\n      \"reduced motion\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\",\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run guide keyboard/focus/axe assertions and the full Playwright lesson at narrow/zoomed/reduced-motion settings, then inspect screen-reader announcements and guide-to-form navigation in the supported runtime. The structured requirements check verifies implementation coverage; the required automated layers are separately bound to the exact Vitest and recorded Playwright runs, and the grader must inspect those actual verdicts. The requirements check result is shared across R-1/R-6/R-12/R-13 and is not evidence for this BAR alone.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"requirements\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Grounded contextual help.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"When AI help is included, answers use the current lesson and minimal permitted app state, exclude secrets/unrelated tenant data, and do not decide domain completion; the deterministic lesson works when AI is unavailable.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a1-9bdd-7142-88e4-12f088a4def7:1\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f6a9-2333-7dd3-a4a9-3434afa55b5b:17\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Optional AI help provides safe, minimally scoped, current-lesson-grounded answers without deciding domain completion or preventing the deterministic lesson during an AI outage.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The payload exposes secrets/another tenant, an AI response marks a domain step complete, or unavailable help prevents the fixed lesson from functioning. Bind P-013 as implementation owner and P-010/P-012 proof owners; retain R-8 safety and exact hosted-artifact acceptance.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"requirements\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Spoken guidance\n\nD-012 adds spoken step guidance and permitted contextual agent answers using the existing voice/TTS and playback controls. Keep visible text with mute, stop and replay controls. Honor the selected voice and mute preference; cancel obsolete playback on scope/step changes, pause/exit and sign-out. Handle blocked autoplay or unavailable/failed speech with usable text. Voice output must not start microphone capture or advance domain completion. D-022 separately permits an explicit opt-in spoken question through the existing two-tier voice agent and tutorial-only profile, with Papercusp's protected ElevenLabs account available to free users. The linked voice plan owns shared-key security, cloud backend support and the voice-release hold; this plan waits on its P-010/P-011 and retains text fallback.\n\n### Interaction model and first lesson\n\nKeep the guide available beside the app. A step explains the action, identifies the relevant control, and waits for the domain action to succeed. A click or the appearance of a DOM element is not proof that the user has connected an account, provisioned a workspace, or launched an agent.\n\nProposed lesson:\n1. Establish the user’s workspace context and check prerequisites.\n2. Connect a supported cloud provider, or recognize the existing connection.\n3. Explain region, machine size, storage, model/account selection, and expected cost using existing product data.\n4. Let the user explicitly provision a workspace, or select an existing ready workspace.\n5. Wait for actual readiness, with a clear explanation of delays and recoverable failures.\n6. Launch the first agent through the existing control surface.\n7. Offer a small task chosen for the tutorial; the user submits it.\n8. Show the result and how to inspect what the agent did.\n9. Mark the lesson complete and offer Help/replay.\n\n### Library recommendation and selection gate\n\nRecommend React Joyride v3 as the first prototype candidate; Driver.js is the alternative candidate. Evaluate both against the same actual React 19/Vite/TanStack Router journey before choosing. Select one walkthrough engine, record the evidence, and pin compatible stable versions. Documentation compatibility is not a passed integration test.\n\n- React Joyride v3: React hooks, async preparation, custom components, target waiting, and explicit React 19 support. Its published package is MIT licensed. Pay particular attention to focus trapping when users must operate highlighted forms.\n- Driver.js: MIT licensed, no dependencies, framework independent, async/manual navigation and dynamic-element waiting. Consider it if the guide mainly needs a lightweight highlighting adapter.\n- Reactour: credible React alternative; its separate mask/popover packages may fit a sidebar-led experience.\n- Shepherd and Intro.js: technically capable, but their vendors direct commercial applications to commercial licenses; they are not the default recommendation.\n- NextStep: documents React Router support, but its Vite setup requires a Next.js navigation mock. That and our TanStack Router integration increase the work.\n- Onborda: centered on Next.js and Framer Motion; not the preferred match for this frontend.\n- TourGuide JS: viable vanilla tours, but no demonstrated advantage over Driver.js for this lesson.\n\nUse XState with its React integration only if branching, waits, retries, and recovery exceed the existing tutorial machinery or a small explicit reducer. If adopted, use the stable XState line, not an alpha. XState provides workflow semantics and snapshot persistence; it does not supply our authenticated storage or domain-success checks.\n\n### Reuse and architecture\n\nMeasured on 2026-10-01:\n- apps/operator-vite/package.json:37,43,56 declares TanStack Router, React 19, and Vite.\n- libs/agent-chat/README.md describes the existing streaming chat library built on assistant-ui.\n- apps/operator/package.json:56,164,230,256,258 declares assistant-ui, Radix Popover, PostHog, axe/Playwright, and Playwright.\n- packages/operator-core/lib/onboarding/tutorial-pack.ts contains shared tutorial curriculum loading.\n- apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/page.tsx uses the existing workspaceHosts.control query and workspaceHosts.action mutation seam.\n- apps/operator/app/_components/PostHogProvider.tsx reads the existing telemetry setting and disables session recording.\n\nThese are source-level observations, not proof of what app.papercusp.com currently serves. Phase 1 must resolve the actual hosted-portal versus embedded-operator boundary, authenticated shell, and available product capabilities before selecting integration paths. Consume byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22 and unified-web-portal-2026-08-29 as dependencies; do not rebuild their infrastructure. The BYOC plan records an initial GCP-first launch cut; use that as the initial lesson candidate and reconcile it with Avi’s current scope at review.\n\nThe implementation should have:\n- A typed lesson definition: identity/version, explanatory content, target identifier, prerequisites, allowed guide actions, and domain completion condition.\n- A lesson controller that consumes existing authenticated app state and produces current step, waiting/error state, and progress events.\n- One adapter for the chosen highlighting library, using stable explicit tutorial targets rather than fragile layout selectors.\n- A guide UI composed from our existing components. Follow design-phase.search_registry before choosing components, then validate/lint the design spec.\n- An authenticated progress adapter using an existing preference/progress storage surface where one fits. Prefer a small extension; a new table or mutator needs a recorded reason.\n- Our existing agent-chat/assistant-ui surface and existing agent backend for questions. Pass the current lesson, its explanation, relevant app-state fields, and user permissions. Exclude secrets and unrelated tenant data.\n- Existing PostHog integration for tutorial events where telemetry is enabled.\n- Tests in the repository’s real Vitest/Playwright suites, with axe and manual interaction checks.\n\nThe tutorial owns no independent provisioning or account-management implementation. It guides the user through existing product actions. Observe confirmed domain state to advance; do not replay a side-effecting action merely because progress restoration found an incomplete step.\n\n### Progress, resilience, and accessibility\n\nProgress must support refresh, later sessions, and workspace switching. Store lesson version and completed logical steps; define how progress changes when the lesson definition changes. Restore only the user/workspace’s authorized progress, then reconcile it against current app state. Concurrent tabs and retries must not corrupt completion or duplicate product actions.\n\nA missing target, insufficient permission, failed provider connection, failed provisioning, agent failure, or unavailable AI response must leave the user a usable app and a understandable next action. Skip/exit should clean up highlighting and restore sensible focus.\n\nKeyboard users must be able to operate highlighted controls, switch between the guide and app, and leave or resume the guide. Verify nested dialogs, zoom, smaller viewports, scrolling, reduced motion, and screen-reader announcements. A library’s accessibility claim is a starting point, not the acceptance result.\n\n### Contextual AI and measurement\n\nThe deterministic lesson remains usable when AI help is disabled or unavailable. AI explains the current step and answers contextual questions; the lesson controller owns completion. Initial guide actions should be limited to approved navigation/highlighting/help affordances. Any later general UI automation is a separately reviewed scope extension.\n\nSuggested events: lesson started, step displayed, step confirmed complete, waiting/recovery encountered, lesson paused/resumed/skipped/completed, and help question requested. Record lesson/version/step and a permitted context identifier; do not send secrets, task content, or full chat transcripts by default. PostHog failures must not block onboarding. Implement a recognizable expressive character with lip-synced mouth shapes driven by the ElevenLabs narration/alignment, eye blinks and directed looks, expression changes and purposeful gestures; produce a short actual speaking preview before compositing the full video. Reuse the existing cup/brand artwork and extend the existing interactive guide, lesson/progress and R2 hosting surfaces. This session remains the implementation route; the tutorial's visible fleet is a product demonstration on the same cloud instance. A dedicated delivery breakdown may sit beneath P-017 so the video release can have coherent independent acceptance without rewriting unrelated parent-guide work.\nRelated: P-017\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"feature-drain-delivery-readiness-and-outcome-accounting-2026-10-01","title":"Feature delivery — truthful outcome counts and less lost worker time","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Feature delivery — truthful outcome counts and less lost worker time\nslug: feature-drain-delivery-readiness-and-outcome-accounting-2026-10-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-02\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-01, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_proof_stale. Next repair: Bind evidence at the current spec revision on the declared evidence plane. (R-10). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nRevision 4 (su-fd916e65, 2026-10-01 ~19:30Z, WI-10004504). Owner directive #1170 [owner:Avi 2026-10-01, session_turn:claude:d14b4bce-e5d9-4292-87b9-47ce1e4f24c4:2] authorizes carrying this plan to shipped on AUTO without further owner review, so revision 3's \"Avi reviews this draft\" step is satisfied (D-007).\n\nRevision 4 rewrites the requirements as atomic acceptance blocks (one observable outcome each, each mapped to exactly one item), confirms the P-006 targets and the R-4/R-17 thresholds (D-007), and updates the scope for execution. Revision 3's measurements and decisions are unchanged.\n\nNext: activation audit over the re-read source conversations, activation, then P-001, P-002, P-004, P-007 and P-008; P-006 after them.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10005019 — Extend the existing fleet outcome metrics and leader brief (fleet-metrics-contract.ts, fleet-metrics-scope.ts, leader-brief.ts) to count the feature cohort for feature fleets, mark each close as flee… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005020 — One dependency representation plus an acceptance-readiness check. (a) work_items:set_blocker treats a work-item ref in any form (bare id or work-item:done:<id>) as a dependency: write the canonical b… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005021 — Stalled-item rotation through existing fleet controls: when a worker's item shows no material advancement for the threshold while ready items wait in the fleet claim set, name it in the leader brief … <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005022 — Keep fleet capacity at target: fleet:launch-on-plan writes a headcount target by default, and a member silent beyond the threshold (heartbeats only, fleet not paused) is named in the leader brief and… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005023 — Investigate the 0930 fleet's context restarts (82 compactions across four workers in 8.4 hours; 1,034 tools:find calls): per restart, context size, largest tool results, effort setting and carry-docu… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10005024 — Run the next feature-drain fleet on the current build with targets fixed before launch (D-007: first fleet-done feature close within 2 hours of launch; no member silent for more than 30 minutes witho… <!-- P-006 -->\n## Purpose, in plain words\n\nFleet nonp2p-feature-drain-sol61-xhigh-0930 ran 8 hours 32 minutes before its first feature closed. The leader then reported zero closures when there were four.\n\nThis plan does three things:\n\n1. Fixes the reporting.\n2. Removes the specific ways worker time was lost.\n3. Checks the result on the next feature-drain fleet.\n\n## What happened (measured)\n\nAll times are UTC, 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01. Durations are wall time, not effort or billing.\n\n- **Launch and first close.** The fleet launched at 17:02:42Z with five members. The first feature close was WI-10003379 at 01:35:14Z. WI-10003377, WI-10003378 and WI-10003380 closed by 01:39Z.\n- **The first four closes were inherited.**\n  - They were Dream P019–P022 verification items, worked on 09-26 by su-5d078eec in an earlier fleet.\n  - They became claimable for this fleet at claim-spec revision 5 (about 18:41Z) and then stayed unclaimed for about 7 hours.\n  - Six members were added at 01:26Z. Four of them claimed these items between 01:28 and 01:32Z and closed each within about 7 minutes.\n  - The five original members closed no features during the window.\n- **One worker went silent almost at once.**\n  - su-1f567b0e's last real call was a loop checkpoint at 17:13Z, followed by one heartbeat at 18:06Z and then nothing.\n  - The fleet had no headcount target (`agent_fleets.headcount_target` is NULL), so nothing replaced it until the 01:26Z top-up.\n  - WI-1454201 is the same class of problem.\n- **The live workers stayed on long items that have passed through several fleets.** None of these closed in the window:\n  - WI-10002828: first claimed 09-24; su-498c946e worked it from 17:22 to 23:58Z.\n  - WI-10002829: first claimed 09-24.\n  - WI-10002830: first claimed 09-26.\n  - WI-1074216 and WI-356.\n- **Pauses.**\n  - Avi's system-wide pause #1090 was issued at 22:34Z and the resume #1095 at 23:46Z. Every member was idle from about 22:40 to 23:48Z, and su-d1608f11 stayed idle until 01:06Z.\n  - The leader also paused the fleet from 19:36 to 20:02Z, and had resumed it from an earlier stop at 18:40Z.\n  - Members show matching 28–36-minute gaps around 17:35–18:41Z and 19:17–20:02Z.\n- **Startup churn.** The claim filter was revised four times between 17:03 and 17:28Z. Three different members claimed and released WI-10001268 within 10 minutes.\n- **Context restarts.**\n  - The four active workers made 82 `session:request-compaction` calls in 8.4 hours. su-173ebe85 made 28 of them, about one every 18 minutes.\n  - They also made 1,034 `tools:find` calls.\n  - The counts are measured. Their cost in throughput is inferred, not measured.\n- **Wrong metric.** The leader's \"zero features\" statement at 01:53:53Z came from an issue-family metric applied to a feature-only fleet. It is retracted (D-005).\n- **Scheduler slowness came later.** The slow `scheduler:get_next` period began at about 01:55Z, after the first closes. It is tracked on EI-23227815561098131 and WI-10002617 and is not part of this delay.\n\n### The R6 case, corrected\n\nWI-10002828 does record its prerequisite, but not in the dependency graph.\n\n- At 01:04:36Z, su-498c946e added an `externalBlockers` row through `work_items:set_blocker`, with ref `work-item:done:WI-10004474` and kind `event`.\n- `set_blocker` refuses a bare work-item id and points to `work_items:link`. It does accept the same dependency when it is written as an event key.\n- So the system has two ways to say \"blocked by another work item\", and the plan-item and graph readers only see the dependency link. That is why the plan item shows `blockedBy=[]`.\n\nTiming:\n\n- The repair task WI-10004474 was created at 01:00Z. A duplicate, WI-10004475, was created at 01:01Z and later dropped.\n- WI-10002828 was marked blocked at 01:04Z.\n- All of this happened at the end of the window, so it did not cause the delay.\n\nThe real cost on WI-10002828 was the hours of work done before anyone learned that the plan's R6 acceptance definition was incomplete. R6 was a draft, had no acceptedBy, and lacked method and check details.\n\n### What remains unknown\n\n- Which cause accounts for how much of the window.\n- Active effort and billing.\n- The exact throughput cost of context restarts.\n- Historical scheduler phases, which were not retained.\n\n## Acceptance and work-item responsibilities\n\n| Level | Responsibility | What it must not become |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Plan | Define the outcome, acceptance requirements, methods, checks and required evidence once. | A vague outcome whose real conditions are added later through private messages. |\n| Plan item / work item | Deliver a bounded output and the evidence for its part of the plan's acceptance. | A newly invented acceptance policy, or an automatic leader-signoff requirement. |\n| Dependency graph | Record which unfinished output another piece of work needs. | A copy of status prose, a leader-only queue, or a second blocker store. |\n| Plan acceptance evaluation | Combine the mapped evidence and apply the plan's acceptance definition. | A separate plan-wide review for every ordinary work item. |\n\n## Requirements\n\nEach block is one observable acceptance outcome mapped to exactly one plan item. Revision 3 prose requirements R-1..R-10 are folded into these blocks; former R-5 (scheduler outcome attribution, continues on EI-23227815561098131 and WI-10002617) and R-6 (end-to-end pilot, replaced by R-10) stay retired.\n\n**R-1 — Count only feature closes as feature-fleet outcomes.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Feature-fleet reports count the feature cohort and list supporting tasks and bugs separately.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A feature fleet outcome count includes only feature closes.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A supporting task or bug close is included in a feature fleet outcome count.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run fleet-metrics contract fixtures with inherited-finish, wrong-family, genuine-zero, paused-interval and proposed-versus-committed controls; reconcile the 0930 fleet report on the current build.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-metrics-contract.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-11 — Label inherited feature closes.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Each close shows whether the fleet did the work or finished work it inherited (prior-fleet history plus a short claim-to-close time).\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A feature close of work that an earlier fleet already did is reported as inherited.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A close whose work history shows an earlier fleet doing the work is reported as fleet-done.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run fleet-metrics contract fixtures with inherited-finish, wrong-family, genuine-zero, paused-interval and proposed-versus-committed controls; reconcile the 0930 fleet report on the current build.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-metrics-contract.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-12 — Exclude paused time from working time.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Paused time (owner and fleet pauses) is reported separately from working time.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Reported fleet working time excludes paused time.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Reported fleet working time includes an owner or fleet pause interval.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run fleet-metrics contract fixtures with inherited-finish, wrong-family, genuine-zero, paused-interval and proposed-versus-committed controls; reconcile the 0930 fleet report on the current build.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-metrics-contract.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-13 — Report unmeasured populations as unknown.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"An unmeasured population reads unknown, never zero.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"An unmeasured outcome population is reported as unknown.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An unmeasured outcome population is reported as zero.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run fleet-metrics contract fixtures with inherited-finish, wrong-family, genuine-zero, paused-interval and proposed-versus-committed controls; reconcile the 0930 fleet report on the current build.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-metrics-contract.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-14 — Keep proposed closes apart from committed closes.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Committed, proposed, pending-human and shipped outcomes stay distinct.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A close with proposed completion authority is reported apart from committed closes.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A close with proposed completion authority is counted as a committed outcome.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run fleet-metrics contract fixtures with inherited-finish, wrong-family, genuine-zero, paused-interval and proposed-versus-committed controls; reconcile the 0930 fleet report on the current build.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-metrics-contract.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Store work-item blockers only as dependency edges.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"A dependency on another work item lives only in the existing graph (D-001).\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A blocker that names another work item is stored only as a dependency edge.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A blocker naming another work item, as a bare id or a work-item:done:<id> event key, is stored as an external blocker.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run set_blocker fixtures with a bare work-item id, a work-item:done:<id> ref and a genuine external event (negative control); confirm plan-item blockedBy and the claim floors read the resulting edge.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/set_blocker.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-15 — Migrate existing work-item external blockers to edges.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Existing rows of that shape are migrated to edges, starting with WI-10002828.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A pre-existing external blocker that names another work item is replaced by a dependency edge.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"After the migration an external blocker naming another work item remains without a matching dependency edge.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Census payload.externalBlockers rows that name a work item before and after the migration; every converted row has a matching blocks edge and genuine external blockers are untouched (negative control).\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/set_blocker.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Hold items whose acceptance requirement is incomplete.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The scheduler does not hand out an item whose plan acceptance contract is incomplete (D-002, D-003).\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"An item bound to an incomplete acceptance requirement is not handed out by the scheduler.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The scheduler hands out an item bound to a draft, unaccepted or method-less acceptance requirement.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run scheduler readiness fixtures: an item bound to a draft, unaccepted or method-less acceptance requirement is held; its repair task is found or filed and linked exactly once; an independent test item in the same plan and an item with a complete contract stay claimable.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scheduler/get_next.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-16 — Link exactly one repair task to a held item.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The scheduler finds the existing repair task for that contract, or files one and links it, never a duplicate.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A held item is linked to exactly one repair task for its incomplete acceptance requirement.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A held item has no linked repair task, or a second repair task is filed for a contract that already has one.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run scheduler readiness fixtures: an item bound to a draft, unaccepted or method-less acceptance requirement is held; its repair task is found or filed and linked exactly once; an independent test item in the same plan and an item with a complete contract stay claimable.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scheduler/get_next.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Name stalled workers in the leader brief.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Stalled work gives way to ready work through one accountable action.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The leader brief names a worker whose claimed item has stalled while ready items wait.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A worker past the stall threshold with ready items waiting is absent from the leader brief, or a paused fleet or instrumented long test is named.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run leader-brief stall fixtures: a worker past 30 minutes without material advancement while a ready item waits is named with the required action; a paused fleet and an instrumented long test are not named.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/leader-brief.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Give drain fleets a default headcount target.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Drain fleets get a headcount target by default.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A drain fleet launched without an explicit headcount receives a headcount target.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A drain fleet launched without an explicit headcount has no headcount target.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Launch a drain fleet without an explicit headcount in launch-on-plan fixtures; the fleet row carries a headcount target equal to the launched count.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet_registry/__tests__/launch-on-plan.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-17 — Treat silent members as missing capacity.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"A member that makes no calls beyond heartbeats for a threshold, while the fleet is not paused, is reported and replaced up to the target.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A member silent past the threshold in an unpaused fleet does not count toward live headcount.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A member with only heartbeats for longer than the threshold in an unpaused fleet still counts toward live headcount.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run headcount fixtures with a member that has only heartbeats for 20 minutes in an unpaused fleet (counted missing and reported) and in a paused fleet (still counted present).\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet_registry/headcount-target.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-18 — Keep ready work claimable while a sibling is held.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Holding one item for an incomplete acceptance contract does not withhold items whose contract is complete or that do not depend on it (D-003: retain real authority boundaries; added by D-009).\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"While one plan item is held for an incomplete acceptance requirement, a sibling item in the same plan whose acceptance requirement is complete, and an independent item with no bound requirement, stay claimable through scheduler:get_next.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The scheduler withholds an item with a complete acceptance contract, or an unrelated item, because a sibling in its plan is held.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run scheduler readiness fixtures with one plan holding three items: one bound to a draft acceptance requirement (held), one bound to a complete, accepted requirement, and one with no bound requirement. get_next hands out both non-held items and names only the first as held. RATING BASIS: the over-blocking control fixture only.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scheduler/get_next.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Explain the 0930 context restarts.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Measure why the 0930 workers restarted their context every 18-35 minutes and file fix items with a target restart rate.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The measured causes of the 0930 fleet context restarts are recorded with filed fix items.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The restart finding lacks per-restart measurements, a target restart rate or owned fix items.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Measure each 0930 worker restart (context size, largest tool results, effort setting, carry-document size) from tool_invocations and session records; record the finding on the P-008 work item with owned fix items and a target restart rate.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Measure the next feature-drain fleet against fixed targets.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Set targets before launch; after the run, report against them and compare with this incident.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The next feature-drain fleet is reported against targets fixed before its launch.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The next-fleet report has no targets fixed before launch or no comparison with the 0930 baseline.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Fix targets before launch (D-007); after the run, report time to the first fleet-done feature close, the share of worker-hours on items that closed, silent-member minutes and paused time against the 0930 baseline.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-7 — State cutoffs and populations in the owner report.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Owner reports explain outcomes, dependencies and uncertainty in plain language with exact cutoffs, without conflating proof, completion, acceptance and shipment.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Every count in the next-fleet owner report states its cutoff and population.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A count in the next-fleet owner report lacks its cutoff or its population.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Review the next-fleet owner report: every count names its cutoff and population; inherited, fleet-done, paused, proposed and shipped figures stay distinct; corrections are persisted in the plan.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-008 | live |\n| R-10 | P-006 | live |\n| R-7 | P-006 | live |\n\nEach requirement maps to exactly one item; item-specific tests supply evidence to these blocks and are not a separate acceptance definition.\n\n### Execution order\n\n- P-001, P-002, P-004, P-007 and P-008 can run in parallel; their files are mostly separate.\n- P-006 runs after P-001, P-002, P-004 and P-007.\n- P-008 is an investigation, and its fix items may land later.\n\n### Thresholds\n\nConfirmed by D-007 (set by su-fd916e65 under #1170; Avi may revise):\n\n- R-4: 30 minutes with no material advancement.\n- R-17: 20 minutes with no calls beyond heartbeats while the fleet is not paused.\n\nRespect intentional pauses and instrumented long tests. Use existing events and ownership, not new monitors.\n\n## Phase 1 — Count outcomes correctly\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend the existing fleet outcome metrics and leader brief (fleet-metrics-contract.ts, fleet-metrics-scope.ts, leader-brief.ts) to count the feature cohort for feature fleets, mark each close as fleet-done or inherited (prior-fleet worked_by_history plus claim-to-close time), report owner and fleet paused time separately, and keep committed/proposed/pending-human/shipped outcomes and supporting tasks/bugs apart. Controls: wrong-family, inherited-finish, genuine-zero and proposed-versus-committed. Absorbs WI-10004580. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005019 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Stop losing worker time\n\n- **P-002** `done` One dependency representation plus an acceptance-readiness check. (a) work_items:set_blocker treats a work-item ref in any form (bare id or work-item:done:<id>) as a dependency: write the canonical blocks edge through linkWorkItem, or refuse with a pointer to work_items:link; migrate existing externalBlockers rows of that shape to edges, starting with WI-10002828. (b) Before the scheduler hands out an item, check its plan acceptance contract; when it is draft/unaccepted or missing method/check details, hold the item and find-or-file-and-link the contract repair task (no duplicates), leaving independent implementation/test items claimable. Absorbs the readiness half of WI-10004581. importance: high — note: ← WI-10005020 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Stalled-item rotation through existing fleet controls: when a worker's item shows no material advancement for the threshold while ready items wait in the fleet claim set, name it in the leader brief and require one accountable action (finish, split, record a real blocker, or release and take the ready item). Exempt pauses and instrumented long tests; status reads are not advancement. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Narrow the global runner-input rule (A)\n\n- **P-001** `done` A1: scope workspace vitest configs to their own workspace. Today any `*/vitest.*config*` anywhere is a GLOBAL runner input (scripts/lib/test-pass-reuse.mjs isGlobalRunnerInput), so a change to libs/generic/search/vitest.config.ts voids every operator-core proof. Instead, a vitest config under directory D should invalidate only proofs whose test file is under D; root vitest.* stays global. Pin it with tests in packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/test-pass-reuse.test.ts. Measured: 6 of 43 global-touching commits in 72h. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004712 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` A2: root package.json changes count as global only when something other than `scripts` changed. Add a content-aware drift seam: selectReusablePasses takes an optional `inertGlobalChange(rel, fromSha, toSha)`, and affected-tests implements it by comparing the JSON at both shas with `scripts` removed. Fail closed: if a read or parse fails, treat the change as global. Measured: 12 of 43. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004713 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` A3: libs/test-config is global only for MAIN-PROCESS files (the vitest config import closure, globalSetup, reporters). Worker-side setup files are already per-proof inputs: all 2,638 operator-core proofs list them in executedModules. DERIVE the main-process set rather than hand-listing it. Candidates: record vite's configFileDependencies plus globalSetup paths in the reporter, or compute a static import closure of libs/test-config/src/vitest-config.ts plus its globalSetup entries. Measured: 14 of 43. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004714 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` A4: a root tsconfig.*.json is global only when the test toolchain reads it, i.e. it sits in the extends/references chain of tsconfig.json or a workspace tsconfig. Derive the set; don't name files. tsconfig.declarations.json looks gen:declarations-only [inferred; verify]. Measured: 4 of 43. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004715 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` A5: narrow package-lock.json and patches/ to the packages that changed. First verify whether proofs' executedModules include node_modules paths. If they do, map changed lock entries and patched packages to node_modules/<pkg>/ prefixes and match them per proof. If they don't, record why and keep these global. Measured: lockfile 14 and patches 4 of 43. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004716 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Pure-lane proofs (B)\n\n- **P-006** `blocked` B1: make the pure lane reusable. It is 3,715 operator-core files (58%), runs isolate:false, never records a proof, and costs 489s per round on 599dbeeb. (1) Record proofs for pure-lane files in isolated proof-capture runs off the gate's critical path, rotating through the lane: decide the cadence and slice size, and name the routine. (2) Let test:lane-pure apply a skip list: scripts/run-vitest-pure-lane.mjs plus an all-reused zero-file pass, because its script lacks --passWithNoTests, so armTestPassReuse filters it out today. (3) Keep the 5% audit, plus the pure lane's own co-residency risk: a pure file that passes isolated is assumed to pass co-resident, which is the lane's premise. Design first, recorded as a plan Decision. — note: ← WI-10004717 blocked (1 external blocker)\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Hub-module granularity (C)\n\n- **P-007** `done` C1: cut false drift through hub modules. Measured from a 29bf7350 to 599dbeeb approximation: of 2,015 capturable stateful proofs, 1,340 die across 349 changed files. libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/schema/generated{,-relations}.ts is in 1,300 proofs, orchestrator blueprint mode-catalog.generated.ts in 990, and 887 proofs had 20+ changed inputs. Investigate first: why do most tests execute the generated DB schema (barrel imports? one import edge?), and would splitting it, or making that edge lazy, remove it from most closures? Alternatively, track symbols or tables instead of whole modules for generated files. Record the choice as a plan Decision. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003 — note: Built per D-010; WI-10004718 closed committed (tests green, 3/3 mutants caught, tsc clean; replay: 79.6% of proof x schema-commit pairs spared vs 0).\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Measure\n\n- **P-008** `todo` M1: acceptance measurement. Preserve bypass events, but zero candidate files stays zero; an unknown file population stays explicitly unknown and prevents a fully qualified overall hit-rate claim. Reuse the existing producer/context/run-correlation repair EI-25888824887514398, the existing selector and ledger; add no parallel metrics system. Acceptance: project-native regression tests cover unknown-population dirty checkout, zero candidates, known 20/20 reuse and mixed known/unknown batches; neither an empty nor an unknown population fabricates eligible files, distorts the known-population fraction, or renders overall coverage complete.
