Keep proof age, isolation/dependency checks and soundness auditing intact. This extends R-1/P-008 measurement correctness; it does not weaken any acceptance BAR or authorize a competing live gate. blocked-by: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005 — note: ← WI-10004719 released\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — Owner chose all three yield levers: A (narrow global rule), B (pure-lane proofs), C (hub-module granularity)\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-01 [turn:d9c6d2d5@2026-10-01T08:34:34.515Z] verdict owner-dialog] Question asked through AskUserQuestion: which fixes for #1159? Options were A (narrow the global rule, recommended), B (proofs for the pure lane), C (finer hub-module tracking), or stop at the metric fix. His answer: A, B and C. Route: this session (from the #1159 dialog, \"You fix it now\"). Soundness backstops stay in place: the 5% audit (TEST_REUSE_AUDIT_RATE) and TEST_PASS_REUSE_ALARM. The A trade-off was disclosed in the question: slightly less conservative invalidation. Evidence: WI-10004617 thread and checkpoint.\n\n### D-002 — Soundness constraints from the pre-start consult (conv-mupbhx2j)\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed, from consult conv-mupbhx2j-0000-096dca6598bd4fdeac770da19120a24a answered 2026-10-01T09:16Z by su-76267046 over su-b0451bbf's transcript] [inferred, consult first-principles; not re-probed] A remaining global runner input appears to stay global because a ReuseProof (executedModules + readPaths) does not record it; treat a narrowing as sound only where the proof can see the input or its effect is confined to a known set of proofs. Constraints per item: (1) P-001: a workspace vitest config may be imported or merged by ANOTHER workspace's config (mergeConfig / extends / a root vitest workspace file listing project configs). Scope a config change to directory D only after resolving that importer set; any config with importers outside D invalidates their proofs too, and the test must cover that case. (2) P-005 stays as written: if proofs' executedModules carry no node_modules paths, lockfile and patches/ remain global and the item records why. (3) P-006: the all-reused zero-file pass for test:lane-pure must reuse scripts/lib/empty-suite-guard.mjs reuseSkipCoversRun (fix 1880386d3d, WI-10004306); never re-append --no-passWithNoTests on a fully reused run, which made every fully-reused workspace a deterministic red. Lanes whose inputs (DB rows, services, live tree walks) are outside executedModules/readPaths stay non-reusable; P-006 covers only the pure lane. (4) P-007: whole-file content hashing of a barrel or re-exporting hub is the only drift the module-load map can prove. Prefer restructuring (split the generated schema, or make the import edge lazy), which keeps file-level soundness. Symbol- or table-level tracking is admissible only if the proof records which export each closure actually resolved, and it must ship with a regression test for the 95f1e72632 case: a tool-name object moved behind a re-export, the importer's text unchanged, the barrel changed, and consumers silently lost 7 tools. (5) Every narrowing must keep reporting through the TEST_PASS_REUSE summary fields (globalInput / unknownDrift / opaque / notCaptured) and keep the 5% audit sample, the only falsifier of a wrong skip.\nMeasured: 2026-10-01T09:18Z on staging b190bcc7 — scripts/lib/test-pass-reuse.mjs:78 `export function isGlobalRunnerInput(rel)` with the narrowing rationale at :74 (\"P-007 measured that 'any package.json or libs/test-config file' discards 12 of 38\"); scripts/lib/empty-suite-guard.mjs:125 `export function reuseSkipCoversRun(...)`; `git cat-file -t` confirms commits 1880386d3d and 95f1e72632 exist.\n\n### D-003 — R-1 judges Phase A on an added second replay pair without a dependency change\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-01 AskUserQuestion answer, owner-dialog, ~10:2xZ] Question: R-1 requires each phase to show more reused files on the fixed replay pair (proofs at 29bf7350, candidate 599dbeeb); Phase A (P-001..P-005) shows 543 -> 543 there because that pair was a dependency bump (package-lock.json stays global by design). Options: add a second replay pair without a dependency change (recommended); judge on live TEST_PASS_REUSE readings over P-008's window; widen P-005 so the recorder captures resolved package roots; accept no gain on this pair. Avi chose: \"Add 2nd replay pair (Recommended)\".\nConsequence: keep the current pair for every phase. For Phase A, ALSO replay a second fixed pair whose diffs touch nested vitest configs / package.json scripts / libs/test-config but NOT package-lock.json or non-script package.json fields; Phase A meets R-1 when that pair shows more reused files after the phase than before. Pin the second pair's shas in the R-1 evidence before measuring. Evidence of the original finding: WI-10004617 comment 1153041 (scratch p001-replay.mts).\n\n### D-004 — P-003 (A3) stays in scope as specified, sequenced after P-005 and P-006\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-01 ~13:21Z AskUserQuestion answer: \"Build as specified you can prioritize the other improvements however if you think they will be more impactful\"].\n\nMeasured yield (WI-10004714 comment 1153413): over 7 days A3 would have saved 3 of 36 test-config submodule commits (8%) from killing every proof. Most churn is in genuine main-process files (vitest-config, both reporters, globalSetup and its pg-* closure).\n\nRuling:\n- Build P-003 as specified: narrow by main-process import closure, deriving the closure (no hand list); do NOT treat the reporters as non-global.\n- Add the guard from consult conv-mupk4hz4-0000-ca9c1fa8718a4993aed12d9f18b4bcdc: executedModules comes from importDurations, which is capped at EXECUTED_SOURCE_MAP_IMPORT_LIMIT. A proof whose module count reaches the cap may be missing setup files, so treat it as opaque (never reusable under the narrowed rule).\n- Order [self-imposed, under the owner's grant to prioritize by impact]: P-005 (lockfile/patches: 18 of 43 global kills) and P-006 (pure-lane proofs: 489s per round) before P-003.\n\n### D-005 — P-006 design: capture pure-lane proofs isolated after each gate verdict, and let test:lane-pure apply the skip list\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed design under D-001 lever B (owner:Avi chose A+B+C); constraints from D-002(3)]\n\nInputs. (a) The reporter records nothing for a non-isolated file: under isolate:false the import record accumulates across the fork (executed-source-map-reporter.ts, measured 2026-09-06). (b) Isolation costs this lane 1.68x wall (dropping it cut 40.5%, lane-split.ts D-013): all 3,715 pure files isolated take ~820s at the gate's worker budget, ~0.22s/file. (c) D-004 rule 1 (gate-file-level-test-reuse-2026-09-27): a proof counts only from a clean run in the same run context, under 24h old. (d) Both reuse filters (affected-tests armTestPassReuse, targeted-task-reuse) need --passWithNoTests in the package.json text; test:lane-pure lacks it although run-vitest-pure-lane.mjs passes it on every shard.\n\n1. CAPTURE: pure-lane-proof-capture, a post-verdict PHASE of the green-checkpoint run (run phase pure-proof-capture), in scripts/lib/pure-lane-proof-capture.mjs, invoked after the verdict and promotion decision are recorded. Not a separate routine: a proof needs a clean tree at a committed sha, deps installed, in the gate's run context, and only the checkpoint tree has all three.\n - Sha: the one just judged. GREEN_CHECKPOINT=1, so run_context is green-checkpoint and rule 1 is unchanged. Runs after any verdict, red or green, in which the pure lane executed: proofs are per file.\n - Population: pure-lane include (resolveLaneInclude). Exclude files with a fail/error test_runs row at this sha (rail, see 3) and files already proven at it.\n - Order, by path within each tier: (i) ran in this run's pure lane and passed; (ii) no proof; (iii) oldest proof first, refreshed before 24h.\n - Execution: the workspace's vitest with PC_TEST_LANE unset (isolated default config), the gate suite env, a positional file list per slice, and --no-passWithNoTests. Recording armed as in armTargetedTaskReuse. PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_SOURCE=local plus a phase run_group_id, so capture rows never pose as source=ci candidate evidence.\n - Slice 250 files (~55s). Budget PC_PURE_PROOF_CAPTURE_BUDGET_MS, default 15 min. Before each slice, stop if it would exceed the budget or end within 2 min of the next scheduled green-checkpoint fire. A kill loses at most one slice.\n - Cadence: one bounded phase per verdict run; a full rotation takes 1 to 2 runs, inside the 24h bound.\n - Passing co-resident but failing isolated: the reporter retires the file (rule 5); log PURE_PROOF_CAPTURE_ISOLATED_FAIL (a hidden neighbour dependency).\n - Kill switch PC_PURE_PROOF_CAPTURE=0; default ON (every failure mode runs more tests).\n\n2. APPLY. (a) Shared predicate scriptRunsZeroFilesAsPass in scripts/lib/empty-suite-guard.mjs (the flag, or the script invokes run-vitest-pure-lane.mjs), used by both reuse filters. Related-test narrowing (affected-tests.mjs:5115) stays unchanged; pure-lane narrowing is a follow-up. (b) run-vitest-pure-lane.mjs reads the skip list via test-config's validating reader (resolveReuseSkipExclude, vitest-config's own decision); remaining = include minus validated skips. If remaining is 0 and reuseSkipCoversRun({ selectedFiles: include }) holds: spawn nothing, emit VITEST_PURE_LANE_SHARD state=all-reused, exit 0 (D-002(3)). Else shardCount = ceil(remaining/750). A rejected list counts as none, so shards are sized for the full lane.\n\n3. AUDIT. The 5% audit (TEST_REUSE_AUDIT_RATE) applies unchanged to pure candidates. An audited file runs co-resident, so TEST_PASS_REUSE_ALARM tests the lane premise (passes isolated implies passes co-resident) on a rolling sample. The co-residency rail: capture never mints a proof over a co-resident fail/error at that sha, and a later co-resident failure retires it (rule 5 precedes the reporter's isolation check).\n\nRejected. Co-resident recording (the record describes the fork). Capture inside the suite (+~330s on the critical path). A routine in another checkout (needs a second install and a widened rule 1).\n\nOrder: 2, then 1. Residue: the test_executed_sources upsert key omits run_context, so a clean-local recording at the same sha rewrites a gate proof's context. Capture is unaffected (it records green-checkpoint); filed separately.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-006 — P-003 design: libs/test-config is global only through its derived main-process import closure; worker setup files are per-proof inputs\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed design under D-004 (owner:Avi: build A3 as specified, derive the closure, no hand list, reporters stay global)].\n\nRule. A libs/test-config path invalidates every proof only when it is in the main-process closure. Other test-config paths are judged like any source file, against each proof's executedModules/readPaths.\n\nClosure (libs/test-config/src/main-process-closure.ts, testConfigMainProcessFiles): a static walk of the src dir. Seeds: vitest-config.ts plus every package.json exports/main target, because a config's bare @papercusp/test-config[/x] import loads natively in the main process. A config's relative imports are already per-proof readPaths. Edges: every relative specifier (static, re-export, import(), require, type-only included) plus resolve(__dirname,'<f>') and new URL('<f>', import.meta.url) literals. Exception: a literal-only reference to a WORKER_SETUP_FILE_PATHS entry is not an edge. A real import of a setup file IS an edge.\n\nWorker setup files: the 6 setup constants moved from vitest-config.ts to worker-setup-files.ts. WORKER_SETUP_FILE_PATHS is built from those same constants, so the excluded set cannot drift from what configs load. A pin test asserts that the built config's setupFiles from test-config are a subset of WORKER_SETUP_FILE_PATHS, and that the reporters and globalSetup are disjoint from it.\n\nSoundness guard (D-002 style): a narrowed drift on a proof whose executedModules count reaches EXECUTED_SOURCE_MAP_IMPORT_LIMIT (1,000,000, a pinned mirror of the recorder cap) is treated as opaque, so a truncated recording cannot pass. If the closure cannot be computed, callers fall back to the old whole-submodule rule: affected-tests.mjs logs TEST_PASS_REUSE_TEST_CONFIG_CLOSURE state=unavailable, and targeted-task-reuse passes null. The TEST_PASS_REUSE line gains a testConfigNarrowed counter.\n\nMeasured at HEAD. The closure is 28 of 40 src files. Outside it: the 6 setup files plus console-noise-filter, handle-leak-delta, hermetic-tmpdir, leak-baseline, leak-census-aggregate, silenced-console-census and timer-leak-ledger. Replaying the 57 test-config src commits from the last 7 days: 40 were global before and 38 after, so 2 are saved (5%). That matches D-004's projection of about 8%. Soundness probe (PG, 24h): every operator-core, web and operator-vite proof (2656, 973 and 199 of them) lists setup-hermetic-env.ts and executed-inputs-capture-setup.ts in executed_modules repo-relative; none arrive via a node_modules symlink; the maximum module_count is 5487.\n\nEvidence: WI-10004714 comments 1153413 (yield) and 1153611 (design).\n\n### D-007 — P-004 design: a tsconfig counts only when the vitest toolchain reads it, derived with tsconfck exactly as vite-tsconfig-paths does\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed design under D-001 lever A (owner:Avi chose A+B+C); soundness bar from D-002]\n\nMeasured 2026-10-01 ~15:20Z on the live tree: there is NO root tsconfig.json; root has tsconfig.base.json and tsconfig.declarations.json. tsconfck.findAll(repo, configNames tsconfig.json|jsconfig.json, skip .git/node_modules), the call vite-tsconfig-paths 5.1.4 makes when no `projects` is given, found 341 entry configs in 737 ms; tsconfck.parse of all of them took 162 ms with 0 errors and reached 348 configs. The only ROOT config reached is tsconfig.base.json (scripts/tsconfig.json extends it). tsconfig.declarations.json is read by gen:declarations only. Zero tracked jsconfig.json.\n\nReaders. Vite's esbuild transform (tsconfck nearest tsconfig.json + extends) and vite-tsconfig-paths (findAll entries or explicit `projects`, each tsconfck.parse'd, following extends and references). Only two files call tsconfigPaths(): libs/test-config/src/vitest-config.ts (defaults) and root vitest.config.ts (explicit projects, all named tsconfig.json).\n\nRule.\n1. libs/test-config/src/toolchain-tsconfigs.ts toolchainTsconfigFiles({ repoRoot }) derives the set with the plugin's own library calls: findAll entries (default names plus any config basename a vite/vitest config source or libs/test-config/src file names as a string literal), parse each, take the file, its extended chain and its referenced configs recursively; realpath, keep in-repo non-node_modules paths. Any parse failure throws, so the caller falls back to the pre-P-004 rule.\n2. scripts/lib/test-pass-reuse.mjs: a root tsconfig.*.json is a global runner input only when in the set (isGlobalRunnerInput third arg). tsconfigUnreadByToolchain(rel, set) also exempts an unread tsconfig*.json from the ancestor-directory config rule, which otherwise still reached every proof through \".\". tsconfig.json / jsconfig.json are entries by definition and are never narrowed, so deleting one still invalidates. An unread file still invalidates a proof whose readPaths name it.\n3. Generalized past the root on purpose: an unread nested tsconfig.build.json is exempt from the ancestor rule by the same argument. jsconfig*.json joins CONFIG_BASENAME_RE (a widening; none tracked).\n4. Reporting (D-002(5)): new summary field tsconfigNarrowed (proofs that survive only because an unread drift tsconfig was narrowed) on every TEST_PASS_REUSE line; TEST_PASS_REUSE_TSCONFIG_CLOSURE state=unavailable is logged when the derivation fails.\n\nSoundness. A config outside the set is read by neither toolchain reader, so it cannot change a transform or a resolution. A test that reads it in-process records it in readPaths (P-009); a test that reaches it through a child process (e.g. generated-declarations.test.ts spawning gen-declarations --check) is opaque and never reused (executed-inputs-capture.ts:178, child-process). A change that drops a config from the set edits the config that stopped extending/referencing it, which stays reached (or is a never-narrowed tsconfig.json), so that change still invalidates.\n\nDependency. tsconfck ^3.1.6 declared in libs/test-config/package.json (and its package-lock workspace entry); the single hoisted copy, 3.1.6, is the one vite-tsconfig-paths imports, so the installed tree is unchanged.\n\nKnown pre-existing approximation, NOT changed here: the ancestor rule assumes a reached config governs only files beneath its own directory, but a solution `references` entry or an `include` glob can govern files elsewhere. Filed separately if measurement shows a live instance.\nRelated: P-004\n\n### D-008 — Phase A R-1, second replay pair (D-003): reused files 0 -> 81 with all levers; per lever 0 -> 127 (P-001), 0 -> 2,927 (P-003), 0 -> 2,928 (P-004)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self, measurement under D-003 (owner:Avi chose 'Add 2nd replay pair'); measured 16:20-16:30Z by su-f35e5c5a]\n\nNatural pairs first. .papercusp/scratch/phaseA-pair-scan.mts scanned first-parent staging commits against the gate proof shas recorded 2026-09-29..10-01 (log: phaseA-pair-scan2.log). Only 9a4319b7 -> 83a5cd53 qualified (198 proofs; its only Phase A path is a scripts-only change to apps/operator-vite/package.json). It reuses 182 -> 182 because that change was not global before Phase A either (globalInput 0 on both sides), so it exercises no Phase A lever (phaseA-replay2-9a43-83a5.out). In this window every narrowable change shipped with a package-lock.json change. Proofs at the synthetic gate candidates 163b61ef, 7fca396a and 599dbeeb could not be recursively diffed against most commits (UNKNOWN-DRIFT).\n\nSecond pair, constructed and pinned. Proofs: all 3,757 green-checkpoint proofs at 87d557e7 (operator-core 2,656, all stateful lane; web 973; agent-mcp 60; cupboard-worker 47; plugin-loader 21). Candidates: built by `bash .papercusp/scratch/phaseA-build-candidates.sh 87d557e7e204196d6dde82a875c4ef71e8679cfd 1219248f0a67a79795d4bd7572034f650986c022`. It uses a temp index, writes no refs, and fixes identity and dates, so the shas are reproducible (a re-run gave identical shas). Each candidate is 87d557e7's tree plus the listed paths taken from 1219248f0a:\n- ALL 0d344732: the 3 nested vitest configs (apps/operator/vitest.config.ts, apps/operator/vitest.integration.config.ts, packages/operator-core/vitest.config.ts), packages/operator-core/package.json (one added script), tsconfig.declarations.json, and libs/test-config at synthetic commit fa038173 (its 9 non-main-process changed files from 72c18075: main-process-closure.ts, toolchain-tsconfigs.ts and 7 *.test.ts).\n- P001 32a0467a (nested configs only). P003 b1c3cb26 (test-config only). P004 15b6bde6 (tsconfig.declarations.json only). SCRIPTS 979c8160 (operator-core package.json only).\n- Excluded, because they stay global under both rules and void every proof either way: package-lock.json; apps/operator/package.json (devDependencies, not scripts); libs/test-config package.json, vitest-config.ts, worker-setup-files.ts, admin-test-runs-reporter.ts, baseline-schema-global-setup.ts, execution-details.ts, pg-container.ts, pg-reachability.ts and test-pass-reuse-skip.ts (the main-process closure at 72c18075, classified by phaseA-classify.mts).\n\nMethod: `npx tsx .papercusp/scratch/phaseA-replay2.mts <proofSha> <candidate>`. BEFORE is .papercusp/scratch/tpr-old.mjs, byte-identical to scripts/lib/test-pass-reuse.mjs at 9d4ef786 (the parent of d82b0a32, which carried P-001). AFTER is the current module with the gate's own seams: recursive gitChangedBetween, gitInertGlobalChange, the main-process closure derived at the candidate's test-config pin, and the toolchain tsconfig set derived from the live tree. That set has 457 configs, a superset of the gate checkout's 114, so AFTER is a lower bound. Both sides use the same proofs, drift, clock (2026-10-01T15:08:47Z), runner identity and audit rate 0.\n\nResults (reused files, BEFORE -> AFTER):\n- ALL: 0 -> 81 (agent-mcp 0 -> 41, cupboard-worker 0 -> 21, plugin-loader 0 -> 19; operator-core stateful 0 -> 0; web 0 -> 0).\n- P001: 0 -> 127. P003: 0 -> 2,927 (operator-core stateful 0 -> 2,029; web 0 -> 771). P004: 0 -> 2,928.\n- SCRIPTS: 81 -> 81 (not a Phase A lever; never global).\nBefore Phase A, globalInput voided 2,928 proofs in every candidate except SCRIPTS (829 more are opaque).\n\nVerdict: Phase A meets R-1's replay leg on the second pair. Every lever shows more reused files after than before.\nWhy ALL is only 81: the operator-core package.json scripts change voids 2,847 proofs per proof on BOTH sides (inputChanged 2,847). Only 1,512 of those list that file in read_paths; the rest come from a rule not yet traced. That is outside Phase A and is tracked as WI-10004940.\nSide finding: toolchainTsconfigFiles throws on unparseable untracked debris configs, which silently drops P-004 back to the global rule on that tree (fail-closed, so sound). Tracked as WI-10004941.\nStill owed for R-1 Phase A: the TEST_PASS_REUSE line of the next full green-checkpoint run. As of 16:15Z the gate is frozen on red repair head 87d557e7.\nEvidence: .papercusp/scratch/phaseA-replay2-constructed.out, phaseA-candidates.txt, phaseA-replay2-9a43-83a5.out.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-008\n\n### D-009 — WI-10004940: a scripts-only WORKSPACE package.json change is judged inert only when no script anywhere can invoke a changed name\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed design under D-001 lever A (owner:Avi chose A+B+C); soundness bar D-002; measured 16:59-17:08Z by su-f35e5c5a]\n\nTrace. On a scripts-only change to packages/operator-core/package.json, every proof not invalidated by a direct read is voided by the ancestor-config rule in scripts/lib/test-pass-reuse.mjs invalidates() (CONFIG_BASENAME_RE + o.dirs.has(dirname(rel))). P-002's inert judgment (gitInertGlobalChange, scripts/lib/executed-source-map.mjs) is asked only for GLOBAL drift paths (root package.json, package-lock.json). On the 2,705 green-checkpoint proofs still at 87d557e7 (.papercusp/scratch/wi10004940/classify.mts): directRead 1,055, readDir 0, ancestorOnly 1,630 (operator-core 899, operator 707, operator-public 24), untouched 20. test_executed_sources keeps the newest proof per file: a gate run at 4167738a (16:32-16:42Z) overwrote 1,052 of the 3,757 rows D-008 measured, so D-008's population cannot be rebuilt from the DB any more.\n\nFrequency (.papercusp/scratch/wi10004940/freq.mjs, 7 days of first-parent staging, 2,224 commits): 32 workspace package.json changes; 14 changed non-script fields, 13 were scripts-only, 11 of those touched no runner-affecting script (operator-core 7, operator 2, operator-docs 1, operator-vite 1), 5 unreadable (add/delete). So about 1.5 per day, each voiding ~60% of proofs under the touched workspace for every gate whose drift spans it.\n\nRule (to build under WI-10004940). A drift path whose basename is package.json and which is NOT the root is inert (it configures nothing beneath its directory; a proof that read it is still invalidated) only when ALL hold:\n1. Both sides parse to objects, non-script fields are canonical-equal (as rootPackageJsonChangeIsInert).\n2. No changed script name (added, removed or changed) is runner-affecting (isRunnerAffectingScript).\n3. No changed name is INVOKABLE: it does not occur as a substring of any script command (other than its own definition) in any package.json of the tree at EITHER sha, superproject AND submodules (recurse gitlinks), and no command anywhere uses a glob run form (run-s / run-p / npm-run-all with '*'). Measured need: 3 of 135 runner-affecting scripts call sibling scripts (papercusp-desktop test -> test:config/test:shell/test:selftests; tools/perf-test/wdio test -> test:unit; libs/papercusp test -> npm run test --workspaces, cross-package), so a per-file judgment is not enough. Substring matching over-approximates (fewer narrowings), never under.\n4. Fail closed on any read error (a path inside a submodule cannot be read by the superproject show and stays not inert unless the reader resolves the gitlink).\nWiring: driftFor asks inertGlobalChange for each non-global package.json drift path too and adds inert ones to `inert`; invalidates() already skips the ancestor rule for `inert` after the direct-read checks. New summary counter for proofs reused only through a workspace-inert path. Tests: rule unit tests (sibling invocation, cross-package --workspaces, glob form, non-script field change) and a selectReusablePasses case where a scripts-only workspace change no longer voids a non-reading proof but still voids a reading one.\n\nOpen check before ship [inferred, unverified]: whether any gate pre-suite step runs a non-task npm script whose output the tests consume (apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts runs `npm run <script>` at the checkout root, ~L14776). If one does, both this rule and P-002's root-scripts narrowing must treat that script as runner-affecting.\n\nNot addressed here: the 1,055 proofs that READ packages/operator-core/package.json directly stay invalidated by any change to it. Finding the hub module that reads it is P-007 (C1 hub-module) territory.\n\n### D-010 — P-007 (C1): the generated DB schema is judged per exported table, not per file; the mode catalog and package.json existence probes stay as they are\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01 [self-imposed design under D-001 lever C (owner:Avi chose A+B+C); soundness bar D-002; measured 17:38-18:00Z by su-f35e5c5a; probe .papercusp/scratch/p007/yield.mts]\n\nFindings (gate proofs at 87d557e7, 2,597 rows, all inputs_captured):\n1. Edge. 1,230 proofs execute libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/schema/generated.ts and generated-relations.ts. All 1,230 also execute connection.ts and schema/index.ts, and 1,229 execute the db barrel src/index.ts. The edge is the @papercusp/db barrel -> connection.ts, which statically imports both generated namespaces to build fullSchema for drizzle({ schema }). It cannot be made lazy: drizzle needs the schema synchronously at getDb time, and these are stateful-lane tests that construct the client anyway.\n2. Churn. generated{,-relations}.ts changed in 47 libs/papercusp commits in 7 days (one per migration). Each one voids all 1,230 proofs today. Most are additive: 21 of 47 touched only new tables.\n3. Granularity yield. Split both files into top-level `export const NAME` blocks. S = blocks added/removed/changed between proof sha and target, plus the owner table of any changed relations block, closed transitively over the relations graph (a table whose relations name a member of S joins S, which covers nested `with`). A proof is affected when an executed module other than the four schema-plumbing files names a member of S as an identifier token, or binds a generated namespace and accesses it dynamically (computed member, Object.keys/values/entries/assign, spread, for-in/of, db.query[...], db._.schema). Over the 47 real commits x 1,230 proofs: 46,016 of 57,810 pairs (79.6%) survive, against 0 today. Dynamic access occurs in only 4 modules (routes/dev/tables.ts, carry-brief.test.ts, remote-access/page.test.tsx, SessionHistoryModal.test.tsx).\n4. Not pursued. (a) orchestrator mode-catalog.generated.ts (956 proofs): 6 commits in 7 days and its exported BUILTIN_MODE_CATALOG_REVISION changes on every edit, so per-symbol tracking yields nothing. (b) The 1,006 proofs that 'read' packages/operator-core/package.json: 904 come from cupboard/self-describing-store.ts walking up to the repo root with existsSync. The recorder logs existence probes as reads (FS_READ_FUNCTIONS). Splitting probes from content reads gains nothing here, because every one of those proofs executes modules beneath packages/operator-core and is already governed by the ancestor-config rule, plus D-009 for scripts-only edits.\n\nRule (implementation, scripts/lib):\n- Applies only when every drifted path a proof executes is one of the two generated schema files. Any other executed-module drift invalidates as before.\n- Header change (anything outside an export block in generated.ts: imports, pgSchema declarations) => whole-file rule. The relations import header is derived from the table list and is ignored.\n- Construction smoke, once per target sha: load the target generated + generated-relations and run drizzle's extractTablesRelationalConfig over them, which is the eager step drizzle({ schema }) performs. Failure or timeout => whole-file rule for every proof. This closes the one path by which a change to an unnamed table can break an unrelated test, a relation callback throwing at construction. Lazy relation-normalization errors only affect queries on the owning table, which S already covers.\n- Mentions are tokenized from the raw source text, comments and string literals included. That over-approximates use, which is safe. Unchanged modules are byte-identical at the proof and target shas, so reading them from the target checkout is sound. Modules that changed already invalidate.\n- Fail closed: any read or git error => whole-file rule. A new summary counter, schemaNarrowed, is printed on the TEST_PASS_REUSE line.\n- Raw SQL against a table depends on migrations, not on generated.ts. Migrations remain their own inputs, and this rule does not touch them.\n\n### D-011 — D-005 correction: post-verdict capture runs once per gate PROCESS, and a repair-queue refire moves the tree first; per-pass capture is deferred until a fresh-candidate run measures yield\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed, su-f35e5c5a; measured] D-005 said capture runs 'after each gate verdict' while 'the lock still holds the tree at the judged sha'. The second premise is FALSE for repair-queue runs.\n\nObserved: runPostVerdictPureProofCapture is called once, in the CLI's .then() after runGreenCheckpoint finally resolves (apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts ~L21811). runGreenCheckpoint recurses IN-PROCESS at two sites: the stale-candidate refire (~L13904, candidate -> tip) and the repair-admission refire (~L15195, judgedRepairHead -> newly admitted repairHead). Each recursion re-materializes the checkout through setupTree. Measured case: the 18:13Z run judged b8eb76cc (5,509 clean source=ci rows), moved the checkout to 3f0e22e9 at 19:07:39Z (checkpoint-tree reflog), and its final pass recorded 0 lane rows there. Capture read HEAD=3f0e22e9 and reported a lane that never ran. That is now reported as skip tree-moved-off-judged-sha(judged=..,head=..) (WI-10004717 fix; 28/28 tests pass; on staging, not yet in the judged candidate). Consequence: while freeze-and-converge holds a red queue, capture mints NOTHING. Over ~/.papercusp/checkpoint-logs today, 0 proofs were captured.\n\nOptions considered for true per-pass capture:\n(1) Capture before each recursion, while the tree is still at the judged head. Cost: delays the next repair pass by up to the capture budget, and spends the shared refire wall budget (refireDeadlineExceeded), so it can make a refire impossible that would otherwise fit. It slows convergence of a gate that holds main for the whole fleet.\n(2) After the final verdict, re-materialize the last sha the lane actually ran at (setupTree(judged)), capture there, and leave the tree for the next run's setupTree. Cost: adds a heavy setupTree step (pc-heavy queue, force node_modules refresh) while the run lock is held. It also interacts with incremental materialization (selectMaterializationClosure's base), and an abandoned setupTree leaves a half-materialized tree.\n\nDecision: neither is built now. Reason: capture has not yet minted a single proof in the real gate, so its base yield is unmeasured, and both options change the recursion or lock-hold path of a gate that is live-converging under another owner. Trigger to revisit: the first fresh-candidate (non-repair) run whose HEAD stays at the judged sha. Measure proofs minted and their reuse on the next run. If yield is material and repair-queue regimes keep capture at zero, implement (2), guarded by a dependency-input fingerprint equality check (dependency-generation.sh --fingerprint-ref, as checkpointDependencyInputFingerprint does), a post-setup HEAD==judged check, and the existing hard deadline. Tracked on WI-10004717.\n\nMeasured: grep -n on apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts at the staging tree, 2026-10-01T22:45Z: L21811 'await runPostVerdictPureProofCapture(cfg, runId, watchdog.cancel)' inside runGreenCheckpoint(...).then(); L13904 'return runGreenCheckpoint(cfg, deps, { ...opts, candidate: tip, ...next })' (stale-candidate refire); L15195 'return runGreenCheckpoint(cfg, deps, { ...opts, candidate: consumed.request.repairHead, admissionRefires: admissionRefires + 1, ... })' (admission refire). These are the only two recursion sites (grep 'return runGreenCheckpoint('). Capture-side skip reason: scripts/lib/pure-lane-proof-capture.mjs plan.notRun branch, tree-moved-off-judged-sha. testing:run packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/pure-lane-proof-capture.test.ts: 28 passed, 0 failed (testRunId 20452613).\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-03\nAmendment-Id: wi10005218-method-check-post1157454-approved1157469\nRequest-Hash: 483b060b4fece1a2013e9512fff69dc8eb12f9c3ea28c1d7971a571db4b0c421\nActor: su-25bc0450-2829-42b9-a2dd-1431c99e4ba8\nReason: WI-10005218 existing source-directed author repair: qualify complete METHOD and runnable checks without changing any stored outcome/falsifier/plane/scope/mandatory threshold. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"jev-memory-timeouts-to-zero-2026-10-01","title":"Jev memory calls: get the timeout rate from 3.7-12% to near zero","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Jev memory calls: get the timeout rate from 3.7-12% to near zero\nslug: jev-memory-timeouts-to-zero-2026-10-01\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n# Jev memory calls: get the timeout rate from 3.7-12% to near zero\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-005 is needs-human: live R-5 remeasurement requires Avi to re-enable Jev after the cost review. Verified 2026-10-15: workspace Jev memory mode remains off; the last memory-injection call was 2026-10-03T03:09:02Z. Existing fixes passed 77 tests across 6 project files; staging carries jev-transport.ts, while release does not yet contain the same blob. This verifies local behavior only, not the <1% live target. Continuation evidence: WI-6554700010014346; product measurement: WI-6554700010014342; original owner boundary: EI-24748208098755918. Plan activation still requires conversation/spec-quality preparation and current independent rubric acceptance; none was bypassed.\n\n**Next:** Avi decides whether to re-enable Jev after the cost review. After an explicit re-enable, resume P-005 in the existing lane, complete admission/independent acceptance preparation, verify runtime containment and >=1,000 real calls against concurrent quiet controls, and bind the unchanged R-5 outcome.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Every timeout is attributable.** Every memory-injection decision call recorded in the decision ledger carries the calling thread's event-loop utilization over the call window, so each timeout can be attributed to our own busy thread or to Jev.\n\n**R-2 — Process launches and the process scan do not stall the main thread.** Launching a child process and the periodic process reconcile scan no longer block the operator's main thread for the hundreds of milliseconds measured before this plan.\n\n**R-3 — Jev connections are reused.** Consecutive Jev calls from one operator process reuse an open keep-alive connection instead of opening a new TLS connection per call.\n\n**R-4 — A busy calling thread does not discard an answer Jev returned in time.** An answer Jev returns within the deadline is used even when the calling thread is blocked past the deadline, while a Jev answer that arrives after the deadline still times out.\n\n**R-5 — The timeout rate on new code is near zero and its residue is explained.** On a build carrying this plan's changes, memory-injection timeouts stay below 1% over at least 1,000 calls, and every remaining timeout is attributed to a named cause.\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Each item is one line:\nsingle id, status token, free text, optional blocked-by.)\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Attribute and fix\n\n- **P-001** `done` Per-call attribution: record the operator event-loop utilization over each decision call (decision_model_calls.loop_busy_ratio), so every timeout says whether our main thread or Jev ate the time. importance: high — note: Implemented in staging and tested (2026-10-02 01:40Z, su-f7ad1084). P-001: decision_model_calls.loop_busy_ms/loop_utilization populated by staging builds (surfaced rows carry them). P-003/P-004: stall fixes committed (D-001 rescope). P-006: jev-transport.ts keep-alive dispatcher wired in ensureJevDecisionClient. P-007: deadlineSignal in libs/generic/decision-model/src/client.ts; deadline.test.ts 3/3 + client.test.ts 44/44 green; proven falsifiable (old AbortSignal.timeout line fails the main case); build:typecheck 0 errors. NOT yet live on :3070 (f52b2457ba): P-005 re-measure owns the live verdict.\n- **P-002** `dropped` Hedged Jev requests: when a memory-filter request has no answer by ~p95 of a quiet single call, send one identical backup request and take the first answer; abort the loser. Bounded extra cost, ledgered. importance: high — note: Dropped per D-002: timeouts are time lost in our own busy event loop (busy p50 816 ms vs latency p50 838 ms); a hedged backup shares that loop and cannot help.\n- **P-003** `done` Stop subprocess launches freezing the big operator hosts: spawn() blocks the main thread ~100 ms per GB of heap (207 ms at 2 GB). Route operator-host child processes through a small long-lived spawn helper process (libs/generic), so the fork happens in a tiny process. importance: high — note: Implemented in staging and tested (2026-10-02 01:40Z, su-f7ad1084). P-001: decision_model_calls.loop_busy_ms/loop_utilization populated by staging builds (surfaced rows carry them). P-003/P-004: stall fixes committed (D-001 rescope). P-006: jev-transport.ts keep-alive dispatcher wired in ensureJevDecisionClient. NOT yet live on :3070 (f52b2457ba): P-005 re-measure owns the live verdict.\n- **P-004** `done` Move the task-manager reconcile scan (scanProcesses -> walkCgroupTree, readProcFacts) off synchronous fs on the main thread. importance: high — note: Implemented in staging and tested (2026-10-02 01:40Z, su-f7ad1084). P-001: decision_model_calls.loop_busy_ms/loop_utilization populated by staging builds (surfaced rows carry them). P-003/P-004: stall fixes committed (D-001 rescope). NOT yet live on :3070 (f52b2457ba): P-005 re-measure owns the live verdict.\n- **P-005** `needs-human` Re-measure against a concurrent quiet-process control on every host (probe .papercusp/scratch/jev-quiet-control-probe.mts); target new-code timeout rate < 1% and attribute the residue. importance: high — note: 2026-10-15 continuation WI-6554700010014346 verified existing fixes with 77/77 local tests in 6 project files. Live R-5 remeasurement is blocked by the current owner setting jev_memory_injection:papercusp-workspace=off (readback 2026-10-15 06:28Z; last memory-injection ledger call 2026-10-03T03:09:02Z). Governing owner-verified relay coord-send-70a134ceeecd0e34a0ca5b2d7cd895649d15b239b7d00c0e951157b34d9004a6 prohibits re-enabling paid shadow/On or funded bulk benchmarks without fresh approval. Preserve R-5: >=1,000 calls on fixed build incl release operator, <1% all no-answer outcomes, zero unattributed. Resume only after owner re-enables following cost review; source-conversation/spec-quality/independent acceptance gates remain required before activation/ship. Existing root item EI-24748208098755918 holds the owner boundary.\n- **P-006** `done` Keep the Jev connection open between calls: a dedicated undici keep-alive dispatcher for the decision client (packages/operator-core/lib/memory/jev-transport.ts), idle timeout sized under api.typesafe.ai's measured server-side idle limit. Measured 2026-10-01: default global fetch closes idle sockets after 4 s while each host calls Jev ~every 10 s, so most calls paid DNS (libuv threadpool) + TCP + TLS: +30-90 ms typical, 400-1400 ms cold, against the 800 ms budget. importance: high — note: Implemented in staging and tested (2026-10-02 01:40Z, su-f7ad1084). P-001: decision_model_calls.loop_busy_ms/loop_utilization populated by staging builds (surfaced rows carry them). P-003/P-004: stall fixes committed (D-001 rescope). P-006: jev-transport.ts keep-alive dispatcher wired in ensureJevDecisionClient. P-007: deadlineSignal in libs/generic/decision-model/src/client.ts; deadline.test.ts 3/3 + client.test.ts 44/44 green; proven falsifiable (old AbortSignal.timeout line fails the main case); build:typecheck 0 errors. NOT yet live on :3070 (f52b2457ba): P-005 re-measure owns the live verdict.\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase — implementation\n\n- **P-007** `done` Stall-tolerant decision deadline: AbortSignal.timeout fires in Node's timers phase BEFORE the poll phase reads a response that arrived while the main thread was blocked, so a Jev answer already in the socket buffer is recorded as a timeout. Defer the deadline abort one setImmediate (after the poll phase) so already-arrived I/O is read first; a provider that genuinely has not answered still times out at the deadline. libs/generic/decision-model/src/client.ts deadlineSignal + real-socket test deadline.test.ts (positive control + budget-preserved case). importance: high — note: Implemented in staging and tested (2026-10-02 01:40Z, su-f7ad1084). P-001: decision_model_calls.loop_busy_ms/loop_utilization populated by staging builds (surfaced rows carry them). P-003/P-004: stall fixes committed (D-001 rescope). P-006: jev-transport.ts keep-alive dispatcher wired in ensureJevDecisionClient. P-007: deadlineSignal in libs/generic/decision-model/src/client.ts; deadline.test.ts 3/3 + client.test.ts 44/44 green; proven falsifiable (old AbortSignal.timeout line fails the main case); build:typecheck 0 errors. NOT yet live on :3070 (f52b2457ba): P-005 re-measure owns the live verdict.\n- **P-008** `done` P-008: Jev transport whose answer survives a busy calling thread (worker thread + synchronous drain at the deadline) — [self-imposed, evidence D-003] Since 02:06Z, 17 of 21 newer-build timeouts had ELU >= 0.9 on the calling thread; P-007 (one setImmediate deferral) rescues an answer only if it is fully buffered by the next poll phase. Design: run the Jev fetch + JSON parse in a per-process worker_thread that owns the keep-alive dispatcher (jev-transport.ts) and posts { answer, workerLatencyMs } on a MessagePort. On the main thread, when the deadline timer fires, call receiveMessageOnPort(port) synchronously before declaring timeout: an answer the worker completed within the deadline is used even though the main thread was busy. A genuinely slow Jev still times out at 800 ms (worker-measured). Record both workerLatencyMs and main-thread latency in decision_model_calls so the split stays measurable. Acceptance: a test that blocks the main thread past the deadline while a local server answers in 100 ms gets an answer; a server that answers at 1,200 ms still times out; then on staging, timeouts with ELU >= 0.9 drop to ~0 over >= 1,000 calls. Seam: libs/generic/decision-model createDecisionClient already accepts an injected fetch; the worker transport plugs in there without touching consumers. importance: high — note: Live acceptance met: 6/1,004 (0.60%) on new builds 04:13-05:53Z; residue attributed (calling-thread ELU 0.84-1.0, post-restart + box load); worker-side timing follow-up WI-10005319. WI-10005266 done.\n\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Plan items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | live |\n| R-2 | P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-007, P-008 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005, P-008 | live |\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append. Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n\n### D-001 — P-003 re-scoped: the spawn helper already exists; remove redundant local forks instead\nDate: 2026-10-01\n[self-imposed, measured 2026-10-01 21:37-21:42Z by su-f7ad1084, bpftrace fentry/fexit kernel_clone + sched_process_exec over the dev-api, bg-host and staging-api cgroups; scratch .papercusp/scratch/p003-clone-trace.out + p003-exec-argv.out]\n\nFinding: the 'small long-lived spawn helper' P-003 proposed already exists. It is the spawner sidecar (fleet/git-via-sidecar.ts, WI-10002709 / WI-10004975), and it is live on all three hosts (sockets /tmp/papercusp-spawner-3194993.sock, -1996367, /tmp/pcv/-3389995). All parent forks were plain fork (no CLONE_VFORK). Parent time inside kernel_clone was 16-55 ms per fork, and one :3070 worker spent 6.0 s of 60 s frozen there (236 forks).\n\nThe steady remaining local forks come from gitPipelinePosition's unit-start probe. git-pipeline-position.ts realProbeUnitStart deliberately bypasses the sidecar with a local pexec (EI-24356772206513832, to dodge a 10 s sidecar-startup timeout). Each gitPipelinePosition({path}) probes the serving unit, then all 4 GENERATION_HOSTS, then the serving-runtime census. Each probe costs 2 forks (systemctl show + ps -o etimes=). work_items:get fans this out over up to 12 evidence paths in parallel (deploymentPositionForEvidence), so one work_items:get can cost on the order of 100 forks on a 1.5-4 GB host. Measured on :3170: 30 systemctl + 30 ps in 30 s.\n\nDecision: P-003 delivers (1) a single-flight, 2 s hard-TTL memo of the unit-start probe via @papercusp/cache, so concurrent paths and repeated reads share one probe; a stale read errs toward 'not yet running your code', the conservative direction; (2) probeServiceStart computes etimes from /proc/uptime and /proc/<pid>/stat exactly as procps does, keeping ps only as the fallback when /proc cannot answer. The bg-host git scan seen in the trace is the worktree-coverage watchdog's boot pass plus hourly runs: transient, not addressed here.\n\n### D-002 — Drop P-002 (hedged Jev requests): the time is lost in our own event loop, which a backup request shares\nDate: 2026-10-01\nEvidence (decision_model_calls, consumer=memory-injection, last 6 h, the 190 rows that carry P-001 loop data): timed-out calls (n=13) had loop_busy_ms p50 816 against latency p50 838, average loop utilization 0.94. Answered calls (n=177) had busy p50 207 against latency p50 233, utilization 0.83. The operator's event loop was busy for almost the entire request window, so the request waits on our own thread, not on Jev. A hedged backup is issued and its response is read by the same blocked loop, so it cannot shorten the wait, and it doubles Jev spend on exactly the calls that are already late. P-002 is therefore dropped.\n\nThe levers that remain: (1) get today's fixes onto :3070, which serves 78% of Jev memory traffic from f52b2457ba with none of P-001/P-003/P-006 (11.0% timeouts on those NULL-surface rows); (2) find and remove what keeps the operator loops at 0.8-0.9 utilization (P-003 and P-004 removed two measured sources); (3) P-005 re-measures after both deploy. Revisit hedging only if a future measurement shows timeouts with a quiet local loop (utilization < 0.3 on timed-out rows).\n\n### D-003 — P-002 (backup/hedged Jev request) stays dropped: the newer-build residue is our busy thread, not Jev\nDate: 2026-10-02\n[self-imposed, measured 2026-10-02 03:2xZ by su-f7ad1084; supersedes my 03:16Z claim that the newer-build residue is Jev's own floor]\n\nEvidence: decision_model_calls consumer=memory-injection, surface IS NOT NULL (the newer builds, :3170 + bg-host), since :3170 began serving P-007 (2026-10-02T02:06:13Z): 21 timeouts in 1,019 calls (2.1%). Event-loop utilization over the call window averaged 0.93 on failed calls vs 0.66 on answered calls. 17 of 21 failures had ELU >= 0.9; 8 of 21 fired the 800 ms timer late (0.9-2 s, one >2 s), i.e. our thread was blocked at the deadline. Only 1 failure had ELU < 0.5 (an idle thread genuinely waiting on Jev).\n\nWhy this is a distinguishing test: if Jev's latency tail caused the failures, a timed-out call's longer window would sample the thread at its ordinary busyness (~0.66); a mean of 0.93 means failures coincide with our thread being unusually busy.\n\nDecision: do not build P-002. A second request issued from the same busy thread is read late for the same reason the first one is. The remaining lever for the newer builds is main-thread busyness on the calling worker (answered calls already average ELU 0.66), not a Jev-side workaround. Revisit only if a measurement shows failures with ELU < 0.5 exceeding ~0.5% of calls.\n\nRetraction: my 03:16Z loop checkpoint and EI-24835843868018036 said the ~2.2% newer-build residue 'sits inside Jev's own measured floor'. That was an inference from comparing rates with the quiet-process floor, not a per-call measurement, and the per-call ELU split above falsifies it.\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-02\nAmendment-Id: ei2474-amend-a1a6-apply-1\nRequest-Hash: 294c6cce5c55fa61a1f55d96cb13182cc143c2254573ab0ae0730e3c35a0cf49\nActor: su-f7ad1084-1707-4238-bb66-0577aa8bc067\nReason: Apply rubric-vetting revisions A1-A6 from consult conv-muqne2yg (reply coord_event_log 22831171): concrete falsifiers, named query methods, bound test checks, requiredTestLayers and intent.sourceRefs. BAR meaning (model text) is unchanged. A2 asked to split R-2 into two BARs; it is expressed instead as two separately falsifiable clauses (a) and (b), each with its pre-plan measurement and its own bound test file, because splitting the BAR key would orphan the spec clauses AUTO-BAR-R-2-P-003 and AUTO-BAR-R-2-P-004 already bound to R-2.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-703575c0-65c0-465d-ab97-9f2dfb0d2b98\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1155160\nApproved-At: 2026-10-02T07:50:41.306Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 23 → 24\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-005 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-02\nAmendment-Id: ei2474-amend-rev4-apply-1\nRequest-Hash: af770ad25d92f6f96cb0ea35674d52fbbdb730da07b07a40905eb0102a3d30cf\nActor: su-f7ad1084-1707-4238-bb66-0577aa8bc067\nReason: R-5 BAR change. Rev 3 counted only inconclusive_reason='timeout' as a failure while every call stayed in the denominator, so a transport that fails fast instead of timing out lowers the measured rate. Measured with dev:pg_query over harness_shared.decision_model_calls (consumer memory-injection): in 24 h the old build (surface NULL) recorded 0 network-error rows in 58,970 calls, while the new builds (surface NOT NULL) recorded 221 network-error rows (1.43%), all in 06:14-06:37Z (WI-10005372). Over the last 2 h of new-build traffic, rev 3 reads timeout_pct 0.21% (healthy) while 15.40% of calls got no answer. Rev 4 bounds the no-answer rate (any non-NULL inconclusive_reason) below 1%, keeps timeout_pct as the reported headline, requires a cause for every failure (a non-timeout failure needs a non-empty inconclusive_detail), and adds the transport columns the rev-3 vetter asked for (unattributed = failures minus the disjoint named causes). R-3 method: the measured server-side idle limit must be stated with its value and source (vetter note 2; method-only).\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-5e71ffb3-0874-46d3-9297-6473f81df0cb\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1155178\nApproved-At: 2026-10-02T08:07:25.148Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 24 → 25\nChanged BARs: R-5\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"observation-candidate-acceptance-promotion-2026-09-30","title":"Drain observation and candidate intake through bulk review, then promote accepted work","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Drain observation and candidate intake through bulk review, then promote accepted work\nslug: observation-candidate-acceptance-promotion-2026-09-30\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-05\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-05, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_missing. P-001/P-002 done; P-003 code committed at f6d543ffd05a, closure waits on EI-24761061357755499.\n\n**Next:** su-fd916e65: settle EI-24761061357755499 and close P-003; then P-005 (acceptance contract + producer enrollment per D-009a/b), P-004, P-006, P-007 (incl. WI-10004706 view floor), P-010, P-008, P-009, P-011, P-012; then rubric vetting, independent grading and ship.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10004564 — Baseline the current filing, consumption, review, promotion, claim and count writers; enumerate supported record/producer paths and existing plan decisions. Produce a same-scope cohort census, the le… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004565 — Extend the existing shared stage/readiness derivation for observations, unverified candidates, accepted work and terminal history; version malformed/missing/legacy behavior explicitly and keep source… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004566 — Extend digest/fold and stable-identity intake adapters to assemble current evidence and existing canonical references; preserve distinct remedies, stale/unknown evidence and occurrence histories. Preserve scope snapshots, livenes… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004568 — Extend agent-review/readiness evidence with the current acceptance contract and revision binding; independent reviewers or authorized existing policy write acceptance, source edits invalidate it, and… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004569 — Implement atomic idempotent acceptance-to-canonical-work promotion using existing create/update/link writers and receipt storage. Preserve source observations, reuse an existing candidate/item when a… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004570 — Wire the current acceptance contract into all ordinary execution and advertised claimability paths using shared predicates; retain existing origin/hold/dependency/plan/fleet safeguards and exact-row … <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004571 — Extend the existing resolver/reviewer launch and registered task lanes to drain intake separately from accepted implementation; route approved scoped investigations to an appropriate work lane. Accep… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004572 — Extend the existing compensation and audit contract for intake dispositions and promotions, including re-review on new evidence and safe handling of taken/completed work. Acceptance: undo/retry is id… <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004573 — Update queue/review/leader presentation and shared aggregation writers to show intake, accepted ready/active/blocked work and verified completion separately, with clear reasons and links to evidence/… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004574 — Execute the approved legacy adoption policy in bounded report-first cohorts and a named current-build canary, preserving active claims and intentional parks. Use backup:snapshot_create before any ris… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004575 — Add and run project-native regression/integration/UI tests, conduct an independent requirement-by-requirement current-build journey review, and record final promotion/shipment against the exact deplo… <!-- P-012 -->\n## Background\n\nThe shared work_items ledger contains observation evidence, unverified reports/proposals, accepted work and terminal history. An open record does not establish executable work. The preceding explanation called a broad, overlapping diagnostic population remaining bugs, which obscured those distinctions. Avi asked why observations appeared, how unapproved candidates reached the queue, whether intake itself could be drained, and whether the existing bulk acceptance process could promote candidates/observations into work.\n\nCurrent source already provides observation-lane exclusion and consumption metadata, duplicate admission, agent review, versioned implementationReadiness, saved bulk runs, live action manifests, action dispatch, confidence/authority controls and compensation. The proposal extends those surfaces. Its new behavior is an explicit, evidence-backed handoff from intake to accepted executable work.\n\n## Goal\n\nMake observations and candidates drainable through attributable triage while ensuring that an ordinary implementation fleet receives only accepted work with current evidence, a defined outcome and a completion check. Explain every queue stage clearly, preserve source evidence, and show useful verified delivery separately from duplicate/invalid closures.\n\n## Scope\n\nThis is a follow-on to issue-intake-outcome-accounting-2026-09-23, work-queue-admission-and-bulk-dedup-2026-08-24, bulk-resolve-dispositions-confidence-2026-08-28, learning-loop-identity-and-consumption-2026-08-08 and the existing independent agent-review lifecycle. It adds intake dispositions and an acceptance-to-execution contract; it does not repeat those plans' capture stamping, duplicate algorithm or general bulk controls.\n\nObservation and candidate are product/lifecycle distinctions, not a mandate for new tables. Reuse existing lane, review/readiness payloads, links, runs and scheduler floors. No second work ledger, independent bulk engine, bespoke agent loop or new recurring routine is proposed. Observation time-series lifecycle remains intact. Current fleet leadership and its active claims are outside the implementation scope.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Keep observations outside executable bug work.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Observations remain evidence outside ordinary implementation claims and bug-work counts.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Observations remain evidence outside ordinary implementation claims and bug-work counts.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An observation is included in ordinary implementation claims or bug-work counts.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run shared stage/readiness fixtures covering observation, pending/revised/accepted candidates, legacy/unknown metadata and SQL parity; inspect current queue projections.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review-policy.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-13 — Keep candidates visible until acceptance.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Candidates remain visible as intake until a qualifying acceptance decision exists.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Candidates remain visible as intake until a qualifying acceptance decision exists.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A candidate is hidden, terminalized, or exposed to implementation before a qualifying acceptance decision exists.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run shared stage/readiness fixtures covering observation, pending/revised/accepted candidates, legacy/unknown metadata and SQL parity; Merge/link adds evidence to an existing candidate or accepted item and preserves its current approval scope. Retain/reject concludes the current triage question while leaving the source evidence intact. Retry/revision remains in intake with a missing-evidence reason, an owner and a specific retry condition.\n\n### Reused implementation surfaces\n\n- Intake classification and readiness: packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review-policy.ts, capture-core.ts, agent-review.ts and the existing work-item payload/link contract.\n- Evidence grouping and consumption: harness/improvements/digest.ts, observation-fold.ts, observation-consumption.ts, Scout pattern references and existing keyed occurrence/coalescing paths.\n- Saved review and actions: attention/bulk-run-store.ts, bulk-dispositions.ts, bulk-run-reversal.ts, agent-tools/inbox/bulk-run.ts, the attention action dispatcher and the existing automation-policy ladder.\n- Owner review: apps/operator/app/_components/inbox/use-inbox-bulk-run.ts and the existing bulk report/card components. Search the design component registry before drafting UI specifications.\n- Execution: scheduler/get-next.ts, work-items.ts, issues-engineer.ts and their shared admission/readiness fragments. Extend one shared acceptance predicate; do not maintain separate hand-written eligibility rules.\n\nImplement classification as a versioned, shared derivation over existing metadata. Extend implementationReadiness/review evidence with the accepted source revision and required completion contract rather than introducing a parallel acceptance store. Keep duplicate admission's duplication-only charter and bounded fail-open; acceptance remains an independent readiness obligation.\n\nUse the existing bulk run's immutable membership/filter/policy snapshot and real live action list. Add intake source adapters and promotion dispositions through that machinery. Choose an additional run-kind case only if the existing run contract cannot represent intake membership, document the reason, and keep the same store/dispatcher/compensation path.\n\nPerform acceptance and promotion at the existing mutation seam with current-row validation and idempotency derived from workspace/harness, stable candidate identity and acceptance revision. A persistence or dispatch failure must not be reported as successful promotion. Link source observations through existing reference edges, and keep a queryable promotion/disposition receipt on the current canonical surfaces.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-24 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-25 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-26 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-27 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-28 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-29 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-30 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-31 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-32 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-33 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-011 | live |\n| R-34 | P-011 | live |\n| R-35 | P-011 | live |\n| R-36 | P-011 | live |\n| R-37 | P-011 | live |\n| R-12 | P-012 | deployed |\n| R-38 | P-012 | deployed |\n| R-39 | P-012 | deployed |\n| R-40 | P-012 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Define intake and group evidence\n\n- **P-001** `done` Baseline the current filing, consumption, review, promotion, claim and count writers; enumerate supported record/producer paths and existing plan decisions. They govern this plan's execution; the existing bug fleet continues on its current work lane.\n\n### D-001 — Intake can be drained while observations remain evidence\nDate: 2026-09-30\nDrain means giving the current observation/candidate an attributable disposition. Source observation rows retain their time-series identity and lifecycle. Only a separately accepted task enters implementation.\n\n### D-002 — Extend existing bulk acceptance and review\nDate: 2026-09-30\nReuse saved bulk runs, real actions, review/readiness, policy controls, source links and compensation. Default review remains agent-based; this proposal creates no requirement for Avi to approve each routine candidate manually.\n\n### D-003 — Duplicate admission is insufficient execution approval\nDate: 2026-09-30\nKeep the existing duplication-only admission charter. Its fail-open/bypass/legacy values cannot independently satisfy the proposed acceptance contract. A valid immediate-policy path must produce an attributable current acceptance receipt, and any emergency scope must be explicit. Final plan/ship acceptance remains a separate later verification step.\n\n### D-004 — Legacy adoption is measured and staged\nDate: 2026-09-30\nBaseline and propose the cohort/cutover policy before applying it. Protect in-flight claims and intentional holds, preserve uncertain evidence and show remaining legacy exemptions explicitly until the adoption completes. No age-only rejection or mass deletion is permitted.\n\n### D-005 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: intake-atomic-bars-v6-lossless-split-apply\nRequest-Hash: 858be55320dfd32af3e9b8704d1c3255710559574f7457f14a481ea95e0281bc\nActor: su-c6ebfcdb-4118-495d-bbfa-d83998682668\nReason: Outside-lineage review post 1152362 rejected revision 5 because its 12 shortened BARs dropped mandatory clauses. The audit corrections are D-009.\n\n### D-011 — P-005 contract shape and non-breaking producer enrollment (refines D-009a/b)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while implementing P-005 (WI-10004568).\n1. Contract: the R-4 acceptance contract lives inside implementationReadiness.evidence.acceptance (no parallel store): problem, evidence[], outcome, scope, completionCheck + contractVersion implementation-acceptance-v1, authority, reason, sourceRevision, acceptedAt. Only sealImplementationAcceptance builds it and it refuses rather than defaults a missing field.\n2. Authority (R-20): agent-review with reviewer different from submittedBy, or an allowlisted existing policy (IMPLEMENTATION_ACCEPTANCE_POLICIES, initially trusted-tool-failure-promotion). Confidence, grade thresholds, dedup admission, severity/security tags and explicit assignment are never authority.\n3. Revision binding (R-21): sourceRevision = src-v1:sha256(item_kind US title US summary), computed identically in TS and SQL (acceptanceSourceRevisionSql). Staleness is enforced at READ time by the shared derivation (deriveWorkItemIntakeStage / workItemIntakeStageSql: acceptance=stale-revision, reReviewRequested=true, stage stays candidate), so no writer can bypass invalidation by skipping a hook. Re-review is requested through the intake queue (P-004/P-008).\n4. Producer enrollment (D-009a): createIssue (the seam every issue-family writer funnels through) stamps rows that arrive without a verdict as status unknown, source creation-enrollment. To keep P-005 non-breaking for running fleets, every claim floor treats creation-enrollment/unknown exactly like the absent-key legacy exception (implementationReadinessIsLegacyEquivalent + SQL twin in implementationReadinessNormalExclusionSql; promoter and triage route it to their absent branches). P-007 bounds BOTH by the recorded enforcement cutover (D-009b) behind the R-37 canary.\n5. capture-core's existing-immediate-capture-policy 'ready' (and trusted-tool-failure 'ready') are left unchanged in P-005: a bare 'ready' never qualifies as acceptance (stage candidate, reason ready-without-executable-acceptance), and converting them changes dedup-merge and triage behaviour, so the conversion belongs to P-011's canary-gated adoption (R-36/R-37).\n6. Agent-review approval seals the producer's proposal when complete; an incomplete proposal is not defaulted (approval stays a bare ready, still intake). Review transitions carry an unsealed proposal forward instead of dropping it.\nRelated: P-005, P-007, P-011\n\n### D-012 — P-004 intake decision shape (refines R-3/R-18/R-19)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while implementing P-004 (WI-10004567).\n1. Vocabulary: six typed intake dispositions promote | merge | investigate | retain | reject | retry live in attention/bulk-dispositions.ts (BULK_INTAKE_DISPOSITIONS). Intake inputs are attention items whose kind is in INTAKE_ATTENTION_KINDS (today: 'improvement').\n2. Storage: one nullable jsonb column attention_bulk_run_items.intake_decision (migration 1296) beside the existing disposition/recommendation columns; no new table, run kind or engine. A CHECK repeats the validator: every decision has a non-blank reason and decidedBy (so reject always has a reason, R-3; attributable, R-18), merge needs targetRef, retry needs missingInformation.\n3. Projection: each intake disposition also projects onto the existing recommendation vocabulary (promote->routed, merge/retain/reject->cleanup_candidate, investigate->investigate, retry->retry_needed) so counters, settle and the report UI keep working unchanged.\n4. Resume (R-19): reports overwrite only the reported rows; unreached rows stay pending and failed rows stay visible; requeue clears intake_decision only for rows it deliberately resets.\n5. Execution of promote/merge (creating or linking canonical work) is P-006 at the existing mutation seam; P-004 records validated decisions with an owned next step and offers the six in the manifest.\n\n### D-013 — P-006 intake execution shape (refines R-5/R-22/R-23/R-28/R-29)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while implementing P-006 (WI-10004569). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. One module, packages/operator-core/lib/attention/intake-promotion.ts, executes a recorded P-004 intake decision (attention_bulk_run_items.intake_decision) for an improvement source issue. It is reached from the existing terminal-action dispatcher when an intake recommendation is applied; no new run kind, table or engine. retry executes nothing (the input stays in intake, owner agent).\n2. Kind (fix/build/investigation): promote carries optional workKind fix|build -> bug|change (default: the candidate's own issue kind; an observation defaults to fix -> bug); investigate executes as promotion to an investigation task (kind task). The P-004 validator is extended to accept workKind on promote only.\n3. Identity (R-22): a suitable candidate (issue-family, lane not observation, non-terminal) is promoted IN PLACE and keeps its id; an observation source yields a DISTINCT new item via the existing createIssue writer and is retained unchanged except for an intakeExecution pointer.\n4. Acceptance (R-5, D-011): promotion seals the P-005 contract with sealImplementationAcceptance using the source proposal; authority agent-review, reviewer = the decision's decidedBy, submittedBy = the source filer (self-review refused). An unsealable proposal REFUSES the promotion (missing fields listed); nothing is created and no ready receipt exists.\n5. Atomicity and idempotency (R-5/R-23): per-source key intake-exec:<sourceId>:<sourceRevision>, serialized with a transaction-scoped advisory lock. A new item is created with its source link (payload.intakeSource), acceptance provenance (implementationReadiness.evidence.acceptance) and promotion receipt (payload.intakePromotion) in ONE insert, so none can be visible without the others. A key lookup makes retries, double accepts and overlapping runs converge on one item; the graph edges and the source pointer are completed idempotently on retry, and the source pointer reads complete only after both exist. A changed source revision is a different key and is refused while an accepted promotion for the prior revision exists.\n6. Merge (R-28): target must exist and be non-terminal. The source evidence is appended to the target (payload.intakeMergedSources, deduped by source id) with bidirectional links (merged-into / merged-from); the target's remedy and acceptance are untouched. The source row is retained; a candidate source is closed as a duplicate only when it carries no distinct remedy (no acceptance outcome, or the same normalized outcome as the target), otherwise it stays open with its own obligation.\n7. Retain/reject (R-29): records payload.intakeDisposition {disposition, reason, decidedBy, runId, itemId, decidedAt, occurrenceWatermark = max work_item_occurrences.occurrence_id}. It never deletes or terminalizes the row or its occurrence series. A later occurrence above the watermark derives state reopened at read time, so new evidence reopens the same decision on the same row instead of creating a new report.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-010\n\n### D-014 — P-006 execution refinements: decision carries proposal + judged revision; apply-intake action (refines D-013)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while implementing P-006 (WI-10004569). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Producers do not write acceptance proposals today (capture-core writes none), so an observation could never be sealed from its own payload. A promote/investigate intake decision therefore MAY carry `acceptance` (problem/evidence/outcome/scope/completionCheck) drafted by the resolver; its fields win over the source proposal. Completeness is judged only at execution: a missing field refuses (acceptance-incomplete) and writes nothing. Authority stays agent-review with reviewer = decidedBy and submittedBy = the source filer; a source with no recorded filer refuses (independence cannot be shown).\n2. Every intake decision records `sourceRevision`, stamped server-side by inbox:bulk-run-report from the live source at report time (not caller-supplied). promote/investigate execution refuses when it is absent (source-revision-unjudged) or differs from the current revision (source-revision-changed), so an edit between decision and execution can never become a ready receipt for unreviewed content.\n3. Execution is reached through the shared terminal dispatcher with actionId `apply-intake` (INTAKE_APPLY_ACTION_ID) on an improvement ref plus the recorded decision; the server injects `executeIntakeDecision`. inbox:bulk-run-act applies it only to a run row that carries a validated intake_decision and whose item is still live; it is not a card button, and the standing automation policy gate still applies. A refusal throws its detail so the item is recorded failed, never resolved.\n4. In-place promotion requires a non-observation candidate whose storage kind equals the target kind (workKind fix->bug, build->change; investigate->task). Otherwise a distinct item is created and the candidate is retained and linked (promoted-to / promoted-from).\n5. retain/reject on a non-observation candidate also writes readiness not-ready (reason intake-retain / intake-reject) so it is held from claiming; the row is never terminalized or deleted.\nRelated: P-006, P-008, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-015 — P-006 idempotency is DB-fenced: unique promotion-key index (migration 1298); the advisory lock is bounded and only orders appends\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while verifying P-006 (WI-10004569). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Finding (measured): the first P-006 integration run created TWO distinct promoted items for a double accept. A probe showed the two concurrent executors' lazily imported DB accessor resolved to different clients, so their transaction advisory locks never contended. A raw begin + pg_advisory_xact_lock on one client serializes correctly. Correctness that depends on every executor reaching the same lock on the same client is too fragile.\n2. Ruling: one row per promotion key is a database guarantee. Migration 1298 adds the UNIQUE partial index work_items_intake_promotion_key_uniq ON work_items ((payload->'intakePromotion'->>'key')) WHERE payload ? 'intakePromotion'. The receipt key is intake-exec:<sourceId>:<sourceRevision>. A source revision is promoted at most once, in place or distinct. Any later decision for the same revision converges on that row.\n3. The executor looks the key up first (findByPromotionKey). On a unique violation (23505 on that index, cause chain walked), the create or in-place write converges on the winning row and completes its edges and pointer idempotently.\n4. The advisory lock stays, but only to order merge appends and disposition writes per source/target. Its WAIT is bounded by lock_timeout (INTAKE_LOCK_WAIT_BUDGET_MS = 10s, reset once held), reusing the acquirePlanAdvisoryLock pattern, so queued waiters cannot pin the org pool. The DB accessor is imported statically.\n5. Verification owed: a lock-bypassed double accept must still yield exactly one row (falsifiable by dropping the index or the 23505 catch).\n\n### D-016 — P-007 claim-floor shape: one shared acceptance floor, cutover 2026-10-02T00:00:00Z, by-id/assignment covered (refines D-009b/c/d)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01\nRecorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) before implementing P-007 (WI-10004706). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Cutover: IMPLEMENTATION_ACCEPTANCE_ENFORCEMENT_CUTOVER = 2026-10-02T00:00:00.000Z (epoch ms 1790899200000), a TS constant in agent-review-policy.ts. The migration repeats the literal and a unit test pins the two. Compared against work_items.created_ts (engineer_issues.created_at). A NULL created_ts is treated as pre-cutover legacy (historical rows only). Chosen a few hours ahead so P-005 producer enrollment is deployed before enforcement begins.\n2. One predicate: implementationReadinessFloorSql gains acceptanceState + createdAt inputs. A row passes when (a) readiness is valid, status ready and acceptance qualifying, or (b) it was created before the cutover and passes the old floor (absent key, ready, or creation-enrollment unknown) and its acceptance is not stale-revision or invalid-authority. Post-cutover rows with absent metadata, unknown, not-ready, or ready without qualifying acceptance are held. A stale or invalid acceptance is held regardless of age (R-6 stale-approved).\n3. Paths: self-pull (claimNextIssueWorkItem, get-next census, issues-engineer listing, work_items:claimable) inherit it through agentReviewNormalExclusionSql. By-id and leader-dispatch (assignment) claims in claimIssue add the same floor for a new holder. Exempt: a same-holder re-claim, the agent-review reviewer admission, and self-filed fallout (the creator claiming its own filing). Creating an item with an assignee is authoring, not taking intake, and is not gated.\n4.
