This resolves WI-10004706.\nRelated: P-005, P-007, P-011\n\n### D-017 — P-007 SQL floor shape: 12-arg work_item_claim_floors overload + TS-rendered helper, no (workspace_id, feature_id) lookup (refines D-016 §SQL)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while implementing P-007 (WI-10004706). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Finding (measured 2026-10-01 ~13:15Z, PG 18.4): D-016 said the 9-arg work_item_claim_floors would look up item_kind/summary/created_ts by (workspace_id, feature_id). That lookup is unindexed (only work_items_pkey (harness_slug, feature_id) and the scoped identity index lead with other columns), the view evaluates it for ~133.6k open issue-family rows, and (workspace_id, feature_id) is NOT unique: 89 duplicate pairs. A lookup would be slow AND ambiguous.\n2. Ruling: migration 1301 adds (a) harness_shared.work_item_implementation_readiness_admits(payload, item_kind, title, summary, created_ts) STABLE PARALLEL SAFE, whose body is implementationReadinessNormalExclusionSql(sql, 'payload', 'work_items') RENDERED by postgres.js with parameters inlined (not hand-translated); (b) a 12-arg overload work_item_claim_floors(<9 args>, item_kind, summary, created_ts) = 9-arg labels + 'implementation-readiness' when (a) refuses; (c) work_items_claimable recreated to call the 12-arg overload with the row's own columns. The 9-arg function is unchanged and documented as lacking floor #16.\n3. Correction to WI-10004706's premise: the agent-review pending/revision-requested floor IS already in the view via work_item_claim_floors_v15 (migration 860); only floor #16 was missing.\n4. Guard: claim-ssot-agreement.integration.test.ts applies 1301, re-renders the TS fragment and asserts the helper body matches it (whitespace-normalized), and checks the view against the TS twin implementationReadinessAdmitsClaim over a pre/post-cutover row matrix.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-018 — Defer post-cutover enforcement to P-011: P-007 ships floor #16 with a sentinel cutover (supersedes D-016 §1 date)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while implementing P-007 (WI-10004706). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Finding: D-016 set IMPLEMENTATION_ACCEPTANCE_ENFORCEMENT_CUTOVER = 2026-10-02T00:00Z. Past that instant every NEW bug/change/task without a qualifying sealed acceptance (absent, creation-enrollment unknown, ready without acceptance) is unclaimable by anyone but its filer or reviewer. Today that is ~69% of new work (D-009), and the intake drain that would review it (P-008) and the cohort baseline/canary (P-011) do not exist yet, so enforcement tonight would strand new work. It also violates the 2026-09-30 decision text 'Baseline and propose the cohort/cutover policy before applying it'. And it plants a wall-clock time bomb: integration tests that createIssue() at real time and claim by id as another agent (e.g. issues-engineer.integration.test.ts) pass today and red the gate after the date.\n2. Ruling: P-007 ships the full mechanism (one shared floor in TS + SQL migration 1301, by-id/assignment coverage, exemptions per D-016 §3). Active now regardless of age: a stale-revision or invalid-authority acceptance refuses (R-6). The created-after-cutover arm is DEFERRED: the cutover constant is the sentinel 2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z (epoch ms 4102444800000); migration 1301 renders the same literal from TS. P-011 owns lowering it: baseline the cohort, propose the cutover, run the named canary, then a new migration + constant bump, and first make every wall-clock claim test independent of the cutover (seed created_ts explicitly).\n3. Tests assert post-cutover behaviour with explicit created_ts = cutover + 60s, so they stay valid when P-011 lowers the constant.\nRelated: D-016, D-017, D-009, P-007, P-011\nRelated: P-007, P-011\n\n### D-019 — P-009 compensation shape: intake inverses live in the existing bulk-item reversal; correction instead of revoke for owned/active/delivered work; apply-time kill-switch recheck\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) before implementing P-009 (WI-10004572). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Seat. No new undo surface. The inverse of an applied intake decision is a new branch of compensateAttentionBulkRunItem (attention/bulk-run-reversal.ts), selected when the run item's actionId is INTAKE_APPLY_ACTION_ID ('apply-intake'). It runs inside executeBulkRunItemReversal's row-locked transaction. That reuses the existing exactly-once fence (FOR UPDATE + already_reverted + reverted_at appended only after compensation succeeds) and the reversal window. The intake-specific logic lives in a new module, attention/intake-compensation.ts. Every write takes the caller's TransactionSql, so any thrown step rolls the whole reversal back and is reported to the caller. A failed inverse is never hidden (R-9 falsifier).\n\n2. Inverse per recorded outcome (R-9):\n- promote, distinct: if the promoted item is revocable (see 3), set it to dropped with a reversal reason. Move its payload.intakePromotion receipt to payload.intakePromotionReversed[], which frees the 1298 unique key so a later re-promotion of the same revision executes fresh instead of converging on a dead row. Move the source's payload.intakeExecution pointer to intakeExecutionReversed[]. The source returns to intake. Links stay as audit.\n- promote, in-place: if the source is revocable, reset implementationReadiness to not-ready (status 'reversed', contract retained under reversedContract) so the acceptance floor excludes it. Move intakePromotion and intakeSource to *Reversed[] history keys.\n- merge: restore a source that closeAsDuplicate terminalized to its pre-merge status, and move its merge pointer to history. On the target, mark the merged-evidence entry reversed:true but never delete it, preserving unique evidence (P-009 acceptance).\n- retain/reject: move payload.intakeDisposition to intakeDispositionReversed[]. The triage decision is open again.\nEvery inverse is a no-op success when the history already records this run+item, so it is idempotent under retry.\n\n3. Ownership guard (R-30). Revocable means: re-read under FOR UPDATE at apply time, state 'open', assignee null, never taken, no checkpoint, and no coord_links edges other than the intake rels (promoted-*/merged-*), i.e. no downstream effects. Anything else is never revoked or deleted. The inverse instead appends a correction record to the item's payload.intakeCorrections[] (runId, itemId, reason, observed holder/state/checkpoint, requestedAt), returns outcome 'correction-recorded', and writes a revert_note that says so explicitly. Delivered work is never deleted.\n\n4. Apply-time recheck (R-31). Before the apply-intake branch of terminal-action-dispatch executes, it re-reads, at execution time, (a) the run row (refuse if stopped/settled) and (b) the FLAGS.INBOX_BULK_RESOLVE kill switch (refuse when off). Changed source rows are already refused by executeIntakeDecision (source-revision-changed). Per WI-41021, the kill switch gates ACTING, never STOPPING: compensation is an owner undo and is not gated by the flag.\n\n5. Tests: unit layer (R-9/R-30/R-31 requiredTestLayers): attention/intake-compensation.test.ts with injected deps, plus dispatcher refusal cases.\n\n### D-020 — P-008 intake drain shape: dedicated intake-triage run kind + registered scheduled seeder; investigations need question/evidence/exit-check/owner; low-confidence promote refused; reports split disposition from delivery (refines D-012)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) before implementing P-008 (WI-10004571). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n0. Finding (measured 15:2xZ, dev:pg_query over attention_bulk_run_items JOIN attention_bulk_runs, 3 days): the only registered resolver launcher, system:inbox-bulk-resolve, seeded 3,800 items in 10 kinds and ZERO item_kind 'improvement'. It seeds from the attention feed, whose improvement source admits only papercusp-improvement + needsHuman rows, so awaiting observations/candidates (10,802 lane='observation' rows created in 7 days) have no registered executor. R-7's falsifier currently holds.\n\n1. Separate stream. Add BulkRunKind 'intake-triage' (migration widens attention_bulk_runs_run_kind_check; the existing per-(workspace, run_kind) single-flight index then keeps intake triage from contending with inbox-resolve). This refines D-012's 'no new run kind': D-012 kept decision STORAGE on existing columns, which stays true; the run kind is the existing discriminator for a separate drain lane, exactly as plan-cleanup (migration 937).\n\n2. Registered executor. New system action system:intake-triage-drain (harness/routines), registered in register-system-actions.ts with a seeded durable schedule, built like makeInboxBulkResolveAction: same bulk-resolve kill switch, single-flight per kind, never-beat backoff, saved launch profile (resolverProfiles['intake-triage'], falling back to 'inbox-resolve'). It seeds at most 200 rows selected by the SHARED awaiting-triage predicate (intakeTriageStateSql, owned by P-010) over the intake population, excluding ids already in an open run, as improvement-kind seed items (itemId improvement:<id>, kind 'improvement', ref {kind:'improvement', issueId, harnessSlug}). The existing P-004/P-006 validation and apply-intake then apply unchanged.\n\n3. Implementation fleets drain only accepted work. The drain never claims; intake rows stay observation-lane (excluded by the observationLane floor), and promoted rows are claimable only through the P-006 sealed acceptance + P-007 floor. Promoted fix decisions become kind bug, so a bug-scoped fleet sees them.\n\n4. Investigations (R-26). investigate executes only with an accountable owner (decision.owner not 'unknown'), a specific unresolved question (acceptance.problem), evidence to collect (acceptance.evidence, >= 1) and an exit check (acceptance.completionCheck). The created task records payload.investigation {question, evidenceToCollect, exitCheck, owner} and stays issue-family task work (the work lane for investigations). Uncertain reports cannot become fix tasks: an intake promote whose item confidenceLevel is low or insufficient is refused at report time and must be investigate or retry.\n\n5. Reports (R-27). Drain reporting gains one pure summarizer that returns intake dispositions separately from implementation delivery. A promote/investigate counts as 'accepted, not delivered' until its promoted item is terminal done with committed completion authority. Intake never feeds the run's resolved/auto_resolved counters.\n\nRelated: P-004, P-006, P-007, P-010 (ca9e0 owns queue-stage presentation; this decision adds no stage UI).\n\n### D-021 — P-008 launch profile: the intake drain launches with the owner's saved inbox-resolve profile; no third resolverProfiles key (refines D-020 §2)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while testing P-008 (WI-10004571). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Finding (read from code): D-020 §2 says the drain reads resolverProfiles['intake-triage'], falling back to 'inbox-resolve'. To do that, P-008 added 'intake-triage' to BULK_RESOLVER_PROFILE_KINDS. But parseBulkResolverLaunchProfiles fills every kind with DEFAULT_BULK_RESOLVER_LAUNCH_PROFILE (model null, account default), so the intake key always existed and the fallback never fired. No settings pane renders an intake profile (BulkResolverSettingsControl only takes inbox-resolve and plan-cleanup), so the key could only ever hold the default. The drain would therefore always launch the default Claude model on the system login. WI-10004887 measured that route failing at its session limit: four scheduled runs in a row died before their first heartbeat.\n\n2. Ruling: BULK_RESOLVER_PROFILE_KINDS stays ['inbox-resolve', 'plan-cleanup']. The intake drain's readLaunchProfile returns resolverProfiles['inbox-resolve'], so it launches exactly as the scheduled Inbox resolver does. Authority (automationMode/minConfidence) still comes from the standing policy, never from the profile. A separate intake profile is added only together with a pane that can edit it.\n\n3. Guard: intake-triage-drain-action.test.ts pins that the production wiring launches with the saved inbox-resolve profile's model.\n\nRelated: D-020, P-008, WI-10004887.\n\n### D-022 — Split enforcement activation out of P-011: the plan ships the claim floor with the cutover still at the sentinel; lowering it is WI-10005016, gated on deploy plus a release-runtime canary (refines D-018 §2)\nDate: 2026-10-01\nDate: 2026-10-01. Recorded by su-fd916e65 (AUTO, D-010) while closing P-011 (WI-10004574). [self-imposed design ruling]\n\n1. Finding (measured 19:31-19:36Z): P-011 built the gate on moving the cutover. authorizeEnforcementCutoverAdvance and ENFORCEMENT_CUTOVER_CANARY_ATTESTATION (R-37) live in legacy-acceptance-adoption.ts. The canary lac-canary-47598d23 passed 4/4 on :3170 build 57d558cc1d, and the bounded cohort apply lac-apply-1c7f425a adopted 3 rows. IMPLEMENTATION_ACCEPTANCE_ENFORCEMENT_CUTOVER is still the 2100 sentinel. The producer creation-enrollment (P-005, issues-engineer.ts) and floor #16 (P-007) are NOT live on :3070. dev:pipeline_position reports deployed=false and blockedOn=gate, and the frozen repair queue has held main for about 9h.\n2. Ruling: lowering the cutover is not part of this plan's ship. Doing it now would put enforcement in the same promotion as the producers. The fleet on :3070 would then file new issue-family work that becomes unclaimable before any producer there can enroll it. That is the broad freeze the P-011 acceptance text forbids, and it would rest on a canary run on a runtime other than the one being enforced. R-37 already refuses an unattested move, so the disarmed state is mechanically held.\n3. Follow-up: WI-10005016 (assigned su-fd916e65). Its preconditions are P-005 and P-007 live on :3070, a passed canary on the release runtime, and an intake drain keeping pace. It then bumps the TS constant, the attestation and a new migration together, and verifies on :3070.\n4. P-011 closes on its item text: producers write attributable intake/acceptance, reviewed legacy rows adopt the contract with evidence, unknowns remain visible, and there is no broad freeze or silent bypass. Rubric criterion 'Canary adoption before broad enforcement' is satisfied by the order this ruling preserves.\nRelated: D-016, D-018, P-005, P-007, P-011\nRelated: P-011, P-007, P-005\n\n### D-023 — A bug is accepted only with a reproduction on the current build; otherwise investigate or reject. Applies to agent-filed and human-filed bugs alike\nDate: 2026-10-05\nAffects: end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05, owner-dialog answer 'Yes, all bugs (Recommended)' [turn:self], following owner directive #1349: 'human bugs should also go through a verification step... should agent bugs also go thorugh a verification step? I don't think these should be claimable until verified a real bug... Should we had this verification as part of that [bulk triage]?']\n\nRuling:\n1. In the saved bulk review run, the `promote` disposition for an issue with kind=bug requires a REPRODUCTION RECEIPT from the current build: a failing test, a scripted repro, or a log or ledger observation produced by the current build. Each receipt names the build sha it was observed on.\n2. If the reviewer cannot reproduce the bug quickly, the disposition is `investigate`, which creates a bounded repro task (verification, not implementation). A bug that no longer reproduces on the current build goes to `reject`, or to `retain` as evidence.\n3. Corroboration (many reporters) and similarity raise review ORDER only. They never substitute for the receipt, consistent with R-16.\n4. The receipt's failing test (where one exists) is the test the eventual fix must turn green. It doubles as the recurrence guard the bug-close rule already requires.\n5. Same rule for agent-filed and human-filed bugs. Human-filed reports (plan end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05) are additionally redacted and treated as untrusted evidence.\n6. This does not change change/task/feature acceptance.\n\nWhy: today a bug is claimable after a duplicate-only admission check (work-items-admission-promoter.ts header), and this plan's acceptance contract never required reproduction. A search of this plan's body and decisions for reproduc / repro / 'real bug' returned 0 matches at 2026-10-05 ~21:30Z. Measured: work_items:claimable { harness:'papercusp', kind:'bug', breakdownOnly:true } at 21:28:10Z returned 246 claimable of 1,378 matched, 67 of them admitted that day.\n\nEnforcement still depends on WI-10005016 (cutover off the 2100 sentinel). That waits on P-005/P-007 serving on :3070, and on 2026-10-05 ~21:50Z the green-checkpoint gate was holding that deploy (gate held by su-e6d99ccf, WI-10006055). Recorded by su-4a152, which is taking over WI-10005016 and the implementation item for this decision. The previous implementer, su-fd916e65, is ended.\n\n### D-024 — Agent-encountered bugs are born verified when the encounter evidence is attached; refines D-023\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05 directives #1359/#1360 [turn:self]: 'if an agent encountered a bug it should be able to skip this step because its already verified' ... 'right? or do you think the behavior should be different for agent encountered bugs?'. The safeguards in points 2-4 are su-4a152's answer to #1360, given to Avi in the same turn; [self-imposed design detail, not owner-ratified].]\n\nRefines D-023:\n1. A bug filed by an agent that directly ENCOUNTERED the failure counts as already reproduced. Its filing carries the encounter as the D-023 reproduction receipt: the failing tool invocation (tool_invocations ref), the failing test run (test_runs ref or output), or the log/ledger line, plus the build sha it ran on. Such a bug is born accepted for the reproduction requirement and skips the bulk review reproduction step.\n2. The receipt is still required, just free at filing time. Without attached encounter evidence the system cannot distinguish 'I saw it fail' from 'I inferred it is broken', so an agent bug with no encounter receipt goes through bulk review like any other. Reason: EI-19448526819046979 recorded a filed bug whose root cause was an unverified inference carried from a carry-note.\n3. The observation is verified; the stated CAUSE is not. A born-verified bug's root-cause text stays labelled as a hypothesis, and the fixer's bug close still needs completion.rootCauseVerification.\n4. Not covered by this skip: tool failures the existing toolFailure classifier attributes to the caller (misuse rather than defect) keep their existing probation path; duplicate admission still runs; human-filed reports always go through review (D-023 point 5).\n5. Where the encounter is machine-checkable (a tool_invocations or test_runs ref), the intake should resolve the ref and confirm it shows a failure on the cited build rather than trusting the filer's text.\n\nImplementation rides on P-013 (WI-10006152).\n\n## Verification\n\nUse the existing Vitest/unit/integration and UI testing conventions with tests adjacent to the source being extended; run focused suites and the repository's required affected-suite checks when implementation is authorized. The drafting verification passed canonical parsing, complete requirement-to-item mapping, dependency validation, source-conversation coverage and saved-store read-back. Each implementation item ships and runs its own project-native tests with the feature; P-012 adds the final cross-path journey and independent shipment verification.\n\nRequired counterexamples: an ordinary unconfirmed bug; a pending change; a rejected or revised candidate; an observation consumed by the digest; legacy NULL admission; dedup fail-open unreviewed; critical/security/assignment shortcut without an acceptance receipt; source edited after recommendation; conflicting simultaneous accepts; revoked run; failed promotion write; merge with a distinct remedy; unowned retry; and undo after a worker claims the result.\n\nRequired positive journey: several source observations form one candidate; a reviewer chooses investigate when the fix is still uncertain; the accepted investigation collects current evidence; a current fix acceptance promotes or updates one canonical bug item; the bug fleet claims it; verification records the actual delivered outcome; source evidence remains navigable.\n\nBefore functional implementation acceptance, use dev:pipeline_position { path, testClass:'operator-api' } to select the currentBuildTestRoute and verify the serving runtime. Final shipment alone uses the exact green/deployed artifact and its identity; do not wait for main to implement or perform ordinary functional checks.\n\n## Conversation coverage and provenance\n\n- Owner source session_turn:codex:01a0f4cf-31ca-7c73-b501-6ca41e6dcc4e:68: observations are separate; explain approval flow. Covered by R-1, R-4, R-10, P-001/P-002/P-005/P-010.\n- Owner source session_turn:codex:01a0f4cf-31ca-7c73-b501-6ca41e6dcc4e:72: clarify what belongs as work and its sources. Covered by Background, R-1/R-2, P-001/P-003.\n- Owner source session_turn:codex:01a0f4cf-31ca-7c73-b501-6ca41e6dcc4e:74: make intake drainable and reuse bulk acceptance for promotion. Covered by R-3/R-5/R-7/R-8, P-004/P-006/P-008/P-009.\n- Accepted proposal source session_turn:codex:01a0f4cf-31ca-7c73-b501-6ca41e6dcc4e:77: promote, merge, investigate, retain/reject; provenance and separate counts. Agent-authored recommendation adopted for drafting by the current owner request; not misrepresented as an earlier owner-authored policy.\n- Owner source session_turn:codex:01a0f539-3fd3-7260-ab2d-24e26a94e806:1: bug-drain work should pass the acceptance boundary. Covered by R-4/R-6/R-11 and D-003.\n- Owner source session_turn:codex:01a0f539-3fd3-7260-ab2d-24e26a94e806:7: write the improvements into a plan and show a detailed summary. This draft and WI-10004495 satisfy the planning deliverable.\n- Derived engineering work: revision binding, idempotency, execution-path parity, safe compensation, legacy staging and regression verification in P-005/P-006/P-007/P-009/P-011/P-012 are necessary to make the requested promotion and acceptance boundary enforceable; they are proposed implementation details, not claimed prior owner instructions.\n\n## Open implementation choices\n\nP-001 should resolve the exact legacy cohort/cutover and the evidence requirements for any authorized immediate-policy or emergency containment path. P-004 should confirm whether intake fits the current run-kind contract or needs one case in that existing type. These are recorded engineering choices delegated to this session by the approved AUTO execution route; resolve them from the P-001 baseline before the corresponding implementation or rollout.\n\n\n## Execution authorization\n\nOwner source session_turn:codex:01a0f539-3fd3-7260-ab2d-24e26a94e806:15: \"the plan looks good.  Put yourself on auto mode and implement it yourslef now until it reaches shipped status\". Route: this session implements directly; no implementation delegation. AUTO is registered with ownerDirected:true. Earlier drafting-only restrictions describe the prior request and are superseded for this approved plan.\n\n\n## Contract ownership clarification\n\nEach acceptance BAR has one primary implementing item in the BAR-to-work map. Supporting implementation and verification remain required by the existing item dependency graph and the full original request preserved in each criterion.intent. P-001 is a read-only baseline investigation with an explicit non-automated specification and an owned, queryable census/writer-map deliverable. This removes ambiguous duplicate contracts across supporting items without dropping any requested behavior, test layer, evidence plane or verification obligation.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"phone-public-telephone-service-2026-10-01","title":"Phone public telephone service — real numbers, calling and verified public readiness","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Phone public telephone service — real numbers, calling and verified public readiness\nslug: phone-public-telephone-service-2026-10-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-06\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-06, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted, bar_snapshot_vetting_stale. resolve and reverify any failures, verify support/portability and number ownership, … <!-- P-016 -->\n## Background\n\nAvi asked: \"write a plan for getting it ready to be a finished public telephone service and then show me the detailed summary\" (session_turn:codex:01a0f780-14e0-7ba1-9e8d-fda266059afc:5, October 1 2026). The preceding status request is session_turn:codex:01a0f780-14e0-7ba1-9e8d-fda266059afc:1.\n\nThe shipped phone-app-2026-08-30 plan delivered a browser-first alpha. Its D-002 records Avi's choice to self-host the media plane. D-016 records his budget-driven carrier deferral, and describes phone-number inbound/outbound calling and emergency/carrier obligations as deferred. This draft is a separately scoped public-telephony sequel; it preserves the closed browser-alpha plan as history.\n\nCurrent source inspected October 1: infra/phone-app/README.md and deployment templates; the existing template-materialized phone-app PROTOCOL.md/GUIDE.md; apps/sidecar/src/api.ts and calls.ts; the existing data and test packages. /api/call currently mints a browser room grant, while /api/simulate-inbound explicitly simulates screening. These are foundations, not current PSTN acceptance. Current deployment source supports PHONE_LIVEKIT_PUBLIC_URL but does not itself provision DNS, TLS, firewall/NAT or TURN/TLS; the template disables TURN TLS. The prior live loopback result is a dated observation, not a fresh certification.\n\nReuse voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01 and its portal microphone/lifecycle evidence where the tested component, revision and runtime match; WI-10004758 is the portal journey item, not proof that carrier calling works. Coordinate shared fixes once; do not duplicate its generic voice release lane. The phone worker, phone sidecar, portal and media/SIP units have distinct release artifacts: inventory each.\n\n## Scope and decisions to review\n\nThe proposed product is a publicly usable AI-assisted telephone service inside the existing web Phone app: real assigned numbers, inbound and outbound voice, assistant screening, human pickup/forwarding, voicemail/transcripts, caller management, permitted scheduled calls, DTMF, transfer, usage/account controls and support. Public release requires account isolation and reliable service when no browser is open; receiving calls through the assistant/forwarding must not depend on an active tab.\n\nImplementation choices under Avi's AUTO go-ahead: target the proposed limited US/English AI-assisted-number rollout, new numbers for an invited pilot, one carrier and an explicit destination allowlist. These are disclosed implementation defaults, not a claim that carrier funding, actual number ownership, market-specific legality or emergency capability are verified. Owner choices required in P-001/P-004/P-014:\n- Launch country and supported calling geography; AI-assisted number versus primary-phone replacement. Determine applicable emergency-service and provider obligations before defining public service claims; a disclaimer is not a substitute for a required emergency route.\n- Telnyx as the starting carrier candidate inherited from infra/phone-app/README.md, or an approved alternative that works with self-hosted LiveKit SIP. Account ownership, KYC/payment, number purchases, porting authorizations and required emergency address are owner-supplied gates.\n- Hard pilot and monthly spending ceilings, source of carrier/AI/hosting funds, hosted paid entitlements versus BYOC, number count and supported concurrency.\n- Recording/transcription defaults, consent language, retention and deletion/export policy. Ordinary call recording is proposed off until opted in; voicemail/transcription consent is explicit.\n- Web/mobile-browser launch coverage and human pickup behavior when the tab is closed. Native iOS/Android system-call integration, SIM service, SMS/MMS, broad international coverage and autonomous mass dialing are separate expansions, not silently included promises.\n- Launch with new numbers for pilot; include a documented, exercised port-in/out capability and number release/export ownership workflow for general availability. Never port an owner's primary number as a development test.\n\nKnown boundaries after the owner go-ahead: paid/live carrier actions require the actual account, secure credentials and spending caps; no duplicate live-gate repair/monitoring mission; no alternate app scaffold, carrier gateway, agent loop or billing service. Existing app templates and typed agent/voice seams remain the foundation. Public routine features ship enabled for entitled tenants; credentialed dialing, recording and new external authority remain behind explicit registered policy controls until their gates are satisfied.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Public service contract and launch decisions.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Make the existing Phone app ready to be a finished public telephone service.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Derived implementation and acceptance detail for Avi's planning request; this block does not claim separate owner approval.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a0f780-14e0-7ba1-9e8d-fda266059afc:5\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The approved release contract identifies launch countries, customers, supported incoming/outgoing call journeys, emergency obligations, paid-service budget and source/deployment ownership before paid provisioning or public exposure.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A required choice is silently assumed, the old browser-only shipment is treated as PSTN proof, or service is represented as primary-phone replacement without an approved emergency/compliance route.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"mandatory\": true\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Review the retained owner decisions, provider capabilities and dated source/runtime inventory; compare each promised user journey with its implementation and evidence route.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Secure reachable media.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Make the existing Phone app ready to be a finished public telephone service.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Derived implementation and acceptance detail for Avi's planning request; Artifact: screenshots of each surface plus the carrier call record for the test attempt.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Architecture and reuse\n\nOrdinary telephone → approved carrier SIP trunk → existing self-hosted LiveKit SIP gateway → one tenant-bound call room → existing phone worker/agent voice contract. The authenticated Phone app controls the same call through the existing sidecar and durable PhoneBackend. Outbound intent uses the approved outbound trunk and LiveKit SIP participant API, not a browser-only room presented as a telephone call.\n\nExtend PhoneBackend/PhoneStore and CallLedger with provider/trunk/number identifiers, durable call intent and observed state transitions, tenant routing, idempotency and reconciled cost events. Reuse existing tables/ledgers wherever their lifetime fits; a tenant-owned number mapping is the smallest necessary domain addition if no current number record fits, kept in the existing data package and migrations rather than a new service. Key inbound routing from carrier-validated destination/trunk configuration, not caller-provided owner fields. Caller ID is a label, not authentication. An inbound room must have its durable tenant/call context before the worker can exercise any tools; an unknown context fails closed to a safe call outcome.\n\nReuse LiveKit server/SIP APIs and existing secure secret injection. SIP TLS/SRTP must be tested against the installed gateway and carrier versions; do not promise end-to-end encryption across the ordinary PSTN. Distinguish public WSS signaling, ICE/RTP reachability and TURN/TLS relay; a healthy HTTP endpoint or working WSS handshake proves none of the other two.\n\nReuse the existing brain/voice adapter, screening, voicemail, scheduling, parent-conversation binding, transcript bridge and notification surfaces. Add PSTN transport events and policies at those boundaries. Scheduled PSTN calls use the existing durable scheduling/work-intent contract with cancellation, timezone and idempotency protection, not a new cron/agent loop. Extend platform signup/subscription entitlement and existing usage surfaces for phone access, provider costs and suspension; choose the missing schema fields only after the source inventory.\n\nIdentify each repository's canonical write/deploy path in P-001: the phone app is an existing managed repository outside the operator staging checkout. Do not edit a release mirror or assume operator git-sync publishes the app. Operator source work stays in canonical staging, with a registered work-item and the effective file locks.\n\n### project's real suites: phone sidecar, data memory/Postgres contracts, worker voice-contract integration, UI tests and template-composition checks; use the portal's existing Playwright mounted-surface journey; use operator deployment/config tests and npm run test:affected for operator changes. Extend existing suites with PSTN, privacy, tenant, quota and failure scenarios; add conventional test files only when the current suites do not fit. The existing test paths named in tree BARs must be extended to falsify the new behavior before their pass is accepted; current old tests are not proof of implemented telephony.\n\nEach live BAR requires retained, repeatable manual operational evidence. The separate mandatory R-12 BAR enforces the original project-suite unit/integration/e2e obligation across every changed behavior under R-2 through R-11. An instrument:none check denotes the real external-phone/provider audit only; R-12's runnable check is a separate gate and neither can substitute for the other. After P-001 source/runtime discovery, bind runnable checks and evidence routes through the canonical BAR workflow before activation; update them when additional test files actually exist. Do not invent a nonexistent test path or claim an unmeasured live test is automated.\n\nDefault implementation evidence uses staging/current isolated phone runtimes and approved test numbers. Use dev:pipeline_position with the relevant functional test class for operator/background work; prepare a missing candidate runtime rather than using an incompatible host. Public production tests in P-015 are specifically needed to verify public DNS/TLS, actual carrier ingress/egress, portal deployment, signed-in tenancy and exact released app/worker/media configuration that a local candidate cannot prove.\n\nRetain source/config fingerprints, runtime artifact IDs, suite run IDs, redacted carrier call IDs and call-room correlation, independent verdict and known residue. External calls use consenting controlled recipients and approved spending caps. Use the carrier's documented emergency test procedure only; never make a live emergency call as a test.\n\n### Proposed acceptance thresholds\n\nThese are reviewable draft thresholds, not measured guarantees: 10 concurrent pilot calls with no tenant leakage or orphaned billable call; 24-hour candidate soak; a seven-day invited pilot covering at least 100 consenting calls across two originating carrier networks within the approved budget; at least 99% successful setup of valid test calls after excluding explicit remote busy/reject/no-answer and separately reporting those outcomes; PSTN conversational response p95 at or below 2.5 seconds and interruption stop p95 at or below 500 ms. Define start/end signals and sample population before testing; record carrier answer delay separately from agent response. Small pilot samples are an acceptance exercise, not proof of a long-term availability SLA.\n\nPublic incident targets proposed for review: detect a material call-path failure within two minutes, notify the named operator, and restore service or activate the approved fallback within fifteen minutes; recovery policy must state what happens to active calls and numbers. Existing voice latency requirements stay intact where their measurement contract applies. Revise thresholds with owner sign-off if budget or provider capability cannot support them; do not silently weaken acceptance.\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract and evidence inventory\n\n- **P-001** `done` Record Avi's AUTO execution/shipment authority and disclosed US/English AI-assisted-number implementation defaults; inventory canonical phone/portal/media source and runtime owners, existing number/provider/secret references (names only), current test evidence and shared voice-release dependencies. Mark shipped only when every mandatory bar and owner launch gate is satisfied; file and assign any out-of-scope follow-up before close. blocked-by: P-015 importance: high\n\n## Execution and critical path\n\nPlanning was done by this session. Avi enabled AUTO mode on October 1 during drafting; this session registered it and selected route self for the requested planning scope. Before a later implementation request, choose the execution route under that standing posture; the product/carrier/payment/legal gates still require real inputs. The efficient build lanes are public media (P-002), data/routing (P-003), policy/privacy/usage (P-009 through P-011), and reused voice/operations preparation (P-008/P-012), once P-001's choices authorize them. Shared files serialize through locks; use visible durable fleets if Avi chooses parallel execution, not client-native hidden subagents.\n\nCritical path: approved service/budget contract → externally reachable media and tenant-bound data → funded/provider-approved numbers and trunks → inbound/outbound and human handoff → full scenario evidence → independent and owner pilot approval → exact public shipment → bounded pilot and general release. The AI/policy/data/operations preparation can proceed while the account/number gate is pending; real carrier verification and shipment cannot.\n\nSource implementing work is registered and verified on current builds; closed milestones do not wait for unrelated live-gate promotion. Final P-015 explicitly requires deployed public-artifact evidence. Do not turn this plan into a duplicate monitor of someone else's gate or voice lane.\n\n## Costs, timing and external dependencies\n\nNo credible calendar or fixed monthly quote is approved yet. P-001 source/runtime inventory should produce implementation estimates per lane; provider verification, number availability/porting and any required emergency/legal setup are external lead-time risks. A planned seven-day pilot is an observation window, not a promise that the full service can be completed in seven days.\n\nCost worksheet: monthly number rent + inbound/outbound charged minutes + any transfer second-leg minutes + AI STT/LLM/TTS usage + self-host compute/egress/TURN + storage/backups + emergency/provider fees and taxes + operating support. Reconcile minimums, rounding, destination rates, fraud controls and concurrency with the carrier's dated rate sheet. Low/base/high scenarios use the approved number count, calling minutes and concurrent sessions. Existing paid account credits do not imply an ongoing free service. Source: AskUserQuestion dialog answered by Avi in session su-2b9fe461 on 2026-10-06 ~03:30Z (turn-provenance OWNER interactive), owner directive #1405.\n\n### D-024 — Public media edge is a small agent-provisioned Hetzner VM; keep waiting on the Telnyx key\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [owner:Avi 2026-10-06]\nAnswers to the AskUserQuestion dialog in session su-2b9fe461 at ~09:26Z (turn-provenance OWNER interactive, under owner directive #1405):\n(1) Telnyx key: \"Keep waiting (Recommended)\". The option text read: Avi adds TELNYX_API_KEY when he can; the agent keeps the plan ready and resumes P-004 (buy numbers, set up trunks) as soon as the key appears. D-020 stands; P-004 stays blocked only on the key.\n(2) Public audio: \"Small public server (Recommended)\". The option text read: the agent creates a small Hetzner VM (roughly EUR 5/month, billed outside the $10/month phone cap) as the public audio/relay edge, plus a papercusp.com subdomain via Avi's Cloudflare account; Avi's home IP stays private.\nEffect: P-002 is unblocked for the agent to provision one small Hetzner VM (public IPv4) as the public WSS/TURN/ICE-RTP and inbound SIP/RTP edge, with DNS under papercusp.com via the existing Cloudflare token. Its cost is approved separately from D-021's $10/month phone-usage cap and is not counted against it. Keep the edge minimal (one VM, smallest suitable type), keep internal control URLs private, enable certificate renewal, and record the VM id/IP/cost on WI-10004984. No other paid resources are authorized by this decision.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, D-020, D-021\n\n### D-025 — Public media edge runs on a GCP e2-micro (Hetzner account dead); VM public IP is routed to the box over WireGuard\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nActor: su-2b9fe461 under AUTO (#1405), implementing D-024. [self-imposed] agent ruling; disclosed to Avi. Body corrected 10:12Z to match the as-built routing (the first draft said the box holds the public IP; it must not).\n\nMeasured 09:29Z: both Hetzner Cloud tokens on this box are rejected (401 'the token you have provided is invalid': ~/.config/hcloud/token-a, token-b, and ~/.papercusp/hcloud-token, the July replacement; the earlier account file is literally named *.old-account-dead-20260703). The org's former Hetzner workloads now run on GCP (instances hetzner-restore-prod/-mesh in active-alcove-504205-q3). D-024's intent ('one small public server, roughly EUR 5/month, as the public edge') is therefore met on GCP: one e2-micro in us-east1 (closest to the box) in project active-alcove-504205-q3 with a static IPv4 address. Expected cost is about USD 6-11/month (e2-micro ~USD 6 unless the billing account's free-tier e2-micro is unused, plus ~USD 3.65 for the static IP, plus ~USD 1 for disk). That is above D-024's ~EUR 5 estimate; it is disclosed and remains outside the D-021 call cap. No other paid resources.\n\nRouting design (as built): the VM is an L4 edge. WireGuard connects VM 10.77.0.1 and box 10.77.0.2 (interface phedge0). The box does NOT hold the VM's public IP: that would make the WireGuard endpoint a local address and loop the tunnel. The VM DNATs the public media ports (RTC UDP 7892, RTC TCP 7891, TURN UDP 7893) to 10.77.0.2 without masquerading, so clients keep their real addresses. On the box, a source rule ('from 10.77.0.2 lookup 7792') policy-routes only tunnel-sourced replies and STUN back through the tunnel; the VM masquerades that outbound traffic to its public IP. LiveKit runs with use_external_ip: true and phedge0 added to interfaces.includes, so its per-interface STUN maps phedge0 to 34.23.13.209 and advertises it as a candidate; no node_ip override is set. Caveat [measured]: LiveKit's nodeIP stays the home IP, which is also the embedded TURN relay address, so the UDP-blocked TURN path must be proven, not assumed. On TCP 443 the VM runs nginx with SNI routing: phone-voice.papercusp.com gets TLS terminated on the VM (certbot HTTP-01, renewal reloads nginx) and is proxied to internal 7890; phone-turn.papercusp.com is passed through to LiveKit TURN/TLS on 7894, whose certificate the box renews with certbot DNS-01 via Cloudflare and a deploy hook that restarts LiveKit. Both DNS records are A records, not Cloudflare-proxied. The internal control URL stays internal. SIP 5070 and RTP 40000-40200 are forwarded on the VM but closed at the GCP firewall until P-004 adds Telnyx source ranges. Source: infra/phone-app/edge/ (edge.sh, edge-config.mjs), tested by apps/operator/scripts/__tests__/phone-app-edge-config.test.ts.\n\nRejected: Hetzner (no valid credential, and asking Avi for one adds an owner round trip for an equivalent server); co-hosting on hetzner-restore-prod or pc-blind-relay-1 (production and customer infrastructure); masquerading inbound DNAT (it hides client IPs and breaks TURN-relay permissions for the co-located SFU); holding the public IP on the box (WireGuard endpoint loop); Tailscale Funnel (TCP only, no UDP media or SIP).\n\n### D-026 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-06\nAmendment-Id: amend-f2a27860960c1a76e3eafd1e\nRequest-Hash: 44be55c3e4b0e6a74262ef551857b052b15dce488f665a6d49ffa367d4fd6227\nActor: su-2b9fe461-077c-4fd4-8cd7-c43499f17892\nReason: Fold rubric-vetting critique (consult conv-muwtj07d posts 1160158 + 1160163) into one amendment: D-020..D-025 traceability (Governs lines, R-1 enumerates approved choices and both budgets); D-023 no-pilot (R-72/R-73 reframed, pilot text removed from release/usage methods and falsifiers); D-021 cap figure + refusal semantics on R-56 with named detectors; D-022 facts on R-42/R-43/R-46; new mandatory R-88 emergency-calling disclosure/handling; per-bar falsifiers (no shared driftMarkers); live groups name their evidence artifact; R-13 non-edge-address clause (D-025). Outside-lineage review su-09e00cff (consult conv-muwu1nuy post 1160170) folded: R-5 recipient-consent clause; R-53/R-54/R-56 'including after an entitlement upgrade or policy change'. R-12/R-74 unchanged (byte-identical to rev 10).\nApproved-By: su-3711c628-78ab-48ee-b238-058a89bec963\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1160219\nApproved-At: 2026-10-06T16:10:11.980Z\nRubric revision: 10 → 11\nSubject plan revision: 76 → 77\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19, R-20, R-21, R-22, R-23, R-24, R-25, R-26, R-27, R-28, R-29, R-30, R-31, R-32, R-33, R-34, R-35, R-36, R-37, R-38, R-39, R-40, R-41, R-42, R-43, R-44, R-45, R-46, R-47, R-48, R-49, R-50, R-51, R-52, R-53, R-54, R-55, R-56, R-57, R-58, R-59, R-60, R-61, R-62, R-63, R-64, R-65, R-66, R-67, R-68, R-69, R-70, R-71, R-72, R-73, R-75, R-76, R-77, R-78, R-79, R-80, R-81, R-82, R-83, R-84, R-85, R-86, R-87, R-88\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-027 — Approved capacity, latency, recovery and barge-in figures for acceptance (r-10, r-50, r-60, r-48)\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed under AUTO, owner directive #1405 — su-2b9fe 2026-10-06] Rubric vetting conv-muww5xzl (rev 11) asked that the 'approved' capacity objective, latency target, recovery objective and barge-in policy be pinned to ONE Decision so r-10, r-50, r-60 and r-48 grade against figures rather than prose. These ratify the plan's own '### Proposed acceptance thresholds' text (plan body, Phase/Acceptance section) and D-022/D-023; nothing here is newly invented. Owner may revise them; per that section, they are never silently weakened.\n\n1. CAPACITY (r-10): 10 concurrent PSTN calls on the pinned candidate with no tenant leakage and no orphaned billable call, then a 24-hour candidate soak. Calls stay within the D-021 $10/month hard cap. (The proposed seven-day invited pilot is dropped by D-023: no pilot.)\n2. LATENCY (r-50): PSTN conversational response p95 <= 2.5 s, measured from caller end-of-speech to first assistant audio. Carrier answer delay is recorded separately and excluded. Start/end signals and the sample population are declared before the run.\n3. RECOVERY (r-60): detect a material call-path failure within 2 minutes, notify the named operator, and restore service or activate the approved fallback within 15 minutes (time objective). Data objective: at most 24 hours of Phone database loss, the daily papercusp-phone-backup.timer cadence; a backup older than 36 h raises backup-stale (PHONE_BACKUP_MAX_AGE_HOURS). The drill must state what happens to active calls and numbers.\n4. BARGE-IN (r-48): the opening AI-assisted / may-be-recorded notice (D-022) plays to completion and is not interruptible, and recording/transcription starts only after it. Every later assistant utterance is interruptible by caller speech: playback stops with interruption-stop p95 <= 500 ms from caller speech onset, the unspoken remainder is discarded, and the assistant answers the new utterance. Echo or noise alone must not trigger a stop.\n\nCited from the methods of r-10, r-48, r-50 and r-60 in acceptance rubric rev 12 (WI-10006727).\n\n### D-028 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-06\nAmendment-Id: amend-c793b9421f724a18456d0242\nRequest-Hash: 612735e681b2284f50dfd6c6fa7037ca7178a1b15bbf99dd6a00e85fa48e71fe\nActor: su-2b9fe461-077c-4fd4-8cd7-c43499f17892\nReason: Rev 12 folds rubric-vetting conv-muww5xzl (rev 11) into one amendment: (1) evidenceRuntime on all 57 live bars, naming runtime_vintage rows that now exist (WI-10006790: worker unit for r-8 and r-48..r-51, sidecar otherwise); (2) Governs edits on 17 bars (D-010/D-014 on r-6, r-41, r-75..r-83; D-014/D-019 on r-12, r-74); (3) D-027 approved figures cited by r-10, r-48, r-50, r-60; (4) named it() detectors on 29 tree bars, each title verified verbatim in its test file, plus suite-level detector text on r-12/r-74; honest gap notes on r-6, r-58, r-76; (5) r-72 gets its own Observable sentence and an intent.rationale co-rater note (r-86/r-11). WI-10006727.\nApproved-By: su-bbd848b7-0af5-4db2-b1ea-66d3c638cd6d\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1160335\nApproved-At: 2026-10-06T17:49:17.036Z\nRubric revision: 11 → 12\nSubject plan revision: 79 → 80\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, R-11, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19, R-20, R-21, R-22, R-23, R-24, R-25, R-26, R-27, R-28, R-29, R-30, R-31, R-32, R-33, R-34, R-35, R-36, R-37, R-38, R-39, R-40, R-48, R-49, R-50, R-51, R-60, R-61, R-62, R-63, R-64, R-65, R-66, R-67, R-68, R-69, R-70, R-71, R-72, R-73, R-85, R-86, R-87, R-88\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"ship-precomputed-doc-vectors-2026-10-01","title":"Ship precomputed doc_sections vectors with each Server release (no per-install embed of shipped docs)","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Ship precomputed doc_sections vectors with each Server release (no per-install embed of shipped docs)\nslug: ship-precomputed-doc-vectors-2026-10-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-01\n---\n\n## Goal\nA fresh or upgraded Papercusp Server must not spend hours of CPU embedding documentation that is byte-identical on every install. Compute the vectors for the shipped doc corpora once per release, ship them, and have the boot sweep embed only rows the shipped seed does not cover.\n\n## Evidence\n[measured 2026-10-01 00:25-00:30Z, GCP VM cap-emb455, Server 0.0.26 .deb, PAPERCUSP_DISABLE_DOGFOOD_HIVE=1, no agents, no data; serve.log] First boot runs '[doc-embed-sync] synced: papercusp-engineering=991/991 pages, 9192 sections · papercusp-guidance=913/913 pages, 3579 sections' = 12,771 doc_sections rows with NULL embedding. The first embed-backfill drain embedded doc_sections=192 in 242 s with local gemma (768 d) on CPU. [inferred from that rate] ~66 five-minute cycles = about 5.5 hours at ~1 core per fresh install, and again for every changed page on each release upgrade. Until it finishes, docs:search's semantic leg covers only part of the corpus. Source: WI-10004455; plan agent-capacity-and-cost-gcp-2026-09-30 (S7 / D-003 cost target).\n\n## Scope\nIn: harness_shared.doc_sections rows for source keys papercusp-engineering and papercusp-guidance (the corpora doc-embed-sync.ts builds from shipped files). Out: harness:<slug> doc sections, user/hive data, every other embed-backfill target.\n\n## Constraints\n- Vectors must be in the shipped embedder's space: same embedder mode (gemma 768 d on Server today) and recipe version that embed-backfill tags rows with, so the sweep treats seeded rows as settled instead of re-embedding them.\n- Release cut is incremental: reuse the previous release's seed for every (source_key, slug, anchor, page_sha) that did not change; embed only changed sections.\n- The papercusp-desktop/bin release scripts are in active use by the p2p endgame lane (su-3ee17, p2p-public-release-endgame-2026-09-01 D-110 holds 0.0.26 publish). Coordinate before editing them; do not change a cut that is mid-drill.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — A seeded first boot embeds no shipped docs.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"On a Server whose active embedder matches the shipped seed, the papercusp-engineering and papercusp-guidance doc_sections rows have no NULL embedding after the boot doc sync, so embed-backfill does no doc_sections work for them.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:cb7f252d-c2a2-41dc-90ef-ccc336f8ddca:5\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:cb7f252d-c2a2-41dc-90ef-ccc336f8ddca:6\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"After the boot doc sync applies a matching seed, every seeded section whose page_sha matches holds the seed vector bit-for-bit with the sweep labels, and the NULL count for those pages is 0.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A matching NULL row stays NULL, a row gets a different vector, an already-embedded row is overwritten, or a row whose page changed gets a seeded vector.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"NULL rows with matching page_sha\",\n      \"already-embedded rows\",\n      \"changed pages\",\n      \"second boot with nothing to fill\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the real-PG integration suite: it syncs rows, applies a seed through the boot entry point (applyShippedDocVectorSeed) and checks per-row vectors, labels and the NULL count, including the no-op second boot.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/search/doc-vector-seed.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — The seed is correct and incremental.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The release-cut exporter writes only rows whose vector is in the shipped embedder space; unchanged (source_key, slug, anchor, page_sha) rows are reused from the previous seed and only changed sections are embedded.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:cb7f252d-c2a2-41dc-90ef-ccc336f8ddca:6\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:cb7f252d-c2a2-41dc-90ef-ccc336f8ddca:12\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Applying the previous seed to a re-synced build DB leaves only changed sections NULL; the export round-trips every vector bit-for-bit, reports uncovered rows, and excludes vectors from other spaces.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An unchanged section is left for re-embedding, a changed section receives the old vector, an exported vector differs from the stored one, or an uncovered or other-space row is silently exported.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"format round-trip\",\n      \"incremental cut flow\",\n      \"other-space rows\",\n      \"uncovered count\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the unit suite (format, exact float round-trip) and the integration suite (cut flow: previous seed, re-sync, apply, embed remainder, export).\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/search/doc-vector-seed.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/search/doc-vector-seed.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — A mismatched embedder is safe.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"When the active embedder mode or profile differs from the seed, the loader skips the seed entirely and the existing backfill embeds as today; no vector from another space is written.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:cb7f252d-c2a2-41dc-90ef-ccc336f8ddca:6\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A seed whose profile, mode or width differs from the active prose space writes nothing, and a disabled embedder skips the seed.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any row receives a vector from a seed in a different space or width, or the seed is applied while embedding is disabled.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"profile mismatch\",\n      \"mode mismatch\",\n      \"width mismatch\",\n      \"embedder disabled\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the unit suite (seedSpaceMismatch cases) and the integration suite (foreign seed writes nothing; disabled embedder skip).\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/search/doc-vector-seed.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/search/doc-vector-seed.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — The idle-cost reduction is measured, not assumed.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"On a GCP VM fresh install the doc_sections NULL count for the two source keys is 0 within one sweep of first boot, and idle Server CPU after first boot is under 0.2 core.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:cb7f252d-c2a2-41dc-90ef-ccc336f8ddca:12\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:cb7f252d-c2a2-41dc-90ef-ccc336f8ddca:13\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A fresh-install Server build that ships the seed reaches 0 NULL rows for the seeded source keys within one sweep of first boot and idles under 0.2 core afterwards.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The NULL count stays above 0 after the first sweep, or idle CPU after first boot is at or above 0.2 core.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"live\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"fresh install\",\n      \"first sweep\",\n      \"idle CPU after first boot\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Provision a GCP VM with scripts/agent-capacity/vm, install a Server build that ships the seed, record the doc_sections NULL count after the first sweep and the cgroup CPU delta over 10 idle minutes; record both on WI-10004455.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"gcp-vm-fresh-install-doc-seed\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nThe seed is a release-time artifact: a directory with manifest.json (row keys + embedding space) and vectors.f32 (little-endian float32). The exporter (P-001, scripts/export-doc-vector-seed.mts) reads profile-current doc_sections rows for papercusp-engineering and papercusp-guidance from a build database, after applying the previous release's seed and letting embed-backfill embed the remainder; it refuses to write while any section is uncovered. The boot loader (P-002, doc-vector-seed.ts applyShippedDocVectorSeed) runs inside runDocSectionsSyncOnce right AFTER the doc sync and before the backfill sweep. It fills only NULL rows whose (source_key, slug, anchor, page_sha) match a seed row, so the seed carries no text and the sync stays the only writer of row content. It applies only when the seed's mode/profile is the active embedder's prose space (storedProseIdentityMatches against the sweep's own embedder cascade); otherwise it skips. The Server finds the seed through PAPERCUSP_DOC_VECTOR_SEED_DIR; wiring the seed into the Server bundle is coordinated with the release lane after the 0.0.27 cut.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | live |\n\n## Phase — Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Release-cut step: build a doc_sections vector seed (engineering + guidance) in the shipped embedder space, incremental against the previous release seed by page_sha; bundle it as a Server resource. Test in vitest with a deterministic embedder. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004883 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Boot loader: right after runDocSectionsSyncOnce's sync (before the backfill sweep), fill NULL doc_sections embeddings from the shipped seed where (source_key, slug, anchor, page_sha) match, only when the seed's mode/profile is the active embedder's prose space; skip otherwise. Test against real PG. importance: high — note: ← WI-10004884 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `todo` Guard + live verification: a fresh-install check on a GCP VM (scripts/agent-capacity/vm) asserting doc_sections NULL count is 0 within one sweep of first boot and idle Server CPU after first boot is under 0.2 core. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-01\nAmendment-Id: wi10004455-bar-atomic-r1-r2\nRequest-Hash: b52be4724e038858ef0098a0176add4de4de17e08eb520dc18d5b46f9ea5a793\nActor: su-9dfd3ffc-fb7b-40bf-b625-d93dbab9f002\nReason: plans:evaluate-spec-quality atomic-observable-behavior failed on the AUTO-BAR projections of R-1 (multiple subjects) and R-2 (semicolon-joined assertions). Each BAR now states one observable outcome; the split-off outcomes (the seed never touches embedded or changed rows; exporter bit-for-bit round-trip; uncovered counting) become separate plan clauses on P-002 and P-001.\nApproved-By: su-a3c04f4e-fffc-449e-943b-41e2f5db3a6b\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1153521\nApproved-At: 2026-10-01T13:53:16.593Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 11 → 12\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — Use immutable commit snapshots for clean test evidence\nDate: 2026-10-01\nMeasured: `computeWorktreeDirty` in `packages/operator-core/lib/testing-worktree.ts` requires the before/after commit SHAs to match and the full `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` output to be empty at both points; missing snapshots fail closed. That is the right safety condition for shared-tree runs because declared path fingerprints alone do not prove the full transitive source loaded by a test. The current `WI-10004898` checkpoint records retained-clone reruns at commit `4dff472a12` with `uncommitted=0`, and a mutation-probe row recorded `worktree_dirty=false` after copy-out named the origin checkout.\n\nDecision: choose option (a): produce clean evidence from a detached, immutable commit snapshot for both `testing:run` and `mutation-probe`, recording that commit and marking the run clean only when the snapshot is clean and stable before/after. Keep shared-tree dirtiness fail-closed; do not narrow it to declared or statically discovered files. Add the explicit freshness message for `test-run-worktree-not-clean` as a separate diagnostic fix. Guard the producer with an integration test that starts from a shared tree containing unrelated dirty paths and proves the snapshot-bound run is current only for its recorded commit.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10004883 — Release-cut step: build a doc_sections vector seed (engineering + guidance) in the shipped embedder space, incremental against the previous release seed by page_sha; bundle it as a Server resource. T… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004884 — Boot loader: right after runDocSectionsSyncOnce's sync (before the backfill sweep), fill NULL doc_sections embeddings from the shipped seed where (source_key, slug, anchor, page_sha) match, only when… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10004885 — Guard + live verification: a fresh-install check on a GCP VM (scripts/agent-capacity/vm) asserting doc_sections NULL count is 0 within one sweep of first boot and idle Server CPU after first boot is … <!-- P-003 -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"staging-api-start-pre-lock-attribution-2026-10-01","title":"Staging API start-pre lock attribution","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Staging API start-pre lock attribution\nslug: staging-api-start-pre-lock-attribution-2026-10-01\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\nDraft the lock-attribution change and preserve the unresolved status of the historical 04:53Z/05:51Z listener windows.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-001 — Correlated start-pre evidence.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Record bounded durable evidence for every :3170 service start-pre attempt so its lock wait and result can be correlated to that startup.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"The current ExecStartPre has no durable attempt-scoped wait/acquisition record.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Do not attribute the historical 04:53Z/05:51Z refusal windows without time-matched evidence.\",\n      \"Do not restart :3170 for verification.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"work-item:WI-10004755\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Every start-pre attempt writes an invocation-correlated unit-journal record with an explicit attempt id or unavailable value, surface/state, lock path and mode, wait start, bounded wait samples, acquisition outcome, elapsed wait, and API unit state/readiness evidence.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A start-pre attempt has no correlated record, omits a required lock/wait/outcome field, or leaves unavailable evidence implicit.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"start-pre\",\n      \"attempt-id\",\n      \"lock-wait\",\n      \"unit-journal\",\n      \"unit-state\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the focused Vitest regressions that exercise start-pre record emission and bounded lock contention using a temporary lock fixture.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/sync-staging-checkout.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-002 — Best-effort holder identity.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Report the identity of a holder contending with the shared staging-sync lock when the lock-file identity supports a direct match.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Holder attribution must be measured from the lock identity rather than inferred from nearby activity.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Use holder=unknown whenever the lock identity or /proc/locks read is incomplete.\",\n      \"Never infer a holder from timing or a similar process.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"work-item:WI-10004755\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"On contention, holder PID and short process name are emitted only after matching the lock file device/inode to /proc/locks; every unavailable or incomplete resolution emits holder=unknown.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A holder is inferred without an identity match, or an incomplete lookup is reported as a known holder.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"holder-pid\",\n      \"holder-command\",\n      \"unknown-fallback\",\n      \"identity-match\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run focused Vitest cases for a known lock holder, unknown/incomplete holder resolution, and contended start-pre evidence.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/sync-staging-checkout.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-003 — Sync lock evidence.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Make staging-sync lock attempts and transitions durably attributable to each sync invocation.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"The sync runner is the exclusive-lock participant that can contend with start-pre.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Preserve single-flight and checkout safety behavior.\",\n      \"Preserve the existing exclusive-to-shared lock transition.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"work-item:WI-10004755\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Each staging-sync invocation records its lock attempt, contention or skip outcome, holder identity when available, and exclusive/shared transitions with one correlation id.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A sync attempt cannot be correlated to its lock outcome or holder evidence, or the evidence change weakens single-flight or checkout safety.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"staging-sync\",\n      \"contention\",\n      \"holder\",\n      \"lock-transition\",\n      \"single-flight\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run focused Vitest coverage for staging-sync contention, holder reporting, and the existing lock transition behavior.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/sync-staging-checkout.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-004 — Preserve startup contract.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Add diagnostics without changing service startup, lock, bundle, readiness, or timeout behavior.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"Observability must not create or prolong a :3170 outage.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Keep the historical 04:53Z/05:51Z refusal causes unknown absent time-matched evidence.\",\n      \"Do not restart :3170 for verification.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"work-item:WI-10004755\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The existing shared/exclusive flock semantics, bundle-host.sh invocation, Type=notify readiness, and 15-minute systemd start deadline remain intact; evidence collection is best-effort and makes no causal claim about the historical refusal windows.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The change alters the lock or startup contract, blocks readiness on diagnostics, changes the start deadline, or asserts a historical outage cause without time-matched evidence.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"flock-semantics\",\n      \"bundle-script\",\n      \"type-notify\",\n      \"start-deadline\",\n      \"historical-cause-unknown\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the focused lock-evidence Vitest suite and the systemd start-limit/readiness regression suite.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/sync-staging-checkout.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/systemd-startlimit-placement-guard.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-005 — Regression coverage.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Add conventional regression coverage for the lock-record parser and both lock contention paths.\",\n    \"rationale\": \"These records only help if future changes fail tests when correlation or safe unknown handling regresses.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Use a temporary lock fixture.\",\n      \"Do not restart :3170.\",\n      \"Add tests to the conventional Vitest suite.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"work-item:WI-10004755\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The Vitest suite covers exact record parsing, known and unknown holder results, contended start-pre evidence, and staging-sync contention with a temporary lock fixture.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any listed behavior lacks a regression assertion, or verification depends on restarting the live :3170 service.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"record-parser\",\n      \"known-holder\",\n      \"unknown-holder\",\n      \"start-pre-contention\",\n      \"staging-sync-contention\",\n      \"temporary-lock-fixture\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the conventional focused Vitest files for staging-sync lock evidence and the systemd startup contract.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/sync-staging-checkout.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/systemd-startlimit-placement-guard.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing `sync-staging-checkout.sh` path with start-pre instrumentation that assigns one attempt ID before lock acquisition and uses it across the invocation's journal records. Emit an initial record before waiting and a completion record for each returned acquisition outcome; both identify the `start-pre` surface, current state, lock path, and shared mode. If the attempt ID cannot be generated, emit the explicit value `unavailable`.\n\nRecord the wait start time, acquisition outcome, and elapsed wait in milliseconds. While contended, emit at most five timestamped wait samples, each with elapsed milliseconds and best-effort holder evidence; the sample cap keeps diagnostic output bounded. On contention, resolve a holder only by matching the lock file device/inode against `/proc/locks`, report only PID and short process name, and emit `holder=unknown` whenever the identity or read is incomplete.\n\nInclude the API unit's observed state and readiness evidence in the correlated completion record, with explicit `unknown` values for unavailable properties. Keep collection best-effort and preserve the existing shared/exclusive flock lifecycle, bundle invocation, Type=notify readiness policy, and 15-minute start deadline. Preserve the unresolved status of the historical 04:53Z/05:51Z listener refusals; the 05:41Z sync evidence does not establish their cause, and verification must not restart :3170.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-001 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-002 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-003 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-004 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-005 | P-002 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Lock attribution\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add invocation-correlated lock and holder evidence to start-pre and staging-sync, preserving current lock and readiness semantics. — note: ← WI-6554700010014358 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Add exact parser, contention, unknown-holder and temporary-lock regressions in the conventional Vitest suite. — note: ← WI-6554700010014359 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAmendment-Id: staging-lock-attribution-check-paths-20261015-v1\nRequest-Hash: 0bd67623d9ce336cc1a30f3d4eca1672e4949d9248254ba1f8d2a87534fc0f75\nActor: su-c6723ee0-b51c-41b8-91f4-e5b0e58b1adb\nReason: Correct verification routing to include the existing conventional attribution suite that actually tests start-pre records, exact/unknown holders and both temporary-lock contention paths. Preserve all five outcome bars, falsifiers, scopes and tree/unit requirements. No startup behavior or historical causal assertion changed.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004, R-005)\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 3 → 4\nChanged BARs: R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004, R-005\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"trigger-automation-consolidation-2026-10-01","title":"Consolidate the six \"when X happens, do Y\" mechanisms into one trigger → action → policy model","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-01","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Consolidate the six \"when X happens, do Y\" mechanisms into one trigger → action → policy model\nslug: trigger-automation-consolidation-2026-10-01\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-01\nupdated: 2026-10-16\n---\n\n# Consolidate the six \"when X happens, do Y\" mechanisms\n\n> **Status: DRAFT for owner review.** Drafted per owner directive #1212, option (b): \"I draft a plan for consolidating the trigger mechanisms for you to review before any build\". The current kickoff authorizes execution of this plan; implementation starts only after supported preparation and admission gates pass.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001 is complete with committed authority. P-002 implementation is present in the shared staging tree: selective spend pause holds launch-plan/start-goal/blueprint-operation receipts (including old pending rows) while deterministic create-work-item receipts drain, and dispatcher active:false disarm remains unchanged. Focused unit evidence passed 2/2 and the private-PG binding-engine integration passed 25/25, but those runs were on a dirty tree and the adequacy evaluator still reports unknown falsifiability and plan-class-risk-floor for all three active P-002 clauses. A background git-sync is currently holding the tree lock after disk-headroom recovery; committed-tree remeasurement and clause-targeted proof binding remain open.\n\n**Next:** After the in-flight git-sync releases git-sync:papercusp, retry the sanctioned background git-sync fire if needed, verify the new local SHA and clean status, rerun the two focused P-002 files with explicit papercusp scope against that committed tree, bind targeted mutation/test and coverage proof to the three current clauses, re-read adequacy and complete P-002.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010016227 — Record the reproducible row inventory and Trigger/Action/Policy mapping of six mechanisms, inactive rows and infrastructure exclusions. Resolve semantic gaps before moving data. () <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010016228 — Implement selective per-action spend policy on existing bindings and preserve deliberate pause intent without pausing the whole dispatcher. () () <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010016229 — Route plan and user-facing blueprint scheduled fires into binding runs using existing DBOS/ephemeral timers, retaining overlap, catchup and arming semantics. () () <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010016230 — Route eligible event reactions and predicate watches into binding runs while preserving match, dedupe, failure/retry and bound lifecycle behavior. () () <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010016231 — Make Workflows consume the common automation read model and explain armed, paused, stale and rate-capped state uniformly. () () <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010016232 — Migrate and retire each duplicate stack only after an audited zero-residue census, preserve triggers:bind for existing packs, and obtain independent
