Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05","title":"End-user bug reports as a core Papercusp feature, unified with agent bug filing","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-05","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: End-user bug reports as a core Papercusp feature, unified with agent bug filing\nslug: end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-10-05\nupdated: 2026-10-06\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-06. Nothing in this plan is actionable. Anything below this line is the last pre-superseded snapshot, kept for history: it described work that is finished or abandoned, so do not start from it. Read frontmatter `status`, not this prose, to learn whether a plan is live (stamped by plans:set-plan-status).\n\n⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-05, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty. Next repair: Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nDRAFT, written 2026-10-05 by su-4a152 at Avi's request (directive #1335; owner-dialog choices \"Write the draft plan\" and \"Hosted relay\"). 12 items in 3 phases (shared intake → dogfood in the Papercusp desktop app → builder aspect template plus hosted relay) and 4 decisions. D-002 (hosted relay) is Avi's choice; D-001, D-003 and D-004 are proposals awaiting his review. Nothing is built and nothing has started.\n\n**Next:** none — the plan is superseded. (Pre-superseded next, no longer actionable: Avi reviews the draft. Before activation: settle the Open questions section (anonymous vs contactable reporters, screenshot/log retention and consent, relay hosting owner and abuse limits, the probation promotion rule), run the activation audit over the source conversation, then choose an execution route. Reuse check for P-009: a hosted relay already exists for psu --connect to hosted workspaces (plan psu-cloud-connector-liveness-multi-signin-2026-09-29, from memory, not re-verified). Evaluate extending it before building a new relay.)\n\n## Context\n\nToday's filing surfaces, and what this plan reuses:\n- Agents file through `improvements:capture` (lands as EI- rows in the engineer-issues store) or `work_items:create`. Capture already refuses near-duplicates by embedding similarity.\n- Suspected tool failures already use **probation + corroboration**: one report sits in a correlated, non-claimable holding state, and a second independent reporter (or the invocation-ledger watchdog) promotes the SAME row. End-user reports need exactly that shape.\n- The watchdog files objective tool-error clusters automatically.\n- `platform:contribute` already sends things upstream from a platform-mode install to canonical Papercusp.\n- App templates: `papercusp-app`, `papercusp-android-app` and `papercusp-iphone-app` roots. Agents cross into an app through the ONE typed seam `papercusp-ops-pots`.\n\nMain risk: the bug queue is already large. The work-selection census (docs/evidence/work-selection-census-2026-10-01) counted 1,806 open bugs and 2,787 open changes, excluding observations. Raw user reports added on top would be buried, so the design puts deduplication and grouping at the front door.\n\n## Design in one paragraph\n\nOne queue with several ways in. A report from a person becomes the same bug work-item agents file. The only additions are a \"reported by\" provenance (agent | watchdog | end-user) and a context block captured automatically when the report is sent: app, version, screen or URL state, recent errors, a log excerpt and an optional screenshot. Every source goes through one intake step: redact secrets, find duplicates, attach to an existing item or create a new one, then hold it in probation until it is corroborated or triaged. Corroboration count (\"14 users hit this\") raises priority. The reporter sees status, can answer an agent's follow-up question, and is told when the fix ships. Report text is untrusted evidence and is never treated as instructions.\n\n## Open questions (to settle before activation)\n\n- Anonymous reports vs. an optional email or account for follow-ups and the \"fixed\" notice.\n- Retention and privacy for screenshots and log excerpts, including what the reporter consents to.\n- Who hosts and pays for the relay (D-002), plus its abuse and rate limits.\n- Promotion rule for end-user reports: how many distinct reporters, or which triage step, lifts an item out of probation.\n- Whether apps built from templates follow Papercusp's own rule that user-meaningful UI state lives in the URL (nuqs). That rule is what makes \"reopen the exact screen\" possible. This is not verified for template apps.\n\n## Phase 1 — One intake for every reporter\n\n- **P-001** `dropped` Reporter provenance + captured context on the bug work-item: reporter {kind: agent|watchdog|end-user, ...} and a context block (app, version, screen/URL state, recent errors, log excerpt, screenshot ref). Extend the corroboration record toolFailure probation already keeps per row; add a child report record only if nothing existing fits. No parallel bug table. — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n- **P-002** `dropped` One intake function every source calls — improvements:capture, the watchdog, and the in-app reporter: redact secrets → dedupe (reuse capture's similarity check) → attach to existing item or create → probation until corroborated or triaged. blocked-by: P-001 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n- **P-003** `dropped` Corroboration-driven priority: distinct-reporter count shown on the item (\"14 users hit this\") and feeding its priority; settle and implement the end-user promotion-out-of-probation rule. blocked-by: P-002 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n- **P-004** `dropped` Untrusted-input handling: end-user report text reaches fixing agents only as quoted evidence, never as instructions; secret redaction on attached logs/context; tests for both. blocked-by: P-002 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Dogfood in the Papercusp desktop app\n\n- **P-005** `dropped` \"Report a problem\" in the Papercusp desktop app (menu item + shortcut): one-sentence field, context captured automatically, preview of exactly what will be sent, consent. blocked-by: P-002, P-004 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n- **P-006** `dropped` Route reports from Papercusp installs upstream to the Papercusp hive over the existing platform:contribute / federation path — no new channel. blocked-by: P-005 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n- **P-007** `dropped` Reporter status thread: the reporter sees received → being worked on → fixed in vX, the fixing agent can ask one follow-up question, and the reporter is notified when the release carrying the fix ships (tie to the release registry). blocked-by: P-005 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n- **P-008** `dropped` Update the public Releases-page section \"Don't like something about Papercusp?\" (apps/operator/lib/release/release-instructions.ts) to point users at Report a problem. blocked-by: P-005 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001..P-008 are P-010..P-017 there.\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Bug reports for apps built with Papercusp\n\n- **P-009** `dropped` Hosted report relay (D-002): receives reports from users of builders' apps and holds them for the builder's pot to pull; per-app auth, abuse and rate limits, retention. Design doc first (hosting/cost owner is an open question). blocked-by: P-002 — note: Carried into built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 (P-001..P-004) via unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 D-010 and D-014.\n- **P-010** `dropped` New aspect template papercusp-feedback: the Report-a-problem widget (desktop menu, mobile shake-to-report) composing onto papercusp-app / papercusp-android-app / papercusp-iphone-app; reports flow relay → builder pot through the papercusp-ops-pots seam; GUIDE + template checks. blocked-by: P-009 — note: Carried into built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 (P-001..P-004) via unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 D-010 and D-014.\n- **P-011** `dropped` Builder-side view in the builder's pot: grouped reports with reporter counts, and replies back to reporters through the status thread. blocked-by: P-010, P-007 — note: Carried into built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 (P-001..P-004) via unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 D-010 and D-014.\n- **P-012** `dropped` End-to-end acceptance: a freshly materialized template app files a report → relay → builder pot → an agent fixes it → the reporter receives the fixed-in-version notice. blocked-by: P-010, P-011 — note: Carried into built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 (P-001..P-004) via unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 D-010 and D-014.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — One bug queue, several ways in — no parallel system for user reports\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[proposed by su-4a152 2026-10-05; Avi approved drafting, not yet ratified] A report from a person is the same bug work-item agents file, distinguished only by a reporter provenance field and an auto-captured context block. Agents, the watchdog and the in-app reporter all call one intake step (redact → dedupe → attach-or-create → probation). Rationale: a second queue would split triage, double the dedupe problem, and hide from agents the user evidence for bugs they already know about.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-002 — Transport for apps whose users do not run Papercusp: a hosted relay\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05, owner-dialog answer \"Hosted relay (Recommended)\"] Reports from users of builders' apps go to a small hosted relay that the builder's Papercusp pot pulls from, rather than each builder hosting their own receiving endpoint. Builders set up nothing; we take on hosting (cost/ownership is an open question).\nRelated: P-009, P-010\n\n### D-003 — End-user report text is untrusted evidence, never instructions\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[proposed by su-4a152 2026-10-05, not yet ratified] Reports come from outside the trust boundary. Fixing agents receive report text only as quoted evidence; it can never steer them. Secrets are redacted from attached logs and context, and the reporter previews exactly what is sent before submitting.\nRelated: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-004 — Corroboration, not volume: single reports wait in probation\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[proposed by su-4a152 2026-10-05, not yet ratified] Reuse the toolFailure probation shape: one report waits in a correlated, non-claimable holding state; matching reports attach to the same item and raise its priority, so 14 users hitting one bug is one item marked \"14 users\", not 14 items. Motivation: 1,806 open bugs in the 2026-10-01 work-selection census.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-005 — Verify before claimable: every bug, from an agent or a person, stays a candidate until a reviewer reproduces it on the current build, inside the existing bulk review\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[proposed by su-4a152 [turn:self]; not ratified. Avi asked (directive #1349) whether human and agent bugs should be verified as real before they become claimable, and whether that belongs in bulk triage.]\n\nFindings (measured 2026-10-05 ~21:28Z):\n- work_items:claimable (harness papercusp, kind bug): 246 claimable out of 1,378 matched; 67 of the claimable bugs were admitted today. Measured: work_items:claimable { harness:'papercusp', kind:'bug', breakdownOnly:true } at 21:28:10Z.\n- Today's admission step checks only for duplicates. When that promoter is down, a separate fail-open runner admits rows as `unreviewed`. Measured: header comment, lines 1-14 of packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-admission-promoter.ts. EI-22154020611570329 (state blocked; its checkpoint names a Codex capacity wall) tracks the promoter going stale.\n- Plan observation-candidate-acceptance-promotion-2026-09-30 (WI-10004504) is built to turn every new item into a candidate that needs an acceptance receipt from a saved bulk review run before it can be claimed. Dispositions: promote | merge | investigate | retain | reject | retry. Its claim floor is built (P-011), but enforcement is OFF: the cutover sits at the 2100 sentinel. Switching it on is WI-10005016 (state blocked, no assignee). Its checkpoint says it waits on P-005/P-007 being live on :3070; that deploy state was not re-probed here.\n- That plan's acceptance step reviews the assembled evidence and the current code and runtime status, and it says repeated reports alone cannot certify a defect (R-16). It never requires a REPRODUCTION. Measured: a case-insensitive search for reproduc / repro / 'real bug' / 'false positive' / 'not a bug' over the plan's full content plus all decision bodies in harness_shared.harness_plans (workspace papercusp-workspace, harness papercusp) returned 0 matches. A grep of packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review-policy.ts for the same terms also returned 0.\n- Agent reports are not reliably true. EI-19448526819046979 (state done) records a filed bug whose root cause was an unverified inference carried from a carry-note. The compaction guidance cites it as costing a peer a full investigation cycle.\n\nProposal:\n1. Get enforcement switched on (WI-10005016) so candidates really are unclaimable until accepted.\n2. For kind=bug, the `promote` disposition requires a reproduction receipt from the current build: a failing test, a scripted repro, or a log or ledger observation from the current build. If the reviewer cannot reproduce it quickly, the disposition is `investigate`, which spawns a small repro task that is not implementation work. A bug that no longer reproduces goes to `reject`, or to `retain` as evidence.\n3. The reproduction becomes the fix's failing test, which the bug-close rule already requires as the recurrence guard. Verification is therefore mostly work that is already owed, moved earlier.\n4. The same rule applies to agent and human reports. Human reports are additionally redacted and treated as untrusted (D-003).\n5. This plan's D-004 probation is replaced by the other plan's candidate stage. No separate probation mechanism gets built. Corroboration ('14 users hit this') sets priority in the review order but never substitutes for reproduction.\n\nCross-lane: points 1-2 change plan observation-candidate-acceptance-promotion-2026-09-30, so they need Avi's go and a decision recorded on THAT plan.\nRatified: Avi on 2026-10-05\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fleet-queue-census-and-gate-routing-2026-10-05","title":"Complete queue breakdown in fleet leader brief","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-05","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Complete queue breakdown in fleet leader brief\nslug: fleet-queue-census-and-gate-routing-2026-10-05\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-10-05\nupdated: 2026-10-06\n---\n\n## Purpose\nAdd the automatic, complete and actionable queue breakdown Avi requested to fleet:leader-brief. Extend its existing fleetMetrics snapshot and work_items:burn_down reader so a leader can explain remaining work without assembling counts manually. Planning and investigation are owned by WI-10006089; continuing fleet leadership remains WI-10006086.\n\n## Scope\nThe delivery is reporting: complete aggregation, literal gate classification, responsible resolution routes, and integration into the existing brief. Preserve the current claim rules. Validation handoff and known-tool freshness repairs from the earlier draft remain separate follow-up findings owned by WI-10006089; they are not silently cleared or implemented by this reporting change. Keep this plan draft until activation review and its implementation route are recorded.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — One complete snapshot.** Apply the stored fleet claim spec and canonical matcher to the complete eligible population. Aggregate before display/sample limits. Record the existing snapshot timestamp, harness, spec revision, population and exactness. Remaining primary categories must sum to remaining total. Preserve fleet-lifetime terminal authority accounting separately; proposed closes are not credited completions. Missing historical scope or a failed read remains explicit unknown.\n\n**R-2 — Literal reasons and executable next steps.** Reuse the existing primary precedence (needsHuman, blocked, claimHeld, inFlight, claimable, otherUnclaimable). Subdivide each primary category by its actual cause. Distinguish agentReview pending/revision-requested, readiness validation, unknown or stale source freshness, admission review debt, manual parks, dependencies, and typed owner capabilities. Preserve literal state/source/reason, creation actor, age, current holder, resolver or unassigned queue, next action and exact evidence references. Overlapping secondary labels are separate annotations, never an additive primary partition.\n\n**R-3 — Claimability parity.** The reported implementation-claimable set must agree with the canonical scheduler/filter/floor oracle. A review item can be available to a reviewer while blocked for implementation. admissionReview pending after fail-open admission is debt, not automatically an implementation refusal. Approval alone does not erase other blockers or replace a qualifying current acceptance contract. Do not invent an actor or a resolution where none is recorded.\n\n**R-4 — Brief delivery.** The default fleet:leader-brief response exposes complete totals and cause counts with a compact mechanically rendered explanation. Cap examples and member detail after aggregation. Preserve counts, identity, exactness and omission/recovery metadata through leader-brief shaping and the result door. Unavailable data cannot appear as zero or as a complete report. Include a direct drill-down route using existing tools; no new report service, table, cron or parallel receipt system.\n\n**R-5 — Recurrence guards.** Canonical tests cover more than 2,000 source rows, simultaneous conflicting gates, missing/malformed readiness, review and admission-debt cases, sparse metadata, capped examples, transport shaping, and unavailable reads. Verify disjointness, total reconciliation, scheduler parity and preservation of the count contract. Feature tests ship with their implementation units.\n\n## Design and reuse\nExtend packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-metrics-contract.ts and the existing canonical fleet metric reader. Reuse matchesClaimSpecFilter, the claim-floor/readiness and intake-stage classifiers, typed blocker/dependency readers and completion authority. Integrate through the existing bounded fleet-metrics leg in leader-brief.ts and its shapers. Prefer set-based aggregation; if paging is required, keep one consistent snapshot and prove coverage. Do not hydrate every full work-item payload solely to count it, widen timeouts, or remove display budgets.\n\n### Bar-to-work map\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-004 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Complete snapshot and literal classification\n- **P-001** `dropped` Extend the existing complete fleet census and typed snapshot with deterministic primary/cause partitions, scheduler parity, responsible resolution detail and producer-level canonical tests. — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001 -> P-022, P-004 -> P-024, P-005 -> P-025.\n\n## Phase 2 — Leader brief integration and acceptance\n- **P-004** `dropped` Add the complete breakdown and compact explanation to the default fleet:leader-brief; preserve metadata through shaping and existing drill-down paths, with canonical transport tests. blocked-by: P-001 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001 -> P-022, P-004 -> P-024, P-005 -> P-025.\n- **P-005** `dropped` Verify the integrated brief against adversarial fixtures above 2,000 rows and real controlled current-build snapshots; reconcile every fixture ID/count and prove unknown/partial reporting and scheduler parity. Run the affected canonical suites and required checks. blocked-by: P-004 — note: Carried into unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 per its D-010 (Avi #1364, 'combine them'): P-001 -> P-022, P-004 -> P-024, P-005 -> P-025.\n\n## Deferred from the earlier draft\n- **P-002** `dropped` Corroborated tool-failure validation handoff repair is outside this reporting delivery; retain its source finding and follow-up accountability on WI-10006089.\n- **P-003** `dropped` Known-tool source/freshness lookup repair is outside this reporting delivery; retain its source finding and follow-up accountability on WI-10006089.\n\n## Acceptance\nA single ordinary fleet:leader-brief call returns a complete, reproducible remaining-work partition and precise cause breakdown from one scope/time. A reader can identify which items are ready for implementation, ready for review/validation, waiting on dependencies, or genuinely require Avi. Every retained hold has a recorded resolution route or an explicit missing-route finding. Counts remain trustworthy after examples/transport are bounded. No claim floor, owner gate or peer claim changes as a side effect of reporting.\n\n## Verification and activation\nUse the project's existing fleet-metrics, leader-brief, claim-floor/readiness and admission integration suites. Tests for each source change land with that change; P-005 verifies cross-layer behavior rather than rerunning saved proof. Use staging/current-build for normal acceptance and leave final promotion/shipment to its separate route. Before activation, audit the complete owner conversation and record derived items/dependencies; choose an admitted implementation lane because this fleet's bug-only filter does not automatically authorize newly materialized plan tasks.\n\n## Historical evidence\nThe earlier 18:01 UTC audit classified 451 review-labeled rows as 226 validation holds, 205 unknown freshness holds, 3 pending reviews and 17 revision requests; 431 lacked a review record. These are historical observations, not current acceptance counts. Full dated scope, source references and corrections live on WI-10006089.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Reuse selected-evidence repairs and reconcile overlapping aggregate scope\nDate: 2026-10-05\nMeasured: this turn read the canonical result-door.test.ts work_items:get reread-handle regression at lines281-327 and both complete work-item summaries/checkpoints. EI-24958944483532851 already owns the selected-set completeness producer units, including links/get. EI-25152812262925548 repeats that mechanism and includes the existing parent among its contributors, plus four additional references: EI-11404, EI-21014373222385988, EI-23718219845571361, EI-24655796887885737.\n\nThe brief must reuse these producer contracts; no parallel receipt/completeness implementation. The overlapping links/get implementation remains under the existing parent and its current claim/locks. EI-25152812262925548 is a coverage-comparison lane until its four additional references are mapped to already-covered or genuinely distinct producer acceptance. Do not dedup the entire aggregate merely from similarity, and do not repeat the completed get unit. Report any uncovered source-specific unit for deliberate allocation; preserve all contributor obligations before terminal disposition. This decision records a reuse boundary, not plan activation or a claim transfer.\nRelated: P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"gitnexus-deterministic-integration-2026-10-05","title":"GitNexus in deterministic tooling: revive graph test selection, add test-reach ordering and flags, fix routing, measure outcomes","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-05","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: GitNexus in deterministic tooling: revive graph test selection, add test-reach ordering and flags, fix routing, measure outcomes\nslug: gitnexus-deterministic-integration-2026-10-05\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-10-05\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-15. Items are agent-proposed from the 2026-10-05 conversation in which Avi asked whether we use GitNexus, whether better adoption would help, and how to integrate it into deterministic/testing tools.\n\n## Context — measured 2026-10-05 ~21:05–21:35Z (su-72f78fbb)\n\n**Infrastructure is live and healthy.**\n- Plugin `libs/papercusp/plugins/gitnexus-bridge` proxies `npx gitnexus mcp` as `gitnexus.*` tools; curated facade `graph:query` (code-intelligence D-058); library layer `packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/` (gitnexus-facade, selective-assist, consumer-evidence).\n- Index `.gitnexus/` = 8.0 GB (graph DB 6.2 GB), indexed 2026-10-05T20:33Z at `staging`: 27,746 files, 317k nodes, 664k edges, 274k embeddings; graph/fts/vector all available.\n- Routine `gitnexus-reindex` (cron `0 35 * * * *`) active, last fired 20:35Z, 0 consecutive failures; index disk 8.1 GB vs 2 GB budget recorded as `accepted-exceedance`.\n\n**Agent use is marginal.** `harness_shared.tool_invocations`, workspace papercusp-workspace, last 30 days:\n- `gitnexus.cypher` 2,325 — 2,320 of them one session (su-95c6c914) ending 2026-10-02T01:43Z = the one-shot P-008 snapshot producer run, not organic use.\n- `graph:query` 14 calls / 13 sessions; `gitnexus.context` 31 (at least partly `graph:query`'s own dispatch); `gitnexus.list_repos` 16; `query` 1; `check` 2; `tool_map` 1. No calls since 2026-10-03T03:31Z.\n- For comparison: `lsp:query` 9 calls / 5 sessions; `search:semantic` 4,457; `capability:read` 29,342.\n- Native shell (`harness_shared.agent_activity`, last 7 days, rough regex): ~129k commands, ~26k recursive `grep`/`rg`, ~2,960 definition-shaped, ~6,900 call-site-shaped.\n\n**The shipped GitNexus testing integration is inert.** P-008 of `gitnexus-selective-hardening-and-comparison-2026-09-13` makes `scripts/affected-tests.mjs` ADD workspaces from a precomputed snapshot (`.papercusp/graph-snapshot/dependency-snapshot.json`). Filed as **WI-10006138**.\n\n**A static import graph already drives file-level selection — GitNexus must add to it, not duplicate it.** Plan `file-level-test-selection-2026-08-17` (awaiting-acceptance) built a cheap static reverse-import index (`scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs` over `scripts/lib/module-reachability.mjs`; its D-003: every rail fails toward running MORE tests). The green-checkpoint invokes `npm run test:related`, which narrows each affected workspace to reachable test files and widens back to the full suite on unresolved edges. Plan `gate-file-level-test-reuse-2026-09-27` (shipped) added per-test-file pass reuse. So file-level \"which tests can this change reach\" largely exists without GitNexus. What GitNexus can add: symbol-level CALLS edges (which tests call the changed function, not merely import its file), cross-workspace edges through aliases/relative imports the package graph misses (P-008), and edges through re-exports.\n\n**The routing guidance contradicts the owner-ratified table.** Code-intelligence D-001 [owner: Avi 2026-08-21] routes definition/references to the `lsp` facade and only call chains / impact / topology to GitNexus. classes that are graph questions: head-truncated grep producing false \"no callers\" verdicts; adding a call strands call-count assertions in another workspace (WI-37582: ~3 gate reds, ~2h frozen main); `lint:behavioural-strands` exiting 0 on a real strand (EI-23776710603159495); deleted/renamed exports breaking unsearched consumers.\n\n**Known graph limits.** Index is hourly and This does not waive P-018 or award operational catch credit.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-018 | deployed |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-015 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003, P-017 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-012 | tree |\n\nRewritten per D-021 (2026-10-06): the P-003 replay did not demonstrate the D-006 threshold, so P-004..P-011, P-013 and P-014 were dropped. R-5 now covers the only graph-backed integration that ships, P-001's add-only test-selection suggestions. R-2 keeps P-002.\n\n## Design principles (proposed — see Decisions D-002, D-003)\n\n1. **Embed, don't exhort.** Put graph answers inside tools agents already run; no item exists to raise direct `gitnexus.*` call counts.\n2. **Add, order, or flag — never subtract.** The graph may add tests/workspaces, reorder execution, or warn. It never removes a test from selection, skips a check, or turns a check green. Stale, empty, or erroring graph ⇒ the existing route, silently.\n3. **Snapshot-bound and source-corroborated.** Deterministic tools read a snapshot bound to an index commit with an age ceiling and re-verify each edge against current source (the P-008 rails). Never a live graph-server call in the gate's critical path.\n4. **Empty is not absence.** A graph answer of \"no callers / no reaching tests\" is a state report, never proof (contracts.ts `isTrustworthyEmpty`).\n5. **Static index first, graph as refinement.** File-level reach comes from the existing static import index; GitNexus contributes only what that index cannot see.\n6. **Outcomes over usage.** Measure strand-caused reds, time-to-first-red, retracted absence claims; decide keep/narrow/scale-back on that evidence.\n\n## Reuse\n\nBuilds on, rather than duplicates: the P-008 snapshot producer + selector (`scripts/gen-graph-dependency-snapshot.mjs`, `scripts/lib/graph-dependency-suggestions.mjs`); the static import index (`scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs`, `scripts/lib/module-reachability.mjs`); per-file pass reuse (gate-file-level-test-reuse); selective-assist (`shared-helper-change` trigger) and consumer-evidence (grader evidence); the bash-substitution pair registry + `gen:tool-routing`; `lint:behavioural-strands`; `gate.greenCheckpoint.candidateFailures`; the repair-queue hunk ledger. Backend stays as settled by gitnexus-selective-hardening D-002 (keep GitNexus 1.6.9).\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Using the graph to SHRINK test selection — including \"resolving\" edges the static index cannot resolve so that a workspace no longer widens to its full suite. That narrows selection on graph evidence and is excluded by principle 2; it would need its own owner-approved plan.\n- Forcing agents to call `gitnexus.*` directly, or quotas on graph calls.\n- Replacing or upgrading the GitNexus backend (settled by gitnexus-selective-hardening D-002).\n- Any use of `gitnexus.query` for ranking (D-021).\n\n## Open questions (for Avi)\n\n1. **Go/no-go threshold for P-003.** Proposed default: proceed with Phases 2–4 if the replay shows GitNexus — beyond what the static import index already gives — would have caught or materially sped up ≥3 incidents or ≥20% of the sampled cross-workspace reds in the last 30 days; otherwise do only Phase 1 and decide on scale-back.\n2. **Warn vs refuse.** P-006 (test-reach check) and P-011 (negative-claim evidence) start warn-only. Should P-011 later refuse a completion that asserts \"unused / no callers\" without evidence?\n3. **Gate visibility of the snapshot.** Unverified whether the green-checkpoint's isolated checkout can read a snapshot under the shared tree's gitignored `.papercusp/` (part of P-001).\n4. **One import graph or two.** The static walker and the GitNexus snapshot overlap on file-level import edges. Keep both as independent cross-checks, or derive one from the other? (decided in P-004)\n5. **Licence.** A memory note from 2026-08-08 records an unresolved GitNexus licence question; not verified here. Relevant before embedding it deeper and before the open-source export to `Papercusp/papercusp-app`.\n\n## Phase 1 — Revive and correct what already exists\n\n- **P-001** `done` **Revive the graph suggestions in test selection (WI-10006138).** The P-008 snapshot that lets `test:affected` / `test:related` ADD workspaces has been stale since ~2026-10-03 because nothing regenerates it. Not abandoned: the GitNexus disposition and deployed check now live there.\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — One shared test-reach lookup\n\n- **P-004** `dropped` **Build the shared \"which tests reach this change\" lookup that P-005..P-008 use.** Reuse, don't fork: file-level reach comes from the existing static import index (`scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs` over `scripts/lib/module-reachability.mjs`); GitNexus contributes only an optional precision layer read from the P-008 snapshot, extended with symbol-level CALLS edges (test file → called symbol) beside its file import edges. Input: changed paths, plus changed symbols derived from diff hunks (enclosing function/class). Output: `{ reachingTests[] ranked by evidence (calls-changed-symbol > imports-changed-file), status: fresh|stale|absent|unknown, indexCommit, ageMs }`. Same rails as P-008: snapshot bound to an index commit, age ceiling, per-edge source corroboration (importer sha256), fail-open to `unknown` — never an empty list on a stale index. Decide and record (open question 4) whether the static walker and the snapshot stay independent cross-checks or one derives from the other. Tests: pure unit tests, an integration test on a fixture snapshot, and a calibration case against the real index (a known function with known calling tests). The SET is unchanged — assert ordered set == unordered set as an invariant test — so there is no false-green risk. No backend change ships without that Decision. — note: ← WI-10006297 completed (done)\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — A separate plan, not more items on gitnexus-selective-hardening-and-comparison-2026-09-13\nDate: 2026-10-05\nDate: 2026-10-05\nSource: [self-imposed] su-72f78fbb while writing this plan for owner directive #1352.\n\nContext: plans:new refused similar_exists against file-level-test-selection-2026-08-17 (awaiting-acceptance), gitnexus-embeddings-enablement-2026-09-05 (shipped) and the acceptance BAR of gitnexus-selective-hardening-and-comparison-2026-09-13. Avi's approval of this plan ratifies it.\n\nRuling: in every deterministic tool this plan touches, a GitNexus-derived answer may (a) add tests or workspaces to a selection, (b) reorder execution, or (c) emit a warning or lead. It may never remove a test from selection, skip a check, mark a check passed, or narrow a workspace that would otherwise widen to its full suite. A stale, empty, erroring or ambiguous graph answer resolves to the existing route, silently. P-007 and P-011 refuse only on MISSING evidence (or on graph evidence that a quarantined test DOES reach changed code, with an override); graph evidence alone never turns anything green.\n\nWhy: the index is hourly and committed-only on a constantly changing shared tree; cypher edge reads flap between full rows, [] and binder errors against one index (EI-24827431110263906); and a false green freezes main for the whole fleet. Under this rule the worst case of a wrong graph answer is wasted work or a spurious warning, never a broken main. It extends rules already in force: P-008's superset-only selector and file-level-test-selection D-003 (every rail fails toward running MORE tests).\n\n### D-003 — (Proposed, awaiting Avi) Embed graph answers in tools; judge by outcomes, never by call volume\nDate: 2026-10-05\nDate: 2026-10-05\nSource: [self-imposed] proposal by su-72f78fbb from the 2026-10-05 conversation with Avi (directives #1344, #1348); NOT owner-ratified.\n\nRuling: adoption is pursued by putting graph answers inside tools agents already run (test selection and ordering, completion and quarantine checks, failure attribution, the strands detector, one edit-time line), not by exhorting or forcing agents to call gitnexus.* directly. If they don't move, P-012 scales GitNexus back (hourly reindex, ~8 GB index, ~2.4 GB bench RSS).\n\nWhy: measured 2026-10-05, the existing Bash advisory coexists with ~3k definition-shaped greps per week while organic graph use is a few dozen calls a month, so encouragement alone has not changed behaviour; call volume is easy to inflate and says nothing about prevented failures.\n\n### D-004 — Licence finding: GitNexus is PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 — compatible with the open-source cut as designed, but internal commercial use is unresolved\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-05\nSource: measured by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376); owner asked \"read our open source plan, will it compatible?\" (owner-dialog answer, 2026-10-05).\n\nMeasured: `npm view gitnexus@1.6.9 license` = PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 (repo github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus). The vendored copy lives at ~/.papercusp/vendor/gitnexus; the bridge runs `npx gitnexus mcp`.\n\nopen-source-release-2026-09-29 (awaiting-acceptance): product licence is Elastic License 2.0 [owner:Avi D-003]; its D-006 [self, under owner AUTO #962] already removes libs/papercusp/plugins/gitnexus-bridge from the public cut and installer builds because a commercial ELv2 product must not download and run GitNexus on a user's machine; R-10 enforces it. Keep it that way: nothing in this plan may add a GitNexus dependency to a shipped surface or a lockfile.\n2. Internal use: NOT settled. PolyForm Noncommercial permits noncommercial purposes (personal use, noncommercial organisations); a for-profit company using it to build a commercial product is likely outside that grant. Not legal advice. In the frozen 2026-07-26 sample, 12 of 24 atoms are '-A N' body reads. lsp:query workspace_symbols returns locations, not bodies. Retargeting the whole pair to LSP therefore leaves 12 atoms, below MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE 20, so the narrowed pair cannot be certified on that sample. D-009's S37c/W01c baseline shows agents using the graph for plain definition lookups.\n\nRuling:\n(a) Location-only definition greps (no -A/-B/-C context) route to lsp:query { op:'workspace_symbols', name }, per code-intelligence D-001 [owner: Avi 2026-08-21].\n(b) Body-reading greps (-A/-B/-C N) are not claimed by that pair. D-001 sends definitions to LSP, not the graph, so they do not stay on gitnexus.context. Guidance may name the two-step lsp:query then capability:read { offset, limit }. The generated table only lists single-tool pairs, so this sub-population stays bash in the generated table until a faithful single-tool form exists.\n(c) Certification uses a fresh frozen sample re-extracted from the fires corpus, with at least 20 atoms and 5 sessions per pair, never the 2026-07-26 sample. If the fresh location-only population is still under 20, the pair stays observe-tier and is disclosed as uncertified rather than certified on a short sample.\n(d) The caller/absence pair routes to graph:query { op:'callers' } as P-002 states. gen:tool-routing regenerates the CLAUDE.md table, and gen:tool-routing:check must be green.\n\nRelated: P-002, P-015, D-009\n\n### D-011 — P-017 bake-off uses the fair-comparison test design; start now, raw answers only\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, directive #1437 + dialog answers to su-0113dc49] The Oct 1-2 engine comparison (5 cases, single run, unsupported intents and crashes scored as wrong, missing arms) is not sufficient to decide keep/switch/drop. P-017 is rebuilt to the fair-comparison design recorded on WI-10006297 (comment 2026-10-06T05:01Z): ~50 stratified cases incl. absence and hard cases; pooled, hand-adjudicated answer key with rescoring; capability-declared per-intent scoring with declined/crashed/timed-out/stale reported separately from wrong; precision/recall/F1 plus confident-false-empty rate; >=3 randomized repetitions on a quiet or CPU-pinned window; index health and freshness proven; arms rg, lsp:query, no-third-party (import index + TS call hierarchy), GitNexus 1.6.9 + latest, codebase-memory-mcp release build, CodeGraph (telemetry off), trace-mcp, CodeGraphContext, each admitted only after its LICENSE file is read; preregistered thresholds; Vitest tests beside the harness. Scope: raw query answers only (no end-to-end agent-task phase). Owner chose su-72f78fbb to build and run it, starting now: P-017 no longer waits on P-003; P-003 replay cases are added to the corpus when available.\n\n### D-012 — P-017 scores every intent on one fixed answer unit, with aliases for other granularities\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), implementing D-011's 'capability-declared per-intent scoring'.\n\nEngines answer the same question at different granularities. GitNexus names the calling function; LSP names the call line. Scoring raw lines would punish one granularity for not being the other. The corpus (packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/fair-comparison-corpus.ts, frozen at 90e6465ad21b) fixes one unit per intent:\n- callers: one unit per calling scope (function, method or module top level). The canonical site is the first line in that scope that calls the subject. Other call lines in the same scope, and the scope's declaration line, are adjudicated as aliases of it.\n- callees: one unit per first-party callee, canonical site = its declaration line. Calls into node built-ins and third-party packages are neutral.\n- impact: one unit per upstream scope within the case depth, canonical site = that scope's declaration line.\n- definition: the subject's declaration line. Overloads, and a .d.ts/.d.mts declaration of a JS implementation, are aliases.\n- references: one unit per referencing line (imports, re-exports, usages, type positions). The subject's own declaration is neutral.\n- symbol-search: the declaration line of every symbol whose name is exactly the subject.\n- text-search: one unit per line containing the literal.\n\nA neutral site is neither credited nor penalised (AnswerKey.neutral, added to fair-comparison.ts with tests). Every non-absence case carries at least one human-verified seed. A case with no seeds is an absence claim and must be tagged absence, so a key is never empty by omission.\n\nRelated: P-017, D-011\nRelated: P-017\n\n### D-013 — P-017 arm adapters pass raw answers on uniform inputs; two adjudication rules extend D-012\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), implementing D-011 ('raw answers only') after probing codegraph 1.6.2, trace-mcp 3.34.6 and CodeGraphContext 0.6.13 on the P-017 micro repo (packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/fair-comparison-micro-repo.ts).\n\nAdapter rules:\n1. Raw answers. An adapter passes the engine's answer through unfiltered. File-level nodes, import edges and self-references are scored, not dropped. The one exception is query construction that the question itself defines: symbol-search and definition keep results whose name equals the subject, because the question asks for exact names. A fuzzy engine is not scored on its fuzzy matches.\n2. Uniform inputs. Every arm gets the subject, plus anchorFile and depth when the case has them and the engine accepts them. With no anchorFile, an engine that finds several same-name definitions is scored on everything it returns (the union). Result limits are raised so no engine truncates silently. A truncated answer is flagged in its detail.\n3. Line resolution from the engine's own data is allowed. trace-mcp's impact report names symbol ids without lines, so its adapter resolves each one with trace-mcp's own get_symbol.\n4. Isolation. Each third-party arm indexes its own hardlinked copy of the frozen snapshot, with an isolated HOME and the admission record's telemetry-off env, so one engine's index files never leak into another's input.\n5. Conformance gate. Before an arm's real-corpus run, its adapter must pass the micro repo (runConformance in fair-comparison-arms.ts). No case may crash. Every plain (untagged) case the arm declares must be correct, or partial with precision 1. A partial answer with precision 1 means every site the engine named is right and some units are missing: the engine answers at a coarser granularity than the key's unit (for example one site per referencing function instead of one per referencing line). That is a property the real-corpus run measures as lost recall, not an adapter defect. A partial answer with any wrong site, or a wrong or empty answer, fails the gate. Hard micro cases are measured, never gated.\n\nAdjudication rules, extending D-012:\n- impact: the subject's own declaration is neutral, as it already is for callers and references. Engines that list the changed symbol among the affected nodes are neither credited nor penalised for it.\n- references: the enclosing scope's declaration line is an alias of the first referencing line in that scope. trace-mcp's find_usages reports the referencing function, not the line. An engine that answers at scope granularity gets credit for one unit per scope and loses recall when a scope holds several references.\n- module scope: engines represent a file's top level as a node at line 1 (codegraph and trace-mcp module nodes, CGC Module nodes). A line-1 site in a callers or references answer is an alias of that file's first top-level answer line (the #top unit), unless line 1 is itself an answer line, in which case it is that line. When the file has no top-level answer for the case, a line-1 site is wrong. In the micro repo this is encoded as a:<case>#top markers on line 1 (report.ts:1 for micro-callers-add, main.ts:1 for micro-references-sort-rows); real-corpus adjudication applies the same rule.\n\nCost observation: CodeGraphContext took 95.5 s to index the 6-file micro repo (53 s of it serialization, KuzuDB backend). Its real-corpus index time is a measured outcome, and an index that exceeds the run's deadline is reported as timed-out, never as wrong.\nRelated: P-017, D-011, D-012\n\n### D-014 — P-017 conformance accepts reproduced engine faults with evidence; CodeGraphContext arm runs over MCP\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), extending D-013 rule 5 after running CodeGraphContext 0.6.13 on the micro repo.\n\n1. Accepted engine faults. A conformance defect that is reproduced by calling the engine directly, outside the adapter, may be recorded as an AcceptedEngineFault (fair-comparison-arms.ts): one case, one outcome, a required error pattern for a crash, and written evidence. runConformance reports it under acceptedFaults and does not block the arm; a different failure on the same case is still a defect, and an acceptance that stops occurring is reported as unused so it gets removed. The fault is still scored on the real corpus like any other answer (a crash counts as crashed, a miss as wrong).\n\n2. CodeGraphContext arm (createCgcArm, fair-comparison-engines.ts). It answers over its own MCP stdio server ('cgc mcp start'), which returns JSON in about 50-100 ms per call; the CLI prints rich tables and pays 7-8 s of Python start-up per call. Its default result caps (15-50) are raised through TOOL_RESULT_LIMITS in its environment. Intent map: callers -> find_callers (call line passed; D-012 aliases the rest), callees -> find_callees (callee declaration line), impact -> find_all_callers with the case depth, definition and symbol-search -> find_code exact-name hits, text-search -> find_code content matches. References is declined: CGC has no references query. cfg.home must be unique per tree, because CGC keeps one global graph per HOME.\n\n3. Measured on the micro repo (fresh index 183 s at load average 251): every plain declared case is correct except three accepted engine faults. (a) impact crashes on both cases: CGC's own find_all_callers Cypher fails on its default KuzuDB backend with 'Binder exception: Expression in WITH must be aliased'. (b) text-search 'grand total' returns nothing: CGC's content search is a single-token full-text index over function sources and docstrings, its own CLI 'cgc find content \"grand total\"' also finds nothing, and module-level text is not indexed. Conformance after acceptance: ok, no unused acceptances.\n\n4. Text-search adjudication, extending D-013's references rule: an engine that answers text-search with the enclosing scope (CGC content matches name the function) is adjudicated like a scope-granularity references answer. The scope's declaration line is an alias of the first matching line inside that scope, and a scope with no matching line is wrong.\nRelated: P-017\n\n### D-015 — P-017 GitNexus and codebase-memory get their own fair adapters; the 2026-10-02 CBM arm never resolved a caller\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), implementing D-011 and D-013 for the last two third-party arms.\n\n1. GitNexus and codebase-memory (CBM) are FairArms in fair-comparison-engines.ts (createGitnexusFairArm, createCbmFairArm), not fromEngineArm over the 2026-10-02 arms. Measured reasons: the 2026-10-02 GitNexus arm reads through the production facade, which caps every answer at 100 sites (MAX_SITES_PER_ANSWER), reduces impact to a count plus a risk grade, and receives only the subject. The 2026-10-02 CBM arm ran trace_path at CBM's default depth 3, so \"callers\" included callers of callers, with a 100-row / 3200-token budget, and search_code at 10 results x 8 matches. The EngineArm interface carries no anchorFile or depth. Each breaks D-013 rule 1 or 2. fromEngineArm remains for rg.\n2. Transport: both answer over their own MCP stdio server, like trace-mcp and CGC, so every graph engine's query latency is measured on a warm server. Indexing reuses production pieces: gitnexusAnalyzeInvocation (heap, stack and WAL pins) for GitNexus; the one-shot CBM index_repository with daemon RSS sampling for CBM.\n3. Same-name resolution: both look the subject up by exact name, narrow to anchorFile when a candidate lives there, otherwise query every candidate (the union). This is the rule trace-mcp's adapter already applies, now shared as narrowToAnchor.\n4. GitNexus: lines use the measured per-version base (1.6.9 is 0-based). Edge rows carry no line, so each node's line comes from GitNexus's own context lookup by uid (D-013 rule 3). A File node is the file's top level and scores as line 1 (D-013 module-scope rule). impact runs upstream with the case depth, includeTests true, limit 100000. Declared: callers, callees, impact, definition, symbol-search. GitNexus has no references query, and its query tool is concept search, so references and text-search are undeclared.\n5. CBM: callers and callees trace at depth 1, impact at the case depth, include_tests true, every cap at its engine maximum (CBM_LIMITS). Declared: callers, callees, impact, definition, symbol-search, text-search; references undeclared (no references tool).\n6. Adapter bug, also present in the 2026-10-02 harness: CBM's name_pattern regex has no non-capturing group. ^report$ matches; ^(?:report)$ matches nothing and reports no error (measured over MCP on the micro repo). The 2026-10-02 CBM arm resolved trace_path names with ^(?:a|b)$, so every CBM callers and callees answer in that comparison came back empty because of the adapter, not the engine. Fixed in both arms with a plain group (cbmNameAlternation); guarded in fair-comparison-engines.test.ts. Any conclusion about CBM callers or callees drawn from the 2026-10-02 run is void.\n7. Conformance on the micro repo (D-013 rule 5): GitNexus 1.6.9 ok=true and CBM (dev build) ok=true, neither with accepted faults. Every plain declared case is correct. Hard-case misses are measured, not gated: both miss micro-callers-by-label-dynamic (dynamic dispatch), and CBM is partial on micro-callers-add (F1 0.80).\nRelated: P-017, D-011, D-013, D-014\nRelated: P-017\n\n### D-016 — P-017 first-party arms: lsp-query through the production adapter, no-third-party through TypeScript's own LanguageService\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), implementing D-011's first-party arms after reading the lsp:query surface.\n\n1. lsp-query arm = the engine behind the lsp:query tool: lspWorkspaceSymbols + lspQuery('references') from lsp-adapter.ts, called in-process through an injected LspDoor (fair-comparison-lsp-door.ts), limit raised to 100000 (the facade caps at MAX_SITES_PER_ANSWER; D-013 rule 2). Intents: definition, references, symbol-search. lsp:query has no call-hierarchy op, so callers/callees/impact are undeclared (coverage, not accuracy). references finds the declaration by workspace symbol, puts the cursor on the name, then asks textDocument/references, the way an agent does. A symbol search covers ONE tsconfig project: the case's anchorFile picks it, else the tree root. Recall lost to that is a measured product property, not an adapter defect.\n2. Production change to support rule 1 of D-013: tsserver's workspace/symbol is fuzzy and the adapter dropped each hit's name, so exact-name filtering was impossible. SymbolSite gains an optional `name` (contracts.ts) and lspWorkspaceSymbols sets it. Optional, so no existing site strands.\n3. no-third-party arm = the vendored TypeScript (~/.papercusp/vendor/lsp, typescript 6.0.2, the same copy typescript-language-server runs) as one LanguageService over every source file in the tree (node_modules excluded; allowJs so .mjs callers count). callers/callees/impact use provideCallHierarchyIncoming/OutgoingCalls, the code tsserver runs for LSP call hierarchy; definition/symbol-search use navigate-to (exact name, default libs excluded); references uses findReferences. Not routed through typescript-language-server: the production adapter has no call-hierarchy intent, and adding one is a readiness and capability-matrix change the bench does not need. In-process also means the program is complete before any query, so no half-loaded-project window. Index cost = program build + checker creation; peak RSS is the process peak, so the CLI runs one arm per process.\n4. callees whose target is declared outside the tree (default-lib or package methods such as Array.map) are omitted with a count in the note. D-012 makes those neutral, and a neutral site carries no score, so omitting them is score-equivalent and spares adjudicating machine-specific lib paths.\n5. The rg baseline's intents are now code (RG_INTENTS, createRgFairArm in fair-comparison-arms.ts), not only a scratch script.\n\nEvidence: micro conformance ok=true for both on real engines (lsp-query warm-up 5.3 s via the production adapter; no-third-party program build 0.7 s), no accepted faults. Both miss the same hard cases: micro-definition-scale and micro-symbol-search-add are partial (tsserver navigate-to lists the barrel's export specifier) and no-third-party scores micro-callers-by-label-dynamic wrong (a function passed by reference is not a call). Tests: fair-comparison-first-party.test.ts 13/13 (no-third-party asserted on the real micro repo), fair-comparison-rg.integration.test.ts pass (test_run 20830489); lint:tsc clean over 11 files.\nRelated: P-017, D-011, D-012, D-013, D-015\n\n### D-017 — P-002(d): the caller pair ships measured needs-widening, held at observe, not certified\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), from measurements on WI-10006282. Amends D-010(d) and P-002's done-when for the caller pair only.\n\nMeasured:\n- Population: harness_shared.session_turn_parts, 30 days to 2026-10-06: 462 recursive greps whose quoted pattern is `IDENT(` (code-search.callers-lookup bashPattern), 131 sessions, 363 distinct identifiers. The handwritten CLAUDE.md row for callers stays, and its 'empty is not absence' caveat is now backed by the measured missed case.\n(d) P-002's done-when ('each pair passes the faithfulness replay') is met for the definition pair (equivalent, 24/24) and is replaced for the caller pair by: measured, recorded, held. Excluding it, counting it as a total failure, or additionally removing the two defective key seeds (below) all give the same answer. gitnexus misses the F1 tie window by about 0.001 (0.7956 vs 0.7964); the CFE bar (0.115 vs <= 0.097) is what separates it.\n\nHand adjudication: 61 undecided impact/symbol-search sites were ruled with 66 verdicts under the adjudicator's own scope model (D-012/D-013), each with an evidence note.\n\nDisclosed key defects: two preregistered seeds (acceptance-bar-amendment.ts:484 barKeyOf, compile-packages.ts:172 only) are local helpers, not upstream of their subjects. No arm reported either. The key was left as preregistered, and the sensitivity run without them gives the same decision.\n\nCosts: no-third-party indexes in 177 s with ~0 on-disk index, vs gitnexus 2,948 s and 8.0 GiB. It peaks at 13.9 GiB RSS and answers a cold query in a median 12 s (gitnexus 0.4 s), so it suits batch consumers; interactive use needs a warm language service.\n\nConsequences:\n(1) Any graph intent behind the P-004 seam uses the first-party arm. WI-10006543 widens graph:query callers on it.\n(2) This Decision does NOT retire gitnexus. P-001's suggestions still read the gitnexus-built snapshot (gen-graph-dependency-snapshot.mjs). Keep/narrow/scale-back stays P-012's measured Decision, with this as an input.\n(3) Re-sourcing P-001's snapshot from first-party edges is a filed follow-up, not in this plan's ship scope.\n\n### D-027 — Caller pair re-measured on the first-party backend: 39 of 40 names answer like grep; promotion waits for the deploy and a population re-scope (amends D-017(b), D-018(b))\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), from measurements on WI-10006543. Amends D-017(b) and D-018(b).\n\nMeasured (evidence: docs/evidence/gitnexus-callers-remeasure-2026-10-06.json; CALLERS_GRAPH_MEASUREMENT in bash-substitution/pairs/code-search.ts):\n- Backend: graph:query callers now dispatches to the first-party TypeScript call hierarchy (D-026), in a forked worker with a 60 s budget and a 3,072 MB heap. It was re-measured through the real handler (op callers, limit 500), in-process on the staging working tree at HEAD b7e4e4e4180b, on the 40 frozen sample identifiers.\n- Outcomes: 38 resolved, 1 no-callers (DBOSUnexpectedStepError: its one grep line is a comment), 1 error (fetch: 2,578 candidate files; the worker exhausted its heap and the tool returned that error). 0 missed. The GitNexus-era classes (ambiguous, file-only, not-found) do not occur: the backend unions every declaration and gives every site a line. joinSharedHarness, the old missed case, now answers with 11 sites.\n- Grep equivalence: library answer against ripgrep `(?<![\\w$])NAME\\s*\\(` over code files outside node_modules, each omitted grep line classified by AST. For all 39 names other than fetch (whose probe timed out), every omitted line was a declaration, comment, JSDoc or string, and the scoped program's sites equalled the full transitive closure's. Two names return one extra site grep cannot see, a call through an alias (buildCarryBrief at events/await/wake-executor.ts, sendMessage at agent-tools/fleet/place_batch.ts).\n- Replay of cover() over the frozen sample: covered goes from 11/40 to 14/40. Of the 26 remaining refusals, 25 are the D-017(a) envelope rule (a search root not anchored inside this repo: `packages`, `apps`, `libs`, `.`, `../../../..`); the 26th is fetch.\n\nRuling:\n(a) CALLERS_GRAPH_OUTCOMES is replaced by this measurement. The outcome type becomes resolved | no-callers | not-found | missed | error. no-callers and not-found count as covered, because grep's answer holds no call either. The pair stays needs-widening, as the replay derives.\n(b) The D-017(b) promotion conditions are restated. Settled: P-017 chose the backend (D-026), and the disambiguator and line resolution are no longer needed. Remaining, in order: (1) agent-tools/gitnexus/query.ts must be live on :3070. routing-table projects any equivalent pair into CLAUDE.md whether or not it is held, and agents call :3070, so certifying first would publish a row for a backend the deployed operator does not run. (2) The pair's population is re-scoped to repo-anchored roots in its bashPattern, as the definition pair's is (REQUIRE_PROJECT_ROOT), with a re-extracted sample and re-measured outcomes. (3) Names in thousands of files stay an error, so the re-scoped replay may still derive needs-widening. That result is recorded as measured, not engineered away.\n(c) WI-10006543 stays open, owns (b) and is blocked on the deploy of query.ts to :3070. The R-2 evidence bound to code-search.test.ts goes stale with this edit and is re-bound after the final post-deploy edit.\n(d) holdAtObserve cites D-027 and WI-10006543, and code-search.test.ts pins both.\n\nRejected alternative: re-scope and certify now. That would project a CLAUDE.md routing row for a backend :3070 does not serve, while main is frozen behind a held repair queue.\n\nRelated: P-002, P-017, D-017, D-018, D-026, WI-10006543\nRelated: P-002, P-017\n\n### D-028 — Caller pair re-scoped and derived equivalent (40/40); held at observe and withheld from routing until graph:query `paths` is deployed (amends D-027)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: [self-imposed] by su-72f78fbb under AUTO (owner directive #1376), from measurements on WI-10006543. Amends D-027.\n\nMeasured (evidence: docs/evidence/gitnexus-callers-remeasure-scoped-2026-10-06.json; CALLERS_GRAPH_MEASUREMENT / CALLERS_GRAPH_OUTCOMES in packages/operator-core/lib/bash-substitution/pairs/code-search.ts):\n- Instrument defect found and fixed: the ripgrep reference ran without --with-filename, and rg prints no path for a single-file operand, so those lines parsed as zero (a false zero). Now --with-filename, and any unparsed line is a hard error.\n- Real non-equivalence found on the first scoped pass: a quoted capitalised `Name(` with no word boundary is a partial-name search. `EventKey(`: 19 of 19 grep lines were other names. Such greps are now outside the population (PARTIAL_NAME_PATTERN / EXCLUDE_PARTIAL_NAME).\n- Population: greps whose EVERY root is anchored in this repo (EXCLUDE_UNANCHORED_ROOT); the tool searches exactly the grep's roots via `paths`. New outcome class `root-missing` (the sampled grep searched a nonexistent path; covered only on the recorded roots).\n- Fixture re-extracted: 192 atoms, 78 sessions; 40-item sample re-drawn. Re-measured 2026-10-06T21:09Z at HEAD 902eb5976a, real handler in-process on the staging tree: 39 resolved + 1 not-found = 40/40 covered, 0 missed, 0 error. A literal `NAME(` census over the same roots found no remaining partial-name search.\n\nRuling:\n(a) code-search.callers-lookup expectedVerdict = equivalent, but it stays at observe (holdAtObserve) AND out of the generated routing table (new optional pair field routingWithheld; routing-table.ts skips equivalent pairs that set it). Reason: the `paths` argument (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/gitnexus/query.ts) is live on staging but not in main or on :3070 (dev:pipeline_position 21:20Z: onStaging true, inMain false, deployed false, blockedOn gate). A routing row naming an argument the deployed tool rejects would mislead every agent.\n(b) After query.ts is live on :3070: lift holdAtObserve and routingWithheld together, run gen:tool-routing, update the CLAUDE.md 'who CALLS this symbol' row via its doc part, and re-bind R-2's caller bindings (26283/26286). Owned by WI-10006543.\n(c) Verification at 21:15-21:19Z: code-search, routing-table, equivalence, match and hook-guard-selection-parity suites pass (5/5 matched; code-search.test.ts uncommitted at the time); gen:tool-routing:check no drift; lint:behavioural-strands --base 781edde2d8 exit 0 (3 source files examined); lint:tsc --files clean over the 5 changed files.\n\nLesson: a word-bounded reference instrument cannot see what the agent's LITERAL grep printed. Compare against the literal command output too, not only the semantic reference.\n\n### D-029 — P-012 provisional KEEP: preserve the shipped snapshot integration; incremental outcome value remains unresolved\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: AUTO solo execution under owner directive #1376; D-008 authorizes a provisional ship-time Decision with an assigned fourteen-day follow-up.\n\nMeasured: docs/evidence/gitnexus-replay-baseline-2026-10-06.json declares its graph threshold unresolved and strand rate a lower bound. This is not a zero-incident census. Historical repair attribution independently supplies WI-6554700010008340, a desktop release-script change stranding three superproject guards. P-012's checkpoint preserves source and query references.\n\nFire98 historical admission replay: git show 94b7ad2a:scripts/affected-tests.mjs resolveAffected plus all 111 historical workspace manifests (including gitlink manifests; missing=[]), with graph explicitly unavailable, admits only @papercusp/desktop for both papercusp-desktop and papercusp-desktop/bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh. Current buildIndex/selectRelatedTests over the complete historical superproject source corpus yields full/no-changed-paths-in-scope for operator-core (7,950 tests) and apps/operator (1,139 tests), covering all three guards CONDITIONAL ON admission. This supersedes any inference of a static miss from the sparse three-test, repo-root probe. Repo-wide guard admission is separate and has not been fully reconstructed. The historical graph snapshot, actual complete changed-path set, executed-map state and selector child receipts are unavailable, so no deployed graph catch/miss is credited.\n\nShip-time evidence artifact: docs/evidence/gitnexus-outcome-remeasure-2026-10-12.json records each of the five required metric dimensions as measured or unavailable-with-reason and exact source references. Behaviour baseline is D-009 (0 of 6 scenarios, 0 of 18 runs); the correctly attributed post-change S37/W01 battery is in progress and its rate is still unavailable, never zero. Preserve these limitations until its receipts are read and the artifact is updated.\n\nComparison: one additional qualified cross-package lead is established; graph-added-workspace true-catch and never-mattered rates remain unknown, as do comparable time-to-first-red and warning-rate changes. Historical pipeline event groups are not incident counts. P-006/P-010 expansion was dropped by the baseline decisions; do not invent a behaviour-change benefit for unshipped integrations. D-026/D-028 retain their backend and caller-routing authority.\n\nRuling: provisionally KEEP the existing snapshot integration through the bounded fourteen-day follow-up. Preserve the first-party backend selection and existing observe hold. This is a conservative, reversible decision under missing outcome evidence, not a finding that third-party indexing pays its cost; no new rollout, retirement, reindex change or index deletion is authorized by this Decision. The separate first-party replacement benchmark is an input, not proof of operational catch credit. Final keep/narrow/scale-back is owned by WI-6554700010008509; adjust its due date to actual shipment+14 days if shipment is later than the provisional anchor. Its receipt already confirms self assignee. No call-count credit.\n\nP-012/P-018 and final shipment remain open until evidence is registered against the acceptance rubric, deployed caller proof is obtained, and P-018 satisfies its 48-hour continuity requirement. Earliest prospective continuity boundary is 2026-10-13T08:35Z. This Decision does not claim shipped or gate green.\nRelated: P-012, P-018\n\n### D-030 — Remaining items fold into the native code-intelligence plan; this plan closes\nDate: 2026-10-15\nDate: 2026-10-15\nSource: native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09#D-016 [owner:Avi 2026-10-15] [turn:35b33faa@2026-10-15T17:55:29.091Z] (owner directive #1925): decide GitNexus now and have one plan own the decision.\nP-012 (re-measure outcomes and keep/narrow/scale back GitNexus) and P-018 (final deployed verification of P-001) move into native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09#P-042. The executor su-72f78fbb has been inactive since about 2026-10-11 (sessionState recorded, no loop), so no live claim is displaced; WI-10006285 is closed as superseded with a pointer.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"mcp-proxy-success-telemetry-2026-10-05","title":"MCP proxy success telemetry and native carry evidence","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-05","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: MCP proxy success telemetry and native carry evidence\nslug: mcp-proxy-success-telemetry-2026-10-05\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-05\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001 is done. P-002 is done. Existing implementation and tests verified on 2026-10-15: canonical proxy.test.ts passed 381 tests at head fccb00a9b6. No source changes required. Staging operator a9a08d8758 contains the proxy implementation. P-003 is needs-human. Sole executor EI-24940162932433128 is needs-human on typed product-decision blocker owner:no-additional-agents:2026-10-15. Draft status retained; plans:start not called. Parent acceptance and shared client routing unchanged.\n\n**Next:** Avi resolves whether the fresh managed Claude-su verification child required by R-4 is allowed under the current no-additional-agents constraint, or supplies matching fresh native initialize/tools-list/process/carry evidence. Preserve the native acceptance contract.\n\n## Background\n\nThe parent plan mcp-host-availability-resilience-2026-06-22 remains awaiting-acceptance with its own terminal implementation items. Its existing MCP proxy work covers reconnect behavior; the separately tracked reconnect-herd effort is out of scope here. This follow-up is limited to positive initialize/tools-list evidence and one fresh managed carry handshake. It does not revise parent acceptance, repoint shared clients, or backfill historical traffic.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Successful initialize telemetry.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Record fresh successful native MCP initialize evidence through the existing proxy telemetry.\",\"constraints\":[\"Do not backfill historical sessions.\",\"Do not store raw request URLs, query strings, request bodies, response bodies, or error text.\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"EI-24940162932433128\",\"coord-send-fafea4f21875fb86c624355c6cda53a9bb68737985a005cd091d9aae27162e41\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each successful initialize emits one initialize_stage success record with the existing request trace, proxy process identity, listen port, resolved target, bounded stage timings, and a pseudonymous native-session identity carrying an explicit source/trust label.\",\"falsifier\":\"A successful initialize has no success record, creates duplicate success records, presents untrusted attribution as verified, or stores a raw URL, query, request, or response payload.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the canonical proxy unit file against a successful stub initialize and assert one success record, bounded timing/process fields, pseudonymous native-session attribution, an explicit trust label, and payload/query redaction.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Bounded tools/list success summary.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Expose which bounded set of MCP tools a fresh managed client discovered, together with the exact returned tool count.\",\"constraints\":[\"Do not record tool descriptions, schemas, arguments, request URLs, or other response payload.\",\"Keep only a fixed-size sample of names.\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"EI-24940162932433128\",\"coord-send-fafea4f21875fb86c624355c6cda53a9bb68737985a005cd091d9aae27162e41\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A successful tools/list response records the exact tool count and at most 64 sanitized names, each capped at 128 characters, in the existing proxy telemetry; no descriptions, input schemas, arguments, raw URL, or response body are recorded.\",\"falsifier\":\"The successful response has no count, the name sample exceeds either cap, the count differs from the decoded list, or non-name response data is persisted.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the canonical proxy unit file with tools/list fixtures below and above the caps; assert exact count, bounded sanitized names, and absence of descriptions/schemas/raw payload.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Privacy-safe attribution with unchanged streaming.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Add success observation without changing streamable-HTTP behavior or widening the existing telemetry privacy boundary.\",\"constraints\":[\"Observe the upstream stream with bounded memory.\",\"Telemetry failure must not affect forwarding.\",\"Never persist req.url or its query string.\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"EI-24940162932433128\",\"coord-send-fafea4f21875fb86c624355c6cda53a9bb68737985a005cd091d9aae27162e41\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Initialize and tools/list response bytes, ordering, headers, and streaming behavior reach the client unchanged; observer and logger failures cannot block or alter the response; attribution contains only bounded pseudonymous session data and an explicit trust label.\",\"falsifier\":\"The proxy buffers or changes response bytes/headers, changes streaming completion, blocks forwarding on telemetry failure, or records raw native-session query data.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Compare stub upstream response bytes and headers with client-visible bytes while forcing observer/logger failures; assert unchanged forwarding and redacted telemetry.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Fresh managed kickoff and carry evidence.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Capture one new managed Claude-su kickoff/carry handshake after the instrumented proxy is serving the staging operator.\",\"constraints\":[\"Use native session/process evidence.\",\"A ptool-only success does not satisfy this requirement.\",\"Do not backfill historical protocol payloads.\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"EI-24940162932433128\",\"WI-10005351\",\"coord-send-fafea4f21875fb86c624355c6cda53a9bb68737985a005cd091d9aae27162e41\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"One fresh managed child completes carry delivery with output seen and turn start verified, and its native initialize/tools-list success records correlate to the child through the pseudonymous native-session attribution and proxy process identity on staging-operator.\",\"falsifier\":\"Evidence comes only from ptool or a stub, predates the instrumented build, lacks a native-session/process correlation, or fails to verify carry output and turn start.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"evidenceRuntime\":\"staging-operator\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inspect the native managed-session transcript/process evidence and the matching proxy records from one fresh kickoff/carry run.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing JSONL record path in apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/proxy.ts. Preserve its current trace, proxy PID, listenPort, and resolved-target fields. Observe successful initialize and tools/list results through a bounded stream tap; do not add a second log, table, or telemetry service. Accept native_session only through the managed hook attribution path, validate and pseudonymize it, and include an explicit trust label. Never persist raw req.url/query, headers, initialize parameters, tool descriptions, schemas, arguments, or response bodies.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Instrumentation and regression controls\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend the existing MCP proxy record path with bounded successful initialize and tools/list summaries, trusted pseudonymous native-session attribution, and a stream-safe nonblocking observer. — note: Verified existing implementation; no new code required. Duplicate auto-created task closed; EI-24940162932433128 remains sole executor.\n- **P-002** `done` Add canonical proxy regression coverage for successful records, exact count/name caps, redaction, attribution trust, unchanged response streaming, and logger/observer failure. blocked-by: P-001 — note: Verified existing canonical proxy regression coverage for successful initialize/tools-list, caps/redaction, streaming and observer/logger failure.\n\n## Phase 2 — Native validation\n\n- **P-003** `needs-human` Run the focused canonical proxy tests and capture one fresh managed Claude-su kickoff/carry handshake against the instrumented staging operator; preserve matching native initialize/tools-list and process evidence, with no historical backfill or ptool-only substitute. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 — note: Exact owner-only blocker recorded on sole executor EI-24940162932433128: R-4 requires fresh managed Claude-su child kickoff/carry on staging, while current owner kickoff forbids additional agents. P-001/P-002 verified-existing; 381 canonical proxy tests pass.
