On an opted-in plan, work_items:complete refuses a successful close when a frozen file changed without a re… <!-- P-022 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012597 — Pilot on 2–3 full plans that Avi picks. Measure per item: frozen tests failing at the first completion attempt (unfinished work caught), re-freezes, extra agent time and cost, false blocks, and bugs … <!-- P-023 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012598 — Deviation transaction via plans:conformance (R-17). op propose-deviation / approve-deviation record Decisions with a fenced deviation block; an owner-sourced requirement needs a turn-provenance-verif… <!-- P-028 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012599 — Spec-discharging closure + directive evidence (R-16, R-18, R-19, R-20). work_items:complete requires completion.discharges/contributesTo for plan-linked work mapped to requirements, refuses non-green… <!-- P-029 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012600 — Independent conformance review (R-21). system:spec-conformance-review files one deduped conformance-review work-item per plan recording the excluded implementer set; closure by an implementer is refu… <!-- P-030 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012601 — Continuous sweep routine + retro-fit report + docs (R-22, R-23). system:spec-conformance-sweep recurring routine with a watermark table, plans:conformance op report census across active plans, the re… <!-- P-031 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience:** Avi and every agent that executes a plan.\n\n**Problem:** A plan's spec is prose promises, checked only at the end (grading, code-truth audit, ship). Between writing and shipping nothing ties each action back to the spec. When an agent meets something the spec did not anticipate (an unmeetable constraint, a new request, a tool that behaves differently), it silently follows its default behaviour. Today's guards are authored but not executable (requirement `check` = none), evaluated too late (ship time), scoped to plan items while work leaks in through side directives, and satisfied by artifacts rather than by the spec.\n\n**Outcome:** For every plan, (1) each requirement compiles to an executable check at activation; (2) checks run during execution and a failure raises a drift alarm that halts dependent work; (3) all work touching the plan's declared footprint is linked to a plan item or flagged; (4) an unmeetable requirement can only be handled by an explicit, approved deviation (spec amendment) before acting; (5) item/directive closure names the requirements it discharges and their checks must be green; (6) an independent periodic spec-vs-implementation review covers what cannot be mechanised.\n\n**Non-goals:** a new parallel review system; replacing ship-time grading (it stays as the final gate); per-agent branch isolation.\n\n**Reuse-first:** requirement `verification.check`, rubric checks + `plans:set-schedule {system:'rubric-rescore'}` + `watch:create rubric:criterion-regressed`, plan Decisions, work-item ↔ plan links, completion evidence, `work_items:set_blocker`. The change makes these mandatory and execution-time, enforced at existing chokepoints (plans:audit activation, work_items:complete, orders:disposition, admission/dispatch).\n\n**Relationship:** This plan now holds two parts. Part A (R-3, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10; P-001…P-024) is the Oct-5 spec-driven tooling work: converge loop, claim-time context pack, triad-noise fix, frozen-test pilot, spec-change propagation. Part B (R-11…R-23; P-025…P-031) is the spec-conformance loop absorbed on 2026-10-14 from spec-conformance-loop-2026-10-14 (Avi's \"Approve, merge drafts\" choice, see D-010 and D-011). Boundary: Part B owns the general check-at-close (R-18/R-19 closure guard) and execution-time drift alarms; Part A's frozen-test completion check (its P-022) and claim-time context pack (its P-020) build on those surfaces instead of adding parallel ones. Part B supersedes the deferred R-5 drift design.\n\n**Source turns (Part A):** see ## Context and each requirement's sourceRefs (Oct 5–6 sessions, owner directives #1400 and #1414).\n\n**Source turns (Part B):** owner directive #1849 (take over, why drift, prevent recurrence) and #1855 (\"im looking for a general solution that solves this universally\"). Trigger case: slack-asana-reproduced-bug-fix-pr-workflow-2026-10-08#D-015; postmortem report rpt_020718f9-d6f4-42a8-b217-c7cfdfa408fc.\n\n**Scenarios:** A requirement authored with no check is refused at activation (or carries a loud `unenforced` flag Avi approved). A commit that violates a requirement's falsifier trips a drift alarm on the plan within minutes and blocks the affected items. A side directive that edits a plan's footprint without a plan link is flagged. An agent that cannot meet a requirement files a deviation and is refused if it tries to complete the item without an approved one. A directive cannot be closed `done` citing only a URL.\n\n## Context\n\n- **Origin.** Owner directives #1342 (\"What do you think of speckit … how would you integrate it?\"), #1345 (\"Do a thorough audit of all the spec tools like speckit, which features do you think we should integrate into papercusp? How?\") and #1351 (\"Write this into a plan\") — [owner:Avi 2026-10-05].\n- **Evidence base.** The audit report `docs/reports/spec-driven-tools-audit-2026-10-05.md` (WI-10006136) covers 16 tools and 2 research designs. External facts come from search summaries, because page fetches were refused all session (EI-25169560193283880).\n- **Owner revisions [owner:Avi 2026-10-06].** Every plan stays on the full track until proper benchmarking exists (D-004, session_turn:claude:2e9514ab-ed12-43c2-ada6-55dde2974fe9:32). Avi then asked for su-e3f60522's review recommendations to be folded in (D-005, D-006; session_turn:claude:2e9514ab-ed12-43c2-ada6-55dde2974fe9:36). The scope is now the friction-reducing items plus two additions: a pilot of tests the implementer cannot edit (from Consort) and a spec-change notification check (from Augment Intent). Sixteen items are deferred, among them all three gaps named under the review-time audit below (tracks, clarify, living specs). The plan is still a **draft**: Avi approved folding these in, not implementation.\n- **Everything except those owner rulings is an agent proposal ([self-imposed]).**\n- **What Papercusp already has** (so this plan does not rebuild it):\n  - Kiro's requirements / design / tasks triad inside plans (WI-36725, epoch 2026-08-09).\n  - `conventions:governing` (scoped standards, the equivalent of steering) and `plans:evaluate-spec-quality` (checklists).\n  - 5,246 revisioned clauses and 23,449 evidence bindings, re-measured when bound files move.\n  - Grading by a non-implementer outside the author's lineage.\n  - Fleets with claims, locks and `blocked-by` waves.\n- **What the review-time audit found** (WI-10002583; plan `review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23`, all items terminal): acceptance cost is dominated by rework. That plan fixed the *mechanics* of evidence and review. It did not change *how much* acceptance a plan owes, how clear intent is before BARs are written, or what happens to a spec after ship. Those three gaps are this plan's scope.\n- **Measured warning.** The triad adoption produced 680 reminder work items: 414 dropped, 147 open, 203 aimed at `acceptance-*` companion plans (EI-25176186379413042). Every new gate in this plan must be proportional and have a sticky exemption.\n\n## Requirements\n\nActive requirements: R-3, R-7, R-8, R-9 and R-10. store and its existing verbs (D-001). Every new gate starts advisory, with a sticky exemption, and is promoted to blocking only on a measured low false-alarm rate (D-003). One bounded exception (D-006): inside opt-in frozen-test pilot plans, the frozen-test completion check blocks from the start, because an advisory freeze is the 'persuasion' mode that Consort's paper reports agents can ignore.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-020 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-021, P-022, P-023 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-024 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-025 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-026 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-026 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-026 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-027 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-029 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-028 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-029 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-029 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-029 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-030 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-031 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-031 | tree |\n\n### R-3 Converge\n- **Recipe first (reuse-first).**\n  - Compose `plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy`, the code-truth phase of `plans:audit`, and the non-passing list from `plans:certify-spec-clauses`.\n  - For each non-passing clause, call `work_items:create` with a link to `spec_id`@revision.\n  - Dedup key: plan, spec_id and revision.\n  - Severity: critical (falsifier observed), major (no evidence), minor (quality or lint), outdated (evidence fingerprint moved).\n- **Promotion.** Turn it into `plans:converge { slug, dryRun }` only after the recipe is reused.\n\n### R-7 Claim-time context pack\n- Extend what `plan-decisions-claim-port.ts` already returns on claim (plan decisions) with the linked clauses, `conventions:governing` for the item's paths, and capability clauses.\n- Bounded by the tool-result cap, with a pointer for the remainder.\n\n### R-8 Triad noise\n- Fix inside `spec-triad-policy.ts` / `spec-triad-sweep.ts` / `spec-triad-filing.ts`:\n  - a reasoned drop writes a sticky suppression, or `specTriad: exempt`;\n  - companion `acceptance-*` plans are exempt by construction.\n- Then close the existing exempt reminders.\n\n### R-9 Frozen tests (pilot)\n- **Opt-in.** Plan frontmatter `frozenTests: pilot`. Only the 2–3 plans Avi picks at P-023.\n- **Who writes the tests.** An agent other than the implementer, routed like independent grading (outside the implementer's lineage). Precedent: the harness V2 tester already writes one black-box test per VAL.\n- **When.** After the item's requirement and falsifier exist, before implementation. Each test must fail against the current code first (red first), which proves it tests something.\n- **Freeze.** The test files' paths and content hashes are recorded on the item when the test author binds them, reusing the spec-evidence binding fingerprints. P-021 also decides whether the file-lock hook should refuse implementer edits to frozen files outright.\n- **Completion.** On a pilot plan, `work_items:complete` refuses a successful close if a frozen file changed without a re-freeze, or if no passing recorded run of the frozen tests exists for the current tree. The implementer may add tests of its own.\n- **Re-freeze.** If a frozen test is wrong, the implementer flags it; the test author amends it and records a `plans:add-decision` naming the item, then the new hash is frozen. P-023 counts re-freezes.\n- **Source.** Consort (Databricks, arXiv 2609.09671): spec and test list frozen at a hashed gate for a unit of work, changed only by a human replan.\n\n### R-10 Spec-change propagation\n- **Check first.** P-024 tests whether amending a clause already notifies holders of linked in-flight items, through the BAR amendment path or clause supersession.\n- **If missing.** On a new clause revision, find in-flight items linked to that clause through `work_item_spec_revision_edges` and send their live holders a `coord:send` naming the clause and both revisions. Items without a live holder get a comment. Deduplicate per (clause, revision, holder).\n\n### R-11–R-23 Spec-conformance loop (Part B, absorbed)\n\nOne module, `packages/operator-core/lib/spec-conformance/`, extends existing surfaces instead of adding a parallel system:\n\n- **Contract.** A plan declares its execution-time contract in a `## Conformance` section holding one fenced `conformance` JSON block: an optional `footprint` (repo-relative path globs) and, per requirement key, `violatedWhen` falsifiers and an optional `unenforced` declaration. The done-when check stays the requirement block's existing `verification.check`. Falsifiers live outside the BAR hash, so adding one never forces a rubric amendment.\n- **Falsifier checks** reuse `rubricCriterionCheckSchema` (`probe`, `instrument`, `tests`). A falsifier whose interface does not exist yet is authored as `pendingBinding { observation, bindWhen }`, which counts as enforced-pending and is listed as unbound by the report, never silently `none`. A check asserts the requirement holds; a `fail` verdict is the falsifier firing.\n- **Activation gate (R-11).** `plans:audit { phase:'activation' }` refuses `conformance_requirement_unenforced` when a requirement has no executable done-when check (absent or `instrumentKey:'none'`), no falsifier and no `unenforced { reason, approvalRef }`.\n- **Conformance run (R-12–R-14).** Evaluates probe/instrument falsifiers through the rubric-rescore machinery, judges `tests` falsifiers from the test-run ledger, re-scores the acceptance rubric's done-when checks, and records every verdict in the results ledger under `conformance:<harness>/<plan>`. A firing falsifier or a done-when pass→fail opens one deduplicated drift-alarm work-item per requirement (identity in `payload.specConformance`), links it `blocks` to every non-terminal work-item mapped to that requirement through the Bar-to-work map, and emits `plan:drift-alarm:<slug>`. An alarm whose checks return green is closed, releasing the blocks. An approved deviation suppresses the alarm for its requirement.\n- **Footprint (R-15).** The sweep reads commits since the plan's watermark that touch footprint globs. A path is covered when a work-item linked to the plan names it in completion `filesChanged` or holds its file lock. Uncovered paths are recorded on one open out-of-plan finding work-item per plan, assigned to the plan driver.\n- **Deviation (R-17).** `plans:conformance { op:'propose-deviation' }` records a Decision carrying a fenced `deviation` block. `op:'approve-deviation'` records the approving Decision. An owner-sourced requirement (owner refs in `intent.sourceRefs`) needs an `ownerTurnRef` that the turn-provenance ledger verifies as an owner turn.\n- **Closure (R-16, R-18, R-19, R-21).** `work_items:complete` for a work-item whose plan item maps to requirements must carry `completion.discharges` and/or `completion.contributesTo` (R-N keys among its mapped requirements). Each discharged requirement's executable done-when check must last have passed. An open drift alarm on a mapped requirement refuses closure without an approved deviation. A conformance-review work-item cannot be closed by a plan implementer.\n- **Directive evidence (R-20).** `orders:disposition { status:'done' }` refuses a note that is only URLs.\n- **Independent review (R-21).** `system:spec-conformance-review` (plan-schedulable) files one conformance-review work-item per plan, recording the implementer set it excludes.\n- **Continuity (R-22, R-23).** `system:spec-conformance-sweep` runs on a recurring routine across active/ready plans with requirements. It runs a plan when its footprint changed, a linked work-item transitioned, or its interval elapsed, and stores the watermark in `harness_shared.spec_conformance_state`. `plans:conformance { op:'report' }` is the retro-fit census.\n\n### Deferred designs (not in active scope; kept for reference)\n\nThese were designed in the original draft and deferred by D-004 (tracks, until benchmarking) and D-005 (the rest, until evidence shows they are needed). They stay here so a later plan can pick them up without redoing the design.\n\n#### R-1 Proportional tracks (deferred)\n- **Field.** `track: quick|standard|full` in plan frontmatter, beside `specTriad:` and the plan class.\n- **Default.** `plans:new` computes a proposal from:\n  - item count;\n  - blast radius: workspaces from `scripts/affected-tests.mjs --print-affected` over declared paths, plus `gitnexus.impact` on named symbols;\n  - plan class;\n  - the dangerous set (auth/security, migrations, outward publish/send, dark flags), which forces `full`.\n- **Overrides.** Changing the track requires `plans:add-decision` with a reason. Going below `full` on a dangerous-surface plan needs an `[owner:…]` tag.\n- **Proposed obligation table** (subject to Q1 / P-007; independent grading is kept on every track):\n\n| Obligation | quick | standard | full |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Triad (Requirements/Design/items) | exempt | required | required |\n| Clarify record (R-2) | exempt | advisory | required |\n| Acceptance criteria | 1–3 | 3–5 | 3–7 |\n| Rubric vetting via consult | skip | skip; the grader critiques instead | required |\n| `mutation_required` on clauses | off | per-clause opt-in | default on |\n| Design-phase evidence (UI) | if UI | if UI | required for UI |\n| Owner UAT walkthrough (GSD verify-work) | no | no | yes, generated checklist |\n| Independent non-implementer grade | yes | yes | yes |\n\n- **Wiring.** `plan-acceptance-gate.ts` and the `plans:audit` refusal builder read the track row instead of a uniform list. Refusal codes keep naming their own repair.\n\n#### R-2 Clarify phase (deferred)\n- **Verb.** `plans:audit { phase:'clarify' }`. This reuses the audit verb and the activation audit's existing re-read of the source conversation; it does not add a new verb.\n- **Inputs.** `## Requirements`, plan Decisions, and `conventions:governing({ about })`.\n- **Taxonomy.** Spec Kit's categories (scope, data model, UX, non-functional requirements, integrations, edge cases, trade-offs, terminology, completion signal), plus Papercusp categories:\n  - evidence plane (tree / staging / deployed);\n  - flag default;\n  - migration and rollback;\n  - multi-machine behaviour;\n  - who grades it.\n- **Output.** A short ranked question list, each question with a recommended answer and the BAR it would change.\n- **Ask mode.** One batched AskUserQuestion, or `coord:ask-owner` when headless.\n- **Assume mode** (subject to Q2 / P-004). Record the recommended answers as `[inferred]` Decisions and list them in `## Now` and the completion.\n- **Skipping.** A plan may record `clarify: skipped (<reason>)`.\n\n#### R-4 Living capability specs (deferred)\n- **Check first.** `harness_shared.project_spec_revisions` exists with 0 rows; P-011 decides whether to reuse it or drop it.\n- **Data.**\n  - Add `capability_slug` and an owner to clauses.\n  - Add `delta_op` and a base-revision pin on `plan_spec_clause_revisions`, reusing `supersedes_spec_id` / `supersedes_revision` / `content_hash`.\n  - The migration number comes from the allocator (`scripts/next-migration.mjs`).\n- **Merge at ship.** It runs inside the existing `plans:set-plan-status → shipped` transaction:\n  - it refuses a stale-base modified (OpenSpec's archive-safety lesson);\n  - a removed delta requires a reason and a migration note;\n  - live bindings carry over.\n- **Read.** `capabilities:get { slug }` plus a plan-viewer page: a `@papercusp/sync` query, with the selection held in nuqs.\n- **Bootstrapping.** Seed only the pilot capabilities (Q3 / P-012) from shipped plans' accepted clauses. No bulk backfill of the 5,246 clauses.\n\n#### R-5 Drift (deferred)\n\n**Superseded 2026-10-14:** Part B (R-11–R-23, P-025–P-031) is this plan's drift design; see D-011.\n- **Mechanism.** Extend the existing evidence re-measurement (bound `sourcePaths` / `testPaths` with hashes) to capability clauses after ship.\n- **Output.** A stale clause raises or updates one deduplicated work item per capability, owned by the capability owner.\n- **Advisory only.** A promotion to blocking at the green-checkpoint needs its own Decision, made after the P-018 pilot.\n\n#### R-6 EARS-shaped clauses (deferred)\n- Optional JSON fields on the clause revision.\n- The lint lives in `evaluate-spec-quality.ts`.\n- Invariant clauses (`behavior_class`) get a property-test suggestion targeting the existing `counterexample` evidence kind.\n\n## Conformance\n\n```conformance\n{\"footprint\":{\"paths\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/spec-conformance/**\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/conformance.ts\"]},\"requirements\":{\"R-20\":{\"violatedWhen\":[{\"id\":\"url-only-done-disposition\",\"failureMode\":\"a directive closed done on a bare URL\",\"stage\":\"delivery\",\"pendingBinding\":{\"observation\":\"an owner directive disposed done after activation whose note is only URLs\",\"bindWhen\":\"P-029 lands the disposition evidence guard\"}}]}}}\n```\n\n## Phase 0 — Groundwork\n\n- **P-001** `done` Fix spec-triad reminder noise (EI-25176186379413042), R-8: a reasoned drop is sticky, `acceptance-*` companion plans are exempt by construction, and existing exempt reminders are closed with the exemption as evidence. Design kept under Design → Deferred designs.\n\n## Measurement\n\n- **Baseline (P-002).** Before any change, record per-plan acceptance wall-time, binding churn (retracted / created), BAR amendments and consult expiry for recent shipped plans. This also seeds the benchmarking Avi wants before any lighter track is enabled (D-004).\n- **Escape baseline (WI-10006249).** Code-changing closes are named by a bug within 14 days at 8.6–11.3% depending on item kind. Reading a sample, about 3% are real escapes, mostly unfinished work closed as done.\n- **Frozen-test pilot (P-023).** Per pilot item: frozen tests failing at the first completion attempt (unfinished work caught), re-freezes, extra agent time and cost, false blocks, and bug citations available at the review cutoff against the historical escape baseline. State the actual cutoff and comparison limits. D-019 removes the 14-day observation requirement: no minimum observation period blocks completion, acceptance or shipment.\n- **Triad noise (P-001).** Reminder items filed, dropped and open, before and after.\n\n## Out of scope / rejected\n\nThese are rejected as D-002:\n- adopting any tool wholesale;\n- a second spec directory in the repo;\n- per-agent git worktrees;\n- spec-as-source regeneration (Tessl);\n- simulated persona teams (BMAD);\n- tests frozen before the build as a fleet-wide default (piloted on opt-in plans instead, D-006);\n- approval dashboards;\n- a library usage-spec registry (Context7 covers it).\n\nDeferred, not rejected (D-004, D-005): proportional tracks, the clarify phase, living capability specs with drift detection, and EARS-shaped clauses.\n\nDeferred until a user asks: importing and exporting `.specify/` and `openspec/` folders in `harness:generate-from-repo` (audit R8).\n\n## Risks\n\n- **A frozen test encodes a misread requirement.** A wrong test blocks a correct implementation. Mitigation: the test author, not the implementer, amends it through a recorded re-freeze Decision, and P-023 counts re-freezes.\n- **The pilot adds cost per item.** A second agent writes tests before implementation. Mitigation: opt-in on 2–3 plans; P-023 weighs the cost against the escapes caught before any wider use.\n- **Implementer and test author share context or lineage.** Mitigation: route the test author like an independent grader, outside the implementer's lineage (P-021).\n- **Converge refiles noise.** Gap items could repeat the triad-reminder problem. Mitigation: P-003 runs after P-001's suppression fix, deduplicates per clause revision, and stays a recipe until it is reused.\n- **Notifications become chatter.** Mitigation: one notification per clause, revision and holder (P-024).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Integrate inside the plan store; adopt no external spec tool wholesale\nDate: 2026-10-05\nProposed by su-18b69883 [self-imposed], not yet owner-ratified. Every feature borrowed from Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Kiro, BMAD, GSD, Tessl and the others is built as structure in Papercusp's plan store and existing verbs (plans:audit, plans:evaluate-spec-quality, clause and evidence tables). There is no .specify/ or openspec/ directory and no second spec store beside Postgres. Precedent: Kiro's triad was adopted inside plans (WI-36725). Source: audit WI-10006136.\n\n### D-002 — Rejected features: per-agent worktrees, spec-as-source, persona teams, pre-build frozen tests by default, approval dashboards, library-spec registry\nDate: 2026-10-05\nProposed by su-18b69883 [self-imposed], not yet owner-ratified.\n- Per-agent git worktrees: the shared staging tree plus locks is deliberate, and a feature was lost to a stray worktree on 2026-06-30.\n- Spec-as-source regeneration (Tessl): model-driven development's old problems plus non-determinism.\n- Simulated persona teams (BMAD): we already have real role blueprints and fleets.\n- Tests frozen before the build as the default (Consort): the rubric is written after implementation by design, and the harness tester already covers per-VAL black-box tests.\n- Approval dashboards: AskUserQuestion, review:approve and the Acceptance gate already exist.\n- Library usage-spec registry: Context7 covers it.\nImport/export of .specify/ and openspec/ is deferred until a user asks.\n\n### D-003 — Every new gate ships advisory first, with a sticky exemption; blocking only on measured accuracy\nDate: 2026-10-05\nProposed by su-18b69883 [self-imposed], not yet owner-ratified. Lesson from the triad adoption: 680 reminder items, 414 dropped, 203 aimed at acceptance-* companion plans (EI-25176186379413042). It freezes tests within a unit of work, separates writer/judge roles and treats real runner results as the green condition. The paper describes its comparative outcome evaluation as future work; this pilot makes no efficacy claim in advance.\n\nProtocol:\n1. A plan opts in with frontmatter frozenTests: pilot; no opt-in means this gate adds no completion obligation. Full-track obligations remain intact (D-004).\n2. Before implementation, an independent test author writes acceptance tests for each implementation item. Reuse grading's ancestor/descendant/rebind exclusion (acceptance-author-identity.ts); compare with the item's assigned implementer and recorded implementation history, fail closed on unreadable identity. The tester is a separately registered task/role, not the implementation item's claimant. Reuse the harness V2 tester/independent grading routing when assigning pilot authors; a child of the implementer is ineligible.\n3. Red-first calibration is a recorded assertion-failing run of those exact test bytes, before freeze/implementation; an infrastructure error, skipped suite, missing case evidence or opaque claim of failure is not red calibration. Tests must collect and demonstrate an unmet promised behavior.\n4. Extend work_items:update with a purpose-shaped frozenTests registration/refreeze argument. Store the protected _frozenTests manifest on the existing item payload, not a new table. Paths are normalized repository-relative files in the harness tree; reuse the spec-evidence repo-file measurement and measurementPin per-file SHA-256s. Record author, implementer identities, red-run references, timestamp and manifest revision. General payload writes cannot forge underscore fields.\n5. A successful work_items:complete on a pilot item requires a manifest, unchanged and present frozen tests, independent author lineage, and current server-measured passing test evidence from the existing test-run/spec-binding ledger covering every frozen file. No run, failure, skip, stale source or unreadable evidence refuses before completion/state writes. Drop/discard is not a success assertion.\n6. Re-freeze is only through the independent author after an explicit plans:add-decision naming the item, changed paths, reason and old/new manifest revisions. Preserve prior freeze evidence and require fresh calibration and passing proof; implementer identity/lineage cannot authorize its own replacement.\n7. This pilot enforces hashes at freeze and completion. Do not add a second file-lock policy: existing locks serialize physical edits, and hash enforcement catches edits/deletions regardless of editor/client. Implementer attempts cannot satisfy completion by editing the target.\n8. P-023 still waits for Avi's 2–3 chosen full plan slugs; measure via rubric checks/results ledger, including first-close catches, re-freezes, incremental time/cost, false blocks and 14-day escapes. No rollout or success claim before those observations.\n\nMeasured reuse: spec-evidence-store.ts exports measureAndPinRepoFilesEvidenceAtRoot and listSpecEvidence; evidence-measurement-pin.ts stores per-file SHA-256. work_items:update.ts already reserves all underscore payload keys. complete.ts accumulates gate refusals before any completion/state write. one snapshot, totals reconcile, unknown… <!-- P-022 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006233 — Whole-pipeline acceptance: the same defect from an agent, the watchdog and a desktop user folds into one candidate, is verified, becomes claimable, is fixed, the reporter is notified; a feature whose… <!-- P-023 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006234 — Leader-brief integration (carried from the census draft's P-004 per D-010): the complete breakdown and a compact, mechanically rendered explanation in the default fleet:leader-brief; metadata survive… <!-- P-024 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006235 — Adversarial verification (carried from the census draft's P-005 and R-5 per D-010): fixtures above 2,000 rows, simultaneous conflicting gates, missing or malformed readiness, and real current-build s… <!-- P-025 -->\n## Purpose\n\n\"Needs review\" and \"blocked\" do not mean what they say, so leaders cannot explain their queues and hundreds of items sit with nobody able to move them. Avi also wants end users to report bugs, unified with agent filing, and every bug verified before it can be worked. These are one problem: one intake, one verification stage, honest hold states. Fix the queue first, then build end-user reporting on the fixed pipeline.\n\n## Measured findings (2026-10-05, dated observations, not live counts)\n\nBugs (all open papercusp bugs, 21:27Z):\n- 449 open bugs (237 readiness `corroborated-tool-failure-awaiting-review`, 212 `deployment-freshness-unknown`) have no review record; all are promoted automatic tool-failure reports; 303 untouched 3+ days; 4 held. Only 15 bugs are in real peer review. `promotedProbationReadiness()` (capture-core.ts) and the triage freshness branch (triage-core.ts) stamp `unknown` without enrolling a review; `agentReviewNormalExclusionSql()` (agent-review-policy.ts) excludes them from ordinary claims while the reviewer lane admits only `agentReview.status='pending'`. No lane can pick them up and every report calls them \"review\". Filed EI-25176539351759672.\n- About 300 bugs blocked: 208 typed `live-dependency` with no next action, 61 with no typed blocker, about half older than 7 days, almost none held. Capture parks agent-filed changes/features in `blocked` while awaiting review.\n- About 126 needs-human bugs; per WI-10006089, 17 boolean-only and 19 without a complete owner question.\n\nFeatures (non-P2P approximated by title filter, not the fleet's exact claim spec, ~21:50Z):\n- Fleet nonp2p-feature-drain-sol61-xhigh-0930 had zero workers (headcount `target: null` under an inherited no-top-up rule) while its leader recorded quiet wakes; Avi overrode it (that plan's D-006), restoration pending at last read.\n- 218 blocked features. 154 blocked by an open dependency (`harness_shared.work_item_is_blocked`). Traced to chain roots: 29 unstarted, unheld roots gate 99 of them, and 23 of those roots carry no gate, so the real cause is that nobody is working them. 10 held roots gate 17; 4 needs-Avi roots gate 10; 2 finished roots with completion still `proposed` gate 7.\n- About 64 blocked features have no blocking dependency now: 18 with finished dependencies still carrying a mirrored `gate:live-dependency` label, 13 with only that label, 6 with no reason, about 10 with product-decision/credential holds that may be real.\n- Four overlapping \"review\" mechanisms: agentReview, implementationReadiness stamps, admission/dedup review (fail-open), and the candidate acceptance stage of observation-candidate-acceptance-promotion-2026-09-30 (built, not enforced: cutover constant `2100-01-01`).\n\n## Relationship to su-4a152 and the earlier drafts\n\nPer D-010 (Avi, #1364, \"combine them\") this plan supersedes both earlier drafts; the mapping below records where each of their items and decisions went.\n\nFormer R-2 (hosted relay) now lives as R-2 of built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 per D-014; hosting and cost are decided in D-013. Source: [owner:Avi 2026-10-05, owner-dialog answer in that session] Apps whose users do not run Papercusp send reports through a hosted relay; builders set up nothing.\n\n- su-4a152 (live) authored end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 and is implementing owner-ratified D-023 (bug accepted only with a reproduction receipt on the current build) in WI-10006152, plus D-024 (agent-encountered bugs with attached encounter evidence are born verified). It holds WI-10005016 (enforcement cutover, blocked on the release gate). This plan builds on that work and does not re-implement it.\n- fleet-queue-census-and-gate-routing-2026-10-05 (bug-drain leader su-f96cf8e8): its R-1..R-5 become P-022; its dropped P-002/P-003 become P-002.\n- end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05: its P-001..P-004 become P-010..P-013, P-005..P-008 become P-014..P-017, P-009..P-012 become P-018..P-021; D-001..D-003 carried; D-004/D-005 replaced by D-023/D-024 there and D-004/D-007 here.\n- Builds on shipped silent-intake-central-resolution-2026-09-01 (frictionless filing, duplicate candidates fed to the resolver); P-011 extends that intake rather than adding one.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Core end-user bug reporting, unified with agent filing.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Let people report bugs and unify those reports with agent bug filing (desktop-app reporters here; built-app reporters in built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 per D-014).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:e2ef1e52-d591-4b1f-9636-fbf4093924e8:0\",\"session_turn:claude:e2ef1e52-d591-4b1f-9636-fbf4093924e8:4\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A report from the desktop Report a problem entry and an agent-filed report of the same defect land as one bug work item through one shared intake, with reporter provenance and captured context, and the reporter sees the fixed-in-version status.\",\"falsifier\":\"A desktop report creates a separate record type or bypasses the shared intake, or the reporter never learns the outcome.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"shared intake\",\"desktop report entry\",\"reporter status thread\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Drive the shared intake with agent and desktop-report sources and assert one work item with provenance; drive the desktop entry headlessly and read the status thread.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/improvements/capture.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/capture-core.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/capture-core-promotion-claimability.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Verified before claimable.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Human and agent bugs are not claimable until verified real on the current build, inside bulk review; agent-encountered bugs count as verified.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:e2ef1e52-d591-4b1f-9636-fbf4093924e8:9\",\"session_turn:claude:e2ef1e52-d591-4b1f-9636-fbf4093924e8:14\",\"session_turn:claude:e2ef1e52-d591-4b1f-9636-fbf4093924e8:17\",\"session_turn:claude:e2ef1e52-d591-4b1f-9636-fbf4093924e8:18\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"No bug is claimable for implementation until the verification stage records a reproduction receipt on the current build or an encounter receipt (D-024, D-011); agent-filed changes and features pass proposal review in the same stage; verification work is claimable by verifier agents.\",\"falsifier\":\"An unverified bug appears as claimable for implementation, or a verified item never becomes claimable.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"claim floor\",\"verification stage\",\"verifier lane\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Seed verified and unverified bugs, changes and features; compare work_items:claimable and the verifier lane against the expected sets.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review-policy.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/capture-core-promotion-claimability.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/claim-floor-classification.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Honest, clearable holds.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Explain and fix why so many items need review or are blocked; no item sits in a hold nobody can clear.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:38a36e93-66f9-4e9a-b870-315f43d48403:0\",\"session_turn:claude:38a36e93-66f9-4e9a-b870-315f43d48403:8\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every non-terminal hold maps to a registered clearer and re-check time; writing an unmapped hold is refused; the stranded promoted tool-failure bugs are verified, retired with evidence (D-012) or routed; zero open items are held with no clearer.\",\"falsifier\":\"An open item sits in a hold reason absent from the registry, or a readiness stamp remains that no lane can claim.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"hold registry\",\"capture promotion\",\"triage freshness\",\"stranded-bug cleanup\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Enumerate every hold-reason producer and assert registry coverage; run capture and triage on promoted tool-failure fixtures and assert each lands in a claimable lane.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/capture-core.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review-policy.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/improvements/triage.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/agent-review-policy.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — A brief that adds up.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Fix the stats the bug-drain leader is confused by; add a queue breakdown to the fleet brief.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:38a36e93-66f9-4e9a-b870-315f43d48403:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"One default fleet:leader-brief call returns a breakdown computed over the complete eligible population (primary partitions, causes, staffing, chain roots) that sums to the total, agrees with the scheduler claimability oracle and survives result shaping; unknown or partial counts are labelled, never shown as zero.\",\"falsifier\":\"Breakdown counts do not sum to the total, are computed after display limits, disagree with the scheduler, or render unknown as zero.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"fleet census\",\"leader brief\",\"result shaping\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the brief over fixtures above 2,000 rows with conflicting gates and malformed readiness; reconcile every count and id.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/leader-brief.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/leader-brief-aggregate.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/fleet-metrics-contract.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Blocked means really blocked, and fleets stay staffed.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Check whether blocked items are blocked by real things, fix what the feature-drain discussion uncovered, and keep fleets staffed.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:38a36e93-66f9-4e9a-b870-315f43d48403:11\",\"session_turn:codex:01a10dd0-c3ba-71b2-8f7f-cb66453cb40e:27\",\"session_turn:codex:01a10dd0-c3ba-71b2-8f7f-cb66453cb40e:30\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Blocked state is computed from current blockers and dependencies so items return to the queue when those clear; every blocker names its target, next action and re-check date; a fleet below its headcount target raises an alarm and a leader cannot record a quiet wake with zero workers.\",\"falsifier\":\"An item with finished dependencies and no live blocker stays blocked, or a fleet runs at zero workers without an alarm.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"blocked computation\",\"blocker contract\",\"headcount governor\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Finish a dependency and assert the dependant returns to the queue without manual action; run the headcount census with target above live workers and assert the alarm.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet_registry/headcount-target.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/blocking-impact.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/goal-headcount-census.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — One unified plan.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"One plan covering all the queue improvements plus a unified bug-report integration; combine the drafts (Phase 5 split out per D-014).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:38a36e93-66f9-4e9a-b870-315f43d48403:8\",\"session_turn:claude:a6e09da3-b93b-4981-998a-17011b188b7a:5\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The same defect reported by an agent, the watchdog and a desktop user folds into one candidate, is verified, becomes claimable, is fixed, and the reporter is notified, with no manual step.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any source takes a separate path, or the journey needs a manual step to progress.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"end-to-end pipeline\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the whole-pipeline integration journey (P-023) on a current-build instance.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/capture-core-promotion-claimability.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n1. **One front door.** Agents, the watchdog and people file through one intake: redact, classify (bug, idea or note; notes go to memory), fold duplicates, attach or create a candidate.\n2. **One verification stage.** Bugs need a reproduction receipt (D-023); an agent that hit the failure attaches it at filing and is born verified (D-024). Changes and features get a proposal review in the same stage. Verification is claimable work for verifier agents, batched through bulk review.\n3. **Every hold names its clearer.** A hold must name who or what clears it and when it is re-checked; holds with no clearer are refused.\n4. **Blocked is computed, never sticky.** Derived from live dependencies and typed blockers; items return to the queue when they clear.\n5. **Honest report.** Five numbers that add up (ready, being verified, in progress, waiting on a named thing, needs Avi), plus stuck-with-no-clearer (target 0), staffing, and the chain roots holding the most work.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-010, P-011, P-014, P-015, P-016, P-017 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-012, P-026, P-029, P-031 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-008, P-011, P-027, P-028 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-022, P-024, P-025, P-030, P-032 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004, P-005, P-007, P-022, P-026, P-030, P-031 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-023, P-033 | tree |\n\nPhase 7 is a proposed queue-flow extension for Avi review (D-058..D-061). The added contributors reuse these existing acceptance bars; test/operational evidence must bind to their own scoped behavior before implementation closure. Updating this map does not approve execution or fleet resources.\n\n## Phase 1: every hold has a clearer\n\n- **P-001** `done` Hold registry and invariant: one code registry mapping every hold reason (readiness reasons, blocker kinds and capabilities, review states, park reasons, needs-human) to its clearer (lane, routine or owner) and a re-check cadence; writes of an unmapped hold are refused; needs-Avi requires a delivered answerable owner question; tests enumerate every writer. — note: ← WI-10006215 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Fix the producers behind EI-25176539351759672: promoted tool-failure and freshness-unknown bugs stop getting a stamp nobody clears; report before/after counts. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10006217 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Live blocked state: derive blocked from live dependencies and typed blockers and return items to the queue when both clear; changes and features get their proposal review (today's agentReview semantics) inside the same candidate stage, so there is one stage, not two. — note: ← WI-10006220 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Verifier lane: verification work is claimable by verifier agents (never the reporter or implementer), fleets can staff it, bulk review batches it; The ~450 stranded bugs exist because two holds had no clearer.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-004\n\n### D-006 — Blocked is computed, never sticky\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[proposed by su-93aaa593 from the #1354 findings, not ratified] Measured: 18 features had finished dependencies but stayed blocked behind a mirrored generic label; 6 had no reason at all.\nRelated: P-004, P-023\n\n### D-007 — Corroboration orders verification, never replaces it\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[consistent with owner-ratified D-023 point 3] Many reporters raise an item's place in the verification queue; they never certify it.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-008 — Staffing is a first-class queue signal\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[proposed by su-93aaa593 from the #1354 findings, not ratified] The feature fleet ran with zero workers while its leader recorded quiet wakes; live workers vs target belongs in every brief and an inherited no-top-up rule cannot silently disable staffing.\nRelated: P-005, P-022\n\n### D-009 — Reuse, no parallel systems\nDate: 2026-10-05\n[proposed by su-93aaa593, not ratified] Extend capture, the shipped silent-intake path, triage, the candidate stage, the headcount governor, fleet-metrics and leader-brief; the only possible new record is a per-report child row, and only if the corroboration record cannot hold it.\nRelated: P-001, P-006, P-010, P-022\n\n### D-010 — Combine the two earlier drafts into this plan\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05 #1364, \"combine them\"] This plan supersedes end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 (su-4a152) and fleet-queue-census-and-gate-routing-2026-10-05 (bug-drain leader su-f96cf8e8); both are set to superseded with a pointer here. Lane intent [decided by su-93aaa593 under the #1364 delegation]: su-4a152 is offered Phases 2-4 because it owns the D-023/D-024 verification work and authored the end-user draft; the final assignment is part of the execution route.\nRelated: P-002, P-010, P-022, P-024, P-025\n\n### D-011 — Watchdog failures with a captured failing call are born verified\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[decided by su-93aaa593 under owner delegation #1364, \"do the rest as you think best\"; extends owner-ratified D-024] A watchdog report that attaches the failing tool_invocations row (or an equivalent ledger record) from the current build counts as reproduced, exactly like an agent's encounter receipt under D-024. A watchdog alert without such a record (a threshold breach, a timeout with no invocation, an inference) enters verification like any other report. Why: the attached record is direct evidence of the failure, not a claim about it.\nRelated: P-002, P-006, P-011\n\n### D-012 — Bulk retirement of stale tool-failure reports\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[decided by su-93aaa593 under the #1364 delegation] P-003 may retire a promoted tool-failure report in bulk only when both hold: the tool's code or schema changed after the report's build, and no matching failing invocation of that tool has been recorded since the change. Each retirement records the report's build, the current build and the last matching failure time on the item. A later matching failure reopens or refiles it through the normal duplicate path. Reports whose tool did not change go to verification, not retirement. Why: these reports describe code that no longer exists, and retirement is evidenced and reversible.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-013 — End-user reporter defaults: anonymous, consented attachments, bounded retention\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[decided by su-93aaa593 under the #1364 delegation; open question carried from end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05] Reports are anonymous by default; contact details are attached only if the reporter opts in. The status thread (P-016) is delivered back to the reporter's install, so it needs no contact details. Screenshots and logs are attached only when the reporter ticks them in the preview (P-014) and are redacted on the device before sending. Attachments are deleted 90 days after the item closes; the report text stays with the item. For the follow-up plan (D-014): Papercusp hosts and pays for the relay, consistent with Avi's R-2 (builders set up nothing), with per-app quotas and rate limits bounding cost; template apps keep user-meaningful UI state in the URL (the repo's nuqs convention) so a report captures the screen. Why: the smallest data footprint that still lets a fix be verified.\nRelated: P-013, P-014, P-016\n\n### D-014 — Split Phase 5 into its own plan\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[decided by su-93aaa593 under the #1364 delegation; Avi saw this recommendation before delegating] P-018..P-021 (reporting for apps built with Papercusp: hosted relay, papercusp-feedback template aspect, builder view, end-to-end test) move to draft plan built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05, which starts after this plan ships. The builder-app half of R-1, and R-2, move with them; this plan delivers the shared pipeline plus reporting from the Papercusp desktop app. This amends R-7 (one plan, #1353). Why: Phase 5 depends on Phases 1-4 and on new hosted infrastructure, and keeping it here would hold this plan's ship on that infrastructure.\nRelated: P-018, P-019, P-020, P-021, P-023\n\n### D-015 — Reuse the selected-evidence producer contracts (carried from the census draft)\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[carried from fleet-queue-census-and-gate-routing-2026-10-05 D-001, authored by the bug-drain leader; lifecycle wording corrected 2026-10-06 per su-f96cf8e8] The leader-brief breakdown reuses the producer contracts owned by EI-24958944483532851 (selected-set completeness, including links/get); no parallel receipt or completeness implementation. (2) P-001's \"one code registry\" is built by EXTENDING the enumeration the scheduler already reads (candidates: packages/operator-core/lib/claim-floor-classification.ts, scheduler/get-next.ts, work-items-durable-park-audit.ts; pick the one get-next consumes), with claimable.ts, claim-hold-guard.ts and complete consuming it, not by adding a parallel registry module. (3) P-002 fixes the missing agentReview enrolment in capture-core.ts and checks the two sibling promotion paths that also stamp readiness, attention/intake-promotion.ts and work-items-admission-promoter.ts, for the same defect before closing.\n\n### D-019 — P-006 design: the acceptance seal is the one verification stage; its check is chosen by kind\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-4a152 2026-10-06, implementing P-006 under D-004/D-016] sealImplementationAcceptance (agent-review-policy.ts) is already the only constructor of a qualifying contract, and both acceptance writers call it: bulk-review promotion (intake-promotion.ts) and agent-review approval (agent-review.ts approvalAcceptance). Before this change only the bulk-review writer enforced the D-023 bug receipt, so an agent-review approval could accept a bug with no reproduction. P-006 moves the kind-specific check into the seal and into its readers (evaluateImplementationAcceptance and the SQL twin implementationAcceptanceStateFromReadinessSql): kind=bug needs a reproduction receipt (the WI-10006152 BugReproductionReceipt, either supplied by the reviewer or the D-024/D-011 encounter receipt stored at filing), recorded on the contract as verification {check:'reproduction', receipt}. kind=change/feature/task needs proposal review, meaning agent-review authority from a reviewer other than the submitter. A policy authority cannot accept them. A contract that fails its kind check reads 'incomplete' (missing 'verification'), so the item stays a candidate. Nothing changes for claimability before the WI-10005016 cutover, because the legacy branch of the floor still admits 'incomplete'. After the cutover the floor holds such an item. P-007 (verifier lane) and P-008 (retire overlapping gates) build on this seal; they do not add a second check.\nRelated: P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-020 — Correction to D-018: the filing seam DID have a concurrent owner; P-002 builds on it\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-93aaa593; correction reported by su-5ae61f36 (consult reviewer 3/3, coord 01:06Z)] D-018 point (1) said no other module owns this work. That was wrong. su-4a152da3's WI-10006152 (P-013 of observation-candidate-acceptance-promotion-2026-09-30, D-023/D-024) edited the same filing seam: capture.ts, capture-core.ts and attention/intake-promotion.ts, adding the bug reproduction receipt (attention/bug-reproduction.ts). It closed 2026-10-05 ~22:34Z, before P-002 started, so there was no live edit collision. P-002 reuses that receipt instead of a parallel one: a promoted tool failure whose filing carries a born-verified receipt (readBornVerifiedReproduction) is stamped ready, and the invocation-friction path builds a tool_invocations:<id> receipt through verifyBugReproductionReceipt (D-011). D-018 (2) and (3) stand. The other open lane is su-4a152's WI-10005016 (enforcement cutover); P-009 still waits on it.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-009\n\n### D-021 — P-007 design: one verifier-conflict rule at every verification door; built in three phases\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-4a152 2026-10-06, implementing P-007 under D-004/D-016/D-019]\nMeasured in the current tree. The agent-review lane already is the verification lane: claimAgentReview, claimNextAgentReview and mintAgentReviewClaimAdmission refuse only `own-submission` (agentReview.submittedBy). Nothing excludes the reporter (payload._ei.created_by, often a different id from submittedBy, e.g. 'improvement-triage') or the implementer. Bulk-review promotion seals {reviewer: decidedBy, submittedBy: source.createdBy}, so it excludes the reporter but not the implementer. `investigate` already promotes to a ready task carrying an `investigation` record (intake-promotion.ts). Dependency satisfaction (work-items.ts depsBlocked SQL) counts any done blocker whatever its completion authority. The work-items.ts note on alreadyTerminallyCompletedExclusionSql (a proposed close stays owned by its closer, never re-queued) covers the claimable pool only, so verifying a proposed completion does not contradict it.\nDesign:\n(1) ONE pure predicate verificationConflict(subject, verifier) -> null | {role:'reporter'|'implementer'} plus its SQL twin, beside the seal in agent-review-policy.ts. Reporters: _ei.created_by, agentReview.submittedBy, the stored reproduction filedBy, verification.reporters. Implementers: terminal_owner and verification.implementers. A subject's prior implementation claimants are captured from its worked_by_history when a verification task is created, never read from the task's own history, so a reviewer of an earlier round is not excluded.\n(2) Applied at every verification door: claimAgentReview, claimNextAgentReview (SQL selector and JS re-check), admission mint/match plus agentReviewPendingAdmissionSql, and the bulk-review promote (implementer check alongside the seal's reporter check). New refusal reasons: 'reporter-conflict', 'implementer-conflict'.\n(3) A verification task is a work item carrying payload.verification {schemaVersion, subject, check: reproduction|proposal-review|completion, reporters[], implementers[]}. `investigate` stamps it on the task it already spawns (the bounded repro task, bounded by its exitCheck, owner and re-check date). The shared claim writer refuses a conflicting claimant on any row that carries the block, so work_items:claim and scheduler:get_next cannot bypass the rule.\nPhases: A = (1)-(3) with SPEC-P-007 / SPEC-P-007-B evidence. B = fleets staff it: scheduler:get_next serves verification work (agentReview pending plus verification tasks) to verifier claimants. C = a proposed completion of an item with live dependents spawns a completion verification task (implementers = [terminal_owner]); dependents count the blocker as satisfied only once that task accepts it. P-007 closes only when A, B and C are done.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009\n\n### D-022 — P-003 design: the stranded tool-failure sweep is a bounded watchdog pass beside the signature fold\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-93aaa593, implementing P-003 under D-011/D-012/D-016]\nThe sweep is NOT a one-off script. It is the fleet-steering surface members already pull from, set by the leader with scheduler:set_claim_spec and inherited fleet-wide, so a leader staffs a verifier fleet with one spec write. The spec's view filter does not narrow review work in this phase.\n(4) get_next marks the served item `lane:'verification'` and names the next call (improvements:agent-review decide for a review; the task's check for a verification task).\nWhy not a fallback on implementation-pool miss: a fleet scoped to one plan would start reviewing out-of-scope work; staffing must be the leader's explicit choice.\nRelated: P-007\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-028 — P-007 Phase C design: a completion verification task gates dependents through the dependency graph and is admitted by one scoped policy\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed, su-4a152 2026-10-06, implementing P-007 Phase C under D-021/D-023/D-027]\nMeasured in the current tree before building: (a) dependency satisfaction is computed in four places (unsatisfiedBlockerSql in work-items.ts, work_item_is_blocked() plus the work_item_blocked sidecar triggers for the feature family, readUnresolvedDepBlockers warnings, and get-next's floors), so changing what counts as a satisfied blocker means changing all four; (b) P-006 makes a change/feature/task contract qualify ONLY through agent-review authority (acceptanceVerificationFor, sealImplementationAcceptance), and the SQL claim floor work_item_claim_floors (migration 1368) carries the same rule; (c) a terminal close lands completionAuthority 'proposed' in work_items:complete (complete.ts, stampedAuthority) and settlement can later upgrade it.\nDesign:\n(1) Trigger. When work_items:complete lands a terminal close with completionAuthority 'proposed' on an item that has at least one LIVE dependent (a non-terminal row it blocks through a 'blocks' edge), it creates a completion verification task. Idempotent per subject: an open completion task for the same subject is reused and only missing edges are added. No dependents, no task.\n(2) Task row. kind 'task', payload.verification = createVerificationTask({ subject, check:'completion', reporters:[], implementers:[terminal_owner] }) plus payload.completionVerification { subject, closer, proposedAt }.\n(3) The gate is dependency EDGES, not a satisfaction rewrite. The task is added through mutateWorkItemDependencies as a 'blocks' blocker (satisfaction 'success') of every live dependent. Every existing reader (claim floors, the feature sidecar, the blocker warnings, cycle admission) then holds the dependents until the task is done, with no change to what 'satisfied' means.\n(4) Claimability. A synthetic agent-review reviewer would be the weak acceptance substitute R-24 forbids. Instead add ONE allowlisted immediate policy, 'completion-verification', valid ONLY on a row whose verification block has check 'completion' (the proposal to verify is fully determined by the subject's own recorded completion; no reviewer judgment is being replaced). TS: seal, acceptanceVerificationFor and its SQL twin. SQL: a migration re-rendering work_item_claim_floors, the 1368 pattern.\n(5) Verdict door. work_items:complete on a row carrying a 'completion' verification block REQUIRES completion.verificationVerdict 'accept' | 'reject' (reject requires a reason) and refuses a close without one. Accept: the task closes done, its edges are satisfied, dependents proceed. Reject: the task closes done with the verdict recorded, and the subject is reopened to its closer (non-terminal, taken_by = terminal_owner, terminal stamps cleared, a comment carrying the reason); the subject's own edges then hold the dependents again. The verifier can never be the closer (implementers = [terminal_owner], D-021 rule at every door).\n(6) Settlement. When settlement upgrades the subject from 'proposed' to a qualifying authority while its completion task is still open, the task is closed as accepted by settlement (system actor), so no verifier spends a turn on a completion whose evidence already qualifies.\nP-007 closes when Phases A, B and C carry bound evidence.\nRelated: P-007, D-021, D-027\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-029 — P-001 correction to D-026: the canonical writer already guards needs-human; the gap is answerability and a bottom-writer bypass\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-93aaa593 2026-10-06, implementing P-001 under D-026]\nRETRACTION. Repairs named: fleet:headcount-target { target, supervise:true }, fleet:launch-on-plan, or fleet:wind-down. Unknown headcount fails open with a warning (unknown is not zero). The engine's no-checkpoint quiet settle is left as is; (6) re-renders on every wake.\nNot done: no change to the R5 opt-in default; no auto-grant of supervise to never-granted fleets.\nAs built (7), 2026-10-06 06:30Z [self-imposed, su-93aaa593]: lib/fleet/fleet-zero-workers-guard.ts holds the pure decideFleetZeroWorkers and checkFleetZeroWorkers (injectable deps). One intake = captureImprovement. No parallel intake function. New stages go into it; new doors are thin wrappers that call it.\n2. Redact: every filing's title and body pass the shared redactSensitiveText at entry; payload.intakeRedaction = { fields, at } records what changed.\n3. Error-signature fold: for a keyless improvement-lane bug, the most recent error in its report context (explicit, or auto-captured from a tool failure) is normalized (case, ids, numbers, paths, wrapper prefixes) and, when specific enough, becomes an INFERRED watchdogKey 'error-signature:<hash>'. That reuses the indexed exact-key lookup and the unique open-identity index, so two concurrent reports cannot mint two candidates. Tool is the error's source when it names a tool; a prior with a different known tool is not folded (the new report files without the inferred key). An inferred-key coalesce keeps the first report's title and body (D-042 precedent); later reports add reporterKinds, repeatCount and an occurrence. The error-signature source is not in the auto-close allowlist, so such rows are never auto-resolved as a watchdog condition.\n4. Classify: agents classify by choosing kind (their notes already go to memory:remember). The in-app door (end-user-intake.ts) classifies the person's text as bug, idea or note; an ambiguous report is a bug, so nothing is lost. A note is stored in memory as quoted, untrusted end-user text (P-013 hardens quoting); bug and idea call captureImprovement with reporterKind 'end-user' and the report context. P-014 adds the UI and transport that call this door; P-015 the upstream path.\n5. improvements:capture accepts reportContext so an agent can attach the error it saw and fold with a person's report of the same error.\n6. Expire: the P-003 sweep gains a candidate pass: an open, admission-pending automatic report (reporter watchdog, or no end-user among its reporter kinds and a structured tool failure) with no accepted receipt is retired with D-012 evidence when retirementFact says the tool changed and no matching failure followed. Person reports never expire this way.\nRelated: P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014, P-003\n\n### D-047 — P-013 design: the one intake quotes end-user text as evidence after redaction; every end-user door gets it by passing reporterKind 'end-user'\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed design ruling, su-4a152 under D-016 (Phases 2-4) and AUTO; implements D-003; not owner-ratified]\n1. Seat. captureImprovement (capture-core.ts) applies quoteEndUserIntake right after redactIntakeText, before any identity, dedup or storage step. Trigger: input.reporterKind === 'end-user', which only an end-user door can set (D-044 pt 2). Agent and watchdog filings are unchanged. A door does NOT quote for itself: the Slack door (slack-messages-to-bug-reports-2026-10-05), P-014's UI transport and P-015's upstream path only pass reporterKind 'end-user', and the intake quotes.\n2. Form (packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/untrusted-evidence.ts, version end-user-evidence-v1). Body = a fixed header line, a blank line, then the text as a Markdown blockquote with EVERY line prefixed '>'. A whole-line prefix leaves no closing delimiter to forge. Title = one line in typographic quotes. dedupSignature strips punctuation, so title dedup is unchanged. Both pass neutralizeToolCallTags. Idempotent: isQuotedEndUserText accepts only an exact known header followed by all-quoted lines, so a person who types the header and then unquoted lines gets re-wrapped. payload.untrustedInput = { quoting, fields } records what was wrapped.\n3. Notes. The in-app door's memory note uses the same form under END_USER_NOTE_HEADER, after redaction. It replaces the earlier plain \"...\" quoting.\n4. Order. Redaction first (D-046 pt 2), then quoting. Neither the intake nor the door logs report text. The test asserts no console channel receives a pasted token.\n5. Out of scope. reportContext is app-captured structured data, already redacted per field (D-044 pt 5) and not typed by the person, so it is not blockquoted. If P-014 lets a person edit context fields, those fields must be added to the quoting set.\nTests: capture-core-untrusted-input.test.ts (SPEC-P-013 and SPEC-P-013-B through the real captureImprovement), end-user-intake.test.ts (note form).\nRelated: P-013, P-014, P-015\n\n### D-048 — P-014 design: in-webview Report a problem dialog; the preview IS the payload, bound by a digest the server re-checks; one door-neutral consented-attachment store with 90-day post-close deletion\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed design ruling, su-4a152 under D-016 and AUTO; implements D-013 and D-046 pt 4; not owner-ratified]\nMeasured: the desktop GUI has no native menubar (papercusp-desktop main.rs builds only the Server tray menu), so the app's menu is the command palette. No attachment table exists, and no DOM-capture library is installed. sensitive-text.ts has no imports, so it runs in the browser.\n1. Entry points: a palette command report.problem (section Help) and a shortcut report.problem, default mod+shift+b, in shortcut-registry.ts with command:'report.problem'. Open state lives in the URL (?report=1, nuqs), so agents can open it with ui:dispatch.\n2. Dialog (ReportProblemDialog, mounted at the router root beside GlobalSearchDialog): one single-line field 'What went wrong?' (one sentence, capped at 280 characters). Step 2 is Review. It shows the exact payload, including automatic context: app version, screen (route path and search), and up to 5 recent client errors from a new client error ring. It also shows opt-in ticks, default off: 'Attach recent log lines'. Anonymous: no contact details are sent, because P-016 delivers status to the install.\n3. The preview is the payload. A pure, browser-safe problem-report.ts builds the payload from the input, redacting on the device with redactSensitiveText. The Review step renders that object, and Send posts that same object. canonicalJson plus SHA-256 (WebCrypto, available in both browser and Node) yields previewDigest, sent with the payload. POST /api/desktop/report-problem parses with a strict zod schema (unknown keys refused), recomputes the digest and refuses 409 on mismatch. Content the preview did not show therefore cannot be sent. The route then calls intakeEndUserReport (the one intake, D-046 pt 1) with reporterKind end-user, so P-013 quoting and redaction apply again server-side.\n4. One consented-attachment store for every door (desktop now, Slack P-005 next): harness_shared.report_attachments(id, workspace_id, work_item_id, door, kind log|text|screenshot|file, external_id, mime, byte_size, content bytea, redaction redacted|not-redactable, created_at). Unique (door, external_id) gives idempotency. Caps: 2 MB per attachment, 5 per item. Text kinds are re-redacted at write. Images are stored marked not-redactable. Deletion: a sweep deletes attachments whose item is terminal and whose state_changed_at is more than 90 days ago. The report text stays on the item. It is an extension of an existing sweep, not a new scheduler.\n5. Screenshot capture is out of P-014 v1, because nothing in the tree can capture the webview. The store accepts screenshots now (for Slack). The desktop capture is filed and owned as a follow-up.\n6. Response: { routed: work-item|memory, id }. The dialog shows the id; P-016 adds the status thread.\nRelated: P-014, P-013, P-016, P-017, D-013, D-046, D-047, slack-messages-to-bug-reports-2026-10-05 P-005\n\n### D-049 — P-012 design: corroboration count = distinct reporters in the occurrence ledger; it orders the verifier lane and is shown on work_items:get; it is never read by the acceptance seal or the claim floor\nDate: 2026-10-07\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed design ruling, su-4a152 under D-016 and AUTO; implements P-012 and D-044 pt 6; not owner-ratified]\nMeasured 2026-10-07 00:20Z (papercusp-workspace, 7 days): harness_shared.work_item_occurrences already records one row per filing with its reporter. Distinct reporters per item: 36,353 items have 1, 1,211 have 2, and the tail reaches 676. Filings per item reach 2,943 (one chatty source inflates volume, not independence). canonical_harness_slug equals the item's harness_slug on 23,067 of 23,068 joined rows.\n1. The count. Corroboration = COUNT(DISTINCT btrim(reporter)) over the item's occurrence rows (non-empty reporters only), keyed by (workspace_id, canonical_harness_slug, canonical_work_item_id) so the existing canonical index serves it. Filings = rows of kind canonical-created, coalesced, duplicate or regression ('promoted' records an admission step, not a new report). reporterKinds comes from payload.reporterKinds (D-044 pt 4). No new column, table or migration: the ledger is the record.\n2. Ordering. claimNextAgentReview orders by feature_order (an authored order stays first), then corroboration DESC, then created_ts. claimNextVerificationTask orders by the corroboration of payload.verification.subject DESC, then created_ts. Owner-curated bulk-review runs keep the owner's own order.\n3. Shown on the item. work_items:get returns corroboration { reporters, filings, reporterKinds, firstFiledAt, lastFiledAt, note } per result. The note states that it orders verification and is not a receipt.\n4. Never a substitute. Known limit: a promoted intake item's count covers only its own ledger rows, not its source candidate's. Following payload.intakeSource.id is a follow-up, not done here.\nRelated: P-012, P-010, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-050 — P-015 reuse direction: installed reports use canonical joined-Pot issue federation, not generic cross-Pot work requests\nDate: 2026-10-07\nMeasured: 2026-10-07 source reads of harness/bootstrap-papercusp-hive.ts, harness/papercusp-hive-join.ts, platform/contribute.ts, pot/contribute-upstream.ts, cross-hive-boundary.ts and sync/hyperbee/projections/engineer-issues.ts; current engineering docs pot-scoped-federation.
