Next repair: Accept the mapped clause: plans:get-specs, then plans:set-specs with lifecycleStatus:\"active\", expectedRevision set to its current revision, and every other field unchanged (keep the sourceBar pin and acceptanceRef; omitting either rides the prior value forward). That provenance-only promotion carries the bound proof and work-item contracts forward: confirm the result reports evidenceCarriedForward > 0 on a clause that had proof. If it is absent, another field changed and the proof must be re-bound at the new revision. Do NOT re-prove or amend the rubric on this code: the proof is not stale, the clause was never accepted. (R-4). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nPlan STARTED 2026-10-06 06:38Z (on :3170 — :3070 d740fc3802 mis-grades sourceBar AUTO-BAR atomicity). Spec quality passed (card EI-25210206665587700, audited). 8 items promoted: P-001=WI-10006480 (DONE: design = Decisions D-003..D-011), P-002..P-008 = WI-10006481..WI-10006487 (verify ids via plans:items). Consult conv-muwb2db3-0000-8aaeb1381d684cee91c533a623775c0e (fork of su-f926974d) open on D-003/D-004 unique-index+lease re-key and D-008 on-demand thumbnails.\n\n**Next:** Read consult reply (coord:thread / consult conversation) and amend D-004/D-008 if it finds a blocker; then P-002: migration via node scripts/next-migration.mjs (desktop_sessions.name + live-scope unique index incl COALESCE(name,'')), desktop-lease.ts re-key by desktopSessionId with pot/hosted wrappers, provision_desktop/release_desktop/list_desktops args per D-006, resolveAgentIdentity(ctx).ownerId for scope_ref; Vitest for keying, coalescing, release. Then P-003 targeting (computer.ts resolveBoundDisplay + ComputerCtx needs ownerId).\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10006480 — Design + decisions (record as plan Decisions): per-agent desktop identity (registry scope:'agent' keyed by ownerId + an agent-chosen name; migration needed?); re-key the in-process lease Map from pot… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006481 — Multi-desktop provisioning for any agent: extend computer:provision_desktop (or a sibling verb, per P-001) so a worker agent can start N agent-scoped desktops, each returning a desktopSessionId + nam… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006482 — Desktop targeting on every computer verb: capability:computer, computer:observe, computer:click_element, computer:record accept a desktop (id or name) and enforce the P-001 ownership rule; screenshot… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006483 — Headroom admission + lifecycle: refuse a new desktop when the machine lacks measured memory/CPU headroom (per-desktop footprint measured, not guessed), with a refusal naming the caller's idle desktop… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006484 — Thumbnails for every live desktop, cloud and local: the capture loop yields a fresh thumbnail (~5s) for every non-terminal desktop while at least one grid is open, and nothing when none is (zero idle… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006485 — The grid (cloud Desktops page): all desktops as tiles — thumbnail, owning agent, work-item, state, last activity; click → live viewer (watch / take over, existing tickets + audit); pin up to 2 tiles … <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006486 — Local parity: the same grid component serves the local app (\"This computer\" beside cloud workspaces on the Desktops page) — local desktops get thumbnails, owner/work-item labels, pinning, live view. … <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006487 — End-to-end verification: real hosted VM (two agents, 5+ desktops, grid, refresh, live, take over, release, admission refusal) and the local app via verify-tauri-headless.sh with VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED… <!-- P-008 -->\n## Goal\n\nAgents on any workspace — a Papercusp-hosted cloud machine AND the local desktop app — can start as many sandboxed GUI desktops as they need (bounded only by the machine's measured headroom), choose which one each computer-use action drives, and the user can see ALL of them at once: a grid of thumbnails that refresh every few seconds, click a tile to open it live (watch / take over), optionally pin one or two tiles live.\n\nSource: owner directives #1448 and #1451 (Avi, 2026-10-06).\n\n## Relationship to earlier plans\n\nFollow-on to two SHIPPED plans (plans:new dedup flagged both; continuing them would reopen shipped work, so this is a new plan): `agent-virtual-desktops-2026-08-23` (DesktopSession registry, KasmVNC sandbox desktops, hosted relay viewer, freeze-first lifecycle, egress accounting) and `hive-frame-desktops-live-view-2026-06-06` (the local Swarm live view).\n\n## Current state (code-read 2026-10-06, su-16da39cf — not live-tested)\n\n- **One desktop per pot.** `computer:provision_desktop` (papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/computer/provision-desktop.ts) is idempotent per pot: `ensureHiveDesktop(potSlug)` keys the in-process lease Map by pot (desktop-lease.ts). Restricted to QUEEN_PLACEMENT_ROLES — a worker agent cannot provision.\n- **Hosted machine serves one shared desktop.** `HOSTED_WORKSPACE_DESKTOP_LEASE = 'hosted-workspace'` (workspace-host/hosted-workspace-host-runtime.ts, D-404): every `desktop.start` coalesces onto it.\n- **No desktop targeting.** `capability:computer` (computer.ts) has no desktop argument; it resolves the caller's pot lease via ctx.harnessSlug, then an env fallback.\n- **Registry already supports more.** `desktop_sessions` has scope pot|agent|workspace (parent D-005); `scope:'agent'` keyed by ownerId is used only by the deployed-frame allocator (deployment/display-allocator.ts).\n- **Cloud Desktops page** (papercusp/apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/DesktopWorkspacePage.tsx → HostedDesktopWorkspace.tsx, D-062): roster of every non-terminal desktop + thumbnails + ONE large live viewer. Thumbnails come from the capture loop (5s) over the relay (parent D-025); a display with no active capture has no thumbnail.\n- **Local Swarm live view** (papercusp/apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvFramesTab.tsx): one tile per deployed-frame display (SSE thumbnails) PLUS every local registry desktop (GET /api/deploy/local-desktops); local tiles have NO thumbnail and open live via noVNC (FrameVncView.tsx, x11vnc ticket route deploy/vnc-session.ts) for watch/takeover.\n- **Two separate grid UIs** (cloud Desktops page, local Swarm view) with different transports.\n- **No count/headroom admission** found for desktop provisioning.\n\n## Scope\n\nIn: per-agent multi-desktop provisioning, desktop targeting on every computer:* verb, headroom admission + per-desktop lifecycle, thumbnails for every desktop, ONE grid experience across cloud and local, built on the current cloud Desktops page; the old local Swarm live view is re-evaluated, not assumed reusable (D-002), end-to-end verification on a real hosted VM and the local app (headless Tauri, isolated DB).\n\nOut: Wayland (parent D-021), non-Linux hosts, all-tiles-live streaming (owner chose thumbnails), visible cloud fleet terminals (parent D-018).\n\n## Verification bar\n\n- Vitest for registry/lease/admission/targeting; tauri-agent-tools via scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh with VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1 for the local grid; a real hosted VM run for the cloud grid. Scenario both places: agent A starts ≥3 desktops, agent B ≥2, the grid shows all 5+, thumbnails refresh, click → live watch → take over, release frees it, admission refuses when headroom is exhausted.\n- design-phase.search_registry before building/merging the grid.\n- Graded acceptance rubric at ship (standard plan completion runbook).\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Any agent can start as many desktops as it needs.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"A worker agent (not only a pot leader) can start several sandboxed GUI desktops of its own, each with its own id and name, and release any one of them by id.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:0\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:13\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Agent A starts 3 agent-scoped desktops and agent B starts 2; each call returns a distinct desktopSessionId and display; computer:list_desktops lists all 5 with their owners; releasing one by id leaves the other 4 live; the pot-shared desktop and the hosted shared desktop still work.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A second provision returns the first desktop, two agents collide on one display, a worker agent is refused, release by id tears down the wrong desktop, or the pot/hosted shared desktop regresses.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"worker-role provisioning\",\n      \"multiple desktops per agent\",\n      \"two agents concurrently\",\n      \"release by id\",\n      \"pot-shared desktop unchanged\",\n      \"hosted shared desktop unchanged\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest suite provisions desktops through the real lease/registry code with a stubbed X server and asserts ids, displays, listing and release.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/computer/agent-desktops.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/desktop/agent-desktops.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Every computer action can name the desktop it drives.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"An agent with several desktops chooses which one each computer-use action (screenshot, click, type, observe, record) targets.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:0\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"capability:computer, computer:observe, computer:click_element and computer:record accept a desktop id or name and act on that display; omitting it keeps working for an agent with one desktop; an agent cannot drive another agent's private desktop.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An action lands on a different display than the one named, an omitted desktop breaks a single-desktop agent, or a foreign private desktop is drivable.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"explicit desktop by id\",\n      \"explicit desktop by name\",\n      \"omitted desktop default\",\n      \"ownership refusal\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest suite resolves desktops for each verb and asserts the DISPLAY the driver is invoked with plus the refusal.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/computer/desktop-targeting.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Desktops cannot exhaust the machine.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Unlimited desktops are bounded by what the machine can actually hold: a new desktop is refused when headroom is gone, idle ones are frozen, and an agent's desktops go away when the agent does.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:0\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:13\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Provisioning is refused with a structured error naming the caller's idle desktops when measured available memory minus the per-desktop footprint falls below the reserve; idle desktops follow the freeze-first lifecycle; desktops owned by an ended agent session are reaped.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A desktop starts with no headroom, the refusal gives no actionable detail, an idle desktop never freezes, or an ended agent leaves desktops running.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"admission refusal\",\n      \"admission allow\",\n      \"idle freeze\",\n      \"reap on owner end\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest suite drives the admission function with injected memory readings and the lifecycle/reap sweep with injected session states.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/desktop/desktop-admission.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — The user sees every desktop in one thumbnail grid on cloud workspaces.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"On a Papercusp-hosted workspace the Desktops page shows every desktop as a tile with a thumbnail refreshing every few seconds; clicking a tile opens it live to watch or take over; one or two tiles can be pinned live.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:0\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:6\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"With 5+ desktops on a hosted machine the grid shows one tile per live desktop labelled with its owning agent, thumbnails refresh while the page is visible and stop when it is not, click opens watch then takeover, pins keep up to 2 tiles live.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A live desktop has no tile, thumbnails freeze or keep streaming with no viewer, click opens the wrong desktop, takeover is unaudited, or a third pin is accepted.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"live\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"grid with 5+ desktops\",\n      \"thumbnail refresh\",\n      \"no viewer no capture\",\n      \"open live watch\",\n      \"takeover\",\n      \"pinning limit\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest render suite for the grid component plus a real hosted VM run whose evidence is parked on the P-008 work-item.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/DesktopGrid.test.tsx\",\n        \"apps/operator/e2e/desktop-grid.spec.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — The local desktop app shows the same grid.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The local desktop app gets the same grid for its own desktops, built on the current Desktops page; the old Swarm view is re-evaluated, not assumed reusable.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:6\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:7f5e5839-2627-4f86-89b2-c51acafd6bca:9\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"In the local app the Desktops page offers This computer; local desktops appear as tiles with thumbnails and open live; the fate of the old Swarm view is recorded as a decision with its reason.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Local desktops are missing from the grid, have no thumbnails, cannot be opened live, or the Swarm view is reused without a recorded evaluation.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"live\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"This computer entry\",\n      \"local thumbnails\",\n      \"local live view\",\n      \"Swarm view decision\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest render suite for the local source plus a headless Tauri run (verify-tauri-headless.sh, isolated DB) parked on the P-008 work-item.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/LocalDesktopSource.test.tsx\",\n        \"apps/operator/e2e/desktop-grid-local.spec.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005, P-006, P-008 | live |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-005, P-007, P-008 | live |\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Agent multi-desktop substrate\n\n- **P-001** `done` Design + decisions (record as plan Decisions): per-agent desktop identity (registry scope:'agent' keyed by ownerId + an agent-chosen name; migration needed?); re-key the in-process lease Map from pot → desktopSessionId while keeping the pot-shared desktop and the hosted 'hosted-workspace' desktop (D-404) working; capability:computer resolution order (explicit desktop arg → caller's only/most-recent agent desktop → pot desktop → env); ownership rule (an agent drives its own + its pot's shared desktops); the grid UI for cloud + local — default is to build on the CURRENT cloud Desktops page (HostedDesktopWorkspace); the old local Swarm live view (AdvFramesTab, hive-frame-desktops-live-view-2026-06-06) is re-evaluated on its merits (age, x11vnc vs KasmVNC transport, whether the deployed-frame lane it serves is still live) and reused only if that evaluation says so, else retired or left alone (D-002); and the local live transport (KasmVNC vs x11vnc tickets). importance: high — note: ← WI-10006480 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Multi-desktop provisioning for any agent: extend computer:provision_desktop (or a sibling verb, per P-001) so a worker agent can start N agent-scoped desktops, each returning a desktopSessionId + name; release by id; computer:list_desktops filters mine / my pot / all. Migration via the atomic allocator if P-001 needs one. Vitest: keying, per-desktop inflight coalescing, release. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006481 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Desktop targeting on every computer verb: capability:computer, computer:observe, computer:click_element, computer:record accept a desktop (id or name) and enforce the P-001 ownership rule; screenshot history / action ledger / trajectory state is per desktop. Update tool guidance within the prompt-weight budget. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006482 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Headroom admission + lifecycle: refuse a new desktop when the machine lacks measured memory/CPU headroom (per-desktop footprint measured, not guessed), with a refusal naming the caller's idle desktops to release; optional per-workspace soft cap; every desktop rides the existing freeze-first lifecycle ladder (desktop-lifecycle.ts) and is reaped when its owning agent session ends. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006483 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — See them all\n\n- **P-005** `done` Thumbnails for every live desktop, cloud and local: the capture loop yields a fresh thumbnail (~5s) for every non-terminal desktop while at least one grid is open, and nothing when none is (zero idle cost, parent D-035); relay on cloud (parent D-025), direct on local (today local Swarm tiles have none). blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006484 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` The grid (cloud Desktops page): all desktops as tiles — thumbnail, owning agent, work-item, state, last activity; click → live viewer (watch / take over, existing tickets + audit); pin up to 2 tiles live; selection/pins/filter in nuqs. Built as the shared component chosen in P-001; design-phase.search_registry first. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006485 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Local parity: the same grid component serves the local app (\"This computer\" beside cloud workspaces on the Desktops page) — local desktops get thumbnails, owner/work-item labels, pinning, live view. What happens to the old Swarm live view follows the P-001 re-evaluation (D-002). blocked-by: P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006486 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` End-to-end verification: real hosted VM (two agents, 5+ desktops, grid, refresh, live, take over, release, admission refusal) and the local app via verify-tauri-headless.sh with VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1 (same scenario); evidence parked on the work-item. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-007 importance: high — note: ← WI-10006487 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Owner choices: thumbnail grid (not all-live), cloud AND local\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, directives #1448 + #1451] Avi asked that agents be able to launch as many virtual desktops as they want and that a user can view them all. Offered (a) every tile live vs (b) thumbnails refreshing every few seconds with click-to-open-live (recommended, plus pinning 1-2 tiles live); Avi chose B. Offered cloud-only vs cloud + local desktop app; Avi chose both.\n\n### D-002 — Do not assume the old Swarm live view is reusable — re-evaluate it\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, directive #1452] \"that view was built a long time ago it might be very out of date, don't build on it unless it makes sense to, which should be re-evaluated\". The local Swarm live view (apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/AdvFramesTab.tsx, from hive-frame-desktops-live-view-2026-06-06) is NOT a presumed base. Default: build the shared grid on the current cloud Desktops page (apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/HostedDesktopWorkspace.tsx) and serve local from it. P-001 evaluates the Swarm view (age, transport, whether the deployed-frame lane it serves is still used) and records whether to reuse parts, retire it, or leave it; reuse only with a stated reason.\n\n### D-003 — Per-agent desktop identity: scope 'agent' + scope_ref=ownerId + new `name` column\nDate: 2026-10-06\nAn agent-owned desktop is a desktop_sessions row with scope='agent', scope_ref = the caller's ownerId (resolveAgentIdentity(ctx).ownerId) and a new nullable `name` column (agent-chosen; default `desktop-<n>`). Migration (atomic allocator) adds `name` and replaces desktop_sessions_live_scope_uq (workspace_id, scope, scope_ref) with (workspace_id, scope, scope_ref, COALESCE(name,'')). Pot and workspace scopes keep name NULL, so their one-live-desktop-per-scope rule is unchanged; deployed-frame allocator rows (scope agent, name NULL) are unaffected. Evidence: 900-desktop-sessions-registry.sql makes a second live row per scope_ref impossible today.\n\n### D-004 — Lease map keyed by desktopSessionId; pot and hosted desktops become scope keys\nDate: 2026-10-06\ndesktop-lease.ts re-keys `leases` from potSlug to desktopSessionId and adds a scope-key index (`pot:<slug>`, `agent:<ownerId>:<name>`) for in-flight coalescing and idempotent re-provision. ensureHiveDesktop/hiveDesktop/releaseHiveDesktop(pot) keep their signatures as wrappers over the scope-key API, so pot desktops and the hosted shared desktop (HOSTED_WORKSPACE_DESKTOP_LEASE='hosted-workspace', D-404) keep working unchanged.\n\n### D-005 — capability:computer resolution order and the ownership rule\nDate: 2026-10-06\nEvery computer verb (capability:computer, computer:observe, computer:click_element, computer:record) gains an optional `desktop` arg (desktopSessionId or the caller's own desktop name). Resolution: (1) explicit `desktop`; (2) the caller's live agent desktops: exactly one -> it, several -> the most recently used; (3) the caller's pot desktop (today's behaviour); (4) env display (frame per-slot); (5) registry pot fallback; else the existing no-lease error. Ownership: an agent may drive its OWN agent-scoped desktops and its own pot's shared desktop; an explicit id owned by any other agent is refused with `desktop_not_owned` before any input is sent. Operator-role sessions (su) may target any desktop in their workspace by explicit id. The model still never names a display.\n\n### D-006 — Provisioning door: extend computer:provision_desktop, open to every agent\nDate: 2026-10-06\nNo sibling verb. computer:provision_desktop: omit `pot` -> provision an agent-scoped desktop for the caller (any role), optional `name`; pass `pot` -> legacy pot-shared desktop, still restricted to QUEEN_PLACEMENT_ROLES inside the handler. Re-provisioning an existing name returns that desktop (idempotent per name). computer:release_desktop accepts `desktop` (id or own name) or `pot`. computer:list_desktops accepts `filter: 'mine'|'pot'|'all'` (default all).\n\n### D-007 — Headroom admission uses measured footprint; refusal names idle desktops\nDate: 2026-10-06\nBefore provisioning, admit only if MemAvailable minus a host reserve covers one desktop footprint, where the footprint is MEASURED from live desktops (median memory of each desktop's process tree) with a conservative floor until one has been measured. A refusal (`desktop_headroom_exhausted`) reports measured available vs needed and lists the caller's own idle/frozen desktops to release. Optional per-workspace soft cap via config, default none. Every desktop rides the existing freeze-first lifecycle (desktop-lifecycle.ts); agent-scoped desktops are released when their owning session reaches sessionState 'ended'.\n\n### D-008 — Thumbnails: on-demand capture with a short cache, no new loop\nDate: 2026-10-06\nToday's thumbnails come from a capture script generated at frame bootstrap with a FIXED display list (deployment/desktop-capture.ts, frame-bootstrap.ts), so a desktop started later never gets one. Add an operator-side desktopThumbnail(desktopSessionId): return the cached JPEG if younger than ~4s, else capture one frame (ffmpeg x11grab -frames:v 1, scaled to tile width) with a small concurrency cap. Only grid reads call it, so cost is zero when no grid is open (parent D-035) without any timer. Hosted: hosted-desktop-backend.thumbnail() falls back to it when the capture-loop file is absent or stale (relay path, parent D-025, unchanged). Local: the same function behind the local grid source.\n\n### D-009 — One grid component for cloud and local, built from HostedDesktopWorkspace\nDate: 2026-10-06\nHostedDesktopWorkspace is already presentational over a HostedWorkspaceDesktopBridge (requestRoster/requestThumbnail/requestStart). Generalise it into a source-agnostic desktop grid: tiles (thumbnail, owning agent, work-item, state, last activity), click -> live viewer (watch/take over, existing tickets + audit), pin up to 2 tiles live, selection/pins/filter in nuqs. Two sources: the existing hosted relay bridge, and a local source over this operator's registry. The work-item label is derived at read time from the owner's current claim, not stored. design-phase.search_registry runs before building.\n\n### D-010 — Local live transport is KasmVNC, same RFB client as cloud\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSandbox desktops are KasmVNC (desktop-provisioner-core.ts), so the local grid opens them with the same kasmvnc-rfb client the cloud viewer uses, dialing the desktop's local websocket with kasmvnc-credentials.ts, and records viewer mode via setDesktopViewer for the audit trail. The x11vnc ticket route (deploy/vnc-session.ts) is not used for registry desktops.\n\n### D-011 — D-002 outcome: Swarm view keeps deployed-frame tiles; its local-desktop tiles move to the new grid\nDate: 2026-10-06\nRe-evaluation of AdvFramesTab (hive-frame-desktops-live-view-2026-06-06, four months old): its deployed-frame tiles serve a separate lane (frames over SSH, x11vnc) that this plan does not touch, so they are left alone. Its local registry-desktop tiles have no thumbnails and use the x11vnc ticket path, which the KasmVNC decision supersedes for registry desktops; they are removed and replaced with a link to the Desktops page 'This computer' grid, so there is exactly one place to see local agent desktops.\n\n### D-012 — Refines D-004: lease map keyed by SCOPE KEY, session id is a reverse lookup\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, from reading desktop-lease.ts] D-004 said re-key `leases` by desktopSessionId. The registry row is written BEST-EFFORT (recordLeaseInRegistry swallows PG failures and heals on the next ensure, WI-10002797), so a live lease can exist with no session id. Keying by it would make such a desktop unaddressable. So `leases`, `inflight` and `sessionIds` are keyed by the scope key (`pot:<slug>` | `agent:<ownerId>:<name>`), and `leasedDesktopBySessionId` / release-by-id resolve through the sessionIds reverse map (then the registry for sibling-process rows). Pot wrappers (ensureHiveDesktop, hiveDesktop, displayForHive, desktopEnvForHive, releaseHiveDesktop, leasedHiveDesktops, hiveDesktopSessionId) keep their signatures. The hosted runtime's soleOwner reconcile must pass EVERY live lease's session id (agent desktops included), or it would mark agent desktops dead.\n\n### D-013 — Refines D-006: who may provision — every WORKING role, not read-mostly roles\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, from roles.ts AUTH INVARIANT] D-006 said 'any role'. roles.test.ts pins that the read-mostly roles (papercup, papercup-deep, kettle) never gain a desktop-provisioning tool. The generic worker role is 'cup', which QUEEN_PLACEMENT_ROLES also excludes. New constant DESKTOP_AGENT_ROLES = QUEEN_PLACEMENT_ROLES + 'cup' gates computer:provision_desktop / release_desktop / list_desktops. Inside the handler, the legacy `pot` path still requires QUEEN_PLACEMENT_ROLES (a cup does not equip its whole pot), and agent-scoped (no `pot`) provisioning is open to every DESKTOP_AGENT_ROLES caller. The invariant test gains an assertion that DESKTOP_AGENT_ROLES excludes papercup/papercup-deep/kettle.\n\n### D-014 — P-004 admission gates on measured MEMORY headroom only; CPU is governed by the freeze ladder; cap + reserve are host env knobs\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, from implementing P-004] The plan text says \"memory/CPU headroom\". Implemented (agent-tools/computer/desktop-headroom.ts):\n- Footprint is MEASURED: median of each live desktop's task-subtree cgroup memory.current (listTasks{rootTaskId} + sampleCgroup, outermost cgroups deduped). Until at least one desktop has been measured a 1 GiB floor stands in.\n- Admit a NEW lease only when MemAvailable - footprint >= reserve, reserve = max(2 GiB, 10% of MemTotal). Reusing an existing lease never asks.\n- CPU is NOT an admission input: an idle desktop costs ~0 CPU and a frozen one exactly 0, and the existing freeze-first lifecycle ladder (desktop-lifecycle.ts) already governs CPU under pressure. Admitting on an instantaneous CPU sample would refuse on transient bursts that the ladder resolves.\n- Optional soft cap PAPERCUSP_DESKTOP_SOFT_CAP and reserve override PAPERCUSP_DESKTOP_HOST_RESERVE_BYTES are host env knobs (host-capacity precedent). On a hosted VM the host IS the workspace, so that is the per-workspace cap.\n- Refusal codes desktop_headroom_exhausted | desktop_soft_cap_reached list the caller's idle/frozen desktops to release.\n- Lifecycle: gc-desktop-sessions reaps agent-scope desktops whose owning session's sessionState is 'ended' (resolveSessionStates), beside the existing freeze ladder.\n\n### D-015 — P-007 local source: frame-vnc bridge gains a KasmVNC upstream; roster labels + sync query; This computer on the Desktops page\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed, from reading ws-guard.ts, frame-vnc.ts, hosted-desktop-backend.ts]\n\n- Transport. Inside the desktop shell a same-origin /api WebSocket is REFUSED (libs/generic/desktop-ipc/src/ws-guard.ts, no-http-anywhere P-013), so the local live view cannot be a new upgrade route. It reuses the existing frame-vnc loopback bridge (own port, 127.0.0.1:3078+, single-use ticket, audited, setDesktopViewer). For a registered local desktop whose lease THIS operator process holds (credentials live only in the leasing process, per hosted-desktop-backend lookup), the bridge dials that desktop's loopback KasmVNC websocket server-side with the role-scoped credential from hostedDesktopGrant (observer -> view user, controller -> control user). The secret never reaches the webview. A desktop leased by a sibling process, or one with no KasmVNC endpoint, keeps the existing x11vnc local path, so nothing regresses. The client opens it with kasmvncRfbClass(noVNC), the same RFB class as cloud (D-010).\n- Roster. /deploy/local-desktops rows gain owner/name/workItemId/workItemIntent, derived at read time with the same claimsForSessions the hosted roster uses (D-009). The grid reads them through a sync query (desktops.local) that calls the same function. It is invalidated on registry writes, and the grid re-reads on its visible 15s tick, because a claim can change with no registry write.\n- Thumbnails. The P-005 loopback route, fetched as blobs on the visible 5s tick, skipping pinned (live) tiles.\n- Page. The Desktops page workspace picker gains 'This computer' beside cloud workspaces; it renders DesktopGrid over the local source.\n- D-011 follow-through. AdvFramesTab's local-desktop tiles are replaced by a link to Desktops > This computer.\n\n### D-016 — Refines D-015: the desktop app gains a /desktops route; This computer is the default only with no cloud workspace\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed, from reading packages/operator-ui/src/surfaces/index.tsx and apps/operator-vite/src/routes]\n\n- DesktopWorkspacePage (the Desktops page) was mounted only as the portal's `desktops` operator surface; the Tauri SPA had no route to it, so 'This computer' would have been unreachable in the local app. New route apps/operator-vite/src/routes/desktops.tsx renders the same component (route tree is vite-plugin generated). Deep links: /desktops?desktopHost=local and /desktops?desktopHost=<workspace id>.\n- The picker always shows, with 'This computer' (value 'local') first. It is the default only when there is no active cloud workspace, so the existing cloud default and every cloud deep link are unchanged.\n- D-011 link target is LOCAL_DESKTOPS_HREF='/desktops?desktopHost=local' (AdvFramesTab). Its count reads the same desktops.local sync query, which removes the Swarm view's 10s setInterval poll of /deploy/local-desktops.\n\n### D-017 — P-008 split: local live e2e now; real hosted-VM run deferred to the host train (EI-25225008797935576)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, from dev:pipeline_position testClass candidate-install-upgrade (readiness 'gap'), the publish-workspace-host-artifacts.mjs contract, consult conv-muwj97k0 (su-2c0dc471, partial), and the r45/r47/r48 host-train work-items EI-24217136033989573 / EI-24270602139941589]\nHosted VMs run IMMUTABLE published workspace-host artifacts (GB server.tgz in the public Cupboard store) installed through the controlled host train (soak gates, controller restart, guest upgrade). The current tree cannot reach a hosted VM until it (1) promotes to main (main is frozen behind a red gate held by a live fixer, not this lane), (2) is cut into a new host artifact and PUBLISHED to the public store, (3) is installed on a VM. Doing (2)+(3) tonight would publish unreleased code outward and run a host upgrade outside the train that another lane owns, so it is not done.\nSo P-008 is split:\n- LOCAL half (verify-tauri-headless.sh, VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1, two real agent desktops, grid + thumbnails + live view) is the pre-release live evidence for the shared grid component, which is the same component the cloud Desktops page renders.\n- HOSTED half pre-release evidence = the hosted backend/relay unit + integration bindings (SPEC-P-005 integration 25873, hosted-desktop-viewer-protocol/HostedDesktopWorkspace tests for P-006).\n- The REAL-VM scenario (two agents, 5+ desktops, grid, refresh, live, take over, release, admission refusal) is DEFERRED to EI-25225008797935576, owned by su-16da39cf: run it on avi-test once a host revision containing these commits is installed by the host train. The plan ships with this deferral disclosed; it is not claimed as verified on a real VM.\n\n### D-018 — Rubric rev 1 binds eight never-created test files — amend to as-built tests; R-4/R-5 e2e layer = two committed Playwright specs\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, from checking every rubric check path on disk 11:11Z] acceptance-agent-multi-desktops-grid-2026-10-06 rev 1 was written at plan start with PREDICTED paths; all 8 check.files are MISSING (agent-desktops.test.ts, agent-desktops.integration.test.ts, desktop-targeting.test.ts, desktop-admission.test.ts, cloud-workspaces/DesktopGrid.test.tsx, e2e/desktop-grid.spec.ts, cloud-workspaces/LocalDesktopSource.test.tsx, e2e/desktop-grid-local.spec.ts). A grader's deterministic tests-check would red every criterion on a missing file, so rev 1 is not vettable as written. Ruling: (1) rubrics:amend to rev 2 re-pointing each criterion's check at the AS-BUILT test files, each criterion owning its own files (no shared file across criteria, per the non-overlap meta criterion). check is bar-hash material (acceptanceBarHashMaterial in packages/operator-core/lib/rubrics.ts), so this goes through the routed amendment-approval flow; the bar TEXT, scope and drift markers stay unchanged. (2) The e2e layer R-4/R-5 require is delivered as two COMMITTED Playwright specs in apps/operator/e2e, modelled on frames-live-view.spec.ts / desktop-render-matrix.spec.ts (hermetic: real SPA, stubbed roster/thumbnail data): desktop-grid.spec.ts (cloud grid: 5+ tiles with owner labels, click opens watch, third pin refused, selection/pins in the URL) and desktop-grid-local.spec.ts (This computer: local roster tiles with thumbnails, open live). (3) The live plane is evidenced by the verify-tauri-headless isolated run of .papercusp/scratch/p007-local-e2e.sh (real desktops, real thumbnails, real VNC) for local; the hosted real-VM run stays deferred per D-017 (EI-25225008797935576). The rev 1 vetting consult conv-muwkbmwu is superseded and will be closed; vetting restarts on rev 2.\n\n### D-019 — Rubric rev 2 folds the rev-1 vetting answer without adding a sixth bar\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, from the rubric-vetting consult conv-muwkbmwu thread-post:1159766 (su-02bd255e)] The reviewer proposed a new R-6 'existing shared desktop and Desktop tab unchanged'. No rev 4. Any amendment voids the vetting read, and the two consult forks so far have been unreliable (one died at its context limit, WI-10006676; one stalled at pickup).\n- Known gap, disclosed rather than amended: R-4's clause 'takeover is audited' is bound to hosted-desktop-backend.test.ts, which only carries auditAction as a fixture field. The tests that assert it are unbound: packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-session-host.test.ts ('dials the view-only credential for a watcher and the control credential for a takeover' asserts auditActions() == ['desktop_watch_started','desktop_takeover_started']) and packages/operator-core/lib/desktop/hosted-desktop-channel.test.ts ('maps controller to the control user with input allowed' asserts auditAction 'desktop_takeover_started'). The meta-attestation rates falsifiable-with-evidence 'weak' for this and names both tests, so the grader reads them directly.\n- failure-mode-coverage is rated 'weak': thaw-after-freeze and reap racing an in-flight computer verb have no test (WI-10006636, owned by su-16da39cf).\n- R-4 (model scoped 'on a hosted machine', passRatings healthy) is expected to grade degraded until EI-25225008797935576 runs the hosted-VM scenario (D-017/D-021/D-023). The ship gate has no below-passRatings refusal (runbook section 4: the author verdict is the plan-level judgment), so the author will record accept with that reasoning. The alternative (split R-4 into a grid-contract bar and a separate hosted-host bar R-6) was considered and rejected: it needs new Requirements, new AUTO-BAR clauses and a fresh activation audit, and it would still leave one bar degraded for the same reason.\n- The e2e layer is re-proven on clean blobs: both Playwright specs re-ran at 13:17Z on HEAD 728748a0 with every spec/fixture/component file byte-identical to HEAD (11 passed), recorded as docs/evidence/agent-multi-desktops-grid-2026-10-06/e2e-playwright-run.json and bound to the R-5 clauses through testing:record-run. This supersedes the dirty-tree ledger rows 20838185/20838186/20838352.\n\n### D-025 — CORRECTION to D-024: the ship gate DOES refuse a mandatory bar graded below pass; the plan ships only after the hosted-VM run\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed; from re-vet conv-muwp6rl2 (su-68d734c3) and a direct read of the gate code]\n\n- D-024 said 'the ship gate has no below-passRatings refusal, so the author will record accept'. That was FALSE. Measured: packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-contract-snapshot.ts:1393 `const gatesShipping = criterion.role === 'outcome' && criterion.mandatory === true;` and :1397 `if (gatesShipping && gradingState === 'not-pass') addCode('bar_snapshot_grading_not_pass');`. rubric-template.ts:1145 isForbiddenMandatoryPassRating also refuses 'degraded' as a pass rating on a mandatory bar. R-4 is mandatory with passRatings ['healthy'] and can only grade degraded until EI-25225008797935576 runs the hosted-VM scenario. So no author verdict can ship this plan before then.\n- Route: complete everything else (vetting, items, per-item audit, independent grading), then record the author verdict 'accept-pending-delivery'. The gate reports bar_snapshot_author_accepted_pending_delivery, which holds delivery open by design (snapshot.ts:828: 'supply the outstanding delivery-plane evidence, then record the final accept; do NOT amend the rubric or re-grade on this code'). After the hosted-VM run: re-grade R-4, record final accept, ship.\n- Splitting R-4 does not change this: every outcome bar must be mandatory (bar_snapshot_mandatory_invalid), so a separate hosted-VM bar would gate shipping the same way. Not splitting.\n- The rest of D-024 stands except its 'no rev 4' point: grading has not started and shipping waits on the hosted run anyway, so a rev-4 amend costs no ship time. Bar text unchanged.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-4)\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 57 → 58\nChanged BARs: R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06","title":"Move Email, Calendar and Phone agent tasks onto durable blueprint execution","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Move Email, Calendar and Phone agent tasks onto durable blueprint execution\nslug: app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-07\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nEvery agent task in the Email, Calendar and Phone apps runs on Papercusp's durable workflow system, the generic blueprint execution delivered by `blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23`. Concretely:\n\n- the task is a **blueprint operation** declared in the app's harness blueprint, with typed input and output schemas;\n- it is started through the **one invocation contract**: `blueprint:submit` with a request key, or a trigger/routine binding that targets the operation;\n- each run is a **durable work item or plan run**, executed with DBOS checkpointing, readable through `blueprint:status` / `blueprint:result` / events, and safe to replay (same key and same input give one execution; a conflicting input is refused);\n- its output still reaches the app **only through the app's existing parse gate**.\n\n## Owner directives (source-tagged)\n\n- [owner:Avi 2026-10-06 #1433] \"Make sure that the agent tasks are built on top of papercusp's durable workflow system? do our email and phone and calendar apps work like that?\"\n- [owner:Avi 2026-10-06 #1434] \"write 2 plans. one to move our other apps we already created to our new durable workflow system.\"\n- [owner:Avi 2026-09-29 #869] \"even after the sync we shouldnt automatically compose a draft reply for emails automatically\". This plan must NOT arm any binding that auto-composes Gmail draft replies.\n\n## Background — measured state on 2026-10-06 (su-7f8d7809, operator DB + git-tracked source)\n\n- `harness_shared.blueprint_operation_invocations` has **zero rows** for `email`, `calendar` or `phone-app`. The only rows belong to the durable plan's own p015 smoke harnesses.\n- **Email.** Its agent task is a blueprint (`email/blueprints/email-draft-proposal`, work-item kind `email-draft-proposal`, draft-only). Its trigger pack calls `work_items:create` directly and launches plans directly, because the app predates the durable invocation path. There are 136 `email-draft-proposal` work items: 5 done and 2 dropped (8/27–8/29), and **129 open and never claimed** (created 8/29–9/15). Every Email trigger binding is disarmed.\n- **Calendar.** Its agent task is a blueprint (`calendar-meeting-prep`). The armed binding `5bbaba69-d03c-40c2-89dc-a039282aabda` launches a plan directly. It has only **2 trigger_runs, both on 2026-08-28** (1 failed, 1 succeeded), and there are zero `calendar-meeting-prep` work items. Cause not yet known [inferred: either no events reach it or the dispatch is failing — re-probe in P-006].\n- **Phone.** The call agent is a LiveKit real-time worker (`phone-app/worker/src/agent.ts`, `brain.ts`, `call-recovery.ts`) that keeps durable call records in the app's own database. A search of git-tracked phone source outside template copies found no use of `pot-app-seam` or work items, although `phone-app/DECISIONS.md` describes it as a \"plan-driven, pot-supervised run\".\n- The external-trigger dispatcher routine is active (checked 2026-10-06).\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- **`blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23`** provides the invocation contract (`blueprint:submit/status/result/events/cancel/signal/resume`), bindings that target operations, and the migration rule that \"existing schedules, inputs, permissions and replay identity survive migration\". It is awaiting acceptance and is being carried to shipped under WI-10006332. Building and testing here can proceed on the current build (staging). Final acceptance of this plan needs that plan shipped. **Reuse its binding-migration mechanism; do not fork a second one.**\n- The CRM plan `crm-agent-sales-onboarding-apps-2026-10-06` depends on P-002 (seam client), P-008/P-009 (Phone's durable call unit) and P-011 (template default) of this plan.\n\n## Scope and exclusions\n\nIn scope: declaring operations, the seam client, rewiring bindings and UI calls, the stranded-task cleanup and its recurrence guard, Phone's durable call unit, verification, and the template/guide default.\n\nOut of scope:\n- Adding any send primitive to Email. The no-auto-draft rule stays exactly as the owner set it.\n- Any new scheduler, queue or workflow engine. Only the existing blueprint invocation, trigger bindings and DBOS machinery are used.\n- Putting each spoken turn of a live call into a durable step. The real-time voice loop stays in the LiveKit worker; the durable unit is the call.\n\n## Constraints\n\n- Each app keeps exactly ONE typed seam (`pot-app-seam`). Blueprint invocation is added to that seam, not as a parallel path.\n- Agent authority stays read/propose-only, exactly as each app's blueprint declares today.\n- Request keys are derived from domain identity: `messageId` for Email, `eventId` plus revision for Calendar, the call/booking id for Phone. A retry or a re-delivered trigger therefore replays one execution and never creates a second draft, prep or call.\n- Tests ship with each change, in each app's own test framework. UI is verified head-lessly per `/internal/docs/testing/agent-e2e`.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Email's draft operation, once migrated: should it stay invoked only on demand (a \"Draft a reply\" action you trigger), or ever run from a binding? Default under the 9/29 rule: on demand only, with the binding migrated but disarmed.\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Apps call one pinned blueprint operation contract.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Make sure the agent tasks are built on top of Papercusp's durable workflow system.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"order:1433\",\"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:96b5694134e6af9d3cac020ca1954157b7b99f3f700a3eae06ef397ccb50f919\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A declared app operation submitted through the public blueprint contract on the current build reaches a terminal result that its returned handle can read.\",\"falsifier\":\"A declared app operation submitted through the public blueprint contract never yields a terminal result readable through its handle.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the contract integration test against the real operation service on PostgreSQL: declare a test operation, submit it, drive it terminal, read status and result by the returned handle.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/app-operation-contract.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — The pot-app-seam client replays one execution per request key.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Make sure the agent tasks are built on top of Papercusp's durable workflow system.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"order:1433\",\"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:96b5694134e6af9d3cac020ca1954157b7b99f3f700a3eae06ef397ccb50f919\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Resubmitting an app operation through the pot-app-seam client with the same request key returns the original handle without minting a second execution.\",\"falsifier\":\"A replayed request key through the seam client mints a second execution or returns a different handle.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit-test the seam client with a fake host for replay, conflicting-input refusal and the parse gate on ready results. Integration-test the seam host adapter against the real operation service for same-key replay.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/generic/pot-app-seam/src/index.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/pot-app-seam-operations.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Email's blueprint declares a draft-only reply operation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Move the apps we already created (Email, Calendar, Phone) onto the durable workflow system.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"order:1434\",\"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:4ec319042d87e2c64b91d93517ff9a257212113fb821b6044a168ce012b7a536\",\"order:869\",\"session_turn:claude:ed2b025e-e16d-47d5-a46f-20ef1af5558f:688df1699b505668646785a31262d755524a0edf8a34b3a646a5dd727c779b54\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Email's harness blueprint validates with a draft-reply operation whose granted authority cannot send mail.\",\"falsifier\":\"Email's harness blueprint fails validation or grants its draft-reply operation a send capability.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Load Email's harness blueprint through the orchestrator blueprint schema and assert the draft-reply operation's input and output schemas plus the absence of any send tool in its authority.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"email/tests/email-operations-blueprint.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Only an owner click starts an Email draft reply.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Even after the sync, Email must never automatically compose a draft reply.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"order:869\",\"session_turn:claude:ed2b025e-e16d-47d5-a46f-20ef1af5558f:688df1699b505668646785a31262d755524a0edf8a34b3a646a5dd727c779b54\",\"order:1434\",\"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:4ec319042d87e2c64b91d93517ff9a257212113fb821b6044a168ce012b7a536\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An owner click on Draft a reply is the only event that starts an Email draft-reply operation.\",\"falsifier\":\"A trigger binding or mail sync starts an Email draft-reply operation without an owner click.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit-test Email's Draft a reply action for its submit call and messageId-derived request key. Integration-test the migrated Email trigger bindings on PostgreSQL: each targets an operation, stays disarmed, and no work_items:create target remains.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"email/tests/draft-reply-action.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/external-triggers/email-operation-bindings.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Never-claimed app tasks raise a finding.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Move the apps we already created (Email, Calendar, Phone) onto the durable workflow system.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"order:1434\",\"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:4ec319042d87e2c64b91d93517ff9a257212113fb821b6044a168ce012b7a536\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An app-originated work item that no executor claims within its window raises an attention finding.\",\"falsifier\":\"A seeded never-claimed app-originated work item older than the window produces no attention finding.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit-test the window predicate. Integration-test the guard on PostgreSQL with a seeded never-claimed app work item, then read the finding. The 129 stranded drafts are dispositioned dropped without execution and counted by query.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/app-task-no-executor.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/app-task-no-executor.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Each upcoming-event signal starts one meeting-prep operation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Move the apps we already created (Email, Calendar, Phone) onto the durable workflow system.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"order:1434\",\"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:4ec319042d87e2c64b91d93517ff9a257212113fb821b6044a168ce012b7a536\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each upcoming-event signal for the armed meeting-prep binding starts exactly one meeting-prep operation keyed by its event revision.\",\"falsifier\":\"An upcoming-event signal for the armed meeting-prep binding starts zero operations or a duplicate one.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Name the root cause of binding 5bbaba69 firing only twice in a plan Decision. Preserve the prior evidence; record request/receipt/target identities, runtime source identity, restart timing, terminal status/result, side-effect counts and Tauri capture for each app. A missing app or restart leg rates unknown and blocks shipment.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Invocation contract\nApps use the public `blueprint:submit/status/result/events/cancel` contract (`packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-contract.ts`), reached through each app's existing MCP tool invoker. Operations are declared per `BlueprintOperationSchema` (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/schema.ts`). The exact shapes are pinned in the P-001 Decision.\n\n### Seam client\n`libs/generic/pot-app-seam` already carries submit/status/result. Add events and cancel, plus one generic tool-invoker host adapter so apps do not hand-map tool envelopes. `launchPlanRuns` is removed rather than kept alongside. Email and Calendar drop their forked seam copies and consume the generic seam. The template copy stays byte-identical.\n\n### Email\nOperations `draft-reply` (work-item target, kind `email-draft-proposal`, propose-only) and `triage-inbox`. Legacy launch-plan bindings migrate through `migrateExternalTriggerPlanBindingToOperation`; the `create-work-item` binding b7976842 is detached and replaced by a disarmed operation binding. Nothing is armed (owner #869).\n\n### Calendar\nRoot-cause the two-run history first, then declare `meeting-prep`, migrate 5bbaba69 preserving arming, and render status from `blueprint:status/result`.\n\n### Phone\nThe durable unit is the call; design recorded as a Decision under P-008 before code.\n\n### Stranded-task guard\nReuse an existing stall/claimability detector; the completion names which one.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-010 | live |\n| R-11 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-010 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Platform readiness\n\n- **P-001** `done` Pin the invocation contract the apps will call. Confirm on the current build which surface each app uses: blueprint:submit/status/result/events/cancel/signal/resume, trigger bindings that target a blueprint operation, and the parent plan's binding migration (from blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23). One call is one durable blueprint operation (or execution program) with named steps: pre-call brief, booking linkage, start of the live session, wait for the session to end (a signal from the LiveKit worker), then wrap-up (transcript, summary, action items, follow-up proposals). The real-time voice loop stays in the worker, never a step per utterance.
