Update the papercusp-app / papercusp-ops-pots template GUIDE and reference so a materialized app declares its agent tasks as blueprint oper… <!-- P-011 -->\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — P-001: apps call the seven public blueprint:* operation tools; contract pinned to operation-contract.ts\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured on the current build 2026-10-06 (code read, not memory): packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-contract.ts + operation-tool-names.ts + operation-client.ts. Parent plan blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23 has all 24 items done (P-005 service contracts, P-017 tool surface) and is in acceptance only (WI-10006332); its acceptance does not change these shapes.\n\nSurfaces each app uses after this plan: Email, Calendar and Phone call blueprint:submit/status/result/events/cancel (signal/resume only where an operation declares signals/waits) through pot-app-seam over their existing platform MCP invoker. Event-driven starts use trigger bindings whose action type is 'blueprint-operation' (binding-engine.ts: requestKey = trigger-run:<id>, input = redacted routing envelope merged with the binding's literal input). Legacy launch-plan bindings move with migrateExternalTriggerPlanBindingToOperation (installs DISARMED replacements). No host operations:* verbs are added (consult conv-muw9m5av: two independent peers confirm blueprint:* is the host surface).\n\nPinned shapes:\n- submit {harness, operationId, requestKey(1-200, idempotency: same key+same input replays, different input refused), input object, title?, summary?} -> {handle}\n- handle {workspaceId, harnessSlug, receiptId, operationId, specificationRevision, target: {kind:'work-item', id} | {kind:'plan', runId, instanceSlug}}; bound to the submitting caller and scope.\n- status {handle, phase accepted|dispatched|waiting|terminal, outcome succeeded|unverified|failed|cancelled|dropped|null, items[{id,state,assignee}], planRun|null, cancellationRequested, wait{name,token}|null}\n- result: pending{status} | failed/cancelled/dropped/unavailable{status,reason} | ready{status,output,evidenceRef,acceptanceEvidenceRef?}. Only ready carries output; apps treat result as the verified outcome and events as progress only (known caveat EI-24253915088430157: events can say succeeded while result rejects output).\n- events {handle, cursor?, limit<=100} -> {status, events[{...body,cursor,at}], cursor, hasMore}\n- cancel {handle, requestKey, reason} -> {eventId, replayed, accepted:true, wakeQueued, handled:false, effected}; effected may be false at return (WI-10004562), so callers re-read status/result rather than assume cancellation.\nPinned by packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/app-operation-contract.integration.test.ts (R-1).\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-06\nAmendment-Id: amend-8dd90c7f2b7320924e2d2b67\nRequest-Hash: 4ded822f2065977c108350d60428f511336435ce24cd6010590fdbade92b268a\nActor: su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6\nReason: Apply rubric-vetting feedback (consult conv-muwae718): widen r-2 to events+cancel, positive controls on r-3/r-4/r-11, r-5 settlement, r-8 as outcome, r-10 integration test decides, idempotency-layer scope note. r-1 untouched.\nApproved-By: su-2183c229-6216-4eca-b736-969f9d48b317\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1159122\nApproved-At: 2026-10-06T06:40:54.645Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 18 → 19\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, R-11\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-003 — App operations (and their worker roles) are declared in the harness ROOT .papercusp/blueprint.yaml; pots-plane blueprints/* are never projected for blueprint:submit\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured by code read (su-64a5417a, P-003): operation-service.ts:126 resolves a harness's operations from its projected specification or, on a miss, `<harnessDir>/.papercusp/blueprint.yaml` (project-to-pg.ts:282, commit-reproject.ts:86). harness_shared.blueprints holds projections ONLY for the two p015 smoke harnesses, whose operations sit in that root file (workItem.kind feature, role worker, both on the same blueprint). orchestrator blueprint/validate.ts:289 refuses an agent operation whose execution.role is not a live role of the DECLARING blueprint (its own roleIds or registered coord roles via registry-sets.ts knownRoles); roles of dependency blueprints do not count.\n\nRuling: each app (Email P-003, Calendar P-006, Phone P-008, and the new-app template default P-011) declares `operations:` AND the worker role(s) those operations execute under in its root `.papercusp/blueprint.yaml` (today `id: <app>, extends: coding`). The pots-plane hive/member blueprints under the app's `blueprints/*` (e.g. email-ops, email-draft-proposal) stay pots-plane definitions and are NOT where operations go; an operation may still target a work-item kind those blueprints mint (e.g. itemKind email-draft-proposal). Each operation's inputSchema/resultSchema are pinned to the app's own Zod contracts by an app-side drift test (z.toJSONSchema equality), and that test also asserts the worker roles hold no send/apply capability. P-003's first placement in blueprints/email-ops is superseded by this ruling and is being moved.\nRelated: P-003, P-006, P-008, P-011\n\n### D-004 — P-004: trigger-fired Email drafting targets a trigger-entry operation; owner-initiated drafting targets draft-reply; the pack's recipe target is removed, not replaced\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured 2026-10-06 by code read + live DB (su-64a5417a, P-004 / WI-10006456).\n\nFacts:\n- A blueprint-operation binding submits input = { ...redactTriggerArgsForPlanInputs(args) , ...binding.action.input } = { trigger: { key, source, event, sourceId, externalId, occurredAt, datatypeId, dedupeKey } } + literals (binding-engine.ts ~1021-1032). The private message payload is DROPPED by design.\n- draft-reply's inputSchema (root .papercusp/blueprint.yaml, pinned to EmailDraftInput by tests/operation-contract-drift.test.ts) is additionalProperties:false and requires messageId/threadId/from/to/subject/text/policy. A binding migrated straight to draft-reply would install cleanly (migration parity does not validate operation input) and then be refused at admission the first time it fires.\n- triggers:read-payload resolves only by planRunId (plan_run_ref); an operation-dispatched run has none. But the envelope already carries sourceId + externalId, which are the message's lookup keys.\n- Live Email bindings: 4 rows, all action launch-plan, all DISARMED, all ext:gmail:message.received (6364f44f, 0fc934f6, bd4836ba -> plan gmail-respond-with-draft-2026-08-22; 05c05c92 -> plan respond-with-draft). No live triage or create-work-item binding exists; the pack's declared mail-to-draft/mail-to-triage were never installed (no pack_installation_id).\n- trigger-pack-materialize.ts materializes only recipe and plan targets.\n\nRuling:\n1. Email declares a second operation, draft-reply-for-trigger, whose inputSchema is exactly the routing envelope { trigger:{...}, policy? } and whose worker resolves the message server-side from trigger.sourceId + trigger.externalId through the existing mail read path, then produces the same EmailDraftProposalSet result as draft-reply. Same worker role (no send capability), same result schema, pinned by the drift test.\n2. The 4 legacy launch-plan bindings migrate to draft-reply-for-trigger via migrateExternalTriggerPlanBindingToOperation (triggers:bind { migrateFromBindingId }) and stay DISARMED per [owner:Avi 2026-09-29 #869]. A test proves a trigger-shaped input is ADMISSIBLE for that operation, so arming later is not a latent failure.\n3. The owner-initiated 'Draft a reply' action calls draft-reply with the full EmailDraftInput and requestKey draft-reply:<messageId> through pot-app-seam.\n4. The trigger pack's work_items:create recipe target and the mail-to-draft binding that feeds it are REMOVED from automations/papercusp.json (requirement c). They are not replaced with an operation target because trigger packs cannot express one today; adding an operation target kind to trigger packs is a platform follow-up, not P-004 scope. mail-to-triage (plan target, never installed) is left as-is.\n\nRejected: a single draft-reply with oneOf input (breaks the EmailDraftInput drift pin and mixes two trust shapes); embedding the payload in operation input (reverses the deliberate payload drop); a new platform payload reader (unnecessary - the envelope already carries the lookup keys).\nRelated: P-004, P-003, P-010\n\n### D-005 — Self-only execution route\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: owner directive #1442, owner-typed turn session_turn:claude:29b7bc7b-53f0-4aa0-b7c0-2533d4a4be8c:0 (turn-provenance OWNER, interactive), recorded for session su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6: \"Put yourself on auto mode and carry the app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06 plan to shipped status yourself now.\"\n\nRoute A: this session (su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6) implements the plan.\n\nRuling: the execution route for the WHOLE plan (every item, whether held or not yet claimed) is self. su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6 implements it directly. There is no fleet and no peer placement. Unheld items are reserved for this session and other agents cannot claim them. A successor of this session (carry-respawn) inherits the route.\n\nNot affected: independent acceptance grading. A non-implementer recruited by plans:set-plan-status { status:'shipped' } still grades the acceptance rubric. The self-only route covers implementation, verification and the code-truth audit only.\n\n### D-006 — Trigger-entry Email worker reads the message with triggers:read-payload { workItemId } (corrects D-004's read-path premise)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured 2026-10-06 (su-64a5417a, P-004 / WI-10006456) by code read: D-004 said the trigger-entry worker resolves the message 'through the existing mail read path'. No such read path exists. personal:search returns bounded snippets only; mail:reply resolves a stored message only for its own WRITE; the capability personal:mail:read named on the email worker ceiling appears nowhere in platform code; triggers:read-payload resolved only by planRunId, and an operation-dispatched trigger run has no plan run.\n\nRuling: extend the existing reader rather than add a parallel one. triggers:read-payload now takes exactly one of planRunId or workItemId. readTriggerOperationPayload (packages/operator-core/lib/external-triggers/plan-run-payload.ts) joins blueprint_operation_invocations to trigger_runs on BOTH request_key = 'trigger-run:<runId>' AND caller_id = 'trigger-binding:<bindingId>', inside the caller's workspace, with target_kind work-item and target_ref = the worker's own work item. That double join is the trust boundary: only an invocation the binding engine minted for that trigger run resolves. No status predicate, because the invocation row is written in the submit transaction before the engine marks the run succeeded. Pinned by plan-run-payload.integration.test.ts (forged caller, cross-binding request key and cross-workspace cases all refuse).\n\nThe draft-reply-for-trigger operation therefore takes the routing envelope as input, and its worker calls triggers:read-payload { workItemId } to get the message body. The private payload still never enters operation input or any federated record. D-004's rejection of 'a new platform payload reader' stands: this widens the one existing reader.\n\n### D-007 — P-006 root cause: binding 5bbaba69 fired only twice because its calendar had only three near-term events ever (all 08-28 test events); no pipeline defect remains to fix\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured by su-64a5417a (P-006 / WI-10006458) from harness_shared.trigger_deliveries, trigger_runs and trigger_sources (workspace papercusp-workspace).\n\nFacts:\n- Event census for bound source f3d8cee9 (super@papercusp.com, gcal poll). Delivery dedupe keys survive payload pruning (72 of 76 payloads are pruned), so this count is complete. 15 distinct events ever: 11 from the initial full sync 2026-08-27 20:07Z (event-created only); 3 acceptance-test events created by su-7422e95d on 2026-08-28 15:27/15:31/15:50Z (the ONLY event-upcoming deliveries, 3 events x 3 sinks = 9 rows, all outcome=delivered including the trigger-bindings sink); 1 event via the new plugin on 2026-10-06 10:46Z that starts 2026-10-20. No calendar event has started on this source since 2026-08-28 16:00Z.\n- Runs: 3d093ff8 (15:31Z) failed external_trigger_plan_run_not_started; 37b682b0 (15:50Z) succeeded (planRunId 1291, minted 4). The failure was root-caused and fixed the same day by su-7422e95d (decision D-019 of plan email-calendar-web-desktop-ship-2026-08-27, regression test with a proven mutant): the trigger-pack input_schema required start/end as objects, while the canonical calendar-event emits strings, so the start gate refused and the engine collapsed that into the opaque error. The 15:50Z retest after the fix succeeded.\n- Not determined: why the first test event (15:27Z) produced no run under any binding. su-7422e95d was reconfiguring these bindings at that moment (the legacy binding was disarmed at 15:36Z).\n- The new provider (libs/papercusp/plugins/google-calendar) emits event-upcoming for single events overlapping [now, now+lead), with lead defaulting to 15 min, on each pass. The connector polls every 300s by default (connector-runtime.ts DEFAULT_CONNECTOR_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS), so consecutive windows overlap at nominal cadence. Events can still be missed when passes are interrupted for more than lead minutes (the window resets to now). That outage gap is filed separately for the provider owner and does not cause the observed symptom.\n\nRuling: P-006's 'fix the cause durably with a regression test' clause is satisfied by the existing D-019 fix and test. There is no further pipeline defect behind 'fired only twice'. 'So the migrated binding actually fires' is demonstrated instead by an end-to-end acceptance of the MIGRATED binding: a replay of the stored 08-28 event-upcoming into it (triggers:run-with-last-event) plus a committed test of the operation-targeting dispatch. P-006 proceeds to the migration: declare a trigger-entry meeting-prep operation in the harness root .papercusp/blueprint.yaml (D-003), following the D-004/D-006 pattern (binding input carries trigger refs only; the worker reads the event with triggers:read-payload { workItemId }), and migrate 5bbaba69 preserving armed state, inputs, permissions and replay identity.\n\n### D-008 — P-008: Phone's durable call unit = the sidecar call row (one per call key) driving two blueprint operations (call-brief, call-wrap-up); deterministic steps stay in the sidecar/worker\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured 2026-10-06 by code read (su-64a5417a, P-008 / WI-10006460), current staging tree:\n- An operation can declare `signals` (payloadSchema) and `waits` (responseSchema) (libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/schema.ts BlueprintOperationSchema). But openBlueprintOperationWait (packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-service.ts:756) has NO production caller: only operation-client's typed wrapper and tests. DBOS.recv appears only in dbos/durable-orchestration-workflow.ts, which is not wired to blueprint operations. So no executor today can suspend one operation mid-run on a wait.\n- blueprint:result carries output only when terminal (D-001). A pre-call brief must exist BEFORE the call, so it cannot be an intermediate product of the same operation that later does wrap-up.\n- The phone-app agent's capability envelope (phone-app/DECISIONS.md, domain-roles) reads contacts/calendar/email/memory/caller history, writes call records and drafts only, and never originates a call.\n- Today the worker posts the transcript (/internal/calls/:room/transcript) and a turn-LATENCY summary (/internal/calls/:room/summary) to the sidecar; no agent produces a wrap-up. DECISIONS.md's `call-session` plan template is referenced by no code.\n\nRuling (design for P-009):\n1. The durable call unit is the sidecar `call` row, unique on a call key: `scheduled:<scheduledCallId>` for a booked call, `inbound:<roomName>` for an answered one. It is created at booking time (scheduled) or at answer (inbound) and records: call key, booking id, brief handle, wrap-up handle, dial claim time, session start/end, transcript segment count and sha256.\n2. Named steps, in order:\n   a. brief: blueprint operation `call-brief` (target work-item, execution agent, role phone-agent), requestKey `call-brief:<callKey>`, input {callKey, bookingId, counterparty, scheduledFor}. Result = the brief, read by the sidecar at join time and handed to the worker. Scheduled calls only; inbound calls skip it (the worker's per-turn context injection covers them).\n   b. booking linkage: the call row stores the booking id and both handles. A duplicate booking delivery resolves to the same call key, so submit replays the same brief handle.\n   c. session start: the ONLY dial/join path is an atomic sidecar claim on the call row (set dial_claimed_at WHERE it IS NULL, RETURNING). A second attempt for the same call key gets no row and does not dial. The agent never dials.\n   d. wait for session end: the worker's end-of-session report. The worker first persists the full transcript to the sidecar, then reports session end; a worker crash is reported by the sidecar's existing orphan recovery with endReason worker-lost and the partial transcript.\n   e. wrap-up: blueprint operation `call-wrap-up` (target work-item, execution agent, role phone-agent), requestKey `call-wrap-up:<callId>`, input {callId, transcriptRef: {segmentCount, sha256}}. Result schema = the existing CallOutcome {callId, disposition, summary, actionItems[], followUpDraft?, screeningVerdict?} through the one parse gate into call / call_action_item.\n3. Recovery: a sidecar boot sweep re-submits wrap-up for every call whose session ended without a terminal wrap-up. The same request key replays the same execution, so a restart cannot duplicate it; the agent re-reads the recorded transcript, never live audio. An operator/DBOS restart leaves the work item durable and requeued.\n4. The real-time voice loop stays entirely in the worker; no step per utterance.\n5. Not chosen: (i) one operation with a declared session-ended wait, because no executor opens waits (above) and the brief must be readable before the call; (ii) an execution program (plan target) with a call-session template, for the same missing suspend-on-signal step plus a plan run per call. Revisit (i) when an executor opens operation waits; the call row and request keys would carry over unchanged.\n6. P-009 updates phone-app/DECISIONS.md (replace the unimplemented call-session template entry) and declares both operations and the phone-agent worker role in phone-app/.papercusp/blueprint.yaml (root file, per D-003).\n\n### D-009 — P-009: corrections to D-008's premises; the durable call unit is a new phone_call_units row keyed by call key, and CallOutcome/call_action_item are built here (they did not exist)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured: `grep -rn --exclude-dir={node_modules,.git,dist} -e CallOutcome -e call_action_item -e actionItems -e call-session .` over the WHOLE phone-app checkout (~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/phone-app, which includes apps/sidecar, packages/*, worker/ and template-kit) returned ONLY DECISIONS.md lines 52, 226, 237, 239, 261 and 331, with zero hits in any .ts/.sql file. Falsifier: any hit in a phone-app source file. Measured: phone-app/packages/data/src/migrations.ts defines phone_calls (PK owner_id,id) and phone_scheduled_calls with no request key; apps/sidecar/src/calls.ts:442-476 builds the phone_calls record with id = roomName inside createCall, called from scheduling.ts:167 at join; scheduling.ts:66 `const id = randomUUID()` per schedule() call; .papercusp/blueprint.yaml is 4 lines (id, extends, knobs.testCommand).\nMeasured 2026-10-06 ~13:30Z by code read (su-64a5417a, P-009 / WI-10006461), canonical phone-app checkout ~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/phone-app (branch staging).\n\nRETRACTION / corrections to D-008 (my own decision, recorded ~13:12Z):\n1. D-008 called CallOutcome 'the existing CallOutcome ... through the one parse gate into call / call_action_item'. WRONG premise: CallOutcome and call_action_item exist ONLY as a documented contract in phone-app/DECISIONS.md (sections contract-shape and app-tables). There is no type, no parse gate, and no table in code. P-009 must BUILD them, not reuse them.\n2. D-008 said the durable call unit 'is the sidecar call row ... created at booking time'. The existing phone_calls row cannot be that: its id is the room name and it is created at JOIN (CallLedger.createCall / backend.unscoped.markJoined), with a status machine (dialing/live/completed/failed) that other code relies on. Creating it at booking would change that lifecycle.\n3. SchedulingService.schedule mints a random UUID per call, so a replayed booking request creates a second booking today. R-9 needs a booking idempotency key.\n4. phone-app's root .papercusp/blueprint.yaml is a 4-line stub with no roles or operations, so P-009 also declares the phone-agent worker role and the call-brief/call-wrap-up operations there (D-003 names the root blueprint as the projected source).\n\nRuling (refines D-008; everything else in D-008 stands):\na. The durable call unit is a NEW table phone_call_units, primary key (owner_id, call_key), call_key = scheduled:<scheduledCallId> | inbound:<roomName>. It links to the phone_calls row by call_id once one exists. It records brief handle/status/result, dial_claimed_at, session start/end and end reason, transcript segment count + sha256, wrap-up handle/status/error, and the parsed outcome.\nb. Booking replay: phone_scheduled_calls gains request_key with a unique index on (owner_id, request_key); schedule() with a known request key returns the existing booking. That gives one call unit, one call-brief request key, and one dial claim.\nc. P-009 adds the CallOutcome type, a single parseCallOutcome gate (a rejection is recorded on the unit and emitted, never silently dropped), and a phone_call_action_items table. Contract output lands in phone_calls (disposition, summary) and phone_call_action_items.\nd. Phone reaches the platform through a vendored copy of the generic pot-app-seam (the same byte-identical vendoring Email uses) over an HTTP tool invoker configured by PHONE_PLATFORM_INVOKE_URL. Without it the seam is disconnected: units still persist and the boot sweep submits once it is configured.\n\n### D-010 — P-009 verification scope: R-9 integration runs against a protocol-faithful in-test MCP operator; the live-operator leg and the wrap-up worker's transcript read path belong to P-010 / WI-10006699\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nMeasured by su-64a5417a (P-009 / WI-10006461).\n\nFacts:\n- R-9 names tests phone-app/apps/sidecar/src/durable-call.test.ts and durable-call.integration.test.ts and asks for an integration test 'against a real operation service with a fake dialer that counts dials'. Both files exist and pass (12/12 unit, 1/1 integration). The integration test boots the REAL sidecar (startPhoneServer) four times over one embedded Postgres, and submits through the REAL vendored pot-app-seam and the REAL HTTP MCP invoker (apps/sidecar/src/platform.ts). The operation service it talks to is apps/sidecar/src/test-blueprint-operator.ts: an MCP JSON-RPC endpoint that keeps the operator's stated replay contract (same request key + same input = one receipt; different input refused). It is not the Papercusp operator itself, because a phone-app test cannot boot the operator.\n- The call-wrap-up operation carries only transcriptRef {segmentCount, sha256} so private call content never enters a Papercusp work item (it would outlive D-022 call-content deletion). No route lets the phone-agent worker read the stored transcript: the sidecar serves it only behind owner sessions, and the worker's ceiling cannot reach the sidecar.\n\nRuling:\n1. P-009 is complete on the protocol-faithful operator above. The live-operator leg of the same flow (real blueprint:submit to the phone-app harness, blueprint_operation_invocations rows, restart replay) is verified in P-010, as P-010's text already requires for phone-app.\n2. The worker transcript read path is WI-10006699 (owner su-64a5417a), modelled on D-006's triggers:read-payload { workItemId }. Until it lands a live wrap-up is durable and submits once, but its worker cannot verify the transcript and must complete with notes and no outcome; the blueprint description says so.\n3. P-010's phone leg depends on WI-10006699 for a wrap-up that produces a CallOutcome.\nRelated: P-009, P-010\n\n### D-011 — P-006/P-007: the Calendar app submits meeting-prep itself (domain-derived key per event revision); the trigger binding is retired, not cut over to an operation-targeting binding\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDecided by su-64a5417a under AUTO (owner directive #1442, D-005 route), disclosed to the owner in the next report.\n\nProblem (measured by code read, 2026-10-06): P-007 requires the Calendar UI to show prep status from blueprint:status/result. Blueprint operation reads are strictly caller-scoped (packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-service.ts readCanonicalOperation refuses receipt.caller_id != caller; D-001: the handle is bound to the submitting caller and scope). Under P-006 as written, the operation-targeting binding submits as callerId 'trigger-binding:<bindingId>' with requestKey 'trigger-run:<runId>' and records the handle only in harness_shared.trigger_runs.outcome.blueprintOperation (binding-engine.ts ~1021-1040). The app is a different caller (its principal slug, agent-tools/blueprint/_operation-tool.ts:52-56), never receives the handle, and cannot read it. Bindings 5bbaba69 and 99387af7 have created_by = an agent session and pack_installation_id NULL, so there is no app-owned binding identity to delegate from.\n\nConsult conv-muwsfvxi-0000-2f2f3fa1fdb148e18cb6be30e8a21149 (answered from the plan author's own transcript, su-7f8d7809 session 9cd811f9): no read path for binding-submitted operations was ever designed; P-007 assumed a handle that P-006 gives to another caller, an authoring gap. A cross-caller read or a widened blueprint:list cuts against the parent plan's stated cross-consumer isolation requirement. Recommended: resolve it on the submit side.\n\nRuling:\n1. The Calendar app is the submitter of meeting-prep. Its ingest paths (POST /api/sync from the platform data producer, and Entry A /api/triggers/calendar) call blueprint:submit for operation 'meeting-prep' through the pot-app-seam client (P-002), with a domain-derived request key per event revision (eventId + start), for events with attendees inside the prep window. The app persists the returned handle with the event revision. Entry A's legacy seam.launchPlanRuns path is replaced by the same submit.\n2. Plan item text and acceptance bars for P-006 and P-007 (R-6, R-7) are revised to this shape before their evidence is bound.\n\nPremises to verify during implementation: (a) [measured] app-data-producer/live-sink.ts delivers every canonical event to the mapped app with no event-key filter (skips only no_app_for_source). (c) [inferred] an event-upcoming delivery re-pushes the row at lead time, which is when the window check first passes for a far-future event.\n\nAlternative rejected: binding submits as the app's principal. It needs an impersonation-capable binding field (auth/security surface) and still leaves the app unable to discover the trigger-run request key or handle without a new lookup read.\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-06\nAmendment-Id: amend-b74ff62ce4732b278eb98bb0\nRequest-Hash: 4ff14f9740c56eea32d2f22f6a85aaa004946ad8e2a2e0efb65afba39b36ebed\nActor: su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6\nReason: D-011 (plan app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06): meeting prep is submitted by the Calendar app itself under a key derived from the event revision; the armed launch-plan binding 5bbaba69 and its operation replacement 99387af7 are retired (detached 2026-10-06 15:28-15:29Z), and Google connect no longer re-creates the built-in binding (EI-25243055141955619). Check path only: R-7's condition, falsifier and method are unchanged.\nApproved-By: su-c750239f-5f46-4d6d-ba69-83a63457f35b\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1160178\nApproved-At: 2026-10-06T15:42:41.919Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 41 → 42\nChanged BARs: R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-014 — WI-10006699: operation private input — a transient, operation-scoped handoff the submitter attaches and only the holding worker reads; deleted at terminal state or TTL by the existing trigger-delivery retention sweep\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDecided by su-64a5417a under AUTO (owner directive #1442), disclosed in the next owner report. Amended 2026-10-06 ~16:25Z with as-built corrections (marked AS-BUILT).\n\nProblem (measured by code read, WI-10006699): the call-wrap-up worker must judge the call transcript, but the operation input deliberately carries only transcriptRef {segmentCount, sha256} so call content never lands in a work-item payload that outlives phone D-022's 30-day deletion. The phone-agent ceiling (work_items:read/write, memory:read) has no route to the sidecar, and no platform->app-sidecar call path exists. Consult conv-muwumlr3 (answered post 1160185 from the plan author's lineage) confirmed no operation-scoped private-input channel exists.\n\nRuling:\n1. A work-item-target operation may declare privateInputSchema. AS-BUILT: any JSON schema type (BlueprintOperationSchema.privateInputSchema = OperationJsonSchema), not only a top-level object; plan-target operations may neither declare nor receive it (invalid_request). blueprint:submit accepts privateInput only for a declaring operation (undeclared -> invalid_request; missing or schema-invalid -> invalid_payload) and stores it OUTSIDE the work item in harness_shared.blueprint_operation_private_inputs (migration 1401), keyed by the invocation's natural key (workspace, harness, caller, operation, requestKey), written before the work item is accepted. AS-BUILT storage: content_text TEXT holding the exact JSON.stringify text plus its sha256, never jsonb (jsonb reorders keys and normalizes whitespace, so a re-serialized read would not reproduce the hash). A replay with the same key and identical content is a no-op; different content is refused with refusal code input_conflict, message private_input_conflict.\n2. A new tool blueprint:read-private-input { workItemId } returns { content, sha256 } where sha256 is over the stored JSON.stringify(content) text. It refuses unless the caller currently holds that work item, the item is the target of an operation invocation, the item is not terminal, and the row has not expired or been deleted (private_input_not_operation / item_missing / not_holder / terminal / absent). AS-BUILT capability: work_items:read.\n3. Deletion: rows are deleted once their operation's work item is terminal or expires_at (7 days, under D-022's 30) has passed, by DBOS step operation-private-input-retention added to the existing 15-minute triggerDeliveryRetention workflow (no new scheduler). Reads refuse terminal items immediately, so the sweep only bounds physical lifetime.\n4. Phone. AS-BUILT: call-wrap-up's privateInputSchema is an ARRAY of [seq, speaker, text] tuples (CALL_WRAP_UP_PRIVATE_INPUT_SCHEMA; tuple length pinned by minItems/maxItems 3 because the operator validates draft-07, no prefixItems), not an object {segments}. The sidecar submits wrapUpTranscript(): the first transcriptRef.segmentCount segments by seq, re-hashed and required to equal transcriptRef.sha256, so a segment persisted after the end changes neither what is judged nor a replayed submit; if they no longer match (content deleted or rewritten) the stage fails phone_transcript_changed and nothing is submitted. transcriptRef.sha256 = sha256(JSON.stringify(tuples)) by transcriptDigest's construction (both share one tuple builder), so the worker verifies by comparing two strings. AS-BUILT correction: the phone-agent CEILING does not change; blueprint:read-private-input needs only work_items:read, already in the ceiling, so the phone blueprint adds the tool to dependencies.tools. pot-app-seam's BlueprintOperationDraft.privateInput is forwarded by submit; the vendored copies (email, calendar, phone-app, templates/papercusp-ops-pots) were synced.\n\nAlternatives rejected:\n- Read the agent_chats mirror (agent-chat-bridge.ts): it maps speaker to user/assistant (lossy), exists only for calls with a chat, and its appends are best-effort, so it cannot reproduce the pinned sha256.\n- Personal Vault datatype + delegated read: a persistent personal-data store with grant and disclosure machinery and no evidenced per-datatype retention; a call transcript is app-owned and needed only for the lifetime of one operation.\n- Transcript in the operation input with a scrub at terminal: rewrites a pinned, replay-hashed input.\nRelated: P-009, P-010\n\n### D-015 — P-005: one human-audience stranded draft (email WI-10000680) is held for the owner, not dropped by an agent\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-64a5417a, 2026-10-06 18:16Z, AUTO mode; disclosed to Avi in the next report]\n\nMeasured 18:15Z (operator DB, harness email, item_kind email-draft-proposal): 128 of the 129 stranded rows are dropped with the reason \"superseded: binding disarmed per owner 9/29; never executed\"; none of the population was ever claimed (first_claimed_at IS NULL on every row), so nothing executed.\n\nThe 129th, email WI-10000680 (\"Draft reply: [Papercusp/papercup] Run failed: .github/workflows/labeler.yml\"), has audience=human. work_items:set_state refuses agents on it with not_agent_work: the agent-work door gate (packages/operator-core/lib/work-nature/agent-work-door-gate.ts) reserves human-audience rows for their owner. That is a deliberate identity rail, not a defect, so no agent drops it and nobody routes around it (no owner-route impersonation, no raw SQL).\n\nIt is not silent: the P-005 guard itself raised open finding WI-10006677 (app-task-no-executor:papercusp-workspace/email/email-draft-proposal, count 1), which is exactly the R-5 \"newly stranded item raises a finding\" behaviour. The owner Queue path is exempt from the gate since WI-10005369 (done).\n\nOwner asked with options A/B/C in conv-muwuq80f (15:47Z); no answer yet. Under AUTO I take option B: P-005 closes with WI-10000680 held for the owner. R-5 handling: if the row is still open when the acceptance rubric is vetted, R-5 is amended to exempt human-audience rows the agent-work gate reserves for the owner, provided an open guard finding names them; if Avi drops it first (option A), no amendment is needed.\n\n### D-016 — P-004/P-010: email-draft-proposal becomes agent-audience work (supersedes the email-draft-proposal row of enterprise-data-sources-2026-10-01 D-007); the owner can overturn\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDecided by su-64a5417a under AUTO (owner directive #1442), disclosed to Avi in the next report with an explicit overturn option. This revises an OWNER-ratified row, so it is flagged, not silent.\n\nMeasured 19:07Z (operator DB + code):\n- work_items.audience is stamped at insert by trigger nature_stamp_from_registry_trg -> work_item_kind_nature(workspace, item_kind), which reads harness_shared.datatype_registry. No datatype manifest declares this kind's audience; the row comes only from migration 1318's named classification.\n- work_item_kind_nature('papercusp-workspace', k): email-draft-proposal = work/HUMAN; email-triage-proposal, calendar-meeting-prep, call-handling, crm-proposal = work/agent.\n- The feature-family claim UPDATE gates on audience='agent' (claim.ts ~L1126, P-009/D-024 of the nature plan); su-7f8d7809 measured work_items:complete refused not_agent_work on a blueprint-created human-audience item (WI-10006731).\n- Email's draft-reply and the second draft operation (email/.papercusp/blueprint.yaml L46, L104) target email-draft-proposal with execution {kind: agent, role: email-draft-worker}. The kind's own datatype blueprint (email/blueprints/email-draft-proposal) defines the same agent worker producing EmailDraftProposalSet. So no agent can ever execute an Email draft: 5 done before ~2026-08-28, none since.\n\nThe conflict: enterprise-data-sources-2026-10-01 D-007 [owner:Avi 2026-10-01, directive #1225, 'Q5. agreed'] classified email-draft-proposal as 'work, audience human (never agent-claimable)'. That premise matched the retired Gmail-binding flow, where the item sat in Avi's Queue for him to act on. Under this plan the human decision (review, then send) happens in the Email app on the operation's result; the work item itself is the drafting job, exactly like its sibling crm-proposal and email-triage-proposal, which are agent-audience.\n\nRejected: (a) a new agent-audience kind for the operation. It re-creates the two-contracts-for-one-concept defect the Email repo's datatype-contract-drift test exists to stop, and leaves the email-draft-proposal pot worker broken. (b) A platform exemption letting an applied worker claim human-audience items. That would hollow out 'human = never agent-claimable' for every kind.\n\nDecision: a forward migration sets datatype_registry audience='agent' for email-draft-proposal in every workspace. Existing rows are NOT restamped (the trigger fires only on item_kind/workspace/nature/audience updates), so the held WI-10000680 stays human-audience (D-015 unchanged). Fixtures that used email-draft-proposal as the canonical human-audience example (work-selection-census.ts, llm scenario S36) move to crm-escalation, which stays human. Safety: operation items remain claimable only by their applied worker (matchOperationWorkerClaim), so DRAIN agents cannot take an Email draft created by an operation. Residual risk: a non-operation email-draft-proposal item becomes agent-claimable; the only minting path for those is the disarmed Gmail binding b7976842.\n\nOverturn path: if Avi wants D-007 kept, revert the migration's row and route Email drafts through a separate agent-audience kind instead (option (a)).\n\n### D-017 — P-010 depends on WI-10006859: build automatic applied-worker placement for accepted agent operations (not a manual-launch descope)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDecided by su-64a5417a under AUTO (owner directive #1442) [turn:self]; disclosed in the next report.\n\nMeasured: 19:13Z (code read)\n- The applied worker for an accepted agent operation is bound only in packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-mcp/bootstrap-role.ts L316-327 (resolveAcceptedOperationWorkerBinding), which psu calls at startup for `psu --role <role> --feature <WI>`.\n- launch-su (routes/adv/launch-su.ts) accepts no role or feature; launchAgent (launch-agent.ts L331-361) sends neither; capability:launch-agent passes role but no feature. So no automated or agent-reachable door can start an applied worker.\n- routinesTick's accepted-root scan (dbos/routines-workflow.ts L1161-1185 -> coord-program-workflow.ts findUnstartedAcceptedCoordPrograms L361) starts execution.kind='program' only, and stamps program_started_at on every non-program receipt at once (L386-394).\n- Live: crm operation items WI-10006707 / WI-10006728 have sat unclaimed since 14:30/15:08Z.\n\nWhy build rather than descope: without placement, an app operation is admitted and never runs. D-011 retired the meeting-prep binding, so Calendar prep would stop entirely. The Goal says each run is 'executed with DBOS checkpointing'. A manual psu launch for the P-010 run would prove nothing an owner relies on.\n\nDesign (WI-10006859):\n1. launch-su accepts optional `role` + `feature` (both or neither; feature requires harness_slug) and passes `--role/--feature` to psu. launchAgent gains opts.role / opts.feature. bootstrap-role keeps sole authority to bind the applied worker, so no new trust path.\n2. A bounded placement step beside the program scan in routinesTick: select accepted work-item receipts whose pinned operation has execution.kind='agent', whose target item is non-terminal and unclaimed, with no live session already placed for that receipt, attempts < 3, and last attempt older than 10 min. Claim each with a conditional UPDATE ... RETURNING (new columns on blueprint_operation_invocations: agent_launch_attempts, agent_last_launch_at, agent_launch_owner_id), then launch headless via launchAgent. Bounded at 4 launches per tick and 4 live operation workers per workspace.\n3. Shipped default ON, with a registered kill-switch flag. After 3 failed attempts the receipt stops being placed; the P-005 stranded-task guard surfaces it.\n\nThe owner decision on cost: each operation costs one headless agent session. That is the plan's intended execution model, not a new spend category.\n\n### D-018 — Correction to D-016: migration 1407 DID restamp already-minted email-draft-proposal items to agent, including email WI-10000680; that item is dropped like its 128 siblings\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-64a5417a, 19:30Z, AUTO mode under owner directive #1442; disclosed to Avi in the next report with an overturn path]\n\nRETRACTION. D-016 and the header comment of migration 1407 say existing work_items rows keep their audience, so email WI-10000680 stays human. That was wrong. I inferred it from the work_items-side trigger (nature_stamp_from_registry_trg, which fires only on item_kind/workspace_id/nature/audience changes) and missed the registry-side trigger.\n\nMeasured 19:24-19:25Z:\n- datatype_registry carries restamp_work_items_on_registry_change (migration 1322), AFTER INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE OF nature, audience, work_item_kind, workspace_id. It nulls nature on every minted item of that (workspace, kind) whose stamp differs, and the BEFORE trigger re-derives it from the registry.\n- 1407 applied to the live DB at 19:21:19Z (schema_migrations).\n- email WI-10000680 now reads nature=work, audience=agent, status=open, taken_by=null.\n- The 1407 integration case failed on exactly this at L185 (expected human, got agent). It now asserts the restamp; testing:run test-run 20852844 passed 6/6.\nThis is a deliberate platform invariant (category derives from the registry), so I keep it rather than work around it. A status-only UPDATE still never restamps an item; only a registry change does. The 1407 file is applied and immutable (migration-immutability-guard), so its stale comment stays and THIS decision is the correction.\n\nCONSEQUENCE FOR D-015. D-015 held WI-10000680 for the owner because the agent-work door gate refused agents on a human-audience row. That premise no longer holds: the row is agent work, so leaving it open makes it an agent-audience task with no executor (no operation, binding disarmed 9/29), which is exactly the stranded class P-005 removes.\n\nDISPOSITION. Drop email WI-10000680 with the reason its 128 siblings carry (\"superseded: binding disarmed per owner 9/29; never executed\"). It is a 28-day-old draft reply to an automated GitHub Actions failure notification and was never claimed. This is option A from conv-muwuq80f, taken by me under AUTO instead of waiting on the owner. It is reversible: Avi can reopen it from the Queue, or run it as a real draft (option C). With the row dropped, R-5 needs no amendment, and D-015's planned R-5 exemption is moot.\nRelated: P-005, P-004, P-010\n\n### D-019 — D-017 as-built: placement reuses the consult-dispatch launch chain; eligibility requires a pinned worker identity and an uncancelled, non-human target\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, su-64a5417a, AUTO under owner directive #1442; disclosed in the next owner report]\nAS-BUILT corrections to D-017 (WI-10006859). D-017's design is superseded where it differs:\n\n1. NO launch-su / launchAgent change. Placement reuses the consult-dispatch launch chain (buildConsoleEnvelope -> buildAgentLaunchCommand -> spawnHeadless) with --role <op role> --feature <target WI>, in packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-agent-placement.ts (launchAgentOperationWorker). bootstrap-role keeps sole authority to bind the applied worker.\n2. Receipt columns from migration 1408 (agent_launch_attempts, agent_last_launch_at, agent_launch_owner_id, agent_placement_retired_at). The backfill retired the 27 receipts older than 72h so placement does not wake stale history.\n3. Step runs in routinesTick (dbos/routines-workflow.ts) behind FLAGS.BLUEPRINT_AGENT_OPERATION_PLACEMENT, default ON. Defaults: perWorkspaceLive 4, retryAfterSec 600, maxAttempts 3. A receipt is re-placed only after the window AND only when its previous worker is no longer live.\n4. Eligibility also requires (measured live 20:06Z, when receipt 38's worker died at bootstrap with 'has no pinned worker identity'):\n   a. the pinned operation has policy.identity (an object). Otherwise bootstrap-role can never bind the worker, so the receipt is retired, not launched.\n   b. the target item is not cancelled. Cancellation is work_items.payload.blueprintCancellation while the item stays open (EI-25262029104530277). A null/false mark is not a cancellation, the same reading as operation-service.\n   c. the target item is not human-audience. Such receipts are skipped but stay unretired, so a later reclassification makes them placeable.\n5. Proof: operation-agent-placement.integration.test.ts, 8/8 pass at 20:13Z (cases: basic claim, program op retired, retry window + liveness + maxAttempts, claimed/terminal target, per-workspace cap, launch failure, identity-less op retired, cancelled op retired with a null-mark control). lint:tsc clean over the 4 changed files.\n\n### D-020 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAmendment-Id: wi10007069-r3-check-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: 1e890aa366cb5256a38a6f5d78ac2b7246e56f0263ea9480eea56806faae76e3\nActor: su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6\nReason: Repair nonexistent pre-implementation Email check path by binding delivered operation-contract guard; no BAR, scope, evidence-plane, layer, or pass-rating change.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-bd5964d1-dd76-47db-9e36-5752b9ad12e4\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1161216\nApproved-At: 2026-10-07T02:59:59.825Z\nRubric revision: 6 → 7\nSubject plan revision: 54 → 55\nChanged BARs: R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-021 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAmendment-Id: wi10007069-r4-r5-r11-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: 0bee41dc135584d3e6adca1aaefb4760234e390312d4a13e41c1435cf0e42b45\nActor: su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6\nReason: Bind existing delivered guard tests instead of preimplementation placeholder names for R-4/R-5/R-11. Preserve all acceptance outcome text, falsifiers, scopes, evidence planes, layers and pass ratings.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-19eb98ed-72c3-4f75-b32e-193e4d81d0e7\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1161254\nApproved-At: 2026-10-07T03:17:51.928Z\nRubric revision: 7 → 8\nSubject plan revision: 55 → 56\nChanged BARs: R-4, R-5, R-11\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-022 — P-010 as-built placement preserves pinned model policy and selects its native backend\nDate: 2026-10-07\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-agent-placement.ts + operation-worker-binding.ts, launcher guard test_runs20878411, PG propagation20878408, binding selector20878381 @2026-10-07T03:24:56Z (current canonical staging source/local verification; not a runtime or deployment claim).\n\nWI-10007071 corrected D-019's placement launch chain: its SQL candidate now carries policy.model from the same immutable accepted specification, and the launcher reuses selectAcceptedOperationWorkerModel (the bootstrap validator) to select the native backend for the SAME first pinned model with the accepted effort. Unknown/unsupported pinned providers fail before spawning; no fallback model outside the policy is introduced, and onUnavailable wait/fail semantics are not converted into substitution. With no accepted model policy the historical Claude/no-model backend default remains unchanged. This does not globally switch agent defaults.\n\nPlaced workers explicitly use the existing account:auto inference gateway and matching envelope marker, rather than implicit one-account default routing. No new service, tool, table, flag or authorization seam: this extends existing placement fields and reuses the existing accepted-model validator and launch/account surfaces.\n\nProof: pre-fix controlled launcher20878360 failed3/4; final launcher20878411 passes4/4, selector20878381 passes12/12, real PG candidate policy propagation20878408 passes9/9; scoped typecheck clean. Still required for P-010: coordinated bg-host reload after the peer's native MCP tool-listing patch is ready, receipt41 reset and actual worker terminal/restart/UI acceptance. Local tests do not imply shipped status.\n\n### D-023 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAmendment-Id: wi10007078-batched-r12-r13-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: 3a24a9a1ffd2763671fe2cd55742eae4aa30fdb868e7d977cb43244316945708\nActor: su-64a5417a-71a9-4e19-b681-361a3a6ac4c6\nReason: Repair rev8 reviewer1161332/1161340 construction gaps: production real-PG finding/drop guard, explicit placement/native model policy and per-app live terminal/restart/Tauri BARs, replication instructions and manual R8 layer. Preserve original outcomes, pass ratings and evidence duties; no tree-only descope.\nApproved-By: su-1fe31ea9-f46b-4406-ab24-9e2e255d8916\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1161363\nApproved-At: 2026-10-07T04:36:35.772Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 59 → 60\nChanged BARs: R-5, R-8, R-12, R-13\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-024 — P-010 current-build readiness requires fixed tested inputs, not unrelated global HEAD stability\nDate: 2026-10-07\n[self-imposed, AUTO under directive #1442; conditional readiness clarification, no acceptance BAR change]\nMeasured: current rubric10 R12 replication requires current source provenance/test-run identities; R13 requires dev:pipeline_position route and runtime source identity. packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/__tests__/mcp-handler-gating-matrix.test.ts imports the real registry/transport stack, so its relevant imported closure extends beyond the three directly modified source files. Peer conversation conv-muxpu9c4 post1161510 reports testing:run uses a registered live checkout with before/after declared input fingerprints and no immutable snapshot.\nRuling: WI10007010 may use a maintained current-build run with an explicitly enumerated/protected full exercised source+test+config/dependency closure and measured identical inputs before/after, ledger-attributed result and exact source/test fingerprints. A global HEAD change consisting only of files outside that closure does not invalidate that narrowly scoped readiness evidence. Do NOT treat a three-file hash or HEAD alone as full closure proof, or infer immutable execution from the runner. A changed/unprotected/unmeasured exercised input makes readiness unknown. The peer retains choice of a stronger exclusive-window route if needed to meet these conditions.\nThis is source-development readiness only. P010 still independently proves actual serving runtime identity, real worker completion, restart/replay/no-duplicate side effects and all3 existing Tauri results. No permission to reload shared runtime/reset receipt41 before explicit readiness; no product/ship pass from this ruling.\nRelated: P-010\n\n### D-025 — P-010 as-built native Vitest environment freshness derives executed witnesses and independently remeasures current local runtimes\nDate: 2026-10-07\nMeasured: canonical packages/operator-core/lib/runtime-vintage.ts, plans/spec-evidence-store.ts, plans/bind-from-test-run.ts; libs/test-config/src/execution-details.ts, admin-test-runs-reporter.ts, vitest-config.ts; packages/operator-core/vitest.e2e.config.ts. Committed8f7048ce7dd1abd70ba1bf2391c4f4e52282ea6d/test-configb9f641a8fd10a244cdbd5947a9b5728b7082f20c. Maintained lint:as-committed exact snapshot passed395tests across8files, no skips/dirty,12:30-12:31Z2026-10-07. This is agent-authored as-built source evidence under owner1442 AUTO self route, not a BAR/scope/acceptance amendment or runtime/deployment claim. Existing repo-files measurement gains runtimeUnits selectors. Runtime-vintage measures local kernel process identity (caller pins stripped), valid source SHA and boot tuple; dead/reused/zombie, remote and legacy unpinned units are unproven. Registered Vitest config supplies a runtime reader; reporter captures strict runtimeEnvironmentBefore/After around execution with its own timestamps and a failsoft bounded reader. Canonical binder loads exact scoped test_runs.execution_details and derives environment ONLY from matching recorded witnesses/units. Current evidence read independently remeasures units and overrides caller-current fingerprints. Historical/incomplete/drifting execution pins remain unknown; never restamp them from runtime-at-bind. Native operational producer is still missing, and old restart record20893455 remains operational with unproven environment; it must not be relabeled e2e. Actual full app/Tauri runtime cohort, current-build containing runtime, new execution proof and independent shipment grade still remain. This decision preserves the existing live/deployed missing-environment guard and records the delivered mechanism only.\nRelated: P-010\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05","title":"Bug reports from users of apps built with Papercusp (follow-up to the unified bug pipeline)","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Bug reports from users of apps built with Papercusp (follow-up to the unified bug pipeline)\nslug: built-app-end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-16\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Draft retained. Preparation repaired on Oct16: durable acceptance BAR seed, feature-ship class, product shaping, relay reuse assessment, 16 active behavioral clauses and complete acceptance methods/replication at rubric revision 3. Spec-quality passes; plan lint has no errors. Existing relay/status/release foundations passed 37 tests at 25a4d82162. Intake integration did not execute: shared test PostgreSQL storage-headroom preflight refused writes (EI-26022982128227097). No product implementation, independent acceptance, relay deployment or parent shipment claimed.\n\n**Next:** Parent unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 must ship first under D-014. Then this execution owner re-reads as-built P-011/P-016 and original source conversation, runs the activation audit, resolves independent rubric vetting and report-only relay provisioning, and implements P-001 under WI-6554700010014272. Re-run the unexecuted intake integration after the supported test substrate has headroom; retain outside-lineage acceptance.\n\n## Product shaping\n\nAudience: builders of Papercusp apps and the people using those apps without a Papercusp installation.\n\nProblem: a builder-app user needs to report a defect into the builder's ordinary bug pipeline and learn when its fix ships, without the builder operating a separate reporting service.\n\nOutcome: the maintained feedback aspect supplies a report entry point; a Papercusp-hosted relay delivers consented reports to the builder pot; ordinary verification controls claimability; the reporter receives status on the reporting install.\n\nNon-goals: a second builder bug queue, a separate verification policy, default collection of contact details or attachments, a replacement for the parent intake/status thread, and bypassing the parent's shipment prerequisite.\n\nSource turns: session_turn:claude:e2ef1e52-d591-4b1f-9636-fbf4093924e8:0 (builder reports and unification), :4 (hosted relay), :9 and :14 (verification before claimability), :17 and :18 (encountered-agent evidence); parent D-013/D-014 and this plan D-001 carry reporter defaults and sequencing. Portfolio authorization session_turn:codex:01a13d6d-a7d4-7ad2-8c54-ebc7e7326525:38 changes execution authority only.\n\nScenarios:\n\n- A user of a freshly materialized app opens Report a problem, previews the captured screen state and sends a report with no builder setup; the builder sees it as an unverified candidate in the shared pipeline.\n- A reporter leaves contact and attachments unselected; the report remains anonymous and transmits no attachment. Consented attachments are redacted on the device and expire 90 days after close.\n- Repeated reports of one defect appear as a group with reporter count and verification state. A builder replies through the shared status thread; the reporting install receives the reply without requiring contact details.\n- A matching published release carrying the repair produces the fixed-in-version notice. A merely committed or tested repair does not establish shipment.\n- Invalid app identity or exhausted app quota prevents report admission without consuming another app's budget.\n\nPreparation boundary: this draft may acquire shaping, source-backed behavioral contracts and acceptance procedures now. Product activation and implementation remain subject to parent D-014: unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 ships first. Re-read its as-built intake P-011 and status P-016 before the activation audit. No source from this preparation asserts parent acceptance or deployed relay availability.\n\n## Purpose\n\nPeople who build apps with Papercusp need their own users to be able to report problems, and those reports should land in the same pipeline as agent-filed bugs: one intake, verified before claimable, with the reporter told when the fix ships. The parent plan builds that pipeline and reporting from the Papercusp desktop app; this plan extends it to apps built with Papercusp.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Builder apps collect user bug reports through the shared pipeline.** [owner:Avi 2026-10-05, session claude:e2ef1e52 turn 0; builder-app half of the parent plan's R-1] Anyone who builds with Papercusp can collect bug reports from their users, and those reports follow the same pipeline as agent-filed bugs.\n\n**R-2 — Hosted relay.** [owner:Avi 2026-10-05, owner-dialog answer \"Hosted relay (Recommended)\" in that session; parent plan R-2] Apps whose users do not run Papercusp send reports through a hosted relay; builders set up nothing.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Parent plan unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05 must ship first: its P-011 (one intake), P-006/P-007 (verification stage), P-013 (untrusted input) and P-016 (reporter status thread) are the foundation here.\n- Reporter defaults follow the parent plan's D-013: anonymous by default, contact only by opt-in, attachments only with consent and redacted on the device, attachments deleted 90 days after close; Papercusp hosts and pays for the relay with per-app quotas and rate limits.\n- Lineage: these items were end-user-bug-reports-2026-10-05 P-009..P-012 (su-4a152's draft), then parent P-018..P-021.\n\n## Design\n\n1. The relay is a thin hosted front for the parent plan's single intake; it adds per-app auth, quotas and rate limits, and nothing else.\n2. The papercusp-feedback aspect template gives every app root the same Report-a-problem widget; builders configure nothing.\n3. Builders see and answer reports through the parent plan's verification stage and status thread; no parallel builder queue.\n\n### Relay reuse assessment (pre-implementation)\n\nThe existing psu --connect transport has a hosted app-http plane in packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-app-relay.ts. It already forwards app traffic over the workspace's outbound connector, refuses non-app bearer credentials, stamps deny-only ingress provenance and enforces workspace rate/bandwidth controls. It is the transport candidate to extend; a second connector or agent orchestration system is not justified.\n\nIts current contract requires a live workspace connector and an app key authorized on the destination machine. Those facts do not establish the new report-only per-app admission policy, a safe public widget identity, per-app quotas, or a reporting route. A distributed feedback widget must not embed a builder's owner/admin credential or general app-tool key. Before implementation, settle the report-only credential/bootstrap seam against the parent intake and existing app registration surfaces. Preserve fail-closed authentication and the parent's untrusted-input verification.\n\nThe parent reporter-status implementation already derives fixed only from a matching published release receipt and current verified completion. Reuse this lifecycle interpretation and its install-scoped follow-up thread; no second status store or builder queue is needed. Existing foundations are code evidence, not proof that this plan's relay or template aspect is implemented or deployed.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002, P-003, P-004 | live |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-004 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1: relay and template\n\n- **P-001** `blocked` Hosted report relay (was parent P-018): per-app auth, abuse and rate limits, retention per the parent D-013; design doc first; evaluate extending the existing psu --connect relay before building a new one; reports enter the parent plan's single intake. — note: ← WI-6554700010014272 blocked (1 external blocker)\n- **P-002** `todo` Aspect template papercusp-feedback (was parent P-019): Report-a-problem widget (desktop menu, mobile shake-to-report) composing onto the app roots templates:list returns; relay to the builder pot through papercusp-ops-pots; captures URL-held UI state; guide and template checks. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 2: builder view and acceptance\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Builder view (was parent P-020): grouped reports with reporter counts and verification state; replies to reporters through the parent plan's status thread (its P-016). blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` End-to-end (was parent P-021): a freshly materialized template app files a report that reaches the builder pot, is verified, fixed, and the reporter gets the fixed-in-version notice. blocked-by: P-002, P-003\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- A user of a freshly materialized template app can report a problem with no builder setup, and the report reaches the builder's pot through the shared intake.\n- The report is verified before it is claimable, exactly like an agent-filed bug.\n- The reporter is told when the fix ships, without having given contact details unless they opted in.\n- Relay cost is bounded per app by quotas and rate limits.\n\n## Acceptance procedure\n\nThis is a pre-implementation verification plan. It is not a claim that any scenario has passed. Independent final acceptance and relay credential/provisioning authority remain separate from implementation.\n\n1. Before activation, re-read the original owner conversation, parent D-013/D-014, as-built P-011/P-016 checkpoints and the parent's shipment record. Complete the source-to-requirement activation audit; keep this plan draft until the ship-first prerequisite is met. Read templates:list at execution time and enumerate every applicable app-scope root rather than assuming a remembered roster.\n2. For focused relay/intake/status behavior, use the current build selected by dev:pipeline_position for the actual owning runtime and test class. Run registered project tests with npm run test:file -- <actual test paths>. Bind passing and mutation/counterexample evidence to exact source/spec revisions; a typecheck is insufficient.\n3. For R-1, materialize fresh apps from each applicable maintained root plus the feedback aspect. Drive desktop UI through Tauri and the mobile root's supported device harness. Send an anonymous report containing a distinctive URL-held state from a user without Papercusp. Verify its source identity reaches only the designated builder pot and enters the shared verification queue. Attempt claim before reproduction and again after verification. Submit a matching report from another install and inspect grouping, reporter count and current verification state.\n4. Exercise preview consent with contact, screenshots and logs unselected; inspect outbound payloads. Repeat with explicit selection and known redaction markers. Verify no unselected attachment or non-opted-in contact is sent and no unredacted marker leaves the reporting device. Close a report and exercise the exact 90-day attachment-retention boundary.\n5. Reply anonymously through the shared status thread and observe the reply on the originating install. Complete a real verification and repair. Confirm the install shows awaiting release before publication, rejects an unrelated artifact as fixed evidence, then displays the fixed-in-version notice for the published artifact containing that repair. Preserve exact install, item, verification, completion, release and artifact evidence references.\n6. For R-2, verify the actual Papercusp-hosted relay endpoint with a valid app and a user without Papercusp; record deployment identity and the target builder pot. Exercise missing/invalid/cross-app identity, quota exhaustion and a second app with remaining budget. Confirm invalid requests admit no report and one app cannot consume another's budget. Provisioning credentials stay in injected external configuration; no secrets enter this plan or the repository.\n7. The independent grader checks the full app-root population, negative controls, current evidence fingerprints and shipped relay artifact. A fixture-only release receipt or local relay test does not prove R-2's deployed outcome. Evidence on the current build supports implementation; final shipment evidence uses the exact shipped artifact. Do not claim parent shipment, independent acceptance or relay deployment from this preparation.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Hosted relay, paid by Papercusp, with the parent plan's reporter defaults\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05, owner-dialog answer \"Hosted relay (Recommended)\" in session claude:e2ef1e52; carried from parent D-002] Apps whose users do not run Papercusp report through a hosted relay and builders set up nothing. [decided by su-93aaa593 under Avi's #1364 delegation; parent D-013] Papercusp hosts and pays for the relay, with per-app quotas and rate limits bounding cost; reports are anonymous by default with opt-in contact, attachments only with consent and redacted on the device, and attachments deleted 90 days after the item closes.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06","title":"Friendly cloud portal documentation and a shared FAQ for Papercup","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Friendly cloud portal documentation and a shared FAQ for Papercup\nslug: cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-18\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** [turn:self] Fleet successor su-9998b763 now holds P-006/WI-10006920 and P-007/WI-10006921; predecessor released both and delivery WI-10006846.
