Production is need… <!-- P-010 -->\n## Background\n\nThe supplied conversation raised confusing terminology, an infrastructure-heavy first experience, cost/privacy/data questions and the value of an FAQ inside documentation. Its statements about plan status are historical context, not completion evidence.\n\nVerified starting points:\n- `public-docs-portal-readiness-2026-10-01` is shipped. Its Design reuses the public manual in `apps/papercusp-docs`, Astro/Starlight/Pagefind and the portal's existing Docs destination. Improve this foundation; do not create another documentation website.\n- Existing public pages cover quickstart, using the app, accounts/billing, cloud workspaces, workspaces/agents, plans, voice, plugins, remote access, snapshots and troubleshooting. The cloud page already distinguishes Papercusp Cloud from customers' own Google Cloud/AWS accounts, but also includes advanced infrastructure details.\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/search.ts` currently routes to project, harness or privileged engineering sources. `agents/docs-retrieval` describes the public manual as a human surface rather than a first-class agent scope. Verify actual Papercup wiring and provide safely scoped access to the same public FAQ; merely telling a prompt to read it is insufficient.\n- `apps/papercusp-docs/scripts/source-contract.mjs` checks guide coverage, concrete source anchors, links and exclusion of internal-doc links. `packages/operator-core/lib/harness/docs/public-manual-drift.test.ts` proves existing anchored manual-doc changes request review, not automatic semantic approval.\n- Current reads found `agentic-docs-qa-2026-07-06` awaiting-acceptance, `ship-precomputed-doc-vectors-2026-10-01` ready, and `tutorial-polish-and-docs-search-2026-07-04` draft. Their stored Now text is not authority to resume them. Inspect current decisions and proof before reusing unfinished capabilities.\n\n## Scope and constraints\n\nTwo workstreams: improve cloud portal user documentation; add a Common questions/FAQ section to that same manual and make actual Papercup chat use it for system questions.\n\nKeep public product docs, authenticated Project docs and internal engineering material separate. Public authored MDX remains canonical; any agent index is a generated projection, not another independently maintained answer store.\n\nPreserve Papercup's ability to answer arbitrary questions using authorized deeper documentation/code. Static FAQ answers cannot establish current account state, prices, installed features, permissions or workspace status.\n\nOut of scope: desktop startup improvements, backup incidents, a new docs platform, providing free/ready-made workspaces, changing hosting/billing/permissions, or rewriting the tutorial engine. Docs should link the relevant tutorial and use consistent terms; tutorial behavior changes need separate approval.\n\nDo not publish secrets, private conversations, tenant content or internal operational details. Use permission-appropriate, redacted examples. Reuse existing source-linked freshness/review mechanisms, not a new parallel cron/service.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Plain-language explanations.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Begin with the user's goal and expected result. Explain what to click, what happens next and how to recover, using exact current UI labels. Define unavoidable terms once and put advanced details behind progressive disclosure. Friendlier wording must preserve accurate cost/destructive-action warnings.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each changed public page opens with the user's goal and expected result, names exact current UI controls and expected transitions, defines unavoidable terms, reveals advanced details progressively, and retains accurate cost and destructive-action warnings.\",\"falsifier\":\"A novice cannot follow the first-task instructions, labels differ from the current UI, jargon is unexplained, or a warning is inaccurate/removed.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-1 — Plain-language explanations.\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Review the changed public pages against exact current portal labels, the page pattern and human-onboarding-copy-quality rubric. Preserve source-backed billing/deletion caveats. A readable source diff alone does not establish comprehension. Open the current-build walkthrough record at docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/walkthrough.md; record build id, each UI label and warning source, and pass/fail observations. Novice comprehension is rated only by R-8. D-002 governs warning accuracy. D-001..D-004 are proposed plan rules carried under D-006's AUTO approval, not direct owner quotations. A missing walkthrough artifact rates unknown. Each listed first-task flow must have a recorded fresh-user or scripted label-asserting run in the applicable runtime; capture exact current UI labels, not a prose-only review.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Complete everyday journeys.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Cover account/organization selection, choosing and connecting a workspace, a small first task and checking its result, approvals/permissions, costs and stopping/deleting, data/privacy/credentials, and common errors/support. Distinguish portal versus desktop and managed versus customer-owned cloud where behavior differs.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The public manual provides a followable source-checked path for account and organization selection, workspace connection, a first task and its result, approvals, costs and stop/delete, data/privacy/credentials, and common errors/support, with applicable portal/desktop and managed/own-cloud distinctions.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any listed journey is absent, cannot be followed in its applicable runtime, or conflates browser/desktop or managed/customer-owned hosting.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-2 — Complete everyday journeys.\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Walk each listed everyday journey on the current portal build and compare documentation with the actual controls and authorized behavior. Review browser/desktop and managed/own-cloud distinctions against code and public guide sources. Open the current-build walkthrough record at docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/walkthrough.md with build id and journey dispositions. Novice comprehension is rated only by R-8. D-001..D-004 are proposed plan rules carried under D-006's AUTO approval, not direct owner quotations. A missing walkthrough artifact rates unknown. The artifact includes a fresh-user or scripted label-asserting run of each listed journey in its applicable runtime and captures the exact UI labels.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Findable portal help.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Preserve the existing Docs entry and add a clear Start here path, task-based guide groups and visible Common questions. Search and stable deep links work, with keyboard/mobile/theme usability. Public Docs and Project docs must remain distinguishable.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Readers can reach Start here, task-based guides and Common questions from the existing Docs destination, use search and stable deep links with keyboard/mobile/theme support, and distinguish public Docs from Project docs.\",\"falsifier\":\"Start here/FAQ are unreachable, search/deep links fail, a keyboard/mobile/theme check fails, or public Docs is confused with private Project docs.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-3 — Findable portal help.\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Extend public-docs.test.ts with FAQ/Start here/source-contract link assertions, build Astro/Starlight/Pagefind and exercise public navigation, search, stable anchors, keyboard, narrow viewport and both themes on the current build. Record browser observations and keep public/project destinations distinct. Open docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/walkthrough.md for current-build keyboard/mobile/theme results and Pagefind queries. D-001..D-004 are proposed plan rules carried under D-006's AUTO approval, not direct owner quotations.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/public-docs.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Reviewed FAQ inside documentation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Start with at least 20 source-checked answers, prioritizing permission-appropriate real user/support questions. Each has a stable public anchor, common alternate wording, a short plain answer, relevant caveats and a fuller-guide link. Sensitive factual claims require appropriate review. Where user-question evidence is unavailable, label seed questions as proposed rather than pretend they are observed demand.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Common questions contains at least 20 source-checked reviewed answers with stable public anchors, alternate wording, short plain answers, relevant caveats and fuller-guide links, with sensitive claims reviewed and unobserved seed-question demand labeled proposed.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fewer than 20 reviewed entries exist or any entry lacks the specified anchor/answer/caveat/guide link/source review; proposed demand is represented as observed.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-4 — Reviewed FAQ inside documentation.\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Review at least 20 FAQ entries with concrete source anchors, stable anchors, alternate wording, short answers, caveats and valid fuller-guide links. Keep proposed seed questions labeled if no permission-appropriate user-question evidence exists. Record billing/privacy/security review and maintainer status. Extend public-docs.test.ts with automated entry count, metadata, anchors and guide-link assertions; the named source-review and proposed-demand record is docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/faq-review.md. D-001/D-004 govern the single source and existing seams; D-006 labels the twenty-entry target as agent-derived. D-001..D-004 are proposed plan rules carried under D-006's AUTO approval, not direct owner quotations.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/public-docs.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Actual Papercup consumption.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Conceptual system questions search the FAQ first, then the fuller public manual, then authorized deeper sources when needed. Natural paraphrases and ordinary misspellings work. Ambiguous/no matches do not force a canned answer. Fresh sessions/installations and the deployed portal chat can access the same content without privileged engineering access or manual index setup.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Conceptual questions in actual fresh and deployed Papercup sessions retrieve relevant canonical FAQ context first, then the fuller public manual and authorized deeper sources when needed, with paraphrase and misspelling support, appropriate ambiguous/no-match fallback, and no privileged access or manual index setup.\",\"falsifier\":\"A conceptual question fails to reach the public FAQ in an actual fresh portal chat, paraphrases fail, no-match forces an answer, or retrieval needs privileged setup.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-5 — Actual Papercup consumption.\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Extend maintained docs routing and Papercup context tests with the public manual/FAQ scope, query paraphrases and misspellings, FAQ-first retrieval, fuller-guide fallback, no-match and fresh-source cases. Exercise an actual fresh portal chat runtime with authorized sources; record the loaded content revision. Rate retrieval and reach only from named case groups: FAQ-first, fuller-guide fallback, two paraphrases per seed, ordinary misspellings, ambiguous/no-match, and fresh-session/install. Actual fresh-chat proof is docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/chat-cases.md with loaded content revision, and remains unknown until it exists; deployed proof is R-9. D-003 governs concept/live distinctions. D-001..D-004 are proposed plan rules carried under D-006's AUTO approval, not direct owner quotations.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/__tests__/routing.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/papercup/papercup-context.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Truthful, safe answers.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Papercup returns concise plain-language answers with relevant public references. Current cost/account/feature/workspace-state questions need live authorized evidence. Stale, conflicting, missing or unavailable evidence triggers explanation and safe verification/fallback, not fabricated certainty. FAQ prose cannot grant permissions or override agent instructions, and retrieval must not expose private documentation.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Papercup's concise answers cite relevant public references, support current facts with live authorized evidence, disclose stale/conflicting/missing/unavailable evidence, preserve agent instructions and permissions against retrieved prose, and do not reveal private documentation.\",\"falsifier\":\"Papercup fabricates a current fact, conceals missing/conflicting evidence, follows instructions from FAQ text, or reveals private documentation.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-6 — Truthful, safe answers.\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Extend maintained routing and Papercup context regressions with tenant/private boundaries, FAQ prompt injection, live-state versus conceptual questions, stale/conflicting evidence and unavailable retrieval. Run actual chat cases to check concise public references and uncertainty; static FAQ content cannot prove live state. Rate source-safety and answer-truth groups only: public/private boundaries, prompt injection, live-state evidence, stale/conflicting context, outages/missing index and unavailable sources. Actual answer observations are docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/chat-cases.md and remain unknown until recorded; deployed proof is R-9. D-003 governs live evidence. D-001..D-004 are proposed plan rules carried under D-006's AUTO approval, not direct owner quotations. The maintained source-isolation fixture in routing.test.ts seeds one public-manual sentinel fact and one private engineering/project sentinel fact; in the SAME successful run assert that the public fact is retrieved and the private fact is absent. An empty or broken retrieval response cannot pass the negative check.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/docs/__tests__/routing.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/papercup/papercup-context.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Maintenance and accountable review.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"FAQ pages reuse concrete source anchors, source contracts and existing drift/review machinery. Record maintainer, review status and content revision; a behavior change updates the guide and FAQ together. Content/index changes invalidate caches. Billing/privacy/security claims receive appropriate review; detected drift alone is not semantic approval.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"FAQ content carries accountable maintainer, review status, revision metadata and concrete source anchors, with relevant behavior changes updating guide/FAQ together and content/index revisions invalidating caches without treating drift as semantic approval.\",\"falsifier\":\"A relevant source or content revision leaves the FAQ/index/cache stale without review, or billing/privacy/security lacks accountable review.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-7 — Maintenance and accountable review.\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Extend public-manual-drift and freshness-sweep regressions to prove FAQ source registration requests review on source change and content/index changes invalidate projections/caches. Verify maintainer/review/revision fields and that drift is not semantic approval. Rate source revision and cache invalidation groups; open docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/faq-review.md for maintainer and billing/privacy/security review. D-001/D-004 govern existing review seams. D-001..D-004 are proposed plan rules carried under D-006's AUTO approval, not direct owner quotations. Source isolation is rated only by R-6, whose named routing.test.ts fixture requires a retrieved public-manual positive control beside a seeded private-source negative control in the same run; this bar rates only source revision, cache invalidation and accountable review.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/docs/public-manual-drift.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/docs/freshness-sweep.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Tests and non-technical validation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Add real regression tests to maintained test/agent-behavior/browser frameworks. Cover retrieval, paraphrases, no-match fallback, source revision changes, stale/conflicting answers, live-state questions, outages/missing index, fresh installs, public/private boundaries and prompt injection. Observe non-technical users and fix confusion before acceptance.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a111ed-32ce-7be3-9144-c900e8c63797:5\",\"cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06#D-006\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Three real non-technical participants complete at least 10 of 12 observed four-task attempts without coaching or misunderstanding billing responsibility, privacy boundaries or destructive actions, with observed confusion repaired before independent acceptance.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fewer than three participants or 12 task attempts are observed, fewer than 10 tasks succeed without coaching, a participant misunderstands billing/privacy/deletion, or observed confusion remains unrepaired before acceptance.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredScope\":[\"R-8 — Tests and non-technical validation.\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Observe the three-participant four-task novice study, retaining exact task outcomes and repairs; require at least 10/12 successes without coaching and no critical misunderstanding. Open docs/evidence/cloud-portal-docs-and-papercup-faq-2026-10-06/novice-study.md with consent-appropriate participant identifiers, four agreed tasks, individual outcomes, coaching, misunderstandings, confusion and repairs. Rate unknown until three real participants are observed. D-006 records three-by-four and ten-of-twelve as agent-derived thresholds, not performed observations. Maintained scenario-matrix proof is mandatory under R-5/R-6/R-7, with unit, integration, browser and agent-behavior evidence; R-8 rates only novice outcomes. No deployed served-artifact probe or no loaded-runtime/content revision means unknown; a source-tree hash or deployment assertion alone cannot pass.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### User manual\n\nExtend the existing public manual and maintained portal/Starlight primitives. Proposed groups: Start here; Everyday tasks; Cloud and costs; Privacy and access; Common questions; Troubleshooting. Confirm grouping/terminology against current UI rather than invent new product words.\n\nPage pattern: what this helps you do; before you start; short numbered steps; expected result; recovery; related next page. Add current redacted screenshots only where they clarify a choice. Show the useful first-task outcome before infrastructure explanation, but document only hosting options the account actually offers; do not promise ready/free workspaces.\n\n### Shared FAQ\n\nSuggested question candidates: what Papercusp/Papercup/workspaces are; where work runs; browser versus desktop; closing the browser; managed versus own-cloud hosting; subscription versus model versus cloud-provider costs; stop versus delete and remaining charges; data access/storage; credentials; approval rules; backups/recovery; mistakes; progress/interruptions; plugins; cloud setup failures; support. These are priorities to validate, not preapproved factual answers.\n\nEach entry has a short answer and direct public guide link. Reuse existing retrieval to match alternate phrasing, adding minimal metadata only where necessary. No duplicated FAQ service, prompt corpus or independent answer database.\n\n### Retrieval and active behavior\n\nExtend `@papercusp/docs-engine` and existing docs-tool/context routing with the smallest explicit read-only public-manual scope needed. Preserve existing project/harness scoping and engineering authorization; do not repoint a global environment variable or loosen access to make the FAQ readable. Reuse lexical/semantic search, deployment/index packaging and revision-aware caches, with lexical fallback when embeddings are unavailable.\n\nTrace actual portal Papercup chat, brain and deep-answer paths. Read the canonical prompt-source runbook before modifying the active policy through existing prompt/blueprint mechanisms. A standalone docs-QA-agent update or a generated/materialized prompt edit does not satisfy this integration. Inject a small retrieval policy and pointers, not the entire FAQ on every turn.\n\nConceptual question -> relevant reviewed FAQ -> fuller public guide -> authorized deeper docs/code if needed. Live-state question -> authorized live lookup, with FAQ as explanatory context only. Use plain answers, relevant public references and explicit uncertainty/conflict handling. Preserve current approvals and arbitrary questions.\n\n### Maintenance and acceptance\n\nRegister FAQ content in the existing namespaced manual-doc source coverage and review pipeline. Relevant source changes request review; content/index revisions invalidate answer caches. Reuse maintained tests/CI. For necessary portal UI changes, component-registry search precedes the UI spec and existing primitives take priority.\n\nProposed behavioral fixture: at least 20 FAQ questions with two natural paraphrases each, plus negative/security/current-state cases. Expected claims and allowed sources are explicit; wording may vary. Record privacy-preserving source/retrieval metadata, not private user text by default.\n\nProposed usability bar for Avi's review: three non-technical participants attempt four tasks each—find the first-task guide, distinguish hosting options, explain billing and stop/delete, and ask Papercup a common question. At least 10/12 succeed without coaching, with no misunderstanding of destructive actions, privacy boundaries or billing responsibility. This is a proposed target, not a claim that testing has happened.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-009 | live |\n| R-9 | P-010 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline and reader experience\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit the portal Docs journey, existing user manual, real Papercup retrieval/prompt paths, source ownership and related-plan decisions/proof. Any portal edit belongs in its own canonical harness source with a registered lane/locks, not an assumed sibling worktree.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — One documentation source\n\nProposed: Common questions is part of the public manual. Papercup retrieves the same canonical answers; no independent FAQ service, duplicated prompt corpus or new docs site.\n\n### D-002 — Friendliness without inaccurate promises\n\nProposed: improve words, ordering and examples, not guarantees. Estimates must be labeled/sourced. Stopped resources are not automatically free, and credentials/deletion/recovery require truthful instructions.\n\n### D-003 — FAQ first for concepts; live evidence for live facts\n\nProposed: FAQ is the preferred conceptual starting point, not authority over current configuration/state or security permissions. Authorized code investigation remains available for questions it cannot answer.\n\n### D-004 — Extend existing mechanisms\n\nProposed: reuse docs navigation, retrieval, indexing and drift review. A public-manual scope is a minimal extension of the existing retrieval seam, not a parallel system; confirm exact design during P-001/P-005.\n\n### D-005 — Draft only\n\nRecorded boundary: Avi requested this plan, not implementation. No extra agents launched.\n\n\n## Goal\n\nBuild the CRM and sales/onboarding tooling as Papercusp apps, the same way Email, Calendar and Phone are built. **Agents are the sales and onboarding team; Avi supervises.**\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Shared relationship graph.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Build the CRM on one shared record of people, companies and interactions that the Email, Calendar and Phone apps already feed, not a CRM-owned contact list.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:0\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:9cd811f9-6b57-4675-9ace-f71a25897120:6\",\n      \"D-001\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Email messages, calendar events and Phone calls for the same person resolve to one platform person record with three interaction records, every field carries source, observed-at and accepted-by provenance, the CRM app stores no contact table of its own, and the team view receives interaction metadata only unless a body is explicitly shared.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An Email, Calendar or Phone interaction that produces no graph interaction, a duplicate person for the same email or phone, a field without provenance, a CRM-owned contact table, or a message body visible in the team view without an explicit share.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"passRatings\": [\n      \"healthy\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"role\": \"outcome\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read the graph datatypes and their Vault ingestion routes, then run the integration test: it ingests one Email, one Calendar and one Phone fixture for the same person and asserts a single merged person, three interactions, provenance on every field and metadata-only team visibility. Search the CRM app source for any contact table.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n for managing customers and sales tools to mange the marketing and sales process. I want to build these tools as apps built on top of papercusp like our email calendar and phone app\".\n- [owner:Avi 2026-10-06 #1424] \"I'll also want agents to run the onboarding, i.e. agents should schedule calls with users, and be the ones to sell the product\".\n- [owner:Avi 2026-10-06 #1433] \"Your recommendations look good. Make sure that the agent tasks are built on top of papercusp's durable workflow system\".\n- [owner:Avi 2026-10-06 #1434] \"write 2 plans ... one to create our crm/sales apps like you recommendeded\".\n- [owner:Avi 2026-09-29 #869] No auto-composed draft replies for synced email. This governs the Email app; the CRM agent sends only from its OWN identity, under a separately granted and scoped authority (D-002, P-013).\n\n## Design summary (as recommended 2026-10-06 and approved \"Your recommendations look good\")\n\n1. **The CRM does not own contacts.** People, organizations and interactions are a platform-level graph. A canonical `contact` datatype already exists; Email has its own contacts surface and contact-frequency projection; Phone has its own `contact` entity. The CRM adds deals, stages, lists, notes and onboarding state on top, keyed to the graph's ids.\n2. **Nobody types records in.** Timelines build themselves from emails, meetings, call transcripts, action items and product usage.\n3. **Every value shows its source**: where it came from, when, and who accepted it. Nothing is silently overwritten.\n4. **Every agent task is a durable blueprint operation** (D-003). Outputs reach CRM tables only through the app's parse gate.\n5. **Each customer's onboarding is a plan run from an app-owned template.** Milestones are measured from telemetry, not from the agent's report.\n6. **Team data vs personal data.** By default the shared CRM receives interaction metadata. Message bodies reach it only through an explicit grant recorded in the Vault disclosure ledger.\n7. **The home screen is a supervision console**: review queue, escalations, live and recent calls, and per-agent conversion, activation and cost.\n\n## Same as existing tools (table stakes)\n\n- People, companies and deals with custom fields (flexible like Attio)\n- Pipelines with board and table views, and saved filtered lists\n- Tasks, notes and reminders\n- CSV import, duplicate merging, full export\n- Gmail and Google Calendar sync\n- Sequences that stop on a reply, out-of-office or bounce\n- Reports: stage conversion, time in stage, source attribution\n- Unsubscribe, opt-out and suppression lists (CAN-SPAM/GDPR)\n\n## Different from existing tools\n\n- The CRM reads data Papercusp apps already hold, instead of being a separate system everything connects to.\n- Agents sell and onboard; people supervise.\n- Agent work is fully auditable: queue, cost, grade, rejections.\n- Stage changes are proposed from evidence, with links.\n- Outreach is low volume and researched per person, from a disclosed AI identity.\n- Local-first or BYOC, in your own Postgres, with easy export.\n\nHonest caveat: automatic email/calendar capture is now table stakes (Attio, folk, Day.ai, Lightfield), and the first wave of AI sales bots mostly earned a reputation for spam. Our edge is the shared graph across apps, graded and auditable agent work, agents that actually set up the product, and data ownership.\n\n## Reuse (check before building)\n\n- **App root:** `templates:list` → the \"Papercusp Official: App\" root (`agents: pots`, plus data-sync and search). Materialize with `templates:new-app`; never scaffold by hand.\n- **Durable agent tasks:** `blueprint:submit/status/result/events/cancel/signal/resume` from `blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23`, plus the pot-app-seam blueprint client from `app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06`.\n- **Onboarding plans:** the Agentic Work Plane template (app-owned plan templates → canonical work-item DAG → stable app agent).\n- **In-product onboarding:** `agent-first-onboarding-2026-07-03` (concierge plus agent tutor in the Onboarding Console). The CRM's in-app onboarding EXTENDS it so tutor milestones report into the customer's onboarding plan run. Never build a second onboarding agent.\n- **Grading:** rubrics and scorecards.\n- **Disclosure:** the Personal Vault disclosure ledger.\n- **Checkout:** the portal app's billing.\n- **Telemetry:** PostHog.\n- **Signups:** papercusp.com's Cloudflare KV signup capture.\n- **Pipeline prior art:** `fundraise-automation-2026-08-23` (WI-41077: one plan per active investor conversation, the Workflows tab as the CRM board, the trigger-activity feed as the log). Evaluate it before designing deal objects.\n\n## Dependencies\n\nCross-plan dependencies on `app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06` (that plan's item ids in parentheses):\n\n- The seam blueprint client (its P-002) lands before this plan's agent operations (P-010 here).\n- Phone's durable call unit (its P-008 and P-009) lands before agent voice onboarding (P-017 here).\n- The template default for durable operations (its P-011) lands before this app is materialized (P-005 here).\n- Calendar on durable execution (its P-006) lands before agent scheduling (P-016 here).\n\n`blueprint-backed-work-item-execution-2026-09-23` must be shipped before this plan's final acceptance.\n\n## Don't build (D-007)\n\nAd management, a landing-page builder, a HubSpot-style visual workflow builder, CPQ/quoting, territories and quotas, or a newsletter delivery engine. Integrate those services and pull their signals into the graph.\n\n## Open questions (owner — resolved in P-001)\n\n1. What may agents commit to without a human: list-price plans, trials, discounts, refunds, roadmap dates, SLAs, security/legal terms? Recommended starting point: list-price self-serve plans and standard trials only; everything else escalates.\n2. Just Avi at first, or multi-user from day one? This sets the tenancy and disclosure work in P-004/P-005.\n3. App target: desktop + web like Email/Calendar (recommended, since a CRM is team-shared and needs the multi-user web host), or web only?\n4. Which mailbox domain and phone number the agent identity uses (P-013).\n\n\n## Design\n\nThe design is the Design summary, Reuse and Phase sections below; this table binds each acceptance requirement to the items that deliver it.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Items | Evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-005, P-006, P-007 | live |\n| R-3 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-008, P-009, P-011, P-012, P-021 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-015, P-016, P-017, P-018 | live |\n| R-6 | P-013, P-014, P-019, P-020, P-022, P-023 | live |\n| R-7 | P-024 | live |\n\n## Phase 0 — Foundations\n\n- **P-001** `done` Get Avi's answers to the plan's four open questions, in one ask: (1) what agents may commit to without a human; (2) single-user first vs multi-user from day one; (3) app target, desktop + web vs web only; (4) the agent identity's mailbox domain and phone number. Agent decision by su-7f8d7809 under AUTO [owner:Avi 2026-10-06 #1441 \"carry the plan to shipped yourself\"]; not an owner statement.\n\n(1) Canonical rows, no new table: each real person/organization is ONE work_items row of the same datatype with a deterministic id PER-<digest> / ORG-<digest>, created by 'relationship-graph:resolver', provider 'relationship-graph', externalId = its own id (so it satisfies the datatype's payload_schema). A merge keeps the oldest id and retires the younger with mergedInto (readers follow it, getCanonicalEntity); a split leaves the id with the majority side; a new id is minted only from a cluster's oldest member.\n(4) Merge policy: an accepted value (acceptEntityField, acceptedBy) outranks every observation; else the most recently observed scalar; lists (emails/phones/domains) union with per-value provenance.\n(5) Person->organization link: an explicit organization record link (sink's organizationWorkItemId) beats an email-domain match; an organization arriving later re-links persons (relinkPersonsForOrganizations).\n(6) Trigger: a 'relationship-graph-resolve' sink appended in connectorSinksFor after the record sink for person/organization only when the source routes the datatype to record (additive; key scheme and routing of the generalized-integrations sink unchanged). resolveIdentities without recordIds is the backfill path. Agent decision by su-7f8d7809 [self-imposed, under owner directive #1441 'carry the plan to shipped yourself']; not an owner statement. Scope: P-011 / WI-10006439.\n\n(1) Review. A gated task (accepted or escalated) gets one review: approve, edit or reject. A reason is required to edit or reject and optional to approve. The review is stored on the agent task (crm_agent_tasks.review); a reviewed task cannot be reviewed again.\n\n(2) Edit re-runs the parse gate. An edited proposal goes through gateAgentOutput (the @crm/contracts gate plus the request match) with the same knowledge base and policy. An edit the gate rejects is refused with the gate's issues. An edit that would escalate is accepted, because Avi is the escalation target.\n\n(3) Applying. Approve and edit apply only CRM-internal effects: the proposed stage move, if the deal is still in fromStageId (a deal already at toStageId counts as applied; anywhere else is a conflict and nothing is recorded), and one note activity on the subject recording the approved summary and reason, both with source {kind:'agent', ref:<requestKey>}. Outgoing actions (email, chat, call) are never sent at this phase (D-006 propose-only; P-014 counsel review and P-016 agent identity gate sending). They are recorded as approved and held, and the console says so.\n\n(4) Feedback to the role. Every CRM operation input gains an optional ownerFeedback: up to 10 of Avi's most recent reviews with a reason for that operation (decision, reason, proposal summary, decidedAt), newest first. AgentTaskService.submit attaches it, so the crm-agent role reads Avi's corrections in its next input. It is excluded from the replay comparison, so new feedback never turns an idempotent resubmit into a conflict. inputSchema is embedded in the blueprint, so blueprint.yaml is regenerated.\n\n(5) Escalations. Reviewing an escalated task in the console closes its escalate-to-owner item with blueprint:cancel (reason: decided in the CRM console), so it does not linger in Avi's Queue. A cancel failure is recorded on the review and does not undo it.\n\n(6) Metrics are per CRM operation. Measured Oct7 Fire53: phone-app worker/src/agent.ts354-370 instantiates createPhoneVoiceTurnAdapter without resolveContext; adapter.ts670 only invokes a supplied resolver. worker/src/brain.ts callPlane calls operator:converse, never createVoiceTurnRouter. D-033's actual-production-reader attribution is RETRACTED; its tested server projection is valid source code but does not prove Phone runtime acceptance. Retain D-033 owner-only, capability-gated, graph/PER provenance and bounded identity-only constraints. Connect the worker's existing authenticated PapercuspBrain MCP seam to maintained people:search for contacts context, and inject this resolver into the actual adapter. No new datastore, API verb or orchestration loop. Verify the actual worker factory wiring plus MCP success/refusal and prohibited principals before runtime acceptance.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-035 — P-012 canonical scorecard seam and producer independence\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAgent decision under owner directive #1441, not an owner statement. Measured: 2026-10-07 09:49-09:50Z focused source tests (pot-app-seam index 22, emit.grading-audit 49) passed on local staging HEAD05503a13ff with dirty test paths; CRM typecheck and 197 unit tests passed at09:50Z. Reuse maintained pot-app-seam for canonical scorecards:emit/get; no app-owned grade ledger. Pin reviewed rubric revision/hash, grade the producing work-item, and refuse producer-lineage emit at the canonical writer. Readback assembles complete criterion evidence with stable card identity and passes the app parser. CRM vendor and platform host are connected. This is preparatory source verification only: reviewer-output persistence, semantic R8 fixtures, source acquisition, console/sample, rubric re-vetting and shipment remain open. App-principal emissions also require actual reviewer-operation independence attribution before runtime acceptance; comparing only caller identity is insufficient to prove the reviewer was independent.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-036 — P012: bind the actual Phone voice producer through session reports and canonical work-item lifecycle\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAffects: app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06\nMeasured: 2026-10-07, source reads by su-0a2c66a2: phone-app/worker/src/sidecar-client.ts:267 reportSession sends only {event,at}; phone-app/apps/sidecar/src/api.ts:246 routes to CallUnitService.onSessionStarted/onSessionEnded; apps/sidecar/src/call-units.ts:162-211 records owner-resolved start/end and stored transcript digest. worker/src/agent.ts:394-418 applies turn instructions to the actual voice.Agent, :500 constructs google.LLM, and :1072-1085 can apply late context. worker-identity.ts:112-124 fingerprints configured STT/TTS/LLM; this is configuration evidence, not provider-observed response identity. packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/operation-worker-binding.ts:406-525 reads applied accepted-operation authority from adv_sessions/session_briefs; its AcceptedProgramRootAttempt alternative is expressly restricted to accepted execution.kind=program. operator/converse.ts:426 has a separate chat-brain session and is only the Phone boundary slow tier. Canonical ledger writers are createWorkItem (work-items.ts:2714) and setWorkItemState (:3636); create supports assigned producer and internal reserved id, terminal writes require attributed completion evidence. CRM InteractionReviewContext requires gradedWorkItemRef; null source/revisions permit unknown grades but missing producer identity does not.\n\nBoundary ruling for P-012 (extends evidence, preserves D-008/D-009 real-time voice runtime):\n1. The actual voice worker is the producing executor. Do not use call-brief/call-wrap-up WIs, operator:converse session ids, or fabricated adv_sessions/acceptedOperation receipts as its producing WI. The checked maintained seams do not currently provide a turnkey accepted external-voice producer receipt.\n2. Extend the existing authenticated Phone reportSession -> CallUnitService path. Reuse phone_call_units and the canonical work-item lifecycle writers for one replay-safe producing work-item per owner/call key, with a typed external-runtime binding on the existing records. This binding is attribution to the actual voice run, not a new blueprint operation or a claim that a CLI launch occurred. The new verifier is required implementation, not an existing callable capability.\n3. Resolve workspace/harness, owner, call key and runtime authority from trusted sidecar records and authenticated worker admission; never from caller metadata or CRM review request. Bind the actual job/run identity (reuse RUN_ID/worker-identity rather than a second identity system). Freeze the first successful registration and check the same owner/call/run at completion; stale or mismatched reports must not create, overwrite or settle another producer. Recovery must replay the same WI; worker-lost remains explicit.\n4. Completion follows transcript flush and the sidecar's stored canonical digest. Use the canonical completion evidence/authority path; do not skip its gates or infer success from a timestamp. Record runtime provenance and the exact interaction-time approved KB/policy snapshots. Requested/resolved configuration and provider-observed model evidence are distinct; absent provider evidence remains unavailable. Since instructions can change mid-call, retain the applied revision/hash/timing sequence or pin them for the call; a start-only snapshot must not claim to describe later consumed context.\n5. CRM acquires this owner-bound receipt alongside the existing Phone review export. The existing blueprint call-review operation remains the reviewer and scorecard author. Refuse review dispatch without producer binding; inside a bound packet, missing content/approved revisions keep affected criteria unknown. No retroactive backfill claiming historical consumption.\n\nVerification required with implementation: normal call readback binds actual voice WI; duplicate/restart registration replays it; concurrent/conflicting/foreign-owner/run receipts refuse; delayed context cannot rewrite earlier provenance; completed transcript matches digest; worker-lost cannot claim full review. Use existing Phone/CRM suites plus canonical writer integration tests. Root made no code, work-scope, role, launch or mode changes; su-7f8d7809 retains its owner-selected SELF route. This decision specifies the extension boundary, not proof that it is implemented.\nRelated: P-012\n\n### D-037 — D036 completion authority: reuse operational evidence grading and add a trusted runtime effect fence\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAffects: app-agent-tasks-durable-execution-2026-10-06\nMeasured: 2026-10-07 source reads by su-0a2c66a2. coord-lifecycle/records.ts CompletionVerificationEvidenceSchema (:728) accepts pathless operational verification: verifiedHow is any nonempty label; testsRun/testResult describe an actual probe/result; PersistedCompletionEvidence (:836) is its stored narrative extension. work-item-completion-authority.ts insufficientEvidenceReason (:599) requires verification fields and demotes known contrary findings; authorityForCompletion (:695) returns committed/proposed. It is not an external-runtime identity verifier: its own tests explicitly preserve the field-presence-only behavior when no findings were supplied. completion-audit.ts derivedTerminalCompletionAuthority (:440) uses that same grader for an ordinary attributed terminal write with no supplied authority; system identities deliberately keep legacy/null semantics. work-items.ts setWorkItemState (:3636) retains terminal evidence, origin/claim/blueprint checks; feature terminal UPDATE (:4360) currently repeats program/accepted-operation predicates, not an external Phone-runtime receipt. dbos/coord-program-workflow.ts supplied validated authority belongs to its accepted program attempt and does not grant voice the same authority.\n\nClarification of D-036, not a new voice executor or a bypass:\n1. The maintained evidence/grading route is PersistedCompletionEvidence -> authorityForCompletion / derivedTerminalCompletionAuthority -> setWorkItemState. No CLI or changed source file is required by that evidence shape. A completed call can supply truthful operational verification with filesChanged/filesDeleted empty and addedTests omitted/false. Do not claim a Vitest run or source change for a call outcome. Supply summary and a durable completionRef identifying the actual admitted call/run and measured verification; populate verifiedHow and testsRun/testResult from the trusted checks actually performed.\n2. Those existing fields alone DO NOT establish Phone execution authority. The remaining implementation gap is a typed trusted external-runtime verifier/effect fence on the existing canonical writer, bound to the admitted producer WI, authenticated execution owner, workspace/harness, call key/id, immutable runtime registration and stored transcript end/digest. Worker/caller assertions are input to verify, not completion proof. Re-read trusted records; reject mismatched, missing, stale, worker-lost or partial-success claims as appropriate. Only actual successful completion earns the normal computed committed result; failed/lost outcomes remain explicit and cannot claim full-source success.\n3. Keep skipCompletionGate and force off. Do not supply validated merely because the DBOS program path does, do not add a system-closer/null-authority exemption, and do not forge adv_sessions/acceptedOperation. Prefer allowing the normal derived judgement after trusted verification; if the adapter supplies computed authority, it must be the canonical grader's actual result with the adapter's verified contrary findings, never a constant selected by an app request.\n4. The runtime-specific binding/attempt fence must be repeated in the canonical terminal UPDATE (current holder/binding and attempt epoch), following the existing acceptedProgramAttempt pattern while remaining a distinct typed non-CLI binding. A pre-read-only check is insufficient: cancellation/rebinding between the read and UPDATE must refuse. Do not insert a new parallel completion store or change the authority of unrelated normal/blueprint workers. Read back the canonical row's terminalOwner, completionRef, _completionEvidence and completionAuthority; ok:true alone is not acceptance.\n5. Tests belong to the existing runtime/canonical writer suites: successful verified voice outcome without code files; missing/contradictory evidence; foreign-owner/call/run; changed binding/claim/attempt epoch during settlement; worker-lost; duplicate/restart completion preserving the first authoritative evidence. D-036 provenance and CRM reviewer-binding requirements continue unchanged.\n\nThis is source-grounded guidance for the existing 7f SELF/P012 lane. The runtime-specific verifier/fence remains to implement; root has not operated an actual call or proven that extension. Needs a public HTTPS r… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006369 — Retire the pre-contract libs/papercusp/plugins/linear-sync and jira-sync plugins: confirm nothing installs or schedules them (live: zero rows in plugin_linear_sync.links / plugin_jira_sync.links), ba… <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006370 — Live acceptance against a real Linear workspace and a real Asana workspace (owner wall: OAuth app registrations + test workspaces): delegate/assign a task → admitted work item appears in the right pr… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006371 — Docs via docs:author: connecting Linear and Asana (user guide), and both providers added as ticket-provider examples to the provider author guide (GI P-015). <!-- P-011 -->\n## Owner request and scope\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05, interactive, directive #1402] \"Wwrite a plan for a linear and asana integration that uses this same system and synces linear/asasa tasks to work items and show me a detailed summary.\" Asked right after a status read of `generalized-integrations-google-migration-cupboard-workflows-2026-10-05`, so \"this same system\" is that plan's provider contract.\n\nIn scope: Linear and Asana as first-party ticket providers on the provider contract; mirroring their tasks, comments and status changes; turning chosen tasks into Papercusp work items; reporting agent progress back; a connect/configure screen; live proof; retiring the old `linear-sync` and `jira-sync` plugins.\n\n## What already exists (verified 2026-10-06 against the tree and the live DB)\n\n| Need | Existing surface | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| Provider contract: descriptor, `describe` / `syncPage` / `invoke`, `host.fetch` (providers never see tokens), egress allowlist | done | GI plan P-001, P-002, D-006 |\n| Descriptor-driven OAuth connect + connection lifecycle | done | GI P-003 |\n| One sync driver: leases, backfill/incremental, cursor commit after durable admit, 429 backoff, provider-declared reset on expired cursor | done | GI P-004 |\n| Canonical `ticket` (nature record), `ticket-comment` (document), `ticket-status-change` (event) datatypes | live in `datatype_registry` | enterprise-data-sources P-019 |\n| Records → work_items rows (`DSR-…`), comments → documents corpus, events → `DSE-…`, all routed by datatype | `packages/operator-core/lib/data-sources/datatype-destination-sink.ts` | GI P-010 / D-015 |\n| A worked ticket provider to copy | `libs/papercusp/plugins/github-issues/` (read-only) | GI P-010 |\n| Ticket becomes work ONLY via an admission rule or a manual promote; one verb `work_items:admit`; `work_admissions` attribution; `admission_rules` per data source; field authority (external owns title, description, assignee; Papercusp owns status, claim, checkpoint); write-back through the provider registry | `work-admission/admit.ts`, `admission-sources.ts`, `admission-rules.ts`, `record-source.ts`, `/admin/admission` | enterprise D-004 (owner answer #1225), D-030 |\n| Old bidirectional Linear and Jira sync plugins (API-key secrets, own schemas, \"harness wins\" conflict rule) | `libs/papercusp/plugins/linear-sync/`, `jira-sync/`; schemas `plugin_linear_sync`, `plugin_jira_sync` with zero rows in `links` | legacy, pre-contract |\n\nGaps: no Linear or Asana provider; the `ticket` schema only knows open/closed, so workflow states (Backlog, In Progress, In Review, Canceled), priority, due date and parent tasks have no canonical home; providers can only READ tickets (`ticket.read`), there is no comment or status write-back capability yet (WI-10006212 is the GitHub follow-up for `ticket.comment`); nothing reacts when a person closes a task that an agent is working on.\n\n## How it works (plain version)\n\n1. Connect Linear or Asana in Settings. Pick the Linear teams or Asana projects to sync.\n2. Every task in those teams or projects is mirrored into Papercusp as a ticket record: searchable, and available to agents as context. Mirrored tasks are NOT work, so a drain never picks them up (enterprise D-001).\n3. A task becomes a Papercusp work item only when a rule says so. The default rule: \"tasks delegated to Papercusp in Linear\" or \"tasks assigned to the Papercusp user in Asana\". Other rules: \"everything in project X\", \"label agent-ready\". You can also promote a single task by hand.\n4. When an agent picks the work item up, the Linear or Asana task moves to In Progress with a short comment. When the agent finishes, it posts its summary as a comment and moves the task straight to Done (owner answer #1417). A question the agent needs answered is posted as a comment.\n5. If a person edits the task's title, description or assignee in Linear or Asana, Papercusp updates its copy. If a person closes or cancels the task, an unstarted work item is dropped with a note, and an in-progress one is held and its agent is told to stop.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Workflow status on canonical tickets.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Sync Linear and Asana tasks, whose workflows have more states than open and closed.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session:claude:f01b92e6-a38a-46fc-8ee3-effe34f4566d\",\n      \"WI-10006319\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A ticket payload carrying a workflow status category validates against the canonical ticket schema.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A ticket payload with a statusCategory field fails canonical ticket schema validation.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Validate Linear-shaped, Asana-shaped and existing GitHub ticket payloads against the live datatype_registry The existing `state: open|closed` stays and is derived from the category. Provider-only fields stay under `extensions.<provider>`.\n- `ticket-status-change.transition` gains `moved`, with `fromCategory` / `toCategory`.\n- Two new provider capabilities: `ticket.comment` and `ticket.transition { toCategory }`. The provider maps a category to its native state (Linear: the team's first workflow state of that type; Asana: `completed`, or a configured section). Both are dispatched from the existing admission write-back path through the provider registry and `host.fetch`; field authority is unchanged, so Papercusp still never edits title, description or assignee.\n- Echo suppression: a write-back records the provider's returned update id; the next sync does not treat our own comment or move as an external change.\n\n### Lifecycle rules (P-003)\n\nMapped per admission rule (defaults shown):\n\n| Papercusp event | Linear / Asana effect |\n|---|---|\n| admitted | comment \"Papercusp picked this up as WI-…\" (optional) |\n| claimed / started | `ticket.transition in-progress` + comment |\n| needs human / blocked | comment with the question |\n| completed | comment with the completion summary + `ticket.transition done` (owner answer #1417) |\n| external title / description / assignee edit | refresh the admitted item (existing D-030.6 behaviour) |\n| external close or cancel, item unclaimed | drop the work item with a note naming who closed it |\n| external close or cancel, item claimed | computed hold \"source closed\" that names its clearer (the holder), plus a coord message to the holder; fits unified-bug-pipeline D-005/D-006 |\n| external reopen of a dropped item | re-admit through the same rule |\n\n### Providers (P-004, P-005)\n\nBoth are first-party plugin packages like `github-issues`: `papercusp.json` declaring `provider`, `index.cjs` exporting `providerAdapter`, node built-ins only, every HTTP call through `host.fetch`.\n\n**Linear** (`libs/papercusp/plugins/linear/`): GraphQL at `api.linear.app`. OAuth app installed with `actor=app` and scopes `read, write, app:assignable, app:mentionable`, which gives Papercusp its own Linear user that people can delegate issues to (Linear keeps the human as assignee; the agent is the delegate). A workspace admin must install it. Config: team ids. `syncPage` walks issues, comments and issue history per team by `updatedAt` watermark, with an opaque cursor `{v, phase, team, after, since}`. Rate-limit responses map to `rate-limited` with the retry time. `invoke`: `ticket.comment` → `commentCreate`; `ticket.transition` → `issueUpdate { stateId }`, following Linear's guidance to move a delegated issue to the first \"started\" state when work begins.\n\n**Asana** (`libs/papercusp/plugins/asana/`): REST at `app.asana.com/api/1.0`. OAuth with task/story read and write scopes. Config: workspace gid + project gids. Backfill = full task crawl per project; incremental = the per-project Events API sync token. A `412` (token expired or older than ~24h) is the provider-declared reset the sync driver already supports: re-crawl, take the new token. Tasks that live in several projects dedupe on task gid. `completed` maps to `done`, sections can map to categories, stories map to `ticket-comment`, subtasks set `parentExternalId`. `invoke`: `ticket.comment` → create story; `ticket.transition` → set `completed` or move section.\n\nPoll intervals: incremental every ~2 minutes per source, inside the providers' published rate limits. Webhooks (Linear signed webhooks, Asana `X-Hook-Secret` handshake) only WAKE a source's reconciliation, never replace it (GI sync runtime). They need a public HTTPS receiver the desktop app does not have, so they are a later, separate item (P-008).\n\n### Admission presets (P-006)\n\nPresets over the existing `admission_rules` JSON match, evaluated at ingest, with backfill when a rule is added: Linear \"delegated to Papercusp\", \"label X\", \"team X\"; Asana \"assigned to the Papercusp user\", \"in project X\", \"tag X\". Each rule names the target harness and the work kind (`bug` when the provider labels or types it a bug, otherwise `change` or `task`). Admitted bugs follow the one bug queue in `unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05`. No second admission path (enterprise D-028).\n\n### UI (P-007)\n\nSettings → Integrations lists Linear and Asana from their descriptors (GI P-003). Configure: team/project picker from `describe()`, rule preset picker, status mapping, target harness. The existing `/admin/admission` page shows mirrored count, admitted count, last sync and errors per source. Verified in the Tauri shell headlessly.\n\n### Retire the old plugins (P-009)\n\n`linear-sync` and `jira-sync` predate the contract (API keys in plugin secrets, their own link tables, \"harness wins on conflicts\" which contradicts the owner-chosen field authority). Live data shows zero linked issues. After confirming nothing is installed or scheduled, delete both packages and drop their schemas in one migration, with a `backup:snapshot_create` first. No compatibility layer (GI D-008). A Jira provider is a natural follow-up on the same contract, not part of this plan.\n\n## Verification and rollout\n\n- Each provider: recorded-fake tests typed with the vendors' published types (`@linear/sdk` GraphQL types; Asana's OpenAPI types), covering backfill, incremental, cursor reset, rate limits, filtering of non-task objects, and both write-back capabilities. Fixtures must not be self-shaped (GI D-009).\n- Integration tests on the real admission path: rule match → `work_items:admit` → linked work item; claim → transition; complete → comment + transition; external close mid-work → hold + holder message; unmatched tasks never become work; a drain never claims a ticket record.\n- Live acceptance against a real Linear workspace and a real Asana workspace (owner wall: OAuth app registrations; see Open questions).\n- Feature ships flag-ON by default per repo rules; an integration does nothing until someone connects it.\n\n## Out of scope\n\nJira, ClickUp, GitHub Projects; Linear's Agent Session UI (needs AgentSessionEvent webhooks that must answer within seconds, so a public receiver); creating new Linear/Asana tasks FROM Papercusp work items; syncing Papercusp-native work items out to Linear/Asana.\n\n## Owner answers (2026-10-05, directive #1417)\n\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05, interactive] \"1.  straight to done.  2.  yes 3.  ill create them now ... 10., you build them\"\n\n1. Completion moves the task straight to Done (D-006).\n2. Only tasks delegated (Linear) or assigned (Asana) to Papercusp, plus project rules he adds, become work (D-006).\n3. Avi is registering the Linear and Asana OAuth apps now; P-010 waits on them.\n4. Not asked separately; follows the Slack answer #1417.5 (each rule names its project).\n5. (4) No authorize-URL extra-params field was seen in the GI descriptor shape; check plugin-sdk/src/provider.ts and papercusp-plugin.schema.json before assuming one for Linear actor=app. Ruling: start both plans as drafted, no re-sequence.\n\n### D-008 — Write-back contract: comment + transition by source capability, ledgered with the provider update id; GitHub declares ticket.comment only\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-002; refines generalized-integrations-google-migration-cupboard-workflows-2026-10-05#D-009 for GitHub]\n(1) Record write-back has two capabilities: <datatype>.comment (args {externalId, text}) and <datatype>.transition (args {externalId, toCategory}; toCategory is a ticket-vocabulary category).
