GitHub has no workflow columns, so ticket.transition is NOT declared and is refused by name; P-003 must treat that refusal as \"skip the move\", not an error.\n(4) Linear (P-004) and Asana (P-005) providers must return an updateId matching their own sync nativeIds for both capabilities.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-009 — Lifecycle rules run in two places: an idempotent outbound pass after each source sync, and an inbound check on every delivered record\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-003; extends D-003/D-004/D-008]\n(1) Outbound (claim -> in-progress + comment; needs-human/blocked -> comment with the question; completion -> summary comment + move to the rule's completeCategory, default done per D-006) is planned from the work item's CURRENT state by reconcileAdmissionLifecycle (work-admission/lifecycle.ts), run for one data source after each successful connector sync pass (connector-runtime afterSourceSynced; a failure is reported on the outcome and never fails the sync). No tool-invocation reaction or new scheduler: polling stays the source of truth (D-003) and a push wake (P-008) reaches it by waking the source. Each event is written once: admission_write_backs.lifecycle_key with a unique index (migration 1387); a lifecycle write is ledgered even when the provider reports no change. A missing capability (provider_capability_unsupported) is skipped, not failed.\n(2) Inbound outside close/cancel/reopen is decided per delivered record by applySourceLifecycle in the admission sink, as a CHANGE between two deliveries (work_admissions.source_category), never a standing state. So a source that cannot move (GitHub) never reopens an item Papercusp finished, and Papercusp's own move to done is not read as an outside close (the item is already terminal). Unclaimed + closed outside -> dropped, completionRef names the closer (payload.closedBy / statusChangedBy / updatedBy). Claimed + closed outside -> computed external blocker ref source-closed:<recordId> (kind event) naming the holder as clearer, state blocked, coord message to the holder; reopened -> blocker cleared, state back to wip/open. Terminal + reopened outside + the admitting rule still enabled and matching -> reopened (person-admitted items are left to the person).\n(3) Providers (P-004 Linear, P-005 Asana) must fill ticket.statusCategory, and should fill closedBy, for (2) to name the closer.\n(4) Per-rule switches live in admission_rules.lifecycle {claim, hold, complete, completeCategory, externalClose, reopen}; {} = all on. Unknown keys are refused.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-008\n\n### D-010 — Linear provider shape: issue UUID identity, history-derived status changes, column-typed transitions; two small provider-contract extensions\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-004 (WI-10006364); extends D-002, D-005, D-008; not owner-ratified]\n\n(1) A ticket's externalId is the Linear issue UUID, not the `ENG-12` identifier: the identifier changes when an issue moves teams, the UUID does not. The identifier rides on the ticket as `identifier`, the team key as `container`.\n(2) Status changes come from each issue's workflow-state `history`, fetched inside the issues query (no separate phase): one `ticket-status-change` per history entry with a toState (nativeId `history:<id>`), plus a synthetic `opened:<uuid>` on first sight, like GitHub. Columns map by Linear state TYPE (triage, backlog, unstarted->todo, started->in-progress, completed->done, canceled/duplicate->canceled); a started state whose name says \"review\" is in-review. A move between two states of the same column is `moved`.\n(3) Comments come from the root `comments` query filtered by team and updatedAt. The cursor walks issues then comments per configured team (config `teamIds`), with inclusive `gte` watermarks folded only at the end of a pass (same discipline as GitHub).\n(4) `ticket.transition { toCategory }` moves the issue to the first workflow state, by position, of its team whose type maps to that column; for in-progress it avoids review-named started states and for in-review prefers them. An issue already in the column is left alone (`changed: false`).\n(5) Two optional, backward-compatible additions to the provider OAuth descriptor (packages/plugin-sdk/src/provider.ts + papercusp-plugin.schema.json; host in integrations/connection-lifecycle.ts): `oauth.identity.method: 'POST'` + `oauth.identity.body` (JSON) because Linear's identity is a GraphQL query, and `oauth.scopeSeparator: ','` because Linear documents comma-separated scopes [inferred from memory of Linear's docs; WebFetch to linear.app was unavailable at build time - verify at P-010 live acceptance]. `actor=app` needs no contract change: it is carried in the descriptor's authorizeUrl query, which the host preserves. The account identity is the Linear organization (data.organization.id).\nRelated: P-004, P-010\n\n### D-011 — Asana provider shape: task gid identity, story-derived status changes, Events-token incremental with 412 reset, section-mapped columns; ProviderInvokeRequest.config\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-005 (WI-10006365); extends D-002, D-004, D-008; not owner-ratified]\n\n(1) A ticket's externalId is the Asana task gid. A task multi-homed in two configured projects is one ticket. Its container is the first CONFIGURED project (config order) among its memberships, so either read maps to the same ticket.\n(2) Columns: completed -> done. Otherwise the column its section in the container project maps to via source config `sectionCategories` (keyed by section gid or name), else todo. statusName/section = the section name ('Completed' when completed).\n(3) Status changes come from stories: marked_complete -> closed (to done), marked_incomplete -> reopened (from done), section_changed -> the vocabulary transition when both sections are mapped, else moved; nativeId story:<gid>. Plus the synthetic opened:<gid>. Comment stories (comment_added) -> ticket-comment, nativeId story:<gid>.\n(4) Sync per project in config order. BACKFILL takes a fresh Events token before crawling a project (token-less GET /events answers 412 + sync), then crawls /projects/{gid}/tasks (50 per page) and each task's stories. Tokens become live only when the whole crawl completes. INCREMENTAL reads /events?resource=<project>&sync=<token> and re-reads every task an event touched (a story event names its task as parent); has_more pages on. A 412 there is cursor-expired, so the driver re-backfills (re-crawl, new tokens). An expired crawl offset (400) restarts that project's crawl.\n(5) Writes: ticket.comment -> POST /tasks/{gid}/stories {text}, updateId story:<gid>. ticket.transition -> done/canceled complete the task; an open column reopens it and moves it to the first section of the container project mapped to that column. An open column with no mapped section is a no-op (changed:false): Asana has no state for it, and throwing would make the lifecycle retry it every pass.\n(6) Contract extension (optional, all providers): ProviderInvokeRequest.config carries the data source config to invoke, exactly as syncPage receives it. record-source passes it. Needed by (5); Linear and GitHub ignore it.\n(7) Tests are typed against Asana's OpenAPI spec, pinned at Asana/openapi@1b1c151. scripts/gen-asana-openapi-subset.mjs cuts packages/operator-core/lib/providers/asana/asana-openapi.subset.json and runs openapi-typescript over it to produce asana-openapi.d.ts. The official asana npm package ships no model types. [inferred, verify at P-010] The spec declares no granular scope for GET /events and GET /projects/{gid}/sections (oauth2: []); whether the app's granular scopes reach them needs a live check.\n\n### D-012 — Admission presets: providers mark the connected account's own roles (selfRoles); presets are canonical-field matches; bug-labelled tickets admit as bug; rules backfill on set\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-006 (WI-10006366); extends D-003, D-005, D-006; not owner-ratified]\n(1) Who is \"Papercusp\": the account the data source is connected as. Neither connection identity names it usably for matching (Linear's identity is the organization, because the app installs per workspace; ticket assignees/delegates are display names, which collide and get renamed). So the PROVIDER marks it: the canonical ticket gains optional selfRoles[] (subset of assignee, delegate), the roles the connected account holds on that ticket. Linear compares assignee.id / delegate.id with viewer.id (the app user under actor=app); Asana compares assignee.gid with GET /users/me (the authorizing user, so connect Asana as a dedicated Papercusp user). Registered in datatype_registry by migration, like 1377.\n(2) Presets are shorthand on the existing work_items:admit rules-set (no second admission path, enterprise D-028/D-030), beside the chat presets: delegated-to-papercusp -> {selfRoles:{contains:'delegate'}}; assigned-to-papercusp -> {selfRoles:{contains:'assignee'}}; label X -> {labels:{contains:X}} (Asana tags arrive as labels); team X -> {container:{eq:X}} (Linear team key); project X -> {projects:{contains:X}}. Matching stays case-insensitive. No provider-name map: a preset whose field a provider never fills simply matches nothing, and the set result reports the backfill count so that is visible.\n(3) Work kind: a ticket whose labels include 'bug' (case-insensitive) admits as bug; otherwise the rule's workKind (default change). Applies to every ticket record rule, evaluated at sync and at backfill.\n(4) rules-set backfills: setting an enabled record rule runs the existing applyAdmissionRule immediately and returns its scanned/admitted/existing counts. Admission stays idempotent per record, so re-setting a rule never duplicates work.\n(5) Records are never drained: un-admitted ticket rows are nature='record', which work_item_is_agent_work already excludes; P-006 adds a test pinning that for ticket records.\n\n### D-013 — P-008 receiver: reuse the existing signed webhook ingress (/api/hooks/:sourceId over own tunnel or Papercusp relay); extend it with provider-declared signature schemes; a delivery only wakes its source\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471 while surveying P-007/P-008; extends D-003; not owner-ratified] P-008 said \"decide the receiver (hosted relay vs none) before starting\". A public receiver already exists: external-app-access-to-workspaces-2026-09-29 P-017 / D-032 #3 shipped signed webhook ingress `POST /api/hooks/:sourceId` (packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/webhooks/index.ts, packages/operator-core/lib/external-triggers/webhook.ts), reachable from outside through the user's own tunnel (apps/operator/bin/external-ingress-paths.ts) or the Papercusp relay (the portal forwards `POST /api/workspaces/:id/hooks/:sourceId`), gated by the workspace Remote access switch. So no new receiver is built and the question is not an owner wall. What P-008 adds: (1) the ingress today verifies only its own `Papercusp-Signature: t=,v1=` HMAC; it gains provider-declared verifiers (Linear: `Linear-Signature` = hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the webhook secret, plus the payload webhookTimestamp freshness check; Asana: the `X-Hook-Secret` handshake echo on subscription, then `X-Hook-Signature` = hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with that secret), selected by the source's provider descriptor, never by a request header naming a provider. (2) Per D-003 a verified delivery never writes a record: it only makes its own source due (sync_next_attempt_at = now) so the next poll reconciles; a delivery for another source or an unverified one changes nothing. (3) Precondition for live use (P-010): Remote access on and either the own tunnel or the relay connected; without it, polling alone still works. Related: P-008, P-010, D-003\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/external-triggers/webhook.ts:11 documents the only accepted header `Papercusp-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(key, `${t}.${raw body}`)>`, :37 `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_HEADER = 'papercusp-signature'`, :96 verifyWebhookSignature checks only that scheme; packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/webhooks/index.ts header comment: `auth: 'public'`, reachable via the own tunnel or the Papercusp relay (read 2026-10-06 12:25Z).\n\n### D-014 — P-007 shape: one Settings → Integrations page from the provider registry; a ticket.containers capability feeds the pickers; config, rules and health reuse the existing write paths\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471 while starting P-007 (WI-10006367); extends D-002, D-006, D-011, D-012; not owner-ratified] P-007 assumed the GI plan built a descriptor-driven Settings → Integrations page and that describe() lists teams/projects. Neither holds, so P-007 builds both pieces, reusing what exists. (1) Page: `/settings/integrations`, rendered from the live provider registry: one card per registered provider whose descriptor has an `oauth` block (displayName, capabilities, Connect/Reconnect via the existing `/api/oauth/start?provider=<id>`), listing the signed-in user's sources of that kind with account label, status, last sync, last error, mirrored and admitted counts. (2) Return path: after OAuth the user lands back on Integrations. `/api/oauth/start` gains an optional `return` parameter, allowlisted to internal `/settings/` paths and carried in the signed state; the callback uses it, else the adapter's returnPath (Google's personal-vault return is unchanged). (3) Pickers: a new provider capability `ticket.containers` (invoke, args {}) returns `{ containers: [{ id, name, kind: 'team'|'workspace'|'project', parentId?, sections?: [{ id, name }] }] }`: Linear lists teams; Asana lists workspaces and their projects with sections. It runs through the same registry + createSourceHostFetch path write-back uses (record-source.ts), never syncs or writes records, and a provider that lacks it is refused provider_capability_unsupported (the UI then offers a plain id field). (4) Config: `POST /api/integrations/sources/:id/config` merges { teamIds | workspaceGid + projectGids, sectionCategories, harnessSlug }, validates the result against the provider descriptor's configSchema (packages/operator-core/lib/json-schema-validation.ts) before saving, and makes the source due. Until then the source keeps failing with linear_teams_missing / asana_projects_missing, which the page shows as \"choose teams/projects\". (5) Rules: the preset picker (TICKET_RULE_PRESETS + value) + target harness + work kind calls setAdmissionRuleAndBackfill, the same path work_items:admit rules-set uses, so no second admission path (D-012); rules are listed and disabled per source. (6) Status mapping: Asana section → category is editable (sectionCategories, D-011); Linear is read-only because the workflow-state type decides (D-010). (7) Health: /admin/admission (today the scheduler's queue-admission page) gains a \"Ticket sources\" table from the same read. (8) Data flow: one sync query `integrations.overview` + notifySyncInvalidate after each write (no hand-rolled polling); the selected source and open panel live in nuqs. Verified with route/integration tests, a component test, and a headless Tauri check (scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh). Related: P-007, P-010, D-010, D-011, D-012\nMeasured: libs/papercusp/plugins/linear/index.cjs:594 `describe: () => DESCRIPTOR` (static descriptor only); :159 and libs/papercusp/plugins/asana/index.cjs:117 throw transient linear_teams_missing / asana_projects_missing on empty config; packages/operator-core/lib/integrations/connection-lifecycle.ts:461-473 provision() upserts a connected source per descriptor with config { accountLabel } only and returnPath '/settings/personal-vault' (:446); apps/operator/app/settings has no integrations page (ls 2026-10-06 12:10Z).\n\n### D-015 — Correction to D-013 for Linear: per-source webhooks need Linear's admin scope, and the OAuth app's own webhook posts every workspace to one URL, so Linear push needs an owner choice; Asana keeps D-013\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471 while starting P-008; corrects D-013 for Linear only; not owner-ratified]\nMeasured from Linear's developer docs (linear.app/developers/webhooks, via web search on 2026-10-06; WebFetch was down per EI-25206021611352116):\n(1) Creating a webhook through the API (webhookCreate) requires an admin user or an OAuth token with the `admin` scope. D-010 requests read, write, app:assignable, app:mentionable, so Papercusp cannot register a per-source Linear webhook.\n(2) An OAuth application can configure a webhook in its own settings. Linear then creates one for every organization that installs the app, all posting to the single URL configured on the app and signed with the app's webhook signing secret. Payloads carry organizationId.\n(3) The signature is `Linear-Signature` = bare hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, plus `webhookTimestamp` (ms) checked within 60s. Headers Linear-Event and Linear-Delivery.\nConsequence: D-013's 'each source's own /api/hooks/:sourceId over its tunnel or the relay' works for Asana (per-project POST /webhooks with the X-Hook-Secret handshake) but not for Linear. Linear push needs one of: (a) stay on polling for now; (b) a hosted router on the Papercusp portal: one app-level URL that verifies with the app's signing secret and forwards a wake to the workspace whose Linear source matches organizationId; (c) add the `admin` scope so each source registers its own webhook (every connecting user must be a Linear admin). Recommendation: (a) now, with Asana push built per D-013. Revisit (b) after P-010 proves polling, consistent with P-008's own 'after polling is proven'. Avi chooses.\nRelated: P-008, P-010, D-003, D-010, D-013\n\n### D-016 — P-008 Asana push shape: descriptor-declared push scheme verified by the host, a push.subscribe reconcile capability, per-source push secrets table, handshake only inside a host-opened window\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-008 (WI-10006368); extends D-003, D-013; Linear part still waits on Avi's D-015 choice; not owner-ratified]\n(1) The provider descriptor gains an optional `push` block, pure data: `{ handshake?: { header }, signature: { header, algorithm: 'hmac-sha256', encoding: 'hex' } }`. The HOST verifies it, so the ingress never branches on a provider name. Asana: handshake header `x-hook-secret`, signature header `x-hook-signature` (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with that webhook's secret).\n(2) One reconcile capability, `push.subscribe { targetUrl, subscriptions }` -> `{ subscriptions: [{ id, resource }] }`: the provider makes its remote webhooks match the source config (Asana: one webhook per configured project; creates missing, deletes ones for unconfigured projects or a different target) and returns the resulting set. `push.unsubscribe { subscriptions }` deletes them all. The host stores the set at data_sources.cursor.push (host-owned key, like `wake`).\n(3) Asana sends one handshake per webhook, inside its create call, carrying only the secret (no webhook id). So the host opens a handshake window (cursor.push.handshakeOpenUntil = now + 60s) before invoking push.subscribe and closes it after. A handshake outside an open window is refused and writes nothing. Each accepted handshake stores one encrypted secret in a new table harness_shared.connector_push_secrets (several per source; trigger_webhook_secrets holds exactly one per source and stays the generic webhook's). A delivery verifies against all of the source's secrets in constant time. Full unsubscribe deletes them.\n(4) Ingress: `POST /api/hooks/:sourceId` keeps its order of checks. A source of kind `webhook` takes today's path unchanged. A connector source whose provider declares `push` takes the push path: remote access must be on; a handshake is accepted only in the window and echoed; a delivery with a valid signature calls wakeConnectorSource and nothing else (D-003), answering 200; anything else is refused with nothing written. The body is never parsed as data.\n(5) The connector-sync routine reconciles push for each syncable source whose provider declares push.subscribe, only when the workspace's Remote access is on and a public URL exists (own tunnel preferred, else the relay; webhookUrls()). Reconcile runs when the target URL or the configured resources changed, or after a failure backoff; a failure is recorded on cursor.push.lastError and never fails the sync pass. Without a URL, polling alone continues.\nRelated: P-008, P-010, D-003, D-011, D-013, D-015\n\n### D-017 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAmendment-Id: linear-asana-approved-preview1162930-20261007\nRequest-Hash: 59f376ff0c003231cfda5993adc764ba5da50ca14ebed948d796c2d8ca04c29a\nActor: su-dab96471-48c6-40bf-a2b6-2ec7c5b052ca\nReason: Independent critique thread-post:1162861: bind existing executable tests, put omitted source-authority/manual/lifecycle/connect/soak outcomes explicitly in remaining live P010 BAR, and align P011 BAR with both guides and live usability. No live acceptance waiver; Linear choice stays unresolved. Fresh reviewer objection thread-post:1162921 resolved: R7 retains e2e and uses honest manual native verification with existing maintained registered suite; component tests cannot satisfy it. R8 binds real Asana push unit tests plus existing host/PG integration tests and declares both layers. No outcome/layer waiver.\nApproved-By: su-c312aa1d-177b-4dae-9e42-8ecbb54c07dd\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1162939\nApproved-At: 2026-10-07T20:04:24.090Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 56 → 57\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-018 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-08\nAmendment-Id: linear-asana-runtime-preview1163247\nRequest-Hash: 54d940d391e659c23232b85c3e4957c9c72a8c3dcfcf6a3ed383b16312ef3d01\nActor: su-dab96471-48c6-40bf-a2b6-2ec7c5b052ca\nReason: Declare staging-operator for both existing live real-vendor and user-guide acceptance checks. No fake vendor evidence, no live test waiver, no final shipped-artifact waiver.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-56c31b66-f511-4184-89f8-46d03a53a773\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1163299\nApproved-At: 2026-10-08T01:16:32.266Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 57 → 58\nChanged BARs: R-10, R-11\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-019 — Avi directs background syncing: polling-first through the existing connector runtime\nDate: 2026-10-08\nOwner turn in this Codex session on 2026-10-08: \"and lets do background syncing. We are doing background syncing for gmail and calendar to our local db, right?\" Follow-up: \"can you unpark them?\"\n\nImplementation interpretation: use the existing host-owned background connector-sync polling/reconciliation path for Linear and Asana, matching Gmail/Calendar's architecture; do not add a hosted Linear webhook router or require Linear admin scope for this delivery. R9 positive controls already exist; preserve all outcomes/layers.\nApproved-By: su-df005151-0ec5-4c01-b897-5309d3bceda6\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1178010\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T02:04:57.251Z\nRubric revision: 7 → 8\nSubject plan revision: 63 → 64\nChanged BARs: R-7, R-8, R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-7, R-8, R-10\n\n### D-023 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: linear-asana-repin-1178096\nRequest-Hash: 8e64cedb427ddbc2cb593552ca4cb42a15b829b4a9dea6749ebf4f3966d907ff\nActor: su-dab96471-48c6-40bf-a2b6-2ec7c5b052ca\nReason: Re-pin exact native e2e candidate after committed stdout/stderr protocol correction and passing noisy-CLI regression. Current native run pending.\nApproved-By: su-29284612-e2fe-488c-8c74-34b4ea84890a\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1178108\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T03:21:02.815Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 64 → 65\nChanged BARs: R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-7\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"operator-e2e-standing-isolated-run-2026-10-06","title":"Operator Playwright suite runs on a cadence against an isolated current-build rig, and every red has an owner","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Operator Playwright suite runs on a cadence against an isolated current-build rig, and every red has an owner\nslug: operator-e2e-standing-isolated-run-2026-10-06\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-06\n---\n\n# Operator e2e standing isolated run\n\n## Context\nSource of truth for the problem: WI-10006736 (its checkpoint carries the measured baseline and the cluster classification). Existing building blocks (reuse, do not rebuild):\n- `scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh` with `VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1` boots a throwaway migrated PG + desktop and exports the isolated identity (PAPERCUSP_HOME etc.) to the assertion command (lines ~4013-4023).\n- `apps/operator` `npm run test:e2e` (= `playwright test`, default config `playwright.config.ts`).\n- The ledger reporter `apps/operator/test/reporters/admin-test-runs-reporter-playwright.ts` writes per-file results to `harness_shared.test_runs` (EI-25232220211651248: passing `--reporter` on the CLI disables it, so the runner must not).\n- Contract guards in `apps/operator/lib/__tests__/playwright-config.test.ts`.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — One command runs the whole operator e2e suite in isolation and its results survive.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"One committed command runs every default-config operator Playwright spec inside the isolated verify-tauri-headless rig, exits with Playwright's own code, and leaves per-file results in the shared test_runs ledger under one run group.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:3a995156-e0c8-4542-a248-812bf5103637:24\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"One invocation of the runner boots the isolated rig, runs the full default suite, writes one shared-ledger test_runs row per collected spec file under a single run_group_id, and exits non-zero when any spec fails.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The runner exits 0 while a spec failed, ledger rows land only in the throwaway isolated DB (none in the shared ledger), rows are split across run groups, or a CLI --reporter flag disables the ledger reporter.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"exit code propagation\",\n      \"ledger rows reach the shared DB from an isolated rig\",\n      \"single run group per invocation\",\n      \"ledger reporter not disabled\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest suite drives the runner's argument/env construction and the reporter's DB-URL precedence with the real modules, and a real rig run is recorded as operational evidence.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/__tests__/e2e-isolated-runner.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — The suite runs on a cadence without anyone starting it.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The isolated runner fires on a schedule through the sanctioned scheduler, not a bare timer, with a cadence and admission class the shared box can carry.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:3a995156-e0c8-4542-a248-812bf5103637:24\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A durable routine for the runner is visible in routines:list and schedule:inventory, and one of its fires produced a run group in the shared test_runs ledger.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The cadence is a bare setInterval, cron line or self-paced loop; the routine is absent from the inventory; or a fire produced no ledger run group.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"sanctioned scheduler\",\n      \"visible in inventory\",\n      \"a fire produces ledger rows\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest asserts the routine declaration (action, tier, cadence) and the fire handler's invocation of the runner; a real fire is recorded as operational evidence.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/__tests__/e2e-isolated-runner.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Every red spec has an owner.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"After each scheduled run, each spec file that failed and has no open owned work-item gets exactly one, deduped by spec path, carrying the failing test ids and output tail.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:3a995156-e0c8-4542-a248-812bf5103637:24\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A spec that fails in two consecutive runs yields exactly one open owned work-item naming that spec, its failing test ids and an output tail; a spec that already has an open owned item gets no duplicate.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A red spec yields no item, a second run files a duplicate, the item is unowned, or it omits the failing test ids.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"one item per red spec\",\n      \"dedupe across runs\",\n      \"owned on creation\",\n      \"failing ids and output tail attached\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Vitest drives the red-filer over two synthetic consecutive run groups and asserts exactly one owned item per red spec path.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/__tests__/e2e-red-filer.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — The known baseline reds are green or owned.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The 34 baseline reds measured on 2026-10-06 (WI-10006791 empty-DB fixtures, WI-10006792 UI specs) are fixed, or each remaining red has an owned item with a stated reason.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:3a995156-e0c8-4542-a248-812bf5103637:24\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"An isolated full-suite run reports 0 failed, or every remaining failing spec maps to an open owned work-item whose body states why it is red.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A full-suite run has a failing spec with no owned item, or a spec was made green by deleting or skipping its assertions without a recorded reason.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"empty-DB fixture specs\",\n      \"UI specs\",\n      \"no silent skips\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"A full isolated run through the R-1 runner, read from the shared test_runs ledger by run group.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/e2e/home.spec.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nRunner (P-001): a committed npm entry wraps `scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh` with `VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1`, picks a free Vite port, and runs `playwright test` with the ledger reporter left on. The rig exports `HARNESS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` pointing at its throwaway PG (verify-tauri-headless.sh:4019), so the reporter must prefer the dedicated `PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUNS_DB_URL`, which the runner pins to the shared operator DB before entering the rig. Otherwise every isolated result dies with the rig (measured 2026-10-06 17:13Z: a 37-pass run left no shared-ledger rows). The runner exits with Playwright's own code.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n\n## Items\n- **P-001** `done` One-command isolated e2e runner: a committed npm entry that runs the full default Playwright suite inside `verify-tauri-headless.sh` with `VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1`, keeps the ledger reporter active, tags the run group, and exits with Playwright's own code. Acceptance: one invocation produces test_runs rows for every collected spec file under one run group, and a deliberately failing spec makes it exit non-zero. — note: WI-10006804 closed: 3/3 spec clauses certified with grading audits passed.\n- **P-002** `done` Cadence: schedule P-001 through the sanctioned scheduler (a tier:durable routine; no bare timers) with a cadence and pc-heavy admission class that fit the shared box (start nightly; a run is ~8-10 min plus a ~5 min rig boot). Acceptance: the routine is visible in routines:list / schedule:inventory and its last fire produced a run group in test_runs. — note: ← WI-10006805 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Every red gets an owner: after each run, each spec file that went fail/error with no open owned work-item gets one, deduped by spec path, with the failing test ids and output tail attached; reuse an existing test-failure filer if one exists. Acceptance: a seeded red spec produces exactly one owned work-item across two consecutive runs. — note: ← WI-10006806 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `todo` Green the known baseline reds: WI-10006791 (12 empty-DB fixture ids) and WI-10006792 (22 UI ids). Acceptance: an isolated run with 0 failed, or every remaining red carries an owned item with a stated reason.\n- **P-005** `todo` Decide gate promotion: once the suite has been green for N consecutive scheduled runs, decide whether it becomes a green-checkpoint leg, recorded as a plan Decision.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10006804 — One-command isolated e2e runner: a committed npm entry that runs the full default Playwright suite inside `verify-tauri-headless.sh` with `VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1`, keeps the ledger reporter activ… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006805 — Cadence: schedule P-001 through the sanctioned scheduler (a tier:durable routine; no bare timers) with a cadence and pc-heavy admission class that fit the shared box (start nightly; a run is ~8-10 mi… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006806 — Every red gets an owner: after each run, each spec file that went fail/error with no open owned work-item gets one, deduped by spec path, with the failing test ids and output tail attached; reuse an … <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006807 — Green the known baseline reds: WI-10006791 (12 empty-DB fixture ids) and WI-10006792 (22 UI ids). Acceptance: an isolated run with 0 failed, or every remaining red carries an owned item with a stated… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006808 — Decide gate promotion: once the suite has been green for N consecutive scheduled runs, decide whether it becomes a green-checkpoint leg, recorded as a plan Decision. <!-- P-005 -->\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Rubric-vet findings (conv-muwz2gya): routine run-group identity, the 'owned' definition, and one batched rubric amendment after P-002..P-005\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: the rubric-vetting consult answer by su-e4d818b8 on conv-muwz2gya-0000-8ca6a19cc3944272bb3354a7a916a159, vetting acceptance rubric rev 1. [self-imposed decision, 2026-10-06 18:03Z]\n\n1. P-002's routine stamps a recognizable run group: PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_GROUP=operator-e2e-nightly:<routine fire id>. That is how a grader tells a routine fire from a manual run, since ledger `source` is 'local' for both. The grader reads the ledger run_group_id; if the routine ever dispatches through testing:run, mind guard-rails test-run-group-origin-ledger-split and spec-evidence-origin-vs-ledger-group.\n2. In P-003's red filer, 'already owned' means an open work-item with a non-null assignee whose body names the spec path. That includes per-cluster items such as WI-10006791/WI-10006792, so the first run does not file ~34 duplicates.\n3. The baseline for R-4 is the first full R-1 run group; record its id here when it exists. R-4 is graded as a delta between two named groups, and 'no silent skips' means the green group's test count >= baseline and its skip count <= baseline.\n4. Rubric amendment is deferred and done ONCE, after P-002..P-005 are implemented. It applies the vet's changes: R-1 adds the outcome that rows carry the caller's workspace/harness and binds a run group, not one spec; R-1's evidence plane is the ledger; R-2 names the group-id stamp; R-3 uses the definition in (2) plus operational evidence that reds with no owned item = 0 after the first scheduled group; R-4 uses (3); add R-5: a plan Decision promotes the suite to a green-checkpoint leg or declines it, citing N named consecutive scheduled run groups. Then re-vet, attest against meta-acceptance-rubric, and recruit grading via plans:set-plan-status shipped. Reason for deferring: each edit invalidates the attestation and any grading, so the edits are batched.\n\n### D-002 — P-003 red filer: who owns a red, how 'already owned' is matched, and why it is a separate hourly routine\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed decision, su-16da39cf, WI-10006806]\n\n1. OWNER. A filed red is assigned to the routine row's payload_template.redOwner (seeded from OPERATOR_E2E_RED_OWNER). Without one, it goes to the current assignee of the umbrella item (payload_template.umbrellaItem, default WI-10006736). With neither, the item is still filed, unassigned, and the fire returns softError plus ownerUnresolved:true. That way the routine's health shows the gap instead of hiding it. Reason: no existing auto-filer assigns a durable owner, and a session id goes stale when its session ends (claims are released then). So the owner is configuration on the routine row, not a hardcoded session.\n\n2. MATCHING 'already owned' (D-001 #2 made concrete). A work item names a spec when its title or summary contains the spec STEM as a whole token, followed by ':<digit>' or '.spec.'. That matches the cluster items' 'home:15' and a filed item's path, but not 'workspace-home:12'. Outcomes: an open assigned item means skip. An item closed after the group finished means skip, because the evidence was already answered. An open unassigned item is assigned to the owner, not duplicated. Otherwise file a bug. This makes the sweep idempotent with no watermark.\n\n3. SHAPE. The filer is a separate durable routine, system:operator-e2e-red-filer, firing hourly at :50 and seeded by the same seed script as P-002. It sweeps the newest nightly group whose run is not in flight. The improvements watchdog's red-test collector was not reused because its thresholds do not fit a nightly suite: it needs >=3 fails in 6h, takes at most 2 captures per tick, and leaves captures unassigned. Its path normalizer and the shared create core ARE reused. The Playwright ledger reporter now records execution_details.failedCaseTitles, so a filed red names its failing tests.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"portable-papercusp-container-and-native-2026-10-06","title":"Portable Papercusp — containerized Server on Linux/macOS/Windows alongside native, plus whole-install export/import","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Portable Papercusp — containerized Server on Linux/macOS/Windows alongside native, plus whole-install export/import\nslug: portable-papercusp-container-and-native-2026-10-06\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-09\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-07, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_work_contract_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing. Phase 0 done (WI-10006429).\n\n**Next:** plans:start once the grading audit lands; then Phase 1 from P-053 (state census).\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10007347 — State census, DERIVED not hand-maintained: classify every path under ~/.papercusp and ~/.config/papercusp, every PG DB, every unit and every secret as state / config / secret / cache / dev-only. Regenerate machine identity (mesh, federation keys, tunnels, hostnames) so the copy never impersonates the sou… <!-- P-056 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007351 — Reference case: export this native dev box (D-001) in full and import it into a scratch VM. This answers the owner's original question with a rehe… <!-- P-057 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007352 — Container image of the Papercusp Server, built from the SAME bundle (apps/operator/bin/bundle-host.sh) and runtime rootfs the Windows WSL distro uses. Reuse the BYOC manifest/signing pipeline (byoc p… <!-- P-058 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007353 — Process supervision inside the container: systemd-in-container with cgroup delegation, so the task manager (packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/managed-spawn.ts) still confines and kills agent pr… <!-- P-059 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007354 — Linux container runtime: rootless podman with a generated systemd unit (quadlet), Docker also supported. Plus a scheduled restore-proof drill … <!-- P-068 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007363 — User docs: choosing native vs container per OS, performance expectations taken from the Phase 0 measurements, and a moving-machines guide (export, then import). <!-- P-069 -->\n## Goal\n\nAny Papercusp installation, native or containerized, can be moved to another machine through a rehearsed **export → import**. The **Papercusp Server** ships as a container on **Linux, macOS and Windows** alongside the existing native installers, built from **one shared pipeline**. **This dev box stays native.**\n\n## Owner direction (verbatim source)\n\n- Directive #1443 [owner:Avi 2026-10-06]: \"how portable is papercusp. like our fulln app with our full db and all the specific settings we have etc. If I wanted to bring that all to a different machine, how hard would it be? Can we make that any easier?\"\n- Directive #1444 [owner:Avi 2026-10-06]: \"can we use that infra [byoc-cloud] to maybe make it easy to containerize any installation? … Currently our linux mac and windows builds are install files, can we change that to be like containerized versions? would that make it easier to transport as well?\"\n- Directive #1445 [owner:Avi 2026-10-06]: \"Would this hurt performance? … if we maintained the native versions alongside this containerized version will that add overhead or will they share most of the same pipeline? Any other capability the native version would have the containerized version wouldn't?\"\n- AskUserQuestion answer [owner:Avi 2026-10-06]: \"#1 and #2 but this machine we'll keep native but I want us to support the container version for all 3 platforms, so we'll support both the containerized and native versions. This machine we'll keep native\" (#1 = measure first, #2 = draft a plan).\n\n## Measured starting point (su-586d6, 2026-10-06 — re-verify before relying on it)\n\n- **Database:** the `papercusp` DB is **142 GB**. harness_shared is 141 GB, of which ~80 GB is session transcript tables (session_archive_files 37G, session_turns 18G, session_turn_chunks 12G, session_turn_parts 7G, session_turn_windows 5G); tool_invocations 11G, coord_thread_posts 10G. Also email_app 5.5 GB, restart 4.7 GB and ~30 small test/template DBs. Native PG 18.4 at /var/lib/postgresql/18/main, with pgvector 0.8.2, pg_trgm, pgcrypto, uuid-ossp and pg_stat_statements.\n- **State folders:** `~/.papercusp` is **191 GB**, mostly rebuildable caches (perf 29G, bench 23G, p046 deps 15G+6G, scratch 8.8G, release-seeds 7.2G). The real state is pot-git 13G, hives 7.6G, session-claude 7.9G, su-codex-homes 24G and models 5G (re-downloadable).\n- **Host wiring (dev box):** 98 user systemd services, 67 of which hardcode `/home/marsh-office`. Only 75 unit files are tracked in the repo. There are also ~16 papercusp units in /etc/systemd/system. Secrets live in 8+ `.env` files plus agent CLI logins. Product source barely hardcodes paths (~2 files).\n- **Backups:** hourly `pg_dump -Fd` of every DB to /mnt/backup/db-dumps (194 GB; last success 2026-10-05 23:35, no failures), kopia every 30 min, and a daily home snapshot. **No rehearsed restore of this box onto a new machine exists.** Backend-reliability audit 2026-09-13 F18: restore readiness not established.\n\n## Existing surfaces to reuse (reuse-first)\n\n- **BYOC plan `byoc-cloud-workspaces-gcp-aws-azure-2026-08-22` (shipped):**\n  - Its item P-048 split the thin GUI from the separate **Papercusp Server** artifact (`papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.server.conf.json`).\n  - Its item P-010 is the workspace-host bootstrap contract; P-022 is backup/restore-into-new-VM; P-046 is workspace pairing/import, which is **pairing only, not full-state migration**.\n  - Its items P-054/P-055 provide the canonical host manifest, reproducible builds and the artifact trust/signing pipeline.\n  - Its items P-013/P-015 provide the SSH connection manager and remote terminal launching.\n  - The bootc image is `infra/images/bootc/workspace-host.Containerfile`.\n- **Native GUI/Server split on Linux:** plan `linux-desktop-split-server-like-mac-win-2026-07-19` (awaiting acceptance). The container Server attaches to the GUI through the same seam.\n- **Windows already runs the backend in a container-derived environment:** `papercup-runtime.tar.gz` is a container export of Ubuntu 24.04, imported as the WSL2 distro `papercup-runtime`. Its checksum-pinned rootfs step is in `apps/operator/bin/release/setup-release-checkout.sh`; desktop code is in `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/wsl_*.rs`.\n- **Server build:** `apps/operator/bin/bundle-host.sh` produces one plain-ESM bundle run by `node`. Both variants must ship this same bundle.\n- **Backups:** the kopia + `backup:*` tools and the infra/estate-backup restore drills (pattern for scheduled restore proofs).\n- **Prior art for moving a whole estate:** `hetzner-full-portability-backup-2026-08-21` (cloud estate, shipped).\n\n## Scope\n\nIn scope:\n- the export/import contract for every install (native and container);\n- the container Server on all three platforms;\n- one release pipeline emitting both variants;\n- the test matrix;\n- user docs.\n\nOut of scope:\n- containerizing this dev box (D-001);\n- containerizing the GUI (D-003);\n- changing the BYOC cloud product beyond reusing its pieces.\n\n## Known risks / native-only capabilities to design around (from 2026-10-06 analysis)\n\n- **Task manager:** confines every agent process tree in systemd scopes (`packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/managed-spawn.ts`) and silently degrades without systemd. In a container this needs systemd-in-container with cgroup delegation.\n- **Host signals:** load, PSI, process lists and service health become container-scoped.\n- **Integration tests** that start Postgres in Docker (testcontainers, 33 files) need the host Docker/podman socket or nested containers. GPU rendering (`vglrun`) needs per-OS passthrough; Xvfb is fine.\n- **Agents see only mounted folders.** Mac file sharing across the VM boundary is slow.\n- **Credentials need forwarding:** SSH agent, git credential helpers, Keychain / Credential Manager, browser OAuth callbacks for agent CLIs.\n- **macOS needs a Linux VM:** it costs reserved memory, and its runtime choice is open. Mac/Win test VMs are nested inside KVM (nested virtualization was flaky for WSL, EI-11320), so real Mac hardware may be needed for the macOS benchmark.\n- **Users need a container runtime:** Docker Desktop has license terms at larger companies; podman is free.\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Phase 0 measured native vs container cost and today's moving cost.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Measure first: would containers hurt performance, and how hard is a move today.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:84d419a0-76cc-4123-b484-f05c017166f6:5\",\"session_turn:claude:84d419a0-76cc-4123-b484-f05c017166f6:8\",\"D-005\",\"D-007\",\"D-008\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Linux and Windows native-vs-container results and a timed full restore rehearsal with a breakage inventory are recorded on the work item.\",\"falsifier\":\"A Phase 0 result the plan relies on has no recorded measurement.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read WI-10006429 posts 1160112, 1160167, 1160265, 1160287 and 1160298 and ~/p0-bench/results.\\n\\nGoverns: D-005, D-007, D-008. Verification conditions: record Linux and Windows native/container measurements and the Phase 0 full restore duration and breakage inventory. Use the named WI-10006429 posts as durable evidence; ~/p0-bench/results alone is insufficient for another grader. A failed condition prevents healthy; missing evidence is unknown.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-17 — Install, upgrade and moves are proven across the matrix.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Support both containerized and native versions on all 3 platforms.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:84d419a0-76cc-4123-b484-f05c017166f6:8\",\"D-002\",\"D-004\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Fresh install, upgrade and export/import pass for each OS and variant, including native-to-container and container-to-native moves, and a scheduled restore-proof drill runs.\",\"falsifier\":\"A matrix cell or cross-variant move has no passing run.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"E2E matrix results and the drill's last run.\\n\\nGoverns: D-002, D-004 and the E2E/restore-proof requirement. Verification conditions: enumerate Linux, Windows and macOS x native/container x fresh install/upgrade/export-import, plus native-to-container and container-to-native moves; attach each result and its exact runtime/artifact identity. Read the registered restore-proof schedule and completed drill receipt. Mark missing cells or a missing drill unknown; partial matrix evidence cannot be healthy.\\nRATING BASIS: the complete model and governing decisions are the pass floor; evaluate each verification condition and the named falsifier. A failed condition prevents healthy; missing evidence is unknown.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-18 — Users can choose a variant and move machines from the docs.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Make moving machines easier.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:84d419a0-76cc-4123-b484-f05c017166f6:0\",\"session_turn:claude:84d419a0-76cc-4123-b484-f05c017166f6:5\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"User docs explain native vs container per OS with the measured performance, and give a step-by-step export/import guide.\",\"falsifier\":\"The docs omit a platform or the moving guide.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the published docs pages.\\n\\nGoverns: D-002, D-004 and the user-docs requirement. Verification conditions: locate the maintained published user-doc pages and corresponding source paths under apps/operator-docs/src/content/docs; verify OS-by-OS native/container choices, measured performance and a complete export/import procedure. Record exact URLs/source paths and check every step against the verified journey. Do not treat an internal plan or a dead URL as published user documentation.\\nRATING BASIS: the complete model and governing decisions are the pass floor; evaluate each verification condition and the named falsifier. A failed condition prevents healthy; missing evidence is unknown.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-19 — This dev box stays native.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"This machine we'll keep native.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:84d419a0-76cc-4123-b484-f05c017166f6:8\",\"D-001\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"No change in this plan moves the dev box's Server, PG or fleet into a container; the dev box is the native reference case.\",\"falsifier\":\"The dev box's operator or PG runs from the container image after this plan.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Check the dev box units after the plan ships.\\n\\nGoverns: D-001. Verification conditions: after the plan's changes, read dev:service_health and the native dev-box Server/PG/fleet process and unit identities; verify the services still execute natively and preserve the box as the native reference. Record exact service names and health/runtime evidence; no plan change may move these services into a container.\\nRATING BASIS: the complete model and governing decisions are the pass floor; evaluate each verification condition and the named falsifier. A failed condition prevents healthy; missing evidence is unknown.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n- **One Server build, two packagings (D-004).** `apps/operator/bin/bundle-host.sh` produces the Server bundle once. The native installers ship it as today. The container image layers the same bundle onto the runtime rootfs that `papercusp-desktop/scripts/build-rootfs.sh` already produces as an OCI export for WSL (WI-10006429 post 1159706). So the WSL distro and the container image are one artifact (P-061).\n- **Declared data roots (P-054).** One data-roots module resolves PG data, state, secrets and cache from environment overrides with per-OS defaults. Native installers and the container image set the same variables; the container mounts each root as a volume. Export/import works on roots, so it is variant-independent and cross-variant moves work.\n- **Export/import (P-055, P-056)** extends `packages/backup` (kopia transport, HKDF password from the DB encryption key) rather than adding a parallel system. Export takes one synchronized PG snapshot, copies state roots minus caches, and seals secrets (including `db-encryption-key`) in an encrypted bundle. Import follows the Phase 0 lessons: all data before any post-data, user triggers disabled during load, `maintenance_work_mem` sized for HNSW, ANALYZE in stages, roles from every source cluster. It rewrites behaviour-driving path columns listed by the census, and regenerates machine identity (node id, device keys, tunnels, federation), so the copy never impersonates the source.\n- **Container defaults from Phase 0 (D-009).** Linux: rootless podman quadlet by default, Docker supported, PG data on a named volume. Windows: run the Server directly in the imported distro on WSL ext4, host networking (podman's 127.0.0.1 forward hangs in mirrored mode, WI-10006715), never /mnt/c. macOS: podman machine on Apple Virtualization.framework, chosen from published data, measured on real Apple silicon at the first Mac E2E (D-007).\n- **Process supervision (P-059).** The image boots systemd as PID 1 with cgroup delegation, so `managed-spawn.ts` keeps confining agent trees; host-signal readers report `scope: container`.\n- **GUI connection (P-063).** The thin GUI reuses the BYOC connection manager: a local container Server is one more Server endpoint.\n- **Proof per requirement.** Tree-plane bars cite unit tests; live-plane bars are verified on real artifacts in the Linux/Windows/macOS test VMs.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-049, P-050, P-051, P-052 | live |\n| R-2 | P-053 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-054 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-055 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-056 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-057 | live |\n| R-7 | P-058 | live |\n| R-8 | P-059 | live |\n| R-9 | P-060 | live |\n| R-10 | P-061 | live |\n| R-11 | P-062 | live |\n| R-12 | P-063 | live |\n| R-13 | P-064 | live |\n| R-14 | P-065 | live |\n| R-15 | P-066 | live |\n| R-16 | P-067 | live |\n| R-17 | P-068 | live |\n| R-18 | P-069 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-057 | live |\n\n\n## Phase 0 — Measure\n\n- **P-049** `done` Linux benchmark: native Server vs the same Server in a container on this box. Run fully isolated: a scratch PG instance on its own port with its own data, low priority, never touching live PG or the fleet. Workloads: pgbench plus representative harness queries on a restored data subset; git status/clone on a large repo; npm ci; one vitest file; agent CLI spawn latency; Server boot time. Compare volume vs overlay writes and host vs bridge networking. Deliverable: results table + verdict on the work-item. importance: high — note: Done by su-586d6 under WI-10006429 (done). Results ~/p0-bench/results/{pg,dev}.csv; summary WI-10006429 post 1160298 s2: dev loop no real difference native vs podman/docker volumes; fsync ~1.8x slower in containers; docker overlay-unmount hang on this host (WI-10003403), podman fine.\n- **P-050** `dropped` macOS benchmark: native Server vs Server in a Linux VM. Candidate runtimes: Apple container / Virtualization.framework, podman machine, Lima/colima. Measure idle memory overhead, CPU, in-VM volume vs a shared Mac folder (virtiofs), git and npm. First establish whether papercup-vm-mac (macOS inside KVM) can host a nested Linux VM. If it cannot, real Mac hardware is needed: surface that to the owner, don't fake it with a non-representative rig. importance: high — note: Dropped for Phase 0 per D-007 (owner answer 'Skip Mac for now'): papercup-vm-mac cannot host an accelerated nested Linux VM (AMD host, kern.hv_support=0; WI-10006429 post 1159006). macOS runtime choice made from published data under P-062; measured on a real Apple-silicon Mac at the first real-Mac E2E (P-068).\n- **P-051** `done` Windows benchmark: the current papercup-runtime WSL distro vs the same image delivered via the container path (OCI export imported as a WSL distro, or podman inside WSL). Parity check, including files on the WSL ext4 filesystem vs files on /mnt/c. Note the known nested-virtualization flakiness of papercup-vm-win (EI-11320) and record rig failures separately from product results. importance: high — note: Done by su-586d6 under WI-10006429. Results post 1160112: containers cost nothing measurable on WSL2; /mnt/c unusable (57x clone, PG refuses datadir); podman 127.0.0.1 port-forward hangs in mirrored mode (WI-10006715), host networking works; papercup-runtime already an OCI export.\n- **P-052** `done` Restore rehearsal: restore last night's DB dumps (/mnt/backup/db-dumps) plus the latest kopia home snapshot onto a scratch VM/machine, natively, the way a move would work today. Time every step. Record everything that broke or needed hand work: systemd units, absolute paths, secrets, agent CLI logins, machine identity. Hard rule: the restored copy must never come up with live identity. No tunnels, mesh, federation keys, git-sync or GitHub pushes, so it cannot impersonate the dev box. Output: today's real moving cost + the input for the state census. importance: high — note: Done by su-586d6 under WI-10006429 (local VM per D-008). Posts 1160167 (DB restore; 681 tables, 0 invalid idx), 1160265 (home 76 GB/33 min), 1160287 (breakage inventory: 1.86M path rows, 41k symlinks, db-encryption-key must travel, P2P node identity), report 1160298.\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 1 — State layout and export/import\n\n- **P-053** `todo` State census, DERIVED not hand-maintained: classify every path under ~/.papercusp and ~/.config/papercusp, every PG DB, every unit and every secret as state / config / secret / cache / dev-only. Produce a generated manifest with a drift check, so a new state path that is not classified fails a check (derived-truth ladder rung 1-2). blocked-by: P-052\n- **P-054** `todo` Canonical data-roots contract for every install: PG data, state root, secrets and cache root as separate declared roots (env-configurable), applied to the native installers on Linux, macOS and Windows. Remove the remaining hardcoded home paths. Migrate existing native layouts in place on upgrade. blocked-by: P-053\n- **P-055** `todo` papercusp export: quiesced, consistent PG backup; state roots minus caches; an encrypted secrets bundle; a manifest (product version, migration head, PG + extension versions, source identity). Optional tiers to exclude the transcript archive and test/template DBs. Kopia as the resumable, incremental transport. Reports size and duration. blocked-by: P-054\n- **P-056** `todo` papercusp import: verify the manifest, restore, then migrate forward. Refuse downgrades. Regenerate machine identity (mesh, federation keys, tunnels, hostnames) so the copy never impersonates the source. Rebind credentials, run health checks, and provide a dry-run mode. blocked-by: P-055\n- **P-057** `todo` Reference case: export this native dev box (D-001) in full and import it into a scratch VM. Health checks pass and the source box is unaffected. This answers the owner's original question with a rehearsed, timed procedure. blocked-by: P-052, P-055, P-056\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Container Server\n\n- **P-058** `wip` Container image of the Papercusp Server, built from the SAME bundle (apps/operator/bin/bundle-host.sh) and runtime rootfs the Windows WSL distro uses. Reuse the BYOC manifest/signing pipeline (byoc plan's P-054/P-055). SBOM; multi-arch amd64 + arm64 (Apple silicon). blocked-by: P-049 — note: Avi authorized AUTO shipment; this session owns WI-10007352 and is implementing the shared-rootfs/sidecar container builder. Existing P-053 holder has been contacted; no duplicate census lane taken.\n- **P-059** `todo` Process supervision inside the container: systemd-in-container with cgroup delegation, so the task manager (packages/operator-core/lib/task-manager/managed-spawn.ts) still confines and kills agent process trees. Host signals (load/PSI/process list/service health) are labelled container-scoped. Document the exact behaviour wherever this is unavailable; no silent degradation. blocked-by: P-058\n- **P-060** `todo` Linux container runtime: rootless podman with a generated systemd unit (quadlet), Docker also supported. Volumes follow the data-roots contract; integrated with GUI auto-start. blocked-by: P-058, P-059\n- **P-061** `todo` Windows container runtime: run the same image via WSL (import the image export as the distro, or podman inside WSL). Converge papercup-runtime.tar.gz with the image so there is one artifact, not two. blocked-by: P-051, P-058\n- **P-062** `todo` macOS container runtime: a Linux VM chosen from the macOS benchmark results. Lifecycle managed by the Server tray / GUI (start at login, memory sizing, updates). Workspaces live in the VM volume by default to avoid slow shared-folder IO. blocked-by: P-050, P-058\n- **P-063** `todo` GUI to container-Server connection via the BYOC connection-manager path: terminals exec/SSH into the container, ports and agent-CLI OAuth callbacks are forwarded, and there is an explicit connect/install flow when no Server is found. blocked-by: P-060\n- **P-064** `todo` Credential and host-integration forwarding: SSH agent, git credential helpers, OS keychains (Keychain / Credential Manager / libsecret), agent CLI logins. Plus a folder-mount UX for repos that live outside the container volume. blocked-by: P-063\n- **P-065** `todo` Upgrade and rollback for the container variant: image tag pinning, migration compatibility checks before switching images, and rollback to the previous image plus a pre-upgrade data snapshot. blocked-by: P-058\n- **P-066** `todo` Dev and test tooling inside the container: testcontainers via the host podman/Docker socket or nested podman, Xvfb, and optional GPU passthrough. Document what is unsupported per OS (e.g. GPU on the macOS VM). blocked-by: P-059\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Release, test matrix and docs\n\n- **P-067** `todo` One release pipeline emits, per platform, the native installer AND the container image (plus the WSL rootfs) from one build, with signing and SBOM. Release notes list both variants. blocked-by: P-058\n- **P-068** `todo` E2E matrix: fresh install, upgrade and export/import across 3 OS x {native, container}, including cross-variant moves (native to container, container to native). Plus a scheduled restore-proof drill modelled on infra/estate-backup/pc-mirror-restore-drill. blocked-by: P-057, P-060, P-061, P-062\n- **P-069** `todo` User docs: choosing native vs container per OS, performance expectations taken from the Phase 0 measurements, and a moving-machines guide (export, then import). blocked-by: P-068\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Dev box stays native\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, AskUserQuestion answer] \"This machine we'll keep native.\" The dev box (shared tree, git-sync, gate, test VMs, Xvfb/GPU, Docker) is not containerized. It is the reference case for NATIVE export/import (P-057).\n\n### D-002 — Support both containerized and native versions on all 3 platforms\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, AskUserQuestion answer] \"I want us to support the container version for all 3 platforms, so we'll support both the containerized and native versions.\" Linux, macOS and Windows each ship a native install AND a containerized Server.\n\n### D-003 — PROPOSED (needs owner review): containerize the Server only; the GUI stays a native installer\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, AskUserQuestion answer \"Approve both\"] Only the Papercusp Server is containerized; the desktop GUI stays a native signed installer on Linux, macOS and Windows. Reuses the BYOC P-048 split: the thin native GUI connects to a Server that runs natively, in a local container, or in the cloud. Reason: a native window, native terminals and OS integration cannot usefully run in a container.\nRatified: Avi on 2026-10-06\n\n### D-004 — PROPOSED (needs owner review): one state layout and one build pipeline for both variants\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, AskUserQuestion answer \"Approve both\"] Native and container installs keep state in the same declared roots (PG data, state, secrets, cache), so export/import is variant-independent and cross-variant moves (native to container and back) work. One build (the bundle-host.sh bundle + runtime rootfs) emits the native installers, the container image and the WSL rootfs. The recurring cost of supporting both is the E2E matrix and the process-supervision layer, not the build.\nRatified: Avi on 2026-10-06\n\n### D-005 — PROPOSED: measure before building\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06 chose \"measure first\" + \"draft a plan\"; the gating below is an agent proposal] Phase 0 results (benchmarks + restore rehearsal) gate the macOS VM runtime choice, the export tiering (transcripts optional?), and the container defaults. Benchmarks run isolated from the live fleet and never touch live PG data.\n\n### D-006 — Phase 0 execution choices\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, AskUserQuestion answers] (1) Route: su-586d6 runs Phase 0 itself in its own session; no fleet. (2) The restore rehearsal (P-052) runs on a cloud VM provisioned via the BYOC tooling, billed to the owner's GCP project; tear it down after measuring. (3) macOS benchmark (P-050): try papercup-vm-mac first. If a Linux VM cannot run inside it (nested virtualization), report that and re-ask; never fake a result on a non-representative rig.\n\n### D-007 — macOS benchmark deferred: no Apple-silicon rig; measure during the first real-Mac E2E\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, AskUserQuestion answer \"Skip Mac for now\"] [turn:7d2501d2@2026-10-06T06:10:03.296Z] papercup-vm-mac cannot host an accelerated nested Linux VM. The host CPU is AMD (svm). The macOS guest runs an emulated Intel model with kern.hv_support=0. Apple container is Apple-silicon only. Evidence: WI-10006429 comment 1159006. So P-050 produces no numbers in Phase 0. The macOS runtime choice (Apple container / podman machine / Lima) is made from published data, then measured on a real Apple-silicon Mac during the first Mac end-to-end test. Linux (P-049), Windows (P-051) and the restore rehearsal (P-052) proceed now.\n\n### D-008 — Restore rehearsal runs locally in the clean-room Linux test VM, not in GCP\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, AskUserQuestion answer \"Local test VM (Recommended)\"] [turn:self] This supersedes D-006 point (2). The box uploads at under 4.2 MB/s: WiFi only, both Ethernet ports have no carrier (WI-10006429 comment 1159085). So uploading the 195 GB of dumps would take ~13 h and saturate the shared uplink, and a full move (dumps plus the 642.9 GB home snapshot) is ~860 GB, ~2.5 days. P-052 therefore restores into the existing clean-room Linux test VM (papercusp-desktop/scripts/linux-test-vm) with its data disk on /mnt/backup (622 GB free). That measures restore time and every fresh-machine breakage with no upload or cloud cost. The network leg of a move is reported as size divided by the measured uplink. The GCP rehearsal bucket gets deleted.\n\n### D-009 — Phase 0 outcomes set the container defaults, export tiering and move contract\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed, AUTO mode under owner directive #1516; derived from owner-approved D-005 'Phase 0 gates the macOS runtime choice, export tiering and container defaults'] Evidence: WI-10006429 posts 1160112, 1160167, 1160287, 1160298.\n(1) Linux container default: rootless podman via a generated quadlet; Docker supported. PG data lives on a named volume, never the container overlay (fsync in containers measured ~1.8x slower than native; the dev loop showed no real difference). Docker's slow overlay unmount on the dev box (WI-10003403) is a host issue, not a reason to drop Docker support.\n(2) Windows: the WSL distro IS the container image export (one artifact). The Server runs directly in the imported distro with host networking (podman's 127.0.0.1 forward hangs in WSL mirrored mode, WI-10006715). All state stays on WSL ext4, never /mnt/c (clone 57x slower; PG refuses a DrvFs datadir).\n(3) macOS: podman machine on Apple Virtualization.framework, chosen from published data (free, OCI-compatible, same tool as Linux; Apple container is macOS 26+/Apple-silicon only). Measured on real Apple silicon at the first Mac E2E (D-007).\n(4) Export tiers: full by default; optional tiers exclude the session transcript archive and the throwaway test/template DBs (papercusp_it_baseline_*, tmpl_*).\n(5) Move contract: the DB encryption key travels inside the encrypted secrets bundle; import uses one PG snapshot, loads all data before post-data with user triggers disabled, sizes maintenance_work_mem for HNSW, restores roles from every source cluster, ANALYZEs in stages, rewrites behaviour-driving path columns named by the census, and regenerates node identity. A restored copy never dual-runs with live identity.\n\n### D-010 — Rubric rev 1 stays canonical; restore, rehearsal and multi-arch assertions also carried as split item clauses\nDate: 2026-10-07\nContext: plans:start refused spec_quality_failed on :3170 build 93cafaab21 because spec quality judged the AUTO-BAR projections of R-2/R-5/R-6/R-7/R-11/R-19. A batched rubrics:amend narrowing those bars (approval thread-post:1160984 on WI-10007004) was OBJECTED by outside review (post 1161004) because narrowing dropped graded assertions.\n\nDecision [self-imposed, su-83cc1, 2026-10-07]: do NOT amend. Rubric acceptance-portable-papercusp-container-and-native-2026-10-06 rev 1 stays canonical with all its assertions. The dropped-at-risk assertions are ALSO carried as atomic, falsifiable item clauses with acceptanceRef to their BAR: PPC-P-056-2 (dry-run writes nothing), -3 (older-version bundle migrates to current schema), -4 (imported install passes health check), -5 (manifest mismatch refused), -6 (no source-root paths in imported config) -> R-5; PPC-P-057-2 (export/import durations recorded), -3 (source dev box services stay healthy), -4 (source dev box keeps its identity) -> R-6; PPC-P-058-2 (image published for amd64 and arm64) -> R-7.\n\nWhy no amend: :3170 build 44c99f8303+ (seen again on 71024e0508) excludes sourceBar-pinned BAR projections from spec quality (\"added or meaning-changed BAR projections are checked on rubric writes\"), so the original blocker is gone. Spec quality now passes on :3170 for specSetHash 2c891ad7… (scorecard EI-25279866518654766, grading audit pending). Any BAR rewording (e.g. R-7 naming an implementation file; R-19 naming the agent fleet) is deferred to the post-implementation rubric vetting step.\n\nAlso: PPC-P-062-1 reworded from \"macOS GUI\" to \"On a Mac, ... desktop app\" because the implementation-independence heuristic flags \"macOS\" as an identifier (false positive, filed).\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"slack-messages-to-bug-reports-2026-10-05","title":"Slack messages to bug reports: one more way into the one bug queue","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Slack messages to bug reports: one more way into the one bug queue\nslug: slack-messages-to-bug-reports-2026-10-05\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-07\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-07, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_rubric_revision_mismatch, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing. Next repair: Before mutating BAR state, run dev:pipeline_position { path: \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/with-plan-lock.ts\", marker: \"synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision\" } to distinguish a stale serving build from a live guard. If the synchronizer is not deployed, land/redeploy it first; otherwise re-seed or amend atomically so subject and rubric revision pins agree.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nDRAFT for Avi's review (directive #1402), written by su-dab96471 under WI-10006319.
