Verified headlessly in the Tauri shell. blocked-by: P-004 — note: ← WI-10006380 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 4 — Live proof\n\n- **P-009** `todo` Live acceptance in a real Slack workspace (owner wall: Slack app xapp-/xoxb- tokens with reactions:read, interactivity and files:read, plus channel ids, per reference/slack-external-trigger-setup.mdx): each of the four signals produces exactly one bug in the configured project; a duplicate thread folds; status replies appear in the thread; unflagged messages never become work; a pasted secret is redacted. blocked-by: P-001, P-006, P-008\n- **P-010** `todo` Docs via docs:author: 'Report bugs from Slack' setup guide (scopes, shortcut, channel rules) and the chat reporter type in the bug-intake docs. blocked-by: P-009 importance: low\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Slack is one more way into the one bug queue\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[follows unified-bug-pipeline-and-honest-queue-2026-10-05#D-001 and #D-009 (reuse, no parallel systems); applied by su-dab96471 under owner directive #1402 (\"it should use that same system as well\"); proposed, not ratified] A Slack report is the same bug work item agents and end users file, with reporter provenance `chat`. No Slack-specific bug store, queue, triage or verification. Related: P-004, P-005\n\n### D-002 — A Slack message becomes a bug only when a person flags it or a channel rule says so\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[inherits enterprise-data-sources-2026-10-01 P-021 (\"becomes a linked work item only when a person or an explicit rule says so\") and #D-004 (owner answer #1225); proposed by su-dab96471, not ratified] The four signals (reaction, shortcut, mention, bug channel) are all a person or a rule. The optional classifier (P-007) only suggests, privately, and never files. Related: P-002, P-003, P-007\n\n### D-003 — Admitting a bug from any source goes through the unified intake, so duplicates fold and secrets are stripped\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[proposed by su-dab96471, not ratified] `work_items:admit { kind: bug }` stops minting directly and calls the unified intake (unified P-011) for every source kind, Slack and Linear/Asana tickets alike; the admission row keeps attribution and the link back. A duplicate gets its own admission row on the existing bug plus a corroboration, which orders verification but never replaces it (unified #D-007). Related: P-004; linear-asana-task-sync-2026-10-05 P-006\n\n### D-004 — Slack identities are recorded, never trusted; Slack text is untrusted evidence; attachments need consent\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[inherits external-triggers-gmail-slack-2026-08-22#D-008, unified #D-003 and #D-013; proposed by su-dab96471, not ratified] A Slack user id never selects a Papercusp principal. Report text reaches agents only as quoted evidence. Files stay as Slack links unless the reporter ticks consent in the shortcut form; then they are redacted and kept 90 days after close. Related: P-002, P-005\n\n### D-005 — Slack stays on its current connector in this plan\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[proposed by su-dab96471, not ratified] Moving Slack onto the generalized provider contract is a separate follow-up. Intake keys on the `chat-message` datatype and the `chat` reporter type, so only signal capture (P-002) is Slack-specific and a later Teams or Discord provider inherits bug reporting unchanged. Related: P-002\n\n### D-006 — Owner answers: all four gestures, per-channel project, thread replies, connector flag on, su-dab96471 builds it\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-05, interactive, directive #1417] \"4.  yes.  5.  yes. 6.  the thread. 7.  yes. ... 10., you build them\". All four report gestures ship, each switched on per channel (P-002, R-2). Each channel rule names its target project (P-003). Status replies go in the originating thread (P-006, R-6). The papercusp-slack-org-connector flag is turned on (P-001, R-1). Route A: this session (su-dab96471) implements the plan. On #1417.8 Avi asked whether Slack is already connected; it is not (no Slack source row, zero chat messages, no stored Slack credential, measured 2026-10-06 03:47Z), so live acceptance P-009 waits on a workspace and tokens. #1417.9 asked for an explanation of suggestions; P-007 stays low priority pending his call. This ratifies D-001..D-005 as drafted. Related: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-006, P-007, P-009\n\n### D-007 — Consult result: P-004 routes through the unified bug intake, as a candidate, with its review enrolled\nDate: 2026-10-06\nSource: consult conv-muw6iwpp-0000-4a2df1ffb1db4bc0869648d3a4d96325, answer by su-c75b933e (fork of su-93aaa593, snapshot 2026-10-06 01:10Z; [peer], mechanism proposed, not owner-ratified). (a) unified-bug-pipeline D-001 says every bug source calls one intake, so P-004 must call that intake rather than mint bugs itself. (b) The intake does not exist yet: it lands in unified-bug-pipeline P-010/P-011 (WI-10006224, WI-10006225, owned by su-4a152 under D-016). P-004 therefore waits on WI-10006225; if Slack must move first, it goes through capture-core captureImprovement with a stable key slack:<channel>:<message_ts>. (c) Rules carried over: report text is untrusted, quoted evidence only (D-003); a Slack-sourced bug has no failing ledger row, so it enters as a candidate and is never stamped verified or ready at admit (D-024/D-011); reporter identity is kept only as provenance with bounded retention (D-013). (d) Do not replicate the capture-core.ts readiness-stamp defect (EI-25176539351759672): any readiness stamp written on admit must also enrol the agent review (agent-review.ts enterAgentReview), or the bug becomes unclaimable.\n\n### D-008 — Slack bug rules are admission_rules rows (chat source kinds + an action column), evaluated by a chat admission sink at ingest\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471 while designing P-003; extends D-002, D-005; not owner-ratified]\n(1) A Slack bug rule is an ordinary harness_shared.admission_rules row on the Slack data source, with source_kind 'chat-message' (admit the flagged message) or 'chat-thread' (admit the thread), and a new column action ('admit' default, or 'suggest'). The channel and trigger are plain match fields over the canonical chat-message payload (channelId, signal, gesture), plus one evaluator-derived field threadStart (true for a top-level post). Presets: report-bug signal files a bug = {channelId:{eq:C}, signal:{eq:'report-bug'}} on chat-message; every new top-level thread is a bug = {channelId:{eq:C}, threadStart:{eq:true}} on chat-thread; suggest only = either preset with action 'suggest'. Each rule names its harness (harness_slug) and work_kind (bug). No new rule table (coordination with trigger-automation-consolidation-2026-10-01: one more source kind on the existing mechanism, not a seventh).\n(2) Evaluation happens at ingest in a 'data-source-chat-admission' sink that createDatatypeDestinationSinks adds for the chat-message datatype beside the document sink. It evaluates the source's enabled chat rules against the event; the subject is the signal's target message (payload.target.ts) or the event's own message. An admit rule calls admitWorkItem with the chat source ref (idempotent on the source key). A suggest rule creates nothing and records the match as the sink outcome (P-007/P-008 read it). No matching rule means no work (D-002): an unflagged message in a non-bug channel never becomes work.\n(3) The chat resolvers read harness_shared.chat_messages, which only the org connector's history backfill writes. The sink therefore upserts the live message first when the event carries its text (post, mention, bug-channel post, shortcut); for a reaction (no text) whose target is not yet stored it fetches that one message through the existing Slack history call before admitting. Failed sink deliveries are not re-driven automatically, so the sink must not rely on a retry.\nRelated: P-003, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-009 — Correction to D-008 (2): the chat admission sink is attached at the Slack ingest, not in createDatatypeDestinationSinks\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471; corrects my own D-008, not owner-ratified]\nD-008 (2) said the 'data-source-chat-admission' sink is added by createDatatypeDestinationSinks beside the document sink. That premise was wrong. Slack Socket Mode events go ingestSlackSocketEnvelope -> ingestExternalTriggerEvent, whose sinks are the event bus, the trigger binding sink and input.additionalSinks; createDatatypeDestinationSinks has one production caller, providers/connector-runtime.ts (GitHub/Linear/Asana provider connectors), so a sink placed there would never see a Slack event.\nMeasured: external-triggers/ingestion.ts `const sinks = [eventBusSink, createTriggerBindingSink(sql), ...(input.additionalSinks ?? [])]`; grep createDatatypeDestinationSinks over packages/operator-core/lib (non-test) -> connector-runtime.ts and relationship-graph/participants.ts only; ingestion.ts discards a sink's return value (finishDelivery stores outcome + error only).\nRuling: the chat admission sink is a provider-neutral module (data-sources/chat-admission-sink.ts) that the Slack socket manager attaches to every ingest through ingestSlackSocketEnvelope's additionalSinks. A later chat provider on the generalized connector contract (D-005 follow-up) attaches the same sink from connector-runtime. Everything else in D-008 stands: rules are admission_rules rows (chat-message / chat-thread source kinds + the action column), the subject is payload.target, a suggest rule creates nothing, no match means no work.\nRefinements found while implementing:\n(a) An event's text is the subject's text only when the event says so (target.text). An in-thread mention targets the thread root and a shortcut carries the reporter's note, so neither may be stored as the subject's body; those subjects are read from chat_messages or fetched from Slack (conversations.history pinned to the ts, else conversations.replies).\n(b) A thread whose opening post has no replies is stored with thread_key NULL, so a chat-thread admission names its rootMessageId and a chat-message admission of a root names its thread; chat-thread rules are evaluated before chat-message rules, so 'this thread is a bug' and 'this message is a bug' fold onto one work item.\n(c) threadStart is true only when the event IS a new top-level post (top-level AND the event carries the post's own text). A reaction, mention or shortcut ABOUT an existing post is not a thread start, so the new-thread preset never files an old post because someone reacted to it. Found by the fold test in data-sources/chat-admission-sink.integration.test.ts.\n(d) Suggest matches are returned by the sink but not persisted (the ingest ledger keeps only outcome/error), so P-007 must add its own store for suggestions.\nRelated: P-003, D-008\n\n### D-010 — P-007 suggestion design: suggest switch routes posts in, local classifier measured on a frozen holdout, note names only gestures that would file, chat_bug_suggestions store\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-007; extends D-002, D-008, D-009(d); not owner-ratified]\n(1) Routing. Measured: normalizeSlackSocketEnvelope drops ordinary channel posts (only mention/dm/report-bug signals reach ingestion), so a suggest rule could never match a plain post. A new per-channel switch reportBug.channels[C].suggest (default OFF, like every gesture switch) makes ordinary top-level posts in C reach the chat admission sink as chat events with target = the post. The switch only routes; the channel's admission_rules decide (a 'new-thread' preset with action 'suggest' is the suggest-only rule).\n(2) Classifier. chat-bug-suggest.ts is a deterministic weighted-phrase scorer (version lexical-v1, threshold 2.5): free, local (no text leaves the machine), auditable. Tuned only on fixtures/chat-bug-suggest-tuning.json (60 msgs: precision 1.000, recall 0.750). Measured once on fixtures/chat-bug-suggest-holdout.json, written before the classifier (80 msgs): precision 0.963 (26/27), recall 0.743 (26/35); bars fixed beforehand at >=0.9 / >=0.6 and pinned in chat-bug-suggest.test.ts. Both samples are self-authored, so this is not live precision; live acceptance (P-009) is the real measure. Changing the classifier to pass the holdout voids it: write a fresh holdout.\n(3) The note. A suggestion is sent only for a person's own top-level post (not a report gesture), only when an enabled admit rule on the source would file a report-bug signal from that channel, and it names only the report gestures switched on there (reaction emoji, shortcut, mention). If none would file, nothing is sent and the row records 'no-route'. Never files (D-002).\n(4) Store (D-009(d)). harness_shared.chat_bug_suggestions (migration 1403): one row per suggested message (unique per source+channel+message, so replays never re-send), with score, classifier version, rule, outcome (notified | no-route | failed + error). A per-author-per-channel cooldown (1 hour) keeps one person from being nagged. No message text is stored there (chat_messages holds it). P-008's view reads it.\nRelated: P-007, P-008, P-009, D-002, D-008, D-009\n\n### D-011 — P-008 Slack-bugs view: work_admissions records its outcome; per-channel counts come from four existing tables\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed by su-dab96471 while designing P-008; extends D-007, D-008, D-010; not owner-ratified]\n(1) harness_shared.work_admissions gains outcome ('created' or 'folded', default 'created'). admit.ts writes 'folded' when the bug intake attached the source to an existing bug. 'Filed' and 'merged into existing' are therefore read from a fact, not inferred from field_authority or row order. Both inferences are wrong for a Slack thread that folds onto a bug an agent filed, which has no earlier admission row.\n(2) The per-channel view reads four tables. Filed and merged: work_admissions of kind chat-message or chat-thread, with the channel taken from the source key (<dataSourceId>:<channelId>:...). Suggested: chat_bug_suggestions with outcome 'notified'. Refused (with reason) and last error: the chat admission sink's failed trigger_deliveries rows. Configured channels come from the chat admission_rules' channelId match, so a channel with rules but no traffic still shows zeros.\n(3) A refusal error now names its channel (chat_admission_refused:<channelId>:<rule>=<code>), like the sink's other errors. Delivery payloads are pruned, so the error text is the durable place for the channel.\n(4) Live refresh: an emit_change_notify trigger on chat_bug_suggestions, and one on trigger_deliveries that fires only for sink_kind 'data-source-chat-admission' (that table carries every external event for every sink). A new sync query, admission.chatBugs, is bridged from those tables plus work_admissions, admission_rules and data_sources.\nRelated: P-008\n\n### D-012 — P-005 design: reporter kind 'chat' is a person's report; the Slack context block is reportContext.chat, assembled from the source (DB) and the gesture (Slack API, only when a rule admits)\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed by su-dab96471 while building P-005; extends D-004, D-007, D-008, unified D-013 and P-010/P-013; not owner-ratified]\n(1) ReporterKind gains 'chat' (provenance.ts). Like 'end-user' it is a PERSON's report, so every rule keyed on 'end-user' now keys on a shared isPersonReporterKind(): intake quoting (capture-core quoteEndUserIntake), the stranded-tool-failure sweep exclusion (TS and SQL), and admit.ts's direct-path and refresh quoting (admittedSourceTitle/Body). admit.ts sets 'chat' for any chat-message or chat-thread source, whoever admits it (a person promoting a Slack thread still files Slack text); a rule admission of any other source stays 'end-user' (P-004). No agent-facing tool can set a reporter kind.\n(2) The chat context block is ReportContext.chat (report-context.ts, schemaVersion stays 1; absent on non-chat rows). Fields: provider, workspace {id, name}, channel {id, name}, permalink, gesture, reportedAt, postedAt, reporter {externalUserId, displayName}, author {externalUserId, displayName}, note, threadExcerpt, attachments [{name, mimetype, size, url}], attachmentConsent. Slack ids are recorded, never resolved to a principal (D-004). Every string is redacted and bounded; note and threadExcerpt are stored quoted as untrusted evidence (quoteEndUserText with Slack headers), display names as one-line quoted titles. attachments are Slack links only (https Slack permalinks, never url_private bytes).\n(3) Two contributors, merged in admitWorkItem: the admission source resolver (DB facts: channel, postedAt, author, bounded thread excerpt) via ResolvedAdmissionSource.reportContext, and the chat admission sink (gesture, reporter, note, consent, plus Slack API facts) via AdmitInput.reportContext. The Slack facts come from a new optional ChatAdmissionAdapter.reportFacts(): chat.getPermalink (no scope), the message's files and user_profile (conversations.history, already used), and users.info for display names. It runs only when an admit rule matched, so ordinary traffic makes no extra Slack calls. The manifest gains users:read; Slack is not installed yet (D-006), so the owner installs it once at P-009.\n(4) The shortcut note is also the first paragraph of the bug body ('Note from the reporter'), since it is the reporter's own description; the intake quotes the whole body.\n(5) Consented downloads (D-004/unified D-013: redacted, deleted 90 days after close) wait on whether unified P-014 (WI-10006228, su-4a152) builds the attachment store; asked 2026-10-06 21:05Z. P-005 records consent in the block either way; it does not build a second store.\n\n### D-013 — Acceptance rubric rev2: as-built bindings, two new BARs, and refusal replies belong to P-006\nDate: 2026-10-07\nDate: 2026-10-06 [self-imposed by su-dab96471 after the non-author vetting critique thread-post:1160898 (consult conv-muxa97ja, reviewer su-e3647c9e); not owner-ratified]\n(1) R-1 and R-10 become behaviours: R-1 is the connector reaching Slack with no overrides (the flag defaulting off is one cause of failure); R-10 is a doc-claims test that fails when the Slack bug-reporting guide and the code disagree. Whether a person can follow the guide moves into R-9, whose live drill runs from the guide alone.\n(2) Two new BARs trace D-004 and D-012 to P-005: R-11 (file bytes are stored only with the consent tick) and R-12 (Slack text is stored only as quoted evidence).\n(3) R-6 now lists the reply states: filed, merged into an existing bug, refused by its rule with the reason, reproduced or not, fix shipped. A refused report gets one reply naming the reason, so the reporter is not left guessing. A gesture in a channel where no rule turns it on is not a report and gets no reply (otherwise every playful bug emoji would draw a bot reply). This widens P-006 by the refusal reply, which needs no unified P-016 event because the sink knows the refusal at ingest.\n(4) R-3 owns channels with no admitting rule and R-7 owns suggest-only channels, so one defect is not counted twice.\n(5) R-8 binds the integration test that checks counts against the admission ledger plus the page component test. The headless desktop run of /admin/admission stays as operational corroboration. The rubric no longer declares an e2e layer for R-8, because no e2e-layer runner records that page.\n(6) R-6 and R-10 keep a requirements check until P-006 and P-010 are built. Binding their tests then is one more check-only amendment, which re-hashes only those two BARs.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-014 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-07\nAmendment-Id: amend-e713f940b84682977c9b9259\nRequest-Hash: 5d6b9e98ebc49ecf8e0476e561ce9594d418a313b11d2703469bc9cb3612fca0\nActor: su-dab96471-48c6-40bf-a2b6-2ec7c5b052ca\nReason: Vetting critique thread-post:1160898 (consult conv-muxa97ja, EI-25264837891479905): rewrite r-1/r-10 as behaviour, add r-11 consent and r-12 quoting (D-004/D-012), tighten falsifiers (r-2 redelivery, r-4 same-problem, r-5 secret classes + non-secret survives, r-6 state set incl. refusal, r-7 note surfaced, r-8 count==ledger), cite D-NNN on every criterion, bind as-built tests on r-1..r-5, r-7, r-8, r-11, r-12.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-41368277-5252-4726-81b3-38cdbe8c3a99\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1161041\nApproved-At: 2026-10-07T00:55:10.154Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 48 → 49\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"voice-two-tier-elevenlabs-agent-2026-10-06","title":"Papercup voice: two-tier ElevenLabs agent and faster brain","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-06","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercup voice: two-tier ElevenLabs agent and faster brain\nslug: voice-two-tier-elevenlabs-agent-2026-10-06\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-07\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001..P-004 done. P-005 (WI-10006878) code complete on both clients per D-008: shared writer in @papercusp/chat-protocol, desktop wiring (20/20), portal host voice-turns route + voice flag on sendTurn, portal browser writer (69/69 portal tests, portal typecheck clean 2954 files). Test evidence bound to SPEC-P-005; mutation probe running. Voice release still held per D-001.\n\n**Next:** Bind the mutation evidence, certify SPEC-P-005, complete WI-10006878; then P-011 (tutorial token route), P-010, P-006, P-014.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10006874 — Verify the current ElevenLabs key can create and update conversational agents (convai_write) and mint conversation tokens. Re-measure the brain's first-word delay for a voice turn on the current buil… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006875 — Keep the agent definition as code and add an idempotent create/update sync to ElevenLabs that stores the agent id; unit tests against a mocked ElevenLabs API. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006876 — Build the ask_papercup brain tool: extend the desktop client tool in elevenlabs-conv.ts and add client tools to the portal's voice-elevenlabs.ts, calling converse for the same conversation, with the … <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006877 — Inject Papercup's persona and recent conversation context at session start through per-session overrides, with secrets and other workspaces' data excluded. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006878 — Write every voice turn (user, front reply, brain answer) into the same Papercup conversation so text chat shows it. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006879 — EI-11963: build a slimmer converse path for voice turns that keeps tool access; measure first-word delay before and after on the same build. <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006880 — Wire the rebuilt engine into desktop and cloud voice settings. Return the ElevenLabs agent, and hosted ElevenLabs TTS once a real hosted call passes, to the release availability sets in `packages/ope… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006881 — Tests in the real suites for the sync, tool bridge, transcript writes and failure/timeout paths, plus a synthetic-voice round trip (voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01#D-006) that records first-rep… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006882 — Avi's real-microphone session on desktop and cloud, the acceptance rubric with an independent grade, then ship. <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006883 — Tutorial voice agent: a tutorial-only agent profile built from the P-002 definition whose single tool is the existing scoped tutorial-help endpoint. Opt-in microphone in the Guide; spoken questions a… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006884 — Protect Papercusp's ElevenLabs key for free tutorial users (D-002): key only on the server; short-lived token minting gated on a signed-in user, same origin and an active tutorial in their own worksp… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006885 — Bring the tutorial plan along: record the spoken-questions requirement and its acceptance on cloud-app-live-tutorial-2026-10-01 and make its final release wait on P-010 and P-011; coordinate with tha… <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006886 — Papercup chat voice keys in the cloud: each user can bring their own key per engine (stored per user, server-side only), plus an entitlement hook so a subscription plan can switch on Papercusp's acco… <!-- P-013 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006887 — Measure every voice backend with a real call on desktop and cloud and record the matrix on the plan: speaking (Kokoro, browser, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Cartesia), listening (local Whisper, Web Speech, De… <!-- P-014 -->\n- [ ] WI-10006888 — Cloud parity: the cloud portal offers every backend the desktop offers (today only ElevenLabs conversation and the LiveKit pipeline), each enabled when a working key exists (Papercusp's or the user's… <!-- P-015 -->\n## Background\n\n- voice-public-release-readiness-2026-07-12 (architecture ratified by Avi 2026-07-12) already made Papercup one identity with two layers: a fast front (papercup-fast, the converse path) and a hidden deep brain (papercup-deep, reached through coord). That \"fast\" front measured 21.9s to its first word (EI-11963, 2026-07-14, :3170: transcription 0.59s, first brain delta 21.9s, about $0.65 per turn), so it cannot hold a live conversation. The dock that hosts papercup-deep has been dark since 2026-07-13. This plan keeps the one-identity, two-layer idea, puts an ElevenLabs agent in the fast-front seat, and makes the converse path the brain it calls.\n- Old ElevenLabs design: desktop `packages/operator-core/lib/voice-engines/elevenlabs-conv.ts` + `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-mcp/operator-elevenlabs-bootstrap.ts`. An ElevenLabs-hosted agent, configured by hand on the ElevenLabs dashboard, owned the conversation; Papercup's brain was reachable only through the in-page client tool `ask_operator` (`askOperatorViaSse`). The portal copied the pattern (`portal/apps/host/src/voice-elevenlabs.ts`, `portal/packages/ui/src/voice-elevenlabs.ts`) with no client tools at all. It broke because of a cost pause (WI-3448), a wrong stored credential (EI-20188752837958263), a key without convai_write (WI-2146515), and the agent being gone from the current account.\n- voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01#D-007: the new ElevenLabs key works for TTS; the full ElevenLabs agent is out of the current release; hosted (cloud) ElevenLabs TTS stays off until the hosted credential passes a real hosted call.\n- Avi (directive #1479): on the cloud app listening already happens on a remote server, so the network latency is paid anyway, which favours ElevenLabs.\n- Trade-off analysis: WI-10006773.\n\n## Goal\n\nTalking to Papercup by voice feels like a conversation (first spoken reply in about a second) and is still one Papercup: same persona, same memory and tools for real work, and the same conversation history as text chat.\n\n## Scope\n\nIn: desktop and cloud portal voice; the ElevenLabs agent definition kept as code; a Papercup brain tool; persona and recent context at session start; one shared transcript; the EI-11963 voice speed-up; tests in the real suites; Avi's real-microphone acceptance.\n\nOut: the TUI and Phone app pipelines (unchanged); the cloud tutorial's read-aloud voice (output only, see Open questions); changes to text chat; reviving the dark dock.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Papercup answers a spoken turn within two seconds.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Voice must feel fast: a fast front holds the conversation (Avi chose fast front + faster brain).\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:25\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:23\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:26\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A synthetic-voice round trip on desktop records the ElevenLabs agent first spoken reply less than 2 seconds after the user stops speaking.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The first spoken reply takes 2 seconds or longer.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"fast front\",\n      \"synthetic round trip\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — A slow brain answer never leaves the call silent.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The front calls Papercup's brain with a holding line, timeout and spoken failure.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:25\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"An ask_papercup tool call that exceeds its timeout returns a spoken failure message to the caller.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A timed-out ask_papercup call returns nothing or hangs.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"brain tool bridge\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Voice turns show up in text chat.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Every voice turn is written into the same Papercup conversation.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:25\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A completed voice turn appears as messages in the Papercup conversation that text chat reads.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The conversation read by text chat lacks a message for a completed voice turn.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"transcript writes\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Voice sessions carry no secrets.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The agent gets Papercup's persona and recent context.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:25\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The per-session voice override omits every secret value from the injected conversation context.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A secret value appears in the session override payload.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"session context injection\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — The brain starts speaking sooner.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"In parallel, speed up the brain's voice path.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:25\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:23\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The slim voice converse path emits its first token sooner than the full converse path on the same build.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The slim path first-token time is equal to or later than the full path on the same build.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"converse latency\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — The tutorial voice agent stays on the lesson.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Add spoken questions to the cloud tutorial now.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:27\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A tutorial voice request for a task outside the lesson receives a refusal from the tutorial agent.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The tutorial agent performs a non-lesson task.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"tutorial voice agent\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Signed-out visitors cannot get a tutorial voice token.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Free users use Papercusp's ElevenLabs key for the tutorial, and the key must be secured.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A tutorial voice token request from a signed-out user is refused.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A signed-out request receives a conversation token.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"token minting\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-8 — A user over the daily limit cannot get a tutorial voice token.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The Papercusp key must not be drainable by free use.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A tutorial voice token request beyond the user daily minute limit is refused.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A token is minted after the user daily minute limit is reached.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"usage limits\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-9 — The kill switch stops tutorial voice tokens.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Papercusp must be able to stop spend on its key immediately.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"No tutorial voice token is minted while the tutorial voice kill switch is on.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A token is minted while the kill switch is on.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"kill switch\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-10 — A user's own voice key stays on the server.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Papercup chat voice can use the user's own key or a subscription.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A user-supplied engine key is never returned to the browser by the voice keys endpoint.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A voice keys endpoint response contains the stored key value.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"user keys\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-11 — A voice backend is offered only after a real call passes.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Every voice backend must be supported on desktop and in the cloud.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12\",\n      \"session_turn:claude:70a32e52-d10e-419f-8fda-3254be7c44dd:0\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The voice settings offer a backend only after that backend has passed a real call.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The settings offer a backend with no passing real call recorded.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"backend matrix\",\n      \"cloud parity\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"automated tests written during implementation; the rubric binds their files once they exist\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n1. The fast front is an ElevenLabs conversational agent running a fast model. It handles greetings, clarifications and simple answers from the injected context. For anything that needs memory, tools or actions it says a short holding line (\"let me check\") and calls ask_papercup.\n2. The agent definition (model, voice, turn-taking, prompt template, tool schema) is versioned in our repo. An idempotent sync creates or updates the agent through the ElevenLabs API and stores its id in config. Nobody edits it by hand on the dashboard.\n3. ask_papercup is a client tool on both desktop and portal, so the desktop needs no public webhook. It calls the converse brain for the same conversation id, and has a timeout with a spoken failure message.\n4. Session start injects Papercup's persona and recent conversation context through per-session overrides. Secrets and other workspaces' data are never included.\n5. Every user utterance, front reply and brain answer is written into the same Papercup conversation (papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06#D-007, one backend), so voice and text show one history.\n6. EI-11963: a slimmer converse path for voice turns (smaller prompt and tool set, fast first sentence), measured before and after on the same build. As the brain gets faster, the front hands more turns straight to it.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-008, P-009 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-010, P-012 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-013 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-007, P-014, P-015, P-009 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Prerequisites and baseline\n\n- **P-001** `done` Verify the current ElevenLabs key can create and update conversational agents (convai_write) and mint conversation tokens. Re-measure the brain's first-word delay for a voice turn on the current build with the EI-11963 method as the baseline. Record both on the plan. — note: ← WI-10006874 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Fast front\n\n- **P-002** `done` Keep the agent definition as code and add an idempotent create/update sync to ElevenLabs that stores the agent id; unit tests against a mocked ElevenLabs API. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10006875 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Build the ask_papercup brain tool: extend the desktop client tool in elevenlabs-conv.ts and add client tools to the portal's voice-elevenlabs.ts, calling converse for the same conversation, with the holding line, timeout and spoken failure message. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10006876 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Inject Papercup's persona and recent conversation context at session start through per-session overrides, with secrets and other workspaces' data excluded. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10006877 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Write every voice turn (user, front reply, brain answer) into the same Papercup conversation so text chat shows it. blocked-by: P-003 — note: WI-10006878 committed close; independently audited SPEC-P-005 proof accepted; real migrated PG integration run 20866218 passed 3/3.\n\n## Phase 3 — Faster brain (in parallel)\n\n- **P-006** `todo` EI-11963: build a slimmer converse path for voice turns that keeps tool access; measure first-word delay before and after on the same build. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 4 — Wire, verify and accept\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Wire the rebuilt engine into desktop and cloud voice settings. Return the ElevenLabs agent, and hosted ElevenLabs TTS once a real hosted call passes, to the release availability sets in `packages/operator-core/lib/voice-release-availability.ts`. blocked-by: P-003, P-004, P-005\n- **P-008** `todo` Tests in the real suites for the sync, tool bridge, transcript writes and failure/timeout paths, plus a synthetic-voice round trip (voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01#D-006) that records first-reply and brain-answer latency. blocked-by: P-007\n- **P-009** `todo` Avi's real-microphone session on desktop and cloud, the acceptance rubric with an independent grade, then ship. blocked-by: P-006, P-008\n\n## Verification\n\nEach item ships tests in the repository's real suites. Latency is measured, not estimated: the P-001 baseline, the P-006 before/after, and the P-008 synthetic round trip. Final acceptance is Avi's real-microphone session (P-009).\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Does this rebuild gate the current public voice release (voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01), or ship after it? D-008 left this open.\n- Cloud tutorial (cloud-app-live-tutorial-2026-10-01, D-012/R-15): its voice only reads lesson steps and typed help answers aloud, with no microphone, so it does not need this agent. It follows the user's chosen voice engine, so it gets the ElevenLabs voice in the cloud as soon as hosted ElevenLabs TTS is verified (P-007). If the tutorial ever accepts spoken questions, it should reuse this agent rather than a second voice stack.\n\n\n## Phase 5 — Spoken tutorial questions\n\n- **P-010** `todo` Tutorial voice agent: a tutorial-only agent profile built from the P-002 definition whose single tool is the existing scoped tutorial-help endpoint. Opt-in microphone in the Guide; spoken questions and answers alongside text; mute and stop; cancel on step, scope, pause, exit and sign-out; text fallback whenever voice is unavailable. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-011** `wip` Protect Papercusp's ElevenLabs key for free tutorial users (D-002): key only on the server; short-lived token minting gated on a signed-in user, same origin and an active tutorial in their own workspace; tutorial-only agent with a maximum session length; one live session per user; per-user, per-workspace and global daily minute limits; kill-switch flag; separate restricted key with an ElevenLabs-side cap; mint audit log and alert. Tests for every refusal path. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: Successor recovered P-005 committed completion; claimed P-011 and identified hosted authenticated tutorial boundary plus durable usage/budget reuse candidates.\n- **P-012** `done` Bring the tutorial plan along: record the spoken-questions requirement and its acceptance on cloud-app-live-tutorial-2026-10-01 and make its final release wait on P-010 and P-011; coordinate with that plan's driver. — note: ← WI-10006885 completed (done)\n\n\n\n## Phase 6 — Every backend on desktop and cloud\n\n- **P-013** `todo` Papercup chat voice keys in the cloud: each user can bring their own key per engine (stored per user, server-side only), plus an entitlement hook so a subscription plan can switch on Papercusp's account. Free users without a key get text plus free read-aloud. blocked-by: P-011\n- **P-014** `todo` Measure every voice backend with a real call on desktop and cloud and record the matrix on the plan: speaking (Kokoro, browser, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Cartesia), listening (local Whisper, Web Speech, Deepgram), full conversation (ElevenLabs, OpenAI Realtime, Gemini Live, LiveKit pipeline), wake word (openWakeWord, Porcupine). Name each missing key. blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-015** `todo` Cloud parity: the cloud portal offers every backend the desktop offers (today only ElevenLabs conversation and the LiveKit pipeline), each enabled when a working key exists (Papercusp's or the user's own). Return each engine to the release sets in packages/operator-core/lib/voice-release-availability.ts only after a real call passes. Tests in the real suites. blocked-by: P-013, P-014\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Avi approves the plan: this session builds it under AUTO; the voice release waits; spoken tutorial questions are added now\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, owner-typed, directive #1489, session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12] Verbatim: \"i approve thge plan.  you build it yourself now on auto mode.  hold the release.  add spoken questions now.\"\nMeaning: (1) plan approved; route = this session (su-5cc3d9e5), AUTO registered via mode:set. (2) voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01 does not ship until this plan's P-009 passes. (3) cloud-app-live-tutorial-2026-10-01 gets spoken questions in its first release through this plan's agent (P-010 to P-012). Builds on voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01#D-008.\nRelated: P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012\n\n### D-002 — Tutorial voice runs on Papercusp's ElevenLabs account for every user, including free; chat voice uses the user's own key or a subscription\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, owner-typed, directive #1489, session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12] Verbatim: \"for the tutorial i want all users to be able to access that so that should use the papercusp elevenlabs key, how can we secure that.  For the papercup chat we can ask them to bring their own key or maybe include that as part of the subscription plan, but i want free users to be able to use our elevnlabs account for the tutorial.\"\nSecurity design [self-imposed under AUTO, disclosed to Avi; implemented in P-011]:\n1. The key never reaches a browser. The hosted server keeps it in hosted secrets and mints short-lived, single-use ElevenLabs conversation tokens.\n2. A token is minted only for a signed-in hosted user, on a same-origin request, with an active tutorial run in that user's own workspace (reusing the existing hosted origin/tenant checks and authorizeTutorialHelp).\n3. Tokens are for a tutorial-only agent: tutorial prompt, a maximum session length, and one tool, the existing scoped tutorial-help endpoint. The free account cannot act as a general assistant or reach Papercup's full tools.\n4. Limits: one live session per user; daily minutes per user and per workspace; a global daily cap; a kill-switch flag. Any limit hit falls back to the text lesson and free read-aloud.\n5. A separate ElevenLabs key (or workspace) restricted to what the tutorial needs, with a usage cap set on the ElevenLabs side, so abuse or a leak cannot drain the main account.\n6. Every mint is logged (user, workspace, seconds) with an alert on unusual use; new accounts need a verified email.\nChat voice: bring-your-own-key first, plus an entitlement hook so a subscription plan can switch on Papercusp's account. Which of the two Avi sells is his pricing call (open question).\nRelated: P-011, P-013\n\n### D-003 — Every voice backend must work in the cloud as well as the desktop\nDate: 2026-10-06\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-06, owner-typed, directive #1489, session_turn:claude:132e32d0-80b4-403b-983b-13ca112c9885:12] Verbatim: \"Also, we had other backends supported other than elevenlabs, i want those supported too, what is the status of those other backends, the cloud versions should support these other backends as well.\"\nStatus read from source 2026-10-06 [from code plus voice-final-public-release-2026-10-01#D-005's 03:34Z key check; live calls not re-run yet, P-014 does that]: speaking voices: Kokoro (free, local) on; browser voice on; ElevenLabs on for desktop, off in the cloud until the hosted key passes a real call; OpenAI and Cartesia built but off because no key is set. Listening: local Whisper (default) and Web Speech on; Deepgram built, key not checked. Full conversation engines: ElevenLabs conversational, OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live are built but off (ElevenLabs agent deleted; OpenAI key unset; Gemini key not checked). Wake word: openWakeWord on; Porcupine off (no Picovoice key). The cloud portal offers only two engines: ElevenLabs conversation and the LiveKit phone pipeline (portal/packages/ui/src/voice-engine-choice.ts).\nRuling: P-013 to P-015 bring every backend to the cloud, each switched on when a working key exists (Papercusp's or the user's own) and only after a real call passes.\nRelated: P-014, P-015\n\n### D-004 — P-001 results: the key is fully capable, the configured agent is gone, brain baseline is ~15.9s to first word\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. Measured by su-5cc3d9e5 (P-001, WI-10006874). [measured]\n\n**ElevenLabs key (stored server-side in operator_voice_credentials; never printed).** Probe .papercusp/scratch/el-key-scope-probe.mts at 19:27Z: GET /v1/user/subscription 200 (tier grant_tier_2_2025_07_23, active, 61 of 33,010,000 characters used); GET /v1/convai/agents 200 with 0 agents on the account; POST /v1/convai/agents/create 200; PATCH agent 200; GET /v1/convai/conversation/token for the new agent 200; DELETE agent 204. So the key can create, update and delete conversational agents and mint conversation tokens.\n\n**The agent id saved in voice settings no longer exists.** prefs.elevenLabsAgentId returns 404 for both conversation/token and get-signed-url, and the account holds zero agents. Desktop ElevenLabs conversational voice therefore cannot start today. Consequence for P-002: the sync must CREATE the agent when the stored id is missing or 404s, store the new id, and treat an unknown id as \"create\", not as an error. Cause (deleted vs. key switched to another account) not established [inferred: the account has 0 agents, so either the agent was deleted or the key belongs to a different account than the one that created it]; asked in consult conv-mux2ra8a.\n\n**Brain first-word baseline (EI-11963 method: one modality:voice operator-converse turn, no conversationId, prompt \"Can you hear me? Answer in one short sentence.\").** Probe .papercusp/scratch/voice-brain-ttft-probe.mts at 19:30Z:\n- :3170 (build b80afaf91e): first text 15,847 ms, done 17,070 ms, cost $0.343; setup (provenance event) at 3,301 ms.\n- :3070 (build d740fc3802): first text 15,948 ms, done 16,555 ms, cost $0.346; setup at 2,817 ms.\nEI-11963 recorded 21.9 s and $0.646 on 2026-07-14. The improvement is real but a 16 s wait is still far too long for live voice, which confirms the two-tier design: the ElevenLabs front must answer immediately and cover the wait while ask_papercup runs. P-006 targets this baseline.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-006\n\n### D-005 — Build on the existing voice seams: release-availability switch, instant-ack filler, and a new token route for the tutorial\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. Source: consult conv-mux2ra8a, answered from su-d7c6542c's voice transcript (fork su-b4e38fdc, 19:33Z). [peer:su-b4e38fdc — file paths named below, behaviour to be re-read before each dependent edit]\n\n- The cloud tutorial's spoken lesson today is plain text-to-speech: apps/operator/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-assistance.tsx POSTs to the tutorial-speech route, which calls synthesize() (tts-synth.ts, EL /v1/text-to-speech). There is NO ElevenLabs conversation-token route in the tutorial path yet; P-011 adds it. That route refuses ElevenLabs on hosted builds via isHostedTtsEngineUnavailable() until the hosted credential is verified.\n- packages/operator-core/lib/voice-release-availability.ts still lists elevenlabs-conv / elevenlabs-conversational in RELEASE_UNAVAILABLE_FULL_AGENT_ENGINES; voice-mode.ts refuses that engine before any provider call and the settings picker disables it. P-007 re-enables it THROUGH that file (remove the entry, update voice-release-availability.test.ts) after P-009 accepts — never by bypassing it.\n- apps/operator/app/_components/voice/VoiceAppBridge.tsx already speaks an instant acknowledgement before the slow converse answer (its comment cites a 15-24 s first token). P-003 reuses that filler pattern while ask_papercup is pending.\n- The working key is Avi's new sk_ key stored locally on 2026-10-06 (WI-10006757); the old agent id most likely lived in the account behind the previous key. Deleted vs. different account cannot be distinguished; either way P-002 provisions a new agent under the working key and stores its id.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-007, P-010, P-011\n\n### D-006 — ask_papercup waits for the brain under a 40 s client deadline; ElevenLabs speaks the holding line via forced pre-tool speech\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO; follows plan Design #1 and #3; supersedes the 'ack now, answer spoken separately' wording in P-002's first definition]\nMeasured live 2026-10-06 20:24Z: an ElevenLabs client tool accepts pre_tool_speech:'force' (read back force_pre_tool_speech:true, execution_mode 'immediate') and response_timeout_secs 60. ElevenLabs has no client API that makes the agent speak arbitrary text; sendUserMessage would put the answer in the transcript as a user turn.\nRuling: (1) ask_papercup has pre_tool_speech 'force', so the front agent always says a short holding line before it runs. (2) The client tool waits for Papercup's answer and returns it as the line to say. (3) It runs under VOICE_BRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 40 s on the client; ElevenLabs waits 50 s, so the user hears our spoken timeout line, never ElevenLabs' generic tool error. (4) Shared contract (tool name, deadline, timeout / failure / empty-question lines, answerVoiceQuestion) lives in libs/generic/chat-protocol/src/voice-brain-tool.ts and is used by the desktop (elevenlabs-conv.ts) and the portal (voice-elevenlabs.ts). P-010's tutorial profile inherits this tool shape; P-006 (faster brain) is what shortens the wait.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-006, P-010\n\n### D-007 — The session prompt override is opt-in per agent; P-007 must switch it on for both desktop and portal\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO; from P-004's build] ElevenLabs refuses the whole session when a client sends an override the agent does not allow, so the two-tier session prompt is sent only when the agent is declared to accept it. Desktop: elevenlabs-conv.ts sends the server-built prompt only when its caller passes twoTier:true. Portal: the token mint carries promptOverride, true only when the host sets PORTAL_ELEVENLABS_PROMPT_OVERRIDE=1; the browser sends overrides.agent.prompt.prompt only then. The portal never builds the prompt itself: GET /api/papercup-chat/conversations/:chatId/voice-session checks chat ownership, then relays the operator's /api/agent-mcp/operator-voice-session (one persona, one redactor, one workspace filter). Consequence for P-007: syncing the front agent must (1) allow the prompt override on the ElevenLabs agent, (2) pass twoTier:true on desktop when that agent is selected, and (3) set PORTAL_ELEVENLABS_PROMPT_OVERRIDE=1 where the portal uses it. Until then both paths run on the agent's stored prompt.\n\n### D-008 — Voice transcript writes: one writer per turn kind, and the brain never re-writes the front's question\nDate: 2026-10-06\nDate: 2026-10-06. [self-imposed under AUTO; P-005 (WI-10006878), serves R-3 and plan Design #5 'voice and text show one history']\n\n[observed from code 2026-10-06 21:55-22:00Z] Desktop two-tier path: /api/agent-mcp/operator-converse persists nothing (the text chat provider writes its own turns), so the user's words, the front's replies and the brain's answer are all absent from the conversation today. Portal: ask_papercup goes through sendTurn, which writes the front's paraphrased question as a text_typed user turn plus the answer; the user's own words and the front's replies are never written.\n\nRuling:\n1. User utterance (ElevenLabs final user transcript) is written by the voice client: role user, source voice_stt.\n2. Front reply (ElevenLabs agent text, including the forced holding line) is written by the voice client: role assistant, source voice_tts, except a reply that repeats a brain answer already written in this session, which is skipped.\n3. Brain answer is written once, as role assistant, source voice_tts. Desktop: by the voice client when ask_papercup returns an answered result. Portal: by the host's sendTurn in voice mode.\n4. The brain path never writes the front's question as a user turn; the user's own words from (1) are the user turn. The question still goes to the brain as its last message.\n5. The dedupe logic lives once, in @papercusp/chat-protocol (libs/generic/chat-protocol), which both surfaces already import.\n6. Portal browsers cannot write turns directly (the append route is loopback-only), so the portal host gets an owned-chat route for voice turns.\nP-007 must wire the two-tier engine through this writer on both surfaces.\n"},{"harness_slug":"portal","plan_slug":"acceptance-portal-small-viewport-no-clipping-2026-10-06","title":"Acceptance BAR — Portal: never clip content on low-resolution / small windows — scroll or compact instead","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-06","owner":"su-85f4857a-35b6-4e7b-929f-3f29b3949d93","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Portal: never clip content on low-resolution / small windows — scroll or compact instead\nslug: acceptance-portal-small-viewport-no-clipping-2026-10-06\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-06\nupdated: 2026-10-06\nowner: su-85f4857a-35b6-4e7b-929f-3f29b3949d93\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Portal: never clip content on low-resolution / small windows — scroll or compact instead\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Diagnosis WI-10007186 is done. The prior self-ownership defect is fixed; this effort addresses additional gaps recommended in turn 45. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nOwner-approved SELF/AUTO operational recovery. Hold WI-10007282; diagnose actual native gateway custody before repairs. Existing streamed-quota failover and credit selection are reused.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Product shaping\n**Audience:** Avi and the custodians of the affected Codex sessions.\n**Problem:** Sessions launched through auto routing showed quota banners or could not resume even while another gateway account had capacity. Native route custody, upstream response delay and missing transcript bytes are distinct failure classes.\n**Outcome:** Each confirmed affected session either resumes productively under its original custody with attributable gateway evidence, or has an exact, owned recovery boundary. Durable code repairs have project-suite regression proof and separately identified runtime adoption.\n**Non-goals:** Rebuild the existing gateway failover or credit selector; change explicit default routes; alter intentional stops, model/effort, fleet scope or carry; restart or change the shared Codex daemon; launch more agents; operate the live release gate.\n**Source turns:** session_turn:codex:01a11806-d0ba-79b1-9764-4c2f4b8abcba:1, :3, :7, :9, :12, :14, :15, :17; session_turn:codex:01a12cc5-b2a5-7371-8c0b-5319cd8abdee:1, :8; session_turn:codex:01a131dc-033a-7660-90aa-9724c2dabd82:8, :13, :16, :18, :19, :26. These indexed CLI turns currently have unenrolled-origin provenance; do not label that metadata owner-verified.\n**Scenarios:** An auto-routed session at a quota banner uses an eligible account and resumes the same native transcript; a route repair refusal leaves the original child intact and obeys the bounded attempt budget; an intentional stop or explicit default route remains respected; a restored transcript identifies its backup cutoff without inventing later bytes; a response timeout is described from measured TTFB rather than an asserted local outage.\n**Acceptance boundaries:** Current-build tests establish local behavior. Stable public normal-wake custody requires the loaded executor guard plus an original-owner gateway request and productive pickup. Source completion alone cannot satisfy that live acceptance. Missing late transcript bytes remain accountable under WI-6554700010009478.\n**Preparation and sequence:** Seeded acceptance BAR adoption epoch/cohort and class on 2026-10-14. Define independent per-item contracts; evaluate the exact spec set, preserve independent grading, then audit canonical source mappings before plan activation. Reconcile historical P-001/P-002 evidence before rebuilding. P-006 custodian ownership and original-session lifecycle permission remain separate from plan preparation.\n\n## Background\nAvi reported usage-limit stalls despite auto routing and available usage credits. EI-25353970836557296 records a stale status/runtime discrepancy, not a proved request-level cause. Existing provider implementation is owned under codex-hot-failover-and-startup-routing-2026-10-07; source custody WI-10006825 remains peer-owned. September recovery plans returned by dedup are shipped; this is new October operational recovery, not their continuation.\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Cause.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Distinguish actual pool exhaustion, gateway bypass, hard pins, stale quota latch and late-stream failure using affected native configuration and attributed request evidence.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Distinguish actual pool exhaustion, gateway bypass, hard pins, stale quota latch and late-stream failure using affected native configuration and attributed request evidence.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A session diagnosis is asserted without native route and attributed request evidence, or a status flag is treated as proof of productive recovery.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read WI-10007282 and linked per-session checkpoints. For each affected owner, compare the persisted account choice, actual native provider, gateway owner-report request outcomes and productive pickup receipt. Retain timestamped evidence and explicitly distinguish verified exhaustion, gateway bypass, hard pins, stale latch and late-stream failure. Historical evidence is labeled historical.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Repair.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Extend existing launch/routing/recovery seams only for a measured remaining defect; conventional regression tests and runtime adoption verification are required.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Extend existing launch/routing/recovery seams only for a measured remaining defect; conventional regression tests and runtime adoption verification are required.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A route-repair refusal destroys the predecessor, a repaired auto resume bypasses the gateway, or stable runtime adoption is claimed while the executing artifact lacks the tested guard.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the project PTY quota-route integration scenarios; inspect baseline/root-cause evidence on EI-25718715891348473 and WI-6554700010011953. Read dev:pipeline_position for wake-executor.ts and psu-pty-host.mjs, select the maintained current-build route and verify its loaded code. Stable public normal-wake acceptance additionally needs the public executor load receipt. No live gate operation is authorized.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host-turn.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Recover.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Resume confirmed issue-stalled Codex sessions with unchanged owner, transcript, fleet scope, claims, model/effort and warm carry; respect intentional stops and prevent replay of tool side effects.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Resume confirmed issue-stalled Codex sessions with unchanged owner, transcript, fleet scope, claims, model/effort and warm carry; respect intentional stops and prevent replay of tool side effects.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Recovery changes custody/native identity or selected session settings, overrides an intentional stop, or replays an owner prompt/tool side effect.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the native identity/owner-input and refused-route PTY recovery controls. Before a permitted live recovery, snapshot exact owner/UUID/home/model/effort/fleet/carry/claims and current stop state; compare after the supported lifecycle action. Do not duplicate an active writer, wake an intentional hold or act on peer-held custody without the custodian.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host-turn.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Delivery.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Verify attributed successful requests and productive pickup per recovered session; record accountable residue. Preserve the separate daemon-settings answer and do not change or restart the Codex daemon.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Verify attributed successful requests and productive pickup per recovered session; record accountable residue. Preserve the separate daemon-settings answer and do not change or restart the Codex daemon.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A recovered-session outcome lacks successful request attribution or productive pickup, residue is unowned, or recovery alters/restarts the shared Codex daemon.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read the per-session gateway success receipt and subsequent productive custodian reply for every recovery claimed. Reconcile exact unresolved suffix/adoption boundaries with owned work-items. Publish the complete owner-facing outcome report and read it back; include daemon-setting consequences and an explicit unchanged-daemon action record. Keep final public acceptance separate from current-build testing.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n## Design\nReuse managed Codex homes, auto gateway selection, quota recovery/stall-waker and supported same-session resume mechanisms. Preserve the current desktop route and account selection; no production release/gate operations, no database changes, no unsafe replay of dispatched writes. EI-25349866237234695 is a separately owned Sessions-summary latency follow-up, not the shared blank-GUI cause.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Superseded incident notebook underD001; allP001-P006 evidence settled through original assigned incidents. Two best-effort presence writes retry indefinitely and monopolize the origin scheduler; sync reads time out before backend dispatch while direct backend reads remain populated.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Restore the dev connection.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Repair the dev GUI connection.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The selected dev operator publishes its own usable IPC endpoint and the actual desktop reads populated accounts, agent roster and pots.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Selected operator has no usable endpoint, desktop IPC is never-connected, or direct populated data remains invisible in that window.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read operator per-port discovery and native endpoint_ipc_status, then compare actual desktop DOM/query evidence to same-runtime populated backend responses.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n\n**R-2 — Prevent starvation.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Prevent stuck heartbeats from blocking data reads.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Presence is background-priority, has one pending request per mounted hook and aborts on a bounded deadline/unmount without replaying dispatched writes.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Overlapping presence calls stack indefinitely, occupy interactive-control slots, or ignore cancellation.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run canonical hook tests with a hanging abort-aware route double, fake timers, repeated heartbeat ticks and unmount.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/ui/use-ui-presence.test.tsx\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n\n**R-3 — Guard recurrence.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Test the repair and verify real desktop data.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Focused regression tests pass and the existing desktop route displays populated data on the fixed current build.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Regression suite fails, data reads still time out before dispatch, or verification uses a different runtime/window.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Record canonical Vitest run and actual native bridge process/URL, IPC status, sync queue and DOM evidence after loading fixed current SPA.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n Compare the observations named in this criterion's method; retain falsifying evidence before corrected passes and clean up synthetic fixtures.\"}}\n```\n## Design\nExtend existing surfaces rather than build another speech/agent stack:\n- One authorized/bounded content representation for extracted text and source references, shared by narration and summary consumers. Agents may supply already-read content; remote/file/document retrieval reuses existing permission-bearing readers and must not introduce unrestricted server-side fetching. Selected text is first class. HTML uses Mozilla Readability and text-bearing PDFs use PDF.js if existing readers do not cover them; scanned sources expose an OCR/access limitation, not invented content.\n- Keep synthesize(), voice preferences, release availability, existing local Kokoro port and playback lease/mute seams. Intl.Segmenter supplies sentence boundaries, with provider-size splitting of unusually long sentences. Speech is nonoverlapping and lossless. No second Kokoro/Transformers stack.\n- Extend voice:say with explicit narration/session behavior while preserving backwards-compatible short replies. UI uses existing output-only playback and maintained controls. Add controls to existing voice surfaces rather than invent a new app/screen scaffold.\n- Normal speech uses a production synthesis path, never settings-preview truncation. Incremental synthesis uses bounded backpressure, cancellation and explicit lifecycle receipts. The chosen provider is stable for a reading; current settings apply when the next reading starts. Never silently change local speech into cloud speech.\n- Summaries use the existing model/account gateway and budget/task primitives. Direct native-agent summaries remain direct when complete input already fits the active context. Large/repeatable jobs use structure/token-aware segmentation and hierarchical synthesis, with source references and explicit coverage/limitations. A framework is not a better brain: @langchain/textsplitters is an optional narrow helper; LlamaIndex tree-summarize is a reference pattern, not a mandatory new Python service.\n- Cache only by authorized subject, source hash/version, summary options and effective model/protocol. Bound/cancel jobs using existing task manager rather than a second queue. Treat extracted material as quoted untrusted data, never execution instructions.\n- Original read and summary-and-read are distinct modes. Preserve the original content and make edits/omissions explicit.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-007, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-9 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-24 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-25 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-26 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-27 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-28 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-29 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-30 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-31 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-32 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-33 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-34 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-35 | P-007, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-36 | P-007, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-37 | P-007, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-38 | P-007, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-39 | P-007, P-008 | deployed |\n| R-40 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-41 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-42 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-43 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-44 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-45 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-46 | P-005 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Shared content and speech foundation\n- **P-001** `done` Implement the bounded shared content intake/provenance contract and maintained extraction adapters; Source session_turn:codex:01a1175d-c148-70c1-92d8-588826ff4234:10. This session implements directly; no client-native subagent fan-out or fleet-route substitution. AUTO is registered, manual file locks apply, and work continues until acceptance and verified shipped status.\n### D-002 — Reuse is the default; libraries support plumbing\n2026-10-07. Source session_turn:codex:01a1175d-c148-70c1-92d8-588826ff4234:7 and session_turn:codex:01a1175d-c148-70c1-92d8-588826ff4234:10 accepting the answer in turn9. Reuse shared speech/model/content/permission/job surfaces. Choose modular maintained extraction/splitting helpers only when existing readers do not fit.
