Reuse the existing workspace-host executors, acceptance journals, Vitest integration suites, Playwright fixtures, and isolated native verifier. This is a new cross-feature acceptance campaign, not a replacement of BYOC, AWS parity, or tutorial implementation plans.\n\nThe owner asked: “Write a plan for putting our cloud features through thorough end to end testing and then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped status yourself now.” No native-agent or fleet delegation. Existing live release ownership is respected.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Complete source-backed feature census.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Enumerate the exposed hosted cloud and GCP/AWS BYOC journeys, supported environments, route writers, dependencies, current acceptance evidence, and resource cleanup. Every census entry must have an assigned scenario and explicit result; unsupported provider options must fail closed rather than appear validated.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Enumerate the exposed hosted cloud and GCP/AWS BYOC journeys, supported environments, route writers, dependencies, current acceptance evidence, and resource cleanup. Every census entry must have an assigned scenario and explicit result; unsupported provider options must fail closed rather than appear validated.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A documented supported cloud journey, provider/runtime, required failure path or resource obligation has no scenario/result entry.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Inspect current hosted/BYOC route and UI writers; enumerate every documented cloud journey/provider/runtime in the P-001 scenario census, partition each into checked/notChecked/notApplicable, and verify each has test and cleanup evidence or an owned gap.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Persistent end-to-end coverage.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Cover sign-in and organization/workspace admission; setup and provider credential validation; configure and cost review; provision to healthy connection; launch and complete an agent task; desktop/browser interaction; stop/start and reconnect; snapshot and restore; repair and failed provisioning; billing/entitlements; tutorial pause/resume; destroy and resource accounting. Add missing regression scenarios in the project's actual test frameworks and affected-suite routing.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Cover sign-in and organization/workspace admission; setup and provider credential validation; configure and cost review; provision to healthy connection; launch and complete an agent task; desktop/browser interaction; stop/start and reconnect; snapshot and restore; repair and failed provisioning; billing/entitlements; tutorial pause/resume; destroy and resource accounting. Add missing regression scenarios in the project's actual test frameworks and affected-suite routing.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A supported happy-path journey lacks a persistent passing end-to-end or integration guard, or the affected suite does not select it.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\",\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run canonical API lifecycle tests and the real-component Cloud first-agent browser journey; inspect the resulting ledger rows, traces and affected-suite selection. Distinguish real provider outcomes from mocked HTTP or fake-provider coverage.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Verify unauthorized access, tenant/workspace switching, stale credentials, delayed or failed operations, retries and duplicate submission, idempotence, reload/reconnect, unavailable provider and transport, redaction, keyboard/accessibility, and cleanup after partial failure. Distinguish real provider outcomes from mocked HTTP or fake-provider coverage.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An unauthorized/duplicate/stale operation succeeds, recovery loses state, secrets leak, or a required failure/recovery scenario remains untested.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\",\n      \"e2e\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Execute isolation, unauthorized access, failure/retry, chaos and UI reload/permission scenarios; include at least one negative control per permission/lifecycle boundary and inspect sensitive output redaction.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/lifecycle-runner.chaos.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-lifecycle-policy.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/workspace-hosts/action.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/e2e/cloud-tutorial.spec.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/provisioning-runner.integration.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/lifecycle-runner.restore.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Verified durable repairs.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"For each discovered in-scope defect, register and own the repair, isolate the root cause with differing predictions, fix the originating layer, add a recurrence guard, and re-run the affected journey. Staging results alone do not meet this bar.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Plan is marked shipped from staging/fixture evidence, deployed artifact differs, final journey fails, or any required acceptance bar or owned residue remains unresolved.\"\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read the authoritative exact deployed app/desktop artifact receipt and authenticated serving identity, execute final cloud smoke/journey acceptance on that artifact, verify promotion/deployment receipts, complete source audit/independent grading and report publication/readback.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003, P-004 | live |\n| R-6 | P-005 | deployed |\n\n### Test matrix and evidence contract\n\nUse four complementary layers: maintained unit/contract regression tests; database and API integration; browser/native UI journeys; real hosted and BYOC lifecycle canaries. Fixtures establish UI/control behavior only. Provider tests must establish actual create/readiness/task/recovery/destroy behavior and resource-accounting closure.\n\nFor each scenario record: feature/provider/runtime, prerequisites, isolated identity, source and served artifact hashes, exact test reference, expected observations, result and evidence path, cleanup receipt, and remaining gap. Census partitions are checked, notChecked and notApplicable, with owned residue separate.\n\nExisting surfaces to extend include apps/operator/e2e/cloud-tutorial.spec.ts, apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces tests, packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host and endpoint-route tests, libs/generic/deployment-driver tests, maintained clean-room/provider executors and acceptance/release journals, scripts/run-operator-e2e-isolated.sh and scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh. Inspect current docs and governing plan decisions before choosing their routes.\n\n### Sequencing and shipment\n\nP-001 defines population and acceptance. P-002 closes persistent coverage gaps. verify the exact deployed artifact and required tests/proof outcomes, then mark shipped and end this work loop. <!-- P-008 -->\n## Background\nReview rpt_0dbb8695-6e88-4a08-8e1d-c722175c4fa3 identified shape-only signature checks in stored governance admission and claimed certificate tallies not independently reconstructed. Six focused Vitest files passed, including fixtures with placeholder signatures; this is not cryptographic or formal security evidence. Existing DAO plan D-019/D-034 keeps P2P ratification authoritative and bounded Safe/Zodiac execution; this effort extends that architecture.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Authenticated governance.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Stored and federated ballot/control events are authenticated to eligible keys/epochs and permitted event roles before admission; invalid, forged, expired, revoked or replayed authority refuses.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a119a5-e2ff-7db1-8c46-b56dd497bda3:36\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Stored and federated ballot/control events authenticate to independently eligible keys, exact epochs and event roles before admission. Invalid, forged, expired, revoked and unauthorized replayed authority refuses; exact duplicate event replay is idempotent and cannot add voting weight or repeat a control effect.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any ONE holds: (1) a forged stored event or ballot signature admits; (2) wrong epoch, revoked/expired signer, unauthorized control role or foreign origin admits; (3) a claimed clean raw snapshot bypasses verification; (4) a self-appointed owner key verifies the signing roster. (5) same-epoch ballot/control replay changes the accepted vote weight or control outcome; (6) a signature replays into another pot, round, revision, action or signed domain.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run canonical test:file on the bound suites. Reuse Ed25519/standard signing helpers; authenticate independent voter keys, canonical domain and authority snapshots rather than trusting a supplied signature string or peer membership alone. Refuse unverifiable legacy authorization records; support an explicit re-ratification/upgrade path.\nP2P: extend current Hypercore/Hyperbee/Hyperswarm admission, provenance, policy and authority surfaces. Census first; identify current test/proof seams before edits.\nProof: choose maintained tooling after checking the local toolchain. Minimize the trusted kernel and state the link between formal model and runtime. Testing, model checking and theorem/SMT proofs are separate evidence classes. Cryptographic security, key custody, external chain/issuer behavior and human factual judgment are assumptions, not consequences of tally correctness.\nDelivery: use current-build acceptance first. Read gate ownership before live release operations; coordinate with any existing live owner once. Shipping requires an honest per-feature matrix naming proved, model-checked, tested and unverified aspects.\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-08\nAmendment-Id: dao-security-rubric-critic-repair-20261008-v3\nRequest-Hash: c13e7dd821cdcf9be0f283e320628cd634fde431811ca05a19e82b48722f2586\nActor: su-6788d0ac-d425-4756-a9b3-3a451df401be\nReason: Correct independent objection thread-post:1164367 as well as both original rubric critiques: explicitly preserve same-epoch replay refusal and mandatory authorized scope/trust safeguards. Split other compound outcomes and retain concrete negatives/real check paths.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-6e6fdafb-635c-4002-81df-7811d965e697\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1164380\nApproved-At: 2026-10-08T07:32:18.361Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 4 → 5\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-004 — One coherent weighted threshold and replacement rule\nDate: 2026-10-08\nDate: 2026-10-08. Derived implementation decision under Avi's AUTO authorization, preserving D-001/D-002. Quorum uses participating delegated weight / exact eligible weight; abstentions count toward quorum, not approval. Approval uses approve weight / non-abstaining cast weight, must meet the signed policy BPS threshold and remain a strict majority (the existing majority safeguard). Use exact positive safe-integer weights and bigint threshold cross-products. Every eligible weight follows one acyclic delegation chain to an active eligible terminal voter. Delegation epoch equals the delegator key epoch; expiry refuses at the boundary. Immutable ballots can be replaced only by a distinct event id and strictly advancing per-member sequence; reconstruction counts the latest ballot deterministically, refuses identical-sequence conflict, and preserves every ballot event id in the certificate. The exact round electorate is mandatory. The new privacy-card audit completion arrived after report publication; report's last-read pending status is a timestamped snapshot, and the current audit record governs closure.\nRelated: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-007 — Explicit finalization trust, clock and committed-ballot-set boundaries\nDate: 2026-10-08\nDerived clarification under Avi's direct AUTO authorization and D-002; preserves D-004's exact authenticated electorate, weighted thresholds, strict majority, advancing replacements and replay refusal. It grants no mainnet authority and makes no stronger proof claim.\nFinalization commits certificate.voteEventIds as the exact immutable ballot history selected by an authorized finalizer. Reconstruction requires every listed ballot to arrive, independently authenticate and reproduce the entire certificate; duplicate IDs refuse. Unlisted ballots cannot revise finality, including authentic backdated ballots or conflicting sequence values received across a partition. The local store refuses an unlisted ballot after seeing that round's finalization. This protects committed finality; it does not prove that the finalizer included every cast or withheld ballot. Authorized finalizers must honestly choose the ballot snapshot for that completeness/liveness property. Malicious finalizers still cannot fabricate selected signatures, bypass the exact roster or certify a false selected-set tally.\nEvent/round/finalization times are signer assertions. Numeric chronology and future-time guards are enforced, but they are not trusted timestamp attestation. Honest signer clocks and verifier time are necessary for expiry/ratification-window meaning; a trusted finalizer can select an older valid snapshot. The round-open role is explicit authority to supersede a round: latest createdAtMs then deterministic ID ordering selects its successor, which may suspend prior admission while incomplete. These roles are not ordinary-voter powers.\nThe pure finalizer now requires an explicit roster at type and runtime boundaries; no fallback to unweighted/unrevoked electorate IDs. It is still a reducer, not a signature verifier; the production certificate source supplies independently owner-anchored members/delegations. Receiver envelope checks plus immutable inserts and consumer full authentication remain separate boundaries. Member devices may relay another authorized signer's authentic immutable event; transport identity never substitutes for its signature. Provisional dependency-order rows are not certificates.\nMeasured: source reads plan-admission-certificate-source.ts135-205, plan-admission-governance-store.ts383-385, hive-settings.ts75-121; local canonical80PASS0skip at dirty130beea0d1 in /tmp/dao-security-explicit-roster-20261008.log, including omitted-roster refusal. Recover the late owner directive through canonical session_turn:codex:01a119c3-d80b-7323-9ad5-f7f0a385fb9d:18.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Background\n\nFull source conversation read: predecessor turns1–18. Avi asked for DAO discovery/join, member information, voting and all DAO areas; approved Workbench C and separate top-level operations / DAO Management tabs. This is distinct from dao-launch-workspace-2026-10-08, which owns a five-step entity setup checklist.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience:** People browsing or joining an organization, admitted members reviewing decisions and work, and operators managing existing organization records.\n\n**Problem:** The operations app exposes platform tools, while members need an organization-centered workspace connecting membership, governed proposals, projects, finances and records.\n\n**Outcome:** Workbench C provides a separate top-level DAO Management product, retains independent operations and DAO URL selections, and presents all nineteen interface areas using maintained data and permissions at desktop and phone widths.\n\n**Non-goals:** New public/global discovery infrastructure, legal formation, new payment/refund or treasury signer, new governance datastore, completing the backend economy/equity/security plans, and HR/people expansion. Existing membership, ordinary plan voting, treasury authority and equity governance remain separate. This acceptance concerns the current build; final deployed release verification remains separate.\n\n**Source turns:** session_turn:codex:01a119c3-d80b-7323-9ad5-f7f0a385fb9d:1 (interface inventory), :8 (three mockups), :18 (Workbench C, AUTO and top-level product switch); session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4 (approval of the implemented scope and one independent reviewer, D-001). Original Codex owner-origin stamps are historically unavailable; the later approval is a separate authenticated record. Do not infer or fabricate historical provenance.\n\n**Scenarios:**\n\n1. A person browses locally maintained directory entries, opens one organization and reads its membership and records. Foreign, unbound, loading, empty and failed reads remain distinguishable.\n2. A member creates a proposal in the selected linked project, reviews its exact persisted revision and uses the existing signed round/open/vote/finalize flow. A failed read, stale revision or unauthorized actor remains ineligible.\n3. A contributor opens Projects or Jobs, selects a linked project and reviews its maintained work and admission status. Finance and ownership screens show their own recorded bindings and permissions.\n4. A person moves from a selected DAO section to operations and back. Each product restores its independent selection, and operations retains its existing tabs/chat.\n5. On a 390-pixel phone and a 1440-pixel desktop, navigation, work fields and actions remain contained and usable. Native acceptance retains all nineteen captures and persisted isolated evidence, with failing controls.\n\n**Open acceptance conditions:** Current exact-source native proof, detector/binding adequacy and the supported independent grading route must be verified before formal completion. One reviewer is authorized; implementation remains self-directed in the current driver session.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Product switch.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Separate top-level Papercusp operations and DAO Management tabs; preserve independent URL selections and existing operations tabs.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Extend maintained app/backend surfaces; preserve the approved implemented scope and one-reviewer limit.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a119c3-d80b-7323-9ad5-f7f0a385fb9d:18\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Separate top-level Papercusp operations and DAO Management tabs; preserve independent URL selections and existing operations tabs.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Switching products loses selected DAO/section or operations tab.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run product-workspaces.test.ts and ChromeShell.test.tsx. Then run scripts/tauri-surface-verify-dao-workbench.sh with an exact committed source ref and explicit tested inputs; require the native reload/product-switch step to retain DAO plus section and restore the operations selection. Mandatory native outcome proof is the exact committed-source isolated wrapper result with retained SQL/signature/geometry/screenshot assertions; conventional tests alone do not establish it.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/app/_components/product-workspaces.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/app/_components/ChromeShell.test.tsx\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/chromeless-routes.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    },\n    \"replication\": \"Positive control: DAO selection and section survive DAO to Ops to DAO; the operations chat returns on Ops. Failing control: a default-only product link or DAO shell with operations rails must fail the bound product-workspaces/ChromeShell/chromeless-routes assertions. Native assertion requires the exact retained organization and governance view after switching.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Workbench C.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Organization sidebar, project workspace, action/evidence panels, responsive layout, existing app theme/components.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Extend maintained app/backend surfaces; preserve the approved implemented scope and one-reviewer limit.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a119c3-d80b-7323-9ad5-f7f0a385fb9d:18\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Organization sidebar, project workspace, action/evidence panels, responsive layout, existing app theme/components.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Narrow viewport clips the page or hides actions; workspace no longer follows C.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run workspace UI tests and scripts/tauri-surface-verify-dao-workbench.sh; inspect desktop/mobile captures and overflow assertions. Positive fixture: dao-workbench-identity-fixture.test.ts requires both boot geometries and isolated DB. In the maintained native Workbench leg visit the nineteen enumerated section IDs and retain directory, proposal and final inbox captures. Any missing section, foreign record or fabricated ready balance fails this BAR; a healthy record in one organization does not satisfy the foreign-scope controls.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Existing governed actions.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Browse/join, propose/vote/review flows reuse existing authorization. Plan voting, treasury signatures and equity governance remain separate. No invented data or parallel governance datastore.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Unsigned, revoked, foreign-origin, role-ineligible or stale-revision vote is accepted; a member ballot authorizes a financial action.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run governance positive/negative suite and isolated native proposal/open/vote/finalize/read/reload against production verifiers. Mandatory native outcome proof is the exact committed-source isolated wrapper result with retained SQL/signature/geometry/screenshot assertions; conventional tests alone do not establish it.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator-vite/src/components/dao/DaoGovernance.test.tsx\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/governance-local-action.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator-vite/src/components/dao/DaoWorkspace.test.tsx\"\n      ]\n    },\n    \"replication\": \"REPLICATION DRILL: run DaoGovernance.test.tsx and governance-local-action.test.ts. Positive control reviews the exact revision then submits the correctly scoped member action; negative controls retain ineligibility for stale review and role/key/peer failures. Run the isolated native Workbench desktop leg: save a real proposal, resolve its dated receipt, open a round, approve and finalize with the generated device key and real policy verifier. Require snapshot integrityErrors empty and exactly round-open, vote and finalize event kinds. A synthetic successful HTTP response alone cannot satisfy these persisted signature assertions; a mismatched creation receipt must keep the draft and emit no success.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Verification.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Conventional suite tests and isolated native desktop create/navigate/read/reload journeys; verify responsive layouts and retained operations behavior.\",\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Extend maintained app/backend surfaces; preserve the approved implemented scope and one-reviewer limit.\"\n    ],\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a119c3-d80b-7323-9ad5-f7f0a385fb9d:18\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Conventional suite tests and isolated native desktop create/navigate/read/reload journeys; verify responsive layouts and retained operations behavior.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Persisted draft or authenticated events are absent; live state/OS keychain changes; negative selector control passes.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run fixture isolation tests and maintained dao-workbench native suite; verify bridge provenance, real PG records, production signature integrity, screenshots and negative control. [owner:Avi 2026-10-08 #1564: \"Write another plan and implement it yourself on auto mode to further improve it based on your insights from assessing these failures.\"]\n\n## Why a new plan (not an extension)\nDedup check matched goal-brief-to-claimed-plan-work-2026-09-23 (all 9 items done, awaiting acceptance; scope = brief selection/delivery) and goal-live-holder-guarantee-2026-08-18 (shipped; holder liveness). WOE has some canonical collectors (packages/operator-core/lib/goal-holder-behavior-metrics.ts).\n- Grading is post-hoc: one grader picks a closed 2h window ~8h after it ends. Of holder d5bfd1's ~17h tenure, 1 window graded. The grader (su-928e075d) has been parked ~16h on WI-10006304; nothing detected or re-dispatched it.\n- Holder failures (su-d5bfd1a5, 2026-10-07): created WI-10007120, launch refused by concurrency cap (\"allows 6; 8 live\") at 12:03Z, no re-placement — item unassigned 24h+; asked the owner the same keep/narrow/drop question twice 17 min apart (12:08Z, 12:25Z); ~59% of non-automatic MCP calls were self-orientation; 23 carry-respawns in ~17h; WOE detector flagged an unplanned 3+ item cluster, no plan written.\n\n## Scope boundaries\n- Reuse first: extend goal-holder-behavior-metrics collectors, scorecards evaluate/emit, tool_invocations goal_id/goal_actor_class columns, existing scheduling (tier:ephemeral trigger or DBOS) and coord:ask-owner supersedes. No new scheduler; a new table only if a receipt cannot be derived.\n- Unknown stays unknown when not measured — never infer a pass from absence (grading-integrity rail unchanged).\n- Goal 60d3a8 and its drain fleet stay paused until this plan and the remaining items of the existing goal-mode plans are done [owner #1564].\n\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Honest unknown labels.**\n```requirement\n{\n \"intent\": {\n  \"request\": \"#1564: grading unknowns that are really unfinished grading must not read as broken instruments.\",\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n   \"session_turn:claude:4f01f5db-aea4-49c9-8600-c16869f09b43:14\",\n   \"session_turn:claude:9cc4fcfc-f2bc-4272-81b0-56802fbcfafb:2\"\n  ]\n },\n \"acceptance\": {\n  \"condition\": \"A goal scorecard criterion the grader has not yet assessed is recorded with unknownReason 'not-assessed', and rubrics:trend counts it separately from 'instrument-unavailable'.\",\n  \"falsifier\": \"A scorecard with an unassessed criterion is stored as 'instrument-unavailable', or rubrics:trend folds 'not-assessed' into the instrument-failure count.\",\n  \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n   \"unit\"\n  ]\n },\n \"verification\": {\n  \"method\": \"Run the named unit tests; inspect the unknownReason enum in scorecards evaluate/emit and observation types; read rubrics:trend output for a card with a not-assessed criterion.\",\n  \"check\": {\n   \"kind\": \"tests\",\n   \"files\": [\n    \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scorecards/emit.not-assessed.test.ts\"\n   ]\n  }\n }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Grading backlog is visible.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"#1564: the grader sat idle about 16 hours with nothing noticing.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:4f01f5db-aea4-49c9-8600-c16869f09b43:14\",\"session_turn:claude:9cc4fcfc-f2bc-4272-81b0-56802fbcfafb:2\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"When a standing goal's ungraded holder-tenure hours or grader idleness exceed the threshold, the detector returns an alert and the routine raises an owner-visible alert and re-dispatches grading through the existing grading-audit dispatch.\",\"falsifier\":\"A goal with ungraded tenure past the threshold, or an idle grader past the threshold, produces no alert or no re-dispatch.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named unit tests (threshold boundaries, healthy case, idle grader case); An end-to-end violation still fails this canary BAR.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Plan items | Evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007, P-008 | live |\n| R-8 | P-008 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Grading truth\n\n- **P-001** `done` Add unknownReason 'not-assessed' (attribution grader) to scorecards emit/evaluate and observation types; rubrics:trend and goal reports count grader-incomplete separately from instrument failures. Resume only at the Phase 4 canary (P-008).\n\n### D-003 — Reuse-first for grading instruments\nDate: 2026-10-08\nExtend goal-holder-behavior-metrics collectors, scorecards evaluate/emit and tool_invocations goal columns; no new scheduler; a new table only when a receipt cannot be derived from existing ledgers. [self-imposed, per repo reuse-first convention]\n\n### D-004 — Bind goal-mode-e2e criteria to computed instruments by model token (rubric rev 60→83)\nDate: 2026-10-08\n[self-imposed, su-d320c0c2, 2026-10-08] P-003 binds all 23 instrumented goal-mode-e2e criteria (8 computed + 15 trigger-census) with a trailing `[instrumentKey: goal-mode.<criterion>]` model token via 23 CAS-guarded rubrics:amend calls (receipts p003-bind-goal-mode.*, revisions 61..83). Consequence: criteriaHash changed from 3c32370d… to the rev-83 hash, so scorecards pinned to rev ≤60 read as older-revision evidence; that is intended — new cards are judged against the instruments. Token route chosen over a full `criteria` array replacement (which would restate all 39 criteria). Found + fixed in the same change: both token parsers (rubrics.ts effectiveCriterionInstrumentKey, scorecards.ts parseCriterionInstrumentKey) used `[a-z0-9-]+`, which can never match a dotted registered key (woe.*, goal-mode.*); now one shared CRITERION_INSTRUMENT_TOKEN accepting dots. The bindings take effect on :3070 only when that parser fix deploys; until then they are inert (identical to rev 60 behaviour).\n\n### D-005 — P-004: one provisional computed goal-mode-e2e card per holder tenure; graders supersede it rating only residual criteria\nDate: 2026-10-08\nDate: 2026-10-08\n[self-imposed, su-d320c0c2, 2026-10-08] Design for P-004 (goal-computed-tenure-card.ts + system-health/goal-computed-tenure-card-sweep.ts).\n- TENURE = maximal run of one owner's holder-agent goal-stamped tool_invocations for one goal, split at a silence > 4h. Ledger-derived, because agent_modes rows vanish once the lease moves on. Ongoing only when the owner is the current lease holder, the goal is active, and the last call is within the gap; window = start..now while ongoing, start..last call once ended.\n- One CURRENT computed card per tenure: rubric goal-mode-e2e, createdBy `goal-grading-computed`, subject {kind:'agent-run', ref:holder, window = the tenure}. 23 instrumented criteria carry the instrument verdict; needs-judgment and the 16 uninstrumented criteria read unknown/not-assessed; computed fails carry a disregard naming the grader as owner of the routing decision. Never terminal, so emit stamps it provisional (9 violatable criteria): it never counts as graded coverage.\n- Rolling cadence: the goal-owner-report watchdog timer (10 min, no new scheduler, same kill-switch). A card is re-filed, superseding the previous one, only when the verdict signature changes, an ongoing tenure's card is over 1h old, or the tenure ends. Ended tenures settle (stop being evaluated) once the card covers the tenure end and CHILD_PROOF_WINDOW + 1h have passed.\n- Grader workflow: supersede the current computed card with terminal:true for the IDENTICAL window and rate only the residual criteria. scorecards:emit adopts the computed card's settled ratings (pass, unknown idle/not-exercised) for omitted criteria (evidence suffixed 'adopted from computed card <id>'); computed fails, needs-judgment and uninstrumented criteria are never adopted, so completeness names them. Once a non-computed card supersedes a computed card the tenure is graded and the sweep stops.\n- P-002 backlog excludes computed cards entirely (they are not grader activity and must not become the grader it wakes); its escalation text now tells the grader the supersede-and-rate-residuals route.\n\n### D-006 — P-006: supersede own overlapping ask; JOIN a goal peer's overlapping ask (never cross-asker supersede)\nDate: 2026-10-08\nDate: 2026-10-08 [self-imposed, su-d320c0c2] coord:ask-owner (askOp in coord-ops/ops/compose.ts) now runs a goal-lineage dedup before opening a thread (coord-ops/goal-ask-dedup.ts). Lineage = sessions whose session_briefs.goal_id equals the caller's, same workspace; candidates = open coord_conversations with kind='question', producer='coord:ask-owner', newest 50. Overlap = title-token Jaccard >= 0.5, reusing titleTokens/jaccardSimilarity from work_items/recent-lexical-dupe-guard.ts (D-003 reuse-first). SAME asker -> supersede via supersedes_conversation_id (as the plan item says). DIFFERENT asker in the same goal -> JOIN: no new thread, no new escalation, the bounded wait polls the existing conversation, result.conversation_id is the existing one. Deviation from the item text, deliberate: supersedeConversation refuses a cross-asker supersede of an owner question (not_owner, the WI-1373235 rail), and widening that rail to 'same goal' would let a misidentified overlap retract a peer's live gate. Fail-safe: dedup read failure -> status 'unmeasured' and the ask opens normally; an auto-supersede that loses a race (target answered in between) falls back to a fresh ask; an explicit caller supersede skips dedup and still fails loudly. Every result carries goal_ask_dedup.status (explicit-supersede | not-in-goal | no-overlap | superseded | joined | unmeasured). Evidence of need: goal 60d3a8 had 2 open owner asks from 2 askers on 2026-10-08 (distinct topics; they correctly stay separate).\n\n### D-007 — Owner #1608 authorizes the P-008 canary tenure now; su-ffacf48e takes custody\nDate: 2026-10-10\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-10 directive #1608, owner-typed in session su-ffacf48e]: \"run the trials\" — answering su-ffacf48e's question (conv-mv2oqjq9) whether the three goal-mode plans that can only finish with live goal runs (goal-brief-to-claimed-plan-work, goal-agent-behavior-feedback, goal-grading-live-coverage) should stay on hold or run their trials.\n\nCustody: the prior trial custodians su-cf569f3f, su-32d1b8df and su-d320c0c2 are absent from coord:presence (measured 2026-10-10 20:50Z, 279 agents, no match), so su-ffacf48e-095b-4eba-89c6-8ec92d0564d8 takes trial custody under WI-10008134.\nVehicle: per owner #1040 (use the real Work-on-everything goal for all testing), the trials run on goal work-on-everything-fresh-grading-and-improvement-60d3a8, resumed from its #1564 pause by goals:update status:'active'. #1608 supersedes #1564 item 3 (keep goal agents paused) for the duration of these trials only.\nSUPERSEDES D-002 (goal agents stay paused until both workstreams are done) for the P-008 canary tenure. These complete ranges were re-read by c05233eb on 2026-10-14, including the full approved proposal at dd61dbe4 turn12.\n\nOutcome: preserve the Goal's recovery, round, idle and alarm bounds, P-006's same-full-file-set 50% target, P-005's five consecutive repair rounds, and P-018's seven consecutive days of live passes. Reach verified shipment through the existing pipeline; local tests establish only their exercised scope.\n\nNon-goals: a parallel gate controller, another proof ledger, unregistered default-OFF features, fabricated historical observations, bypassing the current live gate owner, or substituting a current-build result for exact shipped acceptance.\n\nScenarios:\n- When a failing queue stalls, the ordered actuator fires and records the original queue clock, named next action and actual effect receipt.\n- When an admitted fix is checked, it cannot silently add red; pending work remains in the timing population, and repair fixes survive an allowed re-cut or restart.\n- When a sync batch breaks a guard, the original author or work-item receives the attributed result and required wake; queueing alone does not prove pickup.\n- When a shipped mechanism stops working, its real observation and filing clocks expose a missed tick; a later healthy sample cannot erase the missed interval.\n- When a fixer account is walled, the approved auto gateway supplies the primary/capacity fallback route, with final first-request proof on the exact shipped artifact (D-045).\n- When the commit hop is interrupted or a submodule is unpublished, preserve exact causal evidence and owned blockers until the class guard and publication/promotion acceptance are verified (D-045, D-049).\n- Acceptance keeps missing, unknown, partial and reconstructed data explicit; seven-day qualification and full-gate performance cannot be inferred from unit passes.\n\nOpen acceptance choices: the meaning of typical (the native producer currently proposes median/nearest-rank p90), strict 60min idle deadline versus an after-60min trigger, and malfunction-onset/alarm exercise clocks. No extra tick or relaxed Goal is approved. Producer-backed review input: docs/evidence/green-main-acceptance-proposal-20261014.md; the existing v6 draft remains unapproved and invalid.\n\n## Goal\n\nAfter any red, main is green again within **4h typical (p90 ≤ 8h)**. A repair round takes **≤ 45 min**. No repair queue sits idle **> 60 min** without an actuator firing. Every gate mechanism earlier plans shipped carries a **live invariant** that alarms within one tick when it stops working.\n\n## Context (measured 2026-10-08 ~04:00Z; evidence on WI-10007375)\n\n- **137h since the last green**: main pinned at d740fc38, 2026-10-02 10:54Z.\n- **48.4h with the machine powered off**: 10-03 14:14Z → 10-05 14:37Z (`last -x`).\n- **Queue 2** (candidate 6ca43115, 10-02 11:42Z → 10-03 14:14Z): 13 rounds, red 37 → 6, never 0. Its fixes were not carried into the next queue.\n- **Queue 3** (candidate ad82b273, opened 10-05 15:25Z): 15 rounds in 46.7h. Failing legs went 3→8→7→4→4→4→1→2→2→3→3→3→5→5→2: worse in 4 of 14 transitions. Round-to-round median 3.0h, worst 11.2h.\n- **Stalled since 10-07 14:16Z**: phase `awaiting-fixer`, attempts 0, fixerSpawnId null. `last_fixer.at` = 2026-09-22. The live gate owner's checkpoint says to keep the queue untouched while it is awaiting-fixer. The exclusivity rule stops everyone else. Result: a deadlock.\n- **Whole-blob admissions**: 16 of 25 admissions in queue 3 were whole-blob (138 paths from staging tip). Queue 2's first admission carried 49 paths, and that round went to 37 red.\n- **Long-pole test**: `affected-tests-repo-wide-invariant-guards.test.ts` averaged 13.5 min on 09-30 and 43.4 min on 10-07. Vitest wall per round is 41–138 min at ~2× parallelism (262 CPU-min over 132 wall-min on f07043ba).\n- **Gate code changed mid-red**: 148 commits (+8.3k lines) since 10-02, and 30+ defects filed against the gate itself. The routine executor ran 29 commits behind.\n- **Friction and infra**: 11 false-positive `frozen_candidate_lineage_violation` items. Root disk at 99% (20 GB free of 1.9 TB) for the third time in a week.\n- **Inflow**: 412–1,196 staging commits/day (2.4k–7.2k files) from about 95 live agents. The drain fleets alone have 59 + 19 recently active members.\n\n## Why earlier plans did not hold\n\nThree earlier plans aimed at exactly this outcome and closed their items as done:\n\n- `green-main-fast-2026-08-25` (shipped). Its targeted re-verdict item was dropped.\n- `gate-verdict-liveness-and-repair-reliability-2026-08-31` (shipped, 16/16 done): no-verdict rate alarm, fixer survivability, cheap legs during repair.\n- `green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08` (superseded, 9/9 done): \"fixer auto-dispatch actually spawns\", \"no full-gate fallthrough on repair rounds\", \"admission pre-check at repairHead+patch\", lint legs concurrent with tests.\n\nLive state contradicts at least three of those: no fixer spawn in 15 days, full-radius repair rounds, and admissions that add red. Every acceptance was point-in-time, and nothing keeps checking that a shipped mechanism still works. This plan therefore leads with standing live invariants (P-018) and a regression post-mortem (P-019) before re-building anything.\n\n## Relationship to existing plans\n\n- Absorbs and supersedes the draft `gate-throughput-shift-left-2026-10-06` (never started). Its items 1–3 map to P-011, items 4 and 6 to P-008, item 5 to P-002, item 7 to P-013, and item 8 to P-005.\n- Complements `checkpoint-recovery-and-verdict-clarity-2026-10-07` (ready); P-016 reuses its dashboard item. Also complements `gate-test-reuse-yield-2026-10-01` (ready).\n\n## Constraints\n\n- LIVE_GATE_OPS stay with the registered gate owner (`gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership`). This plan is GATE_SYSTEM_DEV: code, tests, instrumentation, policy. Evidence goes to the live owner, and no item mutates the live queue.\n- Tests ship with each item, in Vitest beside the code they guard. LIVE_GATE_OPS stays with the gate owner; this plan is GATE_SYSTEM_DEV only.\n\n### D-023 — P-021 (bounded queue life) supersedes 'age is never an input' from frozen-candidate-stays-frozen-through-all-fixes-2026-09-03#D-005/#D-011, under anti-treadmill limits\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[self-imposed 2026-10-12, su-cb24e308, resolving a conflict between two owner rulings; disclosed, not owner-confirmed]\n\nConflict: frozen-candidate-stays-frozen-through-all-fixes-2026-09-03#D-005 and #D-011 (owner-ratified 2026-09-03/04) say that a frozen candidate stays frozen until it is green or an owner retires it, so age is not an input to any queue decision (code: packages/operator-core/lib/release/frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts, the comment above DEFAULT_FROZEN_REPAIR_QUEUE_LIMITS). P-021 (audit rpt_c1597a17 rec 4) automatically retires a queue whose failing count has made no new low in 4 consecutive rounds or that is older than 24h. The owner approved adding P-021 on 2026-10-12 (this plan, D-022: 'Add both, activate').\n\nRuling: the newer owner approval governs, so P-021 is built. The 09-03 rule existed to stop the re-cut treadmill (20 retirements and 0 resumes in one day on 2026-09-02, because each re-cut at the bare tip pulled in new reds and dropped the admitted fixes). P-021 keeps those protections in three ways:\n1. It never re-cuts at the bare tip without carrying the work. Re-cut target: the newest known-good staging commit (P-012) when one exists. Until P-012 ships, the target is the current staging tip. Either way, the queue's admitted fix paths are re-admitted onto the new candidate (P-010 carry), and the carried paths are recorded.\n2. Rate limit: at most one automatic P-021 retirement per 24h per install. A second trigger inside that window escalates to the owner instead of retiring again.\n3. No retirement while the failing count is still making new lows and the queue is under 24h old (the item's acceptance clause). Every retirement records its trigger (non-improving or age), its rounds-since-low count, and the carried paths.\nThe owner-only retire verb (release:repair-queue op:'retire') is unchanged; P-021 is a separate, bounded automatic rule. The 8h age-escalation cadence stays as it is.\nReversal: if the owner wants the 09-03 rule restored, drop P-021 and leave FROZEN_REPAIR_AGE_ESCALATION_INTERVAL_MS as the only age signal.\n\n### D-024 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-12\nAmendment-Id: amend-887e3bfb12fef56a8713dfa3\nRequest-Hash: 1fe1c371194b7a0bdfdedc4406e25b26e0e621606424c7565073109b382af8d8\nActor: su-cb24e308-bc28-44ac-821f-84573580ab82\nReason: Split the 11 compound seed bars into 16 atomic bars, one per plan item, so each item has its own observable acceptance contract (spec-quality atomic-observable-behavior and item-contract-coverage failed on the compound seed).
