Additions beyond the prior bars: R-5 falsifier includes the D-023 rate limit (a second automatic retirement inside 24h escalates instead), and R-9 requires red-legs-at-R1 recorded (P-012 text).\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-d47fbca4-0adc-4267-965a-fde08a97833a\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1176353\nApproved-At: 2026-10-12T16:02:13.716Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 51 → 52\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-025 — P-021 carry scope: a staging-tip re-cut carries admitted fixes by construction; re-admission onto a known-good target is P-010's executor\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[self-imposed 2026-10-12, su-cb24e308, implementing P-021 under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\nP-021 retires a non-improving (4 rounds without a new failing-count low) or over-24h frozen queue and the SAME gate pass re-cuts at the re-cut target. Target: deps.resolveKnownGoodRecutTarget() when it names a commit (the P-012 seam, not wired until P-012 ships), else the run's resolved staging tip; the quiet cut is skipped on that pass so the judged commit is exactly the target the carry was measured against.\nCarry: every admission is taken FROM staging (release:repair-queue admit replays staging content onto repairHead), so a staging-tip re-cut contains each admitted fix, or a newer staging version of the same file, by construction. P-021 therefore records the carry (each admitted path compared by blob with the target: contained / superseded / absent-at-target / unverified) and computes readmitPaths only for a known-good target that predates a fix. Executing that re-admission onto the new candidate is P-010's job; until P-012 ships no known-good target exists, so readmitPaths is always empty in production.\nStorage: the retirement record and the 24h rate limit live in routines.metadata.repair_queue_bounded_life (beside repair_queue, which the retire deletes), written in the same locked UPDATE as the retire. Code: packages/operator-core/lib/release/frozen-repair-bounded-life.ts (+ -store.ts), apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts applyFrozenRepairBoundedLife.\n\n### D-026 — P-010 executor: a pending-carry record written with every retire, assessed at the next cut; advance to the staging tip when a still-relevant fix is missing\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[self-imposed 2026-10-12, su-cb24e308, implementing P-010 under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\nMeasured before design (2026-10-12 18:25Z): the claim that queue 6ca43115's rounds were 'lost after the 10-05 reboot' does not hold for the FIXES. The host booted 2026-10-05 14:37Z, and refs/papercusp/frozen/6ca43115268af8a9cbdb6789c51d24177068adb9 still names c697f73983 with 49 admission commits above the candidate, in both the canonical tree and the checkpoint checkout. Queue state lives in routines.metadata (PG) and the lineage ref is reconciled at run start (P-027). What a retire loses is verification PROGRESS, not fix content. How 6ca43115 itself ended was not determined.\nThe real gap: a retire (P-021 bounded-life OR the owner's release:repair-queue retire) is followed by a cut that need not contain the admitted fixes. The quiet cut steps back up to 240s (DEFAULT_QUIET_CUT_SEC), so a fix committed to staging and admitted inside that window can be absent from the first post-retire candidate. P-012's known-good cut will be older still.\nDesign: (1) BOTH retire paths write routines.metadata.repair_queue_carry = { fromCandidate, fromRepairHead, reason, retiredAtMs, admitted:[{path, blob}], truncated } in the SAME locked row update as the retire, so the record survives a restart. (2) At the next fresh cut (not a repair verification, not an explicit candidate) a pure assessment compares each admitted path: still-relevant iff the staging tip holds exactly the admitted blob; carried iff the cut candidate does too; missing = still-relevant and not carried; unverified = lookup failed. (3) Any missing or unverified path makes the gate judge the staging tip instead of the quiet cut. By definition the tip contains every still-relevant fix. The assessment (per-path status, from/to candidate) is recorded and the pending record is consumed in one CAS write. Re-admitting fixes onto an OLDER known-good commit (P-021 readmitPaths) stays with P-012, which must consult this record when it picks such a target.\n\n### D-027 — Amends D-026: after a retire, a fix counts as carried when the next cut holds the admitted blob or the integration-branch tip's current version of that path\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[self-imposed 2026-10-12, su-cb24e308, implementing P-010]\nScope: this applies ONLY to the first fresh cut after a frozen queue has been RETIRED (no live queue exists). It never changes which commit a live frozen queue judges; a live queue keeps judging its own candidate/repairHead.\nD-026 said a fix is still-relevant iff the integration-branch tip holds exactly the admitted blob. That is wrong for hunk-exact admissions (the default since P-020): the admitted blob is synthesized (the admitting agent's hunks replayed onto the old repairHead's blob), so it need not equal any integration-branch blob, and the rule would treat nearly every hunk-exact fix as irrelevant.\nRule as built in packages/operator-core/lib/release/frozen-repair-carry.ts (assessFrozenRepairCarryAtCut), per admitted path of the retired queue: 'carried' = the cut's blob equals the admitted blob; 'carried-via-staging' = the cut's blob equals the integration-branch tip's blob (admissions are taken from that branch, so its current version is the successor of the fix, including a deliberate revert); 'missing' = neither; 'unverified' = a lookup failed. Any missing or unverified path, when the cut is not already the tip, makes that post-retire cut use the tip instead of the quiet cut. Cost: occasionally skipping the quiet cut once after a retire.\n\n### D-028 — P-013 design: one condition item per failing leg, gate-item close refused while the frozen queue holds, gate-red singletons claimable only by a long-lived owner\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12 [self-imposed 2026-10-12, su-cb24e308, implementing P-013 (WI-6554700010009197) under owner directive #1726 AUTO; implements owner-approved D-021 fix 2]\nMeasured before design (23:30-23:40Z): (a) the gate already mints exactly ONE claimable item per frozen queue (frozen-repair-convergence:<pipeline>, via the condition bridge: coord/actionable-conditions.ts registry + coord/condition-bridge.ts) and one gate-red-streak:<pipeline> singleton; no per-leg item exists. (b) work_items:complete already refuses closing a gate-red singleton unless every manifest leg reads admitted or green (gate-red-completion-claim.ts, P-022 of frozen-candidate-stays-frozen). It does not refuse while the queue is still frozen with all legs admitted, so 'complete the gate item while main is red' is still possible. (c) release:repair-queue admit is not ownership-gated, so any agent may already admit.\nDecisions: (1) Per-leg items: a new condition prefix frozen-repair-leg:, key frozen-repair-leg:<pipeline>:<failing entry>. It needs a new harnessFrom mode 'leading-segment': the bridge's suffix mode refuses a suffix containing ':'. routeFrozenRepairToAgents broadcasts one condition per failing entry every tick the hold holds; no oneShot, so the condition-staleness sweep closes an item once its entry leaves the failing set. At most 12 per tick; the rest stay named on the convergence item. Each body carries the failure tail (the candidate's source=ci test_runs output_tail, best-effort) and the exact path-exact admit call, and says no gate ownership is needed. (2) Exclusivity stays LIVE_GATE_OPS only (checkpoint-run, retire, deploy): no ownership check may be added to admit or to per-leg items. (3) The gate-red-completion verdict for a condition item refuses while a frozen repair marker exists for the pipeline (reason main-still-red), even when every leg is admitted. Administrative settlements (duplicate/drop) stay exempt. (4) Long-lived owner: work_items:claim of a gate-red-streak:/frozen-repair-convergence: singleton is refused unless the claimant has a guaranteed re-wake (the same isRewakeGuaranteed verdict loop:status reports). The refusal points to loop:arm or to a per-leg item. This replaces the relay (48 claimants on WI-10006055) with owners whose claim outlives a turn. If a system fixer identity must claim it, exempt it explicitly with a reason.\n\n### D-029 — Amends D-028(1): per-leg items are change-only one-shot conditions, reconciled against the condition fold every tick\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12 [self-imposed 2026-10-12, su-cb24e308, implementing P-013 (WI-6554700010009197) under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\nD-028(1) said routeFrozenRepairToAgents re-broadcasts one condition per failing entry every tick, with no oneShot, so the staleness sweep closes a leg item on absence. Measured while implementing: broadcastSevereEvent sends to '*' on every call (severe-event-broadcast.ts), so up to 12 legs x every gate tick lands in every running agent's inbox for the whole life of a multi-day red. The convergence route also only fires on the long-wall branch, so wiring legs there would leave a normally-dispatched red with no per-leg items (the P-013 falsifier).\nRuling: (a) Legs are routed from the gate's terminal handler (runGreenCheckpoint, beside recordDerivedFreezeDisposition), the one funnel every tick passes, with the queue the tick ended holding; a green tick passes queue:null; an UNREADABLE queue skips routing (never treated as no queue). (b) Each tick reads the open frozen-repair-leg:<pipeline>: keys from the condition fold (computeConditionStates over readConditionEnvelopes), opens only legs not already open (oneShot:true, so the staleness sweep never reads their silence as recovery), and resolves departed legs in ONE broadcastSevereEventResolvedMany message. A lost open or resolve is repaired by the next tick's reconcile. (c) Up to 12 legs (MAX_ROUTED_LEGS) are routed at once, in queue order; the next is routed when one clears. Failure tails are read only for newly opened legs (test_runs source=ci, worktree_dirty=false, commit_sha in candidate/repairHead). Code: release/frozen-repair-agent-routing.ts planFrozenRepairLegRouting (pure), release/frozen-repair-leg-routing.ts routeFrozenRepairLegs (deps), coord/actionable-conditions.ts FROZEN_REPAIR_LEG_CONDITION_PREFIX + harnessFrom 'leading-segment'.\nRelated: P-013\n\n### D-030 — P-016 SLO: named populations, once-per-episode pages, alert targets\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, implementing P-016 (WI-6554700010009198) under owner directive #1726 AUTO; pages implement owner-approved D-021 fix 3]\n\nMeasured before design (01:15Z, harness_shared.attention_notifications since lastGreenAt 2026-10-02): the owner WAS paged during this red episode, heavily. 'Frozen repair queue has held main ~Nh' fired every 15 min at peak (99-141 gate pages/day on 10-06..10-08, 3-15/day from 10-09 once that dedup was fixed). Mobile delivery succeeded 0 times (desktop only; already tracked by EI-22417736870344056). The existing STALLED alarm (12h no green) and verdictless limb share ONE dedup flag (gate_health.watchdogAlerted), so after it fires once a later 6h no-verdict window cannot page. So the gap D-021 #3 closes is a dedicated, exactly-once page per episode, not a missing alarm.\n\nRuling: packages/operator-core/lib/release/green-main-slo.ts computeGreenMainSlo is the single pure source for the /admin/git panel AND the pages. Populations: time-since-green = now - gate_health.lastGreenAt; time-since-verdict = now - newest verdict-bearing green_checkpoint ledger row; round cycle time = gaps between the live queue's convergenceRounds; queue idle = frozenRepairLatency live waits with nothing in flight (red awaiting fixer, or admitted head awaiting run start; time inside a running suite is not idle); rounds-to-converge = live queue round count, labelled converged:false; red-adding admission = an admission whose next round recorded more failures than the round before it (attribution per admission window); per-sync red rate = sync-batch delta check red batches / judged batches, per fleet. Unknown is null, never 0.\n\nPages (severity page): main red >= 12h, keyed on lastGreenAt; no verdict >= 6h, keyed on lastVerdictAt (a gate that never rendered a verdict does not page). Delivery must use notifyAttentionOnce({ dedupeKey: episodeKey }) so each episode pages exactly once. Alerts (severity alert, also once per episode key): newest round interval > 2h, queue idle > 1h, any red-adding admission, a fleet's per-sync red rate > 20% over >= 5 judged batches. The alert targets are my choice, tunable via thresholds; the page thresholds are the owner's.\n\n### D-031 — Amends D-030: per-sync red rate population = sync-batch delta check coverage ticks (green|red), all agents; per-fleet split deferred\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed, su-cb24e308, implementing P-016 (WI-6554700010009198) under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\nMeasured while wiring R-13: the sync-batch delta check keeps no per-batch verdict history beyond routines(name='sync-batch-delta-check').metadata.sync_delta.coverage.ticks (24h retention, max 400). Each tick has a status; 'green' and 'red' mean a git-sync batch window was JUDGED, every other status (skipped, up-to-date, nothing-selected, radius-too-wide, leg-timeout, missed-opportunity) judged no change. Ticks carry NO agent attribution, so a per-fleet split cannot be computed from this population.\nRuling: perSyncRedRate = red ticks / (green+red ticks) over that ledger, one row with fleet:null covering all agents (syncTalliesFromDeltaCoverage in packages/operator-core/lib/release/green-main-slo.ts). Same function feeds the /admin/git panel (git-pipeline-stats gate.slo) and the watchdog alert (green-main-slo-watchdog.ts), so panel and alert agree. Ledger absent/malformed = null (unknown), never []. Per-fleet attribution needs the check to record each judged window's Papercusp-Agent trailers on the tick; filed as an owned follow-up.\n\n### D-032 — P-017 design: red-gate inflow control is an 8h repair-first preference for a stable half of fleet members, extending stop-the-line, behind a registered default-ON flag\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, implementing P-017 under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\n\nMeasured before design (01:40-01:50Z): an older mechanism already throttles intake on a long red. stop-the-line (packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-admission.ts, stopTheLineExclusionSql, STOP_THE_LINE_RED_HOURS = 24) is a claim FLOOR. Once the harness's open gate-red-streak:<harness> condition item is older than 24h, it refuses ALL self-selected non-repair work for EVERY agent; bugs and ACTIONABLE_CONDITION_PREFIXES items stay exempt. P-017 asks for an earlier, gentler rung: past 8h red, move a SHARE of drain-fleet members onto repair items before new backlog.\n\nRulings:\n1. REUSE. The red predicate is the stop-the-line one: an open gate-red-streak:<harness> condition item, here with created_ts older than 8h. Factor it out of stopTheLineExclusionSql as one helper taking the hour threshold, so both rungs read the same population. Do not add a second 'is main red' reader.\n2. PREFERENCE, NOT FLOOR. A selected member gets repair items ranked first. When no repair item is claimable it takes normal backlog, so no member idles. 'Before new backlog' is an ordering claim. The 24h stop-the-line floor stays the hard rung.\n3. REPAIR ITEMS: condition_key LIKE 'frozen-repair-leg:%' (P-013 per-failing-leg items) or 'sync-delta-red:%' (the sync-batch delta check's attributed per-sync reds, conditionKeyForRed). The queue-level frozen-repair-convergence: item and the gate-red-streak singleton are excluded: D-028 restricts those to long-lived owners.\n4. WHO: 'drain fleet member' = a caller of scheduler:get_next with a fleet slug, since get_next IS the self-select drain path. The share is a stable hash of the caller's ownerId, mod 100, below RED_INFLOW_REPAIR_SHARE_PCT = 50. It needs no fleet-roster read, so the same member stays selected across ticks and roughly half of any fleet moves. Unfleeted callers are unaffected.\n5. RELATION SCOPE: harness_features_consolidated has no condition_key column (measured: information_schema). The repair-first ordering must therefore reach only the issue-family (work_items) relation and never the feature tier. A shared compileRank term that references condition_key would be a hard PG error on the feature tier.\n6. FLAG: a registered flag in libs/flags/src/types.ts, default ON (not dark: it is reversible ordering, not one of the dangerous set).\n7. VISIBILITY: the get_next result says when the preference applied, e.g. redInflow { applied, redSinceHours, share }, so a moved member can see why it got a repair item.\n\nAcceptance maps to AUTO-BAR-R-15-P-017@2. Unit tests cover: selected member + 8h red ranks a repair item over an older backlog item; an unselected member, or red under 8h, or flag off, keeps the normal order; no repair item falls back to backlog; and the feature tier never sees condition_key.\n\n### D-033 — Amends D-032: the red-inflow repair preclaim ignores the fleet's lane filter; claim floors still apply\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, implementing P-017 (WI-6554700010009199) under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\n\nFound while writing the P-017 tests: the D-032 preclaim reused scheduler:get_next's claimIssue closure, which passes the fleet's compiled spec.view.filter (specFilterSql), its id allowlist (ids/excludeIds) and its kind narrowing (issueKinds) into claimNextIssueWorkItem. A drain fleet's spec IS its lane (a plan, an id drain-list, kind='feature'), and the repair items are harness-wide gate work (frozen-repair-leg: / sync-delta-red: condition items, filed as kind 'bug'). They match almost no lane, so with the filter kept no lane-scoped fleet member would ever move. That is the first falsifier of AUTO-BAR-R-15-P-017@2 ('no members move during a long red').\n\nRuling: when repairFirstOnly is set, claimIssue omits specFilterSql, ids, excludeIds and issueKinds. redInflowRepairItemSql is the whole selection. Every claim FLOOR still applies unchanged: live-gate-ops exclusion (the gate-red-streak/green-stall singletons stay explicit-ID only, D-028), stop-the-line, admission, readiness/deps, reserved plan lanes, origin, swarm affinity and redundancy. The spec rank (specOrderSql) is kept, so a fleet's ordering among repair items is still its own. The move is a deliberate cross-lane preference that applies only past 8h of red, to the stable 50% share, behind FLAGS.RED_INFLOW_REPAIR_FIRST. Unfleeted callers are unaffected (D-032 ruling 4).\nRelated: P-017\n\n### D-034 — P-020 outcome: exclude-the-breaker promotion is not built; fix-forward stays the standard\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, P-020 (WI-6554700010009201) under owner directive #1726 AUTO; P-020 is an owner-requested decision spike]\n\nMeasured by replay of recorded frozen-queue data (report rpt_a5d11b5e-a272-4a02-aae3-e6e08388aae9). The computation is in packages/operator-core/lib/release/exclude-the-breaker-replay.ts, with unit tests and mutation probes; no gate module imports it. Model: first red verdict + 10 min exclusion build + one full round (median 85.4 min over 22 full rounds). It is valid only if every first-round red is attributable (reach = test + executed modules, intersected with the G..C delta) and no kept change imports an excluded ADDED file.\n\nProjected vs actual time-to-green:\n- d4946901 (calibration): 5.9h vs green at 24.6h.\n- 6ca43115: 4.7h vs never green (held main 75.8h, retired).\n- 70e89c73: 9.4h vs never green (retired at 15.2h).\n\nPreconditions failed on ALL three queues:\n(1) Coupling: kept importers of excluded added files were 53 / 120 / 1,007. The transitive closure widened exclusion from 200 to 272, 179 to 340, and 2,654 to 3,784 paths in 3-4 rounds. That is a lower bound, since symbol coupling is invisible to an import scan.\n(2) Attribution: 70e89c73 had 42 of 578 first-round reds with no executed-sources row and no changed test file. Fix locality: 2/22, 22/46 and 3/3 fixes landed outside the red test's reach, in runtime-read baselines and registries. Exclusion of executed code cannot reach those causes.\n(3) Mass red: on 70e89c73 exclusion = 2,654 paths from 556 agents, i.e. a reset to the last green.\n\nDecision: do not build exclude-the-breaker promotion. Freeze-and-converge fix-forward stays the standard. The measured cost is convergence rounds (the first red verdict came 4.3h / 3.1h after the cut; greening took 20h more or never happened), which P-005, P-007, P-013 and P-017 attack directly.\n\nRevisit only when all three hold:\n(a) test_executed_sources records tracked files a test reads at runtime;\n(b) the exclusion build includes a typecheck of C-minus-closure;\n(c) a non-promoting shadow round measures the real green rate on live queues.\n\nCorrection on record: the first scratch replay (v2) reported d4946901 and 6ca43115 as meeting the preconditions. Its flag skipped the coupling condition that its own model stated. v3 (tested module) supersedes it.\n\n### D-035 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: gmct-asbuilt-files-r4-r15-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: 60d1df92b58f431a84784a75e3b558df44916be44beb033b207db9b0e53e66e1\nActor: su-cb24e308-bc28-44ac-821f-84573580ab82\nReason: Six bars (R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-9, R-15) named test files that were never written: the activation seeder guessed file names before the designs existed (EI-25833725073574319). Grading runs these files, so each bar now names the as-built tests already bound as its evidence (spec_evidence_bindings). Conditions and falsifiers are unchanged. R-10/R-11 (P-005/P-007, still in progress) are deliberately not touched.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-51962bad-025f-4bb6-bd2e-e979588c5e05\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1178130\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T03:51:24.905Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 76 → 77\nChanged BARs: R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-9, R-15\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-036 — P-007 design: extend the R6 admission pre-check with the admitted paths' related-test radius for ordinary admissions\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, P-007 under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\n\nMeasured before design (04:10-04:16Z, by reading code): the admit door already runs an admission pre-check (packages/operator-core/lib/release/admission-fix-precheck.ts, R6 of green-gate-zero-wait-convergence-2026-09-08). It runs the frozen signature's test-file entries plus admitted test files at the BUILT, unpublished admission commit, and refuses admission-imports-red when an admitted test file outside the signature fails. precheckPopulation already accepts affectedTestFiles, but packages/operator-core/lib/release/admission-jobs.ts (immutablePrecheckPopulation, line ~83) computes that radius ONLY for gitlink admissions; an ordinary source admission keeps the exact-file policy. So a source-only fix that breaks a green test elsewhere is published unchecked today. That is the gap P-007 names.\n\nDecision (reuse, no new check or tool):\n1. immutablePrecheckPopulation computes the related-test radius for ordinary admissions too, with the same pinned-tree index (buildIndex + selectRelatedTests at the built commit) the gitlink branch uses, over the admitted non-test paths.\n2. Bound: when selection returns mode 'full', or the radius exceeds a fixed cap, the radius is not added. The verdict records that it was skipped and why (a loud marker, like checkpoint-tree-busy). The next targeted round from P-005 then measures that radius. The precheck never runs the whole suite at admission time.\n3. 'Previously green' = a radius file that is not a signature test-file and is not inside a workspace whose workspace-task leg is in the signature. Only those files can refuse. A radius file inside a red workspace-task leg is measured and reported, but cannot refuse.\n4. The refusal names the leg: admission-imports-red lists each newly red file with the leg it belongs to (its workspace).\n5. Unmeasured radius files follow the existing rule (admission-precheck-unavailable). The existing skipPrecheck opt-out still applies.\n\nRejected: re-running the radius at the current repairHead to prove 'previously green'. It doubles every admission's cost, and the signature already records the head's known reds.\n\n### D-037 — Amends D-036: the P-007 radius is selected per owning workspace with that workspace's tsconfig aliases; Playwright-owned specs are excluded\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, P-007 (WI-6554700010009193) under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\n\nMeasured by reading scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs while implementing D-036: buildIndex marks a test file unresolved when it has an alias import (`@/`, `~/`, `#`) that no alias entry matches, and selectRelatedTests ALWAYS selects unresolved tests. The gitlink branch of immutablePrecheckPopulation builds ONE whole-repo index with aliases=[], so every `@/`-importing test would join every ordinary admission's radius and push it over the cap. P-007 would then be a permanent skip.\n\nDecision:\n1. Each admitted non-test source path is grouped by its owning workspace: the nearest ancestor directory holding a package.json blob at the built commit. Each group gets its own index (rootDir = workspace root, listing only that workspace's sources), with aliases from that workspace's tsconfig.json blob. tsconfigPathEntriesFor gains an optional { readFile } seam, like playwrightOwnedTest already has, so the pinned blob is parsed with the same parser; no second tsconfig reader.\n2. Cross-workspace dependents (tests that import the changed module through a bare @papercusp/* specifier) are outside the related graph by design, same as the gate's related mode. The admission radius does not cover them; the next targeted round (P-005) does.\n3. Playwright-owned specs (playwrightOwnedTest over the pinned playwright.config.* blobs) are excluded from the radius: the per-file precheck runner cannot measure them (TEST_FILE_ROUTE_ERROR), and an unmeasured file would refuse every such admission as admission-precheck-unavailable. The exclusion count is recorded in the radius detail.\n4. A failure while computing the radius (unreadable submodule store, malformed tree) records radius status 'skipped', reason 'radius-unavailable'. It does not refuse the admission: before P-007 an ordinary admission had no radius at all, and the targeted round still measures it.\n5. The radius partition (guarded / reportOnly / legs / marker) is persisted on the queue's admissionPrecheck operation record. The managed worker rebuilds the population from the persisted files, so without it the worker would silently treat every radius file as admitted (refusable) and lose the leg names.\nRelated: P-007, P-005\n\n### D-038 — Amends D-036: operator-core admissions are radius-skipped (over-cap) by measurement; the P-005 targeted round is their guard\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, P-007 (WI-6554700010009193) under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\n\nMeasured at HEAD b01fcd34c9 (load avg ~300-430 on 128 cores):\n- ordinaryAdmissionRadius for three typical operator-core files (release/admission-jobs.ts, release/green-main-slo.ts, work-items-admission.ts) returns over-cap(5572/40) every time (.papercusp/scratch/p007-measure-2.log). Small workspaces measure: scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs -> 1 test; apps/operator-vite GitClient.tsx -> 1 test.\n- The 5573 is genuine static reachability, not graph holes: only 5 of 8812 operator-core tests are unresolved (.papercusp/scratch/p007-phase-probe.log). Hub modules put almost every test in the closure of almost every file.\n- The gate's own narrowing (the executed-source map, P-002 of gate-latency-selection-and-retry-policy-2026-09-06) prunes ZERO of those 5573 at HEAD: noEntry 1413, unknownDrift 1859, stale 2296, prunable 0 (.papercusp/scratch/p007-execmap-probe.log). So no existing mechanism narrows an operator-core change below the whole leg.\n\nRuling: P-007 keeps the 40-file cap. An admission whose radius exceeds it publishes with the radius SKIPPED and disclosed (precheckRadius status 'skipped', reason over-cap(N/40), in the admit response and the audit row). It is never run partially. For operator-core that is every admission today; the guard for those is the P-005 targeted round, which runs the admitted paths' full affected radius on the next repair head. Running ~5.5k tests inside each admission would cost more than the round it protects, against this plan's cycle-time goal.\n\nConsequence for acceptance: AUTO-BAR-R-11-P-007 is amended to say the admission guard applies to radii within the cap, and an over-cap admission must be disclosed as skipped, never silently published as guarded. Narrowing operator-core (hub fan-out, executed-map staleness) is filed as a separate follow-up, not P-007 scope.\n\n### D-039 — R-11 keeps its meaning: the D-038 over-cap carve-out is withdrawn after an outside objection; P-007 is not done while over-cap admissions are unguarded\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, P-007 (WI-6554700010009193) under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\n\nThe R-11 amendment that D-038 called for (preview thread-post:1178548) was objected to by an outside-lineage judge (thread-post:1178554). I accept the objection, and the amendment is not applied:\n1. D-038 measured every typical operator-core admission as over-cap(5572/40). So 'guard within the cap' leaves the main package unguarded, while R-11's intent stays 'an admission never makes a green leg red'.\n2. The cap value was not stated in the BAR, so lowering ADMISSION_RADIUS_CAP would widen the exception without failing anything.\n3. The guard D-038 named for over-cap admissions (the P-005 targeted round) runs after the admission publishes. R-10's BAR does not say it attributes or blocks a red-adding admission, and its check file does not exist yet.\n4. D-038 was self-imposed, not an owner ruling, so it cannot narrow the requirement.\n\nRuling: amends D-038's 'Consequence for acceptance' paragraph. R-11 keeps its current meaning. The over-cap 'skipped' disclosure stays as built and is necessary, but it is not sufficient. P-007 stays open until an over-cap admission is guarded: either its radius narrows under the cap (WI-6554700010009835), or the next targeted round attributes a newly red, previously green test in an over-cap admission's radius to that admission, names the test and leg, and blocks promotion or reverts the admission. That needs a test that exists. Any later R-10/R-11 amendment follows the reviewer's options (a) or (b): state the cap value in the BAR, and tie the over-cap path to a real guard.\nNot affected: the P-007 within-cap guard and its as-built tests; the P-002 idle-queue actuator (R-1).\n\n### D-040 — P-007 over-cap guard (D-039 option b): each red round attributes newly red legs to the admissions in its window, naming test, leg and basis\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed 2026-10-13, su-cb24e308, P-007 (WI-6554700010009193) under owner directive #1726 AUTO]\n\nMeasured by reading code (12:20-12:35Z, HEAD c4f47f8534):\n- markFrozenRepairVerificationRed and recordFrozenRepairSupersededRed (packages/operator-core/lib/release/frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts) are pure reducers. Both recompute the signature via nextRepairSignature and append a convergence round.\n- A published admission does not keep its radius outcome. precheckRecordOf (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/release/repair-queue.ts) writes ran/reason/passing/failing only, and markFrozenRepairAdmitted drops the transient admissionPrecheck that held radius. Nothing on the queue can later say which admissions were over-cap.\n\nDesign:\n1. Persist a bounded radius summary on each admission: precheck.radius = { status, reason, files (guarded plus reportOnly, at most the cap of 40, present only when measured), legs }.\n2. In both red reducers, compute attributions for this round. Newly red = signature entries absent from the prior signature (by kind and id), so previously green relative to the last judged round. Window = admissions after the last judged round's head, up to the measured head. Each newly red entry is attributed to the window admissions, strongest basis first: admitted-file (the test is itself an admitted path), measured-radius (in that admission's measured radius), unmeasured-radius (radius skipped over-cap or unavailable, or no record), or outside-measured-radius (measured, and the test was not in it). An entry with no window admission records basis none. Each attribution names the test (or task id), its leg (workspace) and the admission (actor, toRepairHead, atMs).\n3. Attributions are stored on the convergence round (bounded) and parsed back by parseConvergenceRounds. The round is red, so the queue stays awaiting-fixer and cannot promote until the attributed entry re-measures green. That is the D-039 'blocks promotion' half.\n\nThe pure reducer cannot compute static reachability, so the attribution is sound but not exact when several unmeasured admissions share a window. It never omits the admission that caused a red. Tightening it with per-test closure intersection in the gate flow is a later option, not needed for R-11.\nNot affected: the within-cap admission refusal (D-036/D-037), the P-002 actuator.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-041 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: gmct-r11-overcap-attribution-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: 4b80553a568e8e9e1f00ad44666fe85569c8a884f77d948fb88ee6787dfa9521\nActor: su-cb24e308-bc28-44ac-821f-84573580ab82\nReason: R-11 per green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08#D-039/#D-040, answering outside objection thread-post:1178554 with its option (a): the BAR states the cap (40), keeps the within-cap refusal, and ties the over-cap path to a real guard (D-040 round attribution naming test, leg and admission; the red round keeps the queue awaiting-fixer so promotion is blocked). The old check file targeted-repair-round.test.ts never existed; the six named files are the as-built P-007 tests (the attribution test asserts over-cap attribution and awaiting-fixer).\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-d641555d-c2da-45d9-9557-0ec4198a4847\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1178894\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T13:54:15.905Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 89 → 90\nChanged BARs: R-11\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-042 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: gmct-r10-asbuilt-files-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: 8871c89b96fe21751e6b280102fe9de1217e21ab1064ca83f5f449575734af6e\nActor: su-cb24e308-bc28-44ac-821f-84573580ab82\nReason: R-10 as-built files (same repair as #D-035 for R-4..R-15): the activation seeder named packages/operator-core/lib/release/targeted-repair-round.test.ts, which was never written. P-005 was built in green-checkpoint-repair-signature.test.ts (targeted round = signature entries + admitted-path radius; holds when the radius is unavailable), green-checkpoint-leg-narrowing.test.ts (stage 3, D-040 era) and green-checkpoint.test.ts (a targeted green proceeds to one full gate at that sha before promotion). Model and driftMarkers are unchanged; only the check files and method text change.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-99cbf4ec-f99e-491d-8cf4-cf1e40ee3dc8\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1178914\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T14:10:00.223Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 90 → 91\nChanged BARs: R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-10\n\n### D-043 — Owner-directed session recovery: su-c05233eb continues the whole plan to shipped status under AUTO\nDate: 2026-10-13\nOwner turn in this current session: \"e73c0db9-fdab-4689-be26-eddb9b7d7d1e - Find this session then put yourself on auto mode and continue where they left off. Handoff requested from predecessor with verbatim owner evidence; claims are acquired only after release, no claim conflict override.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-018, P-028, P-029, P-030, P-031\n\n### D-044 — P029 extends the existing SLO ledger, watchdog and Git panel for recurring non-verdict reasons\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured: gate-fire-ledger.ts owns the status classifier and distinguishes terminal skip/no-verdict outcomes from anchor/pending/fixer diagnostics. pipeline-events.ts stores exact workspace/install scope and fire IDs. green-main-slo-watchdog.ts already reads the ledger, opens keyed conditions before once-per-episode owner notification, and positively resolves exact subjects. git-pipeline-stats.ts and GitClient.tsx render this same SLO object.\nImplementation reuses these surfaces; no new table/tool/routine/config. Read grouped terminal skip/no-verdict outcomes in a rolling24h window, one fire/status per count (legacy rows by row ID). Exclude verdicts, pending, promotion failures and dispatch diagnostics. Publish counts and explicit unknown on read failure. Six or more outcomes of one reason in24h creates a reason/day keyed owned follow-up via existing createOneWorkItem, assigned to the verified live gate incident owner; if no owner is measurable, keep the breach loud and record a filing failure rather than minting unowned work. another machine\nslug: instance-machine-transfer-2026-10-08\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-08\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Acceptance BAR seed repaired 2026-10-15 through the canonical migration writer: 8 BARs, 23 projection edges, rubric acceptance-instance-machine-transfer-2026-10-08@1 active. Full activation/acceptance readiness is not certified. This draft remains the customer-migration supplement to portable-papercusp-container-and-native-2026-10-06. P-001 / WI-6554700010014225 is blocked by canonical WI-10007347 (P-053) and WI-10007348 (P-054). P-052 is done; P-053 has substantial producer-census implementation but unfinished proof and a held owner; P-054 waits on P-053. Do not fork those implementations. Current evidence is checkpointed on WI-6554700010014225; CLI test failures are filed to the census owner as EI-26022616555506152.\n\n**Next:** Coordinator su-08effe51 should restore the primary P-053 execution continuation; after canonical P-053/P-054 complete successfully, resume this plan's P-001 alignment and remaining customer-journey refinements.\n\n## Background\n\nA user should be able to install Papercusp on a different machine, restore their instance, and continue working with their data and integrations intact.\n\nCurrent support is partial:\n- Cloud Workspaces exposes restore-to-separate-host for GCP/AWS using a source-owned durable snapshot and existing provider configuration.\n- Kopia workspace backup provides snapshots and file restore-to-clone, promotion/rollback, and offsite replication code.\n- The workspace database hook exports a bounded harness_shared data set. It omits plugin-private schemas and selected history/operational table data, and may defer to a separately produced host backup. File restoration does not itself import a database.\n- Backup decryption requires the source encryption key; credential key sources may be relocated or injected. OS-keychain entries and machine-derived identity fallback encryption need explicit destination handling.\n- instance:capture/boot/clone reproduces a harness descriptor, not its complete persisted state.\n- Local-to-hosted migration-coordinator bundles connection/directory/host metadata and credential rebind requirements, not a complete instance archive.\n- Existing server packaging, provider-neutral host contracts, bootc images, WSL2 onboarding, state census, and seed-bundle manifests are reuse seams.\n\nSource assessment: report rpt_f494cd56-47ad-4316-b723-98026866b088, /reports?sel=rpt_f494cd56-47ad-4316-b723-98026866b088; research WI-10007630. Drafting and container research: WI-10007637.\n\nThe primary plan covers customer installations and explicitly requires a full native dev-box rehearsal (P-057). That reference case remains required; this supplement does not narrow it. The dev box remains native under primary D-001. State census and import must handle or disclose machine-specific dependencies instead of silently claiming they transferred.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Complete retained customer state.** Enumerate and restore workspace files, repositories including uncommitted work and nested repositories, local authoritative database/plugin data, plans, memory, settings, attachments, and retained user/session history. Every discovered state location has an explicit include, rebuild, external dependency, or deliberate-omission disposition. Existing hot-backup exclusions are not automatically a migration policy.\n\n**R-2 — Confidentiality and usable identity.** Encrypt the archive with a user-controlled transfer secret. Preserve or securely rewrap keys needed to read imported data. Handle account/workspace identity separately from device identity, and clearly identify integrations requiring fresh authorization. No cleartext credential export or blind copying of source OS-keychain storage.\n\n**R-3 — Defined compatibility and portable restoration.** Validate manifest, app/schema versions, Postgres/extensions, OS/CPU architecture, paths, storage space, and runtime prerequisites before activation. Publish an explicit supported source/destination matrix. Reinstall platform-specific dependencies instead of assuming executable bytes move across architectures.\n\n**R-4 — Recoverable import.** Restore into a separate destination, validate before activation, record progress durably, resume interruption safely, and retain a rollback option. An invalid, incomplete, incompatible, or corrupt archive never partially replaces a working instance.\n\n**R-5 — Single active executor after a move.** Pause or quiesce source writers and background jobs for the final consistent export. Imported sessions, claims, timers, and process identifiers never masquerade as running processes. A handover protocol prevents duplicate agent work, scheduled actions, and outward sends when both computers are reachable, and has an explicit offline move procedure.\n\n**R-6 — Understandable user journey.** Provide Export instance in Settings and Restore existing instance in first-run setup, with destination validation, progress, data/omission previews, credential reauthorization prompts, final verification, and a recovery path.\n\n**R-7 — Evidence-based runtime alignment.** Reuse the primary plan's Phase 0 evidence and D-009 choices: rootless Podman/Docker on Linux, the common image imported as a WSL distro on Windows, and Podman machine on macOS with real Apple-silicon proof still required. Optional Incus research does not block release or reopen those choices. Record migration compatibility and external-state limits without creating a second lifecycle system.\n\n**R-8 — Real round-trip proof and shipment.** Ship feature tests in the existing framework and complete isolated fresh-install migration drills for the declared platform matrix, including retained content fidelity, credential usability, corruption, interruption, rollback, and duplicate-execution guards. Final shipment is verified on the exact released artifacts after independent acceptance.\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-003, P-005, P-009 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-004, P-005, P-007, P-009 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002, P-005, P-009 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005, P-006, P-009 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003, P-007, P-009 | live |\n| R-6 | P-008, P-009 | live |\n| R-7 | P-002 | live |\n| R-8 | P-009, P-010 | deployed |\n\nTree evidence includes registered tests and migration-contract fixtures. Live implementation evidence uses an isolated current-build installation, not the owner's desktop or production database. Deployed evidence is reserved for final shipment P-010 and the exact release/install artifacts.\n\n### Canonical portable state format\n\nExtend the existing backup/state-inventory and manifest seams to describe an instance, its logical database exports, retained filesystem roots, required keys, compatibility metadata, checksums, and external dependencies. Do not revive the retired snapshot subsystem or add a competing scheduler.\n\nUse fresh verified database exports appropriate to the agreed migration policy. A hot snapshot that omitted required data or skipped its dump because a different host artifact exists is not by itself a complete migration archive. Gather and verify the actual referenced artifact.\n\nPreserve user data as logical state where practical. Rebuild caches, embeddings when declared reconstructible, packages, and platform-specific binaries. Preserve retained history by default until an explicit owner decision changes that policy.\n\nUse a maintained encrypted archive implementation and existing durable operation infrastructure. Authenticate the archive before extraction or database execution; reject traversal, unsafe links, missing payloads, and mismatched checksums. Secret and key exporters are explicit producer adapters, with per-destination rewrap/rebind behavior.\n\n### Alignment with the existing release plan\n\n| This draft | Canonical implementation / evidence | Treatment |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| P-001 | Primary P-053 census and P-054 data roots | Reuse; no second inventory or root layout |\n| P-002 | Primary P-049/P-051/P-052 Phase 0, D-007 and D-009 | Reuse measured choices; no new Incus/Lima release prerequisite |\n| P-003 | Primary P-055 export | Same format, snapshot, transport, and optional export tiers |\n| P-004/P-005 | Primary P-055/P-056 and P-064 credential bridging | Same secret bundle, import, path rewrite, and fresh device identity |\n| P-006/P-007 | Primary P-055/P-056, P-065 reversible upgrades, P-068 tests | Proposed migration resume/rollback/handover refinements; confirm uncovered scope before adding work |\n| P-008 | Primary P-063 native GUI connection | Proposed Settings export/first-run restore UX extension using the same backend |\n| P-009 | Primary P-068 | Extend the existing proof matrix with uncovered fault cases; no parallel matrix |\n| P-010 | Primary P-067 release and P-069 user docs | Same release train and docs, with migration guidance |\n\nThe primary plan owns both distribution and migration: one Server build, native and container packagings, declared PG/state/secret/cache roots, and one export/import contract. A user can move native-to-native, native-to-container, container-to-native, or container-to-container within the verified support matrix. Packaging an image never substitutes for transporting the mutable data and secrets.\n\n### Runtime alignment and optional future research\n\n| Technology | Current / planned role | Effect on this supplement |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Docker / Podman and OCI rootfs | Existing integration; primary D-009 selects rootless Podman by default on Linux and supports Docker | Reuse the selected runtime and capture persistent volumes separately |\n| bootc | Existing cloud workspace-host OS packaging | Remains a separate reuse surface; do not substitute it for the primary Server/runtime-rootfs artifact |\n| WSL2 | Existing Windows onboarding; primary P-061 uses the same OCI rootfs artifact as the container image | Reuse the selected Windows path, with state on WSL ext4 |\n| Podman machine on macOS | Selected in primary D-009 from published data | Preserve the choice; retain the real Apple-silicon validation required by D-007/P-062 |\n| Incus system containers / VMs | Additional technology with no runtime integration found in the reviewed source | Optional future Linux appliance/host adapter research; no first-release dependency |\n| Lima / Colima | Already considered in primary P-050/D-007; Podman machine was selected afterward | Not a new discovery or a reason to repeat runtime selection |\n| CRIU stateful process migration | Outside the restart-based move contract | No dependency on moving running process memory |\n\nEarlier D-002's Incus/Lima recommendation was made without reading the primary plan. This section supersedes that proposal: follow the approved shared build/state contract and selected runtimes. New runtime adoption requires a separate explicit decision after evidence, not an incidental change to the transfer plan.\n\nKeep the GUI native under primary D-003. The existing BYOC connection manager is the shared connection seam for native, local container, and hosted Servers.\n\n### Safe cutover\n\nCreate a consistent export while relevant writers are paused. Restore with execution disabled, verify the destination, then explicitly hand over execution ownership. Keep source data for rollback; deactivation and device revocation follow the approved ownership procedure.\n\nAn offline archive cannot remotely stop an old disconnected computer. The offline move flow must require verified source shutdown/fencing and make that limitation visible, rather than promise an impossible automatic lock across disconnected hosts.\n\n### Scope boundaries\n\nThe first release transfers persisted state and restarts services. It does not migrate RAM, open terminals, active model requests, or native application processes. No automatic deletion of source data, live zero-downtime migration, or general cross-cloud account copying. Preserve the primary plan's full native dev-box scratch rehearsal and native-host constraint. Unsupported external roots and integrations are disclosed and block an unqualified successful-transfer claim.\n\nFirst prove the approved same-OS/same-architecture route. Cross-OS and cross-architecture claims require their own successful drills; the archive format should permit those future adapters.\n\n## Phase 1 — Contract and architecture\n\n- **P-001** `blocked` Reuse primary P-053/P-054's instance-state contract, producer inventory, and shared data roots; align the migration UX with the primary supported matrix. — note: Typed external dependency is recorded on WI-6554700010014225: consume canonical primary P-053/P-054 when finished; existing primary owner su-83cc1cde holds P-053. BAR seed repaired; do not duplicate core work.\n  Acceptance: producer-owned state census has a disposition for each discovered state root/database/secret; external files and plugin schemas are included or explicitly handled; compatibility and fixture datasets are documented. Confirm owner choices listed below before implementation relies on them.\n\n- **P-002** `todo` Reuse the primary runtime decisions and Phase 0 evidence; identify only uncovered migration acceptance refinements. blocked-by: P-001\n  Acceptance: reference primary D-003/D-004/D-007/D-009 and P-049/P-051/P-052. Preserve rootless Podman/Docker, WSL direct Server, and macOS Podman machine defaults. Incus is optional future research and Lima was already considered. Do not repeat runtime benchmarks or introduce a release blocker; preserve the primary real-Mac verification requirement.\n\n## Phase 2 — Export and import primitives\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Use primary P-055's complete export and verified manifest; propose only uncovered migration UX/acceptance refinements, with no second export implementation. blocked-by: P-001, P-002\n  Acceptance: required logical databases, plugin data, local and replicated stores, repositories/uncommitted work, retained history, and external-root mappings are represented; missing or stale required dumps fail export; caches are explicitly reconstructible; interrupted export never publishes a complete-looking archive.\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Use primary P-055/P-056's encrypted secret bundle, data keys, fresh identity, and credential rebind; align customer-facing prompts and failure criteria. blocked-by: P-001, P-002\n  Acceptance: transfer encryption, authenticated verification, key preservation/rewrap, device registration, and integration rebind are tested; wrong passphrase or unavailable required key fails clearly without modifying destination state.\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Use primary P-056's fresh-destination import and the runtime selected by primary D-009; add no independent runtime adapter or import stack. blocked-by: P-003, P-004\n  Acceptance: preflight validates format/checksums/versions/OS/architecture/extensions/space/paths; import restores databases and files into a separate destination, rebuilds declared dependencies, handles UID/permissions and path relocation, and reports external dependencies before activation.\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Propose uncovered migration progress, idempotent resume, staged activation, and rollback refinements for primary P-056 and its existing operation infrastructure. blocked-by: P-005\n  Acceptance: injected crashes at export/import/activation boundaries resume or roll back with no source loss, archive duplication, partially active instance, or stale operation claims.\n\n## Phase 3 — Execution handover and UI\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Propose uncovered customer execution-handover refinements around primary P-055 quiescence and P-056 identity regeneration, using existing controls. blocked-by: P-005, P-006\n  Acceptance: no transferred PID/session claim becomes live; destination agents/jobs remain paused until verification and ownership handover; online and offline move procedures prevent duplicate execution within their stated contract; source recovery remains available.\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Add Export instance and first-run Restore existing instance using registered UI components and existing data-sync surfaces. blocked-by: P-006, P-007\n  Acceptance: isolated native-desktop journey covers scope preview, encryption-secret handling, target validation, progress/resume, reauthorization, verification, handover, and rollback. Use design registry search and spec validation before UI implementation.\n\n## Phase 4 — Acceptance and shipment\n\n- **P-009** `todo` Extend primary P-068's proof matrix with any uncovered migration fault and handover cases; reuse the existing fresh-install drills and independent acceptance. blocked-by: P-007, P-008\n  Acceptance: exact retained-content and credential readback, plugin data, moved paths/hostnames, wrong passphrase, tampering, unsafe archive paths, missing external volume, unsupported version/architecture, disk shortage, interrupted operation, rollback, and dual-execution scenarios pass in the real suites and isolated current-build installations. Record the checked population and explicit residue.\n\n- **P-010** `todo` Use primary P-067/P-068/P-069's release, acceptance, and user-docs path for the shipped migration journey; create no parallel release train. blocked-by: P-009\n  Acceptance: published source/destination support matrix matches successful drills; exact signed installer/server artifacts contain the feature; final migration succeeds on those artifacts; deployed-only evidence is separate from current-build proof. Respect the single-owner live release-gate lane.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Draft authorization and scope\nThe owner requested a plan and container-technology assessment. This plan stays draft; drafting does not activate implementation or select a fleet route. Authorization and execution route are confirmed before activation unless an effective AUTO grant changes that requirement.\n\n### D-002 — Earlier runtime proposal superseded by the primary plan\nThe earlier proposal to make Incus/Lima comparison a prerequisite was based on an incomplete plan inventory. Primary D-003/D-004 already establish a containerized Server with native GUI and one shared build/state contract; D-009 selects the runtimes and full-by-default export policy. Use those decisions. Incus remains possible future research; Lima was already considered and is not the selected macOS route.\n\nMeasured: primary Requirements R-3/R-4/R-5/R-7/R-10/R-11/R-16/R-17, Design, Decisions D-003/D-004/D-007/D-009, and item reads P-053 through P-056 plus P-057/P-063/P-068/P-069 on 2026-10-08. No claim of finished export/import or shipped container release is made.\n\n### D-003 — Restart-based moves and honest data boundaries\nRecommend persisted-state transfer with controlled restart. Do not silently apply hot-backup history exclusions, copy encrypted keychain files across machines, or claim container images include external volumes. Live process migration is outside the proposed first release.\n\n### D-004 — Review only uncovered refinements; preserve approved choices\nThe primary plan already decides full export by default with optional transcript/test-DB exclusions, native and container variants on all three platforms, a native GUI, shared roots/builds, and runtime defaults. Do not present these as unresolved choices again. Review whether Settings/first-run migration UI, interruption/rollback UX, and explicit offline executor shutdown need added scope inside the primary plan. Any new runtime or change to the approved support policy is a separate owner decision.\n\n### D-005 — Canonical migration implementation is the portable release plan\nPrimary plan: portable-papercusp-container-and-native-2026-10-06. This draft is an alignment and customer-journey supplement; it must not activate duplicate census, export/import, runtime selection, E2E, or release work. The alignment map names the existing implementing items. Original requirements remain preserved as proposed acceptance detail, with shared implementation owned by the primary plan.\n\nThe primary plan remains unchanged by this draft correction. Fold only verified gaps into its owning lane after review; keep its independent acceptance rubric and evidence requirements intact.\n\n### D-006 — Shared implementation remains on the portable container/native release plan\nDate: 2026-10-09\nAffects: portable-papercusp-container-and-native-2026-10-06\n[turn:self] This draft is a customer-migration acceptance/UX supplement to the existing portable container/native release plan. That primary plan already owns census/data roots, encrypted whole-install export/import, native/container migration proof, and the shared release/docs path. Its approved Server/GUI and shared-build/state decisions plus the Phase 0 runtime decision remain governing. This draft must not activate duplicate core work or add Incus/Lima selection as a release dependency.\n\nOptional runtime research requires a separate decision. Proposed refinements are Settings/first-run migration UI, interrupted-import/staged rollback behavior, explicit move/clone and offline executor shutdown, and fault tests inside the existing matrix. Review those for actual gaps before adding work to the primary plan. This correction does not change its requirements or activate either plan.\n\nMeasured: primary plan Requirements, Design, Decisions, and relevant canonical item reads were inspected in this turn; snapshot version 48, contentHash bd78dfdda19cc0630790c952dce582d5a58bb9907b4da3fdd79c6a12bcf74b77. The concrete parent-item mapping is in this draft's Design section, under Alignment with the existing release plan. R-1 through R-6 and R-8 derive from the transfer goal and failure boundaries in the saved assessment. R-7 derives from the explicit container question. Actual equity, additional-equity returns, OpenZeppelin foundations and no Tokeny.\n\n**Next:** Activate the conversation-audited plan, implement contracts and unsigned wallet integration, verify real EVM journeys, and ship the software.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-10007432 — Add pinned OpenZeppelin/compiler/EVM test dependencies, reproducible compilation and artifact generation within the existing operator-core testing framework. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007433 — Implement legally committed equity, eligible transfers, grant commitments/accrual, proportional equity-return entitlements and consented recovery with supply invariants. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007434 — Implement OpenZeppelin member-and-holder governance, protected amendment thresholds and timelocked bounded execution; close role/mint/upgrade bypass paths. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007435 — Integrate artifacts, unsigned constructor/action calldata and chain inspection with Papercusp tool framework; document issuer/eligibility/grant/reward activation and limits. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007436 — Register and run real EVM behavior tests, meaningful adversarial invariant sequences, and authenticated current-build integration checks; repair failures. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-10007437 — Finish item code-truth audit, current as-built acceptance rubric and independent grading; verify final artifact/service shipment and mark the plan shipped. <!-- P-006 -->\n## Background\nAvi chose employee ownership with dynamic equity grants, member-approved dilution, equity-paid returns and self-amending DAO rules. This plan extends the existing shared-pot governance/accounting/Safe infrastructure. Research reports are context, not implementation evidence. The current DAO plan explicitly excluded equity; this is the separately authorized equity lane.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Maintained foundations.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Pinned OpenZeppelin compilation produces reproducible deployable artifacts and contains no Tokeny dependency.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Pinned OpenZeppelin compilation produces reproducible Do not invent customer results, prices, Azure deployments, credit awards, or approval guarantees. Prices remain by quote unless Avi supplies approved amounts. Azure use is explicitly a future plan.\n**R-3 — Reviewable and verified delivery.** Reuse the existing website design, build and tests. Reuse its card styles, access dialog and /about founder bio. Existing commercial model: papercusp-monetization-2026-09-04, Product and pricing proposal. Verification report: /reports/rpt_5474b826-3138-4a67-a140-2b597ddafb97.\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Preserve factual boundaries\nThe existing monetization plan does not approve dollar prices or assert a completed customer pilot. Publish pricing by quote and label proof as internal product validation unless Avi provides approved replacements. The founder is Avraham Weiss, using the already public /about biography.\n\n### D-002 — Execution and publication\nImplementation runs directly in this session using the public site's separate canonical repository, not a monorepo worktree. Respect its explicit publication review gate. Next repair: Before mutating BAR state, run dev:pipeline_position { path: \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/with-plan-lock.ts\", marker: \"synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision\" } to distinguish a stale serving build from a live guard. If the synchronizer is not deployed, land/redeploy it first; otherwise re-seed or amend atomically so subject and rubric revision pins agree.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nDraft by su-703445b7 from owner directive #1560 [owner:Avi 2026-10-08]: \"Write a plan for filling the gaps and improving our su ideate and scout pipelines and then put yourself on auto mode and implement them yourself\". Route A (self), AUTO mode. Gym is paused per #1558 and out of scope. Evidence: reports rpt_d49be19f-a171-40a1-8666-cf49f49e59c6 (current) and rpt_263bd0ed (superseded); audit WI-10007368. Overlapping stale plans to reconcile in P-010: scout-idea-grading-2026-06-12 and su-ideate-learning-substrate-2026-07-10.\n\n**Next:** Vet the current acceptance-rubric criteria BEFORE binding proof or emitting adequacy cards (amend → vet → attest → bind → cards → grade): a vetting critique usually becomes an amendment, and proof bound first must then be re-bound.\n\n## Background\n- The outcome resolver leaves 340 scout ideas pending although their WIs are terminal (WI-10007390). 607 gym-rail ideas are pending by code.\n- Scout pays for generation, then dedups 87% and routes ~0 ($56.63 in 7d; WI-10007380). Dedup similarity overlaps true duplicates with distinct ideas (WI-35809).\n- Routed ideas are not claimed: 429 scout + 71 su-ideate improvement items unassigned since July. The idea backlog is 29-44% self-redundant (EI-19480163059215610). Claim-spec cannot target ideation items (EI-18697923246606437).\n- Scout cycle error rate is 8% (inference-gateway transport deaths); the host is stale (EI-18700942267136001).\n- su-ideate volume fell from 24-28/wk to 3/wk. It depends on ad-hoc IDEATE mode. ideate-pass-record fails with invalid_input (EI-24428150977170134).\n- No human grades since August; only 2/513 graded ideas were revised; agent-review is mixed into ideation metrics; lens weights are flat.\n- Producers have failed silently (Red Queen for 11 weeks, the pot switch for 11 days, the Gym idle) with no alarm.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Terminal outcomes resolve.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Every routed scout and su-ideate idea whose work-item is terminal (done, closed, dropped, resolved) resolves won or lost, never pending.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77911c5f-0f59-447b-a449-e15acf7cd05b:21\",\"WI-10007390\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A routed idea whose work-item is in a terminal state (done, closed, dropped, resolved) carries outcome won or lost.\",\"falsifier\":\"A routed scout or su-ideate idea whose work-item reached done, closed, dropped or resolved more than one refresh interval ago still reads outcome pending.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named tests; query routed-idea outcomes joined to work_items for terminal work-items (done, closed, dropped, resolved) still pending; expect none older than one refresh interval. Authority: plan Phase 1 (P-001).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/outcome-feedback.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/routed-ledger.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/routed-ledger.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Paused-rail ideas are classified unresolvable.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Ideas that can never resolve (routed to a paused rail such as the gym) are classified unresolvable.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77911c5f-0f59-447b-a449-e15acf7cd05b:21\",\"WI-10007390\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A routed idea on a paused rail carries outcome unresolvable.\",\"falsifier\":\"An idea routed to a paused rail reads outcome pending or won or lost instead of unresolvable.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named test; count ideas routed to a paused rail by outcome; expect every one unresolvable. Authority: plan Phase 1 (P-002).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/routed-ledger.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Paused-rail ideas leave the denominators.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Ideas that can never resolve are excluded from win-rate denominators.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77911c5f-0f59-447b-a449-e15acf7cd05b:21\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Win-rate denominators in the success metrics exclude ideas routed to a paused rail.\",\"falsifier\":\"A gym-rail idea is counted in a win-rate denominator while the gym is paused.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named test; read blender:success-metrics denominators and confirm paused-rail ideas are absent. Authority: plan Phase 1 (P-002).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/success-metrics.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — No paid generation under deep throttle.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Scout skips or curbs paid generation when its output would predictably be unclaimed (deep admission throttle).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77911c5f-0f59-447b-a449-e15acf7cd05b:21\",\"WI-10007380\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A scout cycle under a deep admission throttle spends no paid generation.\",\"falsifier\":\"A scout cycle that ran while the admission throttle was deep shows nonzero generation spend.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named test; inspect scout cycle records taken under a deep throttle for zero generation spend. Authority: plan Phase 2 (P-003).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/generation-preflight-guard.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — No paid generation after a high dedup rate.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Scout skips or curbs paid generation when its output would predictably be discarded (high recent dedup rate).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77911c5f-0f59-447b-a449-e15acf7cd05b:21\",\"WI-10007380\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A scout cycle whose recent dedup rate exceeds the guard threshold spends no paid generation.\",\"falsifier\":\"A scout cycle that ran while the recent dedup rate exceeded the guard threshold shows nonzero generation spend.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named test; inspect scout cycle records taken while the recent dedup rate exceeded the threshold for zero generation spend; compare spend per routed idea before and after. 'human' AND ts > now() - interval '7 days' returns samples_7d >= 1. human_messages_7d >= 1 is the positive control that the relation and predicates read owner-inbox messages (1151 at 2026-10-08T19:30Z). Authority: plan Phase 4 (P-010), D-012.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"probe\",\"probe\":{\"kind\":\"tool\",\"tool\":\"blender:success-metrics\",\"args\":{\"limit\":2000},\"schemaRevision\":\"live\",\"expect\":{\"path\":\"$.report.verdict\",\"op\":\"eq\",\"value\":\"pass\"}}}}}\n```\n\n**R-21 — An open su-ideate circuit raises a producer-silence signal.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"An open su-ideate attempt circuit is a raised failure, never a silent exemption.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77911c5f-0f59-447b-a449-e15acf7cd05b:21\",\"EI-24428150977170134\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every harness whose su-ideate attempt circuit is open raises a producer-silence:su-ideate-circuit signal.\",\"falsifier\":\"A harness with an open su-ideate attempt circuit raised no producer-silence:su-ideate-circuit signal, or a failed circuit read was reported as a pass instead of unmeasured.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named tests (producer-silence.test.ts covers the su-ideate-circuit cases: an open circuit raises a major signal scoped to its harness, closed circuits raise nothing but report coverage, a failed circuit read is unmeasured; su-ideate-schedule.test.ts covers the circuit state). On the operator DB, read the su-ideate:schedule circuit state per harness and the latest producer-silence collector tick, and confirm every open circuit has a raised producer-silence:su-ideate-circuit signal (D-010). Authority: plan Phase 3 (P-007, P-009), D-010, D-014.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/producer-silence.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/su-ideate-schedule.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\nFix measurement first (Phase 1), because every other metric reads it. Then stop wasted spend (Phase 2), then consumption and producer health (Phase 3), then the grading loop and acceptance (Phase 4).
