Use current source metadata and indexed sections as the source of truth. Do not create another table, embedding store, search verb, or background routine unless P-001 proves the existing surfaces cannot support an essential requirement and records that reason.\n\nSearch the full content; return the useful section plus bounded neighboring context. Results carry source kind, workspace/harness scope, stable parent reference, section/heading, content revision or report lineage, freshness/status, excerpt, and score provenance. Re-read current source state when necessary to validate an old index entry.\n\nMem0 uses its existing memory embedding space; plans/docs/reports use their existing prose/chunk embedding profiles. Do not compare raw scores or reuse a query vector across incompatible spaces. Reuse established fusion/reranking and budgets. Existing mem0 pools and deterministic context remain separate contributions.\n\n### Source and freshness policy\n\nExplicit search remains able to find labeled historical/archived plans when requested. Automatic selection favors active/current relevant plans and maintained procedural docs. Old plan status or a historic report finding never becomes a current instruction by implication.\n\nReport search and context share the server-resolved viewer and visibility predicate. Preserve owner-only defaults; this plan does not authorize widening stored visibility. Default automatic report candidates are the latest accessible non-retired edition per lineage. Store publish/supersede/reindex receipts through existing mechanisms and recover missed async indexing through the existing sweep.\n\n### Delivery and adoption\n\nWire the same source-selection rules into turn-start and mid-turn automatic retrieval and review initialization callers for appropriate reuse. Preserve cross-port dedup, ambient fences, workload admission, current deadlines, and citation resolution. Generic search scopes should expose the relevant sources where that public surface can support them, while dedicated docs:search/plans:search/reports:* remain compatible.\n\nMetrics identify each source's candidates, admitted results, omissions, degradation, and budget/deadline disposition. Do not report an omitted source as an empty healthy search. Reuse the existing injection coverage guard and prove its source inventory cannot silently omit a newly enabled source.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002, P-007 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-007 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003, P-007 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003, P-007 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004, P-007 | live |\n| R-6 | P-004, P-007 | live |\n| R-7 | P-004, P-007 | live |\n| R-8 | P-002, P-004, P-007 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-002, P-003, P-004, P-007 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-003, P-004, P-007 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-004, P-007 | live |\n| R-13 | P-006, P-007 | live |\n| R-14 | P-004, P-006, P-007 | live |\n| R-15 | P-008 | deployed |\n| R-16 | P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-008 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Establish the current source contract\n\n- **P-001** `done` Map existing plan/doc/report text indexes, vectors, access rules, source writers, caller routes, chunk caps, and governing decisions; reproduce the current automatic-source gap with positive controls; record the smallest reuse-first integration and measurable acceptance baseline. importance: high — note: ← WI-10007672 completed (done)\n\n**Verification:** distinguish indexed-but-not-retrieved, inaccessible, unindexed, and old-runtime cases. Use current source reads rather than assuming the audit's serving build is still current. Identify full-body coverage at both indexing and candidate retrieval.\n\n## Phase 2 — Full-content retrieval and Reports search\n\n- **P-002** `done` Adapt existing plan and procedural-doc full-body lexical/semantic searches into source-cited section retrieval; fix any verified chunk/text cutoff and preserve headings, neighboring prerequisites, and access scope. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007673 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Verify and complete Reports coverage in general keyword/semantic search using the existing report source, chunk surface, publish/supersede indexing, and viewer predicate; retain dedicated-tool compatibility and exclude superseded/retired editions from default results. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007674 completed (done)\n\n**Verification:** body-only terms, semantic paraphrases, long tails, title-only distractors, caller visibility matrix, cross-workspace negative controls, supersede/retire transitions, and an existing report search positive control. Reuse Reports work already completed; do not rebuild it.\n\n## Phase 3 — Automatic context, authority, and health\n\n- **P-004** `done` Add plan, procedural-doc, and report section candidates to existing automatic context retrieval at turn start and mid-turn; preserve mem0 and bound-plan context, enforce visibility/ambient fences before limits, and retain citations, dedup, budgets, and deadlines. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007675 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Apply source-aware freshness and procedural-authority ranking; document report-versus-procedure routing and preserve explicit historical search without promoting historical evidence to current instructions. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007676 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Extend existing index/injection coverage and execution receipts for each new source, including non-run and degradation reasons; verify async index recovery and bounded preparation when one source fails. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007677 completed (done)\n\n**Verification:** owner-only Reports remain private; an inaccessible result cannot leak through its title, highlight, receipt, or reranker context. One source failure preserves eligible results from healthy sources within the existing deadline. Compare same-prompt, same-corpus controls before changing any ranking default.\n\n## Phase 4 — Independent acceptance and shipment\n\n- **P-007** `done` Add durable canonical-suite regressions and independently verify R-1 through R-14 plus R-16 against current-build routes; run labeled relevance cases and native-client delivery checks across supported clients with explicit applicable/excluded coverage. blocked-by: P-005, P-006 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007678 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `todo` After current-build acceptance, reuse the elected release owner's promotion/deploy receipts and verify default-enabled retrieval against the exact shipped artifact; deliver Avi the event-to-action flow diagram/table and close only with final report/search/context evidence. blocked-by: P-007 importance: high — note: Preparation repaired under D-013/current-build activation audit#3/spec-quality PASS card EI-25997172489963085 (independent audit pending). Canonical final procedure retained on WI-10007679. No final-test replay, LIVE_GATE_OPS, recurring receipt polling or no-delta loop; resume only on exact new receipt or owner instruction.\n\n**Verification:** source-level keyword and paraphrase discovery; automatic injection without explicit search calls; current-plan/mem0 regression controls; exact citations; current report lineage; visibility negatives; long-document tail; relevant procedure prerequisites; truthful degradation; bounded latency. Tests belong in the project's existing frameworks and CI registration. Choose current-build runtime routes with dev:pipeline_position before live checks. Do not make deployed main a prerequisite for P-001 through P-007.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Full content is the search population; useful sections are the injection unit\nDate: 2026-10-08\nAdopted from Avi's full-text question and the subsequent request to write this plan. A title or summary index is insufficient; dumping complete documents into each turn is unnecessary.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse existing search and context surfaces\nDate: 2026-10-08\nExisting dedicated searches already cover body content, and report search is already implemented in the current tree. This plan extends common retrieval/admission and verifies completeness rather than creating parallel stores or duplicating the Reports feature.\n\n### D-003 — Privacy is unchanged\nDate: 2026-10-08\nOwner-only Reports stay accessible only to the owner and their author; pot/workspace policies remain server-enforced. Expanding recall is not permission to widen audiences.\n\n### D-004 — Preserve current guidance and historical evidence as distinct source types\nDate: 2026-10-08\nA maintained procedural doc describes how to act now. An immutable dated report describes evidence and conclusions at its publication time. Both can be retrieved with their provenance and cross-links.\n\n### D-005 — Draft authorization is not implementation authorization\nDate: 2026-10-08\nThis owner's turn authorizes plan creation. No plan activation, schedule, fleet launch, implementation, or live-gate takeover is part of this deliverable.\n\n### D-006 — Existing shipping ownership remains authoritative\nDate: 2026-10-08\nCoordinate with reports-library-2026-09-15 for its P-004/P-015 final acceptance and with the elected live release owner for deployment. the R-5/R-6 acceptance controls; these enforce D-002 rather than extending product scope.\n\n## Product intent\n\nFor Avi and agents creating plans: make the intended user experience explicit before writing formal requirements. Preserve the requested outcome; surface omitted scenarios and unsupported additions early. Existing full verification is unchanged. Product shaping is advisory and enabled by default in authoring/read flows; it does not create a new approval gate or claim to machine-prove semantic intent.\n\nNormal journey: read owner request/current product → record brief, scenarios, source/assumption distinctions → map scenarios to requirements and tasks → receive gap diagnostics and a reviewer brief → use existing review/activation process.\nRecovery: absent or malformed shaping data is reported explicitly with an actionable authoring scaffold. Legacy plans remain usable.\nNon-goals: external framework adoption, second spec store, automatic reinterpretation of owner speech, simulated reviewers, weakened verification, owner methodology source-turn references; R-N/P-NNN/Decision identities; plan parser and source reader; existing authoring tools and activation consult/preview. No migration, new table, parallel spec store, recurring service or new verb. Extend plans:audit with an advisory shaping preview only if needed; existing activation/completion audits retain their semantics. Interpretive review uses the existing reviewer route and clearly distinguishes deterministic structural diagnostics from independent product judgment.\n\nShaping data contains: audience, current problem, intended outcome, non-goals, original source references, relevant facts/assumptions/decisions, scenarios with trigger/user action/expected outcome, applicable failure/recovery and boundary cases, and links to canonical requirement/implementation identities. Material choices are flagged; ordinary choices get recommended assumptions. A scenario's implementation details are separate from its intended behavior.\n\nTesting: conventional Vitest unit tests for parsing, malformed and partial input, applicability, dangling mappings, source/assumption separation and reviewer context; tool-level tests verify the actual consumer path and legacy behavior. Exercise three representative feature ideas as maintained suite fixtures (bug report retry, notification preferences, collaboration permissions) and record a bounded comparison of shape omissions against an intentionally incomplete direct-spec draft. No invented improvements/accuracy rate and no claim of real owner benchmarking from fixtures. A future observational benchmark may be recorded as owned follow-up; it does not withhold a verified working authoring flow.\n\nAcceptance: focused suites plus required checks; staging/current-build MCP route exercised for authoring/audit/read flows; final live MCP response tied to exact deployed SHA. Design\n\nExtend the existing shared SU session host, native adapters and PTY host execution observation, loop reconciler, stalled-loop guard, and shared wake executor. Keep authorized desired loop state separate from observed turn activity. Normalize native running/settled/failed/unknown observations with owner/session/runtime-generation/turn fences. Reuse durable routine, delivery, command-idempotency, autoloop backoff, and transition stores. Do not add a parallel watchdog service or error-string registry. Prefer existing typed fields over new storage; a migration is justified only if existing records cannot express a required fence or retry deadline.\n\nRecover outside the model. Repair missing wake registration, attempt same-context continuation, verify a native turn starts, and retain a paced durable next action on failure. Controlled interrupt/restart uses existing carry/resume machinery only after confirmed loss of execution; never overlap writers or blindly replay uncertain tool effects. Active inference, long tools, reasoning and compaction require operation evidence; PID heartbeat or PTY repaint alone is insufficient. Missing observation is unknown and triggers bounded observation repair. Explicit stop, owner input, authorization/budget holds, completion, approval waits and intentional cadence remain protected. Persistent prerequisite outage is an explicit accountable block, never a false claim of progress.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-005 | deployed |\n\n## Implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Extend existing native/shared execution observation across Codex, Claude and OMP with unknown-state and generation fences. importance: high — note: ← WI-10007934 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Extend loop reconciliation and stalled-loop recovery to retain durable paced recovery for expected inactivity using existing wake and retry stores. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007935 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Integrate the PTY recovery path with safe same-context wake, controlled resume and verified native turn starts. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007936 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Add cross-client fault-injection and protected-state controls in the project's unit/integration suites, then verify on isolated current-build routes. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007937 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `needs-human` Complete current completion audit, independent acceptance, author verdict, exact-artifact promotion/deployment verification and shipped transition. blocked-by: P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-10007938 needs-human (1 external blocker)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Owner-approved scope and route\n\nAvi's original task is session_turn:codex:01a121d0-86f2-7622-ba48-5313020914a9:1. Present sta… <!-- P-032 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n### Audience, problem and outcome\nThe primary audience is agents working in Papercusp and the people reviewing their changes; Dream also consumes the same evidence. Avi wants useful code knowledge to reach an agent during its existing work, without requiring the agent to discover and request a separate tool. The outcome is a maintained multilingual evidence layer with precise, scoped graph answers and small automatic briefs at the point of need. Existing compiler, parser, snapshot, tooling, test and Dream surfaces remain the implementation seams.\n\n### Source turns and governing choices\nThe original scope is recorded in `codex:01a11e0e-d352-75f3-a157-2ed8aa1f62a2:1..26` and mapped below in Conversation provenance. The proactive-delivery request and choices are `claude:35b33faa-e48e-454c-81b9-39d4a7512e9b:3` and `:11`, recorded by D-016. D-017 transfers execution to this session under AUTO. D-020 moves optional R-25..R-29 evaluations to the named follow-on; D-021 adds R-32..R-34 outcome-measurement criteria. This section restates that scope; it does not alter any acceptance bar or completed-item verdict.\n\n### Scenarios\n- An agent greps an indexed identifier or first reads a source file. The existing client hook supplies a bounded snapshot answer or pre-edit brief, with provenance and freshness, inside the shared budget and dedupe rules.\n- An agent edits an interface or encounters a failing test. It receives a relevant consequence or incident brief through the same channel, with unavailable evidence stated explicitly.\n- An agent declares an intent without claiming a task, or completes a change. The existing intent and completion surfaces supply a scoped task or review brief.\n- An agent requests a definition or callers directly. Supported snapshot answers are fast; uncertain resolution and unavailable backends remain explicit. Judge-role read-only access is exercised separately.\n- A reviewer measures the resulting behavior. Per-leg issued counts, observed follow-through and same-symbol grep use recorded native windows and independent denominators. Missing evidence stays unknown. Issued responses do not prove client receipt, attention or usefulness. D-011's frozen baseline and targets remain unchanged; a persistently low follow-through leg receives a recorded tuning or switch-off disposition.\n- Dream reuses code-backed connections through its established review and evaluation lifecycle. The final acceptance matrix includes proactive delivery before P-026; shipment is verified on the final promoted artifact.\n\n### Non-goals, assumptions and open acceptance\nThis core shipment does not include the transferred optional Phase 7 evaluations, implement a new compiler or agent orchestration system, imply universal language accuracy, or establish commercial-use permission merely from Papercusp's own licence. GitNexus receives an explicit consumer and licensing disposition in P-042. Snapshot scope, freshness, refusal behavior, operating cost and native telemetry remain observable limits. P-041 still needs qualified runtime measurement and a tuning disposition; this shaping repair makes no measurement or shipment claim. The remaining requirements and governing decisions below define acceptance.\n\n## Background\nAvi asked where the GitNexus licensing investigation ended, how our implementation compares, which GitNexus/alternative features we lack, how to support more than TypeScript, how to integrate with Papercusp and Dream, and finally to record everything in a plan.\nThe direction is to own the Papercusp integration while reusing maintained compiler/parser/indexer components. A third-party engine can supply evidence behind the same seam; owning the integration does not require implementing compilers.\n\n### Recorded baseline and its limits\n- GitNexus 1.6.9 is PolyForm Noncommercial. open-source-release-2026-09-29 D-006 excludes its bridge from public/installer builds. Publishing Papercusp under Elastic License 2.0 does not settle internal commercial-use authority. Preserve this distinction; record retained-use licensing before broadening it.\n- gitnexus-deterministic-integration-2026-10-05 D-026 chose the first-party static import/TypeScript arm. This is a backend direction, not proof every graph operation migrated. Source read in this conversation: graph:query callers uses the first-party service; symbol/callees/impact/health still dispatch to GitNexus.\n- October 6 matched repository graph-quality results: first-party graph F1 0.846 vs GitNexus 0.796; confident false-empty graph answers 7.7% vs 11.5%. These are corpus-specific scores, not percent-perfect answers or multi-language certification.\n- Recorded cold setup: first-party 177 s / 13.9 GiB peak vs GitNexus 2,948 s / 11.8 GiB peak, approximately zero vs 8 GiB added on-disk index. Reported pooled query medians were 12 s vs 0.4 s; supported intent sets differ, so this is not a matched per-op speed ratio.\n- Scoped callers had separate sampled 1–6 s / 0.7–1.1 GB measurements. The import-only producer had 25.44 s / 947,992 KiB peak and high overlap with the recorded GitNexus snapshot. These are different workloads, not directly comparable universal runtime claims. WI-10007660 owns the snapshot document's mislabel of 177 s / 13.9 GiB as GitNexus.\n- First-party graph source supports JS/TS variants. lsp:query separately has TypeScript and Rust specs. Neither facts nor grammar availability establish accurate support for all codebases.\n- Dream already uses source/test-backed capability packets, source verification, relation-aware sampling, independent prior-art review, governor/cost accounting and Blender routing. Its source catalog is explicitly partial.\n\n### Existing efforts to reuse\n| Existing lane | Role in this roadmap |\n|---|---|\n| code-intelligence-routing-lsp-gitnexus-2026-08-20 (shipped) | Existing graph/LSP/structural/packing interfaces and evidence contracts |\n| gitnexus-deterministic-integration-2026-10-05 (ready) | D-004/D-005/D-026 and its own P-012/P-018 disposition/acceptance responsibilities |\n| WI-10006809 | Existing first-party snapshot producer evidence; do not rebuild or refile |\n| WI-10006543 | Caller routing follow-up; read current ownership/status before extending |\n| WI-10007660 | Existing documentary baseline correction |\n| spec-driven-tooling-integration-2026-10-05 (draft) | Coordinate source/spec/test evidence integration; avoid a second spec workflow |\n| self-learning-dreaming-verified-shipment-2026-10-03 (draft), rem-dream-recombination-2026-08-17 | Existing Dream execution/review/evaluation lifecycle |\n| dream-performance (active rubric) | Existing independent Dream outcome assessment framework |\nStatuses above were read during drafting. A runtime start-after-mtime heuristic alone does not prove the code executed.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"code-intel:native-adoption-good-use\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n### Extend the existing integration plane\nUse graph:query for topology, lsp:query for compiler navigation, existing search/structural analysis for discovery, and code:pack for bounded source/diff evidence. Retain the shared CodeIntelAnswer envelope and extend its scope/provenance/capability metadata where needed. Reuse registered repositories, testing domains, tool/API schemas, work items, plan/spec evidence and serving-runtime identities.\nCompiler/LSP or SCIP evidence supplies precise language relationships; maintained syntax parsers supply explicitly inferred fallbacks. Unsupported language/intents are unknown or redirected. Preserve per-language build prerequisites. Standard symbol-reference indexes do not automatically supply every call/event edge.\nExisting managed lifecycle owns processes and caches. No new coordination daemon, memory plane, tool family, graph database, routine or config is assumed. Any new durable surface must demonstrate why the existing one cannot be extended before it is selected.\n\n### Evidence model and integration boundaries\nCode sites and edges have repository scope, content identity, language/intents, source/test evidence, exclusions and observed/inferred/unknown disposition. A code edge is not a passing test, runtime execution, causation, compiler equivalence or authorisation.\nDiff → symbols/contracts → source-backed consumer paths → tests/docs/requirement evidence → task/ownership/runtime context is the intended explain-this-change workflow. Human/agent UX should show evidence and expansion links, not unsubstantiated WILL BREAK claims.\nGraph-assisted scheduling is advisory. Live locks/claims remain authoritative. Normal acceptance uses current-build/staging routes selected by dev:pipeline_position testClass; migration/background/native/p2p classes need their actual isolated/candidate runtime. Exact final release properties use deployed evidence. No parallel gate monitor/fixer is introduced.\n\n### Feature inspiration and licence admission\n| Source | Borrowed capability/design |\n|---|---|\n| GitNexus | Multilingual capability matrix; consolidated symbol context; impact/trace; diff-to-process reports; API/tool/shape maps; cross-repository contracts; functional clusters; concept/process retrieval; optional visual/wiki/expert-query/PDG features |\n| CodeGraph | Native/scoped cost-conscious extraction; source-plus-path retrieval; debounced sync; per-file stale banners; reconnect content reconciliation |\n| Codebase-Memory | Broad parser fallback; typed CALLS/CALL_REFERENCE/USAGE and producer-consumer HTTP/RPC/event edges; explicit never-run/skipped/empty status |\n| CodeGraphContext / SCIP | Maintained compiler-index ingestion and language/build prerequisites; portable symbol/reference/implementation evidence |\n| Serena | Language-server abstraction and symbol workflows through our existing LSP interfaces |\n| trace-mcp | Diff impact, per-symbol static test reach/test-gap suggestions and incremental indexing concepts |\nThe earlier alternatives admission read MIT licences for CodeGraph, Codebase-Memory, CodeGraphContext and trace-mcp. Re-read pinned component/indexer licences and telemetry before incorporating them. GitNexus's noncommercial code is not copied. Third-party README feature claims are inspiration, not our correctness or speed evidence. Existing rename/reference/diagnostic tools are reused rather than replaced by another full stack.\n\n### Dream integration\nGraph discovery proposes evidence-backed capability boundaries; capability packets retain implementation/test evidence and source hashes. Sampler relations are version-bound and include compatible producer-consumer interfaces, transferable invariants, purpose-mechanism and complementary lifecycles. Keep open cross-domain exploration and random controls so topology does not trap discovery in existing links.\nThe generator proposes/abstains; independent review checks prior integrations, contracts, scope, ordering, failure behavior and a falsifying experiment. Graph absence never proves novelty. Reuse source verification, anti-alias checks, governor, budgets, run/experiment ledgers and Blender authority. Compare useful verified outcomes and eventual implementation, not idea counts alone.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| R-1 | P-027 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-004, P-005, P-026 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-007, P-017 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006, P-026 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-007, P-008, P-026 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-008, P-026 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-026 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-009, P-011, P-026 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-010, P-026 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-012, P-021, P-026 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-013, P-026 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-014, P-019, P-026 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-015, P-026 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-016, P-029 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-017, P-026, P-027 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-018, P-026 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-019, P-026 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-020, P-026 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-021, P-026 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-022, P-025 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-023, P-025 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-024, P-025 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-025 | tree |\n| R-24 | P-027 | deployed |\n| R-30 | P-033 | deployed |\n| R-31 | P-033 | deployed |\n| R-32 | P-041 | live |\n| R-33 | P-041 | live |\n| R-34 | P-041 | live |\n| R-35 | P-034, P-026 | tree |\n| R-36 | P-034, P-026 | tree |\n| R-37 | P-034, P-026 | tree |\n| R-38 | P-034, P-026 | tree |\n| R-39 | P-034, P-026 | tree |\n| R-40 | P-040, P-026 | deployed |\n\n## Validation and rollout\nP-002 freezes matched corpora, scope exclusions, model/engine pins, operations and budgets before implementation results are seen. Include real project boundaries, non-TS languages, submodules, generated/ignored/dynamic sources, missing build config, re-exports/homonyms, stale/deleted edits, warm/cold paths, negative controls and cache restarts.\nTests live in the existing project suites and affected-test framework. Verify real handlers and user journeys rather than only pure adapters or typechecks. Measure cold setup, warm/cold per-operation latency, resident/peak resources, footprint, false empties, result truncation, task correctness and both tokens processed/context retained. Cache and Dream trials require bounded no-delta/stop budgets.\nFeature adoption proceeds in reversible steps with recorded per-consumer dispositions. Baseline tests remain a superset. Do not silently quarantine false failures, dark-launch routine features, copy licensing-restricted dependencies or force a broken gate. Final rollout uses existing release levers and exact artifact verification under the one live gate owner's control.\nCore and optional-roadmap scope are selected explicitly before activation. Unselected optional items must be preserved in a linked follow-up or dispositioned with a reason before core completion; this whole roadmap cannot be marked shipped with unexplained todo residue.\n\n## Work breakdown\n## Phase 0 — Baseline and decision gates\n- **P-001** `done` Reconcile the current source, prior decisions and owned follow-ups. Acceptance: de… <!-- P-024 -->\n## Background\n\nThe owner asked what enterprise customers will want that Papercusp does not yet have, then requested: \"Write this into a plan and then show me a detailed summary.\"\n\nSource assessment: [Enterprise features Papercusp should prioritize](/reports/rpt_11e890f4-7249-43a2-9679-fb3584596f02), report rpt_11e890f4-7249-43a2-9679-fb3584596f02, research WI-10007819. Drafting task: WI-10007824.\n\nThe assessment identifies eight capability areas: directory/group administration, organization-wide agent policy, comprehensive data governance, compliance/audit export, department budgets and ROI, supported enterprise connectors, approved departmental workflows, and managed deployment/support. Procurement assurance is an associated operational program.\n\nExisting foundations include WorkOS authentication and lifecycle revocation; local memberships and grants; capability/autonomy/sandbox controls; organization documents and source ACLs; disclosure labels; chat retention/legal holds; budget enforcement and billing; plans/recipes/templates; desktop distribution; backups; and AWS/GCP customer-cloud hosting. Presence in source is distinct from supported deployment availability. Product priorities remain hypotheses until validated with buyers.\n\nRelated work to reuse rather than reopen: enterprise-data-sources-2026-10-01 and hosted-byoc-confidentiality-correction-2026-10-02. Both were read as status shipped on 2026-10-09. Their implementations and acceptance evidence must be checked by the capability census; their shipped status does not alone prove every target installation supports the same property. This roadmap adds organization administration, integrated enterprise packaging, business acceptance, and operational commitments across multiple subsystems, rather than duplicating either narrower plan.\n\n## Outcome and scope\n\nBuild an enterprise offering that lets IT administer identity and policy, security control data and audit actions, finance bound and allocate spending, and departments run approved workflows with accepted results.\n\nThe recommended first release combines directory/group administration, central policy, security/audit export, minimum data-governance controls, enforceable budgets, basic recovery/support readiness, and one buyer-selected connector/workflow. Deeper compliance, more connectors, full e-discovery, customer-managed keys, and broad managed rollout are later packages unless the selected customer makes them a prerequisite.\n\nThe roadmap is organized by dependency and acceptance gate, not a promised calendar. Duration, staffing, commercial commitments, model/account choices, and execution route remain open.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Enterprise IT/security administrators, finance owners, department reviewers and employees who need governed agent workflows across teams. Developer-tools support/engineering is the initial internal engineering profile; its customer demand remains a hypothesis.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Existing identity, local grants, policy, source ACLs, disclosure, audit, budgets, workflows and hosting are foundations. Source presence does not establish a complete supported enterprise administration and workflow product with accountable owners, bounded costs, recovery and business acceptance.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Administrators manage directory/groups and inherited policy; employees run a permitted departmental workflow; distinct reviewers accept or reject its result; security follows allowed and denied actions; finance bounds and reconciles costs; operators install, recover and roll back the exact supported artifact. Qualification and shipment retain their evidence gates.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Duplicate existing enterprise data-source, confidentiality, identity or workflow foundations.\",\n    \"Silently qualify every IdP, connector, cloud, region, MDM or deployment combination.\",\n    \"Infer customer acceptance, legal compliance, certification, support commitments or shipment from source/demo evidence.\",\n    \"Contact prospects, send customer output or perform external writes without separately scoped authorization.\",\n    \"Exclude advanced controls that a selected buyer requires; such controls become explicit pilot prerequisites under D-003.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12183-a70f-7663-aa5c-aa86f3880524:1\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12183-a70f-7663-aa5c-aa86f3880524:7\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12183-a70f-7663-aa5c-aa86f3880524:13\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12cd3-b523-79e0-a48b-f6e045265f67:8\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a130a1-42a3-74a3-bf78-e6ae93d51d07:18\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Prepare an enterprise roadmap and detailed summary, then carry it through verified shipment in AUTO; The proposed first segment is developer-tools or infrastructure support/engineering; this remains a hypothesis until attributable buyer evidence is captured in P-002.\n\nProblem: existing identity, local grants, policy, data-source ACLs, disclosure, audit, budgets, plans/recipes and hosting are foundations, but source presence does not establish a complete supported enterprise administration and workflow product. Enterprise qualification must join these controls into one selected deployment and business journey, with explicit costs, recovery and accountable owners.\n\nOutcome: a bounded enterprise profile in which administrators manage directory/groups and inherited policy; employees run one permitted departmental workflow; reviewers accept or reject its result; security can follow allowed and denied actions; finance bounds and reconciles cost; operators install, recover and roll back the exact supported artifact. The core and advanced packages follow D-003 and the existing item graph.\n\nNon-goals: duplicate shipped data-source/confidentiality foundations; silently qualify every IdP, connector, cloud, region or MDM combination; infer customer acceptance, legal compliance, certification, support commitments or shipment from source/demo evidence; contact or recruit prospects without the corresponding authorized activity. Advanced controls required by a buyer become explicit prerequisites, not implicit exclusions.\n\nScenarios: (1) An allowed employee prepares a cited support-to-engineering handoff for a distinct department reviewer, under approved sources/providers and a finite budget. (2) A removed group member or deactivated user loses access across the enumerated transports within the selected bound; permitted users still work. (3) Lower-scope overrides, expired grants/exceptions, self-approval, restricted-source disclosure and exhausted/unbounded cost admission fail closed and leave auditable evidence. (4) An administrator restores or rolls back the candidate profile while preserving selected identity, policy, authorization and data obligations.\n\nFacts versus choices: P-001 supplies the source/reuse census; P-002's discovery packet and the P-003 pilot-contract preparation draft are hypotheses and proposed contracts. Real buyer/workflow evidence, selected scope/thresholds, independent acceptance-rubric review, partner trials, qualified external inputs and final artifact verification remain missing gates. Add approved group mappings and administrative UX to the existing identity/authorization path.\n\nExpose organization policy through existing capability, autonomy, plugin-grant, sandbox, and data-disclosure machinery. The capability census must identify actual enforcement points in every selected execution backend and transport before policy inheritance can be claimed.\n\nExtend the organization corpus/source ACLs, disclosure ledger, connector/source records, retention/hold mechanisms, billing budget reservations, audit/decision ledgers, plans/recipes/templates, cloud hosting, distribution, and backup surfaces. Do not introduce a parallel enterprise auth service, data corpus, policy engine, agent loop, billing ledger, or workflow runner by default.\n\nDesign new admin/workflow screens through design-phase.search_registry, specification, and design-phase.validate_spec/lint_spec before UI implementation. A new standalone app, if later justified, follows the maintained Papercusp app-template flow.\n\n### Proposed release packages\n\nEnterprise core: identity/groups, inherited policy, sensitive-action approval, pilot data contract, action evidence/SIEM export, finite budgets, basic operational recovery, one supported connector/workflow, and reviewable procurement/support terms.\n\nExpansion: a governed workflow catalog, additional demand-backed connectors, delegated finance, cost allocation, outcome dashboards, and repeated customer acceptance.\n\nRegulated and managed estate: region/provider restrictions across data paths, customer-controlled key management, complete retention/e-discovery scope, MDM and update rings, private-network deployment validation, independent security assurance, recovery objectives, and support/SLA obligations.\n\nOptional advanced capabilities become pilot blockers only when a customer prerequisite is explicitly recorded. No unrelated live gate verdict blocks writing or independent implementation.\n\n### Acceptance examples and measurements\n\nIdentity: a user in an approved Finance group receives only the approved grants; removing the group closes access within the documented bound; an unapproved upstream role cannot elevate access.\n\nPolicy: a workspace-local setting cannot bypass an organization restriction; an expired exception stops permitting the action; an approver cannot satisfy both sides of a required separation-of-duties check.\n\nData: revoking a source permission blocks later retrieval and applicable disclosure; canary restricted content cannot exit through the selected model, tool, connector, log, export, or support path; restore preserves intended restrictions.\n\nAudit: an action and its approval/policy references can be exported to the chosen SIEM without secrets; duplicate export/replay does not duplicate events; evidence tampering is detected by the selected mechanism.\n\nFinance: concurrent department requests cannot overspend the parent allocation; cancellation and missing provider bills cannot imply zero cost; an accepted workflow result includes costs, missing-measurement labels, review effort, and rework.\n\nWorkflow: an employee can complete the selected journey using an approved version, and a department owner can accept/reject the result using the stated business criterion.\n\nDeployment: the supported installation can upgrade and restore using documented controls; negative authorization/tenant-isolation cases fail; the corresponding legitimate journeys succeed.\n\nEvidence receipts must pin code/artifact, policy/schema version, test/runtime profile, procedure, outcome, and limitations. Numeric pilot success, cost, review-effort, support-load, revocation, recovery, and stop thresholds are proposed in P-003 and agreed before trials; no invented performance or adoption numbers are treated as measured.\n\n## Phase 0 — Confirm the buyer, current capabilities, and release boundary\n\n- **P-001** `done` Produce a current capability and reuse matrix for the eight enterprise areas, supported deployment profiles, source-only coverage, related plans, existing work-item owners, and verification gaps; identify actual writers/enforcement points and avoid rebuilding shipped data-source or confidentiality work. importance: high — note: ← WI-10007896 completed (done)\n  Acceptance: a reviewable matrix links each capability to current source, actual runtime/support evidence or an explicit unknown, an existing surface to extend, and an accountable discipline. The connector, approvals, and budgets converge in the first workflow; its baseline costs and outcomes converge in pilot evidence; full finance dashboards and additional connector packages can expand independently rather than delay the initial trial; integrated acceptance and owner rollout review precede final shipment.\n\nAdvanced packages are deliberately optional to the initial core chain until required by a customer or the selected release boundary. Each prerequisite is recorded in the plan before execution, not left in a chat message.\n\nSuggested responsible disciplines: product/enterprise lead for buyer scope and acceptance; identity/security for directory/policy/approvals/data; platform/operations for deployment/recovery; integrations for connectors; application/product design for workflows; finance/commercial for cost/support terms; qualified external assurance owners for legal/certification work. Existing per-message chat-message corpus documents for a source are superseded by its units; the rollup cut-over removes them so content is not indexed twice.\nRelated: P-007, P-011, P-016\n\n### D-017 — P-008a redacted SIEM export design: tool_invocations-correlated OCSF JSONL, deny-by-default redaction, hash-chain tamper evidence, id-cursor replay\nDate: 2026-10-14\nContext: P-008 (WI-10007903) needs one accepted and one denied action followable through identity, authorization, policy, resource and result, plus SIEM ingestion, replay, tamper, secret-canary and access-denial tests. P-008a (WI-6554700010011903) builds the P-007c-independent core; census evidence is on that work-item.\n\n1. Denied = error_code authorization_denied, missing_capability or role_not_allowed, or status role-not-allowed / mcp_auth_failed. OCSF 1.3 API Activity (class_uid 6003, category_uid 6), one event per record, carried in the @papercusp/hash-chain canonical JSONL export (libs/generic/hash-chain: a header, then one record per event = link + entry). Rejected: CEF/LEEF, which are flat and lossy for nested identity/policy objects.\n\n3. REDACTION, deny by default. An exhaustive per-column classification of all 37 tool_invocations columns assigns each a CustomerDataClass and a treatment. The integration test pins it to information_schema, and the read selects ONLY classified columns, so a new column never leaves until someone classifies it. Treatments: operational = emit. pii (coord_owner_id) = HMAC-SHA256 pseudonym under a caller-supplied per-workspace key of at least 32 bytes; stable, so a reviewer can follow one actor without seeing the identity. secret (args_json) = top-level key names (identifier-shaped only) plus a keyed HMAC-SHA256 digest. Withheld entirely: error_message (free text can echo inputs), metadata_json, output_ref, output_size and window_key (mutated after insert, or free-form). The test suite plants a secret canary in every withheld/digested column and asserts it is absent from the serialized export.\n\n4. TAMPER EVIDENCE. Per-event links in one stream, papercusp.siem-export:<workspaceId>, via @papercusp/hash-chain appendLinks/entryDigest. SIEM-side verification is verifyChainExport, which reports the first edited, deleted, inserted, reordered or truncated event. Continuing the chain takes a caller-supplied head; persisting that head is P-008b. Rejected: batch-only hashing, which cannot localize the tampered event.\n\n5. CURSOR, DEDUP, REPLAY. Cursor = the last exported id. A page is rows with id > cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT n, truncated at the first row whose invoked_at > now - settle (default 10 min). This keeps buffered or late rows from being skipped, and lets post-insert UPDATEs (output_ref within 30 s) settle. Batch idempotency key = sha256(stream, cursorFrom, cursorTo, schema version). Replaying the same (head, cursor) range gives byte-identical output and the same key, so a SIEM dedups by key. Rejected: an invoked_at cursor, because the value is client-supplied and buffered, so pages would skip rows. Accepted residual risk: an insert transaction left open longer than the settle window could be skipped (inserts are single statements).\n\n6. ACCESS. The export requires a human principal (admin:/user:) holding a covering governance delegation with capability 'approve' on the workspace's leaf policy layer. This reuses governance-policy/authority.ts authorize(); service principals are capped at 'prepare', so they cannot export directly. It fails closed when there is no policy chain or delegation. Reads run in a transaction with app.workspace_id set (tool_invocations RLS) plus an explicit workspace_id predicate. A dedicated audit-read capability and a service connector credential are deferred to the P-008b delivery surface (tool verb, persisted chain head with retention class 'audit', delivery routine).\n\n7. RETENTION. P-008a stores nothing: it is a stateless library. Source retention is unchanged, and SIEM-side retention belongs to the customer.\n\nMeasured (2026-10-14, as built): args digest is keyed HMAC-SHA256 (a plain hash of short args is brute-forceable). status/error_code use emit-code: a live sample showed error_code holding raw DB error text, so non-code values become [withheld:free-text]. Credential scrub is values-only (the OCSF authorizations key trips key-name rules). verifyChain gained startAfter and an empty-segment fix. Delegations need migration 1498 too. Tests: unit 19/19, integration 6/6. Residue: WI-6554700010012184 (P-008b).\n\n### D-018 — P-008b: organization audit stream, delivery tool, key custody and settle horizon for the SIEM export\nDate: 2026-10-14\nExtends D-017 (WI-6554700010012184). Census [measured 2026-10-14]: receipts are rows of papercusp_auth.organization_audit_events (DDL 907, INSERT grant 1473), in the SAME database as harness_shared (both via getOrgPg). id is a uuid with no sequence; recorded_at DEFAULT now(). Live PG holds 0 such rows and 0 governance layers, so nothing below was measured on live data.\n\n1. Stream. Organization audit events export as a SECOND stream per organization, papercusp.siem-export.org-audit:<organizationId>. It uses the D-017 batch format, manifest, hash chain and verifier, but it does not join the per-workspace tool-invocation chain. Three reasons: the cursors are incompatible (bigint id vs uuid plus time); a receipt has no workspace (workspace_id is null, its workspaces sit in metadata); and a time-merged chain would make replay identity depend on two tables' commit timing. \"Into the same stream\" is met as the same pipeline, format, verifier and delivery surface. The stream carries EVERY organization audit event, not only receipts. Deny-by-default metadata (item 4) makes that safe.\n\n2. Correlation and cursor. Correlation key oae:<uuid>. Cursor '<recorded_at ISO, microseconds>|<uuid>', ordered by (recorded_at, id).\n\n3. Settle horizon. Every receipt is written inside its operation's transaction (sql.begin at organization-data-receipts.ts:457/538/632), so recorded_at is that transaction's START. A deletion running longer than the settle window would commit behind a settle-only cursor, and that receipt would never be exported. Export bound = min(now - settle, xact_start of the oldest open writing transaction in this database, from pg_stat_activity). The bound is exact for this table and conservative for tool_invocations. If the export role cannot see every backend (neither superuser nor pg_read_all_stats), the bound falls back to the settle window and the result reports horizon.complete=false. The horizon is returned beside the batch, never inside the hashed manifest, so replay identity is unchanged. The default settle stays at D-017's 10 minutes; the open-transaction bound covers long transactions that settle time alone cannot.\n\n4. Redaction. Classified from the hosted customer-data map, then tightened. Emitted: id, organization_id, workspace_id, actor_kind, action, target_type, occurred_at, recorded_at. Emit-code (code-shaped only, free text withheld): purpose, target_id. Pseudonymized with the same key as coord_owner_id: actor_id. metadata is pii and never emitted raw. A receipt (action in RECEIPT_ACTIONS and receiptVersion organization-data-receipt-v1) gets a declared projection: operation, workspaceIds, populationSize, per-store {store, executor, retention, outcome, rowCount, rowsRemaining, exportedColumns, excludedColumns, reason}, limitations, codeVersion, schemaVersion, holdConflicts (ids, placedAt, retained counts) and revocations. The store reason is withheld when the outcome is failed. providerUserId is pseudonymized. Any other metadata becomes key names plus a keyed digest, as args_json does. The values-only credential scrub still runs last.\n\n5. OCSF. Organization events also use OCSF 1.3 API Activity (6003), activity_id 99, with the action as api.operation, so one consumer parser covers both streams. A more specific class (Datastore Activity) was not adopted: its ids could not be verified this session (WebFetch was unavailable).\n\n6. Access. Org stream: only a human principal with governance approve over the organization's root layer (level='organization', scope_ref = the organization id) may export it. Fails closed, including when no such layer exists.\n\n7. Delivery surface. One defineTool verb, governance:siem-export, which projects to MCP, HTTP and IPC. Ops: status, next, ack. next builds the next batch from the persisted cursor and head and writes nothing, so a redelivery returns the same bytes and idempotency key. ack { idempotencyKey, cursorTo } rebuilds that batch from the stored state up to cursorTo, checks the key, then advances the stream with a compare-and-set on the stored cursor and appends a delivery row. A client cannot ack a fabricated head. New tables via the migration allocator: harness_shared.siem_export_streams (one row per stream: cursor, head, key id) and the append-only harness_shared.siem_export_deliveries.\n\n8. Key custody. The key comes from PAPERCUSP_SIEM_EXPORT_KEY_REF, a reference (env:NAME | file:<path>) resolved at the point of use by the existing resolveSecretRef. This is the convention of the hosted runtime's *_REF settings. The key never enters the repo, the database or a tool argument, and it must be at least 32 bytes. Key id = 'k:' + the first 16 hex characters of sha256(key). It is stamped in the manifest and the idempotency key and stored on the stream. If the configured key id differs from the stream's, next refuses unless acknowledgeKeyRotation:true, because rotation starts new pseudonyms and digests and consumers must see it happen.\n\n### D-019 — P-008b: the SIEM export delivery surface is the loopback admin door, not an agent MCP verb (amends D-018 item 7)\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmends D-018 item 7 (WI-6554700010012184). D-018 item 6 makes export human-only: assertSiemExportAuthorized / assertOrgAuditExportAuthorized refuse any principal that principalKindOf does not classify 'human'. governance-policy/authority.ts (D-015) derives principal kind from the authenticated door, never from input. An agent MCP session is a SERVICE identity, so an MCP projection of governance:siem-export would refuse every caller it can have. Registering it would only add prompt weight and a misleading verb.\n\nRuling: the delivery surface is three loopback POST doors beside the governance-policy pane doors: /api/governance-policy/siem-export/{status,next,ack}. Each door runs the same siem-export-delivery.ts operation, and each takes the actor from the door (governancePolicyActor -> admin:<slug>), exactly like decide/delegate. There is no agent MCP tool. Refusals answer ok:false with a stable code and status: forbidden 403; key_unconfigured/key_too_short 503 (server configuration); bad_request 400; key_rotated, nothing_to_ack, cursor_not_rebuildable, idempotency_mismatch and cursor_moved 409.\n\nNot covered: a hosted-runtime user:* door for a remote SIEM forwarder. A forwarder on the same host uses the loopback door.\n\nAs-built (amends D-018 items 3 and 4; D-018 is at the 5000-character cap, so these land here):\n- Measured: settleHorizon (packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/siem-export.ts:523) takes min(xact_start) over EVERY open client-backend transaction in current_database() except its own, not only writing ones. That is more conservative than D-018 item 3: an idle-in-transaction reader also holds the horizon back. horizon.complete = rolsuper OR member of pg_read_all_stats.\n- Measured: packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/organization-data-receipts.ts writes each receipt inside sql.begin (lines 457, 538, 632), so recorded_at (DEFAULT now()) is the transaction start. This is D-018 item 3's premise.\n- Measured: packages/operator-core/lib/governance-policy/authority.ts:32 HUMAN_PRINCIPAL = /^(admin|user):\\S/, and principalKindOf (line 34) returns 'service' for anything else, so an agent owner id is refused. This is the premise of the ruling above.\n- Ruling (D-018 item 4): the hosted customer-data map classifies organization_audit_events.actor_id as operational, but the export pseudonymizes it as pii. The export may be STRICTER than the data map, never laxer. siem-export-org-audit.test.ts pins this as STRICTER_THAN_DATA_MAP = { actor_id: 'pii' }; any other divergence fails that test.\n- Measured: migration 1499 adds organization_audit_events_export_idx on the 907 table, so it depends on 907 being applied first (the migration runner's numeric order guarantees this).\n\n### D-020 — P-016: private processing routes and the customer-controlled key lifecycle\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14. Source: [self-imposed, AUTO] leader su-1ffaf7b6 building P-016a (WI-6554700010011918), step 4. Context [observed, census comment 1180053 on WI-6554700010011918]: no envelope or customer-key layer exists for content, embeddings, telemetry or backups. Key material today is p2p/artifact-encryption.ts and the workspace-host AWS/GCP KMS clients; the hosted-confidentiality design is plan hosted-byoc-confidentiality-correction-2026-10-02. P-016a added providers and regions to GOVERNED_CATEGORIES, derived from the provider API host (governance-policy/processing-route.ts).\n1. PRIVATE PROCESSING ROUTE = a launch backend whose provider host names its region (bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com, <region>-aiplatform.googleapis.com) or a customer-hosted endpoint. The region is DERIVED from the host, never declared by hand. A global endpoint (api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com) is judged as unresolved-region, so residency must be a regions ALLOW list. Until a region-pinned route exists, a regions allow list refuses every launch (fail-closed; pinned by processing-route.test.ts).\n2. KEY LIFECYCLE = envelope encryption: a per-organization data-encryption key (DEK) wrapped by a customer-managed key-encryption key (KEK) in the customer KMS, reusing the workspace-host AWS/GCP KMS clients. Scope: stored content (documents, chat retrieval units), any future embedding index of organization content (none today; it must use the same DEK), telemetry/log payloads (redacted first per D-017), and backups (dump encrypted under a DEK wrapped by the KEK).\n3. ROTATION: KEK rotation re-wraps DEKs only; DEK rotation re-encrypts lazily on write plus a background sweep.\n4. REVOCATION: a disabled KEK makes every read of that organization content fail closed with a typed error; caches are evicted.\n5. RECOVERY: re-enabling the KEK restores access. A lost KEK is a crypto-shred (irreversible). Backups under a revoked KEK stay unreadable.\n6. Every rotation, revocation and recovery writes a receipt through writeOrganizationDataReceipt (P-007c). No second key store or receipt format.\nRuling: the build is P-016b WI-6554700010012353 (child of P-016 WI-10007911, owned by the leader until placed on a member).\n\n### D-021 — Organization documents under a customer-managed key are sealed at rest and searched via a per-DEK-version blind index (P-016b U2)\nDate: 2026-10-14\nContext: P-016b follow-up WI-6554700010012443 (unit U2) under D-020. Pot- and organization-scope documents of an organization that provisioned a customer-managed key (organization_key_custody, migration 1501) must not be stored as plaintext. Search over them must keep working.\n\nDecision:\n- On write (storedDocumentContent, upsertOrganizationDocuments, upsertPotDocument), title and text are stored empty. The content goes into documents.sealed_content as an envelope-v2 blob of JSON {title,text} under the organization DEK, scope 'content' (data-governance/organization-content-sealing.ts).\n- documents.blind_terms holds HMAC tokens of the row's to_tsvector('english') lexemes. The HMAC key is derived from the DEK version that sealed the row. searchOrganizationDocuments and searchPotDocuments add a sealed leg: the query's lexemes are tokenized under every live DEK version, candidates are selected by array overlap (partial GIN index documents_blind_terms_gin), and each candidate is decrypted before the exact websearch match and ts_rank_cd are applied. The sealed and plaintext legs are then merged.\n- Migration 1503 adds the two nullable columns, the CHECK documents_sealed_content_shape and the GIN index. It also relaxes the 1502 legal-hold rule, which now refuses an UPDATE only when both text and sealed_content end up empty. Applied to the live DB 2026-10-14 10:20Z via db:migrate.\n\nAccepted limitations (a reader of the database learns these):\n- Per organization, which sealed rows share a stemmed term, and term frequency. Not the terms and not the content.\n- Participants and metadata stay plaintext.\n- Sealed rows are absent from text_tsv / documents_bm25, so BM25 ranking does not cover them. Their rank is ts_rank_cd computed after decryption.\n- A shredded or revoked DEK makes the sealed rows unreadable and unsearchable. This fails closed and is proven by the integration test.\n- DEK rotation leaves old rows on their sealing version until the U5 sweep re-seals sealed_content and recomputes blind_terms.\n\nRejected: database-side pgcrypto (puts the key in SQL sessions); dropping search for sealed rows (breaks pilot retrieval); one global blind-index key (it would correlate terms across organizations and DEK versions).\n\nEvidence: organization-content-sealing.test.ts 10/10; organization-content-sealing.integration.test.ts 6/6 (seal, plaintext control, exact search match, DEK rotation, shred fails closed); lint:tsc --files over 7 files clean.\n\n### D-022 — P-016b follow-up U3: sealed organization backup artifacts (frame format and the sealed export producer)\nDate: 2026-10-14\nContext: WI-6554700010012443 U3 [self, su-c982b605, 2026-10-14]. Under D-020, backups of an organization must be unreadable without that organization's customer-managed key. The pilot has no scheduled backup writer (pilot-processing-map: 'No scheduled pilot backup exists').\n\nDecision: a sealed backup artifact is a stream of frames. Each frame is a uint32 big-endian length followed by one envelope-v2 blob sealed under the organization key service with scope 'backup'. The sealed plaintext of a frame is artifactId (16 bytes) | index (uint32 BE) | final flag (1 byte) | chunk (default 1 MiB). openBackupArtifact refuses, as OrganizationKeyUnavailableError 'envelope-malformed', a reordered, truncated, spliced or extended artifact, and a sealed frame longer than 64 MiB before buffering it. Frames are sealed and opened one at a time, so a key revoked mid-stream stops the stream at the next frame. An artifact sealed under an older DEK version opens while that version is live. Shredding makes every artifact unreadable. Re-sealing after a DEK rotation is openBackupArtifact piped into sealBackupArtifact.\n\nProducer: exportOrganizationBackup(sql, input, deps) requires key custody and refuses unprovisioned, revoked and shredded organizations with their typed errors before any data is read. It then runs exportOrganizationData (authorization, secret-class exclusion and the export receipt in one transaction), serializes the result as NDJSON (header, store and row records; bigint as string) and seals it. readOrganizationBackup opens and parses an artifact back into stores and rows.\n\nLimitations: (1) no scheduled backup writes artifacts yet; whoever adds one must write these frames. (2) exportOrganizationData materializes the export in memory before sealing, so the export path is not streaming end to end; sealing and opening are.\n\nEvidence: packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/organization-backup-sealing.ts; its unit test (8/8) and integration test on the real key service and Postgres (run 21244100 pass: roundtrip, cross-organization and cross-scope refusal, sealed export with receipt and no credential_ref, unprovisioned refusal before any read, old DEK after rotateDek, revoke mid-stream, shred).\n\n### D-023 — P-016b follow-up U4: sealed embedding and telemetry formats (helpers, no store wiring)\nDate: 2026-10-14\nWI-6554700010012443 U4. New packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/organization-derived-sealing.ts. Embedding: envelope-v2 scope \"embedding\", plaintext = format byte | uint16 model length | model UTF-8 | uint32 dimension | float32 LE values (number[] input rounds to float32; non-finite values, empty vector or model refused). Telemetry: envelope-v2 scope \"telemetry\", plaintext JSON {v:1, kind, payload} (bigint written as string). Model, dimension and kind sit inside the authenticated plaintext, so a reader naming what it expects is refused another model or kind (envelope-malformed). derivedSealing(sql, organizationId) returns null without key custody (plaintext stays) and a bound sealer for custody in any state (revoked/shredded fail closed at use); workspaceDerivedSealing reuses workspaceOrganization from U2. Re-sealing after rotation is the key service reencrypt/sweep with the same scope (integration-tested). LIMITATION: the pilot has no embedding store (search is lexical; documents-corpus.ts writes no vector) and no enumerated telemetry store (pilot-processing-map: logs-and-telemetry not assessed; siem_export_deliveries holds delivery cursors, not payloads), so U4 ships the formats plus tests, not a wiring into an existing store; a store that starts holding organization-derived data must use these. Evidence: unit 12/12 (testing:run 4938b063), integration 6/6 on the real key service (/tmp/wi12443-u4-int.log), lint:tsc clean over the U3+U4 files (13:17:18Z).\n\n### D-024 — P-016b U5: DEK rotation re-seals sealed documents via a bounded, compare-and-swap system routine\nDate: 2026-10-14\nContext (WI-6554700010012443 U5): rotateDek makes a new organization DEK active immediately. Documents sealed under an older version stay readable (decrypt-only key) and findable (queries tokenize under every live version), but they keep old ciphertext and old blind tokens until re-sealed. The key service's generic sweep() cannot help here because documents carry derived blind terms that must be re-derived under the new key.\n\nDecision: a dedicated system routine `system:organization-content-reseal` (seeded active, every 15 min, batchSize default 200, clamped 1..5000) runs `resealStaleOrganizationDocuments` (packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/organization-document-reseal.ts). Selection: documents with a v2 envelope whose embedded DEK version differs from the organization's active_dek_version, joined through customer_workspaces (kind hosted, not deleted) to organization_key_custody (state enabled), ordered by id, bounded per tick. Each row is opened and re-sealed through the existing content-sealing seam (new ciphertext and new blind terms together), then written back with a compare-and-swap on the exact old sealed_content, so a concurrent writer always wins and the sweep just counts it as raced. Rows whose organization's key cache still reports an older active version are deferred, not forced. Revoked or disabled custody and plaintext rows are never selected.\n\nWhy a routine rather than inline in rotateDek: rotation must stay fast and transactional; re-sealing is unbounded work that has to be resumable and safe to re-run. Reuse: the existing system-actions registry, routine classification, and bespoke active-seed registry; no new scheduler.\n\nLimits: the sweep runs on the operator admin pool (harness_admin, superuser and BYPASSRLS), because customer_workspaces has forced RLS. Under a hosted runtime role it would only see that runtime's organization. customer_workspaces.organization_id is text while custody's is uuid, so the join casts custody's side (`c.organization_id::text = cw.organization_id`); a non-uuid value simply does not match.\n\nMeasured (2026-10-14, su-c982b605): `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/organization-document-reseal.integration.test.ts` passed 4/4 (selection after rotateDek only for the enabled org; CAS refuses a changed row; batchSize 1 loop re-seals with new blind terms and search still finds the document; idempotent, revoked and plaintext rows untouched). The first run failed with `invalid input syntax for type uuid`, which exposed the uuid/text join; the cast above fixed it. Mutating only the status-label mapping fails R-4.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/app/adv/hud/WorkOnEverythingPanel.test.tsx\"]},\"replication\":\"Re-run the named tests against the exact source/build; for live rubric or deployed UI inspect the canonical current revision/artifact.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Stewardship rubric coverage.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The active work-on-everything-stewardship-health rubric measures rubric coverage, rubric improvement and completed grading correction cycles.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a1219a-e998-7a51-b3ed-46b03b90bfed:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a1219a-e998-7a51-b3ed-46b03b90bfed:5\",\"plan:work-on-everything-rubric-stewardship-2026-10-09#section:Requirements\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The active work-on-everything-stewardship-health rubric measures rubric coverage, rubric improvement and completed grading correction cycles.\",\"falsifier\":\"The active rubric permits absent stewardship to count as a pass without falsifiable evidence.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"requiredScope\":[\"live\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"evidenceRuntime\":\"staging-operator\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Deciding live probe reads rubrics:get work-on-everything-stewardship-health and requires active revision 47 and criteriaHash 2bf720c3b50c952723dfef7d307a208681e72a169003a9ca6faebc94a3f4d76e; inspect full contracts for the three new keys. Unit roll-up contract is supporting evidence. Missing/stale/wrong live contract cannot pass.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"probe\",\"all\":[{\"kind\":\"tool\",\"tool\":\"rubrics:get\",\"args\":{\"rubricRef\":\"work-on-everything-stewardship-health\",\"detail\":\"summary\"},\"schemaRevision\":\"projected-tool-registry-v1:48bf0ddeb4ee84ed\",\"expect\":{\"path\":\"results[0].rubric.status\",\"op\":\"eq\",\"value\":\"active\"}},{\"kind\":\"tool\",\"tool\":\"rubrics:get\",\"args\":{\"rubricRef\":\"work-on-everything-stewardship-health\",\"detail\":\"summary\"},\"schemaRevision\":\"projected-tool-registry-v1:48bf0ddeb4ee84ed\",\"expect\":{\"path\":\"results[0].rubric.revision\",\"op\":\"eq\",\"value\":47}},{\"kind\":\"tool\",\"tool\":\"rubrics:get\",\"args\":{\"rubricRef\":\"work-on-everything-stewardship-health\",\"detail\":\"summary\"},\"schemaRevision\":\"projected-tool-registry-v1:48bf0ddeb4ee84ed\",\"expect\":{\"path\":\"results[0].rubric.criteriaHash\",\"op\":\"eq\",\"value\":\"2bf720c3b50c952723dfef7d307a208681e72a169003a9ca6faebc94a3f4d76e\"}}]},\"replication\":\"Re-run the named tests against the exact source/build; for live rubric or deployed UI inspect the canonical current revision/artifact.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Honest before-and-after comparison.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Verified-improvement credit requires an explicit preserved baseline and current audited comparable regrade after verified goal-owned repair with required independent acceptance.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a1219a-e998-7a51-b3ed-46b03b90bfed:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a1219a-e998-7a51-b3ed-46b03b90bfed:5\",\"plan:work-on-everything-rubric-stewardship-2026-10-09#D-003\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Verified-improvement credit requires an explicit preserved baseline and current audited comparable regrade after verified goal-owned repair with required independent acceptance.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any invalid comparison receives verified-improvement credit, or a valid repaired comparable cycle cannot receive it. Raw retrieval and supplied-status presentation belong to R-2 and R-4.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Deciding classifier positive control credits an explicit baseline->verified repair->comparable regrade; isolated negative controls reject correction-only edges, changed target/rubric, missing/unverified/foreign/out-of-order repairs, stale/unsettled/unknown cards and implementer grading. Mutation accepting an invalid repair fails R-6 without changing SQL or GUI.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/goal-rubric-stewardship.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Re-run the named tests against the exact source/build; for live rubric or deployed UI inspect the canonical current revision/artifact.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Shipment.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The exact green deployed artifact includes the Work on everything rubric stewardship GUI.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a1219a-e998-7a51-b3ed-46b03b90bfed:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a1219a-e998-7a51-b3ed-46b03b90bfed:5\",\"plan:work-on-everything-rubric-stewardship-2026-10-09#D-005\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The exact green deployed artifact includes the Work on everything rubric stewardship GUI.\",\"falsifier\":\"Staging-only evidence or an unpromoted commit is described as shipped.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\",\"unit\"],\"requiredScope\":[\"deployed\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"deployed\",\"evidenceRuntime\":\"release-operator\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Deciding final shipment probe is performed by root: release:trace and runtime health identify the same green shipped commit/artifact containing the audited blobs, followed by Tauri observation of three duties, cycle status/evidence/gap rendering on that exact artifact. Preserve artifact/hash, green promotion and GUI observation evidence plus old-artifact counterexample. Missing deployed proof leaves R-7 unproved.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"probe\",\"probe\":{\"kind\":\"tool\",\"tool\":\"release:trace\",\"args\":{\"path\":\"apps/operator/app/adv/hud/WorkOnEverythingPanel.tsx\"},\"schemaRevision\":\"live\",\"expect\":{\"op\":\"eq\",\"path\":\"testedDeployedParity.ok\",\"value\":true}}},\"replication\":\"Re-run the named tests against the exact source/build; for live rubric or deployed UI inspect the canonical current revision/artifact.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Owner control preserved.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"An installed package contract refresh preserves goal lifecycle.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"plan:work-on-everything-rubric-stewardship-2026-10-09#D-004\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An installed package contract refresh preserves goal lifecycle.\",\"falsifier\":\"A contract refresh or evidence read resumes a paused goal, resurrects a killed goal, or otherwise changes lifecycle status.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Deciding goal package-update regression controls run on paused and killed started goals and assert lifecycle status is byte-equivalent after contract refresh; the evidence reader preserves lifecycle status. A paused-goal restart, killed-goal resurrection, or lifecycle-state mutation fails R-8. Owner worklist policy is graded only by R-9.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/goals/package-update.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/goals/package-update.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Run canonical goal-package update unit/integration controls with paused and killed states; do not use owner-policy assertions to decide R-8.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Owner worklist policy preserved.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"An installed package contract refresh preserves the owner worklist policy.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"plan:work-on-everything-rubric-stewardship-2026-10-09#D-004\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An installed package contract refresh preserves the owner worklist policy.\",\"falsifier\":\"An evidence read or package contract update changes owner picks, exclusions, order or policy version.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Deciding package-update controls compare the owner's policy and policy version before/after package contract refresh on started goals; mutation overwriting the policy must fail while lifecycle controls remain unchanged.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/goals/package-update.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/goals/package-update.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Run canonical goal-package update unit/integration controls with saved owner policy and paused/killed states.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\nExtend the maintained Work on everything goal-package body, canonical GOAL/GRADE contract where shared behavior belongs, existing goal detail sync snapshot, existing goal-scoped invocation/scorecard/work-item lineage, existing computed rubric instruments and existing WorkOnEverythingPanel. No new scheduler, database table or parallel grading engine. The component registry returned no card primitive for react-tailwind; reuse the existing console section, chip, link and settings patterns.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004 | live |\n| R-6 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-005 | deployed |\n| R-8 | P-001, P-004 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-001, P-004 | tree |\n\n### Acceptance detector boundaries\nR-1 proves package instructions; R-2 owns canonical attribution/completeness and real goal-scoped GRADE launch/claim/progress; R-3 owns duty labels; R-4 owns presentation of supplied status/references/gaps; R-5 owns the active rubric contract at its live revision; R-6 alone owns improvement eligibility, including explicit baseline lineage distinct from corrections; R-7 is root-owned final deployed artifact/GUI proof; R-8/R-9 trace D-004 lifecycle and owner-policy preservation. Reviewer posts thread-post:1169025 and thread-post:1169037 are amendment rationale, not product acceptance. Deciding checks and isolated mutations are specified per requirement.\n\n### Grading cycle contract\nThe holder owns the portfolio: identify an important in-scope target; search/reuse first; propose and vet only genuine gaps; review weaknesses through versioned rubric rails; launch a bounded GRADE assignment carrying target, immutable rubric revision, baseline requirement, repair scope, budget and exit criterion. Preserve baseline before correction. Launch/route remediation rather than implementing as GOAL holder. Re-grade the same target against the pinned revision; changing rubric meaning needs a fresh baseline. Independent acceptance remains mandatory where the rubric requires it. Stalled cycles trigger the existing audit/strategy-change duty. No duplicate launch against a live claimed lane. No monitoring mission beyond assigned stewardship.\n\n### GUI behavior\nShow all three responsibilities and goal-scoped evidence in the existing Work on everything console. Link to canonical rubric, scorecard and work references where available. Display unknown/unmeasured, incomplete, stale, blocked and completed states honestly. Reuse current role launch settings; any new control must bind to a real existing contract, not a decorative toggle.\n\n### Scope and acceptance\nDo not restart paused/killed standing goals just to prove implementation. Use current-build fixtures/integration evidence, independent acceptance and the exact green shipped artifact. Update the first-party package generation and affected installed package through supported update rails without changing owner worklist choices. Tests ship in the repository suites. Keep LIVE_GATE_OPS exclusively with the verified gate owner; other implementation proceeds independently.\n\n## Phase 1\n- **P-001** `done` Extend the canonical Work on everything package and launch contract with the three duties and bounded grading-cycle terms. — note: ← WI-10007943 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Extend goal-scoped evidence and rubric instrument classification with comparable-cycle verification and negative controls. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-10007944 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Surface duties, evidence, gaps and reference links in the existing Work on everything console with component coverage. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10007945 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Revise the active stewardship-health rubric through versioned canonical rails and update its runbook/contract tests to measure the new duties. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-10007946 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `todo` Obtain independent acceptance, run appropriate tests, promote and deploy through the green pipeline, verify the exact shipped artifact, and close with evidence. blocked-by: P-003, P-004 — note: ← WI-10007947 blocked (1 external blocker)\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Truthful implementation-item provenance (2026-10-09)\nMeasured: 2026-10-09; plans:audit refused owner-backed provenance for canonical direct user refs :1 and :5 in codex 01a1219a-e998-7a51-b3ed-46b03b90bfed.
