No acceptance BAR is weakened, no duplicate source worker is authorized, and LIVE_GATE_OPS remains with its existing driver.\nRelated: P-003, P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"work-on-everything-stewardship-health","title":"Work on everything — standing stewardship health","status":"active","created":"2026-10-09","owner":"su-97f6c152-cc26-4c5d-8867-73d1b0ddebad","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Work on everything — standing stewardship health\nslug: work-on-everything-stewardship-health\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-09\nupdated: 2026-10-09\nowner: su-97f6c152-cc26-4c5d-8867-73d1b0ddebad\n---\n\n# Work on everything — standing stewardship health\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`draft` ⇒ a proposed rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nOngoing operational rubric for the first-party Work on everything standing goal. It borrows the retired autoloop rubric's strongest product questions—continuous movement, explicit capacity behavior, end-to-end closure, owner controls, and deployed-generation parity—without copying Mug/Cup/Kettle mechanics. It composes the canonical goal-mode-e2e scorecard for the general GOAL contract, then grades the distinctive standing steward: deliberate holder lifecycle, owner-ordered worklist, unowned-frontier sovereignty, drain/plan delegation, recovering/cursed/stranded/working placement triage, claim-to-terminal completion integrity, Blender grade+triage+disposition closure, steer-don't-dispatch rails, rolling budget/circuit health, owner reporting, end-to-end stewardship traversal, current instrumentation, and non-resurrection of the retired tier. Default observational window is 24h (48h for the E2E trace). Pause or genuine explicit capacity gating may yield unknown/idle, never an invented pass. Same rating scale as goal-mode-e2e preserves trend comparability. This is an operational standard, not a release gate.\n\nv35 (2026-10-02, WI-10005180, owner directives #1240/#1241): goal-mode-foundation now also inspects the two goal-mode-e2e rev 52 criteria that enforce the contract planning duty (work-placed-into-started-plans, started-plans-staffed-and-claimed) as named critical keys.\n\nv36 (2026-10-02, WI-10005180, review su-32d1b8df 01:28Z): goal-mode-foundation roll-up gains a band for an honest critical unknown (not exercised) backed by a no-trigger census, so a quiet window can grade pass instead of only fail or exemplary. Same concept as grading-integrity rev 9. No criterion added or removed.\n\nv38 (2026-10-02, WI-10005206): goal-mode-foundation band rule completed. An owned critical unknown that is not the no-trigger kind (e.g. instrument-unavailable) previously fit no band (it blocked pass, was fail only if unowned, and the partial band admitted only non-critical ratings); it is now partial. Method text only; the woe.goal-mode-base-scorecard instrument verdict is unchanged.\n\nRev 43 (2026-10-03, plan goal-holder-plans-ideation-truthful-reports-2026-10-03 P-013, owner directive #1303): adds five platform-measured holder-behavior criteria (holder-plan-authorship, ideation-yield, owner-report-truthfulness, stewardship-loop-liveness, nudge-efficacy) so a card fails on the failures witnessed 2026-10-01..03. They are non-critical: a fail fails the card; an unknown (behavior not exercised) does not make it unassessable.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Record known gold/label errors with both r… <!-- P-022 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi, and any reviewer asking \"does today's Papercusp help finish hard engineering work at a fair budget?\"\n\n**Problem.** Benchmarking stalled after June 2026. A FrontierSWE integration was built then (plan `benchmark-suite-frontier-swe-2026-06-18`, ~2.1k lines under `packages/operator-core/lib/external-bench/*frontier-swe*`, untouched since 2026-06-18). It was validated only by a gold and an empty control on one task (`libexpat-to-x86asm`: gold 0.985, empty 0.0). **No agent trial has ever run.** The vendored repo and task images are no longer on disk; only a 17-row v1 `tasks.jsonl` remains. Upstream shipped **FrontierSWE v2** in September 2026: reportedly 34 tasks (13 kept, 4 retired, 21 new), the official **Proximus** harness (mini-swe-agent based, with compaction and git-backed checkpoints), a 20 h budget per task, 5 trials, and ranking by mean score. Those v2 facts come from mirror sites and are re-verified in P-002. Separately, `current-benchmark-modernization-2026-10-09` (being implemented now by su-0f38a) is rebuilding the measurement infrastructure. It has no FrontierSWE work, no suite-portfolio refresh, and no calibration against published numbers.\n\n**Outcome.** (1) A FrontierSWE v2 benchmark that runs the *current* Papercusp product against the official stock harness on identical containers, scorers and budgets. (2) Every external-suite comparison anchored to a published number first: if we can't reproduce the stock model's public score, we don't claim a lift. (3) A dated, evidence-backed suite portfolio stating which suites we can run today and which product capability each one exercises. (4) Optionally, a small budget-capped canary that keeps numbers current with each release.\n\n**Non-goals.** No re-implementation of the modernization plan's infrastructure (launch adapter, budget accounting, preregistration, primary denominator, stats, UI) — this plan consumes it. No public performance claim or leaderboard submission without owner sign-off. No recurring or unbounded spend unless the owner approves it. No redistribution of FrontierSWE-derived data (the upstream repo had no LICENSE as of June; re-check in P-002).\n\n**Source turns.** Owner directives #1625 and #1627, session su-b7657, 2026-10-10.\n\n**Scenarios.**\n- A v1 FrontierSWE number and a v2 number never land in the same table without a version badge.\n- A Papercusp arm and the Proximus stock arm get the same container image digest, the same 20 h wall-clock, the same $ cap and the same scorer bytes.\n- Before any Papercusp claim, the stock arm's measured mean@5 on a stratified subset falls within the confidence interval of the published leaderboard value for that model. If it doesn't, the harness is debugged first.\n- A task whose gold solution scores low, or whose empty submission scores above zero, is quarantined for that version.\n- A reviewer can see, per suite, whether it is runnable today, its upstream version, its license, and which capability it stresses.\n- A capability shipped since June (memory recall, carry-respawn compaction, fleets, locks, consult router, work-item ledger) has a defined ablation, so a result can say which change helped.\n\n## Background\n\n- Existing FrontierSWE surfaces: grader `external-bench/grader/frontier-swe.ts` (+ `-live.ts`); task sets `frontier-swe` / `-pilot` / `-cpu` / `-custom` in `task-sets.ts`; seam/arm/resume/runagent in `external-bench/frontier-swe-*.ts`; aggregation `libs/generic/bench-metrics/src/frontier-rank.ts`; report `external-bench/report/frontier-report.ts`; firewall entry in `gym/report-set-firewall.ts`; docs `benchmarks/frontier-swe` and runbook `grader/FRONTIER-SWE-PILOT.md`.\n- Known drift: `frontier-swe-runagent.ts` is a bespoke in-container opus ReAct loop adapted from metr-hcast `singleOpusDriveArm`, not the product. The runbook hard-codes `claude-opus-4-8` and a June competitor pool. The firewall describes the buckets as 5/9/3 while the docs say 7/7/3. The ingest is a hand-pasted Python heredoc.\n- Infrastructure dependency: modernization plan P-002 (primary denominator), P-003 (current launch adapter), P-004 (stock-native reference + ablations), P-005 (aggregate budget), P-006 (preregistration), P-007 (paired uncertainty, suite readiness), P-008 (UI).\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Version-true corpus.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"FrontierSWE v2 is vendored at a pinned commit with recorded image digests and ingested by committed, tested code; v1 rows remain labelled history and never aggregate with v2 rows.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:7d5abcc1-092a-4fb6-a309-dd1cf8d3f766:0\"],\"constraints\":[\"Avi chose this session itself (D-001); FrontierSWE stays an M2 in-container, own-scorer suite on the existing CloneGradeSeam / run-topology path. The only new code is the v2 ingest, the Proximus reference-arm binding and an in-container bridge from the modernization launch adapter. Statistics, budget enforcement, preregistration and UI come from the modernization plan. Dependent items wait on it; independent items (vendoring, ingest, controls, portfolio audit) can proceed now. Grading runs on a dedicated volume, never the shared dev box. GPU tasks run on rented B200/H100 only with owner approval.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005, P-018 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-007 | live |\n| R-6 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-012 | live |\n| R-11 | P-013 | live |\n| R-12 | P-014 | live |\n| R-13 | P-016 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-011, P-019 | tree |\n\n## Open questions for the owner\n\n1. Network: v2 uses environment.network_mode (e.g. 'allowlist') instead of v1 allow_internet.\n\n### D-003 — FrontierSWE v2 grading contract (separate verifier, artifacts, reward precedence, categories)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-10. Observed by su-b7657 for P-003 from upstream sources only (no image pulled, nothing executed). Related: P-003, P-005, P-007, P-012, P-020.\n\n1. Verifier location. v2 task images bake the verifier at /root/tests (root-only) in BOTH images. Only the published VERIFIER image adds `USER root` and a `/tests/test.sh` shim that execs `/root/tests/test.sh` (registry config history of proximal-evals-public/astronomy-toolkit@sha256:20e84f89…; the agent image @sha256:2fe6512b… has no /tests layer). So `bash /tests/test.sh` (the P-002 ingest's verifierCmd) is correct ONLY inside a fresh container from the verifier image. The v1 path (docker exec into the arm's own container) cannot grade any v2 task. multi-gpu-efficient-finetuning additionally ships a task-level tests/ dir (Harbor standard layout); its verifier image still owns /tests.\n2. Grading flow (Harbor src/harbor/verifier/verifier.py + trial/artifact_handler.py, px-eval grading.py require_separate_verifier): a new sandbox from [verifier.environment].docker_image, run as root; each task.toml `artifacts` entry (source '/app/' plus exclude globs) is collected from the agent env and re-materialized at its ORIGINAL source path in the verifier env after that path is emptied; then /tests/test.sh runs with env = [verifier.env].\n3. Reward precedence (Harbor verifier.py): reward.json is PRIMARY whenever it exists — a dict of name -> finite number (or a bare number); an empty file, a non-numeric or a non-finite value is an error. reward.txt is read only when reward.json is absent (float; empty or non-finite is an error). Neither file is RewardFileNotFoundError. Every one of those errors maps to grader_error (score null), never 0, and a present-but-malformed reward.json never falls back to reward.txt. Our previous grader read reward.txt first; v2 grading must use Harbor precedence.\n4. Categories. task.toml [metadata].category is fine-grained (24 distinct values). The upstream README task table assigns each task to one or two of five suite categories (Implementation, Scientific Computing, Performance Optimisation, Visual Reasoning, AI Research). The category-stratified pilot stratifies on those five README categories, ingested from the pinned README rather than hand-copied.\n5. Bucket counts. v1 coarse tiers are 7 implementation / 7 performance / 3 research (the docs are right; the firewall's 5/9/3 is wrong). v2 coarse tiers from the P-002 mapping are 19/8/7. Counts are derived from the corpus, not restated by hand.\n6. Runnable subset. 11 v2 tasks need GPUs and 5 need Modal or a registry secret (job.yaml runtime profiles), leaving 19 CPU-only tasks with no external needs; that is the v2 cpu set.\n\n### D-004 — Companion boundary agreed with the modernization plan (P-001 outcome)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11. Our P-007, P-008, P-010 and P-009 (after P-008) are independent and proceed now.\n\n### D-005 — R-9 model registry is derived, every arm pins a snapshot, and benchmark code names no concrete model id (P-010)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11. su-b7657, [self-imposed] implementation ruling for P-010 (WI-10008259). Related: R-9, P-010, D-005.\n\nMeasured gap: assertArmModelPin only compared evaluatedModel.snapshotId with the pinned registry's id, so an arm record naming a model absent from its own snapshot passed (the spec's falsifier). And resolveEvaluatedModel accepted a concrete id via the LIVE price table, so resolution was not a function of the snapshot.\n\n1. ModelRegistrySnapshot gains pricedModelIds: every claude-/gpt- key of @papercusp/model-pricing MODEL_PRICES at capture, sorted. The snapshot id now hashes { schema, priceTableVersion, entries, pricedModelIds } (modelRegistrySnapshotId takes that object).\n2. resolveEvaluatedModel resolves a concrete id only through priceKeyFor(id, snapshot.pricedModelIds): exact id, or a dated snapshot of a pinned key. priceKeyFor is the single matching rule, newly exported by model-pricing, and priceFor delegates to it. A concrete id whose registry entry is unpriced is refused too.\n3. assertModelInSnapshot(model, snapshot) re-resolves the recorded alias (or id) against the pinned snapshot and requires the same id and backend. assertArmModelPin calls it, so writeArmSnapshotMerged refuses such a record before writing.\n4. Consumers (su-0f38adbc's frozen-protocol lane, per D-004) should validate a stored pin with assertModelRegistrySnapshot plus assertModelInSnapshot, never by comparing snapshot ids alone.\n\nMeasured: arm-snapshot.test.ts 22/22 (test-run 21024608), including the FSWE falsifier probe (a fixture snapshot omitting still-priced claude-opus-4-1 refuses it); model-pricing index.test.ts 73/73 (21024612); lint:tsc clean over the changed set.\n\n### D-007 — P-009 contamination policy: where cutoffs live, what 'exposed' means, and what the report carries (supersedes the WI-10008258 04:00Z design note)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11. su-b7657, [self-imposed] implementation ruling for P-009 (WI-10008258, clause FSWE-P009-CONTAMINATION@1). Related: R-9, P-009, P-010, D-005, D-006.\n\n1. Cutoffs live in packages/operator-core/lib/external-bench/contamination.ts (MODEL_TRAINING_CUTOFFS), NOT in @papercusp/model-pricing as the 04:00Z note proposed. Reason: a training cutoff is a benchmark-contamination fact, not a price; model-pricing is a generic borrowable submodule consumed far outside benchmarks. The table is derived-truth rung 4 (curated): every row cites the vendor page it was read from and a retrieval date; a unit test refuses a row that does not parse or lacks an https source.\n2. Value used = the vendor's TRAINING DATA cutoff (the broader range), not the reliable-knowledge cutoff. Month precision covers the whole month: a task created in the cutoff month is exposed.\n3. Unknown is never clean. A model with no row, or a task with no parseable creation date, yields 'contamination-unknown'. Rows today: 12 Claude ids from platform.claude.com (read via WebSearch 2026-10-11 because WebFetch was refused, EI-25629787969556836). No GPT row and no row for claude-opus-4-5/4-1/4-0 or claude-sonnet-4-5/4-0: no vendor source was read for them, so they report unknown.\n4. Label precedence per arm: any exposed task => 'contamination-exposed'; else any unknown task or an empty pool => 'contamination-unknown'; else 'post-cutoff'.\n5. bundleFromRollouts always attaches arms[].contamination { policy, label, modelId, trainingDataCutoff, cutoffSource, postCutoff, exposed, unknown }, each subset with its own primary outcome (summarizeAssignedOutcomes over the subset). 'Prefer post-cutoff pools for headline claims' is realised as contamination.postCutoff being the figure a headline should quote; the viewer shows the label and, when exposed, the post-cutoff figure.\n6. The ModelRegistrySnapshot (D-005/D-006) is NOT extended. Reproducibility comes from the report itself recording the cutoff and its source, and from bundleFromRollouts.trainingCutoffs letting a caller pin a stored cutoff.\n7. Task creation dates are a builder input (taskCreatedAt). Wiring the PG report path and the FrontierSWE ingest to supply them is owned residue, filed separately; until then those reports read 'contamination-unknown', which is the honest reading.\n\n### D-008 — P-020 four-way outcome: 'invalid' becomes a canonical GraderStatus, mapped onto the existing modernization primary denominator\nDate: 2026-10-11\nsu-b7657 for P-020 (route A per D-001). Related: P-020, P-022, D-003, D-004; current-benchmark-modernization-2026-10-09 P-002.\n\n1. No new denominator. The modernization primary denominator already exists as summarizeAssignedOutcomes in libs/generic/bench-metrics/src/aggregate.ts: generation failures stay in the denominator as 0; a grader error/timeout or an invalid score is a missing measurement that nulls the primary score. P-020 reuses it unchanged; it does not need su-0f38a's blocked P-002 to land.\n2. Four-way mapping, per attempt whose generation completed: invalid = graderStatus 'invalid' (the pre-grade evidence-integrity check found a protected path changed); grader_error = graderStatus 'error'/'timeout' or a score outside [0,1]; budget_exhausted = completed with capped=true and a valid grade (graded on its end state, counts with that score; matches Harbor, where a timed-out trial is still verified); scored = completed, not capped, valid grade. invalid and grader_error are missing measurements and are disclosed as separate counts. Generation failures (generationStatus error/timeout) are outside the four-way; they keep their existing denominator class and are disclosed as generationFailed.\n3. 'invalid' is a CANONICAL GraderStatus (bench-metrics schema), not 'error' plus detail, because run-topology buildRow drops seam detail and harness_shared.benchmark_run_result only persists grader_status; an invalid verdict stored as 'error' would be indistinguishable from a grader fault. The grader_status CHECK constraint is widened by migration. Additive for the modernization lane: summarizeAssignedOutcomes gains an outcomes breakdown, existing fields keep their values.\n4. An invalid attempt is TERMINAL: frontier-swe-resume must not re-run it (re-rolling a tampered attempt until a clean one appears would launder the tampering).\n5. Protected paths for the FrontierSWE seam: /tests, /solution, /logs/verifier, /root/tests (D-003 item 1), plus an optional per-task graderMeta.protectedPaths list for verifier fixtures under /app (empty until a task declares one; /app itself is the submission and cannot be protected wholesale). The check is `docker diff` of the arm container against its image, run BEFORE v1 test staging. A failed diff is grader_error (integrity unverifiable), never a silent score. Limitation: docker diff sees writes, not reads; reading hidden tests is not detected.\n\nMeasured (2026-10-11 ~05:03Z, su-b7657):\n- Measured: libs/generic/bench-metrics/src/aggregate.ts — classifyAttemptOutcome (line 106) is the single classifier; summarizeAssignedOutcomes (line 129) loops over it, so the four-way counts and the primary score cannot drift. Test run 21034328: aggregate.test.ts 34/34 pass.\n- Measured: packages/operator-core/lib/external-bench/run-topology.ts buildRow (line 190) takes grade {resolved, score, graderStatus} only; the seam's grade.detail is not copied into TaskRunResult. This is the reason for item 3, and why P-022 bundles must retain seam detail separately.\n- Measured: run-topology.ts GRADER_STATUS_SET (line 150) is typed `satisfies Record<GraderStatus, true>`, so a GraderStatus added later without updating coercion fails typecheck.\n- Measured: live constraint benchmark_run_result_grader_status_check at 05:03Z is still CHECK (passed, failed, error, timeout). Migration 1449 is committed in libs/papercusp (398019910adf) and db:migrations reports it 'pending': it applies on the next operator boot. Until then an 'invalid' row insert would be refused by the DB, not silently stored as something else.\n- Measured: frontier-swe-resume.ts isSettledRecord (line 44) = graderStatus 'invalid' OR isScoredRecord; settledTrials (line 76) feeds the resume plan, so an invalid seed is never re-run. Test run 21034369-21034372 (resume 13, seam 11, integrity 12, run-topology 9) all pass.\n- Measured: frontier-swe-seam.ts grade() calls checkFrontierSweIntegrity (line 120) and returns graderStatus 'invalid' on a tampered verdict (line 121) before any v1 test staging.\n\n### D-009 — P-022 dated campaign bundles: one source-agnostic builder, scorer detail carried through, completeness verdict, raw+corrected label errors\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11. su-b7657, [self-imposed] implementation ruling for P-022 (WI-10008269, clause FSWE-P022-BUNDLE@1). Related: P-016, P-020, P-022, D-003, D-008.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-11 ~05:35Z on the staging tree. `grep -rln exportRunBundle packages/operator-core apps` -> only reproducibility/index.ts (barrel), reproducibility/export.ts (definition), reproducibility/reproducibility.integration.test.ts. `grep -rn runFrontierSweArm packages/operator-core apps/operator` (excluding its definition file) -> only frontier-swe-arm.test.ts. frontier-swe-resume.ts:65 appendRunResult appends JSON lines to a results.jsonl path; frontier-swe-arm.ts imports it and never imports reproducibility/emit. run-topology.ts buildRow (~:190) takes grade {resolved, score, graderStatus} only. Falsifier for the 'no production caller' claims: a non-test import of runFrontierSweArm or exportRunBundle appearing in that grep.\n\nFindings: (a) exportRunBundle(runId) writes PG rollout cards + an undated manifest with no completeness check and no production caller. (b) The FrontierSWE arm persists to an append-only results.jsonl and never writes a PG rollout; no production caller yet. (c) run-topology drops the seam's grade.detail (D-008 integrity verdict, D-003 reward source).\n\n1. One pure builder, two sources. New reproducibility/campaign-bundle.ts: buildCampaignBundle({ campaignId, completedAt, entries, labelCorrections }) returns { root, files, manifest } with no I/O; writeCampaignBundle writes it. Root = benchmarks/campaigns/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<campaignId>/ (UTC date of completion). One file per task attempt: tasks/<arm>/<suite>__<taskId>__seed-<n>.json holding { trace, scorer, prediction }. Sources: export.ts gains exportCampaignBundle(runId) sharing exportRunBundle's PG reads (exportRunBundle and its P-016 reproducer layout stay unchanged); FrontierSWE builds entries from results.jsonl. No parallel exporter.\n2. Scorer detail is retained. TaskRunResult gains optional graderDetail; run-topology buildRow carries seam grade.detail into it; FrontierSweResultRecord gains optional graderDetail and traceRef so results.jsonl holds the scorer output and trace pointer.\n3. Completeness is a verdict, not an assumption. manifest.complete is true only when every entry has a trace (a ref, or an explicit absentReason) AND scorer output (a status; a generation failure records status 'not-graded' with a reason). Otherwise complete=false with missing[] { suite, taskId, arm, seed, lacks: ['trace' | 'scorer'] }. An incomplete bundle is still written as evidence of the gap, never dropped.\n4. The owner declined the API-key account; paid stages run on the workspace's existing Codex ChatGPT-subscription accounts.\n\nConsequences [self-imposed, su-a553e619 under AUTO + D-020; the owner ruled only the payment route]:\n1. Route. Codex arms (modernization P-003 host acceptance, FSWE P-012 smoke and later stages) use Codex subscription accounts (codex-cli:/ credentialRefs, oauth-http transport) registered in the benchmark workspace. The API-key-only gates (estimate.ts 'Register an OpenAI API bearer account', current-su authenticateProvider bearer-http-only transport, currentBenchOpenAiInputReader) gain a subscription basis; they are not deleted.\n2. Cap semantics. Subscription traffic is not billed per token, so D-021's $150 smoke cap and every protocol USD budget become a LIST-PRICE-EQUIVALENT cap: provider-reported usage x the frozen price schedule. The dollar figures, the abort-both-arms rule and the aggregate/in-flight structure are unchanged; only the payer changes. Reports must label these costs as list-price equivalents, not money spent.\n3. Per-request bound without the API-key counter. The ChatGPT Codex backend rejects max_output_tokens (the gateway strips it) and offers no input-token count endpoint. The relay refuses connections to an unbound perTask endpoint. An egress with any perTask endpoint admits ONE open task network at a time; a second openTaskNetwork is refused while one is open. A metered assignment gateway is therefore reachable from exactly one task container. Shared endpoints (mcp, hooks) are unchanged.\n2. DockerExecTarget gains originRewrites [{from,to}]. Before every exec the wrapper rewrites the session's config.toml, replacing each exact host origin with its egress origin. It then refuses to start the agent (exit 126) if any http://127.0.0.1 or http://localhost origin remains, so an unmapped host port fails closed instead of dialing the container's own loopback.\n3. AgentRunOutput gains executionPath; runTopology stamps the distinct values of the contributing outputs on armMeta.executionPath (a string when uniform). The adapter reports 'modernization-launch-adapter' (capability:launch-agent -> headless psu via createCurrentSuBenchHarness). Absent means unreported, never inferred.\n4. New frontier-swe-launch-adapter.ts composes, per run: startCodexHookBridge, then startBenchEgress {gw perTask, mcp, hooks}. WI-6554700010020598 owns this detector repair.\nRelated: P-006, P-019\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"bm25-lexical-search-evoke-adoption-2026-10-10","title":"Real BM25 ranking for papercusp lexical search (pg_textsearch, chosen by bake-off over Evoke)","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-10","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Real BM25 ranking for papercusp lexical search (pg_textsearch, chosen by bake-off over Evoke)\nslug: bm25-lexical-search-evoke-adoption-2026-10-10\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-10\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nReplace papercusp's lexical search ranking (`tsvector` + `plainto_tsquery` + `ts_rank_cd`, which has no inverse-document-frequency) with real BM25. Engine: **pg_textsearch** (Timescale, PostgreSQL licence), chosen by the P-001 bake-off over **Evoke** (Apache-2.0) under the D-001 rule; see D-002. The new ranking must be in place for every lexical call site, within a latency budget, and shipped inside embedded Postgres in the desktop app.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Audience:** agents and the owner using papercusp search. That covers `search:fulltext`, `sessions:search`, memory/corpus recall injection, work-item and plan search, recipe and convention lookup, and the consult relevance router.\n- **Problem:** measured in WI-10008233 on 76,156 work items. Today's lexical leg finds the intended item in the top 10 for only **16%** of full-title queries and **23%** of 4-keyword queries. OR-ing the terms makes it worse (5–17%) and 100–1000× slower, because `ts_rank_cd` ignores how rare a word is.\n- **Outcome:** lexical retrieval finds the intended item **2–3× more often**. With Evoke preloaded in the trial: 46% / 41%, MRR 0.340 vs 0.103 and 0.257 vs 0.165. This holds within a p95 latency budget, in dev, staging and the desktop app.\n- **Non-goals:**\n  - replacing the embedding/semantic leg or the fusion design\n  - Evoke's semantic SSR mode\n  - external search services (OpenSearch, Meilisearch, Typesense)\n  - CJK-specific tokenization\n  - the Stage-B reranker, which belongs to plan search-core-rerank-adoption-2026-05-30\n- **Scenarios:**\n  1. An agent searches \"git-sync missed scheduler intervals crm\" and gets the matching incident item first, not a long document that repeats \"git\".\n  2. The consult router ranks the peer transcript that actually discusses a rare symbol above transcripts full of common words.\n  3. A fresh desktop install creates the BM25 indexes during migration, and search works offline with no extra setup.\n  4. An item created a moment ago is findable by its distinctive words.\n- **Source turns:**\n  - owner `session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29` (\"write the evoke adoption into a plan. Also are there any alternatives to evoke that we should consider?\")\n  - the earlier owner dialog answer \"do the evoke trial\" (same session), which produced WI-10008233\n\n## Scope\n\n- All 32 source files that rank with `ts_rank_cd` / `plainto_tsquery` / `websearch_to_tsquery`, enumerated under Approach.\n- The corpora behind them: work items, plans, session turns, memory/corpus recall, knowledge sources, reports, recipes, conventions, registries.\n- Engine packaging for the dev box (native PG 18.4), staging, and embedded Postgres in the desktop sidecar (`bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh`, which already bundles pgvector).\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Work-item ranking at least 1.5x today.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"Lexical search ranks with real BM25 instead of ts_rank_cd.\", \"rationale\": \"Known-item trial WI-10008233 and bake-off WI-10008294: today finds the target in the top 10 for 16-23% of queries.\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\", \"session_turn:claude:6dd7777c-87bc-4c01-b22a-000251976853:32\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"On the work-item known-item benchmark over the live work_items corpus, the minimum of the four ranking ratios {recall@10, MRR@10} x {full-title, 4-keyword} of the production lexical leg over the tsv_and baseline, measured in the same run on the identical query sample, is at least 1.5.\", \"falsifier\": \"BROKEN if any of the four ratios {recall@10, MRR@10} x {full-title, 4-keyword} is below 1.5, if either query form has fewer than 1,000 queries, or if tsv_and was not computed in the same run on the identical sample.\", \"requiredScope\": [\"work-items\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"live\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"integration\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/bm25-bakeoff-cli.ts --corpus work-items: the live harness_shared.work_items corpus is copied from the dev-box operator database into a pg_textsearch container with the production index configuration (row count, server and extension versions recorded in the evidence), with a seeded query sample of at least 1,000 full-title and 1,000 4-keyword known-item queries; the seed, the sample size and the tsv_and baseline are recorded in the same run. Evidence: docs/evidence/bm25-bakeoff-work-items-*.json via testing:record-run (operational, live plane). The bound ranking suite is the seam floor (known-item MRR@10 floor, rare-term ordering), not the ratio. Decisions D-001 (engine choice rule), D-002 (work-item bake-off result).\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/bm25-ranking.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — p95 latency budget.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"BM25 search stays fast enough for interactive and agent use.\",\"rationale\":\"Interactive and agent search calls run in the hot path.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"On the work-item known-item benchmark, with the production index configuration over a copy of the live work-item corpus, the p95 lexical query latency is at most 50 ms.\",\"falsifier\":\"p95 above 50 ms.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"latency\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"The same bm25-bakeoff run as R-1 times every query of the production lexical leg, one engine at a time, after a warm-up pass; p95 over at least 1,000 timed queries, with the host load average, server version and row count recorded. Evidence: docs/evidence/bm25-bakeoff-work-items-*.json (operational, live plane). The bound latency suite is the fixture floor. Decision D-001 (latency clause of the engine choice rule). Scope of the timed path: the bake-off times the engine query alone (the pgts arm's BM25 SQL in the container). The D-016 exact list (plainto_tsquery AND + ts_rank_cd, fused by mergeExactAndBm25 in packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/search/sources.ts) is a separate query and is NOT inside this timed path; its end-to-end cost on the search:semantic path is bounded by R-18 (D-019, D-020), measured by bm25-hybrid-recall-cli.ts.\\n\\nNamed maintained assertions (navigation, not proof of a passing run): packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/bm25-latency.integration.test.ts: 'meets the p95 and p50 budgets on the seeded corpus, warm' (case line 42; expect lines 45, 46). The independent grader reads the complete named callbacks and current source pins; a filename or excerpt alone does not establish falsifier coverage.\\n\\nThe acceptance outcome is read from the SAME original operational artifact and run identity as R-1, docs/evidence/bm25-bakeoff-work-items-2026-10-11.json. Select exactly summaries[] where method='pgts', both variants 'short' and 'title'; the tsv_and rows are the baseline and cannot satisfy this outcome. Each selected form must have summaries[].n >= 1000. Judge the maximum p95Ms over both pgts forms against 50 ms for R-2 and maximum p50Ms against 10 ms for R-3; either form breaching its bound fails. The artifact's top-level queries[] is empty and is not the timed-count witness. Record original generatedAt, commit, SHA256, corpus.key='work-items', corpus.source='operator-db-copy', corpus.rows, serverVersion, versions.bake_pgts and loadavg start/end/cores. Run identity must equal the artifact identity cited for R-1; a different generatedAt/commit, wrong corpus source, absent row count or missing/malformed selected row is incompatible evidence and remains unknown, never pass. Load context is reported, never used as a threshold or waiver. Structured instrument evidence is an explicitly supplied original artifact snapshot; do not claim the JSON is executed or provenance is platform-computed. The independent grader derives the fields from the original bytes and supplies honest snapshot provenance under the exact instrument key. Missing/stale artifact evidence remains unknown. bm25-latency.integration.test.ts remains a necessary recurrence prerequisite for percentile/budget and health-verdict wiring, and its seeded fixture pass is insufficient for the live-corpus outcome.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"docs/evidence/bm25-bakeoff-work-items-2026-10-11.json:summaries[method=pgts].p95Ms|p50Ms,n,corpus.rows,corpus.source,generatedAt,commit,serverVersion,versions.bake_pgts,loadavg\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — p50 latency budget.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"BM25 search stays fast enough for interactive and agent use.\",\"rationale\":\"Interactive and agent search calls run in the hot path.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"On the work-item known-item benchmark, with the production index configuration over a copy of the live work-item corpus, the p50 lexical query latency is at most 10 ms.\",\"falsifier\":\"p50 above 10 ms.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"latency\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Same timed sample and run as R-2: p50 over at least 1,000 warm queries. Evidence: docs/evidence/bm25-bakeoff-work-items-*.json (operational, live plane). Decision D-001.\\n\\nNamed maintained assertions (navigation, not proof of a passing run): packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/bm25-latency.integration.test.ts: 'meets the p95 and p50 budgets on the seeded corpus, warm' (case line 42; expect lines 45, 46). The independent grader reads the complete named callbacks and current source pins; a filename or excerpt alone does not establish falsifier coverage.\\n\\nThe acceptance outcome is read from the SAME original operational artifact and run identity as R-1, docs/evidence/bm25-bakeoff-work-items-2026-10-11.json. Select exactly summaries[] where method='pgts', both variants 'short' and 'title'; the tsv_and rows are the baseline and cannot satisfy this outcome. Each selected form must have summaries[].n >= 1000. Judge the maximum p95Ms over both pgts forms against 50 ms for R-2 and maximum p50Ms against 10 ms for R-3; either form breaching its bound fails. The artifact's top-level queries[] is empty and is not the timed-count witness. Record original generatedAt, commit, SHA256, corpus.key='work-items', corpus.source='operator-db-copy', corpus.rows, serverVersion, versions.bake_pgts and loadavg start/end/cores. Run identity must equal the artifact identity cited for R-1; a different generatedAt/commit, wrong corpus source, absent row count or missing/malformed selected row is incompatible evidence and remains unknown, never pass. Load context is reported, never used as a threshold or waiver. Structured instrument evidence is an explicitly supplied original artifact snapshot; do not claim the JSON is executed or provenance is platform-computed. The independent grader derives the fields from the original bytes and supplies honest snapshot provenance under the exact instrument key. Missing/stale artifact evidence remains unknown. bm25-latency.integration.test.ts remains a necessary recurrence prerequisite for percentile/budget and health-verdict wiring, and its seeded fixture pass is insufficient for the live-corpus outcome.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"docs/evidence/bm25-bakeoff-work-items-2026-10-11.json:summaries[method=pgts].p95Ms|p50Ms,n,corpus.rows,corpus.source,generatedAt,commit,serverVersion,versions.bake_pgts,loadavg\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Health check catches a missing preload.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"The engine running without its required configuration must not go unnoticed.\", \"rationale\": \"pg_textsearch needs shared_preload_libraries; without it BM25 is unavailable and the seam would fall back.\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"The BM25 health check reports unhealthy when pg_textsearch is missing from shared_preload_libraries.\", \"falsifier\": \"BROKEN if (1) the health check reports healthy on a server without the preload, or (2) it reports healthy while lexical search is serving the ts_rank_cd fallback.\", \"requiredScope\": [\"health-check\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"integration\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"Integration test on a containerized pg_textsearch server with and without the preload. Decisions D-003 (availability gate and health check), D-008 (the dev box served the legacy fallback silently).\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/bm25-health.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Desktop ships BM25.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"The engine works in embedded Postgres inside the shipped desktop app.\", \"rationale\": \"The desktop app is the product; licence must permit distribution (PostgreSQL licence).\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"A fresh desktop install with an isolated database returns BM25-ranked search results offline.\", \"falsifier\": \"BROKEN if (1) a fresh install lacks the extension, fails migration, or ranks with ts_rank_cd; (2) the bundled embedded Postgres is below 18.4; (3) the postmaster fails to start with pg_textsearch preloaded (palloc_mul).\", \"requiredScope\": [\"desktop-sidecar\", \"migrations\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"live\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"unit\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"Build the sidecar, boot scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh with VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1, read the BM25 health check and run a ranked search. Evidence: the headless transcript docs/evidence/bm25-r5-headless-2026-10-11.json via testing:record-run (operational, live plane); the bound sidecar test checks the bundle step. Decisions D-003, D-014.\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"papercusp-desktop/test/build-desktop-sidecar-pg-textsearch.test.js\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — New writes are searchable quickly.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"Newly written items are searchable while the fleet writes continuously.\", \"rationale\": \"Agents search for items created moments ago.\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"Under sustained concurrent writes, a committed work item is returned by a search on its distinctive terms within 5 seconds.\", \"falsifier\": \"A committed item is missing from results beyond 5 seconds.\", \"requiredScope\": [\"write-visibility\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"integration\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"Write-load integration test (bm25-write-load, case R-6): 4 concurrent writers, 250-row insert batches plus 100-row updates, at least 30 batches each, maintenance every second, at least 20 probes of which at least 10 are title updates; each probe searched through the lexical seam until found. Decision D-010 (maintenance runs during the load).\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/bm25-write-load.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Index stays compact under writes.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"The index stays healthy as the fleet writes continuously.\", \"rationale\": \"Unbounded segment growth would degrade latency and disk.\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"After the write-load run, every BM25 index is at most 1.5 times the size of its fresh rebuild.\", \"falsifier\": \"Any index exceeds 1.5x its REINDEX size.\", \"requiredScope\": [\"maintenance\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"integration\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"Write-load integration test (bm25-write-load, case R-7): maintenance (compaction plus the D-010 reclaim) runs every second during the load and to quiescence after it; then each BM25 index is compared with its own REINDEX. The case also asserts the load passed the reclaim floor and that maintenance reclaimed work_items_bm25. Decision D-010.\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/bm25-write-load.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Maintenance runs as a DBOS workflow.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"Index maintenance runs through the platform scheduler, not raw timers.\", \"rationale\": \"Repo rule: recurring durable work is a DBOS scheduled workflow.\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"The DBOS scheduled maintenance workflow body compacts a BM25 index that bm25_needs_compaction reports as eligible, and rebuilds an index whose file exceeds the D-010 bloat ratio over its live data with REINDEX CONCURRENTLY, at most one per run.\", \"falsifier\": \"BROKEN if (1) an eligible index stays uncompacted after the workflow runs; (2) an index over the reclaim floor and bloat ratio is not rebuilt; (3) one run rebuilds more than one index.\", \"requiredScope\": [\"maintenance\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"integration\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"Integration test on the workflow body (runBm25Maintenance): make an index eligible and assert it is compacted within the step budget; churn two indexes past the bloat ratio and assert one run rebuilds exactly one and the next run the other. Decisions D-010, D-013 (concurrent DDL).\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/bm25-maintenance.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — One lexical seam.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"Every lexical call site ranks through one seam.\", \"rationale\": \"32 call sites hand-roll tsquery ranking today.\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"The lexical source guard test fails when ts_rank_cd is used outside the lexical seam.\", \"falsifier\": \"ts_rank_cd appears outside the seam or allowlist and the guard passes.\", \"requiredScope\": [\"call-sites\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"unit\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"Source guard test with a planted violation control. Decision D-009.\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"tests\", \"files\": [\"packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/lexical-source-guard.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Kill-switch restores legacy ranking.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"A safe cutover with a working kill-switch.\", \"rationale\": \"Cutover must be reversible while it soaks.\", \"sourceRefs\": [\"session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29\"]}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"With the BM25 flag off, lexical search returns the legacy ts_rank_cd ordering, both before and after legacy-column retirement.\", \"falsifier\": \"BROKEN if (1) flag off still ranks with BM25 or errors; (2) after retirement a legacy fragment fails with column-does-not-exist or returns a different ordering.\", \"requiredScope\": [\"feature-flag\"], \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\", \"requiredTestLayers\": [\"unit\", \"integration\"], \"passRatings\": [\"healthy\"], \"mandatory\": true, \"role\": \"outcome\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"Flag-flip test on the seam, and the retirement integration suite, which runs the legacy query fragments against the same-named virtual generated columns after retirement. The engine sits behind it, chosen in P-001. RRF fusion with the embedding leg is unchanged, and the Stage-B reranker (separate plan) consumes its output.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-003, P-005, P-007 | live |\n| R-2 | P-004, P-007 | live |\n| R-3 | P-004, P-007 | live |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002, P-003, P-009 | live |\n| R-6 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-001 | live |\n| R-12 | P-001 | live |\n| R-13 | P-005 | live |\n| R-14 | P-009 | live |\n| R-15 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-005 | live |\n\n## Approach\n\n- **Reuse first.**\n  - Benchmarking reuses the WI-10008233 harness (to be promoted into the repo as a committed bench in P-001) and the existing `memory/bench/corpus-leg-lexical-acceptance-cli.ts` and `search/bench/chunk-search-ab-cli.ts`.\n  - Packaging extends the pgvector path in `bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh`.\n  - Maintenance uses a DBOS scheduled workflow.\n  - Schema changes go through the migration allocator.\n- **Bake-off first, then commit.** The engine is chosen by P-001 and recorded as a plan Decision before any packaging or migration work.\n- **Production configuration is part of the feature, not tuning.** pg_textsearch must be in `shared_preload_libraries` (the server needs a restart to load it); without it `CREATE EXTENSION` and BM25 index scans are unavailable, so the seam must detect that and say so rather than silently fall back.\n- **The 32 lexical call sites (P-005; recheck with git grep at start):**\n  - `packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/features/search.ts`\n  - `packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/search/query.ts`\n  - under `packages/operator-core/lib/`: `adv-session-search.ts`, `agent-tools/plans/search.ts`, `agent-tools/search/{knowledge-sources,report-source,sources}.ts`, `blueprint/package-doc-resources.ts`, `code-recipes-search.ts`, `consult/relevance-router.ts`, `conventions/registry.ts`, `data-sources/{documents-corpus,granted-sources-injection}.ts`, `datatype-registry-store.ts`, `event-key-registry-store.ts`, `issues-engineer.ts`, `memory/{corpus-query-clarity,corpus-recall-io,corpus-recall}.ts`, the `memory/bench/*` benches, `personal-vault/store.ts`, `report-library.ts`, `search/{configure-search-defaults,embed-backfill,prose-min-score}.ts`, `search/bench/chunk-search-ab-cli.ts`, `sync-resolver/design-features-list-query.ts`, `work-items.ts`\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\nR-1 through R-5 as written above. Each is graded by an outside-lineage grader before ship.\n\n## Exclusions\n\n- Evoke SSR semantic mode, which needs an encoder model.\n- External search services.\n- ParadeDB pg_search, because its AGPL-3.0 licence is unsuitable for the desktop distribution.\n- TensorChord vchord_bm25: its repository was not found at the expected path on 2026-10-10.
