So preload is conditional: embedded-postgres-server preloads it only when the binary tree holds `pg_textsearch.{so,dylib,dll}` (`OPTIONAL_PRELOAD_LIBRARIES`); the dev box and staging preload it through `scripts/pg-autotune.ts`; Linux sidecars bundle it (apt `postgresql-18-pg-textsearch`); darwin and Windows do not yet (WI-6554700010008388).\n2. **Migration (P-003).** One migration defines `harness_shared.bm25_ensure_indexes()`, which, only when pg_textsearch is preloaded and available, runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_textsearch` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS <corpus>_bm25 ... USING bm25 (<text expr>) WITH (text_config=..., compaction='manual')` for every registered corpus; otherwise it raises a NOTICE and returns. The migration calls it once. The maintenance workflow (P-006) calls it again each run, so a host whose library appears later (an upgrade that starts bundling it, a dev box preloaded after the migration applied) converges without a new migration. The DDL lives only in the migration-defined function. Large dev-box tables (session_turns 1.35M rows / 18 GB, coord_thread_posts 1.1M) are pre-built with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` before the migration is armed, so `IF NOT EXISTS` makes the boot-time call a no-op there.\n3. **One corpus registry.** `packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/` holds the single list of corpora: table, BM25 index name, indexed text expression (identical to the migration's, pinned by a test), text config, and legacy tsvector column. Field weights (setweight A/B/C) are not representable in pg_textsearch; the index covers the concatenated text, which the bake-off measured.\n4. **Seam and fallback (P-005).** Call sites rank through the seam. It uses BM25 (`ORDER BY <expr> <@> to_bm25query($q, '<index>')`, explicit index name always, score = -distance) when the flag is on and the corpus index exists; otherwise the legacy `ts_rank_cd` path. Falling back is never silent: the BM25 health check (P-004) reports degraded when the flag is on and the library, extension or any expected index is missing.\n5. **Kill-switch (P-009/R-10).** A registered cutover flag, default ON, restores the legacy ordering when off.\n6. **Tests.** BM25 integration tests run against a dedicated container (pgvector/pgvector:pg18 + postgresql-18-pg-textsearch, preloaded), built from a committed Dockerfile; the shared integration container is unchanged, so existing suites keep exercising the fallback path.\n\n### D-004 — Weighted lexical+cosine fusion sites move to rank fusion (RRF), for both engines\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs the remaining P-005 call sites]\n\nThree call sites fuse a lexical score and a cosine by WEIGHTED SUM, not by rank: `findSimilarDatatypes` and `findSimilarPublishedDatatypes` (datatype-registry-store.ts) and the text+embedding branch of capability-class-registry-store.ts, all `GREATEST(ts_rank, 0.4*ts_rank + 0.6*cosine)`. The RRF observation behind P-005 (hybrid.ts fuses by position, so swapping ts_rank_cd for BM25 needs no rescaling) does not hold for these: ts_rank sits in [0,1), while a BM25 score is unbounded (about 1-30 here), so a raw swap would let the lexical leg swamp the cosine leg.\n\nRuling: these sites fuse by reciprocal rank, sum of 1/(RRF_K_DEFAULT + rank) per leg (k=60, the same `@papercusp/rrf` constant hybrid.ts uses), through one seam helper `rrfTerm(sql, matched, score)` in packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/rank.ts. Applies to BOTH engines, so flipping the kill-switch (P-009) changes which rows match and their lexical order, never the fusion arithmetic.\n\nRejected: (a) a bounded squash s/(s+K) of the BM25 score. BM25's IDF grows with log N, so any fixed K drifts as a registry grows (datatype_registry has 35 rows, code_recipes 28,692), and it would keep the legacy and BM25 paths on different arithmetic. (b) normalizing by the top lexical score in the candidate set, which lifts a weak-only lexical match to 1.0 above a strong vector neighbour.\n\nPreserved: the returned candidate population (WHERE unchanged; a vector leg counts only when cosine > 0, matching the old `score > 0` filter). `score` stays documented as a ranking weight that must never be thresholded (EI-10562); its magnitude changes. Lexical-only branches use the seam's own `leg.score`/`leg.order`.\n\n### D-005 — Memory/documents corpus bench confirms pg_textsearch over today's lexical leg (recall up, p50 latency up, p95 down)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; P-001 bench extension to the memory corpus]\n\nMeasured: /home/marsh-office/bm25-bench-runs/documents3.log and bm25-documents.json (bench packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/bm25-bakeoff-cli.ts --corpus documents, finished 2026-10-11T04:27Z, exit 0). 81,352 memory/corpus documents, query = title, body = text, 1,000 known-item queries per form, one throwaway PG 18.6 container, arms run one at a time. Evoke arms were not run (D-002 already selected pg_textsearch on the work-item corpus), so the bench prints 'D-001 not evaluated'; this run compares the chosen engine against today's leg only.\n\n| form | arm | recall@1 | recall@10 (95% CI) | MRR@10 | p50 / p95 ms |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 4 keywords | pg_textsearch 1.5.1 | 0.219 | 0.397 (0.367-0.428) | 0.279 | 9.2 / 25.0 |\n| 4 keywords | tsv_and (today) | 0.185 | 0.297 (0.269-0.326) | 0.223 | 1.5 / 39.7 |\n| full title | pg_textsearch 1.5.1 | 0.311 | 0.486 (0.455-0.517) | 0.367 | 10.3 / 29.9 |\n| full title | tsv_and (today) | 0.197 | 0.282 (0.255-0.311) | 0.228 | 1.4 / 26.8 |\n\nResult: pg_textsearch improves recall@10 on both forms with non-overlapping 95% CIs (+0.100 and +0.204), and MRR@10 on both. Cost: p50 latency rises from about 1.5 ms to 9-10 ms per query on 81k documents, while p95 falls on the 4-keyword form (39.7 to 25.0 ms) and rises slightly on full titles (26.8 to 29.9 ms). Errors 0 on every arm. D-002 stands for the memory corpus; no engine change. The p50 rise is recorded for P-004/P-010 latency budgets rather than treated as a blocker, since every value stays well under the search surfaces' 1.5 s statement timeout.\n\n### D-006 — Result lists from different corpora merge by position (fuseByPosition), never by raw lexical score\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs the remaining P-005 call sites that union several corpora]\n\nSome call sites rank each corpus separately and then sort the UNION by the raw score (search:query sorts tasks, goals, projects and audit hits by `score`). After P-005 those per-corpus scores come from different engines and different indexes: BM25 is unbounded and each BM25 index carries its own IDF statistics, while ts_rank_cd sits in [0,1). A score-sorted union therefore hands every top slot to whichever corpus happens to use the larger scale (measured shape in the unit test: goals at BM25 scale 10-12 would take all slots ahead of a project at ts_rank 0.09).\n\nRuling: a call site that merges best-first lists from DIFFERENT corpora merges them by in-list position with reciprocal rank fusion, via `fuseByPosition` in packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/rank.ts (wraps @papercusp/rrf `rrfCombine`, k=60; keys are scoped per list so equal ids from different corpora stay distinct; equal positions keep the lists' input order). The merged `score` is the fused RRF score; the corpus's own relevance is kept separately (search:query: `kindScore`, `kindRank`) and is only comparable within its corpus. ILIKE fallback rows take their returned position like any other row. This is the cross-corpus companion of D-004 (D-004: lexical+cosine legs over ONE corpus fuse with `rrfTerm` in SQL; D-006: separate corpora fuse with `fuseByPosition` in JS).\n\nApplied first to packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/search/query.ts (search:query), which also reports per-kind `engines` (bm25 | fts | ilike | unavailable) so a fallback is visible in the response. Tests: packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/rank.test.ts, packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/search/query.test.ts, packages/agent-mcp/src/tools/search/query.integration.test.ts.\n\n### D-007 — Under BM25, websearch query syntax keeps filtering; fixed relevance floors stay on ts_rank_cd; per-question lexical scores are relative to the best hit\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs P-005 call sites whose legacy query is websearch_to_tsquery, and any consumer that compares a lexical score to a fixed number]\n\n1. **Operator syntax.** pg_textsearch tokenizes the query and ignores websearch syntax, so under BM25 `report -draft` would rank reports CONTAINING 'draft' first, and a quoted phrase or OR would be ignored. A caller whose legacy match uses `websearch_to_tsquery` and documents that syntax passes `querySyntax: 'websearch'` to `lexicalLeg` (search/lexical/rank.ts). When the query actually uses an operator (a double quote, a term starting with `-`, or the word `or` between terms; `usesWebsearchOperators`), the BM25 leg's match becomes `bm25 match AND legacy websearch predicate`: the syntax filters exactly as before and BM25 only orders. A plain query keeps BM25's any-term match. Applied to: report-library.ts searchReports (reports:search documents phrases/OR/-negation), data-sources/documents-corpus.ts searchOrganizationDocuments + searchPotDocuments. Tested on real pg_textsearch in search/lexical/bm25.integration.test.ts ('websearch operator syntax under BM25').\n\n2. **Fixed floors.** A BM25 score is unbounded and corpus-relative (its IDF changes with the corpus), so it cannot be compared to a fixed constant. GRANTED_SOURCES_RELEVANCE_FLOOR (0.05) was calibrated on ts_rank_cd; the documents searches now return `tsRank` (ts_rank_cd against the websearch query, computed under either engine, 0 when the row does not match all of it) and the floor compares `tsRank`, while BM25 orders. Prompt-driven injection is a precision surface; BM25's any-term recall is not wanted there.\n\n3. **Per-question scores shown as [0,1].** Where a lexical score is reported or clamped as a [0,1] value (consult/relevance-router.ts embed-free lexical fallback, which used clamp01(ts_rank_cd)), the score becomes the row's score divided by the best row's score for the same question (`relativeLexicalRanks`). Clamping a BM25 score would read 1 for nearly every owner and hand the order to the owner-id tie-break.\n\nRejected: a BM25-calibrated absolute floor (no calibration data; would drift with corpus size); ignoring operator syntax under BM25 (silently inverts negation for reports:search, which documents it).\n\n### D-008 — Correction to D-003 §1: the dev box is NOT preloaded today; P-004 owns adding pg_textsearch to pg-autotune\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; corrects my own D-003 text]\n\nD-003 §1 says the dev box and staging preload pg_textsearch through `scripts/pg-autotune.ts`. That is wrong as of 2026-10-11 06:05Z. Measured on the dev box's native PG 18.4 (`sudo -n -u postgres psql -d papercusp`): `shared_preload_libraries = pg_stat_statements`, no `pg_textsearch` row in `pg_extension`, and no index with access method `bm25`. The package `postgresql-18-pg-textsearch 1.5.1-1.pgdg24.04+1` IS installed (`/usr/lib/postgresql/18/lib/pg_textsearch.so`, available extension version 1.5.1). `scripts/pg-autotune.ts` builds its preload list as the live value plus `pg_stat_statements` and never adds `pg_textsearch`.\n\nConsequence: lexical search on the dev box (and on staging, which shares that cluster) runs entirely on the legacy ts_rank fallback, and nothing reported it, because `bm25Health` had no production caller.\n\nWhat survives: the availability gate itself (D-003 §1 for embedded PG via OPTIONAL_PRELOAD_LIBRARIES, Linux sidecar bundling) and every other part of D-003.\n\nRuling: P-004 adds `pg_textsearch` to pg-autotune's preload list when the library file exists, sizes `pg_textsearch.memory_limit` (default 2 GiB, sighup), and wires `bm25Health` into service-health as the `bm25-lexical` portless probe, which reports DOWN in exactly this state. Activating the preload needs a postmaster restart of the shared cluster; that restart is a separate, announced step, not a side effect of a code change.\n\n### D-009 — Two Approach-list sites stay on ts_rank: plan-decision elements (conventions) and pack-doc parts\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; scopes P-005's 'all 32 call sites']\n\nP-005 moves every lexical ranking site onto lexicalLeg. Two sites on the Approach list cannot use a BM25 index, so they keep their ts_rank ranking. They do not call the seam.\n\n1. conventions/registry.ts relevantPlanDecisions. It ranks single plan DECISIONS, which are elements of the harness_plans.decisions jsonb array, not rows of any table. A pg_textsearch index ranks the rows of one table expression. The nearest corpus, harness_plans_bm25, indexes whole plans, so it would rank plans, not decisions. harness_decisions is a different thing, a verb/args decision log, and does not hold plan decisions. Measured 2026-10-11: 13,698 decision elements across non-archived plans (all workspaces), each scored with an on-the-fly to_tsvector per call. Putting decisions under BM25 needs a normalized decisions table first. That is follow-up WI-6554700010008456; it is not part of this plan.\n\n2. blueprint/package-doc-resources.ts searchWearerPackageDocs. It searches harness_doc_parts. Measured 2026-10-11: 325 rows and one doc (claude-md), and the query narrows further to the parts addressed to the wearer's applied pack keys. BM25's gain comes from corpus-wide IDF and length normalization, and over at most 325 rows (in practice a handful) it changes nothing measurable. An index and a migration for that corpus cost more than they return. The site keeps ts_rank_cd with OR-ed lexemes.\n\nThe other Approach-list files are on the seam, or never ranked (fixed floors per D-007, registry, docs-only mentions, the plans TF scorer). WI-6554700010008382's completion lists each file in its coverage.\n\n### D-010 — Maintenance gains a RECLAIM step: one bloat-triggered REINDEX CONCURRENTLY per run, because compaction never shrinks a pg_textsearch index file\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; changes the P-006 maintenance contract so R-7 can hold]\n\n**Measured** (pg_textsearch 1.5.1, PG 18.6 test container, scratch db, index created with compaction='manual', 2026-10-11 07:2xZ): with distinct-token rows the memtable spills about every 3,000 rows (memtable_pages_threshold=64). 20,000 inserts gave 7 level-0 segments and a 7.0 MB file. One bm25_compact_step merged them into one L1 segment, and the file GREW to 9.55 MB: the merged segment (+2.55 MB) equals the fresh-rebuild size (REINDEX gave 2.55 MB), but the 7 old L0 segments' pages are recycled, never returned. After an update/delete churn, VACUUM and a second compaction the file was 11.36 MB against a 2.55 MB REINDEX: 4.5x, so R-7 (every index at most 1.5x its fresh rebuild after the write-load run) FAILS on compaction alone. bm25_summarize_index reports per-segment pages and alive/dead docs (example: 740 segment pages, 26,143 alive of 31,372 docs, 1,034 on-disk pages), and REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY works on a bm25 index (2.76 MB, one segment).\n\n**Ruling.** runBm25Maintenance gets a fourth step, RECLAIM, after COMPACT. For each live index that no longer needs compaction and is at least reclaimMinBytes on disk (default 8 MiB: below that the absolute waste is under ~4 MB and a rebuild is not worth its churn), estimate live bytes as segment pages x 8192 x alive/docs from bm25_summarize_index. When on-disk exceeds maxBloatRatio (default 1.4) times that estimate, rebuild it with REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY on a reserved connection, at most ONE per run and never in a run that already built an index (the same one-concurrent-DDL-per-run rule as BUILD), under a session advisory lock so overlapping ticks cannot run two. A leftover INVALID <name>_ccnew from a rebuild that died is dropped first. An unparsable summary on an index above the floor is reported in errors (a pg_textsearch output change must be noticed, not silently skipped). The threshold 1.4 sits under R-7's 1.5 so a reclaimed index lands near 1.0x. The R-7 test (bm25-write-load.integration.test.ts) runs the real maintenance body during and after the load and then compares every BM25 index against its REINDEX size; it also asserts the load pushed the index over the floor so the reclaim path is exercised, not skipped.\n\n### D-011 — Legacy-column retirement keeps the kill-switch working: each dropped tsvector column is replaced by a same-named SQL function over the row type\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs P-009's retirement step, R-10 and R-14]\n\n**Problem.** R-14 drops each corpus's legacy tsvector column (`_search`, `text_tsv`, `body_tsv`, `note_tsv`, `title_tsv`, `content_tsv`, `search_tsv`; one per corpus in `corpora.ts` `legacyTsvColumn`) and its GIN index. R-10 says the kill-switch (flag off) restores the legacy `ts_rank_cd` ordering, and the legacy fragments every call site passes to `lexicalLeg` read those columns (`ts_rank_cd(w._search, q)`, `w._search @@ q`). Extension-less hosts (darwin/Windows desktops, WI-6554700010008388) rank only through that path. A plain drop would make the kill-switch and the fallback raise `column does not exist`.\n\n**Measured (dev box, 2026-10-11 ~08:05Z).** Legacy GIN indexes: documents 1.26 GB, session_turns 751 MB, coord_thread_posts 522 MB, work_items 140 MB, carry_notes 131 MB, harness_plans 23 MB, others under 10 MB; about 2.85 GB in total. Estimated column data (avg_width x rows) about 550 MB. 13 of 16 columns are `GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED`; harness_brainstorm.content_tsv is trigger-maintained; harness_decisions/harness_escalations body_tsv have no tsv trigger (writer to be located before the drop). Connection search_path is `harness_shared, papercusp_shared, public`.\n\n**Decision.** 1. Retirement replaces each legacy column with an IMMUTABLE `LANGUAGE sql` function in harness_shared named exactly like the column and taking the table's row type, e.g. `harness_shared._search(harness_shared.work_items) RETURNS tsvector`, whose body is the column's generation (or trigger) expression. PostgreSQL resolves `w._search` to that function once the column is gone, so every existing legacy fragment keeps working unchanged and yields the identical tsvector, which preserves R-10's ordering exactly. It is unindexed, so the kill-switch path becomes slow on the million-row corpora; that is acceptable for an emergency switch, not for normal serving.\n2. The functions are created unconditionally (a real column wins over the function where one is retained). The column drop (which drops its GIN index with it) is availability-gated per host and per corpus: only when `pg_textsearch` is installed and that corpus's BM25 index exists and is valid. Extension-less hosts keep their columns and indexed legacy ranking.\n3. The drop runs in a migration-defined SQL function `bm25_retire_legacy_columns()`, called once by the migration and on every P-006 maintenance run, so a host whose BM25 index becomes valid later (fresh installs, a rebuild) retires then. Each table's drop uses a short lock_timeout and skips that table on timeout, so the migration and maintenance never block on a busy table and never fail boot.\n4. Storage accounting: the function returns per-table freed index bytes and the column's estimated bytes. Dropping a column frees its GIN file at once; the heap bytes are reclaimed only as rows are rewritten, and the accounting says so.\n5. The migration is armed only after the soak (D-012) on the dev box. A fresh install has nothing to soak and retires at first maintenance after its BM25 indexes exist.\n\n**Rejected.** (a) Rewriting the legacy fragments at the seam into on-the-fly `to_tsvector(...)` expressions: every call site's tsquery form (plainto, websearch, prefix) and field weights would have to be re-derived, risking a changed legacy ordering. (b) Removing the kill-switch at retirement: the plan keeps it (P-009, R-10), and extension-less hosts still need the legacy path. (c) An unconditional static drop: it would strip indexed ranking from extension-less desktops and, on the dev box today, from corpora whose BM25 index is not built yet.\n\n### D-012 — Supersedes D-011's mechanism: retirement swaps each stored legacy tsvector column for a same-named VIRTUAL generated column (PG 18), not a same-named function\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs P-009's retirement step, R-10 and R-14; replaces D-011 §1 and corrects its measurement paragraph. D-011 §2-§5 (availability gate per host and corpus, bm25_retire_legacy_columns() called by the migration and every maintenance run, short lock_timeout with skip, storage accounting, arm after soak) still hold.]\n\n**Why D-011 §1 cannot work (measured 2026-10-11 ~08:15Z, staging tree).** A same-named function over the row type is reached only through attribute notation on a qualified reference (`w._search`) or function-call syntax. A bare column name never resolves to a function. The legacy fallback branches reference the columns unqualified at about 30 sites, for example `issues-engineer.ts` `searchIssues` (`AND _search @@ websearch_to_tsquery(...)`), `work-items.ts` (`ts_rank(_search, ...)`), `personal-vault/store.ts` (`ts_rank_cd(text_tsv, ...)`), `datatype-registry-store.ts` (`title_tsv @@ ...`), and `agent-mcp/src/tools/features/search.ts` (`_search` on the view `harness_features_consolidated`). Four views also output the columns unqualified and block a DROP COLUMN through pg_depend: `engineer_issues`, `harness_features_consolidated` (which has views of its own) and `work_items_claimable` on `work_items._search`, and `personal_documents` on `documents.text_tsv`. Correction to D-011's measurement paragraph: harness_decisions and harness_escalations DO have tsv triggers (`harness_decisions_tsv_trigger`, `harness_escalations_tsv_trigger`), like harness_brainstorm.\n\n**Decision.** 1. On an eligible host and corpus, retirement drops the stored legacy column and adds a column of the same name and type defined `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (<the exact legacy expression>) VIRTUAL`. For the 13 stored generated columns the expression is read from pg_attrdef at run time. For the three trigger-maintained columns it is the trigger body's expression, and the trigger and its function are dropped. A virtual column has no heap bytes, no GIN index and no write-time computation, so the storage and write-amplification goals of R-14 are met. Every legacy fragment, qualified or not, and every view keeps resolving the same name to the identical tsvector, so R-10's flag-off ordering is unchanged. It is unindexed, so the flag-off path is slow on the million-row corpora; that is acceptable for an emergency switch.\n2. Dependent views are kept with their grants, triggers, comments and dependent views. Inside the same per-table subtransaction, each view is first redefined with CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW using a copy of its definition in which the column reference is replaced by `NULL::tsvector`. Then the column is swapped, and the view is redefined again from its ORIGINAL pg_get_viewdef text, preserving reloptions. Other sessions never see the intermediate definition. If the column still has a dependent after the first redefinition, or any step fails, the subtransaction rolls back and that table keeps its stored column, with the reason reported.\n3. Eligibility adds PostgreSQL >= 18 (`server_version_num >= 180000`; the embedded desktop PG is 18 on every platform, `EMBEDDED_PG_MAJOR:-18`). A column whose `attgenerated` is already `'v'` reports `already-retired`.\n4. R-14 reading: after retirement the table keeps a zero-storage computed column named like the legacy one. This decision is the recorded decision R-14's falsifier allows. The legacy STORED column and its GIN index are gone, and the computed column exists only so the flag-off and extension-less code paths keep working.\n\n**Measured cost of reading the virtual column** (dev box, 2,000 rows, EXPLAIN ANALYZE with a `::text` cast so the value is materialised): work_items 291 ms computed vs 229 ms to detoast and print the stored value that `SELECT *` already pays today; documents 1,235 ms vs 561 ms (500 rows); session_turns 765 ms vs 49 ms. Selecting the column is the only extra cost. The sync-resolver projections already exclude `_search` for size reasons.\n\n**Rejected.** (a) D-011's same-named function: it breaks every unqualified reference (above). (b) Qualifying all ~30 legacy fragments, then using functions: it edits many lanes' files, and future unqualified references would still break silently at retirement. (c) Dropping only the GIN indexes and keeping the stored columns: it keeps the column's heap bytes (~550 MB estimated) and its write-time computation, so it falls short of R-14.\nRelated: P-009, P-006\n\n### D-013 — The recorded soak before legacy-column retirement: one dev-box window of at least 24 h, six measured criteria; migration 1452 is armed only when it passes\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; defines the 'recorded soak' named by P-009, R-14 and D-011 §5. D-011 §5 says 'the soak (D-012)'; that number was taken by the column-swap mechanism, so this decision is the soak D-011 §5 means.]\n\n**What the soak protects.** R-10's rationale: the cutover must stay reversible while it soaks. Until migration 1452 runs, flag-off returns to INDEXED legacy ranking. After retirement the flag-off path is unindexed (D-012 §1) and slow on the large corpora. So the soak has to show that BM25 serving on real data is stable enough that a fast fallback is no longer needed.\n\n**Scope.** One window, on the dev box: the only host with real data and real traffic. Staging :3170, bg-host and :3070 share its database, so queries from any of them count. Desktops and fresh installs have no soak; maintenance retires there once each corpus's BM25 index is valid (D-011 §5).\n\n**Start.** The window opens when every corpus in corpora.ts that has a legacy column has a valid BM25 index on the dev box (pg_index.indisvalid). Measured 2026-10-11 08:45Z: three did not (work_items_bm25 invalid; session_turns_bm25 and coord_thread_posts_bm25 absent). Every maintenance build of work_items_bm25 was cancelled by the pool role's lock_timeout = 15s (harness_admin rolconfig), and the one-build-per-run fixed order kept the other two from ever being tried. Fixed in bm25-maintenance.ts (CONCURRENT_DDL_LOCK_TIMEOUT for steps 2 and 4; orderBuildCandidates puts never-attempted builds before failed ones), guarded by a new case in bm25-maintenance.integration.test.ts. One window, not one per corpus, because bm25_retire_legacy_columns gates each corpus only on index validity: once 1452 is armed it retires every valid corpus in the same run.\n\n**Pass criteria. All must hold at the end, each measured:**\n1. Duration: at least 24 h since the window opened.\n2. Valid throughout: every corpus's BM25 index is valid at every check, and no maintenance report in the window (bg-host journal, `[bm25-maintenance]` lines) names a build, rebuild or compaction error for a corpus. Any such error restarts the window.\n3. Served: BM25 statements (`<@> to_bm25query`) in pg_stat_statements gain calls during the window against a baseline snapshot taken at the start. Each corpus table appears in at least one BM25 statement by the end, or has a recorded live search through its own search tool during the window.\n4. No errors: zero error-level journal lines matching `bm25|pg_textsearch|to_bm25query` in the operator, staging and bg-host units during the window.\n5. Kill-switch untouched: flag `papercusp-bm25-lexical-ranking` stays at its default ON for the whole window. Any OFF restarts the window.\n6. Bloat: no index is left in `reclaim pending` and every file/live ratio is below 1.5 at the end (R-7).\n\n**Recording.** Start: a checkpoint on P-009's work item (WI-6554700010008386) with the open timestamp, the per-index validity rows and the pg_stat_statements baseline. End: a plan decision recording pass or fail, with the evidence for each criterion; on a fail, it names the criterion and the restarted window. On pass, 1452 is armed (`scripts/next-migration.mjs --arm`) and the schema pulled. The next boot or maintenance run retires. R-14's live evidence is the bm25_retire_legacy_columns rows plus a pg_attribute read showing every legacy column with attgenerated = 'v'.\n\n**Not a criterion: :3070 serving BM25.** :3070 runs green main, whose serving code dates from 2026-10-02 (dev:pipeline_position serving.codeAsOfMs). The release gate is held by another agent. Requiring :3070 would tie R-14 to an unrelated gate, and what the soak tests (index validity under fleet write load, maintenance, query errors) is the same whichever host sends the query.\n\n**Rejected.** (a) A 7-day window: this is alpha with no users. 24 h covers a full day of fleet writes and many maintenance runs, and retirement stays recoverable by migration (ALTER the column back to STORED and rebuild its GIN index). (b) Per-corpus windows: they would need new per-corpus clearance state inside bm25_retire_legacy_columns for a one-time event. (c) Arming now: three of the largest corpora have never served BM25 on live data, and the others only since 2026-10-09 (pg_stat_statements stats_reset).\nRelated: P-009, P-006, R-14, R-10, D-011, D-012\n\n### D-014 — Embedded Postgres must be >= 18.4: the pgdg pg_textsearch build needs palloc_mul, which embedded 18.3 lacks; installers refuse a preload library newer than the tree\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs P-002 (sidecar bundling), P-009 R-5 and the dev-tree installer]\n\n**Measured 2026-10-11 ~09:33-09:40Z.** The host package postgresql-18-pg-textsearch 1.5.1-1.pgdg24.04+1 (/usr/lib/postgresql/18/lib/pg_textsearch.so) references the symbol palloc_mul. The dev box's native PG 18.4 exports it (nm -D: T palloc_mul). The embedded npm binary @embedded-postgres/linux-x64 18.3.0-beta.17, which both the dev tree and the desktop sidecar use (libs/papercusp/packages/embedded-postgres-server: embedded-postgres ^18.3.0-beta.17), does not: with the library in lib/postgresql the postmaster refused to START (FATAL could not load library ... undefined symbol: palloc_mul). Because embedded-postgres-server preloads pg_textsearch whenever the file is present (presentPreloadLibraries), the P-002 sidecar block as committed would ship a Linux desktop whose database cannot start, not one that falls back to legacy ranking. A scratch copy of @embedded-postgres/linux-x64 18.4.0-beta.17 (npm latest; pg-symlinks.json applied) starts with shared_preload_libraries=pg_textsearch, CREATE EXTENSION gives 1.5.1, a bm25 index builds and to_bm25query ranks (row 3 -1.155 above row 1 -0.869, unrelated row excluded).\n\n**Decision.** (1) Bump embedded-postgres (and the @embedded-postgres/* platform packages in every lock that pins them) to 18.4.0-beta.17. A minor upgrade keeps the on-disk format, so existing embedded data directories open unchanged. (2) Installers must never place a preload library the tree's server cannot load: scripts/install-embedded-pgvector.mjs (now provisions pgvector + pg_textsearch) refuses pg_textsearch with status 'incompatible' unless the tree's PG minor >= the host server minor the build targets (read from dpkg's postgresql-<major> record; unknown = refuse). The sidecar bundle block gets the same gate. (3) Copies replace by rename (new inode), never in place, so a running postgres that mapped the old library cannot SIGBUS.\n\n**Rejected.** Building pg_textsearch from source against 18.3 headers: the npm tree ships no include/ and it adds a pinned source build to every release for no gain once 18.4 is used. Leaving the dev tree without pg_textsearch: then R-5's verification route (verify-tauri-headless with VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1, which boots the dev tree's embedded PG) can only ever observe legacy ranking.\n\n### D-015 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAmendment-Id: bm25-acceptance-rev2-vet-fold-apply-1\nRequest-Hash: 166cfdc6dca69f728e138f8455cf0cc7b7e357b4f1fe54319e5cfaed312c4c47\nActor: su-bc44ac7e-de9c-4270-8222-fbc9da93161b\nReason: Fold the rubric-vetting reply (consult conv-mv3psir9-0000-bc5beebfe584477e981b3d886ba0d403, thread posts 1174098 and 1174101): R-14 follows D-012 (virtual column), R-5 path and D-014, bench-measured bars name their artifacts and same-run baselines, R-8 owns the D-010 reclaim, R-10 holds after retirement, new R-16 (D-004/D-006) and R-17 (D-007), container-tested bars move to the tree plane, every method cites its Decisions. Not taken: the manual-provenance layer (not in RECORDED_TEST_LAYERS, WI-10006536); bench proof is the live operational binding.\nApproved-By: su-d9fbea4a-8677-48ae-a92e-db75e6d6535e\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1174128\nApproved-At: 2026-10-11T11:28:17.982Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 32 → 33\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-016 — BM25 sources also run a gated exact list (legacy AND + ts_rank_cd) fused with the BM25 list; this is what makes R-13 pass, and it keeps the stored tsvector + GIN that list reads\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs P-005 (lexical seam), R-13, R-2's reading, and R-14 / D-011..D-013's retirement scope. Tracked as WI-6554700010008530.]\n\n**Measured failure.** R-13 run 2 (2026-10-11 12:05Z, :5432, pg_textsearch 1.5.1, sample ffe5c12af735; docs/evidence/bm25-hybrid-recall-2026-10-11.{json,md}): fused recall@10 work_item legacy 59/60 vs BM25 54/60, session_turn 49/60 vs 48/60 -> fail. Every work_item loss was a fragment-style query (keyword style 30/30 both arms). On the five losses, legacy (plainto_tsquery AND + ts_rank_cd cover density) ranked the target 1,1,2,2,1 lexically; BM25 (to_bm25query: OR semantics, no proximity; pg_textsearch 1.5.1 has no AND/phrase/proximity operator) ranked them 11, 60, 286, 402, >500.\n\n**Retraction.** The P-005 comment in lexicalSql's BM25 branch said BM25's summed per-term IDF already ranks a document matching more query terms above one matching fewer, so the AND filter and coverage grading were unnecessary. That is false for a verbatim fragment of a long document made of common terms. The comment is corrected in place.\n\n**Rejected: BM25 top-K pool reranked by coverage + cover density.** It recovers all five losses at K=1000 (3/5 at K=300), but a pg_textsearch top-1000 scan alone costs 124-232 ms and the rerank 160-580 ms (700-1,550 ms once the tsvector is computed on the fly), far past R-2's 50 ms p95.\n\n**Chosen.** When BM25 is live, the work_item and session_turn sources of search:semantic also run an EXACT list and fuse it with the BM25 list by RRF over row identity (packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/rank.ts mergeExactAndBm25; sources.ts). The exact list is lexicalSql's AND mode, i.e. legacy's ranking exactly, and runs only when a capped GIN probe finds 0 < AND-set <= EXACT_LIST_MAX_AND_ROWS = 5000. The cap was 2,000 first; the one remaining session-turn loss had an AND set of 3,925, so it is now 5,000 (probe 21-25 ms; list 73-80 ms warm at 3,925). A non-selective query (e.g. 'the gate is red': AND set over 10,000) skips the exact list and is carried by BM25 + cosine.\n\n**Result.** Same sample, cap 5000 (docs/evidence/bm25-hybrid-recall-2026-10-11-exact-list.{json,md}): work_item 59/60 vs legacy 59/60, session_turn 50/60 vs 50/60 -> R-13 pass; no BM25-only or legacy-only pairs. MRR@10 is slightly lower than legacy (0.860 vs 0.905; 0.783 vs 0.790). The BM25 arm's end-to-end latency rises from p50 43/89 ms, p95 71/248 ms to p50 67/127 ms, p95 152/324 ms (work_item/session_turn), still well below legacy's p95 675/3,227 ms in the same run. R-2 measures the BM25 index query itself, which is unchanged; the exact list is added cost on top of it, disclosed here.\n\n**Consequence for retirement (R-14, D-011..D-013).** The exact list reads the stored tsvector and its GIN index (work_items._search, session_turns.text_tsv). So retirement must keep both columns and their GIN indexes for these two corpora. It may retire them only for corpora whose sources run no exact list. The R-14 rubric bar and migration 1452 must be amended to that scope before 1452 is armed.\n\n**Guards.** rank.test.ts (merge semantics, cap admits the measured losses); bm25-hybrid-fusion.integration.test.ts (container: BM25 alone drops a long document's verbatim fragment from the top 10, the merged list ranks it first); the live R-13 instrument search/bench/bm25-hybrid-recall-cli.ts.\n\n**Not covered.** Other BM25 call sites (plainLexicalLeg sources, work-items.ts, documents-corpus, memory) still rank BM25-only and likely have the same fragment weakness; R-13 measures only search:semantic's work_item and session_turn. Follow-up to be filed and owned.\n\n### D-017 — R-13 is measured on search:semantic's work_item and session_turn sources, not the memory store: the memory store's lexical leg is not BM25, so a memory-store A/B cannot detect anything this plan changes\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; governs R-13 and corrects one line of D-016. Source requirement: R-13 intent 'Keep the existing hybrid fusion; this replaces only the lexical leg' (session_turn:claude:436a5bee-104f-44d5-8a39-eb2f680c74d0:29); rationale 'Fusion quality must not regress.']\n\n**Measured.** The R-13 acceptance condition (seeded by me) names 'a known-item recall sample of the live memory store', and its method names packages/operator-core/lib/memory/bench/ab-live-recall-cli.ts. The memory store's hybrid backend is hybrid-pg: HybridBackend(new LexicalLegBackend(mem0), mem0) (packages/operator-core/lib/memory/configure.ts). Its lexical leg is lexicalSearchCanonical in libs/generic/memory/src/mem0-client.ts, a field-weighted token match over the canonical memory table. It never calls the lexical seam, and the memory table is not a corpus in packages/operator-core/lib/search/lexical/corpora.ts. So PAPERCUSP_FLAG_PAPERCUSP_BM25_LEXICAL_RANKING changes nothing on that path, and a flag-on/flag-off A/B there always reports equal recall. That is a vacuous pass, not a measurement. The named instrument is flag-blind for the same reason (first found 2026-10-11 ~07:51Z).\n\n**Decision.** R-13 is measured on search:semantic's hybrid surfaces whose lexical leg this plan swaps: the work_item and session_turn sources, the two largest BM25 corpora. The instrument is packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/bm25-hybrid-recall-cli.ts: both arms in one process, the same seeded known-item sample, the flag toggled per arm, an explicit DSN (WI-6554700010008528). The passing record is docs/evidence/bm25-hybrid-recall-2026-10-11-exact-list.{json,md} (D-016). The rubric's R-13 bar and method are amended to this scope.\n\n**Correction to D-016.** D-016's 'Not covered' line lists 'memory' among the BM25-only call sites. That is wrong: the memory store's lexical leg is not BM25 (above). The other BM25-only call sites stand and are tracked on WI-6554700010008535.\n\n**Not covered by R-13.** The remaining BM25 corpora that search:semantic and other callers read (plans, documents, coord posts, decisions, escalations, brainstorm and others) have no known-item sample in R-13. WI-6554700010008535 owns measuring them.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-018 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAmendment-Id: bm25-acceptance-rev3-d016-d017-apply-1\nRequest-Hash: 86b0bf5a97109f9da75f23376509fce7a190ea0dbac8172335219c93d472b9f6\nActor: su-bc44ac7e-de9c-4270-8222-fbc9da93161b\nReason: R-13 follows D-017 (measured on search:semantic work_item + session_turn with bench/bm25-hybrid-recall-cli.ts; the memory store's lexical leg is not BM25, so the old scope was vacuous) and D-016 (the gated exact list); R-14 follows D-016 (work_items._search and session_turns.text_tsv keep their stored column and GIN index because the exact list reads them; migration 1452 amended to that scope).\nApproved-By: su-5719d833-1693-49b1-b049-977a7462a53c\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1174248\nApproved-At: 2026-10-11T13:04:58.545Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 35 → 36\nChanged BARs: R-13, R-14\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-019 — The D-016 exact-list path gets its own latency bar (R-18): end-to-end search:semantic p95 with BM25 live may not exceed the legacy arm's p95 in the same run; R-2's 50 ms stays the engine-query budget\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; closes rubric rev-4 vetting gap G1 (consult conv-mv3u93f8-0000-ccabe84c061d422185cb490fbd11507a, post 1174258, vetter su-4662693e). Governs new bar R-18 and the R-2 method scope sentence added in rubric rev 4.]\n\n**Gap.** D-016 added a second query (capped GIN probe + plainto_tsquery AND + ts_rank_cd exact list, fused with the BM25 list) to the work_item and session_turn sources of search:semantic. R-2 (p95 <= 50 ms) is measured by bm25-bakeoff, which times only the engine's BM25 SQL in a container, so after rubric rev 4 nothing bounded the latency of the user-facing path that now includes the exact list.\n\n**Measured (2026-10-11, this session).** packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/bm25-hybrid-recall-cli.ts times the whole runHybridSearch call per pair (vector leg, lexical leg incl. the exact list, RRF fusion), both arms in one process, alternating which runs first. On sample ffe5c12af735 (docs/evidence/bm25-hybrid-recall-2026-10-11-exact-list.json, :5432, pg_textsearch 1.5.1): work_item p95 BM25 arm 151.6 ms vs legacy 675.2 ms; session_turn 324.1 ms vs 3226.7 ms. The legacy path itself is far above 50 ms on this measure, so 50 ms is not a meaningful end-to-end budget: it was set for the engine query, where the plan swaps engines.\n\n**Ruling.** (1) R-2 keeps its 50 ms engine-query bar unchanged. (2) New bar R-18: on the search:semantic work_item and session_turn sources, the BM25 arm's end-to-end p95 (BM25 list + gated exact list + fusion, measured by bm25-hybrid-recall-cli.ts) is at most the legacy arm's p95 measured in the same run on the same pairs, per source. It fails if the exact list (or anything else on the BM25-live path) makes user-facing search slower than before the plan. (3) The judgment is code, not prose: judgeLatency / overallLatencyVerdict in packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/bm25-hybrid-recall.ts, written into the artifact as latencyVerdict, unit-tested in bm25-hybrid-recall.test.ts.\n\n**Rejected.** The vetter's literal marker (end-to-end p95 including the exact list <= 50 ms): it would hold the whole hybrid path (vector leg included) to the engine-only budget and fail on the legacy baseline too, so it would measure the vector leg, not this plan's change.\n\n**Not covered.** An absolute end-to-end budget for search:semantic is outside this plan (the vector leg dominates and is not changed here).\n\n### D-020 — R-18 also carries absolute per-source p95 ceilings (work_item 200 ms, session_turn 400 ms) on top of D-019's relative-to-legacy bound\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self, AUTO under owner directive #1661; amends D-019. Source: rubric rev-4 vetting reviewer 2, consult conv-mv3u93f8-0000-ccabe84c061d422185cb490fbd11507a post 1174260 (su-aa54b9ea).]\n\n**Gap in D-019.** D-019's R-18 passes when the BM25 arm's end-to-end p95 is at or below the legacy arm's p95 in the same run. Legacy's own p95 on search:semantic was 675 / 3,227 ms (work_item / session_turn, D-016's run), so a BM25 path running at 2-3 s would still pass. A bar that cannot fail at a latency users would notice does not bound the user-facing path.\n\n**Ruling.** R-18 fails a source when EITHER (1) the BM25 arm's p95 exceeds the legacy arm's p95 in the same run (D-019), OR (2) it exceeds that source's absolute ceiling: work_item 200 ms, session_turn 400 ms. The ceilings are D-016's measured BM25-arm p95 after the exact list (152 / 324 ms) with about 30% headroom. Rejected: the 50 ms end-to-end marker reviewer 1 proposed (post 1174258), because the CLI times the whole runHybridSearch call (vector leg + lexical leg + fusion) and D-016's own evidence would rate it broken on arrival; R-2 keeps 50 ms as the ENGINE-query budget only.\n\n**Implementation.** packages/operator-core/lib/search/bench/bm25-hybrid-recall.ts: LATENCY_P95_CEILING_MS + judgeLatency(arms, ceilingMs); summarizeSource passes the source's ceiling. A source with no ceiling is judged against legacy only and its reason says so. A stale 0 empties the list through `bm25_d < 0`; a stale negative keeps non-matches. So `runBm25TopK` trusts a list only when it has >= 2 rows with differing scores (a stale value is one constant); otherwise it compares the best row with a one-row standalone `LIMIT 1` and, on disagreement, re-runs with the select-list distance, counts it (`bm25ScanScoreFallbacks`) and warns (rate-limited). A row both lists hold takes its earlier slot, and the merge stops at limit. A row at rank r in the exact list lands at merged position at most 2r, and a BM25 rank-r row at most 2r-1. The interleave has no parameter. Each row's rank is 1/(RRF_K_DEFAULT + position), so order and score agree (R-16). BM25 goes first because BM25 is the plan's ranking (R-1). The exact list's head stays within the top two. Both sources that merge (work_item, session_turn) change. P-006 (final shipment) is blocked by P-010. A green ship with the backlog still unworkable does not satisfy this plan.\n4. Unchanged safety boundaries: never take a live peer claim, never clear a real credential/destructive-action/owner pause, never treat a generic wake as condition proof, and never synthesize bug acceptance from age or score.\n\n### D-006 — Unreproduced bugs route to claimable validation work, not back to the submitter\nDate: 2026-10-10\nDate: 2026-10-10\nSource: su-6baa8 P-007 measurement (WI-10008130 comment); implements [owner:Avi 2026-10-10 #1594] amendment 3.\n\nFinding: for kind='bug', agent-review returns any bug without a current-build reproduction receipt to its submitter as revision-requested (agent-review.ts ~L1040). Of the 748 open revision-requested bugs, ~715 have a submitter that is a system sweep or an agent inactive/gone. These rows are excluded from claiming, so the state is a dead end that only renamed the 'pending' pile.\n\nRuling: a bug whose only refusal is 'no current reproduction' is VALIDATION work owned by the drain lane, not a revision owed by the submitter. P-009 makes such rows claimable as validation work under the non-P2P drain fleet's claim spec (reproduce on the current build, then accept or close as not-reproducible with evidence). Returning to the submitter remains correct only when the submitter is live AND the refusal is about the report's content rather than missing reproduction. The reproduction guard on IMPLEMENTATION is unchanged: no fix starts without an accepted receipt.\n\nApplies to: P-002 (adoption routes), P-009 (routing), P-010 (category (b) 'claimable to validate').\n\n### D-007 — Measured split of revision-requested bugs: automatic validation covers the reproduction-only class (69), not all 765\nDate: 2026-10-10\nDate: 2026-10-10\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement while implementing D-006 on WI-10008042 (dev:pg_query, open non-observation papercusp-workspace rows, agentReview.status='revision-requested', ~16:50Z). [self-imposed scoping under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover]\n\nFinding: bug=765 rows. 69 have stored review grade >3 (AGENT_REVIEW_MAX_REVISION_GRADE=3), i.e. the content grade PASSED and the only refusal was a missing/failed current-build reproduction receipt (agent-review.ts reproduction branch). 683 have grade <=3 (the content-revision branch); 13 carry no stored grade. change=727 (4 legacy-submitter). Exhaustive partition of the 684 low-grade bug round comments: 395 mention reproduction/receipt only, 152 mention reproduction AND stale/duplicate/already-fixed/non-reproducible language, 121 mention neither, 16 stale/dup only (sums to 684). A keyword mention is NOT proof the refusal was reproduction-only — low-grade reviewers name content defects too.\n\nRuling:\n1. D-006's automatic validation route covers exactly the reproduction-only class. agent-review stamps agentReview.revisionKind='reproduction' when the grade passes but the receipt is missing/failed, and 'content' on the low-grade branch. Only 'reproduction' rows are admitted by the intake-stage claim floor as validation work; the claimant may resubmit them (holder fence kept; no submitter-liveness proof needed). Backfill stamps only the grade-passed rows. Low-grade rows are NOT reclassified by regex.\n2. Content revisions whose submitter is gone are P-002's revision-ADOPTION class, not validation work by default. They need their own executable route (discover -> adopt under the existing orphan-rebind liveness proof -> revise -> resubmit); designed and recorded separately.\n3. The 13 no-grade rows are triaged individually.\n\nCorrection: the WI-10008042 checkpoint framing that D-006 'unblocks ~757 dead-ended rows' overstated its reach about 11x; the measured reach of the automatic route is 69 bug rows. P-010 must count category (b) from revisionKind, not from status alone.\nRelated: P-002, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-008 — Revision adoption is discovered and claimed through the reviewer door (adopt / adopt-next), authorized only by the existing orphan-rebind proof\nDate: 2026-10-10\nDate: 2026-10-10\nSource: su-6baa8 design for P-002 Left#2, implementing D-007 ruling 2 [self-imposed design under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover, owner directive #1594].\n\nMeasured (dev:pg_query ~17:27Z, open non-observation papercusp bugs, agentReview.status='revision-requested'): 773 rows = 424 synthetic submitter system:stranded-tool-failure-sweep (406 unheld, 18 held) + 349 agent submitters (328 unheld, 21 held). The intake-stage floor keeps every one of them off ordinary claim doors (review-in-progress leg); resubmitAgentReview's orphan branch could already ADOPT a proven orphan, but nothing let an agent FIND one, and an adopter could not hold the row while revising.\n\nRuling:\n1. Discovery + claim live on the existing reviewer door improvements:agent-review as two new modes, mirroring claim/claim-next: { mode:'adopt', id } (directed) and { mode:'adopt-next' } (oldest-first scan, bounded batch of 25). No new tool, no claim-floor leg: submitter liveness is an oracle verdict, not a SQL fact, so it cannot be a floor predicate without inventing an age proxy (the ADOPTION falsifier).\n2. Authority is EXACTLY resubmit's orphan proof, extracted into one shared helper so the two cannot drift: recover legacy synthetic reporter provenance / signed spawn alias; refuse a system: submitter with neither (not-submitter:authority-unknown); fail closed on an unmeasured liveness verdict (not-submitter:liveness-unknown); refuse REBIND_BLOCKING_SESSION_STATES (not-submitter); refuse a row held by a third party (orphan-revision-held-by-other). Age, grade and synthetic identity grant nothing.\n3. Scope: revision-requested rows whose revisionKind is not 'reproduction' (those take the D-006 validation route) and whose submitter is not LEGACY_AGENT_REVIEW_SUBMITTER (already claimable). The adopter's own revisions return alreadySubmitter.\n4. Write order: CAS-claim first (claimWorkItem with fromHolder only when the holder is the proven-gone submitter), re-read and re-verify the review snapshot (status/round/submittedBy) after the CAS — release and refuse 'state-changed' on drift — then rebind agentReview.submittedBy to the adopter and record payload.agentReviewAdoption { from, effectiveSubmitter, sessionState, round, adoptedBy, at } plus a round comment. The adopter then revises and resubmits as the submitter through the unchanged resubmit path, or closes the report if revision shows it invalid.\n5. The adoption response carries a lane brief { lane:'revision-adoption', round, previousSubmitter, next[] } so the claimant knows it holds report revision, not implementation; readiness stays not-ready until a reviewer round approves.\n\nNon-goals: no bulk adoption; no reclassification of content rows as validation work; no change to the 18+21 held rows (P-008 settles stale holds).\n\n### D-009 — Evidence-based durable-park clearer gets an agent door on work_items:hold_open (reconcile option); 65 live parks have no reachable clearer\nDate: 2026-10-10\nDate: 2026-10-10\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement on P-004 (WI-10008044) [self-imposed design under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover, owner directive #1594].\nFinding (measured ~18:35Z, harness papercusp): 108 blocked non-observation bugs carry a durable park (payload._claimHold='true'); 3 have a live taken_by, 14 have no reason, 43 have a typed claim_hold_release.trigger, 65 have none. Reasons (regex classification, not per-row verified): deploy/promotion 22, owner/human 28, lock 5, external 4, p2p 6, other 26.\n- The event resolver (reconcileEventDurableParks, called from events/await/store.ts on a fire) can only clear the 43 triggered parks.\n- The evidence-based clearer runWorkItemDurableParkReconciliation (fingerprint CAS + reasonCode + evidence + DURABLE_PARK_CLEAR_AUDIT_ACTION) is reachable ONLY via the system action work-item-durable-park-audit with payload.mode='reconcile'. No file under packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools imports it, planDurableParkClear or DURABLE_PARK_CLEAR_AUDIT_ACTION. routines:fire takes no payload. The only on-demand reconcile run on record (admission_runs 'ubp-p028-exact-software-EI-16685-20261008') appears in none of the 854 tool_invocations in its 2-minute window, so it ran outside any agent tool.\n- So for 65 live parks SPEC-BQL-P-004-CLEARER's falsifier holds: the park stays excluded with no clearer an agent can reach. The only agent path is work_items:hold_open { clear, force }, which bypasses the fingerprint/evidence contract.\nRuling (design): expose the existing reconciler through the existing clear verb instead of adding a new verb or giving routines:fire a payload. work_items:hold_open { id, clear:true, reconcile:{ reasonCode, evidence, expectedParkFingerprint?, dryRun? } } runs runWorkItemDurableParkReconciliation for that one decision with a deterministic runId (id + fingerprint) so a retry is idempotent. dryRun (or an omitted fingerprint) writes nothing and returns the planned outcome plus observedParkFingerprint, giving the two-step read-then-CAS flow. The reconciler's outcomes ('cleared', 'stale-fingerprint', 'unverified-condition', 'assigned', ...) are returned verbatim. The force path stays for leader overrides but is not the settlement route for condition-satisfied parks. Then settle the live cohort per row with evidence, starting with deploy-conditioned parks checked by content containment against the deployed sha (state:read deploy.3070.sha), never by age or parker death.\n\n### D-010 — improvement-retriage is a legacy triage submitter; 178 creator-less retriage rows stay authority-unknown\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement on P-002 (WI-10008042) [self-imposed design under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover, owner directive #1594]. Extends D-008.\n\nFinding (measured ~02:15Z, open non-observation papercusp rows, agentReview.status='revision-requested', submittedBy='improvement-retriage'): 243 rows, all ideaLifecycle triaged/gate. 65 record a creator (_ei.created_by, mostly su-* sessions); 178 record none (sourceRole Scout, ideaOrigin scout). triage-core enrolled review with submittedBy: by until 0be339d360 (2026-10-10 01:05 local) switched it to effectiveReporter(issue).id ?? by, so these are legacy enrollments of the same shape as improvement-triage/Queen. readLegacySyntheticSubmitter recognised only improvement-triage and Queen, so adopt/adopt-next refused every retriage row as liveness-unknown.\n\nRuling:\n1. 'improvement-retriage' joins the legacy triage submitters (LEGACY_TRIAGE_SUBMITTERS in agent-review.ts). The same proof applies unchanged: dated triaged/gate (or reviewed place) lifecycle, _ei.created_by equal to createdBy, agent reporter. This only selects whose liveness to measure. Adoption still needs the D-008 orphan proof (a measured, non-blocking verdict for the recovered reporter); the label itself is never measured.\n2. The 178 retriage rows with no recorded creator stay authority-unknown: there is no identity whose liveness could be measured, and inventing one would launder authority. They are not adoptable through the reviewer door. Their route is tracked as a separate residue item, not silently left.\n3. Recurrence: the enrollment writer now records the reporter, so no new rows of this shape are minted; the legacy set is closed (three labels).\n\n### D-011 — P-009 design: receipt-guard terminal criterion, claim-spec revisionAdoption:'first' pull, and stable-refusal scan convergence\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement + design on P-009 (WI-6554700010008405) [self-imposed design under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover, owner directive #1594]. Implements D-006 and D-008 for the routing half.\n\nMeasured (2026-10-11 ~04:05Z, papercusp, open non-observation rows):\n- 46 open bug rows are reproduction-validation (agentReview revision-requested + revisionKind 'reproduction'); the drain fleet nonp2p-bug-drain-luna-max-0930 DOES pull them (15 closed, 7 held, 21:31Z..02:23Z).\n- ~700 open bug rows are revision-requested on CONTENT (241 unheld agent submitters, 398 system sweep, 44 improvement-triage, 12 held, 5 other). Only 2 adoptions exist fleet-wide, both by su-6baa8 outside any fleet: adoption is NOT pulled.\n- work_items:claimable { kind:'bug' } = 560. An adoption leg that runs only on an empty lane would therefore never fire.\n- EI-25318915268790777 (reproduction-validation bug) closed 'done' with authority 'committed' by implementing a fix with no accepted receipt; its agentReview still reads revision-requested/reproduction. complete.ts has no reproduction check; the claim brief (reproductionValidationBrief) is advisory.\n\nRuling:\nA. Receipt guard = a new terminal criterion 'reproduction-receipt' in work_items/terminal-criteria.ts (reuse, not a new gate). A SUCCESSFUL close (done/resolved/passed) of item kind 'bug' whose payload is still reproduction-validation (the shared predicate agentReviewIsReproductionValidation) is rated fail and DOWNGRADES authority to 'proposed', with a warning naming the two legitimate exits: improvements:agent-review resubmit with a reproduction receipt, or close 'dropped' as not reproducible with the attempt cited. Non-success closes are not-applicable. It downgrades rather than refuses, per that module's D-003/D-015 contract: a validator who already landed a fix can no longer reproduce on the current build, so a refusal would trap a truthful close. It rides the existing TERMINAL_CRITERIA_ENFORCEMENT kill-switch and is downgrading by default (unlike durable-change).\nB. Adoption pull = new optional claim-spec field revisionAdoption: 'first' (absent = off; no other spec changes behavior). On an implementation-lane spec, getNextForBee runs adoptNextAgentReviewRevision BEFORE the ordinary claim and after the concurrency gate, scoped by the spec's view.filter (compileFilter + matchesClaimSpecFilter, the verifier-lane pattern). An adoption returns the row with the existing revisionAdoptionBrief; no adoption falls through to the ordinary claim. 'first', not fallback, because of the 560 measurement. Authorization is unchanged: only the D-008 orphan proof admits an adoption. The leader steers it via scheduler:set_claim_spec.\nC. Scan convergence: adoptNext scans the 25 oldest candidates, so STABLE refusals (liveness-unknown, authority-unknown) at the head of the queue would pin the window forever and stop all adoption once the adoptable head is consumed. A stable refusal records payload.agentReviewAdoptionProbe { reason, round, at }; the candidate SQL skips a row probed for the SAME round within 24h. Transient refusals (submitter-live, claim-refused, state-changed, held) record nothing.\nD. Rollout: after B/C reach :3170, set revisionAdoption:'first' on the drain fleet spec through its leader (coordinate, do not override), then verify P-009 by OBSERVED pulls (adoptions by fleet members, payload.agentReviewAdoption.adoptedBy in the fleet) within a measured window.\n\nApplies to: P-009.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-012 — Admission rescreen has no correction input by design; three producer gaps (claimed fail-open rows never re-reviewed, pending-row holds unnamed, cross-member release churn) owned by BQL\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement answering fleet leader su-055e916b (msg coord-send-f4ae1c30..., WI-10008207; nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08#D-128 and #D-153) [self-imposed design under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover, owner directive #1594]. No hold clearance, admission override, rescreen or claim action is taken or implied.\n\nMeasured (2026-10-11 ~06:10Z, papercusp):\n1. Screening input. runAdmissionPromoterWithRecovery passes the screener only targetItemIds and beforePersist; request note/body reach only the later dispatch (work-item-admission-recovery.ts screen then dispatch, ~L376-389). It failed open at 10:29Z; admissionReview is pending with retryAttempts 0, lastRetryAt null, reviewDueAt 2026-10-06T11:29Z. It has not been re-reviewed in 5 days.\n3. Census: 1,826 unclaimed pending/unreviewed rows vs 61 claimed unreviewed rows. The scheduled promoter window (readPromoterItems with demoteGuardBlocked) sorts rows with taken_by set LAST. EI-25220422162112859 has been claimed continuously since 2026-10-06 (su-f5fc3980, then su-3067d). [inferred mechanism from the ORDER BY plus census; per-tick selection not observed]\n4. EI-25396682599838692 (promoted spill-write-failed tool-failure row, admission unreviewed, retryAttempts 1): 31 worked_by entries since 2026-10-08, about 16 distinct members between 05:12Z and 05:43Z today, each releasing 1-7 min after finding no new correlated artifact. The scheduler release cooldown is per-bee only (fleet-scope-admission.ts ~L1742, last_released_by = self), so the next member gets it at once. events:catalog has no key for a new reporter on a tool-failure signature. D-011 C (stable-refusal convergence) covers agent-review adoption scans only and does not cover this.\n\nRuling:\nA. The existing supported rescreen door is the same-item admission recovery request (requestAdmissionRecovery: one item, one durable request, no override, no screening bypass). A correction enters screening only through durable row state; for EI-25220422162112859 the relevant state (comparison dropped) is already present. A same-item retry screens current state but is NOT evidence that retraction prose was considered, and note/body are not a correction channel (agrees with nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08#D-153). No new correction-input field: screening from durable rows is the design. A correction that must reach screening belongs in the row it corrects, not in a dispatch note.\nB. Fix: persist the hold reason and runId on the item for pending rows too.\nD. Gap 3, scheduler (accountable lane: BQL, su-6baa8, separate work-item): cross-member reselect churn. Today's legitimate member exits are work_items:hold_open with a typed trigger (D-009) when an awaitable event exists, or a close as not reproducible with the attempt cited (D-006, D-011 A). A promoted tool-failure row waiting on \"a new correlated artifact\" has no typed trigger to park on. Fix: item-level damping when distinct members release with no new evidence, plus a typed event for a new reporter on the same signature.\nE. Until B-D land: the D-128 screening hold on EI-25220422162112859 stands; do not rescreen it to attach prose. The leader's hold decisions are unchanged. Members on EI-25396682599838692 keep their existing exits; this decision makes no validity claim about that bug.\n\nApplies to: answer to nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08#D-153 producer-contract question.\n\n### D-013 — P-005 cohort exceptions: every reopen-recommended row of the fixed 2143 gets an owner and a disposition; 10 were instrument false positives (WI-6554700010008454)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement on P-005 (WI-10008045) [self-imposed design under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover, owner directive #1594].\n\nMeasured: fresh census of the fixed 2143 cohort on :3170 03397e3b25 at 2026-10-11T06:13Z (.papercusp/scratch/6baa8-p005-census/census-summary.json; 04:56Z run kept in prev-0456/). 2143/2143 accounted for; terminal 225, parked 876, unclaimed 892, in-flight 150; reopenRecommended 39 (was 41).\n\nRulings, by class:\n1. Placement belongs to the D-135 fleet leader (su-055e916b) or the parent holder by self-assignment.\n\nNo claim is made that any contributor is fixed or shipped.\n\n### D-018 — Correction to D-012 gap 1: overdue claimed fail-open rows need a judged path, not just an earlier turn\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 code read for WI-6554700010008443 [self-imposed under D-005; owner directive #1594]. Corrects the fix shape stated in D-012 gap 1; D-012's measurements stand.\n\nD-012 said an overdue claimed fail-open row should get a guaranteed turn ahead of the demote key. That alone does nothing. In packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-admission-promoter.ts (HEAD 08b335177f), the scheduled-window reader puts every row where endpointProtection(snapshot, 'promote') is non-null into selfBlockedIds and skips its pair read. endpointProtection returns 'claimed' for any assignee. A claimed row at the head of the window is still never judged, and its retryAttempts/lastRetryAt never advance.\n\nRuling: WI-6554700010008443 part 1 is redesigned as follows. A claimed row with admissionReview.state='pending' past reviewDueAt is judged instead of self-blocked. A distinct verdict promotes it: the 'claimed' guard is exempted for the 'promote' role only, because changing admission does not move held work. A duplicate verdict holds it with a persisted reason and never merges it, so the 'loser' protection for claimed rows stays. Either outcome advances lastRetryAt/retryAttempts. Part 2 (persisted hold reasons on pending rows) is unchanged. Detail: WI-6554700010008443 comment 1173793.\n\n### D-019 — Clarifies D-018: the claimed re-review exemption covers promote, hold and reference roles; loser/canonical stay protected\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 implementation of WI-6554700010008443 [self-imposed under D-005; owner directive #1594]. Narrows how D-018 is read; D-018's intent stands.\n\nD-018 said the 'claimed' guard is exempted 'for the promote role only'. Implemented literally, its own ruling cannot persist. In packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-admission-promoter.ts the persistence guard checks a hold disposition with role 'hold' and a non-merge verdict with role 'reference', and endpointProtection refuses both as 'claimed'. So the duplicate-verdict hold D-018 requires, and the distinct-verdict adjudication that makes a promote coherent, would both be refused unwritten, and the retry watermark would never advance.\n\nRuling: an overdue claimed re-review row (admission pending/unreviewed, admissionReview.state pending, reviewDueAt passed, assignee set) is not refused as 'claimed' for roles promote, hold and reference. Each writes only admission-review state or a see-also link and never moves held work. Roles loser and canonical stay protected: any merge verdict touching such a row is rewritten to a hold before persistence (applyClaimedReReviewHolds), and because no merge is approved its merge adjudication is not persisted, so the pair is judged again after the claim ends. Every other protection (review-gated, blocked, external blocker, dependency, owner-blocked) still applies. Scheduled-window ordering: such a row whose admissionReview.lastRetryAt is null or older than 24h leads the model window for one turn.\n\n### D-020 — WI-6554700010008444 release damping: a third leg of the issue cooldown floor; 3 distinct releasers per 4h since the last new evidence\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 implementation of WI-6554700010008444 under D-012 gap 3 [self-imposed design under owner-approved plan; D-005 takeover, owner directive #1594]. Implements D-012's ruling on cross-member release churn.\n\nRuling:\n1. Placement. Damping is leg (c) of issueCooldownExclusionSql in packages/operator-core/lib/work-items.ts, not a parallel fragment. That function's own contract (WI-5939) is to extend the existing cooldown floor rather than add a parallel mechanism. It feeds every issue-family self-select, listing and diagnosis site (work-items.ts claimable listing, claimNextIssueWorkItem self-select, diagnoseClaimNextMiss; scheduler/get-next.ts diagnosis), so they cannot drift apart. Damped rows count in the existing 'cooldown' breakdown bucket. A by-id claim (claimWorkItem) never reads the fragment, matching D-015's self-select-only rule for floors.\n2. Predicate. A row is withheld from self-selection while COUNT of harness_shared.work_item_release_cooldowns rows (one per agent, so count = distinct releasers) with released_at within the window AND after payload.evidenceAdvancedAt is >= the threshold. The leg is item-level, so it applies with or without an assignee.\n3. Parameters. Threshold 3 distinct releasers (PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_DAMPING_RELEASERS); window 14400 s = 4 h (PAPERCUSP_RELEASE_DAMPING_WINDOW_SEC). 0 for either disables. Bound: absent new evidence, at most ~3 member stints per item per 4 h, versus the measured ~16 distinct members in 31 minutes on EI-25396682599838692 (D-012).\n4. Evidence epoch. payload.evidenceAdvancedAt, stamped by capture-core when a tool-failure row gains a reporter it never had, which also fires work-item:tool-failure-reporter:<id> (part B). New evidence re-admits at once.\n5. Fail-open. An absent or unparsable epoch is treated as -infinity via pg_input_is_valid (PG >= 16; embedded PG is 18.3). The window always ages releases out, so no row is permanently withheld.\n\nFalsifier: packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-issue-release-cooldown.integration.test.ts, the 'release damping' describe block (real PG): threshold boundary at 2 vs 3, evidence after/before releases, window age-out, malformed epoch, disable switch, and by-id claim. Revisit the parameters if the drain fleet's measured re-pick rate on damped rows stays above 3 per 4 h, or if a valid bug sits damped while a member holds new evidence that capture-core does not stamp.\n\n### D-021 — P-005 COHORT census on :3170 a5827f2d5b (09:57Z): 2143/2143 accounted; 30 reopen rows = 29 ruled in D-013 + EI-25432118938606124 routed to its owner\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement on P-005 (WI-10008045) [self-imposed under bug-queue-legitimacy-and-actionable-validation-2026-10-10#D-005; owner directive #1594]. Extends D-016.\n\nMeasured: the fixed-2143 cohort census on :3170 at a5827f2d5b (/api/health; contains 1767df3894 and 3919325981, i.e. WI-6554700010008443/-8444/-8464/-8465), 2026-10-11T09:57:15Z. File: .papercusp/scratch/6baa8-p005-census/census-0957-summary.json, rows in census-0957-rows.json. 2143 requested, 2143 returned, 0 unaccounted. Buckets: terminal 234, parked 905, unclaimed 855, in-flight 149. EI-25432118938606124 joined it: closed done at 07:32:19Z by su-8aa83a0b with completionAuthority 'proposed'. Its filesChanged (launch-agent.ts, launch-agent.test.ts) are committed in 1767df3894 at 09:15:10Z (HEAD blob = tree), but it was still 'proposed' at 09:57Z. The other 29 (28 resolved/missing fold-sweep rows + WI-10007996) are the population ruled in D-013.\n\nRuling: every reopen row has an owner and a decision. The 29 per D-013. EI-25432118938606124: owner su-8aa83a0b (terminalOwner, live), sent coord-send-fe43f864 at 09:58:56Z to re-run its completion so it settles, or re-verify it if the committed blob differs from the fingerprinted one. The 1909 non-terminal rows are the live queue; their owners are their assignees or the scheduler, not exceptions.\n\nSame-moment live census check (WI-6554700010008464, closed 09:56Z): work_items:burn_down {harness:papercusp, kind:bug} on :3170 = nonTerminal 2991 / terminal 53130, equal to SQL over top-level non-observation rows at 09:55:40Z. Child rows (42 open / 618 terminal) are excluded by the shared includeChildren=false list contract.\n\n### D-022 — R-4: a park trigger that fired BEFORE the park never certifies its condition; the parked item's own generic status event never certifies (EI-25664119449929994)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement on P-005 J6 (WI-10008045) [self-imposed under D-005; owner directive #1594]. Extends D-009 and SPEC-BQL-P-004-WAKE.\n\nMeasured 2026-10-11 ~11:15Z, burn_down on :3170 b7e59a74ce (.papercusp/scratch/6baa8-p005-census/journey-oracle-burn-down.json) plus raw payload SQL: all 9 unclaimed parks labelled satisfied-still-parked cite a latch fire that PREDATES the park (e.g. EI-24937591709395249 fired 2026-10-10 17:12Z, parked 2026-10-11 06:18Z; EI-25152107634140832 dependency done 10-05, parked 10-10). Cause: buildDurableParkReleaseContract (packages/operator-core/lib/durable-park-release-contract.ts) stamped 'satisfied' from readEventConditionReachability's LIFETIME latch at park time, and the audit refresh did the same. 5 of the 9 were work-item:status:<own id>, which fires on any transition of the item, the parker's own included.\n\nRuling:\n1. A fired trigger certifies a park's condition only when the fire POSTDATES the park (claim_hold_at). At park time no fire can, so a new park is never born 'satisfied'; a pre-park fire yields reachability 'blocked' with evidence naming both times.\n2. work-item:status:<the parked item's own id> never certifies (generic any-transition key). Specific own transitions such as work-item:unblocked:<own id> keep their stamp (pinned by work-items-claim-hold.integration.test.ts).\n3. Legacy stored 'satisfied' stamps are re-classified only when the record PROVES the fire predates the park (writer evidence 'event fired at <ts>' with explicit offset vs claim_hold_at); free-text evidence keeps its stamp.\n4. The explicit agent door (work_items:hold_open reconcile, D-009) is unchanged: its dry-run 'cleared' is an agent-attested preview, not machine verification of the condition. The J6 journey asserts no-write plus outcome-enum validity and discloses this, rather than demanding the door judge evidence.\n\nOwner-facing correction sent: conv-mv31xrs1 superseded by conv-mv3qlcft, withdrawing EI-25152107634140832 (its fire predated its park); WI-10002862/-2393/-3251 re-measured as post-park fires.\n\n### D-023 — Item-contract coverage repair: P-010 gets a behavioral outcome clause; P-007 and P-008 get explicit non-automated exemptions\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: su-6baa8 measurement on the plan ship path [self-imposed under D-005; owner directive #1594].
