Completed tasks, explicit owner pauses and verified blocking dependencies remain valid reasons to park.\n\n### D-001 — Owner approved the Phase 3 prevention plan; su-92de4154 builds it directly\nDate: 2026-10-10\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-10 ~16:15Z, AskUserQuestion answer in su-92de4154, directive #1583] Approved P-004..P-013 and chose route 'Me, directly' (this session, no fleet). Execution order: P-004 + P-005 first (same psu-pty-host surface, serial), then P-006..P-011, then P-012 and P-013. The draft-to-active activation audit is still owed before plans:start.\n\n### D-002 — Do NOT respawn the currently wedged agents before the durable fixes land\nDate: 2026-10-10\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-10 ~16:15Z, AskUserQuestion answer 'Wait for the fixes'] The ~116 wedged sessions (59 dead-auth/quota/403/model, 57 failed carry-respawn binding) stay parked until P-004/P-005 land; remediate them under P-012 afterwards. No ad-hoc mass respawn or wake sweep before then.\n\n### D-003 — P-005(a) recovers the successor id from the exact-child writer lock, not the newest rollout; window anchored to child spawn\nDate: 2026-10-10\n[self-imposed, su-92de4154 2026-10-10 ~18:25Z; measured] P-005(a)'s text says 'recover the successor native id from the session's codex home newest rollout'. Measured on live homes: Codex creates the rollout file LAZILY at the first turn (healthy respawns: thread-writer lock born 0.5-2s after spawn, rollout born 2-50s later, after the carry write). At binding time the newest rollout in the home is therefore the PREDECESSOR's thread, so a newest-rollout resolver would bind the wrong identity. Decision: (a) keeps the existing exact-child oracle (codexNativeIdForPty: thread-writer lock held by this PTY's native pid) as the only identity source, and the bounded retries are its polling within a window anchored to the child's SPAWN (default 120s, env PAPERCUSP_PSU_PTY_UNBOUND_CHILD_WINDOW_MS), not a fresh 600s per attempt. Window basis: lock birth after respawn on 103 confirmed carry bindings since 2026-10-07: p50 1.1s, p90 2.8s, p99 5.6s (one lock-reuse outlier). The p99 545s confirmation tail is the operator re-anchor report, so only successor-native-id-missing (never successor-reanchor-unconfirmed) triggers (b). (b) relaunches through recycleChild in carry-respawn mode, re-delivering the stashed undelivered carry, bounded (default 2, env PAPERCUSP_PSU_PTY_UNBOUND_RELAUNCH_MAX), skipped when the owner typed into the child. (c) after the budget is spent, turn/reset deliveries are refused at admission with 'successor-unbindable' (re-probing the oracle each time, so a child that later binds self-heals) instead of being ACKed into an endless pending-delivery-id loop.\n\n### D-004 — P-006 turn-start proof is a separate ledger dimension resolved from real-time signals only; window 600s\nDate: 2026-10-10\n[self-imposed, su-92de4154 2026-10-10 ~19:35Z; measured] Verified the peer claim: wake-executor.ts degradeToInboxOrDrop returns {kind:'delivered', channel:'inbox'}; inbox, pty-inject, resume*, cold-fresh-successor and unconfirmed psu injects are all booked status='delivered' with no turn proof. Measured 24h: inbox 21,970 delivered / 13,131 with no tool_use within 10m; psu-socket-inject 1,119 / 259; resume-headless 1,943 / 222; resume-rehome-backend 6 / 6.\n\nDesign:\n(1) status='delivered' keeps its meaning (handed to a channel / persisted). A NEW column turn_proof carries the turn: host-attested (psu host replied 'delivered' under requireNativeTurnStart, i.e. its native-turn-start-confirmed event; or quota-recovery pickup confirmed) | observed (a real-time turn signal after delivered_at) | awaiting (no proof yet, before pickup_deadline_at) | not-picked-up (deadline passed with no signal) | superseded (coalesced / suppressed-redundant: content rides another delivery). Plus turn_started_at, pickup_deadline_at, pickup_escalated_at.\n(2) Evidence sources are REAL-TIME only: tool_invocations by the subscriber after delivered_at, and the psu host's own execution.turnStartedAt / native-turn-start-confirmed event. The transcript store is excluded: measured ingestion lag p50 434s, p90 1241s, so it would mark live pickups as missed.\n(3) Window default 600s (env PAPERCUSP_WAKE_PICKUP_WINDOW_SEC). Basis: delivery-to-first-tool-use p95 is 200s (resume-headless), 834s (inbox), 1006s (psu-socket-inject); 600s covers resume p95 and psu p90 (160s).\n(4) not-picked-up emits wake:not-picked-up:<subscriberId>. Host-recovery escalation is per delivery and bounded to ONE re-queue, only when the subscriber's psu host reports a condition P-004/P-005 recover (auth/quota blocked, unbound successor). Inbox not-picked-up rows are reported, never mass re-woken (D-002); loop-level repair stays with P-007, alarms with P-011.\n(5) coord:wake/send/dispatch report pickup from this column: pickupConfirmed is true only when the queued deliveries are host-attested or observed.\n\n### D-005 — P-006 slice 3: pickup is reported by a LATER seam; the enqueue result keeps pickupConfirmed:false\nDate: 2026-10-10\n[self-imposed, su-92de4154 2026-10-10 ~20:05Z; amends D-004 (5)] D-004 (5) said coord:wake/send/dispatch set pickupConfirmed true when the queued deliveries are host-attested or observed. Verified against the code: those tools return as soon as the wake is ENQUEUED (wakeRecipients -> emitAwaitedEvent -> insertDeliveries; the pump runs afterwards via setImmediate), so at that seam no delivery can yet carry host-attested/observed. The doc-claim packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/wake-pickup-unconfirmable.ts (EI-22733985246154315) pins exactly this: pickupConfirmed is the literal false at the enqueue seam, and a real handshake must report LATER from a different seam. Decision: (1) the enqueue results keep pickupConfirmed:false; (2) they gain a pickup handle per woken target: the event key wake:not-picked-up:<target> (emitted by the slice-2 pickup sweep) and the pickup window, so a sender awaits failure instead of trusting 'queued'; (3) the later seam is the delivery read: listRecentDeliveries / events:status report turn_proof + turn_started_at per delivery. No positive 'picked-up' event is emitted: at ~20k turn-capable deliveries/day it would flood the key-fire latch; an expired window with no not-picked-up emit is the positive reading. Slice 2 (pickup sweep) is landed and tested; slice 3 follows this shape.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-006 — P-007 slice 2: silent-halt stops counting a session's own inbox watcher as a wake source; host-aware wake; fleet-leader alert; no at-disarm await\nDate: 2026-10-10\nDate: 2026-10-10\n[self-imposed, su-92de4154 2026-10-10 ~23:40Z; measured, evidence on WI-10008158 checkpoint]\n\nMEASURED. The real sweepSilentHalts({dryRun:true}) against the operator DB (control: port 5432, routine row present) checked 118 sessions, halted 3, exempted 115 — every exemption 'pending-await xN (a live wake source)' (silent-halt-reconcile.ts:228). SQL split: 51-53 AUTO claim-holding sessions with a disarmed loop hold ~87-132 work items and their ONLY pending await is their own `coord:inbox-wake:<self>` watcher, which fires only on an inbound message. Host classification of those 51 with the slice-1 reader+classifier: 44 healthy host (87 items; 22 idle >6h; 25 fleet members), 6 needs-relaunch:unbound-successor (36 items), 1 needs-relaunch:quota-blocked. silent-halt woke 29/14/2 sessions on 10-07/08/09 and none since 10-09 02:51Z.\n\nDECISION.\n(1) silent-halt-reconcile's candidate read excludes the subscriber's OWN inbox-wake await (key = inboxWakeKey(owner), COORD_INBOX_WAKE_PREFIX) from pending_awaits. Every other pending await still exempts (a named producer may legitimately be pending). The owner page text says so.\n(2) Host-aware wake leg: before the R1 wake, classify the host with readStalledLoopHost + classifyStalledLoopHost (slice 1). needs-relaunch => NO wake (a wake bounces off an unbound/walled child; keeps D-002's no-wake-sweep-of-wedged rule) and page immediately with the HOST UNHEALTHY why + remedy. healthy / recoverable-on-wake / no-host / read failure => wake as today (fail-open to current behaviour).\n(3) Fleet-leader alert: when the halted session is a fleet member and its owner page is NEWLY created (not deduped), also send to @fleet-leader:<slug> (resolved with audience.ts expandAudience, the coord:send resolver) and wake that leader. Rides the page's per-(owner, disarm-epoch) dedupe, so one alert per halt epoch.\n(4) Page cap counts only NEWLY created pages, so a standing deduped page (a still-halted session) can no longer starve new halts out of the 5-per-sweep cap.\n(5) NO bounded await armed at stalled-loops disarm. With (1), silent-halt is the bounded fallback (fires within max(30 min, 5 intervals) of the disarm). An await armed at disarm would itself count as a pending await and re-hide the session — the exact blind spot measured above.\n\nEFFECT ON DEPLOY: about 44 healthy-host parked AUTO sessions become visible at once; MAX_WAKES_PER_SWEEP=5 at the routine's cadence spreads their wakes over roughly 2-3 hours. D-002 is respected: P-004/P-005 are done, and wedged (needs-relaunch) hosts are paged, not woken; P-012 still owns their remediation.\n\nOUT OF SCOPE / follow-up: 23 AUTO sessions (~75 items) whose awaits are untimed bound event awaits (work-item:done/unblocked, conversation:answered) remain exempt; whether those producers progress needs its own measurement. P-007's 'pending duplicate deliveries' host input is slice 3.\nRelated: P-007, P-012\n\n### D-007 — P-007 slice 3: precise unbound-successor judge + pending-turn-stuck host condition, one shared tail judge for P-006 and P-007\nDate: 2026-10-10\nDate: 2026-10-10 [self-imposed, su-92de4154 2026-10-10 ~23:50Z; measured, evidence on WI-10008158 checkpoint]\n\nMEASURED (read-only probes over all ~262 live psu hosts, 6h window):\n(1) duplicate-delivery-id alone is routine host dedupe: 86/222 healthy hosts emit it. Not a wedge signal by itself.\n(2) The slice-1 unbound-successor judge OVER-REPORTS. It took the newest binding event KIND (respawn-binding-unconfirmed | respawn-carry-dropped) from the per-owner tail, ignoring reason, host generation, and later turns. Of 33 hosts it called unbound, only 6 carry reason successor-native-id-missing (the only reason the host itself treats as unbindable, psu-pty-host.mjs isUnbindableChild / retry predicate); 12 are 'superseded', 10 'successor-reanchor-unconfirmed', the rest mixed; 10 delivered a turn after the event; 4 events predate the current host process. 8 of 11 hosts the precise rule reclassifies made tool calls after the event, and 5 'superseded'/carry-dropped hosts run 95-245 tool calls/hour. Since slice 2 pages (not wakes) needs-relaunch sessions, the over-report would leave healthy sessions unwoken. The same judge drives the P-006 pickup sweep (hostRecoverableCondition), so both inherit it.\n(3) Pending duplicate deliveries ARE a real wedge signal when they persist: hosts holding >=2 deliveries as state:'pending' with the oldest >=30m and no turn-delivered since = 6 hosts; 5 already caught (incl. the 2 true P-005 wedges with ~180 pending re-sends over 70m), 1 classified healthy (no turn in 13h).\n(4) No host has ever emitted successor-unbindable-refused: the host's duplicate-delivery-id short-circuit runs BEFORE the P-005(c) refusal, so a delivery ACKed before the child became unbindable re-polls as pending-delivery-id forever.\n\nDECISION:\n(a) One shared pure tail judge in turn-proof.ts, used by BOTH readPickupHostView (P-006) and classifyStalledLoopHost (P-007); the two duplicated latest-binding scans go away. PickupHostView carries the verdicts (unboundSuccessor, stuckPending), not a raw event kind.\n(b) unbound-successor := within the CURRENT host process (event ts >= host startedAt), the newest of {respawn-binding-unconfirmed, respawn-binding-confirmed, respawn-carry-delivered, successor-unbindable-refused, turn-delivered} is successor-unbindable-refused, or respawn-binding-unconfirmed with reason successor-native-id-missing. respawn-carry-dropped and other unconfirmed reasons no longer imply unbound.\n(c) New PickupRecoverable 'pending-turn-stuck' := within the current host process, >=2 duplicate-delivery-id state:'pending' events, the oldest older than the pickup window (D-004, 600s default), no turn-delivered after it, and the host not visibly mid-turn (execution phase running with progress inside the window). Ordered after auth/quota/unbound. Never wake-recoverable: classifyStalledLoopHost -> needs-relaunch (remedy: identity-preserving relaunch, P-012); the pickup sweep reports it without the one re-queue, since a re-queued wake is ACKed into the same stalled pipeline.\n(d) (4) is recorded as a P-005(c) residue, not fixed here: the host-side ordering fix (refuse before the duplicate short-circuit, or expire pending ids of an unbindable child) is psu-pty-host work, filed separately.\n\n### D-008 — One wake-source predicate for silent-halt and P-009; dead work-item awaits never count (measured: none is a sole source today)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self-imposed, su-92de4154 2026-10-11 ~00:40Z; measured, WI-10008290]\n\nMEASURED (read-only): the real sweepSilentHalts({dryRun:true}) against the operator DB (control line: port 5432, routine row present) checked 131 sessions, halted 39, exempted 68 for 'pending-await'. Probe: .papercusp/scratch/p007e-untimed-awaits.mts, outputs p007e-untimed-awaits{,2,3}.out. Each exempt owner was classified by its STRONGEST open await, ignoring the own coord:inbox-wake watcher (D-006):\n- timed await (expires_ts set): 18 owners, 28 claims\n- untimed work-item:claimable watch: 27 owners, 13 claims\n- untimed conversation:answered: 9 owners, 28 claims\n- untimed system events (fleet:*, plan:acceptance, goal:*, composed-root:*, release:*, escalation:*): 10 owners, 13 claims\n- untimed work-item:unblocked on an item the owner itself holds as blocked: 3 owners, 24 claims\n- ONLY dead work-item awaits: 0 owners.\nDead work-item awaits do exist but are never the sole source today: 11 awaits on work-item:done:<an item the subscriber itself holds> (self-deadlock, 5 owners), and 17 untimed awaits on items no one holds (done:open 7, unblocked:open 4, unblocked:blocked 3, done:blocked 3).\n\nDECISION. (1) There is ONE wake-source predicate, shared by silent-halt (evaluateSilentHalt's pendingAwaits) and P-009's loop:end guard. It is not re-derived per caller. It does NOT count: the session's own inbox watcher (D-006); a done-await on an item the subscriber holds; an await on a terminal or missing target. Today this flips 0 sessions; it prevents a false exemption by construction. (2) OPEN for P-009, deliberately not ruled here: whether an UNTIMED claimable/conversation/system-event await counts as a sole wake source for a claim-holding AUTO session. That is the unverified mass (46 owners, 54 claims). If P-009 requires a timed await there, its refusal's recovery template (a bounded events:await) already supplies one.\n\n### D-009 — P-009 rules D-008 (2): a claim-holding autonomous session needs a GUARANTEED wake source to end its loop; silent-halt keeps counting untimed live awaits\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed, su-92de4154 2026-10-11 ~01:10Z; measured]\n\nMEASURED (read-only, 2026-10-11 ~00:50Z, open non-inbox awaits by family): work-item:claimable is an id-less backlog-interest watch (114 awaits / 110 owners, filtered by kind/plan; the last batch of fires was ~11:09Z, ~13h earlier) -- it says 'I am idle, wake me for new work', not 'wake me for the work I hold'. conversation:answered rows are auto-armed when a question is asked (bound_to conversation-question, 71 awaits / 55 owners); the sampled keys had 0 fires in 24h.\n\nDECISION.\n(1) loop:end, for an owner in an autonomy-implying mode that still holds non-terminal work-items: the stop proceeds only when a GUARANTEED wake source survives -- a deliberate park that is a wake source under the D-008 (1) predicate AND bounded with wake-on-timeout (awaitGuaranteesRewake, the same rule as the turn-end halt tripwire), or a pending deliberate wake delivery. Untimed claimable / conversation / system-event watches do NOT count: they make no promise to fire, and 'untimed watch + held claim + no loop' is the strand shape this plan measured. acknowledgeWakeLessAutonomy does NOT override this refusal. Exits: the goal is achieved (disposition 'achieved', through the acceptance gate), the claims are released, a verified owner stop directive (new arg ownerStopDirectiveId: exists, same workspace, belongs to the loop owner, hook-captured), or a typed fleet wind-down cue. The refusal's recovery is a bounded events:await keyed to the blocker a held item states (typed event blocker ref with its recheckAt as the bound, else work-item:unblocked:<id> for a blocked item; never work-item:done:<held id>), or the checkpoint+release path when no item states a blocker.\n(2) silent-halt keeps counting untimed LIVE awaits as exemptions (policy any-live). It is a retroactive detector; making it stricter would page the unverified 46-owner mass at once, and that is P-011's call with its own measurement. The two callers share the D-008 (1) predicate for what is DEAD and differ only in this one strictness.\nCode: packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-source-predicate.ts (shared), packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/loop/end.ts (guard). Tracked on WI-10008160.\n\n### D-010 — P-010: a hold parked on a typed external blocker stops counting against maxConcurrentClaims (narrows EI-11796)\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self-imposed, su-92de4154 ~02:30Z; measured]\n\nMEASURED (read-only, all tenants, 02:29Z): 188 claim holders; 56 hold >=1 item that is state blocked/needs-human WITH >=1 active external blocker (78 such items, max 5 on one holder). 113 holders are at >=2 held claims; 18 of them are at a 2-claim cap ONLY because of those holds (24 at a 1-claim cap). Matches the census's 16 parked agents citing 2/2.\n\nDECISION. The one concurrency oracle (claim-spec-store getActiveClaimsForBee / readClaimConcurrencyBatch -> evaluateClaimConcurrency) excludes a held row from activeClaims when BOTH hold: (1) status is blocked or needs-human, and (2) activeExternalBlockers(payload) is non-empty. Classification runs in JS with the real external-blockers parser over the selected externalBlockers array, so SQL cannot drift from the parser. The verdict gains blockerParkedIds so every surface still names those holds; they are not hidden. work_items:set_blocker is the lever: recording a typed blocker on a held item frees its slot without releasing it.\n\nWHAT STILL COUNTS (EI-11796's protection kept): a wip item even if it carries a blocker (the holder says it is working it); a plain claim-hold park with no typed blocker; an item blocked only by a work-item link (work_items:link rel:blocks) -- out of P-010 scope; resource-governor receipts stay excluded as before.\n\nWHY THIS NARROWS RATHER THAN BREAKS EI-11796. EI-11796 stopped a member from parking items without explanation and accumulating lanes. A typed external blocker is not an unexplained park: it names kind/capability/ref/evidence/next action, the hold registry re-checks it, and the reaper applies owner-ask defaults. Accumulation is self-limiting: when blockers clear, those items count again and the member cannot pull until it is back under its cap. No separate ceiling for parked holds; P-013's re-measure watches max parked-per-holder (5 today).\n\nSURFACES UPDATED WITH IT: get_next concurrencyBlockedRefusal text (drops 'declaring a blocker does not buy a slot', names set_blocker as the lever and lists blocker-parked ids), fleet:assignments capacity comment, loop/arm EI-20304485841686120 comment, P-008's HELD_BLOCKED_ITEM_STAYS_HELD advice. The workspace fact guard-rail:fleet-assignments-blocked-holds-count-for-claim-capacity is superseded when this lands.\n\n### D-011 — P-011(a): a wedged host makes the liveness oracle say suspect + wedged, not parked; default-on wherever the host is trusted as proof of life\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self-imposed, su-92de4154 ~03:20Z; code read, measurement pending on WI-10008162]\n\nREAD (code): liveness-oracle.ts psuHostPositiveAuthority RESCUES a subject to parked/recorded whenever findLiveHost returns a live host process (deriveVerdict, 'psuHostLive && psuHost.positive' branch). The host record and its lifecycle tail already carry the cannot-take-a-turn conditions (authBlocked, quotaBlocked, unbound successor, stuck pending deliveries) and one judge reads them (turn-proof.ts judgeHostTail / hostRecoverableCondition, D-007). The oracle never consulted it, so a dead-auth codex or an unbound successor read exactly like a healthy parked agent on every routing surface that trusts the host (recipient-liveness, inbox-wake, fleet:assignments, grading-audit and consult routing, owner-directive routing, gate-ownership).\n\nDECISION.\n(1) No new SessionState. A wedged session is 'suspect' (already non-actionable in classifyReadActionability, already confirmLiveness=true) and the verdict carries wedged: PickupRecoverable naming the condition. A new state would ripple through every consumer for no behavioral gain.\n(2) Eligible states: parked, draining, recorded. Never live (a live turn contradicts a stale host flag), never suspect/ended/null.\n(3) A post-pass in resolveSessionStates reads the host view through the SAME judge as the pickup sweep and stalled-loops guard (pickupHostView + hostRecoverableCondition over a 64 KB async tail), 16 at a time, only for non-cup subjects with a live host and an eligible verdict.\n(4) Default ON wherever psuHostPositiveAuthority is on (opts.hostCondition defaults to it): a caller that trusts a live host as proof of life must also hear when that host's child cannot think. Other callers opt in with hostCondition:true (the P-011(b) alarm will).\n(5) Absent wedged means not wedged OR not checked, never checked-healthy.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-11 ~03:15Z, .papercusp/scratch/p011a-live-wedge.mts (read-only, real resolveSessionStates over listPresence, 414 subjects, psuHostPositiveAuthority on, leg OFF vs ON): 40 flips, all explained (28 quota-blocked, 8 pending-turn-stuck, 4 unbound-successor; 39 parked->suspect, 1 recorded->suspect); live 105 -> 105 untouched; cost 362 ms -> 562 ms for the whole roster. Flipped owners' last activity: 1 under 15 min (14 min), median ~5 h. psu-pty-host.mjs quota detector is level-based (observe(): not blocked -> reset(); published field = quotaBlockDetector.isBlocked()), so quota-blocked is current state, not sticky history. Tests: liveness-oracle-host-condition.test.ts 20/20 (test_runs 21027934) + 4 oracle suites 50/50 + 6 positive-authority caller suites 244/244; lint:tsc clean; behavioural-strands EXIT=0.\n\n### D-012 — P-011(b)+(c): one standing count alarm (agents-wedged / agents-stranded) on the coordination panel; why nothing alarmed while 61 loops stalled\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self-imposed, su-92de4154 ~03:40Z; measured unless tagged]\n\n(c) WHY NOTHING ALARMED. Four independent gaps, each now closed by an item of this plan:\n1. The repair path removed the evidence: stalled-loops-guard DISARMED a loop that stopped producing turns instead of repairing it, so the stalled population left the guard's own view (P-007) [per P-007 record].\n2. The retroactive detector was blind: silent-halt counted every session's own coord:inbox-wake watcher as a live wake source, so 115 of 118 checked sessions were exempt 'pending-await' and only 3 were judged halted (D-006, measured). After D-006 the same sweep judged 39 halted.\n3. Presence called a wedged host parked: the liveness oracle's psu-host positive authority rescued any session with a live host process to parked, so dead-auth / quota-walled / unbound sessions read as healthy idle and wakes to them reported woken:1 (D-011; 40 of 414 flipped once the host condition was judged).\n4. Nothing COUNTED the population [code read 2026-10-11]: EVALUATED_LIVENESS_SIGNATURES had no agent-population key; agent-productivity-watchdog only covers sessions that never produced an agent-origin call (never-booted / booted-never-worked), not a session that worked and then wedged; silent-halt pages one owner per halted session (capped at 5 a sweep). Per-victim remedies with no population count meant a correlated mass stall looked like N unrelated quiet sessions.\n\n(b) RULING. One census, no new panel or watchdog: packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/agent-strand-census.ts counts (i) WEDGED = the oracle's own wedged verdict (resolveSessionStates with psuHostPositiveAuthority + hostCondition explicitly ON) by class, and (ii) STRANDED = sweepSilentHalts({dryRun:true}).halted. It never re-derives liveness or wake sources. It rides the existing coordination panel (per-class metrics on /admin system health) and the existing infra-liveness alarm, signatures agents-wedged (>= 10) and agents-stranded (>= 5), severity blocker (pages once, deduped + flap-suppressed). The panel only WARNS: a crit would also raise the generic panel:coordination catch-all for the same condition. An unreadable leg, an errored panel, or a computed panel missing the census (older build's snapshot) is UNOBSERVED, never a recovery.\nStrictness: STRANDED uses D-008's wake-source predicate, NOT D-009's guaranteed-wake rule. An untimed watch on a live, reachable event is a real wake source; D-009's stricter bound governs only loop:end's refusal. Widening the alarm to 'no guaranteed wake' is not done here.\nThresholds: a single wedge is the pickup sweep's job and a single halt is silent-halt's; >= 10 wedged / >= 5 stranded means those remedies are not keeping up, usually behind one shared cause.\n\nMEASURED (live, operator DB control port 5432, .papercusp/scratch/p011b-strand-census.mts, 2026-10-11 ~03:35Z): checked 416, wedged 41 (quota-blocked 29, pending-turn-stuck 7, unbound-successor 5), stranded 32. Both alarms would fire today. Census cost ~1 s warm (13 s cold first call) inside the 30 s tick, in parallel with the panel's other reads.\n\n### D-013 — P-012: the quota-blocked class is a real wall on the shared default codex account; no respawn onto that route; host latch must expire at the stated reset\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed, su-92de4154 ~04:15Z; measured unless tagged]\nMEASURED (read-only, .papercusp/scratch/p012-quota-walls.mts + p012-quota-hosts.mts): all 63 P-012 population owners run codex; 62 of 63 codex homes symlink auth.json to ~/.codex/auth.json, one ChatGPT account (id suffix 09ce2f). Its child transcripts report usage_limit_exceeded, 'try again at Oct 14th, 2026 8:24 PM', credits balance 0. 28 of the 29 quota-blocked hosts show that error; the newest is 03:32Z, so launches onto this account are still walling on their first turn. This retracts the 04:02Z WI-10008163 inference that these hosts were stale-blocked; the gateway accounts the burn signals reported as recovered are not the ones these sessions use.\nRULING. (1) P-012 does not respawn any codex session onto the default route while that account is walled; a respawn spends a launch and re-walls on the first turn. (2) Which route those sessions run on after this is the owner's call (account routing), asked on WI-10008163. (3) Durable defect, built regardless: the codex quota latch in psu-pty-host.mjs (makeQuotaBlockDetector) has no expiry and no corroborator, and the recycle recovery requires accountMode 'auto'. So a default-route codex host stays deadlocked after the provider's reset [inferred from code; a test will pin it]. The host must parse the stated reset ('try again at <date>' / 'try again in <duration>') into the latch, expire the latch at that time, and publish quotaResetAtMs on its record so liveness can say 'walled until X' instead of 'wedged'.\n\n### D-014 — Corrects D-013: the shared codex account recovered early (~04:25Z); P-012 relaunches on the same route are valid; the host latch also needs a probe\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed, su-92de4154 ~04:35Z; measured unless tagged]\nD-013's premise that the 09ce2f account stays walled until Oct 14 is WRONG as of 04:25Z. (1) D-013 (1) is withdrawn: relaunching a latched codex host on its SAME route is the approved P-012 remediation (account preserved) and is effective now. (2) No owner routing decision is needed; the 04:08Z owner question was retracted by coord:send. (3) D-013 (3) stands and is extended: expiring the latch at the stated reset cannot see an early top-up, so a latched codex host must also probe. It lets one deferred wake through after a bounded, backed-off interval; a still-walled account repaints the banner and re-latches. (4) [inferred, not measured] host-code adoption after the WI-6554700010008412 edit is already relaunching hosts (31 started after 04:14Z; quota-blocked fell from 29 to 17). The current held_work_items subquery in silent-halt-reconcile.ts counts all nonterminal, non-observation holds without inspecting state or externalBlockers. D-010 already classifies the same legitimate park for claim concurrency.\n\nDecision: Extend D-010/P-010's exact predicate to silent-halt's held-work justification. A held row is excluded from this detector's actionable-work count only when status is blocked or needs-human AND the shared activeExternalBlockers parser finds at least one active typed external blocker. Reuse isParkedOnExternalBlocker; do not re-spell blocker semantics in SQL. When all held rows are blocker-parked, report a named exemption with the parked item IDs. When actionable and parked rows coexist, retain the halt verdict based on actionable rows and include the excluded IDs in the wake/page context. The blocker-held rows remain visible and still count again in the scheduler after their blockers clear.\n\nThis narrows only silent-halt's stranded-work predicate; it does not change D-010's concurrency oracle or its treatment of wip, unexplained claim holds, internal work-item dependencies, or resource-governor receipts.\nRelated: P-013\n\n### D-024 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-16\nAmendment-Id: parked-fire97-method-coverage-424d5-v2\nRequest-Hash: 0987b7f30f072b36e8923a29daca0cf442efeb0442b855d4f37b6830e94b7fc4\nActor: su-424d5476-0b13-401a-a926-0aaa9f212391\nReason: Method-only Fire96 construction clarification. All fourteen original outcome fields, scopes, check declarations, fingerprints and pass semantics remain exactly unchanged; this does not claim atomic supplement coverage or runtime acceptance.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive ()\nRubric revision: 7 → 8\nSubject plan revision: 65 → 66\nChanged BARs: \nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14\n\n### D-025 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-17\nAmendment-Id: parked-resume154-add18-preview-424d5-v1\nRequest-Hash: f306c6c67de3a0cc75ea6b9821a904c24cd858109ead6028b7c82ce804a5ea28\nActor: su-424d5476-0b13-401a-a926-0aaa9f212391\nReason: Add only18 independently reviewed construction outcomes R15..19/R22..34 from immutable Resume151 after A1..A7. Original14 complete criterion objects resubmitted exactly unchanged, original R12 terminal proof preserved. R20/R21 withheld. Construction targets explicitly unlocated; no bindings/grades/acceptance claimed.\nApproved-By: su-d5657ad4-21e4-470d-8e4f-ea552ca7d380\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1188647\nApproved-At: 2026-10-17T17:48:49.753Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 67 → 68\nChanged BARs: R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19, R-22, R-23, R-24, R-25, R-26, R-27, R-28, R-29, R-30, R-31, R-32, R-33, R-34\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-026 — Silent-halt: a blocker park excuses a stop only when it names its wake; otherwise ONE wake, never a page (narrows D-010's silent-halt use)\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\n[self-imposed, su-cb4d4302, AUTO under owner directive #2094; implements report rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98 item #4; WI-6554700010018551]\n\nMEASURED (live, 2026-10-21 ~00:50Z): of 96 active blockers held by loop-off AUTO sessions with no actionable held work, 91 carry no recheckAt (runtime 45, gate 22, event 20, human 4). These are pre-default rows: updateExternalBlockerHistory stamps a default recheckAt on every set/re-declaration, but the blocker reaper selects on recheckAt <= now, which NULL never matches. So nothing revisits them and, with no await, nothing wakes the holder.\n\nDECISION. In evaluateSilentHalt, a blocker-parked hold keeps the 'holds-only-active-external-blockers' exemption only when every active blocker on it names a parseable re-check time (external-blockers.ts activeBlockersWithoutRecheck is the one predicate). A hold whose blocker names none falls through the usual clocks as a WAKE-ONLY halt: verdict.wakeOnly, listed in SilentHaltSweepResult.wakeOnly, woken once per disarm epoch with name-your-wake text (re-declare via work_items:set_blocker, which stamps recheckAt, or events:await with a timeout), queued after actionable halts under the per-sweep wake cap, and NEVER paged, never in the owner-facing alarm:silent-halt broadcast. They stay in result.halted, so the agent-strand census still counts them as stranded.\n\nUNCHANGED: D-010's claim-concurrency exclusion; D-009 (the detector still counts untimed live awaits; widening that remains P-011's call); actionable held work still pages after its wake.\n\nDRY RUN (real sweep, dryRun:true, 437 candidates): halted 238 = 180 pageable + 58 wake-only; the blocker exemption now spares 0 (previously those 58). The pageable count matches the live sweep's 179-180, so owner pages do not change.\n\n### D-027 — A confirmed wake miss on a warm-idle owner overrides positive psu-host authority (refines D-011)\nDate: 2026-10-21\nRuling (su-1622829b, 2026-10-21, AUTO, EI-26597499932248750). In `deriveVerdict`'s positive psu-host rescue (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/liveness-oracle.ts), a live host no longer rescues an `ended`/`suspect` derivation to `parked`/`draining`/`recorded` when BOTH of these hold: `wakeAttemptMiss` is true (a turn-burning wake outlived WAKE_PICKUP_GRACE_MS with no activity after it) AND `warmIdle` is true (no turn for WARM_IDLE_ACTIVITY_MS). Such an owner now reads `suspect` + `wedged:'pending-turn-stuck'`, the same report the host-condition leg gives a host whose deliveries are stuck pending.\n\nWhy: measured on su-c5e6d0e3, a Codex host up 5.7 days whose child had sat at 0% CPU for 4.96 days. coord:presence and coord:send (positive authority) read it as parked and wakeable, and a send returned woken:1 with no recipient_dead. Every consumer without positive authority, including scorecards:emit's author-seat gate, read it as `ended`. D-011 already holds that a live host is not proof the session can think; this extends that from host-tail evidence to the oracle's own wake-ledger evidence.\n\nPrecision (D-007): either signal alone keeps the rescue. A miss alone (recent activity) is the ambiguity the rescue exists for, and warm-idle alone describes a legitimately parked owner. Both alone are pinned by unit cases in liveness-oracle-host-condition.test.ts.\n\nAlternative rejected: making every consumer pass identical authority options. That would leave the wedged host reading `parked` everywhere instead of `ended` everywhere, which hides the defect rather than fixing it.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"simplify-integration-setup-2026-10-10","title":"Simplify Slack / Asana / GitHub setup so any Papercusp user can run the Slack→Asana bug workflow without curl or a hand-built OAuth app","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-10","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Simplify Slack / Asana / GitHub setup so any Papercusp user can run the Slack→Asana bug workflow without curl or a hand-built OAuth app\nslug: simplify-integration-setup-2026-10-10\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-10-10\nupdated: 2026-10-11\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Source turns:** [owner:Avi 2026-10-10 #1628] \"how would another papercusp user be able to use this workflow with their own accounts?\"; [owner:Avi 2026-10-10 #1634] \"Anyway we can simplify this process for users?\"\n\n**Audience:** a Papercusp desktop user other than Avi, with their own Slack workspace, Asana account and GitHub account.\n\n**Problem (measured 2026-10-10, su-0dd6b):**\n- Asana: each installation needs its own Asana developer app registered in `$PAPERCUSP_HOME/oauth-apps.json`, read by `resolveOAuthProvider` in `packages/operator-core/lib/integrations/connection-lifecycle.ts`. Setting it up means a client id, a secret file, callbacks, the Full permissions switch, and the distribution setting. Asana requires `client_secret` at both token exchange and refresh ([Asana OAuth docs](https://developers.asana.com/docs/oauth)), so a secret-less desktop client is not possible.\n- Slack: the customer's own internal Slack app (`slack-org-connector.ts`). Setup is copying the manifest, generating xapp/xoxb tokens, then curl with the superuser token to `/admin/triggers/slack/connect`. The runbook `reference/slack-external-trigger-setup` states there is no UI path.\n- Bug routing: the `configure-slack-bugs` op on the admin external-triggers route (channels + Asana source/project; both sources must be owned by the caller) is API-only.\n- GitHub: PRs use the single `gh auth token` identity of the machine (`identity/gh-token.ts`). It is not per user and not visible in the UI.\n\n**Outcome:** the whole setup lives on one page in the desktop app, and the only things a user does outside Papercusp are click \"Create app\" in Slack and consent or copy a token.\n\n**Non-goals (this plan):** a Papercusp-hosted OAuth broker or relay (P-007 records it as a decision, not a build); Slack Marketplace listing; per-user GitHub identity on a shared installation.\n\n**Scenarios:**\n1. A new user opens Settings → Integrations, clicks \"Create Slack app\" (Slack opens with the manifest pre-filled), installs it, and pastes the two tokens into masked fields. Slack shows as connected with the team and bot names.\n2. The same user connects Asana either by pasting a personal access token (no developer app needed) or through OAuth once a client is registered from the UI.\n3. The same user picks channels the bot is in and an Asana project from dropdowns. Bug routing is armed.\n4. The page shows which GitHub account PRs will come from, and offers a sign-in if none.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — No terminal.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Another Papercusp user can set up the Slack→Asana bug workflow with their own accounts, more simply than today.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:8\",\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:21\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every setup step for Slack, Asana, bug routing and GitHub is reachable from Settings → Integrations, and none requires a terminal, the superuser token, or editing a file under $PAPERCUSP_HOME.\",\"falsifier\":\"Some setup step for these integrations can only be completed with curl, a terminal command, the superuser bearer, or a hand-edited file.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Boot the desktop with scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh and VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1, open Settings → Integrations, and drive each card to its connected or configured state through the webview only; run each card's unit tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Reuse existing surfaces.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Simplify setup without building a parallel setup system.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:8\",\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:21\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every setup step this plan adds is offered and completed only on the one Settings → Integrations page, and its result is reported by the same connection status that automation and agents already read.\",\"falsifier\":\"A setup step this plan adds is offered in two different places, or a step completed in Settings → Integrations is not reflected in the connection status automation and agents read.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Complete each new setup step from Settings → Integrations in the desktop shell, confirm the connection status automation reads reports the result, and confirm no second screen or command offers the same step.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Secrets stay safe.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Keep user tokens and client secrets safe while moving setup into the UI.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:8\",\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:21\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Tokens and client secrets are never shown back on any page or returned by any read, are never written into a repository, remain usable after an app restart, are readable on disk only by the owning OS user, and are never stored unencrypted in the database.\",\"falsifier\":\"A stored token or secret appears in a rendered page or response, is written to a file inside a repository, is lost on restart, is readable on disk by another OS user, or appears unencrypted in the database.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run unit tests asserting the status and connected-state responses contain no token or secret values; restart the app and confirm the connection still works; check that stored credentials are not inside a repository, are readable only by the owning user, and that the database holds no plaintext token or secret.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Asana without a developer app.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Let a user connect Asana without registering their own Asana developer app.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:8\",\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:21\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A user can connect Asana by pasting a personal access token, and the resulting source syncs and files tasks like an OAuth-connected one.\",\"falsifier\":\"A personal-access-token Asana source fails to sync or to create a task where an OAuth source succeeds.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run unit tests proving sync and ticket.create accept a PAT credential, then paste a token on the Asana card in the headless shell and confirm the source syncs.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Customer-owned Slack app.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Keep Slack usable at full rate limits for each user's own workspace.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:8\",\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:21\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The Slack app stays customer-owned (created from the manifest inside the user's own workspace), because commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps get conversations.history clamped to 1 request/min and 15 messages (Slack changelog 2025-05-29) while internal apps keep Tier 3.\",\"falsifier\":\"The setup flow installs a shared Papercusp-owned Slack app instead of one the user creates in their own workspace.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Check that the Slack card builds its create-app link from the user's own manifest and posts the user's own tokens to /admin/triggers/slack/connect; run the card's unit tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Verified in the real shell.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"New setup screens must actually work in the desktop app.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:8\",\"session_turn:claude:f82a4caa-8c48-4635-9ba6-e89d16ea0d94:21\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every new UI path is exercised headlessly in the desktop shell against an isolated database and covered by registered tests.\",\"falsifier\":\"A new UI path has no registered test or was never driven in the headless Tauri shell.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the registered tests for each new UI path and review the headless Tauri run evidence recorded on each item's work-item.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nAll setup moves onto the existing Settings → Integrations page (`apps/operator/app/settings/integrations/page.tsx`), which already connects Asana/Linear over OAuth and picks projects. The desktop webview calls the admin routes with its cookie session, which `require-principal.ts` resolves as `trust: 'verified'`, satisfying the Slack routes' `['verified','trusted']` tier without the superuser bearer. The pre-filled Slack link (`manifest_json`) is undocumented, so the manifest copy fallback stays.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-004, P-005 | live |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | live |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-007 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-005, P-006 | live |\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` Slack card on Settings → Integrations: a \"Create Slack app\" button that opens Slack's create-from-manifest page pre-filled from `/admin/triggers/slack/manifest` (`api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1&manifest_json=…`, with a copy-manifest fallback because the parameter is undocumented), masked xapp-/xoxb- fields that POST to the existing `/admin/triggers/slack/connect` with the desktop session, and a connected state showing team, bot and status. — note: Verified in headless desktop (WI-10008245). Reference UX per D-005; replaced by cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10 P-005.\n- **P-002** `dropped` Bug-routing picker on the same page: list the channels the bot is a member of and the user's Asana sources with their projects; save through the existing `configure-slack-bugs` op and show the bug-classification binding's armed state. — note: Superseded by D-005 (owner #1646/#1650): moved to cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10 P-004 (x-options pickers).\n- **P-003** `dropped` Asana personal access token as an alternative to OAuth: paste on the Asana card, verify with GET /users/me, store through the existing token storage, create the user's Asana source in the same shape as OAuth; tests prove sync and ticket.create work with a PAT credential. — note: Superseded by D-005 (owner #1646/#1650): moved to cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10 P-009 (Asana personal token via setup.credentials).\n- **P-004** `dropped` Register an Asana or Linear OAuth client from the UI (client id + secret written to the 0600 client file outside the repo) instead of editing oauth-apps.json by hand, with the exact callback URLs and the Full-permissions / distribution checklist shown inline. — note: Superseded by D-005 (owner #1646/#1650): moved to cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10 P-009 (generic OAuth client registration form).\n- **P-005** `dropped` GitHub on the same page: show which account PRs will be opened as (from `gh auth status`) and offer a \"Sign in to GitHub\" action using gh's browser/device flow when none is signed in. — note: Superseded by D-005 (owner #1646/#1650): moved to cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10 P-010 (GitHub identity on the generic card).\n- **P-006** `dropped` Rewrite the user guides `guides/linear-asana-ticket-sync` and `reference/slack-external-trigger-setup` around the in-app flow (curl becomes the fallback), via docs:author. — note: Superseded by D-005 (owner #1646/#1650): moved to cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10 P-012 (docs).\n- **P-007** `dropped` Write the decision record + design note for the hosted option: a Papercusp-hosted OAuth broker holding Papercusp-owned Asana/Linear apps (distribution: any workspace) and a GitHub App, which would make Asana/Linear/GitHub one-click; Slack stays customer-owned per R-5. Not built in this plan. — note: Superseded by D-005 (owner #1646/#1650): moved to cupboard-distributable-integrations-2026-10-10 P-013 (hosted one-click OAuth decision).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-10\nAmendment-Id: su0dd6-r6-wording-apply-1\nRequest-Hash: 2180280a735ba741a62049bdc841d7ed053237c095f6bb03ab7c3709a40aa126\nActor: su-0dd6b9aa-3d59-4727-991e-377d05bc2459\nReason: Sync R-6 with the plan text: drop the implementation-file name (spec-quality implementation-independence). Wording only, same meaning.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-81bb90ac-39ad-413f-b1e5-bc6bc458c32e\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1172955\nApproved-At: 2026-10-10T23:07:11.629Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 6 → 7\nChanged BARs: R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-10\nAmendment-Id: su0dd6-r2-wording-apply-1\nRequest-Hash: c7873d3b02e96c1ae8cc05d32918bfe4cef733046366adbc9312d0fb446311a6\nActor: su-0dd6b9aa-3d59-4727-991e-377d05bc2459\nReason: Sync with plan text after spec-quality grading audit EI-25636763786619191: restate as observable behaviour (no route names, page reuse, or storage mechanism). Same intent.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-b047fb18-007f-48d5-9c3e-2c682a4ad4b7\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1172998\nApproved-At: 2026-10-10T23:33:51.907Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 13 → 14\nChanged BARs: R-2\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-10\nAmendment-Id: amend-9cdc1c0855d1ce5457dee584\nRequest-Hash: d6a836c9c0f361cac5e948321e199430a568a9c69bcbd77985f16560bef4685a\nActor: su-0dd6b9aa-3d59-4727-991e-377d05bc2459\nReason: Adopt reviewer wording (thread-post:1172997): observable behaviour, keeps encryption-at-rest\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-3af6f7a7-99ad-4089-bb9b-24b8ff80f4a2\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1173000\nApproved-At: 2026-10-10T23:36:47.318Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 14 → 15\nChanged BARs: R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-10\nAmendment-Id: amend-96b7eced808bb6486ac9e6ee\nRequest-Hash: 121ae77fda199fcfb78e11d1a40d83648bff27a0e422e285661edfe0ac18d3ae\nActor: su-0dd6b9aa-3d59-4727-991e-377d05bc2459\nReason: Spec-quality atomic-observable-behavior: restate R-2 as one assertion, same two properties.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-f3bd8d9f-3bc4-4da6-a4a0-99e4e081d998\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1173009\nApproved-At: 2026-10-10T23:42:57.499Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 16 → 17\nChanged BARs: R-2\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-005 — Integrations ship as Cupboard packages; setup is declared, not hardcoded\nDate: 2026-10-10\nSource: [owner:Avi 2026-10-10 directive #1646] — the plan hardcodes one integration; the owner wants integrations distributable via the Cupboard so anyone can build and publish one. Ruling: no new provider-specific code in the app. Setup steps are declared by provider packages (setup.credentials, setup.appRegistration, host-held socket ingress) and trigger packs (inputs JSON Schema with x-options option sources), and Settings → Integrations renders them generically. Slack ingestion and the Slack→Asana bug workflow move into a slack provider package and a datatype-bound bug-triage trigger pack, published through the Cupboard as the worked example. P-001 stays as reference UX and is replaced by the generic card; P-002..P-005 are superseded by the re-scoped plan; P-006/P-007 carry over. Design: report rpt_7df541d5-70ec-4c5d-b82b-f686052d3431.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-bm25-lexical-search-evoke-adoption-2026-10-10","title":"Acceptance BAR — Real BM25 ranking for papercusp lexical search (pg_textsearch, chosen by bake-off over Evoke)","status":"active","created":"2026-10-11","owner":"su-bc44ac7e-de9c-4270-8222-fbc9da93161b","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Real BM25 ranking for papercusp lexical search (pg_textsearch, chosen by bake-off over Evoke)\nslug: acceptance-bm25-lexical-search-evoke-adoption-2026-10-10\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-11\nupdated: 2026-10-13\nowner: su-bc44ac7e-de9c-4270-8222-fbc9da93161b\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Real BM25 ranking for papercusp lexical search (pg_textsearch, chosen by bake-off over Evoke)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. The activation-source review found no omitted product requirement.\n\n**Next:** Reproduce and fix WI-10007560's stale bulk recommendation report race against a successful terminal action, then verify preserved receipts, metadata, audit linkage, revert handle, counters, Stop ordering, and ordinary pending rows.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Papercusp maintainers and operators using Inbox bulk resolve.\",\n  \"problem\": \"A delayed recommendation report can acquire the run lock after a terminal bulk action and overwrite the canonical item outcome, action metadata, and derived counter.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Completed and dismissed outcomes remain canonical when stale reports arrive. The store returns current receipts for preserved rows, and the report boundary does not auto-accept them again.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Do not retry, reopen, or replay the historical failed bulk run.\",\n    \"Do not change terminal action authority, Stop ordering, or resolver recommendation behavior.\",\n    \"Do not add a tool, service, table, or new outcome state.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:1\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:15\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:48\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:52\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:54\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"observed-fact\",\n      \"text\": \"The original resolver kickoff and close are agent-generated session turns, not an owner request for this follow-up. They establish the historical run boundaries and confirm the old run was closed.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:1\",\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:16\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"observed-fact\",\n      \"text\": \"The resolver recorded a possible late-report overwrite in turn 15 and later confirmed the store still updated terminal outcomes in turn 48; the race remained unverified in turn 54.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:15\",\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:48\",\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:54\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"observed-fact\",\n      \"text\": \"Turns 52 and 54 record a pre-change baseline of 14 selected unit tests and 3 isolated PostgreSQL tests; the race was not exercised and no source files changed.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:52\",\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a11c77-c857-7f12-bb47-8d863c0bf60b:54\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"assumption\",\n      \"text\": \"The implementation-approval question remains unanswered, and this session's registered AUTO mode authorizes proceeding with the scoped follow-up. The historical run remains closed.\",\n      \"recommendation\": \"Implement the store guard and report-boundary regression tests only.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"scenarios\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-001\",\n      \"title\": \"An ordinary pending report is recorded\",\n      \"kind\": \"normal\",\n      \"trigger\": \"The resolver reports a non-action outcome for an item that is still pending while the run accepts reports.\",\n      \"action\": \"The store records the report, recomputes counters, and returns the row as updated.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"The normal pending outcome remains available to the existing auto-accept eligibility path.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-7\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-002\",\n      \"title\": \"A stale report arrives after a terminal action\",\n      \"kind\": \"concurrency\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A previously prepared recommendation report waits while the terminal action commits auto_resolved first.\",\n      \"action\": \"The report writer sees the current terminal row and returns its canonical receipt without rewriting it.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Outcome, action/reversal metadata, audit linkage, and counters remain canonical; the preserved id is excluded from auto-accept.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-3\",\n        \"R-4\",\n        \"R-5\",\n        \"R-6\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-003\",\n      \"title\": \"A dismissed item receives a stale report\",\n      \"kind\": \"boundary\",\n      \"trigger\": \"The owner dismisses an item before its earlier non-action report reaches the store.\",\n      \"action\": \"The store preserves the dismissed row and returns its current receipt.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Dismissal and its metadata remain unchanged and the item is not auto-accepted.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-3\",\n        \"R-5\",\n        \"R-6\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-004\",\n      \"title\": \"A batch contains a pending item and an unknown id\",\n      \"kind\": \"boundary\",\n      \"trigger\": \"One report batch includes an ordinary pending item and an id absent from the run.\",\n      \"action\": \"The store updates the pending item and classifies the absent id as unknown.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Updated, preserved, and unknown results remain distinguishable.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-6\",\n        \"R-7\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-005\",\n      \"title\": \"Stop commits before a report\",\n      \"kind\": \"authorization\",\n      \"trigger\": \"The owner stops the run before a non-action report obtains the run-row lock.\",\n      \"action\": \"The existing report path refuses the write under the current Stop boundary.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"No report is written and Stop ordering and terminal-action authority remain unchanged.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  \"considerations\": [\n    {\n      \"category\": \"terminal action authority\",\n      \"disposition\": \"covered\",\n      \"reason\": \"The fix is limited to non-action reports; terminal effects continue through bulk-run-act.\",\n      \"scenarioIds\": [\n        \"SC-002\",\n        \"SC-005\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"category\": \"historical run replay\",\n      \"disposition\": \"not-applicable\",\n      \"reason\": \"The prior run remains closed; this task adds no retry, reopening, or replay.\",\n      \"scenarioIds\": [\n        \"SC-002\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Preserve terminal item outcomes.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A delayed recommendation report must not overwrite an item's terminal outcome after a terminal bulk action or dismissal.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A delayed report preserves the addressed item's stored terminal outcome.\",\"falsifier\":\"The delayed report changes that item's canonical outcome away from its stored auto_resolved or dismissed value.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts` and compare the persisted item outcome before and after the delayed report.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Return canonical preserved receipts.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The report result must distinguish updated rows, terminal rows preserved from a stale report, and unknown item ids.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each protected terminal row is returned as its current canonical receipt, while updated ids and unknown ids remain separately identifiable.\",\"falsifier\":\"A protected row is missing or returned with stale fields, or updated and unknown ids are conflated.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the bulk-run store integration test and compare each preserved receipt to the database row read inside the reporting transaction.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Prevent repeat auto-accept.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The report-tool boundary must not auto-accept an item whose terminal receipt was preserved by the store.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The bulk-report tool excludes every preserved item id from its auto-accept candidate set.\",\"falsifier\":\"A preserved id appears in the auto-accept candidate set or receives an auto-accept action.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/inbox/bulk-run.test.ts` and inspect auto-accept candidates for a mixed preserved/pending response.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/inbox/bulk-run.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Preserve terminal action audit linkage.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A delayed recommendation report must preserve the audit record written for a terminal bulk action.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"After the delayed report, the harness_shared.attention_triage row remains keyed to the same workspace_id and item_id and retains its action, note, triaged_by, and triaged_at values.\",\"falsifier\":\"The triage row is missing, linked to another item, or any of its action, note, triaged_by, or triaged_at values changes.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts` and compare the attention_triage row for the item before and after the delayed report.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Preserve terminal action metadata.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A delayed recommendation report must not replace action or reversal metadata stored when a bulk terminal action succeeded.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A delayed report preserves the protected metadata snapshot for the addressed terminal state (auto_resolved fields: actionId, rationale, draftAnswer, confidence, consulted, consultReply, decidedAt, revertHandle, reversalWindowUntil, revertedAt, revertNote / dismissed fields: rationale, draftAnswer, confidence, consulted, consultReply, decidedAt, disposition).\",\"falsifier\":\"A delayed report changes any listed metadata field for an auto_resolved item or any listed dismissal field for a dismissed item.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts` and compare auto_resolved action/reversal metadata and dismissed rationale/decision metadata before and after the delayed report.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Preserve derived run counters.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A delayed recommendation report must not make stored run counters disagree with the run's item outcomes.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"After a delayed report, each stored run counter equals its item-outcome tally with dismissed items counted in skipped.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any stored run counter differs from its recomputed tally over the run's item outcomes.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts` and compare stored counters with a tally of item outcomes, counting dismissed in skipped.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/bulk-run-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Continue processing ordinary pending rows.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A mixed report batch must continue applying valid outcomes to ordinary items that remain pending.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For a pending item in a mixed batch, the incoming report is written and the item is returned among updated rows.\",\"falsifier\":\"An eligible pending item remains pending or is omitted from the updated results.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/inbox/bulk-run.test.ts` and inspect an ordinary pending row alongside a preserved terminal receipt.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/inbox/bulk-run.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n## Tasks\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Add the store guard and canonical preserved receipts, with a real-PostgreSQL delayed-action/report race regression.\n- **P-002** `todo` Update the bulk-report boundary to surface preserved receipts and exclude them from auto-accept candidates, with tool tests. blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Design\nThe existing run-row lock remains the serialization boundary. A non-action report that reaches a row already completed or dismissed returns its stored receipt and does not rewrite it. The terminal action audit remains linked through the existing `harness_shared.attention_triage` row. The report handler uses the store receipt list as the authoritative exclusion set for auto-accept. P-002 remains blocked by P-001 because the report boundary consumes the store's preserved receipts.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-002 | tree |\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAmendment-Id: apply-r5-dismissed-review-2026-10-11-01\nRequest-Hash: bdda4ee4cc96759ae2695439e29a69aef1b12f8847740cff8c2fb326cfce2964\nActor: su-8aa83a0b-722e-4e39-bb2c-d29b85a295b3\nReason: Apply the approved seven-criterion replacement after outside-lineage approval 1174084 for preview 1174071.\nApproved-By: su-0110737b-412d-4243-b669-2303fb8d8af6\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1174084\nApproved-At: 2026-10-11T10:48:27.896Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 6 → 7\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAmendment-Id: bulk-late-atomic-preview-20261015-7e0ba-v2\nRequest-Hash: 9f1794854462d373ef8e96fbc1a7c12fe88c1f082aaf3e94402be7163a6f6ee8\nActor: su-7e0ba54d-8ab4-4b5a-9afe-e84d794584bc\nReason: Express R-1/R-5/R-6 as single invariants without changing protected outcomes, per-state field lists, dismissed tally semantics, test layers, methods, or non-goals; the plan-class boundary/draft repairs are separately verified.\nApproved-By: su-2aef5e5a-4182-43ac-a26c-37c029470aa5\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1182862\nApproved-At: 2026-10-15T05:29:48.817Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 11 → 12\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-5, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-5, R-6\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"dao-hr-people-2026-10-11","title":"DAO HR + people: hiring, legally binding contracts, configurable equity terms, org view","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-11","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: DAO HR + people: hiring, legally binding contracts, configurable equity terms, org view\nslug: dao-hr-people-2026-10-11\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-11\nupdated: 2026-10-20\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-12, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing. Next repair: Vet the current acceptance-rubric criteria BEFORE binding proof or emitting adequacy cards (amend → vet → attest → bind → cards → grade): a vetting critique usually becomes an amendment, and proof bound first must then be re-bound.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nDRAFT for Avi's review (WI-6554700010008422). No implementation until Avi approves scope, answers the open choices below, and picks an execution route. Before activation: convert requirements to structured `requirement` blocks and run the activation audit.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008607 — Versioned contract-template registry per engagement type and jurisdiction (employee/contractor agreement, IP assignment, equity grant agreement, onboarding forms list) with merge fields, counsel-appr… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008608 — Work profile on the shared person record, linked to DAO member identity and wallet (R-1). <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008609 — Versioned equity + hiring policy settings with bounds, per-offer overrides, audit, and admin execution of chain-enforced values within immutable maxima, no vote (R-2, D-004). <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008610 — Equity contract version with vesting cliff, immutable return ceiling and minimum payout share/% preview, approvals (R-4). <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008612 — Contract generation from approved templates + e-signature adapter + countersignature + stored executed document bound to the grant (R-5). <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008613 — Onboarding: identity, wallet binding, governance grant proposal, on-chain acceptance, membership admission, checklist (R-6). <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008614 — Amendments and offboarding (R-7). <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008615 — People directory + profile pages in the Workbench (R-8). <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ]
