grading, ship. <!-- P-013 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** (1) DAO admins/hiring managers bringing on people. (2) New hires going through offer → signature → onboarding. (3) Every member who needs to see the organization.\n\n**Problem.** The DAO software can admit members and has tested equity contracts (grants, vesting, share returns), but there is no way to hire someone: no offer, no contract, no signature, no onboarding, no per-person equity settings. The Workbench Members tab shows only name, username, membership status and device count; Ownership shows only org totals plus raw JSON and a raw contract-call form. No profiles, no org chart, no per-person cap table.\n\n**Outcome.** A hiring manager opens a role, makes an offer with equity sized from configurable policy, the hire signs a legally binding contract electronically, the company countersigns, the equity grant goes through governance and lands on chain, and the hire is onboarded. The Workbench shows a people directory, profiles, an org chart and a cap table.\n\n**Non-goals.** Cash payroll and tax withholding (use a payroll provider later; open choice O-4). Writing legal terms: the software fills in and executes counsel-approved templates; it never drafts legal language itself. Bounties/one-off task payments (covered by agent-economy-flywheel-2026-08-30 P-011/P-014). Recruiting/sourcing candidates. A new app scaffold or a separate contact database.\n\n**Source turns.** [owner:Avi 2026-10-11] orders #1667 (\"The DAO will need like HR software to bring on new hires… a gui for viewing the whole organization, members, profiles, equity\") and #1668 (\"draft the hr+ people plan. When we hire them we also want to create a real legally binding contract. And we want to be able to configure the size of their equity payments and any other related settings.\"), session claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847. Also the hiring successor approved for drafting in shared-pot-dao-cupboard-v1-2026-09-04 (never drafted; this plan covers its hiring half).\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. *Hire an engineer.* Admin opens \"Senior engineer\" role. Policy says that level gets 20,000 shares over 4 years, 1-year cliff. Admin bumps it to 25,000 (within the per-grant limit). The offer preview shows shares and % of fully diluted ownership. Candidate signs the employment agreement and IP assignment electronically; an authorized company signer countersigns. A governance proposal to register the hire and commit the grant opens automatically; members vote; after the timelock it executes. The hire verifies identity, binds a wallet, accepts the issuer terms on chain and appears in the directory and cap table.\n2. *Change a policy.* Admin changes the default cliff from 12 to 6 months for new offers. Existing grants are unchanged. A change touching an on-chain value (e.g. per-grant maximum) is executed by an authorized admin, stays within the contract's immutable maximum, and is recorded in the audit log; no member vote (D-004).\n3. *Someone leaves.* Admin proposes ending the engagement; members vote; after the timelock, unvested future equity stops; earned equity stays (already how the contract works). Access is removed; records are kept.\n4. *Look at the org.* A member opens People: directory with photos, titles, teams; clicks a profile (role, manager, start date, contract status, equity summary per visibility rules); switches to the org chart; opens the cap table to see holdings, grants (earned/unvested/claimed) and return entitlements.\n\n## Current equity facts this plan builds on (code-verified 2026-10-11)\n\nFrom packages/operator-core/lib/equity (PapercuspEquity.sol, README): grants are linear between two timestamps with **no cliff support**; per-grant maximum starts at 10% of the share cap, governance-adjustable within that bound; every grant/registration needs a governance vote (60% default) plus a ≥1-day timelock; at most 256 registered holders; share returns are **declared one at a time by governance vote** and claimed by each holder — **nothing is automatic**; the 10%-per-year return ceiling and 30-day minimum interval are hard-coded constants; termination keeps earned equity. Contracts are tested on a simulated EVM only; nothing is deployed, and issuer activation requires a formed company and signed issuer documents (agent-economy-flywheel P-045, P-002).\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — One person record.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi wants HR software to bring on new hires and to see members and profiles; hires, candidates and members must be one person, not a separate HR contact list.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:0\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each hire, candidate and member is a single shared person record carrying a work profile (title, team, manager, level, start date, engagement type employee|contractor, jurisdiction, status, regular pay terms) linked to DAO member identity and verified wallet; no HR-owned contact table exists.\",\"falsifier\":\"A second person/contact table is introduced for HR, or a work profile can exist without a person record, or the profile cannot represent both employee and contractor engagement types.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"db\",\"api\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration test against real Postgres migrations: create person → attach work profile → link member identity + wallet; assert uniqueness and that engagement types employee and contractor (D-003) and pay terms (D-005) round-trip.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/work-profile.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/work-profile.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Configurable equity and hiring policy.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi: configure the size of hires' equity payments and any other related settings.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\",\"session_turn:claude:95a8fd78-329b-4ee6-a1ba-f4d361ba439c:3\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Org-level versioned, audited policy settings (default grant per role/level, vesting length, cliff, start rule, per-grant limit, return rate and cadence, compensation visibility) with per-offer overrides validated against bounds; changing a chain-enforced value is executed by the admin role within immutable maxima with no governance vote (D-004); existing grants never change.\",\"falsifier\":\"An override outside bounds is accepted, a policy change mutates an existing grant, a change is unaudited, or a chain-enforced policy change opens a governance vote.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"api\",\"db\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit + integration tests over policy versioning, bounds validation, override clamping/refusal, audit rows, and the admin-execution path (no proposal created). Governing: D-004.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/equity-policy.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/equity-policy.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Contracts support the settings; votes only for hire and fire.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi asked whether equity automatically earns equity interest, then ruled that voting should only happen for hire/fire.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:12\",\"session_turn:claude:95a8fd78-329b-4ee6-a1ba-f4d361ba439c:3\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A new equity contract version supports vesting cliffs; admin-set return rate and cadence under immutable ceilings (10%/yr, 30-day minimum) with payouts triggerable when due without a vote; a bounded admin role for policy values; holder registration + grant creation (hire) and stopGrant (fire) callable only through governance; no path lets the admin reduce earned equity, stop a grant, register a holder, or exceed ceilings.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any hostile EVM call succeeds: admin stops a grant, admin registers a holder or creates a grant, a payout exceeds the ceiling or interval, earned equity decreases, or a cliffed grant releases before the cliff.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"contracts\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Real-EVM tests (existing evm-test-helpers) covering cliff vesting, scheduled payouts, admin bounds, and hostile calls for every forbidden path. Governing: D-004.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/equity/equity-v2.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Hiring flow.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi wants an interface to bring on new hires as ongoing roles with regular pay, both employees and contractors.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:0\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:14\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:20\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Role → candidate → offer (terms from policy + overrides, preview in shares and % fully diluted, regular pay terms, engagement type) → internal approval → contract → governance hire proposal; every step has state and history; contractor offers whose terms look like employment are flagged.\",\"falsifier\":\"An offer can skip a step, the % fully-diluted preview disagrees with chain share totals, state history is missing, or an employment-like contractor offer is not flagged.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"api\",\"db\",\"ui\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration tests drive the state machine end to end with a fake chain reader; unit tests pin the dilution math and misclassification flag.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/hiring.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/hiring.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Legally binding contract execution.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi: when we hire them we also want to create a real legally binding contract; chose Documenso.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:11\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:17\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Contracts are generated only from versioned registry templates with merge fields per engagement type and jurisdiction; signing goes through the Documenso adapter (consent, signer identity, timestamps, sealed document + audit certificate); a company signer countersigns; the executed document and certificate are stored and their hash bound into the grant record; a contract from a non-counsel-approved template or without a formed entity is stamped Non-binding sample and never shown as binding (D-006).\",\"falsifier\":\"A contract is generated outside the registry, shown as binding while the template is unapproved or no entity exists, finalized without countersignature, or the stored hash does not match the executed document.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"api\",\"db\",\"integration\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit tests for template rendering and the binding gate; adapter contract tests against a Documenso sandbox (or recorded fixtures of its API) for create/sign/complete/webhook; hash binding asserted. Governing: D-002, D-006.\\n\\nBinding-gate falsifier detectors: packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/contract-templates.test.ts, SPEC-P-001 — an unapproved template yields a Non-binding sample > the gate stamps a contract whose template has no counsel approval, even with a formed entity; packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/contract-templates.integration.test.ts, SPEC-P-001-B — an approved template without a formed entity is stamped Non-binding sample > approved template, no issuing entity → stamped, reason no_formed_entity. These supplement the existing contracts-esign unit/integration check; require both refusal branches and unchanged Non-binding sample output. Live provider signing, certificate identity and independent stored/provider hash equality also require the isolated R-9 native journey; tree tests alone do not establish the live plane.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/contracts-esign.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/contracts-esign.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Onboarding.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi wants new hires brought on end to end.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:0\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:4\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"After signature: identity verification and uniqueness, wallet binding (cupboard:bind-wallet), the hire governance proposal (register + grant), on-chain terms acceptance, DAO membership admission, and an onboarding checklist; each step's status is visible.\",\"falsifier\":\"Onboarding completes with an unbound wallet, without an executed hire proposal, without terms acceptance, or the checklist misreports a step.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"api\",\"chain\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration test over the onboarding orchestrator with test-chain runtime and bind-wallet; asserts ordering and refusals.\\n\\nThe live plane also requires the maintained R-9 isolated native case packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/native.e2e.test.ts > P012 actual native hiring journey > creates, approves, signs, votes, accepts and admits one candidate, then reads People, org and cap table, with canonical collected/passed ledger metadata, signed V2 transaction evidence, bound-wallet and admission proof. Governing: D-004.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/engagement-changes.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/onboarding.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/pot/hiring.test.ts\",\"apps/operator-vite/src/components/dao/people/EngagementViews.test.tsx\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Org view.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi asked for a GUI to view the whole organization: members, profiles, equity; everyone sees everyone's equity.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:0\",\"session_turn:claude:71aa78d4-20ec-4d0d-abcd-f557bd1ab847:14\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The DAO Workbench has People directory, profile pages, org chart from reporting lines, and a cap table (per-person shares, grants committed/earned/claimed/unvested, return entitlements, % owned, fully diluted) read from chain, plus a My equity view; every member sees everyone's equity (D-001) and pay terms only for self and admins (D-005); selection/view state lives in the URL (nuqs).\",\"falsifier\":\"A member cannot see another member's equity, pay terms leak to non-admins, the cap table disagrees with chain reads, or view state is held in useState.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"ui\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Component tests for directory, profile, org chart and cap table with visibility fixtures; headless Tauri check of the People tab.\\n\\nFor URL-owned selection state, use the maintained directory/profile/org/cap URL restore and write round-trip cases as the behavioral detector: a selected view must survive reconstruction from its URL and changes must update the URL. Inspect the nuqs state owner when classifying an internal useState drift; local transient form fields are outside selection state. A source-text identifier grep alone does not establish this bar. Preserve server-authorized pay fixtures and failed-chain-read refusal evidence.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator-vite/src/components/dao/people/PeopleViews.test.tsx\",\"apps/operator/e2e/dao-hr-people-views.spec.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Verification.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Avi asked to carry the plan to shipped status.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:95a8fd78-329b-4ee6-a1ba-f4d361ba439c:3\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Suite tests pass; an isolated headless desktop journey hires a person end to end on the test chain with Documenso in sandbox mode and shows them in the directory and cap table; independent grading passes before ship.\",\"falsifier\":\"The journey is skipped, runs against live state, or any step is stubbed out of the UI path.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"e2e\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh with VERIFY_TAURI_ISOLATED_DB=1 driving the hire journey; evidence recorded on the plan.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/native.e2e.test.ts\"],\"testName\":\"P012 actual native hiring journey > creates, approves, signs, votes, accepts and admits one candidate, then reads People, org and cap table\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nExtend, don't fork: the DAO Workbench (dao-workbench-management-2026-10-08) for all screens; the CRM person record for profiles; the existing equity contracts, pot:equity and cupboard:bind-wallet for chain work; existing DAO governance proposals for approvals; Postgres (migrations) for policy, offers, contract records. E-signature through a maintained provider behind one adapter (O-1), never a hand-rolled signature scheme; wallet signatures stay for on-chain acceptance only.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002, P-012 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003, P-012 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005, P-012 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-006, P-012 | live |\n| R-6 | P-007, P-012 | live |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012 | live |\n| R-9 | P-012 | live |\n\n## Open choices for Avi\n\nAll resolved (2026-10-11):\n- **O-1 E-signature provider** → Documenso, self-hosted (D-002).\n- **O-2 Equity payouts** → no vote; admin-set rate and cadence, triggered when due, under immutable ceilings (D-004).\n- **O-3 Hire approval** → a full member vote per hire (D-004).\n- **O-4 Cash pay** → pay terms recorded on offers and contracts; disbursement deferred until the company exists (D-005).\n- **O-5 Visibility** → everyone sees everyone's equity (D-001).\n- **O-6 Who we hire** → employees and contractors (D-003).\n\n## Owner-gated prerequisites\n\nCompany formed and bank accounts (agent-economy-flywheel-2026-08-30 P-045); counsel's legal brief (same plan, P-002); counsel-approved templates (P-001 here). Until these exist, everything runs on test chain + e-signature sandbox and is labeled non-binding.\n\n## Phase 0 — Legal prerequisites\n\n- **P-001** `done` Versioned contract-template registry per engagement type and jurisdiction (employee/contractor agreement, IP assignment, equity grant agreement, onboarding forms list) with merge fields, counsel-approval status and the binding gate; ships labelled non-binding sample templates (D-006). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008607 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — Foundation\n\n- **P-002** `done` Work profile on the shared person record, linked to DAO member identity and wallet (R-1). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008608 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Versioned equity + hiring policy settings with bounds, per-offer overrides, audit, and admin execution of chain-enforced values within immutable maxima, no vote (R-2, D-004). blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008609 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Equity contract version with vesting cliff, immutable return ceiling and minimum payout interval, admin-triggered due payouts with no vote, a bounded admin role per D-004, governance-only holder registration, grant creation and stopGrant, and a holder-only self-stop for resignation per D-008; real EVM tests including hostile calls (R-3). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008610 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Hiring\n\n- **P-005** `done` Hiring flow: roles, candidates, offers with share/% preview, approvals (R-4). blocked-by: P-003 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008611 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Contract generation from approved templates + e-signature adapter + countersignature + stored executed document bound to the grant (R-5). blocked-by: P-005 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008612 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Onboarding: identity, wallet binding, governance grant proposal, on-chain acceptance, membership admission, checklist (R-6). blocked-by: P-006, P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008613 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Amendments and offboarding (R-7). blocked-by: P-007 — note: ← WI-6554700010008614 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Org view\n\n- **P-009** `done` People directory + profile pages in the Workbench (R-8). blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008615 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Org chart from reporting lines (R-8). blocked-by: P-009 — note: ← WI-6554700010008616 completed (done)\n- **P-011** `done` Cap table + \"my equity\" from chain reads with visibility rules (R-8). blocked-by: P-009 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008617 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Verify and ship\n\n- **P-012** `todo` Suite tests + isolated desktop end-to-end hire journey on test chain with sandbox e-signature (R-9). blocked-by: P-008, P-011 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008618 released\n- **P-013** `todo` Acceptance rubric, independent grading, ship. blocked-by: P-012\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Everyone sees everyone's equity; hires are ongoing roles with regular pay, not per-project\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-11, directive #1675, interactive] Verbatim: \"Equity visibility: everyone sees everyone's,\" and \"I want regular work and regular payments. not per project\". Resolves O-5 = everyone sees everyone's equity (the cap table and profiles show every member's holdings to all members). Sets the engagement model: ongoing roles with regular, scheduled payments; per-project/bounty work stays out of scope. Still open: O-6 employee vs contractor (agent recommendation [inferred]: employees by default, because ongoing controlled work with regular pay is the legal profile of employment and misclassification is the main risk) and O-4 cash pay (regular cash pay to employees implies a payroll provider; US employees cannot be paid in equity alone).\n\n### D-002 — E-signature provider: Documenso (self-hosted)\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-11, directive #1676, interactive] Verbatim: \"okay lets go with Documenso\". Resolves O-1. P-006 integrates a self-hosted Documenso (AGPL-3.0 Community Edition, Postgres) behind one e-signature adapter. Follow-ups for P-006 [self-imposed]: obtain a trusted signing certificate (a self-signed one makes PDF readers warn); verify on a test install that Community embedded signing is free (unconfirmed, search-summary evidence only); keep Documenso unmodified or publish modifications per AGPL. Comparison evidence: WI-6554700010008422 comment 2026-10-11T14:43Z.\n\n### D-003 — Hire both employees and contractors\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-11, directive #1678, interactive] Verbatim: \"let's hire both employees and contractors\". Resolves O-6 = both, chosen per hire. Consequences [inferred, for counsel to confirm]: P-001 needs both an employment agreement and a contractor/consulting agreement (plus IP assignment for each); the offer flow (P-005) records engagement type per hire and applies the matching template, tax form and pay path; employees need cash wages with withholding (bears on O-4 payroll provider); contractors on ongoing retainers carry misclassification risk, so the offer flow should flag contractor offers whose terms look like employment (full-time, directed, open-ended).\n\n### D-004 — Member votes only for hire and fire; payouts, policy and amendments run without a vote\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-11, directive #1679, interactive] Verbatim: \"and voting should only happen for the hire/fire.\"\n\nMember votes (governance proposals) are used for exactly two things:\n- **Hire** — registering the hire and committing their equity grant. Resolves O-3 = a full member vote per hire (as the contracts do today).\n- **Fire** — ending an engagement: a proposal whose execution calls stopGrant (earned equity stays).\n\nResolves O-2: equity payouts need **no vote**. An admin sets the return rate and cadence; when a payout is due it can be triggered without a proposal; the contract's ceilings (10% per year, 30-day minimum interval) stay immutable.\n\n[inferred from \"only for hire/fire\"] Policy changes — including chain-enforced values such as the per-grant maximum — are executed by an authorized admin role within immutable contract maxima, audited, no vote. Equity-changing amendments are admin-executed within the per-grant limit, no vote. The admin role can never reduce earned equity, stop a grant (firing is vote-only), register a holder or create a grant outside a hire vote, or exceed the immutable ceilings — no admin seizure path.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-007, P-008\n\n### D-005 — Cash pay: pay terms recorded on every offer and contract; disbursement deferred until the company exists\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed — AUTO judgment under directive #1679, 2026-10-11] Resolves O-4. To honour D-001's \"regular work and regular payments\", every offer and contract records regular pay terms (amount, currency, cadence, engagement type) and the profile shows them to the person and admins only (equity visibility per D-001 is unchanged). Actual cash disbursement through a payroll provider is out of scope here: it needs a formed company and bank account (agent-economy-flywheel-2026-08-30 P-045), so it becomes a follow-up plan once those exist. No payroll adapter is built speculatively.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-009\n\n### D-006 — Legal templates: build the template registry and binding gate now; counsel approval is an owner follow-up, not a ship blocker\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed — AUTO judgment under directive #1679, 2026-10-11] P-001 (counsel-approved templates) cannot be produced by software. Rescoped: this plan builds the software side — a versioned template registry per engagement type (employee / contractor, D-003) and jurisdiction, merge fields, a counsel-approval status per template version, and a binding gate. It ships with clearly labelled sample templates that are NOT counsel-approved. A contract generated from an unapproved template, or without a formed issuing entity, is stamped \"Non-binding sample\" and the product never presents it as binding (R-5). Getting counsel to approve real templates is filed as its own owner-side work-item. This matches the plan's existing legal prerequisites: everything runs on test chain + e-signature sandbox, labelled non-binding, until those exist.\nRelated: P-001, P-006\n\n### D-007 — Hire order: the contract is signed before the vote but only takes effect when the hire proposal passes\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed — AUTO judgment under directive #1679, 2026-10-11, resolving bar critique conv-request-ac639974 X-1] The hire flow is: offer drafted → internal approval by an admin who is not the offer's author → contract generated from the offer and signed by both parties, carrying a condition precedent (\"effective only upon passage of the DAO hire proposal\") → hire governance proposal (the ONE vote, D-004) whose execution registers the holder and commits the equity grant → contract status moves signed → binding only when that proposal executes. If the proposal is rejected or expires, the contract moves to lapsed and is never presented as binding. Rationale: members vote on a signed, concrete offer, the on-chain grant is only ever created for someone who has signed, and a failed vote leaves no binding obligation. The no-entity / unapproved-template stamp (D-006) still applies on top: a contract can be binding only if it is condition-satisfied AND counsel-approved AND issued by a formed entity. Membership admission is a consequence of the passed hire proposal, never a second vote.\nRelated: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-012\n\n### D-008 — Resignation needs no vote: the holder can stop only their own grant\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed — AUTO judgment under directive #1679, 2026-10-11, resolving bar critique conv-request-ac639974 R-7(b)] D-004 makes the fire proposal the only way to end someone else's engagement, and stopGrant is governance-only. Without a second path nobody could leave without a vote, which contradicts 'voting only for hire/fire' (a resignation is neither). The equity contract therefore gains a holder-only self-stop: the holder can stop vesting on their OWN grant (earned equity stays); no admin or third party can call it, so it adds no seizure path. Product: a person resigns from their profile, which calls the self-stop, records the end, and runs the same offboarding (access revoked, records retained). Firing is unchanged (fire proposal → stopGrant).\nRelated: P-004, P-008\n\n### D-009 — Bar-critique findings are discharged by atomic spec clauses; BAR text and evidence planes stay as seeded\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed — AUTO judgment under owner directive #1679] Two independent bar critiques (C1 conv-request-ac639974, C2 conv-request-8078e32f) found the 9 BARs under-specified. Rewriting the BAR conditions was refused (rubrics:amend: acceptance_bar_non_atomic_projection — a meaning-changed BAR must be one observable behavior). So every accepted finding now lives as ONE atomic, falsifiable spec clause on the implementing item: 69 new clauses SPEC-P-001-A..SPEC-P-012-E, plus revised SPEC-P-008 r2 (firing needs a passed fire proposal; resignation needs no vote, D-008) and SPEC-P-009 r2 (the directory lists members without a work profile). Implementers and graders treat those clauses as the binding detail behind R-1..R-9. Also accepted: the P-004 text now says immutable return ceiling, admin-triggered due payouts, governance-only register/create/stopGrant, and holder-only self-stop; R-9 maps to P-012 only, because P-013 is the ship process, not an implementation. DECLINED: moving R-5/R-6/R-8 from the live to the tree plane. Live is the stronger bar, and the P-012 headless journey, already mapped to all three, supplies it. A plane change would also need a reviewed BAR amendment for no gain. DECLINED: pinning evidenceRuntime desktop-shell on R-9 (also a reviewed amendment). SPEC-P-012-D requires the journey evidence to name desktop-shell, the Documenso sandbox and the test chain as runtime units. Disposition source: .papercusp/scratch/dao-hr-fleet/build-specs.mjs.\n\n### D-010 — Execution route: leader implements directly (claim-by-id) instead of a headless fleet, while papercusp stop-the-line holds\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed, AUTO mode, su-3daacab2 2026-10-11] The owner directive #1679 (\"carry it to shipped status\") names no route; the earlier headless-fleet x3 route was this session's own AUTO choice, not an owner choice. Measured 16:40Z: plans:start / fleet:launch-on-plan refused admission_refused claimFloors=3 because the ONLY failing claim-floor leg is stopTheLineExclusionSql (papercusp gate-red-streak open >24h, gate held-live by su-521c53be on WI-10006055; P-013/D-012 withholds non-repair self-select). Per the policy's own exemption (a leader can dispatch BY ID), the leader claimed the ready rows by id (WI-6554700010008607 P-001, WI-6554700010008608 P-002, WI-6554700010008610 P-004) and plans:start then passed (caller-held acknowledgement). Route: the leader implements items directly in dependency order (critical path P-002 -> P-003 -> P-005 -> P-006 -> P-007 -> P-008 -> P-012 -> P-013), claiming each by id. Why not a fleet now: the throttle's intent (do not pile non-repair work onto a red line), two pool accounts at 0.93/0.98 7d utilization with projected exhaustion, and critical-path depth 8 bounding fleet parallelism to width<=3. Revisit (fleet via coord:dispatch workItemIds) once the papercusp gate greens and stop-the-line lifts. Diagnosability defect filed: EI-25701810217121737.\n\n### D-011 — DAO HR state lives in dedicated dao_hr_* tables keyed to the PER- person; enterprise-data-sources D-011 does not apply\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed — AUTO judgment under owner directive #1679, su-3daacab2, while implementing P-002 / WI-6554700010008608]\n\nQuestion: enterprise-data-sources-2026-10-01#D-011 (owner ruling: 'no records table') + #D-018 say a new ENTITY datatype's instances stay in harness_shared.work_items as nature=record rows. Does that forbid a dedicated table for HR work profiles (and the later offer/contract/grant state)?\n\nRuling: no. D-011 scopes INSTANCES OF INGESTED DATATYPES (DSR-/DSE- rows minted by the data-source sinks, which need search/embeddings/federation keyed on work_items). DAO HR state is internal operational state of the DAO, not an ingested record: it carries relational invariants a work_items payload cannot enforce (one profile per (DAO, person); one DAO member identity per DAO; onboarding finished only with a verified wallet link; manager links between persons; pay terms all-or-nothing). The repo precedent for such state is a dedicated harness_shared table (hive memberships, personal_vault_import_jobs).\n\nWhat stays on the shared record (R-1): the PERSON is the canonical PER- entity in harness_shared.work_items (item_kind='person'). dao_hr_* tables store only work facts plus the PER- id (the merge survivor, resolved via getCanonicalEntity) and never a name, email, phone or postal address. The dao-hr schema guard (packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/schema-guard.ts, SPEC-P-002-B) fails any dao-hr migration that adds a contact column to a table other than the person record, so later items (P-001 template registry, P-003 offers, P-004 grants) must name descriptive columns title/label/key, never *_name/*email*/*phone*/postal address.\n\nFirst instance: migration 1456-dao-hr-work-profiles (harness_shared.dao_hr_work_profiles).\n\n### D-012 — DAO HR admins are a per-DAO roster of person records; a formed issuing entity is an admin-recorded row; both live in dao_hr_* tables\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self-imposed — AUTO judgment under owner directive #1679, su-3daacab2, while implementing P-001 / WI-6554700010008607]\n\nQuestion: SPEC-P-001-E needs a server-side 'is this actor an admin' check and SPEC-P-001-B needs a 'formed issuing entity' fact. Neither exists in operator-core: dao-launch.ts founders/legal sections are drafts that 'never confer membership', and the company formation itself is agent-economy-flywheel-2026-08-30 P-045 (not built).\n\nRuling: (1) harness_shared.dao_hr_admins is the DAO HR admin roster: (workspace, dao_slug, person_id PER-). An admin is a shared person record (R-1, D-011). The first admin of a DAO is seeded only by an operator surface (grantDaoHrAdmin { bootstrapOperator }), refused once a roster exists; later grants need an existing admin. P-003 (policy admin), P-005 (offer approval by a non-author admin, D-007) and P-006 reuse this roster — do not add a second admin concept. The on-chain bounded admin role (D-004, P-004) is a separate contract role; P-007/P-008 map roster admins to it. (2) harness_shared.dao_hr_issuing_entities holds at most one formed company per DAO (registered title, jurisdiction, registration reference, formed date), recorded by a roster admin. No row = no formed entity = every contract stamped Non-binding sample (D-006). When agent-economy P-045 ships a company record, this row becomes a projection of it rather than a second source. (3) Column names avoid *_name (registered_title, approver_ref) so the dao-hr schema guard (R-1) stays strict.\n\nImplemented in migration 1457-dao-hr-contract-templates.sql and packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/contract-templates.ts.\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-005, P-006, D-004, D-006, D-007, D-011\nRelated: P-001, P-003, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-013 — V2 equity governance surface: five vote-gated functions, five bounded admin functions, everything else caller-scoped\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[self-imposed — AUTO judgment under owner directive #1679, su-3daacab2, while implementing P-004 / WI-6554700010008610; realizes D-004 and D-008 in code]\n\nThe new contract version (packages/operator-core/lib/equity/contracts/PapercuspEquityV2.sol + EquityGovernorV2.sol) fixes who can call what. The single source is packages/operator-core/lib/equity/v2-function-classes.ts; equity-v2.test.ts asserts it matches the compiled ABI exactly.\n\n1. Vote required (callable only by the timelock after a passed member proposal): registerHolder and commitGrant (the hire), stopGrant (the fire; earned equity stays), setEligibility (legal freeze/restore), replaceAdmin (replace a lost or compromised admin). The governor refuses any proposal whose call is not one of these, so routine admin work can never be put to a vote and a vote can never do anything else.\n2. Admin, no vote (bounded): transferAdmin, setGrantLimit (prospective, at most the immutable maxGrantLimit = cap/10), setReturnPolicy (rate <= ANNUAL_RETURN_CAP_BPS = 1000, i.e. 10% per 365 days; interval between MIN_RETURN_INTERVAL = 30 days and MAX_RETURN_INTERVAL = 365 days), raiseGrant (unvested grant only, within the per-grant limit; earned equity can only grow), triggerPayout (only when due and within the rolling 365-day ceiling).\n3. Caller-scoped (anyone, but only their own position): claimGrant, resignGrant (D-008 self-stop; earned equity stays), claimReturn, acceptTerms, recovery, transfers and delegation (eligible parties only). activateGenesis and bindGovernance are issuer-bootstrap-only, once.\n\nThe return ceiling and minimum interval are compile-time constants with no setter. Grants carry a cliff: nothing is earned before it. The V1 contracts stay deployed and untouched; inspectEquity still reads V1 only (V2 inspection belongs to P-011).\n\n### D-014 — AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-001 is proven by the P-006 live journey; P-001 stays open until then\nDate: 2026-10-11\nDate: 2026-10-11 [self-imposed — AUTO judgment under owner directive #1679, su-3daacab2, while closing P-001 / WI-6554700010008607]\n\nObservation: work_items:complete on P-001 was refused because AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-001@2 (bar R-5, evidencePlane live, layers integration+unit) has no bound evidence. All seven tree-plane clauses SPEC-P-001, -A..-F pass (plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy 7/7, bindings 37679-37694 and 37759-37762).\n\nRuling: bar R-5 describes the whole contract journey (registry generation, Documenso signing, company countersignature, executed document + certificate stored with its hash bound into the grant, Non-binding sample stamping). P-001 delivers only the registry half and exposes no surface on a running operator; generation and signing reach a live surface in P-006, which carries its own copy AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-006@2. A live-plane binding on P-001 now would claim an observation that did not happen. So: P-001 is implementation-complete but stays open; when P-006 exposes contract generation on a running operator, ONE live observation of that journey (an unapproved template / no formed entity renders as Non-binding sample; an approved template with an entity renders binding from the registry) is bound to BOTH AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-001 and AUTO-BAR-R-5-P-006, and P-001 closes then. Nothing is blocked by this: no item depends on P-001.\n\nDo not edit packages/operator-core/lib/dao-hr/contract-templates.ts in the meantime unless a defect is found (its tree bindings are fingerprinted).\n\n### D-015 — A hire proposal reserves before terms acceptance; hire_passed vesting anchors to execution\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[self-imposed, existing AUTO/self scope].\n\nMeasured: equity-policy.ts START_RULES includes hire_passed, but PapercuspEquityV2.commitGrant stores literal start/cliff/end and calls _requireEligible, which includes terms acceptance. EVM regression /tmp/daohr-p007-contract-before.log proves atomic registerHolder+commitGrant reverts for a new candidate. Corrected queued-execution timing probe /tmp/daohr-p007-timing-before.log proves a start0 grant stores start0 rather than execution timestamp1800950543 (test input). These prevent R6's single hire vote followed by terms acceptance and cannot reflect hire_passed chosen before execution. Extend existing commitGrant, preserving ABI and D013 caller classes: start0 denotes execution block timestamp, with cliff/end supplied as relative seconds; validate durations before converting. Absolute schedules still use nonzero start. An eligible registered holder may receive a reserved grant before acceptance; claimGrant and every issuance/transfer gate retain _requireEligible, and candidate alone accepts issuer terms. Thus one vote registers+reserves, then candidate accepts, then product membership admission follows verified proof; no second proposal. P007 transaction builder must derive start_date/contract_signed as absolute schedules and hire_passed as relative, and verify stored grant times against execution receipt's block. Reuse existing contract/action/state surfaces; no new vote path or parallel grant system.\nRelated: P-004, P-007\n\n### D-016 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-12\nAmendment-Id: daohr-existing-test-mapping-r3-v1-apply\nRequest-Hash: 86f0e53995855d881634a4a63876b495ca4a950f11beece9f079572ed36e2d1e\nActor: su-d14d0d3e-762b-4661-a73b-473c8cfdb422\nReason: Replace nonexistent check.files R2/R4/R7 with the actual maintained implementation test files; add the existing unit test to R6. This records evidence locations without changing requirements, BARs, execution route or acceptance criteria.\nRelated: P-012, P-013\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"degradation-signals-on-condition-rail-2026-10-11","title":"Every silent fallback raises a condition: generic degradation detector + system-wide audit of the watchdog rail","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-11","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Every silent fallback raises a condition: generic degradation detector + system-wide audit of the watchdog rail\nslug: degradation-signals-on-condition-rail-2026-10-11\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-11\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Goal\n\nAny mechanism that silently falls back or fails open, and any detector that notices a failure, reports through one durable, generic path that raises a condition on the existing alarm rail. An agent then gets an auto-filed work item, and the item closes itself when the signal recovers. Nobody has to ask. The primitive and watchdog are generic for any mechanism. The audit, migration and guard cover the five rail-bypass classes R-4 names; a sixth class needs a plan amendment (D-006).\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** The owner, who should not discover silent degradations by asking; and every agent, who should be handed an owned work item instead of finding the problem in a log.\n\n**Problem.** On 2026-10-11 the green-checkpoint gate reused 0 of ~7,689 test files on the frozen repair head (run 762a13a6). The selector expected pass proofs in format v3 and the frozen candidate recorded v2 (root cause: WI-6554700010008589, owned by su-521c53be). Nothing alarmed. The only record was `TARGETED_TEST_PASS_REUSE ... reused=0 otherRunner=6646` text in one run log. The structured record `gate_health.testPassReuse` is written only from full-suite runs, so it was 9 days stale (last written 2026-10-02, the last green). Its alarms cover soundness and recorder write failures, not yield. It was the sixth silent reuse collapse in a month (EI-23170536217137589, WI-10003597, EI-24538088938561684, WI-10004617, EI-25182316675000761, WI-6554700010008589), each found by hand. An agent noticed \"no pass reuse\" at 15:06Z the same day and recorded it as a planning fact (observation EI-25695997838749406).\n\nThe platform already has a failure-surfacing rail: `broadcastSevereEvent` (condition-keyed alarm to every agent plus a routed wake to the owner, ~28 producer files), `coord:conditions` (open/resolved fold), `condition-staleness-alarm` (re-alarms stale, clears verified-healthy), the condition bridge (WI-7272: an actionable condition becomes one work item, closed on resolve), `alarm-attention.ts` (owner toast with cooldown) and `signal-actor-registry.ts` (every signal needs an acting consumer). The gap is that many failure signals never enter it: they stay as log text, owner-only toasts (~63 files call `notifyAttention`), health-panel flags, or bespoke watchdogs. The one existing rate-based degradation primitive (`libs/generic/search/src/leg-health.ts`) is an in-process 512-sample ring, non-durable and per-process (WI-39438), so it cannot see decisions made in a child process like the gate's test runner.\n\n**Outcome.** (1) A durable, cross-process primitive records each fail-open decision (eligible, applied, reason) per mechanism. (2) One generic watchdog turns a collapsed rate into a `degraded:<mechanism>:<reason>` condition on the existing rail, which auto-files one work item and auto-closes it on recovery. (3) Gate pass reuse, in full-suite and repair rounds, is the first producer. (4) A system-wide audit inventories every failure/degradation signal that bypasses the rail, and each is migrated or dispositioned with a reason. (5) A shrink-only guard stops new bypasses.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- Detecting arbitrary failures with zero instrumentation. Each mechanism still makes one recording call; the guard makes forgetting it visible.\n- Fixing the proof-format mismatch itself (WI-6554700010008589, su-521c53be).\n- Changing what the gate reuses or its soundness rules.\n- A second delivery path. Everything rides `broadcastSevereEvent` and the condition bridge.\n\n**Source turns.**\n- `session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:0` (owner, 2026-10-11 15:45Z): \"was this failure logged anywhere? shouldnt have a failure like this been logged somehwere and our system have a way for an agent to automatically detect and fix the issue\"\n- AskUserQuestion answer in the same session (~15:59Z): \"Are you adding a detector for this specific issue or a generic detector for all failures? Can we make this generic? Do we have existing infra for detecting failures and surfacing them? Is this re-using that?\"\n- AskUserQuestion answer (~16:01Z): chose the generic option, then \"also audit an entire system for places where we aren't using the watchdog system like this but should be. Make this plan a plan to fix all these places. Write it into a plan and then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped status yourself now\"; route: \"Me, this session\".\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. A gate repair round reuses 0 of 6,646 candidates because every proof is `otherRunner`. Within one watchdog tick a `degraded:gate-pass-reuse:<task>:otherRunner` condition opens, every agent sees it, and one work item is filed. When reuse recovers, the condition resolves and the item closes.\n2. A watchdog that today only toasts the owner via `notifyAttention` also raises a condition, so an agent owns the problem even when the owner is away.\n3. A new module adds a fail-open branch or an owner-only alarm without the rail. The guard fails the build with a message naming the primitive to use.\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Avi and the agents operating Papercusp: failures should become actionable work without a human first finding a log.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Silent fail-open decisions and detector signals can bypass the existing condition rail. Gate repair-round pass reuse exposed this gap: a collapsed reuse rate was log-only and the last structured full-suite health record did not describe the repair round.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Record eligible/applied decisions durably across processes; detect rate collapse generically; raise and recover exact conditions through the existing actionable-condition bridge; inventory, migrate and guard the five agreed bypass classes.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Fix the separate reuse proof-format defect WI-6554700010008589.\",\n    \"Change reuse soundness or selection policy.\",\n    \"Detect uninstrumented arbitrary failures.\",\n    \"Add a parallel delivery or scheduling system.\",\n    \"Expand the five audit classes without a reviewed plan amendment.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:0\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:7\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:12\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Make the detector generic, reuse existing failure infrastructure, audit and fix system-wide bypasses, and carry the approved self/AUTO route to shipment.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:7\",\n        \"session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:12\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"observed-fact\",\n      \"text\": \"The existing condition-keyed broadcast, condition fold and actionable-condition bridge supply the delivery path; bespoke owner-only escalations do not supply it.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"D-002\",\n        \"D-005\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"product-choice\",\n      \"text\": \"Audit and migration cover the five R-4 classes with immutable seed row identities and independently reviewed amendments.\",\n      \"decisionRef\": \"D-006\",\n      \"material\": true,\n      \"resolved\": true\n    }\n  ],\n  \"scenarios\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-001\",\n      \"title\": \"A repair or full-suite reuse round collapses\",\n      \"kind\": \"normal\",\n      \"trigger\": \"Eligible gate tasks reject pass proofs, including an all-otherRunner round.\",\n      \"action\": \"Record each decision, summarize the durable task-scoped window and sweep the registered mechanism.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"The exact degraded:gate-pass-reuse:<task>:<reason> condition opens and the real bridge creates one work item.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-3\",\n        \"R-7\",\n        \"R-8\",\n        \"R-10\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-002\",\n      \"title\": \"Repeated detection and measured recovery\",\n      \"kind\": \"recovery\",\n      \"trigger\": \"Repeated sweeps find the same collapse, followed by enough measured applied decisions.\",\n      \"action\": \"Deduplicate by exact condition key and resolve at the pinned recovery threshold.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"One work item remains open during the failure and becomes terminal after verified recovery.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-7\",\n        \"R-8\",\n        \"R-11\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-003\",\n      \"title\": \"A detector pages while Avi is away\",\n      \"kind\": \"failure\",\n      \"trigger\": \"An inventoried owner-only alarm or condition-less watchdog measures a breach.\",\n      \"action\": \"The original caller raises its own keyed condition independently of notification cooldown, then resolves only on measured recovery.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Agents can act without waiting for an owner page; unknown measurements preserve the condition.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-4\",\n        \"R-5\",\n        \"R-11\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-004\",\n      \"title\": \"A mechanism fails open or a watchdog heals\",\n      \"kind\": \"failure\",\n      \"trigger\": \"An inventoried fallback or actuating watchdog takes its fallback/heal path.\",\n      \"action\": \"Record the registered mechanism, scope, eligible/applied counts and actual reason; record primary/non-heal success too.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Persistent fallback/heal behavior becomes a generic degradation condition and subsequent healthy measurements enable recovery.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-5\",\n        \"R-9\",\n        \"R-10\",\n        \"R-13\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-005\",\n      \"title\": \"Small samples and borderline rates\",\n      \"kind\": \"boundary\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A window has19rather than20eligible decisions, rate0.21rather than0.20, recovery0.49rather than0.50, or dominant reason share0.79rather than0.80.\",\n      \"action\": \"Apply the D-006 defaults and explicit registered mechanism overrides.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Insufficient/noncollapsed samples do not open; sub-recovery rates do not resolve; a nondominant reason keys as mixed.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-7\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-006\",\n      \"title\": \"Another process reads a decision after restart\",\n      \"kind\": \"concurrency\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A child process writes a fail-open decision and another process reads the trailing window.\",\n      \"action\": \"Use the existing host datastore through the durable batched observation writer/reader.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Counts and reasons remain readable across processes; retention and window cutoffs exclude expired rows.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-12\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-007\",\n      \"title\": \"The observation store fails\",\n      \"kind\": \"failure\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A batched observation insert rejects.\",\n      \"action\": \"Keep the caller decision path best effort and count the lost rows.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"The recording failure is observable without throwing into the mechanism's decision.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-14\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-008\",\n      \"title\": \"A new bypass or unreviewed exclusion appears\",\n      \"kind\": \"boundary\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A new R-4site bypasses the rail or an immutable seed row is deleted/relabelled without a reviewed amendment.\",\n      \"action\": \"Run site-granular inventory, independent token census, immutable manifest and shrink-only lint controls.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Verification fails with the exact site identity; migrating a sibling site cannot hide it.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-4\",\n        \"R-5\",\n        \"R-6\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-009\",\n      \"title\": \"Independent completion acceptance\",\n      \"kind\": \"authorization\",\n      \"trigger\": \"Implementation reports completion of all agreed seed migration rows.\",\n      \"action\": \"Use strict live-seed acceptance per D-076, real original-producer cases, independent BAR vetting/grading and final shipment evidence.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Incremental passing guards cannot certify unfinished rows; this implementer cannot substitute for independent acceptance.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-4\",\n        \"R-5\",\n \"Existing acceptance and amendment reviewer boundaries remain binding; the structured brief adds no self-approval route.\",\n      \"scenarioIds\": [\n        \"SC-008\",\n        \"SC-009\"\n does not introduce provider secrets, phone validation or a new outward publishing path.\",\n      \"scenarioIds\": []\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Fail-open decisions are recorded durably and readable across processes.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Owner asked for a generic detector that reuses existing failure infrastructure; the gate's reuse decision happens in a child process that the in-process leg-health ring cannot see.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A fail-open observation (mechanism, eligible, applied, reason) recorded from one process is returned by the trailing-window reader in another process, with the applied rate and per-reason counts.\",\"falsifier\":\"The reader returns no data for a sample written by a separate process, or the window summary miscounts reasons in the unit fixture.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"degradation-signals\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit tests for the window summariser; an integration test writes samples through the public writer and reads them back through the reader against real Postgres.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/degradation/fallback-observations.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/degradation/fallback-observations.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — A collapsed rate opens a condition on the existing rail, auto-files one work item, and resolves on recovery.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Owner asked that the system detect such failures automatically and route them to an agent, reusing the existing watchdog infrastructure.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:a47806eb-937c-4344-a587-6fabf68a2f48:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"When a registered mechanism's trailing window holds at least its minimum eligible count (default 20) at an applied rate at or below its collapse threshold (default 0.2), repeated watchdog sweeps leave exactly one open work item for the condition key degraded:<mechanism>[:<scope>]:<reason> through the real condition bridge, which closes it once the rate reaches the recovery threshold (default 0.5).\",\"falsifier\":\"Three sweeps over a collapsed window leave zero or several open work items, a recovered window leaves the item open, a window with 19 eligible or a 0.21 applied rate opens a condition, or removing the degraded: catalog entry leaves the integration test tests drive the pure decision function at the pinned defaults (19 versus 20 eligible, 0.20 versus 0.21 applied rate, 0.49 versus 0.50 recovery). Durable in Postgres (one new table via the migration allocator), because the gate's decisions are made in child processes and the existing leg-health ring is per-process. Writers are best-effort and batched per run so a hot path is never slowed. Retention is bounded.\n- **Watchdog (R-2).** One periodic sweep over registered mechanisms. A pure decision function decides open/resolve from the window (minimum sample floor, collapse threshold, dominant-reason share). It emits through `broadcastSevereEvent` with `conditionKey: degraded:<mechanism>:<reason>` and resolves through the existing resolution call. `degraded:` is added to `coord/actionable-conditions.ts`. Registered in `signal-actor-registry.ts`. Scheduled as a declared ephemeral trigger or managed interval, never a bare setInterval.\n- **Gate reuse producer (R-3).** `scripts/lib/targeted-task-reuse.mjs` and `scripts/lib/test-pass-reuse.mjs` record per task: eligible = candidates, applied = reused, reason = dominant rejection bucket or off reason. Starts after su-521c53be's edit to the same file lands.\n- **Audit (R-4).** A measuring script (`scripts/lib/condition-rail-inventory.mjs`), not a hand grep, enumerates the five classes and emits a machine-readable list. Results and dispositions go in this plan; migrate items are added per cluster.\n- **Guard (R-6).** The same script in lint mode against a shrink-only baseline.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-017 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-005, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-014 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-015 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-002 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Primitive, watchdog, first producer, audit\n\n- **P-001** `done` Audit (R-4): build the measuring inventory script for the five classes with a positive control per class, run it over the tree, record per-site dispositions in this plan, and add one migrate item per cluster. — note: Inventory built and run: scanner scripts/lib/condition-rail-inventory.mjs (+ .d.mts), CLI scripts/condition-rail-inventory.mjs, dispositions scripts/lib/condition-rail-dispositions.mjs. 307 sites over 10191 files, all dispositioned (243 migrate across P-005, P-007..P-015; 64 not-applicable with reasons); --check exits 0 with 0 undispositioned and 0 stale. Done when each of the 12 seed-manifest row IDs routed to P-015 has a passing coverage-matrix case asserting both observation shapes under a mechanism registered with the degradation watchdog (R-13, R-11). blocked-by: P-002, P-003 — note: ← WI-6554700010008688 released\n- **P-017** `todo` Harden the inventory (R-4, R-5): site-granular on-rail predicate (rail call in the site's own enclosing function, call position only), per-site stable row IDs (class|file|enclosing symbol|ordinal), the 307-row seed pinned as an immutable manifest at docs/evidence/condition-rail-inventory-seed-2026-10-11.json with a per-row route (condition|observation) and an amendment log (reason + reviewer ref), mutation fixtures for every recognised syntactic form plus mixed-file and variable-named-conditionKey controls, a git-grep census reconciliation test, a manifest test (a row leaves only through an amendment-log entry whose reviewer ref differs from its author), a generated coverage matrix (manifest row ID -> table-driven test case) that fails on any row whose route is missing or not condition|observation and on any migrate row whose owning item is done but lacks a passing case, honouring the amendment log exactly as the manifest test does, and stale dispositions failing --check (D-006). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010008689 blocker cleared\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Fallback observations are durable in Postgres, not an in-process ring\nDate: 2026-10-11\nThe gate's reuse decisions run in child processes (affected-tests / gate-cli), and the only existing rate primitive, libs/generic/search/src/leg-health.ts, is a per-process 512-sample in-memory ring (WI-39438). A durable PG table, written through a best-effort batched writer, is the only store the watchdog can read across processes and restarts. Considered and rejected: extending the leg-health ring (cannot cross processes); parsing gate log lines (fragile; that is the current failure).\n\n### D-002 — No new delivery path: degradations ride broadcastSevereEvent and the condition bridge\nDate: 2026-10-11\nConditions use conditionKey degraded:<mechanism>:<reason> through broadcastSevereEvent and its resolution call; the degraded: prefix joins coord/actionable-conditions.ts so the WI-7272 bridge files and closes one work item per key; owner toasts, where wanted, go through alarm-attention.ts. The owner explicitly asked whether this reuses existing infra (AskUserQuestion answer, 2026-10-11 ~15:59Z). Considered and rejected: treating any openEscalation as on-rail (it would hide the 93 sites this plan exists to close).\n\n### D-006 — BAR critique round 2: scope the Goal to the five classes, make the inventory site-granular with a pinned row-ID manifest, pin thresholds, and quantify every migrate clause over its row IDs\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: two independent bar-critique consults on rubric rev 3. conv-request-86f0 (answer thread-post 1174665, su-f831f830) and conv-request-d58ea0b7 (answer thread-post 1174670, su-36f75511). Both returned blocking defects. Ruling [self, plan author, 2026-10-11]:\n\n1. **Goal scope.** The primitive and watchdog are generic for any mechanism. The audit, migration and guard cover the five rail-bypass classes R-4 enumerates: owner-only alarms without a conditionKey, log-only fail-open decisions, condition-less health flags, bespoke rate watchdogs, and signal-actor-registry waivers. A sixth class needs a plan amendment. It does not count as an implicit miss.\n2. **The inventory is site-granular and pinned.** A site is on-rail only if the rail call sits in its own enclosing function. File-wide matches and token matches within ±40 lines no longer count; the token must be in call position, not a variable name. The 307-site audit becomes an immutable seed manifest (docs/evidence/condition-rail-inventory-seed-2026-10-11.json) with a stable row ID per site (class|file|enclosing symbol|ordinal) and a per-row route (condition|observation). A row can leave only through an amendment-log entry giving a reason and a reviewer ref. A census reconciliation ties each scanner row to an independent enumerator (a literal git grep over each class's call tokens). Every syntactic form the scanner recognises has a mutation fixture. Stale dispositions fail the check. Implemented by P-017.\n3. **Thresholds are pinned defaults.** minEligible 20 per trailing window; collapse at applied/eligible <= 0.2; recovery at >= 0.5; dominant-reason share >= 0.8 (else the key's reason is `mixed`). A mechanism can override these at registration. Mechanisms register once. An observation's scope partitions windows, and conditionKey = degraded:<mechanism>[:<scope>]:<reason>. Gate pass reuse is mechanism gate-pass-reuse with scope = task, which needs no per-task registration.\n4. **End-to-end proof uses the real bridge.** R-2 adds an integration test against real Postgres and the real actionable-condition bridge: repeated broadcasts yield one condition_key and one work item, closed after recovery. R-8 uses that test as its pickup evidence. R-3 composes the recorder, window, decision and conditionKey for both round types.\n5. **Migrate clauses quantify over row IDs.** Each P-007..P-015 clause covers every manifest row ID assigned to it. Condition-route rows assert open AND resolve (R-11). Observation-route rows assert an observation for a mechanism registered with the watchdog (R-13). A generated coverage matrix (row ID → table-driven test case) fails on any migrate row lacking a case. P-015: a non-heal tick records eligible=1, applied=1 and a heal records eligible=1, applied=0, reason=<heal kind>. P-007 keys are per caller.\n6. **Writer properties are graded.** R-12: retention default 14 days (FALLBACK_RETENTION_MS); the pruner removes rows past it and window reads never count rows older than the window. R-14: a failed write never throws into the caller and increments the lifetime failure counter.\n\nThis ruling is implemented by a rubrics:amend round to rev 4 (outside-lineage approval), new item P-017 (inventory hardening, blocks P-005..P-015), clause rewrites, and a re-emitted spec-quality scorecard (EI-25704648587573846 becomes stale).\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAmendment-Id: deg-signals-critique2-v4b\nRequest-Hash: 4bcbf7427373bebff8f9d92e34cbde9e4d05f241a63aa3cba668ae4912934839\nActor: su-78fe9a1e-475c-485a-86ee-a4e13ea8cb2a\nReason: D-006: two independent bar-critique consults (thread-posts 1174665, 1174670) found blocking defects in R-2..R-8 and R-11. have different outer interfaces. Existing cloud E2E and parity campaigns have unresolved real-workflow acceptance; exposing the portal in Tauri without native adapters would lose desktop capabilities.\n\nOutcome: First finish the existing cloud E2E and desktop-parity acceptance, then use the maintained portal interface in Tauri. Both clients allow explicitly selecting a local or remote instance. Desktop retains its native integrations and a locally available interface.\n\nClarification: Avi explicitly says to keep the existing local/dev/prod controls and only replace the interface.\n\nSource turn: Avi's 2026-10-11 request in this Codex session: finish cloud portal E2E and desktop feature parity, then update Tauri to the portal interface; both web and desktop should connect to remote or local instances; explain local detection and desktop differences.\n\nScenarios:\n1. Installed desktop opens the shared portal interface and discovers an existing local operator from its advertised address, verifies health/identity/protocol, and offers its workspaces.\n2. Desktop connects to a hosted or self-hosted remote instance using that instance's authenticated transport. Switching clears the previous instance's active sessions and caches.\n3. Browser opens a local instance's own portal URL, or connects an explicitly paired local instance through the maintained hosted connector. A hosted server probing its own loopback does not detect the customer's computer.\n4. Local discovery is stale or blocked: show unavailable or detection-blocked truthfully and offer Start local instance, Retry, Open local portal, or Enter address as applicable.\n5. Native terminal/files/notifications/secure credentials use desktop capability adapters. Remote files and terminals belong to the selected remote machine.\n6. Disconnecting remote access does not silently select local data. A local workspace can continue with locally available services; externally hosted voice/model services still require connectivity.\n\nNon-goals: No new app scaffold, copied portal screens, new cloud provisioning system, broad local-network port scan, or remote-page access to unrestricted Tauri commands.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** This sole continuation owns P-005/P-001 after sanctioned reclaim. Implement and test within maintained suites. blocked-by: P-001, P-005 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Extend existing instance selection and discovery to support explicit local/remote connections in both clients, including browser pairing/local-origin entry, protocol validation, stale discovery, permission-blocked detection, session/cache isolation and no silent switch. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n\n## Phase 3 — Installed acceptance and delivery\n\n- **P-004** `todo` Verify the packaged desktop portal UI on supported OS runtimes with local startup, authenticated remote connection, switching, reconnect, native capability limits, offline startup and preserved Local/Dev/Prod/Staging controls; ship the verified coexistence/candidate implementation while the established public release pipeline remains on the old interface, and publish a scenario-level report. Record the separate cutover decision; do not flip public defaults without it. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Existing campaigns stay authoritative\n\nCloud campaign WI-10007600 and parity plan cloud-portal-desktop-parity-closure-2026-10-09 remain the existing sources for acceptance. This plan adds desktop adoption after their acceptance, not a duplicate testing campaign.\n\n### D-002 — Both clients support local and remote\n\nAvi explicitly requested both connection choices. Client platform and workspace location are separate dimensions. Native privileges follow the desktop capability boundary, not a local/cloud label.\n\n### D-003 — Unresolved voice privacy is preserved\n\nAvi has been asked whether configured external speech providers may receive audio for either workspace or local-workspace voice must stay entirely local. Do not infer permission to transmit microphone audio from approval of the interface change.\n\n### D-004 — Interface replacement preserves desktop Local/Dev/Prod behavior\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAvi's explicit correction in this session: \"our cloud version aslo doesnt have the local/dev/prod stuff. to be clear I want to keep that, I just want to replace the interface\". Scope is presentation replacement, preserving existing desktop environment selectors, persisted target, native functions, sidecar/bootstrap and frontend/API routing. Local/remote instance selection is separate from build/environment selection. Measured: papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/src/env_switch.rs TARGETS declares dev, prod, staging and local, with api_port_for_target mapping the local SPA target to its existing operator API. Preserve those semantics and distribution-profile eligibility; this decision does not add internal dev hosts to the public cloud portal.\nRelated: P-002, P-004\n\n### D-005 — Maintain both interfaces; public R2 pipeline stays legacy until approved cutover\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAvi's owner-typed instruction: \"until we are confident we've acheived feature parity can we maintain both versions. And our whole publish build pipeline that publishes to https://pub-cb5359a346e94c0c88562bd41db9295a.r2.dev/HK70BNWvxXWRRRkMgl3PXqgdZyWYLsCG/index.html should continue using the old version until we are ready for the cutover\". Maintain the old desktop interface alongside an explicitly selected portal candidate. Ordinary build/package/sign/upload, public installers, updater feeds and download-page publication remain on the existing interface until parity evidence and Avi's explicit cutover readiness decision. AUTO/self through-shipment approval authorizes verified coexistence/candidate delivery, and preserves this hold. Existing Local/Dev/Prod/Staging and native/runtime behavior are retained.\n\nMeasured: papercusp-desktop/bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh:1029 selects apps/operator-vite as its SPA source; check-spa-freshness.js checks its dist against sidecar/spa. upload-release.sh writes installer/signature objects plus permanent and per-channel latest.json; record-release-cli.ts generates index.html separately. Typechecks and screenshots alone are insufficient.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"mutation-probe-evidence-value-2026-10-11","title":"Mutation probe: auditable evidence, honest survivals, visible re-aims, less friction and prompt tax","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-10-11","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Mutation probe: auditable evidence, honest survivals, visible re-aims, less friction and prompt tax\nslug: mutation-probe-evidence-value-2026-10-11\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-10-11\nupdated: 2026-10-12\n---\n\n# Mutation probe: auditable evidence, honest survivals, visible re-aims, less friction and prompt tax\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-12, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing. Next repair: Run plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy for the mapped outcome with current fingerprints; fix every fail/unknown proof obligation before ship. A read-only shipReadiness probe supplies no current fingerprints, so freshness rates unknown and this code can persist however good the evidence is — supply current fingerprints before concluding the evidence itself is at fault. (R-1). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nP-002, P-003 and P-004 are done with committed completion authority after independent audits. P-005 is done with accepted proof but authority proposed only for an uncommitted CLAUDE.md blob; git-sync settlement owns its upgrade. P-001/P-008/P-006 remain open.
