P-006 reviewed 52 legacy candidates: 14 duplicate requests dropped; remaining 13 await P-001/P-008; 25 distinct follow-ups have verified owners (24 self, one peer). Full plan is not shipped.\n\n**Next:** su-c04397d1 verifies that managed git-sync committed the overflow fix and corrected tests, then reruns clean committed verification and refreshes P-008 source proof before current R1/R7/R8 certification, remaining dispositions and final shipment.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008632 — Record a reporter-written mutation descriptor on every probe ledger row: `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` generates one probeInvocationId per invocation and exports `PAPERCUSP_MUTATION_DESCRIPTOR` (JSON: … <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008633 — `testing:runs` never hides an explicitly requested probe row: `testRunIds` lookups bypass the default source exclusion; a filePath lookup with source-filtered matches reports `omittedBySourceFilter` … <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008634 — Historical mode consumption control: before a historical SURVIVED verdict, re-run the guard against a poisoned snapshot; if it still passes, exit 2 INCONCLUSIVE naming the likely fixed-path import. F… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008635 — Bind-time re-aim detection in `plans:bind-spec-evidence` (D-003): a caught mutant row is refused `mutation_reaim_unjustified` when a mutant-leg pass row with the same test file and testFileSha256 but… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008636 — Ledger-derived caught and grader-visible mutation provenance in `plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy` (D-003): a descriptor-bearing mutant fail counts as caught only when a baseline-leg pass shares its… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008637 — Replace the CLAUDE.md \"Proving a guard is falsifiable\" doc part (set-doc-part, then project) with a pointer of at most 1,200 characters measured heading to next heading; move the full guidance (tier … <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010008638 — Consolidate the open mutation-probe work items: close each as superseded by its P-00N on completion, drop duplicates with a reason, and assign any remaining distinct items. <!-- P-006 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Agents who prove a guard is falsifiable with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` and bind the result as plan evidence; graders/auditors who must re-check a bound proof; Avi, who relies on a shipped plan's evidence meaning something.\n\n**Problem.** Measured 2026-10-11 (report `rpt_69139ebc-2aa2-440b-a05f-33ad5b03c14a`): since the probe became the L4 evidence source for `spec-test-adequacy` (~2026-09-21) volume rose ~100x. The raw signal is sound (94.6% caught by real assertions) but the value is thin: (1) a mutant ledger row never records WHAT was mutated, so a bound \"caught\" proof cannot be audited or re-run; (2) `testing:runs` hides probe rows by default, re-filed ~5 times; (3) historical mode can report a confident SURVIVED when the guard never read the snapshot; (4) 25-35 of 50 recaught survivors were caught again with the test file unchanged — legitimate re-aim and gate-shopping are indistinguishable; (5) a ~2k-token CLAUDE.md section rides on every request although ~2% of sessions run a probe; (6) 49 open probe work items, many duplicates.\n\n**Outcome.** A bound mutation proof names its subject, mutation and diff hash; probe rows are findable by id; historical SURVIVED is only reported when the guard demonstrably consumed the snapshot; binding a catch that follows a survival on an unchanged test requires a stated justification; the CLAUDE.md section is a short pointer; the open probe backlog is consolidated.\n\n**Non-goals.** Removing the probe or the L4 adequacy rung; redesigning `spec-test-adequacy`; a new ledger table (the descriptor reuses `test_runs.execution_details`); changing copy-out/in-tree verdict semantics beyond the descriptor.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner directive #1686 (\"what's the point of our mutation probe? Is it providing good results? Is it draining a lot of tokens? is the benefit worth the token spend?\") and #1691 (\"put this into a plan and then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped status\"), both 2026-10-11, this session.\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. A grader opens a plan's bound mutation proof and reads the mutated path, mutation expression and diff hash from the ledger row, and can re-run it.\n2. An agent cites `testRunIds:[N]` for a probe row and `testing:runs` returns it.\n3. A historical-mode probe whose guard imports its subject by a fixed path ends INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2) instead of SURVIVED.\n4. An agent's mutant survives, they change the mutation until it is caught without touching the test, and binding that catch is refused until they give a one-line justification, which is stored with the binding.\n5. A fresh session's CLAUDE.md carries a short pointer instead of ~8k chars of probe instructions.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Self-describing mutation proofs.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Record what was mutated on every mutation-probe test_runs row so a bound proof can be audited and re-run.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A mutation-probe run writes execution_details.mutation with subject path, mode, mutation expression or historical commit, before/after subject hashes and a mutant diff hash, and testing:runs plus the spec-evidence reader expose it.\",\"falsifier\":\"A mutant row is written without a descriptor, or the descriptor is dropped before testing:runs or the evidence reader.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-001\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the descriptor unit tests covering the reporter, the runs reader and the evidence reader.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/testing/mutation-descriptor.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Probe rows are findable.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"testing:runs must return mutation-probe rows requested by id and say when a source filter hid matches.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"testing:runs { testRunIds } returns mutation-probe rows without a source argument, and a filePath lookup reports omittedBySourceFilter with a hint naming source mutation-probe.\",\"falsifier\":\"A testRunIds lookup for an existing mutation-probe row returns zero rows.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-002\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the testing:runs visibility tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/testing/runs-mutation-probe-visibility.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Hidden probe rows are announced.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"testing:runs must say when its default source filter hid mutation-probe matches.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A testing:runs filePath lookup whose matching rows the default source exclusion hid reports omittedBySourceFilter above zero with a hint naming source 'mutation-probe' and testRunIds.\",\"falsifier\":\"A filePath lookup whose only matches are mutation-probe rows returns omittedBySourceFilter of zero or no hint naming source 'mutation-probe'.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-002\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the testing:runs visibility tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/testing/runs-mutation-probe-visibility.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Honest historical survivals.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Historical mode must not report a confident SURVIVED when the guard never consumed the relocated snapshot.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"When the guard passes against the historical snapshot, the probe runs a consumption control against a poisoned snapshot and exits 2 INCONCLUSIVE if the guard still passes.\",\"falsifier\":\"A guard that imports its subject by a fixed path yields exit 1 SURVIVED in historical mode.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-003\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the historical-mode consumption-control tests against fixture repositories.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/testing/mutation-probe-historical-consumption.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Visible re-aims.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Make re-aiming a mutation until it is caught visible at bind time.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"plans:bind-spec-evidence refuses mutation_reaim_unjustified when a caught mutant row is bound without reaimJustification while the same test file, unchanged, had a surviving mutant in the preceding 4 hours.\",\"falsifier\":\"A re-aimed catch on an unchanged test binds without a justification.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-004\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the bind-time re-aim detection tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/bind-from-test-run-reaim.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Justified re-aims are recorded.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A justified re-aim binds, and its justification stays on the binding so the re-aim remains visible.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"plans:bind-spec-evidence binds a caught mutant row that would otherwise be refused mutation_reaim_unjustified when reaimJustification is supplied, and the stored binding carries that reaimJustification.\",\"falsifier\":\"A justified re-aim is refused, or the stored binding lacks the supplied reaimJustification.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-004\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the bind-time re-aim detection tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/bind-from-test-run-reaim.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Prompt tax cut.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Shrink the CLAUDE.md mutation-probe section to a pointer so sessions that never probe stop paying ~2k tokens per request.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The projected CLAUDE.md falsifiability section is at most 1,200 characters and points to an agent-insights doc that carries the full guidance.\",\"falsifier\":\"The section exceeds 1,200 characters or its pointer target does not resolve.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-005\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the doc-claims size-cap and pointer test.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/claude-md-mutation-probe-pointer.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Caught means caught.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A mutation counts as caught only when the ledger proves the fail was the mutant's, not because the binder said so.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy rates a bound descriptor-bearing mutant fail as caught only when a baseline-leg pass row shares its probeInvocationId and subjectBeforeSha256, and rates it unknown when no such row exists or the binder-supplied outcome contradicts the ledger.\",\"falsifier\":\"A descriptor-bearing mutant fail with no linked baseline pass, or with a contradicting binder outcome, is rated caught.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-008\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the spec-test-adequacy mutation linkage and evidence tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy-mutation-linkage.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Graders see the mutation.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A grader must see what was mutated and how the catch was reached without a side query.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:1686\",\"owner-directive:1691\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The per-criterion falsifiability evidence that plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy emits for a bound mutation row names its leg, probeInvocationId, full 40-character commit sha, subject path, mutation expression or againstCommit, failed case titles and any re-aim survivor row ids.\",\"falsifier\":\"The evidence for a bound mutation row omits one of those fields while the row or binding carries it.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-008\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the spec-test-adequacy mutation linkage and evidence tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy-mutation-linkage.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-008 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Evidence quality\n\n- **P-001** `done` Record a reporter-written mutation descriptor on every probe ledger row: `scripts/mutation-probe.sh` generates one probeInvocationId per invocation and exports `PAPERCUSP_MUTATION_DESCRIPTOR` (JSON: schemaVersion, probeInvocationId, leg = baseline|mutant|consumption-control, mode, repo-relative subjectPath, literal mutateExpression or full againstCommit, subjectBeforeSha256, subjectAfterSha256, bounded unified mutantDiff, testCommandSha256) to every leg; `scripts/with-test-pg.mjs` passes it through; the reporter persists it at `execution_details.mutation` with testFileSha256 of the test file it ran; `testing:runs` returns it inline. Ships expand-then-contract per D-001; field set per D-003. Supersedes EI-25631227095524512, EI-25639876132855670, EI-25642448008405501, EI-25642614044512978. — note: Canonical WI-6554700010008772 completed with current R1 proof; legacy hub WI-6554700010008632 dropped as duplicate. Preserve the canonical successful lane outcome.\n- **P-002** `done` `testing:runs` never hides an explicitly requested probe row: `testRunIds` lookups bypass the default source exclusion; a filePath lookup with source-filtered matches reports `omittedBySourceFilter` plus a hint naming `source:'mutation-probe'`. Supersedes EI-25681589997808942, EI-25661534372957803, EI-25640937560550198. — note: ← WI-6554700010008633 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Historical mode consumption control: before a historical SURVIVED verdict, re-run the guard against a poisoned snapshot; if it still passes, exit 2 INCONCLUSIVE naming the likely fixed-path import. Fixes EI-25263495315968521 and WI-10006508. — note: ← WI-6554700010008634 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Bind-time re-aim detection in `plans:bind-spec-evidence` (D-003): a caught mutant row is refused `mutation_reaim_unjustified` when a mutant-leg pass row with the same test file and testFileSha256 but a different probeInvocationId exists and `reaimJustification { survivorTestRunIds, reason }` does not name it, or when that survivor carries the catch's own mutation expression (flakiness, never justifiable); the refusal names each survivor with its expression; an accepted justification is persisted on the binding. Depends on P-001. — note: ← WI-6554700010008635 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Ledger-derived caught and grader-visible mutation provenance in `plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy` (D-003): a descriptor-bearing mutant fail counts as caught only when a baseline-leg pass shares its probeInvocationId and subjectBeforeSha256, and a contradicting binder outcome rates unknown; pre-descriptor rows are labelled linkage=unverified-legacy; the per-criterion falsifiability evidence names leg, probeInvocationId, full commit sha, subject path, mutation expression or againstCommit, failed case titles and any re-aim survivor ids. Depends on P-001, P-004. blocked-by: P-001, P-004 — note: ← WI-6554700010008636 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Cost and friction\n\n- **P-005** `done` Replace the CLAUDE.md \"Proving a guard is falsifiable\" doc part (set-doc-part, then project) with a pointer of at most 1,200 characters measured heading to next heading; move the full guidance (tier table, exit codes, invocation forms, sweep-lock recipe) into an agent-insights doc via `docs:author`; pin both with a doc-claims test. — note: ← WI-6554700010008637 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Consolidate the open mutation-probe work items: close each as superseded by its P-00N on completion, drop duplicates with a reason, and assign any remaining distinct items. — note: ← WI-6554700010008638 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — P-001 ships expand-then-contract: parser first, probe export after deploy\nDate: 2026-10-11\nlibs/test-config/src/execution-details.ts parses execution_details strictly; an unknown key makes the row unproven. The deployed operator (:3070) parses rows that the working-tree reporter writes, and mutation-probe rows run at about 1,455 a day (test_runs, source='mutation-probe', last 24h, measured 2026-10-11). So P-001 lands in two hops: (1) the parser accepts an optional, strictly validated `mutation` descriptor, and the reporter copies PAPERCUSP_MUTATION_DESCRIPTOR into it only when that env var is present; (2) scripts/mutation-probe.sh exports the descriptor only after (1) is deployed to :3070. Until then no probe row carries the key, so no deployed reader sees an unknown key. [self-imposed, su-f7c06fac, 2026-10-11]\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAmendment-Id: mpev-r4-r6-split-1\nRequest-Hash: 5153a55552e2c2f05cca000ec1f0e913aae731f080543d19d852656614e4e156\nActor: su-f7c06fac-e1dc-4a3e-8f6f-7133936dbd6b\nReason: R-4 atomicity split: refusal stays in R-4; accept-with-justification and persistence move to new R-6 (reviewer objection thread-post:1174442; approved thread-post:1174464).\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-9598d9a8-025e-4069-95f1-6045c1dcb124\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1174464\nApproved-At: 2026-10-11T15:51:49.896Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 7 → 8\nChanged BARs: R-4, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-003 — Bar critique adopted: reporter-written invocation-linked descriptor, ledger-derived caught, fingerprint-scoped re-aims\nDate: 2026-10-11\nSource: bar-critique consult conv-request-9ae75fa01e6e0ff94cc86419bda09fd36b953116f6f734585f68eda9937f5d2d, posts 1174504 (su-84b47fdb) and 1174514 (su-ace8bd70); both say amend before plans:start.\nMeasured 2026-10-11: test_runs 20466815 and 20471763 are execution_details.mutationPhase='baseline' passes, 20468203 is a mutationPhase='mutant' PASS (a surviving mutant) and 20473143 the later caught mutant, all source='mutation-probe' at 8c1be2ef. The reporter already records the phase, but no reader surfaces it and nothing links a baseline row to its mutant (runGroupId null; the probe sets no group).\nRulings:\n1. leg reuses the probe's existing phase vocabulary (baseline = the calibration leg, mutant, consumption-control) and is carried in execution_details.mutation.leg with a probeInvocationId shared by every leg of one invocation.\n2. The descriptor carries the literal mutation expression (or the full 40-character againstCommit) plus a bounded unified diff, not a diff hash; the reporter adds testFileSha256 of the test file it ran.\n3. Re-aim scope = same test file, same testFileSha256, different probeInvocationId; no time window. Survivors are mutant-leg pass rows. Detection is best-effort over ledgered rows: a probe whose --test writes no test_runs row (for example grep) is invisible; R-1's end-to-end test pins that every leg exports the descriptor.\n4. reaimJustification becomes { survivorTestRunIds, reason } and must name every detected survivor; a survivor whose mutation expression equals the catch's is flakiness and is never justifiable.\n5. caught is ledger-derived (R-7, P-008): a descriptor-bearing mutant fail counts only when a baseline-leg pass shares its probeInvocationId and subjectBeforeSha256; a contradicting binder outcome rates unknown. Pre-descriptor rows keep today's rule with evidence labelled linkage=unverified-legacy; failing them would strand in-flight plans on a provenance gap they could not close, and re-running the probe upgrades them.\n6. Grader visibility (R-8, P-008): the adequacy evaluator's per-criterion falsifiability evidence names leg, probeInvocationId, full commit sha, subject path, mutation expression or againstCommit, failed case titles and any re-aim survivor ids.\n7. R-5 asserts on the projected section (heading to next heading), produced from its doc part, and on the agent-insights doc carrying the tier table, exit codes, invocation forms and sweep-lock recipe. The psu playbook splices this same projected text, so no separate rendered-weight lint is added.\n8. R-3's poison is a stub that cannot load and contains none of the --positive-control literals (as implemented); the bar names it.\n[self-imposed, su-f7c06fac, 2026-10-11; grounded in reviewer posts 1174504 and 1174514]\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAmendment-Id: mpev-bar-critique-d003-2\nRequest-Hash: e0e6fa07c8790eccc6d815de0f5fee67b21db10c8915970cd9ac6bea2d0ff360\nActor: su-f7c06fac-e1dc-4a3e-8f6f-7133936dbd6b\nReason: Bar critique D-003 (consult posts 1174504 and 1174514): invocation-linked reporter-written descriptor (R-1), tighter R-2/R-3/R-5 falsifiers, fingerprint-scoped structured re-aims (R-4, R-6), new R-7 ledger-derived caught and R-8 grader-visible provenance (P-008). Resubmitted with mode restored to R-1 per reviewer objection thread-post:1174534.\nApproved-By: su-0024b0c3-285e-465a-9b3b-dd5ab74ca44c\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1174543\nApproved-At: 2026-10-11T16:29:20.881Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 17 → 18\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-005 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nAmendment-Id: mpev-spec-atomicity-5\nRequest-Hash: aeb34fcd2e2f3ea3045fd31d1945c2597d3aac15942f038f73cda3644476bc7f\nActor: su-f7c06fac-e1dc-4a3e-8f6f-7133936dbd6b\nReason: Spec-quality atomicity and implementation-independence repair after D-003 (plans:evaluate-spec-quality specSetHash 68b82bb7 failed atomic-observable-behavior on R-1/R-2/R-4/R-6 and implementation-independence on R-5). Each model is rewritten as one observable outcome, checked locally with specBehaviorNonAtomicReason; R-2's second outcome (omittedBySourceFilter hint) moves to new R-9 for P-002. At 18:10Z :3070 served d740fc3802, whose libs/test-config gitlink (bf397e6) lacks src/mutation-descriptor.ts, and main was frozen behind a red gate held live by su-521c53be (WI-10006055, held since 2026-10-10 16:41Z). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nP-003 is implemented in canonical staging and locally verified on package mapping, installed-package discovery, shared connector/vault ingestion, owner OAuth/account isolation, SDK expiry policy, and legacy poll removal (WI-6554700010011936 checkpoint). Final corrected callback/loader tests and clean committed proof/bindings remain. P-026/P-027/P-028 remain held by su-29c0fedf; no takeover. This session runs directly as Avi's single requested headless GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh agent; no extra agents launched.\n\n**Next:** su-01f596a7: finish P-003 exact committed evidence and SPEC-P-003 acceptance, retain the honest R-5-wide blocker, then continue the next unclaimed plan lane without disturbing live claims.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Audience:** Avi, who wants agents to market Papercusp on social platforms; then any Papercusp user who installs a social provider from the Cupboard.\n- **Problem:** the nine social connectors in app code were never wired up (D-003): no network path, nothing registers them, and they have never run against a real account. So no agent can read or post on any social platform today, and the connectors cannot be installed, updated or removed from the Cupboard the way gmail, google-calendar, asana and linear can.\n- **Outcome:** each platform is a provider package in libs/papercusp/plugins built on providerAdapter { describe, syncPage, invoke }, reaching the network only through host.fetch and declaring its setup, so the generic Settings → Integrations card renders it. social:post, social:reply and social:delete reach it through provider invoke with the host rails unchanged, and the existing social-* trigger packs receive its events. Order (D-005): the shared pieces, then Facebook Pages, Instagram and X, then Bluesky and Reddit, then the remaining ports and the additions Avi picked (D-002).\n- **Non-goals:** a Papercusp-hosted one-click OAuth client; Meta App Review or LinkedIn partner approval for other people's accounts (testing uses Avi's own accounts in development mode); changing the publish ratification flag; moving any of Avi's existing mail into the CRM (separate item WI-6554700010011427).\n- **Source turns:** [owner:Avi 2026-10-13] 9e2c8dc1 turn 11 (\"What about a connector for facebook instagram x linkedin any others we should add? That we can use to market papercusp\"), turn 14 (directive #1825, release on the Cupboard infra), turn 20 (dialog: route A, the four additions), turn 21 (directive #1827, the audit); [owner:Avi 2026-10-14] 691a13ca turn 11 (dialog: approach, separate Meta packages, Bluesky and Reddit accounts), turn 14 (directive #1838, Facebook, Instagram and X first), turn 19 (dialog: accounts, app creation via verdict, $25 X cap). Earlier: owner directive #1650 [owner:Avi 2026-10-10] and report rpt_965ee3de-fdca-43c3-b9d7-98eaff3acd32.\n- **Scenarios:** (1) Avi installs facebook-pages from the Cupboard and connects his Page on the Integrations card; the social-facebook-pages trigger pack records a new comment, and an agent answers it with social:reply. (2) An agent posts a launch announcement to X; the $25 monthly cap bounds what it can spend. (3) An outside author copies the facebook-pages package, runs the SDK conformance kit against it, and publishes a package for another platform. (4) Someone adds a social-platform module to app code and the census test fails.\n- **Assumptions:** Facebook Pages and Instagram are separate packages, with the Graph helpers restated in each (D-004). Platforms without a live account ship verified only against fakes and the kit, and say so (D-004 item 3).\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Avi, using agents to market Papercusp, and Papercusp users installing social providers from the Cupboard.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Built-in social connectors lacked a registered network path and could not be installed, updated or removed through the Cupboard provider infrastructure.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Social platforms install as provider packages, declare their setup on the generic Integrations card, receive events through existing trigger packs, and support agent actions through the existing host rails. Build Facebook Pages, Instagram and X first, then Bluesky and Reddit, the remaining ports and the approved additions.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Papercusp-hosted one-click OAuth client.\",\n    \"Meta App Review or LinkedIn partner approval for other people's accounts.\",\n    \"Changing the publish ratification flag.\",\n    \"Moving Avi's existing mail into the CRM; separate WI-6554700010011427.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:claude:9e2c8dc1-b1ca-4c03-83c6-f62113302330:11\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:9e2c8dc1-b1ca-4c03-83c6-f62113302330:14\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:9e2c8dc1-b1ca-4c03-83c6-f62113302330:20\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:9e2c8dc1-b1ca-4c03-83c6-f62113302330:21\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:691a13ca-ad6b-4c8d-b61d-f8397209fb2b:11\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:691a13ca-ad6b-4c8d-b61d-f8397209fb2b:14\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:691a13ca-ad6b-4c8d-b61d-f8397209fb2b:19\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Ship social connectors on the existing Cupboard provider infrastructure so agents can market Papercusp.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:claude:9e2c8dc1-b1ca-4c03-83c6-f62113302330:11\",\n        \"session_turn:claude:9e2c8dc1-b1ca-4c03-83c6-f62113302330:14\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"product-choice\",\n      \"text\": \"Facebook Pages and Instagram are separate packages; rebuild on providerAdapter while reusing tested mapping logic.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:claude:691a13ca-ad6b-4c8d-b61d-f8397209fb2b:11\"\n      ],\n      \"decisionRef\": \"D-004\",\n      \"material\": true,\n      \"resolved\": true\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Build Facebook Pages, Instagram and X first; Avi provides account access later. these bounded vendor mappings do not need another third-party HTTP or orchestration library.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"notApplicable\": null\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Each social connector installs from the Cupboard.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Release the social connectors built on top of our Cupboard infra, as was done for the email, calendar, Asana and Linear apps.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9e2c8dc1-b1ca-4c03-83c6-f62113302330:14\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each delivered social, blog or Discord connector installs from the Cupboard and shows its declared setup on Settings → Integrations without an app update or provider-specific UI.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if a delivered connector cannot install/load from the Cupboard or requires provider-specific Settings UI or an application update to expose its declared setup.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run every registered check against the same immutable source cohort. The population currently contains eleven delivered social packages: facebook-pages, instagram, x (provider id x-twitter), threads, tiktok, linkedin (personal profile), linkedin-company (company page), youtube, mastodon, reddit and bluesky. social-package-registry.integration.test.ts exercises real Cupboard review/consent/install, refuses missing daemon declarations before side effects, loads each installed sandbox daemon through the registry and executes its source-bound host.fetch against fakes. blog/blog-package-registry.integration.test.ts adds real Cupboard consent/install, registry discovery, installed sandbox-daemon execution and host-held API-key header injection for dev.to and Hashnode, including draft and explicit-publish invocation against fakes. Those two publishing packages together with linkedin-company bring the delivered population to thirteen. apps/operator/app/settings/integrations/page.test.tsx renders the actual thirteen descriptors through generic Integrations cards, including fixed OAuth, instance-scoped registration app-password setup and the two publishing API-key forms; ProviderOAuthClientForm.test.tsx covers shared registration controls. Each actual-package unit suite validates its descriptor and runs the shared conformance kit. A present but unloadable package fails R-1; an entirely absent addition requested by R-6 is rated only under R-6. Later deliveries extend this same population and its registered files before delivery. No vendor is contacted, and this does not satisfy live-account R-3 or R-8. The linkedin/linkedin-company-provider.test.ts suite adds real Cupboard review/consent/install, registry discovery and shipped daemon loading for the separate company registration. The actual package and host both refuse the explicit partner-approval wall before OAuth, identity or network; an offline future-approved manifest control exercises reads and writes against fakes. Its grant and Page-admin prerequisites remain unresolved and are never inferred from offline success. The admitted positive delivery returns 200; R-10 separately grades authentication, source ownership, valid records and duplicate suppression.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/providers/connector-push-normalize.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Run testing:run with harness papercusp and exactly the files in this criterion check, then inspect their named positive and inverse assertions at the recorded commit; refuse suite passes with skipped assertions or an unmatched source cohort.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nEach platform is a self-contained CommonJS provider package in libs/papercusp/plugins/<id>/ (papercusp.json `provider` descriptor + index.cjs exporting providerAdapter { describe, syncPage, invoke }), modelled on libs/papercusp/plugins/linear. The host connector runtime owns credentials, leases, cursors, retry and backoff; packages reach the network only through host.fetch inside egressHosts. Package tests live in packages/operator-core/lib/providers/<id>/ and run the SDK conformance kit (P-026). social:* writes go through capability-verbs/provider-dispatch.ts (P-002) after the existing host rails. Existing social-* trigger packs bind the `ext:<provider-id>:<event>` keys the packages emit, so each package's provider id equals the trigger pack's sourceKind (facebook-pages, instagram, x, bluesky, reddit, ...).\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-027, P-028, P-023, P-030, P-031, P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-027, P-028, P-023 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-029 | live |\n| R-4 | P-026, P-032 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-007 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-022, P-023, P-024, P-025 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-027, P-028, P-023, P-029, P-030, P-031, P-001 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-030, P-031 | live |\n| R-9 | P-035 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-035 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-035 | tree |\n\n## Census baseline\n\nMeasured 2026-10-11 by provider-specific-census.test.ts: 62 entries. Slack (15) migrates in the parent plan's P-008; this plan owns social (39), facebook-vault (3), google-workspace (1), discord (3) and asana (1).\n\n## Conformance\n\n```conformance\n{\n  \"requirements\": {\n    \"R-3\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"facebook-instagram-x-live-acceptance-incomplete\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"Facebook Pages, Instagram, or X is delivered as live-verified without an account-scoped artifact proving a recent-post read, one test post, and deletion of that same test post under the owner-supplied account and X cost gate.\",\n          \"stage\": \"delivery\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"Check the P-029 live-acceptance artifact for each of facebook-pages, instagram, and X: account identity, timestamped read result, created test-post id, deletion confirmation for that exact id, and the recorded X cost-envelope approval plus pre-first-call $25 cap.\",\n            \"bindWhen\": \"P-029 implements its live-acceptance artifact interface; That audit is the first step and its findings shape P-001/P-002.\n\n### D-002 — Scope adds LinkedIn company page, X, dev.to + Hashnode, and a Discord community bot\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-13, AskUserQuestion owner-dialog, multi-select] Avi picked all four additions: (1) a LinkedIn company page, i.e. organization posting through LinkedIn's Community Management API, which is partner-review-walled; agents draft the application and Avi submits it. (4) A Discord community bot for our own server, posting announcements and answering questions, extending P-005's outbound notifications.\n\n### D-003 — Social connectors are rebuilt on the provider contract, not moved (P-021 audit finding)\nDate: 2026-10-14\nSOURCE: P-021 audit for owner directive #1827 [turn:9e2c8dc1@2026-10-14T00:42:27.497Z], report rpt_5a292af1-21d2-41b6-a7df-fdb3b353a702 (2026-10-13).\n\nFINDING (measured). All nine social connectors (packages/operator-core/lib/external-triggers/social/, 12.4k src + 13.5k test lines) were written 2026-08-23 (WI-40944, WI-40947, WI-40954, WI-40968, WI-40970, WI-40991, WI-41010, WI-41109, WI-41120), before the host connector runtime (providers/connector-runtime.ts) and the Cupboard provider-package model. They are not wired: (a) every *Client HTTP interface is implemented only by test fakes, and LinkedIn alone calls raw global fetch; (b) no production code calls registerSocialWriteAdapter or any create*Adapter; (c) reconcile has no non-test caller, so the social-* trigger packs bind ext:<platform>:* events that nothing emits; (d) none were ever exercised against a live account.\n\nMeasured: grep -rlw for each of BlueskyReadClient, MastodonReadClient, RedditReadClient, YouTubeActivitiesClient, FacebookPostsClient, InstagramCommentsClient, ThreadsConversationClient, TikTokVideosClient, RedditWriteClient, BlueskyRepoClient over packages/apps/libs (excluding dist/node_modules) found each ONLY in its own module and that module's .test.ts. A non-test importer search for each of the 18 *-adapter modules found none outside external-triggers/social/ (the only in-folder importers are the write adapters reusing read-adapter helpers). registerSocialWriteAdapter appears only at its definition, capability-verbs/social.ts:859. linkedin-write-adapter.ts:169 and :257 call global fetch. testing:runs latestPerFile over external-triggers/social/ for 720h: 0 fail/error rows. Superseded-plan text: 'the only non-test caller of adapter.reconcile is the conformance kit'. Side-by-side read: reddit-adapter.ts:240, youtube-common.ts:43 and tiktok-common.ts:217 have identical retry-delay bodies; facebook-common.ts:477, instagram-common.ts:376, youtube-common.ts:62 and social-watermark.ts:55 parse instants identically.\n\nRULING. Packaging means rebuilding each platform as a provider package (providerAdapter { describe, syncPage, invoke }, network only via host.fetch + egressHosts, auth via oauth/clientRegistrationRef or setup.credentials). The per-platform normalization functions and their tests are ported. Reconcile loops are replaced by syncPage. Per-adapter retry/backoff (redditRetryDelayMs, youtubeRetryDelayMs, tiktokRetryDelayMs and the Bluesky and Mastodon variants), the ~14 per-platform error classes, social-egress.ts, and cursor-expiry backfill triggering are deleted: the host runtime already owns them (connector-runtime.ts header: retryAfterSeconds backoff, cursor reset on cursor-expired, lease, version-scoped dedupe). Each port removes its provider-specific-census entries.\n\nSHARED PIECES FIRST (before any platform port): (1) lift social/conformance.ts into the plugin SDK as a provider conformance kit that runs against any syncPage; (2) add catch-up path plus lossRisk reporting to the SDK sync page; (3) route social:* verbs through provider invoke (social.post/social.reply/social.delete) instead of the in-app WRITE_ADAPTERS registry, keeping the D-020 rails in the host; (4) one watermark/instant helper, replacing the facebook/instagram/tiktok/youtube copies of social-watermark.ts. Bluesky is the reference port, because it needs only an app password and is the cheapest to verify live. OPEN DESIGN CHOICE: Meta packaging, either one package covering Facebook Pages + Instagram or a helper bundled into each; Threads stays separate (its own Meta app).\n\n### D-004 — Owner rulings after the P-021 audit: Bluesky first, separate Meta packages, Bluesky + Reddit live accounts\nDate: 2026-10-14\nSOURCE: [owner:Avi 2026-10-14 AskUserQuestion dialog answer] [turn:self], answering the questions raised after report rpt_5a292af1-21d2-41b6-a7df-fdb3b353a702.\n\n1. Rationale: P-005 requires the route to leave app code, and P-025's community bot extends this same package, so the community surface belongs here.\n\n### D-036 — P-004 Google Workspace becomes the `google` descriptor credential group; a google-contacts package joins gmail + gcal; live refs migrate in place\nDate: 2026-10-20\n[self-imposed su-0af18b76 2026-10-20, AUTO under owner directive #2034] Measured: gmail and google-calendar packages already declare credentialGroup `google` with clientRegistrationRef `google` and oauth.identity; the descriptor connection adapter provisions one source per group member with kind = provider id (gmail, gcal). Snapshot before bg-host picks it up; rollback = reverse prefix rewrite plus restoring the copied token fields.\nRelated: P-004, P-007\n\n### D-038 — P-025 Discord community bot: the host socket ingress gains a declarative gateway session; the discord package adds chat-message ingress and chat.reply\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20 [self-imposed su-0af18b76, AUTO under owner directive #2034]\n\nMeasured: provider-socket-ingress.ts holds a host-side socket per source, but only in Slack's shape: POST open with Bearer, echo an ack per envelope, reconnect on a field. The Discord Gateway also needs (a) GET https://discord.com/api/v10/gateway/bot with `Authorization: Bot <token>`, with `?v=10&encoding=json` added to the returned URL, (b) IDENTIFY (op 2) carrying the bot token inside a socket frame after HELLO (op 10), (c) heartbeats (op 1, d = last sequence `s`) every `d.heartbeat_interval` ms, plus an immediate one when the gateway sends op 1, and (d) only DISPATCH frames (op 0) are data. Discord has ONE bot token for the gateway and REST, while Slack has separate app and bot tokens.\n\nDecision:\n(1) SDK ProviderSocketIngressDescriptor gains optional data, with no provider names: `open.query` (string map appended to the opened socket URL) and `session { hello { match, intervalPath }, identify { frame }, heartbeat { frame, requestMatch? }, sequencePath?, deliver? }`. Frames are JSON objects. A string value that is exactly `{{credential}}` (allowed only in identify.frame) or `{{sequence}}` is substituted by the HOST, so the credential still never reaches provider code. With `deliver` set, only matching envelopes reach ingress.normalize, so protocol frames never do. Validator (provider.ts ingressDescriptorIssues) and papercusp-plugin.schema.json change together.\n(2) The open request's Authorization comes from the ingress credential field's own declared `auth.scheme` (providerCredentialHeaderValue). This is derived, not a new field: Slack's app_token (no auth) stays Bearer and Discord's bot_token (scheme bot) sends `Bot <token>`. An ingress credential may also carry `hosts` (only perPrincipal is refused).\n(3) Heartbeats run from the existing managed reconcile tick (15s). No new timer: a beat is sent when now >= lastBeat + interval - tick, and at once on the gateway's request. The last sequence is read from every envelope. There is no RESUME: each reconnect (op 7 RECONNECT, op 9 INVALID_SESSION, via the existing `reconnect` match) re-identifies, so messages sent during a reconnect gap are not backfilled (disclosed in the package README).\n(4) The discord package goes to 0.2.0. It adds datatype chat-message and capabilities ingress.normalize and chat.reply, with intents GUILDS|GUILD_MESSAGES|DIRECT_MESSAGES|MESSAGE_CONTENT = 37377. MESSAGE_CONTENT is privileged and must be switched on in the Developer Portal. normalize maps MESSAGE_CREATE from non-bot authors (filtered to the source's guildId when set; DMs kept) to chat-message records: nativeId `<channel>:<message>`, payload { id, channelId, threadId = message id, threadKey = message_reference.message_id or null, sender, text, mentions, extensions.discord }. chat.reply posts to /channels/{channelId}/messages with message_reference { message_id: threadId, fail_if_not_exists:false }, allowed_mentions { parse:[], replied_user:false } and a nonce derived from the idempotency inputs, and returns { channelId, threadId, messageTs: <new message id> }. Text over Discord's 2000 characters is refused with invalid_text.\n(5) Verified against a fake gateway and fakes. Labelled not live-verified until Avi supplies a bot token with MESSAGE_CONTENT on (D-004 item 3 pattern).\n\n### D-039 — Amends D-038: Discord answers members through a discord-community-responder trigger pack bound to mentions; request-free capabilities are exempt from the kit's fault check; three disclosed gateway limits\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20 [self-imposed su-0af18b76, AUTO under owner directive #2034]\n\nMeasured: before the kit change, discord-provider.test.ts failed with 'invoke-fault-not-retried: ingress.normalize resolved although its first request was rate-limited' (/tmp/su0af18-p025/dp2.log, 17:42Z). Source read: provider-conformance.ts guardedFetch returns the fault only on call 1, and the invoke loop failed any invocation that resolved, even with zero calls. After the change: provider-conformance.test.ts passed (TEST_FILE_RESULT status=passed, 17:46:55Z start) and discord-provider.test.ts passed (17:47:45Z start).\n\n(1) 'Answers member questions' (P-025) is delivered by a new trigger pack libs/papercusp/plugins/discord-community-responder, mirroring slack-thread-responder: one binding, sourceKind discord, event ext:discord:mention, target member-reply. \"reason\": \"Cache layout changes sit behind registered flags.\", \"scenarioIds\": [\"SC-006\"]}\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Background\n\nSource turns: session_turn:codex:01a12cde-9c65-7080-b81d-aab41e5f0e79:1, :10, :14, :17; session_turn:codex:01a12d16-2c76-7cd1-99a4-ac0f0f37acad:15, :18, :23; owner directive #1699 (this revision). Earlier context: audit report /reports?sel=rpt_ea008b89-c23e-4b3e-9d60-36e9b5fc478b (209.16B seven-day tokens, 96.2% input reuse, about $17.5k write-equivalent cost, mostly estimated) and /reports?sel=rpt_bafdb0eb-5e27-4fa8-b5ba-1b475a88b5aa.\n\n### Audit findings (revision 2)\n\nMeasured on 2026-10-12 with existing instruments; probes are kept under `.papercusp/scratch/tokplan/`.\n\n1. **Startup cache writes are the largest single cost and have a fixable root cause.** In the gateway's `startup-cache-evidence/v1` journal, first requests account for half of all cache writes. In the dominant su group, the last system block (~131 KB playbook) has 413 distinct hashes across 450 starts, so it and the shared CLAUDE.md block behind it (6 distinct hashes) are rewritten on every start. Cause: `applySuPromptOverlays` (`packages/operator-core/lib/su-persona-render.ts`) appends per-session provenance, mode and instruction-precedence text (owner id, timestamp) after the playbook. `buildLaunchSpec` only emits `PSU_CACHE_BOUNDARY` when a launch context exists, so most launches have no boundary and the gateway split never runs. The 20 starts that did carry a boundary read a median of 84,637 tokens.\n2. **The repo-guide block can only be shared once the tail is moved.** The relocation from WI-10005042 (`relocateSystemTailToFirstUserTurn`) is built and tested but gated by an unregistered env var and off by default. This conflicts with the feature-flag policy.\n3. **Paging spills is the largest attributable behavior waste.** About 12.8k base64 page reads a day (about 5 pages per spill) each repeat a full-context model round trip. There is no way to search inside a saved result. This is the concrete form of the owner's Context Mode request.\n4. **A compaction dead end loops.** 2,695 refused `session:request-compaction` calls a day from 17 agents carry the same stale-artifact refusal.\n5. **Hook/server version skew is not a bug in this plan.** The 1,329 `locks:release {retain}` and 1,862 `activity:report {wake_delivery_id}` invalid-input calls come only from :3070 (green main d740fc3802); staging already accepts both keys. They clear when main deploys and are noted for P-014's after-measurement.\n6. **The always-loaded guide is large.** CLAUDE.md (and its AGENTS.md mirror) is 108,821 bytes, despite its own \"invariants + pointers only\" rule. The largest part is a 20 KB gate/containment section.\n7. **The original plan was not shippable as written.** It had 16 near-identical requirement blocks, matched-cohort statistics requiring paid budget, external compressor benchmarks requiring package installs, and a persistent chunk index over spills. None of these targeted the measured costs above. They were dropped or right-sized (D-009..D-011).\n\n### Research (unchanged from revision 1, summarized)\n\n| Candidate | State checked 2026-10-11 | Disposition |\n|---|---|---|\n| RTK | v0.51.0; shell hooks only; byte/4 estimates | Not installed on this host; no measured gap it fills here (D-009) |\n| Headroom | v0.40.0; proxy + transforms | Not adopted: a parallel proxy in front of our gateway (D-009) |\n| Tare | v0.2.0; proxy lacks Codex Responses route | Not adopted (D-009) |\n| Context Mode | v1.0.169; ELv2 | Pattern borrowed for P-005 (reference-scoped query, bounded excerpts); nothing installed |\n| QMD / LlamaIndex / CocoIndex / PageIndex | — | Patterns borrowed: source-positioned hits, line-window expansion, honest coverage |\n| LLMLingua-2, Claw Compactor, anvanster/compressor | older or overlapping | Not adopted |\n\nPrimary sources are listed in revision 1 (plan revision history) and report rpt_d334428f-183b-4bd0-a3c1-78028dad45be.\n\n### Baseline (frozen 2026-10-12 by P-001)\n\n| Metric | Instrument | Baseline |\n|---|---|---|\n| First-request cache write / read, dominant su group (opus-5-5, 3 system blocks) | `npm run measure:startup-cache` | median 78,258 / 3,689 tokens (n=461 requests, 330 with usage; window 2026-10-11 00:00Z..10-12 03:05Z) |\n| First-request cache write / read, boundary-split group (4 system blocks) | same | median 86,077 / 77,767 tokens (n=20); repo-guide block (messages[0] block 0) median 137,556 bytes |\n| Startup requests (owners) / usage measured / unknown | same | 770 (683) / 369 / 401 — unknown kept unknown |\n| First-request share of all journaled gateway cache writes | same | 29,886,228 tokens, 49.6% |\n| Launch census median total / written / read | `npm run measure:launch-cost` | 138,824 / 121,069 / 17,304 (n=579, 2026-10-04..12) |\n| Spill page reads per day | tool_invocations, `capability:read` with result-door refs | 12,820 (411 agents) |\n| Refused compaction calls per day | tool_invocations, `session:request-compaction` error | stale-artifact 2,683/24h (deploy skew, D-012); no_live_pty_host 1,204/24h from 27 owners (WI-6554700010008779, not this plan's fix) |\n| CLAUDE.md bytes | `wc -c CLAUDE.md` | 108,821 |\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\nEach bar's implementing items and evidence plane, mirroring the bar's own `requiredScope` and `evidencePlane`.\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-015 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006, P-015 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-011 | deployed |\n| R-8 | P-014 | deployed |\n| R-9 | P-014, P-015 | deployed |\n| R-10 | P-005 | tree |\n\n## Requirements\n\nAll requirements share one intent: deliver Avi's selected token-efficiency scope (#1/#2/#5), excluding #3/#4, with owner authority and evidence preserved. Source turns: session_turn:codex:01a12cde-9c65-7080-b81d-aab41e5f0e79:14 and :17, and owner directive #1699.\n\n**R-1 — Honest before/after instrument.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Measure startup cache reuse from the gateway journal with the existing launch-cost module.\",\"constraints\":[\"Unknown usage stays unknown\",\"No new ledger\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a12cde-9c65-7080-b81d-aab41e5f0e79:14\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"measure:startup-cache reports per-group first-request write/read medians and totals, keeps rows with missing usage as unknown, and counts each request once\",\"falsifier\":\"A duplicate journal line is counted twice or a missing counter is reported as zero\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-001\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"startup-cache-real-journal.test.ts runs summarizeStartupCacheEvidence and the real measure:startup-cache command (npx tsx scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts --input --json) over 150 verbatim gateway journal lines, including 30 real missing-usage rows (D-018). No new ledger.\n- Cache layout: `su-persona-render.ts` (boundary), `inference-gateway/cache-policy.ts` (existing split and relocation), `libs/flags/src/types.ts` (flag). WI-10005042 is completed here rather than reimplemented (D-002 preserved).\n- Saved-result query: extend `agent-tools/capability/read.ts` and the existing scratch-reference authorization. Line windows use `@papercusp/search` `splitWindows`-style ranges. Matching is literal or all-terms, which is cheap, deterministic and testable. No persistent chunk table, embeddings or LLM summaries (D-011). The result-door `next` hint advertises `query`.\n- Dead end: `session:request-compaction` refusal shape; no change to who is allowed.\n- Guide: doc parts in `harness_shared.harness_doc_parts` via `npm run set-doc-part`, then `scripts/project-doc-parts.mjs`. Long form goes to existing agent-insights docs.\n\n### Rollout and rollback\n\nNormal pipeline: git-sync → green-checkpoint → deploy. The boundary is inert without the split, and is reverted by the existing `PAPERCUSP_CACHE_SPLIT_BOUNDARY=0` switch. Relocation is reverted by its registered flag. Before acting on the live gate, read `state:read gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership`. LIVE_GATE_OPS stands down for a peer-held gate.\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline\n\n- **P-001** `done` Turn the gateway startup-cache probe into a tested instrument: `summarizeStartupCacheEvidence` in launch-cost-metrics.ts (dedupe by owner+request, first-request filter, per-group medians and totals, unknown usage kept unknown), `scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts` and `npm run measure:startup-cache`. This draft is a proposal; do not activate, implement, install packages/hooks, launch agents or spend on new inference based solely on its creation. Model/provider switching and separate effort tuning are out of scope.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse existing mechanisms and implementation lanes\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[derived from owner-selected scope; proposed implementation choice] Reuse the shipped launch-context plan and ready cache-efficiency plan, WI-10005042 and the two owned audit follow-ups. This consolidated plan sequences evaluation and delivery; it does not supersede the old cache plan, reopen its completed work or create a second gateway/session-memory store.\n\n### D-003 — Existing experiment gates remain binding\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[observed existing authority] The cache plan's D-017/D-073 paid stop/budget constraints remain intact. Drafting this plan is not paid-trial authorization. Prepare offline and use natural already-authorized traffic where appropriate; a new paid quality/TTL attempt requires its exact existing approval before dispatch.\n\n### D-004 — Adoption follows accepted-task value\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[proposed methodology] Keep the current configured models/effort and compare matched accepted tasks. Compressor headline percentages and byte/4 counters do not establish bill savings. Include cache-priced reads/writes, expanded originals, compression latency and failed-task retries. Proposed combined target is 20%; quality and authority fixtures remain mandatory even when tokens shrink.\n\n### D-005 — No duplicate compression or monitoring plane\nDate: 2026-10-11\n[proposed implementation choice; refined by D-007] RTK coverage/upgrade remains the baseline. Headroom output-only transforms are the first complementary benchmark; Tare is a secondary local candidate with an unproven Codex Responses proxy path. Saved-result retrieval is a Papercusp-native extension of the existing session/document search infrastructure, inspired by Context Mode, QMD, LlamaIndex, CocoIndex and PageIndex. No full third-party MCP/memory installation, new search engine, hook overwrite or duplicate supervisor is selected. Then restarted the gateway (dev:restart, drained, audited): new MainPID 2051620, process start 2026-10-12T14:42:25Z (10:42:25 local), /healthz 200, serving build 93f1beccf1 with containsChange:true.\n\nR-9 procedure from here: the window since 2026-10-12T14:42:25Z (10:42:25 local) is the same-build control cohort (flag OFF). Once measure:startup-cache --since \"2026-10-12 10:42:25\" reports >=20 measured opus su first requests with no messages[0] breakpoint, clear the override (flags:set enabled:null, so the code default ON governs, which is the shipped state) and record the flip time; the window after it is the relocated cohort. Both cohorts must share MainPID 2051620 / build 93f1beccf1; if the gateway restarts mid-run, restart the measurement.\n\n### D-025 — Correction to D-024: R-9 also waits on :3070, and the 14:42-16:00Z window is not a valid control\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[self-imposed, 2026-10-12 16:30Z, su-8cec8a78; corrects D-024]\n\nFalse premise, corrected: D-024 said P-015/R-9 ship by gateway restart alone. The gateway half is live (relocation code, flag default ON). But relocation only moves a tail that the boundary split created, and the split needs PSU_CACHE_BOUNDARY in the prompt. P-006 emits that sentinel for every su launch (su-persona-render.ts), and the psu launcher renders through :9071 -> :3070. :3070 serves d740fc3802, which lacks P-006 (dev:pipeline_position su-persona-render.ts: release-operator containsChange:false; staging, bg-host and gateway true).\n\nMeasured 16:20Z:\n- Only 35 of 529 launch renders in the last 24h (~/.papercusp/launch-context/session-*.md) carry the sentinel: the launch-context path that already emitted it before P-006. The newest plain psu render (session-41681.md, 128,968 B) has none.\n- Gateway startup-cache-evidence since the 16:00:02Z flag clear: plain opus su launches keep 3 system blocks with no messages[0] marker (no split, so nothing to relocate).\n- Three opus launches at 16:12:13-14Z (su-0f72f9a4, su-16ef2cf3, su-1744cc66) carry the sentinel and show the RELOCATED layout: the same 185,502 B stable system block, messages[0] = 111,319 / 5,508 / ~700 B (the 5.5 KB wrapped tail moved in), and a breakpoint on messages[0] block 0. First-request cache_read was 113,857 tokens each. So relocation works on real request shapes, and the 111 KB CLAUDE.md block was read from cache. Earlier [inferred] candidate (b), 'relocation refuses on the real su request shape', is refuted.\n\nRuling:\n1. R-9 needs the deployed build to carry P-006. Both cohorts must come from a :3070 build containing su-persona-render.ts at cec57ab34 or later.\n2. The 14:42-16:00Z window is NOT the R-9 control. 19 of its 22 opus launches had no boundary at all, and R-9 requires a boundary-only control (flag off, no messages[0] breakpoint) from the same build. Its numbers (median read 3,689) must not be used.\n3. The flag stays ON (the shipping default) until :3070 deploys. After the deploy: pin the flag OFF, collect >=20 boundary-only opus su launches, clear the pin, and collect >=20 relocated launches. Then compare median_on - median_off with G = floor(relocated med m0b0 bytes / 5) (about 22,263 at 111,319 B).\n4. P-015 cannot close before that. P-011, P-014 and P-015 all wait on the same :3070 deploy.\n\n### D-026 — Retraction: D-023's RTK and Tare reasoning rested on a wrong shell-share number and an untested assumption\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[self-imposed, 2026-10-12 18:35Z, su-8cec8a78; prompted by owner directives #1753 and #1754, which asked whether the test was fair and whether shell output is really only 0.5%]\n\nFalse premise, retracted: D-023 said shell output is ~0.5% of tool output, so RTK could save at most ~0.5%. That number counted only top-level shell tools and classified Codex code-mode `exec` as non-shell (p016-tool-output-volume.mts line 94). But `exec` scripts run shell commands inside them through tools.exec_command.\n\nMeasured: .papercusp/scratch/tokplan/shell-share-v2.mts over 24h, 3,432 Codex rollouts, 999.8 MB of tool output.\n- exec scripts that run only shell commands: 328 MB, 32.8% of bytes, 30.8% of carried bytes.\n- exec scripts mixing shell and MCP calls: 266 MB, 26.6%.\n- exec scripts with MCP calls only: 304 MB, 30.4%.\n- other exec: 7.3%. Top-level shell: ~0%.\nShell output is therefore at least ~33% of Codex tool output and up to ~59%, not 0.5%. Of the shell-only bytes, `ptool` (our own MCP CLI, 74 MB) is not RTK territory. The rest is dominated by sed (57 MB), rg (48 MB), python3 (36 MB) and git (9 MB). Per-command bytes are split evenly across a script's shell calls, so they are approximate.\n\nAlso retracted: 'Tare stays excluded (no Codex Responses route)'. That applies only to Tare's proxy. Tare also ships a CLI that works on any stdin, in-process Python transforms and an MCP server, and its README lists `tare wrap codex`. None of these was tested.\n\nRTK status (measured 18:30Z): not in use. No binary on PATH or in common install dirs, and no rewrite hook. ~/.config/rtk/config.toml dates from 2026-07-09, and the bash resource-gate still lists rtk as a command wrapper (2026-07-06 incident). None of the 1,183 Claude transcripts still on disk runs an rtk command.\n\nRuling: D-023's 'adopt nothing' stands only for Headroom, whose fidelity test was real. RTK and Tare get a fair benchmark on the commands agents actually run: replay the same read-only commands now, with and without each tool, in isolated directories without network; measure bytes and token estimates; check preservation of ids, paths, line numbers, error lines and truncation notices. Tracked as WI-6554700010009277. Adoption needs both a material saving and no lost content agents depend on.\n\n### D-027 — Fair RTK + Tare benchmark (WI-6554700010009277): keep RTK with the early-exit-pipe fix; do not adopt Tare\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\nRelated: D-023 (RTK/Tare reasoning, retracted by D-026), D-026, owner #1753/#1754 (asked whether the test was fair), #1759/#1764 (RTK reintegrated).\n\n[self-imposed, 2026-10-13 01:20Z, su-8cec8a78] Measured, 24h Codex rollouts (2,557 rollouts, 58,046 shell calls inside exec scripts, 323 MB shell output); byte-weighted (PPS) seeded samples; replays in a read-only, network-less bwrap sandbox in each command's original cwd; scored uncapped AND under each call's own max_output_tokens (set on 194/200 sampled calls), against the FULL raw output.\n\nRTK 0.51.0: rewrites commands carrying 38.4% of shell bytes (CI 34.1-42.7, n=500; the big untouched sources are ptool 22%, python 19%, sed range reads 20%). On rewritten commands (n=62 valid replays) it saves 13.4% of tokens uncapped (CI 6.3-20.7) and 7.2% under the call's own cap (CI 2.6-12.7), while showing LESS of the real output under that cap (line recall 0.75 vs 0.85 raw; id recall 0.71 vs 0.81); 22/62 rows lossy, 11 signalled. Whole-shell projection ~2.5-2.7%, about 1-1.6% of all tool output. Defect found and fixed: RTK broke pipe early exit (`rg | head -60` 0.5 s raw vs 28.5 s through rtk; 28% of rewritten commands pipe into head) -> WI-6554700010009543. Filed: periodic `rtk init -g` nag in agent output -> WI-6554700010009529.\n\nTare 0.2.0 at our own seam (CLI): lossless `compress` saves ~0% per output (-0.1%, CI -0.5..0.1, n=177) and 0.1% across 40 whole conversations (= the exact-duplicate share). Labelling outputs `tool_output` makes Tare keep only the LATEST output (every earlier one dropped as Superseded) - a fake 99% that would destroy context. `skeletonize` saves 30.8% on code reads but is lossy (line recall 0.68, error-line recall 0.56).\n\nRuling: keep RTK as integrated (owner #1759) with the early-exit-pipe skip rule in both rewrite seams; do not adopt Tare. Report: reports:publish 'RTK and Tare: a fair benchmark' (WI-6554700010009277). Evidence: .papercusp/scratch/wi9277/ (sample.json, rows.jsonl, analysis-valid.json, ctx.out, ctx-fileread.out).\n\n### D-028 — Fixture absence is an evaluator proof gap; do not bypass lineage or self-grade\nDate: 2026-10-14\nMeasured 2026-10-14 on staging source and current evaluator: spec-test-adequacy.ts rev29 correctly rates fixture-calibration unknown when executable bindings have null fixtureFingerprint, even when binder details.adequacy.fixtureFree=true. It can clear only through the existing server-certified outside-lineage independent-verification path, which matches source/test/run/cases and is exposed by spec-evidence-store.ts; prior EI-25889625242363568 implemented and tested this path (529/529 retained tests). The current ship dry-run for token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11 is blocked earlier at pre-grading by R-7/R-8/R-9 proof missing/inadequate/evidence-plane-unmet on the old deployed runtime; its refusal explicitly forbids peer recruitment for contract repairs. Therefore this session will not relabel production subjects as fixtures, self-grade, recruit a peer manually, or bypass the gate. The remaining question is orchestration: whether a supported system recruiter can dispatch an outside-lineage verifier for tree/source fixture absence before pre-grading, or whether each binding must carry genuine measured fixture calibration. Existing code/tests are preserved; no source edit is justified until that route is confirmed.\nRelated: P-011, P-014, P-015\n\n### D-029 — P-011 deployed-only exception is limited to release-plane stale-artifact measurement\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\nMeasured: P-011 text at the current plan revision names the 24h stale-artifact count for session:request-compaction after the fix reaches deployed main.\n\nP-011 has a narrow deployed-only exception. The deployed-only property is the 24h stale-artifact count on the release operator (:3070/green-checkpoint) after deployment. Staging/current-build cannot exercise that property because those callers and stale-artifact outcomes are produced by the deployed release plane, not the staging process; this is because the fix's caller-row launch selection is only exercised by the release operator. The exception does not waive source tests, current-build acceptance, independent verification, grading, or shipment checks; all other P-011 implementation and acceptance work uses staging/current-build.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-030 — Name canonical source falsifier scenarios without changing accepted behavior\nDate: 2026-10-22\nMeasured 2026-10-22: spec-test-adequacy.ts:2935-2944 rejects own-specId-only mutation proof when an explicit observation exists; spec-test-adequacy.test.ts:2754-2818 guards that rule. set-specs.ts:253-271 protects sourceBar-pinned behavior text, while unchanged behavior plus preserved sourceBar permits falsifier scenario enrichment. Archived consult conv-mvjjn0m4-0000-7b09c89a36614cdfb00cbc3a985367f3 independently confirmed this maintained route.\nAppend immutable revisions for the five scoped source clauses, preserving behavior, sourceBar, acceptanceRef, observation, evidence plane and all lifecycle/test requirements verbatim. Declare guide-size-ceiling and doc-claim-drift-detected for R6; default-on-relocation, environment-override-wins and disabled-layout-identical for R3; session-tail-sections-preserved and system-authority-wrapper-preserved for R4; the corresponding single scenario for each explicit SPEC clause. Bind canonical passing case identities to each scenario and the existing measured caught mutant to the exact scenario it exercised. Do not relabel a case to a scenario it does not exercise or claim all scenarios were mutation-tested. Preserve history and rebind only from authoritative measured receipts; no source rerun without relevant drift.\nThis enriches proof obligations, not the product contract or rubric4. D-028 remains binding: fixture absence still needs outside-lineage verification or genuine measured calibration, no self-grade/manual recruitment or production-subject relabeling. Whole-plan shipment and deployed R7/R9/R8 remain open.\nRelated: P-004, P-015\n\n### D-031 — Extend canonical source scenario linkage to the remaining source BARs\nDate: 2026-10-22\nMeasured: fire107 current-build inventory /tmp/c270-inventory107.json and read-only evaluator /tmp/c270-eval107-before.json show genuine source drift in su-persona-render.ts, capability/read.ts and scratch-reference.ts for R2/R4/R5/R10. R1 mutation receipts are current but lack a current positive binding. Current real-journal, real-playbook and real-spill conventional tests name the claimed scenarios; read.ts now delegates to read-handler.ts, whose bytes must be part of the reader's measurement basis.\nExtend D-030's maintained route to AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001, R2/P006, R4/P006, R5/P005 and R10/P005: append immutable revisions preserving behavior, observation, sourceBar, acceptanceRef and all lifecycle/test requirements. Declare only scenarios exercised by canonical tests: deduplicated requests and unknown usage; boundary placement/uniqueness/shared prefix; byte-preserved sections and authority wrapper; decoded matches, final-line match, negative coverage and refused references; all-page serialized-size ceiling. Bind exact passing cases and caught mutants to the scenarios they actually exercised. Refresh genuinely drifted source via maintained committed-snapshot tests and contained overlay mutations; reuse unchanged authoritative R1 receipts. Do not infer mutation coverage for unexercised scenarios. Preserve D-028, rubric4, accepted self route and separate deployed R7/R8/R9 obligations. This changes proof association, not accepted product behavior.\nRelated: P-001, P-005, P-006\n\n## Open approvals and dependencies\n\n- None owner-gated: D-008 records execution authorization.\n- Live evidence for P-014 depends on the green-checkpoint gate promoting staging to main. A peer-held gate is not this plan's lane.\n\n\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\nRecorded during the current source-proof recovery; this does not claim to reconstruct historical pre-design searches. No new durable surface is introduced by this recovery.\n\n```reuse\n{\n  \"searched\": [\n    {\n      \"where\": \"Current source-proof recovery on 2026-10-22\",\n      \"how\": \"Read canonical completeness and measured mutation proofs already cover the route.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"reused\": [\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"plans:set-specs\",\n      \"kind\": \"tool\",\n      \"provides\": \"Append proof obligations while preserving behavior and sourceBar provenance\",\n      \"items\": [\n        \"P-004\",\n        \"P-015\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"plans:bind-spec-evidence\",\n      \"kind\": \"tool\",\n      \"provides\": \"Bind current measured tests and mutations from recorded ledger runs\",\n      \"items\": [\n        \"P-004\",\n        \"P-015\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/cache-policy.ts\",\n      \"kind\": \"file\",\n      \"provides\": \"Existing prompt split, tail relocation and environment/flag resolution\",\n      \"items\": [\n        \"P-015\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"packages/operator-core/lib/su-persona-render.ts\",\n      \"kind\": \"file\",\n      \"provides\": \"Existing production prompt composition and per-session sections\",\n      \"items\": [\n        \"P-006\",\n        \"P-015\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"ref\": Existing work-items are the implementation records. No fleet or substitute work-items.\n\n### D-001 — Credential repair is optional to code acceptance; preserve source plan shipment\nDate: 2026-10-11\nThe implementation lane remains this AUTO self session and the six existing work-items. The shipped parent is not reopened. Source item comment1174051 withdrew the earlier re-login wall: aviynw10 repair is optional and no plan step waits on it. Runtime promotion is not inferred from these current-tree test results.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAmendment-Id: vpf-methods-checks-20261015-v1\nRequest-Hash: 7d72b7d394a70f3072b60e98612537b31435e2cb23168eaecbe42d9500d37112\nActor: su-ceb7cbd6-0692-4100-bc65-33bcee35d158\nReason: Bind the six existing follow-up outcomes to their canonical regression suites, preserving all BAR wording, mappings and the D-001 credential boundary.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6)\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 10 → 11\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-agent-control-mutex-root-migration-2026-10-12","title":"Acceptance BAR — Move agent mutex leases to a durable control-plane root","status":"active","created":"2026-10-12","owner":"su-1b17f319-1964-4537-bb02-fdd9b4cd67c0","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Move agent mutex leases to a durable control-plane root\nslug: acceptance-agent-control-mutex-root-migration-2026-10-12\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-12\nowner: su-1b17f319-1964-4537-bb02-fdd9b4cd67c0\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Move agent mutex leases to a durable control-plane root\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric).
