Fresh handoff unit18/18(test21251026), PTY adoption1pass120filtered(test21251095), native migration3/3(test21250613), fs-mutex54/54(test21250554), and caught mutant handoff21251094 plus saved five migration mutants. Terminal item closes remain refused while independent grading-integrity audits are pending. Acceptance rubric@1 still needs vetting and its four draft BAR projections need accepted evidence. Vetting consult conv-mv97jyjy-0000-f4a380cd8f0f47ccb09663d204b3bca6 returned no_available_responder; no response is incoming. P4 read-only07:17:40Z found legacy path already symlinking durable root; no live mutation or historical zero-census receipt is claimed.\n\n**Next:** Finish author-side BAR preparation and completion audit, settle exact seven independent adequacy audits through scorecards:repair, then obtain independent acceptance; preserve P4 as pre-existing-alias no-op without claiming cutover history.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014200 — Move the default mutex root to ~/.papercusp/fs-mutex-locks while preserving PAPERCUSP_FS_MUTEX_LOCK_DIR as the authoritative override. — note: Typed external admission blocker cleared after independe… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014278 — Propagate PAPERCUSP_FS_MUTEX_LOCK_DIR across SDK bootstrap, launcher, PTY handoff, host-code adoption, and host re-exec. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014279 — Implement the fail-closed legacy-root census and alias transition; preserve old markers and test active, unknown, unreadable, and quiesced cases in the project suite. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014288 — Perform live cutover only after a fresh read-only census reports zero active and zero unknown legacy leases; otherwise leave the old root untouched. <!-- P-004 -->\n## Background\n\n`ptool` acquires filesystem mutex leases before operator dispatch. The observed default places those control files on the shared bulk-scratch `/tmp` device, so ENOSPC can prevent the control plane from starting. The latest recorded read-only census (2026-10-12 12:49:19Z) found 5 active reader leases, 85 stale markers, and 0 unknown; no marker was changed, so live cutover remained blocked. The running `papercusp-dev-api.service` had no fs-mutex ordering. The normal launcher/PTY path preserves the explicit root, but host-code adoption drops it.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Preserve one durable mutex identity across a safe root migration.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Use a stable per-user home-directory default for fs-mutex control files while preserving PAPERCUSP_FS_MUTEX_LOCK_DIR through every process and host handoff, and retain a fail-closed legacy-root cutover.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"New Linux/macOS sessions resolve to ~/.papercusp/fs-mutex-locks unless the explicit override is set; the override survives SDK bootstrap, PTY handoff, and host-code adoption/re-exec; legacy-path aliasing occurs only after a fresh read-only census proves zero active and zero unknown leases, while the old markers remain preserved as evidence.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any covered handoff drops or changes the explicit override; new and legacy sessions can use distinct lock roots concurrently; an active, unknown, or unreadable census allows cutover; or stale legacy marker evidence is removed.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Add and run project-suite regression tests for default-root resolution, explicit override precedence, SDK/bootstrap and PTY/host handoffs, legacy-path aliasing, and fail-closed active/unknown/unreadable census cases. Use isolated temporary roots; do not mutate the live legacy marker tree.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/fs-mutex.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/scripts/ptool.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host.integration.test.ts\",\"scripts/npm-install-safe.test.mjs\"]},\"replication\":\"Run the listed canonical unit and integration suites with isolated temporary mutex roots. Verify default and override resolution across every named process handoff; exercise active, unknown, unreadable, and zero-active/zero-unknown legacy census states; confirm no live legacy marker is modified and stale evidence is retained.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nKeep the existing filesystem-mutex protocol and environment override. Change the default root to `~/.papercusp/fs-mutex-locks`; include the override in the host-code adoption allowlist. Preserve exclusion by making old and new paths resolve to one canonical lock directory. The only supported legacy transition is a read-only liveness preflight followed by an alias after active and unknown lease counts both reach zero. On any ambiguity, leave the legacy root untouched and fail closed. Preserve the old directory and its stale markers as quarantine evidence. Service ordering may be a secondary safeguard, never the sole ptool migration mechanism.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Implement and verify\n\n- **P-001** `done` Move the default mutex root to ~/.papercusp/fs-mutex-locks while preserving PAPERCUSP_FS_MUTEX_LOCK_DIR as the authoritative override. — note: ← WI-6554700010014200 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `blocked` Propagate PAPERCUSP_FS_MUTEX_LOCK_DIR across SDK bootstrap, launcher, PTY handoff, host-code adoption, and host re-exec. — note: ← WI-6554700010014278 blocked (1 external blocker)\n- **P-003** `blocked` Implement the fail-closed legacy-root census and alias transition; preserve old markers and test active, unknown, unreadable, and quiesced cases in the project suite. — note: ← WI-6554700010014279 blocked (1 external blocker)\n- **P-004** `blocked` Perform live cutover only after a fresh read-only census reports zero active and zero unknown legacy leases; otherwise leave the old root untouched. — note: ← WI-6554700010014288 blocked (2 external blockers)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Keep mutex-root migration in a focused plan\nDate: 2026-10-12\nAffects: durable-disk-and-checkpoint-recovery-2026-10-09\nKeep P-001 through P-004 in this focused plan rather than folding them into durable-disk-and-checkpoint-recovery-2026-10-09. That plan covers disk attribution, retention/admission, and checkpoint qualification; this plan changes filesystem-mutex identity and gates legacy-root aliasing on a fresh zero-active/zero-unknown census. The current read showed the related plan's P-001 todo and P-002 blocked, with no WIP items; current assignees were not established, so the scope decision does not rely on a live ownership claim.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"consult-backed-parking-2026-10-12","title":"Consult-backed parking: park is a peer review with a default and deadline; fix consult launch failures","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-10-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Consult-backed parking: park is a peer review with a default and deadline; fix consult launch failures\nslug: consult-backed-parking-2026-10-12\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-13, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate. Next repair: Run plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy for the mapped outcome with current fingerprints; fix every fail/unknown proof obligation before ship. A read-only shipReadiness probe supplies no current fingerprints, so freshness rates unknown and this code can persist however good the evidence is — supply current fingerprints before concluding the evidence itself is at fault. (R-10). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nAuthored 2026-10-12 by su-a2d144e1 under owner directive #1743 (AUTO); activation audit #1 recorded. Owner directive #1745 added Phase 4 (cross-backend psu --resume across claude, codex, omp, and resume inside PUI): R-10, R-11, P-010 to P-013. Consult launch overlap with get-feedback-reliability-usefulness-adoption-2026-10-03#P-002 (WI-10005889, su-e16e0da4) raised with its owner.\n\n**Next:** Re-audit activation for the Phase 4 scope, pass spec quality, plans:start, then implement P-001 (WI-6554700010009204).\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009489 — Diagnose and fix consults that select experts but record no launch attempt (WI-6554700010009204). (R-1) <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009490 — Launch a fresh answering session briefed with the expert's cited turns when the expert session cannot be forked or converted (Codex). (R-1) <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009491 — Give selected-but-unlaunchable consults their own state and update the get_feedback verdict and routing-health readers. (R-2) <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009492 — consult:reply stance for decision-review consults: support, object or no-view; objection needs reason plus alternative, or hazard evidence, or owner-authority basis. (R-4) <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009493 — work_items:set_blocker product-decision park door: require default and deadline, open the decision-review consult, record it on the blocker, register the setter's verdict wake, notify Avi. (R-3) <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009494 — Park resolver and triggers: deadline proceed with blocker clear, objection wake, adopt or rebut, owner question with both options, owner override; emit the verdict event. (R-10, R-11) <!-- P-013 -->\n## Goal\n\nMake parking a short peer review instead of a stop. When an agent cannot decide alone, it states its default and a deadline; the consult system routes the question to peers; objections must carry an alternative; silence means proceed; real disagreement reaches Avi as one two-option question, and owner-only topics (spend, destructive, publish, credentials, security) open the review but never auto-proceed, reaching Avi the same way; the parked agent is woken with the verdict. Prerequisite: fix the consult launch failures (WI-6554700010009204) so peers actually answer. Evidence measured 2026-10-12 is on WI-6554700010009204.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Autonomous agents that hit a judgment call mid-task, the peers who review their proposals, and Avi as owner.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Agents park on judgment calls they could decide (161 open product-decision holds on 2026-10-12, 122 written by agents), and the peer-consult system that should answer them ends without any answer for 60-75% of agent questions since 2026-10-07 because selected experts cannot be launched. Moving a session to another backend uses the same session-port seam and is unreliable: over 21 days claude to codex ports failed 131 times out of 267, and omp has never been a port target.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Parking becomes a short peer review: the agent states what it will do and by when, peers can object only with a reason and an alternative, silence means proceed, real disagreement or owner-only topics reach Avi as a two-option choice, and the parked agent is woken with the verdict.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Changing expert selection, the relevance floor or min-fill, which already work.\",\n    \"Letting peers approve spending, deletion, publishing, credentials or security changes.\",\n    \"Reworking the 21 improvement-policy holds and 18 plan-lane cascaded holds, or re-parking the existing 122 agent-written holds (follow-up work-items).\",\n    \"The Sep 9-24 undispatched grading-integrity consults, which stopped on Sep 24.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n Governing decisions: consult-backed-parking-2026-10-12#D-006.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/psu-pui-resume.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/lib/pui-resume.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n## Design\n\nReuse, not new systems: the park door is the existing work_items:set_blocker product-decision path; the review is a get_feedback consult with a decision-review cascade flavour; the resolver rides the existing cascade advance and the consult expiry sweep; the verdict is a latched awaited event registered for the parking agent at park time; the owner notice and owner question reuse notifications and coord:ask-owner.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-010, P-011, P-013 | live |\n| R-11 | P-012 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-005, P-006 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-010, P-011 | tree |\n| R-24 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-25 | P-012 | tree |\n\nResume across backends reuses the existing session-port convert (packages/operator-core/lib/session-port, psu-launcher launchSessionPort) and native adapters for claude, codex and omp; no new conversion path. Consult conversions use the same seam, so fixes here also serve R-1.\n\n## Phase 1 — Consults reach an answer\n\n- **P-001** `done` Diagnose and fix consults that select experts but record no launch attempt (WI-6554700010009204). (R-10, R-11) blocked-by: P-010, P-011, P-012 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010009500 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n## Non-goals and follow-ups\n\n- System-generated product-decision holds (21 improvement-policy, 18 plan-lane cascaded) and the existing 122 agent-written holds: follow-up work-items.\n- Expert selection and min-fill are unchanged; they work.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Park door is the existing product-decision blocker, not a new verb\nDate: 2026-10-12\nAgents already reach for work_items:set_blocker product-decision (122 open agent-written holds on 2026-10-12). Avi's adherence argument (session_turn:claude:4065dd5b-bd45-4315-9b5f-c1907901712d:0): keep the safe-feeling door and change what is behind it. Reuse-first: no new park verb.\nRelated: P-005\n\n### D-002 — Silence means proceed at the deadline\nDate: 2026-10-12\nMost consults end with no reply, so a park that waits for an answer would stall like parking does today. A park with no standing objection at its deadline resolves to proceed. Default deadline 60 minutes, bounded 15 to 1440. Sources: session_turn:claude:4065dd5b-bd45-4315-9b5f-c1907901712d:3, session_turn:claude:4065dd5b-bd45-4315-9b5f-c1907901712d:25.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-003 — Objections must carry a reason and an alternative\nDate: 2026-10-12\nOwner requirement (session_turn:claude:4065dd5b-bd45-4315-9b5f-c1907901712d:16). Two exceptions may block without an alternative: a hazard with evidence, and an owner-authority topic (spend, destructive, publish, credentials, security).\nRelated: P-004, P-006\n\n### D-004 — Peer outcomes are never recorded as owner approval\nDate: 2026-10-12\nA proceed or adopt outcome is recorded as peer review on the blocker history and work-item. Owner-authority parks never auto-proceed; they become one owner question with both options while the agent keeps working.\nRelated: P-005, P-006\n\n### D-005 — Consult launch reliability is a prerequisite\nDate: 2026-10-12\nMeasured 2026-10-12: 60-75% of agent consults since 2026-10-07 end without an answering session because selected experts cannot be launched (Codex fork-unsupported, plus an unrecorded path). Phase 1 ships before parking depends on consults. Evidence: WI-6554700010009204.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-006 — PUI resume keeps the session's original backend\nDate: 2026-10-12\nOwner directive #1745 (session_turn:claude:8a2e6ec3-72a8-4bbb-bf45-e804ed2b99d1:7) says PUI 'can just use the original backend because our pui interacts with it through the model tui and wraps around it'. Reading [inferred from that turn]: a PUI resume reopens the session in its original backend's TUI inside the PUI wrapper; converting to another backend from PUI is not required. A cross-backend pick from PUI must still either complete through the normal session port or be refused with a clear message, never leave a broken pane. Cross-backend psu --resume outside PUI must work for all six claude/codex/omp pairs (R-10).\nRelated: P-012, P-013\n\n### D-007 — Cross-backend resume reuses the session port\nDate: 2026-10-12\npsu --resume to another backend already routes through the session port (psu-launcher launchSessionPort, packages/operator-core/lib/session-port) with native adapters for claude, codex and omp. Phase 4 fixes that seam rather than adding a second conversion path. Measured 2026-10-12 over 21 days of harness_shared.session_ports: claude>codex 131 delivered / 131 failed / 5 expired; codex>claude 98 / 12 / 8; codex>codex 53 / 2; claude>claude 25 / 10 / 5; omp>codex 1 delivered; omp never a target. Consult conversions share the seam, so the same rows include consult traffic (no purpose field to separate them). The seam is also in scope of get-feedback-reliability-usefulness-adoption-2026-10-03#P-002 (WI-10005889, su-e16e0da4); coordination sent 2026-10-12 17:59Z.\nRelated: P-010, P-011\n\n### D-008 — P-002 narrows to sources the session port skips on purpose; P-001 finding\nDate: 2026-10-12\nRuling from su-e16e0da4 (owner of get-feedback-reliability-usefulness-adoption-2026-10-03#P-002, WI-10005889), coord-send-18943bb5 2026-10-12 18:06Z: WI-10005889 already converts tracked plain-SU Codex consult sources through the isolated session port; reuse it, no second answering launcher. Skips stay intentional for untracked native and non-plain-SU sources. P-002 therefore covers ONLY those skipped sources: a fresh answering session briefed with the expert's cited turns, launched under a distinct identity with explicit provenance that it is a cited-turn brief, never presented as transcript continuity. su-e16e0da4 is not changing psu-launcher or session-port/service in its current continuation, so Phase 4 may edit them.\n\nP-001 measurement (consult_state, papercusp-workspace, non-system requesters, 5 days to 2026-10-12 18:05Z): 162 consults ended no_qualified_responder with a non-empty selection and empty dispatch_attempts. All 162 carry latency_contract 'proceed'; wakes_used 4/4 on 78, 0 on 34, 1-3 on 50; exchanges_used 0 on all; 83 record a selection refill 'cascade exhausted with 0 answer(s) < min 1'. Reading [inferred, to verify in code]: these consults woke live experts through the cascade instead of launching an answering session, and nothing launches one when the live experts stay silent. Overlap with WI-10007567 (su-e16e0da4, get-feedback-core recovery semantics) to be checked before editing get-feedback-core.ts.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-009 — R-10 is proven live, and no backend pair may be refused wholesale\nDate: 2026-10-12\nContext: the outside-lineage reviewer of the R-10/R-11 bar amendment (thread-post 1176525 on WI-6554700010009204) objected that R-10 as a tree/unit bar could be graded healthy while psu --resume delivery still failed, because request-shape unit tests and implementer-written codex transcript fixtures cannot catch a mismatch with what the real CLI writes. Decision: R-10's evidence plane is live on staging-operator; the grader cites, per ordered pair, a session_ports row in state delivered and the target CLI's native transcript in which the production reader finds the seed (P-013). Per-cause unit regression tests stay. The refusal clause covers only a single session that cannot be resumed (untracked, missing source transcript); refusing or hiding a whole pair fails R-10, so P-011 must support OMP in both directions rather than refuse OMP pairs. Rejected: an integration layer that drives real target CLIs in CI, because it needs live provider credentials in the test environment; the live P-013 run already exercises real CLIs.\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-12\nAmendment-Id: consult-backed-parking-r10-r11-live-v2\nRequest-Hash: cee0f7a58d299bacf94abc7005fffed18d3b99ef7e95b8d07d83a2d3da103838\nActor: su-a2d144e1-4576-4511-8c32-3bf4de08bd29\nReason: Add R-10 (cross-backend psu --resume, now live-plane per outside-lineage objection thread-post:1176525) and R-11 (PUI resume) from owner directive #1745; D-009 records the repair.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-2af68b37-02df-4067-b76d-55103f852c94\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1176616\nApproved-At: 2026-10-12T18:24:21.890Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 22 → 23\nChanged BARs: R-10, R-11\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-011 — Split compound acceptance bars into single-behavior bars (R-12..R-25)\nDate: 2026-10-12\nplans:start was refused by spec quality (atomic-observable-behavior): BAR R-1, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-10 and R-11 each held several observable behaviors. Plan revisions 24-26 split them into 25 single-sentence bars (R-12..R-25 added) and every existing bar-to-item pair is kept, so no AUTO-BAR projection is orphaned. R-10 stays the live delivery bar for P-010/P-011/P-013; picker rows (R-22), single-session refusal before spawn (R-23) and the four measured session-port causes (R-24) are now separate tree bars. Every clause removed from a condition reappears as its own bar or in a falsifier. All 25 conditions pass specBehaviorNonAtomicReason (positive control: the old R-10 is flagged). Rubric amendment rev 2 -> 3 awaits an outside-lineage reviewer (preview thread-post:1177825 on WI-6554700010009204).\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-12\nAmendment-Id: cbp-atomic-bar-split-v1\nRequest-Hash: 67d7266c88a4b16c471a3f98126c1286e05912d6bb26852929e4c3bb23c63da3\nActor: su-a2d144e1-4576-4511-8c32-3bf4de08bd29\nReason: Spec quality (atomic-observable-behavior) refused plans:start. Split compound BARs R-1, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-10 and R-11 into single-behavior bars (R-12..R-25 added). Every existing bar-to-item pair is kept, meaning is unchanged, and every clause removed from a bar's condition reappears as a separate bar or in a falsifier. Plan revision 26 carries the matching requirement blocks and bar-to-work map.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-c2da6da4-b3dd-4e6b-9f39-c74bd665c130\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1177827\nApproved-At: 2026-10-12T23:41:21.780Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 28 → 29\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19, R-20, R-21, R-22, R-23, R-24, R-25\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-013 — Park storage contract between P-004/P-005 and the P-006 resolver\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAgreed 2026-10-13 between su-d03468f4 (P-004, P-005) and su-dac6e2ea (P-006). One pure module, packages/operator-core/lib/consult/decision-review.ts, owns the shapes. Park identity rides consult_state.routing.cascade as DecisionReviewCascadeMeta {flavor: decision-review, workItemId, setterId, defaultAction, deadlineAt (ISO), ownerAuthorityTopic: spend, destructive, publish, credentials, security or null}, read with decisionReviewMetaFromRouting; the consult id is consult_state.conversation_id. Reviewer stances are stored on consult_post_meta.stance jsonb (migration 1482) as DecisionReviewStance: support or no-view with optional reason, or object with basis alternative (reason, alternative), hazard (reason, evidence list) or owner-authority (topic, optional reason). Only responder replies carry a stance, validated by validateDecisionReviewStance. Parker adopt and rebut responses are owned by P-006. The verdict event key is consult:park-verdict:<consultId> with the payload proposed by su-dac6e2ea in coord-send-321a072b; P-005 registers the setter's await on it.\n\n### D-014 — R-10 live evidence comes from the P-013 matrix; P-013 waits on code on :3170, not on item closure\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\nContext: su-ce4ad82a (P-011, WI-6554700010009276) reported a cycle. AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-011@3 (and AUTO-BAR-R-10-P-010@3) need R-10's live evidence per D-009: a session_ports row in state 'delivered' plus the target CLI's native transcript in which the production reader finds the seed, for each ordered pair. That evidence is P-013's matrix, and P-013 is blocked-by P-010, P-011 and P-012.\nRuling: (1) The bar-to-item pairs stay. AUTO-BAR-R-10 is not removed from P-010 or P-011, so there is no rubric amend and no re-vetting. (2) P-013's blocked-by edges mean that the P-010/P-011/P-012 code is committed and served by the staging operator :3170. They do not mean those items are closed. P-013 starts as soon as that code is on :3170. (3) The fleet leader (su-a2d144e1) runs P-013. It covers all six ordered pairs across claude, codex and omp, including both OMP directions. Each pair records its session_ports row id, the target transcript path and the reader hit in a committed docs/evidence JSON registered with testing:record-run. (4) Each item owner binds the resulting test runs to its own AUTO-BAR-R-10 clause as evidenceKind test with live-plane adequacy, then closes. P-010 and P-011 stay blocked (work_items:set_blocker naming the P-013 work item) until those rows exist. (5) R-11 (PUI resume) stays inside P-012.\n\n### D-015 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: cbp-vet-repair-r4-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: ce0622c6e3a6fe6aa35b4bfa6240596dd70f92ff488585f6807e9d1c78c66654\nActor: su-a2d144e1-4576-4511-8c32-3bf4de08bd29\nReason: Rubric vet (conv-mv5yv4pf, su-345115d9, rev 3 NOT attestable): (A) R-10 is live per D-009, so its check moves from the R-22 unit file to manual-provenance instrument none with per-pair artifact citation; (B) check.files path fixes for R-2 (lane answer f4fac2af), R-23/R-24 (no routes/), R-11/R-25 (psu-pui-resume.test.ts, lane answer ce4ad82a), R-8 (lane answer d03468f4); (D) numbered falsifier markers on R-8, R-10, R-24; (F) partition notes R-14/R-17 and R-5/R-9; (G) governing D-numbers in method text. Bar meaning is unchanged.\nApproved-By: su-2363588e-3bcc-46e5-8095-852d9f581f9b\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1177975\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T01:27:33.631Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 36 → 37\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-8, R-10, R-11, R-23, R-24, R-25\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-016 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: cbp-r24-bind-causes-v1\nRequest-Hash: 4c17c70da89284b84b9b056fa5a2edb34c057da0f970a7e1a41f839b99800653\nActor: su-a2d144e1-4576-4511-8c32-3bf4de08bd29\nReason: Rubric rev4 vet (conv-mv608ktc, su-2dd3ceee, thread-post:1177986) B2: R-24 method demands one regression case per measured cause but its check bound only the files for cause (2). Bind the existing tracked tests for causes (1), (3) and (4) and name the case per cause in the method. Bar sentence unchanged; additive per approvalClassification.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-24)\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 40 → 41\nChanged BARs: R-24\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-017 — Rubric rev 5: R-24 binds one test per measured cause; R-9 path kept, P-009 reassigned\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\nRubric rev4 vet (conv-mv608ktc, su-2dd3ceee, thread-post:1177986) was NOT attestable: B1 R-9's bound file packages/operator-core/lib/consult/park.integration.test.ts does not exist; B2 R-24 bound only the files for cause (2); P1 R-8's test was untracked.\nRulings: (1) R-24 amended to rev 5 (additive, no approval required; idempotencyKey cbp-r24-bind-causes-v1). Check now binds psu-pty-host.integration.test.ts (cause 1 child-exit; cause 3 refusal side missing-native-marker), psu-pty-host-kickoff-activity.test.ts (cause 3 codex reader past 256 KiB), bootstrap-su.test.ts (cause 4 prepared auto account), beside the two cause-2 files. requiredTestLayers unit+integration. (2) R-9 keeps its path. The test is written at that exact path, not re-pointed. P-009 (WI-6554700010009498) moved from su-dac6e2ea (who keeps P-006/P-007) to su-d03468f4. (3) R-8's files are committed in 4dd2030bfc, so P1 is cleared. Re-vet rev 5 once park.integration.test.ts is committed.\n\n### D-018 — Amendment-seeded AUTO-BAR clauses promoted to active; emit on :3070 refuses draft clauses\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n\nContext: The acceptance BARs added by amendment D-012 and later (R-12..R-25) were seeded as DRAFT AUTO-BAR clauses. Two problems followed. (1) On :3070 (build d740fc3802), scorecards:emit replays the evaluator with includeDraft:false, so a terminal card for a draft clause is refused 'evaluator replay refused: selection_empty'. That build forces the flag; source fixed it in 7e52d79c25 (2026-10-06); :3170 has the fix. (2) At ship, the acceptance BAR gate raises bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted for any BAR whose clauses are all draft (acceptance-bar-lifecycle-evaluator.ts phase 'ship').\n\nRuling: the leader promoted all 16 draft AUTO-BAR clauses to lifecycleStatus 'active' at 02:12Z via plans:set-specs, with behavior, falsifier, sourceBar and acceptanceRef unchanged. Each promotion appended one revision (most @1 -> @2; R-23-P-010 and R-23-P-011 -> @3; R-24-P-010 -> @4; R-12-P-001 -> @2) and carried bound evidence forward (evidenceCarriedForward reported per clause).\n\nWhat members do: re-read your clause revision with plans:get-specs before evaluating. Evaluate with includeDraft:false. A scorecard already filed against a pre-promotion revision is stale for that clause: re-evaluate and re-emit at the current revision. Do not re-bind evidence that was carried forward.\n\nEvidence: emit refusal on WI-6554700010009489 (02:01Z); tool_invocations 37255386/37255388 show the replay with includeDraft:false; R-12-P-001 emitted after promotion as EI-25828339234183319. Filed defect: EI-25827796148921513.\n\n### D-019 — P-002 live evidence: forced organic probe in P-002 itself, not the P-013 matrix\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\nContext: su-f4fac2af (P-002, WI-6554700010009490) reports that organic consult routing prefers plain live sessions, so the brief launch (an expert that cannot be forked) is never reached. They proposed a D-014-style ruling in which P-013's matrix supplies P-002's R-1 live evidence.\nRuling: (1) P-013 does NOT absorb the P-002 probe. P-013 exercises psu --resume session ports, a different surface from the consult router, and mixing them would blur both evidence sets. (2) P-002 owns its live probe and forces it ORGANICALLY. Pick an expert whose session cannot be forked (role != null, or an untracked source), and compose the consult:get_feedback question from a distinctive passage of that expert's transcript, so the router ranks it first through normal scoring. Record the consult_state.routing showing the brief launch plus the answering session's dispatch. (3) No test-only routing pin goes into production code. (4) If two crafted questions still fail to rank the unforkable expert first, that is a routing finding: file it as a work item with the scores, and P-002 closes on the committed tests, the mutation probe and that filed finding, which records the residue.\nWhy: a live R-1 claim must come from the production router, and a pin would prove the pin, not routing.\n\n### D-020 — P-002 keeps SPEC-P-002's live requirement; fix the router (WI-6554700010009707) instead of narrowing the spec\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n\nContext: su-f4fac2af (P-002, WI-6554700010009490) reports SPEC-P-002@1 requires live-plane evidence while D-019(4) lets P-002 close without the P-013 matrix. Organic consult routing never surfaces an unforkable (Codex role) expert as a candidate (WI-6554700010009707), so the brief launch P-002 builds is never reached live.\n\nRuling (adopts su-f4fac2af's stated default b): (1) SPEC-P-002 is NOT narrowed to the tree plane. If organic routing cannot reach the brief launch, the feature is unreachable in production; narrowing the spec would hide that defect. (2) P-002 is blocked on WI-6554700010009707 (work_items:set_blocker / link blocks). su-f4fac2af fixes the relevance router so an unforkable expert is surfaced as a candidate, with a regression test. (3) After the fix is live on :3170, P-002 runs the forced organic probe per D-019(2) and binds it to SPEC-P-002 and AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-002 as operational evidence. (4) D-019's other rulings stand; this decision supersedes only D-019(4)'s implication that P-002 may close without live evidence. Recorded by the plan leader su-a2d144e1.\n\n### D-021 — Live resume matrix re-run is the last evidence step; psu-launcher/psu-pty-host edits stale it\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\nContext: The P-013 live matrix receipt bindings (40554, 40607, 40608) pin apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs and apps/operator/scripts/psu-pty-host.mjs by content hash. Freshness is server-measured per file, so any edit to either file stales the live plane for R-10-P-010, R-10-P-013 and SPEC-P-010. The WI-6554700010009740 fix (psu-pty-host.mjs 87b4114a -> 93cb45ea) staled all three.\nRuling: (1) The leader re-runs the matrix exactly once, after every in-flight edit to those two files has landed (P-011 included), then rebinds superseding the stale rows. (2) After that re-run, any member about to edit either file messages the leader first, because the edit forces another hour-long live re-run. (3) Unit and integration R-24 bindings pinning psu-pty-host.mjs are rebound after the commit, independently of the matrix.\n\n### D-022 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAmendment-Id: su212d-r12-detector-binding-apply-20261015-v1\nRequest-Hash: 927c28318c277ef5775eb8e262c514910307443954cfeb0bfad8be492198d704\nActor: su-212d9806-6115-4ef6-9f90-55d0da7211ea\nReason: Repair detector under-binding found by rev7 attestation audit EI-26034687869449907: R12 covers every selected expert, whereas its existing bound dispatch file tests one expert/model-rank walk. Blocked by P-004, P-005, P-006. <!-- P-007 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi (owner), plus every agent and service on this dev box. When / or /mnt/data runs out, git fetches, builds, Postgres writes, the gate and /tmp scratch writes all start failing.\n\n**Problem.** The disk refills within days of every manual cleanup: Sep 26 (#637/#638), Oct 5 (#1346), Oct 6 (WI-10006692) and Oct 10 (#1611). Owner turn #1704 (2026-10-12): \"we are low on disk space again but another agent was supposed to have written a durable fix already, why didn't it work?\" Measured cause:\n- Every 'durable' follow-up was parked or unowned: WI-10008196 (testcontainer leak fix) and WI-10006692 (standing reclaim). WI-10007558 (/mnt/data reclaim) was dropped. Plan durable-disk-and-checkpoint-recovery-2026-10-09 has been stuck in draft on bar-readiness since 2026-10-10.\n- What exists either only detects (disk alarms, 100 GiB floor live since 2026-10-12 08:12 EDT) or reclaims classes that are not growing. papercup-docker-reclaim reclaimed -3 MiB on 2026-10-12; tmp-scratch-reclaim covers /tmp only. VH retention fires only below the 40.28 GiB reserve and is gated never-auto.\n- The one reclaim that needed an owner decision asked it through coord:ask-owner (conv-mv2bf0pz). Its default-if-unanswered was 'do nothing', and it sat unanswered for 2 days.\n\n**Outcome.** / and /mnt/data stay at or above 100 GiB free with no manual cleanup. When automatic reclaim can't reach that, Avi gets one alarm that names the consumers and the decision needed, through a channel that reaches him.\n\n**Non-goals.** Never delete owner data: /mnt/data Backup/kopia repo, recordings, Debug, back, db. No swapfile resize (needs a reboot). No schema change to evidence tables without a recorded decision. Not the GB/GiB label bug EI-25776083529742160 (owned by su-7a64881b). Not checkpoint candidate/finalization repair (stays on durable-disk-and-checkpoint-recovery-2026-10-09 P-003).\n\n**Source turns.** #1611 (2026-10-10, \"aim for an 100gb buffer\"), #1704 (2026-10-12), owner choice C on #1704 (2026-10-12; uncaptured, recorded on WI-6554700010008919).\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. A week passes with normal fleet load. Both devices stay at or above 100 GiB free, and each reclaim run leaves a receipt (what it deleted, bytes freed).\n2. A new artifact class starts growing. The daily census shows it within 24h; the alarm names it before the 100 GiB floor is crossed.\n3. Reclaim can't reach the floor without touching protected data. Avi gets one actionable alarm; nothing protected is deleted.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Consumer census.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Find what is filling / and /mnt/data so a 100 GiB free buffer can be held (owner #1611; session 24f9a988 turn 6).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A per-consumer size census for / and /mnt/data is written to Postgres on a schedule, and one read shows each consumer's size and its 24h growth.\",\"falsifier\":\"A device with no census rows in the last 24h, or a consumer larger than 10 GiB that the census does not list.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Extend packages/operator-core/lib/storage/usage.ts. Run the unit test (consumer attribution, 24h delta) and the integration test that writes and reads census rows in PG; then compare the live top consumers for both devices against du on the same paths.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/usage.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-consumer-census.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Written retention policy.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A written keep/delete rule so the cleanup can delete on its own without asking (owner D-002, session 24f9a988 turn 9).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every agent-generated artifact class that the census reports has exactly one keep rule in the written retention policy.\",\"falsifier\":\"A census consumer that maps to no policy class or to two conflicting ones; a policy with no explicit protected (never-delete) set, or one missing a D-002 never-delete path (/mnt/data Backup/kopia, recordings, Debug, db, back, or the swapfile); or a protected path that the reclaim selector would yield.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the policy unit test, which loads the policy and asserts every class has a keep rule and the selector never yields a protected path; then match the latest census consumers to policy classes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/retention-policy.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Standing reclaim.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"One scheduled cleanup that keeps both disks at or above 100 GiB free (owner #1611 and choice C).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every scheduled reclaim run leaves a Postgres receipt showing each device at or above 100 GiB free or with no policy-eligible artifact left.\",\"falsifier\":\"No scheduled reclaim routine, or a scheduled interval with no run and receipt; a run with no Postgres receipt for either device; a run that deletes a path the retention policy does not make eligible (kept by its class keep rule, or in no class); a run that deletes a newer eligible artifact while an older one of the same class remains (not oldest first); a run that skips expired, unprotected policy-eligible artifacts merely because free space is already at or above 100 GiB; a census or df reading taken at the end of a run that shows a device under 100 GiB free while unprotected policy-eligible artifacts remain; a deleted path from the protected set; or a second reclaim actor for the same artifact class.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-reclaim.test.ts for selection by class keep rule, oldest first and never protected. Run packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-reclaim.integration.test.ts on a fixture tree: verify expired items are removed even without low-space samples and above the 100 GiB target; recent descendants, symlinks, live holders and incomplete holder scans stay protected; audit failure prevents effects; read the exact receipt from real Postgres. Inspect the existing DBOS diskRetentionReclaim schedule (hourly at :12) and recorded disk-retention-reclaim step/audit_log receipts; confirm a scheduled interval produced a receipt for both devices. D-005 makes expiry independent of free space; the 100 GiB target remains the alarm floor.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/prune.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-reclaim.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-reclaim.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Testcontainer leak fixed.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Fix the leaking test containers (owner choice C scope).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Repeated test runs leave no superseded or failed-start Postgres test container behind.\",\"falsifier\":\"An exited or orphaned Postgres test container that outlives the run that created it, or growth in exited test containers over a day.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the pg-container unit test with a failed start and a superseded container, asserting both are removed; then count exited test containers with docker ps -a before and after a test run.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/test-config/src/pg-container.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Postgres growth bounded.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Check Postgres growth (owner choice C scope).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Per-table growth of the papercusp database is measured, and every growing table without retention either gets a retention rule or has an owner decision recorded on this plan.\",\"falsifier\":\"A table among the 20 largest or fastest-growing with neither a retention rule nor a recorded decision.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the native storage.pg-table-growth instrument over a completed plan window. It reads two same-workspace, same-host, same-database per-table catalog samples 24–30 hours apart from the existing storage alarm audit ledger, reports the top 20 largest and fastest-growing tables, and leaves missing, recreated, incomplete or unowned-retention coverage unknown.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"storage.pg-table-growth\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Actionable alarm.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The alarm must say what is filling the disk, and owner questions must reach Avi instead of defaulting to nothing (session 24f9a988 turn 0).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Whenever either device is under 100 GiB free, a disk alarm naming the top consumers on both devices is raised.\",\"falsifier\":\"A census sample under 100 GiB free with no alarm; an alarm with no consumer names or no link to the last reclaim receipt; or a pending owner decision with no owner-facing ask on a channel that reaches Avi.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the alarm unit tests with a census fixture and a receipt, asserting the rendered alarm names consumers on both devices and carries the receipt link; then inspect the last live alarm.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-space-alarm.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/storage/storage-growth-alarm.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Soak.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Prove the buffer holds (owner #1611).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For 72 hours after the reclaim ships, / and /mnt/data stay at or above 100 GiB free, or the alarm fires naming the consumers.\",\"falsifier\":\"A census sample under 100 GiB free with no alarm, or an alarm that names no consumers.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the census rows for both devices across the 72h window and every alarm fired in it; confirm each dip under 100 GiB has an alarm naming consumers.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"storage:disk-headroom-post-shipment-72h\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nReuse first: extend the existing storage layer (packages/operator-core/lib/storage: usage, storage-growth-alarm, disk-space-alarm, prune) and the existing reclaim actors (bin/reclaim-docker-disk.sh on papercup-docker-reclaim.timer, papercup-tmp-scratch-reclaim, the VH pruneRunsWithReport). P004's already-authorized scratch work may proceed independently of R5 governance; no historical cleanup/test replay merely to settle a record.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-007\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"mobile-agent-sessions-2026-10-12","title":"Mobile agent sessions — view and talk to every agent session from iPhone and Android","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Mobile agent sessions — view and talk to every agent session from iPhone and Android\nslug: mobile-agent-sessions-2026-10-12\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-22, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted. (R-42). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nP-007 is blocked/self-owned on WI-6554700010009772 with typed dependency harness:papercup-rust-mobile. This session's papercusp hive cannot access mobile core/CI; coordinator confirmed the launch grant does not expand that scope. Permitted preparation is complete: current :3170 lint has no errors and five advisory dependency warnings, and spec-quality verdict passes. P-001–P-006 and P-017 are done. P-005 is done with completionAuthority proposed; independent acceptance is not asserted. No source changes, phone acceptance, credential actions, or independent acceptance upgrades claimed.\n\n**Next:** Coordinator/Avi: resolve the explicit mobile-hive scope boundary or rescope/handoff with authoritative evidence; then this assigned route resumes from WI-6554700010009772's checkpoint by inspecting existing core/UniFFI before rebuilding and obtaining the named cross-platform CI proof. No recurring monitor is armed while this external authority blocker remains.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Source turn:** owner directive #1747, 2026-10-12 [owner:Avi 2026-10-12]: *\"do our android and iphone apps allow for viewing all agent sessions and interacting with them?  If not write a plan for adding that feature\"*. The owner-dialog answers in the same session (turn 15) set D-001..D-004.\n\n**Audience:** the owner, using the paired iPhone/Android companion app (papercup-rust-mobile) away from the desktop.\n\n**Problem:** On the phone today, the owner can see how many agents exist but not which ones, what any of them is doing, or how to reach one. The desktop already does all three through the Sessions roster and the session chat popup.\n\n**Outcome:** From either phone, the owner can:\n1. see every agent session in the paired workspace (live, parked, recently ended);\n2. open any session and read its current intent, held work item and live/recent transcript;\n3. send that session a message that wakes it, and see what happened to the message;\n4. end a session;\n5. get a push notification when an agent messages them.\n\n**Non-goals (v1):**\n- Launching or resuming sessions from the phone.\n- An interrupt/yield control (not selected, D-003).\n- Approving tool permissions or editing files from the phone.\n- Browsing sessions outside the device's workspace.\n- A raw tool-output viewer.\n- Per-device send rate limiting or abuse throttling (D-011).\n- Replacing the Operator tab's chat with the operator brain.\n\n**Scenarios:**\n- **S1 — Roster.** Fleet → Sessions shows every session, grouped by fleet/pot, with its state badge, intent and last activity. It can be filtered and searched.\n- **S2 — Read.** Tapping a session shows a header (intent, work item, state) and a condensed transcript. The transcript keeps updating while the screen is open, and older turns load on scroll.\n- **S3 — Talk.** The owner sends \"stop and checkpoint\". The app shows the outcome: woken, staged, queued or agent ended.\n- **S4 — Push.** An agent messages the owner, a push arrives, and tapping it opens that session.\n- **S5 — End.** The owner ends a session from the phone after a confirm dialog. Its state turns to ended on both the phone and the desktop.\n- **S6 — Revocation.** The owner revokes the phone, and every session route refuses it immediately.\n\n## Current state (evidence, 2026-10-12)\n\n- **Mobile apps** (`papercup-rust-mobile`, SwiftUI + Compose over a Rust core with UniFFI). The iPhone `Tab` enum in `ios/Papercup/Sources/Papercup/AppRoot.swift` is inbox / operatorTab / plans / brew (\"Fleet\") / settings, and Android `MainActivity.kt` `Route` mirrors it.\n  - Fleet (`BrewView`) only shows aggregates from `/api/device/monitoring`: per fleet the member count, live count and leader; per pot the agent count and live count (`crates/papercup-core/src/types.rs`).\n  - The Operator tab talks to the single operator brain (`/api/device/operator/converse`), not to individual sessions.\n- **Device API** (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/*`, ingress list `packages/operator-core/lib/device-ingress-paths.ts`): has no session roster, transcript, send or end route. `/device/rest-query` is an explicit `switch` allowlist with nothing session-related in it.\n- **Desktop pieces to reuse, not fork (D-005/D-011 of goals-tab-improvement-2026-08-09):**\n  - Sync queries `advRoster.list`, `advSessions.list`, `agentDetail.byOwner` and `agentOrders.byOwner` (`packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/index.ts`).\n  - Transcript SSE `/api/adv/session/thinking`, built by `buildSessionStreamUrl`. It includes the ended-session archive fallback (EI-16982).\n  - Send: `sendToSessionOwner` calls `/api/admin/coord/send { wake:'required' }`, and `deliveryFromSendResponse` classifies the result. Both are in `apps/operator/app/_components/chat/use-owner-session-chat.ts`.\n  - Session-window routes under `/adv/sessions/*` (e.g. `close-window`).\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Roster population.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"view all agent sessions on the phone\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Over the complete unfiltered cursor walk of a fixed roster snapshot, GET /device/sessions returns exactly the desktop Sessions roster population for the device's workspace\",\"falsifier\":\"the complete unfiltered cursor walk omits a desktop session identity or includes an identity outside that workspace's desktop population\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run sessions.test.ts over a fixed fixture containing active, starting, pending, ended and workspace-agnostic sessions plus foreign-workspace controls. Walk all unfiltered bounded pages to nextCursor=null, union row identities and compare that set with the desktop reader for that snapshot. R-22 independently checks visit-once and no-gap traversal.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Transcript.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"see what a session is doing\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"GET /device/sessions/:owner/transcript returns, one bounded page at a time, the same condensed entries the desktop session stream shows for the same session and cursor range\",\"falsifier\":\"for the same session and cursor range the device entries differ from the desktop stream, an ended session returns nothing while the desktop shows its archive, a cursor page repeats or skips entries, or a request with no limit returns more than one page\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the route test with live, ended (archive) and paged fixtures, comparing device pages with the desktop stream entries for the same range, plus a request with no limit.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-transcript.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Send.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"interact with a session\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"POST /device/sessions/:owner/messages delivers through the same coord:send path as the desktop with wake required and returns the delivery outcome as woken, staged, queued or absent\",\"falsifier\":\"the device send bypasses coord:send, does not request a wake, or reports an outcome that differs from the coord:send result for the same send\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run session-messages.test.ts and device-actions.integration.test.ts for route/real-PG dispatch and retry behavior, plus owner-sessions/actions.test.ts for the real shared sender's woken, staged, queued and absent classification and desktop/device dispatch parity. Require all four distinct outcomes with wake required.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-messages.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/owner-sessions/device-actions.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/owner-sessions/actions.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Authority and safety.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"sessions on the phone must not widen who can act as the owner\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every device session route refuses a request that has no valid device JWT, or whose device lacks the per-device Agent sessions capability, including a device whose capability was revoked before that request\",\"falsifier\":\"the matrix inventory differs from registered session routes/stream/deviceSessions.list; an auth-state cell is missing; or a request without a valid device JWT or live Agent sessions capability returns session data or performs an action\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run sessions-auth.test.ts. Derive the canonical device session route registrations (including transcript stream mode and deviceSessions.list), assert set equality with the auth-matrix doors, then cover each door against missing/invalid/expired/revoked-device JWT, valid JWT without grant, revoked capability and valid capable positive control. Denied reads return no session data; denied sends/ends invoke no action. R-49 separately requires both-platform real-phone live proof.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions-auth.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Data minimisation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"transcripts leaving the host must not leak secrets\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"No device session payload contains a seeded secret, a raw tool output or raw tool arguments\",\"falsifier\":\"a seeded secret, a raw tool output or raw tool arguments appears in a roster row, a transcript page, an archived transcript, a streamed entry, a cursor page or a push payload\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the roster, transcript and push route tests with a planted-secret fixture whose tool calls carry the secret in both arguments and output, covering roster, transcript tail, archive fallback, stream, cursor page and push.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-transcript.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/session-push.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Platform parity through the shared core.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"both the Android and iPhone apps\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Session types, client methods, the cursor follower and delivery classification live in papercup-core behind UniFFI, with no session logic in the SwiftUI or Compose layers\",\"falsifier\":\"a required core session type/client method/cursor follower/delivery classifier is missing or cannot be compiled and used through generated UniFFI on either platform; its positive fixture is absent or unexercised; or Swift/Kotlin session UI parses transcript entries, computes cursors or classifies delivery instead of calling the facade\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Manual mobile-CI evidence per D-006/D-012, required during P-007: cite canonical papercup-core and papercup-bindings cargo test run ids plus iOS/Android CI run ids (tools/ios-ci.py and tools/android-ci.py). Require a positive session API compile/use contract through generated UniFFI Swift and Kotlin facades: construct/round-trip the exported roster/transcript/delivery types, invoke roster/transcript/send/end client methods against request-recording fixtures, advance the exported cursor follower across initial/older/new pages, and assert woken/staged/queued/absent delivery classification. A missing/renamed API or an unused facade must fail the positive contract. Also run the existing required mechanical Swift/Kotlin session-screen guard against local transcript parsing, cursor computation or delivery classification. A negative guard or unrelated cargo pass alone cannot satisfy R-6; future fixture names/source paths and actual per-platform CI run ids must be cited, never assumed present.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Tests in the canonical frameworks.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"the feature ships with tests\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every device session route and the agent-to-owner push fanout have a passing Vitest suite with no skipped or quarantined test\",\"falsifier\":\"a device session route or the push fanout has no Vitest file, or one of those suites is red, skips a test or is quarantined\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run testing:run for every check-bound suite below: five device-session route suites, session-push orchestration, device-push-dispatcher provider/fanout, and device-store.integration target eligibility. Read the per-file/case result for each exact file; each must pass with zero skipped and zero quarantined cases. A missing file/result is unknown, never a pass.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-transcript.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-messages.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions-auth.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-end.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/session-push.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/device-push-dispatcher.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/device-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Joins the current release candidates without breaking them.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"ship in the current iPhone/Android release candidates (D-004)\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The feature is included in the current iOS and Android candidates of iphone-public-release-2026-08-11 and android-public-release-2026-10-01 with each release-plan owner's recorded agreement\",\"falsifier\":\"either current candidate build lacks the session feature, or either release-plan owner's agreement is absent\",\"evidencePlane\":\"deployed\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Cite the Decision/thread post on each release plan recording its owner's agreement before candidate changes, identify both exact candidate build versions/artifacts, and confirm the session feature on each installed candidate. R-42 and R-43 separately require privacy-packet updates and preservation of prior candidate acceptance.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — End session.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"end a session from the phone (D-003)\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"POST /device/sessions/:owner/end ends the target session through the same server action the desktop Stop agent control uses\",\"falsifier\":\"the device route dispatches a different server action than desktop Stop agent (fleet:kill, D-008). The bound tree tests establish action parity; they do not establish actual session termination. Oracle/readback propagation is graded by R-26. A session still live after a successful end remains an R-9 outcome failure requiring live evidence, with R-46 phone/desktop-oracle observations and R-49 successful pre-revocation end controls; those live obligations cannot be discharged by the mocked oracle.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the end-route test, which asserts the route invokes the same fleet:kill action the desktop Stop agent control calls (D-008) and reads the session state afterwards.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-end.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/owner-sessions/actions.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Push fanout.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"get notified when an agent messages me (D-003)\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A coord message from an agent session addressed to the owner produces one push to each paired device of that workspace that holds the Agent sessions capability\",\"falsifier\":\"an agent-to-owner message (to human, or an ask-owner) produces no push for a capable paired device, or produces more than one push for it\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run session-push.test.ts, device-push-dispatcher.test.ts and device-store.integration.test.ts. The composed notifySessionOwnerMessage -> notifyWorkspace -> real dispatchPush test uses one then two capable devices across FCM/APNs provider doubles; record recipient identities and assert exactly one provider dispatch per eligible device and none missing/duplicated. Keep R-31's denied-target eligibility controls separate and R-37's production phone-arrival proof mandatory.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/session-push.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/device-push-dispatcher.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/device-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-11 — Transcript live follow.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"see new turns as they happen\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A new turn in a live session reaches an already-open device transcript stream without the client reopening it\",\"falsifier\":\"a new turn reaches the device only after the stream is reopened\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the transcript route stream case, which appends a turn to a live fixture while a stream is open.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-transcript.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-12 — Send idempotency.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"a retried send must not double-post\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Two sends from one device carrying the same idempotency key and body deliver exactly one message\",\"falsifier\":\"a retried send with the same key and body delivers a second message, or the same key used by two different devices delivers only one message\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the send route test, which posts twice with one key from one device, once with that key from a second device, and counts delivered messages.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-messages.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/owner-sessions/device-actions.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-13 — Send attribution.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"the agent knows the message came from me\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A message sent from the phone reaches the session labelled as sent by the owner from a paired device\",\"falsifier\":\"the delivered message is attributed to an agent or an anonymous sender, or carries no paired-device label\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the send route test, which reads the delivered envelope.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-messages.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/owner-sessions/actions.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-14 — Biometric window.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"sending with owner authority needs my face or fingerprint\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each phone app issues a session send only inside the configured biometric unlock window (D-002/D-009)\",\"falsifier\":\"either app issues a send with no unlock or an expired unlock, or refuses a send solely for the biometric gate during a fresh configured window\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"In papercup-rust-mobile CI, run the canonical papercup-core send unlock-window test and iOS/Android send-unit fixtures for no unlock, expired unlock and fresh unlock. Assert no send request in the first two cases and a send request in the fresh case; cite cargo and both platform CI run ids. R-44 independently checks end. The server does not verify a client unlock per D-009.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-15 — Action audit.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"every phone action is on the record\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every accepted send and end writes one device actions audit row naming the device, the target session and the action\",\"falsifier\":\"a send or end completes with no audit row, or the row names the wrong device, session or action\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the send and end route tests, which read the device actions log after each accepted request.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-messages.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/session-end.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/owner-sessions/device-actions.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-16 — Phone transcript cache.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"a lost phone must not leak transcripts\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each phone's transcript cache is readable only after a biometric unlock\",\"falsifier\":\"either phone can read cached transcript text without a biometric unlock, or the positive unlocked read fixture cannot read the safe cached transcript\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"In papercup-rust-mobile CI, cite the papercup-core transcript_cache_locked_and_cleared_on_unpair test's independent read-lock assertions and iOS TranscriptCacheLockTests / Android TranscriptCacheLockTest CI run ids. Require locked/unlocked positive and negative read controls on both platforms. R-45 separately owns delete-on-unpair.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-17 — Same layout on both phones.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\": {\"request\": \"the two apps work the same way\"}, \"acceptance\": {\"condition\": \"The iOS and Android apps present the same session screens and controls: the Sessions segment under Fleet with its roster filters, the session detail screen, the send composer and the End session control\", \"falsifier\": \"a session screen or control exists on one platform but not the other, or is reached by a different path\", \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\"}, \"verification\": {\"method\": \"In papercup-rust-mobile CI, cite the run ids and screenshots of the XCUITest SessionsNavigationUITests (tools/ios-ci.py) and the Compose UI SessionsNavigationTest (tools/android-ci.py), each walking Fleet to Sessions to detail to composer to End session.\", \"check\": {\"kind\": \"instrument\", \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-18 — End session confirmation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"don't end a session by accident\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Both phone apps require confirmation before sending an End session action\",\"falsifier\":\"either phone invokes an end action before confirmation or after cancellation\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Require independently named confirmation/cancel/confirm assertions in XCUITest EndSessionUITests and Compose EndSessionTest; cite both mobile CI run ids. On each paired platform in P-016, show that the initial tap and cancel invoke no end action, then confirm the test session's end. R-46 owns resulting-state UI.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-19 — Workspace isolation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"a phone paired to one workspace must not reach another workspace's agents\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every device session route refuses a request whose target session owner belongs to a workspace other than the device's workspace\",\"falsifier\":\"a capable device in one workspace reads the transcript of, sends to or ends a session in another workspace\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the auth route test with a capable device from workspace A against sessions in workspace B on the transcript, messages and end routes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions-auth.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-20 — Roster row fields.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"see who each session is and what it is doing\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each GET /device/sessions row carries the owner id, label, role, harness, pot, fleet, intent, held work item and last activity time of its session\",\"falsifier\":\"a row omits one of those fields, or a field value differs from the value the desktop roster shows for the same session\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run sessions.test.ts and compare presence/value of all nine fields for every active/starting/pending/ended row against the desktop snapshot. Ended archival rows retain owner id, label, role and harness; pot, fleet, intent and heldWorkItem remain present with null values; last activity is desktop lastActiveAt ?? endedAt ?? startedAt ?? null. Exercise each fallback and present empty label/intent controls; omitted fields fail.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-21 — Roster session state.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"trust the state badge\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The session state on each GET /device/sessions row equals the state the shared presence oracle reports for that owner at the same moment\",\"falsifier\":\"a row reports a different state (live, parked, draining, suspect, ended or recorded) than the presence oracle reports for that owner at the same moment\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the route test, which reads the presence oracle and the device rows from one fixture snapshot and compares the state per owner.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/device/sessions.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-22 — Roster On top of them: `GET /device/sessions`, `GET /device/sessions/:owner/transcript`, `POST /device/sessions/:owner/messages` and `POST /device/sessions/:owner/end`, with auth = device JWT plus a per-device Agent sessions capability. Agent-to-owner coord messages feed the existing push pipeline.\n- **Transport:** SSE for live appends on a direct connection, cursor polling over the BYOC sealed relay if it cannot stream (verified first, in P-003).\n- **Clients:** all logic in papercup-core behind UniFFI; screens only render. Send and end sit behind a biometric unlock window (D-002).\n- **Reused, not new:** the presence oracle, coord:send delivery classification, the device actions log, PushManager/PushService and the BiometricPrompt callback. New durable surfaces: four routes and one per-device capability flag. Nothing existing fits them, because the device API has no session route today.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-003, P-009, P-012 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-004, P-009, P-012 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005, P-007, P-016 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003, P-007, P-014, P-015 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-007, P-008, P-011 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-006, P-014 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-015, P-019 | deployed |\n| R-9 | P-017, P-018 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-003, P-007, P-009, P-012 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-004, P-006 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-007, P-009, P-012, P-018 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-004, P-017 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-007, P-015 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-008, P-011 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-016, P-018 | live |\n| R-19 | P-002, P-003, P-004, P-006, P-017 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-001, P-002, P-008, P-011 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-002, P-007 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-002, P-008, P-011 | tree |\n| R-24 | P-016 | live |\n| R-25 | P-003, P-005 | tree |\n| R-26 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-27 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-28 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-29 | P-009, P-012, P-014 | tree |\n| R-30 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-31 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-32 | P-007, P-016 | live |\n| R-33 | P-004, P-006 | tree |\n| R-34 | P-004, P-006 | tree |\n| R-35 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-36 | P-004, P-017 | tree |\n| R-37 | P-016 | live |\n| R-38 | P-016 | live |\n| R-39 | P-010, P-013 | tree |\n| R-40 | P-009, P-010, P-012, P-013 | tree |\n| R-41 | P-007, P-016 | live |\n| R-42 | P-015, P-019 | deployed |\n| R-43 | P-019 | deployed |\n| R-44 | P-007, P-018 | tree |\n| R-45 | P-007, P-015 | tree |\n| R-46 | P-016, P-018 | live |\n| R-47 | P-016 | live |\n| R-48 | P-009, P-012 | tree |\n| R-49 | P-005, P-007, P-016 | live |\n| R-50 | P-007, P-009, P-012, P-016 | live |\n\n## Resolved questions\n\n- Q1 send gate → D-002 (an unlock window). Q4 push → D-003 (yes).\n\n## Phase 1 — Server: device sessions API (papercusp)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Move the roster, transcript tail+cursor, send-with-delivery-classification and end-session logic into shared server-side modules, so the admin/adv routes and the new device routes call ONE implementation (no fork). It runs the same fleet:kill action as the desktop Stop agent control (D-008), enforces the capability (the biometric window is a papercup-core client gate, D-009), refuses targets that are not agent sessions (R-27), returns the post-end presence state (R-26), is safe to repeat on an ended session (R-28), writes an audit row for accepted and refused ends, and has Vitest coverage including a revoked device and a foreign-workspace owner. — note: ← WI-6554700010009771 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Rust core + bindings (papercup-rust-mobile)\n\n- **P-007** `blocked` papercup-core work (R-6, R-4, R-5): `SessionRow`/`TranscriptEntry`/`Delivery` types, client methods, a cursor/stream follower and cache keys; a biometric gate on send/end (unlock window, D-002); transcript cache cleared on unpair; UniFFI UDL with Swift/Kotlin bindings regenerated from the same revision; Rust unit tests.
