Depends on P-007.\n- **P-013** `todo` Android unit and Compose UI tests for the roster, detail, send and revoked-device states (R-7).\n\n## Phase 5 — Attention, privacy, acceptance\n\n- **P-014** `todo` Push for agent-to-owner messages (R-10, D-003): route coord messages addressed to the owner (to human, or an ask-owner) from agent sessions into the existing push pipeline (PushManager/PushService) for capability-holding devices, with the payload deep-linking to the session (S4). The payload is limited to the session reference plus a redacted preview (R-30), and no push reaches another workspace or a device without the capability (R-31). Unit test in `session-push.test.ts`.\n- **P-015** `todo` Update the App Store and Play privacy/review packets (`store/APP-STORE-REVIEW.md`, `store/PLAY-STORE-REVIEW.md`) for transcript display on the device (R-5, R-8).\n- **P-016** `todo` Paired-device acceptance: run S1–S6 on an iPhone and an Android device against the live operator, over LAN and over the BYOC relay. Record evidence: the phone roster count equals the desktop's, a parked agent woken from the phone shows the message in its transcript, an ended session reads ended on the desktop, and a revoked device is refused.\n- **P-018** `todo` Add an End session control to the iPhone and Android session detail screens (R-9, D-003): a confirm dialog naming the agent, the biometric window, and a result state, with XCUITest and Compose UI tests.\n- **P-019** `todo` Release-candidate integration (R-8, D-004): before changing a candidate build, coordinate with the owners of iphone-public-release-2026-08-11 and android-public-release-2026-10-01. Agree how this feature joins the in-flight candidates, then re-run the acceptance evidence it affects (privacy disclosures, reviewer notes, UI test suites).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Route: the authoring su session implements the plan itself (route A)\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-12, AskUserQuestion answer, session turn 15] Route A chosen: \"You, this session\". No fleet. The authoring session (su-440f5011) implements every phase directly, in plan order.\n\n### D-002 — Send gate: one biometric unlock covers sends for a time window\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-12, AskUserQuestion answer, turn 15] Resolves Q1. Sending to (or ending) an agent session needs a biometric unlock within a short window, modelled on the existing workspace-switch gate (papercup-core biometric.rs, RiskLevel Medium). A prompt on every send was rejected as too much friction for conversation. The window length is an implementation constant defaulting to the existing gate's; the server also enforces the per-device Agent sessions capability.\n\n### D-003 — v1 scope adds End session and push for agent-to-owner messages; no interrupt control\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-12, AskUserQuestion multi-select answer \"End session, Push for agent→you\", turn 15] Resolves Q2 and Q4. v1 includes: (a) End session from the phone, through the same server-side path the desktop uses, with no new kill path (R-9, P-017, P-018); (b) a push when an agent messages or asks the owner, deep-linking to that session (R-10, P-014). Interrupt/yield (turn:interrupt) was NOT selected and is out of v1.\n\n### D-004 — Release train: ship in the current iPhone and Android release candidates\nDate: 2026-10-12\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-12, AskUserQuestion answer \"Current candidates\", turn 15] Resolves Q3. The phone feature goes into the in-flight releases (iphone-public-release-2026-08-11, android-public-release-2026-10-01), not the next version. R-8 becomes \"join the candidates without breaking their acceptance\". Coordinate with those release plans' owners before changing candidate builds and re-run the acceptance evidence the feature affects (P-019, P-015).\n\n### D-005 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-12\nAmendment-Id: amend-a9ddb7ea246837578afe6dd1\nRequest-Hash: c1a55b63e8c90f3007d1f36f0f200d3a5942d917b04505c8bf4ccd75a97c9d5e\nActor: su-440f5011-1dcd-4466-86d7-c20957d251ec\nReason: Split compound BARs R-2..R-6 and R-9 into single-behavior BARs R-11..R-19 (spec-quality atomic-observable-behavior); repaired per outside review thread-post:1176795 (JWT requirement, from-device attribution, screen+control parity, cross-workspace isolation R-19).\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-f4caecee-cbe1-487c-8684-a96c89b47d07\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1177004\nApproved-At: 2026-10-12T19:08:33.744Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 18 → 19\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-9, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-006 — R-16, R-17 and R-18 are manual BARs: drop requiredTestLayers\nDate: 2026-10-12\nTheir proof is CI runs in papercup-rust-mobile (XCUITest via tools/ios-ci.py, Compose UI via tools/android-ci.py, unit tests). That repo's runs never reach this harness's test-run ledger, so the checks are explicitly manual (instrumentKey none). A manual BAR cannot also declare requiredTestLayers: the :3170 build refuses it as acceptance_bar_amendment_check_layer_mismatch, and the ledger could never satisfy a declared layer anyway. The METHOD text keeps naming the exact test runs and CI run ids the grader must cite, so no requirement is weakened. [self, 2026-10-12]\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: amend-93ce498ed4d99481ab7199c9\nRequest-Hash: ed9849d7142c0854216a2310818e769ec16e8572657d6923b2c6409142d12711\nActor: su-440f5011-1dcd-4466-86d7-c20957d251ec\nReason: Reword BAR text to remove implementation tokens flagged by spec-quality implementation-independence (route parameter :ownerId -> :owner, field names ownerId/sessionState -> owner id/session state, product name iPhone -> iOS), and make R-16/R-17/R-18 consistent manual BARs by dropping requiredTestLayers (their check is instrumentKey none: proof is papercup-rust-mobile CI runs this harness ledger never records; plan decision records it). No requirement meaning changes; methods still name the required test runs.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-6c84b1a9-6343-478f-8377-d97c3f480a9f\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1177745\nApproved-At: 2026-10-12T22:17:23.821Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 31 → 32\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-008 — R-9 / P-017: the desktop 'End session' path is the Stop agent action, which runs fleet:kill\nDate: 2026-10-13\nR-9 requires POST /device/sessions/:owner/end to end a session through the same server path the desktop uses. The desktop's owner-facing end action is the chat action 'Stop agent' (id session-stop). It sends POST /api/admin/coordination/fleet/kill { owner, close_terminal: true, reason } to the generic /admin/coordination/:group/:verb dispatcher, which runs the fleet:kill tool (killOne). session:end is not the path: it only ends the caller's own session.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-13 by grep in the papercusp staging tree — papercusp/apps/operator/lib/chat-actions/SessionActions.ts:117 `export async function stopAgent`, :119 `postText('/api/admin/coordination/fleet/kill', {`, :121 `close_terminal: true`, :199 `id: 'session-stop'`; papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/admin/coordination.ts:127 `path: '/admin/coordination/:group/:verb'`; papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/kill.ts:37-38 (self-kill refused, required reason, every kill audited), :322 `export async function killOne`, :335 `code: 'self_kill_refused'`.\n\nDecision: P-017's device end route dispatches fleet:kill with the same arguments the desktop sends (owner, close_terminal: true, a required reason). It inherits fleet:kill's rules unchanged: self-kill is refused, a reason is required, and the kill is audited. The route must not add a second kill implementation. R-9's 'End session action' means this Stop agent action.\n\n### D-009 — R-14 is a papercup-core client gate per D-002; the BAR states that and is proven in mobile CI, not at the route\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self, su-440f5011] Responds to bar critique conv-request-2fbd33fe… item 2 (critic su-7ce688aa, 2026-10-13 03:00Z): R-14 as worded ('the device presents a biometric unlock inside the configured window', checked by a route test) is unfalsifiable at the route, because nothing the server receives proves an unlock happened.\nMeasured 2026-10-13 ~03:15Z: no server code in apps/operator/lib, packages/operator-core/lib or apps/operator/app/api mentions a biometric unlock, and no /device/sessions route exists yet, so no verification design is already built.\nRuling: D-002 [owner:Avi 2026-10-12] models the send gate on the existing CLIENT-side workspace-switch gate (papercup-core biometric.rs, RiskLevel Medium) and assigns the SERVER the per-device Agent sessions capability. So R-14 is reworded as a papercup-core behaviour: papercup-core refuses to issue a send or end request when the last biometric unlock is older than the window, proven by papercup-rust-mobile unit tests with CI run ids (a manual BAR, same evidence contract as R-16). The server-side defences stay R-4 (device JWT, revocation) and the capability check. The critic's alternative, a server-verified signed unlock assertion bound to the device key, would change D-002's security design; that is the owner's call and is asked separately, not assumed here.\n\n### D-010 — R-13 / R-35: a phone-sent message is labelled as the owner's from a paired device but stays agent-origin in turn provenance (owner-ask default A)\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self-imposed default, pending owner answer] Owner ask conv-mv63ym1m-0000-176e576bdb7749be8337b8781a27ef07 (2026-10-13 03:15Z) Q2 offered A = keep agent-origin plus a 'sent from a paired device' label, or B = add an owner-device origin so a phone message counts as owner speech. Avi has not answered yet. As that ask said, the plan proceeds on default A, and this decision is reversible.\nWhy A: a stolen or leaked device token must not be able to create owner directives fleet-wide. B would widen who can issue owner directives and change every su's directive-provenance rules, which is a security change that needs the owner.\nEffect: R-13 asserts the label. R-35 asserts turn provenance classifies a phone-sent message as agent-origin, never owner-typed. P-004 no longer stamps owner-directed provenance.\nIf Avi picks B: replace R-35 with an owner-device-origin BAR, amend P-004, and add a provenance-classifier work item.\n\n### D-011 — Per-device send rate limiting is a v1 non-goal\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[self] Disposition of bar-critique point 17 (WI-6554700010009280 thread post 1178103). v1 adds no per-device rate limit or abuse throttle on phone sends or ends.\nWhy that is acceptable for v1: the Agent sessions capability is per-device, granted only by the owner on the desktop, and revocable at once, which also closes open streams (R-4, R-25). Every accepted and refused action is audited (R-15, R-36). Sends need an idempotency key (R-12, R-33, R-34). The biometric window gates send and end on the phone (D-002, R-14).\nRevisit if the device actions audit shows abuse, or if the owner asks for a limit. Agree how this fea… <!-- P-019 -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"oversized-tool-results-reduction-2026-10-12","title":"Reduce oversized tool results at the source (fleet-wide audit, 2026-10-12)","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Reduce oversized tool results at the source (fleet-wide audit, 2026-10-12)\nslug: oversized-tool-results-reduction-2026-10-12\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-21\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Audience:** every agent on the fleet (context cost and extra round-trips), and the operator host (CPU, PG and serialization load from UI and in-process callers).\n- **Problem:** [owner:Avi 2026-10-12 #1713] \"do an audit of all of our oversized tool calls and reduce them\". The census on WI-6554700010008923 found two populations:\n  - (A) agent calls whose result exceeds the door and spills. The worst are work_items:get (~9.9k/day, p50 15KB) and write tools that echo their input.\n  - (B) non-agent callers serializing huge payloads: the UI memory:list (avg 2.2MB, 325GB/week), the in-process dev:pipeline_position behind state:read cells (187KB x 206k/week), admin plans:attention (2.4MB) and the UI accounts:status poll.\n- **Outcome:** each offender's DEFAULT shape fits the door, or its caller asks for a narrow shape. Full detail stays behind an explicit arg. Writes return a receipt rather than an echo.\n- **Non-goals:** raising the door; removing fields that are reachable on request; changing the result-door mechanism.\n- **Source turns:** owner directive #1713 (2026-10-12, session su-c4d0b731).\n- **Scenarios:** an agent reads one work-item and gets state, assignee and checkpoint in under 6KB. An agent completes an item and gets a receipt back. The desktop memory pane stops pulling 2MB every poll.\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\nRetrospective disclosure of the implementation surfaces already used by this plan; no additional build scope or dependency is introduced. D011 extends existing immutable generation/task-ledger runtime ownership, and D012 attaches the existing notifier rather than creating a parallel notification system.\n\n```reuse\n{\"searched\":[{\"where\":\"Canonical source paths, tools catalog and the existing invocation census on WI-6554700010008923\",\"how\":\"Read current result-door/projection handlers, plan-audit notification sources, native guards and original source conversation; tools:find and recorded census identified existing extension points.\",\"found\":\"Extend existing default/full/page contracts, result projector, receipt handlers, cache notifier and native test router.\"}],\"reused\":[{\"ref\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/result-door.ts\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Existing bounded result tier and explicit recovery routes; preserve omitted-detail access.\",\"items\":[\"P-001\",\"P-008\"]},{\"ref\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/result-projection/apply.ts\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Existing JSON projection and byte-boundary behavior.\",\"items\":[\"P-001\",\"P-002\",\"P-007\",\"P-008\"]},{\"ref\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Existing read, write receipt, memory, account, coordination, planning, event and scorecard handlers; Re-run the bounded census by serving_build_sha and call_origin, excluding metadata_json ? 'nestedDispatch', report NULL/unknown rows and sample windows, and inspect the table saved on WI-6554700010008923. Require exact release artifact containment and readback. This observational audit uses a declared manual check; it does not authorize live gate operations.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    },\n    \"replication\": \"Use the saved bounded SQL and before/after results on the work item/report, positive controls for any zero-row absence claim, and exact shipped SHA from the gate owner. A grader independently reads table and runtime proof; no 24-hour claim is inferred from a shorter post-deploy window.\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Conformance\n\n```conformance\n{\n  \"requirements\": {\n    \"R-3\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"exact-release-census-proof-missing\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"P009 or whole-plan shipment is claimed while the persisted before/after table or exact shipped-artifact/caller-cohort proof is absent, incomplete, or based on staging.\",\n          \"stage\": \"delivery\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"The persisted R3 measurement table and its exact release-operator artifact, caller cohorts, denominators, exclusions and residual dispositions; detect a shipment claim without that complete proof. The manual BAR and independent review remain required.\",\n            \"bindWhen\": \"P009 publishes the machine-readable before/after table and exact-release proof interface. Replace this pending entry with a runnable ledger-backed falsifier before P009 completion or whole-plan shipment; this declaration does not satisfy R3.\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nMeasurement: spill = output_ref IS NOT NULL. Raw size = output_size (UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify(result.content), written at libs/generic/tooldef/src/dispatch-stack.ts:1917). Attribute tools:invoke to args_json->>'name'.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-010 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-010 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010 | deployed |\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` work_items:get: shrink the default (trimmed) tier so a single-id read is under 6KB at p50 (currently 15-17KB). Audit what the trimmed tier keeps (checkpoint 3000 chars/row, interestWatch, holder, enrichment) and push the rest behind payloadTier:'full'. — note: ← WI-6554700010010174 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Write echoes: make work_items:complete (p50 20KB), improvements:capture (8KB), loop:checkpoint (13KB), work_items:create (full row + memory recall) and scheduler:get_next (7KB) return receipts by default. Keep advisories that change the next action; drop replays of the caller's own input. — note: Verified on the current build (2026-10-13 03:53Z, tool_invocations since 2026-10-12 21:00Z, no caller projection): :3170 vs :3070 p50 — improvements:capture 2,473 vs 5,847 B (n=113/1163); work_items:create 2,737 vs 5,430 B; work_items:complete 3,861 vs 5,123 B; scheduler:get_next 1,298 vs 7,095 B (12h). :3070 lacks the fix until the gate promotes main (define-tool gitlink afcee6bc there, fix ea88d40 is in 6f9821c2). Residual tail: work_items:complete p90 29-36KB, tracked as WI-6554700010009725.\n- **P-003** `done` UI memory:list: the desktop UI (loopback/pui-*) calls memory:list { harness_slug } with no limit, avg 2.2MB, ~149k calls/week. Find the UI caller; page or limit it, and make memory:list's own default bounded. — note: memory:list now returns 200 rows by default (MEMORY_LIST_DEFAULT_LIMIT=200; max 5000). It takes limit and offset, and returns total, truncated and next_offset when more remain. Code: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/memory/list.ts. Tests: list.test.ts ('bounded by default' block) plus list-search.test.ts PASS (testing:run a2fbe63c). lint:tsc clean at 14:01Z. The measured caller is the stale `pui hud` (pid 3605988): 348 calls/h at 2.27 MB each. The new response fields are serde-compatible with the TUI's MemoriesPayload.\n- **P-004** `done` In-process dev:pipeline_position: state:read cells (system:cell-read:*) and predicate-watch (system:predicate-watch:*) compute the full 187KB result to read one value, ~206k calls/week. Give them a lean computation path. — note: readCell (packages/operator-core/lib/cell-read.ts) now shares IDENTICAL CONCURRENT resolver dispatches through one in-flight promise. The key is tool+args+workspace+harness+role+onBehalfOf+callerContext; a call with an AbortSignal is never shared. Nothing is cached after settle, so the read-RIGHT-NOW contract is unchanged. Measured cause: the TUI status bar reads deploy.3070.sha, git.mainBehindStaging and gate.greenCheckpoint.candidate together, and each dispatched dev:pipeline_position {} (1,041/h at 228 KB and ~1.3 s; 28,497/day across system:cell-read). Each tick now costs 1 computation instead of 3. The stale-binary join is on WI-6554700010008750.\n- **P-005** `done` Admin plans UI and accounts poll: pc-admin-plans-ui calls plans:attention { harness:all, payloadTier:full } (2.4MB) and plans:list (915KB). The UI polls accounts:status (52KB x 128k/week). Narrow the shapes they request, or slow the cadence. — note: accounts:status defaults to a summary view (drops rate.history7d + credentialRef; detail:full / account:<id> restore them). Verified 15:15Z: accounts.test.ts green, lint:tsc clean (accounts.ts + test), weight 1444 chars. Root cause of the earlier reds: a weak-type generic constraint on toAccountStatusSummaryRow, and a billing-join test that expected full rows.\n- **P-006** `done` Read-side agent offenders: events:status (p50 26-37KB), coord:orient (17-37KB), coord:inbox (29KB), plans:get (15-19KB), plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy (68KB), plans:get-spec-evidence (14-23KB). Tighten their default shapes. — note: ← WI-6554700010009314 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` tools:find (p50 9.6KB): hits carry a full argSchema with long per-arg prose (for example, plans:* `harness` is ~1KB). Return compact schemas by default. — note: Already met on current main: tools/find.ts returns a compact structural schema under a byte budget. Measured 2026-10-13 13:05Z on d740fc3802 (6h, payloadTier not full): 8,243 calls, p50 4.3KB, 71 over cap (0.9%); 48 of those are untiered Codex sessions fixed by WI-6554700010009993. Residual tiered tail (23 calls returning near-full schemas) filed as WI-6554700010010158.\n- **P-008** `done` Appended noise: the dev:pg_query advisory prose (~2KB), the batch-hint skeleton (~1.2KB), the testing:run-status provenance banner, and the PostToolUse behavioural-strand hook dump. Cap or dedupe each. — note: ← WI-6554700010011026 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `blocked` Re-measure after deploy and record the before/after table on WI-6554700010008923. — note: ← WI-6554700010010673 blocked (1 external blocker)\n\n\n## Phase — Reductions\n\n- **P-010** `done` scorecards:list returns full per-criterion evidence on every row. Measured 2026-10-12 (24h): { rubricRef:'spec-test-adequacy', limit:200 } ran 87 times at 7.7 MB raw each, and the limit:500 variants reached 24-39 MB. About 1.1 GB of agent scorecards:list output in 6h. The tool deliberately ignores the session payload tier (EI-21437537919383948: reshaping the nested ratings map can fake a complete scorecard). So the fix is NOT trimming the map. Add an explicit lean row mode for browsing (ratings keys and scores without evidence text, plus a completeness count) and keep full evidence for subject-scoped reads. Then find the caller that loops over limit:200 spec-test-adequacy. — note: Verified 14:41Z: scorecards:list test TEST_EXIT=0; lint:tsc --files clean.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — loop:checkpoint: de-duplicate READ rows instead of adding a write receipt\nDate: 2026-10-12\nMeasured 2026-10-12 (harness_shared.tool_invocations, 3 days, workspace papercusp-workspace): loop:checkpoint WRITES n=21,890, p50 1.5KB, p90 3.1KB, only 110 (0.5%) over the 6KB result cap — a write receipt has almost no leverage. READS n=3,126 (3,103 self-reads by 403 agents, ~50MB), p50 14KB, p90 34KB, 2,568 (82%) over the cap. Shape probe of spilled reads: the payload is ~all `note`, and the parsed walls[]/checks[] (added by EI-22415684247504410) duplicate the note's own ## Walls/## Checks sections. Census of 848 loop carry-notes (updated since 2026-10-09): rows are 73% of the 199 >6KB notes whose body alone fits, 11% of the 131 that are large even without rows. Decision [self-imposed, AUTO]: drop the loop:checkpoint write receipt from P-002; instead return the note BODY (rows stripped) once plus the rows once as walls[]/checks[], with a noteRowsOmitted marker; contentHash/length still describe the full stored note; a note with no rows is returned byte-identically; round-trip of the body as a raw note keeps all rows (rows carry forward from storage). Guarded by checkpoint.test.ts round-trip + byte-identical tests. Residual: 131 notes are >6KB on prose alone and agents self-read a note that is already injected at wake — candidate for P-009 re-measure / guidance, not done here.\n\n### D-002 — coord:inbox default window fits the result door\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1713 scope]\n\nMeasured 2026-10-13 (harness_shared.tool_invocations, 24h, papercusp-workspace, transport=mcp): a no-args coord:inbox read is 165 calls/day from 79 owners at p50 61KB. The per-result door is ~1500 tokens (~6000 chars), so every default read spills and the agent sees only the first few entries plus a pointer. DEFAULT_INBOX_LIMIT=50 and INBOX_ENTRY_BUDGET=15000 were sized for an older, larger cap; the budget's doc claim (\"so a default read never overflows the agent result cap\") is no longer true.\n\nDecision: when the caller passes no `limit` (and did not request payloadTier full), coord:inbox keeps priority-ranked entries until the serialized rows reach a share of the door, derived from computeTurnDoors(0).resultEach x CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE (the enforcer's own constants). It reports `window: { shown, omitted }` when it trims. An explicit `limit` keeps its exact meaning. coord:orient's nested call passes an explicit limit, so it is unaffected. summary counts and the unanswered signal are computed over the full read, so nothing actionable becomes invisible.\n\nAlso in P-006 (same file): bounded reads keep one copy of a sectioned message's prose (body is the join of sections[].text), and strip the severe-event emitter trailer that tail-biased clipping kept on every alarm (42 of 50 entries on a measured read kept only the trailer), stating its rule once as `emitter_note`.\n\n### D-003 — work_items:complete/claim standard tier digests the authored completion/outputPayload echo\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1713 scope]\n\nMeasured 2026-10-13 (harness_shared.tool_invocations, 6h, papercusp-workspace, calls without payloadTier): work_items:complete on current :3170 builds p50 3.1-7.3KB; a 06:07Z field split had `completion` at 2.7KB of 6.9KB. :3070 main d740 (p90 26KB) predates the P-002 receipt and is promotion lag, not a source defect.\n\nDecision: write-echo-shape.ts standard tier now DIGESTS the authored echoes instead of replaying them (supersedes context-trimming-tiers-2026-07-01 D-004's 'standard keeps them'). completion becomes { summary (clipped to 160), status, workItem, agent, fields, chars }: the server-filled defaults plus the field list and size, so a dropped or renamed field stays visible. outputPayload becomes { fields, chars }. Trimmed still drops both. One envelope echo_note names payloadTier:'full' for the recorded form.\n\nWhy safe: the lifecycle `emits` rule reads the raw handler result (complete.ts header), and applyPayloadTier shapes at serialize time, after the handler. Handler-level tests that read r.completion.* call the handler directly and are unaffected. Pinned by write-echo-shape.test.ts.\n\n### D-004 — Measure oversize by the result-door spill (output_ref), not output_size > 6000; P-001's 15-17KB premise was mostly instrument artifact\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1713 scope]\n\nCorrection to this plan's own numbers. `harness_shared.tool_invocations.output_size` records the size the tool PRODUCED inside the dispatch, not what reached the agent. Verified 2026-10-13 13:12-13:13Z with the same item (WI-6554700010009522) from one trimmed Claude session on main d740: a plain read logged 2,344; the same read with a `pipe` projection logged 69,017, because a pipe projection promotes the inner dispatch to the 'full' tier (`_mcp-host.ts` projectionMaterializationContext) and the result door then cut it to ~5.4KB. code:run inner calls also log full-tier sizes (39-41KB rows for reads whose agent-facing result was a small script summary). `args_json` does not record the projection, so these rows are indistinguishable by args.\n\nThe agent-received truncation signal is the door's spill backfill: `output_ref IS NOT NULL` (`_mcp-host.ts` backfillResultDoorOutputRef). For work_items:get single-id reads on d740 over 6h: 1,454 of 3,609 rows have output_size > 6000, but only 805 (22%) actually spilled; 653 large rows never reached the agent at that size.\n\nRuling for P-009 and any later measurement in this plan: count an oversized result as `output_ref IS NOT NULL`, split by session tier (`metadata_json->'requestOrigin'->'query'->>'ctx_tier'`) and client kind. Report output_size only as the produced size. Earlier figures in D-001..D-003 and the item texts that use `output_size > 6000` are upper bounds, not spill counts.\n\nWhat survives for P-001: of the 805 real single-id spills, 635 came from untiered Codex sessions (full tier); WI-6554700010009993's role-launch-spec ctx_tier fix covers them once it reaches main. Trimmed-tier plain reads are already bounded: re-reading 15 of the spilled items with an explicit trimmed tier returned 3.8-5.9KB, except terminal items, whose completion record was emitted twice (fixed in get-shape.ts, COMPLETION_EMITTED_AT_ROW). Trimmed-tier spills with plain args are pipe-projection promotions, tracked separately.\n\n### D-005 — A pipe-only projection over a JSON body runs its line operators over the indented rendering\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1713 scope]. Supersedes the rendering half of EI-20437640729173444 (which kept compact one-line JSON under `pipe` and only added a warning); its disclosure half stays.\n\nEvidence: compact JSON is one rendered line, so `grep` over it keeps everything or nothing and `head`/`tail` cannot cut it. A pipe projection therefore never reduced a JSON result: the agent got the whole body, door-truncated by position. Live probe on :3170 8d4e03db14 (tool_invocations 37639904): work_items:get with pipe [grep state, head 2] delivered the 'JSON on 3 line(s)' warning, output_size 6,558, spilled. With no explicit payloadTier the same call is also promoted to the full tier (_mcp-host.ts projectionNeedsFullSource = !('payloadTier' in args)), 69,017 chars on d740 at 13:12Z. `pick` already hands `pipe` an indented rendering (apply.ts `JSON.stringify(picked, null, 2)`), so pick+pipe worked and pipe-only did not.\n\nDecision: when a projection has `pipe` and no `pick` and the body parses as JSON, apply.ts renders that JSON with 2-space indentation before the line operators run. grep then selects matching fields, head/tail cut by line, and the full-tier promotion stops being harmful because the operators can reduce it. The warning stays and now states that operators ran over the indented rendering and that `count` is a rendered-line count, not an item count; `pick` remains the item-level form. Tracked as WI-6554700010010307 fix (b).\n\n### D-006 — Recovery orient stubs plan-authority and held checkpoints the same-epoch carry document already delivered\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 [self-imposed, AUTO, owner directive #1713 scope]. Implements EI-23452465962348473 under P-006.\n\nMeasured 2026-10-13 15:58Z (tool_invocations, 24h, papercusp-workspace): coord:orient {afterCompaction:true} is the dominant orient shape, 1,736 agent calls from 318 owners at p50 16.5KB (81MB/day), 106 spilled. Joined against session:request-compaction by the same owner: 843 calls came <15m after a carry-respawn, 358 at 15-60m, 147 at 1-2h, 447 with no respawn in 2h. On :3170 the trimmed recovery body is ~16KB, of which planAuthority is 3,568 chars and checkpoints 2,922 chars; the carry document renders both from the same buildAutomaticCompactionRecovery call.\n\nDecision: when the carry document is built, record a per-leg digest of what it delivered (plan authority source revision: planSlug, version, contentHash, scoped item statuses, spec revisions; and per held item: id plus a hash of its checkpoint text) together with the session memory epoch, in a nullable session_briefs column. A recovery orient reads that record and, only when the owner's current memory epoch equals the recorded epoch, replaces each leg whose digest still matches with a stub that names the carry delivery time and the exact re-fetch call (plans:get / work_items:get with harness). A leg whose content changed since the carry is delivered in full. Any read/compare failure delivers the full leg.\n\nWhy the epoch guard: memory epoch is bumped by session:request-compaction and by cold loop wakes, so a matching epoch means no context wipe has happened since the carry document reached this session; a mismatched or missing epoch means the content may be gone and must be re-delivered.\n\nRejected: (a) asking agents to pass the marker's digests back in orient args, because agents call the fallback as written ({afterCompaction:true}) and a missing arg would silently fall back to full anyway; (b) dropping the legs from orient outright, because orient afterCompaction is also the fallback when the marker is absent or incomplete, and then it is the only delivery.\n\n### D-007 — Mode-contract omission requires current-incarnation delivery after the context epoch and exact pinned prompt bytes\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/orient.ts previously re-sent selected mode prose unconditionally. session-identity-attribution.ts records applied events with native_session_id and recorded_at; memory/session-epoch-ledger.ts advances bumped_at when context is wiped; orchestrator specificationPrompt returns exact rendered prompt bytes. Focused tests passed 14 cases (run21216140); full orient+shape suites passed detached caa08b34-d8bd-42a1-b26b-edb85f97a4e5, local source at c8661b4793 with dirty tested path.\n\nDecision: reuse those existing stores, never assume activation.applied alone means text remains in context. Compare desired/applied revisions, the latest adv_sessions native incarnation against the applied event, event time at/after the memory epoch, and every selected contract against exact pinned rendered prompt bytes. Only a complete match permits contracts:'' with contractsInPrompt:true and contractsRefetch:'mode:get { contracts: true }'; keep active attribution and definitionRevisions. Unknown/missing/changed proof, source/read failure, afterCompaction:true, and explicitly requested full tier retain full prose. Implicit projection materialization does not impersonate an explicit full request. A pointer must save whole JSON UTF8 bytes. No new durable store or config flag.\n\nNative compaction advances epoch without a new applied event, so it forces full text; managed respawn must deliver/apply the new native prompt before deduplication. WI-6554700010009954 owns source/runtime verification; no shipment claim until exact release containment. This decision governs implementation only and does not alter R1-R3 promises.\nRelated: P-006, P-009\n\n### D-008 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: oversized-results-check-inventory-d007-20261013\nRequest-Hash: c75abc48d84368f9e70ac4402dd019be99f12e74985173391c70c48c9ef6777e\nActor: su-1c4234ac-daad-4171-8282-479adcf4c88a\nReason: Correct the nonexistent inbox test path and include the D-007 current-context mode-delivery regression suite; preserve every BAR identity, outcome promise, role, scope, evidence plane and manual R3 measurement.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-76f7c7f3-d841-4721-b7ab-92024526d476\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1179355\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T18:58:41.059Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 20 → 21\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-009 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: oversized-results-additive-detector-inventory-20261013\nRequest-Hash: 3a1b8777e010260bad7f3f48dd75d381e54eafae6f4ecf4772bc183a2a1ade8e\nActor: su-1c4234ac-daad-4171-8282-479adcf4c88a\nReason: Add the as-built reduction detector files confirmed by rubric-vetting posts1179392/1179402 and direct assertion/source reads. Preserve all criterion fields, BAR outcomes, scopes, evidence planes, roles, existing files and R3 manual measurement.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-1, R-2)\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 21 → 22\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: oversized-results-additive-multitext-p008-20261013\nRequest-Hash: dff9580e507178112cb6f8d297fa5d7bb3e3715355f9edc99302bce853f0068d\nActor: su-1c4234ac-daad-4171-8282-479adcf4c88a\nReason: Add multi-text projected body preservation and remaining P008 SQL advisory/testing output guards to the complete detector inventory. Preserve all20 existing files, all BAR promises, roles, scopes, evidence planes and R3 exact release measurement.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-1, R-2)\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 22 → 23\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2\n\n### D-011 — Exact audit runtime ownership retains replay source across process loss\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAUTO/self implementation under owned EI-25971079852455067. Measured source: grading-integrity.ts binds judges to spawn-host; repair.ts releases staging-server after dispatch; sync-staging-checkout.sh prune_staging_generations retains current alias/process references only. Extend existing immutable candidate generation and task_ledger.detail surfaces: bounded pending-audit source pins bridge process-loss recovery; a per-build managed runtime owns an exact verified bundle/loopback endpoint and is shared by bound audits. Reuse maintained bundle/source/dependency pipeline, managedSpawn enrollment, existing grading-audit mutex and private launch-context seam. Verify exact sha/version before launch, preserve request-only EI126 knobs, rehydrate from retained source after a crash, stop unneeded tasks and release pins when no audit needs them. No new public tool/table/config/routine; no weakening evaluator fences. First implementation unit is source pin/pruner behavior with native lifecycle tests; endpoint ownership is required before the bug may close. Historical runtime-loss actor remains unknown.\nRelated: P-009\n\n### D-012 — Repair the existing plan-audit notification producer and its coverage gap under EI-26582812922777022\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAUTO/self follow-up implementation sequence for already-owned EI-26582812922777022; no new platform system, no LIVE_GATE_OPS. Measured2026-10-21: live catalog has zero active noninternal plan_audits triggers; positive controls harness_plans and plan_revisions carry emit_change_notify. Actual recordPlanAudit writes only the row; plan_audited appends coordination/await hints without bumping plan_audits. plans:get tags this table, but existing consumer regression manually invalidates and TABLE_TO_QUERY_NAMES omits the table, excluding it from the real-migration trigger coverage guard. Receipt /tmp/cache-trigger-probe-20261021.json; full source trace and competing-notification-lag diagnosis on the EI checkpoint.\nExecution steps under the existing single claimed EI: (1) extend TABLE_TO_QUERY_NAMES with the actual affected plan-read query names, reserve and draft an idempotent attachment of the existing emit_change_notify trigger; (2) extend conventional native tests with a real PostgreSQL before/after audit insert→notification→cache refresh check, mapped-table trigger coverage and repeat-apply/scope checks; (3) run focused native verification and final affected-file typecheck, arm only the validated migration, then verify committed/current-build behavior before completion. Reuse generic notification function, cache mapper and migration allocator; add no table/tool/service/config/flag. This decision does not claim fixes or shipment.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"papercup-compact-tool-profile-2026-10-12","title":"Papercup compact tool profile — smaller than su, scoped to its workflows","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercup compact tool profile — smaller than su, scoped to its workflows\nslug: papercup-compact-tool-profile-2026-10-12\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-18\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"People using Papercup through workspace chat, desktop, or voice, including authenticated hosted-workspace customers.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Papercup is instructed to answer from workspace state, but hosted chat uses a generic capability-door list without the necessary direct reads. Giving it the whole su catalog would add irrelevant tools and token cost.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Papercup starts with a compact, purpose-specific tool set, answers real workspace questions, and can discover additional approved tools without acquiring host administrator powers.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Rebuild the su delivery system or change su profiles.\",\n    \"Give Papercup shell execution, arbitrary file access, deployment, credential, database, or fleet-launch controls.\",\n    \"Change papercup-deep's investigative charter.\",\n    \"Grant anonymous visitors workspace access or permission to send email, make calls, or publish externally.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12d3e-b285-7b31-afd8-5ef5f63eb1ac:1\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12d3e-b285-7b31-afd8-5ef5f63eb1ac:7\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12d3e-b285-7b31-afd8-5ef5f63eb1ac:9\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12d3e-b285-7b31-afd8-5ef5f63eb1ac:11\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a12d3e-b285-7b31-afd8-5ef5f63eb1ac:20\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Write a tool-list plan like the su trimmed list, but smaller and limited to Papercup needs.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a12d3e-b285-7b31-afd8-5ef5f63eb1ac:20\"\n      ],\n      \"material\": true,\n      \"resolved\": true\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"A different trimmed version may use fewer tools than su; bar_snapshot_work_contract_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing. Do not start items or launch agents until the approach and execution route are approved. Related issue: EI-25726961381110056.\n\n**Next:** Vet the current acceptance-rubric criteria BEFORE binding proof or emitting adequacy cards (amend → vet → attest → bind → cards → grade): a vetting critique usually becomes an amendment, and proof bound first must then be re-bound.\n\n## Background\n\nThe quoted Oct 6 response exposed two different problems: a mandatory status-style greeting and an insufficient hosted tool surface. The greeting source fix is already completed; preserve it and verify model behavior here. The exact Oct 6 runtime request remains unlocated, so do not claim a proven historical deployment cause.\n\nThe su mechanism already selects full, compact, and deferred tool definitions. Reuse resolveToolDelivery, compactInputSchema, summaryGuidanceDescription, compactWireBytes, and applyCompactTier instead of building another catalog/transport. The current su generator configures a 100,000-byte budget; this is a configured ceiling, not measured Papercup consumption.\n\nAuthority follows the authenticated principal and server-side checks. BYOC D-417/D-421/D-423 preserve customer/service/runtime isolation. Papercup chat D-007 currently uses a public capability-door profile; any change to that contract must be recorded and approved explicitly. Papercup's existing role envelope denies shell execution and file writes.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Papercup workflows.** The smaller profile supports authorized workspace status, plan/work-item questions, public product help, choice cards, deep-answer delegation, and user-requested work filing/handoffs. Every initially advertised tool has a named workflow justification; generic su lifecycle and administration tools are excluded.\n\n**R-2 — Reuse compact delivery.** Use the same full/compact/deferred machinery as su with a role-specific permitted catalog, floors and budget. Keep argument names, required fields, types, bounds, discriminators and safety guidance sufficient for valid calls. Do not copy the whole su floor or apply global demand rankings before permission/profile filtering.\n\n**R-3 — Preserve authority boundaries.** Hosted sessions use customer-scoped credentials; listing, discovery, invocation and delegation remain limited to the authenticated user's workspace/membership and Papercup role. No platform administrator bearer, host/service-state access, unrestricted shell/file/database operations, deploy, credential management, fleet launch, or silent outward send/publish grant.\n\n**R-4 — One executable profile per session.** Derive prompt catalog, MCP listing/compaction, invocation ceiling, native CLI allowed tools, discovery, and reconnect state from the same profile. Distinguish initially advertised tools from permitted deferred tools. A tool omitted from the initial seed can be discovered only inside the unchanged permission/profile ceiling. Do not advertise tools without a working credential/mount.\n\n**R-5 — Demonstrably smaller.** Proposed acceptance target: at least 50% fewer initial definition wire bytes and model input tokens than the existing su trimmed profile, measured on the same registry/build/client/model. Also report tool count, rendered prompt size, workflow latency and invalid-call rate. Test actual delivered definitions, not generator output alone. If required floors cannot fit, report the measured tradeoff for approval; do not drop a needed workflow to meet the target.\n\n**R-6 — Grounded conversational behavior.** Plain greetings stay natural with or without tools. Unavailable access is not an empty workspace. Do not ask for a harness already known to the session. Mention a limitation only when it blocks the requested action, in plain language; avoid unsolicited internal blackboard jargon.\n\n**R-7 — Meaningful regression evidence.** Project-native unit/integration and configured-model behavioral tests cover SC-001 through SC-010, allowed and denied calls, empty/missing credentials, cross-workspace attempts, discovery/reconnect, successful deep-answer return, status with seeded facts, and requested handoff. Preserve the existing greeting/FAQ tests. No pass based on mocks alone proves hosted end-to-end acceptance.\n\n**R-8 — Safe rollout and truthful shipment.** Verify ordinary implementation against staging/current-build; verify final shipment against the exact promoted artifact. Enable the approved role profile by default for eligible sessions while preserving anonymous/member distinctions. Use the existing release/rollback mechanisms, record footprint and behavior evidence, and state any unsupported surface explicitly.\n\n## Design\n\n### Tool candidates and tiers\n\nThis is a proposed starting selection; P-001 confirms each tool's live contract and authorization. Do not grant entire namespaces just because examples belong to them.\n\n| User need | Initial compact candidates | Deferred candidates within the approved profile |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Current workspace and blockers | fleet:assignments, curation:feed, plans:attention | curation:state-of-pot, curation:change-feed; scoped activity/coordination reads when justified |\n| Plan and work questions | work_items:get, plans:get | scoped list/search/history tools only if the workflow needs them |\n| Product help | docs:search, docs:get, retaining public-manual scoping | additional approved public-help reads |\n| Clarification and investigation | chat:ask_choice, voice:delegate_deep | ui:dispatch or tui:dispatch only on the corresponding supported surface |\n| Requested work and handoff | work_items:create, work_items:set_priority, coord:send, coord:escalate | only additional actions justified by an approved handoff scenario |\n| Scoped reachability | tools:find and tools:invoke, if their server-side paths enforce the exact role/principal ceiling | no general catalog expansion or su fallback |\n\nPrefer the compact tier initially. Use full detail only where measured call errors show that retaining more guidance helps. Existing email/calendar/phone summaries may remain in the injected context; this plan does not introduce new external send permissions. The deep brain retains its separately governed role; front-end trimming cannot widen or strip its required investigative authority.\n\n### Preliminary source audit — 2026-10-12\n\nThe current source has three distinct paths that P-001/P-004 must preserve:\n\n| Surface | Current selection and credential | Constraint for the compact profile |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Local owner chat | Existing operator working set; owner MCP mount | Reduce Papercup delivery without changing unrelated operator/su profiles. |\n| Hosted owner chat running as customer | Generic owned-loop doors; short-lived workspace-bound PI bearer with exact allowedTools | converse.ts explicitly says this route does not carry a hosted membership principal. Derive permitted customer reads/actions from a documented authenticated membership/workspace mapping before expanding this exact allowlist; do not infer a grant from a tool capability declaration alone. |\n| Public portal chat | Generic door selection filtered against the supplied PI principal capabilities | Preserve anonymous/member distinctions and the existing public manual boundary; no owner bearer fallback. |\n\nSource: converse.ts principalOk/selectedOperatorTools at lines 329–358 and customerPiSession at lines 476–496; converse-toolset.ts selectConverseTools/buildConverseMcpMount; role-principal-caps.ts Papercup capabilities; capability-envelope/policy.ts Papercup denies shell/file writes. These are source findings, not current-host acceptance or a claim that the October 6 request used this exact build.\n\nThe selected catalog is currently reused by prompt and mount construction. The compact profile must keep this alignment while adding the existing tools_compact delivery parameter and a separate permission ceiling for deferred discovery. No permission widening or implementation was performed in this preliminary audit.\n\n### P-001 measured source inventory and P-002 initial profile — 2026-10-18\n\nOwner directed this session to continue in AUTO after the draft was written; the earlier planning-only hold no longer applies. Runtime authority is still constrained by the customer/workspace security requirements.\n\nThe project-native test `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/operator/__tests__/converse-toolset-catalog.test.ts` registers the real tool catalog, checks all selected names exist, checks mount listing names and customer-token separation, and compares compactWireBytes with applyCompactTier's actual definition output. Final measured source registry: 978 tools, SHA-256 `68e10684d8c210ddb5ab66a92a4d1e45bcc7d00ff8957ff54eee31549bd569fc`. Test ran against local dirty/untracked source at root HEAD `43a8a5f95d6f33e019488cdeecc97a52c4fdd4e1`; this identifies the source measurement, not a shipped artifact. Measurement client = normalized MCP definitions in Vitest; no model inference was used, so provider token counts and user-workflow latency remain unverified for P-007.\n\n| Current source selection | Tools | Full definition bytes | Compact definition bytes |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Local owner text | 109 | 184826 | 59126 |\n| Hosted owner text | 30 | 61575 | 19679 |\n| Public text before request principal filtering | 30 | 61575 | 19679 |\n| Local owner voice (existing slim filter) | 87 | 134076 | 45645 |\n| Hosted owner voice | 28 | 56652 | 18699 |\n| Public voice before request principal filtering | 28 | 56652 | 18699 |\n| Same-build su trimmed seed | 65 | not measured here | 101092 |\n| Proposed Papercup compact seed, not enabled | 15 | not measured here | 20622 |\n\nThe generic owned-loop selector has 26 registered names. 106 is the operator working-set count, not the su seed. The generated su artifact reports 99971 bytes; its source-schema estimate is stale for this measured registry, so comparisons above use the recomputed 101092 bytes. Earlier import-time failures were bootstrap/termination problems: the final bare import DID output the owned-loop list before timing out on live module side effects. The Vitest route gives repeatable evidence without relying on a standalone process exiting.\n\nThe initial Papercup budget is **25000 definition bytes**, using the existing compact projection and real-catalog measurement. Initial floors map to scenarios: fleet:assignments / curation:feed / plans:attention → SC-002; work_items:get / plans:get → SC-003; docs:search / docs:get → SC-003; chat:ask_choice → SC-003/SC-005; voice:delegate_deep → SC-004; work_items:create / work_items:set_priority / coord:send / coord:escalate → SC-005; tools:find / tools:invoke → SC-006. The 20622-byte seed is 79.6% below the measured su seed. This is a source definition-byte result; the separate model-token requirement is not claimed satisfied.\n\nPermitted deferred candidates are curation:state-of-pot, curation:change-feed, plans:list, plans:items, work_items:list, activity:recent, coord:inbox, coord:presence, coord:read, and the surface-appropriate ui:dispatch/tui:dispatch. Exclude arbitrary capability doors, host/process/credential/database/deploy/fleet-launch administration, and generic su lifecycle. Both seed and deferred sets are subject to tool registration, actual modality support, Papercup role/capability policy, and customer/membership intersection; an unsupported tool is not silently granted.\n\nHosted prerequisites remain explicit: authenticate the membership/workspace binding before granting workspace reads or work-filing actions; do not mint them merely from the tool's declared capabilities. tools:find/tools:invoke additionally require the existing agent_tools:read capability and exact permitted-tool filtering on discovery and dispatch; metadata visibility alone is not permission. Public anonymous help remains a separate restricted view. These are P-004 implementation/negative-test obligations, not reasons to abandon the independent delivery work.\n\nThe existing voiceProfile slim/standard selection landed after the initial draft (converse-toolset.ts, Oct 13). Extend and test that surface; do not create a competing voice selector.\n\n### Implementation seams to extend\n\n- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/operator/converse-toolset.ts and converse.ts: role/trust-specific selection, customer credential mount, allowed tool names and session lifecycle.\n- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/tool-delivery-policy.ts, scripts/gen-tool-delivery.ts, and apps/operator/lib/tool-delivery-floors.ts: reuse the budget/floor/tier model; represent Papercup as a role profile, not a new client implementation.\n- libs/generic/tooldef/src/compact-schema.ts and transport/tool-allowlist.ts / _mcp-host.ts: retain measured-versus-delivered equivalence and scoped dynamic discovery.\n- transport/role-principal-caps.ts, capability-envelope/policy.ts and existing customer/principal provisioning: enforce existing role and customer/workspace boundaries across reads and actions.\n- Canonical apps/operator/prompts/papercup.*.md and existing project-native Papercup suites: keep prompts consistent with the actual available surface.\n\nReuse-first review also read omp-profile-system-2026-05-24: that shipped plan defines OMP engineer/power metadata gating and installer selection, not a Papercup role working set or compact definition delivery. Reuse any applicable existing profile checks; this is a distinct Papercup extension, not a reopening of that installer project.\n\nNo new service, table, tool verb or parallel discovery system is planned. If a current primitive cannot preserve membership scope, document that exact gap and extend it minimally before enabling the affected tool.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\nShipment BARs map to the proof-producing item that can establish the complete outcome after its dependencies. Earlier inventory, profile proposal, generator, authorization and prompt tasks remain governed by their independent PCP contracts; they do not need future runtime shipment proof to close. R-7 retains SC-001 through SC-010 and is therefore discharged by final P-008, with earlier evidence reused by identity. Generated delivery-map figures in D-002 are diagnostics; the delivered comparator is measured fresh from the same running build under P-001/P-007.\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-006 | live |\n| R-4 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-007 | live |\n| R-6 | P-006 | live |\n| R-7 | P-008 | live |\n| R-8 | P-008 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Audit and specify\n\n- **P-001** `wip` Inventory Papercup's real workflows and tool/principal paths on desktop, voice, authenticated portal and hosted owner chat; audit scope at each writer/reader; measure same-build su and current Papercup delivered footprints; identify governing decision changes and record the exact scope matrix. importance: high — note: Independent reviewer approved thread-post:1182804 via thread-post:1182868; external blocker cleared.\n- **P-002** `todo` Specify the initial Papercup floor, permitted deferred tools, tier choices and smaller budget from P-001; tie every tool to a scenario; reuse delivery inputs instead of su's whole floor; record membership/trust variants and approve any change to papercup-chat-one-component-one-contract-2026-09-06#D-007 before implementation. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n\n## Phase 2 — Implement the approved profile\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Extend the existing delivery generator/policy with the approved Papercup role profile and feed actual compact definitions through the existing MCP transport; retain schema and safety semantics; add byte-parity and deterministic-generation tests. blocked-by: P-002 importance: normal\n- **P-004** `todo` Wire the approved customer/workspace/role-scoped allowed set into prompt, MCP mount, invocation, CLI native tools and delegation; implement scoped discovery only inside that ceiling; test tenant/member/role denial and credential cleanup with no administrator-token fallback. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high\n- **P-005** `todo` Align canonical Papercup prompts and session-reconnect behavior with the real profile; preserve the completed natural-greeting fix and public FAQ boundaries; advertise no inaccessible tools and handle requested-action failures honestly. blocked-by: P-004 importance: normal\n\n## Phase 3 — Prove behavior and ship\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Add and run project-native regressions and seeded configured-model scenarios for SC-001 through SC-008; exercise real current-build customer credentials and mount with successful status, plans/help, discovery, deep-answer return and requested handoff plus denied cross-workspace/admin/anonymous cases. blocked-by: P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Measure actual delivered catalogs and full model prompts for SC-009 against same-build su; demonstrate the proposed 50% footprint reduction and record latency/call validity for all selected workflows; revise the profile on evidence and rerun only changed proofs. blocked-by: P-006 importance: normal\n- **P-008** `todo` Complete final promotion and exact-artifact verification for SC-010 using existing pipeline ownership/release rules; enable for eligible Papercup sessions, verify supported owner/hosted/voice/portal surfaces and rollback contract, publish the measured report, and close EI-25726961381110056 with evidence and owned residue. blocked-by: P-007 importance: normal\n\n## Source conversation and activation gate\n\nSource: codex session 01a12d3e-b285-7b31-afd8-5ef5f63eb1ac, turns 1–20. The exact original quote is turn 1; tool-set question turn 7; smaller-role correction turn 9; prompt-fix request turn 11; explicit plan request turn 20. Source refs are in Product shaping. Retrieval currently classifies these file-backed user turns as unenrolled origin, so do not invent a proven owner-origin stamp.\n\nBefore draft-to-ready/active or plans:start, re-read the complete related source conversation and record the activation mapping/audit. Lead implementation approval with the shaping walkthrough. Do not treat this draft as authorization to change permissions or execute its items.\n\n## Proposed choices and assumptions\n\nThe profile covers the quick Papercup front end; deep delegation and su remain separately governed. The 50% footprint target is an agent-proposed acceptance threshold, not an owner-stated number. The exact seed/floor and allowed membership variants are outputs of Phase 1, not guessed facts. No implementation route is selected by this plan-only request.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAmendment-Id: papercup-compact-approved-bars-20261015-v2\nRequest-Hash: 28ab29a072b29c4a5501a93169558e996a3125ddad355a27ba042a311f11cc65\nActor: su-09924a8c-5be3-475c-8c3f-7b1d2074c9ce\nReason: Repair spec-quality preparation by making atomic BAR conditions, retaining the complete original requirements in intent and verification, and declaring executable checks/test layers. No feature scope is removed.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-f451513d-20ac-469f-9f25-25d56b2f47f0\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1182868\nApproved-At: 2026-10-15T05:31:20.750Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 5 → 6\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — D-002 — P-001 source inventory: reuse role-specific selection plus compact delivery; keep hosted PI scope explicit\nDate: 2026-10-17\nMeasured 2026-10-18, correction of the preliminary wording: 106 unique entries belong to ALL_AGENT_MCP_TOOLS, the operator/Papercup local-owner working set; this is not the su seed. The generated su seed lists 65 compact tools (its artifact reports 99,971 bytes), while the same-build live-registry measurement is 101,092 compact bytes. These are different measurements; use current emitted definitions for comparisons. The persistent project test packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/operator/__tests__/converse-toolset-catalog.test.ts registers the actual catalog and applies selectConverseTools and applyCompactTier. It passed with 26 owned-loop tools. Text: local owner 109 tools / 184,826 full / 59,126 compact bytes; hosted-owner and public 30 / 61,575 / 19,679. Voice: local owner 87 / 134,076 / 45,645; hosted-owner and public 28 / 56,652 / 18,699. Client/model: this is a source/Vitest MCP definition measurement, not an LLM-token or deployed-host acceptance test. Lists precede request-specific PI capability filtering. The bare import DID print the owned-loop list before its 100s timeout; the process remained alive due module side effects. Retracted: saying no owned-loop count was produced. The registered Vitest route removes that measurement blocker. The existing all-catalog guard passed 7/7; selector guard passed 12/12. Hosted selection still lacks direct workspace reads and uses derived PI allowedTools/capabilities; source still states no hosted membership principal is carried. Preserve explicit role/workspace membership authorization before adding hosted tools. Reuse role-specific initial seed + permitted deferred ceiling with existing compactInputSchema/summaryGuidanceDescription/applyCompactTier/tools_compact. Model token, latency and actual runtime membership evidence remain for later planned steps.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-17\nAmendment-Id: papercup-compact-semantic-bars-20261017-v1\nRequest-Hash: fcefb5b7299ccd012e452ef032f6d629ede7869408f56d44993a74ca284e0d88\nActor: su-09924a8c-5be3-475c-8c3f-7b1d2074c9ce\nReason: Apply independent review1189472/1189411/1189436: remove circular/premature BAR mappings without dropping scenarios, replace tautological falsifiers, preserve the already-promised measured-tradeoff branch, and enforce live/model/customer/exact-artifact proof using the existing adequacy ledger. Probe checks cannot pass from pre-existing green files. No permissions or product behavior are expanded.\nApproved-By: su-a6ca9ed8-74a0-4bf6-8e4d-79296423cd8e\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1189499\nApproved-At: 2026-10-17T23:39:40.925Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 10 → 11\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n## Conformance\n\nThese falsifiers are pending until their named implementation interfaces exist. Each pending binding must become a runnable check by its binding milestone; it does not count as product acceptance evidence.\n\n```conformance\n{\n  \"requirements\": {\n    \"R-1\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"workflow-path-missing\",\n          \"stage\": \"implementation\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"A required Papercup workflow has no permitted executable path in the approved profile.\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"A required SC-001..SC-008 workflow has no selected tool path or an inaccessible selected tool.\",\n            \"bindWhen\": \"P-002 approved seed and P-004 authority mapping land; bind before P-006 acceptance.\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-2\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"delivery-contract-drift\",\n          \"stage\": \"implementation\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"Papercup delivery changes the existing compact/deferred contract semantics.\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"A Papercup definition loses required schema/safety content or bypasses the existing delivery \"authority-boundary-breach\",\n          \"stage\": \"integration\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"A hosted Papercup session exceeds its authenticated workspace, membership, role, or credential ceiling.\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"A cross-workspace, admin, anonymous, or missing-credential probe returns private data or performs a denied action.\",\n \"profile-path-divergence\",\n          \"stage\": \"delivery\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"Session prompt, MCP, invocation, discovery, native CLI, or reconnect uses a different profile.\",\n tool.\",\n            \"bindWhen\": \"P-004 profile wiring and P-005 reconnect interfaces land.\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-5\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"footprint-target-missed\",\n          \"stage\": \"operation\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"The matched initial footprint misses the declared reduction target while preserving required }\n}\n```\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12","title":"Papercusp performance improvement — 12 Oct 2026 audit","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-10-12","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercusp performance improvement — 12 Oct 2026 audit\nslug: papercusp-performance-audit-2026-10-12\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-13\n---\n\n# Papercusp performance improvement — 12 October 2026 audit\n\nAudit report: Reports library, \"Papercusp performance audit — 12 Oct 2026\"; work item WI-6554700010009184. Builds on the September audit (WI-10002792) and plan papercusp-log-performance-remediation-2026-09-23; that plan's still-open items are finished there and tracked here by P-011, not duplicated. Related shipped plan application-performance-implementation-2026-09-04 is complete and not reopened.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Audience:** the agents that do the work (every wake/start runs coord:orient, scheduler:get_next, fleet:assignments, work_items:list) and Avi, who waits on them; secondarily desktop users of the operator UI.\n- **Problem:** at roughly constant call volume the agent wake path got 2–10× slower in two weeks — coord:orient median 2.8 s (09-28) → 11.2 s (10-12); scheduler:get_next 4.5 s → 7.8–9.8 s; work_items:list 0.3 s → 3.4 s. HTTP itself is fast (health 1–20 ms); the time is in database work, on a host whose 128 cores were fully busy during the audit.\n- **Outcome:** agents start and pick work in a few seconds again, with numbers that prove it, and per-phase timings that make the next regression attributable within a day.\n- **Non-goals:** rewriting coordination semantics; moving off PostgreSQL; changing agent permissions; optimizing non-Papercusp workloads on the host beyond giving the app priority over them.\n- **Source turns:** [owner:Avi 2026-10-12] directive #1734 — \"give a thorough audit to the performance of our application and come up with a plan for improving it.\"; [owner:Avi 2026-10-12] directive #1744 — build a performance rubric from the audit measurements, score a baseline, then \"carry the improvement plan to shipped status, using the rubric to validate the improvements have worked with better measurements.\" (#1744 also approved execution in AUTO mode.)\n- **Scenarios:** (1) an agent wakes and orients in ≤ 3 s median; (2) a fleet member claims next work in ≤ 3 s median; (3) when one of these slows again, per-phase timing names the slow phase from one day of data; (4) a heavy test run on the shared box no longer multiplies orient latency.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Attributable latency.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Per-phase timings on every wake-path call and host contention history, so any slowdown is attributable to a phase and to load.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"coord:orient, scheduler:get_next, fleet:assignments and work_items:list persist per-phase timings in tool_invocations.metadata_json on every completed call; host PSI and per-slice CPU are sampled once a minute; pg_stat_statements occupancy is below 60%.\",\"falsifier\":\"A day of tool_invocations rows where orient phase timings are absent or attribute < 90% of wall time to named phases; or no PSI samples in the last hour; or pg_stat_statements occupancy >= 60%.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the phase-attribution and PSI replication SQL in rubric papercusp-app-performance (criteria wake-path-attribution, host-cpu-pressure, pg-stat-statements-headroom) and the unit test below.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/orient-phase-telemetry.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Wasteful queries fixed.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Each measured Postgres hotspot has an EXPLAIN-backed fix or a reasoned drop, guarded by a regression test.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The issues/work-items 300-row list uses an index-ordered plan with no full sort; the unanswered-directed roster no longer rolls up a multi-day coord_event_log window per call; the scout accumulator reads incrementally; each second-tier query has a fix or a recorded drop.\",\"falsifier\":\"EXPLAIN of the list query shows a Sort over all workspace work_items, or the roster p95 stays above 300 ms, or a regression test for a fixed query is missing.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the integration tests below (they assert the query plans and old-vs-new equivalence), then compare pg_stat_statements mean time for each statement against the baseline scorecard EI-25797437572523561.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/issues-engineer.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/unanswered-directed.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/scout/signal-accumulator.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — App priority on the shared host.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The serving path (release operator, bg-host, PostgreSQL) is protected from background load by resource weights.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"systemd CPUWeight/IOWeight for the serving units exceed those of the test-run, agent-session and bash-job slices, and orient p50 under comparable PSI does not regress.\",\"falsifier\":\"systemctl show reports equal or lower weights for the serving units than for background slices.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"systemctl --user show -p CPUWeight,IOWeight on the serving units and background slices; compare orient p50 at similar PSI using the rubric wake-orient-latency criterion.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Host hygiene.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Leaked test containers are reaped automatically and disk retention keeps every volume below 85%.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"No test container older than 6 h without a live task-ledger owner; df shows /, /mnt/data and /mnt/backup below 85%.\",\"falsifier\":\"docker ps shows a test container older than 6 h with no live owner, or any of the three volumes is at or above 85%.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the rubric criteria test-container-leaks and disk-headroom replication drills (docker ps age listing; df -h).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Frontend budget.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Initial-route JavaScript is measured and guarded by a CI budget, and startup Web Vitals have a recorded baseline.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A CI bundle budget fails the build when initial-route JS exceeds its budget, and a startup Web Vitals baseline is recorded on the rubric desktop-startup-vitals criterion.\",\"falsifier\":\"No budget check runs in CI, or the desktop-startup-vitals criterion is still unmeasured.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Inspect the CI budget check and re-score rubric criteria frontend-initial-js and desktop-startup-vitals.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Proven result.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Re-measure with the audit instruments and show the improvement against the baseline, validated by the performance rubric (owner directive #1744).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A comparison report re-measures with this audit's instruments and meets: orient p50 <= 3 s and p95 <= 8 s; get_next p50 <= 3 s; work_items:list p50 <= 1 s; fleet:assignments p50 <= 2 s; Postgres statement execution <= 5 backend-cores in a comparable 90 s window. The verdict is a re-score of rubric papercusp-app-performance compared criterion-by-criterion with baseline scorecard EI-25797437572523561.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any listed threshold missed in the re-score, or no re-score scorecard exists.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"scorecards:emit against papercusp-app-performance using its replication SQL, then diff ratings with EI-25797437572523561 and publish the comparison report.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Prior plan closed.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Close out papercusp-log-performance-remediation-2026-09-23.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every open item of papercusp-log-performance-remediation-2026-09-23 reaches done or an explicit drop with reason.\",\"falsifier\":\"plans:items on that plan lists any todo, wip, blocked or needs-human item.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"plans:items { slug: papercusp-log-performance-remediation-2026-09-23 } and inspect each terminal note.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nOrder of work: instrument first (P-001–P-003) so every later fix is measured against a phase-level baseline; fix the cheapest high-confidence query (P-004) immediately; P-005 starts with a real-parameter EXPLAIN ANALYZE before any redesign; host policy (P-008) is owner-gated; P-012 verifies with the same instruments used in the audit.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | live |\n| R-2 | P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-008 | live |\n| R-4 | P-009 | live |\n| R-5 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-012 | live |\n| R-7 | P-011 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Instrument\n\n- **P-001** `done` R-1. Persist per-phase timings on EVERY call (today orient emits phaseDiagnostics only on its deadline fallback) for coord:orient, scheduler:get_next, fleet:assignments and work_items:list into tool_invocations.metadata_json; reuse orient.ts createOrientPhaseTracker and the dispatch-stages-v1 shape; add a dev:telemetry per-phase rollup. Issues/work-items 300-row list (issues-engineer.ts / work-items.ts): EXPLAIN GENERIC_PLAN shows it reads every workspace work_item (~17.5k wide rows incl. body/payload) and sorts on to_timestamp(created_ts/1000.0), which no index serves, to return 300. 130,591 calls at 1.02 s mean since 10-09 (~0.5 Postgres core continuously). Target p95 < 300 ms. — note: WI-6554700010009282 closed: ask-driven roster statement, migration 1479, plan test + 2 caught mutants, PERF-P005-ROSTER@1 pass, audited card EI-25816768730780668. 100-recipient bulk call measures 324 ms vs a 300 ms target; post-deploy p95 re-measure at plan re-grade.\n- **P-006** `done` R-2. Second tier, each an EXPLAIN-backed fix or reasoned drop: pg_advisory_xact_lock(int, hashtext) waits (292/90 s at 116 ms mean — find key + holders; contention, not CPU); presence-wakeability last-activity (344/90 s at 88 ms); memory lexical ranking (93/90 s at 309 ms); goal-pots linked query (libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/goal-pots.ts, 1.7 s); session-search FTS (315–531 ms); session_turns embedding UPDATE (978/90 s) within WAL ≈ 2.3 MB/s (~200 GB/day). — note: ← WI-6554700010009307 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Shared host\n\n- **P-008** `done` R-3. The shipped SPA (papercup-release apps/operator-vite/dist/assets) is 35 MB of JS in 857 chunks; largest are porcupine 3.38 MB (wake word), a 1.74 MB shared chunk, elk.bundled 1.37 MB and UiwMdPane 1.0 MB.
