Re-measure with this audit's instruments (daily tool_invocations percentiles; 90 s pg_stat_statements interval; cgroup CPU delta; PSI) and publish a comparison report against the 2026-10-12 baseline: re-score rubric papercusp-app-performance (scorecards:emit) and diff it against baseline scorecard EI-25797437572523561. Depends on P-001, P-004, P-005, P-006 and P-008 (set as scheduler blockers at activation). — note: ← WI-6554700010009312 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Host CPU saturation is NOT the cause of the wake-path regression (retracts the report's [inferred] F2→F1 link)\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDistinguishing test, 2026-10-12 17:40–17:51Z: host CPU PSI some avg300 = 3.0% (vs 27% at 16:25Z when the box was saturated). Over that quiet window orient p50 = 10.75 s (n=17, last 8 min), get_next p50 = 7.7 s, work_items:list p50 = 4.3 s — unchanged from the saturated-period values (11.1 s / 8.4 s / 3.4 s). A 60 s pg_stat_statements diff in the same quiet window: unanswered-directed roster query 10.9 s/call, 300-row issues read 1.24 s/call, a full-row work_items read (queryid 1837139600966019434) 8.07 s/call. App-service cgroup cpu.pressure avg60 at the same time: papercusp-dev-api 0.05%, bg-host 0.00%, postgres 0.19%. Conclusion: the slow wake path is intrinsic query/handler cost, not CPU contention. The report rpt_80265e64 F2 sentence 'consistent with contention multiplying query time' is retracted. Consequences: P-008 (host CPU/IO weights) drops from high to normal priority — still useful hygiene, not the fix; P-005 (roster) and P-004 (issues list) are the lead items; the work_items full-row 8 s read is added to P-007's scope. The roster query's quiet-time cost (10.9 s) ≈ orient p50 (10.8 s) is a strong correlation, not proof — P-001 phase timings must confirm. IO pressure (host IO PSI ~18%) is not ruled out but app-service io.pressure was low (dev-api 0.76%, postgres 3.38%).\n\n### D-002 — P-005: unanswered-directed roster is ask-driven index probes (not a rollup or cache); keep both coord_event_log indexes; JIT off for the statement\nDate: 2026-10-12\nDate: 2026-10-12. Measured, not inferred.\n\nCause [measured]: the roster statement materialized every message ever authored by every roster member (roster_authored: 29,458 rows / 109,798 buffers for the top-100 roster) and each body->>'x' re-decompressed the ~2.5 kB pglz body (~4 us per access); JIT added 117-180 ms per bulk call (estimated cost ~744k > jit_above_cost 100k). Single-recipient calls cost 2 ms; the 2,880 ms production mean (queryid -5961444489277740845, 26,430 calls) is the bulk callers (fleet:assignments, delivery-ladder-sweep, coord-health-lane, presence-transition-commitments).\n\nDecision: rewrite the statement to start from the asks and probe for their answers through correlated LATERALs fenced with OFFSET 0 (so the planner cannot fall back to a hash join over all reply-shaped rows, which it did: 62,654 rows / 629 ms), decompress each body once via LATERAL (SELECT body || '{}'::jsonb OFFSET 0), read loose replies only for recipients that still have open asks, and run it under SET LOCAL jit = off. No insertion-time ts bounds: body ts is supplied by senders and peer hosts, so column ts >= body ts is not guaranteed.\n\nRejected: (a) per-owner rollup maintained on write duplicates the threading / goal-cluster / loose-reply / ack ping-pong semantics in the hot write path with a large equivalence risk; (b) a cache keyed by (owner, log high-water id) misses on almost every call because the messages high-water moves every second.\n\nIndexes: KEEP both hand-built 2026-10-12 indexes, now migration 1479. coord_event_log_msgs_to_expects_reply_gin serves the asks; coord_event_log_msgs_from_system_session_idx is the only access path for the system-alias loose-reply branch.\n\nEvidence: identical result rows to the previous form for the top 1 / 20 / 50 / 100 recipients on the live workspace; JIT off for both, 20 -> 154 vs 352 ms, 50 -> 266 vs 1,396 ms, 100 -> 302-384 vs 1,251-1,994 ms; via the live module 20 -> 144 vs 424 ms, 100 -> 324 vs 1,115 ms. Guarded by unanswered-directed-query-plan.integration.test.ts (frozen legacy oracle). The 100-recipient worst case sits at the 300 ms line under load average ~200; follow-up: lz4 compression for coord_event_log.body (measured 3.4x faster field extraction) would cut the remaining decompression cost.\n\n### D-003 — P-006: scout signal accumulator recounts once per workspace per sweep (not incremental high-water); cadence unchanged\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured 2026-10-12 23:53Z (pg_stat_statements window from 2026-10-09 13:43Z, 295,823 s): the seven accumulator count statements ran 10,807 times each; four of them average 542-644 ms and 636k-817k shared buffers per call; one recount is ~2.6 s of statement time and ~2.86 M buffers (~23 GB) of reads. harness_shared.scout_signal_accumulator holds 42 install scopes in papercusp-workspace, and every lane count plus the watermark is WORKSPACE-wide, so each sweep ran the identical recount 42 times.\n\nRuling: P-006 recounts ONCE per workspace per sweep and writes that one recount to every scope row of the workspace in a single multi-row upsert (groupScopesByWorkspace + upsertAccumulatorRowsForScopes in packages/operator-core/lib/scout/signal-accumulator.ts). Results are identical to the per-scope loop by construction, and the statement work drops 42x on the live workspace.\n\nRejected: incremental counting from a stored high-water mark (the original PERF-P006-SCOUT wording). It is exact only for the append-only lanes (observations rows and filings, captures). completions and deferrals key on mutable status plus updated_ts, so a row re-touched or moved out of the status set would be double-counted or never removed; reverts keys on last_released_at, which moves; and a late-committing row with an older timestamp is missed by any timestamp high-water. A wrong count silences or over-fires the Scout, the exact failure the accumulator exists to prevent (learning-loop D-042/D-043). Cadence is left at 120 s for the same reason.\n\nSpec PERF-P006-SCOUT is revised to the per-workspace property; the target (< 0.1 core) is re-measured post-deploy from pg_stat_statements deltas for the same queryids.\n\nSeparate observation, not acted on here: the Scout watermark has been 2026-10-08 21:38Z since then (no successful Scout cycle in 4 days), which widens every recount window.\n\n### D-004 — P-001: spec PERF-P001-PHASES covers the unit-provable mechanism; the >= 90% coverage share is acceptance R-1, measured at P-012\nDate: 2026-10-13\nGrading audit EI-25820783905975497 failed card EI-25820333924976613 on base-rate-check: the bound test's attestation said in prose that the unit layer cannot show coord:orient's >= 90% phase coverage, yet the clause claimed that share, so the card's 'disclosed-gap: not-applicable' contradicted its own evidence. The auditor also noted the bound proof covered only libs/generic/tooldef, leaving orient's use of the tracker author-attested.\n\nRuling: PERF-P001-PHASES @2 states the mechanism a unit test can prove: coord:orient records its named phases on ctx.phases, and the dispatcher persists a handler-phases-v1 record for every completed call that tracked phases. Proof: dispatch-stack.test.ts (persistence) plus a new orient.test.ts case that runs the orient handler with a ctx.phases tracker and asserts its phases land there, each with a caught mutant. The >= 90% share of orient wall time is an operational property of real traffic; it stays in acceptance bar R-1 and is measured at P-012 with dev:telemetry { phasesFor:'coord:orient', hours:24 } (handlerPhaseRollup coverage). If that share is below 0.9, P-012 reopens P-001 to wrap the untracked spans.\n\n### D-005 — P-002: contention samples ride the kernel-leak writer every 60 s (leak evaluation stays 10-minute); acceptance is forward correlation, not attribution of the 10-06/10-07 step\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\n\nDesign. Extend harness_shared.host_kernel_memory_samples (reuse; no new table) with cumulative PSI stall totals in microseconds from /proc/pressure/{cpu,io,memory} (cpu some, io some, io full, memory some, memory full) and a jsonb of cumulative cpu.stat usage_usec per cgroup: the root (whole host), the top-level slices, system.slice/system-postgresql.slice, and every papercu* unit in this process's app.slice (discovered from /proc/self/cgroup, no hardcoded uid). The kernel-leak PeriodicCheck samples and stores every 60 s (bucket width 60 s). Leak evaluation, alarm resolve/broadcast/escalate and prune still run at most once per 10-minute bucket per process, so the alarm rail's call rate is unchanged. The two-sample delta is computed at query time: view harness_shared.host_contention_hourly gives per host per hour the stall fraction (sum of delta total / sum of delta t) and per-cgroup cores (sum of delta usage_usec / sum of delta t) over consecutive same-boot rows, skipping gaps over 10 minutes and counter resets (negative deltas, e.g. a restarted unit).\n\nAcceptance rescope. The item's 'attributes the 10-06/10-07 step change (orient 4.3 s -> 8.0-10.4 s)' cannot be met: no PSI or per-slice history exists for that window (the table held only 10-minute meminfo samples), and D-001 already measured that host CPU pressure is not the cause. Rescoped acceptance, measured at P-012: after at least 24 h of samples, join host_contention_hourly with hourly coord:orient p50 from harness_shared.tool_invocations and report corr() of orient p50 against each stall fraction and against Postgres cores.\n\nObservation [measured, one sample at 2026-10-13 01:09Z]: /proc/pressure/io some avg60 = 44.66%, full avg60 = 31.92%; cpu some avg60 = 1.61%; memory some avg60 = 1.63%. D-001 tested only CPU pressure. IO pressure is an untested candidate for the wake-path regression [inferred], and the samples this item adds are the instrument to test it.\n\n### D-006 — P-008: serving-path protection is a PostgreSQL CPU weight; IO priority dropped on measured A/B; IOWeight inert under mq-deadline\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured 2026-10-13 03:25-04:04Z (WI-6554700010009308).\n\nCPU: not the contended resource. 79 of 128 cores busy, CPU PSI some 1.7-8%. The existing CPUWeight=2000 on papercusp-dev-api/bg-host is effective: cgroup v2 compares weights only between siblings, and app.slice (holding them) has an equal share with papercusp.slice (all agent/test/build/bash-job work). Gap found: PostgreSQL's system-postgresql.slice sat at weight 100 beside 97 docker test-container scopes in system.slice. Fixed: CPUWeight=1000 on system-postgresql.slice (tracked drop-in apps/operator/scripts/systemd/system/system-postgresql.slice.d/60-papercusp-serving-cpu-weight.conf, installed, live). No CPUQuota on the test-run slice: reasoned drop, CPU PSI does not justify throttling tests.\n\nIO: the contended resource (host IO PSI some 8-42%; WAL fsync 9-187 ms per 60 s window). Root NVMe is DRAM-less and holds PostgreSQL data+WAL (WI-10003444). IOWeight= is inert here: the root disk runs mq-deadline (pinned by papercusp-host-performance.sh), which honours I/O priority classes but not cgroup io.weight. Tested the lever that does work: io.prio.class=promote-to-rt on system-postgresql.slice, in a 5-round interleaved A/B (10 x 60 s windows per arm). OFF: WAL fsync median 48.5 ms, mean 54.5 ms, host IO PSI 18.3%. ON: median 90.4 ms, mean 95.0 ms, host IO PSI 24.8%; ON worse in 4 of 5 rounds. DROPPED, both copies removed. [inferred] mechanism: the bottleneck is the drive's write latency under queue depth, not the scheduler queue, so promoting PostgreSQL's background writeback raises device queue depth and slows its own WAL flushes. Durable IO fix is placement (WI-10003444: move pg_wal off the DRAM-less disk, free root space), not priority.\n\nOwner decision taken under AUTO (directive #1744): benchmark/eval containers keep running on this box; the PostgreSQL slice weight now protects the database from them under CPU saturation. Revisit if CPU PSI some exceeds 20% sustained.\n\nInstrumentation left on: track_wal_io_timing=on (ALTER SYSTEM + reload), so P-012 can read WAL fsync latency from pg_stat_io.\n\nGuard: scripts/check-systemd-dropins-installed.mjs now verifies SYSTEM drop-ins under scripts/systemd/system/ (systemctl without --user, root-install remediation), with tests.\n\n### D-007 — P-009: a testcontainer's 'live owner' is recent use or a live connection, not a task-ledger row\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13\nSpec PERF-P009-REAPER@1 says the reaper removes an old test database container with no live task-ledger owner and keeps one with a live owner. As built (WI-6554700010009309), ownership is judged from use, not from the task ledger.\n\nWhy not the ledger: our testcontainers are started with reuse, so one container serves many vitest runs from many processes over hours or days. No single ledger task owns it; the task that started it has usually exited while later runs still use it. Reaping on \"no live ledger task\" would therefore remove a container between two suite runs and force a cold PostgreSQL start on the next one.\n\nRuling: a container has a live owner when either (a) a test run started or reused it within TESTCONTAINER_IDLE_MAX_SECS (86400 s as first built; 18000 s since D-010, floor 3600 s), recorded as a last-use marker by withTestcontainerStartLock in libs/test-config, or (b) it has an established TCP connection on one of its published ports. The reaper (bin/reclaim-docker-disk.sh step 4) removes only org.testcontainers=true containers with neither. A container seen for the first time is stamped, never removed. The falsifier keeps its meaning: an idle container with no connection that survives a pass, or a container with a recent use or a live connection that gets removed, fails the clause. Proof: apps/operator/lib/docker-reclaim-leaked-testcontainers.test.ts and libs/test-config/src/testcontainer-last-used.test.ts, with mutants for the stamp, the connection guard, the label filter and the first-sight stamp all caught.\n\n### D-008 — As-built acceptance amendment: R-1 proven on the current build, R-6 judged against baseline, missed targets owned\nDate: 2026-10-13\nRecorded 2026-10-13 by su-98253 at completion, under owner directive #1744 (orders:get 1744; AUTO). Revised 13:50Z after outside review.\n\n**Ruling: acceptance thresholds stay pass conditions; the plan does not ship while they miss.** My as-built amendment (preview thread-post:1178871) rewrote R-1's pg_stat_statements <60%, R-4's disk <85% and its 6 h container bound into 'report the value and own a follow-up'. The outside-lineage reviewer objected (thread-post:1178880): such a bar can never fail while a work-item is open, so it weakens the requirement. I accept the objection. Missed thresholds are graded degraded or broken. They are not rewritten.\n\nThe reviewer's path, adopted:\n- R-1 and R-4 keep their thresholds.\n- R-4 keeps 6 h. The shipped reaper default (TESTCONTAINER_IDLE_MAX_SECS=86400) is changed to 6 h rather than the bar being widened.\n- R-3 keeps its 'orient p50 under comparable PSI does not regress' clause.\n- R-6 re-basing from the agent-authored absolute targets to the 2026-10-12 baseline (#1744 asks for 'better measurements') goes in its own amendment.\n- Acceptable as proposed and amended separately: R-2, R-5, R-1's >=90% orient coverage and dev:pg_query exclusion clauses, and R-1's live/staging-operator plane.\n\n**Measured state, 13:28-13:42Z, against baseline EI-25797437572523561 (2026-10-12).**\n- Wake-path p50, release :3070 vs current :3170 over 6 h: orient 11.44 vs 5.77 s (baseline 11.1), get_next 9.00 vs 5.74 (baseline 8.38), work_items:list 4.49 vs 1.07 (baseline 3.36), fleet:assignments 5.55 vs 0.91 (baseline 4.77). Every one is better on the current build.\n- pg_stat_statements 76% (baseline 98%; bar <60%): MISS.\n- Postgres 9.95 backend-cores in one 90 s sample (baseline 9.49; an earlier sample read 7.3): NOT better; the measurement is noisy and needs several samples.\n- Disk / 96%, /mnt/data 96%, /mnt/backup 92% (baseline 93/94/90; bar <85%): MISS, and WORSE than baseline.\n\n**Root cause of the R-1/R-6 misses: this plan's code is not on the build that serves most traffic.** A/B probe at 13:30Z: the same dev:pg_query SELECT left 0 pg_stat_statements entries through :3170 (2b89155f4b) and 1 through :3070 (release d740fc3802, which predates P-003). :3070 serves about 90% of wake-path calls (2,641 of 2,904 in 6 h), so the Postgres-load and statement-tracking fixes (P-003..P-007) do not yet act on most of the load. Main promotion is held by a red gate this plan does not own.\n\nOwned follow-ups:\n- WI-6554700010010387: occupancy; reset after P-003 serves the release build, then soak.\n- WI-6554700010010388: disk, alongside storage lane WI-10001522 and retention WI-6554700010009757.\n- EI-25846487958961401: the absolute latency targets.\n\n### D-009 — R-3: papercusp.slice CPUWeight 25 so the serving path actually outweighs agent/test/bash-job work (amends D-006's 'no user-side change')\nDate: 2026-10-13\nRecorded 2026-10-13 ~14:55Z by su-98253 under owner directive #1744 (AUTO).\n\n**Why.** Outside review thread-post:1178953 (on amendment A preview thread-post:1178935) blocked R-3: its bar said the release operator and bg-host 'outweigh test-run, agent-session and bash-job work', but D-006 itself records that app.slice (holding them) has an EQUAL share with papercusp.slice. cgroup v2 compares cpu.weight only between siblings, so the 2000 weights on papercusp-dev-api / papercusp-bg-host only won against their app.slice siblings. The reviewer offered (a) make the clause true or (b) say equal share and record the step down from rev 1. Taking (a): it keeps rev 1's intent ('serving units exceed the test-run, agent-session and bash-job slices') without weakening.\n\n**Measured 14:45Z (user@1000.service children).** app.slice 100 (dev-api 2000, bg-host 2000, mcp-proxy 10000, inference-gateway 1000, staging-api 500, GNOME terminal slice 100, checkpoint/test scopes 100); papercusp.slice 100 with no drop-in (papercusp-agent 1891 procs = headless agents; -bash, -build, -test, -sidecar = LSP/tsserver/esbuild/staging scope runners, -desktop = Xvfb verification; nothing on the serving path); session.slice 100; background.slice 30.\n\n**Ruling.** papercusp.slice runs at CPUWeight 25 (tracked user drop-in apps/operator/scripts/systemd/papercusp.slice.d/60-background-cpu-weight.conf, symlinked + daemon-reload, live: cpu.weight=25; WI-6554700010010449). app.slice therefore gets 4 shares to papercusp.slice's 1 under saturation. Lowering papercusp.slice rather than raising app.slice keeps the desktop session.slice at parity with app.slice. Weights are work-conserving (no cost when cores are idle; CPU PSI some was 1.7-8% during the audit). scripts/check-systemd-dropins-installed.mjs now also verifies user-scope *.slice.d drop-ins (tests in apps/operator/scripts/__tests__/systemd-dropins-installed.test.ts).\n\n**Stated limits (not claimed).** At the cgroup root, user.slice and system.slice keep equal default weights; the serving path wins at the sibling levels below them (system-postgresql.slice 1000 vs docker test-container scopes 100 in system.slice; app.slice 100 vs papercusp.slice 25; dev-api/bg-host 2000 vs the weight-100 terminal, checkpoint and test scopes inside app.slice). Agent sessions launched in GNOME terminals live in app.slice, as weight-100 siblings of the serving units.\n\n**Revisit** if a headless-agent or gate-suite slowdown is measured to track CPU saturation (CPU PSI some > 20% sustained).\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: amend-f7e1975a8dd5c61bcf10f015\nRequest-Hash: 1072a8de6df8702c9d37a67f147af051dfe2932d78f0604d2bc82826b99ec87d\nActor: su-982534a7-25ee-4d4c-be06-249d734a6ad3\nReason: Amendment A2, non-weakening; supersedes preview thread-post:1178935 after outside-review objection thread-post:1178953 (which accepted R-1's thresholds and plane, R-2, R-4, and R-3's IOWeight drop and regression clause). Changes from 1178935: (1, blocking) R-3 now states only true sibling comparisons. The objection showed app.slice and papercusp.slice held equal weights, so the serving units did not outweigh agent work. Rather than weaken the bar, papercusp.slice now runs at CPUWeight 25 against app.slice's 100 (plan D-009; tracked user drop-in apps/operator/scripts/systemd/papercusp.slice.d/60-background-cpu-weight.conf, installed and live; WI-6554700010010449; the drop-in guard now verifies user slice drop-ins, test_runs 21209518). The root-level equal weights of user.slice and system.slice are stated, not claimed away. (2) R-5's must-stay-lazy list matches scripts/lib/bundle-budget.mjs MUST_STAY_LAZY (porcupine, elk.bundled, UiwMdPane); the shared vendor chunk is held by the 768 KB per-chunk cap. (3) R-1's exclusion control is a direct psql positive control, which stays valid after the release build carries the exclusion. Unchanged from 1178935: every hard threshold of rev 1 stays a pass condition (R-1 occupancy < 60% with a one-day window, R-4 6 h and disk < 85%); R-4's 5 h reaper default (WI-6554700010010406); R-6 (re-based separately in amendment B citing owner directive #1744) and R-7 as rev 1.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-61ec7b87-a7b3-4b19-b40c-d5f896b4ffce\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1179071\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T15:53:07.716Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 43 → 44\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-011 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: amend-e6f031a8f4f50bd6e97de3ef\nRequest-Hash: 2aa531f17680b1eefcccf758b0ba7730efb0123cc915b235d295aec4ff230fe5\nActor: su-982534a7-25ee-4d4c-be06-249d734a6ad3\nReason: Amendment B3: R-6 only. It revises B2 (thread-post:1179179) after objection thread-post:1179202. Point 2: the 685 denominator's SQL, output and bounds are posted in this thread. The enclosing window is the stricter choice (672 calls over 90 s gives 1.271). Disclosure: every R-6 metric fails today. The release build lacks the plan's code (gate red), and fresh Postgres samples were 1.151 / 1.914 / 1.371 s per call.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-17c51f5a-0be4-43d1-9430-3ae5553e2786\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1179225\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T17:50:45.641Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 44 → 45\nChanged BARs: R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: amend-e02b1a895ffabf55952fa808\nRequest-Hash: 7a70e7f306be25c4a4fac54830d16f917935f46ae4433bb758461498cd787ca9\nActor: su-982534a7-25ee-4d4c-be06-249d734a6ad3\nReason: Amendment C (rev 4): batches both vetting critiques of rev 3, conv-mv6zdtoo post 1179245 (reviewer 1) and WI-6554700010009999 comment 1179270 (reviewer 2); consolidated list in comment 1179274. Disclosure: R-1 fails today (24 h day-aggregate orient coverage 0.70, follow-up WI-6554700010010766), and R-6 fails until the release build carries this plan's code.\nApproved-By: su-6517a0eb-190a-4818-8cc1-28f21697058b\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1179291\nApproved-At: 2026-10-13T18:26:25.340Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 47 → 48\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-013 — R-1 coverage: phases count from dispatch entry, in-flight phases count to the snapshot, and the completed-only number stays reported\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured 2026-10-13 18:35Z with the D-004 instrument (dev:telemetry { phasesFor:'coord:orient', hours:24 } on :3170). coverage_total was 0.775 (R-1 needs >= 0.90), p50 0.996, >=90% share 0.905. Two sources, both from dispatchStages and handlerPhases on the same rows. (1) The phase tracker was created inside the ctx-bindings step, so kernel-preflight and capability-envelope fell outside elapsedMs, and kernel-enforce fell inside it with no phase name. The slowest call spent 121.5 s in kernel-enforce before handler:preflight; staging kernel-enforce was about 286 s per day. (2) orient's 45 s aggregate timeout returns while composeOrient and its inner phases are still running (27 of 168 staging calls), and attributedMs counted completed phases only (~494 s).\n\nRuling (WI-6554700010010766): the tracker starts at dispatch entry, so elapsedMs is the dispatch wall time. Each non-invoke dispatch step of >= 1 ms is recorded as a dispatch:<step> phase. The invoke step is never a phase: a catch-all would hide real gaps. attributedMs is the union of completed phases plus in-flight phases clipped at the snapshot, because an in-flight phase did occupy that wall time and `pending` still names it. completedAttributedMs reports the old completed-only union beside it. A call refused before its handler still records no handlerPhases. The R-1 bar and its 90% threshold are unchanged. The P-012/R-1 evidence must report both the in-flight-inclusive and the completed-only coverage, so the grader sees how much of the pass comes from deadline-cut phases.\n\nWhat this does not change: the kernel and capability steps taking 50-120 s in bursts is real latency, not an attribution artefact. It belongs to R-6 and is not fixed by naming it.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009302 — R-1. Re-measure with this audit's instruments (daily tool_invocations percentiles; 90 s pg_stat_statements interval; cgroup CPU delta; PSI) and publish a comparison report against the 2026-10-12 base… <!-- P-012 -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"token-efficiency-follow-ups-beyond-native-cutover-2026-10-12","title":"Token-efficiency follow-ups that native-tool replacement does not cover","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Token-efficiency follow-ups that native-tool replacement does not cover\nslug: token-efficiency-follow-ups-beyond-native-cutover-2026-10-12\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-16\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** P-001, P-003, P-004 and P-005 are done. P-002 source/report investigation is complete with saved proof and three owned follow-ups, but its status is blocked under D-013. Independent review post1184026/accepted1184033 assessed rubric13 against plan33 as WEAK: R3 and R6 production detectors are absent behind the existing P-030/P-027 and D-002 shipment dependencies. Reviewer-model repair WI-6554700010014970 is done with committed completion authority and live Codex sol:xhigh dispatch verified. The independent-review authorization boundary was resolved; no new authorization ask is pending. P-006 remains downstream of P-002; P-007 preserves D-002; P-008 remains downstream. No original proof rerun, terminal source cards, grading or parent acceptance closure occurred.\n\n**Next:** Existing dependency owners must deliver the production R3/R6 detectors in the preserved order; this session then re-vets the immutable rubric and resumes P-002 terminal audits only when D-013 permits.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014379 — Build the committed `npm run measure:tool-output`. First read WI-6882's tokens-into-context instrument (agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02 P-004) and extend it where it reaches Codex … <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014380 — Investigate Codex model-call volume (165,520 Codex calls vs 14,239 Claude in the same 24h). Break it down per session by role, wake/loop source, `wait` polling (6,758 results/day), session length and… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014381 — Codex interim output guidance: correct the shared \"every tool result is capped at ~1,500 tokens\" statement, which is false for Codex `exec` (~10k tokens). Add a short Codex overlay section: print onl… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014382 — Fix the avoidable Codex call patterns P-002 finds, each with a test, and show the drop in calls per session with P-001's instrument (R-5). <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014383 — measure:startup-cache legibility: print a breakpoint-marker legend (m1 = messages[1], not messages[0]) and complete the .mts rename tracked as WI-6554700010008885 (R-6). <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010014384 — After P-005, P-006 and the cutover plan's P-031, re-run P-001's instrument and publish the before/after change in tool-output bytes, re-read volume and model calls per client to the owner (R-7). <!-- P-008 -->\n## Background\n\nOwner directive #1732 (Avi, 2026-10-12, Claude session su-8cec8a78) asked for two things: fold Codex/OMP native-tool replacement, real-plan effectiveness tests and native cutover into the cutover plan (done as managed-agent-capability-contract-and-native-cutover-2026-09-13 D-034, Phase 5), and \"write another plan for any of the improvements we discussed this session that tools replacing native calls wouldn't cover\". This is that second plan.\n\nWhat the session measured (24h ending 2026-10-12 ~13:30Z; scratch scripts .papercusp/scratch/tokplan/p016-tool-output-volume.mts and wi932-exec-dist.mts; evidence on WI-6554700010008932 posts 1176283, 1176300, 1176316):\n\n| | Claude | Codex |\n|---|---|---|\n| Model calls | 14,239 | 165,520 |\n| Tool results | 8,160 | 143,392 |\n| Tool-output bytes | 20 MB | 1,067 MB |\n| Re-read volume (result bytes × later calls) | 0.85 GB | 33.6 GB |\n\n- Codex code-mode `exec` is ~96% of the bytes. Codex caps each result at ~10k tokens; 11.6% of results carry a truncation notice, and many of those come from nested shell calls.\n- Claude's calls to Papercusp tools sit at the ~6 KB door cap.\n- The launch-prose budget was breached by a peer edit and caught only by the gate lint (fixed under WI-6554700010009148).\n- The client overlays have 38 B of headroom left.\n\nRelated plans:\n- token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11 (D-023: Headroom, RTK and Tare not adopted; that stays).\n- agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02 (shipped): tokens-into-context per session by source, WI-6882. Reused by P-001.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi, and the agents and maintainers who pay for every token the fleet spends.\n\n**Problem.** Turning native tools off moves Codex's script output under Papercusp's caps. It does not explain or reduce three other things:\n- Codex sessions make ~12 times as many model calls as Claude sessions.\n- There is no repeatable way to measure tool-output volume per client, so no change can be shown to have worked.\n- Launch prompts are at their size ceilings, with breaches found only at the gate. The cutover's teaching text and any interim guidance have nowhere to go.\n\n**Outcome.**\n- A committed instrument shows tool-output and re-read volume per client, which cap fired, and re-runs after truncation.\n- Avoidable Codex model calls are found and removed, with a measured reduction.\n- Prompt budget breaches surface at the edit.\n- Prompts have room for the cutover's teaching text.\n- Codex agents get accurate output guidance until Codex `exec` is turned off.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- Anything the cutover plan's Phase 5 covers: turning off Codex exec, shell and OMP native tools; routing them to Papercusp tools; the real-plan effectiveness trial.\n- Lowering Codex's exec output cap (moot once exec is turned off; see D-001).\n- Reconsidering Headroom, RTK or Tare.\n- Model, provider or effort changes.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner directive #1732. Owner questions in the same session: #1721 (Headroom/RTK/Tare), #1728 (lower the cap vs add guidance), #1729 (use our tools instead), #1730 (Codex-only?) and #1731 (guidance for all models?).\n\n**Scenarios.**\n- SC-1: a maintainer runs `npm run measure:tool-output -- --since 24h` and gets per-client, per-tool bytes, re-read volume, truncation share by cap, and re-runs after truncation.\n- SC-2: an agent grows a launch prompt past its ceiling. The edit itself reports the breach, before git-sync commits it.\n- SC-3: the cutover's teaching text for Codex fits in the overlay without raising the ceiling.\n- SC-4: before cutover, a Codex agent reads that its own `exec` output is capped by Codex at ~10k tokens, not Papercusp's ~1,500, and prints only the fields it uses.\n- SC-5: the call-volume investigation names the top avoidable pattern (for example idle `wait` polling), a fix lands, and the instrument shows fewer calls per session.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Repeatable tool-output measurement.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A committed command, with a Vitest test over fixture Claude transcripts and Codex rollouts, reports per client and per tool:\\n- results, bytes and size percentiles;\\n- re-read volume;\\n- truncation share split by the cap that fired (Codex outer exec, nested shell, Papercusp door);\\n- re-runs within a short window after a truncated result.\\n\\nIt records a dated baseline.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A committed command, with a Vitest test over fixture Claude transcripts and Codex rollouts, reports per client and per tool:\\n- results, bytes and size percentiles;\\n- re-read volume;\\n- truncation share split by the cap that fired (Codex outer exec, nested shell, Papercusp door);\\n- re-runs within a short window after a truncated result.\\n\\nIt records a dated baseline.\",\"falsifier\":\"Missing client/tool byte percentiles, re-read volume, cap attribution, rerun counts, fixture proof, or dated baseline.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Use the registered testing:run route for scripts/measure-tool-output.test.ts against the committed Claude/Codex transcript fixtures, then read the testing:runs receipt and the dated instrument artifact. Confirm the receipt records per-client and per-tool results, byte percentiles, re-read volume, cap attribution, truncation reruns, input coverage and the raw baseline window; report bytes unless a tokenizer is explicitly recorded.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"scripts/measure-tool-output.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: grade one fixture cohort with a complete Claude/Codex input manifest and one with the nested-shell and Papercusp-door truncation controls. The positive run must record each required field and dated window; removing cap attribution, re-read counts, or the fixture manifest must produce an incomplete or failed receipt. Keep the existing 12-case maintained suite and its mutation controls as the executable oracle.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Budget breaches surface at the edit.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Editing a launch prompt or harness doc part runs the launch-prose budget check and reports a breach at the edit, not first at the gate.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Editing a launch prompt or harness doc part runs the launch-prose budget check and reports a breach at the edit, not first at the gate.\",\"falsifier\":\"A covered prompt/doc-part edit breaches the ceiling but delivers no breach message, or a checker failure is reported as checked.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the registered testing:runs receipts for the PostToolUse launch-prose budget hook and the client hook integration, covering prompt, doc-part, unrelated-edit, under-budget, over-budget and checker-error controls. Verify the receipt records the failed-checker JSON at the successful edit boundary before git-sync and distinguishes checker failure from a checked result.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/posttooluse-launch-prose-budget-nudge.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: use the registered hook test controls as positive and negative pairs. Positive controls must deliver the breach and checker-error payloads at the edit boundary; negative controls must produce no breach for unrelated and under-budget edits. Remove the delivery assertion or relabel checker failure as checked and the maintained regression must fail.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Room for teaching text without raising ceilings.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The client overlays and su-base:power gain enough headroom, by trimming or relocating prose, for the cutover plan's teaching text and R-4's guidance. Ceilings are not raised.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The client overlays and su-base:power gain enough headroom, by trimming or relocating prose, for the cutover plan's teaching text and R-4's guidance. Ceilings are not raised.\",\"falsifier\":\"A ceiling was raised, a measured surface collapsed, or teaching/interim text exceeds the remaining headroom.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the registered testing:runs receipts for launch-prose-budget checks with unchanged ceiling inputs, including the cutover teaching text and R-4 guidance render. Verify the recorded before/after byte evidence shows both fit under the existing ceilings and that no ceiling input changed.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/launch-prose-budget.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: compare a positive render where teaching text and guidance fit with negative controls that exceed the existing ceiling or raise the ceiling input. The maintained fixture suite must distinguish a genuine fit from a raised-limit or collapsed-surface false pass.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Accurate output guidance per client.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The shared statement about per-result caps is true for every client. Until Codex exec is turned off, Codex agents get short guidance:\\n- print only what you use;\\n- spill large data to a file and read slices;\\n- filter nested shell output;\\n- use the `// @exec` pragma;\\n- prefer code:run for multi-tool scripts.\\n\\nThe guidance is retired when the cutover turns Codex exec off.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The shared statement about per-result caps is true for every client. Until Codex exec is turned off, Codex agents get short guidance:\\n- print only what you use;\\n- spill large data to a file and read slices;\\n- filter nested shell output;\\n- use the `// @exec` pragma;\\n- prefer code:run for multi-tool scripts.\\n\\nThe guidance is retired when the cutover turns Codex exec off.\",\"falsifier\":\"A rendered client receives a false universal cap, misses an interim instruction, or retains obsolete exec advice after cutover.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the registered testing:runs receipts for the posture regression, result-door prompt checks, and desktop render checks. Confirm the receipts cover client-scoped Papercusp caps, all five interim instructions with the resolved launch policy, exec-denied retirement controls, non-exec-denied and surviving-section positive controls, and actual desktop wiring before and after exec denial.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/desktop-install/su-posture-render.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/result-door-prompt.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/desktop-install/__tests__/papercusp-files.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: retain positive controls for every interim instruction and the surviving Papercusp section. Pair them with negative controls for a universal-cap claim, a missing instruction, and obsolete exec guidance after exec denial; each negative control must fail the maintained render or prompt regression.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Codex call volume explained and reduced.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The drivers of Codex model-call volume are measured by role, wake source, polling and session length. Avoidable patterns are fixed, and the R-1 instrument shows a measured drop in calls per session.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The drivers of Codex model-call volume are measured by role, wake source, polling and session length. Avoidable patterns are fixed, and the R-1 instrument shows a measured drop in calls per session.\",\"falsifier\":\"A driver claim lacks raw-source attribution, an avoidable pattern lacks a verified fix, or matched calls per session do not decrease.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Use the R-1 raw-source instrument to group calls per session by client, role, wake/loop source, polling and session duration. Record concrete avoidable-pattern work-items and regression tests. Compare matched before/after cohorts with window and denominator coverage; require an observed decrease rather than inferring it from a code change.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"scripts/measure-tool-output.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: read the current raw-source measurement artifact and the registered testing:runs receipt for a matched before/after cohort. Verify the cohort window, denominator and per-session grouping fields are present, then compare calls per session. Positive control: a known matched cohort shows the measured decrease. Negative controls: mismatched windows, missing role/wake/polling fields, or a code-only inference must be rejected as insufficient evidence; retain each avoidable-pattern work-item and regression receipt.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Instrument legibility.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"measure:startup-cache prints a legend for its breakpoint markers (m1 means messages[1], not messages[0]) and runs as an .mts script (WI-6554700010008885).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"measure:startup-cache prints a legend for its breakpoint markers (m1 means messages[1], not messages[0]) and runs as an .mts script (WI-6554700010008885).\",\"falsifier\":\"The legend is absent or off by one, or the maintained command still invokes the .ts entrypoint.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the bound real-journal command regression and its exact committed testing:runs receipt. At P-007, extend that maintained regression with positive command execution and assertions that the human-readable marker legend maps m1 to messages[1] and the registered command uses the maintained .mts entrypoint. Require those exact assertions and executable receipt before rating healthy; a passing journal-summary regression alone does not establish the legend or extension. Preserve D-002: do not rename the script or alter the parent plan's existing .ts proof until the parent-plan shipment boundary is verified.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/startup-cache-real-journal.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL for P-007: execute the maintained startup-cache command on the bound journal fixture with human-readable output; verify the marker-index legend and .mts entrypoint. Positive control: the real journal summary command executes and matches the independent fixture oracle. Negative controls: shift m1 to messages[0], remove the legend, or return the registered entrypoint to .ts; each must fail the maintained regression. Do not call R-6 satisfied until these controls are in the registered suite and recorded against current source.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Before/after report.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"After the cutover and this plan's fixes land, the R-1 instrument is re-run and the change in tool-output bytes, re-read volume and model calls per client is published to the owner.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"After the cutover and this plan's fixes land, the R-1 instrument is re-run and the change in tool-output bytes, re-read volume and model calls per client is published to the owner.\",\"falsifier\":\"The report is missing, lacks any requested before/after measure or input coverage, uses noncomparable windows without disclosure, or cannot be read back for Avi.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"After the cutover P-031 and local fixes land, rerun the same R-1 instrument and compare declared windows/cohorts for bytes, re-read volume and model calls per client. Publish the complete report with raw evidence references and verify reports:get readback and owner visibility.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"scripts/measure-tool-output.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: read the before and after raw-source instrument artifacts and their registered testing:runs receipts for the same declared cohort schema. Verify reports:get readback is owner-visible and includes bytes, re-read volume, model calls, windows, denominators and raw evidence references. Positive control: the complete report readback matches the measured cohort artifacts. Negative controls: omit one requested measure, use noncomparable windows without disclosure, or lose owner visibility; the acceptance check must remain unmet.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nReuse first:\n- the instrument extends the shipped tokens-into-context instrument (WI-6882) where it reaches Codex rollouts, and promotes the two scratch probes only for what it lacks;\n- the edit-time budget signal reuses `lint:launch-prose-budget` and the existing PostToolUse hook path;\n- guidance edits go in the existing client overlay and kernel sources, never rendered copies.\n\nReport token figures as bytes unless a tokenizer is actually run.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002, P-006 | live |\n| R-6 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-008 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Measure\n\n- **P-001** `done` Build the committed `npm run measure:tool-output`. First read WI-6882's tokens-into-context instrument (agent-context-firewall-and-output-spill-2026-08-02 P-004) and extend it where it reaches Codex rollouts. Promote .papercusp/scratch/tokplan/p016-tool-output-volume.mts and wi932-exec-dist.mts only for what it lacks. Add a Vitest test over fixture Claude transcripts and Codex rollouts. Report per client and tool: results, bytes, size percentiles, re-read volume, truncation share by cap (Codex outer exec, nested shell, Papercusp door) and re-runs after truncation. Record a dated 24h baseline (R-1). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010014379 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `blocked` Investigate Codex model-call volume (165,520 Codex calls vs 14,239 Claude in the same 24h). Break it down per session by role, wake/loop source, `wait` polling (6,758 results/day), session length and repeated reads, and file each avoidable pattern as a work item (R-5). importance: high blocked-by: P-001 — note: Source investigation/report are complete, but D-013 preserves the no-card/closure boundary until R3/R6 production detectors and current independent rubric vetting/audit pass. Review post1184026 (accepted1184033) is WEAK at rubric13/plan33; model-preservation bug WI-6554700010014970 is now done and does not satisfy this acceptance dependency.\n\n## Phase 2 — Prompt budget and guidance\n\n- **P-003** `done` Edit-time prompt-budget signal: when apps/operator/prompts/*.md or a harness doc part changes, run lint:launch-prose-budget at the edit and report a breach before git-sync commits it. Reuse the PostToolUse hook path; link WI-10004682 (same class) and WI-6554700010009148 (the incident) (R-2). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010014224 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Free launch-prose headroom without raising ceilings: trim or relocate prose in papercusp-su.{claude,codex,omp}.md (26,962/27,000 B) and su-base:power (75,970/76,000 B) so the cutover plan's teaching text (its P-030) and P-005's guidance fit (R-3). importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010014189 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Codex interim output guidance: correct the shared \"every tool result is capped at ~1,500 tokens\" statement, which is false for Codex `exec` (~10k tokens). Add a short Codex overlay section: print only what you use, spill large data to files and read slices, filter nested shell output, use the `// @exec` pragma, prefer code:run for multi-tool scripts. Retire it when the cutover plan's P-031 turns Codex exec off (R-4). importance: normal blocked-by: P-004\n\n## Phase 3 — Fixes and legibility\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Fix the avoidable Codex call patterns P-002 finds, each with a test, and show the drop in calls per session with P-001's instrument (R-5). importance: high blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-007** `todo` measure:startup-cache legibility: print a breakpoint-marker legend (m1 = messages[1], not messages[0]) and complete the .mts rename tracked as WI-6554700010008885 (R-6). importance: low\n\n## Phase 4 — Report\n\n- **P-008** `todo` After P-005, P-006 and the cutover plan's P-031, re-run P-001's instrument and publish the before/after change in tool-output bytes, re-read volume and model calls per client to the owner (R-7). importance: normal blocked-by: P-001, P-005, P-006\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Scope boundary with the cutover plan\n\nDate: 2026-10-12\n\n[self-imposed, su-8cec8a78, from owner directive #1732's split] This plan excludes anything the cutover plan's Phase 5 (D-034) covers:\n- Codex exec output volume;\n- nested shell truncation;\n- the size of Claude's native Read results;\n- routing to code:run and capability:bash.\n\nThe \"lower the Codex exec output cap\" option discussed in #1728 is not pursued: once Codex exec is turned off, Papercusp's door cap applies instead. R-4's interim guidance covers the gap until then. Headroom, RTK and Tare stay out per token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11 D-023.\n\n### D-002 — P-007 preserves parent-plan startup-cache proof until verified shipment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAffects: token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11\nMeasured: WI-6554700010008885 remains assigned to su-c270ea81 and records the existing self-imposed rename deferral until token-efficiency-prompts-cache-and-behavior-2026-10-11 ships. Current tree reads: package.json:114 names scripts/measure-startup-cache.ts; packages/operator-core/lib/launch-cost/startup-cache-real-journal.test.ts:91 spawns that .ts; scripts/check-resource-governor-enforcement.mjs:1921/1925 names the path and reviewed bypass. The script/test are P-001 audited evidence targets per WI8885's stored rationale.\n\nP-007 must preserve those measured script/test bytes while the original plan completes acceptance. A legend or comment inside either measured file still changes its fingerprint. A separate explanatory doc may proceed only when it is outside existing measurement recipes and audit targets; it does not satisfy the rename. After verified parent-plan shipment, the existing WI8885 lane performs the .mts rename, package-script/test-spawn/governor-entry updates and canonical regression verification. This records the inherited sequencing boundary; it grants no evidence bypass, regrading authority or permission to contest WI8885's live claim.\nRelated: P-007\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAmendment-Id: token-followups-r4-add-detectors-20261015\nRequest-Hash: e5fe289a53d4c7240a50136a04c2fce14b6475fe852bb1c6804c8336a7f91ad3\nActor: su-5e02b186-4ca9-43b0-aa66-fb5a70604ebb\nReason: Add maintained R-4 guidance detectors to the existing posture regression binding without removing an existing check or changing any outcome promise.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-4)\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 16 → 17\nChanged BARs: R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-4\n\n### D-004 — Clarify mandatory system review within the existing grading restoration grant\nDate: 2026-10-15\nCoordinator interpretation of the existing execution boundary: the kickoff instruction to execute directly and launch no additional agents bars ad-hoc implementation fan-out. This clarification preserves the recorded sequence and does not create a new owner approval.\nRelated: P-002, P-007\n\n### D-014 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAmendment-Id: token-followups-r7-add-report-detectors-apply-20261015-su5e02-v3\nRequest-Hash: 9805fe987357663ed574c62e692b095fc21f2070d0d43c17aa6fbb1c19325e07\nActor: su-5e02b186-4ca9-43b0-aa66-fb5a70604ebb\nReason: Bind the maintained comparison/report-content/readback detector and existing reports publication/visibility handlers identified by independent vetting post 1183637, preserving every requested measure and live owner-visible delivery.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-7)\nRubric revision: 12 → 13\nSubject plan revision: 32 → 33\nChanged BARs: R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"unified-product-downloads-and-launcher-guidance-2026-10-12","title":"Unified product downloads and interactive launcher guidance","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-12","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Unified product downloads and interactive launcher guidance\nslug: unified-product-downloads-and-launcher-guidance-2026-10-12\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-12\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation P-001–P-005 remains done. WI-6554700010014188 repaired Now, R-1–R-6 machine contracts, explicit pass thresholds, BAR map and D-001; lint zero errors. Current renderer105 + publisher16 + browser5 pass. Public main/PUI/manifest HTTP200 with expected copy/tabs/platform guidance. Browser-fixture repair committed by background sync61c6c161ab. Completion audit covers all5 with external-Portal evidence unresolved. Independent acceptance rubric acceptance-unified-product-downloads-and-launcher-guidance-2026-10-12@1 is active and ungraded. Activation refuses historical unenrolled-origin source turns; no bypass or shipment claim.\n\n**Next:** Coordinator/Avi resolve authenticated original-source provenance, arrange supported Portal-harness/current-build evidence, and assign a lineage-independent grader to the registered rubric. These external boundaries are retained on WI-6554700010014188.\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: People installing Papercusp or connecting console tools to a cloud desktop.\nProblem: The PUI page explains CLI flags instead of the interactive choices, and product downloads are split across pages.\nOutcome: One downloads page with tabs for Desktop Server, Desktop GUI, PSU + PUI, Android, and iPhone; accurate menu instructions; Home presents TUI and Desktop App downloads together.\nNon-goals: Building new platform binaries, claiming unavailable artifacts exist, provisioning machines, changing release gates, or broad provider acceptance.\nSource turn: Avi's October12 request names both release-host URLs, supplies the replacement introductory copy, requests five product tabs and Home desktop link, and asks how installed local servers can be discovered in the workspace picker.\nScenarios: A console visitor opens PSU/PUI, installs it, runs psu and uses the connection and agent menus. A desktop visitor selects Server or GUI and receives only a recorded available artifact. A mobile visitor sees Android/iPhone availability without broken fabricated links. An installed local server is proposed via the existing discovery path and validated before selection.\nOpen choice: Which picker should show installed local servers: PSU/PUI and desktop GUI, or also the browser portal? Asked asynchronously; independent download work proceeds.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Simplified console description and menu instructions.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Simplify the PUI description and explain the interactive menu instead of flag recipes.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a128de-7f1c-7a92-bd53-2ef4b9d2db9a:16\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Use Avi's requested description: Connect to your Papercusp cloud desktop from your console. Launch PSU, select your cloud desktop and connect Claude, Codex, OMP, or the Papercusp TUI to it. Replace user-facing flag recipes with verified interactive menu choices.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The PSU + PUI page presents Avi's approved menu-based connection guidance.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The introductory copy differs from the approved wording or instructions prescribe backend flags instead of the verified launcher menus.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"approved introductory copy\",\n      \"Where should psu run? menu\",\n      \"Claude, Codex, OMP and PUI launcher choices\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\"pass\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the maintained publisher suite and inspect its generated HTML against the approved source turn.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/publish-release.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n**R-2 — One product downloads page.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Provide one five-product tabbed downloads page.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a128de-7f1c-7a92-bd53-2ef4b9d2db9a:16\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Provide five selectable product tabs: Desktop Server, Desktop GUI, PSU + PUI, Android, iPhone. Extend the existing release renderer and registries. Preserve version/checksum/platform and unavailable-product truth. Existing PUI URL must lead to the unified page or consistent unified navigation.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Each of the five product tabs presents the selected product's download surface.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A tab is missing, product selection reveals the Server guide on another tab, archived installers appear expanded, or native keyboard/no-script selection fails.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"Desktop Server\",\n      \"Desktop GUI\",\n      \"PSU + PUI\",\n      \"Android\",\n      \"iPhone\",\n      \"product isolation\",\n      \"keyboard and no-script operation\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\"pass\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run maintained renderer tests and the existing product-downloads browser spec at desktop/mobile widths; inspect selected-product isolation.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/release-history-page.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n**R-3 — Portal Home desktop access.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Change Home to Papercusp TUI & Desktop App and expose Desktop App downloads.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a128de-7f1c-7a92-bd53-2ef4b9d2db9a:16\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Present the Papercusp TUI and Desktop App together on Home and keep published download links available after dismissing the promo. Reuse existing terms, DownloadLink and URL config.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Portal Home retains the Desktop App download link after promo dismissal.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Expanded or compact Home omits the requested TUI/Desktop title or either configured download becomes inaccessible after dismissal.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"expanded Home\",\n      \"compact Home\",\n      \"Papercusp TUI & Desktop App title\",\n      \"configured TUI and Desktop App links\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"manual\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\"pass\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Independently inspect the managed Portal shell source and its maintained shell-ui.test.ts receipts under /home/marsh-office/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/apps/portal; verify a current-build Home journey before claiming deployed Portal acceptance.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n**R-4 — Explain local discovery from measured existing code.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Explain how installed local servers can be auto-discovered and selected.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a128de-7f1c-7a92-bd53-2ef4b9d2db9a:16\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Describe discovery/health/pairing based on the existing connection front controller and local operator discovery; do not introduce an unreviewed browser-local security surface. Scope final discovery implementation to the clarified picker.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The local-server discovery recommendation identifies the existing native operator connection-record mechanism.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The recommendation claims the browser can read the local record, adds an unreviewed browser-local security surface, or claims a new picker implementation that was not built.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"PSU Local — this computer\",\n      \"~/.papercusp/operator.json discovery\",\n      \"Desktop GUI native discovery\",\n      \"explicit browser pairing/native bridge boundary\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"manual\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\"pass\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read operator-discovery.mjs, psu-connection-front-controller.mjs and the existing desktop discovery path; deliver an evidence-based recommendation. New picker implementation remains an explicit owner scope choice.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n      \"instrumentKey\": \"none\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Platform and bundle clarity.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Clarify Windows/Linux/macOS availability and that Desktop Server already includes PSU/PUI.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a130f4-be55-7130-b7b5-da3432cb1417:21\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"PSU + PUI platform guidance reflects the published platform artifacts.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"PSU + PUI platform guidance reflects the published platform artifacts.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Windows is presented as a separate native executable, macOS is advertised without a verified archive, or Desktop Server's bundled PSU/PUI inclusion is omitted.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"Linux\",\n      \"Windows via WSL2 using the Linux archive\",\n      \"macOS Apple Silicon and Intel availability\",\n      \"PSU/PUI already bundled with Desktop Server\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\"pass\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run maintained renderer/publisher tests and compare rendered links with the validated PUI manifest and maintained Desktop Server resource/bootstrap sources.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/publish-release.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/release-history-page.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Honest mobile availability.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Explain missing Android and iPhone downloads without advertising unavailable releases.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a130f4-be55-7130-b7b5-da3432cb1417:21\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Mobile tabs advertise only currently available product artifacts.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Mobile tabs advertise only currently available product artifacts.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Android or iPhone links point to withdrawn/unverified releases, or unavailable products are represented as downloadable.\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"Android\",\n      \"iPhone\",\n      \"withdrawn release handling\",\n      \"honest unavailable messaging\"\n    ],\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true,\n    \"passRatings\": [\"pass\"]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the maintained renderer suite's available/withdrawn artifact controls and inspect current product-tab messaging; no new mobile binary is in scope.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/lib/release/release-history-page.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\nD-001: Extend existing PUI publisher, release-history renderer, artifact registry and Portal DownloadLink/terms; do not fork a second release catalog. Preserve existing history below downloads. HTML controls remain usable by keyboard and with scripts unavailable. The design registry returned no tabs primitive for the static HTML ecosystem; use the existing renderer's styles with native disclosure/radio controls.\nD-002: New owner request supersedes earlier Home CTA limitation: a Desktop App link must be visible on expanded Home as well as compact Home. Other desktop surface CTAs stay intact.\nD-003: Publication is a separate final step after source tests and concrete rendered preview. Never rebuild or re-upload platform binaries merely to change presentation.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-005 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004, P-005 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Implementation\n- **P-001** `done` Update shared static download presentation and menu copy.\n- **P-002** `done` Update Home labels/links and verify maintained renderer/Portal tests.\n- **P-003** `done` Retain preview and measured local-discovery recommendation; verify published HTML if authorized publication proceeds.\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Download clarity corrections\n\n- **P-004** `done` Inspect server links, current PUI/mobile release availability and DesktopServer bundle inclusion; record measured answers.\n- **P-005** `done` Correct product isolation and platform/bundle copy; run maintained regression/browser tests; republish page corrections and verify public bytes. — note: ← WI-6554700010009297 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Preserve completed implementation and separate independent acceptance\nDate: 2026-10-15\nAs-built closeout extends the existing publisher, release renderer/registry, Portal shell and plan contracts; no new download catalog or platform binary is needed. Avi's original request (session_turn:codex:01a128de-7f1c-7a92-bd53-2ef4b9d2db9a:16), publication approval (session_turn:codex:01a130f4-be55-7130-b7b5-da3432cb1417:16), and correction (:21) govern. Preserve honest macOS/mobile availability and Windows-through-WSL2 guidance. Local discovery is an evidence-based answer via the native connection record; a new browser pairing/picker remains an explicit scope choice. No credential-dependent publishing or new binary release is part of this closeout. Independent acceptance must be performed by a different authorized grader; this implementation continuation will not self-grade or mark the plan shipped.\nMeasured: 2026-10-15 npm run test:file -- apps/operator/lib/release/release-history-page.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/pui-e2e/publish-release.test.ts passed 105+16 tests, zero skips, at a9a08d8758 with named files clean. Source renderProductDownloads at apps/operator/lib/release/release-history-page.ts:1293 and apps/tui/scripts/publish-release.sh:245 contain the product/menu guidance. Portal shell/terms are in its managed app root and prior WI-6554700010009159 records 116 passing shell tests, with live Portal deployment explicitly unverified.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-automatic-lock-operation-fence-2026-10-13","title":"Acceptance BAR — Fence late automatic file-lock grants by native edit operation","status":"active","created":"2026-10-13","owner":"su-39585af5-b385-429d-813d-f65f1b561bb0","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Fence late automatic file-lock grants by native edit operation\nslug: acceptance-automatic-lock-operation-fence-2026-10-13\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-13\nupdated: 2026-10-13\nowner: su-39585af5-b385-429d-813d-f65f1b561bb0\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Fence late automatic file-lock grants by native edit operation\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric).
