Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"automatic-lock-operation-fence-2026-10-13","title":"Fence late automatic file-lock grants by native edit operation","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Fence late automatic file-lock grants by native edit operation\nslug: automatic-lock-operation-fence-2026-10-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-13\nupdated: 2026-10-20\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: agents and peers editing the shared staging tree. Problem: an automatic PreToolUse acquire can commit after the HTTP hook timed out and after its recovery queue read; no cached lock token reaches PostToolUse. The orphan blocks publication and prevents exact native edit attribution. Outcome: each native edit operation ends with a received grant or a serialized cancellation/completion receipt, and a late grant cannot survive that operation's terminal fence.\nNon-goals: owner-wide release, time-based holder guesses, timeout increases, new lock services/tables, live gate operations, or replay of unchanged passing checks.\nSource turns and evidence: session_turn:codex:01a12c53-fa75-7442-b64d-ce14abedf53e:1 (full takeover/AUTO), session_turn:codex:01a12ce4-bdf4-7f82-94e5-2d456b0d14d2:6 (prevent unnecessary passed-test reruns). owner-authorized SELF/AUTO full-session takeover is retained on WI-6554700010008664 and owner fact mode-instructions:auto; this is a derived fix for owned EI-23241836994497967. Its checkpoint783ab38f68e5 distinguishes timeout21:44:27, late grant21:44:31.245 and native edit success21:44:32.257. Managed continuation explicitly selects this operation-correlated fence as an independent next action.\nScenarios: cancellation may serialize before acquire, after acquire, or while the caller cannot receive its reply. A successful edit must release and attribute only its own newly held paths. An overlapping explicit same-owner lock must remain held. Duplicate retries must refer to the same operation. Native functions.exec parent completion must settle the child edit's operation without a cached .lock token.\nOpen implementation choice: audit the existing @papercusp/locks waiter ticket and authority route before choosing the smallest typed extension. No new durable surface is approved by this draft.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Correlated terminal fence.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A stable native operation identity, established before acquire, has a serialized terminal outcome preventing an uncached late grant, including cancellation-before-acquire.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A stable native operation identity, established before acquire, has a serialized terminal outcome preventing an uncached late grant, including cancellation-before-acquire.\",\"falsifier\":\"A delayed or duplicate acquire leaves operation-owned rows after a terminal cancellation or completion.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run new operation-fence SQL integration cases with controlled transaction ordering: finish/cancel before acquire, acquire before finish, delayed reply, duplicate acquire, and owner/domain collision.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/__tests__/su-lock-store.integration.test.ts\",\"libs/papercusp/packages/locks/src/su-lock-store.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Exact scope and attribution.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Reconciliation releases only operation-new paths, preserves deliberate and foreign holds, and attributes successful native edit proof through the maintained release path.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Reconciliation releases only operation-new paths, preserves deliberate and foreign holds, and attributes successful native edit proof through the maintained release path.\",\"falsifier\":\"A fence releases an explicit or foreign hold, releases a different operation's rows, or loses successful native attribution.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run new isolation and native-proof cases; inspect exact released and attributed path sets and surviving explicit lock IDs.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/__tests__/su-lock-store.integration.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/pretooluse-locks-decision.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Existing lifecycle and routes.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The typed operation fence uses maintained lock/waiter storage and local/remote authority routing with explicit unknown outcomes.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The typed operation fence uses maintained lock/waiter storage and local/remote authority routing with explicit unknown outcomes.\",\"falsifier\":\"A remote path falls back to local writes, bypasses operation identity, or adds a parallel service/table.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read existing waiter schema and route adapters; run new authority contract cases for operation acquire/completion/cancellation and domain/owner isolation.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/authority/__tests__/file-lock-authority-ops.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/__tests__/su-lock-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Recurrence evidence.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Canonical new tests prove delayed grant handling, cancellation ordering, duplicate retries, native parent completion and deliberate-hold preservation without unnecessary passing-test replay.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Canonical new tests prove delayed grant handling, cancellation ordering, duplicate retries, native parent completion and deliberate-hold preservation without unnecessary passing-test replay.\",\"falsifier\":\"The observed late-grant order still leaks a lock, parent settlement requires a .lock token, or verification repeats unchanged passing checks.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run only newly added or failed operation-fence cases using focused test selectors; record executable test commands, terminal results, changed source hashes, and no old PASS replay.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/pretooluse-locks-decision.test.ts\",\"libs/papercusp/packages/locks/src/su-lock-store.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/__tests__/su-lock-store.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/authority/__tests__/file-lock-authority-ops.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\nReuse-first read: pretooluse-locks-acquire.sh _locks_acquire_once/_recover_ambiguous_acquire; posttooluse-locks-release.sh; locks/acquire.ts and cancel_wait.ts; file-lock-authority-ops.ts; existing @papercusp/locks waiter store. The immediate acquire contract presently lacks an operation key and cancel_wait accepts only an already-issued ticket. Reuse that lifecycle after checking its transaction and authority guarantees. P-001 records the exact contract and source files before production edits.\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n\n## Tasks\n- **P-001** `done` Audit existing waiter/authority primitives; record exact operation-correlated acquire, cancellation and native-completion contract. — note: ← WI-6554700010009521 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement the smallest maintained hook/store/authority extension with canonical race and isolation tests. blocked-by: P-001 — note: ← WI-6554700010009522 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `todo` Run only new or failed focused cases; verify correlated terminal outcomes and record scoped source/runtime evidence. blocked-by: P-002 — note: ← WI-6554700010009523 released\n\n## Decisions\nD-001: This plan is derived from the owned bug and retains the existing SELF/AUTO route. It is a draft until the required activation/source-conversation audit is recorded. No live gate lane is claimed.\n\n### D-001 — Reuse waiter tickets as operation lifecycle records at the lock authority\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured: 2026-10-13 source reads of libs/papercusp/packages/locks/src/su-lock-store.ts (AcquireParams, tryAcquire, tryInsertWaiter, tryCancelWait), src/sql/002-tables.sql, in-workspace-txn.ts, acquire.ts, cancel_wait.ts and file-lock-authority-ops.ts. Immediate acquires have no operation key; waiter ticket UUID and terminal cancelled/granted rows already exist. Cancellation currently updates only existing waiting tickets. Hook stores sidecars only after receiving a grant; timeout recovery is one queue snapshot. Extend existing waiter records with operation lifecycle metadata, using a deterministic native-operation ticket ID persisted before HTTP. Acquire and terminal fence serialize under the existing authority transaction/path scope. A cancellation-before-acquire inserts a cancelled tombstone; retry reads the same operation. Immediate grants retain newly_held paths in operation metadata; final release selects exact operation lock ID plus those paths, preserves deliberate and foreign locks, and uses existing native proof attribution. Parent completion reconciles operation sidecars even without .lock. Route cancellation/completion to the same authority as acquire, refuse unknown outcomes, do not use owner-wide releases or timeout increases. Existing terminal-waiter GC needs explicit tombstone safety for late requests; audit that retention before implementation. No new table/service, no live-gate operation.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-002 — Pin operation admission and terminal proof before HTTP\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured: read existing AcquireParams/tryAcquire/tryRelease/waiter store, 24h terminal waiter GC, file-lock-routing, authority boot adapter, release native proof ledger and CC acquire/release tests. Contract: (1) hook persists operation UUID, native session/tool ID, exact domain+paths, intent and fixed admission deadline before sending acquire; retries reuse that metadata. Authority accepts a deadline only within the existing maximum lease horizon, and refuses every acquire after it, including after terminal-row GC. Deadline is request admission, never a holder-identity timestamp guess. (2) Existing agent_lock_waiters gains typed hook-operation metadata; immediate operation records are not FIFO waiting entries. Ticket ID is operation UUID; mismatched owner/domain/paths/deadline/intent refuses without mutation. No new table/service. (3) Acquire and finish serialize on existing domain/path scope and operation row. Duplicate grant returns its original newly-held set without refreshing an explicit hold. Finish-before-acquire persists a terminal tombstone; any late request refuses. Finish-after-grant releases only stored operation-new paths by exact lock ID+owner+domain. Cancel and completion are terminal; a later positive native proof may enrich a cancelled operation but cannot reacquire it. (4) Extend maintained acquire/release/cancel_wait and same authority adapter; an operation transport error cannot silently write another local store. Ordinary legacy requests keep compatibility. Hook retains operation sidecars on unknown outcomes and settles via native PostToolUse, successful retry or provably terminal parent completion; a yielded parent must not settle a live nested edit. (5) Successful native proof must match stored requested scope and recognized tool; release uses maintained attribution with a stable operation-derived dispatchCallId for duplicate-safe recording, including fail-open completion with no received grant. Explicit holds remain held. Cancellation has no edit proof. (6) Terminal operation rows keep existing24h GC, safely beyond the fixed maximum admission horizon. Current focused guards must exercise cancel-before-acquire, delayed grant after lost reply, duplicate request/completion, path/owner/domain mismatch, explicit/foreign preservation, parent yield vs completion, attribution once and expired-request-after-GC. P001 is source/contract audit only; P002 owns code/tests and P003 new/failed execution.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Protocol skew must retain operation admission; legacy deny removal is unlocked fail-open\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured: 2026-10-13 current apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/pretooluse-locks-acquire.sh:1357–1361 constructs req_without_coordination_domain only when hook_operation is absent; lines1938–1945 deny protocol rejection, then the None branch calls allow() without acquiring. Current operation requests carry hook_operation. Therefore deleting1938 does not restore a protected legacy acquire: it permits an edit with no operation grant or late-request terminal fence. This is a clarification of D-002, not a scope expansion. Preserve operation/domain and the prepared authority pin. Qualify the selected native origin against maintained acquire/release/cancel_wait schemas and read-only preparation before activating operation hooks; verify positive native terminal completion. Installer provenance/syntax alone does not qualify wire protocol. No arbitrary origin fallback, guard bypass, shared restart or LIVE_GATE_OPS in P-002. Ordinary legacy non-operation callers retain the compatibility promised by D-002. P-002 continues independent regression/retention review; P-003 acceptance requires the qualified native journey.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-004 — Edit route while the native lock hook denies every edit: server-side capability:edit/write only\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13 (fleet leader su-51c5f29f, fleet byoc-cloud-carry-1013; ruling requested by P-002 holder su-c21ef110).\nMeasured: 08:30Z, a native Claude Write by su-51c5f29f to a gitignored .papercusp/scratch path was refused: \"locks: running operator rejected the operation scope\". su-c21ef110 measured the same at 08:20Z. The installed ~/.papercusp/hooks/cc/pretooluse-locks-acquire.sh (sha e4dbb4a24f41, equal to the staging source) sends hook_operation unconditionally. :3070 runs d740fc3802, which predates the operation protocol, and D-003 correctly denies rather than downgrading. So every native Claude Edit/Write and Codex apply_patch on this host has been refused since at least about 05:17Z (EI-25839007779877415 is the earliest of about ten duplicate filings). EI-25844893207306564 (su-07164, 06:27-06:33Z) observed capability:edit and capability:write through tools:invoke succeeding, with the per-path lock taken on the server.\nRuling: (1) Until the P-002 fix is reinstalled, the edit route for every member of this fleet, and for P-002 itself, is capability:edit / capability:write dispatched through tools:invoke. The server acquires the per-path lock inside the same request that writes the file, so lock arbitration holds and there is no client-side timeout window in which a late grant can strand a lock, which is the race D-002/D-003 fence. [inferred from the request shape; the P-002 holder verifies it with one focused read of the server edit path]. This neither modifies nor routes around the native hook. (2) Raw Bash writes to tracked files (sed -i, heredocs, > redirects) remain forbidden. (3) The client-side secrets, content-lint, migration and generated-file guards do not run on a tools:invoke dispatch. So through this route, make no edits to migrations (libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql), generated files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, BORROWABLE.md and the like) or anything secret-bearing; those wait for the fix. (4) P-002 lands the D-003 origin-qualification gate through route (1). When the origin is not qualified, no operation record is created and the legacy acquire runs; when it is qualified, operation mode applies; an operation is never stripped once created. It needs focused canonical tests, then the maintained installer (installClaudeHooks) reinstalls the bundle, and the holder announces readiness once with a native-Write positive control. (5) Route (b), waiting for a :3070 deploy that carries the protocol, is rejected: it is the gate owner's lane and is the slow path. Route (c), reinstalling an older bundle, is unnecessary once (4) lands. The duplicate outage filings are linked to WI-6554700010009522 and closed when (4) is verified.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n### D-005 — An inert operation record (never pinned, past its admission deadline) is retired, not replayed\nDate: 2026-10-13\nDate: 2026-10-13. Measured: between 12:49 and 13:16Z, 10 hook_operation acquires from 8 owners replayed <tool_use_id>.operation.json records written before the fix, and every one had an admission deadline that had already passed. The origin was unqualified, so each replay produced the outage deny (EI-25871003145591038). Basis: the authority admits only a pinned acquire, and the hook persists the pin before it sends that acquire. The authority also refuses every acquire after the admission deadline (D-002). Ruling: a record with no authority pin, no terminal state and a deadline more than INERT_OPERATION_GRACE_SEC=300s in the past (the grace absorbs authority clock skew) is INERT. No acquire under it was admitted, and none can be. The PreToolUse hook retires an inert record by renaming it to <path>.expired before the D-003 operation-mode gate, and that call then proceeds as if no record existed: a legacy acquire at an unqualified origin, a fresh operation at a qualified one. settle_lock_operation treats an inert record as settled: it sends no preparation acquire and retires the record. This is not a D-003 strip. D-003 protects an operation that may still be admitted or granted, and an inert record can be neither. Records that are pinned, terminal, unreadable or still admissible keep the never-strip rule unchanged. Implemented in apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/mcp_response.py (lock_operation_inert, retire_inert_lock_operation, settle_lock_operation) and pretooluse-locks-acquire.sh. Tests: four cases in __tests__/lock-operation-fence.test.ts. Deferred: a GC for inert records of dead sessions that never recur. They are inert and harmless, so this is clutter only.\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-13\nAmendment-Id: 39585-operation-fence-detector-binding-20261013-1\nRequest-Hash: b2d8bf663183ac21ed803bb2382bbb436230367fa777d9856f3d2ca0c72f69ef\nActor: su-39585af5-b385-429d-813d-f65f1b561bb0\nReason: Detector-binding and verification-method correction under existing D-002/D-003/D-004(4)/D-005; preserve all four outcome BARs, hashes, required scopes/layers and current-build acceptance. External rubric-vetting consult conv-mv6s834j-0000-3546b39333c44ffaa8bcca7012079564 returned no qualified responder; no outside-lineage approval is asserted.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4)\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 14 → 15\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-007 — P-003 binds final native validation to the post-WI10405 hook source\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured: 2026-10-13T20:32Z authoritative WI-6554700010009523 is unclaimed/open and in scope for existing validator su-respawn-bb278a02; WI-6554700010010405 is open/assigned su-c21ef110. P-002 completed20:23Z. c21's directed request reports WI10405 is changing the same PreToolUse hook and would invalidate earlier P-003 source evidence. Governing D-002/D-003 require qualified native terminal proof; D-006 retains historical but revision-ineligible evidence. Clarification of those current-source requirements: P-003 may prepare its focused cases now, but its final correlated native evidence must use the containing source after WI10405 succeeds. Record a success dependency from WI10405 to WI9523; retain the separate bb278a02 validator and every existing BAR. Preserve original reds and passing audit history; do not replay previously passed unchanged expensive cases solely to reconstruct proof. No acceptance waiver, no hook guard bypass, no LIVE_GATE_OPS.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-008 — Keep operation-fallback overlap read-only until P-003 native custody clears\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAffects: nonp2p-bug-drain-2026-08-08\nRuling: keep EI-25836573308210587 read-only and leave its operation-enabled source/test unchanged until P-003's native hook activation hold clears. D-003 remains the governing authority: operation/domain and any prepared authority must be preserved, with no arbitrary legacy fallback. Measured: EI-25836573308210587 checkpoint check operation-rejection-no-downgrade reports the focused test passed 1/1 (61 skipped) at staging HEAD 07a9ea0bcc, asserting one native request, denial, no lock token, and retained operation record. WI-6554700010009523 remains unassigned with next action to preserve its inactive loop until containing-source and native custody evidence arrives. This ruling assigns no shared-file edit to the overlap lane now; the existing passing guard is the current implementation boundary.\nRelated: P-003\n\n### D-009 — P-003 acceptance cannot use canonical legacy fallback\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\nMeasured: current apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/pretooluse-locks-acquire.sh:2088-2117 retains the operation record and denies a hook_operation rejection both before and after authority preparation; it does not retry this operation as a legacy acquire. Lines2121-2130 also deny an operation-scoped compatibility rejection without settlement. The older fallback evidence supplied by coord message at15:37Z is historical and does not establish that the source defect persists. This corrects the initial D-009 factual wording.\nRuling (unchanged from D-003): a hypothetical legacy fallback is insufficient P-003 acceptance. D-003 requires preserved operation/domain and prepared authority pin, native-origin qualification against maintained acquire/release/cancel_wait schemas, and measured positive native terminal completion. Ordinary non-operation legacy compatibility remains governed by D-002. Current source denial alone does not prove native end-to-end acceptance; that remains P-003's existing obligation. No new requirement, scope, dependency or proof waiver is introduced.\nRelated: P-002, P-003\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-14, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing. Next repair: Bind evidence at the current spec revision on the declared evidence plane. (R-4). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nP-001 and P-002 are done. P-003 (WI-6554700010009523) is open, unassigned and durably claim-held pending actual current native Pre/Post hook activation under EI-25920487778813638, owned by live fleet leader su-51c5f29f-f7cc-4c96-aa72-0be374f2f5f6. The source fix/current staging writer and installed script equality have saved qualified prerequisite evidence, but actual loaded-hook/dispatch and correlated native terminal/path proof remain unverified. Spec-quality evaluation and activation dry-run passed at plan revision 22. WI-6554700010010405 is done. Acceptance rubric rev 3 remains current/vetted; no BAR, evidence, or independent acceptance waiver was applied.\n\n**Next:** The existing native-activation owner must provide qualified client hook load/dispatch/custody evidence and satisfy work-item:done:EI-25920487778813638; then the assigned validator re-reads the hold, clears it through supported tools, claims P-003, runs only new/failed native terminal cases and binds current evidence before independent acceptance and shipment.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009521 — Audit existing waiter/authority primitives; record exact operation-correlated acquire, cancellation and native-completion contract. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009522 — Implement the smallest maintained hook/store/authority extension with canonical race and isolation tests. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010009523 — Run only new or failed focused cases; verify correlated terminal outcomes and record scoped source/runtime evidence. <!-- P-003 -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"capability-shell-dispatch-task-correlation-2026-10-13","title":"Recover shell task identity after orchestration response loss","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Recover shell task identity after orchestration response loss\nslug: capability-shell-dispatch-task-correlation-2026-10-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-13\nupdated: 2026-10-16\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: agents recovering an interrupted shell launch. Problem: code:run detachedCalls carries a dispatch call ID, but capability:bash enrollment drops it, so recovery relies on command/time heuristics. Outcome: exact bounded task lookup through existing surfaces. Non-goals: changing timeouts, cancellation, authority, deployment, native cutover, or claiming the historic timeout cause. Source scope: WI-6554700010008664 owner-authorized SELF/AUTO full-session takeover; repair derived from owned EI-25881913089307268 source investigation.\nScenario: an uncertain capability:bash launch is looked up by detachedCalls.callId after its response is lost. Customers need workspace diagnostics and usage visibility without giving Papercusp access to private agent work or their provider billing account.\n\nProblem: cloud browser analytics is currently skipped; health, usage and lifecycle evidence exists but has no coherent cloud monitoring contract. The initial recommendation mixed centrally observable signals with customer-private BYOC data.\n\nOutcome: a working, privacy-scoped monitoring system with useful activation/reliability/cost views, actionable alarms, explicit export choices and verified deployed evidence.\n\nNon-goals: migrating PostHog to a new vendor/account; collecting provider-wide customer usage or invoices; exporting prompts, source, files, terminals or desktop content; session replay; broad browser autocapture; introducing a second host probe, usage ledger or incident supervisor.\n\nSource turns:\n- [owner:directive-1806] session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:1 — cloud monitoring/tracking and reuse of existing PostHog.\n- [owner:directive-1807] session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:8 — BYOC token/account usage is private; central collection must respect that boundary.\n- [owner:directive-1808] session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:12 — capture the agreed scope as a plan, enable AUTO and carry it to shipped.\n- [owner:directive-1809] session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:13 — resume the same route and work.\n- Approved context: superseding recommendation report rpt_83fc254c-80a9-4eb6-a1b6-fba243deb91b replaces rpt_15d41057-ed84-47ac-b67a-a73dc4eaabd2.\n\nScenarios:\n1. A consenting customer signs in and creates a workspace. PostHog receives fixed portal milestones and confirmed provisioning outcomes, with opaque identity and environment/release/provider metadata.\n2. A BYOC customer runs an agent using their own model account. Their local dashboard shows the runtime's per-call tokens and labeled cost estimates. Central analytics receives no token totals, task results or account data by default.\n3. A customer explicitly enables a narrowly defined diagnostic export. Only the stated aggregate metadata leaves the customer runtime; revoking the choice stops subsequent export. Prompts/code/terminal content remain excluded.\n4. A provisioning operation fails or our relay loses connectivity. The existing control-plane evidence identifies the failure and recovery; an internal alarm names an accountable responder.\n5. PostHog is unavailable or telemetry is disabled. Sign-in, provisioning and agent work continue; diagnostics distinguish unavailable from zero and do not replay private historical data on later consent.\n\nOwner walkthrough: ship portal analytics and service monitoring first, preserve customer-local diagnostics, prove opt-out and tenant separation, then verify the exact deployed build and plan acceptance. AUTO was explicitly authorized; route is this session implementing directly. No fleet/subagent route is chosen.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-13, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty. Next repair: Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nPlanning and implementation in the canonical staging tree. A 60-second warm work loop is armed for this owner-directed objective. Customer diagnostic export is deliberately opt-in because it sends customer data off their host; routine operational monitoring stays active. No new default-OFF product feature flag is proposed.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012154 — Implement the shared cloud monitoring policy and strict event/export schemas; preserve customer-local BYOC usage/content, verified-principal scope, environment separation and revocation. Add positive… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012155 — Implement consented explicit hosted portal analytics and confirmed provisioning/tutorial outcomes through the existing PostHog delivery/configuration seam, with opaque identity, deduplication and non… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012156 — Extend existing control-plane health/lifecycle/API/public-ingress evidence into operator reliability views and actionable registered alarms; validate exact error/latency/connection recovery signals, … <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012157 — Complete customer-local workspace/agent/token/cost diagnostics using existing ledger/views, separate Papercusp-owned billing, and add a clearly disclosed opt-in aggregate-export control with destinat… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012158 — Run focused suites/typecheck and current-build hosted journeys covering consenting/opted-out users, tenant boundaries, managed/BYOC hosting, hostile payloads, analytics outages, local diagnostics, ex… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010012159 — Drive final acceptance and promotion through the supported audited plan/rubric/grade and release mechanisms; verify exact deployed artifact, stop the work loop and close owner directives only when sh… <!-- P-006 -->\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Privacy boundary.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Central monitoring contains only portal/control-plane observations and Papercusp-owned costs. BYOC tokens, model costs, internal tasks/logs, customer infrastructure/billing and all workspace content stay customer-side by default. Fixed allowlists and tenant authorization enforce this at the writer/export boundary.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:12\",\"session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:8\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Central monitoring contains only portal/control-plane observations and Papercusp-owned costs. BYOC tokens, model costs, internal tasks/logs, customer infrastructure/billing and all workspace content stay customer-side by default. Fixed allowlists and tenant authorization enforce this at the writer/export boundary.\",\"falsifier\":\"A customer-private BYOC measurement/content or cross-tenant identity reaches central analytics without the specific current customer export authorization.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the registered focused suites (packages/operator-ui/src/browser-telemetry.test.tsx, packages/operator-core/lib/telemetry-kinds.test.ts, packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-relay-confidentiality-registry.test.ts), then exercise this behavior on the current-build runtime and bind newly added scenario-level tests/evidence to the plan specs before completion.\\n\\nRegistered tenant-authorization detectors: record-telemetry.test.ts asserts rejection of a non-administrator despite prior diagnostics consent, rejects spoofed organization identity and hostile payloads beside a working positive sender control, and checks opaque identity separation across tenants/environments. record-telemetry.integration.test.ts exercises persisted tenant-scoped consent and hostile/default/revoked exports. Preserve every original privacy outcome and tree/integration evidence floor. Discriminator vs R-5: R-1 judges the BYOC/tenant boundary, that no customer data (provider-call measurements are customer data, cloud-monitoring-byoc-privacy-2026-10-13#D-002) reaches a central writer; free-form content in error/audit export is judged by R-5.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-ui/src/browser-telemetry.test.tsx\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/telemetry-kinds.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-relay-confidentiality-registry.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-byoc-vendor-outage.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/record-telemetry.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/record-telemetry.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Cloud product analytics.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Reuse PostHog for disclosed, consented hosted portal events: sign-in/setup/tutorial progression, workspace creation/provision readiness, retention and feature adoption that the portal actually observes. Successful provisioning is a confirmed server outcome, not a click. Events have bounded metadata and opaque user/organization identity, environment and release separation, idempotence, and no broad browser SDK capture/replay.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:12\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each consented hosted-portal outcome is recorded in PostHog exactly once as an opaque-identity event.\",\"falsifier\":\"An unconsented portal event is exported, an intent click is counted as confirmed provisioning, duplicate retries inflate outcomes, or a telemetry outage blocks product work. A consented outcome is missing from PostHog; provisioning is counted on anything other than the server-confirmed ready outcome; a session-replay or autocapture call is made; or an event lacks environment/release tags, carries non-allowlisted or unbounded metadata, or carries a non-opaque identity.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the registered focused suites (packages/operator-ui/src/browser-telemetry.test.tsx, apps/operator/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-analytics.integration.test.ts, packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-profile.test.ts), then exercise this behavior on the current-build runtime and bind newly added scenario-level tests/evidence to the plan specs before completion.\\n\\nLive pass floor: retain the configured PostHog project query-API response (event UUID, timestamp, stable opaque person/organization ids, closed property set and server environment/release) for a consented portal event and server-confirmed provisioning-ready outcome. In the same window retain observed positive ingestion beside opted-out/revoked/no-autocapture/replay absence queries. Retain the activation dashboard and query, excluding disclosed synthetic markers. A green tree suite alone rates unknown. Read access or a retained complete receipt must allow an independent grader to replay. Release-operator receipts: one PostHog query receipt for a consented portal event and one for a server-confirmed provisioning outcome, each showing opaque identity and environment/release tags. Reusing PostHog is method guidance (cloud-monitoring-byoc-privacy-2026-10-13#D-003); a missing receipt is unknown (cloud-monitoring-byoc-privacy-2026-10-13#D-004).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-ui/src/browser-telemetry.test.tsx\",\"apps/operator/lib/onboarding/cloud-tutorial-analytics.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-profile.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/record-telemetry.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/record-telemetry.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/telemetry-flush.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Operational reliability.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Extend existing lifecycle, health, public-ingress and API instrumentation for provisioning success/duration, API latency/errors, connector loss/recovery, service/database/queue health, and Papercusp-managed capacity. Metrics, structured logs/correlation and actionable alarms are available independently of PostHog. Customer-local stalled tasks/provider errors remain in the customer plane. No competing probe/monitor is introduced.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:12\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each named control-plane failure (provisioning, API, connector, service/db/queue, managed capacity) produces a metric, a correlated structured log and one accountable alarm that resolves on measured recovery, with no PostHog dependency and no new host probe.\",\"falsifier\":\"A witnessed service failure/recovery is absent, mislabeled, lacks an accountable alarm, or a competing host probe is introduced. Provisioning duration, API latency/error or connector loss has no metric or correlated log; a customer-local stalled task or provider error appears centrally; or an alarm or metric depends on PostHog availability.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the registered focused suites (packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/standing-health.test.ts, packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-workspace-session.test.ts, packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/hosted-public-ingress-probe-action.test.ts), then exercise this behavior on the current-build runtime and bind newly added scenario-level tests/evidence to the plan specs before completion.\\n\\nLive pass floor: retain a current-build witnessed failure/recovery pair, accountable existing watch alarm delivery and resolution, latency/error sample and populated reliability/Papercusp-owned cost views with their queries. Verify an owned-spend threshold alarm using a private fixture independently of PostHog; never infer customer bills. Code-read the reuse map to verify no competing host probe. A green tree suite alone rates unknown.\\n\\nRegistered alarm detectors: the existing liveness-alarm.test.ts and thresholds.test.ts cover deduplication, unknown/failure/recovery and Papercusp-owned spend thresholds; liveness-alarm-current-build.e2e.test.ts witnesses the existing hosted control-plane alarm router in a private current-build runtime. Retain its actual emitted alarm, recipient, deduplication and exact resolution receipt. The original live view, connector and spend observations remain mandatory. Release-operator receipts: a witnessed failure/recovery pair with its metric and correlated log, plus the alarm delivery and its resolution on measured recovery. Extending existing instrumentation is method guidance; a missing observation is unknown (cloud-monitoring-byoc-privacy-2026-10-13#D-004).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/standing-health.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-workspace-session.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/hosted-public-ingress-probe-action.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/liveness-alarm.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/thresholds.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/liveness-alarm-current-build.e2e.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Cost and customer diagnostics.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Reuse the runtime usage ledger and existing workspace diagnostics for per-call token counts, provider-reported versus estimated/unknown cost, task/agent failures and customer-local resource health. Keep Papercusp charges separate from customer model/cloud bills. Provide useful local views and an explicit, narrowly scoped, default-disabled aggregate export choice; account-wide bills require separately granted access and are not inferred.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:12\",\"session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:8\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Customer per-call usage is viewable locally without leaving the customer's host.\",\"falsifier\":\"Local per-call usage is inaccessible, unknown/estimated cost is labeled as actual, provider-wide usage is inferred, or customer usage leaves their host by default or after revocation. Papercusp charges are mixed into or presented as customer model/cloud bills; aggregate export is enabled without an explicit customer choice, is broader than its narrow declared scope, or is on by default; or customer-local task/agent failures and resource health are not viewable on the customer's host.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the registered focused suites (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-usage-telemetry.test.ts, packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-byoc-vendor-outage.integration.test.ts), then exercise this behavior on the current-build runtime and bind newly added scenario-level tests/evidence to the plan specs before completion.\\n\\nLive pass floor: retain a current-build BYOC local usage/diagnostic view with the recorded sample, real configured sink positive control and zero unauthorized customer-usage observation in that same window. Missing observations are unknown (cloud-monitoring-byoc-privacy-2026-10-13#D-004).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-usage-telemetry.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-byoc-vendor-outage.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/record-telemetry.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Security, error capture and governance.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Reuse restricted audit records for login/access/membership/credentials/workspace lifecycle and billing changes. Evaluate existing PostHog error capability before adding another vendor; any central error event contains a safe code/fingerprint and reviewed fields. Document exact collected/exported fields, destination, purpose, retention and revocation. Analytics failure never blocks product work; sensitive content is excluded even under hostile input.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a136f2-8f5d-7a62-ae60-7bc2c6d518b6:12\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every centrally exported audit or error record contains only reviewed safe fields.\",\"falsifier\":\"Sensitive free-form content reaches analytics/error export, an audit or error record is read or exported without human or tenant authorization, the published disclosure omits an exported field, its destination, purpose, retention or revocation effect, or analytics failure blocks service. Retain the canonical document reader receipt as a separate delivery observation. These additions preserve the original privacy, error, outage and disclosure obligations. Discriminator vs R-1: R-5 judges free-form content and safe fields in central error/audit export and its published disclosure; the BYOC/tenant data boundary is judged by R-1. Evaluating existing PostHog error capability is method guidance (cloud-monitoring-byoc-privacy-2026-10-13#D-003), not a bar.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/record-telemetry.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/record-telemetry.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-ui/src/browser-telemetry.test.tsx\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/siem-export-delivery.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/data-governance/siem-export-delivery.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/doc-claims/cloud-monitoring-disclosure.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Verified shipment.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The real project suite includes privacy/tenant/consent/failure and lifecycle tests. The six operator-core surfaces must be contained by the loaded release-operator runtime; the browser and disclosure sources must be contained by the exact deployed artifact. The writer gates each containment value on a matching accepted-source fingerprint, and unknown cannot pass. Design\n\nReuse:\n- packages/operator-ui/src/browser-telemetry.tsx and cloud tutorial analytics for explicit client events; do not enable cloud autocapture.\n- record-telemetry, telemetry-flush and posthog-config for existing optional delivery, consent and retention mechanisms; extend with a distinctly scoped cloud policy instead of spreading arbitrary payloads.\n- workspace-host/observability-store, standing-health and hosted-workspace-session audit producers for lifecycle/reliability facts.\n- agent-usage-telemetry for customer-local per-call tokens and labeled costs.\n- existing hosted authentication/profile and scoped settings stores for identity, authorization and consent.\n- existing diagnostics/operator views and PostHog dashboards rather than a new app or durable parallel metrics ledger.\n\nArchitecture: keep the portal/control plane and customer runtime as separate evidence planes. The central ingest accepts a closed event schema, derives identity from the verified principal, and rejects extra/free-form fields. The customer runtime retains local data; optional export constructs an explicit aggregate from local records after checking current consent, with no maintainer-build bypass for BYOC. Local usage and operational audit rows are never interpreted as analytics consent.\n\nDelivery choice: use the existing PostHog instance/configuration and verify its actual ingestion/product support. Managed PostHog migration is not required to ship this scope. Native Error Tracking is optional only if safely supported; the required central error/reliability signals work without a new vendor.\n\nMechanisms: alert subscriptions use watch:create; repeatable health/latency checks bind registered instruments to rubric criteria/results and use scorecards:emit fromLedger, with plans:set-schedule then plans:arm-schedule for recurrence if the existing registered producer does not already supply it. Extend existing public-ingress probing and use an independent controlled vantage for final uptime acceptance. No hand-rolled keep-alive or duplicate monitor.\n\nVerification layers: focused unit/integration tests; staging/current-build operator-api and background-federation routes selected by dev:pipeline_position; hosted journey evidence; then exact artifact promotion/deploy and plan acceptance. LIVE_GATE_OPS ownership is read before any current-gate action; an existing live fixer is the sole driver while this development continues.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-005 | live |\n| R-3 | P-003, P-005 | live |\n| R-4 | P-004, P-005 | live |\n| R-5 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-005, P-006 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Boundaries and implementation\n\n- **P-001** `done` Implement the shared cloud monitoring policy and strict event/export schemas; preserve customer-local BYOC usage/content, verified-principal scope, environment separation and revocation. Add positive/negative privacy and tenant tests. importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010012154 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Implement consented explicit hosted portal analytics and confirmed provisioning/tutorial outcomes through the existing PostHog delivery/configuration seam, with opaque identity, deduplication and non-blocking outage behavior. Add browser/route integration tests and verify ingestion. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010012155 completed (done)\n- **P-003** `done` Extend existing control-plane health/lifecycle/API/public-ingress evidence into operator reliability views and actionable registered alarms; validate exact error/latency/connection recovery signals, audit scope and safe error capture. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010012156 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Complete customer-local workspace/agent/token/cost diagnostics using existing ledger/views, separate Papercusp-owned billing, and add a clearly disclosed opt-in aggregate-export control with destination/retention/revocation. Prove zero central BYOC private usage export by default. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010012157 completed (done)\n- **P-007** `done` Wire the missing portal analytics producers found by blind gap review #41 (G-1..G-3). G-1: the running portal (portal/packages/ui OperatorHostProvider) sends cloud_portal_session action=returned once per page load in the hosted location; today only the operator-vite root mounts that producer. G-2: cloud_feature_adoption is sent for workspace_list (Workspaces surface), connection_setup (connect drawer / BYOC grant form), billing (signed-in Billing panel) and cloud_tutorial (tutorial start), alongside the existing monitoring producer. G-3: cloud_error render_failure is sent when a hosted portal surface crashes, with a fingerprint computed from one shared code/type input so browser and server fingerprints agree. Same consent route (/api/hosted/browser/monitoring/event), no new event kinds, no new properties. Tests in operator-ui, apps/operator and the portal suites. importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010018517 completed (done)\n\n\n## Phase 2 — Acceptance and shipment\n\n- **P-005** `done` Run focused suites/typecheck and current-build hosted journeys covering consenting/opted-out users, tenant boundaries, managed/BYOC hosting, hostile payloads, analytics outages, local diagnostics, export revocation and alarm recovery; publish complete operator/customer collection documentation and actual dashboard evidence. blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010012158 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `blocked` Drive final acceptance and promotion through the supported audited plan/rubric/grade and release mechanisms; verify exact deployed artifact, stop the work loop and close owner directives only when shipment is evidenced. importance: high blocked-by: P-005, P-007 — note: ← WI-6554700010012159 blocked (2 external blockers)\n\n## Decisions\n\n- **D-001 — Execution route and authorization.** Owner directive #1808 enables AUTO and requests shipment; #1809 resumes it. Implement directly in this session, with durable plan/work-item claims and manual file locks. No client-native delegation.\n- **D-002 — BYOC privacy governs the earlier broad proposal.** The correction at source turn 8 and approved context at turn 11 limits central telemetry. Provider-call measurements are customer data even when they are numeric.\n- **D-003 — Reuse existing PostHog, verify support.** Do not make a vendor migration or unsupported error-tracking feature a prerequisite; no customer data export to a new destination is implied.\n- **D-004 — Honest acceptance.** First-success/task metrics are central only when the control plane is their legitimate witness or the customer explicitly authorizes the specific diagnostic export. Missing observations remain unknown, not success or zero.\n\n### D-001 — Execution route and authorization\nDate: 2026-10-13\n[owner:directive-1808] AUTO implementation through shipment was requested; [owner:directive-1809] resumes that work. Implement directly in this session under work-item claims and manual file locks. No client-native delegation.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-002 — BYOC privacy governs the earlier broad proposal\nDate: 2026-10-13\nThe owner's source turn 8 corrects the initial broad central monitoring proposal. Customer tokens, model costs, internal tasks, host metrics/bills and all workspace content stay local by default; explicit customer export consent is separate from local collection. Central observations are portal/control-plane facts.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-004, P-005\n\n### D-003 — Reuse existing PostHog and verify support\nDate: 2026-10-13\nUse the existing configured PostHog delivery surface and verify actual ingestion/product support. Do not add a vendor migration or unsupported Error Tracking product as a prerequisite. A new telemetry destination is not implicitly authorized by enabling diagnostics.\nRelated: P-002, P-003, P-005\n\n### D-004 — Honest outcome and billing evidence\nDate: 2026-10-13\nA click is an attempt, not successful provisioning. Customer first-task success is central only when the control plane is its legitimate witness or the customer explicitly exports that metric. Tokens measure only calls this runtime observes, not provider-account usage/invoices. Next repair: Vet the current acceptance-rubric criteria BEFORE binding proof or emitting adequacy cards (amend → vet → attest → bind → cards → grade): a vetting critique usually becomes an amendment, and proof bound first must then be re-bound.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nPlan STARTED 2026-10-13 ~23:14Z (status ready, 25 work-items promoted, unadmitted to fleets, consistent with route A). Activation audit seq 1 recorded on plan rev 6; acceptance rubric acceptance-cloud-portal-public-release-2026-10-13 rev1 seeded; 25 SPEC-P-NNN clauses (22 active, 3 exempt) pass spec quality, with grading-integrity passed by su-59a2acd4. su-99dec684 holds P-001 (WI-6554700010011214) and P-003 (WI-6554700010011216). Key P-001 finding: the hosted control plane on :3880 (app.papercusp.com API paths) uses DATABASE_URL localhost:5432/papercusp, the SAME database as the dev operator, and shares the dev dbos schema. Detail: WI-6554700010011127 comment post 1179648.\n\n**Next:** P-001: trace the portal store (embedded PG?) and journald/pg_dump PII exposure, capture a live write delta across one signup journey, classify fields, and write the agent-insights data-map doc plus the system-of-record table. P-003: price Cloud SQL HA + PITR vs alternatives (region, compute GCE vs Cloud Run with DBOS/long-running constraints), reusing libs/generic/deployment-driver, then bring the cost comparison to Avi (spend is owner-gated, Q1). Q2 (existing 253 users / 147 orgs) waits on P-002.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** (1) Members of the public who sign up at `app.papercusp.com`. (2) Avi, the operator accountable for their data and payments. (3) The agents that maintain the hosted stack.\n\n**Problem (measured 2026-10-13, this session plus report `rpt_4c61e9f2-72df-47dc-99dc-77429296da6d`).**\n- `app.papercusp.com` → Cloudflare tunnel `1814c48a…` (cloudflared on the dev box) → `localhost:3880` `papercusp-hosted-control-plane.service`. That unit is launched from the shared **staging working tree** (`papercusp/apps/operator`, `PAPERCUSP_BUNDLE_ALLOW_STALE_START=1`), not from a green release. A dev-box reboot, crash or broken in-flight edit therefore reaches customers directly.\n- Customer records are in the `papercusp_auth` schema: 27 tables, about 7.6 MB. They include 253 users and 147 organizations, plus 12 subscriptions, all `canceled` in Stripe test mode. The schema also holds memberships, legal acceptances, sessions, WorkOS sealed sessions, Stripe customer mappings, webhook receipts, entitlements, and usage and budget receipts. These records, plus `harness_shared.customer_workspaces` (19 rows), `harness_shared.cloud_resource_obligations` and the DBOS provisioning state, live inside the 142 GB dev `papercusp` database at `localhost:5432`. Roughly 400 agent sessions share that database.\n- The portal's own application state (preferences, app registry, chat and proposal records) lives in an embedded Postgres under `~/.papercusp-portal/postgres` on a dynamically chosen loopback port.\n- Stripe is in TEST mode (`livemode:false`). Checkout does not start a trial, and trial start and end dates are not persisted.\n- Backups: an hourly kopia db-dump timer runs on this same box. Critical item WI-10000694 records a past period when backups went stale. Restoring the customer data on its own has never been drilled.\n\n**Outcome.** A customer can sign up, start a 14-day trial, create a workspace, and then upgrade, change or cancel. They can also export or delete their data. None of this depends on the dev box being up, and none of it shares a database with agent workloads.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- Moving the 142 GB agent/harness database (transcripts, tool invocations, plans). That state stays on the dev box.\n- Moving customer workspace VMs. They already run in Papercusp's GCP project or the customer's own cloud.\n- Rebuilding what Stripe or WorkOS already provide: card storage, invoices, the payment-method UI, password, MFA and SSO.\n- The marketing site `papercusp.com`, which is deployed separately.\n- Azure/AWS parity and BYOC expansion, which belong to `byoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01` and `aws-byoc-gcp-parity-2026-10-01`.\n\n**Source turns (owner).** `session_turn:codex:01a136f6-13da-7c80-a7c8-22f1821e4c47:1` (14-day trial, where data is stored), `…:10` (subscription page, build vs Stripe, analytics with su-96eda), `…:11` and `…:13` (we need our own server DB; data must not live on this machine), and owner directive #1811 (this plan).\n\n**Scenarios.**\n- **S1.** Dana signs up from her laptop, verifies her email through WorkOS, accepts the terms, starts a 14-day trial and provisions one workspace. The dev box is powered off the whole time.\n- **S2.** On day 12, `/billing` shows Dana \"2 days left\" and her allowance used. She upgrades through Stripe Checkout, the confirmed webhook turns on paid entitlement, and her workspace keeps all its data.\n- **S3.** A teammate opens **Manage billing** (the Stripe customer portal) to change plan, update a card, download an invoice or cancel. Our `/billing` page reflects the change within a minute.\n- **S4.** A trial expires unpaid. Billable compute stops, and the data is kept for the retention window with an export link. It is then deleted on schedule with a deletion receipt.\n- **S5.** Dana deletes her organization. Our rows are removed or anonymized, her WorkOS user is removed, her Stripe customer is handled per retention rules (invoices kept only where law requires), and her workspace is torn down. An audit record proves each step.\n- **S6.** Someone drops a production table. The database is restored to a point in time within the agreed RPO and RTO, a procedure rehearsed before launch.\n- **S7.** An agent breaks the staging tree. `app.papercusp.com` is unaffected because production runs a pinned release.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Dev-box independence.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Public customer journeys must not depend on the dev 2026-10-13. The per-table and per-column authority is `packages/operator-core/lib/auth/hosted/customer-data-map.ts`, which `customer-data-map.integration.test.ts` keeps in step with the schema. [agent-insights/hosted-customer-data-map](/internal/docs/agent-insights/hosted-customer-data-map) explains it. Table names below are `papercusp_auth.*` unless marked; the value in brackets is the module's `systemOfRecord`.\n\n| Data | System of record | Tables today | Papercusp production DB keeps |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Credentials, email verification, MFA/SSO | WorkOS | `external_identities`, `workos_sealed_sessions`, `workos_lifecycle_entity_cursors`, `webhook_event_receipts` [workos-mirror] | user-id link, verified email, display name, sealed session, webhook ledger |\n| Users, organizations, memberships, roles, org audit events, directory-sync role mappings | **Papercusp DB** | `hosted_users`, `organizations`, `organization_memberships`, `organization_audit_events`, `directory_group_role_mappings`, `directory_user_observations` [papercusp] | everything |\n| Invitations | WorkOS (invitation lifecycle); **Papercusp DB** (intended role) | `organization_invitation_refs` [workos-mirror] | invitee email, intended role, status |\n| Terms and privacy acceptances (version and time) | **Papercusp DB** | `legal_acceptances` [papercusp] | everything, because we must be able to prove consent |\n| Sessions, CLI and MCP OAuth grants, workspace connectors, support access | **Papercusp DB** | `hosted_sessions`, `hosted_cli_device_grants`, `hosted_cli_tokens`, `hosted_mcp_oauth_clients`, `hosted_mcp_oauth_requests`, `hosted_workspace_connectors`, `hosted_workspace_connector_tickets`, `support_access_grants` [papercusp] | everything; secrets stored hashed or sealed |\n| Workspace ownership, provisioning state, cloud resource obligations | **Papercusp DB** | `harness_shared.customer_workspaces`, `harness_shared.cloud_resource_obligations` [papercusp] | everything |\n| Cards, payment methods, invoices, receipts, tax | Stripe | `hosted_billing_customers` [stripe-mirror] | Stripe ids only |\n| Subscription, price, renewal and cancellation | Stripe (source of truth) | `hosted_subscriptions`, `hosted_billing_webhook_events` [stripe-mirror] | a webhook-synced mirror for fast entitlement checks. As built: status, price, plan, `current_period_end`, `cancel_at_period_end`, `canceled_at`. `trial_start`, `trial_end` and `cancel_at` are not stored yet. |\n| Trial eligibility and history (abuse prevention) | **Papercusp DB** | `hosted_signup_attempts` [papercusp] holds signup idempotency and per-email rate limits; no trial-history table exists yet | per organization and per verified identity |\n| Entitlements, allowances, usage and budget ledger | **Papercusp DB** | `hosted_entitlements`, `hosted_prepaid_allocations`, `hosted_usage_receipts`, `hosted_budget_receipts`, `hosted_budget_allocations`, `hosted_budget_allocation_holds`, `hosted_outcome_cost_records`, `hosted_app_relay_usage`, `tutorial_voice_reservations` [papercusp] | everything (Stripe metered billing optional later) |\n| Product analytics | PostHog (su-96eda's lane) | none | nothing; pseudonymous ids only |\n| Workspace files and runtime database | Workspace host (GCP or customer cloud) | none | pointers only |\n| Per-user portal preferences | **Papercusp DB** | `hosted_user_preferences` [papercusp] | everything |\n| Portal app registry, chat and proposal records | **Papercusp DB** (target) | measured 2026-10-13: the portal's own embedded Postgres at `~/.papercusp-portal/postgres`, outside the map; where it goes in production is P-006's decision | everything |\n| Legacy pre-hosted users, sessions and magic links | none (empty) | `users`, `sessions`, `magic_link_requests` [papercusp, legacy-empty] | nothing; drop candidates |\n\nWhy we keep our own database rather than relying on Stripe and WorkOS for everything:\n- Every request needs an authorization answer (which organization, which workspace, which role), and it must come from our database.\n- We must own consent records and the audit trail.\n- A Stripe or WorkOS outage must not lock customers out of workspaces they have already paid for.\n\n### Target architecture (proposal; provider is decided in P-003)\n- **Managed PostgreSQL.** Recommended: GCP Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL in the existing hosted GCP organization, which already runs customer workspaces. Configuration: HA, private IP, TLS only, automated backups with 7–14 days of PITR, deletion protection and encryption at rest. Two databases, `papercusp_hosted` and `portal`, with least-privilege roles: migrator, hosted RLS role, service role and read-only ops role. No default credentials.\n- **Production compute.** Run the hosted control plane and portal on production hosts in the same VPC (a small GCE managed instance group under systemd is the default candidate, with Cloud Run as an alternative if DBOS workers allow). Ingress is a Cloudflare tunnel or load balancer terminating on the production hosts.\n- **Secrets.** GCP Secret Manager, behind the existing `*_REF` secret-reference resolver. No new secret mechanism.\n- **Releases.** Production deploys only green-`main` release artifacts, reusing `release:deploy`/`deploy-cli` and the portal standalone reconcile, and supports rollback. The dev box keeps a **staging** hosted instance (e.g. `app-staging.papercusp.com`) on its own staging database, for Stripe test-mode and agent verification.\n- **Schema.** The same migration runner and files are used. Whether the hosted database receives the full migration set or a hosted subset is settled in P-001/P-005. No runtime DDL.\n\n### Reuse (no parallel systems)\n- `byoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01#P-001` (\"Deploy and operate the hosted control plane at app.papercusp.com\") is **delivered by** P-004–P-008 and P-024 of this plan. That item is linked, not duplicated.\n- `byoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01#P-002` (hosted security acceptance gate) and `#P-007` (external pentest and legal/privacy sign-off) are consumed by P-013/P-021.\n- `byoc-deferred-cut-carrier-2026-09-01#P-008` and `papercusp-monetization-2026-09-04#P-012` (self-service billing) overlap P-014–P-017; see open question Q4.\n- `cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03` (shipped) provides the existing checkout, webhooks, `/billing` and Manage billing. This plan extends it.\n- The existing billing seams are extended, not forked: `stripe-billing-client.ts`, `stripe-billing-events.ts`, `entitlement-seam.ts`, `budget-policy.ts` and `usage-service.ts` under `packages/operator-core/lib/auth/hosted/billing/`.\n- Analytics: the shared PostHog layer su-96eda is expanding.\n- WI-10000694 (backup staleness) feeds P-009.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-025 | live |\n| R-2 | P-005 | live |\n| R-3 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-009 | live |\n| R-5 | P-007 | live |\n| R-6 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-015 | live |\n| R-12 | P-018 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-012 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-017 | live |\n| R-15 | P-024 | live |\n\n## Open questions (owner)\n\n- **Q1 — Hosting provider.** Recommended: GCP Cloud SQL plus GCE in the existing hosted GCP organization. One instance holds two databases: the customer database and a dedicated DBOS system database. The dev box's test accounts stay on the dev and staging databases.\n\nRejected: carrying only the 2 gmail accounts forward (the plan's original Q2 default, which assumed real external customers existed), and carrying the gmail accounts plus the active papercusp.com accounts.\n\n### D-007 — Production runs in a dedicated GCP project, papercusp-cloud-prod, not in papercusp-hosted-workspaces\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAffects: P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-023\n\n[self-imposed, su-99dec684, P-004 design] The production Cloud SQL instance, its VPC, the production VM (P-007) and the production secrets (P-008) live in a new project, `papercusp-cloud-prod`. It sits under the same organization (118335394393) on the same billing account as the hosted workspaces. D-004 fixed the region (us-central1), the tier and private-IP networking. It did not fix the project.\n\nWhy: `papercusp-hosted-workspaces` runs customer workspace VMs, which execute customer code, and holds one isolated VPC per customer host. The customer database and the Stripe, WorkOS and session secrets should not share a project IAM boundary, quota pool or blast radius with those VMs. The organization already uses one project per purpose (`papercusp-org-identity`, canary projects), so this follows the existing pattern. It adds no cost. The hosted control plane gets a cross-project IAM grant to manage workspace VMs in `papercusp-hosted-workspaces` (P-007).\n\nVerified before deciding: super@papercusp.com already holds resourcemanager.projects.create on the organization and billing.resourceAssociations.create on billing account 0113AC-50E9A0-8BB71D (testIamPermissions, 2026-10-14), so no IAM change is needed. The decision is reversible: the project can be deleted, with a 30-day recovery window.\n\nRejected: provisioning inside `papercusp-hosted-workspaces`. That would be simpler by one project, but it shares IAM with customer-code VMs.\n\n### D-008 — Build a remote-resource identity check for live spec evidence (WI-6554700010011907) inside this plan\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAffects: P-004, P-005, P-023\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-14, interactive dialog answer 'Build the fix now (Recommended)']\nThe spec-evidence checker can only give an environment identity to LOCAL pid-pinned runtimes (measureRuntimeVintageEnvironment), so live proof against a Cloud SQL instance can never read as current. P-004 cannot close for that reason, even though its proof is complete (bindings 43286 live, 43319 test, 43320 mutation). The same gap would block every clause in this plan that checks a cloud resource. Avi chose to build the fix now, in this session, on route A (D-003). The change adds a remote-resource runtime unit whose identity is read through gcloud when evidence is bound and again when it is graded. Proof goes out of date after any settings change. A failed read is unknown, never a pass. Tracked as WI-6554700010011907.\n\n### D-009 — Production mode is the explicit env PAPERCUSP_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT=production; database resolution fails closed under it\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAffects: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-023\n[self-imposed, su-99dec684, P-005 design]\n\nThe repo had no production-deployment signal. NODE_ENV=production and PAPERCUSP_DISTRIBUTION_PROFILE=hosted-control-plane cannot serve: both are already set by the dev-box papercusp-hosted-control-plane.service, which attaches to the local dev database through the operator .env.local and derives its app-role URL with the default harness_app credentials. Keying fail-closed on either would take that unit down before cutover.\n\nRuling:\n- Production mode is PAPERCUSP_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT=production. Unset or 'development' keeps today's resolution chain. Any other non-empty value is an error, so a typo such as 'prod' cannot silently disable the policy.\n- Under production mode, libs/papercusp/libs/db/src/connection.ts resolves the admin URL only from process env HARNESS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL then DATABASE_URL, and the app URL only from HARNESS_DATABASE_URL. It never reads the operator .env.local, the embedded-pg discovery file or the native localhost fallback, and never re-keys the app role with default credentials. Each URL must be a postgres URL with a non-loopback host, no host= socket override, and a password that is present and not a documented default (harness_app_pwd, harness_admin_pwd, postgres). Violations throw ProductionDatabaseConfigError with redacted endpoints.\n- apps/operator/bin/serve.ts checks this at boot. In production it refuses embedded Postgres (PAPERCUSP_USE_EMBEDDED_PG must be 0) and runs the same assertion before anything else, so a misconfigured production boot exits non-zero (R-3).\n- The P-007 production unit sets PAPERCUSP_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT=production. The dev-box unit does not. P-006 and P-008 reuse the same signal for their own fail-closed checks rather than adding another.\n\n### D-010 — Production database roles: harness_admin runs migrations as a non-superuser with createrole_self_grant='set, inherit'; harness_app and harness_zero are pre-created\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAffects: P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-023\n\n[self-imposed, su-99dec684, P-005 design; measured, not owner-directed]\n\nWhy: every existing bootstrap creates harness_admin as SUPERUSER (build-reference-schema.ts, verify-baseline.ts, gym-db-init.ts, frame-bootstrap.ts). Cloud SQL has no superuser. Live catalog probe of pc-cloud-prod-pg, 2026-10-14 ~07:20Z, read-only, as postgres: PostgreSQL 18.6; postgres has rolsuper=false, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB, no BYPASSRLS; postgres is a cloudsqlsuperuser member WITHOUT admin option; createrole_self_grant=''; cloudsqlsuperuser holds pg_read_all_stats only through pg_monitor, WITHOUT admin option; every database (papercusp_hosted, portal, dbos_system) is owned by cloudsqlsuperuser.\n\nMeasured on a local PG18 cluster shaped like Cloud SQL (.papercusp/scratch/cpr/cloudsql-rehearsal/run.sh), running the full set as non-superuser harness_admin:\n- No bootstrap: 1253 of 1284 applied, 31 failed. Root causes: 179 (no CREATE on schema public); 733 (GRANT pg_read_all_stats needs ADMIN OPTION); 978 (\"must be able to SET ROLE hosted_owner\", because a PG16+ CREATEROLE creator gets no SET membership by default; 28 failures cascade from this one).\n- With the bootstrap below: 1283 of 1284 applied. The only failure left is 733.\n\nRuling (bootstrap, run as postgres through the P-004 ExecuteSql path before the first migration; code = scripts/cloud-prod/role-sql.ts productionRoleSql, called from provision-cloud-sql.ts up):\n1. harness_admin: LOGIN, CREATEROLE, NOCREATEDB, password in Secret Manager (cloudsql-harness-admin-password). It is the migration user and the D-009 admin URL (secret cloudsql-harness-admin-url). It is created by SQL as postgres, NOT by `gcloud sql users create`: an Admin-API user joins cloudsqlsuperuser, which owns every database on the instance, so it would void P-004's one-owner-per-database isolation. Set ALTER ROLE harness_admin SET createrole_self_grant = 'set, inherit', so the hosted_owner, hosted_app and hosted_service roles it creates in 978 give it SET and INHERIT membership, as superuser did on dev. 978's post-condition checks only the hosted_* roles' own attributes, never memberships, so this does not weaken FORCE RLS for hosted_app and hosted_service.\n2. REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE papercusp_hosted FROM PUBLIC; GRANT CONNECT, CREATE, TEMPORARY ON DATABASE papercusp_hosted and GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO harness_admin.\n3. harness_app: LOGIN, non-superuser, password in Secret Manager (cloudsql-harness-app-password), CONNECT and TEMPORARY on papercusp_hosted only. TEMPORARY because packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/get-next.ts creates temp tables at runtime and P-004 revoked PUBLIC's default TEMPORARY. It is the D-009 app URL (secret cloudsql-harness-app-url). Migration 997 gives it NOINHERIT membership in hosted_app.\n4. harness_zero: NOLOGIN. It exists only because the migrations name it in REVOKE statements.\n5. Allowlisted extensions (vector, pg_trgm, pg_stat_statements, pgcrypto, citext, btree_gist, uuid-ossp; HOSTED_DB_EXTENSIONS) are created by postgres. pg_textsearch stays absent; migration 1447 has an availability gate for that.\n6. Every role is upserted so a re-run converges: the ALTER branch never states NOSUPERUSER, NOREPLICATION or NOBYPASSRLS, and verify --logins checks those attributes instead.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-14 ~07:30Z, PG18 local cluster (alter-probe.sh): as a non-superuser CREATEROLE role, ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER / NOREPLICATION / NOBYPASSRLS each fail (\"Only roles with the SUPERUSER attribute may change the SUPERUSER attribute\", same for REPLICATION and BYPASSRLS); ALTER ROLE ... LOGIN NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE CONNECTION LIMIT PASSWORD and ALTER ROLE ... SET createrole_self_grant succeed. P-004's original ownerRoleSql restated all of them, so a second `up` would have failed; fixed in the same change.\nMeasured: 2026-10-14 ~07:40Z, scripts/cloud-prod/role-sql.integration.test.ts (test run 21239989, 5/0): least-privilege shape (harness_admin not a cloudsqlsuperuser member, databases owned by cloudsqlsuperuser, PUBLIC revoked), bootstrap run twice as a non-superuser postgres stand-in, then the full migration set as harness_admin: the only failure is 733.\n\nOpen: migration 733 cannot pass on Cloud SQL as written, and nothing can be pre-granted to fix it. The migration-immutability guard (WI-38352) refuses an in-place edit, and a follow-up migration cannot help, because a fresh install stops at 733. Owner question conv-mv7s6wyw-0000-3e3d77cb54b746e68409fd3c0c13f035, tracked on WI-6554700010011218. With this design harness_admin has no route to pg_read_all_stats on Cloud SQL at all.\n\nOpen [inferred, to verify in the P-005 RLS step]: on dev, harness_admin bypasses FORCE RLS as a superuser. In production it does not, so admin-URL code that reads hosted tables will see rows filtered by policy.\n\n### D-011 — Production hosted runtime uses a dedicated attached identity for secrets and GCP delegation\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[self-imposed, AUTO, su-2b9c0] P-007 must attach pc-hosted-control-plane@papercusp-cloud-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com to the production VM. Production readiness and SPEC-P008 live billing proof are NOT complete.\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n\n### D-012 — Deletion ERROR recovery preserves the operation and records an explicit DBOS recovery lineage\nDate: 2026-10-15\nSelf-imposed implementation decision under the existing SELF/AUTO route. Measured: node_modules/@dbos-inc/dbos-sdk/dist/src/system_database.js resumeWorkflows excludes ERROR; bulkForkWorkflows preserves the source, writes forked_from, copies checkpoints before startStep and supports an explicit version/queue. P-010 client currently refuses ERROR, so bounded provider retries strand the operation. Extend the existing pinned DBOS client with the SDK's forkWorkflow at the first failed journal step. The immutable customer operation/input and original failed workflow remain intact. Serialize support recovery on the organization+operation lock; commit staff/grant/attempt audit before DBOS, record original and recovery workflow IDs in the result audit. This is an explicit recovery attempt, never a replacement operation, purge, raw status rewrite or false claim that SDK resume handles ERROR.
