Owner-authorized 2026-10-15 follow-up WI-6554700010014178 freshly verifies 5 unit files/385 tests (ledger21250262-21250266) and real-PG lifecycle19 tests (21250268) at a9a08d8758; no skips. Shared current-tree evidence only: integration ledger worktreeDirty=true; no immutable/current import-graph or deployed-main claim. Acceptance still pre-grading: rubric rev1 unvetted, R-1/R-2 proof bindings absent, R-2 live evidence plane unmet. Review/evidence in post1182757; exact external vetting dependency recorded on blocked self-owned follow-up. Retrieval-only consult returned unrelated archive; no agents launched or pass inferred. Existing separately owned harness residues EI-25892586878606558, EI-25891108828268139, EI-25894671456911747 remain outside this follow-up.\n\n**Next:** The rubric author or eligible successor must obtain/record current-revision independent critique and attestation before proof binding; WI-6554700010014178 is blocked at that authority boundary under the explicit no-additional-agents launch constraint.\n\n## Background\nFleet leader su-51c5f29f assigned the repair in coord-send-4051cfd4bb801652aa70ec08664a8b74d22dcdc709215f9301273ac9545c4c5f and coord-send-90353a811343c79d570e1ebbd86993d46485973595be58265a9c7fe91533d43c. WI-6554700010010429 posts1178967/1178982/1178984 contain observed evidence, timing correction and six-step design. Delivery751659 resumed the deliberately killed owner30s after fleet.kill_headless; the resume claim cleared ended_at/ended_by. Governor retirement is excluded because this fleet has no launch transaction.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Persistent deliberate retirement.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Fence killed owners; preserve explicit relaunch and crash recovery.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Deliberate retirement survives ordinary wake/resume and clears on successful explicit operator relaunch.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A routine wake starts a retired owner, a failed relaunch clears retirement, or a crash-only row is refused.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run npm run test:file for maintained retirement reservation, explicit relaunch, crash recovery, kill stamping and wake no-spawn tests; run targeted mutation proof.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/adv-sessions.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-executor-matrix.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/kill.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Executable recurrence guard.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Maintain executable guards and mutation proof.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Retirement regression tests pass and the targeted removal of the wake guard fails the no-spawn assertion.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A removed retirement guard escapes the maintained no-spawn test.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run npm run test:file for maintained retirement reservation, explicit relaunch, crash recovery, kill stamping and wake no-spawn tests; run targeted mutation proof.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/adv-sessions.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-executor-matrix.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/fleet/kill.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n\n## Design\nExtend existing adv_sessions, fleet:kill, resume reservation and wake-executor surfaces. Add retired_at/retired_by/retired_reason through the existing next-migration allocator (.DRAFT until verified, then arm). acquireAdvSessionResume returns retired unless allowRetired is explicitly authorized through capability:launch-agent resume. Fence every process-starting wake channel before the existing Channel2 boundary; a claim retirement result also drops. No new scheduler, identity system or governor-based retirement. Preserve manual file locks, canonical staging tree and background git-sync ownership.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | live |\n\n## Implementation sequence\n1. Inspect kill/resume writers, add retirement schema/type/store and kill stamps.\n2. Guard reservation and wake process starts; thread explicit relaunch opt-in.\n3. Add maintained tests, prove regression failure before fix and caught mutation, run focused suites.\n4. Apply/verify current-build route and disposable kill→wake drop, then close original bug with structured causal evidence.\n\n## Phase 1\n- **P-001** `done` Drive existing claimed WI-6554700010010429 through retirement fence implementation, canonical tests/mutation and bounded disposable current-build verification. Existing bug is the accountable work-item. — note: Implementation/guard/current-build disposable proof complete at originalc866; audit2 verified six citations. Main causal work-item closure next. Three separately owned verification-harness residues retained; no shipped-main claim.\n\n## Decisions\n- **D-001** Source is the leader-authored six-step design in post1178984; the plan decomposition is agent-derived. Do not use governor.retiredMemberIds, kill live customer-probe members, replay docs/FAQ tests, or perform LIVE_GATE_OPS. Explicit relaunch restores a retired session intentionally; accidental wake never does.\n\n### D-002 — Use separate persistent retirement and explicit operator relaunch\nDate: 2026-10-13\nMeasured: adv-sessions.ts acquireAdvSessionResume and claimAdvSessionResume accept terminal rows and clear terminal markers; wake-executor.ts Channel2 claims before resume-headless. Follow leader-authored post1178984 six-step specification. Extend existing adv_sessions, kill, resume and wake seams. Preserve retirement until a successful explicit relaunch; invalidate in-flight reservations on kill. P-001 reuses existing owned bug. No governor-only fence, live customer-probe member kill, docs/FAQ test replay or LIVE_GATE_OPS.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"fixer-gateway-routing-2026-10-13","title":"Blueprint-launched agents route through the inference gateway with declared backup models (main-green unblock)","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-13","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Blueprint-launched agents route through the inference gateway with declared backup models (main-green unblock)\nslug: fixer-gateway-routing-2026-10-13\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-13\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-16, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_vetting_stale. Next repair: Re-vet the current acceptance-rubric criteria before binding more proof or commissioning grading (amend → vet → attest → bind → cards → grade).. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nThe solo executor su-1bc3fa93 holds P001/WI0802 and P004/WI0805; P003 is done. R4@5/SPEC-P004@1 deterministic clean137/mutation proof is complete and bound. Joint R6 clean attempt21257947 at7b5547179b recorded one passing primary case (real Codex200, exact identity/account correlation, all shared claim/file/resource/granular lock counters0) and one failed Claude prepare (fixed sync240s builder timeout; execute blocked, noClaude request). Assigned blocker EI-26061127848650879 now extends the existing prepare wrapper with bounded progress builder240s/420s; focused local tests42PASS, source TSC2+importers error0, clean guard verification running. Independent review stays with existing supervisor08eff/WI14887; vetting repairWI14860 is separate. P001 remains blocked and jointR6 remains unaccepted.\n\n**Next:** Drain the original clean progress-regression handle recorded on EI-26061127848650879, then follow WI0805’s exact current native joint-R6 proof action in the same solo route.\n\n## Goal\nAuto-repair of a red papercusp gate never stalls because one local credential is walled, and every blueprint-launched agent declares how it routes and what it falls back to.\n\n## Product shaping\n- **Audience:** Avi (owner) and the release pipeline; secondarily every blueprint author.\n- **Problem:** the release fixer launches on the box's local codex login. `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/spawn-mcp.ts` L610-614 symlinks `~/.codex/auth.json` into each spawn, and gateway routing is read from the orchestrator PROCESS env (L618-626), not per spawn. `packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/launch-blueprint.ts` resolves model+backend per role (`fleet/role-launch.ts` resolveRoleLaunchLive) but no account route and no backup models. With the local login walled (until 2026-10-18 03:58Z) the capacity preflight withholds repair although pool accounts have credits. main has not been green since 2026-10-02.\n- **Outcome:** a walled account fails over inside the gateway pool; if the whole primary-provider pool is walled, the fixer launches on a declared backup model; the substitution is visible.\n- **Non-goals:** items already on green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08 (P-005 targeted repair rounds for #1796, P-028 lint shift-left, P-029 skip-reason breakdown, P-031 commit-hop guard); buying accounts.\n- **Source turns:** owner #1793 (audit), #1796 (lint-only reds pay a full round), #1797 (fixer not on the auto gateway; \"credits are available, the auto gateway should switch accounts\"), #1800 (can blueprints specify gateway settings and backup models), #1802 (this plan + fleet). Reports: rpt_07d65917 (superseded), rpt_0b337850 (corrected).\n- **Scenarios:** S1 local codex walled, pool has headroom: fixer dispatched via the gateway, no withhold. S2 whole codex pool walled: fixer launches on the declared backup (e.g. claude-code) and the launch records it. S3 a blueprint author sets route + backups in one place and authoring validates it.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Per-spawn account route.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Blueprint-launched release-fixer, merge-resolver, content-fixer and doc-steward receive an explicit account route per spawn; preserve the legacy env fallback only for an absent route.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For an auto-routed blueprint spawn whose orchestrator env lacks PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY, the written config.toml selects the gateway provider with no account-pin header.\",\"falsifier\":\"M1: auto selects local-credential config or includes a pin. M2: an absent request route stops honoring PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY env fallback. M3: pin:<account> lacks the requested pin header. M4: explicit default with no env fails to select local-credential config. M5: an unresolvable explicit auto gateway silently falls back to local credentials instead of refusing before spawn. M6: explicit default is overridden by PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY in the parent environment. M7: requested pin X is replaced by parent PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ID Y. M8: tests still pass after deliberately inverting route precedence or restoring the env-only config writer. M9: a primary non-substituted launch's spawn row omits the resolved account route, requested backend/model/effort, or stable spawn/owner correlation key.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run npm run test:file -- libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/spawn-mcp.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/launch-blueprint.test.ts; execute and record each named case (zero collected cases cannot pass). Marker M1 is pinned by 'auto route writes gateway config without pin when orchestrator env is unset': gateway model_provider/base_url and no pin. Marker M2 is pinned by 'absent route preserves gateway env fallback': legacy env gateway config. Marker M3 is pinned by 'pinned route writes requested account header': exact requested pin. Marker M4 is pinned by 'default route writes local config without env': local config. Marker M5 is pinned by 'unresolvable auto gateway refuses spawn': no spawn and typed route-resolution refusal. In spawn-mcp.test.ts, M1-M5 assert the actual written config; launch-blueprint.test.ts additionally pins route propagation through direct and durable requests. M6 case 'explicit default overrides gateway environment' requires local config with gateway env set; M7 'explicit pin overrides parent account environment' requires requested pin X with parent Y. M8 records discriminating mutation runs for the changed writer/precedence; surviving those mutations cannot pass. Case 'primary spawn persists resolved route and stable owner correlation' in launch-blueprint.test.ts pins M9: exact route, requested backend/model/effort and stable key on the primary spawn row, with a deterministic mismatch/omission control.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/spawn-mcp.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/launch-blueprint.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Preflight measures the routed pool.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Fixer capacity preflight measures only accounts usable by the resolved route across primary and declared backups; unknown capacity remains fail-open.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"With a walled local codex credential and headroom in the resolved auto route, fixer capacity preflight permits dispatch.\",\"falsifier\":\"M1: local-wall masks auto-pool headroom. M2: a pinned route is judged against other pool accounts or auto is judged only against the local credential. M3: probe throw withholds instead of dispatching with an unknown-capacity summary. M4: capacity withhold occurs while any declared backend has usable headroom. M5: an all-declared-backends-walled withhold summary omits the walled pools or the fact that nothing was spent.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run npm run test:file -- apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.test.ts; execute and record each named case (zero collected cases cannot pass). Marker M1 is pinned by 'auto pool headroom permits fixer despite local wall': dispatch permitted. Marker M2 is pinned by 'capacity preflight measures only resolved routable accounts': pin/local/auto account sets match route. Marker M3 is pinned by 'capacity probe error dispatches with unknown summary': dispatch and unknown summary. Marker M4 is pinned by 'backup headroom prevents capacity withhold': dispatch permitted. Marker M5 is pinned by 'all declared backends walled withholds without spend': no spawn; summary names walled pools and nothing spent. Routable means a member of the resolved route's account set, never an unrelated pool account. M5 also asserts the spawn function was never called; the summary alone is insufficient. Both primary and backup probe failures follow unknown-capacity fail-open behavior.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Declared route and backups.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Roles and blueprints declare auto/default/pin account routes and ordered backend/model/effort backups, validated at authoring and preserved by live role resolution.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The effective launch configuration preserves a valid declared role route and ordered backup list unchanged.\",\"falsifier\":\"M1: valid route or backup order is lost. M2: authoring accepts an unknown backend. M3: authoring accepts a model unavailable for its backend. M4: authoring accepts effort outside the supported enum. M5: authoring accepts duplicate backups or a backup equal to primary. M6: an undeclared role no longer inherits the prior host AGENT_CMD behavior. M7: release-fixer lacks its declared auto route and claude-code backup defaults. M8: authoring accepts invalid primary backend/model/effort or an invalid account selector. M9: a maintained blueprint role has neither a declared account route nor an explicit env-inheritance declaration. M10: an explicit per-launch caller account override loses to the role declaration, or an absent override loses the declared role route to ambient env.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/role-launch.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/registry-validation.test.ts; execute and record each named case (zero collected cases cannot pass). Marker M1 is pinned by 'declared route and ordered backups survive live resolution': exact route and order. Marker M2 is pinned by 'blueprint authoring rejects unknown backup backend': authoring refusal. Marker M3 is pinned by 'blueprint authoring rejects unavailable backup model': authoring refusal. Marker M4 is pinned by 'blueprint authoring rejects invalid backup effort': authoring refusal. Marker M5 is pinned by 'blueprint authoring rejects duplicate or primary backup': authoring refusal. Marker M6 is pinned by 'undeclared role preserves host command inheritance': prior host inheritance. Marker M7 is pinned by 'release fixer defaults to auto route and claude backup': auto and claude-code default. Registry-validation.test.ts case 'blueprint authoring rejects invalid primary launch and account selector' pins M8; case 'maintained blueprint roles declare route or explicit env inheritance' enumerates the live registry and pins M9. Preserve existing validated primary model/effort checks rather than duplicating them. Undeclared external/custom roles retain M6 inheritance. Case 'caller account override precedes role route then ambient inheritance' pins M10 in role-launch.test.ts across the three precedence levels. Registry-validation.test.ts M2-M5/M8 cases invoke the real blueprint:extend handler/door with an invalid child and assert its refusal; a disconnected validator alone cannot pass.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/role-launch.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/registry-validation.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Cross-provider failover.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A fully walled primary backend selects the first available declared backup in order; the requested and launched models plus capacity reason are observable.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"With the primary backend walled, the blueprint launch issues a spawn request for the first declared backup with usable capacity.\",\"falsifier\":\"M1: backup headroom is ignored. M2: a walled first backup prevents choosing the second or order changes. M3: spawn row omits requestedBackend/requestedModel, launchedBackend/launchedModel or reason=capacity, or observeFallback/coord notice is absent. M4: primary headroom produces a substitution. M5: every declared backend walled still spawns or records a substitution instead of withholding with the R-2 summary. M6: a backup's unknown capacity is treated as a measured wall instead of fail-open. M7: substitution drops declared effort or a doubled spawn boundary conceals an orchestrator schema rejection. M8: the suite still passes when backup order is reversed or the available backup path is removed. M9: the claude-code backup's auto route omits ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/owner routing headers, preserves a stale account pin on an unpinned route, or a requested pin loses to the parent PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ID.\",\"role\":\"outcome\",\"mandatory\":true,\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run testing:run with harness papercusp and files packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/launch-blueprint.test.ts and packages/operator-core/lib/blueprint/launch-blueprint-fallback.test.ts (the maintained CLI equivalent is npm run test:file -- followed by both paths). Execute and record every named case; zero collected or unexecuted cases cannot pass. Capacity-failover cases below belong to the describe block 'blueprint ordered capacity failover (P-004 R-4)' in launch-blueprint.test.ts; launch-blueprint-fallback.test.ts additionally retains actual defaultFire spawn-record/cleanup bookkeeping coverage. M1 and M3: 'issues the first usable declared backup on both direct and durable paths, preserving effort and primary evidence' asserts the first usable declared backup, requested/launched backend/model/effort, reason=capacity, observeFallback and coord notice. M2: 'skips a walled first backup and selects the second without reordering'. M4: 'keeps a primary with headroom and does not record a substitution'. M5: 'withholds when every declared pool is measurably walled' requires no spawn/substitution and the R-2 walled-pools/nothing-spent summary. M6: 'fails open on unknown backup capacity instead of skipping it'; also run 'keeps an unknown primary, including a failed status read, without claiming a capacity substitution'. M7 and M9: 'carries the backup through the actual invoke parser, metadata writer, and Claude gateway env' bridges the real production body builder, actual invoke request parser, backend model/effort resolver, route metadata writer and Claude gateway env. Require declared effort and the actual backend-specific request validator and command/config builder: a doubled spawn boundary cannot hide schema rejection. M3 additionally records launchedEffort and sends the substitution notice to the current operation/fleet owner. M9 requires auto unpinned env, explicit pin precedence, stable owner routing header and no ambient pin leakage through the actual gatewaySpawnEnv/command-config builder; an omission/mismatch must fail. Also run 'preserves explicit direct and pinned overrides instead of switching their provider', 'honors the same account allow-list as the invoke env and ignores unrelated headroom', and 'uses a backup account declaration while preserving an explicit caller route override'. M8 requires discriminating selection/order mutation runs that fail if backup order is reversed or the available backup path is removed, with passing unmodified and copy controls. Retained control/mutation references: order 21257261/21257265 PASS -> 21257269 caught; actual metadata writer 21257262/21257266 PASS -> 21257270 caught. These retained runs require current measured evidence bindings and are not a fresh acceptance verdict. Unknown primary/backup probe results dispatch fail-open and raise no headroom alarm. The condition deduplicates and clears when the next preflight dispatches or the candidate is removed.\n- The preflight withholds only if every account of every declared backend is walled; explicit unresolvable gateway routes fail closed before spawn. Primary/backup choices retain order.\n- Extend existing x-papercusp-owner and gateway request/servingAccount telemetry into exact first-request metadata on the stable spawn record; this persistence/correlation seam must be implemented by P-001 and preserved by P-004. R-6 proves real primary and declared-backup first requests through an isolated current-build operator-api route, with exact key equality and a measured serving-runtime fingerprint. Live-spend tests use the maintained e2e lane and are excluded from ordinary affected gate selection; deterministic schema/config/correlation coverage remains in that gate.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-004 | live |\n\n## Main green (fleet duty, not a plan item)\nThe gate (WI-10006055) has exactly ONE live owner in fleet main-green-1013; everyone else stays off LIVE_GATE_OPS.\n\n## Cross-plan fleet\nsu-cb24e308 continues green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08 inside this fleet; that plan's P-030 is a pointer to this plan (D-001).\n\n## Items\n- **P-001** `blocked` Per-spawn account route for blueprint launches (R-1, R-6): pass the resolved route per spawn (launch-blueprint.ts request body -> orchestrator invoke.ts / spawn-mcp.ts) instead of reading PAPERCUSP_CODEX_GATEWAY / PAPERCUSP_ACCOUNT_ID from orchestrator process env; route auto writes gateway config without the pin header. P003: committed88c122da80,202 tests+4path tsc clean, caught descriptor-linked mutation21247447 and bindings45266/45268, audit3 with structured shaping/R7 pendingBinding. Release build remains stale; staging is authoritative. scorecards:repair was mistakenly invoked and launched one judge; task was terminated with processes:kill, one zombie awaiting reap. No more agents or repair launches.\n\n**Next:** Verify/bind P004 mutation and run scoped adequacy preview; then await coordinator's existing independent reviewer for P003/current spec-quality before any terminal close or plan start.\n\n## Product shaping\n```product-shaping\n{\"audience\":\"A fleet leader launching members onto explicit ad-hoc lanes alongside an existing plan.\",\"problem\":\"The recorded launch required model archaeology, unrelated exact-plan admission triage, unreadable refusals and hand-authored claim-spec repair before members could work.\",\"outcome\":\"One launch resolves aliases, creates and admits exactly the requested lane ids before startup, or returns a bounded actionable refusal and supported repair.\",\"nonGoals\":[\"Change whole-plan admission or global claim floors for fleets that claim the full plan.\",\"Restore retired Mug/nursery cups.\",\"Solve general fleet assignments latency or code:run timeout policy.\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:a19f47d5-b350-4b06-ae99-a7955a7fbb5c:6\",\"session_turn:claude:a52514c8-7aae-48f2-8e60-c279b9534cb9:8\"],\"context\":[{\"kind\":\"owner-request\",\"text\":\"Avi asked for improvements derived from the previous fleet launch and for this exact plan to be carried to shipped status.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:a19f47d5-b350-4b06-ae99-a7955a7fbb5c:6\"]},{\"kind\":\"observed-fact\",\"text\":\"The existing Product shaping prose and original launcher transcript record alias lookup, unrelated duplicate coverage and missing fleet claim specs.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session:claude:a52514c8-7aae-48f2-8e60-c279b9534cb9\"]},{\"kind\":\"product-choice\",\"text\":\"Reuse both existing launch doors and scheduler:set_claim_spec; preserve exact lane-id fences and independent acceptance.\",\"resolved\":true,\"material\":true}],\"scenarios\":[{\"id\":\"SC-001\",\"title\":\"S1: create, admit and assign lanes before startup\",\"kind\":\"normal\",\"trigger\":\"Leader requests four sol6.1 xhigh members and four lane briefs.\",\"action\":\"Resolve the shared model registry and create exact per-member lane assignments in the launch transaction.\",\"outcome\":\"Each first turn already holds its assigned lane; no unrelated id enters the fleet claim spec.\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-1\",\"R-2\",\"R-6\",\"R-11\",\"R-12\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-002\",\"title\":\"S2: unrelated duplicate is outside admission scope\",\"kind\":\"boundary\",\"trigger\":\"Plan contains duplicate promoted rows for an item no lane targets.\",\"action\":\"Check promotion and floors only for the claimed plan-item scope.\",\"outcome\":\"The unrelated item does not refuse a lanes-only launch.\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-3\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-003\",\"title\":\"S2: targeted duplicate or floor refuses legibly\",\"kind\":\"failure\",\"trigger\":\"A lane targets a duplicate-promoted item or a named claim floor blocks its rows.\",\"action\":\"Refuse before startup and retain full details behind the existing cursor.\",\"outcome\":\"Reason, message, exact blocking ids, named floor and repair call are available within6000characters.\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-4\",\"R-13\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-004\",\"title\":\"S3: aliases and candidate discovery\",\"kind\":\"failure\",\"trigger\":\"Leader supplies an unknown or ambiguous model alias.\",\"action\":\"Resolve through the shared catalog before placement.\",\"outcome\":\"No member launches; candidates are returned and the existing read surface lists the alias catalog.\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-8\",\"R-9\",\"R-10\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-005\",\"title\":\"S4: one-call exact scope repair\",\"kind\":\"recovery\",\"trigger\":\"Running member files follow-up work outside its admitted cohort.\",\"action\":\"Return and send the leader an exact appendIds call; leader admits the named id.\",\"outcome\":\"The next scheduler claim succeeds after one supported revision bump.\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-5\",\"R-14\",\"R-15\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-006\",\"title\":\"Concurrent repairs preserve the union\",\"kind\":\"concurrency\",\"trigger\":\"Two appendIds calls race on one fleet cohort.\",\"action\":\"Serialize merge and revision under the existing claim-spec transaction.\",\"outcome\":\"Both successful additions survive with incumbent fences intact.\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-16\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-007\",\"title\":\"Current-build acceptance and maintained guide\",\"kind\":\"normal\",\"trigger\":\"Implementation reaches P007 verification.\",\"action\":\"Run the maintained S1-S4 check on the measured current build, verify first-turn claims and cleanup, and update existing launch guide.\",\"outcome\":\"Passing scenario ledger and current guide precede independent ship acceptance; pending R7 binding is replaced.\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-7\",\"R-17\"]}],\"considerations\":[{\"category\":\"Authorization and credentials\",\"disposition\":\"covered\",\"reason\":\"Owner chooses execution route; no credential, phone or external publication boundary is widened.\",\"scenarioIds\":[\"SC-001\",\"SC-007\"]},{\"category\":\"Concurrency and peer claims\",\"disposition\":\"covered\",\"reason\":\"Targeted duplicate/refusal and exact append transaction preserve live ownership and claim floors.\",\"scenarioIds\":[\"SC-003\",\"SC-006\"]},{\"category\":\"Runtime and independent acceptance\",\"disposition\":\"covered\",\"reason\":\"Current-build evidence is separate from final shipment; independent grading and cleanup are required.\",\"scenarioIds\":[\"SC-007\"]}]}\n```\n\n\n\n**Audience.** A fleet leader (an su session or an owner-directed agent) who launches N members onto per-member ad-hoc lanes alongside an existing plan.\n\n**Problem (measured).** On 2026-10-13, owner directive #1799 asked su-07164fdb to launch a fleet of \"sol 6.1 xhigh\" agents. The launch took about 31 minutes of leader time (14:51-15:22Z), 49 tool calls of which roughly 15 were pure friction, and four member round-trips. Evidence: session a52514c8-7aae-48f2-8e60-c279b9534cb9 between 14:51Z and 15:22Z, and the refusal spill `~/.papercusp/scratch/papercusp-workspace/tools:invoke/fed3e64b-2df7-43c0-ab5e-3390bd7972d0/result-door-1791904171959.md`.\n\n1. **Model alias.** No catalog maps \"sol 6.1 xhigh\" to a launchable id. The leader recovered `agent: codex, model: gpt-6.1-sol:xhigh` by archaeology on an earlier fleet: memory_search, tools_find (no catalog tool exists), sessions_search, a `fleet:assignments` call that hung past 120 s, and two raw SQL reads of `adv_sessions` with wrong column names. That took about 10 minutes.\n2. **Admission refused for an item no lane targeted.** `fleet:launch-on-plan` returned `admission_refused`, reason `duplicate-coverage`: P-521 had three promoted rows (WI-10004928, WI-2144482, WI-10004750) belonging to a peer lane. This fleet would never claim P-521; its members ran per-member ad-hoc lanes via `perMemberLaunchContext`.\n3. **Illegible refusal.** The refusal was 38 KB. It opened with an unrelated promotion-failsafe `spec_quality_failed` (`atomic-observable-behavior`), and the deciding `reason`/`message` sat at the very end. The leader first misread it as a spec-quality failure.\n4. **Members stranded in fleet_scope_missing.** The fallback `capability:launch-agent { fleet }` launched members with no fleet claim spec. Each member's mandated `work_items:create { assign_to: 'self' }` was downgraded `fleet_scope_missing` (assignee null), and each member had to message the leader. The leader then hand-authored `scheduler:set_claim_spec` with an id-cohort filter, discovering the JSON shape by docs_search plus raw SQL on `cup_claim_specs` (column `bee_id`, not `cup_id`), and assigned each item. The system's auto-message said only \"a revision bump of default-fixed-ordering whose view.filter admits this work\", with no concrete call.\n5. **Batch repair was fragile.** The leader batched spec + four claims in one `code:run`; it hit the 30 s script timeout with 3 of 4 writes settled, and a follow-up batch hit ECONNRESET with outcome unknown. That forced a readback and per-call retries. A one-call admission path removes the need for the batch.\n\n**Outcome.** Launching N members onto per-member ad-hoc lanes alongside a plan is ONE call. It resolves the model alias, creates, admits and assigns each lane before members start, and either succeeds or refuses within the 1.5k-token result cap with the reason, the blocking ids and one ready-to-run repair call.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- Changing exact-plan admission semantics or claim floors for fleets that DO claim plan items.\n- The retired Mug/nursery cup tier.\n- `fleet:assignments` latency (file it separately if it reproduces).\n- `code:run`'s general timeout policy.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner #1799 (session a52514c8 turn 8, 2026-10-13 14:51Z) and owner #1803 (session a19f47d5, about 15:25Z). su-07164fdb's own launch transcript (session a52514c8, 14:51-15:22Z) is the evidence, not owner speech.\n\n**Scenarios.**\n- **S1.** The leader asks for 4 \"sol 6.1 xhigh\" members on plan X with 4 lane briefs. One `fleet:launch-on-plan` call with `lanes[]` launches 4 members, and each holds its own lane work-item at its first turn. No `fleet_scope_missing` occurs.\n- **S2.** Plan X has a duplicate-promoted item that no lane targets: the lanes launch proceeds. If a lane DOES target it, the refusal leads with reason, message, blocking ids and a repair call, within the cap.\n- **S3.** The leader passes `model: 'sol 6.1', effort: 'xhigh'`. It resolves to `agent: codex, model: gpt-6.1-sol:xhigh`, and the result echoes the resolution. An unknown or ambiguous alias refuses with the candidate list.\n- **S4.** A member of a running fleet files a follow-up lane item and is refused `fleet_scope_missing`. The refusal and the leader's auto-message carry a ready-to-run admit call; the leader runs that one call, and the member claims on its next `scheduler:get_next`.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Model }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Original outcome promises\n\n**R-1 — Model alias resolution.** A launch accepts a human model alias plus effort (for example \"sol 6.1\" and \"xhigh\") and resolves both from one registry to the exact agent, model string and effort it will launch, echoing that resolution in the result. An unknown or ambiguous alias refuses with the candidate list, and a read surface lists the catalog.\n\n**R-2 — Ad-hoc lanes in one launch.** `fleet:launch-on-plan` accepts per-member lanes (a title and a brief or launch-context path). Before any member starts it creates each lane work-item assigned to its member and sets the fleet claim spec to admit exactly those ids, so every member holds its lane at first turn.\n\n**R-3 — Admission scoped to what the fleet will claim.** Exact-plan admission refusals (duplicate-coverage and floor-gated) consider only the plan items the fleet will claim. A lanes-only launch is never refused because of a plan item that no lane targets.\n\n**R-4 — Legible admission refusals.** Every `admission_refused` result leads with the reason, the message, the blocking plan-item and work-item ids, the named claim floor when floors gate, and one ready-to-run repair call, all inside the 1.5k-token result cap. Promotion-failsafe and spec-quality detail moves behind a cursor and never precedes the reason. This absorbs EI-25878055537331948, EI-25258192204352881, EI-25647350625398256, EI-25246822174159848 and EI-25850638907096434.\n\n**R-5 — One-call admission repair.** `scheduler:set_claim_spec` gains an append mode that atomically adds work-item ids to a fleet's id-cohort spec (revision bump) without the caller re-authoring the spec JSON. Every `fleet_scope_missing` receipt, and the auto-message to the leader, carries that exact call with the refused id.\n\n**R-6 — launch-agent parity.** `capability:launch-agent` with `fleet` set establishes the same claim-spec default as `fleet:launch-on-plan`, including lanes when `members[]` carry lane titles, so the fallback door never strands members in `fleet_scope_missing`.\n\n**R-7 — Regression guard and docs.** Tests in the project's canonical frameworks pin S1-S4. The launching-agents agent-insights doc and the affected tools' guidance describe the lanes form, the alias resolution and the append-admit repair.\n\n\n- **Model effort parity.** Both launch doors accept top-level `effort`; reuse the existing claim-path scope repair emitter for create-path repairs (supervisor evidence 2026-10-13 15:43-15:46Z).\n- **Reuse first.** Search before adding a surface: the psu `--model` / `--model-source` parsing, `launch_spec.model`, the account/route registry, and the existing `scheduler:set_claim_spec`. Prefer one more option on an existing verb over a new verb, and record what was reused.\n- **Keep the fence.** Lane admission admits EXACTLY the lane ids created in the same call. Never widen a fleet spec to \"any item the member creates\" without an explicit leader opt-in and a cap.\n- **Verify on staging.** Use :3170 or an isolated current build for the S1-S4 end-to-end checks. Launch throwaway headless members against a scratch plan, and end them afterwards.\n- **Related plans (why this is a new effort).** `fleet-launch-admission-clarity-2026-09-13` (archived, awaiting acceptance, 3 items) covered queue screening and verified pickup. `agent-launch-resume-primitives-2026-07-12` introduced `capability:launch-agent`. `improve-fleet-launch-autokickoff-2026-06-30` and `fleet-dispatch-wake-clarity-2026-06-22` covered kickoff and dispatch. None covers lanes, alias resolution, admission scoping or append-admit, and five admission-legibility items are still open after them.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | live |\n| R-8 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-007 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Build\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Model alias registry and resolution (R-1): one registry maps a human alias plus effort (e.g. \"sol 6.1\" + \"xhigh\") to agent, model string and effort; fleet:launch-on-plan and capability:launch-agent resolve through it and echo the resolution; an unknown or ambiguous alias refuses with candidates; a read surface lists the catalog. Reuse the psu --model parsing and launch_spec.model before adding anything.\n- **P-002** `todo` Legible admission refusals (R-4): admission_refused leads with reason, message, blocking plan-item and work-item ids, the named claim floor and one ready-to-run repair call inside the 1.5k-token cap; promotion-failsafe and spec-quality detail moves behind a cursor. The title specifies daily measurement, while the observed existing routine next-fire interval is one hour; authoring intent must be recovered before altering that policy.\nOutcome: a documented, executable rescore using the current rubric and results ledger, with the intended recurrence and an exact regression-event subscription verified.\nNon-goals: improving every measured performance result; changing rubric thresholds; replacing the scheduler or instrument registry; assuming staging proves deployed-main acceptance; taking peers' claimed defects; credential changes; additional agent launches.\nSource refs: session_turn:claude:decf9b3f-7e71-429f-b7d7-e4f45426812c:19 and :42 (original unification direction); session_turn:codex:01a13d6d-a7d4-7ad2-8c54-ebc7e7326525:38 (portfolio execution authorization); shipped parent test-rubric-unification-2026-10-12 R-7/R-8/R-10 and D-008 (derived implementation contract). Kickoff is execution authority in this session, not proof of owner authorship for activation auditing.\n\nScenarios:\n- SC-001 normal: on a scheduled fire, existing checks run and persist one result per executable binding; a ledger-derived scorecard reports their actual ratings. Maps R-1/R-2.\n- SC-004 boundary: activation or acceptance requires independent or owner-only evidence; record the exact unmet gate and preserve it. Maps R-4.\nObserved facts are the staging rubric and successful routine read above. The intended recurrence is unresolved; no new credential or acceptance authority is inferred.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Executable current rubric.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Verify the inherited current-rubric measurement without recreating implemented behavior.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every current executable criterion has an accurately classified result recorded by the completed rescore.\",\"falsifier\":\"Broken if any current criterion has no check or no recorded row without an explicit gap; broken if a NULL measurement is reported as meets or a routine execution-success flag is treated as proof that all criteria pass.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the full current rubric and completed routine's exact test_runs IDs, enumerate the complete binding population, and run the maintained rescore scheduling/dispatch tests. Record serving bg-host build separately from the staging API.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/rubric-rescore-schedule.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/rubric-rescore-dispatch.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Ledger-derived reporting.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Report the recurring measurement from its results ledger rather than by hand.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A complete current-revision scorecard derives every executable criterion through fromLedger:true and is read back with its exact result-row evidence and honest unknowns.\",\"falsifier\":\"Broken if any ledger-owned rating is hand-authored, a missing/error row is silently rated meets, a poor result loses its disposition, or the stored card has missing/extra criterion keys.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the project from-ledger integration test, emit through scorecards:emit with fromLedger:true, then verify scorecards:get/list and result references. Keep measurement success distinct from meeting performance targets.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/scorecards/emit-from-ledger.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Existing schedule and regression delivery.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Preserve the existing scheduled regression measurement and verify its policy.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The existing armed rescore schedule delivers threshold-crossing notifications under its reconciled cadence policy.\",\"falsifier\":\"Broken if the schedule is merely authored but unarmed, targets a replacement bespoke scheduler, silently changes held cadence, or its regression key differs from the subscription. Broken if no actual crossing evidence or focused crossing test is available.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the canonical schedule and live owner's disposition before any retuning; verify the exact event's fire evidence and existing subscription receipt. Run the maintained schedule/crossing tests. Any autonomy/owner-only refusal stays an explicit boundary.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/rubric-rescore-schedule.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Evidence and authority boundaries.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Execute the assigned verification autonomously while preserving peer ownership and independent acceptance.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The completed verification stays within its explicitly assigned execution authority.\",\"falsifier\":\"Broken if a live peer claim is contested, a gate is bypassed, standard measurement reporting is described as independent acceptance/shipment, or undocumented implementation changes occur without registered work and required locks.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Audit this session's durable claims, plan decisions, exact source turns and supported tool receipts. The ledger-adoption integration test independently guards against caller overrides; operational authorization is reviewed separately.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nReuse the existing plan-schedulable system:rubric-rescore action in packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/rubric-rescore-action.ts. It runs registered instrument and probe checks, writes the existing check-results ledger, judges before/after values at current thresholds, and emits exact pass-to-fail crossings. The plan recurrence materializes the existing plan-schedule routine; the subscription primitive is watch:create. Reporting uses scorecards:emit {fromLedger:true}; a passing test or a successful rescore does not imply application-performance targets pass.\n\nNo new table, tool, service, config or scheduler is required. Existing project tests cover scheduling, probe dispatch, rescore crossings and ledger fill. Run their canonical Vitest routes and preserve exact ledger evidence. Read the serving runtime before any current-build probe; staging is the functional plane. Plan APIs internally serialize plan writes; no repository file edit is currently required. Canonical owner-source mapping and independent acceptance gates remain mandatory.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Bar | Work items | Evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | live |\n| R-2 | P-003 | live |\n| R-3 | P-002 | live |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Verification and closeout\n\nTasks are added through plans:add-item after this preparation rewrite. Existing routine/probe bugs remain separate owned lanes.\n- **P-001** `blocked` Verify the existing current-rubric rescore checks, complete ledger coverage and project regression tests (R-1, R-4); rebuild only if evidence shows a genuine gap. — note: ← WI-6554700010014198 blocked (1 external blocker)\n- **P-002** `todo` Recover intended cadence and verify the existing authored/armed plan schedule and exact regression subscription; repair only a confirmed gap using maintained schedule/watch tools (R-3, R-4). blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Emit and read back a current ledger-derived scorecard, record accountable residue, and complete evidence-qualified closeout without claiming independent acceptance or deployment (R-2, R-4). blocked-by: P-001\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Verify the inherited measurement; preserve live ownership and truthful unknowns\nDate: 2026-10-15\nMeasured: staging rubrics:get papercusp-app-performance rev8 projects 23 checks; the 04:30:53Z routine fire wrote test_runs 21250191–21250213. testing:runs shows row 21250212 scout-accumulator-db-cost returns NULL and status error; the rev8 method explicitly defines an idle 20s window as unknown, never meets. Root cause of the earlier reporting error: lastFire error/softError describe execution, not per-check measurement verdicts. Corrective rule: inspect exact ledger rows before claiming measurement completeness or performance health. Existing project tests passed 28/28 at a9a08d8758 (ledger 21250272, 21250273, 21250280). Reuse maintained system:rubric-rescore, plan schedules and watch:create; do not rebuild. Parent test-rubric-unification-2026-10-12#D-008 specifies daily as a design choice, while the inherited routine fires hourly. Preserve that live cadence while its current owner answers intent; no silent policy change. Keep independent acceptance and live release-gate lanes separate. No new durable runtime surface is needed.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAmendment-Id: rescore-atomic-bar-apply-20261018-v1\nRequest-Hash: 4e6c812741f95029cf61682611c002c8817a8b83b1d552e32bf6ef1d0218795d\nActor: su-5a09c09c-3d74-47ef-9d46-6a66084e89a8\nReason: Apply the independently approved R-1/R-3/R-4 outcome sentence and mapping correction for the daily app-performance rescore plan after fresh revision-bound preview.\nApproved-By: su-98b08e88-7374-4c37-812a-701ac366f6da\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1189815\nApproved-At: 2026-10-18T02:38:25.785Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 18 → 19\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-3, R-4\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-3, R-4\n\n### D-003 — Preserve approved R-2 while isolating the implementation-independence blocker\nDate: 2026-10-18\nMeasured on staging 2026-10-18: the approved R-1/R-3/R-4 amendment committed as rubric revision 2 and subject-plan revision 19; activation audit #2 recorded at plan revision 20. plans:evaluate-spec-quality now passes stable identity, item coverage, atomic behavior and falsifiability, but fails only implementation-independence because unchanged AUTO-BAR-R-2-P-003 names the implementation construct `fromLedger`. The independent reviewer approved only R-1/R-3/R-4 hashes; do not alter R-2 or weaken its BAR without a fresh revision-bound preview and outside-lineage approval. Follow-up WI-6554700010017235 owns a compliant evaluator or newly approved amendment path.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n\n## Conformance\n\n```conformance\n{\"requirements\":{\"R-4\":{\"violatedWhen\":[{\"id\":\"execution-authority-boundary\",\"failureMode\":\"A completed verification check lacks accountable execution authority or independent acceptance boundary.\",\"stage\":\"implementation\",\"pendingBinding\":{\"observation\":\"A completed verification check lacks an accountable execution authority or independent acceptance boundary.\",\"bindWhen\":\"P-003 records the authority-boundary check and binds its tree evidence.\"}}]}}}\n```\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-acceptance-bar-probe-20261014-1835-2026-10-14","title":"Acceptance BAR — Acceptance BAR server seeded probe 2026-10-14","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-14","owner":"su-10a90eaf-4bf1-4a45-ad9e-2e9881f115ab","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Acceptance BAR server seeded probe 2026-10-14\nslug: acceptance-acceptance-bar-probe-20261014-1835-2026-10-14\nstatus: superseded\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-14\nupdated: 2026-10-14\nowner: su-10a90eaf-4bf1-4a45-ad9e-2e9881f115ab\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Acceptance BAR server seeded probe 2026-10-14\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Extend `memory_session_surfaced` with an outcome (contradicted / used); record contradicted when the same session supersedes, updates or forgets a surface… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010013441 — Return-path scenario test (R-9), blocked by P-001, P-002 and P-003: checkpoint with probes and references, change a referenced work item, retract a referenced fact, change a probe value; the wake blo… <!-- P-009 -->\n## Context\n\nSource: report [rpt_27cb4abf-63a5-4fdd-a079-20f8e49ebf53](/reports?sel=rpt_27cb4abf-63a5-4fdd-a079-20f8e49ebf53) (WI-6554700010012316). In scope: ideas 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. Out of scope: ideas 3, 7 and 8 [owner:Avi 2026-10-14, turn 6].\n\nBinding constraint [owner:Avi 2026-10-14, turn 4]: no expensive model call on the wake path. Most respawns are short continuous-loop wakes, so wake-time work must be deterministic (database, git and read-only tool reads), bounded, and print nothing when nothing changed.\n\nExisting surfaces to extend (reuse-first, no parallel stores):\n- Carry: `packages/operator-core/lib/carry-note.ts` (`CheckEntry`, with `probe?: ContinuityProbe`), `agent-tools/loop/checkpoint.ts`, `harness/routines/loop-fire.ts` (`renderLoopChecksBlock`), `events/await/wake-executor.ts` (the LIVE RE-CHECK block at delivery), `agent-tools/coordination/{recovery-delivery,compaction-recovery}.ts`, `agent-tools/session/request-compaction.ts`, `agent-tools/work_items/checkpoint.ts` (`dependsOn`).\n- Facts: `agent-facts/store.ts` (`depends_on` = state-cell digests, `supersedes_id`, `retracted_at`, `confidence`), `agent-facts/assumptions.ts` and `cited-facts.ts` (completion `assumptions` cite fact keys).\n- Memory: `memory/audit-anchors.ts` (anchor kinds: file, plan, migration, feature, symbol), `memory/audit-memory-anchors.ts`, the nightly anchor job in `dbos/periodic-workflows.ts`, `memory/session-epoch-ledger.ts` (writes `memory_session_surfaced`), `agent-tools/memory/{remember,search,sweep}.ts`.\n- Ledger: `harness_shared.tool_invocations`; dispatch-level arguments (the `projection` precedent).\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Avi and every Papercusp agent that resumes work after a loop wake, cold wake or carry-respawn, or that relies on shared memory and facts.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Carried claims and shared memories go stale between wakes and the automatic wake and recovery paths re-check none of them: stored check probes run only on an explicit coord:orient, which the recovery marker tells agents to skip (D-004), carry references record no version, retracting a fact leaves the work that relied on it untouched, institutional claims have no lineage, memory anchors cover only files, a carry rewrite can silently drop rows, and nothing records whether a surfaced memory helped or was contradicted.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"A waking agent sees, at no model cost, which carried claims still hold and which changed; retractions reach what depended on them; promoted claims link to their sources; memories go stale when their non-file evidence changes; carry rows survive compaction individually; and memory ranking learns from contradiction.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Report idea 3: independent-evidence promotion gate\",\n    \"Report idea 7: single compiled context builder\",\n    \"Report idea 8: background consolidation\",\n    \"Any model call on the wake or delivery path\",\n    \"Adopting Meko or another third-party memory platform\",\n    \"A new parallel memory, fact, trace or carry store\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:0\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:4\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:8\"\n  ],\n  \"scenarios\": [\n    {\"title\": \"Short loop wake, nothing changed\", \"narrative\": \"An agent on a 60-second loop wakes. Its carried checks still hold and its referenced work item is unchanged. The wake shows no change lines and makes no model call.\"},\n    {\"title\": \"Cold wake after teammates moved on\", \"narrative\": \"An agent returns after six hours. A work item it referenced was closed by a peer, a fact it relied on was retracted, and one probe now returns a different value. The wake lists exactly those three changes with the new values.\"},\n    {\"title\": \"Retracted assumption\", \"narrative\": \"A peer retracts a fact that a closed work item cited as an assumption. The closed item gets a visible flag naming the retracted fact, and its owner is notified.\"},\n    {\"title\": \"Irreversible call on a guess\", \"narrative\": \"An agent calls an irreversible tool citing a suspected fact as its premise. The call is refused and names the fact; with a confirmed fact it proceeds and the premise is recorded on the invocation.\"},\n    {\"title\": \"Where did this convention come from\", \"narrative\": \"A convention fact, an agent-insights doc and a plan decision each record what they were promoted from, and a reverse lookup lists every claim promoted from a given source.\"},\n    {\"title\": \"Memory whose work item was dropped\", \"narrative\": \"A memory names a work item as the open fix for a bug. When that item is dropped, the anchor audit marks the memory stale and recall shows it.\"},\n    {\"title\": \"Carry rewrite loses a row\", \"narrative\": \"A successor rewrites its carry note and omits an open row. The write keeps the row, or under replace reports each dropped row id instead of losing it silently.\"},\n    {\"title\": \"Memory keeps being contradicted\", \"narrative\": \"A memory is surfaced to five sessions and three supersede or forget it. Its outcomes record the contradictions, and recall ranks it below an uncontradicted peer.\"}\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Run stored probes at wake.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Run each carried check's stored probe when a wake is delivered and show whether it still holds.\",\"constraints\":[\"No model call\",\"Read-only probes only\",\"Bounded count and per-probe timeout\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:4\",\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"At wake delivery every carried check within the per-delivery bound (at most 8 probes) whose probe no longer matches its expect value is rendered as changed with the observed value, and every probe that could not run is rendered as could-not-run with the reason and checks beyond the bound are rendered in the not-run count.\",\"falsifier\":\"(1) A probe is printed without being run at wake delivery; (2) a probe that no longer matches renders as matching or renders no line; (3) a probe that could not run renders as matching or changed, or renders without its reason.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-001\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest test 'renders a changed probe with its observed value and a probe that could not run with its reason' in carry-probe-eval.test.ts; the cap case 'caps the probes run per delivery and says how many were left un-run' verifies the eight-probe bound and not-run count; the grader cites those tests by name from the run output; wiring: wake-executor.test.ts 'runs the delivery-time carried probes and places their result inside the live re-check block'.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/carry-probe-eval.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-executor.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Report only changed references.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Record a version for each object a carry note references and, on wake, report only the references that changed or disappeared.\",\"constraints\":[\"Deterministic reference extraction\",\"No model call\",\"Empty output when nothing changed\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:4\",\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Wake delivery renders one line for each carried reference to a work item, plan decision, fact or file whose stored version stamp no longer matches the current source\",\"falsifier\":\"A carried work item, plan decision, fact or file reference whose stored stamp no longer matches its source produces no line at wake delivery\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-002\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest test 'places the delivery-time carried-reference changes inside the live re-check block' in wake-executor.test.ts; the grader cites that test by name from the run output; renderer: carry-ref-stamps.test.ts 'reports changed and gone references and nothing for unchanged ones'\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-executor.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/carry-ref-stamps.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Retractions reach completions.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"When a fact is retracted or superseded, flag the closed work items whose completion assumptions cited it.\",\"constraints\":[\"Use the existing assumptions and cited-facts records\",\"Flag and notify; do not silently reopen\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Retracting a fact, or superseding it with a changed body, adds a flag naming the fact and the reason to every terminal work item whose recorded completion assumptions cite that fact, readable on work_items:get\",\"falsifier\":\"Such a terminal work item shows no flag on work_items:get, or its flag omits the fact or the reason\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-003\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest test 'flags EVERY closed item citing a retracted fact, naming the fact and reason' in retraction-cascade.test.ts; the grader cites that test by name from the run output; surface: get-shape.test.ts 'keeps the flag line at the compact single-item floor'. Cap evictions and byte-identical refreshes are out of scope (D-009)\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-facts/retraction-cascade.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/get-shape.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Premises on calls; irreversible calls need confirmed premises.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Let any tool call name the facts it relies on, record them on the invocation, and refuse irreversible calls whose premises are unconfirmed.\",\"constraints\":[\"One dispatch-level argument, not per-tool arguments\",\"Gate applies to tools marked irreversible\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A call to a tool marked irreversible is refused, naming the fact, when any premise in its dispatch-level premises argument is missing, retracted, superseded, expired, provisional or suspected\",\"falsifier\":\"An irreversible call whose premises argument names a missing, retracted, superseded, expired, provisional or suspected fact proceeds, or its refusal does not name that fact\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-004\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest in premises-gate.test.ts: it.each title 'refuses an irreversible call naming its %s premise before invoking', for missing, retracted, superseded, expired, provisional and suspected; assert refusal names the fact and the handler is not invoked. The grader must cite the matching recorded test cases and their assertions; rate unknown if the required behavior is not exercised.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/premises-gate.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Promotion lineage.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Record where institutional claims were promoted from.\",\"constraints\":[\"Extend facts:assert, docs:author and plans:add-decision; no new write verb\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A claim written through facts:assert, docs:author or plans:add-decision with typed lineage references returns those references when it is read back\",\"falsifier\":\"A claim written with lineage references through any of facts:assert, docs:author or plans:add-decision reads back without them or with different ones\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-005\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest in promotion-lineage.test.ts: 'preserves typed lineage through fact JSON parsing and the bounded facts:list projection', 'round-trips document lineage in canonical frontmatter and preserves it on overwrite', and 'returns structured decision lineage from the canonical plan parser'; inspect each destination read-back. The grader must cite the matching recorded test cases and their assertions; rate unknown if the required behavior is not exercised.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/promotion-lineage.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Non-file memory anchors.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Anchor memories to non-file evidence so the existing audit can mark them stale.\",\"constraints\":[\"Extend memory_anchors and the existing audit\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The anchor audit marks a memory broken when an object named by one of its deterministically extracted non-file anchors no longer resolves\",\"falsifier\":\"A memory whose non-file anchor names an object that no longer resolves is never marked broken\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-006\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest test 'marks a memory broken when an anchored object no longer resolves' in non-file-anchors.test.ts; the grader cites that test by name from the run output (one case per anchor kind: work item, plan decision, session turn, report)\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/memory/non-file-anchors.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Carry rows survive rewrites.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Keep carried rows individually across rewrites so compaction cannot silently drop them.\",\"constraints\":[\"Stable row ids\",\"Deterministic\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A checkpoint write that omits an open carried row keeps that row with its stable id unless the write closes it by id\",\"falsifier\":\"An open carried row absent from a replace-style write is missing from the stored note without having been closed by id\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-007\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest test 'keeps an open carried row omitted from a checkpoint write unless the write closes it by id' in carry-row-ids.test.ts; the grader cites that test by name from the run output\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/carry-row-ids.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Surfaced-memory outcomes feed ranking.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Record what happened to each surfaced memory and use it in ranking.\",\"constraints\":[\"Deterministic signals only\",\"Extend memory_session_surfaced\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Recall ranks a memory with two or more recorded contradicted outcomes below an otherwise equal memory with none\",\"falsifier\":\"Two otherwise-equal memories are returned with the one having two or more contradicted outcomes ranked at or above the one with none\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-008\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest in surfaced-outcomes.test.ts: 'demotes repeatedly contradicted memory, preserving source scores and stable unaffected ordering'; inspect the repeated-contradiction ranking comparison. The grader must cite the matching recorded test cases and their assertions; rate unknown if the required behavior is not exercised.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/memory/surfaced-outcomes.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Return path end to end.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Prove the return path end to end: an agent leaves, peers change state, the agent returns.\",\"constraints\":[\"No model call on the wake path\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:4\",\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The wake block rendered after a scenario that changes a referenced work item, retracts a referenced fact and changes a probe value lists exactly those three changes\",\"falsifier\":\"Any of the three changes is missing from the rendered wake block, or the block lists a change for an object the scenario did not change\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-009\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest in carry-return-path.integration.test.ts: parametrized title '${path} renders exactly the moved item, retracted fact and changed probe with stable ids', for wake and compaction recovery. R-9 requires the moved item, retracted fact and changed-probe assertions; R-19 requires the unchanged negative-control assertion; R-27 requires the recorded no-model-call assertion. Grade this criterion only from its named assertion within the shared scenario. The grader must cite the matching recorded test cases and their assertions; rate unknown if the required behavior is not exercised.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/carry-return-path.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Non-read-only probes are refused.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Refuse a carried probe that is not provably read-only.\",\"constraints\":[\"No model call on the wake path\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:4\",\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A carried probe that names a tool not provably read-only is reported as could-not-run without being dispatched\",\"falsifier\":\"A write-capable or unprovable tool probe is dispatched at wake delivery\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-001\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest test 'reports a write-capable tool probe as could-not-run (not_read_only) and never calls the dispatcher' in carry-probe-eval.test.ts; the grader cites that test by name from the run output\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/carry-probe-eval.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-11 — Changed references at compaction recovery.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Report changed carry references on compaction recovery as well as wake delivery.\",\"constraints\":[\"No model call on the wake path\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:4\",\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Compaction recovery renders one line for each carried reference whose stored version stamp no longer matches the current source\",\"falsifier\":\"A changed carried reference produces no line at compaction recovery\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-002\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest in carry-ref-delivery.test.ts: 'renders changed (R-11) and gone (R-20) references across the loop note and held checkpoints';
