Before the following wake restore the probed value to the original expect value; the delivered prompt must show no changed-probe line.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n**R-34 — Retracted fact anchors are broken.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Retracted fact anchors are broken\",\"constraints\":[\"Extend memory_anchors and the existing audit\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The anchor audit marks a memory broken when a fact named by one of its anchors is retracted\",\"falsifier\":\"A memory whose anchor names a retracted fact is never marked broken\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-006\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest test 'marks a memory broken when an anchored fact is retracted' in non-file-anchors.test.ts; the grader cites that test by name from the run output\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/memory/non-file-anchors.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-35 — Unpremised irreversible calls are not refused.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Unpremised irreversible calls are not refused\",\"constraints\":[\"One dispatch-level argument, not per-tool arguments\",\"Gate applies to tools marked irreversible\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An irreversible call that carries no premises argument is not refused for lacking premises\",\"falsifier\":\"An irreversible call is refused because it carries no premises argument\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-004\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest in premises-gate.test.ts: 'allows an irreversible call without premises and records that absence'. The shared test serves R-31 through its explicit no-premises invocation-record assertion, and R-35 through its non-refusal/handler-execution assertion; grade only the assertion belonging to this criterion. The grader must cite the matching recorded test cases and their assertions; rate unknown if the required behavior is not exercised.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/premises-gate.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-36 — A real wake shows a changed reference.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A real wake shows a changed reference\",\"constraints\":[\"No model call on the wake path\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:4\",\"session_turn:claude:9cc4e4f0-e723-4319-96f9-b1eadd965b8d:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A loop wake delivered by the running operator renders a changed carried reference in the delivered prompt\",\"falsifier\":\"A delivered wake whose carried work-item reference changed state after the checkpoint omits the changed-reference line, or a wake following a new stamping checkpoint with the reference untouched prints one.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-009\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[],\"mandatory\":true},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Arm the loop through the staging operator at :3170, with a carry note citing a private work item, and write loop:checkpoint so the reference is stamped. After that checkpoint, a different session changes the cited item's state with work_items:set_state; the parking session must not perform that update. A checkpoint-only write on the cited item is not the stimulus. The grader cites the delivered wake turn (session_turn ref) showing the changed-reference line and the serving bg-host build sha. Negative control: in that wake's turn, the parking session writes loop:checkpoint again to stamp the reference at its new token; nothing then touches the cited item, and the following wake's delivered prompt must show no changed-reference line.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-24 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-25 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-26 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-27 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-28 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-29 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-30 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-31 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-32 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-33 | P-009 | live |\n| R-34 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-35 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-36 | P-009 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Wake re-checks (report idea 1)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Run stored carried-check probes at wake delivery (R-1). Reuse the existing bounded read-only runner (`runContinuityProbeBatch` / `runContinuityProbesForOwner` in `continuity-probes.ts`, today called only by coord:orient — D-004) and call it from the LIVE RE-CHECK block in `events/await/wake-executor.ts` and from compaction recovery. Refuse non-read-only tools; cap probe count and per-probe time; render holds / changed (observed value) / could-not-run (reason). No model call. — note: ← WI-6554700010012441 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Version-stamp carry references and report only changes (R-2). At `loop:checkpoint` and `work_items:checkpoint` write time, deterministically extract referenced work items, plan decisions, facts and files and store a version stamp for each (row `updated_at`/state, plan revision, fact retracted/superseded state, git blob). On wake delivery and compaction recovery, re-read and render one line per changed or unresolvable reference; print nothing when none changed. — note: ← WI-6554700010012556 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Premises and retraction repair (report idea 2)\n\n- **P-003** `done` Cascade fact retraction and supersession to completions (R-3). Using the completion `assumptions` records (`agent-facts/assumptions.ts`, `cited-facts.ts`), flag every closed work item whose assumptions cite a fact when that fact is retracted or superseded, naming the fact and reason, and notify the item's terminal owner. Flag, don't reopen. — note: ← WI-6554700010012896 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Dispatch-level `premises` argument (R-4). Accept `premises: [factKey]` on every tool at the dispatch layer (like `projection`), resolve each fact, record premises on `tool_invocations`, and refuse calls to tools marked irreversible when any premise is missing, retracted, superseded, expired, provisional or suspected. — note: ← WI-6554700010013436 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Promotion lineage (report idea 4)\n\n- **P-005** `done` `promotedFrom` lineage on `facts:assert`, `docs:author` and `plans:add-decision` (R-5). Typed references (memory, session turn, work item, report, fact, plan decision) validated to resolve, persisted, returned on read, with a reverse lookup of claims promoted from a source. — note: ← WI-6554700010013437 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 4 — Evidence anchors (report idea 5)\n\n- **P-006** `done` Non-file memory anchors (R-6). Add anchor kinds for work items, plan decisions, facts, session turns and reports to `memory/audit-anchors.ts`; extract them deterministically in `memory:remember`; checkers mark a memory `broken_anchor` when a referenced work item or decision no longer resolves or a referenced fact is retracted. — note: ← WI-6554700010013438 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 5 — Itemized carry and usage signals (report idea 6)\n\n- **P-007** `done` Carry rows survive rewrites (R-7). Stable ids on carried check and wall rows; a `loop:checkpoint` or `work_items:checkpoint` write that omits an open row keeps that row unless the write closes it by id (D-010 #8, report idea 6 'removed individually, never re-summarized whole'). — note: ← WI-6554700010013439 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Surfaced-memory outcomes feed ranking (R-8). Extend `memory_session_surfaced` with an outcome (contradicted / used); record contradicted when the same session supersedes, updates or forgets a surfaced memory and used when it fetches or cites it by id; expose per-memory counts; demote repeatedly contradicted memories in recall. — note: ← WI-6554700010013440 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 6 — End-to-end proof\n\n- **P-009** `done` Return-path scenario test (R-9), blocked by P-001, P-002 and P-003: checkpoint with probes and references, change a referenced work item, retract a referenced fact, change a probe value; the wake block reports exactly those three changes, and a no-change control run reports none. — note: ← WI-6554700010013441 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Deterministic wake path only — no model calls\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-14, turn 4 of claude session 9cc4e4f0] Most respawns are short continuous-loop wakes, so everything this plan adds to wake delivery, compaction recovery and carry rendering must be deterministic: database rows, git blobs and read-only tool/state-cell reads only. No LLM/model call anywhere on the wake or delivery path. Wake-time work is bounded (probe count cap, per-probe timeout) and prints nothing when nothing changed.\n\n### D-002 — Premises are a dispatch-level argument, not per-tool arguments\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[self-imposed] P-004 adds `premises: [factKey]` once, at the tool dispatch layer (the same seam that already accepts `projection` on every tool), rather than as an argument on each tool's own schema. One resolution + recording path covers the whole catalog; per-tool schemas stay unchanged. Premises are recorded on the invocation row; only tools whose registry metadata marks them irreversible/destructive are gated.\n\n### D-003 — Reuse existing surfaces — no parallel stores\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[self-imposed] Every item extends an existing surface: carry-note CheckEntry/ContinuityProbe and loop:checkpoint for P-001/P-002/P-007; the work-item checkpoint and the wake-executor LIVE RE-CHECK block for delivery; agent-facts assumptions/cited-facts for P-003; the tool dispatch + tool_invocations for P-004; facts/docs/plan-decision rows for P-005 lineage; memory_anchors + the existing anchor audit for P-006; memory_session_surfaced for P-008. No new memory, fact, trace or carry store and no new write verb. Where a column is needed it is added by migration to the existing table.\n\nScope note for report idea 1's second half (owner turn 4 quoted it: \"also lists open obligations the carry doc didn't mention, such as held work items, unanswered directed messages and open directives\"): that listing already exists deterministically — the carry document's Standing carry block lists open owner directives, held-item checkpoints and deferred unclaimed work-items, and the turn-start Orientation block lists unanswered directed messages. This plan does not rebuild it; P-002 adds only the per-reference change report.\n\n### D-004 — Correction: probes already run on coord:orient; P-001 extends the existing runner to delivery and recovery\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[self-imposed] CORRECTION of an earlier claim by su-b8faed4c (carry note, observation EI-25943542766935513, plan Product shaping, and report rpt_27cb4abf idea 1): 'stored check probes are printed but never run' is WRONG. coord:orient already replays executable carried-check probes via runContinuityProbesForOwner (packages/operator-core/lib/continuity-probes.ts, WI-42290; called from agent-tools/coordination/tools/orient.ts ~L3895). What survives: the auto-delivered paths do NOT run them — wake-executor's LIVE RE-CHECK block, recovery-delivery.ts and compaction-recovery.ts contain no probe execution (grep, 2026-10-14), and the post-compaction recovery marker tells agents NOT to call coord:orient when it is complete, so on a carry-respawn the probes are skipped. P-001 therefore REUSES runContinuityProbeBatch/runContinuityProbesForOwner (same bounds: CONTINUITY_PROBE_MAX_PER_WAKE, CONTINUITY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, read-only validation) on the delivery/recovery paths; it does not build a second evaluator.\n\n### D-005 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: amend-582283022894f6b330f0c6f6\nRequest-Hash: e65e10b184e9c63ddbd5a283607a8d1bbb3657c5e0368ea2102f401b35703561\nActor: su-b8faed4c-47ce-4467-acae-1a5e1e46edf0\nReason: Atomize compound BARs by SPLITTING (per outside-lineage objections thread-post:1180613 and thread-post:1180653): R-1,R-2,R-4,R-6,R-7,R-8,R-9 narrowed to one outcome each; every dropped sub-requirement re-added as its own BAR R-10..R-22 (incl. R-20 gone-at-compaction-recovery, R-21/R-22 silence for unchanged references at wake delivery / compaction recovery). Plan not yet started.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-aab2ed4a-9c2d-4e45-a2c9-00e9b0cc96b5\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1180712\nApproved-At: 2026-10-14T09:17:43.187Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 35 → 36\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-4, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19, R-20, R-21, R-22\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-006 — P-002 stores reference version stamps as carry_notes.deps.refs, beside (not inside) the declared freshness stamps\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14 [self-imposed]\nP-002's write-time stamps reuse the existing `harness_shared.carry_notes.deps` jsonb column (D-003: no new store, no migration). They go under a separate `refs` key and not into `deps.stamps`. `deps.stamps` is the author-declared `dependsOn` set: it drives `computeFreshness` and the fresh/stale verdict, and `parseDeclaredDeps` returns null when it is empty, so a refs-only payload `{v:1, stamps:[], refs:[...]}` keeps the verdict 'undeclared' and existing behaviour is unchanged. Extraction and resolution live in the new packages/operator-core/lib/carry-ref-stamps.ts. Work items and files reuse the existing freshness resolvers. `decision:<slug>#D-NNN` (sha of title+body, so an unrelated plan edit does not flag every decision) and `fact:<key>` (live / retracted / superseded / evicted / expired) are resolved locally there. They are deliberately NOT added to `DEP_RESOLVERS`, because that registry is also the declarable `dependsOn` vocabulary rendered into two tool descriptions. A reference that does not resolve at write time is not stamped (it has no baseline). At read time a null token renders as GONE. A resolver failure or overrun renders an explicit COULD NOT RE-CHECK line, never silence.\n\n### D-007 — Independent item behavior clauses complement the BAR projections\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[self-imposed] Spec-quality rubric rev6 rates item contracts over independently authored active clauses only; sourceBar AUTO-BAR rows are copies of acceptance BARs and are excluded. The grading-integrity audit EI-25948035915813635 failed spec-quality card EI-25947540098740786 because every active clause here was a sourceBar projection. Resolution: each plan item P-001..P-009 gets one independently authored ACTIVE clause stating a single observable outcome that complements (does not restate) its BARs: P-001 probe cap line, P-002 own-item self-exclusion, P-003 flag-not-reopen, P-004 non-irreversible tools unaffected, P-005 unresolvable lineage refused, P-006 resolving anchors stay healthy, P-007 stable ids survive restatement, P-008 untouched surfaced memories record no outcome, P-009 no spurious change lines. The items themselves trace to owner directive #1876 [owner:Avi 2026-10-14].\n\n### D-008 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: crgm-r5-split-apply\nRequest-Hash: ef83085c9a6f294398c1d692423a19a7875448236c0ad2fda20895a23d36eb17\nActor: su-b8faed4c-47ce-4467-acae-1a5e1e46edf0\nReason: [self-imposed] Split compound R-5 (D-005 precedent): R-5 narrowed to read-back; dropped sub-requirements re-added as R-23 (unresolvable lineage refused) and R-24 (reverse lookup), all three scoped to facts:assert, docs:author and plans:add-decision per outside-lineage objection thread-post:1180927. R-5 also named an internal lower-camel argument identifier, which newer spec-quality builds fail as implementation coupling. Plan not yet started. Carried by WI-6554700010012572.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-99759626-7fb7-4c3e-908f-965fffb4350f\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1180936\nApproved-At: 2026-10-14T10:34:39.712Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 45 → 46\nChanged BARs: R-5, R-23, R-24\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-009 — P-003 cascade scope: unchanged-body supersession is a refresh; cap evictions are not cascaded; flags surface on work_items:get\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14 [self-imposed] Implementation rulings for P-003 (R-3), recorded so the per-item audit and the grader read the as-built scope rather than inferring it. (1) A supersession whose new body is byte-identical (trimmed) to the superseded version is a REFRESH, not a change: supersessionChangedBody() returns false and the cascade skips with skipped:'body-unchanged'. A failed read of the old body answers true (flag rather than miss a real change). Rationale: assertFact supersedes on EVERY re-assert of an existing key, so flagging refreshes would bury real retractions in noise. (2) Versions evicted by the fact-store cap are NOT cascaded; only retractFact and assertFact's explicit supersession (supersedes_id + retired_keys) emit. (3) Only TERMINAL items (ANY_FAMILY_TERMINAL_STATES) are flagged, and the state is never changed (CRGM-P-003-flag-not-reopen); the flag is an idempotent append to payload._assumptionFlags keyed by dedupeKey, and the terminal owner (fallback: taken_by) is notified once per new flag. (4) The visible surface is work_items:get -> assumptionFlags [{ condition, factRef, key, reason, at, line }], kept at every shaping tier (compact floor keeps condition/factRef/line) with { shown, total } truncation disclosure. (5) The cascade's candidate query repeats migration 1506's partial-index predicate verbatim and caps at CASCADE_ITEM_LIMIT=500 with a truncation marker.\n\n### D-010 — Dispositions for bar critiques #1 (thread-post:1181510) and #2 (thread-post:1181487) on bar set d7d74e7c96b5\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[self-imposed] Owner meaning is taken verbatim from report rpt_27cb4abf-63a5-4fdd-a079-20f8e49ebf53, whose ideas 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 the owner adopted in directive #1876 [owner:Avi 2026-10-14]. Applied as one rubrics:amend (all bars rewritten together, then both consults closed so each pins the amended contract).\n\nACCEPTED\n1. R-1 contradicted idea 1 ('Print one line per item that changed or disappeared, and nothing for items that didn't') and D-001 ('prints nothing when nothing changed'). R-1 now covers changed and could-not-run probes only; new R-25 bars silence for a probe that still matches. CODE CHANGE: P-001's renderCarriedProbeBlock stops printing a HOLDS line per probe and prints nothing when every probe matches (the cap line and could-not-run lines stay).\n2. Probes at compaction recovery (D-004; recovery marker suppresses coord:orient) were unbarred: new R-26 (P-001).\n3. No model call on the wake path (D-001 owner, idea 1 'deterministic, no LLM call') was unbarred: new R-27 (P-009, recorded-inference spy over both blocks). Per-probe timeout: new R-28 (P-001).\n4. Falsifier clauses that duplicated a sibling bar were removed or rewritten: R-1 (=R-10), R-2 (=R-21), R-4 (=R-14), R-8 (=R-16), R-9 (=R-19). R-11 and R-20 are rephrased so they no longer depend on wake delivery passing.\n5. R-3: 'superseding' narrowed to a changed-body supersession (D-009 refresh rule), the flag surface named (work_items:get), and notify split into new R-29 (exactly one notification per retraction event, replay sends none; as-built behaviour, dedupeKey).\n6. R-4 was vacuous without a marked set. Idea 2(b) names the set ('forced deploy, destructive database work, outward publishing'): new R-30 bars that those tools carry the irreversible marking. New R-31: an irreversible call with no premises argument proceeds and records that none were given (idea 2(b) refuses only on provisional or suspected cited evidence; refusing every unpremised irreversible call is not in the owner text). New R-32: a premises argument never changes a tool's own argument validation (P-004 'on every tool at the dispatch layer').\n7. R-6 uses 'broken' in condition and falsifier, and audits all five anchor kinds R-15 extracts (adds session turns and reports), so no extracted anchor is dead data (idea 5: 'tell when a memory's evidence has changed or disappeared').\n8. R-7 takes the stronger reading from idea 6 ('removed individually, never re-summarized whole'): a write that omits an open row keeps it unless the write closes it by id. P-007 item text is updated to match.\n9. R-8: 'repeated' defined as two or more contradicted outcomes. R-18 names its surface (memory:list).\n10. R-9 becomes the integration wiring proof (carry-return-path.integration.test.ts drives the real wake-executor and compaction-recovery entry points). New R-33 (P-009, evidencePlane live): a real wake delivered by the running operator shows a changed probe and a changed reference.\n11. Recovery-path bars (R-11, R-20, R-22, R-26) are bound to the entry-point tests in compaction-recovery.test.ts, not only the renderer file. Every bar's method names one it() title (critique #1 A3).\n12. Duplicate item clauses replaced: CRGM-P-009-no-spurious-lines -> each change line carries the stable id of the row or reference it reports; CRGM-P-005-unresolvable-refused -> a reverse lookup by a source with no promoted claims returns an empty list.\n\nREJECTED\n- Surfaced-memory dedupe (critique #1 C2, #2 U3): the owner text (idea 6) says 'record whether each surfaced memory was used, ignored or contradicted ... and use that for ranking and pruning'; it never mentions dedupe. 'Pruning' is met by demotion in recall (R-8); hard deletion of memories is destructive and not requested.\n- Re-projecting stale AUTO-BAR rows by hand (critique #1 A1): rubrics:amend re-seeds every bar whose meaning changes; bars whose meaning is unchanged keep their projection by design.\n\n### D-011 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: crgm-d010-amend-apply\nRequest-Hash: 8bd98d2eec3904fcee0cf735d6c646486d36a5083048080b1d2095792b554395\nActor: su-ae8a88db-3c34-48b5-9991-d80119e7bca9\nReason: [self-imposed] D-010: dispositions for bar critiques thread-post:1181510 and thread-post:1181487 on bar set d7d74e7c96b5. Verify successful auto recovery, interactive transcript persistence, stale error replay, route repair failure, owner-edit refusal, automatic transient/unavailable handling, and auth separation.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher-codex-home-guard.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host-turn.integration.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-executor.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Verification.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Retain project-native regression coverage that exercises the repaired child boundary and quota recovery safety contract.\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a1373f-a6fc-72b0-8ec9-40300ae6e849:10\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Use the repository test router and current staging source.\",\n      \"Source verification does not establish historical live terminal adoption or final release.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Registered launcher/PTY/wake suites execute the selected-route, quota, carry and auth recovery cases with zero failures. Real PTY tests check route before replacement, exact conversation continuation and refusal boundaries; ledger evidence identifies the tested source and executed versus skipped cases.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A required scenario is skipped or fails, an ad hoc check substitutes for registered tests, or a fixture/source-only pass is reported as historical live terminal or release acceptance.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"P-003\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_HARNESS=papercusp npm run test:file for the four named files with selected Codex route|quota|carry|auth recovery; retain the stamped per-file run IDs, execution counts and provenance. Independently grade these bars after code-truth audit; do not self-grade acceptance.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher-codex-home-guard.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/lib/psu-pty-host-turn.integration.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/events/await/wake-executor.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\nExtend existing launcher and PTY recovery under completed EI-25674330292058027; direct execution in the assigned session, no delegation. Reuse prepareCodexGatewayLaunch and hostThroughPty; no new routing or orchestration surface.\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation and finite verification are complete: all3 source items verified in completion audit4, activation audit2 seeded active acceptance rubricrev1. This session stops at that external review dependency, with no release-gate operations.\n\n## Acceptance boundaries\nHistorical, already-running TUIs keep their loaded launcher/host code until safely resumed. No mass restart, credential change, quota bypass, deliberate route override, or held live release-gate operation is authorized by this closeout. Independent acceptance must be performed outside the implementation lineage; this assigned agent will not launch additional agents or manufacture independent approval.\n\n## Phase 1 — Fix\n- **P-001** `done` Repair route preservation. importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010011623 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Extend guarded recovery. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `done` Run regression tests. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010011687 completed (done)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"gateway-admission-congestion-only-2026-10-13","title":"Inference gateway: back off only on real congestion, pace uploads not requests","status":"awaiting-acceptance","created":"2026-10-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Inference gateway: back off only on real congestion, pace uploads not requests\nslug: gateway-admission-congestion-only-2026-10-13\nstatus: awaiting-acceptance\ncreated: 2026-10-14\nupdated: 2026-10-14\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience:** Avi and every agent session on the auto inference gateway (:8788).\n\n**Problem:** since 2026-10-13 21:00Z, Codex model calls wait 4-14 min in the gateway's Codex admission queue (queueWait p50 661s) while upstream answers in ~7s. Every failed upstream attempt (gateway.ts:8880), including each failover retry of one slow request, halves the shared Codex window (floor 4). Evidence: WI-6554700010011426; report rpt_337011d4-7d86-4bb2-848f-574ccec6958a.\n\n**Outcome:** Codex and Claude turns are back to ~10-30s. The gateway limits only the resource that is actually scarce: upload bandwidth during a mass resume. In normal operation there is no request limit at all.\n\n**Non-goals:** changing per-account usage pacing or burn-governor policy; changing the account-selection or affinity policy.\n\n**Source turns:** owner directives #1820, #1826, #1829, #1830, #1831 (Avi, 2026-10-13/14).\n\n**Scenarios:**\n1. A few huge prompts are slow to start and time out. Other sessions are unaffected and the window does not collapse.\n2. An account is out of usage (weekly wall). That account is blocked; the shared window does not move.\n3. A ~200-agent mass resume saturates the uplink (the 10-12 incident). The gateway still queues uploads instead of collapsing, then recovers fast.\n4. A genuine too-many-requests throttle that cannot be routed around moves the window, gently.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Only congestion errors shrink the window.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Only congestion errors (too-many-requests style) may affect the cap; an out-of-usage error blocks the account and must not affect the cap [owner:Avi #1830]. Transport/TTFB failures count only when sustained across distinct requests (D-001).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:b79a7726-7af9-4bc8-a136-ab6519bd96fd:14\",\"session_turn:claude:b79a7726-7af9-4bc8-a136-ab6519bd96fd:16\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"On both lanes, an outcome classified account-scoped (out-of-usage, weekly wall, auth) or neutral (routed-around 429, client error, cancel) leaves the admission window unchanged, while sustained non-routable transient 429s or transport failures across distinct requests still contract it.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any ONE: (1) an out-of-usage or weekly-wall 429 changes the window on either lane; (2) a 429 that was failed over to another account adds congestion pressure; (3) sustained non-routable transient 429s or transport failures from distinct requests never contract the window.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the provider-admission lifecycle and gateway proxy Vitest suites; read the classifier cases (account-scoped and neutral leave the window unchanged, congestion contracts) for both the codex and claude lanes. Cases: 'an out-of-usage / weekly-wall 429 leaves the window unchanged, however many arrive', 'a 429 that was failed over to another account is neutral', and 'a many-request herd (the 2026-10-12 mass resume) still contracts', parameterized over both lanes (D-001/D-002/D-003).\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/provider-admission-lifecycle.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway-openai-proxy.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Shrink gently.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Be less aggressive in the reduction [owner:Avi #1830]: at most one pressure unit per request across failovers, hard failures need sustained pressure, a gentler fraction, a floor sized to healthy accounts, and faster recovery while the queue is deep.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:b79a7726-7af9-4bc8-a136-ab6519bd96fd:14\",\"session_turn:claude:b79a7726-7af9-4bc8-a136-ab6519bd96fd:16\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"One request whose attempts fail any number of times adds at most one unit of congestion pressure to its lane.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any ONE: (1) a single request with N failed attempts contracts the window; (2) one hard failure from one request contracts the window; (3) one contraction removes more than 25% of the window; (4) with queue depth above the window and zero pressure, a clean success does not grow the window. (5) a contraction takes a lane's window below its live count of healthy (non-walled) accounts.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the provider-admission lifecycle Vitest suite; read the per-request dedupe, threshold, fraction and deep-queue recovery cases. Named cases: 'one request with N failover attempts adds congestion pressure ONCE', 'removes at most a quarter of the window per contraction', 'never contracts a lane below its count of healthy accounts', 'a few large-prompt timeouts, each failing over many times, leave the window open', and 'recovers on every clean success while demand is queued and pressure is zero'.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/provider-admission-lifecycle.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Pace uploads, not requests.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Pace the uploads (bytes being sent), not the number of requests in flight; a streaming response must not hold an admission slot [owner:Avi #1831].\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:b79a7726-7af9-4bc8-a136-ab6519bd96fd:16\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A request on a remote provider lane (claude or codex) whose response is streaming does not hold its lane admission slot.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if (1) a Claude- or Codex-lane request still holds its lane admission slot while its response streams, or (2) its slot is released before its request body has finished uploading, so concurrent uploads are not bounded by the admission window. The previous live queueWait marker is retained as R-8.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Governs: D-004 (release-for-stream applies to remote provider lanes only; a local lane keeps its slot while it streams because that streaming is the GPU work its slot paces, and the per-account governor slot stays held). Run gateway-openai-proxy.test.ts cases 'frees the Codex slot while the stream is open, admits a second request, then relays the rest' and 'holds the Codex slot through the upload until the upstream sends its first response byte'; gateway-claude-stream-release.test.ts case 'frees the claude lane slot while the stream is open, admits a second request, then relays the rest' (the claude lane, through the real /v1/messages handler); and request-kernel.test.ts 'frees the slot once the response streams, so a second request is admitted while the first is still open' with its CONTROL 'without the hook the stream keeps its slot'. Also run gateway-claude-stream-release.test.ts 'holds the claude slot through the upload until the upstream sends its first response byte'. The live targets formerly mixed into R-3 are independently graded as R-8/R-9/R-10.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway-openai-proxy.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway-claude-stream-release.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/request-kernel.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Claude parity.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Handle Claude the same way [owner:Avi #1830 asked how Claude is handled]: one classifier and one policy for both lanes in the shared provider-admission-lifecycle.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:b79a7726-7af9-4bc8-a136-ab6519bd96fd:14\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For the same upstream outcome, the claude and codex lanes change their admission window the same way.\",\"falsifier\":\"BROKEN if any ONE: (1) one outcome class - account-scoped (out-of-usage, weekly wall, auth), lane congestion (a transient 429 not routed around, or a transport failure), neutral (a 429 failed over to another account), or success - moves the claude window differently from the codex window; (2) either lane contracts its window on an outcome the shared classifier marks account-scoped or neutral.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Governs: D-001, D-002. Contraction is deduped per requestId and gated by sustained pressure. The admission gate covers the upload phase / bytes in flight, so streaming responses hold no slot. Large-prompt TTFB failover is bounded. Wake fan-out pacing lives in the shared wake-delivery path.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-007 | live |\n| R-9 | P-007 | live |\n| R-10 | P-007 | live |\n\n## Acceptance\n\nLive on :8788 after a gateway restart: Codex queueWait p50 under 2s with no herd; the Codex window is not pinned at its floor; a short new Codex turn completes in under 30s; the Claude lane is unchanged or better (P-007).\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `done` Shared outcome classifier for both lanes: account-scoped (out-of-usage, weekly wall, auth), lane congestion (a transient 429 that cannot be routed around; a transport failure while uploads are slow), or neutral. Wire both lanes through it (R-1, R-4). — note: Implemented by su-36b03d7d (WI-6554700010011426 done): shared classifier upstream-outcome-classifier.ts:61 classifyUpstreamOutcome, consumed at provider-admission-lifecycle.ts:375. Code audit seq 4 verified.\n- **P-002** `done` Contraction policy: once per request across failovers; sustained-pressure threshold for hard failures; gentler fraction; floor sized to healthy accounts; faster recovery when the queue is deep (R-2). — note: Implemented by su-36b03d7d (WI-6554700010011426 done): only sustained throttle/transport failures contract the window, at most 25% (MIN_CONTRACTION_FRACTION 0.75, #contract at provider-admission-lifecycle.ts:421). Code audit seq 4 verified.\n- **P-003** `done` Pace uploads, not requests: measure whether the admission slot is held through streaming; release it after the body is written, or gate on bytes in flight (R-3). — note: releaseForStream frees the admission slot at first response byte; the stream is relayed outside the slot (request-kernel.ts:1214/1289, gateway.ts:10576 remote lanes only per D-004). Tests: request-kernel.test.ts:1115, plus the upload-hold falsifier in gateway-openai-proxy.test.ts (mutation probe caught; awaiting git-sync commit). Code audit seq 5 verified.\n- **P-004** `done` Bound failover of large uncached prompts that hit the TTFB timeout (R-5). — note: TTFB failover bound TTFB_TIMEOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 (D-005) at gateway.ts:411, enforced by maxTtfbTimeouts in request-kernel.ts:1139; tests request-kernel.test.ts:506 and gateway-egress-circuit.test.ts:546. Code audit seq 4 verified.\n- **P-005** `done` Wake fan-out pacing at the source: coordinate WI-6554700010009434 with su-1192cdb1, or take it over if stalled (R-6). — note: Implemented by su-2ba0d6ac under WI-6554700010009434 (closed 2026-10-14T06:01Z): durable bulk wake pacing, burst of 5 then one wake per 6s per workspace (wake-fanout-pacing.ts:8-9, reserveWakeFanout at :69), applied to inbox wakes (inbox-wake.ts:343) and awaited-event fan-out (events/await/store.ts:2195). WI-6554700010011426 closed. durable source: docs/evidence/gateway-admission-congestion-only-2026-10-13/live-admission-operational-2026-10-14.json\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Transport/TTFB failures count as congestion only when sustained across distinct requests\nDate: 2026-10-14\nContext: R-1(b) asks that transport/TTFB failures shrink the window only \"while uploads are measurably slow\". The gateway has no per-request upload-duration signal today, and the two observed incidents differ by population, not per-request shape: on 10-12 thousands of DISTINCT requests timed out during a mass resume; on 10-13 a few very large prompts timed out repeatedly while failing over.\n\nDecision: each request contributes at most ONE unit of congestion pressure across all of its failover attempts (deduped by request id), and the window contracts only once pressure from at least the contraction threshold of distinct requests accumulates net of successes. That is the measurable proxy for \"uploads are slow\": many unrelated requests failing at once. A lone slow prompt can never contract the window by itself.\n\nConsequence: P-003 (release the slot once the body is sent) still removes streaming from the slot accounting; if a direct upload-throughput signal is later added it can replace this proxy without changing the classifier contract.\nRelated: P-001, P-002\n\n### D-002 — Work split: the Codex-slowness fix agent owns P-001/P-002; su-b70be62e owns P-003, P-004 and P-007\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAvi put a second agent on the Codex-slowness work (owner directives #1833, #1835) while su-b70be62e carries this plan to shipped (#1833). To avoid two agents editing the same code:\n- The Codex-slowness fix agent (brief: /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/briefs/codex-slowness-fix-WI-6554700010011426.md) owns P-001 and P-002, their regression tests within P-006, and WI-6554700010011426. Its edits stay in provider-admission-lifecycle.ts and the recordThrottle/recordHardFailure/recordSuccess call sites in gateway.ts.\n- su-b70be62e owns P-003 (the admission run wrapper in gateway.ts), P-004 (the failover loop), the remaining P-006 tests, and P-007 (restart, live verification, acceptance, shipping).\n- P-005 is WI-6554700010009434 (a separate brief at /home/marsh-office/.papercusp/briefs/wake-fanout-pacing-WI-6554700010009434.md).\ngateway.ts is shared; file locks serialize edits. Restructuring outside your own region needs a coord:send to the other owner first.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: amend-177053dbe3b5ed7a3b217b4f\nRequest-Hash: a0d364f03d56f6b055d36669cfe8cb57f36246c030a14032fb77c5c7d4e62f15\nActor: su-b70be62e-7c14-4c72-a7ca-51149ea0eb32\nReason: Split four compound bars into one-behaviour bars taken verbatim from the plan's requirement conditions (R-2, R-3, R-5, R-7). Every clause the old bars carried survives as a numbered falsifier in that criterion's driftMarkers. Revised after amendment review thread-post:1179714 (WI-6554700010011465): R-5 driftMarkers now also break on no client error after the bound and on every eligible account being attempted; R-7 names its four recurrence scenarios (herd contracts and queues, large-prompt first-byte timeouts leave the window open, N failovers add pressure once, out-of-usage 429 leaves the window unchanged) inside the criterion, matching its unchanged intent, instead of pointing at Product shaping. Revised again after thread-post:1179755: R-3 driftMarkers add (3) an admitted request's slot (or byte budget) released before its request body has finished uploading, so the 'pace uploads' half of the old bar keeps a falsifier; evidenced by the new upload-hold case in gateway-openai-proxy.test.ts.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-b069d853-1cc6-4d43-9150-b9f3d99abf8c\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1179794\nApproved-At: 2026-10-14T02:43:33.252Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 17 → 18\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-3, R-5, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-004 — R-3 release-for-stream applies to remote provider lanes only; the per-account governor still bounds concurrency\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAs built (P-003). A streaming response hands its lane admission slot back at the request kernel's commit point: the response is committed and no further attempt can be chosen. Only the remote provider-lane controller implements `releaseForStream` (gateway.ts ~10576-10582). A LOCAL lane omits it on purpose, because a local model's streaming IS the GPU work its slot paces. Releasing the lane slot does NOT release the per-account governor slot (`gov.acquire`): Claude per-account concurrency is still bounded while the stream relays (gateway.ts ~7067-7071). The self-heal in-flight registry entry leaves with the lane slot, so the registry stays a subset of held slots. Until the commit point the slot is held through the whole upload: R-3 falsifier (3), evidenced by the upload-hold case in gateway-openai-proxy.test.ts. Why: the owner asked to 'pace the uploads (bytes being sent), not the number of requests in flight' [owner:Avi #1831]. A streaming response sends no request bytes, so holding a slot for it only throttled requests. A local lane has no upload cost to pace and is GPU-bound, so it keeps its slot.\n\n### D-005 — R-5 first-byte (TTFB) timeout bound: 2 per request; Claude's stall-absorb is not re-entered past it\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAs built (P-004). `TTFB_TIMEOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2` (gateway.ts:411). The request kernel takes it as `policy.maxTtfbTimeouts` and stops failing over once that many attempts in a run have timed out on first byte. It then returns the error to the client (request-kernel.ts ~1139; tests request-kernel.test.ts:506 plus a CONTROL at :516). Claude lane: the bound is per REQUEST across kernel passes. `ttfbTimeoutsUsed` is carried between passes, each pass gets max(1, 2 - used) (gateway.ts ~7049), and the stall-absorb rung is NOT re-entered once the bound is spent (gateway.ts ~7972). Codex lane: the bound is per kernel pass (gateway.ts ~9046, ~10171), because the Codex path makes a single failover pass per request. Why: on 10-13, one large uncached prompt that timed out on first byte was uploaded to every account in turn. Each upload counted as fresh lane pressure and collapsed the window. A bound of 2 still lets one failover recover from a single slow account, but one request can no longer burn the pool (R-5 falsifiers 1-3).\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: amend-d7e3f48579b76497533e07bf\nRequest-Hash: 0b6f10c5d67daeff6d4f52ee6212d062c8bebf202b7b721c6ef4f5bea371c8bb\nActor: su-b70be62e-7c14-4c72-a7ca-51149ea0eb32\nReason: Grading-integrity audit EI-25935743320595356 failed the vetting attestation: R-3's bar omitted D-004's remote-lane-only scope; R-4 restated the diff instead of an outcome (restated as provider-lane outcome parity); R-7 named scenarios without requiring they fail on the pre-fix behaviour (rescoped to incident cases that fail under each scenario's named regression). Every prior falsifier clause survives.\nApproved-By: su-68b3361b-419c-406b-a0ce-b140a59746ff\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1180326\nApproved-At: 2026-10-14T07:27:43.084Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 31 → 32\nChanged BARs: R-3, R-4, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: amend-r3-claude-lane-test-2026-10-14\nRequest-Hash: fa4215648b1a8a0cc5513d0266b3e5ebc9adf8d058f5402b0aa3a7c2e083a830\nActor: su-b70be62e-7c14-4c72-a7ca-51149ea0eb32\nReason: Additive: R-3's check gains the claude-lane test gateway-claude-stream-release.test.ts, so both remote provider lanes named in the bar (claude and codex) carry a direct test. No existing file, case or falsifier is removed.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-3)\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 32 → 33\nChanged BARs: R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-008 — P-002's 'floor sized to healthy accounts' clause completed late; contraction never takes a lane below its healthy-account count\nDate: 2026-10-14\nDate: 2026-10-14\nFound by the rev-4 rubric vetting (consult conv-mv7t5z56, post 1180421): P-002 was marked done, but its as-built used one static floor (DEFAULT_AIMD_FLOOR = 4, gateway.ts:484) for both lanes, so 'a floor sized to healthy accounts' was never implemented.\nDecision: completed under WI-6554700010012367. ProviderAdmissionLifecycle takes `healthyAccountsFor(lane)`; a contraction never takes a lane below max(configured floor, live healthy-account count). It is read at contraction time only and never raises a window; null, zero, NaN or a throwing reader leave the configured floor in charge. gateway.ts wires claude = serviceableHealthyCount() and codex = codexServiceableCount(codexPool) + codexServiceableCount(codexCliPool), the same readers /stats publishes. snapshotFor().minimumWindow reports the effective floor.\nEvidence: provider-admission-lifecycle.test.ts 'never contracts a lane below its count of healthy accounts' and 'treats an unknown, zero or throwing healthy-account reader as the configured floor' (both lanes); suite 49/49, run 21240683; copy-out mutant (contraction ignores the floor) CAUGHT, ledger test_runs:21241709 vs baseline 21241193.\nConsequence: R-2 gains driftMarker (5) in the rev-5 amendment. Live only after the gateway restart in P-007.\n\n### D-009 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-14\nAmendment-Id: gateway-recovery-atomic-approved-1180902-rev4-to5\nRequest-Hash: 8a73d60a6afe1d1702a8b68549257a860570a8918fb87a17d68c5bbe1e869f29\nActor: su-2564a37a-107c-48a0-a6fe-d97929063a1f\nReason: Address complete rev4 critique with atomic outcomes: keep R3 stream/upload behavior on tree, move its queueWait marker to R8, and independently retain P007 short-turn and Claude latency targets as R9/R10. R2 floor marker, explicit R5 bound2 and directed-wake R6 marker preserved. Each live bar names one executable test case.\nApproved-By: su-5afb70a1-95af-46dc-a865-db3326d5f871\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1180902\nApproved-At: 2026-10-14T10:06:34.985Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 36 → 37\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-3, R-5, R-6, R-8, R-9, R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-2, R-3, R-5, R-6\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010011659 — Shared outcome classifier for both lanes: account-scoped (out-of-usage, weekly wall, auth), lane congestion (a transient 429 that cannot be routed around; a transport failure while uploads are slow),… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010011660 — Contraction policy: once per request across failovers; sustained-pressure threshold for hard failures; gentler fraction; floor sized to healthy accounts; faster recovery when the queue is deep (R-2). <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010011661 — Pace uploads, not requests: measure whether the admission slot is held through streaming; release it after the body is written, or gate on bytes in flight (R-3). <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010011662 — Bound failover of large uncached prompts that hit the TTFB timeout (R-5). <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010011663 — Wake fan-out pacing at the source: coordinate WI-6554700010009434 with su-1192cdb1, or take it over if stalled (R-6). <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010011664 — Regression tests for scenarios 1-4 in the gateway / provider-admission Vitest suites (R-7). <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010011665 — Ship: restart the gateway; verify live Codex queueWait p50 < 2s, a short Codex turn < 30s, and Claude unchanged; close WI-6554700010011426. <!-- P-007 -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"grading-integrity","title":"Grading integrity — audit of a terminal scorecard's grading (grade-the-grader, D-004)","status":"active","created":"2026-10-14","owner":"su-1b950fbc-44eb-4ba3-a149-f341d97add25","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Grading integrity — audit of a terminal scorecard's grading (grade-the-grader, D-004)\nslug: grading-integrity\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-14\nupdated: 2026-10-14\nowner: su-1b950fbc-44eb-4ba3-a149-f341d97add25\n---\n\n# Grading integrity — audit of a terminal scorecard's grading (grade-the-grader, D-004)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`draft` ⇒ a proposed rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nP-013 of goal-mode-design-intent-hardening-2026-08-16 [owner-endorsed D-004]. Grades a GRADING, not a subject: the audit scorecard's subject is a TERMINAL standard-rubric scorecard ({ kind:'scorecard', ref:'<issueId>' }), and scorecards:emit enforces auditor ≠ the graded card's author (mirror of the acceptance grader ≠ author rule), settles the graded card's gradingAudit stamp passed/failed from the audit's ratings, and never stamps the audit card itself (one level deep — nobody grades the auditor). Criteria are the five measured grading-failure classes from the WI-39348 graded run plus a degenerate-distribution check. METHOD DISCIPLINE (D-004 bound 3): the audit is SAMPLED evidence re-runs — re-run the probes behind every fail/severe rating plus N random others — never a full re-derivation of the grading; downgrade errors are the expensive ones (they drive enforcement changes), so the fail/severe set is always in the sample.\n\nRevision note 2026-10-02 (WI-10005198, from WI-10005180 / owner directives #1240/#1241): base-rate-check is now symmetric. Downgrades still need a satisfiability showing, and passes resting on a zero count now need a trigger census or a compliance artifact. No criterion was added or removed, so in-flight audit skeletons keep the same keys.\n\nRevision note rev 9 (2026-10-02, WI-10005198, review su-32d1b8df 01:28Z): base-rate-check no longer contradicts itself on the no-trigger case. An absence-based pass on a positive-duty criterion is honest only with a positive compliance artifact; a no-trigger census means unknown (not exercised). Prohibition criteria pass on a zero violation count when the card states instrument coverage. The drill lexicon adds did not / never / not once. No criterion added or removed.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"inference-api-key-and-web-tools-2026-10-14","title":"Anthropic API-key settings and web-tool adoption analysis","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Anthropic API-key settings and web-tool adoption analysis\nslug: inference-api-key-and-web-tools-2026-10-14\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-14\nupdated: 2026-10-14\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: Avi and Papercusp users configuring inference and agent web research.\nProblem: Inference links Claude subscriptions but cannot add an Anthropic Console API key through settings. Search settings expose an OMP-specific provider list, while the actual reusable web-reading capabilities are unclear.\nOutcome: Add an Anthropic API-key account next to existing accounts, label paid usage, preserve the gateway's existing billing policy, remove the old search-provider settings section without deleting credentials, and deliver a cited adoption analysis.\nNon-goals: No new web-search provider integration, crawler, paid research run, credential migration, deployment control, or account routing redesign.\nSource turns: session_turn:codex:01a13ab4-4a1d-7130-a3cd-47f1337cc983:1, :3, :7. Avi chose route A (this session) in the current conversation.\nScenarios: A user opens Inference, chooses Anthropic API key, enters an account id/key, sees its paid API identity in the list, and can keep using the existing Max accounts. A user asks for a page summary and is directed to existing readers plus documents:read rather than a duplicate implementation.\n\n## Now\nRoute A approved. Reuse the account pool and apikey:file credential resolver. Inspect existing document tools and current primary web sources.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Add API account.** Inference accepts a Console API key through an explicit entry alongside Claude/Codex accounts, stores it privately outside the repository, and registers it with API-key authentication.\n**R-2 — Explain billing and protect secrets.** Label API-credit billing and existing overflow behavior, distinguish API credentials from subscription tokens, clear secret drafts when switching modes, and never echo keys in responses.\n**R-3 — Preserve existing accounts.** Browser login, setup-token, and Codex registration continue working, with meaningful frontend and route regression tests.\n**R-4 — Retire OMP settings.** Remove the OMP search-provider section from settings while preserving its stored credentials and other key settings.\n**R-5 — Research adoption.** Inventory page reading/summarization already implemented; search current primary sources; recommend tool APIs and wholesale adoption versus adapters or our own small implementation; publish and read back an owner-visible analysis.\n\n## Design\nExtend the existing registration endpoint and Inference form; use credentialRef apikey:file and the existing credential resolver/account-pool policy. No additional durable tool or credential store. Use existing reports library for the research deliverable.\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Implementation and research\n- **P-001** `done` Implement Anthropic Console API-key registration in Inference and remove the OMP-only search settings section; verify focused frontend and route tests. importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010012937 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `todo` Inventory existing tools, research web alternatives, and publish a cited recommendation with explicit adoption/build choices. importance: normal\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Execute here; research before adopting providers\nAvi approved implementation and route A. Search research is authorized; implementing a new search integration is outside this change.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"papercusp-app-performance","title":"Papercusp application performance","status":"active","created":"2026-10-14","owner":"su-7faf0bc9-ae87-43cd-9e24-6d1987c31883","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercusp application performance\nslug: papercusp-app-performance\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-14\nupdated: 2026-10-15\nowner: su-7faf0bc9-ae87-43cd-9e24-6d1987c31883\n---\n\n# Papercusp application performance\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). No prior passing cases may replay. HTTP acceptance remains independently unresolved.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"rubric-rescore-native-adoption-2026-10-14","title":"Hourly native code-intelligence adoption re-score from the results ledger","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Hourly native code-intelligence adoption re-score from the results ledger\nslug: rubric-rescore-native-adoption-2026-10-14\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-14\nupdated: 2026-10-14\n---\n## Product shaping\nAudience: Avi and the native code-intelligence plan executor.\nProblem: native tools must be measured for actual use and the frozen good-use target.\nOutcome: an hourly deterministic re-score reads the results ledger and emits exact criterion-regression events without creating a second scheduler or measurement store.\nNon-goals: no separate scheduler, agent turn, measurement table, or movement of D-011's target; no takeover of parent P-033 implementation or its deployed acceptance.\nSource: native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09 P-033, D-009/D-011, R-30/R-31; Avi-directed continuation of session 1136a865-7edb-4a6f-80a2-64e32b2248e0; current owner assignment to execute this carrier.\nScenario: every hour, measure the completed trailing 72-hour window in the rubric's canonical workspace. Insufficient samples remain unknown. A pass-to-fail criterion crossing injects an exact event-key notice. Final D-011 matched post-intervention comparison remains independently owned by the parent acceptance lane.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Deterministic hourly carrier.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Reuse the approved hourly deterministic carrier\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The persisted plan schedule and its one materialized routine are active, UTC FREQ=HOURLY, concurrency skip/catchup skip-old, and target system:rubric-rescore with the exact parent rubric input.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Inactive, duplicate or differently configured plan/routine; any system:plan-run cloning instead of deterministic rescore.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read the exact plan/routine join scoped to papercusp-workspace/papercusp; compare schedule, trigger_config, target_role, payload_template, active and fire history. Run the existing materialization/arming tests.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/arm-schedule.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/arm-plan-schedule.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Ledger-backed regression signal.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Measure native use on the existing ledger and report criterion regression\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The scheduled rescore reuses native R30/R31 instrument bindings and the test_runs results ledger; a regression is a measured pass-to-fail crossing only.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A scheduled fire omits native instrument rows, treats unknown/error as pass, or emits a crossing for unknown/error.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\",\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read exact r-30:instrument/r-31:instrument ledger paths and the routine result; distinguish scheduler output from deployed parent acceptance. Use existing rescore and ledger integration tests for detector behavior.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/rubric-rescore-schedule.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/check-results-ledger.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Independent acceptance boundary.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Preserve parent P033 ownership and fixed D011 comparison\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Carrier completion records that parent R30/R31 remain independently owned and require release-operator SHA/intervention proof plus the unchanged D011 matched72h window; no parent bar is graded by this task.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Carrier evidence is presented as parent R30/R31 outcome acceptance, the frozen target moves, or the live parent claim is taken.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"operational\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Probe the exact frozen D011 decision body and release-operator runtime declaration for R30/R31 in the active parent rubric. Read parent WI-6554700010012122 claim/checkpoint and record the boundary; carrier completion must not grade or change those outcomes.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"probe\",\n      \"probe\": {\n        \"kind\": \"tool\",\n        \"tool\": \"plans:get\",\n        \"schemaRevision\": \"live\",\n        \"args\": {\n          \"harness\": \"papercusp\",\n          \"slug\": \"native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09\",\n          \"decisionId\": \"D-011\",\n          \"projection\": {\n            \"pick\": [\n              \"results[].decisions[].id\",\n              \"results[].decisions[].body\"\n            ]\n          }\n        },\n        \"expect\": {\n          \"path\": \"$.results[0].decisions[0].body\",\n          \"op\": \"eq\",\n          \"value\": \"Date: 2026-10-14\\nDate: 2026-10-14\\nAgent-derived [self-imposed] under D-009 (AUTO) and R-31's constraint that the target is frozen from the baseline before any intervention.\\n\\nInstrument: packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/native-adoption.ts (version 1), keys code-intel:native-adoption-measured / code-intel:native-adoption-good-use. Measured with that same instrument on the live ledgers. Raw output: /tmp/p033-baseline.json (scratch, not durable). The numbers are restated here.\\n\\nBaseline window: [2026-10-11T06:00Z, 2026-10-14T06:00Z), 72h, workspace papercusp-workspace. No P-033 intervention had shipped.\\n- lookups 1857 by 350 agents. Native ok 129 of 158 calls (refused 28, all judge role; lsp:query refused 27/51). GitNexus direct 11. Raw-text lookups 1688 (660 definition, 1028 call-site) by 311 agents.\\n- agent adoption 0.060 (21/350); native call share 0.0706; refusal rate 0.177.\\n- Reported but not gated: follow-through proxy 0.054 (7/129); p50 latency lsp:query 11.7s, graph:query 4.7s, code:pack 1.6s.\\n\\nTarget rule (fixed now, never adjusted afterwards): double agent adoption, double native call share, halve the refusal rate. The sample floor is a quarter of baseline lookups.\\n- minAgentAdoptionRate 0.12; minNativeCallShare 0.14; maxRefusalRate 0.088; minLookups 464.\\n\\nComparison: one 72h post-intervention window, equal in length to the baseline. It starts after the interventions are live on the deployed operator (:3070) and is measured on the deployed ledgers. A miss is reported as fail; too few lookups is reported as inconclusive (unknown). The target is not moved.\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Cheap exact watch.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Subscribe to native rubric regression through the existing watch mechanism\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Supported watch:create returns a standing event subscription for the exact parent rubric criterion-regressed key with wake false and no expiry.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Different key/kind, a model wake/polling loop, or absent subscription receipt.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Read the watch:create receipt and idempotently verify the exact event subscription; existing event-subscriptions tests guard update/delivery semantics.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/event-subscriptions.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\nReuse `plans:set-schedule` → `plans:arm-schedule` and the registered `rubric-rescore` action. The saved schedule is UTC hourly with skip concurrency and skip-old catch-up. The action uses existing instrument/check/probe seams and results-ledger rows; no bespoke storage is allowed. The exact watch is a standing event-key inbox subscription.\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | live |\n| R-2 | P-001 | live |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Carrier preparation and verification\n- **P-001** `todo` Verify the saved UTC hourly rubric-rescore action schedule is active, skip-concurrent, skip-old, and has a fire record; preserve the existing executor and ledger boundaries. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Register and verify the exact wake:false criterion-regressed event watch; record the subscription receipt and key. importance: normal blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Record independent acceptance and shipment boundary: R-30/R-31 require release-operator deployed-ledger evidence and remain on parent P-033 owner WI-6554700010012122; do not claim those bars from carrier evidence. importance: high blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Carrier operational verification passed: exact saved/materialized hourlyUTC schedule active; R30/R31 ledger rows21247000(pass)/21247001(fail), exact wake:false standing event watch registered,38focused tests pass. Preparation repaired with activation audit1 and4 active clauses; admission currently fails atomicity of projected R2/R3 condition.\n\n**Next:** Repair canonical R2/R3 criterion models through rubrics:amend; preserve original behavior/proof boundaries, re-audit current plan meaning, re-evaluate and emit exact spec-quality scorecard, then plans:start and evidence-qualified P001/P002/P003 closeout. Parent P033 release-operator outcome remains independent.\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Carrier reuses existing action and schedule seams\nThe deterministic `rubric-rescore` action is the only measurement executor. No second scheduler, measurement table, or agent turn is introduced.\n### D-002 — Parent acceptance remains independent\nR-30/R-31 are active rubric revision 11 criteria with release-operator and frozen-window requirements. Carrier evidence is preparatory and cannot close parent P-033.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"spec-conformance-loop-2026-10-14","title":"Spec-conformance loop: stop plan-spec → implementation drift universally","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-14","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Spec-conformance loop: stop plan-spec → implementation drift universally\nslug: spec-conformance-loop-2026-10-14\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-10-14\nupdated: 2026-10-14\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-14, after item-dropped): bar_snapshot_rubric_unresolved. Between writing and shipping nothing ties each action back to the spec. When an agent meets something the spec did not anticipate (an unmeetable constraint, a new request, a tool that behaves differently), it silently follows its default behaviour. Today's guards are authored but not executable (requirement `check` = none), evaluated too late (ship time), scoped to plan items while work leaks in through side directives, and satisfied by artifacts rather than by the spec.\n\n**Outcome:** For every plan, (1) each requirement compiles to an executable check at activation; (2) checks run during execution and a failure raises a drift alarm that halts dependent work; (3) all work touching the plan's declared footprint is linked to a plan item or flagged; (4) an unmeetable requirement can only be handled by an explicit, approved deviation (spec amendment) before acting; (5) item/directive closure names the requirements it discharges and their checks must be green; (6) an independent periodic spec-vs-implementation review covers what cannot be mechanised.\n\n**Non-goals:** a new parallel review system; replacing ship-time grading (it stays as the final gate); per-agent branch isolation.\n\n**Reuse-first:** requirement `verification.check`, rubric checks + `plans:set-schedule {system:'rubric-rescore'}` + `watch:create rubric:criterion-regressed`, plan Decisions, work-item ↔ plan links, completion evidence, `work_items:set_blocker`. The change makes these mandatory and execution-time, enforced at existing chokepoints (plans:audit activation, work_items:complete, orders:disposition, admission/dispatch).\n\n**Relationship:** `spec-driven-tooling-integration-2026-10-05` (draft, awaiting Avi's scope approval) proposes a converge loop, claim-time context and a frozen-test pilot. Frozen tests are one form of item 1/2 below. Avi chose to keep the plans separate (D-001). Boundary: this plan owns the general check-at-close (R-8/R-9 closure guard) and execution-time drift alarms; the Oct-5 plan's frozen-test completion check (its P-022) and claim-time context pack (its P-020) build on these surfaces instead of adding parallel ones.\n\n**Source turns:** owner directive #1849 (take over, why drift, prevent recurrence) and #1855 (\"im looking for a general solution that solves this universally\"). Trigger case: slack-asana-reproduced-bug-fix-pr-workflow-2026-10-08#D-015; postmortem report rpt_020718f9-d6f4-42a8-b217-c7cfdfa408fc.\n\n**Scenarios:** A requirement authored with no check is refused at activation (or carries a loud `unenforced` flag Avi approved). A commit that violates a requirement's falsifier trips a drift alarm on the plan within minutes and blocks the affected items. A side directive that edits a plan's footprint without a plan link is flagged. An agent that cannot meet a requirement files a deviation and is refused if it tries to complete the item without an approved one. A directive cannot be closed `done` citing only a URL.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Unenforced requirements are refused at activation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Every requirement the trigger selection.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/spec-conformance/sweep-action.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Architecture\n\nOne module, `packages/operator-core/lib/spec-conformance/`, extends existing surfaces instead of adding a parallel system:\n\n- **Contract.** A plan declares its execution-time contract in a `## Conformance` section holding one fenced `conformance` JSON block: an optional `footprint` (repo-relative path globs) and, per requirement key, `violatedWhen` falsifiers and an optional `unenforced` declaration. The done-when check stays the requirement block's existing `verification.check`. Falsifiers live outside the BAR hash, so adding one never forces a rubric amendment.\n- **Falsifier checks** reuse `rubricCriterionCheckSchema` (`probe`, `instrument`, `tests`). A falsifier whose interface does not exist yet is authored as `pendingBinding { observation, bindWhen }`, which counts as enforced-pending and is listed as unbound by the report, never silently `none`. A check asserts the requirement holds; a `fail` verdict is the falsifier firing.\n- **Activation gate (R-1).** `plans:audit { phase:'activation' }` refuses `conformance_requirement_unenforced` when a requirement has no executable done-when check (absent or `instrumentKey:'none'`), no falsifier and no `unenforced { reason, approvalRef }`.\n- **Conformance run (R-2–R-4).** Evaluates probe/instrument falsifiers through the rubric-rescore machinery, judges `tests` falsifiers from the test-run ledger, re-scores the acceptance rubric's done-when checks, and records every verdict in the results ledger under `conformance:<harness>/<plan>`. A firing falsifier or a done-when pass→fail opens one deduplicated drift-alarm work-item per requirement (identity in `payload.specConformance`), links it `blocks` to every non-terminal work-item mapped to that requirement through the Bar-to-work map, and emits `plan:drift-alarm:<slug>`. An alarm whose checks return green is closed, releasing the blocks. An approved deviation suppresses the alarm for its requirement.\n- **Footprint (R-5).** The sweep reads commits since the plan's watermark that touch footprint globs. A path is covered when a work-item linked to the plan names it in completion `filesChanged` or holds its file lock. Uncovered paths are recorded on one open out-of-plan finding work-item per plan, assigned to the plan driver.\n- **Deviation (R-7).** `plans:conformance { op:'propose-deviation' }` records a Decision carrying a fenced `deviation` block. `op:'approve-deviation'` records the approving Decision. An owner-sourced requirement (owner refs in `intent.sourceRefs`) needs an `ownerTurnRef` that the turn-provenance ledger verifies as an owner turn.\n- **Closure (R-6, R-8, R-9, R-11).** `work_items:complete` for a work-item whose plan item maps to requirements must carry `completion.discharges` and/or `completion.contributesTo` (R-N keys among its mapped requirements). Each discharged requirement's executable done-when check must last have passed. An open drift alarm on a mapped requirement refuses closure without an approved deviation. A conformance-review work-item cannot be closed by a plan implementer.\n- **Directive evidence (R-10).** `orders:disposition { status:'done' }` refuses a note that is only URLs.\n- **Independent review (R-11).** `system:spec-conformance-review` (plan-schedulable) files one conformance-review work-item per plan, recording the implementer set it excludes.\n- **Continuity (R-12, R-13).** `system:spec-conformance-sweep` runs on a recurring routine across active/ready plans with requirements. It runs a plan when its footprint changed, a linked work-item transitioned, or its interval elapsed, and stores the watermark in `harness_shared.spec_conformance_state`. `plans:conformance { op:'report' }` is the retro-fit census.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-018 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-018 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-018 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-019 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-021 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-020 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-021 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-021 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-021 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-022 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-023 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-023 | tree |\n\n## Conformance\n\n```conformance\n{\"footprint\":{\"paths\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/spec-conformance/**\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/conformance.ts\"]},\"requirements\":{\"R-10\":{\"violatedWhen\":[{\"id\":\"url-only-done-disposition\",\"failureMode\":\"a directive closed done on a bare URL\",\"stage\":\"delivery\",\"pendingBinding\":{\"observation\":\"an owner directive disposed done after activation whose note is only URLs\",\"bindWhen\":\"P-021 lands the disposition evidence guard\"}}]}}}\n```\n\n## Origin proposal\n\nThe seven proposed items from the 2026-10-14 draft became P-017…P-023; their full wording is in plan revision 5.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Spec-conformance loop\n\n- **P-017** `done` Conformance contract + activation gate (R-1).
