Missing, stale, hostless, malformed, incomplete or ambiguous evidence is non-pass; a floor breach or failed/incomplete run fails.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"storage:durable-headroom-targets-72h\"},\"replication\":\"Use the maintained measureDurableHeadroomTargets and assessDurableHeadroomTargets adapter plus rubric-instrument-registry platform rescore seam. Preserve native census/start/receipt and predecessor-disposition identity; retain the conventional retention-interval-evidence tests for exact-floor positive controls, middle dips, missing census hours, vanished/silent runs, incomplete receipts, failed delegates, host mismatch, duplicate/unsorted samples and unfinished windows. No sparse sample set or empty receipt population may pass.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nReuse, not a parallel system: the existing hourly disk census (`harness_shared.disk_census_*`), the disk alarm, the written policy (`packages/operator-core/lib/storage/retention-policy.ts`) and the standing reclaim actor (`packages/operator-core/lib/storage/disk-reclaim.ts`) stay the only census, policy and deleter. The change is in what they enforce. Today the policy defaults to keep: an unmatched path is never deleted, so every new agent folder lands in \"keep\". This plan inverts the default for agent-owned parents only. A path under a known agent parent that no class names expires after 72 h; owner and system roots stay explicit keep classes, and `validatePolicy` keeps refusing any deletable root under an owner root (D-002 of the superseded plan carries over).\n\nThe cold tier is plain XFS on the two HDDs, mounted by UUID with `nofail` so a missing disk never blocks boot. Backups go to cold-a (sda), and owner copies go to cold-b (sdb), so no single HDD holds both.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002, P-003 | live |\n| R-2 | P-004 | live |\n| R-3 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-008 | deployed |\n| R-7 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-010 | live |\n| R-9 | P-011 | deployed |\n| R-10 | P-012 | live |\n\n## Phase 0 — Emergency and cold tier\n\n- **P-001** `done` Emergency root offload: move idle agent copies (38 GB cargo-target under `~/.papercusp/evidence/p005-native8-audit-*`) to `/mnt/bench/root-offload-2026-10-15` with verify, then a symlink back; move, never delete; log and MANIFEST in that directory. — note: move.log EXIT=0 13:41:58Z: 56870 entries / 37845832430 bytes verified, source replaced by symlink; root 20G to 55G free; git-sync fetch reserve (40.3G) cleared\n- **P-002** `done` Format sda2 (5.84 TB, random bytes only, owner-approved 13:18Z) as XFS `cold-a`; fstab UUID + nofail; mount at `/mnt/cold-a`; GPT backed up to `/mnt/bench/root-offload-2026-10-15/sda-gpt-backup.bin`.\n- **P-003** `done` sdb: back up the MBR, convert MBR→GPT in place (`sgdisk -g`; sdb1/sdb2 keep their sectors), create sdb3 on the 5.85 TB tail (start 4207996928), format XFS `cold-b`, add an fstab UUID + nofail entry, mount at `/mnt/cold-b`. Leave sdb1 untouched. — note: sdb MBR to GPT (sdb1/sdb2 sectors unchanged); sdb3 4207996928..15628053134 XFS cold-b UUID b5c448f8-2a7a-49ae-9424-06d3f5cfe523 mounted /mnt/cold-b, fstab nofail (backup /etc/fstab.bak-2026-10-15-coldb). Pre-change MBR + first/last MiB in /mnt/cold-a/meta/disk-layout-2026-10-15/\n- **P-004** `done` Move cold bulk from `/mnt/data` to the cold tier: kopia repo (2.7 TB) and papercusp-backups (0.2 TB) to cold-a; owner `Debug*`/`back` (364 GB) to cold-b. rsync, verify, swap, then remove the source. Repoint kopia/backup routines and the retention-policy roots, and prove one backup run after the move. — note: ← WI-6554700010014784 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 1 — Expire by default\n\n- **P-005** `done` Extend `packages/operator-core/lib/storage/retention-policy.ts`: an agent-root default of max-age 72 h, a build-dir rule of 24 h for `node_modules` and `target`, and unclassified agent paths under known agent parents defaulting to expire. Owner/system stays an explicit keep list. Tests in `retention-policy.test.ts`. — note: ← WI-6554700010014936 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Pins: owner, reason, expiry. Tests. — note: ← WI-6554700010014939 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Postgres retention\n\n- **P-010** `blocked` 30-day retention for `tool_invocations`, routing and telemetry tables. Close disk-headroom-standing-reclaim-2026-10-12 as superseded, absorb WI-10007751, and fold in plan durable-disk-and-checkpoint-recovery-2026-10-09.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — R-3 scope: ~/.papercusp is mixed state, not an expire-by-default parent; its run output is matched by name\nDate: 2026-10-15\nContext: R-3 says unclassified agent paths under known agent parents default to expiring. ~/.papercusp has 584 top-level entries. A code-reference derivation (ripgrep over packages/apps/libs/scripts/bin/papercusp-desktop plus ~/.claude, ~/.codex and systemd user units) found 219 names referenced neither exactly nor by stem, and that set includes credentials and live state: aws-console-login, gcloud-auth, marketplace-keys, pglite-data, desktop-wal-backups, private-native-offline-home. Read-only files such as db-encryption-key (May) and claude-token (June) are older than 72 h, because reads never update mtime. Expire-by-default on ~/.papercusp would delete them.\nDecision [self-imposed, su-271cfdc6, reversible]: known agent parents are the dirs created only for agent output (scratch, tmp, evidence, artifacts, a checkout's .papercusp scratch/tmp/vitest-tmp/tsx-*/node-compile-cache/spawn-results, offload work copies). Every path under them that no narrower class claims inherits their 72 h expiry. ~/.papercusp stays keep by default, and its run output is matched by naming convention instead (class papercusp-home-run-dirs): plan-item prefixes (p046-...), work-item ids (wi7747, EI-...) and date stamps. Names that look like a backup, key, credential, login, signing, custody or password never match. wh-release-* dirs are review, because the release tool exports their evidence first. A checkout's .papercusp outside those agent roots (blueprint.yaml, memory, state, dependency-generations, worktrees) is harness state and stays keep.\nOwner basis: turn session_turn:claude:956a3058-a3e5-440a-ba0d-68f4f36bc6ed:9 (\"3 days\" for agent-made folders, pins for longer). Close disk-headroom-standing-reclaim-2026-10-12 as superseded, absorb WI-10007751, and fold in plan durable-disk-and-che… <!-- P-012 -->\n\n\n## Conformance\n\nExecutable native checks replace the three pending interfaces under WI-6554700010015302. Requirement acceptance conditions are unchanged.\n\n```conformance\n{\n  \"requirements\": {\n    \"R-1\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"persistent-cold-mounts\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"A required cold mount is missing, fstab is not UUID/nofail based, or either mount fails across a real reboot.\",\n          \"stage\": \"operation\",\n          \"check\": {\n            \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n            \"instrumentKey\": \"storage:cold-mounts-reboot\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-2\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"verified-cold-bulk-cutover\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"A required bulk move lacks equal entry/byte verification before source removal, a writer/reader still targets the old path, or no post-cutover backup succeeds.\",\n          \"stage\": \"operation\",\n          \"check\": {\n            \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n            \"instrumentKey\": \"storage:cold-bulk-cutover\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-10\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"exact-headroom-targets-held\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"The actual 72-hour window has a missing hourly census sample, root free below 400 GB, /mnt/data free below 2 TB, or an incomplete reclaim receipt; superseded-work disposition is missing.\",\n          \"stage\": \"operation\",\n          \"check\": {\n            \"kind\": \"instrument\",\n            \"instrumentKey\": \"storage:durable-headroom-targets-72h\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"gate-repair-plane-on-current-build-2026-10-15","title":"Gate repair control plane runs on the current build, so fixes to it don't wait behind the red they repair","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Gate repair control plane runs on the current build, so fixes to it don't wait behind the red they repair\nslug: gate-repair-plane-on-current-build-2026-10-15\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-15\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-15, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty. Next repair: Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\n- State: DRAFT, awaiting Avi's approval. No code written. [self-imposed: plan before code, per the #1920 dialog]\n- Next: on approval, P-001 (measure the map, record the executor Decision).\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi, and every agent that greens main or fixes the repair machinery.\n\n**Problem.** Measured 2026-10-15:\n- The gate's repair machinery runs on the release operator (:3070, build d740fc3802 = green main).\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/bootstrap.ts:642` arms `startGreenStallWatchdog` in DBOS bootstrap, and the idle-repair-queue actuator (`packages/operator-core/lib/release/idle-repair-queue-actuator.ts`, rungs dispatch-fixer / wake-gate-owner / escalate-owner) runs inside that watchdog.\n- `dev:pipeline_position` lists release-operator and staging-operator as owners of `green-stall-watchdog.ts`.\n- The fixer-routing code lives in `release/frozen-repair-agent-routing.ts`, `release/gate-red-ownership.ts` and `harness/routines/release-actions.ts`.\n- MCP calls to `release:repair-queue` go through the :9071 proxy, whose default upstream is :3070.\n\nSo a fix to any of these reaches the host that runs it only after main goes green, which is the outcome the machinery exists to produce.\n\n**Prior instances (the same loop, four times):**\n- WI-2143424 (2026-09-03): the freeze-and-converge fix couldn't deploy. Force-deploy was refused at live-certification, so it is not an escape.\n- WI-10002410 and WI-10002411: the frozen queue was waiting on a dead fixer.\n- WI-6554700010014878: the frozen queue sat idle for 17h.\n\n**General problem [owner #1920].** `packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/recovery-dependency-audit.ts` already checks whether each recovery mechanism can still RUN during the failure it recovers (\"fate-sharing\"). It does not check whether a FIX to that mechanism can SHIP during that failure. Code-delivery fate-sharing is the missing dimension. The gate repair plane is one instance of it; this plan fixes the instance and adds the check for the class.\n\n**Outcome.**\n- A committed change to a repair component is executing within ~10 min (staging/bg-host cadence) while main is red.\n- Exactly one host runs each repair limb.\n- The release operator still runs the suite verdict, fast-forwards main and deploys.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- Moving the verdict or promotion off the release operator.\n- Changing freeze-and-converge semantics.\n- Fixing the current red legs. Those belong to the live gate owner (su-d6d37b55) [owner:Avi #1920 \"let them take care of the fixes\"]. No LIVE_GATE_OPS in this plan.\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. Main is red and the actuator has a bug that stops it dispatching a fixer. A peer commits the fix. Within ~10 min the next actuator pass runs the fixed code and dispatches, with no green main required.\n2. Both :3070 and the current-build host are up. Only one of them dispatches a fixer per episode.\n3. The idle-repair-queue alarm files a work item. It arrives already assigned to the live gate owner, not unclaimed.\n4. Someone adds a new watchdog that recovers the gate but runs only on the release operator. The audit test fails and names the delivery dependency.\n\n## Requirements (draft; converted to BAR blocks at activation)\n- R1 Every gate-repair limb (idle-repair-queue actuator, lost-run alarm, release-fixer dispatch, repair-queue writes) executes on a runtime whose build advances without a green main. Its pass record carries the executing build sha.\n- R2 The release operator's copies of the moved limbs stand down, so they never double-act. A lease or single-executor guard enforces this, and a test proves two hosts produce one dispatch.\n- R3 `release:repair-queue` verbs execute on the current build regardless of which host the MCP call lands on.\n- R4 Alarm work items about the gate or repair queue are assigned to the live gate owner (`gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership`) at creation, and are left unassigned only when no live owner exists. [agent-proposed in the 12:49 dialog question, \"either way\"; not contested by Avi]\n- R5 `recovery-dependency-audit` gains a code-delivery dimension. Each mechanism declares its build source (release-gated or continuous). A mechanism that recovers the release gate on a release-gated build fails the audit test unless it carries a stated mitigation.\n- R6 Live proof: a harmless marker change to the actuator is observed executing (pass record build sha contains the marker commit) while main is red, before :3070 has it.\n\n## Open choice (resolved in P-001 as a Decision)\nWhich current-build host owns the repair limbs:\n- (a) bg-host. It runs from the canonical tree (`papercusp-bg-host.service`, WorkingDirectory `papercusp/apps/operator`) and restarts on its own cadence.\n- (b) The staging operator :3170. It advances about every 5 min, but restarts ~200×/day, so its leases must tolerate churn.\n\nRecommendation pending measurement: bg-host, if its restart cadence picks up commits within ~10 min. Otherwise :3170 with a DB lease.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Map and decide\n\n- **P-001** `done` Measure the repair-plane map, don't assume it. For each limb (idle-repair-queue actuator, lost-run alarm, release-fixer dispatch, repair-queue verb writes), record: the host that executes it today, the build that host runs, and how fast that build advances. Measure bg-host's commit pickup latency and :3170's. Record the executor choice (bg-host vs :3170) as a plan Decision with the numbers. importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010015277 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — Move the repair plane\n\n- **P-002** `todo` Run the repair limbs (actuator, lost-run alarm, fixer dispatch) on the chosen current-build host. Stand down the release operator's copies behind a single-executor lease. Stamp each pass record with the executing build sha. Vitest coverage: two hosts arming produce exactly one dispatch per episode, and the stood-down host does nothing. (R1, R2) blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Make release:repair-queue writes execute on the current build whichever host receives the MCP call. Either the proxy routes the verb to the current-build host, or :3070 delegates the write through a DB-queued command. Choose by P-001's measurement and record the choice as a Decision. Tests cover both the routed path and the fallback. (R3) blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Assign gate and repair-queue alarm work items to the live gate owner at creation, read from gate.greenCheckpoint.ownership. Leave them unassigned only when there is no live owner, and say so on the item. Vitest coverage for owned, unowned and stale-owner cases. (R4)\n\n\n\n## Phase 3 — Close the class\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Extend packages/operator-core/lib/system-health/recovery-dependency-audit.ts with a code-delivery dimension. Each mechanism declares its build source (release-gated or continuous). A mechanism that recovers the release gate on a release-gated build fails recovery-dependency-audit.test.ts unless it carries a stated mitigation. Prove the guard is falsifiable with scripts/mutation-probe.sh. (R5) importance: high\n\n## Phase 4 — Live proof\n\n- **P-006** `todo` Live proof while main is red: commit a harmless marker change to the actuator. Observe its pass record carrying the marker commit's build sha on the current-build host within ~10 min, while :3070 still lacks it (dev:pipeline_position servingRuntimes). Record the evidence on the plan. (R6) blocked-by: P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — P-001 executor decision: repair limbs run on current-build bg-host; release operator keeps verdict/promotion\nDate: 2026-10-15\nCorrection / false premise: my prior wording treated source ownership from dev:pipeline_position as proof of execution on the release operator. That was wrong. Measured: apps/operator/bin/host-bootstrap.ts:2180 gates startDbos on backgroundWorkers AND PAPERCUSP_DBOS_ENABLE=1; packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/bootstrap.ts:642-646 arms startGreenStallWatchdog; green-stall-watchdog.ts:3926 invokes idle-repair-queue-actuator and :3955 arms the lost-run alarm. Read-only whitelist of the actual service process environments: bg-host BG=1, DBOS_ENABLE=1, port3271; staging BG=0, DBOS_ENABLE=1, port3170; release BG=0, DBOS_ENABLE unset. Therefore these watchdog limbs already run on the continuously updated bg-host, not the release operator. The plan must not duplicate or relocate already-correct machinery. Measured bg-host build 02b32de35a committed 2026-10-15T19:54:28Z; service started 19:56:23Z from canonical staging/apps/operator: one observed pickup bound is 115 seconds, not an SLA. Staging build c2ebf8b88f and release build d740fc3802 differ. Decision: retain existing bg-host execution; finish verifying repair-queue write routing, build stamps, single-executor protection and code-delivery audit. Extend those existing seams where missing. Live gate operations remain with su-d6d37b55. P-001 continues until direct timer and staging pickup evidence and the remaining write-route map are recorded.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-002 — P-001 limb map measured: watchdog limbs on current bg-host; repair-queue writes 96% on the 13-day-old release build; fixer dispatch skips lint-only queues\nDate: 2026-10-15\nMeasured 2026-10-15 ~23:00Z by su-58cdd289; completes the evidence D-001 left open.\n\nBuilds (/api/health): :3070 release d740fc3802 (main, 13 days old); :3170 staging d5b292ed83; :3271 bg-host 3355796413 (= staging tip, committed 22:19:12Z).\n\nLimb map (journal of papercusp-bg-host / staging-api / dev-api, 6h window):\n- idle-repair-queue actuator: executes on bg-host. Direct fires 18:15:50, 19:01:48, 19:45:44, 20:30:46, 21:46:17Z (one per green-checkpoint pass). Each: dispatch-fixer=failed ('dispatcher returned no spawn; reservation released'), wake-gate-owner=acted (su-d6d37b55); 20:30 escalate-owner=acted.\n- release-fixer dispatch: executes on bg-host inside green-checkpoint. Every pass (18:15:45, 19:01:40, 19:45:40, 21:46:13Z) logged 'release-fixer dispatch skipped for 0e2f2291: frozen repair queue has no measured failing tests (failingTestsMeasured=false)'. The frozen queue holds only 7 lint-leg entries, so the automated fixer never engages a lint-only red. This is direct evidence for green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08#P-036.\n- green-stall-watchdog D-006 refire: bg-host, ~8 min cadence (22:31, 22:39, 22:46Z), advisory-only for non-home pots.\n- lost-run alarm: armed on bg-host (D-001); no matching journal line in 6h. [observation] Absence of a fire, consistent with no lost run; not proof the alarm works.\n- release:repair-queue writes: served by whichever host receives the MCP call. tool_invocations, last 12h: port-3070 d740fc3802 = 344 calls (last 22:58:59Z); port-3170 = 16 calls across 7 builds. About 96% of repair-queue writes execute on the 13-day-old release build. That is the P-003 problem, measured.\n\nPickup latency (commit -> service ActiveEnterTimestamp): bg-host 3355796413 22:19:12Z -> 22:38:45Z = 19m33s (D-001 sample: 115s; n=2, range 2-20 min). :3170 d5b292ed83 21:35:09Z -> 21:46:38Z = 11m29s, and at 22:59Z it is 11 commits behind tip (staging-sync defers while :3170 has live clients, up to 1800s).\n\nDecision: keep D-001 (watchdog, actuator and fixer-dispatch limbs stay on bg-host; no relocation). The two gaps to close are P-003 (repair-queue writes must run current-build logic regardless of the receiving host) and P-036 (lint-leg paths so fixer dispatch and admission can target lint-only reds). The actuator's 'dispatcher returned no spawn' on every fire is a third gap, not yet diagnosed.\nRelated: P-001, P-003\n\n### D-003 — Correction to D-002: 'dispatcher returned no spawn' is the lint-only refusal, not a third gap\nDate: 2026-10-15\nD-002 recorded the idle-repair-queue actuator's every-fire `dispatch-fixer=failed (dispatcher returned no spawn)` as an undiagnosed third gap. That was wrong. Re-probed 2026-10-15 23:3xZ (journalctl --user, 6h): each actuator failure is immediately preceded by `[green-checkpoint] release-fixer dispatch skipped for 0e2f2291: frozen repair queue has no measured failing tests (failingTestsMeasured=false)` (15:45:40/44, 17:46:13/17). dispatchReleaseFixer (harness/routines/release-actions.ts) deliberately returns null under the WI-2140605 guard, and the actuator (idle-repair-queue-actuator.ts:365-371) collapses every null into the generic message. Root cause = the lint-only queue carries no measured failing paths, which is the same cause as green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08#P-036. The defect that remains is that the actuator hides the reason and re-dispatches a deterministic refusal. It is filed as WI-6554700010015397. What survives from D-002: the per-limb host/build map and the pickup-latency measurements are unchanged.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"machine-first-access-and-signup-utility-download-2026-10-15","title":"Machine-first access and psu+pui signup download","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Machine-first access and psu+pui signup download\nslug: machine-first-access-and-signup-utility-download-2026-10-15\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-15\nupdated: 2026-10-18\n---\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"People using Papercusp from a browser or psu/pui on a laptop, across local, managed-cloud, BYOC and personally owned remote machines.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Machine choice is less discoverable than workspace choice; signup does not yet provide a truthful psu+pui download path and explanation; personal-machine attachment and repeated local/remote configuration need a clear journey.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"A person chooses the execution machine first, then that machine's workspace and agent context; signup makes one compatible utility request with honest fallback and GUI continuation; personal connections and release identities remain explicit.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Replacing the existing relay\",\n    \"Duplicating workspace/host registries\",\n    \"Changing provider billing\",\n    \"Automatically installing software\",\n    \"Exposing the ordinary administration port publicly\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a14187-8f38-7b83-aedf-db07205ce9af:1\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a14187-8f38-7b83-aedf-db07205ce9af:3\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a14187-8f38-7b83-aedf-db07205ce9af:11\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Provide machine switching in both portal and local GUI.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a14187-8f38-7b83-aedf-db07205ce9af:1\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"After signup request compatible psu+pui download, explain Method-only clarification; no behavior, grading or shipment claim.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive ()\nRubric revision: 9 → 10\nSubject plan revision: 28 → 29\nChanged BARs: \nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-2\n\n### D-013 — Correct D-011 approval wording for method-only changes\nDate: 2026-10-18\nMeasured: independent exact-current critique thread-post:1189022 C; complete saved rubric9→10 comparison after amendment machine-first-r2-receipt-separation-20261018-v12 changes only r-2.method, preserves all 10 BARs and barSetHash fe144b3bd77edba3e84dca89b4524da52d36d8f9b3a2e453a2979dff3654c6a5. Current packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-bar-amendment-additivity.ts:74-111 requires outside approval only when reviewedBars is nonempty; canonical v12 preview at rubric9/plan28 returned changedBars:[], reviewedBars:[], additiveBars:[], approvalRequired:false and changes:[R-2/method-only]. Its lack of required outside amendment approval rests on unchanged BAR meaning and no reviewed BAR, not a claim that every prose change was additive. This decision corrects that record; it does not attest feature behavior, grant acceptance, waive independent vetting, or claim shipment. D-012 carries the A/B procedure repair; current P006 independent adequacy audits remain pending.\nRelated: P-002, P-006\n\n### D-014 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAmendment-Id: machine-first-r5-r10-detector-contract-20261018-v2\nRequest-Hash: 1df47ec48b3a6b248f1cc4807686d3d20b639aafa76c78c9e97b4d8d8f26a61c\nActor: su-de38f55f-e1e1-45c4-a486-6a8ab84acf15\nReason: Apply exact retained v2 detector-contract delta1190862, independently approved1190878 to original preview1190856 after evidence1190866. Preserve all acceptance outcomes, R2, original prerequisite files and required layers. R5 adds evidence evaluator detectors and measured matrix requirements; R10 selects both existing plaintext refusal and sealed positive control. No feature, clean release or shipment acceptance claim.\nApproved-By: su-907e8851-10cc-4f05-818a-ad1febf41f76\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1190878\nApproved-At: 2026-10-18T13:26:49.939Z\nRubric revision: 10 → 11\nSubject plan revision: 32 → 33\nChanged BARs: R-5, R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-5, R-10\n\n## Low-level remote psu execution flow\n\n### Low-level flow\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  L[\"Laptop: terminal + local psu\"] <-->|\"WSS terminal relay\"| R[\"Papercusp cloud control plane\"]\n  R <-->|\"Host's outbound connector\"| H[\"Cloud machine: host service + remote psu\"]\n  H --> A[\"Customer account: Claude Code / Codex\"]\n  A <-->|\"Context, MCP tools, hooks\"| O[\"Papercusp operator on cloud machine\"]\n  A <-->|\"Model requests, direct or gateway-routed\"| M[\"Model provider\"]\n```\n\n1. **Local psu chooses the execution target first.** The connection front controller runs before the ordinary role, workspace, project, plan and fleet pickers. A forwarded remote launch suppresses the recursive connection picker. Choosing local continues on the laptop; choosing remote hands the terminal to a process on that target. Source: apps/operator/scripts/psu-launcher.mjs main; psu-connection-front-controller.mjs runPsuConnectionFrontController.\n\n2. **Cloud sign-in authorizes the device.** If needed, local psu requests /api/hosted/cli/device/code, opens the verification page, and polls /api/hosted/cli/device/token after you approve the code. The resulting token is bound to the signed-in user and organization and saved in the local connection profile. Separate organization/user sign-ins can coexist. It is a Papercusp access credential, not your Claude/OpenAI login. Source: psu-connection-front-controller.mjs hostedLogin.\n\n3. **The portal resolves the workspace and grants a terminal connection.** psu lists /api/hosted/cli/workspaces and selects an authorized reachable workspace. It POSTs /api/hosted/cli/workspaces/:id/terminal with a session key, program=psu and the allowed launch arguments. The server checks organization membership, workspace:operate permission and connector liveness, then issues a single-use ticket tied to the workspace, host, user, session and connector generation. Source: packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/hosted-cli/index.ts.\n\n4. **The laptop connects to a relay, and the machine connects outbound.** Local psu opens wss://<portal>/api/hosted/connectors/socket with the ticket. The cloud machine already maintains its own outbound authenticated connector to the control plane. The relay joins the two legs. This managed connection does not require opening an inbound public SSH port on the machine. It is a terminal channel; the graphical desktop uses a separate desktop channel. Source: psu-connection-front-controller.mjs defaultOpenHostedTerminal; hosted-connector-client.ts; hosted-session-host.ts.\n\n5. **The host starts remote psu inside a PTY.** A PTY is the operating-system terminal interface that makes an interactive CLI behave as though a keyboard and screen were attached. For the current psu channel, the host starts the release's psu entrypoint directly, with only allowlisted arguments. psu is supervised under the service account; this connection does not provide an arbitrary service-account shell. Source: packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-psu-session.ts hostedPsuPtySpawnSpec.\n\n6. **Remote psu bootstraps the agent against the cloud machine's operator.** The launcher calls POST /api/agent-mcp/console/bootstrap-su. The operator records the tracked session/native identity and prepares the working directory, rendered instructions, MCP configuration and launch environment. Claude receives the rendered prompt through its system-prompt file and its prepared configuration. Codex receives a per-session CODEX_HOME containing AGENTS.md and MCP/hook configuration. Context is selected at launch and retrieved further through tools/hooks; the entire memory/documentation database is not copied to the laptop. Sources: psu-launcher.mjs launchFreshSu and suLaunchArgs; packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-mcp/bootstrap-su.ts.\n\n7. **The actual agent CLI runs as the customer workspace account.** The identity wrapper stages the permitted launch material and crosses to the customer account using loopback SSH on the same cloud machine. That internal hop is separate from the laptop-to-cloud relay. It substitutes the customer agent toolchain, filters environment/configuration, links the customer's agent credentials, and refuses the service's superuser/database secrets. Agent shell commands and file edits therefore run on the cloud machine in that workspace account. Source: packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/hosted-agent-identity.ts.\n\n8. **Model calls and terminal display follow different paths.** Claude Code/Codex sends model requests using the remote launch's configured provider/account route; a configured inference gateway can sit in that route. Model inference normally happens at the provider. Papercusp tool calls go to the configured operator/MCP surface with the session identity and are checked by its policies. The local terminal sends base64-encoded pty.input frames, receives pty.output/pty.snapshot frames, and sends pty.resize when its dimensions change. Base64 is framing, not encryption; transport security comes from the connection protocol. Source: defaultOpenHostedTerminal and the launch/account code.\n\n### Where things live\n\n| Place | Role |\n| --- | --- |\n| Laptop | Terminal display/keyboard, local connection profile and Papercusp sign-in credential. |\n| Cloud machine | Remote psu supervisor, Claude Code/Codex processes, checked-out files, native agent session state and that machine's Papercusp runtime. |\n| Papercusp cloud control plane | Sign-in, authorization, workspace discovery, one-use terminal tickets and connector relay. |\n| Model provider / configured gateway | Model requests under the remote session's account route. The connection itself does not transfer the laptop's provider login. |\n\nDisconnecting the laptop is different from exiting the remote process. A detached hosted terminal is retained for a bounded idle period; current source defaults to 15 minutes after detachment, then destroys it. Reconnection requests a fresh ticket and reuses the terminal session key. This is not a promise that every agent survives every network outage or a reboot.\n\nOlder hosts/relays can fall back to a customer-account shell and try to execute psu there. If psu is unavailable, that compatibility path explains the limitation and stays in the customer shell; it does not fall back to a service-account shell.\n\nThe managed-host flow above should not be assumed to certify BYOC CLI transport. The broker contains a distinct sealed-channel requirement for BYOC, whereas the local CLI bridge inspected here handles the ordinary terminal protocol. A real BYOC connection needs its own acceptance evidence.\n\n\n\n## Source audit\n\nRe-read session_turn:codex:01a14187-8f38-7b83-aedf-db07205ce9af:1 through :13 using sessions:read, including owner turns :1 (four requirements and popup copy), :3 (low-level flow), and :11 (AUTO, plan, portal and shipped directive). No requirement was inferred from assistant speech. P-005 derives from requested BYOC operation and P-006..P-008 derive from the explanation/shipment request. Original popup wording is preserved in source turn :1; the plan's truthful download notice keeps its substantive explanation without claiming browser completion that cannot be observed.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"native-code-intelligence-optional-evaluations-2026-10-15","title":"Native code intelligence: optional evaluations split from the core plan (visualisation, generated docs, expert query, taint/dependence, unreached code)","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Native code intelligence: optional evaluations split from the core plan (visualisation, generated docs, expert query, taint/dependence, unreached code)\nslug: native-code-intelligence-optional-evaluations-2026-10-15\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-15\nupdated: 2026-10-15\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: Avi and whoever later runs the optional native code-intelligence evaluations.\nProblem: five optional \"evaluate\" items in native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09 (its Phase 7, P-028..P-032) all waited on that plan's acceptance matrix and kept the core plan from shipping.\nOutcome: the core plan ships on its own; these evaluations are picked up later, each deciding with evidence whether the capability is worth building.\nNon-goals: no work here blocks or reopens the core plan; nothing here is committed product scope until Avi selects it.\nSource: native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09#D-016 [owner:Avi 2026-10-15] [turn:35b33faa@2026-10-15T17:55:29.091Z] (owner directive #1925), which split Phase 7 off.\nScenario: once the core plan has shipped and its graph/evidence APIs are stable, an agent takes one evaluation, measures it against the existing surfaces, and records a build / do-not-build decision.\n\n## Background\nMoved verbatim from native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09 Phase 7 (former P-028..P-032). Prerequisite for every item: the core plan's P-026 acceptance evidence. Preparatory analyzer-admission work already done under the former P-031 (WI-10007894, parent D-015) carries over to this plan's taint/dependence item.\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Optional evaluations\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Evaluate a graph visualization in the existing product UI after reliable edge/evidence APIs exist. Generated explanations must cite current source and update via existing drift/steward machinery. Treat as optional product scope pending Avi's selection rather than an implicit prerequisite for core correctness. (Moved from native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09 P-029 by D-016.) importance: low\n- **P-003** `todo` Evaluate an expert graph-query escape hatch using the existing query surface/store where possible. Select a bounded structural-query design only after reuse search and demonstrated needs; retain auth/scope/cost limits. Do not introduce Cypher or a new durable graph database merely to imitate GitNexus. (Moved from native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09 P-030 by D-016.) importance: low\n- **P-004** `todo` Evaluate statement-level control/data dependence and taint/security integration as a separate validated capability using maintained analyzers where suitable. Compare precise positive/negative and dynamic-boundary cases before routing security claims. GitNexus's optional PDG index does not establish our vulnerability-detection accuracy; licences and build prerequisites require explicit admission. (Moved from native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09 P-031 by D-016.) importance: low\n- **P-005** `todo` Evaluate apparently-unreached exports, test gaps and reusable/duplicate mechanism discovery across languages. Account for reflection, plugins, public entry points and generated consumers. Present static hypotheses with evidence rather than declaring code dead. Integrate with existing search, review and work records only if the independent evaluation shows value. (Moved from native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09 P-032 by D-016.) importance: low\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Requirements\nThe five evaluation contracts below are transferred from parent R-25 through R-29 under D-016. Their mandatory acceptance conditions, falsifiers, evidence planes, test layers and detector controls are preserved from D-014; this draft remains a follow-on to core shipment. Item references are local to this plan.\n\n**R-1 — Optional graph visualization.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Optional graph visualization in the native code-intelligence roadmap\",\n    \"sourceRefs\": [\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a11e0e-d352-75f3-a157-2ed8aa1f62a2:10\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a11e0e-d352-75f3-a157-2ed8aa1f62a2:14\",\n      \"session_turn:codex:01a11e0e-d352-75f3-a157-2ed8aa1f62a2:26\"\n    ],\n    \"constraints\": [\n      \"Agent-derived implementation detail under Avi's approved AUTO/self execution recorded in D-003.\",\n      \"Reuse the existing platform surface and preserve explicit uncertainty.\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A graph UI inspection reveals the source provenance of the selected edge.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An edge is shown without its source scope or uncertainty.\",\n    \"evidencePlane\": \"tree\",\n    \"requiredScope\": [\n      \"P-001\"\n    ],\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"e2e\"\n    ],\n    \"mandatory\": true\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the canonical tests and acceptance fixtures owned by P-001 against the exact changed source; bind recorded results and fingerprints at the selected evidence plane. Genuine tool/account/owner-only resource refusal remains a recorded external blocker after all independent preparation is completed.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"owner-question-delivery-and-review-route-scope-2026-10-15","title":"Owner questions reach the owner from any session; route constraints never switch off routed review","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-15","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Owner questions reach the owner from any session; route constraints never switch off routed review\nslug: owner-question-delivery-and-review-route-scope-2026-10-15\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-15\nupdated: 2026-10-18\n---\n\n# Owner questions reach the owner from any session; route constraints never switch off routed review\n\n## Product shaping\n- **Audience:** Avi (owner), plus every agent doing acceptance work.\n- **Problem (2026-10-15):** the gate-throughput-shift-left-2026-10-06 rubric amendment sat unreviewed for hours. su-88ed2d5a, a headless Codex session, skipped the routed outside-lineage review. Its kickoff, written by the launching agent and not by Avi, said \"launch no additional agents\". It then asked Avi for an exception through a native Codex question that no human could see.\n- **Outcome:** owner questions from any session land in the owner inbox. Routed reviewers and graders are never suppressed by a route constraint. A review left un-requested is caught automatically instead of being parked on the owner.\n- **Non-goals:** changing who reviews (the relevance router, shipped in review-routing-through-relevance-router-2026-09-26, stays as it is). Changing route semantics for implementation work.\n- **Source turns:** owner directives #1918 and #1921 (session su-666c00da), both owner-typed.\n\n### Scenarios\n- Codex or OMP asks a native question; the inbox reflects the wait and clears on its answer.\n- A headless session needs Avi: use coord:ask-owner; unsupported native UI cannot silently strand the ask.\n- A solo implementation requests a rubric review through the relevance router with no owner exception.\n- An omitted review older than 30 minutes gets one actionable nudge; unrelated owner choices remain untouched.\n- The bounded cleanup records each known case and any owned residue.\n\n## Evidence (historical investigation, 2026-10-15)\n- `harness_shared.session_pending_gates`, last 14 days: claude/hook 361, claude/watcher 2, **codex 0, omp 0**.\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.ts` header: Codex/OMP transcript roots are \"left for a later plan item\". `apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/ask-gate-mirror.sh` is a Claude-only hook.\n- su-88ed2d5a kickoff (`session_turn:codex:01a13de6-1e8c-7783-831e-cbb455bfc972:1`, origin fleet-kickoff, so agent-authored): \"Execute directly in this session within this plan; launch no additional agents.\"\n- WI-6554700010008333 checkpoint: \"reviewerModel/reviewPreviewPost removed to honor no-new-agents\"; \"Native UI question asks Avi for limited exception to noadditionalagents\".\n- `rubrics:amend` dry run returns `review.state:'not-requested'`. Its next-step text (`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/rubrics/amend.ts` lines 45 and 638) says nothing about route constraints.\n- Filed: EI-26064444269829747 (route constraint over-applied to reviewers) and EI-26064446346458542 (headless native questions invisible).\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Capture native questions across clients.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Codex and OMP native unanswered questions open the existing pending-gate record, then close on their correlated result; real native session identities and byte watermarks are preserved.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An unanswered Codex or OMP question appears in Avi's inbox until that same question receives its answer.\",\"falsifier\":\"A native question is missed, misattributed, duplicated, or stays open after its answer.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.integration.test.ts. The integration assertion must read the canonical owner-inbox pending-gate projection after tickGateWatch, verify one visible question with native session identity, then verify the row disappears/closes only after the correlated result; retain the bounded census only for R-5.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Deliver headless owner questions.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Headless sessions use durable owner channels; unsupported native dialogs have an explicit guard or watcher fallback, and captured questions are not claimed answerable without a working response path.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A headless session's question requiring Avi reaches a durable answerable owner channel or reports an explicit delivery limitation before it waits.\",\"falsifier\":\"A headless question parks invisibly or an inbox reply cannot reach the asking session without an explicit fallback.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run npm run test:file -- apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/ask-gate-mirror.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.integration.test.ts. Exercise the headless fallback: deny the native dialog with coord:ask-owner/coord:escalate, create the durable owner question, observe it on the owner channel, post a correlated answer, and verify delivery/wake to the asking session; retain the explicit delivery-limitation branch when no response path exists.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/ask-gate-mirror.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/gate-watch.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Keep platform acceptance independent of implementation route.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Solo/no-extra-agent route constraints govern implementation fan-out; canonical review, grading and consult remain allowed, and tool/kickoff guidance states this at the decision point. Agent-authored constraints are resolved with their launcher.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Choosing a single implementation agent still permits platform-routed independent acceptance review without a new owner exception.\",\"falsifier\":\"An ordinary one-agent route disables required independent acceptance or sends the owner an invented exception request.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/agent-launch-core.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/rubrics/amend.test.ts.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-launch-core.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/rubrics/amend.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Detect omitted review without owner noise.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Existing gate-watcher cadence detects an approval-required preview older than 30 minutes with no review request and a blocked/needs-human/parked carrier, sends the holder the exact retry once, and clears only a proven machine-actionable owner wall.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A parked carrier of an approval-required preview with an omitted review receives exactly one actionable reminder after thirty minutes without clearing unrelated owner decisions.\",\"falsifier\":\"Eligible omitted reviews get no nudge, repeated ticks duplicate it, or an unrelated owner decision is cleared.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/attention/review-stall-reaper.integration.test.ts. For R-5 also retain the bounded live census and dispositions on its work-item.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/attention/review-stall-reaper.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Reconcile the known stalled population.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Inspect the two named work-items and newly surfaced current Codex questions, record dispositions, and route or assign remaining genuine blockers with evidence.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each case in the agreed cleanup population has an evidence-based disposition naming the accountable agent for any remaining blocker.\",\"falsifier\":\"A known case is skipped or a remaining blocker is left without a verified owner.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Use an immutable bounded cleanup-population snapshot whose artifact records a population identifier or hash and its cardinality. Enumerate each case exactly once with the closed disposition enum resolved, routed, owned-blocker, or excluded-with-reason. Record authoritative evidence timestamp and a verified assignee for every non-resolved case, and require zero uncovered or residue cases. Inspect each named case's authoritative work-item state, checkpoint, and assignee; bind the census and per-case ownership evidence through the operational/requirements evidence plane. Retain gate-watch and review-stall-reaper integration tests only as supporting checks. Keep the census artifact and accountable-agent dispositions on WI-6554700010017174.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"requirements\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing gate watcher, gate store, owner channels, rubric review workflow, and launch baseline. Reuse completed EI fixes. Add the omitted-review check to the existing gate-watcher action, with receipt-key idempotency; do not create a scheduler or a second inbox.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n\n## Capture Codex and OMP native questions in the owner-gate tracker. Extend gate-watch roots and line-shape adapters to Codex `request_user_input` and the OMP equivalent, so they open and close `session_pending_gates` rows and show in the owner inbox like Claude ones. Test: per-client fixture transcripts produce an open row, then a closed row. — note: Avi approved all five items and direct route; claim P-001 while independent canonical BAR clarification is reviewed. Implementation acceptance remains gated.\n- **P-002** `wip` Headless sessions ask through coord:ask-owner, not a native dialog. First verify whether an answer given in the owner inbox can resolve a headless session's native dialog. If it cannot, deny the native question tool for headless launches where the client supports a deny (Claude: add AskUserQuestion beside NO_SUBAGENT_TOOLS_DENY), with refusal text pointing at coord:ask-owner. P-001 stays the fallback where no deny exists. Test: the headless launch spec carries the deny.\n- **P-003** `wip` Route constraints never cover platform-recruited reviewers. Add one kernel rule. Solo, no-fleet and \"no additional agents\" constraints govern agents you launch to do the work. They never cover reviewers, graders or consult responders the platform recruits (`rubrics:amend requestReview`, `plans:set-plan-status` grading, consult). Asking for an exception to a constraint goes to whoever set it: a kickoff-authored constraint belongs to its launcher, not the owner. Repeat the sentence at the decision points: `REVIEW_NOT_REQUESTED_NEXT` in rubrics:amend, the acceptance-grader recruit response, and a fixed line every plan kickoff from fleet:launch-on-plan / capability:launch-agent carries. Test: a doc-claims test pins the kernel part, the tool text and the kickoff line.\n- **P-004** `wip` Detector for an un-requested review. A `rubric_amend_receipts` row in state `previewed` with `approvalRequired` and no review request, older than 30 minutes, whose carrying work-item is needs-human, blocked or parked: nudge the holder with the exact `requestReview` call and mark the park as not an owner wall. Reuse an existing ephemeral sweep; do not add a new scheduler. Test: an integration test with a seeded receipt and a parked item yields exactly one nudge.\n- **P-005** `wip` Sweep the current population once. Check other items whose kickoff says \"no additional agents\" (for example WI-6554700010014180, blocked, and WI-6554700010014285); I have not verified that they are stalled the same way. Also handle any open Codex questions P-001's first run surfaces. Unblock or route each one. — note: Run the approved one-time sweep of the two named blocked items and current Codex pending gates; record evidence and assign any residue.\n\n## Notes\n- Every plan ships with a graded acceptance rubric. maintained Playwright detectors. An unknown, failed, stale or unexecuted required branch cannot yield a passing card.\n\nSource turns and provenance: owner directive #1785, sourceTurnRef 9de76438-7f9c-4844-a6a8-cf6e02a31df5:8a0344e06edf91d324e3a4644ac1ffaf00f016ba980ac23bfc98cf2317920753, directs the existing byoc-cloud-carry-1013 fleet to carry its plans to shipped. Current agent-origin carry text is not owner approval.\n\nScenarios:\n1. Tests pass, but a mandatory browser case is absent/skipped or its workspace/source/runtime/served manifest differs: refuse a passing claim.\n3. Receipt predicates pass, but live tests fail or cannot run: refuse a passing claim; old successful test rows cannot replace the execution branch.\n4. Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"cloud-connection-pairing-unification-2026-10-16","title":"Cloud computer connections and mobile pairing unification","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cloud computer connections and mobile pairing unification\nslug: cloud-connection-pairing-unification-2026-10-16\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-16\nupdated: 2026-10-17\n---\n## Product shaping\n### Audience\nCloud portal users connecting computers and pairing mobile apps.\n### Problem\nSSH, portal relay, hosted connectors, browser sessions, and mobile pairing have distinct authorities but overlapping UI language.\n### Outcome\nShip a shared inventory/lifecycle presentation while preserving separate credentials and trust boundaries.\n### Non-goals\n- No SSH-to-QR replacement, no mobile shell access, no credential-table migration, no relay protocol redesign.\n### Source turns\n- Owner requested the comparison and recommendation; selected direct execution; then directed plan, AUTO, and shipment.\n### Scenarios\n1. Machine selection distinguishes SSH, relay, and hosted connector.\n2. Remote access shows paired phones with device-specific actions.\n3. Details show authority, transport, scope, health, and actual revoke effect.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Typed connection inventory.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Represent SSH profile, portal relay, hosted connector, browser session, and mobile device in one typed model while retaining distinct credential references.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Normalization returns class, sourceRef, scope, transport, lifecycle, health, authoritySummary, and actions without secrets.\",\"falsifier\":\"A class is omitted, credentials are merged, or secret material is copied.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run normalization tests over representative fixtures and inspect returned fields.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/app/settings/remote-access/page.test.tsx\",\"apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/MachineSwitcher.test.tsx\"]}}}\n```\n**R-2 — Authority and health visibility.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Make authority and current health understandable in Remote access.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each entry shows class, authority summary, scope, transport, health/liveness, and class-specific action label.\",\"falsifier\":\"The UI implies local profile deletion revokes remote access or shows stale connector state as live.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Render fixtures for each class and assert labels, health, and action text.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/app/settings/remote-access/page.test.tsx\"]}}}\n```\n**R-3 — Authoritative adapters.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Reuse local psu profile, portal relay, hosted connector/liveness, and connected_apps sources without duplicating credentials.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Adapters expose references and state from existing stores and persist no bearer, JWT, private key, or Noise secret.\",\"falsifier\":\"A new credential registry is introduced or a cache becomes authoritative.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Exercise source adapter seams and inspect writes/calls.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/remote-access/relay-opt-in.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-workspace-connector.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/device-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n**R-4 — Explicit revoke semantics.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Make every action accurately describe what it revokes and what remains active.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Confirmation copy and routing are class-specific and preserve existing endpoints.\",\"falsifier\":\"A generic revoke is wired across authority classes or copy overstates revocation.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run action mapping tests for all classes, including SSH forget-only.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/app/settings/remote-access/page.test.tsx\",\"apps/operator/scripts/psu-connection-front-controller.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n**R-5 — Clear product language.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Distinguish the SSH helper from portal relay enrollment in user-facing labels.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Machine switcher copy identifies SSH/private-network access and links to the distinct relay surface.\",\"falsifier\":\"A user could read the SSH helper as QR pairing or relay enrollment.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Assert accessible names and instructional text in both surfaces.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/MachineSwitcher.test.tsx\",\"apps/operator/app/settings/remote-access/page.test.tsx\"]}}}\n```\n**R-6 — Security boundary preservation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Unify presentation without changing trust boundaries or granting mobile credentials machine control.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Pairing, JWT revocation, Noise sealing, and hosted channel allowlists retain their wire contracts.\",\"falsifier\":\"A mobile JWT opens PTY/desktop, BYOC carries plaintext, or pairing skips revocation.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"e2e\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run existing pairing, JWT, sealed relay, and channel-policy tests.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/e2e/device-pair.spec.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/device-jwt.property.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/hosted-workspace-connector.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n**R-7 — Regression coverage.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Leave recurrence guards in the real test suites for inventory and renamed copy.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Focused and affected tests pass with required cases present.\",\"falsifier\":\"Verification relies only on typecheck or ad-hoc scripts, or pairing/SSH contracts regress.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run focused tests and the affected test command with receipts.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/app/cloud-workspaces/MachineSwitcher.test.tsx\",\"apps/operator/e2e/device-pair.spec.ts\",\"scripts/affected-tests.mjs\"]}}}\n```\n**R-8 — Promotion.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Carry implementation through staging, green promotion, deployment, and exact artifact verification.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The deployed artifact contains the change and green checkpoint is verified first.\",\"falsifier\":\"Shipment is claimed from staging-only evidence, a red gate is bypassed, or artifact identity is unknown.\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read pipeline position, run checkpoint, deploy only after green, and verify deployed artifact/report.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n- Shared presentation contract: ConnectionInventoryEntry { id, class, label, scope, transport, state, health, lastSeen, authoritySummary, actions, sourceRef }.\n- Classes: ssh-profile, portal-relay, hosted-connector, browser-session, mobile-device.\n- Actions remain class-specific: forget-local, revoke-remote-key, disconnect-relay, revoke-connector, revoke-session, pause-device, revoke-device.\n- Keep source adapters and endpoints separate; use Remote access as inventory surface The original workstation gallery/tunnel is retired.\nUse the configured server-side ElevenLabs credential, with no secret persisted in source or browser assets.\nKeep the original recognizable cream/brown cup silhouette. Extend the existing vector mascot as a deterministic articulated 2D character with speech-timed visemes, eye/brow expression, blinks, gaze, arms and gesture cues. A vector rig fits the current brand assets and remains reproducible across video and browser.\nUse ElevenLabs alignment data for speech timing and align captions to the same narration. Validate silence, pause, replay, seek and stop behavior.\nProposed story: Workshop Planner → Plans/HUD/Work → private preview → rubric/grade/scorecard → Git → project memories/procedures → psu same-host attachment → visible desktop fleet → real automatic context → second scorecard.\npsu commands verified in current launcher help: psu --connect-login; psu --connect-list; psu --connect. Hosted customer arguments are allowlisted; select project in session rather than forwarding arbitrary --harness flags.\nA cloud desktop with visible terminals is a rehearsal prerequisite. Do not substitute local-desktop agents or headless workers for that recorded scene.\nGuide actions preserve learner scope. Watching does not trigger billable actions, auto-navigate the application or confirm task completion.\nPersist video position through existing scoped preference/progress surfaces; keep real product receipts separate.\nGit narration describes the example project's actual configuration. A staging/main gate is shown only when configured.\nExact full narration, prompts and shot directions: report rpt_83edd1ec-9dd8-4e14-872f-95b81207c3d4 (/reports?sel=rpt_83edd1ec-9dd8-4e14-872f-95b81207c3d4), body SHA256 d2152b56fc3c438950b4411fb9a58fecb693e6ba784df879a5d7361d98c74d9b.
