No rubric evidence or shipment verdict is implied.\nApproved-By: su-de57a384-08c9-4d7a-8857-d1c799635d67\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1188718\nApproved-At: 2026-10-17T18:24:19.417Z\nRubric revision: 7 → 8\nSubject plan revision: 18 → 19\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16\n\n## Approved full script and practice flow\n\n### Papercusp guided project tutorial — combined video and interactive script, draft 2\n\nApproved for implementation by Avi, 2026-10-16. Supersedes the workshop-notes quickstart script. Retain PaperCup's first-person narrator persona and familiar screen-driven style; use ElevenLabs for the eventual voice. Proposed edited duration: 12–15 minutes, with chapters so a user can stop after the initial getting-started section and return for deeper topics. Duration is an editorial target, not measured narration.\n\n## Combined tutorial experience\n\nExtend the existing cloud-app-live-tutorial-2026-10-01 plan and AccountProductTutorial, its lesson catalogue, scope-aware navigation, Help and authenticated progress. Add video chapters to this maintained guide.\n\nEach chapter offers **Watch** and **Try it**. Watch plays the corresponding segment of the shared video. Try it pauses playback and opens the relevant real portal destination, retaining the learner's authorized workspace, project and tutorial position. The guide stays reachable for resuming. Offer copyable prompts, captions/transcript, chapters and a continuous-watch option. Users can also skip video and use the interactive guide.\n\nPractice uses the learner's own project, not a link into the recorded demonstration's tenant. Account/setup lessons remain available before a workspace exists. Do not treat a watched clip, opened tab or reviewed explanation as evidence that a project was created, a grade ran, or a fleet did work. Extend the existing product-observation checks for the new practice steps rather than creating another tutorial/progress engine. Watching or seeking never starts billable work or executes the demonstration prompts.\n\nOne tutorial entry appears alongside the existing public app.papercusp.com content and is easy to reopen after signup, including through the existing product-guide return controls.\n\n## One continuous example\n\nBuild a small browser app called **Workshop Planner**. Users can add workshop tasks with an owner and due date, mark them complete, and retain them across reloads. Data stays in the browser. Start with a real maintained Papercusp app template. Keep hosting/publication out of the initial build.\n\nLater, the same project receives filters and CSV export through a visible desktop fleet on the same cloud instance. The rubric, scorecards, plan, work items, Git history, memories, procedure docs and agent sessions all belong to this project.\n\nA learner can substitute another small project, while the guide keeps the same goal → plan → work → evidence → improvement sequence.\n\n## Chapter 1 — Meet PaperCup and choose where work runs\n\n**Screen:** app.papercusp.com → signup/sign-in → welcome → Workspaces. Choose the recorded account's available managed-cloud route, review costs, and select the connected workspace. Briefly show model/account readiness. Cut over private login and provisioning waits.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“Hi, I'm PaperCup, the operator of Papercusp.\n\nLet's create a small project together, follow the agents doing the work, and check what they built. Then we'll improve it and continue from the command line.\n\nYou can watch each chapter or choose Try it to follow along in your own workspace.\n\nStart at app dot papercusp dot com. Create an account or sign in, then select a connected workspace. That's the environment where your agents run.\n\nI'm using a cloud workspace here. Review the setup and costs shown for your account, and make sure the workspace and model account are ready before you start.”\n\n**Try it:** Sign in and select a ready workspace. Keep full local/BYOC setup available through the existing separate guidance.\n\n## Chapter 2 — Ask PaperCup to create a project\n\n**Screen:** Open Ask Papercup. Enter the following prompt. Show the actual proposed project, template choices and plan. Choose the current maintained web-app template from the options returned.\n\n**Prompt:**\n\n> Create a project called Workshop Planner in this cloud workspace.\n>\n> I want a small browser app for organizing workshop tasks. Let me add a task with a title, owner and due date, mark it complete, and keep the tasks after a page reload.\n>\n> Keep the data in the browser. Start from an available maintained Papercusp web-app template. Show me the template choice and plan before implementation. Keep the app private for this tutorial.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“Give me the outcome you want, the important constraints, and what a successful result should do.\n\nHere, we're creating Workshop Planner. It needs a task list, owners, due dates, and saved progress.\n\nI've also said where the data should live and asked to review the plan before implementation.\n\nI'll identify the project, offer the appropriate app template, and turn the request into work you can inspect.”\n\n**Screen:** Review the actual proposal and target. Approve in the implementing conversation:\n\n> Approve this template and plan. Implement the first version yourself in this project, test the main user flows, and give me a private preview. Do not publish it publicly.\n\n**Try it:** Create the learner's own project through the real prompt and approval controls. Keep the returned project, plan and work references.\n\n## Chapter 3 — Follow Plans, HUD and Work\n\n**Screen:** As the build proceeds, open Plans for this project. Open the actual plan and its requirements, items and decisions. Visit HUD and open the implementing session. Visit Work, open a corresponding work item and its evidence. Keep the project identity visible across destinations.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“You can follow the work without reading every line of the conversation.\n\nPlans shows the goal, the steps and the decisions we've agreed on. If we change our minds, the decision belongs here so the next agent can find it.\n\nHUD shows the agents and their current activity. Open a session when you want to see what an agent is doing.\n\nWork shows individual work items: who's responsible, what's next, and whether anything is blocked.\n\nThese are different views of the same project. An agent being active tells you work is happening. The work item's result and verification tell you what was accomplished.”\n\n**Try it:** Open the learner's plan, implementing session and one linked work item. A completed task needs actual result evidence, not just navigation.\n\n## Chapter 4 — Inspect the first version\n\n**Screen:** Open the private preview. Add “Book the room,” owner “Mira,” with a due date. Add another task, mark one complete and reload. Show the real persisted result. Show the implementing agent's verification.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“Let's check the app itself.\n\nI'll add a task, assign an owner and due date, mark a task complete, and reload the page.\n\nCompare what happens with the original request. If something is missing or behaves unexpectedly, tell the agent what you observed.\n\nWe now have a first version and a concrete way to judge whether it works.”\n\n**Try it:** Exercise the learner's actual preview and compare it with their requirements.\n\n## Chapter 5 — Create a rubric and enter grade mode\n\n**Screen:** Return to the project conversation. Enter the prompt below. Open the created rubric and show its criteria, checks and evidence expectations. Show the registered grade mode and a real grading run.\n\n**Prompt:**\n\n> Create a reusable Workshop Planner rubric from this project's requirements.\n>\n> Cover adding tasks, owners and due dates, completion, persistence after reload, understandable empty/error states, and keyboard usability.\n>\n> Bind repeatable checks where possible and say what still needs human review. Enter grade mode and grade the current app against this rubric. Show the resulting scorecard and evidence. Keep this grade pass to assessment; leave implementation of findings for our next approved step.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“A rubric makes our expectations explicit and reusable.\n\nFor Workshop Planner, we'll check the required task flows, saved data and basic usability. Each criterion should say what good looks like and how to check it.\n\nNow I'll enter grade mode and assess the app against those criteria.\n\nA rubric is the standard. A scorecard records the results of applying that standard to a particular version of the project.”\n\n**Try it:** Create or reuse an appropriate project rubric and run the learner's explicit assessment. Preserve the requested assessment-only boundary.\n\n## Chapter 6 — Read the scorecard and turn findings into work\n\n**Screen:** Open the real scorecard from the grading run. Open a criterion and its evidence. Show the actual statuses; if everything passes, say so and use the planned enhancement for later work. If gaps exist, show them honestly and record actionable follow-ups.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“Here's the scorecard for this run.\n\nOpen a criterion to see the finding and the evidence behind it. A passing result should have support. A failure identifies a gap. If a check couldn't be completed, keep that visible too.\n\nThe rubric stays available for the next assessment. Each new grading run produces its own scorecard, so we can compare results over time.\n\nUseful findings become work we can assign and verify. That's how we move from judging the app to improving it.”\n\n**Try it:** Inspect one real criterion and its evidence. Follow an actual finding into an owned work item when one exists. Do not manufacture defects or a perfect grade for the recording.\n\n## Chapter 7 — Understand git-sync\n\n**Screen:** Open the project's Git view. Show an actual task's file changes, an automatically created commit, the configured branch/destination and its corresponding revision. Where this project has a promotion gate, show its real status and promoted revision. No manual git add/commit/push for the demonstration.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“As agents work, git-sync records their changes in Git and synchronizes them with the configured remote.\n\nHere's a change from the task we just followed, and here's the commit that contains it.\n\nThis gives the project a history you can inspect. It also lets you trace a result back to the work that produced it.”\n\n**Conditional narration, only if this tutorial project's actual configuration uses staging → tested main:**\n\n“In this project, agents work on staging. Main receives a version after the configured checks pass.\n\nA saved commit, a passing test run and a deployed app are separate steps. Use the actual revision and delivery status to see how far a change has reached.”\n\n**Try it:** Find the learner's real change and commit; inspect the project's configured checks and delivery status. Do not imply every project inherits the Papercusp platform repository's branch policy.\n\n## Chapter 8 — Inspect memories and procedural documentation\n\n**Screen:** Open a real project memory retaining the local-data requirement and a real project procedure covering tests and checking persistence. Show their source links. If the build did not create these records naturally, request them explicitly on camera:\n\n> Retain the verified project decisions as project memories. Document the tested procedure for running this project's checks and verifying task persistence. Link the procedure to the code and evidence it describes.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“The project keeps useful knowledge as well as code.\n\nA memory can retain a decision or constraint—for example, that Workshop Planner keeps its data in the browser.\n\nProcedural documentation records how to do something again, such as running the checks and verifying saved tasks.\n\nOpen these records to see what was retained and where it came from.\n\nAs agents continue the project, relevant knowledge can be brought into their context. We'll look at that as it happens in the next part.”\n\n**Try it:** Inspect an actual project memory and procedure, with sources. Explicitly authored knowledge must be described as explicitly authored.\n\n## Chapter 9 — Connect psu to the same cloud instance\n\n**Screen:** Open a terminal on the user's computer, using the downloaded utility. Run these current supported commands, complete browser authentication, then select the exact same cloud workspace from the picker:\n\n```sh\npsu --connect-login\npsu --connect-list\npsu --connect\n```\n\nShow the selected workspace/host identity, then compare it with the portal's identity. Select the same project in the remote session; do not create another project or copy the repository to a different machine.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“The psu utility gives you a terminal interface to your Papercusp agents.\n\nYou can use it from your own computer while the agent runs in the cloud.\n\nFirst, sign in to the portal from psu. Then choose the same workspace we've been using in the browser.\n\nWe're connecting to the same cloud instance and continuing the same project. The existing plan, work items and retained knowledge are still there.\n\nA terminal connection may start a new agent conversation. That agent can pick up the project's durable state without us pasting the earlier conversation into it.”\n\n**Prompt in the connected agent:**\n\n> Continue Workshop Planner in this cloud workspace. Read the current plan and work-item state. Propose the next steps for the remaining rubric findings, plus owner/status filters and a CSV export of the visible tasks. Show the proposed work before starting it.\n\n**Try it:** Connect the learner's utility to the same selected workspace and locate their project and existing plan. Keep authentication tokens off screen.\n\n## Chapter 10 — Continue with a visible desktop fleet\n\n**Screen:** Review the new scoped work and approve it in the connected psu session. The agent should reuse the current plan or record a linked follow-up where appropriate. Launch through fleet:launch-on-plan. Open this same cloud workspace's browser Desktop view and show real visible member terminals. Show actual registration, claims and working activity, then revisit Plans/HUD/Work.\n\n**Approval prompt:**\n\n> Approve this continuation. Lead a visible desktop fleet on this same cloud instance and project. Split genuinely independent work into separate lanes, choose the member count to fit the plan, and use the available model/account choices we review. Verify the changes and report the results. Keep the app private.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“Some work can happen independently. A fleet gives us a leader and coordinated agents working on those separate pieces.\n\nHere, we'll continue the same project with a visible desktop fleet on this cloud instance.\n\nOpen the workspace's desktop to see the member terminals. We can also follow their assignments through HUD and Work.\n\nThe leader coordinates the work. Shared plans, work items and file locks help the agents work together.\n\nWe'll confirm that the members actually picked up their tasks, then look at the results they produce.”\n\n**Try it:** Offer this chapter after the single-agent path. Review resources and costs before launching. Require a desktop-enabled cloud host and real visible terminals; never silently substitute headless sessions or another machine.\n\n## Chapter 11 — See relevant context arrive without asking for it\n\n**Screen:** Zoom into a real fleet member's session. Show the startup orientation briefly, then a later relevant context injection as the member works on a task. Examples to capture: a source-backed local-data memory, a procedure related to the tests being run, and a relevant coordination/plan update. Tie each to its earlier source record. Preserve the actual time and transcript ordering. Do not issue “recall memory,” “search docs,” or manual context-paste commands as a substitute for automatic injection.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“Watch the context arriving in this agent's session.\n\nIt receives project orientation when it starts. As its task develops, Papercusp can also supply relevant memories, procedural documentation and coordination updates.\n\nHere is the retained project constraint, and here is the procedure relevant to the check the agent is performing.\n\nWe didn't ask the agent to fetch those records or paste them into this conversation. They were supplied as relevant context.\n\nThe agent still needs to check the source and use the information appropriately. The benefit is that useful project knowledge can meet the agent where it's working.”\n\n**Try it:** Inspect a real injection in the learner's supported session view. A startup briefing alone does not satisfy the mid-task demonstration; a manual retrieval call does not count as automatic injection. Narration names only the kinds of records actually observed.\n\n## Chapter 12 — Verify the improvement and return later\n\n**Screen:** Open the updated preview and exercise filters/export plus any repaired findings. Run the same rubric again; compare the new scorecard with the prior one on comparable criteria and check definitions. Show actual results. Return to the combined guide chapter list, Sessions and Inbox. Briefly show stop controls.\n\n**PaperCup:**\n\n“Let's check what changed.\n\nOpen the updated app, try the new behavior, and run the rubric again. This scorecard belongs to the new assessment. Compare its evidence with the earlier run.\n\nWe've followed one project from a request, through planning and implementation, into grading and further improvement—from both the portal and psu.\n\nYou can return through the tutorial chapters or your project sessions. Inbox holds questions that need your attention.\n\nWhen you want work to stop, use the agent or fleet controls and check the acknowledgement. Closing a browser tab or terminal doesn't necessarily stop remote agents. Stopping cloud compute is a separate action.”\n\n**Try it:** Verify the learner's result and inspect a second scorecard where the same rubric applies. Preserve explicit unknowns and unresolved findings.\n\n## Integration map\n\n| Video chapters | Existing guide area to extend | Interactive action |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| 1 | welcome, workspace, account, billing | Select a ready workspace |\n| 2–4 | planning, work, cloud-first-agent | Create project; open Plans, HUD, Work and preview |\n| 5–6 | operations, knowledge | Create/reuse rubric; grade; inspect scorecard and finding |\n| 7 | operations → Git | Inspect real commit, checks and delivery |\n| 8 | knowledge → Learning/Docs | Inspect retained memory and procedure |\n| 9 | workspace/work plus psu guidance | Authenticate utility and attach to same cloud instance |\n| 10–11 | work → agents/HUD/Work/Desktop | Launch approved visible fleet; inspect actual dynamic context |\n| 12 | operations/work/help | Verify result, compare scorecards, resume or stop |\n\n## Production and review boundaries\n\n- Avi's original instructions still apply: cloud portal replaces the desktop app as the main product interface; practical teaching for users rather than a pitch; ElevenLabs voice; original PaperCup persona/style; public app page placement and easy post-signup access.\n- The cloud desktop scene is the fleet's remote desktop viewed through the portal, not a switch back to the deprecated desktop app.\n- The current interactive guide already has lesson navigation, scope-aware targets, Help, pause/resume and saved progress. Video chapter mapping, the integrated practice flow and grading/psu/fleet checks are proposed extensions.\n- Preserve the existing broader guide, optional setup routes, accessibility and account/org-scoped progress. Bind project practice receipts to the actual workspace/project.\n- Rehearse remote psu → same project → visible fleet → remote desktop as one path before recording. A terminal attachment alone does not establish visible desktop support.\n- Grade mode implies an autonomy posture in the mode registry; the tutorial prompt must explicitly bound this first pass to assessment and defer fixes to the approved continuation.\n- Git-sync narration must match this project's actual configuration. Do not promise staging/main gating for a project without that policy.\n- Retained knowledge and dynamic injection must be real, inspectable and source-linked. Do not promise all knowledge appears in every turn.\n- Keep secrets and unrelated customer context off screen. Use a dedicated tutorial project.\n- All displayed IDs, results, grades and progress must come from the actual run. Compress waits with visible cuts.\n- Avi approved AUTO implementation through shipped status. PaperCup now requires expressive speech-synced character animation, replacing the prior bobbing icon.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"complete-four-unplanned-features-2026-10-16","title":"Finish the four unplanned features directly","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Finish the four unplanned features directly\nslug: complete-four-unplanned-features-2026-10-16\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-16\nupdated: 2026-10-18\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: Avi and Papercusp operators.\nProblem: Four open unplanned features match the paused fleet revision-7 filter.\nOutcome: Finish F-FIX-053, WI-4480, WI-10007840, and WI-10005829 directly with their original acceptance requirements.\nNon-goals: No new agents or resumed fleet workers; no invented platform, payment, customer, or shipment evidence.\nSource turns: Avi asked how many features match the filter, received four, then instructed: finish the 4 features yourself now on auto mode.\nScenarios: safe storage writes; opt-in shortcuts tested on required platforms; measured rubric stewardship visible in the GUI; genuine monetization shipment.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Preserve acceptance.** Fulfill the four original work-items without replacing their requirements.\n**R-2 — Direct execution.** This session implements and verifies, preserving peer work and lawful claims.\n**R-3 — Evidence.** Close only on verified evidence; keep exact external prerequisites explicit.\n\n## Design\nReuse existing work-items, source plans, native rigs, tests, release pipeline, and ledgers. This plan coordinates execution and adds no product surface.\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | live |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004 | live |\n\n## Execution\n- **P-001** `wip` Diagnose and finish existing F-FIX-053 storage write incident.\n- **P-002** `todo` Finish existing WI-4480 cross-platform shortcut acceptance.\n- **P-003** `todo` Finish existing WI-10007840 rubric stewardship and original shipped acceptance.\n- **P-004** `todo` Obtain lawful handoff and finish existing WI-10005829 monetization shipment.\n\n## Decisions\nAvi chose direct-self AUTO execution. Fleet workers remain paused; this session left fleet membership to execute directly. Claims for first three items succeeded. Monetization handoff request coord-send-0d74e98f873260b2c6be4026b515050fd0c02dd4644b75830c1daefff8d9613b is queued, not accepted. Existing source plans and hard acceptance gates remain authoritative.\n\n### D-001 — Retain the failed native generation; require source containment before final WOE acceptance\nDate: 2026-10-18\nMeasured: 2026-10-18. Verified coord:whoami is su-81bb8095-b84c-4d05-82d5-c857e979124b and read original coord:thread rooted at coord-send-25ee0a64a256a8e70e3dd5dc2830f7e574989da98814a10ca837b88efaee8411. The ruling preserves dccbbe21/c49127/lock1df5152f, failed doctor, unchanged pins/no re-export/no doctor exception; it permits independent preparation, not an alternate-ref workaround. Existing Windows0.0.23 predates required native source; Mac signed/paint proof leaves ordinary-profile and key prerequisites open. D010 camera/shared-voice exclusions remain.\n\nRead WOE plan36 D010-D015 and both P005 current spec clauses. Shared ledger row21024594 independently confirms original a44756aa native pass, worktreeDirty=false, isScratchConfig=false. Exact Git object probes at known frozen artifact d740fc3802877d1c8c3b1068768681ee32ef0025 find none of four named tested panel/CSS/test/stewardship-reader paths, while all four a44756aa source hashes match the historical receipt. This does not measure the current serving runtime or universal GUI absence. Current-build proof cannot establish deployed R7/SPEC-WOE-SHIP.\n\nBounded qualification saved in docs/evidence/original-four-qualification-2026-10-18.json SHA25644b06babfef79cb548e94645641ac6461defbb7be3df9f9951854a1c241a38d9. JSON/source-hash/path assertions and git diff --check passed; no native/test/build replay, export, install, storage mutation or LIVE_GATE_OPS. Preserve successful historical proof. Next independent unit is exact required-source closure preparation for a qualified containing artifact, without mutating the peer-owned live admission/gate. Do not spend another wake merely re-reading ruling25ee or repeat the completed Windows visibility smoke. Original four-feature mission remains unfinished.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-16","title":"Personal Vault — enterprise agent privacy and security hardening","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-16","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Personal Vault — enterprise agent privacy and security hardening\nslug: personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-16\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-16\nupdated: 2026-10-17\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n### Audience\nThe owner of a personal vault and the engineers maintaining Papercusp's agent, tool, storage, and provider boundaries.\n\n### Problem\nPersonal Vault already has default-deny grants, local embeddings, privacy labels, disclosure tracking, sealed shared-store content, archive encryption, and restricted-session network isolation. These controls are distributed across separate paths. A vault read can be confused with permission to use an external model, send data to a provider, export it, or retain derived copies. Normalized personal documents and derived data also need a stronger storage and key-custody boundary.\n\n### Outcome\nPapercusp provides a coherent enterprise-grade privacy boundary: every read is attributable and scoped; external inference and outward actions are separately authorized; vault content is protected through its full data lineage; execution and credentials are isolated; lock and revocation have immediate effect; and the owner can audit and delete data with clear evidence.\n\n### Scenarios\n1. A meeting-preparation agent receives read access to Gmail and Calendar for a bounded date range and prepares a local summary.\n2. External inference requires a separate, expiring approval naming provider, region, retention, and data-handling terms.\n3. A sender-only email constrains later sends, exports, and provider actions; document text cannot widen the reader set.\n4. Lock or revocation stops new reads/actions and invalidates active context receipts.\n5. Purge returns a lineage receipt covering primary rows, embeddings, indexes, caches, transcripts, traces, backups, and legal holds.\n\n### Non-goals\n- Building a second agent framework or vault.\n- Treating no-training terms as equivalent to no retention.\n- Claiming server-side encryption protects against an operator holding both ciphertext and keys.\n- Giving every agent personal-data access.\n- Removing legal-hold or accountable retention requirements.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Typed least-privilege capabilities.** Grants MUST distinguish `read`, `infer:local`, `infer:external`, `send`, `export`, and `admin`, and bind to user, agent, plan/binding, purpose, source/account, time/volume limits, expiration, and approver. Read MUST NOT imply inference, export, or send.\n\n**R-2 — One retrieval gateway.** `personal:search`, `personal:ask`, ambient recall, archive inspection, and sealed-content opening MUST use one gateway that resolves identity/purpose, filters before plaintext leaves the vault, minimizes output, records a content-free audit, and returns a short-lived context receipt.\n\n**R-3 — Separate inference policy.** Inference MUST use a broker that re-checks the receipt before dispatch. Private mode MUST use local inference with no external egress. External inference MUST name provider/model/region/endpoint/retention/training/caching/files/tracing/tool policy and require a separate expiring grant.\n\n**R-4 — Encrypted data plane.** Normalized personal content, sensitive metadata, embeddings, indexes, sealed copies, archives, caches, transcripts, traces, exports, and backups MUST have an explicit protection policy. Personal records MUST extend existing envelope/key-version primitives with per-user/vault keys, rotation, recovery, and documented search leakage. Decryption MUST stay in the retrieval gateway.\n\n**R-5 — Brokered actions and credentials.** Sends, provider mutations, exports, and other outward effects MUST be typed proposals checked outside the model against receipt, destination, payload, labels, approval, and limits. Long-lived secrets MUST stay in a broker/secrets manager outside general agent environments.\n\n**R-6 — Lock, revoke, and lifecycle.** Lock MUST remove usable key material, stop background retrieval, invalidate receipts, and reject reads/actions. Revocation MUST be checked before retrieval, inference, and actions. Step-up authentication MUST protect export, recovery, bulk purge, and privacy loosening.\n\n**R-7 — Retention, deletion, and audit.** Retention/deletion MUST cover source archives, normalized records, embeddings/indexes, summaries/transcripts, caches/traces, exports, backups, and provider-side state. Purge MUST distinguish deleted data, backup expiry, and legal holds. Audit records MUST identify user, agent, purpose, grant, source/account, document IDs/hashes, operation, destination, provider/model, approval, and outcome without ordinary-log bodies.\n\n**R-8 — Untrusted content and bypass resistance.** Imported records, web pages, prompts, and tool output MUST NOT grant capabilities, alter policy, or widen reader sets. Every client/tool path MUST use broker and restricted execution controls, including shell, foreign MCP, runtime files, shared stores, and planted code.\n\n**R-9 — Verification and operator transparency.** Tests and status MUST cover policy decisions, grant expiry/revocation, provider posture, key/lock state, deletion residue, and audit completeness. “Local-only,” “zero retention,” and “deleted” MUST be backed by a measured check with stated scope.\n\n## Design\n\nPapercusp will extend `authorizePersonalAccess`, Personal Vault grants, disclosure labels/ledger, `sealed-contents`, archive encryption, local embeddings, and restricted-egress enforcement. It will not create a parallel grant or vault system.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  U[Owner / user] --> P[Vault policy service]\n  A[Agent identity + plan run] --> P\n  P --> R[Scoped retrieval gateway]\n  R --> V[(Encrypted vault data)]\n  R --> C[Short-lived context receipt]\n  C --> I[Inference broker]\n  I --> L[Local model]\n  I --> E[Approved external model]\n  C --> X[Action broker]\n  X --> S[Send / export / mutate]\n  P --> AU[Content-free audit + revoke]\n```\n\nThe retrieval gateway alone decrypts or returns vault plaintext. Brokers accept receipts, not raw authority. Privacy reader sets intersect as restricted records are read, so additional sensitive records can only narrow allowed destinations.\n\nExternal model policy records endpoint behavior, retention/training terms, region, caching, files, tracing, and third-party tools. Provider claims have expiry and review. Encryption reuses organization envelope/key-version code with personal scope and separate custody; search leakage is documented. Action execution is a typed non-model seam; credentials are injected only there.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-005, P-008 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-008 | tree |\n\n## Acceptance bar\n\n- Cross-user, cross-agent, and cross-plan retrieval fails closed.\n- A read grant cannot invoke external inference, export, or send without its matching capability.\n- Expiry and revocation hold across retrieval, inference, and action races.\n- Private mode produces no provider traffic, including retries, telemetry, caches, or tools.\n- External mode sends only approved minimum fields to the named provider/region and records its policy decision.\n- Prompt injection cannot change grants, destinations, or tool permissions.\n- Content, embeddings, indexes, caches, traces, exports, and backups meet the documented policy.\n- Key rotation/recovery work; locked or unavailable keys never fall back to plaintext.\n- Purge evidence distinguishes removed data, pending backup expiry, and legal holds.\n- Audit records are attributable and content-minimized.\n- Existing vault suites plus new policy, broker, crypto, lifecycle, and egress tests pass.\n\n## Phase 1 — Policy and retrieval\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Define typed Personal Vault capabilities and grant schema, including purpose, source/account, time/volume bounds, expiration, approver, and migration compatibility.\n- **P-002** `todo` Implement the single retrieval gateway and short-lived context receipts; route search, ask, ambient recall, archive, and sealed-content reads through it.\n\n## Phase 2 — Inference and storage\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Implement the inference broker with local-only default, external provider policy, minimum excerpts, revocation recheck, and no-egress enforcement.\n- **P-004** `todo` Extend envelope/key-version encryption to personal records and derived indexes, with key custody, rotation, recovery, lock behavior, and search leakage documentation.\n\n## Phase 3 — Actions and lifecycle\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Implement the typed action broker for sends, exports, provider mutations, and credentials, including reader-set checks, approvals, limits, and bypass resistance.\n- **P-006** `todo` Implement vault lock, step-up authentication, revocation races, receipt invalidation, background-job stop, and owner-visible lock/recovery status.\n\n## Phase 4 — Retention, audit, and verification\n\n- **P-007** `todo` Implement lineage-aware retention/deletion receipts and content-minimized audit records across primary data, derivatives, caches, traces, exports, backups, and legal holds.\n- **P-008** `todo` Build acceptance and operational verification for isolation, prompt injection, enumeration, no-egress, provider policy, ciphertext/index inspection, key lifecycle, deletion propagation, action policy, and status checks.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Superseded by the merged privacy and reliable execution plan\nDate: 2026-10-17\nAffects: personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17\nAvi directed on 2026-10-17: “Combine the the 2 unstarted plans into a single plan with all of your recommendations from this discussion”. Canonical successor: personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17, titled Personal Vault — privacy, security and reliable agent execution. The successor preserves this plan's P-001..P-007 as P-001..P-007 and carries P-008 through P-008/P-016; it also contains the source-item and requirement mapping tables. This draft is archived as superseded, not implemented or completed. Do not start its items independently; use the successor. Measured: plans:get showed this draft unstarted at version 1; plans:set-archived receipt confirmed archived:true. Successor plan creation/readback confirmed draft with 17 items.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"tracing-failure-recovery-and-data-governance-2026-10-16","title":"Tracing, failure recovery and model data governance","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-16","owner":null,"archived":true,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Tracing, failure recovery and model data governance\nslug: tracing-failure-recovery-and-data-governance-2026-10-16\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-16\nupdated: 2026-10-17\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-17, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty. Next repair: Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nDraft for Avi's review. This request authorizes planning and comparison only. No implementation workers, product edits, collector installation, plan activation or external telemetry export have been started.\n\nThe scope is exactly: OpenTelemetry plus a collector; DLQ-style failure handling; enforced model-data governance. Governance is an extension/verification lane over existing enterprise implementation, not a duplicate enterprise project.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Papercusp operators diagnosing agent work, enterprise administrators controlling data destinations, and developers maintaining workflow and model integrations.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Workflow, tool, model and policy evidence exists in several ledgers, but the inspected application wiring does not establish a correlated OpenTelemetry pipeline or one consistent failed-work recovery journey. New telemetry and recovery payloads can introduce additional data sinks unless they inherit the enterprise policy contract.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Follow a permitted operation across API, durable workflow, agent, tool and model boundaries; find and safely recover failed work; enforce the existing enterprise data policy on the new paths with useful denial evidence.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Adopt Redis, Kafka or Datadog.\",\n    \"Build NRTM or shared-session features.\",\n    \"Replace Postgres/DBOS, existing governance policy, audit ledgers or enterprise administration.\",\n    \"Re-implement enterprise roadmap items already owned elsewhere.\",\n    \"Export raw prompts, retrieved documents, secrets or complete evaluation evidence by default.\",\n    \"Start implementation, activate this draft or launch workers as part of this planning request.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:10\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:12\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Write \\\"OpenTelemetry + a collector\\\", \\\"DLQ-style failure handling\\\" and \\\"Enforced model-data governance\\\" into a plan; skip the others; explain alternatives and current use.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:10\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Check overlap with the enterprise-features plan.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:12\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"product-choice\",\n      \"text\": \"Use a companion plan for tracing and cross-cutting failure recovery; retain existing enterprise governance ownership. No parallel policy engine.\",\n      \"material\": true,\n      \"resolved\": true\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"product-choice\",\n      \"text\": \"Recommend the standard OpenTelemetry Collector for the initial local-only supported profile; qualify it against Alloy and the existing-ledger baseline in P-001. This is an author-proposed engineering default, not an owner approval or a paid-backend selection.\",\n      \"material\": true,\n      \"resolved\": true\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"assumption\",\n      \"text\": \"The first acceptance profile can be an isolated current-build operator and background executor with fake model/tool endpoints and a local collector sink. P-001 must pin its actual components and measurable overhead budget.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"scenarios\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-001\",\n      \"title\": \"Explain a delayed agent operation\",\n      \"kind\": \"normal\",\n      \"trigger\": \"An allowed API operation queues durable work that launches an agent, calls a tool and reaches a model.\",\n      \"action\": \"Follow trace identity and linked attempts through existing operation records and the collector output.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Queue wait, execution and external-call time are distinguishable; restart or replay does not invent new business effects.\",\n      \"requirementIds\": [\n        \"R-1\",\n        \"R-2\",\n        \"R-7\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-002\",\n      \"title\": \"Recover a failed operation safely\",\n      \"kind\": \"recovery\",\n      \"trigger\": \"A selected durable operation exhausts its retry policy.\",\n      \"action\": \"An authorized operator inspects safe failure metadata, corrects the cause and requests one supported replay.\",\n      \"outcome\": \"Failure history and attempt lineage remain; Final artifact shipment is a distinct P-010 observation.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### OpenTelemetry decision and alternatives\n\nRecommend OpenTelemetry API/instrumentation and OTLP as the standard boundary, with the smallest supported local collector deployment. Reuse DBOS instrumentation and avoid competing global tracer providers or duplicate workflow spans. Enable required optional dependencies explicitly only where used.\n\nThe Collector receives/processes/forwards signals; it is not a trace database or dashboard. For acceptance use a local recording sink. Production destination and long-term trace storage remain explicit configuration choices; no SaaS service or paid backend is selected. Existing admin ledgers remain usable without an external backend.\n\n| Choice | Specific tradeoff | Decision |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Standard OpenTelemetry Collector | Vendor-neutral processors/receivers/exporters; small supported component set can serve the initial profile. | Recommended starting collector, qualified in P-001/P-004. |\n| Grafana Alloy | OpenTelemetry distribution with built-in Prometheus pipelines and integrations for logs/profiles. | Compare deployment/maintenance value if we need those signals; not an alternative tracing standard. |\n| Existing PostgreSQL activity ledgers + metrics/log collection | Lowest new infrastructure and durable local evidence; requires custom correlation/search and does not inherently supply cross-process trace context. | Keep as authoritative evidence and compare as the minimal baseline. |\n| Vendor-specific APM SDK | More packaged product integration, but vendor coupling and a new data/export boundary. | Record as an alternative; no vendor adoption in this scope. |\n| Prometheus | Strong metrics/alerting; cannot alone reconstruct one agent operation's span chain. | Complement or narrower option, not a complete replacement. |\n| Linux eBPF instrumentation (for example Beyla) | Automatic HTTP/gRPC spans and RED metrics; Linux permissions/platform constraints and no intrinsic business-level workflow semantics. | Optional later supplement, not required by this plan. |\n\nReferences: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/ ; https://grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest/introduction/ ; https://prometheus.io/docs/introduction/overview/ ; https://grafana.com/docs/beyla/latest/ . These are product-fit alternatives, not authorization to install them.\n\n### Reused implementation seams\n\nTracing: packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/bootstrap.ts; dbos/event-reaction-workflow.ts; endpoint-route/telemetry.ts; projected-tool-deps.ts; existing invocation/operation IDs. Preserve correlation through durable enqueue and process launch rather than depending only on an in-process context manager. Span attempts use parent/link relationships consistent with workflow replay; never infer fresh execution from DBOS replayed outputs.\n\nFailure handling: existing DBOS workflow/status/steps, events/reaction-dedup.ts and current connector/SIEM outboxes. Prefer a projection and operation-specific recovery adapters. Any durable field/table added must have a recorded gap analysis and migration/retention treatment. An original failure and its replay are linked immutable history, not a reset that erases evidence.\n\nGovernance: governance-policy/inherited-policy.ts, enforce.ts, session-governance.ts, processing-route.ts; auth/hosted/customer-data-map.ts; data-governance/pilot-processing-map.ts; existing source ACL/disclosure, redaction, customer-key and SIEM surfaces. These already implement enterprise policy; this plan inventories actual outbound paths before proposing an extension.\n\nOperational versus security evidence: operational spans may be sampled or dropped under a documented degradation policy. Required authorization and security audit evidence retains the enterprise fail-closed and retention contract. Collector failure cannot silently downgrade that contract.\n\nThe collector must authenticate/isolate its receive/export boundary, accept only approved operational attributes, reject untrusted context/baggage as authority, and avoid raw payload logging. Apply data minimization before export; a collector-side scrub is defense in depth. Permission-restricted failed payloads use protected references and current authorization rather than an always-visible copy.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-003, P-008 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-004, P-008 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-005, P-008 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006, P-008 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-007, P-008 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-002, P-006, P-008 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-001, P-004, P-008 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-008, P-009, P-010 | deployed |\n\nAll implementation acceptance uses isolated current-build routes. R-8 is final release acceptance: its P-008/P-009 preparation uses current-build, and P-010 alone adds exact shipped-artifact evidence. Enterprise final-release claims remain under the enterprise plan.\n\n### Verification contract\n\nFreeze a manageable selected population in P-001: one permitted API-to-DBOS-to-agent/tool/model journey; its duplicate/restart variants; selected workflow/reaction and existing delivery failures; allowed and denied policy cases; tenant/read-only/revoked-authority cases; collector outage and recovery; and the supported packaging profile. Explicitly list unsupported operations rather than implying universal replay support.\n\nUse project-native Vitest/integration and relevant UI/e2e suites. The named requirement paths are extension targets; P-001 must identify which already exist and which tests must be delivered. No filename or receipt parser proves behavior alone. Cover one actual allowed journey and hostile/counterexample branches with recording sinks and observed effects, source-bound assertions and no skipped required paths. Never attach experimental DBOS workers to the shared live system database or enqueue crash drills on live queues.\n\nOverhead is measured against a repeated pinned baseline before the implementation is accepted; P-001 records the proposed budget and procedure for review. Operational capacity follows the existing governor; do not add fixed maximum-agent/worker/queue/batch defaults.\n\n## Phase 1 — Qualify the existing surfaces and boundaries\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Freeze the supported current-build profile, operation/failure/source/sink population and reuse/ownership matrix; verify DBOS tracing/version/dependencies and current runtime collector/export configuration; compare standard Collector, Alloy and the existing-ledger baseline; record trace retention/destination choices, an overhead budget and any actual governance gaps. Acceptance: reviewable source-to-runtime map and alternatives decision, explicit unknowns, exact test-extension paths and no duplicate enterprise work. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Extend the existing enterprise governance contract only where P-001 demonstrates a missing tracing/failure/replay boundary; specify safe attribute/payload references, current-policy checks, destination/provider/region/classification decisions, revocation and audit behavior through the same enterprise modules. Acceptance: allowed and denied recording-sink tests and an updated single processing map; no parallel policy engine. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n\n## Phase 2 — Trace execution and operate the collector\n\n- **P-003** `todo` Correlate the selected API, DBOS enqueue/dequeue, agent launch, tool and model operations using existing identities and DBOS/OpenTelemetry hooks; persist necessary context through durable/process boundaries and link retry/recovery attempts without duplicate completed side effects or conflicting tracer providers. Acceptance: inspectable linked spans with separate queue/execution timing and restart/duplicate controls. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Package the selected local collector and OTLP configuration through existing runtime/install surfaces, implement approved metadata-only export and collector/export health, and exercise outage/degradation/recovery against the frozen overhead baseline. Acceptance: local recording sink receives permitted spans only; legitimate work continues through collector failure with truthful loss/export status. blocked-by: P-002, P-003 importance: high\n\n## Phase 3 — Find and safely recover failed work\n\n- **P-005** `todo` Project the selected DBOS, reaction and delivery failures into one scoped recovery view over existing authoritative records, preserving owner, cause, attempts, status, protected input references and next action. Acceptance: retryable/denied/exhausted/canceled/ambiguous examples remain discoverable after restart without a competing state machine. blocked-by: P-001, P-002 importance: high\n- **P-006** `todo` Implement operation-specific replay/resume adapters over existing recovery mechanisms with current authorization, atomic duplicate protection, immutable lineage and completed-effect reconciliation. Acceptance: concurrent replay, permission revocation, cross-tenant, version mismatch and ambiguous-effect controls; unsupported recovery is explicit. blocked-by: P-003, P-005 importance: high\n- **P-007** `todo` Extend existing admin/operation views with failure inspection, trace correlation and permitted recovery actions. Follow the component-registry/spec validation workflow before UI design. Acceptance: an authorized operator completes inspect-correct-replay-confirm; read-only and foreign-tenant users cannot access or act beyond their scope; safe denial and unsupported-action explanations. blocked-by: P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n## Phase 4 — Verify, document and prepare shipment\n\n- **P-008** `todo` Run the frozen integrated population in isolated current-build DBOS and collector runtimes, including successful work, failure/retry/restart, duplicate replay, policy refusal/revocation, secret/content canaries, tenant isolation, collector outage and measured overhead. Acceptance: project-native assertion/fixture/source identities plus runtime and UI receipts, explicit checked/notChecked/notApplicable population and owned residue; no live queues or fabricated full-coverage claim. blocked-by: P-004, P-006, P-007 importance: high\n- **P-009** `todo` Document supported operation classes, collector configuration/destinations, policy/retention boundaries, recovery runbooks, packaging/upgrade/rollback and enterprise evidence handoff. Acceptance: one maintained operating guide, explicit unsupported cases and references back to enterprise P-008/P-021/P-022 rather than duplicate ownership. blocked-by: P-008\n- **P-010** `todo` After plan/route approval and implementation acceptance, verify the exact promoted/released artifact and collector configuration, upgrade/rollback and governance behavior for the selected profile; deliver shipment evidence. This is the sole deployed-only step because installed artifact/configuration identity cannot be proved by a staging source run. Acceptance: actual final artifact receipts, limitations and operating ownership; no force past a red gate. blocked-by: P-009 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Exactly three selected areas; draft only\n\nAvi selected OpenTelemetry plus a collector, DLQ-style failure handling and enforced model-data governance, asked to skip the others, and requested a plan and detailed summary. Redis, Kafka, Datadog adoption, NRTM and shared-session feature work are excluded. No implementation execution route or activation is inferred from permission to draft.\n\n### D-002 — Enterprise governance remains the authority\n\nThe roadmap already owns inherited policy (P-005), core data governance (P-007), audit/SIEM (P-008) and provider/region/classification/private-processing/key extensions (P-016). Their recorded done state is implementation evidence only; integrated acceptance remains separate. This plan reuses those surfaces and adds only demonstrated new-boundary work, retaining existing owners for existing defects. No mutation of the enterprise plan is part of drafting.\n\n### D-003 — Recommend OpenTelemetry; qualify the collector and keep destinations explicit\n\nReuse DBOS instrumentation and plain compatibility adapters carefully. Recommend the standard Collector initially, with Alloy compared as a distribution option. Keep canonical ledgers and security exports authoritative; traces are optional operational projections. Collector storage/viewer choice is separate, and no external service or raw payload export is defaulted on.\n\n### D-004 — DBOS remains the execution authority\n\nFailure handling is a recovery journey over existing workflow/reaction/outbox records, not a new message broker or scheduler. Interrupted steps may execute again; every supported redrive must prove idempotency or require reconciliation. Tests use isolated DBOS storage.\n\n### D-005 — Superseded by the merged privacy and reliable execution plan\nDate: 2026-10-17\nAffects: personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17\nAvi directed consolidation of both unstarted drafts on 2026-10-17. Canonical successor: personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17. Old-to-new mapping: P-001→P-009, P-002→P-010, P-003→P-011, P-004→P-012, P-005→P-013, P-006→P-014, P-007→P-015, P-008→P-016, P-009/P-010→P-017. The successor retains OpenTelemetry/Collector, accountable failed work, safe replay, privacy/enterprise policy reuse, alternatives, isolated testing and exact final-artifact evidence. This source draft is archived as superseded; no work is claimed implemented. Do not start it independently. Measured: plans:get showed this draft unstarted at version 3; plans:set-archived confirmed archived:true; successor readback confirmed the single merged draft.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010\n\n## Review and activation prerequisites\n\nPresent the product walkthrough and this enterprise overlap map to Avi. Before activation: re-read the complete canonical source conversation, record the activation audit, re-read governing enterprise decisions, settle material collector/destination/retention/overhead choices and confirm the implementation route. No fleet or route is offered here because implementation has not been requested.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"work-queue-exclusion-alarm-duplicates-2026-10-16","title":"Keep alarm conditions and duplicate reports out of the admitted work queue","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-16","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Keep alarm conditions and duplicate reports out of the admitted work queue\nslug: work-queue-exclusion-alarm-duplicates-2026-10-16\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-16\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-17, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_work_contract_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing. condition/attention surface and cannot mint admitted scheduler work-items.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Alarm-condition events stay on the condition/attention surface and cannot mint admitted controls; compare persisted admission and payload.\\n\\nR4 grades unresolved adjudication state independently of condition source. Frozen1188995/96/native1188997 remain unapplied; historical adequacy supplies no fresh parser signature, amendment/apply, grade, activation or shipment authorization.\nRelated: P-002\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"generalize-install-assumptions-2026-10-17","title":"Generalize hard-coded install, workspace and platform assumptions","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-17","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Generalize hard-coded install, workspace and platform assumptions\nslug: generalize-install-assumptions-2026-10-17\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-17\nupdated: 2026-10-18\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Avi authorized AUTO self delivery through shipped. Driver WI-6554700010017007; route this session, no implementation fan-out (D-001). Source conversation0–22 audited and activation audit1 recorded at revision5. Requirements now carry executable METHOD/check/layer/falsifier contracts and implementation conformance;14-bar acceptance rubric seeded.15 sourceBar-pinned AUTO-BAR clauses promoted active; extra P003 state-home data-integrity clause active. No source implementation yet. Start is progressing through spec-quality/required acceptance preflight; all15 items remain unfinished.\n\n**Next:** Finish current spec-quality scorecard and any required non-author acceptance checks, start the plan, claim P001, then implement and verify the detector before any migrations. Preserve full scope and actual shipped-evidence requirement.\n\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi as owner; anyone running Papercusp somewhere other than this dev box (a second machine, a second workspace, another hive on the green gate, the macOS/Windows desktop builds); agents adding the next client, model or provider.\n\n**Problem.** Product code bakes in this machine's specifics: the checkout folder `~/papercupai-workspace`, a hand-built `~/.papercusp`, the dogfood workspace `papercusp-workspace`, the repo slug `papercusp`, the branch names `staging`/`main`, ports 3070/3170/9071/8788, Linux-only system calls, and the `/mnt/data` mount. Core lists (agent clients, model ids, endpoints, env vars, provider keys) are copied in dozens of places. None of it fails a test, because the tests run on exactly the setup the literals describe. Evidence: audit report rpt_8353969a-4b7d-489e-b1c2-5a2b3f3abc33.\n\n**Outcome.** With a non-default home folder, checkout folder, workspace, ports or platform, Papercusp either works or reports \"not supported here\"; it never silently does nothing or acts on the wrong target. Adding a client, model or provider is one registry edit. A lint with a shrink-only baseline blocks new instances.\n\n**Non-goals.** Translating on-screen text; auditing numeric thresholds and timeouts; changing the dogfood-workspace concept itself (it stays, it just stops being a fallback); supporting forges other than GitHub; multi-person workspaces (the `'human'` owner address); auditing SQL migrations.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner directive #1963 (audit request, 2026-10-17); owner directive #1971 (\"Yes, draft the full plan\", choosing the full option from escalation mvcy9zps).\n\n**Scenarios.**\n- S1. Avi installs Papercusp on a second machine whose checkouts live in `~/code`. Disk cleanup, red-test matching and locks all work there.\n- S2. An isolated instance sets only `PAPERCUSP_HOME`. All of its state, including the database key, lands under that folder; the real `~/.papercusp` is untouched.\n- S3. A watchdog runs in a workspace other than `papercusp-workspace` and reports on that workspace, not the dogfood one.\n- S4. Another hive (e.g. oddsmith) on the green gate uses its own branch names. Its gate watchdogs and parity checks are about it.\n- S5. An agent adds a fourth agent client. One registry entry; every launcher, hook and UI picks it up; a leftover hard-coded list fails lint.\n- S6. A model is retired. One catalog edit moves every purpose that used it.\n- S7. On the macOS desktop, Linux-only host checks answer \"not supported on this platform\" instead of a silent empty result that reads as healthy.\n- S8. Someone adds `~/papercupai-workspace` or a bare port number in new code; lint fails with a pointer to the resolver.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Detector.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"A portability lint covers dev-box folder literals, hand-built `~/.papercusp`, fallbacks to `papercusp-workspace` or `papercusp`, port numbers outside the endpoint resolver, re-declared client lists, unregistered `PAPERCUSP_*` reads, `/mnt/data`, and raw branch refs outside release-config. Its baseline is seeded from a measuring `--list` run, can only shrink, and runs where the gate runs.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A portability lint covers dev-box folder literals, hand-built `~/.papercusp`, fallbacks to `papercusp-workspace` or `papercusp`, port numbers outside the endpoint resolver, re-declared client lists, unregistered `PAPERCUSP_*` reads, `/mnt/data`, and raw branch refs outside release-config. Its baseline is seeded from a measuring `--list` run, can only shrink, and runs where the gate runs.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A specified R-1 family is undetected, a new offender/baseline increase passes, or the check is absent from the gate lint leg.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Measure detector --list on canonical runtime sources; prove every R-1 family with positive and negative fixtures, reject a new offender and baseline growth, and verify the check is reachable from the configured lint leg.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/install-assumptions-detector.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Second-environment proof.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"An automated run with a non-default HOME/PAPERCUSP_HOME, checkout folder, workspace id and ports demonstrates S1–S3 (and S7 where the platform allows).\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"An automated run with a non-default HOME/PAPERCUSP_HOME, checkout folder, workspace id and ports demonstrates S1–S3 (and S7 where the platform allows).\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A fixture targets the default home/dogfood workspace/dev-box directory/port, or an unsupported platform reports empty success.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"integration\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Start an isolated current-build process with temporary HOME/PAPERCUSP_HOME, a checkout under a different parent, a non-dogfood workspace and nondefault endpoints. Exercise resolver, retention discovery and test-path normalization against fixtures and assert the real default home is untouched; assert explicit unsupported platform responses for injected non-Linux platform.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/install-portability.integration.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — One workspace-root resolver.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"All 12 re-implementations of the checkout-root default use one resolver; stored test paths are repo-relative at write time and no SQL or regex strips a folder name; retention roots derive from the resolver and configured data mounts.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"All 12 re-implementations of the checkout-root default use one resolver; stored test paths are repo-relative at write time and no SQL or regex strips a folder name; retention roots derive from the resolver and configured data mounts.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Any listed consumer retains an independent root fallback or normalizes by the literal dev-box folder; configured retention roots or test matches differ by folder name.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise the shared workspace-root resolver and each migrated test-path/retention consumer with two non-default directory layouts, nested paths and already-relative paths. Compare written test paths and reader matching without folder-name stripping.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-root-portability.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-4 — One home-folder resolver.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"`papercuspHome()` lives in `libs/host-platform` and every hand-built `~/.papercusp` site uses it, so `PAPERCUSP_HOME` is honored everywhere, including the database key default.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"`papercuspHome()` lives in `libs/host-platform` and every hand-built `~/.papercusp` site uses it, so `PAPERCUSP_HOME` is honored everywhere, including the database key default.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A production consumer bypasses papercuspHome/PAPERCUSP_HOME, the database key lands in the real default state folder, or a competing resolver stays authoritative.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise papercuspHome with explicit state override, alternate HOME and platform-aware paths; run migrated db-encryption key path and state consumers under an isolated home and inspect detector residue to ensure no hand-built production home remains.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"libs/host-platform/src/install-home.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-5 — No dogfood-workspace fallback.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"No runtime path falls back to `papercusp-workspace`; the workspace is a required argument or comes from `activeWorkspaceId()`.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"No runtime path falls back to `papercusp-workspace`; the workspace is a required argument or comes from `activeWorkspaceId()`.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A runtime path substitutes papercusp-workspace or silently targets another workspace when context is absent.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise representative watchdog, sweep, plan-scope, spend-cap and desktop-session entry points with an explicit alternate workspace, an active workspace and missing context; require exact target preservation or a typed missing-context refusal, then scan runtime fallback residue.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-context-portability.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Release machinery is per-hive.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The install/harness slug is required, every branch ref goes through release-config, and gate legs come from the hive's config rather than hard-coded npm script names.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The install/harness slug is required, every branch ref goes through release-config, and gate legs come from the hive's config rather than hard-coded npm script names.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Release/parity/actuator behavior uses papercusp, staging/main or fixed npm gate names despite the selected hive config.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Use two hive release configs with different install slugs, candidate/green branches and gate leg names; exercise parity and watchdog/actuator composition and assert missing install identity is refused.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/release/hive-config-portability.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Agent client registry.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"One capability-keyed registry (hooks, resume, carry, MCP) replaces every re-declared claude/codex/omp list.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"One capability-keyed registry (hooks, resume, carry, MCP) replaces every re-declared claude/codex/omp list.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A registry addition needs a second hard-coded client list edit or an unsupported capability is silently assumed.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Add a fourth synthetic client through the canonical registry and assert launcher/hook/resume/carry/MCP/UI capability enumeration sees it. Test unsupported capabilities explicitly and scan duplicated runtime client-list residue.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-client-registry.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Model catalog.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"One catalog with purpose names (for example fast classifier, default worker); generic libraries take a purpose name or a required model argument, never a hard-coded default.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"One catalog with purpose names (for example fast classifier, default worker); generic libraries take a purpose name or a required model argument, never a hard-coded default.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A retired catalog model remains selected through an independent runtime default/table or a generic library supplies its own model default.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise all migrated purpose consumers against an injected purpose catalog and retire one model in that catalog; verify launch/window/gateway/chat/TUI resolution moves consistently and generic libraries require a model/purpose.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/model-purpose-catalog.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Endpoint resolver.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"One resolver covers operator, staging, gateway, proxy and Vite endpoints, and port numbers appear nowhere else (including `apps/operator-vite/flags-bootstrap.ts`).\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"One resolver covers operator, staging, gateway, proxy and Vite endpoints, and port numbers appear nowhere else (including `apps/operator-vite/flags-bootstrap.ts`).\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A migrated consumer ignores configured endpoints or runtime port defaults remain outside the canonical endpoint resolver.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Resolve operator, staging, gateway, proxy and Vite endpoints under alternate ports/hosts including flags bootstrap, service-health and pipeline consumers; validate malformed inputs and scan port-literal residue.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-registry-portability.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Environment-variable registry.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"A typed registry (name, type, default, owner, description) generates the docs; synonyms for one concept collapse to one name; on/off switches move into `libs/flags`.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"A typed registry (name, type, default, owner, description) generates the docs; synonyms for one concept collapse to one name; on/off switches move into `libs/flags`.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A runtime read is unregistered, generated docs drift, synonyms disagree or an ordinary on/off switch bypasses flags.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Compare runtime PAPERCUSP_* reads with typed registry entries and generated docs; validate type/default metadata, canonical-name precedence and legacy-alias compatibility. Verify on/off switches resolve through the existing flags registry.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/environment-registry.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-11 — Provider-key list.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"One list feeds save_key, the settings pages and the secrets-guard hook.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"One list feeds save_key, the settings pages and the secrets-guard hook.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Provider surfaces disagree on supported keys, require multiple list edits or fail to recognize an enrolled key in the secrets guard.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Add a synthetic provider-key entry to the shared registry and exercise save-key validation, integration settings options and secrets-guard matching; verify unknown keys are rejected and secret values never enter generated docs.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/provider-key-registry.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-12 — Platform seam.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Linux-only host operations (service status, logs, process inspection) go through `libs/host-platform` with an explicit unsupported answer, and systemd unit names and data mounts come from configuration.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Linux-only host operations (service status, logs, process inspection) go through `libs/host-platform` with an explicit unsupported answer, and systemd unit names and data mounts come from configuration.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A raw Linux-only operation bypasses host-platform or configured service/mount selection, or unsupported platform returns apparent success.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Exercise service/log/process adapters with injected Linux and non-Linux platforms, configured service names and data mounts; assert unsupported is a typed result distinct from empty healthy output and check production consumers use the seam.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"libs/host-platform/src/host-operations.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-13 — Generic libraries are generic.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"`libs/generic/deployment-driver`, `verification-harness`, `memory` and `search-core` carry no papercusp names, mounts or model defaults; each is parameterized or moved out of `libs/generic`.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"`libs/generic/deployment-driver`, `verification-harness`, `memory` and `search-core` carry no papercusp names, mounts or model defaults; each is parameterized or moved out of `libs/generic`.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A generic package requires a Papercusp name/mount/model or silently substitutes one despite caller-supplied configuration.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run parameterized deployment-driver, verification-harness, memory and search-core consumers with non-Papercusp names, directories and injected model choices; scan those runtime packages for retained product-specific defaults.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"libs/generic/deployment-driver/src/portability.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-14 — Shared prompts are stack-neutral.**\n\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"The base blueprint's `infra-reviewer.md` uses pot-provided endpoints and commands, and the morning brief's timezone comes from a workspace/owner setting.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The base blueprint's `infra-reviewer.md` uses pot-provided endpoints and commands, and the morning brief's timezone comes from a workspace/owner setting.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"Shared prompt output contains the development stack's endpoint/commands or ignores the workspace/owner timezone.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Render infra-reviewer under two pot stacks with different endpoint/test/build commands and render the morning brief under two configured timezones; inspect canonical prompt source and assert no fixed npm/port/timezone assumptions.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/shared-prompt-portability.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nProposed, pending owner approval:\n\n- Detectors first, so every later item shrinks a measured baseline rather than an estimate. P-002 to P-013 depend on P-001.\n- Reuse existing seams instead of new ones: `libs/host-platform` (home folder, platform), `activeWorkspaceId()`, release-config, `SU_SESSION_BACKENDS` as the seed of the client registry, `libs/flags` for switches.\n- The six audit items are absorbed, not duplicated: WI-6554700010016980 (lint half) → P-001; WI-6554700010016975 and WI-6554700010016976 → P-002; WI-6554700010016977 → P-003; WI-6554700010016978 → P-004; WI-6554700010016979 → P-005; WI-6554700010016980 (second-environment half) → P-014.\n- Large migrations (P-003 home folder, P-009 env vars) proceed directory by directory, each step lowering the lint baseline.\n- Phases 2 to 4 touch mostly disjoint files, so they can run in parallel after P-001.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n|
