freeze that holds its own invariant","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-17","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make main's failing count non-increasing by construction: ratchet promotion, and a freeze that holds its own invariant\nslug: green-main-ratchet-convergence-2026-10-17\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-17\nupdated: 2026-10-21\n---\n\n## Goal\nmain's failing-test count can only stay flat or fall, and main advances whenever a candidate introduces no new failures. Green main becomes the end of a monotone sequence, not a single perfect run.\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: the owner, plus every agent whose work waits on main and on the :3070 deploy (the fleet's own control plane runs there).\n\nProblem: main was last green 2026-10-02 10:54Z (d740fc38). The frozen-candidate system was meant to get one candidate green, but its count does not converge.\n- Queue ad82b273 was frozen for 161h over 24 rounds. Its failing count went 3 -> 28 and rose in 8 of 23 steps (report rpt_c1597a17).\n- A frozen candidate's code changes only by admitted fixes, so a rising count means the freeze's own invariant is broken.\n- A bounded-life rule (green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08 P-021) now retires a queue after 24h, or after 4 rounds without a new low, and re-cuts onto newer staging code. That re-imports ungated staging breakage every day: 8,953 commits since main was last green, and the source-side check completed only 3 of about 261 slots in its last ~24h.\n- Four queues since 10-13 started at 8-36 failures, bottomed out at 6-9, and none reached 0 (report rpt_f4553ecc).\n- Promotion requires zero failures across a radius that now spans 15,616 changed files.\n\nOutcome:\n1. Inside a freeze, the failing count never rises.\n2. main advances whenever a candidate adds no new failures. It carries an owned known-failing ledger that only shrinks.\n3. Ledger size, and new failures introduced vs. fixed per day, are visible and alarmed.\n\nNon-goals:\n- Fixing the specific currently-failing tests; ledger owners fix them through normal work.\n- Replacing the gate runner or git-sync's commit model, adding test frameworks, or changing deploy mechanics.\n- The cycle-time work in green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08, which is complementary. Its bounded-life rule and red attribution are reused here, not replaced.\n\nSource turns (all [owner 2026-10-17], session claude:ed0df986-266c-4395-826a-505cace2fea1):\n- Owner directive #1947: think from first principles about whether the design should make failing counts come down, and what to improve if not.\n- Answer to the next-step question: \"#3 [draft redesign plan now] but I thought we had a frozen candidate system, we should be trying to get the frozen candidate green, not the tip of staging, so your diagnosis doesn't make sense unless that system isn't working, is that system not working?\"\n- Answer to the ratchet question: \"#1 [yes, ratchet main] but who decides which failing tests are acceptable? What should be their guidance?\"\n\nScenarios:\n- S1: A candidate fails exactly the ledger's tests, or a subset of them. It is promoted and the ledger shrinks to the candidate's failing set.\n- S2: A candidate fixes 3 ledgered tests and adds 1 new failure attributable to commit X. X is ejected from the candidate, the affected radius is re-tested, and the candidate is promoted. X's author gets a bug for the red.\n- S3: An admission to a frozen repair head fixes 1 test and breaks 2. The admission is rejected automatically, the repair head is unchanged, and the author is told why.\n- S4: A test fails and then passes on the same commit. It moves to an owned flaky quarantine, stops counting toward the gate, and a de-quarantine work-item is filed.\n- S5: A new failure lands in a release-blocking area. It is never ledger-eligible and blocks promotion until fixed.\n- S6: The owner approves the one-time seed (the current frozen candidate's failures, after the release-blocking screen), and main advances off d740fc38.\n\n## Which failures block main: everything, by default (D-002)\n\nAdopted [owner 2026-10-17, D-002]. Every test, and every gate leg (typecheck, lint, build), blocks main unless it carries an active downgrade record. When a blocking test fails, the response order is: fix it; else eject the commit it is attributed to, after confirming the test passes on the base without that commit (D-003); else downgrade it with a written reason, an owned bug, a warning and a digest entry. Downgrades in critical areas are allowed with a forceful warning: an explicit acknowledgement and an immediate owner notice (R10b, D-006).\n\nWhere 'existing' failures come from when everything blocks: (1) the backlog at cutover, handled once by P-005; (2) breaks with no code change (date, external service, timing), which have no commit to eject; (3) tests the gate never ran, because it runs only the tests affected by the delta since the last promotion (AFFECTED_BASE, green-checkpoint.ts), so a break outside that set promotes and surfaces later against an unrelated change. P-001 measures how often (3) happens; P-013 closes it if material.\n\n### Superseded: per-test severity tiers (kept for the record; replaced by D-002)\nOwner proposal [owner 2026-10-17]: every test carries a severity, assigned once in bulk and enforced on every test write. The severity maps to what a failing test blocks, and one of those things is the main gate. This replaces deciding at failure time.\n\nWhy decide when the test is written, not when it fails: a decision made while main is red is made under pressure to unblock, by whichever of hundreds of agents happens to be there. It is inconsistent, and it makes the gate verdict depend on a judgment call. A declared severity is decided calmly, reviewed with the code, consistent, and lint-checkable.\n\nRefinements (proposed):\n- **Three tiers, mapped in one registry,** so a policy change is one edit.\n  - **blocker:** must pass for main to advance and for deploy. Never ledger-eligible. A flaky blocker escalates at once instead of being quietly quarantined.\n  - **standard** (the default): a NEW failure blocks main (the ratchet). An existing failure may stay on the measured, shrink-only ledger with an owner.\n  - **advisory:** never blocks. A failure auto-files an owned bug. Intended for perf, LLM scenarios and exploratory tests.\n- **Derive, then declare.** An area registry gives every path a severity floor:\n  - blocker: migrations/schema, auth/secrets, data integrity, deploy/release, the agent control plane, and the gate itself;\n  - advisory: perf and LLM scenarios.\n  Every test file must declare its severity (lint-enforced on each write). A declaration below the area floor is refused unless it carries a reason.\n- **Protected downgrades.** Lowering a severity cannot take effect in the same candidate where that test fails, and every downgrade appears in the daily digest.\n- **Granularity:** per file, with a per-case override.\n- **Gate legs too.** Typecheck, lint and build legs get tiers in the gate-script registry; typecheck and build are blockers.\n- **One-time bulk pass.** Derive severities for all existing tests from the registry, then review the exceptions. The owner approves the area-to-tier mapping, not each file. This replaces the one-time ledger seed.\n- **Watch the blocker share.** If blockers grow past a set share of the suite, flake exposure comes back, so alarm on it.\n\n### Superseded proposal (kept for the record): who decides which failures are acceptable\n- **Day to day, nobody decides; the rule does.** The ledger is measured, never authored. It is exactly the set of tests failing on main, and it can only shrink. A failure that is not on the ledger blocks promotion. No agent can add an entry.\n- **The only human decision is the one-time seed,** made by the owner, from an explicit list. Guidance for admitting an entry to the seed:\n  - (a) It fails reproducibly on the candidate. A flaky test goes to quarantine instead.\n  - (b) It is not in a release-blocking area.\n  - (c) It has an owner and a work-item.\n  - (d) Shipping it to :3070 does not break something the fleet relies on there today.\n- **Release-blocking areas (never ledger-eligible):** DB migrations and schema; auth, permissions and secrets; data integrity or loss; deploy, rollback and release; build/typecheck of shipped code; the agent control plane (coordination, locks, work-items, MCP dispatch); and the gate itself.\n- **Leaving the ledger:** an entry leaves automatically when the test passes on a promoted candidate. Deleting or skipping a ledgered test needs a recorded reason on its work-item and appears in the daily digest. An entry older than 3 days escalates to its owner's lead and then the owner.\n- **Granularity:** entries are per test case where the runner reports one. A new failing case in an already-ledgered file counts as a NEW failure.\n\n## Rules in brief (labels R1–R10 used in item text)\n- R1 Every test blocks main by default (D-002). Nothing needs declaring. A test is non-blocking only through a recorded downgrade, or when written as non-blocking in an allowed class (perf, LLM scenarios). Gate legs (typecheck, lint, build) follow the same default.\n- R2 Promotion rule: main advances only when no blocking test fails on the candidate, so main is green on every blocking test at every promotion.\n- R3 Downgrade record (the override store): test (per file, with a per-case override where the runner reports cases), written reason, owner, filed bug, author and timestamp. A downgrade shows a warning, appears in the daily digest, and is undone by deleting the record.\n- R10 Downgrade guardrails: (a) the response to a blocking failure is fix, then eject (R5), then downgrade; (b) a downgrade of a test in the critical-area registry (migrations/schema, auth/permissions/secrets, data integrity, deploy/rollback/release, typecheck/build of shipped code, the agent control plane, the gate itself) is allowed with a forceful warning: an explicit acknowledgement naming the area and risk, and an immediate owner notice (D-006); (c) every downgrade is digested and counted (R7).\n- R4 Admission ratchet: an admission advances a repair head only if it adds no failure that was absent at the previous head, measured over the admission's radius. Otherwise it is rejected with the attributed tests named.\n- R5 New-red ejection: a new failure attributed to a specific commit removes that commit from the candidate, re-tests the affected radius, and routes the red to the commit's author. Before ejecting, the failing test is re-run on the base without that commit; if it fails there too, the commit is not the cause and the failure is unattributable (D-003). Only an unattributable failure freezes the candidate, until it is fixed or downgraded under R10.\n- R6 Determinism: a test whose verdict differs on the same commit goes automatically to an owned quarantine and stops counting. Round counts are compared only over the same measured population.\n- R7 Metrics and alarm: downgraded tests currently failing, downgrades per day, and new failures introduced vs. fixed per day. A rubric check alarms when downgrades or downgraded-failing debt grow, or introductions exceed fixes over 24h.\n- R8 The source-side sync-batch check runs on reserved capacity, so host load cannot skip it. Target: at least 95% of slots evaluated.\n- R9 Docs and rules: update the freeze-and-converge guide part, the gate-ownership guidance, and the hand-quarantine rule to the ratchet model.\n\n## Requirements\n\nEach requirement is one acceptance bar, mapped to exactly one plan item (see the bar-to-work map in Design).\n\n**R-1 — A downgrade needs a complete record.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A test downgrade is refused unless it carries a complete downgrade record\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:7\",\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:3\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A test downgrade is refused unless it carries a complete downgrade record\",\"falsifier\":\"FAIL if any is observed: (1) a downgrade is stored without a written reason; (2) without an owner; (3) without a filed bug id; (4) without author or timestamp; (5) a stored downgrade shows no warning in the verb response; (6) a downgrade made today is missing from the daily digest query; (7) deleting the record leaves the test non-blocking. UNKNOWN if the test run for the named file cannot be resolved.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"release-gate\",\"test-downgrades\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\",\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest drives the downgrade validator, the release:test-downgrade verb and the blocking rule over a mocked SQL client (unit), and the Postgres store against the real migrated schema of migration 1530 (integration): each missing field is refused by the validator and by the schema, a complete record is stored with a warning and listed in the daily digest, a second active downgrade for the same case is refused, and a revoke restores blocking.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/release/test-downgrade-store.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/release/test-downgrade-store.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Critical-area downgrades need an explicit acknowledgement.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A critical-area test downgrade is refused unless it carries an explicit risk acknowledgement for that area\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:bebfa512-731b-4f1e-b761-50f0a7da734f:15\",\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:7\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A critical-area test downgrade is refused unless it carries an explicit risk acknowledgement for that area\",\"falsifier\":\"FAIL if any is observed: (1) a test under migrations/schema, auth/permissions/secrets, data integrity, deploy/rollback/release, typecheck/build of shipped code, the agent control plane, or the gate itself is downgraded without an acknowledgement naming its area; (2) an accepted critical-area downgrade produces no immediate owner notice; (3) a non-critical path is classified critical. UNKNOWN if the registry test run cannot be resolved.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"release-gate\",\"critical-areas\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest classifies representative paths per area, then a falsifiability probe shows a critical-area downgrade without the acknowledgement is refused and one with it emits an owner notice.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/release/critical-area-registry.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Promotion only when no blocking test fails.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The gate promotes a candidate only when no blocking test fails on it\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:7\",\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The gate promotes a candidate only when no blocking test fails on it\",\"falsifier\":\"FAIL if any is observed: (1) a candidate with a failing test that has no active downgrade record is promoted; (2) a candidate whose only failures are downgraded tests is held; (3) gate_health lacks the blocking-failure count or the downgraded-failing count; (4) a typecheck, lint or build leg failure is treated as non-blocking without a downgrade. UNKNOWN if the verdict test run cannot be resolved.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"green-checkpoint\",\"release-gate\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest feeds failing sets with and without active downgrade records to decidePromotionRatchet, the promotion rule green-checkpoint uses, and asserts promote vs hold, fail-closed handling of unresolvable files and collection crashes, case-level coverage, and the gate_health blocking and downgraded counts.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/release/promotion-ratchet.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Cutover moves main off d740fc38.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"main advances off d740fc38 under the ratchet promotion rule\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:0\",\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"main advances off d740fc38 under the ratchet promotion rule\",\"falsifier\":\"FAIL if any is observed: (1) origin main still resolves to d740fc38 after cutover; (2) the promotion that moved main was forced past the gate; (3) a failure on the promoted candidate was neither fixed, ejected nor downgraded with a record; (4) the triage report to the owner is absent. UNKNOWN if state:read gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict or the :3070 health sha cannot be read.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredScope\":[\"release-gate\",\"cutover\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"The state-cell probe passes once the :3070 deploy is no longer d740fc38. Record state:read gate.greenCheckpoint.verdict, git rev-parse main before and after, the :3070 /api/health sha, and the published triage report id; PASS requires main past d740fc38 with no force deploy.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"probe\",\"probe\":{\"kind\":\"state-cell\",\"cell\":\"deploy.3070.sha\",\"schemaRevision\":\"live\",\"expect\":{\"path\":\"value\",\"op\":\"ne\",\"value\":\"d740fc3802877d1c8c3b1068768681ee32ef0025\"}}}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Admission ratchet on the repair head.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The repair queue rejects an admission that adds a failure absent at the previous repair head\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:6\",\"session_turn:claude:bebfa512-731b-4f1e-b761-50f0a7da734f:15\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The repair queue rejects an admission that adds a failure absent at the previous repair head\",\"falsifier\":\"FAIL if any is observed: (1) an admission that turns a passing test red advances repairHead; (2) an admission that adds a new test which fails advances repairHead; (3) a refusal does not name the attributed tests; (4) the refusal is not routed to the admitting author; (5) an admission adding no new failure is rejected. (6) an inconclusive measurement (an unmeasured verdict after the admission, or an unmeasured previous verdict for a test that now fails) publishes the admission. UNKNOWN if the ratchet test run cannot be resolved.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"release-gate\",\"repair-queue\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest runs the admission ratchet over previous-head and post-admission verdict sets measured on the admission radius, including the S3 shape and a new failing test.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/release/admission-ratchet.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Blame-checked ejection.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The gate ejects a commit only when its attributed failing test passes on the base without that commit\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:77a3a671-f2b9-46cc-8178-9847b23fa42b:6\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The gate ejects a commit only when its attributed failing test passes on the base without that commit\",\"falsifier\":\"FAIL if any is observed: (1) a commit is ejected while the failing test also fails on the base without it; (2) an attributable new failure freezes the candidate instead of ejecting; (3) the ejected red is not routed to the commit author; (4) after ejection the affected radius is not re-tested before promotion. UNKNOWN while the planner runs in shadow (gate_health.ratchetShadow records a plan for the run but the gate did not act on it), or if the ejection test run cannot be resolved.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"ejection\",\"release-gate\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest drives the pure ejection planner (packages/operator-core/lib/release/new-red-ejection.ts) with base-without-commit verdicts for the S2 shape and an unattributable control. It does not eject, route to authors or change the verdict; ratchet-shadow.test.ts and green-checkpoint-ratchet-shadow.test.ts cover that wiring. UNKNOWN if the determinism test run cannot be resolved.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"release-gate\",\"determinism\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Vitest feeds same-commit verdict histories for the S4 shape and asserts quarantine, ownership and same-population comparison.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/release/verdict-flip-quarantine.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Sync-batch checks run on reserved capacity.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The sync-batch checks evaluate at least 95 percent of five-minute slots under host load\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:bebfa512-731b-4f1e-b761-50f0a7da734f:15\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Host load cannot skip the sync-batch checks: both run every slot on reserved capacity, record per-slot coverage, and alarm when coverage falls below 95 percent over 24 hours\",\"falsifier\":\"FAIL if any is observed: (1) sync-batch-delta-check or sync-batch-lint-guards is skipped because of host load admission; (2) a check does not record one coverage slot per five-minute opportunity, or does not credit a slot whose commits a later run judged within that check's slot-credit deadline (for the delta check COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS, derived in code from its leg budgets per D-031; for the lint guards their fixed deadline; current values are in the method); (3) coverage below 95 percent over at least 144 slots in 24 hours raises no alarm. A test is non-blocking only through an active downgrade record (P-002), or when written as non-blocking in an allowed class (perf, LLM scenarios). The response to a blocking failure is fix, then eject (P-007), then downgrade. A downgrade in a critical area (P-003) needs an explicit acknowledgement naming the area and risk, and notifies the owner immediately.\n- **Flow.**\n  - Cut from the staging tip, or resume the frozen head. Round 1 records every affected test verdict even when an early typecheck or lint leg fails (P-016), tracked per test case and per typecheck/lint error (P-017).\n  - If no blocking test fails, promote (P-004).\n  - Otherwise attribute each new failure. Blame-check it on the base without the commit, then eject the commit (P-007).\n  - Only unattributable failures freeze the candidate. A freeze admits fixes under the admission ratchet (P-006): an admission that adds any failure, including a new failing test, is rejected.\n  - After an admission, re-run only what the fix can affect. A fix whose transpiled JavaScript is unchanged triggers no runtime tests, and a lint leg re-runs only if it failed or its inputs changed. The promotion proof is composed from round 1 plus each admission's radius, with the full gate kept only when a radius cannot be computed (P-018, D-008).\n  - Same-commit verdict flips leave the count (P-008). A periodic full-suite run of main backstops dependency-graph misses (P-013). Sync-batch checks on reserved capacity catch breaks before they reach a candidate (P-009). Metrics and an alarm show whether fixing outpaces breaking (P-010).\n- **Why this converges.** main is green on every blocking test at every promotion, so its failing count cannot rise. The admission ratchet makes a freeze non-increasing apart from nondeterminism, which P-008 removes from the count. Like-for-like measurement (P-016) stops population growth from reading as regression. The P-010 metric shows whether fixes outpace breaks.\n- **Reuse, don't fork.** Attribution reuses frozen-repair red attribution and sync-batch-delta pickRedAuthor. Ejection reuses the bounded-life re-cut and carry paths. Quarantine extends the existing hand-quarantine. New logic lives in pure decision modules under packages/operator-core/lib/release/, wired into green-checkpoint.ts and frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts.\n- **Decision this plan reverses.** frozen-candidate-stays-frozen-through-all-fixes-2026-09-03#D-001 (\"frozen through ALL fixes\"). Under this plan a freeze only has to clear unattributable failures, not reach absolute zero. [inferred] The owner approved the plan text stating this reversal (D-001), and confirmed the ratchet (D-002); the owner may still veto.\n- **Item numbering.** Decisions D-004, D-005, D-007 and D-008 call three items P-014, P-015 and P-016. The plan store numbered them P-016 (round-1 measurement), P-017 (case-level tracking) and P-018 (composed promotion proof). The warning text states that the change may ship broken behaviour in that area.\n- The critical-area registry (P-003) stays; it now drives the stronger warning instead of a refusal.\n\n### D-007 — Typecheck/lint failures: catch at sync time, never let them hide tests, track per error, eject by attribution. Adopted unless the owner objects.\n\nA. Typecheck/lint legs are deterministic whole-program checks, so they get different handling from tests:\n1. Catch them within minutes of landing. But they evaluated about 3 of ~261 five-minute slots on 10-16/17 under host load. P-009 moves both onto reserved capacity.\n2. They must not hide tests. 'lint:tsc:workspaces' failing is one entry today however many errors it holds, so fix progress and new errors are invisible. Folded into P-015.\n4. Eject by attribution. Because these checks are deterministic, comparing errors on the base and on the candidate names the introducing commit reliably (P-007 with the D-003 base check). A type error can surface in file B while its cause is in file A; the base comparison handles that.\n\nB. No separate test-suite freeze. Tests live in the same commit as the code, so freezing the candidate already freezes its tests. New tests reach a frozen candidate only through an admission. R4 already refuses an admission that adds any failure absent at the previous head, and that includes a new failing test. P-006's text is aligned to R4. Freezing tests separately would drop the tests a fix brings, which are its evidence that it works. On re-cuts, new tests from the tip are handled by fix, eject or downgrade (D-002, P-007).\n\n### D-008 — Re-run what a fix can affect, never what merely failed: compose the promotion proof instead of a final full re-run; skip runtime tests for type-only changes\nDate: 2026-10-17\nDate: 2026-10-17\nAuthority: owner questions [owner 2026-10-17, directive #1954] verbatim: \"can we give the lint tests the same dont rerun previously passed ones treatment? do lint tests trigger real tests re-running? they shouldn'y\". Already-passing tests and legs outside that set are not re-run at that step. But a green selective step then 'proceeds to that full gate, which is the promotion proof', so every test and every lint leg runs again before promotion, whatever the fix touched. Anything not selectively re-runnable also forces the full gate.\n\nRule: whether something re-runs depends on what files the fix changed, never on which check failed.\n- A lint/typecheck fix that changes runtime code must re-run the tests that depend on that code. P-001 found 82 of 87 real breaks arrived through dependencies.\n- A fix whose change is erased at runtime (type annotations, comments, lint baselines) cannot change any runtime test result, so no runtime tests re-run. Check it mechanically: if the transpiled JavaScript of every changed file is identical before and after, the change is type-only.\n- Lint legs get the same treatment as tests: re-run a leg only if it failed or its inputs were changed.\n- Promotion proof is composed: the candidate's full round-1 results (P-014), plus each admission's radius re-run (P-006). Results outside every admission's radius carry over. Keep the full gate only when a radius cannot be computed. Not an owner directive.\n\n1. Storage. An automatic verdict-flip quarantine is a row in the existing harness_shared.test_downgrades store (P-002), distinguished by a new kind column ('downgrade' | 'flaky-quarantine', default 'downgrade'). No parallel quarantine table. Each row names an owner (default 'human', override env PAPERCUSP_FLAKY_QUARANTINE_OWNER) and opens the owner's de-quarantine work-item before the row is written. The store has no expiry column; a row stays active until it is lifted.\n2. Detection. In green-checkpoint runGreen, a file that failed in the suite and then passed when re-run alone on the same tree (the isolation retry) has flipped on one commit, and it is quarantined. This also runs on a green, because an isolation-absorbed green still saw the flip. It fails closed: with no gate target, no candidate sha, or a failed read, the count stays exactly as measured. A test in a critical area (P-003 registry) is still quarantined, but its row carries a riskAcknowledgement and the owner is notified at once (severity major). It is never silently excluded.\n3. Exclusion from counts. Only ACTIVE flaky rows feed a decidePromotionRatchet call, which removes their failures from failingTests and quarantinedFileLabels with the same file/case coverage and critical-area rule as a downgrade. If every failure is quarantined, the run is green. The gate records excludedFromCount (quarantine.txt + flaky + downgrades) on the result, and it rides measuredSignature onto each repair-round red marker.\n4. Same-population rule (falsifier 3 in production). likeForLikeTrajectory removes the union of every round's excludedFromCount from every round's failingTests before comparing round counts, so a quarantine taken mid-queue cannot read as an improvement. When something was excluded, a round with no list is skipped as 'population-unknown'.\n5. Known limits, accepted. (a) Cross-run observations from test_runs (the same sha red in one run and green in another) are not yet fed to detection; only the in-run isolation retry is. observationsFromTestRuns exists (verdict-flip-quarantine.ts:369) but has no production caller. A follow-up work-item is filed. (b) The second decidePromotionRatchet call still reads ALL rows, so a flaky row the flaky step missed acts as a downgrade. This fails open toward exclusion. Not an owner directive; reversible.\n\nMeasured (routines.metadata.sync_delta.coverage, 291 slots 10-17 01:40Z to 10-18 01:37Z): 104 completed runs, 187 missed-opportunity slots. 122 of those missed slots (65%) followed the 21 runs that ended leg-timeout (all on the affected-tests leg, 25-min budget, one commit each); 29 (16%) followed 7 missing-terminal-break-set runs; the 46 host-load skips were quick and absorbed 20. Half of all runs took more than 6 minutes. sync-batch-lint-guards keeps no coverage history at all and was last skipping on host-load 384.91 > 384 hard ceiling.\n\n1. Load never skips. evaluateCapacity no longer returns skip: load above the hard ceiling, or an unreadable load, only reduces the confirm/attribution budget (same as the soft band). Applies to both sync-batch-delta-check and sync-batch-lint-guards, which share it.\n2. Reserved capacity. Heavy legs run in their own top-level user slice source-checks.slice (CPUWeight=100, IOWeight=100) via systemd-run --user --scope, instead of nice 19 + ionice inside the operator cgroup. Not named papercusp-* (that nests under papercusp.slice, CPUWeight=25, which is why nothing launched by the task manager can be reserved). Weight 100 is the systemd default, so the checks get an equal share with app.slice and cannot starve the gate. If the scope cannot launch, the leg runs unwrapped at normal priority and says so in its diagnostic.\n3. What 'slot evaluated' means. Measured above: even if every run evaluated, one completed run per five-minute slot caps coverage at 104/291 = 36%, because a single affected-tests run on an operator-core radius takes longer than 5 min. So a slot is evaluated when its own run evaluated, OR when the first later run that evaluated finished within 30 minutes of the slot (COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS) — the commits that arrived in that slot were judged within 30 minutes. A slot judged later than 30 minutes, or never, stays not evaluated, so slow checks still lower coverage. Credited slots keep their original status and carry judgedAtMs, so the alarm can report how many were judged late. Alternative considered and rejected: parallel runs over disjoint commit windows (needs a cursor lease; too large for P-009).\n4. Alarm. Both checks raise a condition-keyed coverage alarm when coverage over 24 hours is below 95% (window 24h, minimum 144 slots = 12h of history), and clear it on recovery. lint-guards gets its own coverage history and condition key (sync-lint-guards-coverage-low).\n\nVerification owed beyond unit tests: live coverage at or above 95% over 24 hours after the change is serving, read from the routine rows.\n\n### D-018 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: apply-r8-asbuilt-20261020\nRequest-Hash: 419a24bbf5d95a2830c34d497eaa96c7e11d9f2778c01820b1ef8d5dc622256b\nActor: su-807ee9d7-200a-4664-808d-c6000c52e818\nReason: As-built (P-009): the registered file sync-batch-reserved-capacity.test.ts was never created. Not an owner directive; reversible.\n\n1. Promotion history = the release ref's reflog (`git reflog show --format=%H%x09%ct main` in the integration root). main moves only by green-checkpoint's fast-forward, so each entry is one promotion; no new table. If the previous full run's sha is not in the reflog, every new failure is reported unattributable ('no-baseline'), never guessed.\n2. Attribution per new failing file: re-run at tip (a pass = verdict flip → flaky quarantine), re-run at the previous full run's sha (a fail = break with no code change, e.g. time/environment → no promotion to blame), then binary search over the promotions between. The invariant passes-at-lo / fails-at-hi makes every attribution a single promotion that passes on the base without it (D-003's blame check by construction). Probes are grouped by sha and capped at 16 distinct probe points per full run; an exhausted budget is 'budget-exhausted', never a guess. Each probe runs ONE file per clean-tree invocation (a multi-file run can abort at collection).\n3. Routing is an escalation ladder in the D-002 order: a new attributed failure → fix (one deduped bug per file, conditionKey periodic-full-run:<file>, naming the culprit promotion); still failing ≥24h later → eject (revert the culprit's change on staging); still failing ≥24h after that → downgrade (critical-area tests need the D-006 acknowledgement). Unattributable failures have no promotion to eject: fix, then downgrade; a flip goes straight to the flaky quarantine. The routine files the route; it never reverts or downgrades by itself.\n4. Cadence and capacity: the routine fires every 30 min (:22/:52) and runs the suite when ≥6h have passed since the last full run. The whole suite and every probe run through runReservedArgv in source-checks.slice (P-009) and the module has no host-load skip (R-11 falsifier 3). An inconclusive run (no terminal break-set line, ENOSPC, unmeasured spawn) never moves the baseline (P-016's like-with-like rule). Not an owner directive; reversible.\n\nMeasured 2026-10-20 08:45-09:00Z: `affected-tests.mjs --print-affected --related` on each of the last 15 first-parent staging commits (14 measured; run in clean root /tmp/pcv/papercusp-lint-as-committed-d0e0c5a654-Q9bEDt because the deployed frozen-lineage classifier refuses the canonical-root form). Projected wall time = history EWMA per task (~/.papercusp/cache/papercusp-affected-task-durations-v1.json), narrowed suites scaled by RELATED_SELECTION selected/total, 2-lane longest-first. Results: 23s x2 (guard-only), 588s x6, 1176-1333s x6, 1750s x1. Evidence: .papercusp/scratch/ratchet/sample-18036/analysis.txt (+ per-commit logs; script analyze-18036.mts).\n\n1. Root cause of WI-6554700010018036: the radius caps (maxTaskCommands=32, maxGuards=26) are a COUNT proxy for TIME and are wrong in both directions. They refused 9/14 commits, including two 588s radii (d0e0c5a654, cfecf8f20a), and they admitted e1f292b7d8 (29 tasks) whose operator-core suites run in full (RELATED_SELECTION mode=full reason=no-changed-paths-in-scope, ~1750s class). Guard counts dominate task counts but guards are cheap (EWMA total ~356s).\n2. Fix: the probe runs with --related (as the real run does) and affected-tests.mjs emits the runner's own projected wall time in print mode (one AFFECTED_ETA line, from the same estimateBudgetedTaskWallMs + duration history the run's admissionIntent uses, with narrowed suites scaled by their related selection). evaluateRadius admits by projected time against a fraction of SYNC_DELTA_TIMEOUTS_MS.affected and refuses with an explicit 'projected Ns > budget Ms, heaviest <task>' detail. Count caps stay only as high backstops, and as the fallback when no ETA line is present. On the sample this admits 13/14. Peak-based admission was rejected: every non-guard-only radius has a peak projection >= 3214s, so it would admit nothing useful; the leg watchdog stays the worst-case backstop.\n3. R-17 consequence: one run at a time plus R-8's 30-minute credit (COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS, D-017 #3) means a slot arriving mid-run is judged when the NEXT run ends, about 2xD later. With D ~ 10-22 min, roughly half the slots of the ~20-min class are judged after 30 min. D-017 #3 chose 30 min assuming a few-minute run ('half of all runs took more than 6 minutes'); the measured typical radius falsifies that premise. Re-specification (follow-up item, needs a rubric amend of R-8 with outside approval and re-vet): a slot counts as judged when a check that is keeping up judged it, deadline = 2 x the affected leg budget + the 5-minute slot interval, derived from the constants rather than chosen. Not done in this change, so R-17 is not graded until it lands.\n4. Narrowing limits found, not fixed here: scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs L1077-1086 runs a workspace in full when any changed path is outside its root (even a non-code report JSON), and dependents of operator-core (web :: test, ~588s) always run in full (no-changed-paths-in-scope). Filed as a follow-up; it changes the gate's own selection semantics.\n\n### D-031 — D-031 - Slot-credit deadline = 2 x one run's leg budget (probe + tsc + affected) + the 5-min interval, derived in code; refines D-030 #3\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAuthority: [self-imposed] design decision by su-807ee9d7 for WI-6554700010018046. Not an owner directive; reversible. Refines D-030 #3 (whose formula was 2 x affected + interval = 55 min).\n\n1. Model. The delta-check runs one at a time on a 5-minute cron (COVERAGE_EXPECTED_INTERVAL_MS). One run is probe -> tsc -> affected in series (runSyncBatchDeltaCheck: deps.probeRadius, then deps.runTsc, then deps.runAffected), and each leg is killed at its SYNC_DELTA_TIMEOUTS_MS budget (probe 10 min, tsc 10 min, affected 25 min). A slot at time t that arrives while run A is in flight is judged by the next run B: B starts <= R + I after t and ends <= 2R + I after t, where R is one run's wall. So a check that is keeping up judges every slot within 2R + I, and any later judgment means it fell behind.\n2. R is the sum of the three leg budgets (45 min), so COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS = 2 x 45 + 5 = 95 min. D-030 #3 counted only the affected leg. That omitted the probe, which now runs --related and was measured at ~4.4 min (timeout raised to 10 min by WI-6554700010018036), and the tsc leg, which runs whenever TS files changed. With those omitted, a normal in-budget run would still miss credit by construction, which is the defect D-030 #3 named.\n3. Excluded: the red-confirm leg (up to MAX_CONFIRM_RUNS=3 single-file runs of 10 min) and the held-red re-confirm path. They run only after a red was already found, which is rare, and the 95% target absorbs their slots. Including them would give 155 min and would credit a check that is badly behind.\n4. Derived, not chosen. SYNC_DELTA_TIMEOUTS_MS moves into sync-batch-delta-check.ts, and sync-batch-delta-check-deps.ts re-exports it, because deps imports the logic module and the reverse import would be a cycle. Both DEFAULT_RADIUS_CAPS.maxProjectedSec (0.9 x affected) and COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS are computed from it. The listing keep-window (keepWindowMs) uses the same constant and widens with it. A Vitest pin asserts the formula.\n5. What stays honest. A slot is never credited if no run judged its commits: leg-timeout and radius-too-wide advance the cursor past them. A slot judged after 2R + I is not credited either, for example when runs were skipped for longer than a run budget. Slots skipped while green-checkpoint holds the box are credited only when a run reaches them within 95 min.\n6. Rubric. R-8 states 30 minutes in its hashed text. It needs a rubrics:amend (rev 9) naming the derived constant, outside approval, and a re-vet before R-17 is graded.\n\n### D-032 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: d031-derived-credit-deadline-20261020\nRequest-Hash: 81caa74856d7ca076a06d2422fc4787369f45c75db88bdef5f87f90d577887b0\nActor: su-807ee9d7-200a-4664-808d-c6000c52e818\nReason: D-031 amend (rev 8 -> 9): R-8 named a fixed 30-minute slot-credit window for both sync-batch checks. For the delta check that window is unreachable by construction: one run is probe -> typecheck -> affected in series with budgets 10 + 10 + 25 minutes, so a slot that arrives while a run is in flight is judged by the next run up to ~95 minutes later and could never be credited, which made R-17 (95 percent of slots judged) unreachable even with every commit judged (green-main-ratchet-convergence-2026-10-17#D-030 #3, measured 2026-10-20). The delta check now uses COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS = 2 x run budget + interval (95 min), derived in code from the leg timeouts; the lint guards keep 30 minutes. R-8 method and FAIL clause (2) now name each check's deadline. Model, bar, check files, the 95 percent / 144-slot alarm and every other bar are unchanged. WI-6554700010018046.\nApproved-By: su-e76998ed-75ba-4787-b43d-25fefed1bb39\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1191559\nApproved-At: 2026-10-20T09:39:39.194Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 87 → 88\nChanged BARs: R-8\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-8\n\n### D-033 — D-033 - Cross-root related selection for the sync-batch delta check (WI-6554700010018067): rules, controls and measurements\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAuthority: [self-imposed] design decision by su-807ee9d7 for WI-6554700010018067, from measurement. Not an owner directive; reversible.\n\n1. Scope. Cross-root selection is OPT-IN via `scripts/affected-tests.mjs --related-cross-root` and is passed only by the sync-batch delta check (packages/operator-core/lib/release/sync-batch-delta-check-deps.ts). The green-checkpoint gate's own selection is unchanged.\n\n2. Rules (scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs). (a) A workspace with NO changed path inside its root (a reverse-dependency workspace such as `@papercusp/web`) relates its tests across roots: a test is selected when any file in its import closure is a changed path or an unresolved import (a closure hole selects, never drops). (b) If the workspace's runner-config closure reaches a changed file, the workspace runs in full (`runner-config-reaches-change`); a hole in that closure also runs it in full (`runner-config-unresolved`). (c) An out-of-root change that no import edge describes (e.g. README.md) runs in full (`cross-root-unrelatable-change`). (d) A workspace whose cross-root selection is empty has its test task dropped, keyed on reason `cross-root-unreached`, never on emptiness alone. (e) A workspace with local changes keeps the default rules.\n\n3. Falsifiability. Six copy-out mutation probes, one per rail (closure-hole, rc-change, rc-hole, reason-key, local-unreached, unrelatable), all CAUGHT (.papercusp/scratch/ratchet/xroot/probes-xroot-summary.log, 12:28-12:39Z). packages/operator-core/lib/__tests__/related-tests-selection.test.ts 91/91 pass.\n\n4. Measurement, end to end from a clean lint:as-committed root at fcdfe978bf (12:42-12:49Z, .papercusp/scratch/ratchet/xroot/e2e-summary.log): change packages/operator-core/lib/sync-sse.ts -> web full 1319/1319 (`no-changed-paths-in-scope`) without the flag, 364/1319 `mode=related` with it; operator-core 4674 vs 4861 selected (cross-root mode applies the closure-hole rule in-root too, so it selects more, not fewer). Test-only change (promotion-ratchet.test.ts) -> operator-core 8 tests, web not selected. README.md -> full in both workspaces. Earlier 23-commit sample (11:55-12:13Z): web ~403/1319 on operator-core source commits, dropped on test-only commits.\n\n5. Expected effect: removes the dominant ~588s `web :: test` term from most delta-check runs (D-030), raising R-17 slot coverage. Not yet live: bg-host runs a stale bundle (dist-host/hono-host.mjs 11:51Z, flag absent) because the bundle build fails (WI-6554700010018092, held by su-8131472d). bg-host restart follows that fix. The default selector's narrower hole check is tracked separately (WI-6554700010018081).\n\n### D-034 — D-034 - Delta-check throughput: the 25-min affected leg is shorter than one commit's radius; raise it to 45 min and derive the routine timeout and stale-backlog cutoff from the run budget (WI-6554700010018126)\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAuthority: [self-imposed] design decision by su-807ee9d7 for WI-6554700010018126, from measurement. Not an owner directive; reversible.\n\n1. Measurement (13:05-13:50Z, bg-host on the --related-cross-root bundle since 13:05:24Z; harness_shared.routines sync-batch-delta-check metadata->'sync_delta'->'coverage'->'ticks' + bg-host journal): 1 of 9 slots judged. The one completed run (13:05:46 -> 13:31:25, 25.6 min) judged a single commit. The next single commit db14e1d04fe3 was refused radius-too-wide (8 workspaces, 39 tasks, projected 1453s > maxProjectedSec 1350s; heaviest operator-core::test:lane-stateful 668s). Then 9 commits were backlog-skipped (>120 min). Earlier: leg-timeout at 1500928ms on single commit 9a64e1acb8. D-030's sample had single commits at 1176-1750s. One commit's radius regularly exceeds 0.9 x 25 min, so R-17 (>=95% of slots judged) cannot pass: collecting the planned 24h window under the current budget would only measure a known failure. This supersedes the self-imposed 'do not edit the delta check during the R-17 window' sequencing.\n2. Change: SYNC_DELTA_TIMEOUTS_MS.affected = 45 min. Per D-030/D-031, admission (0.9 x affected = 2430s) and COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS (2 x (10+10+45) + 5 = 135 min) derive from it. Runs are already back to back (concurrency:'skip'), so the duty cycle and host load do not rise. Work that would have finished is no longer killed or refused, and each run judges the whole backlog since the previous cut as one batch.\n3. SYNC_BATCH_DELTA_ROUTINE_TIMEOUT_MS was a fixed 45 min, equal to the run budget, which left no room for the red-confirm legs. It becomes derived: SYNC_DELTA_RUN_BUDGET_MS + 3 x confirm + 5 min.\n4. STALE_BACKLOG_MS was a fixed 120 min. Its own comment says a commit older than the slot-credit deadline earns no credit, so it becomes COVERAGE_JUDGE_DEADLINE_MS.\n5. R-8's falsifier wording '95 minutes today' becomes 135 minutes. The operative clause is the derivation per D-031, which still holds. The parenthetical should be corrected in the next rubric amend, batched with any other revision BEFORE independent grading is requested.\n6. Next lever, only if R-17 still fails after this: concurrency (AFFECTED_MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS, default 2) for the delta check's own runs. It is held back because host load is ~150 on 128 cores.\n7. R-17's 24h window restarts when bg-host runs the new bundle.\n\n### D-035 — D-035 - R-17's 24h window from 14:37:22Z has already failed; the 95%-slot bar looks unreachable on this host as built; owner asked whether to keep, rescope or drop it\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAuthority: [self-imposed] finding by su-807ee9d7 for P-009 (WI-6554700010016943), from measurement. Not an owner directive. The choice of option is the owner's; see #5.\n\n1. Measurement, 14:37:22-17:08Z (harness_shared.routines sync-batch-delta-check coverage ticks; bg-host journal): 29 five-minute slots, 1 judged (14:37:40 red). Causes:\n- bg-host was restarted twice by peers, at 15:10:39Z and 16:55:26Z (systemctl ActiveEnterTimestamp; MainPID now 2739155). Each restart killed an in-flight run. The 16:13Z run died 36 min into its affected leg (pid 367698, 17 paths, leg from 16:19:30Z) and recorded no outcome.\n- 1 leg-timeout: 27a78e35c6a0 (5 files) ran more than 45 min (16:05:50Z), although admission projected it within the 2430s cap.\n- 1 radius-too-wide: e59a838a7ea4, 1452 paths (WI-6554700010018174).\n- 2 backlog-skips: 12 commits at 16:08Z and 17 at 16:56Z, all older than 160 min.\n- Load-reduced budgets: host-load 209-251 > 153.6, and 420 > hard ceiling 384 at 17:00Z.\n2. Arithmetic: 95% of 288 slots allows 14 unjudged. 28 are unjudged already. The 14:37-16:00Z slots can no longer be credited: their commits sit behind the backlog-skip anchor or outside the 135-min credit deadline. So this window has failed whatever the next 21h do.\n3. Structure [inferred from ~7h of measurement since 10:00Z; not proven]. One run takes 55-65 min, and 10-20 sync commits land during it. Single commits already project 1453-1839s or overrun 2700s, so the union radius of one run's backlog exceeds the 2430s admission cap. Peer bg-host restarts are outside the check's control. This is the 4th throughput iteration on this bar (D-030, D-031, D-034).\n4. Delivered and tested regardless: the checks run source-side on reserved capacity; load reduces the budget instead of skipping; every slot is accounted for, with no silent drop. Only the 95% coverage target is unmet.\n5. Decision: the 14:37Z window is no longer acceptance evidence, and I will not restart it until the owner chooses (coord:ask-owner, this date). Options: (A, default if unanswered by the stated deadline) rescope R-17 by amendment: keep the coverage alarm and per-slot cause accounting, record honestly that 95% coverage was not delivered, and ship P-009 on its other bars. (B) Keep 95% and fund a redesign: restart-safe resume of in-flight runs, plus sampling the newest commits when a backlog exceeds one run's budget; no guarantee it passes on this host. (C) Keep R-17 as written and restart the 24h window now; expected to fail again.\n\n### D-036 — D-036 - Owner chose option A of D-035: rescope R-17 by amendment, record that 95% slot coverage was not delivered, ship P-009 on its other bars\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAuthority: [owner directive #2076, 2026-10-20, typed interactive turn: \"go with option A\"], answering the D-035 question (conv-mvgxw6ys-0000-34bfcc01542b49ebbef78ec416cff894).\n\nWhat A means (as defined in D-035 #5): amend R-17 in acceptance-green-main-ratchet-convergence-2026-10-17. Keep the coverage alarm and the per-slot cause accounting (every unjudged slot carries a recorded status: missed-opportunity, radius-too-wide, leg-timeout, backlog-skipped). Drop the 95%-of-slots-over-24h pass condition. State plainly in the bar that 95% coverage was not delivered on this host, citing D-035 (1 of 29 slots judged 14:37-17:08Z; two peer bg-host restarts killed in-flight runs; throughput below the commit rate). Batch the pending R-8 parenthetical fix ('95 minutes today' -> 135, D-034 #5) into the same amendment, so the rubric is re-vetted once. P-009 (WI-6554700010016943) is then evaluated on its delivered properties: source-side checks on reserved capacity; host load reduces the budget instead of skipping; honest slot accounting. The R-17 24h window is no longer acceptance evidence and is not restarted. Follow-ups WI-6554700010018174, -18068, -18081, -18111 stay filed as throughput improvements; they no longer gate P-009.\n\n### D-037 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: d036-r17-rescope-r8-135-20261020\nRequest-Hash: b45e5ba8a7f6ef5029d2f413459b12d7b786f1f9508e7f29ff844d62c40ba433\nActor: su-807ee9d7-200a-4664-808d-c6000c52e818\nReason: D-036 amend (rev 9 -> 10), owner directive #2076 (\"go with option A\", answering #D-035): R-17 no longer passes on 95 percent of five-minute slots judged over 24 hours. On this host that bar failed in the 14:37Z window (1 of 29 slots judged; two bg-host restarts killed in-flight runs; one run is slower than the commit rate) and the owner chose to rescope rather than redesign. R-17 now requires that both routines account for every slot (judged, or a recorded cause) and that a routine under 95 percent has its coverage alarm open, and its bar states plainly that 95 percent coverage was not delivered. R-8: the delta check's slot-credit deadline parenthetical is corrected from 95 to 135 minutes (D-034 #5: affected leg 25 -> 45 min, 2 x (10 + 10 + 45) + 5). No other bar changes.\nApproved-By: su-3bbbd6e3-c767-4dd5-99ac-9ec0aea93e44\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1192054\nApproved-At: 2026-10-20T17:48:22.784Z\nRubric revision: 9 → 10\nSubject plan revision: 105 → 106\nChanged BARs: R-8, R-17\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-8, R-17\n\n### D-038 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: d036b-r8-n1-r17-alarm-fresh-20261020\nRequest-Hash: f05a6a7c95f06dee0ab49cb3ae4e0ad87e593b5a3f1bda30a5c0a4f8f195b071\nActor: su-807ee9d7-200a-4664-808d-c6000c52e818\nReason: D-036 follow-up amend (rev 10 -> 11), from the outside-lineage review of rev 10 (thread-post:1192054 on WI-6554700010016943, items N1, N2 and N4). () <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010017398 — Personal Vault access, after-read holds, transcript visibility and automatic recall in the vault owner's stack settings (R-8), set or widened only by the vault owner, never inherited through a shared… <!-- P-015 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010017399 — Integrated verification in an isolated current-build runtime whose workspace config comes from migrating the live config, never from P-014's seed, using the P-001 census instrument; one clause per ca… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010017400 — Document layers and named stacks, the contribution-minus-restriction rule, layer grants and stack settings, the loosening rule and fixed floors for publishers and installers; verify the promoted arti… <!-- P-011 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"The workspace owner (Avi); organizations and individuals who install Cupboard identities and configure them for their own structure and policy; publishers who author identities; engineers maintaining the capability envelope, install consent, provider bindings, governance policy, billing, secrets and Personal Vault surfaces.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Identities are distributed on the Cupboard to many organizations, each with its own structure, apps and policies, but install-specific facts are mixed into identities or hard-coded beside them. The identity format accepts every workspace runtime field (accounts, cost caps, placement, build commands). Identities inherit the workspace runtime base. su fixes its profession. The engineering prompt hard-codes this machine's git setup and the owner's subagent mandate. The per-role tool ceiling and the vault role-name fence are code tables. Nothing per installation says who may wear an identity, what it may spend, or which secrets and vault data it may read. Identities are already stackable: layers fill slots that take one layer or several, and su is a named stack. But every ceiling in the chain must allow a call, so per-layer ceilings would collapse a stack of several practices, no layer can restrict the stack, and nothing stops a stack change from quietly widening access. Vault disclosures are presently tracked only for restricted documents; user, data-context and organization authority do not yet share a complete resource policy, and the originating agent can search its restricted transcript.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Identities are layers that fill registered slots, and named stacks combine them. A portable layer declares who it is, what it asks for (required and optional capability classes, tools, kinds of secret, data-handling requirements), the most it may contribute, any restrictions it imposes on the whole stack, and nothing install-specific. Each layer contributes at most its own asks, within its own maximum and its installation's grants for that layer. A session gets everything its layers contribute, minus anything any layer restricts; organization, department and workspace policy then narrow it, under fixed floors. Each installation holds layer grants (which asks are granted, which app provides each capability) and stack settings for each named stack (wearers, spend cap, secret scope, Personal Vault access), attached to the stack by name. Loosening a grant or setting, a stack change that widens access, or an identity version that asks for more needs the owner's typed approval or fresh consent. su behaves exactly as today in Avi's workspace. Owner amendment D-020 makes every retained vault contribution a persistent narrowing policy source, unifies scoped resource decisions, and keeps personal data and protected derivatives out of general session-history indexes while authorized vault search remains available.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Session confinement for directed pairs: it stays per launch, because implementer versus director is a launch choice, not an identity or installation property.\",\n    \"Unrelated role grant values stay unchanged; D-020 intentionally changes vault-derived context, resource and transcript-search behavior, including su.\",\n    \"Cupboard listing, discovery, publisher billing and listing visibility.\",\n    \"Workspace (pot) blueprints: they keep their runtime fields; only identity documents narrow.\",\n    \"Migrating other organizations' installations: there are none yet.\",\n    \"Mode and fleet-posture authority: modes and fleet posture fill slots at launch, but what they change stays decided by the kernel mode registry; they contribute no tool grants.\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"the exemption shouldnt be hard coded either it should be part of their identity definition. D-020 incorporates the four owner questions and assessment rpt_f728a193-dc87-4a89-af81-2ad1c51490c1. This changes the contract, not implementation status.\n\n## Background — what exists today (read from code 2026-10-17)\n\nBuilds on two shipped plans: `agent-capability-confinement-2026-06-13` (the capability envelope and its per-role table) and `portable-identity-packages-2026-09-26` (identity definitions, grants, install consent and wearer authority). Paths are under `papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/` unless they start with `libs/`.\n\n**Already shaped right (reuse, do not rebuild):**\n\n| Surface | What it does | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Identity asks | `grants` holds `requires`, `optional` and `suggestedProviders`: these are requests, not grants. | `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/schema.ts` (`GrantsSchema`) |\n| Install consent | The admin consents to this exact artifact and set of permissions. The publisher's manifest is checked against what the package actually carries. | `cupboard/identity-install-consent.ts` |\n| Provider bindings | Contributions name a capability class (for example `papercusp.mode-state@1`), and each workspace binds which provider supplies it. | `capability-class-registry-store.ts` |\n| Per-workspace prompt layer | `instance:su.instance` | rendered su prompt layers |\n| Stacking | Layers fill registered slots; each slot takes one layer or several, and the registry is authoritative. su is a named stack of `papercusp-engineer`, `su-collaborator` and `su.practice`; client, fleet posture and modes are added at launch. | `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/slots.ts` (`SLOT_SPECS`); `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/su/blueprint.yaml` |\n| Live stack changes | `attachLayer` / `detachLayer` / `applyStackMutation` change a running session's layers. Its `StackBinding` type means the set of layers a session runs, not an installation binding; this plan says \"layer grants\" and \"stack settings\" to avoid the clash. | `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/stack-mutation.ts` |\n| Launch settings | Model, effort, account and carry are chosen at launch; the su identity grants no role or authority. | `libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/su/blueprint.yaml` |\n| Org policy | Organization, department and workspace layers for models, tools, plugins, egress, data use and actions, enforced at the shared kernel seat and judged per workspace. | `governance-policy/enforce.ts`, `inherited-policy.ts` (enterprise P-005) |\n| Governance authority | Non-human principals can only prepare changes; self-approval is refused by a database trigger. | `governance-policy/authority.ts:15-40` (enterprise P-006) |\n\n**Wrongly bundled or hard-coded (audit rpt_38002133):**\n\n| Problem | Evidence |\n|---|---|\n| The identity format accepts every workspace runtime field: `roles[].account`, `backups[].account`, `dispatch.costCapUsd`, `concurrency`, `safetyCeiling`, `placement`, `environment`, `knobs.agentCmd` and `triggers`. Every check names one new test case that does not exist today, so no bar can pass on the unchanged tree (D-011 item 1).\n\n**R-1 — Identities have their own portable format.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Identity documents get their own narrow schema: id, extends, version, description, slots, contributions, asks (grants), ceiling, floors, lexicon, mode, publisher and attestation. The schema is a closed allowlist: every other key, including every workspace runtime field (role accounts and backups, dispatch and dispatch.costCapUsd, placement, environment, knobs, triggers, params), is refused at parse time and Cupboard publish naming the key. The inheritance and parse-compatibility clauses are what the allowlist must not break: narrowing the identity schema is exactly the change that could leave a built-in identity inheriting the workspace base, make one fail to parse, or change a workspace blueprint's parse. The allowlist itself is rated by the three refusal cases; the other clauses by 'R-1: every built-in identity resolves without the workspace base', which also asserts every built-in identity parses, and 'R-1: built-in workspace blueprints parse unchanged'.\\n\\nRating basis: the condition is the pass floor; every falsifier clause is rated; any observed clause prevents healthy.\\n\\nRequired case 'R-1: Cupboard publish refuses an unknown identity key, naming the key' in packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/blueprint-release.integration.test.ts submits a synthetic non-workspace, out-of-schema key at the actual Cupboard publish entry point, asserts refusal naming that key and no published release, and uses a valid identity publish as its control. Reproduce a pre-change failure, then attach revision-bound positive and hostile-path proof; enumerate the selected path population and any residue.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  I[Granted identity layer contributions minus restrictions] --> E[One kernel permission evaluator]\n  U[User policy] --> E\n  O[Organization / department / workspace] --> E\n  V[Every vault represented by retained context] --> E\n  F[Fixed platform floors] --> E\n  D[Explicit / ambient / delegated / federated delivery] --> P[Persistent provenance before delivery]\n  P --> V\n  E --> A[Native / MCP / nested / plugin / process / service adapters]\n  H[Safe history references] --> Q[Authorized direct vault retrieval]\n```\n\n**Effective permission:** granted identity aggregate AND user policy AND organization/department/workspace policy AND every active-context vault ceiling AND fixed floors. Apply this to the requested action, resolved resource target and arguments. A missing optional narrowing layer is neutral only when the absence is verified; an unreadable required policy denies. Explicit empty allowlists deny. Explanation traces carry policy revisions and the deciding authority.\n\n**Preserve composable identities.** Layers still combine internally by D-009: own asks within own maximum and grants, minus every layer restriction. External authorities intersect with that aggregate; a layer, stack, mode or su override cannot widen any vault, user or organization ceiling. Publishers own definitions; installers own layer grants and stack settings; users/data owners and organizations own their respective narrowing policy.\n\n**Data arrival is an authority transition.** Extend the disclosure ledger to all vault contributions and persist provenance/restrictions before delivery. Derived answers, summaries, compaction, forks and handoffs inherit labels. Revalidate revocation and fence queued/in-flight work. TTL, truncation and model assertions do not clear context; restore authority only after verified clean reset or authorized scoped release.\n\n**Resources reuse the existing permission system.** Extend capability classes, governance categories, policy storage and kernel trace, then bind adapters to network destinations, paths, stores, accounts/recipients and processing routes. Tool permission is necessary but insufficient. Actual execution boundaries resolve targets and enforce the decision; required containment failure refuses. Approved inference does not imply arbitrary network access.\n\n**Keep personal history out of general search.** All self/successor/peer history search, embedding, recall and summary indexes exclude vault payloads and protected derivatives. Store safe metadata/protected references, seal any necessary raw transcript retention under current vault access, and retrieve authorized content from the vault directly. Inventory native logs/caches/backups and existing indexed derivatives; snapshot before destructive backfill, rebuild and validate restore/rollback. A release never makes old protected history generally searchable.\n\n**Binding settings cannot defeat source policy.** Wearers/spend/secrets/grants still follow their established owners. Recall and direct owner transcript viewing remain configurable within the ceilings. D-020 supersedes only inconsistent move-only and su holds-off/transcripts-open preservation; unrelated existing behavior and portability stay required. Vault access is granted separately from what reading its data later permits.\n\n**Reuse and verification.** Extend install consent/provider bindings, governance-policy, disclosure/transcript exclusion, existing sandbox/egress adapters and the current testing ledger. No parallel permission registry. Workspace blueprints retain runtime fields. Verification runs on isolated current-build routes; green-main evidence is reserved for final shipment. Prior acceptance proof is historical until amended BAR/spec pins and audits are current.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-012 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-015 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-013 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-012 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-016 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-018 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Baseline by observation. Obtain current independent acceptance and author verdict on amended pins; verify final shipment without reusing pre-D-020 grades. blocked-by: P-010\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Scope: groups B, C and D; group A lives in the vault plan\nDate: 2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog answer, verbatim] \"do A,B,C,D\"\n\nGroup A (vault settings) is recorded in personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17 D-010. This plan carries group B (tool ceiling, testing override), group C (identity policy layer, route-referenced inference) and group D (wearers, spend cap, secret scope). Group D was recommended for later; Avi chose to include it now. Superseded in part by D-005 and D-006 (2026-10-17): group A's vault settings now move into this plan as a binding.\n\n### D-002 — Ceiling chain and fixed floors\nDate: 2026-10-17\nBasis: report rpt_0281ae32-cd67-4379-a5b3-417d7087d8bf, accepted by Avi with \"do A,B,C,D\".\n\nOrganization, department, workspace, then identity; each layer narrows the one above. Fixed floors no identity can remove: the never-auto protected set, agents cannot approve governance changes, content-free receipts/audit/SIEM export, and retention/legal holds. The chain is superseded by D-005 (2026-10-17); the fixed floors stand.\n\n### D-003 — Loosening needs the owner's typed approval\nDate: 2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog answer, verbatim] \"Yes, needs my approval (Recommended)\"\n\nLoosening any identity setting needs the owner's own typed approval for that exact change, using the release-authority proof. Tightening is free. This applies to every field in this plan and to the Personal Vault section in vault-plan D-010. Refined by D-007 (2026-10-17).\n\n### D-004 — Move, not redesign\nDate: 2026-10-17\nBasis: [self-imposed] behaviour preservation for R-1.\n\nMoving the tool ceiling into identity definitions keeps today's values exactly, proven by a before-and-after census. Tuning any role's ceiling is a separate later change.\n\n### D-005 — Identities declare, installations grant, org policy narrows\nDate: 2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, typed, directive #1959, verbatim] \"we will be distributing the identiries on the cupboard.  Lots of different organizations with differetnt structures and policies should be able to use and configure them, and same for personal vault. [...] we need this permission layer one level removed from the identity I think.\"\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog answer, verbatim] \"Revise into one plan (Recommended)\"\nBasis: audit report rpt_38002133-3a42-4204-86f5-4f6177314577 (directive #1960).\n\nThe identity holds only what is true wherever it is installed: persona, asks, publisher ceiling and floors. Supersedes revision 1's placement of wearers, spend cap and secret scope in the identity, and its \"identity as fourth policy layer\" chain. Refined by D-009 (2026-10-17) for stacks: \"ceiling\" becomes each layer's maximum and restrictions, and the binding splits into layer grants and stack settings.\n\n### D-006 — Personal Vault access is a binding\nDate: 2026-10-17\nBasis: D-005; [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, typed, directive #1959] \"same for personal vault [...] someone may want to use su identity without an email vault even installed some will want to use the email app and restrict acces and some will want to grant access\".\n\nVault access, standing-grant terms and after-read holds are set by the vault owner's binding for each installed identity; the identity only declares an optional vault ask. Avi's earlier \"Exempt su entirely\" and \"Open, recall on\" become Avi's settings for su (all effects, no expiry, no per-use approval, holds off, transcripts open, recall on), preserving today's behaviour there. All four D-010 settings (grant terms, after-read holds, transcript visibility, recall) move into stack settings. This replaces personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17 D-010. D-010 is not built (no code matches its fields as of 2026-10-17), so the supersession is recorded on that plan when Avi approves this revision.\n\n### D-007 — Loosening authority sits with the binding owner\nDate: 2026-10-17\nBasis: D-003 and D-005.\n\nThe approval D-003 requires comes from whoever owns the binding being loosened: the installation's administrator, which in Avi's workspace is Avi. A publisher cannot widen an installation by shipping a new version; a version that asks for more waits for re-consent.\n\n### D-008 — Identities name requirements, never routes or accounts\nDate: 2026-10-17\nBasis: audit report rpt_38002133-3a42-4204-86f5-4f6177314577.\n\nIdentities state requirements such as data-handling needs, capability classes and kinds of secret. Concrete routes, provider regions, accounts, branches and hosts are installation facts, chosen by the binding, org policy or launch.\n\n### D-009 — How stacked identities combine\nDate: 2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, typed, directive #1965, verbatim] \"are our identities stackable?  should they be?  if they should how would this effect this implementation?\"\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog answer, verbatim] \"Yes, write rev 3 (Recommended)\"\nBasis: code read 2026-10-17 (`slots.ts` cardinality, su composition, `blueprint-envelopes.ts` intersection); worked example report rpt_85e1a62a-c74a-4c54-8eef-bfb74cc10029 (directive #1968).\n\n1. Each layer contributes only what it asked for and was granted, within its own maximum. The session gets every layer's contribution, minus anything any layer restricts, then org policy narrows it, under fixed floors.\n2. Layer grants (asks granted, providers) attach to each installed layer. Stack settings (wearers, spend cap, secret scope, Personal Vault access) attach to each installed named stack.\n3. A stack change that widens access, by adding a contributing layer or removing a restricting one, is loosening and needs the owner's approval (D-003, D-007). This covers live attaches through the stack-mutation primitive.\n4. Modes and fleet posture keep their kernel-governed authority and contribute no grants.\n\nStack settings attach to the stack by name, not to one exact version: a new version keeps them unless it widens access. [self-imposed design call, disclosed to Avi in the worked example] Pinning to exact versions would re-prompt every wearer on every minor update.\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAmendment-Id: amend-0448dc22882dfa720c33c99b\nRequest-Hash: 0ffdb93d54c9617dd0d8a7cb85146cc9d4fcf815b7ae4c34b896609f22efbc93\nActor: su-c0dfd243-0305-4108-b98a-ed1823b2de6d\nReason: Re-pin acceptance rubric to plan revision 9. Checks must fail on today's tree. It enumerates modes x fleet positions from a source independent of the code under change, and records each tool's effective argument scope and a count control. Granting its asks later is the loosening, and it needs the binding owner's approval. Classification stays on effective permissions (R-11); classifying on asks would reopen D-009. (critique 2, C1)\n4.
