Unset wearers, secrets and vault access deny; an unset spend cap falls back to the project allocation. [self-imposed design call] (critique 2, C4; critique 1 goal gap)\n7. No hidden global override. Every session's effective tool set equals the chain result whatever the environment, query parameter (including ?superuser=1) or principal kind. P-001 lists the override channels. (both)\n8. SC-009 lists the exact expected tool set for each organization, so extra tools fail R-9 and R-14. (critique 2, X5)\n9. P-010 gets a clause, or a falsifier part, for each integrated case it lists: three-install su, the SC-009 two-organization stack, the SC-010 to SC-012 attacks, the restricted enterprise install, agent loosening plus a version upgrade, runtime-field refusal, and the census unchanged. (both)\n\nRejected: none in substance. Redundant SPEC clauses are repurposed onto the loopholes rather than deleted (critique 2), so each gap has one clause and its mutation requirement.\n\nNext: rubrics:amend rev 3, with outside-lineage approval for changed outcome bars; plans:set-specs; plan text for the new requirements (provenance derived); re-run the activation audit; spec-quality card and grading audit; two fresh critiques; plans:start.\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance contract revision after two outside critiques (per bar)\nDate: 2026-10-18\nBasis: D-011 (same two critiques and triage). [self-imposed] triage.\n\n- R-1: a closed allowlist schema that refuses unknown keys, tested with every workspace-schema key including dispatch.costCapUsd. Parse only; SPEC-P-012 keeps publish.\n- R-2: the falsifier adds 'a session is evaluated against the layers of the stack it wears'. SPEC-P-003 becomes its positive control: a seeded one-tool change that the comparator must flag.\n- R-3: adds a session-level case, a repo-wide search with a positive control, and a test identity that cannot be worn outside tests. SPEC-P-004 becomes the any-channel override check (D-011 item 7).\n- R-5: covers every session-creation path, not only launch: resume, fork, carry-respawn, wake and consult fork. A non-member gets no session record, process or inference call. Adds a revoked-member case. A stack with no groups denies [self-imposed design call]. SPEC-P-007 covers the non-launch paths.\n- R-6: the cap is checked before the call, and concurrent calls cannot overshoot it. Two installs of one named stack in one project do not share a cap. A cap above the project allocation is refused. SPEC-P-008 becomes 'an identity carrying a cost cap is refused'.\n- R-7: checks the secrets read path and the launch-time environment and materialization, not the launch-authority suite. SPEC-P-009 covers launch-time injection.\n- R-8: a stack with holds on, transcripts closed and recall off gets exactly that. Only the vault owner sets or widens vault fields. SPEC-P-001-VAULT names the four settings: grant terms, after-read holds, transcript visibility and recall. SPEC-P-015 becomes 'a non-owner cannot set the vault grant'.\n- R-9: one case per policy level. An approved loosening still cannot breach org policy or the fixed floors (D-002). Folds in SPEC-P-005's misattribution part.\n- R-10: asserts on the route that actually served the call (the gateway receipt), with a per-kind fixture and a failover fixture. SPEC-P-006 stays as the selection check, with the same failover case. Critique 1 suggested merging the two; critique 2 showed that selection and refusal differ.\n- R-11: says 'binding owner', not 'owner'. Forged approvals are refused, and so are replayed ones (an approval for change X reused for X'). Adds net classification, a shared-layer edit, and a new stack built from granted layers. SPEC-P-002 becomes 'approval from anyone other than the binding owner is refused'.\n- R-12: a frozen render of Avi's su prompt, captured at P-001, is the baseline. The falsifier covers renderer fallbacks, not only prompt files. SPEC-P-013 asserts that the rendered domain equals the workspace setting.\n- R-14: mapped to P-014 only. Narrowed to stack-keyed settings, no leaking of wearers or spend cap (SC-011), and non-widening versions keeping their settings. Its duplicates of R-8, R-9 and R-11 are removed. The vault-through-a-shared-layer case stays with R-8 and SPEC-P-015.\n- SPEC-P-010-ATTACKS: restated per attack, with positive outcomes (SC-011 keeps the granted tools; SC-012 neutral or narrowing changes apply), a positive control and two more attacks.\n- SPEC-P-014: kept, with a fixture identity that marks a grant as required.\n- P-011 docs: falsifier 'a listed topic is absent from the promoted artifact's served pages', pinned by a doc-claims test. The pages are named.\n- Goal gap (critique 1): a portability round-trip. Export, then import, reproduces the same effective outcome.\n\n### D-013 — Coordinate the frozen su baseline and shared identity seams with the identity-system migration\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAffects: identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18\nCo-signed sequencing from identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18#D-008 (co-sign coord-send-aa77ef5d8fe8ee8326b633bcf7ab785a5aa918524d83527ebe3b2423968303cc). IDOP owns the permission, wearer and schema seams; the other plan owns the prompt seams. Its P-002 precedes this plan's P-001 snapshot. That plan reuses this plan's frozen su render for parity rather than taking a second baseline. Any further change to su's prompt must precede the snapshot or be recorded here as an accepted delta before R-12 is checked.\n\nThe system-launched wearer model is jointly designed with P-007 and must cover judge/harness, consult, resume, fork and wake creation paths. The other plan's wearer generalization waits for P-012/P-003 and uses the effective chain from P-005; capability requests reuse P-014 layer asks, and identity revision widening reuses P-002's classifier and binding-owner approval.\n\nIf P-012/P-003 have not landed by about 2026-10-19 05:40Z, its P-003 may implement a thin launch-record generalization adopting asks/maximum/restrictions, keeping today's bound behind the one function P-003 replaces, and adding no new per-role table. This fallback does not change this plan's acceptance contract or authorize widening.\n\nMeasured: read the complete cross-plan D-008 from plans:get on 2026-10-18 05:52Z; its recorded co-signature, baseline order, dependencies and fallback match this ruling.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-005, P-007, P-012, P-014\n\n### D-014 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAmendment-Id: idop-r3-required-cases-apply-20261018-v1\nRequest-Hash: 8b0beb92c79930d0bdd8d36f632f1252a714246ceee7987537ae6321aa172610\nActor: su-c0dfd243-0305-4108-b98a-ed1823b2de6d\nReason: Apply D-011/D-012 acceptance refinements after the two critiques, corrected for outside objection thread-post:1190030. Existing tests-check cases selectors require all 61 named new cases across every declared file, preventing a passing pre-feature suite from discharging a BAR. R-14 maps to P-014 only and its old duplicate obligations remain on R-8/R-9/R-11 and their first-class specs; new R-15 adds the derived cross-installation export/import parity check. R-15 records its own pre-implementation declaration rather than copying R-14 provenance. R-2, R-8 and R-12 comparators are paired at grading (pre-change blob vs post-change code over the same catalog, fixtures or commit base; the R-12 render masks the generated guide sections), with the frozen P-001 artifacts kept as calibration, so drift from other lanes neither fails a bar nor licenses a re-freeze. Declined: deduping R-14's widened-version clause into R-11, because R-14's method already proves the layer grant itself is absent until re-consent, which is separate from R-11's stack approval hold (D-012). Not taken (optional): executable structural searches and a deployed su census check; D-013 gives the deployed census to identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18. No case exists yet and nothing is graded, so no proof or grade is invalidated, and no requirement is weakened. Bar/check alignment (critique 1, R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-6): the critic's preferred repair, expanding each condition, is refused by rubrics:amend as acceptance_bar_non_atomic_projection, and splitting would add bars with no plan requirement behind them. So each condition stays one observable behavior, and the method now says why each extra outcome is a regression of that behavior, rated as a falsifier clause by its own case or named search. New: an R-3 case for the named test identity; falsifier clauses for R-4's required-provider refusal and R-6's unset fallback; R-4's method case list now matches check.cases. This is a judgment call the reviewer may contest. R-9 (critique 2, vetting 4g): the single mid-session tightening case becomes a five-row live-session matrix with unchanged controls, one row a policy-level narrowing. R-14 (critique 2, vetting 4h): a live session cannot use a widened or reinstalled capability through a grant held before fresh consent, and a non-widening layer version keeps its layer grant. R-13 (vetting 3a): the Cupboard-publish half of the slot refusal gets its own case. Named mechanisms (vetting 3b, 6): the pre-change arm for R-2, R-8 and R-12 is materialized from P-001's base commit and blob-checked; the exact ceiling-table, env-reader and hard-coded-branch searches are named. Disclosures (vetting 5): R-11/R-14 widened-version overlap (authority D-011, D-016) and the R-4/R-8 selector overlap. Layers: R-5 adds unit (cold-loop wake case, new group-name case); R-13 adds integration (publish case). Implementation-review notes from both critiques are written into the R-5, R-7, R-8, R-10, R-12 and R-15 methods. Carry per directive #1983.\nApproved-By: su-b83fc5f9-2e9c-42e0-a2de-df78266f9d26\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1193344\nApproved-At: 2026-10-21T20:37:59.941Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 23 → 24\nChanged BARs: R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-9, R-11, R-13, R-14\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15\n\n### D-018 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: idop-rev7-ebe9-20261022-v1\nRequest-Hash: 8c94adefffaad31d6fa6b63ab0428ddfd76162131e2dfbfb020241e2a0956024\nActor: su-ebe9b9b1-f43d-4eb4-839d-e281da578e4b\nReason: Pre-implementation revision 7 batches the remaining independent revision-6 critiques. thread-post:1193349 requires R-3 org-policy enforcement to have its own case and R-8 non-owner mutation to be an explicit falsifier. thread-post:1193366 requires the R-9 live-session matrix to enumerate each grant, secret, layer and policy-level narrowing separately. R-3 adds the named org-policy case with a successful unchanged control; R-8 explicitly rates unauthorized changes to the four vault settings; R-9 replaces disjunctive families with ten separately bound rows, each asserting same-session next-action refusal before side effects, deciding source and an unchanged control. Carry on WI-6554700010019369.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive (R-1, R-10, R-8)\nRubric revision: 7 → 8\nSubject plan revision: 26 → 27\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-8, R-10\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-8, R-10\n\n### D-020 — Owner amendment: vault context narrows unified permissions and stays out of general history\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAffects: personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17\nOwner-directed amendment, 2026-10-22. Avi asked that the four vault/resource/history/intersection updates from report rpt_f728a193-dc87-4a89-af81-2ad1c51490c1 be written into this permissions plan. This is a change to the product contract, not an assertion that implementation exists.\n\n1. Every explicit or automatic vault disclosure carries server-owned vault/document/version/policy provenance. Register restrictions before delivery. Retained derivatives, summaries, compaction, forks and handoffs inherit them; a TTL, context truncation or model assertion does not release them. Revalidate queued/in-flight actions when authority narrows.\n2. Extend the existing capability and governance machinery to authorize scoped action/resource/argument requests (network destination, file path, store, account/recipient, model-processing route). A permitted tool grants no implicit resource access. Enforce at actual native/MCP/plugin/subprocess and service boundaries; required policies or containment unavailable means deny.\n3. Personal-vault payloads and their protected derivatives do not enter general session-history, embedding or recall indexes, including the originating agent and successor identities. Retain references/safe metadata; required transcript payloads are sealed under current vault access. Authorized searches query the vault directly. Cover native logs/caches/backups and cleanup of historical indexes; release does not retroactively make private history generally searchable.\n4. At one kernel evaluator, the identity stack's granted contribution-minus-restriction result is ANDed with user, organization/department/workspace and every vault ceiling represented by retained context, under fixed platform floors. Tools, actions, targets and arguments use one policy vocabulary and explanation trace. Identity layers still combine internally per D-009. Empty allowlists deny; no active context adds no restriction; unreadable required policy denies. Revocation/policy changes reach retained contexts; only the affected policy owner can authorize a permitted scoped release.\n\nThis supersedes D-004's move-only scope and the R-8/D-006 legacy su holds-off/transcripts-open preservation wherever inconsistent. su retains its authorized vault access and convenience settings, but cannot bypass owner/vault/org history and resource restrictions. Unrelated identity portability, grants, wearer, spend, secret and runtime-separation requirements remain. Refresh affected requirement/BAR/spec revisions and validation; old reviews and scorecards are historical and cannot authorize the amended plan.\n\nMeasured: disclosure-ledger.ts:244-285 records restricted disclosures only; transcript-exclusion.ts:106-113 exempts self; capability/bash.ts:774-858 requires offline execution when restricted; governance-policy/inherited-policy.ts defines the existing narrowing category chain. Full source assessment is preserved in the report.\nRelated: P-002, P-005, P-010, P-015\n\n### D-021 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: avi-vault-policy-amendment-20261022-v2\nRequest-Hash: 3c3bb94bc14f381a056d42ca230fbad85019fb389ad9ec9d1814347a4410adf2\nActor: su-ebe9b9b1-f43d-4eb4-839d-e281da578e4b\nReason: Apply exact independently approved D-020 preview1196178; retain every unrelated BAR. Source-origin authentication remains a separate activation gate.\nApproved-By: su-bb9513af-3995-41e2-82d5-dc0258da5820\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1196213\nApproved-At: 2026-10-22T16:25:07.216Z\nRubric revision: 8 → 9\nSubject plan revision: 37 → 38\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-4, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-16, R-17, R-18\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-2, R-4, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-16, R-17, R-18\n\n### D-022 — P-001 frozen baseline findings and source answers\nDate: 2026-10-22\nDate: 2026-10-22\nArtifact: docs/evidence/idop-p001-baseline-2026-10-22.json. Base commit 4ad5a574aa64e2f1579334706509f7c31d803e85; exact su render apps/operator/prompts/papercusp-su.codex.md blob 48a110ada584a80270337ac21ec7bccae76d5cf0, sha256 773df2049c2ca9a8b9438449e0dff447dacda4cd3bd6c8f00a43ac2eb9024fcd. The artifact enumerates 2 harness roles, 29 built-in identities and 1,020 exact argument schemas from a real launched Codex home's managed tool prompts, with real activation/tool-invocation receipts and explicit refusal rows.\n\nMeasured answers:\n1. Identity launch applies base knobs/params because compositions extend base before slotted contributions.\n2. Current session-governance judges model/provider/data-use from launch records but does not consume the worn identity stack; D-020's unified evaluator is not implemented.\n3. P-016 is blocked work added by D-020. No P-019 exists in the current IDOP plan.\n4. Current wearer-authority resolves launch role and capability ceilings only; it has no directory-group wearer support.\n5. Secret scope is planned stack state; current launch materialization remains host/path-specific rather than an identity-stack binding.\n6. Current Cupboard identity install consent binds one exact artifact hash plus its computed subject set, not each layer or named stack independently.\n7. Consent subjects can name grants and pot provider bindings, but provider bindings cannot hold per-layer grant decisions or stack settings; those are unimplemented.\n8. Modes and fleet posture add no grants today; observed differences are principal/role authorization or kernel mode narrowing. Full-access override channels are launch environment, legacy ?superuser=1, authenticated principal kind, role envelope, mode registry and fleet posture.\n9. Legacy su vault baseline is all effects/no expiry/no per-use approval, holds off, transcripts open and recall on. D-020 supersedes that as the future contract: retain it only as calibration, never as authority to bypass vault/org history or resource restrictions.\n\nObserved defect: five identities advertised launchable cannot compile because practice prompts are missing; blueprint-operation-worker launches but agent_tools:list is role-refused. Tracked as EI-26700090355079325 rather than omitted from the census.\n\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-identities/idop-p001-baseline.test.ts and identity-surface-census.test.ts passed 29/29 locally; per-file lint:tsc passed. Give the measurement to `parked-agent-census-resumption-and-root-cause-2026-… <!-- P-010 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi, and any agent asked to audit or resume parked agents. Also every agent that reads its own Orientation block at turn start.\n\n**Problem.** The 2026-10-17 parked-agent sweep (report `rpt_7a449b1b-64f6-4097-b3bd-5b5ec00d6eab`, author su-637d70bf) reached a sound result, but only through manual assembly. Its author had to:\n\n- join six separate sources (presence, claims, checkpoints, real event waits, registered modes, wake delivery and turn evidence), finally with raw SQL after bulk reads ran out of budget;\n- force an explicit full lens, because the default roster read drops rows past a cap;\n- keep three look-alike field pairs apart by hand: the always-armed inbox listener vs. a real blocker; `wakeMode:auto` vs. registered AUTO; queued/delivered vs. a turn that actually started. These were the previous edition's mistakes (WI-6554700010016838);\n- carry the owner's request across compaction by hand, where it degraded to an \"unverified\" quote;\n- preserve earlier corrections by hand;\n- spend too long finding the existing pieces.\n\nTwo more gaps came up while reading the report on 2026-10-17. Both were checked against the database and the code:\n\n- **The follow-ups have no owner.** The report says WI-6554700010017003 and WI-6554700010017004 are owned by its author. `harness_shared.work_items` shows both released by su-637d70bf at 23:06:12 UTC, about two minutes after the report was published (23:03:56). Both are open with `taken_by` empty. The report still says they are owned.\n- **Orientation has the same listener-as-blocker problem.** `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-obligation-providers.ts` (around line 1608) maps every event await to `status:'blocked'`. It also maps `onTimeout:'expire'` to `priority:'high'`. So the always-armed `coord:inbox-wake:<self>` listener shows as \"[BLOCKED] Awaiting coord:inbox-wake:… (expires SILENTLY)\". It appeared in the Orientation block of the session that wrote this plan.\n\n**Outcome.** The next parked-agent audit is one paginated, read-only `coord:roster` call, with complete, counted coverage and no caller SQL. Look-alike fields cannot be confused, either there or in Orientation. The owner's request and earlier corrections travel with the audit. The ten unconfirmed pickups each have a disposition. Every follow-up has an owner.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n\n- No new table, verb, cron or monitor (the report's own constraint).\n- No replacement sessions, account or credential changes, or parallel monitoring loops, unless Avi chooses relaunch for ended recipients (see Open choices).\n- Do not change the frozen historical acceptance population of `parked-agent-census-resumption-and-root-cause-2026-10-09`, and do not fork its P-013 re-measure. This plan feeds it.\n- Not a fix for why agents park. The earlier plan owns root cause.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner directive #1973 (Avi, 2026-10-17): \"read this report and then write a plan for filling the gaps this report identified\". Report `rpt_7a449b1b-64f6-4097-b3bd-5b5ec00d6eab`. Proposal WI-6554700010017003. Ten-pickup follow-up WI-6554700010017004.\n\n**Scenarios.**\n\n1. Avi asks \"are any agents parked that shouldn't be?\" An agent calls `coord:roster { view:'audit' }`, pages to the end, and answers, for example: \"478 parked, 478 covered, 0 missing, 0 duplicates; 41 waiting on a real gate; 12 parked with executable work\". No SQL is written.\n2. The audit asks 12 agents to resume. Next day the same view shows each request as queued, delivered, turn started and replied, and shows \"unknown\" where there is no evidence.\n3. An agent compacts mid-audit. Its successor reads the audit's owner request by directive id, sees that Avi typed it, and sees the previous audit and its corrections.\n4. At turn start, every agent sees its inbox listener described as a listener, not as BLOCKED.\n\n**Assumptions.**\n\n- [inferred] The two follow-ups were released by the author's wind-down (completing WI-6554700010016973 or ending its loop), not by a deliberate hand-off. P-001 checks this before anything is filed.\n- The turn-start proof built by `parked-agent-census-resumption-and-root-cause-2026-10-09#P-006` is recorded in `harness_shared.event_wake_deliveries` and can be joined per message. P-005 confirms this first.\n\n**Open choices for Avi.**\n\n- **Ended recipients among the ten:** report only (default), or relaunch them with identity preserved under the earlier plan's D-014 rule.\n- **Owner-visibility reports:** `reports:get` returns `not_found` to an agent for an owner-visibility report, even when Avi hands that agent the id, so this plan's author read the report with SQL. Letting Avi share an owner report with a named agent is a visibility (security) decision. It stays out of this plan unless Avi wants it in.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Complete audit without SQL.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Complete parked-agent audit through one read surface, no caller SQL\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"directive:1973\",\"report:rpt_7a449b1b-64f6-4097-b3bd-5b5ec00d6eab\",\"work_item:WI-6554700010017003\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Paging coord:roster view:'audit' to the end returns the complete parked population for one asOf. The clean test-run21376667 is an execution receipt for this actual production path; the old generic audit e2e file contains no R7 test and cannot substitute.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-obligation-providers.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/parked-agent-orientation.e2e.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Findable.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The next auditor finds the audit view without a search expedition\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"report:rpt_7a449b1b-64f6-4097-b3bd-5b5ec00d6eab\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"tools:find and docs:search for 'parked agent audit' each return coord:roster view:'audit' or its how-to doc in the top three results.\",\"falsifier\":\"Either tools:find or docs:search for 'parked agent audit' misses the intended coord:roster audit view or its how-to doc in its top three results. An unavailable, degraded, or skipped live search measurement cannot establish healthy.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredScope\":[\"docs:search\",\"tools:find\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"e2e\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the maintained R-8 live discovery detector in parked-agent-audit.e2e.test.ts with PAPERCUSP_PARKED_SEARCH_LIVE=1 and PAPERCUSP_APP_OPERATION_LIVE_PROFILE=packages/operator-core/test/parked-agent-audit.live-profile.json. It calls both authenticated current-build searches with the exact query 'parked agent audit', checks fixed coord:roster view=audit and agent-insights/parked-agent-audit-roster-view identities at rank <=3 on EACH surface, records both ranks, and rejects unavailable/degraded measurements. Its independently constructed controls reject omission, rank four, and lookalike identity on either surface; a measured e2e run without live opt-in fails rather than passing controls alone.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/parked-agent-audit.e2e.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nThese choices are proposals. They become recorded Decisions once Avi approves.\n\n- **D-001 (proposed): extend `coord:roster` with a read-only `view:'audit'`.** No new table, verb, cron or monitor. Code: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/coordination/tools/roster.ts` and `packages/operator-core/lib/adv-roster.ts`. It reuses the presence oracle (`sessionState`), claims (`work_items.taken_by`), the work-item checkpoint store, the mode registry, recorded external blockers, `event_wake_deliveries`, coord replies (`related_msg_id`), the orders ledger, `report_library` lineage, `audits/` text artifacts and the oracles in `parked-agent-audit.e2e.test.ts`. Why: each source already exists. The gap is composition, completeness and labelling.\n- **D-002 (proposed): one wait classifier (`listener` | `substantive` | `none`)** shared by the audit view and the Orientation obligation provider, so the two cannot disagree.\n- **D-003 (proposed): snapshot paging.** `auditId` is derived from asOf and the population. Every cursor page reads the same snapshot and carries a coverage block. Totals are checked against the roster writer's whole-population count.\n- **D-004 (proposed): the earlier plan keeps its frozen population and its P-013.** This plan supplies the instrument for that re-measure and does not repeat it.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-003, P-009, P-010 | live |\n| R-9 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-003, P-009 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-004, P-005, P-009 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-004, P-009 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-006, P-009 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-006, P-009 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-001, P-002 | live |\n| R-7 | P-007 | live |\n| R-8 | P-008 | live |\n\n## Phase 1 — Make the open follow-ups real (operations, no product code)\n\n- **P-001** `done` Re-own the orphaned follow-ups and correct the record. WI-6554700010017003 and WI-6554700010017004 were released by su-637d70bf at 23:06:12 UTC, after the report described them as owned. If the author is live, ask whether the release was intended. Otherwise: WI-6554700010017003 becomes this plan's implementing item; WI-6554700010017004 is claimed by whoever runs P-002. Ask the author to publish a correction edition (supersedes `rpt_7a449b1b-…`). Find out what released them. If a wind-down released residue that a completion had just counted as owned, file that defect with evidence; the cause is only inferred so far. — note: ← WI-6554700010017498 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Settle the ten unconfirmed pickups (WI-6554700010017004). For each recipient/message pair recorded on the item, read `sessionState`, the exact delivery row and turn-start proof, any reply linked to that message, and activity since. Record one disposition each: picked up (with proof), alive but not taking turns, ended, or unknown. Re-wake once only the alive, parked recipients whose work is still executable. Never count queued or delivered as pickup. Ended recipients are reported; relaunch only if Avi chooses it. Close with coverage over all ten. — note: ← WI-6554700010017499 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 2 — The audit view\n\n- **P-003** `done` Population, snapshot and complete pagination. Add read-only `view:'audit'` to `coord:roster`. It returns `auditId`, `asOf` and cursor pages over one snapshot. Every page has a coverage block: total (from the roster writer's whole-population parked count), covered so far, missing and duplicates. This lens is not cut by `EXPLICIT_LIVENESS_ROW_CAP`; any bound is marked `truncatedByLimit` with its count. Unit and integration tests ship with it. (R-1) — note: ← WI-6554700010017500 completed (done)\n- **P-004** `done` Per-agent evidence. For each agent: owned work (claims), the latest checkpoint's next/left/blockers, recorded external blockers, gate ownership, owner holds, registered modes from the mode store, and whether independently executable work exists. Add the shared wait classifier (D-002): the always-armed `coord:inbox-wake:<self>` is a listener and never justifies parking. Every field carries known/unknown, source and observedAt; a stale or missing value reads as unknown. Depends on P-003. (R-2, R-3) — note: ← WI-6554700010017501 completed (done)\n- **P-005** `done` Wake outcome ladder. For each resumption request (coord:send, wake or dispatch message id), report queued, delivered, turnStarted and replied as separate steps. Sources: `event_wake_deliveries` (turn-start proof from `parked-agent-census-resumption-and-root-cause-2026-10-09#P-006`) and replies linked by `related_msg_id`. A missing step is unknown, neither failed nor succeeded. Activity inside the window is reported as activity, not as caused by the request. Depends on P-003. (R-2) — note: ← WI-6554700010017502 completed (done)\n- **P-006** `done` Owner request, previous audit and corrections. The audit records the requesting owner directive id. The view resolves it to the verbatim turn and its turn origin, labels unverified or agent-origin text, and never upgrades it to owner authority. It also returns the last comparable audit (`audits/` text artifacts plus `report_library` lineage) with its correction history. Resumption messages carry the directive id, so recipients read the original turn instead of a pasted quote. Depends on P-003. (R-4, R-5) — note: ← WI-6554700010017503 completed (done)\n\n## Phase 3 — Same fix in Orientation, discovery, proof\n\n- **P-007** `done` Orientation: the inbox listener is not BLOCKED. `agent-obligation-providers.ts` (around line 1608) maps every event await to `status:'blocked'`, and `onTimeout:'expire'` to `priority:'high'`. Use the P-004 classifier so the listener renders as a listener (not blocked, not high priority) while real awaits are unchanged. Test both cases. Check the other readers of the same rows (`coord:orient`, the leader brief) for the same mistake. Depends on P-004. (R-7) — note: ← WI-6554700010017522 completed (done)\n- **P-008** `done` Discovery. Update `coord:roster` guidance (`when`) so \"audit parked agents\" routes to `view:'audit'`. Measure the change with `npm run tool-weight -- coord:roster` against the prompt-weight gate. Author an agent-insights doc with `docs:author`: how to run the audit, the field-meaning table (listener vs blocker, wakeMode vs registered AUTO, queued vs started vs replied) and the oracle tests. Confirm `tools:find` and `docs:search` return both. Depends on P-003..P-006. (R-8) — note: ← WI-6554700010017523 completed (done)\n- **P-009** `done` Regression oracles against the live view. Extend `parked-agent-audit.e2e.test.ts` so its population and wake-outcome oracles run against `view:'audit'` bundles. Add cases for: multi-page completeness and truncation, missing or duplicate owners, a stale or unknown blocker treated as cleared, the listener treated as a real wait, wakeMode treated as AUTO, queued treated as pickup, and forged or lost owner provenance. Prove each new guard catches its mutant with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh`. Depends on P-003..P-006. (R-1..R-5) — note: ← WI-6554700010017524 completed (done)\n- **P-010** `done` Dogfood and hand off. Run the next parked-agent audit using only `view:'audit'` (no SQL), save it, and publish the report. Give the measurement to `parked-agent-census-resumption-and-root-cause-2026-10-09#P-013` (its re-measure) instead of repeating it here. Success: zero caller SQL, complete coverage, every unknown labelled. Depends on P-007..P-009. — note: ← WI-6554700010017525 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n(None recorded yet. D-001..D-004 above are proposals until Avi approves.)\n\n### D-001 — Avi approved AUTO execution in this session; adopt the proposed design and default scope\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAvi explicitly instructed this session to register AUTO and carry this plan to shipped status itself: session_turn:codex:01a14c3b-0ad7-7483-884b-e639ed198399:17. This is the implementation route, with no implementation fan-out. Adopt the four proposed design choices in the Design section: extend coord:roster, share the listener/substantive/none classifier with Orientation, freeze and completely page the population, and preserve the historical census/P-013. Ended recipients remain report-only by default; no new replacement sessions, credential changes or parallel monitor. Owner-visibility sharing changes remain out of scope. Existing implementation/regression evidence is reused before adding source changes. execution","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-17","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Personal Vault — privacy, security and reliable agent execution\nslug: personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-17\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-17\nupdated: 2026-10-17\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-17, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty. Next repair: Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nRevised 2026-10-17 by su-c0dfd243 (WI-6554700010016881) after review report rpt_b4a297fd-ce3f-4f1f-94c6-f79bc7f8bd41; Avi chose to have it revised along that review's lines [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog]. P-009 is a short baseline, after which Track A (vault policy and protection, P-001 to P-008) and Track B (execution observability and recovery, P-010 to P-015) run in parallel. Each vault item names the shipped code it extends. Telemetry is metadata-only (D-009); v1 traces live in Postgres and the collector waits for a destination (D-008); identity profiles keep su unrestricted while allowing stricter enterprise identities (D-007); Redis and Kafka are deferred entirely (D-006).\n\nThis plan replaced the unstarted drafts personal-vault-agent-privacy-security-2026-10-16 and tracing-failure-recovery-and-data-governance-2026-10-16 (archived, readable). It is still a draft: nothing is activated and no workers are running. su gets a standing all-effects vault grant with no expiry or per-use approval (D-007, resolved 2026-10-17); su's identity definition turns after-read holds off, and vault access is configured per identity definition rather than hard-coded (D-010, 2026-10-17).\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"The owner of a Personal Vault, operators diagnosing agent work, enterprise administrators controlling data destinations, and engineers maintaining Papercusp's agent, tool, storage, provider and DBOS boundaries.\",\n  \"problem\": \"Vault privacy controls, inference policy, action authorization, retention and audit are distributed across separate paths. Reliable agent execution adds a second boundary: operations need trace correlation, accountable failed-work recovery and safe replay, but telemetry and failure records can themselves leak personal or enterprise data. A read must never be mistaken for permission to infer, export, send, retain or replay.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Papercusp provides one governed privacy and reliable-execution boundary: every read and action is attributable and scoped; local versus external inference is enforced; vault data and derived artifacts are protected across their lineage; operations can be followed across API, DBOS, agent, tool and model boundaries; failed work can be inspected and safely recovered; lock, revocation, deletion and policy decisions remain effective during races, retries and collector outages.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Build a second vault, agent framework, grant system, policy engine, message broker, scheduler or workflow runner.\",\n    \"Adopt Redis, Kafka or Datadog; choose a paid telemetry backend; or build NRTM/shared-session features.\",\n    \"Treat no-training terms as no retention, or claim encryption protects against an operator who holds both ciphertext and keys.\",\n    \"Export raw prompts, retrieved documents, secrets, credentials or complete evaluation evidence as operational telemetry by default.\",\n    \"Claim customer acceptance, legal compliance, certification, support commitments or final shipment from source-only or current-build evidence.\",\n    \"Start implementation, activate the plan or launch workers in this planning operation.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:10\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:19\",\n    \"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:12\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Select OpenTelemetry plus a collector, DLQ-style failure handling and enforced model-data governance; Before activation, re-read the complete source conversation and audit every requirement, scope boundary, dependency and recommendation.\n\n## Background\n\nPapercusp already has the important authorities to extend: Personal Vault grants/retrieval/receipts, inference and action policy, envelope/key-version sealing, lock/revocation and retention/audit; DBOS workflow checkpoints and recovery; event/reaction deduplication; route/tool records; enterprise inherited governance and SIEM/data-processing contracts; and OpenTelemetry-related DBOS/evaluation support. Source presence is not deployed or end-to-end evidence.\n\nOpenTelemetry findings:\n- The installed DBOS SDK supports OpenTelemetry tracing and OTLP export. The inspected application DBOS bootstrap does not explicitly establish an active collector or configured exporter endpoint.\n- `toOpenTelemetryOpenInferenceTrace` is a plain compatibility projection for evaluation evidence, not application-wide operational collection. It may contain full trajectory content and must not be exported as operational telemetry without a separate data contract.\n- Optional OpenTelemetry packages are accounted for in bundling, which proves packaging support rather than live traces.\n\nv1 records trace and span ids on existing Postgres records (D-008). When export is added, the standard OpenTelemetry Collector with OTLP is the recommended component, verified against a local recording sink. Grafana Alloy is the strongest distribution alternative; it is OpenTelemetry-based, not a different tracing standard. Existing PostgreSQL activity records plus metrics/logs remain the minimal-infrastructure baseline. Prometheus is metrics/alerting, not a complete span chain; eBPF tools such as Beyla are optional network-level supplements. No paid backend is selected.\n\n## Existing implementation baseline\n\nThree Personal Vault plans have shipped: `personal-vault-2026-08-22` (charter, D-001), `personal-vault-live-integrations-2026-08-23` and `personal-data-reader-set-labels-2026-10-01`. Track A extends their code and does not build a second vault, grant table, gateway or label system. Paths are relative to `papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/`. The Today column comes from reading module headers and key functions on 2026-10-17; P-009 confirms it by observation.\n\n| Item | Today (shipped) | Gap | Change |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| P-001 grants | `harness_shared.personal_grants` rows (principal binding, agent-role or plan-template; scopes; revoked_at; expires_at) checked by `personal-vault/authorization.ts`. The vault module has no retention policy. | No lineage receipt across derived artifacts. | Lineage-aware purge receipts reusing legal holds; add a vault retention policy. |\n| P-008 untrusted content | Transcript exclude-at-read (`personal-vault/transcript-exclusion.ts`); coord and shared-store sealing; owner-only loosening against prompt injection (`personal-vault/release-authority.ts`); provider-egress refusal at shell and fetch seams. | Foreign MCP, runtime files, replay inputs and telemetry baggage are not covered. | Extend the existing seams to those inputs. |\n\n## Threat model and deployment shape\n\n**Deployment shapes.** The product is the Tauri desktop app: one install with an embedded Postgres, an operator sidecar and, by default, one user. The hosted/enterprise shape (`papercusp-enterprise-readiness-roadmap-2026-10-09`) adds several users and organizations on one operator. Every requirement is judged in the desktop shape unless it says otherwise; tenant-isolation checks (R-8, R-14, R-15) apply to the hosted shape.\n\n**In scope.**\n1. A prompt-injected or misbehaving agent whose context tries to widen grants, change destinations or exfiltrate. This is the primary adversary.\n2. Another user or tenant on a shared operator (hosted shape).\n3. External model providers: retention, training and logging of what they receive, controlled through identity profiles (D-007).\n4. Leak paths: logs, telemetry, failure records, caches, exports and backups.\n5. A lost or stolen device: at-rest encryption, with key custody specified in P-004.\n\n**Out of scope.** An attacker holding both ciphertext and keys, root compromise of the host, and malicious Papercusp code.\n\n## Enterprise reuse and authority boundaries\n\n| Authority | Owns | This merged plan does |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Personal Vault | Grants, retrieval receipts, inference destinations, encryption/key custody, action authorization, lock/revocation, retention/deletion and personal audit | Extends these authorities to traces, collector buffers, failure metadata and replay lineage; never creates a second policy or vault system. |\n| Enterprise roadmap `papercusp-enterprise-readiness-roadmap-2026-10-09` | Organization policy, provider/region/classification rules, SIEM export, enterprise retention, private processing, keys and integrated enterprise acceptance | Reuses P-005/P-007/P-008/P-016 and their decisions; does not duplicate or close their remaining acceptance/shipment obligations. |\n| DBOS | Workflow checkpoints, queue execution, retry/recovery and versioned operation history | Remains execution authority. Recovery projections and adapters link to DBOS; they do not become a scheduler or competing state machine. |\n| Existing audit/SIEM | Authoritative security/action evidence and redacted export | Operational traces may be sampled/dropped; they never replace required audit evidence. |\n\nExisting enterprise P-005/P-007/P-008/P-016 are recorded implementation work, not a claim that enterprise acceptance or shipment is complete. Reuse decisions include the enterprise data map, SIEM correlation/redaction/replay, processing/key/derived-data contracts and shared receipt writers. The mapped P-item must independently prove required operational/current-build or final-artifact outcomes; a green narrow suite is insufficient.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/admin/failure-recovery.integration.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/e2e/admin-failure-recovery.spec.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat in an isolated supported profile with the same pinned code, policy and configuration. Final artifact evidence is separate for R-17.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-16 — Integrated privacy, execution and recovery verification.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Isolated current-build DBOS runtimes under su/owner and restrictive test profiles exercise allowed work, private/external inference, retries/restarts, concurrent replay, revoked/locked receipts, secret/content canaries, tenant isolation, deletion propagation, telemetry export loss and overhead. Required paths have source-bound assertions, runtime receipts and explicit checked/notChecked/notApplicable coverage.\",\"rationale\":\"Merged from the two unstarted owner-requested drafts and refined by the recorded overlap recommendations; source turns are retained in Product shaping.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:10\",\"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:19\",\"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:12\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The frozen integrated population runs in isolated current-build DBOS storage with recording model and tool endpoints, never shared live queues, under both the su/owner and a restrictive test profile, and records checked, notChecked and notApplicable coverage per scenario.\",\"falsifier\":\"Tests enqueue into shared live queues, skipped/missing paths are claimed verified, or an isolated success is generalized to all operations and sinks.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"Integrated privacy, execution and recovery verification\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"e2e\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"P-009 freezes the population, route, policy versions, sinks and evidence procedure. Extend maintained project-native tests at the listed reuse targets or their conventional adjacent suites. Use legitimate and violating controls; retain raw receipts, unknowns and owned residue. A source file or compatibility projection alone is not proof of runtime behavior. The files are reuse/extension targets, not a claim that current assertions cover the new feature. Future suites (including admin-failure-recovery and privacy-recovery-artifact) must be delivered in the project framework and registered for CI before acceptance. The mapped P-item must independently prove required operational/current-build or final-artifact outcomes; a green narrow suite is insufficient.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/events/engine-durable.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/governance-policy/sensitive-action.integration.test.ts\",\"apps/operator/e2e/admin-failure-recovery.spec.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat in an isolated supported profile with the same pinned code, policy and configuration. Final artifact evidence is separate for R-17.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-17 — Documentation, support and exact shipment.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Document supported operation classes, policy/retention boundaries, collector configuration/destinations, recovery runbooks, unsupported cases and upgrade/rollback. Verify the exact promoted/released artifact, collector configuration and policy behavior separately from staging/current-build preparation.\",\"rationale\":\"Merged from the two unstarted owner-requested drafts and refined by the recorded overlap recommendations; source turns are retained in Product shaping.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:10\",\"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:19\",\"session_turn:codex:01a146af-dd5c-7140-91d9-ca09282a5d2b:12\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Documentation covers supported operations, identity profiles, policy and retention boundaries, telemetry configuration, recovery runbooks and unsupported cases; the promoted artifact and its configuration are verified separately from staging evidence.\",\"falsifier\":\"A source or staging run is presented as shipment, an unsupported replay is undocumented, or release configuration is not verified.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"Documentation, support and exact shipment\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"deployed\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"e2e\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"P-009 freezes the population, route, policy versions, sinks and evidence procedure. Extend maintained project-native tests at the listed reuse targets or their conventional adjacent suites. Use legitimate and violating controls; retain raw receipts, unknowns and owned residue. A source file or compatibility projection alone is not proof of runtime behavior. The files are reuse/extension targets, not a claim that current assertions cover the new feature. Future suites (including admin-failure-recovery and privacy-recovery-artifact) must be delivered in the project framework and registered for CI before acceptance. The mapped P-item must independently prove required operational/current-build or final-artifact outcomes; a green narrow suite is insufficient.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/e2e/admin-failure-recovery.spec.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/release/privacy-recovery-artifact.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat in an isolated supported profile with the same pinned code, policy and configuration. Final artifact evidence is separate for R-17.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n### Privacy and retrieval\n\nThe retrieval gateway alone decrypts or returns vault plaintext. It resolves identity, purpose, source ACLs and reader sets, minimizes excerpts, records content-free audit and returns a short-lived context receipt. Privacy reader sets intersect as restricted records are read, so additional sensitive records can only narrow allowed destinations.\n\n### Inference and actions\n\nThe inference broker rechecks current receipts and the caller's identity-profile policy before every model call (D-007). The su/owner profile is unrestricted. A restrictive profile can impose local-only mode, which forbids provider traffic, including telemetry, retries, caches and tools, or require a separate expiring grant naming provider/model/region/endpoint/retention/training/caching/files/tracing/tool policy. The typed action broker handles sends, exports, provider mutations, credentials and replay proposals; models never hold action authority or long-lived secrets.\n\n### Encryption and lifecycle\n\nExtend existing envelope/key-version primitives with personal scope and separate custody. Protect primary records, embeddings, indexes, caches, transcripts, failed-work input references, replay lineage, exports and backups. Operational telemetry is metadata-only and outside this lineage (D-009). Lock removes usable key material; revocation invalidates receipts and stops eligible work. Purge emits lineage receipts distinguishing removed data, pending backup expiry and legal holds. Search leakage remains documented.\n\n### Tracing and collector\n\nUse OpenTelemetry API/instrumentation. v1 stores trace and span ids on existing Postgres records and shows them in admin views (D-008); OTLP export through a collector follows once a destination is chosen. Reuse DBOS spans without installing competing global tracer providers or duplicating workflow spans. Carry operation identity through API, enqueue/dequeue, process launch, agent, tool and model boundaries; preserve parent/link relationships across retries and replay. Collector receives only approved metadata/protected references, authenticates boundaries and rejects untrusted baggage as authority. Collector outage follows a bounded degradation policy; business work continues and export loss is observable. Security audit failure remains independently fail-closed.\n\nThe collector transports/processes signals; it is not a trace database or viewer. Acceptance uses a local recording sink. Production trace storage, viewer, destination, retention and export permission remain explicit configuration/design choices; no paid backend is selected and existing admin ledgers remain usable without an external backend.\n\n### Failed-work recovery\n\nProject selected DBOS, reaction and delivery failures over authoritative records. Preserve original operation, owner, cause, attempts, protected references, status, current policy decision and next action. A replay is a new immutable attempt linked to the original; current authorization, lock/revocation, source permissions and action policy are rechecked. Concurrent redrives converge through atomic claims. Completed or ambiguous external effects require reconciliation; unsupported DBOS/version cases are explicit.\n\n### Alternatives\n\n| Option | Role and tradeoff | Decision |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Standard OpenTelemetry Collector | Vendor-neutral receive/process/export boundary; focused initial component set. | Recommended once an export destination is chosen (D-008). |\n| Grafana Alloy | OpenTelemetry distribution with Prometheus, logs and profiling integrations. | Qualify if combined collection reduces operations. |\n| PostgreSQL activity plus metrics/logs | Minimal new infrastructure and durable local evidence; custom trace propagation/exploration required. | v1 trace store; remains the authority (D-008). |\n| Vendor APM SDK | Packaged UI/integration with vendor coupling and another data boundary. | Not selected. |\n| Prometheus | Aggregate metrics and alerting. | Complement only. |\n| eBPF/Beyla | Automatic Linux HTTP/gRPC/RED observations. | Optional supplement, not business workflow tracing. |\n\n### Verification and evidence\n\nUse isolated DBOS system storage, recording fake model/tool endpoints and a recording network sink. Never enqueue crash drills into shared live queues. Freeze populations in P-009: allowed/denied reads, local/external inference, provider/region cases, lock/revocation races, retries/restarts, duplicate/ambiguous replay, secret/content canaries, su/owner and restrictive identity profiles, tenant isolation (hosted shape), telemetry export loss, deletion propagation and overhead. Record checked/notChecked/notApplicable coverage and owned residue. Source tests, compatibility JSON and current-build evidence do not prove deployment, buyer, legal or final-artifact acceptance.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-012 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-013 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-015 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-016 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-017 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — Baseline, then Track A: vault policy and protection\n\n- **P-009** `todo` Baseline: confirm current OpenTelemetry/DBOS wiring by observation, freeze the supported current-build profile and the operation/failure population, measure the overhead baseline and confirm the existing-implementation table. Owner choices (export destination, retention) are decisions, not part of this item. importance: high\n- **P-001** `todo` Type the existing `personal_grants` scopes by effect (read, infer:local, infer:external, send, export, admin, replay) with purpose, source/account, time/volume bounds, expiry and approver; add a vault section to the identity definition (D-007, D-010) holding the standing-grant effects with expiry/approval terms and an after-read-holds switch honoured by git-sync-hold, coord-seal, shared-store-seal, the outbound send check and the provider-egress binding, a transcript-visibility switch (transcript-exclusion) and an automatic-recall switch (ambient recall); widening it takes the owner's own action; replace the coding-role regex with that section's default in the coding-role definitions; the su definition grants all effects with no expiry or per-use approval, turns holds off, leaves transcripts open and turns automatic recall on; restrictive enterprise identities use the same fields; migrate existing grants without loss. importance: high blocked-by: P-009\n- **P-002** `todo` Route every existing vault read path (personal search, ask, open-sealed, ambient recall, delegated reads) through one gateway over `authorizePersonalAccess` and the disclosure ledger that minimizes excerpts, records content-free audit and returns a short-lived receipt. importance: high blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-003** `todo` Inference policy per identity profile (D-007): reuse enterprise processing-route provider/region resolution for personal scope, recheck the receipt and profile before each model call, and enforce restrictive options (local-only, provider allow-list, minimum fields); the su/owner profile stays unrestricted. importance: high blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-004** `todo` Add per-user key derivation, key versions and rotation to the existing archive and sealed-store encryption; specify desktop key custody; cover normalized records, embeddings, indexes, caches, transcripts, failed-work input references, exports and backups (telemetry excluded per D-009); document search leakage. importance: high blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-005** `todo` Extend the reader-set and sensitive-action checks used by gated outbound verbs to exports, provider mutations, credential use and replay proposals; record completed-effect evidence for reconciliation. importance: high blocked-by: P-002\n- **P-006** `todo` Add vault lock, receipt invalidation, background retrieval/replay stop on lock or revocation, step-up for export/recovery/purge/loosening in restrictive profiles, and owner-visible lock/recovery status. importance: high blocked-by: P-002, P-005\n- **P-007** `todo` Add lineage-aware purge receipts across primary records and derived artifacts (embeddings, summaries, caches, exports, backups, failed-work input references), reusing enterprise legal holds, plus a vault retention policy. importance: high blocked-by: P-004, P-006\n- **P-008** `todo` Extend untrusted-content resistance (transcript exclusion, coord/shared-store sealing, release authority, provider-egress refusal) to foreign MCP, runtime files, replay inputs and telemetry baggage; tenant checks apply to the hosted shape. importance: high blocked-by: P-001, P-003, P-005\n\n## Phase 2 — Track B: execution observability (runs in parallel with Track A)\n\n- **P-010** `todo` Telemetry data contract (D-009): an in-process span-attribute allow-list, a protected-reference format and a failure-record field contract, with a restricted-canary test proving no content reaches spans, logs or failure records. importance: high blocked-by: P-009\n- **P-011** `todo` Propagate W3C trace context across API, DBOS enqueue/dequeue, agent launch, tool and model boundaries using DBOS's OpenTelemetry support without a competing global tracer; record trace and span ids on existing Postgres records (D-008); link retry and recovery attempts without duplicate completed effects. importance: high blocked-by: P-010\n- **P-012** `todo` After the owner picks an export destination (D-008), add OTLP export through the standard OpenTelemetry Collector with metadata-only export, authentication, health, sampling/backpressure and outage behavior; export loss never blocks business work. importance: high blocked-by: P-011\n\n## Phase 3 — Track B: failed-work recovery\n\n- **P-013** `todo` Project DBOS ERROR/RETRIES_EXCEEDED workflows and reaction/delivery failures into one scoped, read-only recovery view over authoritative records: owner, cause, attempts, status, protected input references, trace id and next action. importance: high blocked-by: P-010\n- **P-014** `todo` Implement operation-specific resume/fork/replay adapters with current authorization, atomic duplicate protection, immutable attempt lineage, lock/revocation checks and completed-effect reconciliation. importance: high blocked-by: P-005, P-006, P-011, P-013\n- **P-015** `todo` Extend existing admin/operation views with failure inspection, trace correlation from the Postgres trace ids and permitted recovery actions; follow component-registry/spec validation before UI implementation. importance: high blocked-by: P-013, P-014\n\n## Phase 4 — Integrated verification and shipment\n\n- **P-016** `todo` Run the frozen integrated population in isolated current-build DBOS runtimes under su/owner and restrictive test profiles: successful work, private/external inference, retries/restarts, duplicate/ambiguous replay, policy refusal/revocation, lock races, secret/content canaries, tenant isolation, deletion propagation, telemetry export loss and measured overhead. Record complete coverage, runtime receipts and owned residue. importance: high blocked-by: P-007, P-008, P-014, P-015\n- **P-017** `todo` Document supported operation classes, policy/retention boundaries, collector configuration/destinations, recovery runbooks, unsupported cases, upgrade/rollback and enterprise evidence handoff; then verify the exact promoted/released artifact and configuration separately from staging/current-build evidence. importance: high blocked-by: P-016\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — One merged authority\n\nThe two draft plans are superseded by this canonical plan. Personal Vault owns privacy, grants, receipts, inference/action policy, encryption, lock/revocation and deletion. Tracing/collector and generic failed-work recovery are integrated as later phases that consume those authorities.\n\n### D-002 — Reuse enterprise and DBOS authorities\n\nReuse enterprise P-005/P-007/P-008/P-016, their data map, SIEM and processing/key contracts, and DBOS workflow/reaction/outbox records. Do not introduce a parallel policy engine, data map, audit ledger, broker, scheduler, message broker or workflow runner.\n\n### D-003 — OpenTelemetry boundary\n\nRecommend OpenTelemetry API/instrumentation plus OTLP and initially qualify the standard Collector. Alloy and the existing-ledger baseline are explicit alternatives. No paid backend is selected; operational traces never replace required security audit evidence.\n\n### D-004 — Safe recovery semantics\n\nDBOS remains execution authority. Interrupted steps may execute again. Every replay must be operation-specific, authorization-checked, idempotency-protected and linked to immutable history; ambiguous completed effects require reconciliation rather than automatic resend.\n\n### D-005 — Data minimization and lifecycle\n\nRaw prompts, retrieved documents, secrets, credentials and complete evaluation evidence are not operational telemetry defaults. Trace, collector, failed-work and replay records are derived data subject to the Vault/enterprise protection, retention, deletion and legal-hold contracts.\n\n### D-006 — Explicit exclusions\n\nRedis and Kafka are deferred entirely [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog answer \"defer entirely\"]; the analysis is report rpt_407b2fdb-db12-4067-9971-121a0e439786. Datadog, NRTM/shared-session feature work, paid telemetry backends and final customer/legal/shipment claims are also outside this plan.\n\n### D-007 — Identity profiles: su keeps full capability on a system that can restrict\nDate: 2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, AskUserQuestion answer, verbatim] \"leave it to you. but mark this as a decidion. I don't want to restrict capability for our su agents. su agents should ahve full capability but built on top of a system that allows for these stricter controls so that we can add more restrictive identities that enterprises will want later\"\n\nRuling: grants, receipts and inference/action checks run for every identity, but what they allow comes from the identity's profile. The su/owner profile adds no new restriction on inference, egress or actions. Restrictive profiles (local-only inference, provider/region allow-lists, no export, step-up) are configurations of the same mechanism for enterprise identities. P-016 exercises them through a restricted test identity now, so the stricter path is proven rather than assumed.\n\nResolved [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog option 'Via a grant', then typed, verbatim: \"#1 but can we make a way to give su agents all grants with no time limit without approval?\"]. su is removed from the hard coding-role fence (papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/personal-vault/coding-roles.ts). This amends charter personal-vault-2026-08-22 D-001 for su only; other coding roles stay fenced. The su profile carries one standing grant: every effect (read, infer:local, infer:external, send, export, admin, replay, plus any effect added later), no expiry and no per-use approval. The owner creates it once, and that act is the approval. It is audited, the owner can revoke it, and vault lock stops it (a design default that can be changed). Content-free receipts and audit still apply.\n\nUnchanged and separate: the reader-set label layer (personal-data-reader-set-labels-2026-10-01). After an su session reads restricted content, its coord writes are sealed, its outbound sends are checked against the reader set, and its file edits are held at git-sync (personal-vault/git-sync-hold.ts) until the disclosure is released. Exempting su from those holds would let vault content reach pushed commits and coord, so it needs its own owner decision. Resolved by D-010 (2026-10-17): vault access and after-read holds become fields of the identity definition, and the su definition turns holds off.\n\n### D-008 — v1 traces in Postgres; collector after a destination is chosen\nDate: 2026-10-17\nBasis: review rpt_b4a297fd-ce3f-4f1f-94c6-f79bc7f8bd41 point 4; Avi chose to revise along that review's lines [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog].\n\nv1 propagates W3C trace context across API, DBOS, agent, tool and model boundaries, reusing DBOS's built-in OpenTelemetry support with no competing global tracer. It records trace and span ids on existing Postgres records (DBOS workflow status, event reaction and delivery rows, tool invocations), and admin views read them there. OTLP export through the standard OpenTelemetry Collector (Grafana Alloy as the alternative) is P-012. P-012 starts only after Avi picks a destination, because choosing a destination is an egress decision under this plan's policy.\n\n### D-009 — Operational telemetry is metadata-only\nDate: 2026-10-17\nBasis: review rpt_b4a297fd-ce3f-4f1f-94c6-f79bc7f8bd41 point 3; Avi chose to revise along that review's lines [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog].\n\nAn in-process allow-list drops every span attribute that is not on the list before anything is recorded or exported. Protected references are opaque ids. Traces, span stores and collector buffers therefore sit outside the per-scope encryption and deletion lineage (R-4, R-7) and follow an ordinary retention limit. Failed-work records hold only protected references to inputs; the referenced data stays in its vault lifecycle. This replaces the source drafts' requirement to encrypt and purge collector buffers: per-scope encryption of a third-party process's queue is impractical, and metadata does not need it.\n\n### D-010 — Vault access and after-read holds are fields of the identity definition\nDate: 2026-10-17\nDate: 2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog answer, verbatim] \"Exempt su entirely\"\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, typed, directive #1955, verbatim] \"the exemption shouldnt be hard coded either it should be part of their identity definition.  Are the permissions/grants in this system configureable per identity?  If not, should they eb?\"\n\nMeasured 2026-10-17 by reading the code (paths under papercusp/packages/operator-core/lib/): personal-vault/coding-roles.ts:15-16 (role-name regex, su included); personal-vault/authorization.ts:55 (that fence runs before the grant lookup); personal-vault/types.ts:1 (grant principal types); capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.ts:2 (identity grants narrow the role envelope); capability-envelope/policy.ts:88 (ROLE_ENVELOPES).\n\nToday three permission layers exist, and only one is per identity:\n- Tool access is per identity. An identity definition (blueprint) declares grants; the tools a session gets are wearer grants ∩ declared needs ∩ pot/role ceiling (capability-envelope/identity-grants-port.ts, blueprint-envelopes.ts). These grants can only narrow. The ceiling is ROLE_ENVELOPES in capability-envelope/policy.ts, plus per-hive blueprint overrides.\n- Vault access is per role, outside the identity definition. A personal_grants row names a principal (agent-role, binding or plan-template) and scopes (personal-vault/authorization.ts). A hard-coded role-name regex (personal-vault/coding-roles.ts, su included) denies 13 roles before any grant is read.\n- After-read holds have no per-identity setting. The reader-set label layer (git-sync hold, coord seal, shared-store seal, outbound send check, native provider-egress binding) applies to every session that reads restricted content. Transcript exclusion (personal-vault/transcript-exclusion.ts) also hides those turns from other agents' transcript reads; it becomes setting (c) below. Release needs an owner-typed release code (personal-vault/release-authority.ts).\n\nRuling: the identity definition gains a vault section, read at the same kernel seat as tool grants. It holds (a) which vault effects the identity's standing grant covers, with its expiry and approval terms, and (b) whether after-read holds apply to its commits, coord writes, writes to shared work stores (work-item comments and checkpoints, facts, memory: personal-vault/shared-store-seal.ts) and outbound sends, including native mail/chat provider routes (personal-vault/provider-egress.mjs); (c) whether other agents' transcript reads show its vault-reading turns (personal-vault/transcript-exclusion.ts); and (d) whether granted vault content is recalled into its turns automatically (personal-vault/ambient.ts). The coding-role fence becomes the default value in the coding-role identity definitions; the regex is deleted, not kept as a second source. The su definition sets all effects, no expiry, no per-use approval, holds off, transcripts open and automatic recall on [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog, verbatim: \"Open, recall on\"]. Enterprise identities set restrictive values in the same fields. personal_grants stays the record of who granted what: an identity's standing grant is a row there that the owner creates, not a separate store.\n\nAccepted consequence [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog, chosen over 'Keep holds' and 'su releases its own']: vault content an su session reads can reach commits pushed to GitHub and coord messages other agents read. Content-free receipts and audit still apply, and vault lock still stops su's grant.\n\nGuard [owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog, confirmed: \"Yes, needs my approval (Recommended)\"]: tool grants can only narrow, but these vault fields widen access. Widening them must therefore take the owner's own action, using the same owner-typed proof release-authority.ts requires. An agent edit alone (for example blueprint:extend) cannot widen vault fields. Otherwise vault content an agent read could tell it to edit its own identity and lift its holds.\n\nSupersedes D-007's open paragraph on reader-set holds, and replaces D-007's 'remove su from the regex' mechanism with the identity-definition default.\n\n### D-011 — D-010 is superseded: vault settings move to per-install stack settings\nDate: 2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, dialog answer, verbatim] \"Approve rev 3 (Recommended)\" (identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17 revision 3)\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-17, typed, directive #1959] identities are distributed on the Cupboard; each organization configures them, including Personal Vault (no email vault, restricted access, granted access).\n\nD-010 placed vault access and after-read holds in the identity definition. That is superseded by identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17#D-006 and #D-009: a published identity only declares an optional vault ask, and the vault owner's stack settings for each installed named stack decide all four D-010 settings: (a) which effects the standing grant covers, with expiry and approval terms; (b) after-read holds on commits, coord writes, shared work stores and outbound sends, including native provider routes; (c) transcript visibility of vault-reading turns; (d) automatic recall. Avi's values for su are unchanged and become his settings for su: all effects, no expiry, no per-use approval, holds off, transcripts open, recall on. The role-name fence is still deleted; a stack with no vault grant gets no access, which keeps today's denial for the fenced coding roles. D-010's guard (widening needs the owner's typed approval) stands, now as identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17 R-11. D-010 was never built, so no code changes here; implementation is identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17#P-015.\n\n## Activation prerequisites\n\nThis draft is not active. Before activation, re-read the complete owner conversation and source plans, record the activation audit mapping every original requirement and item, verify the product walkthrough, confirm retention choices, confirm the execution route, and preserve the enterprise plan's independent acceptance/shipment obligations. No implementation workers should start until the owner approves the merged plan and route. The export destination is chosen at the start of P-012, not before activation.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-bug-inflow-one-problem-one-row-2026-10-18","title":"Acceptance BAR — Cut bug inflow: one problem = one row (counted repeats, duplicate-of field checked by the admission gate)","status":"active","created":"2026-10-18","owner":"su-fa17f2e8-ff04-4241-ac73-07d6866f0e2c","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Cut bug inflow: one problem = one row (counted repeats, duplicate-of field checked by the admission gate)\nslug: acceptance-bug-inflow-one-problem-one-row-2026-10-18\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-18\nupdated: 2026-10-20\nowner: su-fa17f2e8-ff04-4241-ac73-07d6866f0e2c\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Cut bug inflow: one problem = one row (counted repeats, duplicate-of field checked by the admission gate)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context.
