Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"bug-inflow-one-problem-one-row-2026-10-18","title":"Cut bug inflow: one problem = one row (counted repeats, duplicate-of field checked by the admission gate)","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-18","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Cut bug inflow: one problem = one row (counted repeats, duplicate-of field checked by the admission gate)\nslug: bug-inflow-one-problem-one-row-2026-10-18\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-18\nupdated: 2026-10-20\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Audience:** Avi (owner) and the bug-drain fleet leader/members.\n- **Problem:** The backlog stays ~4,000+ because filing outruns closing. About half of inflow is watchdog-filed agent tool errors. Brief glitches and agent misuse get filed as bugs, one defect splits into many rows (the key includes the error-message fingerprint), and duplicate screening runs after filing and fails open.\n- **Outcome:** One problem = one row. Repeats increment a counter on that row, and a recurrence reopens it instead of filing again. Duplicates are a typed FIELD set at filing time, and the existing admission (duplicate) gate refuses to admit/claim a row whose field points at a live canonical item. The brief shows inflow by source next to closes per day.\n- **Non-goals:** Taking over the red release gate (owned elsewhere). Merit triage of bugs. Changing observation-lane notes.\n- **Source turns:** owner directives #1985, #1987, #1989, #1990 (2026-10-18 UTC, this session). #1990: \"why not make this a field. thats stronger than a comment? We also have a gate to catch duplicates right? the gate should check this field. The rest looks good. Fold this all into the plan and then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped status\".\n- **Scenarios:** (1) A tool times out 40 times in an hour → no bugs; at sustained outage rate → exactly one per tool. (2) An agent sends a bad argument 30 times → one usability item for that tool+field, count 30. (3) The same structural error with different ids in the message → one row, repeatCount rises. (4) An agent files a bug matching an open one → the new row gets duplicate_of=<canonical>, the gate keeps it out of the queue, and the canonical row's occurrence count rises. (5) The leader reads the brief → sees filed/day by source vs closed/day.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Transient errors are counted, not filed.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A transient tool error creates no bug unless one tool stays above a sustained transient-rate threshold, then one row per tool.\",\"rationale\":\"Owner-approved bug-inflow fix (#1989/#1990).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:a79f1614-5049-45e2-9ba8-5912f2fd070a:21\",\"session_turn:claude:a79f1614-5049-45e2-9ba8-5912f2fd070a:22\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Per tool and window, transient-class tool errors yield one watchdog signal when the tool is at or above all three sustained-rate thresholds (at least 15 transient failures, a transient share of at least 0.20 of its calls, and at least 3 active hours of the window) and none otherwise.\",\"falsifier\":\"A tool short of any one of the three sustained-rate thresholds yields any transient signal, or a tool at or above all three yields zero or more than one signal in one window.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tool-error-watchdog\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts at the pinned revision. The sustained-rate threshold is the invocation watchdog's transient bar: at least 15 transient failures for the tool, a transient share of at least 0.2 of its calls, spread over at least 3 active hours of the window. The R-1 describe's three 'boundary at the default' cases call the watchdog with no threshold options, so they judge the shipped defaults, each with the other two dimensions comfortably met: 15 failures file and 14 do not; a 0.20 share files and 0.19 does not; 3 distinct active hours file and 2 do not. A tool at or above all three thresholds yields exactly one signal per window, keyed by the tool; the watchdog skips a tool when any one is short (watchdog.ts: r.n < transientMin || rate < transientMinRate || active_hours < transientMinHours). Pass-after at clean sha e59a838a7e: test_runs:21443293. Fail-before: copy-out mutants moving each default one step down (to 14, to 0.19, to 2 hours) are each caught by those cases: test_runs:21443304, 21443311, 21443315.\\n\\nWindow. Every R-1 threshold is judged over the invocation watchdog's tool-error window, 24 hours by default. A tool's active hours are the distinct clock hours inside that window that hold at least one transient failure of that tool. At the defaults a tool files only when all three hold in one window: at least 15 transient failures, at least 0.20 of the tool's calls, and at least 3 active hours. The check binds the five cases of the R-1 describe (check.cases); the file's other describes serve R-2 and R-3.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\"],\"cases\":[{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"R-1: transient failures are counted, not filed, unless sustained > below the sustained-rate bar: zero signals, however many wordings\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"R-1: transient failures are counted, not filed, unless sustained > above the bar: exactly ONE signal keyed by the tool, from many distinct wordings\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"R-1: transient failures are counted, not filed, unless sustained > count boundary at the default: 15 failures file, 14 do not\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"R-1: transient failures are counted, not filed, unless sustained > share boundary at the default: 0.20 of the calls files, 0.19 does not\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"R-1: transient failures are counted, not filed, unless sustained > hours boundary at the default: 3 distinct hours file, 2 do not\"}]},\"replication\":\"Repeat against the same pinned source revision and retain pass/fail/unknown evidence.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Misuse folds into one usability item.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Caller-class errors become one usability item per tool, naming the arguments agents get wrong with a per-argument occurrence counter (D-010).\",\"rationale\":\"Owner-approved bug-inflow fix (#1989/#1990).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:a79f1614-5049-45e2-9ba8-5912f2fd070a:21\",\"session_turn:claude:a79f1614-5049-45e2-9ba8-5912f2fd070a:22\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Caller-class errors on one tool produce exactly one change-kind signal, keyed by the tool alone whatever their field paths, ids or message text, whose per-argument occurrence counter holds one entry per argument agents get wrong (ids, indices and values under one field path are one entry, a different field path is a separate entry), each entry equal to that argument's caller failures in the window, the entries summing to the signal's caller-failure total and listed most-wrong first.\",\"falsifier\":\"Two caller errors on one tool yield more than one signal key, or the key contains a field path, error code, id or message text; or the item carries no per-argument counter; or an entry's count differs from the caller failures on that argument; or the entries do not sum to the caller-failure total; or two values or indices under one field path count as separate entries, or two different field paths share one entry; or the item does not list the arguments most-wrong first with their counts.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tool-error-watchdog\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts at the pinned revision and inspect its caller-class assertions: errors on one tool that differ in field path, id or message text derive one change-kind key that names only the tool. Receipts at clean committed sha efadf734a9 (worktree_dirty=false): pass-after test_runs:21445668; fail-before, a copy-out mutant that drops the caller class from the tool-keyed classes, so caller failures key by error code and field path again, is caught, test_runs:21445934 (fails 'R-2 (D-010): caller failures are ONE usability item per tool, with a per-argument counter'). The check binds the two cases of the R-2 describe (check.cases). Counter: the case 'different values / indices under the same field share one item and one counter entry' files 12 caller failures under items.N.status with 12 different indices and values and asserts one item whose counter is { total: 12, counts: { 'items.n.status': 12 } }; the case 'a different field is NOT a different item: the one item counts each argument agents get wrong' files 10 failures on request_key and 4 on summary and asserts { total: 14, counts: { request_key: 10, summary: 4 } } and the body line 'Arguments agents get wrong (failures in the window): request_key ×10, summary ×4.'. Counter receipts at clean committed sha 9a951b017d (worktree_dirty=false): pass-after test_runs:21449672. Fail-before, two copy-out mutants of watchdog.ts, each caught: one corrupts the counter (addFieldCount stores 1 per argument instead of adding each failure), test_runs:21449714 (fails 'R-2 (D-010): caller failures are ONE usability item per tool, with a per-argument counter > different values / indices under the same field share one item and one counter entry' and 'R-2 (D-010): caller failures are ONE usability item per tool, with a per-argument counter > a different field is NOT a different item: the one item counts each argument agents get wrong'); one drops it (the caller signal no longer carries the callerArguments counter), test_runs:21449780 (fails 'R-2 (D-010): caller failures are ONE usability item per tool, with a per-argument counter > different values / indices under the same field share one item and one counter entry' and 'R-2 (D-010): caller failures are ONE usability item per tool, with a per-argument counter > a different field is NOT a different item: the one item counts each argument agents get wrong').\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\"],\"cases\":[{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"R-2 (D-010): caller failures are ONE usability item per tool, with a per-argument counter > different values / indices under the same field share one item and one counter entry\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"R-2 (D-010): caller failures are ONE usability item per tool, with a per-argument counter > a different field is NOT a different item: the one item counts each argument agents get wrong\"}]},\"replication\":\"Repeat against the same pinned source revision and retain pass/fail/unknown evidence.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Structural errors key without message text.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Structural key is tool + error code + field path; repeats count; closed recurrence reopens; one new row per tool per day.\",\"rationale\":\"Owner-approved bug-inflow fix (#1989/#1990).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:a79f1614-5049-45e2-9ba8-5912f2fd070a:21\",\"session_turn:claude:a79f1614-5049-45e2-9ba8-5912f2fd070a:22\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Structural errors whose messages differ only in ids, paths or values map to one signal key, and under the default per-tool daily cap a tool mints at most one new row per UTC day, deferring the rest.\",\"falsifier\":\"Two such errors yield different keys, or the key still embeds a message fingerprint, or two structural errors on one tool with different error codes or field paths map to one key; or, under the default cap, a tool mints more than one new row in one UTC day, or a capped signal is discarded rather than deferred.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tool-error-watchdog\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-inflow.test.ts at the pinned revision. Structural errors whose messages differ only in ids, paths or values must derive one key; and, the other side, two structural errors on one tool with a different error code or a different field path must derive different keys. The same file bars the per-tool daily cap: with the default cap of 1 (the tick case passes no cap), a tool mints at most one new row per UTC day, highest severity first, counting rows it already minted that day; a further signal that day is deferred to a later tick, not dropped. Receipts at clean committed sha efadf734a9 (worktree_dirty=false): pass-after test_runs:21445668. TOOL_KEYED_TOOL_ERROR_CLASSES gains caller, so collector, agent capture and key migration all give `<tool>:caller`; the caller signal names the most-wrong arguments with counts and the payload carries callerArguments; D-004/D-005 tests move to the new key; open `<tool>:caller:<code>:<field>` rows re-key through the existing migration + fold. + vitest. — R-2, R-3, R-9 — note: ← WI-6554700010018129 completed (done)\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — D-001 duplicate_of is a typed work_items column that the admission predicate reads\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-18 #1990] asked for a FIELD, not a comment, checked by the existing duplicate gate.\n\nShape: harness_shared.work_items gains duplicate_of text NULL (feature_id of the canonical row, same workspace_id) and duplicate_source text NULL (one of: create-exact, admission-promoter, fold, agent). Match evidence stays where it already lives (payload.dedupCandidates, coord_links rel 'duplicates'); the column is the single authoritative verdict.\n\nWriters: (1) work_items:create sets it only on a STRONG match: an exact watchdog/signature key match or an agent-declared links[{rel:'duplicates'}] target that is open. Cosine similarity alone does NOT set it (silent-intake-central-resolution-2026-09-01#D-001: cosine cannot separate duplicates from distinct filings in this corpus). (2) The admission promoter's existing merge (persistAdmissionDuplicateLink) also writes the column. (3) The P-008 backlog fold writes it on folded rows.\n\nReaders: the admission predicate in work-items-admission.ts (the single source of is-this-claimable) treats a row whose duplicate_of names a non-terminal item as not admitted, so claimable reads, claim floors and the fail-open promoter all inherit it. A canonical that later closes releases nothing automatically: the duplicate is dropped at write time (status dropped) except when the writer cannot verify the canonical, in which case it stays pending.\n\nReuse: extends the existing admission column/predicate and the promoter's merge path; no parallel dedup system.\n\n### D-002 — As-built amendments to D-001: create-time writer uses the calibrated hard band; any duplicate_of blocks claim; verdict withdrawn by unlink\nDate: 2026-10-18\nSupersedes three details of D-001 to match what P-005/P-006 shipped (migration 1534, _create-core.ts stampCreateTimeDuplicate, work-items.ts stampDuplicateVerdictFromLink, work-items-admission.ts admittedWhereSql). [self-imposed design, recorded for review; owner ask is #1990: \"make this a field ... the gate should check this field\"]\n\n1. Create-time writer (owner proposal: \"the filing call would search open bugs first and attach a strong match\"). The strong match is the existing semantic-dupe-guard HARD band: cosine >= 0.93, or the co-signal cosine >= 0.86 AND pg_trgm title similarity >= 0.45. That band was the former refusal band; its calibration block (WI-38056) records that the co-signal fires on none of the four measured flagged-but-distinct pairs. The SOFT band never sets the field. D-001 said cosine alone does not set it; the as-built rule is narrower than \"cosine alone\": only the precision-calibrated hard band, never the advisory band. Skipped when the filer passes force (asserts distinct work) or severity is critical. Source enum value is create-match (was create-exact in D-001; exact-identity creates are already refused before a row exists, so they need no stamp). duplicate_confidence = the match similarity, duplicate_evidence = {matchedOn, similarity, candidates}.\n\n2. Gate: ANY non-null duplicate_of makes a row not admitted (admittedWhereSql: admission IS DISTINCT FROM pending AND duplicate_of IS NULL; isAdmitted twin). Simpler than \"names a non-terminal item\" and needs no join. A canonical that closes does not release its duplicates.\n\n3. Reversibility instead of drop: D-001 said duplicates are dropped at write time. As built, the row keeps its status and is only made unclaimable. The verdict rides a coord_links rel duplicates edge; unlinking that edge clears the verdict that names its target (unlinkWorkItem). A false match therefore costs a hidden row that one unlink restores, not a lost filing.\n\nWriters today: create-match (create), admission-promoter (persistAdmissionDuplicateLink), agent (work_items:link rel duplicates, inline create links, complete-as-duplicate; first writer wins), fold (P-008).\n\n### D-003 — Watchdog tool-error rows key on toolFailureSignatureKey (no message fingerprint)\nDate: 2026-10-18\nFrom the P-001 survey (WI-6554700010017181 comment 1190706). [self-imposed design; P-002..P-004, P-008 implement it]\n\nToday one tool defect can be filed twice: the invocation-friction watchdog keys repeated-tool-error rows as <tool>:<class>[:md5 message-skeleton fingerprint] (tool-error-classifier.ts toolErrorSignalKey), so wording changes split one problem into many rows (the R-3 defect); agent-reported captures key the same defect as tool-failure-signature:<tool>:<family>:<errorCode>:<fieldPath>[:identity-<cause>] (toolFailureSignatureKey, review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23#D-010).\n\nDecision (reuse-first): the watchdog collector derives errorCode from tool_invocations.error_code and fieldPath from error_message (zod \"<path>: ...\" with numeric segments normalized to [], or Unrecognized key \"x\"), and keys STRUCTURAL and CALLER signals with toolFailureSignatureKey, so a watchdog repeat and an agent report land on ONE row. TRANSIENT signals key by tool alone (R-1). The fieldPath derivation exists in TS and as a SQL mirror (the collector groups in SQL), parity-tested like toolErrorFingerprint. Repeats increment the row counter; a recurrence after close reopens; a per-tool daily cap bounds new rows. watchdog-key-migration re-keys open rows (P-004) and the P-008 fold merges rows that collapse onto one key.\n\n### D-004 — As-built shape of the structural tool-error key, transient bar and daily cap (P-002..P-004)\nDate: 2026-10-18\nDate: 2026-10-18. [self-imposed design, recorded for review; implements D-003 for owner directive #1990]. Source: packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/tool-error-classifier.ts (toolErrorKeyParts / toolErrorKeyPartsSql / toolErrorSignalKey), watchdog.ts (collect + capToolErrorMintsPerTool), structural-error-verifier.ts, watchdog-key-migration.ts, apps/operator/scripts/recompute-watchdog-keys.ts.\n\n1. Key shape. repeated-tool-error rows key as <tool>:<class>:<errorCode>:<fieldPath> for structural and caller classes, and as <tool>:<class> for the TOOL-keyed classes transient and rate-limit (TOOL_KEYED_TOOL_ERROR_CLASSES). No message fingerprint segment. Missing parts render as error-code-unknown / field-unknown, so the key always has the same arity.\n\n2. errorCode precedence. (a) the tool_invocations.error_code column when it is not generic; else (b) a JSON envelope field \"reason\"|\"error\"|\"code\" holding a snake_case code; else (c) a leading snake_case `code:` prefix after stripping handler_error:/invalid_input: wrappers; else the column as-is. GENERIC_TOOL_ERROR_CODES = handler_error, invalid_input, error, internal_error. invalid_input is generic on purpose: it is the dispatch envelope (about 4.4k rows/day), and the inner invalid_args code in the message is the real cause. That way an agent report and a ledger row agree on one key.\n\n3. fieldPath. First match of: zod `Unrecognized key(s): \"x\"`, the zod path after `invalid_args:`, or the Postgres error `column \"x\" [of relation \"y\"] does not exist` (TOOL_ERROR_PG_COLUMN_PATTERN). The PG rule keeps distinct missing columns on distinct keys, e.g. the EI-22437036851108668 half-repair siblings. Numeric path segments are normalized to `.n` (array indexes never split a key).\n\n4. One parser, two runtimes. toolErrorKeyPartsSql is the SQL mirror of toolErrorKeyParts and builds on the same pattern constants. tool-error-classifier.integration.test.ts asserts the two parsers return the same result for a corpus plus edge cases on real PG.\n\n5. Verifier. structural-error-verifier re-checks a current key by code_key/field_key. A row still on a LEGACY fingerprint key is verified by its fingerprint until the key migration re-keys it.\n\n6. Transient bar (R-1). A transient row is filed only when, over the window, n >= 15 failures AND failure rate >= 0.2 AND the failures span >= 3 distinct active hours (CollectOptions transientMinCount / transientMinRate / transientMinActiveHours). Below that bar a transient error is counted, not filed. Caller errors (R-2) need >= 10 (callerMinCount) and key on tool+code+field.\n\n7. Daily cap (R-3). capToolErrorMintsPerTool admits at most 1 NEW repeated-tool-error row per tool per 24h; repeats of an open row count onto that row and are not capped. Capped signals are DEFERRED, not dropped (they surface again on the next tick and the next day's budget). The cap fails OPEN if its PG read fails.\n\n8. Key migration. recompute-watchdog-keys.ts looks up error_code per legacy row in tool_invocations (same tool, left(error_message,800) = sample, 30d) and passes it to the key builder. Several legacy rows that fold onto one new key are REPORTED as collisions, not merged. Folding them is P-007's job.\n\n### D-005 — D-005 capture-core tests move to the D-004 key contract; the review-system-rework-reduction D-010 missing-dimension message key is retired\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20. [self-imposed design, recorded for review; implements owner directive #1990 via D-003/D-004]\n\nFinding: after the tool-error key refactor landed (commit 2fae02c616), five tests in packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/capture-core.test.ts failed on a clean clone at 376951c831. They pinned the older rule from review-system-rework-reduction D-010: when any class dimension is missing, key on the exact message, so differently-worded reports stay on separate rows. That rule is the R-3 defect this plan removes (wording splits one problem into many rows).\n\nRuling: the tests now assert the D-004 contract.\n1. Wording alone never splits a key. Reports with the same tool + class + errorCode + fieldPath share one row and are counted onto it.\n2. Real dimensions still split. A different errorCode, or a different field parsed from the message, keys a different row. Each rewritten test carries a separation case so the guard against over-merging stays falsifiable. The field comes from the measured message, never from the reporter's own fieldPath (normalizeSuspectedToolFailure).\n3. Transient and rate-limit failures are tool-keyed (R-1). Example: a timed-out capability:bash report is counted onto the standing capability:bash transient row.\n4. EI-25714783883986261 (two lock-acquire HTTP 502 incidents merged; the newer one was not on record): those incidents are the same transient problem, so they are now counted on one row by design. The coalesce refreshes title, body and lastSeenAt, so the newest incident stays on record.\n5. Legacy reconciliation keeps its guard: a legacy row is never reconciled into a DIFFERENT exact report. The test now builds that difference from a real code (`not_found:` prefix), not from wording.\n\nResidual risk, accepted: two genuinely different structural defects of one tool that share an errorCode and have no parseable field now share one counted row. Recovery comes from two places: the coalesce refresh keeps the newest sample on the row, and a closed row reopens on recurrence (P-004 REOPEN). Observed but not fixed here: on a probation row, a repeat by an earlier reporter after a second reporter is recorded in the occurrence ledger (3 occurrences) but does not bump payload.repeatCount. The test asserts occurrences and reporters, not repeatCount.\n\nResult: capture-core.test.ts 246 passed / 0 failed on the shared tree, 2026-10-20 ~04:10Z.\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: amend-8ac9d1e5276ae5cdb69c52de\nRequest-Hash: 31a72453347792ca9501c1c037487cac9116e96919fcea07402faf3bbf342d3e\nActor: su-fa17f2e8-ff04-4241-ac73-07d6866f0e2c\nReason: As-built correction: R-6's BAR names packages/operator-core/lib/bug-inflow-cell.test.ts, which was never created; the P-007 inflow cell and its unit test landed as packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/bug-inflow.ts + bug-inflow.test.ts. Each fix still needs a regression test in top-tool-error-fixes.test.ts that fails on the pre-fix code.\n\n### D-009 — R-9 is measured as a same-input replay on the plan's inflow population; keying alone gives 0.708, so R-9 is NOT yet met\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20. [self-imposed measurement design + finding, recorded for review; implements R-9/P-010 for owner directive #1990]\n\nFinding 1 (live drop not attributable, measured 07:25Z, WI-6554700010017611): repeated-tool-error rows filed per day fell from a 7d mean of 1358.4 (2026-10-11..17, all lanes) to 204 on 10-19. Tracked as a follow-up; P-010 stays open until then.\n\n### D-010 — Caller-class tool errors key once per TOOL (approved proposal item 2); D-004 item 6's tool+code+field caller key is a deviation to correct\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20. [self-imposed correction toward the owner-approved proposal; owner approval = directive #1990 'The rest looks good', referring to proposal session a79f1614 turn 21]\n\nThe approved proposal (session a79f1614-5049-45e2-9ba8-5912f2fd070a turn 21, item 2) says: 'Turn misuse into one ease-of-use item per tool, saying which argument agents keep getting wrong, with a counter.' D-004 item 6 instead keys caller errors on tool+code+field, and capture-core uses the same key (D-005). That multiplies caller rows: caller is 58% of the distinct new keys in the 7-day pre-change replay (D-009).\n\nRuling: the caller class joins transient and rate-limit as TOOL-keyed (repeated-tool-error:<tool>:caller). The errorCode/fieldPath of each occurrence goes into the row's payload as a per-argument counter (which argument agents get wrong) rather than into the key. Author: su-fa17f2e8 [self]. Prompted by rev-15 bar critique #1 (su-1c07249a, post 1191669), which asked R-7's operational falsifier to name the open, unclaimed population and to pin its census the way D-013 pins R-8's.\n\nPopulation. harness_shared.work_items rows with workspace_id = 'papercusp-workspace', payload->>'watchdogKey' LIKE 'repeated-tool-error:%', and status NOT IN ('done','dropped','resolved','closed'), all lanes. Claimed means taken_by IS NOT NULL. Rows are grouped by (workspace_id, payload->>'watchdogKey').\n\nViolation. A key violates R-7 when its group holds at least 2 rows and at least one of them is unclaimed. Reason: R-7's canonical rule puts a claimed row before an unclaimed one, so in any multi-row group an unclaimed row is never the canonical row and should have been dropped. A group of only claimed rows is not a violation, because the fold deliberately keeps a claimed loser.\n\nInstrument. dev:pg_query (read-only transaction) against the operator database. The SQL, verbatim:\nWITH r AS (SELECT workspace_id, payload->>'watchdogKey' AS k, taken_by IS NOT NULL AS claimed, lane FROM harness_shared.work_items WHERE workspace_id = 'papercusp-workspace' AND payload->>'watchdogKey' LIKE 'repeated-tool-error:%' AND status NOT IN ('done','dropped','resolved','closed')), g AS (SELECT workspace_id, k, count(*) AS n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT claimed) AS unclaimed FROM r GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT now() AS measured_at, (SELECT count(*) FROM r) AS rows, (SELECT count(*) FROM r WHERE claimed) AS claimed_rows, count(*) AS keys, count(*) FILTER (WHERE n >= 2) AS keys_multi_row, count(*) FILTER (WHERE n >= 2 AND unclaimed >= 1) AS keys_violating FROM g\n\nReadings. The live fold apply ran at about 10:48Z (216 rows re-keyed, 1,307 folded onto 118 keys, 102 skipped, 1 link stamped). A first census at 11:14:23Z read 2669 non-terminal rows and 0 keys holding more than one row (work-item comment 1191612). The census above, re-run at 2026-10-20 12:37:35Z, read rows 2650, claimed_rows 109, keys 2650, keys_multi_row 0, keys_violating 0. The non-zero row count is the positive control: the predicate matches the live population.\n\nUse. R-7's operational evidence slot cites this decision. Re-running the SQL at any later time gives a fresh reading; R-7 passes operationally when keys_violating is 0.\n\n### D-026 — R-8 mutant receipts are attributed by the describe each one fails (corrects D-023's rank 4/5 receipt list)\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20. TOOL_KEYED_TOOL_ERROR_CLASSES gains caller, so collect… <!-- P-011 -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"detached-hook-home-resolution-2026-10-18","title":"Make installed hooks resolve host paths without workspace packages","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-18","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Make installed hooks resolve host paths without workspace packages\nslug: detached-hook-home-resolution-2026-10-18\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-18\nupdated: 2026-10-21\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: Papercusp users running Claude or Codex hooks installed outside the repository.\nProblem: five hooks import a workspace-only package, causing ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before their handlers run.\nOutcome: hooks load and retain their safety/provenance behavior from their installed directory.\nNon-goals: changing guard policy, gate operations, framework or runtime upgrades.\nSource turns: owner reported plans:new hook crash; clarified it happened in Claude; requested durable fix yourself now on auto mode.\nScenario: a plan write invokes the detached guard; valid writes pass silently, phantom artifact claims are denied, and verified artifact claims pass.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation complete and installed, P-001 done. Shared pc_home.mjs packages exact canonical host-platform home.mjs bytes for five affected hooks; installer registry and declarations updated. Eight focused files passed (132 tests, one optional global live parity probe skipped), declarations checked, installed payloads match and guard deny/harvest/allow smoke passes. Normal source commit is pending an already-running system git-sync; attempted expedite correctly skipped held_exclusive. No release shipment claim.\n\n**Next:** No further implementation action. Evidence and code review references are recorded on WI-6554700010017209; the normal shared git-sync owns source persistence.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Detached loading.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Implement the durable fix for the installed Claude hook package-resolution failure.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The five affected hooks and their dependent launch-prose nudge load from a copied installation without workspace node_modules.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A copied hook import exits nonzero or stderr reports an unresolved package; removing the relative helper does not fail the negative control.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run installed-hooks-parity.test.ts and inspect the detached-install test: it copies hook payloads outside the repo, clears NODE_OPTIONS, imports the affected hooks, and then requires ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND after removing pc_home.mjs. Read the installer registry to confirm pc_home.mjs is shipped.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/installed-hooks-parity.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Shared semantics.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Make the hook fix durable while preserving the existing host-platform home behavior.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The installed helper has exactly the canonical host-platform/home source bytes, and the artifact ledger respects PAPERCUSP_HOME.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The helper differs from canonical home.mjs or the ledger path escapes the explicit PAPERCUSP_HOME.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run installed-hooks-parity.test.ts for canonical helper equality and artifact-url-delivery-guard.test.ts for environment-scoped ledger selection; compare the actual installed pc_home.mjs with the committed helper.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/installed-hooks-parity.test.ts\",\n        \"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/artifact-url-delivery-guard.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Preserved protection.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Fix the installed guard dependency failure without weakening its artifact verification policy.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"The detached guard denies an unverified artifact URL in a plan write, records a successful Artifact response in its scoped ledger, and then allows the verified URL.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"The detached CLI permits the unverified URL, fails to record verification, or continues denying after successful ledger harvest.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run artifact-url-delivery-guard.test.ts and inspect the real CLI deny/harvest/allow test; it must assert the denial JSON, scoped ledger contents, and silent allowance after verification.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/__tests__/artifact-url-delivery-guard.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\nShip a byte-identical standalone copy of libs/host-platform/src/home.mjs alongside hooks as pc_home.mjs; enforce canonical equality in the existing installation test. Extend CC_HOOK_FILES so desktop and standalone installers carry the helper. Replace all five bare imports with relative imports, reuse the existing package implementation, and keep each original handler policy.\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Fix and verify\n- **P-001** `done` Implement the shared helper packaging fix, run affected hook and installer tests, reinstall and verify installed behavior. Execution owner and completion evidence: WI-6554700010017209. importance: high\n\n## Decisions\nOwner authorized direct self implementation on AUTO; no additional implementation agents.\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: acceptance-detached-hook-home-resolution-rev2-apply-1191659\nRequest-Hash: d9602b98a2fc2c2be59f9159d4e06463f7c0c5e5a8476d286c410908d41fda6e\nActor: su-189aed58-a6c6-430a-93c3-7f1c99c48bf7\nReason: Apply the reviewer-approved R-3 repair: scope the atomic ledger-membership rule to durable writes citing artifact URLs, preserving explicit PAPERCUSP_HOME in model, falsifier, and method; retain accepted R-1 and R-2 changes.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-77201d97-fe81-4c18-8db0-d98ed7403d48\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1191659\nApproved-At: 2026-10-20T12:09:27.525Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 5 → 6\nChanged BARs: R-2, R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: acceptance-detached-hook-home-resolution-r3-single-relation-apply-2026-10-21\nRequest-Hash: dd0051dacafa72f731ed1ba7f3cc4fcde5368a0a8fd48fb02d3e052906f02d10\nActor: su-189aed58-a6c6-430a-93c3-7f1c99c48bf7\nReason: Retain R-2's explicit installed-copy drift clause and executable gated parity proof while tightening R-3 to one observable ledger-membership relation; preserve the deny, scoped harvest, and post-harvest allow falsifier sequence.\nApproved-By: su-a427a292-f2c8-4f02-83c4-533d2531ecb2\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1192727\nApproved-At: 2026-10-21T04:53:11.743Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 6 → 7\nChanged BARs: R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18","title":"Move every agent behavior surface onto the identity system (incl. the self-learning system)","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-18","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Move every agent behavior surface onto the identity system (incl. the self-learning system)\nslug: identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-18\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-21, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet. Next repair: Accept the mapped clause: plans:get-specs, then plans:set-specs with lifecycleStatus:\"active\", expectedRevision set to its current revision, and every other field unchanged (keep the sourceBar pin and acceptanceRef; omitting either rides the prior value forward). That provenance-only promotion carries the bound proof and work-item contracts forward: confirm the result reports evidenceCarriedForward > 0 on a clause that had proof. If it is absent, another field changed and the proof must be re-bound at the new revision. Do NOT re-prove or amend the rubric on this code: the proof is not stale, the clause was never accepted. (R-17). (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\n7 of 18 items done. Every remaining item is gated on identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17 (IDOP) per #D-017: the Gym items wait on IDOP's loosening guard, product agents on IDOP's layer grants, and the six layer-authoring items on IDOP's identity format. IDOP has been stalled pre-activation since 2026-10-18T08:00Z.\n\n**Next:** su-7a61b3ed proposed carrying IDOP from its rubric-review step (coord-send-01b7a9a9, default at 2026-10-21T16:00Z unless su-c0dfd243 or su-3b04ef5e objects). The gated items resume as the IDOP items they wait on land.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi (the owner), and every agent the platform launches. Secondary: pot authors who install or extend identities.\n\n**Problem.** Identities can only be worn by su launches (`agent-identities/wearer-authority.ts`: *\"Every identity-bearing launch record is an SU launch record\"*), and they cover only part of the su prompt. Everything below sits outside the identity system, in flat files, TypeScript constants and global hooks:\n- the judge role (7,774 launches in 30 days);\n- about 55 harness role prompts in `harness/blueprints/base/prompts/`;\n- the product agents;\n- the chat personas;\n- about 16 engineering nudge hooks;\n- the domain-specific kernel splices (WORKSPACE-MAP, PROMOTION-MODEL, SHARED-BASE-NOTES);\n- the self-learning system: the Gym edits flat role markdown only, the turn-end observation practice is duplicated, Scout lenses are hard-coded, and memory recall has fixed global budgets.\n\nThe effects: domain text leaks into the neutral kernel, non-coding agents get coding nudges, the optimizer cannot reach the behavior that matters, and splices fail silently (the shared-base notes reached 6 of 5,211 renders).\n\n**Outcome.** Every prompt text that shapes behavior, and every per-agent configuration, is an identity document: versioned, previewable, slot-validated and omission-marked. Every agent role can wear an identity stack, and the self-learning system reads and writes identity revisions.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- Moving authority or safety enforcement out of host code.\n- Turning engines (memory retrieval, the Gym loop, the Scout scheduler) into identities. They are configured by identities and target them.\n- Changing what any role does, except where a requirement says so.\n- Outward publishing.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner-typed, session su-7a61b3ed, 2026-10-17/18:\n- #1976: the audit request.\n- #1980: *\"make sure you also check our self learning system?\"*\n- #1982: *\"why not move them all to the identity system, including the self-learning ones, is there a good reason they shouldn't be built around it?\"*\n- #1983: *\"Okay write a plan for moving them all to our identity system then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped statys\"*\n\n**Scenarios.**\n- **S1.** A CRM agent's prompt is composed from a CRM domain identity plus shared practices. It gets no Papercusp engineering nudges and no gate-repair memories.\n- **S2.** An acceptance-grading judge wears the judge domain plus the acceptance-grading practice. The brief carries only the subject.\n- **S3.** A Gym change to the observation practice is a new identity revision, canaried and rolled back automatically on regression. The Gym can never edit the judge identity that grades its proposals.\n- **S4.** A non-coding pot's su session renders without Papercusp's workspace map, promotion model or deploy pipeline text.\n- **S5.** Scout lenses are identity documents rendered into single model calls. A new lens is an installed identity, not a code change.\n- **S6.** A removed, broken or malicious identity package cannot remove or weaken a safety guard.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Non-su wearers.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Non-su launches can wear identity stacks without gaining authority.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A judge launch record that carries an identity stack renders that stack's layers and is granted no more than its host-computed role and pot ceiling.\",\"falsifier\":\"A non-su launch record with an identity stack is refused by wearer authority, renders without the worn layers, or is granted authority beyond its role and pot ceiling.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the wearer-authority integration test; preview a judge launch with a worn stack and compare the rendered layers and tool grant against the role ceiling.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-identities/generic-identity-launch-authority.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Domain-neutral kernel.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The always-worn su kernel is domain-neutral.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The rendered su kernel contains none of the WORKSPACE-MAP, PROMOTION-MODEL or deploy-pipeline sections.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any of those section markers appears inside a rendered su kernel document, or a Papercusp su render loses their text instead of receiving it from the papercusp-engineer domain or instance layer.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the su decomposition test; render a Papercusp su session and a non-coding su session and diff the kernel and domain layers.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/su-decomposition.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Judge as an identity stack.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The judge is an identity stack.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every judge mission launch renders the judge domain identity plus exactly one mission practice layer.\",\"falsifier\":\"A judge mission brief still embeds grading craft text in TypeScript, or the A/B comparison shows grading verdicts drifting beyond the agreed threshold.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the launch-blueprint tests; compare A/B grading verdicts for the old and new judge on the same subjects.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/launch-blueprints.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — One observation practice.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"One observation practice serves every role.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every role prompt receives its turn-end observation guidance from one shared practice identity.\",\"falsifier\":\"The TURN_END_OBSERVATION or friction-tripwire TypeScript constant still exists, or the su prompt carries a second copy of the guidance.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the su composition test; grep the source for the retired constants; render two different roles and confirm the same practice layer.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/su-composition.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Gym edits identity revisions.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The Gym edits identity revisions.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An accepted Gym proposal produces a new revision of one identity document and records that identity id and revision in gym_proposals.\",\"falsifier\":\"A Gym proposal still writes a flat role markdown file, or a gym_proposals row lacks the identity id or revision.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the Gym tests; inspect gym_proposals rows created after the migration for identity id and revision.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/gym.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — No self-grading.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The learning path cannot tune its own grader.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The host refuses every learning proposal that targets an identity layer worn by a judge that grades learning proposals.\",\"falsifier\":\"A Gym or other learning proposal against a judge-worn layer is accepted or reaches canary.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the Gym tests, including the case that proposes an edit to a judge-worn layer and expects a host refusal.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/gym.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Blast-radius control.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Widely worn layer changes are canaried.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An accepted revision of a widely worn layer rolls out pinned to a canary fraction and rolls back automatically on a measured regression.\",\"falsifier\":\"A widely worn revision reaches every wearer at once, or a forced regression in the canary does not roll it back.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"live\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the stack-mutation tests, including a forced-regression rollback case.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/stack-mutation.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Scout lenses as identities.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Scout lenses are identity documents.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each Scout lens prompt is rendered from an identity document by the render-only consumer.\",\"falsifier\":\"A Scout lens prompt string remains hard-coded in TypeScript, or the lens census is empty or differs from the shipped lens identity Splice markers become identity documents rather than hand splices.\n- **Phase 1:** P-001 to P-005 (foundations).\n- **Phase 2:** P-006 to P-010 (observation practice, judge, Gym).\n- **Phase 3:** P-011 to P-013 (lenses, memory recall, nudges).\n- **Phase 4:** P-014 to P-018 (roles, then retiring flat paths).\n- **Verification:** a render-diff parity test plus focused Vitest suites for each moved surface; live launch probes on the staging build or an isolated current build; an A/B agreement check for the judge; a canary plus forced-rollback drill for the Gym.\n\n## Tasks\n\n- **P-001** `done` Census: a script-derived, checked-in inventory of every behavior-shaping surface outside the identity system (flat role prompts, TypeScript prompt constants, injection hooks, kernel splices). Blocked by P-014, P-015, P-016 and P-017. blocked-by: P-014, P-015, P-016, P-017\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Safety and authority rails stay always-on and host-enforced\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-18 #1982/#1983 scope; constraint derived by su-7a61b3ed] Safety guards and mode authority can be EXPRESSED in the identity system only as always-worn kernel rules enforced in host code. They must apply with no identity package or a broken one, and are never budget-dropped. Reason: identities are optional, and some come from installed Cupboard packages (agent-identities/source.ts). Evidence that guards fit the system: sync-hook-rules.ts evaluatePreToolGuards is fail-closed.\n\n### D-002 — Engines are configured by identities, not turned into identities\nDate: 2026-10-18\nMemory retrieval, the Gym loop and the Scout scheduler stay host engines. Identities configure them (scopes, budgets, targets), and the Gym writes identity revisions. This mirrors modes: the prose is an identity, the authority is code.\n\n### D-003 — The learning path cannot tune its own grader; widely worn layer changes are canaried\nDate: 2026-10-18\nNo learning edit path may change identity layers worn by the judges that evaluate its proposals (the gym blueprint spine has a JUDGE step). Accepted revisions to widely worn layers roll out pinned, to a canary fraction, with automatic rollback on measured regression.\n\n### D-004 — Single model calls get a render-only identity consumer\nDate: 2026-10-18\nScout lenses are prompts for single model calls (llmCall in scout/cycle-deps.ts), not agent sessions. They become identity documents rendered by a render-only consumer; hooks and turn budgets do not apply.\n\n### D-005 — P-002 relocates WORKSPACE-MAP, PROMOTION-MODEL and the deploy-pipeline note to the base-homed su.instance layer, not into the papercusp-engineer identity document\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[self-imposed, su-7a61b3ed 2026-10-18] P-002's text says 'relocate ... to papercusp-engineer'. Implementing it literally would put PAPERCUSP-SU: splice markers inside an identity document (blueprints/papercusp-engineer/prompts/agent-base-overlay.md). identity-lint's `generated-marker` rule (libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/identity-lint.ts:24,157) forbids exactly that, and a standalone (non-su) wearer of papercusp-engineer, which P-003 enables, would ship the literal marker and lose the text. R-2's acceptance already allows the alternative: the text may reach a Papercusp su render 'from the papercusp-engineer domain or instance layer'. The integration audit (docs/audits/identities-v1-integration-audit.md rows S4f/S4g) classes both seams as instance-derived (env / release config). Ruling: the WORKSPACE-MAP and PROMOTION-MODEL tiles move from kernel to `instance` (su.instance.md, base-homed, which already carries PROJECT-GUIDE). The deploy-pipeline note renders with the PROMOTION-MODEL seam for the engineer profile, so it follows that seam into the instance layer. The SHARED-BASE-NOTES seam (now wait-loop, peer-wake, coupling, read-the-cell only) moves from kernel to `practice` (su.practice.md). The kernel-end boundary (SU_KERNEL_END) is placed after the seal by position, not by marker name, so kernel sections stay non-deferrable. su.md text does not change; the change is reclassification plus render wiring. Relocation-only render parity is proven by test.\n\n### D-006 — R-9 is split into four atomic recall bars, not narrowed\nDate: 2026-10-18\nDate: 2026-10-18 [self-imposed, su-7a61b3ed, accepting outside-lineage objection thread-post:1189719 on WI-6554700010017138]\nR-9 keeps only the budget-share bound at turn start, with a falsifier that matches it. The coverage the first rewrite dropped now sits in three sibling bars, all mapped to P-012: R-17 (a declared memory scope restricts turn-start recall), R-18 (declared knowledge corpora restrict turn-start knowledge selection) and R-19 (declared recall bounds also bound mid-turn recall). Reason: the plan's outcome covers the self-learning system (owner directive #1983 source turns), and memory scopes and knowledge packs already exist in code (selected-knowledge-launch.test.ts bundle-scope / knowledge-pack conflict), so dropping them would be an unrecorded weakening.\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAmendment-Id: amend-7870ce17e0369b213036e2ab\nRequest-Hash: b6b64aebbbad3ad7be557bcce9fb18fb6326016892a8ac5dc1c0a98a2ac5cadd\nActor: su-7a61b3ed-841b-4d7c-b177-f87c76073391\nReason: R-9 split per plan decision identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18#D-006 (accepting the outside-lineage objection thread-post:1189719 on WI-6554700010017138). R-9 keeps only the turn-start budget-share bound, with a falsifier that matches it. The coverage the first R-9 rewrite dropped moves to three new BARs, each mapped to P-012: R-17 (declared memory scope restricts turn-start recall), R-18 (declared knowledge corpora restrict turn-start knowledge selection) and R-19 (declared recall bounds also bound mid-turn recall). The plan is still a draft and P-012 is unstarted, so no implementation evidence depends on the old wording.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-fec15347-d6cf-4dff-8d38-c4c370052e3f\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1189836\nApproved-At: 2026-10-18T02:53:21.848Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 21 → 22\nChanged BARs: R-9, R-17, R-18, R-19\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-008 — Overlap with identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17: P-003 builds on its wearer model; Phase 1 proceeds independently\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[Ruling by su-7a61b3ed, 2026-10-18 ~05:35Z. CO-SIGNED by su-c0dfd243, IDOP's author, at 05:40:08Z (coord-send-aa77ef5d8fe8ee8326b633bcf7ab785a5aa918524d83527ebe3b2423968303cc). The co-signature confirms that this plan's P-002 precedes IDOP's P-001 snapshot, that IDOP's frozen su render is this plan's P-001 parity baseline, and that the stall fallback is approved provided it adds no new per-role table. IDOP P-012/P-003 had not started at co-sign time; they sit behind IDOP's own rubric amendment, activation audit and plan activation. Grounded in consult conv-mvddveuf-0000-08163f8d43b941d39554553091b71504, answer post 1190207 by su-0dc4cc33, plus a direct read of both plans.]\n\nMeasured:\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-identities/wearer-authority.ts:16,21`: 'Every identity-bearing launch record is an SU launch record'; `IDENTITY_WEARER_ROLE = 'su'`.\n- `agent-identities/generic-identity-launch-authority.integration.test.ts` exists. Its last change was 2026-09-30, commit 4c65360b6b, from an earlier plan. It holds only the 'confers no SU authority' cases, none of IDOP's R-3/R-5 cases, so IDOP's wearer change has NOT landed.\n- IDOP (identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17) is at v14, draft, with all 15 items todo. This plan's P-002 is already done.\n\n**Ruling: run both plans in parallel. IDOP goes first on the permission, wearer and schema seams; this plan goes first on the prompt seams.**\n\nParallel now (no IDOP dependency): P-001 surface census, P-005 shrink-only lint, P-004 always-worn kernel rules, P-011's render-only consumer, and the non-vault parts of P-012. P-004 rules are built as HOST code, or as IDOP P-012's identity root, never as a stack layer, because a layer would occupy a slot and fall under contribution and restriction rules.\n\nBlocked on IDOP (external gates, recorded as blockers on the promoted work-items when reached):\n- P-003 is blocked on IDOP P-012 (layer and stack format) and IDOP P-003 (delete the per-role ceiling table). It is co-designed with IDOP P-007 (directory-group wearers). P-003's grant bound is restated from 'role and pot ceiling' to 'the effective chain (IDOP P-005)'. The joint design must define who the 'wearer' of a system-launched stack is (judge, harness roles, consult/resume/fork/wake paths), the R-5 loophole the IDOP review flagged.\n- P-015 (capability requests) is blocked on IDOP P-014: those requests ARE IDOP layer asks, granted at install.\n- P-008, P-009 and P-010 (Gym edits identity revisions) are blocked on IDOP P-002. Gym revisions that widen asks are held for the binding owner's typed approval by design. P-009/P-010 classify changes through IDOP P-002, never a second classifier.\n- Every item that authors new layers is blocked on IDOP P-012's schema and slot rules: P-006 observation practice, P-007 judge domain and mission, P-011 Scout lenses, P-013 rule bundles, P-014 and P-016 domain and stance identities, P-017.\n\nCarried constraints:\n- **Seeding.** IDOP P-014 makes new-stack settings unset, and unset means deny. Every migration item (P-007, P-014–P-017) must seed its stack settings (wearers, spend cap, secret scope, vault) and include a launch probe proving the migrated role still launches.\n- **Recall.** P-012's memory-recall configuration is an identity field, not a workspace runtime field (IDOP refuses those). Identity-declared recall corpora never include the Personal Vault (IDOP P-015 / D-006).\n- **Census.** The populations differ, so both censuses are kept. IDOP P-001 is a live observation of permissions from real sessions. This plan's P-001 is a static inventory of prompt surfaces. The one shared datum is the su prompt render: this plan's census references IDOP's frozen render as the su parity baseline and does not make a second one.\n- **Ordering trap (satisfied).** This plan's P-002 changed su's rendered prompt and landed BEFORE IDOP P-001 took any snapshot. Any further change by this plan to su's rendered prompt must land before IDOP's P-001 snapshot, or be recorded as an accepted delta in IDOP. It never lands between that snapshot and IDOP R-12's check.\n\n**Stall fallback (co-signed).** If IDOP has not landed IDOP P-012 and P-003 by about 2026-10-19 05:40Z (one day after co-sign), P-003 lands a thin first step that adopts IDOP's asks/maximum/restrictions contract. That step generalizes the identity-bearing launch record only, keeps today's bound behind the single function IDOP P-003 will replace, and adds NO new per-role table.\n\n**Why.** Two plans editing wearer-authority.ts and the layer schema with different semantics would fork the identity model, and layers authored before IDOP P-012 would have to be re-authored.\n\n### D-009 — The P-001 census and the P-005 lint live in operator-core; R-16's check file moves there\nDate: 2026-10-18\nDate: 2026-10-18 [self-imposed, su-7a61b3ed, while implementing P-001 / WI-6554700010017313]\n\nThe surfaces R-16 polices span two repositories: orchestrator prompt constants and base role prompts in the libs/papercusp submodule, and chat personas, su tools playbooks, operator-core prompt constants and the installed hook list (CC_HOOK_FILES) in the superproject. No orchestrator test reads superproject files, so a census or lint rooted in libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator cannot see more than half the population.\n\nRuling: the census lives at packages/operator-core/lib/agent-identities/identity-surface-census.ts, with the checked-in inventory identity-surface-census.generated.json beside it, regenerated by `npm run gen:identity-surface-census` (`:check` exits 1 on drift). Its tests are identity-surface-census.test.ts. It reuses BASE_ROLE_LIBRARY_DISPOSITION, SU_PART_DOCUMENTS and CLIENT_SEAM_MARKER from @papercusp/orchestrator/blueprint and CC_HOOK_FILES / CC_HOOK_LIB_FILES from desktop-install/papercusp-files.ts, now exported.\n\nP-005 builds the shrink-only lint over that inventory in operator-core. When P-005 lands, amend R-16's check.files from libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/identity-lint.test.ts to the operator-core test that holds the lint, via rubrics:amend. identity-lint.ts stays the composed-stack linter; it is unchanged.\n\nThe inventory records surface identity only (class, id, path, name, kind), never content hashes, so editing a prompt's text does not churn it. The baseline at P-001: 282 surfaces (109 flat-role-prompt, 90 prompt-constant, 55 injection-hook, 28 kernel-splice). Hook kinds: 5 identity-dispatch (marked inside), 18 guard, 28 context, 4 plumbing.\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAmendment-Id: amend-915d81d6d4362c996fd27303\nRequest-Hash: addfb7bde40d6632c8014a57bc91962e7142fd4de7a53ef3858b25d7218087ca\nActor: su-7a61b3ed-841b-4d7c-b177-f87c76073391\nReason: R-16 check file moves to the operator-core identity-surface lint per plan decision identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18#D-009: the census and the shrink-only lint that R-16 polices span both repositories, so they live in packages/operator-core/lib/agent-identities/. The previously named libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/identity-lint.test.ts tests the identity-document lint, not the R-16 detector. Only R-16 verification.check.files changes; every other BAR is reproduced unchanged from plan revision 29.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-4f6852be-283b-4c8d-9e73-274c221b84e5\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1190478\nApproved-At: 2026-10-18T08:33:19.666Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 29 → 30\nChanged BARs: R-16\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-011 — P-011's four Scout lens layers were authored before IDOP P-012, against D-008; keep them render-only and re-author if IDOP P-012 changes the layer format\nDate: 2026-10-18\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[Ruling by su-7a61b3ed, ~12:20Z; found while re-reading D-008 during P-011 closure. CO-SIGNED by su-c0dfd243 (IDOP author, D-008 co-signer) at 12:21:21Z, msg coord-send-16cc17f3489dac14e6d85abbdcf1619c719ab802d07e0b39473c8b976ba92c87: \"ok. Keep the four Scout lens texts render-only under D-011 ... Keep the actual layer-authoring path behind IDOP P-012 as D-008 requires; re-author these files if P-012 changes the layer/slot format.\" This amends D-008 for P-011 only.]\n\nMeasured:\n- D-008 lists 'P-011 Scout lenses' among the items that author new layers and are therefore blocked on IDOP P-012's schema and slot rules. Only P-011's render-only consumer was cleared to run in parallel.\n- P-011 as built (committed in fe552a16de, libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/scout.lens-{analogical,constraint-removal,first-principles,reframing}/blueprint.yaml + prompts/lens.md) authors four abstract layers in TODAY's blueprint format, each with `slots: - slot: practice`. That is the case D-008 deferred.\n- All four declare no grants, asks, tools, permissions, maximum or restrictions (grep over the four blueprint.yaml files: zero such keys; the one keyword hit is description prose). Their only consumer is `renderOnlyStack` (orchestrator/src/blueprint/render-stack.ts): one structured LLM call with no kernel, no tools and no dispatch seat, which refuses a grant at render time.\n- IDOP P-001 is todo and IDOP P-012 / P-003 are blocked as of 12:18Z.\n\n**Ruling: keep the four lens layers.** D-008's reason for deferring layer authoring was (a) two plans editing wearer-authority and the layer schema with different semantics would fork the identity model, and (b) layers authored before IDOP P-012 would need re-authoring. (a) does not apply: these layers carry no grants, no wearer and no permission semantics, and nothing here edits wearer-authority.ts or the layer schema. (b) does apply, and is accepted as a known cost: if IDOP P-012 changes the layer or slot format, the four lens documents are re-authored to it as part of that migration (four small YAML files plus verbatim prompt text; lens weights stay keyed by the same identity ids).\n\nScope: this covers P-011's four render-only lens texts only. The general layer-authoring path, and every other item D-008 holds behind IDOP P-012 (P-006, P-007, P-013, P-014, P-016, P-017), stays blocked.\n\n### D-012 — Co-sign D-011: keep Scout lens texts render-only; defer layer authoring to IDOP P-012\nDate: 2026-10-18\nIDOP author/co-signer decision: ok to keep P-011's four Scout lens texts render-only under D-011 because they declare no grants, asks, tools, permissions, maximums or restrictions and are consumed only by renderOnlyStack without a kernel or dispatch seat. The actual layer-authoring half remains behind IDOP P-012 as D-008 requires. If P-012 changes the layer/slot format, re-author these four files against that schema.\n\nMeasured: `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/render-stack.ts:244-256` rejects reserved kernel/instance layers and any grants for render-only stacks; `packages/operator-core/lib/scout/lenses.ts:158-181` routes lens identity documents through `renderOnlyStack`; `libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/blueprint/render-stack.test.ts:113-124` covers those refusals.\nRelated: P-011\n\n### D-013 — Rubric vetting (thread-post:1190831) requires amending R-11, R-16 and R-8 before their proof counts; the 12:5xZ bindings and cards are provisional\nDate: 2026-10-18\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[self-imposed, su-7a61b3ed, ~12:58Z; from rubric-vetting consult conv-mvdsmkwu-0000-f47471bbc4084a09acc6ebcdd4398c7a, answer thread-post:1190831 by su-bc2387bb (outside the author lineage). Full text saved at .papercusp/scratch/p-identity/vetting-answer.md.]\n\nMeasured findings accepted:\n- R-11 (P-004): 'every listed safety rail' names no list, so a test can cover any subset and pass. Amend to enumerate the rail ids (or cite a checked-in manifest with exact set equality), require one violating-call fixture per rail under absent AND corrupted identity packages, assert the population is non-empty, and add an exhausted-budget case for 'never budget-dropped'. Independently corroborated by grading-integrity finding EI-26319167582150892: the SPEC-P-004 clause (lock arbitration blocks a peer-held edit with no identity package) is not exercised by sync-hook-rules.worn-rules-cache.test.ts.\n- R-16 (P-001 census integrity, P-005 enforcement): require three named mutations (flat role prompt, behavior-prompt constant, context-injection hook), each independently non-zero, plus a clean-tree pass; state that 'baseline count is zero' means unallowlisted detector violations, not census population (the census holds 282 surfaces per D-009); add a non-empty exact-set assertion tying the generated census to the checked-in inventory. D-009/D-010's two operator-core test files are confirmed correct.\n- R-8 (P-011): the bar covers lens rendering only; identity-keyed weights appear only in driftMarkers. Add the weight-key invariant (or a sibling BAR), define a non-empty Scout-lens census with exact coverage.\n- Later, before their proof: R-3 (declare A/B metric, sample and threshold), R-4 (role census with exact coverage), R-6 (judge-worn-layer census), R-7 (thresholds for widely worn, canary fraction, regression), R-12 (cite the pipeline-role census).\n- The R-9 split (D-006/D-007) is sound.\n\nRuling: amend the rubric (one batched rubrics:amend covering R-11, R-16 and R-8, with matching plan requirement blocks) before P-001/P-004/P-005/P-011 can close. Then add the missing test cases, rerun the clean root, rebind, and re-emit. The six terminal cards emitted 12:50-12:53Z (EI-26321674643430083, -695275144602, -723638369075, -745381447076, -768432643435, -787776221573) prove the pre-amendment clauses only, so they are provisional and will be superseded. R-3/R-4/R-6/R-7/R-12 are amended before their items' proof, in the same batch where practical, because any rubric edit invalidates vetting and grading.\n\n### D-014 — SPEC-P-004 names the kernel git rails, not lock arbitration; the kernel rails now refuse shell input over the guard input bound\nDate: 2026-10-18\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[self-imposed, su-7a61b3ed, ~13:20Z; triggered by auditor finding EI-26319167582150892 and rubric vetting thread-post:1190831 (D-013).]\n\nMeasured:\n- The SPEC-P-004 clause said 'the lock arbitration guard blocks an edit to a peer-held file when the session wears no identity package'. Lock arbitration is the operator lock table plus apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/pretooluse-locks-acquire.sh; it reads only the session owner id, never an identity package, and P-004 never touched it. Its peer-held deny is already pinned by pretooluse-locks-decision.test.ts 'block-on-held (busy)'. The four rails P-004 built (kernel-safety-rails.ts) are destructive shared-tree git commands. The clause named the wrong rail, so no test of P-004's code could exercise it.\n- Real defect found while pinning 'never budget-dropped': the tool-guard port sends input:null when the adapter flags inputTruncated (input over SYNC_HOOK_GUARD_INPUT_MAX_BYTES = 64 KiB). Worn guards already refused such a call (sync-hook-rules.ts:163), but the kernel rails saw no command and returned no verdict, so ANY shell call over 64 KiB passed every kernel rail. That contradicts the adapter's own contract (hooks/inject/core.mjs guardCall: over the bound the server refuses the call for any guard that matches the tool).\n\nRuling:\n1. Correct SPEC-P-004 (plans:set-specs) to: 'A destructive shared-tree git command is refused when the session wears no identity package.' Falsifier: 'With the identity package removed, git reset --hard passes the pre-tool guard.' Lock arbitration stays out of P-004.\n2. Kernel rails carry an appliesTo tool condition; a call whose input is over the guard input bound is refused by the kernel (rule kernel:guard-input-bound, naming every rail it hides from) for any tool a rail reads. Shell calls over 64 KiB are therefore refused for every session; the refusal tells the agent to write long content with the Write tool or split the command.\n3. Tests (in the tree, green 13:13-13:15Z): sync-hook-rules.worn-rules-cache.test.ts adds the exact non-empty rail set, a corrupted-package worn state, and per-rail and per-worn-state over-bound refusals; identity-hook-sinks.test.ts adds port-level refusals with an exhausted hook-turn budget (turn never read or charged) and with over-bound shell input; the worn truncation test moves to a non-shell tool, and the integration assertion for truncated capability:bash now expects the kernel refusal.\n4. The R-11 amendment (D-013) names both test files; draft at .papercusp/scratch/p-identity/amend-draft.md.\n\n### D-015 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-18\nAmendment-Id: amend-64bc7efb4190445f5c995e50\nRequest-Hash: 10e158e9d9f0d1cebf0cacc4010184101c3132b00891a19feb547b2f8f663a3f\nActor: su-7a61b3ed-841b-4d7c-b177-f87c76073391\nReason: Batched amendment per plan decisions identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18#D-013 (rubric vetting thread-post:1190831) and #D-014. R-11: the method and check name the exact non-empty kernel rail set (kernel:git-reset-hard, kernel:git-clean-force, kernel:git-checkout-all, kernel:git-stash), a violating-call fixture per rail under absent, throwing, broken, corrupted and empty identity packages, the exhausted hook-turn budget and over-bound shell input; identity-hook-sinks.test.ts joins the check. R-16: three named seeded mutations each fail the lint, zero at ship means zero unallowlisted violations, and the census is non-empty, has exactly four classes and equals the checked-in inventory. R-8: the lens census is non-empty and equals the shipped scout.lens-* identity documents; lenses.test.ts joins the check, and the weight-key clause moves out of R-8. New R-20 (P-011): Scout lens weights are keyed by lens identity ids, checked by outcome-feedback.test.ts and lenses.test.ts. Bars (model) of R-8, R-11 and R-16 are unchanged; every other BAR is reproduced unchanged from plan revision 39.\nApproved-By: su-092e053f-0e71-4fd9-b2c0-9d9ff5b6fc81\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1190895\nApproved-At: 2026-10-18T13:43:58.940Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 39 → 40\nChanged BARs: R-8, R-11, R-16, R-20\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-8, R-11, R-16\n\n### D-016 — Rubric rev 4 is vetted attestable; R-3, R-4, R-6, R-7 and R-12 must be amended before their own proof binds\nDate: 2026-10-18\nDate: 2026-10-18\n[self-imposed, su-7a61b3ed, ~13:56Z; from rubric-vetting consult conv-mvdvubpa-0000-131439124aa24f22b3d1828aef3e5d60, answer thread-post:1190902 by su-0f2cd5d6 (codex/sol, outside the author lineage). Text saved at .papercusp/scratch/p-identity/vetting-answer-rev4.md.]\n\nMeasured: rubric acceptance-identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18 rev 4 (D-015, approval thread-post:1190895) changes only R-8/R-11/R-16 driftMarkers, method and check, and adds R-20; the other 16 BARs are byte-unchanged from rev 3. R-11 enumerates the exact non-empty kernel rail set and five package states plus exhausted-hook and over-bound-shell fixtures; R-16 has three seeded mutations, an explicit zero-at-ship definition and a four-class census equal to the inventory; R-8 requires a non-empty lens census equal to the shipped scout.lens-* documents; R-20 separately binds identity-keyed lens weights. The fallback was pre-agreed for exactly this case.\n\n### D-018 — su-7a61b3ed carries identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17 (IDOP) from its rubric-review step\nDate: 2026-10-21\n**Context.** Per identity-system-everything-migration-2026-10-18#D-017, every remaining item of this plan waits on an IDOP item: P-008/P-009/P-010 on identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17#P-002, P-015 on identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17#P-014, and P-006/P-007/P-013/P-014/P-016/P-017 on identity-definitions-own-policy-2026-10-17#P-012. D-017's boundary is unchanged. IDOP's acceptance contract (D-011/D-012) and its coordination with this plan (IDOP D-013) stand as written.\n\n**Reversal.** If su-c0dfd243 or su-3b04ef5e objects with an alternative, su-7a61b3ed checkpoints the current IDOP step, releases its claims, and records a superseding decision.\n\n### D-019 — Make existing P-012 recall falsifiers explicit canonical scenario obligations\nDate: 2026-10-22\n[Self-imposed proof repair; 2026-10-22, umbrella WI-6554700010018194.] The fresh R-17 controls 21772367/21772373 pass and mutant 21772382 is caught; bindings 64646/64649 are current with exact saved paths/fixtures/case metadata. Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context.
