Five original bug records are terminal with root-cause verification. Focused suites and scoped TypeScript checks passed. Final report rpt_d72eebb7-ac80-47c0-8cd2-6264da255f43 verified with complete body and owner visibility. This coordination checklist did not create duplicate implementation work. Some exact-blob completion settlement remains automatic; no deployment claim.\n\n**Next:** No implementation work remains in this checklist. Automatic git-sync and promotion own delivery; later deployment verification is a separate explicit task.\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: operators depending on safe DBOS recovery. Problem: uncertain effects are skipped/repeated, and invocation identities can cross lifetimes. Outcome: durable recovery with no guessed outcomes. Non-goals: fleets, new workflow engine, live destructive drills, unrelated gate work. Source: owner explicitly requested AUTO and direct implementation of the five findings in report rpt_9190d05a-d3a6-49c1-8457-45ed5bd029ca.\n\n## Execution\nRoute: this session, existing owned bug work-items. Reuse existing effect/receipt/persistence surfaces and preserve authority checks. Regression tests belong in canonical suites. Do not duplicate implementation WIs.\n\n## Requirements\n\nThese bars are an explicit post-implementation backfill of the five original fixes, not a claim that they were declared before implementation. Production activation is a separate owner-requested closeout obligation on WI-6554700010020374.\n\n**R-1 — Pipeline invocations stay stable within a lifetime and distinct across reopened lifetimes.** Epoch zero retains historical identities; epochs1 and2 cannot reuse each other's completed agent output.\n\n**R-2 — Unavailable prior output cannot authorize another spawn.** Successful absence returns null; successful stored output is reused; a rejected read throws with cause before spawn.\n\n**R-3 — Reaction replay distinguishes completed effects from uncertain claims.** Independent PG completion receipt permits replay without dispatch; unfinished/legacy claims and thrown/returned failures halt visibly for reconciliation and preserve identity.\n\n**R-4 — Generic coordination replay reuses thread and member identities.** Trusted run+step effect identity feeds the existing conflict-safe conversation store and a stable per-member invocation key; independent runs remain distinct.\n\n**R-5 — Ledger recovery preserves the original transaction and independent receipt.** Persist intent before broadcast, pin original root/window, recover saved receipt or rebroadcast same signed bytes; arbitrary uncertain non-replayable backends stop.\n\n## Design\n\nReuse existing workflow invocation, reaction ledger, conversation store, and anchor publication store. Uncertain effects require reconciliation; completed effects reuse independently persisted results.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-005 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Agent outcomes\n- **P-001** `done` Namespace invocation identities by pipeline epoch; same-lifetime replay stays stable (WI-6554700010018136). — note: Implementation and focused regression verification completed under the five original bug work-items; see their structured completions. Scoped operator-core and orchestrator TypeScript checks passed. Completion content manifests settle through git-sync.\n- **P-002** `done` Fail closed when prior invocation outcome cannot be read (WI-6554700010018137). — note: Implementation and focused regression verification completed under the five original bug work-items; see their structured completions. Scoped operator-core and orchestrator TypeScript checks passed. Completion content manifests settle through git-sync.\n\n## Phase 2 — External effects\n- **P-003** `done` Recover or reconcile pending event-reaction outcomes and thrown dispatch (WI-6554700010018128). — note: Implementation and focused regression verification completed under the five original bug work-items; see their structured completions. Scoped operator-core and orchestrator TypeScript checks passed. Completion content manifests settle through git-sync.\n- **P-004** `done` Make coordination thread and fan-out member effects replay-safe (WI-6554700010018132). — note: Implementation and focused regression verification completed under the five original bug work-items; see their structured completions. Scoped operator-core and orchestrator TypeScript checks passed. Completion content manifests settle through git-sync.\n- **P-005** `done` Persist and reconcile chain publication identity before any resubmission (WI-6554700010018135). — note: Implementation and focused regression verification completed under the five original bug work-items; see their structured completions. Scoped operator-core and orchestrator TypeScript checks passed. Completion content manifests settle through git-sync.\n\n## Phase 3 — Verification\n- **P-006** `done` Run focused regression suites, record root-cause verification on original bugs, publish final status. — note: Verification and owner report delivery complete; report rpt_d72eebb7-ac80-47c0-8cd2-6264da255f43 full-body readback verified.\n\n## Decisions\nOwner selected AUTO and direct implementation, no subagents. Existing bugs are the execution authority; this plan coordinates them. Prior DBOS completion/prompt plans concern the original migration and are shipped/superseded; these five newly evidenced defects are a new effort. New provider seams must use existing receipt/config stores where possible.\n\n### D-001 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: amend-a74523e0890998dcfdebb800\nRequest-Hash: e23a8313b4ca6f8129d075682f2e7e9a7930837e7d81d1055a8901cddc024adf\nActor: su-4f8732f8-16d7-4929-92aa-46a2f8c2356c\nReason: Apply independently approved restoration of authored check/METHOD/falsifier and honest post-implementation provenance after cohort seed loss. Approval explicitly references preview thread-post1195694; no implementation scope weakened.\nApproved-By: system:judge/su-9eb0b302-b3ee-467d-a903-b549ff5142c3\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1195756\nApproved-At: 2026-10-22T14:17:09.902Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 11 → 12\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: dbos-provenance-correction-20261022\nRequest-Hash: 0f423edca15533abdad862653e0a49de7d65f4e53f4621121936d5c4d0a8e83f\nActor: su-4f8732f8-16d7-4929-92aa-46a2f8c2356c\nReason: Correct the false pre-implementation lifecycle label to legacy-backfilled, matching plan Requirements and D-001 and independent audit EI-26700923394314153. Change provenance lifecycle only; retain declaration actor/time, all bar meaning, hashes, checks and accepted proof.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive ()\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 12 → 13\nChanged BARs: \nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"e2e-probe-p010-section-gates-2026-10-20","title":"E2E probe for P-010 section gates","status":"superseded","created":"2026-10-20","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: E2E probe for P-010 section gates\nslug: e2e-probe-p010-section-gates-2026-10-20\nstatus: superseded\ncreated: 2026-10-20\nupdated: 2026-10-20\n---\n\n# E2E probe for P-010 section gates\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⛔ PLAN CLOSED — SUPERSEDED 2026-10-20. Add a wait leg beside resolveDependencyGraphEdges (sync-resolver/dependency-graph-edges.ts) … <!-- P-009 -->\n## Goal\n\nA work item that waits on an event — a typed `event`/`gate` blocker (`work_items:set_blocker`) or a durable park trigger (`claim_hold_release.trigger`) — goes back to the queue as soon as a fire that PROVES its condition happens: the wait is cleared with history kept, the item's state is restored, claimable lists refresh, and the holder is woken. A wait that no fire can ever prove is refused when it is written, instead of stranding silently.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Audience:** agents that park work on a condition; fleet leaders and the owner, who see stranded items.\n- **Problem:** the system already has the parts (a completion event per work item, an await engine, a settlement function, a blocker re-check sweep), but they only connect in narrow cases. Event waits settle only when the key was ANNOUNCED; gate-kind waits never settle; feature-family items are left `blocked` after a system clear; and set_blocker accepts conditions no fire can prove. Agents do the bookkeeping by hand: about 211 of 234 cleared event blockers were cleared by an agent.\n- **Outcome:** event waits behave like dependency edges — they release themselves when the thing happens, on any emit path, with the same evidence trail.\n- **Non-goals (recommended by su-42565716 in its reply to directive #2022 [self-imposed]; the owner proceeded with the narrow plan in #2024 without ruling on them, and reversed non-goal 2 in #2038 / D-003):** (1) moving blockers into `work_item_deps` (storage merge); (2) ~~projecting session `events:await` registrations into the dependency graph~~ — WITHDRAWN by D-003 (owner directive #2038, 2026-10-20): the Work-tab graph view now shows them (P-009); storage stays separate; (3) folding plan-lane holds into a new mechanism; (4) shipping the already-built work-item-ref auto-clear and edge routing — they ride the release gate, which is owned by the live gate lane; (5) changing the refusal of a new dependency edge behind a held item.\n- **Source turns:** owner directives #2018 (\"Is there any way we can unify our DAG and event await systems?\"), #2022 (\"do you think this is a good idea?\"), #2024 (\"before you write the plan give our code a thorough look through so you understand the best implementation\") — session su-42565716, 2026-10-20.\n- **Scenarios:**\n  - S1. An agent holding WI-A blocks it on `release:deployed:<sha>` and its session ends. The deploy fires (not announced). WI-A returns to `open`, shows up as claimable within one emit, and the blocker history records what cleared it.\n  - S2. An agent tries to block on `coord:inbox-wake:<self>` or `git-sync:committed`. set_blocker refuses, says that key fires for unrelated reasons, and names the options: a key that proves the condition, an announced gate, a predicate watch, or a runtime/human blocker with a re-check date.\n  - S3. A feature-family item whose last blocker is cleared by the system goes from `blocked` back to `open`; its holder is told.\n  - S4. A gate-kind blocker on an announced key (for example an announced fleet gate `fleet:<slug>:<gate>`) clears when the gate fires. A broad key such as `release:green:papercusp` is not a valid example: set_blocker refuses it and no fire of it settles a wait (D-008).\n  - S5. The process crashes between the fire latch and settlement; the recovery pass settles the wait within one sweep interval.\n  - S6. A blocker naming `work-item:done:WI-B` clears when WI-B finishes by ANY path (plan cascade, resolve, merge), not only via `work_items:complete`.\n  - S7. WI-X is held by an agent whose session waits on event K (an `events:await` bound to WI-X). The Work-tab dependency graph shows WI-X waiting on K as a holder wait, next to any event/gate blocker on WI-X itself, labels whether a fire of K can prove anything, and marks the wait stale when that agent's session has ended. | What clears it automatically |\n|---|---|---|\n| Typed external blocker | `work_items.payload.externalBlockers` (external-blockers.ts) | `reconcileEventExternalBlockers` (work-items.ts) — only from `stampAnnouncementsFired` / announcement retirement (events/await/store.ts), i.e. only ANNOUNCED keys, and only `kind:'event'`; kept off the ordinary emit path because the probe was a ~350ms scan (EI-20721448404004954). The re-check sweep (attention/work-item-blocker-reaper.ts) — only when `recheckAt` is set and due. Work-item-ref auto-clear (work-item-ref-blocker-auto-clear*.ts) — a reaction on the `work_items:complete` / `work_items:set_state` TOOL calls. Plan-lane reconcile. |\n| Durable claim park | `payload._claimHold` + `claim_hold_release.trigger` | `reconcileEventDurableParks` (work-items-durable-park-audit.ts) — announced fires only. |\n| Dependency edge | `work_item_deps` | Readiness is derived when the blocker is terminal. set_blocker routes pure work-item refs (bare ids, `work-item:done:<id>`) to edges (work-item-ref-blocker-edges.ts). A new edge behind a held item is refused. |\n\nOther facts that shape the design:\n- `eventHasSpecificCondition` (external-condition-reachability.ts) treats any catalogued id-scoped key with a concrete subject as proof. It does not separate COMPLETION families (`work-item:done`, `plan-run:finished`, `task:terminal`, `lock:grant`, `escalation:resolved`, `conversation:answered`, `report:published`…) from CHANGE notifications (`work-item:status`, `work-item:claimed`, `work-item:blocked`, `work-item:unblocked`, `goal:plan-placement`, `goal:edit-claim`). The re-check sweep already clears on that basis.\n- `emitAwaitedEvent` (events/await/engine.ts) records every fire on the per-key latch with one statement (`recordKeyFire`), which already returns the key's standing subscribers in the same round trip.\n- `clearExternalBlockersOnLockedRow` (work-items.ts) is the shared per-row clear; `followUpAutoClearedBlockers` (work-item-ref-blocker-auto-clear.ts) already does un-park + message + wake after a system clear, but only the auto-clear path calls it.\n- The work-item-ref auto-clear and the edge routing were committed on 2026-10-12 but are NOT in `d740fc3802`, the build serving :3070, so they have not run on the main operator.\n- The header comment of work-item-ref-blocker-guard.ts says settlement runs \"when a key fires\"; the code only does that for announced keys.\n\n## Evidence (measured 2026-10-20, papercusp-workspace)\n\n- Cleared `event` blockers: 234. 22 by the re-check sweep, 1 by the auto-clear (staging), the rest by agents; 38 of the agent clears were migrations to dependency edges. No clear carries the settlement signature.\n- Active event/gate blockers on open items: 755 (161 event, 594 gate): 363 `plan-lane:*` (cleared by plan reconcile), 62 free text, the rest key-shaped. Of the 41 whose key fired after the blocker was set, 22 name an inbox-wake key and about 10 name broad notifications (`git-sync:committed`, `work-item:claimable`, `scorecard:emitted:*`, `green-checkpoint:red:*`) — a fire of those proves nothing. Only 5 (`work-item:done:<id>` with a finished referent) were genuinely releasable.\n- 9 active GATE blockers name an announced key; settlement ignores the gate kind.\n- 14 items are `blocked` with every blocker cleared and nothing else holding them (11 feature-family, median idle 17.6 days, 7 unheld).\n- The settlement probe on live data: ~98 ms and 25k buffer hits (4,419 rows carry blocker history; the only index is a partial btree on workspace_id).\n\n## Design\n\n1. **Classify what a fire proves (curated, pinned).** Add a field to the event catalogue entry (events/await/catalog.ts) saying whether a fire of a concrete key means the subject reached its final condition. Add `fireCertifiesCondition(key, producerDeclared)` next to `eventHasSpecificCondition`. A test lists EVERY id-scoped family with its classification, so a new family cannot ship unclassified. Switch the re-check sweep and durable-park settlement to the new predicate.\n2. **Index the wait refs (derived, not hand-maintained).** One migration: a partial GIN `jsonb_path_ops` index on `payload->'externalBlockers'` and a partial btree index on the park trigger. Rewrite both settlement queries to the indexable expressions. Derived from the payload, so it cannot drift the way a second registration table would.\n3. **One follow-up after every system clear.** Reuse `followUpAutoClearedBlockers`: un-park feature-family items set_blocker parked, refresh claimable (`notifySyncInvalidate`), message and wake the holder. Wire it into announced settlement, the new fire settlement, the re-check sweep and park settlement.\n4. **Settle on every proving fire.** In `emitAwaitedEvent`, have `recordKeyFire` also return whether any item waits on the key (indexed EXISTS in the same statement, no extra round trip). Only when it does AND `fireCertifiesCondition` holds: open one transaction under the same per-key advisory lock announcements use, settle event AND gate blockers plus parks, then run the follow-up. Fail-soft, never breaks the emit.\n5. **Recovery pass, no new routine.** In the existing re-check sweep tick: settle active waits whose proving key's latch shows a fire after the wait was created (exact for \"fired since\"). Also repair items left `blocked` with every blocker cleared.\n6. **Validate at write time.** set_blocker (event/gate kinds) and durable-park triggers classify the ref with the existing reachability reader: proving key, announced key or live predicate watch is accepted; a proving key that already fired is refused as already satisfied; a broad, uncatalogued or free-text ref is refused with guidance. Correct the stale guard comment.\n7. **Drive the work-item-ref auto-clear from the completion fire.** Today it reacts to two tool names, so closes through other paths miss it. Call it from the settlement hook on `work-item:done:<id>`, which the DB trigger + outbox emit on terminal transitions. Check whether that event fires for dropped items (EI-21564741982937381 reported it does not) and cover dropped referents.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| Requirement | Items | Evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | live |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-005 | live |\n| R-11 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-006 | live |\n| R-13 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-009 | live |\n| R-20 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-004 | tree |\n\n8. **Show event waits in the dependency graph (D-003).** Add a wait leg next to the edge resolver: each item's own event/gate blockers plus its holder's session awaits (bound to the item, or held by the holder), read at query time from event_awaits and work_items.payload. Render as event nodes in the Work-tab pane, labelled by fireCertifiesCondition and marked stale when the subscriber's session has ended.\n\n## Open choices for the owner\n\nAll resolved by D-001 (owner directive #2036); kept for history.\n\n1. **Existing mis-modelled blockers** (about 35 on broad keys, 62 free text): (a) give each a re-check date so the sweep escalates it to its holder once — default; (b) leave them; (c) clear them.\n2. **Strictness at write time:** refuse (default) or accept with a warning.\n3. **Change notifications stop counting as proof** in the re-check sweep (for example a blocker on `work-item:status:<id>` no longer clears on any status change). Default: yes.\n\n## Risks\n\n- **Emit hot path:** the EXISTS probe runs inside every fire's latch statement; it must be index-only. Measure emit latency before and after.\n- **Wrong classification** releases work early; the pinned family list is the guard.\n- **Workspace namespaces:** event tables use `workspace_id='default'`, work items the tenant id; today's settlement query matches by key across workspaces. Keep and test that behaviour deliberately.\n- **Delivery:** ships through the release gate; :3070 currently serves a pre-2026-10-12 build. Verify on staging :3170.\n\n## Verification\n\nExtend the existing suites: agent-tools/work_items/set_blocker.test.ts and set_blocker.park.test.ts, attention/work-item-blocker-reaper.test.ts and .integration.test.ts, events/await/store.integration.test.ts, work-item-ref-blocker-auto-clear.test.ts and .integration.test.ts, work-items-durable-park-audit.test.ts, the catalogue tests. Derived from the plan's own R-6 falsifier and scenario S1, which name `release:deployed:<sha>` as THE unannounced proving key.\n\nFinding (measured 2026-10-20 ~17:25Z with a scratch probe of fireCertifiesCondition at the P-001 head): `release:deployed:abc123def` certified false both unannounced and announced. Cause: the deploy family's `<sha>` param is optional, so deriveSubjectScope returns 'global'; bindsConcreteSubject requires 'id', and P-001's fireProves applies only to id-scoped families. As P-001 left it, R-6 could not pass as written.\n\nRuling: the `deploy` catalogue entry (events/await/catalog.ts) carries an explicit `subjectScope: 'id'` override (the derivation cannot express 'optionally id-scoped') and `fireProves: 'condition'` (a fire certifies that this sha landed on :3070; a later deploy does not undo that). The bare `release:deployed` still binds nothing (bindsConcreteSubject refuses the bare prefix), so only the per-sha key releases waits. The P-001 pin table in catalog.test.ts gains `deploy: 'condition'`.\n\nNot changed: `release:green:<harness>` stays a non-proving (scope) key. The wait leg is `resolveDependencyGraphWaits` in packages/operator-core/lib/sync-resolver/dependency-graph-edges.ts, beside `resolveDependencyGraphEdges`, served as a SIBLING sync query `workItems.depWaits`. depEdges keeps its contract that every row is a `blocks` edge; its consumers (integrity findings, depth) never see event endpoints. The model (apps/operator/app/adv/harnesses/dep-graph-model.ts) keeps waits out of depth and integrity.\n2. Waits shown: session events:await rows bound to an item (bound_to.kind work-item-claim | work-item-blocked, ANY subscriber, so a contender parked on claim:released:<id> shows too), the holder's other non-inbox-wake awaits (derive-awaiting.ts Leg 1 exclusions; capped 3 per holder, 600 rows overall, newest items first), and the item's own active event/gate blockers. A capped leg stamps legTruncated and the pane says so.\n3. stale = subscriber sessionState ended|suspect from the shared liveness oracle (resolveSessionStates), or the await expired unfired. A liveness failure or 3 s overrun reads as not measured (null), never alive.\n4. Invalidation: work_items bridge for blockers/claims; event_awaits had NO notify trigger, so migration 1546 adds one with a row-level WHEN that skips coord:inbox-wake rows (measured 32 non-inbox creates/hour).\n5. R-19 is timed over depEdges + depWaits together, as the pane loads them. Its falsifier text names resolveDependencyGraphEdges; the as-built wording fix goes through WI-6554700010018330's rubric amend.\n\nMeasured 2026-10-21 06:58-07:00Z on live papercusp (build tree, scratch .papercusp/scratch/ews/p009/time-r19*.log): holder cap 1500 gave 2,351 rows / 1.6 MB with 1,185 stale; cap 600 gives 1,451 rows / 985 KB, edges+waits max 1,062 ms vs the 10 s deadline.\n\n### D-008 — One release predicate on every path: announced settlement certifies too (R-1 keeps rev-3 wording; R-7 method and S4 example change)\nDate: 2026-10-21\nSource: [self-imposed] su-42565716 (plan builder), enforcing owner ruling D-001 item 3 [owner:Avi 2026-10-20, directive #2036]. Triggered by the outside-lineage amend review conv-mvhydkn6 (su-0416b1d6, thread-post:1192934), which objected to amend preview thread-post:1192929.\n\nFinding (measured 2026-10-21 10:20-10:40Z): the announced blocker settlement (events/await/store.ts settleWaitsOnFiredKey with announced:true, and retireAnnouncement) called reconcileEventExternalBlockers with no fireCertifiesCondition check. A producer announcing work-item:status:<id> would therefore clear blockers on it on fire or retirement. That contradicts D-001 item 3, which has no announced carve-out. Durable parks (reconcileEventDurableParks) and write-time admission (wait-ref-admission.ts via readEventConditionReachability requireSpecificCondition) already applied fireCertifiesCondition(key, producerDeclared). Probe .papercusp/scratch/ews/amend/certify-probe.mts, announced: fleet:<slug>:<gate> true, gate:<x> true, work-item:done:<id> true, release:deployed:<sha> true; release:green:papercusp false (broad), work-item:status:<id> false (change-notification), git-sync:committed false (broad).\n\nRuling:\n1. Every releasing path applies fireCertifiesCondition(key, producerDeclared). store.ts gains reconcileCertifiedEventBlockers, used by settleWaitsOnFiredKey and retireAnnouncement. reconcileEventExternalBlockers (work-items.ts) is not given the import, because that would load the event store into every work-items consumer.\n2. Supersedes the 'Not changed' paragraph of D-005: the announced path no longer settles without a certification check. release:green:<harness> stays a non-proving (broad) key. A blocker on it is refused at write time (P-006) and is not settled even when the key is announced.\n3. R-1 keeps its rev-3 wording; the r4 narrowing to unannounced keys is withdrawn. R-7's model stands, but its method and driftMarkers change: they name an announced fleet gate and the shared predicate instead of 'settles without a certification check' and release:green:<harness>. S4's example key changes from release:green:papercusp to an announced fleet gate (fleet:<slug>:<gate>, the key events:emit { announce:true } returns).\n4. Tests: store.integration.test.ts gains two AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-004 cases (an announced fire, and retirement of an announced gate) plus a broad-key pin. The AUTO-BAR-R-7-P-004 case moves to fleet:ews-p004:release-ready.\n\nNot changed: D-001 itself. This decision enforces it on the one path that skipped it.\n\nMeasured: before the fix, store.integration.test.ts with the two new R-1 cases and R-7 still on release:green:papercusp failed 3 of 123 (testing:run 253d03e3: R-7 'expected blocked to be open'; both new R-1 cases saw a follow-up call, an assertion corrected to followUp.calls.flat()). After the fix and the R-7 key move: npm run test:file store.integration.test.ts EXIT=0 (.papercusp/scratch/ews/amend/store-int-run1.log, 10:27Z); engine.test.ts exit 0 and cancel.test.ts exit 0 (.papercusp/scratch/ews/amend/related-run1/summary.txt). Code: store.ts reconcileCertifiedEventBlockers beside settleWaitsOnFiredKey; the retireAnnouncement call site.\n\n### D-009 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-4db85e63878830ded536a24d\nRequest-Hash: efbab7ccfe21316ac4f44d91674e6d299e27115ab2ca984495583375bb7aff08\nActor: su-42565716-6d11-4087-93d3-1b2b0d5ded7b\nReason: As-built amend (WI-6554700010018330; D-008). Test titles are bound in full at the re-proof binding, not here.\nApproved-By: su-e97ab3d3-5f93-49e1-b8f8-32bdf263eb08\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1192949\nApproved-At: 2026-10-21T10:30:43.057Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 49 → 50\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-7, R-11, R-20\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-7, R-11, R-20\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plan-class-general","title":"Plan class: general (shared acceptance invariants)","status":"active","created":"2026-10-20","owner":"first-party-bundle","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Plan class: general (shared acceptance invariants)\nslug: plan-class-general\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-20\nupdated: 2026-10-20\nowner: first-party-bundle\n---\n\n# Plan class: general (shared acceptance invariants)\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Status\n`active` ⇒ a active rubric.\n\n**Next:** An independent reviewer (or the owner/su) ratifies a proposed rubric by promoting\nthis plan to `active` (rubrics:ratify / plans:set-plan-status); the proposer cannot\nself-ratify. Revise the criteria via plans:set-template-data.\n\n## Background\n\nThe CLASS rubric general plans' acceptance rubrics reference (plan-verification-profiles-2026-10-17 D-003: the general verification profile maps to this class, with investigation as a general sub-class). A general plan delivers documents, decisions, research, operations or artifacts rather than code; it is done when each deliverable is durable, current and fit for the request. Independent grading stays mandatory (D-002). Graded at plan completion by a NON-implementer.\n\n## Criteria — the structured `template_data`\n\nThe per-criterion model / method / drift markers live in `template_data` (read via\nrubrics:get or plans:get-template-data). Agents read/write the rubric structured, never\nby parsing this markdown.\n\n## Decisions\n\n(Use plans:add-decision to append.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plan-item-code-anchors-2026-10-20","title":"Ground plan items in the code: anchors that flow to work items, and research that is not redone","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-20","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Ground plan items in the code: anchors that flow to work items, and research that is not redone\nslug: plan-item-code-anchors-2026-10-20\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-20\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-22, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_proof_missing, bar_snapshot_evidence_plane_unmet, bar_snapshot_clause_not_accepted, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing. Next repair: Vet the current acceptance-rubric criteria BEFORE binding proof or emitting adequacy cards (amend → vet → attest → bind → cards → grade): a vetting critique usually becomes an amendment, and proof bound first must then be re-bound.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nAvi approved continuing the remaining implementation in this session on staging/current-build (D-015). P-002 guidance and P-004 anchor resolution/storage are implemented and undergoing evidence certification. Final promotion and shipment remain release-gated; no LIVE_GATE_OPS takeover.\n\n**Next:** Finish clean-source evidence and closure for P-002/P-004, then continue the approved dependency order and P-010 research-overlap measurement.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018279 — Diagnose and fix why code-intelligence pushes fire about 19 times a week (R-1). Per leg (grep, first-touch, interface, intent): eligibility rules, serving build, Claude vs Codex hook coverage, snapsh… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018280 — One guidance line in `plans:new` / `plans:add-item` tool guidance and the planner, scoper and architect role prompts: before writing an item, run `graph:query` impact on the symbols it changes and pa… <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018281 — Decide anchor storage and identity by Decision: a `plan_item_anchors` table vs a jsonb column on `harness_shared.plan_items`; symbol identity + content hash + path, recorded consumers and tests; how … <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018282 — `plans:add-item` and the item-edit verb accept `anchors: [{ symbol } | { path }]`, resolve them through the first-party snapshot/LSP, store identity, hash, consumers and tests, and keep unresolved an… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018283 — Stale-anchor check: a bounded sweep (declared as a routine, not a raw timer) re-hashes anchored symbols, marks moved or missing ones stale on the plan item using the memory-anchor freshness model, an… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018284 — Promotion copies anchors: extend `WorkItemCreateSpec` (`packages/operator-core/lib/plan-workitem-promotion.ts`) and its wiring (`plan-workitem-promotion-run.ts`) so each work item gets `payload.paths… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018285 — Resync on anchor edit: editing a plan item's anchors rewrites `payload.paths` / `payload.anchors` on open linked work items through both linkage mechanisms (`payload.plan_item` and `source_plan_item_… <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018286 — Claim-time code-intelligence brief from the exact linked functions (D-003): when a work item carries `payload.anchors`, `code-intelligence/task-brief.ts` automatically runs code intelligence starting… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018287 — Completion advisory: `work_items:complete` (`agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts`) compares anchored files with `filesChanged` and names unplanned and untouched files as advice, never a refusal. Work … <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018288 — Measure before building: on 3 recently authored code plans, compare what the author read, grepped and queried (transcript, `tool_invocations`, `code_intel_pushes`) with what the plan cited. Record pr… <!-- P-010 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018289 — Record the trail: the PostToolBatch push channel stores per-session Read and Grep subjects (files, resolved symbols) beside `code_intel_pushes`, with bounded retention. Verify the Codex seam; if Code… <!-- P-011 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018290 — Suggest anchors: `plans:new` and `plans:add-item` return ranked suggested anchors from the calling session's trail only, never another session's (a session is the caller's coord owner id, which survi… <!-- P-012 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018291 — Extend `code-intelligence/native-adoption.ts` with five metrics over the populations of report rpt_63d990a4: the share of plan items with anchors among plan items updated in the last 30 days (baselin… <!-- P-013 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018292 — Post-ship reading: with `plans:set-schedule`, re-run the adoption measurement 7 days after P-001 is deployed, reading grep and first-touch pushes per recorded search or first file read for the 7 days… <!-- P-014 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Agents who write plans, agents who carry plan items to done, and Avi reviewing plans.\n\n**Problem.** Measured 2026-10-20 (report rpt_63d990a4-f093-4bd4-be75-19810cae5a0e, WI-6554700010018079):\n- Only 609 of 6,431 plan items updated in the last 30 days (9.5%) name any source file; 130 (2.0%) name a file and line.\n- Only 165 of 2,149 work items created from plans in the last 30 days (7.7%) carry `payload.paths`. Promotion copies just the item text and the plan link (`WorkItemCreateSpec` in `packages/operator-core/lib/plan-workitem-promotion.ts`); paths appear only when the text happens to contain them (`_derive-paths.ts` fallback in `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/_create-core.ts`).\n- Everything code-aware downstream reads that one list, so it sits idle for ~92% of plan work: the claim-time task brief returns nothing without paths (`getClaimTimeTaskBrief`, `packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/task-brief.ts`); scheduler affinity and claim matching (`scheduler/claim-spec-match.ts`, `scheduler/claim-spec-store.ts`); sibling-overlap and stale-path warnings at claim (`sibling-path-overlap-claim-port.ts`, `stale-path-hints-claim-port.ts`); the completion path check (`agent-tools/work_items/complete.ts`).\n- Agents research with grep, not code intelligence: `graph:query` 4 calls and `lsp:query` 5 in 3 days vs 7,655 `capability:bash`. The automatic pushes built under native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09#D-016 delivered only 19 times in 7 days (`code_intel_pushes`: 13 grep, 5 first-touch, 1 interface).\n- Code grounding happens only at ship time (`plans:audit` code-truth citations, spec evidence fingerprints), after the work is built.\n\n**Outcome.** A plan item lists the functions or files it will change, resolved by code intelligence to a stable identity. When the plan starts, that list becomes the work item's file list, stays in sync if the plan item changes, and drives the claim-time briefing. Research the planner already did is offered back as suggestions, not redone.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- No new code index or graph; reuse the first-party snapshot and LSP surfaces.\n- No line-number anchors; they break on the first edit.\n- Anchors are never auto-filled from research; they are suggestions the author keeps or drops.\n- Does not replace the ship-time `plans:audit` code-truth check.\n- Does not touch the GitNexus keep/retire decision (native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09#P-042).\n- Anchors are not mandatory for non-code plans.\n\n**Source turns.** Owner directive #2021 (questions 1-3: code intelligence in research; grounding plans in code; filling links and saving research). Owner directive #2033 (how links flow from plan item to work item). AskUserQuestion answer 2026-10-20: \"Yes, new plan (Recommended)\".\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. A planner adds an item \"make lock expiry configurable\" and names `acquireLock`. The tool resolves it, records its 6 callers and 3 tests, and stores the anchor. The planner never types a path.\n2. The plan starts. The work item for that item has `acquireLock`'s file in its list. The agent that claims it gets the code briefing: consumers, tests that reach them, live locks on consumer files.\n3. Two weeks later someone renames `acquireLock` before the item is claimed. The plan item shows a stale-anchor warning, and the open work item's holder is told.\n4. At claim, the briefing says \"since this was planned, 2 new callers appeared\".\n5. At completion, the agent changed a file nobody planned. The completion carries an advisory naming it; it is not refused.\n6. A planner spent 20 minutes grepping and reading. When they call `plans:add-item`, the tool lists the functions they looked at as suggested anchors; they keep two and drop the rest.\n\n**Assumptions.** The first-party snapshot resolves TypeScript symbols well enough for anchors (native-code-intelligence P-040 targets p50 < 1 s). Codex sessions have a hook seam comparable to Claude's PostToolBatch for the research trail; P-011 verifies this.\n\n**Open choices for Avi.**\n- Should anchors be required on items of code plans (a lint refusal) or optional with a warning? Draft default: optional with a warning, revisit after P-013 measures uptake.\n- Phase 4 (research suggestions) is gated on P-010's measurement. If research and final anchors barely overlap, Phase 4 is dropped.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — The cause of rare code-intelligence pushes is fixed and pinned by a regression test.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Find and fix why grep and first-touch pushes reach agents so rarely, so research gets code-intelligence answers without asking.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2021\"],\"rationale\":\"Push-channel fixtures already deliver pushes, so a fixture pass cannot show the production cause is fixed. This bar pins the diagnosed cause; R-9 measures the production effect. The grep and first-touch legs are in scope; the interface and intent legs are diagnosed and reported in the Decision but not barred. If the cause is a missing client seam, the regression case exercises the new seam and fails on the pre-fix code because the seam is absent.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The push-channel regression case for the cause named in P-001's Decision passes on the fixed code and fails on the pre-fix code.\",\"falsifier\":\"P-001 records no Decision naming the cause and the pre-fix commit, or the named regression case passes on the pre-fix code or fails on the fixed code.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-001\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the 'push delivery regression (P-001 Decision)' describe in push-channel.integration.test.ts on the fixed code, then against the pre-fix commit with scripts/mutation-probe.sh --against-commit, and read the P-001 Decision for the named cause.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/push-channel.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Plan items carry resolved code anchors.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Let a plan item name the symbols or files it changes and store them as resolved identities with content hashes, recorded consumers and reaching tests.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2021\"],\"rationale\":\"Code links are the source of truth every later bar reads. The bar grades symbol links; file links, unresolvable links, link edits and the no-links warning (D-002) are SPEC-P-004-PATH, SPEC-P-004-UNRESOLVED, SPEC-P-004-EDIT and SPEC-P-004-NOLINK-WARN. How links render in the plan viewer is UI and deliberately not barred.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Adding a plan item with a symbol code link stores the symbol's resolved identity, content hash, file, callers and reaching tests, readable through plans:get.\",\"falsifier\":\"A symbol link is stored as free text or a line number, silently dropped, or stored without its resolved identity, content hash, file, callers or reaching tests.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-004\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the 'plan item anchors' describes in item-anchors.test.ts (unit, injected CodeIntelAnswer resolver) and item-anchors.integration.test.ts (first-party snapshot over a fixture repository and the migrated schema), and read the item through plans:get.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/item-anchors.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/item-anchors.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Work items inherit plan-item anchors and stay in sync.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Copy a plan item's anchors onto the work item it becomes, and keep open work items in sync when the anchors change.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2033\"],\"rationale\":\"Directive 2033 asks that work items carry the plan item's code. Copying into payload.paths leaves the existing readers unchanged; resync and the holder notice keep the copy from drifting. The bar is joint: P-006's share is SPEC-P-006 and its boundaries (copy at promotion, stored code links, text fallback), P-007's share is SPEC-P-007 and its boundaries (resync, notice, closed items).\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every open work item created from a plan item carries that plan item's current linked files.\",\"falsifier\":\"A work item started from a linked plan item lacks its linked files or code links, a link edit leaves an open linked work item's file list stale or its holder unnotified, or a closed work item is rewritten.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-006\",\"P-007\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the 'promotion copies anchors' describe in plan-workitem-promotion-run.integration.test.ts and the resync, holder-notice and closed-item cases in plan-items/anchor-resync.integration.test.ts on a fixture plan.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/plan-workitem-promotion-run.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/plan-items/anchor-resync.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Stale code links are surfaced on the plan item.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Warn when anchored code changes or disappears before the work is done, and tell the claimant when consumers changed since planning.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2021\"],\"rationale\":\"A stale link misleads the claimant more than no link. The sweep compares a whitespace-normalized hash so formatting edits raise no noise. That it runs as a declared routine, raises one recorded notice per plan and leaves done items alone are SPEC-P-005-ROUTINE, SPEC-P-005-NOTICE, SPEC-P-005-RECORD and SPEC-P-005-TERMINAL. File links are not swept by this plan.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Editing, renaming or removing a linked symbol before the work is done marks that plan item's link stale at the next freshness sweep.\",\"falsifier\":\"A plan item whose linked symbol was edited, renamed or deleted still shows the link as current after a freshness sweep, or a whitespace-only edit marks a link stale.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-005\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run plan-items/anchor-freshness.test.ts: the edit, rename, delete and whitespace-only cases.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/plan-items/anchor-freshness.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Completion compares planned code with changed code.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"At work-item completion, compare the anchored files with the files actually changed and report the difference as advice.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2021\"],\"rationale\":\"The advisory shows the reviewer where planned and actual work diverged without blocking completion. Only work items with code links get it, because text-derived file lists are guesses.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A completion that changes an unanchored file or leaves an anchored file untouched returns an advisory naming each, and the completion still succeeds.\",\"falsifier\":\"The difference goes unreported, the advisory refuses the completion, or a work item without code links gets the advisory.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-009\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the 'completion anchor advisory' describe in work_items/complete.test.ts, which compares linked files with completion.filesChanged; its cases fail on the code before this plan.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/work_items/complete.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Research becomes suggested anchors, never automatic ones.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Record what an agent researched in a session and offer it as suggested anchors when the agent writes plan items, so research is not redone.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2021\"],\"rationale\":\"Directive 2021 asks that research is not redone. Suggestions are never stored without the author's choice. The bar is joint: P-011's share is SPEC-P-011 (the trail is recorded), P-012's share is SPEC-P-012 and its boundaries. This bar holds only if P-010's Decision keeps P-011 and P-012; if that Decision drops them, R-6 is retired by a rubric amendment citing it. Suggestion ranking and trail retention are not barred.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"After a fixture session reads files and searches for symbols, plans:add-item from that session returns those files and symbols as suggestions, and stores none of them unless the caller passes them as anchors.\",\"falsifier\":\"Researched code is not suggested, a suggestion is stored as an anchor without the caller choosing it, or a session without a recorded trail gets an empty suggestion list with no reason.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-011\",\"P-012\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the research-trail integration tests (a fixture session reads files and searches for symbols, then calls plans:add-item) and the suggested-anchors unit tests for plans:new and plans:add-item, including the trail-unavailable and other-session cases.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/research-trail.integration.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/suggested-anchors.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — The adoption measurement counts the baseline population.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Measure whether plans and work items actually carry code links and whether claim briefings fire, against the baseline in report rpt_63d990a4.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2021\"],\"rationale\":\"The effect can only be compared with report rpt_63d990a4 if the measurement counts that report's populations: plan items updated in the last 30 days, and work items created from plans in the last 30 days excluding observations. Claim-brief records (written by P-008) count for work items in that population, stale-link notices (written by P-005) for its plans, and pushes per leg by push time within the window. Stale-link alert precision has no labelled truth, so the measurement reports a notice count instead. The production reading is R-9.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Over fixture rows that include rows outside each metric's population, the adoption measurement reports linked plan-item share, plan-born work items with file lists, claim briefs delivered and skipped, pushes per leg and stale-link notices from in-population rows only.\",\"falsifier\":\"A metric is missing or differs from the fixture's known value, or it counts a plan item not updated in the 30-day window, a work item outside the window, not created from a plan or an observation, a claim-brief record or stale-link notice outside that population, or a push from another leg in a leg's count.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-013\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the 'plan item anchor adoption' describe in native-adoption.test.ts over a fixture that includes out-of-population rows for every metric.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/native-adoption.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — The claim brief runs code intelligence from the exact linked functions.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"At claim time, automatically enrich the work item's brief with code intelligence starting from the exact functions it changes, so the agent does not have to research them by hand.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2041\"],\"rationale\":\"Directive 2041 asks that the claim brief uses code intelligence automatically. Starting from the linked functions keeps the brief on topic. The bar grades the brief contents; the budget cut, the unchanged no-links brief and the brief records are SPEC-P-008-BUDGET, SPEC-P-008-NOLINKS and SPEC-P-008-RECORD.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Claiming a work item linked to one of two functions in a fixture file returns a brief listing that function's callers, reaching tests, affected files, anchored docs, dependent spec requirements, consumer-file locks and callers added since planning, and none of the other function's callers.\",\"falsifier\":\"The brief omits a fixture caller, reaching test, affected file, anchored doc, dependent spec requirement, consumer-file lock or post-planning caller, or lists a caller of the unlinked function.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-008\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the 'claim brief from linked functions' describe in task-brief.test.ts and task-brief-anchors.integration.test.ts over a fixture repository with linked functions, docs, spec evidence and held locks.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/task-brief.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/task-brief-anchors.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Grep and first-touch pushes per search or file read rise after the fix ships.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Make sure the push fix reaches agents in production: more grep and first-touch pushes per search or first file read in the week after it ships than in the week before.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2021\"],\"rationale\":\"A fixture pass cannot show production delivery. Raw push counts move with fleet activity, so this bar compares rates: grep and first-touch pushes (D-006) per search or first file read recorded in agent_activity, for the 7 days before and after the P-001 deploy. Interface and intent pushes are not counted. A search is a Bash grep or rg command that classifyShellLookup in native-adoption.ts classifies as a symbol lookup; a first file read is the first Read of a path in a session within the window. The bar needs at least 100 searches and first file reads in each window and a post-deploy rate at least twice the pre-deploy rate, so noise cannot pass it (D-009). The report states both rates and their counts. P-014's 14-day reading after Phase 3 is reported, not barred.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"In the 7 days after the P-001 deploy, grep and first-touch pushes per recorded search or first file read are at least twice the same rate for the 7 days before it, with at least 100 searches and first file reads in each window, read by one query recorded in a report.\",\"falsifier\":\"The post-deploy rate is below twice the pre-deploy rate, either window has fewer than 100 searches and first file reads, the reading counts interface or intent pushes or searches that classifyShellLookup does not classify as symbol lookups, its windows do not meet at the deploy time recorded with the deployed commit, or no report records both rates with their counts and query.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredScope\":[\"P-014\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the P-014 report: grep and first-touch pushes, recorded searches and first file reads, and the resulting rates for the 7 days before and after the P-001 deploy, with the deployed commit, the deploy time, the classifyShellLookup rule and the query that produced them.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"}}}\n```\n\n## Conformance\n\n```conformance\n{\"requirements\":{\"R-9\":{\"violatedWhen\":[{\"id\":\"post-deploy-push-rate\",\"failureMode\":\"Grep and first-touch pushes per recorded search or first file read in the 7 days after the P-001 deploy are below twice the rate for the 7 days before it, or either window has fewer than 100 searches and first file reads.\",\"stage\":\"operation\",\"pendingBinding\":{\"observation\":\"The adoption measurement reports a grep and first-touch push rate for the 7 days after the P-001 deploy below twice the rate for the 7 days before it.\",\"bindWhen\":\"P-013 lands the per-leg push rate in the adoption measurement; P-014 then binds it as the runnable check.\"}}]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\n\nReuse, not a parallel system:\n\n| Need | Existing surface |\n|---|---|\n| Symbol identity and content hash | `CodeIntelAnswer` contract, `packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/contracts.ts` (native-code-intelligence P-003) |\n| Consumers and reaching tests | `graph:query` impact / callers, `task-brief.ts` |\n| Freshness model for anchors | `harness_shared.memory_anchors` (`last_checked_at`, `last_check_ok`) |\n| Where the work item reads files | `payload.paths` (all readers listed under Problem) |\n| Telling the holder when a plan item changes | `packages/operator-core/lib/plan-items/text-drift-report.ts`, both linkage mechanisms |\n| Research trail | `tool_invocations`, `code_intel_pushes`, the PostToolBatch push channel (`code-intelligence/push-channel.ts`) |\n| Measurement | `code-intelligence/native-adoption.ts` |\n\nFlow: plan item anchors (source of truth) → promotion copies files into `payload.paths` and anchors into `payload.anchors` → anchor edits resync open linked work items and notify holders → claim brief runs code intelligence from the anchored functions (callers, reaching tests, impact, anchored docs, dependent spec requirements, consumer-file locks) and shows the delta since planning (D-003) → completion compares planned and changed files. The work item's copy is derived, never hand-edited.\n\nWhy copy rather than resolve through the link at read time: about seven readers already consume `payload.paths`; copying changes one seam (promotion) instead of every reader. Automatic resync (P-007) removes the usual drift risk of a copy.\n\nCoordination: native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09#P-041 (WI-6554700010016419, wip) measures push outcomes; P-001 here fixes delivery. P-001 reuses its instrument and does not duplicate it.\n\nNot barred on purpose: how links render in the plan viewer, and suggestion ranking.
