Plan not started; no implementation evidence exists.\nApproved-By: su-78f73f1e-885b-4e82-8e24-79d3fe733816\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1191915\nApproved-At: 2026-10-20T16:12:16.307Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 54 → 55\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-008 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: amend-b9f9b6024b9fb88a0fc2040c\nRequest-Hash: 0fb36a1935070be0432a787557b8252860ce86169bb18e5639d717e1622625f7\nActor: su-fdb30ece-9d04-4520-b353-459fdab74c4b\nReason: Amend #4 (plan v73): adopt both rev-4 bar critiques (posts 1191946, 1191941). R-9 could pass with no fix because it counted all pushes, so a busy week or more interface/intent pushes would lift it. It now compares grep and first-touch pushes per recorded search or first file read for the 7 days before and after the P-001 deploy, with the windows meeting at the recorded deploy. R-7 names each metric population from report rpt_63d990a4 and the writers P-008 and P-005 now own. R-8 grades only the brief contents (budget, no-links and records are SPEC clauses). R-2 grades symbol links only. R-4 drops its architectural routine leg. R-1 requires the pre-fix commit in the Decision. R-3 and R-6 state their per-item SPEC split. Plan not started; no implementation evidence exists.\nApproved-By: su-b2d802f0-a37d-4f82-a26c-00130624236e\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1191978\nApproved-At: 2026-10-20T16:47:44.636Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 73 → 74\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-009 — Adopt the round-4 bar critiques before plans:start (amend #5)\nDate: 2026-10-20\nContext: two outside-lineage bar critiques of rubric revision 5 (conv-request-8c458669 post 1192000, conv-request-707512c0 post 1192001). The first critic could read only 6 of 69 clauses (server truncation); its R-2 path, R-3 split, R-4 routine and R-8 named-check points are already met by SPEC-P-004-PATH, the per-item SPEC split, SPEC-P-005-ROUTINE and SPEC-P-008-BUDGET/-NOLINKS/-RECORD.\n\nRulings:\n1. R-9 denominator: a search is a Bash grep or rg command that classifyShellLookup (code-intelligence/native-adoption.ts) classifies as a symbol lookup; agent_activity records no Grep tool rows, so counting tool names gives zero or every Bash call. A first file read is the first Read of a path in a session within the window.\n2. R-9 floor: the bar needs at least 100 searches and first file reads in each window and a post-deploy rate at least twice the pre-deploy rate. A strict increase with no floor passes on one extra push. Twice is a floor, not a target: the baseline is about 22 grep and first-touch pushes a week against thousands of eligible events, so a working fix should exceed it by far more.\n3. P-013 is blocked by P-005 and P-008 so its metrics read the records those items write, not invented fixture shapes. P-014 is blocked by P-008 and P-009 because its 14-day reading starts after Phase 3 ships.\n4. P-008 records each claim brief as a code_intel_pushes row with leg claim-brief (reused ledger); the stale-link notice record lives with the anchor storage P-003 decides (declared as a new surface).\n5. A session for anchor suggestions (P-012) is the caller's coord owner id, which survives a carry-respawn. A client with no trail seam gets 'trail not captured for this client'; a session that recorded nothing gets 'nothing recorded'.\n6. The plan's audience for stale-link notices (P-005) is the @plan:<slug> selector plus holders of open linked work items.\n7. Anchor resolution over its time budget stores the link as unknown with reason timeout (P-004). Promotion and task-brief share one exported anchor type (P-006, P-008). The no-links golden comes from deterministic fixture inputs; removed callers are reported but not graded (P-008).\n8. P-014 saves the pre-deploy counts at the P-001 deploy and keeps only the legs grep and first-touch (reviewer notes on thread-post:1191978).\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAmendment-Id: amend-1c1509e80109a0028619cac2\nRequest-Hash: 6e8df7b0c70fad0b48913c72e6e921e190c2ec4a7a9cfee164cebd979b5eef94\nActor: su-fdb30ece-9d04-4520-b353-459fdab74c4b\nReason: Amend #5 (plan v93, D-009): adopt the round-4 bar critiques of revision 5 (conv-request-8c458669 post 1192000, conv-request-707512c0 post 1192001). Only R-9 changes. Its denominator was undefined: agent_activity records no Grep tool rows, so a search is now a Bash grep or rg command that classifyShellLookup classifies as a symbol lookup, and a first file read is the first Read of a path in a session. A strict increase with no floor passed on one extra push, so R-9 now needs at least 100 searches and first file reads in each window and a post-deploy rate at least twice the pre-deploy rate. The other findings are SPEC clause, dependency and declaration changes recorded in D-009. Plan not started; no implementation evidence exists.\nApproved-By: su-2cad6a9c-7e4d-4a85-b4ef-4c292cd53cec\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1192046\nApproved-At: 2026-10-20T17:45:09.858Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 93 → 94\nChanged BARs: R-9\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-011 — Owner dispatches P-001 and P-003 past the papercusp stop-the-line\nDate: 2026-10-20\nSource: [owner:Avi 2026-10-20, interactive AskUserQuestion answer 'Dispatch P-001 + P-003 now'] [turn:b8ae7a08@2026-10-20T20:29:11.507Z].\n\nContext: plans:start promoted all 14 items but could not move the plan to active. The papercusp release gate has gone about 439h without a green (gate-red-streak:papercusp condition WI-10006055, held by su-290e7a2d), and the stop-the-line floor holds back non-repair work from self-select. Only a leader or the owner may dispatch items by id past it.\n\nRuling: the owner dispatches P-001 (diagnose and fix the low push rate) and P-003 (anchor storage) to the authoring su session by id, to start now. The other 12 items wait for the gate to green; then plans:start moves the plan to active. This does not touch the release gate or its repair lane.\n\n### D-012 — P-001 root cause: a workspace package.json pinned by full content suppressed pushes; pin it by name\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nSource: [self, su-fdb30ece] measured diagnosis for P-001 (WI-6554700010018279). Not an owner ruling; owner dispatch is D-011.\n\nCause (measured). corroboratePushSources (packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/push-snapshot.ts), the per-fact gate in codeIntelPushText, rejects a fact when any proof source's sha256 differs from disk. The symbol-snapshot producer (scripts/lib/code-intel-symbol-snapshot.mjs) added each workspace's package.json as a FULL-CONTENT proof source to every symbol defined or called in that workspace. Any manifest edit (a script, a version, a dependency) therefore suppressed every push for the package. Distinguishing test, same code + same snapshot 9320948fc411: while packages/operator-core/package.json was an uncommitted rewrite (its only mismatch), all 6 operator-core subjects failed corroboration and the grep leg pushed 0 chars; after the file returned to HEAD the same pipeline pushed 572 chars. Producer hashing was correct (recorded == committed); the proof's breadth was the defect.\n\nRuling. A workspace manifest proof pins only `name`, the one field the resolver reads (workspacePackagesFrom in scripts/gen-graph-dependency-snapshot.mjs maps name -> dir; bare specifiers resolve through that dir via baseCandidates, never main/exports/types). Encoded as digest 'package-name-v1' in packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/proof-digest.ts, one definition shared by producer and consumer. Unknown digests fail closed. queryPushSnapshot still reports a true full-source contentHash in supportingFiles (the content it corroborated). An unparseable manifest keeps a full-content pin. Snapshots written before the fix keep full-content pinning until the gitnexus-reindex routine regenerates them (45 min).\n\nPre-fix commits: producer 0d9a54a71c76d9ee38a9b775ccb7477cf28940f0; consumer push-snapshot.ts 500d627fa9edd3f68dfb0555bd862c8734e9b021; push-channel.ts d6b55bdf2722876e1e5172b9aaa3f163463405f8.\n\nRegression guard: push-channel.test.ts 'pins a workspace manifest by its name only, so unrelated package.json edits keep the push' (real producer + codeIntelPushText), plus push-snapshot-query.test.ts P-001 case for the query path. Falsified with scripts/mutation-probe.sh, overlay relocation, reverting manifestProof to the pre-fix full-content pin: verdict=caught, baseline test_runs:21457728 pass, mutant test_runs:21457733 fail ('expected false to be true' at the post-edit corroboration). Descriptor reader was :3170 (PAPERCUSP_MUTATION_DESCRIPTOR_READER_HEALTH_URL) because :3070's d740fc3802 predates the descriptor parser; P-001's close is evaluated on :3170 to match.\n\nOut of R-1's fix (still open): push-channel.ts and push-snapshot.ts are absent from deployed main d740fc3802, so hooks served by :3070 cannot push until the papercusp gate goes green (WI-10006055, held by su-290e7a2d). The per-turn ceiling CODE_INTEL_PUSH_TURN_CHARS=1500 allows about 2 pushes per long turn: a design question, reported, not in the R-1 bar. The harness-slug gate (mid-turn-context.ts) was not confirmed as a cause and needs an isolated re-test now that this fix is in.\n\n### D-013 — P-001 second cause: superuser-scope hooks sent harness '', so the push had no snapshot\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nSource: [self, su-fdb30ece] measured, for P-001 (WI-6554700010018279). Settles the open question D-012 left: 'The harness-slug gate (mid-turn-context.ts) was not confirmed as a cause and needs an isolated re-test.'\n\nCause (measured). The mid-turn hook handler (packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/agent-mcp/mid-turn-context.ts) passed raw body.harness to codeIntelPushText. Operator/superuser-scope sessions never export PAPERCUSP_HARNESS_SLUG (EI-18893248175645463), so their hook sends harness ''. The push's default snapshot dependency then returns null, and no grep or first-touch push can fire for those sessions, independent of the D-012 manifest cause.\n\nFix (WI-6554700010018438, done, commit 203fcf4ab0). resolveMidTurnHarness uses the declared harness, else the one detected from the hook's cwd (detectHarnessSlugSync), else ''. It is resolved once per request and shared by the push and the recall.\n\nProof. Route cases in mid-turn-context.test.ts drive the real handler with harness '' plus a cwd inside the tree, with a declared harness, and with neither. A copy-out mutant restoring the raw read fails the cwd case and the neither-sent case (test_runs:21469728, verdict caught); the fixed code passes 118/118 (test_runs:21469743).\n\nConsequence for P-001. P-001 has two real causes, D-012 and this one; each fix is needed on its own. Live bar R-9 (P-014) measures the combined effect.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-20 22:55Z, dev:pipeline_position { path: mid-turn-context.ts } -> servingRuntimes: release-operator d740fc3802 (role owner, the runtime that serves the hook route) containsChange=false; staging-operator 9ac8f45aaf containsChange=false; bg-host and gateway false. positions: onStaging=true, inMain=false; blockedOn=gate (WI-10006055). The fix reaches hooks only when main deploys to the release operator.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-014 — P-003: code links live in a plan_item_anchors table (not a plan_items column), keyed by snapshot symbol id + normalized content hash\nDate: 2026-10-20\nDate: 2026-10-20\nSource: [self, su-fdb30ece] design ruling for P-003 (WI-6554700010018281), owner-dispatched under D-011. SPEC-P-003 makes this Decision the deliverable; P-004's clauses test what it designs.\n\n1. Storage: a new table harness_shared.plan_item_anchors, one row per link, keyed by (workspace_id, harness_slug, plan_slug, item_id). Not a jsonb column on plan_items: writePlanIndexRows (packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/plan-index-rows.ts:108-141) deletes and re-inserts every plan_items row on each plan write, so a column there is wiped by any plan edit. No foreign key to plan_items for the same reason (a cascade would erase links on every edit). Rows whose item has left the plan are skipped by reads and the sweep (join on plan_items) and kept for audit.\n2. Reuse: memory_anchors (migration 1514) is the freshness model to copy: last_checked_at, last_check_ok and a NULLS FIRST recheck index. It is not extended, because its key is a memory uuid and it has no hash, consumers, tests or unknown reason; changing that key would touch every memory reader. ledger_anchors is unrelated (publication ledger).\n3. Columns: anchor_kind ('symbol' | 'path'); requested (the author's text, verbatim); symbol_id and symbol_name (SnapshotSymbol.id / .name); path; signature (snapshot, up to 300 chars); content_hash; consumers jsonb (snapshot callers as {path,line}, capped at 50, plus consumers_total); tests jsonb (test files among those consumers and importers, capped); resolution ('resolved' | 'unknown') with unknown_reason ('timeout' | 'not-found' | 'ambiguous' | 'no-snapshot'; D-009 ruling 7); freshness ('fresh' | 'stale' | 'missing'), stale_since, last_checked_at, last_check_ok; resolved_commit (snapshot commit); stale_notice_id; created_at, created_by. A line number is stored only as an informational column, never as identity.\n4. Identity and hash: a symbol link is identified by symbol_id, falling back to symbol_name + path. content_hash for a symbol is sha256 of its declaration text with whitespace runs collapsed to one space and trimmed, computed by P-004 from the source span. It is not the file sha256, which would mark a link stale on any edit to the file. A path link stores the file sha256 and is not swept (P-005). The sweep marks a link stale when the hash changes or the symbol moves, and missing when it no longer resolves.\n5. Notices (D-009 ruling 4): harness_shared.plan_anchor_notices, one row per raised notice: plan, raised_at, audience (@plan:<slug> plus holders of open linked work items), the anchor ids, and the coord message id. P-005 raises a notice only for stale links whose stale_notice_id is null, then stamps them; P-013 counts these rows.\n6. One exported type (D-009 ruling 7): PlanItemAnchor in packages/operator-core/lib/plan-items/anchors.ts (created by P-004). plans:get, promotion (P-006) and the task brief (P-008) all import it.\n7. Rendering: links are never written into the plan markdown; the table is canonical. plans:get returns items[].anchors, and its markdown view appends a generated line per link under the item, for example '  ↳ code: `codeIntelPushText` packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/push-channel.ts · fresh · 4 consumers · 2 tests' or '  ↳ code: `X` unknown (timeout)'. The plan writer drops lines that start with the '↳ code:' marker, so pasting a read back cannot turn rendered links into item text; P-004 tests that round trip. The plan viewer reads links through a @papercusp/sync resolver, invalidated after link writes and sweeps.\n8. Migration: P-004 allocates and arms it (node scripts/next-migration.mjs, DRAFT then --arm, R-2). P-003 ships no schema.\n\nMeasured (2026-10-20 ~23:15Z, su-fdb30ece): (a) packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/plan-index-rows.ts lines 108-141 read: an unconditional DELETE FROM harness_shared.plan_items for the plan, then INSERT ... FROM jsonb_to_recordset of the parsed items. (b) dev:pg_query describe harness_shared.memory_anchors: exactly 6 columns (memory_id uuid, kind, value, created_at, last_checked_at, last_check_ok), PK (memory_id, kind, value), index memory_anchors_recheck_idx (last_checked_at NULLS FIRST). Falsifier for (b): a describe showing a hash, consumers, tests or reason column. (c) push-snapshot.ts:45 SnapshotSymbol = { id, name, path, line, column, sha256 (whole file), signature, aliases, sources?, callers[] }, so no per-symbol body hash exists today. (d) describe '*anchor*' lists only ledger_anchor_leaves, ledger_anchor_publications, ledger_anchors, memory_anchors.\nRelated: P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-008, P-013\n\n### D-015 — Owner lifts D-011 implementation hold; continue this session on staging\nDate: 2026-10-22\nSource: [owner:Avi, interactive Codex session, 2026-10-22] In response to the self-contained question asking permission to lift D-011's hold and continue the remaining plan in this session on staging, keeping final shipment gated, Avi replied: \"I authorize you\".\n\nRuling: Supersede D-011's requirement that the remaining plan items wait for the release gate before implementation. The authoring session continues the remaining approved plan itself (D-002 route: self, no implementation fleet), using staging/current-build for implementation and non-final verification. Begin with the ready P-002, P-004 and P-010 work, then follow the existing dependency order. Final promotion and shipment still require the release gate. This authorizes dispatch of the remaining plan items by id where the stop-the-line self-selection floor otherwise holds them. It does not authorize forcing a red release or taking over another agent's LIVE_GATE_OPS.\nRelated: P-002, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010, P-011, P-012, P-013, P-014\n\n### D-016 — P-010 measured research overlap: retain optional trail suggestions; whole-session noise is not a relevance verdict\nDate: 2026-10-22\nDate: 2026-10-22\nSource: P-010 measurement saved on WI-6554700010018288, independently reconciled against source turns this continuation. This is the implementer's measured gate ruling under approved P-010, not a new owner directive.\n\nMethod: three recent non-fixture code plans. R is the distinct explicit repository paths in two hours of recorded Read/shell research, graph/LSP/search arguments and push cited_paths before plans:new. C is the paths in the saved canonical plan snapshot. Precision=|R∩C|/|R|; recall=|R∩C|/|C|. The source writers were inspected on the work item. These are literal path overlaps; they do not measure semantic relevance, causality, new proposed files, or unrecorded reads.\n\nResults (R,C,intersection; precision,recall): canonical-source-plan-route-reservation-2026-10-22: 34,3,2; 5.88%,66.67%. sidecar-forkserver-2026-10-21: 3,10,1; 33.33%,10%. loop-fire-proof-identity-2026-10-21: 23,3,1; 4.35%,33.33%. Exact path sets, record IDs, positive controls and plan hashes are on the item.\n\nSensitivity: inspected source turns session_turn:codex:01a162d2-a243-77a0-af22-0fc68a954481:3, session_turn:claude:7986a278-5448-47ed-a7f6-a34e4644ac75:10, session_turn:codex:01a15f84-7965-78c1-a785-be895aabc342:13. Restricting recorded native activity to those task-specific turns through plans:new yields respectively R=4/intersection=2 (50% precision,66.67% recall), R=1/intersection=1 (100%,10%), and no recorded native research in the final 87 seconds (precision undefined, recall 0). This narrower sensitivity excludes separate capability invocations and is not substituted for the primary sample. It shows that the low two-hour precision is sensitive to unrelated work; missing final-window activity does not prove no research.\n\nRuling: retain P-011 and P-012. There is useful positive signal, but insufficient evidence that an optional caller-session suggestion list should be dropped. No predeclared numeric cutoff exists, and choosing one after observing confounded samples would manufacture a no-go. Suggestions remain optional, caller-scoped, and never stored automatically. Preserve explicit unavailable/empty reasons, bounded retention, and manual anchor entry. This does not authorize automatic selection or claims of high suggestion recall. Do not retire R-6 on this measurement. Follow the existing P-004/P-011 dependencies before implementing P-012.\nRelated: P-010, P-011, P-012\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"plan-item-types-registry-cupboard-2026-10-20","title":"Generalize plan item types into a registry and distribute them on the Cupboard","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-20","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Generalize plan item types into a registry and distribute them on the Cupboard\nslug: plan-item-types-registry-cupboard-2026-10-20\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-20\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** [self-imposed, su-94bf93fd] 2026-10-21 18:10Z. P-001..P-006 done. P-008's e2e (item-type-cupboard-e2e.integration.test.ts) is green 6/6 and typechecks clean. Pot A publishes an item-type pack and two plan types, pot B installs and ships a typed plan through the real ship gate without force. Its close waits on P-007 (plan dependency). Two defects the e2e found are fixed: D-010 (BAR-seed rebuilds now derive item-type bars; bug WI-6554700010019322 closed) and D-011 (criteria-template verification). Mutation probes against the e2e catch both regressions. P-007 (Plans-pane UI) has a headless Tauri run 10 queued. It starts once git-sync commits a peer's verifier input, scripts/lib/committed-source-loader.mjs. P-009 (docs) is written; its close waits on a stranded grading audit that needs the emit.ts fix (EI-26603560331923072) live on :3170.\n\n**Next:** Read P-007 headless run 10 (task 0mvifdj1tkpzp64f3ps, .papercusp/scratch/su94bf/p007-headless10.log). Bind the P-007 proofs and close P-007, then close P-008. Once emit.ts is committed and on :3170, run scorecards:repair on the P-009 grading audit and close P-009. Plan acceptance then follows the runbook: plans:audit per item, rubrics:amend to as-built, vet, attest, bind, independent grade, acceptance verdict, ship.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018623 — Registry and definition schemas. Allocate the migration with the atomic allocator and add revisioned item-type and plan-type definitions. Seed today's six deliverable kinds, the coding/general profil… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018624 — Open the parser and route policy through the registry. `deliverable:` and the plan-level type accept any namespaced slug, checking grammar only. resolveVerification reads the pinned definitions, and … <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018625 — Generalize anti-escape to module sets. Lowering means the resolved module set shrinks after activation, which still needs a Decision and a fresh audit (plan-verification-profiles-2026-10-17#D-004/#D-… <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018626 — Completion fields and criteria templates. `work_items:complete` validates the item type's completion schema, inline or via a datatype reference. Activation seeds acceptance bars from the type's crite… <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018627 — Authoring tools for both definitions (define, get, list, retire) with floor, catalog and schema validation. Plans pin the plan type and item-type revisions they resolved at activation, so a later rev… <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018628 — Cupboard. Generalize the `pack` kind to carry item types and plan types (D-002). Add manifest validation at install, item-type to pack dependency resolution and `requires_plan_type` on plan templates… <!-- P-006 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018629 — Plans-pane UI: plan-type and item-type badges, the resolved checklist, and the completion form. State lives in nuqs, data comes through a sync query, and it is verified headless in Tauri. <!-- P-007 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018630 — End-to-end test. Pot A publishes an item-type pack and two plan types that both reference one shared item type. After review, pot B installs a template, which pulls in its plan type and the shared pa… <!-- P-008 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010018631 — Docs. Write an agent-insights doc on plan types, item types and packs via docs:author. Update the plan-completion runbook and the CLAUDE.md part via set-doc-part, then re-project. <!-- P-009 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Source turns:**\n  - #2016 [owner:Avi 2026-10-20]: \"Can we generalize plan item types and allow them to be distributable on the cupboard.\"\n  - #2025 [owner:Avi]: plan types versus plan item types — which one should be on the Cupboard?\n  - #2027 [owner:Avi]: \"item types should also be on the cupboard so multiple plan types can reference the same one ... a similar relationship with tools and tool packs.\"\n- **Audience:** plan authors (agents and humans) in any pot, and Cupboard publishers who want to ship a domain's way of running work, for example a legal-review, data-migration or launch plan type.\n- **Problem:** plan and item types are closed, hard-coded and split up.\n  - Item kinds are a fixed list (`DELIVERABLE_KINDS`: code, doc, decision, research, operation, artifact). Their policy only tells code from non-code.\n  - \"Plan type\" is spread across three axes: the verification profile (coding or general, a fixed list), the plan class (which picks the acceptance rubric), and the plan template (the Cupboard `plan` listing).\n  - Nothing but templates can be shared between pots.\n- **Outcome:**\n  - Item types and plan types are both registered, revisioned definitions, and both are distributable.\n  - Several plan types can reference the same item type instead of each copying its own.\n  - The six built-in kinds and today's profiles and classes keep identical verdicts as seeded first-party definitions.\n- **Non-goals:**\n  - Changing item lifecycle statuses.\n  - Weakening `plan-verification-profiles-2026-10-17#D-002` (independent grading stays mandatory) or the anti-escape rules in `#D-004`/`#D-008`.\n  - Executable code inside a type package.\n\n## Model: the same as tools and packs\n\nThis mirrors `tool-distribution-granularity-2026-06-05` D-001 to D-003, where a tool is the atom, a pack is the distribution unit, and a declarer depends on tools that the resolver maps to packs.\n\n| tools (shipped) | this plan |\n|---|---|\n| tool: the atomic capability and the dependency unit | **item type**: the atomic definition of one kind of step, its required proof and its completion fields; plans and plan types depend on it |\n| pack: the distribution unit, n≥1 tools; a single tool is an n=1 pack | **item-type pack**: n≥1 item types; a single item type is an n=1 pack |\n| blueprint `dependencies: {tools, packs, plugins}`, resolved per tool to the providing pack | **plan type**: declares the item types it uses by name; the resolver maps each to its providing pack or the built-in catalog and installs it |\n| plugin: a pack plus a runtime | a plan-type package may also define NEW item types, which become referenceable by others like any pack's |\n| template `requires_rubrics` | **plan template** (the existing `plan` listing) gains `requires_plan_type`, so installing a template pulls in its plan type and item types |\n\nOne deliberate difference from tools: an item type decides what must be proven before shipping. So:\n- references pin a revision or a compatible range;\n- a plan pins the resolved revisions at activation, so a later revision never re-grades it;\n- publishes land PENDING operator review;\n- no definition may drop the generic-core checks.\n\n## Current state (measured 2026-10-20 by su-94bf93fd)\n\n- **Item vocabulary:** `libs/generic/plan-parser/src/verification-vocabulary.ts`.\n- **Policy:** `packages/operator-core/lib/plan-verification-profile.ts` (`VERIFICATION_MODULES`, `PROFILE_DEFAULT_DELIVERABLE`, `resolveVerification`). There are 15 non-test consumers, including `plan-acceptance-gate.ts`, `plan-audits.ts`, `plan-verification-escape.ts`, the `plans/*` tools and the `work_items` spec-adequacy gate.\n- **Plan class:** `PLAN_CLASS_RUBRIC_REFS` (feature-ship, bugfix, migration, investigation, general), used by `plans/activation-class-ref.ts` and the spec-quality evaluators.\n- **Cupboard:** `packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/types.ts` has 15 `LISTING_KINDS`.\n  - `pack` is a runtime-less code-tool pack (n≥1) and `plugin` is a pack with a runtime.\n  - `plan` is a plan template that may declare `requires_rubrics`.\n  - `rubric`, `datatype` and `rule` are declarative kinds with publish and install cores. `rule` lands PENDING review.\n- **In-flight predecessor:** `plan-verification-profiles-2026-10-17` (ready). Each plan stores the plan type and item-type revisions it resolved at activation.\n4. **Parser:** the `deliverable:` keyword (plus a plan-level `type`) accepts any namespaced slug and checks grammar only. Policy moves fully into the resolver.\n5. **Resolver:**\n   - It reads the plan's pinned plan type and item types.\n   - Code-ness means \"the module set includes `code`\".\n   - An unknown type resolves to the strictest set, with a refusal that names the install.\n   - The existing shrink-only lint is extended so that nothing branches on kind literals.\n   - Anti-escape is generalized to module-set comparison.\n6. **Authoring tools:** define, get, list and retire for both definitions, with floor and schema validation.\n7. **Cupboard:**\n   - An item-type pack and a plan type, each with a manifest validated at install.\n   - Dependency resolution from item type to its providing pack, following D-002.\n   - `requires_plan_type` on plan templates.\n   - PENDING review, install receipts, provenance pinning, and co-install of referenced rubrics and datatypes.\n8. **Surfaces:**\n   - `plans:new` takes a plan type.\n   - `plans:get` and `plans:add-item` show the resolved checklist.\n   - `work_items:complete` validates the type's completion fields.\n   - The Plans pane shows type badges and the completion form (nuqs state, a sync query, verified headless in Tauri).\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-21 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-22 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-23 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-24 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-25 | P-007 | tree |\n\n## Settled choices\n\nAvi settled these choices on 2026-10-20:\n- D-001: the tools-and-packs model.\n- D-002: item types and plan types ride the existing `pack` listing kind.\n- D-003: packages are declarative-only; implementation starts after plan-verification-profiles-2026-10-17 ships; route is su-94bf93fd's own session.\n\n## Phase 1 — Build\n\n- **P-001** `done` Registry and definition schemas. Update the plan-completion runbook and the CLAUDE.md part via set-doc-part, then re-project. blocked-by: P-006 — note: ← WI-6554700010018631 completed (done)\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Item types and plan types follow the tools-and-packs model\nDate: 2026-10-20\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-20, directives #2025 and #2027] Item types also ship on the Cupboard, so that several plan types can reference the same one. The relationship mirrors tool-distribution-granularity-2026-06-05#D-001..D-003:\n- An ITEM TYPE is the atomic definition and the dependency unit, like a tool.\n- An item-type PACK (n>=1) is the distribution unit; a single item type is an n=1 pack.\n- A PLAN TYPE declares, by name, the item types it uses. The resolver maps each one to its providing pack or the built-in catalog and installs it.\n- A PLAN TEMPLATE (the existing `plan` listing) declares the plan type it requires, the same way it declares required rubrics.\n\nThe plan type unifies today's verification profile and plan class instead of adding a fourth axis. Coupling stays loose, so mixed plans still work. Difference from tools [self-imposed, safety]: item types govern ship verification. References therefore pin a revision or range, plans pin the resolved revisions at activation, publishes land PENDING review, and no definition may drop the generic-core checks. Retracts su-94bf93fd's earlier proposal of 'no standalone item-type listing'.\n\n### D-002 — Item types and plan types ride the existing `pack` listing kind\nDate: 2026-10-20\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-20, dialog answer 'Extend pack (Recommended)'] Instead of adding new listing kinds, generalize the existing Cupboard `pack` kind (a runtime-less pack, n>=1, in packages/operator-core/lib/cupboard/types.ts) so that a pack may carry tools, item types and/or plan types. Dependency resolution reuses the per-capability install path from tool-distribution-granularity-2026-06-05#D-002. [inferred, to confirm in P-006] Plan types ship inside packs too, so no separate plan-type kind is needed.\n\n### D-003 — Scope, sequencing and route\nDate: 2026-10-20\nAffects: plan-verification-profiles-2026-10-17\n[owner:Avi 2026-10-20, dialog approval of plan revision 2]\n- Packages are declarative-only: they compose existing verification modules and declarative rubric checks, with no executable code.\n- Implementation starts after plan-verification-profiles-2026-10-17 ships. Its last two items (tests and docs) were held by su-8c1d0917 and progressing at 2026-10-20 12:18Z.\n- Route: implemented by su-94bf93fd in its own session (route A); no fleet.\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-79849d204c526dc6eba4cdd3\nRequest-Hash: 13293bd9333c967f50c36f30783901c22f312f87c4001d95be82af91ef7c0bb5\nActor: su-94bf93fd-3bb5-4b0a-807f-c5a2e40017d0\nReason: Fold both pre-start bar critiques (conv-request-4038f8bb..., conv-request-214f561e...) into the BAR set, matching plan v25 requirement blocks; adds R-24 and R-25.\nApproved-By: su-141dfdcb-e2bf-4293-9009-4543af7113c9\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1192624\nApproved-At: 2026-10-21T01:57:07.915Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 25 → 26\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8, R-9, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13, R-14, R-15, R-16, R-17, R-18, R-19, R-20, R-21, R-22, R-23, R-24, R-25\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-005 — R-8 escape rows land with the items that create each route\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAffects: P-003, P-005, P-006\n[self-imposed, su-94bf93fd, implementer sequencing call under AUTO]\n\nR-8's table has six escape routes: plan-level type swap, item deliverable swap, parent via extends, retire, same-id pack install and pin edit. Only the first two exist before P-005 (extends, retire, pins) and P-006 (pack install).\n\n- P-003 delivers the shared check. Lowering means the resolved module set loses a module, judged by a pure `droppedModules(before, after)` over two resolutions; it replaces the code-only test. P-003 also wires the check into the existing chokepoints (plan content writes, including `type:` swaps; set-verification-profile; start and ship freshness), adds the generic-core floor validator (R-9) and removes the audit.ts kind branch baselined by the R-7 guard (EI-26556818458018317).\n- P-005 and P-006 call the same check from their own writes (retire, define with extends, pin edit, same-id install) and add their rows to `item-type-escape.integration.test.ts`.\n- P-003 stays wip until the full R-8 table passes; it closes after P-006.\n\nRationale: a single shrink check that every route calls; no second, route-specific copy.\n\n### D-006 — Revision pins are rows; every registry write runs the shared shrink check over unpinned activated plans\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAffects: P-005, P-006, P-003\n[self-imposed, su-94bf93fd, implementer design call under AUTO]\n\nR-14 pins and the R-8 escape routes are designed together.\n\n- Pins live in a new table `harness_shared.plan_type_pins`, one row per type a plan resolves: (workspace, harness, plan slug, kind item-type|plan-type, type id) -> revision and content hash. Parents reached via `extends` are pinned as well. Pins are written at activation and when an activated plan first references a new type (insert-if-absent, never overwritten). Only the pin tool changes an existing pin.\n- The resolver honours a pin's exact revision even after that revision is retired, so neither retire nor a newer revision re-grades an activated plan (R-14). Unpinned references resolve to the latest admitted, non-retired revision, as today.\n- Plans already activated when the migration applies are backfilled with pins to the first-party revisions they resolve. A test fixes the content hash of every built-in revision, so a built-in cannot change content without bumping its revision.\n- The registry write tools (define a new revision, retire, and in P-006 a same-id pack install) call the P-003 `droppedModules` check over every activated plan that resolves the type without a pin. This covers plans activated by a lagging build that does not pin yet. Any shrink is refused unless that plan has a recorded Decision and a fresh activation audit.\n- A pin edit (`plan-types:pin`) runs the same check against the plan being re-pinned.\n- Definitions are immutable. A trigger refuses updates to definition, type id or revision; only the retire columns may change (R-12).\n\nRationale: one shrink check at every route. With pins, the routes are inert for pinned plans by construction; the check guards the unpinned remainder and the deliberate re-pin.\n\n### D-007 — R-14's completion-schema and checklist legs land with P-004\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAffects: P-005, P-004\n\n[self-imposed, su-94bf93fd, implementer sequencing call under AUTO] R-14's verification names four checks an activated plan must keep on its pinned revision: ship, start, work_items:complete and the plans:get checklist. Two of them do not exist yet. P-004 adds the item type's completion-schema validation in work_items:complete and the checklist that plans:get renders from criteria templates, and P-004 is blocked on P-002.\n\n- P-005 delivers the pins (migration 1545, plan_type_pins, D-006) and the R-14 test packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plan-types/__tests__/revision-pinning.integration.test.ts. That test covers activation pins keyed by id, revision and content hash; the start door (checkPlanStartable), the ship door (plans:set-plan-status shipped, code_deliverable_unverified) and the completion code-ness check (readCloseDeliverablesAreNonCode, which work_items:complete calls) all staying on revision 1 after revision 2 is defined; a counterfactual plan activated after revision 2; and migration 1545's legacy backfill. Revision 2 in that test already carries a different completion schema.\n- P-004 adds two assertions to the same test file when it lands: work_items:complete validates against revision 1's completion schema, and the plans:get checklist follows revision 1's criteria template. P-004's completion schema and checklist readers must resolve through withPinnedPlanTypes, as ship, start and completion code-ness do.\n- P-005 closes once its own legs pass. R-14 is graded at plan acceptance, after P-004.\n\n### D-008 — P-006 design: type packs are packs with a declarative typePack manifest, installed by a plan-then-apply core\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAffects: P-006, P-007, P-008, P-003\n[self-imposed, su-94bf93fd, implementer design call under AUTO; extends D-002 and D-006]\n\n- Manifest. A pack's papercusp.json may carry `typePack: { itemTypes, planTypes, rubrics?, datatypes? }` with inline definitions. The definitions use the existing strict schemas (plan-types/definitions.ts), so unknown keys are refused. Check kinds must be declarative rubric-check kinds; nothing executable is accepted (D-003). Bundled rubrics and datatypes are the co-install sources.\n- Publish and review. The publish path derives `provides_item_types` and `provides_plan_types` ([{id, revision}]) from the manifest. A Worker migration stores them, plus `requires_plan_type` on plan listings. The Worker's review predicate becomes content-aware: a listing declaring item or plan types lands pending, and tool-only packs keep today's policy. At install, a manifest's types must match its listing's declarations, otherwise the install is refused. This stops a publisher skipping review by leaving the declaration out.\n- Install plan (write-free). Validate every definition (parse, floor, first-party namespace, duplicates). Refuse an item-type reference with no revision or range. Resolve each reference in order: the same pack, then the registry (built-in and installed), then Cupboard packs that declare it. A Cupboard candidate is eligible only when approved and content-pinned. Pending or unpinned candidates are never chosen; no eligible candidate, or more than one, refuses. Dependency packs are fetched and planned recursively (bounded depth) before anything is written.\n- Install apply. Rubrics are provisioned through provisionPinnedRubric (no-clobber, exact pin). Then one PG transaction upserts datatypes, writes every definition through the authoring define path with origin 'pack' and route 'install' (so the shared shrink check covers the same-id install escape row, D-005), and writes one receipt per pack. Any refusal rolls the whole transaction back.\n- Receipt. New table `harness_shared.type_pack_installations`, one row per (workspace, listing): pack name and version, listing id, commit sha, tree digest, release content hash, plus the installed definitions, rubrics, datatypes and resolved dependencies with content hashes. trigger_pack_installations does not fit: it is harness-scoped and carries a configuration lifecycle. Type packs are workspace registry entries.\n- Plan templates. A plan listing's `requires_plan_type` ({id, minRevision?, maxRevision?}) is derived at publish from the template's declared plan type. Install resolves it the same way and installs the providing pack closure before seeding. Anything pending or unresolvable refuses the whole install before any row is written.\n- Scope limit. A dependency pack reached through resolution gets its type content installed. Any tools it also provides are reported as an installable dependency, not installed (the existing advisory pattern).\n\n### D-009 — P-007 design: one server type view behind a sync query; the completion form validates through checkTypeFields\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAffects: P-007, P-008\n[self-imposed, su-94bf93fd, implementer design call under AUTO]\n\n- Server. `packages/operator-core/lib/plan-types/item-type-view.ts` resolves every item of a plan at its pinned revisions (withPinnedPlanTypes + resolveVerification, the resolver plans:get, work_items:complete and the ship gate use). Per item it returns the resolved item type, revision, builtIn, the resolved module set, the completion source and the completion JSON schema (inline, or the installed datatype's payload schema; `completionUnresolved` when the datatype is not installed), plus criteria and rubricRef. The plan-level `planType` is the declared `type:`.\n- Data. A new sync query `plans.itemTypeView { slug, harness }` serves that view. It is invalidated with the plan rows and on registry writes. plans:get stays lean: the agent-facing checklist (P-004) is unchanged.\n- Submit. `checkPlanItemTypeFields` runs `checkTypeFields` (the validation work_items:complete applies to completion.typeFields) against the item's pinned contract, behind a small admin POST route. The form shows the verdict and the validated `completion.typeFields` JSON. Closing a work item stays an agent action with evidence; the pane does not close items.\n- UI. In PlanDashboard item rows: `PlanItemTypeBadge` (R-19); the header gets the plan-type badge. Selecting the badge opens a type panel keyed by a nuqs param holding the item id, showing `ResolvedModuleChecklist` (R-25) and, when the type has completion fields, `ItemTypeCompletionForm` (R-20). Test files are the ones the BARs name under apps/operator/app/_components/plans/. Verified headless with scripts/verify-tauri-headless.sh + tauri-agent-tools.\n\n### D-010 — Every BAR-seed rebuild derives the item-type bars the way activation does\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAffects: P-004, P-008\n\n[self-imposed, su-94bf93fd, implementer call under AUTO]\n\n- Measured (P-008 e2e run 8, SYNC_DIAG): after a neutral plans:set-status write on a plan whose item type carries a criteria template, synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision rebuilds the seed with preserveExistingBars but WITHOUT itemTypeBars. buildAcceptanceBarSeed then refuses bar_rubric_conflict (\"active rubric contains criterion(s) outside the current Requirements set: t-...\"), the synchronizer returns false, and the rubric's subjectPlanRevision never advances. Every door then refuses bar_snapshot_rubric_revision_mismatch. rubrics.ts's projection-only repair rebuilds the same way and would throw acceptance_bar_projection_repair_invalid on such a plan.\n- Ruling: every rebuild of a plan's BAR seed takes its item-type bars from deriveSeedItemTypeBars (plan-types/item-type-contract.ts) over the body being validated, under the plan's pins. This is the input the activation seeder (seedAcceptanceBarsInTransaction) already uses. Callers today: acceptance-bar-amendment.ts synchronizeAcceptanceBarSubjectRevision and rubrics.ts's projection-only repair. If the derivation fails, the rebuild refuses (returns false or throws). It never guesses.\n- Rejected: teaching buildAcceptanceBarSeed to tolerate unknown T- criteria under preserveExistingBars. That would let a removed item type's bars survive silently, and the seed would no longer have one source of truth for which bars exist.\n- Guard: P-008's e2e test (item-type-cupboard-e2e.integration.test.ts) ships such a plan through the real gate, so the pin has to advance.\n\n### D-011 — Criteria-template criteria may carry their own verification, so a distributed item type's bars arrive gradable\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAffects: P-004, P-006, P-008\n\n[self-imposed, su-94bf93fd, implementer design call under AUTO]\n\n- Measured (P-008 e2e run 9, after D-010): the contract pin is current, but every item-type (T-) bar still refuses bar_snapshot_method_missing and bar_snapshot_check_missing. A criteria-template criterion is only {key, title, description}, so the bars it seeds carry no METHOD or check. Every pot that installs the type would have to rubrics:amend each bar by hand. For a type that is meant to be distributed, that defeats the point.\n- Ruling: criterionTemplateSchema (plan-types/definitions.ts) gains an optional `verification: { method, check?, replication? }`. `check` uses the definitions module's own declarative {kind, params} shape, so definitions.ts does not import rubric-template.ts. deriveSeedItemTypeBars (plan-types/item-type-contract.ts) carries it on ItemTypeBar. buildAcceptanceBarSeed (acceptance-bar-seed.ts) turns it into rubric criterion fields ({kind, ...params} validated by rubricCriterionCheckSchema) and applies them to the seeded T- bar the same way methodProjection applies a Requirements block's verification. An invalid check refuses the seed (bar_requirement_parse_failed), never a silent drop. Type packs validate it with the existing declarative-check predicate (cupboard/type-pack.ts, D-003/D-008).\n- Pinned revisions (R-14): verification is part of the definition, so it is covered by the content hash and the pin. Adding it is a new revision of the type.\n- Absent verification keeps today's behaviour: the bar is seeded without METHOD and the plan author fills it via rubrics:amend.\n- Guard: P-008's e2e test authors the shared memo type with verification on each criterion and ships the plan without force. Unit cases cover the schema, the derive, the seed projection and the pack refusal of a non-declarative check.\n\n### D-012 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-91f2f997f0f90920ef5937cb\nRequest-Hash: e1fc94b4282a606a1aee1fce00baff6e3d045233d11473ebe520c4c9b887eab8\nActor: su-94bf93fd-3bb5-4b0a-807f-c5a2e40017d0\nReason: As-built METHOD alignment at completion (method text only; no bar, check, layer or drift-marker change): R-8 names the file that tests the papercusp/ namespace refusal, R-11 records D-011 (template criteria carry their own verification), R-21 records the in-process Worker harness and D-010.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive ()\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 43 → 44\nChanged BARs: \nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-8, R-11, R-21\n\n### D-013 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-0b6d6517df1a0e17b4fa841a\nRequest-Hash: edcd8ba64ab0114ca778818a810723f882b4d6be08ba53f4e72b8b82f7c570b4\nActor: su-94bf93fd-3bb5-4b0a-807f-c5a2e40017d0\nReason: Rubric-vetting fixes (consult conv-request-2497f7bb, meta-acceptance-rubric rev 5): R-11 gains F(4) for D-010 with its own case and mutation probe; R-3 F(1) and method state the paired-re-run attribution rule for the live census; R-18 defers the generic-core floor to R-9; co-bound bars (R-1/R-2, R-5/R-6, R-21/R-22) bind their owning cases as selectors; stale Pre-implementation sentences dropped from R-4..R-7.\nApproved-By: su-9af4e425-21de-469f-bd39-bbb1b970b67e\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1193275\nApproved-At: 2026-10-21T18:51:56.057Z\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 44 → 45\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-5, R-6, R-11, R-21, R-22\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-11, R-18, R-21, R-22\n\n### D-014 — Refresh explicit falsifier scenario identities and exact existing mutation-case links before acceptance\nDate: 2026-10-22\n[self-imposed, continuation of su-94bf93fd under AUTO] Measured: staging plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy on 2026-10-22 reports falsifiability and plan-class-risk-floor unknown for the seven P-007/P-008 clauses. Canonical falsifiers have observation text but no requiredScenarios; existing proof targets only the spec id. Current spec-test-adequacy.ts mutationTargetMatchesMeasuredCase intentionally requires a scenario for a non-null falsifier (the explicit scenario-linkage regression tests pin this). Existing WI-6554700010019655 provides the accepted data repair precedent. Preserve behavior, sourceBar, evidence/test-layer requirements, original falsifier observations, and immutable run ids. Append CAS spec revisions declaring a distinct scenario id for each original falsifier. Rebind the existing passing baseline and actually caught mutant to the new revision with that scenario and exact measured case association; re-evaluate and obtain required independent proof audits. No evaluator bypass, bar weakening or fabricated new execution. P-007 native evidence still requires a successful corrected canonical /adv navigation run.\nRelated: P-007, P-008\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"psu-backend-availability-installation-2026-10-20","title":"PSU backend availability and optional installation","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-20","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: PSU backend availability and optional installation\nslug: psu-backend-availability-installation-2026-10-20\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-20\nupdated: 2026-10-20\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Implementation complete under WI-6554700010018075. Startup checks all three backends; missing tools can be installed optionally or directly by menu selection, retaining installed choices and retry/fallback selection. Installer specs are shared locally with desktop onboarding. Codex has an official standalone fallback when npm is absent. Final changed suites passed 19 + 12 tests with no substituted children, plus existing launcher/backend and OS/arch suites. Scoped typechecks, declarations and guards passed.\n\n**Next:** Carry the staging change into the next normal psu/pui utility release; published artifact verification is outside this implementation result.\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: standalone psu users.\nProblem: users cannot see all backend installation states before choosing, and installation depends on operator HTTP.\nOutcome: show Claude Code, Codex and OMP status, offer installation, continue with any one backend, and install a missing selected backend.\nNon-goals: account sign-in, hosted-customer provisioning, model selection.\nSource: current owner turn in this Codex session.\nScenarios: one installed → continue; none → choose one to install; missing selected → install and launch; failed install → choose again.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Availability and choice.** Check all three backends, keep every choice selectable and label missing choices.\n**R-2 — Optional installation.** Offer installation at startup; permit continuing with one available backend; install missing selections and verify current-process discovery.\n**R-3 — Shared standalone installers.** Reuse the existing desktop installer commands locally; preserve noninteractive and hosted-customer restrictions.\n\n## Design\nExtend the existing resolver, ensureBackendInstalled and picker. Extract the existing pure platform install builder into ESM shared by psu and the desktop endpoint.\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001 | tree |\n\n## Work\n- **P-001** `done` Implement startup and picker installation behavior and shared local installer specs; verify in canonical Vitest suites. Work-item WI-6554700010018075. — note: Final verification passed, including actual installer subprocess and npm-free Codex installer branch. Implementation is complete in staging; no published binary release claimed.\n\n## Decisions\nImplement directly in this session using existing installer and resolver surfaces.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"acceptance-claude-dialog-answer-provenance-2026-10-21","title":"Acceptance BAR — Preserve automatic Claude choices and record who answered","status":"active","created":"2026-10-21","owner":"su-52eb8d6e-7e32-485e-8a46-c6a1ee7ea8b0","archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Acceptance BAR — Preserve automatic Claude choices and record who answered\nslug: acceptance-claude-dialog-answer-provenance-2026-10-21\nstatus: active\ntemplate: rubric\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-22\nowner: su-52eb8d6e-7e32-485e-8a46-c6a1ee7ea8b0\n---\n\n# Acceptance BAR — Preserve automatic Claude choices and record who answered\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** Rubric-template plan (template:rubric). Its structured fields (characteristic,\ncriteria, ratingScale, methodRef) live in `template_data`, queried via\nrubrics:list/get/search; this body is the narrative model/method context. Problem: automatically supplied choices can be recorded as owner decisions. Outcome: preserve selection and carry actual answer origin into live context and history. Non-goals: change choice policy or grant new authority. Sources: session_turn:codex:01a15c0d-00f8-7af0-afe6-e1dc808a15d9:1 and :9. Scenarios: machine Enter; human Enter while AUTO is active; missing or mixed evidence; historical verification after compaction.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Preserve selection and attribute the exact response.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Keep existing input behavior. Distinguish automatic, human and unknown source using the exact session and tool-use identity.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A completed dialog answer receives automatic, human or unknown source attribution matched to its exact session and tool-use identity.\",\"falsifier\":\"Production hook/PTY/history regression fails for this requirement.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run apps/operator/lib/claude-dialog-answer-provenance.test.ts against the production PTY observer, combined hook and raw/indexed/relay history readers, including automatic/human/unknown and stale-source negative controls.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/claude-dialog-answer-provenance.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n**R-2 — Inform the model and retain provenance.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Show the source before continuation, retain it in transcript/indexed readers, and never treat automatic choices as new owner instructions. Unknown source stays unknown.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A completed dialog answer displays its observed source to the continuing agent before continuation.\",\"falsifier\":\"Production hook/PTY/history regression fails for this requirement.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run apps/operator/lib/claude-dialog-answer-provenance.test.ts against the production PTY observer, combined hook and raw/indexed/relay history readers, including automatic/human/unknown and stale-source negative controls.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/claude-dialog-answer-provenance.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n**R-3 — Verify the behavior.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Regression tests cover automatic/human/unknown input, stale identity, and history classification.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Regression tests cover automatic/human/unknown input, stale identity, and history classification.\",\"falsifier\":\"Production hook/PTY/history regression fails for this requirement.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run apps/operator/lib/claude-dialog-answer-provenance.test.ts against the production PTY observer, combined hook and raw/indexed/relay history readers, including automatic/human/unknown and stale-source negative controls.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"apps/operator/lib/claude-dialog-answer-provenance.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Retain source in history.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A completed dialog answer retains its observed source through raw, indexed and relay history This records stronger falsification of already-approved requirements, not additional product scope or integration-layer requirements.\nRelated: P-001\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"client-native-features-adoption-2026-10-21","title":"Adopt the useful new Claude Code and Codex client features (Codex subagents off; mods skipped)","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Adopt the useful new Claude Code and Codex client features (Codex subagents off; mods skipped)\nslug: client-native-features-adoption-2026-10-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-22, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_proof_stale, bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate, bar_snapshot_grading_missing, bar_snapshot_work_contract_stale, bar_snapshot_vetting_missing. R-1..R-6 written; R-2..R-6 test paths are provisional until each item's design is verified. D-001 scope, D-002 OpenTelemetry dropped (retraction). Not yet activated.\n\n**Next:** Verify designs for P-002..P-006 (StopFailure/PostToolUseFailure payloads, plugin generation source, channel protocol, idle-compaction switch name from a >=2.1.299 binary), finalize test paths, then the activation audit on :3170 and plans:start. Implement P-001 first.\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019305 — Turn off Codex native subagents and goals per D-003/D-005: `[features] multi_agent = false` and `goals = false` in every managed home; the gateway strips `multi_agent_version`/`multi_agent_reasoning_… <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019325 — Enroll a Claude `StopFailure` hook in every psu Claude session that durably records turns ending on an API error (session, error kind, time). <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019326 — Enroll a Claude `PostToolUseFailure` hook that durably records failed native tool calls (tool name, session, failure). <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019327 — Generate a `papercusp` Claude Code plugin from the hook-enrollment source, install it instead of duplicate settings.json entries, and detect a psu launch whose plugin rails are missing or disabled. <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019328 — Channels spike: prototype a coord-wake channel emitter, measure it against the current wake delivery, record an adopt/do-not-adopt Decision and publish the spike report. <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019306 — Add `idleCompaction: false` to the per-session `--settings` layer of every psu Claude launch (never ~/.claude/settings.json), next to the existing DISABLE_COMPACT/DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT env, with a tes… <!-- P-006 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.** Avi (owner) and every psu agent session (Claude Code and Codex).\n\n**Problem.** Claude Code and Codex shipped features that change how our agents behave.\n- Two are already ON in psu Codex sessions without anyone choosing it: native subagents (`multi_agent`) and native goals (`goals`). Subagents defeat the 2026-07-02 rule that fan-out goes through fleets (visible, locked, claimed, restart-durable).\n- Two hook events would give us signals we miss today: a Claude turn that ends on an API error (`StopFailure`; `Stop` does not fire then) and a Claude native tool that fails (`PostToolUseFailure`).\n- Our Claude hooks are enrolled by editing `~/.claude/settings.json`; a Claude Code plugin is the native, versioned packaging.\n- Channels (`--channels`) lets an MCP server push events into a live session, a possible native wake path.\n- Claude CLI native idle compaction (setting `idleCompaction`, needs 2.1.290+) is already in our installed 2.1.293. Today it is suppressed only as a side effect of DISABLE_COMPACT/DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT (D-004); a future CLI that decouples the two could silently fight Papercusp-owned compaction.\n\n**Outcome.**\n1. psu Codex sessions get no native subagent or goal tools unless explicitly opted in, with the same opt-in as Claude subagents.\n2. A Claude turn that ends on an API error, and a failed Claude native tool call, each leave a durable Papercusp record.\n3. The Claude hook integration installs as one `papercusp` Claude Code plugin generated from the same source as today's enrollment, and missing rails are detected rather than silently absent.\n4. Channels has a measured spike against the current wake delivery and a recorded adopt/do-not-adopt decision.\n5. psu Claude sessions keep native idle compaction off on any CLI version that has it, and a test fails if the switch goes missing.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- Claude mods: the owner said to skip them for now (#2142).\n- OpenTelemetry export: dropped, see the Decisions section (it duplicates the transcript usage ingest).\n- Claude agent teams, Task/Agent/Workflow, `--worktree`, Code Review levels, Claude auto mode, `/loop`: not adopted (same reasoning as the subagent deny, or not applicable to our workflow).\n\n**Source turns.** `session_turn:claude:78d46e16-17a1-4369-9437-a0c97985ed61:0` (directive #2137, the question); `session_turn:claude:78d46e16-17a1-4369-9437-a0c97985ed61:13` (directive #2142: \"turn off codex subagents. Write all this into a plan including all the other features you presented and then put yourself on auto mode and carry it to shipped status. We'll skip using claude mods for now\").\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. A psu Codex agent launched without the subagent opt-in has no `spawn_agent`/`followup_task`/`send_message`/`wait_agent`/`interrupt_agent`/`list_agents` and no `create_goal` tool.\n2. The same agent launched with the opt-in has the subagent tools.\n3. A Claude turn ends on a rate-limit or overloaded API error: a durable record names the session, the error kind and the time.\n4. A native Bash/Edit/Write call fails in a Claude session: the failure is recorded with its tool name and session.\n5. A machine is set up for Papercusp: the Claude integration arrives as the `papercusp` plugin, and a psu launch with the plugin's rails missing is detected.\n6. The Claude CLI is upgraded past 2.1.293 (for example to 2.1.306): psu sessions still run with native compaction, including idle compaction, off.\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Avi (owner) and every psu agent session, Claude Code and Codex.\",\n  \"problem\": \"New Claude Code and Codex features change how our agents behave. Codex native subagents and goals are already on in psu Codex sessions without anyone choosing it, which defeats the rule that fan-out goes through fleets. Two Claude hook events (StopFailure, PostToolUseFailure) would give signals we miss today. The Claude integration is hand-merged into settings.json. Channels may be a native wake route. Native idle compaction is suppressed only as a side effect of other switches.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"psu Codex sessions have no subagent or goal tool unless opted in; turns that end on an API error and failed native Claude tool calls leave durable records; the Claude integration installs as one generated papercusp plugin with missing rails detected; Channels has a measured adopt/do-not-adopt Decision; native compaction, including idle compaction, stays off on any CLI version.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"Claude mods: the owner said to skip them for now.\",\n    \"OpenTelemetry export: dropped because it duplicates the transcript usage ingest (D-002).\",\n    \"Claude agent teams, Task/Agent/Workflow, --worktree, Code Review levels, Claude auto mode, /loop: not adopted.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:claude:78d46e16-17a1-4369-9437-a0c97985ed61:0\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:78d46e16-17a1-4369-9437-a0c97985ed61:13\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Turn off Codex subagents, plan every other presented feature, skip Claude mods, run in AUTO and carry the plan to shipped.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:claude:78d46e16-17a1-4369-9437-a0c97985ed61:13\"\n      ],\n      \"decisionRef\": \"D-001\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"observed-fact\",\n      \"text\": \"Codex multi-agent is switched on by the model catalog's multi_agent_version; [features] multi_agent=false alone changes nothing. discovery keeps working (D-005).\",\n      \"scenarioIds\": [\n        \"SC-001\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Codex native subagent and goal tools are off unless opted in.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Turn off Codex subagents in psu sessions, keeping the same explicit opt-in Claude subagents have; turn off Codex native goals for the same reason native memories are off.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:78d46e16-17a1-4369-9437-a0c97985ed61:13\",\"session_turn:claude:78d46e16-17a1-4369-9437-a0c97985ed61:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every supported psu Codex launch preserves the D-008 creation-time native-tool policy: fresh sessions default to subagents and goals off, explicit fresh opt-in enables subagents only, and resume/fork inherit their goals; a resume/fork changes its inherited setting, emits no no-effect notice, or carries an inert override; or a launch/home route escapes these rules.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Enumerate fresh su/role/fleet launches and resume/fork descendants of both creation-time states, on gateway and non-gateway home routes. Run every bound file; record each requested/executed file and named assertion without skips. The launcher test covers fresh su/role argv and resume/fork notices; home/catalog/capability tests cover defaults, opt-in and both catalog routes. Validate actual native behavior with the versioned rollout turn_context.payload.multi_agent_version instrument from D-008, not model self-report. Record CLI version, parent/child rollout paths, creation-time setting and observed disabled/v1 values. Goals must remain false with opt-in. A missing route, lineage receipt or executed assertion is unknown.
