So the per-message cache-write split is already populated.\n\n### D-003 — Codex subagents are switched on by the model catalog, not [features]: disable needs a stripped model_catalog_json plus multi_agent=false plus goals=false\nDate: 2026-10-21\n[self-imposed, measured] P-001's planned lever (`[features] multi_agent = false`) is a NO-OP on the models psu Codex sessions run. The real switch needs three settings together.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-21 ~14:25-14:32Z (su-c5ca4868), codex-cli 0.163.0, model gpt-6.1-sol, `codex exec -c model_reasoning_effort=low` asked to list every callable tool (rollouts under ~/.codex/sessions/2026/10/21/):\n- default: 116 tools, including collaboration.spawn_agent/followup_task/interrupt_agent/list_agents/send_message/wait_agent and create_goal/get_goal/update_goal; `<multi_agent_role>` developer message injected.\n- features.multi_agent=false + features.multi_agent_v2=false: the same collaboration.* tools and the same developer message. `codex features list` reports both false, so the keys are accepted and change nothing.\n- cause: ~/.codex/models_cache.json gives each model `multi_agent_version` (v2: gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra; v1: gpt-reserve, gpt-5.6-luna, codex-auto-review). The catalog value turns multi-agent on regardless of [features].\n- `-c model_catalog_json=<catalog with multi_agent_version + multi_agent_reasoning_effort removed>` ALONE: 113 tools; v2 collaboration tools gone, but multi_agent_v1__spawn_agent/close_agent/resume_agent/send_input/wait_agent and the goal tools remain.\n- stripped catalog + features.multi_agent=false + features.goals=false: 108 tools, no subagent or goal tool, no multi_agent_role message.\n\nDecision: P-001 disables Codex subagents with all three: (a) the managed CODEX_HOME points `model_catalog_json` at a Papercusp-written copy of the best available model catalog with multi_agent_version / multi_agent_reasoning_effort removed; (b) `[features] multi_agent = false`; (c) `[features] goals = false`. The opt-in (`--allow-subagents`) re-enables subagents with `-c features.multi_agent=true` (v1 tools; Scenario 2 needs subagent tools, not a particular version). Open risk to settle in implementation: whether `model_catalog_json` overrides the gateway's `model_catalog_url` discovery. If it does, the gateway route must strip the field in the catalog it serves instead of using a local file. R-1's test must cover the catalog file as well as the features block.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-004 — Idle compaction already exists in CLI 2.1.293 and is already off in psu (gated on DISABLE_COMPACT/DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT); P-006 adds idleCompaction:false as defence in depth\nDate: 2026-10-21\n[self-imposed, measured] Correction to the plan's premise that idle compaction arrives in CLI 2.1.299: it is already in the installed 2.1.293, and our existing env switches already suppress it.\n\nMeasured: 2026-10-21 ~14:35Z (su-c5ca4868). String search of the installed binary ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.293 and of @anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.306 (npm pack into /tmp/su-c5ca-cc306, not installed):\n- Both read `CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS` and the settings key `idleCompaction` (default true). The 2.1.306 changelog text says `\"idleCompaction\": false` in settings.json turns it off and that both need v2.1.290 or later.\n- 2.1.293: the idle-compaction decision function returns \"disabled\" when the server flag tengu_sunny_locket mode is off, then `if(!im())return\"compaction_off\"`, where im() returns false when `DISABLE_COMPACT || DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT` is set. 2.1.306 has the same gate (`if(!up())return\"compaction_off\"`, up() returns false on `DISABLE_COMPACT || DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT`).\nSo psu sessions, which set DISABLE_COMPACT and DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT, do not idle-compact today on either version.\n\nDecision: P-006 stays as defence in depth. Every psu Claude launch also sets `idleCompaction: false` as a per-session setting (not in ~/.claude/settings.json, which would change the owner's own non-psu sessions), so idle compaction stays off if a future CLI decouples it from the auto-compact gate. R-6's test asserts all three (DISABLE_COMPACT, DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT, idleCompaction:false) on the psu Claude launch.\nRelated: P-006\n\n### D-005 — Codex subagent off-switch per route: the gateway strips multi_agent fields from the catalog it serves; non-gateway homes get a local stripped model_catalog_json\nDate: 2026-10-21\n[self-imposed, measured] Settles the open risk D-003 left: whether a local `model_catalog_json` overrides the gateway's `model_catalog_url`.\n\nMeasured 2026-10-21 ~14:43Z (su-c5ca4868), codex-cli 0.163.0, gpt-6.1-sol, two throwaway CODEX_HOMEs routed through the live :8788 gateway (provider table copied from a current su-codex-home; no account pin; probe script .papercusp/scratch/su-c5ca-gwprobe.sh, results /tmp/su-c5ca-cx/gwprobe.log):\n- A: gateway route + `[features] multi_agent=false, goals=false`, no catalog file: 19 tools, including collaboration.spawn_agent/followup_task/interrupt_agent/list_agents/send_message/wait_agent; `multi_agent_role` developer message present. So the catalog the gateway serves carries multi_agent_version (gateway.ts codexModelsResponse merges the account's native catalog), and [features] does not override it.\n- B: A plus `model_catalog_json` = the stripped catalog: 13 tools, no subagent or goal tool, no role message. So a local catalog file does override the gateway catalog.\n\nBecause the file overrides the gateway catalog, using it on the gateway route would freeze the session's model list and lose the live per-account discovery that `model_catalog_url` exists for (codex-gateway-config.ts comment: without it newly released models disappear in --account=auto sessions). D-003 pre-registered this case.\n\nDecision: P-001 uses one switch per route, plus the [features] keys everywhere.\n1. Gateway route (pin or auto): the gateway removes `multi_agent_version` and `multi_agent_reasoning_effort` from every model in the Codex `/v1/models` catalog it serves. No local catalog file on this route.\n2. Non-gateway route (`default` account, Codex fetches its own catalog): the managed CODEX_HOME writer writes a stripped copy of the freshest available models_cache.json (the home's own, else ~/.codex/models_cache.json) and points `model_catalog_json` at it. When no source catalog exists, the writer records that in the home's diagnostics, and the features block still applies.\n3. Every managed home: `[features] multi_agent = false` and `goals = false`.\n4. Opt-in (`--allow-subagents`): `features.multi_agent = true`, which brings back the v1 subagent tools on a stripped catalog (measured in D-003: stripped catalog with default features kept multi_agent_v1__spawn_agent and the other v1 tools).\nAlso checked and rejected: the binary has an `[agents]` table (`max_threads`, `max_concurrent_threads_per_session`). Capping threads still exposes the tools, so it does not meet R-1.\nRelated: P-001\n\n### D-006 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-a25c9826e577c28e0e1db23c\nRequest-Hash: 7d7b85d22809e265d5683e360a0c0143281eb79886958cddf8ada5c40838c2d1\nActor: su-c5ca4868-c4df-43ab-86e1-f4bb9c726ff7\nReason: rubrics:amend acceptance-client-native-features-adoption-2026-10-21\nApproved-By: su-2fce7412-7351-42fd-aa6d-b2a788301e9f\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1193096\nApproved-At: 2026-10-21T15:20:52.580Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 13 → 14\nChanged BARs: R-4, R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-6\n\n### D-007 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-b2c242f76f925da9eafbf42f\nRequest-Hash: f0984fc80c55a6dfdfbc6583f0020b72bea36e2ab4209aedc4f8d8e1cf6afcb8\nActor: su-c5ca4868-c4df-43ab-86e1-f4bb9c726ff7\nReason: rubrics:amend acceptance-client-native-features-adoption-2026-10-21\nApproved-By: su-31c89d55-ce99-4ba3-a7da-877d25582f52\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1193108\nApproved-At: 2026-10-21T15:30:46.924Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 15 → 16\nChanged BARs: R-6\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-008 — Codex fixes native subagents when a session is created: --allow-subagents works on a fresh launch only; resume/fork inherit the creation-time setting\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21 [self-imposed, measured] Changes P-001's opt-in design, which assumed a per-launch `-c features.multi_agent=true` works on every launch shape including `resume`/`fork`.\n\nInstrument: the rollout JSONL `turn_context.payload.multi_agent_version` (\"disabled\" vs \"v1\"), read from the file. This replaces the model's self-report of its tool list, which is weak with a dummy MCP server. In run 2 it agreed with a positive self-report: SUB listed multi_agent_v1__spawn_agent/close_agent/resume_agent/send_input/wait_agent. codex-cli 0.163.0, gpt-6.1-sol, homes built by the real writeRoleCodexHome (`multi_agent = false`, `goals = false`, stripped `model_catalog_json`). Scripts .papercusp/scratch/su-c5ca/p001-live2..5.sh plus pty driver ptydrive.py. Measured 2026-10-21 16:50-17:06Z (su-c5ca4868):\n- `codex exec`, plain: disabled. `codex -c features.multi_agent=true exec ... -c model_reasoning_effort=low`: disabled (a root -c is not applied to exec when exec has its own -c). `codex exec -c features.multi_agent=true`: v1.\n- Fresh TUI with psu's flags (the suLaunchArgs/roleLaunchArgs shape), plain: disabled. Same with root `-c features.multi_agent=true`: v1.\n- `resume <uuid>` of a session created disabled: disabled for plain, root -c before `resume`, and `resume -c ...` after the subcommand.\n- Plain `resume <uuid>` of a session created v1: v1. Plain `fork <uuid>` of it: v1. Root-opt-in `fork` of a session created disabled: disabled.\n\nDecision:\n1. `psu --allow-subagents` opts in a NEW Codex session (su launch, role launch, `fleet:launch-on-plan { allowSubagents }`, which re-emits the flag on a fresh launch). That session keeps subagents for its whole native lineage: every resume and fork inherits it, the same way a Claude session's own transcript continues.\n2. resumeArgsFor no longer emits the inert `-c features.multi_agent=true` for Codex `resume`/`fork`. When `--allow-subagents` or `--no-subagents` is passed on a Codex resume or fork, psu prints that the flag has no effect and that the session keeps the setting it was created with. It does not silently imply a capability.\n3. The managed home stays `multi_agent = false` / `goals = false`, so every NEW session is deny-by-default. The earlier claim \"the home stays deny-by-default for every later resume\" is corrected to \"for every new session\".\n4. The main su launch's notice \"subagent allow/deny is claude-only ... codex keeps its native subagent tool\" was false for Codex after P-001. It now names only omp.\nRejected: keeping the inert resume -c \"in case a later Codex honours it\". It advertises a capability that does not exist, and a later Codex that changes this is caught by re-running the run-5 instrument, not by leaving dead argv.\n\n### D-009 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-9a2050e0fa7fe3ce80de54c8\nRequest-Hash: 01c214c7f785995061a9275c420f889f0224eb3566995c0fb5a4c19d141866aa\nActor: su-c5ca4868-c4df-43ab-86e1-f4bb9c726ff7\nReason: Method-only as-built evidence for R-1 (P-001, WI-6554700010019305): name the passing tests, the mutation-probe receipts, and the D-008 opt-in scope with its live instrument. The bar text is unchanged.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive ()\nRubric revision: 3 → 4\nSubject plan revision: 20 → 21\nChanged BARs: \nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1\n\n### D-010 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: amend-07918469a58903bd7062a77b\nRequest-Hash: 7b7466b26f2831d3d2c8582a4ce891a751eb2eaacb4d3e024395e611814ac9d0\nActor: su-c5ca4868-c4df-43ab-86e1-f4bb9c726ff7\nReason: Method-only as-built evidence for R-6 (P-006, WI-6554700010019306): name the passing test file, what it covers, and the mutation-probe receipts, including the survived probe that led to the successor-site scan. The bar text is unchanged.\nApproval: not required — every change is additive ()\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 21 → 22\nChanged BARs: \nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-6\n\n### D-011 — P-003 records a failed tool call as a post-phase tool row with the error in summary, via a shared hook helper\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21 [self-imposed, measured]\n\nShape of the PostToolUseFailure record (R-3). Payload read from the claude 2.1.293 binary: common fields + hook_event_name:\"PostToolUseFailure\", tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, error, is_interrupt, duration_ms.\n\n- activity:report { kind:'tool', phase:'post', status:'error' (or 'interrupted' when is_interrupt), tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input, summary:'✖ tool failed: <tool> — <error>' }. One harness_shared.agent_activity row carries the tool name (tool_name column), the session (session_id) and the failure (status + summary).\n- The error goes in summary, not detail: with tool_name set, the server derives detail from the tool input (activity-bridge summariseActivity), so an error carried in tool_input would be dropped. A supplied summary is stored as given.\n- tool_input is reduced to its scalar fields, strings clipped to 512 chars, at most 20 fields, so a failed Write of a large file cannot bloat the report and the server can still name the file or command.\n- kind:'tool' runs the same benign side effect as every PostToolUse report (ensureInboxWakeArmedForActiveSession re-arm); no lifecycle side effect.\n- No matcher: every tool's failure counts.\n- Reuse: three .mjs hooks each hand-rolled the activity:report POST. P-003 adds apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/pc_activity_report.mjs (str, clip, operatorBase, readSuperuserToken, readHookStdin, postActivityReport), a 0644 hook library in CC_HOOK_LIB_FILES. stop-failure-record.mjs moves onto it after P-002 closes, so P-002's probed blob is not disturbed before its close.\n\n### D-012 — P-004 ships the papercusp Claude plugin as a settings-enrolled directory marketplace, and it becomes the only carrier of our Claude hooks\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21 [self-imposed, measured]\n\nMeasured on claude 2.1.293 in an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (/tmp/su-c5ca-plugin-cDZ7). Marker hooks write to a log, and SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit fire before the API auth refusal, so no tokens are spent:\n1. A directory-marketplace plugin is read from its SOURCE folder (`claude plugin list --json` readFromFolder), not from the cache copy under plugins/cache. A SessionStart hook added to the source after install fired while the cache copy lacked it. The generated plugin can be regenerated in place with no reinstall or version bump.\n2. Settings-only enrollment works: `extraKnownMarketplaces: { papercusp-local: { source: { source: 'directory', path } } }` plus `enabledPlugins: { 'papercusp@papercusp-local': true }` in settings.json, with no `claude plugin install`, loaded the plugin on the first launch (installed_plugins.json stayed empty).\n3. One command enrolled both inline in settings.json hooks and in the plugin fired TWICE. There is no cross-source dedupe, so inline entries must be removed when the plugin carries them.\n4. Per-session `--settings '{\"enabledPlugins\":{\"papercusp@papercusp-local\":false}}'` turns off a user-enabled plugin. `--plugin-dir` for a plugin of the same name replaces the installed one (it fired once). `--setting-sources` without `user` drops the plugin.\n5. Every psu Claude session runs on a per-session settings.json that writeSessionSettings rebuilds on each materialize as a merged copy of ~/.claude/settings.json; plugins/ is symlinked through. Claude re-reads that settings file on a self-re-exec but drops argv, so `--plugin-dir` is not a durable carrier.\n\nDesign:\n- Generator packages/operator-core/lib/claude-plugin/papercusp-claude-plugin.ts builds the plugin hooks as `mergeClaudeHookSettings({}, hookDir, { present }).hooks`, the same source as today's enrollment. It writes ~/.papercusp/claude-plugins/{.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, plugins/papercusp/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/papercusp/hooks/hooks.json}, with plugin id papercusp@papercusp-local. Hook commands keep pointing at the installed ~/.papercusp/hooks/cc scripts, so only the carrier changes. A drift check compares the hooks.json on disk with a fresh build.\n- Both installers (installClaudeHooks in papercusp-files.ts, and install-standalone-mcp.sh through a tsx CLI) write the plugin, enroll it in settings.json, then strip our inline hook commands, keeping any foreign command that shares an entry. statusLine and enableAllProjectMcpServers stay inline, because a plugin cannot carry them. If the plugin cannot be written, the inline enrollment stays, so there is never zero carriers.\n- Launch-time detection: a pure .mjs verdict (packages/operator-core/lib/claude-plugin/plugin-rails.mjs, imported by psu-launcher.mjs like the other operator-core .mjs modules) extends the existing WI-4394 enrollment guard. A hook counts as enrolled when it is inline OR in the enabled papercusp plugin's hooks.json. The verdict reports `double` (inline plus an enabled plugin), `plugin-disabled` and `plugin-missing`. On a miss the guard runs the existing self-repair route and prints a loud banner. The file-lock acquire hook joins the guarded set.\n- Out of scope: Codex and OMP keep their own hook carriers. `-p` workers whose minimal config dir resolves zero plugins had no hooks before this change and still have none.\n\n### D-013 — P-005 Channels: do not adopt as the coord wake transport now; keep the tested prototype emitter\nDate: 2026-10-21\nDate: 2026-10-21 [self-imposed, measured]\n\nVerdict: do not adopt. Keep `packages/operator-core/lib/channels/coord-channel-emitter.ts` (+ its test against the CLI's own schema) as the prototype; revisit on the triggers at the end.\n\nMeasured on claude 2.1.293, 2026-10-21 19:37-19:41Z (su-c5ca4868). Channel server: `.papercusp/scratch/su-c5ca/channel-probe/server.mjs`, stdio, declaring `experimental[\"claude/channel\"]` and pushing the emitter's exact message shape.\n\n1. Interactive session in a PTY (`--dangerously-load-development-channels server:coordwake --setting-sources local`). Debug log: `Channel notifications registered` 13 ms after connect (protocolEra legacy). Push emitted 19:40:13.518Z; CLI receipt 13.520Z; queued 13.523Z; meta user turn 13.561Z with origin `{kind:channel, server:coordwake}`; API call 13.904Z. **Emit to turn start: 43 ms.** The model call failed (the system OAuth account is at its weekly limit), so no model reply was measured. A second push (19:40:23.514Z) was queued but started no turn while the rate-limit menu was open.\n2. Headless print mode (`-p --input-format stream-json`). The server connected (legacy era), but no channel registration was logged and neither push (1.5 s and 15 s after init) produced a turn. Headless sessions (our `resume-headless` wakes) do not receive channels.\n3. Launch cost, read from the binary and seen on screen. A `server:` entry needs `--dangerously-load-development-channels`, which shows a blocking `WARNING: Loading development channels` dialog on every launch. Avoiding the dialog needs a plugin on the approved channels allowlist (`allowedChannelPlugins` in managed settings for orgs). Registration is also skipped for non-first-party providers, when the `tengu_harbor`/`allow_channels` gates are off, on team/enterprise without `channelsEnabled: true`, and on modern-protocol-era connections.\n4. Current wake delivery (`harness_shared.event_wake_deliveries`, last 7 days). psu-socket-inject delivered 9,330 wakes; delivered_at minus created_at was p10 47 s, p50 59 s, p90 280 s, and min_sleep_sec averaged 60. That delay is the deliberate min-sleep/coalescing window plus the wait for the target to go idle. The transport hop itself is not recorded separately. Channels also queue with priority `next` and never interrupt a running turn, so they would not shorten either part. 946 of 9,330 inject deliveries (10%) were never picked up (`turn_proof = not-picked-up`). Channels do not address that either, because the CLI queue also needs an idle session.\n\nWhy not adopt: the only measured gain is transport latency, tens of milliseconds, inside a delay that is set by a 60 s policy window. The costs are a blocking dialog on every launch (or an allowlist we do not control), a second MCP server per session, and no headless coverage.\n\nWorth keeping in mind: a channel turn arrives `isMeta` with origin kind `channel`, so it is distinguishable from an owner-typed turn.\n\nRevisit when: the CLI accepts a local channel without the development dialog for individual accounts, or channels register in headless/print mode.\n\n### D-014 — Name canonical falsifier scenarios while preserving the existing outcomes\nDate: 2026-10-22\nMeasured: 2026-10-22T13:19Z; command: plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy on staging 6430ced5a6 plus source read packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-test-adequacy.ts mutationTargetScenarioMatchesMeasuredCase. The current evaluator requires exact canonical scenario-to-measured-failed-case links; an own-specId target proves identity only when a structured falsifier exists. The twelve active AUTO-BAR/SPEC clauses retain their behavior, falsifier observation, required layers, evidence planes and BAR provenance. Their falsifiers now add one named scenario per item: P-001 codex-subagents-default-disabled; P-002 claude-api-error-recorded; P-003 claude-tool-failure-recorded; P-004 disabled-plugin-detected; P-005 channel-notification-shape; P-006 native-compaction-disabled. Bind the actual recorded failed case and same-file passing baseline to that scenario, rather than treating an undifferentiated mutant as proof. P-004 needs a disabled-plugin mutant for its missing/disabled launch-rails clause; double-enrollment evidence alone is insufficient for that clause. Refresh source-stale proof and bind only after current rubric vetting. These names strengthen proof identity without changing product scope, the promised outcomes, or the D-013 do-not-adopt verdict.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006\n\n### D-015 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: apply-c5ca-rubric-critique-1195658\nRequest-Hash: e0a3eea2faf6391e07449e6af19186b88938de04ef621e3b53ddbc97f4ba1b70\nActor: su-c5ca4868-c4df-43ab-86e1-f4bb9c726ff7\nReason: Apply independent rubric critique post 1195585 from consult conv-request-897d9e40371009828cd4775c5d0ca3264b23e75344bc6efe108aeec4d633f595. Clarify D-008/D-011/D-012/D-013 outcomes, bind missing detectors, retain persistence/native semantics, and make the pre-existing minimal-config worker exclusion explicit rather than silently counting it as hook coverage. Product scope and Channels no-adopt verdict remain governed by #2142 and the recorded Decisions.\nApproved-By: su-46efcd15-51d8-4bec-9746-10528e6005ee\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1195658\nApproved-At: 2026-10-22T13:56:24.758Z\nRubric revision: 5 → 6\nSubject plan revision: 28 → 29\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6\n\n### D-016 — Correct the Channels emit-to-engine-turn boundary: 77ms, not 43ms\nDate: 2026-10-22\nMeasured: 2026-10-22T14:30Z; command: read /tmp/su-c5ca-chanpty-2Ex9/server.log and debug.log around2026-10-21T19:40:13. The server emit is19:40:13.518Z, notification receipt19:40:13.520Z, and explicit [engine] turn1 start19:40:13.595Z. RETRACTION: D-013/report rpt_3b79b02b-ac54-4682-afbd-84a555ade893 used43ms as emit-to-turn; the explicit engine marker yields77ms. Earlier telemetry/hook events are different boundaries and cannot substitute for engine turn start. The current wake transport hop remains unmeasured, so neither figure supports a measured like-for-like transport speedup. D-013 DO-NOT-ADOPT survives: blocking development dialog, no headless registration, and policy/coalescing delay remain. Correct the report by supersession, preserve original provenance, and archive exact event lines in docs/evidence/client-native-features-operational-2026-10-22.json.\nRelated: P-005\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"code-intel-relevance-routing-2026-10-21","title":"Feed code-intelligence signals into the consult relevance router","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Feed code-intelligence signals into the consult relevance router\nslug: code-intel-relevance-routing-2026-10-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-21, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty. Next repair: Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nDraft. Driving item WI-6554700010019295. Next: activation audit, plans:start.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019459 — Subject resolution module `code-subject-resolution.ts` + unit tests (R-1, R-8, R-9, R-12, R-14, R-15). <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019460 — Familiarity measurement module `code-familiarity.ts` + integration test (R-2). <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019461 — Wire resolved subjects and familiarity into the relevance-router authorship signal and snapshot evidence; integration tests for R-3, R-4, R-12 and R-13. <!-- P-003 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019462 — Grader exclusion: `resolvePlanImplementerIdentities` adds plan-attributed editors + integration test (R-5, R-10, R-11). <!-- P-004 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019463 — Offline replay over 30 days of consult_state routing snapshots; record the measurement (R-6). <!-- P-005 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019464 — Live proof on :3170: consult naming an identifier persists code evidence (R-7). <!-- P-006 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"Every agent that calls consult:get_feedback, and the acceptance-grader recruiter behind plans:set-plan-status shipped; both rank agents with packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router.ts.\",\n  \"problem\": \"The router's authorship signal (15% of the blend) fires only when the question contains a literal file path, and then matches it by ILIKE substring against payload->'paths' of the candidate's committed work-items. Questions that name a function or module, and agents who edited code without a work-item path list, contribute nothing.\",\n  \"outcome\": \"Code questions route to agents who edited or studied that code, with the evidence persisted in the routing snapshot, while the honesty rules (similarity floor, no recency term, all-time evidence) still hold.\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [\n    \"No new table or index.\",\n    \"No change to the similarity embedding.\",\n    \"No recency weighting.\",\n    \"No weight re-calibration beyond what the offline replay justifies.\"\n  ],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [\n    \"session_turn:claude:151eda92-21a7-41de-9e05-2b9ecfbfc085:18\",\n    \"session_turn:claude:151eda92-21a7-41de-9e05-2b9ecfbfc085:21\"\n  ],\n  \"context\": [\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Use the code-intelligence tools to enhance the relevance router.\",\n      \"sourceRefs\": [\n        \"session_turn:claude:151eda92-21a7-41de-9e05-2b9ecfbfc085:18\"\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"kind\": \"owner-request\",\n      \"text\": \"Write it into a plan, run in AUTO mode, and carry it to \"SC-002\"\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Subject resolution.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Resolve a consult question to the code files it is about: explicit paths plus identifiers resolved to defining files through the existing symbol index.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\",\"owner-directive:2150\"],\"constraints\":[\"Identifiers resolve through an injected resolver seam; the production resolver reads the existing git index (git grep for exported declarations, bounded by a timeout and a file cap); no new index or table.\",\"A question with no code subject resolves to an empty set.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A question that names an identifier without a path resolves to the file that defines that identifier.\",\"falsifier\":\"An identifier-only question resolves to no files.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit tests with a fixture symbol resolver.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-subject-resolution.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Familiarity from ledgers.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Measure each candidate's familiarity with the resolved files from what it actually did: edits strongly, reads and code queries weakly.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Sources are edit_attribution_ledger and tool_invocations only; counted over all time (relevance-router D-007); no time term.\",\"One bounded query per source per route.\",\"Wording from bar critique #2 (thread-post:1193229): an as-of cut used by offline replay counts only activity before a fixed instant. It is not a time weight and is permitted.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The familiarity measure scores an editor above a reader above an untouched candidate for the same file, with no recency weighting of the activity.\",\"falsifier\":\"A reader outranks an editor, or older activity scores lower than identical newer activity.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration test against a fixture Postgres with ledger rows for three owners.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-familiarity.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Router uses the code signal.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Feed resolved code subjects and familiarity into the router's authorship signal and persist the evidence in the routing snapshot.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"BlendWeights keeps no recency member; simFloor and relevanceFloor semantics unchanged.\",\"Snapshot candidates carry the code subjects and per-owner edit/read counts (D-008).\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An identifier-only code question gives the editing candidate authorship > 0 with evidence in the snapshot, and a candidate below the similarity floor stays unqualified however many edits it has.\",\"falsifier\":\"The editor gets authorship 0, the evidence is missing from the snapshot, or edits promote a below-floor candidate.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Relevance-router integration tests with a deterministic embedder and fixture ledgers.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router-code-signal.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Non-code questions unchanged.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Questions with no code subject route exactly as before.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"No extra queries when no subject resolves.\",\"Wording from bar critique #2 (thread-post:1193229): the baseline is the same router with the code signal absent.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For a non-code question the ranking and scores deep-equal the same router run with no resolver (the pre-change path), and no ledger query is issued.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any score or rank differs from the resolver-less run for a non-code question, or a ledger query is issued.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Same integration file, non-code fixture compared with the unchanged path.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router-code-signal.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Grader exclusion by edits.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Use edit attribution to exclude implementers from acceptance grading, not just work-item claimants, auditors and the author lineage.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Extend resolvePlanImplementerIdentities so the editors land in the existing D-009 exclusion set.\",\"An editor is an agent whose edit_attribution_ledger rows name the plan (plan_slug) or one of its work-items.\",\"Revised on bar critique #3 (thread-post:1193253): set membership alone did not prove the grading exclusion. The bound test runs the acceptance-grader eligibility check with the real implementer resolver over a fixture ledger and asserts the grader_in_implementer_lineage refusal.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An agent whose only link to the plan is recorded edits attributed to the plan or one of its work-items is refused as a plan implementer when it asks to grade the plan.\",\"falsifier\":\"Such an agent is allowed to grade the plan, or is missing from the plan's implementer set.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration test against a fixture Postgres: the acceptance-grader eligibility check (grader-eligibility.ts), fed by the real implementer resolver, refuses a plan-attributed and a work-item-attributed editor as plan implementers.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-author-identity-edits.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Measured effect.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Measure the change on real routings before claiming improvement.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Replay reads persisted consult_state routing snapshots; it never rewrites them.\",\"Revised on bar critique #2 (thread-post:1193229). controlDrift counts replayable routings whose control re-score differs from the stored ranking; it must be 0 or the replay is a re-implementation and every delta is suspect.\",\"Routings whose stored snapshot predates the current format (stored relevance does not recompute from stored signals) are counted as unreplayable, keep their stored outcome on both sides, and are excluded from controlDrift.\",\"Revised on bar critique #3 (thread-post:1193253). The decision passes only when all of these hold on the paired cohort: at least 30 paired code-related routings; controlDrift = 0; the treated share with a non-zero code signal is above the paired control share; at least one top candidate changes; the treated no-qualified-responder share is not above the paired control; resolver-unavailable is under 5% of replayable routings; familiarity-unmeasured is under 5% of familiarity attempts. These thresholds are REPLAY_BAR in code-signal-replay.ts, fixed before the measured run.\",\"Baseline: the paired control arm on the same selector and window. The 12.2% figure quoted in the source question is not used: it was computed over all code-related routings including legacy snapshots held at their stored outcome on both arms (EI-26614576274993500), so it is a different population.\",\"Population and attrition: the report gives total, replayable, unreplayable and code-related counts. Unreplayable legacy snapshots are reported only as attrition and a sensitivity bound. They are excluded from every efficacy denominator, and the result is not claimed to generalize to them.\",\"The recorded report carries the selector, window, build sha, attrition block, cohort shares with numerators and denominators, the decision and its failures, and the examples.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"On the paired replayable code-related cohort of a frozen trailing 30-day replay, the recorded replay decision passes.\",\"falsifier\":\"The recorded replay decision fails, or the report with its decision, selector, window end and build sha is not recorded on P-005.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredScope\":[\"live\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run replayCodeSignal (packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-signal-replay.ts) with a fixed window end and build sha on a read-only connection to the live database; record the report on P-005. The cohort denominators and the threshold decision are unit-tested in code-signal-replay.test.ts.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-signal-replay.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Live routing evidence.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Prove the router uses the new signal in the running system.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2150\"],\"constraints\":[\"Run on :3170 after the change is committed and served.\",\"Revised on bar critique #2 (thread-post:1193229): field presence alone passed even when every count was 0.\",\"Evidence read from consult_state.routing: codeSubjects.files names the defining file, codeSubjects.edits gives the editor a count above 0, and that candidate's signals.authorship is above 0.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"On :3170 (citing its /api/health build sha and the consult id), a consult naming an identifier whose defining file has a recorded editor persists a routing snapshot that credits that editor with code authorship above 0.\",\"falsifier\":\"The persisted snapshot credits no candidate with code authorship above 0, or its code subjects omit the defining file.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"live\",\"requiredScope\":[\"live\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Call consult:get_feedback via --port 3170 and read consult_state.routing for that consult.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router-code-signal.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-8 — Explicit paths kept.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Explicit paths named in a question stay in its resolved code subjects.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Split from R-1 so each bar states one outcome.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An explicit file path named in a question stays in the set of files that question resolves to.\",\"falsifier\":\"An explicit path named in the question is missing from the resolved set.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit tests with a fixture symbol resolver.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-subject-resolution.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-9 — Non-code questions resolve to nothing.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A question with no code subject resolves to an empty set.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Split from R-1 so each bar states one outcome.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A question that names no path and no identifier resolves to no files.\",\"falsifier\":\"A question with no code subject resolves to one or more files.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit tests with a fixture symbol resolver.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-subject-resolution.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-10 — Other plans' editors stay eligible.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Editors attributed only to other plans are not excluded from grading this plan.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Split from R-5 so each bar states one outcome.\",\"Revised symmetrically with R-5 on bar critique #3 (thread-post:1193253). The same test carries a positive control: the eligibility path that admits the other-plan editor refuses a plan-attributed editor.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An agent whose recorded edits are attributed only to other plans is not refused as a plan implementer when it asks to grade the plan.\",\"falsifier\":\"An editor attributed only to another plan is refused as a plan implementer, or appears in the plan's implementer set.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration test against a fixture Postgres: the acceptance-grader eligibility check returns no refusal for editors attributed only to another plan or its work-items.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-author-identity-edits.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-11 — Implementer resolution fails eligibility check itself rejects when the ledger is unreadable; it does not catch the resolver error.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"If the edit ledger cannot be read, implementer resolution proceeds.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration test against a fixture Postgres whose edit route.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A failing symbol lookup degrades the code signal; it never breaks routing.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Bar added on bar critique #2 (thread-post:1193229).\",\"The lookup is bounded by a timeout, a per-identifier file cap and a per-question identifier cap (D-002).\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A symbol resolver that throws or times out never fails the routing.\",\"falsifier\":\"A resolver throw or timeout makes the routing fail or reject.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit tests with a throwing and a timed-out resolver (identifiers left unresolved, resolver reported unavailable); integration test with an unavailable resolver completing the route.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-subject-resolution.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router-code-signal.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-13 — Resolver failure credits no code authorship.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A failing symbol lookup never credits code authorship.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Split from the single resolver-failure bar proposed on bar critique #2 (thread-post:1193229) so each bar states one outcome.\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"When the symbol resolver is unavailable, no candidate is credited with code authorship.\",\"falsifier\":\"A candidate is credited with code authorship while the resolver is unavailable.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Integration test routing a code question with an unavailable resolver.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router-code-signal.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-14 — Resolution stays within its caps.**\n\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Symbol resolution stays bounded per question.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"owner-directive:2149\"],\"constraints\":[\"Bar added on bar critique #3 (thread-post:1193253): R-1's constraints promise the caps; R-12 covers only failure degradation.\",\"Caps are CODE_SUBJECT_MAX_IDENTIFIERS (4) and CODE_SUBJECT_MAX_FILES_PER_IDENTIFIER (3) in code-subject-resolution.ts (D-002).\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Resolving one question keeps at most the configured number of identifiers and at configured.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredScope\":[\"tree\"],\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Unit tests capping the identifier count and the defining files (D-002).\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A symbol lookup that runs past the configured deadline is reported unavailable.\",\"falsifier\":\"A symbol lookup that runs past the configured deadline is implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-005 | live |\n| R-7 | P-006 | live |\n| R-8 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-004 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-002 | tree |\n\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-subject-resolution.ts`: `resolveQuestionCodeSubjects(question, { resolveSymbol })` = `extractPathTokens` paths plus identifier tokens resolved through an injected resolver backed by the existing symbol/graph index.\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/consult/code-familiarity.ts`: `measureCodeFamiliarity(sql, owners, files)` = per-owner edit count (edit_attribution_ledger) and read/query count (tool_invocations args naming the files), all-time.\n- `relevance-router.ts` step 4: authorship = clamp01(max(existing work-item path score, edits/2 + reads/8)); snapshot gains `codeSubjects` and per-candidate `authorshipEvidence`.\n- Grader eligibility: `resolvePlanImplementerIdentities` (`packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-author-identity.ts`) also returns `edit_attribution_ledger` agents whose rows name the plan or its work-items, so they join the D-009 `excluded` set. Editing a cited file for another plan does not exclude an agent: those are often the best-qualified graders.\n- Read signal: `tool_invocations` holds MCP calls only, so the read leg is weak by construction. It runs under a statement timeout; on timeout the snapshot records reads as unmeasured and no candidate gets read credit (D-002).\n- Production symbol resolver: `git grep` over the router host's checkout for `export (async function|function|const|class|interface|type|enum) <name>`, capped at 4 identifiers and 3 files each, 1s timeout. One-hop caller expansion is deferred (D-002).\n- No flag: ships on (no dangerous surface).\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\n```reuse\n{\n  \"searched\": [\n    {\n      \"where\": evidence (R-7). — note: ← WI-6554700010019464 completed (done)\n\n## Validation and rollout\n\nFocused tests per item, `lint:tsc --files` over the changed set, live proof on :3170, then the acceptance rubric seeded from R-1..R-15, vetted, independently graded, and shipped.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Code familiarity enters only through authorship, with the router's honesty rules unchanged\nDate: 2026-10-21\nThe code signal (edits from edit_attribution_ledger, reads and code queries from tool_invocations) feeds the existing `authorship` blend member only. It does not add a new blend weight, and it does not change the similarity embedding.\n\nInvariants kept from the relevance router (packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router.ts module header):\n- No recency term. BlendWeights gains no recency member, and familiarity counts carry no time decay (consult-expert-routing-2026-09-22#D-001).\n- All-time evidence. Edits and reads are counted over all time, like verification (consult-expert-routing-2026-09-22#D-007).\n- simFloor and relevanceFloor semantics unchanged. A candidate below the similarity floor stays unqualified however many edits it has (get-feedback-relevance-consults-2026-08-16#D-003), so track record cannot promote an irrelevant agent.\n- Non-code questions run no extra queries and produce identical scores.\n\nRationale: the blend's honesty depends on similarity gating relevance. Code familiarity is evidence about the candidate, not about the question, so it may only re-order already-relevant candidates. Source: the owner's request at session_turn:claude:151eda92-21a7-41de-9e05-2b9ecfbfc085:18.\n\n### D-002 — Git-index symbol resolver, timeout-bounded read leg, one-hop callers deferred\nDate: 2026-10-21\nMeasured 2026-10-21 before activation:\n- Postgres has no symbol table, and lsp:query workspace_symbols has a known false-empty mode (WI-6554700010018131). So the production identifier resolver is a bounded `git grep` for exported declarations in the router host's checkout, behind an injected seam that tests replace with a fixture.\n- `tool_invocations` records MCP calls only. In 7 days it holds 52,258 capability:read rows across 1,968 owners, but an all-time read lookup for 20 owners took 1.8s. The read leg therefore runs under a statement timeout. On timeout the snapshot records reads as unmeasured, and no candidate gets read credit, so the timeout cannot bias one candidate over another.\n- The edit leg (edit_attribution_ledger, 265,559 rows) answered for 60 owners in 0.6s, so it runs without that fallback beyond the shared statement timeout.\n- The optional one-hop caller expansion from the approved proposal is deferred. `graph:query` callers is still measured as needs-widening (WI-10006543), and an empty callers answer is not proof of no callers. It can follow once that index is trustworthy.\n\nSource: the approved proposal (session_turn:claude:151eda92-21a7-41de-9e05-2b9ecfbfc085:20, approved at turn 21).\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-21\nAmendment-Id: ci-relevance-bars-split-2\nRequest-Hash: b686b0f702d9f5a5ae84c2b976941f31d98ed86a17026fd83fe74c50c7c58869\nActor: su-611f037a-a3b8-460d-8e65-ea9801692de4\nReason: R-2/R-3: internal names replaced by the observable contract. Activation audit3 accepted revision15; D006 resolves draft choices and D007 records integration seams. Full20-item implementation remains open. Current spec-quality hash110c06be passes evaluator; independent audit EI-26689749363936738 is pending. Current-build bar critique accepted as conv-request-f21084002290430bf56bcaa5da21a1be2f60424a5d818cffee5828bcc29f33da. No implementation fleet launched or source edited. Review routing recovery EI-23972388180457924 is claimed by same session. Native tools serve olderrelease; acceptance calls use verified current :3170 CLI.\n\n**Next:** Complete exact spec-quality audit and two closed outside-lineage BAR critiques, then plans:start on :3170 and launch three visible Codex members, with this session leading acceptance and final shipment. No owner approval is pending; AUTO is authorized.\n\n## Goal\n\nStop agents from silently duplicating code, and give them the code facts they lack today, delivered where they decide: while writing a plan item, when claiming a work-item, while editing, and when completing.\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Audience.**\n- The coding agents in the fleet, who consume the signals.\n- Avi (owner), who reviews the outcome and pays the cost when copies drift apart.\n\n**Problem.**\n- **Agents copy and rename code instead of extending shared code.** A 2026-10-21 measurement over 10,339 first-party TypeScript files found 164 structural clone families (404 functions) after excluding vendored and retired copies. The largest is 10 copy-and-renamed governor-gate functions.\n- **Our code intelligence lacks the signals to catch it.** It has no clone detection and no code embeddings (concept-search is lexical). It also has no change-history signal, no code-to-Postgres lineage, no complexity metric and no per-test coverage.\n- **Prompt rules alone do not hold.** RepoReuse found duplicated logic in 50.8% of agent task chains by turn 5. SlopCodeBench found quality guidance lowers initial bloat but not the degradation rate.\n\n**Outcome.**\n1. An agent about to write, or having just written, a copy is told specifically where the existing code is.\n2. New copies cannot accumulate unnoticed: a ratchet catches them per change, and a nightly sweep files families.\n3. Agents claiming or completing work see, for the exact functions they change: copy siblings, co-change partners, who last reshaped them and why, table readers and writers, and which tests actually run them.\n4. Reuse is measured per agent and model.\n\n**Non-goals.**\n- No pull-request review bot.\n- No ML predictive test selection.\n- No graph visualization, architecture wiki, expert graph query or statement-level dataflow. Those are already queued in native-code-intelligence-optional-evaluations-2026-10-15.\n- No blocking hook and no blocking lint without a later owner decision.\n- Only TypeScript/TSX in the first cut.\n- No change to the anchors plan's claim-brief item while its acceptance bars are under repair, unless Avi chooses that.\n\n**Source turns.**\n- Owner directive #2101: detect duplication, and survey prior art online.\n- Owner directive #2115: which other code-intelligence features we lack.\n- Owner directive #2117: should the new signals also feed the enriched work-item briefs and plan information.\n- Owner directive #2120: write it into a plan with a detailed summary.\n- Reports: rpt_b888fe6c-e4e3-4ab2-8b45-a8ec1d003e5a (duplicates, corrected edition), rpt_5351029e-4ba3-4d45-b727-428136675151 (gap analysis), rpt_6da91525-9088-4766-baf8-44ad8360c276 (brief mapping).\n\n**Scenarios.**\n1. **Edit-time copy warning.** An agent writes a governor gate that matches an existing one. Right after the edit it sees a two-line note naming the existing function, the 9 other copies and a shared-factory hint.\n2. **Authoring reuse hint.** A planner writes \"add retry with backoff to X\". Adding the item returns existing similar functions, so the item says *use or extend* rather than *build*.\n3. **Claim-time brief.** An agent claims a work-item anchored on a function that has copies. The brief says a fix probably applies to the siblings. It also lists files that usually change with it, names the work-item that last reshaped it, and lists the tables it writes.\n4. **Completion advisory.** At completion the advisory notes \"1 of 10 copies changed; 9 untouched\" and \"this change introduced a new copy of Y\".\n5. **Nightly sweep.** New clone families become one work-item each and are never re-filed. Intentional copies go on an accept list.\n6. **Anti-pattern flag.** An agent writes a log-only catch or a `?? 0` fallback on a database read, and the edit-time note flags the error-masking pattern.\n7. **Lineage query.** \"Who writes this table column?\" is one `graph:query` call.\n8. **Reuse score.** Avi reads a reuse score per agent and model: redundancy rate, and whether the agent searched before writing.\n\n## Relationship to existing plans\n\n- **Duplicate discovery.** The duplicate-detection work here is the build of the duplicate half of item 5 of `native-code-intelligence-optional-evaluations-2026-10-15` (dead exports, test gaps, duplicate discovery). That item stays the evaluation of record.\n- **Brief integration.** It plugs into `plan-item-code-anchors-2026-10-20` (authoring items 2, 4 and 12; claim-time brief item 8; completion advisory item 9) through section providers. It does not edit that plan's items unless Avi chooses to widen them; that choice is an open card in his Inbox.\n- **Measurement.** Every new push leg reports through the push-outcome instrument (item 41) and the adoption instrument (item 33) of `native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09`.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Clone index.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"TS/TSX function bodies get Type-1 (exact) and Type-2 (renamed) fingerprints and a Type-3 (near-miss) leg, are classified as vendored, retired or test, and are updated incrementally per file blob SHA. On the 2026-10-21 tree the index reproduces the probe's family counts within a stated tolerance and finds the 10-copy governor-gate family.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:2589f593-aa14-4892-9abd-c152eca07a4d:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The incremental TS/TSX clone index returns the expected exact, renamed and near-miss families for the declared corpus.\",\"falsifier\":\"A labelled copy is missed, unrelated functions group together, classification is wrong, or a changed blob leaves stale members. Unfrozen/missing corpus or a count difference on its exact manifest, a floor/exclusion mismatch, or latency telemetry presented as an invariant.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Build the cold corpus and update one changed file through the index; verify exact/renamed/near fixtures, the governor-gate fixture, vendored/test/retired classification, SHA invalidation, and recorded cold/incremental latency. Use testing:run for the named suite and preserve the exact source/test fingerprints. Verify frozen original probe path/blob/source manifests before implementation; after80-node floor and vendor/retired exclusion reproduce164families/404functions exactly (tolerance0) and ten-member governor-gate. Missing manifest cannot be replaced with current-tree counts. Record latency workload/hardware/repetitions as telemetry only; test SHA removal/update and syntax/classification cases.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/clone-index.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Query surface.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"`graph:query` gains `similar` (a name, a file and line, or a snippet) and `clones` (paths). `similar` returns ranked matches (exact, renamed, near or semantic), each with a score, path:line and signature; `clones` returns copy families. No new tool. Golden queries over fixtures pass.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:2589f593-aa14-4892-9abd-c152eca07a4d:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The existing graph query surface returns ranked, located similarity matches and clone families.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any supported name, path/line or snippet query fails or a result omits match kind, score, signature or location. Uncalibrated scores, nondeterministic ties, guessed ambiguous locations, stale data presented current, unbounded limits, or increased tool weight.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Invoke graph:query similar by name, path/line and snippet, and clones by paths against a known corpus; assert rankings, tags, scores, signatures and source locations. Use testing:run for the named suite and preserve the exact source/test fingerprints. Pin Design score units/cutoffs/kind+score+location tie order; exercise default10/max50 and version-pinned cursors, ambiguous names, invalid lines, stale index and unchanged graph tool weight.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/reuse-graph.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Edit-time advisory.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"After a TS/TSX edit that introduces a copy, the agent gets a note of at most 3 lines naming the existing code and giving a call, extract or widen-the-signature hint. There is no note when nothing matches. Only hash lookups run on the hot path. It is advisory only. A latency-budget test with a fake clock passes, and deliveries are recorded.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:2589f593-aa14-4892-9abd-c152eca07a4d:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A TS/TSX edit introducing a clone delivers a bounded advisory through the existing push channel.\",\"falsifier\":\"A clone edit receives no note, a non-match receives one, the note exceeds three lines, or the hot path performs unbounded work. Duplicate native emissions, >25ms fake-clock work, hot-path parsing/network/judging, stale index represented as no clones, or missing issued record.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Exercise native Edit/Write/MultiEdit delivery with match and non-match fixtures; assert three-line cap, fake-clock budget, hash-only hot-path lookups and code_intel_pushes delivery records. Use testing:run for the named suite and preserve the exact source/test fingerprints. PostToolBatch is the only emission boundary. Test20changed files/100000-indexed-functions with fake-clock<=25ms, per-batch/family deduplication and at most3lines; assert no hot-path AST parse, I/O, scan, embedding or judge calls. Edit/Write/MultiEdit use the same path.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/clone-advisory.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Ratchet.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A diff-scoped `lint:new-clones` reports newly introduced Type-1/2 copies against a shrink-only baseline, warn-only. A planted copy is reported; an unchanged tree reports nothing.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:2589f593-aa14-4892-9abd-c152eca07a4d:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The warn-only clone ratchet reports only new Type-1/2 duplication in changed paths.\",\"falsifier\":\"An unchanged baseline warns, a new clone is missed, accepted baseline growth occurs, or the warning blocks promotion. A rename-only member creates a new warning or baseline removal permits later growth.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run lint:new-clones against unchanged and planted-copy fixtures with changed-path filters; verify shrink-only baseline handling and test:affected warn-only wiring. Use testing:run for the named suite and preserve the exact source/test fingerprints. Use canonical identity/version semantics from Design; include unchanged historical copies, removed copies and an attempted baseline-growth mutation.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/clone-ratchet.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Sweep.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A durable nightly routine files one work-item per clone family, keyed by family hash so it is never re-filed, with an accept list. Vendored copies become derive-and-sync items. Two consecutive runs on an unchanged tree file nothing new.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:2589f593-aa14-4892-9abd-c152eca07a4d:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The separately armed nightly sweep durably files each eligible clone family once at its declared cadence with the exact stored action.\",\"falsifier\":\"A repeated unchanged sweep files another item or accepted/vendor families receive the wrong disposition. Concurrent/restarted runs duplicate an unchanged identity/version, or merged/split/expired acceptance has no defined disposition. The dedicated sweep schedule is absent, unarmed, has wrong cadence/timezone/action/input, or fails to dispatch its due action.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the routine twice on an unchanged labelled corpus and inspect the canonical family key, owned work-items, ranking, accept list, vendored derive-and-sync disposition and extracted-family regression tests. Use testing:run for the named suite and preserve the exact source/test fingerprints. Use versioned signature identity, merge/split aliases, explicit accept-list owner/reason/expiry and unique durable filing key. Exercise concurrent runs, restart, unchanged closed tasks, membership rename/add/remove and expired acceptance. P020 remediation has independent R17. P008 extends the existing plan-schedulable system-action registry with clone-family-sweep, since no existing action performs this scan. Author a dedicated clone-family-sweep-papercusp plan using plans:set-schedule schedule={kind:cron,cron:0 2 * * *,tzid:America/New_York,concurrency:skip,catchup:skip-old,action:{system:clone-family-sweep,input:{harness:papercusp,clonePolicy:reuse-signals-v1}}}; then separately plans:arm-schedule. The integration check exercises both verbs and the due dispatch with a controlled clock, and rejects absent/unarmed/wrong-action/wrong-input schedules. P008 must also preserve readback of the actual stored schedule, armed state and registered planSchedulable action; a sweep-action fixture alone is insufficient.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/clone-sweep.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — Engine choice by evidence.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The Type-3 engine is chosen from a recorded bench of jscpd v5, similarity-ts and an in-house candidate in the existing fair-comparison harness, on a labelled sample.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:2589f593-aa14-4892-9abd-c152eca07a4d:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The recorded labelled benchmark determines the near-miss engine selection.\",\"falsifier\":\"The selected engine lacks comparable precision, recall, runtime and dependency evidence against the declared candidates. Only one candidate runs, corpus/thresholds move after results, candidate unavailability is treated as a pass, or P004 implements a different winner.\",\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the existing fair-comparison harness with the labelled positives and hand-checked negatives for jscpd v5, similarity-ts and the in-house candidate; preserve unavailable-engine evidence honestly, record comparable results and the selection Decision. Use testing:run for the named suite and preserve the exact source/test fingerprints.
