Existing project has no Postgres parser dependency; do not hand-roll SQL grammar.\",\n      \"candidates\": [\n        {\n          \"name\": \"libpg-query\",\n          \"verdict\": \"chosen\",\n          \"why\": \"Uses the real PostgreSQL query parser and the current18-series type schema; best fits CTE/quotedidentifier/migration cases.\"\n        },\n        {\n          \"name\": \"pgsql-ast-parser\",\n          \"verdict\": \"rejected\",\n          \"why\": \"MIT version12.0.2 uses a separate nearley/moo grammar; prefer PostgreSQL's parser for the declared syntax contract.\"\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    {\n      \"need\": \"Structural anti-pattern execution and near-miss comparison host\",\n      \"decision\": \"skip-research\",\n      \"reason\": \"Reuse the existing native ast-grep façade and existing fair-comparison host; they already fit. P-003 executes all declared candidate tools and records the winner before any P-004 production adapter dependency is added; update this declaration with that measured winner.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"notApplicable\": null\n}\n```\n\n## Conformance\n\n```conformance\n{\n  \"requirements\": {\n    \"R-20\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"claim-provider-delivery-missing\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"The actual claim response loses an expected provider, mandatory base, issued identity or declared cap.\",\n          \"stage\": \"delivery\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"A current-build anchored claim replay misses its expected capped clone/history/SQL/coverage payload or uses the wrong build/source identity.\",\n            \"bindWhen\": \"P-010 integrates the P-009 seam with all P-013/P-014/P-016 producers; bind to its exact runtime replay probe before completing P-010/R-20 and repeat on final shipped artifact.\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-21\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"authoring-provider-delivery-missing\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"The actual plan authoring response omits expected similar-function/copy-family hints or violates base/caps.\",\n          \"stage\": \"delivery\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"plans:new or plans:add-item on the named fixture loses expected hints or per-provider issued identity.\",\n            \"bindWhen\": \"P-010 implements authoring delivery; bind to exact current-build authoring replay probe before completing P-010/R-21 and repeat on final shipped artifact.\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"R-22\": {\n      \"violatedWhen\": [\n        {\n          \"id\": \"completion-provider-delivery-missing\",\n          \"failureMode\": \"The actual completion response omits a declared consequence, blocks completion or turns unknown coverage into absence.\",\n          \"stage\": \"delivery\",\n          \"pendingBinding\": {\n            \"observation\": \"Completing the named WI fixture loses one of five expected provider payloads, breaks budget/base or omits runtime/source identity.\",\n            \"bindWhen\": \"P-010 implements completion delivery; bind to exact current-build completion replay probe before completing P-010/R-22 and repeat on final shipped artifact.\"\n          }\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n- **One index, existing readers and channels.** Extend packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/ and existing graph:query operations, push-snapshot/working-set invalidation, code_intel_pushes, anchors brief sections and completion/authoring advisories. D-007 remains the integration authority. No parallel query tool or brief system. Hooks/lints stay advisory.\n\n### Deterministic delivery and budgets\n\nPostToolBatch is the single delivery boundary for Edit/Write/MultiEdit. Deduplicate a batch by (owner, invocation, provider, file blob, canonical family); aggregate all changed files before emitting at most one three-line copy note. The synchronous hook uses precomputed hash/index lookups only: no parsing, near-miss scan, embedding, network, SQL scan or LLM. Index refresh happens off the hook; a stale/missing index yields unknown/no note. A fake-clock test on 100,000 indexed functions and 20 changed files permits <=25ms of lookup/format work. Cold <60s and incremental <200ms are telemetry only: record CPU/cores/RAM, commit, file/function counts, 5 cold runs and p50/p95 over 100 one-file changes; do not fail BARs using host-dependent elapsed time.\n\nExisting mandatory brief content is rendered first, charged to the same 3,000 Unicode-code-point limit and retained unchanged; if it uses the budget, omit every optional provider. Provider envelopes/labels count. Use the remaining budget in the order below; truncate only at complete line boundaries, never exceed a provider cap or add a new section. Each provider has a 750ms soft deadline and all optional providers share a 6,000ms hard deadline including serialization. Expiration/failure cancels that provider, records unknown and preserves other providers/base content.\n\n| priority | provider | cap in characters | claim destination |\n|---|---|---:|---|\n| 10 | clone siblings / similar functions | 600 | impact |\n| 20 | co-change partners | 250 | one existing co-change line |\n| 30 | work-item provenance | 400 | what-changed-since-planning |\n| 40 | SQL readers/writers | 450 | impact |\n| 50 | dynamic coverage or labelled static fallback | 400 | tests |\n\nAuthoring and completion use the same ordering/caps/global limits, with surface-specific payloads. plans:new/plans:add-item show existing similar functions and copy-family flags; claim shows siblings, co-change, provenance, SQL and coverage; completion shows untouched siblings, new copies, untouched co-change partners, unchecked readers and uncovered changed lines. Overlap advisory includes unanchored co-change partners. Each source has a separate code_intel_pushes row containing provider, surface, invocation, work-item/plan-item, source/index version and truncation/error state. Match/no-match, overflow, timeout and provider-failure cases are tested independently on all three surfaces.\n\n### Clone and query contracts\n\nBefore implementing P-002, freeze the original 2026-10-21 probe input manifest (path/blob SHAs, probe source/version, exclusions and normalization) as a fixture artifact; do not retune it to the new implementation. The recorded population is the cited 10,339 first-party TS/TSX files: compare after the 80-AST-node body floor and after vendored/retired exclusion. Required reproduced counts are 164 Type-2 structural families / 404 member functions, tolerance zero on that exact frozen manifest, plus the ten-member governor-gate family. A missing original manifest is an explicit unverified prerequisite, never a new live-tree baseline. Tests include exact, renamed, near-miss, test/vendor/retired, parse-error and changed-blob cases.\n\nCanonical family identity is a versioned normalization digest plus language/detector class, independent of member paths/order. Adding/removing/renaming members preserves identity when the canonical signature stays identical. Changed signatures produce a new version linked to the prior family; merges use the lexicographically smallest surviving identity and alias the others; splits retain identity only for the part containing the prior canonical representative and link the other parts as children. A unique durable (workspace, family identity, version, disposition) key arbitrates concurrent sweeps. Accept-list entries pin identity/version, reason, owner and optional expiry; changed versions require renewed acceptance. Never re-file an unchanged identity/version, including after task closure. Vendor families produce derive-and-sync tasks. Test two concurrent runs, restarts, membership changes, merge/split and expired acceptance. P-020 separately proves a shared factory's behavior/caller equivalence and measured duplicate reduction.\n\ngraph:query similar supports unambiguous symbol name, path/line and snippet; ambiguity returns candidates rather than guessing, invalid locations return typed errors and stale index reports stale/unknown. Default limit 10, maximum 50 with opaque version-pinned cursor; ties sort kind exact, renamed, near, semantic then score descending then path/line/signature lexical. Exact and renamed scores are 1 within their separately tagged kinds; near uses token Jaccard [0,1]; semantic uses the recorded calibrated hybrid score [0,1], never raw cosine/RRF masquerading as probability. Filter near >=0.75 and semantic >=0.70; fixtures pin scores, cutoff and ties. Query tool weight remains the existing graph:query weight; record before/after catalog weight and use no new tool.\n\nP-003 preregisters a versioned labelled corpus before timing: >=40 Type-1/2 positives, >=40 near-miss positives, >=20 semantic positives and >=100 hand-labelled hard negatives sampled across distinct subsystems with fixed seed. All three candidates (jscpd v5, similarity-ts, in-house MinHash/LSH) run identical inputs/exclusions in five repeats. Report exact precision/recall counts, Wilson 95% intervals, p95 elapsed time, added direct/transitive dependencies, native binary/download requirement and package bytes. Eligible Type-3 winner requires precision >=0.90 and recall >=0.80 on labelled near-miss/negative cases. Rank eligible engines by F1, then fewer native requirements, fewer added transitive dependencies, lower p95, then lexical engine id. A candidate unavailable after a documented install/build attempt makes comparison incomplete; never select from only one runnable candidate. No eligible winner means repair the candidates/corpus through a recorded decision; P-004 consumes and asserts the recorded winner, version and settings.\n\nP-012 reuses pgvector/embedding sidecar. A versioned relevance set of >=20 concept queries pins expected relevant functions in top10. Type-4 filing requires the existing configured judge's exact model id, prompt digest/version, candidate/source blob ids, recorded request/structured output and confidence >=0.90 with duplicate=true. Unavailable, malformed or abstaining judge output files nothing and records unknown; replay fixtures test accept/reject/abstain/outage. Model or prompt changes invalidate previous decisions.\n\n### Other signal populations and unknown semantics\n\nP-011 initial rule IDs: error-empty-catch, error-log-only-catch, db-read-fallback, unsafe-as-any, newly-skipped-test, widened-test-timeout, sync-io-in-async, await-in-serial-loop, unbounded-promise-all and full-table-read-filter. Match only documented AST shapes; use positive/negative syntax fixtures and BEFORE/AFTER fixtures for new skips and widened numeric timeouts. Unchanged historical findings do not become newly introduced warnings. Each advisory is bounded to three lines and is warn-only.\n\nP-013 co-change uses a declared rolling 90-day first-parent commit window, excluding merge commits' duplicate second-parent changes, generated/vendor/retired files and mass changes >100 eligible files. File identity follows recorded rename pairs (>=50% git similarity); ambiguous moves are unknown. Score is shared eligible commits / union eligible commits, min 3 shared commits; ties by path. Provenance joins successful Edit/Write/MultiEdit invocation id -> exact session owner -> work-item assignment interval -> changed symbol's file/blob/range. Fixtures name the expected invocation/session/WI join, including multiple/absent assignments; ambiguous, stale, missing or truncated ledger yields unknown, never git author attribution.\n\nP-014 uses a maintained Postgres parser on statically resolvable SQL strings/tagged templates. Supported grammar: SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with schema-qualified or quoted identifiers, aliases, joins, WITH/CTEs and resolvable column refs; classify migrations' CREATE/ALTER/DROP as schema writes. Resolve sync resolver and invalidation declarations through their existing typed registry references. Parameter values are safe; dynamic table/column identifiers, unresolved helper fragments, ambiguous unqualified columns, procedural SQL and parser failures yield explicit partial/unknown edges and source locations. Never infer complete no-read/no-write from partial parsing. Tests cover each grammar case, resolver/invalidation linkage and unsupported dynamic cases.\n\nP-015 complexity v1: cyclomatic=1 + if/for/for-in/for-of/while/do/catch/case-without-default/conditional-expression/&&/||/?? branches; nesting is maximum branch/function-body depth; cognitive is sum(1+current branch nesting) for those branches, excluding nested function bodies. Pin TypeScript compiler and metric version. Existing symbol identity uses file + export/name + signature; recorded renames carry baseline, splits partition by predecessor ranges and new functions get baseline0. Ratchet warns on a positive per-symbol delta; removals reduce the shrink-only baseline. Unknown predecessor identity is labelled unknown, never a zero historical value. Health/hotspot providers use the efficacy policy below before inclusion.\n\nP-016 coverage identity is (source commit + file blob + canonical test id + test-run id + collector version). Keep at most30days and the latest10 complete runs per source/test pair. A map is fresh only for matching source blobs and a successful complete declared test population; partial/failed/expired runs cannot prove a line unexecuted. Show observed execution from valid rows; otherwise label unknown and static-reach fallback explicitly. A no-test-executes warning requires complete fresh population; changed-line advisory carries its exact run/population.\n\nP-017 reports hot implementation invocation counts and \"not observed in [start,end)\" over a declared rolling7day window of successful dispatched tool traffic. Snapshot registry-link version/completeness and ledger retention with the counts. Missing links, partial retention, missing sessions or failed reads yield unknown. Unobserved never means dead/never-executed. No health/hot-cold provider enters a brief merely because the index exists.\n\nP-018 computes an as-of snapshot (source graph/blob version, lock generation, working-set generation, peer presence timestamps) and repeats once if generations change during collection; unresolved races return unknown. Peers are other workspace owners with nonexpired lock or working set and live heartbeat <=120s. Caller scope is direct statically resolved callers, including same-file caller functions; indirect/unresolved callers are labelled partial, never guessed. Exported signature is TS compiler public parameter/return/type-parameter/export metadata; body-only compatible changes do not trigger. Test locks-only, working-set-only, both, stale/dead, same-file, indirect, graph-stale, race and no-peer cases. Extend snapshotInterfaceLeg rather than duplicate it.\n\n### Measurement and scoped runtime proof\n\nP-008 registers clone-family-sweep as a planSchedulable system action on the existing system-action registry: this is a new case on the maintained scheduler, required because no registered action scans clone families. Its dedicated clone-family-sweep-papercusp recurrence is authored with plans:set-schedule using cron 0 2 * * *, America/New_York, concurrency skip and catchup skip-old, action {system:clone-family-sweep,input:{harness:papercusp,clonePolicy:reuse-signals-v1}}. Separately arm with plans:arm-schedule. Preserve actual stored schedule and armed-state readback plus the registered action; integration tests exercise due firing and falsify absent/unarmed/wrong-action/input/cadence/timezone.\n\n\"Issued\" means included in a server response, \"delivered\" requires independently observed client receipt; do not equate them. For every provider/leg, denominator partitions are observed acted-on, observed not-acted-on and unknown. Each row pins observation window and completeness. Use a per-leg/provider selector for follow-up relevant file/symbol reads/edits and grep-after-push in the next20 invocations or30minutes, whichever ends first; missing/truncated activity is unknown, never zero. Metrics are redundancy per1000 added non-generated lines, successful search before first write per eligible work-item, and resolved cross-file calls / all resolved calls; unresolved calls are a separate unknown count.\n\nUse the existing outcomes reader and registered rubric checks. plans:set-schedule authors a daily rubric-rescore recurrence and plans:arm-schedule separately arms it; verify both stored schedule and armed state, emit scores from ledger, and watch rubric:criterion-regressed. Provider efficacy is preregistered: deterministic work-item hash holds out10% of eligible exposures by provider; after >=14days, >=100 observed treatment and >=100 observed holdout windows within28days, compare acted-on rate and relevant grep-after-push rate with Wilson95% intervals. If treatment's upper bound is <= holdout's lower bound for both measures, reversibly disable the provider via its existing flag, record evidence/reason, and preserve the kill-switch reversal. Incomplete/immature populations produce an explicit keep/disable recommendation with unknown confidence and no disabling. Fixture populations prove mature-disable, mature-keep and unknown/immature behavior; no shipment claim requires fabricating14days of live traffic.\n\nTree BARs have no generic runtime boilerplate. P-009 owns a current-build claim replay on a disposable anchored WI whose fixture code has clone siblings/co-change/provenance/SQL/coverage: assert response/base preservation, deterministic caps and per-provider issued identities. P-010 owns separate current-build authoring (plans:new/add-item) and completion replays on disposable plan/WI fixtures: assert existing-function hints and the five completion payloads. Capture action, response/independent client receipt, source+test fingerprints, runtime/build SHA and fixture object ids. After promotion, replay these same three actions against the exact shipped artifact; only final shipment uses release-operator. P-001 owns reconciliation only and receives no runtime proof.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002, P-004 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-008 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-012 | tree |\n| R-8 | P-011 | tree |\n| R-9 | P-013 | tree |\n| R-10 | P-014 | tree |\n| R-11 | P-015 | tree |\n| R-12 | P-016 | tree |\n| R-13 | P-017 | tree |\n| R-14 | P-018 | tree |\n| R-15 | P-009 | tree |\n| R-16 | P-019 | tree |\n| R-17 | P-020 | tree |\n| R-18 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-19 | P-010 | tree |\n| R-20 | P-010 | live |\n| R-21 | P-010 | live |\n| R-22 | P-010 | live |\n\n## Open choices for Avi\n\n1. **Brief scope:** pluggable brief sections now (recommended), or widen the anchors plan's claim-brief item now. Type-4 uses our pgvector 0.8.2 and the embed sidecar.\n\n### D-004 — New signals extend existing brief sections through capped providers, measured per signal\nDate: 2026-10-21\n[agent-proposed from rpt_6da91525] Signals become sources for sections the claim-time brief already has, not new sections:\n- impact gains copy siblings and table readers/writers;\n- tests gains dynamic coverage;\n- what-changed-since-planning gains work-item provenance;\n- one new co-change line.\n\nEach provider has a priority and a character cap inside 3,000 characters / 6 seconds, and its own code_intel_pushes record. Order: clone siblings, co-change and provenance, SQL lineage, dynamic coverage. Health and hot/cold flags only if measurement shows agents act on them. That was incomplete: native-code-intelligence-optional-evaluations-2026-10-15#P-005 already covers it (moved there by D-016 of the native plan). The prior request to maximize predecessor context was already completed by that session and imposes no implementation requirement.\nRelated: P-001, P-009\n\n### D-007 — Reconciliation: extend interface delivery, task briefs and the existing push outcome reader\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAffects: plan-item-code-anchors-2026-10-20, native-code-intelligence-ecosystem-and-dream-2026-10-09\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/push-channel.ts:675–709 implements snapshotInterfaceLeg with static consumers/tests and pinned strand checks, but it never reads peer locks or working sets. firstTouchFact at :309–319 already filters peer consumer locks, so P-018 extends the interface leg using this existing context rather than introducing a parallel advisory. Measured: PUSH_LEG_FLAGS at :27–37 and PushLegId are a closed typed map; new hook legs must extend that map/registration and their tests. Measured: task-brief.ts:19–20 already owns the 6000ms/3000-character budget, so P-009 extends this assembler with capped providers. Measured: native-adoption.ts:499 accepts leg:string, readNativePushOutcomes at :600 reads every code_intel_pushes row in a bounded window, and summarizeNativePushOutcomes at :690 groups arbitrary nonempty leg names; new leg/provider identities need no parallel outcome table. Measurement semantics: issued means placed in a server hook response, not proven client receipt; acted-on is evidence from the closed turn window, and missing/truncated activity remains unknown. The grep-after-push rubric selector currently scopes to the grep leg, so P-019 must explicitly extend/evidence new-provider interpretation instead of treating absent measurements as zero. Existing plans stay the authorities for duplicate evaluation and anchor/brief base scope. This decision supplies P-001's reconciliation deliverable; implementation remains subject to activation/start.\nRelated: P-001, P-009, P-018, P-019\n\n### D-008 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: reuse-signals-critique1195865-amend-v2\nRequest-Hash: 507d7812f75f089bce6d7063d27515309dee86df30499fa42ece1250dbbb6844\nActor: su-0dd61ff4-d577-4fe7-9f60-ea00a582bfea\nReason: Disposition all18 objections in thread-post:1195865 with predeclared populations, thresholds, unknown semantics, atomic delivery/remediation BARs and narrowly scoped current-build replays; Self route A remains selected at :4.\nScenarios: bursts are spaced; a transient 429 slows its own account; retries use the destination account's bucket; cancellation leaves no permit held; quota/overload behavior stays distinct.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Shared implementation.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Make Codex use the adaptive account governor already used by Claude while sharing its code.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Codex upstream attempts acquire pacing from the existing provider/account-keyed RateLimitGovernor; smoothing follows the same policy as Claude.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"A Codex attempt bypasses pacing or uses a duplicate provider-specific rate algorithm.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the named tests through npm run test:file; inspect the real gateway request traces and governor state rather than HTTP status alone.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway-account-rate-pacing.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n**R-2 — Isolated feedback.**\n```requirement\n{\n  \"intent\": {\n    \"request\": \"Handle repeated Codex rate 429s without shrinking unrelated account capacity.\"\n  },\n  \"acceptance\": {\n    \"condition\": \"Transient 429 feedback reduces only the affected Codex rate factor; quota/auth/overload/cancellation do not lower learned RPM and retries/hard pins retain their routing semantics.\",\n    \"falsifier\": \"An account-rate event penalizes a sibling/provider, a quota wall lowers RPM, or a hard pin switches credentials.\",\n    \"requiredTestLayers\": [\n      \"unit\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"verification\": {\n    \"method\": \"Run the named tests through npm run test:file; inspect the real gateway request traces and governor state rather than HTTP status alone.\",\n    \"check\": {\n      \"kind\": \"tests\",\n      \"files\": [\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway-account-rate-pacing.test.ts\",\n        \"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/upstream-outcome-classifier.test.ts\"\n      ]\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n**R-3 — Lifecycle verification.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Prove the integration enforces pacing and cleans up correctly.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Each first or retry attempt confines its selected-account governor permit and upstream TTFB budget to upstream execution, including when cancellation unwinds the attempt.\",\"falsifier\":\"A cancelled waiter sends upstream, cancellation releases an acquired permit zero or multiple times, local pacing consumes upstream TTFB, or a first/retry send skips its selected account rate bucket.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named tests through npm run test:file; inspect the real gateway request traces and governor state rather than HTTP status alone.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway-account-rate-pacing.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/request-kernel.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n## Design\nGeneralize the existing governor factory and extend the existing kernel admission lifecycle for per-attempt pacing before auth/upstream timers. Provider parsers translate feedback into the same governor policy. Preserve quota-aware selection, soft/hard pins and shared observability. No new capacity knobs or parallel limiter.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Integrate and prove\n- **P-001** `done` Integrate Codex attempts and normalized 429 feedback with the shared adaptive per-account governor. importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010019674 completed (done)\n- **P-002** `done` Add provider-parity regression tests, run focused checks, and report runtime activation requirements. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high — note: ← WI-6554700010019675 completed (done)\n\n## Now\nImplement in the owner-selected self route. Registration work-item WI-6554700010019510 holds the change while plan activation inputs are completed.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] R-1 retains shared Claude/Codex implementation and smoothing parity, R-2 retains feedback classification/isolation, and R-3 retains first/retry pacing, waiter cancellation, acquired-permit cleanup and local-wait exclusion from upstream TTFB. Committed141test suite and caught pacing mutation now exercise the production path.\nApproved-By: su-96f524b4-619c-481a-a77b-25a53b796d47\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1193506\nApproved-At: 2026-10-22T02:45:43.216Z\nRubric revision: 4 → 5\nSubject plan revision: 7 → 8\nChanged BARs: R-3\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-3\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"dbos-durability-right-sizing-2026-10-21","title":"Right-size durability: keep DBOS history bounded, and move the action half of four in-process jobs onto DBOS","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Right-size durability: keep DBOS history bounded, and move the action half of four in-process jobs onto DBOS\nslug: dbos-durability-right-sizing-2026-10-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: the owner and every agent that relies on claims, release requests, grading and notifications working after a bg-host restart.\nProblem: the 2026-10-21 audit (report rpt_22813d36-b65f-4a04-a53d-00b0c91fe28b) confirmed that keeping re-derivable checks, watchdogs, caches and lifecycle timers off DBOS was right (EI-1622). It also found three problems. (1) The DBOS history cleanup is behind: dbos.workflow_status had 421,051 rows / 597 MB, more than the 328k rows that froze the routine engine in June, with 290,291 finished rows past the 2-day retention. (2) Some in-process jobs record a decision and then carry out more steps, so a process exit in between loses those steps for good. (3) acceptance-grading-sweep, set to run every 60 s, took 42.6 min per tick, and its tick after the 18:56Z restart had not finished.\nOutcome: DBOS history stays under a fixed ceiling. A crash between \"decided\" and \"done\" no longer loses a promised consequence, a holder notice, or an owner push. The grading sweep finishes inside its interval. Empty ticks still write zero DBOS rows.\nNon-goals: moving watchdogs, sampling health checks, cache refreshers, socket/SSE/PTY keepalives, swarm pumps or file watchers onto DBOS; changing separate processes (inference gateway, MCP proxy, psu-launcher); re-architecting the routines engine; LIVE_GATE_OPS.\nSource turns: session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0 (owner: was the in-process design right, and audit what should move to DBOS); session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:9 (owner: write this into a plan). The item list and ordering are the agent's proposal from that audit [self-proposed, pending owner approval].\nScenarios:\n- The bg-host restarts after release-request-sweep has marked a request resolved but before it releases the claim. On the next boot the claim is released and both parties are told.\n- The cleanup has fallen behind. Within one day it is back under the ceiling. If the table ever crosses the ceiling, an alarm fires instead of the engine quietly slowing down.\n- A grading pass has 30 plans to dispatch. Its tick returns in seconds, each dispatch runs as its own durable workflow, and a restart mid-pass resumes the dispatches that had not finished.\n- A managed tick hangs. Within a few intervals an alarm names the timer, instead of the cadence going silent until the next restart.\n- A health check finds nothing to do. It writes nothing to DBOS, exactly as today.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — DBOS history stays bounded.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"dbos.workflow_status stays under a fixed row ceiling, finished rows older than the retention are removed, and the largest writer (routineFire, about 46k rows/day) is reduced or justified.\",\"rationale\":\"Measured 2026-10-21: 421,051 rows / 597 MB, 290,291 terminal rows past the 2-day retention; the daily GC has a 30 s budget (EI-26619264681971676).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Cleanup runs at least hourly (or loops until no victims remain, within a liveness bound), removes the oldest terminal rows first, and an alarm fires when the table exceeds the ceiling. After 48 h on the deployed build, terminal rows older than retention are under 5% of the table and the table is under the ceiling.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fail if any conjunct fails: a cleanup gap >3600000 ms without bounded drain, an out-of-order eligible deletion, deletion of nonterminal/not-expired data, missing zero-work log, count>C without an independent alarm within60000 ms, N>=300000 at24h or48h, expiredTerminal/N>=0.05 at48h (N=0 ratio0), or any >2000/day routine without measured reduction or individual justification. Missing settings/window/cadence/volume/alarm evidence is unknown, never pass.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"dbos-workflow-gc\",\"routine-fire-volume\",\"workflow-status-ceiling-alarm\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"deployed\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Contract parameters and conjunctive evidence: Cleanup runs at least hourly (or loops until no victims remain, within a liveness bound), removes the oldest terminal rows first, and an alarm fires when the table exceeds the ceiling. After 48 h on the deployed build, terminal rows older than retention are under 5% of the table and the table is under the ceiling. Ceiling C=300000; retention=2 days; terminal statuses are SUCCESS, ERROR, MAX_RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED and CANCELLED. Eligibility is updated_at < observationTime−retention; oldest-first order is created_at ascending, workflow_uuid ascending as tie-breaker. In-flight rows and their recovery data remain untouched. At 24 h after deployment N<C (catch-up); at 48 h N<C AND expiredTerminal/N<0.05, defining the empty-table ratio as zero. Enabled cleanup starts at intervals <=3600000 ms or drains all eligible work within its declared bounded invocation; each pass logs even zero removals. A count>C raises an alarm independent of DBOS within 60000 ms of the crossing. Each routine measured above 2000 committed starts per rolling 24 h has either a measured reduction or an individual durable-execution justification. These are conjunctive, separately evidenced obligations.\\n\\nBind named unit safety, budget, resume and cadence tests plus real-SQL eligibility/order and alarm integration tests. Match required unit+integration layers to the structured files; create/register the planned integration file before binding. Retain a complete bg-host deployed provenance bundle: build SHA, runtime identity, window start/end, GC/retention/ceiling/cadence configuration, status/age counts at24h and48h, GC run ledger including zero runs, an alarm receipt and latency, and committed-start counters grouped by routine over the same defined24h interval. Retained GC-pruned history is not a write-rate counter. Every conjunct needs separate evidence; a test pass cannot substitute for deployed time.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/dbos-workflow-gc.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/dbos-workflow-gc.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: seed mixed terminal/nonterminal rows with conflicting created_at/updated_at order and equal timestamps; run bounded passes, interrupt/resume, assert eligibility, deterministic ordering, dependent-row safety and zero logs. Independently falsify cadence, ordering, ceiling/5% equality, alarm latency and writer justification. Preserve build/config/window provenance and repeat actual bg-host count/age measurements at24h and48h; fake time does not satisfy deployed windows.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — The grading sweep finishes inside its interval, and its dispatches survive restarts.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"acceptance-grading-sweep ticks finish well inside 60 s, and each per-plan grader dispatch is a durable workflow keyed by plan and gradeable-since.\",\"rationale\":\"Measured tick of 2,557 s with 42 fires skipped, and a tick stuck since boot (EI-26619271533407778).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"On the deployed build, no acceptance-grading-sweep tick exceeds its interval for 24 h, and a restart during a pass completes the outstanding dispatches without duplicating any.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fail on any tick >60000 ms, an unfinished over-budget tick, missing/unaccounted tick/slot/error/observation gap, disabled/unregistered/non-running timer, absent nonempty positive control, or lost/duplicate logical dispatch after restart before admission, after admission before dispatch, or after effect before acknowledgement. Missing complete24h bg-host or deployed restart provenance is unknown, never pass.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"acceptance-grading-sweep\",\"grader-dispatch-workflow\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"deployed\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Contract parameters and conjunctive evidence: On the deployed build, no acceptance-grading-sweep tick exceeds its interval for 24 h. The enabled timer executes at configured interval60000 ms, with every tick duration <=60000 ms; complete records include starts, finishes, unfinished ticks, failures, skipped slots and observation gaps. Nonempty positive-control work is dispatched. A restart during a pass completes every outstanding scoped(plan, gradeable-since) logical dispatch exactly once across repeated/concurrent scans; a new gradeable-since permits a distinct action. Timing and restart recovery are separate conjuncts, each mandatory.\\n\\nCapture every deployed bg-host tick's start/end/duration and disposition over an actual24h window; reconcile scheduled slots, errors, unfinished work, restarts and gaps. An empty warning-log grep is insufficient because warning thresholds omit short overruns. Unit-test bounded scans and integration-test fresh-process recovery on the same durable store at discovery/admission/effect/ack boundaries; use durable dispatch receipts and receiver deduplication keyed by workspace,harness,plan,gradeable-since. Retain build/settings/window, timer registration/liveness and deployed restart artifacts separately from unit+integration bindings. Create/register the planned integration file before binding.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-grading-sweep-run.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-grading-sweep-run.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: enable a60s timer; feed empty then multiple eligible plans and verify the positive control. Crash before admission, after admission before dispatch and after the dispatch effect before ack; restart on the same store and reconcile outstanding identities/effects with zero losses or logical duplicates. Repeat/concurrent scans reuse the same identity; a changed gradeable-since yields a distinct identity. Collect a second complete actual24h window for replication without replacing the first24h requirement.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — A release-request consequence is never lost to a process exit.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Once release-request-sweep resolves a request, the announced consequence (reclaim, escalate, or notice) completes even if the process exits partway.\",\"rationale\":\"Code read: the request is marked resolved before the release and notices, and later ticks only see unresolved requests (EI-26619273576946393; same symptom as dropped EI-21195984035964741).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For each resolved release request, the promised consequence completes exactly once logically after any process exit and restart.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fail if any applicable comment, lock release, claim release, hold clear, required party notice or escalation is missing or logically duplicated after restart at any resolve/admission/step/effect/ack boundary, or if recovery alters a successor's ownership. A test that still passes when durable handoff is disabled fails the required mutation control.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"release-consequence-workflow\",\"release-request-sweep\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Contract parameters and conjunctive evidence: After a release request is resolved, every applicable promised consequence completes exactly once logically after process exit/restart: comment, lock release, claim release, hold clear, required notices to both parties and branch-required escalation. Cover reclaim, escalate and notice branches; record explicit non-applicability per branch. Recovery preserves any successor's claim/lock/hold and never applies a prior claimant's release to its successor.\\n\\nUse the actual resolving CAS and consequence runner with a fresh-process restart over the same durable store. Persist recoverable action identity with the resolve before advancing; stable logical effect IDs plus transactional receiver deduplication (or equivalent guarantee) cover effect-before-ack replay. Enumerate the branch/effect matrix, include successor-claim negative controls, and bind the integration test. Mutation required: disable durable handoff/run the consequence outside its durable workflow and show the crash-recovery test fails; DBOS replay alone does not establish external exactly-once effects.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-release-request.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: for each reclaim/escalate/notice branch seed a request and expected effect matrix; exit after resolve before admission, after admission, between each applicable effect and after effect before ack. Start a fresh process on the same store; reconcile all effects exactly once and successor preservation. Run paired baseline/mutant disabling durable handoff; require baseline pass and mutant caught.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Claim-release follow-ups survive a process exit.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"When stale-claim-sweep releases a claim, the holder notice, dead-letter broadcast and audit row are delivered even if the process exits right after the release commits.\",\"rationale\":\"The release commits first and the notices follow, and the next tick cannot find that release again.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A committed stale-claim release completes its full holder-notice, dead-letter-broadcast and audit follow-up set exactly once logically after process exit and restart.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fail if holder notice OR dead-letter broadcast OR audit row is absent or logically duplicated after a fresh-process restart following release commit or any effect/ack boundary; also fail on an unrecoverable release/admission gap or an altered successor claim.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"stale-claim-sweep\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Contract parameters and conjunctive evidence: After a stale claim release commits, the holder notice, dead-letter broadcast and audit row each complete exactly once logically despite process exit. The release remains recoverable until all three effects complete; repeated delivery and recovery do not duplicate any logical effect or change a successor claim.\\n\\nExercise the actual stale-claim sweep and delivery path. Persist follow-up intents with release in one transaction/outbox, or another durable action identity admitted before the release can become undiscoverable; starting a workflow only after commit is insufficient. Retain stable batch membership/identity and deduplicate receivers. Add/register the planned integration file; exit after release commit and each effect/ack boundary, restart fresh on the same store, inspect all three effects. Generic timer unit tests alone are insufficient.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/work-items-stale-claim-sweep.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: release a stale claim with all three expected effects; terminate immediately after commit, then at each effect/ack boundary. Restart using the same store, retry/concurrently rescan and assert one logical holder notice,broadcast,audit row plus preserved successor state. Deliberately drop/duplicate each of the three to prove each detector fails.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Owner- and agent-visible fire-and-forget side effects are durable.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Notifications and messages fired with un-awaited promises from request handlers either go through a durable path or are recorded as safe to lose, and new ones are blocked.\",\"rationale\":\"84 files use `void (async`; sampled sites include the plans:set-status needs-human push. The repo shows repeated fire-and-forget losses (EI-10800, WI-10000734).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every un-awaited call to a notify/send/escalate function is classified as durable or safe-to-lose with a reason. Each owner-facing one goes through a durable path. A shrink-only lint fails on a new unclassified one.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fail if the pinned source-revision census omits a matching tracked source site, has a missing/duplicate classification/reason/path, labels a mandatory push/notice safe-to-lose, accepts a synthetic new unclassified site, or loses/duplicates a required converted delivery after restart. An absent/unregistered/unrun planned detector or incomplete population partition is unknown/unmet.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"fire-and-forget-inventory\",\"fire-and-forget-lint\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Contract parameters and conjunctive evidence: A closed, reproducible census covers every in-scope un-awaited notify/send/escalate call in tracked product source, including wrapper/alias calls. Each stable site ID has classification, reason and a durable delivery-path reference when durable. Every required owner push and mandatory R-3/R-4 notice is durable; safe-to-lose cannot waive those promises. A shrink-only check rejects each new unclassified site. Other required owner/agent-visible conversions survive request-process exit without lost or duplicate logical delivery; R-3/R-4 retain ownership of their specific consequence recovery.\\n\\nRecord the lint --list population with source SHA and stable site IDs; classify each entry with reason and durable-path ref, and explicitly reconcile additions/removals. Historical84-file counts do not prove completeness. P-008 creates and registers fire-and-forget-classification.test.ts before any proof binding. Run synthetic-new-site rejection and classification controls, plus fresh-process request/delivery integration recovery for P-009's needs-human push and other conversions; create/register the planned integration file. Retain the complete coverage population/checked/notChecked/notApplicable/residue partition and owners for residue.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/fire-and-forget-classification.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/fire-and-forget-classification.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: regenerate the census at the pinned revision, compare every stable ID against classifications and delivery paths, inject a new unclassified aliased/wrapped notify site and require lint failure. Remove it and require pass. Crash a committed needs-human push before delivery and after effect before ack, restart fresh and inspect exactly one logical delivery.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-6 — A hung managed tick is reported.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"When a managed timer's tick holds the re-entrancy guard for several intervals, an alarm names the timer.\",\"rationale\":\"scheduled-registry only logs 'still running', so a hung tick silently stops its cadence until restart (observed on acceptance-grading-sweep).\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A tick held past a threshold (default 5 intervals, at least 5 min) raises a resolvable alarm naming the timer and its held time, and resolves when the tick ends.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fail if an alarm raises below/atT, none raises pastT within the watcher bound, name/held-time/episode is wrong, each interval creates another alarm, a different tick resolves it, or the ending tick fails to resolve it. Log output without actual alarm state is insufficient; DBOS unavailability must not stop raise/resolve.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"managed-tick-hang-alarm\",\"scheduled-registry\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Contract parameters and conjunctive evidence: A managed tick held longer than T raises one resolvable alarm per(timer,active-hang identity), naming that timer and its elapsed held time; the alarm resolves when that same tick ends. Default T=max(5*intervalMs,300000 ms). A positive finite custom threshold overrides the five-interval term while retaining the300000 ms minimum: T=max(customThresholdMs,300000 ms). At elapsed<=T no alarm; elapsed>T raises within the next independent watcher check, whose interval is<=min(intervalMs,60000 ms). Detection/resolve remain operational independently of DBOS.\\n\\nUse fake-clock unit tests atT−1,T,T+1 and watcher deadline, default/custom/clamped thresholds, actual alarm raise/resolve calls and one episode across repeated checks. Verify timer identity and measured held time. Exercise production wiring with DBOS unavailable and declare the watchdog in RECOVERY_MECHANISMS. Keep RECOVERY_MECHANISMS and watchdog implementation details in method.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"libs/generic/scheduled-registry/src/index.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: hold a tick unresolved; advance to below/at/pastT and watcher deadline; inspect alarm state, one episode and held duration. Repeat for intervals below/above60s and custom values below/above the minimum. Finish that tick and assert its alarm resolves; a later hang gets a new episode. Repeat with DBOS unavailable.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-7 — Empty ticks stay free.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"No change in this plan makes an empty in-process tick write a DBOS row. DBOS rows grow with actions taken, not with ticks.\",\"rationale\":\"EI-1622: one stored row per periodic tick froze the routine engine.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:cc8cb599-73b9-4227-9716-9cc216bba6c8:0\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"For each converted sweep, attributable durable work follows the exact mapping empty/no-action tick → zero rows and submissions, same eligible action episode → one execution identity, distinct episode → distinct identity across repeated/concurrent ticks, re-arm and fresh-process restart.\",\"falsifier\":\"Fail if any actual registered sweep/wrapper creates a durable submission/row for empty or no-action input, duplicates the same action identity across repeat/re-arm/restart, conflates distinct episodes, or never runs/dispatches the eligible positive control. A fake start counter without persistence evidence is insufficient.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"acceptance-grading-sweep\",\"release-request-sweep\",\"stale-claim-sweep\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\",\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Contract parameters and conjunctive evidence: For each converted grading, release-request and stale-claim sweep, an executed empty tick or nonempty-but-no-action tick creates zero new attributable durable workflow rows and zero durable submissions, including wrapper activity. Repeated ticks, re-arm and fresh-process restart retain that zero-write result. Repeated/concurrent observation of one logical action reuses one durable execution identity; a distinct action episode receives a distinct identity and completes its expected positive-control effect.\\n\\nKeep the action half in DBOS with an ID derived from scoped action identity; detection stays in-process. For each actual registered sweep, test empty,no-action,repeated,re-arm,restart and concurrent cases; assert the sweep ran, count submissions and query attributable DBOS workflow rows on a real durable store. Then supply eligible action and inspect the identity and effect; same episode reuses identity, distinct episode changes it. Bind unit and planned persistence-integration tests separately from R-2/R-3/R-4 crash-completion proof; create/register the planned file before binding.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/in-process-periodic.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-grading-sweep-run.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/sweep-zero-write.integration.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"REPLICATION DRILL: measure DBOS attributable rows before/after each sweep's empty and nonempty-no-action execution, repeat,re-arm and fresh-process restart; all deltas/submissions are0. Feed one eligible action, repeat/concurrently scan/restart and require one logical identity and effect. Change the action episode and require a distinct identity. Re-enable an unconditional wrapper start to show the zero-write guard fails.\"}}\n```\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\n```reuse\n{\"searched\":[{\"where\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos\",\"how\":\"Read GC and periodic workflow registration; rg for existing DBOS schedules and action tests.\",\"found\":\"Existing GC loop and periodic workflow registration.\"},{\"where\":\"libs/generic/scheduled-registry; packages/operator-core/lib; scripts\",\"how\":\"rg --files for scheduled-registry, outbox, unawaited and fire-and-forget surfaces.\",\"found\":\"Managed timer registry, existing cross-hive and substrate outbox paths.\"},{\"where\":\"dbos.workflow_status\",\"how\":\"dev:pg_query describe, read through code:run.\",\"found\":\"Existing DBOS system history table, millisecond timestamps and indexes.\"}],\"reused\":[{\"ref\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/dbos-workflow-gc.ts\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Terminal-only retention loop and injectable query seams.\",\"items\":[\"P-001\"]},{\"ref\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/periodic-workflows.ts\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Existing scheduled workflow registration and maintenance telemetry.\",\"items\":[\"P-001\",\"P-002\"]},{\"ref\":\"libs/generic/scheduled-registry/src/index.ts\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Managed timer registration and tick lifecycle accounting.\",\"items\":[\"P-005\"]},{\"ref\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/in-process-periodic.test.ts\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Existing sweep regression test framework.\",\"items\":[\"P-006\",\"P-007\"]},{\"ref\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/acceptance-grading-sweep-run.ts\",\"kind\":\"file\",\"provides\":\"Existing grading scan and dispatch boundary.\",\"items\":[\"P-004\"]},{\"ref\":\"docs:author\",\"kind\":\"tool\",\"provides\":\"Canonical runbook publication and projection.\",\"items\":[\"P-010\"]}],\"newSurfaces\":[{\"name\":\"Un-awaited notification classification check\",\"kind\":\"lint extension\",\"nearestExisting\":\"Existing repository TypeScript lint scripts and notification delivery paths.\",\"whyNotReused\":\"Extend the existing lint runner with classification for the audited notification sites; do not add another scheduler, queue or delivery service.\"}],\"notApplicable\":null}\n```\n\n## Third-party libraries\n\n```libraries\n{\"needs\":[{\"need\":\"Durable execution and replay of committed actions\",\"decision\":\"already-in-project\",\"package\":\"@dbos-inc/dbos-sdk\",\"existingUse\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/periodic-workflows.ts\",\"reason\":\"Extend existing workflow registration rather than adding a new workflow engine.\"},{\"need\":\"Retention SQL and transactional outbox access\",\"decision\":\"already-in-project\",\"package\":\"postgres\",\"existingUse\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/dbos-workflow-gc.ts via @papercusp/db-org\",\"reason\":\"Reuse current database client and schema.\"},{\"need\":\"Regression tests\",\"decision\":\"already-in-project\",\"package\":\"vitest\",\"existingUse\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/dbos-workflow-gc.test.ts\",\"reason\":\"Use the repository's canonical tests.\"}],\"notApplicable\":null}\n```\n\n## Design\nPlacement test: if the process dies halfway through a tick, does the next tick finish the job? If yes, the job stays on its in-process timer. If the tick commits a decision and then has more steps, those steps become a DBOS workflow.\n\nPattern: detect in-process, act durably. The scan stays on the timer, and an empty tick writes nothing. For each action found, the sweep starts a DBOS workflow whose ID comes from the action (for example `release-consequence:<item>:<deadline>`), so a repeated tick cannot start it twice and stored rows grow with actions, not ticks. The routines engine already works this way (`routinesTick` starts one `routineFire` per due routine).\n\nOrder: Phase 1 comes first because every later item adds DBOS workflows, and the history table is already above the June freeze level.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | deployed |\n| R-2 | P-004 | deployed |\n| R-3 | P-006 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-007 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-008, P-009 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-005 | tree |\n| R-7 | P-004, P-006, P-007 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Keep DBOS history bounded (do first)\n- **P-001** `todo` Make dbos-workflow-gc keep up: run hourly or loop until drained within a per-batch liveness bound, delete oldest terminal rows first (ORDER BY created_at, using workflow_status_created_at_index), and log every run, including runs that delete zero rows. Bug EI-26619264681971676. (R-1)\n- **P-002** `todo` Alarm when dbos.workflow_status crosses a row ceiling (start at 300k, the freeze threshold the GC already names). The alarm must not run on DBOS. (R-1)\n- **P-003** `todo` Break down routineFire volume (about 46.6k/day) by routine. Reduce each source above 2,000/day, or record why it needs a durable fire. (R-1)\n\n## Phase 2 — Bound and harden the lossy sweeps\n- **P-004** `todo` acceptance-grading-sweep: measure what holds a tick for about 40 min, cap the scan's wall time, and run each per-plan grader dispatch as a DBOS workflow keyed by plan and gradeable-since. Bug EI-26619271533407778. Blocked by P-001. (R-2, R-7) blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-005** `todo` scheduled-registry: raise a resolvable alarm when a managed tick holds its re-entrancy guard past the threshold, and declare it in RECOVERY_MECHANISMS. (R-6)\n- **P-006** `todo` release-request-sweep: after the resolve, run the consequence (comment, lock release, claim release, hold clear, notices/escalation) as a DBOS workflow with ID derived from item and deadline. Add a crash-injection test and a mutation probe. Bug EI-26619273576946393. Blocked by P-001. (R-3, R-7) blocked-by: P-001\n- **P-007** `todo` stale-claim-sweep: make the holder notice, dead-letter broadcast and audit row durable with the release (outbox written in the release transaction, or one DBOS workflow per release batch). Blocked by P-001. (R-4, R-7) blocked-by: P-001\n\n## Phase 3 — Fire-and-forget side effects\n- **P-008** `todo` Inventory un-awaited notify/send/escalate calls (start from the 84 files using `void (async`), classify each as durable or safe-to-lose with a reason, and add a shrink-only lint seeded from its own --list. (R-5)\n- **P-009** `todo` Move the owner-facing ones onto a durable delivery path, starting with the plans:set-status needs-human push. Blocked by P-008. (R-5) blocked-by: P-001, P-008\n\n## Phase 4 — Write it down\n- **P-010** `todo` Update agent-insights/two-tier-scheduler-and-timer-visibility via docs:author with the placement test (\"if this tick dies midway, does the next one finish the job?\") and the detect-in-process / act-durably pattern. Blocked by P-006. blocked-by: P-006\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Preserve in-process detection; make committed consequences durable after bounded-history repair\nDate: 2026-10-22\nPlacement rule: if a process exits during a scan, its next scan must finish the work; otherwise persist the action before advancing past the decision. Keep re-derivable checks, watchdogs, lifecycle timers and empty scans in process. Use a stable action identity for durable consequences, so retries resume the same action. Repair history retention before increasing durable action volume. Use the selected self implementation route; acceptance uses the platform's independent review path. Historical audit counts are dated evidence, not assertions about current runtime state.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003, P-004, P-005, P-006, P-007, P-008, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-002 — Keep aggregate BAR provenance separate from narrow item contracts and preserve outcome windows\nDate: 2026-10-22\n[self-imposed] Consolidated response to independent posts1195748,1195765,1195767. Retain all seven R identities and mandatory conjunctive evidence. R-1 retains its exact48h deployed retention sentence and the shaping24h catch-up checkpoint. R-2 retains its24h deployed timing outcome plus separate restart proof. No fake-time/unit result substitutes for these bg-host deployed observations.\nMeasured: packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/spec-quality.ts:607–615,665 excludes sourceBar-pinned canonical BAR copies from independent item coverage/atomicity. packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/plans/set-specs.ts:250–270 refuses edits to projected behavior; rubrics:amend is the canonical BAR writer. Therefore preserve canonical AUTO-BAR projection pins, and keep narrow independent per-item clauses unpinned, with acceptanceRef tracing the governing rubric revision/BAR hash after amendment. A narrow clause is neither a replacement for the aggregate BAR nor proof of other items' contributions. Add independent empty/no-action and action-identity controls for P-004,P-006,P-007. P-010 remains documentation with explicit readback/falsifier.\nThe new falsifier/verification contract names thresholds, all applicable consequences, logical receiver deduplication, commit/admission/effect/ack restart boundaries, complete tick observations, a closed call-site census and positive/negative controls. R-4's outbox/workflow alternatives and R-7's action-derived workflow IDs remain method choices, while their conditions describe outcomes.\nGC-first means P-001 implementation repair landing unblocks P-004,P-006,P-007,P-009; final48h observation is still required for plan acceptance and is not a prerequisite to coding those items. P-009 also retains P-008. Alarm default/custom threshold parameters and planned test files remain explicit pre-implementation declarations; every planned detector must exist, be registered and run before proof binding. Missing conjunct evidence is unknown/unmet, never pass.\nRelated: P-001, P-004, P-006, P-007, P-009, P-010\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: dbos-r1-r7-consolidated-20261022-d\nRequest-Hash: 4ebdb0f5a56ab14464c4bfbeb0f69bdb0c52b1dee4043d9cb401bb9e24c64a49\nActor: su-2b61b6ab-2086-4204-9607-a50f17b2ff42\nReason: Consolidated pre-implementation repairs from thread-post:1195748, thread-post:1195765 and thread-post:1195767; preserve all seven IDs, 48h/24h deployed outcomes and conjunctive evidence. Clarify thresholds, complete consequence sets, crash boundaries, closed census and no-op persistence controls.\nApproved-By: su-d3a67cdc-dbfb-46fc-bd07-cff49974dfd0\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1195921\nApproved-At: 2026-10-22T14:58:02.638Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 7 → 8\nChanged BARs: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-5, R-6, R-7\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: dbos-r7-restore-zero-20261022-a\nRequest-Hash: 69e5f3937e825e52aded9ffe41266d433f9834a7ef7ff4cbbd8b5617f863d0c9\nActor: su-2b61b6ab-2086-4204-9607-a50f17b2ff42\nReason: Restore explicit empty/no-action zero rows and submissions in canonical R-7 as requested by first critic post1195965.
