(R-5) <!-- P-009 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010020620 — Update agent-insights/two-tier-scheduler-and-timer-visibility via docs:author with the placement test (\"if this tick dies midway, does the next one finish the job?\") and the detect-in-process / act-d… <!-- P-010 -->\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"hashline-anchored-edits-2026-10-21","title":"Hash-anchored edits for Papercusp's edit tool (borrowed from oh-my-pi's hashline)","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Hash-anchored edits for Papercusp's edit tool (borrowed from oh-my-pi's hashline)\nslug: hashline-anchored-edits-2026-10-21\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-21\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n**Source:** owner directive #2148, 2026-10-21 [owner:Avi]: \"let's '4. Edits that point at a line by a short hash' thats the only thing id borrow from the reasearch you did other than maybe acp\". The idea comes from report rpt_b98ee94d-156e-4fa7-b848-fb0fcac09863.\n\n**Audience:** agents that edit files through Papercusp's own tools, `capability:read` / `capability:edit`.\n- Today these are mostly frontier-model Claude and Codex sessions.\n- Later: cheaper or local models, and ACP agents.\n\n**Problem:**\n- With string-replace edits, the model must retype the old text exactly. Weaker models often fail at this; omp's own benchmark reports Grok Code Fast 1 going from 6.7% to 68.3% with hashline.\n- Every edit also spends output tokens re-typing old code.\n\n**Outcome:**\n- An agent can read a file with anchors and edit by anchor.\n- An edit against stale anchors (a peer changed the file since it was read) is refused, or safely merged.\n- Lock arbitration still applies to every edit.\n\n**Non-goals:**\n- Changing Claude Code's or Codex's native edit tools; we can't.\n- Forcing frontier sessions off their native Edit.\n- ACP integration.\n- The separate known gap that `capability:edit` edits do not reach the edit ledger used by repair-queue admission.\n\n**Scenarios:**\n1. A cheaper-model fleet member reads `foo.ts` with anchors, replaces lines 40–52 by anchor, and the edit lands.\n2. A peer edits lines 45–47 between that agent's read and its edit. The edit is refused with \"stale anchor, re-read\" (or 3-way merged), never silently applied.\n3. A frontier agent replaces a large block without echoing it, and spends fewer output tokens.\n\n## Evidence at drafting time (measured 2026-10-21)\n\n- All of the 400 most recent sessions (2 days) ran frontier models: Claude Opus/Fable, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol.\n- omp, the only backend that already has hashline, ran 7 sessions in 7 days, against 3,304 Codex and 2,281 Claude.\n- `capability:edit`: 1,223 calls in 30 days from 36 owners. 12 were refused (5 not_found, 2 no_op, 2 not_unique, 1 file_locked), 1 timed out, 1 had invalid input.\n- **Implication:** the big gains reported for weaker models do not apply to today's fleet. Value today is token savings plus stale-edit safety. The large win arrives only if fleets move to cheaper models.\n\n## Reuse candidate\n\n`@oh-my-pi/hashline` (MIT, npm 18.1.5) is a standalone patch language and applier with a pluggable Filesystem and SnapshotStore:\n- Each file section carries a 4-hex content tag.\n- Edits target line ranges or syntactic blocks.\n- Stale tags are refused, or recovered by 3-way merge.\n\nRisks: its default filesystem is Bun-based, and it depends on the native `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` package. Papercusp's operator runs on Node.\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Measure the baseline: edit failure rate and output tokens per edit, by model and client, for capability:edit and for native edits (from transcripts); pick the evaluation models.\n- **P-002** `todo` Spike, reuse vs build: can @oh-my-pi/hashline load and run in the operator's Node runtime with a Node Filesystem subclass? Decide whether to reuse it or write a small native implementation.\n- **P-003** `todo` Anchored read: capability:read gains opt-in anchors, recording a snapshot for stale detection. Blocked by P-002.\n- **P-004** `todo` Anchored edit: capability:edit accepts anchor-addressed edits, refuses or 3-way merges stale ones, and keeps lock arbitration. Blocked by P-002.\n- **P-005** `todo` Vitest tests: anchored read/edit round trip, a stale anchor after a peer edit, a lock-held refusal, and multi-hunk preflight (no partial apply). Blocked by P-003 and P-004.\n- **P-006** `todo` A/B and decision: run the same edit tasks on one cheaper and one frontier model, with and without anchors; then decide the default and the guidance agents get. Blocked by P-001 and P-005.\n\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"loop-fire-proof-identity-2026-10-21","title":"Bind loop start and completion proof to the exact fire","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Bind loop start and completion proof to the exact fire\nslug: loop-fire-proof-identity-2026-10-21\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-21\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: agents relying on loop continuation and the people supervising them.\nProblem: a delayed earlier loop wake can arrive after a newer fire dispatch. Timestamp-only proof associates the real turn with the wrong fire.\nOutcome: a fire is settled or protected only by evidence bound to that fire.\nNon-goals: shared-runtime restarts, provider/model changes, peer-loop rearm, LIVE_GATE_OPS, authorization widening, and a replacement delivery ledger.\nSource: owned WI-6554700010019416 and parent EI-25961011491313417; delivery930844 has wakeCount10 while session_turn:codex:01a15f82-00e4-7bc1-a50b-d7726024165a:1 explicitly has fire9.\nScenarios: old queued fire9 arriving after fire10 dispatch never clears fire10; genuine fire10 does; missing legacy identity stays unverified and bounded retry survives.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Exact identity.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Loop-start and completion proof identify the exact routine fire in addition to clock bounds.\",\"rationale\":\"Measured source bug WI-6554700010019416; typed seam selected in D-001.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15fd9-1ea9-7050-bd0d-2423f6ba84af:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A loop fire's start and completion proof carry and require the same routineId and wakeCount identity.\",\"falsifier\":\"A proof can settle a fire using only timestamps, owner-wide activity, or a different routineId/wakeCount.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"loop-fire-marker\",\"provenance-ledger\",\"loop-turn-start\",\"reconcile\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the bound provenance, loop-turn-start, and reconcile unit tests and inspect the typed identity through marker, ledger, activity detail, and reconciliation readers.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/turn-provenance.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-turn-start-stamp.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/reconcile-loop-routines.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat with stale9/current10 and matching10 fixtures; retain test receipts and the source revision.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Distinguishing controls.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A delayed earlier fire must not satisfy the latest fire, while a genuine matching fire does.\",\"rationale\":\"Measured delivery930844: fire9 prompt arrived after fire10 dispatch; timestamp window alone accepted it.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15fae-97f3-7703-942d-d90528fba193:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The stale9/current10 negative remains unsettled and matching10 positive settles; routine identity and wakeCount are compared exactly.\",\"falsifier\":\"A stale fire clears the current fire or a matching fire is rejected solely because its clock differs.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"stale-fire-negative\",\"matching-fire-positive\",\"same-owner-overlap\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run conventional reconciliation tests with fire9 and fire10 markers sharing a routine but differing wakeCount, then assert the expected negative and positive outcomes.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/reconcile-loop-routines.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat with reversed arrival order and delayed ingestion; retain both controls and their receipts.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Legacy handling.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Missing or legacy fire identity remains explicitly unverified and uses bounded retry/fail-soft behavior.\",\"rationale\":\"Historical rows without typed identity must not be promoted to a successful proof.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15fd9-1ea9-7050-bd0d-2423f6ba84af:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A missing identity never settles the newest fire and reaches only the existing bounded retry path; malformed legacy rows do not throw or become owner/current proof.\",\"falsifier\":\"Unknown identity is treated as matching, causes an unbounded hold, or fails the wake path hard.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"legacy-row\",\"missing-identity\",\"bounded-retry\",\"fail-soft\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run missing-identity and malformed-row unit controls through status and reconciliation helpers, including the stuck-park bound.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/reconcile-loop-routines.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-turn-start-stamp.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat with absent, malformed, expired, and legacy provenance rows; retain bounded retry evidence.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-4 — Existing seams.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Extend existing provenance enrollment, lifecycle telemetry, and loop metadata without a parallel ledger or changed origin authority.\",\"rationale\":\"D-001 chooses existing typed records and rejects a replacement delivery ledger or carry-prose parsing.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15fd9-1ea9-7050-bd0d-2423f6ba84af:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The implementation reuses the existing provenance ledger, loop marker, loop-turn-start activity detail, and reconciliation/status readers; no new table or origin authority is introduced.\",\"falsifier\":\"A second ledger/table is added, identity is inferred from quoted text/clocks, or the origin authority changes.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"reuse-census\",\"no-new-ledger\",\"origin-authority\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Review the diff and run structural/source tests that exercise the reused seams and reject prose/time-only identity.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/turn-provenance.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-turn-start-stamp.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat the reuse census against the final source revision and retain the structural receipt.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-5 — Recurrence guard.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Conventional tests guard overlapping fire identities, matching positive control, missing identity, warm/cold delivery, and arm changes.\",\"rationale\":\"The recurrence guard is the acceptance contract for WI-6554700010019416 and P-001.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15fd9-1ea9-7050-bd0d-2423f6ba84af:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The project's conventional test suite fails the old timestamp-only predicate and passes the repaired identity controls across warm/cold and arm changes.\",\"falsifier\":\"Tests omit the stale negative, only mirror implementation, or pass without exercising the exact identity mismatch.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"unit-regression\",\"warm\",\"cold\",\"arm-change\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"],\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"],\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\"},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the named conventional test files with the old predicate mutation and the repaired implementation; retain fail/pass receipts and mutation identity.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/reconcile-loop-routines.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/harness/routines/loop-turn-start-stamp.test.ts\",\"packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/turn-provenance.test.ts\"]},\"replication\":\"Repeat on a clean pinned tree and retain both mutation failure and repaired pass receipts.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\nInspect the existing turn-provenance ledger, tagWakeText enrollment, loop-turn-start lifecycle marker and status/reconciler readers. Prefer a typed extension to those records over another table. Do not infer fire identity from clocks or quoted carry-note prose. Record the chosen seam as a Decision before edits. Keep the existing bug claim and explicit manual file locks. This draft must pass source-conversation/activation audit before activation; no source edits have started.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-001 | tree |\n\n\n## Phase 1 — Exact fire proof\n- **P-001** `todo` Select and record the smallest typed fire-identity seam; implement exact start/completion attribution end to end with conventional stale9/current10, matching10 and missing-identity controls. Track implementation through owned WI-6554700010019416. Tests must fail under the old timestamp-only predicate and pass after repair; local proof does not establish historical live recovery or final shipment.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Use provenance ledger fire identity plus loop-turn-start detail\nDate: 2026-10-21\nBind each loop wake to the existing provenance ledger row with typed loopFire { routineId, wakeCount }. At UserPromptSubmit, resolve the envelope nonce to that ledger row and store the typed identity in the existing loop-turn-start agent_activity detail. Reconciliation and loop:status will require an exact routineId+wakeCount match for the latest fire before pairing assistant output; rows without identity remain legacy/unknown and follow the existing bounded retry path. This extends existing provenance/lifecycle records and does not add a ledger/table or parse carry prose.\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"papercusp-engineering-architecture-presentation-2026-10-21","title":"Papercusp architecture and design — live senior-engineer presentation","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Papercusp architecture and design — live senior-engineer presentation\nslug: papercusp-engineering-architecture-presentation-2026-10-21\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n## Now\nCreate the speaker brief, build the presentation kit, verify it independently, and ship it through the canonical acceptance workflow.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019620 — Write the complete narrative, concept coverage, design-tradeoff brief and source-backed speaker notes. deliverable: doc <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019621 — Produce the offline browser presentation with existing maps, two integration traces, concept appendix and PDF fallback. deliverable: artifact <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010019622 — Verify the actual package in a browser and PDF, obtain independent acceptance, publish the delivery report and ship the plan. deliverable: operation <!-- P-003 -->\n## Product shaping\n\n```product-shaping\n{\"audience\":\"Small group of senior engineers in a live presentation\",\"problem\":\"The architecture and Cupboard references need a bounded live teaching sequence.\",\"outcome\":\"A usable three-pass presentation kit with map views, independent concept contracts, integration traces, notes and an offline fallback.\",\"nonGoals\":[\"Change the product or public site\",\"Claim human rehearsal or audience approval\",\"Run irreversible live demonstrations\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:1\",\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:11\",\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:12\",\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:25\"],\"context\":[{\"kind\":\"owner-request\",\"text\":\"Three passes: overall architecture and design reasons, low-level concepts separately, then their fit inside the high-level design.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:1\"]},{\"kind\":\"observed-fact\",\"text\":\"The current architecture and Cupboard pages have zoomable maps, narration controls and article mode.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"rpt_7d590147-9370-45d2-8e61-c2ff57f08d46\"]},{\"kind\":\"assumption\",\"text\":\"30-minute core talk with a complete appendix; offline HTML presentation document and PDF.\",\"material\":false,\"resolved\":true},{\"kind\":\"product-choice\",\"text\":\"Reuse both public-site maps rather than rebuild the architecture visual.\",\"decisionRef\":\"D-002\",\"material\":false,\"resolved\":true}],\"scenarios\":[{\"id\":\"SC-001\",\"title\":\"Learn architecture and reasons\",\"kind\":\"normal\",\"trigger\":\"The live talk starts\",\"action\":\"Show overall map, explain boundaries and tradeoffs\",\"outcome\":\"Engineers understand the architecture before detailed vocabulary\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-1\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-002\",\"title\":\"Learn each contract\",\"kind\":\"normal\",\"trigger\":\"Pass two begins\",\"action\":\"Teach concepts on isolated cards and retain a full appendix\",\"outcome\":\"Audience can distinguish tools/events/rules/state/work/identity/reuse before placement\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-1\",\"R-2\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-003\",\"title\":\"Follow execution and reuse\",\"kind\":\"normal\",\"trigger\":\"Pass three begins\",\"action\":\"Trace one work item on the map and one reusable guard across Cupboard\",\"outcome\":\"Audience understands how concepts compose across runtime and distribution\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-2\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-004\",\"title\":\"Present without network\",\"kind\":\"failure\",\"trigger\":\"Public pages cannot be reached\",\"action\":\"Use the local deck/maps and PDF\",\"outcome\":\"Core presentation and notes remain usable\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-2\",\"R-3\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-005\",\"title\":\"Distinguish availability\",\"kind\":\"boundary\",\"trigger\":\"A development or coming-soon mechanism is discussed\",\"action\":\"Display labels and source snapshot date; avoid claiming released verification\",\"outcome\":\"Audience can judge what evidence the presentation actually provides\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-2\",\"R-3\"]}],\"considerations\":[{\"category\":\"Authority and delivery\",\"disposition\":\"covered\",\"reason\":\"AUTO authorizes preparation and owner-visible delivery; no external messages or site deployment are needed.\",\"scenarioIds\":[\"SC-001\",\"SC-004\"]}]}\n```\nAudience: a small group of senior engineers attending a live Papercusp architecture/design presentation.\n\nProblem: the current architecture and Cupboard pages are rich references, but the live talk needs a bounded narrative that teaches the vocabulary before combining it.\n\nOutcome: a presenter-ready, offline-capable three-pass presentation kit using the existing architecture and Cupboard maps, with notes, tradeoffs, source references and PDF fallback.\n\nNon-goals: change papercusp.com, build a new application or map engine, run a production fleet/release during the talk, present incomplete authoring flows as live, or pretend a human has rehearsed/delivered the talk.\n\nSource turns: session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:1; session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:11; session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:12; session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:25. The complete conversation from turns 1–25 has been read, including the revised recommendation in turn 24 accepted by turn 25. Earlier assessment: rpt_7d590147-9370-45d2-8e61-c2ff57f08d46.\n\nScenarios:\n- The presenter opens with the whole-machine map and explains why durable shared coordination surrounds fallible agent sessions.\n- An engineer learns tools, policies, events, durable work and extension concepts as individual contracts without locating them on the diagram yet.\n- The presenter returns to the same map and follows work through failure/retry/resume, then follows a reusable guard across the Cupboard boundary.\n- Network access fails: local snapshots and PDF preserve the core talk; detailed live pages and code remain optional drill-downs.\n\nAssumptions: approximately 30 minutes of prepared material, with an appendix for questions; a local HTML presentation document is the default delivery format because it can embed existing map visuals and needs no proprietary editor. These are agent-selected implementation choices under AUTO, not previously specified owner preferences. No additional implementation agents are launched; platform-routed independent acceptance is still required.\n\n## Background\nUse both existing public maps as complementary views: architecture for execution and coordination; Cupboard for extensibility and distribution. The inspected live Pages-alias HTML matched the local built public-site pages. Availability is development-source unless separately verified on a released build.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Faithful three-pass architecture narrative.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A live presentation for a small group of senior engineers explains Papercusp architecture and design reasons in three passes: overall architecture, low-level concepts taught independently of diagram placement, then those concepts located in runtime traces on the same high-level map.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:1\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A live presentation for a small group of senior engineers explains Papercusp architecture and design reasons in three passes: overall architecture, low-level concepts taught independently of diagram placement, then those concepts located in runtime traces on the same high-level map with a full concept appendix.\",\"falsifier\":\"Any pass is absent; concepts are located in the system before their independent introduction; or the narrative is a feature inventory without design tradeoffs.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"audience\",\"concept vocabulary\",\"design rationale\",\"three passes\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Read the presenter brief and ordered slides. Locate each pass and its transitions. Check that pass two uses isolated contract cards, that pass three returns to the original map, and that speaker notes cover the reasons and costs for shared state, CLI/MCP agents, lock arbitration, continuity and verification. Compare against source owner turns 1, 11, 12 and 25; inspect the entire concept appendix so broad coverage does not crowd the core talk.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"instrument\",\"instrumentKey\":\"none\"},\"replication\":\"A second reviewer opens the same delivery files and follows the written walkthrough; no live service mutations are required.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Presentable and reusable map-based package.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"A presenter can open an offline browser deck, navigate its prepared architecture/Cupboard views with narration muted, read presenter notes, and use a PDF fallback. The package covers both runtime cooperation and local-to-versioned-Cupboard reuse while preserving development-source/released/coming-soon distinctions.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:25\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"A presenter can open an offline browser deck, navigate prepared architecture/Cupboard views with narration muted, read presenter notes, use a PDF fallback, and see runtime cooperation plus local-to-versioned-Cupboard reuse with development-source, released, and coming-soon distinctions preserved.\",\"falsifier\":\"The deck requires network assets to display its core content; a map or concept is unreadable at presentation size; the traces omit Cupboard composition or agent recovery; controls trap navigation; or unsupported flows are presented as shipped.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"architecture map\",\"Cupboard map\",\"notes\",\"offline deck\",\"PDF\",\"reuse trace\",\"runtime trace\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Open the delivered index.html with the network disabled; navigate every core slide and appendix, toggle notes, use overview and return links, and inspect at 1440x900 and 1280x720. Follow the same prepared work-item through claim, guarded call, event/state effects, checkpoint/resumption, verification and release. Follow one installed guard through package, publish/review, install and identity activation. Compare selected contract statements with current source/pages and inspect the rendered PDF page count and legibility. Run the bound rendering and corrupt-layout cases. The existing verifier exercises both disabled-network viewports, notes, overview, deep links, map zooms and PDF page/title coverage; the corrupt CSS fixture must be rejected. Preserve manual semantic review of trace fidelity, contract clarity, engineering accuracy, availability labels and legibility under D-005. R-2 owns offline/PDF rendering and usability; R-3 owns artifact presence, integrity and delivery resolution.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/presentation-artifact.test.ts\"],\"cases\":[{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/presentation-artifact.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"architecture presentation artifact > renders the complete presentation without network\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/presentation-artifact.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"architecture presentation artifact > rejects a layout that displays inactive slides\"}]},\"replication\":\"A second reviewer opens the same delivery files and follows the written walkthrough; no live service mutations are required.\"}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Verified and delivered presentation kit.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The final kit contains editable source, complete speaker notes, a 30-minute timing proposal, setup/rehearsal instructions, local map snapshots with attribution, PDF fallback, and a verified owner-facing delivery link. Acceptance records actual browser/content checks and independent review without claiming a human live rehearsal or audience approval.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:codex:01a15ee1-e0bd-7d92-9454-19cde523da09:25\"]},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The final kit provides editable source, complete speaker notes, a 30-minute timing proposal, setup/rehearsal instructions, attributed local map snapshots, a PDF fallback, a resolving owner-facing delivery link, recorded browser/content checks and independent review, and no claim of human rehearsal or audience approval.\",\"falsifier\":\"An essential artifact is missing or its link cannot be resolved; evidence is only a generation receipt; the timing is unbounded; source claims lack traceable references; or the plan is labelled shipped before canonical independent acceptance.\",\"requiredScope\":[\"availability labels\",\"delivery\",\"independent acceptance\",\"rehearsal evidence\",\"timing\"],\"evidencePlane\":\"tree\",\"mandatory\":true,\"role\":\"outcome\",\"passRatings\":[\"healthy\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the bound intact-kit, missing-source and changed-source cases: fixed contract file inventory, source attribution, current digests, exact archive member bytes, PDF presence and proposed versus human timing. Then resolve the owner-facing report and its deck/notes/PDF/source references, read the complete notes, and verify independent grading and the author verdict before final ship. Record report readback separately from publication. This criterion owns presence, integrity, resolution, timing and delivery honesty; PDF legibility, offline rendering and navigation usability are graded only under R-2. Narrative clarity and source accuracy remain manual judgments under D-005.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/presentation-artifact.test.ts\"],\"cases\":[{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/presentation-artifact.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"architecture presentation artifact > delivers an intact editable kit with source attribution\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/presentation-artifact.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"architecture presentation artifact > rejects missing editable source\"},{\"file\":\"packages/operator-core/lib/presentation-artifact.test.ts\",\"testName\":\"architecture presentation artifact > rejects source bytes that disagree with the verified package\"}]},\"replication\":\"A second reviewer opens the same delivery files and follows the written walkthrough; no live service mutations are required.\"}}\n```\n\n## Design\nReuse the current public-site SVG/maps and their visual vocabulary. Build a standalone presentation document and local captures, not a new site or app. Core slides use fixed readable views; full source maps are available for deliberate zoom and questions. Keep stable colors/names across the three passes. no recurring executable conformance monitor is applicable.\",\"approvalRef\":\"D-005\"}}}}\n```\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"sidecar-forkserver-2026-10-21","title":"Spawn sidecar children from a tiny forkserver so forks stop blocking governed admission","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-21","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Spawn sidecar children from a tiny forkserver so forks stop blocking governed admission\nslug: sidecar-forkserver-2026-10-21\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-21\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\n- **Audience:** every agent whose work lands through git-sync, and every caller of the bg-host spawner sidecar (git-sync, test admission, deploy vintage checks).\n- **Problem:** the sidecar (RSS ~500MB) forks each child on its own event loop. Each fork costs ~11.5ms in clone() plus ~12ms waiting for the child to exec, ~24 times a second under git-sync load, so the loop is blocked 35-59% of the time. Governed admission makes several PG round trips on that loop; each statement runs in <1ms in Postgres, but the round trips wait 40-90ms for the loop, so admission takes ~5s (p50, >5s tail). git calls then take 10-13s and one git-sync sweep ran 16:18-~19:00Z on 2026-10-21 while every later sweep skipped behind it.\n- **Outcome:** forks happen in a separate minimal process; the sidecar's event loop only does RPC, admission I/O and bookkeeping. Admission round trips stop waiting on forks.\n- **Non-goals:** changing governed-admission semantics, receipts or the lazy-receipt policy; cutting git-sync's call volume; changing libuv/Node.\n- **Source turns:** owner dialog answer session_turn:claude:7986a278-5448-47ed-a7f6-a34e4644ac75:10 (route \"Me, now\", design \"Tiny forkserver\").\n- **Scenarios:** S1 a git-sync sweep with ~40 submodules runs while test admissions spawn concurrently; the sidecar loop delay stays low. S2 a child is killed by timeout; its whole process group dies with SIGTERM then SIGKILL, exactly as today. S3 the forkserver crashes mid-exec; the in-flight exec settles as an infrastructure fault (never replayed) and the next exec succeeds on a restarted forkserver.\n\n```product-shaping\n{\"audience\":\"Every agent whose work lands through git-sync, and every caller of the bg-host spawner sidecar (git-sync, test admission, deploy vintage checks).\",\"problem\":\"The ~500MB spawner sidecar forks each child on the event loop that runs its governed-admission Postgres round trips; at ~24 spawns/s the loop is blocked 35-59%, admission takes ~5s and one git-sync sweep held the lease for hours.\",\"outcome\":\"Forks happen in a separate minimal process; the sidecar event loop only does RPC, admission I/O and bookkeeping, so admission no longer waits on forks.\",\"nonGoals\":[\"Change governed-admission semantics, receipts or the lazy-receipt policy\",\"Cut git-sync's call volume\",\"Change libuv or Node\"],\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:7986a278-5448-47ed-a7f6-a34e4644ac75:10\"],\"context\":[{\"kind\":\"owner-request\",\"text\":\"Who builds the fix: Me, now. Which design: Tiny forkserver.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"session_turn:claude:7986a278-5448-47ed-a7f6-a34e4644ac75:10\"]},{\"kind\":\"observed-fact\",\"text\":\"A 3 s strace of the sidecar main thread showed clone() ~11.5 ms plus exec-wait ~12 ms per spawn and the loop blocked 35-59%, while Postgres ran admission statements in under 1 ms.\",\"sourceRefs\":[\"WI-6554700010019379\"]},{\"kind\":\"assumption\",\"text\":\"A small Node forkserver forks in a few ms and keeps up with the ~24 spawns/s git-sync peak.\",\"material\":false,\"resolved\":false},{\"kind\":\"product-choice\",\"text\":\"The forkserver source is embedded and started with node -e, so packaged single-bundle builds need no extra file.\",\"material\":false,\"resolved\":true}],\"scenarios\":[{\"id\":\"SC-001\",\"title\":\"Git-sync sweep under concurrent spawns\",\"kind\":\"normal\",\"trigger\":\"A git-sync sweep over ~40 submodules runs while test admissions spawn\",\"action\":\"The sidecar routes every child exec through the forkserver\",\"outcome\":\"Sidecar event-loop delay stays low and admission round trips stop waiting on forks\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-1\",\"R-4\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-002\",\"title\":\"Timed-out child\",\"kind\":\"failure\",\"trigger\":\"A child exceeds its timeout\",\"action\":\"The sidecar signals its process group SIGTERM then SIGKILL\",\"outcome\":\"The whole group dies exactly as with a direct spawn\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-2\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-003\",\"title\":\"Forkserver crash mid-exec\",\"kind\":\"failure\",\"trigger\":\"The forkserver dies while an exec is running\",\"action\":\"The sidecar kills the orphaned group and settles the exec\",\"outcome\":\"The exec returns an infrastructure-fault result, is not replayed, and the next exec succeeds on a restarted forkserver\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-3\"]},{\"id\":\"SC-004\",\"title\":\"Regression is visible\",\"kind\":\"normal\",\"trigger\":\"Something blocks the sidecar loop again\",\"action\":\"An operator reads the sidecar health payload\",\"outcome\":\"The event-loop delay p99 shows the regression without strace\",\"requirementIds\":[\"R-5\"]}]}\n```\n\n## Design\n\n- `packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/forkserver/`: a minimal Node entry (imports only node built-ins) started by the spawner sidecar as a long-lived child (inherits the sidecar's cgroup; not detached). It spawns each requested child with `detached:true` (own process group), opens the stdin/stdout handoff paths itself, relays stdout/stderr chunks, pid, and exit code/signal over a framed channel, and accepts group-signal requests.\n- The sidecar's `execProcess` keeps every current guard (timeouts, idle timeout, output bound, UTF-8 decoding, abort, kill grace, group-exit confirmation) and swaps only the spawn primitive for a forkserver-backed child handle compatible with `processGroupLifetime`.\n- The forkserver's detached spawn site is registered with `lint:no-unenrolled-spawn` (allowlist entry with reason: children of the sidecar's enrolled cgroup).\n- Health: the sidecar reports event-loop delay (perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay p99) so a regression is visible without strace.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n|---|---|---|\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-004 | live |\n| R-5 | P-003 | tree |\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Forkserver process and wire protocol: minimal Node entry under packages/operator-core/lib/fleet/forkserver/ that spawns detached process-group children, opens handoff paths, relays pid/stdout/stderr/exit and group signals over a framed channel; client handle in the sidecar; lint:no-unenrolled-spawn allowlist entry; unit + integration tests (R-2, R-3).\n- **P-002** `todo` Route sidecar execProcess spawns through the forkserver with every existing guard intact; sidecar starts/restarts the forkserver and settles in-flight execs as infrastructure faults on its death; integration test with a 50-exec burst measuring parent loop delay plus a mutation probe (R-1, R-2, R-3). Blocked by P-001.\n- **P-003** `todo` Sidecar health reports event-loop delay p99 (perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay) with a unit test that blocks the loop (R-5). Blocked by P-002.\n- **P-004** `todo` Deploy to bg-host and verify live: strace of the sidecar main thread and the bg-host slow-exec admission distribution before/after, recorded on the work item; then close WI-6554700010019379 (R-4). Blocked by P-003.\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\nOnly the fork moves. The instrument docs/evidence/sidecar-forkserver-live-probe.py traces the actual sidecar and forkserver with stable runtime and positive activity controls; its parser test rejects ptrace refusal/empty trace as proof. Plan body to be filled in.\n\n**Next:** human reviews scope and lists Phase 1 items.\n\n## Background\n\n(Why this plan exists; what problem it addresses.)\n\n## Product shaping\n\nShape the product before requirements/tasks: record audience, current problem, intended outcome, non-goals and original source refs. Walk concrete user scenarios including relevant failure/recovery and boundaries; keep observed facts, assumptions and material product choices distinct. Investigate existing behavior and recommend defaults; ask only consequential product choices, never engineering methodology. Map scenarios to R-N requirements and the Design BAR-to-work map. plans:audit phase:shaping returns advisory gaps, the ownerWalkthrough and a two-pass blind intent-review brief; lead the owner's approval ask with the ownerWalkthrough, not the requirements. Save edits with plans:set-content. Full verification remains unchanged.\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"\",\n  \"problem\": \"\",\n  \"outcome\": \"\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [],\n  \"context\": [],\n  \"scenarios\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-001\",\n      \"title\": \"\",\n      \"kind\": \"normal\",\n      \"trigger\": \"\",\n      \"action\": \"\",\n      \"outcome\": \"\",\n      \"requirementIds\": []\n    }\n  ],\n  \"considerations\": []\n}\n```\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\nThis section records the check for existing infrastructure made before anything new was designed, so nothing is duplicated. It names where the search looked (the code via lsp:query, graph:query and grep; the tool catalog via tools:find; the database via dev:pg_query describe; BORROWABLE.md; the docs) so a reviewer can judge the search. Each reused piece is listed by exact reference: a repo path, path#Symbol, tool name, schema.table, package, routine name or doc slug. Each new table, tool, service, routine or module the plan adds names the nearest existing thing and why it did not fit. A plan that builds nothing records a one-line notApplicable reason.\n\n```reuse\n{\n  \"searched\": [\n    {\n      \"where\": \"\",\n      \"how\": \"\",\n      \"found\": \"\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"reused\": [\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"\",\n      \"kind\": \"file | symbol | tool | table | package | routine | doc\",\n      \"provides\": \"\",\n      \"items\": []\n    }\n  ],\n  \"newSurfaces\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"\",\n      \"kind\": \"\",\n      \"nearestExisting\": \"\",\n      \"whyNotReused\": \"\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"notApplicable\": null\n}\n```\n\n## Third-party libraries\n\nThis section lists each need a third-party library could meet, one row per need, with how the library was chosen. No research is needed when the owner already named the library (owner-specified: sourceRef cites the owner turn), when the project already uses a library for this (already-in-project: package names it and existingUse says where it is used), or when the job is small or no suitable library is expected (skip-research: reason gives one line why). Research only when a library would remove a lot of work and fits the use case: the realistic options are compared, one is picked, and the runners-up are recorded with why (researched). A second library is never added for a job an existing dependency already does. A plan that needs no library records a one-line notApplicable reason.\n\n```libraries\n{\n  \"needs\": [\n    {\n      \"need\": \"\",\n      \"decision\": \"owner-specified | already-in-project | skip-research | researched\",\n      \"package\": \"\",\n      \"reason\": \"\",\n      \"sourceRef\": null,\n      \"existingUse\": null,\n      \"candidates\": [\n        {\n          \"name\": \"\",\n          \"verdict\": \"chosen | rejected\",\n          \"why\": \"\"\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  \"notApplicable\": null\n}\n```\n\n## Phase 1 — TODO\n\n(Use plans:add-item to populate. Full verification remains unchanged.\n\n```product-shaping\n{\n  \"audience\": \"\",\n  \"problem\": \"\",\n  \"outcome\": \"\",\n  \"nonGoals\": [],\n  \"sourceRefs\": [],\n  \"context\": [],\n  \"scenarios\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"SC-001\",\n      \"title\": \"\",\n      \"kind\": \"normal\",\n      \"trigger\": \"\",\n      \"action\": \"\",\n      \"outcome\": \"\",\n      \"requirementIds\": []\n    }\n  ],\n  \"considerations\": []\n}\n```\n\n## Existing infrastructure reused\n\nThis section records the check for existing infrastructure made before anything new was designed, so nothing is duplicated. It names where the search looked (the code via lsp:query, graph:query and grep; the tool catalog via tools:find; the database via dev:pg_query describe; BORROWABLE.md; the docs) so a reviewer can judge the search. Each reused piece is listed by exact reference: a repo path, path#Symbol, tool name, schema.table, package, routine name or doc slug. Each new table, tool, service, routine or module the plan adds names the nearest existing thing and why it did not fit. A plan that builds nothing records a one-line notApplicable reason.\n\n```reuse\n{\n  \"searched\": [\n    {\n      \"where\": \"\",\n      \"how\": \"\",\n      \"found\": \"\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"reused\": [\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"\",\n      \"kind\": \"file | symbol | tool | table | package | routine | doc\",\n      \"provides\": \"\",\n      \"items\": []\n    }\n  ],\n  \"newSurfaces\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"\",\n      \"kind\": \"\",\n      \"nearestExisting\": \"\",\n      \"whyNotReused\": \"\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"notApplicable\": null\n}\n```\n\n## Third-party libraries\n\nThis section lists each need a third-party library could meet, one row per need, with how the library was chosen. No research is needed when the owner already named the library (owner-specified: sourceRef cites the owner turn), when the project already uses a library for this (already-in-project: package names it and existingUse says where it is used), or when the job is small or no suitable library is expected (skip-research: reason gives one line why). Research only when a library would remove a lot of work and fits the use case: the realistic options are compared, one is picked, and the runners-up are recorded with why (researched). Each decision is a third-level\nheading with a date line and a body paragraph.)\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"bounded-gitlink-admission-inventory-2026-10-22","title":"Bound immutable gitlink admission inventory while preserving paired dependency coverage","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-22","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Bound immutable gitlink admission inventory while preserving paired dependency coverage\nslug: bounded-gitlink-admission-inventory-2026-10-22\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-22\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Product shaping\n\nAudience: the gate owner and engineers admitting verified submodule repairs.\n\nProblem: EI-26651207402060575 records an R6 inventory timeout for a small gitlink repair. immutablePrecheckPopulation recursively reads source blobs across the complete built repository before deciding which tests to run. The caller has the old repair head, but ImmutablePrecheckInput carries only the built commit, so a small pin delta becomes a directory-wide change.\n\nOutcome: select a bounded, immutable, explainable qualification population for a small pin delta without losing paired parent/sibling coverage or treating an unmeasured precheck as passing.\n\nNon-goals: change gate ownership, bypass the current checkpoint, lower the acceptance ratchet, raise the file cap, weaken import completeness, or replace the existing admission worker/test router. Current candidate 5b9f0cf7 already contains the original federation/prompt repair; this performance work does not block that run.\n\nSource: agent-derived follow-up to owned EI-26651207402060575 and WI-10006055, carried explicitly into the 2026-10-22 continuation. This draft is design preparation; source-conversation activation audit and independent acceptance preparation remain required before activation.\n\nScenarios:\n- A small nested submodule source delta selects its affected supported tests and parent/sibling dependents using pinned objects, even when ambient worktrees differ.\n- A missing parent helper remains a measured failing paired test, as required by the existing WI-8351 fixture.\n- Missing git objects, unknown dependency edges, unsupported native-only test populations, or broad config/migration changes cannot become a successful zero-test qualification.\n\n## Requirements\n\n**R-1 — Pin the compared commits.** Persist the exact pre-admission repair head and unpublished built commit in the existing immutable inventory job. Validate the pair before selection and preserve queue compare-and-swap behavior.\n\n**R-2 — Expand nested pin deltas.** Reuse collectRecursiveDiff for nested pin additions, removals and updates. Seed selection from changed pinned paths; preserve added/deleted-path and unresolved-object semantics.\n\n**R-3 — Preserve paired dependencies.** Preserve WI-8351 paired-dependency coverage across parent/sibling boundaries. D-037's ordinary-admission radius deliberately excludes cross-workspace dependents and skips unavailable radius work; it is insufficient as the gitlink qualification contract. A gitlink inventory failure must remain a refusal, never an ordinary-radius skip.\n\n**R-4 — Reuse measured selection.** Reuse the existing related-test graph, pinned blob readers, worker, test router and result ledger. Index by pinned content identity and retain enough reverse dependency coverage to prove the selected population. If safe bounded coverage cannot be established, return an explicit unavailable/broad-qualification requirement. No guessed empty population, silent omission, cap increase or skipPrecheck.\n\n**R-5 — Require measured qualification.** Acceptance continues to require status=passed plus verdict.ok and verdict.ran on the exact built commit. A busy checkpoint tree or deferred precheck is not passing evidence.\n\n**R-6 — Guard preservation and bounded work.** Regression fixtures must prove nested diffs, paired-parent failures, dirty/untracked ambient exclusion, missing pins, native-only refusal, configuration/migration fallback, and a bounded small-delta inventory. Verification must measure work/bytes or read-set cardinality with a writer-defined unit; wall-clock timing alone is not a deterministic bound.\n\n## Design\n\nExtend the existing ImmutablePrecheckInput, its repair-queue caller and admission worker serialization. Keep inventory read-only. Carry the base explicitly rather than reconstructing it from current HEAD after a cold wake.\n\nUse scripts/lib/executed-source-map.mjs collectRecursiveDiff for immutable changed-path discovery. Reuse pinned tree metadata and content-hash edge caches for dependency selection. Before implementation, resolve how to include reverse dependents outside changed workspaces without reading every source blob on every admission. Candidate design: reuse a content-addressed dependency index keyed by the complete pinned tree tuple; an unavailable/incomplete index must produce an explicit qualification requirement. Do not introduce a parallel persistent graph without first proving existing related-test/index surfaces cannot supply this contract.\n\nExisting controls to preserve: packages/operator-core/lib/release/admission-offthread.test.ts WI-8351 cases; immutablePrecheckPopulation's missing-pin/native-only refusal; admissionPrecheck's measured-pass ratchet; green-main-cycle-time-2026-10-08#D-037 only for ordinary admissions.\n\nOpen design choice: the precise reusable reverse-dependency index and broad-input qualification route. This must be settled with source evidence before an implementation item is activated.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-001, P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-002, P-003 | tree |\n| R-6 | P-003 | tree |\n\n## Items\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Resolve dependency-index reuse and explicit broad/unknown-input behavior; audit source conversation and map provenance to the final specification.\n- **P-002** `todo` Implement the base-to-built job contract and safe selection in the existing surfaces, using EI-26651207402060575 as the source work record rather than minting a duplicate defect.\n- **P-003** `todo` Independently verify the preservation fixtures and measured inventory bound on a current-build route; only then qualify a real small pin repair through measured R6. Final release shipment remains WI-10006055's separate responsibility.\n\n## Acceptance evidence\n\nTree/current-build evidence is sufficient for source implementation. Require maintained regression tests and an independent mutation/counterexample that removes a paired dependency and is caught. Record exact source/test blobs, selected and excluded populations with reasons, and the deterministic read-work bound. A passing typecheck alone is insufficient. Deployed main is not required for source closure.\n\n## Now\n\n**State:** ⚠ BAR READINESS BLOCKED (2026-10-22, after decision-added): bar_snapshot_cohort_incomplete, bar_snapshot_rubric_missing, bar_snapshot_bar_set_empty. Next repair: Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.. (re-evaluated in the same write by the scope-write cascade, P-030/P-031)\n\nDraft only. Design and source reuse investigation are saved; no source edits or plan activation have occurred. The live checkpoint and existing compiler/manifest workers retain priority.\n\n**Next:** Repair the server-owned adoption epoch/cohort seed on the subject plan.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D-001 — Reuse the existing parsed-edge cache and cross-root graph; keep the cold-index coverage choice explicit\nDate: 2026-10-22\nMeasured 2026-10-22 source: scripts/lib/related-tests.mjs:1009-1171 already exposes RelatedFs.key, EdgeCache, edgeCacheKey(path,blob), buildIndex crossRoot package resolution and unresolved-edge widening. packages/operator-core/lib/release/admission-jobs.ts:110-125 already retains radiusState.edges in the long-lived admission worker with a 200000-entry bound. The ordinary admission branch uses this cache; immutablePrecheckPopulation:370-421 instead eagerly reads every pinned source blob, builds a root-wide graph without the cache or crossRoot option, and marks every gitlink descendant changed. repair-queue.ts:1760 has only built commit in the inventory message; the exact pre-admission base is absent from ImmutablePrecheckInput.\n\nDecision: extend the existing immutable inventory job and reuse these graph/cache seams; do not introduce a parallel persistent dependency graph merely for gitlink admission. Cache parsed specifiers/runtimePaths by pinned blob and path, but resolve edges against each exact built tree: cached edges alone do not prove old resolutions remain valid after deletes, exports/config changes or a paired parent change. Missing/unparsed edges must retain conservative coverage, never become an empty success.\n\nThis settles the reuse surface, not the whole design. A cold cache still requires source reads for complete reverse-dependency coverage. P-001 remains open until it specifies an explicit bounded cold-index/broad-qualification route and distinguishes small ordinary source deltas from config/migration/unknown changes. Reusing ordinary radius skipping or dropping parent/sibling tests is prohibited by R-3/R-5 and governing green-main-cycle-time D-037 (ordinary admissions only). Acceptance must separately measure cold and warm work, counting source blobs/bytes read at the blob-reader boundary, and catch a missing paired parent dependency. Do not activate implementation based only on a warmed-cache benchmark.\nRelated: P-001, P-002, P-003\n"},{"harness_slug":"papercusp","plan_slug":"canonical-source-plan-route-reservation-2026-10-22","title":"Honor direct-route reservations on canonical source-plan work","status":"ready","created":"2026-10-22","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Honor direct-route reservations on canonical source-plan work\nslug: canonical-source-plan-route-reservation-2026-10-22\nstatus: ready\ncreated: 2026-10-22\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n## Now\nRepair WI-6554700010020092 directly in this session under the existing AUTO fleet-leadership scope. Fleet revision16 exclusions remain a temporary mitigation.\n\n\n## Promoted\n\n<!-- plan-pipeline: do not edit this block manually -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010020231 — Reproduce the canonical source-only reservation miss in the maintained PostgreSQL agreement suite with item, tenant and unbound controls. <!-- P-001 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010020232 — Extend the existing TypeScript and compatible DB decision floors with canonical source identity; preserve itemRefs and by-ID access. <!-- P-002 -->\n- [ ] WI-6554700010020233 — Verify focused regression and existing reservation agreement cases, record immutable source/test evidence, and complete WI20092 with measured scope limits. <!-- P-003 -->\n## Product shaping\nAudience: agents dispatching plan-related work and Avi, who chooses the execution route.\nProblem: generated conformance work can carry source_plan_slug without payload.plan_item; a recorded self-only plan decision is then invisible to generic scheduler selection.\nOutcome: existing direct-route reservations cover that canonical identity while deliberate by-ID pickup and unrelated work remain usable.\nNon-goals: changing route authority, assigning the original conformance work, broadening fleet revision16/cap2, changing admission screening, operating the release gate, or crossing Portal/WI9165 owner walls.\nSource turns: session_turn:codex:01a15d2d-dd00-7ce2-a1a8-9e22eb354263:3 establishes AUTO continuation. This repair and its requirements are agent-derived from WI-6554700010020092 and get-feedback-reliability-usefulness-adoption-2026-10-03#D-002; they are not new owner-authored requirements.\nScenarios:\n1. A source-only conformance alarm for a plan with a plan-wide self-only decision is excluded by generic issue and feature selectors and the DB floor.\n2. An item-specific decision affects a matching canonical source item, and leaves another source item or a source-only record without that item unreserved.\n3. Unbound work, another tenant, and rejected or absent direct routes remain available; the explicit by-ID route can still claim reserved work.\n\n## Background\nWI20077 reproduced the missed floor with canonical source_plan_slug, null source_plan_item_ids, no payload.plan_item, and DB floors=[]. Reuse reservedPlanLaneExclusionSql, work_item_claim_floors and the maintained real-Postgres claim-ssot-agreement integration suite. Prior repairs WI-41737/WI-10006159/WI-10006417 cover the existing route forms.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Canonical source identity.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Source-only plan work reserved by a direct execution decision is unavailable to generic claim selection.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Source-only plan work reserved by a direct execution decision is unavailable to generic claim selection.\",\"falsifier\":\"A source-only reserved row is served by a generic selector or the TS and DB floor disagree.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the maintained real-Postgres claim-ssot-agreement integration suite; inspect source-only, canonical-conflict, itemRefs, tenant, fixed-cohort and by-ID assertions.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/claim-ssot-agreement.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Narrow reservation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"An item-scoped direct-route decision reserves only source work whose item IDs overlap its item references.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"An item-scoped direct-route decision reserves only source work whose item IDs overlap its item references.\",\"falsifier\":\"A nonmatching item or unrelated tenant is reserved, or a matching source item escapes.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the maintained real-Postgres claim-ssot-agreement integration suite; inspect source-only, canonical-conflict, itemRefs, tenant, fixed-cohort and by-ID assertions.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/claim-ssot-agreement.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Deliberate access and agreement.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Explicit by-ID pickup remains available, fixed-cohort diagnostics see the same reservation, and maintained real-PG tests bind both implementations without altering the stable public DB signature.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Explicit by-ID pickup remains available, fixed-cohort diagnostics see the same reservation, and maintained real-PG tests bind both implementations without altering the stable public DB signature.\",\"falsifier\":\"A named pickup fails, fixed-cohort diagnostics miss the source identity, or the public SQL function is incompatible.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"integration\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run the maintained real-Postgres claim-ssot-agreement integration suite; inspect source-only, canonical-conflict, itemRefs, tenant, fixed-cohort and by-ID assertions.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/scheduler/claim-ssot-agreement.integration.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n\n## Design\nExtend only the existing decision-reservation seam. Keep existing payload.plan_item decision identity when it names a plan; otherwise resolve source_plan_slug/source_plan_item_ids from the candidate work-item. This bounds the repair to source-only records and preserves pre-existing lane authority. The compatible SQL wrapper resolves canonical identity by workspace + feature_id, adds the matching route floor once, and leaves prior floors intact. Preserve existing affirmative route patterns and itemRefs semantics. Keep lifecycle/lease/dependency behavior out of this source-only repair.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-003 | tree |\n\n## Phase 1 — Reservation repair\n- **P-001** `todo` Reproduce the canonical source-only reservation miss in the maintained PostgreSQL agreement suite with item, tenant and unbound controls. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Extend the existing TypeScript and compatible DB decision floors with canonical source identity; preserve itemRefs and by-ID access. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Verify focused regression and existing reservation agreement cases, record immutable source/test evidence, and complete WI20092 with measured scope limits. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n### D-001 — Direct source repair under inherited AUTO\nThe current registered fleet leader implements this bounded repair directly. This is agent-derived work required by measured WI20092, not delegation of get-feedback implementation. No LIVE_GATE_OPS or production migration application is included. Existing automatic locking, fleet scope, admission, proof and owner walls remain in force.\n\n### D-002 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: wi20092-source-only-r1-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: 911a79ce6e1f482954b307cc67411c41417f53f7ba1d2dc8feea604026eb2f76\nActor: su-6c30dac5-f3fb-4c45-937e-34ee5ed96cc2\nReason: Narrow the agent-derived bar to the reproduced source-only defect; preserve existing payload-linked route authority. Plan revision3 and regression controls record the scope.\nApproved-By: su-e2cf302c-d4e3-4797-b109-e8e2a14f063d\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1194466\nApproved-At: 2026-10-22T09:16:23.396Z\nRubric revision: 1 → 2\nSubject plan revision: 4 → 5\nChanged BARs: R-1\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\nRequirements re-rendered from the amended criterion: R-1\n\n### D-003 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: wi20092-r2-atomic-map-r1-r3-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: d6257e52f6cd985b704400fff09db577fd0321d8686b0890b59e6ef272ea3acf\nActor: su-6c30dac5-f3fb-4c45-937e-34ee5ed96cc2\nReason: Repair evaluator-confirmed compound R2 and duplicate projections. R2 becomes one item-scope outcome; independent controls remain in plan Design and tests. Unchanged R1 and R3 map only to their implementing/verification items.\nApproved-By: su-600c9cd3-0908-444b-87f7-e1a101bca706\nApproval-Ref: thread-post:1194504\nApproved-At: 2026-10-22T09:24:10.017Z\nRubric revision: 2 → 3\nSubject plan revision: 6 → 7\nChanged BARs: R-2\nMapping delta: R-1 P-001, P-002, P-003 (tree) → P-002 (tree)\nMapping delta: R-3 P-002, P-003 (tree) → P-003 (tree)\nPrior evidence, grades, vetting, author verdicts, and ship verdicts remain audit history and are revision-ineligible.\n\n### D-004 — Acceptance BAR amendment\nDate: 2026-10-22\nAmendment-Id: wi20092-r2-map-apply-v1\nRequest-Hash: f96c69e9e8886d2bf60c437a28185559d4c63360c469dc2eedad2d17d7eb2d28\nActor: su-6c30dac5-f3fb-4c45-937e-34ee5ed96cc2\nReason: Complete one-to-one BAR mapping after the approved atomic R2 repair. preparation","status":"draft","created":"2026-10-22","owner":null,"archived":false,"template_slug":null,"origin":"local","is_blender_origin":false,"content":"---\ntitle: Overlap independent Codex home repair preparation\nslug: codex-home-preparation-concurrency-2026-10-22\nstatus: draft\ncreated: 2026-10-22\nupdated: 2026-10-22\n---\n\n## Product shaping\nAudience: Avi and agents blocked during Codex continuation. The exact reported su2585 incident combines an unshipped compatibility/detector fix with a current repair handler that can complete after the client's unchanged 10-second request deadline. Outcome: remove independent serial preparation and verify a real managed carry without changing identity, account, funding or release safety. Non-goals: raising timeouts, skipping policy/funding checks, or taking over held LIVE_GATE_OPS. Source turn: session_turn:codex:01a163dd-67d0-73b3-bb3c-875974650568:18. The citation question is answered from its exact native transcript and recorded separately on EI-26693182978373950.\n\n## Requirements\n**R-1 — Preserve repair authority.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"The exact owner/native/model/account, funding gate, ambient-context policy and compaction budget must reach the canonical writer; owner mismatch still exits before rebuild or writing, and pinned-source errors retain their current behavior.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"Every home write uses the resolved authorization and configuration for its exact requested session.\",\"falsifier\":\"The behavioral route test fails, or a repair writes before its owner, policy, budget and funding results are resolved.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run testing:run for packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/adv/sessions-ensure-codex-home.test.ts and inspect the independent-preparation regression plus existing funding/policy/pinned-source cases.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/adv/sessions-ensure-codex-home.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-2 — Overlap independent preparation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Launch-record and session-row reads may overlap. Policy and budget reads must run alongside the funded rebuild, with all results settled before any home write. The production client timeout remains unchanged. A behavioral test must fail under the original serialization and pass after the change.\"},\"acceptance\":{\"condition\":\"The funded instruction rebuild starts before pending independent preparation reads resolve.\",\"falsifier\":\"The behavioral route test fails, or a repair writes before its owner, policy, budget and funding results are resolved.\",\"requiredTestLayers\":[\"unit\"]},\"verification\":{\"method\":\"Run testing:run for packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/adv/sessions-ensure-codex-home.test.ts and inspect the independent-preparation regression plus existing funding/policy/pinned-source cases.\",\"check\":{\"kind\":\"tests\",\"files\":[\"packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/adv/sessions-ensure-codex-home.test.ts\"]}}}\n```\n\n**R-3 — Verify actual continuation.**\n```requirement\n{\"intent\":{\"request\":\"Focused tests and typecheck must pass. Extend shared dispatch/request context and invocation metadata, preserve current request UUIDs, and propagate W3C context across the selected boundaries. Add safe model and error observations to the existing PostHog project, preferring its maintained SDK/integration and respecting the deployed endpoint's actual capabilities. Keep export bounded, asynchronous and fail-open; recheck existing consent/tenant authority. Select only safe scalar metadata. External vendor runtimes remain an explicit observation boundary. No additional vendors or services are introduced.\n\n### Bar-to-work map for this plan\n\n| bar | implementing plan items | evidence plane |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| R-1 | P-001 | tree |\n| R-2 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-3 | P-002 | tree |\n| R-4 | P-003 | tree |\n| R-5 | P-004 | deployed |\n\n## Phase 1 — OpenTelemetry and PostHog\n\n- **P-001** `todo` Add standard OpenTelemetry runtime context and spans at shared request/dispatch boundaries with stable invocation references and concurrency tests. importance: high\n- **P-002** `todo` Export safe consented model/error observations to existing PostHog with bounded delivery and failure/privacy tests. blocked-by: P-001 importance: high\n- **P-003** `todo` Prove production composition and connected request/export behavior on an isolated current-build route; complete acceptance and runtime documentation. blocked-by: P-002 importance: high\n- **P-004** `todo` Drive canonical acceptance, green promotion and release deployment, and verify the exact shipped artifact and synthetic PostHog evidence. blocked-by: P-003 importance: high\n\n## Decisions\n\n- **D-001** Owner-selected scope: OpenTelemetry and PostHog only. Every other assessed monitoring/tracing tool is deferred.
